Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not speak too much without mentioning God, for speaking too much without mentioning God hardens the heart, and the people farthest from God are those with hard hearts. In Musnad al-Bazzar, on the authority of Anas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Four things are a source of misery: a dull eye, a hard heart, long hopes, and greed for this world." The Almighty said: So they are like stones or even harder. Or it was said that it has the meaning of and, as He said: A sinner or an ungrateful one. “An excuse or a vow.” And the poet said: He attained the caliphate or it was his destiny Any and it was. It was said: It means rather, as God Almighty said: And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more meaning rather they are more. And the poet said: You looked like the sun's horn in the brilliance of the morning, and its image or you are more beautiful in the eye No, but you. It was said: Its meaning is to make the addressee vague, and from this is the saying of Abu Al-Aswad Al-Du’ali: I love Muhammad very much, and Abbas, and Hamza, and Ali If their love is right, I will follow it, and I am not mistaken if it is wrong. Abu Al-Aswad did not doubt that their love was apparent guidance, but he intended to be vague. It was said to Abu Al-Aswad when he said that: Do you have doubts? He said: No, then he cited as evidence the words of God Almighty: And either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. And he said: Or was he doubting who told this? It was said: Its meaning is choice, that is, they likened them to stones that strike, or to something harder than stones that strike. This is like the saying of someone: Sit with Al-Hasan or Ibn Sirin, and learn jurisprudence or hadith or grammar. It was said: Rather, it is in its category of doubt, and its meaning with you, O addressees, and in your view, is that if you saw its hardness, you would doubt: Is it like stones or harder than stones? This meaning has been said about the words of God Almighty: Up to a hundred thousand or more. A group said: God Almighty only meant that among them are those whose hearts are like stones, and among them are those whose hearts are harder than stones. So the meaning is: They are two groups. The Almighty said: or more severe. More severe is in the nominative case in apposition to the position of the kaf in His statement, like stones, because the meaning is: they are like stones or more severe. It is permissible to say or more severe in apposition to stones. “Harshness” is in the accusative case as a specification. Abu Haywah read harshness, and the meaning is the same. God the Almighty said: And indeed, among the stones are those from which rivers burst forth, and indeed, among them are those that split asunder and water issues from them. The meaning of bursting forth has already been mentioned. The root of bursting is bursting, with the ta’ assimilated into the sheen. This refers to springs that have not grown large enough to become rivers, or to stones that crack even if no water flows. Ibn Masraf read yanshaq with a noon, and he read lama yatafujar lama yatafujar with a shaddah on lama in both places. This is an incorrect reading. Malik ibn Dinar read yanfajar with a noon and a kasrah on the jim. Qatada said: He excused the stones, but did not excuse the wretched of the children of Adam. Abu Hatim said: It is permissible to say lama tafujar with a ta’, but it is not permissible to say lama tafujar with a ta’, because if he said tafujar, he would feminize it by feminizing the rivers, and this does not happen in tashquq. An-Nahhas said: What he denied is permissible based on the meaning, because the meaning is: Indeed, among them are stones that crack, and as for yatafujar, it is based on the word ma. The crack is one of the cracks, so it is originally a source. You say: In the hand of so-and-so and his feet are cracks, and do not say: shaqāq, rather, the crack is a disease that affects animals, and it is a crack that affects their ankles and may rise to their shoulders, on the authority of Ya’qub. The crack: the morning. And what is in his saying: When it bursts forth is in the accusative case, because it is the name of in and the lam is for emphasis. From it is on the word what, and it is permissible from it on the meaning, And from it is what is cracked and water comes out of it. Qatada read in in both places, lightened from the heavy. God the Almighty says: And indeed, among them are those that descend for fear of God. He says that among the stones are those that are more beneficial than your hearts, because water comes out of them and they fall. Mujahid said: No stone falls from the top of a mountain, nor does a river gush forth from a rock, nor does water come out of it, except for fear of God. The Noble Qur’an revealed this. And something similar was narrated by Ibn Jurayj. Some of the theologians said about His statement: And indeed, among them are those that descend for fear of God. The hail descending from the clouds. It was said: The word descend is a metaphor, because since the stones are considered by their creation, and are humbled by looking at them, the humility of the one looking at them was attributed to them, as the Arabs said: A merchant’s camel, meaning it prompts whoever sees it to buy it. At-Tabari narrated from a group that fear for the stones is borrowed, just as will was borrowed for the wall in His statement: It wants to collapse, and as Zayd al-Khayl said: When the report of Al-Zubayr came, the city walls and the mountains were humbled. Ibn Bahr mentioned that the pronoun in the Almighty’s saying: And among them refers to the hearts, not to the stones, meaning among the hearts because of what they submit to out of fear of God. I said: Everything that has been said is possible due to the wording, and the first is correct, because it is not impossible for some inanimate objects to be given knowledge and thus rational, like the one who... It was narrated about the tree trunk that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to lean on when he gave a sermon. When he turned away from it, he went crazy. It was confirmed that he said: A stone used to greet me in the pre-Islamic era, and I recognize it now. And “It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Thabeer said to me: Come down, for I fear that they will kill you on my back and God will punish me.” So Hiraa’ called out to him: Come to me, O Messenger of God. And in the revelation: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains (al-Baqarah 2:14). And he said: If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and coming apart from fear of God (al-Baqarah 2:14). Meaning, humility and submission, and more clarification of this will come in Surat Subhan, God willing. God the Almighty says: And God is not unaware of what you do. Ghafil is in the accusative case in the dialect of the people of Hijaz, and in the nominative case in the dialect of Tamim. The ya is for emphasis. Of what you do means of your deeds, so that He does not leave anything small or great without counting it against you. So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it. “Ma” does not need a pronoun unless it is made in the sense of who, in which case the pronoun is deleted due to the length of the noun, meaning of what you do. Ibn Kathir read ya’malun with the ya, and the addressee in this case is Muhammad, peace be upon him.
2:75: God Almighty says: Do you then hope that they will believe in you while a party of them used to hear the word of God and then distort it after they had understood it while they knew? There are four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying, Do you then hope that they will believe in you? This is a question that contains a sense of denial, as if He made them despair of the belief of this group of Jews, meaning that if they disbelieved, then they had a precedent in that. The address is to the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is because the Ansar were keen on the conversion of the Jews to Islam due to the alliance and neighbourhood that existed between them. It was said that the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Meaning, do not be sad about their denial of you, and inform him that they are among the evil people who have passed away. And that is in the accusative case, meaning that they will believe, it is in the accusative case because of that, and that is why the nun was deleted from it. It is said: He coveted it with greed and greed - lightened - it is greed, on the weight of fa’l. And someone else made him covet it. And it is said in astonishment: The man coveted - with a damma on the meem - meaning he became very greedy. Greed is the provisions of the soldiers. It is said: The prince ordered them to have their greed, meaning their provisions. And a woman who is greedy: she covets but is not able. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And there was a party of them. The party is a collective noun with no singular form, and its plural in the smallest number is afarqahu, and in the largest number it is afarqa’. They hear is in the accusative case as the predicate of kana. It is possible that the predicate is from them, and they hear is an adjective for a party, and there is some distance in that. The speech of God is the reading of the group. Al-A’mash read God spoke as the plural of word. Sibawayh said: And know that some people from Rabi’ah say from them with a kasra on the ha’ following the secret of the meem, and the dwelling was not a strong barrier for them. The speech of God is the object of they hear. What is meant are the seventy whom Moses, peace be upon him, chose, so they heard the speech of God but did not obey His command, and they distorted the statement in their informing their people. This is the saying of al-Rabi’ and Ibn Ishaq, and there is weakness in this saying. Whoever says that the seventy heard what Moses heard has made a mistake, and has taken away the virtue of Moses and his being singled out for speaking. Al-Suddi and others said: They could not bear to hear it, and their minds were confused and they wanted Moses to hear it and repeat it to them. When they finished and left, a group of them changed what they had heard of the words of God on the tongue of their prophet Moses, peace be upon him, as God Almighty said: And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of God. If it is said: Al-Kalbi narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The people of Moses asked Moses to ask his Lord to let them hear his words, so they heard a voice like the voice of a hyena: I am God, there is none but I, the Living, the Eternal. I brought you out of Egypt with a high hand and a strong arm. I said: This is a false hadith that is not authentic. It was narrated by Ibn Marwan on the authority of Al-Kalbi, and both of them are weak and cannot be used as evidence. Rather, speech is something that was given to Moses specifically from among all the children of Adam. If he also spoke to his people so that they could hear his speech, then what is Moses’ superiority over them? He said, and His statement is the truth: I have chosen you over mankind with My messages and My speech. This is clear. Third: People differed about how Moses knew the speech of God, as he had not heard His speech before that. Some of them said: He heard speech that was not letters and sounds, and in which there was no interruption or breath, so then he knew that it was not the speech of evil, but rather the speech of the Lord of the Worlds. Others said: When he heard speech from no direction, and the speech of humans is heard from one of the six directions, he knew that it was not the speech of humans. It was said: His entire body became ears until he heard that speech with them, so he knew that it was the speech of God. It was said about it: The miracle indicated that what he heard was the speech of God, and that is because it was said to him: Throw down your staff, so he threw it and it became a snake, so that was a sign to him of the truth of the situation, and that the one who was saying to him: I am your Lord is God Almighty. It was said: He had concealed something in his soul that only the Knower of the Unseen can comprehend, so God Almighty informed him in His address with that pronoun, so he knew that the one who was addressing him was God Almighty. In Surat Al-Qasas, the meaning of the Almighty’s saying will be explained: He was called from the right side of the valley in the blessed spot from the tree, God willing. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: Then they distort it. Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: They are the Jewish scholars who distort the Torah, making what is forbidden permissible and what is permissible forbidden, following their whims. After they have understood it, meaning they have come to know it and learned it. This is a rebuke to them, meaning that these Jews had done evil and stubborn deeds in the past, and these people are following that tradition, so how can you hope for their faith?! This statement also indicates that the one who knows the truth but is stubborn about it is far from guidance, because he knew the promise and the threat, but that did not stop him from his stubbornness.
2:76: God Almighty says: “And when they meet those who believe, they say, ‘We believe.’ But when they are alone with one another, they say, ‘Do you tell them what God has disclosed to you so that they may dispute with you about it before your Lord? Then will you not reason?’”
2:77: The Almighty said: And when they meet those who believe, they say, 'We believe.' This is about the hypocrites. The root of laqa is laqiwu, and it has been mentioned before. And when they are alone with one another the verse is about the Jews, because some of them converted to Islam and then became hypocrites, so they used to tell the believing Arabs about what their fathers were punished with, so the Jews said to them: Do you tell them about what God has revealed to you? meaning the punishment that God has decreed upon you, so that you may say, We are more honorable to God than you, according to Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi. It was also said: “When Ali was fighting Qurayzah on the day of Khaybar, he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, being cursed. He turned to him and said: ‘O Messenger of God, do not go to them.’ He approached him and said: ‘I think you heard my cursing from them. If they saw me, they would stop.’ He got up to go to them, but when they saw him, they stopped. He said to them: ‘You have broken the covenant, O brothers of apes and pigs. May God disgrace you and bring down His vengeance upon you.’ They said: ‘You were not ignorant, O Muhammad, so do not act ignorantly towards us. Who told you this? This report came from us only!’” It was narrated on the authority of al-Ma’na on the authority of Mujahid. God the Almighty said: And when he is alone. The root of khala is khalu, the waw was changed to alif because of its movement and the openness of what preceded it. The meaning of khala was presented at the beginning of the surah. The meaning of fatha is ruling. Fath among the Arabs means judgment and ruling, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of judges. That is, the judge. Al-Fattah is the judge in the language of Yemen. It is said: Between me and you is the Fattah. This was said because he supports the oppressed against the oppressor. Fath means victory, and from this is His saying: They seek victory against those who disbelieve, and His saying: If you seek victory, victory has already come to you. It can mean the difference between two things. God the Almighty said: to argue with you is in the accusative case with the lam of ki, or if you wish, with the omission of an, and the sign of the accusative is the deletion of the nun. Yunus said: Some Arabs open the lam of ki. Al-Akhfash said: Because the opening is the original. Khalaf al-Ahmar said: It is the language of Bani al-Anbar. The meaning of to argue with you is to taunt you and say, We are more honorable to God than you. It was also said: The meaning is to argue with you with your words, saying, You disbelieved in him after you knew his truthfulness. It was also said that a Jewish man would meet his Muslim friend and say to him: Hold fast to the religion of Muhammad, for he is truly a prophet. "With your Lord" was said in the afterlife, what he said: "Then on the Day of Resurrection, you will dispute before your Lord." It was also said: When mentioning your Lord. It was also said: "With" means in, i.e. to argue with you about your Lord, so that they will be more deserving of it than you because the argument has become clear to you. This was narrated from al-Hasan. Argument is straight speech in general, and from that is the path of the road. I argued with someone and defeated him, meaning I defeated him with an argument. From this comes the hadith: So Adam made the pilgrimage to Moses. Do you not understand? It was said: It is from the statement of the followers. It was said: It is an address from God Almighty to the believers, meaning: Do you not understand that the Children of Israel do not believe while they are in these conditions? Then He rebuked them with a recitation that is recited, saying: Or do they not know? The verse. It is a question that means rebuke and reprimand. The majority read they know with a ya, and Ibn Muhaysin with a ta, addressing the believers. What they concealed was their disbelief, and what they declared their denial of.
2:78: God Almighty says: And among them are unlettered people who do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking, and they do nothing but conjecture. There are four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And among them are the unlettered ones, meaning among the Jews. It was said: Among the Jews and the hypocrites are the unlettered ones, meaning those who neither write nor read, and the singular of them is illiterate, attributed to the illiterate nation that is, based on the birth of their mothers, they did not learn to write or read, and from this is his saying, peace be upon him: We are an illiterate nation; we neither write nor calculate. The hadith. They were called illiterate because they did not believe in the Mother of the Book, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abu Ubaidah said: They were called illiterate because the Book was revealed to them, as if they were attributed to the Mother of the Book, so it was as if he said: And among them are the People of the Book who do not know the Book. Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak: They are the Arab Christians. It was said: They are a people from the People of the Book, whose Book was lifted because of sins they committed, so they became illiterate. Ali, may God be pleased with him: They are the Magians. I said: The first statement is more apparent, and God knows best. The second: The Almighty’s saying: They do not know the Scripture except in wishful thinking. “Except” here means but, so it is an interrupted exception, like the Almighty’s saying: They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And Al-Nabigha said: I took an oath that was not dualistic or knowledgeable except for a good opinion of the owner Abu Ja`far, Shaiba and Al-A`raj read except for āmānī with a light ya’, deleting one of the two ya’s for the sake of lightness. Abu Hatim said: Everything that comes in this manner and its singular is doubled, so you have the option of double or lightening it, such as athāfī, aghānī, āmānī, and the like. Al-Akhfash said: This is like what is said in the plural of miftah: mafātih and mafātih, and it is the plural ya’. Al-Nahhas said: Deletion is more common in weak words, as the poet said: Does the delivery return or does the blindness reveal the three stoves and the barren drawings? Wishes is the plural of wish, which means recitation. Its root is amnawiyah, with the weight of af’ulah, then the waw was assimilated into the ya’ and the nun was broken because of the ya’, so it became amniyyah. From this is the saying of God Almighty: Except when he recites, Satan casts into his wish, meaning when he recites, Satan casts into his recitation. Ka’b ibn Malik said: Wish for the Book of God the first night and the last night he will find the dove of destiny Another said: The Book of God was wished for on the last night, as David wished for the Psalms on the messengers. Wishes also mean lies, such as the saying of Uthman may God be pleased with him: I have not wished for anything since I converted to Islam, meaning I have not lied. And the saying of some Arabs to Ibn Dab while he was narrating: Is this something you saw or something you wished for? meaning you made it up. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid interpreted wishes in the verse with this meaning. Wishes are also what a person wishes and desires. Qatada said: Except for wishes, meaning that they wish from God what they do not have. It was said: Wishes are estimation. It is said: He wished for him, meaning he estimated it. Al-Jawhari said this, and Ibn Bahr narrated it, and he recited the words of the poet: Do not feel safe even if you spend the night in a sanctuary until you find what God has promised you. That is, the destined one is destined for you. Third: The Almighty’s statement: And they only assume. “In” means what the negative, as the Almighty said: The disbelievers are only in delusion. “And they assume” means they lie and invent things, because they have no knowledge of the truth of what they recite, but rather they are imitating their rabbis in what they recite. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Nahwi told us that the Arabs make conjecture knowledge, doubt, and falsehood. He said: If the evidence of knowledge is established and is more than the evidence of doubt, then conjecture is certainty. If the evidence of certainty and the evidence of doubt are equal, then conjecture is doubt. If the evidence of doubt exceeds the evidence of certainty, then conjecture is falsehood. God Almighty said: They only conjecture, meaning they only lie. Fourth: Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: God the Almighty described their rabbis as those who change and distort, so He said, and His statement is true: So woe to those who write the Scripture with their own hands Al-An’am 4:17. That is because when the matter became obsolete among them, and the subjects of their scholars became bad, and they turned to the world out of greed and covetousness, they sought things that would turn people’s faces towards them, so they innovated in their law and changed it, and they attached that to the Torah, and they said to their fools: This is from God, so that they would accept it from them and their leadership would be confirmed and they would gain the debris and filth of the world through it. Among the innovations they innovated was that they said: We have no right to the illiterate people, and they are the Arabs, meaning whatever we take from their money is permissible for us. Among the innovations they innovated was that they said: No sin will harm us, for we are His beloved and His children, God is exalted above that! It was in the Torah, O my rabbis and O sons of my messengers, but they changed it and wrote, O my beloved ones and O my sons. Then God revealed their denial: And the Jews and the Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God and His beloved.’ Say, ‘Then why does He punish you for your sins?’ They said, God will not punish us, and if He punishes us, it will be for forty days, the same as the days of the calf. Then God revealed: And they say, ‘The Fire will not touch us except for a few days.’ Say, ‘Have you taken a covenant from God?’ Ibn Muqsim said: He means monotheism, as evidenced by the words of God, Except for he who has taken a covenant from the Most Merciful, meaning there is no god but God. “So God will not break His covenant. Or do you say about God that which you do not know?” Then He denied them and said, “Yes, whoever earns evil and his sin encompasses him - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally. But those who believe and do righteous deeds - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.” So God made it clear that eternity in the Fire and Paradise is according to disbelief and belief, not according to what they said.
2:79: It has five issues: First: His saying: Woe. There is a difference of opinion about what woe is. Uthman bin Affan narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: It is a mountain of fire. Narrated by Abu Saeed Al-Khudri. Woe is a valley in Hell between two men, into which the afflicted person falls for forty autumns. It was narrated on the authority of Sufyan and Ata bin Yasar: That the woe in this verse is a valley flowing in the courtyard of Hell from the pus of the people of Hell. It was also said: A cistern in Hell. Al-Zahrawi narrated on the authority of others: It is one of the gates of Hell. Ibn Abbas said: Woe is the hardship of torment. Al-Khalil said: Woe is the intensity of evil. Al-Asma'i: Woe is grief, and woe is mercy. Sibawayh: Woe to he who has fallen into destruction, and woe is a warning to he who is on the verge of destruction. Ibn Arafa: Woe is sadness. It is said: A man calls out for woe, and this is only said when he is sad and distressed, and from this is His statement: So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands. It was said: Its origin is destruction, and everyone who falls into destruction calls out for woe, and from this is His statement, the Most High: Oh, woe to us! What is this Book? It is woe and misery, and they are destruction, and the plural is woes. He said: Woe to him if he lives without Umm Hashim He also said: And the calamities said to you that you are my mantle Woe is raised by the beginning, and it is permissible to begin with it even if it is indefinite because it has the meaning of supplication. Al-Akhfash said: The accusative case is permissible with an implied verb, meaning may God impose woe upon them. Al-Farra’ said: The origin of woe is woe, meaning sorrow, as you say: Woe to so-and-so, meaning sorrow for him, so the Arabs connected it with lam and estimated it from it and parsed it. The best thing for it if it is separated from the addition is the nominative case, because it requires occurrence. The accusative case is correct with the meaning of supplication, as we mentioned. Al-Khalil said: “Only waih, waiwais, waih, waik, wail, and waiba have been heard with its construction, and all of them are close in meaning. Some people have differentiated between them, and they are verbal nouns from which the Arabs did not pronounce a verb.” Al-Jarmi said: “Among the nouns that are in the accusative case are wailah, waihah, waihah, and waiysa. If the lam is inserted, they are raised, so qatal means wailah, waih lahu.” Second: God Almighty says: For those who write. Writing is well-known. The first person to write with a pen was Idris, peace be upon him. This was mentioned in the hadith of Abu Dharr, narrated by Al-Ajurri and others. It has been said that Adam, peace be upon him, was given writing, so it became an inheritance for his children. Third: The Almighty’s statement, in their hands, is an emphasis, for He knows that writing can only be done by hand. It is like His statement, nor a bird that flies with its wings, and His statement, they say with their mouths. It was said: The benefit of in their hands is a clarification of their crime and proof of their public declaration, for the one who undertakes the action is more severe in its occurrence than the one who does not undertake it, even if it is his opinion. Ibn al-Sarraj said: in their hands is a metaphor for them being of their own accord without it being revealed to them, even if it is not actually in the books in their hands. Fourth: In this verse and the one before it there is a warning against changing, altering, and adding to the Sharia. Whoever changes, alters, or innovates in the religion of God something that is not part of it and is not permissible in it is included under this severe threat and painful punishment. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, warned his nation when he knew what would happen at the end of time, saying: Behold, those before you from the People of the Book split into seventy-two sects, and this nation will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one. The hadith, and it will come. So he warned them not to introduce into the religion on their own anything contrary to the Book of God or His Sunnah or the Sunnah of his Companions, thereby leading people astray. What he warned against has happened and has become widespread, increased and well-known. So to God we belong and to Him we shall return. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: To exchange it for a small price. God the Almighty described what they take as little, either because it is perishable and not permanent, or because it is forbidden, because there is no blessing in what is forbidden and it does not increase with God. Ibn Ishaq and Al-Kalbi said: The description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their book was that he was of medium build and dark skin, so they made him a tall, straight-chested man, and they said to their companions and followers: Look at the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who will be sent at the end of time, and this description does not resemble him. The rabbis and scholars had leadership and earnings, so they feared that if they made it clear, their food and leadership would be lost, so they changed it. Then God Almighty said: So woe to them for what their hands have written and woe to them for what they earn. It was said that it was from food. It was said that it was from sins. And he repeated the woe to make their actions more severe.
2:80: There are three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And they said, meaning the Jews, The Fire will not touch us except for a few days. There is disagreement about the reason for its revelation. It was said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the Jews: Who are the people of Hell? They said: We are, then you will succeed us. He said: You have lied, you know that we will not succeed you. So this verse was revealed, as Ibn Zayd said. Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina and the Jews were saying: This world is only seven thousand years, and people are only tormented in Hell for every thousand years of this world, one day in Hell from the days of the Hereafter, but it is only seven days. So God revealed the verse, and this is the saying of Mujahid. A group said: The Jews said that in the Torah it says that Hell is a journey of forty years, and that they will cut off a year every day until they complete it and Hell goes away. Ad-Dahhak narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Jews claimed that they found written in the Torah that the distance between the two ends of Hell is a journey of forty years until they reach the tree of Zaqqum. They said: We are only tormented until we reach the tree of Zaqqum, and Hell goes away and is destroyed. On the authority of Ibn Abbas and Qatada: The Jews said that God swore that He would put them in Hell for forty days, the number of days for which they worshipped the calf, but God denied them, as mentioned above. Second: In this verse there is a response to Abu Hanifa and his companions, as they cited as evidence the saying of peace be upon him: Leave the prayer during the days of your menstrual cycle. The duration of menstruation is what is called the days of menstruation, and the minimum is three, in which there are eleven. They said that what is less than three is called one day or two days, and what is more than ten is called eleven days, and it is not called days, but rather it is called days from three to ten. God Almighty said: Then fast three days during the Hajj, “Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days,” He subjected them to seven nights and eight days in succession. It is said to them: God Almighty said about fasting: A numbered number of days, meaning the entire month, and He said: The Fire will not touch us except for a numbered number of days, meaning forty days. Also, if the days are added to an incident, it is not intended to specify a number, but rather it is said: the days of your walking, your travel, and your stay, even if it is thirty or twenty or whatever number you want, and perhaps He meant what was customary for it, and the custom is six or seven, so the statement was excluded from it, and God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: Have you taken” The discussion of took has already been presented, so there is no point in repeating it, a covenant with God meaning, have you done a good deed in advance, then believed and obeyed, and thus deserved to be released from the Fire! Or did you know that through His revelation that He entrusted to you? God will not fail in His covenant, or do you say about God that which you do not know? A rebuke and rebuke.
2:81: God Almighty says: Yes, whoever earns evil and his sin encompasses him - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
2:82: There are three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: By God means that the matter is not as you mentioned. Sibawayh said: By God and Na’am are not nouns. Rather, they are two letters like bal and others, and it is a response to their saying: The Fire will not touch us. The Kufians said: Its origin is bal which is used to contradict the first, and the letter ya was added to it to make the pause better, and the letter ya included the meaning of affirmation and blessing. So bal indicates the rejection of denial, and the letter ya indicates the affirmation of what comes after. They said: If someone said: Didn’t you take a dinar? and you said: Yes, the meaning would be: No, I did not take, because you confirmed the negation and what comes after it. So if you said: By God, the meaning would be: I have taken.” Al-Farra’ said: If a man says to his friend: You owe him something, and the other says: Yes, that is confirmation, because he has nothing against him. If he said: By God, it would be a response to his saying, and its meaning is: Yes, I owe you. In the Qur’an: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes. If they had said: Yes, they would have disbelieved. Second: The Almighty’s saying: evil. Evil is polytheism. Ibn Jurayj said: I said to Ata’: Who committed evil? He said: Polytheism. Then he recited: And whoever brings evil - their faces will be thrown into the Fire. And this is what Al-Hasan and Qatada said. They said: And the major sin. Third: When God Almighty said: Yes, whoever has earned evil and his sin has encompassed him, it indicates that what is suspended on two conditions is not fulfilled with the least of them. Similar to it is God Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, and his saying, peace be upon him, to Sufyan ibn Abdullah al-Thaqafi when he said to him: O Messenger of God, tell me something about Islam that I will not ask anyone else about after you. He said: “Say: ‘I believe in God,’ then be steadfast.” Narrated by Muslim. This meaning and what the scholars have said about it have already been discussed in the words of God the Almighty to Adam and Eve: And do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers. Nafi’ read his sins in the plural, while the rest read them in the singular, and the meaning is abundance, like the words of God the Almighty: If you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them.
2:83: It contains ten issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And when We took a covenant from the Children of Israel. We have already discussed these words. There is disagreement about the covenant here. Makki said: It is the covenant that was taken from them when they were brought out from the loins of Adam like atoms. It was said: It is a covenant that was taken from them while they were rational in their lives on the tongues of their prophets, and it is His saying: Worship none but God. And worshipping God is affirming His Oneness, believing in His messengers, and acting according to what He revealed in His books. Second: The Almighty said: Do not worship. Sibawayh said: Do not worship is related to an oath, and the meaning is: And if We make them successors, by God, you will not worship. Al-Mubarrad, Al-Kisa’i, and Al-Farra’ permitted it. Abi and Ibn Mas’ud read Do not worship as a prohibition, and that is why the speech was connected to a command, so He said: And stand up, “Say,” Establish, and Give. It was said: It is in the position of a state, meaning We took their covenant to be monotheists, or not to be stubborn. This was also said by Qatrub and Al-Mubarrad. This is only correct according to the reading of Ibn Kathir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i, They worship with the ya from below. Al-Farra’, Al-Zajjaj, and a group said: The meaning is: We took their covenant that they will not worship except God, and that they will be good to their parents, and that they will not shed blood. Then an and ba were deleted, so the verb was raised because they were gone, like the Almighty’s saying: Do you command me to do other than God? Al-Mubarrad said: This is wrong, because everything that is implied in Arabic works like an explicit noun. You say: And a country I cut off, meaning there is a country. I said this is not a mistake, rather they are two correct views, and based on them Sibawayh recited: Oh you who deters, come to the battlefield and witness the pleasures. Are you immortal? In the accusative and nominative cases, the accusative case is based on the omission of an, and the nominative case is based on its deletion. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And to parents, good treatment. That is, We commanded him to be good to his parents. In this verse, God the Almighty linked the right of the parents to monotheism, because the first upbringing is from God, and the second upbringing - which is education - is from the parents. For this reason, God the Almighty linked thanking them with thanking Him, saying: That you be grateful to Me and to your parents. And being kind to one’s parents means treating them kindly, being humble towards them, obeying their commands, praying for forgiveness after their death, and maintaining ties with their loved ones, as will be explained in detail in Al-Isra’, God willing. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: and the relatives. The relatives are connected to the parents. The relatives mean kinship, and it is a verbal noun like raj’i and al-‘uqba, meaning, and We commanded them to be kind to the relatives by maintaining ties of kinship. This will be explained in detail in Surat al-Qital, God willing. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying, And the orphans. Orphans is also an appositive, and it is the plural of an orphan, like companions is the plural of companion. Orphanhood among the children of Adam is due to the loss of a father, and among animals is due to the loss of a mother. Al-Mawardi narrated that an orphan is said among the children of Adam in the loss of a mother, and the first is well-known. Its origin is isolation, it is said: an orphan boy, meaning isolated from his father. An orphan house: meaning there is no poetry before or after it. An orphan pearl has no equal. It was said: Its origin is slowness, so the orphan was named after it, because righteousness is slow to come to him. It is said: he becomes orphaned, he becomes an orphan, like he becomes great. And he becomes orphaned, he becomes an orphan, he becomes an orphan, like he hears, Al-Farra’ mentioned the two faces. And God has made him an orphan. This indicates compassion for the orphan and the urging to sponsor him and protect his money, as will be explained in An-Nisa’. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The one who takes care of an orphan, whether he is his or someone else’s, he and I will be like these two in Paradise. Malik pointed with his index and middle fingers. Narrated by Abu Hurayrah and included in Muslim’s collection. Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad Abd Al-Ghani bin Saeed included in his collection a hadith on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Dinar Abu Saeed Al-Basri, who is Al-Hasan bin Wasil, who said: Al-Aswad bin Abd Al-Rahman told us on the authority of Hissan on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No orphan sits with people on their plate and the devil approaches their plate. It was also narrated from the hadith of Hasan ibn Qays, who is Abu Ali al-Rahabi, on the authority of Ikrimah, “on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever takes an orphan from among the Muslims to his food and drink until God Almighty makes him independent, his sins will be forgiven for all, unless he does an unforgivable deed. Whoever God takes away his two most precious things and he is patient and seeks reward from God, his sins will be forgiven.” They said: And what are his two most precious things? He said: His two eyes. They said: And whoever has three daughters or three sisters and spends on them and treats them well until they grow up or die, his sins will be forgiven for all, unless he does an unforgivable deed. Then a Bedouin who had emigrated called out to him and said: O Messenger of God, or two? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Or two. Whenever Ibn Abbas narrated this hadith, he would say: By God, this is one of the strangest and most deceptive hadiths. Sixth: The index finger is the finger next to the thumb. In the pre-Islamic era, it was called the index finger because they used it to curse. When God brought Islam, they hated this name and called it the index finger because they used it to point to God in monotheism. It is also called swimming. It was named thus in the hadith of Wa’il bin Hajar and others, but the language followed what was known in the pre-Islamic era and it prevailed. It was narrated that the fingers of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were longer than the middle finger, then the middle finger was shorter than it, then the ring finger was shorter than the middle finger. Yazid bin Harun narrated: “Abdullah bin Yazid bin Muqsim al-Ta’ifi told us that my aunt Sarah bint Muqsim told me that she heard Maymunah bint Kurdam say: ‘I went out on a pilgrimage that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed, and I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on his mount, and my father asked him about some things. I saw myself amazed, as I was a girl, by the length of his finger next to the thumb over the rest of his fingers.’ So his, peace be upon him, saying: “He and I are like these two in Paradise,” and his saying in the other hadith: I, Abu Bakr and Umar will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection like this, and he pointed with his three fingers. He only wanted to mention the stations and the supervision over creation, so he said: We will be gathered like this and we will be supervised, and likewise the one who takes care of an orphan will have a high station. Whoever does not know the status of the fingers of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, interprets the hadith as meaning that they will be joined together and close to one another in a place of closeness. This is a far-fetched meaning, because the stations of the messengers, prophets, truthful ones, martyrs and righteous ones are different ranks and stations. Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: and the needy. The needy is also an appositive, meaning that We commanded them to be kind to the needy, who are those who have been afflicted by need and humiliated. This includes urging charity, sympathy, and checking on the conditions of the needy and weak. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “He who strives for the widow and the poor is like one who strives in the cause of God - and I think he said - and like one who stands in prayer without tiring and like one who fasts without breaking his fast.” Ibn al-Mundhir said: Tawus considered striving for sisters to be better than striving in the cause of God. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And speak to people in a good way. Hasan is an accusative of the verbal noun in the sense, because the meaning is to improve your speech. It was said that the meaning is: And speak to people a good word, so it is a verbal noun not in the sense. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read Hasan with the opening of the Ha’ and the Seen. Al-Akhfash said: They have the same meaning, like Bukhl and Bukhl, and Rushd and Rushd. Al-Akhfash narrated: Hasna without a tanween on Fa’la. Al-Nahhas said: This is not permissible in Arabic. Nothing of this is said except with the Alif and Lam, like Al-Fadhla and Al-Kubra and Al-Husna. This is the saying of Sibawayh. Isa bin Omar read Hasan with two dhammahs, like Al-Halm. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is: Say to them there is no god but God and command them to do so. Ibn Jurayj: Speak to people truthfully regarding the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and do not change his description. Sufyan Al-Thawri: Command them to do good and forbid them from evil. Abu Al-Aaliyah: Say good words to them, and deal with them in the best way you would like to deal with. All of this is an exhortation to good morals. A person should speak to people gently and have a cheerful face, with the righteous and the wicked, the Sunni and the innovator, without flattery and without speaking to him in a way that he thinks will please his school of thought, because God the Almighty said to Moses and Aaron: And speak to him with gentle speech. The speaker is not better than Moses and Aaron, and the wicked is not more evil than Pharaoh, and God the Almighty commanded them to be gentle with him. Talhah ibn Umar said: I said to Ata’ that you are a man who gathers people with different desires, and I am a man of sharpness, so I say some harsh words to them. He said: Do not do that! God the Almighty says: And speak to people kindly. This verse includes the Jews and Christians, so how about the Hanafi? It was narrated that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said to Aisha: Do not be obscene, for if obscenity were a man, he would be a bad man. It was said: By people he meant Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, as in his saying: Or do they envy people for what God has given them of His bounty? It is as if he said: Speak to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, in a good way. Al-Mahdawi narrated on the authority of Qatadah that his saying: And speak to people in a good way was abrogated by the verse of the sword. Abu Nasr Abd al-Raheem narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas said: This verse was revealed at the beginning, then the verse of the sword abrogated it. Ibn Atiyyah said: This indicates that this nation was addressed with similar wording at the beginning of Islam. As for the report about the Children of Israel and what they were commanded to do, there is no abrogation in it, and God knows best. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: And establish prayer and give zakat. This has been discussed above. The address is to the Children of Israel. Ibn Atiyyah said: Their zakat is what they used to pay, and the fire would descend on what was accepted, and it would not descend on what was not accepted, and it was not like the zakat of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: This needs to be transmitted, as it was proven in the spoils of war. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The zakat that they were commanded to give is obedience to God and sincerity. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: Then you turned away. The address is to the contemporaries of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He attributed to them the turning away of their ancestors, as they were on the same path in turning away from the truth as they were, as he said - a Shanshana I know from Akhzam - except a little like Abdullah bin Salam and his companions. A little is in the accusative case as an exception, and the excepted according to Sibawayh is in the accusative case because it is similar to the object in reality. The meaning is: I excepted a little: And you are turning away is the subject and predicate. Turning away and turning away have the same meaning, but they differ in wording. It was said: turning away is with the body, and turning away is with the heart. Al-Mahdawi said: And you are turning away is a state, because turning away indicates turning away.
2:84: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And when We took your covenant, which was previously discussed. Do not shed your blood, referring to the Children of Israel, and after them was included in the meaning. Do not shed your blood is like Do not worship in grammar. Talhah bin Musarraf and Shu’ayb bin Abi Hamzah read it with a damma on the fa’, which is a language, and Abu Nahik read it with a damma on the ta’, a shaddah on the fa’, and a fathah on the seen. Pouring means pouring, which was previously mentioned. And do not go out is conjoined. Yourselves: the soul is taken from the preciousness, so the soul of a person is the most noble thing in him. The house: is the home that contains the buildings of residence, unlike the home of a traveler. Al-Khalil said: Every place that a people inhabit is a house for them, even if there are no buildings in it. It was said: It was called a house because of its rotation around its inhabitants, just as a wall was called a wall because it encloses what it contains. You acknowledged is from acknowledgment, meaning with this covenant that was taken from you and your forefathers. And you bear witness from the testimony, meaning you are witnesses with your hearts to this. It was said: The testimony means attendance, meaning you are present to shed your blood and expel yourselves from your homes. Second: If it is said: Does anyone shed his blood and expel himself from his home? It is said to him: Since their religion was one and their command was one and they were among the nations like one person, killing one another and expelling one another was considered killing themselves and banishing themselves. It was said: What is meant is retaliation, meaning that no one is killed and killed in retaliation, as if he shed his blood. Likewise, he does not commit adultery or apostasy, as that makes blood permissible. Nor does he corrupt himself and be banished, as if he expelled himself from his home. This is an interpretation that is far-fetched, even if its meaning is correct. The matter was that God Almighty took a covenant from the Children of Israel in the Torah that they would not kill each other, nor exile each other, nor enslave each other, nor allow each other to steal, and other acts of obedience. I said: All of this is forbidden to us, and all of this has happened due to the tribulations among us. To God we belong and to Him we shall return! And in the revelation: Or He may confuse you into sects and make you taste the violence of one another. And it will come. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: It is possible that what is meant by it is the apparent meaning, that a person does not kill himself, nor leave his home foolishly, as the Indians kill themselves. Or a person kills himself from the hardship and calamity that befalls him, or wanders in the desert and does not take shelter in homes out of ignorance in his religion and foolishness in his patience, so it is general in all of that. And it has been narrated: “Uthman ibn Maz’un pledged allegiance with ten of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they resolved to wear hair-scarves, wander in the desert, not stay in houses, not eat meat, and not have intercourse with women. report of this reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he went to the house of Uthman ibn Maz’un but did not find him. He said to his wife: What is the hadith that I have heard from Uthman? She hated to divulge her husband’s secret and to lie about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: O Messenger of God, if something has reached you, then it is as it has reached you. He said: Tell Uthman, are you breaking my Sunnah or not following my religion? I pray and sleep, I fast and break my fast, I have intercourse with women, I stay in houses, and I eat meat. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me. So Uthman and his companions turned back from what they were doing.”
2:85: God Almighty said: “Then you are those who kill yourselves and expel a party of you from their homes, supporting each other against them in sin and aggression. And if they come to you as captives, you ransom them, although their expulsion was forbidden to you. Do you believe in part of the Scripture and disbelieve in part? Then what is the reward of those who do that among you except disgrace in worldly life, and on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned to the severest of punishment. And God is not unaware of what you do.”
2:86: The Almighty said: Then you are these You are in the nominative case as a subject, and it is not expressed, because it is implied. The taa' of you is damma because it was fatha if you addressed a single masculine, and kasra if you addressed a single feminine, so when it was dual or plural, nothing remained but the damma: these Al-Qutbi said: The meaning is O these. An-Nahhas said: This is a mistake according to Sibawayh, and this is not permissible. Az-Zajjaj said: These mean those. And you kill is included in the relative clause, meaning: then you are the ones who kill. It was said: These are nominative as a subject, and you are the predicate that comes before, and you kill is a state of these. It was said: These are accusative with the implication of I mean. Az-Zuhri read you kill with a damma on the taa' with emphasis, and likewise Why did you kill the prophets of God? This verse is addressed to those confronted and does not allow it to be attributed to the ancestors. It was revealed about Banu Qaynuqa, Qurayza and Nadir from the Jews. Banu Qaynuqa were enemies of Qurayza, and Aws were allies of Banu Qaynuqa, and Khazraj were allies of Banu Qurayza. Nadir, Aws and Khazraj were brothers, and Qurayza and Nadir were also brothers. Then they separated and would fight each other, and when war broke out they would ransom their prisoners. So God reproached them for that, saying: And if they come to you as captives, ransom them. The Almighty says: You cooperate. The meaning of you cooperate is that you cooperate. It is derived from the word back, because some of them strengthen others and thus become like a back to them. From this comes the poet’s saying: You pretended to be a teacher, you gathered around one person, you are still one century Sin: the act for which its doer deserves blame. Aggression: excessive injustice and transgression. The people of Medina and Mecca read tathaharoon with emphasis, assimilating the taa into the dhaal due to their proximity to it. The original form is tatathaharoon. The Kufians read tathaharoon with a lightened form, deleting the second taa because the first indicates it. The same applies to wa-in tathaharoon alayhi. Qatada read tathaharoon alayhi, and all of it goes back to the meaning of cooperation. From this: And the disbeliever is, against his Lord, a supporter. And His statement: And the angels after that are a supporter. So inform him. The Almighty said: And if they come to you as captives, ransom them, although it is forbidden for you to expel them. There are six issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: And if they come to you as captives is a condition, and its answer is tafawwadhum, and as-sara is an accusative case of state. Abu Ubaid said: Abu Amr used to say: Whatever is in their hands is the captives, and whatever comes as a prisoner is the prisoners. The linguists do not know what Abu Amr said, rather it is as you say: sakārī and sakārī. The group read as-sārī except for Hamzah, who read as-sara on fa’lā, the plural of asīr meaning captive, and the ḍab - in its breaking if that is the case - is fa’lā, as you say: qaṭil and qaṭilā, and jareekh and jareekhā. Abu Hatim said: as-sārī is not permissible. Al-Zajjaj said: as-sārī is said as-sārī, and fa’ālā is the original, and fa’ālā is included in it. It was narrated from Muhammad ibn Yazid, who said: as-sārī and isrā’ are said, like ẓarif and ẓarifā’. Ibn Faris said: it is said in the plural of asīr and as-sārī, and it was read with them. It was said: Asari with the opening of the hamza and it is not high. Second: The prisoner is derived from the word Isar, which is the rope with which the litter is tied. He was called Asir because it is tied tightly. The Arabs say: Qad Asrar Qutbah, meaning he tied it. Then every captured person was called Asir, even if he was not taken prisoner. Al-A’sha said: Poetry tied me to its house as captors tie donkeys. That is, I am in his house, meaning that he reached the end there. As for the family in the Almighty’s saying: And We strengthened their family, it refers to creation. A man’s family is his relatives, because he is strengthened by them. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Ransom them This is how Nafi’, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read it. The rest said: Tafdawhum from al-fidda. And al-fidda is the request for ransom for the prisoner in their hands. Al-Jawhari said: If the first letter of al-fidda is broken, it is lengthened or shortened, and if it is opened, it is shortened. It is said: Get up - my father ransomed you. Some Arabs break fida with tanween if it exceeds the lam of the jar specifically, so they say: fida lak, because it is indefinite and they mean by it the meaning of a supplication. Al-Asma’i recited for Al-Nabigha: Wait, may all people be sacrificed for you, and for the wealth and children you have produced. It is said: Fadaahu and Fadaahu if he gave his ransom and saved him. He ransomed him with his soul, and Fadaahu yafdihi if he said I made you my ransom. And they ransomed each other, meaning they ransomed each other. Ransom, redemption and redemption all have the same meaning. And Fadaatu nafsi if you release it after paying something, meaning I ransomed, and from this is the saying of Al-Abbas to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I ransomed myself and ransomed Aqil. They are two verbs that take two objects, the second of them with a preposition. You say: I ransomed myself with my money and I ransomed him with my money. The poet said: Stand up, redeemer of your prisoner. My people and yours, I do not see any meeting between them. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying, And it is forbidden for you to expel them. is the subject and a metaphor for expulsion, and forbidden is its predicate, and expelling them is a substitute for he, or if you wish, it is a metaphor for the conversation and story, and the sentence that follows it is its predicate, meaning, and it is forbidden for you to expel them. So expelling them is a second subject, and forbidden is its predicate, and the sentence is the predicate of he, and in forbidden is a pronoun whose agent is not named, Jews, which takes the place of the predicate of forbidden, and the sentence is the predicate of he. Al-Farra’ claimed that he is an imaad, but according to the Basrans, this is a meaningless mistake, because he is not at the beginning of a sentence. It is read he with a silent ha because of the weight of the damma, as the poet said: His throw does not increase his wealth nor does it increase his number. Likewise, if you use the letter lam and thumma, as has been mentioned previously. Our scholars said: God Almighty had taken four covenants from them: to refrain from killing, to refrain from expelling, to refrain from demonstrating, and to ransom their prisoners. But they turned away from everything they were commanded to do except ransom. So God rebuked them for that with a rebuke that is recited, saying: Do you then believe in part of the Scripture? which is the Torah, and disbelieve in part? I said: By God, we have turned away from everyone with the tribulations, so some of us have supported each other, whether it is against the Muslims or against the infidels, until we have left our brothers humiliated and subdued, and the rule of the polytheists applies to them. There is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Almighty. Our scholars said: The ransom of the captives is obligatory even if not a single dirham remains. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: The verse includes the obligation to free the captives, and the reports from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he freed the captives and ordered their release, and this is the practice of the Muslims and there is consensus on it. The release of the captives must be from the public treasury, and if it is not, then it is an obligation on all Muslims, and whoever among them does it, the obligation is dropped from the rest, and this will come. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: So what is the reward for he who does that among you except disgrace in the life of this world? Subject and predicate. Disgrace is humiliation. Al-Jawhari said: Khaza with a kasra means to be humiliated and disgraced. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: He fell into a calamity. And God disgraced him. Khaza also means to be ashamed, so he is Khazayyan. A people are Khazayyan and a woman is Khazayyan. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And on the Day of Resurrection they will be returned. The general reading is they will be returned with the letter ya, while Al-Hasan read they will be returned with the letter ta as a direct address. “To the most severe punishment. And God is not unaware of what you do.” This was previously discussed, as well as: Those are the ones who purchased the verse, so there is no meaning to the repetition. Day is governed by they will be returned.
2:87: The Almighty said: And We gave Moses the Scripture meaning the Torah. And We followed means We followed. Following means following and riding behind, taken from following the nape of the neck, which is the back of the neck. You say I followed him if you came from behind him, and the rhyme of poetry is named from it, because it follows the rest of the speech. The rhyme is the nape, and from it the hadith: The devil ties a knot at the back of your head. Al-Qafi and Al-Qafwa: as milk and other things are saved for someone you want to honor. Qafwat a man: I accused him of immorality. So-and-so Qafoni means I accused him. Qafwati means I chose him. Ibn Duraid said: Ibn Duraid said: It is as if it is one of the opposites. The scholars said: This verse is like the saying of God the Almighty: Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every messenger who came after Moses came to confirm the Torah and command its adherence until Jesus, peace be upon him. It is said: Rusul and Rusul are two languages, the first is the language of Hijaz, and the second is the language of Tamim, and whether it is with an addition or not. And Abu Amr used to lighten it if he added to two letters, and make it heavy if he added to one letter. The Almighty said: And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs, meaning the arguments and evidence, which are what God mentioned in Al Imran and Al Ma’idah. Ibn Abbas said: And We strengthened him, meaning We strengthened him. Mujahid and Ibn Muhaisin read We strengthened him with a long vowel, and they are two dialects. With the Holy Spirit, Abu Malik and Abu Salih narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Muammar on the authority of Qatada, who said: Gabriel, peace be upon him. Hassan said: Gabriel is the Messenger of God among us, and the Holy Spirit is not hidden. An-Nahhas said: Gabriel was called a spirit and was added to the Holy One, because he was created by God Almighty as a spirit without the birth of his son’s father, and Jesus was also called a spirit for this reason. Ghalib bin Abdullah narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The Holy One is God Almighty. And Al-Hasan said the same: The Holy One is God, and His spirit is Gabriel. Abu Rawq narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas: By the Holy Spirit, he said: It is the name by which Jesus revived the dead, and Saeed bin Jubair and Ubaid bin Umair said the same, and it is the greatest name of God. And it was said: What is meant is the Gospel, and He called it a spirit just as God called the Qur’an a spirit in His statement, the Most High: And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command. And the first is more apparent, and God Almighty knows best. The Almighty said: So, whenever there came to you a Messenger with what your souls did not desire, meaning, what did not agree with them and suit them, and the ha was deleted due to the length of the name, meaning, what you did not desire, you were arrogant about answering him, despising the messengers and rejecting the message. The origin of hawa is the inclination toward something, and the plural of ahwa is ahwa, as it came in the revelation, and the plural of ahwa is not ahwa, although they said in nada “andiya,” as the poet said: On a night in Jumada al-Adan, in whose darkness the dog cannot see the trumpet. Al-Jawhari said: It is anomalous. Desire was called desire because it causes its owner to fall into the Fire. Therefore, it is usually only used in what is not right and in what is not good, and this verse is one of those. It may also be used in what is right, and from that is the saying of Umar, may God be pleased with him, about the prisoners of Badr: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, liked what Abu Bakr said and did not like what I said. Aisha said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the authentic hadith: By God, I see that your Lord hastens to fulfill your desires. Narrated by Muslim. The Almighty said: A group you denied. A group is governed by you denied, and likewise and a group you kill. Among those they denied were Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, and among those they killed were John and Zachariah, peace be upon them, as will be explained in Subhan, God willing.
2:88: God Almighty said: And they said, ‘Our hearts are covered.’ Rather, God has cursed them for their disbelief, so little do they believe. God the Almighty said: And they said meaning the Jews Our hearts are covered with a sukoon on the lam, the plural of aghlaf, meaning they have coverings. It is like His statement Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us meaning in vessels. Mujahid said: Ghalaf has a covering over it. Ikrimah said: It has a seal over it. The linguists said that ghalfat means to sheathe the sword, so the heart is aghlaf, meaning concealed from understanding and discrimination. Ibn Abbas, Al-A’raj and Ibn Muhaysin read ghalaf with a damma on the lam. Ibn Abbas said: meaning our hearts are filled with knowledge and do not need the knowledge of Muhammad (peace be upon him) or anyone else. It was said: it is the plural of ghalaf, like khimar and khamr, meaning our hearts are vessels for knowledge, so why do they not understand from you when we have comprehended so much knowledge? It was said: the meaning is how can the knowledge of Muhammad (peace be upon him) be hidden from them. God responded to them by saying: Rather, God has cursed them for their disbelief, so little do they believe. Then He explained that the reason for their aversion to faith is that they were cursed for their previous disbelief and audacity, and this is the punishment for a sin that is greater than it. The origin of the word curse in the speech of the Arabs is expulsion and banishment. The wolf is called la’een accursed, and the banished man is called la’een accursed. Al-Shamakh said: The quail was terrified by him and I denied him the status of a wolf like a cursed man The point of the speech: The status of the cursed wolf is like that of a man, so the meaning is that God has distanced them from His mercy. It was said: From His success and guidance. It was said: From all good, and this is general. So little is an adjective for a deleted source, the meaning of which is: So little faith they believe. Muammar said: The meaning is that they do not believe except a little of what is in their hands and they disbelieve in most of it, and little is the accusative by removing the letter of description. And what is a relative clause, meaning they believe little. Al-Waqidi said: Its meaning is they do not believe little or much, as you say: How little he does such-and-such, meaning he does not do it at all. Al-Kisa’i said: The Arabs say we passed by a land that rarely grows leeks and onions, meaning it does not grow anything.
2:89: The Almighty said: And when there came to them meaning the Jews. A Book meaning the Qur'an. From God confirming is an attribute of the Book. It is permissible in other than the Qur'an to put it in the accusative case as a state, and that is in the Mushaf of Abi in the accusative case as narrated. When they had with them meaning the Torah and the Gospel informing them of what was in them. And before that they used to ask for victory meaning they used to seek help. And asking for help is seeking help. I asked for help: I asked for help. And in the hadith: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek victory through the vagabonds of the emigrants, i.e., he sought victory through their supplications and prayers.” And from this is Perhaps God will bring victory or a command from Him. Victory means opening something that is closed, so it goes back to their saying I opened the door. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn Abi Waqqas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has given victory to this nation through its weak ones, through their supplications, prayers, and sincerity. Al-Nisa’i also narrated on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Seek me the weak, for you are provided for and aided only by your weak ones. Ibn Abbas said: The Jews of Khaybar were fighting Ghadhfan, and when they met, the Jews were defeated. The Jews returned with this supplication and said: We ask you by the right of the unlettered Prophet whom you promised us to bring forth for us at the end of time, to grant us aid against them. He said: So whenever they met, they supplicated with this supplication, and Ghadhfan were defeated. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent, they disbelieved, so God revealed: And before, they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved meaning, through you, O Muhammad, until His saying: So the curse of God is upon the disbelievers. The Almighty’s saying: And when there came to them is an answer to lama when they and what follows it in His saying: And when there came to them they did not recognize according to Al-Farra’, and the answer to the second lama is they disbelieved. Al-Akhfash Saeed said: The answer to lama is omitted because the listener knows, and Al-Zajjaj said the same. Al-Mubarrad said: It is an answer to lama in His saying: they disbelieved, and the second lama was repeated because of the length of the speech. This indicates confirmation of the sin and emphasis on it.
2:90: The Almighty said: What an evil thing they have purchased. In the speech of the Arabs, Ba'sa is a complete expression of blame, just as Na'am is a complete expression of praise. And in each of them there are four languages: Ba'sa, Ba'sa, Ba'sa, Na'am, Na'am, Na'am, and the doctrine of Sibawayh is that ma is the agent of Ba'sa, and it is only used with generic and indefinite nouns. And so is Na'am, so you say Na'am al-rajul Zayd, and Na'am rajul Zayd, so if it is accompanied by a noun without an alif and lam, it is always in the accusative case, but if it has an alif and la, it is always in the nominative case. And rajul is in the accusative case as a distinguishing feature. And in Na'am there is an implied word according to the condition of interpretation, and Zayd is in the nominative case in two ways: as a predicate of a deleted subject, as if it was said: Who is the one being praised? I said: He is Zayd, and the other as a subject and what precedes it is its predicate. Abu Ali permitted it to be followed by a relative or non-relative ma, as long as it is vague and applies to a large number and is not specific to one person in particular. The meaning according to Sibawayh is: Basah al-shay’ bih ath-thaqqahu yu-kaffaru. “An-an-yakfaru” is in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is in what precedes it, like your saying: Basah al-rajul Zayd, and ma according to this statement is a relative pronoun. Al-Akhfash said: Ma is in the accusative case as a specification, like your saying: Basah al-rajul Zayd, so the meaning is: Basah al-shay’an ath-thaqqahu yu-kaffaru. So Bah-a-rajul yu-kaffaru according to this statement is an attribute of ma. Al-Farra’ said: Basahma as a whole is one thing, like hubbatha. And in this statement there is an objection, because it remains a verb without a subject. Al-Kisa’i said: Ma and ibtiratu are like one noun that stands on its own, and the meaning is: Basah al-shay’u yu-kaffaru. This is rejected, because na’am and ba’as do not enter upon a specific definite noun, and buying has been identified by adding it to the pronoun. An-Nahhas said: The clearest of these sayings is the saying of Al-Akhfash and Sibawayh. Al-Farra’ and Al-Kisa’i said: That they disbelieve, if you wish, the an is in the accusative case in response to the ha in bih. Al-Farra’ said: That is, they bought themselves by disbelieving in what God has revealed. So bought means sold and purchased, and the meaning is: What a bad thing they have chosen for themselves, since they have exchanged falsehood for truth and disbelief for faith. God the Almighty said: Baghyan means envy, as Qatada and As-Suddi said, and it is an object of the verb for which, and in reality it is a verbal noun. Al-Asma’i: It is taken from their saying that the wound has become corrupted. It was said: Its origin is the request, and that is why the adulteress was called Baghyan. That God may send down is in the accusative case, meaning that He may send down, meaning for the sake of God sending down favor upon His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ya’qub, and Ibn Muhaisin read that He may send down in a lightened form, and so is the rest of what is in the Qur’an, except for and what We send down in Al-Hijr, and in Al-An’am that He may send down a verse. God the Almighty said: So they returned meaning they returned, and this is what is said most of the time about evil, and it has been mentioned before. With wrath upon wrath has been mentioned before, meaning God’s wrath upon them, which is His punishment. It was said: The first wrath was for their worship of the calf, and the second was for their disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was said by Ibn Abbas. Ikrimah said: Because they disbelieved in Jesus and then disbelieved in Muhammad, meaning the Jews. Saeed narrated on the authority of Qatadah: The first was for their disbelief in the Gospel, and the second was for their disbelief in the Qur’an. Some people said: Support and severity of the situation upon them, not that He meant two wraths caused by two sins. Humiliating is taken from humiliation, which is what necessitates eternal residence in Hell, unlike the eternal residence of the disobedient Muslims, for that is a test and purification for them, like stoning the adulterer and cutting off the hand of the thief, as will be explained in Surat An-Nisa’ from the hadith of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, God willing.
2:91: God Almighty says: “And when it is said to them, ‘Believe in what God has revealed,’ they say, ‘We believe in what was revealed to us,’ and they disbelieve in what came after it, although it is the truth confirming what is with them. Say, ‘Then why did you kill God’s prophets before, if you were believers?’” God the Almighty said: “And when it is said to them, ‘Believe’ meaning, believe ‘in what God has revealed’ meaning the Qur’an, ‘they say, ‘We believe’ meaning, we believe ‘in what was revealed to us’ meaning the Torah. ‘And they disbelieve in what is beyond it’ meaning other than it, according to al-Farra’ and Qatada: in what is beyond it, and this is the saying of Abu Ubaidah, and the meaning is the same. Al-Jawhari said: ‘Behind’ means behind, and it may mean in front.’ It is one of the opposites. God the Almighty said: ‘And behind them was a king’ meaning in front of them, and its diminutive is ‘Waray’ah’ with a ‘ha’ and it is irregular. ‘Wara’ah’ is in the accusative case as an adverb. Al-Akhfash said: It is said, ‘I met him from behind’, so you raise it to the extreme if it is not an adjective, making it a noun when it is not established, like you say, ‘from before’ and ‘from after’, and he recited: If I did not believe in you and I did not meet you except from behind behind I said: And from it is the saying of Abraham, peace be upon him, in the hadith of intercession: I was only a friend from behind behind. Behind behind: also the son's son. The Almighty’s saying: “And it is the truth” is subject and predicate. Confirming is a confirmatory state according to Sibawayh. When they are with them is in the accusative case with the preposition lam, and with them is its relative clause, and with them is in the accusative case with stability, and whoever old made it a letter. God the Almighty said: “Say: Why then did you kill the prophets of God before?” This is a response from God the Almighty to them in their saying that they believed in what was revealed to them, and a denial and rebuke from Him. The meaning is: How did you kill when you were forbidden to do so? The address is to those who were present with Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and what is meant is their ancestors. The address is to their children, and because they were the guardians of those who were killed, as He said: And if they had believed in God and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. So if they took them as allies, then they are in their position. It was said: Because they were pleased with their action, so it was attributed to them. And the word you kill came in the future tense, which means the past tense, when the ambiguity was removed by His saying: before. If there is no ambiguity, then it is permissible for the past tense to mean the future, and the future tense to mean the past.
