Al-Hutay’ah said: Al-Hutaiah will testify on the day he meets his Lord that Al-Walid is more deserving of an apology. Shahada means testify. If you are believers meaning if you are believing in faith then why did you accept the killing of the prophets? It was said that in means what, and the root of lam is lam, the alif was deleted to differentiate between the question and the report, and it should not be stopped on because if it is stopped on without a ha’ it would be a mistake, and if it is stopped on with a ha’ it will be increased in blackness.
2:92: The Almighty said: And Moses came to you with clear signs. The lam is the lam of the oath. And the clear signs are the Almighty's saying: And We gave Moses nine clear signs. They are the staff, the years, the hand, the blood, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the splitting of the sea. It was said: The clear signs are the Torah and what it contains of evidence. The Almighty’s saying: Then you took the calf is a rebuke, and then is more eloquent than and in rebuke, meaning after looking at the verses and bringing them, you took. This indicates that they only did that after a period of time to look at the verses, and that is greater than their crime.
2:93: The Almighty said: And when We took your covenant and raised the Mount above you, [saying], 'Take what We have given you with strength and listen.' We have already discussed this. The meaning of listen is obey. It does not mean the command to understand the statement only, but rather what is meant is to act upon what you have heard and adhere to it. From this is their saying: God hears whoever praises Him, meaning He accepts and responds. He said: I called upon God until I was afraid that God might not hear what I was saying. That is, he accepts. The rajaz poet said: Hearing, obedience and submission are better and more beneficial for Banu Tamim. They said, We heard. There is disagreement as to whether this expression actually came from them verbally, or whether they did an action that took the place of speech, in which case it would be a metaphor, as he said: The basin was filled and my cotton said, Slow down, you have filled my stomach. This is an argument against them in their saying: We believe in what was revealed to us. The Almighty said: And they made the calf drink into their hearts. That is, the love of the calf. The meaning is: their hearts were made to drink it. This is a simile and metaphor expressing the fact that the matter of the calf was firmly established in their hearts. In the hadith: “Trials are presented to the hearts like a mat, stick by stick. So whichever heart absorbs them, a black dot will be placed on it.” Hadith, narrated by Muslim. It is said that his heart is imbued with the love of such-and-such. Zuhair said: I woke up from it after an inner love, and love is what your heart drinks as a disease The love of the calf was expressed by drinking rather than eating, because drinking water penetrates the organs until it reaches their interior, while food passes them and does not penetrate them. One of the followers added to this meaning and said about his wife Uthma, who he had rebuked for some matter and divorced her, and he loved her: Othma's love has penetrated my heart, so his desert walks with the hidden He penetrated where no drink, no sorrow, and no joy reached. When I remember the covenant, I almost fly, if only a human could fly. Al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj said: Moses, peace be upon him, cooled the calf and scattered it in the water, and said to the Children of Israel: Drink from that water. So they all drank, and whoever loved the calf, gold filings came out on his lips. It was narrated that no one drank it except that he went crazy, as narrated by Al-Qushayri. I said: As for scattering it in the sea, this is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: Then We will scatter it into the sea as a blast. As for drinking the water and the appearance of the coolness on the healing, this is refuted by the Almighty’s saying: And they drank into their hearts the calf. And God Almighty knows best. God Almighty says: “Say: ‘Evil is that which your faith enjoins upon you.’” That is, your faith which you claimed in your saying: We believe in what was revealed to us. It was said that this statement is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was commanded to rebuke them, that is, say to them, O Muhammad: Evil are these things which you have done and which your faith enjoins upon you. We have already discussed evil and praise be to God alone.
2:94: God Almighty says: “Say: If the home of the Hereafter with God is exclusively yours, to the exclusion of all other people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful.”
2:95: When the Jews made false claims, God Almighty narrated them in His Book, such as His saying: And they said, ‘The Fire will not touch us except for a few days,’ and His saying: And they said, ‘None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian,’ and they said: We are the children of God and His beloved. God the Almighty denied them and made them face the proof, saying: Say to them, O Muhammad: If the home of the Hereafter is yours, meaning Paradise, then wish for death, if you are truthful, in your statements, because whoever believes that he is from the people of Paradise, death is more beloved to him than life in this world, because of the bliss of Paradise that he will attain, and the harm of this world will be removed from him. So they refrained from wishing for that out of fear of God for the ugliness of their deeds and their knowledge of their disbelief in their saying: We are the children of God and His beloved, and their eagerness for this world. For this reason, God the Almighty said, informing us with His true statement: “And they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have put forth. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers,” confirming their lie. Also, if they wished for death, they would die, as was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If the Jews had wished for death, they would have died and seen their place in Hellfire. It was said that God prevented them from expressing their wish and limited them to holding back so that He would make that a sign for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So these are three aspects of their abandoning their wish. Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, and they wished for death, that what was meant was that they claimed death for the more lying of the two groups, from us and from you, but they did not pray because they knew of their lie. If it is said: Wishing is sometimes done with the tongue and sometimes with the heart, so how do we know that they did not wish it in their hearts? It is said to him: The Qur’an speaks about that in its saying: And they will never wish it. If they had wished it in their hearts, they would have expressed it with their tongues in response to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to invalidate his argument, and this is clear. The Almighty said: Purely is in the accusative case as a predicate of was, and if you wish, it is a state, and it is with God in the position of the predicate. Forever is a time adverb that applies to little and much, like now and time, and here it is from the beginning of life to death. Ma in his saying by what means who, and the pronoun is omitted, and the estimation is that you brought it forward, and it is a source and does not need a pronoun. And their hands is in the position of raising, the damma was omitted from the ya’ because of its heaviness with the kasra, even though it is in the position of the accusative of its movement, because the accusative is light, and it is permissible to make it sukoon in poetry. And God is Knowing of the wrongdoers is a subject and predicate.
2:96: The Almighty said: And you will find them the most greedy of people for life meaning the Jews. And more greedy than those who associate others with God It was said: The meaning is and more greedy, so and more greedy than those who associate others with God was omitted because of their knowledge of their sins and that there is no good for them with God, and the polytheists of the Arabs do not know anything but this life and have no knowledge of the Hereafter. Do you not see the saying of their poet: Enjoy the world, for you will perish from the pleasures and beautiful women. The pronoun in one of them in this statement refers to the Jews. It was said that the speech was about life, then the story was resumed about a group of polytheists. It was said that they are the Magians, and that is clear in their supplications for someone who sneezes in their languages, which means live a thousand years. The thousand was mentioned specifically because it is the end of the decade in the calculation. Al-Hasan believed that those who associated others with God are the polytheists of the Arabs, and they were singled out for that because they do not believe in resurrection, and they wish for a long life. The root of sannah is sanah. It was said that it is sanwah. It was said that there is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is that you will find them and a group of those who associated others with God the most eager for life. The Almighty said: One of them would wish that he could live a thousand years. The root of yud is yuddud and it was assimilated so as not to combine two letters of the same type with vowels, and the vowel of the dal was changed to the waw, to indicate that he does something. Al-Kisa’i narrated: I wished, so according to this it is permissible to say yudd with a kasra on the waw. The meaning of yudd is: to wish. The Almighty said: And it will not remove him from the punishment that he should live long. Grammarians differed about he. Some said: It is the pronoun of the one who preceded, the meaning is that one of them will not be removed, and the predicate of the beginning is in the accusative. That he should live long is the subject of muhazzah. A group said: It is the pronoun of al-ta’mir, and the meaning is al-ta’mir will not be removed, and the predicate is in the accusative, that he should live long is a substitute for al-ta’mir according to this statement. Al-Tabari narrated from a group that they said: It is a pillar. I said: There is some distance in it, because the right of the pillar is to be between two related things, like his saying: If this is the truth, and his saying: But they were the wrongdoers, and the like. It was said: Ma is a Hijazi verb, and it is its name, and the predicate is in bi-muzahzahu. A group said: It is the pronoun of the matter and the affair. Ibn Atiyyah: There is some distance in it, because what is preserved from grammarians is that it is interpreted by a sentence free of a preposition. And his saying: bi-muzahzahu, zahatha means distancing and moving away. It is said: I moved him away, meaning I distanced him, so he moved away, meaning he moved away and distanced himself. It can be intransitive and transitive. The poet said about the aggressor: O Taker of the soul from a dying soul and Forgiver of sin, save me from the Fire. And Dhu al-Rummah recited: O He who takes the soul from a body that has disobeyed for a long time and forgives sins, save me from the Fire. Another said in the necessary: My friend, why does the darkness not move and why does the light of dawn not become clear? Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever fasts one day for the sake of God, God will remove his face from the Fire for a distance of seventy years. God the Almighty said: And God is Seeing of what they do. That is, what these people do, one of whom would like to live a thousand years. Whoever reads it with the letter ta’, then the meaning is: Say to them, O Muhammad: God is Seeing of what you do. The scholars said: God the Almighty described Himself as Seeing in the sense that He is All-Knowing of the hidden aspects of things. And the All-Knowing in the speech of the Arabs is the one who knows something and is an expert in it. From this is their saying: So-and-so is All-Knowing in medicine, and All-Knowing in jurisprudence, and All-Knowing in meeting men. He said: If you ask me about women, I am a doctor who specializes in women’s diseases. Al-Khattabi said: Al-Basir is the All-Knowing, and Al-Basir is the One who sees. It was said: God Almighty described Himself as Al-Basir in the sense of making visible things with sight, meaning perceiving visible things through what He created for them of perceiving tools and power. So God is Al-Basir of His servants, meaning He makes His servants sighted.
2:97: God Almighty said: Say, ‘Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - it is he who has brought it down to your heart by permission of God, confirming what was before it and as guidance and good tidings for the believers.’ The reason for its revelation is that the Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is no prophet among the prophets except that an angel from the angels comes to him from his Lord with the message and revelation, so who is your companion so that we may follow you? He said: Gabriel. They said: That is the one who descends with war and fighting, that is our enemy! If you had said: Michael who descends with rain and mercy, we would have followed you. So God revealed the verse until His saying: for the disbelievers. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. And the Almighty’s statement: For He has sent it down upon your heart The pronoun in for has two possible meanings. The first is that God sent Gabriel down upon your heart. The second is that Gabriel sent down the Qur’an to your heart. And the heart was specifically mentioned because it is the seat of reason, knowledge, and the reception of knowledge. The verse indicates the honor of Gabriel, peace be upon him, and condemns its enmity. And the Almighty’s statement: By God’s permission means by His will and knowledge. Confirming what was before it means the Torah. Guidance and good tidings for the believers Its meaning has been presented, and praise be to God.
2:98: The Almighty's saying: Whoever is an enemy to God is a condition, and its answer is Indeed, God is an enemy to the disbelievers. This is a threat and a condemnation of the enemies of Gabriel, peace be upon him, and a declaration that the enmity of some necessitates God's enmity towards them. The servant's enmity towards God is disobeying Him and avoiding His obedience, and the enmity towards His friends, and God's enmity towards the servant is to punish him and show the effect of enmity upon him. If it is said: Why did God single out Gabriel and Michael for mention even though He mentioned the angels in general? It is said: He singled them out for mention to honor them, as He said: In them are fruits, palm trees, and pomegranates. It is said: They were singled out because the Jews mentioned them, and the verse was revealed because of them, so mentioning them was obligatory so that the Jews would not say: We did not oppose God and all of His angels. So God, the Most High, mentioned them specifically to invalidate what they interpreted as specificity. Linguists have different meanings for Gabriel and Michael, peace be upon them. As for the one about Gabriel, there are ten: The first: Gabriel, which is the language of the people of Hijaz. Hassan bin Thabit said: Gabriel is the Messenger of God among us The second: Gabriel with an open jim and this is the reading of Al-Hasan and Ibn Kathir. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Kathir that he said: I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a dream and he was reading: Gabriel and Michael, and I will never stop reading them like this. The third: Gabriel with a ya’ after the hamza, like Gabriel, as the people of Kufa read and chanted: We witnessed that no battalion was presented to us throughout the ages except that Gabriel was in front of it. It is the language of Tamim and Qais. Fourth: Gabriel on the same weight as Gabriel is shortened, and this is the reading of Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim. The fifth is similar, and it is the reading of Yahya bin Ya`mar, except that he stressed the lam. Sixth: Gabriel with an alif after the ra’ then a hamza, and this is how Ikrimah read it. Sixth: The same, except that after the hamza there is a ya. The eighth is Gabriel with two Ya’s without a hamza, and this is how Al-A’mash and Yahya bin Ya’mar also read it. Ninth: Jibra’een with an open jim with a broken hamza followed by a ya and a noon. Tenth: Jibreen with a kasra on the jim and a sukoon on the yaa with a noon without a hamza, and it is the language of Banu Asad. Al-Tabari said: It was not recited with it. Al-Nahhas said - and mentioned the recitation of Ibn Kathir - Fa'leel is not known in the speech of the Arabs, and it has Fa'leel, such as Dahliz, Qatmeer, and Bartil. It is not denied that there is in the speech of the non-Arabs what has no equivalent in the speech of the Arabs, and it is not denied that it changes frequently, as they said: Ibrahim, Ibraheem, Ibraheem, and Ibrahim. Someone else said: Jibreel is a foreign name that the Arabs Arabized, so these languages have it and that is why it is not declined. I said: It was mentioned at the beginning of the book that the correct wording of these words is Arabic, revealed by Gabriel in clear Arabic. An-Nahhas said: The plural of Gabriel is broken into Jabaril. As for the languages in Michael Fest: The first: Mika’il, Nafi’s reading. Mika’il with a ya’ after the hamza is Hamza’s reading. Mika’il, the language of the people of Hijaz, and it is the reading of Abu Amr and Hafs on the authority of Asim. The three versions were narrated on the authority of Ibn Kathir. Ka’b ibn Malik said: And on the day of Badr, we met you, and Michael and Gabriel were our support for victory. Another said: They worshipped the cross, lied about Muhammad, about Gabriel, and about Michael. Fourth: Michael, like Michael. This is the reading of Ibn Muhaisin. Fifth: Michael with two yaas, which is the reading of Al-A’mash, but it differs from him. Sixth: Michael, which is said Isra’il with an open hamza, and it is a foreign name, so it is not declined. Ibn Abbas mentioned that Jabr, Mika, and Israf are all in foreign languages meaning: slave and owned. And El: is the name of God Almighty, and from it is the saying of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, when he heard the rhyme of Musaylimah: This is speech that did not come from El. And in the revelation They do not observe towards a believer any pact or covenant in one of the two interpretations, and it will come. Al-Mawardi said: Gabriel and Michael are two names, one of them is Abdullah and the other is Ubaid God, because El is God Almighty, and Jabr is Abd and Mika is Ubaid, so it is as if Gabriel is Abdullah and Michael is Ubaid God. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas, and there is no one who disagrees with him among the commentators. I said: Some commentators added: And Israfil is the servant of the Most Gracious. An-Nahhas said: Whoever interprets the hadith as Jabr, the servant of God, must say: This is Gabriel, and I saw Gabriel, and I passed by Gabriel, and this is not said, so the meaning of the hadith must be that it is named with this. Another said: If it were as they said, it would have been declined, so leaving the decline indicates that it is a single, singular noun, not an adjective. Abdul Ghani Al-Hafiz narrated from the hadith of Aflat bin Khalifa - who is Falit Al-Amiri, who is Abu Hassan - on the authority of Jasra bint Dajajah on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, Lord of Gabriel, Michael and Israfil, I seek refuge in You from the heat of the Fire and the torment of the grave.
2:99: God Almighty says: And We have certainly sent down to you clear verses, and none disbelieve in them except the defiantly disobedient. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: This is an answer to Ibn Suriya when he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, you have not brought us anything that we recognize, and what clear sign has been revealed to you that we may follow you with? So God revealed this verse, as mentioned by Al-Tabari.
2:100: The Almighty said: Or every time they make a covenant, He throws it away. The waw is the waw of conjunction, and the alif of interrogation is added to it just as it is added to the fa' in his saying: Then did you judge the time of ignorance?, Can you then make the deaf hear?, Do you then take him and his descendants? And on then like his saying: Athman if he occurs. This is the saying of Sibawayh. Al-Akhfash said: The waw is redundant. Al-Kisa'i's school of thought is that it is or, the waw was moved from it for ease. Some people read it or, with the waw silent, so it comes with the meaning of but, as the speaker says: I will strike you, and the respondent says: Or is God sufficient? Ibn Atiyyah said: All of this is forced, and the correct saying of Sibawayh. Every time it is accusative as an adverb, and the meaning in the verse is Malik bin al-Saif, and it is said about him Ibn al-Dayf, he had said: By God, we did not take a covenant from our book to believe in Muhammad nor a pact, so the verse was revealed. It was said that the Jews made a covenant that if Muhammad came out, they would believe in him and be with him against the polytheists of the Arabs. But when he was sent, they disbelieved in him. Ata’ said: These are the covenants that were between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Jews, but they broke them, as did the Qurayza and Nadir. The evidence for this is the statement of God Almighty: Those among them with whom you made a covenant, but they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear God. The Almighty said: A party of them cast it aside. Casting away means throwing away and discarding, and from this comes wine and the castaway. Abu Al-Aswad said: And tell me from whom you sent it, but you took my book to an exhibition in your north. I looked at his address and threw it away as I would throw away a worn-out sandal from yours. last: Those whom you commanded to be just have rejected your Book and made lawful what is forbidden. This is a proverb used for someone who is too busy with something to do anything about it. The Arabs say: Put this behind your back, behind you, and under your foot, meaning leave it and turn away from it. God Almighty said: And you have taken it behind you as a back. Al-Farra’ recited: Tamim bin Zaid: Do not let my need be in the back, lest I become tired of answering it. But most of them is the beginning. They do not believe is a future verb in the position of the predicate.
2:101: The Almighty's saying, And when there came to them a Messenger from God, confirming what was with them, is an attribute of the Messenger, and it is permissible to use it in the accusative case as a state. A group threw away is the answer to when. "Of those who were given the Scripture, the Book of God is in the accusative case with throw away," and what is meant is the Torah, because their disbelief in the Prophet, peace be upon him, and their denial of him is a throwing away of it. Al-Suddi said: They threw away the Torah and took the Book of Asif, and the magic of Harut and Marut. It was said: It is permissible to mean the Qur'an. Al-Sha'bi said: It is in their hands and they read it, but they threw away acting upon it. Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: They wrapped it in silk and brocade, and adorned it with gold and silver, and they did not make permissible what it made permissible nor forbid what it made forbidden, so that is throwing away. Its explanation has been presented in full. "As if they do not know" is a simile for those who do not know, since they acted like the ignorant, so it comes from the wording that they disbelieved knowingly.
2:102: It contains twenty-four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And they followed what the devils had recited during the reign of Solomon. This is a statement from God the Almighty about the group who rejected the Book that they also followed magic, and they are the Jews. Al-Suddi said: The Jews opposed Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the Torah, and the Torah and the Qur’an agreed, so they rejected the Torah and took the Book of Asif and the magic of Harut and Marut. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned Solomon among the messengers, some of their rabbis said: Muhammad claims that the son of David was a prophet! By God, he was nothing but a magician, so God the Almighty revealed: And Solomon did not disbelieve, but the devils disbelieved. That is, they conveyed to the children of Adam that what Solomon did of riding the sea and subjugating the birds and devils was magic. Al-Kalbi said: The devils wrote magic and magic spells on the tongue of Asaf, the scribe of Solomon, and buried him under his prayer rug so that God would take away his kingdom without Solomon noticing. When Solomon died, they took him out and said to the al-Nas 114:This is your kingdom, so learn it. As for the scholars of the Children of Israel, they said: God forbid that this is the knowledge of Solomon! As for the lowly ones, they said: This is the knowledge of Solomon, and they accepted his teaching and rejected the books of their prophets until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then God Almighty revealed to His Prophet the excuse of Solomon and they declared his innocence of what he was accused of, so He said: And they followed what the devils recited. Ata’ said: Recite is read from recitation. Ibn Abbas said: Recite is follow, as you say: The people came following one another. Al-Tabari said: They followed and went astray. I said: Because whoever follows something and makes it his priority has preferred it over something else. The meaning of taltala means talaqat, so it means to proceed. The poet said: If you pass by his grave, bury the camels in the ground, with every limb swimming. And sprinkle the sides of his grave with her blood, for he may be a brother of blood and sacrifices. Meaning: It was. And it was the object of the verb they followed, meaning they followed what the devils said about Solomon and his recitation. It was said: What is negated, and it is nothing, neither in the system of speech nor in its correctness, as Ibn al-Arabi said. On the kingdom of Solomon meaning on his law and prophethood. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is during the reign of Solomon. It was said: The meaning is in the kingdom of Solomon, meaning in his stories, descriptions and report. Al-Farra’ said: On and in are suitable in such a place. He said: On and not yet because of the Almighty’s saying: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he recited, Satan cast into his recitation. That is, in his recitation. The meaning of the devil and its derivation have been mentioned previously, so there is no point in repeating it. And the devils here are said to be the devils of the jinn, and this is what is understood from this name. It was said: What is meant are the devils of mankind who rebel in misguidance, like the saying of Jarir: Days they call me the devil because of my flirting, and they used to love me when I was a devil The second: The Almighty’s saying: And Solomon did not disbelieve is an exoneration from God for Solomon, and it was not mentioned in the verse that anyone attributed disbelief to him, but the Jews attributed it to magic, but since magic is disbelief, it became like someone who attributed it to disbelief, then He said: But the devils disbelieved so He established their disbelief by teaching magic. And they know is in the accusative case as a state, and it is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a second predicate. The Kufians except for Asim read but the devils with a lightened but and raising the nun of the devils, and that is in al-Anfal 8:But God threw and Ibn Amir agreed with them. The rest read it with emphasis and in the accusative. But is a word that has two meanings: negating the past predicate and affirming the future predicate, and it is built from three words: La, Ka, In. La is a negation, and Kaf is an address, and In is an affirmation and confirmation, so the hamza was removed due to heaviness, and it is heavy and light, so if it is heavy, it is in the accusative case like the heavy in, and if it is light, it is raised with it as it is raised with the light in. Third: Magic. It was said: Magic is originally deception through tricks and illusions. It is when the magician does things and meanings, and the bewitched person imagines that they are different from what they are, like someone who sees a mirage from afar and imagines that it is water, and like the passenger of a ship moving quickly and imagines that what he sees of trees and mountains is moving with him. It was said that it is derived from the verb sahartu al-sabi, meaning to deceive a boy, and likewise if you make him sick. And sihr is similar to it. Labid said: If you ask us what we are, then we are birds from this enchanted people last: He showed us two places for an unseen matter and we were enchanted by food and drink. Friendly birds and flies, bolder than a pack of wolves. God the Almighty says: You are only one of those bewitched. It is said: the bewitched is the one who was created with magic, and it is said: one of the deceivers, meaning one who eats food and drinks. It is said: its origin is concealment, because magic is done in secret. And its origin is diversion, it is said: what bewitched you from such-and-such, meaning what diverted you from it, so magic is diverted from its direction. And it is said: its origin is attraction, and whoever bewitches you has bewitched you. And it is said: in His Almighty saying: Rather, we are a people bewitched, meaning he bewitched us, so he made us slip by imagination from our knowledge. Al-Jawhari said: Magic is taking, and everything that has a subtle and delicate take is magic, and he bewitched him, bewitches him with magic. And the magician is the scholar, and his magic also means he deceived him, and we have mentioned it. Ibn Masoud said: We used to call magic in the pre-Islamic era the bite... and the bite among the Arabs: the intensity of slander and the camouflage of lies. The poet said: I seek refuge in my Lord from the slanderers who bite the biting one. Fourth: There is a difference of opinion as to whether it is real or not. Al-Ghaznawi al-Hanafi mentioned in his book, ‘Uyun al-Ma’ani: According to the Mu’tazila, magic is deception that has no basis, and according to al-Shafi’i, it is whispers and diseases. He said: According to us, its origin is a talisman based on the influence of the characteristics of the planets, like the influence of the sun on the mercury of Pharaoh’s staff, or the glorification of the devils to make easy for him what was difficult. I said: And we believe that it is true and has a reality, and God creates with it what He wills, as will come. Then there is magic that is done by sleight of hand like sorcery. And the sorcerer is the messenger because of the lightness of his gait. Ibn Faris said in Al-Mujmal: Magic is not from the speech of the Bedouins, and it is sleight of hand and taking like sorcery, and from it there is what is memorized speech, and incantations from the names of God Almighty. And it may be from the covenants of the devils, and it may be medicines and smokes and other than that. Fifth: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called eloquence in speech and the tongue in it magic, and he said: Indeed, some eloquence is magic. Narrated by Malik and others. This is because it supports falsehood until the listener thinks it is true. Based on this, his statement, peace be upon him: Indeed, some eloquence is magic was made to criticize eloquence and fluency, as he likened them to magic. It was also said that it was made to praise eloquence and prefer eloquence. This was stated by a group of scholars. The first is more correct, and the evidence for it is his statement, peace be upon him: Perhaps some of you will be more eloquent in his argument than others, and his saying: The most hated of you to me are the chatterboxes and the arrogant. Chattering means talking a lot and repeating it. It is said: A man chattered, so he is a chatterbox and a babbler. The same applies to the one who is arrogant. Ibn Duraid said: So-and-so is arrogant in his speech if he elaborates and is pedantic. He said: Its origin is fahaq, which means to be full, as if he filled his mouth with it. I said: And with this meaning that we mentioned, Amer Al-Sha’bi, the narrator of the hadith, and Sa’sa’ah bin Suhan interpreted it and said: As for his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, some eloquence is magic, a man may be in the right but he is more eloquent in his arguments than the one who is in the right, so he bewitches the people with his eloquence and takes away the truth while he is in the right. Scholars only praise eloquence and the tongue as long as it does not go to the extent of prolixity and verbosity, and portraying falsehood as truth. This is clear, and praise be to God. Sixth: There is magic that constitutes disbelief on the part of the one who does it, such as what they claim of changing people’s forms, and making them appear as animals, and traveling a distance of a month in one night, and flying in the air. So whoever does this to make people think that he is right, then that is disbelief on his part, as stated by Abu Nasr Abd al-Raheem al-Qushayri. Abu Amr said: Whoever claims that the magician can change an animal from one form to another, and makes a person into a donkey or something similar, and is able to move bodies and destroy them and change them, then this person sees the killing of the magician because he is a disbeliever in the prophets, and he claims the same as their signs and miracles, and with this the knowledge of the truth of prophethood is not possible, since the like of it can be obtained through trickery. As for whoever claims that magic is deception, trickery, camouflage and imagination, then it is not obligatory on the basis of his principle to kill the magician, unless he kills someone by his action, in which case he is killed by it. Seventh: The Sunnis believed that magic is proven and has a reality. The majority of the Mu'tazila and Abu Ishaq al-Istrabadi, one of the followers of al-Shafi'i, believed that magic has no reality, but rather it is a deception, illusion, and illusion of something being other than what it is, and that it is a type of sleight of hand and sorcery, as God the Almighty said: It appeared to him from their magic that it was moving. He did not say that it was moving in reality, but rather He said that it was made to appear to him. He also said: They bewitched the eyes of the people. There is no proof in this, because we do not deny that illusion and other things are part of magic, but behind that there are proven matters that reason allows and that have been heard, such as what came in this verse about mentioning magic and teaching it, and if it had no reality it would not have been possible to teach it, nor did God the Almighty inform that they taught it to the people, which indicates that it has a reality. God the Almighty said in the story of Pharaoh's magicians: And they produced a great magic. Surat Al-Falaq, with the agreement of the commentators that the reason for its revelation was the magic of Labid bin Al-A’sam, which is what Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: A Jew from the Jews of Banu Zuraiq, called Labid bin Al-A’sam, cast a spell on the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). The hadith states: “When the spell was cast, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: ‘God has healed me.’” Healing is achieved by removing the illness and eliminating the disease, which indicates that it has a right and a reality, and it is certain that it exists and occurs through the information of God the Most High and His Messenger. According to this, the people of authority and contract who are the ones who make the consensus are responsible for it, and no attention should be paid to their agreement with the dregs of the Mu’tazilah and their opposition to the people of truth. Magic was widespread and well-known in the past, and people talked about it, and none of the Companions or the Followers denied its origin. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Abu Al-A’war on the authority of Armah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Magic was taught in a village in Egypt called Al-Farma, so whoever denies it is an unbeliever, a liar to God and His Messenger, and a denier of what he saw and saw with his own eyes. Eighth: Our scholars said: It is not denied that the magician can cause a breach of the norm that is beyond the capacity of humans, such as illness, separation, disappearance, and deformation of a limb, and other things that have been proven to be impossible for people to be capable of. They said: It is not far-fetched in magic that the magician’s body becomes so thin that it can enter into niches and holes, and stand erect like a reed, and run on a thin thread, and fly in the air, and walk on water, and ride a dog, and other things. Despite this, magic does not cause this, nor is it a reason for its occurrence, nor a generative cause, and the magician is not independent of it. Rather, God, the Most High, creates these things and brings them about when magic occurs, just as He creates satiety when eating, and satisfaction when drinking water. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Ammar al-Dahni that a magician was with al-Walid ibn Uqbah who walked on a rope, and entered the donkey’s anus and exited from its mouth, so Jundub grabbed his sword and killed him - this is Jundub ibn Ka’b al-Azdi, and it is said al-Bajali - and he is the one about whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There will be in my nation a man called Jundub who will strike with the sword and distinguish between truth and falsehood. They used to think of him as Jundub, the killer of the magician. Ali ibn al-Madini said: Haritha ibn Mudrib narrated from him. Ninth: Muslims have agreed that there is magic that God does, such as sending down locusts, lice, and frogs, splitting the sea, turning the staff upside down, bringing the dead back to life, making dumb people speak, and similar great miracles of the Messengers, peace be upon them. This and similar things must be determined that God does not happen or do it when the magician wants it. Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Tayyib said: We only forbade it by consensus, and if it were not for that, we would have permitted it. Tenth: Regarding the difference between magic and miracles, our scholars said: Magic is performed by the magician and others, and there may be a group who know it and can perform it at the same time. And God cannot allow anyone to perform a miracle like it or to oppose it. Then the magician did not claim prophethood, so what comes from him is distinct from the miracle, because the condition of a miracle is the coupling of the claim of prophethood and the challenge with it, as mentioned in the introduction to the book. Eleventh: The jurists differed regarding the ruling on a Muslim or non-Muslim magician. Malik held that if a Muslim practices magic on himself with words that constitute blasphemy, he should be killed and not given a chance to repent, nor should his repentance be accepted, because it is something he does secretly, like a heretic or an adulterer, and because God Almighty called magic blasphemy by saying: And they did not teach it to anyone until they had said, ‘We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve.’ This is the opinion of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Thawr, Ishaq, al-Shafi’i, and Abu Hanifa. Killing a sorcerer was narrated on the authority of Umar, Uthman, Ibn Umar, Hafsah, Abu Musa, Qais ibn Sa’d, and on the authority of seven of the Tabi’un. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The punishment for a sorcerer is to strike him with the sword. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, but it is not strong. Ismail bin Muslim is the only one who narrated it, and they consider it weak. It was narrated by Ibn Uyaynah from Ismail bin Muslim from Al-Hasan, as a mursal. Some of them attributed it to Al-Hasan from Jundub. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: We have narrated from Aisha that she sold a sorceress who had bewitched her and put her price towards freeing slaves. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: If a man admits that he had bewitched her with words that constitute kufr, he must be killed if he does not repent. Likewise, if evidence is established against him and the evidence describes words that constitute kufr. If the words that he said he had bewitched with are not kufr, it is not permissible to kill him. If he caused the bewitched person to commit a crime that necessitates retaliation, then retaliation is taken from him if he did that intentionally. But if it is something for which there is no retaliation, then blood money is due for that. Ibn al-Mundhir said: If the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) differed on an issue, it is obligatory to follow the one who is most similar to the Book and the Sunnah. It may be possible that the magic that ordered the one among them to kill the magician was magic that constituted disbelief, and that would be in accordance with the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It is possible that Aisha may God be pleased with her ordered the sale of a witch whose magic was not disbelief. If someone uses as evidence the hadith of Jundub from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The punishment for the magician is to strike him with the sword, if it were authentic, it would be possible that he ordered the killing of the magician whose magic constituted disbelief, and that would be in accordance with the reports that came from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: A person's blood is not permissible to be shed except in one of three cases. I said: This is correct, and the blood of Muslims is forbidden and cannot be made permissible except with certainty, and there is no certainty with disagreement, and God knows best. Some scholars said: If the people of the craft say that magic is not done except with disbelief and arrogance, or glorifying Satan, then magic if it indicates disbelief is based on this estimation, and God knows best. It was narrated from Al-Shafi’i: The magician is not killed unless he kills with his magic and says I intentionally killed, and if he says I did not intentionally, he is not killed, and the blood money is paid for it like accidental killing, and if he harms him, he is disciplined according to the extent of the harm. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is false for two reasons, the first of which is that he did not know magic, and its reality is that it is composed speech by which someone other than God is glorified, and destinies and beings are attributed to Him. The second is that God, the Exalted, has stated clearly in His Book that he disbelieved, saying: And Solomon did not disbelieve by saying magic, but the devils disbelieved in it and in teaching it. And Harut and Marut say: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve and this is an emphasis on the statement. Malik's companions argued that his repentance is not accepted, because magic is hidden and its doer does not show it, so his repentance is not known, like the zindiq. Rather, repentance is called upon only for the one who shows disbelief and apostasy. Malik said: If the magician or zindiq comes repentant before testifying against them, their repentance is accepted. The evidence for that is the statement of God the Almighty: But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. This indicates that their faith did benefit them before the punishment descended, and so it is with these two. Twelfth: As for the sorcerer of the dhimmi, it was said that he should be killed. Malik said: He should not be killed unless he kills by his sorcery and he is liable for what he has committed, and he should be killed if he does something that he did not promise. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: As for if he is a dhimmi, the narrations from Malik differ. He said once: He should be given a chance to repent and his repentance is Islam. He said once: He should be killed even if he converts to Islam. As for the combatant, he should not be killed if he repents. Malik said the same about the dhimmi who curses the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He should be given a chance to repent and his repentance is Islam. He said once: He should be killed and he should not be given a chance to repent like the Muslim. Malik also said about the dhimmi if he practices sorcery: He should be punished, unless he killed by his sorcery or caused an accident, in which case it should be taken from him according to his share. Another said: He should be killed because he has broken the covenant. The sorcerer does not inherit from his heirs, because he is an unbeliever, unless his sorcery is not called unbelief. Malik said about a woman who marries a husband for herself or for someone else: She should be punished but not killed. Thirteenth: They differed as to whether the magician should ask the one who is bewitched to remove the magic. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab permitted it according to what Al-Bukhari mentioned, and Al-Muzani leaned towards it, but Al-Hasan Al-Basri disliked it. Al-Sha’bi said: There is nothing wrong with the leaflet. Ibn Battel said: In the book of Wahb bin Munabbih: To take seven leaves of green Sidr, crush them between two stones, then throw them in water and recite Ayat Al-Kursi over it, then take three sips of it and wash yourself, for everything that is in him will go away, God willing. It is good for a man if he is prevented from his family. Fourteenth: Most of the Mu'tazila denied the devils and the jinn, and their denial indicates their lack of concern and the weakness of their religion. There is nothing impossible in proving them rationally, and the texts of the Book and the Sunnah indicate their proof. It is the right of the wise man who holds fast to the rope of God to prove what reason has decided to be right, and the Shari'ah has stated its proof. God Almighty said: But the devils disbelieved and He said: And among the devils are those who dive for him and other verses, and Surat al-Jinn dictates this, and he, peace be upon him, said: The devil runs through the son of Adam as blood runs through him. Many people have denied this report, and have transformed two souls into one body. The mind does not deny their behavior among humans if their bodies are thin and simple, as some people say, rather most of them. If they were dense, this would also be true of them, just as it is true that food and drink enter the empty space of the body. Likewise, worms may be in the sons of Adam while they are alive. Fifteenth: The Almighty’s saying: And what was revealed to the two angels is what is negated, and the waw is for conjunction with His saying: And Solomon did not disbelieve because the Jews said: God sent Gabriel and Michael with magic, so God denied that. And in the speech there is an inversion, the meaning is: And Solomon did not disbelieve, and what was revealed to the two angels, but the devils disbelieved, teaching people magic in Babylon, Harut and Marut, so Harut and Marut are substitutes for the devils in His saying: But the devils disbelieved. This is the first interpretation that the verse is based on, and the most correct of what has been said about it, and no attention should be paid to anything else, for magic is from the extraction of devils due to the delicacy of their essence, and the subtlety of their understanding, and what most of the people practice it is women, especially during their menstruation, God Almighty said: And from the evil of those who blow on knots. And the poet said: I seek refuge in my Lord from the slanderers.... Sixteenth: If someone says: How can two be a substitute for a group, when the substitute is only on the same level as the one being replaced? The answer is from three aspects. The first: That two may be called a group, as God Almighty said: But if he has brothers, then to his mother is a sixth. And nothing prevents her from a third to a sixth except two brothers or more, as will be explained in the chapter on women. The second: That since they were the head in education, He specified them without following them, as God Almighty said: Over it are nineteen. The third: They were only mentioned specifically from among them because of their rebellion, as God Almighty said: In them are fruits and palm trees and pomegranates and His statement: And Gabriel and Michael. This is common in the Qur’an and in the speech of the Arabs. Some general people may be mentioned either for their honor or for their virtue, such as the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him and this Prophet and His saying: And Gabriel and Michael, or for their goodness, such as His saying: Fruits, date palms, and pomegranates, or for their majority, such as the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The earth has been made for me a place of prostration and its soil is pure, or because of his rebellion and insolence as in this verse, and God knows best. It has been said that ma is conjoined with magic and it is the object, so according to this, ma has the meaning of who, and magic is sent down to the two angels as a trial for the people and a test, and God has the right to test His servants as He wills, as He tested Talut with the river, and for this reason the two angels say: We are only a trial, meaning a test from God, we inform you that the work of the magician is disbelief, so if you obey us, you will be saved, and if you disobey us, you will perish. It has been narrated from Ali, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, Kaab al-Ahbar, al-Suddi, and al-Kalbi, meaning that when corruption increased among the children of Adam, peace be upon him - and that was during the time of Idris, peace be upon him - the angels taunted them, so God, the Most High, said: If you were in their place and I had instilled in you what I had instilled in them, you would have done the same deeds as they did, so they said: Glory be to You! We should not have done that. He said: So choose two angels from among your best, and they chose Harut and Marut. He sent them down to earth and rode lust in them. Not a month had passed before they were tempted by a woman whose name in Nabataean was Bidakht, in Persian Nahil, and in Arabic, Zahra. They argued with them and tried to seduce her, but she refused unless they entered her religion, drank wine, and killed the soul that God had forbidden. They agreed to it and drank wine and had intercourse with her. A man saw them and they killed him. She asked them about the name by which they would ascend to heaven, so they taught it to her and she spoke it, so she ascended and was transformed into a planet. Salim said on the authority of his father on the authority of Abdullah: Kaab al-Habr told me that they did not complete their day until they did what God had forbidden them. And in another hadith: So they were given the choice between the torment of this world and the torment of the Hereafter, and they chose the torment of this world. So they are being tormented in Babylon in a region of the earth. It was said: Babylon of Iraq. And it was said: Babylon of Nahavand. Ibn Omar, according to what is narrated on the authority of Ata, whenever he saw Al-Zahra and Suhayl, he would curse and insult them, saying: Suhayl was a tax collector in Yemen who used to oppress people, and Al-Zahra was the companion of Harut and Marut. We said: All of this is weak and far from Ibn Omar and others. None of it is authentic, as it is a statement that is rejected by the fundamentals regarding the angels who are the trustees of God over His revelation and His ambassadors to His messengers: They do not disobey God in what He commands them and do what they are commanded. “Rather, they are honored servants. They do not precede Him in speech and they act by His command.” They glorify God night and day, never slackening. As for the mind, it does not deny that the angels commit sins and that they go against what they were commanded to do, and that desires are created in them, as everything is imaginary in the power of God, the Most High. This is the fear of the prophets and the virtuous and knowledgeable saints, but the occurrence of this possibility can only be perceived by hearing and it is not authentic. What indicates its invalidity is that God, the Most High, created the stars and planets when He created the sky, as in the report: When the heaven was created, seven planets were created in it: Saturn, Jupiter, Bahram, Mercury, Venus, the sun, and the moon. This is the meaning of the statement of God Almighty: And each floats in an orbit. Thus it is proven that Venus and Canopus existed before the creation of Adam. Then the statement of the angels: It was not fitting for us is shameful: they are not able to tempt us. This is blasphemy, from which we seek refuge with God, and from attributing it to the honorable angels, may God’s prayers be upon them all. We have declared them to be pure, and they are pure, from everything that the commentators have mentioned and transmitted. Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Majesty, from what they describe. Seventeenth: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Abi Zayd, Ad-Dahhak, and Al-Hasan read the two kings with a kasra on the lam. Ibn Abi Zayd said: They are David and Solomon. So ma according to this statement is also a negative, and Ibn Al-Arabi weakened this statement. Al-Hasan said: They are two kings in Babylon, so ma according to this statement is a non-negative object. Eighteenth: The Almighty’s saying: in Babylon. Babylon is not declined due to being feminine, definite, or foreign. It is a region of the earth. It was said: Iraq and its neighbors. Ibn Masoud said to the people of Kufa: You are between Al-Hirah and Babylon. Qatada said: It is from Nasibin to Ras Al-Ain. Some people said it is in the Maghreb. Ibn Atiyya said: This is weak. Some people said: It is Mount Nahavand. And God Almighty knows best. There is a difference of opinion about its name, Babel. It was said that it was named thus because the languages were confused there when the palace of Nimrod fell. It was also said that it was named thus because when God Almighty wanted to create discord among the languages of the children of Adam, He sent a wind that gathered them from the horizons to Babel. God confused their languages with it, then that wind dispersed them in the lands and caused confusion. The best of it is what was narrated by Dawud ibn Abi Hind on the authority of Alba’ ibn Ahmar on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When Noah, peace be upon him, descended to the bottom of Mount Judi, he built a village and named it Thamanin. One day, their languages were confused in eighty languages, one of which was the Arabic language, and they could not understand each other. Nineteenth: Abdullah bin Busr Al-Mazini narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of this world, for by Him in Whose hand is my soul, it is more enchanting than Harut and Marut. Our scholars said: This world is more enchanting than them because it enchants with its deceptions, and conceals its temptations from you, so it calls you to be keen on it and compete in it, and to gather for it and withhold it, until it separates you from obeying God the Most High, and separates you from seeing the truth and observing it. This world is more enchanting than them, for it takes your heart away from God, and from fulfilling His rights, and from His promise and threat. The enchantment of this world is loving it and enjoying its desires, and making you desire its false wishes until it takes hold of your heart. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Loving you is something that blinds and deafens. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth: The Almighty said: Harut and Marut Harut is not declined, because it is a foreign proper noun, and so is Marut, and the plural of Hawarit and Mawarit, like Tawagheet, and it is said: Hawaratah and Hawar, and Mawaratah and Mawaar, and the same is true of Goliath and Talut, so know. And it was mentioned before, are they two angels or other than them? There is disagreement. Al-Zajjaj said: It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: That is, by the One who sent down to the two angels, and that the two angels teach the people a warning against magic, not a call to it. Al-Zajjaj said: This is the opinion held by most linguists and theorists, and its meaning is that they teach the people the prohibition, so they say to them: Do not do such-and-such, and do not use such-and-such to separate a man from his wife. And what was sent down to them is the prohibition, as if it were a statement to the al-Nas 114:Do not do such-and-such, so they know in the sense of they know, as He said: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam, meaning We have honored. Twenty-first: The Almighty’s saying: And they do not know anyone Min is an additional word for emphasis, and the meaning is: And they do not know anyone. Until they say Until they say is in the accusative case with until, and that is why the letter nun was deleted from it. The language of Hudhayl and Thaqif is with the unvoiced ayn. The pronoun in they know refers to Harut and Marut, and there are two opinions regarding they know, one of them is that it is in its category from education. The second is that it is from information and not from education, so they know means they know. And in the speech of the Arabs it has come to mean I know, as mentioned by Ibn al-A’rabi and Ibn al-Anbari. Ka’b ibn Malik said: The Messenger of God learned that you will catch up with me and that a threat from you is like taking me by the hand. Al-Qatami said: Learn that after error comes guidance and that error will be dispelled. Zuhair said: Learn, by God, this is a division, and be able to use your arm and see where you slip away. Another said: Know that there is no bird except upon a bird of prey, which is death. We are only a trial. When he informed of their trial, the world was more magical than them when it concealed its trial. So do not disbelieve. One group said that it teaches magic, and another group said that it uses it. Al-Mahdawi said that it was mockery, because they were saying this to someone whose misguidance we had confirmed. Twenty-second: The Almighty’s statement: And they learn from them. Sibawayh said: The meaning is that they learn. Something similar to him said: Be, and it is. It was said that it is connected to the position of what they know, because his statement: And what they know, even if the negative ma enters into it, then its dammah indicates the affirmation of teaching. Al-Farra’ said: It is returned to his statement: They teach people magic, so they learn, and it is, so they learn is connected to his statement: We are only a trial, so they come and learn. Al-Suddi said: They used to say to whoever came to them: We are only a trial, so do not disbelieve. If he refused to return, they would say to him: Go to these ashes and urinate in them. When he urinates in them, a light comes out of it shining to the sky, which is faith, then black smoke comes out of it and enters his ears, which is disbelief. So when he tells them what he saw of that, they teach him what they use to separate a man from his wife. A group of scholars said that the magician is not capable of doing more than what God has told us about causing division, because God mentioned that in the context of censuring magic and the purpose of teaching it. If he had been capable of doing more than that, he would have mentioned it. A group said: That is most likely, and it cannot be denied that magic has an effect on hearts, through love and hatred and by casting evils until the magician separates a man from his wife, and comes between a man and his heart, by causing pain and great illness. All of that is perceived through observation, and denying it is stubbornness. This has been mentioned before, and praise be to God. Twenty-third: The Almighty’s statement: And they can not harm anyone thereby except by God’s permission. What they are refers to is the magicians. It was also said to the Jews, and it was also said to the devils. Harming anyone thereby means by magic. Of anyone means anyone, and of is redundant. Except by God’s permission means by His will and decree, not by His command, because the Almighty does not command indecency and decree it upon creation. Al-Zajjaj said: Except by God’s permission means by God’s knowledge. Al-Nahhas said: Abu Ishaq’s statement Except by God’s permission means by God’s knowledge is a mistake, because knowledge is only said to be permissible, and I have given permission. But since He did not prevent what was between them and Him and they continued to do it, it was as if He permitted it metaphorically. Twenty-fourth: The Almighty’s statement: And they learn what harms them. He means in the Hereafter, even if they take it for a little while in this world. It was said: It harms them in this world, because the harm of magic and separation returns to the magician in this world if he stumbles upon it, because he is disciplined and warned, and the evil of magic befalls him. The rest of the verses are clear because their meanings have been presented. The lam in and certainly knew is a lam of emphasis. For whoever purchased it is a lam of an oath, and it is also for emphasis. The position of man is raised by the beginning, because what comes before the lam does not work on what comes after it. Man means who. Al-Farra’ said: It is for recompense. Al-Zajjaj said: This is not a position of condition, and man means who, as you say: I have learned, for whoever comes to you who has no intellect. Man khalaq is redundant, and the meaning is that he has no khalaq in the Hereafter, and it is not added to the obligatory, this is the saying of the Basrans. The Kufians said: It is redundant in obligatory words, and they provided evidence for it with the words of God Almighty: He will forgive you some of your sins. And al-Khalaq means share, Mujahid said. Al-Zajjaj said: And it is also the case with the linguists, except that it is hardly used except for a share of good. He was asked about the words of God Almighty: And they certainly knew that whoever buys it will have no share in the Hereafter, so he informed that they knew, then he said: And evil is that for which they sold themselves, if they only knew, so he informed that they did not know. So the answer, which is the saying of Qatrub and Al-Akhfash, is that those who know are the devils, and those who sold themselves are the humans who do not know. Al-Zajjaj said: Ali bin Sulayman said: I think it is better to say and they certainly knew for the two angels, because they are more deserving of knowing. He said: They knew, as it is said: The two Zayds stood up. Al-Zajjaj said: Those who knew were the Jewish scholars, but it was said: If they had known, meaning they entered into the position of someone who is told: You are not a scholar, because they abandoned working with their work and sought guidance from those who practiced magic.
2:103: God Almighty says: And if they had believed and feared God, the reward from God would have been better, if they only knew. God the Almighty said: And if only they had believed and feared God meaning, they had feared magic. For a reward The reward is the recompense, and it is the answer to And if only they had believed among some people. Al-Akhfash Saeed said: There is no answer for ‘law’ here in wording, but in meaning, and the meaning is that they would have been rewarded. The position of an in His statement: And if only they had believed is in the nominative case, meaning if their belief had occurred, because law is only followed by a verb, whether explicit or implicit, because it is like the letters of condition, since it must have an answer, and a verb must follow it. Muhammad bin Yazid said: And it was not permissible to use “law because the way of all letters of reward is to change the past tense to a future meaning, so since this was in law, it was not permissible to reward with it.
2:104: God Almighty said: “O you who have believed, do not say, ‘Ra’ina,’ but say, ‘Unzurna,’ and listen. And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment.” There are five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, do not say, ‘Ra’ina’ 1:136 mentions another thing from the ignorance of the Jews, and the intended meaning is to forbid Muslims from such a thing. The true meaning of ra’ina in the language is ra’ina and linda’ika, because the reciprocal verb is from two verbs, so it is from ra’aka God, meaning protect us and we will protect you, and ra’abana and linda’abaka. It is also possible that it is from ra’ana sama’ka, meaning free your hearing of our words. There is ambiguity in addressing them in this way, so He ordered the believers to choose the best of words and the most delicate of meanings. Ibn Abbas said that the Muslims used to say to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ra’ana. On the side of request and desire - from consideration - that is, he turned to us, and this was in the language of the Jews an insult, that is, listen, do not hear, so they seized it and said: We used to insult him secretly, but now we insult him openly, so they would address the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with it and laugh among themselves, so Saad bin Muadh heard it and he knew their language, so he said to the Jews: May the curse of God be upon you! If I hear one of you say it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, I will strike his neck, so they said: Do you not say it? So the verse was revealed. And they were forbidden from it, so that the Jews would follow its example in wording and intend the corrupt meaning in it. Second: In this verse there are two proofs: One of them is to avoid words that are likely to imply the opposite or to belittle. From this comes the understanding of slander by insinuation, and this requires the punishment according to us, contrary to Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i and their companions when they said: Insinuation is likely to imply slander and other things, and the punishment is what is dropped by doubt. And an explanation of this will come in An-Noor, God willing. The second evidence: Adherence to blocking and protecting the means, which is the doctrine of Malik and his companions and Ahmad ibn Hanbal in a narration from him. This principle is indicated by the Qur’an and Sunnah. The means is something that is not forbidden in itself, but one fears that committing it will lead to falling into something forbidden. As for the Book, this verse, and the reason for adhering to it is that the Jews used to say that and it was an insult in their language, so when God knew that from them, He forbade them from using that word, because it is a pretext for insulting, and the Almighty’s saying: And do not insult those they invoke other than God, lest they insult God in enmity without knowledge, so He forbade insulting their gods for fear of responding to them with the same, and the Almighty’s saying: And ask them about the city that was by the sea, the verse, so the Blessed and Exalted forbade them from hunting on the Sabbath, so the whales would come to them on the Sabbath by law, that is, openly, so they blocked them on the Sabbath and took them on Sunday, and the dam was a pretext for hunting, so God transformed them into monkeys and pigs, and God mentioned that to us in the meaning of warning against that, and the Almighty’s saying to Adam and Eve: And do not approach this tree, and it has been mentioned before. As for the women, there are many authentic and correct hadiths, including the hadith of Aisha may God be pleased with her: “Umm Habibah and Umm Salamah may God be pleased with them mentioned a church they saw in Abyssinia with pictures on it, so they mentioned that to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘When a righteous man dies among them, they build a mosque over his grave and make those pictures in it. They are the worst of creation in the sight of God.’” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. Our scholars said: Their forefathers did that so that they would be comforted by seeing those pictures and remember their righteous deeds, so they would strive as they did and worship God the Almighty at their graves. So they did that for ages, then after them came successors who were ignorant of their purposes, and Satan whispered to them that your fathers and grandfathers used to worship this picture, so they worshipped it. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) warned against such a thing, and he strongly denounced and threatened whoever did that, and he blocked the means that lead to that, saying: God’s wrath was intense against a people who took the graves of their prophets and righteous people as places of worship. He said: O God, do not make my grave an idol to be worshipped. Muslim narrated on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “What is lawful is clear and what is unlawful is clear, and between the two of them are matters that are ambiguous. So whoever avoids doubtful matters clears himself in regard to his religion and his honor. And whoever falls into doubtful matters falls into what is unlawful, just as a shepherd who pastures his flock around a sanctuary is likely to fall into it.” The hadith. So he was prevented from embarking on doubtful matters for fear of falling into what is unlawful, and this is to block the means. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A servant will not attain the status of being among the righteous until he abandons that which is permissible out of fear of that which is permissible. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Among the major sins is for a man to insult his parents. They said: O Messenger of God, does a man insult his parents? He said: Yes. He insults a man’s father, so he insults his father, and he insults his mother, so he insults his mother.” So he made exposing oneself to insulting one’s parents to insulting one’s fathers. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If you engage in ‘inah transactions, take the tails of cows, are content with agriculture, and abandon jihad, God will send upon you a humiliation that will not be removed from you until you return to your religion.” Abu Ubaid al-Harawi said that ‘inah is when a man sells a commodity to another man for a known price for a specified period, then buys it back from him for less than the price he sold it for. He said: If he buys a commodity from another man in the presence of the one seeking ‘inah for a known price and takes possession of it, then sells it to the one seeking ‘inah for a price higher than what he bought it for a specified period, then the buyer sells it to the first seller for cash for less than the price, then this is also ‘inah, and it is easier than the first, and it is permissible according to some of them. It is called ‘inah because the cash is given to the owner of the ‘inah, because the ‘inah is the present money, and the buyer only buys it to sell it for a present cash that reaches him immediately. Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Malik that the mother of a slave of Zayd ibn al-Arqam mentioned to Aisha may God be pleased with her that she had sold a slave to Zayd for eight hundred dirhams in cash, then he bought him back from him for six hundred in cash. Aisha said: “What a bad purchase, what a bad purchase! Tell Zayd that he has nullified his jihad with the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) if he does not repent.” Such a thing cannot be said based on opinion, because the nullification of deeds can only be known through revelation, so it is proven that it was traced back to the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace). Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him said: Leave usury and suspicion. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him forbade dirhams in their house with a fence between them. I said: This is the evidence we have for blocking the means, and upon it the Malikis based their book on terms and other issues in sales and other matters. The Shafi’is do not have a book on terms, because for them that is different, independent contracts. They said: The origin of things is based on appearances, not on conjectures. The Malikis made the commodity so that it can be used to obtain dirhams with more than it, and this is usury itself, so be aware of it. Third: The Almighty’s saying, Do not say ‘ra’ana’ is a prohibition that implies a ban, as mentioned above. Al-Hasan read ‘ra’ana’ with a tanween. He said: meaning, a desertion of speech, and it is a source and its accusative is ‘saw’, meaning, do not say rashness. Zur ibn Hubaish and Al-A’mash read ‘ra’una’. It is said when we come down from a mountain: ‘ra’ana’, and the mountain is ‘ar’ana’. An army is ‘ar’ana’, meaning scattered. And so is a man ‘ar’ana’, meaning scattered in his arguments and not united in his mind, according to An-Nahhas. Ibn Faris said: A man is ‘ar’ana’, meaning reckless. And a woman is ‘ar’ana’. Basra was called ‘ra’ana’ because it resembles the ‘ra’ana’ of a mountain. Ibn Duraid said that, and he recited for Al-Farazdaq: If it weren't for Ibn Utbah Amr and my hope for him, the reckless Basra would not have been my homeland. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And say, ‘Look at us.’ They were commanded to address him, may God bless him and grant him peace, with reverence, and the meaning is, Turn to us and look at us. So the transitive letter was omitted, as He said: The appearance of beauty and goodness is seen as the arak gazelle sees the deer That is, to the arak tree. Mujahid said: The meaning is that we understood and he explained it to us. It was also said: The meaning is that we waited and he took his time with us. He said: If you give me an hour, it will benefit me with Umm Jundub. It appears that it calls for the eye to look at the situation, coupled with contemplation of the situation. This is the meaning of ra’ina, so the word was changed to refer to the believers, and the Jews’ attachment was removed. Al-A’mash and others read unzurna with a severing of the alif and a kasra on the dhaal, meaning delay us and give us time until we understand from you and receive from you. The poet said: Aba Hind, do not rush us and wait for us to tell the truth Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And listen to what He, the Majestic and Exalted, has forbidden and commanded, He has urged listening, which includes obedience. And know that whoever disobeys His command and disbelieves will face a painful punishment.
2:105: God Almighty says: “Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists do not like that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord. And God chooses for His mercy whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.” God the Almighty said: He does not desire meaning he does not wish, and it has been mentioned before. Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture, nor the polytheists is in apposition to People. It is permissible to say: nor the polytheists, in apposition to those, as An-Nahhas said. That He should send down upon you any good is redundant, good is the name of what its agent is not named. And that is in the accusative case, meaning that He should send down. And God chooses for His mercy whom He wills Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: He chooses for His mercy meaning with His prophethood, He chose for it Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some people said: Mercy is the Qur’an. It was said: Mercy in this verse is general for all its types that God has bestowed upon His servants in the past and present. It is said: He has mercy, has compassion, if he is tender. Womb, mercy, and mercy are one and the same, as Ibn Faris said. And God’s mercy to His servants is His favor upon them and His forgiveness for them. And God is the possessor of great bounty means possessor.
2:106: There are five issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten. “Nusooha” is in apposition to Naskh, and the ya was deleted for the sake of jussive. Whoever reads Nansaaha deleted the damma from the hamza for the sake of jussive, and its meaning will come. Na’at is the answer to the condition, and this is a great verse in rulings. The reason for it is that when the Jews envied the Muslims for facing the Kaaba and attacked Islam for that, and said: Muhammad commands his companions to do something and then forbids them from it, this Qur’an was only from his side, and for this reason some of it contradicts itself, so God revealed: And when We substitute a verse in place of another verse. And He revealed: Whatever verse We abrogate. Second: Knowing this chapter is certain and its benefit is great. Scholars cannot do without knowing it, and only the ignorant and the rich deny it, because of the new rulings that result from it, and knowing what is permissible from what is forbidden. Abu Al-Bukhtari narrated that Ali, may God be pleased with him, entered the mosque and saw a man frightening the people, so he said: What is this? They said: A man who reminds people. He said: He is not a man who reminds people! Rather, he says: I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so, so recognize me. So he sent for him and said: Do you know the abrogating and the abrogated?! He said: No. He said: Then leave our mosque and do not mention it in it. In another narration: Do you know the abrogating and the abrogated? He said: No. He said: You are ruined and you cause others to be ruined! And the same was narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. Third: Abrogation in the speech of the Arabs has two aspects: One of them: Transfer, such as transferring one book from another. Based on this, the entire Qur’an is abrogated, I mean from the Preserved Tablet and its revelation to the House of Honor in the lowest heaven. This has nothing to do with this verse, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, We were transcribing what you used to do, meaning We commanded its abrogation and confirmation. Second: Nullification and removal, which is what is meant here, and it is divided in the language into two types: One of them: invalidating something, removing it, and establishing another in its place.
