From this, the sun abrogates the shadow if it removes it and replaces it. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten, We bring forth one better than it. And in Sahih Muslim. There was never a prophecy that did not transmute, that is, change from one state to another, meaning the matter of the nation. Ibn Faris said: Abrogation is the abrogation of the Book, and abrogation is when you remove a matter that was previously acted upon and then abrogate it with other hadiths, like a verse that is revealed with a matter then is replaced by another. And everything that succeeds something has abrogated it. It is said: the sun abrogated the shadow, and gray hair abrogated the youth. And the transmigration of heirs: when heirs die after heirs and the original inheritance remains and has not been divided, and likewise the transmigration of times and centuries. The second: removing something without another taking its place, like their saying the wind abrogated the trace. From this meaning is the saying of God Almighty: Then God abrogates what Satan casts, meaning He removes it so that it is not recited nor is it recorded in the Qur’an in its place. Abu Ubaid claimed that this second abrogation was when a surah was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was removed so that it was not recited or written. I said: And from it is what was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab and Aisha, may God be pleased with them, that Surat Al-Ahzab was equal to Surat Al-Baqarah in length, as will be explained there, God willing. And what indicates this is what Abu Bakr Al-Anbari mentioned: My father told us, Nasr bin Dawud told us, Abu Ubaid told us, Abdullah bin Salih told us, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Yunus and Uqayl, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Umamah bin Sahl bin Hanif told me in the assembly of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab: “A man got up at night to recite a surah from the Qur’an, but he was not able to do anything of it. Another got up but he was not able to do anything of it. Another got up but he was not able to do anything of it. So they went to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). One of them said: ‘I got up last night, O Messenger of God, to recite a surah from the Qur’an, but I was not able to do anything of it.’ So the other got up and said: ‘And by God, I am the same, O Messenger of God.’ So the other got up and said: ‘And by God, I am the same, O Messenger of God.’ So the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: ‘It is one of the things that God abrogated last night.’” In one of the narrations: Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab heard what Abu Umamah was saying and did not deny it. Fourth: Groups of later converts to Islam denied its permissibility, and they are proven by the consensus of the previous predecessors that it is included in the Sharia. Groups of Jews also denied it, and they are proven by what is stated in their Torah, claiming that God Almighty said to Noah, peace be upon him, when he left the ship: I have made every animal food for you and your descendants, and I have released it to you like the plants of grass, except for blood, do not eat it. Then He forbade Moses and the Children of Israel many animals, and because Adam, peace be upon him, married his brother to his sister, and God forbade that to Moses, peace be upon him, and others, and because Abraham, the friend of God, was ordered to slaughter his son and then said to him: Do not slaughter him, and because Moses ordered the Children of Israel to kill those among them who worshipped the calf, then he ordered them to lift the sword from them, and because his prophethood was not worshipped before his mission, then it was worshipped after that, and so on. This is not a matter of beginning, but rather it is transferring the servants from one form of worship to another, and from one rule to another, for a kind of interest, to demonstrate His wisdom and the perfection of His kingdom. There is no disagreement among rational people that the laws of the prophets were intended for the religious and worldly interests of creation, but beginning would have been necessary if He did not know the nature of things. As for the one who knows that, his speech changes according to the changing interests, like the doctor who takes into account the conditions of the sick, so he takes that into account in his successor by His will and desire. There is no god but Him, so His speech changes, but His knowledge and will do not change, for that is impossible with regard to God Almighty. The Jews considered abrogation and badā’ to be one and the same thing, and therefore they did not permit it and went astray. An-Nahhas said: The difference between abrogation and badā’ is that abrogation is the conversion of worship from one thing to another that was permissible and then becomes forbidden, or was forbidden and then becomes permissible. As for badā’, it is abandoning what you intended, like saying: Go to so-and-so today, then you say: Do not go to him, and it appears to you that you have changed your mind about the first statement. This is something that applies to humans due to their shortcomings. Similarly, if you said: Plant such-and-such this year, then you said: Do not do it, then that is badā’. Fifth: Know that the abrogator in reality is God Almighty. The legal discourse is called the abrogator metaphorically, since abrogation occurs through it, just as it may be called metaphorically, and the thing in which it is abrogated, so it is said: The fast of Ramadan abrogates the fast of Ashura. So the abrogated is the removed, and the thing from which it is abrogated is the one who performs the removed worship, and he is the one who is charged. Sixth: The expressions of our Imams differed regarding the definition of abrogation. What the experts among the people of Sunnah agree upon is that it is the removal of what has been established of the Shari’ah ruling by a delayed speech. This is how Judge Abdul Wahhab and Judge Abu Bakr defined it. They added: If it were not for that, the previous one would have been established. They preserved the linguistic meaning of abrogation, as it means lifting and removing, and to guard against the rational ruling. They mentioned the speech to include all aspects of evidence from the text, the apparent meaning, the implied meaning, and other things, and to exclude analogy and consensus, as abrogation cannot be imagined in them or by them. They restricted it to delayed speech, because if it were connected to it, it would be a clarification of the purpose of the ruling, not abrogating, or the end of the speech would lift its beginning, like your saying, Stand up, do not stand up. Seventh: The abrogated, according to our Sunni scholars, is the established ruling itself, not its like, as the Mu’tazila say, which is the discourse indicating that the like of the established ruling in the future based on the previous text will be removed. What led them to this is their doctrine that commands are intended, and that good is a psychological attribute of good, and that God’s will is good, and our scholars have nullified this in their books. Eighth: Our scholars differed on whether abrogation is included in the report. The majority are of the opinion that abrogation is only limited to commands and prohibitions, and abrogation is not included in the report because it is impossible to lie about God Almighty. It was said: If the report ofcludes a legal ruling, it is permissible to abrogate it, like the Almighty’s statement: And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant. And there will come the statement about it, God Almighty willing. Ninth: Specialization from generality gives the impression that it is abrogation, but it is not, because the specialization was never included in the generality. If it were proven that the generality included something - something - and then that thing was excluded from the generality, then it would be abrogation, not specialization. The predecessors called specialization abrogation by extension and metaphor. Tenth: Know that there may be reports in the Shariah that appear to be general and comprehensive, but are restricted in another place, and that generality is removed, such as the statement of God the Almighty: “And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me.” This ruling appears to be a report about answering every supplicant in every situation, but what restricts it has been mentioned in another place, such as His statement: He removes that to which you call, if He wills. One who does not have insight may think that this is a case of abrogation in reports, but it is not so. Rather, it is a case of generality and restriction. This issue will be further explained in its proper place, God willing. Eleventh: Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: It is permissible to abrogate the heavier to the lighter, such as abrogate the proof of ten by the proof of two. And it is permissible to abrogate the lighter to the heavier, such as abrogate the Day of Ashura and the days counted in Ramadan, as will be explained in the verse on fasting. And the like is abrogates with its like in heaviness and lightness, such as the Qiblah. And the thing is abrogates without a substitute, such as the secret charity. And the Qur’an is abrogates with the Qur’an, and the Sunnah with the expression, and this expression means the definitive, continuous report. And the report of one person is abrogates with the report of one person. The most skilled imams are of the opinion that the Qur’an is abrogated by the Sunnah, and this is found in his, peace be upon him, saying: There is no will for an heir. This is the apparent meaning of Malik’s issues. Al-Shafi’i and Abu al-Faraj al-Maliki rejected this, but the first is more correct, based on the evidence that all of them are the rulings of God Almighty and from Him, even if the names differ. Also, flogging is not prescribed for the punishment of adultery for a married woman who is stoned, and there is no excuse for this except the Sunnah and the actions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is clear. The experts also agree that the Sunnah is abrogated by the Qur’an, and this is found in the case of the Qiblah, as praying towards the Levant was not in the Book of God Almighty. And in His Almighty’s saying: So do not return them to the disbelievers, their return was only due to the peace treaty between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Quraysh. The experts allow the abrogation of the Qur’an by a single report rationally, but they differed as to whether it occurred legally. Abu al-Ma’ali and others held that it occurred in the incident of the Quba Mosque, as will be explained, but some people rejected that. It is not valid to abrogate a text by analogy, since one of the conditions of analogy is that it does not contradict a text. All of this was during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). However, after his death and the establishment of the Shariah, the Ummah agreed that there is no abrogation. This is why consensus does not abrogate nor is it abrogated by it, since it was established after the cessation of revelation. So if we find consensus that contradicts a text, we know that the consensus was based on an abrogating text that we do not know of, and that that contradictory text should not be acted upon, and that its implication was abrogated and remained a Sunnah that is read and narrated, like the verse of the number of Sunnahs in the Qur’an that is recited. So ponder this, for it is valuable, and it is from the category of abrogating the ruling without the recitation, and the same applies to the secret charity. Recitation may be abrogated without the ruling, such as the verse of stoning. Recitation and ruling may be abrogated together, and from this is the saying of As-Siddiq may God be pleased with him: We used to recite: Do not turn away from your fathers, for it is disbelief, and there are many like it. The expert opinion is that whoever is not informed of the abrogating verse must abide by the first ruling, as will be explained in changing the direction of prayer. The experts are of the opinion that it is permissible to abrogate the ruling before it is done, and this is found in the story of the slaughtered animal, and in the imposition of fifty before it is done by five, as will be explained in Al-Isra and As-Saffat, God willing. Twelfth: There are ways to know the abrogator, including: that there is something in the wording that indicates it, such as his saying, peace be upon him: “I forbade you from visiting graves, so visit them. I forbade you from drinking except in leather containers, so drink from any vessel, but do not drink intoxicants.” And the like. Among them is that the narrator mentions the date, such as saying: I heard in the year of the Trench, and the abrogated had been known before that. Or he says: The ruling of such-and-such was abrogated by such-and-such. Among them is that the nation agrees on the ruling that it was abrogated and that its abrogator came before. This topic is explained in detail in the principles of jurisprudence. We have pointed out what is in it for those who limit themselves to it, and God is the Grantor of success in guidance. Thirteenth: The majority of scholars read ma naksah with a fatha on the nun from nasakh, which is the apparent word used to mean: We do not remove the ruling of a verse and keep its recitation, as mentioned above. It is possible that the meaning is: We do not remove the ruling of a verse and its recitation, as we mentioned. Ibn Amir read naksah with a damma on the nun, from ankhat al-kitab, meaning I found it abrogated. Abu Hatim said: This is a mistake. Al-Farisi Abu Ali said: It is not a language, because it is not said nasha and ankha in one meaning, unless the meaning is what we find abrogated, as you say: Ahmadtu al-rajul wa abkhaluhu, meaning you found him praiseworthy and stingy. Abu Ali said: And we do not find it abrogated except by “naksah, so the two readings agree in meaning even if they differ in wording. It was said: We do not abrogate what we make a copy for you, it is said: I copied the book if you wrote it, and Antaskhatu ghayri if you made a copy for him. Al-Makki said: It is not permissible for the hamza to be transitive, because the meaning changes, and the meaning becomes: We do not abrogate you of a verse, O Muhammad, and His abrogate it is His sending it down to him, so the meaning becomes: We do not send down to you of a verse or cause you to forget it, We bring one better than it or similar to it, so the meaning is that for every verse that was sent down, He brought one better than it, so the entire Qur’an becomes abrogated, and this is not possible, because only a small part of the Qur’an was abrogated. So since it is impossible for af’al and fa’ala to have the meaning of ‘did not hear’, and it is impossible for the hamza to be transitive because the meaning is corrupted, nothing remains possible except for it to be from the category of ahmadtuhu and abkhaluhu if you find him praiseworthy or stingy. Fourteenth: The Almighty’s saying: Or We cause it to be forgotten. Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read it with the opening of the noon, the seen, and the hamza. This is how Umar, Ibn Abbas, Ata’, Mujahid, Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Ubayd ibn Umair, Al-Nakha’i, and Ibn Muhaisin read it, from the word delay, meaning that We delay the abrogation of its wording, meaning that We leave it at the end of the Mother of the Book so that it does not happen. This is the saying of Ata’. Others than Ata’ said: The meaning of or We cause it to be forgotten is that We delay its abrogation to a known time, from their saying: I delayed this matter, meaning that I postponed it. This is similar to their saying: I sold it for a while, meaning that I delayed it. Ibn Faris said: They say: May God delay your lifespan, and May God delay your lifespan. People have also been delayed and distanced, and I caused them to be delayed, meaning that I delayed them. So the meaning is that We delay its revelation or its abrogation, as we mentioned. It was also said: We remove it from them so that it is not read or remembered. The rest read it with a damma on the noon, from the word nansiyān which means to leave, meaning we leave it and do not change it or abrogate it. This was said by Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi. From this is the saying of God Almighty: They forgot God, so He forgot them, meaning they abandoned His worship, so He left them in torment. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this reading. Abu Ubaid said: I heard Abu Nu`aym al-Qari’ say: I read to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a dream according to the reading of Abu Amr, and he did not criticize me except for two letters. He said: I read to him arna, so he said: arna, so Abu Ubaid said: And do you think the other letter is or we forget it, so he said: or we forget it. Al-Azhari narrated nansiyā, “we order to leave it.” It is said: I forgot the thing, meaning I ordered it to be left, and nasituhu means I left it. The poet said: I have an obstacle to overcome, I will not forget it nor will it be forgotten Nor do I command you to abandon it. Al-Zajjaj said: The reading with the damma on the noon does not carry the meaning of abandonment. It is not said: Ansi meaning left. What Ali bin Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas, Or we forget it, he said: We leave it, we do not change it, is not correct. Perhaps Ibn Abbas said: We leave it, but he did not make it precise. What most linguists and scholars agree on is that the meaning of Or we forget it is We barked at you for abandoning it, from Nasa if you leave it, then you punish him. Abu Ali and others said: This is correct, because it means We make you abandon it. It was said: From al-Nisyan in its original form, which is the absence of remembrance, meaning Or we forget it, O Muhammad, so do not remember it. It was transmitted with the hamza, so the verb takes two objects, which are the Prophet and the ha’, but the name of the Prophet is deleted. Fifteenth: The Almighty’s statement: And brought something better than it. The word better here is an adjective of preference, and the meaning is more beneficial to you, O people, in the immediate future if the abrogating verse is lighter, and in the future if it is heavier, and similar to it if it is equal. Malik said: A decisive abrogated verse. It was said: What is meant by better is not preference, because the speech of God is not differentiated, but rather it is like His statement: Whoever brings a good deed will have something better than it, meaning he will have something better than it, meaning benefit and reward, not the good that means something better. The first statement is indicated by His statement: or something similar to it.
2:107: God Almighty says: Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that you have not besides God any protector or helper? God the Almighty said: Have you not known? The verb is jussive with lam, and the interrogative letters do not change the function of the agent. An is opened because it is in the accusative case. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, meaning the creation and invention, the dominion and authority, and the enforcement of the command and will. Dominion is raised by the subject, and the predicate is His, and the sentence is the predicate of An. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation, because He said: And you have not besides God any protector or helper. It was said that the meaning is: Say to them, O Muhammad, do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and you have not besides God any protector or helper? From wali the matter of so-and-so, meaning I carried it out, and from this comes the crown prince, meaning the one who is responsible for what is entrusted to him of the affairs of the Muslims. The meaning of besides God is other than God and after God, as Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said. O soul, you have no protector but God, and no one can endure the events of time. The group reads nor helper in the accusative case, in apposition to guardian. It is also permissible to say nor helper in the nominative case, in apposition to place, because the meaning is that you have no protector or helper other than God.
2:108: The Almighty said: Or do you want? This is the disconnected umm which means rather, meaning rather you want, and the meaning of the speech is rebuke. That you ask is in the accusative case with want, as was asked the kaf is in the accusative case as an attribute of a source, meaning a question as. And Moses is in the nominative case as its agent was not named. From before: their asking him to show them God openly, and they asked Muhammad to bring God and the angels before them. From Ibn Abbas and Mujahid: they asked that Al-Safa be made into gold for them. Al-Hasan read as was flown, and this is according to the language of those who said: I asked, I ask, and it is permissible for it to be instead of the hamza a silent ya in a way that is not standard, so the seen before it was broken. Al-Nahhas said: The alternative of the hamza is far, and the middle of everything is: the middle. Abu Ubaidah Ma'mar ibn Al-Muthanna said this, and from it is his saying: in the middle of Hell. Isa bin Omar narrated: I kept writing until my limbs were exhausted, and he recited the words of Hassan mourning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Woe to the companions of the Prophet and his family after sunset in the midst of the atheists It was said: The path is the right path, according to Al-Farra’, meaning he went astray from the right path and its direction, meaning the path of obedience to God Almighty. And according to Ibn Abbas also: The reason for the revelation of this verse is that Rafi’ bin Khuzaymah and Wahb bin Zaid said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Bring us a book from the heaven that we may read, and cause rivers to flow for us so that we may follow you.
2:109: The Almighty said: Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy from themselves [out of] themselves [after the truth has become clear to them]. There are two issues in this: The first: wish means to wish, and it was mentioned before. Disbelievers is the second object of they return you. “From yourselves” is said to be related to wish. It is also said to be related to envy, so the pause is at his saying: disbelievers. And envy is the object for it, meaning they wished that out of envy, or a source that what preceded it indicated the action. The meaning of from theirselves is from their own accord, without finding it in a book or being commanded to do so. The word envy gives this, meaning from their own selves, as confirmation and obligation, as God Almighty said: They say with their mouths, “They write the book with their hands,” And no bird flies with its wings. The verse is about the Jews. Second: Envy is of two types: blameworthy and praiseworthy. The blameworthy type is to wish for the removal of God’s blessing from your Muslim brother, regardless of whether you wish for it to return to you or not. This is the type that God the Most High has condemned in His Book when He says, Or do they envy people for what God has given them of His bounty? It is only blameworthy because it belittles the Truth, glory be to Him, and that He bestowed a blessing on someone who does not deserve it. As for the praiseworthy type, it is what came in the authentic hadith from his saying, peace be upon him: “There is no envy except in two cases: a man to whom God has given the Qur’an and he recites it during the night and during the day, and a man to whom God has given wealth and he spends it during the night and during the day.” This envy means envy. Al-Bukhari also titled it the chapter on envy in knowledge and wisdom. Its true meaning is: that you wish to have what your Muslim brother has of goodness and blessings and that his goodness not be taken away from him. It may be permissible to call this competition, as in the saying of God the Almighty: And for this let the competitors compete. “After the truth has become clear to them” meaning after the truth has become clear to them, which is Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and the Qur’an that he brought. The Almighty’s saying: So pardon and overlook contains two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: So pardon. The original is afūwū. The damma was deleted because of its heaviness, then the waw was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Pardon means leaving the blame for a sin. Forgiveness means removing its effect from the soul. You pardoned someone if you turned away from his sin. You turned away from him if you turned away from him and left him. From this is the Almighty’s saying: Should We then turn away from you the Reminder? Second: This verse was abrogated by the statement, Fight those who do not believe until the statement, submissive, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said that what abrogated it was Kill the polytheists. Abu Ubaidah said: Every verse in which fighting is not mentioned is Meccan and abrogated by fighting. Ibn Atiyyah said: His ruling that this verse is Meccan is weak, because the Jews’ opposition only occurred in Medina. I said: It is correct. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode on a donkey wearing a Fadak cloak, and Usamah was behind him, visiting Sa`d ibn `Ubadah in Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj before the Battle of Badr. They traveled until they passed by a gathering in which `Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was present - and that was before `Abdullah ibn Ubayy had converted to Islam - and in the gathering there was a mixture of Muslims, idolaters, and Jews, and among the Muslims was `Abdullah ibn Rawahah. When the dust of the animal covered the gathering, `Abdullah ibn Rawahah covered his nose with his cloak and said: Do not dust us! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, greeted them, then he stood up and got off, and called them to God the Most High and recited the Qur’an to them. `Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul said to him: O man, I do not like what you say if it is true! Do not bother us with it in our gatherings. Go back to your man, and whoever comes, tell him. `Abdullah ibn Rawahah said: Yes, O Messenger of God, and cover us in our gatherings, for we like that. The polytheists, Muslims and Jews were so angry that they almost quarreled. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept calming them down until they calmed down. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mounted his mount and rode until he entered upon Sa`d ibn `Ubadah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Sa`d, did you not hear what Abu Hubab said - meaning `Abdullah ibn Ubayy - he said such and such. He said: “O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you! Forgive him and pardon him, for by He who sent down the Book to you, God has brought the truth that He sent down to you. The people of this lake agreed to crown him and tie him with a headband. When God returned that with the truth that He gave you, he was pleased with that. That is what you saw happening. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pardoned him.” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions would pardon the polytheists and the People of the Book as God the Almighty commanded them, and they would be patient in the face of harm. God the Almighty said: And you will surely hear much abuse from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with God. And He said: Many of the People of the Scripture wish that they would be pardoned. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) interpreted his pardon of them as God had commanded him to do until He gave him permission to deal with them. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fought the Battle of Badr, God killed the leaders of the infidels and the chiefs of Quraysh who He had killed, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions returned victorious and triumphant, with captives from the leaders of the infidels and the chiefs of Quraysh. Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and the polytheists and idol worshippers who were with him said: This is a matter that has been decided, so they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Islam, and they became Muslims. The Almighty said: Until God brings about His command meaning Banu Qurayzah and the expulsion of Banu Nadir. “Indeed, God is over all things competent. And establish prayer and give zakah” has been presented. And praise be to God Almighty.
2:110: God Almighty said: And whatever good you send forward for yourselves, you will find it with God. It was stated in the hadith: When a servant dies, the people say, ‘What did he leave behind?’ and the angels say, ‘What did he send forward?’ Al-Bukhari and Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abdullah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you loves the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none of us but loves his wealth more than the wealth of his heir. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is none of you but loves the wealth of his heir more than his own wealth. Your wealth is what you have sent forward, and the wealth of your heir is what you have delayed.” The wording of al-Nasa’i. The wording of al-Bukhari: Abdullah said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Which of you loves the wealth of his heirs more than his own wealth? They said: O Messenger of God, there is none among us who does not love his wealth more. He said: His wealth is what he has sent forward, and the wealth of his heirs is what he has left behind. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him passed by Baqi’ al-Gharqad and said: “Peace be upon you, people of the graves. What report do we have? Your women have married, your houses have been inhabited, and your wealth has been divided.” A voice answered him: O Ibn al-Khattab, what report do we have? What we sent forward we have found, what we spent we have gained, and what we left behind we have lost. The speaker spoke well: Do good deeds before your death and work, for there is no way to immortality. Another said: May you have a repentance that is hoped for before death and before tongues are silenced. Another said: I gave birth to you when your mother gave birth to you crying and the people around you laughed with joy So work for a day when, when they weep over your death, you will be laughing and happy. Another said: Be the first to do good and take the initiative, for what you know is behind you. And do good, for every person will do good for what he has done. Better than all of this is what Abu Al-Atahiya said: Be happy with your money in your life, but there will remain behind you a reformer or a corruptor If it is left to a corrupt person, it will not remain, and the brother of righteousness, even a little, will increase. If you can, be your own heir, for death itself is a guide. God is All-Seeing of what you do.
2:111: God Almighty says: “And they say, ‘None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian.’ Those are their wishful thoughts. Say, ‘Produce your proof, if you should be truthful.’”
2:112: God Almighty says: “Yes, whoever submits his face to God while being a doer of good will have his reward with his Lord. And no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.” God the Almighty said: And they say, ‘None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian.’ The meaning is: The Jews said, None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew. And the Christians said, None will enter Paradise except one who is a Christian. Al-Farra’ permitted Hood to mean Jewish, with the redundant word removed, and it to be the plural of Ha’id. Al-Akhfash Sa’id said: Except for whoever was made kan singular in the form of man, then he said Hood, making it plural, because the meaning of man is plural. Those are their desires is also permissible, and this has been discussed previously. Praise be to God. God the Almighty said: “Say: Bring your proof.” The root of hatawa is hatiwa. The damma was dropped because it was heavy, then the ya was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It is said for a singular masculine: hat, like ram, and for a feminine: hatti, like ramy. Proof is the evidence that establishes certainty. Its plural is baraheen, like qurban and qurbani, and sultan and sultans. Al-Tabari said: Seeking proof here requires establishing the view and responding to those who deny it. If you are truthful, meaning in your faith or in your saying that you will enter Paradise, meaning explain what you said with proof. Then God the Almighty said: Yes, in response to them and belying them, meaning it is not as you say. It was said: Yes, he who submits his face to God means he who submits is he who submits and submits. It was also said that he who does his work sincerely. The face was mentioned specifically because it is the most honorable thing that can be seen in a person, and because it is the seat of the senses, and in it glory and humiliation appear. The Arabs use the word face to describe the whole thing, and it is correct that the face in this verse is the intended meaning. And He is a doer of good is a sentence in the position of a state, and the pronoun in his face and for him is in the form of from and that is his reward and it is in upon them in the meaning, and likewise in they grieve and it has been mentioned before.
2:113: God Almighty said: “And the Jews say, ‘The Christians are not upon anything,’ and the Christians say, ‘The Jews are not upon anything,’ while they recite the Scripture. Thus say those who do not know the same as they say. So God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.” It means that each group of them claimed that the other was not doing anything, and that he was more deserving of God’s mercy than him. And they recite the Book means the Torah and the Gospel, and the sentence is in the position of a circumstantial. What is meant by those who do not know according to the majority is the Arab disbelievers, because they do not have a book. Ata' said: What is meant are nations that existed before the Jews and Christians. Al-Rabi' bin Anas: The meaning is that the Jews said the same before the Christians. Ibn Abbas. The people of Najran came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Jewish rabbis came to them. They disputed before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and each group of them said to the other: You have nothing, so the verse was revealed.
2:114: It contains seven issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned therein? “From” is raised as a subject, and more unjust is its predicate, and the meaning is no one is more unjust. And that is in the accusative case as a substitute for masajid, and it is possible that the estimation is: dislike that it be mentioned, then it is deleted. And it is possible that the estimation is: from that it be mentioned therein, and the letter of genitive case is deleted with that due to the length of the speech. And what is meant by masajid here is the Holy House and its niches. And it is said that it is the Kaaba, and it is plural because it is the qibla of the mosques or for glorification. And it is said that what is meant is all the mosques, and the singular is masjid with a kasra on the j, and some Arabs say masjid with a fatha on it. Al-Farra’ said: Everything that is based on the pattern of fa’il yaf’al, such as dakhala yakhul, the fa’il of it is with fat-ha, whether it is a noun or a verbal noun, and there is no difference in it, such as dakhala yakhul madhaklan, and this is its madhak, except for letters of the nouns that they required to break the ‘ayn, such as: al-masjid, al-matla’, al-maghreb, al-mashq, al-maqtas, al-mafraq, al-mafraq, al-majzar, al-maskan, al-marfaq from rafq yarfaq, al-manbt and al-mansik from nisak yansak, so they made the kasra a sign of the noun, and perhaps some Arabs opened it in the noun. Al-masjid with fat-ha: the forehead of a man where the scars of prostration affect him. And the seven Arabs, said al-Jawhari. Second: People differed about the meaning of this verse and about whom it was revealed. The commentators mentioned that it was revealed about Bukht Nasr, because he destroyed the Holy House. Ibn Abbas and others said: It was revealed about the Christians, and the meaning is: How do you claim, O Christians, that you are from the people of Paradise! And you destroyed the Holy House and prevented the worshippers from praying in it. The meaning of the verse according to this: astonishment at what the Christians did to the Holy House despite their veneration of it, and they only did what they did out of enmity towards the Jews. Saeed narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: Those are the enemies of God, the Christians, and their hatred of the Jews led them to help Bukht Nasr the Babylonian Zoroastrian in destroying the Holy House. It was narrated that this destruction continued until the time of Umar, may God be pleased with him. It was said: It was revealed about the polytheists when they prevented the worshippers and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and turned them away from the Sacred Mosque in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah. It was said: What is meant by preventing someone from entering a mosque is until the Day of Resurrection, and this is correct, because the wording is general and was mentioned in the plural form, so specifying it to some mosques and some people is weak, and God knows best. Third: The destruction of mosques may be real, such as the destruction of the Holy House by Nebuchadnezzar and the Christians, as it was mentioned that they invaded the Children of Israel with some of their kings - it was said: his name was Natus bin Espisanos the Roman, according to what Al-Ghaznawi mentioned - so they killed and took captive, burned the Torah, and threw filth into the Holy House and destroyed it. It is a metaphor, like the polytheists preventing the Muslims when they prevented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from entering the Sacred Mosque. In general, preventing the mosques from being used for prayer and displaying the symbols of Islam in them is destructive to them. Fourth: Our scholars said: This is why we said that it is not permissible to prevent a woman from performing Hajj if it is necessary, whether she has a mahram or not. She is also not prevented from praying in the mosques unless she fears temptation. Likewise, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not prevent the female servants of God from the mosques of God. That is why we said: It is not permissible to demolish, sell, or disuse a mosque, even if the neighborhood is ruined. The construction of mosques is not prohibited unless they intend to cause discord and disagreement, such as building a mosque next to or near it, intending thereby to separate the people of the first mosque and cause ruin and division of opinion. The second mosque is demolished and its construction is prohibited. That is why we said: It is not permissible for there to be two mosques in a city, nor for one mosque to have two imams, nor for two congregations to pray in a mosque. All of this will be further explained in Surat Bara’ah, God willing. In An-Noor, there is a ruling on mosques and their construction, God willing. The verse also indicates the importance of prayer, and that since it is the best of deeds and the greatest in reward, preventing it is a greater sin. Fifth: Every place where God can be worshipped and prostrated to is called a mosque. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The earth has been made for me a place of prostration and purification, narrated by the Imams. The nation is unanimously agreed that if a spot or area beyond it is designated for prayer by word, it is removed from the group of properties reserved for its owner and becomes common to all Muslims. So if a man builds a mosque in his house and reserves it for the people and keeps it for himself, it remains his property and does not go beyond the limits of being a mosque. But if he permits it to all people, its ruling is the same as that of all public mosques, and it is removed from the specificity of properties. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Those are not to enter it except in fear. Those is the subject and what follows is its predicate. Fearing is a state, meaning if the Muslims take control of it and it comes under their authority, then the disbeliever will not be able to enter it. But if they enter it, it is out of fear that the Muslims will expel them and discipline them for entering it. And in this is evidence that the disbeliever is not allowed to enter the mosque under any circumstances, as will come in Bara’ah, God willing. And whoever attributed the verse to the Christians narrated that a period of time passed after Umar built the Holy House in Islam, and no Christian entered it except that he was severely beaten after it had been their place of worship. And whoever attributed it to the Quraysh said: Thus was the command of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, proclaimed: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no one shall circumambulate the House naked. It was said: It is good and its purpose is to command, i.e. fight them and eradicate them until none of them enters the Sacred Mosque except in fear, like his saying: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God, for it is a prohibition and the wording of the report was transmitted. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: For them in this world is disgrace. It was said that killing is for the combatant, and the jizya is for the dhimmi, according to Qatada. Al-Suddi: The disgrace for them in this world is the rise of the Mahdi, and the conquest of Amorium, Rumayyah, Constantinople, and other cities of theirs, according to what we mentioned in the Book of Remembrance. And whoever attributed it to the Quraysh attributed the disgrace to them in the conquest, and the punishment in the Hereafter for whoever among them died as a disbeliever.
2:115: It has five issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: To God belong the East and the West. The East is the place of sunrise and the West is the place of sunset, meaning that they are His and everything between them of directions and creatures through creation and invention, as mentioned above. He singled them out for mention and addition to Him as an honor, like: the House of God, and the she-camel of God, and because the reason for the verse required that, as will come. The second: The Almighty’s saying: So wherever you turn is a condition, and therefore the letter nun was deleted, and ayn is the operator, and ma is redundant, and the answer is then there is the face of God. Al-Hasan read tawlawu with the opening of the ta and the lam, and the original is tattawlawu. And thumma is in the accusative case as an adverb, and its meaning is distance, except that it is built on the opening and is not declined because it is ambiguous, it is like there for distance, but if you mean closeness, you say here. Third: The scholars differed regarding the meaning of Wherever you turn in five statements: Abdullah bin Aamer bin Rabi’ah said: It was revealed regarding someone who prays in a direction other than the qiblah on a dark night. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on his authority on the authority of his father, who said: “We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey on a dark night, and we did not know where the qiblah was, so each of us prayed separately. When morning came, we mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this verse was revealed: ‘So wherever you turn, there is the face of God.’” Abu Eisa said: This hadith has a weak chain of transmission. We do not know it except from the hadith of Ash'ath al-Samman, and Ash'ath ibn Sa'id Abu al-Rabi' is considered weak in hadith. Most scholars have held this view. They said: If someone prays in the clouds, not facing the qiblah, then it becomes clear to him later that he prayed not facing the qiblah, then his prayer is valid. This is what Sufyan, Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq say. I said: This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and Malik, except that Malik said: It is recommended for him to repeat it in time, and it is not obligatory for him, because he has performed his obligation as he was commanded, and the completion is made up in time, based on the Sunnah of the one who prayed alone and then caught up with that prayer in its time in a group, that he repeats it with them, and he does not repeat it in time as recommended except for the one who turned his back to the qiblah or to the east or west, very diligently, and as for the one who turned to the right or to the left a little, diligently, he does not have to repeat it in time or otherwise. Al-Mughira and Al-Shafi’i said: It does not suffice for him, because the qiblah is a condition of the prayer. What Malik said is more correct, because the direction of the qiblah permits necessity to leave it in combat, and the concession also permits it in the case of travel. Ibn ‘Umar said: It was revealed about the traveler who performs voluntary prayers wherever his mount faces. Muslim narrated it from him, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray while he was coming from Mecca to Medina on his mount, wherever he was facing.” He said: And in this regard, ‘Wherever you turn, there is the Face of God’ was revealed. There is no disagreement among scholars regarding the permissibility of performing voluntary prayers on a mount, based on this hadith and similar hadiths. It is not permissible for anyone to intentionally abandon the qiblah in any way, except in cases of extreme fear, as will come. Malik's opinion differed regarding a sick person praying on his camel. Once he said: He should not pray an obligatory prayer on the back of a camel, even if his illness is severe. Sahnun said: If he does so, he should repeat it. Al-Baji narrated it. And another time he said: If he is one of those who does not pray on the ground except by gestures, then he should pray on the camel after it is stopped for him and he faces the qiblah. They agreed that it is not permissible for a healthy person to pray an obligatory prayer except on the ground, except in cases of extreme fear in particular, as will be explained. The jurists differed regarding the traveler on a journey in which the prayer is not shortened. Malik and his companions and al-Thawri said: He does not perform voluntary prayers on a mount except on a journey in which the prayer is shortened. They said: Because the journeys in which it was narrated that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) performed voluntary prayers were those in which the prayer is shortened. Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifah and their companions, al-Hasan ibn Hayy, al-Layth ibn Sa’d and Dawud ibn Ali said: It is permissible to perform voluntary prayers on a mount outside the city in any journey, regardless of whether the prayer is shortened or not, because the narrations do not specify one journey from another, so it is permissible in any journey, unless a particular journey is specified for something that must be submitted to. Abu Yusuf said: He prays in the city on the mount by gesturing, based on the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa’id on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that he prayed on a donkey in the alleys of Madinah, gesturing by gesturing. Al-Tabari said: It is permissible for every rider or pedestrian, whether present or traveling, to perform voluntary prayers on his mount or on his feet by gesturing. It was narrated from some of the companions of Al-Shafi’i that their school of thought was that it is permissible to offer voluntary prayers on an animal while at home and while traveling. Al-Athram said: Ahmad ibn Hanbal was asked about praying on an animal while at home, so he said: As for traveling, I have heard it, but I have not heard it while at home. Ibn Al-Qasim said: Whoever offers voluntary prayers on his mount, he offers voluntary prayers while sitting, standing cross-legged, bowing, placing his hands on his knees, then raising his head. Qatada said: It was revealed about Al-Najashi, and it is as if: When he died, the Prophet (peace be upon him) called the Muslims to pray for him outside of Medina. They said, How can we pray for a man who died while he was praying towards a direction other than ours? The Negus, the king of Abyssinia, whose name was Ashamah, which is Atiyah in Arabic, used to pray towards Jerusalem until he died. The direction of prayer was changed to the Kaaba, so the verse was revealed, and it was about him: And indeed, among the People of the Scripture is he who believes in God. This was an excuse for the Negus. The Prophet (peace be upon him) led his companions in prayer in the ninth year of the Hijra. This was used as evidence by those who permitted praying for the dead, namely Al-Shafi’i. Ibn Al-Arabi said: “One of the strangest issues regarding praying for the dead is what Al-Shafi’i said: ‘Pray for the dead is offered in absentia.’ I was in Baghdad in the assembly of Imam Fakhr Al-Islam, and a man from Khurasan would enter and say to him, ‘How is so-and-so?’ He would say, ‘He has died.’ He would say, ‘To God we belong and to Him we shall return!’ Then he would say to us, ‘Stand up, so that I may lead you in prayer.’ So he would stand up and pray for him with us. This was after a period of six months, and between him and his country there were a year and months.” The basis for this, according to them, is the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) prayer for the Negus. Our scholars may God have mercy on them said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) is specifically mentioned in this for three reasons: One of them: The earth was spread out for him to the south and north until he saw the coffin of the Negus, just as it was spread out for him to the north and south until he saw the Al-Aqsa Mosque. The opponent said: What is the benefit in seeing it? The benefit is in attaining its blessing. Second: The Negus did not have a faithful guardian there to pray over him. The opponent said: This is normally impossible! A king with a religion that has no followers, and interpreting it as impossible is impossible. Third: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only intended by praying over the Negus to bring mercy upon him and to reconcile the rest of the kings after him if they saw that he was being cared for, alive and dead. The opponent said: The blessing of the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others reaches the dead by consensus. Ibn al-Arabi said: What I have regarding the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayer over the Negus is that he knew that the Negus and those who believed with him did not have any trace of the Sunnah of praying over the dead, so he knew that they would bury him without praying, so he hastened to pray over him. I said: The first interpretation is better, because if he saw him, he would not have prayed for someone who was absent, but rather he would have prayed for someone who was seen and present, and the absent is that which is not seen. And God Almighty knows best. The fourth statement: Ibn Zayd said: The Jews approved of the Prophet’s prayer, may God bless him and grant him peace, facing Jerusalem, and they said: He was only guided by us. So when he turned to the Kaaba, the Jews said: What turned them away from their qiblah that they were facing? So this verse was revealed: And to God belongs the East and the West. The basis of the system according to this statement is that when the Jews denied the matter of the qiblah, God Almighty explained that He has the right to command His servants to worship as He wishes. If He wishes, He commands them to face Jerusalem, and if He wishes, He commands them to face the Kaaba, they do so. There is no proof against Him, and He is not questioned about what He does, but they are questioned. The fifth statement: That the verse was abrogated by the statement: And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it, as mentioned by Ibn Abbas. So it seems that it was permissible at the beginning for a person to pray however he wished, then that was abrogated. Qatada said: The abrogating statement is the statement of God Almighty: So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram, meaning toward it. This was narrated by Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi. Sixth statement: It was narrated from Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak that it is decisive, meaning: Wherever you are in the East or West, there is the Face of God which He has commanded us to face, which is the Kaaba. Also from Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr, when the verse Call upon Me; I will respond to you was revealed, they said: To where? So it was revealed: So wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. And from Ibn Umar and An-Nakha’i: Wherever you turn in your travels and your departures, there is the Face of God. It was said: It is connected to the verse of God the Almighty: And who is more unjust than he who prevents the mosques of God from being mentioned therein? The verse, so the meaning is that the lands of God, O believers, are sufficient for you, so do not let the destruction of those who destroyed mosques prevent you from turning your faces towards the Qiblah of God wherever you are in His land. It was said: It was revealed when the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, was prevented from entering the House in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and the Muslims were distressed by that. So these are ten statements. Whoever considers it abrogated, there is no objection to him on the grounds that it is report, because it is possible for the meaning of a command. It is possible that the meaning of Wherever you turn, there is the face of God is: Turn your faces toward the face of God. This is the verse that Saeed bin Jubair, may God have mercy on him, recited when he ordered Al-Hajjaj to slaughter him on the ground. Fourth: People differed in the interpretation of the face attributed to God the Most High in the Qur’an and Sunnah. The experts said: This refers to existence, and the expression of the face is a metaphor for speech, if the face is the most visible and most important of the limbs in the witness. Ibn Furak said: The description of a thing may be mentioned and what is meant by it is the described by extension, as when someone says: I saw the knowledge of so-and-so today, and I looked at his knowledge, what he means by that is I saw the scholar and I looked at the scholar. Likewise if the face is mentioned here and what is meant is the one who has the face, meaning faces. Based on this, the statement of God the Most High: We feed you only for the sake of God is interpreted because what is meant by it is God who has the face. Likewise, His statement: Except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High means the one who has the face. Ibn Abbas said: The face is an expression of Him, the Most High, as He said: And the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor, will remain. Some of the imams said: This is an attribute established by hearing in addition to what the minds require of the attributes of the Eternal, the Most High. Ibn Atiyyah said: Abu al-Ma’ali weakened this statement, and it is also weak, and what is meant is His existence. It was said: What is meant by the face here is the direction towards which we face, that is, the qiblah. It was also said: The face is the intention, as the poet said: I ask God for forgiveness for a sin that I cannot count. Lord of the servants, to Him belongs the face and the work. It was said: The meaning is that there is the pleasure and reward of God, as He said: We feed you only for the sake of God, meaning for His pleasure and the goodness of His reward. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever builds a mosque seeking thereby the Face of God, God will build for him the like of it in Paradise. And His statement: “On the Day of Resurrection, sealed scrolls will be brought and placed before God the Most High. He will say to His angels, ‘Throw this down and accept this.’ The angels will say, ‘By Your glory, O our Lord, we have seen nothing but good.’ And He knows best. He will say, ‘This was done for other than My sake, and I do not accept any deed except that which was done purely for My sake.’” This was narrated by Ad-Daraqutni. It was said that what is meant is, ‘Then there is God,’ and ‘Facing’ is a connection, and it is like His statement, ‘And He is with you.’” This was said by Al-Kalbi and Al-Qutbi, and something similar is the statement of the Mu’tazilah. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is All-Encompassing and Knowing. That is, He is generous to His servants in their religion, and He does not burden them with what is beyond their capacity. It was said: Vast means that His knowledge encompasses everything, as He said: His knowledge encompasses all things. Al-Farra’ said: Vast is the Generous One whose giving encompasses all things, as evidenced by the Almighty’s saying: And My mercy encompasses all things. It was also said: Vast in forgiveness, meaning no sin is too great for Him. It was also said: He is generous to His servants and independent of their deeds. It is said: So-and-so is generous to what is asked, meaning he is not stingy. God the Almighty said: Let the one with an abundance spend from his abundance, meaning let the rich spend from what God has given him. We have already mentioned this in the Most Sublime Book, and praise be to God.
2:116: God Almighty says: “And they say, ‘God has taken a son.’ Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.” There are five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And they say, ‘God has taken a son.’ This is a report about the Christians in their saying that the Messiah is the son of God. It was also said about the Jews in their saying that Ghazir is the son of God. It was also said about the infidel Arabs in their saying that the angels are daughters of God. Similar reports have come from the ignorant infidels about Mary and the prophets. The second: His saying: Glory be to Him! Rather, to Him belongs the verse. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God Almighty said: The son of Adam denied Me, although he had no right to do so, and he insulted Me, although he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his claiming that I am not able to restore him as he was, and as for his insulting Me, it is his saying that I have a son. So glory be to Me that I should take a wife or a son.” Third: Subhan is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, and its meaning is exoneration, sanctification, and avoidance, from their saying: God took a son. Rather, He is God, the Most High, One in His Essence, One in His Attributes. He did not give birth, so He would need a companion. How could He have a son when He has no companion and He created all things? He did not give birth, so He would be preceded. He is exalted and glorified above what the wrongdoers and deniers say, far above! Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. What is raised by the subject and the predicate in the genitive, meaning that all of that is His by creation and invention. And the one who says that He took a son is included in the heavens and the earth. It was previously mentioned that the meaning of Subhan God is: God’s innocence from evil. Fourth: The son can only be of the same kind as the father. How can the Truth, glory be to Him, take a son from among His creatures when nothing resembles Him? He said: There is none in the heavens and earth but comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. Just as He said here: Rather, to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Sonship requires genus and occurrence, and eternity requires oneness and permanence. He, glory be to Him, is the Eternal, the One, the Unique, the Self-Sufficient, who neither begets nor was begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. Moreover, sonship contradicts slavery and servitude—as will be explained in Surah Maryam, God willing—so how can a son be a servant! This is impossible, and what leads to the impossible is impossible. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: All are obedient to Him is a subject and predicate, and the meaning is for them, then the ha’ and the mim were deleted. Obedient means obedient and submissive, so all creatures are obedient to God, meaning they submit and obey. And the obedience of inanimate objects is in the manifestation of creation over them and in them. So obedience is obedience, and silence is from it the saying of Zaid bin Arqam: We used to talk during prayer, a man would talk to his companion next to him until the verse: And stand before God, obedient, was revealed, so we were commanded to be silent and forbidden from speaking. And silence is prayer, the poet said: Obedient to God, reciting His Book and deliberately separating himself from people Al-Suddi and others said regarding his statement: Everyone is devoutly obedient to Him, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan said: Everyone who stands by the testimony that he is a servant. And the root of qunut in the language is standing, and from it comes the hadith: The best prayer is the one that is prolonged in qunut, said Al-Zajjaj. So people are obedient, meaning they perform servitude, either by acknowledging it or by doing otherwise. So the effect of creation is clear to them. It was said: Its origin is obedience, and from that is the saying of God Almighty: and the obedient men and women. This will be further explained in His saying, God Almighty: And stand before God, obedient.
2:117: It has six issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Originator of the heavens is a superlative form of fa’il, and it is raised as a predicate of an omitted subject, and the active participle is mubdi’, like seer from mubsi’r. You innovated something without an example, so God Almighty is the Originator of the heavens and the earth, meaning their Creator, Inventor, Maker, and Inventor without limit or example. And whoever innovates something that no one has ever done before is called an innovator, and from this are the people of innovations. Innovation is called innovation because its speaker innovated it without the action or statement of an imam, and in Bukhari: And what an excellent innovation this is, meaning the standing in Ramadan. Second: Every innovation that comes from a created being must have a basis in the Shari’ah or not. If it has a basis, it falls under the generality of what God has commanded and urged His Messenger to do, so it is praiseworthy. If its example does not exist, such as a type of generosity, liberality, or doing good, then his action is a praiseworthy action, even if the doer has not done it before. This is supported by the statement of ‘Umar may God be pleased with him: “This is a good innovation, because it is a good action and falls within the scope of praise. Even though the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) performed it, he left it and did not maintain it or gather the people to do it.” So ‘Umar’s may God be pleased with him maintaining it, gathering the people to do it, and urging them to do it is an innovation, but it is a praiseworthy and commendable innovation. If it is contrary to what God and His Messenger have commanded, then it is blameworthy and denounced. Al-Khattabi and others said the same. I said: This is the meaning of what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon: The worst of matters are their innovations, and every innovation is misguidance. He means what does not agree with the Book or the Sunnah, or the actions of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. He explained this by saying: “Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam will have the reward for it and the reward of those who act upon it after him, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. And whoever establishes a bad practice in Islam will bear its burden and the burden of those who act upon it after him, without that detracting from their burden in the slightest.” This is an indication of what has been innovated, good or bad, and it is the basis of this topic. And with God is protection and success, there is no god but Him. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. That is, when He wants to perfect and complete it - as previously mentioned in His knowledge - He says to it, Be. Ibn Arafa said: The decree of something is its perfection, its implementation, and its completion. The judge is called this because when he rules, he has completed what is between the two opponents. Al-Azhari said: The word qada in the language has several meanings, referring to the cessation and completion of something. Abu Dhu’ayb said: And upon them are two chains of narration, which David ruled or the making of the chains of narration. Al-Shamakh said about Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him: I did things and then left with calamities in my sleeves that have not yet been solved Our scholars said: The word qada is a common word that means creation. God the Almighty said: So He completed them as seven heavens in two days meaning He created them. It can also mean informing, God the Almighty said: And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book meaning He informed us. It can also mean ordering, as in His saying: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him. It can also mean imposing and enforcing rulings, and from this the ruler is called a judge. It can also mean fulfilling the right, as in His saying: So when Moses had fulfilled the term Qadi. It can also mean will, as in His saying: So when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is meaning when He wants to create something. Ibn Atiyyah said: The meaning of qada is that He has decreed, and it can also mean He has passed, and both meanings are applicable in this verse according to the doctrine of the Sunnis: He has decreed in eternity and passed it. According to the doctrine of the Mu’tazila, He passed it upon creation and bringing into existence. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: A matter. The matter is one of matters, and it is not a source of the verb to command. Our scholars said: The matter in the Qur’an is used in fourteen ways. First: Religion. God Almighty said: Until the truth came and the command of God became apparent, meaning the religion of God, Islam. The second: The statement, including the Almighty’s saying: So when Our command comes, meaning Our statement, and His saying: And they disputed their affair among themselves, meaning their statement. Third: Punishment, including the Almighty’s saying: When the matter has been decided, meaning when the punishment of the people of Hell has become obligatory. Fourth: Jesus, peace be upon him. God Almighty said: When He decrees a matter, meaning Jesus, and he knew that he would be without a father. Fifth: The killing at Badr. God Almighty said: So when the command of God comes meaning the killing at Badr. And God Almighty said: That God may accomplish a matter which was to be done meaning the killing of the infidels of Mecca. Sixth: The conquest of Mecca. God Almighty said: Then wait until God brings about His command, meaning the conquest of Mecca. Seventh: The killing of Qurayzah and the expulsion of Banu Nadir. God Almighty said: So pardon and overlook until God brings about His command. Eighth: The Resurrection. God Almighty said: The command of God has come. Ninth: Judgment. God Almighty said: He directs the affair. Meaning judgment. Tenth: Revelation. God Almighty said: He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth. He says: Revelation descends from heaven to earth, and his saying: The command descends between them means revelation. Eleventh: The matter of creation. God Almighty said: Unquestionably, to God do all matters return, meaning the matters of creation. Twelfth: Victory. God Almighty said: They say, ‘Do we have any part in the matter?’ They mean victory. Say, ‘Indeed, the whole matter belongs to God.’ Meaning victory. Thirteenth: Sin. God Almighty said: So she tasted the evil consequences of her deed, meaning the punishment for her sin. Fourteenth: The affair and the action. God Almighty said: And Pharaoh’s command was not right, meaning his action and affair. And He said: So let those beware who dissent from his command, meaning his action. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Be. It was said: The kaf is from His being, and the nun is from His light, and it is what is meant by His saying, peace be upon him: I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from the evil of what He has created. It is also narrated: In the perfect word of God in the singular. So the plural is because this word is in all matters, so if He says to every matter, Be, and to every thing, Be, then they are words. Evidence for this is what was narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what is narrated on the authority of God Almighty: My gift is speech and my punishment is speech. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi in a long hadith. The word in the singular also means words, but when the single word is dispersed in matters at times, it becomes words and their reference is to one word. It is called complete because the minimum speech according to the linguists is three letters: a letter that begins, a letter that fills the word, and a letter that is left blank. If it is two letters, then it is considered defective, like kid, “dam,” and mouth. It is only defective for a reason. From the human beings, it is among the defective because it is two letters, and because it is a word pronounced with tools. From our Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, it is complete because it is without tools. He is Exalted above resembling created beings. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: So it is was read with the nun raised as a resumption. Sibawayh said: So it is or then it is. Another said: It is conjoined with ‘says’, so according to the first, it is “being after the command, even if it is non-existent, then it is like something that exists, since it is known to Him, as will be explained. According to the second, it is being with the command, and Al-Tabari chose it and said: His command to the thing with but does not precede existence nor does it come after it, so the thing is not commanded to exist except that it exists with the command, nor does it exist except that it is commanded to exist, as will be explained. He said: “And similar to it is the people rising from their graves, it does not precede the supplication of God nor come after it, as He said: “Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will emerge.” Ibn Atiyyah weakened this statement and said: It is a mistake in terms of meaning, because it requires that the statement is with creation and existence. The summary of the belief in this verse is: God Almighty has always been commanding non-existent things on condition of their existence, capable even though the capabilities are delayed, and knowledgeable even though the information is delayed. So everything in the verse that requires the future is according to the commands, since the new things come after they did not exist. And everything that is attributed to God Almighty of power and knowledge is eternal and has always existed. And the meaning required by the phrase Be is eternal and self-existent. Abu al-Hasan al-Mawardi said: If it is said: In what state does He say to it, Be, and it is? In a state of nonexistence, or in a state of existence? If it is in a state of nonexistence, it is impossible for Him to command anyone except one who is commanded, just as it is impossible for a command to be from anyone except one who commands. And if it is in a state of existence, then that is a state in which it is not permissible for Him to command existence and occurrence, because He is an existing and occurring entity. Three answers have been given to this question: One of them: It is report from God Almighty about the influence of His commands on His existing creation, just as He commanded the Children of Israel to be despised apes, and this is not applicable to the creation of non-existent things. Second: God Almighty knows what is before it came into being. So the things that did not exist and existed were, by His knowledge before they came into being, similar to those that exist. So it is permissible for Him to say to them: Be, and to command them to emerge from a state of nonexistence into a state of existence, because all of them are conceived by Him and because He knows them in a state of nonexistence. Third: That this is general report from God Almighty about everything that He creates and brings into being if He wills to create and establish it, it will be and exist without there being a statement that He says, but rather it is a decree that He wills, so He expressed it with a statement even though it is not a statement, like the saying of Abu al-Najm: The belly button said the truth There is no statement there, but he meant that the back has joined the stomach, as Amr bin Juma Al-Dawsi said: So I became like an eagle whose young ones fly away. When it wants to fly, it says to it, Qu’a. As the other said: His wings said to his legs, Go on, and save your flesh from being torn apart.
2:118: The Almighty said: And those who do not know said Ibn Abbas said: They are the Jews. Mujahid: The Christians, and Al-Tabari preferred it, because they are the ones mentioned in the verse first. Al-Rabi', Al-Suddi and Qatada said: The polytheists of the Arabs. And lawla means why not as an incitement, as Al-Ashhab bin Ramila said: You consider the hamstring of the camel to be your greatest glory, Bani Dhutri, if it were not for the masked Al-Kami. This is not lawla which prevents something due to the existence of something else. The difference between them according to linguists is that lawla means incitement and is only followed by a verb, whether explicit or implied, while lawla for impossibility is followed by the beginning, and it is customary to delete the predicate. The meaning of the speech is “why does God not speak to us about the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that we know that he is a prophet and we believe in him, or he brings us a sign that is a sign of his prophethood.” The sign is the indication and mark, and it has been mentioned before. Those before them are the Jews and Christians according to the one who made those who do not know the Jews and Christians, or the Jews according to the one who made those who do not know the Christians. Their hearts are alike It was said: in the difficulty and suggestion and abandonment of faith. Al-Farra’ said: Their hearts are alike in their agreement on disbelief. We have made clear the verses for a people who are certain previously mentioned.
2:119: The Almighty said: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings. “Bishara” is in the accusative case as a state, and nadhir is in apposition to it, and their meanings have already been presented. And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire. Muqatil said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If God had sent down His punishment on the Jews, they would have believed, so God revealed: And do not ask about the companions of Hellfire, raising the word tas’al, which is the reading of the majority, and it is in the place of a state in apposition to a bringer of good tidings and a warner. The meaning is: We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, not questioned. Sa’id al-Akhfash said: And do not ask with the opening of the ta’ and the damma of the lam, and it is in the place of a state in apposition to a bringer of good tidings and a warner. The meaning is: We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, not questioning about them, because God’s knowledge of their disbelief after warning them makes it unnecessary for Him to ask about them. This is the meaning of not questioned. The meaning of not questioned is that he who disbelieves after being given good tidings and warning will not be held accountable for their disbelief. Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day: ‘I wish I knew what happened to my parents.’” So this verse was revealed, and this is according to the reading of those who read and do not ask in the subjunctive mood, which is a reading that is a negation alone, and there are two views on it: One of them: He forbade asking about those who disobeyed and disbelieved among the living, because their condition may change and they may move from disbelief to faith, and from disobedience to obedience. The second: and it is more apparent, that he forbade asking about someone who died in his disbelief and sin, to magnify his situation and to make his status more severe. This is like saying: Do not ask about so-and-so, meaning he has reached beyond what you think. Ibn Mas`ud read: And you will not ask. And my father read: And you will not ask. And their meaning is in agreement with the reading of the majority, denying that he will be asked about them. It was said: He only asked about which of his parents had died, so this was revealed. We mentioned in the Book of Remembrance that God the Most High revived his father and mother and they believed in him, and we mentioned his saying, peace be upon him, to the man: Your father and my father are in Hell. We have explained that, and praise be to God.
2:120: . The Almighty said: And never will the Jews or the Christians be pleased with you until you follow their religion. There are two issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And never will the Jews or the Christians be pleased with you until you follow their religion. The meaning is: Their aim, O Muhammad, is not to believe in the signs they suggest, but if you bring them everything they ask for, they will not be pleased with you.
