Rather, what will please them is to abandon your Islam and follow them. It is said: Radi yirdi riddan wa riddan wa ridwanan wa ridwanan wa ridaat, and it is from the words with waw. It is also said in the dual: ridwan, and Al-Kisa’i reported: ridyan. It was reported that ridha is extended, and it is as if it is the source of radi yirdi radhaat wa ridaat. And tataba’ is accusative with an, but it does not appear with hatta, as Al-Khalil said. This is because hatta is a prepositional phrase for a noun, like his saying: until the break of dawn. And what works on a noun does not work on a verb at all, and what prepositional phrases a noun does not presume anything. An-Nahhas said: tataba’ is accusative with hatta, and hatta is a substitute for an. And the religion: is the name for what God has legislated for His servants in His books and on the tongues of His messengers. So the religion and the law were the same, but as for religion, he differentiated between it and the religion and the law, because the religion and the law are what God called His servants to do, and religion is what the servants did based on His command. Second: A group of scholars, including Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i, Dawud, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, held fast to this verse, arguing that all disbelief is one religion, based on the Almighty’s saying: their religion, thus unifying the religion, and the Almighty’s saying: To you be your religion, and to me mine, and the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: People of two religions do not inherit from each other, meaning Islam and disbelief, as evidenced by his saying, peace be upon him: A Muslim does not inherit from an infidel. Malik and Ahmad, in the other narration, said that infidelity is a religion, so a Jew does not inherit from a Christian, nor do they inherit from a Zoroastrian, taking the apparent meaning of his, peace be upon him, saying: People of two religions do not inherit from each other. As for the Almighty’s statement: their religion, what is meant by it is the majority, even though it is unified in wording, as evidenced by its addition to the pronoun of majority, as you say: I took from the scholars of the people of Medina, for example, their knowledge, and I heard their hadith, meaning their knowledge and their hadiths. God Almighty says: “Say: ‘Indeed, the guidance of God is the [only] guidance.’” The meaning is that what you are upon, O Muhammad, of the true guidance of God that He places in the heart of whomever He wills is the true guidance, not what these people claim. God the Almighty said: And if you were to follow their desires. Desires is the plural of hawwa, just as you say jamal and ajmal. Since they are different, they are pluralized. If it had been applied to the individuals of the religion, He would have said their desires. There are two aspects to this address: One of them is that it is for the Messenger, because the address is directed to him. The second is that it is for the Messenger, and what is meant by it is his nation. According to the first, there is a lesson in it for his nation, since their status is lower than his. The reason for the verse is that they were asking for peace and a truce, and they promised the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Islam. So God informed him that they would not be pleased with him until he followed their religion, and He commanded him to fight them. God the Almighty says: From knowledge. Ahmad ibn Hanbal was asked about someone who says: The Qur’an is created. He said: He is an infidel. It was said: Why do you consider him an infidel? He said: Because of verses from the Book of God the Almighty: And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, and the Qur’an is from God’s knowledge. So whoever claims that it is created has committed infidelity.
2:121: God Almighty says: “Those to whom We have given the Scripture recite it with its true recitation. Those believe in it. But whoever disbelieves in it - then it is those who are the losers.”
2:122: God Almighty says: O Children of Israel, remember My favor which I bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds.
2:123: The Almighty said: Those to whom We gave the Scripture. Qatada said: They are the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Scripture according to this interpretation is the Qur'an. Ibn Zayd said: They are those who converted to Islam from the Children of Israel. The Scripture according to this interpretation is the Torah, and the verse is yes. And those who are raised by the beginning, We gave them its connection, recite it is the predicate of the beginning, and if you wish, the predicate is those believe in it. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of recite it as it should be recited. It was said: They follow it as it should be followed, by following the commands and prohibitions, making lawful what it makes lawful and making unlawful what it makes unlawful, and acting in accordance with what it includes. This was said by Ikrimah. Ikrimah said: Have you not heard the statement of God the Most High: And the moon when it follows it, meaning follows it, and this is the meaning of the statement of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with them. The poet said: I made my bucket fill me Nasr bin Issa narrated on the authority of Malik on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Omar on the authority of: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in the words of God the Almighty: They recite it with its true recitation: They follow it with its true following. Its chain of transmission includes more than one unknown narrator, as mentioned by Al-Khatib Abu Bakr Ahmad, but its meaning is correct. Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari said: Whoever follows the Qur’an will descend with him to the gardens of Paradise. And on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him: They are those who, when they pass by a verse of mercy, ask God for it, and when they pass by a verse of torment, seek refuge from it. This meaning has been narrated: “On the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): When he passed by a verse of mercy, he would ask, and when he passed by a verse of torment, he would seek refuge.” Al-Hasan said: They are those who act according to its clear verses, believe in its ambiguous verses, and leave whatever is unclear to its scholar. And it was said: They recite it with its true recitation. I said: There is some distance in this, unless the meaning is that they recite its words and understand its meanings, for by understanding the meanings, the one who is guided is followed.
2:124: It contains twenty issues: First: When the Kaaba and the Qiblah were mentioned, this was connected to the mention of Abraham, peace be upon him, and that he was the one who built the House. So it was the right of the Jews - who are descendants of Abraham - not to be averse to his religion. And the trial is the test and examination, and its meaning is something distant. And the interpretation of Abraham in Syriac, according to what Al-Mawardi mentioned, and in Arabic, according to what Ibn Atiyah mentioned, is: a merciful father. Al-Suhayli said: And often there is agreement between Syriac and Arabic, or something close to it in pronunciation. Don’t you see that the interpretation of Abraham is a merciful father, for his mercy towards children, and for that reason he and his wife Sarah were made guardians of the children of the believers who die young until the Day of Resurrection. I said: What indicates this is what Al-Bukhari included in the long hadith of the vision on the authority of Samurah, in which it says: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Abraham, peace be upon him, in the Rawdah, surrounded by the children of the people.” We have mentioned this in the Book of Remembrance, and praise be to God. This Abraham is the son of Tarikh bin Nakhur, according to some historians. In the revelation: And when Abraham said to his father Azar, and also in Sahih al-Bukhari, and there is no contradiction in that, as will come in Al-An’am, God willing. He had four sons: Ishmael, Isaac, Midian, and Mada’in, as mentioned by Al-Suhayli. It was presented before the subject for emphasis, since the fact that the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, is the tester is known, and the fact that the object pronoun in Arabic is connected to the subject necessitates the object being presented, so the speech was built on this emphasis, so be aware of it. The common people read Abraham in the accusative, and his Lord in the nominative, as we mentioned. It was narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Zaid that he read it the opposite, and he claimed that Ibn Abbas read it likewise. The meaning is that Abraham called upon his Lord and asked, and there is some distance in it, because of the preposition with in His statement with words. The second: The Almighty’s saying: with words. Words is the plural of word, and its realization goes back to the speech of the Almighty, but He expressed it in terms of the functions that Abraham, peace be upon him, was charged with. And since it was charged with speech, it was called by it, just as Jesus was called a word, because it was issued from a word, which is Be. And naming something by its introduction is one of the two divisions of metaphor, as Ibn al-Arabi said. Third: The scholars differed regarding what is meant by the words, with some sayings: One of them is the laws of Islam, which are thirty shares, ten of them in Surat Bara’ah: The repentant worshippers to the end, and ten in al-Ahzab 33:Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women to the end, and ten in al-Mu’minun 23:The believers have succeeded to His saying: They maintain their prayers and His saying in A questioner asked “Except those who pray” to His saying: And those who maintain their prayers. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: God did not test anyone with them and he fulfilled them all except Ibrahim, peace be upon him. He was tested with Islam and completed it, so God wrote for him the declaration of innocence, so He said: And Ibrahim who fulfilled. Some of them said: With the command and prohibition, and some of them said: With the slaughter of his son, and some of them said: With the fulfillment of the message, and the meaning is close. Mujahid said: It is the saying of God the Almighty: I am testing you with a matter, He said: Will you make me an imam for the people? He said: Yes. He said: And from my descendants? He said: My covenant will not include the wrongdoers. He said: Will you make the House a place of return for the people? He said: Yes. He said: And security? He said: Yes. He said: And show us our rites and accept our repentance? He said: Yes. He said: And provide its people with fruits? He said: Yes. According to this statement, it is God who completed. More authentic than this is what Abd al-Razzaq mentioned on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Ibn Tawus on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And when his Lord tested Abraham with commands, and he fulfilled them. He said: God tested him with purification, five for the head and five for the body: trimming the moustache, rinsing the mouth, sniffing water in the nose, using the siwak, and parting the hair. And for the body: trimming the nails, shaving the pubic hair, circumcision, plucking the armpit hair, and washing the place of defecation and urination with water. According to this statement, it is Abraham who completed, and it is the apparent meaning of the Qur’an. Matar narrated on the authority of Abu al-Jild that they are also ten, except that he made the place of parting the washing of the knuckles, and the place of istinja’ the removal of the pubic hair. Qatada said: They are the rituals of Hajj specifically. Al-Hasan: They are the six characteristics: the planet, the moon, the sun, fire, migration, and circumcision. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: These statements are not contradictory, because all of this was something that Abraham, peace be upon him, was tested with. I said: In Al-Muwatta’ and others, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, he heard Saeed bin Al-Musayyab say: Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to be circumcised, the first to host a guest, the first to shave, the first to cut his nails, the first to trim his moustache, and the first to grow grey hair. When he saw the grey hair, he said: What is this? He said: Dignity. He said: O Lord, increase my dignity. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Ibrahim on the authority of his father who said: The first to preach on the pulpit was Abraham, the friend of God. Another said: The first to cook tharid, the first to strike with the sword, the first to use a miswak, the first to clean oneself with water, and the first to wear trousers. Muadh bin Jabal narrated that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: If a pulpit is used, then my father Abraham used it. If a staff is used, then my father Abraham used it. I said: These are rulings that must be explained, understood, and discussed. The first of these is circumcision and what has been said about it, which is the issue: Fourth: The scholars agreed that Abraham, peace be upon him, was the first to be circumcised. There is disagreement about the age at which he was circumcised. In Al-Muwatta’, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission ending with him: He was one hundred and twenty years old, and he lived eighty years after that. Something like this cannot be an opinion. Al-Awza’i narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abraham, peace be upon him, was circumcised when he was one hundred and twenty years old, and he lived eighty years after that.” This was mentioned by Abu Omar. It was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, other than the narration of Yahya, from various sources: He was circumcised when he reached the age of eighty, and he was circumcised with an axe. This is in Sahih Muslim and others. Eighty years old. This is what is preserved in the hadith of Ibn Ajlan and the hadith of Al-A’raj on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ikrimah said: Ibrahim was circumcised when he was eighty years old. He said: No one circumambulated the House after that according to the religion of Ibrahim except one who was circumcised. This is what Ikrimah said, and Al-Musayyab bin Rafi’ said, as Al-Marwazi mentioned. Al-Qudum is narrated with a shaddah and a khafdah. Abu Al-Zinad said: Al-Qudum with a shaddah: a place. Fifth: The scholars differed regarding circumcision. The majority of them are of the confirmed Sunnahs and the fitrah of Islam, which men cannot neglect. A group said: It is obligatory, based on the words of God the Almighty: To follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth. Qatadah said: It is circumcision, and some of the Malikis tended towards this, and it is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i. Ibn Surayj provided evidence for its obligation by consensus on the prohibition of looking at the private parts, and he said: If circumcision were not obligatory, it would not have been permissible for a circumcised person to look at them. The response to this is that such a thing is permissible for the benefit of the body, such as the doctor’s examination, and medicine is not obligatory by consensus, as will be explained in An-Nahl, God willing. Some of our companions provided evidence for this by what Al-Hajjaj bin Artah narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Malih on the authority of his father on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Circumcision is a Sunnah for men and an honor for women. Al-Hajjaj is not one of those who can be cited as evidence. I said: The highest proof in this regard is the hadith of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: "There are five things that are part of the fitrah: circumcision"... the hadith, and it will come. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Atiyyah that a woman used to circumcise women in Madinah, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Do not go to extremes, for that is more sinful for the woman and more pleasing to the husband. Abu Dawud said: This hadith is weak and its narration is unknown. In a narration mentioned by Razin: And do not go to extremes, for that brightens the face and is more pleasing to the man. Sixth: If the boy is born circumcised, then the cost of circumcision has been spared. Al-Maymuni said: Ahmad said to me: There is a man here who had a circumcised boy born to him, and he was very sad about that, so I said to him: If God has spared you the cost, then what is your sadness about this? Seventh: Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: I was told by Ka’b al-Ahbar who said: Thirteen prophets were created circumcised: Adam, Seth, Idris, Noah, Sam, Lot, Joseph, Moses, Shu’ayb, Solomon, John, Jesus, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad ibn Habib al-Hashemi said: They are fourteen: Adam, Seth, Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, Shu’ayb, Joseph, Moses, Solomon, Zachariah, Jesus, Hanzala ibn Safwan the prophet of the companions of the message, and Muhammad, may God bless him and them all. I said: The narrations differed regarding the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Naim Al-Hafiz mentioned it in the book Al-Hilya with his chain of transmission. That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was born circumcised. Abu Omar narrated in Al-Tamhid: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ahmad told us, Muhammad bin Isa told us, Yahya bin Ayoub bin Badi Al-Alaaf told us, Muhammad bin Abi Al-Sarri Al-Asqalani told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Shuaib, on the authority of Ata Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That Abdul Muttalib circumcised the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on his seventh day, and held a banquet for him and named him Muhammad. Abu Omar said: This is a strange, chained hadith. Yahya bin Ayoub said: I sought this hadith but did not find it with any of the people of hadith who… I found it only with Ibn Abi Al-Sarri. Abu Omar said: It has been said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was born circumcised. Eighth: They differed as to when a boy should be circumcised. It was confirmed in the reports from a group of scholars that they said: Abraham circumcised Ishmael at the age of thirteen. And he circumcised his son Isaac at seven days. It was narrated from Fatima that she used to circumcise her son on the seventh day, but Malik denied that and said that it was the practice of the Jews. Ibn Wahb mentioned it from him. Al-Layth ibn Saad said: A boy should be circumcised between the ages of seven and ten. Ibn Wahb narrated something similar from Malik. Ahmad said: I did not hear anything about that. In Al-Bukhari, from Saeed ibn Hubair, he said: Ibn Abbas was asked: Who were you when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died? He said: I was circumcised on that day. He said: They did not circumcise a man until he reached puberty or was close to puberty. Scholars recommended that an old man who converts to Islam be circumcised. Ata’ used to say: His conversion to Islam is not complete until he is circumcised, even if he reaches the age of eighty. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he permitted an old man who converts to Islam not to be circumcised, and he saw no harm in that, nor in his testimony, his slaughter, his Hajj, or his prayer. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: The majority of scholars agree on this. The hadith of Buraydah regarding the Hajj of the uncircumcised is not proven. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Jabir ibn Zayd, and Ikrimah: The slaughter of the uncircumcised is not permissible and his testimony is not acceptable. Ninth: His saying: And the first to use a sharp blade. Sharpening means using iron to shave the pubic hair. Umm Salamah narrated: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, applied ointment, he would wipe his pubic hair with his hand.” Ibn Abbas narrated: “A man anointed himself with the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he reached his pubic area. Then he said to him: ‘Get away from me.’ Then he anointed himself with his hand.” Anas narrated: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not use an oven, and if his pubic hair grew too much, he would shave it.” Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: This indicates that most of what he did was shave, and he used an oven only rarely, so that it is correct to reconcile the two hadiths. Tenth: In trimming the nails. Trimming the nails means cutting them, and clippings are what is removed from them. Malik said: I prefer for women to trim their nails and shave their pubic hair as is the case for men. Al-Harith bin Maskeen and Sahnoon mentioned it on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim. Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim mentioned in his Nawader al-Usul the twenty-ninth principle: Umar bin Abi Umar told us, Ibrahim bin al-Ala’ al-Zubaidi told us on the authority of Umar bin Bilal al-Fazari, who said: I heard Abdullah bin Bishr al-Mazini say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Cut your nails, bury your clippings, clean your knuckles, brush your teeth, and do not bring in a dirty, dirty place. Then he spoke about it and did well. Al-Tirmidhi said: As for cutting the nails, it is because it scratches, scratches, and causes harm, and it collects dirt. So a person may become ritually impure and water does not reach the skin because of the dirt, so he is still ritually impure. And whoever becomes ritually impure and the area of a needle’s length on his body remains unwashed after washing, he is ritually impure and remains ritually impure until the washing covers his entire body. That is why he encouraged them to cut their nails. Athfar is the plural of athfur and athfar is the plural of nail. In the hadith of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when he forgot during his prayer, he said: “Why should I not be deceived while one of you has a nail between his fingertip and his fingernail, and one of you asks me about the heavens while there is ritual impurity and uncleanliness in his nails?” This hadith was mentioned by Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tabari al-Maruq al-Kiya in his Ahkam al-Quran, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Faraj Abu Wasil, who said: I came to Abu Ayyub, may God be pleased with him, and shook hands with him. He saw that my nails were long, so he said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him about the heavens, so he said: One of you comes asking about the report of the sky, and his nails are like the nails of birds, and dirt and dung collect in them. As for his saying: Bury your clippings. The body of the believer is sacred. Whatever falls from it and is removed from it, its preservation of sanctity remains. It is his right to bury it, just as if it died, it would be buried. If some of it dies, its sanctity is also maintained by burying it, so that it does not disperse or fall into the fire or into dirty garbage dumps. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded that his blood be buried where he was cupped so that dogs would not search for it. My father, may God have mercy on him, told us that Musa bin Ismail told us that Al-Hunayd bin Al-Qasim bin Abdul-Rahman bin Ma’iz told us that he heard Aamer bin Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr say that his father told him that he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was being cupped. When he finished, he said: O Abdullah, go with this blood and pour it out where no one can see you. When he left the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he took the blood and drank it. When he returned, he said: O Abdullah, what did you do with it? He said: I put it in the most hidden place, thinking it was hidden from the people. He said: Perhaps you drank it? He said: Yes. He said: Why did you drink the blood? Woe to the people from you and woe to you from the people. My father told me that Malik bin Sulayman Al-Harawi told us that Dawud bin Abdul-Rahman told us on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to order the burial of seven things from a person: hair, nails, blood, menstruation, teeth, foreskin, and placenta. As for his saying: Cleanse your knuckles. The knuckles are the wrinkles of the joints, and they are the place where the dirt singular knuckle meets, and it is the back of the node of each joint. The back of the node is called a knuckle, and what is between the two nodes is called a rajbah, and its plural is rawajib, and that is what is next to its back, and it is the shin of the finger. So every finger has two knuckles and three rajabs except for the thumb, which has a knuckle and two rajabs. So it is commanded to clean it so that it does not become dirty and the crime remains in it, and the dirt comes between the water and the skin. As for his saying: Clean your gums. The gum is one, and the gums are a group. It is the flesh above the teeth and below them, and it is their place of growth. The 'umur is the small amount of flesh between the teeth, and its singular is 'umr. So he ordered to clean it so that no food would remain in it, and the flavor would change and the smell would be unpleasant, and the two angels would be harmed, because it is the path of the Qur'an, and the seat of the two angels is at his canine tooth. It was narrated in the hadith in the words of God the Almighty: Not a word does he utter except that there is a watcher by him ready to record it. He said: At his canine tooth. Muhammad bin Ali Al-Shaqiqi told us that he heard my father mention that on the authority of Sufyan bin 'Uyaynah, and what he said was correct, because the utterance is the work of the lips, he utters the words from his tongue to the feces. And his saying at his means at him, and al-ladda and 'and in their common language have the same meaning, and so is their saying ladun, so the nun is redundant. So it is as if the verse is informing that the watcher is ready to record the harsh words, which is the canine tooth. As for his saying, clean the teeth, which is the siwak, it is taken from the word san, meaning clean the teeth. And he said: Do not enter upon me a person who has a bad smell. The word qahla has been preserved for me. I heard al-Jarud mentioning on the authority of al-Nadr who said: “The one who has a bad smell in his teeth has turned yellow until they smell bad from the inside. I do not know the word “qahla.” And bakhr means the one whose skin has a bad smell. It is said: a bad smelling man, and bad smelling men.” al-Jarud told us, he said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu Ali, on the authority of Abu Ja`far ibn Tamam ibn al-`Abbas, on the authority of his father, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Why do you come to my house with a cold? Eleventh: In trimming the moustache. It is to take from it until the edge of the lip appears, which is the frame, and not to cut it so that it represents himself, Malik said. Ibn Abd al-Hakam mentioned from him that he said: I think that whoever shaves his moustache should be disciplined. Ashhab mentioned from him that he said about shaving the moustache: This is an innovation, and I think that whoever does it should be severely hurt. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said that Malik said: I think that whoever shaves it should be severely hurt, as if he sees it as representing himself, and likewise with plucking the hair, and trimming it is better in his view than shaving it. And likewise: It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a tuft of hair, and his companions were either full-haired or short-haired, and he shaved and they shaved for the ritual. It was narrated: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to trim his nails and moustache before going out to the Friday prayer. At-Tahawi said: We did not find anything explicitly narrated from Al-Shafi’i about this. His companions whom we saw, Al-Muzani and Ar-Rabi’, used to shave their moustaches, and this indicates that they took that from Al-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him. He said: As for Abu Hanifa, Zufar, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, their school of thought regarding hair on the head and moustache was that shaving is better than cutting it. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad mentioned on the authority of Al-Shafi’i that his school of thought regarding shaving the moustache is the same as that of Abu Hanifa. Abu Bakr Al-Athram said: I saw Ahmad ibn Hanbal trimming his moustache severely, and I heard him being asked about the Sunnah regarding trimming the moustache, and he said: Shave it as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Trim the moustache. Abu Omar said: There are only two roots for this matter: One of them is: Trim, which is a word with open interpretation. The second is: Trim the moustache, which is an explanatory word, and the explanatory word rules out the general, which is the practice of the people of Medina, and it is the most appropriate thing to say in this matter. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to trim his moustache and say: Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, used to do that. He said: A good and strange hadith. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The fitrah is five things: circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, trimming the moustache, clipping the nails, and plucking the armpit hairs.” And in it, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Differ from the polytheists. Trim the moustache and grow the beard.” The non-Arabs trim their beards and grow their moustaches together, which is the opposite of beauty and cleanliness. Razin reported on the authority of Nafi’ that Ibn Umar used to trim his moustache until he could see the skin, and he would take these two, meaning the area between the moustache and the beard. In Al-Bukhari: Ibn Umar used to take from the length of his beard what was longer than a fistful if he went for Hajj or performed Umrah. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to take from the width and length of his beard.” He said: This is a strange hadith. Twelfth: As for the armpit, it is recommended to pluck it, just as it is recommended to shave the pubic hair. If it is reversed, it is permissible to achieve cleanliness. The first is more appropriate, because it is the usual and available option. Thirteenth: Parting the hair: Separating it in the parting. In his description, may God bless him and grant him peace: If his hair is parted, he parted it. It is said: I parted the hair, I parted it in parts. He says: If the hair of his head is parted, he parted it in the parting. If it is not parted, he left it loose. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to let his hair hang down, while the polytheists used to part their hair. He used to like to follow the People of the Book in matters in which he was not commanded to do anything. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, parted his hair after that.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim on the authority of Anas. Al-Qadi Iyad said: Letting the hair hang down means letting it hang down, and what is meant here by scholars is letting it hang over the forehead and making it like a story. Parting the hair is a Sunnah, because it is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, preferred. It has been narrated that when Umar ibn Abdul Aziz returned from Friday prayers, he would station guards at the door of the mosque who would cut the forelock of anyone who did not part his hair. It has been said that parting was from the Sunnah of Abraham, peace be upon him, and God knows best. Fourteenth: As for gray hair, it is light and it is disliked to pluck it. In Al-Nasa’i and Abu Dawud, on the authority of Amr bin Shu’aib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not pluck out grey hair. No Muslim who grows a grey hair in Islam will have a light on the Day of Resurrection, and God will write down a good deed for him and erase a sin from him.” I said: Just as it is disliked to pluck it, it is also disliked to change it to black. As for changing it to something other than black, that is permissible, because of what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding Abu Quhafah - when he was brought with his beard as white as an ostrich’s: Change this with something and avoid blackness. And he who said it well said: Its top becomes black and its bottom becomes white, and there is no good in the top if the bottom becomes corrupt. Another said: O you who dyes your gray hair with henna to cover it, ask the King to cover it from the fire. Fifteenth: As for Tharid, it is the best and most blessed of all foods. It is the food of the Arabs, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, testified to its superiority over all other foods, saying: The superiority of Aisha over other women is like the superiority of tharid over all other foods. In Sahih Al-Busti, it is narrated on the authority of Asma bint Abi Bakr that: When she made tharid, she would cover it with something until it had gone away and she would say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: It is greater in blessing. Sixteenth: I said: This has a meaning similar to what Abd al-Razzaq mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and what Saeed ibn al-Musayyab said. And others. Mention of rinsing the mouth, inhaling water in the nose, and the siwak will be made in Surat An-Nisa’, and the ruling on istinja’ will be made in Bara’ah, and the ruling on hospitality will be made in Hud, God willing. Muslim narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: A time has been set for us to trim the moustache, cut the nails, pluck the armpit hair, and shave the pubic hair. We should not leave it for more than forty nights. Our scholars said: This is a specification of the maximum period, and it is preferable to check that from Friday to Friday. This hadith is narrated by Ja’far ibn Sulayman. Al-Uqayli said: There is a problem with his hadith. Abu Omar said about it: It is not an argument, due to his poor memory and many mistakes. This hadith is not strong in terms of transmission, but some people have said it, and most of them are of the opinion that there is no specific time for that. And God is the Grantor of success. Seventeenth: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, I will make you an Imam for the people. Imam means role model, and from it comes the word Imam for the thread of construction, and Imam for the road, because one leads in it for paths, i.e. one intends. So the meaning is: We have made you an Imam for the people, so that they may follow you in these qualities, and the righteous may take you as an example. So God Almighty made him an Imam for the people of His obedience, and for that reason the nations agreed to claim that he was a Hanif - and God knows best. Eighteenth: The Almighty’s saying: And from my descendants is a supplication to God the Almighty, meaning: O my descendants, O Lord, make. It was said: This is from him in the form of a question about them, meaning: And from my descendants, O Lord, what will it be? So God the Almighty informed him that among them was a disobedient person who did not deserve the imamate. Ibn Abbas said: Abraham, peace be upon him, asked to make an imam from his descendants, so God informed him that among his descendants was someone who would disobey, so He said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers. Nineteenth: The Almighty’s saying: And of my descendants. The root of dharīyah is a verbal noun from dhar, because God Almighty brought forth creation from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, like dharī’ when He made them witness against themselves. It was said: It is taken from dharā’ God li-khalaq yadhrū’uhum dharī’a He created them, and from it is dharīyah, which is the offspring of the two heavy things, except that the Arabs dropped the hamzah, and the plural is dharāri. Zayd ibn Thabit read dharīyah with a kasrah on the dhal and dharīyah with a fathah on the dhal. Ibn Jinni Abu al-Fath Uthman said: The root of this letter can have four meanings: The first is dharā’, the second is dharr, the third is dharū, and the fourth is dharā. As for the hamzah, it is from dharā’ God al-khalaq, and as for dharr, it is from the word dhar and its meaning, and that is because of what was mentioned in the hadith: That creation was like an atom. As for the waw and the yaa, they are from the word dharuwat al-hubb and dharituhu, both of which are said together, and that is the saying of God the Almighty: Then it became chaff, scattered by the winds. This is for its softness and lightness, and that is also the case of the atom. Al-Jawhari said: The wind scattered the dust and other things, scattering them and scattering them, dhawran and dhariya, meaning it blew them away. And from that is their saying: dhara al-nas al-hanita, and arzayt al-shay if you throw it, like you throw the grain for the crop. And he stabbed it and scattered it on the back of his animal, meaning he threw it. Al-Khalil said: We called it dhariya because God the Almighty scattered it on the earth as the zar scatters the seed. It was said: The root of dhariya is dharurah, but when doubling became frequent, one of the raa’s was replaced with a yaa, so it became dharuwiyah, then the waw was assimilated into the yaa, so it became dhariya. What is meant by offspring here is the children in particular, and it may also refer to both fathers and sons, as in the Almighty’s saying: And a sign for them is that We bore their offspring, meaning their fathers. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth: The Almighty’s saying: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers. There is a difference of opinion regarding what is meant by the covenant. Abu Salih narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it is prophethood. As-Suddi and Mujahid said: Imamate. Qatadah: Faith. Ata’: Mercy. Ad-Dahhak: The religion of God the Almighty. It was said: His covenant is His command: and the covenant is used to mean the command. God the Almighty said: Indeed, God has made a covenant with us, meaning He has commanded us. And He said: Did I not make a covenant with you, O children of Adam, that means did I not present to you the command to do so? If the covenant of God is His commands, then His saying: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers means that it is not permissible for them to be in the position of those who accept God’s commands and do not abide by them, as will be explained later, God willing. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatadah regarding the Almighty’s saying: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers, he said: God’s covenant in the Hereafter does not include the wrongdoers. As for in this world, the wrongdoer has reached it, believed in it, ate, lived, and seen. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a good statement, meaning, the oppressors will not attain their hopes, meaning, I will not make them feel safe from My punishment. Saeed bin Jubair said: The oppressor here is the polytheist. Ibn Masoud and Talha bin Musarraf read My covenant is not attained by the oppressors with the oppressors in the nominative case. The rest read it with the accusative case. Hamzah, Hafs, and Ibn Muhaisin made the ya’ in My covenant silent, while the rest opened it. Twenty-first: A group of scholars used this verse as evidence that the one who is to be judged must be one of the people of justice, benevolence, and virtue, with the ability to do so. This is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them not to dispute authority with its people, based on what was previously said about it. As for the people of immorality, injustice, and oppression, they are not worthy of it, because God Almighty said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers. For this reason, Ibn al-Zubayr and al-Hasan ibn Ali, may God be pleased with them, rebelled. The best of the people of Iraq and their scholars rebelled against al-Hajjaj, and the people of Medina expelled the Umayyads and rose up against them, and this led to the Harrah that Muslim ibn Uqbah inflicted on them. Twenty-second: Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: Everyone who is unjust is not a prophet, nor a caliph, nor a ruler, nor a mufti, nor an imam of prayer, and what he narrates from the owner of the Shariah is not accepted from him, nor is his testimony accepted regarding rulings, except that he is not dismissed for his immorality until the people of authority and contract dismiss him. And what preceded from his rulings is in accordance with what is correct and is past and not invalidated. Malik stated this explicitly regarding the Khawarij and rebels that their rulings are not invalidated if they hit upon an aspect of ijtihad, and did not violate the consensus, or contradict the texts. We only said that because of the consensus of the Companions, and that is because the Khawarij came out in their days and it was not reported that the imams followed their rulings, nor did they invalidate any of them, nor did they re-take the zakat or establish the punishments that they had taken and established, so this indicates that if they hit upon an aspect of ijtihad, their rulings were not to be interfered with. Twenty-third: Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: As for taking provisions from oppressive leaders, there are three cases for that: If everything in their hands was taken according to the Shariah, then it is permissible to take it, and the Companions and Followers took it from the hands of Al-Hajjaj and others. If it was mixed, lawful and unjust, as is the case in the hands of the rulers today, then piety is to leave it, and it is permissible for Al-Hajjaj to take it, and he is like a thief who has stolen money in his hand, and good, lawful money that a man has entrusted him with, and the thief comes to give it in charity to a person, so it is permissible for charity to be taken from him. It is permissible for the thief to give some of what he stole in charity, if it is not something known to be stolen. Likewise, if he sells or buys, the contract is valid and binding - although piety is to refrain from it - and that is because money is not forbidden in and of itself, but rather it is forbidden because of its sources. If what is in their hands is clearly unjust, then it is not permissible for it to be taken from their hands. Even if the money in their hands was usurped, but its owner and claimant are not known, it is as if it was found in the hands of thieves and highwaymen. It is placed in the treasury and its claimant is awaited according to the amount of effort. If it is not known, the imam spends it on the interests of the Muslims.
2:125: The Almighty’s saying: And when We made the House a place of return for the people and a place of safety. There are two issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: We made means we made it, because it takes two objects, and this has been mentioned previously. The house means the Kaaba. Mathaba means a place of return. It is said: thaba yathub mathaban wa mathabah wa thawwaban wa thawban. Mathaba is a source of description and it means the place to which one is rewarded, i.e. one returns to it. Waraqa ibn Nawfal said about the Kaaba: A place where all the tribes' annihilations are held, to which the weak and oppressed flock. Al-A'mash read Muthabat as a plural. It is possible that it is from thawaab, meaning they will be rewarded there. Mujahid said: No one will satisfy his desire from it. The poet said: Make the house a place of rest for them, not a place where they spend their time. The original is mathubah, the vowel of the waw was changed to the tha’, so the waw was changed to an alif, following the command thaba yathub, and it was in the accusative case as the second object, and the ha’ was added for emphasis from yathub, meaning to return, because rarely does someone leave the house without realizing that he has not had his fill of it, so it is like nasabah and ’alama, as Al-Akhfash said. Another said: It is the ha’ of the feminization of the first letter and is not for emphasis. If it is said: Not everyone who comes to him returns to him, it is said: It is not specific to those who come to him, but rather the meaning is that he is not devoid of the whole, and he does not lack a person who intends to come to him, and God Almighty knows best. Second: The Almighty’s statement: And We have made you safe. Abu Hanifa and a group of jurists from the regions used it as evidence to refrain from carrying out the prescribed punishment in the Sacred Sanctuary on the married person or the thief if he takes refuge in it. They supported that with the statement of the Almighty: And whoever enters it is safe. It is as if He said: Safe are those who enter the House. The correct view is to carry out the prescribed punishments in the Sacred Sanctuary, and that this is one of the abrogated texts, because it is agreed that one should not be killed in the House, and one should be killed outside the House. The only difference of opinion is whether one should be killed in the Sacred Sanctuary or not. The name of the House does not apply to the Sacred Sanctuary in reality. They agreed that if one is killed in the Sacred Sanctuary, he should be killed in it, and if he commits a prescribed punishment in it, and if he fights in it, he should be fought and killed on the spot. Abu Hanifa said: Whoever takes refuge in the Haram should not be killed in it, nor should he be prosecuted, and he should continue to be oppressed until he dies or leaves. We kill him with the sword, and he kills him with hunger and rejection. What killing is more severe than this? And in his saying, We believe, there is an emphasis on the command to face the Kaaba, meaning that there is no such virtue in the Holy House, and people do not need it. Whoever seeks refuge in the Sacred Sanctuary is safe from being raided. This will be explained in Al-Ma’idah, God willing. The Almighty’s saying: And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer. There are three issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying, And they took. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read it with a fatha on the kha’ as a report about those who took it from the followers of Abraham, and it is conjoined to We made, meaning We made the House a place of return and they took it as a place of prayer. It was said that it is conjoined with the estimation of when, as if he said: And when We made the House a place of return and when they took, so according to the first the statement is one sentence, and according to the second two sentences. The majority of the reciters read and they took with a kasra on the kha’ as a command, they separated it from the first and made it conjoined one sentence to another. Al-Mahdawi said: It is possible that it is conjoined with Remember My favor, as if he said that to the Jews, or with the meaning of when We made the House, because its meaning is remember when We made. Or with the meaning of his saying: a place of return, because its meaning is reward. Second: Ibn Omar narrated that he said: Omar said: I agreed with my Lord on three matters: on the station of Abraham, on the veil, and on the prisoners of Badr. Narrated by Muslim and others. Narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of Anas, who said: Omar said: I agreed with God in three things, or my Lord agreed with me in three things... The hadith, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi included it in his Musnad, and he said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, Ali bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Anas bin Malik. He said: Omar said: I agreed with my Lord in four matters. I said: O Messenger of God, what if you prayed behind the Maqam? Then this verse was revealed: And take the station of Abraham as a place of prayer. I said: O Messenger of God, what if you imposed a veil on your wives so that the righteous and the wicked would enter upon them? Then God revealed: And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition. And this verse was revealed: And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay. When it was revealed, I said: Blessed be God, the best of creators. Then this verse was revealed: So blessed be God, the best of creators. I entered upon the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Either you stop or God will replace him with wives better than you. Then this verse was revealed: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you. I said: There is no mention of prisoners in this narration, so Omar’s agreement is on five. Third: The Almighty’s saying: From the place of standing. The place of standing in the language: the place of the feet. An-Nahhas said: The place of standing from the verb qama yaqoom, is a verbal noun and a name for the place. And the place of standing from the verb iqama, as for the saying of Zuhair: They have beautiful faces and clubs that are filled with words and deeds. Its meaning is: Among them are people of stations. There are different opinions about specifying the station, the most correct of which is that it is the stone that people know today, where they pray the two rak’ahs of the Tawaf of Arrival. This is the opinion of Jabir ibn Abdullah, Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and others. In Sahih Muslim, from the long hadith of Jabir: “When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw the House, he touched the corner, jogged three times and walked four times, then he advanced to the Station of Abraham and recited: ‘And take the Station of Abraham as a place of prayer. ’ So he prayed two rak’ahs in which he recited ‘Say: He is God, the One’ and ‘Say: O you disbelievers. ’” This indicates that the two rak’ahs of circumambulation and other prayers for the people of Mecca are better, and it indicates from one perspective that circumambulation for strangers is better, as will come. In Bukhari, it is the stone on which Abraham climbed when he was too weak to lift the stones that Ishmael used to bring him to build the House, and his feet sank into it. Anas said: I saw the traces of his fingers, his heel, and the soles of his feet on the Station, except that the people wiped them with their hands, as narrated by Al-Qushayri. Al-Suddi said: The Station is the stone that the wife of Ishmael placed under the feet of Abraham, peace be upon him, when she washed his head. Also from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Ata’: The entire Hajj. On the authority of Ata’: Arafat, Muzdalifah, and the Jamarat. Al-Sha’bi said: Al-Nakha’i: The entire Sanctuary is the Station of Abraham. Mujahid said the same. I said: The correct opinion in this case is the first statement, according to what is proven in Sahih. Abu Naim narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Suqah on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at a man between the corner and the station, or the door and the station, and he was supplicating and saying: O God, forgive so-and-so. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What is this? He said: A man entrusted me to supplicate for him in this station, so he said: Go back, for your companion has been forgiven.” Abu Nu`aym said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Qadi told us, he said: Muhammad ibn `Asim ibn Yahya al-Katib told us, he said: `Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim al-Qattan al-Kufi told us, he said: Al-Harith ibn `Imran al-Ja`fari told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Suqah, and he mentioned it. Abu Nu`aym said: This is how `Abd al-Rahman narrated it on the authority of al-Harith on the authority of Muhammad on the authority of Jabir, and it is only known from the hadith of al-Harith on the authority of Muhammad on the authority of `Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn `Abbas. The meaning of musalla is a place where supplication is made, said by Mujahid. It was also said: a place of prayer where one prays, said by Qatadah. It was also said: a qiblah where the imam stands, said al-Hasan. God Almighty says: And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, saying, ‘Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf, and those who stay there, and those who bow and prostrate.’ There are six issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And Our covenant It was said that it means Our command. It was also said that it means We revealed. That you purify “that” is in the accusative case, assuming that the preposition is deleted. Sibawayh said that it has the meaning of any which is explanatory, so it has no place in parsing. The Kufians said that it can be in the meaning of saying. And purify, it was said that it means: from idols, according to Mujahid and Al-Zuhri. Ubayd ibn Umair and Saeed ibn Jubayr said: from plagues and doubt. It was also said: from the infidels. Al-Suddi said that he built it and founded it on purity and the intention of purity, so it comes like his saying: He founded it on piety. Yaman said: He created it and created it. My house He added the house to himself as an addition of honor and respect, which is the addition of a creature to a Creator, and a slave to a Master. Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, the people of Medina, Hisham and Hafs read: My house with the opening of the ya’, and the others with the closing of the ya’. Second: The Almighty’s statement: For those who circumambulate it apparently means those who circumambulate it, and this is the statement of Ata’. Saeed bin Jubair said: Its meaning is for strangers who have come to Mecca, and there is some distance in that. And those who stay: those who are residents from my country and a stranger, according to Ata’. Likewise His statement: For those who circumambulate it. In the language, staying means adherence and turning towards something, as the poet said: The Nabataeans are playing the Fenjga Mujahid said: The ones who stay in seclusion are those who are nearby. Ibn Abbas said: The ones who pray. It was also said: Those who sit without performing tawaf. The meaning is close. And bowing and prostrating means those who pray at the Kaaba. He specifically mentioned bowing and prostration because they are the closest states of the one praying to God Almighty. The meaning of bowing and prostration in language has already been mentioned. Praise be to God. Third: When God the Almighty said: Purify My House, the meaning includes all of His houses, so their ruling is His ruling in purification and cleanliness. He only mentioned the Kaaba specifically because there was no other, or because it is His greatest sanctuary, and the first is more apparent, and God knows best. And in the revelation: In houses which God has permitted to be raised, and there comes the ruling on mosques, God willing. It was narrated on the authority of Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he heard a man’s voice in the mosque and said: What is this! Do you know where you are!? And Hudhayfah said that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “God has revealed to me, ‘O brother of the warners, O brother of the messengers, warn your people not to enter any of my houses except with sound hearts, truthful tongues, pure hands, and clean private parts, and not to enter any of my houses as long as someone has wronged them, for I curse him as long as he stands before me until he returns that wrong to its people, and I become his hearing with which he hears and his sight with which he sees, and he will be among my friends and chosen ones, and he will be my neighbor with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous.” Fourth: Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, Al-Thawri and a group of the Salaf used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of performing obligatory and voluntary prayers inside the house. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: If someone prays inside it, facing one of its walls, his prayer is valid. If he prays towards the door and the door is open, his prayer is invalid. The same applies to someone who prays on its roof, because he is not facing any of it. Malik said: He should not pray obligatory or voluntary prayers in it, but he may pray voluntary prayers in it. However, if he prays obligatory prayers in it, he must repeat them during the prescribed time. Asbagh said: He must repeat them forever. I said: It is correct, because Muslim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Usama bin Zaid told me: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the House, he supplicated in all its corners and did not pray in it until he left it. When he left, he bowed two rak’ahs facing the Kaaba and said: This is the qiblah.” This is a text. If it is said: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the house with Usama bin Zaid, Bilal, and Uthman bin Talha al-Hajabi, and they closed the door behind them. When they opened it, I was the first to enter. I met Bilal and asked him: Did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pray in it? He said: Yes, between the two right-hand pillars.” Narrated by Muslim, in which he said: He placed two pillars on his left, one on his right, and three pillars behind him. At that time, the house had six pillars. We said: This may mean that he prayed in the sense of supplicated, as Usama said, or it may mean that he prayed the customary prayer. If both are possible, then the evidence for it is invalid. If it is said: Ibn al-Mundhir and others narrated on the authority of Usamah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw pictures in the Kaaba, so I brought water in a bucket to beat those pictures with.” Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b narrated to us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Mihran, who said: Umair, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, narrated to us, on the authority of Usamah ibn Zayd, who said: “I entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Kaaba, and he saw pictures. He said: So he called for a bucket of water, so I brought it to him, and he began to wipe them away and said: ‘May God curse a people who depict what they do not create.’” It is possible that while Usamah was still searching for water, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Bilal, who Usamah did not see. So he who affirmed was more deserving than he who denied. Usamah himself said: So the people accepted Bilal’s statement and abandoned my statement. Mujahid narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Safwan, who said: I said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: What did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do when he entered the Kaaba? He said: He prayed two rak’ahs. We said: This applies to voluntary prayers, and we do not know of any disagreement among scholars regarding the validity of voluntary prayers in the Kaaba. As for obligatory prayers, no, because God Almighty specified the direction in His statement: So turn your faces toward it, as will be explained later, and the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he went out: This Qiblah is the same as God Almighty has specified it. If the assumption was valid within it, he would not have said: This Qiblah. Thus, it is correct to reconcile the hadiths, and this is better than omitting some of them, so there is no contradiction, and praise be to God. Fifth: They also differed regarding praying on its roof. Al-Shafi’i said what we mentioned. Malik said: Whoever prays on the roof of the Kaaba must repeat the prayer in its proper time. It was narrated from some of Malik’s companions: He must repeat it forever. Abu Hanifa said: Whoever prays on the roof of the Kaaba does not have to do anything. Sixth: They also differed as to which is better, praying at the House or circumambulating it? Malik said: Circumambulating is better for the people of the cities, and praying is better for the people of Mecca. It was reported from Ibn Abbas, Ata’, and Mujahid. The majority are of the opinion that praying is better. In the hadith: If it were not for the men who are humble, the elders who bow, and the children who are breastfed and graze their beauty, we would have poured out punishment upon you abundantly. Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Ali bin Thabit al-Khatib mentioned in the book Al-Sabiq wa Al-Lahiq on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If there were not among you men who are humble and whose beauty is pleasing, and children who are breastfed, punishment would have been poured out upon the sinners in infancy. He did not mention elders who bowed. In the hadith of Abu Dharr: Prayer is the best thing, so do it often or infrequently. Narrated by Al-Ajurri. There are many hadiths about the virtue of prayer and prostration that bear witness to the opinion of the majority, and God Almighty knows best.
2:126: It contains three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: A secure city meaning Mecca. So he prayed for his offspring and others to be safe and to live comfortably. It was narrated that when he prayed with this prayer, God Almighty ordered Gabriel to uproot Taif from the Levant and circumambulate it around the House for a week, so it was called Taif for that reason. Then he brought it down to Tihamah. At that time, Mecca and what was next to it was barren, with no water or vegetation, so God blessed what was around it, such as Taif and others, and caused all kinds of fruits to grow in it, as will be explained in Surat Ibrahim, God willing. Second: Scholars differed about Mecca as to whether it became a safe sanctuary through Abraham’s question or whether it was like that before him, with two opinions: One of them: It has always been a sanctuary from the tyrants who have power, and from eclipses and earthquakes, and all the other calamities that befall the country. He has placed in the rebellious souls such reverence and awe for it that its people have become distinguished by security from other people of the villages. And He, the Almighty, has placed in it one of the great signs of His Oneness in what has been seen of the matter of hunting in it, so that the dog and the prey come together in it and the dog does not agitate the prey nor flee from it, until when they leave the sanctuary the dog attacks it and returns to fleeing and running away. Rather, Abraham asked that it be made safe from famine, drought, and raids, and that his family be provided with fruits, not as some people thought, that it was to prevent the shedding of blood on behalf of those who were obligated to be killed, for that is far from being what Abraham intended, peace be upon him, so that it can be said: He asked God to include in His law a prohibition on killing those who sought refuge in the sanctuary. This is very far-fetched. Second: Mecca was permissible before the call of Abraham, peace be upon him, like all other countries, and with his call it became a safe sanctuary, just as Medina became safe with the prohibition of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after it had been permissible. The people of the first article cited the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: “This country was made sacred by God Almighty on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God Almighty until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted for anyone before me, and it was only permitted for me for an hour of the day. It is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. No thorn is to be cut, its game is not to be scared away, and its lost property is not to be picked up except by one who recognizes it, and no one is to be alone in it.” Al-Abbas said: O Messenger of God, except for the idhkar, for it is for their minions and for their houses. He said: Except for the idhkar. Similar to it is the hadith of Abu Shuraih, narrated by Muslim and others. In Sahih Muslim also, on the authority of Abdullah bin Zaid bin Asim, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Abraham made Mecca sacred and prayed for its people, and I have made Medina sacred just as Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I have prayed for its saa’ and mudd twice as much as Abraham prayed for the people of Mecca.’” Ibn Atiyyah said: There is no contradiction between the two hadiths, because the first is a report of God’s prior knowledge and decree concerning it, and the sanctity being for the duration of Adam and the times of the country’s inhabiting with faith. The second is a report of Abraham renewing its sanctity and showing that after the destruction. The first statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the second day of the conquest was a report of the great sanctity of Mecca for the believers by attributing the prohibition to God, the Most High, and he mentioned Abraham when he made Medina sacred as an example of himself. There is no doubt that the prohibition of Medina is also from God, the Most High, and from the enforcement of His decree and prior knowledge. Al-Tabari said: Mecca was sacred, but God did not command His creation to do so until Abraham asked Him to make it sacred. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And provide his family with fruits from whoever believes. The meaning of provision has already been presented. Fruits is the plural of fruit, and it has already been presented. Whoever believes is a substitute for whoever believes, a substitute for part for all. And belief is belief, and it has already been presented. “He said: And whoever disbelieves.” Whoever in his saying whoever disbelieves is in the accusative case, and the meaning is: And provide for whoever disbelieves. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a subject, and it is a condition, and the predicate is so enjoy him, and it is the answer. There is a difference of opinion as to whether this statement is from God or from Abraham, peace be upon him. Abi bin Kaab, Ibn Ishaq and others said: It is from God, the Most High. They read Famatahu with a damma on the hamza, a fatha on the meem and a shaddah on the taa. Then I compelled him with a severing of the alif and a damma on the raa. This is the case with the seven reciters except Ibn Amir, who made the meem sukoon and the taa light. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj narrated that in Abi’s reading it is Fana’matuhu a little while then we compelled him with a noon. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: This statement is from Abraham, peace be upon him. They read Famatahu with a fatha on the hamza and a sukoon on the meem, then I compelled him with a connected alif and a fatha on the raa. So it is as if Abraham, peace be upon him, prayed for the believers and against the disbelievers. Accordingly, the pronoun in said is for Abraham. It was repeated because of the length of the statement, or because it moved from praying for some people to praying against others. The subject in the word said in the group reading is the name of God Almighty, and Al-Nahhas chose it, and he made the reading with the opening of the hamza and the stillness of the meem and the connection of the alif anomalous. He said: The order of the speech and the interpretation together indicate something else. As for the order of the speech, God Almighty is reporting from Abraham, peace be upon him, that he said: My Lord, make this a secure city. Then He came with His saying, the Almighty: And provide its people with fruits - whoever of them believes in God and the Last Day. He did not separate it with a word. Then He said after that: He said, and whoever disbelieves, this was an answer from God, and He did not say after that Abraham said. As for the interpretation, it was authenticated from Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, and Muhammad bin Kaab, and this is the wording of Ibn Abbas: Abraham, peace be upon him, prayed for whoever believed, not the people in particular, so God Almighty informed him that He provides for the disbelievers as He provides for the believers, and that He will give them enjoyment for a little while, then He will force them to the torment of the Fire. Abu Jaafar said: And God Almighty said: No, We provide for these and those from the gift of your Lord. And He, the Most High, said: And nations We will give enjoyment to. Abu Ishaq said: Abraham, peace be upon him, knew that there would be disbelievers among his descendants, so he singled out the believers, because God Almighty said: My covenant does not include the wrongdoers.
2:127: God Almighty said: “And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House, [saying], ‘Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.’” The Almighty said: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House. The foundations: its foundation, according to Abu Ubaidah and Al-Farra’. Al-Kisa’i said: they are the walls. It is known that it is the foundation. In the hadith: When the House was demolished, large stones were taken out of it. Ibn al-Zubayr said: “These are the foundations that Abraham, peace be upon him, raised.” It was said: The foundations had been destroyed, so God showed them to Abraham. Ibn Abbas: The House was built on pillars that he saw two thousand years before the creation of the world, and then they were pushed to the ground beneath it. The singular form of foundations is qa’idah. The singular form of qā’idah is for women, and the singular form is qā’id. People differed about who built the Kaaba first and laid its foundations. Some said: The angels. It was narrated on the authority of Ja`far ibn Muhammad who said: My father was asked, while I was present, about the beginning of the creation of the Ka`bah. He said: When God the Almighty said: Indeed, I will place a successive authority on earth, the angels said: Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we glorify You with praise and sanctify You? So He became angry with them, so they sought refuge behind His Throne and circled around it seven times seeking to please their Lord until God was pleased with them. He said to them: Build for Me a House on earth so that whoever among the children of Adam with whom I am angry may seek refuge in it and circle around it as you circled around My Throne, so that I may be pleased with him as I am pleased with you. So they built this House. Abdul Razzaq mentioned on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, Ibn al-Musayyab, and others: God the Almighty revealed to Adam: When I descend, build Me a house and surround it as you saw the angels surrounding My throne in the heavens. Ata’ said: The people claimed that he built it from five mountains: Hira’, Mount Sinai, Lebanon, Judi, and Tur Zita, and its suburb was from Hira’. Al-Khalil said: The suburb here is the circular foundation of the house made of rock, and from it what is around the city is called a suburb. Al-Mawardi narrated on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When Adam was sent down from Paradise to Earth, He said to him: O Adam, go and build Me a house and circumambulate it, and remember Me when you see the angels doing around My Throne. So Adam began to step forward and the earth was folded up for him, and the desert was held back for him, and his foot did not land on anything on the earth except that it became populated until he reached the location of the Sacred House. And Gabriel, peace be upon him, struck the earth with his wings and revealed a firm foundation on the seventh lowest earth, and the angels threw rocks to him, and thirty men could not bear the rock from it, and he built it from five mountains as we mentioned. It has been narrated in some of the reports that a tent from the tents of Paradise was sent down to Adam, peace be upon him, and it was pitched in the location of the Kaaba so that he could live in it and circumambulate around it, and it remained until God, the Almighty, took Adam, then it was removed. This is from the path of Wahb ibn Munabbih. In another narration: A house was sent down with him, and the believers from his descendants would circle around it like this until the time of the drowning. Then God raised it up and it was in the sky, and it is called the Frequented House. This was narrated on the authority of Qatada, who narrated from Al-Halimi in his book Minhaaj ad-Din. He said: It is possible that the meaning of what Qatada said, that a house was sent down with Adam, is that the size of the Frequented House was sent down with him in length, width and thickness. Then the tent, it may have been sent down and pitched in the place of the Kaaba, and when he was ordered to build it, he built it. It was around the Kaaba, a place of reassurance for the heart of Adam, may God bless him and grant him peace, as long as he lived, then it was raised up. So these narrations agree. This is the building of Adam, peace be upon him, then it was built by Abraham, peace be upon him. Ibn Jurayj said: Some people said: God, the Exalted, sent a head in it, and the head said: O Abraham, your Lord commands you to take the size of this cloud, so he looked at it and wrote its size, then the head said: I have done so, so it dug and emerged from a firm foundation in the ground. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that when God Almighty commanded Abraham to build the House, he left Syria with his son Ishmael and his mother Hagar, and sent with him the serenity that had a tongue with which it spoke. Abraham would go with her in the morning when she went out, and her in the evening when she went back, until she reached Mecca. She said to Abraham: Build on my foundation. So he and Ishmael raised the House until they reached the place of the corner. He said to his son: O my son, find me a stone that I can make a sign for the people. So he brought him a stone, but he was not satisfied with it and said: I will find something else. So he went to look for it, and he came to him and he had brought the corner and placed it in its place. He said: O my father, who brought you this stone? He said: Who did not entrust me to you? Ibn Abbas: Abu Qubais shouted: O Ibrahim, O Khalil al-Rahman, you have a trust with you, so take it. And behold, it was a white stone of the ruby of Paradise, which Adam had brought down from Paradise. When Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the House, a square cloud with a head came and called out: Raise your heads on my square foundation. This was the building of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. It was narrated that when Ibrahim and Ismail finished building the House, God gave them horses as a reward for raising the foundations of the House. Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim narrated: Omar ibn Abi Omar told us, Naim ibn Hammad told us, Abdul Wahhab ibn Hammam, the brother of Abdul Razzaq, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malikah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The horses were wild animals like all other wild animals. When God permitted Ibrahim and Ismail to raise the foundations, God, Blessed be His Name, said: I am giving you a treasure which I have stored up for you. Then Ismail inspired me to go out to Ajyad and call for the treasure to come to you. So he went out to Ajyad - which was his homeland - and he did not know what the supplication or the treasure was, so God inspired him, and there was not a horse on the face of the earth in the land of the Arabs except that it came to him and he took hold of its forelocks and subdued it for him, so ride it and feed it, for it is auspicious, and it is the inheritance of your father Ishmael, for the horse was called Arab because Ishmael was commanded to supplicate and it came to him. And Abdul-Munem bin Idris narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, who said: The first one to build the House with clay and stones was Seth, peace be upon him. As for the Quraysh’s building of it, it is well-known, and the story of the snake in that regard is mentioned, and it was preventing them from demolishing it until the Quraysh gathered at the station and cried out to God Almighty and said: Our Lord, do you not fear? We wanted to honour and decorate your house, so if you are satisfied with that, otherwise do whatever you like. Then they heard a rustle from the sky - and the rustle is the rustling of the wings of a huge bird - and behold, it was a bird larger than an eagle, black in back, white in belly and legs. It sank its claws into the nape of the snake, then it took off with it, dragging its tail, larger than so-and-so, until it took off with it towards Ajyad. The Quraysh demolished it and began to rebuild it with stones from the valley, which the Quraysh carried on their necks. They raised it twenty cubits into the sky. While the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was carrying stones from Ajyad, and he was wearing a cloak, the cloak became too small for him, so he tried to lift the cloak on his shoulder, and his private parts were visible because of the smallness of the cloak. Then it was called: O Muhammad, cover your private parts, and he was not seen naked after that. There were five years between the construction of the Kaaba and what was revealed to him, and between his exit and its construction there were fifteen years. It was mentioned by Abd al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Abdullah ibn Uthman on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl. It was mentioned on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Zuhri: When they had built it and reached the place of the corner, the Quraysh argued about the corner, which tribe would be the first to raise it? Until a dispute arose among them, and they said: Come, let us judge who will be the first to appear to us from this path, so they agreed on that, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared to them as a young boy wearing a tiger’s sash, so they judged him, and he ordered the corner to be placed in a garment, then he ordered the chief of each tribe to give him a corner of the garment, then he climbed up and they raised the corner to him, and he was the one who placed it, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Ishaq said: It was narrated that the Quraysh found a book in Syriac in the corner, but they did not know what it was until a Jewish man read it to them. It said: I am God, the possessor of Mecca.
