I created it on the day I created the heavens and the earth, and I formed the sun and the moon, and I surrounded it with seven upright angels who will not perish until their wood perishes. Blessed for their people in water and milk. And on the authority of Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Ali, he said: The door of the Ka`bah was on the ground during the time of the Amalekites, Jurhum, and Abraham, peace be upon him, until the Quraysh built it. Muslim narrated on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her who said: I asked the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about the wall: Is it part of the House? He said: Yes. I said: Why did they not put it in the House? He said: Your people were short on money. I said: Why is its door high? He said: Your people did that so that they could let in whomever they wanted and prevent whomever they wanted. Were it not that your people had recently converted to the Age of Ignorance and I feared that their hearts would disapprove, I would have considered putting the wall in the House and attaching its door to the ground. He narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr may God be pleased with him who said: My aunt meaning Aisha (may God be pleased with her) told me that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: O Aisha, were it not that your people had recently converted to polytheism, I would have demolished the Kaaba and attached it to the ground and made two doors for it, an eastern door and a western door, and I would have added six cubits of stone to it, for the Quraysh had limited it when they built the Kaaba. On the authority of Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: If it were not for the recent conversion of your people to disbelief, I would have demolished the Kaaba and built it on the foundations of Abraham. When the Quraysh built the Kaaba, they made it too short and added a door to it. In Al-Bukhari, Hisham bin Urwah said: He meant a door. In Al-Bukhari also: I would have made two doors to it, meaning two doors. This is the construction of the Quraysh. Then when the people of Ash-Sham invaded Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr and the Kaaba was destroyed by their fire, Ibn Az-Zubayr demolished it and rebuilt it as Aisha had told him, and he added five cubits of stone to it, until a foundation appeared that people could see, so he built the structure on it. The length of the Kaaba was eighteen cubits, but when he added to it, he shortened it, so he increased its length by ten cubits, and he made two doors for it, one for entering and the other for exiting. This is in Sahih Muslim, and the wording of the hadith differs. Sufyan mentioned on the authority of Dawud ibn Shabur on the authority of Mujahid who said: When Ibn Az-Zubayr wanted to demolish the Kaaba and rebuild it, he said to the al-Nas 114:Demolish. He said: They refused to demolish and feared that the punishment would descend upon them. Mujahid said: So we went out to Mina and stayed there for three days awaiting the punishment. He said: Ibn Az-Zubayr climbed the wall of the Kaaba himself, and when they saw that nothing had happened to him, they dared to do so. He said: So they demolished it. When he built it, he made two doors for it: one for them to enter through, and one for them to exit through. He added six cubits to what was next to the stone, and he added nine cubits to its length. Muslim said in his hadith: When Ibn al-Zubayr was killed, al-Hajjaj wrote to Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan informing him of that, and telling him that Ibn al-Zubayr had placed the building on a foundation that the just people of Mecca had seen. Abd al-Malik wrote to him: We are not of Ibn al-Zubayr’s taint in anything. As for what he added to its length, he confirmed it, and as for what he added to it of the stone, he returned it to its construction, and closed the door that he opened, so he demolished it and returned it to its construction. In another narration: Abd al-Malik said: I did not think that Abu Khabib meaning Ibn al-Zubayr heard from Aisha what he claimed to have heard from her. Al-Harith ibn Abdullah said: Yes, I heard it from her. He said: I heard her say what? He said: She said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Your people have shortened the construction of the House, and were it not for the recent conversion to polytheism, I would have restored what they left of it. If your people decide after me to rebuild it, then come and I will show you what they left of it. I see it to be close to seven cubits.” In another narration: Abd al-Malik said: If I had heard it before I demolished it, I would have left it as Ibn al-Zubayr built it. This is what came about the construction of the Kaaba from the narrations. It was narrated that Al-Rashid mentioned to Malik bin Anas that he wanted to demolish what Al-Hajjaj had built of the Kaaba, and to return it to the construction of Ibn Al-Zubayr, because of what came from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ibn Al-Zubayr complied with it. Malik said to him: I implore you by God, O Commander of the Faithful, not to make this House a playground for kings, so that none of them would wish to do anything but demolish the House and rebuild it, so that its awe would be lost from the hearts of the people. Al-Waqidi mentioned: Muammar told us on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih, who heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade cursing As`ad al-Himyari, who was a Tubba`, and he was the first to cover the Ka`bah, and he was the other Tubba`. Ibn Ishaq said: It was covered with Coptic cloth, then it was covered with cloaks, and the first to cover it with brocade was al-Hajjaj. Scholars said: Nothing should be taken from the Kaaba’s covering, as it was given to it as a gift, and nothing should be taken from it. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he disliked taking any perfume from the Kaaba for healing purposes. Whenever he saw a servant taking a handful of it, he would not hesitate to hurt it. Ata’ said: Whenever one of us wanted to seek healing, he would bring some perfume from himself, wipe the stone with it, and then take it. The Almighty said: Our Lord, accept from us. The meaning is: And they say, Our Lord, but it was deleted. And it is also in the reading of Abu and Abdullah bin Masoud: And when Abraham and Ishmael raised the foundations of the House and they said, Our Lord, accept from us. The interpretation of Ismail: Hear, O God, because El in Syriac means God, and it has been mentioned before. It was said: When Abraham called upon his Lord, he said: Hear, O El. When his Lord answered him and gave him a son, he named him after what he called upon. Al-Mawardi mentioned it. The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. These are two of the names of God Almighty that we have mentioned in the Most Sublime Book explaining the Most Beautiful Names of God.
2:128: The Almighty said: Our Lord, and make us Muslims to You meaning make us, and Muslims is the second object, they asked for steadfastness and permanence. Islam in this context: faith and deeds together, and from it the Almighty said: Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam so in this is evidence for those who said: faith and Islam are one thing, and they supported this with the Almighty's saying in another verse: So We brought out whoever was therein of the believers * And We found therein not but one house of Muslims. Ibn Abbas and Awf Al-A'rabi read Muslims in the plural. God the Almighty said: And from our descendants, a nation submissive to You meaning, from our descendants, so make. It is said: No prophet called except for himself and his nation except Abraham, for he called with his call for himself and his nation and for this nation. And the word from in His statement: and from our descendants is for partiality, because God the Almighty had informed him that among them were wrongdoers. Al-Tabari narrated that he meant by His statement: from our descendants the Arabs specifically. Al-Suhayli said: And their descendants are the Arabs, because they are the sons of Nabt bin Ismail, or the sons of Tayman bin Ismail. And it is said: Qaydar bin Nabt bin Ismail. As for the Adnanites, they are from Nabt, and as for the Qahtanites, they are from Qaydar bin Nabt bin Ismail, or Tayman according to one of the two opinions. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is weak, because his call appeared among the Arabs and among those who believed from among others. The nation: the group here, and it becomes one if it is followed in goodness, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about Zaid bin Amr bin Nufayl: He will send a nation alone because he did not associate anyone else with him in his religion, and God knows best. The word nation may also be used for a meaning other than this, such as the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, we found our fathers upon a nation. That is, upon a religion and creed. Such as the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, this nation of yours is one nation. It may also mean time and age, such as the Almighty’s statement: And remember after a nation. That is, after a time and age: This nation of Zayd, that is, Zayd’s mother. The word nation also means stature, it is said: So-and-so has a good nation, that is, good stature. He said: And Muawiyah is the most generous of the handsomest of the nations It was said: The nation is the wound that reaches the mother of the brain. It is said: A man who is led in prayer and a leader. The Almighty said: And show us our rites. Show us is from seeing with the eyes, so it takes two objects. It was also said: from seeing with the heart, and the speaker must take the verb from it to take three objects. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is separated by the fact that there is a transitive verb with a hamza from seeing with the heart to two objects like the non-transitive verb. Hatayit bin Ya’far, the brother of Al-Aswad bin Ya’far, said: Show me a horse that died of humiliation, because I see what you see, or an immortal miser. Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, Qatada, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Al-Suddi, Ruh from Yaqub, Rawis and Al-Soussi read: Arna with a sukoon on the ra in the Qur’an, and Abu Hatim chose this. Abu Amr read it with a stolen kasra on the ra, and the rest read it with a kasra, and Abu Ubaid chose this. Its original form is Arna with a hamza, so whoever reads it with a sukoon says: The hamza is gone and its vowel is gone and the ra remains silent as it is, and he provided evidence for this with the saying of the poet: Show us Abdullah's water jug so we can fill it with Zamzam water, for the people are thirsty. And whoever breaks it, he transfers the movement of the deleted hamza to the ra’, and Abu Amr asked for lightness. And on the authority of Shuja’ bin Abi Nasr, who was a trustworthy and truthful man, that he saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a dream, and he mentioned to him some of the letters of Abu Amr, but he did not respond to him except for two letters: this, and the other, what we abrogate from a verse or forget, with a hamza. The Almighty said: Our rites. It is said that the root of the word ritual in the language is washing. It is said: He washed his garment if he washed it. In Islamic law, it is a name for worship. It is said: A man is a devout worshipper. Scholars differed about what is meant by the rituals here. Some said: The rituals of Hajj and its landmarks, as stated by Qatada and Al-Suddi. Mujahid, Ata’ and Ibn Jurayj said: The rituals are the slaughterhouses, meaning the places of slaughter. It was also said: All the places of worship. Everything that is used as an act of worship to God Almighty is called a ritual or a ritual. The ritualist is like the worshipper. An-Nāṣik said: It is said naṣik yansuk, so it should have been said mansak based on this, except that there is no maf’al in the speech of the Arabs. On the authority of Zuhair bin Muhammad, he said: When Abraham, peace be upon him, finished building the Sacred House, he said: O Lord, I have finished, so show us our rituals. So God Almighty sent Gabriel to him, so he performed Hajj with him. Then when he returned from Arafat and the Day of Sacrifice came, Satan appeared to him and said to him: Pebble it. So he pebbled it with seven pebbles, then the next day, then the third day. Then he ascended Thabir and said: O servants of God, answer his call. So his call was heard from among the seas by those who had in their hearts an atom’s weight of faith, so he said: Here I am, O God, here I am. He said: And there remained on the face of the earth seven Muslims or more, had it not been for that, the earth and all who were on it would have been destroyed. And the first to answer him were the people of Yemen. On the authority of Abu Majlaz, he said: When Ibrahim finished performing Tawaf around the House, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and showed him the circumambulation of the House - he said: I think he said: Safa and Marwa - then they went to Aqaba and Satan appeared to them, so Gabriel took seven pebbles and gave Ibrahim seven pebbles, so he threw and said Allahu Akbar, and said to Ibrahim: Throw and say Allahu Akbar, so they threw and said Allahu Akbar with each throw until the devil disappeared. Then they went to the middle Jamrah, and Satan appeared to them, so Gabriel took seven pebbles and gave Ibrahim seven pebbles, and said: Throw and say Allahu Akbar, so they threw and said Allahu Akbar with each throw until the devil disappeared. Then they came to the furthest Jamrah and Satan appeared to them, Gabriel took seven pebbles and gave Ibrahim seven pebbles and said: Throw and say Allahu Akbar, so they threw with each throw until the devil disappeared. Then he brought him a group and said: This is where the people gather for prayers. Then he brought him to Arafat and said: Do you know? Yes, and that is why it was called Arafat. It was narrated that he said to him: Do you know, do you know, do you know? That is, Mina and the plural is this, so he said: Yes, so that place was called Arafat. On the authority of Khasif bin Abd al-Rahman that Mujahid told him: When Abraham, peace be upon him, said: And show us our rites, meaning Safa and Marwa, and they are among the rites of God according to the text of the Qur’an, then Gabriel took him out, and when he passed by Jamrat al-Aqaba, Satan was on it, so Gabriel said to him: Say Allahu Akbar and throw it, so Satan rose to the middle one, so Gabriel said: Say Allahu Akbar and throw it, then at the farthest Jamrat that is. Then he took him to al-Mash’ar al-Haram, then he brought him to Arafat and said to him: Did you know what I showed you? He said: Yes, so it was called Arafat for that, according to what was said, he said: So he announced the Hajj to the people, he said: How should I say it? He said: Say: O people, respond to your Lord, three times, so he did, and they said: Here I am, O God, here I am. He said: Whoever responds on that day is a pilgrim. In another narration: When he called, he turned and called in every direction, and people responded from every east and west, and the mountains lowered themselves even after his voice. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: When Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him, finished building the Sacred House, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said to him: Go around it seven times. So he and Ishmael, peace be upon them, went around it seven times, touching all the corners in each circumambulation. When they completed seven, they prayed two rak’ahs behind the station. He said: Gabriel stood up and showed him all the rituals: Safa, Marwah, Mina, and Muzdalifah. He said: When he entered Mina and descended from Aqaba, Satan appeared to him..., and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Ibn Ishaq said: It has reached me that Adam, peace be upon him, used to touch all the corners before Abraham, peace be upon him. He said: Isaac and Sarah performed Hajj from Syria, and Abraham, peace be upon him, used to perform Hajj every year on Buraq, and after that, the prophets and nations performed Hajj. Muhammad bin Sabit narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “The Prophet was one of the prophets who, when his nation perished, would go to Mecca and worship there, he and those who believed with him, until they died. Noah, Hud, and Salih died there, and their graves are between Zamzam and Al-Hijr.” Ibn Wahb mentioned that Shu’ayb died in Mecca, he and those who believed with him, and their graves are in the west of Mecca, between Dar Al-Nadwa and Bani Sahm. Ibn Abbas said: In the Sacred Mosque there are two graves, and there is no other, the grave of Ismail and the grave of Shu’ayb, peace be upon them. The grave of Ismail is in Al-Hijr, and the grave of Shu’ayb is opposite the Black Stone. Abdullah bin Damrah Al-Saluli said: Between the corner and the station and Zamzam are the graves of ninety-nine prophets who came as pilgrims and were buried there, may the prayers of God be upon them all. The Almighty said: And forgive us. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of the words of Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them, And forgive us, even though they were infallible prophets. A group said: They sought steadfastness and permanence, not that they had committed a sin. I said: This is good, and what is better than that is that when they knew the rituals and built the House, they wanted to explain to the people and let them know that that situation and those places are the place for absolving oneself of sins and seeking repentance. It was said that the meaning is: And repent to the oppressors among us. The discussion of the infallibility of the prophets, peace be upon them, has already passed in the story of Adam, peace be upon him, and the meaning of His statement, Indeed, You are the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful, has been presented, so there is no need to repeat it.
2:129: The Almighty said: Our Lord, and send among them a Messenger from among themselves meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. In the reading of Abi, And send at the end of them a Messenger from among them. And "Khalid bin Ma'dan narrated: A group of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: O Messenger of God, tell us about yourself, he said: Yes, I am the supplication of my father Abraham and the good report of Jesus." And a Messenger means a messenger, and it is a fa'ul from the message. Ibn al-Anbari said: It seems that its origin is from their saying: a she-camel that is a messenger and a messenger, if it is easy to walk and goes ahead of the she-camels. And the neglected group that is sent is called rusul, and its plural is arsil. And it is said: The people came arsil, meaning some of them follow each other, and from this the word rasul is used for the camel, because it is sent from the udder. God the Almighty said: And teaches them the Book and wisdom. The Book means the Qur’an. Wisdom means knowledge of religion, understanding of interpretation, and understanding which is a characteristic and light from God the Almighty. Malik said this, and Ibn Wahb narrated it from him. Ibn Zayd said this, and Qatadah said: Wisdom is the Sunnah and the explanation of the laws. It was also said: Judgment and decree in particular, but the meaning is close. Teaching was attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in that he gives the matters that he looks into, and teaches the way to look into them through what God sends to him from His revelation. And purifies them means cleanses them from the harm of polytheism, according to Ibn Jurayj and others. Zakat means purification, and this has been mentioned previously. It was also said that the verses are the recitation of the apparent meaning of the words. The Book means the meanings of the words. Wisdom means judgment, and this is what God intended by the address, whether absolute or restricted, explanatory or ambiguous, general or specific, and this is the meaning of what was mentioned previously, and God the Almighty knows best. The Mighty means the inaccessible, which cannot be reached or overcome. Ibn Kaysan said: Its meaning is the one who is not incapable of anything, and its evidence is: And nothing in the heavens or on the earth could make God incapable of anything. Al-Kisa’i: The Almighty, the Victorious, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: And He made me powerful in speech. And in the proverb: Whoever is powerful, is spoiled. That is, whoever is powerful, is robbed. And it was said: The Almighty is the one who has no equal, and its explanation is: There is nothing like Him. We have further explained this meaning in His name Al-Aziz in the book Al-Asna fi Sharh Asma God Al-Husna. The meaning of Al-Hakim was mentioned previously, and praise be to God.
2:130: The Almighty said: And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except he who makes a fool of himself? "Min is an interrogative in the nominative case as a subject, and yirghib is the relative clause of min". "Except he who makes a fool of himself" is in the predicate. It is a rebuke and a reproach in which the meaning of negation is found, i.e. and what is desired, said Al-Nahhas. The meaning is: he renounces it and distances himself from it, i.e. from the religion, which is the religion and the law. "Except he who makes a fool of himself" Qatadah said: They are the Jews and Christians, they turned away from the religion of Abraham and adopted Judaism and Christianity as an innovation that is not from God Almighty. Al-Zajjaj said: "Safa" means ignorance, i.e. he was ignorant of his own affairs and did not think about them. Abu Ubaidah said: The meaning is he destroyed himself. Tha'lab and Al-Mubarrad narrated that safa with a kasra on the fa' is transitive like safa with a fatha on the fa' and a shaddah on it. It was narrated from Abu Al-Khattab and Yunus that it is a language. Al-Akhfash said: He acted foolishly towards himself meaning he did something foolish to make him foolish. It is also narrated from him that it is a language meaning foolishness, as narrated by Al-Mahdawi, and the first was mentioned by Al-Marudi. As for foolishness with a damma on the fa, it is intransitive, as Al-Mubarrad and Tha’lab said. Al-Kisa’i narrated from Al-Akhfash that the meaning is ignorance of himself, so the fi was deleted and it was made accusative. Al-Akhfash said: The same applies to the marriage contract, meaning on the marriage contract. This follows the doctrine of Sibawayh in what he narrated of their saying: So-and-so struck the back and the stomach, meaning in the back and the stomach. Al-Farra’: It is a distinction. Ibn Bahr said: Its meaning is ignorance of himself and what is in it of indications and signs indicating that it has a Creator like whom nothing is, so he knows through it the oneness of God and His power. I said: This is the meaning of Al-Zajjaj’s statement: “He thinks about himself, of two hands with which he strikes, two feet on which he walks, an eye with which he sees, an ear with which he hears, a tongue with which he speaks, molars that grow for him when he no longer needs to be breastfed and needs food to grind food with, a stomach prepared for cooking food, a liver to which the cream ascends, veins and passages through which it reaches the extremities, and intestines into which the weight of the food settles and protrudes from the lower part of the body. This is evidence that he has a Creator who is capable, all-knowing, and wise. This is the meaning of the Most High’s statement: ‘And in yourselves, then will you not see?’ Al-Khattabi, may God have mercy on him, pointed to this. More clarification will come in Surat Adh-Dhariyat, God willing.” This verse was used as evidence by those who said: The law of Abraham is our law except for what was abrogated from it. This is like his saying: The religion of your father Abraham, “I follow the religion of Abraham.” And its explanation will come. The Almighty said: And We had chosen him in this world meaning, We chose him for the message and made him pure from impurities. The root of istafinahu is istafinahu, the ta was replaced with a ta to match the sad in emphasis. The word is derived from al-safwah, and its meaning is to choose the purest. God the Almighty said: And indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. The righteous in the Hereafter is the one who wins. Then it was said: How is it permissible to present in the Hereafter while it is included in the relative clause? An-Nahhas said: The answer is that the meaning is not he will be among the righteous in the Hereafter, so the relative clause would have been presented. The Arab scholars have several opinions on this: One of them is that the meaning is and he will be righteous in the Hereafter, then it was deleted. It was said: in the Hereafter is related to a deleted source, meaning his righteousness in the Hereafter. The third opinion is that the righteous does not mean those who are righteous, but it is a name that stands on its own, just as one says man and boy. I said: A fourth statement is that the meaning is that he is among the righteous in the work of the Hereafter, so the speech is about the deletion of an adjective. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: There is an inversion in the speech, its meaning is that We have chosen him, and he is the world and the Hereafter, and he is among the righteous. Hajjaj ibn Hajjaj narrated - and he is Hajjaj al-Aswad, and he is also Hajjaj al-Ahwal, known as Saq al-Asal - he said: I heard Muawiyah ibn Qurra say: O God, the righteous are You who have made them righteous and provided for them if they act in obedience to You and You are pleased with them. O God, as You have made them righteous, make us righteous, and as You have provided for them if they act in obedience to You and You are pleased with them, provide for us to act in obedience to You, and be pleased with us.
2:131: God Almighty said: When his Lord said to him, ‘Submit,’ he said, ‘I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds.’ The factor in when is his saying: meaning, We chose him when his Lord said to him, Submit. This saying was from God when He tested him with the planets, the moon, and the sun. Ibn Kaysan and Al-Kalbi said: meaning, Purify your religion for God through monotheism. It was also said: Submit and be humble. Ibn Abbas said: He only said that to him when he left the flock, as will be mentioned in Al-An’am. Islam here is in its most perfect form. Islam in the speech of the Arabs: submission and obedience to the one who submits. Not every submission is faith, and not every faith is Islam, because whoever believes in God has submitted and obeyed God. Not everyone who submits believes in God, because he may speak in fear of the sword, and that is not faith, contrary to the Qadarites and the Khawarij, who said: Islam is faith, so every believer is a Muslim, and every Muslim is a believer, based on His saying: Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam. This indicates that Islam is the religion, and that whoever is not a Muslim is not a believer. Our evidence is the saying of God the Almighty: The desert Arabs say, ‘We believe.’ Say, ‘You have not believed, but say, ‘We have submitted,’ (al-Baqarah 2:170). So God the Almighty informed us that not everyone who submits to Islam is a believer, indicating that not every Muslim is a believer. And the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said to Sa`d ibn Waqqas when he said to him, Give to so-and-so, for he is a believer. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said, Or a Muslim. The hadith was narrated by Muslim, indicating that faith is not Islam, for faith is inward and Islam is outward, and this is clear. Faith may be used to mean Islam and Islam, and what is meant by it is faith, because one of them is necessary for the other and emanates from it, like Islam, which is the fruit of faith and an indication of its correctness, so inform him. And God is the Grantor of success.
2:132: God Almighty says: And Abraham enjoined it upon his sons and so did Jacob, [saying], ‘O my sons, indeed God has chosen for you this religion, so do not die except as Muslims.’ God the Almighty said: And Abraham enjoined it meaning the religion. It was said: with the word which is his saying: I have submitted to the Lord of the worlds and this is more correct because it is the closest mentioned, meaning say we have submitted. And wasā and awsā are two dialects of the Quraysh and others with the same meaning, like karāmna and akramna, and it was recited with them. In the Mushaf of Abdullah it is wasā and in the Mushaf of Uthman it is wasā and it is the reading of the people of Medina and Ash-Sham. The rest of them are wasā and it has the meaning of abundance. And Abraham raised with his action, and Jacob is conjoined with it. It was said: it is a disconnected and renewed sentence, and the meaning is: And Jacob enjoined and said, O my sons, indeed God has chosen for you the religion, so Abraham enjoined his sons, then Jacob enjoined his sons after him. And the sons of Abraham were Ishmael, and his mother was Hagar the Copt, and he was his eldest son, Abraham moved him to Mecca while he was an infant. It was said: He was two years old, and it was said: He was fourteen years old, and the first is more correct, as will be explained in Surat Ibrahim, God willing. He was born fourteen years before his brother Isaac, and he died when he was one hundred and thirty-seven years old. It was said: One hundred and thirty. And he was eighty-nine years old when his father Abraham, peace be upon them, died, and he was the sacrificed one according to one opinion. And Isaac was Sarah’s slave girl, and he was the sacrificed one according to another opinion, and this is more correct, as will be explained in Surat As-Saffat, God willing. Among his descendants are the Romans, the Greeks, the Armenians, and those who are like them, and the Children of Israel. Isaac lived one hundred and eighty years, and died in the Holy Land and was buried next to his father Abraham, the friend of God, peace be upon them. Then when Sarah died, Abraham married Qantour, the daughter of Yaqtan the Canaanite, and she bore him Midian, Madain, Nahshan, Zimran, Nashiq, and Shuyukh. Then he died, peace be upon him. There were about two thousand six hundred years between his death and the birth of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Jews reduce that by about four hundred years. The sons of Jacob will be mentioned in Surat Yusuf, God willing. Amr bin Faid Al-Aswari and Ismail bin Abdullah Al-Makki read: And Jacob in the accusative case in apposition to his daughter, so Jacob would be included among those who made a will. Al-Qushayri said: “And Jacob was read in the accusative case in apposition to his sons, and this is far-fetched, because Jacob was not among the sons of Abraham when he made a will to them, and it is not reported that Jacob met his grandfather Abraham, but rather he was born after the death of Abraham, and that Jacob also made a will to his sons as Abraham did. The naming of the sons of Jacob will come, God willing.” Al-Kalbi said: When Jacob entered Egypt, he saw them worshipping idols, fires, and cows. He gathered his children and feared for them and said: What will you worship after me? It is said that he was called Jacob because he and Esau were twins, and he came out of his mother's womb following the heel of his brother Esau. There is a problem with that, because this is an Arabic derivation, and Jacob is a foreign name, even though it agrees with the Arabic name for it, like the male partridge. He lived, peace be upon him, for one hundred and forty-seven years and died in Egypt. He ordered that he be carried to the Holy Land and buried near his father Isaac, so Joseph carried him and buried him near him. The Almighty’s saying: O my son means that O my son, and this is also the reading of Abi, Ibn Masoud and Ad-Dahhak. Al-Farra’ said: “I omitted ‘an’ because the recommendation is like the statement, and every statement that refers to the statement can be entered into by ‘an’ and its omission can be permitted. He said: The grammarians’ saying that he only meant ‘an’ so it was omitted is nothing. An-Nahhas: ‘O my son’ is a vocative with an added letter, and this ‘ya’ of the self cannot be opened here except because if it were quiescent, two quiescent letters would meet, and the same is in “bi-mushrikhi”. Indeed, God broke ‘an’ because ‘awsā’ and ‘qāl’ are one. It was said: on the implication of the statement. Istafa means chose. The rajaz poet said: O son of kings, you have inherited the kingdoms of succession from God, which He has given you. He chose her for you and she chose you for him The religion is yours meaning Islam, and the alif and lam in religion are for the covenant, because they had known it. Do not die except as Muslims is a clear brevity. The meaning is: adhere to Islam and continue upon it and do not leave it until you die. So he used a concise expression that includes the intended meaning, and includes an admonition and a reminder of death, because a person realizes that he will die and does not know when, so if he is ordered to do something that death will not come to him except while he is upon it, then the address has been directed from the time of the order, constantly and constantly. And there is no prohibition of do not die in the place of a jussive with a prohibition, emphasized with the heavy nun, and the waw was deleted due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. Except as you are Muslims is a subject and predicate in the place of a state, meaning having good thoughts about your Lord, and it was said sincere, and it was said entrusted, and it was said believers.
2:133: The Almighty said: "Or were you witnesses?" Shahada is the predicate of kana, and it was not declined because it contains the feminine alif, and it was added to feminize the group just as the ha' is added. The address is to the Jews and Christians who attribute to Abraham what he did not command his sons, and that they are Jewish and Christian, so God rejected their statement and their lie, and said to them by way of rebuke: Did you have Jacob as witnesses and you knew what he commanded, so you claim based on knowledge? That is: You did not witness, rather you are fabricating. And or means rather, that is, rather your ancestors Jacob witnessed. The factor in the first idh is the meaning of testimony, and the second idh is a substitute for the first. And shahidaa is the plural of shahid, meaning present. The meaning of "Jacob was present at death" is its preliminaries and causes, otherwise if death had been present he would not have been able to say anything. He referred to the object of worship as what and did not say who because he wanted to test them. If he had said who his aim would have been to see who among them would be guided. Rather, he wanted to test them, so he said what. Also, the commonly known objects of worship other than God are inanimate objects such as idols, fire, the sun, and stones. So he asked about what they worshipped from these. The meaning of after me is after my death. It was narrated that when Jacob was given the choice as the prophets were given the choice, he chose death and said: Give me time so that I may advise my children and family. So he gathered them and said this to them, and they were guided and said: We will worship your God. So they showed him their steadfastness in religion and their knowledge of God Almighty. God the Almighty said: They said, ‘We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac.’ “Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac” is in the accusative case as a substitute, and it was not declined because it is foreign. Al-Kisa’i said: If you wish, you can decline Isaac and make him from the word crushing, and decline Jacob and make him from the word bird. God called each of the paternal uncles and grandfathers a father, and began by mentioning the grandfather, then Ishmael the paternal uncle because he is older than Isaac. Ilaha is a substitute for Ilahak as a substitute for the indefinite noun from the definite noun, and it was repeated for the benefit of the description of oneness. It was said: Ilaha is a state. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is a good statement, because the purpose is to prove the state of oneness. Al-Hasan, Yahya ibn Ya’mar, Al-Jahdary, and Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi read Ila Abika and there are two interpretations for it: One of them: That they were individuals and he wanted Abraham alone, and he hated to make Ishmael a father because he was an uncle. An-Nahhas said: This is not necessary, because the Arabs call the uncle a father. Second: According to Sibawayh’s doctrine, Abiyk is the plural of Salamah. Sibawayh narrated Ab, Aboon, and Abeyan, as the poet said: We said, "Submit, for we are your brothers." Another said: When our voices became clear, we cried and offered our fathers. The Almighty’s saying, And we are Muslims to Him, is a subject and predicate, and it is possible that it is in the position of a state, and the agent is we worship.
2:134: The Almighty said: That is a nation that has passed away. That is the subject, and nation is the predicate. Has passed away is an adjective for nation, and if you wish, it is the predicate of the subject, and nation can be a substitute for that. For it is what it has earned. What is in the nominative case as a subject or as an adjective according to the Kufians. And for you is what you have earned is similar to it, meaning good and evil. In this is evidence that deeds and earnings are attributed to the servant, and if God Almighty has enabled him to do that, if it is good then it is by His grace and if it is evil then it is by His justice. This is the doctrine of the people of the Sunnah, and there are many verses in the Qur'an with this meaning. So the servant acquires his actions, in the sense that he was created with an ability that is comparable to the action, by which he realizes the difference between the movement of choice and the movement of trembling, for example, and that is the ability to fulfill the basis of obligation. The Jabriyah said that the servant does not acquire, and that he is like a plant that is moved by the winds. The Qadarites and Mu'tazilites said the opposite of these two statements, and that the servant creates his actions. God Almighty says: And you will not be asked about what they used to do. That is, no one will be held accountable for another’s sin, like God Almighty says: And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. That is, no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another, and it will come.
2:135: God Almighty says: And they say, ‘Be Jews or Christians [so] you will be guided.’ Say, ‘Rather, [we follow] the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists.’ God the Almighty said: And they said, ‘Be Jews or Christians [so] you will be guided.’ Every group called to what they were upon, so God the Almighty responded to them by saying: Rather, a religion. That is, say, O Muhammad: Rather, we follow a religion. This is why the word religion was attributed to. It was said that the meaning is, Rather, we are guided by the religion of Abraham. So when the preposition was deleted, it became accusative. Al-A’raj and Ibn Abi Ubaidah read: Rather, a religion in the nominative case, and the meaning is, Rather, guidance is a religion, or our religion is the religion of Abraham. And Hanif is inclined away from the hated religions to the truth, the religion of Abraham. And it is in the accusative case as a state, as Al-Zajjaj said. That is, rather, we follow the religion of Abraham in this case. Ali bin Sulayman said: It is accusative on I mean, and the state is incorrect. It is not permissible for a young Hind man to come to me in a hurry. And Abraham was called Hanif because he leaned toward the religion of God, which is Islam. And hanif means inclination, and from it a man is Hanifa, and a man is a hanaf, and he is the one whose feet lean each one of them toward the other with its toes. Umm Al-Ahnaf said: By God, if it weren't for Hanf's foot, there wouldn't be anyone like him among your young men. The poet said: If the evening shade turns, his banner is pure, and in the morning he is victorious. Which chameleon faces the Qiblah in the evening, and the East in the morning, and it is the Qiblah of the Christians. Some people said: Hanif is uprightness, so the religion of Abraham was called Hanif because of its uprightness. And the crooked-footed person was called Hanif, in optimism for uprightness, just as someone who has been bitten is called safe, and someone who has been destroyed is called a desert, according to most of them.
2:136: The Almighty said: Say, ‘We believe in God.’ Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The People of the Book used to read the Torah in Hebrew and explain it in Arabic to the people of Islam. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not believe the People of the Scripture, nor disbelieve them, but say, ‘We believe in God and in what was revealed to us,’ (al-Anfal 2:10). Muhammad ibn Sirin said: If it is said to you, Are you a believer? then say, We believe in God and in what was revealed to us, and in what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac (al-Anfal 2:10). Most of the early Muslims disliked a man saying, I am a true believer. This will be explained in Al-Anfal, God willing. Some of the early Muslims were asked about a man who was asked, Do you believe in so-and-so the Prophet? So he called him by a name he did not know. If he said, Yes, then perhaps he was not a prophet, as he had testified to the prophethood of someone other than a prophet. If he said, No, then perhaps he was a prophet, as he had denied a prophet. So what should he do? He said, He should say, ‘If he is a prophet, then I believe in him.’ The address in this verse is to this nation, teach them faith. Ibn Abbas said, “A group of Jews came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and asked him about the prophets he should believe in, so the verse was revealed.” When Jesus was mentioned, they said: We do not believe in Jesus or anyone who believes in him. God the Almighty said: And what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes. The plural of Abraham is Abraham, and Ishmael is Sma’il, as Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said, and the Kufians said so, and they narrated Brahimah and Sma’ala, and they narrated Brahim and Sma’il. Muhammad bin Yazid said: This is a mistake, because this is not the place for the hamza to be added, but I say: Abarah and Asma’, and it is permissible to Abariyah and Asma’. Ahmad bin Yahya permitted Barah, as it is said in the diminutive Barih. The plural of Ishaq is Asa’iq, and the Kufians narrated Asa’aqah and Asa’aq, and likewise Ya’qub and Ya’aqib, and Ya’qub and Ya’aqub. An-Nahhas said: As for Israel, we do not know of anyone who permits the deletion of the hamza from the beginning of it, but rather it is said Asareel, and the Kufians narrated Asarlah and Asarl. The rule in all of this is to pluralize Muslim and say: Ibrahimoon, Ishaaqoon, and Ya’quboon, and Muslim is not used. The tribes: the descendants of Jacob, peace be upon him, and they are twelve sons, each of whom had a nation of people, and each one of them is a tribe. The tribe in the Children of Israel is like the tribe in the children of Ishmael. They were called the tribes from the tribe, which means succession, so they are a group that follows one another. It was said: Its origin is from the tribe with a fat-ha, which means trees, meaning they are in large numbers like trees, the singular is a tribe. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: This is explained to you by what Muhammad ibn Ja`far al-Anbari told us, he said Abu Nujayd al-Daqqaq told us, he said al-Aswad told us from the Children of Israel except ten: Noah, Shu`ayb, Hud, Salih, Lot, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Ishmael, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. No one had two names except Asa and Jacob. The tribe: the group and the tribe that go back to one origin. The hair of the tribe and the tribe is not curly. We do not differentiate between any of them. Al-Farra’ said: That is, we do not believe in some of them and disbelieve in others, as the Jews and Christians did.
2:137: God Almighty says: “If they believe in the same as you believe, then they are rightly guided. But if they turn away, then they are only in dissension. So God will suffice you against them. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” The Almighty says: If they believe in the same as you believe in, they have been guided. The address is to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation. If they believe like your belief, and are truthful like your belief, they have been guided. Thus, the similarity occurred between the two beliefs. It was said that the ba is an additional letter for emphasis. Ibn Abbas used to read, as narrated by al-Tabari: If they believe in that which you believe in, they have been guided. This is the meaning of the reading, even if it differs from the Qur’an. Mithl is an additional letter as it is in His statement: There is nothing like Him, meaning there is nothing like Him. The poet said: So become like eaten straw And the rest of it was narrated that Shu'bah narrated to us on the authority of Abu Hamza on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Do not say: If they believe in the same as you believe in, then God has no equal, but say: In that in which you believe. Ali bin Nasr Al-Jahdhami followed him on the authority of Shu'bah, and Al-Bayhaqi mentioned it. The meaning is: If they believe in your Prophet and in general the Prophets and do not differentiate between them as you have not differentiated, then they are guided, but if they refuse except to differentiate, then they are the ones who have turned away from the religion and are dissidents. Then God will suffice you against them. It was narrated on the authority of a group of the people of insight who said: It is possible that the Kaf in his statement: There is nothing like Him is redundant. He said: What was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his prohibition of general recitation is something he went to for the sake of exaggeration in denying likeness to God Almighty. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is from Ibn Abbas in terms of interpretation, meaning that it is thus, so let it be interpreted. It was also said: The Baa' means on, and the meaning is: If they believe in the same as your belief. It was said: It is like its door, meaning like the house. Its evidence is his saying: And say, ‘I believe in what God has revealed of the Book.’ And his saying: And say, ‘We believe in that which was revealed to us and revealed to you.’ The Almighty said: But if they turn away meaning from faith they are only in dissension. Zayd ibn Aslam said: Dissension is dispute. It was also said: Dissension is argument, opposition, and hostility. Its origin is from shaq which means side, so it is as if each of the two groups is in a different side than the other. The poet said: How long will you kill scholars by force and explode with discord and hypocrisy? Another said: Otherwise, know that you and I are rebels as long as we remain in discord. It was said: Discord is taken from the verb to make difficult, so it is as if each of the two groups is keen on what is difficult for the other. His saying: God will suffice you against them means God will suffice His Messenger against his enemy. This was a promise from God to His Prophet, peace be upon him, that He will suffice him against those who opposed him and those who opposed him from the guardians by guiding him from the believers, so He fulfilled the promise to him, and that was in killing Banu Qaynuqa and Banu Qurayza and expelling Banu Nadir. The kaf, ha and mim are in the accusative case as objects. It is permissible in other than the Qur’an to say: God will suffice you against them. This letter God will suffice you against them is the one upon which the blood of Uthman fell when he was killed by the Prophet, peace be upon him, informing him of that. The All-Hearing is for the words of every speaker, The All-Knowing is what He carries out in His servants and conducts upon them. It was narrated that Abu Dulamah entered upon al-Mansur wearing a long skullcap, a coat of mail with written between its shoulders God will suffice you against them, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, and a sword hung from his waist. Al-Mansur had ordered the soldiers to wear this uniform, so he said to him: How are you, Abu Dulamah? He said: Be glad, O Commander of the Faithful! He said: How is that? He said: What do you think of a man whose face is in the middle, his sword is in his anus, and who has thrown the Book of God behind his back! Al-Mansur laughed at him and ordered that that outfit to be changed immediately.
2:138: God Almighty says: The dye of God, and who is better than God at dyeing? And we are His worshippers. There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: The dye of God. Al-Akhfash and others said: The religion of God, and it is a substitute for millet. Al-Kisa’i said: It is in the accusative case, assuming they followed. Or it is an inducement, meaning they adhered. If it was read in the nominative case, it would be permissible, meaning it is the dye of God. Shaiban narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: The Jews dye their children as Jews, and the Christians dye their children as Christians, and the dye of God is Islam. Al-Zajjaj said: What indicates this is that dye is a substitute for millet. Mujahid said: Meaning the nature of God upon which He created people. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: Mujahid’s statement goes back to Islam, because the nature is the beginning of creation, and the beginning of what they were created upon is Islam. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aliyah, and Qatada: The dye is the religion. The origin of that is that the Christians used to dye their children in water, which is what they call baptism, and they used to say: This is a purification for them. Ibn Abbas said: It is that when a child was born to the Christians and seven days passed, they would dip him in their water called baptismal water, and they would dye him with it to purify the place of circumcision, because circumcision is purification. So when they did that, they would say: Now he has truly become a Christian. So God Almighty responded to them by saying: The dye of God, meaning the dye of God is the best dye, which is Islam. So religion was called dye as a metaphor and a figure of speech, because its actions and mark appear on the religious person, just as the trace of dye appears on a garment. And some of the poets of the kings of Hamdan said: Every people have a dye, and Hamdan's dye is the best dye. We dyed our children on that, so be generous with dyeing us in dyeing It was said: The dye is the bathing for those who want to enter Islam, instead of Christian baptism, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. I said: According to this interpretation, washing the infidel is an obligatory act of worship, and this is the issue: Second: Because the meaning of the dye of God is the washing of God, that is, wash yourselves when you become Muslim with the washing that God has made obligatory upon you. And with this meaning came the second Sunnah in Qais bin Asim and Thamamah bin Aththal when they became Muslim. Abu Hatim Al-Basti narrated in his Sahih Musnad “On the authority of Abu Hurairah on his authority: That Thamamah Al-Hanafi was taken prisoner and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by him one day and he became Muslim, so he sent him to the garden of Abu Talha and ordered him to wash himself, so he washed himself and prayed two rak’ahs, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your companion’s Islam is good.” And he also came out. On the authority of Qais bin Asim that he converted to Islam, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to wash himself with water and lotus leaves. Al-Nasa’i mentioned it and Abu Muhammad Abdul Haqq authenticated it. It was said that drawing close to God Almighty is called dyeing, as narrated by Ibn Faris in Al-Mujmal. Al-Jawhari said: The dye of God is His religion. It was said that dyeing is circumcision. Abraham was circumcised, so the dye was used for circumcision because of their dyeing the boys in water, as Al-Farra’ said. And we are His worshippers is a subject and predicate.
2:139: God Almighty said: “Say: Do you argue with us about God while He is our Lord and your Lord? For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds, and we are sincere to Him.” Al-Hasan said: The argument was that they said: We are closer to God than you, because we are the sons of God and His beloved. It was also said: Because of the precedence of our fathers and our books, and because we did not worship idols. So the meaning of the verse is: Say to them, O Muhammad, that is, say to these Jews and Christians who claimed that they are the sons of God and His beloved and claimed that they are closer to God than you because of the precedence of their fathers and their books: Do you argue with us? That is, do you seek from us the proof for your claim and the Lord and the challenge, and everyone is rewarded according to his deeds, so what effect does the precedence of the religion have? The meaning of in God means in His religion and closeness to Him and favor for Him. The reading of the group is: Do you argue with us? It is permissible to combine two similar letters of the same type with vowels, because the second is like a separate letter. Ibn Muhaisin read atahajawuna with assimilation because of the combination of similar letters. Al-Nahhas said: This is permissible except that it is contrary to the majority. It is permissible to say atahajawuna by deleting the second nun, as Nafi’ read fa bima tabashrun What do you give good tidings of?”. God the Almighty said: And We are sincere to Him meaning sincere in worship, and it contains the meaning of rebuke, meaning that you have not been sincere, so how do you claim what We are from you? Sincerity in reality is purifying the action from the observation of creation, “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God the Almighty says: I am the best partner, so whoever associates a partner with Me, he is for My partner. O people, make your deeds sincere for God the Almighty, for God the Almighty does not accept anything except that which is sincere for Him. And do not say: This is for God and for the womb, for they are for the womb and God has nothing of them. And do not say: This is for God and for your faces, for they are for your faces and God the Almighty has nothing of them.” Narrated by Ad-Dahhak bin Qais Al-Fihri, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said:... and he mentioned it. Ad-Darqutni included it. Ruwaym said: Sincerity in action is that its doer does not want any compensation for it in the two abodes or a share from the two angels. Al-Junayd said: “Sincerity is a secret between the servant and God. No angel knows it to write it down, no devil to corrupt it, and no desire to make it sway.” Abu al-Qasim al-Qushayri and others reported that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I asked Gabriel about sincerity, what it is. He said: I asked the Lord of Glory about sincerity, what it is. He said: It is a secret of my secrets that I have entrusted to the heart of the one of my servants whom I love.”
2:140: The Almighty said: Or do you say meaning they said, and Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and Asim read in the narration of Hafs you say with a ta', and it is a good reading, because the speech is consistent, as if the meaning is: Do you argue with us about God or do you say that the prophets were of your religion? So it is the connected umm, and according to the reading of those who read it with a disconnected ya, so it would be two statements and umm would mean rather. Hud is the predicate of kana and the predicate of in in the sentence. And it is permissible in places other than the Qur'an to raise Hud as the predicate of in, and kana would be cancelled, as mentioned by Al-Nahhas. God Almighty says: “Say: Are you more knowing or is God?” This is a confirmation and rebuke of their claim that they were Jews or Christians. God responded to them by saying that He knows them better than you do, meaning that they were neither Jews nor Christians. God the Almighty said: And who is more unjust? The wording is a question, and the meaning is: No one is more unjust. than he who conceals testimony meaning their knowledge that the prophets were Muslims. It was said: what they concealed of the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was said by Qatada, and the first is more similar to the context of the verse. And God is not unaware of what you do is a warning and notification that He did not leave their affair in vain and that He will reward them for their deeds. The unaware is the one who does not pay attention to matters out of negligence on his part. It is taken from the word ghafl which means a land that is known but has no trace of cultivation. A ghafl camel means that it has no mark. A ghafl man means that he has not experienced matters. Al-Kisa’i said: A ghafl land that has not rained. Ghaflat an al-shay’ I neglected something means I neglected it while remembering you.
2:141: He repeated it because it included the meaning of threat and intimidation, meaning that if those prophets were rewarded for their leadership and virtue, then you are more deserving of it, so emphasis was required, and that is why he repeated it.
2:142: God Almighty says: “The foolish among the people will say, ‘What has turned them away from the qiblah which they used to face?’ Say, ‘To God belong the east and the west. He guides whom He wills to a straight path.’” There is one issue: First: The Almighty’s saying: The foolish among the people will say. God the Almighty knows that they will say about the believers’ conversion from Ash-Sham to the Kaaba: What has turned them away? And will say means said. He made the future tense the place of the past, indicating the continuity of that and that they will continue with that saying. He specified by His saying: of the people because foolishness can be in inanimate objects and animals. What is meant by fools is all those who say what has turned them away. Fools are a plural, the singular of which is safiyah, which means light-minded, from their saying: a lightly woven garment, as mentioned earlier. Women are safiyah. Al-Mu’arraj said: The fool is the liar who deliberately goes against what he knows. Qatrab: the unjust and ignorant. What is meant by fools here are the Jews in Madinah, as Mujahid said. As-Suddi: the hypocrites. Az-Zajjaj: the infidels of Quraysh, when they denied the conversion of the Qiblah, they said: Muhammad longs for his birth and will soon return to your religion. The Jews said: His matter has become confusing and bewildered for him. The hypocrites said: What turned them away from their Qiblah? And they mocked the Muslims. And turning them away means turning them away and diverting them. Second: The imams narrated, and the wording is Malik’s, on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: While the people were praying Fajr in Quba, someone came to them and said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) has received a Qur’an tonight, and he has been commanded to face the Kaaba, so they faced it. Their faces were towards Ash-Sham, so they turned towards the Kaaba. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) prayed towards Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, and he liked that his qiblah should be towards the Kaaba. The first prayer he prayed was the ‘Asr prayer, and some people prayed with him. A man who had prayed with the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) came out and passed by the people of the mosque while they were bowing and said: I bear witness by God that I prayed with the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) towards Makkah. So they turned as they were towards the Kaaba. The ones who died facing the qiblah before it was changed to face the Kaaba were men who were killed, and we did not know what to say about them. Then God the Almighty revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste. In this narration, it is the ‘Asr prayer, and in the narration of Malik, it is the Fajr prayer. It was said: This was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque of Bani Salamah while he was praying the noon prayer after two rak’ahs of it, so he turned during the prayer, and that mosque was called the Mosque of the Two Qiblas. Abu al-Faraj mentioned that Ibad ibn Nahik was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this prayer. Abu Omar mentioned in al-Tamhid on the authority of Nuwaylah bint Aslam, who was one of those who pledged allegiance, she said: We were praying the noon prayer when Abbad bin Bishr bin Qayzi came and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has faced the qiblah - or he said: the Sacred House - so the men moved to the women’s places, and the women moved to the men’s places. It was said: The verse was revealed in a prayer other than that, and this is most likely. The first prayer towards the Kaaba was the afternoon prayer, and God knows best. It was narrated: “The first person to pray facing the Kaaba when the qibla was changed from Jerusalem was Abu Saeed bin Al-Mu’alla. He was passing by the mosque and heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressing the people about changing the qibla from the pulpit while he was reciting this verse: ‘We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven’ until he finished the verse. So I said to my companion: ‘Come, let us pray two rak’ahs before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descends so that we will be the first to pray.’ So we hid ourselves behind a camel and prayed them. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended and led the people in the noon prayer that day.” Abu Omar said: Abu Saeed bin Al-Mu’alla has no other hadith than this one, and the hadith: ‘I used to pray’ is about the virtue of Al-Fatihah, narrated by Al-Bukhari, and it has been mentioned previously. Third: There is a difference of opinion regarding the time of the change of the Qiblah after his arrival in Medina. It was said: It was changed after a year, ten months or seventeen. A month, as in Bukhari. And it was also narrated by Al-Daraqutni on the authority of Al-Baraa, who said: We prayed with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) for sixteen months after his arrival in Medina, facing Jerusalem. Then God knew the inclination of His Prophet, so He revealed: We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven Al-Masjid an-Nabawi. In this narration, there is no doubt sixteen months. Malik narrated from Yahya ibn Sa`id from Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab that the turning was two months before the Battle of Badr. Ibrahim ibn Ishaq said: That was in Rajab of the year two. Abu Hatim al-Busti said: The Muslims prayed facing Jerusalem for seventeen months and three consecutive days, because his arrival in Medina was on Monday, twelve nights before the end of the month of Rabi` al-Awwal, and God the Almighty commanded him to face the Ka`bah on Tuesday, the fifteenth of Sha`ban. Fourth: The scholars also differed on how he faced Jerusalem, with three opinions: Al-Hasan said: It was from his opinion and effort, and Ikrimah and Abu Al-Aaliyah said it. The second: He was given a choice between it and the Kaaba, so he chose Jerusalem hoping for the Jews to believe and win them over, said Al-Tabari. Al-Zajjaj said: As a test for the polytheists because they were accustomed to the Kaaba. The third - which is what the majority say: Ibn Abbas and others - is that he was obliged to face it by the command of God Almighty and His revelation without a doubt, then God abrogated that and commanded him to face the Kaaba in his prayer, and they provided evidence for that with the words of God Almighty: And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face except that We might make evident who would follow the Messenger from who would turn on his heels Al-Akhbar 2:13. Fifth: They also differed when the prayer was first imposed on him in Mecca, was it towards Jerusalem or towards Mecca? There are two opinions. A group said: towards Jerusalem and in Medina for seventeen months, then God directed him to the Kaaba, as Ibn Abbas said. Others said: The first thing that was imposed on him was towards the Kaaba, and he continued to pray towards it throughout his stay in Mecca in the same way as the prayer of Abraham and Ishmael was. Then when he came to Medina, he prayed towards Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, according to the difference of opinion, then God directed him to the Kaaba. Abu Omar said: This is the more correct of the two opinions in my opinion. Another said: That is because when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, he wanted to renew his faith with the Jews, so he faced their Qiblah so that this would be more conducive to them. But when their stubbornness became clear and he despaired of them, he wanted to move towards the Kaaba, so he looked at the sky. His love for the Kaaba was because it was the Qiblah of Abraham, according to Ibn Abbas. It was said: Because it was more conducive to the Arabs’ conversion to Islam, and it was said: To oppose the Jews, according to Mujahid. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah Al-Riyahi that he said: It was the mosque of Salih, peace be upon him, and his qiblah was towards the Kaaba. He said: Moses, peace be upon him, used to pray towards the rock towards the Kaaba, and it is the qiblah of all the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them all. Sixth: In this verse there is clear evidence that in the rulings of God Almighty and His Book there is abrogating and abrogated, and the nation agreed upon this except for those who deviated, as mentioned above. And the scholars agreed that the qiblah was the first to be abrogated twice, according to one of the two opinions mentioned in the issue before. Seventh: It also indicates the permissibility of abrogating the Sunnah by the Qur’an, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards Jerusalem, and there is no Qur’an about that, so the ruling was only from the perspective of the Sunnah, then that was abrogated by the Qur’an. Based on this, I was on it means you are on it. Eighth: It contains evidence of the permissibility of certainty based on a single report, as facing Jerusalem was a certainty in their Sharia. Then, when the people of Quba came to them and informed them that the qiblah had been changed to the Sacred Mosque, they accepted his words and turned towards the Kaaba, so they abandoned the continuous report based on a single report, which was presumed. Scholars differed about its permissibility rationally and its occurrence. Abu Hatim said: The preferred opinion is that it is permissible rationally even if the Shari’ah is required to do so, and that it occurred during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) based on the story of Quba’ and the fact that he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to send individual governors to the regions and they would convey all the abrogating and abrogated narrations. However, this is forbidden after his death (peace and blessings of God be upon him), based on the consensus of the Companions that the Qur’an and the known mutawatir narrations cannot be lifted by a single narration, so no one from the early Muslims or later Muslims would permit it. Those who forbade this argued that it leads to the impossible, which is lifting the certain by the conjectural. As for the story of the people of Quba’ and the governors of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), it is based on indications that provide knowledge, either through transmission and verification, or through possibility and estimation. The completion of this is a question and answer in the principles of jurisprudence. Ninth: This is evidence that whoever was not informed of the abrogating act is bound by the first ruling, contrary to those who said: The first ruling is lifted by the existence of the abrogating act, not by knowledge of it. The first is more correct, because the people of Quba continued to pray toward Jerusalem until the one who came and informed them of the abrogating act, so they turned toward the Kaaba. So if the abrogating act occurs in existence, it is inevitably lifted, but on the condition of knowledge of it, because the abrogating act is a statement, and it is not a statement regarding someone who was not informed of it. The benefit of this difference is in acts of worship performed after abrogation and before the statement, whether they are repeated or not. Accordingly, the issue of the agent in his actions after the dismissal of his principal or his death and before his knowledge of that is based on two opinions. The same applies to the one who is in debt, and the ruler if the one he appointed dies or is dismissed. The correct view is that what each of these did is carried out and his ruling is not returned. Judge Iyad said: The school did not differ regarding the rulings of someone who freed a slave without knowing of his emancipation, that they are the rulings of a free man between him and the people, but between him and God the Most High, they are permissible. They did not differ about the freed woman, that she does not repeat what she prayed after her freedom and before she knew about it without covering, but they differed about the one who is affected by a reason that changes the ruling of his worship while he is in it, by analogy to the issue of Quba. So whoever prays in one state and then his state changes before he completes his prayer, he completes it and does not interrupt it, and what he has done is sufficient for him. And likewise, like the one who prays naked and then finds a garment during the prayer, or begins his prayer while healthy and then becomes sick, or while sick and recovers, or while sitting and then is able to stand, or a slave woman who is freed while she is in prayer, she takes her veil and builds. I said: And as for someone who entered into prayer with tayammum and water came upon him, it does not interrupt his prayer, as Malik and al-Shafi’i - may God have mercy on them - and others say. And it was said: It interrupts his prayer, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifa - may God Almighty have mercy on him - and it will come. Tenth: It contains evidence for the acceptance of a single report, which is agreed upon by the predecessors and is known by continuous transmission from the habit of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in directing his governors and messengers individually to the horizons, to teach the people their religion and convey to them the Sunnah of their Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, of commands and prohibitions. Eleventh: It contains evidence that the Qur’an was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, little by little and in one situation after another, according to the need for it, until God completed His religion, as He said: This day I have perfected for you your religion. The Almighty’s saying: “Say: To God belong the East and the West.” He established an argument, meaning that He owns the East and the West and what is between them, so He has the right to command turning in any direction He wishes, and this has been mentioned previously. The Almighty’s saying: He guides whom He wills is a reference to God Almighty’s guidance of this nation to the Qiblah of Abraham, and God Almighty knows best. The path is the road. The straight path is that which has no crookedness, and this has been mentioned previously.
2:143: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And thus We have made you a just community. The meaning is: Just as the Kaaba is in the middle of the earth, so We have made you a just community, meaning We have made you below the prophets and above the nations. The middle is justice, and the origin of this is that the most honorable of things is the middle. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed bin Al-Khudri. On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And thus We have made you a just community, he said: Just. He said: This is a good, authentic hadith. And in the revelation: Their most just said, meaning the most just and best of them. And Zuhair said: They are the middle ground that people are satisfied with their judgment if one of the nights descends upon most of them. last: You are the middle of the neighborhood, know the small matter or one of the big ones Another said: Do not go into matters excessively. Do not ask too much if you ask. Be moderate among all people The middle of the valley: the best place in it and the most grass and water. And since the middle is far from extremism and negligence, it is praiseworthy. That is, this nation did not go to extremes like the Christians did with regard to their prophets, nor did they fall short like the Jews with regard to their prophets. In the hadith: The best of things are those that are in the middle. And in it, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: You should follow the middle path, for to it descends the high and to it ascends the low. So-and-so is from the middle of his people, and he is the middle of his people, and the middle of his people, meaning from their best and most noble. He was in the middle, but not from the middle that is between two things in anything. The middle with a sukoon on the seen is the adverb, you say: I prayed in the middle of the people. And I sat in the middle of the house with a sukoon because it is a noun. Al-Jawhari said: And every place where there is reconciliation between the two is in the middle, and if there is no reconciliation between the two, then it is in the middle with a sukoon, and sometimes it is in the middle but that is not correct. Second: The Almighty’s saying: So that you may be is in the accusative case with the letter kay, meaning that you may be. Witnesses is the predicate of kan. “On the people” meaning on the Day of Resurrection for the prophets over their nations, as was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Noah, peace be upon him, will be called on the Day of Resurrection and will say, ‘At Your service and at Your pleasure, O Lord.’ He will say, ‘Did you convey the message?’ He will say, ‘Yes.’ It will be said to his nation, ‘Did you convey the message?’ They will say, ‘No warner came to us.’ He will say, ‘Who will bear witness for you?’ They will say, ‘Muhammad and his nation.’ They will bear witness that he conveyed the message and the Messenger will be a witness over you.” This is what the Almighty said: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. Ibn Mubarak mentioned this hadith in length with its meaning, and in it: “Then those nations will say, ‘How can someone who did not live to see us bear witness against us?’ The Lord, glory be to Him, will say to them, ‘How can you bear witness against someone you did not live to see?’ They will say, ‘Our Lord, You sent to us a Messenger and sent down to us Your covenant and Your Book and related to us that they had conveyed the message, so we bore witness to what You entrusted us with.’ The Lord will say, ‘They have spoken the truth.’” This is what the Almighty said: And thus We have made you a just community - and the middle is justice - that you will be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you. Witnesses over the people, and the Messenger will be a witness over you.” Ibn An’am said: It has reached me that on that day the nation of Muhammad, peace be upon him, will bear witness, except for those who have compassion for their brothers in their hearts. A group said: The meaning of the verse is that some of you will bear witness over others after death, as was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Anas: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said when a funeral passed by him and he spoke well of it, he said: It is due, due, due. Then another passed by him and he spoke ill of it, he said: It is due, due, due. Umar said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! A funeral passed by and he spoke well of it, so I said: It is due, due, due. Then another funeral passed by and he spoke ill of it, so I said: It is due, due, due. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever you speak well of, Paradise is due for him, and whoever you speak ill of, Hell is due for him. You are God’s witnesses on earth. You are God’s witnesses on earth. You are God’s witnesses on earth.” Narrated by al-Bukhari with the same meaning. In some of its chains of transmission other than in the two Sahihs, he recited: So that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you. Abaan and Laith narrated on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “My nation has been given three things that were not given to anyone except the prophets: Whenever God sent a prophet, He would say to him, ‘Call upon Me and I will respond to you,’ and He would say to this nation, ‘Call upon Me and I will respond to you.’ Whenever God sent a prophet, He would say to him, ‘He has not placed any difficulty upon you in religion,’ and He would say to this nation, ‘He has not placed any difficulty upon you in religion.’ When God sent a prophet, He would make him a witness over his people and He would make this nation witnesses over the people.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah, in Nawadir Al-Usul. Third: Our scholars said: Our Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, informed us in His Book of what He bestowed upon us of His favor upon us in the name of justice and His taking on the burden of witnessing over all of His creation. He made us first in place even though we were last in time, as He, peace be upon him, said: We are the last, the first. This is evidence that only the just will testify, and the word of another will not be implemented against another unless he is just. The explanation of justice and its ruling will come at the end of the surah, God willing.
