Fourth: It is evidence of the validity of consensus and the obligation to rule by it, because if they were just, they would testify against the people. Every era is a witness against those who came after it, so the words of the Companions are evidence and a witness against the Successors, and the words of the Successors are against those who came after them. Since the nation was made witnesses, then it is obligatory to accept their words. There is no meaning to the statement of those who said: It is intended for the entire nation, because then there is no consensus on it until the Day of Judgment. This is explained in the books of Usul al-Fiqh. The Almighty says: And the Messenger will be a witness over you. It was said: It means with your deeds on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: Upon you means for you, meaning he will testify to your faith. It was also said: It means he will testify to you that he conveyed the message to you. The Almighty said: And We did not make the qiblah which you used to face. It was said that what is meant by qiblah here is the first qiblah, because He said: I used to face it. It was also said: the second, so the kaf is redundant, meaning you are facing it now, as mentioned above, and as He said: You are the best nation produced for mankind, meaning you, according to some of them, and it will come. God the Almighty said: Except that We may know who follows the Messenger. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: The meaning of except that We may know is to see. The Arabs place knowledge in place of seeing, and seeing in place of knowledge, as in the Almighty’s saying: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with you? meaning Have you not known? It was also said: The meaning is except that you may know that We know, for the hypocrites were in doubt about God’s knowledge of things before they came to be. It was also said: The meaning is to distinguish the people of certainty from the people of doubt, as narrated by Ibn Fawrak, and mentioned by al-Tabari on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was also said: The meaning is except that the Prophet and his followers may know, and God the Almighty informed us of that about Himself, just as it is said: The prince did such-and-such, but his followers did it. Al-Mahdawi mentioned it and it is good. It was also said: Its meaning is to know Muhammad, so He attributed His knowledge to Himself, the Almighty, as a specification and distinction, just as He referred to Himself, the Almighty, in His saying: O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit me. The first is more apparent, and that its meaning is the knowledge of witnessing that necessitates recompense, and He, glory be to Him, is the Knower of the unseen and the seen. He knows what will be before it is. Conditions differ based on information, but His knowledge does not differ, rather it relates to everything with a single relation. And thus everything that is mentioned in the Book of this meaning from the Almighty’s saying: And that God may make evident those who believe and take from among you witnesses, “And We will surely test you until We make evident those who strive hard among you and the patient,” and the like. The verse is an answer to the Quraysh in their saying: What has turned them away from their Qiblah which they used to face? The Quraysh were accustomed to the Kaaba, so God the Almighty wanted to test them with something other than what they were accustomed to, to show who follows the Messenger and who does not. Al-Zuhri read except to know, so who is in the nominative case according to this reading, because it is the name of what its agent is not named. And according to the reading of the group, it is in the accusative case as the object. Follows the Messenger means in what he was commanded to face the Kaaba. Of those who turn back on their heels means of those who turn away from their religion, because when the Qiblah was changed, some Muslims turned away and some became hypocrites. That is why He said: And if it is a great sin, meaning changing it, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah said. The meaning in Arabic is: And if the change is. The Almighty said: And if it were a great burden. Al-Far’i said that in and lam have the same meaning as ma and illa, while the Basrans say: it is the heavy in that has been lightened. Al-Akhfash said: meaning, even if the qiblah, the turning, or the turning away were a great burden. Except for those whom God has guided, meaning He has created guidance, which is faith, in their hearts, as God the Almighty said: Those are the ones in whose hearts He has inscribed faith. God the Almighty said: And God would never let your faith go to waste. The scholars agreed that it was revealed about someone who died while praying towards Jerusalem, as was proven in Bukhari from the hadith of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, as mentioned above. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) turned towards the Kaaba, they said: O Messenger of God, what about our brothers who died while praying towards Jerusalem? So God the Almighty revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste, the verse. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. So he called prayer faith because it includes intention, words, and deeds. Malik said: I am reminded by this verse of the Murji’ah’s statement: Prayer is not part of faith. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: And God would not let your faith go to waste meaning facing the Qiblah and believing in your Prophet. This is what most Muslims and scholars of the principles of jurisprudence agree with. Ibn Wahb, Ibn al-Qasim, Ibn Abd al-Hakam, and Ashab narrated on the authority of Malik: And God would not let your faith go to waste. He said: Your prayers. God the Almighty said: Indeed, God is to the people Kind and Merciful. Kindness is more intense than mercy. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: Kindness is more intense than mercy, and the meaning is close. We have already discussed its language, poetry, and meanings in the Most High Book in Explaining the Beautiful Names of God, so let us look there. The Kufians and Abu Amr read Ra’uf with the weight of fa’l, which is the language of Banu Asad, and from it is the saying of al-Walid ibn Uqbah: And the worst of seekers, so do not be like him fighting his uncle, the compassionate and merciful. Al-Nasa’i narrated that the language of Banu Asad is ra’af on the pattern of fa’al. Abu Ja’far ibn al-Qa’qa’ read ra’uf with a heavy fa’al without a hamza, and likewise he made easy every hamza in the Book of God Almighty, whether it is silent or moving.
2:144: God Almighty says: “We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And God is not unaware of what they do.” Scholars said: This verse was revealed before the words of God the Almighty: The foolish among the people will say. The meaning of turn your face is to turn your face to the sky, as stated by At-Tabari. Az-Zajjaj said: Turn your eyes to look at the sky, and the meanings are similar. He mentioned the sky specifically because it is specifically mentioned to glorify what is attributed to it and returns from it, such as rain, mercy, and revelation. The meaning of be pleased with it is to love it. As-Suddi said: When he prayed towards Jerusalem, he would raise his head to the sky, waiting for what he was commanded to do. He loved to pray towards the Kaaba, so God the Almighty revealed: Indeed, We have seen the turning of your face towards the heaven. Abu Ishaq narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed towards Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, loved to face towards the Kaaba, so God the Almighty revealed: Indeed, We have seen the turning of your face towards the heaven. This meaning and the statement about it have already been presented, and praise be to God. The Almighty’s saying: Then turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque. There are five issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: Then turn is a command. Turn your face toward meaning toward the Sacred Mosque, meaning the Kaaba, and there is no disagreement about this. It was said: Facing the entire House, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Omar said: Facing the gutter of the Kaaba, as Ibn Atiyya said. The gutter is the qibla of Medina and the people of Ash-Sham, and there is the qibla of the people of Andalusia. I said: Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The House is the qiblah for the people of the mosque, and the mosque is the qiblah for the people of the sanctuary, and the sanctuary is the qiblah for the people of the earth in its east and west from my nation. Second: The Almighty’s saying: half of the Sacred Mosque. The part has several meanings: it can be the side or direction, as in this verse, and it is a circumstance of place, as you say: facing it, his direction. The circumstance is in the accusative case because it is a superfluous noun in the position of the direct object, and also because the verb occurs in it. Dawud ibn Abi Hind said: In the letter of Ibn Masoud, Turn your face towards the Sacred Mosque. The poet said: I say to Umm Zinba’: Set the chests of Al-Eisa towards Banu Tamim. Another said: And a terror has enveloped you from one side of your mouth, and it is an injustice that will completely overwhelm you. Another said: Except for the one who conveys Amr as a messenger, and the message is of no avail to half of Amr. Halving something: half of it, and from it the hadith: Purity is half of faith. It is one of the opposites. It is said: Shatar ila kada if he approached it, and Shatar ‘an kada if he distanced himself from it and turned away from it. As for the clever man, it is because he has embarked on a path other than straightness, and he is the one who has exhausted his family with wickedness. He has been clever in both of them. Some of them were asked about the clever man, and he said: He is the one who has embarked on distancing himself from what God has forbidden. Third: There is no disagreement among the scholars that the Kaaba is a Qiblah in every horizon, and they agreed that whoever sees it and witnesses it is obligated to face it, and that if he neglects to face it while he sees it and knows its direction, then his prayer is not valid, and he must repeat every prayer he has prayed, as mentioned by Abu Omar. They agreed that whoever is absent from it must face its direction, its side, and its direction, and if it is hidden from him, then he must infer that with everything he can from the stars, winds, mountains, and other things that can be used to infer its direction. And whoever sits in the Sacred Mosque, let his face be toward the Kaaba and look at it with faith and hope, because looking at the Kaaba is an act of worship, as stated by Ata’ and Mujahid. Fourth: They differed as to whether the obligation of the absent person is to face the eye or the direction. Some of them said the first. Ibn al-Arabi said: It is weak, because it is an obligation for something that cannot be reached. Some of them said the direction, and this is correct for three reasons: The first: It is the possible thing to which the obligation is connected. The second: It is what is commanded in the Qur’an, as God Almighty said: “So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you are” meaning on the earth, east or west, turn your faces toward it. Third: The scholars used as evidence the long row, which is known for certain to be several times the width of the house. Fifth: This verse is a clear proof for what Malik and those who agreed with him said, that the ruling for the worshipper is that he should look in front of him, not at the place of his prostration. Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i and Al-Hasan ibn Hayy said: It is preferable for him to look at the place of his prostration. Sharik Al-Qadi said: He should look at the place of prostration when standing, at the place of his feet when bowing, at the place of his nose when prostrating, and at his lap when sitting. Ibn Al-Arabi said: He should only look in front of him, because if he bends his head, some of the standing that is required of him will be lost in the head, which is the most honorable of the limbs. If he raises his head and forces himself to look at the ground, then that is a great hardship and difficulty, and there is no difficulty that has been placed upon us in religion. However, that is better for whoever is able to do it. The Almighty said: And indeed, those who were given the Scripture meaning the Jews and Christians know that it is the truth from their Lord meaning changing the qiblah from Jerusalem. If it is said: How do they know that when it is not part of their religion nor in their Scripture? Two answers have been given: The first is that when they knew from their Scripture that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a prophet, they knew that he only spoke the truth and commanded only it. The second is that they knew from their religion that abrogation was permissible, even though some of them denied it, so they became knowledgeable about the permissibility of changing the qiblah. The Almighty said: And God is not unaware of what they do. Its meaning was mentioned earlier. Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read ya ta’malun with a ta’, addressing the People of the Book or the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. In both cases, it is a notification that God Almighty does not neglect the deeds of His servants nor is He unaware of them, and it includes a threat. The rest read it with a ya’ from below.
2:145: The Almighty said: And if you brought to those who were given the Scripture every sign, they would not follow your qiblah because they disbelieved and the truth had become clear to them, and the signs, i.e. the marks, would not benefit them. The plural of qiblah in broken form is qabl. In taslim: qiblat. It is permissible to replace the kasra with a fatha, so you say qiblat. It is permissible to delete the kasra and make the ba sukun, so you say qiblat. And la'an is answered with the answer to law, and it is its opposite in that la'an requires the past and occurrence in its answer, and la'an requires the future. Al-Farra' and Al-Akhfash said: It is answered with the answer to law because the meaning is: And if you came. And likewise, law is answered with the answer to la'an, so you say: If you did well, I would do well to you. And similar to it is the Almighty's saying: And if We sent a wind and they saw it yellow, they would remain meaning, if We sent a wind. Sibawayh disagreed with them and said: The meaning of la’an is different from the meaning of law, so neither of them applies to the hereafter. The meaning is: And if you bring to those who were given the Scripture every sign and they do not follow your qiblah. Sibawayh said: The meaning of And if We sent a wind and they saw it yellow, they would surely go astray is they would surely go astray. The Almighty’s statement: And you will not follow their Qiblah is a statement and includes a command, meaning do not incline towards any of that. Then the Almighty informed us that the Jews do not follow the Qiblah of the Christians, nor do the Christians follow the Qiblah of the Jews, according to al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. This is information about their differences, their mutual hatred, and their misguidance. Some people said: The meaning is that none of those who follow you from among those who have submitted to Islam will follow the Qiblah of one who has not submitted to Islam, nor will one who has not submitted to Islam follow the Qiblah of one who has submitted to Islam. The first is more apparent, and God Almighty knows best. God the Almighty says: {And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, indeed, you would then be among the wrongdoers.} The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation, from among those who may follow their desires and thus become wrongdoers by following them. It is not permissible for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do something that would make him a wrongdoer. It is based on the will of his nation due to the infallibility of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we are certain that this would not be from him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was addressed to magnify the matter and because it was revealed to him. Desires is the plural of desire, and this has been mentioned previously, and so has of knowledge as well, so there is no point in repeating it.
2:146: God Almighty says: “Those to whom We gave the Scripture know him as they know their own sons. But indeed, a party of them conceal the truth while they know.” God the Almighty said: Those to whom We gave the Scripture know him as they know their own sons. “Those” is in the nominative case as the subject and the predicate is they know him. It is also correct for it to be in the accusative case as an attribute of the wrongdoers, and they know is in the circumstantial case, meaning they know his prophethood and the truth of his message. The pronoun refers to Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, as stated by Mujahid, Qatada, and others. It was said: They know that changing the Qiblah from Jerusalem to the Kaaba is true, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jurayj, Ar-Rabi’, and Qatada as well. He mentioned sons specifically in the knowledge, not souls, even though they are more closely related, because a period of time passes by a person in which he does not know himself, and no time passes by in which he does not know his son. It was narrated that Umar said to Abdullah ibn Salam: Do you know Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, as you know your son? He said: Yes, and more. God sent His trustworthy one in His heaven to His trustworthy one on His earth with his description, so I recognized him, but I do not know what happened to my son from his mother. The Almighty said: And indeed, a party of them conceal the truth meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as stated by Mujahid, Qatada, and Khasif. It was also said: facing the Kaaba, as we mentioned earlier. The Almighty’s saying: And they knew is clear in the validity of disbelief out of stubbornness, and similar to it is: And they denied it, although their souls were convinced thereof. And His saying: But when there came to them that which they recognized, they disbelieved in it.
2:147: The Almighty's saying: The truth is from your Lord means facing the Kaaba, not what the Jews told you about their qiblah. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he read the truth in the accusative case with they know meaning they know the truth. It is correct to put it in the accusative case with the assumption that the truth is binding. And the nominative case is in the beginning or with the implied subject, and the estimation is it is the truth, or with the implied verb, meaning the truth has come to you. An-Nahhas said: As for what is in Al-Anbiya' the truth is they are turning away we do not know of anyone who read it except in the accusative case, and the difference between them is that what is in Surat Al-Baqarah is the beginning of a verse, and what is in Al-Anbiya' is not like that. The Almighty said: So do not be among the doubters meaning among the doubters. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation. It is said: So-and-so had doubts about something if he was faced with certainty at one time and doubt at another, so he repelled one of them with the other. And from this comes the word murā’ because each one of them doubts the statement of the other. And doubting something means doubting it, and so is arguing. Al-Tabari recited as evidence that the doubters are the doubters the saying of Al-A’sha: The fastest way to run is to see the mirage Ibn Atiyah said: He made a mistake in this, because Abu Ubaidah and others said: Those who doubt the verse are those who pass the horses with their feet, humming to make them run, as if they were milking the running from them, and there is no meaning of doubt in the verse, as al-Tabari said. I said: The meaning of doubt is present, because it is possible that the horse is being tested by its owner to see if it is running as he is used to, lest something happen to it, or this may be when he first buys it, so he makes it run to see how much it runs. Al-Jawhari said: And you exhort the horse if you extract what it has of running with a whip or something else. The noun is mariyah with a kasrah, and it may be with a damma. And you exorcise the she-camel with a damma: if you wipe its udder to make it produce milk. And you exorcise her if her milk flows, and the noun is mariyah with a kasrah, and the damma is a mistake. And mariyah is doubt, and it may be with a damma, and both are recited with it.
2:148: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And for each is a direction. The weight of the word direction is fa’la from the word confrontation. Direction, direction, and face have the same meaning, and what is meant is the qiblah, meaning that they do not follow your qiblah and you do not follow their qiblah. And for each there is a direction either by right or by desire. The second: The Almighty’s saying: He is its Master refers back to the word all not to its meaning, because if it had been in the meaning, He would have said: They turn their faces to it, so the ha’ and the alif are the first object and the second object is omitted, meaning He turns his face and himself to it. The meaning is: And for every follower of a religion there is a qiblah, the follower of the qiblah turns his face to it, according to the word all, and this is the saying of al-Rabi’, Ata’ and Ibn Abbas. And Ali bin Sulayman said: Its Master means its one who turns to it. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Amir read its Master without naming its agent. The pronoun in this reading refers to one, meaning that for every one of the people there is a qiblah, the one is its Master, meaning he is turned to it, as al-Zajjaj said. It is possible that in the reading of the group it is the pronoun of the name of God, the Almighty, even if it is not mentioned, since it is known that God, the Almighty, is the agent of that, and the meaning is: For every follower of a religion there is a qiblah, God turns it to him. At-Tabari narrated that some people read: And for every follower of a religion there is a qiblah, by adding all to direction. Ibn Atiyah said: Al-Tabari made a mistake in it, and it is directed, meaning, so race to do good deeds in every direction and do not contradict them, and do not object in what you are commanded between this and that, meaning, you are only required to obey in all of them. He presented his statement, and for every direction before the command in his statement, so race to do good deeds to emphasize the direction, just as the object is presented. Abu Amr Al-Dani mentioned this reading from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. The waw was left in wayhah to differentiate between several weights, because wayhah is a circumstance, and those are verbal nouns. Abu Ali said: Some people went to the fact that it is a verbal noun that deviated from the analogy, so it was left. Some people went to the fact that it is a noun and not a verbal noun. Other than Abu Ali said: If you want the verbal noun, you say wayhah, and wayhah may be said in the circumstance. Second: The Almighty’s statement: So race to do good deeds meaning to do good deeds. The letter was omitted, meaning hasten to do what God the Almighty has commanded you of facing the Sacred House, even though it includes the urging to hasten and rush to all acts of obedience in general, so what is meant is what was mentioned about facing due to the context of the verse. The intended meaning is to hasten to pray at the beginning of its time, and God the Almighty knows best. An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “The example of one who migrates to prayer is like the example of one who offers a camel, then the one who follows him is like the one who offers a cow, then the one who follows him is like the one who offers a ram, then the one who follows him is like the one who offers a chicken, then the one who follows him is like the one who offers an egg.” Ad-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: One of you prays the prayer at its time and has left from the first time what is better for him than his family and his wealth.” Malik narrated it on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed. Al-Darqutni also narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best of deeds is prayer at the beginning of its time. And in the hadith of Ibn Masoud: The first of its time with the omission of in. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abdul Malik on the authority of Abu Mahdhura on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The beginning of the time is the pleasure of God, the middle of the time is the mercy of God, and the end of the time is the forgiveness of God. Ibn al-Arabi added: Abu Bakr said: The pleasure of God is more beloved to us than His forgiveness, for His pleasure is with the good-doers and His forgiveness is with the negligent. This is the choice of al-Shafi’i. Abu Hanifa said: The end of the time is better, because it is the time of obligation. As for Malik, he made the final statement. As for the dawn and sunset prayers, the beginning of the time is better for them. As for the dawn prayer, it is because of the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pray the dawn prayer, the women would leave wrapped in their cloaks, and they would not be recognized because of the darkness” - in one narration - wrapped up. As for the sunset prayer, it is according to the hadith of Salamah ibn al-Akwa’: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray Maghrib when the sun had set and was hidden by the veil.” Both of them were narrated by Muslim. As for the Isha prayer, delaying it is better for those who are able to do so. Ibn Umar narrated: We waited one night for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pray the last Isha prayer. He came out to us when a third of the night had passed or after that. We do not know whether he was occupied with his family or something else. When he came out, he said: You are waiting for a prayer that no other religion awaits. Were it not that it would be too much for my Ummah, I would have led them in prayer at this hour.” And in Bukhari, on the authority of Anas, he said: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) delayed the ‘Isha’ prayer until midnight, then he prayed…” and mentioned the hadeeth. Abu Barzah said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) preferred to delay it. As for the noon prayer, it comes to people by surprise, so it is recommended to delay it a little so that they can prepare and gather. Abu al-Faraj said: Malik said: The beginning of the time is better for every prayer except for the noon prayer in intense heat. Ibn Abi Uways said: Malik disliked praying the noon prayer at noon, but after that, and he said that is the prayer of the Khawarij. In Saheeh al-Bukhari and Saheeh al-Tirmidhi, “On the authority of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, who said: We were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a journey, and the muezzin wanted to call the noon prayer, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Cool down. Then he wanted to call the adhan, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Cool down until we saw the shade of the hills, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Intense heat is from the breath of Hell, so when the heat becomes intense, cool down with prayer.” In Saheeh Muslim, on the authority of Anas, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: He used to pray Dhuhr when the sun had passed its zenith. What unites the two hadiths is what Anas narrated, that he should cool down the prayer, and if it was cold, he should hasten it. Abu ‘Eisa al-Tirmidhi said: Some scholars preferred to delay Dhuhr prayer in intense heat, and this is the opinion of Ibn al-Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq. Ash-Shafi’i said: Cooling down the Dhuhr prayer is only if there is a mosque whose people are affected by it from a distance. As for the one who prays alone and the one who prays in the mosque of his people, what I prefer for him is not to delay the prayer in intense heat. Abu ‘Eisa said: The meaning of those who went to delay Dhuhr in intense heat is more appropriate and more similar to the followers. As for what Ash-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him went to, that the concession is for the one who is affected by it from the servant and for the hardship on the people, then in the hadith of Abu Dharr may God be pleased with him there is what indicates the opposite of what Ash-Shafi’i said. Abu Dharr said: We were with the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) on a journey, and Bilal called the Dhuhr prayer, so the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: O Bilal, cool down, then cool down. If the matter was as Al-Shafi’i believed, then delaying the prayer at that time would have had no meaning, because they had gathered while traveling and they did not need to come back from far away. As for the afternoon prayer, bringing it forward is better. There is no disagreement in our school of thought that delaying the prayer in the hope of praying in congregation is better than praying it forward, because the virtue of praying in congregation is known, but the virtue of the beginning of the time is unknown, and attaining what is known is better, as Ibn Al-Arabi said. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Wherever you may be is a condition, and its answer is: God will bring you all together, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Then He described Himself, the Almighty, as having the power over all things, in order to fit the description with what was mentioned about the return after death and decay.
2:149: God Almighty says: “And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And God is not unaware of what you do.”
2:150: The Almighty said: And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. It was said: This is an emphasis on the command to face the Kaaba and pay attention to it, because the location of the turning was very difficult for them, so He emphasised the command so that people would see the attention paid to it, so it would be easier for them and their souls would be at peace with it. It was said: By the first, He meant: Turn your face toward the Kaaba, meaning see it when you pray facing it. Then He said: And wherever you are, O Muslims, in all the mosques in Madinah and elsewhere, turn your faces toward it. Then he said: And from wherever you go out, meaning the obligation to face the Kaaba when traveling. This was an order to face the Kaaba in all places on the Earth’s sides. I said: This statement is better than the first because it interprets each verse to have a benefit. Ad-Darqutni narrated: “On the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on a journey and wanted to pray on his mount, he would face the qiblah and say takbir, then pray in whatever direction he was facing.” Abu Dawud also narrated it, and this is what Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Abu Thawr said. Malik held that he was not required to face the qiblah, based on the hadith of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pray while facing from Mecca to Medina on his mount.” He said: “And in this was revealed: ‘So wherever you turn, there is the face of God,’ which has already been mentioned.” I said: There is no contradiction between the two hadiths, because this is a case of absolute and qualified, so the statement of Al-Shafi’i is more appropriate, and the hadith of Anas in this regard is an authentic hadith. It is narrated that Ja’far ibn Muhammad was asked: What is the meaning of repeating stories in the Qur’an? He said: God knows that not all people memorize the Qur’an, so if the story were not repeated, it would be possible for some people to have it and others not to have it, so it was repeated so that it would be for those who memorized some of it. God the Almighty said: So that mankind will have no argument against you, except for those among them who are unjust. Mujahid said: They are the polytheists of the Arabs. Their argument was their saying: We have returned to our Qiblah. This was answered by His saying: “Say: To God belongs the East and the West.” It was said: The meaning of So that mankind will have no argument against you is so that they will not say to you: You were ordered to face the Kaaba, but you do not see it. So when God the Almighty said: And wherever you are, turn your faces toward it, this was removed. Abu Ubaidah said: Except here has the meaning of and, meaning and those who are unjust. So it is an exception with the meaning of and, and from it is the saying of the poet: The city is not a house other than the house of the Caliph, other than the house of Marwan As if he said: Except the house of the Caliph and the house of Marwan, and the same was said in the words of God Almighty: Except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted meaning those who believe. Al-Zajjaj invalidated this statement and said: This is a mistake according to the skilled grammarians, and it invalidates the meanings, and except and what follows it do not need to be mentioned. The statement according to them is that this is an exception not from the first, meaning but those who are unjust among them, then they argue. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: That is, God made you aware of the matter of arguing in the direction of the qiblah in His words: And each one has a direction towards which he turns "so that the people will have no argument against you" except for the one who is unjust by arguing in what has been made clear to him, as you say: You have no argument against me except injustice or except that you oppress me, meaning you have no argument at all, but you oppress me, so it was called an argument because the one arguing with it called it an argument even if it is invalid. Qatrib said: It is possible that the meaning is so that the people will have no argument against you except against those who are unjust, so those is a substitute for the kaf and the mim in upon you. A group said: Except those is a connected exception, the meaning of which was narrated from Ibn Abbas and others, and it was chosen by Al-Tabari who said: God denied that anyone has an argument against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions in facing the Kaaba. The meaning is: No one has an argument against you except a refuting argument. As they said: He did not turn to them, and Muhammad was confused in his religion, and he did not turn towards our Qiblah except that we were more guided than him, and other statements that were not issued except by a pagan worshipper, a Jew, or a hypocrite. Argument means argumentation, which is quarreling and disputing. God called it an argument and ruled that it was corrupt because it was from oppression. Ibn Atiyyah said: It was said that the exception is disconnected, and this is on the basis that what is meant by the people are the Jews, then He excepted the infidels of the Arabs, as if He said: But those who did wrong will argue with you, and His saying: from them rejects this interpretation. The meaning is but those who did wrong, meaning the infidels of Quraysh in their saying: Muhammad has returned to our Qiblah and will return to our entire religion. This includes everyone who spoke about the incident other than the Jews. Ibn Abbas, Zayd ibn Ali, and Ibn Zayd read ala alladhi zulam with a fatha on the hamza and a light lam, meaning to open the speech, so alladhi zulam is the subject, or with the meaning of enticement, so alladhi is the subject of an implied verb. The Almighty says: So do not fear them, meaning people, but fear Me. Fear is originally a sense of reassurance in the heart that prompts one to be cautious. And fear is the terror of the heart that makes the limbs fearful, and because the limbs are fearful of it, it is called fear. The meaning of the verse is to belittle everyone other than God Almighty, and to command us to abandon their command and to heed the command of God Almighty. The Almighty’s saying: And that I may complete My favor upon you is in apposition to so that it may not be, meaning and that I may complete, as Al-Akhfash said. It was also said: It is in the nominative case as the subject and the predicate is implied, the meaning: And that I may complete My favor upon you, I will make you know my qiblah,” as Al-Zajjaj said. The completion of the favor is guidance to the qiblah, and it was also said: entering Paradise. Saeed bin Jubair said: And the favor of God is not completed upon a servant until He admits him to Paradise. And and perhaps you will be guided was mentioned above.
2:151: The Almighty said: As We have sent The Kaf is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted source, meaning: And I will complete My favor upon you as We have sent, as Al-Farra' said. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is the best of the sayings, meaning: And I will complete My favor upon you in explaining the Sunnah of Abraham, peace be upon him, as We have sent. It was said: The meaning is: And perhaps you will be guided as We have sent. It was said: It is in the accusative case as a state, and the meaning is: And I will complete My favor upon you in this state. The simile is based on the fact that the favor in the Qiblah is like the favor in the message, and that the remembrance commanded is as great as the favor. It was said: The meaning of the speech is to advance and delay, meaning, remember Me as We have sent. It was narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him, and Al-Zajjaj chose it. Meaning, just as We sent among you a Messenger whom you know to be truthful, remember Me by monotheism and belief in Him. Stopping at you will be guided according to this statement is permissible. I said: This is the choice of the wise Tirmidhi in his book, meaning, just as I have done this to you from the blessings that I have enumerated for you, so remember Me with gratitude, and I will remember you with more, because in your remembering that is gratitude to Me, and I have promised you more for your gratitude, and that is His saying: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you, so the kaf in His saying as here, and in Al-Anfal as your Lord brought you forth and at the end of Al-Hijr as We sent down upon the dividers is related to what comes after it, as will be explained.
2:152: God Almighty says: “So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful.”
2:153: The Almighty's saying: So remember Me, and I will remember you is a command and its answer, and it contains the meaning of recompense, which is why it is in the subjunctive mood. The origin of remembrance is to be alert with the heart to what is being remembered and to be awake to it. Remembrance with the tongue is called remembrance because it indicates remembrance of the heart. However, since remembrance is often used to refer to verbal speech, it has come to be the one that comes first to understanding. The meaning of the verse: Remember Me with obedience, and I will remember you with reward and forgiveness. Said Saeed bin Jubair. He also said: Remembrance is obedience to God, so whoever does not obey Him does not remember Him, even if he glorifies and praises God a lot and recites the Qur’an. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Whoever obeys God has remembered God, even if his prayers, fasts, and good deeds are few. Whoever disobeys God has forgotten God, even if his prayers, fasts, and good deeds are many.” Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Khuwaiz Mandad mentioned this in his Ahkam al-Quran. Abu Uthman al-Nahdi said: I know the time in which God will remember us. He was asked: How do you know it? He said: “God Almighty says: ‘Remember Me, and I will remember you.’” Al-Suddi said: “There is no servant who remembers God except that God Almighty remembers him. No believer remembers him except that God remembers him with His mercy, and no disbeliever remembers him except that God remembers him with torment.” Abu Uthman was asked: We remember God but do not find sweetness in our hearts? He said: Thank God Almighty for beautifying a limb of yours with His obedience. Dhu al-Nun al-Misri, may God have mercy on him, said: Whoever remembers God Almighty in a true manner, will forget everything else in the face of his remembrance, and God will preserve everything for him, and will be a substitute for everything. Muadh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, said: No action done by the son of Adam is more effective in saving him from the punishment of God than the remembrance of God. There are many hadiths on the virtue of remembrance and its reward, narrated by the imams. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Busr: “An Arab said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: The laws of Islam have become too many for me, so tell me something of them that I can hold on to. He said: Keep your tongue moist with the remembrance of God Almighty.” It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God the Almighty says, ‘I am with My servant when he remembers Me and his lips move with Me.’ This chapter will be further explained when God the Almighty says, O you who have believed, remember God with much remembrance, and that what is meant is remembrance of the heart, which must be maintained in all situations. God the Almighty said: And be grateful to Me and do not be ungrateful. Al-Farra’ said: It is said: I thanked you and I thanked you and I advised you. The first is the eloquent. Gratitude is knowing and speaking about kindness, and its root in the language is appearance, and it has been mentioned before. So the servant’s gratitude to God the Almighty is His praise of him by mentioning His kindness to him, and the Truth, glory be to Him, is His gratitude to the servant by His praise of him by his obedience to Him, except that the servant’s gratitude is uttered by the tongue and acknowledged in the heart by the Lord’s favor along with acts of obedience. The Almighty’s saying: And do not disbelieve is a prohibition, and therefore the group’s nun was deleted from it. This is the speaker’s nun and the ya was deleted because it is the beginning of a verse, and it is better to prove it in places other than the Qur’an, meaning do not disbelieve in My blessings and favors. So disbelief here is concealing the blessing, not denying it. We have already discussed disbelief in language, and we have also discussed the meaning of seeking help through patience and prayer, so there is no point in repeating it.
2:154: This is like what God Almighty said in the other verse: “And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision.” There comes the discussion of martyrs and their rulings, God Almighty willing. If God the Almighty revives them after death to provide for them - as follows - then it is permissible for Him to revive the infidels to torment them, and this would be evidence of the torment of the grave. The martyrs are alive as God the Almighty said, and this does not mean that they will be revived, because if that were the case, there would be no difference between the martyrs and others, since everyone will be revived. This is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: But you do not perceive, and the believers perceive that they will be revived. The word dead was raised with an implied subject, and so is rather alive, meaning they are dead and they are alive. It is not correct to apply the word said to it because there is no connection between it and it, just as it is correct in your saying: I said a word and an argument.
2:155: The Almighty said: And We will surely test you This waw is open according to Sibawayh due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. Another said: When it is added to the heavy noon, the verb is built on the level of fifteen. The affliction can be good or bad. Its root is the trial, as mentioned above. The meaning is that We will surely test you to teach the one who strives and is patient the knowledge of its meanings so that the reward will befall him, as mentioned above. It was said: They were only tested with this as a sign for those who come after them, so that they will know that they were only patient with this when the truth was made clear to them. It was also said: He informed them of this so that they would be certain that it would befall them, so that they would prepare themselves for it and be further from impatience. In it is the hastening of the reward of God Almighty for the resolve and preparing the soul. God the Almighty says: With something is a singular word but its meaning is plural. Ad-Dahhak read with things in the plural, while the majority read it in the singular form, meaning with something of this and something of that, so he was satisfied with the first for brevity. From fear meaning fear of the enemy and panic in battle, as Ibn Abbas said. Ash-Shafi’i said: It is the fear of God the Almighty. And hunger means famine due to drought and famine, according to Ibn Abbas. Ash-Shafi’i said: It is hunger in the month of Ramadan. And a decrease in wealth due to being busy fighting the infidels. It was said: The devastating calamities. Ash-Shafi’i said: With the obligatory zakat. And souls Ibn Abbas said: With killing and death in jihad. Ash-Shafi’i said: He means diseases. And fruits Ash-Shafi’i said: What is meant is the death of children, and a man’s child is the fruit of his heart, as came in the hadith, as will come. Ibn Abbas said: What is meant is the scarcity of plants and the cessation of blessings. The Almighty says: And give good tidings to the patient, meaning the reward for patience. Patience originally means confinement, and its reward is not specified, as has been mentioned before. However, this can only be achieved by being patient at the first shock, as Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Anas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Patience is only at the first shock. Muslim narrated it in a more complete manner, meaning that the patience that is difficult for the soul and for which the reward is great is only when a calamity strikes and its heat is felt, for it indicates the strength of the heart and its steadfastness in the position of patience. However, when the heat of the calamity cools down, everyone is patient at that time. Therefore, it was said: Every wise person must adhere to what a fool must do at the time of a calamity after three days. Sahl ibn Abdullah al-Tustari said: When God the Almighty said: And give good tidings to the patient, patience became a livelihood. Patience is of two types: patience from disobeying God, for this is a mujahid, and patience in obeying God, for this is a worshipper. So if he is patient from disobeying God and patient in obeying God, God will grant him contentment with His decree. The sign of patience is the heart’s tranquility with what befalls the soul of disliked and beloved things. Al-Hawaas said: Patience is steadfastness in adhering to the rulings of the Book and the Sunnah. Ruwaym said: Patience is abandoning complaint. Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: Patience is seeking help from God the Almighty. Professor Abu Ali said: The limit of patience is not to object to the decree. As for showing the affliction in a way other than complaining, it does not contradict patience. God Almighty said in the story of Job: Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant, along with what was reported about him that he said: Harm has touched me.
2:156: God Almighty says: Those who, when disaster strikes them, say, ‘Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return.’
2:157: It has six issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: A calamity. A calamity is everything that harms or befalls a believer. It is said: He was afflicted with an injury, “a calamity,” and a calamity. A calamity is the singular of calamities. Al-Masuba with a damma on the sad is like al-Masiba. The Arabs agreed on the hamza of al-Masa’ib, and its root is waw, as if they likened the root to the extra, and it is pluralized as al-Masawib, which is the root. A calamity is al-Isaba, as the poet said: Aslam, your affliction is a man who gave peace as a greeting of injustice. The arrow hit the paper, it hits a loss, a language for it hit him. al-Qari’ah 101:the disaster that befalls a person, even if it is small, and it is used to mean evil. Ikrimah narrated: “The lamp of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out one night, and he said: ‘To God we belong and to Him we shall return.’ It was said: ‘Is this a calamity, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘Yes, everything that harms a believer is a calamity.’” I said: This meaning is confirmed in Sahih. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed and Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with them both, that they heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: No fatigue, nor illness, nor sorrow befalls a believer, not even a worry that worries him, but that some of his sins are expiated thereby. Second: Ibn Majah included in his Sunan: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us: Waki’ bin Al-Jarrah told us: Hisham bin Ziyad told us: His mother told us: Fatima bint Al-Hussein told us: Her father told us: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever is afflicted with a calamity and remembers his calamity and says ‘I seek refuge in God from evil’, even if the calamity has passed, God will write for him a reward equal to that of the day he was afflicted.” Third: One of the greatest calamities is the calamity in religion. Abu Omar mentioned on the authority of Al-Faryabi that he said: Fatar bin Khalifa told us that Ata bin Abi Rabah told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If any of you is afflicted with a calamity, let him remember my affliction, for it is among the greatest of calamities. It was narrated by Al-Samarqandi Abu Muhammad in his Musnad. Abu Na’im told us: Fitr told us…, and he mentioned something similar. He also attributed something similar to it on the authority of Makhul, without a chain of transmission. Abu Umar said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke the truth, because his affliction is greater than any affliction that will befall a Muslim after him until the Day of Resurrection. Revelation was cut off and prophethood died. The first appearance of evil was the apostasy of the Arabs and other things, and it was the first cessation of goodness and the first decrease in it. Abu Sa’id said: We did not remove the dust from the grave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until our hearts rejected it. Abu Al-Atahiya did a good job in composing the meaning of this hadith, where he says: Be patient for every calamity and be patient, and know that a person is not immortal. Or do you not see that the calamities are many and that death is on the horizon for the servants? Who among those you see has not been afflicted with a calamity? This is a path in which you are not alone. If you mention Muhammad and his affliction, then mention your affliction with the Prophet Muhammad. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: “They said: ‘Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return.’” God the Almighty made these words a refuge for those afflicted with calamities, and a protection for those who are tested, because they contain blessed meanings. His saying: Indeed we belong to God is monotheism and an acknowledgment of servitude and dominion. His saying: And indeed to Him we will return is an acknowledgment of our own destruction and resurrection from our graves, and the certainty that the return of all matters to Him as they are to Him. Saeed bin Jubair, may God have mercy on him, said: These words were not given to any prophet before our Prophet, and if Jacob had known them, he would not have said: Oh, my grief over Joseph. Fifth: Abu Sinan said: I buried my son Sinan, and Abu Talha Al-Khawlani was on the edge of the grave. When I wanted to go out, he took my hand and encouraged me and said: Shall I not give you good report, O Abu Sinan? Ad-Dahhak told me on the authority of Abu Musa that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If the slave’s child dies, God says to His angels, ‘Have you taken the soul of My slave’s child?’ They say, ‘Yes.’ He says, ‘Have you taken the fruit of his heart?’ They say, ‘Yes.’ He says, ‘Then what did My slave say?’ They say, ‘He praised You and sought refuge in You.’ God says, ‘Build a house for My slave in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.’” Muslim narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said, “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no Muslim who is afflicted with a calamity and says what God the Almighty has commanded him: ‘Indeed we belong to God and indeed to Him we shall return. O God, reward me for my affliction and compensate me with something better than it,’ except that God will compensate him with something better than it.” This is a reminder of the words of God the Almighty: And give good tidings to the patient, either by compensation, as God compensated the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) for Umm Salamah, for he married her when her husband Abu Salamah died. Or by a great reward, as in the hadith of Abu Musa. It may be by both. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy. These are blessings from God the Almighty to the patient and those who seek His return. God’s blessings upon His servant: His pardon, mercy, blessing, and honoring him in this world and the hereafter. Al-Zajjaj said: The blessings from God the Almighty are forgiveness and good praise. From this, the prayers upon the dead are only praising him and supplicating for him. He repeated mercy when the wording differs, to emphasize and satisfy the meaning, as He said: Of the clear proofs and guidance, and His saying: Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? And the poet said: Pray for Yahya and his followers, a generous Lord and an obeyed intercessor. It was said: By mercy he meant relieving distress and fulfilling need. In Bukhari, Omar may God be pleased with him said: What a good just person and what a good bonus! “Those who, when disaster strikes them, say, ‘Indeed we belong to God, and indeed to Him we will return.’ Those are the ones upon whom are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided.” What he meant by just people is prayer and mercy, and by bonus is guidance. It was said: To deserving reward and generous recompense, and it was said: To making calamities easier and relieving grief.
2:158: It contains nine issues: First: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Asim bin Sulayman, who said: I asked Anas bin Malik about Safa and Marwa, and he said: We used to think that they were from the pre-Islamic era, but when Islam came, we refrained from doing them. Then God the Almighty revealed: “Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs Umrah - there is no blame upon him for walking between them.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Awrah who said: I said to Aisha: No one has ever seen anything wrong with not circumambulating between Safa and Marwa, and I do not care if I do not circumambulate between them. She said: What a bad thing you have said, O my nephew! The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) circumambulated and so did the Muslims, but the people of Manat, the tyrant in Al-Mushallal, did not circumambulate between Safa and Marwa. Then God revealed: So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs ‘Umrah, there is no blame upon him for walking between them. If it were as you say, it would have been: There is no blame upon him for walking between them. Al-Zuhri said: I mentioned that to Abu Bakr bin ‘Abd al-Rahman bin al-Harith bin Hisham, and he was pleased with it and said: This is knowledge. I have heard men of knowledge say: Only those Arabs who did not walk between Safa and Marwa used to say that our circumambulation between these two stones was a matter of the Age of Ignorance. Others from the Ansar said: We were only commanded to circumambulate the House, but we were not commanded to do so between Safa and Marwa. Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God. Abu Bakr bin Abd al-Rahman said: I think it was revealed about these and those. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Al-Bukhari narrated it with the same meaning, and in it after his saying: Then God revealed: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God: Aisha said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had prescribed circumambulation between them, so no one should neglect circumambulating between them. Then she informed Abu Bakr bin Abd Al-Rahman, who said: This is knowledge that I had not heard, and I heard men of knowledge mention that the people - except those whom Aisha mentioned - who used to enter ihram for Manat, used to all circumambulate between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. Then when God mentioned circumambulating the House and did not mention As-Safa and Al-Marwah in the Qur’an, they said: O Messenger of God, we used to circumambulate between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, but God revealed circumambulation of the House and did not mention As-Safa. Is there any blame on us if we circumambulate between As-Safa and Al-Marwah? Then God, the Almighty, revealed: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God 10:13. Abu Bakr said: Listen to this verse, it was revealed about both groups: about those who used to deviate from performing Tawaf between Safa and Marwa in the pre-Islamic era, and those who used to perform Tawaf between them and then hesitated to perform Tawaf between them in Islam, because God Almighty commanded Tawaf around the House, and did not mention Safa until He mentioned that after Tawaf around the House. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Asim bin Sulayman al-Ahwal, who said: Anas bin Malik asked about Safa and Marwa. He said: They were among the symbols of the Jahiliyyah. When Islam came, we refrained from performing them. Then God the Almighty revealed: “Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God. So whoever makes Hajj to the House or performs Umrah, there is no blame upon him for walking between them.” He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. It was also narrated by Al-Bukhari. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: During the Jahiliyyah, there were devils who would play music all night between Safa and Marwa. There were gods between them. When Islam appeared, the Muslims said: O Messenger of God, we should not walk between Safa and Marwa, for they are polytheism. Then this verse was revealed. Al-Sha’bi said: During the Jahiliyyah, there was an idol on Safa called Isaf and on Marwa an idol called Na’ilah. They would touch them when they walked around. The Muslims refrained from walking around them because of this, so this verse was revealed. Second: The root of Safa in the language is smooth stone, and here it is a well-known mountain in Mecca, and so is Marwa, which is why they were mentioned with the definite article. Safa was mentioned because Adam, the Chosen One, peace and blessings be upon him, stood on it and was named after it, and Eve stood on Marwa and was named after a woman, so it was made feminine for that reason, and God knows best. Al-Sha’bi said: There was an idol on Safa called Isaf and on Al-Mura an idol called Na’ila, and this is in the masculine and feminine, and the masculine was brought forward, and this is good, because the aforementioned hadiths indicate this meaning. And the dislike of circumambulating between them was only for this reason, until God removed the hardship in that. The People of the Book claimed that they committed adultery in the Kaaba, so God transformed them into two stones and placed them on Safa and Marwa to take a lesson from them, and when the period was long, they were worshipped instead of God, and God knows best. Safa short is the plural of safa, which means smooth stones. It was said: Al-Safa is a singular noun and its plural is Safi with a damma on the sad and Asfa’ like Arja’. The rajaz poet said: As if his back is like the places of birds on a fine rock It was said: The conditions of safa are whiteness and hardness, and its derivation is from safa yasefu, meaning pure from dirt and clay. And marwah singular marw are the small stones that have bricks in them. It was said that it is hardness. The correct view is that marw is the hard and soft stones that crack and its edge becomes thin, and in this it is said: marw is more common and it is said about the cross. The poet said: He turned to the ground, withered, and when he came across a rock, he yielded. Abu Dhuayb said: As if I am a Marwa, a clear, shining star, knocking every day for the events. It has been said: They are black stones. It has also been said: They are shiny white stones in which there is fire. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Of the symbols of God meaning of His landmarks and places of worship. It is the plural of sha’irah. The symbols are the acts of worship that God Almighty has made known, meaning He has made them signs for the people, such as standing, running, and slaughtering. The symbol is the mark. It is said: I made the sacrificial animal known meaning I made it known by sticking an iron rod in its hump, from your saying: I made known, meaning I made it known. Al-Kumait said: We kill them generation by generation, you see them as ritual sacrifices through which people draw near. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: So whoever makes Hajj to the House means intending. The root of Hajj is intention. The poet said: I witness from Aouf many pilgrims who curse the saffron-colored Al-Zubayrkan. Insult: a common word. Abu Ubaidah said: Insult with a kasra is the one who curses a lot. Also, the one who curses you is called sabk. The poet said: Do not curse me, for I am not the one who curses. If I curse a noble man, I will curse him. The veil is also cursed, as is the turban. Al-Mukhbal Al-Saadi said: They curse the saffron zabraqan And the word curse also means rope in the language of Hudhayl. Abu Dhu’ayb said: He hung down on it between a thread and a barren string like a palm branch, and its crows stumbled over it. As-subub: ropes. As-sab: a thin piece of linen. As-sabibah is its rope, and the plural is as-subub and as-saba’ib, as Al-Jawhari said. The doctor examined the wound if he probed it with a skewer. The poet said: A woman performs Hajj in the depths of her body Al-Lajf: the sinking. The well became hollow: its bottom sank. Then this name was used specifically for the intention to go to the Sacred House for specific actions. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Or perform Umrah, meaning visit. Umrah means visiting. The poet said: Ibn Muammar was exalted when he set out on a faraway expedition and was patient. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: There is no blame upon him meaning there is no sin. Its origin is from januwh which means inclination, and from it comes the word jawaneh for limbs due to their crookedness. Aisha’s interpretation of this verse has been presented. Ibn al-Arabi said: The truth of the statement is that the statement of the speaker: There is no blame upon you if you do, is the permissibility of the action. And his statement: There is no blame upon you if you do not do, is the permissibility of leaving the action. So when he heard the weakness of the statement of God the Almighty: There is no blame upon him if he goes around them both, he said: This is evidence that leaving the circumambulation is permissible. Then he saw the Shari’ah applied to the effect that there is no permission to leave the circumambulation, so he sought to reconcile these two contradictions. Aisha said to him: His saying: There is no blame upon him if he circumambulates them is not evidence of abandoning the circumambulation. Rather, it would have been evidence of abandoning it. If there was no blame upon him if he circumambulated them, then this wording would not have come to permit abandoning the circumambulation, nor is there evidence for it. Rather, it came to indicate the permissibility of circumambulation for those who were embarrassed by it in the pre-Islamic era, or for those who circumambulated it in the pre-Islamic era intending to worship the idols that were in it. So God Almighty informed them that circumambulation is not forbidden if the circumambulator does not intend a false intention. If it is said: Ata’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he recited: There is no blame upon him if he does not circumambulate them both, and this is the recitation of Ibn Mas’ud. It is thought that it is also in the Mushaf of Abu Bakr, and something similar is narrated on the authority of Anas. The answer is that this is contrary to what is in the Mushaf, and what has been established in the Mushaf should not be abandoned for a recitation whose authenticity is not known or not. Ata’ often transmitted it on the authority of Ibn Abbas without hearing it. It has been said that the narration in this on the authority of Anas is not accurate, or that it is an additional la for emphasis, as he said: I do not blame the whites for not laughing when they saw the ugly, disheveled one. Seventh: Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Jabir: “When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) arrived in Mecca, he circumambulated the House seven times and recited: ‘And take, [O Muhammad], the standing place of Abraham as a place of prayer. ’ He prayed behind the standing place, then he came to the Black Stone and touched it, then he said: ‘We begin with that with which God began. ’ So he began with Safa and recited: ‘Indeed, Safa and Marwa are among the symbols of God. ’ He said: This is a good and authentic hadith, and the scholars act upon this, that he begins with Safa before Marwa. If he begins with Marwa before Safa, it is not permissible for him, and he begins with Safa.” Eighth: The scholars differed regarding the obligation of walking between Safa and Marwa. Al-Shafi’i and Ibn Hanbal said: It is a pillar, and this is the well-known view of the Maliki school of thought, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Strive, for God has prescribed striving for you. Narrated by Al-Daraqutni. Written means obligated, as God Almighty says: Fasting has been prescribed for you, and as the Prophet, peace be upon him, says: Five prayers have been prescribed by God for His servants. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Umm Walad Lashaiba, who said: “I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walking between Safa and Marwa and he said: ‘One should not cross the valley except by running.’” So whoever omits it or a part of it, forgetfully or intentionally, should return from his country or from where he mentioned to Mecca, and perform Tawaf and Sa’i, because Sa’i can only be performed in conjunction with Tawaf. According to Malik, it is the same whether that is during Hajj or Umrah, even if it is not obligatory during Umrah. If he has intercourse with women, he must perform Umrah and offer a sacrifice, according to Malik, along with completing his rituals. Al-Shafi’i said: He must offer a sacrifice, and there is no meaning to Umrah if he returns, performs Tawaf and Sa’i. Abu Hanifah and his companions, al-Thawri and al-Sha’bi said: It is not obligatory. If one of the pilgrim omits it until he returns to his country, he must make up for it with blood money, because it is a Sunnah of Hajj. This is the opinion of Malik in al-‘Utbiyyah. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Al-Zubayr, Anas bin Malik and Ibn Sirin that he volunteered, based on the words of God the Almighty: And whoever volunteers good. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read yatawa’ in the subjunctive mood, and likewise So whoever volunteers good, it is better for him. The rest read yatawa’ in the past tense, which is what the believer does of his own accord. So whoever does something from the voluntary acts, God will thank him. And the evil of God for the servant is his reward for obedience. What is correct is what Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, went to for what we mentioned, and his saying, peace be upon him: Take from me your rituals, so it became a statement of the entirety of the Hajj. It must be obligatory, like his statement of the number of rak’ahs and what was like that if it was not agreed that it was a Sunnah or voluntary. Talib said: Ibn Abbas saw some people circumambulating between Safa and Marwa, so he said: This is what your mother, the mother of Ismail, taught you. I said: This is confirmed in Sahih Al-Bukhari, as will be explained in Surat Ibrahim. Ninth: It is not permissible for anyone to circumambulate the House or between Safa and Marwa while riding, except for one who has an excuse. If he circumambulates with an excuse, he must offer a sacrifice. If he circumambulates without an excuse, he must repeat it if he was in the presence of the House. If he was absent from it, he must offer a sacrifice. We only said that because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulated himself and said: Learn your rituals from me, but we only allowed that as an excuse. Because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, circumambulated on his camel and touched the corner with his stick. He said to Aisha when she said to him, I am sick, so he said, Perform the Tawaf behind the people while you are riding. Our companions differentiated between performing the Tawaf on a camel or on the back of a person. If he performs the Tawaf on the back of a person, it is not valid, because in that case he is not performing the Tawaf, but rather the one carrying him. If he performs the Tawaf on a camel, he is the one performing the Tawaf. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said, “This is a differentiation of choice. As for the sufficiency, it is valid. Do you not see that if he faints and is carried while being carried, or stands at Arafat while being carried, it is valid for him?”
2:159: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear to the people in the Scripture - those are cursed by God and cursed by those who curse. It has seven issues: First: God the Almighty informed us that whoever conceals the clear proofs and guidance that He has revealed is cursed. They differed about who is meant by that. It was said: The Jewish rabbis and Christian monks who concealed the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Jews concealed the matter of stoning. It was also said: What is meant is everyone who conceals the truth. It is general for everyone who conceals knowledge of the religion of God that needs to be spread. This is explained in the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever is asked about knowledge that he knows and conceals it, God will bridle him on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire. Narrated by Abu Hurairah and Amr ibn al-‘As, narrated by Ibn Majah. It is contradicted by the words of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud: If you tell people something that their minds cannot comprehend, it will be a trial for some of them. And he, peace be upon him, said: “Tell people what they understand. Do you like that God and His Messenger be called liars?” This applies to some sciences, such as theology, or what not all common people understand equally. The ruling of the scholar is that he should tell what he understands, and he should treat each person according to his status. And God knows best. Second: This is the verse that Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him meant when he said: Had it not been for a verse in the Book of God, the Most High, I would not have narrated to you a hadith. And with it, the scholars have proven the obligation of conveying true knowledge and explaining knowledge in general, without taking payment for it, since one does not deserve payment for what he must do, just as one does not deserve payment for Islam. We have already discussed this. The meaning of the verse is: If a scholar intends to conceal knowledge, he has disobeyed, and if he does not intend to, he is not obligated to convey it if he knows that it is with someone else. As for the one who is asked, he is obligated to convey it, based on this verse and the hadith. As for it being impermissible to teach a disbeliever the Qur’an and knowledge until he becomes Muslim, likewise it is impermissible to teach an innovator argumentation and pilgrimage so that he may argue with the people of truth, nor to teach an opponent an argument against his opponent that will cut off his wealth, nor to teach the ruler an interpretation that will lead to the misdeeds of the subjects, nor to spread concessions among the foolish so that they may make that a path to committing forbidden acts, abandoning obligatory duties, and the like. It is narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Do not withhold wisdom from its people, lest you wrong them, and do not give it to those who are not worthy of it, lest you wrong them. It was narrated that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not hang pearls around the necks of pigs, meaning to teach jurisprudence to those who are not qualified for it. Sahnun said: The hadith of Abu Hurairah and Amr ibn al-Aas only came about testimony. Ibn al-Arabi said: The correct view is the opposite, because in the hadith. Whoever is asked about knowledge and he did not say about testimony, and remains on the apparent until something comes to him that changes it, and God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s statement: Of the clear proofs and guidance includes what is explicitly stated and what is inferred, because the name guidance includes everyone. It is evidence of the obligation to act on the statement of one person, because clear proofs are not obligatory on him unless his statement is accepted. He said: Except for those who repent, reform, and declare [the truth], so he ruled that clear proofs are established by their statement. If it is said: It is possible that each one of them was forbidden from concealment and commanded to clarify so that the informants would increase and the report would be transmitted by them. We say: This is wrong, because they were not forbidden from concealment except when they were among those who were permitted to collude in it, and among those among them who were permitted to collude in concealment, their report would not be a reason for knowledge, and God Almighty knows best. Fourth: When he said: Of the clear proofs and guidance, he indicated that what was other than that is permissible to conceal, especially if there was fear with that, because that is more emphatic in concealing. Abu Hurairah left that when he was afraid, so he said: I memorized two vessels from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for one of them, I spread it, and as for the other, if I spread it, this throat would be cut. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. Abu Abdullah said: The throat is the passageway for food. Our scholars said: What Abu Hurairah did not spread, and he feared for himself in it temptation or killing, is only related to the matter of temptations and the text on the names of the apostates and hypocrites, and the like of this that is not related to clear proofs and guidance. And God knows best. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: After We made it clear. The metaphor in We made it clear refers to what was revealed of clear proofs and guidance. The Book is a generic noun, so what is meant is all the revealed books. Sixth: The Almighty said: And the cursers curse them. Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ said: What is meant by the cursers are the angels and the believers. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is clear and in accordance with the meaning of the statement. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: They are the insects and animals who are afflicted with drought because of the sins of the evil scholars who conceal [the truth], so let them curse them. Az-Zajjaj said: The correct statement is that of the one who said: The cursers are the angels and the believers. As for that being for the beasts of the earth, its reality cannot be ascertained except by a text or a related report, and we did not find anything from those two. I said: A report has been reported about this, narrated by Al-Bara’ bin Azib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the words of God Almighty: God curses them and those who curse curse them, he said: The beasts of the earth. It was narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Sabah, who told us on the authority of Ammar bin Muhammad, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Abu Al-Munhal, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of Al-Bara’, with a good chain of transmission. If it is said: How can those who do not have reason be grouped together as those who have reason? It is said: Because the action of those who have reason is attributed to them, as He said: I saw them prostrating to me and did not say prostrating to me, and He said: Why did you bear witness against us? and He said: And you see them looking at you, and there are many similar examples, and they will come, God willing. Al-Bara’ bin Azib and Ibn Abbas said: The cursers are all creatures except the two heavy things: the jinn and mankind, and that is because “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the disbeliever is struck in his grave and cries out, everyone hears him except the two heavy things, and every listener curses him”.
