Ibn Mas’ud and Al-Suddi said: It is the man who curses his companion, so the curse rises to the sky then descends and does not find the one about whom it was said worthy of it, so it returns to the one who spoke it and does not find him worthy, so it goes off and falls on the Jews who concealed what God Almighty revealed, so this is His statement: And the cursers curse them, so whoever among them dies, the curse is lifted from him and remains on whoever of the Jews remains.
2:160: God Almighty says: “Except for those who repent, reform, and declare [the truth]. Those - I will turn to them in forgiveness, and I am the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.” God the Almighty said: Except those who repent. God the Almighty excluded the repentant, righteous in their deeds and words, and those who turn back to their repentance. According to our scholars, it is not sufficient for a person to say: I have repented, until he shows in the second instance that he is different from the first. If he was an apostate, he returned to Islam, manifesting its laws. If he was one of the people of sin, righteous deeds appeared from him, and he avoided the people of corruption and the conditions he was in. If he was one of the people of idols, he avoided them and mixed with the people of Islam, and thus the opposite of what he was in appears. The explanation of repentance and its rulings will come in the chapter on women, God willing. Some scholars said about His statement: and they made clear that is, by breaking the wine and pouring it out. It was said: and they made clear means what is in the Torah about the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the obligation to follow him. The generality is more appropriate for what we have explained, that is, they made clear the opposite of what they were in, and God the Almighty knows best. Then those, I will turn to them in forgiveness, and I am the Forgiving, the Merciful. This has been presented, and praise be to God.
2:161: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - upon them is the curse of God and of the angels and of mankind, all together.
2:162: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And they are disbelievers. The waw is the waw of state. Ibn al-Arabi said: Many of my sheikhs told me that it is not permissible to curse a specific disbeliever, because his state upon death is not known. And God the Almighty stipulated in this verse in the release of the curse: death upon disbelief. As for what was narrated from the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that he cursed specific people from the disbelievers, that was only because he knew their end. Ibn al-Arabi said: What is correct in my opinion is that it is permissible to curse him based on his apparent state and the permissibility of killing and fighting him. And “it was narrated from the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that he said: O God, Amr ibn al-Aas satirized me and he knew that I am not a poet, so curse him and satirize him as many times as he satirized me.” So he cursed him, even though faith, religion, and Islam were his end. He concluded by saying: The number of times he satirized me, and he did not add anything to show justice and fairness. He added satire to God Almighty in the chapter on retribution without beginning with the description of that, as deceit, mockery, and trickery are added to it. Glory be to Him and He is far above what the wrongdoers say, far above. I said: As for cursing the infidels as a whole without specifying them, there is no disagreement about that, because Malik narrated on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn that he heard al-A’raj say: I never knew people except that they cursed the infidels in Ramadan. Our scholars said: It is the same whether they had a covenant with them or not, and it is not obligatory, but it is permissible for whoever does it, because of their denial of the truth and their enmity towards the religion and its people. Likewise, everyone who migrates with sins such as drinking alcohol and taking usury, and whoever among women imitates men and whoever among men imitates women, and other things that have been mentioned in the hadiths, he is cursed. Second: Cursing an unbeliever is not a way to deter him from unbelief, but rather it is a punishment for unbelief and a demonstration of the ugliness of his unbelief, whether the unbeliever is dead or insane. Some of the early Muslims said: There is no benefit in cursing one of them who has gone mad or died, neither as a punishment nor as a deterrent, because he will not be affected by it. The meaning of the verse in this sense is that people will curse him on the Day of Resurrection so that he will be affected by that and be harmed and his heart will be pained, and that will be a punishment for his disbelief, as God the Almighty said: Then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disbelieve in others and curse others. This statement is indicated by the fact that the verse indicates the report from God the Almighty about cursing them, not the command. Ibn al-Arabi mentioned that cursing a specific sinner is not permissible by consensus, because “it was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that a drunkard was brought to him repeatedly, and some of those who were present said: May God curse him, how often he is brought to him! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not be the help of Satan against your brother.” So he gave him the sanctity of brotherhood, and this necessitates compassion, and this is an authentic hadith. I said: It was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. Some scholars have mentioned a difference of opinion regarding cursing a specific sinner. He said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Do not be the helper of Satan against your brother regarding Nu’ayman after the prescribed punishment was carried out on him. Whoever has the prescribed punishment carried out on him should not be cursed, and whoever has not been prescribed, his curse is valid, whether he was named or specified or not, because the Prophet (peace be upon him) only curses whoever is required to be cursed as long as he is in that state that requires cursing. If he repents from it, desists, and the prescribed punishment purifies him, then no curse is directed at him. This is explained by his (peace be upon him) saying: If one of your female slaves commits adultery, let him flog her with the prescribed punishment and not rebuke her. This hadith, despite its authenticity, indicates that rebuke and cursing should only be done before the prescribed punishment is carried out and before repentance. And God Almighty knows best. Ibn al-Arabi said: As for cursing the sinner absolutely, it is permissible by consensus, because it was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: May God curse the thief who steals an egg and has his hand cut off. Third: The Almighty’s statement: Upon them is the curse of God and of the angels and of all mankind, meaning that they will be removed from His mercy. The root of curse is expulsion and banishment, as mentioned above. So the curse from the servants is expulsion, and from God is punishment. Al-Hasan al-Basri read al-Ankiyyah wa al-Nasun in the nominative case. Its interpretation is: Those, their reward is that God curses them, the angels curse them, and all mankind curses them, just as you say: I hated that Zaid, Amr, and Khalid stood up, because the meaning is: I hated that Zaid stood up. Al-Hasan’s reading is contrary to the copies of the Qur’an. If it is said: Not all people curse them because their people do not declare them, three answers have been given to this, the first of which is that the curse from most people is called the curse of people, giving precedence to the rule of the majority over the least. The second: Al-Suddi said: Everyone curses the oppressor, and if the disbeliever curses the oppressor, then he has cursed himself. The third: Abu Al-Aaliyah said: What is meant by it is on the Day of Resurrection, their people will curse them along with all people, as God the Almighty said: Then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disbelieve in others and curse one another. Then God the Almighty said: They will abide therein meaning in the curse, that is, in its punishment. It was said: Their abiding in the curse is that it is perpetual upon them, nor will they be reprieved meaning they will not be delayed from the punishment for any time. And they will abide is in the accusative case as a state of the ha’ and the mim in upon them, and the factor in it is the circumstance of His saying: upon them because it has the meaning of the curse being established.
2:163: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And your God is one God. When the Almighty warned against concealing the truth, He made clear that the first thing that must be revealed and cannot be concealed is the matter of monotheism. He connected that with mentioning the proof and teaching the way of contemplation, which is thinking about the wonders of creation, so that one may know that it must have a doer who is not like anything. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The infidels of Quraysh said: O Muhammad, describe to us your Lord. So God Almighty revealed Surat Al-Ikhlas and this verse. The polytheists had three hundred and sixty idols, so God made clear that He is One. Second: The Almighty’s saying: There is no god but He is negation and affirmation. The first is disbelief and the last is faith, and its meaning is there is no god but God. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Shibli, may God have mercy on him, that he used to say: God, and not say: There is no god. So he was asked about that and he said: I fear that I will start with a word of denial and not reach a word of acknowledgment. I said: This is one of their subtle sciences, which has no reality. God, the Most High, mentioned this meaning in His Book, denying and affirming it, and repeated it, and promised a great reward to the one who says it on the tongue of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was reported by Al-Muwatta’, Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever’s last words are ‘There is no god but God’ will enter Paradise. Narrated by Muslim. What is meant is the heart, not the tongue. If he said ‘There is no god’ and died with his belief and conscience being Oneness and the attributes that are due to Him, then he would be among the people of Paradise according to the consensus of the people of Sunnah. We have already discussed the meaning of His name, ‘The One’, ‘There is no god but Him’, and ‘The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful’ in the Most Sublime Book, in the explanation of the beautiful names of God. Praise be to God.
2:164: It has four issues: First: Ata’ said: When the verse And your God is one God was revealed, the infidels of Quraysh said: How can one God be enough for the people! So the verse Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth was revealed. Sufyan narrated it on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha who said: When the verse And your God is one God was revealed, they said: Is there any proof for that? So God the Most High revealed: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth It was as if they were seeking a sign, so He showed them the proof of monotheism, and that this world and wondrous construction must have a Creator and a Maker. He gathered the heavens together because they are different kinds, each heaven being of a different kind than the other. And He made the earth unified because it is all dust, and God the Most High knows best. The sign of the heavens: their elevation without pillars beneath them or connections above them, this indicates power and a breach of custom. If a prophet had come and challenged a mountain to stand in the air without a connection, it would have been a miracle. Then what is in them of the sun, the moon, the moving stars, and the shining planets, rising and setting, bright and obliterated, is a second sign. The sign of the earth: its seas, rivers, minerals, trees, plains and rugged areas. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And the alternation of the night and the day. It was said: Their alternation is in the approach of one and the retreat of the other from where he does not know. It was also said: Their alternation is in the descriptions of light and darkness, length and shortness. Night is the plural of night, like tiger and date and palm tree and bee. It is also pluralized as nights and nights with the same meaning, and it is one of the exceptions to the standard of plurals, like similarity and similarity and need and needs and remembrance and memories, and it is as if nights in the standard is the plural of night. And they used that in poetry. He said: Every day and every night Another said: Every day has its own special nights, until every person who sees it says, Oh, what a miserable camel he is! Ibn Faris said in Al-Mujmal: It is said that some birds are called Laila, but I do not know it. The word day is the plural of river and rivers. Ahmad bin Yahya Tha’lab said: River is the plural of river, which is the plural of day. It was said that day is a singular noun that is not pluralized because it means a source, like light, which applies to both little and much. The first, the poet said: If it weren't for Tharidan, we would have perished from hunger. Tharid at night and Tharid by the river. Ibn Faris said: The day is well-known, and the plural is river and rivers. It is said that the day is pluralized as river. Day is the light between sunrise and sunset. A man of the river is a person of the day. It is said that the day is the chick of the bustard. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The beginning of the day is sunrise, and what comes before that is not counted from the day. Tha’lab said: The beginning of the day among the Arabs is sunrise, and he cited as evidence the statement of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt. And the sun rises every last night red, its color turning rosy And he recited the words of Adi bin Zaid: And He made the sun a place of refuge, between which there is no concealment, and between the day and the night He has separated them. Al-Kisa’i recited: If the sun rises during the day, it is a sign of my greetings to you, so greet me. Al-Zajjaj said in the Book of Meteors: The beginning of the day is the peak of the sun. Ibn al-Anbari divided time into three parts: a part he made pure night, which is from sunset to sunrise. A part he made pure day, which is from sunrise to sunset. A part he made shared between day and night, which is between sunrise and sunrise, due to the remnants of the darkness of the night and the exchange of light of the day. I said: The correct view is that the day is from sunrise to sunset, as narrated by Ibn Faris in Al-Mujmal, and is indicated by what is proven in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Adi bin Hatim, who said: When the verse was revealed: ‘Until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread,’ Adi said to him: O Messenger of God, I put two ropes under my pillow: a white rope and a black rope, by which I can tell night from day. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your pillow is wide, for it is only the blackness of the night and the whiteness of the day.” This hadith dictates that the day is from sunrise to sunset, and this is what is required by jurisprudence in oaths, and rulings are connected to it. So whoever swears not to speak to someone during the day and then speaks to him before sunrise, he has broken his oath, but according to the first view, he does not break his oath. The statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the decisive factor in that and the ruling. As for the apparent meaning of the curse and its being taken from the Sunnah, it is from the time of dawn when the time of day is wide, as he said: I held her in my hand and opened her rupture, and what was behind her could be seen. Hudhayfah has reported evidence for this statement, as reported by Al-Nasa’i. It will come in the verses on fasting, God willing. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And the ships that sail through the sea. The word al-Falak means ships. Its singular and plural are the same, and it is masculine and feminine. The vowels in the singular are not the same as in the plural, but it is as if He built the plural with another construction, as indicated by the dual in their saying: Falakana. The singular al-Falak is masculine. The Almighty said: In the laden ship, so He made it masculine. He said: And the ships that sail through the sea, so He made it feminine. It is possible for it to be singular or plural. He said: Until, when you were in the ship and they sailed with them with a good wind, so He made it plural. It is as if He is taking it, if it is singular, to the boat, so it is masculine, and to the ship, so it is feminine. It was said: The singular is al-Falak, like asad and asad, and khashab and khashab, and its origin is from dawwar, and from it: falak al-samaa on which the stars revolve. The young woman’s breast is round, and from it is falaka, the spindle. The ship was called al-Falak because it revolves in the water with the easiest rotation. The meaning of the verse in the ark is that God subjected it so that it would float on the surface of the water and stop on it despite its weight. The first person to make it was Noah, peace be upon him, as God Almighty has informed us. Gabriel said to him: Make it on the crown of a bird. So Noah, peace be upon him, made it as an inheritance in the worlds, as Gabriel showed him: The ark is an inverted bird, and the water at its bottom is like the air at its top, as Ibn al-Arabi said. Fourth: This verse and others like it are evidence of the permissibility of sailing in general, whether for trade or worship, such as Hajj and Jihad. From the Sunnah is the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we ride the sea and carry with us a little water. Hadith. The hadith of Anas bin Malik in the story of Umm Haram, both of them were narrated by the Imams: Malik and others. The hadith of Anas was narrated by a group from him from Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Talhah from Anas, and it was narrated by Bishr bin Omar from Malik from Ishaq from Anas from Umm Haram, and he included it in the Musnad of Umm Haram, not from the Musnad of Anas. This is how Bandar Muhammad bin Bashar narrated it from him, so it is clear evidence for riding the sea in jihad for men and women, and if riding it for jihad is permissible, then riding it for the obligatory Hajj is more appropriate and obligatory. It was narrated from Omar bin Al-Khattab and Omar bin Abdul Aziz, may God be pleased with them, that it is forbidden to ride it. The Qur’an and Sunnah refute this statement, and if riding it was disliked or not permissible, the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, would have forbidden it to those who said to him: We ride the sea. This verse and others like it are clear on the purpose and to it is the resort. What was narrated from the two Omars in this regard may be interpreted as meaning that it is carried on caution and refraining from deceiving the soul in seeking the world and acquiring more of it, but not in performing the obligatory duties. What indicates the permissibility of riding it in terms of meaning is that God Almighty made the sea in the middle of the earth and made creation in the two sides, and divided the benefits between the two sides so that they cannot be brought except by splitting the sea for it, so God made its path easy with His help, said Ibn al-Arabi. Abu Omar said: Malik disliked for women to ride by sea for Hajj, and it is for jihad, so he disliked it. The Qur’an and Sunnah refute his statement, except that some of our companions from Basra said: Malik disliked it because the ships in Hijaz are small, and women are not able to cover themselves when relieving themselves in them due to their narrowness and the crowding of people in them, and the road from Madinah to Mecca by land is possible, so Malik disliked it. As for large ships like the ships of the people of Basra, there is nothing wrong with that. He said: The basic principle is that Hajj is for every free adult who can find a way to it, whether they are women or men, if the majority of the way is safe, and it does not specify a sea over a land route. I said: The Book, the Sunnah and the meaning indicate that riding it is permissible for both purposes: worship and trade. This is the proof and the example. However, people differ in their circumstances when it comes to riding the sea. There may be a rider who finds it easy and not difficult, and another who finds it difficult and weak, like the one who is overloaded with food, or the one who is unable to perform the obligatory prayer and other obligatory duties with it. The first one is permitted to do so, and the second one is forbidden and prevented from doing so. There is no disagreement among the scholars regarding riding the sea, and it is: Fifth: If the sea is rough, it is not permissible for anyone to ride it under any circumstances, during the time of its roughness, nor at a time when safety is most likely. Rather, it is permissible for them to ride it at a time when safety is most likely. Those who ride it at a time of safety and are saved have no one to stop them, and those who perish in it are stopped. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: That which benefits people meaning that which benefits them from trade and other interests that improve their conditions. And by sailing the sea, profits are earned, and the one who carries the goods to it also benefits. Some of those who have criticized the religion have said: God Almighty says in your book: We have neglected nothing in the Book. So where is the mention of spices that improve food, such as salt, pepper, and other things? So it was said to him regarding His saying: That which benefits people. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And what God sends down from the sky of water, meaning by this the rains that revive the world and produce plants and provisions, and He made it stored and used for benefit at a time other than its time of descent, as the Almighty said: And We settled it in the earth. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And He has scattered therein every kind of moving creature, meaning He has scattered and dispersed it. From this comes the word like scattered moths. A moving creature gathers animals for it. Some people have mentioned birds, but this is rejected. God Almighty said: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, for the bird crawls on its feet in some cases. Al-A’sha said: The crawling of the sand cat in every watering place Alqamah bin Abdah said: Its thunderbolts make their birds crawl Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: And the changing of the winds. Its changing: sending them barren and fertilizing, and rain and victory and destruction, and hot and cold, and gentle and stormy. It was said: Its changing: sending them south and north, and wasps and downpours, and calamities, and they come between the blows of two winds. It was said: Its changing: that the large ships come according to what they can carry, and the small ones as well, and what harms them is diverted from them, and no consideration is given to the size of the castles or their smallness, because if the wind came as one body, it would hit the castles and sink them. The winds are the plural of wind, and it was named thus because it usually brings the soul. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The wind is from the spirit of God. It brings mercy and it brings torment. So when you see it, do not curse it. Ask God for its good and seek refuge in God from its evil.” It was also included by Ibn Majah in his Sunan. Abu Bakr Ibn Abi Shaybah told us. Yahya Ibn Saeed told us, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Thabit Al-Zarqi told us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not curse the wind, for it is from the spirit of God and brings mercy and torment. Rather, ask God for its good and seek refuge in God from its evil.” It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not curse the wind, for it is from the breath of the Most Gracious. The meaning is that God Almighty has made it a means of relief, relaxation, relaxation, and addition through action. The meaning is that God Almighty has made it thus. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: I was aided by the north wind and destroyed by the south wind. This is the meaning of what came in the hadith that God, the Most High, relieved his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the wind on the day of the Confederates, as God, the Most High, said: So We sent against them a wind and soldiers you did not see. It is said that God relieved someone of a worldly distress, meaning He relieved him. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him: Whoever relieves a Muslim of a worldly distress, God will relieve him of a distress on the Day of Resurrection. That is, He will relieve him. The poet said: As if the morning breeze is a wind that, when it blows on a worried heart, reveals its worries. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The breeze is the first blowing of the wind. The root of wind is ruh, and for this reason the plural of paucity is called arwah, and it is not said ariyyah, because it is one of the words with the letter waw. Rather, it is said riyyah because of the abundance and the desire to make the letter ya consistent with it. In the Mushaf of Hafsa and the derivation of arwah. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: And the direction of the winds. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read al-rih in the singular, and so it is in Al-A’raf, Al-Kahf, Ibrahim, An-Naml, Ar-Rum, Fatir, Ash-Shura, and Al-Jathiyah. There is no disagreement between them on that. Ibn Kathir agreed with them in Al-A’raf, An-Naml, Ar-Rum, Fatir, and Ash-Shura. Hamzah isolated al-rihah wa as-sahab. Ibn Kathir isolated and He is the One Who sent the winds in Al-Furqan. The rest read it in the plural in all of them except for Ibrahim and Ash-Shura. Only Nafi’ read them in the plural, and the seven did not differ on anything other than these places. What we mentioned in Ar-Rum is the second God who sends the winds. There is no disagreement between them on the winds are good tidings. Abu Ja’far Yazid ibn Al-Qa’qa’ used to pluralize the winds if they had an alif and lam in them throughout the Qur’an, except for tahwu bih al-rih and ar-rih al-‘aqim. If it did not have an alif and lam, he would singularize it. Whoever used the singular of al-rih did so because it is a generic noun that indicates little or much. And whoever combined it, it is because of the different directions from which the winds blow. And whoever combined it with mercy and made it singular with torment, he did so based on the majority in the Qur’an, such as: the winds are good tidings and the barren wind. So it came in the Qur’an combined with mercy and singular with torment, except in Yunus, in His statement: And they sailed with them with a good wind. And it was narrated: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when the wind blew: ‘O God, make it a wind and do not make it a wind.’” This is because the wind of torment is strong and its parts are joined together as if it were a single body, while the wind of mercy is gentle and intermittent, and therefore it is a wind. It was singled out with the ark in Yunus, because the wind that moves the ships is only one continuous wind, then it was described as pleasant, so the similarity between it and the wind of torment was removed. Eleventh: The scholars said that the wind moves the air, and it may be strong or weak. If the air movement appears from the direction of the qiblah going in the direction of the qiblah, that wind is called the saba. If the air movement appears from behind the qiblah and is going in the direction of the qiblah, that wind is called the dabur. If the air movement appears to be to the right of the qiblah going to its left, it is called the south wind. If the air movement appears to be to the left of the qiblah going to its right, it is called the north wind. Each of these winds has a nature, so its benefit is according to its nature. The saba wind is hot and dry, the dabur wind is cold and humid, the south wind is hot and humid, and the north wind is cold and dry. The differences in their natures are like the differences in the natures of the seasons of the year. God Almighty has set four seasons for time, which are based on the change in the conditions of the air. He made spring, which is the first of the seasons, hot and humid, and arranged the generations in it, so the waters descend in it, the earth produces its flowers and its plants appear, and people begin to plant trees and many crops, and animals reproduce in it and milk increases. When spring ends, it is followed by summer, which is similar to spring in one of its natures, which is heat, and different from it in the other, which is humidity, because the air in summer is hot and dry, so the fruits ripen and the grains planted in spring dry up. When summer ends, it is followed by autumn, which is similar to summer in one of its two natures, which is dryness, and different from it in the other, which is heat, because the air in autumn is hot and dry, so the fruits reach their peak of ripeness and dry up and become stored, so the fruits are picked, the grapes are harvested and the trees are emptied of their harvest. When autumn ends, winter follows it, which is compatible with autumn in one of its two natures, which is coldness, and different from it in the other, which is dryness, because the air in winter is cold and mixed, so rain and snow increase and the ground is smoothed like a resting body, so it does not move unless God Almighty restores to it the heat of spring. When it combines with moisture, then there will be growth and development, by the permission of God Almighty. Many winds may blow other than what we have mentioned, except that the principles are these four. So every wind that blows between two winds, its ruling is the ruling of the wind that blows closest to its place and is called the Nakba. Twelfth: The Almighty said: And the clouds controlled between the sky and the earth. The clouds are called clouds because they drift in the air. I dragged my tails a cloud. So-and-so dragged on so-and-so a person dared to do so. Drag a person who is severely eating and drinking is called musakhar the one who is subdued, and tasakhar subjugated means sending him from one place to another. It was said: Taakhar subjugated means his being fixed between the sky and the earth without pillars or connections, but the first is more apparent. It may be with water or torment. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: While a man was in a desert, he heard a voice in a cloud saying, Water the garden of so-and-so. The cloud moved away and its water spread out in a lava field. Then one of those clouds absorbed all of that water. He followed the water and saw a man standing in his garden, moving the water with his shovel. He said to him, O servant of God, what is your name? He said, So-and-so, for the name he heard in the cloud. He said, O servant of God, why did you ask me about my name? He said, “I heard a voice in the cloud whose water is this saying, ‘Water the garden of so-and-so, for your name. So what do you do with it?’ He said, “Since you have said this, I look at what comes out of it and give a third of it in charity, and I and my family eat a third, and I return a third of it.” In another narration: And I give a third of it to the poor, the beggars, and the wayfarer. In the revelation: And God is He who sends the winds, and they stir up the clouds, and We drive them to a dead land. And He said, Until, when they carry heavy clouds, We drive them to a dead land. This is often mentioned in the revelation. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Aisha. “Whenever the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw a cloud approaching from a certain horizon, he would leave whatever he was doing, even if he was praying, until he faced it and said: ‘O God, we seek refuge in You from the evil of that which You have sent.’ If it rained, he would say: ‘O God, make it beneficial rain,’ two or three times. If God removed it and it did not rain, he would praise God for that.” Muslim narrated it with the same meaning on the authority of Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: “When it was a windy and cloudy day, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would show it on his face and he would come and go. When it rained, he would be pleased with it and it would go away from him. Aisha said: So I asked him and he said: I feared that it would be a punishment that would be inflicted on my nation.” “And he would say when he saw rain: ‘Mercy.’” In another narration, he said: Perhaps, O Aisha, it is as the people of Aad said: But when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, ‘This is a cloud bringing us rain.’ These hadiths and verses indicate the correctness of the first statement and that its being subjected does not mean its being fixed, and God knows best. For fixity indicates the absence of movement. If what is meant by fixity is that it is in the air, not in the sky or on the earth, then that is correct, because He said, And yet it is subjected and carried, and that is greater in power, like the bird in the air. God Almighty said: Have they not seen the birds controlled in the atmosphere of the sky? None holds them up except God. And He said: Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading out their wings and folding them in? None holds them up except the Most Gracious. Thirteenth: Ka'b al-Ahbar said: The clouds are a sieve for rain. Were it not for the clouds when water descends from the sky, they would spoil whatever land it falls upon. Narrated by Ibn Abbas. Al-Khatib Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ali mentioned it on the authority of Mu'adh ibn Abdullah ibn Khabib al-Juhani, who said: I saw Ibn Abbas passing by on a mule while I was in Bani Salamah. Tabi' ibn Aunt Ka'b passed by him and greeted Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas asked him: Have you heard Ka'b al-Ahbar say anything about the clouds? He said: Yes. He said: The clouds are a sieve for rain. Were it not for the clouds when water descends from the sky, they would spoil whatever land it falls upon. He said: Did you hear Ka'b say about the earth that it grows one plant each year and another the next year? He said: Yes, I heard him say: The seed descends from the sky. Ibn Abbas said: I heard that from Ka'b. Fourteenth: The Almighty’s saying: Signs meaning indications that indicate His Oneness and Power. Therefore, He mentioned these matters after His saying: And your God is one God to indicate with them the truth of the report of what He mentioned before it about His Oneness, glory be to Him, and to mention His mercy and compassion for His creation. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Woe to he who reads this verse and does not reflect on it or consider it. If it is said: Why did you deny that they created themselves? It is said to him: This is impossible, because if they created themselves, they would have created them while they existed or they were nonexistent. If they created them while they were nonexistent, then this would be impossible, because creation can only come from a living, knowledgeable, capable, and willing being, and what does not exist cannot be described as such. If they exist, then their existence suffices from creating themselves. Also, if what they said were permissible, then it would be permissible for the building itself to come into existence, and likewise carpentry and weaving, and this is impossible, and what leads to the impossible is impossible. Then God the Most High did not limit His Oneness to mere report, but rather He linked that with contemplation and consideration in verses of the Qur’an, so He said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say: ‘Look at what is in the heavens and the earth.’” The address is to the disbelievers, because God the Most High said: And signs and warners do not avail a people who do not believe. And He said: Have they not considered the dominion of the heavens and the earth? By the dominion, He means the signs. He said: And in yourselves, do you not see? He says: Have they not looked at this with thought and deliberation, so that they can deduce from its being the place of accidents and changes that they are created, and that the Creator cannot do without a Maker to create it, and that Maker is Wise, All-Knowing, All-Powerful, Willing, All-Hearing, All-Seeing, and All-Speaking, because if He did not have these attributes, man would be more perfect than him, and that is impossible. And God Almighty said: And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay, meaning Adam, peace be upon him, Then We made him, meaning We made his offspring and descendants, a sperm-drop in a secure lodging, until the words: You will be resurrected. So if man thinks about this warning with what He has given him of reason in himself, he will see it managing and disposing of various conditions. He was a sperm, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then flesh and bones. He knows that he did not transfer himself from a state of deficiency to a state of perfection, because he is not able to create for himself in the best state, which is the perfection of his mind and the attainment of his prime, a limb from the limbs, nor can he add a limb to his limbs. This indicates to him that in his state of deficiency and the time of his weakness, he is unable to do that. He may see himself as a young man, then an adult, then an old man, and he did not transfer himself from a state of youth and strength to a state of old age and decrepitude, nor did he choose it for himself, nor is it within his power to remove the state of gray hair and regain the strength of youth. He knows from this that he is not the one who did those actions himself, and that he has a Maker who made him and a Transmitter who transferred him from one state to another. Were it not for that, his states would not have changed without a Transmitter or Manager. Some of the wise men said: Everything in the greater world has a counterpart in the smaller world, which is the human body. Therefore, God the Almighty said: Indeed, We created man in the best stature. And He said: And in yourselves, then will you not see? The senses of man are more noble than the shining planets, and hearing and sight are like the sun and moon in perceiving what is perceived by them. His limbs, when they wear out, turn into dust of the same kind as the earth, and in it is sweat and all the moistures of the body, and in it is the spirit and soul, and in it is the yellow bile. His veins are like the rivers in the earth, and his liver is like the eyes from which the rivers are drawn, because the veins are drawn from the liver. His bladder is like the sea, because what is in the vessels of the body flows into it as the rivers flow into the sea. His bones are like the mountains, which are the pegs of the earth. His limbs are like trees, so just as every tree has leaves or fruits, so too every limb has an action or effect. Hair on the body is like plants and grass on the earth. Then man narrates with his tongue every sound of an animal, and imitates with his limbs the action of every animal, so he is the small world with the great world, created and brought into existence by one Maker, there is no god but Him.
2:165: When God Almighty informed in the verse before what indicated His Oneness, His Power, and the Greatness of His Authority, He informed that with these verses that overpower those with reason, there are those who take rivals with Him, and the singular of which is rival, and it has been mentioned before. What is meant are the idols and statues that they worshipped as worship of God, despite their weakness, as Mujahid said. God the Almighty said: They love them as they love God meaning they love their idols in falsehood as the believers love God in truth. This was stated by Al-Mubarrad. Al-Zajjaj said its meaning. That is, despite the weakness of the idols, they love them as the believers love God despite His power. Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi said: What is meant by peers are the leaders who are followed, they obey them in disobeying God. The pronoun in they love them came in this way according to the original, and according to the first, the pronoun of someone who has reason came in a way other than the original. Ibn Kaysan and Al-Zajjaj also said: The meaning of they love them as they love God is they equate the idols with God the Almighty in love. Abu Ishaq said: This is the correct statement, and the evidence for its correctness is: And those who believe are stronger in love for God. Abu Raja’ read they love them with a fat-ha on the ya’. This is also what was mentioned in the Qur’an, and it is a language. It is said: I loved the man, so he is beloved. Al-Farra’ said: Abu Turab recited to me: I love Sudan for its love, even the black dogs love it The word min in his statement man yakhadahu is in the nominative case as a subject, and yakhadahu is in the verbal form. It is permissible in other than the Qur’an to say yakhadahu in the meaning, and yahbubhum in the meaning, and yahbubhum in the verbal form. It is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in yakhadahu meaning lovers. If you wish, it is an adjective for the peers, meaning beloved. The kaf in kahab is an adjective for a deleted source, meaning they love them with a love like the love of God. And those who believe are stronger in love for God meaning stronger than the love of the idolaters for their idols and the followers for their followers. It was said that He said And those who believe are stronger in love for God because God, the Most High, loved them first, then they loved Him. And whoever his beloved testifies to his love, his love is more complete. God, the Most High, said: He loves them and they love Him. The statement of the believers’ love for God, the Most High, and His love for them will come in Surah Al Imran, God willing. God the Almighty said: And if those who did wrong could see when they see the punishment that all power belongs to God and that God is severe in punishment. The people of Medina and Ash-Sham read it with a ta’, and the people of Mecca, Kufa, and Abu Amr read it with a ya’, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid. There is a problem and an omission in this verse, so Abu Ubaid said: The meaning is: If those who did wrong in this world saw the punishment of the Hereafter, they would know when they see it that all power belongs to God. And see on this is from seeing with the eyes. An-Nahhas said in his book Ma’ani al-Quran: This is the statement that the people of interpretation are upon. And he said in his book I’rab al-Quran: It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid that he said: This interpretation that Abu Ubaid came up with is far-fetched, and his expression in it is not good, because he estimates: And if those who did wrong could see the punishment, so it is as if he makes it doubtful and God the Almighty has made it obligatory, but the estimate, which is the statement of Al-Akhfash, is: And if those who did wrong could see that all power belongs to God. And see means to know, meaning if they knew the reality of God’s power and the severity of His punishment, so see is used to indicate that all power belongs to God, and it replaces the two objects. And those who are the subject of sees, and the answer to if is omitted, meaning that they may realize the harm of their taking gods, as the Almighty said: And if you could but see when they are made to stand before their Lord, “And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire,” and there is no answer to if. Al-Zuhri and Qatada said: The omission is more severe for the threat, and it is similar to the saying of the one who says: If you could see so-and-so and the whips seizing him! And whoever reads with the ta’, then the meaning is: And if you could see, O Muhammad, those who did wrong when they see the punishment and are terrified by it and think it is too great for them, they would realize that power belongs to God. So the answer is omitted in this manner of meaning and it is the factor in that and another meaning is: And if you could see, O Muhammad, those who did wrong when they see the punishment and are terrified by it, you would know that power belongs to God entirely. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that, but he was addressed and what was meant was his nation, for among them are those who need to strengthen their knowledge by seeing something like this. And it is possible that the meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, to the wrongdoer: This. It was said: An is in the position of an accusative object for the sake of which, meaning because all power belongs to God. Sibawayh recited: Forgive the generous person’s shortcomings and turn away from the slander of the ignoble person out of generosity. That is, to save it, and the meaning is: And if you could but, O Muhammad, those who did wrong when they see the punishment, because power belongs to God, you would know the extent of their punishment and you would not have considered what happened to them great. And the particle if was included in what preceded in establishing these future events to approximate the matter and correct its occurrence. Ibn Amir alone read yarowu with a damma on the ya’, and the rest read it with a fatha on it. Al-Hasan, Ya’qub, Shaibah, Salam, and Abu Ja’far read inna al-quwwa and inna lahu with a kasra on the hamza in both of them, as a resumption or as an estimate of the statement, that is, and if you could but see those who did wrong when they see the punishment, they would say, Indeed, power belongs to God. And the power is established by the text of this verse, contrary to the statement of the Mu’tazila in their denial of the meanings of the eternal attributes, God is exalted above what they say.
2:166: The Almighty said: When those who followed disavowed themselves meaning the masters and leaders disavowed those who followed them in disbelief, according to Qatada, Ata' and Ar-Rabi'. Qatada also said and As-Suddi: They are the misguiding devils who disavowed mankind. It was said: It is general for every followed person. And they saw the punishment meaning the followers and the followed. It was said: With their certainty of it when they saw it in this world. It was said: When they are presented and questioned in the Hereafter. I said: Both are possible. They will see at death what humiliation they will become, and in the afterlife they will taste painful torment and punishment. The Almighty said: And their ties were severed meaning the connections that they used to have in this world, such as kinship and other things, according to Mujahid and others. The singular is reason and connection. The root of reason is a rope that is tied to something and pulls it. Then everything that pulls something is made a cause. Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: The causes are their actions. The cause is the direction, and from this is the saying of Zuhair: Whoever fears the causes of death will be overtaken by it, even if he seeks the causes of heaven with a ladder.
2:167: The Almighty said: And those who followed said, 'If only we had another chance' The an is in the nominative case, meaning if it were proven that we would return, then we would disown them is the answer to the wish. The against is the return and reversion to a state that had been, meaning the followers said: If only we were returned to the world so that we could do good and disown them as they disowned us meaning disown as so the kaf is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted source. It is permissible for it to be accusative as a state, its confirmation being disowning, and disowning is separation. God the Almighty said: Thus will God show them their deeds as regrets for them. The Kaf is in the nominative case, meaning that is the matter. That is, just as God showed them the punishment, so will God show them their deeds. God will show them was said to be from seeing with the eyes, so it is transitive with two objects: the first is the Ha and the Meem in show them. The second is their deeds, and regrets is a state. It is possible that it is from seeing with the heart, so regrets is the third object. Their deeds. Al-Rabi’ said: meaning the corrupt deeds that they committed, which made Hell obligatory for them. Ibn Mas’ud and Al-Suddi said: the righteous deeds that they abandoned, which made them miss out on Paradise. Hadiths were narrated on this statement. Al-Suddi said: Paradise will be raised up for them, so they will look at it and at their homes in it, if they had obeyed God the Almighty. Then it will be divided among the believers, and that is when they will regret it. These deeds were attributed to them because they were commanded to do them, but the corrupt deeds were attributed to them because they did them. Regret is one of the regrets, like a date and dates, a plate and eyelids, and desire and desires. This is if it is a noun, then its description is quiescent, like you say: huge and huge, and obscene and oblate. Regret is the highest degree of remorse for something lost. Regret is yearning, it is said: I regretted it in the kasra ahsr regret and regret. It is derived from the thing hasir that has been cut off and its strength has gone, like a camel when it becomes tired. It was said: it is derived from hasir if it is uncovered, and from it hasir in war: the one who has no armor with him. And retreat: exposure. The Almighty’s saying: And they will not come out of the Fire is evidence of the infidels’ eternity in it and that they will not come out of it. This is the saying of the majority of the people of the Sunnah, regarding this verse, and the Almighty’s saying: And they will not enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. And it will come.
2:168: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O mankind verse. It was said that it was revealed about Thaqeef, Khuza’ah, and Banu Mudlij regarding the livestock they forbade themselves, and the wording is general. Here, good means permissible, so it is an emphasis on the difference in wording. This is what Malik said about good. Al-Shafi’i said: Good means pleasant, so it is a variation, and therefore it is forbidden to eat dirty animals. This will be explained in Al-An’am and Al-A’raf, God willing. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Lawful and good. “Lawful” is a state, and it was said that it is a passive participle. And the lawful was called lawful because the prohibition was dissolved from it. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Salvation is in three things: eating lawful things, performing the obligatory duties, and following the example of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Abdullah al-Saji, whose name is Saeed ibn Yazid, said: Five characteristics complete knowledge, and they are: knowing God Almighty, knowing the truth, sincerity in action for God, acting according to the Sunnah, and eating lawful things. If one of them is missing, the action is not lifted. Sahl said: Eating lawful things is not valid except with knowledge, and money is not lawful until it is free from six characteristics: usury, unlawful things, ill-gotten gains - and this is a general name - embezzlement, what is disliked, and suspicion. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And do not follow is a prohibition in the footsteps of Satan. “Khatwat” is the plural of Khatwat and Khatwat means the same thing. Al-Farra’ said: Khatwat is the plural of Khatwat with a fat-ha. Khatwat with a damma is what is between the feet. Al-Jawhari said: The plural of “Khatwat is Khatwat and Khatwat and Khatwat and the plural of Khatwat with a fat-ha is Khatwat like Rukwat and Rukwat. Imru’ al-Qais said: She has leaps like the leaps of gazelles, a heart full of mistakes and a valley of rain. Abu Samal Al-Adawi and Ubaid bin Umair read Khatawat with a fatha on the kha and ta. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, Qatada, Al-A'raj, Amr bin Maymun and Al-A'mash Khatawat with a damma on the kha and ta and a hamza on the waw. Al-Akhfash said: They went with this reading to the effect that it is the plural of sin, from khata', not from khatwa. The meaning according to the reading of the majority is: Do not follow the traces of Satan and his work, and whatever the Shari'ah did not refer to is attributed to Satan. Ibn Abbas said: The steps of Satan are his works. Mujahid: His sins. Al-Suddi: His obedience. Abu Majlaz: They are vows to commit sins. I said: The correct wording is general in all innovations and sins except the Sunnahs and laws. The discussion of Satan has been presented in full. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: Indeed, Satan is to you a clear enemy. God the Almighty informed us that Satan is an enemy, and His report is true and honest. So, it is the duty of the wise person to take heed of this enemy who has made his enmity clear since the time of Adam, and has devoted himself and his life to corrupting the affairs of the children of Adam. God the Almighty has commanded us to beware of him, as He, the Most High, said: “And do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy. He only orders you to evil and immorality, and to say about God that which you do not know.” And He said: Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to immorality. And He said: Satan wants to lead them far astray. And He said: “Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?” And He said: “Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze.” This is the ultimate warning, and there are many examples of it in the Qur’an. Abdullah bin Omar said: Satan is chained in the lowest earth, and if he moves, then every evil on earth between two or more is due to his movement. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Abu Malik Al-Ash’ari, in which it says: “And I command you to remember God, for the example of that is like that of a man who is pursued by the enemy quickly until he reaches a strong fortress and protects himself from them. Likewise, the servant does not protect himself from Satan except by remembering God.” The hadith. And he said about it: A good, authentic, strange hadith.
2:169: God Almighty says: He only commands you to do evil and immorality and to say about God what you do not know. God the Almighty said: He only orders you to do evil and indecency. Evil is called evil because it makes its doer miserable with bad consequences. It is the source of sa’ahu which means it saddens him. Sa’atahu means it makes him sad, so he is sad. God the Almighty said: The faces of those who disbelieve will be made ugly. The poet said: If this life has made me sad, life has always made me happy. The matter is the same for me in both cases, for one, thanks and for the other, patience Obscenity is originally an ugly sight, as he said: Good as the gazelle's, not obscene Then the word was used in ugly meanings. The Sharia is what makes good and bad, so everything that the Sharia forbids is indecency. Muqatil said: Everything in the Qur’an that mentions indecency is adultery, except for His statement: Satan threatens you with poverty and orders you to indecency, which is the prohibition of zakat. I said: Based on this, it was said: Evil is that for which there is no limit, and obscenity is that for which there is a limit. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and others, and God Almighty knows best. The Almighty said: And that you say about God what you do not know. Al-Tabari said: He means what they forbade of the bahīrah and the sā’ibah and the like of what they made lawful. And that you say is in the accusative case in apposition to the Almighty’s saying: with evil and indecency.
2:170: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And when it is said to them meaning the Arab infidels. Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about the Jews. Al-Tabari: The pronoun in them refers to the people from the Almighty’s saying: O mankind, eat. And Qay: It refers to who in the Almighty’s saying: And among mankind are those who take others besides God the verse. And His saying: Follow what God has revealed meaning by accepting and acting. “They said: Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.” We found: we found. And the poet said: I found him not repenting or remembering God except a little. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Or if their fathers had been… The alif is for interrogation, and the waw is opened because it is a waw of conjunction, conjoining one sentence of speech to another, because the ultimate corruption in commitment is for them to say: We will follow our fathers even if they did not understand, so they decided on this commitment of theirs, since it was the state of their fathers. Question: Our scholars said: The strength of the words of this verse invalidates imitation, and its counterpart is: And when it is said to them, ‘Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger,’ they say, ‘Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers’ 1:10. This verse and the one before it are connected to what preceded them, and that is that God, the Exalted, informed us of the ignorance of the Arabs in what they controlled with their foolish opinions in the Bahira, Sa’ibah, and Wasila, so they argued that it was a matter they found their fathers doing and followed them in that, and they abandoned what God revealed to His Messenger and commanded in His religion, so the pronoun in them refers back to them in both verses. Third: Some people have relied on this verse to condemn imitation, because God Almighty condemned the infidels for following their fathers in falsehood and imitating them in disbelief and disobedience. This is correct in falsehood, but imitation in truth is a fundamental principle of the religion and a protection from the protection of Muslims to which the ignorant who is unable to comprehend the insight resorts. Scholars differed about its permissibility in matters of principles, as follows. As for its permissibility in matters of branches, it is correct. Fourth: The reality of imitation according to scholars is accepting a statement without proof. Based on this, whoever accepts the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, without looking into his miracle is an imitator, but whoever looks into it is not an imitator. It was said: It is believing in the validity of a fatwa of someone who does not know the validity of his statement. In the language, it is taken from the necklace of perfume, as the Arabs say: I tied the camel if you put a rope around its neck to lead it, so it is as if the imitator leaves his entire affair to whoever leads him wherever he wants. And their poet said likewise: And they entrusted you with your command, may God reward you, and may your soul be steadfast in the matter of war, and may you be fully aware of it. Fifth: Imitation is not a path to knowledge nor a means of reaching it, neither in the fundamentals nor in the branches. This is the opinion of the majority of rational people and scholars, contrary to what is said about the ignorant literalists and the Tha’labiyyah that it is a path to knowing the truth, and that this is what is obligatory, and that contemplation and research are forbidden, and that arguing against them in the books of fundamentals. Sixth: It is obligatory for the layman who is not busy deriving rulings from their origins due to his lack of qualification in matters of his religion that he does not know and needs to do so, to seek out the most knowledgeable of his time and country and ask him about his case and then comply with his fatwa, based on the statement of God the Almighty: So ask the people of knowledge if you do not know. He is required to strive to search for the most knowledgeable of his time until the majority of people agree on it. It is also obligatory for the scholar to imitate a scholar like him in a case in which the evidence and reasoning are unclear to him, and he wants to renew his thinking and reasoning until he finds what is required, but time is short for that, and he fears that the act of worship will be missed, or that the ruling will be lost, whether that other mujtahid is a companion or someone else. This is what Judge Abu Bakr and a group of scholars agreed with. Seventh: Ibn Atiyyah said: The nation has agreed to invalidate imitation in matters of belief. Others have mentioned a difference of opinion on this, such as Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi and Abu Amr Uthman ibn Isa ibn Darbas al-Shafi’i. Ibn Darbas said in his book Al-Intisar: Some people said that imitation is permissible in matters of monotheism, and this is a mistake, because God the Almighty said: Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion. So he condemned them for imitating their fathers and not following the Messengers, like the people of whims did in imitating their elders and not following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his religion. And because it is obligatory upon every accountable person to learn the matter of monotheism and to be certain of it, and this can only be achieved through the Book and the Sunnah, as we explained in the verse on monotheism, and God guides whom He wills. Ibn Darbas said: The people of deviation have often said that those who adhere to the Book and the Sunnah are imitators. This is a mistake on their part, rather it is more appropriate for them and more befitting for their schools of thought, since they accepted the words of their masters and elders in matters in which they contradicted the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger and the consensus of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. Thus, they were included among those whom God condemned in His saying: Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our elders until His saying: greatly, and His saying: Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion, and we are following in their footsteps. Then He said to His Prophet: He said, ‘Even if I brought you better guidance than that which you found your fathers upon,’ they said, ‘Indeed, we, in that with which you have been sent, are disbelievers.’ Then He said to His Prophet, peace be upon him: Then We took vengeance on them At-Tirmidhi. Thus, God, the Almighty, made clear that guidance is in what His Messengers, peace be upon them, brought. The saying of the people of the Sunnah in their beliefs: We found our imams, our fathers, and the people following the Book and the Sunnah and the consensus of the righteous predecessors of the nation, is not from their saying: We found our fathers and we obeyed our masters and elders in a way, because these attributed that to the revelation and to following the Messenger, and those attributed their slander to the people of falsehoods, and thus they increased in misguidance. Do you not see that God, the Exalted, praised Joseph, peace be upon him, in the Qur’an where He said: “Indeed, I have left the religion of a people who do not believe in God and are, in the Hereafter, disbelievers. * And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It was not for us to associate anything with God. That was from the favor of God upon us and upon mankind.” So since his fathers, peace be upon them, were prophets who followed the revelation, which is the pure religion that God was pleased with, his following his fathers was one of the attributes of praise. What they came up with did not mention symptoms and their connection to substances and their transformation into them, which indicates that there is no guidance in them and no right path in their creators. Ibn Al-Hisar said: The use of these terms appeared in the time of Al-Ma'mun after the two hundredth year, when the books of the ancients were translated and their differences appeared in them regarding the eternity and occurrence of the world, and their differences regarding the essence and its stability, and the accident and its nature. So the innovators and those in whose hearts there was deviation hastened to preserve those terms, and they intended by them to alienate the people of the Sunnah, and to introduce doubts among the weak among the people of the religion. So the matter remained like this until innovation appeared, and the innovators became sects, and the matter became confused for the sultan, until the prince said that the Qur’an was created, and forced people to do so, and struck Ahmad ibn Hanbal for that. Then men from the Sunnis, such as Sheikh Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, Abdullah ibn Kulab, Ibn Mujahid, al-Muhasibi and their likes, were appointed. They engaged with the innovators in their terminology, then they fought them and killed them with their weapons. And those Muslims who came of age from this nation held fast to the Book and the Sunnah, turning away from the doubts of the atheists. They did not consider the essence and the accident. That was the way the predecessors were. I said: Whoever now looks into the terminology of the theologians when he argues with that for the religion, his status is close to that of the prophets. As for those extremist theologians who criticize the path of those believers who took the narration, and urge the study of the books of theology, and that the truth is not known except from their side with those terminologies, then they have become blameworthy for their rejection of the path of the predecessors from the past imams, and God knows best. As for the dispute and argument with evidence and proof, that is clear in the Qur’an, and its explanation will come, God willing.
2:171: God the Almighty likened the preacher and caller of the infidels, who is Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, to a shepherd who calls out to the sheep and camels, but they hear nothing but his call and cry, and do not understand what he says. This is how Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, As-Suddi, Az-Zajjaj, Al-Farraa and Sibawayh explained it, and this is the ultimate in brevity. Sibawayh said: They did not liken it to the one calling out, but rather to the one being called out to. The meaning is: And your example, O Muhammad, and the example of those who disbelieved is like the one calling out and the one being called out to, from among the animals that do not understand. So the word was omitted to indicate the meaning. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is that the example of those who disbelieved in their supplication to inanimate deities is like that of a caller in the dead of night who is answered by an echo. He calls out to something that cannot be heard, and what answers him is that which has no truth or benefit. Qatrib said: The meaning is that the example of those who disbelieved in their supplication to something that cannot be understood, meaning the idols, is like that of a shepherd who calls to his sheep and does not know where they are. Al-Tabari said: What is meant is that the example of the disbelievers in their supplication to their deities is like that of someone who calls to something far away and is not heard because of the distance. So the caller has nothing of that except the call that tires him and exhausts him. In these three interpretations, the disbelievers are likened to the caller who calls, and the deaf to the one who is being called. Calling is driving the sheep and shouting at them. It is said: The shepherd called to his sheep, calling, and shouting, and shouting at them. Al-Akhtal said: Go to your sheep, Jarir, for you have only lost your way in the wilderness. Al-Qatabi said: Jarir was not a shepherd, but he meant that the Banu Kulayb were mocked for herding sheep, and Jarir was one of them, so he was as ignorant as them. The Arabs use the example of a shepherd in terms of ignorance and say: More ignorant than a shepherd. Al-Qatabi said: Whoever adopted this meaning of the verse was following a school of thought, but none of the scholars adopted it as far as we know. The call is for those far away, and the supplication is for those near. That is why the call to prayer is called a call for those far away. The letter nun may be included in the call, but the original is the kasra. Then the Almighty likened the disbelievers to being deaf, dumb, and blind. This was mentioned at the beginning of the surah.
2:172: God Almighty says: O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided for you and be grateful to God if it is Him that you worship. This is an emphasis on the first matter, and the believers were mentioned specifically here as a preference. What is meant by eating is benefiting from all aspects. It was said: It is the usual food. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, God is good and does not accept anything but good. God commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, saying: ‘O messengers, eat from the good foods and work righteousness. Indeed, I, of what you do, am Knowing.’ And He said: ‘O you who have believed, eat from the good things We have provided for you.’ Then he mentioned the man who travels a long way, disheveled and dusty, stretching his hands to the sky, ‘O Lord, O Lord,’ while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with unlawful things. So how can that be answered?” And be grateful to God if it is Him that you worship. The meaning of gratitude has been presented, so there is no point in repeating it.
2:173: God Almighty says: “He has only forbidden you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limits], there is no sin upon him. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” It contains thirty-four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: He has only forbidden you dead animals. The word only is used for restriction, and includes negation and affirmation, so it confirms what the speech includes and negates what is other than it. Here, the prohibition is restricted, especially since it came after the permission in the Almighty’s saying: O you who believe, eat from the good things which We have provided for you. So it indicates permissibility in general. Then He followed it by mentioning the forbidden with the word only which restricts, so this necessitated the inclusion of the two parts, so there is no forbidden thing outside this verse, and it is Medinan. And it was confirmed by the other verse which was narrated to have been revealed in Arafat: “Say, ‘I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it. ’” to the end of it, so the explanation was completed first and last, as Ibn al-Arabi said. And we will discuss that in Al-An’am, God willing. The second: the dead is in the accusative case with haram and ma is a comprehensive word. It is permissible to make it mean who, separate in writing, and raise the dead, blood, and pork flesh as the predicate of in, which is the reading of Ibn Abi Ubla. In haram there is a pronoun referring back to who, and similar to it is the saying of God the Almighty: They only made a magician's trick. Abu Ja'far read haram with a damma on the ha' and a kasra on the ra' and raised the nouns after it, either as a subject whose agent is not named, or as a predicate of in. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa' also read the dead with a shaddah. At-Tabari said: A group of linguists said: The shaddah and the lightening in mayt and mayt are two dialects. Abu Hatim and others said: What has died is said in it, and what has not died yet is not said in it with a lightening, its evidence is the saying of God the Almighty: Indeed, you will die and indeed, they will die. The poet said: Not everyone who dies and finds rest is dead, but the dead are the dead of the living. No one read with a light pronunciation of ma lam yamta except what Al-Bazzi narrated on the authority of Ibn Kathir: And he is not dead. The well-known reading from him is the heavy pronunciation. As for the poet’s saying: If a Tamim man dies and you want him to live, bring provisions. There is nothing more eloquent in satire than that he meant the dead person in reality, and some people have said that he meant someone who is close to death, and the first is more famous. Third: Dead: That which has lost its soul without being slaughtered, and that which is not edible, its slaughter is like its death, such as wild animals and others, as will be explained here and in the livestock, God willing. Fourth: This verse is general, but it was made specific by the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: “Two dead animals have been made lawful for us: fish and locusts, and the blood of the liver and spleen.” Narrated by Al-Daraqutni. Likewise, the hadith of Jabir about ambergris specifies the generality of the Qur’an with the authenticity of its chain of transmission. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, along with the words of God Almighty: Lawful for you is game from the sea, as will be explained there, God willing. Most scholars permit eating all sea creatures, alive or dead. This is the Maliki school of thought. He hesitated to answer about the capybara and said: You say a pig! Ibn al-Qasim said: I avoid it and do not see it as forbidden. Fifth: People have differed about specifying the Book of God Almighty with the Sunnah, and despite their differences in that, they have agreed that it is not permissible to specify it with a weak hadith, as Ibn al-Arabi said. Evidence for specifying this verse may also be found in what is in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, who said: We fought with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) in seven battles, just as we ate locusts with him. It appears that it is permissible to eat it, whether it dies by treatment or by natural death. This is what Ibn Nafi', Ibn Abd al-Hakam and most scholars said, and it is the view of al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa and others. Malik and the majority of his companions forbade eating it if it dies by natural death, because it is land game. Don't you see that it is sufficient for a person in ihram to kill it, so it is similar to a gazelle? Ashhab said: If it dies from a severed leg or wing, it is not eaten, because it is a condition in which it may live and reproduce. The ruling on locusts will be further explained in Al-A'raf when it is mentioned, God willing. Sixth: The scholars differed as to whether it is permissible to benefit from a dead animal or from any impurity. They differed from Malik on this as well. He said once: It is permissible to benefit from it, because “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by a blessed sheep and said: Why did you not take its hide?” And he said once: Its entirety is forbidden, so it is not permissible to benefit from any of it, or any of the impurities in any way, so it is permissible to water crops or animals with impure water, or feed animals impurities, or feed dead animals to dogs and wild beasts. Even if they eat them, they are not prevented. The basis for this statement is the apparent meaning of the statement of God the Almighty: Forbidden to you are dead animals and blood, and He did not specify one aspect from another. It is not permissible to say: This address is general, because generality is that which is not understood from its apparent meaning. The Arabs understood the meaning of the statement of God the Almighty: Forbidden to you are dead animals, and also the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not benefit from anything that is dead. In the hadith of Abdullah bin Ukaim. Do not benefit from the skin or sinews of a dead animal. This is the last thing he wrote a month before his death. This report and discussion of it will come in An-Nahl, God willing. Seventh: As for a female camel, or a cow or a sheep, if it is slaughtered, and there is a dead fetus in its belly, it is permissible to eat it without slaughtering it in itself, unless it comes out alive, in which case it is slaughtered, and it has the same ruling as itself. This is because if the fetus comes out of it after slaughtering dead, it is treated like one of its organs. What makes this clear is that if he sells a sheep and excludes what is in its belly, it is not permissible, just as if he excludes a part of it, and what is in its belly is part of it like the rest of its organs. Likewise, if he frees it without signing the initial freeing of what is in its belly, even if it is separate from it, it does not follow it in the sale or freeing. Jabir, may God be pleased with him, narrated: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a cow or a sheep being slaughtered, or a she-camel being slaughtered, and there being a dead fetus in its belly. He said: If you wish, eat it, because its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother.” Abu Dawud narrated it with its meaning from the hadith of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, and it is an explicit text that is not to be accepted. Further explanation of this will come in Surat Al-Ma’idah, God willing. Eighth: There is a difference of opinion regarding the narration of Malik regarding the skin of a dead animal, whether it is purified by tanning or not. It was narrated from him that it is not purified, and this is the apparent opinion of the school of thought. It was narrated from him that it is purified, based on his saying, peace be upon him: Any hide that is tanned is pure. The reason for his statement that it is not pure is that it is a part of a dead animal that if it were taken from it while it was alive it would be impure, so the tanner must not purify it by analogy with meat. The reports about purity are understood to mean that the tanner removes dirt from the hide so that it can be used for dry things and for sitting on it. It is also permissible to use it in water by giving it to drink, because water is originally pure unless its description changes, as will come from its ruling in Surat al-Furqan 25:Purity in the language refers to removing dirt, just as it refers to legal purity, and God knows best.
