Ninth: As for the hair and wool of a dead animal, it is pure, based on what was narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There is nothing wrong with touching a dead animal if it has been tanned, or its wool and hair if it has been washed. Because it was pure for him when it was taken from it while it was alive, it must be so after death. However, since the meat was impure when it was alive, it is so after death, so the wool must be the opposite when it is dead, just as it was the opposite when it was alive, based on the opposite evidence. This does not necessarily mean milk or eggs from a dead chicken, because milk is pure after death according to us, and so is the egg. However, they were taken from an impure container, so they became impure because of their proximity to the container, not because they became impure because of their death. Further clarification of this issue and the one before it, and the scholars’ differences of opinion on them, will come in Surat An-Nahl, God willing. Tenth: As for that into which a mouse has fallen, it has two states: A state in which if the mouse is brought out alive, it is pure. And if it dies in it, it has two states: A state in which it is liquid, in which case all of it becomes impure. And a state in which it is solid, in which case it makes impure whatever is next to it, so it is thrown away along with whatever is around it, and what remains is used while it is pure, based on what was narrated: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a mouse that fell into ghee and died. He, peace be upon him, said: If it is solid, throw it and what is around it away, and if it is liquid, pour it out.” The scholars differed about whether it is washed. It was said: It is not purified by washing, because it is an impure liquid, so it is similar to blood, wine, urine, and other impurities. Ibn al-Qasim said: It is purified by washing, because it is a body that has become impure due to being in contact with impurities, so it is similar to clothing. This does not apply to blood, because it is impure in and of itself, nor to wine and urine, because washing consumes them and is not possible for them.” Eleventh: If we rule that it is pure by washing, it returns to its original state in terms of purity and all other aspects of benefit, but it should not be sold until it is made clear, because that is a defect in people’s minds that their souls reject. Some of them believe that it is forbidden and that it is unclean, so it is not permissible to sell it until the defect is made clear, like all other defective things. As for before washing, it is not permissible to sell it under any circumstances, because impurities, in their view, are not permissible to sell, and because it is an impure liquid, so it is similar to wine. And because “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the price of wine, so he said: God cursed the Jews. Fat was forbidden to them, so they rendered it, sold it, and ate its price.” And when God forbids something, He forbids its price. This liquid is forbidden because of its impurity, so its price must be forbidden by the apparent ruling. Twelfth: There is a difference of opinion if an animal, bird or other falls into the pot and dies. Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Malik that he said: What is in the pot may not be eaten, as it has become impure due to the dead animal mixing with it. Ibn al-Qasim narrated on his authority that he said: The meat should be washed and the broth poured out. Ibn Abbas was asked about this issue and he said: The meat should be washed and eaten. None of his companions disagreed with him regarding the broth, as mentioned by Ibn Khuwayz Mandad. Thirteenth: As for the rennet of a dead animal and the milk of a dead animal, Al-Shafi’i said: This is impure due to the generality of the Almighty’s statement: Forbidden to you are dead animals. Abu Hanifa said that they are pure, and he did not make the place of creation have any effect on the impurity of what is adjacent to it from what was created in it. He said: Therefore, meat is eaten with the veins in it, while it is certain that blood is adjacent to its interior without purification or washing by consensus. Malik said something similar to what Abu Hanifa said, that this does not become impure due to death, but it becomes impure due to being adjacent to an impure vessel, which is something that cannot be washed. Likewise, an egg comes out of a chicken after its death, because the egg is soft and is considered a liquid before it comes out, and it only solidifies and hardens in the air. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: If it is said: Your statement leads to a contradiction to the consensus, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims after him used to eat cheese that was brought to them from the land of the Persians, and it is known that the slaughtered animals of the Persians, who are Magians, were dead, and they did not consider it frozen with the rennet of a dead animal or a slaughtered animal. It was said to him: The amount of rennet that falls into the curdled milk is small, and a small amount of impurity is excused if it is mixed with a large amount of liquid. This is an answer to one of the two narrations. According to the other narration, this was only in the beginning of Islam, and no one can say that the Companions ate cheese brought from the land of the Persians, rather, cheese is not part of the food of the Arabs. When the Muslims spread throughout the land of the Persians through conquests, the slaughtered animals became theirs, so how do we know that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Companions ate cheese, let alone it being brought from the land and made from the rennet of their slaughtered animals? Abu Omar said: There is nothing wrong with eating the food of idolaters, Magians, and all the infidels who do not have a book, as long as it is not from their slaughtering and does not require slaughtering, except for cheese, which does not contain rennet from a dead animal. In Sunan Ibn Majah, cheese and ghee: Ismail bin Musa al-Suddi told us, Saif bin Harun told us, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, on the authority of Salman al-Farsi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about ghee, cheese, and fur. He said: What is permissible is what God has permitted in His Book, and what is forbidden is what God has forbidden in His Book, and whatever He is silent about is something He has pardoned. Fourteenth: The Almighty said: and blood. The scholars agreed that blood is forbidden and impure and is not to be eaten or benefited from. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: As for blood, it is forbidden as long as it is not a widespread disease, and what is a widespread disease is excused. What is a widespread disease is blood in the flesh and its veins, and a small amount of it in the body and clothing in which one prays. We only said that because God the Almighty said: He has forbidden you dead animals and blood, and He said in another place: Say, ‘I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be dead animals or blood poured forth.’ So spilled blood is forbidden. Aisha may God be pleased with her narrated: “We used to cook a pot during the time of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and the yellowish color of blood would rise to the top of it, so we would eat it and not disapprove of it,” because avoiding this is a burden and hardship, and burden and hardship in religion are invalid. This is a principle in the Sharia, that whenever the nation is in difficulty in performing the act of worship and it becomes difficult for it, the act of worship is dropped from it. Do you not see that the one in need eats carrion, and the sick person breaks the fast and performs dry ablution in such cases? I said: God the Almighty mentioned blood here in an absolute sense, and restricted it to livestock by saying poured out. The scholars here have unanimously interpreted the absolute to mean the restricted. So blood here means spilled, because whatever is mixed with meat is not forbidden by consensus, and the same is the case with the liver and spleen, which are agreed upon. There is a difference of opinion regarding the blood of the whale that has been released. It was narrated from Al-Qabisi that it is pure, and its purity necessitates that it is not forbidden. This is the choice of Ibn Al-Arabi, who said: Because if the blood of fish was impure, its slaughter would have been permissible. I said: This is the doctrine of Abu Hanifa regarding whale blood. I heard some Hanafis say: The evidence that it is pure is that when it dries it turns white, unlike other bloods which turn black. This is their point in their argument against the Shafi’is. Fifteenth: The Almighty’s saying: And the flesh of swine. God Almighty specifically mentioned the flesh of the pig to indicate the prohibition of its meat, whether it was slaughtered or not, and to include fat and other cartilage and other things there. Sixteenth: The Ummah has unanimously agreed that pork fat is forbidden. Malik and his companions have provided evidence that whoever swears not to eat fat and eats meat has not broken his oath by eating meat. If he swears not to eat meat and eats fat, he has broken his oath, because meat and fat are called meat, so fat is included in the name of meat, but meat is not included in the name of fat. God has forbidden pork, so mentioning its meat instead of its fat, because it is included under the name of meat. God has forbidden fat to the Children of Israel by saying: We have forbidden them their fat, so the prohibition of meat did not apply to them and it was not included under the name of fat. For this reason, Malik distinguished between the one who swears by fat and the one who swears by meat, unless the one who swears has the intention of meat but not fat, in which case he does not break his oath. And God knows best. He does not break his oath according to the opinion of Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr and the people of opinion, if he swears not to eat meat and eats fat. Ahmad said: If he swears not to eat meat and eats fat, there is nothing wrong with it, unless he intended to avoid fat. Seventeenth: There is no disagreement that all pigs are forbidden, except for hair, which is permissible to use for sewing. It has been narrated: “A man asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about sewing with pig hair, and he said: There is nothing wrong with that.” This was mentioned by Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad, who said: Because sewing was done during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and was present and apparent after him, we do not know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disapproved of it, nor did any of the imams after him. And what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted is like an innovation in the Shari’ah. Eighteenth: There is no disagreement about the prohibition of wild pigs, as we mentioned, but there is disagreement about aquatic pigs. Malik refused to answer anything about it, and said: You say pigs! It has been mentioned before, and its explanation will come in Al-Ma’idah, God willing. Nineteenth: Most linguists have said that the word pig is a quadriliteral word. Ibn Sidah narrated from some of them that it is derived from khazra al-‘ayn to look in the eye, because it is like that, and the word is triliteral. In Al-Sahah: A man takhazar means to narrow his eyelid to sharpen his gaze. Khazra means to narrow and make the eye small. A man is akharaz a narrow eye. It is said that it is when a person looks from the back of it. The plural of pig is khazayr. “Khazayr” is also a well-known disease, which is hard sores that occur on the neck. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth: The Almighty’s saying: And that which is dedicated to other than God meaning that a name other than God’s was mentioned over it, and it is the sacrifice of the Zoroastrian, the pagan, and the one who denies anything. The pagan slaughters for an idol, the Zoroastrian for fire, and the one who denies anything does not believe in anything, so he slaughters for himself. There is no disagreement among the scholars that what the Zoroastrian slaughters for his fire and the pagan for his idol is not eaten, and their slaughter is not eaten according to Malik, Al-Shafi’i, and others, even if they did not slaughter for his fire and idol. Ibn Al-Musayyab and Abu Thawr permitted it if it was slaughtered for a Muslim by his order. This will be further explained, God willing, in Surah Al-Ma’idah. Ihlil means raising the voice. It is said: He declared something, meaning he raised his voice. Ibn Ahmar said, describing a desert: Its riders arrive at Al-Farqad as a pilgrim arrives for Umrah Al-Nabigha said: Or a pearl shell, its diver is delighted, whenever he sees it he bows down and prostrates himself And from it is the boy’s ihram and his ihram, which is his cry at birth. Ibn Abbas and others said: What is meant is what was slaughtered for idols and statues, not what the name of the Messiah was mentioned over, as will be explained in Surat Al-Ma’idah, God willing. The Arabs used to cry out in the name of the intended sacrifice, and this was prevalent in their usage until it was used to express the intention that is forbidden. Do you not see that Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, took into consideration the intention in the camels that Ghalib Abu Al-Farazdaq slaughtered and said: They are among those that were dedicated to other than God, so the people left them. Ibn Atiyyah said: I saw in the report of Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan that he was asked about a luxurious woman who made a wedding for her toys and slaughtered a camel, so Al-Hasan said: It is not permissible to eat it because it was slaughtered for an idol. I said: And from this meaning is what we narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Yahya al-Tamimi, a Muslim sheikh, who said: Jarir told us on the authority of Qabus, who said: My father sent a woman to Aisha may God be pleased with her and ordered her to convey his greetings to her and to ask her which prayer the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) liked the most and which he would perform regularly. She said: He used to pray four rak'ahs before noon, standing for a long time and bowing and prostrating well. As for what he never neglected, whether healthy or sick or present, two rak'ahs before the dawn prayer. At that time, a woman from among the people said: O Commander of the Faithful, we have some Persian relatives who always have a festival and they give us gifts from it. Can we eat some of it? She said: As for what was slaughtered for that day, do not eat it, but eat from their trees. Twenty-first: The Almighty’s saying: So whoever is forced It was read with a damma on the noon for the sake of conformity and with a kasra, which is the original because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and it contains an implication, meaning whoever is forced to do one of these forbidden things, meaning he is in need of it, so it is an ifta’ala from necessity. Ibn Muhaisin read So whoever is forced with the assimilation of the dad into the ta’. Abu al-Samal read So whoever is forced with a kasra on the ta’. Its original form is Idtarara but when it was assimilated, the vowel of the ra’ was transferred to the ta’. Twenty-second: Compulsion is either due to coercion from an oppressor or hunger in a state of famine. What the majority of jurists and scholars agree on regarding the meaning of the verse is that it is due to poverty and hunger, which is hunger for that, and this is correct. It was said: Its meaning is that he was forced and overwhelmed to eat these forbidden things. Mujahid said: He means he was forced to do it, like a man who is captured by the enemy and forced to eat pork and other acts of disobedience to God Almighty, except that compulsion permits that, and so on.
2:174: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who conceal what God has revealed of the Book meaning the Jewish scholars, concealed what God revealed in the Torah about the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the authenticity of his message. The meaning of revealed is made manifest, as God the Almighty said: And whoever says, I will send down the like of what God has revealed" meaning I will make manifest. It was said: It is in its category of revelation, meaning what His angels sent down to His messengers. "And they exchange it meaning the concealed thing for a small price" meaning taking a bribe. He called it "little" because its duration was short and its consequences were bad. It was said: Because what they used to take as bribes was little. I said: Even though this verse is in the report, it includes those Muslims who conceal the truth by choice because of worldly gain, and this meaning has been presented. God the Almighty says: In their bellies. Mentioning bellies is an indication and confirmation of the reality of eating, as it may be used metaphorically in the example of someone eating something from the earth and the like. Mentioning bellies also draws attention to their greed and that they sold their afterlife for their share of food that has no value. The meaning of except the Fire is that it is forbidden and God will punish them for it with the Fire. So what they ate of bribes was called Fire because it leads them to the Fire, as most of the commentators said. It was said: That is, He punishes them for their concealment by eating the Fire in Hell in reality. So He informed about the outcome in the state, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly are only consuming fire into their bellies. That is, the outcome leads to that, and from this is their saying: They were born for death and built for destruction He said: Death is what the mother gives birth to last: Our role is to build the ruins of time It is found in the Qur’an and poetry a lot. God the Almighty says: And God will not speak to them means He is angry with them and does not accept their pleasure. It is said: So-and-so does not speak to so-and-so if he is angry with him. At-Tabari said: The meaning of and God will not speak to them is what they like. In the Qur’an: Be gone therein, and do not speak to them. It was said: The meaning is He will not send angels to greet them. And He will not purify them means He will not correct their evil deeds and cleanse them. Al-Zajjaj said: He will not praise them well nor call them pure. Painful means painful, and this has been mentioned before. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three whom God will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, nor will He look at them, and they will have a painful punishment: an old adulterer, a lying king, and an arrogant beggar.” These people were singled out for the painful punishment and severe penalty because of the sheer stubbornness and contempt that drove them to commit those sins, as no need drove them to do so, nor did a necessity call them to it as one who was not like them would. The meaning of will not look at them is that He will not have mercy on them or be kind to them. This will come in Al Imran, God willing.
2:175: God Almighty says: “Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance and punishment in exchange for forgiveness. How patient they are in the Fire.” The Almighty says: Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance and punishment in exchange for forgiveness. This has been discussed previously. Since punishment is subordinate to error and forgiveness is subordinate to the guidance that they have rejected, this is included in the permissibility of the purchase. God the Almighty said: How patient they are with the Fire! The opinion of the majority - including Al-Hasan and Mujahid - is that what means astonishment, and it is attributed to the creatures, as if he said: Be amazed at their patience with the Fire and their stay in it. In the revelation: How ungrateful is man! and He hears them and sees them. Abu Ali began with this meaning: Al-Hasan, Qatada, Ibn Jubayr and Al-Rabi' said: By God, they have no patience with it, but how bold they are with the Fire! This is a well-known Yemeni dialect. Al-Farra' said: Al-Kisa'i told me: The judge of Yemen told me that two opponents brought their case before him, and one of them was required to swear an oath, so he swore, and his companion said to him: How patient you are with God? That is, how bold you are with it. The meaning is: How courageous they are with the Fire when they do work that leads to it. Al-Zajjaj narrated that the meaning is: How long they remain in the Fire, from their saying: How patient so-and-so is with imprisonment! That is, how long he remains in it. It was said: The meaning is: How little their anxiety about the Fire, so little anxiety was made patience. Al-Kisa’i and Qatrib said: What made them persist in doing the deeds of the people of Hell? It was also said: What is an interrogative meaning a rebuke, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Al-Suddi, Ata’, and Abu Ubaidah Muammar ibn Al-Muthanna. Its meaning is: What made them endure the deeds of the people of Hell?! It was also said: This is to belittle them and make light of their matter.
2:176: God Almighty says: That is because God has sent down the Book in truth, and indeed those who differ over the Book are in extreme dissension. God the Almighty said: That That is in the nominative case, and it is an indication of the ruling, as if he said: That ruling is with the Fire. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that matter, or that order, or that punishment for them. Al-Akhfash said: The predicate of that is implied, meaning that is known to them. It was said: Its position is accusative, meaning we did that to them. Because God sent down the Book meaning the Qur’an in this place with the truth meaning with honesty. It was said: with proof. And those who differed over the Book meaning the Torah, so the Christians claimed that it contained the description of Jesus, and the Jews denied his description. It was said: They differed from their fathers and predecessors in adhering to it. It was said: They differed from what was in the Torah about the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and differed over it. It was said: What is meant is the Qur’an, and those who differed are the infidels of Quraysh, some of them say: It is magic, and some of them say: Legends of the ancients, and some of them: It is fabricated, and so on. The meaning of discord has been discussed previously, and praise be to God.
2:177: It contains eight issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: Righteousness is not. There is a difference of opinion about what is meant by this address. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that a man asked the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about righteousness, so God revealed this verse. He said: Before the obligatory duties, if a man testified that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and then died upon that, Paradise was obligatory for him, so God revealed this verse. Al-Rabi’ and Qatada also said: The address is to the Jews and Christians because they differed in direction and orientation. The Jews are towards the west before Jerusalem, and the Christians are towards the east, where the sun rises. They spoke about changing the direction of prayer and each group preferred its orientation, so it was said to them: Righteousness is not what you are in, but righteousness is the one who believes in God. Second: Hamzah and Hafs read al-barr in the accusative case, because laysa is one of the sisters of kana kan, after which two definite nouns come, so you make whichever one you want the noun or predicate. When al-barr came after laysa, he made it the accusative case, and made an tawala the noun. The verbal noun kan is more definite because it cannot be indefinite, and al-barr can be indefinite, but the verb is stronger in definiteness. The rest read al-barr in the nominative case, as the noun of laysa, and its predicate is an tawala, meaning: Al-barr is not your turning your faces away, and according to the first, Al-barr is not your turning your faces away, as in His statement, Their only argument was that they said, “Then the worst was the outcome of those who did evil, because they denied,” So their outcome was that they were both in the Fire, and what is similar to it. What strengthens the nominative reading is that the second is accompanied by the preposition ba, unanimously in His statement, And it is not righteousness that you enter houses from their backs, and nothing is permissible in it except the nominative case, so applying the first to the second is more definite than contradicting it. And it is also in the Mushaf of Abi with the letter Baa. Al-Birr is not that you turn away, and it is also in the Mushaf of Ibn Masoud, and most of the reciters agree with it, and both readings are good. Third: The Almighty’s saying: But righteousness is of him who believes in God. Righteousness here is a comprehensive name for goodness, and the meaning is: But righteousness is of him who believes, so the complement was omitted, like the Almighty’s saying: And ask the town, “And they made the calf drink into their hearts,” as Al-Farra’, Qatrub, and Al-Zajjaj said. And the poet said: It is only an advance and a retreat That is, she has a good appetite and is well-mannered. Al-Nabigha said: How do you communicate with someone who has become like Abu Marhab? That is, like his intercession with Abi Marhab, so he deleted it. It was said: The meaning is, but of righteousness, like the Almighty’s saying: They are of degrees with God meaning of degrees. That is because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina and the obligatory duties were imposed and the Qiblah was turned towards the Kaaba and the boundaries were defined, God revealed this verse and said: Not all righteousness is that you pray and do not do other than that, but righteousness - meaning righteousness - is he who believes in God, to the end of it, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Ata’, and Sufyano Az-Zajjaj also said. It is possible for righteousness to mean righteous and righteousness, and the agent may be called in the sense of the source, as it is said: a just man, and fasting and breaking the fast. In the revelation: If your water were to become sunken meaning sunken, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaidah. Al-Mubarrad said: If I were one of those who read the Qur’an, I would have read but of righteousness with the opening of the ba’. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made it, and the patient. It was said: The patient is in apposition to who because who is in the plural and nominative case, as if he said: But righteous are the believers and those who fulfill, as Al-Farra’ and Al-Akhfash said. And the patient is in the accusative case for praise, or by implying a verb. The Arabs put the accusative case for praise and blame as if they want to isolate the praised and blamed, and they do not follow it with the beginning of the speech, and put it in the accusative case. As for the praise, his saying: And those who establish prayer. Al-Kisa’i recited: Every nation obeyed the command of their guide except Namir, who obeyed the command of her seducer. The departing ones, and they have not yet departed, and those who say, Whose house shall we abandon? Abu Ubaidah recited: They do not distance my people who are the poison of the enemy and the scourge of the islands Those who enter every arena and are good at the knots of the blue Another said: We are the sons of Dhuba, the owners of the camels So it is used for praise. As for blame, it is the Almighty’s saying: Cursed wherever they are found verse. And Urwah ibn al-Ward said: They gave me wine to drink, then they surrounded me with the enemies of God, with lies and sin. This is acceptable in the adjectives, there is no objection to it in terms of grammar, it is found in the speech of the Arabs as we have explained. Some of those who were arbitrary in their speech said: This is a mistake of the writers when they wrote the Imam’s Mushaf. He said: The evidence for that is what was narrated from Uthman that he looked in the Mushaf and said: I see a mistake in it and the Arabs will correct it with their tongues. And he said the same in Surat An-Nisa and those who establish prayer, and in Surat al-Ma’idah 5:and the Sabians. The answer is what we mentioned. It was said: Al-Muwaffieen is raised as the subject and the predicate is omitted, its meaning is they are the Muwaffieen. Al-Kisa’i said: And the patient ones are in apposition to the relatives as if he said: And He gave to the patient ones. Al-Nahhas said: This statement is a mistake and a clear error, because if you put the patient ones in the accusative and coordinate it with the relatives, it enters into the connection of man and if you raise the patient ones as if it is coordinated with man, then you coordinate it with man before the connection is complete, and you separate the connection and the relative with the conjoined. Al-Kisa’i said: In the reading of Abdullah: Al-Muwaffieen and the patient ones. Al-Nahhas said: They can be arranged according to kinship or praise. Al-Farraa said: In Abdullah’s reading in An-Nisaa’: And those who establish prayer and give zakat. Ya’qub and Al-A’mash read Al-Muwaffoon and Al-Sabirun in the nominative case in both of them. Al-Jahdary read Bi’uhudhum. It has been said: Indeed, and Al-Muwaffoon are in apposition to the pronoun in “Aman, but Abu Ali denied it and said: The meaning is not according to it, since what is meant is not that righteousness is the righteousness of the one who believes in God, he and Al-Muwaffoon, meaning we both believed. Just as you say: The brave is the one who is oldest, he and Amr. Rather, what comes after his saying whoever believes is an enumeration of the actions of the one who believes and their descriptions. Fifth: Our scholars said: This is a great verse from the mothers of rulings, because it includes sixteen principles: belief in God and His names and attributes - and we have mentioned them in the Most Sublime Book - and the Resurrection and Gathering and the Balance and the Bridge and the Pool and intercession and Paradise and Hell - and we have mentioned them in the Book of Remembrance - and the angels and the revealed books and that they are a truth from God - as mentioned above - and the prophets and spending money on what is required of what is obligatory and recommended and maintaining kinship and not severing ties with them and looking after the orphan and not neglecting him and the poor as well, and taking care of the wayfarer - it was said the one who is stranded with him, and it was said: the guest - and begging and freeing slaves. This will be explained in the verse on charity, and maintaining prayer and paying zakat and fulfilling covenants and patience in hardships. Each of these principles requires a book. We have mentioned most of them above, and the rest of them will be explained including them in their places, God willing. There is a difference of opinion as to whether an orphan should be given voluntary charity as soon as he becomes an orphan, as a form of kinship, even if he is rich, or whether he should not be given charity until he becomes poor. There are two opinions of scholars. This is on the condition that the money is given other than the obligatory zakat, as we will explain above. Sixth: The Almighty’s statement: And he gives his wealth, in spite of his love for it. It was used as evidence by those who said that there is a right in wealth other than zakat, and that it is the perfection of righteousness. It was said that what is meant is the obligatory zakat, and the first is more correct, because of what was reported by Al-Daraqutni: “On the authority of Fatima bint Qays, she said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is a right in wealth other than zakat. Then he recited this verse: “Righteousness is not that you turn your faces” to the end of the verse. Ibn Majah included it in his Sunan and al-Tirmidhi included it in his Jami’ and said: This hadith has a weak chain of transmission. Abu Hamza Maymun al-A’war is considered weak. Bayan and Ismail ibn Salim narrated this hadith on the authority of al-Sha’bi, and it is more authentic. I said: Even though there is some criticism of the hadith, its authenticity is indicated by the meaning of the verse itself, where God the Almighty says: And establishes prayer and gives zakat. Zakat is mentioned along with prayer, and this is evidence that what is meant by His saying: And gives wealth, in spite of love for it, is not the obligatory zakat, because that would have been a repetition, and God knows best. The scholars agreed that if a need befalls the Muslims after paying zakat, then the money must be spent on it. Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: People must ransom their prisoners, even if that takes up all their money. This is also a consensus, and it strengthens what we have chosen, and God is the Grantor of success. Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: For His love. The pronoun in For His love has been disputed as to whether it refers back. Some say: It refers back to the giver of the money, and the object, which is the money, has been omitted. It is permissible to put relatives in the accusative case with love, so the meaning would be for the love of the giver of relatives. It has also been said: It refers back to the money, so the source would be added to the object. Ibn Atiyyah said: His statement for His love comes as a powerful objection during the statement. I said: Its counterpart is the statement of the Truth: And they give food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, for it combines the two meanings, the objection and the addition of the source to the object, i.e., in spite of the love of the food. And from the objection is the statement of the Truth: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer - those are the ones who have attained the goal. This is called completion, and it is a type of eloquence, and it is also called caution and precaution, so it was completed by His statement: in spite of their love for it and His statement: and he is a believer, and from it is the statement of Zuhair: Whoever meets an old man with all his faults one day will find generosity and kindness in him Imru Al-Qais said: On the structure, he gives you before asking him any of the ways of running, other than Kz and Wan His saying: With his faults and before his question is a good completion, and from it is the saying of Antarah: Praise me for what you know, for it is easy to disobey me if I am not wronged. His saying, If I am not wronged, is a good completion. Tarafa said: May the spring rain water your home, not spoiling it, and may it always flow. Al-Rabi’ bin Daba’ Al-Fazari said: I am finished, but my work and my speech will not be finished, and every person except his speech will perish. His saying: It does not spoil it, otherwise his hadiths are a completion and precaution. Abu Hafan said: Death has consumed our souls without being unjust, and generosity has consumed our wealth without being blameworthy. His saying not unjust and not absent is a completion and precaution, and it is found frequently in poetry. It was said: It refers to giving, because the verb indicates its source, and it is like the saying of God Almighty: And let not those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty think that it is good for them meaning stinginess is good for them, so if people are afflicted with need or poverty, then giving money is beloved to them. It was said: It refers to the name of God Almighty in His saying: Whoever believes in God. The intended meaning is that a person gives charity in these ways while he is healthy and stingy, fearing poverty and feeling secure about survival. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And those who fulfill their covenant when they have made it meaning between themselves and God Almighty and between themselves and the people. And those who are patient in poverty and hardship Poverty: hardship and poverty. And hardship: sickness and time, as Ibn Masoud said. And he, peace be upon him, said: God the Almighty says: “Any of My servants whom I afflict with a trial in his bed and he does not complain to Me, I will replace his flesh with better flesh and his blood with better blood. If I take him, then he is in My mercy, and if I heal him, I will heal him even though he has not sinned.” It was said: O Messenger of God, what flesh is better than his flesh? He said: Flesh, he has not sinned. It was said: What blood is better than his blood? He said: Blood, he has not sinned. Adversity and hardship are two nouns that are based on their verbs, and they do not have a verb, because they are nouns and not descriptions. And at the time of battle means at the time of war. The Almighty said: Those are the ones who were truthful, and those are the righteous. He described them as being truthful and pious in their affairs and fulfilling them, and that they were serious about religion, and this is the ultimate praise. Truthfulness is the opposite of lying. It is said: They were truthful to them in fighting. A friend is one who adheres to truthfulness. In the hadith: “Be truthful, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to be truthful and seeks to be truthful until he is recorded with God as truthful.”
2:178: It contains seventeen issues: First: Al-Bukhari, Al-Nasa'i and Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Retaliation was practiced among the Children of Israel, but blood money was not practiced among them. So God said to this nation: “Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder: the free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female. But if a remission is made by his brother, then he should accept the blood money in the case of premeditated murder. “Then follow up in kindness and pay it back with goodness.” He should follow up in kindness and pay back with goodness. That is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy. What was prescribed for those who came before you. But whoever transgresses after that will have a painful punishment. Killing after accepting the blood money. This is the wording of Al-Bukhari: Al-Humaidi narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, Amr narrated to us, he said: I heard Mujahid say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: Al-Sha’bi said about the words of God, the Most High: The free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female. He said: It was revealed about two tribes of Arabs who fought and said: We will kill for our slave, so-and-so, son of so-and-so, and for our female slave, so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so. And something similar was narrated by Qatada. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Retaliation is prescribed for you. The meaning of prescribed is imposed and established. From this is the saying of Omar bin Abi Rabi’ah: Killing and fighting are written on us and on the prostitutes who drag their tails It has been said: Here, the book is a report of what was written in the Preserved Tablet and what was previously decreed. Retribution is taken from Qass al-Athar which means following it, and from it comes al-Qass because he follows traces and report. And cutting poetry is following its trace, so it is as if the killer took a path of murder and traced its traces in it and walked in his path in that, and from it comes So they returned upon their traces, tracing. And it has been said: Qass is cutting, it is said: I cut what was between them. And from it comes al-Qisas, because he wounds him like his wound or kills him with it, it is said: The judge cut so-and-so from so-and-so and he refused it, so he took revenge on him, meaning he exacted retribution from him. Third: The image of retaliation is that the killer is required, if the guardian wants to kill, to submit to God’s command and obey His lawful retaliation, and that the guardian is required to stand by the killer of his guardian and refrain from transgressing against anyone else, just as the Arabs used to transgress and kill someone other than the killer, and this is the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: “The most rebellious people to God on the Day of Resurrection will be three: a man who kills someone other than his killer, a man who kills in the Sacred Sanctuary, and a man who takes the spoils of the Age of Ignorance.” Al-Sha’bi, Qatada, and others said: The people of the Age of Ignorance were unjust and obeyed Satan. If a tribe was powerful and strong and one of their slaves was killed, another group of slaves would kill him. They would say: We will not kill anyone but a free man for him. If one of their women was killed, they would say: We will not kill anyone but a man for him. If one of their lowly people was killed, they would say: We will not kill anyone but a noble man for him. They would say: Killing is more protective of killing with the letter waw and the letter qaf. It is also narrated as abqa with the letter ba and the letter qaf, and it is also narrated as anfa with the letter nun and the letter fa. So God forbade them from rebellion, saying: “Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder: the free for the free, the slave for the slave” al-Baqarah 2:17. He also said: And there is life for you in retaliation. There is a great difference between the two statements in terms of eloquence and clarity. Fourth: There is no disagreement that retaliation for murder can only be carried out by those in authority. It is obligatory upon them to undertake retaliation and the implementation of the prescribed punishments and other things, because God Almighty addressed all believers with retaliation, and it is not possible for all believers to come together to carry out retaliation, so they appointed the ruler in their place in carrying out retaliation and other prescribed punishments. Retaliation is not obligatory, but what is obligatory is that retaliation and other prescribed punishments not go beyond aggression. However, if consent is given without retaliation, such as blood money or forgiveness, then that is permissible, as will be explained. If it is said: The meaning of the Almighty’s statement: It is prescribed for you is an obligation and a necessity, so how can retaliation not be obligatory? It is said to him: Its meaning is if you want, then know that retaliation is the goal in the case of quarreling. The slain is the plural of slain, a feminine noun for the feminine of the group, and it is something that people are forced to do, so it came in this structure like wounded, weak, foolish, fallen, drowned, and the like. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: The free for the free, the slave for the slave, the female for the female verse. There is a difference of opinion regarding its interpretation. A group said that the verse was built on the ruling of the species if it kills its own species, so it clarified the ruling of the free man if he kills a free man, the slave if he kills a slave, and the female if she kills a female, and it did not address either of the two species if it kills the other. So the verse is decisive and contains ambiguity, which is clarified by the Almighty’s saying: And We ordained for them therein that a life is for a life verse, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, clarified it when he killed a Jew for a woman, as Mujahid said, and Abu Ubaid mentioned it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was abrogated by the verse of Al-Ma’idah, and this is the opinion of the people of Iraq. Sixth: The Kufians and Al-Thawri said: A free man is killed for a slave, and a Muslim for a dhimmi. They argued with the words of God Almighty: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is retaliation for those murdered 1:100, so it is general. And His words: And We prescribed for them therein a life for a life 1:100, they said: The dhimmi and the Muslim are equal in the sanctity that is sufficient for retaliation, which is the sanctity of blood that is established forever. The dhimmi’s blood is sanctified forever, and so is the Muslim, and both of them have become people of the abode of Islam. What confirms this is that the Muslim’s hand is cut off for stealing the property of the dhimmi, and this indicates that the property of the dhimmi is equal to the property of the Muslim, so it indicates its equality with his blood, since property is only forbidden by the sanctity of its owner. Abu Hanifa and his companions, Al-Thawri and Ibn Abi Laila agreed that a free man is killed for a slave just as a slave is killed for it, and this is the saying of Dawud, and it was narrated from Ali and Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with them, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Qatada, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and Al-Hakam bin Uyaynah said the same. The majority of scholars do not kill a free man for a slave, due to the diversity and division in the verse. Abu Thawr said: Since they all agreed that there is no retaliation between slaves and free people in matters other than souls, souls were more deserving of that, and whoever among them differentiated between them has contradicted himself. Also, the consensus regarding the one who kills a slave by mistake is that he is only liable for the value, so just as he is not like a free man in the case of accident, he is not like him in the case of deliberate killing. Also, the slave is a commodity among commodities that is bought and sold, and the free man disposes of him as he wishes, so there is no equality between him and the free man and no resistance. I said that this consensus is correct, and as for his saying first: And since they all agreed - until his saying - then it contradicted, because Ibn Abi Laila and Dawud said that retaliation is permissible between free people and slaves in the soul and in all the limbs, and Dawud provided evidence with his saying, peace be upon him: The blood of Muslims is equal, so he did not differentiate between a free man and a slave. This will be explained in the chapter on women, God willing. Seventh: The majority also agree that a Muslim should not be killed for killing an infidel, based on the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: A Muslim shall not be killed for killing an infidel. Narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib. What they narrated from the hadith of Rabi’ah is not authentic: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed a Muslim on the day of Khaybar for an unbeliever,” because it is disconnected. From the hadith of Ibn al-Baylamani, who is weak, on the authority of Ibn Umar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Al-Daraqutni said: It was not supported by anyone except Ibrahim ibn Yahya, whose hadith is rejected. The correct version is on the authority of Rabi’ah, on the authority of Ibn al-Baylamani, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn al-Baylamani is weak in hadith and cannot be used as evidence if the hadith is connected, so how about if it is transmitted by a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? I said: There is nothing authentic in this chapter except the hadith of Al-Bukhari, and it specifies the generality of the Almighty’s statement: Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder Al-Bukhari 1979, and the generality of His statement: A life for a life. Eighth: It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib and Al-Hassan bin Abi Al-Hassan Al-Basri that the verse was revealed explaining the ruling on the two mentioned, to indicate the difference between them and a free man killing a slave or a slave killing a free man, or a male killing a female or a female killing a male. They said: If a man kills a woman, if her guardians want, they kill their companion and pay his guardians half of the blood money, and if they want, they spare him and take the blood money of the woman from him. If a woman kills a man, if his guardians want to kill her, they kill her and take half of the blood money, otherwise they take the blood money of their companion and spare her. This was narrated by Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Ali, but it is not authentic, because Al-Sha’bi did not meet Ali. Al-Hakam narrated on the authority of Ali and Abdullah, who said: If a man kills a woman intentionally, he is to be killed in retaliation for her. This contradicts the narration of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Ali. Scholars have agreed that if a one-eyed or paralyzed person kills a healthy man, his guardian is not allowed to kill the one-eyed man and take half of the blood money from him, because he killed a man with two eyes while he was one-eyed, and killed a man with two hands while he was paralyzed. This indicates that a soul is equal to a soul, and a child is equal to an adult in this regard. And it is said to the one who says this: If the man is not equal to the woman and does not fall under the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The blood of Muslims is equal. So why did she kill a man with it when it is not equal to him and then take half the blood money? The scholars have agreed that blood money cannot be combined with retaliation, and that if blood money is accepted, blood is forbidden and retaliation is lifted. So your statement is not based on a principle or analogy. This was said by Abu Omar, may God be pleased with him. If a free man kills a slave, if the master of the slave wants to kill him and give the free man’s blood money except for the value of the slave, and if he wants to, he can take the slave’s value. This was mentioned from Ali and Al-Hasan, and it was also denied from them. Ninth: The scholars agreed on killing a man for a woman and a woman for a man, and the majority do not see any return. A group sees following with the surplus of blood money. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Al-Thawri, and Abu Thawr said: And likewise the retaliation between them for what is less than a life. Hammad bin Abi Sulayman and Abu Hanifa said: There is no retaliation between them for what is less than a life for a life, but it is in a life for a life, and they are refuted by attributing what is less than a life to a life in a more appropriate and preferable way, based on what was mentioned above. Tenth: Ibn al-Arabi said: Ignorance has reached the point where they said: A free man is killed for his own slave. They narrated in a hadith on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of Samurah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever kills his slave, we will kill him. This is a weak hadith. Our evidence is the Almighty’s saying: And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed limits in [the matter of] taking life. The heir here is the master, so how can he be given authority over himself? Everyone has agreed that if the master kills his slave by mistake, his value is not taken from him for the public treasury. Amr ibn Shu’aib narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather: “A man intentionally killed his slave, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, flogged him, banished him for a year, and erased his share from the Muslims and did not retaliate for him.” If it is said: If a man kills his wife, why do you not say: Marriage is established as a doubt in order to ward off retaliation from the husband, since marriage is a type of slavery, and Al-Layth ibn Sa`d stated that? We say: Marriage is concluded for her on him, as evidenced by the fact that he does not marry her sister or four others besides her, and she demands from him the right to intercourse as he demands from her, but he has the advantage of guardianship over her that God has given him over her because of what he spent from his money, that is, because of what is required of him in terms of dowry and maintenance, so if he created a doubt, he would give her an inheritance on both sides. I said: This hadith, which Ibn al-Arabi weakened, is authentic. It was narrated by al-Nasa’i and Abu Dawud, and the completion of its text is: Whoever mutilates his limbs, We will mutilate him, and whoever castrates him, We will castrate him. Al-Bukhari said on the authority of Ali ibn al-Madini: The hearing of al-Hasan ibn Samurah is authentic, and he accepted this hadith. Al-Bukhari said: I also agree with him, for if the hadith were not authentic, these two imams would not have agreed with it, and they are enough for you! A free man is killed for killing his own slave. Al-Nakha’i and al-Thawri said in one of his two opinions: It has been said that al-Hasan did not hear from Samurah anything except the hadith of the ‘aqeeqah, and God knows best. They differed regarding retaliation between slaves in matters less than a soul. This is the opinion of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Salim ibn Abdullah, al-Zuhri, Qaran, Malik, al-Shafi’i, and Abu Thawr. Al-Sha’bi, al-Nakha’i, al-Thawri, and Abu Hanifa said: There is no retaliation between them except for a soul. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The first is more authentic. Eleventh: Al-Darqutni and Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Suraqah bin Malik, who said: I was present with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the father was being punished for his son, but the son was not being punished for his father. Abu Isa said: This is a hadith that we do not know of as a hadith of Suraqah except from this source, and its chain of transmission is not authentic. It was narrated by Ismail bin Ayyash on the authority of Al-Muthanna bin Al-Sabah, and Al-Muthanna is considered weak in hadith. This hadith was narrated by Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar on the authority of Al-Hajjaj on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather on the authority of Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This hadith was narrated on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib as a mursal, and this hadith is confused. The scholars act upon this, that if a father kills his son, he is not to be killed for it, and if he slanders him, he is not to be punished. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The scholars differed regarding a man who kills his son intentionally. A group said: There is no retaliation against him, but he is to pay blood money. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and the people of opinion. It was also narrated on the authority of Ata’ and Mujahid. Malik, Ibn Nafi’ and Ibn Abd al-Hakam said: He is to be killed for it. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This is what we say based on the apparent meaning of the Book and the Sunnah. As for the apparent meaning of the Book, it is the Almighty’s saying: “Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder: the free for the free, the slave for the slave,” and what is proven from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: The blood of the believers is equal. We do not know of any authentic hadith that would exclude the father from the verse. We have narrated unconfirmed hadiths about it. Al-Kaya al-Tabari narrated on the authority of Uthman al-Batti that a father is killed for his son, due to the generalities in retaliation. The same was narrated on the authority of Malik, and perhaps they do not accept individual hadiths in contrast to the generalities of the Qur’an. I said: There is no disagreement in the Maliki school that if a man kills his son intentionally, such as by lying him down and slaughtering him or by beating him, for which he has no excuse and no doubt about claiming error, then he is to be killed for it according to one opinion. But if he threw a weapon at him out of discipline or anger and killed him, then there are two opinions in the school: he is to be killed for it, and he is not to be killed for it and the blood money is increased, and this is what the majority of scholars said. And a stranger is to be killed for something like this. Ibn al-Arabi: I heard our Sheikh Fakhr al-Islam al-Shashi say in al-Nazar: A father is not to be killed for his son, because the father was the reason for his existence, so how can he be the reason for his nonexistence? This is invalidated by the fact that if he committed adultery with his daughter, then he is to be stoned, and he was the reason for her existence and she is the reason for his nonexistence. Then what is the jurisprudence under this, and why is he not the reason for his nonexistence if he disobeyed God in that? And they have transmitted from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: A father is not to be killed for his son is a false hadith. Their argument is that Umar may God be pleased with him ruled that blood money should be paid heavily for the murderer of his son, and none of the companions objected to him. The rest of the jurists may God be pleased with them took the issue as recorded and said: A father is not to be killed for his son. Malik took it as a detailed ruling and said: If he struck him with the sword, and this is a possible case of intent to kill or not, and his fear of fatherhood is a suspicion that is established as evidence of the lack of intent to kill, then the blood money is dropped. If he lays him down, he removes the cover from his intent, so it is connected to its origin. Ibn al-Mundhir said: Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq used to say: If a son kills his father, he is to be killed for it. Twelfth: Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal used this verse as evidence for his statement: Do not kill a group for one person. He said: Because God Almighty stipulated equality and there is no equality between a group and an individual. God Almighty said: “And We ordained for them therein: A life for a life, an eye for an eye.” The answer is that what is meant by retaliation in the verse is killing whoever kills, whoever he may be, in response to the Arabs who wanted to kill for whoever killed someone who did not kill, and kill in return for one person a hundred, out of pride and to show off their prestige and power. So God Almighty commanded justice and equality, by killing whoever killed, and… Omar, may God be pleased with him, killed seven people in Sana’a and said: If the people of Sana’a conspired against him, I would have killed them all. Ali, may God be pleased with him, killed the Kharijites in the name of Abdullah bin Khabab, so he stopped fighting them until they spoke. When they slaughtered Abdullah bin Khabab as a sheep is slaughtered, and Ali was informed of that, he said: God is Great! Call them to bring out to us the killer of Abdullah bin Khabab. They said: We all killed him, three times. Ali said to his companions: Take the people and they will be killed. It was not long before Ali and his companions killed them. Al-Daraqutni included the two hadiths in his Sunan. And in Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Saeed and Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: If the people of the heavens and the earth were to share in the blood of a believer, God would throw them all into the Fire. He said about it: A strange hadith. Also, if the group knew that if they killed one person, they would not be killed, the enemies would cooperate in killing their enemies by sharing in killing them, and they would achieve the hope of revenge. Observing this rule is more appropriate than observing words, and God knows best. Ibn al-Mundhir said: Al-Zuhri, Habib ibn Abi Thabit, and Ibn Sirin said: Two people should not be killed for one person. We narrated that from Muadh ibn Jabal, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Abdullah. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This is more correct, and there is no argument with those who permit killing a group for one person. What we have mentioned has been proven from Ibn al-Zubayr. Thirteenth: The Imams narrated on the authority of Abu Shuraih Al-Kaabi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Behold, you, the people of Khuza’a, have killed this man from Hudhayl, and I am his blood money. So whoever has another man killed after what I have said, his family has two choices: either take the blood money or kill him.” The wording of Abu Dawud. Al-Tirmidhi said: A good and authentic hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Shuraih Al-Khuza’i that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If someone is killed, he has the right to kill, pardon, or take blood money. Some scholars have adopted this view, and it is the opinion of Ahmad and Ishaq. Fourteenth: The scholars differed about taking blood money from a premeditated murderer. A group said: The guardian of the murdered person has the choice: if he wishes, he may exact retribution, or he may take blood money, even if the murderer does not agree. This is narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Ata’, and Al-Hasan. It was narrated by Ashab on the authority of Malik, and Al-Layth, Al-Awza’i, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr said the same. Their evidence is the hadith of Abu Shuraih and what is similar to it, and it is a text in a matter of disagreement. Also, from the point of view of consideration, he was only obligated to pay blood money without his consent, because it was obligatory upon him to revive himself, and God Almighty said: And do not kill yourselves. And his saying, But if his brother pardons him anything, meaning he leaves him his blood money, in one of the interpretations, and he is satisfied with the blood money, then the blood money should be followed according to what is acceptable, meaning the one who has the blood money should follow according to what is acceptable in demanding the blood money, and the killer should pay it to him with kindness, meaning without procrastination or delaying it from the time, That is an alleviation from your Lord and a mercy, meaning that those who came before us, God did not impose anything on them except a life for a life, so God favored this nation with blood money if the guardian of the blood money is satisfied with it, as will be explained. Others said: The guardian of the murdered person has nothing but retaliation, and he does not take blood money unless the killer is satisfied. This was narrated by Ibn al-Qasim from Malik, and this is the well-known view from him, and al-Thawri and the Kufians said the same. They cited as evidence the hadith of Anas: In the story of Al-Rabi’ when the woman’s front tooth was broken, the Imams narrated that they said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled with retaliation and said: Retaliation is the Book of God, retaliation is the Book of God, and did not give the victim the choice between retaliation and blood money, it was proven that what is required by the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger in the case of premeditated murder is retaliation, and the first is more correct, according to the hadith of Abu Shuraih mentioned above. Al-Rabi’ narrated on the authority of Al-Shafi’i, who said: Abu Hanifa bin Samak bin Al-Fadl Al-Shihabi told me, who said: Ibn Abi Tha’lab told me on the authority of Al-Maqburi on the authority of Abin Shuraih Al-Ka’bi that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the year of the conquest: “Whoever has someone killed has the better of two options: if he likes, he may take blood money, and if he likes, he may take retaliation.” Abu Hanifa said: “I said to Ibn Abi Tha’lab: ‘Will you take it, O Abu Al-Harith?’ He hit my chest and shouted at me a lot and insulted me and said: ‘I am telling you about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you say: ‘You take it!’ Yes, I will take it, and that is obligatory upon me and upon whoever hears it. God, the Exalted, the Majestic, chose Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the people and guided them through him and by his hand, and chose for them what He chose for him and through his tongue, so it is upon the people to follow him, willingly or unwillingly. There is no way out for a Muslim from that.’ He said: ‘And he did not keep quiet about me until I wished that he would keep quiet.’” Fifteenth: The Almighty’s saying: But if a brother pardons him anything, then there should be a reasonable follow-up and payment to him with good treatment. Scholars differed in the interpretation of whoever pardons into five interpretations: One of them: That the killer is meant by it, and pardon includes pardoning, which is the blood guardian, and the brother is the murdered person, and something is the blood that is pardoned and returns to taking the blood money. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Mujahid, and a group of scholars. Pardon in this saying is according to its chapter, which is leaving. The meaning is: If the murderer is pardoned by the guardian of the murdered person for the blood of his murdered person and drops the retaliation, then he takes the blood money and is followed up with what is good, and the murderer pays him with kindness. The second: It is the statement of Malik that whoever is meant by it is the guardian and pardoned is made easy, not in the same way as pardoning, and the brother is meant by the killer, and something is the blood money, meaning that if the guardian is inclined to pardon retaliation over taking the blood money, then the killer has the choice between giving it or surrendering himself, sometimes it is made easy and sometimes it is not made easy. And other than Malik says: If the guardians are satisfied with the blood money, then the killer has no choice, rather it is obligatory upon him. This statement was narrated from Malik, and many of his companions preferred it. Abu Hanifa said: The meaning of pardoned is giving, and pardon in the language is giving, and for this reason God the Almighty said: Take what is easy, meaning what is easy. Abu Al-Aswad Al-Du’ali said: Forgive me, and you will continue to love me He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The beginning of time is the pleasure of God, and its end is the forgiveness of God. That is, God bears witness over His servants. It is as if He said: Whoever is offered something from the blood money, let him accept it. And let him follow it with kindness. Some people said: And let the killer be paid to him with kindness. So God the Almighty urged him to take the money if that is easy on the part of the killer, and He informed that it is a relief and mercy from Him, as He said after mentioning retaliation in Surat al-Ma’idah 5:But whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. So He urged the mercy of forgiveness and charity, and likewise He urged in what was mentioned in this verse to accept the blood money if the offender offered it by giving the blood money, then He ordered the guardian to follow and ordered the offender to pay it with kindness. Some people said: These words refer to the specific people about whom the entire verse was revealed and who paid the blood money to each other as a set-off. The meaning of the verse is: Whoever from the two groups has something of that blood money left over from the other, and ‘afi’ means ‘surplus’. Sufyan bin Hussein bin Shuwa narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: There was fighting between two tribes of Arabs, and some of them were killed. One of the tribes said: We will not be satisfied until a man is killed for a woman and a man for a woman. So they went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Killing is the same. So they agreed on blood money, and one tribe was preferred over the other. This is what he said: He wrote until he said: But if someone pardons something from his brother, meaning if someone has a preference over his brother, then let him repay it according to what is acceptable. Al-Sha’bi informed about the reason for the revelation of the verse, and Sufyan mentioned pardon here as preference, and this is a meaning that the wording allows. Fifth interpretation: It is the statement of Ali, may God be pleased with him, and Al-Hassan regarding the difference between the blood money of a man and a woman, a free man and a slave, meaning whoever has that difference should follow what is known, and pardon in this place also means a difference. Sixteenth: This verse is an exhortation from God the Almighty to demand good from the claimant, and to pay well from the payer. Is that obligatory or recommended? The nominative reading indicates obligation, because the meaning is that he must follow what is good. An-Nahhas said: So whoever is pardoned is a condition and the answer is then he must follow, which is nominative by beginning, and the meaning is that he must follow what is good. It is permissible in other than the Qur’an to say then he must follow and perform by making them two sources. Ibn Atiyah said: Ibrahim bin Abi Ubla read it in the accusative. The nominative is a way for obligations, like the Almighty’s saying: then keep [them] in an acceptable manner. As for what is recommended, it comes in the accusative, like His saying: then strike the necks. Seventeenth: The Almighty’s saying: This is a concession from your Lord and a mercy, because the people of the Torah were allowed to kill and nothing else, and the people of the Gospel were allowed to pardon and were not allowed retaliation or blood money, so God Almighty made this a concession for this nation, so whoever wanted to kill, whoever wanted to take blood money, and whoever wanted to pardon. The Almighty’s statement, But whoever transgresses after that is a condition and its answer, meaning, if he kills after taking the blood money and the blood money has been paid, the killer of his guardian will have a painful punishment. Al-Hasan said: If a man in the pre-Islamic era killed someone, he would flee to his people. Then his people would come and make peace with the blood money, and the guardian of the one killed would say, I accept the blood money, until the killer feels safe and leaves, then he would kill him and then throw the blood money to them. Scholars differed about someone who was killed after receiving the blood money. A group of scholars, including Malik and al-Shafi’i, said: He is like someone who was killed in the first place. If the guardian wishes, he may kill him, or if he wishes, he may pardon him, but his punishment will be in the Hereafter. Qatada, Ikrimah, al-Suddi, and others said: His punishment is to be killed for good, and the ruler does not allow the guardian to pardon. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not pardon the one who killed after taking the blood money. Al-Hasan said: His punishment is that he only pays the blood money and his sin remains until the punishment of the Hereafter. Omar bin Abdul Aziz said: His matter is up to the Imam to do with him as he sees fit. In Sunan Al-Darqutni, on the authority of Abu Shuraih Al-Khuza’i, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever is afflicted with blood or is insane - insane means limping - has the choice between one of three things. If he wants the fourth, then seize his hand and either take retribution, pardon, or take blood money. If he accepts any of that and then transgresses after that, then he will be in Hell, abiding therein forever.”
2:179: God Almighty says: And there is life for you in retaliation, O people of understanding, that you may become righteous. There are four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And there is life for you in retaliation. This is eloquent and concise speech, as mentioned above. Its meaning is: Do not kill one another. It was narrated by Sufyan on the authority of al-Suddi on the authority of Abu Malik. The meaning is that when retaliation is carried out and the ruling is fulfilled, whoever wants to kill another will be deterred, fearing that retaliation will be taken from him, and thus they will both live. When the Arabs killed another man, their tribes would become enraged and fight each other, and this would lead to the killing of a large number. When God legislated retaliation, everyone was content with it and stopped fighting, and in that there was life for them. Second: The imams of fatwa agreed that it is not permissible for anyone to take revenge on someone for his right without the authority, and people do not have the right to take revenge on each other. Rather, that is for the authority or whoever the authority has appointed for that purpose. For this reason, God made the authority so that people can restrain one another. Third: The scholars agreed that the ruler must take revenge on himself if he transgresses against one of his subjects, since he is one of them, and he only has the privilege of looking after them, like the guardian and the agent, and that does not prevent retaliation, and there is no difference between them and the common people in the rulings of God Almighty, because He, the Most High, said: Retaliation is prescribed for you in cases of murder. It was proven from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, that he said to a man who complained to him that a worker had cut off his hand: If you are truthful, I will take revenge on him for you. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distributing something, a man leaned over him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stabbed him with a palm branch that he had with him, so the man cried out, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Come and take revenge. He said: Rather, I have pardoned, O Messenger of God. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated on the authority of Abu Firas, who said: Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him gave a sermon and said: Whoever is wronged by his ruler, let him report it to me so that I may take revenge on him. Amr bin Al-Aas stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, if one of us disciplines one of his subjects, will you take revenge on him? He said: How can I not take revenge on him when I saw the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) take revenge on himself?! Abu Dawud Al-Sijistani narrated that he said: Omar bin Al-Khattab gave a sermon to us and said: I did not send my workers to beat your bodies or take your money, so whoever does that to him, let him report it to me so that I may take revenge on him. He mentioned the hadith with both its chains of transmission. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Perhaps you will become righteous. Its meaning has been presented above. What is meant is that you will become righteous by being killed and thus be safe from retaliation. Then this will be a call for various types of righteousness in other matters, for God rewards obedience for obedience. Abu al-Jawza’ Aws ibn Abdullah al-Rab’i read: And for you in the stories is life. An-Nahhas said: Abu al-Jawza’s reading is anomalous. Another said: It is possible that it is a source like retaliation. It was said: By the stories he meant the Qur’an, meaning that for you in the Book of God in which retaliation was prescribed is life, meaning salvation.
2:180: It contains twenty-one issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: It is prescribed for you This is the verse of the will, and there is no mention of the will in the Qur’an except in this verse, and in An-Nisa’: after making a will and in al-Ma’idah 5:at the time of the will. The one in Al-Baqarah is the most complete and perfect of them and was revealed before the revelation of the obligatory duties and inheritances, as will be explained. In the speech, the conjunction and is assumed, meaning and it is prescribed for you, and when the speech became long, the conjunction and was dropped. And similar to it in some sayings: None shall pray it except the most wretched * Who denied and turned away meaning who, so it was dropped. And it was said: When it was mentioned that the heir of the blood has the right to exact retribution, this is the one who is on the verge of being exacted from and he is the cause of death, so it is as if death has come to him, so this is the time of the will, so the verse is connected to what precedes it and connected to it, and therefore the conjunction and was dropped. And the meaning of was prescribed is imposed and established, as mentioned above. And the presence of death: its causes, and when the cause is present, the Arabs are with it from the effect, their poet said: O rider, mixing your mount, ask the Banu Asad, what is this sound? And tell them to hasten to make an excuse and seek a word that will acquit you, for I am death. Antara said: Death is at my disposal if I reach my fingertips to the Hindu gods. Jarir said in his satire of Al-Farazdaq: I am the death you spoke about, so no one can escape me Second: If it is said: Why did he say wrote and not I wrote, and the will is feminine? It is said to him: That is because he meant by the will bequest. And it is said: Because there was a separator in between, so the separator was like a replacement for the feminine taa. The Arabs say: A woman attended the judge today. And Sibawayh narrated: A woman stood up. But that is good only when the barrier is long. Third: The Almighty’s saying: If he leaves behind any good, if he stipulated, and in his answer to Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash there are two opinions. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is the will, then the fa was deleted, as the poet said: Whoever does good deeds, God will reward them, and evil is recompensed for evil in the sight of God. The other answer: The past tense may have its answer before it after it, so the estimate would be the will for the parents and relatives if he left something good. If the fa is estimated, then the will is raised by the beginning, and if the fa is not estimated, it is permissible to raise it by the beginning, and to raise it on what its doer is not named, i.e. the will was written upon you. It is not correct according to the majority of grammarians for the will to work in if because it is in the rule of the relative clause for the source which is the will and it has been presented, so it is not permissible for it to work in it as if it was presented. It is permissible for the agent in if to be: wrote and the meaning is: God’s obligation is directed to you and the requirement of His book is present, so the direction of the obligation is expressed by written to connect to this meaning that it is written in eternity.
