Abu Omar said: The hadith of Shaddad, Rafi’ and Thawban is supported by the hadith of Ibn Abbas, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was cupped while he was fasting and in a state of ihram.” Because in the hadith of Shaddad bin Aws and others, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by a man who was being cupped in the year of the conquest eighteen nights before the end of Ramadan, and he said: The cupper and the one being cupped have broken their fast.” And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was cupped in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage while he was in a state of ihram and fasting. So if his Hajj, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage, then it is inevitably abrogating, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not witness Ramadan after that, because he died in Rabi’ al-Awwal, may God bless him and grant him peace. Eighteenth: The Almighty’s saying: Then complete the fast until the night is a command that requires obligation without dispute. And until a limit, if what comes after it is of the same type as what came before it, then it is included in its ruling, like your saying, I bought the acre to its edge, or I bought from you from this tree to this tree - and the sale is a tree, then the tree is included in the sale. Unlike your saying: I bought the acre to the house, then the house is not included in the specified because it is not of the same type. So the Almighty stipulated the completion of the fast until the night becomes distinct, just as He permitted eating until the day becomes distinct. Nineteenth: Part of the completion of fasting is to maintain the intention without lifting it. If he lifts it during some of the day and intends to break the fast, but he does not eat or drink, then in the Mudawwana he is considered to have broken the fast and must make up for it. In the book of Ibn Habib, it is stated that he is still fasting. He said: And nothing takes him out of the fast except breaking the fast by action, not by intention. And it was said: He must make up for it and offer expiation. Sahnun said: Only the one who intends to break the fast must expiate. As for the one who intends to do so during the day, it does not harm him, but he must make up for it based on preference. I said: This is good. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth: The Almighty’s saying: until the night When the night becomes clear, breaking the fast is prescribed by the Sharia, whether one eats or does not eat. Ibn al-Arabi said: Imam Abu Ishaq al-Shirazi was asked about a man who swore by divorce three times that he would not break his fast with anything hot or cold, so he answered that when the sun sets he breaks his fast and there is nothing wrong with him, and he cited as evidence the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If the night comes from here and the day departs from here, then the fasting person has broken his fast. Imam Abu Nasr ibn al-Sabbagh, the author of al-Shamel, was asked about it and he said: He must break his fast with something hot or cold. Imam Abu Ishaq’s answer is more appropriate, because it is what is required by the Book and the Sunnah. Twenty-one: If he thought that the sun had set due to clouds or something else, and he broke his fast, then the sun appeared, he must make up for it according to the majority of scholars. In Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, may God be pleased with them both, she said: We broke our fast during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a cloudy day, then the sun rose. It was said to Hisham: So they ordered us to make it up? He said: We must make it up. Umar said in Al-Muwatta’ about this: “The matter is simple. We have exerted our efforts in the time to make it up.” It was narrated on the authority of Umar that he said: He does not have to make it up. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said the same: He does not have to make it up like the one who forgets. This is the opinion of Ishaq and the people of the apparent meaning. God’s statement: until the night refutes this opinion, and God knows best.
2:188: It contains eight issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And do not consume one another’s wealth. It was said that it was revealed about Abdan bin Ashwa’ Al-Hadrami, who claimed money from Imru’ Al-Qais Al-Kindi and they disputed before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Imru’ Al-Qais denied it and wanted to swear an oath, so this verse was revealed. So how about an oath when Abdan ruled over his land and did not dispute with him? Second: The address in this verse includes all the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the meaning is: Do not eat each other’s money unjustly. This includes: gambling, deception, usurpation, denial of rights, and what the owner does not like, or what the Shari’ah has forbidden even if the owner likes it, such as the dowry of a prostitute, the fee of a soothsayer, the prices of alcohol and pigs, and other things. It does not include fraud in a sale when the seller knows the truth of what he sold, because fraud is like a gift, as will be explained in Surat An-Nisa. Money was added to the pronoun of the prohibited because each of them is prohibited and prohibited, as God says: You kill yourselves. Some people said: What is meant by the verse is: And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly, meaning in entertainment, singing, drinking, and idleness. Accordingly, money is added to the pronoun of the owners. Third: Whoever takes someone else’s money without the permission of the Shari’ah has taken it unlawfully. Taking unlawfully is when a judge issues a ruling in your favor while you know that you are doing something wrong. The unlawful does not become lawful by the judge’s ruling, because he only issues rulings based on what appears to be the case. This is a consensus regarding money, although according to Abu Hanifa, his ruling is enforceable in matters of private parts. If the judge’s ruling does not change the ruling of the inside regarding money, then it is more appropriate regarding private parts. Imams narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You bring your disputes to me, and perhaps some of you are more eloquent in their arguments than others, so I will rule in his favor based on what I hear. So whoever I cut off from his brother’s right, he should not take it, for I have only cut off for him a piece of fire - in one narration - so let him carry it or leave it.” The majority of scholars and imams of jurists agree with this hadith. It is a clear statement that the judge’s ruling on the outward appearance does not change the ruling on the inward appearance, and this is the same in cases of wealth, blood, and private parts, except for what was narrated from Abu Hanifa regarding private parts. He claimed that if a false witness testified against a man that he had divorced his wife and the judge ruled based on their testimony because of their justness in his view, then her private parts would be permissible for the man who married her - from someone who knows that the ruling is invalid - after the waiting period. Likewise, if one of the witnesses married her, it would be permissible in his view, because since she was permissible for husbands outwardly, the witness and others were equal, because the judge’s ruling severed her chastity, and in that he created what is permissible and forbidden in both the outward and inward aspects, and were it not for that, she would not have been permissible for husbands. He argued with the ruling on cursing and said: It is known that the wife only reached the point of separating from her husband through false cursing, and if the ruler had known that she lied in it, he would have punished her and would not have separated them. So this is not included in the generality of his, peace be upon him, saying: If you decide for someone something from his brother’s right, he should not take it. Hadith. Fourth: This verse is the basis for every party and opponent to hold fast to every ruling they claim for themselves that it is not permissible, and they cite as evidence for it the words of God Almighty: And do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly. The answer to this is to say to him: We do not accept that it is invalid until you explain it with evidence, and then it is included in this generality, so it is evidence that invalidity in transactions is not permissible, and it does not specify what is invalid. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: with falsehood. Falsehood in the language means: that which is gone and vanishes. It is said: batala yabtalan he became invalid and batalaan falsehood. The plural of batala is bawatil falsehood. Abatil is the plural of batula falsehood. Tabtal means to follow amusement. Tabtal means to follow amusement. So-and-so abtalated if he came with falsehood. And the Almighty’s saying: Falsehood will not come to it Qatada said: He is Iblis, he does not add to the Qur’an nor subtract from it. And His saying: And God erases falsehood means polytheism. And batala means magicians. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And bring it down to the judges Al-Ma’idah 6:17. It was said: It means the deposit and what there is no evidence for, according to Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan. It was also said: It is the orphan’s money that is in the hands of the guardians, and he brings it up to the judges if he is asked for it so that some of it can be taken and an argument can be established for him on the surface. Al-Zajjaj said: You do what the apparent rulings require and leave what you know is the truth. It is said: A man brought down his argument or the matter that he hopes to succeed in, likening it to the one who sends a bucket into a well. It is said: He lowered his bucket: he sent it down. And he lowered it, he took it out. The plural of bucket and buckets is: adala, buckets, and bucketli. The meaning of the verse: Do not combine eating money unjustly with bringing false arguments to the judges, and it is like His saying: And do not mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth. It is similar to your saying: Do not eat fish and drink milk. It was said: The meaning is: Do not bribe the rulers with your money and do not bribe them to decide for you more than that, so the ba’ is a simple attachment. Ibn Atiyah said: This statement is more likely, because the rulers are suspected and bribery is not permitted except for those who are protected, which is the least. Also, the two words are compatible: dalelu is from sending the bucket, and bribery is from bribery, as if he extends it to fulfill a need. I said: This is strengthened by his saying: And you shower it with it. Spoil it is in the accusative case in apposition to eat, as we mentioned. In the Mushaf of Abu, do not pour it with the repetition of the letter of prohibition, and this reading supports the accusative case of Spoil it in the reading of the group. It was said that Spoil it is in the accusative case as an adverb, and what is accusative in such a case according to Sibawayh is that it is implied. The ha’ in his saying with it refers to the money, and according to the first opinion to the argument and it was not mentioned, so the second opinion is strengthened by the mention of the money, and God knows best. In Al-Sahah: Bribery is well-known, and bribery with the damma is like it, and the plural is rasha and rasha, and he bribed him, he bribed him. And he bribed: he took the bribe. And he was bribed in his judgment: he asked for a bribe from him. I said: The rulers today are the epitome of bribery, not the suspect, and there is no power or strength except with God! Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: That you may eat is in the accusative case with the lam of ki. “A group” means a piece and a portion, so He expressed the group as a piece and a part. The group is a piece of sheep that is an exception to most of them. It was said: There is an inversion in the speech, the meaning being that you may eat the wealth of a group of people. By sin means by injustice and transgression, and it was called a sin because the sin is related to its doer. And you know meaning the invalidity of that and its sin, and this is an exaggeration in boldness and disobedience. Eighth: The Sunnis agreed that whoever takes what is called money, whether little or much, is committing a sin by doing so, and that it is forbidden for him to take it. This is contrary to what Bishr ibn al-Mu'tamir and those who followed him from the Mu'tazilah, who said: The accountable person is not committing a sin except by taking two hundred dirhams, and he is not committing a sin without that. This is contrary to what Ibn al-Jubba'i said: He is committing a sin by taking ten dirhams, and he is not committing a sin without that. This is contrary to what Ibn al-Hudhayl said: He is committing a sin by taking five dirhams. This is contrary to what some of the Qadarites of Basra said: He is committing a sin by taking one dirham or more, and he is not committing a sin with less than that. All of this is rejected by the Qur'an and Sunnah and by the consensus of the scholars of this ummah. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Your blood, your property and your honor are sacred to you. Hadith, agreed upon as authentic.
2:189: It contains twelve issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: They ask you about the new moons. This is one of the things that the Jews asked about and objected to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with. Muadh said: O Messenger of God, the Jews visit us and ask us a lot about the crescent moons. Why does the crescent moon appear thin and then increase until it becomes straight and round, then decrease until it returns to how it was? So God revealed this verse. It was said that the reason for its revelation was that some Muslims asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the crescent moon and the reason for its disappearance and fullness and its difference from the state of the sun. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Qatada, al-Rabi’ and others. The second: The Almighty’s saying: About the new moons. New moons is the plural of crescent, and it is a plural and is one in reality in that it is one crescent in one month, not a crescent in another. Rather, he pluralized its states from the new moons. And by the new moons he means their months, and the new moon may be used to refer to the month because it occurs in it, as he said: Brothers from Najd, trustworthy as a nail clipping It was said: It was called a month because the hands point to the place of sighting and they indicate it. The term crescent is used for two nights at the end of the month, and two nights at the beginning. It was also said: For three nights at the beginning. Al-Asma’i said: It is a crescent until it becomes a stone and becomes round like a thin thread. It was also said: Rather, it is a crescent until it dazzles the sky with its light, and that is on the seventh night. Abu al-Abbas said: It was called a crescent because people raise their voices to announce it. From this, the boy begins to cry when his life appears with his screams. And his face begins to shine with joy and beams when happiness appears in it. Abu Kabir said: And if you look at his face, it will shine like the lightning of a cheerful star. It is said: We entered the crescent if we entered it. Al-Jawhari said: The crescent appeared and it appeared is for an unspecified agent. It is also said: It became clear meaning it became apparent, but it is not said: It appeared. It is said: We entered the crescent for such and such a night, but it is not said: We entered it, so it entered, as it is said: We entered it and it entered, and this is its analogy. Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahim al-Qushayri said in his interpretation: “It is said: “The crescent appeared” and We entered the crescent and We announced the crescent and We announced the crescent. Third: Our scholars said: If someone swears to pay his debtor or to do such and such on the crescent moon or at the beginning of the crescent moon or at the crescent moon, and he does that one or two days after seeing the crescent moon, he has not broken his oath. All months are suitable for all acts of worship and transactions, as follows. The Almighty’s saying: Say, ‘They are time limits for mankind and for Hajj.’ This is an explanation of the wisdom behind the waxing and waning of the moon, which is to remove confusion about terms, transactions, oaths, Hajj, numbers, fasting and breaking the fast, the duration of pregnancy, rents and leases, and other interests of the servants. Similar to this is the saying of the Truth: “And We have made the night and the day two signs, and We have erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible that you may seek bounty from your Lord and that you may know the number of years and account.” As will come. And His saying: It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and account. Counting the new moons is easier than counting the days. Fourth: With what we have decided, we respond to the people of the apparent meaning and those who said as they said: that musaqat is permissible for an unknown period of time, for unknown years. They argued that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a deal with the Jews regarding half of the crops and palm trees as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw fit without setting a time. There is no evidence for this, because he, peace be upon him, said to the Jews: He has confirmed you in it as long as God has confirmed you. This is the clearest evidence and the most obvious way that this was specific to him, so he was waiting for the judgment of his Lord in this matter, and no one else is like that. The Shari’ah has perfected the meanings of leases and all other transactions, so nothing of them is permissible except according to what the Qur’an and Sunnah have made clear, and what the scholars of the Ummah have said. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: set times. “set times” is the plural of set time, which means time. It was said: set time is the end of time. set times is not declined, because it is a plural that has no equivalent in singulars. It is a plural and the end of a plural, since it is not pluralized, so it is as if the plural is repeated in it. Qawarir was declined in His saying: Qawariran because it occurred at the beginning of a verse and was given a tanween like the rhymes, so it is not the tanween of inflection that indicates the presence of the noun. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And the Hajj with the opening of the Ha’ is the reading of the majority. Ibn Abi Ishaq read with the Kasra in the entire Qur’an, and in His saying: The Hajj of the House in Al Imran. Sibawayh: Hajj is like returning and tightening, and Hajj is like remembrance, so they are two sources with the same meaning. It was said: The opening is like the chest, and the Kasra is the name. Seventh: God Almighty singled out Hajj for mention because it is something that requires knowing the time, and it is not permissible to postpone it from its time, unlike what the Arabs saw, as they used to perform Hajj based on the number and change the months, so God invalidated their words and actions, as will be explained in Bara’ah, God willing. Eighth: Malik, may God have mercy on him, Abu Hanifa and their companions used this verse as evidence that entering ihram for Hajj is valid in months other than the months of Hajj, because God the Almighty made the new moons a time for that, so it is valid to enter ihram for Hajj in all of them. Al-Shafi’i disagreed with that, because God the Almighty said: Hajj is [during] well-known months, as will be mentioned. The meaning of this verse is that some of them are times for people and some of them are times for Hajj. This is like saying: The slave girl is for Zayd and Amr. This requires that some of them are for Zayd and some of them are for Amr. It is not permissible to say: All of them are for Zayd and all of them are for Amr. The answer is to say: The apparent meaning of His statement: They are times for people and Hajj requires that all of them are times for people and all of them are times for Hajj. If He had intended to make a distinction, He would have said: Some of them are times for people and some of them are times for Hajj. This is like saying: The month of Ramadan is a time for the fasting of Zayd and Amr. There is no disagreement that what is meant by that is that all of it is a time for the fasting of each of them. What they mentioned about the slave girl is correct, because it is impossible for her to be all for Zayd while she is all for Amr, and it is not like that in our question, because the time can be a time for Zayd and a time for Amr, so what they said is invalid. Ninth: There is no disagreement among scholars that whoever sells a known commodity for a known price for a known period of time in the Arab months or for a known number of days, the sale is permissible. They also said the same about the Salam sale for a known period. They differed about whoever sells for the harvest or for the threshing or for the giving and the like. Malik said: That is permissible because it is known, and Abu Thawr said the same. Ahmad said: I hope there is no harm in it. And the same is true for the arrival of the warriors. It was narrated from Ibn Umar that he used to buy for the giving. A group said: That is not permissible, because God the Almighty set the times and made them a sign for their terms in their sales and interests. Ibn Abbas said the same, and Al-Shafi’i and Al-Nu’man said the same. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The statement of Ibn Abbas is correct. Tenth: If the crescent is seen as large, our scholars say: It is not to be relied upon as large or small, but rather it is the date of its sighting. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu al-Bukhtari who said: We went out for Umrah, and when we stopped at Batn Nakhalah, he said: We saw the crescent. Some of the people said: It is three days old, and some of the people said: It is two nights old. He said: We met Ibn Abbas and said: We saw the crescent. Some of the people said: It is three days old, and some of the people said: It is two nights old. He said: Which night did you see it? We said: On such and such a night. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God extended its sighting, so it is the night you saw it. Eleventh: The Almighty’s saying: And righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs. This is connected to the mention of the times of Hajj, because the two issues coincided with the time of the question about the new moons and about entering houses from their backs, so the verse was revealed regarding both of them. When the Ansar performed Hajj and returned, they would not enter through the doors of their houses, because when they entered ihram for Hajj or Umrah, they were legally committed to not letting anything stand between them and the sky. So if a man of them went out after that, that is, after he entered ihram from his house, and returned for a need, he would not enter through the door of the room because the roof of the house would stand between him and the sky. So he would climb the roof of his house on the walls, then stand in his room and order what he needed to be done, and it would be brought out to him from his house. They considered this to be an act of worship and righteousness, just as they believed that some things were acts of worship, so He responded to them in this, and the Almighty Lord explained that righteousness is in obeying His command. Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Abu Saleh: “In the pre-Islamic era and in the beginning of Islam, if a man among them entered ihram for Hajj, if he was from the people of Madar - meaning from the people of the houses - he would dig a hole in the back of his house, from which he would enter and from which he would exit, or he would place a ladder to climb up and down. If he was from the people of the hair - meaning the people of the tents - he would enter the tent from behind the tents, except for those who were from the Hams.” Al-Zuhri narrated: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the state of Umrah at the time of Al-Hudaybiyah, and he entered his room, and an Ansari man from Banu Salamah entered behind him. He entered and broke the custom of his people, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Why did you enter when you had entered the state of Ihram? He said: You entered, and you entered with your entry. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: I am Ahmas, meaning from a people who do not believe in that. The man said to him: My religion is your religion,” so the verse was revealed, and Ibn Abbas, Ata’, and Qatadah said the same. It was said that this man was Qutbah ibn Amir Al-Ansari. Al-Hamas: Quraysh, Kinanah, Khuza'ah, Thaqif, Khatham, Banu Amir ibn Sa'sa'ah, and Banu al-Nadr ibn Mu'awiyah. They were called Al-Hamas because of their severity in their religion. Al-Hamasah means severity. Al-Ajjaj said: How many baskets of Hamas we cut Any strong ones. Then they differed in its interpretation, and it was said what we mentioned, and this is correct. And it was said: It is the postponement and delaying the Hajj with it, until they made the permissible month forbidden by delaying the Hajj to it, and the forbidden month permissible by delaying the Hajj from it, so the mention of the houses in this way is an example of violating the obligation in the Hajj and its months. The explanation of the postponement will come in Surat Bara’ah, God willing. Abu Ubaidah said: The verse is an example: The meaning is that righteousness is not that you ask the ignorant, but fear God and ask the scholars, so this is like saying: I came to this matter from its door. Al-Mahdawi and Makki narrated from Ibn Al-Anbari, and Al-Mawardi from Ibn Zaid that the verse is an example of intercourse with women, an order to come to them in the front, not the back. And women were called houses to shelter them like shelter in houses. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is far-fetched and changes the pattern of speech. Al-Hasan said: They used to take omens, so whoever traveled and did not get what he needed, would come to his house from behind his back, fearing disappointment. So it was said to them: There is no righteousness in taking omens, rather righteousness is to fear God and trust in Him. I said: The first statement is the most correct of these statements, because of what Al-Baraa narrated, saying: When the Ansar performed Hajj and returned, they did not enter houses through their doors. He said: Then a man from the Ansar came and entered through his door, and he was asked about that, so this verse was revealed: Righteousness is not that you enter houses from their backs. This is a clear text about houses in reality. It was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. As for those sayings, they are taken from another place, not from the verse, so reflect on it. It has been said that the verse was issued as a warning from God the Most High to approach righteousness from its direction, which is the direction that God the Most High commanded. So He mentioned entering houses through their doors as an example to indicate that we approach things from their source, which God the Most High urged us to do. I said: Accordingly, what was mentioned of the sayings is correct. And the houses are the plural of house, and it was read with the damma and kasra of the ba. The meaning of piety and success was mentioned previously, perhaps, so there is no point in repeating it. Twelfth: In this verse there is a statement that what God has not prescribed as an act of worship or recommended does not become an act of worship by someone drawing near to Him. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: If what is righteous and an act of worship is confused with what is not righteous and an act of worship, then that knowledge should be examined. If it has a counterpart in the obligatory and recommended acts, then it is permissible. If not, then it is neither righteousness nor an act of worship. He said: And this is what the reports from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came with. He mentioned the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: “While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was delivering a sermon, he saw a man standing in the sun. He asked about him and they said: ‘He is Abu Israel. He vowed to stand and not sit, not seek shade, not speak, and to fast.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Tell him to speak, seek shade, sit, and complete his fast.’” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, invalidated what was not an act of worship that had no basis in his Shari’ah, and he validated what was an act of worship that had a counterpart in the obligatory and recommended acts.
2:190: It contains three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Fight. This verse is the first verse revealed in the command to fight. There is no dispute that fighting was prohibited before the migration, as He said: Repel evil with that which is better, and His saying: Pardon them and overlook, and His saying: And leave them with gracious leave, and His saying: You have no control over them, and what was similar to it that was revealed in Mecca. Then when he migrated to Medina with the command to fight, the verse was revealed: And fight in the way of God those who fight you, as stated by Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas and others. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr As-Siddiq that the first verse revealed in fighting was: Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought because they have been wronged. The first is more, and that the verse of permission was revealed regarding fighting in general, for those who fought and those who did not fight from the polytheists. This is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with his companions to Mecca for the Umrah. When he arrived at Al-Hudaybiyah near Mecca - and Al-Hudaybiyah is the name of a well, so that place was named after that well - the polytheists prevented him from entering the House. He stayed at Al-Hudaybiyah for a month, so they made peace with him that he would return from that year as mentioned, on the condition that Mecca would be vacated for him in the coming year for three days. They made peace with him that there would be no fighting between them for ten years, and he returned to Medina. When the following year came, he prepared for the Umrah of Compensation, and the Muslims feared the treachery of the infidels and hated fighting in the Sacred Sanctuary and in the sacred month, so this verse was revealed, meaning that it is permissible for you to fight if the infidels fight you. So the verse is connected to what came before about the mention of Hajj and entering houses from their backs, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, would fight whoever fought him and refrain from whoever refrained from him, until kill the polytheists was revealed, so this verse was abrogated, as stated by a group of scholars. Ibn Zayd and Al-Rabi’ said: And fight the polytheists altogether abrogated it, so he ordered fighting all the infidels. Ibn Abbas, Umar ibn Abdul Aziz and Mujahid said: It is decisive, meaning fight those who are in the same situation as those who are fighting you, and do not transgress in killing women, children, monks and the like, as will be explained. Abu Ja’far Al-Nahhas said: This is the more correct of the two opinions in the Sunnah and reasoning. As for the Sunnah, it is the hadith of Ibn Umar: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a woman killed during one of his campaigns, and he disliked that, and he forbade the killing of women and children,” narrated by the Imams. As for looking, the doer is usually only two people, such as the fighter, the one who insults, and the one who quarrels. Fighting is not done with women or children and those like them, such as monks, the lame, the elderly, and the hired workers, so they are not killed. This is what Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, advised Yazid on behalf of Abu Sufyan when he sent him to the Levant, unless they were to cause harm. This was narrated by Malik and others. The scholars have six images regarding them: First: Women, if they fight, are killed. Sahnun said: In the case of fighting and afterwards, due to the generality of his statement: And fight in the way of God those who fight you, “And kill them wherever you overtake them.” Women have great effects in fighting, including providing money and inciting people to fight. They may go out with their hair disheveled, wailing, arousing and reproaching for fleeing, and that permits their killing. However, if they are captured, then slavery is more beneficial because of the speed with which they convert to Islam and return from their religions, and the difficulty of their escaping to their homelands, unlike men. Second: Boys are not to be killed because of the established prohibition against killing offspring, and because they are not responsible. If a boy kills a boy, he is to be killed. Third: Monks are not killed or enslaved, but they are left with what they can live on from their money, and this is if they are isolated from the infidels, according to what Abu Bakr said to Yazid: And you will find people who claim that they have dedicated themselves to God, so leave them to what they claim that they have dedicated themselves to, for if they are with the infidels in the churches, they will be killed. And if a woman becomes a nun, Ashhab narrated that she is not to be agitated. And Sahnun said: Monasticism does not change her ruling. Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: The correct narration in my opinion is Ashhab’s narration, because it falls under his statement: So leave them to what they have dedicated themselves to. Fourth: Temporal. Sahnun said: They are killed. Ibn Habib said: They are not killed. The correct thing is to consider their circumstances. If there is harm in them, they are killed. Otherwise, they are left as they are in the temporal state and become property and stuff as they are. Fifth: The elderly. Malik said in the book of Muhammad: They are not to be killed. The majority of jurists are of the opinion that if he is an old man who cannot fight, and is not of benefit in opinion or defense, then he is not to be killed. Malik and Abu Hanifa said the same. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions: One of them is like the opinion of the group. The second is that he and the monk are to be killed. The first is correct, based on the opinion of Abu Bakr to Yazid, and there is no one who disagrees with him, so it is proven that it is a consensus. Also, he is one of those who do not fight or help the enemy, so it is not permissible to kill him, like a woman. But if he is one of those whose harm is feared in war, opinion, or money, then if he is taken prisoner, the imam has a choice between five things: killing, favor, ransom, enslavement, or a dhimmi contract to pay the jizyah. Sixth: Al-Asfa, who are the hired workers and farmers. Malik said in the book of Muhammad: They are not to be killed. Al-Shafi’i said: The farmers, hired workers, and elderly people are to be killed unless they convert to Islam or pay the jizya. The first is more correct, because of what he, peace be upon him, said in the hadith of Rabah bin Al-Rabi’: Follow Khalid bin Al-Walid and do not kill children or farmers. Omar bin Al-Khattab said: Fear God in children and farmers who do not wage war against you. Omar bin Abdul Aziz did not kill a farmer, as mentioned by Ibn Al-Mundhir. Second: Ashhab narrated on the authority of Malik that what is meant by his saying: And fight in the way of God those who fight you are the people of Hudaybiyyah who were commanded to fight those who fought them. The correct view is that it is addressed to all Muslims, commanding everyone to fight whoever fights him because no one else is allowed to fight him. Do you not see how he explained it in Surat Bara’ah by saying: Fight those of the disbelievers who are near you? That is because the people of Mecca were intended first, so it was necessary to start with them. Then when God conquered Mecca, the fighting was for whoever was near from those who were causing harm until the call became widespread and the word reached all horizons and no one of the disbelievers remained. This will continue until the Day of Resurrection, extending to an end which is his saying, peace be upon him: Horses have goodness tied to their forelocks until the Day of Resurrection, reward and spoils. It was said: Its ultimate goal is the descent of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, and it is in agreement with the hadith before it, because his descent is one of the signs of the Hour. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And do not transgress. It was said in its interpretation what we have presented, so it is decisive. As for the apostates, there is nothing but killing or repentance, and likewise the people of deviation and misguidance, there is nothing but the sword or repentance. And whoever is kept in false belief and then becomes apparent upon it, he is like a heretic who is killed and not given the opportunity to repent. As for the Khawarij against the Imams of justice, they must be fought until they return to the truth. A group said: The meaning is do not transgress in fighting for the sake of God, such as zeal and gaining fame, but fight in the way of God those who fight you, meaning religion and to make the word manifest. It was said: Do not transgress, meaning do not fight those who do not fight. Based on this, the verse is abrogated by the command to fight all the infidels, and God knows best.
2:191: God Almighty said: “And kill them wherever you overtake them and expel them from where they expelled you. And persecution is worse than killing. And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.”
2:192: God Almighty says: But if they desist, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. There are five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: You have gained control of them. It is said: Thaqafah yathaqafan thaqfan and Thaqafah man means he is well-versed in the matters he undertakes. This is evidence for killing the captive, and this will be explained in Al-Anfal, God willing. And expel them from where they expelled you, meaning Mecca. Al-Tabari said: The addressee is the Muhajireen, and the pronoun refers to the infidels of Quraysh. Second: The Almighty’s statement: And persecution is worse than killing. That is, the persecution that they forced you to commit and sought to make you return to disbelief is worse than killing. Mujahid said: That is, than killing a believer, so killing is easier for him than persecution. Another said: That is, their associating partners with God and their disbelief in Him is a greater crime and worse than the killing with which they reproached you. This is evidence that the verse was revealed concerning Amr ibn al-Hadrami when he was killed by Waqid ibn Abdullah al-Tamimi on the last day of Rajab, the sacred month, according to what is mentioned in the expedition of Abdullah ibn Jahsh, as will be explained, as stated by al-Tabari and others. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you there (al-Baqarah 2:170). Scholars have two opinions on this verse: One of them is that it was abrogated, and the second is that it is decisive. Mujahid said: The verse is decisive, and it is not permissible to fight anyone in al-Masjid al-Haram except after he fights, and Tawus said the same, and it is what the text of the verse requires, and it is the correct of the two opinions, and Abu Hanifa and his companions went with it. In Sahih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: “This city was made sacred by God on the day He created the heavens and the earth, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection. Fighting in it was not permitted for anyone before me, and it was not permitted for me except for an hour of the day, so it is sacred by the sanctity of God until the Day of Resurrection.” Qatada said: The verse was abrogated by the words of God the Almighty: So when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. Muqatil said: It was abrogated by the words of God the Almighty: And kill them wherever you find them. Then this was abrogated by the words: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. So it is permissible to initiate fighting in the sanctuary. Among the evidence they used as evidence is that Surat al-Bara’ah was revealed two years after Surat al-Baqarah, and that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) entered Mecca wearing a helmet, and it was said that Ibn Khatal was clinging to the curtains of the Kaaba, so he said: Kill him. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque is abrogated, because the consensus has been established that if an enemy took control of Mecca and said: I will fight you, and prevent you from performing Hajj, and I will not leave Mecca, then it is obligatory to fight him even if he did not initiate the fighting. Mecca and other lands are the same. It was only said about it: It is sacred, to magnify it. Do you not see that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid bin Al-Walid on the day of the conquest, and he said: I will harvest them with the sword until you meet me on Al-Safa, until Al-Abbas came and said: O Messenger of God, Quraysh has gone, so there is no Quraysh after today. Do you not see that he said in glorifying them: None shall pick up its lost property except one who announces it, and the lost property is the same with it or without it. It is permissible that it was abrogated by the saying: And fight them until there is no more persecution. Ibn al-Arabi said: I was present in Jerusalem - may God purify it - in the school of Abu Uqba al-Hanafi, and the judge al-Zanjani was giving us a lesson on a Friday. While we were there, a handsome man entered upon us, wearing a cloak on his back. He greeted us like a scholar and took his place in the front of the gathering wearing the robes of a shepherd. The judge al-Zanjani said: Who is the master? He said: “A man who was robbed by the clever ones yesterday. My destination was this holy sanctuary, and I am a man from the people of Sagan, a seeker of knowledge.” The judge said quickly: Ask him - as is the custom in honoring scholars by taking the initiative to ask them questions - and the lot fell on the question of the infidel who seeks refuge in the sanctuary, should he be killed or not? He issued a fatwa that he should not be killed. He was asked about the evidence, and he said: The words of God the Almighty: And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram until they fight you therein were read as Do not kill them and Do not fight them. If it was read as Do not kill them, then the issue is a text, and if it was read as Do not fight them, then it is a warning, because if it forbids fighting, which is the cause of killing, then it is clear and apparent evidence of the prohibition of killing. The judge objected to him, defending al-Shafi’i and Malik, even though he did not share their school of thought, as is the custom, and he said: This verse is abrogated by the words of God the Almighty: Then kill the polytheists wherever they may be. Al-Saghani said to him: This is not befitting of the position of the judge and his knowledge, because this verse that you objected to is general in places, and the one you used as evidence is specific, and it is not permissible for anyone to say that the general abrogates the specific. Judge al-Zanjani was dumbfounded, and this is one of the strangest of words. Ibn al-Arabi said: If a disbeliever resorts to it, then there is no way to do so, because of the text of the verse and the established Sunnah that forbid fighting therein. As for the adulterer and the murderer, the punishment must be carried out on him, unless the infidel starts the killing, in which case he is killed according to the text of the Qur’an. I said: As for what they used as evidence of killing Ibn Khatal and his companions during a Hajj, that was at the time when Mecca was made permissible for him, and it was a land of war and disbelief, and he had the right to shed the blood of whomever he wanted from its people at the time when fighting was made permissible for him. So it is proven and correct that the first statement is more correct, and God knows best. Fourth: Some scholars said: This verse is evidence that the one who rebels against the ruler is different from the infidel. The infidel is killed if he fights in any case, and the rebel if he fights fights with the intention of repelling. He does not pursue a fleeing person nor finish off a wounded person, as will be explained in the rulings on rebels in Al-Hujurat, God willing. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: If they desist meaning from fighting you by faith, then God will forgive them all that has happened before, and will have mercy on each of them by pardoning what they have committed. Similar to His saying: Say to those who have disbelieved, if they desist, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them. And it will come.
2:193: God Almighty says: “And fight them until there is no more persecution and religion is for God. But if they cease, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers.” There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: And fight them is a command to fight every polytheist in every place, for those who see it as abrogating. And those who see it as not abrogating say: The meaning is fight those about whom God said: If they fight you, and the first is more apparent, and it is a command to fight absolutely, not on condition that the infidels initiate. The evidence for that is the Almighty’s statement: And religion will be for God, and he, peace be upon him, said: I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ The verse and the hadith indicate that the reason for fighting is disbelief, because He said, until there is no more fitnah, meaning disbelief, so He made the goal the absence of disbelief, and this is clear. Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Ar-Rabi’, As-Suddi and others said: Fitnah there is polytheism and the harm that accompanies it to the believers. The root of fitnah is testing and examining, taken from the word fitna testing of silver, meaning to put it in the fire to distinguish its bad from its good. The explanation of its meanings will come, God willing. Second: The Almighty’s statement: If they desist meaning from disbelief, either by Islam as mentioned in the previous verse, or by paying the jizyah for the People of the Book, as will be explained in Bara’ah. Otherwise, they will be fought, and they are the wrongdoers, and there is no aggression except against them. What is done to the wrongdoers is called aggression because it is the recompense for aggression, since injustice includes aggression, so the recompense for aggression is called aggression, like His statement: And the recompense for an evil act is an evil act like it. The wrongdoers, according to one of the two interpretations, are those who initiate fighting, and according to the other interpretation, those who remain in disbelief and strife.
2:194: It contains ten issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: The sacred month. The derivation of the word month has already been mentioned. The reason for its revelation is what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Mujahid, Muqsim, As-Suddi, Ar-Rabi’, Ad-Dahhak and others. They said: It was revealed in the Umrah of Al-Qadiyah and the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah. That is because the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) went out to perform Umrah until he reached Al-Hudaybiyyah in Dhul-Qa’dah of the year six. The polytheists, the infidels of Quraysh, prevented him from entering the House, so he turned back. God, the Almighty, promised him that he would enter it, so he entered it in the year seven and completed his rituals, so this verse was revealed. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that “the polytheists said to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): Have you forbidden fighting, O Muhammad, in the sacred month? He said: Yes. So they wanted to fight him, so the verse was revealed.” The meaning is: If they consider that permissible in it, then fight them. God permitted by the verse to defend themselves against them. The first opinion is more famous and most agree with it. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And the sacred things are retaliation. Sanctities is the plural of sanctity, just as darkness is the plural of darkness, and rooms is the plural of room. The sanctities were pluralized because He meant the sanctity of the sacred month, the sanctity of the sacred city, and the sanctity of ihram. Sanctity is that which is forbidden from being violated. And retaliation is equality, meaning I exacted retribution for you from them when they turned you back in the year six, so you completed the Umrah in the year seven. So and the sacred things are retaliation according to this is connected to what came before it and related to it. It was said: It is severed from it. It is the beginning of a command that was in the beginning of Islam: Whoever violates your sanctity, you will take from him the same as he assaulted you. Then that was abrogated by fighting. A group said: What the verse includes of transgression between the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and crimes and the like, has not been abrogated, and it is permissible for someone who transgressed against him in money or injury to transgress in the same way that he transgressed against him if that was hidden from him, and there is nothing between him and God Almighty in that, as Al-Shafi’i and others said, and it is a narration in the Maliki school. A group of Maliki’s companions said: He does not have that, and matters of retaliation are left to the rulings. Money is covered by his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Return the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you. Narrated by Al-Daraqutni and others. So the one who was entrusted by the one who betrayed him is not permitted to betray him and take his right from what was entrusted to him. This is the well-known opinion of the school of thought, and Abu Hanifa said the same, adhering to this hadith and the statement of God the Almighty: Indeed, God commands you to render trusts to those to whom they are due. This is the opinion of Ata’ Al-Khurasani. Qudamah bin Al-Haitham said: I asked Ata’ bin Maysarah Al-Khurasani and said to him: I have a right over a man, and he has denied it to me and I have failed to produce evidence. Should I take revenge from his money? He said: What if he had intercourse with your slave girl, and you knew what you would have done? I said: The correct view is that it is permissible to do so, however one takes his right, as long as he is not considered a thief. This is the view of al-Shafi’i, and al-Dawudi narrated it from Malik. Ibn al-Mundhir said the same, and Ibn al-Arabi chose it. This is not treachery, but rather it is taking one’s right. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Support your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. Taking the right from an oppressor is support for him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Hind bint ‘Utbah, the wife of Abu Sufyan, when she said to him: “Abu Sufyan is a stingy man. He does not give me enough money to suffice me and my children, except for what I take from his money without his knowledge. Is there any sin on me?” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Take what suffices you and your children in a reasonable manner. So he permitted her to take and not to take more than the amount that is due to her. All of this is proven in the Saheeh. The saying of God the Most High: But whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you. is decisive in the matter of disagreement. Third: They differed if he finds money that is not of the same type as his money. It was said: He should not take it except by the judge’s ruling. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions, the most correct of which is to take it, by analogy to if he finds the same type of money as his. The second opinion is that he should not take it because it is of the opposite type. Some of them said: He should investigate the value of what he owes him and take that amount. This is the correct opinion based on the evidence we have explained, and God knows best. Fourth: If we base it on taking, is what he owes of debts and other things taken into consideration? Al-Shafi’i said: No, rather his money is taken from him. Malik said: What he obtains with the creditors in terms of bankruptcy is taken into consideration, and this is analogy, and God knows best. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: But whoever has transgressed against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you. This is an agreed-upon generality, either directly if possible, or by judges. People differed as to whether retaliation is called aggression or not. Those who said: There is no metaphor in the Qur’an said: Reciprocity is aggression, and it is permissible aggression, just as metaphor in the speech of the Arabs is permissible lying, as in the saying of the one who said: The eyes said to him, I hear and obey. And also: The basin was full and my cotton said And also: My camel complained to me about the long journey It is known that these things do not speak. The definition of lying is: reporting something in a way that is different from what it is. Whoever says that there is metaphor in the Qur’an called this an aggression against the path of metaphor and the confrontation of speech with something similar, as Amr ibn Kulthum said: Let no one be ignorant of us, lest we become more ignorant than the ignorant. The other said: I have a horse bridled with dreams, I have a horse saddled with ignorance, I have a horse bridled with ignorance Whoever seeks to straighten me, I will be straight, and whoever seeks to make me crooked, I will be crooked. He means: I reward the ignorant and the crooked, not that he was praised for his ignorance and crookedness. Sixth: The scholars differed regarding someone who consumed or spoiled an animal or merchandise that cannot be measured or weighed. Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, their companions, and a group of scholars said: He must pay the equivalent in that regard, and the value is not to be changed except when there is no equivalent, based on the Almighty’s statement: But whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you and His statement: And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were punished. They said: This is general in all things, and they supported this by the fact that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept the broken bowl in the house of the woman who broke it and gave away the healthy bowl and said: A vessel for a vessel and food for food. Narrated by Abu Dawud. He said: Musaddad told us, Yahya told us, and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, Khalid told us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was with one of his wives, and one of the mothers of the believers sent a servant with a bowl of food. He said: She struck it with her hand and broke the bowl. Ibn al-Muthanna said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took the two pieces of food and put one of them together, and began to gather the food in them and say: Your mother is jealous.” Ibn al-Muthanna added: Eat. So they ate until they came to her bowl that was in her house. Then we returned to the wording of the hadith of Musaddad, and he said: Eat. And the Messenger and the bowl were kept until they finished, so he gave the intact bowl to the Messenger and kept the broken one in his house. Abu Dawud told us: Musaddad told us, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, and Falit al-Amiri told us - Abu Dawud said: He is Aflat ibn Khalifa - on the authority of Jasra bint Dajajah, who said: Aisha may God be pleased with her said: “I have never seen a maker of food like Safiyyah. She made food for the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and sent it. I started eating and broke the vessel. I said: O Messenger of God, what is the expiation for what I have done? He said: A vessel like a vessel and food like food.” Malik and his companions said: In animals and goods that are not measured or weighed, the value is required, not the equivalent, as evidenced by the fact that the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) who freed half of his slave was responsible for the value of his partner’s half, and he did not compensate him for the equivalent of half of his slave. There is no disagreement among scholars about compensating for the equivalent in foods, drinks and weighed goods, as the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: Food for food. Seventh: There is no disagreement among scholars that this verse is the basis for similarity in retaliation. So whoever kills with something is to be killed in the same way he killed with, and this is the opinion of the majority, unless he kills with an act of immorality such as sodomy or drinking alcohol, in which case he is to be killed with the sword. The Shafi’is say that he is to be killed with that, so a stick is made in that manner and stabbed in his anus until he dies, and he is to be given water instead of alcohol until he dies. Ibn al-Majishun said: Whoever kills with fire or poison is not to be killed with it, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: None punishes with fire except God. Poison is an internal fire. The majority of scholars are of the view that it kills people because of the general meaning of the verse. Eighth: As for retaliation with a stick, Malik said in one of the two narrations: If killing with a stick involves prolongation and torture, he is to be killed with the sword. This was narrated by Ibn Wahb and said by Ibn al-Qasim. In the other narration: He is to be killed with it even if that is the case, and this is the opinion of al-Shafi’i. Ashhab and Ibn Nafi’ narrated from Malik regarding stones and sticks that he is to be killed with them if the blow is prepared, but if he strikes blows, then no. Accordingly, he is not to be shot with arrows or stones because it is torture, and this was said by Abd al-Malik. Ibn al-Arabi said: The correct opinion of our scholars is that retaliation is obligatory, unless it falls under the category of torture, in which case it should be left to the sword. Our scholars agreed that if he cuts off his hand and foot and puts out his eye with the intention of torture, this is to be done to him, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did when he killed the shepherds. If it was in self-defense or fighting, he is to be killed with the sword. A group went against all of this and said: There is no retaliation except with the sword, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifa, al-Sha’bi, and al-Nakha’i. They supported this with what was narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: There is no retaliation except with iron, and the prohibition of mutilation, and his saying: None punishes with fire except the Lord of the Fire. The correct view is that of the majority, based on what the imams narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik: A slave girl's head was found crushed between two stones. They asked her: Who did this to you? So-and-so, so-and-so? Until they mentioned a Jew. She nodded her head. The Jew was taken and he confessed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that his head be crushed with stones. In another narration: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed him between two stones. This is a clear and correct text, and it is required by the words of God the Almighty: And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were punished and His words: Then transgress against him in the same way that he transgressed against you. As for what they used as evidence from the hadith of Jabir, it is a weak hadith according to the hadith scholars, and it is not narrated via a sound chain of transmission. If it were sound, we would say according to its basis, and that if someone kills with an iron object, he is killed with it. This is indicated by the hadith of Anas: A Jew crushed the head of a slave girl between two stones, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, crushed his head between two stones. As for the prohibition of mutilation, we also say according to its basis if he did not mutilate. So if we mutilate him, this is indicated by the hadith: Al-Arniyyin, and it is authentic and was reported by the Imams. His statement: None punishes with fire except the Lord of the Fire is authentic if he is not burned. If he is burned, he is burned, as indicated by the general meaning of the Qur’an. Al-Shafi’i said: If he is thrown into the fire intentionally, he is thrown into the fire until he dies. Al-Waqar mentioned it in his Mukhtasar on the authority of Malik, and it is the statement of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hakam. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The statement of many of the people of knowledge regarding a man who strangles another is: He must be subject to retaliation. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan disagreed with that and said: If he strangled him until he died or threw him into a well and he died, or threw him from a mountain or roof and he died, there is no retaliation on him and the blood money is on his family. If he was known for that - he strangled more than one person - then he must be killed. Ibn al-Mundhir said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed retaliation against the Jew who crushed the head of a slave girl with a stone, this was in its meaning, so his statement has no meaning. I said: This statement was narrated by someone else on the authority of Abu Hanifa, who said: Abu Hanifa has made it very strict and said about someone who is killed by strangulation, poison, being thrown from a mountain or well, or with a piece of wood: He is not to be killed and no retaliation is to be taken from him, unless he is killed with a sharp object: iron, stone, or wood, or he is known for strangulation and being thrown, and the blood money is to be paid by his family. This is a rejection of the Book and the Sunnah, and an innovation that was not the order of the nation, and a pretext to lift the retaliation that God has prescribed for souls, so there is no escape from it. Ninth: They differed about someone who imprisons a man and another kills him. Ata’ said: The killer is to be killed and the one who imprisons him is to be imprisoned until he dies. Malik said: If he imprisons him and he thinks that he wants to kill him all together, according to the statement of Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr and Al-Nu’man, the one who imprisons him is to be punished. Ibn Al-Mundhir chose this. I said: The statement of Ata’ is correct, and it is what the revelation requires. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a man catches another man and another man kills him, the killer is to be killed and the one who caught him is to be imprisoned. Narrated by Sufyan al-Thawri on the authority of Ismail ibn Umayya on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar. It was narrated by Muammar and Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ismail as a mursal. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: But whoever transgresses. Transgression is overstepping. God the Almighty said: And whoever transgresses the limits of God, meaning he exceeds them. So whoever wrongs you, take your right from him in proportion to your injustice. And whoever insults you, respond to him in kind. And whoever takes your honor, take his honor. Do not transgress against his parents, his son, or his relative. And you do not have the right to lie to him even if he lies to you, because sin is not met with sin. So if he says to you, for example: O disbeliever, it is permissible for you to say to him: You are the disbeliever. And if he says to you: O adulterer, then your retribution is to say to him: O liar, O false witness. And if you say to him: O adulterer, then you are a liar and have sinned in lying. And if he delays your divorce while he is rich without an excuse and says: O oppressor, O devourer of people’s wealth, the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: He who has it, his honor and punishment are lawful. As for his honor, it is as we have explained, and as for his punishment, it is imprisonment in which he is detained. Ibn Abbas said: This was revealed before Islam became strong, so it ordered whoever among the Muslims was harmed to be punished in kind, or to be patient or to forgive, then that was abrogated by His statement: And fight the polytheists altogether. It was said: That was abrogated by making it the responsibility of the ruler. It is not permissible for anyone to take revenge on anyone except with the permission of the ruler.
2:195: There are three issues: First: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah: And spend in the way of God and do not throw [yourselves] with your [own] hands into destruction. He said: It was revealed about spending. Yazid bin Abi Habib narrated on the authority of Aslam Abi Imran who said: We invaded Constantinople, and Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Walid was in charge of the group, and the Romans had their backs to the city wall. A man charged at the enemy, and the people said: Stop, stop, there is no god but God, he is throwing himself into destruction! Abu Ayyub said: Glory be to God! This verse was revealed about us as companions of the Ansar when God aided His Prophet and made His religion prevail. We said: Come, let us stay and improve our wealth. Then God the Almighty revealed: And spend in the cause of God 1:13. Throwing one’s hand into destruction means staying with our wealth and improving it, and abandoning jihad. Abu Ayyub continued to strive in the cause of God until he was buried in Constantinople, and his grave is there. Abu Ayyub informed us that throwing one’s hand into destruction means abandoning jihad in the cause of God, and that the verse was revealed about that. A similar verse was narrated from Hudhayfah, al-Hasan, Qatadah, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak. I said: Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib on the authority of Aslam Abi Imran this report with the same meaning. He said: We were in the city of the Romans, and they brought out to us a large column of the Romans. A similar number of Muslims or more came out to them, and Uqbah bin Amir was in charge of the people of Egypt, and Fadalah bin Ubaid was in charge of the group. A man from the Muslims charged the column of the Romans until he entered them. The people shouted and said: Glory be to God! He is throwing himself into destruction. Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari stood up and said: O people, you interpret this verse in this way. This verse was revealed about us, the Ansar, when God made Islam victorious and its supporters increased. Some of us said to one another secretly, without the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him): Our wealth has been lost, and God has made Islam victorious and its supporters increased. If we stay with our wealth and repair what has been lost from it, then God revealed to His Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in response to what we had said: And spend in the way of God and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction. So the destruction was staying with the money and fixing it and we left the conquest, so Abu Ayyub continued to go out in the way of God until he was buried in the land of the Romans. Abu Eisa said: This is a good, strange and authentic hadith. Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Ata’, Mujahid and the majority of people said: The meaning is do not throw yourselves into destruction by abandoning spending in the way of God and fearing poverty, so a man says: I have nothing to spend. Al-Bukhari went to this meaning as he did not mention anything else, and God knows best. Ibn Abbas said: Spend in the way of God, even if you have nothing but an arrow or a spear, and let none of you say: I have nothing. And something similar was narrated from al-Suddi: Spend even a hobble, and do not throw yourselves into destruction and say: I have nothing. And a third statement was made by Ibn Abbas, and that is that when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) ordered the people to go out for jihad, some Bedouins present in Madinah stood up to him and said: What should we prepare ourselves for? By God, we have no provisions and no one feeds us. Then the words of God the Most High were revealed: And spend in the cause of God meaning, O people of means, give charity in the cause of God, meaning in obedience to God. And do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction meaning, do not withhold your hands from charity or you will perish. This is what Muqatil said. The meaning of Ibn Abbas’s statement: And do not withhold charity or you will perish is, do not withhold spending on the weak, for if they stay behind you, the enemy will overcome you and you will perish. A fourth statement: It was said to Al-Bara’ bin Azib about this verse: Is it the man who attacks the battalion? He said, “No, but it is the man who commits a sin and throws his hands up and says, ‘I have gone too far in sin and there is no benefit in repentance.’ So he despairs of God and then indulges in sins. So destruction is despair of God, and this is what Ubaidah Al-Salmani said. Zayd ibn Aslam said: The meaning is do not travel in jihad without provisions. Some people did that and it led to them being cut off on the road, or becoming a burden on people. So there are five opinions. The path of God here is jihad, and the wording includes all of His paths. The letter ba in bi yadikumus is redundant, meaning throw your hands. Similar to it is: “Does he not know that God sees?” Al-Mubarrad said: bi yadikumus means with yourselves, so he used some to refer to all, like his saying: Because of what your hands have earned, “Because of what your hands have put forth.” It was said: This is a proverb, you say: So-and-so threw his hand in such-and-such a matter if he surrendered, because the one who surrenders in battle throws his weapon with his hands, so this is the action of every helpless person in any action, and from this is the saying of Abdul Muttalib: By God, throwing our hands to death is helplessness. Some people said: The meaning is do not throw yourselves with your hands, as you say: Do not spoil your situation with your opinion. And destruction with a damma on the lam is a verbal noun from the verb ḥalaka yahliku ḥalak wa ḥalak wa ḥalaka, meaning do not spend in that which will destroy you, as stated by al-Zajjaj and others. That is, if you do not spend, you will disobey God and be destroyed. It was said that the meaning of the verse is do not hold on to your wealth lest someone else inherits it from you, and you will be destroyed by being deprived of the benefit of your wealth. Another meaning is: do not hold on, lest your successors in this world and your reward in the hereafter be lost. It is said, And do not throw yourselves into destruction, meaning do not spend from what is forbidden, lest it be returned to you and you will be destroyed. A similar version was narrated from Ikrimah, who said, And do not throw yourselves into destruction, and he said, And do not aim toward the bad of it, spending. At-Tabari said, “His statement, and do not throw yourselves into destruction is general in all that was mentioned, because it is included in it, as the wording includes it. Second: The scholars differed regarding a man charging into war and attacking the enemy alone. Al-Qasim bin Mukhaymara, Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, and Abdul-Malik, among our scholars, said: There is nothing wrong with a man charging alone against a large army if he has the strength and his intention is purely for God. If he does not have the strength, then that is a form of destruction. It was said: If he seeks martyrdom and his intention is pure, then he should charge, because his goal is one of them, and that is clear in the words of God the Almighty: “And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God.” Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: As for a man charging against a hundred or against the entire army or a group of thieves, warriors, and Khawarij, then there are two cases for that: If he knows and is convinced that the one he charges against will be killed and he will escape, then that is good. Likewise, if he knows and is convinced that he will be killed but will be severely injured or worn out or have an effect that will benefit the Muslims, then that is also permissible. It has been reported to me that when the Muslim army met the Persians, the Muslims' horses were frightened by the elephants. So one of them made an elephant out of clay and Anas bin Malik surrounded his horse until he tamed it. When morning came, his horse was not frightened by the elephant, so he charged the elephant that was leading it. It was said to him: He is your killer. He said: There is no harm in me being killed and the Muslims being victorious. Likewise on the day of Yamamah, when Banu Hanifa fortified themselves in the garden, a Muslim man said: Put me in the box and throw me to them. So they did and he fought them alone and opened the door. I said: And from this is what was narrated: “A man said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘What do you think if I am killed in the cause of God, patiently and seeking reward?’ He said: ‘You will have Paradise.’ So he plunged into the enemy until he was killed.” In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was singled out on the day of Uhud with seven of the Ansar and two men from Quraysh. When they overwhelmed him, he said: ‘Whoever repels them from us will have Paradise or he will be my companion in Paradise.’ So one of the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. Then they overwhelmed him again, and he said: ‘Whoever repels them from us will have Paradise or he will be my companion in Paradise.’ So one of the Ansar stepped forward and fought until he was killed. He continued like that until the seven were killed, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘We did not treat our companions fairly.’” This is how the narration is: We treated our companions fairly with a sukoon on the fa’ and a fatha on the ba’, meaning we did not lead them to fight until they were killed. It was narrated with a fatha on the fa’ and a fatha on the ba’, and its meaning is that it refers to whoever of his companions fled from him, and God knows best. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: If one man attacks a thousand men of the polytheists while he is alone, there is no harm in that if he hopes to escape or harm the enemy, but if that is not the case, then it is disliked, because he exposed himself to destruction without benefit to the Muslims. If his intention was to reward the Muslims for doing the same as he did, then it is not far-fetched to permit it, because it benefits the Muslims in some ways. If his intention was to terrorize the enemy and to teach the Muslims the steadfastness of religion, then it is not far-fetched to permit it. If it benefits the Muslims and he sacrifices himself to glorify the religion of God and weaken disbelief, then this is the noble status for which God praised the believers in His statement: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives (al-Baqarah 2:17), and other verses of praise in which God praised the one who sacrifices himself. Based on this, the ruling on enjoining good and forbidding evil should be that whenever he hopes to benefit from religion and sacrifices himself for it until he is killed, he is in the highest ranks of martyrs. God the Most High said: “And enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination.” Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The best of martyrs is Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib and a man who spoke a word of truth to an unjust ruler and was killed. This will be discussed in the chapter on the family of Amr, God willing. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And do good meaning in spending in obedience, and have good thoughts about God in His failure to fulfill His promise to you. It was said: And do good in your actions by complying with acts of obedience. This was narrated from some of the Companions.
2:196: The Almighty’s saying: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God contains seven issues: First: The scholars differed regarding the meaning of completing Hajj and Umrah for God. It was said: Performing them and coming with them, like His statement: Then complete them and His statement: Then complete the fast until night meaning come with the fast. This is according to the opinion of those who made Umrah obligatory, as will come. And those who did not make it obligatory said: What is meant is completing them after starting them, because whoever enters ihram enters ihram for a ritual that he must continue with and not break. Al-Sha’bi and Ibn Zayd said its meaning. And on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: Completing them means entering ihram for them from the circle of your family. This was narrated on the authority of ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab and Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, and ‘Imran ibn Husayn did it. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Completing them means going out intending them, not for trade or anything else. This is strengthened by His statement for God. And ‘Umar said: Completing them means doing each one of them separately, without tamattu’ or qiran, and Ibn Habib said the same. Muqatil said: Completing them means that you do not make permissible in them what is not appropriate for you. This is because they used to associate partners in their ihram, saying: “Here I am, O God, here I am. You have no partner except a partner who is Yours, whom You own and what He owns.” So he said: Complete them and do not mix them with anything else.
