I said: As for what was narrated on the authority of Ali and what Imran bin Husayn did in entering ihram before the miqats that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set, Abdullah bin Masoud and a group of the Salaf said this, and it was proven that Umar entered ihram from Ilya, and Al-Aswad, Alqamah, Abd al-Rahman and Abu Ishaq entered ihram from their homes, and al-Shafi’i permitted it. Abu Dawud and al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever enters ihram from Jerusalem for Hajj or Umrah, his sins will be as if they were on the day his mother bore him. In another narration, His past and future sins will be forgiven. It was narrated by Abu Dawud who said: May God have mercy on Wakee’! He entered ihram from Jerusalem, meaning to Mecca. This indicates that entering ihram before the miqat is permissible. Malik, may God have mercy on him, disliked anyone entering ihram before the miqat. This was narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, who denounced Imran ibn Husayn for entering ihram from Basra. Uthman denounced Abdullah ibn Amir for entering ihram before the miqat. Ahmad and Ishaq said: The basis of the action is the miqats, and the evidence for this statement is that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set the miqats and specified them, so they became a clarification of the entirety of the Hajj. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not enter ihram from his house for his Hajj, rather he entered ihram from the miqat that he set for his ummah, and what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did is preferable, God willing. This is what the majority of the Companions and the Followers after them did. The people of the first article argued that this is better, based on the words of Aisha: Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given a choice between two matters, he chose the easier of the two. This is based on the hadith of Umm Salamah, along with what was mentioned about the Companions in this regard. They witnessed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entering ihram during his pilgrimage from his miqat, and they knew its purpose and outcome, and they knew that his entering ihram from his miqat was a facilitation for his nation. Second: The Imams narrated: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) specified Dhu’l-Hulayfah for the people of Madinah, al-Juhfah for the people of Ash-Sham, Qarn for the people of Najd, and Yalamlam for the people of Yemen. These are for them and for those who come to them from outside their people who want to perform Hajj or Umrah. And whoever is less than that, then he should start from wherever he starts, even the people of Makkah enter ihram from Makkah. The scholars agreed on the apparent meaning of this hadith and its use, and they do not contradict any of it. They differed regarding the miqat of the people of Iraq and who specified it. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, set the time for the people of the East at Al-Aqiq. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good hadith. It was narrated that Umar set the time for the people of Iraq at Dhat Irq. In the book of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Aisha: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) set the time for the people of Iraq at Dhat Irq, and this is the correct view. Whoever narrated that Umar set the time because Iraq was conquered during his time, was negligent on his part. Rather, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) set the time for it as he set the time for the people of Ash-Sham at Al-Juhfah. At that time, all of Ash-Sham was a land of unbelief, just as Iraq and other countries were at that time. Iraq and Ash-Sham were not conquered except during the time of Umar, and there is no disagreement among the scholars of the biography about this. Abu Umar said: Every Iraqi or Easterner who enters ihram from Dhat Irq has entered ihram from his miqat, according to everyone. Al-Aqeeq is more cautious and more appropriate than Dhat Irq, and Dhat Irq is also their miqat by consensus. Third: The scholars have agreed that whoever enters ihram before arriving at the miqat is in a state of ihram. This was only prohibited by those who saw entering ihram at the miqat as better, out of aversion to making things difficult for oneself when God has made them easy, and to expose oneself to something that one cannot be certain of doing during one’s ihram. All of them required him to enter ihram if he did that, because he increased and did not decrease it. Fourth: This verse is evidence of the obligation of Umrah, because God the Almighty ordered its completion as He ordered the completion of Hajj. Al-Sabi bin Ma’bad said: I came to Omar may God be pleased with him and said: I was a Christian and I converted to Islam, and I found that Hajj and Umrah were prescribed for me, and I entered into ihram for both of them. Omar said to him: You are guided to the Sunnah of your Prophet. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: He did not object to his saying: I found Hajj and Umrah prescribed for me. Ali bin Abi Talib, Ibn Omar, and Ibn Abbas said that they were obligatory. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj that Nafi’ informed me that Abdullah bin Omar used to say: There is no one among God’s creation who does not have to perform Hajj and Umrah, and they are obligatory for whoever is able to do so. Whoever does more after that, it is better and voluntary. He said: I did not hear him say anything about the people of Mecca. Ibn Jurayj said: I was informed on the authority of Ikrimah that Ibn Abbas said: Umrah is obligatory like Hajj is obligatory for whoever is able to do so. Among those who considered it obligatory from the followers were Ata’, Tawus, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Al-Sha’bi, Sa’id Ibn Jubayr, Abu Burdah, Masruq, Abdullah Ibn Shaddad, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Ubaid Ibn Al-Jahm from the Malikis. Al-Thawri said: We heard that it is obligatory. Zaid Ibn Thabit was asked about Umrah before Hajj, and he said: Two prayers, and it does not matter which one you start with. Al-Daraqutni mentioned this. It was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Zaid Ibn Thabit, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hajj and Umrah are two obligatory acts, and it does not matter which one you start with. Malik used to say, Umrah is a Sunnah, and we do not know of anyone who has permitted abandoning it. This is the opinion of al-Nakha’i and the people of opinion, as reported by Ibn al-Mundhir. Some of the people of Qazwin and Baghdad reported on the authority of Abu Hanifa that he made it obligatory like Hajj, and that it is an established Sunnah, as stated by Ibn Mas’ud and Jabir ibn Abdullah. Al-Daraqutni narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Zakariya told us, Muhammad ibn al-Ala’ Abu Kurayb told us, Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: A man asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) about prayer, zakat and Hajj: Are they obligatory? He said: Yes. He asked him about Umrah: Is it obligatory? He said: No, and performing Umrah is better for you. Narrated by Yahya ibn Ayoub on the authority of Hajjaj and Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ibn al-Munkadir on the authority of Jabir, with a chain of transmission ending with Jabir. This is an argument for those who do not make it obligatory from the Sunnah. They said: As for the verse, there is no argument in it for obligation, because God, the Exalted, only linked it to the obligation of completion, not to begin. He began with prayer and zakat, saying: And establish prayer and give zakat. And He began with the obligation of Hajj, saying: And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind. And when He mentioned Umrah, He commanded its completion, not its initiation. So if a person performs ten Hajj pilgrimages, or ten Umrahs, he must complete them all. The verse came to oblige completion, not to oblige initiation. And God knows best. The opponent argued from the point of view of its obligation by saying: The pillar of Hajj is standing at Arafat, and there is no standing in Umrah. So if it were like the Sunnah of Hajj, it would be obligatory for it to be equal to it in its actions, just as the Sunnah of prayer is equal to its obligatory prayer in its actions. Fifth: Al-Sha’bi and Abu Haywah read Umrah with the ta raised, which indicates that it is not obligatory. The group read Umrah with the ta lowered, which indicates that it is obligatory. In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas’ud, it says: And complete the Hajj and Umrah to the House for God. It was narrated from him: And establish the Hajj and Umrah to the House. The benefit of specifying the mention of God here is that the Arabs used to go to Hajj to gather, demonstrate, compete, compete, meet their needs, and attend the markets. None of that is obedience to God, nor is there any share in intention, nor is there any closeness to God through belief. So God Almighty commanded us to go to Him to perform His obligation and fulfill His right, then He forgave us in trade, as will come. Sixth: There is no disagreement among scholars regarding someone who witnessed the Hajj without intending to perform Hajj or Umrah - and the pen is in his favour and against him - that witnessing it without intention or purpose is not sufficient for him, and that the intention is obligatory, due to the Almighty’s saying: And complete it. And part of the perfection of worship is the presence of intention, and it is obligatory like the ihram when entering ihram. Because he, peace be upon him, said when he mounted his mount: I respond to Your call for Hajj and Umrah together, as follows. And Rabi’ mentioned in the book of Al-Buwayti on the authority of Al-Shafi’i that he said: If a man responds to the call but does not intend Hajj or Umrah, he is not a pilgrim or a person performing Umrah. And if he intends but does not respond to the call until he has completed the rituals, it is a complete Hajj. And he used as evidence the hadith of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Actions are judged by intentions. He said: Whoever does what Ali did when he declared his intention to perform the ritual prayer based on the intention of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that intention will suffice him, because it was based on an intention of someone else that had already been made, unlike prayer. Seventh: The scholars differed regarding the adolescent and the slave who enter ihram for Hajj, then one of them has a wet dream and the other is freed before standing at Arafat. Malik said: They have no way to reject ihram, nor does anyone, adhering to the words of God the Almighty: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God 1:17. Whoever rejects his ihram does not complete his Hajj or Umrah. Abu Hanifa said: It is permissible for a boy who reaches puberty before standing at Arafat to renew his ihram. If he persists in his Hajj, it does not count as Hajj al-Islam. He argued that since Hajj does not count for him, and the obligatory prayer was not obligatory for him when he entered ihram for Hajj, then it became obligatory for him when he reached puberty, it is impossible for him to be distracted from an obligatory prayer that was required of him by a voluntary prayer and neglect his obligatory prayer, like someone who enters into a voluntary prayer and the obligatory prayer is established for him and he fears missing it, he should cut off the voluntary prayer and enter into the obligatory prayer. Al-Shafi’i said: If a boy enters ihram, then reaches puberty before standing at Arafat and stands there in ihram, it counts as Hajj al-Islam. The same applies to a slave. He said: If he was freed at Muzdalifah and the boy reached puberty there, and they returned to Arafat after being freed and reaching puberty, and they reached the standing place there before dawn, it would be sufficient for them as part of the Hajj of Islam, and they would not have to offer a blood sacrifice. If they were to be on the safe side and shed a blood sacrifice, that would be more preferable to me, but that is not clear to me. He provided evidence for dropping the renewal of ihram with the hadith of Ali, may God be pleased with him, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him when he came from Yemen, taking his time for the Hajj: What did you enter into the state of ihram? He said: I said: At your service, O God, with an ihram like the ihram of your Prophet. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I have entered into the state of ihram for Hajj and brought the sacrificial animals. Ash-Shafi’i said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not disapprove of his statement, nor did he order him to renew his intention for Ifrad, Tamattu’, or Qiran. Malik said about a Christian who converts to Islam on the eve of Arafah and enters into the state of ihram for Hajj: It suffices him for the obligatory Hajj. Likewise, a slave may be freed and a child may reach puberty if they were not in the state of ihram, and no blood money is due on either of them. Blood money is only due on the one who intended to perform Hajj but did not enter the state of ihram from the miqat. Abu Hanifa said: The slave must pay blood money. He is like a free man in their view with regard to passing the miqat, unlike the child and the Christian, who are only required to enter the state of ihram to enter Makkah because the obligation has been waived for them. If a non-Muslim converts to Islam and the child reaches puberty, their ruling is the ruling of a Makkan, and nothing is due on them for leaving the miqat. The Almighty’s saying: But if you are prevented, then what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. There are twelve issues in this: First: Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a complex verse, a muscle from the muscles. I said: There is no problem with it, and we will explain it very clearly, so we say: Ihsar is the prevention from the direction you intend by obstacles in general, so the general meaning: for any excuse, whether it was the confinement of an enemy, the injustice of a ruler, illness, or whatever. The scholars differed in identifying the obstacle here, with two opinions: The first: Alqamah, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and others said: It is the illness, not the enemy. It was said: The enemy in particular, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ibn, Anas, and al-Shafi’i. Ibn al-Arabi said: It is the choice of our scholars. The majority of linguists and those who study it are of the opinion that Ihsar is an occurrence of illness, and Ihsar is the occurrence of an enemy. I said: What Ibn al-Arabi narrated that it is the choice of our scholars, only Ashab alone said it, and the rest of Malik’s companions disagreed with him on this and said: Ihsar is only an illness, and as for the enemy, it is only said about it: He was confined, so he is confined, as al-Baji said in al-Muntaqa. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj narrated that it is like this according to all the linguists, as will come. Abu Ubaidah and al-Kisa’i said: He was confined by illness, and he was confined by the enemy. In al-Mujmal by Ibn Faris it is the opposite, so he was confined by illness, and he was confined by the number. A group said: It is said Ihsar in both of them from the quadriliteral, as Abu Umar narrated it. I said: It is similar to the statement of Malik, where he translated in his Muwatta’ as Ihsar fihuma, so ponder it. Al-Farra’ said: They have the same meaning in sickness and running. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: The Shafi’is claimed that Ihsar is used in running, but as for sickness, Ihsar is used in it, but the correct view is that they are used in both. I said: What the Shafi'is claimed, Al-Khalil bin Ahmad and others stated otherwise. Al-Khalil said: "I confined a man, I prevented him and detained him. I prevented a pilgrim from performing the rituals due to illness or the like." This is what he said, making the first a triliteral from I confined, and the second in illness a quadriliteral. Based on this is the statement of Ibn Abbas: There is no confinement except the confinement of the enemy. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: I confined him if he prevented him from traveling or from a need he wanted. The army confined him if they restricted him and set him free, and they besieged him, besieging and blockading. Al-Akhfash said: I confined the man, so he is confined, meaning I detained him. He said: And my urine confined me, and my illness confined me, meaning it made me confine myself. Abu Amr Al-Shaibani said: The thing confined me and confined me, meaning it imprisoned me. I said: Most linguists agree that hasar refers to the enemy, and aḥṣar refers to illness. This has been said in the words of God Almighty: For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God. Ibn Mayada said: Laila did not abandon you because she was distant from you, nor because she was busy with things. Al-Zajjaj said: “According to all linguists, ‘Ihsar’ is due to illness. As for ‘Anti’, it is only said ‘Hisar’. It is said ‘Hisar’ ‘Hisran’, and in the first case ‘Ahsar’ ‘Ihsaran’, which indicates what we have mentioned. The root of the word is ‘Habs’, and from it comes ‘Hasir’ for the one who confines himself from revealing his secret. ‘Hasir’ is the king because he is like someone confined behind a veil. ‘Hasir’ is the one on whom he sits, because some of the papyrus mats are joined together, like confining something with something else.” Second: Since the origin of the confinement is the Hanafi school, the Hanafis said: The confined one is the one who becomes prevented from entering Mecca after entering the state of ihram due to illness, enemy, or something else. They argued based on the requirement of confinement in general, and said: The mention of security at the end of the verse does not indicate that it does not occur due to illness. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A cold is a protection from leprosy, he said. Whoever says Al-Hamdulillah first when someone sneezes will be safe from shus, laws, and ‘ulus. Shus is a toothache. Laws is an earache. ‘ulus is the plural of stomach. Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan. They said: We made the confinement of the enemy a siege by analogy to illness if it is considered to be such, not by the apparent meaning. Ibn ‘Umar, Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn ‘Abbas, al-Shafi’i, and the people of Madinah said: What is meant by the verse is the confinement of the enemy, because the verse was revealed in the sixth year during the ‘Umrah of al-Hudaybiyyah when the polytheists prevented the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) from Mecca. Ibn ‘Umar said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the infidels of Quraysh prevented us from entering the House. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered a sacrifice and shaved his head. This is indicated by the words of God Almighty: Then when you are secure. He did not say: You are innocent. And God knows best. Third: The majority of people are of the opinion that the one who is besieged by an enemy is released from the place where he is besieged, and he slaughters his sacrificial animal if there is one, and he shaves his head. Qatada and Ibrahim said: He sends his sacrificial animal if he is able to, and when it reaches its place it becomes permissible. Abu Hanifa said: The blood of the one who is besieged is not dependent on the day of sacrifice, rather it is permissible to slaughter it before the day of sacrifice if it reaches its place, and his two companions disagreed with him and said: It is dependent on the day of sacrifice, and if he slaughters it before that it is not acceptable. More clarification of this issue will follow. Fourth: The majority of scholars agree that whoever is besieged by an enemy, whether a disbeliever or a Muslim, or is imprisoned in a prison, must offer a sacrificial animal. This is the opinion of Ash-Shafi’i, and Ashhab also said the same. Ibn Al-Qasim used to say: Whoever is prevented from the House during Hajj or Umrah is not required to offer a sacrificial animal unless he brings it with him. This is the opinion of Malik. One of their proofs is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered a sacrificial animal on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah, which he had marked and adorned when he entered ihram for Umrah. When that sacrificial animal did not reach its destination at the front, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered it to be slaughtered, because it was a sacrificial animal that was required by marking and adorning, and it went out for the sake of God, so it is not permissible to go back on it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not slaughter it because of the prevention. Therefore, the one who is prevented from the House is not required to offer a sacrificial animal. The majority argued that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not become halal on the day of Al-Hudaybiyah and did not shave his head until he had slaughtered the sacrificial animal. This indicates that one of the conditions for the halal of the one who is prevented is to slaughter a sacrificial animal if he has one. If he is poor, then whenever he finds it and is able to afford it, he is not halal except with it. This is what is required by his statement: But if you are prevented, then offer whatever is easy of sacrificial animal. It has been said that he becomes halal and offers a sacrificial animal if he is able to do so. The two opinions are those of Al-Shafi’i. Likewise, the one who does not find a sacrificial animal to buy, there are two opinions. Fifth: Ata’ and others said: The one who is prevented by illness is like the one who is prevented by an enemy. Malik, Ash-Shafi’i and their companions said: The one who is prevented by illness is not released except by circumambulating the House, even if he stays for years until he recovers. The same applies to the one who makes a mistake in counting or the crescent moon is hidden from him. Malik said: The people of Mecca are like the people of other lands in this regard. He said: If the sick person needs medicine, he treats himself with it and redeems himself and remains in his state of ihram, he is not released from anything until he recovers from his illness. When he recovers from his illness, he goes to the House and circumambulates it seven times, and walks between Safa and Marwa, and is released from his Hajj or Umrah. All of this is the opinion of Ash-Shafi’i, and he went in this regard with what was narrated from ‘Umar, Ibn ‘Abbas, ‘Aisha, Ibn ‘Umar and Ibn Az-Zubayr that they said about the one who is prevented by illness or makes a mistake in counting: The only thing that is released from him is circumambulating the House. The same applies to the one who suffers from a fracture or a ruptured abdomen. The ruling for someone in this situation according to Malik and his companions is that he has a choice if he fears missing standing at Arafat due to his illness. If he wishes, he may proceed to the House when he recovers, perform Tawaf and become released for Umrah. If he wishes, he may remain in his state of Ihram until the following year. If he remains in his state of Ihram and does not do anything that is forbidden to the pilgrim, then he does not have to offer a sacrifice. Among his proofs for this is the consensus of the companions that whoever makes a mistake in counting, this is his ruling and nothing can release him except Tawaf around the House. He said about the Meccan who remains prevented until the people have finished their Hajj: He should go out to the area outside of the Haram, recite the Talbiyah, do what the pilgrim does, and become released. When the following year comes, he should perform Hajj and offer a sacrifice. Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri said about the one who is prevented from standing at Arafat from the people of Mecca: He must stand at Arafat, even if he is carrying a bier. Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Bakir al-Maliki chose this statement and said: Malik’s statement about the one who is prevented from entering Mecca that he must do what is required of those who are outside of the country in terms of repeating the Hajj and offering the sacrificial animal is contrary to the apparent meaning of the Book, because God the Almighty says: This is for those whose family are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram. He said: My statement on this is the statement of al-Zuhri that God the Almighty permits those whose family are not present at al-Masjid al-Haram to stay due to the long distance and seek medical treatment even if he misses the Hajj. As for the one who is between him and al-Masjid al-Haram what is not shortened in such a case, then he attends the viewing even if he is biered because of the short distance to the House. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: Whoever is prevented from reaching the House due to an enemy, illness, loss of money, the loss of a mount, or the bite of a snake, then he must remain in his place in his state of ihram and send his sacrificial animal or the price of his sacrificial animal. Then when he slaughters, he is released from his state of ihram. This is what Urwah, Qatada, Al-Hasan, Al-Nakha’i, Mujahid, and the people of Iraq said, based on the Almighty’s saying: But if you are prevented, then whatever can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals Al-An’am 2:17. Sixth: Malik and his companions said: It does not benefit the pilgrim to stipulate a condition in the Hajj if he fears being confined due to illness or an enemy. This is the opinion of al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa and their companions. The condition is that he says when he enters ihram: Here I am, O God, here I am, and my place is where You confine me on earth. Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh and Abu Thawr said: There is nothing wrong with stipulating and he has his own condition. This was said by more than one of the Companions and Followers. Their proof is the hadith of Duba’ah bint al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib that she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I want to perform Hajj. Should I stipulate any conditions? He said: Yes. She said: How should I say it? He said: Say: Here I am, O God, here I am. My place on earth is where You have detained me. Narrated by Abu Dawud, Al-Daraqutni and others. Al-Shafi’i said: If the hadith of Duba’ah had been proven, I would not have repeated it, and his place on earth was where God detained him. I said: It has been authenticated by more than one person, including Abu Hatim al-Basti and Ibn al-Mundhir. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It is proven that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Daba’ah bint al-Zubayr: Perform Hajj and stipulate.” Al-Shafi’i said the same when he was in Iraq, then he stopped talking about it in Egypt. Ibn al-Mundhir said: I say the first opinion. Abd al-Razzaq mentioned it, Ibn Jurayj told us, Abu al-Zubayr told me that Tawus and Ikrimah told him on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Duba’ah bint al-Zubayr came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I am a heavy woman and I want to perform Hajj. How do you command me to enter ihram? He said: Enter ihram and stipulate that my place of departure is where you detain me. He said: So she did. This is a sound chain of transmission. Seventh: The scholars also differed regarding the obligation of making up for the one who is prevented. Malik and Al-Shafi’i said: Whoever is prevented by an enemy does not have to make up for his Hajj or Umrah unless it was a necessity and it was not a Hajj, in which case Hajj is obligatory for him according to its obligation upon him. The same applies to Umrah according to those who made it obligatory. Abu Hanifa said: Whoever is prevented by illness or an enemy must perform Hajj and Umrah, and this is the opinion of Al-Tabari. The people of opinion said: If he is in a state of ihram for Hajj, he must perform Hajj and Umrah, because his ihram for Hajj became Umrah. If he is in a state of qiran, he must perform Hajj and two Umrahs. If he is in a state of ihram for Umrah, he must perform Umrah. According to them, it is the same whether he is prevented by illness or an enemy, as mentioned above. They cited as evidence the hadith of Maimun bin Mihran, who said: I went out to perform Umrah in the year that the people of Ash-Sham besieged Ibn Az-Zubayr in Mecca, and he sent men from my people with a sacrificial animal with me. When I reached the people of Ash-Sham, they prevented me from entering the sanctuary, so I slaughtered the sacrificial animal in my place, then I became free from ihram and returned. When it was the next year, I went out to perform my Umrah, so I came to Ibn Abbas and asked him, and he said: Replace the sacrificial animal, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his companions to replace the sacrificial animal that they had slaughtered in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah with the Umrah of completion. They cited as evidence the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Whoever breaks or is lame has become free from his obligation and must perform another Hajj or Umrah. Narrated by Ikrimah on the authority of Al-Hajjaj ibn Amr Al-Ansari, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever breaks or is lame has become free from his obligation and must perform another Hajj. They said: So the Umrah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions performed in the following year after the year of Al-Hudaybiyah was only to make up for that Umrah. They said: That is why it was called the Umrah of Compensation. Malik argued that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not command any of his companions or those who were with him to make up for anything or to return for anything, nor did he preserve that from any source, nor did he say in the following year: This Umrah of mine is to make up for the Umrah in which I was prevented, and that was not transmitted from him. They said: The Umrah of Compensation and the Umrah of Recompense are the same, and it was only called that because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a deal with the Quraysh and made peace with them in that year on the condition that they return from the House and go to it the following year, so it was called the Umrah of Compensation. Eighth: None of the jurists said that someone who broke or limped should be released with the same fracture except Abu Thawr based on the apparent meaning of the hadith of Al-Hajjaj bin Amr, and according to that, Dawud bin Ali and his companions. The scholars agreed that someone who broke the hadith should be released, but they differed on what releases him. Malik and others said: He is released by circumambulating the House, and nothing else releases him. And whoever among the Kufians disagreed with him said: He is released by intention, action, and what releases him, based on what was mentioned above from his school of thought. Ninth: There is no disagreement among scholars of the countries that the confinement is general in Hajj and Umrah. Ibn Sirin said: There is no confinement in Umrah, because it is not temporary. It was answered that even if it is not temporary, there is harm in waiting until the excuse is removed, and the verse was revealed about that. It was narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr that whoever is confined by the enemy or sickness, then nothing is permissible for him except circumambulating the House, and this also contradicts the text of the hadith of the year of al-Hudaybiyyah. Tenth: The one who besieges the people may be either a disbeliever or a Muslim. If he is a disbeliever, it is not permissible to fight him even if he is confident that he will be victorious over them, and he may be released from his position, due to the statement of God the Almighty: And do not fight them at al-Masjid al-Haram The Sacred Mosque, as mentioned above. If the disbeliever asks for a reward, it is not permissible, because that is a weakness in Islam. If he is a Muslim, it is not permissible to fight him under any circumstances, and he must be released from his position. If he asks for something and leaves the road, it is permissible to pay him, but fighting is not permissible because it involves the loss of life, and that is not necessary in performing acts of worship, because religion is more tolerant. As for offering a reward, it is because it removes the greater of two harms with the lesser of them, and because Hajj is one of the things on which money is spent, so this is considered an expenditure. Eleventh: The besieging enemy is either certain to remain and settle due to its strength and numbers or not. If it is the first, the besieged person will be released from his place immediately. If it is the second, and it is hoped that it will go away, then he is not besieged until there remains between him and the Hajj an amount of time in which he knows that if the enemy goes away, he will not be able to perform the Hajj. Then he is released according to Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn al-Majishun. Ashhab said: The one who is prevented from Hajj by an enemy does not release himself until the Day of Sacrifice, and he does not stop the Talbiyah until the people go to Arafat. The reason for Ibn al-Qasim’s statement is that this is a time when one despairs of completing his Hajj due to a victorious enemy, so it is permissible for him to release himself in it. The origin of that is the Day of Arafat. The reason for Ashhab’s statement is that he must perform the ruling of ihram as much as he can and adhere to it until the Day of Sacrifice, the time when it is permissible for the pilgrim to release himself as much as he can, so that is upon him. God the Almighty said: Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal is in the nominative case, meaning it is obligatory or upon you is whatever is easy. It is also possible that it is in the accusative case, meaning slaughter or offer a sacrificial animal. According to the majority of scholars, what is easy is a sheep. Ibn Umar, Aisha, and Ibn al-Zubayr said: What is easy is a camel less than a camel, and a cow less than a cow, and it cannot be from other than them. Al-Hasan said: The highest sacrificial animal is a camel, the middle one is a cow, and the lowest one is a sheep. This is evidence for what Malik held, that the one who is prevented by an enemy is not obligated to make up for it, because he said: Then whatever is easy of the sacrificial animal and he did not mention making up for it. And God knows best. Twelfth: The Almighty’s saying: Of the guidance. Guidance and guidance are two languages. It is what is offered to the House of God, whether as a sacrificial animal or something else. The Arabs say: How many camels are there for the children of so-and-so? Abu Bakr said: It is called guidance because some of it is offered to the House of God, so it is called by what is attached to some of it, as the Almighty said: But if they commit an immorality, then upon them is half of the punishment of free women. He meant that if slave girls commit adultery, then upon the slave girl if she commits adultery is half of what is upon the free virgin if she commits adultery. So God mentioned the free women while He meant the virgins, because chastity is in most of them, so they were named after something that is found in some of them. The free woman who is chaste is the one who has a husband, and she must be stoned if she commits adultery, and stoning is not divisible, so the slave girl is half of it. So it is revealed from this that the free women are meant to be virgins, not those who have husbands. Al-Farra’ said: The people of Hijaz and Banu Asad pronounce the hadi lightly. He said: Tamim and Lower Qais pronounce it heavy and say: hadi. The poet said: I swear by the Lord of Mecca, the place of prayer, and the necks of the sacrificial animals He said: The singular of hadi is hadiya. The plural of hadi is ahdaa.
2:197: It contains fourteen issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: The Hajj is [during] well-known months. When He mentioned Hajj and Umrah in His saying: And complete the Hajj and Umrah for God, He explained their difference in time. The whole year is a time for entering into ihram for Umrah, and a time for Umrah. As for Hajj, it occurs once a year, and it cannot be in any other months. Hajj is [during] well-known months is a subject and predicate, and there is an omission in the speech, the meaning of which is: the months of Hajj are months, or the time of Hajj is months, or the time of performing Hajj is months. It was said that the meaning is: Hajj is in months, and with the omission of the preposition, it is necessary to place the months in the accusative case, but no one read it in the accusative case, except that it is permissible in the speech to place the months in the nominative case as a circumstance. Al-Farra’ said: The months are in the nominative case, because its meaning is the time of Hajj, the well-known months. Al-Farra’ said: I heard Al-Kisa’i say: Summer is only two months, and the tilasan is only three months. He meant the time of summer, and the time of wearing the tilasan, so it was omitted. Second: There is a difference of opinion regarding the known months. Ibn Masoud, Ibn Omar, Ata, Ar-Rabi’, Mujahid and Az-Zuhri said: The months of Hajj are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah and all of Dhul-Hijjah. Ibn Abbas, As-Suddi, Ash-Sha’bi and An-Nakha’i said: They are Shawwal, Dhul-Qa’dah and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. This was narrated from Ibn Masoud, and Ibn Az-Zubayr said the same. Both opinions were narrated from Malik. The latter was narrated by Ibn Habib, and the former by Ibn Al-Mundhir. The benefit of the difference is the connection of blood. Whoever said: All of Dhul-Hijjah is one of the months of Hajj, did not see blood being shed from actions after the Day of Sacrifice, because they are in the months of Hajj. According to the latter opinion, Hajj ends on the Day of Sacrifice, and blood is required for actions after that because they were delayed past their time. Third: God Almighty did not name the months of Hajj in His Book, because they were known to them. The word months may refer to two months and some of a third, because some of the month is considered as the whole, as it is said: I saw you in such-and-such year, or during the time of so-and-so. Perhaps he only saw him at one hour of it, so time is mentioned in part with the whole, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The days of Mina are three. But they are actually two days and part of a third. They say: I saw you today, and I came to you this year. It was said: Since two and more are plural, he said months. And God knows best. Fourth: There is a difference of opinion regarding entering ihram for Hajj outside the months of Hajj. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: It is part of the Sunnah of Hajj to enter ihram for Hajj during the months of Hajj. Ata, Mujahid, Tawus and Al-Awza’i said: Whoever enters ihram for Hajj before the months of Hajj, it does not count as Hajj and it is considered Umrah, like someone who starts a prayer before its time, it does not count as a voluntary prayer. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr said the same. Al-Awza’i said: He becomes halal for Umrah. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: This is disliked. It was narrated from Malik, and the well-known opinion from him is that entering ihram for Hajj is permissible throughout the year, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifa. Al-Nakha’i said: He does not become halal until he has completed his Hajj, based on the statement of God the Almighty: “They ask you about the new moons. Say, ‘They are measurements of time for mankind and for Hajj.’” [Al-Bukhari and Muslim], and we have already discussed this. What Al-Shafi’i went with is more correct, because that verse is general and this verse is specific. It is possible that it is from the category of textual evidence for some of the general individuals, due to the superiority of these months over others, and based on that, the statement of Malik is correct, and God knows best. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon himself therein means he has obligated himself to begin it with the intention inwardly, and with the ihram outwardly, and with the talbiyah verbally and audibly. This was stated by Ibn Habib and Abu Hanifa regarding the talbiyah. According to al-Shafi’i, the talbiyah is not one of the pillars of Hajj, and this is the saying of al-Hasan ibn Hayy. al-Shafi’i said: The intention is sufficient for the ihram for Hajj. The talbiyah was made obligatory by the people of the outward and others. The root of the word fard in the language is: cutting and severing, and from it comes the fard of the bow, the river, and the mountain. So the obligation of Hajj is binding upon the free slave as the fard is binding upon the cup. It was said: Fard means to separate, and this goes back to the severing, because whoever cuts something has separated it from something else. And man is raised by the beginning and its meaning is condition, and the predicate is his saying: Fard, because man is not a relative pronoun, so it is as if he said: A man who made it obligatory. And he said in them and did not say in it, so some people said: They are the same in usage. Al-Mazini Abu Uthman said: The plural of the inanimate is like the feminine singular, but the plural of the inanimate is not like that. You say: the trunks were broken, and the trunks were broken. This is supported by the statement of God Almighty: The number of months is… Then He said: And from it. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: No obscenity. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Al-Suddi, Qatada, Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Al-Zuhri, Mujahid, and Malik said: Obscenity is sexual intercourse, meaning no sexual intercourse because it spoils it. The scholars agreed that sexual intercourse before standing at Arafat invalidates the Hajj, and upon it is the Hajj that follows and the sacrifice. Abdullah Ibn Omar, Tawus, Ata’, and others said: Obscenity is speaking obscenely to a woman, as he said: When we become halal, we will do such and such to you, without euphemism. Ibn Abbas also said the same, and he recited while he was in a state of ihram: They whisper to us, if the bird is truthful, we will be yours His companion Husayn ibn Qays said to him: Are you speaking indecently while you are in a state of ihram? He said: Rafath is what is said in front of women. Some people said: Rafath is indecent talk about women, whether that is in their presence or not. It was also said: Rafath is a comprehensive word for whatever a man wants from his wife. Abu Ubaidah said: Rafath is idle talk, and he recited: And the flocks of pilgrims refrain from idle talk and obscene speech. It is said: Rafth yarfith, with the fa’ with a damma or a kasra. Ibn Masoud read fa la rafuth in the plural. Ibn al-Arabi said: What is meant by his saying fa la rafuth is its negation as permissible, not existing. So we find and witness the rafth in it, and the report of God, the Most High, cannot occur in a way that is contrary to what it tells us. Rather, the negation goes back to its existence as permissible, not to its existence as perceptible, like His, the Most High’s, saying: Divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods. Its meaning is: legally, not physically. We find that divorced women do not wait, so the negation goes back to the legal ruling, not to the physical aspects. This is like the saying of God Almighty: None shall touch it except the purified, if we say: It is mentioned in reference to humans - and this is correct - that its meaning is that none of them shall touch it according to the Shari’ah. If touching occurs, then it is contrary to the ruling of the Shari’ah. This is the subtlety that the scholars missed, so they said: The report can mean a prohibition, and that has never occurred, and it is not correct for it to occur, for they are different in reality and contradictory in description. Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: nor transgression means all sins, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ata’ and Al-Hasan. Ibn Umar and a group also said: Transgression is committing sins against God the Almighty while in a state of ihram for Hajj, such as killing game, cutting nails, removing hair, and the like. Ibn Zayd and Malik said: Transgression is slaughtering for idols, and from this is the statement of God the Almighty: or transgression dedicated to other than God. Ad-Dahhak said: Transgression is calling one another by nicknames, and from this is His statement: What an evil name is transgression. Ibn Aram also said: Transgression is cursing, and from this is the statement of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Insulting a Muslim is an act of immorality, and fighting him is an act of disbelief. The first statement is more correct, because it includes all statements. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever performs Hajj and does not utter obscenities or commit sins will return as on the day his mother bore him. “And an accepted Hajj has no less than Paradise as a reward.” Narrated by Muslim and others. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, what is between the heaven and the earth? There is no deed better than jihad in the cause of God or an accepted Hajj in which there is no obscenity, no wickedness, and no disputing.” The jurists said: An accepted Hajj is one in which God Almighty is not disobeyed during its performance. Al-Farra’ said: It is one in which God Almighty is not disobeyed after it. Ibn al-Arabi, may God have mercy on him, mentioned both opinions. I said: An accepted Hajj is one in which God the Almighty was not disobeyed, neither during it nor after it. Al-Hasan said: An accepted Hajj is when its performer returns guided in this world and eager for the hereafter. Other than this has been said, and will come. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And let there be no disputing during Hajj. The word no obscenity nor disobedience was read in the nominative case with tanween in both of them. They were also read in the accusative case without tanween. They agreed on the fat-ha in no disputing, which strengthens the accusative reading of what precedes it, and because the intended meaning is the general negation of obscenity, disobedience, and disputing, and so that the speech would be on one system in the generality of all of the negated, and most of the reciters are in the accusative case. The three nouns are in the nominative case, each with no. His saying in Hajj is a predicate of all of them. The reason for reading the nominative case is that no means not, so the noun was raised after it, because it is its name, and the predicate is omitted, its meaning is: no obscenity nor disobedience in Hajj, as indicated in the second apparent Hajj, which is the predicate of no disputing. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: The nominative case means let there be no obscenity nor disobedience, meaning nothing that comes out of Hajj, then he began the negation by saying: and no disputing. I said: It is possible that kāna is complete, like his saying: And if he is in hardship, so it does not need a predicate. It is possible that it is incomplete and the predicate is omitted, as mentioned earlier. It is possible that rafth and fusuq are raised by the beginning, and la for negation, and the predicate is also omitted. Abu Ja`far ibn al-Qa`qa` read in the nominative case in the three. It was narrated from `Asim in some chains of transmission, and based on that, in al-Hajj, the predicate of the three is as we said in the accusative reading. It is not good that in al-Hajj, the predicate of all of them is with the difference in the reading, because the predicate of la is accusative and the predicate of wa la jidāl is raised, because wa la jidāl is cut off from the first and it is in the place of raising by the beginning, and two factors are not possible in one noun. It is possible that wa la rafth and wa la fusuq are linked to the place. The grammarians recited: There is no lineage or friendship today, the tear is too wide for the patcher to fix It is permissible in speech, so there is no obscenity, no immorality, and no argument during Hajj, in apposition to the word, as it was required in no. Al-Farra’ said: And similar to it: There is no father and son like Marwan and his son, who are dressed in glory and girded with glory. Abu Raja Al-Attardi said: There is no obscenity or immorality in them, in the accusative case, and no argumentation in the nominative case and with the tanween. Al-Akhfash recited: This is your grandfather, the same as your little ones. I have no mother, if that is the case, and no father. It was said: The meaning of no obscenity and no wickedness is the prohibition, i.e., do not engage in obscenities and do not commit wickedness. The meaning of no argument is negation, so since they differed in meaning, there was a difference of opinion between them in wording. Al-Qushayri said: There is a consideration in this, since it was said: no argument is also a prohibition, i.e., do not argue, so why was there a difference between them? Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: And there is no dispute. The weight of the word al-jadalah is fa’al from the word al-mujadala, and it is derived from al-jadal, which means twisting, from which comes zamam majdool. It was said: It is derived from al-jadalah, which means the ground. So it is as if each of the two opponents is resisting his companion until he defeats him, and it is as if he has struck him with a jadalah. The poet said: I may ride machine after machine and leave the helpless to argue Dusty, there is no escape Tenth: The scholars differed on the intended meaning here, with six opinions. Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and Ata’ said: Argument here is to argue with a Muslim until he gets angry and ends up cursing him. As for discussing knowledge, there is no prohibition on it. Qatada said: Argument is cursing. Ibn Zayd and Malik ibn Anas said: Argument here is when people differ as to which of them is true to the position of Abraham, peace be upon him, as they used to do in the pre-Islamic era when the Quraysh would stand in a position other than that of the rest of the Arabs, then they would argue after that. So the meaning according to this interpretation is: There is no argument in its places. A group said: Argument here is when a group says: Hajj is today, and a group says: Hajj is tomorrow. Mujahid and a group with him said: Argument is disputing about the months according to what the Arabs used to do with the postponement. They would sometimes make Hajj in a month other than Dhul-Hijjah, and some of them would stand in Jam’ and some in Arafat, and they would argue about the correctness of that. I said: According to these two interpretations, there is no dispute about its time or its place. These two statements are the most correct of what has been said in interpreting his statement: And there is no dispute, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Time has returned to the way it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth, the hadith will be mentioned in Bara’ah. This means that the matter of Hajj has returned to the way it was, i.e. it has returned to its day and time. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he performed Hajj: Take from me your rituals. Thus, he explained the positions and locations of Hajj. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: “The argument is when a group says: Our Hajj is more righteous than your Hajj. And another says the same.” It was said: The argument was about boasting about one’s fathers, and God knows best. Eleventh: The Almighty’s saying: And whatever good you do, God knows it. This is a condition and its answer, and the meaning is: God will reward you for your deeds, because reward only comes from the one who knows something. It was said: It is an incitement and encouragement to good speech instead of obscenity, and to righteousness and piety in morals instead of immorality and argumentation. It was said: Making doing good an expression of controlling themselves so that what they were forbidden from does not occur. Twelfth: The Almighty’s saying: And take provisions is a command to take provisions. Ibn Umar, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd said: The verse was revealed about a group of Arabs who used to come to Hajj without provisions, and some of them would say: How can we perform Hajj to the House of God when He does not feed us? So they would remain dependent on the people, so they were forbidden from doing that and were commanded to take provisions. Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: People were relying on each other for provisions, so they were ordered to provide provisions. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on a journey carrying provisions, and three hundred men from Muzaynah came to him. When they wanted to leave, he said: O Umar, provide the people with provisions. Some people said: Provision yourself with good companions. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is a weak specification, and the first meaning of the verse is: Provision yourself for your return with righteous deeds. I said: The first statement is more correct, because what is meant is the provisions taken for the Hajj journey that are actually eaten, as we mentioned, as Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The people of Yemen used to perform Hajj without taking provisions and they would say: We are the trustworthy. When they arrived in Mecca, they would ask people for help. So God revealed: And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of God. This is the text of what we have mentioned, and most of the commentators agree with it. Al-Sha’bi said: Provisions are dates and gruel. Ibn Jubayr: Cakes and gruel. Ibn Al-Arabi said: God commanded those who had money to take provisions, and whoever did not have money, if he had a profession that he could spend on the road or was a beggar, then there is no blame on him. Rather, God addressed the wealthy who used to leave their money and go out without provisions and say: We are the trustworthy. Trust has conditions. Whoever fulfills them will go out without provisions and is not included in the address, because he went out, in most cases, and they are the ones who fall short of the degree of trust and are heedless of its realities. And God knows best. Abu Al-Faraj Al-Jawzi said: Satan deceived a people who claimed to trust, so they went out without provisions and thought that this was trust, but they were extremely mistaken. A man said to Ahmad ibn Hanbal: I want to go to Mecca on trust in God without any provisions. Ahmad said to him: Go out without a caravan. He said: No, except with them. He said: So you have put your trust in the scabies of the people? Thirteenth: The Almighty’s saying: Then indeed, the best provision is fear of God. The Almighty informed us that the best provision is avoiding prohibitions, so He commanded them to add provisions to fear of God. His saying, Then indeed, the best provision is fear of God came to be understood in the meaning, because the meaning of and provision yourself is: Fear God in following what He commanded you to do in going out with provisions. It was said: It is possible that the meaning is: The best provision is that which the traveler uses to protect himself from destruction or the need to ask and beg. It was said: It is a warning that this home is not a permanent home. The scholars of allusions said: God Almighty reminded them of the journey to the Hereafter and urged them to provision themselves with fear of God, because fear of God is the provision of the Hereafter. Al-A’sha said: If you do not depart with provisions of piety and you meet after death someone who has provisions I regret not being like him and that you are watching as he was watching Another said: Death is a raging sea that destroys the swimmer's tricks. O soul, I am speaking, so listen to the words of a compassionate advisor. Nothing accompanies a person in his grave except piety and good deeds. Fourteenth: The Almighty said: And fear God, O you of understanding. He addressed those of understanding specifically - even though the command includes everyone - because they are the ones upon whom God’s proof was established, and they are the ones who accepted His commands and rose up to them. Al-albab is the plural of lab, and the lab of anything is its essence, and that is why the mind is called lab. An-Nahhas said: I heard Abu Ishaq say: Ahmad bin Yahya Tha’lab said to me: Do you know in the speech of the Arabs something of a doubled form that comes in the form of fa’l? I said: Yes. Sibawayh narrated on the authority of Yunus 10:labbat talab, and he approved of it and said: I do not know of anything similar to it.
2:198: The Almighty’s saying: “There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord.” There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: Janah meaning sin, and it is the noun of laysa. “That you seek” is in the accusative case as the predicate of laysa, meaning that you seek. According to Al-Khalil and Al-Kisa’i, it is in the genitive case. And when the Almighty commanded that the Hajj be free from obscenity, immorality, and argument, He permitted trade, meaning: There is no blame upon you for seeking the bounty of God. Seeking bounty is mentioned in the Qur’an in the sense of trade, God the Almighty said: So spread throughout the land and seek from the bounty of God. The evidence for the correctness of this is what Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “Ukaz, Majannah, and Dhu’l-Majaz were markets in the pre-Islamic era, and they considered it a sin to trade during the seasons, so the verse: “There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord” was revealed during the seasons of Hajj. Second: If this is proven, then the verse is evidence of the permissibility of trade during Hajj for the pilgrim while performing the act of worship, and that the intention to do so is not polytheism and does not remove the person responsible from the duty of sincerity required of him, unlike the poor. As for Hajj without trade, it is better, because it is free from worldly impurities and the heart is attached to other things. Al-Darqutni narrated in his Sunan, “On the authority of Abu Umamah al-Taymi, he said: I said to Ibn Umar: I am a man who rents for this purpose, and some people say: You have no Hajj. Ibn Umar said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him the same thing that you asked me, and he remained silent until this verse was revealed: ‘There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. ’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have a Hajj.” God Almighty says: So when you depart from Arafat, remember God at the Sacred Monument and remember Him as He has guided you, even though you were before that among those astray. There are sixteen issues in this. The first: The Almighty’s saying: Then when you have poured out meaning you have rushed out. It is said: The vessel has overflowed when it is filled to the point that it spills over its sides. A man is fayyadh, meaning he is overflowing with giving. Zuhair said: White and generous, his hands are like a cloud over those who are generous, his generosity never fades A widespread hadith, i.e. common. The second: The Almighty’s saying: From Arafat The reading of the group is Arafat with the tanween, and the same is true if a woman is called Muslimat, because the tanween here is not a difference between what is declined and what is not declined, so you delete it, but it is like the nun in Muslims. An-Nahhas said: This is good. Sibawayh narrated from the Arabs the deletion of the tanween from Arafat, he says: This is Arafat, O this one, and I saw Arafat, O this one, with the kasra on the ta’ and without the tanween. He said: When they made it definite, they deleted the tanween. Al-Akhfash and the Kufians narrated the opening of the ta’, in imitation of the ta’ of Fatima and Talha. And they recited: Her skirt is from the arms and her people are in Yathrib, the lowest high view The first statement is better, and that the tanween in it is the same as in Muslimāt, the kasra is the opposite of the ya in Muslimīn and the tanween is the opposite of the noon. Arafāt: a proper noun, named after a plural like ḍrā’āt. It was also said that it was named after what was around it, like the land of Sabāsib. It was also said that that spot was named Arafāt because people get to know each other there. It was also said that when Adam descended, he ended up in India, and Eve in Jeddah, so they met after a long search for Arafāt on the Day of Arafāt and got to know each other, so the day was named Arafāt and the place was named Arafāt, as Ad-Dahhāk said. Other than this was said because of what was mentioned previously in the verse of the Almighty: And show us our rites. Ibn ‘Atīyah said: It appears that its name was improvised like all the names of places. Arafāt is Nu’man Al-Arak, and the poet says about it: I got a supply of arak wood from Naaman for Hind, but who will deliver it to Hind? It was said: It is taken from the word ‘arf, which means perfume. God Almighty said: He made it perfume for them, meaning He made it perfume. It is unlike Mina, which is full of dung and blood. That is why it was called ‘Arafat. The day of standing is the day of ‘Arafat. Some of them said: The origin of these two names is from patience. A man is called ‘arf,’ if he is patient and humble. It is said in the proverb: The soul is ‘arf, but it can bear whatever it carries. He said: So I was patient, knowing that and free Any patient soul. And Dhu al-Rummah said: He is known for what fate has decreed for him. That is, patient with God’s decree. It was given this name because of the pilgrims’ submission and humility, and their patience in supplication and various types of affliction and enduring hardships, in order to perform this act of worship. Third: The scholars have agreed that whoever stands in Arafat on the Day of Arafat before noon and then departs from it before noon, his standing before noon is not counted. They have agreed that the Hajj of whoever stands in Arafat after noon and departs during the day before night is complete, except for Malik ibn Anas, who said: He must take some of the night. As for whoever stands in Arafat at night, there is no disagreement among the Ummah regarding the completion of his Hajj. The evidence for the majority is the general statement of God the Almighty: So when you depart from Arafat and He did not specify night from day, and the hadith of Urwah ibn Mudras who said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was standing in Jam’, and I said: O Messenger of God, I have come to you from the mountains of Tayy, I have tired my mount and exhausted myself, and by God I have not left a rope but I have stood on it, so is there Hajj for me, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever prays the dawn prayer with us in Jam’ and has come to Arafat before that, at night or during the day, has fulfilled his obligation and his Hajj is complete. It was narrated by more than one of the imams, including Abu Dawud, An-Nasa’i, and Ad-Darqutni, and the wording is his. At-Tirmidhi said: A good and authentic hadith. Abu Umar said: The hadith of Urwah ibn Mudris At-Ta’i is an authentic and sound hadith. It was narrated by a group of trustworthy companions of Ash-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi, on the authority of Urwah ibn Mudris, including Isma’il ibn Abi Khalid, Dawud ibn Abi Hind, Zakariya ibn Abi Za’idah, Abdullah ibn Abi As-Safar, and Mutraf, all of them on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi, on the authority of Urwah ibn Mudris ibn Aws ibn Haritha ibn Lam. Malik’s evidence from the authentic Sunnah is the long hadith of Jabir, narrated by Muslim, in which it says: He remained standing until the sun set and the yellowness faded a little until the disk disappeared. His actions are obligatory, especially during Hajj, and he said: Learn your rituals from me. Fourth: The majority of scholars differed regarding the one who performed the Ifadah before sunset and did not return, what is required of him, even though the Hajj is valid. Ata’, Sufyan Ath-Thawri, Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Abu Thawr, the People of Opinion, and others said: He must offer a blood sacrifice. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: He must offer a sacrificial animal. Ibn Jurayj said: He must offer a camel. Malik said: He must perform the next Hajj, and the sacrificial animal must be slaughtered in the next Hajj, and he is like someone who missed the Hajj. If he returns to Arafat until he leaves after sunset, Ash-Shafi’i said: He does not have to do anything. This is the opinion of Ahmad, Ishaq, and Dawud, and At-Tabari said the same. Abu Hanifa and his companions and Ath-Thawri said: He does not have to offer a blood sacrifice even if he returns after sunset, and Abu Thawr said the same. Fifth: There is no disagreement among scholars that standing at Arafat while riding is better for those who are able to do so, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood like that until he left it after sunset, and Usama bin Zaid rode behind him, and it is preserved in the long hadith of Jabir. And the hadith of Ali, and in the hadith of Ibn Abbas also. “Jabir said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode until he reached the place of standing, and he made the belly of his she-camel Al-Qaswa’ towards the rocks, and he put the walking rope in front of him and faced the qiblah, and he did not stop standing until the sun set and the yellowness went away a little until the disk disappeared, and Usama bin Zaid rode behind him,” the hadith. If he was not able to ride, he would stand standing on his feet supplicating, as long as he was able, and there is no blame on him for sitting if he was not able to stand, and for standing while riding to show off and glorify the Hajj And whoever honors the symbols of God, then indeed, it is from the piety of the hearts. Ibn Wahb said in his Muwatta’ that Malik said to me: Standing at Arafat on mounts and camels is more beloved to me than standing standing. He said: And whoever stands standing, there is no blame on him for resting. Sixth: It is proven in Sahih Muslim and others, On the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, that when he set out from Arafat, he would quickly free the slaves, and if he found a gap, he would release them. Hisham bin Urwah said: The release is above the neck. This is appropriate for the leaders of the pilgrims and those below them, because in hastening the journey to Muzdalifah, the prayer is performed there, and it is known that the Maghrib prayer is not performed that night except with the Isha prayer in Muzdalifah, and that is its Sunnah, as will be explained, God willing. Seventh: The apparent generality of the Qur’an and the established Sunnah indicate that all of Arafat is a place of standing. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And I stood here, and all of Arafat is a place of standing. Narrated by Muslim and others from the long hadith of Jabir. In Muwatta’ Malik, it was reported to him that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘All of Arafat is a place of standing, and they went up from Batn ‘Urnah, and all of Muzdalifah is a place of standing, and they went up from Batn Muhsir.” Ibn ‘Abd al-Barr said: This hadith is connected from the hadith of Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, from the hadith of Ibn ‘Abbas, and from the hadith of ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, and most of the narrations do not exclude Batn ‘Urnah from Arafat, and Batn Muhsir from Muzdalifah. This was transmitted by the trustworthy and reliable hadith scholars in the hadith of Ja’far ibn Muhammad from his father from Jabir. Abu ‘Umar said: The jurists differed concerning the one who stands at Arafat in ‘Urnah. Malik said, as Ibn al-Mundhir reported from him: He sheds blood, and his Hajj is complete. This is a narration narrated by Khalid ibn Nizar from Malik. Abu al-Mus’ab said that he is like the one who did not stand, and his Hajj is missed, and he must perform Hajj the following year if he stands at Batn ‘Urnah. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Whoever departs from Urna has no Hajj. This is the opinion of Ibn Al-Qasim and Salim. Ibn Al-Mundhir mentioned this opinion on the authority of Al-Shafi’i, and he said: And I say the same: It is not sufficient for him to stand in a place where the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) ordered not to stand. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: The exception to the valley of Arafat from Arafat did not come in a way that would make his Hajj obligatory, neither from the perspective of transmission nor from the perspective of consensus. His Hajj is from the view of Abu Al-Mus’ab that standing in Arafat is an obligation agreed upon in a specific place, so it is not permissible to perform it except with certainty, and there is no certainty with disagreement. The valley of Urna is said with the opening of the ra’ and the closing of it, and it is to the west of the mosque of Arafat, so some scholars have said: If the western wall of the mosque of Arafat falls, it falls in the valley of Urna. Al-Baji narrated on the authority of Ibn Habib that Arafat is in the open area, and Urna is in the sanctuary. Abu Omar said: As for the valley of Muhsar, Waki’ mentioned: Sufyan told us on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was placed in the womb of Muhsir." Eighth: There is nothing wrong with introducing people in mosques on the Day of Arafah other than on the Day of Arafah, in imitation of the people of Arafah. Shu’bah narrated on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: The first one to do that was Ibn Abbas in Basra. He meant the gathering of people on the Day of Arafah in the mosque in Basra. Musa bin Abi Aisha said: I saw Omar bin Harith giving a sermon on the Day of Arafah and the people had gathered around him. Al-Athram said: I asked Ahmad bin Hanbal about introducing people in the cities, as they gather on the Day of Arafah, and he said: I hope there is nothing wrong with it. More than one person did it: Al-Hasan, Bakr, Thabit, and Muhammad bin Was’, they used to attend the mosque on the Day of Arafah. Ninth: The virtue of the Day of Arafah. The virtue of the Day of Arafah is great and its reward is immense. God forgives great sins on it and multiplies good deeds. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fasting on the Day of Arafah expiates the sins of the previous and coming year. Narrated by Sahih. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The best supplication is the supplication on the Day of Arafah, and the best thing that I and the prophets before me have said is: ‘There is no god but God alone, with no partner or associate.’” Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no day on which God frees more people from the Fire than on the Day of Arafah. He, the Almighty and Majestic, draws near and then boasts about them to the angels, saying: ‘What did these people want?’” In Al-Muwatta’, on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Kurayz, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Satan has never been seen on a day smaller, more insignificant, more defeated, or more angry than on the Day of Arafah. This is only because he saw the descent of mercy and the forgiveness of great sins by God, except what he saw on the Day of Badr.” It was said: And what did he see on the Day of Badr, O Messenger of God? He said: He saw Gabriel admonishing the angels. Abu Omar said: This hadith was narrated by Abu al-Nadr Ismail bin Ibrahim al-Ajli, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abi Ubla, on the authority of Talha bin Ubayd God bin Kurayz, on the authority of his father. No one else said anything about this hadith on the authority of his father, and it is nothing. The correct version is what is in al-Muwatta. Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim mentioned in Nudar al-Usul: Ibn Na’im al-Tamimi or Ruh told us, he said: Hisham bin Abdul Malik Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi told us, he said: Abdul Qahir bin al-Sarri al-Salami told us, he said: Ibn Lukanah bin Abbas bin Mirdas told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather Abbas bin Mirdas. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, supplicated for his nation on the eve of Arafah for forgiveness and mercy, and he supplicated a lot, and he was answered: ‘I have done nothing except wrong some of them to others, but as for their sins between me and them, I have forgiven them.’ He said: ‘O Lord, You are able to reward this wronged person with something better than his wrong and forgive this wrongdoer.’ But He did not answer him that evening. Then, when it was the morning of Muzdalifah, he strove hard in supplication, and He was answered: ‘I have forgiven them.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled. It was said to him: ‘You smiled, O Messenger of God, at a time when you do not usually smile?’ He said: ‘I smiled because of the enemy of God, Iblis, for when he knew that God had answered my supplication concerning my nation, he began to supplicate for woe and destruction, throwing dust on his head and fleeing.’” Abu Abd al-Ghani reported that al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us from Abd al-Razzaq, who narrated to us from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A’raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If it is the day of Arafah, God forgives the sincere pilgrim. If it is the night of Muzdalifah, God forgives the merchants. If it is the day of Mina, God forgives the camel drivers. If it is the day of Jamrat al-Aqaba, God forgives the beggar. No one who says, ‘There is no god but God’ witnesses that gathering but that he is forgiven.” Abu Umar said: This is a strange hadith from the hadith of Malik, and it is not preserved from him except through this source. I do not know Abu Abdul Ghani. The people of knowledge have always been lenient with themselves in narrating the desires and virtues from everyone, but they were strict in the hadiths of rulings. Tenth: Scholars recommend fasting on the Day of Arafah except on Arafah. The imams narrated, and the wording is from Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) broke his fast in Arafah, and Umm al-Fadl sent him some milk, and he drank it.” He said: A good and authentic hadeeth. “It was narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: I performed Hajj with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he did not fast it - meaning the day of ‘Arafah - and with Abu Bakr, and he did not fast it, and with ‘Umar, and he did not fast it.” This is what most scholars act upon. They recommend breaking the fast in ‘Arafah so that a person may gain strength for supplication. Some scholars fasted on the day of ‘Arafah in ‘Arafah. He attributed a hadeeth similar to the first hadeeth to Ibn ‘Umar, and added at the end of it: And with ‘Uthman, and he did not fast it. I do not fast it, nor do I command it, nor do I forbid it. This is a good hadeeth. Ibn al-Mundhir mentioned it. ‘Ata’ said about fasting on the day of ‘Arafah: I fast in the winter, but I do not fast in the summer. Yahya al-Ansari said: It is obligatory to break the fast on the day of ‘Arafah. ‘Uthman ibn Abi al-‘Aas, Ibn al-Zubayr, and ‘Aa’ishah used to fast on the day of ‘Arafah. Ibn al-Mundhir said: “Breaking the fast on the day of Arafah in Arafah is more beloved to me, following the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Fasting outside of Arafah is more beloved to me.” This is based on the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was asked about fasting on the day of Arafah. He said: It expiates the sins of the previous and coming year. We have narrated on the authority of Ata’ that he said: Whoever breaks his fast on the day of Arafah in order to gain strength for supplication will have a reward like that of the one who fasts. Eleventh: In the words of God the Almighty: So remember God at Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram, meaning remember Him with supplication and Talbiyah at Al-Mash’ar Al-Haram. It is called Jam’ because it is combined, then Maghrib and Isha’, as Qatada said. It was said: because Adam met Eve there, and he approached her, meaning he drew near to her, and that is why Muzdalifah was named. It is permissible to say: it was named after the action of its people, because they draw near to God, meaning they draw near by standing there. It was named Mash’ar from the word al-sha’ar, which means the mark, because it is a landmark for Hajj, prayer, and spending the night there, and supplication at it is one of the rituals of Hajj. It was described as Sacred because of its sanctity. Twelfth: It has been proven that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed Maghrib and Isha prayers together at Muzdalifah. The scholars agreed - there is no disagreement among them - that the Sunnah is for the pilgrim to combine Maghrib and Isha prayers. They differed about the one who prays them before he comes to combine them. Malik said: Whoever stands with the imam and pushes forward as he pushes forward should not pray until he comes to Muzdalifah and combines them. He provided evidence for that by the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Usama bin Zaid: The prayer is ahead of you. Ibn Habib said: Whoever prays before reaching Muzdalifah without an excuse must repeat it whenever he knows, in the same way as someone who prayed before noon, based on the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): The prayer is ahead of you. Abu Hanifa said the same. Ashhab said: He does not have to repeat it, unless he prays them before sunset, in which case he must repeat the Isha prayer alone. Al-Shafi’i said the same, and Judge Abu al-Hasan supported him. He provided evidence for him by saying that these are two prayers that it is recommended to combine, so that was not a condition for their validity, but rather it was in the sense of desirability, like combining Dhuhr and Asr at Arafat. Ibn al-Mundhir chose this statement, and narrated it from Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, and Ya’qub.
