Ibn Abbas read: and God bears witness to what is in his heart. The reading of the group is more eloquent in its blame, because he forced himself to adhere to good speech, then his opposite appeared from within him. Abi and Ibn Mas’ud read: and God bears witness to what is in his heart and it is an argument for the reading of the group. Second: Our scholars said: In this verse there is evidence and a warning to be cautious regarding matters of religion and the world, and to investigate the conditions of witnesses and judges, and that the ruler does not act on the outward conditions of people and what appears of their faith and righteousness until he investigates their inner selves, because God Almighty has made clear the conditions of people, and that among them are those who express beautiful words while intending ugly ones. If it is said: This contradicts his saying, peace be upon him: I was commanded to fight people until they say there is no god but God, the hadith, and his saying: Then I will rule in his favor according to what I hear, then the answer is that this was in the early days of Islam, when their Islam was their safety, but now that corruption has become widespread, no, Ibn al-Arabi said. I said: The correct view is that what is apparent is to be acted upon until the opposite is proven, based on the statement of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, in Sahih al-Bukhari: O people, revelation has ceased, and we only take you now based on what appears to us of your deeds. So whoever shows us good, we trust him and bring him close, and we have no say in his secret. God will hold him accountable for his secret. And whoever shows us evil, we will not trust him or believe him, even if he says that his secret is good. The third: The Almighty’s saying: And he is the most fierce of opponents. Al-Alad means the fiercely quarrelsome, and he is a stubborn man, and a stubborn woman, and they are the people of Laddah. And I have become Laddat - with a kasra on the dal - talda - with a fatha - Laddan, meaning I have become stubborn, I gave birth to him - with a fatha on the dal - Alda - with a damma - if I argued with him and defeated him, and Al-Alad is derived from Al-Ladayn, and they are the two sides of emancipation, meaning on whichever side he took from the dispute he was defeated. The poet said: And the one who is most angry with me, as if the enmity in his chest is boiling in a cauldron Another said: Under the soil there is determination, resolve, and a fierce enemy with a closed door. The word al-Khisam in the verse is a verbal noun derived from khasama dispute, as stated by Al-Khalil. It was also said that it is the plural of khasam dispute, as stated by Al-Zajjaj, like kalb dog and kalab dogs, sa’ab difficult and sa’ab severe and dhamam heavy and dhamam heavy. The meaning is the most argumentative of the disputants, i.e. he is argumentative. If he speaks to you and argues with you, you will see that his words are smooth and false in their essence. This indicates that argumentation is not permissible except with what is both apparent and hidden, and in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Aisha, she said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The most hated of men to God is the persistent disputant.
2:205: And the Almighty’s saying: And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein. It was said: (Turn away and strive) are from the action of the heart, so (Turn away) means he went astray, became angry, and became arrogant in his soul, and (Sahā’) means he strived with his cunning and will to turn against Islam and its people, according to Ibn Jurayj and others. It was said: They are the actions of the person, so (Turn away) means he turned away and departed from you, O Muhammad, and (Sahā’) means with his feet, he cut off the road and corrupted it, according to Ibn Abbas and others. Both strivings are corruption. It is said: A man strived happily, meaning he ran, and likewise if he worked and earned, and so-and-so strives for his family, meaning he worked to benefit them. The Almighty said: And he destroys is in apposition to to corrupt. In Abi’s reading, it is and to destroy. Al-Hasan and Qatada read and he destroys in the nominative case. There are sayings about its nominative case: it is in apposition to you like. Abu Hatim said: it is in apposition to striving because its meaning is striving and destroying. Abu Ishaq said: and he destroys. It was narrated from Ibn Kathir: and he destroys with the opening of the ya’ and the damma of the kaf, cultivation and offspring are in the nominative case with he destroys. This is the reading of Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Abu Haywah, and Ibn Muhaisin. It was narrated by Abd al-Warith from Abu Amr. Some people read and he destroys with the opening of the ya’ and the lam, and the nominative case of cultivation. The language of halaka yahlik, like rukan yarkan, and abi ya’aba, and salli yasla, and qala yaqala, and the like. The meaning in the verse is Al-Akhnas in his burning of the crops and killing of the donkeys, as At-Tabari said. Others said: but it became Generally for all people, whoever does such a thing deserves that curse and punishment. Some scholars said: Whoever kills a donkey or burns a pile deserves blame, and shame will follow him until the Day of Resurrection. Mujahid said: What is meant is that the oppressor spreads corruption on earth, so God withholds the rain, destroying the crops and offspring. It was said: The crops are women and children. This is because hypocrisy leads to division of speech and the occurrence of fighting, and in it is the destruction of creation. Al-Zajjaj said that its meaning is that walking quickly on earth means causing discord and division among people. And God knows best. In the hadith: If people see the oppressor and do not stop him, God will soon punish them all with His punishment. This will be explained later. God Almighty. God the Almighty said: The tillage and the offspring. The tillage in the language means splitting, and from it the plow is what is used to split the earth, and the plowing is earning and collecting money, and in the hadith: Plough for your world as if you will live forever, and the plowing is the planting, and the plow is the farmer, and he plowed and tilled, like he planted and planted, and it is said: I plowed the Qur’an, meaning the Qur’an, meaning I studied it, and I plowed the she-camel and plowed it, meaning I walked on it until it became thin, and the fire plowed its movement, and the plow is what is used to stir the fire of the oven, according to Al-Jawhari, and the offspring: what comes out of every female of offspring, and its origin is the exit and the fall, and from it is the offspring of hair, and the feathers of the bird, and the future is plowing, and from it is to their Lord they rush (Ya-Sin 36:51): from every mound they rush (al-Anbiya 21:96), and Imru’ al-Qais said: So, remove my clothes from your clothes and let them slip away I said: The verse indicates plowing and cultivating the land, and planting it with trees to carry on the crops, and seeking offspring, which is the growth of the animal, and through that the human being’s foundation is completed, and it refutes those who say that the causes should be abandoned, and its explanation will come in this book, God willing. God Almighty says: And God does not love corruption. Al-Abbas bin Al-Mufaddal said: Corruption is devastation. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Cutting off dirhams is corruption on earth. Ata’ said: “A man called Ata’ bin Munabbih entered ihram wearing a cloak, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to take it off.” Qatada said: I said to Ata’: We used to hear that it was torn, so Ata’ said: God does not love corruption. I said: The verse in its generality includes all corruption in land, money, or religion, and this is correct, God Almighty willing. It was said: The meaning of He does not love corruption is that He does not love it from the people of righteousness, or He does not love it as a religion. It is possible that the meaning is that he does not command it, and God knows best.
2:206: God Almighty says: “And when it is said to him, ‘Fear God,’ pride in sin takes hold of him. Sufficient for him is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.” This is the characteristic of the unbeliever and the hypocrite who is proud of himself, and it is disliked for the believer to cause him hardship in some of this. Abdullah said: It is enough of a sin for a man that his brother says to him: Fear God, and he says: Take care of yourself, someone like you advises me? And pride means strength and dominance, from ‘izzahu ya’izzuhu if he overcomes him, and from it: And he made me proud in the speech [p. 23], and it was said: pride here is zeal, and from it the saying of the poet: He was overcome by pride due to his ignorance, so he angrily did the act of boredom. It was said: Pride here means strength and strength of soul, meaning he was proud in himself and took a step back, so that pride caused him to fall into sin when it seized him and forced him to do it. Qatada said: The meaning is that if he is told, Slow down, he will increase his boldness towards sin, and the meaning is that pride led him to sin. It was said: Pride took him with what made him sin, meaning he committed disbelief out of pride and the passion of ignorance. Similar to it is: Rather, those who disbelieve are in pride and discord, [p. 2]. It was said: The ba in with sin has the meaning of the lam, meaning pride and passion took him from accepting the sermon because of the sin in his heart, which is hypocrisy. From this is the saying of Antarah describing the vein of the camel: As if a complex kohl or a rib had been filled with fuel on the sides of a bottle Any fuel was filled for him, and it was said: The baa means with, meaning pride took him along with sin, so the meaning of the baa differs according to interpretations, and it was mentioned that a Jew had a need from Harun al-Rashid, so he went to his door for a year, but he did not fulfill his need, so he stood one day at the door, and when Harun came out, he ran until he stood in front of him and said: Fear God, O Commander of the Faithful? So Harun got off his mount and fell prostrate, and when he raised his head, he ordered his need to be fulfilled, and when he returned, it was said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, did you get off your mount because of what a Jew said? He said: No, but I remembered the saying of God the Most High: “And when it is said to him, ‘Fear God,’ pride in sin takes hold of him. So Hell is sufficient for him, and an evil resting place indeed.” Sufficient for him means sufficient for him as punishment and recompense, as you say to a man: What happened to you is enough for you! And you consider what happened to him great and great. The cradle is the plural of cradle, which is the place prepared for sleeping, and from it comes the cradle of a child. Hell was called a cradle because it is the resting place of the infidels. It was also said that it is a substitute for a cradle for them, like His statement: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment (Al Imran 3:21). Similar to this statement is their statement: Greetings between them are painful
2:207: God Almighty says: “And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And God is kind to His servants.” Seeking is an accusative of the object of purpose. When he mentioned the actions of the hypocrites, he mentioned the actions of the believers after that. It was said: It was revealed about Suhaib, for he came as an immigrant to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a group of Quraysh followed him. He got down from his mount, took what was in his quiver, and took his bow, and said: You know that I am one of your best archers, and by God you will not reach me until I shoot what is in my quiver, then I will strike with my sword whatever is left in my hand, then do whatever you wish. They said: We will not let you go away from us rich, for you have come to us as a vagabond, but show us your wealth in Mecca, and we will leave you alone. They made a covenant with him on that, and he did so. When he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the following verse was revealed: And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Abu Yahya has made a profit in the sale, and he recited the verse to him. Razin transmitted it and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, may God be pleased with them both, said it. The commentators said: The polytheists seized Suhaib and tortured him, and Suhaib said to them: I am an old man, your security will not harm you. Or from someone other than you, so would you like to take my money and leave me and my debt? So they did that, and he stipulated that they should provide a mount and expenses. So he went out to Medina and was met by Abu Bakr and Umar may God be pleased with them and some men. Abu Bakr said to him: Your sale is profitable, Abu Yahya. So Suhaib said to him: And your sale does not result in a loss. So what is that? He said: God revealed such-and-such about you, and he recited the verse to him. Al-Hasan said: Do you know about whom this verse was revealed? It was revealed about a Muslim who met an infidel and said to him: Say there is no god but God, and if you say it, your wealth and your life will be protected. But he refused to say it, so the Muslim said: By God, I will sell myself to God. So he advanced and fought until he was killed. It was said: It was revealed about one who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong, and this is how Umar, Ali, and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, interpreted it. Ali and Ibn Abbas said: The two men fought, meaning the rebel said to the corrupter: Fear God, but the corrupter refused and pride took hold of him, so the rebel sold himself to God and fought, and they fought. Abu Al-Khalil said: Umar ibn Al-Khattab heard a man reciting this verse, so Umar said: To God we belong and to Him we shall return. A man stood up enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong and was killed. It was said: Umar heard Ibn Abbas say: The two men fought when the reciter recited this verse, so he asked him about what the interpreter had said to him in this interpretation, so Umar said to him: To God May God bless you, Ibn Abbas! It was said: It was revealed about those who rush into battle. Hisham bin Amir charged the ranks in Constantinople and fought until he was killed. Abu Hurairah recited: And among the people is he who sells himself, seeking the pleasure of God. And something similar was narrated by Abu Ayyub. It was said: It was revealed about the martyrs of the Battle of Raji’. Qatada said: They are the Muhajireen and the Ansar. It was said: It was revealed about Ali, may God be pleased with him, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, left him on his bed the night he went out to the cave, as will be explained in Bara’ah, God willing. It was also said: The verse is a turban that includes every fighter in the way of God, or a martyr in his own right, or one who changes an evil. The ruling on one who charges the ranks has already been mentioned, and the mention of one who changes an evil, his conditions and rulings will come in Al Imran, God willing. The word yashri means to sell. From this comes the phrase and they sold him for a cheap price (Yusuf 12:20), meaning they sold him. Its origin is to exchange. From this comes the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise (al-Tawbah 9:111). From this comes the statement of the poet: And if the vicissitudes of time have made you spend in the company of those who have exchanged this world for His eternal gardens. Another said: I drank cold water, I wish I was a dreamer after the cold Bard here is the name of a young boy, and another said: He is given a price for it, but he refuses it and its owner says, Why don’t you give me a share? Selling the soul here means giving it up for the sake of God’s commands. Seeking is an object for which, and Al-Kisa’i stopped at mardhaat with a ta’, while the rest stopped at a ha’. Abu Ali said: Al-Kisa’i stopped at a ta’ either in accordance with the language of those who say: talhat and ‘alaqmat, and from this is the saying of the poet: Rather, her two halves are like the back of a camel Either because this complement was included in the word, the ta’ was proven as it was proven in the connection, so that it is known that the complement is intended, and contentment is satisfaction. It is said: Radi yirdi radhan and murdhatan. Some people have related that it is said: Sharā means bought. This is needed by the one who interprets the verse in Suhayb, because he bought himself with his money and did not sell himself, unless it is said: Suhayb’s offer to fight them was a sale of himself from God, in which case the wording is correct in the meaning of sold.
2:208: God Almighty says: “O you who have believed, enter into Islam completely and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.” When God Almighty divided people into believers, unbelievers, and hypocrites, He said: Be of one religion, and unite upon Islam and remain steadfast upon it. So peace here means Islam, as Mujahid said, and Abu Malik narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and from it is the saying of the poet Al-Kindi: I called my tribe to peace when I saw them turn their backs That is, to Islam when Kinda apostatized after the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with Al-Ash’ath bin Qais Al-Kindi, and because the believers were never commanded to enter into peace, which is reconciliation, but rather the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was told to incline toward peace if they inclined toward it, but not to initiate it, as Al-Tabari said. And it was said: He commanded those who believed with their mouths to enter into it with their hearts, and Tawus and Mujahid said: Enter into the matter of religion, Sufyan Al-Thawri: In all types of righteousness, and it was read ((peace)) with a kasra on the seen. Al-Kisa’i said: As-Salam and As-Salam have the same meaning, and this is also the case with most of the Basrans. They both refer to Islam and peacemaking. Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala’ distinguished between them, so he read it here: ((Enter into peace)) and said it is Islam. He read the one in (Al-Anfal) and the one in Surat (Muhammad), may God bless him and grant him peace, (As-Salam) with the fatha on the seen, and said: It is peacemaking with the fatha. Al-Mubarrad denied this distinction. Asim Al-Jahdari said: As-Salam is Islam, As-Salam is peace, and As-Salam is submission. Muhammad ibn Yazid denied these distinctions and said: Language is not taken like this, but rather it is taken by hearing, not by analogy. And whoever differentiates needs evidence. The Basrans have narrated: Banu so-and-so are As-Salam, As-Salam, and As-Salam have the same meaning. Al-Jawhari said: As-Salam is peace, it is opened and closed, masculine and feminine, and its origin is from submission and obedience, and for this reason peace was called: As-Salam. Zuhair said: You both said that if we achieve peace with money and a known fact, we will be safe. Al-Tabari preferred to carry the word to mean Islam as mentioned above. Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman said about this verse, Islam is eight shares, prayer is a share, zakat is a share, and fasting is a share. He who has no share in Islam has failed. Ibn Abbas said: The verse was revealed about the People of the Book, and the meaning is, O you who believe in Moses and Jesus, enter Islam with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, all of you. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one from this nation, Jew or Christian, hears of me and then dies without believing in that with which I was sent, except that he will be among the companions of the Fire.” And kafa’ah means all of you, so it is an accusative in the state of peace or from the pronoun of the believers, and it is derived from their saying: I prevented, meaning that none of you should be prevented from entering Islam. The word kaf means prevention, and from it is the word kafah of a shirt with a dammah because it prevents the garment from spreading, and from it is the word kafah of a scale with a kasrah that gathers the weighed and prevents it from spreading, and from it is the word kafah of a person who gathers his benefits and harms, and everything is round. A balance, for their refusal to differentiate: And do not follow a prohibition, the footsteps of Satan, the object, and it was mentioned before, and Muqatil said: Abdullah bin Salam and his companions asked permission to read the Torah in prayer, and to act according to some of what was in the Torah, so And do not follow the footsteps of Satan was revealed, for following the Sunnah is more appropriate after Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent than the footsteps of Satan, and it was said: Do not take the path to which Satan calls you, He is to you a clear enemy, apparent enmity, and it was mentioned before.
2:209: If you slip means you deviated from the path of righteousness. The root of slip is in the foot, then it is used in beliefs and opinions and other things. It is said: he slipped, slipped, slipped, and slipped, meaning his foot slipped. Abu al-Samal al-Adawi read (Zallaltum) with a kasra on the lam, and they are two languages. The root of the letter is from slipping, and the meaning is you went astray and were hasty about the truth. After the clear proofs have come to you means the miracles and verses of the Qur'an, if the address is to the believers. If the address is to the People of the Book, then the clear proofs are what came in their law of informing about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and introducing him. In the verse is evidence that the punishment of the one who knows about sin is greater than the punishment of the one who is ignorant of it, and the one who has not received the call to Islam is not a disbeliever by abandoning the laws. Al-Naqqash narrated that when Ka'b al-Ahbar converted to Islam, he was learning the Qur'an, so he taught him what he had taught (Know that God is Forgiving and Merciful), so Ka'b said: I find it strange that it should be like this. A man passed by them and Ka’b said: How do you read this verse? The man said: Know that God is Exalted in Might and Wise. Ka’b said: This is how it should be, and Exalted in Might does not prevent what you want from Him. He is Wise in what He does.
2:210: Do they wait? means those who have abandoned entering into peace, and (do) here means denial, i.e. what do they wait for: except that God should come to them in shades of clouds and the angels. I looked at him and waited for him means, and waiting is waiting. Qatada, Abu Ja`far Yazid bin Al-Qa`qa` and Ad-Dahhak read (in shades of clouds) and Abu Ja`far read (and the angels) in the accusative case in apposition to the clouds, and its meaning is with the angels. The Arabs say: The prince came with the army, i.e. with the army. (Shade) is the plural of shade in the broken form, like darkness and oppression, and in the surrender there are shades. Sibawayh recited: If the beast embraces the beast in its shadows, falling from the heat, and it was apparent Shades and shadows, the plural of shadow in the word kathirah, and qathilah is azlaal, and it is possible that dhalaal is the plural of azla, like his saying: qalah and qallal, as the poet said: Mixed with water Al-Akhfash Saeed said: “And ‘the angels’ in the accusative case means ‘and among the angels’. He said: The nominative case is better, as He said: ‘Do they await except that the angels should come to them?’ (al-An’am 6:158), ‘And your Lord will come with the angels, rank upon rank?’ (al-Fajr 89:22). Al-Farra’ said: In the reading of ‘Abdullah: ‘Do they await except that God and the angels should come to them in the shadows of the clouds?’ Qatada said: ‘The angels’ means they come to them to take their souls. It is also said: ‘On the Day of Resurrection’, which is more apparent. Abu Al-‘Aliyah and Al-Rabi’ said: ‘The angels come to them in the shadows of the clouds, and God comes to them as He wills.’ Al-Zajjaj said: ‘The estimate is in the shadows of the clouds and among the angels.’ He said: The speech is not according to its apparent meaning regarding Him, glory be to Him, but rather the meaning is that the command and judgment of God will come to them.’ It was said: That is, what He promised them of reckoning and punishment in the shadows, like: ‘Then God came to them from where they did not expect.’ (al-Hashr 59:2), that is, by abandoning them. This is the saying of Al-Zajjaj, and the first is the saying of Al-Akhfash Saeed. It is possible that the meaning of coming refers to the reward, so He called the reward coming just as He called the intimidation and torture in the story of Nimrod coming, so He said: “So God attacked their building from the foundations, and the roof fell upon them from above them” (al-Nahl 16:26). He said in the story of An-Nadir: So God attacked them from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts (al-Hashr 59:2). He said: And if it were the weight of a mustard seed, We would bring it (al-Anbiya 21:47). He only considered these meanings because the root of coming according to the linguists is the intention to do something, so the meaning of the verse is: Do they wait for anything but for God Almighty to show an action from the actions with one of His creations intending to punish them and decide in their matter what He decides? Just as He, glory be to Him, created an action that He called descent and ascension, so He creates an action that He calls coming, and His actions are without a tool or cause, glory be to Him! Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Abu Salih: This is from the hidden that is not explained, and some of them were silent about its interpretation, and some of them interpreted it as we mentioned, and it was said: The fa’ is in the meaning of the ba’, meaning He comes to them with shadows, and from it the hadith God comes to you in a form meaning in a form as a test for them, and it is not permissible to carry this and what is similar to it from what came in the Qur’an and the report of the way of transition, movement and disappearance, because that is from the attributes of bodies and bodies, exalted is He, the Great, the Exalted, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor, far above the likeness of bodies, and the clouds: the thin white clouds, it was named that because it covers, that is, it conceals, as mentioned above, and Muadh bin Jabal read and the decree of the matter, and Yahya bin Ya’mar read and the decree of the matter, in the plural, and the majority read and the decree of the matter, so the meaning is that the punishment occurred and the people of disobedience were punished, and Ibn ‘Amir and Al-Kisa’i read and the matters return in the form of the verb for the agent, and it is the origin, its evidence is unquestionably to God do matters return (al-Shura 42:53), and to God is your return (al-Ma’idah 5:48, 105). ] And the rest read it as tarja’u in its fa’ul construction, and it is also a good reading, its evidence is Then you will be returned (al-Tawbah 9:94), Then you will be returned to God (al-An’am 6:62), and If I am returned to my Lord (al-Kahf 18:36). Both readings are good in meaning, and the original is the first, and its construction as fa’ul is an expansion and a branch, and all matters return to God before and after, and he only drew attention by mentioning that on the Day of Resurrection to the disappearance of what was of it to the kings in the world.
2:211: The Almighty said: Ask the Children of Israel how many clear signs We gave them. "Ask" is from the question: with a lightened hamza, so when the seen moved, there was no need for the alif of connection. It was said: The Arabs have two views in dropping the alif of connection in "sal and keeping it in as'al": One of them is deleting it in one of them and keeping it in the other, and the Qur'an came with them, so it followed the line of the Mushaf in its proof of the hamza and its omission. The second view is that its proof and omission differ according to the speech in which it is used, so the hamza is deleted in the beginning speech, such as His saying: "Ask the Children of Israel", and His saying: "Ask them which of them is responsible for that" (N: 40) and it is proven in conjunction, such as "And ask the town" (Yusuf 12:82), "And ask God of His bounty" (al-Nisa 4:32). This was said by Ali bin Isa, and Abu Amr read in the narration of Ibn Abbas from him ask, according to the original, and a group of people read Asal... on transferring the movement to the seen and keeping the alif of connection, according to the language of those who said: the red and kam in the accusative case because it is a second object of atayyhum, and it was said: yafe’al is implied, its meaning is kam aatiyyana aatiyyum, and it is not permissible for the verb to precede it because it is at the beginning of the speech, from a verse in the accusative case as a distinction according to the first estimate, and according to the second it is a second object of atayyhum, and it is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as the subject and predicate in atayyhum, and it becomes a referent to kam, its meaning is kam aatiyyum, and it is not parsed and it is a noun because it is in the position of letters when the meaning of the question occurs in it, and if you differentiate between kam and the noun, the choice is to bring man as in this verse, and if you delete it, it is accusative in the question and the predicate, and the genitive is permissible in the predicate as the poet said: How many a generous person has attained glory, while his stinginess has put him down? What is meant by the verse is how many signs of knowledge and evidence of Muhammad, peace be upon him, came to them regarding him. Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and others said: It means the signs that Moses, peace be upon him, brought, such as splitting the sea, the clouds, the staff, the hand, and other things. God Almighty commanded His Prophet to ask them in order to rebuke and rebuke them. The Almighty’s statement: Who would change the favor of God after it has come to him? is a general expression for all the common people, even though the one referred to is the Children of Israel, because they changed what was in their books and denied the command of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The expression is applicable to everyone who changes the favor of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Tabari said: The favor here is Islam, and this is close to the first. The expression also includes the infidels of Quraysh, because Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent among them as a favor upon them, but they changed accepting it and thanking for it into infidelity. The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is severe in penalty is report that includes a threat, and punishment is taken from the word heel, as if the one being punished walks with the reward for him in the traces of a heel, and from this comes the word heel of the rider and alert of fate. So punishment and chastisement are in the wake of the sin, and He punished him for his sin.
2:212: The Almighty said: The life of this world has been made fair-seeming to those who disbelieve in the sense that its agent was not named, and what is meant is the leaders of Quraysh. Mujahid and Hamid bin Qais read it in the form of the agent. An-Nahhas said: It is an anomalous reading, because the agent was not preceded by a male. Ibn Abi Ubla read adorned with the sign showing, and this came about because the feminine is not real, and the one who adorns is its creator and inventor and the creator of disbelief. Satan also adorns it with his whisperings and temptations. He singled out those who disbelieved for mention and its inventor because of their acceptance of the adornment as a whole, and their turning towards the world and their turning away from the Hereafter because of it. God made what is on the earth an adornment for it to test the creation as to which of them is best in deeds. The believers who are on the path of the Shari'ah were not tempted by the adornment, and the disbelievers were possessed by it because they do not believe in anything other than it. Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, said when he brought him money: O God, we cannot do anything but rejoice in what You have adorned for us. God the Almighty said: And they ridicule those who believe referring to the infidels of Quraysh, for they used to magnify their worldly status and rejoice in it, and they ridiculed the followers of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said: In their quest for the Hereafter. It was said: Because of their poverty and lack of wealth, such as Bilal, Suhayb, Ibn Mas’ud, and others, may God be pleased with them. So God the Almighty drew attention to the lowering of their status due to the ugliness of their actions by saying: And those who fear God will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. Ali narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever humiliates a believing man or woman or belittles him or her because of his or her poverty and lack of means, God will expose him or her on the Day of Resurrection and then disgrace him or her. Whoever slanders a believing man or woman or says something about him or her that is not true, God the Almighty will set him or her on a mound of fire on the Day of Resurrection until he or she comes out of what he or she said about him or her. Indeed, the greatness of a believer is greater in the sight of God and more honorable to Him than a close angel. And nothing is more beloved to God than a repentant believing man or woman. Indeed, a believing man or woman is known in the heavens as a man knows his or her family and children.” Then it was said: The meaning of and those who fear God is: Above them on the Day of Resurrection, meaning in degree, because they are in Paradise and the disbelievers are in Hell. It is possible that what is meant by above is the place, since Paradise is in the heavens and Hell is in the lowest of the low. It is possible that the preference is based on what the disbelievers claim, for they say: If there is a return, then we have a greater share in it than you. From this is the hadith of Khabbab with Al-Aas bin Wa’il. Khabbab said: I had a debt from Al-Aas bin Wa’il, so I went to him to collect it, and he said to me: I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said to him: I will not disbelieve in him until you die and then you are resurrected. He said: And I will be resurrected after death?! I will pay you if you return to wealth and children, the hadith, and it will come in full, God willing. It is said: I mocked him and I mocked him, and I laughed at him and I laughed at him, and I mocked him and at him, and all of that is said: Al-Akhfash narrated it, and the noun is mockery and mockery and mockery, and it was read with them in the words of God Almighty: So that some of them may take others in mockery (al-Zukhruf 43:32) and His words: So you took them in mockery (al-Mu’minun 23:110), and a man is mockery, he mocks him and mockery - with the opening of the kha - he mocks people and so-and-so is mockery in work, it is said: a female servant is mockery, and mockery is a task he assigns to him without pay. God the Almighty says: And God provides for whom He wills without account. Ad-Dahhak said: He means without any responsibility in the Hereafter. It was said: It is a reference to these weak ones, meaning He provides them with a high status. So the verse is a reminder of the great blessing upon them, and He made their provision without account, as it is permanent and never ends, so it is not counted. It was said that His statement without account is a description of God the Almighty’s provision, how it is spent, if He, the Almighty, is in power, He will not spend after that. So all of His grace is without account, and that which is accounted for is what was for the work that the servant has done. God the Almighty says: A reward from your Lord, a gift of account. (An-Naba’: 36), and God knows best. It is possible that the meaning is without account from those who are provided for, as He said: And He provides for him from where he does not expect. (al-Talaq 65:3)
2:213: The Almighty said: Mankind was one nation meaning of one religion. Abi bin Kaab and Ibn Zayd said: What is meant by people are the children of Adam when God brought them forth as a soul from his back and they acknowledged His Oneness. Mujahid said: People are Adam alone, and the one was called by the plural form because it is the origin of the lineage. It was also said: Adam and Eve. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: What is meant by people are the generations that were between Adam and Noah, and they were ten. They were on the truth until they differed, so God sent Noah and those after him. Ibn Abi Khaithama said: From the time God created Adam, peace be upon him, until He sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, five thousand eight hundred and six years, and it was said: more than that, and between him and Noah there were one thousand two hundred years, and Adam lived nine hundred and sixty years, and the people in his time were people of one religion, adhering to the religion, the angels shook hands with them, and they continued to do so until Idris, peace be upon him, was raised and they differed. This is questionable, because Idris came after Noah according to the correct view. Some of them, including Al-Kalbi and Al-Waqidi, said: What is meant is Noah and those on the ship, and they were Muslims, then after the death of Noah they differed. Ibn Abbas also said: They were one nation in disbelief, meaning during the time of Noah when God sent him. And from him also: People were one nation during the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, all of them disbelievers, and Abraham was born in ignorance, so God Almighty sent Abraham and other prophets, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Was according to these sayings according to its chapter of the past and gone, and whoever estimated the people in the verse as believers estimated in the speech, so they differed, so he was sent, and this deletion is indicated by: And none differed therein except those who were given it, meaning the people were on the religion of truth, then they differed, so God sent the prophets, bringing good tidings to those who obeyed and warning those who disobeyed, and everyone whom he estimated as disbelievers, the mission of the prophets was to them. It is possible that was is for confirmation, and what is meant is to inform about the people who are the entire species that they are one nation in their lack of laws, and their ignorance of the truths, were it not for God’s favor upon them, and His favor with messengers to them, so was is not specific. “On this interpretation, it is only by the past tense, but its meaning is the meaning of His statement: “And God is Forgiving and Merciful” (An-Nisa’: 96), and nation has one purpose, and one is called a nation, meaning a purpose other than the purpose of the people, and from it is “the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Quss bin Sa’idah: He will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection as one nation,” and likewise he said about Zayd bin Amr bin Nufayl, and the nation is the stature, as if it is the purpose of the rest of the body, and the nation with the kasra: the blessing: because the people intend to intend it, and it was said: an imam, because the people intend to intend what is done, from An-Nahhas, and Abi bin Ka’b read that mankind was one nation, and Ibn Mas’ud read that the people were one nation, then they differed, so he was sent.” The Almighty said: Then God sent the prophets. Their total was one hundred and twenty-four thousand, and the messengers among them were three hundred and thirteen, and those mentioned in the Qur’an by proper name were eighteen, and the first of the messengers was Adam, according to what came in the hadith of Abu Dharr, narrated by Al-Ajurri and Abu Hatim Al-Basti, and it was said: Noah, because of the hadith of intercession, for the people would say to him: You are the first of the messengers, and it was said: Idris, and an explanation of this will come in Al-A’raf, God willing. God the Almighty said: Bringing good tidings and warnings is in the accusative case as a state. And He sent down with them the Book is a generic noun meaning books. At-Tabari said: The alif and lam in the book are for the covenant, and what is meant is the Torah. Li-hakam is attributed to the book according to the majority of scholars, and it is in the accusative case with the omission of an, meaning li-hakam, and it is a metaphor like This is Our Book that speaks against you with the truth (Al-Jathiyah: 29). It was said: That is, so that every prophet may judge by his book, and if he judges by the book, then it is as if he judged by the book. Asim Al-Jahdary’s reading li-hakam bayna al-nas is without an agent, and it is an anomalous reading, because the book has been mentioned before. It was said: The meaning is that God judges, and the pronoun in fih refers back to ma from His statement fih, and the pronoun in fih Al-Qaniyah may refer back to the book, meaning that no one differed about the book except those who were given it. The position of those is raised by their action, and watuhu means they gave it to him, and it was said: it refers to the one who was sent to him, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Al-Zajjaj said, meaning that no one differed about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except those who were given his knowledge, out of envy among themselves is in the accusative case as the object of the verb, meaning that they did not differ except out of envy, and its meaning has been presented, and in this is an indication of the foolishness in their action, and the ugliness that they committed, and guidance means he guided, meaning that God guided the nation of Muhammad to the truth by explaining to them what those who came before them differed about, and a group said, the meaning of the verse is that the nations denied the book of each other, so God Almighty guided the nation of Muhammad to believe in all of it, and a group said: God guided the believers to the truth in what the people of the two books differed about, from their saying: that Abraham was a Jew or a Christian, and Ibn Zayd and Zayd bin Aslam said: from their direction, for the Jews are towards Jerusalem, and the Christians are towards the east, “for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on al-Jumuah 62:This is the day in which they differed, so God guided us to it And for the Jews tomorrow and for the Christians the day after tomorrow” and from their fasting, and from all that they differed about, and Ibn Zayd said, and they differed about Jesus, so the Jews made him a lie, and the Christians made him a god, so God guided the believers by making him a servant of God. Al-Farra’ said: It is from the inverted - and al-Tabari chose it - he said: And its meaning is, so God guided those who believed to the truth for what they differed about. Ibn Atiyyah said: And he was prompted to this estimation by fear that the wording might mean that they differed about the truth, so God guided the believers to some of what they differed about, and perhaps it is not the truth in itself. Al-Tabari tended towards this in his narration from al-Farra’, and claiming the inversion of the wording of the Book of God without a necessity that prompts that is a weakness and bad opinion, and that is because the speech is derived in its face and description because his saying: so he guided requires that they hit the truth, and the meaning is completed in his saying: in it and it is made clear by his saying: of the truth the type of what the difference occurred about, al-Mahdawi said: And he presented the wording of difference before the wording of truth out of concern, since the concern is only in mentioning the difference, Ibn Atiyah: This is not strong in my opinion. In the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud, when they differed about the truth, meaning about Islam, and with His permission, Al-Zajjaj said: It means with His knowledge. An-Nahhas said: This is a mistake. The meaning is with His command that they use it. In His statement, And God guides whom He wills to a straight path, there is a response to the Mu’tazila in their saying: The servant takes control of his own guidance.
2:214: The Almighty’s saying: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise? “Hasabtum” means you thought. Qatada, Al-Suddi and most of the commentators said: This verse was revealed during the Battle of the Trench when the Muslims were afflicted with hardship and difficulty, heat and cold, poor living conditions and various types of hardships. It was as God the Almighty said: And hearts reached the throats (al-Ahzab 33:10). It was said: It was revealed during the Battle of Uhud, similar to it - in Al-Imran - Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive? (Al-Imran: 142). A group said: The verse was revealed to console the Muhajireen when they left their homes and wealth in the hands of the polytheists, and preferred to please God and His Messenger, and the Jews showed enmity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of the rich people concealed hypocrisy, so God the Almighty revealed to soothe their hearts: Or do you think? The or here Disjointed, meaning rather, and some linguists have said that it may come as an interrogative alif to begin with, and Hasabtum requires two objects, so grammarians said: Antadkhulu fills the place of the two objects, and it was said that the second object is omitted: Did you think that your entry into Paradise would happen, and Lama means lam, and mithl means like, meaning that you were not tested with what those before you were tested with, so be patient as they were patient, and Hiyya Al-Nadr bin Shumayl said that mithl can be in the sense of an attribute, and it is possible that the meaning is: And you have not been afflicted with what afflicted those before you, meaning of the affliction, Wahb said: Seventy prophets were found between Mecca and Taif, the cause of their death was hunger and lice, and similar to this verse “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left to say, “We believe” and they will not be tested? And We have certainly tested those before them” (al-Ankabut 29:1, 2, 3) as will come, so God Almighty called them to patience, and promised them victory for that, saying: Unquestionably, indeed, “God’s victory is near, and earthquake is the intensity of movement, which occurs in people and situations. It is said: God shook the earth with an earthquake and an earthquake - with a kasra - so it shook if it moved and was disturbed. The meaning of they shook is they frightened and moved. “Earthquake” - with a fatha - is the noun, and earthquake is the hardships. Al-Zajjaj said: The origin of earthquake is from zala something from its place. So if you say: I shook it, then its meaning is I repeated its shaking from its place. The doctrine of Sibawayh is that earthquake is a quadrilateral verb like to traverse. Nafi’ read until you say in the nominative case, and the rest read it in the accusative case. The doctrine of Sibawayh in until is that the accusative is in what comes after it from two directions and the nominative is from two directions. You say: I walked until I entered the city in the accusative case, on the basis that both walking and entering had passed, meaning I walked until I entered it. This is the ultimate goal, and according to the reading of those who read in the accusative case, and the other face in the accusative case in other than the verse is I walked until I entered it, meaning so that I could enter it. The two faces in the nominative case are I walked until I entered it, meaning I walked. So he entered it, and they both went, meaning I walked and entered, and do not use until here with the omission of an, because after it is a sentence, as Al-Farazdaq said: Oh wonder, even the clip is Tsini Al-Nahhas said: According to this reading with the nominative, the meaning is clearer and more correct, that is, and they were shaken until the Messenger said, that is, until this is his condition, because the statement was only about the earthquake and not interrupted by it, and the accusative for the purpose does not have this meaning, and the Messenger here is Sha’ya in the statement of Muqatil, and he is Al-Yasa’, and Al-Kalbi said: This is in every Messenger who was sent to his nation and strove in that until he said: When is the victory of God? It was narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said: He means Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is what the verse was revealed to indicate, and God knows best. The other interpretation in other than the verse is: I walked until I entered it, meaning that the walking had already happened and the entry is now. Sibawayh narrated: He became ill until they did not hope for it, meaning that it is now not hoped for. The same applies to: I walked until I entered it, I do not prevent. Mujahid, Al-A’raj, Ibn Muhaisin, and Shaibah read it in the nominative case, and Al-Hasan, Abu Ja’far, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Shibl, and others read it in the accusative case. Makki said: This is the preferred opinion because the group of reciters are on it. Al-A’mash read: (And they were shaken and the Messenger says) with the waw instead of hatta, and in the Mushaf of Ibn Mas’ud (And they were shaken, then they were shaken and he says), and most of the interpreters are of the opinion that the speech to the end of the verse is from the speech of the Messenger and the believers, meaning that the effort reached them until they were impatient for victory, so God Almighty said: Behold, the victory of God is near. This would be from the speech of the Messenger, requesting to hasten victory, not with doubt or suspicion, and the Messenger is a generic name. A group said: There is an introduction to the speech. And delay, and the estimate: until those who believe say, When is the victory of God? So the Messenger says: Indeed, the victory of God is near. So the Messenger was presented in rank because of his status, then the statement of the believers was presented because he was the one who came first in time. Ibn Atiyah said: This is arbitrary and carrying the statement in its proper form is not impossible, and it is possible that Indeed, the victory of God is near is report from God the Most High, renewed after the statement was completely mentioned. The Almighty’s saying: When will God’s victory come? is raised by the beginning according to Sibawayh, and according to Abu al-Abbas it is raised by a verb, meaning when will God’s victory come, and close is the predicate of if Al-Nahhas said: And in places other than the Qur’an, it is permissible to say “close meaning a place that is close, and close is not dualized by the Arabs, nor pluralized, nor feminine in this meaning. God the Almighty said: Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good (al-A’raf 7:56). The poet said: Woe to him if he spends the night without Umm Hashim near or Basbasa, his daughter, to thank him. If you say: So-and-so is a relative of mine, you use dual and plural forms, and say: relatives, relatives, and relatives.
2:215: God Almighty says: “They ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘Whatever you spend of good is for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveler. And whatever good you do - indeed, God is Knowing of it.’” There are four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: They ask you. If you lighten the hamza, you put its vowel on the seen, then open it and delete the hamza, so you say: They ask you. The verse was revealed about Amr ibn al-Jamuh, who was a very old man. He said: O Messenger of God, I have a lot of money, so what should I give in charity, and on whom should I spend it? So the verse was revealed: They ask you what they should spend. The second: The Almighty’s saying: What do they spend? “What” is in the nominative case as a subject, and that is the predicate, and it means which, and the ha was deleted due to the length of the noun, meaning what is it that they spend? If you wish, what is in the accusative case with they spend, and that with what is like one thing and does not need a pronoun. Whenever it is a compound noun, it is in the accusative case, except for what came in the saying of the poet: What can the slanderers say except that I am in love with you? Because ‘asa does not work in it, ma is in the nominative case and is a compound, as it has no connection to tha. The second: It was said: The questioners are the believers, and the meaning is that they ask you about the ways in which they spend, and where they put what must be spent, what must be spent, Al-Suddi said: This verse was revealed before the zakat was made obligatory, then the obligatory zakat abrogated it. Ibn Atiyyah said: Al-Mahdawi made a mistake regarding Al-Suddi in this, so he attributed to him that he said: The verse is about the obligatory zakat, then the parents were abrogated from it, and Ibn Jurayj and others said: It is recommended, and the zakat is upon the rich man to spend on his needy parents what is suitable for them according to their situation compared to his situation, from food, clothing, and other things. Malik said: He is not obligated to marry his father, and he is obligated to spend on his father’s wife, whether she is his mother or a foreigner. Malik only said that he is not obligated to marry his father because he saw that he usually does not need to marry, and if he needed a pressing need, he would have been obligated to marry him, otherwise he would not have been obligated to spend on them, but as for what is related to worship from the money, he is not obligated to give him what he can use to perform Hajj or Jihad, and he is obligated to give it to him. Zakat al-Fitr, because it is due by spending and Islam. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: ‘What you have spent’” ma is in the accusative case with anfaktum and so is what you spend (al-Baqarah 2:272). It is a condition, and we have already discussed the orphan, the needy, and the wayfarer. Similar to this verse is the Almighty’s saying: Then give the relative his right, and [also] the needy and the wayfarer (al-Rum: 38). Ali ibn Abi Talib read yaf’alu with the ya’, mentioning the absent person. The apparent meaning of the verse is the report, and it includes the promise of recompense.
2:216: God Almighty says: “Fighting has been prescribed for you, although you dislike it. But perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you; and perhaps you like a thing and it is bad for you. And God knows, while you do not know.” There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: It is written means it is obligatory, and something similar to it has been mentioned before. Some people read: Fighting is written upon you, and the poet said: Killing and fighting are written on us and on the prostitutes who drag their tails This is the obligation of jihad. God Almighty has made it clear that this is one of the things with which they were tested and made a link to Paradise. What is meant by fighting is fighting the enemies of the infidels, and this was known to them by the indications of the circumstances. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not permitted to fight during his stay in Mecca. When he migrated, he was permitted to fight whoever fought him from the polytheists in general. They differed about what is meant by this verse. It was said: The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in particular. So fighting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was an individual obligation upon them. When the law was established, it became a communal obligation. This was said by Ata’ and Al-Awza’i. Ibn Jurayj said: I said to Ata’: Is jihad obligatory upon the people in this verse? He said: No, it was written for those. The unknown people of the nation said: The first obligation was only for the sake of sufficiency without specifying, except that if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, provoked them, it was obligatory for them to go out because of the obligation of obeying him. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Jihad is an obligation on every Muslim in his own eyes forever, as narrated by Al-Mawardi. Ibn Atiyyah said: What the consensus has continued to be upon is that jihad is an obligation on every nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so if those Muslims who do it do it, it is dropped from the rest, unless the enemy descends on the arena of Islam, in which case it is an individual obligation. This will come clearly in Surat Al-Bara’ah, God willing. Al-Mahdawi and others mentioned on the authority of Al-Thawri that he said: Jihad is voluntary. Ibn Atiyyah said: This statement, in my opinion, is only in response to a questioner’s question and he has undertaken jihad, so he was told: That is voluntary. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And it is hateful to you is a subject and a predicate, and it is hate in nature. Ibn Arafa said: Hatred is hardship, and hatred with the fat-ha is what you are forced to do. This is the preferred choice, and the damma is permissible in the meaning of the fat-ha, so they are two languages. It is said: I hated something with hatred, hatred, dislike, and hatred, and I forced him to do it with compulsion. Jihad was hateful because it involves spending money, leaving one’s homeland and family, and exposing one’s body to wounds, injuries, amputations, and loss of life. So their hatred was for that, not because they hated the obligation of God Almighty. Ikrimah said about this verse: They hated it, then loved it and said: We hear and obey. This is because obeying the command involves hardship, but if one knows the reward, enduring hardships becomes easy for one. I said: Its example in this world is removing what pains a person and what he fears, such as cutting off a limb, extracting a tooth, bloodletting, and cupping, seeking wellness and lasting health. There is no bliss better than eternal life in the abode of eternity and dignity in a seat of truth. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And perhaps you dislike a thing. It was said: ‘asa means may, as Al-Asamm said. It was also said: It is obligatory, and ‘asa from God is obligatory in all of the Qur’an except for the Almighty’s saying: Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will give him [or her] in exchange (al-Tahrim 66:5). Abu Ubaidah said: ‘asa from God is an obligation, and the meaning is perhaps you dislike the hardship in jihad, which is good for you in that you are victorious, triumphant, gain booty, and are rewarded, and whoever dies dies a martyr. And perhaps you love ease and abandoning fighting, which is bad for you in that you are victorious, humiliated, and your affair is lost. I said: This is true and there is no doubt about it, as happened in the land of Andalusia, they abandoned jihad and were cowardly in fighting and fled a lot, so the enemy took control of the country, and what country?! And took prisoners, killed, captured and enslaved, so to God we belong and to Him we shall return! That is because of what our hands have put forth and earned! Al-Hasan said about the meaning of the verse: Do not hate the calamities that befall, for there may be a matter that you hate in it your salvation, and there may be a servant of God: Sometimes a matter you fear may lead to a matter you are pleased with. The beloved was hidden from him and the hated appeared in him
2:217: It contains twelve issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: They ask you. It was mentioned earlier. Jarir bin Abdul Hamid and Muhammad bin Fadil narrated on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I have never seen a people better than the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They only asked him about thirteen issues, all of which are in the Qur’an: And they ask you about menstruation. (al-Baqarah 2:222), They ask you about the sacred month. (al-Baqarah 2:217) They only asked about what would benefit them. Ibn Abdul Barr said: There are only three of the thirteen issues in the hadith. Abu Al-Suwar narrated on the authority of Jundub bin Abdullah: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a group led by Abu Ubaidah bin Al-Harith or Ubaidah bin Al-Harith. When he went to set out, he cried out of longing for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He sent Abdullah bin Jahsh and wrote him a letter and ordered him not to read the letter until he reached such and such a place. He said: Do not force your companions to travel. When he reached the place, he read the letter and said: I hear.” And obedience to God and His Messenger, he said: So two men returned and the rest of them went on, and they met Ibn al-Hadrami and killed him, and they did not know that that day was from Rajab, so the polytheists said: You were killed in the sacred month, so God the Most High revealed: They ask you about the sacred month. It was narrated that the reason for its revelation was that two men from Banu Kalb met Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri, and he did not know that they were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was on the first day of Rajab, so he killed them, so the Quraysh said: He killed them in the sacred month, so the verse was revealed, and the opinion is that it was revealed eight times, in Jumada al-Akhira two months before Badr, and it was said in Rajab, Abu Omar said, in his book al-Durar, and when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from seeking Karz ibn Jabir, that expedition was known to Jahsh ibn Ri’ab al-Asadi and with him eight men from the Muhajireen, and they were Abu Hudhayfah ibn Utbah, Ukasha ibn Muhsin, Utbah ibn Ghazwan, Suhayl ibn Bayda al-Fahri, Saad ibn Abi Waqqas, and Amir ibn Rabia, Waqid ibn Abdullah al-Tamimi, and Khalid ibn Bakir al-Laithi. He wrote a letter to Abdullah ibn Jahsh, and ordered him not to look at it until he had traveled for two days, then to look at it and proceed as he was ordered to do and not to force any of his companions. He was their leader. Abdullah ibn Jahsh did what he was ordered to do. When he opened the letter and read it, he found in it: When you look at this letter of mine, proceed until you reach Nakhl between Mecca and Taif, and watch the Quraysh there, and learn for us some of their report. When he read the letter, he said: We hear and obey. Then he informed his companions of that, and that he would not force any of them, and that he would stand up for his face with whoever obeyed him, and that if no one obeyed him, he would go alone. Whoever loves martyrdom should stand up, and whoever hates death should return. They said: We all desire what you desire, and there is none of us who does not hear and obey the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They set out with him, and he went to the Hijaz, and Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas and `Utbah ibn Ghazwan had a camel that they were following. So they stayed behind in pursuit of him, and Abdullah bin Jahsh went with the rest of them on his way until he stopped at Nakhalah, and a caravan of Quraysh passed by them carrying raisins and merchandise in it was Amr bin Al-Hadrami, and the name of the Hadrami is Abdullah bin Abbad from the truth, and the Sadf is a clan of Hadhramaut, and Uthman bin Abdullah bin Al-Mughira, and his brother Nawfal bin Abdullah bin Al-Mughira Al-Makhzumi, and Al-Hakam bin Kaysan, a client of Banu Al-Mughira. The Muslims consulted and said: We are in the last day of Rajab, the sacred month, so if we fight them we will violate the sanctity of the sacred month, and if we leave them tonight they will enter the sanctuary, then they agreed to meet them, so Waqid bin Abdullah Al-Tamimi shot Amr bin Al-Hadrami and killed him, and they took Uthman bin Abdullah and Al-Hakam bin Kaysan prisoner, and Nawfal bin Abdullah escaped, then they brought the caravan and the two prisoners, and Abdullah bin Jahsh said to them: Set aside from what we have taken as spoils the fifth for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they did, and it was the first fifth in Islam, then the Qur’an was revealed: And know “Whatever you gain of anything, a fifth of it belongs to God (al-Anfal 8:41). So God and His Messenger approved the action of Abdullah bin Jahsh and were pleased with it and established it for the nation until the Day of Resurrection. It was the first booty gained in Islam, and the first emir, and Amr bin Al-Hadrami was the first to be killed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, denounced the killing of Ibn Al-Hadrami in the sacred month, so the people fell into the hands of the people, so God, the Almighty, revealed: They ask you about the sacred month - about fighting therein until His saying: They will abide therein eternally. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted the ransom for the two prisoners. As for Uthman bin Abdullah, he died in Mecca as an unbeliever, and as for Al-Hakam bin Kaysan, he converted to Islam and stayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he was martyred at Bir Ma’unah. Sa’d and Utbah returned to Medina safely. It was said that the departure of Sa’d bin Abi Waqqas and Utbah in search of their camel was with permission from Abdullah bin Jahsh, and “when Amr bin Al-Hadrami and his companions saw the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they feared them, so he said: Abdullah bin Jahsh, the people have been frightened by you, so shave the head of one of you and let him approach them, and if they see him shaved they will believe and say: The people of Ammar, there is no harm upon you, and they consulted about fighting them, the hadith, and the Jews were optimistic and said: Waqid ignited the war, and Amr Amr Najm the war, and Al-Hadrami attended the war, and the people of Mecca sent to ransom their prisoners, and he said: We will not ransom them until Saad and Utbah come, and if they do not come we will kill them in exchange for them, so when they came he ransomed them, and as for Al-Hakam he converted to Islam and stayed in Medina until he was killed as a martyr on the day of Bir Ma’unah, and as for Uthman he returned to Mecca and died there as an unbeliever, and as for Nawfal he struck the belly of his horse on the day of the Confederates to enter the trench on the Muslims, so he fell into the trench with his horse and they were both crushed, so God killed him, and the polytheists demanded his corpse as a price, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Take him, for he is a filthy corpse and a filthy blood money, this is the reason for the revelation of the words of God, the Most High: “They ask you about the sacred month.” Ibn Ishaq mentioned that the killing of Amr ibn al-Hadrami was on the last day of Rajab, as mentioned above. Al-Tabari mentioned on the authority of al-Suddi and others that it was on the last day of Jumada al-Akhira, and the first is more famous. However, it was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was on the first night of Rajab, and the Muslims thought it was from Jumada. Ibn Atiyyah said: Al-Sahib ibn Abbad mentioned in his letter known as al-Asadiyyah that Abdullah ibn Jahsh was named the Commander of the Faithful at that time because he was appointed over a group of believers. Second: The scholars differed about the abrogation of this verse. The majority are of the opinion that it was abrogated, and that fighting the polytheists in the sacred months is permissible. They differed about its abrogator. Al-Zuhri said: It was abrogated by And fight the polytheists all together (al-Tawbah 9:365). It was said: It was abrogated by the Prophet’s invasion of Thaqeef in the sacred month, and Abu Amir’s opposition to Awtas in the sacred month. It was also said: It was abrogated by the Pledge of Ridwan to fight in Dhul-Qa’dah. This is weak, because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of the killing of Uthman in Mecca and that they were determined to fight him, he then pledged allegiance to the Muslims to repel them, not to initiate fighting them. Al-Bayhaqi mentioned on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, other than the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, following the story of al-Hadrami: Then God Almighty revealed: They ask you about fighting in the sacred month. He said: So God told them in His Book that fighting in the sacred month is forbidden as it was, and that what they consider permissible from the believers is greater than that, such as their preventing them from the path of God when… They imprisoned them, tortured them, and prevented them from migrating to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their disbelief in God and their preventing the Muslims from the Sacred Mosque during Hajj and Umrah and praying in it, and their expulsion of the people of the Sacred Mosque who were its Muslim residents, and their temptation of them from the religion, so it reached us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made Ibn al-Hadrami insane and forbade the sacred month as he used to forbid it, until God the Almighty revealed: Disavowal from God and His Messenger (al-Tawbah 9:1), and Ata’ used to say: The verse is decisive, and fighting is not permissible in the sacred months, and he would swear to that, because the verses that came after it are general in terms of time, and this is specific and the general does not abrogate the specific by agreement, and “Abu al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of Jabir who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not fight in the sacred month unless he was raided.” Third: The Almighty’s saying: Fighting therein. Sibawayh substituted fighting for it with a substitute of inclusion, because the question included the month and the fighting, meaning that the infidels ask you in astonishment at the violation of the sanctity of the month, so their question about the month was only for the sake of fighting in it. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that they ask you about fighting in the sacred month. Al-Qutbi said: They ask you about fighting in the sacred month, is it permissible? So he substituted fighting for the month, and Sibawayh recited: Qais's death was not the death of one person, but rather the destruction of a people's edifice. And Ikrimah read ((They ask you about the sacred month - killing therein. Say, killing)) without an alif in both of them. It was said that the meaning is that they ask you about the sacred month and about fighting therein. Ibn Mas`ud read this way, so it is in the accusative case with ‘an for repetition. Al-Kisa’i said this. Al-Farra’ said: It is in the accusative case with the intention of ‘an. Abu Ubaidah said: It is in the accusative case with the preposition of ‘an. Al-Nahhas said: It is not permissible to parse something in the accusative case in the Book of God or in any other speech. Rather, the preposition is a mistake. It only occurred in something irregular, which is their saying: This is a hole of a ruined lizard. The evidence that it is a mistake is the Arabs’ saying in the dual: These two: a hole of a ruined lizard. Rather, this is like the recitation. It is not permissible to interpret anything from the Book of God in this way, and it is only in the most eloquent and correct of languages. Ibn `Atiyyah said: Abu Ubaidah said: It is in the accusative case with the preposition of ‘an. His saying this is a mistake. Al-Nahhas said: It is not permissible to omit ‘an, and the statement about it is that it is a substitute. Al-A`raj read (They ask you about the sacred month - fighting therein) in the nominative case. Al-Nahhas said: It is ambiguous. In Arabic, the meaning is: They ask you about the sacred month. Is it permissible to fight in it? So his saying: (They ask you) indicates a question, as Imru’ al-Qais said: My friend, do you see lightning? I will show you its flash, like the sparkle of hands, crowned with love for me. The meaning is: Do you see lightning? The interrogative alif was deleted because the alif in asah indicates it, even though it is a letter of address, as the poet said: Do you leave the neighborhood or innovate? The meaning is: I go, so the alif was deleted because the word umm indicates it. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: Say, ‘Fighting therein is great’: a subject and a predicate, meaning something objectionable, because the prohibition of fighting in the sacred month was established at that time, since the initiator was from the Muslims, and the month in the verse is a generic noun, and God had made the sacred month a basis for the Arabs to be moderate in, so they did not shed blood, nor did they change the sacred months, which are Rajab, Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, and Muharram, three in a row and one in isolation, and more clarification of this will come in Al-Ma’idah, God willing. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: And he averted from the way of God is an introduction. And disbelieved in it is an appositive to averted. “And the Sacred Mosque” is an appositive to the way of God. “And expelling his people from it” is an appositive to averted which is the predicate of the introduction. Greater in the sight of God means greater in sin than fighting in the sacred month. This was stated by Al-Mubarrad and others, and this is correct, due to the length of time that people were prevented from circumambulating the Kaaba. And disbelieved in it means in God. It was also said: And disbelieved in it means the Hajj and the Sacred Mosque. And expelling his people from it is greater means greater in punishment with God than fighting in the sacred month. Al-Farra’ said: Averted is an appositive to great, and and the mosque is an appositive to the ha in it, so the speech is a continuous sequence that is not interrupted. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is wrong, because the meaning leads to his statement: And disbelieved in it meaning in God is also an appositive to great. And it comes from that that expelling the people of the mosque from it is greater than disbelief in God, and this is clearly corrupt. The meaning of the verse, according to the majority of scholars, is: You, the infidels of Quraysh, consider fighting in the sacred month too great for us. What you do in terms of turning away from the path of God whoever wants Islam, and your disbelief in God and your expulsion of the people of the mosque from it, as you did to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, is a greater crime before God. Abdullah ibn Jahsh, may God be pleased with him, said: You consider murder in a forbidden manner a great sin, and worse than that, if only a mature person could see the right path. You turned away from what Muhammad said and disbelieved in him, and God is the witness and the seer. And you expel the people of God from the mosque, lest anyone be seen prostrating to God in the house. Even if you reproach us for killing him and spread rumors about Islam, he is a rebel and an envious person. We watered our spears with the help of Ibn Al-Hadrami in a palm tree when he kindled the war. Blood and Ibn Abdullah Othman are among us, and he is being disputed by spite from the old man who has become stubborn Al-Zuhri, Mujahid, and others said: The Almighty’s statement, Say, ‘Fighting therein is great,’ was abrogated by His statement, And fight the polytheists all together (al-Tawbah 9:36) and His statement, Then kill the polytheists (al-Tawbah 9:5). Ata’ said: It was not abrogated, and fighting is not appropriate during the sacred months, as has been mentioned previously. Sixth: The Almighty’s statement: And persecution is worse than killing. Mujahid and others said: The persecution here is disbelief, meaning your disbelief is greater than our killing of those people. The majority said: The meaning of the persecution here is their temptation of the Muslims from their religion until they perish, meaning that this is more serious than your killing in the sacred month. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And they will not cease is the beginning of a report from God Almighty, and a warning from Him to the believers against the evil of the infidels. Mujahid said, meaning the infidels of Quraysh, and they will turn you back is in the accusative case with until because it is an abstract goal. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And whoever turns back meaning, returns from Islam to disbelief their deeds have become worthless meaning, they have become invalid and corrupt. From this comes the word habat, which is a corruption that affects livestock in their stomachs from eating too much grass, so their stomachs swell, and they may die from that. So the verse is a threat to the Muslims to remain steadfast in the religion of Islam. Ninth: Scholars differed regarding the apostate: should he be given the opportunity to repent or not? Are his deeds nullified by the apostasy itself or not, except in the case of declaring unbelief? Is he to be inherited or not? These are three issues: The first: A group said: He is given a chance to repent, and if he repents, well and good, otherwise he is killed. Some of them said: One hour. Others said: He is given a chance to repent for a month. Others said: He is given a chance to repent for three times, based on what was narrated from Umar and Uthman, and it is the opinion of Malik narrated from him by Ibn al-Qasim. Al-Hasan said: He is given a chance to repent a hundred times. It was narrated from him that he is killed without being given a chance to repent, and this is what al-Shafi’i said in one of his two opinions, and it is one of the opinions of Tawus and Ubayd ibn Umair. Sahnun mentioned that Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salamah al-Majshun used to say: The apostate is killed and is not given a chance to repent. He used as evidence the hadith of Muadh and Abu Musa, in which it says: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abu Musa to Yemen, Muadh ibn Jabal followed him. When he arrived, he said: Get down, and he threw a pillow to him. There was a man with him who was bound. He said: What is this?
