He said: This man was a Jew who converted to Islam, then he returned to his bad religion and became a Jew. He said: I will not sit down until he is killed, the decree of God and His Messenger. He said: Sit down. He said: Yes, I will not sit down until he is killed, the decree of God and His Messenger - three times.” Abu Yusuf reported on the authority of Abu Hanifa that the apostate is offered Islam, and if he converts to Islam, then fine, otherwise he is killed on the spot, unless he asks for a reprieve. If he asks for that, he is given a reprieve of three days. The well-known opinion from him and his companions is that the apostate is not killed until he is given a chance to repent. According to them, the heretic and the apostate are the same. Malik said: The heretics are killed and are not given a chance to repent. This was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. They differed regarding the one who leaves disbelief for disbelief. Malik and the majority of the jurists said: He is not to be exposed, because he has moved to what he was upon at the beginning, he would have been left in it. Ibn Abd Al-Hakam reported on the authority of Al-Shafi’i that he is to be killed, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Whoever changes his religion, kill him. He did not specify a Muslim from a disbeliever. Malik said: The meaning of the hadith is whoever leaves Islam for disbelief. As for whoever leaves disbelief for disbelief, this hadith does not mean that. This is the opinion of a group of jurists. The well-known opinion from Al-Shafi’i is what Al-Muzani and Al-Rabi’ mentioned, that the one who changes his religion from the People of the Covenant is to be placed by the Imam in the land of war and expelled. From his country and his money is made permissible with the money of the belligerents if he has taken control of the house, because he was only given the protection of the religion that he had at the time of the covenant. They differed regarding the apostate. Malik, Al-Awza’i, Al-Shafi’i and Al-Layth ibn Sa’d said: She is killed just as the apostate is killed, and their proof is the apparent meaning of the hadith: Whoever changes his religion, kill him. The word whoever is valid for both males and females. Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah and his companions said: The apostate is not killed. This is the opinion of Ibn Shabramah, and Ibn Ulayyah agreed with him. This is the opinion of Ata’ and Al-Hasan. They argued that Ibn Abbas narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever changes his religion, kill him. Then Ibn Abbas did not kill the apostate. Whoever narrated a hadith is more knowledgeable about its interpretation, and something similar was narrated from Ali. And “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the killing of women and children.” The first scholars cited as evidence his saying, peace be upon him: “The blood of a Muslim man is not permissible except in one of three cases: disbelief after faith.” So it included everyone who disbelieved after his faith, and this is more correct. Tenth: Al-Shafi’i said: If someone apostatizes and then returns to Islam, his deeds and the Hajj he completed are not nullified. Rather, if he dies, then his deeds are nullified. Malik said: They are nullified by the apostasy itself. The difference of opinion appears regarding a Muslim who performs Hajj, then apostatizes and then converts to Islam. Malik said: Hajj is obligatory for him, because the first one was nullified by apostasy. Al-Shafi’i said: He does not have to repeat it, because his deeds remain. Our scholars have cited as evidence the words of God Almighty: If you associate others with God, your deeds will surely become worthless (al-Zumar 39:65). They said: This is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation, because apostasy is impossible for him according to the Shari’ah. The companions of Al-Shafi’i said: Rather, it is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in order to be harsh on the nation and to clarify that if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, despite his noble status, were to associate others with God, his deeds would become worthless. So how about you? But he does not associate because of the superiority of his rank, as He said: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her (al-Ahzab 33:30), and that is because of the honor of their status, otherwise it is not conceivable that they would commit it to protect their honored and respected husband, Ibn Al-Arabi. Our scholars said: God only mentioned the agreement as a condition here because He made eternal punishment in the Fire a condition for us, so whoever agreed to disbelief, God will make him eternal in the Fire by this verse, and whoever associates partners, his work will be nullified by the other verse, so they are two verses that provide two different meanings and rulings, and what he was addressed with, peace be upon him, is for his nation until its specificity is proven, what was mentioned about his wives, it was only said about them to show that if it were conceivable, it would be two violations, one of them to the sanctity of the religion, and the second to the sanctity of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for every violation of sanctity there is a punishment, and that is placed in the position of someone who disobeyed in the sacred month or in the sacred land or in the sacred mosque, the punishment will be doubled for him by the number of Violation of sanctities, and God knows best. Eleventh: The scholars differed regarding the inheritance of the apostate. Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, al-Sha’bi, al-Hakam, al-Layth, Abu Hanifa, and Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said: The inheritance of the apostate goes to his Muslim heirs. Malik, Rabi’ah, Ibn Layla, al-Shafi’i, and Abu Thawr said: His inheritance goes to the public treasury. Ibn Shabramah, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, and al-Awza’i said in one of the two narrations: What the apostate acquired after apostasy goes to his Muslim heirs. Abu Hanifa said: What the apostate acquired during his apostasy is spoils of war, and what was acquired during his time as a Muslim and then he apostatized is inherited by his Muslim heirs. As for Ibn Shabramah, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad, they do not differentiate between the two matters. The absolute statement of the Prophet, peace be upon him: There is no inheritance between people of two religions, indicates the invalidity of their statement. They agreed that his infidel heirs do not inherit from him, except for Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said: They inherit from him.
2:218: The twelfth: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who believed and those who emigrated the verse, Jundub bin Abdullah and Urwah bin Az-Zubayr and others said, when Waqid bin Abdullah At-Tamimi killed Amr bin Al-Hadrami in the sacred month, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stopped taking the fifth of it that Abdullah bin Jahsh had succeeded in imposing on him and on the two captives, so the Muslims were harsh with Abdullah bin Jahsh and his companions until it was difficult for them, so God Almighty compensated them with this verse in the sacred month and relieved them, and informed that they will have the reward of those who emigrated and fought, so the reference to them in His saying: Indeed, those who believed then it remains in everyone who did what God Almighty mentioned, and it was said: If they did not commit a sin then they will have no reward, so God revealed: Indeed, those who believed and those who emigrated to the end of the verse. And migration means moving from one place, and the intention to leave the first is to prefer the second, and migration is the opposite of connection, and he abandoned it with abandonment and abandonment, and the noun is migration, and migration from one land to another is leaving the first for the second, and migration is crossing, and whoever said: migration is moving from the desert to the city has misled, because that was the most common among the Arabs, and the people of Mecca are not migrants according to his saying: (And strive) is a mutual action from jahada if he extracted effort, striving and jihad, and striving and striving: exerting one’s effort and exerting one’s utmost, and jihad with the fat-ha: the solid ground, (and they hope) means they covet and seek closeness, and he only said (they hope and he praised them because no one in this world knows that he will go to Paradise even if he reaches every level in the obedience of God, for two reasons: one of them - he does not know what will be his end, and the second - so that he does not rely on his work, and hope is a blessing, and hope is always with fear and inevitably, just as fear is with hope, and hope is from hope Extended, it is said: I hoped for so-and-so with hope and hope, it is said: I only came to you hoping for good, and I hoped for him and I hoped for him and I hoped for him and they all mean I hoped for him, Bishr said addressing his daughter: Please be patient and wait for my return if Al-Qaradh Al-Anzi is not here I have no hope in so-and-so, that is, I do not hope. Hope and rajaa may mean fear. God Almighty said: What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God? (Nuh: 13), that is, you do not fear the greatness of God. Abu Dhu’ayb said: If a bee stings him, he does not want to be stung by it, and he opposes it in the house of Nubb factors That is, he was not afraid and did not care. The hope - shortened - is the side of the well and its edges, and every side is a hope. The common people make a mistake when they say: O great hope, so they shorten and do not extend.
2:219: It contains nine issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: They ask you. The questioners are the believers, as mentioned above. Wine is taken from the word khamr which means to cover, and from it is the word khimar for a woman. Everything that covers something has been khamr, and from it is khamrū anītakum cover your vessels. Wine khamrizes the mind, that is, it covers it and conceals it. And from that, the intertwined tree is called khamr with the mīm open because it gives what is beneath it and conceals it. It is said from it that the earth khamrāt means its wine has increased. The poet said: Oh Zaid and Ad-Dahhak, go ahead, for you have crossed the road’s wine. Either you walk in peace, for you have crossed the valley in which the wolf and others hide. Al-Ajjaj said, describing an army that walks with banners and armies, not being disdainful: In the shining of eagles, the wine does not walk, the earth is directed and the trees are driven And from this is their saying: He entered the midst of the people and their wine, meaning he is in a hidden place, so since wine conceals and covers the mind, it was called that. And it was said: Wine was called wine because it was left until it ripened, just as it is said: The dough has fermented, meaning it has reached its ripeness, and the opinion was fermented, meaning it was left until the face became clear in it. And it was said: Wine was called wine because it mixes with the mind, from fermentation, which is mixing. And from this is their saying: He entered the wine of the people, meaning it mixed with them, so the three meanings are close, so the wine was left and fermented until it ripened, then it mixed with the mind, then it fermented it, and the origin is concealment. Wine: is the water of grapes that has been boiled or cooked. Whatever intoxicates the mind is subject to its ruling, because the consensus of scholars is that all gambling is forbidden. Gambling was mentioned among them, so it was all made an analogy to gambling. Gambling was only gambling in the islands specifically, so likewise everything that was wine is in its place. Second: The majority of the nation is of the opinion that whatever intoxicates in large quantities other than grape wine is forbidden, whether in small quantities or in large quantities, and the prescribed punishment for that is obligatory. Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, Ibn Abi Layla, Ibn Shabrama, and a group of the jurists of Kufa said: Whatever intoxicates in large quantities other than grape wine is not permissible, and if someone becomes intoxicated by it without intentionally reaching the point of intoxication, then there is no prescribed punishment for him. This is weak and is refuted by consideration and the hadith, as will be explained in al-Ma’idah wa al-Nahl, God willing. Third: Some commentators said: God Almighty did not leave anything of honor and righteousness without giving it to this nation, and from His honor and kindness is that He did not impose the laws on them all at once, but rather imposed them time after time, so likewise the prohibition of alcohol, and this verse was the first to be revealed regarding the matter of alcohol, then after it Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated (An-Nisa’: 43), then His saying: “Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling and to avert you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. So will you not desist?” (al-Ma’idah 5:91), then His saying: Intoxicants, gambling, idolatry, and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it (al-Ma’idah 5:90) as will be explained in (Al-Ma’idah). Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And gambling. Gambling is the gambling of the Arabs with arrows. Ibn Abbas said: In the pre-Islamic period, a man would gamble with his family and his money. Whichever of them the other gambled with, he would take his money and his family. So the verse was revealed. Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Sirin, al-Hasan, Ibn al-Musayyab, Ata’, Qatadah, Mu’awiyah ibn Salih, Tawus, Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and Ibn Abbas also said: Everything in which there is gambling, such as dice and chess, is gambling, even children playing with nuts and dice, except for what is permitted of betting on horses and drawing lots to allocate rights, as will come. Malik said: Gambling is of two types: gambling of amusement and gambling of gambling. Among the gambling of amusement are dice, chess, and all amusements. Gambling of gambling is what people gamble on. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: Chess is the gambling of the Persians, and everything that is gambled with is gambling according to Malik and other scholars. More clarification of this chapter will come in Yunus, God willing. Gambling is derived from the word yusr, which means that something is obligatory for its owner. It is said: He made such-and-such easy for me if it is obligatory, so he makes it easy, yusr, and yasir. The gambler is the player with lots, and he may make it easy, yasr. The poet said: So help them and make things easy for them, and if they are in distress, then make things easy for them. Al-Azhari said: Maysar is the camel that they used to gamble on. It was called Maysar because it is divided into parts, so it is as if it is the place of division, and everything that you divide, you have made easy. Al-Yasir is the butcher, because he divides the meat of the camel. He said: This is the origin of Al-Yasir. Then it is said to those who throw lots and gamble on the camel: Yasroon, because they are butchers since they were the cause of that. In Al-Sahah: And the people cut the camel, meaning they cut it and divided its parts. Suhaim bin Watheel Al-Yarboui said: I say to them, by the people, when they make me easy, have you not despaired that I am the son of a knight who has asceticism? He was captured and shot with arrows. It is said: The people gambled when they gambled. A man is yasar and yasar means the same thing, and the plural is yasar. Al-Nabigha said: I complete my left hand, I give them both hands, and I clothe the eyelid with blood. Tarafa said: They are the wealth of Luqman when winter brings heavy rains. Whoever volunteered to slaughter it was praised by them. The poet said: And Najiah slaughtered for the sake of the truthful people, and I did not call out to the left of the islands. Fifth: Malik narrated in Al-Muwatta’ on the authority of Dawud ibn Husayn that he heard Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab say: It was gambling among the people of the Jahiliyyah to sell meat for one or two sheep. This is understood by Malik and the majority of his companions to refer to one type, one animal for its meat. According to him, this is a case of muzabanah, “gharar,” and gambling, because one does not know whether the animal has the same meat as the one given, or less or more. Selling meat for meat is not permissible if it is different. So selling an animal for meat is like selling meat hidden in its hide if they are of the same type. According to him, one type is camels, cows, sheep, gazelles, ibex, and all wild animals. Quadrupeds are all one type. It is not permissible to sell anything from an animal of this type, and the entire type for one thing from its meat in any way, because according to him it is a case of muzabanah, like selling raisins for grapes, olives for oil, and shirj for sesame, and the like. According to him, birds are all one type, as are whales, fish and other things. It was narrated from him that locusts alone are a type. Al-Shafi’i and his companions and Al-Layth ibn Saeed said: No. It is permissible to sell meat for an animal in any case, whether of the same type or of two different types, according to the generality of the hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that camels were slaughtered during the time of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and divided into ten parts. A man said: Give me a part of it for a sheep. Abu Bakr said: This is not permissible. Al-Shafi’i said: I do not know of any Companions who disagreed with Abu Bakr on this. Abu Umar said: It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he permitted the sale of a sheep for meat, but not for a live one. Abd al-Razzaq mentioned on the authority of al-Thawri on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab that he disliked selling a live animal for a dead one, meaning a slaughtered sheep for a live one. Sufyan said: We do not see anything wrong with it. Al-Muzani said: If the hadith is not authentic regarding the sale of an animal for meat, then analogy is that it is permissible. If it is authentic, analogy is invalidated and the tradition is followed. Abu Umar said: The Kufians have many arguments regarding the permissibility of selling meat for an animal from the perspective of analogy and consideration. However, if the tradition is authentic, analogy and consideration are invalidated. Malik narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he forbade the sale of animals for meat,” Abu Omar said, “I do not know of it being connected to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, through a reliable source. The best of its chains of transmission is the mursal of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, according to what Malik mentioned in his Muwatta’, and al-Shafi`i agreed with it. His principle is that mursals are not accepted, except that he claimed that he looked for the mursals of Sa`id and found them, or most of them, to be authentic. So he disliked selling types of animals for types of meat based on the apparent meaning of the hadith and its generality, because there is no trace that specifies it or consensus, and it is not permissible for him to specify the text by analogy. Animal, in his view, is the name for everything that lives on land and in water, even if its types differ, like food, which is the name for everything that is eaten or drunk, so know.” Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: In them” meaning wine and gambling there is a great sin. The sin of wine is what comes from the drinker of quarreling, cursing, saying obscene and false words, and the loss of reason by which he knows what is due to his Creator, and neglecting prayers and sweating from the remembrance of God, and other than that. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, who said: Avoid wine, for it is the mother of all evils. There was a man from among those who came before you who worshipped, but a woman who was a pervert caught him. She sent her slave girl to him and said to him: We call you to bear witness. So he went with her slave girl, and she began to close every door she entered, until he reached a beautiful woman who had a boy and a bowl of wine. She said: By God, I did not call you to bear witness, but I called you to have intercourse with me, or to drink a cup of this wine, or to kill this boy. He said: Then give me a cup of this wine. So she gave him a cup. He said: Add more, but he did not throw anything until he had intercourse with her and killed the soul. So avoid wine. By God, faith and addiction to alcohol do not come together, except that one of them will soon drive the other out. Abu Omar mentioned in Al-Isti’ab, and it was narrated that when Al-A’sha headed to Madinah to convert to Islam, some of the polytheists met him on the road and said to him: Where are you going? He told them that he wanted to go to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: Do not go to him, for he orders you to pray. He said: Serving the Lord is obligatory. They said: He orders you to give money to the poor. He said: Doing good is obligatory. It was said to him: He forbids adultery. He said: It is obscene and ugly in the mind, and I have become an old man, so I do not need it. It was said to him: He forbids drinking alcohol. He said: As for this, I cannot be patient with it! He returned and said: I will drink wine for a year and then return to it. He did not reach his home until he fell from the camel and his neck was broken and he died. Qais bin Asim Al-Manqari used to drink it in the pre-Islamic era, then he forbade it to himself. The reason for that was that he winked at his daughter Uqnah while he was drunk, and he cursed his parents, and he saw the moon and said something, and he gave the drunkard a lot of his money, so when he came to his senses he was informed of that and he forbade it to himself. In it he says: I saw that wine is good, but it has qualities that corrupt a patient man. I swear to God, I will never drink it while healthy, nor will I ever cure a sick person with it. I would not give my life for it, and I would never pray for a companion for it. Wine disgraces its drinkers and brings about great harm to them. Abu Omar said: Ibn al-A’rabi narrated on the authority of al-Mufaddal al-Dhabi that these verses were written by Abu Mahjan al-Thaqafi, who said them about his abandonment of alcohol. He is the one who said, may God be pleased with him: If I die, bury me next to a vine, so that its roots will water my bones after my death. Do not bury me in the desert, for I fear that when I die I will not taste it. And Omar flogged him repeatedly for it, and exiled him to an island in the sea, so he joined Saad, so Omar wrote to him to imprison him, so he imprisoned him, and he was one of the brave men, and when what happened to him in the Battle of Al-Qadisiyyah was what is known, he removed his chains and said: We will never flog you for alcohol again, Abu Mihjan said: And by God, I will never drink it, so he did not drink it after that, in a narration: I used to drink it when the punishment was carried out on me and I was purer than it, but as it dazzled me, by God, I will never drink it, and Al-Haytham bin Adi mentioned that he was informed by someone who saw the grave of Abu Mihjan in Azerbaijan, or he said: in the regions of Gorgan, and three vine roots had grown on it and had grown tall and bore fruit, and they were trellised over his grave, and written on the grave was (This is the grave of Abu Mihjan) He said: So I began to wonder and remember his saying: If I die, bury me next to a vine Then the drinker becomes a laughingstock for the wise, playing with his urine and excrement, perhaps wiping his face, until some of them were seen wiping their faces with their urine and saying: O God, make me among those who repent and make me among those who purify themselves, and some of them were seen with a dog licking his face and saying to him: May God honor you. As for gambling, it causes enmity and hatred, because it is the unjust consumption of others’ money. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And benefits for people. As for wine, it is the profit of trade, as they used to bring it from the Levant at a low price and sell it in the Hijaz at a profit, and they did not see any resistance to it, so the one seeking wine would buy it at a high price. This is the most correct of what has been said about its benefits. It has been said about its benefits: it digests food, strengthens weakness, helps with sexual desire, makes the miser generous, encourages the coward, and purifies the complexion, in addition to other pleasures in it. Hassan ibn Thabit, may God be pleased with him, said: We drink it and it leaves us kings and lions, and the encounter will never end. And other joys, and another said: If I drink, I am the Lord of Al-Khawarnaq and Al-Sudair And if I wake up, I am the master of the little girl and the camel The benefit of gambling is that something is given to a person in a game without toil or fatigue. They would buy camels and shoot their arrows. Whoever’s arrow came out would take his share of the meat and would not have to pay anything from the price. Whoever’s arrow remained would have to pay the entire price of the camels and would not have any of the meat. It was said that its benefit was to provide for the needy, because whoever gambled among them would not eat from the camels and would distribute them to the needy. The arrows of gambling are eleven arrows, seven of which have shares and have duties according to the number of shares, and they are: (Al-Fadh), in which there is one mark and he has a share and he has a share if he fails, the second (Al-Tawam), in which there are two marks and he has two shares and he has a share, the third (Al-Raqeeb), in which there are three marks as we mentioned, the fourth (Al-Halas), and it has four, the fifth (Al-Nafiz) and also Al-Nafiz and it has five, the sixth (Al-Musabil) and it has six, the seventh (Al-Mu’alla) and it has seven, so that is twenty-eight duties and the shares of the roots are likewise according to Al-Asma’i, and four arrows remain, which are the Ighfal, which have no duties or shares, and they are (Al-Masdar), (Al-Mud’af), (Al-Munih) and (Al-Safeh) and it was said that the remaining three are the Ighfal: (Al-Safeh), (Al-Munih) and (Al-Raghdah) These three are added so that the arrows are many for the one who is juggling them so that he does not find a way to incline with anyone, and it is called The Mujil al-Mufidh, al-Darib, and al-Darib, and the plural is al-Dariba. It was said: He places a guard behind him so that he does not favor anyone. Then the Dharib kneels on his knees, covers himself with a garment, sticks out his head, and puts his hand in the rababa and comes out. It was the custom of the Arabs to strike camels with these arrows in the winter, when time was tight and the cold was severe on the poor. He would buy the camels and the wealthy would guarantee their price and satisfy their owner with his right. They would be proud of that and criticize whoever did not do that among them, and they would call it (al-Barm). Mutammam bin Nuwaira said: Nor do women bring gifts to his wedding when the stubble is crackling from the cold of winter. Then it is slaughtered and divided into ten parts. Ibn Atiyah said: Al-Asma’i made a mistake in dividing the camels, as he mentioned that they are twenty-eight parts according to the shares of the arrows, and this is not the case. Then it is multiplied by ten, and whoever wins his arrow by coming out of the rababah first takes his shares and gives them to the poor. The rababah with a kasrah on the ra’ is similar to the quiver in which the arrows of gambling are collected, and perhaps they called all the arrows a rababah. Abu Dhu’ayb said, describing the donkey that came to him: As if they were a lute, and as if it were joy overflowing onto the cup and cracking The rababa also means the covenant and the pact. The poet said: I was a man who entrusted my lute to you, and before you I was a lute, and I lost my lute. Sometimes they may advance for themselves, and then the one whose share did not win is charged the price, as mentioned above. The poor people of the neighborhood live by this method, and from it is the saying of Al-A’sha: They feed the guest when they are hungry and provide food for the poor. And from it the other said: In their hands are broken and locked, and the provisions of the chaste are returned to them. And al-Munih in this verse is the one who is given a gift, because they borrow the arrow that has been smooth and has many victories, so that is the praised al-Munih. As for al-Munih who is one of the ignorant, that is only described as a generous one, and that is what al-Akhtal meant when he said: They turned to Fazara with the kindness of the generous, and then they turned and looked around. In Al-Sahah: Al-Manih is a share of the shares of gambling, which has no share unless its owner is given something. And from gambling is the saying of Labid: If they were to be affluent, their affluence would not cause them to commit indecencies that would be remembered in summer resorts. All of this is the benefit of gambling, except that it is consuming money unjustly. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And their sin is greater than their benefit. God, the Almighty, the Majestic, knows that sin is greater than benefit, and that harm returns in the Hereafter. So the major sin after the prohibition and benefits is less prohibition. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read katheer with a triple tha’, and their argument is: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed alcohol and cursed ten with it: its seller, its buyer, the one for whom it is purchased, its presser, the one for whom it is pressed, its server, its drinker, its carrier, the one for whom it is carried, and the one who eats its price.” Also, the collection of benefits is appropriate with the collection of sins, and katheer with a triple tha’ gives that. The rest of the readers and the majority of people read kabeer with a unified ba’, and their argument is that the sin of gambling and drinking alcohol are major sins, so describing it as major is more appropriate. Also, their agreement on akbar is an argument for kabeer with a single ba’, and they agreed to reject akhar with a triple tha’, except in the copy of Abdullah bin Mas’ud. It contains: “Say: There is much sin in them” and Their sin is greater with the letter tha in both letters. Ninth: Some people of insight said: Wine was forbidden by this verse, because God Almighty said: “Say: My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed - and sin” (al-A’raf 7:33). So He informed in this verse that there is a sin in it, so it is forbidden. Ibn Atiyah said: This view is not good, because the sin in it is what is forbidden, not it itself, as this view requires. I said: Some of them said: In this verse there is evidence of the prohibition of alcohol because He called it a sin, and sin has been prohibited in another verse, which is the saying of the Almighty: “Say: My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed” (al-A’raf 7:33). And some of them said: He meant by sin alcohol, based on the saying of the poet: I drank sin until my mind went astray, so sin takes away minds I said: This is also not good, because God Almighty did not call wine a sin in this verse, but rather He said: “Say: In them is a great sin,” and He did not say: Say: They are a great sin. As for the verse of Al-A’raf and the verse of poetry, the discussion of them will come there clearly, God Almighty willing. Qatada said: In this verse there is only condemnation of wine, as for the prohibition it is known from another verse, which is the verse of Al-Ma’idah, and this is what most of the commentators agree with. God Almighty says: “And they ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘The excess.’ Thus does God make clear to you the signs that you may give thought * In this world and the Hereafter.” There are three issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: ‘Al-Afuw’” The reading of the majority is in the accusative case, and Abu Amr alone read it in the nominative case, and Ibn Kathir differed on it. Al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read in the nominative case. An-Nahhas and others said: If you make tha in the sense of who, then the preferred nominative case is based on the meaning: what they spend is what is pardon, and the accusative case is permissible. If you make ma and tha one thing, then the preferred case is in the accusative case based on the meaning: say they spend what is pardon, and the nominative case is permissible. The grammarians said: What did you learn, grammar or poetry? In the accusative and nominative cases, based on the fact that they are both good and fine, except that the interpretation in the verse is in the accusative case. The second: The scholars said: Since the question in the previous verse in the Almighty’s saying And they ask you, what they should spend, was a question about spending to whom it should be spent, as we explained and the answer indicated, and the answer came out in accordance with the question, the second question in this verse was about the amount of spending, and it is in the case of Amr ibn al-Jamuh - as mentioned above - because when the verse was revealed, “Say: Whatever you spend of good is for the parents” (al-Baqarah 2:215), he said: How much should I spend? Then the verse was revealed, “Say: ‘The excess.’” And the excess is what is easy, simple, and extra, and it is not difficult for the heart to give it out. From this is the saying of the poet: Pardon me, so that you may maintain my affection, and do not speak ill of me when I am angry. The meaning is: Spend what is left over from your needs, and do not harm yourselves with it so that you become dependent. This is the first thing that has been said in the interpretation of the verse, and it is the meaning of the statement of Al-Hasan, Qatada, Ata, Al-Suddi, Al-Qurazi Muhammad bin Kaab, Ibn Abi Laila and others. They said: Pardon is what is left over from the family, and something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid said: Charity from one’s surplus wealth. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) also said: The best charity is that which is spent from one’s surplus wealth. And in another hadith: The best charity is that which is given from one’s surplus wealth. Qais bin Saad said: This is the obligatory zakat. The majority of scholars said: Rather, it is voluntary expenditures. It was said: It was abrogated. Al-Kalbi said: After the revelation of this verse, if a man had money of gold, silver, crops or livestock, he would look at what would suffice his family for a year’s expenses, keep it and give the rest in charity. If he was one of those who worked with his hands, he would keep what would suffice him and his family for a day and give the rest in charity, until the verse of the obligatory zakat was revealed, and this verse was abrogated and all of it was abrogated. Charity that they ordered, and some people said: It is a ruling, and in money even other than zakat, and the apparent meaning indicates the first statement. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Thus does God make clear to you the signs. Al-Mufaddal bin Salamah said: That is, in the matter of spending: so that you may reflect.
2:220: "In this world and the Hereafter" So you keep from your wealth what will benefit you in this worldly life and spend the rest on what will benefit you in the Hereafter. It was said: There is an inversion in the speech, meaning that thus God explains to you the signs concerning the matter of this world and the Hereafter so that you may reflect upon this world and its passing and passing away and become indifferent to it, and upon the coming of the Hereafter and its permanence and desire it. The Almighty’s saying: They ask you about orphans to His saying wise contains eight issues: First: Abu Dawud and Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: When God the Almighty revealed: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best (al-An’am 6:152), and Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly (An-Nisa’: 10), whoever had an orphan set aside his food and held it back for him until he ate it or spoiled it. This was difficult for them, so they mentioned it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God the Almighty revealed: “And they ask you about orphans. Say, ‘Improvement for them is best.’” So they mixed their food with his food and their drink with his drink. The wording of Abu Dawud, and the verse is connected to what came before it, because the mention of money was coupled with the command to preserve the money of orphans. It was said that the questioner was Abdullah bin Rawahah, and it was said that the Arabs considered mixing the money of orphans in eating with them a bad omen, so this verse was revealed. Second: When God Almighty permitted mixing with orphans with the intention of reforming them by looking at them and in them, this was evidence of the permissibility of disposing of the orphan’s money, such as the guardian’s disposal of the sale, division, and other things, in general terms, according to this verse. So if a man takes care of an orphan and possesses him and is in charge, his action is permissible even if he does not put him in charge of his guardianship, because the verse is general and guardianship is general authority. It has not been reported from any of the caliphs that he put anyone in charge of an orphan even though they were present in their time, but rather they were limited to them being with them. Third: The reports have been transmitted in paying the orphan’s money as speculation and trading in it, and in the permissibility of mixing his money with his own money, indicating the permissibility of disposing of his money by buying and selling if it is in accordance with what is good, and the permissibility of paying it as speculation, and other than that as we will mention clearly. And there is a difference of opinion regarding his doing it as a loan, so Ashhab forbade it, and compared it to his being forbidden from selling to them from himself or buying for them, and another said: If he takes it for a portion of the profit in proportion to a loan like it in it, it is valid, like his buying something for the orphan by following up, so it is better for the orphan. Muhammad bin Abdul Hakam said: And he has the right to sell to him on credit if he sees that as a consideration. Ibn Kinanah said: And he has the right to spend on the orphan’s wedding what is suitable from work and perfume, and his interest according to his situation and the situation of the one he marries to and according to the amount of his money. He said: And likewise in his circumcision, if he fears that he will be accused of raising that authority, he orders him to be moderate, and everything he does as a consideration is permissible, and what he does as a favoritism and bad consideration is not permissible, and the apparent meaning indicates that the guardian of the orphan informs him of the matter. This world and the Hereafter, and he hires and rents for him someone who teaches him crafts. If he gives something to an orphan, then the guardian has the right to take it because of the reform in it. This will be further explained in Women, God willing. Fourth: As for what the guardian and guarantor spend from the orphan’s money, there are two cases: a case in which he can have witnesses to it, so his statement is not accepted except with evidence, and a case in which he cannot have witnesses to it, so his statement is accepted without evidence. So whatever real estate he buys and what is customary to be documented in it is not accepted without evidence. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: Therefore, our companions distinguished between the orphan being in the guardian’s house and he spending on him, so he is not required to have witnesses to his expenses and clothing, because it is difficult for him to have witnesses to what he eats and wears at all times. But if he says: I spent for a year, it is accepted from him, and between him being with a slave girl or his nanny, so the guardian claims that he was spending on him, or that he was giving the mother or nanny expenses and clothing, so the statement of the mother or nanny is not accepted except with evidence that she was receiving that for him monthly or as a contribution. Fifth: Scholars differed regarding a man who marries his orphan girl. Does he have the right to buy something for himself from the money of his orphan girl or woman? Malik said: The guardianship of marriage through sponsorship and custody is stronger than through kinship, so he said about the Bedouins who hand over their children in times of famine: They marry them as they marry them. As for the marriage of the sponsor and the custodian for himself, its explanation will come in An-Nisa’, God willing. As for buying from him, Malik said: He buys according to the well-known sayings. And Abu Hanifa said likewise: He has the right to buy the property of the orphan child for himself for more than the price of the like, because it is a reform indicated by the apparent meaning of the Qur’an. Al-Shafi’i said: This is not permissible in marriage or in sale, because the verse did not mention the disposal, rather he said: Reforming them is better without mentioning in it the one who is permitted to look at it. Abu Hanifa says: If the reform is better, then it is permissible to marry him and it is permissible to marry from him. Al-Shafi’i does not see in marriage reform except from the aspect of fulfilling a need, and there is no need before puberty. Ahmad ibn Hanbal permits the guardian to marry because it is a reform, and Al-Shafi’i permits the grandfather to marry with the guardian, and the father in the case of his son whose mother has died, not by the ruling of this verse. And Abu Hanifa allows the judge to marry off an orphan based on the apparent meaning of the Qur’an, and these schools of thought arose from this verse. If it is proven that marriage is a reform, then the apparent meaning of the verse requires its permissibility. It is possible that the meaning of the Almighty’s statement: And they ask you about orphans is that the guardians of the orphans ask you, and this is general and does not know the identity of the guardian and the guardian and what is required of them from the descriptions. If it is said: It is necessary to leave Malik’s origin in suspicion and pretexts since he permitted him to buy from his orphan, then the answer is that this is not necessary, but rather it is a pretext in what leads from forbidden actions to a forbidden thing that is stipulated. As for here, God Almighty has permitted the form of mixing, and entrusted the guardians in that to their trustworthiness by saying: And God knows the corrupter from the reformer. And every matter that is feared, and God Almighty entrusts the one charged with it to his trustworthiness, it is not said that he resorts to a forbidden thing by it and is prevented from it, just as God made women trustworthy with their private parts, with the great consequences that result from that. Their saying about that is from the rulings, and it is connected to it from the solution and the package and the lineages, even if it is permissible for them to lie, and when Tawus was asked about something from the orphans he would recite: And God knows the corrupter from the reformer, and Ibn Sirin loved the things in the orphan’s money for his advisors to gather and look for what is best for him, mentioned by Al-Bukhari, and in this is evidence of the permissibility of buying from him and he is subject to suspicion in that unless the sale in that is the sale of the ruler in a crowd of people, and Muhammad bin Abdul Hakam said: He does not buy from the estate, and there is nothing wrong with him sneaking someone to buy from it for him if he does not know that it is from him. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers. This mixing is like mixing like with like, like dates with dates. Abu Ubaid said: Mixing with orphans is when one of them has money and it is difficult for his sponsor to separate his food from him, and he finds no alternative but to mix him with his family, so he takes from the orphan’s money what he sees is sufficient for him by investigation and puts it with the expenses of his family. This may occur in excess or deficiency, so this abrogating verse came with permission for it. Abu Ubaid said: This, in my opinion, is a basis for what companions do on journeys, as they share expenses among themselves equally, and they may differ in the little or much food, and not everyone whose food is little will be content with being generous to his companion. So since this is ample in the money of orphans, it is ample in others, and were it not for that, I would have feared that the matter would be difficult for people. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: So your brothers is the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning they are your brothers, and the fa is the answer to the condition. The Almighty’s saying: And God knows the corrupter from the reformer is a warning, meaning He knows the corrupter of the orphans’ money from the reformer, so He rewards each for his reform and corruption. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And if God had willed, He would have made you suffer. Al-Hakam narrated on the authority of Muqsim on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And if God had willed, He would have made you suffer. He said: If He had willed, He would have made what you took from the orphans’ money a destructive and severe punishment, but He only willed to make it easy for you. It was said: That is, He would have charged you with what would be difficult for you to pay and your sin in mixing with them would be, as He did to those who came before you, but He made it easier for you. And suffering: hardship. And you have suffered and suffered from something else. And it is said of a mended bone if something happens to it and makes it difficult: I have suffered from it, so it is suffering and suffering. And the animal suffers from suffering from suffering, if a fracture occurs in its legs after it has been healed and it is not possible for it to run. And a blind man is a difficult climb. Ibn al-Anbari said: The origin of suffering is severity, so when the Arabs say: So-and-so is suffering from so-and-so and suffering from him and suffering from him, then it means that he is making things difficult for him and obligating him to do what is difficult for him to pay, then it was transferred to the meaning of destruction, and the origin is what we have described. God Almighty says: Indeed, God is Exalted in Might, meaning nothing is impossible for Him. Wise, He disposes of His kingdom as He wills, and nothing is restricted from Him. Glory and Exaltation be to Him, far above.
2:221: The Almighty said: “And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even though she might please you.” There are seven issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And do not marry. The majority read with the opening of the ta’, and it was read in the anomalous with the damma, as if the meaning is that the one who marries her married her from himself, and the root of the word nikah is sexual intercourse, and it is used in marriage figuratively and broadly, and its explanation will come, God willing. Second: When God, the Almighty, permitted mixing with orphans, and mixing in marriage, He made it clear that marriage with polytheists is not valid. Muqatil said: This verse was revealed about Abu Marthad al-Ghanawi, and it was said: about Marthad bin Abi Marthad, whose name was Kanaz bin Husayn al-Ghanawi. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Mecca secretly to expel a man from his companions. He had a woman in Mecca whom he loved in the pre-Islamic era, and her name was Anaq. She came to him, and he said to her: Islam has forbidden what was in the pre-Islamic era. She said: Then marry me. He said: Until he asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked his permission, but he forbade him from marrying her, because he was a Muslim and she was a polytheist. This will be explained in An-Noor, God willing. Third: The scholars differed in the interpretation of this verse. A group said: God forbade marriage to polytheistic women in Surat Al-Baqarah, then He abrogated from this sentence the women of the People of the Book, and made them permissible in Surat Al-Ma’idah. This statement was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and Malik bin Anas, Sufyan bin Sa’id Al-Thawri, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Amr Al-Awza’i said the same. Qatada and Sa’id bin Jubayr said: The wording of the verse is general for every disbelieving woman, and what is meant by it is specific for the People of the Book. The specificity was clarified in the verse of Al-Ma’idah, and the generality never included the People of the Book. This is one of the two statements of Al-Shafi’i. According to the first group, the generality includes them, then the verse of Al-Ma’idah abrogated some of the generality. This is the view of Malik, may God have mercy on him. Ibn Habib mentioned it, and he said: And marriage to a Jewish or Christian woman, even though God Almighty has permitted it, is reprehensible on its own. Ishaq bin Ibrahim Al-Harbi said: Some people went so far as to make the verse in Al-Baqarah the abrogating verse, and the verse in Al-Ma’idah the abrogated one, so they forbade marriage to every polytheistic woman. Whether written or not, Al-Nahhas said: And among the proofs for the one who says this, from what is authentically transmitted, is what Muhammad bin Rayyan told us, he said: Muhammad bin Ramh told us, he said: Al-Layth told us on the authority of Nafi’ that Abdullah bin Omar, when he was asked about a man marrying a Christian or a Jewish woman, he said: God has forbidden polytheists to the believers, and I do not know of anything greater than polytheism than a woman saying that her Lord is Jesus, or a servant of God! Al-Nahhas said: This is a statement that is outside the statement of the group that the proof is established upon, because Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Tawus, Ikrimah, Al-Sha’bi, Ad-Dahhak, and the jurists of the cities have said that it is permissible to marry the women of the People of the Book from the Companions and the Followers. Also, it is impossible for this verse from Surat Al-Baqarah to abrogate the verse in Surat Al-Ma’idah, because Al-Baqarah is one of the first to be revealed in Madinah, and Al-Ma’idah is one of the last to be revealed, and the latter abrogates the former. As for the hadith of Ibn Umar, there is no proof in it, because Ibn Umar, may God have mercy on him, was a man who hesitated, so when he heard the two verses, one of which was permission, and the other of which was prohibition, and the abrogation did not reach him, he hesitated, and the mention of abrogation was not taken from him, but rather it is interpreted according to him, and the abrogating and abrogated are not taken by interpretation. Ibn Atiyyah mentioned, and Ibn Abbas said in some of what was narrated from him: The verse is general in paganism, Zoroastrianism, and People of the Book, and everyone who is not a Muslim is forbidden, so on this basis it abrogates the verse in (Al-Ma’idah) This is seen in the statement of Ibn Umar in Al-Muwatta’: I do not know of any greater polytheism than a woman saying that her Lord is Jesus. It was narrated on the authority of Umar: He separated Talha bin Ubaidullah and Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman between two captains, and they said: We will divorce you, O Commander of the Faithful, and do not get angry. He said: If your divorce was permissible, then your marriage would be permissible! But I will separate you with a small amount of dirt. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is not well-founded, and it is based on the fact that Umar wanted to separate them, so Hudhayfah said to him: Do you claim that she is forbidden, so I will set her free, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: I do not claim that it is forbidden, but I fear that they will engage in prostitution among them. Something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Ibn al-Mundhir mentioned the permissibility of marrying women of the Book from Umar ibn al-Khattab, and from those mentioned from the Companions and Followers in the statement of al-Nahhas. He said at the end of his speech, and it is not authentic from any of the early scholars that he forbade that. Some scholars said, as for the two verses, there is no contradiction between them, because the apparent meaning of the word polytheism does not include the People of the Book, because God Almighty says: Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists do not wish that any good should be sent down to you from your Lord (al-Baqarah 2:105), and He said: Those who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture and the polytheists were not like (al-Bayyinah 2:1), so there is a difference between them in the wording, and the apparent meaning of the conjunction requires a difference between the conjoined and the conjoined to. Also, the name of polytheism is general and not explicit. God Almighty says: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture (al-Ma’idah 5:5), after His saying: And chaste women from among the believers (al-Ma’idah 5:5) is explicit, so there is no contradiction. If it is said: He meant by his saying: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you (Al-Imran: 199), and his saying: Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing (Al-Imran: 133), it is said to him: This is contrary to the text of the verse in his saying: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you and contrary to what the majority said, because it does not pose any problem to anyone regarding the permissibility of marrying someone who has converted to Islam and has become one of the prominent Muslims. If they say: God Almighty said: Those invite to the Fire so He made the reason for the prohibition of marrying them the invitation to the Fire, and the answer is that this is a reason for the saying of God Almighty: And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist because the polytheist invites to the Fire, and this reason is applied to all disbelievers, so the Muslim is better than the disbeliever absolutely, and this is clear. Fourth: As for marrying the People of the Book if they are at war, it is not permissible. Ibn Abbas was asked about that and he said: It is not permissible. He recited the words of God Almighty: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day until His words: subdued (al-Tawbah 9:29). The narrator said: I told Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i about that and he liked it. Malik disliked marrying women at war, because of the reason for leaving children in the land of war and because of her spending on wine and pork. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, informing that a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even if she is of noble lineage and wealth. Even if she pleases you, in beauty and other things. This is the saying of al-Tabari and others. It was revealed about Khansa’, a black slave girl who belonged to Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. Hudhayfah said to her: O Khansa’, you have been mentioned in the highest assembly despite your blackness and ugliness, and God Almighty has mentioned you in His Book. So Hudhayfah freed her and married her. Al-Suddi said: “It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Rawahah. He had a black slave girl, so he slapped her in anger and then regretted it. He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: What is she, O Abdullah? He said: She fasts, prays, performs ablution well, and bears witness to the two testimonies. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is a believer. Ibn Rawahah said: I will free her and marry her. So he did, and some of the Muslims criticized him and said: He married a slave girl.” They thought that they should marry polytheists, and they married them out of desire for… Their accounts, so this verse was revealed, and God knows best. Sixth: The scholars differed regarding marriage to female slaves of the People of the Book. Malik said: It is not permissible to marry a female slave of the People of the Book. Ashhab said regarding the Book of Muhammad, regarding someone who converted to Islam and had a female slave of the People of the Book under him: There is no difference between them. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: It is permissible to marry female slaves of the People of the Book. Ibn al-Arabi said: We studied with Sheikh Abu Bakr al-Shashi in Madinat al-Salam. He said: The companions of Abu Hanifa argued for the permissibility of marrying a female slave [of the People of the Book] with the words of God Almighty: And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist. The evidence from the verse is that God Almighty gave a choice between marrying a believing slave woman and a polytheist. If it were not permissible to marry a female slave of the People of the Book, God Almighty would not have given a choice between them, because the choice is only between two permissible things, not between what is permissible and what is forbidden, nor between two opposites. The answer is that the choice between two opposites is permissible linguistically and in the Qur’an, because God Almighty said: The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be the best place to settle and the best place to rest. (al-Furqan 25:24), and Omar said in his letter to Abu Musa: ( Returning to the truth is better than persisting in falsehood) Another answer, the Almighty’s saying: And for a female slave does not mean the owned slave, but rather He meant by it the human being, and the human women and men as a whole are the male and female slaves of God, said the judge in Basra, Abu al-Abbas al-Jurjani. Seventh: They differed about marrying Zoroastrian women. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, Al-Awza’i, and Ishaq forbade that. Ibn Hanbal said: I do not like it. It was narrated that Hudhayfah ibn Al-Yaman married a Zoroastrian woman, and that Umar said to him: Divorce her. Ibn Al-Qassar said: Some of our companions said: According to one of the two opinions, they have a book that allows their marriage. Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik that a Zoroastrian slave woman may not be penetrated by right of possession, and the same applies to idolaters and other disbelieving women. This is the view of a group of scholars, except for what Yahya ibn Ayoub narrated from Ibn Jurayj from Ata’ and Amr ibn Dinar that they were asked about marrying Zoroastrian slave women, and they said: There is nothing wrong with that. They interpreted the statement of God, the Almighty, And do not marry polytheistic women, so this, according to them, refers to the marriage contract, not to the purchased slave woman. They cited as evidence the captives of Awtas, and that the Companions married their slave women by right of possession. Al-Nahhas said: This is… An odd statement. As for the captives of Awtas, it may be possible that the female slaves converted to Islam, so it was permissible to marry them. As for the argument based on the words of God Almighty: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe, it is a mistake, because they interpreted marriage as meaning the contract, and marriage in the language refers to the contract and intercourse. So when He said: And do not marry polytheistic women, He forbade every marriage that occurs to polytheistic women, from marriage and intercourse. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: Al-Awza’i said: I asked Al-Zuhri about a man who buys a Zoroastrian woman, can he have intercourse with her? He said: If you testify that there is no god but God, he has intercourse with her. On the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: It is not permissible for him to have intercourse with her until she converts to Islam. Abu Omar said: The statement of Ibn Shihab, It is not permissible for him to have intercourse with her until she converts to Islam. This is because he is the most knowledgeable person about military campaigns and expeditions. This is a false statement by those who claim that the captives of Awtas had intercourse with them but did not convert to Islam. This was narrated on the authority of a group of them, including Ata’ and Amr ibn Dinar, who said: There is nothing wrong with having intercourse with a Zoroastrian woman. None of the jurists in the cities paid attention to this. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who was one of those who did not have a military campaign or a military campaign against the people of his region except the Persians and those behind them from Khurasan, and none of them were from the People of the Book. This shows you how the conduct was with their women if they were taken captive. He said: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asad informed us, he said: Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Firas informed us, he said: Ali ibn Abd Al-Aziz informed us, he said: Abu Ubaid informed us, Hisham informed us on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: A man said to him: O Abu Saeed, how were you? What would you do if you took them captive? He said: We would turn her towards the Qiblah and order her to submit and testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, then we would order her to wash herself, and if her husband wanted to have intercourse with her, he would not have intercourse with her until he had purified her. This is the interpretation of the group of scholars regarding the statement of God the Most High: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe, that they are idolaters and Zoroastrians, because God the Most High has permitted the women of the Book by His statement: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you (al-Ma’idah 5:5), meaning the chaste, not the Muslim women whose adultery was known. Some of them disliked marrying her and having intercourse with her by right hand possession unless they repented, because that would corrupt the lineage. The Almighty says: “Do not marry polytheistic men until they believe. And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even though he pleases you.” There are eleven issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And do not marry meaning do not marry a Muslim woman to a polytheist. The nation agreed that a polytheist should not have intercourse with a believing woman in any way, because that would be a disgrace to Islam. The reciters pronounce the ta in tankhawa with a damma. Ali bin Al-Hussein: Marriage with a guardian is in the Book of God, then he recited: And do not marry polytheistic women. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: It has been proven that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no marriage except with a guardian. The people of knowledge differed regarding marriage without a guardian, so many of the people of knowledge said: There is no marriage except with a guardian. This hadith was narrated on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and Ali bin Abi Talib, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, and Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with them, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Umar bin Abdul Aziz, Jabir bin Zaid, Sufyan Al-Thawri, Ibn Abi Laila, Ibn Shubramah, Ibn Al-Mubarak, Al-Shafi’i, Ubaidullah bin Al-Hasan, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Ubaid said the same. I said: It is the statement of Malik, may God be pleased with them all, and Abu Thawr and al-Tabari. He said: Abu Omar is the proof of those who say: There is no marriage without a guardian, that it has been proven that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no marriage without a guardian. This hadith was narrated by Shu’bah and al-Thawri on the authority of Ishaq on the authority of Abu Burdah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mursal hadith. So whoever accepts the mursal hadith is obligated to accept it, but whoever does not accept the mursal hadith is also obligated to do so, because those who transmitted it are people of preservation and trust, and among those who transmitted it are Isra’il and Abu ‘Awanah, both of them on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Burdah on the authority of Abu Musa on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Isra’il and those who followed him are preservers of hadith, and the preserver’s addition is accepted, and this addition is supported by principles. God Almighty said: Do not prevent them from marrying their husbands [al-Bathrah 232]. This verse was revealed about Mu’qil ibn Yasar when he prevented his sister from returning to her husband, as al-Bukhari said, and if he had not had a right to marriage, he would not have been forbidden from preventing her. I said: What also indicates this from the Book is His statement: Then marry them with the permission of their people (An-Nisa’: 25), and His statement: And marry those among you who are single (al-Nur 24:32). God Almighty did not address marriage to anyone but men. If it were to women, He would have mentioned them, and this will be explained in An-Nur. God Almighty said, narrating from Shu’aib in the story of Moses, peace be upon them both: Indeed, I want to marry you (al-Qasas 28:27), as will be explained in Surat Al-Qasas. God Almighty said: Men are the protectors and maintainers of women (An-Nisa’: 34). The Book and the Sunnah have agreed that there is no marriage except with a guardian. Al-Tabari said: In the hadith of Hafsah when she became a widow and Umar concluded the marriage contract with her and she did not conclude it, there is a nullification of the statement of those who said: The adult woman who has the right to marry herself and conclude the marriage contract without her guardian. If that were her right, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have refused to propose to Hafsah for herself if she had more right to herself than her father, and proposed to her to someone who does not have the right to marry her. And in it is an explanation of his saying, peace be upon him, The widow has more right to herself than her guardian, that the meaning of that is that she has more right to herself in that a marriage contract is concluded with her except with her consent, not that she has more right to herself in that a marriage contract is concluded with herself without her guardian. And Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A woman does not marry a woman, nor does a woman marry herself, for the adulteress is the one who marries herself. He said: A sound hadith. And Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Any woman who marries without the permission of her guardian, her marriage is invalid three times. If he has intercourse with her, then the dowry is hers for what he took from her. If they quarrel, then the ruler is the guardian of the one who has no guardian.” And this hadith is sound, and no consideration is given to what Ibn Ulayyah said on the authority of Ibn Jurayj that he said: I asked Az-Zuhri about it, but he did not know it. And no one said this on the authority of Ibn Jurayj except Ibn Ulayyah. And a group narrated it on the authority of Az-Zuhri, but they did not mention it. And if this was proven on the authority of Az-Zuhri, then there would be no proof in it, because It was narrated from him by trustworthy people, including Sulayman ibn Musa, who is a trustworthy imam, and Ja`far ibn Rabi`ah. If al-Zuhri had forgotten it, it would not have harmed him, because forgetfulness does not protect the son of Adam. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Adam forgot, so his descendants forgot. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to forget, so anyone other than him is more likely to forget. Whoever memorizes is an argument against whoever forgets. So if a trustworthy person narrates a report, the forgetfulness of the one who forgot it would not harm him. This is if what Ibn `Ulayyah narrated from Ibn Jurayj is correct, so how about when the people of knowledge have denied his narration and did not pay attention to it? I said: This hadith was narrated by Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hibban al-Tamimi al-Basti in his Musnad al-Sahih, according to the divisions and types, without any break in its chain of transmission, nor any proof of any injury to its transmitter, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ghiyath, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no marriage except with a guardian and two just witnesses. And whatever marriage is done otherwise is invalid. But if they quarrel, then the ruler is the guardian of whoever has no guardian.” Abu Hatim said: No one said in this report of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, on the authority of al-Zuhri: And two just witnesses, except three al-Nas 114:Suwayd ibn Yahya al-Umawi, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ghiyath, Abdullah ibn Abd al-Wahhab al-Jumahi, on the authority of Khalid ibn al-Harith, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Yunus al-Raqi, on the authority of Isa ibn Yunus. And nothing is authentic regarding the two witnesses other than this report. And if this report is proven, then the Book and the Sunnah have clearly stated that there is no marriage except with a guardian, so there is no meaning to what contradicts them. And al-Zuhri and al-Sha’bi used to say: If a woman is married, Abu Hanifa used to say: If a woman marries herself to a suitable man with two witnesses, then that is a valid marriage. This is the opinion of Zufar. If she marries herself to someone who is not suitable, then the marriage is valid, and the guardians have the right to separate them. Ibn al-Mundhir said: As for what al-Nu’man said, it is contrary to the Sunnah and outside the opinion of most scholars. We say with the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Abu Yusuf said: Marriage is not valid except with a guardian. If the guardian accepts Islam, then it is valid. If he refuses to accept Islam and the husband is suitable, then the judge approves it. The marriage is only completed in his opinion when the judge approves it. This is the opinion of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan used to say: The judge orders the guardian to approve it. If he does not, then he starts a new contract. There is no disagreement between Abu Hanifa and his companions that if her guardian gives her permission and she contracts the marriage herself, then it is valid. Al-Awza’i said: If she takes charge of her affairs as a man and marries her to a suitable man, then the marriage is valid, and the guardian does not have the right to separate them, unless she is an Arab woman who married a freed slave. This is similar to the Maliki school of thought, as follows. Those who follow the school of thought of al-Zuhri, Abu Hanifa, and al-Sha’bi interpreted his saying, peace be upon him: There is no marriage without a guardian, as meaning perfection, not obligation, just as he, peace be upon him, said: There is no share in Islam for one who abandons prayer. They provided evidence for this with the words of God Almighty: So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands (al-Baqarah 2:234), and His words, There is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner (al-Baqarah 2:234), and with what al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, who said: A man came to Ali, may God be pleased with him, and said: A woman, of whom I am the guardian, married without my permission? Ali said: We will look at what she did. If she married someone suitable for her, we will permit that for her. If she married someone who was not suitable for her, we will leave that to you. In Al-Muwatta’, it is reported that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, married the daughter of her brother Abd al-Rahman while he was absent. The hadith was narrated by Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she married a man, al-Mundhir ibn al-Zubayr, to a woman from her brother’s family. She put a curtain between them, then she spoke until nothing remained but the marriage contract. She ordered a man to marry him, then she said: There is no obligation on women to marry. The correct view in Malik’s hadith is that Aisha decided on the dowry and the conditions of marriage, and one of her relatives took charge of the marriage contract. The contract was attributed to Aisha because it was decided by her. Third: Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: The narrations from Malik differed regarding the saints. Who are they? He said once, whoever places a woman in a good position is her guardian, whether he is from the agnates or from the relatives or from the strangers or the imam or the executor. He said once: The guardians are from the agnates, so whoever places them in a good position is the guardian. Abu Omar said: Malik said, according to what Ibn al-Qasim mentioned from him: If a woman is married by someone other than her guardian with her permission, then if she is noble among the people, her guardian has the option to annul the marriage or approve it. If she is lowly, such as a freedwoman, a black woman, a solicitor, a Muslim woman, or someone who has no status, her marriage is permissible, and her guardian has no option because each one is a match for her. It was narrated from Malik that the noble and lowly woman cannot be married except by her guardian or the ruler. This statement was chosen by Ibn al-Mundhir. He said: As for Malik’s differentiation between the poor woman and the one who has status, it is not permissible, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made their rulings equal in blood money, saying: The blood of Muslims is equal, and if they are equal in blood money, then they are one thing in other things. Ismail bin Ishaq said: When God Almighty commanded By marriage, the believers are made guardians of one another, as God the Almighty said: And the believing men and believing women are guardians of one another (al-Tawbah 9:71). And the believers in general inherit from one another, so if a man dies and has no heir, then the inheritance is for the group of Muslims, and if he commits a crime, then the Muslims pay blood money for him. Then guardianship is closer than guardianship, and kinship is closer than kinship. If the woman is in a place where there is no authority and she has no guardian, then she entrusts her matter to someone she trusts from among her neighbors, so he marries her and he is her guardian in this case, because people must marry, and they only do what is best possible. Based on this, Malik said about a woman who is weak in her situation: He marries her to someone to whom she entrusts her matter, because she is one of those who are weak in relation to the authority, so she is like someone who has no authority in her presence, so in general she returns to the Muslims being her guardians. But if she entrusts her matter to a man and leaves her guardians, then she has taken the matter in a wrong way, and has done what the ruler and the Muslims disapprove of, so that marriage is annulled without knowing that it is in reality forbidden, for what we have described. The believers are guardians of one another, and because of the difference in that, but it is annulled to approach the matter from another side, and because it is more cautious for the private parts and to protect them, so if the consummation occurs and the matter is prolonged and children are born and it was correct, then annulment is not permissible, because if the command is different, then nothing is intended from it except what is forbidden that is not in doubt, and what is missed from that is similar to the ruling of the judge if he rules and does not allow it unless it is a mistake that is not in doubt, and as for Al-Shafi’i and his companions, then marriage according to them without a guardian is annulled forever before consummation and after it, and they do not inherit from each other if one of them dies, and the guardian according to them is one of the obligations of marriage, because of the evidence they have from the Book and the Sunnah: God Almighty said: And marry those among you who are single (al-Nur 24:32), as He said: Then marry them with the permission of their people (al-Nisa 4:25), and He said addressing the guardians: So do not prevent them and he, peace be upon him, said: There is no marriage except with a guardian, and they did not differentiate between the lowly and the noble, because of the consensus of the scholars that there is no difference between them in blood, Because he, peace be upon him, said: The blood of Muslims is equal, and all other rulings are likewise, and there is no difference in any of this between the high and the lowly in the Book or the Sunnah. Fourth: They differed about the marriage contract that takes place without a guardian and then he approves it before consummation. Malik and his companions, except for Abd al-Malik, said: That is permissible, if his approval of it is close, and whether he consummated the marriage or not. This is if the marriage contract is concluded without a guardian and the woman does not conclude it herself. If the woman marries herself and concludes the marriage contract without a guardian, whether close or distant, from the Muslims, then this marriage is never confirmed in any case, even if it lasts a long time and she gives birth to children. However, the child is attributed to him if he consummates the marriage, and the punishment is dropped, and that marriage must be annulled in any case. Ibn Nafi’ said on the authority of Malik that the annulment is without divorce. Fifth: The scholars differed regarding the status of guardians and their order.
