Malik used to say: The first of them are the sons, even if they are descended, then the fathers, then the brothers of the father and mother, then the father, then the sons of the brothers of the father and mother, then the sons of the brothers of the father, then the grandfathers of the father even if they are known, then the paternal uncles in the order of the brothers, then their sons in the order of the sons of the brothers even if they are descended, then the master, then the ruler or his judge. The guardian has precedence in marrying orphans over the guardians, and he is the successor and agent of the father, so his situation is similar to if the father were alive. Al-Shafi’i said: No one has guardianship with the father. If he dies, then the grandfather, then the grandfather’s father’s father, because they are all fathers. Guardianship after the grandfather is for the brothers, then the closest. Al-Muzani said: He said in the new: Whoever is alone with a mother has more right to marriage, like inheritance. He said in the old: They are equal. I said: The Medinans narrated from Malik the same statement as al-Shafi’i, that the father is more deserving than the son, and this is one of the two statements of Abu Hanifa, as narrated by al-Baji. It was narrated from al-Mughira that he said: The grandfather is more deserving than the brothers, and the well-known view of the school is what we have presented. Ahmad said: The one who has the most right to a woman is the one who is married by her father, then the son, then the brother, then his father, then the paternal uncle. Ishaq said: The son is more deserving than the father, as Malik said, and Ibn al-Mundhir chose it, because ‘Umar ibn Umm Salamah married her with her permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: al-Nasa’i narrated it from Umm Salamah and he titled it The Son Marrying His Mother. I said: Our scholars often use this as evidence, but it is nothing. The evidence for this is what is established in the Sahihs: “Umar ibn Abi Salamah said: I was a boy in the care of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and my hand would wander around the plate, so he said: Boy, say Bismillah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.” Abu Omar said in the book Al-Isti’ab: Umar ibn Abi Salamah was called Abu Hafs, and he was born in the second year of the Hijrah in the land of Abyssinia. It was said that he was nine years old on the day the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died. She said: Whoever is this age is not fit to be a guardian, but Abu Omar mentioned that Abu Salamah had another son from Umm Salamah named Salamah, and he was the one who married the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to his mother Umm Salamah. Salamah was older than his brother Omar ibn Abu Salamah, and I do not remember any narration from him on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but his brother Omar narrated on his authority. Sixth: They differed about the man who marries the most distant of the guardians, as it happened. The closest expression is to say: They differed about the woman who marries her from her most distant of guardians and the one who is disabled is present. Al-Shafi’i said: The marriage is invalid. Malik said: The marriage is permissible. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: If the one who is disabled does not object to anything of that or reject it, it is valid. If he objected to it and she is a married woman or an adult virgin who is an orphan and has no guardian, then the statement of Malik and his companions and a group of the people of Medina differed about that. Some of them said that it is not invalidated and is valid, because it was concluded with the permission of a guardian from the thigh and clan. Whoever of them said that it is not valid said: The rank in the guardians came according to the best and the first, and that is recommended and not obligatory. This is the conclusion of the Maliki school of thought according to most of his companions and Ismail bin Ishaq and his followers chose it. It was said: The ruler looks into that and asks the closest guardian about what he objected to, then if he sees that he approves it, he approves it, and if he sees that he rejects it, he rejects it. It was said: Rather, the one who is disabled has the right to reject it in any case, because it is his right. It was said: He has the right to reject it and approve it as long as she does not stay for a long time and give birth to children. All of these are the sayings of the people of Medina. Seventh: If the closest guardian is imprisoned or insane, the next closest guardian may marry her off, and he is considered as if she had died. Likewise, if one of her guardians is absent for a long time or is absent for a period of time in which there is no hope of her quick return, she may marry him off to the next closest guardian. It has been said: If the closest of her guardians is absent, the next closest guardian may not marry her off, and the ruler may marry her off. The first is the opinion of Malik. Eighth: If the two guardians are equal in number and one of them is absent and the woman delegates her marriage contract to the one who is present, the absent one, if he comes, does not have the right to deny it. If they are both present and she delegates her matter to one of them, he does not marry her except with the permission of his companion. If they disagree, the judge should consider that and approve of the opinion of the one who best considers her. This was narrated by Ibn Wahb on the authority of Malik. Ninth: As for the testimony of the marriage, it is not a pillar according to Malik and his companions, and it is sufficient for it to be known and announced, and it is not a secret marriage. Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik: If he marries with evidence and orders them to conceal it, the marriage is not permissible, because it is a secret marriage. If he marries without evidence and without secrecy, it is permissible, and he bears witness to what they will face. Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Malik regarding a man who marries a woman with the testimony of two men and conceals it from them. He said: He is separated by his divorce and the marriage is not permissible, and she is entitled to her dowry if he had intercourse with her, and the two witnesses are not punished. Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi’i and their companions said: If he marries her with two witnesses and tells them: Conceal it, the marriage is permissible. Abu Umar said: This is the statement of Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi al-Andalusi, our companion, who said: Every marriage that is witnessed by two men has been removed from the limits of secrecy, and I think he narrated it on the authority of al-Layth ibn Sa’d. The secret according to al-Shafi’i and the Kufians and those who followed them: Every A marriage that is not witnessed by two or more men, and is annulled in any case. I said: The statement of Al-Shafi’i is more correct due to the hadith that we mentioned. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: There is no marriage except with two just witnesses and a sane guardian. There is no one who disagreed with him among the Companions as far as I know. Malik provided evidence for his school of thought that the sales that God Almighty mentioned require witnessing at the time of the contract, and evidence has been established that this is not one of the obligatory duties of sales. The marriage in which God Almighty did not mention witnessing is more likely not to have witnessing among its conditions and obligations. Rather, the purpose is to announce and make it apparent in order to preserve lineages. Witnessing is appropriate after the contract for disputes and disagreements regarding what is concluded between the two parties to the marriage. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: They announced the marriage. This statement of Malik is the statement of Ibn Shihab and most of the people of Medina. Tenth: The Almighty’s statement: And a believing slave meaning a slave is better than a polytheist meaning a man of noble lineage, even if he pleases you meaning his lineage and wealth, as mentioned above. It was said that the meaning is: And for a believing man, and likewise for a believing slave girl, meaning for a believing woman, as we explained. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All your men are slaves of God and all your women are female slaves of God, and he said: Do not prevent the female slaves of God from the mosques of God, and the Almighty said: What an excellent slave he is! Indeed, he frequently turns back [to God] (Sad: 30, 44). This is the best interpretation of the statement in this verse, and with it the dispute is resolved and the disagreement is eliminated, and God is the Grantor of success. Eleventh: The Almighty’s statement: Those refers to the polytheists, both men and women. They invite to the Fire to the deeds that lead to the Fire, for their company and association necessitates degradation in many of their desires, along with their raising of offspring. And God invites to Paradise meaning to the deeds of the people of Paradise, by His permission, meaning by His command, as Al-Zajjaj said. Or
2:222: It contains fourteen issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And they ask you about menstruation. At-Tabari mentioned on the authority of As-Suddi that the questioner was Thabit bin Ad-Dahhaah, and it was said: Asid bin Hudayr and Abbad bin Bishr, and this is the opinion of the majority. The reason for the question, according to what Qatada and others said, is that the Arabs in Medina and its environs had followed the example of the Children of Israel in avoiding eating with and living with menstruating women, so this verse was revealed. Mujahid said: They used to avoid women during menstruation, and they would have intercourse with them in their anuses for the duration of menstruation, so it was revealed. In Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Anas: That the Jews, when a woman among them menstruated, would not eat with her or have intercourse with them in their homes. So the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God Almighty revealed: “And they ask you about menstruation. Say: It is a harmful thing, so keep away from women during menstruation.” to the end of the verse. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do everything except differ from us, except intercourse. So that reached the Jews, and they said: This man does not want to leave anything of our affair except differ from us in it. So he came. Usaid bin Hudhair and Ubad bin Bishr said: O Messenger of God, the Jews say such and such, so should we not have intercourse with them? The face of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) changed so much that we thought he was angry with them. They went out and were met by a gift of milk to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). He sent after them and gave them something to drink, and they knew that he was not angry with them. Our scholars said: The Jews and Magians used to avoid menstruating women, and the Christians used to have intercourse with menstruating women, so God commanded moderation between these two. The second: The Almighty’s saying: About menstruation. Menstruation is menstruation, and it is a source. It is said that a woman menstruated, menstruated, and menstruated, so she is menstruating, and also menstruating, according to Al-Farra’, and he recited: Like a menstruating woman who commits adultery with someone who is not pure And menstruating women and menstruating women, and menstruation: the single time with a kasra the noun, and the plural is menstruation, also menstruation, the rag with which a woman cleans herself. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: I wish I were a menstrual period thrown away, and likewise the menstruating woman, and the plural is menstruating women, and it was said: Menstruation is an expression for time and place, and for menstruation itself, and its origin in time and place is a metaphor for menstruation, and Al-Tabari said: Menstruation is a name for menstruation, and similar to it is the saying of Ru’bah in Al-Aish: To you I complain of the hardship of life and the years that have passed while I pluck my feathers The origin of the word is from flow and explosion. It is said: the flood overflowed and flowed, and the tree overflowed, meaning its moisture flowed. From this comes menstruation, meaning the basin, because the water overflows into it, meaning it flows. The Arabs add the waw to the ya’ and the ya’ to the waw, because they are from the same place. Ibn Arafa said: Menstruation and menstruation are the gathering of blood in that place, and the basin was named after it because of the gathering of water in it. It is said: the woman menstruated and menstruated, and studied and trained, and menstruated. She menstruates, menstruates, and is menstruated, if the blood flows from her at known times. If it flows on days other than known days, and from other than the vein of menstruation, you say: istihadha, so she is mustahaza. Ibn al-Arabi, and it has eight names: the first is menstruating, the second is ‘Arak, the third is Farik, the fourth is Tamis, the fifth is Daris, the sixth is Kabir, the seventh is Dahik, and the eighth is Taamith. Mujahid said in the words of God Almighty: So she laughed (Hud 11:71) meaning she menstruated. It was said in the words of God Almighty: So when they saw him, they glorified him [Yusuf].:31] It means hugging, and it will come in its place, God willing. Third: The scholars agreed that there are three rulings for a woman when she sees visible blood flowing from her vagina. Among them is the well-known menstruation, and its blood is black and clotted with a reddish tinge, so she should stop praying and fasting. There is no disagreement about that. It may continue or stop, or it may continue or stop. If it continues, then the ruling is valid for her. If it stops, and she sees blood one day and purity one day, or she sees blood two days and purity two days or one day, then she should stop praying during the days of blood, and she should perform ghusl when it stops and pray, then she should combine the days of blood and cancel the days of purity that are in between, and she should not count them as purity in her waiting period or istibra’. Menstruation is a natural characteristic of women and a well-known habitual nature of them. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out on Eid al-Adha or Eid al-Fitr to the prayer place and passed by the women and said: ‘O group of women, give charity, for I have seen you as the majority of the people of Hell. ’ They said: ‘Why, O Messenger of God? ’ He said: ‘You curse a lot and are ungrateful to your husbands. I have not seen anyone deficient in intelligence and religion who is more refined than the mind of a wise man than one of you. ’ They said: ‘And what is deficient? ’” Our mind and our religion, O Messenger of God? He said: Is not the testimony of a woman worth half of that of a man? They said: Yes. He said: That is due to the deficiency of her mind. Is it not the case that when she menstruates she does not pray or fast? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: That is due to the deficiency of her religion. The scholars agreed that a menstruating woman must make up the fast but not the prayer, based on the hadith of Mu’adhah who said: I asked Aisha, saying: Why does a menstruating woman make up the fast but not the prayer? She said: Are you a Kharijite? I said: A Kharijite, but I am asking. She said: That used to happen to us and we were commanded to fast but not to make up the prayer. Narrated by Muslim. So if it stops, her purification from it is ritual bath, as will come. Fourth: The scholars differed regarding the length of menstruation. The jurists of Medina said that menstruation does not exceed fifteen days, and it is permissible for it to be fifteen days or less. Anything that exceeds fifteen days is not menstruation but rather istihadah. This is the school of Malik and his companions. It was narrated from Malik that there is no time for a short or long menstruation except what is found in women. It is as if he abandoned his first statement and returned to the custom of women. Muhammad ibn Maslamah said that the minimum period of purity is fifteen days, and this is the choice of most of the Malikis from Baghdad. It is the statement of al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifah, their companions, and al-Thawri, and it is the correct statement in this regard, because God Almighty has made the number of menstruating women three menstrual periods, and He has made the number of those who do not menstruate, whether old or young, three months. So each menstrual period is a portion of a month, and the month combines purity and menstruation. So if menstruation is short, purity is long, and if menstruation is long, purity is short. So since the maximum period of menstruation is fifteen days, one month is completed with a menstrual period and purity, which is what is commonly known from the creation and nature of women with evidence from the Qur’an and Sunnah. He said: Al-Shafi’i: The minimum period of menstruation is one day and one night, and the maximum is fifteen days. It has been narrated from him, like the statement of Malik: That is based on the custom of women. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: The minimum period of menstruation is three days, and the maximum is ten. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: According to them, what is less than three days is istihadah, and prayer is not prevented except when it first appears, because the length of its duration is known. Then the woman must make up the prayers of those times. Likewise, according to the Kufians, what is more than fifteen days is istihadah. According to the Hijazis, what is more than fifteen days is istihadah. What is less than one day and one night according to al-Shafi’i is istihadah. This is the statement of al-Awza’i and al-Tabari. Among those who said that the minimum period of menstruation is one day and one night, and the maximum is fifteen days are ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, Abu Thawr, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Al-Awza’i said: We have a woman who menstruates in the morning and becomes pure in the evening. We have already mentioned what the scholars have said in this regard regarding the maximum period of menstruation, the minimum period, and the minimum period of purity, and in al-Istithhar. The evidence for that is in al-Muqtabas in the explanation of the Muwatta’ of Malik ibn Anas. If she is a virgin who has just started menstruating, then she should sit as soon as she sees blood, according to the statement of al-Awza’i and al-Tabari. Al-Shafi’i: Fifteen days, then she should wash herself and repeat the prayer for fourteen days. Malik said: She should not make up the prayer and her husband should abstain from her. Ali bin Ziyad said: She sits until she has given birth. This is the opinion of Ata’, Al-Thawri and others. Ibn Hanbal said: She sits for a day and a night, then she washes herself and prays, but her husband does not come to her. Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf said: She leaves prayer for ten days, then she washes herself and prays for twenty days, then she leaves prayer for ten days after the twenty. This is her condition until the bleeding stops. As for the one who has known days, she should count her known days by three days. Malik said: As long as they do not exceed fifteen days. Al-Shafi’i said: She should take a bath if her days have passed without counting them. The second type of blood is the blood of postpartum bleeding at birth. It also has a known limit among scholars, about which they differed. It was said: two months, which is the opinion of Malik. It was said: forty days, which is the opinion of al-Shafi’i. Others said: her purity is when it stops, and the ritual bath for it is like the ritual bath for major ritual impurity. Judge Abu Muhammad Abd al-Wahhab said: The blood of menstruation and postpartum bleeding prevent eleven things: the obligation of prayer and the validity of performing it, and the performance of fasting without its obligation. The benefit of the difference is the necessity of making up for fasting and its negation in prayer, intercourse in the vagina and less, the waiting period, divorce, circumambulation, touching the Qur’an, entering the mosque and seclusion in it. There are two narrations regarding reciting the Qur’an. The third type of blood: Blood that is not a habit, nor a natural part of them, nor a creation, but rather a vein that has stopped, and its flow is red blood that does not stop except when it is cured. The ruling on this is that the woman is pure from it and it does not prevent her from praying or fasting, according to the consensus of the scholars and the agreement of the reports that were transmitted from the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, if it is known that it is blood from a vein and not menstrual blood. Malik narrated on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: Fatima bint Abi Hubaish said: O Messenger of God, I do not become pure! Should I give up prayer? The Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: It is only a vein and not menstruation. If menstruation begins, then give up prayer, and when its time has passed, wash the blood off yourself and pray. In the hadith, despite its authenticity and few words, there is what explains to you the rulings on the menstruating woman and the woman who is experiencing istihadah, and it is the most authentic of what has been narrated in this regard, and it refutes what was narrated on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir and Makhul: that the menstruating woman should wash herself and perform ablution at every time for prayer, and face the qiblah, remembering God Almighty while sitting. It contains that the menstruating woman does not pray, and this is the consensus of all scholars except for groups of the Khawarij who consider that the menstruating woman must pray. It contains what indicates that the woman with irregular bleeding is not required to do anything other than the ritual bath that she does after her menses. If something else was required of her, he would have ordered her to do it. It contains a refutation of the opinion of those who saw that she should do it for every prayer, and of the opinion of those who saw that she should combine the two prayers of the day with one ritual bath, and the two prayers of the night with one ritual bath and perform ritual bath for the morning prayer, and of the opinion of those who said: She performs ritual bath from one period of purity to another, and of the opinion of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab from one period of purity to another, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not order her to do any of that. It contains a refutation of the opinion of those who said that it is permissible to assume that, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered her, if she knew that her menses had ended and gone, to perform ritual bath and pray, and he did not order her to leave prayer for three days in anticipation of menses that may or may not come, and caution is only in performing the prayer, not in leaving it. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: It is a harmful thing.” That is, it is something that harms a woman and others, that is, the smell of menstrual blood. Harm is a metaphor for filth in general, and is used to refer to a disliked statement. From this is the Almighty’s saying: Do not invalidate your charities with reminders or harm. (al-Baqarah 2:264), that is, with what you hear of something disliked. From this is the Almighty’s saying: And leave their harm. (al-Ahzab 33:48), that is, leave the harm of the hypocrites. Do not punish them unless you are commanded to do so. In the hadith: And remove the harmful thing from him. He means by harm the hair that forms on the head of the boy when he is born. It is shaved off on the day of his week, and it is the ‘aqeeqah. In the hadith of faith: And the least of it is removing the harmful thing from the road, that is, moving it away, meaning thorns and stones, and the like that harm the passerby. And the Almighty’s saying: And there is no blame upon you if there is harm upon you from rain. (An-Nisa’: 102) and it will come. Sixth: Those who forbade intercourse with a woman with istihadah used the flow of istihadah blood as evidence, saying: All blood is harmful and must be washed from clothing and body, so there is no difference in intercourse between menstrual blood and istihadah blood because it is all impure. As for prayer, it is a concession mentioned in the Sunnah, just as one prays with urinary incontinence. This is the opinion of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Sulayman ibn Yasar, al-Hakam ibn ‘Uyaynah, ‘Amir al-Sha’bi, Ibn Sirin, and al-Zuhri. There is a difference of opinion about it from al-Hasan, and it is the opinion of ‘A’ishah, her husband should not come to her. Ibn ‘Ulayyah and al-Mughira ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, who was one of the highest companions of Malik, and Abu Mus’ab, said the same, and he used to issue fatwas with it. The majority of scholars said: The woman with istihadah fasts, prays, performs tawaf, and recites Qur’an, and her husband comes to her. Malik said: The scholars of jurisprudence and knowledge are in agreement with this, even if her blood is abundant. This was narrated by Ibn Wahb. Ahmad used to say: I prefer that he not have intercourse with her unless it lasts a long time. Ibn ‘Abbas said about the woman with istihadah: There is nothing wrong with her husband having intercourse with her even if the blood flows down her heels. Malik said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, it is a vein and not menstruation. So if it is not menstruation, then what prevents him from having intercourse with her while she is praying? Ibn Abd al-Barr said: Since God Almighty ruled that the blood of a woman with irregular menstruation does not prevent prayer and worship in it with worship other than the worship of a menstruating woman, it is necessary that he not rule for it with anything from the ruling of menstruation except in what they agreed upon regarding washing it like all other blood. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: So keep away from women during menstruation, meaning during the time of menstruation, if you take menstruation as a source, or in the place of menstruation if you take it as a name. The purpose of this prohibition is to refrain from intercourse. The scholars have differed regarding intercourse with a menstruating woman and what is permissible from her. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ubaidah al-Salmani that a man must keep away from his wife’s bed when she menstruates. This is an odd statement that is outside the statement of the scholars, even though the generality of the verse requires it, but the established Sunnah is contrary to it. Ibn Abbas’s aunt Maymunah stood up to him and said to him: Are you averse to the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf and a great group of scholars said that he has what is above the izar, because of his saying, peace be upon him, to the questioner when he asked him: What is permissible for me with my wife while she is menstruating? He said: Tie her izar around her and then do what is above it. And his saying, peace be upon him, to Aisha when she menstruated: Tie your izar around yourself and then return to your bed. Al-Thawri, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and some of the companions of Al-Shafi’i said: The place of blood should be avoided, because of his saying, peace be upon him: Do everything except intercourse. It was mentioned earlier and it is the saying of Dawud, and it is the correct saying of Al-Shafi’i. Abu Ma’shar narrated on the authority of Ibrahim on the authority of Masruq who said: I asked Aisha what is permissible for me with my wife while she is menstruating? She said: Everything except the vagina. The scholars said: Direct contact with a menstruating woman while she is wearing a belt is a precaution and to cut off the means, and because if he had permitted her thighs, that would have been a means for him to the place of blood, which is forbidden by consensus, so he ordered that as a precaution, and the place of blood itself is forbidden, so the meanings of the narrations are in agreement with that and do not contradict each other, and success is from God. Eighth: They differed about what a man must do if he has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating. Malik, Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa said: He should seek forgiveness from God and nothing is due from him. This is the opinion of Rabi’ah and Yahya ibn Sa’id, and Dawud said the same. It was narrated from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan: He should give charity of half a dinar. Ahmad said: How beautiful is the hadith of Abdul Hamid from Muqsim from Ibn Abbas from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He should give charity of a dinar or half a dinar. Abu Dawud narrated it and said: This is the correct narration. He said: A dinar or half a dinar. At-Tabari recommended it. If he does not do that, nothing is due from him. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i in Baghdad. A group of the people of hadith said: If he has intercourse while she is menstruating, he must give a dinar, and if he has intercourse when it has stopped, he must give half a dinar. Al-Awza’i said: Whoever has intercourse with his wife while she is menstruating must give charity of five dinars. The chains of transmission for all of this are in Sunan Abu Dawud, Ad-Darqutni and others. In the book of At-Tirmidhi from Ibn Abbas from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: If it is red blood, then a dinar, and if it is yellow blood, then half a dinar. Abu Umar said: The proof of those who did not do that is… He must pay expiation except for seeking forgiveness and repentance. This hadith is confused about Ibn Abbas, and something like it cannot be used as evidence. The covenant is based on innocence, and nothing must be proven for a poor person or anyone else except with evidence that cannot be refuted or challenged, and that is non-existent in this matter. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: And do not approach them until they are pure. Ibn al-Arabi said: I heard al-Shashi in the Majlis al-Nazar say: If it is said, Do not approach with the opening of the ra’, it means: Do not wear the act, and if it is with the damma of the ra’, it means: Do not come near him. Nafi’, Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Asim read in the narration of Hafs from him (they purify) with the emphasis on the ta’ and the ha’ and the fatha on them, and in the Mushaf of Abi and Abdullah (they purify), and in the Mushaf of Anas ibn Malik (and do not approach women during their menses and keep away from them until they are pure) and al-Tabari returned to the reading with the emphasis on the ta’, and said: It means they wash themselves, because of the consensus of all that it is forbidden for a man to approach his wife after the bleeding has stopped until she is pure. He said: The difference of opinion is only about what purity is. Some people said: It is washing with water, and some people said: It is ablution like the ablution for prayer, and some people said: It is washing the vagina, and that makes her permissible for her husband even if she has not washed herself from menstruation, and the most likely Abu Ali Al-Farsi reads the letter Taa’ with a light reading, as it is a trilateral letter, the opposite of Menstruation, which is a trilateral letter. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: And when they have purified themselves means with water. This is what Malik and the majority of scholars have said, and that the purity by which intercourse with a menstruating woman is permissible and the blood goes away is her purification with water, like the purification of a person in a state of major ritual impurity. Neither dry ablution nor anything else is sufficient for that. Malik, al-Shafi’i, al-Tabari, Muhammad ibn Maslama, the people of Medina and others said this. Yahya ibn Bakir and Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: If a menstruating woman purifies herself and performs dry ablution where there is no water, she is permissible for her husband even if she does not perform ghusl. Mujahid, Ikrimah and Tawus said: The cessation of the blood makes her permissible for her husband, but by performing ablution. Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said: If the blood stops after ten days, it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her before ghusl. If it stops before ten days, it is not permissible until she performs ghusl or the time for prayer begins. This is a ruling that has no basis. They have ruled for a menstruating woman after her blood stops according to the ruling of confinement during the waiting period, and they said to her husband: She must return to him as long as she does not perform ghusl from the third menses. So, based on their statement, this is not obligatory. That she be penetrated until she washes herself, with the consent of the people of Medina, and our evidence is that God Almighty has made the ruling on it conditional on two conditions: one is the cessation of bleeding, which is His Almighty’s saying: until they are pure, and the second is washing with water, which is His Almighty’s saying: and when they have purified themselves, meaning that they perform the washing with water. This is like the permissibility of paying money on two conditions: one is the person who is obligated to marry, and the second is the awareness of maturity, and likewise His Almighty’s saying regarding the divorced woman: Then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband (al-Baqarah 2:230). Then the Sunnah came with the condition of the honey, so the permissibility was stopped on both matters, which are the conclusion of the marriage and the existence of intercourse. Abu Hanifa argued and said: The meaning of the verse, the goal in the condition is what is mentioned in the goal before it, so His saying: until they are pure is lightened and is in the same sense as His saying: they are pure is stressed, but He combined the two languages in the verse, as God Almighty said: In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves (al-Tawbah 9:230). 108] Al-Kumait said: The Ansar were not humiliated or absent in it when the people were absent. Also, the two readings are like the two verses, so they must be acted upon. We interpret each one of them to mean something. We interpret the light reading as meaning if her bleeding stops for the lesser amount, then we do not permit intercourse with her until she washes herself, because there is no guarantee that it will return. We interpret the other reading as meaning if her bleeding stops for the greater amount, then intercourse with her is permissible even if she does not wash herself. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is their strongest argument. The answer to the first is that this is not from the speech of the eloquent, nor the tongues of the articulate, because that requires repetition in the enumeration. If it is possible to interpret the wording to mean an abstract benefit, then it is not interpreted as repetition in the speech of people, so how about in the speech of the All-Knowing, All-Wise! And regarding the second: that each one of them is carried on a meaning other than the meaning of the other, so it is necessary for them if the blood stops that she not be ruled as menstruating before she washes herself in the return, and they do not say that as we have explained, so she is then menstruating, and it is not permissible to have intercourse with a menstruating woman by consensus, and also what they said requires the permissibility of intercourse when the blood stops for the majority and what we said requires prohibition, and if what requires prohibition and what requires permission conflict and their motives prevail, then the motive of prohibition prevails, as Ali and Uthman said about combining two sisters by right hand possession, one verse permitted them and another forbade them, and prohibition is more appropriate, and God knows best. Eleventh: Our scholars differed on whether a woman of the People of the Book should be forced to perform ghusl or not. Malik said in the narration of Ibn al-Qasim: Yes, so that it is permissible for the husband to have intercourse with her. God Almighty said: “And do not approach them until they are pure. And when they have purified themselves” al-Baqarah 2:256, meaning with water. He did not specify a Muslim woman from others. Ashhab narrated from Malik that she should not be forced to perform ghusl after menstruation, because she does not believe in that, because God Almighty said: And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs if they believe in God and the Last Day al-Baqarah 2:228, which is menstruation and pregnancy. God Almighty only addressed the believing women with that, and said: There is no compulsion in religion al-Baqarah 2:256. This is what Mahmoud ibn Abd al-Hakam used to say. Twelfth: The description of the menstruating woman’s ablution is the description of her ablution from major ritual impurity, and she does not have to undo her hair for that, because of what Muslim narrated, “On the authority of Umm Salamah, she said, I said: O Messenger of God, I tightly braid my hair, should I undo it for the ritual ablution from major ritual impurity? He said: No, it is sufficient for you to throw three handfuls of water over your head, then pour water over yourself and you will be purified.” In another narration: “Should I undo it for menstruation and major ritual impurity? He said: No.” Abu Dawud added: And submerge your hair at every handful. Thirteenth: The Almighty’s saying: So have intercourse with them from where God has commanded you, meaning, have intercourse with them, which is a command of permission, and he used intercourse as a metaphor. This command strengthens what we said, that what is meant by purification is washing with water, because the command form from God the Almighty does not occur except in the most perfect manner, and God knows best. And from means in, meaning where God the Almighty has commanded you, which is the front. Similar to this is the Almighty’s saying: Show me what they have created from the earth (Fatir 35:40), meaning in the earth, and His saying: When the call is made for prayer on Friday (Al-Jumu’ah: 9), meaning on Friday. It was said: The meaning is, from the manner in which you have been permitted, meaning without fasting, ihram, or seclusion. This was said by Al-Asamm. Ibn Abbas and Abu Razin said: From before purification, not from before menstruation. This was said by Ad-Dahhak. Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah said: The meaning is from before what is permissible, not from before fornication. Fourteenth: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God loves those who repent and loves those who purify themselves. There is a difference of opinion regarding it. It was said: Those who repent from sins and polytheism, and those who purify themselves, that is, with water from major ritual impurity and impurity, as stated by Ata’ and others. Mujahid said: From sins, and from him also: From having intercourse with women in their backsides. Ibn Atiyyah: It is as if he looked at the Almighty’s saying, narrating about the people of Lot: “Drive them out of your city. Indeed, they are people who purify themselves.” (al-A’raf 7:82), and it was said: Those who purify themselves are those who have not sinned. If it is said: How did He mention the one who sinned before the one who did not sin? It is said: He mentioned it so that the one who repented would not despair of mercy and the one who purified himself would not be pleased with himself, as mentioned in another verse: And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds. (Fatir 35:32), as will be explained, God willing.
2:223: It has six issues: The first: Your women are a place of cultivation for you. The imams narrated, and the wording is from Muslim, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Jews used to say: If a man comes to his wife from behind in her vagina, the child will be cross-eyed. Then the verse was revealed: Your women are a place of cultivation for you, so go to your place of cultivation however you wish. He added in a narration on the authority of Al-Zuhri: If he wishes, she is covered, and if he wishes, she is not covered, except that it is in one valve. And he narrates: In one poison with a sin, said Al-Tirmidhi. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Nafi’, who said: When Ibn Umar recited the Qur’an, he would not speak until he finished it. So I took him to task one day, and he recited Surat Al-Baqarah until he reached a place where he said: Do you know why it was revealed? I said: No. He said: It was revealed about such and such, then he went on and on the authority of Abd al-Samad he said: My father told me he said Ayoub told me on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar: (So approach your tilth however you wish) he said: He comes to her in, al-Hamidi said: He means the vagina. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas he said: Indeed, Ibn Umar, by God, is forgiven for their delusion, for this tribe of the Ansar, who were idolaters, were with this tribe of the Jews, who were People of the Book, and they saw that they had superiority over them in knowledge, so they used to follow many of their actions. It was the command of the People of the Book that they should not approach women except on the verge, and that is the most modest way for a woman to be, so this tribe of the Ansar had taken that from their actions, and this tribe of the Quraysh used to treat women in an abhorrent manner, and they would enjoy them facing forward, backward, and lying down. When the Muhajirun came to Madinah, an important man married a woman from the Ansar, and he went to do that to her but she disapproved of him and said: We were only approached on the verge! Do that or else avoid me, until their affair was settled? This reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God Almighty revealed: And go to your tilth however you will, meaning from the front, back, and side, meaning the place of the child. Al-Tirmidhi narrated, “On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: ‘Umar came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I am ruined! He said: What ruined you? He said: I turned the night.’ He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not answer him at all. He said: Then this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Your women are a tilth for you, so go to your tilth however you will,” coming forward and back, and avoid the anus and menstruation. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu al-Nadhir that he said to Nafi’, the freed slave of Ibn Umar: They have said too much about you. You say on the authority of Ibn Umar that he issued a fatwa that women should be approached from their backsides. Nafi’ said: They have lied about me! But I will tell you how it was: Ibn Umar showed me the Qur’an one day while I was with him until he reached: Your women are a tilth unto you. He said, “O Nafi’, do you know the matter with this verse? We, the Quraysh, used to take wives, but when we entered Madinah and married the women of the Ansar, we wanted from them what we wanted from our women. But they disliked that and considered it very difficult. The women of the Ansar used to have intercourse on their sides. So God, the Exalted, revealed: “Your women are a tilth unto you, so go to your tilth however you wish.” Second: These hadiths are explicit in permitting all situations and forms if intercourse is in the place of cultivation, i.e. however you wish, from behind, from the front, kneeling, lying down, or supine. As for intercourse in a place other than the vagina, it is not permissible, and is not permissible! The mention of the vagina indicates that intercourse in a place other than the vagina is forbidden, and cultivation is a simile, because they are the place where offspring are planted, so the word cultivation indicates that permissibility only occurred in the vagina specifically, since it is the place where offspring is planted. Tha’lab recited: The wombs are our cultivated lands. We have to plant it and God will do the work The woman’s vagina is like the earth, the sperm is like the seed, and the child is like the plant. So, harth means the one who plows, and harth is singular because it is a source, just as it is said: a fasting man, and a fasting people. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Wherever you wish means, according to the majority of the Companions, Followers, and Imams of Fatwa: From whichever direction you wish, coming or going, as we mentioned earlier. Where comes as a question and as information about a matter that has aspects, so it is more general in the language than how, “where,” and when. This is the Arabic usage of where. People have interpreted where in this verse with these words, and Sibawayh interpreted it as how and where by combining them. A group of those who interpreted it as where went so far as to say that anal intercourse is permissible. Among those to whom this statement is attributed are: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Nafi’, Ibn Umar, Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, and Abdul Malik bin Al-Majishun. This was narrated from Malik in a book of his called The Book of Secret. The most skilled companions of Malik and their sheikhs deny this book, and Malik is more honorable than how he could have a book of secrets. This statement occurred in Al-Utbiyyah. Ibn al-Arabi mentioned that Ibn Sha’ban attributed this statement to a large group of the Companions and Followers, and to Malik from many narrations in the book Jama’ al-Nusun wa Ahkam al-Qur’an. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: It was narrated from Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi that he saw no harm in that, and he interpreted it as the saying of God Almighty: Do you approach males from among the worlds * and leave what your Lord has created for you as mates? (al-Shu’ara’: 165-166). He said: Its meaning is that you leave such a thing from your wives. If such a thing from mates had not been permitted, it would not have been valid. What is permitted in the other place is not an example of it, so it can be said: You do that and leave what is permitted. Al-Kaya said: This is questionable: And you leave what your Lord has created for you as mates, which calms your desire, and the pleasure of intercourse is achieved by both of them, so it is permissible to rebuke this meaning. In the saying of God Almighty: And when they have purified themselves, then come to them from where God has commanded you with His saying: Then come to your tilth there is what indicates that there is a specificity in the place of intercourse. And it is limited to the place of the boy. I said: This is the truth in the matter: Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr mentioned that the scholars did not differ in the fact that the vagina that does not lead to intercourse is a defect that should be returned, except for something that came from Omar bin Abdul Aziz from a source that is not strong that the vagina or anything else should not be returned, and all the jurists are against that, because touching is what is sought in marriage, and in their consensus on this is evidence that the anus is not a place of intercourse, and if it were a place of intercourse, then the one who does not lead to intercourse in the vagina would not be returned, and in their consensus also that the barren woman who does not give birth is not returned, and the correct thing in this matter is what we have explained, and what is attributed to Malik and his companions from this is false and they are innocent of that, because the permissibility of intercourse is specific to the place of cultivation, because God Almighty said: Go to your tillage, and because the wisdom in creating spouses is to spread offspring, so the property of marriage is not attained by the place of offspring, and this is the truth, and the companions of Abu Hanifa said: According to us, the male vagina is equal in ruling, and because filth and harm are more common in the place of excrement. From menstrual blood, it was more hideous. As for the urinary valve, it is not the valve of the Most Gracious. Ibn al-Arabi said in his Qabas, the Sheikh Imam Fakhr al-Islam Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, the jurist and imam of the time, told us: The vagina is most similar to thirty-five, and he extended his hand, crossing it, and said: The urinary tract is what is below thirty, and the penis and vagina are what are included in the five. God Almighty has forbidden the vagina during menstruation because of the impurity that occurs, so it is more appropriate to forbid the anus because of the permanent impurity. Malik said to Ibn Wahb and Ali ibn Ziyad when they told him that people in Egypt were talking about him permitting that, so he was repelled by that, and hastened to deny the narrator, saying: They lied about me, they lied about me! Then he said: Are you not an Arab people? Did not God Almighty say: Your women are a place of cultivation for you? And is there a place of cultivation except in the place of growth? And the evidence that the opponent used, that the Almighty’s saying: However you wish includes all paths by virtue of its generality, is not an argument in it, since it is limited by what we have mentioned, and by authentic, good and famous hadiths narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by twelve companions in different texts, all of which are in agreement on the prohibition of intercourse with women in the anus, mentioned by Ahmad ibn Hanil in his Musnad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, al-Tirmidhi and others, and Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi collected them by their chains in a section called the prohibition of the disliked place, and our Sheikh Abu al-Abbas also has a section on that called the disclosure of the anus, of those who permit intercourse in the anus, I say: This is the truth that is followed and correct in the issue, and it is not appropriate for a believer in God and the Last Day to turn in this case to the slip of a scholar after it has been authenticated from him, and we have warned against the slip of a scholar, and it has been narrated from Ibn Umar that this is contrary to this, and that whoever does it is an unbeliever, and this is what is appropriate for him, may God be pleased with him, and likewise Nafi’ lied when he reported that from him, as al-Nasa’i mentioned. It was mentioned before, and Malik denied it and considered it great, and he who attributed it to him lied. Al-Darimi Abu Muhammad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Saeed bin Yasar Abi Al-Habbab, who said: I said to Ibn Omar: What do you say about female slaves when I make them sour? He said: What is souring? So I mentioned to him the anus, and he said: Does any Muslim do that? And he narrated on the authority of Khuzaymah ibn Thabit: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: O people, God is not ashamed of the truth. Do not approach women in their backsides. And the same on the authority of Ali ibn Talq. And he narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever approaches a woman in her anus, God Almighty will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection.” And Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb on the authority of his father on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: That is the lesser act of sodomy,” meaning approaching a woman in her anus. And it was narrated on the authority of Tawus that he said: The beginning of Lot’s action was approaching women in their backsides. Ibn al-Mundhir said: If something is proven on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then it is sufficient in place of anything else. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And send forth for yourselves meaning send forth what will benefit you tomorrow, so the object was omitted, and it was stated explicitly in the Almighty’s saying: And whatever good you send forth for yourselves, you will find it with God (al-Baqarah 2:110). So the meaning is send forth for yourselves obedience and righteous deeds. It was said that it is seeking children and offspring, because children are the best of this world and the hereafter, so they may be an intercessor and a paradise. It was said that it is marrying chaste women, so that the child will be righteous and pure. It was said that it is sending forth excesses, as the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Whoever sends forth three children who have not yet reached puberty, the Fire will not touch him except for the sake of breaking an oath. And it will come in Maryam, God willing. Ibn Abbas and Ata’ said that it means send forth the remembrance of God before intercourse, as the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “If one of you, when he comes to his wife, says: ‘In the name of God, O God, keep Satan away from us and keep Satan away from what You have provided us,’ then if a child is decreed between them, Satan will never harm him.” Narrated by Muslim. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: And fear God is a warning. And know that you will meet Him is a statement that requires exaggeration in the warning, meaning that He will reward you for righteousness and sin. Ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar who said: I heard Saeed ibn Jubayr “on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was delivering a sermon saying: You will meet God barefoot, naked, walking, and uncircumcised. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “And fear God and know that you will meet Him.” Muslim narrated it with the same meaning. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And give good tidings to the believers is a comfort to the doer of good deeds and the seeker of the ways of guidance.
2:224: It has four issues: The first: The scholars said: When God the Almighty commanded spending and treating orphans and women with good manners, He said: Do not refrain from any of the good deeds on the pretext that we swore not to do such and such. Ibn Abbas, Al-Nakha’i, Mujahid, Al-Rabi’ and others said its meaning. Sa’id bin Jubayr said: It is the man who swears not to be righteous, nor to connect with people, nor to make peace between people, so it is said to him: Be righteous, so he says: I have sworn. Some of the commentators said: The meaning is do not swear falsely by God if you want righteousness, piety and reform, so there is no need to estimate (la) after (an. It was said: The meaning is do not swear too much by God, for it is more frightening to the hearts, and for this reason God the Almighty said: And guard your oaths (al-Ma’idah 5:89), and He condemned the one who swears too much, so God the Almighty said: And do not obey every worthless swearer (al-Qalam 68:10). The Arabs praise oaths, so one of them said: He who makes few oaths keeps his oath, and if he makes a mistake, it is forgiven. And on this basis, that you be righteous means: reduce oaths because of the righteousness and piety in them, because increasing them leads to breaking one’s oath and lack of observing the right of God Almighty. This is a good interpretation: Malik bin Anas: It has reached me that it is swearing by God in everything. And it has been said that the meaning is do not make the oath trivial in every right and wrong. Al-Zajjaj and others said: The meaning of the verse is that if a man is asked to do a good deed, he excuses himself by God and says: I swear an oath, and he did not swear. Al-Qutbi: The meaning is if you swear that you will not maintain ties of kinship, nor give charity, nor make things right, and similar to that from the chapters of righteousness, then disbelieve in the oath. I said: This is good for what we have explained, and it is what the reason for revelation indicates, as we will explain in the issue after this. The second: It was said: It was revealed because of Abu Bakr when he swore not to spend on Mastih when he spoke about Aisha, may God be pleased with her, as in the hadith of the slander, and its explanation will come in An-Nur on the authority of Ibn Jurayj. It was also said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr when he swore not to eat with the guests, and it was said that it was revealed about Abdullah bin Rawahah when he swore not to speak to Bashir bin An-Nu’man, who was his brother-in-law after his sister, and God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s saying: A target for your oaths, meaning an object, according to Al-Jawhari. So-and-so is a target for that, meaning a target for that, meaning someone who is strong enough to do so. Target: ambition. He said: They are the supporters who presented the meeting So-and-so is vulnerable to al-Nas 114:they will continue to fall into it. I made so-and-so vulnerable to such-and-such, meaning I set him up for it. It was said: vulnerability comes from severity and strength, and from it is their saying to a woman, vulnerable to marriage, if she is suitable for it and strong for it. So-and-so has vulnerability: meaning strength for travel and war. Ka’b ibn Zuhair said: From every fresh-skinned woman, if she sweats, her appearance is obscured and unknown. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr said: This is for the days of war, this is for passion, and this is subject to our migration. Any number: Another said: Don't make me vulnerable to blame Aws bin Hajar said: And blood-red like a stallion, one day I presented it to my companions, and it was shaking and tossing Meaning: Do not make the oath by God a strength for yourselves, or a means of refraining from righteousness. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: That you be righteous and fear God is a subject and its predicate is omitted, meaning righteousness, piety and reform are more appropriate and better, like obedience and good speech (Muhammad 47:21), according to Al-Zajjaj and Al-Nahhas. It was said that its place is in the accusative case, meaning that the oath by God Almighty does not prevent you from righteousness, piety and reform, also according to Al-Zajjaj. It was said that it is an object for the sake of which, and it was said that its meaning is that you do not be righteous, so la was omitted like the Almighty’s saying: God makes clear to you lest you go astray (An-Nisa’: 176), meaning lest you go astray, as Al-Tabari and Al-Nahhas said. A fourth aspect of the accusative case is the dislike of you being righteous, then Al-Nahhas and Al-Mahdawi mentioned it. It was said that it is in a place according to the saying of Al-Khalil and Al-Kisa’i, the estimate: in that you are righteous, so fi was implied and lowered with it, and Hearer meaning of the words of the servants, Knower of their intentions.
2:225: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: with idle talk: the source of laghā yalghū is laghā yalghā and laghā yalghā laghā means to say something that is not needed in speech, or something that is not good. Abu Bakmah yalghā is sinful. In the hadith: If you say to your companion while the imam is delivering the sermon on Friday, ‘Listen,’ then you have spoken idle talk, and the language of Abu Hurairah is then you have spoken idle talk, and the poet said: And the pilgrims' flocks are restrained from idle talk and obscene speech. Another said: I am not held accountable for what you say if you do not intend to do so. The second: The scholars differed regarding the oath that is idle. Ibn Abbas said: It is a man saying in the course of his speech and his haste in the conversation: No, by God, and Yes, by God, without intending to swear. Al-Marwazi said: The idle oath that the scholars consider to be idle is a man saying: No, by God, and Yes, by God, in his speech and words without believing in the oath or intending it. Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Ibn Shihab that Urwah told him that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Idle oaths are those that are in argument, jest, joking, and conversation that the heart does not accept. In Al-Bukhari on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: The verse of God Almighty: God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths was revealed regarding a man saying: No, by God, and Yes, by God. It was said: Idle is what is sworn based on suspicion, so it is the opposite of it. Malik said it, Ibn Al-Qasim narrated it on his authority, and a group of the Salaf said it. Abu Hurairah said: If a man swears on something, he does not think it is anything other than it, but it is not, then it is idle.:Idle talk, and there is no expiation for it, and something similar to that from Ibn Abbas, and it was narrated: “A group of people exchanged opinions before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while they were shooting in his presence, and one of them swore, ‘I hit and missed, O so-and-so,’ and the matter turned out to be different, so the man said, ‘He broke his oath, O Messenger of God,’ and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘The oaths of archers are idle talk, there is no breaking of the oath and no expiation for it.’” In Al-Muwatta’, Malik said: The best thing I have heard about this is that idle talk is when a person swears to do something and is certain that it is so, then it turns out to be otherwise, so there is no expiation for it. And the one who swears to do something while he knows that it is a sinful and false oath in order to please someone, or to apologize to a creature, or to extract money from it, this is greater than there is expiation for it, and expiation is only for swearing not to do something that is permissible for him to do and then he does it, or to do it and then he does not do it, such as if he swears not to sell his garment for ten dirhams and then sells it for the same, or he swears to hit his slave and then does not hit him. And it was narrated from Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, There is no oath in anger. Narrated by Muslim. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is the prohibition of what is permissible, so he says: What is forbidden to me if I do such and such, and what is permissible to me is forbidden. Makhul al-Dimashqi and Malik also said this, except in the case of a wife, for he made it obligatory for her to be forbidden unless the one who swore in his heart expelled her. It was also said that it is an oath of disobedience. Saeed bin al-Musayyab, Abu Bakr bin Abd al-Rahman, Urwah and Abdullah bin al-Zubayr said this, like the one who swears to drink alcohol or to sever family ties, so his righteousness is to leave that action and there is no expiation upon him. Their proof is the hadith of Amr bin Shuaib on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him leave it, and if he leaves it, its expiation is due. Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, and it will also come in al-Ma’idah. Zaid bin Aslam said: The idle oath is a man’s supplication against himself: May God blind his sight, may God take away his wealth, he is a Jew, he is a polytheist, it is idleness if he does such and such. Mujahid: They are two men who are exchanging goods and one of them says: By God. I will not sell it to you for this much, and the other says: By God, I will not buy it for this much. An-Nakha’i: It is a man who swears not to do something and then forgets and does it. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak also said: The idle oath is the one that is disliked, meaning if the oath is atoned for, it is dropped and becomes idle, and God does not hold one accountable for atoning for it and returning to what is better. Ibn Abd Al-Barr narrated a saying: The idle oaths are the oaths of one who is forced. Ibn Al-Arabi said: As for the oath with forgetfulness, there is no doubt about its being annulled, because it came contrary to his intention, so it is pure idle. I said: The oath of one who is forced is like it, and the ruling on one who swears under duress will come in An-Nahl, God willing. Ibn Al-Arabi said: As for the one who said that the oath of disobedience is invalid, because the oath of one who swears to refrain from disobedience is binding as an act of worship, and the oath of one who swears to commit a disobedience is binding as a disobedience, and it is said to him: Do not do it and disbelieve, so if he proceeds to do the act, he sins in proceeding and is righteous in his oath. As for the one who said: It is a person’s supplication against himself, if such and such is the case, then it is a meaningless statement, in the way of expiation, but it is binding in intent, it is disliked, and he may be held accountable for it, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let none of you supplicate against himself, for perhaps he encounters an hour in which no one asks God for something except that He gives it to him. As for the one who said that it is an oath of anger, then he is refuted by the oath of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in anger not to bear the burden of the Ash’aris and their burden, and he expiated for his oath, and it will come in Bara’ah. Ibn Al-Arabi said: As for the one who said: It is the expiatory oath, there is no connection to it that can be narrated, and Ibn Attia also said: God Almighty has lifted the punishment for idle talk in general, so its reality is that there is no sin or expiation in it, and the punishment for oaths is the punishment of the Hereafter in the case of a false oath that is patient, and in what is left out of expiation for which there is expiation, and the punishment of this world in obligating expiation, so the statement that it is the expiatory oath is weak, because the punishment has occurred in it, and specifying the punishment as being in the Hereafter only is a ruling. Third: The Almighty’s saying: In your oaths. Oaths are the plural of oath, and an oath is a vow. Its origin is that when the Arabs made an alliance or contract, a man would take the oath of his companion with his oath. Then this became widespread until the oath and covenant itself was called an oath. It was said: an oath is a verbal noun from the word yemen, which means blessing. God Almighty called it this because it preserves rights. An oath is masculine and feminine, and its plural is oaths and hand-wraps. Zuhair said: So gather the right ones from us and from you Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned is like His statement: But He will hold you accountable for what you have sworn in deed (al-Ma’idah 5:89), and there we will discuss it in full, God willing. Zayd ibn Asm said: The Almighty’s statement: But He will hold you accountable for what your hearts have earned is the man who says: He is a polytheist if he did, meaning this idle talk, unless he has sworn in deed of polytheism in his heart and earns it, and Forgiving, Forbearing are two attributes that are appropriate to what was mentioned about the rejection of accountability, as it is a door of leniency and expansion.
2:226: It contains twenty-four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: For those who swear. “Ya’loon” means they swear, and the source is ila’, alia, al-wah, and al-wah. Abi and Ibn Abbas read For those who swear. It is known that yaqsimoon is an interpretation of ya’loon. It was also read For those who swear. It is said: ala ya’lo ila’, ta’ala ta’liyan, and itala itila’, meaning he swore. From this is And let not those among you who are endowed with virtue swear. (al-Nur 24:22), and the poet said: I swear that I will never stop writing a poem that will be an example for her and me after me. Another said: He who does little wrong is faithful to his oath, and if he does wrong he will be absolved. Ibn Duraid said: A mechanism by which salvation is thrown between the edges of the desert Abdullah bin Abbas said: The oath of the pre-Islamic era was for one or two years or more, with the intention of harming the woman when they were abused, so they were given a time limit of four months. So whoever swears an oath for less than that is not a legal oath. I said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, swore an oath and divorced them. The reason for his oath was that his wives asked him for more money than he had. This is in Sahih Muslim. It was also said that it was because Zainab returned his gift to him, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry and swore an oath against them. This was mentioned by Ibn Majah. Second: The oath is binding on everyone who is required to divorce. The free man, the slave, and the drunkard are required to oath, as are the foolish and the one under his care if he is an adult and not insane. The same applies to the eunuch if he is not castrated, and the old man if he still has some life and energy left in him. Al-Shafi’i’s opinion differed regarding the eunuch who swears an oath. In one opinion, he has no oath, and in another opinion, his oath is valid. The first is more correct and closer to the Book and the Sunnah, because the oath is what cancels the oath, and the oath by word does not cancel it. If the oath that prevents perjury remains, the ruling on the oath remains. The oath of the mute by what is understood from him in writing or a comprehensible sign is binding on him, as is the case for the foreigner if he swears an oath from his wives. Third: The scholars differed regarding the oath by which the oath is performed. Some people said: The oath is only performed by swearing by God Almighty alone, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Whoever swears, let him swear by God or remain silent. This is what Al-Shafi’i said in Al-Jadeed. Ibn Abbas said: Every oath that prevents intercourse is an oath. This is what Al-Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i, Malik, the people of Hijaz, Sufyan Al-Thawri, the people of Iraq, Al-Shafi’i in the other opinion, Abu Thawr, Abu Ubaid, Ibn Al-Mundhir, and Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: Every oath by which its owner is unable to have intercourse with his wife for her sake except by breaking it is a wali, if his oath is for more than four months. So whoever swears by God or by one of His attributes or says: I swear by God, or I bear witness by God, or by God’s covenant, guarantee, pledge, and responsibility, then the oath is required of him. If he says: I swear or I resolve and does not mention God, then it is said: The oath is not included in it, unless he meant God. )) And he intended it, and whoever said that it is an oath that is entered upon him, and its explanation will come in (Al-Ma’idah) God willing, then if he swore by fasting not to have intercourse with his wife and said: If I have intercourse with you, then I must fast for a month or a year, then he is a sworn oath, and likewise everything that is required of him of Hajj, divorce, manumission, prayer, or charity, and the origin of this sentence is the generality of the Almighty’s saying: For those who swear and he did not differentiate, so if he swore by charity or manumission of a slave, whether specific or not, then the oath is required. Fourth: If he swears by God that he will not have intercourse and makes an exception, saying: If he wishes, then he is considered a guardian. If he has intercourse with her, then there is no expiation upon him, according to the narration of Ibn al-Qasim on the authority of Malik. Ibn al-Majshun said in al-Mabsut: He is not a guardian, and this is more correct, because the exception dissolves the oath and makes the one who swore as if he had not sworn, and this is the doctrine of the jurists of the regions, because it is clear by the exception that he is not intending to do the act. The reason for what Ibn al-Qasim narrated is based on the fact that the exception does not dissolve the oath, but it does affect the expiation, as will be explained in al-Ma’idah. So since his oath remained binding, the ruling of ila’ is binding upon him, even if he is not required to make expiation. Fifth: If he swears by the Prophet, the angels, or the Kaaba that he will not have intercourse with her, or he says he is a Jew, a Christian, or an adulterer if he has intercourse with her, then this is not a mawl, as Malik and others have said. Al-Baji said: The meaning of that, in my opinion, is that he mentioned it in a way other than an oath. But if he mentioned it as a mawl because of what he said of that or something else, then in Al-Mabsut: Ibn Al-Qasim was asked about a man who says to his wife: No welcome, meaning by that an oath, is he a mawl, he said: Malik said: Every word with which he intends divorce is divorce, and this and divorce are the same. Sixth: The scholars differed regarding the oath mentioned in the Qur’an. Ibn Abbas said: He is not considered to be a divorcee until he swears that he will never touch her. A group said: If he swears that he will not approach his wife for a day or less or more, and then does not have intercourse for four months, she is separated from him by the oath. This was narrated from Ibn Mas’ud, Al-Nakha’i, Ibn Abi Layla, Al-Hakam, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and Qatada. Ishaq said the same. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: Many scholars rejected this statement. The majority said: The oath is that he swears that he will not have intercourse for more than four months. If he swears for four or less, he is not a divorcee. According to them, it is a pure oath. If he has intercourse during this period, he is not required to do anything like any other oath. This is the opinion of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Abu Thawr. Al-Thawri and the Kufians said that the oath is to swear for four months or more, and this is the opinion of Ata’. The Kufians said: God made the waiting period for the oath four months, just as He made the waiting period for death four months and ten, and the waiting period is three menstrual cycles, so there is no waiting period after that. They said: After the period, the oath must be dropped, and it is not dropped except by the oath of nullity, which is intercourse within the period, and divorce after the expiration of the four months. Malik and Al-Shafi’i provided evidence and said: God has given the oath-taker four months, so they are his in full and his wife has no objection to him in them, just as the deferred debt is not entitled to its owner to demand it except after the completion of the period. The reason for Ishaq’s statement that in a short period, its owner is considered to be a nullifier if he does not have intercourse is the analogy to someone who swears for more than four months, for he is considered to be a nullifier, because it is harmful by the oath, and this meaning is present in the short period. Seventh: They differed that if someone swears not to have intercourse for more than four months, and the four months have passed and his wife has not demanded it from him nor has she referred him to the ruler to stop him, then nothing is binding on him according to Malik and his companions and most of the people of Medina. Some of our scholars say that nothing is binding on him according to Malik and his companions and most of the people of Medina. Some of our scholars say that a revocable divorce is binding on him after the four months have passed. Some of them and others say that an irrevocable divorce is binding on him after the four months have passed. What is correct is what Malik and his companions went to, and that is that the master is not bound by divorce until the ruler stops him with his wife demanding it from him so that he can return to his wife by intercourse and atone for his oath or divorce her, and he does not leave her until he returns or divorces her. And the revocation is intercourse with someone with whom intercourse is possible. Sulayman ibn Yasar said, nine men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to stop the oath. Malik said: And that is the matter according to us, and Al-Layth, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr said the same, and Ibn Al-Mundhir chose it. Eighth: The deadline for the master is from the day he swore, not from the day his wife disputed with him and brought him to the judge. If she disputed with him and was not satisfied with his refusal to have intercourse, the ruler sets a deadline for him of four months from the day he swore. If he has intercourse, he has fulfilled his wife’s right and atoned for his oath. If he does not fulfill his oath, he is given a revocable divorce. Malik said: If he takes her back, it is not valid until he has intercourse during the waiting period. Al-Abhari said: This is because the divorce only occurred to prevent harm, so if he did not have intercourse, the harm remains, so there is no meaning to taking her back unless he has an excuse that prevents him from having intercourse, in which case his taking her back is valid, because the harm has gone away, and his refusal to have intercourse is not because of the harm, but rather because of the excuse. Ninth: The scholars differed regarding the oath not taken in a state of anger. Ibn Abbas said: There is no oath except in anger. It was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, in the well-known report from him. Al-Layth, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Hasan and Ata’ said the same. They all say: The oath is only taken in a state of anger, intimidation, embarrassment and opposition, so that he does not have intercourse with her in her vagina to harm her, regardless of whether that is aimed at improving a child or not. If it is not taken out of anger, then it is not an oath. Ibn Sirin said: Whether the oath was taken in anger or otherwise, it is an oath. Ibn Mas’ud, Al-Thawri, Malik, the people of Iraq, Al-Shafi’i and his companions and Ahmad said the same, except that Malik said: As long as the purpose is not to improve a child. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: This is more correct, because since they agreed that the oath of zihar, divorce and all other oaths are the same in a state of anger and satisfaction, then the oath is the same. I said: The generality of the Qur’an indicates this, and specifying the state of anger requires evidence and is not taken from a necessary aspect, and God knows best.
