Tenth: Our uncles said: Whoever refuses to have intercourse with his wife without swearing an oath to harm her, he is ordered to have intercourse with her. If he refuses and continues to refuse to harm her, he is separated from her without setting a deadline. It has been said: A deadline for ila’ is set. It has been said: A man is not subject to ila’ in his desertion of his wife even if he stays for years without having intercourse with her. Rather, he is admonished and ordered to fear God Almighty and not to keep her to harm her. Eleventh: They differed concerning the one who swore not to have intercourse with his wife until she weaned her child, lest her child become a child, and he did not intend to harm her until the period of breastfeeding ended, his wife, according to Malik, had no claim with the intention of reforming the child. Malik said: It has reached me that Ali ibn Abi Talib was asked about that and he did not see it as an oath, and al-Shafi’i said the same in one of his two opinions, and the other opinion is that he is an oath, and the breastfeeding of the child is not taken into account, and Abu Hanifa said the same. Twelfth: Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa and their companions, Al-Awza’i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal held that he is not considered a guardian if he swears not to have intercourse with his wife in this house or in this home because he finds a way to have intercourse with her in another place. Ibn Abi Layla and Ishaq said: If he leaves her for four months, she is divorced by the oath. Do you not see that he stops at the four months? If he swears not to have intercourse with her in his city or country, then he is considered a guardian according to Malik. This only occurs when he is traveling and incurs expenses and costs, not his garden or his nearby farm. Thirteenth: The Almighty’s statement: from their women includes free women, non-Muslim women, and female slaves if they marry. The male slave is obligated to swear an oath from his wife. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Abu Thawr said: His oath is like the oath of a free man. Their proof is the apparent meaning of the Almighty’s statement: for those who swear an oath from their women. So that was for all husbands. Ibn al-Mundhir said: And I say the same. Malik, al-Zuhri, Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, and Ishaq said: Its term is two months. Al-Hasan and al-Nakha’i said: His oath from his female slave wife is two months, and from a free woman four months. Abu Hanifa said the same. Al-Sha’bi said: The oath of a female slave is half the oath of a free woman. Fourteenth: Malik and his companions, Abu Hanifa and his companions, Al-Awza’i, Al-Nakha’i, and others said: The one who has been penetrated and the one who has not been penetrated are the same in the necessity of the oath in both cases. Al-Zuhri, Ata’, and Al-Thawri said: There is no oath except after penetration. Malik said: There is no oath from a young girl who has not yet reached puberty. If he swears an oath from her and she reaches puberty, the oath is necessary from the day she reaches puberty. Fifteenth: As for the dhimmi, his ila’ is not valid, just as his zihar and divorce are not valid. This is because the marriage of the polytheists is not a valid marriage according to us, but they have only a hand full, and because they are not required to abide by the laws, they are required to pay expiations for oaths. If they brought a case to us regarding the ruling on ila’, our ruler should not rule between them, and they should go to their rulers. If this is done in accordance with the system between them, they will rule according to the ruling of Islam, just as if a Muslim had not had intercourse with his wife to cause harm without swearing an oath. Sixteenth: The Almighty said: Wait four months. Waiting means to be patient and to delay, the opposite of patience. The poet said: Death is waiting for her, perhaps she will divorce him one day or her husband will die. As for the benefit of setting a four-month limit, as Ibn Abbas mentioned about the people of ignorance, as mentioned above, God forbade that and made a period of four months for the husband to discipline the woman by deserting her, based on the Almighty’s saying: And desert them in their beds (An-Nisa’: 34). The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, swore to be away from his wives for a month as a form of discipline for them. It has been said that the four months are the period during which a woman cannot be patient with her husband for more than that. It has been narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was walking around Medina one night and heard a woman chanting: Oh, how long is this night, how dark is its side, and I am kept awake by the fact that I have no lover to play with. By God, if it weren’t for God and nothing else, the sides of this bed would have been shaken. The fear of my Lord and modesty are enough for me, and the honor of my husband is enough for his ships to reach me. The next day, Umar summoned the woman and said to her: Where is your husband? She said: I sent him to Iraq! So he summoned the women and asked them about the woman: How long can she be patient without her husband? They said: Two months. Her patience diminishes in three months, and her patience runs out in four months. So Umar made the period of a man’s campaign four months. When four months had passed, he would take the fighters back and send other people. And this, and God knows best, strengthens the restriction of the period of the oath to four months. Seventeenth: The Almighty’s saying: Then if they return means they come back, and from it is until it returns to the command of God (al-Hujurat 49:9), and from it the shadow after noon is called shade, because it returns from the side of the east to the side of the west, fa’a means shade, and it is quick to return, meaning to return. He said: It came and did not fulfill what it came for, and there are human needs that cannot be fulfilled. Eighteenth: Ibn al-Mundhir said: All of the scholars who have memorized it have agreed that the fare’ is intercourse for someone who has no excuse. If he has an excuse of illness, imprisonment, or something similar, then his taking her back is valid and she is his wife. If the excuse is removed by his arrival from his travel or his recovery from his illness, or his release from his imprisonment and he refuses intercourse, then they are separated if the period has been reduced. Malik said this in al-Mudawwanah and al-Mabsut. Abd al-Malik said: She is irrevocably divorced from him on the day the period has expired. If his excuse for the fare’ is true when she is able to do so, then his truthfulness is ruled in the past. If what he claims of the fare’ is false by abstaining when he is able to do so, then his matter is considered a lie and stubbornness, and the rulings are carried out according to what was required at that time. A group said: If a witness testifies to his fare’ in the case of an excuse, then it is sufficient for him. This was said by al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and al-Nakha’i. Al-Awza’i said this, and al-Nakha’i also said: The fare’ is valid by word and testimony only, and the ruling of the oath is dropped. Have you seen if he did not… It is spread for intercourse, Ibn Atiyah said: This statement is attributed to the issue of harm if he did not have intercourse, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: If he has an excuse, he should return to his heart, and Abu Qilabah said the same, and Abu Hanifa said: If he is unable to have intercourse, he should say: I have returned to her, Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: Abu Hanifa says about someone who swore an oath while he was sick and there was a period of four months between him and her, and she was a virgin or a minor or he was castrated: If he returns to her with his tongue and the period passes and the excuse remains, then that is a valid return, and Al-Shafi’i disagrees with him according to one of his two schools of thought, and a group said that the return is only by intercourse in the case of an excuse or otherwise, and Saeed ibn Jubayr said the same, he said: And also if he was traveling or in prison. Nineteenth: Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, their companions, and the majority of scholars made expiation obligatory for the master if he fulfilled his desire to have intercourse with his wife. Al-Hasan said: There is no expiation upon him. Al-Nakha’i said the same. Al-Nakha’i said: They used to say: If he fulfilled his desire, there is no expiation upon him. Ishaq said: Some of the people of interpretation said about the words of God Almighty: But if they fulfilled their desire, meaning the oath that they broke. This is a doctrine regarding oaths of some of the followers regarding someone who swore an oath of righteousness, piety, or a good deed not to do it, then he does it and there is no expiation upon him. The evidence for this is the words of God Almighty: But if they fulfilled their desire, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, and He did not mention expiation. Also, this is based on the fact that an oath is void if he swore an oath of disobedience, and not having intercourse with one’s wife is a disobedience. I said: This statement may be proven from the Sunnah by the hadith of Amr ibn Shu`ayb on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever swears an oath and then sees something else that is better than it, let him leave it, and if he leaves it, its expiation is due. It was included by Ibn Majah in his Sunan. This will be further explained in the verse on oaths, God willing. The evidence of the majority is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever swears an oath and then sees something else that is better than it, let him do what is better and expiate for his oath. Twenty: If he expiates for his oath, the oath is dropped from him. Our scholars said this. This is evidence of the expiation being given precedence over the oath in the school of thought. This is a consensus on the issue of the oath, and evidence for Abu Hanifa on the issue of oaths, as he does not see the permissibility of giving precedence to the oath, as Ibn al-Arabi said. Twenty-first: I said: With this verse, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan used as evidence the impossibility of expiation before breaking the oath. He said: Since God Almighty ruled for the guardian with one of the two rulings, whether compensation or the intention of divorce, if it were permissible to bring expiation forward before breaking the oath, the oath without compensation or the intention of divorce would be invalidated, because if he broke the oath, nothing is required of him by the oath, and whenever the one who broke the oath is not required to do anything, he is not a guardian. And in the permissibility of bringing expiation forward, the ruling of the oath is dropped without what God mentioned, and that is contrary to the Book.
2:227: Twenty-second: God Almighty said: And if they decide on divorce - then indeed, God is Hearing and Knowing. Resolve: is completing the contract on something. It is said: he resolved on it, he resolves, he resolves, he resolves, he resolves, he resolves, he resolves, and I resolved upon you to do it, meaning I swore upon you. Shammar said: Resolve and resolve are what your soul resolves upon you to do, and divorce is from the word talaq divorce, the woman divorces on the weight of nasr, yansr with a divorce, so she is divorced and divorced also. Al-A'sha said: Oh neighbor between me, you are divorced It is permissible to say talaqat with a damma on the lam like azam ya’zam, and Al-Akhfash denied it. Divorce is the dissolution of the marriage contract, and its origin is intilaaq, and al-mukhalliyat, and al-Talaq 65:the release. It is said: a divorced ewe, meaning neglected, left in the pasture with no restrictions on it or a shepherd, and a divorced camel with a damma on the ta’ and the lam is not restricted, and the plural is atlaaq, and habbed someone in the prison talqan, meaning without restrictions. And the divorced camel is the one that the shepherd leaves for himself and does not milk it at the water. It is said: the shepherd released a camel for himself, so the woman who is released is called what the ewe or the she-camel whose affairs are neglected is called, and it is said: it is taken from the talaq of the horse, which is its going a distance without preventing it, so the released woman is called divorced and is not prevented from herself after she was prevented. Twenty-third: In the words of God Almighty: And if they decide to divorce is evidence that she is not divorced after the passage of four months, as Malik said, unless the divorce is initiated after the period. Also, he said: All-Hearing and All-Hearing implies that it is heard after the passage. Abu Hanifa said: All-Hearing of his oath, All-Knowing of his intention, which was indicated by the passage of four months. Suhayl ibn Abi Salih narrated on the authority of his father, who said: I asked twelve men from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about a man who swears to divorce his wife, and all of them said: There is nothing upon him until four months have passed, then he should stop. If he returns, otherwise he should divorce. Judge Ibn al-Arabi said: The truth of the matter is that the verse, according to us, is: “For those who swear to divorce their wives, a waiting period of four months. If they return” after its expiration, “then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. And if they swear to divorce their wives, a waiting period of four months. If they return” and its estimation according to them is: “For those who swear to divorce their wives, a waiting period of four months. If they return” in it, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. God is Forgiving and Merciful. But if they decide to divorce, by leaving the group in it, meaning the waiting period in it, then God is Hearing and Knowing, Ibn al-Arabi. This is an equal possibility, and because of its equality the Companions hesitated about it. I said: If the possibility is equal, then the statement of the Kufians is stronger, based on analogy to the woman who observes the waiting period of months and menstrual cycles, since all of that is a term set by God Almighty, so when it expires, the bond of marriage is severed and she is declared divorced without dispute, and her husband has no way to deal with her except with her permission. So it is the same with the oath, even if he forgets the compensation and the period expires, the divorce takes place, and God knows best. Twenty-fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And if they decide on divorce, is evidence that a slave woman who is owned by the right hand cannot be subject to ila’, since divorce does not take place upon her, and God knows best.
2:228: The Almighty’s saying: Divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods. There are five issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And divorced women When God the Almighty mentioned the oath and that divorce may occur in it, God the Almighty explained the ruling on the woman after the divorce. In the book of Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said regarding the saying of God the Almighty: And divorced women shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods, that is because if a man divorced his wife, he had more right to her, even if he divorced her three times, so he abrogated that and said: Divorce is twice, and the word divorced is a general term, and what is meant by it is specific to those who have been consummated with, and the divorced woman before consummation was excluded by the verse of al-Ahzab 33:So you have no waiting period to count for them (al-Ahzab 33:49) as will come, and likewise the pregnant woman by His saying: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth (al-Talaq: 4), and what is meant by the menstrual periods is purification, unlike the waiting period of death, which is an act of worship, and God made the waiting period of the young girl who has not menstruated and the old woman who has despaired of menstruation months as will come, and some people said: The generality in divorced women includes these, then it was abrogated, and this is weak, and the verse is only for those who menstruate specifically, and this is the custom of women. Most of them are like that. The second: The Almighty’s saying: They shall wait. Waiting is waiting, as we have presented, and this is report and what is meant, like the Almighty’s saying: And mothers shall nurse their children (al-Baqarah 2:233). And the plural of a man wearing his clothes, and a dirham is enough for you, meaning be satisfied with a dirham, this is the saying of the people of the language without disagreement among them in what Ibn Al-Shajari and Ibn Al-Arabi mentioned, and this is false, rather it is report about the ruling of the Shari’ah, so if you find an absolute one who does not wait, then it is not from the Shari’ah, and it does not necessitate that the report of God Almighty occurs in opposition to its informant. It was said: Its meaning is that they shall wait, so the lam was deleted. Third: The majority of people read (quru’) in the weight of fa’ul, the lam is a hamza, and it is narrated from Nafi’ (quru’) with a kasra on the waw and a shaddah on it without a hamza, and al-Hasan read (qur’) with a fatha on the qaf and a sukoon on the ra’ and tanween, and qur’ is the plural of aqru’ and aqra’, and the singular is qur’ with a damma on the qaf, as al-Asma’i said, and Abu Zaid said (qur’) with a fatha on the qaf, and both of them said: A woman read if she menstruated, so she is a muqri’, and aqra’t became pure, and al-Akhfash said: A woman read if she became a woman of menstruation, so when she menstruated you say: qara’t without an alif, it is said: A woman read one menstrual cycle or two menstrual cycles, and qur’ is the cessation of menstruation, and some of them said: what is between the two menstrual cycles, and aqra’t hajatak: it approached, according to al-Jawhari, and Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: Some Arabs call menstruation qur’, and some of them call purity qur’, and some of them combine them both, so they call purity with menstruation. Qur’an, mentioned by An-Nahhas. Fourth: The scholars differed regarding the menstrual periods. The people of Kufa said that it is the menstruation, which is the opinion of Omar, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Abu Musa, Mujahid, Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, Ikrimah, and As-Suddi. The people of Hijaz said that it is the purity, which is the opinion of Aisha, Ibn Omar, Zaid bin Thabit, Az-Zuhri, Abaan bin Othman, and Ash-Shafi’i. Whoever made the menstrual period a name for it called it that because of the blood gathering in the womb, and whoever made it a name for purity, because of its gathering in the body. What confirms this principle regarding the menstrual period is the time. It is said: The wind blew for its menstrual period and its reciter, meaning for its time. The poet said: I hated the barrenness of the Banu Shaleel when the winds blew for its reader It was said that menstruation has a time, and that purity has a time, because they both return to a known time. Al-A’sha said about purity: Every year you are a raider, and your determination to console you reaches its furthest point. A heritage of honor and elevation in menstruation, because of the menstrual periods of your women that are lost in it. Another said about menstruation: Oh God, whoever has a grudge against me, make him menstruate like a menstruating woman. Meaning that he stabbed him and he had blood like the blood of a menstruating woman. Some people said: It is taken from the word qara’a to gather water in a basin, which means to collect it. From this comes the word Qur’an the Qur’an for the meanings coming together, and it is said for the letters coming together. It is said: The she-camel has never gathered a placenta, meaning it has never gathered in its stomach. Amr ibn Kulthum said: My arms are broken, my blood is broken, my color is mixed, I have never read a fetus The uterus collects blood during menstruation, and the body collects it during purification. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: The statement of those who said that the menstrual period is taken from their saying: I drank water in the basin is not a matter of anything, because the menstrual period is hamzated and this is not hamzated. I said: This is correct according to the linguists, Al-Jawhari and others, and the name of that water is Qara with a kasra on the qaf and a shortened one. It was said: Qir’, the exit either from a state of purity to a menstruation or from a menstruation to a state of purity. Based on this, Al-Shafi’i said in a statement: Qir’ is the transition from purity to menstruation, and he does not see the exit from menstruation to purity as Qir’, and it would be necessary by virtue of derivation that it be Qir’, and the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And divorced women shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods, meaning three cycles or three transitions, and the divorced woman is described by only two states, sometimes she moves from purity to menstruation, and sometimes from menstruation to purity, so the meaning of the speech is correct, and its indication of purity and menstruation together, so the name becomes common, and it is said: If it is proven that Qir’ is the transition, then her exit from purity to menstruation is not intended by the verse at all, and therefore divorce during menstruation is not a Sunnah divorce that is commanded, and it is divorce for the waiting period, because divorce for the waiting period is what is during purity, and that indicates The menstrual cycle is taken from the transition, so if the divorce during purity is Sunnah, then the meaning of the statement is: Their waiting period is three transitions, the first of which is the transition from the period of purity in which the divorce occurred, which is the transition from menstruation to purity, and it is not considered a menstrual cycle, because the language does not indicate it, but we know from another proof that God the Most High did not intend the transition from menstruation to purity, so if one of them is no longer intended, the other remains intended, which is the transition from purity to menstruation, so based on this her waiting period is three transitions, the first of which is purity, and based on this it is possible to complete three full menstrual cycles if the divorce occurred during a state of purity, and this is not carried on metaphor in any way, Al-Kaya Al-Tabari said: This is a very precise view in the direction of the Shafi’i school, and we can mention in that a secret that is not far from understanding the subtleties of the ruling of the Shari’ah, which is that the transition from purity to menstruation was only considered a menstrual cycle because it indicates the purity of the womb, because the pregnant woman does not menstruate in most cases, so by her menstruation the purity of her womb is known, and the transition from menstruation to purity is the opposite. A menstruating woman may become pregnant following her period. If the pregnancy continues and the child is strong, her bleeding will stop. Therefore, the Arabs agreed that their women should become pregnant during a state of purity. Aisha praised the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the words of the poet: And free from all menstrual irregularities, breastfeeding corruption, and debilitating disease. It means that a nation did not become pregnant with him during the rest of her menstruation. This is what the scholars and the people of the language have in interpreting the menstrual cycle. They said: A woman menstruates when she menstruates or becomes pure, and she also recites when she becomes pregnant. They agreed that the menstrual cycle is the time. So if you say: And divorced women wait by themselves for three times, the verse becomes interpreted in terms of the number and is possible in terms of what is counted. So it is necessary to seek clarification for what is counted from someone other than her. Our evidence is the statement of God the Most High: So divorce them at their prescribed period (al-Talaq 65:1). There is no disagreement that divorce is commanded at the time of purity, so it must be what is considered in the waiting period, for He said: So divorce them meaning a time for which she observes the waiting period. Then God the Most High said: And count the waiting period (al-Talaq 65:1). He means what the divorced woman observes, which is the period of purity in which she is divorced. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said to Umar: “Tell him to take her back, then to hold her until she is pure, then menstruates, then becomes pure. That is the waiting period that God has commanded women to be divorced for.” Narrated by Muslim and others. It is explicit in that the time of purity is Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman said: We did not find anyone among our jurists who did not say what Aisha said, that the menstrual periods are the periods of purity. So if a man divorces during a period of purity in which he has not had intercourse, she observes the waiting period for what remains of it, even if it is an hour or a moment. Then she begins a second period of purity after a menstrual period, then a third period after a second menstrual period. If she sees blood from the third period, she is permitted to marry and exits the waiting period. If a divorcer divorces during a period of purity in which he has had intercourse, then the divorce is binding on him, and he has done wrong. She observes the waiting period for what remains of that period of purity. Al-Zuhri said about a woman who was divorced during some of her period of purity: She observes the waiting period for three periods of purity in addition to the rest of that period of purity. Abu Umar said: I do not know anyone who said: The menstrual periods are the periods of purity except Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, for he said: She cancels the period of purity in which she was divorced, then she observes the waiting period for three periods of purity, because God Almighty He says: Three menstrual periods. I said: According to his statement, the divorced woman is not permissible until she enters the fourth menstrual period, and the statement of Ibn al-Qasim, Malik, the majority of his companions, al-Shafi’i, and the scholars of Medina: If the divorced woman sees the first drop of the third menstrual period, she is no longer married. This is the view of Zayd ibn Thabit, Aisha, and Ibn Umar, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said the same, and Dawud ibn Ali and his companions agreed with him. The evidence against al-Zuhri is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted the divorce of a woman who is pure without intercourse, and he did not say the beginning of purity or the end of it. Ashhab said: The marriage and inheritance are not severed until it is confirmed that it is menstrual blood, lest it be a sudden burst of blood other than menstruation. The Kufians used as evidence the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Fatima bint Abi Hubaish when she complained to him about the blood: It is only a vein, so look, so when your menstrual period comes, do not pray, and when the menstrual period passes, purify yourself and then pray from menstrual period to menstrual period. And God Almighty said: And for those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their period is three months. (al-Talaq: 4), so he made the hopeless one Menstruation, so it indicates that it is the waiting period, and making the symptom of it the most famous if it is non-existent, and Omar said in the presence of the companions: The waiting period of a slave woman is two menstrual periods, half the waiting period of a free woman, and if I were able to make it one menstrual period and a half I would have done so, and no one objected to him, so it indicates that it is a consensus from them, and it is the saying of ten of the companions, including the four caliphs, and what they said is enough for you! And the saying of God the Almighty: And divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods indicates that: because the meaning is they shall wait three menstrual periods, meaning complete ones, and this cannot be except according to our saying that the menstrual periods are menstruation, because whoever says: It is purity allows her to observe two menstrual periods and some of another, because if he divorces her during purity, she observes according to him the remaining menstrual period as a menstrual period, and according to us she starts over from the beginning of the menstruation until the name is true, so if a man divorces a woman during a period of purity in which he has not had intercourse, she begins a menstrual period, then a menstrual period, then a menstrual period, so if she performs ghusl from the third, she exits the waiting period. I said: This is refuted by the statement of God Almighty: He subjected them to them for seven nights and eight days (al-Haqqah 69:7). So He confirmed the letter ha in eight days because the day is masculine, as is the menstrual cycle, so it indicates that it is what is meant. Abu Hanifa agreed with us that if she is divorced while menstruating, she does not observe the waiting period in which she was divorced nor the period of purity that follows it, but rather she observes the period that follows the period of purity, and in our view she observes the period of purity, as we have explained. The linguists have permitted expressing some by the name of all, as God Almighty said: The Hajj is in well-known months (al-Baqarah 2:197), and what is meant by it are two months and some of the third, so likewise His statement: three menstrual cycles and God knows best. Some of those who say that it is menstruation said: If she becomes pure from the third, the waiting period ends after the ritual bath and she is divorced again. This was said by Saeed bin Jubayr, Tawus, Ibn Shabramah, and Al-Awza’i. Sharik said: If a woman neglects the ritual bath for twenty years, then her husband has the right to take her back as long as she does not perform the ritual bath. It was narrated on the authority of Ishaq bin Rahwayh said: If a woman menstruates for the third time, she is divorced and the husband’s right to return to her is cut off, except that it is not permissible for her to marry again until she washes herself from her menstruation. Something similar was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and it is a weak statement, based on the statement of God Almighty: And when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves (al-Baqarah 2:234), as will come. As for what Al-Shafi’i mentioned, that the transition from purity to menstruation itself is called a menstrual period, its benefit is to shorten the woman’s waiting period, because if he divorces the woman in the last hour of her purity and she enters menstruation, his waiting period is a menstrual period, and by the transition from the third period of purity itself, the marriage bond is cut off and she becomes permissible, and God knows best. Fifth: The majority of scholars agree that the waiting period of a slave woman who menstruates after her husband’s divorce is two menstrual cycles. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin that he said: I do not see the waiting period of a slave woman as being like the waiting period of a free woman, unless a year has passed in that regard, in which case the Sunnah is more deserving of being followed. Al-Asamm Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan, Dawud ibn Ali, and a group of scholars of the Zahir said that the verses on the waiting period of divorce and death in months and menstrual cycles are general for the slave woman and the free woman, so the waiting period of a free woman and a slave woman are the same. The majority of scholars have cited as evidence the words of the Prophet, peace be upon him: A divorce is two divorces and her waiting period is two menstrual cycles. It was narrated by Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Muzahir ibn Aslam on the authority of his father on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: The divorce of a slave woman is two divorces and her menstrual cycle is two menstrual cycles. So he added to them both the divorce and the waiting period, except that Muzahir ibn Aslam was the only one who narrated this hadith and it is weak. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that whichever of them is weak, his divorce is invalid, and a group of scholars said this. The Almighty’s saying: It is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs. There are two issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, meaning menstruation, as stated by Ikrimah, Az-Zuhri, and An-Nakha’i. It was also said: pregnancy, as stated by ‘Umar and Ibn ‘Abbas. Mujahid said: menstruation and pregnancy together, and this is on the basis that the pregnant woman menstruates. The intended meaning of the verse is that since the matter of the waiting period revolves around menstruation and purity, and no one can know about them except the women, the majority of the statement is her statement if she claims that the waiting period has ended or not, and He made them trustworthy in that, and this is what is required by the Almighty’s saying: And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs, and Sulayman ibn Yasar said: We were not commanded to open women’s vaginas so that we could look at their private parts, but rather that is up to them since they are trustworthy. The meaning of the prohibition of concealment is the prohibition of harming the husband and taking away his right, so if the woman who has been licked says, I menstruated, and she has not menstruated, she has taken away his right from… The return, and if she says: I did not menstruate, and she did menstruate, then he is obligated to pay him maintenance that he is not obligated to pay, so he is struck with it, or she intends by her lie in denying menstruation that she will not return until the waiting period ends and the law cuts off his right, and likewise the pregnant woman conceals the pregnancy, to cut off his right to return. Qatada said: It was their custom in the pre-Islamic era to conceal the pregnancy in order to attribute the child to the new husband, so the verse was revealed about that, and it was narrated that a man from Ashja’ came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I divorced my wife while she was pregnant, and I am not sure that she will marry and my child will be for someone else, so God revealed the verse, and the Ashja’i woman returned to him. Second: Ibn al-Mundhir said: And all of the scholars I have memorized from said: If a woman says in ten days: I have had three menstrual periods and my waiting period has ended, she is not to be believed and that is not accepted from her, unless she says: I have miscarried a fetus whose nature has become apparent. And they differed regarding the period in which a woman is to be believed. Malik said: If she says: My waiting period has ended within a period in which the waiting period ends before her statement, then if she informs that the waiting period has ended within a period that occurs rarely, then there are two opinions. He said in al-Mudawwanah: If she says: I have had three menstrual periods in a month, she is to be believed if the women believe her. And Shuraih said the same, and Ali ibn Abi Talib said to him: They said! That is, you are right and well. And he said in the book of Muhammad: Do not believe her except in a month and a half. And similar to it is the opinion of Abu Thawr. Abu Thawr said: The least that can be in forty-seven days, because the least period of purity is fifteen days, and the least period of menstruation is one day. And al-Nu`man said: Do not believe her in less than sixty days, and al-Shafi`i said the same. The Almighty’s statement: If they believe in God and the Last Day is a great and severe warning to emphasize the prohibition of concealment, and an obligation to fulfill the trust in informing about the womb with the truth of what is in it, meaning that the path of the believing women is not to conceal the truth. His statement: If they believe in God does not mean that it is permissible for someone who does not believe to conceal, because that is not permissible for someone who does not believe. Rather, it is like your saying: If you are my brother, then do not wrong me, meaning that faith should prevent you from it, because that is not the action of the people of faith. The Almighty’s saying, And their husbands have more right to take them back. There are eleven issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And their husbands. Ba’ulah is the plural of Ba’l, which is the husband. He was called Ba’l because of his superiority over the wife by virtue of what he possessed of her marriage. From this is the saying of the Almighty: Do you call upon Ba’l? (al-Saffat 37:125), meaning Lord, because of his superiority in Lordship. It is said: Ba’l and Ba’ulah, just as it is said in the plural of male: Dhakr and Dhakruh, and in the plural of Fahl: Fahl and Fahulah. This Ha’ is an additional letter that emphasizes the femininity of the group, and it is anomalous and cannot be used as a basis for analogy. It is considered in it by hearing, so it is not said in La’b: La’ubah. It was said: It is a feminine Ha’ that entered Fa’ul. Ba’ulah is also the source of Ba’l, and the man’s Ba’l is Ya’bal like Mana’a yanma’a with Ba’ulah, meaning he became a Ba’l, and Muba’ala and Ba’al: sexual intercourse. From this is his saying, peace be upon him, about the days of Tashreeq: They are days of eating, drinking, and Ba’al. So the man is the woman’s husband, and the woman is his Ba’al, and Ba’al Muba’ala if he has intercourse with her, and so-and-so is the husband of this, meaning. Malika and his Lord, and it has many meanings that will come, God willing. The second: The Almighty’s saying: more entitled to take them back meaning to return to them. Returning is of two types: Returning during the waiting period according to the hadith of Ibn ‘Umar, and returning after the waiting period according to the hadith of Mu’qil. If this is the case, then the verse is evidence of the specificity of what is included in the generality in the names, because the Almighty’s saying: And divorced women shall wait concerning themselves for three menstrual periods is general in regard to those who have been divorced three times, and there is no disagreement about what is less than that. Then His saying: And their husbands have more right is a specific ruling for those whose divorce was less than three times. The scholars agreed that if a free man divorces his free wife, and she has been consummated with him with one or two divorces, he has more right to take her back as long as her waiting period has not expired, even if the woman dislikes it. If the divorcer does not return her until her waiting period has expired, then she has more right to herself and becomes a stranger to him, and she is not permissible for him except through a proposal and a new marriage with a guardian and witnesses, not according to the Sunnah of returning. This is a consensus of the scholars. Al-Muhallab said: And whoever returns during the waiting period, then nothing of the rulings of marriage is required of him other than witnesses to the return only, and this is a consensus of the scholars. Because God Almighty said: “And when they have reached their term, either keep them according to acceptable terms or part from them according to acceptable terms. And bring to witness two just men from among you.” (al-Talaq 65:2), so He mentioned witnessing in the case of taking them back, but He did not mention it in the case of marriage or divorce. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: What we have mentioned from the Book of God, along with the consensus of the people of knowledge, is sufficient to mention what was narrated from the ancients in this matter, and God Almighty knows best. Third: They differed about what constitutes a man returning to her during the waiting period. Malik said: If he has intercourse with her during the waiting period and he intends to return her and he does not know that there is a witness, then it is a return, and the woman should prevent him from intercourse until he witnesses. Ishaq said the same, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Actions are by intentions, and each person will have what he intended. If he has intercourse during the waiting period and does not intend to return her, then Malik said: He should return to her during the waiting period and not have intercourse until he has purified her from his corrupted semen. Ibn al-Qasim said: If her waiting period has expired, neither he nor anyone else should marry her during the remainder of the period of purification. If he does, then his marriage is annulled, and her prohibition to him does not last forever because the semen is his semen. A group said: If he has intercourse with her, then he has returned to her. This is what Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn Sirin, al-Zuhri, Ata’, Tawus, and al-Thawri said. He said: And he should bear witness. This is what the people of opinion, al-Awza’i, and Ibn Abi Layla said, as narrated by Ibn al-Mundhir. Abu Umar said: It has been said: His intercourse is a return in any case, he intended it. Or he did not intend it, and this is narrated from a group of Malik’s companions, and Al-Layth went to it, and they did not differ regarding the one who sold his female slave with the option that he has intercourse with her during the option period, and that he has thereby returned her to his possession, and he chose to annul the sale by his action, and the woman who has been divorced with a revocable right has a ruling from this, and God knows best. Fourth: If he kisses or touches her with the intention of returning, then it is a return. If he does not intend to return with the kiss or touch, then he is sinful and is not a return. The Sunnah is that he testifies before he has intercourse or before he kisses or touches her. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: If he has intercourse with her or touches her with lust or looks at her vagina with lust, then it is a return. This is the opinion of al-Thawri, and he should testify. According to the opinion of Malik, al-Shafi’i, Ishaq, Abu Ubaid, and Abu Thawr, it is not a return. Ibn al-Mundhir said in al-Muntaqa: There is no disagreement about the validity of returning by word. As for action, such as intercourse and kissing, Judge Abu Muhammad said: It is valid with it and with all other forms of enjoyment for pleasure. Ibn al-Mawaz said: And such as touching for pleasure, or looking at her vagina or similar parts of her charms if he intends to return by that, contrary to al-Shafi’i’s saying: Return is not valid except by word. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated it from Abu Thawr, Jabir ibn Zayd, and Abu Qilabah. Fifth: Al-Shafi’i said: If he has intercourse with her, whether he intends to return her or not, then it is not a return, and she is entitled to a dower similar to hers from him. Malik said: She is not entitled to anything, because if he took her back, he would not have had to pay a dower, so intercourse without taking her back is not more deserving of a dower than taking her back. Abu Omar said: I do not know of anyone who made a dower similar to hers obligatory from him other than Al-Shafi’i, and his statement is not strong, because she is like a wife and inherits from him and he inherits from her, so how is a dower similar to hers obligatory for intercourse with a woman whose ruling in most of her rulings is the ruling of a wife! However, the doubt in Al-Shafi’i’s statement is strong, because she is forbidden to him except by taking her back, and they have agreed that a woman who has been intercourse with under suspicion is entitled to a dower, and that is enough for you! Sixth: They differed as to whether he may travel with her before returning her. Malik and Al-Shafi’i said: He may not travel with her until he returns her. Abu Hanifa and his companions said the same, except for Zafar, for Al-Hasan bin Ziyad narrated from him that he may travel with her before returning her. Amr bin Khalid narrated from him that he may not travel with her until he returns her. Seventh: They differed as to whether he may enter upon her and see any of her beauty, and whether she adorns herself for him and shows herself. Malik said: He should not be alone with her, and he should not enter upon her except with permission, and he should not look at her unless she is wearing her clothes, and he should not look at her hair, and there is nothing wrong with him eating with her if there are others with them, and he should not spend the night with her in a house and move away from her. Ibn al-Qasim said: Malik went back on that and said: He should not enter upon her or see her hair. Abu Hanifa and his companions did not differ as to whether she adorns herself for him, perfumes herself, wears jewelry, and appears beautiful. On the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, he said: If a man divorces his wife with one divorce, then he should ask permission to enter upon her, and she should wear whatever clothes and clothing she wants. If they only have one house, then they should put a curtain between them, and he should greet her when he enters. Qatadah said something similar, and he should make her feel when he enters by spitting and clearing his throat. Al-Shafi’i said: A woman who is divorced with a divorce that he has the right to take back is forbidden to her divorcer as a divorced woman is forbidden until he takes her back, and he does not take her back except by speaking, as mentioned above. Eighth: The scholars agreed that if the divorcer says after the expiration of the waiting period: I took you back during the waiting period, and she denies it, then her word is valid with her oath, and he has no way to her. However, Al-Nu’man did not see an oath in marriage or in taking her back, and his two companions disagreed with him and said the same as the rest of the scholars. Likewise, if the wife is a slave woman and the master and the slave woman disagree, and the husband claims to have taken her back during the waiting period after the expiration of the waiting period and she denies it, then the word of the slave wife is valid, even if her master denies it. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, and Al-Nu’man. Ya’qub and Muhammad said: The word of the master is valid, and he has more right to her. Ninth: The word return implies the end of the marriage bond, except that our scholars said: The revocable marriage is forbidden to have intercourse, so the return is returned to the place. Al-Layth bin Saad and Abu Hanifa and those who said what they said, that the return permits intercourse, said that the benefit of divorce is reducing the number that was specifically made for it, and that the rulings of marriage remain and nothing of them has been dissolved. They said: And the rulings of marriage, even if they remain, the woman, as long as she is in the waiting period, is on the path to ending with the expiration of the waiting period, so the return is a return from this path that the woman has taken, and this is a metaphorical return, and the return that we ruled with is a real return, because there is an accomplished ending, which is the prohibition of intercourse, so the return from it occurred in reality, and God knows best. Tenth, the word more deserving is used when two rights conflict, and one of them is preferred. The meaning is that the husband’s right during the waiting period is more deserving than her right to herself, as she only owns herself after the waiting period has ended. An example of this is his saying, peace be upon him: The widow has more right to herself than her guardian, and it has been mentioned previously. Eleventh: The man is recommended to review, but if he intends to reform by improving his situation with her and removing the estrangement between them. However, if he intends to harm and prolong the waiting period and cut her off from the bond of marriage, then it is forbidden, because God Almighty says: And do not keep them, to injure them, in order to transgress (al-Baqarah 2:231). Then whoever does that, then the return is valid, even if he committed the prohibition and wronged himself. If we had known that intention, we would have divorced him. The Almighty’s saying: And women have rights similar to those against them according to what is equitable. There are three issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And for them means they have marital rights over men just as men have over them. For this reason, Ibn Abbas said: I adorn myself for my wife just as she adorns herself for me, and I do not like to purify all my rights that I have over her so that she deserves her rights that she has over me, because God Almighty said: And for them are rights similar to those over them according to what is equitable, meaning adornment without sin. And from him also: meaning they have from good companionship and treatment according to what is equitable from their husbands just as they have from obedience in what is obligatory upon them for their husbands. And it was said: They have from their husbands the right to leave them harming them just as it was upon them for their husbands. Al-Tabari said: And Ibn Zayd said: You fear God in them just as it is upon them to fear God Almighty in you, and the meaning is close, and the verse includes all of that from the rights of marriage. The second: The saying of Ibn Abbas: (I adorn myself for my wife) The scholars said: As for men’s adornment, it varies according to their circumstances, as they do that out of politeness and harmony. Perhaps an adornment is appropriate at one time and not at another, and an adornment is appropriate for youth, and an adornment is appropriate for old men and not for young men. Do you not see that if an old man or a middle-aged man trims his moustache, it suits him and beautifies him, but if a young man does that, he looks ugly and hates it? And because the beard has not yet grown, so if he trims his moustache when it first appears, his face looks ugly, and if he grows his beard and trims his moustache, it beautifies him. It was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: My Lord commanded me to let my beard grow and trim my moustache. The same applies to clothing, as in all of this there is seeking rights, so he only works out of politeness and harmony so that he will be with his wife in an adornment that pleases her and keeps her chaste from other men. Likewise, kohl for men, some of them look appropriate for them and some of them do not. As for perfume, siwak, toothpicks, and archery… With tuberculosis, excess hair, purification, and nail clipping, it is between suitable for everyone, and dyeing for the elderly and the ring for all young and elderly is an adornment, and it is the ornament of men as will be explained in Surat An-Nahl. Then he must be careful of the times when she needs men, so that he may keep her chaste and make her independent of looking at anyone other than him. If the man sees in himself an inability to fulfill her right in her bed, he should take medicines that increase his sexual desire and strengthen his desire until he keeps her chaste. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And men have a degree over them, meaning a status. The path’s staircase is its upper part, and its origin is folding. It is said: they lengthened their lifespan, and from it is the degree that one ascends. It is said: a man between the two men, meaning the strongest of the two men, and a horse, meaning strong, from it is the man, for its strength to walk. So the increase in a man’s degree is through his mind and strength, and through spending, and through blood money, and through inheritance, and through jihad. Hamid said: The degree is the beard, and if this is authentic from him, then it is weak and is not required by the wording of the verse or its meaning. Ibn al-Arabi said: So blessed is the servant who refrains from what he does not know, especially in the Book of God Almighty! It is not hidden from the intelligent person that men are superior to women, and if it were only that woman was created from man, he is her origin, and he has the right to prevent her from acting except with his permission, so she does not fast except with his permission and does not perform Hajj except with him. It was said: The degree is the dowry, said by Al-Sha’bi, and it was said that good manners are permissible, and in general, a degree requires preference, and indicates that the husband’s right over her is more obligatory than her right over him, and for this reason “he, peace be upon him, said: If I ordered anyone to prostrate to other than God, I would have ordered the woman to prostrate to her husband.” Ibn Abbas said: The degree is an indication of urging men to treat each other well, and to be generous to women in money and character, meaning that the one who is better should be patient with himself, Ibn Atiyah said: This is a good and brilliant statement. Al-Mawardi said: It is possible that it is in the rights of marriage, he has the right to cancel the contract without her, and she is obligated to answer him to bed, but he is not obligated to answer her. I said: And from this is his saying, peace be upon him: Any woman whose husband calls her to his bed and she refuses, the angels will curse her until morning. “And God is Almighty” meaning His authority is impregnable and there is no objection to Him. Wise meaning He is All-Knowing and Correct in what He does.
2:229: The Almighty’s saying: Divorce is twice, then either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment. There are seven issues in it: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Divorce is twice. It is proven that the people of ignorance did not have a number for divorce, and they had a known and determined waiting period. This was at the beginning of Islam for a while. A man would divorce his wife as many times as he wanted, and if she was about to become permissible from his divorce, he would take her back as much as he wanted. A man said to his wife during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I will not take you in nor will I let you become permissible. She said: How? He said: I will divorce you, and when your waiting period is about to end, I will take you back. The woman complained about that to Aisha, and she mentioned it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty revealed this verse explaining the number of divorces in which a man can take her back without renewing the dowry or guardian, and abrogated what they had been doing. Its meaning was said by Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and others. Ibn Mas`ud, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and others said that what is meant by the verse is to define the Sunnah of divorce, meaning that whoever divorces twice should fear God in the third time, and either leave her without wronging her in any of her rights, or keep her and treat her well. The verse includes these two meanings. The second: Divorce is the dissolution of the bond of marriage established between spouses with specific words, and divorce is permitted by this verse and others, and by the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him, in the hadith of Ibn Umar: If he wishes, he may keep it, and if he wishes, he may divorce it, and “The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, divorced Hafsa and then took her back,” narrated by Ibn Majah. The scholars agreed that whoever divorces his wife while she is pure and in a state of purity in which he did not touch her, he is divorced according to the Sunnah and the waiting period that God Almighty commanded, and that he has the right to take her back if she was consummated with before her waiting period ends, and if it ends, he is a suitor among those who are proposed to. The Book, the Sunnah, and the consensus of the nation indicate that divorce is permitted and not prohibited. Ibn al-Mundhir said: There is no proven report prohibiting it. Third: Al-Daraqutni narrated that Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Ali al-Dulabi and Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told us, they said: Al-Hasan ibn Arfa told us, Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Humayd ibn Malik al-Lakhimi, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: O Muadh, God has not created anything on the face of the earth more beloved to Him than manumission, nor has God created anything on the face of the earth more hateful to Him than divorce. So if a man says to his slave, You are free, God willing, then he is free and there is no exception for him. And if a man says to his wife, You are divorced, God willing, then he has the right to make an exception and there is no divorce upon him. Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Ali told us, Humayd ibn al-Rabi’ told us, Yazid ibn Harun told us, Ismail ibn Ayyash told us with his chain of transmission similarly. Humayd said: Yazid ibn Harun said to me: What hadith would there be if Humayd ibn Malik al-Lakhimi were well-known! I said: He is my grandfather! Yazid said: You have made me happy, now it has become a hadith! Ibn al-Mundhir said: Among those who saw the exception in divorce are Tawus, Hammad, al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, and the people of opinion. The exception in divorce is not permissible according to Malik and al-Awza’i, and it is the opinion of al-Hasan and Qatada in divorce specifically. He said: I say the first opinion. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Then keep her in an acceptable manner, as a beginning, and the predicate is better or better, and it is correct to raise it on the predicate of an omitted beginning, meaning, you must keep her in an acceptable manner or it is your duty to keep what is known to be the truth, and it is permissible in other than the Qur’an (Then keep) as a source, and the meaning of (with kindness) is that he does not wrong her in any of her right, and he does not transgress in a statement, and keeping is the opposite of releasing, and letting go is sending something, and from it is letting the hair down, to free some from others and letting the livestock go: he sent them out, and letting go in its word has two meanings: one of them is leaving her until the waiting period from the second divorce is completed, and she is in control of herself, and this is the saying of al-Suddi and al-Dahhak, and the other meaning is that he divorces her a third time and lets her go, this is the saying of Mujahid and Ata’ and others, and it is more correct for three reasons: One of them: What Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Anas that a man said: O Messenger of God, God Almighty said: Divorce is twice, so why did it become three? He said: Keeping her in good faith or releasing her with kindness. And in another narration: It is the third: Ibn Al-Mundhir mentioned it. Second: The verb to release is one of the words of divorce. Don’t you see that it was read if they decide to release? Third: The verb tafa’ilaan means that it has created a repeated action for the second divorce, and there is no action expressed by tafa’ilaan in leaving it. Abu ‘Umar said: The scholars agreed that the Almighty’s saying: or release with good treatment is the third divorce after the two divorces, and it is what He meant by the Almighty’s saying: But if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband. They agreed that whoever divorces his wife with one or two divorces has the right to take her back. If he divorces her a third time, she is not lawful to him until she marries another husband. This was from the decisive verses of the Qur’an, the interpretation of which was not disputed. Similar things have also been narrated from the reports of just people. Sa’id ibn Nasr told us, Qasim ibn Asbagh told us, Muhammad ibn Wadah told us, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Sami’, on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of the Almighty’s saying: “Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.” So where is the third? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Either keep her in good faith or release her with kindness. Al-Thawri and others narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’ on the authority of Abu Razin, similarly. I said: Al-Kaya al-Tabari mentioned this report and said: It is not proven from the aspect of transmission, and he preferred the statement of al-Dahhak and al-Suddi and that the third divorce is only mentioned in the context of the address in the Almighty’s saying: And if he divorces her, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him (al-Baqarah 2:230). The third is mentioned in the body of this address, indicating the separation that causes prohibition except after a husband, so it is necessary to interpret his saying or release with kindness to mean a renewed meaning, which is the occurrence of separation with two divorces upon the expiration of the waiting period, and that the intended meaning of the verse is to clarify the number of divorces that cause prohibition, and to abrogate what was permissible of pronouncing divorce without a specific number. If his saying: or release with kindness was the third, it would not have clarified the purpose of pronouncing prohibition with three, because if it had been limited to that, it would not have indicated the occurrence of the separation that prohibits her except after a husband. Rather, the prohibition is known by the Almighty’s saying: And if he divorces her, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him (al-Baqarah 2:230). So it is necessary that the meaning of his saying:: Or release her with kindness the third. If his saying, Or release her with kindness had meant the third, his saying would have followed that, If he divorces her the fourth, because the fa is for following, and he required her divorce in the future after what was mentioned above. Thus it is proven that the Almighty’s saying, Or release her with kindness means leaving her until her waiting period ends. Fifth: Al-Bukhari translated this verse as “Chapter: Whoever permits triple divorce with the words of God the Almighty: Divorce is twice, then either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.” This is an indication from him that this multiplicity is only a way out for them, so whoever is restrictive on himself is bound by it. Our scholars said, and the imams of fatwa agreed on the necessity of pronouncing the triple divorce in one word, which is the saying of the majority of the predecessors. Tawus and some of the people of the apparent meaning deviated to the point that the triple divorce in one word is considered one divorce. This is narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq and Al-Hajjaj ibn Artah, and it was said from them that nothing is required from it, which is the saying of Muqatil. It is narrated from Dawud that he said that it is not considered valid. The well-known opinion from Al-Hajjaj ibn Artah and the majority of the predecessors and imams is that it is considered valid and occurs three times, and there is no difference between pronouncing it three times together in one word or separately in words. As for those who went to the point that nothing is required from it, they argued with the evidence of the words of God the Almighty: And divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods (al-Baqarah 2:228), and this includes every divorced woman. Except for what was specified from it, and it was mentioned before, and he said, Divorce is twice, and the third: Then keep her in an acceptable manner or release her with good treatment, and whoever divorces three times in one word is not obligated, since it is not mentioned in the Qur’an, and as for those who went to that it occurred once, they provided evidence with three hadiths: the first is the hadith of Ibn Abbas from the narration of Tawus, Abu al-Sahbaa, and Ikrimah, and the second is the hadith of Ibn Umar according to the narration of the one who narrated that he divorced his wife three times, and that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to take her back and it was counted as one for him, and the third is that Rukanah divorced his wife three times and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to take her back, and taking her back requires the occurrence of one, and the answer to the hadiths is what al-Tahawi mentioned that Saeed bin Jubayr, Mujahid, Ata, Amr bin Dinar, Malik bin al-Huwayrith, Muhammad bin Iyas bin al-Bukair, and al-Nu’man bin Abi Ayyash narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the one who divorced his wife three times that he has disobeyed his Lord and his wife has separated from him and he cannot marry her except After a husband, and in what these imams narrated from Ibn Abbas that agrees with the group, what indicates the weakness of the narration of Tawus and others, and Ibn Abbas would not have disagreed with the companions to his own opinion, Ibn Abd al-Barr said, and the narration of Tawus is a mistake and an error that none of the jurists of the countries of the Hijaz, the Levant, Iraq, the East and the West have paid attention to, and it has been said: Abu al-Sahba is not known among the clients of Ibn Abbas, Judge Abu al-Walid al-Baji said: ((And I believe that the narration from Ibn Tawus is correct, for the imams narrated from him: Muammar, Ibn Jurayj and others, and Ibn Tawus is an imam and the hadith to which they refer is what Ibn Tawus narrated from his father from Ibn Abbas, who said: Divorce during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and any virgin and two years of the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab was one divorce, so Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: The people have hastened in a matter in which they had time, so why don’t we enforce it on them! So he passed it on them, and the meaning of the hadith is that they were issuing one divorce instead of the people issuing three divorces now, and what indicates the correctness of this interpretation is that Omar said: People have rushed in a matter that they had time to think about, so he criticized them for innovating in divorce by rushing in a matter that they had time to think about, so if their situation had been like that at the beginning of Islam in the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would not have said it, nor would he have criticized them for rushing in a matter that they had time to think about, and what indicates the correctness of this interpretation is what was narrated from Ibn Abbas through other chains of transmission that he issued a fatwa that the three divorces are binding on whoever issues them together, so if this is the meaning of the hadith of Ibn Tawus, then it is what we said, and if the hadith of Ibn Abbas is interpreted according to what is not taken into account by those who do not pay attention to his statement, then Ibn Abbas returned to the statement of the group and consensus was reached on it, and our evidence from the perspective of analogy is that this is a divorce issued by someone who owns it, so it must be binding on him, the origin of that is if he issues it individually. I said: What Al-Baji interpreted is what Al-Kaya Al-Tabari mentioned in its meaning from the scholars of Hadith, that is, they used to issue one divorce, this is what they issue three, that is, they did not issue one divorce in each menstrual cycle, but rather they issued one divorce during the entire waiting period until she became clear and the waiting period ended. And Judge Abu Muhammad Abdul Wahhab said, its meaning is that the people used to limit themselves to one divorce, then during the days of Umar they issued three more. The judge said: This is more similar to the narrator’s statement: The people during the days of Umar hastened the three, so he hastened them, meaning he imposed its ruling on them. As for the Hadith of Ibn Umar, Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ahmad Ibn Subayh on the authority of Tarif Ibn Naseh on the authority of Muawiyah Ibn Ammar Al-Dahni on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, who said: I asked Ibn Umar about a man who divorced his wife three times while she was menstruating, so he said to me: Do you know Ibn Umar? I said: Yes. He said: I divorced my wife three times during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while she was menstruating, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned her to the Sunnah. Al-Daraqutni said: They are all Shiites. It is well-known that Ibn Umar divorced his wife once during menstruation. Ubaydullah said: His divorce of her during menstruation was one, but he contradicted the Sunnah. Salih ibn Kaysan, Musa ibn Uqbah, Ismail ibn Umayyah, Laith ibn Sa`d, Ibn Abi Dhi`b, Ibn Jurayj, Jabir, and Ismail ibn Ibrahim ibn Uqbah said the same on the authority of Nafi`: that Ibn Umar divorced her once. Al-Zuhri said the same on the authority of Salim on the authority of his father, Yunus ibn Jubayr, Al-Sha`bi, and Al-Hasan. As for the hadith of Rukanah, it was said: It is a confused and disconnected hadith, and it cannot be relied upon from any source that can be used as evidence. Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of some of the sons of Abi Rafi`, and there is no one among them who can use it as evidence, on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and he said in it: “Rukana ibn Abd Yazid divorced his wife three times, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: And he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Take her back.” It was also narrated through various chains of transmission on the authority of Nafi’ ibn Ujayr that Rukanah ibn Abd Yazid divorced his wife irrevocably, so the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, made him swear: What did he mean by her? So he swore that he only meant one thing, so he returned her to him. This is a confusion in the name and the action, and nothing like this can be used as evidence. I said: This hadith was narrated by Al-Daraqutni in his Sunan. He said in some of them: “Muhammad bin Yahya bin Mirdas narrated to us, Abu Dawud Al-Sijistani narrated to us, Ahmad bin Amr bin Al-Sarh and Abu Thawr Ibrahim bin Khalid Al-Kalbi and others said: Muhammad bin Idris Al-Shafi’i narrated to us, my uncle Muhammad bin Ali bin Shafi’ narrated to me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ali bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Nafi’ bin Ujair bin Abd Yazid: “That Rukanah bin Abd Yazid divorced his wife Suhaymah Al-Muzaniyyah irrevocably, so he informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, and he said: By God, I only intended one divorce. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, I only intended one divorce? Rukanah said: By God, I only intended one divorce. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned her to him, and he divorced her a second time during the time of Umar bin Al-Khattab, and a third time during the time of Uthman.” Abu Dawud said: This is a sahih hadith. What is sahih from Rukanah’s hadith is that he divorced his wife irrevocably, not three times. There is disagreement about irrevocable divorce, as will be explained, so the argument is invalidated, praise be to God, and God knows best.” Abu Omar said: Al-Shafi’i’s narration of Rukanah’s hadith on the authority of his uncle is more complete, and he added an addition that is not refuted by the original sources, so it must be accepted because its transmitters are trustworthy. Al-Shafi’i, his uncle, and his grandfather are the people of Rukanah’s household, all of them from Banu Abd al-Muttalib ibn Abd Manaf, and they are more knowledgeable about the story as it was presented to them. Chapter: Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Mughith al-Tulaitili mentioned this issue in his documents and said: Divorce is divided into two types: Sunnah divorce and heretical divorce. Sunnah divorce is that which occurs in the manner that the Shari’ah has recommended, and heretical divorce is its opposite, which is that he divorces her during menstruation or postpartum bleeding or three times in one word. If he does so, then the divorce is binding on him. Then the scholars differed after their consensus that it is absolute, about how many divorces are binding on him. Ali bin Abi Talib and Ibn Mas’ud said: He is bound by one divorce. Ibn Abbas said the same, and he said: His saying three times has no meaning because he did not divorce three times. Rather, his saying three times is permissible if he is informing about what has passed, so he says: I divorced three times, so he is informing about three actions that were done by him at three times, like a man who said: Yesterday I read such-and-such Surah three times, then that is valid. If he read it once and said: I read it three times, then he is lying. Likewise, if he swears by God three times and repeats the oath, then it is three oaths. But if he swears and says: I swear by God three times, then it is only one oath, and the divorce is the same. Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awam and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said this, and we narrated all of this from Ibn Wadah, and Ibn Zinba’, the Sheikh of guidance of Muhammad ibn Taqi ibn Mukhallad, Muhammad ibn Abd al-Salam al-Hasani, the unique jurist of his time, Asbagh ibn al-Habbab, Jama’ and others said the same. And Ibn Abbas’s proof was that God Almighty differentiated the word divorce in His Book, so He, the Most High, said: Divorce is twice, meaning the most common divorce after which is keeping her in a good manner, which is taking her back during the waiting period. And the meaning of His saying: or releasing her with kindness, means leaving her without taking her back until her waiting period ends, and in that is kindness to her if regret occurs between them. God Almighty said: You do not know; perhaps God will bring about after that something new (al-Talaq: 1), meaning regret over the separation and the desire to take her back. And the position of the three is not good because it leaves the way out that God has made it easy and pointed out, so God Almighty mentioned divorce in separate forms, indicating that if it is combined, it is one word, and it may be derived by analogy from other issues in the Mudawwana that indicate this. From that, a person says, I have no charity for the poor, that a third of that is sufficient for him. And in Al-Ishraf by Ibn Al-Mundhir: And Saeed bin Jubair, Tawus, Abu Al-Shatha’, Ata’, and Amr bin Dinar used to say: Whoever divorces a virgin three times, it is only one. I said: And perhaps they argued and said: There is no waiting period for a woman who has not been consummated with, so if he says: You are divorced three times, she is separated by the very fact that he finished saying: You are divorced, so he returns three times to her and she is irrevocable, so it does not affect anything, and because his saying: You are divorced is independent in itself, so it is necessary that the separation in a woman who has not been consummated with does not depend on what comes after it: its origin is if he says: You are divorced. Sixth: Al-Shafi’i used as evidence the words of God Almighty: Or release them with kindness and His words: And set them free (al-Ahzab 33:49), that this word is an explicit form of divorce. Scholars have differed on this meaning. Judge Abu Muhammad held that the explicit form is that which includes the word divorce in any way, such as saying: You are divorced, or you are divorced, or I have divorced you, or divorce is binding. Any other word of divorce that is used in it is a metaphor. Abu Hanifa said this. Judge Abu al-Hasan said: The explicit words of divorce are many, and some of them are clearer than others: divorce, release, separation, forbidden, free, and free. Al-Shafi’i said: The explicit form is three words, which are what the Qur’an mentions of the words divorce, release, and separation. God Almighty said: Or separate them on good terms (al-Talaq 65:2), Or set them free with kindness, and He said: So divorce them during their waiting period (al-Talaq 65:1). I said: If this is established, then divorce is of two types: explicit and implicit. The explicit is what we mentioned, and the implicit is what is other than it. The difference between them is that the explicit does not require intention, rather divorce occurs with the mere utterance, while the implicit requires intention. The argument for those who said that the haram, the khaliyyah, and the bariyyah are explicit divorces is their frequent use in divorce until they became known by it, and they became clear evidence in the occurrence of al-Talaq 65:like the excrement that was placed on the ground for the one who is at peace, then it was used metaphorically to come to the relief of need, so it was clearer, more apparent, and more famous in it than in what it was placed for. And likewise in our question, it is similar. Then, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said: If divorce were a thousand, nothing of it would remain at all. So whoever said: absolutely, has thrown away the ultimate goal. Malik narrated it. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ali, who said: The khaliyyah, the bariyyah, the irrevocable, the irrevocable, and the haram are three. She is not permissible for him until she marries another husband. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the irrevocable is three, through a path that is weak. Al-Daraqutni narrated it, and it will come when he says: God Almighty says: And do not take the verses of God in jest (al-Baqarah 2:231), God Almighty willing. Seventh: The scholars did not differ regarding the one who said to his wife, I have divorced you, that it is an explicit divorce for the one who has been consummated with and the one who has not been consummated with. So whoever said to his wife, You are divorced, it is one divorce unless he intended more than that. If he intended two or three, then what he intended is binding on him. If he did not intend anything, it is one divorce and she has the right to take him back. If he said, You are divorced, and said, I intended from the bond, his statement is not accepted and binding on him, unless there is something that indicates his truthfulness.
