And whoever said, You are divorced once, I have no right to take you back, it is invalid, and he has the right to take her back because he said one divorce, because one divorce cannot be three. If he intended by his statement, I have no right to take you back, three, then it is three according to Malik. They differed about the one who said to his wife, I have set you free, or You are free, or I am free, or I have divorced you, or You are forbidden to me, or Go back to your family, or I have given you to your family, or I have set you free, or I have no right over you. Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf said: It is an irrevocable divorce. It was narrated from Ibn Mas’ud who said: If a man says to his wife, Do what you want, or Your matter is yours, or Go back to your family, and they accept it, then it is one irrevocable divorce. It was narrated from Malik about the one who said to his wife, I have separated from you, or I have set you free, that it is an explicit divorce, like his saying, You are divorced. It was narrated from him that it is a metaphor in which it is referred to the intention of the one who said it, and he is asked what he intended of the number, whether she was entered into or not. Ibn al-Mawaz said: The most correct of his two opinions about the one with whom he did not enter is that it is one, unless he intended more. Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn Abd al-Hakam said the same. Abu Yusuf said: It is three, and the same applies to You have divorced, or No. And as for the rest of the euphemisms, they are three according to Malik in every woman who has been entered into without intending it, and intending it in the case of someone who has not been entered into, so if he swears and says I intended one, he is a suitor among the suitors, because he does not release the woman with whom her husband has entered, nor separate her, nor acquit her except with three divorces, and the one with whom he has not entered, he releases her, acquits her, and acquits her with one, and it has been narrated from Malik and a group of his companions, and it is the saying of a group of the people of Medina, that he intends in all of these words and it is binding on him in them, neither in the case of the woman who has been entered into nor in the case of the woman who has not been entered into, and Al-Thawri and Abu Hanifa and his companions said, he has his intention in all of that, so if he intended three, then they are three, and if he intended one, then it is one irrevocable divorce and it is more entitled to itself, and if he intended two, then it is one, and Zafar said: If he intended two, then it is two, and Al-Shafi’i said: In all of that, he is not absolute until he says: I intended by the way the words came from me a divorce, then what he intended will happen, and if he intended less than three, then it is revocable, and if he divorced her once irrevocably, then it is revocable, and he said: Isaac, every word that resembles divorce is what he intended of divorce, and Abu Thawr said: It is a revocable divorce and he is not asked about his intention, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he did not see a final divorce except in the case of Khul’ or Ila’, and this is what was preserved from him, said Abu Ubaid, and Al-Bukhari translated ((Chapter: If he said I separated from you or I set you free or the wilderness or the seclusion or what he meant by divorce, then it is according to his intention)). This is an indication from him of the statement of the Kufians, Al-Shafi’i and Ishaq in his statement: (or what he meant by divorce) and the evidence for that is that every word that may be a divorce or not divorce, it is not permissible to make divorce binding unless the speaker says: he intended divorce by it, then that binds him by his admission, and it is not permissible to invalidate the marriage because they have agreed on its validity with certainty. Abu Omar said: Malik’s statement differed regarding the meaning of a man saying to his wife: I have transgressed, or I have left you, or your rope is on your neck. He said once, he does not intend it and it is three, and he said once: he intends it all, and in the one who has been penetrated and the one who has not been penetrated, and I say the same. I said: What the majority have said, and what has been narrated from Malik that he intends in these words and rules on you accordingly is correct, due to the evidence we have mentioned, and the authentic hadith that Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, al-Darqutni and others narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Rukanah: “Rukanah ibn Abd Yazid divorced his wife Suhaymah irrevocably, so he informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, and he said: By God, I only intended one? Rukanah said: By God, I only intended one, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned her to him.” Ibn Majah said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Tanafisi say: How noble this hadith is! Malik said about a man who says to his wife: You are to me like a dead animal, blood, or pork, I see it absolutely, even if he had no intention, so she is not permissible except after a husband. And in the saying of al-Shafi’i: If he intended divorce, then it is a divorce, and whatever number of divorces he intended, and if he did not intend divorce, then it is nothing after he swears an oath. Abu ‘Umar said: The basis of this chapter in every euphemism for divorce is what was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: To the one he married when she said: I seek refuge in God from you, I have sought refuge in Mu’adh, go back to your family, so that was a divorce. And Ka’b ibn Malik said to his wife when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to leave her, go back to your family, so that was not a divorce. So it indicates that this word is in need of intention, and that it is not decided in it except according to what the utterer intended with it, and likewise with all the euphemisms that may indicate separation and other things, and God knows best. As for the words that are not words of divorce and are not used as euphemisms for separation, most scholars do not consider any of them to be divorce. And if the speaker intended it, Malik said: Whoever intended divorce by any word, the divorce is binding on him, even by saying: Eat, drink, stand up, and sit down. And no one followed Malik in that except his companions. It contains fifteen issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And it is not lawful for you to take back anything of what you have given them (that) is in the nominative case with (permissible) and the verse is addressed to the husbands, forbidding them to take anything from their wives in a way that causes harm, and this is the divorce which is not valid unless the man is not the only one who causes harm, and what the husbands gave to their wives was specifically mentioned, because it is customary among people for the man to demand in the event of discord and corruption what came out of his hand for her as a dowry and trousseau, so that is why it was specifically mentioned, and it has been said: His saying and it is not lawful is an interrupting separation between the Almighty’s saying: Divorce is twice and His saying: But if he divorces her (al-Baqarah 2:230). Second: The majority of scholars agree that taking ransom for divorce is permissible, and they agreed on prohibiting taking what she owes him unless the rebellion is on his part and she divorces him, in which case it is permissible and valid and he is a sinner, what he did is not permissible for him, and he is not forced to return what he took. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This of his saying is contrary to the apparent meaning of the Book of God, and contrary to the established report from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and contrary to what the majority of scholars have agreed upon regarding that. I do not think that if it were said to someone: Exert yourself in seeking the error, he would not find anything greater than that the Book speaks of the prohibition of something and then confronts it with the contradiction explicitly, and says: Rather, it is permissible, and he is not forced to return what he took. Abu al-Hasan ibn Battaal said: Ibn al-Qasim narrated something similar from Malik, and this statement is contrary to the apparent meaning of the Book of God Almighty, and contrary to the hadith of the woman Thabit, which will come. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Except if they both fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God. God Almighty forbade in this verse that one should not take except after fearing that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, and He emphasized the prohibition with a threat to whoever transgresses the limit. The meaning is that each of them thinks of himself that he will not be able to keep within the rights of marriage for his partner as is required of him due to the dislike he believes in. So there is no blame on the woman to ransom herself, and there is no blame on the husband to take. The address is to the spouses, and the pronoun in that they fear refers to them, and that they will not be able to keep within is the direct object, and feared is transitive to a single direct object. Then it was said: This fear is in the sense of knowledge, that is, that they know that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, and it is from true fear, which is fear of the occurrence of something disliked, and it is close to the meaning of suspicion. Then it was said: Except if they fear is an interrupted exception, that is, but if there is disobedience on their part, then there is no blame upon you in taking the ransom. Hamza read except if they fear, with a damma on the ya’ for what the agent is not named. The subject is omitted, which is the governors and rulers, and Abu Ubaid chose it. He said: Because God Almighty said: If you fear. He said: So fear was made for someone other than the spouses. If he had meant the spouses, he would have said: If they fear. In this is an argument for those who make the divorce up to the ruler. I said: This is the saying of Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Hasan, and Ibn Sirin. Shu’bah said: I said to Qatada: From whom did Al-Hasan take the cloak to the Sultan? He said: On the authority of Ziyad, who was a governor for Umar and Ali. Al-Nahhas said: This is well-known from Ziyad, and this statement has no meaning, because if a man divorces his wife, it is only on what they agree upon, and the ruler does not force him to do so. There is no meaning to the statement of the one who said: This is up to the ruler. Abu Ubaid’s choice was denied and rejected, and I do not know of anything in his choice that is further from this letter, because it is not required by grammar, nor by wording, nor by meaning. As for grammar, Abdullah bin Masoud read (except that they fear) (you fear), so this in Arabic, if it is referred to what its doer is not named, it is said: except that he fears. As for the wording, if it is on the wording (they fear), it is obligatory to say: if it is feared, and if it is on the wording (if you fear), it is obligatory to say: except that you fear. As for the meaning, it is far-fetched to say: it is not permissible for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless someone else fears, and God Almighty did not say: there is no blame upon you if you take a ransom from her for him, so the divorce is up to Sultan. Al-Tahawi said: It has been authenticated from Omar, Othman, and Ibn Omar that it is permissible without the Sultan. Just as divorce and marriage are permissible without the Sultan, so is khul’, and this is the opinion of the majority of scholars. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: But if you fear that they will not be able to observe meaning that they will not be able to observe the limits of God meaning in what is required of them of good companionship and good treatment, and the address is to the rulers and those who mediate for such a matter even if he is not a ruler, and not observing the limits of God is the woman’s disdain for her husband’s right, and her disobedience to him. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Malik bin Anas and the majority of the jurists. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan and some with him said, if the woman says, I will not obey you in any matter, nor will I wash myself for you from major ritual impurity, nor will I fulfill my oath to you, then khul’ is permissible. Al-Sha’bi said, They will not observe the limits of God means they will not obey God, because anger leads to abandoning obedience. Ata bin Abi Rabah said, khul’ and taking are permissible if the woman says to her husband, I hate you and I do not love you and the like. There is no blame upon them for what she ransomes herself with. Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Ayoub on the authority of Ikrimah, “On the authority of Ibn Abbas that the wife of Thabit bin Qays came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, Thabit bin Qays, what is wrong with me?” He has good character and religion, but I cannot stand him! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Will you return his garden to me? She said: Yes. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Jamlah bint Salul came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: By God, I do not find fault with Thabit in his religion or character, but I hate disbelief in Islam and cannot stand it out of hatred! The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Will you return his garden to him? She said: Yes. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to take his garden from her and not to take more. It is said that she hated him intensely, and he loved her intensely. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, separated them by way of khul` divorce, and it was khul` in Islam. Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The first person to take khul` in Islam was the sister of Abdullah ibn Ubayy. She came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, my head and his head will never meet. I lifted the side of the tent and saw him approaching with a group of people. He was the blackest of them all, the shortest of them all, and the ugliest of them all! He said: Will you return his garden to him? She said: Yes, and if he wishes, he may increase it, so separate them.” This hadith is the basis for khul‘, and the majority of jurists agree on it. Malik said: I have not ceased to hear that from the people of knowledge, and it is the matter agreed upon among us, which is that if the man has not harmed the woman or mistreated her, and she has not been harmed by him, and she wants to leave him, then it is permissible for him to take from her everything with which she ransomed herself, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did with the wife of Thabit Qays. And if the rebellion is on his part, such as making things difficult for her and harming her, he returns to her what he took from her. Uqbah ibn Abi al-Sahba’ said: I asked Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani about a man whose wife wants to divorce him, and he said: It is not permissible for him to take anything from him. I said: Where is the statement of God Almighty in His Book: But if you fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits of God, then there is no blame upon them for that by which she ransomes herself? He said: It was abrogated. I said: Where was it made? He said: In Surah An-Nisa’: “And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount [of wealth], do not take from it anything. Would you take it by falsehood and manifest sin?” (An-Nisa’: 20) An-Nahhas said, This is an odd statement, outside of consensus due to its oddity, and neither verse negates the other, so abrogation occurs, because his statement, If you fear, is not removed by that verse, because if they feared this, the husband would not be included in And if you wish to replace one wife with another, because this is specifically for men. At-Tabari said, The verse is decisive, and there is no meaning to Bakr’s statement, If she wanted the gift, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, permitted Thabit to take from his wife what he gave her, as mentioned above. Fifth: This verse was held by those who saw that khul‘ is specific to the case of discord and harm, and that it is a condition for khul‘. This was supported by what Abu Dawud narrated: “On the authority of Aisha: Habeeba bint Sahl was with Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas, and he beat her and broke her breast. She came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the morning prayer and complained to him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Thabit and said: Take some of her wealth and leave her. He said: Is that permissible, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: I gave her two gardens as a dowry, and they are in her hand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Take them and leave her. So he took them and left her.” The majority of jurists are of the view that khul‘ is permissible without complaining of harm, as indicated by the hadith of al-Bukhari and others. As for the verse, there is no proof in it, because God, the Almighty, did not mention it as a condition, but rather mentioned it because it is the most common case of khul‘, so the statement was based on the most common, and what cuts off the excuse and requires knowledge is the statement of God, the Almighty: But if they give up willingly to you anything of it, then take it. Blessed and happy (al-Nisa 4:4).
2:230: The Almighty’s saying: But if he divorces her, she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband. There are eleven issues in this: First: Some of the Hanafi sheikhs of Khorasan used this verse as evidence that divorce is applicable to a woman who has been divorced by khul‘. They said: God Almighty has explicitly prescribed divorce after redemption by divorce, because the letter fa’ is a subsequent letter, so it is unlikely that it should be referred to His statement: Divorce is twice, because what has been interposed in the speech prevents the construction of His statement: If he divorces her on His statement: Divorce is twice. Rather, it is closer to refer to what follows it, as in the exception, and it does not refer to what precedes it except by indication, just as God Almighty said: And your stepdaughters who are in your guardianship from your women to whom you have consummated the marriage (An-Nisa’: 23), so it became limited to what follows it and does not refer to what precedes it, so that consummation is not required of the mothers of women. The scholars differed after the divorce in the waiting period. A group said: If a man divorces his wife and then divorces her while she is in the waiting period, the divorce is valid for her as long as she is in the waiting period. This is what Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Shuraih, Tawus, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Zuhri, Al-Hakam, Hammad, Al-Thawri and the people of opinion said. There is a second opinion, which is that the divorce is not binding on her. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Al-Zubayr, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Jabir bin Zaid, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and Abu Thawr. This is the opinion of Malik, except that Malik said: If she redeems herself from him on the condition that he divorces her three times in succession in sequence when he divorced her, then this is valid for him. If there were silences between that, then what followed after the silences is nothing. This is because the sequence of the words, one after the other, is continuous and requires a single ruling for it. Likewise, if the exception is connected to the oath by God, it has an effect and the ruling of the exception is valid for it. If it is separated from it, it has no connection to what preceded from the words. Second: What is meant by the Almighty’s saying: If he divorces her the third divorce, then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries another husband. This is agreed upon and there is no disagreement about it. They differed about what is sufficient for marriage, and what makes it permissible to make it permissible for it to be permissible. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and those who agreed with him said that merely contracting the marriage contract is sufficient. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan said: Mere intercourse is not sufficient until there is ejaculation. The majority and all of the jurists went to the view that intercourse is sufficient in that, and it is the meeting of the two circumcised parts that requires the punishment and ritual washing, and invalidates the fast and the Hajj, and protects the spouses with the completion of the dowry. Ibn Al-Arabi said: I did not come across a more difficult issue in jurisprudence than this, and that is that one of the principles of jurisprudence is whether the ruling is related to the first or last names? If we say that the ruling is related to the first names, then we must say Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, and if we say that the ruling is related to the last names, then we must stipulate ejaculation with the disappearance of the glans in order for it to be permissible, because it is the last taste of the honey according to what al-Hasan said. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The meaning of the taste of the honey is intercourse, and this is the opinion of a group of scholars, Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: As for the people, they say: She is not permissible for the first until the second has intercourse with her. And I say: If he marries her in a valid marriage, not intending thereby to make her permissible, then there is no problem with the first marrying her. And this is a statement that we do not know of anyone who agreed with him on it except a group of the Khawarij, and the Sunnah is sufficient in everything else. I said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said the same as Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Nahhas mentioned him in his book, The Meanings of the Qur’an. He said: The people of knowledge agree that marriage here means sexual intercourse, because he said: A husband other than him. The marriage has come before, so the marriage became sexual intercourse, except for Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Marriage here means a valid marriage if he does not intend to make her permissible. I said: I think that the hadith of the honey did not reach them or it was not authentic in their view, so they took the apparent meaning of the Qur’an, which is the Almighty’s saying: Until she marries another husband. And God knows best. The imams narrated, and the wording is from al-Darqutni, on the authority of Aisha, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a man divorces his wife three times, she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband and each of them tastes the honey of the other.” Some Hanafi scholars said: Whoever contracts according to the school of thought of Saeed bin al-Musayyab, the judge has the right to annul it, and his disagreement is not considered in it because it is outside the consensus of the scholars. Our scholars said: What is understood from his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Until each of them tastes the honey of the other, is that they are equal in realizing the pleasure of intercourse, and it is evidence for one of the two opinions in our view that if he had intercourse with her while she was asleep or unconscious, she is not permissible for her divorcer, because she did not taste the honey if she did not realize it. Third: Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abdullah who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who tattoos and the one who gets tattooed, the one who extends hair and the one who gets it extended, the one who consumes usury and the one who pays it, the one who permits it and the one for whom it is permitted.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who permits it and the one for whom it is permitted.” He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. This hadith has been narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, through more than one chain of transmission, and the scholars of knowledge from the Companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, acted upon this, including ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar and others. It is the opinion of the jurists from the Tabi’in, and Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Shafi’i, Malik, Ahmad and Ishaq said this. I heard al-Jarud mentioning that Wakee’ said this, and he said: This should be thrown out of the category of the people of opinion. Sufyan said: If a man marries a woman to permit her, then he decides to keep her, she is not permissible for him until he marries her in a new marriage. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: The scholars differed regarding the marriage of a muhallil. Malik said: The muhallil does not remain in his marriage until he enters into a new marriage. If he has intercourse with her, she is entitled to a dower like hers, and his intercourse with her does not make her permissible for her first husband. Whether they knew or not, if he married her to make her permissible, he does not remain in his marriage and it is annulled. Al-Thawri and Al-Awza’i said the same. There is a second opinion narrated from Al-Thawri regarding the marriage of a muhallil and a muhallil, that the marriage is permissible and the condition is invalid. This is the opinion of Ibn Abi Layla regarding that and regarding the marriage of pleasure. It was narrated from Al-Awza’i regarding the marriage of a muhallil: What he did is bad, and the marriage is permissible. Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad said: The marriage is permissible if he has intercourse with her, and he has the right to keep her if he wishes. Abu Hanifa and his companions said once: She is not permissible for the first if he married her to make her permissible. And once they said: She is permissible for him by this marriage if he has intercourse with her and divorces her. They did not differ regarding the fact that the marriage of this husband is valid, and that he has the right to remain. And there is a third opinion in it. Al-Shafi’i said: If he says, I will marry you to make you permissible, and then there will be no marriage between us after that, then this is a type of temporary marriage, and it is invalid and should not be confirmed and should be annulled. If he has intercourse with her on this basis, it is not a tahlil marriage. If he marries her in an absolute marriage, without stipulating or stipulating tahlil upon her, then Al-Shafi’i has two opinions on this in his old book: one of them is like the opinion of Malik, and the other is like the opinion of Abu Hanifa. His opinion in his new Egyptian book does not differ, that the marriage is valid if he does not stipulate it, and this is the opinion of Dawud. I said: Al-Mawardi narrated on the authority of Al-Shafi’i that if he stipulated the tahlil before the contract, the marriage is valid and makes her permissible for the first wife, and if he stipulated it in the contract, the marriage is void and does not make her permissible for the first wife. He said: This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i. Al-Hasan and Ibrahim said: If one of the three intends tahlil, the marriage is invalid, and this is a strict ruling. Salim and Al-Qasim said: There is nothing wrong with him marrying her to make her permissible if the two spouses do not know, and he will be rewarded. Rabia bin Saeed said the same, and Dawud bin Ali said it if his stipulation did not appear at the time of the contract. Fourth: The basis of the permissibility of tahlil according to our scholars is the husband who has intercourse, whether he stipulated that or intended it. Whenever any of that occurs, his marriage is invalid and is not approved of, and his intercourse with the woman is not permissible for her husband. The knowledge of the divorced husband or his ignorance of that is the same. It has been said that if he knows that the husband has intercourse with her for that reason, he should refrain from taking her back, and according to Malik, he should not make her permissible except through a marriage of desire due to his need for her, and he does not intend tahlil by it, and his intercourse with her is permissible intercourse, she is not fasting or in a state of ihram or during her menstruation, and the husband is an adult Muslim. Al-Shafi’i said: If he has intercourse with her through a valid marriage and inserts the glans into her vagina, then he has tasted the honey, and it is the same in that, whether the intercourse is strong or weak, and whether he inserted it with his hand or hers, and it was from a boy or an adolescent or a castrated person, he has what remains to insert it as it is inserted from a non-castrated person, and whether the husband has intercourse with her while she is in a state of ihram or fasting. All of this is according to what Al-Shafi’i described, the saying of Abu Hanifa and his companions, Al-Thawri, Al-Awza’i, Al-Hasan ibn Saleh and his saying some of Malik’s companions. Fifth: Ibn Habib said: If he marries her, and if he likes her, he should keep her. Otherwise, he would have considered it a reward to make her permissible, and it is not permissible, because his marriage was mixed with the intention of making her permissible, and she is not permissible for the first one because of that. Sixth: The master’s intercourse with his female slave whose husband has already divorced her is not permissible, because he is not a husband. It was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, and it is the opinion of Ubaydah, Masruq, Al-Sha’bi, Ibrahim, Jabir ibn Zayd, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and Abu Al-Zinad, and a group of the jurists of the regions agree with this. It was narrated from Uthman, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Al-Zubayr that he is different from that, and that he makes her permissible if her master has intercourse with her, not intending by that to deceive or make her permissible, and she returns to her husband with a proposal and a dowry. The first opinion is more correct, because God Almighty says: Until she marries a husband other than him. The master only has power through right hand possession, and this is clear. Seventh: In Muwatta’ Malik, it was reported to him that Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Sulayman bin Yasar were asked about a man who married a female slave to his slave girl, and the slave divorced her irrevocably, then her master gave her to him as a gift. Is she permissible for him by right of possession? They said: She is not permissible for him until she marries another husband. Eighth: It was narrated on the authority of Malik that he asked Ibn Shihab about a man who had a slave girl under him and he bought her after he had divorced her once. He said: She is permissible to him by right of possession as long as he has not decided to divorce her. If he decides to divorce her, then she is not permissible to him by right of possession until she marries another husband. Abu Omar said: And this is the view of the group of scholars and imams of fatwa, Malik, al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr. Ibn Abbas, Ata’, Tawus, and al-Hasan used to say: If the one who decided to divorce her bought her, then she is permissible to him by right of possession, based on the generality of the words of God Almighty: Or what your right hands possess (al-Nisa’: 3). Abu Omar said: This is a mistake in the statement, because the words of God Almighty: Or what your right hands possess do not permit mothers or sisters, and so do all other forbidden women. Ninth: If a Muslim divorces his non-Muslim wife three times, and a non-Muslim marries her and consummates the marriage with her, then divorces her, then a group says: The non-Muslim is her husband, and she has the right to return to the first one. This is what Al-Hasan, Al-Zuhri, Sufyan Al-Thawri, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Ubaid, and the people of opinion said. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: We also say this, because God Almighty said: Until she marries another husband, and the Christian is a husband. Malik and Rabi’ah said: He does not make her permissible. Tenth: A corrupt marriage does not make permissible a woman who has been divorced three times, according to the majority of scholars, Malik, al-Thawri, al-Shafi’i, al-Awza’i, the people of opinion, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Ubaid. They all say: She is not permissible for the first husband except through a valid marriage. The judge used to say: He is a husband. Ibn al-Mundhir said: He is not a husband, because the rulings of husbands regarding zihar, ila’, and li’an are not established between them. All of the scholars who have been preserved from him agree that if a woman says to the first husband: I have married and my husband has consummated the marriage with me and he believes her, then she is permissible for the first. Al-Shafi’i said: It is pious not to do that if it occurs to him that she has lied to him. Eleventh: It was reported from Omar bin Al-Khattab in this regard that he was severely strict, and he said: If a man who is being permissible for a woman to marry is brought to me, I will stone them both. Ibn Omar said: Permissibility is fornication, and they will remain adulterers even if they remain for twenty years. Abu Omar said: Omar’s statement does not bear anything but strictness, because it was authentically reported from him that he set the punishment for the one who had unlawful intercourse with a vagina, while he was ignorant of its prohibition and excused himself by ignorance, so the interpretation is more appropriate for that, and there is no disagreement that he should not be stoned. God Almighty says: “But if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them if they return to each other if they think they can keep within the limits of God. And these are the limits of God which He makes clear to a people who know.” There are four issues in it: The first: The Almighty’s saying: But if he divorces her meaning the second husband: there is no blame upon them meaning the woman and the first husband, as Ibn Abbas said, and there is no disagreement about it. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The people of knowledge agreed that if a free man divorces his wife three times, then her waiting period ends and she marries another husband and he consummates the marriage with her, then he divorces her, and her waiting period ends and she marries her first husband, she is considered to be with him on three divorces. They differed concerning a man who divorces his wife once or twice, then she marries another man and then returns to her first husband. A group said: She is subject to what remains of her divorce. This is what the great companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Imran ibn Husayn, and Abu Hurayrah. It is narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit, Mu’adh ibn Jabal, and Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-’As. This is what Ubaydah al-Salmani, Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Hasan al-Basri, Malik, Sufyan al-Thawri, Ibn Abi Layla, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Ubaydah, Abu Thawr, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ibn Nasr said. There is a second opinion, which is that the marriage is new and the divorce is new. This is the opinion of Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas. This is what Ata’, al-Nakha’i, Shuraih, al-Nu’man, and Ya’qub said. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah said: Abu Mu’awiyah and Waki’ told us on the authority of al-A’mash on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: The companions of Abdullah used to say: Does a husband destroy three divorces, but not one? And the two! He said: Hafs told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Talha, on the authority of Ibrahim, that the companions of Abdullah used to say: One husband destroys the two as he destroys the three, except for Ubaidah, who said: She is subject to what remains of her divorce. Abu Omar mentioned it. Ibn al-Mundhir said: I say the first opinion. And there is a third opinion, which is: If the latter had intercourse with her, then it is a new divorce and a new marriage, and if he had not intercourse with her, then it is subject to what remains. This is the opinion of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i. Second: The Almighty’s saying: If they think that they can maintain the limits of God is a condition. Tawus said: If they think that each of them will treat his partner well. It was said: The limits of God are His obligations, meaning if they know that there will be reconciliation between them through a second marriage, then whenever the husband knows that he is unable to provide for his wife or her dowry or any of her rights that are obligatory upon him, it is not permissible for him to marry her until he makes it clear to her, or knows from himself that he is able to fulfill her rights. Likewise, if he has an ailment that prevents him from enjoying himself, he must make it clear, so that he does not deceive the woman about himself. Likewise, it is not permissible for him to deceive her with a lineage that he claims, nor with money or a trade that he mentions while lying about it. Likewise, if the woman knows from herself that she is unable to fulfill the rights of the husband, or if she has an ailment that prevents enjoyment, such as madness, leprosy, vitiligo, or a disease in the vagina, it is not permissible for her to deceive him and she must explain to him what is in her of that, just as the seller of the goods must explain the defects in his goods, and whenever one of the spouses finds a defect in his partner, he has the right to return it. If the defect is If the man has consummated the marriage with her, then she is entitled to the dowry, and if he has not consummated the marriage, then she is entitled to half of it. If the defect is with the woman, then the husband should return her and take what he had given her as dowry. It has been narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, married a woman from Banu Ghafar, and he found leprosy on her side, so he returned her and said: You have deceived me. There are different narrations from Malik regarding the impotent woman who surrenders herself and then they are separated due to impotence. He said once: She gets the entire dowry, and he said once: She gets half the dowry. This is based on the difference in his statement: What does she get the dowry for, surrender or consummation? There are two opinions. Third: Ibn Khuwaizmandad said, and our companions differed as to whether the wife is required to provide service or not? Some of our companions said: The wife is not required to provide service. This is because the contract deals with enjoyment, not service. Do you not see that it is not a contract of hire or ownership of a slave, but rather a contract for enjoyment, and what is due in the contract is enjoyment and nothing else, so do not demand more than that. Do you not see the words of God the Most High: But if they obey you, seek no way against them (An-Nisa’: 34). Some of our companions said: She is required to serve her peers. If she is of noble status due to the ease of parenthood or luxury, then she is required to manage the house and take care of the servant. If she is of average means, then she is required to furnish and so on. If she is below that, then she is required to clean the house, cook and wash. If she is from the women of the Kurds, Daylamites and the mountain women in their country, she is required to do what their women are required to do. This is because God the Most High said: And they women have rights similar to those of men over them, according to what is equitable. The custom of the Muslims in their countries, in ancient and modern times, has been as we have mentioned. Do you not see that the wives of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and his companions used to take care of the flour, baking, cooking, spreading the bedding, bringing food and the like, and we do not know of a woman who refused to do that, and it is not permissible for her to refuse, rather they used to beat her? Their women, if they are negligent in that, and they take them to service, if she were not deserving of it, they would not have demanded that of them. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And these are the limits set by God which He makes clear for a people who know. The limits of God are what He has forbidden. A limit is a deterrent from committing immoral acts. A woman is forbidden from adornment. A man is forbidden from good. A doorman is a blacksmith, meaning he prevents. This has been fully presented. He only said: for a people who know because if the ignorant person is given many commands and prohibitions, he will not memorize them or observe them. The scholar memorizes and observes them. For this reason, He addressed the scholars and did not address the ignorant.
2:231: It has six issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And they have reached their term. The meaning of reached is that they approached, by consensus of scholars, and because the meaning compels him to do so, because after reaching the term he has no choice in keeping it, and in the verse after it it means the end, because the meaning requires that, so it is a reality in the second and a metaphor in the first. The second: The Almighty’s saying: So keep them in kindness. Keeping them in kindness means fulfilling what is due to her from her husband. Therefore, a group of scholars said: One of the ways of keeping them in kindness is that if the husband does not find what he can spend on his wife, he should divorce her. If he does not do so, he has gone beyond the bounds of kindness, and the ruler divorces her because of the harm that will befall her from her remaining with someone who cannot afford her expenses, and hunger cannot be tolerated. This is what Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, Abu Ubaid, Yahya Al-Qattan, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi said. Among the Companions, Umar, Ali, and Abu Hurairah said it, and among the Tabi’un, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: This is a Sunnah. Abu Hurairah narrated it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. A group said: There is no difference between them, and she must be patient with him, and the expenses are his responsibility by the ruling of the ruler. This is the saying of Ata’ and Al-Zuhri, and the Kufians and Al-Thawri agreed with it. They cited as evidence the saying of God Almighty: But if he is in hardship, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him. [Al-Baqarah, 280], and he said: And marry those among you who are single (al-Nur 24:32). So God Almighty encouraged the marriage of the poor, so poverty cannot be a reason for separation, and it is encouraged with it to marry. Also, the marriage between the spouses was concluded by consensus, so they cannot be separated except by a similar consensus, or by a Sunnah from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that has no opposition. The evidence for the first is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in Sahih Al-Bukhari: The woman says, ‘Either you feed me or you divorce me.’ This is a text in a disputed matter, and separation due to insolvency, according to us, is a revocable divorce, contrary to what Al-Shafi’i said: It is an irrevocable divorce, because this is a separation after consummation, and the number of divorces was not completed, nor was it for compensation or harm to the husband, so it was revocable, its origin is the divorce of a master. Third: The Almighty’s statement: Or release them on good terms, meaning divorce them. It was previously stated: And do not keep them, to the exclusion of harm, in order to aggravate the situation. Malik narrated on the authority of Thawr ibn Zayd ad-Dailami that a man would divorce his wife and then take her back, and he had no need for her and did not want to keep her, in order to prolong her waiting period and harm her. So God the Almighty revealed: “And do not keep them, to the exclusion of harm, in order to aggravate the situation. And whoever does that has wronged himself,” God admonishes them with it. Az-Zajjaj said: He has wronged himself, meaning he has exposed himself to punishment, because doing what God has forbidden exposes one to God’s punishment. This report is in agreement with the report that was revealed about abandoning what the people of ignorance were doing of divorce and taking back their wives, according to what was previously explained when God the Almighty said: Divorce is twice. These two reports informed us that the revelation of the two mentioned verses was in one similar meaning, which is the man’s confinement of the woman and his taking her back, intending to harm her, and this is clear. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And do not take the verses of God in jest. Its meaning is: Do not take the rulings of God in jest, for they are all valid, and whoever makes a joke about them is bound by them. Abu al-Darda’ said: A man would divorce during the pre-Islamic era and say: I divorced only in jest. He would free and marry and say: I was jesting. Then this verse was revealed, and he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever divorces or frees or marries or is married and thinks that he is joking, then he is serious. It was narrated by Muammar, who said: Isa bin Yunus told us on the authority of Amr on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, and he mentioned it with its meaning. In the Muwatta’ of Malik, it was reported to him that a man said to Ibn Abbas: I divorced my wife a hundred times, so what do you think of me? Ibn Abbas said: I have divorced you with ninety-seven and three, and you have taken God’s verses in jest. Al-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of Ismail bin Abi Umayya Al-Qurashi on the authority of Ali who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard a man who had divorced irrevocably, so he became angry and said: ‘Do you take God’s verses in jest or God’s religion in jest and play? Whoever divorces irrevocably, we will impose on him three times. She is not permissible for him until she marries another husband.’” Ismail bin Abi Umayya was from Kufa and his hadith is weak. It was narrated from Aisha that a man would divorce his wife and then say: ‘By God, I will not inherit from you nor will I leave you.’ She said: ‘How is that?’ He said: ‘If you are about to end your waiting period, I will take you back.’ Then the verse was revealed: ‘And do not take God’s verses in jest.’ Our scholars said that all the statements are included in the meaning of the verse, because it is said to someone who mocks God’s verses: ‘I have taken them in jest.’ It is said to someone who disbelieves in them, and it is said to someone who has rejected them and not taken them and acted according to other than them. Based on this, these statements are included in the verse. Verses are evidence, His commands and His prohibitions. Fifth: There is no disagreement among scholars that if someone divorces in jest, the divorce is binding on him. They differed concerning other matters, as will be explained in Bara’ah, God willing. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three things that are serious in earnest and serious in jest: marriage, divorce, and sexual intercourse.” It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Mas’ud, and Abu al-Darda’, all of whom said: There are three things that are not to be played with, and the one who plays with them is serious: marriage, divorce, and manumission. It was said: The meaning is do not abandon God’s commands, lest you be negligent and playful. This verse includes seeking forgiveness for sin verbally while persisting in action, and so is everything that has this meaning, so inform him. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And remember the favor of God upon you, meaning Islam and the clarification of the rulings and wisdom: It is the Sunnah explained on the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God’s intention in what He did not state in the Book: He admonishes you with it, meaning He frightens you. And fear God and know that God is Knowing of all things, as mentioned above.
2:232: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: So do not prevent them. It was narrated that Muqal ibn Yasar’s sister was married to Abu al-Badah, so he divorced her and left her until her waiting period was over. Then he regretted it and proposed to her, and she agreed, but her brother refused to marry her and said: My face is forbidden to you if you marry him. So the verse was revealed. Muqatil said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Muqal and said: If you are a believer, then do not prevent your sister from al-Badah. He said: I believe in God, and he married her to him. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of al-Hasan: The husband of Muqal ibn Yasar divorced her sister until her waiting period was over, so he proposed to her, but Muqal refused, so the verse: So do not prevent them from marrying their husbands. was revealed. Ad-Daraqutni also narrated it on the authority of al-Hasan, who said: Muqal ibn Yasar told me: I had a sister who proposed to me, so I used to prevent people from marrying her. Then Ibn Umar came to me and proposed to her, so I married her to him, and they spent as long as God willed. Then he divorced her with a revocable divorce, then he left her until her waiting period was over. So he proposed to her with the suitors, so I said: People prevented her and I married her to you, then I divorced her with a revocable divorce, then I left her until her waiting period was over. So when she proposed to me, you came to me to propose to her with the suitors! I will never marry you to her! So God revealed, or he said revealed: And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their term, do not prevent them from marrying their [former] husbands. So I atoned for my oath and married her to him. In a narration by Al-Bukhari: Ma’qil became very angry about that and said: Let her go while he is able to have her and then propose to her! So God revealed the verse, so the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) called him and recited the verse to him, so he abandoned his anger and submitted to the command of God the Most High. It was said: He is Ma’qil ibn Sinan with a nun. An-Nahhas said: Ash-Shafi’i narrated it in his books on the authority of Ma’qil ibn Yasar or Sinan. And At-Tahawi said: He is Ma’qil ibn Sinan. The second: If this is proven, then in the verse there is evidence that marriage is not permissible without a guardian, because the sister of Ma’qil was previously married, and if the matter was up to her and not her guardian, she would have married herself, and she would not have needed her guardian, Ma’qil. So the address in the Almighty’s saying: So do not prevent them is to the guardians, and that the matter is up to them in marriage with their consent. It has been said that the address in that is to the husbands, because taking back a woman is harmful, preventing her from marrying someone else by prolonging her waiting period. The companions of Abu Hanifa used it as evidence that a woman can marry herself. They said: Because God Almighty attributed that to her, as He said: Then she is not lawful to him afterward until she marries a husband other than him, and He did not mention the guardian. The statement on this issue has been presented in full, and the first is more correct because of what we mentioned about the reason for revelation, and God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And when they have reached their term. Reaching the term in this place means its end, because the beginning of marriage can only be imagined after the expiration of the waiting period. You detain them means you imprison them. Al-Khalil narrated: A hen withheld eggs: its eggs have been withheld. It was said: The constraint means constriction and prevention, and it goes back to the meaning of confinement. It is said: A matter, so you prevented me from it, meaning you prevented me from it and made it difficult for me. The matter is difficult, if you are unable to find a way to deal with it. Al-Zuhri said: The origin of the constraint is from their saying: The she-camel became difficult if her offspring grew and it was not easy to come out. The hen became difficult means its eggs grew. In the hadith of Mu’awiyah, a difficult matter and Abu Hassan, meaning a difficult issue with narrow exits. Tawus said: There have been cases of difficult decisions that only Ibn Abbas has undertaken, and every problem among the Arabs is difficult. From this is the saying of Al-Shafi’i: If the dilemmas confront me, I will reveal their truths by looking. It is said: The matter became difficult if it became severe and an incurable disease, meaning that it was very difficult to cure and exhausted the doctors. So-and-so prevented his mother means he prevented her. He prevented her and he prevented her with dammah and kasrah are two dialects. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: This is an admonition to whoever is. He did not say that because it is understood to mean the plural. If it had been that it would have been permissible, like that is purer for you and cleaner, and God knows meaning what is good for you in it: and you do not know that.
2:233: It contains eighteen issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And mothers begins: They shall nurse their children in the place of the report, two complete years is a time adverb, and when God Almighty mentioned marriage and divorce, He mentioned the child, because the spouses may separate and then have a child, so the verse is then about divorced women who have children from their husbands, as Al-Suddi, Ad-Dahhak and others said, meaning they are more entitled to nurse their children than foreign women because they are more affectionate and gentle, and taking away a young child is harmful to him and to her, and this indicates that even if the child is weaned, the mother is more entitled to his custody due to her superior affection and compassion, and she is only more entitled to custody if she does not remarry, as will come, and based on this, His saying: And the father of the child shall bear their food and clothing according to what is acceptable is problematic, because the divorced woman does not deserve clothing if it is not revocable, but rather she deserves wages, unless it is interpreted as good morals, in which case it is said: It is better that the wages not be less than what is sufficient for her food and clothing, and it was said: The verse is general in regard to divorced women who have children. And in wives, and it is more apparent that it is in wives while the marriage remains, because they are the ones who are entitled to maintenance and clothing, and the wife is entitled to maintenance and clothing whether she breastfeeds or not, and maintenance and clothing are in exchange for empowerment, so if she is busy with breastfeeding, the empowerment is not complete, so it may be thought that maintenance is dropped, so that illusion was removed by the words of God Almighty: And upon the father of the child meaning the husband is their provision and clothing in the case of breastfeeding because it is busy with the interests of the husband, so it became as if she traveled for the need of the husband with his permission, then maintenance is not dropped. Second: The Almighty’s saying: They shall breastfeed is a statement that means an order of obligation for some mothers, and a recommendation for some of them, as will come. It was said: It is a statement of legitimacy, as mentioned above. Third: People differed about breastfeeding, is it a right for the mother or is it a right upon her? The wording is ambiguous, because if he wanted to state that it is upon her, he would have said: And upon the mothers is the breastfeeding of their children, as God Almighty said: And upon the father of the child is their provision and their clothing. But it is upon her in the case of marriage, and it is a custom that is binding since it has become like a condition, unless she is noble and has luxury, so it is customary for her not to breastfeed, and that is like a condition upon her if the child does not accept anyone else, it is obligatory, and it is upon her if it is not due to her being exclusive to it. If the father dies and the boy has no money, then the Maliki school of thought, in Al-Mudawwana, is that breastfeeding is obligatory upon the mother, unlike maintenance. In the book of Ibn Al-Jalab: His breastfeeding is from the public treasury. Abdul Wahhab said: He is a poor person from the poor Muslims. As for the woman who was divorced with a final divorce, she is not obligated to breastfeed, and breastfeeding is upon the husband unless she wishes, in which case she is more entitled to the wages of her peers. This is with the husband’s wealth. If he is poor, she is not obligated to breastfeed unless the child does not accept anyone else, in which case she is forced to breastfeed. And whoever is obligated to breastfeed, if she is afflicted with an excuse that prevents her from it, the breastfeeding returns to the father. It was narrated on the authority of Malik that if the father is poor and the boy has no money, then breastfeeding is the responsibility of the mother. If she has no milk and has money, then breastfeeding is her responsibility from her money. Al-Shafi’i said: Breastfeeding is not obligatory except for a father or grandfather, no matter how high. What the scholars have said about this will come in the words of God Almighty: And the same is upon the heir. It is said: a breastfed child breastfeeds breastfeeding and breastfeeding, and breastfed child breastfeeds with a kasra on the ra’ in the first and a fatha on it in the second. The active participle is breastfed in both of them, and breastfeeding is meanness with a fatha on the ra’ only. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: two years means two years, from the state of something when it changes, so the year changes from the first time to the second, and it was said: The year was called a year because things are mostly impossible in it, complete, the condition is complete because the speaker might say: I stayed with so-and-so for two years, and he means one year and part of another year, God Almighty said: But whoever hastens in two days (al-Baqarah 2:203), and he only hastens in one day and part of the second, and the Almighty’s saying: For whoever desires to complete the nursing is evidence that breastfeeding for two years is not obligatory, as it is permissible to wean before the two years, but it is a limitation to end the dispute between the spouses regarding the period of breastfeeding, so the husband is not obligated to give the wage for more than two years, and if the father wants to wean before this period and the mother does not agree, he is not allowed to do so, and the increase or decrease over the two years is only when there is no harm to the newborn and when the parents agree, and Mujahid and Ibn Muhaisin read (for whoever desires to complete the nursing) with the opening of the ta’ and raising (breastfeeding) on the basis of attributing the action to it, and Abu Haywah, Ibn Abi Ubla, and Al-Jarud Ibn Abi Sabra with a kasra on the ra’ from (al-Rida’ah) and it is a language like al-Hadhara and al-Hadhara. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he read al-Rida’ah, on the weight of al-Fa’la. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he read that he completes the breastfeeding. Al-Nahhas: The Basrans do not know al-Rida’ah except with a fatha on the ra’, nor al-Rida’ except with a kasra on the ra’, like al-Qital. The Kufians narrated the kasra on the ra’ with the ha’ and its fatha without the ha’. Fifth: Malik, may God have mercy on him, and those who followed him, and a group of scholars, extracted from this verse that the prohibited breastfeeding that is considered as a lineage is only what was within two years, because with the expiration of the two years, breastfeeding is complete, and breastfeeding after the two years is not considered. This is his statement in his Muwatta’, and it is the narration of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hakam from him, and it is the statement of Umar and Ibn Abbas, and it was narrated from Ibn Mas’ud, and al-Zuhri, Qatada, al-Sha’bi, Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, and Abu Thawr said the same. Ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated from him the two years and a few days more. Abd al-Malik: like a month and the like. Ibn al-Qasim narrated from Malik that he said: Breastfeeding is the two years and the two months are after the two years. Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated from him that he said: Whatever was after the two years of breastfeeding by a month or two or three is from the two years, and whatever was after that is in vain. It was narrated from al-Nu’man that he said: Whatever was after the two years up to six months is breastfeeding, and the correct view is that the newborn breastfed after the two years, and it was narrated Sufyan, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no breastfeeding except what occurs within the first two years. Al-Daraqutni said: It was not transmitted from Ibn Uyaynah except by Al-Haytham ibn Jameel, and he is a trustworthy hafiz. I said: This report, with the verse and the meaning, negates the breastfeeding of an adult and that he has no sanctity. It was narrated from Aisha that she said this, and Al-Layth ibn Saeed, among the scholars, says this. It was narrated from Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari that he believed in the breastfeeding of an adult, and it was narrated from him that he retracted it, and it will come in Surat An-Nisa’, explaining it, God willing. Sixth: The majority of commentators said: These two years are for every child. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: It is in the case of a child who remains in the womb for six months. If he remains seven months, then his breastfeeding is twenty-three months. If he remains eight months, then his breastfeeding is twenty-two months. If he remains nine months, then his breastfeeding is twenty-one months, based on the words of God Almighty: And his gestation and weaning is thirty months (al-Ahqaf 46:15). Based on this, the period of pregnancy and the period of breastfeeding overlap and one takes from the other. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And upon the one for whom the child was born meaning and upon the father. In Arabic, it is permissible to say And upon the one for whom the child was born like the Almighty’s saying: And among them are those who listen to you (Yunus 10:42) because the meaning is And upon the one for whom the child was born and who is used to express the singular and the plural as mentioned above. Eighth: The Almighty’s statement: Their provision and their clothing. Provision in this ruling means sufficient food, and in this is evidence of the father’s obligation to provide for the child due to his weakness and inability. God Almighty called it the mother, because the food reaches him through her in breastfeeding, as He said: And if they are pregnant, then spend on them (al-Talaq 65:6), because the food does not reach him except through her. The scholars agreed that a man must provide for his children who have no money. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Hind bint ‘Utbah when she said to him: “Abu Sufyan is a stingy man and he does not give me enough money to suffice me and my children except what I take from his money without his knowledge. Is there any sin on me for that?” He said: Take what is sufficient for you and your children in a reasonable manner. Clothing means garments. His statement: in a reasonable manner means what is customary in the custom of the Shari’ah, without being excessive or negligent. Then the Most High explained that spending is according to the husband’s wealth and position, and he does not charge a person more than he can bear, by saying: No soul is charged except with that within its capacity, as will be explained in divorce, God willing. It was said that the meaning is: The woman is not charged with patience in stinginess in wages, and the husband is not charged with what is extravagance, but moderation is taken into consideration. Ninth, in this verse is evidence for Malik that custody belongs to the mother, for the boy is until puberty, and for the girl until marriage, and that is her right, and Abu Hanifa said the same, and Al-Shafi’i said that when the boy reaches eight years of age, which is the age of discernment, he is given a choice between his parents, because in that case his ambition is moved to learn the Qur’an, etiquette, and the duties of worship, and this is the same for the boy and the girl. Al-Nasa’i and others narrated “On the authority of Abu Hurairah: A woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: My husband wants to take my prophet away. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: This is your father and this is your female slave, so take whichever one you want, so he took his mother’s hand.” And in the book of Abu Dawud “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: A woman came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while I was sitting with him, and she said: O Messenger of God, my husband wants to take my son away, and he gave me water from the well of Abu Utbah, and it has benefited me, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Draw lots for him, so her husband said: Who will argue with me regarding my child? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is your father and this is your mother, so take the hand of Whichever one you wish, he took his mother’s hand and she set off with him.” Our evidence is what Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Al-Awza’i, who said: Amr ibn Shu’ayb told me on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather Abdullah ibn Amr, “A woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, my womb was a vessel for this son of mine, my breast was a drink for him, and my lap was a shelter for him, and his father divorced me and wanted to take him away from me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: You have more right to him as long as you do not remarry.” Ibn Al-Mundhir said: All of the scholars who have memorized his hadith are unanimously agreed that if a couple separates and they have a child, the mother has more right to him as long as she does not remarry. Abu Umar also said: I do not know of any disagreement among the early scholars regarding a divorced woman who marries, that she has more right to her child than his father, as long as he is a small child who does not distinguish anything, if he is with her in a safe and sufficient condition and there is no evidence of immorality or immodesty in her. Then they differed after that about giving him the choice if he distinguishes and is rational between his father and his mother and who is more deserving of him. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It is proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled regarding his son Hamza in favor of his maternal aunt without giving him the choice. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ali who said: Zaid bin Haritha went out to Mecca and lost Hamza’s daughter. Ja’far said: I will take her, I have more right to her, she is the daughter of my paternal uncle and her maternal aunt is with me and the maternal aunt is a mother. Ali said: I have more right to her, she is the daughter of my paternal uncle and the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is with me, and she has more right to her. Zaid said: I have more right to her, I went out to her and traveled and brought her. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and mentioned a hadith in which he said: As for the girl, I rule that she is with Ja’far and she is with her maternal aunt, but the maternal aunt is a mother. Tenth: Ibn al-Mundhir said: All the scholars who have been preserved from him have agreed that the mother has no right to the child if she marries. I said: This is what he said in his book Al-Ashraf, and Judge Abdul Wahhab mentioned in his explanation of the message on the authority of Al-Hasan that her right to custody is not lost by marriage, and Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Al-Nu’man and Abu Thawr agreed that the maternal grandmother is more entitled to custody of the child, and they differed if she did not have a mother and had a grandmother who was the father’s mother, so Malik said: The paternal mother is more entitled if the boy does not have an aunt, and Ibn Al-Qasim said Malik said: It reached me that he said: The maternal aunt is more entitled than the paternal grandmother, and in the statement of Al-Shafi’i and Al-Nu’man: The paternal mother is more entitled than the maternal aunt, and it has been said: The father is more entitled to his son than the paternal grandmother, Abu Omar said: This is according to me if he does not have a foreign wife, then the sister after the father, then the aunt, and this is if each one of these is trustworthy with the child, and he is in safekeeping and sufficiency with him, so if that is not the case then he has no right to custody, and rather the consideration in that is who protects the boy and who is good to him in protecting him and teaching him good, and this is according to the statement of those who said that custody is the right of the child, and this has been narrated from Malik A group of his companions said this, and they also do not see custody for a profligate woman or a weak woman who is unable to fulfill the rights of the boy due to illness or time. Ibn Habib mentioned on the authority of Mutraf and Ibn al-Majshun on the authority of Malik that custody is for the mother, then the maternal grandmother, then the maternal aunt, then the paternal grandmother, then the boy’s sister, then the boy’s paternal aunt, then the boy’s niece, then the father. The paternal grandmother is more deserving than the sister, and the sister is more deserving than the aunt, and the aunt is more deserving than those after her, and the guardians are more deserving than all the men. The daughter of the maternal aunt, the daughter of the paternal aunt, and the daughters of the boy’s sisters do not have any custody of him. If the guardian does not fear that the child will be lost or corrupted, then he is his guardian forever until he reaches puberty. It has been said: until he reaches maturity, and until the slave girl marries, unless the father wants to move and settle, in which case he is more deserving of his child than his mother or anyone else if she does not want to move. If he wants to go out for trade, he is not allowed to do so. The same applies to the guardians of the boy whose destination is if they move to settle. The mother does not have the right to move her child from the place of residence of the father except for a distance that is close to the distance that does not… She shortens her prayer, and if he stipulated to her when he moved from her country that he would not leave his child with her unless she committed to his expenses and maintenance for a specified number of years, then if she committed to that, then it is binding on her. If she died, then her heirs would not be held accountable for that in her estate. It has been said: That is a debt that is taken from her estate, and the first is more correct, God Almighty willing, just as if the child died or if he reconciled with her regarding the expenses of pregnancy and breastfeeding and she miscarried, then she would not be held accountable for anything of that. Eleventh: If the mother marries, her child is not taken from her until her husband consummates the marriage with her, according to Malik. Al-Shafi’i said: If she marries, her right is cut off. If he divorces her, she does not have the right to take it back, according to Malik, according to the most popular view of his school of thought. Judge Ismail mentioned, and Ibn Khuwayz Mandad also mentioned it, on the authority of Malik, that his opinion differed on that. He said once: He is returned to her, and he said once: He is not returned. Ibn al-Mundhir said: If the mother leaves the country in which her child is and then returns to it, she is more entitled to her child, according to al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, and the people of opinion. Likewise, if she marries and then divorces or her husband dies, her right to the child is likewise. I said: Judge Abu Muhammad Abdul Wahhab said the same. If the husband divorces her or dies, she has the right to take it because the excuse that allowed him to leave it has disappeared. Twelfth: If a woman abandons custody of her child and does not want to take him, and she is free and not busy with a husband, then after that she wants to take him, then she is considered. If she abandoned him for an excuse, then she is entitled to take him. But if she abandoned him out of rejection and hatred for him, then she is not entitled to take him after that. Thirteenth: They differed concerning the spouses who separate by divorce and the wife is a dhimmi. A group said: There is no difference between a dhimmi and a Muslim woman, and she is more entitled to her child. This is the opinion of Abu Thawr, the People of Opinion, and Ibn al-Qasim, the companion of Malik. Ibn al-Mundhir said: We have narrated a hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet that agrees with this opinion, but there is an argument about its chain of transmission. There is a second opinion in it that the child is with the Muslim one of them. This is the opinion of Malik, Suwar, and Abdullah ibn al-Hasan, and this was narrated from al-Shafi’i. Likewise, they differed concerning the spouses who separate, one of them free and the other a slave. A group said: The free man is more entitled. This is the opinion of Ata’, al-Thawri, al-Shafi’i, and the People of Opinion. Malik said: Concerning the father, if he is free and has a free child and the mother is a slave: the mother is more entitled to him unless she is sold and transferred, in which case the father is more entitled to him. Fourteenth: The Almighty’s saying: A mother shall not be harmed by her child, nor shall a father by his child. The meaning is: The mother shall not refuse to breastfeed him to harm his father or to demand more than the reward of her peers, and it is not permissible for the father to prevent the mother from that while she desires to breastfeed. This is the saying of the majority of commentators. Nafi’, Asim, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read tadhar with a fatha on the doubled ra’, and its position is in the jussive mood for prohibition. Its original form is la tadharar according to the original, so the first ra’ was assimilated into the second and the second was opened because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. This is what is done in the doubled form if it is preceded by a fatha or an alif. You say: ‘Adh ya rajul wa dharar fulan ya rajul: meaning the child shall not be taken from her if she is satisfied with breastfeeding and the child is familiar with her. Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, and Aban from Asim and a group read tadhar with the nominative case in apposition to His saying: Takkalnafs which is report and what is meant by it is the command. Yunus narrated from Al-Hasan who said: He says: Do not harm her husband, she says: I will not breastfeed him. And he does not harm her, so he takes it from her while she says: I am breastfeeding him. It is possible that the original is (tadaarru) with the first ra’ broken, and Aban narrated it from Asim, and it is the language of the people of Hijaz (walida) is the subject, and it is possible that (tadaarru) (walida) is the object of what its subject is not named, and it was narrated from Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he read (la tadaarru) with the first two ra’s open, and Abu Jaafar bin Al-Qaqa’ read (tadaarru) with the ra’ silent and light, and likewise (la yudaar katabi) and this is far-fetched because if two similar words come together and they are original, it is not permissible to delete one of them for lightening, so either assimilation or idhhar, and it was narrated from him sukun and shaddah, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan (la tadaarru) with the first ra’ broken. Fifteenth: The Almighty’s saying: And upon the heir is the same is connected to His saying: And upon the newborn. They differed in the interpretation of His saying: And upon the heir is the same. Qatada, al-Suddi, al-Hasan, and Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: It is the heir of the boy if he died. Some of them said: His heir from men in particular is obligated to breastfeed him, just as it would be obligatory for the father of the boy if he was alive. Mujahid and Ata’ said this. Qatada and others said: It is the heir of the boy, whether men or women, and they are obligated to breastfeed him according to the amount of their inheritance from him. Ahmad and Ishaq said this. Judge Abu Ishaq Ismail ibn Ishaq said in his book, The Meanings of the Qur’an: As for Abu Hanifa, he said: The maintenance of the young boy and his breastfeeding are obligatory upon every mahram relative, such as if a man has a young nephew who is in need and a young cousin who is in need and he is his heir, then the maintenance is obligatory upon the maternal uncle for his nephew who does not inherit from him, and it is dropped from the paternal uncle for his paternal cousin who is the heir. Abu Ishaq said: So they said something that is not… In the Book of God, and we do not know anyone who said it: Al-Tabari narrated on the authority of Abu Hanifa and his two companions that they said: The heir who is obligated to breastfeed is his heir if he is a mahram relative to him. If Ibn Umar and others are not mahram relative, then nothing is obligatory on him. It was said: What is meant is the father’s agnates, upon whom are the expenses and clothing. Ad-Dahhak said: If the father of the boy dies and the boy has money, his breastfeeding is taken from the money. If he has no money, it is taken from the agnates. If the agnates have no money, the mother is forced to breastfeed him. Qubaydah bin Dhu’ayb, Ad-Dahhak, and Bashir bin Nasr, the judge of Umar bin Abdul Aziz, said: The heir is the boy himself. They interpreted his statement: And upon the heir the newborn, as upon what is upon the newborn, meaning upon him in his money if he inherits his father, breastfeeding himself. Sufyan said: The heir here is the one who remains from the parents of the newborn after the death of the other of them. If the father dies, then upon the mother is the child’s sustenance if he does not have money, and the agnate shares with her in breastfeeding the newborn according to his share of the inheritance.
