Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: If the orphan is poor and has no money, the Imam must take care of him from the public treasury. If the Imam does not do so, then the Muslims must do so, the one who is most special to him, and the mother is most special to him, so she must breastfeed him and take care of him, and she does not have recourse to him or anyone else. Breastfeeding is obligatory, and maintenance is recommended. The reason for the recommendation is the Almighty’s saying: Mothers shall breastfeed their children for two complete years. It is obligatory for husbands to take care of them. If it is not possible to fulfill their right due to the death of the husband or his insolvency, the right is not dropped from them. Do you not see that the waiting period is obligatory for them, and maintenance and housing are on their husbands? If maintenance is not possible for them, the waiting period is not dropped from them? Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated in al-Asadiyyah on the authority of Malik ibn Anas, may God have mercy on him, that he said: A man is not obligated to provide maintenance for a brother, a relative, or a blood relative. He said: And the saying of God Almighty: And the heir is responsible for the same is abrogated. An-Nahhas said: This is the wording of Malik, and he did not explain what abrogated it, nor did Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, nor did I know that any of their companions explained that. What is It seems that the abrogator has it with him, and God knows best, that when God Almighty made it obligatory for the woman whose husband died to have a year’s maintenance and housing from the deceased’s money, then abrogated that by removing it, that was also abrogated for the heir. I said: According to this, the expenses are on the boy himself from his money, and the heir is not responsible for anything from it, as will come. Ibn al-Arabi said: His statement, And the heir is responsible for the same, Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik that it is abrogated. This is a statement that disgusts the hearts of the heedless, and confuses the minds of the deviants, and the matter is close! This is because the early scholars of jurists and commentators used to call specialization abrogation, because it lifted some of what was included in the generality as a concession, and this was common in their tongues until it became difficult for those who came after them. The realization of the statement in it is that the Almighty’s saying: And upon the heir is the same, is an indication of what came before, so some people returned it to all of it from the obligation of purification and the prohibition of causing harm, among them Abu Hanifa from the jurists, and from the predecessors Qatadah and Al-Hasan and it is attributed to Umar. A group of scholars said: The meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And upon the heir is the same, does not refer to all of what came before, but rather it refers to the prohibition of causing harm, and the meaning is: And upon the heir is from the prohibition of causing harm to the mother what is upon the father, and this is the origin, so whoever claims that the conjunction in it refers to all of what came before, then he must provide evidence. I said: His saying: (And this is the origin) means in his referring the pronoun to the closest mentioned, and it is correct, because if he had meant all of them, which are breastfeeding, spending, and not causing harm, he would have said: And upon the heir are the likes of these, so it indicates that it is conjoined with the prohibition of harm, and all the commentators interpreted it according to what Judge Abdul Wahhab narrated, which is that what is meant by it is that the mother does not harm her child in that if the father offers her a fair wage not to breastfeed him, nor a child for him with his child, in that if the mother offers to breastfeed him for a fair wage, then she has that right, because the mother is kinder and more compassionate towards him, and her milk is more beneficial to him than the milk of a foreign woman. Ibn Atiyyah said: Malik, may God have mercy on him, and all of his companions, and al-Sha’bi also and al-Zuhri and al-Dahhak and a group of scholars said: What is meant by his saying like that is not to cause harm, and as for sustenance and clothing, none of it is obligatory, and Ibn al-Qasim narrated from Malik that the verse included that sustenance and clothing are upon the heir, then that was abrogated by the consensus of the nation that the heir is not to be harmed, and the disagreement Is he entitled to provision and clothing or not? Yahya bin Ya`mar read and upon the heirs in the plural, and that requires generality. If they use as evidence the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): God does not accept charity while a relative is in need, it is said to them that the relative is general in all relatives, whether they are forbidden or not. There is no disagreement that giving charity to a relative is more appropriate, because the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Put it among the closest relatives. So the hadith is interpreted according to this, and there is no proof in it for what they intended, and God knows best. An-Nahhas said: As for the saying of the one who said and upon the heir is the same, that he should not be harmed, then this is a good saying, because people’s money is forbidden, so nothing is taken from it except with conclusive evidence. As for the saying of the one who said upon the heirs of the father, then the proof is that the expenses were upon the father, so his heirs are from the heirs of the son. As for the proof of the one who said upon the heirs of the son, he says: As they inherit him, they take care of him. An-Nahhas said: Muhammad bin Jarir used to choose the saying of the one who said the heir here is the son, and even if it is a strange saying, the proof of it is correct and the proof of it is clear, because his money is more appropriate for him. The jurists, except for a few exceptions, have agreed that if a man has a young son and the son has money, and the father is well-off, then the father is not obligated to provide for his children or breastfeed them, and that is from the boy’s money. If it is said: God Almighty said: And the father shall bear the cost of their food and clothing on equitable terms, it is said: This pronoun refers to the feminine. However, the consensus is a limit to the verse that explains it, and a Muslim cannot deviate from it. As for the one who said: That is upon whoever of the parents remains, his argument is that it is not permissible for the mother to neglect her child, and the one who used to spend on him and her has died. Al-Bukhari has a chapter in refuting this statement: “Chapter: And the heir has the same, and does the woman have any of it?” He cited the hadith of Umm Salamah and Hind, the meaning of which is: “Umm Salamah had sons from Abu Salamah and they did not have money, so she asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he informed her that she would have a reward for that.” This hadith indicates that she is not obligated to provide for her children, and if it were obligatory upon her, she would not have said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And I will not abandon them, and what The hadith of Hind: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that she should take her expenses and the expenses of her children from the father’s money, and he did not make it obligatory for her as he made it obligatory for the father. Al-Bukhari deduced from this that since mothers were not obligated to pay the expenses of their children during the life of their fathers, they are also not obligated to pay them when their fathers die. As for the statement of those who said that expenses and clothing are on every mahram relative, their proof is that a man must spend on every mahram relative if he is poor. An-Nahhas said: This statement has been objected to because it was not taken from the Book of God Almighty, nor from consensus, nor from an authentic Sunnah. Rather, no statement is known other than what we have mentioned. As for the Qur’an, God Almighty said: And the heir is responsible for the same. If the heir is responsible for expenses and clothing, they contradicted that and said: If he leaves behind his maternal uncle and paternal cousin, then the expenses are on his maternal uncle and his paternal cousin is not responsible for anything. This contradicts the text of the Qur’an, because the maternal uncle does not inherit with the paternal cousin according to one opinion, nor does he inherit alone according to the opinion of many scholars. What they used as proof of spending on every mahram relative, most of the scholars Science is the opposite. Sixteenth: The Almighty’s saying: If they both desire weaning. The pronoun desire refers to the parents, and weaning means weaning from breastfeeding, i.e. from nourishment with his mother’s milk to other foods. Weaning and separation: weaning, and its origin is separation, so it is the separation between the child and the breast, and from it the young camel is called, because it is separated from its mother, by mutual consent i.e. before two years, there is no blame upon them i.e. in separating it, and that is because when God Almighty made the period of breastfeeding two years, He made clear that their weaning is weaning, and their weaning is weaning, and no one has a right to refrain from it, except that the parents spend less than that number without harming the child, so that is permissible with this explanation. Qatada said: Breastfeeding was obligatory in the two years, and weaning before that was forbidden, then it was made easier and breastfeeding was permitted for less than two years by His saying: If they both desire weaning. And in this is evidence of the permissibility of independent reasoning in rulings by God’s permission. Parents are to consult each other regarding what will lead to the well-being of the child. This depends on their most likely assumptions, not on truth and certainty. Consultation means extracting an opinion, as well as consultation. Advice is like assistance. I extracted honey, I extracted it. I excavated the animal and made it run to extract its gait. The furniture of the house is the furniture because it is visible to the observer. The sign is the appearance of the man. The sign is to bring out what is in your soul and show it. Seventeenth: The Almighty’s saying: And if you wish to have a female nurse for your children meaning for your children other than the mother. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Nahhas said: The meaning in Arabic is that you should have a female nurse for your children, like they measured for them or weighed for them (al-Mutaffifin 83:3), meaning they measured for them or weighed for them, and the lam was deleted because it takes two objects, one of which is with a letter. Sibawayh recited: I have commanded you to do good, so do what I have commanded you to do, for I have left you with wealth and lineage. It is not permissible to say: I called Zaid, meaning I called for Zaid, because it leads to confusion. In this type, hearing is considered. I said: And on this basis, the verse is evidence of the permissibility of taking a wet-nurse if the fathers and mothers agree on that. And Ikrimah said about the words of God the Almighty: Let no mother be harmed that it means the wet-nurse, as narrated by Ibn Atiyyah. And the basic principle is that every mother is obligated to breastfeed her child as God the Almighty informed us, so He commanded wives to breastfeed their children, and He made it obligatory for them from the husbands to provide for them and clothe them, and the marriage is still valid. So if breastfeeding was the responsibility of the father, he would have mentioned it along with what he mentioned about their sustenance and clothing. However, Malik, may God have mercy on him, and not the jurists of the countries, excepted the noble woman and said: She is not obligated to breastfeed him. So he excluded her from the verse and specified her with a principle of the principles of jurisprudence, which is acting according to custom. And this is a principle that only Malik realized. And the wonderful principle in it is that this was a matter in the pre-Islamic era for those of high status, and Islam came and did not change it. And those of wealth and high status continued to free up mothers for pleasure by giving the sucklings to wet-nurses until his time, so he said it, and until our time, so we have realized it in the Shari’ah. Eighteenth: The Almighty’s saying: If you surrender meaning the fathers, that is, you surrender the wage to the wet nurse. Sufyan and Mujahid said: You surrender the wage to the mothers according to what they breastfed until the time of the intention to breastfeed. The six of the seven read what you gave meaning what you gave, and Ibn Kathir read you came meaning what you came and did, as Zuhair said: Whatever good they did was inherited by their fathers. It was said: Qatada and Al-Zuhri said: The meaning is that you have submitted what you have given of the intention of breastfeeding, that is, each of the parents submitted and was satisfied, and that was with their agreement and good intention and the intention of what is known from the matter, and according to this possibility, the address includes the men and women (you have submitted), and according to the two previous opinions, the address is to the men, Abu Ali said: The meaning is if you submitted what you have given, then the pronoun was deleted from the relative clause, and according to this interpretation, the address is to the men, because they are the ones who are given the reward for breastfeeding, Abu Ali said: It is possible that (ma) is a source, that is, if you submitted the coming, and the meaning is like the first, but the description is dispensed with by deleting the complement and then deleting the pronoun.
2:234: It contains twenty-five issues: The first is the saying of the Most High: And those among you who die When the Most High mentioned the waiting period for divorce and connected it to mentioning breastfeeding, He also mentioned the waiting period for death, so that it would not be thought that the waiting period for death is like the waiting period for divorce. And those meaning the men among you who die and leave wives meaning they leave wives, meaning they have wives, so the wives wait, Al-Zajjaj said its meaning and An-Nahhas chose it. The subject is often omitted in speech, like the saying of the Most High: “Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire” (al-Hajj 22:72) meaning it is the Fire. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: Its meaning is And those among you who die and leave wives who wait after them, and it is like your saying: The fat is two dirhams for a dirham, meaning two dirhams for it. It was said that the meaning is And the wives of those among you who die wait, so the expression came in the utmost brevity. Al-Mahdawi narrated from Sibawayh that the meaning is: And among what is recited to you are those who die. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: The report about those is omitted, and the intention is Telling their wives that they are waiting, and this expression means telling about the legitimacy in one of the two aspects as mentioned above. The second: This verse is about the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died. Its apparent meaning is general, but its meaning is specific. Al-Mahdawi narrated from some scholars that the verse included pregnant women, then it was abrogated by the statement: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth (al-Talaq 65:4). Most scholars are of the view that this verse abrogates the statement of God the Almighty: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall bequeath to their wives a year’s maintenance, without removing them (al-Baqarah 2:240), because people lived for a period of time in Islam, when a man died and left his wife pregnant, he would bequeath to her her maintenance for a year and housing as long as she did not go out and marry. Then this was abrogated by four months and ten days, and by inheritance. Some people said, there is no abrogation in this, but rather it is a reduction of a year, like the prayer of the traveler, when it is reduced from four to two, this was not abrogated, and this is a clear mistake, because if her ruling was that she should observe the waiting period of one year if she did not go out, then if she went out, she was not prevented, then this was removed and her waiting period of four months and ten days was required of her. This is abrogation, and the prayer of the traveler is not part of this in Something, and Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The prayer was made obligatory, two rak’ahs at a time, two rak’ahs at a time, so the prayer of residence was increased and the prayer of travel was left as it was, and it will come. Third: The waiting period of a pregnant woman whose husband has died is the delivery of her pregnancy according to the majority of scholars. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ibn Abbas that the completion of her waiting period is the last of the two periods, and Sahnun from our scholars chose this. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he went back on this. The evidence for what was narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Abbas is to combine the words of God Almighty: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days and His words: And those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth (al-Talaq 65:4). This is because if she waits the longest of the two periods, then she has acted in accordance with the requirements of the two verses. If she completes her waiting period by giving birth, then she has abandoned acting in accordance with the verse of the waiting period of death. Combining is more appropriate than giving preference according to the consensus of the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence. This is a good view, were it not for what is clouded by “the hadith of Subay’ah al-Aslamiyah, that she gave birth after the death of her husband by nights, and that she mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he ordered her to get married.” It was narrated in Sahih. The hadith explains that the words of God Almighty: And those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth (al-Talaq 65:4), are interpreted in its generality in Divorced women and those whose husbands have died, and the waiting period for death is specific to those who are prevented from having intercourse from both categories. This is supported by the words of Ibn Masoud: And whoever wants to say to his family that the verse of the shortened women was revealed after the verse of the waiting period for death, our scholars said: The apparent meaning of his words is that it abrogates it, but that is not what he meant, and God knows best, but rather he means that it is specific to it, for some of its implications were excluded from it, and likewise the hadith of Subai’ah is later than the waiting period for death, because the story of Subai’ah was after the Farewell Pilgrimage, and her husband was Sa’d ibn Khawlah, and he was from Banu Amir ibn Lu’ay, and he was one of those who witnessed Badr, and he died in Mecca at that time while she was pregnant, and he is the one for whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mourned that he died in Mecca, and she gave birth after him by half a month, and Al-Bukhari said: by forty nights, and Muslim narrated from the hadith of Umar ibn Abdullah ibn Al-Arqam: that Subai’ah asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and she said: So he gave me a fatwa that I became permissible when I gave birth, and he ordered me to marry if I wished, Ibn Shihab said: I do not see any harm in her marrying when she gave birth even if she was bleeding, except that her husband should not approach her until she is pure, and this is what the majority of scholars and imams of jurists said, and Al-Hasan, Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Nakha’i said And Hammad: A woman in postpartum bleeding should not be married as long as she is in the state of postpartum bleeding. So they stipulated two conditions: the delivery of the fetus, and purification from the blood of postpartum bleeding. The hadith is an argument against them, but they have no argument in his statement: (So when she recovered from her postpartum bleeding, she adorned herself for the suitor) as in Sahih Muslim and Abu Dawud, because (she recovered) even if its original meaning is she recovered from the blood of postpartum bleeding according to what Al-Khalil said, it is possible that what is meant by it here is she recovered from the pains of postpartum bleeding, meaning she recovered from her pains. And even if we assume that its meaning is what Al-Khalil said, then there is no argument in it. Rather, the argument is in his saying, peace be upon him, to Sabi’ah: You have become permissible when you have given birth. So he made the permissibility at the time of delivery and made it dependent on it, and he did not say when your bleeding stopped or when you became pure, so what the majority said is correct. Fourth: There is no disagreement among scholars that the term of every divorced pregnant woman, whether the husband has the right to take her back or not, whether she is free, a slave, a freed slave, or a freedwoman, is until she gives birth. They differed regarding the term of a pregnant woman who died, as mentioned above. Everyone agreed without any disagreement among them that if a man died and left a pregnant woman, and four months and ten days passed, she would not be permissible until she gave birth. So it is known that what is meant is childbirth. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: They shall wait. Waiting means to be patient and patient about marriage, and not to leave the marital home, which is by not leaving it at night. God Almighty did not mention housing for the deceased in His Book as He mentioned it for the divorced woman in His saying: Lodge them (al-Talaq 65:6). There is nothing in the wording of the waiting period in the Book of God Almighty that indicates mourning. Rather, He said: They shall wait. So the Sunnah clarified all of that, and the hadiths from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, are consistent that waiting for death is only mourning, which is refraining from adornment and wearing beautiful dyed and perfumed clothing and the like. This is the saying of the majority of scholars. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan said: Mourning is nothing, rather she waits for the husband, and she may adorn herself and use perfume. This is weak because it is contrary to the Sunnah, as we will explain, God willing. It is proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Al-Fari’ah bint Malik ibn Sinan, who had died: Stay in your house until the appointed time comes. She said: So I observed my waiting period for four months and ten days. This is an authentic hadith narrated by Malik on the authority of Saeed bin Ishaq bin Kaab bin Ujrah. It was narrated by Malik, al-Thawri, Wahib bin Khalid, Hammad bin Zaid, Isa bin Yunus, and many others, Ibn Uyaynah, al-Qattan, and Shu’bah. Malik narrated it on the authority of Ibn Shihab, and that is enough for you! Al-Baji said: No one else narrated from him, and Uthman bin Affan adopted it. Abu Omar said: And he ruled with it regarding the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died in her house. It is a well-known hadith that is famous among the scholars of Hijaz and Iraq, that a woman whose husband has died must observe the waiting period in her house and not leave it. This is the opinion of a group of jurists in the regions of Hijaz, Syria, Iraq and Egypt. Dawud used to say that a woman whose husband has died does not have to observe the waiting period in her house and she can observe the waiting period wherever she wants, because residence is only mentioned in the Qur’an for divorced women. His proof is that the issue is a matter of disagreement. They said: This hadith is only narrated by a woman who is not known for carrying knowledge, and requiring residence is requiring a ruling, and rulings are not obligatory except by the text of the Book of God, the Sunnah or consensus. Abu Omar said: As for the Sunnah, it is established, praise be to God, and as for consensus, it is dispensed with by the Sunnah, because if disagreement arises in an issue, the proof is in the opinion of the one who agrees with the Sunnah. And success is from God. And what was narrated from Ali, Ibn Abbas, Jabir and Aisha is similar to what Dawud said, and Jabir bin Zaid, Ata’ and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said the same. Ibn Abbas: God the Almighty said: They shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days, and He did not say: They shall observe their waiting period in their homes, and let them observe their waiting period wherever they wish. It was narrated from Abu Hanifa, and Abd al-Razzaq mentioned that Muammar told us on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah who said: Aisha went out with her sister Umm Kulthum when her husband Talhah ibn Ubaydullah was killed, to Mecca for Umrah, and she used to issue a fatwa for the woman whose husband had died to go out during her waiting period. He said: And al-Thawri told us on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Umar that he heard al-Qasim ibn Muhammad say: The people refused that for her. He said: And Muammar told us on the authority of al-Zuhri who said: Those who were lenient with regard to the woman whose husband had died took the statement of Aisha, and the people of piety and determination took the statement of Ibn Umar. In al-Muwatta’: That Umar ibn al-Khattab used to turn away the women whose husbands had died from the desert and prevent them from performing Hajj. This is an ijtihad from Umar, may God be pleased with him, because he saw that the woman’s waiting period in the house of her deceased husband was obligatory for her, and it is required by the Qur’an and Sunnah, so it is not permissible for her to go out for Hajj or Umrah until… Her waiting period expires, and Malik said: She is returned unless she becomes forbidden. Sixth: If the husband owns the title deed of the house, then the wife has the waiting period in it, and this is the opinion of most of the jurists: Malik, Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and others, based on the hadith of Al-Fari’ah. Is it permissible to sell the house if it was owned by the deceased and the heirs wanted that? The opinion of the majority of our companions is that it is permissible, and the waiting period is stipulated for the woman. Ibn Al-Qasim said: Because she is more entitled to the residence than the creditors. Muhammad Ibn Al-Hakam said: The sale is invalid, because she may have doubts and her waiting period may be extended. The reason for Ibn Al-Qasim’s statement: The most common is safety, and doubt is rare, and that does not affect the invalidity of contracts. If the sale takes place in it with this condition and she has doubts, Malik said in the book of Muhammad: She is more entitled to stay until the doubt ends. It is preferable to us that the buyer has the option to cancel the sale or continue it and not return anything, because he has entered the usual waiting period. If the sale takes place on the condition of removing the doubt, it is invalid. Sahnun said: There is no proof for the buyer even if the doubt extends to five years, because he has entered the waiting period and the waiting period may be five years. Abu Zaid on the authority of Ibn Al-Qasim. Seventh: If the husband has the residence but not the slave, then she has the residence during the waiting period, contrary to Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i: because of what he, peace be upon him, said to the branch, and it is known that her husband does not own the slave of the residence: Stay in your house until the term of the book is fulfilled. It cannot be said that the house was hers, so why did he not say: Stay in your house? For Muammar narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri that she mentioned to the Prophet, peace be upon him, that her husband was killed, and that he left her in a residence that was not hers and she asked his permission, and he mentioned the hadith, and for us from the aspect of meaning that he left a house that he owned to live in with no responsibility for it, so it is necessary for the wife to observe the waiting period in it, the origin of that is if he owned her slave. Eighth: This is if he has paid the rent. As for if he has not paid the rent, then what is in the Mudawwana is that she has no right to reside in the property of the deceased, even if he was wealthy, because her right is only related to what he owns of residency as a complete property, and what he did not pay in exchange for, he did not own as a complete property, but rather he owned the exchange in his hand, and the wife has no right to that except by inheritance without residency, because that is property and not residency. Muhammad narrated on the authority of Malik that the rent is binding on the deceased from his property. Ninth: His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the young woman: Stay in your house until the term of the book is fulfilled. It is possible that he ordered her to do this because her husband had paid the rent for the house, or he had lived in it until his death, or the people of the house permitted her to observe the waiting period in it with or without rent, or whatever God Almighty willed of that which he saw as binding for her to stay in it until her waiting period ended. Tenth: They differed regarding a woman who is forbidden by her husband while she is in a house other than her husband’s house, so he ordered her to return to his residence and residence. Malik ibn Anas, and this was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, may God be pleased with him. Saeed ibn al-Musayyab and al-Nakha’i said: She observes her waiting period wherever the report reaches her, and she does not leave it until the waiting period ends. Ibn al-Mundhir said: Malik’s statement is correct, unless the husband moved her to a place, in which case she must remain in that place. Eleventh: It is permissible for her to go out for her needs from the time of the early morning until the time of calm after the evening prayer, and she does not spend the night in that house. In Bukhari and Muslim, on the authority of Umm Atiyyah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A woman should not mourn for a dead person for more than three days, for a husband, four months and ten days, and she should not wear dyed clothing except a garment made of ‘asab, and she should not apply kohl, nor touch perfume except when she purifies herself with a little costus or nails.” In the hadith of Umm Habibah: It is not permissible for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days except for a husband, four months and ten days. The hadith. Mourning is a woman leaving all adornment from clothing, perfume, jewelry, kohl, and dyeing with henna as long as she is in her waiting period, because adornment is a call to husbands, so she was forbidden from that to cut off the means and to protect the sacred things of God Almighty from being violated. A woman has nothing to do with oiling her head with oil or sherj from perfume. It is said: a woman who has been mourned and mourned. Al-Asma’i said: We did not know of (hadat) and the doer of (ل الل). The source that can be formulated from challenge with the intended that, so it is as if he said: mourning. Twelfth: His, peace be upon him, description of the woman as having faith indicates the validity of one of the two opinions we have regarding a woman of the People of the Book whose husband has died, that she does not have to observe mourning. This is the opinion of Ibn Kinanah and Ibn Nafi’, and Ashab narrated it on the authority of Malik. Abu Hanifa and Ibn al-Mundhir said the same. Ibn al-Qasim narrated on his authority that she must observe mourning like a Muslim woman. Al-Layth, al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, and most of our companions said the same, because it is a ruling of the waiting period, so the woman of the People of the Book is obligatory for a Muslim woman, just as she must live in a home and observe the waiting period. Thirteenth: In his saying, peace be upon him: More than three days except for a husband, there is evidence of the prohibition of Muslim women mourning for anyone other than their husbands for more than three days, and the permissibility of mourning for them for three days, starting with the waiting period from the night that follows it until the end of the third. If her intimate partner dies during the remaining day or night, she cancels it and counts it from the next night. Fourteenth: This hadith, by virtue of its generality, includes all wives whose husbands have died, so it includes female slaves and free women, adults and children, and this is the view of the majority of scholars. Abu Hanifa held that there is no mourning for a female slave or a young girl, as reported by Judge Abu al-Walid al-Baji. Ibn al-Mundhir said: As for the female slave who is a wife, she is included in the group of husbands and in the generality of the reports, and this is the view of Malik, al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr and the people of opinion. I do not remember any disagreement on this from anyone, nor do I know of them differing about mourning for the mother of a child if her master dies, because she is not a wife, and the hadiths only came about husbands. Al-Baji said: If the young girl is one of those who understand the commands and prohibitions and adheres to what is set for her, she is commanded to do so, and if she does not realize any of that due to her young age, Ibn Muzain narrated on the authority of ‘Isa that her family should avoid everything that an adult woman avoids, and that is obligatory for her. The evidence for the obligation of mourning for a young girl is what was narrated that a woman asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about her daughter whose husband had died and she complained about her eyes, should she apply kohl to them? The Prophet said: May God bless him and grant him peace, not twice or three times. He always said no, and he did not ask about her age. If the ruling differed between young and old, he would have asked about her age so that the ruling could be clarified. Delaying clarification in such a case is not permissible. Also, every woman who is required to observe the waiting period due to death is required to observe mourning, just like an adult woman. Fifteenth: Ibn al-Mundhir said: I do not know of any disagreement that dyeing is included in the category of forbidden adornments. They agreed that it is not permissible for her to wear dyed or saffron-colored clothes, except for what is dyed black, as it was permitted by Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Malik, and al-Shafi’i, and al-Zuhri disliked it. Al-Zuhri said: Do not wear a garment made of ‘asab, which is contrary to the hadith. In al-Mudawwanah, Malik said: Do not wear the thin ‘asab of Yemen, and he was generous in his thick garments. Ibn al-Qasim said: Because its thin garments are like dyed garments, and thin and thick garments of silk, linen, and cotton are worn. Ibn al-Mundhir said: Everyone from whom I have memorized permitted wearing white. Judge ‘Iyad said: al-Shafi’i held that every dye is an adornment that the one who wears it should not touch, whether it is thin or thick. Judge ‘Abd al-Wahhab said something similar: All colors that women adorn themselves with for their husbands should be avoided by the one who wears it. Some of our later sheikhs said: Good white that is used for adornment, as well as thin black. Ibn Al-Mawaz narrated on the authority of Malik: Do not wear jewelry, even if it is iron. In short, everything that a woman wears in the manner in which jewelry is used for adornment, she should not wear iron. Our companions did not specify jewels, rubies, and emeralds, which are included in the meaning of jewelry, and God knows best. Sixteenth: People agreed that mourning is obligatory for a woman whose husband has died, except for Al-Hasan, who said: It is not obligatory. He cited as evidence what was narrated by Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Haad, “On the authority of Asma bint Umays, who said: When Ja’far bin Abi Talib was killed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: ‘Put on three days of mourning, then do as you wish.’ Al-Mundhir said: Al-Hasan Al-Basri was among the scholars who did not believe in mourning. He said: A woman who has been divorced three times and a woman whose husband has died should apply kohl, dye her hair, and do as they wish. The reports from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding mourning have been established, and no one who has received them has the right to accept it. Perhaps Al-Hasan did not receive them, or they did, so he interpreted them based on the hadith of Asma bint Umays, who asked permission from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to mourn for Ja’far, who was his wife. He gave her permission for three days, then after three days he sent to her to purify herself and apply kohl. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The scholars rejected this hadith with various aspects. Ahmad bin Hanbal said: This strange hadith is not to be taken into account. Ishaq said the same.. Seventeenth: Malik and Al-Shafi’i held that there is no mourning for a woman who has been divorced revocably or irrevocably once or more, which is the opinion of Rabi’ah and Ata’. The Kufians, Abu Hanifa and his companions, Al-Thawri, Al-Hasan bin Hayy, Abu Thawr and Abu Ubaid, held that a woman who has been divorced three times must mourn, which is the opinion of Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab, Sulayman bin Yasar, Ibn Sirin and Al-Hakam bin Uyaynah. Al-Hakam said: It is more emphatic and more severe for her than for a woman whose husband has died, and from the point of view of meaning, they are both in a waiting period by which lineage is preserved. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and Ishaq said: The precaution is for the divorced woman to avoid adornment. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: In the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “It is not permissible for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to mourn for a dead person for more than three days except for a husband, for whom it is four months and ten days,” is evidence that a woman who has been divorced three times while the divorced husband is alive does not have to mourn. Eighteenth: The scholars agreed that if a man divorces his wife with a divorce in which he has the right to take her back, and then dies before the end of the waiting period, she must observe the waiting period of death and inherit from him. They differed regarding the waiting period of a woman who has been divorced three times due to illness. A group said that she must observe the waiting period of divorce. This is the opinion of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ya’qub, Abu Ubaidah, and Abu Thawr. Ibn Al-Mundhir said, And we say the same, because God Almighty made the waiting period of a woman who has been divorced menstrual cycles. They agreed that if a woman who has been divorced three times dies, the divorcer does not inherit from her, because she is not a wife, and if she is not a wife, then he is not her husband. Al-Thawri said: She must observe the maximum of the two waiting periods. Al-Nu’man and Muhammad said: She must observe four months and ten days, completing three menstrual cycles. Nineteenth: They differed concerning a woman who is informed of her husband’s death or divorce. A group said: The waiting period in divorce and death is from the day he dies or divorces her. This is the opinion of Ibn Umar, Ibn Mas’ud, and Ibn Abbas. Masruq, Ata’, and a group of the Tabi’un said the same. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Ubaid, Al-Thawri, Abu Thawr, the People of Opinion, and Ibn Al-Mundhir agreed with it. There is a second opinion, which is that her waiting period is from the day she is informed of the report. This opinion was narrated from Ali, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatada, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and Jalas bin Amr said the same. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Umar bin Abdul Aziz said: If evidence is established, her waiting period is from the day he dies or divorces her. If no evidence is established, then it is from the day the report reaches her. The first is correct, because God Almighty has made the waiting period conditional on the death or divorce. If she knew of his death and left the mourning period, the waiting period would have expired. If she left it without knowing, then it is easier. Do you not see that the waiting period of a young girl ends and there is no mourning for her? Also, the scholars have agreed that if she was… A pregnant woman who does not know about her husband’s divorce or death, then gives birth, her waiting period has expired. There is no difference between this issue and the disputed issue. The view of those who say that the waiting period is from the day she is informed of the report is that the waiting period is an act of worship by refraining from adornment, and that is not valid except with intention and purpose, and it only occurs after knowledge, and God knows best. The twenty-first: The waiting period of death is obligatory for a free woman, a slave woman, a young woman, an old woman, a woman who has not reached menstruation, a woman who has menstruated, a woman who has despaired of menstruation, and a woman of the Book, whether she has been consummated with or not, if she is not pregnant. The waiting period of all of them except the slave woman is four months and ten days, due to the generality of the verse in the words of God Almighty: They shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days. The waiting period of a slave woman whose husband has died is two months and five nights. Ibn al-Arabi said: Half the waiting period of a free woman, by consensus, except for what is narrated from al-Asam, who equated a free woman with a slave woman, and the consensus preceded him, but due to his deafness he did not hear. Al-Baji said: We do not know of any disagreement on that except what is narrated from Ibn Sirin, and it is not proven that he said: Her waiting period is the waiting period of a free woman. I said: The statement of Al-Asamm is correct from the point of view of consideration, because the verses that were reported regarding the waiting period for death, divorce by months, and menstrual periods are general with regard to the slave woman and the free woman, so the waiting period for the free woman and the slave woman are the same according to this consideration, because there is no distinction between the free woman and the slave woman in the generalities, and just as the slave woman and the free woman are equal in marriage, so too are they equal in the waiting period, and God knows best. Ibn Al-Arabi said: It was narrated from Malik that the woman of the People of the Book observes a waiting period of three menstrual periods, because with them the womb is healed, and this is very corrupt on his part, because he excluded her from the generality of the verse regarding death, although it is part of it, and included her in the generality of the verse regarding divorce, although it is not part of it. I said: Accordingly, based on what is in the Mudawwana, there is no waiting period for her if she has not been consummated with, because he knows that her womb is pure. This requires that she marry a Muslim or someone else after his death, because if she does not have a waiting period for death or a waiting period for consummation, then she is permissible for husbands. Twenty-first: They differed regarding the waiting period of a woman whose master dies. A group said: Her waiting period is four months and ten days. This was said by a group of the Tabi’in, including Sa’id, Al-Zuhri, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and others. Al-Awza’i and Ishaq said the same. Abu Dawud and Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Qubaysah bin Dhu’ayb on the authority of Amr bin Al-Aas, who said: Do not confuse us with the Sunnah of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The waiting period of a woman whose husband dies is four months and ten days. He meant the mother of a woman. The wording of Abu Dawud. Al-Darqutni said: It is suspended, and this is correct. It is mursal because Qubaysah did not hear Amr. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: Ahmad and Abu Ubaid declared this hadith weak. It was narrated on the authority of Ali and Ibn Mas’ud that her waiting period is three menstrual periods. This is the opinion of Ata’, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Sufyan Al-Thawri, and the people of opinion. They said: Because it is a waiting period that is required in a state of freedom, it must be a complete waiting period. Its origin is the waiting period of a free woman. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Abu Thawr said: Her waiting period is one menstrual period, which is the opinion of Ibn Umar. It was narrated on the authority of Tawus said that her waiting period is half the waiting period of a free woman whose husband has died, and Qatada said the same. Ibn al-Mundhir said: I say the same as Ibn Umar, because it is the least of what has been said and there is no Sunnah to follow in it nor consensus to rely on. He mentioned their disagreement regarding her waiting period for emancipation as it is for death, except that al-Awza’i made her waiting period for emancipation three menstrual periods. I said: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of Malik, because God Almighty said: Divorced women shall wait, concerning themselves, three menstrual periods, so He stipulated that the waiting period for menstrual periods should be for a divorce, so it is negated by that that it could be for anything else. And His statement: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait, concerning themselves, four months and ten days, so He made the obligation of that conditional on the one who is waiting being a wife, so it indicates that the slave girl is different from her. Also, this is a slave girl who was cohabited with by the right hand, so her purification was by a menstrual period, the origin of that is the slave girl. Twenty-second: If this is proven, is the waiting period of the mother of the child purely a period of purification or a period of waiting? What Abu Muhammad mentioned in his Ma’unah is that the menstruation is a period of purification and not a period of waiting. In Al-Mudawwanah, the mother of the child must observe a period of waiting, and her waiting period is one menstrual period like the waiting period of a free woman, which is three menstrual periods. The benefit of the disagreement is that if we say it is a period of waiting, then Malik said: I do not like her to promise anyone to marry her until she menstruates once. Ibn Al-Qasim said: It has reached me that he said: She should not spend the night except in her house. So he established the ruling of the waiting period for her waiting period. Twenty-third: The scholars have agreed that the maintenance of a woman who has been divorced three times or who has been divorced by her husband again while she is pregnant is obligatory, based on the Almighty’s saying: And if they are pregnant, then spend on them until they give birth (al-Talaq 65:6). They differed about the obligation of maintenance for a pregnant woman whose husband has died. A group said: She is not entitled to maintenance. This is what Jabir ibn Abdullah, Ibn Abbas, Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, Ata’, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Abdul Malik ibn Ya’la, Yahya al-Ansari, Rabia, Malik, Ahmad, and Ishaq said. Abu Ubaid narrated this from the people of opinion. There is a second opinion, which is that she is entitled to maintenance from all of her wealth. This opinion was narrated from Ali and Abdullah, and Ibn Umar, Shuraih, Ibn Sirin, al-Sha’bi, Abu al-Aaliyah, al-Nakha’i, Jalas ibn Amr, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, Ayoub al-Sakhtiyani, Sufyan al-Thawri, and Abu Ubaid said the same. Ibn al-Mundhir said: I agree with the first opinion, because they agreed that the maintenance of anyone who was obligated to provide for him while he was alive, such as his young children, his wife, and his parents, is dropped from him. Likewise, the maintenance of his pregnant wife is dropped from him. Judge Abu Muhammad said: Because the maintenance of pregnancy is not a fixed debt, so it is attached to his wealth after his death, as evidenced by the fact that it is dropped from him. Insolvency, then it is more appropriate for it to be dropped by death. Twenty-fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Four months and ten days. The scholars differed regarding the four months that God made the time for the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died. Does she need to menstruate during them or not? Some of them said: She is not absolved if she was someone who had intercourse with him except by a menstrual period that she brings during the four months and ten days, otherwise she is doubtful. Others said: She does not have to do more than four months and ten days, unless she has clear doubts about herself, because menstruation is usually required during this period in women’s affairs, unless the woman is someone who menstruates or someone who knows about herself or it is known about her that her menstruation does not come to her except during more than this period. Twenty-fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And ten. Waki’ narrated on the authority of Abu Ja’far al-Razi on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Asan on the authority of Abu al-A’lya that he was asked: Why were ten added to the four months? He said: Because the soul is breathed into it. This will be explained in Hajj, God willing. Al-Asma’i said: It is said that the child of every pregnant woman runs halfway through her pregnancy, running. Another said: She ran, so she is running. He recited: And the center of frankness, her father, the girl and the boy are humiliated for her Al-Khattabi said: His saying and ten means - and God knows best - the days and their nights. Al-Mubarrad said: He made the word ten feminine because what is meant by it is the period, meaning and ten periods, each period of a day and a night, so the night with its day is a known period of time. It was said: He did not say ten to give precedence to the ruling of the nights, since the night precedes the day and the days are included in it. and ten is lighter in wording, so the nights prevail over the days if they meet in the date, because the beginning of the months is at night at the beginning, so when the beginning of the month is the night, the night prevails. You say: We fasted five of the month, so the nights prevail even if the fasting was during the day. Malik, Al-Shafi’i and the Kufians held that what is meant by it are the days and nights. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: If a man contracts marriage with her according to this statement and four months and ten nights have passed, it is invalid until the tenth day has passed. Some of the jurists held that if four months and ten nights have passed, she is permissible for husbands, from the jurists and Abu Bakr Al-Asamm from the theologians, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas. He read (four months and ten nights). God Almighty says: “And when they have reached their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” There are three issues in this: First: God Almighty added a term to them, as it is limited and imposed on their matter, and it is an expression of the expiration of the waiting period. Second: The Almighty’s saying: There is no blame upon you is addressed to all people, and the obligation to adhere to this ruling is for the rulers and guardians, in what they have done He means by it marriage in what is less than that of adornment and abandoning mourning, in a reasonable manner, that is, in what the Shari’ah has permitted of choosing the specific spouses and determining the dowry without directly performing the contract, because it is a right for the guardians as mentioned above. Third: In this verse is evidence that guardians may prevent women from flaunting themselves and looking forward to their husbands during the waiting period. It is a response to Ishaq’s statement that if a divorced woman experiences her third menstrual period, she is divorced and the return of her first husband is cut off, except that it is not permissible for her to marry again until she washes herself. And from Sharik that her husband has the right to return to her unless she washes herself, even after twenty years. God Almighty said: And when they have fulfilled their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves. And reaching the term here is the expiration of the waiting period by her entering the blood from the third menstrual period, and he did not mention washing. So when her waiting period expires, she is permissible for husbands and there is no blame upon her for what she does of that. And the hadith from Ibn Abbas, if it is authentic, may be from him on the recommendation, and God knows best.
2:235: The Almighty’s saying: And there is no blame upon you for that which you express of marriage proposal to women to His saying in a proper manner contains nine issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And there is no blame meaning no sin. And blame is sin, and this is more correct in the Sharia. And it was said: Rather, it is the difficult matter, and this is more correct in the language. Al-Shamakh said: If you ride it up a bay, remember what a wing it has. And his saying: Upon you in what you have presented is addressed to all people, and what is meant by its ruling is the man who in his mind marries a woman in her waiting period, meaning there is no sin in hinting at the engagement during the waiting period of death. And hinting is the opposite of stating clearly, and it is to make the meaning understood by something that is possible for him and for others, and it is from the aspect of something, which is its side, as if he is hovering over something and not showing it. And it was said, it is from your saying I presented the man, meaning I presented him with a gift. And in the hadith: That a group of Muslims presented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr with white clothes, meaning they presented them with gifts, so the one who hints with speech conveys to his companion speech whose meaning is understood. Second: Ibn Atiyah said: The nation has agreed that speaking to a woman in her waiting period in a manner that is explicit about her marriage and drawing attention to it is not permissible. Likewise, the nation has agreed that speaking to her in a manner that is obscene and mentioning intercourse or inciting it is not permissible, and so is what is similar to it. Other than that is permissible. Among the things that bring it closer to being explicit is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Fatimah bint Qays: Be with Umm Sharik and do not get ahead of me with yourself. It is not permissible to hint at proposing to a woman who has been divorced by revocable divorce by consensus because she is like a wife. As for the one who is in the waiting period of separation, the correct view is that it is permissible to hint at proposing to her, and God knows best. Many expressions have been narrated in the interpretation of hinting, the sum of which can be divided into two categories: The first: that he mentions it to her guardian and tells him, Do not get ahead of me with her. The second: that he points to her without an intermediary, and says to her, I want to get married, or, You are beautiful, you are righteous, God is driving good to you, I desire you, and who desires you? You are a good woman, and my need is in women, and if God decrees a matter, it will be. This is the representation of Malik and Ibn Shihab. Ibn Abbas said: There is nothing wrong with him saying, Do not get ahead of me with yourself, and there is nothing wrong with him giving her a gift, and taking care of her during her waiting period if that is his concern. Ibrahim said: It is permissible for him to praise himself and mention his good deeds in a way that hints at marriage, and Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Ali ibn Husayn did so. Kayna bint Hanzala said, “Muhammad ibn `Ali asked permission from me, and my waiting period had not ended since my husband’s death, so he said, ‘I know my kinship to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and my kinship to `Ali, and my position among the Arabs.’ I said, ‘May God forgive you, O Abu Ja`far!’” You are a man who is taken from, you propose to me during my waiting period! He said: I only told you about my kinship to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and to Ali. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered upon Umm Salamah while she was in the waiting period from Abu Salamah and said: I know that I am the Messenger of God and the best of my people is my position. That was a proposal. Al-Daraqutni reported it. A gift to a woman in her waiting period is permissible, but it is an insinuation. This was said by Sahnun and many scholars, and Ibrahim said it. Mujahid disliked that he should say to her: Do not get ahead of me with yourself, and he saw it as a secret promise. Judge Abu Muhammad ibn Atiyah said: I think this is based on the interpretation of the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) statement to Fatimah as being in the form of her opinion about who to marry, not that he wanted her for himself. Otherwise, it is contrary to the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Third: The Almighty’s saying: From the sermons of women. The sermon with a kasra on the kha’ is the action of the suitor in speech, intent, and kindness through an action or saying. It is said: He proposed to her, a sermon, and a man who is a suitor is very active in the sermon. From this is the saying of the poet: The eyes of the suitor are filled with a sigh of relief, saying that I am a suitor, but he lied. He is only asking for a bride from Aleppo Al-Khatib: the suitor. Al-Khatibi: the sermon. Adi bin Zaid said, mentioning Juthayma Al-Abrash’s intention to propose to Al-Zaba’: To my fiancée who betrayed and deceived me, and they are the ones who bring calamity to my life Al-Khattab, the man who proposes to a woman, and it is also said: it is a sermon and his sermon that he proposes to her, and the sermon is an action like sitting and sitting: and the sermon with a damma on the kha is the speech that is said in marriage and other things, Al-Nahhas said: The sermon is what has a beginning and an end, and likewise what is on the basis of an action like eating and pressing. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Or you concealed it within yourselves means you concealed it and concealed it from marrying her after her waiting period had ended. Concealment is covering and concealing. It is said: I concealed it and I concealed it have the same meaning. It is also said: I protected it means I preserved it so that no harm would befall it, even if it was not concealed. From this comes the word hidden eggs and hidden pearls. “I concealed it” means I kept it secret and concealed it. It is also said: I concealed the thing of the objects if I covered it with a garment, house, land, or something similar. I concealed the matter in my soul. It was not heard from the Arabs: I concealed it in my soul. It is said: I concealed the house, the person. Something like this has caused God to separate the wing from whoever wanted to marry a woman in her waiting period with insinuation and concealment. He forbade making promises that are explicitly about marriage and based on it and agreeing on a promise. He permitted it because of His Almighty’s knowledge of the dominance of souls and their ambition and the weakness of humans in possessing them. Fifth: The Shafi’is used this verse as evidence that there is no punishment for insinuation. They said that since God Almighty removed the difficulty of insinuation in marriage, this indicated that insinuation of slander does not require punishment, because God Almighty did not make insinuation in marriage a substitute for explicitness. We said: This is invalid because God Almighty did not permit explicitness of marriage in the engagement, and He permitted insinuation from which marriage is understood. This is evidence that insinuation is understood as slander, and honor must be protected, and this requires the punishment of the one who exposes, lest the immoral people approach taking honor by insinuation from which what is understood is understood by explicitness. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: God knows that you will mention them, meaning either secretly or openly in your souls and with your tongues. So He permitted insinuation without explicitness. Al-Hasan: Its meaning is that you will propose to them. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: But do not make secret appointments with them. That is, in secret. So the letter was deleted because it is one of the verbs that takes two objects, one of which is with a preposition. The scholars differed about the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: secretly. It was said: Its meaning is marriage, meaning that the man does not accept this woman in her waiting period: Marry me, but rather he offers if he wants, and he does not take her covenant and promise not to marry anyone else in secret and concealment. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Malik and his companions, Al-Sha’bi, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Suddi and the majority of the people of knowledge. And secretly according to this interpretation is in the accusative case as a state, meaning secretly. It was said: The secret is adultery, meaning that there should not be an agreement among you to commit adultery during the waiting period and then marry after it. Jabir bin Zaid, Abu Majlaz Lahiq bin Hamid, Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Al-Nakha’i and Al-Dahhak said that its meaning is adultery, meaning do not promise them adultery, and Al-Tabari chose this, and from it is the saying of Al-A’sha: Do not approach a neighbor whose secret is forbidden to you. Marry her or stay forever. Al-Hutay'ah said: Their neighbor's secret is forbidden to them, and their neighbor eats the tip of the bowl. It was said: The secret is intercourse, meaning do not describe yourselves to them with frequent intercourse to encourage them to marry, because mentioning intercourse with someone other than the husband is obscene. This is what Al-Shafi’i said. And Imru’ Al-Qais said: Didn't you claim today that I have grown old and that people like me don't like to keep secrets? Ru'bah said: Stop keeping it a secret after the honeymoon That is, he refrained from having intercourse with her after he had done so regularly. The secret may be the marriage contract, whether secret or public. Al-A’sha said: They will not seek her secret to get rich, nor will they surrender her to make her lose her temper. He meant: They will not ask to marry her because of her great wealth, and they will not hand her over because of her little wealth. Ibn Zayd said that the meaning of his statement: But do not make a secret promise to them is that you do not marry them and conceal that, but when she becomes permissible, you reveal it and consummate the marriage with them. This is the meaning of the first statement. Ibn Zayd, on this, is a speaker of the first statement. He only deviated in calling the marriage contract a promise, and that is confusion. Makki and al-Tha’labi narrated from him that he said: The verse was abrogated by the statement of God Almighty: And do not resolve on the marriage contract. Eighth: Judge Abu Muhammad ibn Atiyah said: The nation agreed on the undesirability of a promise during the waiting period for a woman in herself, for a father in his virgin daughter, and for a master in his female slave. Ibn al-Mawaz said: As for the guardian, who does not have the power to force, I dislike him, and if he declines, I do not annul it. Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: A man who promises during the waiting period and then marries after it: I prefer to separate from her, whether he has intercourse with her or not, and it is one divorce. Then when she becomes permissible, he proposes to her with the suitor. This is the narration of Ibn Wahb. Ashab narrated from Malik that he separates them by affirmation, and Ibn al-Qasim said the same, and Ibn al-Harith narrated the same from Ibn al-Majishun, and he added what necessitates that the prohibition is permanent. Al-Shafi’i said: If he explicitly proposes and she explicitly accepts him, and the marriage contract is not concluded until the waiting period is over, then the marriage is valid, and explicitly stating it to them is undesirable, because the marriage occurred after the engagement, Ibn al-Mundhir said. Ninth: The Almighty’s statement: Unless you say a proper word is an interrupted exception with the meaning of but, like His statement: Except by mistake (An-Nisa’: 92). The proper statement is what is permitted of insinuation. Ad-Dahhak mentioned that the proper statement is to say to the woman in her waiting period: Keep yourself to yourself, for I desire you. So we say to her: And I am like that. This is similar to an appointment. The Almighty’s saying: And do not determine to tie the marriage knot until the prescribed term has been fulfilled. There are nine issues in this. The first: The Almighty’s saying: And do not resolve. The meaning of resolve has already been discussed. It is said: He resolved something and he resolved to do it. The meaning here is: And do not resolve to tie the knot of marriage. It is clear that the Qur’an is the most eloquent speech, so what is mentioned in it is not objectionable, and there is no doubt about its authenticity and eloquence. God Almighty said: And if they decide on divorce (al-Baqarah 2:227), and He said here: And do not resolve to tie the knot of marriage. The meaning is: do not resolve to tie the knot of marriage during the waiting period. Then it was deleted based on what was mentioned above. Sibawayh narrated: So-and-so struck the back and the stomach, meaning on. Sibawayh said: The deletion in these things is not comparable. Al-Nahhas said: It is permissible for it to be (And do not tie the knot of marriage), because the meaning of (resolve) and (conclude) is one, and it is said: (resolve) with a damma on the zay. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Until the Book reaches its term, meaning the completion of the number, and the Book here is the limit that was set and the amount of time that was drawn. He called it a Book because the Book of God has set and imposed it, as He said: The Book of God is upon you (An-Nisa’: 24), and as He said: Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times (An-Nisa’: 103). So the Book is the obligation, meaning until the obligation reaches its term, meaning until the obligation of the Book reaches its term. So the Book, according to this interpretation, means the Qur’an, and according to the first, there is no deletion, so it is more appropriate, and God knows best. Third: God Almighty has forbidden the marriage contract during the waiting period, as He Almighty says: And do not resolve on the marriage contract until the prescribed term has been fulfilled. This is one of the decisive verses that are agreed upon in its interpretation, that the completion of its term is the expiration of the waiting period. He has permitted insinuation during the waiting period, as He says: And there is no blame upon you for that which you make indirect proposal to women. The scholars did not differ in permitting this, and they differed in the wording of insinuation as mentioned above. They differed about a man who proposes to a woman during her waiting period out of ignorance, or makes a promise to her and concludes the marriage contract after the waiting period. This was mentioned in the verse before it. They differed about whether he resolved to conclude the marriage contract during the waiting period and it was discovered and the judge annulled his marriage, and that is before consummation, which is: Fourth: The statement of Umar ibn al-Khattab and a group of scholars that this does not constitute a permanent prohibition and that he is a suitor from among the suitors, and Malik and Ibn al-Qasim said in al-Mudawwana at the end of the chapter that follows (Striking the term of the missing) and Ibn al-Jalab narrated from Malik a narration that the prohibition is permanent in the contract even if it is annulled before consummation, and the reason is that it is a marriage during the waiting period so it is necessary for the prohibition to be permanent with it, its origin is if he consummates the marriage with her, and as for if he contracted during the waiting period and consummated the marriage after its expiration, which is: Fifth: A statement from the people of knowledge said: That is like entering into the waiting period, the prohibition between them is permanent. A group of the people of knowledge said: The prohibition is not permanent because of that. Malik said: The prohibition is permanent. He said once: The prohibition is not clear because of that. The two statements are in the Mudawwana regarding divorce from the Sunnah. As for if he entered into the waiting period, which is: Sixth: Malik, Al-Layth and Al-Awza’i said: They should be separated and she will never be permissible for him. Malik and Al-Layth said: Nor by right of possession, although they permitted marriage to the woman with whom he committed adultery and they argued that Umar ibn Al-Khattab said: They will never be together. Saeed said: She has her dowry for what he made permissible of her vagina. Malik included it in his Muwatta’ and it will come. Al-Thawri, the Kufians and Al-Shafi’i said: They should be separated and the prohibition will not be permanent, rather their marriage will be annulled and then she will have her waiting period from him, then he will be a suitor from the suitors. They argued that the consensus of the scholars is that if he committed adultery with her, it would not be forbidden for him to marry her, so likewise his intercourse with her during the waiting period. They said: This is the opinion of Ali, mentioned by Abd Al-Razzaq, and he mentioned something similar from Ibn Mas’ud, and from Al-Hasan also, and Abd Al-Razzaq mentioned from Al-Thawri from Ash’ath from Al-Sha’bi from Masruq that Umar went back on that and made them come together. Judge Abu Al-Walid Al-Baji mentioned in Al-Muntaqa and said: The man who marries during the waiting period if he consummates the marriage with her is not free to consummate the marriage with her during the waiting period or after it. If he consummated the marriage with her during The waiting period: The well-known view of the school of thought is that the prohibition is permanent, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said the same. Sheikh Abu al-Qasim narrated in his branch: There are two narrations regarding the woman whom a man marries during the waiting period due to divorce or death, knowing that it is forbidden. One of them is that his prohibition is permanent, as we have mentioned, and the second is that he committed adultery and must be punished, and the child is not attributed to him, and he may marry her when her waiting period has ended. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa said the same. The basis of the first narration, which is the well-known one, is what is proven from the ruling of ‘Umar regarding that, and his implementation of that among the people, and his rulings were widespread and transmitted in the cities, and no one is known to have opposed him, so it is proven that it is a consensus. Judge Abu Muhammad said: This has been narrated from ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, and there is no one who opposes them despite its fame and prevalence, and this is the ruling of consensus. The basis of the second narration is that this is forbidden intercourse, so its prohibition is not permanent, as if she married herself or married for pleasure or committed adultery. Judge Abu al-Hasan said: The well-known view of Malik regarding that is weak from the point of view, and God knows best. Abu ‘Umar narrated: ‘Abd al-Rahman told us: Al-Warith bin Sufyan narrated to us Qasim bin Asbagh, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ismail, on the authority of Naim bin Hammad, on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: It reached Umar bin Al-Khattab that a woman from Quraysh had married a man from Thaqeef during her waiting period. So he sent for them and separated them and punished them and said: Never marry her again and put her dowry in the public treasury. This spread among the people and reached Ali, who said: May God have mercy on the Commander of the Faithful! What is the matter with the dowry and the public treasury! It is only ignorance, so the Imam should return them to the Sunnah. It was said: What do you say about them? He said: She is entitled to the dowry for what he has made permissible of her vagina, and they are to be separated and there is no flogging on them, and she completes her waiting period from the first, then she observes a full waiting period of three menstrual periods from the second, then he may propose to her if he wishes. This reached Umar, so he addressed the people and said: O people, return ignorance to the Sunnah. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: There is no disagreement among the jurists that if a man contracts a marriage contract with a woman while she is in her waiting period from someone else, then the marriage is invalid. In the agreement of Umar and Ali, which negated the punishment for them, there is evidence that an invalid marriage does not require punishment, except that with ignorance of the prohibition, it is agreed upon, and with knowledge of it, it is disputed, and they differed as to whether she observes her waiting period from both of them, and this is the issue of the two waiting periods, which is: Seventh: The Medinans narrated from Malik that she completes the rest of her waiting period from the first, and begins another waiting period from the second. This is the opinion of Al-Layth, Al-Hasan bin Hayy, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. It was narrated from Ali as we mentioned, and from Umar as follows. Muhammad bin Al-Qasim and Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik that her waiting period from the second is sufficient for her from the day he separated from her, whether it was by pregnancy, menstruation, or months. This is the opinion of Al-Thawri, Al-Awza’i, and Abu Hanifa. Their proof is the consensus that the first does not marry her during the rest of her waiting period from him, so this indicates that she is in the waiting period from the second, and if it were not for that, he would have married her during her waiting period from him. The first responded and said: This is not necessary because preventing the first from marrying her during the rest of her waiting period is only required for what follows it from the waiting period of the second, and they are two rights that are required of her for two spouses like all the rights of two human beings, one of them does not enter into the other. Malik narrated from Ibn Shihab from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and from Sulayman bin Yasar that Tulayha Al-Asadiyya was married to Rashid Al-Thaqafi, so he divorced her, and she married During her waiting period, Umar ibn al-Khattab beat her and her husband beat her with a whip and separated them. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: Any woman who gets married during her waiting period, if her husband who married her did not consummate the marriage with her, they are separated, then she observes the remainder of her waiting period from the first husband, then the other is a suitor from the suitors. If he consummated the marriage with her, they are separated, then she observes the remainder of her waiting period from the first, then she observes the waiting period from the other, then they will never meet again. Malik said: Saeed ibn al-Musayyab said: And she is entitled to her dowry for what he made permissible of her vagina. Abu Umar said: As for this Talha, she is Talha bint Ubaydullah, sister of Talha ibn Ubaydullah al-Taymi. In some copies of al-Muwatta’, according to the narration of Yahya: Talha al-Asadiyyah. This is a mistake and ignorance, and I do not know anyone who said it. Eighth: His saying, So Umar struck her with the whip and her husband struck her with blows, meaning as punishment for what they had committed of the forbidden, which is intercourse during the waiting period. Al-Zuhri said: I do not know how many lashes that amounted to. He said: And Abd al-Malik struck each of them forty lashes for that. He said: So Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb was asked about that and he said: If you had struck the whip, you would have been flogged twenty! Ibn Habib said about a woman who gets married during her waiting period and a man touches her, kisses her, has intercourse with her, winks at her, or looks at her with pleasure, that the punishment is upon both spouses, as well as upon the guardian and the witnesses, and upon whoever among them knows that she is in her waiting period. And whoever among them is ignorant of that, there is no punishment upon him. Ibn Al-Mawaz said: The spouses are to be flogged the prescribed punishment if they did that intentionally, so Ibn Habib’s statement is to be interpreted as referring to whoever knew about the waiting period, and perhaps he was ignorant of the prohibition and did not intentionally commit the prohibited act, so he is the one who is to be punished. Accordingly, Umar’s beating of the woman and her husband with whips was a lashing, and it is that they knew about the prohibition and rushed into committing the prohibited act out of boldness and daring. Sheikh Abu Al-Qasim said: There are two narrations regarding intentionality, one of them is to be flogged, and the second is to be punished but not flogged. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: And know that God knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him. This is the ultimate warning against falling into what He has forbidden.
2:236: It contains eleven issues: The first is the saying of God the Almighty: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women. This is also one of the rulings on divorced women, and it is the beginning of the report of removing the hardship from the divorced man before consummation and intercourse, whether a dowry was imposed or not. And when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade marriage for the sake of taste and satisfying desire, and commanded marriage to seek protection and seek God’s reward and intend to maintain good health, it occurred to the souls of the believers that whoever divorces before consummation has committed a part of this disliked thing, so the verse was revealed removing the blame in that if the origin of the marriage was for a good purpose.
