And the saying: There is no blame upon you means there is no request for the entire dowry, but you have half of the dowry imposed for the one for whom it was imposed, and enjoyment for the one for whom it was not imposed. And it was said: Since the matter of the dowry is confirmed in the Shari’ah, it may be imagined that there must be a dowry, either a specified dowry or a dowry similar to it, so the hardship was removed from the divorced man at the time of divorce even if there was no dowry in the marriage. And some people said: There is no blame upon you means that you send the divorce during the time of menstruation, unlike the woman who has been consummated with, since the woman who has not been consummated with has no waiting period.. The second: There are four types of divorced women: a divorced woman who has been consummated with and whose dowry has been prescribed, and God mentioned her ruling before this verse, and that nothing of the dowry is taken back from her, and that her waiting period is three menstrual periods; a divorced woman who has not been consummated with and who has not been consummated with, so this verse is about her and she has no dowry, rather the Lord Almighty commanded that she be given enjoyment, and He explained in Surat Al-Ahzab that if a woman who has not been consummated with is divorced, then there is no waiting period for her, and this will come; a divorced woman who has been consummated with and who has not been consummated with, He mentioned her after this verse when He said: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have specified for them a dowry, and a divorced woman who has been consummated with and whose dowry has not been prescribed, God mentioned her in His saying: And for whatever you have enjoyed of them, give them their due compensation (An-Nisa’: 24), so God Almighty mentioned in this verse and the one after it a divorced woman before consummation and before the prescribed dowry, and a divorced woman before consummation and after the prescribed dowry, so He gave the first the enjoyment, and gave the second half of the dowry because of the wife’s annulment of the contract, and He described the permissibility that occurred to the husband through the contract, and He met the consummation with the dowry. the duty. Third: Since God Almighty divided the status of the divorced woman here into two categories: a divorced woman for whom a dowry was named, and a divorced woman for whom no dowry was named, this indicates that the marriage of delegation is permissible, which is every marriage contracted without mentioning the dowry, and there is no disagreement about it, and the dowry is imposed after that. If it is imposed, it is attached to the contract and is permissible. If it is not imposed for her and the divorce takes place, no dowry is required by consensus, as stated by Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi. Al-Mahdawi narrated from Hammad Ibn Abi Sulayman that if he divorced her and did not consummate the marriage with her and no dowry was imposed for her, he is forced to pay half of the dowry of her peers. If it was imposed after the marriage contract and before the divorce occurred, Abu Hanifa said: It is not divided by the divorce, because it was not required by the contract. This is contrary to the apparent meaning of God Almighty’s statement: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have specified for them a dowry (al-Baqarah 2:237), and also contrary to analogy, because the dowry after the contract is attached to the contract, so it must be divided by the divorce. Its origin is the dowry connected to the contract. He was asked about a man who married a woman for whom he did not specify and he did not consummate the marriage with her until he died. Ibn Mas`ud said: She has the same dowry as her other wives, neither too much nor too much, and she has to observe the waiting period and inherit. Then Ma`qil ibn Sinan al-Ashja`i stood up and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled in the case of Baru` bint Washiq, a woman from among us, as you ruled. Ibn Mas`ud was happy with that. Al-Tirmidhi said: The hadith of Ibn Mas`ud is a good and authentic hadith. It has been narrated from him through more than one chain of transmission. This is the practice of some of the scholars among the Companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others. This is what al-Thawri, Ahmad, and Ishaq say. Some of the scholars among the Companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, including Ali ibn Abi Talib, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn `Umar, said: If a man marries a woman but does not consummate the marriage with her and does not set a dowry for her until he dies, they say: She has the inheritance and no dowry, and she has to observe the waiting period. This is the opinion of al-Shafi`i. He said: If the hadith of Yaru` bint Washiq had been proven, then it would have been evidence in what was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is narrated from al-Shafi`i that he returned to Egypt after this opinion, and he said the hadith of Baru` bint Washiq. I said: There is a difference of opinion regarding the authenticity of the hadith of Baru’. Judge Abu Muhammad Abdul Wahhab said in his explanation of the epistle of Ibn Abi Zayd: As for the hadith of Baru’ bint Washiq, it was rejected by the preservers of hadith and the imams of the people of knowledge. Al-Waqidi said: This hadith occurred in Madinah and none of the scholars accepted it. Al-Tirmidhi authenticated it as we mentioned from him and Ibn Al-Mundhir. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The same statement of Abdullah Ibn Mas’ud has been proven from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we say the same. It was mentioned that it is the statement of Abu Thawr and the people of opinion. It was mentioned from Al-Zuhri, Al-Awza’i, Malik and Al-Shafi’i the same statement of Ali, Zayd, Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar. There is a third opinion on the issue, which is that there is no inheritance until there is a dowry, as Masruq said. I said: And the proof for what Malik went to is that it is a separation in a marriage before the obligation, so no dowry is required for it, its origin is divorce, but if the hadith is authentic, then the analogy in its opposition is invalid, and Abu Muhammad Abdul Hamid narrated from the school what agrees with the hadith, and praise be to God, and Abu Omar said: The hadith of Baru’ narrated by Abdul Razzaq from Ath-Thawri from Mansur from Ibrahim from Alqamah from Ibn Masoud, the hadith, and in it: So Muqal bin Sinan stood up, and Ibn Al-Mahdi said in it from Ath-Thawri from Firas from Al-Sha’bi from Masruq from Abdullah and said: Muqal bin Yasar, and the correct opinion in my opinion is the opinion of the one who said Muqal bin Sinan, not Muqal bin Yasar, because Muqal bin Yasar is a man from Muzaynah, and this hadith only came about a woman from Ashja’, not from Muzaynah, and Dawud narrated it likewise from Al-Sha’bi from Alqamah, and in it: So some people from Ashja’ said and Muqal bin Sinan was killed on the day of Al-Harrah, and on the day of Al-Harrah the poet says: Are not those the Ansar crying over their leaders and the bravest crying over Muqal bin Sinan? Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Unless you have touched them (ma) means who, that is, if you divorced the women whom you have not touched, and (tamsuhunna) was read with the opening of the ta’ from the triliteral, and this is the reading of Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Asim, and Ibn Amir, and Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read (tamaasuhunna) from the mufa’ala, because intercourse was done by them, and in the chapter of mufa’ala the fa’il may appear with the meaning of fa’ala, such as taraqat an-na’l, and `aqabat al-lis, and the first reading requires the meaning of mufa’ala in this chapter with the passive meaning of touch, and Abu Ali preferred it, because the verbs of this meaning came in the triliteral with this weight, it came: nakaah, safd, qara’, daftu, and daraba al-fahl, and both readings are good, and (aw) in (aw fardaw) it was said that it is in the meaning of waw, that is, that is, unless you touched them and did not impose for them, like the Almighty’s saying: And how many a town have We destroyed, and Our punishment came to it by night or while they were asleep (al-A’raf 7:4) ], meaning those who say: And His statement: And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more (al-Saffat 37:147) meaning and more. And His statement: And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate (al-Insan 76:24) meaning an ingrate. And His statement: And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy (An-Nisa’: 43), meaning and one of you comes from the privy while you are ill or travelling. And His statement: Except what their backs carry or their entrails or what is mixed with a bone (al-An’am 6:146), and what was like it. This is supported by the fact that the Most High conjoined to it after that what was imposed, then it is for her, so He said: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry, so if the first had been to clarify the divorce and what was imposed for her before touching, He would not have repeated it. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And provide for them: meaning give them something that will be a provision for them. Ibn Umar, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Abu Qilabah, Al-Zuhri, Qatada, Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim interpreted it as obligatory, while Abu Ubaid, Malik ibn Anas and his companions, Judge Shuraih and others interpreted it as recommended. The people of the first opinion adhered to the requirement of the command, and the people of the second opinion adhered to the Almighty’s saying: It is a duty upon the doers of good and upon the righteous. If it were obligatory, He would have applied it to all of creation. The first opinion is more appropriate, because the generality of the command to provide for them in His saying: Provide for them and adding the provision to them with the lam of ownership in His saying: And for the divorced women there is provision is more apparent in the obligation than in the recommendation. His saying: upon the righteous is an emphasis on its obligation, because everyone must fear God in associating partners with Him and disobeying Him. The Almighty said in the Qur’an: A guidance for the righteous (al-Baqarah 2:2). Seventh: They differed regarding the pronoun attached to his saying, And provide for them. Who is meant by it from the women? Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, Jabir bin Zaid, Al-Hasan, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ata’, Ishaq, and the people of opinion said: Mut’ah is obligatory for the divorced woman before consummation and the obligatory marriage, and it is recommended for others. Malik and his companions said: Mut’ah is recommended for every divorced woman, even if he has intercourse with her, except for the one with whom he has not consummated the marriage and has imposed a marriage contract for her. What he imposed for her is sufficient for her and there is no Mut’ah for her. Abu Thawr said: Mut’ah is due to every divorced woman. The people of knowledge agreed that the one for whom he has not imposed a marriage contract and has not consummated the marriage contract has nothing but Mut’ah. Al-Zuhri said: The judge shall rule for her. The majority of people said: He shall not rule for her. I said: This consensus is only for the free woman. As for the slave woman, if she is divorced before the obligatory marriage contract and touching, the majority are of the opinion that she is entitled to Mut’ah. Al-Awza’i and Al-Thawri said: There is no Mut’ah for her because she belongs to her master and he is not entitled to money in return for the harm caused to his slave woman by the divorce. As for the connection of Malik’s school of thought, Ibn Sha’ban said: Mut’ah is due in return for the grief of divorce. Therefore, the woman who has been divorced by khul’, the woman who has been divorced by mutual consent, and the woman who has been cursed has no Mut’ah before consummation or after it, because she is the one who chose the divorce. Al-Tirmidhi, Ata’, and Al-Nakha’i: There is a pleasure for the divorced woman. The people of opinion said: There is a pleasure for cursing. Ibn al-Qasim said: There is no pleasure in a dissolved marriage. Ibn al-Mawaz said: Nor in what annulment enters after the validity of the contract, such as one of the spouses owning the other. Ibn al-Qasim said: The origin of that is the saying of God Almighty: And divorced women shall have a provision according to what is acceptable. So this ruling is specific to divorce and not annulment. Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Malik that the woman who has the choice has the pleasure, unlike the slave woman who is freed under the slave and she chooses herself, so she has no pleasure. As for the free woman, she has the choice or she owns or marries a slave woman and she chooses herself in all of that, so she has the pleasure, because the husband is a reason for separation. Eighth: Malik said: There is no known limit for the pleasure according to us, whether it is little or much, and people have differed on this. Ibn Omar said: The minimum that is sufficient for the pleasure is thirty dirhams or something similar. Ibn Abbas said: The highest pleasure is a servant, then clothing, then maintenance, a gift, the middle of which is a shield, a veil, and a blanket. Abu Hanifa said: That is the lowest. Ibn Muhayriz said: The owner of the office must pay three dinars, and the slave must pay the pleasure. Al-Hasan said: Each one is given pleasure according to his capacity, this one with a servant, this one with clothing, this one with a garment, and this one with maintenance. Malik bin Anas said the same, and it is required by the Qur’an, for God Almighty did not determine it or limit it, but rather said: The wealthy one must pay according to his capacity, and the poor one must pay according to his capacity. Al-Hasan bin Ali prohibited twenty thousand and a skin of honey, and Shuraih was given pleasure with five hundred dirhams. It has been said that the woman’s condition is also taken into consideration, as some Shafi’is said. They said: If we considered the man’s condition alone, it would follow that if he married two women, one of whom was noble and the other lowly, then divorced them before touching them and did not name them, They should be equal in enjoyment, so the inferior woman should have what the noble woman should have. This is contrary to what God Almighty said: Provision according to what is acceptable. It is necessary from this that if a wealthy man of great wealth marries a inferior woman, he should have the same status as hers, because if he divorces her before consummation and the obligation, the enjoyment is obligatory on him according to his situation, the dowry of hers. So the enjoyment according to this is multiples of the dowry of hers. So she is entitled before consummation to multiples of what she is entitled to after consummation of the dowry of her like which is vulgarity, which is intercourse. The people of opinion and others said that the enjoyment of the one who is divorced before consummation and the obligation is half the dowry of her like, nothing more, because the dowry of her like is due by the contract, and the enjoyment is part of the dowry of her like, so it is obligatory for her just as half of the specified amount is obligatory if he divorces before consummation. This is refuted by God Almighty’s statement: Upon the wealthy is his ability, and on the poor is his ability. This is evidence of rejecting the limitation, and God knows the truth of matters. Al-Tha’labi mentioned a hadith in which he said: There is no blame upon you if you divorce women was revealed about a man from the Ansar who married a woman from Banu Hanifa and did not specify a dowry for her, then he divorced her before touching her, so the verse was revealed. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Enjoy her even with your skullcap. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Suwaid bin Ghafla who said: Aisha al-Khathamiyya was with al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abi Talib. When Ali was killed and al-Hasan was pledged allegiance to as caliph, she said: May the caliphate be yours, O Commander of the Faithful! He said: Ali will be killed and you show gloating! Go, for you are divorced three times. So she wrapped herself in her cloak and sat until her waiting period was over. Then he sent her ten thousand as a mut’ah and the remainder of her dowry. She said: A little pleasure from a departed lover When he heard what she said, he wept and said: Had I not heard my grandfather, or had my father told me that he had heard my grandfather say: Any man who divorces his wife three times, whether vaguely or three times during menstruation, she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband, I would take her back. In another narration: The Messenger informed him, so he wept and said: Had I not made the divorce clear to her, I would have taken her back. But I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Any man who divorces his wife three times, one divorce at each period of purity, one divorce at the beginning of each month, or one divorce at the beginning of each month, or divorces her three times all together, she is not permissible for him until she marries another husband.” Ninth: If someone is ignorant of the pleasure until years have passed, then he should pay it to her even if she marries, and to her heirs if she dies. It was narrated by Ibn al-Mawaz on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim. Asbagh said: There is nothing upon him if she dies because it is a consolation for the wife from divorce and that has passed away. The first aspect is that it is a right that is established upon him and is transferred from her to her heirs like all other rights. This indicates its obligation in the school of thought, and God knows best. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: Upon the wealthy is his due, and on the poor is his due is evidence of the obligation of enjoyment. The majority read the wealthy with a silent waw and a broken seen, which is the one whose means are abundant. It is said: So-and-so is satisfied with his means, meaning according to his means. Abu Haywah read with a fatha on the waw and a stressed seen and a fatha on it. Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, Abu Amr, and Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr read his measure with a silent dal in both places. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Asim in the narration of Hafs read with a fatha on the dal in both. Abu Al-Hasan Al-Akhfash and others said, they have the same meaning. It is read in the Book of God: And the valleys flow according to their measure (al-Ra’d 13:17), and its measure, and God Almighty said: And they did not estimate God with His true measure (al-An’am 6:91). If you had moved the dal, it would have been permissible. The poor is the one who has little money, and enjoyment is an accusative of the source, meaning, enjoy them with enjoyment, “with what is known” means with what is known in Sharia is part of economics. Eleventh: The Almighty’s statement: It is a duty upon the doers of good. That is, it is a duty upon them. It is said: I have made the judgment and made it obligatory upon him, meaning, I have made it obligatory. This is evidence of the obligation of pleasure with the command to do it. His statement: It is a duty is an emphasis on the obligation. The meaning of It is a duty upon the doers of good and It is a duty upon the righteous is upon the believers, since no one has the right to say: I am neither a doer of good nor a righteous person. People are commanded to all be doers of good and righteous, so they do good in performing the duties of God and avoid His disobedience so that they do not enter the Fire. So it is a duty upon all of creation to be doers of good and righteous. Truly is an attribute of His statement: Enjoyment, or it is an accusative of the source, and that is more conducive to emphasizing the command, and God knows best.
2:237: It contains eight issues: First: People differed regarding this verse. A group, including Malik and others, said that it excludes the woman who has been divorced after the obligation from the ruling on enjoyment, since it is included in the words of God Almighty: And provide for them. Ibn al-Musayyab said: This verse abrogated the verse in al-Ahzab because that included providing for everyone who had not consummated the marriage with her. Qatada said: This verse abrogated the verse before it. I said: The statement of Saeed and Qatada is questionable, since the condition of abrogation is not present and combining is possible. Ibn al-Qasim said in al-Mudawwana: The enjoyment was for every divorced woman by the words of God Almighty: And for divorced women there is a provision according to what is acceptable and for the one who has not been consummated with by the verse in Surat al-Ahzab. So God Almighty made an exception for the one who was obligated before consummating with her by this verse, and established for the one who was obligated only half of what was obligated. A group of scholars, including Abu Thawr, said: The enjoyment is for every divorced woman in general, and this verse only clarifies that the one who was obligated takes half of what was obligated for her, and the verse did not mean dropping her enjoyment, rather she gets the enjoyment and half of what was obligated. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Then half of what you have imposed meaning that what is due is half of what you have imposed, meaning of the dowry, so half is for the husband and half is for the woman by consensus, and half is a part of two, so it is said: half of the water is the cup, meaning it reaches half of it, and half of the garment is the leg, and everything that reaches half of something else has half of it, and the majority read (Fansu) in the nominative case, and (Fansu) read with the accusative of the fa, meaning then pay half, and Ali bin Abi Talib and Zaid bin Thabit read (Fansu) with the damma of the nun in the entire Qur’an and it is a language, and likewise Al-Asma’i narrated a reading from Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’, it is said: half, half, and half, three languages for half, and in the hadith: If one of you were to spend the equivalent of Mount Uhud in gold, it would not reach the mudd of one of you or half of it, meaning half of it, and half of it, and the half is also the veil. Third: If he gave her a dowry and then divorced her before consummation and the dowry grew in her hand, Malik said: Every commodity that he gave her a dowry or a slave, its growth is for both of them and its decrease is between them, and it is divided between them both, and the woman is not obligated to do anything from it. If he gave her a dowry of gold or silver and she bought with it a slave or a house, or she bought with it from him or someone else perfume or clothes or something else that she has the right to dispose of for her trousseau and to improve her condition in staying with him, then all of that is in the same position as if he gave her a dowry of it, and its growth and decrease are between them. If he divorced her before consummation, then she is only entitled to half of it, and she is not obligated to pay him half of what she received from him. If she bought with it or from him something that is her own, then she must pay him half of the dowry that she received from him. Likewise, if she bought from someone else a slave or a house with the thousand that he gave her a dowry and then he divorced her before consummation, he can take back from her half of the thousand. Fourth: There is no disagreement that if a man has intercourse with his wife and then dies, and he has named for her that she is entitled to that named amount in full and the inheritance, and she must observe the waiting period. They differed about a man who is alone with a woman and does not have intercourse with her until he leaves her. The Kufians and Malik said: He owes the entire dowry, and she must observe the waiting period, based on the hadith of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Rightly-Guided Caliphs ruled that a woman who closed a door or lowered a curtain is entitled to the inheritance and must observe the waiting period. It was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, and it was included by al-Daraqutni and will be mentioned in al-Nisa’. Al-Shafi’i does not require a full dowry or waiting period if there has been no intercourse, based on the apparent meaning of the Qur’an. Shuraih said: I have not heard God Almighty mention in His Book a door or a curtain, if he claims that he did not touch her, then she is entitled to half the dowry. This is the view of Ibn Abbas, and what our scholars have said about this will come in Surat al-Nisa’, God willing, when God Almighty says: And you have gone in unto one another (al-Nisa’: 21). Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Unless they forgive or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives verse Unless they forgive is an interrupted exception, because their forgiveness of half is not the same as their taking, and they forgive means they leave and overlook, and its weight is they do, and the meaning is unless they leave the half that is due to them from the husband, and the nun was not dropped with an because the feminine plural in the present tense is in one state in the nominative, accusative, and jussive, so it is a pronoun and not a sign of inflection, so that is why it was not dropped, and because if the nun was dropped it would be more like the masculine, and the afiyat in this verse are every woman who owns her own affairs, so God Almighty permitted them to drop it after it is due, since He made it their sole right, so they dispose of it by ratifying and dropping it as they wish, if they own their own affairs and are adults, rational, and mature. Ibn Abbas and a group of jurists and followers said: The forgiveness of a virgin who has no guardian is permissible, and Sahnun narrated it in Al-Mudawwana on the authority of someone other than Ibn Al-Qasim after he said: Ibn Al-Qasim mentioned that it is not permissible for her to give half of her dowry, but as for the one who is in the custody of a father or guardian, it is not permissible for her to give half of her dowry, according to one opinion, and there is no disagreement about it as far as I know. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives is conjoined to the first, and this is parsed. Al-Hasan read or he forgives with a silent waw, as if he found the fat-ha in the waw heavy. People differed about what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Jubayr ibn Mut’im that he married a woman from Banu Nasr and divorced her before consummating the marriage with her. He sent her the full dowry and said: I am more deserving of forgiveness than her. God Almighty said: Unless they forgive or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives. And I am more deserving of forgiveness than her. He interpreted the Almighty’s saying: Or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives to mean himself in every situation before and after the divorce, meaning his marriage contract. So when he inserted the lam, he deleted the ha like his saying: For Paradise is the refuge (al-Nazi’at 79:41), meaning his refuge. An-Nabigha said: They have a quality that God has not given to anyone else, such as generosity and patience, and they are not single. Any of their dreams, and also his saying: The marriage contract meaning the marriage contract, and Al-Daraqutni narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet from the hadith of Qutaybah bin Saeed, Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us from Amr bin Shu’ayb from his father from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The guardian of the marriage contract is the husband, and he attributed this to Ali, Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Shuraih, who said: And likewise said: Nafi’ bin Jubayr, Muhammad bin Ka’b, Tawus, Mujahid, Al-Sha’bi, and Saeed bin Jubayr, and others added, and Mujahid and Al-Thawri, and Abu Hanifa chose it, and it is the correct opinion of Al-Shafi’i, all of them do not see a way for the guardian to have anything from her dowry, because of the consensus that if the guardian releases the husband from the dowry before the divorce, it is not permissible, and so it is after it, and they agreed that the guardian does not have the right to give away anything from her money, and the dowry is her money, and they agreed that among the guardians are those whose forgiveness is not permissible, and they are the sons of the uncles and the sons of the brothers, and so is the father, and God knows best, and some of them said he is the guardian, Al-Darqutni also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It is the saying of Ibrahim, Alqamah, and Al-Hasan, and others added, and Ikrimah, Tawus, Ata, Abu Al-Zinad, Zaid bin Aslam, Rabiah, Muhammad bin Kaab, Ibn Shihab, Al-Aswad bin Yazid, Al-Sha’bi, Qatadah, Malik, and Al-Shafi’i in the old, so it is permissible for the father to forgive half of the dowry of his virgin daughter if she is divorced, whether she has reached menstruation or not. Isa bin Dinar said: She does not have to return anything from it to her father, and the evidence that what is meant is the guardian is that God Almighty said at the beginning of the verse: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry, then half of what you specified, so He mentioned the husbands and addressed them with this address, then He said: Unless they forgive, so He mentioned the women: Or he in whose hand is the marriage tie forgives, so it is a third, so it is not returned to the husband who came before unless there was no one else present, and he did exist, and he is the guardian, so it is what is meant. Makki said its meaning and Ibn Al-Arabi mentioned it, and also that God Almighty said: “Unless It is known that not every woman forgives, as the young girl and the one under guardianship cannot be forgiven. So God explained the two categories and said: “Unless they forgive” meaning if they are qualified for that, or he in whose hand is the marriage contract forgives which is the guardian, because the matter is up to him. Likewise, Ibn Wahb, Ashhab, Ibn Abd al-Hakam and Ibn al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Malik that he is the father in his virgin daughter and the master in his female slave. The guardian’s forgiveness is only permissible if he is one of the people of rectitude, and his forgiveness is not permissible if he is foolish. If it is said: We do not accept that he is the guardian, rather he is the husband, and this name is more appropriate for him, because he has more control over the contract than the guardian based on what was mentioned above. The answer is that we do not accept that the husband has more control over the contract than the father in his virgin daughter. Rather, the father of the virgin owns him specifically and not the husband, because what is contracted upon is the virgin’s vagina, and the husband does not have the right to contract upon that, rather the father owns it. Shuraih permitted the brother’s forgiveness of half the dowry, and likewise Ikrimah said: The one who contracted the marriage contract between them is permissible to forgive, whether he was an uncle, father or brother, even if she disliked it. Abu Nahik and Al-Shaabi (or forgive) with a sukoon on the waw, likening it to the alif. Similar to it is the poet’s saying: Amer did not blacken me from inheriting my father, God willing, that I should be elevated by neither mother nor father Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And that you pardon is closer to righteousness. This is a subject and a predicate. The original is ta’afu, the first waw was made quiescent due to the heaviness of its vowel, then it was deleted due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. It is addressed to men and women according to Ibn Abbas, so the males prevailed. The lam means to, meaning closer to righteousness. The majority read ta’afu with two ta’s above it, and Abu Nahik and al-Sha’bi read wa an ta’afu with a ya’, and that refers to the one in whose hand is the marriage contract. I said: He did not read (and that you forgive) with a ta’, so it would be for women. The majority read (and do not forget the favor) with a damma on the waw, and Yahya bin Ya’mar read it with a kasra. Ali, Mujahid, Abu Haywah, and Ibn Abi Ubla read (and do not forget the favor), and it is a reading that has a complete meaning, because it is a place of forgetting, not forgetting, except in the form of a simile. Mujahid said: The favor is the man completing the entire dowry, or the woman leaving the half that is hers. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is Seeing of what you do. This is a statement that includes a promise to the doer of good and deprivation to the one who does not do good, meaning that your forgiveness and your judgment are not hidden from Him.
2:238: It contains eight issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Guard is addressed to the entire nation, and the verse is an order to maintain the establishment of prayers at their times with all their conditions. Maintaining is to persevere in something and to be consistent with it. The middle is the feminine of the middle, and the middle of something is its best and most just. From this is the Almighty’s saying: And thus We have made you a just community (al-Baqarah 2:143), and it has been mentioned before. An Arab said, praising the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O you who are the most honorable of people in your glories and the most generous of people in your pious mother and father And the middle of so-and-so among the people is in the middle of them, meaning he is in their middle. The middle prayer was mentioned separately, and it was previously included in the general prayers in order to honor it, like the Almighty’s saying: And when We took a covenant from the prophets and from you and from Noah (al-Ahzab 33:7), and His saying: Therein is fruit and palm trees with sheaths (al-Rahman 55:68). Abu Ja`far al-Wasiti read and the middle prayer in the accusative case for the purpose of enticement, meaning and they were obligated to pray the middle prayer. Al-Halwani read it likewise: Qaloon read on the authority of Nafi` the middle prayer with a sad because of the proximity of the ta to it, because they are from one area, and they are two languages like the path and the like. Second: People differed in specifying the middle prayer, with ten opinions: The first: It is Dhuhr, because it is the middle of the day, according to the correct of the two opinions, that the day begins with the break of dawn, as mentioned above. We began with Dhuhr because it was the first prayer performed in Islam. Among those who said that it is the middle prayer are Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, `Abdullah ibn `Umar, and `Aisha, may God be pleased with them. What indicates that it is the middle prayer is what `Aisha and Hafsa said when they dictated: Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the `Asr prayer, with the letter waw. It was narrated that it was more difficult for the Muslims, because it came in the middle of the day and their work had exhausted them in their wealth. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Zayd who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pray Dhuhr in the middle of the day, and no prayer was prayed more difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than it. Then this verse was revealed: Guard strictly the prayers, and the middle prayer, and he said: There are two prayers before it and two prayers after it. Malik narrated in his Muwatta’ and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit who said: The middle prayer is the Dhuhr prayer. Al-Tayalisi added: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He prays it at noon. The second: It is the afternoon prayer, because before it are two prayers of the day and after it are two prayers of the night. An-Nahhas said: The best argument for this is that it is called the middle prayer because it is between two prayers, one of which is the first of what was prescribed and the other is the second of what was prescribed. Among those who said that it is the middle prayer are Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Abu Hurairah, and Abu Saeed Al-Khudri. This is what Abu Hanifa and his companions chose, and it was said by Al-Shafi’i and most of the people of Athar. Abdul Malik ibn Habib went to it, and Ibn Al-Arabi chose it in his Qabas and Ibn Atiyyah in his Tafsir. He said: The majority of people agree with this statement, and there are other sayings about it. They argued with the hadiths that were reported in this chapter, narrated by Muslim and others, and the most correct of them is the hadith of Ibn Mas’ud, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The middle prayer is the afternoon prayer. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, who said: A good and authentic hadith. We have already mentioned more than this in Al-Qabas in the explanation of the Muwatta of Malik ibn Anas. Third: It is Maghrib, as stated by Qubaysah bin Abi Dhu’ayb and a group of people. Their evidence is that it is moderate in the number of rak’ahs, neither the least nor the most, and it is not shortened while traveling. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not delay it from its time nor did he hasten it. After it are two loud prayers and before it are two silent prayers. It was narrated from the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The best of prayers with God is the Maghrib prayer. He has not reduced it for a traveler or a resident. God has opened the night prayer with it and concluded the day prayer with it. Whoever prays Maghrib and prays two rak’ahs after it, God will build for him a palace in Paradise. Whoever prays four rak’ahs after it, God will forgive him the sins of twenty years - or he said - forty years.” Fourth: The last Isha prayer, because it is between two prayers that cannot be shortened, and it comes at the time of sleep and it is recommended to delay it, which is difficult, so emphasis was placed on maintaining it. Fifth: It is the Fajr prayer, because before it are two night prayers in which the recitation is loud and after it are two daytime prayers in which the recitation is quiet, and because its time begins while people are asleep, and standing up for it is difficult in the cold season due to the severity of the cold and in the summer season due to the shortness of the night. Those who said that it is the middle one are Ali ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Abbas, and Al-Muwatta’ reported it as a report, and Al-Tirmidhi reported it on the authority of Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas as a suspended report, and it was narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, and it is the opinion of Malik and his companions, and Al-Shafi’i leaned towards it in what Al-Qushayri reported on his authority, and the correct opinion on the authority of Ali is that it is the Asr prayer, and it was narrated on his authority from a well-known and authentic source. Those who said that it is the Fajr prayer used as evidence the words of God Almighty: And stand before God, devoutly obedient, meaning in it, and there is no prescribed prayer in which there is qunut except the Fajr prayer. Abu Raja’ said: Ibn Abbas led us in the Fajr prayer in Basra, and he qunuted in it before bowing and raised his hands, and when he finished he said: This is the middle prayer in which God Almighty commanded us to stand devoutly, and Anas said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, qunuted in a prayer in the Fajr prayer after bowing.” The ruling on Qunut and what the scholars have said about it will come in Al Imran, when God Almighty says: You have no part in the matter (Al Imran 3:128). Sixth: Friday prayer: because it was specifically designated for gathering and the sermon in it, and it was made a holiday. This was mentioned by Ibn Habib and Makki, and Muslim narrated on the authority of Abdullah, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to people who were absent from Friday prayers: I was about to order a man to lead the people in prayer, then I would burn the houses of the men who were absent from Friday prayers.” Seventh: That they are Fajr and Asr together, as stated by Sheikh Abu Bakr Al-Abhari, and he provided evidence with the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Angels take turns among you at night and angels take turns during the day, the hadith narrated by Abu Hurairah, and “Jarir ibn Abdullah narrated: We were sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: You will see your Lord as you see this moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome by a prayer before sunrise and a prayer before its setting,” meaning Asr and Fajr. Then Jarir recited: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting (Ta-Ha 20:130). ‘Ammarah ibn Ru’aybah narrated that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: No one who prays before sunrise and before sunset will enter Hell, meaning Fajr and ‘Asr. And from him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever prays the two cool ones will enter Paradise, all of which is proven in Sahih Muslim and others. We called them the two cool ones because they are They do it in my cold time. Eighth: It is the Isha and Fajr prayers. Abu al-Darda’ may God be pleased with him said during his illness in which he died: “Listen and convey to those behind you. Maintain these two prayers, meaning the Isha and Fajr prayers in congregation. If you knew what was in them, you would come to them even if you had to crawl on your elbows and knees.” This was said by Umar and Uthman. The imams narrated from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that he said: “If they knew what was in the Isha and Fajr prayers, they would come to them even if they had to crawl. He said that they are the most difficult prayers for the hypocrites.” He made the one who prays Fajr in congregation stand for a night and the Isha for half a night. Malik mentioned it as being attributed to Uthman and Muslim raised it. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from him. He said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘Whoever attends the Isha prayer in congregation will have stood for half a night, and whoever prays the Isha and Fajr prayers in congregation will have stood for a night. ’” This is contrary to what Malik and Muslim narrated. Ninth: They are the five daily prayers in their entirety, as stated by Muadh ibn Jabal, because the Almighty’s statement: Guard strictly the prayers includes both obligatory and voluntary prayers, then He specifically mentioned the obligatory prayers. Tenth: It is not specific. Nafi’ said it on the authority of Ibn Umar, and Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham said it. So God the Most High hid it in the prayers just as He hid the Night of Decree in Ramadan, and just as He hid the hour of Friday and the hours of the night in which supplications are answered, so that they may stand at night in the darkness to commune with the Knower of the Unseen. What indicates the correctness of its being vague and not specific is what Muslim narrated in his Sahih at the end of the chapter on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: This verse was revealed: Guard strictly the prayers and the ‘Asr prayer, so we recited it as God willed, then God abrogated it and revealed: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer. A man said: Is it then the ‘Asr prayer? Al-Bara’ said: I have told you how it was revealed and how God the Most High abrogated it, and God knows best. So it follows from this that after it was specified, its specification was abrogated and it was made vague, so the specification was removed, and God knows best. This is the choice of Muslim, because he mentioned it at the end of the chapter, and more than one of the later scholars said it, and it is correct, God Almighty willing, due to the conflict of evidence and the lack of preference, so there is nothing left but to preserve all of them and perform them at their times, and God knows best. Third: This difference in the middle prayer indicates the invalidity of the one who established (and the afternoon prayer) mentioned in the hadith of Abu Yunus, the freed slave of Aisha, when she ordered him to write her a copy of the Qur’an. Our scholars said: Rather, it is like an interpretation from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is indicated by the hadith of Amr ibn Rafi’ who said: Hafsah ordered me to write her a copy of the Qur’an. The hadith, in which it says: So she dictated to me: Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer, which is the afternoon prayer, and stand before God, devoutly obedient. She said: This is how I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reciting it. So her saying (and it is the afternoon prayer) is evidence that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, interpreted the middle prayer from the words of God Almighty by His saying (and it is the afternoon prayer. Nafi’ narrated from Hafsah (and the afternoon prayer) as it was narrated from Aisha and from Hafsah also (the afternoon prayer) without the waw. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: This difference in this additional wording indicates its invalidity and the correctness of what is in the imam of the congregation of the Muslims. And upon it is another argument, which is that whoever said: and the middle prayer And the Asr prayer made the middle prayer different from the Asr prayer, and in this there is a refutation of the hadith of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which was narrated by Abdullah, who said: “The polytheists distracted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of the Confederates from the Asr prayer until the sun turned yellow, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They distracted us from the middle prayer, may God fill their bellies and graves with fire,” the hadith. Fourth: In the Almighty’s saying: And the middle prayer is evidence that the Witr is not obligatory, because the Muslims agreed that the number of obligatory prayers is less than seven and more than three, and there is no odd number between three and seven except five, and the pairs have no middle, so it is proven that they are five. And in the “Hadith of the Night Journey: They are five and they are fifty, the statement does not indicate anything to me.” Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And stand before God, devoutly obedient. It means in your prayer. People differed about the meaning of His saying: devoutly obedient. Al-Sha’bi said: Obeying. Jabir bin Zaid, Ata’, and Sa’id bin Jubayr said the same. Ad-Dahhak said: Every qunut in the Qur’an means obedience. Abu Sa’id said it on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The people of every religion today stand disobediently, so it was said to this nation: Stand before God, obediently. Mujahid said: The meaning of qunut is humble. Qunut is prolonged bowing, humility, lowering the gaze, and lowering the wing. Al-Rabi’ said: Qunut is prolonged standing. Ibn ‘Umar said the same, and he recited: Is he who is devout during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing? (al-Ramzah: 9), and he, peace be upon him, said: The best prayer is prolonged qunut. Narrated by Muslim and others. The poet said: Obedient to God, calling upon his Lord, and deliberately separating himself from people It was mentioned earlier, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Qâtin supplicating, and in the hadith: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for a month, supplicating against Ra’l and Dhakwan. Some people said: Its meaning is he supplicated, and some people said: Its meaning is his prolonged standing. Al-Suddi said: Qâtin slowly means silent. Its evidence is that the verse was revealed to prohibit speaking during prayer, and that was permissible in the early days of Islam. This is the correct view, as narrated by Muslim and others, “On the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: We used to greet the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was praying, and he would respond to us. When we returned from the Negus, we greeted him, but he did not respond to us. O Messenger of God, we used to greet you during prayer and you would respond to us? He said: There is distraction in prayer.” And Zayd bin Arqam narrated, who said: We used to speak during prayer, and a man would speak to his companion while he was beside him in prayer, until the verse, And stand before God, devoutly obedient, was revealed, so we were commanded to be silent and forbidden from speaking. It was said: The root of qunut in the language is to persist in something, and from where the root of qunut in the language is to persist in something It is permissible to call the one who constantly obeys God devout, as well as the one who prolongs standing, reading, and supplication in prayer, or prolongs humility and silence. All of these are performers of qunut. Sixth: Abu Omar said: The Muslims unanimously agreed that speaking intentionally during prayer, if the worshipper knows that he is praying and that it does not improve his prayer, spoils the prayer, except for what was narrated from Al-Awza’i, who said: Whoever speaks to revive a soul or something similar from the serious matters, his prayer is not spoiled by that, and it is a weak statement in view of the statement of God Almighty: And stand before God, devoutly obedient. And Zaid bin Arqam said: We used to speak during prayer until the following was revealed: And stand before God, devoutly obedient. And Ibn Mas’ud said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God has innovated from His command that you not speak during prayer. And the serious hadith is not one for which it is obligatory to interrupt the prayer and for which it is forbidden to start over. So whoever interrupts his prayer because he sees the virtue of reviving a soul or money or something that was for that purpose, he should start over with his prayer, and this is not clear. This is the correct statement in the matter, God willing. Seventh: They differed regarding speaking absentmindedly in it. Malik, Al-Shafi’i and their companions held that speaking absentmindedly in it does not spoil it. However, Malik said: Deliberately speaking during it does not spoil the prayer if it is related to its matter and its improvement. This is the opinion of Rabi’ah and Ibn Al-Qasim. Sahnun narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-Qasim on the authority of Malik, who said: If the imam prayed two rak’ahs with some people and said the salutation while they were absentminded, and they glorified God while he was praying, but he did not understand, and a man from behind him who was with him in the prayer said to him: You did not complete it, so complete your prayer. He turned to the people and said: Is what this person is saying true? They said: Yes. He said: The imam leads them in prayer for the rest of their prayer and they pray with him the rest of their prayer, those who spoke and those who did not speak, and there is nothing wrong with them, and they do in that what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did on the day of Dhu al-Yadayn. This is the statement of Ibn al-Qasim in his book al-Mudawwana and his narration from Malik, and it is the well-known view of the Maliki school of thought, and Ismail ibn Ishaq followed it and provided evidence for it in his book in response to Muhammad ibn al-Hasan. Al-Harith ibn Maskeen mentioned that all of Malik’s companions disagreed with Malik’s statement in the issue of Dhu al-Yadayn except Ibn al-Qasim alone, for he says what Malik says in it, and others reject it and say, this was only in the early days of Islam, but now people have become familiar with their prayer, so whoever speaks in it must repeat it. This is the statement of the Iraqis: Abu Hanifah and his companions and al-Thawri, for they went to the view that speaking in prayer spoils it regardless of whether it was by mistake or intentionally for prayer or for something else, and it is the statement of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Ata’, al-Hasan, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and Qatadah. The companions of Abu Hanifah claimed that this hadith of Abu Hurayrah in the story of Dhu al-Yadayn was abrogated by the hadith of Ibn Mas’ud and Zayd. Ibn Arqam, they said: Even if Abu Hurairah converted late, he sent the hadith of Dhi al-Yadayn as he sent the hadith: Whoever is overtaken by dawn while in a state of ritual impurity, his fast is not valid. They said: He sent many hadiths, and Ali ibn Ziyad mentioned that Abu Qurrah told us that he heard Malik say: It is recommended that if a man speaks during prayer, he should return to it and not continue. He said: Malik told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke and his companions spoke with him on that day because they thought that the prayer had been shortened and that is not permissible for anyone today. Sahnun narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim about a man who prayed alone and finished the four rak’ahs by himself. A man next to him said to him: You only prayed three rak’ahs, so he turned to another and said: Is what this man says true? He said: Yes. He said: His prayer is invalidated and he should not have spoken to him or paid attention to him. Abu Omar said: They used to differentiate in this issue between the imam with the congregation and the one praying alone, so they would permit the imam and those with him to speak about the prayer in a way that they would not permit the one praying alone. Others than these used to interpret Ibn al-Qasim’s answer to the one praying alone in this issue and in the imam and those with him in a different way from his statement in using the hadith of Dhi al-Yadayn, just as Malik’s statement differed in that regard. Al-Shafi’i and his companions said: Whoever deliberately speaks while knowing that he has not completed the prayer and that he is in it, his prayer is invalidated. If he speaks absentmindedly or speaks while thinking that he is not in the prayer, because he has completed it in his mind, then he should continue. Ahmad’s statement differed in this issue. Al-Athram mentioned from him that he said: Whatever a person speaks in his prayer to correct it, his prayer is not invalidated. If he speaks for something other than that, it is invalidated. This is the famous statement of Malik. Al-Kharqi mentioned from him that his doctrine regarding whoever speaks intentionally or absentmindedly, his prayer is invalidated, except for the imam Khasaba, for he speaks for the benefit of his prayer, his prayer is not invalidated. Sahnun made an exception from Malik’s companions. If someone says: If he finishes two rak'ahs of a four-rak'ah prayer and then speaks, the prayer is not invalidated, but if he speaks otherwise, the prayer is invalidated. The correct view is that of Malik in the well-known view, adhering to the hadith and basing it on the general principle of the transgression of rulings and the generality of the Shari'ah, and repelling what is imagined of a specificity since there is no evidence for it. If someone says: The speech was made about prayer and forgetfulness as well, and the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) had said to them: Tasbih is for men and clapping is for women, so why did they not say tasbih? It is said: Perhaps at that time he had not commanded them to do that. If it was as you mentioned, then they did not say tasbih because they imagined that the prayer had been shortened, and this came in the hadith in which he said: And the people quickly went out and said: Has the prayer been shortened? So there was no alternative to speaking for that reason, and God knows best. Some of the opponents said: Abu Hurairah’s statement: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with us may mean that he prayed with the Muslims, although he was not one of them, as was narrated on the authority of An-Nazzal ibn Sabrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: We and you were called Banu Abd Manaf, and today you are Banu Abd God and similar to Banu Abd God. What he meant by that is that he said that to his people, and this is far-fetched, because it is not permissible for him to say that he prayed with us, while he was a disbeliever and not one of the people of prayer, and that would be a lie. The hadith of An-Nazzal is that he was among the people and heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, what he heard. As for what the Hanafis claimed of abrogation and mursal, our scholars and others responded to their statement and invalidated it, especially Al-Hafiz Abu Umar ibn Abd Al-Barr in his book called Al-Tamhid, and he mentioned that Abu Hurairah converted to Islam in the year of Khaybar, and came to Madinah in that year, and accompanied the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for four years, and witnessed the story of Dhu al-Yadayn and attended it, and that it did not happen before Badr as they claimed, and that Dhu al-Yadayn was killed in Badr. He said: And attending Abu Hurairah, the day of Dhi al-Yadayn, is preserved from the narration of trustworthy preservers, and the shortcomings of those who fell short of that are not an argument against those who knew it, preserved it, and mentioned it. Eighth: Qunut: standing, which is one of its divisions according to what Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari mentioned. The Ummah agreed that standing in the obligatory prayer is obligatory for every healthy person who is able to do so, whether he is alone or an imam. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The imam is only appointed to be followed, so if he prays standing, then pray standing. The hadeeth was narrated by the imams, and it is an explanation of the words of God the Most High: And stand before God, devoutly obedient. They differed regarding the healthy follower who prays sitting behind a sick imam who is unable to stand. A group of scholars, indeed the majority of them, permitted that, based on the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding the imam: And if he prays sitting, then pray sitting together. This is the correct view on the issue, as we will explain above, God the Most High willing. A group of scholars permitted the prayer of one who stands behind a sick imam, because each person performs his obligatory prayer according to his ability, following the example of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): If he prayed sitting during his illness in which he died, and Abu Bakr was standing beside him, he would pray with him and the people would stand behind him. He did not refer to Abu Bakr or to them. By sitting, and he completed his prayer with them sitting while they were standing, and it is known that this was from him: after he fell from his horse, so it was known that the second of his actions abrogates the first, Abu Omar said: Among those who went to this school of thought and used this argument as evidence are Al-Shafi’i and Dawud bin Ali, and it is the narration of Al-Waleed bin Muslim and from Malik he said: And I prefer that he stand next to him from those who know the people of his prayer, and this narration is strange from Malik, and a group of the people of Madinah and others said this and it is correct, God willing, because it is the last prayer that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed, and the well-known opinion from Malik is that he does not lead the standing prayer sitting, so if he leads them sitting, his prayer and their prayer are invalidated, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one after me leads the prayer sitting, he said: If the imam is ill, the imam’s prayer is complete and the prayer of those behind him is invalid, he said: And whoever prays sitting without an illness repeats the prayer, this is the narration of Abu Mus’ab in his Mukhtasar from Malik, and based on it, it is obligatory for whoever prays sitting to repeat it in the time and after it, and it was narrated from Malik in this that they repeat it in the time specifically, and the statement of Muhammad bin Al-Hasan in this is like Malik’s famous statement, and he supported his statement and his school of thought with the hadith mentioned by Abu Mus’ab, narrated by al-Daraqutni on the authority of Jabir on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one after me will believe while sitting. Al-Daraqutni said: No one narrated it except Jabir al-Ja’fi on the authority of al-Sha’bi, and his hadith is rejected, mursal and cannot be used as evidence. Abu ‘Umar said: Jabir al-Ja’fi cannot be used as evidence for anything he narrates with a chain of transmission, so how about what he narrates with a mursal? Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: If the imam prays while sitting with healthy and sick people sitting, then his prayer and the prayer of those behind him who are unable to stand are valid and permissible, and the prayer of those who prayed behind him who are ruled to stand is invalid. Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf said: His prayer and their prayer are valid. They said: If he prays while gesturing with people who are bowing and prostrating, it is not permissible for them according to all of them, and the imam’s prayer is valid. Zafar used to say: Their prayer is valid, because they are obligatory and their imam prayed according to his obligation, as al-Shafi’i said: I said: As for what Abu ‘Umar mentioned, And other scholars before and after him that it was the last prayer that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed. I have seen others who disagree with that, who collected the chains of transmission of hadiths in this chapter, and spoke about them and mentioned the differences of opinion among the jurists in that. We will mention what he mentioned in summary so that the truth will become clear to you, God willing, and the correctness of the statement of those who said that the prayer of a healthy follower sitting behind a sick imam is permissible. Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hibban al-Basti mentioned in his authentic Musnad on the authority of Ibn Umar, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with a group of his companions and said: Do you not know that I am the Messenger of God to you? They said: Yes, we bear witness that you are the Messenger of God! He said: Do you not know that whoever obeys me has obeyed God, and part of obeying God is obeying me? They said: Yes, we bear witness that whoever obeys you has obeyed God, and part of obeying God is obeying you. He said: It is part of obeying God that you obey me, and part of obeying me that you obey your leaders. If they pray sitting, then pray sitting.” In his chain of transmission is Uqbah ibn Abi al-Sahba’, and he is trustworthy. Yahya bin Ma’in said: Abu Hatim said: In this report there is a clear statement that the prayer of the followers while sitting if their imam prays while sitting is from the obedience of God Almighty that God has commanded His servants, and in my opinion it is a type of consensus that they agreed to permit it, because four of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, issued fatwas on it: Jabir bin Abdullah, Abu Hurairah, Asid bin Hudhair, and Qais bin Fahd, and no one from the companions who witnessed the descent of the revelation and were protected from distortion and alteration has narrated anything contrary to these four, neither with a continuous nor a disconnected chain of transmission, so it is as if the companions agreed that if the imam prays while sitting, it is upon the followers to pray while sitting, and Jabir bin Zaid, Al-Awza’i, Malik bin Anas, Ahmad bin Hanbal, Ishaq bin Ibrahim, Abu Ayyub Sulayman bin Dawud Al-Hashemi, Abu Khaithama, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad bin Ismail, and those of the companions of hadith who followed them, such as Muhammad bin Nasr and Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Khuzaymah, and this is the Sunnah. It was narrated from the Chosen One, may God bless him and grant him peace, by Anas bin Malik, Aisha, Abu Hurairah, Jabir bin Abdullah, Abdullah bin Omar bin Al-Khattab, and Abu Umamah Al-Bahili. The first person in this nation to invalidate the prayer of a person who is led in prayer while sitting if his imam prays while sitting was Al-Mughira bin Muqsim, a companion of Al-Nakha’i. Hammad bin Abi Sulayman took it from him, then he took it from Hammad and Abu Hanifa, and those of his companions who followed him in it after him. The highest thing they used as evidence for it is what Jabir Al-Nakha’i narrated from Al-Sha’bi, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one after me believes while sitting. If its chain of transmission was authentic, it would be mursal, and a mursal report and what is not narrated are the same in our judgment. Then Abu Hanifa says: I have not seen anyone better than Ata’ among those I met, nor anyone more lying than Jabir Al-Ju’fi among those I met. I have never brought him any opinion except that he brought me a hadith about it. He claimed that he had so-and-so thousand hadiths from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he did not utter. So this is Abu Hanifa criticizing Jabir. Al-Ja’fi and his denial of it against the statement of those of his companions who adopted his doctrine. Abu Hatim said: As for the prayer of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, during his illness, the reports came in general and brief, and some of them are detailed and clear. In some of them: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and sat next to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr was following the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people were following Abu Bakr. In some of them: He sat to the left of Abu Bakr, and this is explained. In it: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with the people while sitting, and Abu Bakr was standing. Abu Hatim said: As for the generality of this report, Aisha narrated this prayer to this point, and the end of the story with Jabir bin Abdullah: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to sit also in this prayer, as he ordered them when he fell from his horse. Muhammad bin al-Hasan bin Qutaybah informed us, saying: Yazid bin Muhabb informed us, saying: Al-Layth bin Sa’d told me on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell ill, so we prayed behind him while he was sitting, and Abu Bakr was hearing the people. He said: He turned to us and saw us standing, so he motioned to us, so we sat down and prayed with him while sitting. When he finished his prayer, he said: You almost did what the Persians and Romans did, they stand over their kings while he is sitting, so do not do that. Follow your imams. If he prays standing, then pray standing, and if he prays, then pray sitting. Abu Hatim said: In this explanatory report, there is a clear statement. A clear statement that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat on the left of Abu Bakr and Abu Bakr turned to be a follower, following his prayer and saying the takbir, so that the people could hear the takbir so that they could follow his prayer, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to sit when he saw them standing. When he finished his prayer, he also ordered them to sit if their imam prayed while sitting. Jabir ibn Abdullah witnessed the prayer of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he fell from his horse and injured his right side. His fall, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the month of Dhul-Hijjah, the last year of the fifth year of the Hijrah. He witnessed this prayer during his illness, may God bless him and grant him peace, at a time other than this, so he conveyed each report with its wording. Do you not see that he mentions in this Prayer: Abu Bakr raised his voice in glorification so that people would follow his example. That prayer which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed in his house when he fell from his horse, he did not need to raise his voice in glorification so that people would hear his glorification despite the smallness of Aisha’s room, but rather he raised his voice in glorification in the Great Mosque where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed during his illness. So when what we have described is authentic, it is not permissible for us to make some of these reports abrogate others. This prayer was when he, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to it between two men, and he was the imam in it and prayed with them while sitting and ordered them to sit. As for the prayer which he prayed at the end of his life, his going out to it was between Barira and Nawbah, and he was safe in it, and he prayed while sitting behind Abu Bakr in one garment wrapped around him. Anas bin Malik narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the last prayer with the people in one garment wrapped around him while sitting behind Abu Bakr, so he, peace be upon him, prayed two prayers in the mosque in congregation, not one prayer. And in the report of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah from Aisha that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out between two men, one of whom wanted Al-Abbas and the other Ali. In the report of Masruq from Aisha: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, felt light in himself, so he went out between Barira and Nubah. I see his sandals dragging in the pebbles and I see the soles of his feet, the hadith. This indicates to you that they were two prayers, not one prayer. Abu Hatim said: Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Khuzaymah told us, he said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Badal bin Al-Muhber told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Musa bin Abi Aisha, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah, on the authority of Aisha that Abu Bakr prayed with the people and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the row behind him. Abu Hatim said: Shu’bah bin Al-Hajjaj disagreed with Za’idah bin Qudamah in the text of this report from Musa bin Abi Aisha, so Shu’bah made the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a follower when he prayed sitting and the people were standing, and Za’idah made the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, an imam when he prayed sitting and the people were standing, and they are both skilled and memorizers, so how is it permissible to make one of them a follower? The two narrations that apparently contradict each other in one action abrogates a previous absolute command! Whoever considers one of the two reports to be abrogating what preceded from the command of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and leaves the other without proof that proves its authenticity, then he has permitted his opponent to leave out what he took from the two reports and leave out what he took from them. Similar to this type of Sunnah is the report of Ibn Abbas: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, married Maymunah while he was in ihram,” and the report of Abu Rafi’: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her while they were both in ihram.” So the two reports contradict each other in one action on the surface, without there being anything between them in our view. So a group of the scholars of hadith considered the two reports that were narrated about the marriage of Maymunah to be contradictory, and they went to the report of Uthman ibn Affan from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The one in ihram does not marry nor is he given in marriage. So they took it, because it agrees with one of the two reports that were narrated about the marriage of Maymunah, and they left out the report of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her while he was in ihram. So whoever does this must say: The two reports contradict each other in the prayer of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in its cause, according to what we mentioned before, so he must come to The report which contains the command for the followers to pray while sitting if their imam prays while sitting, then it is taken into account, since it agrees with one of the two narrations that were narrated about the prayer of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his illness, and the report that is separate from them is abandoned, as he did in the marriage of Maymuna. Abu Hatim said: Some of the Iraqis who used to follow the school of thought of the Kufians claimed that his saying: If he prays while sitting, then pray while sitting, meant by it: And if he bears witness while sitting, then bear witness while sitting, all of them. So he diverted the report from the generality of what the report mentioned without evidence that was proven for him to interpret it.
2:239: It contains nine issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: If you fear of fear which is panic, then on foot meaning, then go on foot, or riding is conjoined to it, and men is the plural of rajil or rajul from their saying rajul man yarjul man if he does not have a mount and walks on his feet, so he is rajul, rajul, and rajul with a damma on the jim, and it is the language of the people of Hijaz, they say: So-and-so walked to the House of God barefoot, on foot, as narrated by al-Tabari, and rajulan, rajil, and rajul, and it is pluralized as rajul, rajul, rajul, rajulan, rajul with a fatha on the jim, and arjilah, arajil, and arajil, and rajul which is the generic name is also pluralized as rajul. Second: When God Almighty commanded that one stand for Him in prayer in a state of qunut, which is dignity, tranquility, and calmness of the limbs, and this is in the prevailing state of security and reassurance, He mentioned the state of fear that sometimes arises, and explained that this act of worship is not dropped from the servant in any case, and He permitted His servants to pray on foot or riding on horses and camels and the like, gesturing and indicating with the head wherever he is directed. This is the saying of the scholars, and this is the prayer of the individual who has been distressed by fear for his life in the case of combat or from a wild animal pursuing him or from an enemy following him or a flood carrying him, and in short, every matter that he fears for his life is a sale of what this verse includes. Third: This license includes the consensus of scholars that a person should be wherever he is in the heavens, and should turn and act according to his view of his own salvation. Fourth: There is a difference of opinion regarding the fear in which it is permissible to pray on foot or on horseback. Al-Shafi’i said: It is when the enemy appears to them and they see each other, while the Muslims are not in a fortress until the weapon reaches them from shooting or more so that the enemy approaches them from stabbing and striking, or someone comes whose report is true and informs him that the enemy is close to him and they are marching towards him. If one of these two meanings does not exist, then it is not permissible for him to pray the prayer of fear. If they pray the prayer of fear based on the report and then the enemy leaves, they do not repeat it. It was said: They repeat it, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifa. Abu ‘Umar said: The situation in which it is permissible for the one who is afraid to pray on foot or riding, facing the qiblah or not facing it, is the situation of intense fear. The situation in which the reports were reported is not this, which is the prayer of fear with the imam and the division of the people, and its ruling is not in this verse. This will be explained in Surat An-Nisa’, God willing. Malik differentiated between fear of a fighting enemy and fear of a wild animal or the like, such as an attacking camel or a flood or something that is most likely to lead to death, as it is recommended without fear of the enemy. Repeating it in time if there is security, and most of the jurists of the countries agree that the matter is the same. Fifth: Abu Hanifa said: Fighting spoils the prayer, and the hadith of Ibn Umar refutes him, and the apparent meaning of the verse is the strongest evidence for it, and this will come in An-Nisa’, God willing. Al-Shafi’i said: When God Almighty permitted the omission of some conditions, this indicates that fighting during the prayer does not spoil it, and God knows best. Sixth: There is no reduction in the number of rak’ahs in fear from the prayer of the traveler according to Malik, Al-Shafi’i and a group of scholars. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan, Qatada and others said: He prays one rak’ah by gesture. Muslim narrated on the authority of Bakir bin Al-Akhns on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: God imposed prayer on the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the city four rak’ahs, in travel two rak’ahs, and in fear one rak’ah. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: Bakir bin Al-Akhns was the only one to report it, and it is not an argument in what he reported alone. Prayer is the first thing to be cautious about, and whoever prays two rak’ahs in his fear and travel has moved from disagreement to certainty. Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said: The one who fears death in combat or otherwise prays one rak’ah, and if he is unable to do so, then he should say two takbirs. Ishaq bin Rahawayh said: If he is only able to say one takbir, it is sufficient for him. Ibn Al-Mundhir mentioned this. And the Almighty’s saying: And when you are secure, then remember God as He taught you. That is, return to what you were commanded to do in completing the pillars. Mujahid said, You are secure means you left the place of travel for the place of residence. Al-Tabari responded to this statement, and a group said, You are secure means your fear that forced you to perform this prayer has gone away. Seventh: The scholars differed on this matter regarding the construction of the one who is afraid if he feels safe. Malik said: If he prays a rak’ah while safe and then becomes afraid, he should mount and build.
