Likewise, if he prays a rak’ah while riding and he is afraid and then feels safe, he should dismount and build. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi’i, and al-Muzani said the same. Abu Hanifa said: If he begins the prayer while safe and then feels afraid, he should face forward and not build. If he prays while afraid and then feels safe, he should build. Al-Shafi’i said: The one who dismounts should build, but the one who rides does not. Abu Yusuf said: He does not build in any of these. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: So remember God. It was said: Its meaning is thank Him for this blessing in teaching you this prayer that has been sufficient, and you have not missed any prayer, which is what you did not know. So the kaf in His saying as means thanks. You say: Do to me as I did to you such and such as a reward and thanks. And the ma in His saying: as long as is the object of He taught you. Ninth: Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said that the origin of prayer is supplication, and the state of fear is more deserving of supplication, so that is why prayer is not dropped by fear. If prayer is not dropped by fear, then it is more deserving that it is not dropped by anything else, such as illness or the like. God Almighty commanded us to maintain prayers in every situation, whether in health or illness, presence or travel, ability or inability, fear or security. They are not dropped from the person obligated under any circumstances, and their obligation is not affected by any defect. The ruling on the sick person will be explained at the end of Al Imran, God willing. What is meant by this is that prayer is performed as much as possible, and it is not dropped under any circumstances, even if it is not done except by a gesture with the eye, it is obligatory to do it. This distinguishes it from all other acts of worship, all of which are dropped by excuses and concessions are permitted in them. Ibn al-Arabi said: That is why our scholars said: And it is a great issue, that the one who abandons prayer is killed, because it is similar to faith, which is not dropped under any circumstances. They said about it: One of the pillars of Islam is not permissible to replace it with a body or money, so the one who abandons it is killed. Its origin is the two testimonies, and what the scholars have said about the one who abandons prayer will come in (Innocence) God willing.
2:240: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, a group of commentators interpreted this verse to mean that the woman whose husband died used to stay in the house of the deceased for a year, and he would spend on her from his money as long as she did not leave the house. If she left, then there would be no blame on the heirs for cutting off the maintenance from her. Then the year was abrogated by four months and ten, and the maintenance was abrogated by a quarter and an eighth in Surat An-Nisa’. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and Ar-Rabi’. There is a difference of opinion among the scholars regarding residence. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr who said: I said to Uthman, this verse in al-Baqarah 2:And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, to His saying: other than their leaving behind them, was abrogated by the other verse, so why did you not write it or leave it? He said: O son of my brother, I will not change anything of it from its place. At-Tabari said on the authority of Mujahid: This verse is decisive and there is no abrogation in it. The waiting period had been established as four months and ten days, then God made for them a will from Him to reside for seven months and twenty nights. If the woman wishes, she may reside in her will, and if she wishes, she may go out. This is the saying of God Almighty: But if they go out, there is no blame upon you. Ibn Atiyyah said: All of this has been removed by the agreed-upon abrogation except for the saying of At-Tabari and Mujahid, may God Almighty have mercy on them both. There is a view on At-Tabari regarding that. Judge Iyad said: The consensus is that the year has been abrogated and that her waiting period is four months and ten days. Others said that the meaning of his saying a will is that it is from God Almighty that it is obligatory for women after the death of the husband to remain in their homes for a year, then it was abrogated. I said: What At-Tabari mentioned on the authority of Mujahid is correct and proven. Al-Bukhari narrated that Ishaq told us, that Ruh told us, that Shibl told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, he said: This was the waiting period. She is obliged to observe the waiting period with her husband’s family, so God Almighty revealed: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them to His saying: from what is acceptable. He said: God made for her the completion of the year seven months and twenty nights as a will, if she wishes she may live in her will and if she wishes she may go out, and this is the saying of God Almighty: except for turning them out, then there is no blame upon you. However, the first statement is more apparent because of his saying, peace be upon him: It is only four months and ten, and one of you in the pre-Islamic era used to throw dung at the beginning of the year, the hadith. This is a statement from him, peace be upon him, about the condition of those whose husbands died before the advent of the law, so when Islam came, God Almighty ordered them to stay in their homes for a year, then it was abrogated by the four months and ten. This, despite its clarity in the established Sunnah transmitted by individual reports, is a consensus among Muslim scholars with no disagreement about it, as Abu Omar said, he said: And so is the rest of the verse, so His saying, the Almighty: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall bequeath to their wives a year’s maintenance without turning them out was all abrogated according to the majority of scholars, then the will to live in it was abrogated. For wives during the year, except for a strange and abandoned narration that came from Ibn Abi Nujayh from Mujahid, and it was not followed, nor did any of the Muslim scholars from the Companions and Followers and those after them say it regarding what exceeds four months and ten, as far as I know. Ibn Jurayj narrated from Mujahid what the people say, so the consensus was reached and the disagreement was resolved, and success is from God. The second: The Almighty’s saying: A will. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Al-Kisa’i, and Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr read a will in the nominative case as the subject, and its predicate is for their wives. It is possible that the meaning is that there is a will upon them, and His saying for their wives is an attribute. Al-Tabari said: Some grammarians said: The meaning is that a will was written upon them, and His saying for their wives is an attribute. He said: This is also the reading of Abdullah bin Mas’ud. Abu Omar, Hamza, and Ibn Amir read a will in the accusative case, and this is based on the verb, meaning let them make a will. Then the dead person does not make a will, but he meant when they are close to death. And for their wives in this reading is also an attribute. It was said: The meaning is that God made a will, provisions, meaning provide them with provision, or God made that provision for them because the speech indicates it. It is possible that it is accusative as a state or with the source which is the will, like His saying: Or feeding on a day of famine * an orphan. al-Balad 90:14-15], and the goods here are the expenses of her year. Third: The Almighty’s saying: other than expelling means that the heirs of the deceased and the heirs of the house do not have the right to expel it. Other than is in the accusative case as a source according to Al-Akhfash, as if he said no expelling. It was said: It is in the accusative case because it is a description of the provision. It was said: It is in the accusative case as a state of the testators, meaning, provide for them other than expelling them. It was said: By removing the preposition, meaning, without expelling them. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: If they go out the verse, meaning by their own choice before the year, there is no blame upon you meaning there is no blame upon anyone, whether a guardian or a ruler or anyone else, because she is not obligated to stay in her husband’s house for a year. It was said: meaning there is no blame upon them for cutting off their maintenance, or there is no blame upon them for looking forward to husbands, since your supervision over them, O heirs, has been cut off. Then she must not marry before the end of the waiting period by a year, or there is no blame upon them for marrying them after the end of the waiting period, because He said from what is acceptable which is what is in accordance with the Shari’ah, And God is Exalted in Might is an attribute that necessitates a threat with regard to whoever violates the limit in this case and sends the woman out when she does not want to go out, Wise meaning He is the One who decides what He wants of the affairs of His servants.
2:241: Divorced women shall have a right to provision according to what is acceptable - a duty upon the righteous.
2:242: Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may understand. People differed regarding this verse. Abu Thawr said: It is decisive, and the pleasure is for every divorced woman. Al-Zuhri also said that. Al-Zuhri said that even for a slave woman who is divorced by her husband. Saeed bin Jubair also said that every divorced woman has a pleasure, and this is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i regarding this verse. Malik said: Every woman who has been divorced twice or once, whether he has consummated the marriage with her or not, whether he has named a dowry for her or not, the pleasure, except for the woman who was divorced before consummation and he has named a dowry for her, then half of it is enough for her. If he had not named it for her, then the pleasure is less than the dowry of her peers or more. This pleasure is not a limit, as Ibn Al-Qasim narrated from him. Ibn Al-Qasim said in Irkha’ Al-Sutour from Al-Mudawwana, he said: God Almighty made the pleasure for every divorced woman with this verse, then he made an exception in the other verse for which he had imposed a condition and had not consummated the marriage, so he excluded her from the pleasure. Ibn Zayd claimed that it abrogated it. Ibn Atiyyah said: Ibn Al-Qasim fled from the wording of abrogation to the wording of exception, and the exception is not valid in this place, rather it is pure abrogation as Zayd bin Aslam said. If Ibn Al-Qasim committed to his saying: And for the divorced women It is general for every divorced woman, and it is necessary to say that it is abrogated. Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah and others said: This verse is about married women who have had intercourse, since it was mentioned in the case of touching, it was never included in the generality. This comes on the basis that the saying of God Almighty: And if you divorce them before you have touched them (al-Baqarah 2:237), is specific to this category of women. When it is said that this generality includes her, then that is abrogation, not specification. Al-Shafi’i said in the other opinion: There is no enjoyment except for the one who was divorced before intercourse, and there is no touching or imposition, because the one who is entitled to something from the dowry does not need enjoyment in her right. The saying of God Almighty about the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then come, I will provide for you (al-Ahzab 33:28), is understood as a voluntary act from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, not an obligation. His saying, So you have no waiting period to count for them, so provide for them (al-Ahzab 33:49), is also understood as non-imposed. Al-Shafi’i said: And the one for whom the dowry is imposed, if she is divorced before touching, there is no enjoyment for her, because She took half of the dowry without intercourse taking place, and if the woman who was consummated with was divorced, she is entitled to a compensation, because the dowry is in exchange for intercourse and compensation due to the vulgarity of the contract. Al-Shafi’i made compensation obligatory for the woman who was divorced by khul’ and the woman who was granted mutual consent. The companions of Malik said: How can the woman who was redeemed have compensation when she gives, so how can she take compensation! There is no compensation for the woman who chooses separation from the woman who was divorced by khul’, redeemed by mutual consent, reconciled, cursed, or freed woman who chooses separation, whether he had intercourse with her or not, whether he named a dowry for her or not, and this has been explained previously.
2:243: It has six issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Have you not seen? This is a vision of the heart meaning have you not learned, and the meaning according to Sibawayh is to be alerted to the matter of those, and this vision does not need two objects. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami read Have you not seen? with the jazm of the ra’, and the hamza was deleted without adding a vowel because the original is Have you not seen? The story of these people is that they were a people from the Children of Israel who were afflicted with an epidemic, and they were in a village called Dawurdan. They fled from it and went down into a valley, so God Almighty killed them. Ibn Abbas said, they were four thousand who left fleeing from the plague and said: We will go to a land where there is no death, so God Almighty killed them, and the Prophet of God Almighty passed by them and brought them back to life. It was said that they died for eight days, and it was said: seven, and God knows best. Al-Hasan said: God killed them before their appointed times as a punishment for them, then He resurrected them for the rest of their appointed times. It was said that He did that to them as a miracle for one of their prophets. It was said that his name was Shimon. Al-Naqqash narrated that they fled from the fever, and it was said that they fled from jihad, and when He commanded them… God revealed it through the tongue of the Prophet Ezekiel, peace be upon him, so they feared death by being killed in jihad, so they left their homes fleeing from that, so God caused them to die so that they would know that nothing could save them from death, then He revived them and commanded them to jihad by His Almighty saying: And fight in the cause of God (al-Baqarah 2:190), as Ad-Dahhak said. Ibn Atiyyah said: The entire story is weak in its chains of transmission, and what is necessary from the verse is that God Almighty informed His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, in a manner that alerts and warns about a group of people who left their homes fleeing from death, so God Almighty caused them to die, then He revived them, so that they and all those who came after them would see that death is in the hand of God Almighty and not in the hand of anyone else, so there is no meaning to the fear of a fearful person or the deceit of a deceived person, and God made this verse an introduction before His command to the believers from the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, to jihad. This is what At-Tabari said, and it is the apparent arrangement of the verse. God Almighty said: And they are thousands The majority said, it is the plural of a thousand, some of them said: they were six hundred. A thousand, and it was said: They were eighty thousand, Ibn Abbas: Forty thousand, Abu Malik thirty thousand, Al-Suddi: Thirty-seven thousand, and it was said seventy thousand, said Ata bin Abi Rabah, and from Ibn Abbas also forty thousand, and eight thousand, narrated from him Ibn Jurayj and from him also eight thousand, and from him also four thousand, and it was said: Three thousand, and the correct is that they exceeded ten thousand because of the Almighty’s saying: And they are thousands and it is the plural of abundance, and it is not said about ten or less than it thousands, and Ibn Zayd said in his wording thousands, rather its meaning is and they are united, meaning that the division of their people did not expel them nor was there strife between them, rather they were united, so this group differed and went out fleeing from death and seeking life according to their claim, so God caused them to die in their place of safety according to their claim, so thousands according to this is the plural of thousand, like sitting and sitting, Ibn Al-Arabi said: God Almighty caused them to die for a period of time as a punishment for them then He brought them back to life, and the death of punishment after it is life, and the death of the appointed time there is no life after it, he said Mujahid said: When they were revived, they returned to their people, knowing that they had been dead, but the appearance of death was on their faces. None of them wore a garment except that it became a thick shroud until they died at the appointed times that were written for them. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The smell remained on that tribe of the Children of Israel until today. It was narrated that they were in the middle of Iraq, and it is said that they were revived after they had become stinking, so that smell is present in their descendants until today. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Beware of death meaning to beware of death, so it is in the accusative case because it is an object for which, and die is a command to form, and it is not far-fetched to say: They were called and it was said to them: Die, and it has been narrated that two angels shouted at them, Die, and they died, so the meaning is that God said to them through the two angels, Die, and God knows best. The third: The most correct, clearest and most famous of these sayings is that they went out fleeing from the plague. It was narrated by Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They went out fleeing from the plague and died, so one of the prophets called upon God to revive them so that they might worship Him, and God revived them. Amr bin Dinar said about this verse: The plague struck their village, so some people went out and others stayed, and those who went out were more than those who stayed. He said: Those who went out were saved and those who stayed died. When the second verse came, they all went out except a few, so God killed them and their animals, then He revived them and they returned to their country and their offspring multiplied. Al-Hasan said: They went out to beware of the plague, so God killed them and their animals in one hour, and they were forty thousand. I said: And this is how the rulings are arranged in this verse. The imams narrated, and the wording is from Al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Aamer bin Saad bin Abi Waqqas that he heard Usama bin Zaid telling Saad, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the pain and said: ‘A punishment or torment with which some nations were afflicted, then a remnant of it remains, so it goes away one time and comes another. Whoever hears of it in a land should not go there, and whoever is in a land where it has occurred should not leave fleeing from it. ’” And Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: Qutaybah told us, Hammad bin Zaid informed us, from Amr bin Dinar, from Aamer bin Saad, from Usama bin Zaid, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the plague and said: ‘A remnant of a punishment or torment sent upon a group of the Children of Israel. So if it occurs in a land while you are in it, do not leave it, and if it occurs in a land where you are not in it, do not descend upon it. ’” He said: A good and authentic hadith. And based on these hadiths, ‘Umar and the Companions, may God be pleased with them, acted when they returned from Sargh when ‘Abd Al-Rahman bin ‘Awf informed them of the hadith, according to what is well-known in Al-Muwatta’. And others, and some people hated fleeing from the epidemic and the sick land, it was narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: Fleeing from the epidemic is like fleeing from the battle, and the story of Omar in his departure to the Levant with Abu Ubaidah is well-known, and in it: that he returned, and Al-Tabari said: In the hadith of Saad there is evidence that a person must avoid calamities before they descend, and avoid fearful things before they attack, and that he must be patient and not panic after they descend, and that is because he, peace be upon him, forbade whoever was not in the land of the epidemic from entering it if it occurred to him, and he forbade whoever was in it from leaving it after it occurred to flee from it, so likewise it is obligatory that the ruling of every one who fears matters be their dangers, his path in that is the path of the plague, and this meaning is similar to his saying, peace be upon him: Do not wish to meet the enemy and ask God for well-being, and if you meet them then be patient, I said: This is the correct view in this matter, and it is what the saying of the Messenger, peace be upon him, requires, and his righteous and noble companions, may God be pleased with them, acted upon it, and Omar said to Abu Ubaidah, arguing with him when he said to him: Fleeing from fate God! Omar said: If someone other than you had said it, O Abu Ubaidah! Yes, we flee from the decree of God to the decree of God, meaning: There is no escape for man from what God has decreed for him and against him, but God the Most High has commanded us to beware of fears and calamities, and to do our utmost to ascend from the disliked things, then he said: Have you seen if you had camels and you descended into a valley with two valleys, one of which is fertile and the other is barren, is it not that if you graze the fertile one you graze them according to the decree of God, and if you graze the barren one you graze them according to the decree of God the Almighty, so Omar returned from that place to Medina, Al-Kaya Al-Tabari said: We do not know of any disagreement that if the infidels or highwaymen intend to go to a weak town whose people are unable to handle those who intend to go, then they have the right to move away from their presence, even if the appointed terms do not increase or decrease, and it has been said: Fleeing from it was only forbidden because the one who is in the place where the epidemic is may have taken a share of it, because the people of that place share in the cause of that general disease, so there is no benefit to his fleeing, rather it adds to what he has suffered from the beginnings of the epidemic the hardships of travel, so the pains are doubled and the harm increases They perish in every way and are thrown into every gap and narrow strait, and for this reason it is said: No one fled from the epidemic and was saved, as narrated by Ibn al-Madaini. It is sufficient in this regard to be admonished by the words of God Almighty: Have you not seen those who went forth from their homes, and they were thousands, for fear of death? So God said to them, ‘Die.’ Perhaps if he fled and was saved, he would say: I was only saved because I left it, and his belief would be bad. In short, fleeing from it is forbidden for what we have mentioned, and because it involves emptying the al-Balad 90:it is not empty of weak people for whom it is difficult to leave it, and they are not able to do so, and they are harmed by the country being empty of the wealthy who were pillars of the country and a support for the weak. If the epidemic is in a land, no one should go there, taking precautions and being cautious and avoiding places of harm, and repelling the confused illusions of the human soul, and entering it with the crescent moon, and that is not permissible in the judgment of God Almighty, because protecting oneself from harm is obligatory, and he may fear that he will have a bad belief by saying: If I had not entered this place, no harm would have befallen me. This is the benefit of the prohibition of entering a land in which there is a plague or Leaving it, and God knows best. Ibn Mas`ud said: The plague is a trial for the resident and the fugitive. As for the fugitive, he says: By my fleeing I was saved. As for the resident, he says: I stayed and died. Malik referred to something similar to this when he was asked about the undesirability of looking at a leper, so he said: I have not heard of any undesirability in it, and I do not see that what came of the prohibition of that is except for fear that something might happen to him that might frighten him or frighten him. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the plague: If you hear of it in a land, do not go to it, and if it breaks out while you are in it, do not leave fleeing from it.” He was also asked about a town in which death and diseases occur, is it undesirable to leave it? He said: I do not see anything wrong with whether one leaves or stays. Fourth: In his saying, peace be upon him: If an epidemic breaks out in a land while you are in it, do not leave it fleeing from it, is evidence that it is permissible to leave a plague-stricken town for anything other than fleeing from it, if he believes that what befell him could not have missed him. Likewise, the ruling on one who enters if he is certain that entering it will not bring upon him a destiny that God had not destined for him, so He permits him to enter it and leave it according to this limit that we have mentioned, and God knows best. Fifth: On the virtue of patience in the face of the plague and its explanation. The plague is of the form fa’ul from the word stabbing, but when it was changed from its original form, it was used to indicate general death by epidemic. Al-Jawhari said: It is narrated from the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The demise of my nation will be by stabbing and plague. She said: We know the stabbing, but what is the plague? He said: A gland like the gland of a camel that emerges in the omentum and armpits. The scholars said: This is an epidemic that God may send as a punishment and a punishment upon whomever He wills of His disobedient servants and their infidels. He may send it as a testimony and mercy for the righteous, as Muadh said about the plague of Emmaus: It is a testimony and mercy for you and a supplication of your Prophet. O God, give Muadh and his family their share of your mercy. So he was stabbed in the hand, may God be pleased with him. Abu Qilabah said: I know the testimony and mercy, but I do not know what your Prophet supplication was? So I asked about it and it was said: He, peace be upon him, prayed that the annihilation of his nation be by stabbing and plague when he prayed that the affliction of his nation not be among them, so he prevented it and prayed with this. It is narrated from the hadith of Jabir and others on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: The one who flees from the plague is like the one who flees from the battle, and the one who is patient in it is like the one who is patient in the battle. And in Bukhari on the authority of Yahya bin Ya’mar “On the authority of Aisha that she told him that she asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, about the plague, so the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, told her: It was a punishment that God sends upon whomever He wills, so God made it a mercy for the believers. So no servant in a land where the plague occurs and remains patient, knowing that he knows that he will be afflicted with nothing but what God has decreed for him, will have the reward of a martyr.” This is an explanation of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: The plague is martyrdom and the one who is stabbed is a martyr, meaning the one who is patient and expects his reward from God, knowing that nothing will befall him except what God has decreed for him. Therefore, Muadh wished to die in it because he knew that whoever dies is a martyr. As for the one who is afraid of the plague and hates it and flees from it, he is not included. In the meaning of the hadith, and God knows best. Sixth: Abu Omar said: It has not been reported to me that any of the scholars fled from the plague except what Ibn al-Madaini mentioned that Ali bin Zaid bin Jud’an fled from the plague to al-Siyala. He used to gather every Friday and return. When he gathered, they would shout at him: Flee from the plague! So he died in al-Siyala. He said: Amr bin Ubayd and Ribat bin Muhammad fled to al-Rabatiyya. Ibrahim bin Ali al-Fuqaimi said about that: When death provoked every liar, I was patient, but neither Ribat nor Amr was patient. Abu Hatim reported on the authority of Al-Asma’i, who said: One of the Basrans fled from the plague, so he rode his donkey and went with his family towards Safwan. He heard a camel driver urging behind him: God will not outpace a donkey or a powerful bird. Or death comes at a certain rate, and God may be in front of the traveler Al-Madaini said: The plague broke out in Egypt during the reign of Abd al-Aziz ibn Marwan, so he fled from it and settled in a village in Upper Egypt called Sukkar. When a messenger from Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan settled there, he came to him. Abd al-Aziz said to him: What is your name? He said: Talib ibn Mudrik. He said: Oh, I do not see myself returning to Fustat! So he died in that village.
2:244: God Almighty says: And fight in the cause of God and know that God is Hearing and Knowing. This is a speech to the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to fight in the way of God, according to the majority of scholars. It is what is intended by it that the word of God is supreme, and the paths of God are many, so they are general in every path. God Almighty said: “Say: This is My path” [Yawm 108]. Malik said: The paths of God are many, and there is no path except that one fights on it, in it, or for it, and the greatest of them is the religion of Islam. There is no disagreement on this. It was said that the speech is to those of the Children of Israel who were revived. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak, and the waw on this in his saying: And fight is a conjunction to the previous command, and in the speech its estimation is left out, and he said to them fight, and according to the first opinion it is a conjunction of a sentence of speech to the previous sentence, and there is no need for an implied meaning in the speech. An-Nahhas said: And fight is a command from God Almighty to the believers not to flee as these fled. And know that God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing meaning He hears your words if you say what these said and He knows what you mean by it. At-Tabari said: There is no basis for the statement of those who said: The command to fight is for those who were revived, and God knows best..
2:245: It contains eleven issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? When God the Almighty commanded jihad and fighting for the sake of truth, since there is nothing in the Shari’ah except that fighting for it and about it is permissible, and the greatest of them is the religion of Islam, as Malik said, which urged spending for that, so this report ofcluded the fighter in the way of God, for he lends it in the hope of reward. As Uthman, may God be pleased with him, did in the army of hardship, and who is the subject, and that is its predicate, and who is an adjective for that, and if you wish, a substitute. When this verse was revealed, Abu Al-Dahdah hastened to give his money in charity seeking the reward of his Lord. The Sheikh, the jurist, the imam, the hadith scholar, the judge Abu Aamer Yahya bin Aamer bin Ahmad bin Mani’ Al-Ash’ari, by lineage and doctrine, told us in Cordoba, may God restore it in Rabi’ Al-Akhir in the year six hundred and twenty-eight, a reading from me to him. He said: My father told us with permission. He said: I read to me Abu Bakr Abdul Aziz bin Khalaf bin Madyan Al-Azdi on the authority of Abu Abdullah bin Sa’dun, hearing from him. He said: Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Mihran told us. He said: Abu Al-Hasan Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Zakariya bin Haywah Al-Naysaburi told us in the year three hundred and sixty-six. He said: My uncle Abu Zakariya Yahya bin Zakariya told us. He said: Muhammad bin Mu’awiyah bin Salih told us. He said: Khalaf bin Khalifa told us on the authority of Hamid Al-A’raj on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Abd ibn Mas`ud said: When the verse: Who is he that would loan God a goodly loan was revealed, Abu Ad-Dahdah said: O Messenger of God, does God want a loan from us? He said: Yes, O Abu Ad-Dahdah. He said: Show me your hand. He said: So give it to him. He said: Then I have loaned God a garden with six hundred palm trees. Then he came walking until he reached the garden and Umm Ad-Dahdah and his children were in it. He called her: O Umm Ad-Dahdah, she said: At your service. He said: Come out, you have loaned my Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, a garden with six hundred palm trees. Zaid ibn Aslam said: When the verse: Who is he that would loan God a goodly loan was revealed, Abu Ad-Dahdah said: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God! God is asking us for a loan, and He is independent of the loan? He said: Yes, He wants to admit you into Paradise through it. He said: Then if I loan my Lord a loan, will He guarantee Paradise for me and my two children Ad-Dahdah with me? He said: Yes. He said: Give me your hand. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him his hand and said: I have two gardens, one of them is in the lower part and the other is in the upper part. By God, I do not own anything else. I have made them a loan to God Almighty. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give one of them to God and leave the other as a livelihood for you and your family. He said: I bear witness, O Messenger of God, that I have made the better of the two gardens for God Almighty, and it is a garden with six hundred palm trees. He said: Then God will reward you with Paradise for it. So Abu Ad-Dahdah set off until he came to Umm Ad-Dahdah while she was with her children in the garden, walking around under the palm trees. He began to say: May God guide you to the right path and the path of goodness and righteousness Between me and the one who has been in love, he has become a loan to the one who calls I lent it to God on my reliance, willingly, not out of spite or reluctance. Except for the hope of weakness in the afterlife, so depart with your soul and children And righteousness is undoubtedly the best provision that a person can bring to the afterlife. Umm Al-Dahdah said: Your sale is profitable! May God bless you in what you bought. Then Umm Al-Dahdah answered him and began to say: May God give you good report and happiness like you, she did what she could and advised May God bless my family and grant them black dates and dates of happiness. The servant strives and gets what he has toiled for all night long, and he is responsible for what he has committed. Then Umm Al-Dahdah turned to her children, taking out what was in their mouths and shaking what was in their sleeves until she reached the other wall. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How many a ripening cluster of dates and a fragrant house does Abu Al-Dahdah have. Second: Ibn al-Arabi said: When the creation heard this verse, by the Creator’s judgment, wisdom, power, will, decree, and destiny, they were divided into three groups. The first group was the vile group, who said: The Lord of Muhammad is in need of us and we are rich. This is ignorance that is not hidden from anyone with sense. So God responded to them by saying: “God has certainly heard the statement of those who said: ‘God is poor, and we are rich.’” (Al-Imran: 181). When the second group heard this statement, they preferred miserliness and stinginess and put forward the desire for money, so they did not spend in the way of God, nor did they free a prisoner, nor did they help anyone, out of laziness in obedience and dependence on this world. When the third group heard this, they hastened to comply with it and preferred those among them who responded quickly with their money, such as Abu al-Dahdah, may God be pleased with him, and others. And God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s saying: A good loan. Loan is the name for everything for which a reward is sought. So-and-so lent so-and-so, meaning he gave him something to repay him. The poet, Labid, said: If you are given a loan, then give it back. Only the young man gives back, not the camel. Al-Qard with the kasra is a language in which Al-Kisa’i narrated it. I borrowed from someone means I asked him for a loan, so he lent me. I borrowed from him means I took the loan. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Qard in the language means good affliction and bad affliction. Umayyah said: Every person will be repaid for his loan, good or bad, and he will be indebted for what he has lent. Another said: Loans are repaid in kind, so good is repaid in kind and evil is repaid in kind. Al-Kisa’i said: “A loan is what you have advanced of good or bad deeds. The root of the word is to cut off, and from it comes the word ‘scissors’. I loaned him, meaning I cut off a piece of my money for him to be rewarded for. The people became extinct: their traces were cut off and they perished. The loan here is a noun, and if it were not for that, he would have said ‘loaning’ here. The invocation of a loan in this verse is only to familiarize and bring closer what they understand. God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy, but the Most High likened the giving of the believer in this world to what he hopes for his reward in the Hereafter to a loan, just as He likened the giving of souls and money in taking Paradise to buying and selling, according to what will be explained in “Bara’ah,” God willing. It was said that what is meant by the verse is the encouragement to give charity and spend money on the poor and needy and to be generous to them, and in the way of God by supporting the religion. God Almighty referred to the poor person by his lofty self, free from needs, as an encouragement to give charity, just as He referred to the sick, needy, and thirsty person by his holy self, free from deficiencies and pains. In the authentic hadith, it is reported from God Almighty: “O O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me. I asked you for food but you did not feed Me. I asked you for a drink but you did not give Me a drink. He said, “My Lord, how can I give You a drink when You are the Lord of the worlds?!” He said, “My servant so-and-so asked you for a drink but you did not give him a drink. If you had given him a drink you would have found that with Me.” And likewise in what came before it. Narrated by Muslim and al-Bukhari. All of this was stated in a manner of honor for the one who is referred to by a metaphor, encouraging the one who is addressed by it. Fourth: The borrower must return the loan, because God the Almighty has said that whoever spends in the way of God will not lose it with God the Almighty, but rather the reward will be returned for sure, and the recompense is unclear. And in the hadith: Spending in the way of God is multiplied up to seven hundred times and more, as will be explained in this surah when God the Almighty says: The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a seed [of grain] which grows seven ears (al-Baqarah 2:261), the verse, and He said here: Then He will multiply it for him many times over, and this has no end or limit. Fifth: The reward for lending is great, because it provides a relief for the Muslim and relieves him. Ibn Majah narrated in his Sunan: “On the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: On the night of my ascension, I saw written on the door of Paradise: Charity is worth ten times its like and a loan is worth eighteen times its like. So I said to Gabriel: Why is a loan better than charity? He said: Because the beggar is asked while he has it, and the borrower does not borrow except out of need.” He said: Muhammad bin Khalaf al-Asqalani narrated to us, Ya’la narrated to us, Sulayman bin Yasir narrated to us, on the authority of Qays bin Rumi, he said: Sulayman bin Adhanan used to lend Alqamah a thousand dirhams in addition to his stipend. When his stipend came out, he demanded it from him, and he was upset with him, so he paid him back. It seemed that Alqamah became angry and stayed for months, then he came to him and said: Lend me a thousand dirhams in addition to my stipend. He said: Yes, and by God! O Umm Utbah, bring me that sealed map that you have. He said: So she brought it, and he said: By God, they are your dirhams that you paid me, and I did not move a single dirham from them. He said: By God, may your father be?” What made you do what you did to me? He said: What I heard from you. He said: What I heard from me? I heard you mention on the authority of Ibn Masoud that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no Muslim who lends a loan to another Muslim twice but it is as if it were charity once. He said: That is what Ibn Masoud told me. Sixth: A human loan to another person is one, meaning that he should be given back the same amount of what he lent. The scholars have agreed that borrowing dinars, dirhams, wheat, barley, dates, raisins, and everything that has a similar amount from other foods is permissible. The Muslims have agreed, based on the narration of their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that stipulating an increase in a loan is usury, even if it is a handful of fodder, as Ibn Mas`ud said, or a single grain. It is permissible to return something better than what he borrowed if he did not stipulate that, because that is a matter of kindness, based on the hadith of Abu Hurayrah regarding the young camel: The best of you are the best at repaying debts. Narrated by the imams: Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and others. So, may God bless him and grant him peace, praised the one who repays debts well, and he made that general and did not restrict it to a specific description. Likewise, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled regarding the young camel, which is the best of the camels, a four-year-old camel. The best is the chosen one, and the four-year-old is the one that has entered its fourth year, because it sheds its front teeth, which are the ones next to the incisors, and they are four four-year-olds with a light ba’. This hadith is evidence of the permissibility of lending to animals, and it is The doctrine of the majority, and Abu Hanifa forbade it, as mentioned above. Seventh: It is not permissible for the one who borrowed to give a gift to the lender, and it is not permissible for the lender to accept it unless it is their custom. This is what the Sunnah says: Ibn Majah narrated that Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, saying: Ismail ibn Ayyash narrated to us, Utbah ibn Hamid al-Dhabi narrated to us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Ishaq al-Hanani, saying: I asked Anas ibn Malik about a man among us who lends money to his brother and he gives him a gift. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you lends his brother a loan and he gives him a gift or carries him on his mount, he should not accept it or ride it unless it has been agreed upon between them before that. Eighth: The loan may be from money, and we have explained its ruling, and it may be from honor. In the hadith, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Is one of you unable to be like Abu Damdam, who, when he left his house, would say: O God, I have given my honor in charity to Your servants?” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: Lend from your honor for the day of your poverty, meaning whoever insults you, do not take any right from him and do not carry out a punishment on him until you come on the Day of Resurrection with ample reward. Abu Hanifa said: It is not permissible to give charity from honor because it is the right of God Almighty. It was narrated on the authority of Malik Ibn al-Arabi: This is corrupt. He, peace be upon him, said in the Sahih: Your blood, your money, and your honor are sacred to you, the hadith. This requires that these three prohibitions be treated as one in that they are, by respecting the right of man. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: Good. Al-Waqidi said: He is counting on his own goodness. Amr bin Othman Al-Sadfi said: He does not show off or harm. Sahl bin Abdullah said: He does not believe in a reward for his loan. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: He will multiply it for him. Asim and others read He will multiply it for him with an alif and half a fa’, and Ibn Amir and Ya’qub read it with emphasis on the ‘ayn, with the alif dropped and the fa’ in the accusative case. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja`far and Shaybah read it with emphasis and raising the fa`, while the others read it with an alif and raising the fa`. Whoever raised it arranged it according to his saying: (He lends) and it was said: on the assumption that he multiplies it, and whoever put it in the accusative case, then it is an answer to the question with the fa`, and it was said: by implying (that) and emphasis and lightening are two dialects, the evidence for emphasis is many times because emphasis is for multiplication, and Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: We do not know this doubling except for God alone, because God Almighty said: {And He will give from Himself a great reward} (An-Nisa’: 40), Abu Hurairah said: This is in the expenses of jihad, and we used to calculate while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among us that a man’s expenses on himself, his companions and his back were two thousand thousand. Eleventh: The Almighty’s saying: And God contracts and expands. This is general in everything, for He is the Constrictor and the Expander, and we have mentioned them in the explanation of the Most Beautiful Names in the Most Sublime Book. And to Him you will return is a threat, so He will reward everyone according to his deeds.
2:246: In incitement to fighting, he mentioned another story that happened in the Children of Israel, and the noble elite of the people, as if they were full of longing, and Al-Zajjaj said: They were called that because they were full of what they needed from them, and the elite in this verse is the people, because the meaning requires it, and the elite is a name for the group like the people and the group, and the elite is also good character, and from it the hadith: Be kind to the crowd, for you will all be satisfied. Narrated by Muslim. God the Almighty said: After Moses meaning after his death: When they said to their prophet, ‘Send us a king.’ It was said that he was Samuel bin Bal bin Alqamah, who was known as Ibn Al-Ajouz, and it was also said about him: Shimon, as Al-Suddi said. It was only said: Ibn Al-Ajouz because his mother was old and asked God for a child and she had grown old and barren, so God the Almighty granted him to her. He was also called: Simon because she asked God to grant her a child, so He heard her prayer and she gave birth to a boy and named him Simon, meaning: God heard my prayer. The letter seen becomes something in the Hebrew language. He is from the descendants of Jacob. Muqatil said: He is from the descendants of Aaron, peace be upon him. Qatadah said: He is Joshua bin Nun. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is weak because the period of David was after Moses by centuries of people, and Joshua is the young man of Moses. Al-Muhasibi mentioned that his name was Ishmael, and God knows best. This verse is report about a people from the Children of Israel who were humiliated and defeated by an enemy, so they asked for permission to wage jihad and to be commanded to do so. When they were ordered, most of them disobeyed and the few were patient, so God gave them victory. The good report is that these mentioned are the ones who were killed and then brought back to life, and God knows best. The Almighty said: We fight with the letter nun and the letter jazm. The majority of reciters read it as a response to the command. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Abi Ubla read it with the letter ya and raised the verb, so it is in the position of an attribute of the king. God the Almighty said: He said, ‘Asethum?’ ‘Asethum with the fat-ha and the kasra are two dialects. Nafi’ read it with the second, and the rest read it with the first, which is the most common. Abu Hatim said: There is no basis for the kasra, and al-Hasan and Talhah read it with it. Makki said in the active participle, ‘Asethum, this indicates the kasra of the seen in the past tense and the fat-ha of the seen in the common language. Abu Ali said: The basis for the kasra is the Arabs’ saying: He is ‘Asethum with that, like hara free and shaja brave. The verb and the verb have come in the likes of na’am (peace) and na’am (peace), and likewise ‘Asethum and ‘Asethum. If the verb is attributed to an apparent meaning, then the analogy of ‘Asethum is to say: ‘Asethum Zayd may God be pleased, like ‘Adhi may God be pleased. If it is said, then it is the analogy, and if it is not said, then it is permissible to take both dialects and use one in place of the other. The meaning of this statement is: Are you close to turning away and fleeing? If fighting is prescribed for you, then do not fight. Al-Zajjaj said: Will you not fight? is in the accusative case, meaning would you fight? “They said: ‘And why should we not fight in the cause of God?’” Al-Akhfash said: An is redundant. Al-Farra’ said: It is based on the meaning, meaning what prevented us, as you say: Why don’t you pray? Meaning what prevented you? It was said: The meaning is: What do we have to do with not fighting in the cause of God? An-Nahhas said: This is the best of them. And is in the accusative case, And we were expelled from our homes is an explanation, and so is and our children meaning because of our offspring. God the Almighty said: But when fighting was prescribed for them meaning it was imposed on them they turned away. God the Almighty informed us that when fighting was imposed on them and they saw the truth, and their thoughts returned to engaging in war and that their souls might go, they turned away meaning their intentions became disturbed and their resolve weakened. This is the nature of nations that are pampered and inclined to ease. They wish for war at times of arrogance, but when war comes, they become complacent and submit to their nature. Concerning this meaning, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade it by saying: Do not wish to meet the enemy and ask God for well-being, but when you meet them, then stand firm.” The Imams narrated this. Then God the Almighty informed us about a few of them who remained steadfast in their original intention and their resolve to fight in the way of God the Almighty continued.
2:247: God Almighty said: And their prophet said to them, 'Indeed, God has sent you Talut as a king.' That is, He answered you to what you asked. Talut was a water-carrier, and it was said: a tanner, and it was said: a mule, and he was a scholar, so God raised him up as follows. He was from the tribe of Benjamin, and he was not from the tribe of prophecy nor from the tribe of kingship. Prophethood was in the children of Levi, and kingship was in the tribe of Judah, so they denied it. Wahb bin Munabbih said: When the leaders of the children of Israel said to Samuel bin Bel what they said, he asked God Almighty to send them a king and guide him to him. God Almighty said to him: Look at the horn of a sheep in which there is oil in your house, and if a man enters upon you and the oil in the horn is sprouted, he is the king of the children of Israel, so anoint his head with it and make him king over them. He said: Talut was a tanner, so he went out in search of an animal that he had lost, so he went to Samuel, hoping that he would pray for him regarding the matter of the animal or find relief with him. The oil was added, as they claimed. He said: So Samuel went to him, took it, and anointed Talut’s head with it, and said to him: You are the king of the Children of Israel whom God Almighty commanded me to present. Then he said to the Children of Israel: God has sent you Talut as a king. Talut and Goliath are two foreign names that have been Arabized, and for that reason they are not declined, and so is David. The plural is Talut, Jawalit, and Dawawid. If you named a man Tawus and Raqoud, you would decline it, even though they are foreign. The difference between this and the first is that you say: Tawus, and the alif and lam are inserted, so this is possible in Arabic, but this is not possible in that. God Almighty says: How can he have dominion over us? That is, how can he have dominion over us when we are more deserving of dominion than he? They followed their tradition in their torment of the prophets, their only one, about the command of God the Most High, so they said: How? meaning from which side, How is in the accusative case as an adverb, and we are from the tribe of kings, and he is not like that, and he is poor, so they left the strongest reason, which is the power of God the Most High and His previous judgment, until their prophet argued with them by saying: God chose him, meaning He selected him, and it is the conclusive proof, and he explained to them with that the reason for choosing Talut, which is his expansion in knowledge, which is the essence of man, and the body, which is his support in war and his equipment when meeting, so it included a statement of the description of the Imam and the conditions of the Imamate, and that it is deserved by knowledge, religion and strength, not by lineage, so lineage has no role in it with knowledge and the virtues of the soul and that it precedes it, because God the Most High informed that He chose him over them for his knowledge and strength, even though they were more noble in lineage, and what was mentioned at the beginning of the Surah is sufficient and sufficient, and this verse is the basis for it, Ibn Abbas said: Talut was at that time the most knowledgeable man among the Children of Israel and the most handsome. And he completed it, and the increase in the body is what intimidates the enemy, and it was said: He was named Talut for his height, and it was said: The increase in the body was due to the abundance of meanings of goodness and courage, and the greatness of the body was not intended, did you not see the saying of the poet: You see a thin man and you despise him, but in his clothes is a raging lion. You like the fresh man, so you test him, but he turns out to be a fresh man. The camel has grown big without a core, so the camel's bone is not sufficient. I said: And from this meaning is his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, to his wives: The one who will join me first will be the one with the longest hand. So they were reaching out to each other, and Zaynab was the first of them to die, because she used to work with her hands and give charity. Narrated by Muslim. And some of the interpreters said: What is meant by knowledge is the knowledge of war, and this is a specification of the generality without evidence. And it has been said: The increase in knowledge is that God revealed to him, and based on this, Talut was a prophet, and it will come. God the Almighty said: And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills. Some commentators have said that this is from the words of God the Almighty to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It has also been said that it is from the words of Samuel, which is more apparent. He said this to them because he knew of their stubbornness and their arguments in the arguments, so he wanted to complete his words with the definitive that could not be objected to, so God the Almighty said: And God gives His kingdom to whom He wills. Attributing the kingdom of the world to God the Almighty is like attributing a slave to a king. Then he said to them, as a way of contempt and warning, without them asking: Indeed, the sign of His kingdom. It is possible that they asked him for evidence of his truthfulness in his words: Indeed, God has sent you Saul as a king. Ibn Atiyyah said: The first is more apparent in the context of the verse, and the second is more similar to the reprehensible morals of the Children of Israel, and al-Tabari agreed with this.
2:248: The Almighty said: “And their prophet said to them: ‘The sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you.’” That is, the Ark will come. The Ark was mentioned to have been sent down by God to Adam, peace be upon him, so it was with him until it reached Jacob, peace be upon him. It was among the Children of Israel, and they used it to overcome those who fought them until they disobeyed and overcame the Ark. The giants overcame them: Goliath and his companions, according to al-Suddi: and they took the Ark from them. I said: This is the clearest evidence that disobedience is the cause of failure, and this is clear. An-Nahhas said: The sign in the Ark, according to what was narrated, is that a groan was heard in it, so when they heard that, they marched to fight them, and when the groaning subsided, they did not march and the Ark did not march. It was said: They used to place it in a difficult battlefield and it would not cease to prevail until they disobeyed and were defeated and the Ark was taken from them, and that was their command. So when they saw the sign of the destruction and the disappearance of remembrance, some of them became disgusted and spoke about their matter until their leaders gathered and said to the Prophet of the time: Send us a king. So when he said to them: Your king is Talut, they referred him to him as God informed them about them. So when he cut them off with the argument, they asked him for evidence of that, according to the statement of At-Tabari, so when they asked their Prophet for evidence of what he said, he called upon his Lord and the statement was revealed that those who took the Ark were sick because of it. There is a difference of opinion about that. It was said: They placed it in a synagogue for them in which there were idols, so the idols would wake up upside down. And it was said that they placed it in the house of their idols under the idol. The elder one, so they woke up and he was on top of the idol, so they took him and tied him to his feet, and they woke up and the hands and feet of the idol had been cut off and thrown under the coffin, so they took him and put him in the village of a people, and those people suffered from pain in their necks, and it was said: They put him in the dung beetle of a people, and they were afflicted with hemorrhoids, so when their affliction became great, however it was, they said: This is only for this coffin! So let us return it to the Children of Israel. So they put it on a wheel between two bulls and sent them across the land towards the land of the Children of Israel. God sent angels to drive the two cows until they entered upon the Children of Israel, and they were in the matter of Talut, so they were certain of victory. This is the angels carrying the Ark in this narration. It was narrated that the angels came carrying it, and Joshua bin Nun had placed it in the wilderness. It was narrated that they saw the Ark in the air until it descended among them. This was said by Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham. Wahb bin Munabbih said: The size of the Ark was about three cubits by two cubits. Al-Kalbi said: It was made of Shamsar wood, from which combs are made. Zaid bin Thabit read al-tabuh, which is his language, and the people read it with a ta’, and it has been mentioned previously. It was narrated from him al-taybut, mentioned by Al-Nahhas. Hamid bin Qais read yahmulhu with a ya’. God the Almighty said: In it is tranquility from your Lord and a remnant. People differed about tranquility and remnant. Tranquility is a verbal noun derived from stillness, dignity and reassurance. His statement: In it is tranquility means that it is the reason for the tranquility of your hearts in what you differed about regarding the matter of Talut. Similar to it is: So God sent down His tranquility upon him (al-Tawbah 9:40), meaning He sent down upon him what calmed his heart. It was said that he meant that the Ark was the reason for the tranquility of their hearts, so wherever they were, they would be calm towards it and would not flee from the Ark if it was with them in war. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Tranquility is a spirit from God that speaks, so if they differed about a matter, it would speak clearly about what they wanted, and if it cried out in war, victory would be theirs. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: It is a violent wind with a face like a human face. It was narrated from him that he said: It is a raging wind with two heads. Mujahid said: An animal like a cat with two wings and a tail and its eyes have rays, so if it looks at the army, it is defeated. Ibn Abbas said: A golden basin from Paradise, in which the hearts of the prophets were washed. Al-Suddi said this. Ibn Atiyah said: The correct view is that the coffin contained excellent things from the remains and traces of the prophets, so the souls were comforted by that, and were strengthened by it. I said: In Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Al-Bara’, he said: A man was reciting Surat Al-Kahf and he had a horse tied to two ropes. A cloud covered it and it began to circle and draw near, and his horse began to flee from it. When morning came, he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him. He said: That is the tranquility that descended for the Qur’an.” And in the hadith of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri: “That one night, Asid bin Al-Hudayr was reciting in his garden, the hadith in which it says: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those were the angels listening to you. If you had recited, people would have seen them in the morning, as they were hidden from them.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us of the descent of tranquility once, and once of the descent of the angels, which indicates that tranquility was in that shade, and that it always descends with the angels. In this there is evidence for those who say that tranquility is a spirit or something that has a spirit, because it is not permissible for anyone to listen to the Qur’an except for someone who has reason, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: And the remainder. There are different opinions about the remainder. Some say: The staff of Moses, the staff of Aaron, and the fragments of the tablets, because they were broken when Moses threw them down. Ibn Abbas said this. Ikrimah added: The Torah. Abu Salih said: The remainder: The staff of Moses, his clothes, Aaron’s clothes, and two tablets of the Torah. Atiyah ibn Sa’d said: It is the staff of Moses, the staff of Aaron, their clothes, and the fragments of the tablets. Al-Thawri said: Some people say the remainder is a qafiz from a golden basin, the staff of Moses, the turban of Aaron, and the fragments of the tablets. Some of them say: The staff and the sandals. The meaning of this is what was narrated that when Moses came to his people with the tablets and found that they had worshipped the calf, he threw the tablets down in anger and they were broken. He took away what was intact from them and took the fragments of what was broken and put them in the chest. Ad-Dahhak said: The remainder: Jihad and fighting the enemies. Ibn Atiyah said: That is, the command to do that in the chest, either it is written in it, or the very act of bringing it is like the command to do that. And he attributed it to The Turks go back to the family of Moses and the family of Aaron, as the matter was transmitted from one people to another, and all of them are the family of Moses and the family of Aaron, and the family of a man is his kinship, and it was mentioned previously.
2:249: It contains eleven issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: So when Talut set out with the soldiers fasl means he went out with them. I set out something and it was separated, i.e. he cut it off and it was cut off. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: When Talut set out, they said to him: The waters will not carry us, so ask God to make a river flow for us. So Talut said to them: God will test you with a river. The number of soldiers was, according to al-Suddi, eighty thousand. Wahb said: No one stayed behind except someone with an excuse, such as young or old or sick. Testing is a trial. River and an-Nahr are two languages, and its derivation is from spaciousness, from which comes the word nahar, which has been mentioned previously. Qatada said: The river with which God tested them is a river between Jordan and Palestine. The majority read bi-Nahr with the ha’ open, and Mujahid and Hamid al-A’raj read bi-Nahr with the ha’ closed. The meaning of this trial is that it is a test for them. Whoever’s obedience is apparent in leaving the water, it is known that he is obedient in everything other than that. Whoever’s desire for water overcomes him and he disobeys the command, then he is more likely to disobey in hardships. It was narrated: They came to the river and were overcome by thirst, and it was extremely sweet and beautiful. Therefore, He permitted the obedient to drink in the room, so that the harm of thirst would be lifted from them somewhat, and so that they would break the conflict of the soul in this situation. He explained that the room is the entire harm of thirst for the patient, patient people in the hardship of life, whose concern is not luxury, as Urwah said: Feel the coolness of the water and the coldness of the water I said: And from this meaning is his saying, peace be upon him: A few mouthfuls are enough for a man to straighten his back. And some of those who deal with the mysteries of meanings said, this verse is a parable that God gave for the world, so God likened it to a river and the one who drinks from it and the one who inclines toward it and the one who takes a lot of it, and the one who abandons drinking it to the one who deviates from it and is indifferent to it, and the one who scoops up a handful with his hand to the one who takes from it as much as he needs, and the states of the three are different with God. I said: How good this is, were it not for the distortion in interpretation and the departure from the apparent meaning, but its meaning is correct without this. Second: Those who said that Talut was a prophet used as evidence his saying: Indeed, God is testing you, and that God revealed this to him and inspired him, and made the inspiration a test from God for them. And those who said that he was not a prophet said: Their prophet Samuel the Wise informed him when Talut informed his people of this, and this test only occurred to distinguish the truthful from the liar. Some people have said that Abdullah bin Hudhafah Al-Sahmi, the companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only ordered his companions to light a fire and enter it as a test of their obedience, but he interpreted his joke as a sign of fearing the harshness of the matter that he had imposed on them, and this will be explained in An-Nisa’, God willing. Third: The Almighty’s saying: So whoever drinks from it is not of me. It was said that drinking means guzzling, and the meaning of is not of me is that he is not one of my companions in this war, and that did not remove them from the faith. Al-Suddi said: They were eighty thousand, and there is no doubt that among them were the believer, the hypocrite, the diligent, and the lazy. And in the hadith: Whoever deceives us is not one of us, meaning he is not one of our companions nor on our path or guidance. He said: If you try to commit adultery with a lion, then I am not from you and you are not from me This is common in Arabic speech. A man says to his son if he does not behave in a manner similar to his: You are not one of me. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And whoever does not taste it, then indeed he is of Me. It is said: I tasted the thing, meaning I tasted it, and I fed him the water, meaning I made him taste it. He did not say and whoever does not drink it, because it is the custom of the Arabs, when they repeat something, to repeat it with another word, and the language of the Qur’an is the most eloquent of languages, so no attention should be paid to the criticism of someone who says: It is not said ‘I tasted the water.’ Fifth: Our scholars have used this as evidence for the statement of blocking the means, because the slightest taste is included in the word taste. So if the prohibition of taste occurs, then there is no way for someone who avoids food to drink. And because of this exaggeration, the words and whoever does not drink from it did not come. Sixth: When God Almighty said: And whoever does not feed it, it indicates that water is food, and if it is food, it is sustenance for its survival and the sustenance of the body, so it is necessary that usury be applied to it. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is the correct view of the school. Abu Umar said: Malik said: There is nothing wrong with selling water on the shore for water with a difference and on credit, and this is the view of Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: It is both measured and weighed, so according to this view, it is not permissible for him to have a difference, and in his view it is usury, because its cause in usury is the measure and weight. Al-Shafi’i said: It is not permissible to sell water with a difference and it is not permissible to have a credit, and its cause in usury is that it is an edible species. Seventh: Ibn al-Arabi said: Abu Hanifa said: Whoever says, My slave so-and-so drinks from the Euphrates, he is free, then he is not freed unless he sips from it. Sip is when a man drinks from the river with his mouth. If he drinks with his hand or scoops from it with a vessel, he is not freed, because God Almighty differentiates between sips from the river and drinking with the hand. He said: This is invalid, because drinking water is applied to every form and description in the Arabic language, from scooping with the hand or sipping with the mouth, all in one go. So if he finds the drinking that he swore upon linguistically and in reality, he has broken his oath, so know that. I said: The statement of Abu Hanifa is more correct, because the linguists distinguished between them as they did in the Qur’an and the Sunnah. Al-Jawhari and others said: And he drank from the water karoo’an if he took it with his mouth from its place without drinking with his hands or from a vessel. And there is another language for it (karoo’) with a kasra on the ra’, yakru’ kar’an, and karoo’ is the rain water from which one drank. As for the Sunnah, Ibn Majah mentioned in his Sunan: Wasil ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Amir, “on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: We passed by a pond and we began to drank from it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not drank from it, but wash your hands and then drink from it, for there is no vessel purer than the hand.” And this is the text, and Muslim narrated from Laith ibn Abi Sulaym, and he is weak. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: Except for he who scoops up a handful with his hand. Scooping up means taking from something with the hand and with a tool, and from it the ladle, and scooping up is like scooping up, and it was read (ghurfa) with the opening of the ghain and it is a source, and he did not say scooping up, because the meaning of scooping up and scooping up is one, and ghurfa is one time, and it was read (ghurfa) with the damma of the ghain and it is the thing scooped up, and some of the commentators said: ghurfa is with one hand and ghurfa is with both hands, and some of them said: both of them are two languages with one meaning, and Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: The palms are the cleanest vessels, and this is what Al-Hasan said: They do not enter water with a vessel except to scoop from the pools with wine. Al-Daleef: walking slowly. I said: Whoever wants pure, lawful money in these times without doubt, uncertainty or suspicion, let him drink with both hands water from the enchanted springs and rivers running during the night and during the day, seeking thereby from God to earn good deeds, put away sins and join the righteous Imams. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever drinks with his hand while he is able to hold a vessel, intending thereby to be humble, God will write for him the number of good deeds as many as his fingers. This is the vessel of Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon them, when he threw down the cup and said: ‘Uff is this with this world.’” It was narrated by Ibn Majah from the hadith of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade us from drinking on our stomachs, which is the dregs, and he forbade us from scooping up with one hand. He said: ‘Let none of you lap as a dog laps, nor drink with one hand as the people with whom God is angry drink, nor drink at night from a vessel until he stirs it, unless it is a fermented vessel. Whoever drinks with his hand while he is able to hold a vessel...’” The hadith is as mentioned above, and in its chain of transmission is Baqiyya ibn al-Waleed. Abu Hatim said: His hadith is to be written down but it is not to be used as evidence. Abu Zar’ah: If the rest of the narrations are narrated by trustworthy people, then he is trustworthy. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: So they drank from it, except for a few of them. Ibn Abbas said: They drank according to their certainty. The infidels drank like wild animals, and the sinners drank less than that. Seventy-six thousand of the people departed, and some of the believers remained without drinking anything, and some of them took a handful. As for those who drank, they were not quenched, but rather thirst overcame them. As for those who left the water, their solution was good and they were more steadfast than those who took a handful. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: And when he crossed it The ha’ refers to the river, and he is an emphasis. And those is in the nominative case in apposition to the pronoun in he crossed it. It is said: I crossed the place by crossing and passing, and metaphor in speech is what is permissible in usage and is implemented and continues in its proper form. Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi said: Four thousand men crossed the river with him, among them were those who drank, and when they looked at Goliath and his soldiers, and they were one hundred thousand, all of them doubting their weapons, three thousand, six hundred and eighty-some returned from them. So based on this statement, the believers who were certain of the resurrection and the return to God Almighty said at that time, and they were the number of the people of Badr: How many a small company has overcome a large company by permission of God. Most of the commentators said: Only those who did not drink crossed the river with him at all, so some of them said: How can we bear the enemy with their large number! The resolute ones among them said: How often has a small group overcome a large group by God’s permission? Al-Bara’ bin Azib said: We used to say that the number of the people of Badr was like the number of the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, three hundred and some men, and in another narration, thirteen men, and none crossed with him except a believer. Eleventh: The Almighty said: Those who think said. Here, thinking means certainty, and it is possible that it is doubt, not knowledge. That is, those who think that they will be killed with Talut and meet God as martyrs said, so doubt arose about the killing. The Almighty says: How often has a small company overcome a large company. The group: a group of people or a group of them. Whoever cuts off his head with the sword and cuts it off, their saying, may God be pleased with them: How often has a small company overcome a large company verse, is an incitement to fight and a sense of patience and following the example of those who are true to their Lord. I said: Is this how we should act? But the ugly deeds and corrupt intentions prevented that until the large number of us was broken in front of the small number of the enemy as we witnessed more than once, and that is because of what our hands have earned! And in Bukhari: Abu Darda said: You fight with your deeds, and in it is a chain of transmission “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you receive provision and victory except through your weak ones?” So the deeds are corrupt, the weak are neglected, patience is little, reliance is weak, and piety is fleeting! God the Almighty said: Be patient and endure and remain steadfast and fear God (Al Imran 3:200), and He said: And upon God rely (Al Ma’idah: 23), and He said: Indeed, God is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good (An Nahl: 128), and He said: And God will surely support those who support Him (Al Hajj: 40), and He said: When you meet a company, stand firm and remember God much that you may be successful (Al Anfal: 45). These are the reasons for victory and its conditions, which are non-existent with us and do not exist in us. Indeed, to God we belong and to Him we shall return, despite what has befallen us and has befallen us! Rather, nothing remains of Islam except its mention, and nothing remains of the religion except its form, due to the emergence of corruption, the increase in tyranny, and the lack of guidance, until the enemy has taken control of the east and the west, on land and sea, and tribulations have become widespread and trials have become great, and there is no protector except for those whom He has mercy upon!
