2:250: God Almighty said: And when they came forward to face Goliath and his soldiers, they said, ‘Our Lord, pour out upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.’ They came out they went out into the open, which is the widest part of the land, and Goliath was the prince of the giants and their king, his shadow was a mile long, and it is said that the Berbers were from his descendants, and he was, according to what was narrated, three hundred thousand horsemen, and Ikrimah said: ninety thousand, and when the believers saw the great number of their enemy they supplicated to their Lord, and this is like His saying: And how many a prophet fought with him many pious men until His saying: And their only saying was that they said, 'Our Lord, forgive us our sins' (Al Imran 3:146-147) the verse, and "When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met the enemy he would say in battle: O God, I seek refuge in You from their evils and I will make You in their throats," and he supplicated on the day of Badr until his cloak fell from his shoulders, seeking God's fulfillment of His promise as will be explained in (Al Imran) God willing.
2:251: The Almighty’s saying: So they defeated them by God’s permission meaning God sent down victory upon them, (So they defeated them), so they broke them. Defeat is breaking, and from this comes the word Mutazammu a water skin meaning that some of it folded over some of it due to dryness. From this comes what was said about Zamzam: It is Gabriel’s defeat, meaning Gabriel defeated it with his foot and the water came out. Defeat is what is broken from dry wood. God Almighty said: And David killed Goliath. This is because King Talut chose him from among his people to fight Goliath. He was a short, sick, yellow, blue-eyed man. Goliath was one of the strongest and most powerful people, and he defeated armies by himself. He killed Goliath, the leader of the giants, with his hand. He is David bin Ishi, with a broken hamza. It is also said: David bin Zakariya bin Rashwa. He was from the tribe of Judah bin Jacob bin Isaac bin Abraham, peace be upon them. He was from the people of Jerusalem. He combined prophethood and kingship for him after he had been a shepherd and was the youngest of his brothers. He used to tend sheep and had seven brothers among the companions of Talut. When the war came, he said to himself: I will go and see this war. When he got up on his way from a stone, he called out to it: O David, take me, for with me you will kill Goliath. Then another stone called out to him, then another, so he took it and put it in his saddlebags and walked. Goliath went out looking for a duel, but the people held back from him until Talut said: Whoever comes out to him and kills him, I will marry him to him. My daughter and I rule over my money, so David, peace be upon him, came and said: I will go out to him and kill him, but Talut despised him when he saw him because of his young age and short stature, so he sent him back, and David was blue-eyed and short, then he called a second and third time and David came out, and Talut said to him: Have you tried yourself with anything? He said yes, he said with what? He said: A wolf fell into my sheep, so I struck it, then I took its head and cut it off from its body, Talut said: The wolf is weak, have you tried yourself with something else? He said: Yes, a lion entered my sheep, so I struck it, then I took its jawbone and tore it, do you think this is stronger than a lion? He said no, and Talut had a shield that would not be fit except for someone who kills Goliath, so he told him about it and threw it on him and it was fit, so Talut said: Then ride my horse and take my weapon, so he did, and when he had walked a little he returned and the people said: The young man is a coward! Then David said: If God does not kill him for me and help him against me, this horse and this weapon will be of no use to me, but I would like to fight him as I usually do. He said: David was one of the best slingers of people, so he got down and took his saddlebags and put them on and took his sling and went out to Goliath, who was doubting his weapon and on his head was an egg containing three hundred pounds, according to what Al-Mawardi and others mentioned. Goliath said to him: You, young man, are you coming out to me? He said: Yes. He said: Like you go out to a dog! He said: Yes, and you are more insignificant. He said: I will feed your flesh today to the birds and wild beasts. Then they drew near and Goliath intended to take David by the hand in contempt of him, so David put his hand into the stones. It was narrated that they healed and became one stone. He took it and put it in the sling and said the name of God and turned it and threw it and it hit Goliath’s head and killed him. He cut off his head and put it in his saddlebags. The people mixed and Talut’s companions carried it and the defeat occurred. It was said: He only hit the nose of the egg with the stone, and it was said: His eye and it came out from the back of his head, and it hit a group of his army and killed them. It was said: The stone shattered until it hit everyone in the army with something, and it was like the fist that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, threw at Hawazin on the day of Hunayn. And God knows best. People have told many stories about these verses, and I have mentioned to you the intended meaning, and God is the Praiseworthy. I said: And in the saying of Talut: (And whoever comes out to him and kills him, I will marry him to my daughter and make him the judge of my wealth) its meaning is established in our law, and it is that the imam says whoever brings a head will have such and such, or a prisoner will have such and such, as will be explained in (Al-Anfal), God willing. And in it is evidence that dueling does not take place except with the permission of the imam, as Ahmad, Ishaq and others say, and there is a difference of opinion about it from Al-Awza’i, so it was narrated from him that he said: No one should attack except with the permission of the imam, and it was narrated from him that he said: There is nothing wrong with it, so if the imam forbids dueling, then no one should duel except with his permission, and a group permitted dueling and did not mention with the permission of the imam or without his permission. This is the saying of Malik. Malik was asked about a man who says between the two rows: Who will duel? He said: That depends on his intention. If he intends God by that, then I hope that there is no harm in it. He may have done that in the past. Al-Shafi’i said: There is nothing wrong with dueling. Ibn al-Mundhir said: Dueling with the permission of the imam is good, and there is no blame on the one who duels without the permission of the imam. It is not disliked because I do not know of any report that forbids it. And God gave him the kingdom and wisdom. Al-Suddi said: God gave him the kingdom of Talut and the prophethood of Simeon, and what he taught him was the making of armor and the language of birds and other types of what he, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught him. Ibn Abbas said: It is that God gave him a chain connected to the galaxy and the heavens and its head was at the monastery of David, so nothing happened in the air except that the chain would rattle and David would know what happened, and no one with a defect would touch it except that he would be cured. The sign of his people entering the religion was that they would touch it with their hands and then wipe their palms over their chests, and they would resort to it for judgment after David, peace be upon him, until it was removed. The Almighty says: From what He wills meaning from what He wills. The future tense may be used in place of the past tense, and this has been mentioned previously. The Almighty’s saying: “And had God not repelled some people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted. But God is full of bounty to the worlds.” There are two issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And had it not been that God repels some people by means of others, this is the reading of the group, except for Nafi’ who read (def’a) and it is permissible for it to be a source for a verb as it is said: I calculated the thing, and he returned, and I met him meeting, and likewise he wrote it a book, and from it is (the book of God upon you) (An-Nisa’: 24). An-Nahhas: This is good, so defense and defense are two sources for defense, and this is the doctrine of Sibawayh. Abu Hatim said: defense and defense have one meaning, like I struck the sandal and I struck it, meaning I sewed one of them over the other, and the stitching is the beads, and Abu Ubaidah chose the reading of the majority And had it not been that God repelled, and he denied that it should be read (def’a) and said: Because no one can overcome God, the Almighty. Makki said: This is a mistake in which he imagined the door of the mutual action, but it is not, and the name (God) is in the place of the nominative case of the verb, meaning had it not been that God repels, and (def’a) is raised by the beginning according to Sibawayh, (the people) is the object, (some of them) is a substitute for the people, (with some) is in the place of the second object according to Sibawayh, and it is like your saying, I went with Zaid, so Zaid is in the position of the object, so pay attention to it. Second: Scholars differed about the people who are driven to corruption. Who are they? It was said: They are the Abdal, and they are forty men. Whenever one of them dies, God replaces him with another. When the Day of Resurrection comes, they will all die, twenty-two of them in Syria and eighteen in Iraq. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The Abdal will be in Syria and they are forty men. Whenever one of them dies, God replaces him with a man who will provide water through them for the unseen, grant victory through them over the enemies, and avert calamity from the people of the earth through them. Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim mentioned this in Nawadir al-Usul. It was also narrated on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ who said: The prophets were pegs on the earth, and when prophethood ceased, God replaced them with people from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who are called the Abdal. They did not excel people by much fasting or prayer, but by good character, sincere piety, good intentions, and soundness of hearts for all Muslims, and advising them to seek the pleasure of God with patience, forbearance, understanding, and humility without humiliation. They are the successors of the prophets, people whom God chose for Himself and selected with His knowledge for Himself. They are forty truthful ones among them. Thirty men with the same certainty as Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, through whom God repels calamities from the people of the earth and disasters from the people, and through whom they receive rain and sustenance. Not a single one of them dies until God has created someone to replace him. Ibn Abbas said: Had God not repelled the enemy with the soldiers of the Muslims, the polytheists would have been victorious and killed the believers and destroyed the lands and mosques. Sufyan al-Thawri said: They are the witnesses through whom rights are extracted. Makki narrated that most of the commentators said that the meaning is: Had God not repelled those who pray from those who do not pray and those who fear God from those who do not fear God, people would have been destroyed for their sins. An-Nahhas and al-Tha’labi also mentioned this. Al-Tha’labi said: And the rest of the commentators said: Had God not defended the righteous believers from the wicked and the infidels, the earth would have been corrupted, meaning destroyed. He mentioned a hadith: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God repels punishment from those of my nation who pray from those who do not pray, from those who pay zakat from those who do not fast, from those who fast from those who do not fast, from those who perform Hajj from those who do not perform Hajj, and from those who strive from those who do not strive. Even if they were to unite to abandon…” These things, God did not look at them for the blink of an eye. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And if God did not repel some people by means of others, the earth would indeed be corrupted. And “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: God has angels who call out every day, ‘Were it not for the worshippers who bow, the children who graze, and the beasts who graze, He would pour down punishment upon you abundantly.’” Abu Bakr al-Khatib transmitted it with its meaning from the hadith of al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad. Mansur told us, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of ‘Alqamah, on the authority of ‘Abdullah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Were it not for the men among you who are humble, the beasts who graze, and the children who graze, He would pour down punishment upon the believers abundantly.’” Some of them took this meaning and said: If it were not for the servants of God who bowed down and the orphan girls who were breastfed And the wastelands graze in the desert, and the most painful torment is poured upon you. Jabir narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Verily, God reforms, through the righteousness of a man, his children, his children’s children, the people of his household, and the households around him, and they remain in God’s protection as long as he is with them.” Qatada said: God tests the believer with the disbeliever and heals the disbeliever with the believer. Ibn Umar said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Verily, God repels, through the righteous believer, a hundred of his family members and neighbors from calamity. Then Ibn Umar recited: And were it not that God checks some people by means of others, the earth would indeed be corrupted. It was said: This repelling is due to what was prescribed by the tongues of the Messengers of laws, and were it not for that, people would have robbed and plundered and perished. This is a good statement, for it is general in restraint and repelling and other things, so ponder it. But God is full of bounty to the worlds. The Almighty made clear that His repelling the evil of the disbelievers through the believers is a bounty and blessing from Him.
2:252: Those is the beginning, the verses of God is its predicate, and if you wish, it can be a substitute, and the predicate is We recite them to you in truth, and indeed, you are among the messengers is the predicate of in, meaning: and indeed, you are a messenger. God Almighty alerted His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that these verses that were mentioned earlier are only known to a messenger prophet.
2:253: The Almighty said: Those are the messengers. He said: (those) and did not say: that, taking into consideration the feminine form of the collective noun, and it is raised by the beginning, and (the messengers) is its description, and the predicate of the beginning is the sentence, and it was said: The messengers is an explanatory apposition, and We preferred is the predicate, and this is a problematic verse and the hadiths are established that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not choose between the prophets and Do not prefer between the prophets of God both of them were narrated by the trustworthy imams, meaning do not say: So-and-so is better than so-and-so, nor so-and-so is better than so-and-so, it is said: So-and-so chose between so-and-so and so-and-so, and prefer emphasized if he said that, and the scholars differed in the interpretation of this meaning, so some said: This was before the revelation of preference was sent to him, and before he knew that he was the master of the children of Adam and that the Qur’an abrogates the prohibition of preference, and Ibn Qutaybah said: What he meant by his saying: I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection is because The intercessor on that day will have the banner of praise and the Pool. He meant by his saying: Do not give me precedence over Moses, as a way of humility, as Abu Bakr said, I am your guardian, and I am not the best of you. Likewise, the meaning of his saying: Let no one say, ‘I am better than Jonah, son of Matta,’ is in the sense of humility. In the saying of God the Most High: And do not be like the companion of the fish (al-Qalam 68:48), there is what indicates that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is better than him, because God the Most High said: And do not be like him. This indicates that his saying: Do not give me precedence over him, is a way of humility. It is possible that he means do not give me precedence over him in knowledge, for perhaps he is better in action than me, nor in trial and testing, for he is a greater trial than me. What God gave to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, of leadership and superiority on the Day of Resurrection over all the prophets and messengers is not due to his action, but rather due to God’s preference of him and His choosing him for him. This interpretation was chosen by al-Muhallab, and some of them said: He only forbade delving into that, because delving into that is a pretext for argument, and that leads to mentioning from them what should not be mentioned. And their respect is diminished when arguing. Our Sheikh said: It is not said: The Prophet is better than all the prophets, nor better than so-and-so, nor better, as is apparent from the prohibition due to what is imagined of deficiency in the one who is preferred, because the prohibition required preventing the use of the word, not preventing the belief in that meaning, for God Almighty informed us that the messengers are distinguished, so do not say: Our Prophet is better than the prophets, nor better than so-and-so the prophet, avoiding what He forbade and being polite with it and acting in accordance with the belief in what the Qur’an includes of preference, and God is All-Knowing of the truths of matters. I said: Better than this is the statement of the one who said: The prohibition of preference is only from the aspect of prophethood, which is a single characteristic in which there is no differentiation, and preference is only in the increase of conditions, specialness, honors, kindnesses, and different miracles. As for prophethood in itself, it is not differentiable, but rather it is differentiable by other matters in addition to it. Therefore, among them are messengers and those of resolve, and among them are those who were taken as friends, and among them are those whom God spoke to and raised some of them in degrees. God Almighty said: And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Psalms (al-Isra’ 17:55), and He said: “Those are the messengers. We preferred some of them over others.” I said: This is a good statement, for it combines the verses and hadiths without abrogation. The statement that some are preferred over others is only due to the virtues they were granted and the means they were given. Ibn Abbas referred to this and said: God preferred Muhammad over the prophets and the people of heaven. They said: O Ibn Abbas, how did He prefer him over the people of heaven? He said: God the Most High said: “And whoever among them says, ‘I am a god besides Him’ - We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers” (Al-Anbiya’: 29), and He said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest, that God may forgive you what preceded of your sin and what will follow (al-Fath 48:1-2). They said: So what is his preference over the prophets? He said, God Almighty said: And We did not send any messenger except with the language of his people to make things clear to them (Ibrahim 14:4), and God Almighty said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And We have not sent you except as a mercy to mankind (Saba 34:28), so He sent him to the jinn and mankind. Abu Muhammad al-Darimi mentioned this in his Musnad, and Abu Hurayrah said: The best of the sons of Adam are Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are the resolute messengers. This is a text from Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayrah in designation, and it is known that the one who was sent is better than the one who was not sent, for the one who was sent was preferred over others with the message and they were equal in prophethood until what the messengers encounter of their nations’ denial and killing of them, and this is something that is not hidden, except that Ibn Atiyah Abu Muhammad Abdul Haqq said: The Qur’an requires preference, and that is in general without designating anyone who is preferred, and so are the hadiths, and for this reason the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the most honored of the sons of Adam to my Lord and he said: I am the master of the sons of Adam, and he did not… He appointed, and he, peace be upon him, said: No one should say I am better than Jonah, son of Matta, and he said: Do not prefer me over Moses, and Ibn Atiyah said: In this is a strong prohibition against appointing the inferior, because Jonah, peace be upon him, was young and had disintegrated under the burdens of prophethood, so if the appointment was for Muhammad, peace be upon him, then it is more appropriate for someone else. I said: What we have chosen is more appropriate, God willing, because when God Almighty informed that He preferred some of them over others, He began to clarify some of those who were preferred and to mention the conditions by which they were preferred, so He said: “Among them are those to whom God spoke, and He raised some of them in degree. And We gave Jesus, the son of Mary, clear proofs.” And He said: And We gave David the Psalms. (al-Isra’ 17:55), and God Almighty said: And We gave him the Gospel. (al-Ma’idah 5:46), And We had certainly given Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous. (Al-Anbiya’: 48), and God Almighty said: And We had certainly given David and Solomon knowledge. (Al-Naml: 15), and He said: And when We took a covenant from the prophets, and from you and from Noah. (al-Ahzab 33:7), so He generalized and then made it specific and began with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is clear. I said: And this is what is said about the Companions, God willing. They shared in companionship, then differed in virtues through the talents and means that God bestowed upon them. They are distinguished by that, although they were all included in companionship, justice, and praise. And it is sufficient for you to have His true statement: Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and those with him are strong against the disbelievers (al-Fath 48:29) to the end of the surah. And He said: And He made them adhere to the word of piety, and they were more deserving of it and more worthy of it (al-Fath 48:26). Then He said: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought (al-Hadid 57:10). And He said: God was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree (al-Fath 48:18). So He made it general and specific, and He denied them any shame or deficiency. May God be pleased with them all and benefit us through their love, amen. The Almighty said: Among them are those to whom God spoke, the one who spoke was Moses, peace be upon him. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about Adam, was he a prophet sent? He said: Yes, a prophet who was spoken to,” Ibn Atiyah said, and some people have interpreted that Adam was spoken to in Paradise, so based on this, the specificity of Moses remains, and the ha’ was deleted due to the length of the name, and the meaning is from whom God spoke. God the Almighty said: And He raised some of them in degrees. An-Nahhas said: Some of them here, according to the statement of Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha’bi, and Mujahid, are Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, “He said, may God bless him and grant him peace: I was sent to the red and the black, and the earth was made a place of prostration and purification for me, and I was aided by terror, a distance of a month’s journey, and spoils were made lawful for me, and intercession was given.” And from that is the Qur’an, and the splitting of the moon, and his speaking to the trees, and his feeding food, a great creation of dates and milk from the sheep of Umm Ma’bad after it had dried up. Ibn Atiyyah said its meaning, and he added: And he is the greatest of people in nation, and the prophets were sealed with him, and other great creations that God gave him. And the wording may mean Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others whose signs were great, and the statement is an emphasis. And it may mean the raising of Idris to the high place and the ranks of the prophets in heaven, as in the hadith of the Night Journey, and it will come, and the signs of Jesus are the revival of the dead, the healing of the blind and the leper, and the creation of birds from clay, as stated in the revelation. And We supported him strengthened him with the Holy Spirit Gabriel, peace be upon him, and it has been mentioned before. God the Almighty said: And if God had willed, those after them would not have fought one another. That is, after the messengers: It was said: The pronoun refers to Moses and Jesus, and both are plural. It was also said: The messengers came after them, and what is apparent is that people did not fight one another after every prophet. This is like saying: I bought horses and then sold them. This expression is permissible for you, and you only bought a horse and sold it, then another and sold it, then another and sold it. Likewise, these calamities: people differed after every prophet, some of them believed and some of them disbelieved out of envy and envy and for the ruins of this world. All of that is by the decree, destiny and will of God the Almighty. If He had willed otherwise, it would have been, but He is the One who keeps the secret of the wisdom in that action for what He wills. The nun in but they differed was broken due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, and it is permissible to delete it in places other than the Qur’an. Sibawayh recited: I will not come, nor can I. Give me a drink if your water is plentiful. Some of them believed and some of them disbelieved. “Some” is in the nominative case as a subject and an adjective.
2:254: Al-Hasan said: It is the obligatory zakat. Ibn Jurayj Saeed bin Jubair said: This verse includes the obligatory zakat and the voluntary zakat. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is correct, but the verses that preceded it mentioning fighting and that God repels the believers in the hearts of the disbelievers indicate that this exhortation is only for the sake of God, and this is strengthened by the statement at the end of the verse: And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers, meaning, fight them by fighting with your lives and spending money. I said: According to this interpretation, spending money is sometimes obligatory and sometimes recommended, depending on whether jihad is necessary or not. God Almighty commanded His servants to spend from what God has provided for them and bestowed upon them, and warned them against withholding until a day comes when it will be impossible to buy or sell or to make up for the expenses, as He said: Then he will say, ‘My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term so I could give charity.’ (al-Munafiqun 63:10), and friendship is pure affection taken from the sharing of secrets between two friends, and friendship, kinship, and kinship and affection are friendship and affection. The poet said: How do you communicate with someone who has become like Abu Marhab? Abu Marhab is the nickname of the shadow, and it is said: he is the nickname of Arqoub about whom it was said: Arqoub’s appointments, and Khallah also with the dammah: what is devoid of plants, it is said: Khallah is the bread of camels and the sour is its fruit, and Khallah with the fathah: need and poverty, and Khallah: the son of a young camel, on the authority of Al-Asma’i, it is said: he came to them with a loaf like the horse of Khallah, and the female is also Khallah, and it is said to the dead: O God, fix his Khallah, meaning the gap that he left, and Khallah: sour wine, and Khallah with the kasrah: one of the Khallahs of swords, and they are linings that were used to cover the lids of swords engraved with gold and other things, and they are also belts that are worn on the back of the bow’s handle, and Khallah is also: what remains between the teeth, and the derivation of Khalil and its meaning and its meaning will come in (An-Nisa), so God Almighty informed that there is no Khallah in the Hereafter and no intercession except with the permission of God. Its reality is the mercy of God Almighty, with which He honored the one whom He permitted to intercede. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read there is no sale in it, nor friendship, nor intercession in the accusative case without tanween. Likewise in Surat Ibrahim there is no sale in it, nor friendship and in At-Tur there is no idle talk in it, nor sin. Hassan bin Thabit recited: No stabbing, no ordinary knights, except your belching at the skirts The interrogative alif does not change the function of la like when you say: Is there no man with you? It is permissible to say Is there no man and no woman just as it is permissible in non-interrogative cases, so learn from it. The rest read all of that with the nominative and tanween as al-Ra’i said: I did not cut you off until I said openly, I have no camel or horse in this It is narrated: (And I did not abandon you), so the opening is on the general negation that includes all aspects of that type, as if it is an answer to someone who said: Is there any sale in it? So he asked a general question and was given a general answer with the negation and (La) with the negated noun is like a single noun in the place of raising the subject, and the predicate is (in it) and if you wish you can make it an attribute of the day, and whoever raises it makes (La) like there is not, and makes the answer non-general, and as if it is an answer to someone who said: Is there any sale in it? By dropping from, so the answer came without changing its raising, and the raised is the subject or the name of not and (in it) is the predicate, Makki said: The choice is the raising, because most of the reciters are on it, and it is permissible in other than the Qur’an, there is no sale in it nor friendship, and Sibawayh recited for a man from Madhhij: This is for your young age, I have no mother, if that is the case, and no father. It is permissible to construct the first and put the second in the accusative and add a tanween, so you say: There is no man in it nor a woman. Sibawayh recited: There is no lineage today, nor any friendship, the tear is too wide for the patcher There is no redundancy in both places, the first is in apposition to the place and the second to the word. A fifth way is to raise the first and build the second, like when you say: There is no man in it nor a woman. Umayya said: There is no idle talk or idle talk in it, and what they say is permanent. These five aspects are permissible in your saying: There is no power or strength except with God. This has been mentioned before, and praise be to God: And the disbelievers is the beginning, they is the second beginning, the wrongdoers is the predicate of the second, and if you wish, they is redundant for separation and the wrongdoers is the predicate of the disbelievers, said Ata’ ibn Dinar. Praise be to God who said: And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers and did not say and the wrongdoers are the disbelievers.
2:255: The Almighty said: God, there is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. This is the Throne Verse, the master of the verses of the Qur'an and the greatest verse, as was explained in Al-Fatihah. It was revealed at night and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Zaid and he wrote it down. It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah that he said: When the Throne Verse was revealed, every idol in the world fell down, and likewise every king in the world fell down and the crowns fell from their heads, and the devils fled, striking one another until they came to Iblis and informed him of that, so he ordered them to search for it. So they came to Madinah and it reached them that the Throne Verse had been revealed. The Imams narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Abu Al-Mundhir, do you know which verse of the Book of God with you is the greatest? I said: God, there is no god except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. He struck me on the chest and said: May knowledge be blessed for you, O Abu Al-Mundhir. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, this verse has a tongue and two lips that sanctify the King at the foot of the Throne. Abu Abdullah said: This is a verse that God, the Most High, revealed, and made its reward for its reader both immediate and future. As for the immediate, it is a guard for whoever recites it from calamities. It was narrated to us from Nawf Al-Bakali that he said: The Throne Verse is called in the Torah the guardian of God, meaning that the one who recites it is called the Mighty in the Kingdom of the Heavens and the Earth. He said: When Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf entered his house, he would recite the Throne Verse in the four corners of his house, meaning that he was seeking thereby for it to be a guard for him from its four sides, and to repel Satan from him from the corners of his house. It was narrated from Omar that he wrestled with a jinn, and Omar, may God be pleased with him, defeated him. The jinn said to him: Leave me alone until I teach you how you can protect yourself from us. So he left him and asked him, and he said: You protect yourself from us with the Throne Verse. I said: This is correct. In the hadith: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every prayer, the One who takes charge of taking his soul will be the One with Majesty and Honor, and he will be like one who fought with the Prophets of God until he was martyred. And on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, he said: I heard your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say while he was on the steps of the pulpit: Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every prayer, nothing will prevent him from entering Paradise except death, and none will persevere in it except a friend or a worshipper. And whoever recites it when he goes to bed, God will make him safe for himself, his neighbor, his neighbor’s neighbor, and the houses around him. And in al-Bukhari: On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entrusted me with guarding the zakat of Ramadan, and he mentioned a story in which: So I said: O Messenger of God, he claimed that he would teach me words by which God would benefit me, so I let him go. He said: What are they? I said: He said to me: When you go to bed, recite Ayat al-Kursi from the beginning until you finish: God, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Sustaining. And he said to me: There will remain a guardian from God over you, and no devil will come near you until morning. And they were the most eager for goodness. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “He has told you the truth, although he is a liar. Do you know who you have been talking to for the past three nights, O Abu Hurairah?” He said: No. He said: That was Satan. In Musnad al-Darimi, Abu Muhammad, al-Sha’bi said: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: A man from the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, met a man from the jinn and wrestled with him. A human defeated him. The human said to him: “I see that you are weak and weak, as if your arms were the arms of a dog. Is that how you are with the jinn? Or are you also one of them?” He said: “No, by God! I am one of them, but come back to me a second time. If you defeat me, I will teach you something that will benefit you.” He said: Yes. So he defeated him. He said: “Do you recite the Throne Verse: ‘God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining’?” He said: We curse. He said: For you do not recite it in a house except that the devil leaves it with a gait like the gait of a donkey, and he does not enter it until morning. Abu Naim narrated it on the authority of Abu Asim Al-Thaqafi on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, and Abu Ubaid mentioned it in Gharib Hadith Umar. Abu Mu’awiyah narrated it on the authority of Abu Asim Al-Thaqafi on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Abdullah, who said: It was said to Abdullah: Is it Umar? He said: It could be none other than Umar! Abu Muhammad al-Daraami said: Da’il means thin, Shakhit means emaciated, Dhale’ means well-ribbed, and Khabaj means wind. Abu Ubaidah said: Khabaj means flatulence, and it is also Habaj with a ha. In al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever recites “Ha Meem” - the believer - To Him is the destination and Ayat al-Kursi when he wakes up will preserve them until the evening, and whoever recites them when he goes to bed will preserve them until the morning.” He said: A strange hadith. Abu Abdullah al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim said: It was narrated that the believers were encouraged to preserve their recitation after every prayer. Anas traced the hadith back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God revealed to Moses, peace be upon him: Whoever persists in reciting “Ayat al-Kursi” after every prayer, I will give him more than what I give to the grateful, and the reward of the prophets and the deeds of the truthful, and I will extend my right hand over him with mercy, and nothing will prevent me from admitting him to Paradise except that the Angel of Death comes to him.” Moses, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, who has heard of this and does not persist in it? He said: I do not give it to any of My servants except that I give it to them. “To a prophet, a friend, a man I love, or a man I want to kill in My path,” and “On the authority of Abi bin Ka’b, he said: God Almighty said: O Moses, whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi after every prayer, I will give him the reward of the prophets,” Abu Abdullah said: Its meaning, in my opinion, is that I will give him the reward of the deeds of the prophets. As for the garment of prophethood, it is not for anyone except the prophets. This verse includes monotheism and the sublime attributes, and it is fifty words, and in each word there are fifty blessings, and it is equal to a third of the Qur’an. This was mentioned in the hadith, mentioned by Ibn Atiyah. God is the subject, and there is no god is a second subject and its predicate is omitted, its meaning is worshipped or exists, and except Him is a substitute for the place of there is no god, and it was said: God, there is no god except Him is the subject and predicate, and it is raised and carried on the meaning, that is, there is no god except Him, and it is permissible in other than the Qur’an, there is no god except Him, the accusative as an exception. Abu Dharr said in his long hadith: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which verse God revealed to you from the Qur’an is the greatest? He said: God, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Sustaining. Ibn Abbas said: The most honorable verse in the Qur’an is the Throne Verse. Some scholars said: Because the name of God Almighty is repeated in it, both implicitly and explicitly, eighteen times. Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum is an attribute of God the Almighty, and if you wish, it is a substitute for (He), and if you wish, it is a predicate after a predicate, and if you wish, it is an implied subject. It is permissible in other than the Qur’an to put it in the accusative case for praise. (Al-Hayy) is one of His beautiful names by which He is called. It is said that it is the greatest name of God the Almighty. It is said that when Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, wanted to revive the dead, he would call out with this supplication: O Al-Hayy, O Al-Qayyum. It is said that when Asaf bin Barkhiya wanted to bring the throne of Bilqis to Solomon, he called out by saying: O Al-Hayy, O Al-Qayyum. It is said that the Children of Israel asked Moses about the greatest name of God, and he said to them: O Yahya Sharahiya, meaning O Al-Hayy, O Al-Qayyum. It is said that it is the supplication of the people of the sea when they fear drowning, they call out with it. Al-Tabari said on the authority of some al-Nas 114:It is said that Al-Hayy Al-Qayyum as He described Himself, and this is accepted without looking into it. It is said that He called Himself Al-Hayy because He directs matters according to their expenditures and measures things according to their amounts. Qatada said: The Al-Hayy is the one who does not die. Al-Suddi: What is meant by the living is the eternal. Labid said: If you see me today, I am safe and sound, and I am no more alive than dogs and jafar It has been said: This name is the greatest name of God, Al-Qayyum from Qaam, meaning the one who is in charge of managing what He created, according to Qatada. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is the one who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned until He rewards it for its work, since He is aware of it and nothing of it is hidden from Him. Ibn Abbas said: Its meaning is the one who does not change or disappear. Umayyah ibn Abi Al-Salt said: The sky, the stars, and the sun were not created with a moon rising His power is dominant, self-sustaining, and the gathering, and Paradise, and bliss. Except for a matter of great importance Al-Bayhaqi said: I saw in Uyun al-Tafsir by Ismail al-Dharee’ in the interpretation of al-Qayyum, he said: It is said that it is the one who does not sleep, and it is as if he took it from the saying of the Almighty after it in the Throne Verse: Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. Al-Kalbi said: The Qayyum is the one who has no beginning, Abu Bakr al-Anbari mentioned it, and the origin of Qayyum is Qayyum, the waw and the ya’ came together and one of them was preceded by a sukoon, so the first was assimilated into the second after changing the waw to a ya’, and Qayyum is not fa’ul, because it is from the waw, so it would be qawwam. Ibn Mas’ud, Alqamah, al-A’mash, and al-Nakha’i read (al-Hayy al-Qiyam) with an alif, and this was narrated from Umar, and there is no disagreement among the linguists that al-Qayyum is more familiar to the Arabs and more correct in construction and more proven in cause, and al-Qiyam is transferred from al-Qawam to al-Qiyam, diverted from al-Fa’al to al-Fa’aal, as al-Sarraagh is al-Sayyaagh, the poet said: Verily, the Lord of the Throne is He who provides for mankind and inspires them with knowledge. Then the Almighty denied that drowsiness or sleep would overtake Him. Drowsiness is drowsiness according to everyone, and drowsiness is what comes from the eye, but when it reaches the heart it becomes sleep. Adi bin Al-Ruqa’ said, describing a woman with a dull gaze: And Sinan, I mean sleepiness, I saw a squint in his eye, but he is not asleep Al-Mufaddal distinguished between them, saying: Sleeping is in the head, drowsiness is in the eye, and sleep is in the heart. Ibn Zayd said: The sleepy one is the one who gets up from sleep and is not conscious, to the point that he might draw his sword against his family. Ibn Atiyah said: What Ibn Zayd said is questionable, and it is not understood from the speech of the Arabs. Al-Suddi said: Sleeping is the smell of sleep that takes hold of the face and makes a person drowsy. I said: In short, it is a lethargy that befalls a person without causing him to lose his mind. What is meant by this verse is that God Almighty is not affected by any defect or boredom under any circumstances. The original form of sunnah and sunnah was deleted from yasan as it was deleted from yasan. Sleep is the heavy burden that causes the mind to go away in the case of humans, and the waw is for conjunction, and la is for emphasis. I said: And the people mention in this chapter “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating about Moses on the pulpit. He said: It occurred to Moses whether God, may His praise be glorified, would sleep. So God sent an angel to him who kept him awake for three days. Then he gave him two bottles, one in each hand, and ordered him to keep them. He said: So he would sleep and his hands would almost meet, then he would wake up and move one away from the other until he slept and his hands clapped together and the two bottles broke. He said: God gave him an example that if he slept, the heavens and the earth would not hold together.” This hadith is not authentic, and it was deemed weak by more than one of them, including Al-Bayhaqi. The Almighty says: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, meaning by dominion, for He is the Owner of all and its Lord. The phrase came with what even though there is in the sentence someone who has a mind in terms of what is meant by the sentence and the existent. Al-Tabari said: This verse was revealed when the infidels said: We only worship idols so that they may bring us closer to God. God the Almighty says: Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? “Min” is the subject and dha is its predicate, and alladhi is an adjective for dha or, if you wish, a substitute. It is not permissible for dha to be redundant as it was added with ma because ma is ambiguous, so dha was added with it because of its resemblance to it. It is established in this verse that God gives permission to whomever He wills to intercede, and they are the prophets, scholars, mujahidin, angels, and others whom God has honored and glorified. Then they do not intercede except for whom He is pleased with, as He said: And they do not intercede except for whom He is pleased with (Al-Anbiya’: 28). Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: What appears is that the scholars and righteous intercede for those who did not reach the Fire and are between the two stations, or did reach it but had righteous deeds. In Al-Bukhari in The Chapter of the Remainder of the Chapters of Vision: The believers say: Our Lord, our brothers used to pray with us and fast with us, and this is intercession for those whose matter is brought near. And just as the child who is in love intercedes at the gates of Paradise, this is only for their relatives and acquaintances, and the prophets intercede for those who are in the Fire from the sinners of their nations without kinship or acquaintance except through the same faith, then remains the intercession of the Most Merciful of the Merciful for those who are immersed in sins and wrongdoings for whom the intercession of the prophets did not work, and as for the intercession of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to hasten the reckoning, it is specifically for him. I said: Muslim has explained in his Sahih the manner of intercession in a clear explanation, and it is as if, may God have mercy on him, he did not read it, and that the intercessors enter Hell and bring out of it people who deserved punishment. Based on this, it is not far-fetched that the believers will have two intercessions: intercession for those who did not reach Hell, and intercession for those who reached it and entered it, may God protect us from it. He mentioned from the hadith of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri: Then the bridge will be struck over Hell and intercession will be permitted and they will say, O God, save, save. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is the bridge? He said: A slippery slope in which there are hooks and claws and thorns in Najd in which there is a thorn called Al-Sa’dan. The believers will pass by like the blink of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like birds, like the best horses and riders. Some will be saved, some will be deceived, some will be sent away, and some will be crushed into the fire of Hell until the believers are freed from the Fire. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, there is none among you who will implore God more fervently to fulfill his right than the believers on the Day of Resurrection for their brothers who are in Hell. They will say, Our Lord, they used to fast with us, pray, and perform Hajj. Then it will be said to them: Bring out whomever you know. Their images will be forbidden to the Fire. They will bring out a large number of people, the Fire having taken up half of their shins and up to their knees. Then they will say: Our Lord, there is no one left in it whom You have commanded us to do. Then the Almighty will say: Go back, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of a dinar of goodness, bring him out. Then they will bring out a large number of people. Then they will say: Our Lord, we have not left in it anyone whom You have commanded us to do. Then He will say: Hopefully, whoever you find in his heart the weight of half a dinar of goodness, bring him out. Then they will bring out a large number of people. Then they will say: Our Lord, we have not left in it anyone whom You have commanded us to do. Then He will say: Go back, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of an atom of goodness, bring him out. Then they will bring out a large number of people. Then they will say: Our Lord, we have not left in it any of those... say: Our Lord, we have not left in it any of those whom You have commanded us to do. Then He will say: Go back, and whoever you find in his heart the weight of an atom of goodness, bring him out. Then they will say: Our Lord, we have not left in it any of those whom You have commanded us to do The prophets and the believers will intercede, and none will remain except the Most Merciful of the merciful. He will take a handful of fire and bring out of it a people who never did any good and have turned into charcoal. He mentioned the hadith and mentioned the hadith of Anas, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I will say, ‘O Lord, give me permission regarding those who said, ‘There is no god but God.’ He will say, ‘That is not for You,’ or he will say, ‘That is not up to You. By My glory, majesty, greatness, and might, I will bring out those who said, ‘There is no god but God.’” He mentioned the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God bless him and grant him peace, “Until when God has finished judging between His servants and wants to bring out by His mercy whomever He wants from the people of the Fire, He will command the angels to bring out of the Fire whoever did not associate anything with God, whom God Almighty wanted to have mercy on, from those who say, ‘There is no god but God.’ They will recognize them in the Fire, they will recognize them by the mark of prostration. The Fire will consume the son of Adam except the mark of prostration. God has forbidden the Fire to consume the mark of prostration.” The hadith in its entirety. I said: These hadiths indicate that the intercession of the believers and others is only for those who have entered the Fire and are in it, may God protect us from it! Ibn Atiyyah’s statement: For those who did not pray or did pray may have been taken from other hadiths, and God knows best. Ibn Majah included in his Sunan on the authority of Anas ibn Malik who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘On the Day of Resurrection, people will be in rows.’” Ibn Numayr said: “The people of Paradise will stand in rows. A man from the people of the Fire will pass by another man and say: ‘O so-and-so, do you not remember the day you asked for water and I gave you a drink?’ He will shine for him. A man will pass by another man and say: ‘Do you not remember the day I gave you purification?’ He will intercede for him. Ibn Numayr said: ‘And so-and-so will say: ‘Remember the day you sent me for such-and-such a need and I went to you?’ He will intercede for him.’ As for the intercessions of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, there is disagreement about them. It was said that they were three, and it was said that they were two, and it was said that they were five. Their explanation will come in “Glory be to God,” God willing. We have already mentioned them in the Book of Remembrance, and praise be to God. The Almighty says: He knows what is before them and what is behind them. The two pronouns refer to every rational being included in His statement: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Mujahid said: What is before them is this world, and what is behind them is the Hereafter. Ibn Atiyyah said: All of this is correct in itself, there is nothing wrong with it, because what is before is everything that a person has done, and what is behind him is everything that comes after him. Al-Suddi and others said something similar to what Mujahid said. The Almighty says: And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills. Knowledge here means the known, that is, they do not encompass anything of His information. This is like what Al-Khasr said to Moses, peace be upon him, when the bird pecked at the sea: My knowledge and your knowledge do not decrease from the knowledge of God except as this bird decreased from this sea. This and what is similar to it refer to the information, because the knowledge of God, glory be to Him, which is an attribute of His essence, is not divisible, and the meaning of the verse is known to everyone except what God wills him to know. God the Almighty said: His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth. Ibn Asakir mentioned in his history on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Throne is a pearl and the Pen is a pearl, and the length of the Pen is seven hundred years, and the length of the Throne is such that no one knows it except God.” Hammad bin Salamah narrated on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, who is Asim bin Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: Between every two heavens is a journey of five hundred years, and between the seventh and the Throne is five hundred years, and between the Throne and the Throne is a journey of five hundred years, and the Throne is above the water, and God is above the Throne, and He knows what you are in and upon. It is said: Kursi and Kursi, and the plural is Kursi. Ibn Abbas said: His Kursi is His knowledge, and al-Tabari preferred it. He said: And from it is the notebook that holds knowledge, and from it is said for scholars: the Kursi, because they are relied upon, just as it is said: the pegs of the earth. The poet said: They lighten their faces and make them a group of chairs when events come That is, the scholars of the events of things. It was said: His throne is His power by which He holds the heavens and the earth, as you say: Make a throne for this wall, meaning what supports it. This is close to what Ibn Abbas said in his statement: (His throne encompasses all things) Al-Bayhaqi said: We narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud and Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas in his statement: (His throne encompasses all things) He said: His knowledge. The rest of the narrations on the authority of Ibn Abbas and others indicate that what is meant by it is the throne that is famous with the throne. Israel narrated on the authority of Al-Saddī on the authority of Abu Malik in his statement: (His throne encompasses the heavens and the earth) He said: The rock on which the seventh earth is and the end of creation on its sides, on it are four angels, each of them has four faces: the face of a human, the face of a lion, the face of a bull, and the face of an eagle. They are standing on it and have surrounded the earths and the heavens, and their heads are under the thrones and the throne is under the throne and God has placed His throne above the throne. Al-Bayhaqi said: In this there is an indication of two thrones: one under the throne, and the other placed on the throne. In the narration of Asbat on the authority of Al-Saddī on the authority of Abu Malik, and on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Marra Al-Hamdani on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Marra Al-Hamdani on the authority of Ibn Masoud on the authority of some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, His Throne encompasses the heavens and the earth, for the heavens and the earth are in the interior of the Throne, and the Throne is between the hands of the Throne, and the masters of heresy attribute it to the greatness of the Kingdom and the majesty of the Sultan, and they deny the existence of the Throne and the Throne, and they are nothing, and the people of truth permit them, since in the power of God there is room, so it is necessary to believe in that. Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari said: The Throne is the place of the feet and it has the creaking of a saddle. Al-Bayhaqi said: We have also narrated on this from Ibn Abbas and we mentioned that its meaning, in what he sees, is that it is placed on the Throne in the place of the feet on the bed, and it does not establish a place for God Almighty. And on the authority of Ibn Buraidah on the authority of his father, he said: When Ja’far came from Abyssinia, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What is the most amazing thing you have seen? He said: I saw a woman with a basket of food on her head, and a knight passed by and scattered it, so she sat down and gathered her food, then she turned to him and said to him: Woe to you on the day when the King places his Throne and takes for the oppressed from the oppressor! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in confirmation of her words: No nation is sanctified - or how can a nation be sanctified - whose weak do not take their right from their strong. Ibn Atiyyah said: In Abu Musa’s statement, The Throne is the place of the feet, he meant that it is to the Throne of the Most Merciful like the place of the feet in the beds of kings. It is a great creation in front of the Throne, and its relation to it is like the relation of the Throne to the king’s bed. Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan said: The Throne is the Throne itself, and this is not acceptable to me. What the hadiths require is that the Throne is created in front of the Throne, and the Throne is greater than it. Abu Idris al-Khawlani narrated, “On the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: I said, O Messenger of God, which of what God has revealed to you is the greatest? He said: The Throne Verse. Then they said, O Abu Dharr, what are the seven heavens in comparison to the Throne except like a ring thrown in a desert land, and the superiority of the Throne over the Throne is like the superiority of the desert over the ring.” It was narrated by al-Ajurri and Abu Hatim al-Basti in his Sahih Musnad and al-Bayhaqi, and he mentioned that it is authentic. Mujahid said: The heavens and the earth in comparison to the Throne are nothing but like a ring thrown in a desert land. This verse indicates the greatness of God Almighty’s creations, and from that we learn the greatness of God Almighty, as He is not burdened by the preservation of this great matter. The meaning of ya’udah is ya’duhu he weighs him down. It is said: Adani means it weighed me down and I endured hardship from it. This is how the word was interpreted by Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatada, and others. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for the ha to be for God Almighty, and it is permissible for it to be for the Throne. If it is for the Throne, then it is from the command of God Almighty. And the Most High means the loftiness of status and position, not the loftiness of place, because God is exalted above being localized. Al-Tabari narrated on the authority of some people that they said: He is the Most High above His creation by the elevation of His place above the places of His creation. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is the saying of ignorant anthropomorphists, and it should not have been narrated. And on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Qut that on the night of his ascension the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard glorification in the high heavens: Glory be to God, the Most High, the Most High, glory be to Him and Most High. The Most High and the Most High: the Conqueror, the Victorious over things. The Arabs say: So-and-so overtook so-and-so, meaning he overcame and subdued him. The poet said: Then, when we had gained control over them, we left them slain before an eagle and a bird of prey. And from it is the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land (al-Qasas 28:4), and the great is an adjective meaning great in status, danger, and honor, not in the sense of greatness of bodies. Al-Tabari narrated from some people that the great means the honored, just as it is said: the ancient means the freed, and he recited the verse of Al-A’sha: The old wine was made from the spout mixed with pure water. It was narrated that some people denied this and said: If it had the meaning of great, then it would have been necessary for Him not to be great before He created creation and after their annihilation, since He would not have had a greatness at that time.
2:256: The Almighty’s saying: There is no compulsion in religion has two issues: The first is the Almighty’s saying: There is no compulsion in religion. Religion in this verse is belief and faith, as indicated by His saying: The right course has become distinct from error. Compulsion in rulings such as faith, sales, gifts, and others is not its place, but rather comes in the interpretation of His saying, such as except for one who is forced. (al-Nahl 16:106) Abu Abd al-Rahman read: The right course has become distinct from error. This was also narrated from al-Hasan and al-Sha’bi. It is said: Rashd yurshid rasdhan, and Rashd yurshid rasdhan, if he attains what he loves, and ghawwa is its opposite, from al-Nahhas. Ibn Atiyyah narrated from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami that he read al-rashad with an alif. It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan: Al-Rashd with a damma on the ra’ and the sheen. Al-Ghay is derived from ghawa to mislead if one persists in a belief or opinion. Al-Ghay is not said in the sense of misguidance in general. Second: Scholars differed on the meaning of this verse into six opinions: First: It was said that it was abrogated, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forced the Arabs to convert to the religion of Islam and fought them and was not satisfied with anything from them except Islam. This was said by Sulayman ibn Musa, who said: It was abrogated by O Prophet, fight the disbelievers and the hypocrites (al-Tawbah 9:73). This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud and many of the commentators. Second: It is not abrogated, but rather it was revealed specifically regarding the People of the Book, and that they are not forced to convert to Islam if they pay the jizyah, and those who hate the people of idols, nothing but Islam is accepted from them, and they are the ones regarding whom it was revealed: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites (al-Tawbah 9:73). This is the saying of Al-Sha’bi, Qatadah, Al-Hasan, and Ad-Dahhak. The evidence for this saying is what Zaid bin Aslam narrated on the authority of his father, who said: I heard Umar bin Al-Khattab say to an old Christian woman: Convert to Islam, O old woman, and you will be safe, for God sent Muhammad with the truth. She said: I am an old woman, and death is great for me, and death is near me! So Umar said: O God, bear witness, and he recited: There is no compulsion in religion. Third: What Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This was revealed about the Ansar. A woman would be a miser and would promise herself that if she had a child alive, she would convert to Judaism. When Banu Nadr were expelled, there were many sons of the Ansar among them, so they said: We will not abandon our sons! So God revealed: “There is no compulsion in religion. Verily, the right course has become distinct from the wrong.” Abu Dawud said: And the miserly women who do not have a child alive, in another narration, we only did what we did because we saw that their religion was better than ours. But if God brings Islam, we will force them to it, so this was revealed: There is no compulsion in religion. Whoever wants to join them may join them, and whoever wants to enter Islam may enter. This is the statement of Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Sha’bi, and Mujahid, except that he said: The reason for their being among Banu Nadhir was breastfeeding. Al-Nahhas said: The statement of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse is the most reliable statement due to the soundness of its chain of transmission, and the likes of it are not taken as an opinion. Fourth: Al-Suddi said: The verse was revealed about a man from the Ansar called Abu Husayn who had two sons. Some merchants from Ash-Sham came to Madinah carrying oil. When they wanted to leave, the two sons of Al-Husayn came to them and invited them to Christianity. They became Christians and went with them to Ash-Sham. Their father came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, complaining about their situation and wishing that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would send someone to return them. So, There is no compulsion in religion was revealed, and he did not command to fight the People of the Book. He said: May God distance them, they were the first to disbelieve. Abu Husayn felt sorry for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he did not send someone to seek them out. So God, may He be glorified and exalted, revealed: But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute (An-Nisa’: 65). Then, He abrogated There is no compulsion in religion and commanded to fight the People of the Book in Surat Bara’ah. The correct reason for God Almighty’s statement, But no, by your Lord, they will not believe is the hadith of Al-Zubayr with his Ansari neighbor in the watering place, as will come in An-Nisa’. Its explanation, God willing. It was said: Its meaning is do not say to those who converted under the sword, forced and compelled, and this is the fifth opinion. The sixth opinion is that it was mentioned regarding captives when they were from the People of the Book, they were not forced if they were adults, and if they were young or old Zoroastrians or pagans, then they were forced to convert to Islam, because the one who captured them does not benefit from them while they are pagans. Do you not see that their slaughtered animals are not eaten, nor are their women intercourse, and they are guilty of eating dead meat and impurities and other things, and the owner finds them disgusting and it is difficult for him to benefit from them due to ownership, so it is permissible for him to force them? Ibn al-Qasim narrated something similar to this from Malik. As for Ashhab, he said: They are on the religion of the one who captured them, so if they refuse, they are forced to convert to Islam. The young have no religion, so that is why they were forced to enter the religion of Islam so that they do not go to a false religion. As for the rest of the types, when they pay the jizyah, we do not force them to convert to Islam, whether they are Arabs or non-Arabs, Quraysh or others. This will be explained and what the scholars have in The tribute and whoever accepts it from him in (Bara’ah), God willing. God the Almighty said: So whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in God is in the subjunctive mood, and Taghut is feminine from the verb to transgress - and al-Tabari narrated to transgress - if he exceeds the limit by adding to it, and its weight is fa’lūt. The doctrine of Sibawayh is that it is a singular masculine noun as if it were a generic noun that applies to little and much, and the doctrine of Abu Ali is that it is a source like karhūbut and jabrūt, and it is used to describe the singular and the plural, and its lam was changed to the position of the ayn and its ayn is the position of the lam like jabḍand jadhb, so the waw was changed to an alif because of its movement and the movement of what preceded it, so it was said Taghut, and this statement was chosen by al-Nahhas, and it was said: The origin of Taghut in the language is taken from tughā and it conveys its meaning without derivation, as it was said: la’al min al-lūl. Al-Mubarrad said: It is a plural. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is rejected. Al-Jawhari said: Taghut is the soothsayer, the devil, and every head in misguidance, and it may be one. God the Almighty said: They want to refer judgment to Taghut, while they have been commanded to disbelieve. “By Him” (An-Nisa’: 60), and it may be a plural. God Almighty said: Their allies are the false gods, and the plural is the false gods, and believes in God is an appositive, then he has grasped the firmest handhold is the answer to the condition, and the plural of the firm is the trust, like the best and the best, so the most trustworthy is from the trust, and this verse is a simile, and the expression of the commentators differed in the thing being compared to, so Mujahid said: the handhold is faith, and Al-Suddi said: Islam, and Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr, and Ad-Dahhak said: there is no god but God, and these are expressions that go back to one meaning, then he said: Its rupture is not possible, Mujahid said, meaning God does not change what is established until they change what is in themselves, meaning He does not remove the name of faith from them until they disbelieve, and rupture is breaking without separation, and qasm is breaking with separation, in the authentic hadith: Then the revelation is severed from him, and his forehead is dripping with sweat, meaning it is removed. Al-Jawhari said: Fasam something means breaking it without making it clear, you say: I silenced it, so it was severed, God Almighty said: It has no break and it breaks like it. Dhu al-Rummah said, mentioning a gazelle that he likened to Damlaj Fasa: As if he were a silver bullet, he woke up in a neighborhood playground, torn apart. Rather, He made it separated because of its bending and stooping when it sleeps, and He did not say maqsum with a qaf, so that it would be separated by two. And the rain separated: and the fever separated from it. And since disbelief in the tyrant and belief in God are among the things that the tongue utters and the heart believes in, History is good in the attributes because of the speech, Knowing because of the belief.
2:257: The Almighty’s saying: God is the ally of those who believe. The ally is a fa’il active participle meaning an agent. Al-Khattabi said: The ally is the supporter who supports his believing servants. God the Almighty said: “God is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darkness into the light.” And He said: That is because God is the ally of those who believe, and because the disbelievers have no ally. (Muhammad 47:11), Qatada said: Darkness is misguidance, and light is guidance. Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ said the same thing. Mujahid and Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah said: His saying: God is the ally of those who believe was revealed about a people who believed in Jesus, but when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, they disbelieved in him. That is their being taken out from the light into the darkness. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: So it is as if this belief secured a light in the belief from which it was taken out into the darkness. The wording of the verse is independent of this specification. Rather, it is established in every disbelieving nation, some of which believed, such as the Arabs. That is because whoever among them believed, God is his ally. He brought him out from the darkness. Disbelief into the light of faith, and whoever disbelieves after the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the caller sent, then his devil is his seducer, as if he has taken him out of faith since he is prepared with him and qualified to enter it, and he has ruled that they will enter the Fire for their disbelief, out of justice from him, and he will not be asked about what he does. And Al-Hasan read, Their allies are the tyrants, meaning the devils, and God knows best.
2:258: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Have you not seen? This is the alif of stopping, and in the speech there is a meaning of astonishment, that is, be amazed by it. Al-Farra’ said: Have you not seen? means have you seen, that is, have you seen the one who argued with Abraham, and have you seen the one who passed by a village, and he is Nimrod bin Cush bin Canaan bin Sam bin Noah, the king of his time and the owner of the fire and the mosquito! This is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, Al-Rabi’, Al-Suddi, Ibn Ishaq, Zaid bin Aslam and others. His destruction was when he intended to fight with God Almighty, by God Almighty opening a door for him from mosquitoes, so they covered the eye of the sun and ate his army and left nothing but bones, and one of them entered his brain and ate it until it became like a mouse, so the most precious person to him after that was the one whose brain he struck with a hammer for that, so he remained in the affliction for forty days. Ibn Jurayj said: He is the first king on earth. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is rejected. Qatada said: He is the first to be arrogant and he is the owner of the palace in Babylon. It was said: He is the king of the entire world, and he is one of the disbelievers, and the other is Hatansar. It was said: The one who argued with Abraham was Nimrod bin Falikh bin Eber bin Shalih bin Awfakhshad bin Sam. Ibn Atiyyah narrated all of it, and Al-Suhayli narrated that he was Nimrod bin Kush bin Canaan bin Ham bin Noah, and he was a king over the black land, and his kingdom was… Al-Dahhak, who is known as Al-Azdahhak, and his name is Biurasp bin Andrast, and he was the king of all the regions, and he is the one who was killed by Afridun bin Athqyan, and about him Habib says: As if he is laughing at his killings in the worlds, and you are unique Ad-Dahhak was a tyrant and his reign lasted for a thousand years, as they say. He was the first to be crucified and the first to cut off hands and feet. Nimrod had a son named Kusha or something like that, and he had a son named Nimrod the Younger. Nimrod the Younger’s reign lasted one year, while Nimrod the Great’s reign lasted four hundred years, as they say. There are two versions of the stories of this argument: One of them is that they went out to a festival of theirs, and Abraham entered upon their idols and broke them. When they returned, he said to them: Do you worship what you carve? They said: Who do you worship? He said: I worship my Lord, who gives life and causes death. Some of them said: Nimrod used to hoard food, so when they needed food, they would buy it from him, and when they entered upon him, they would prostrate to him. Abraham entered and did not prostrate to him, so he said: Why do you not prostrate to me? He said: I prostrate only to my Lord. Nimrod said to him: Who is your Lord?! Ibrahim said: My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. Zaid bin Aslam mentioned: This Nimrod sat and ordered the people to provide food, and whenever a people came, he would say: Who is your Lord and your God? Ibrahim said: My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. When Nimrod heard that, he said: I give life and cause death. Ibrahim opposed him with the command of the sun, and the disbeliever was dumbfounded and said: Do not leave him. Ibrahim returned to his family without anything, and passed by a sand dune like flour. He said to himself: If I fill my two jars with this, then when I enter with it the children will be happy until I see them. So he went with that, and when he reached his house, the children were happy and started playing on the two jars, and he fell asleep from exhaustion. His wife said: If I made him food so that he would find it ready when he woke up. So she opened one of the jars and found the best of the maidens, so she baked it. When he got up, she placed it in front of him. He said: Where did this come from? She said: From the flour that I have made. Ibrahim knew that God Almighty had made it easy for them. I said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaiba mentioned on the authority of Abu Salih that he said: The Prophet Ibrahim, peace be upon him, went out to buy food but was unable to find any. He passed by a red basket and took some of it, then returned to his family. They said: What is this? He said: Red wheat. So they opened it and found it to be red wheat. He said: When he planted something from it, its ear would come from its root to its branch as overlapping grains. Al-Rabi’ and others said in this story: When Nimrod said: I give life and cause death, he brought two men and killed one of them and sent the other and said: I have given life to this one and caused death to this one. When he responded to him with the command of the sun, he was astonished. It was narrated in the hadith: God Almighty said: By My glory and majesty, the Hour will not come until I bring the sun from the west so that it may be known that I am the one capable of that. Then Nimrod ordered Abraham to be thrown into the fire. This is the custom of the tyrants, for if they are confronted with something and are unable to provide an argument, they are preoccupied with punishment. So God saved him from the fire, as will come. Al-Suddi said: When Abraham came out of the fire, they brought him to the king and he had not entered upon him before that, so he spoke to him and said to him: Who is your Lord? He said: My Lord is He who gives life and causes death. Nimrod said: I give life and cause death. I will take four men and put them in a house and they will not be fed or given anything to drink until they become hungry. I will take them out and feed two and they will come back to life, and I will feed two and they will die. So Abraham confronted him with the sun and he was dumbfounded.
