2:278: God Almighty says: O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of interest if you should be believers.
2:279: God Almighty says: “But if you do not, then be warned of war from God and His Messenger. But if you repent, you may have your capital sums. Deal not unjustly, nor be dealt with unjustly.” The three verses include the rulings on usury, the permissibility of sales contracts, and the threat to those who consider usury permissible and persist in doing so. There are thirty-eight issues in this regard: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Those who consume interest eat, they take, so He expressed taking as eating, because taking is intended for eating. And interest in the language is an increase in general. It is said: The thing grows if it increases, and from this the hadith: By God, we did not take a single morsel except that we received riba from beneath it, meaning the food for which the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed for blessing. The hadith was narrated by Muslim may God have mercy on him. The rule for writing it with a yaa is because of the kasra at the beginning, and they wrote it in the Qur’an with a waw. Then the Shari’ah has dealt with this generality and restricted it to some of its sources. Once it was used to refer to unlawful earnings, as God the Almighty said about the Jews: And they took usury, although they had been forbidden from it. He did not mean the legitimate usury that He ruled to be forbidden to us, but rather he meant unlawful money, as God the Almighty said: Listeners to falsehood, devourers of unlawful gain. He meant unlawful money from bribery, and what they considered permissible from the money of the illiterate, as they said: We have no responsibility for the unlettered. Based on this, it includes the prohibition of all unlawful money, regardless of how it was acquired. The usury that the Shari’ah has defined as being based on two things: the prohibition of women, and the differential in contracts and food items, as we will explain. Most of it is what the Arabs used to do, such as saying to the debtor: Will you pay or will you increase it? The creditor would increase the amount of money and the claimant would be patient with him. All of this is forbidden by consensus of the nation. Second: Most of the prohibited sales are prohibited due to the meaning of an increase, either in the form of money, or in a benefit to one of them from delay and the like. And among the sales are those that do not have the meaning of an increase, such as selling fruit before it ripens, and selling at the time of the call to prayer on Friday. If the one who does it is told, He is consuming usury, then this is an exaggeration and a simile. Third: The imams narrated, and the wording is from Muslim, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, and salt for salt, for example, hand to hand. Whoever gives more or asks for more has committed usury, both the giver and the taker.” In the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit: If these types differ, then sell them as you wish, as long as it is hand to hand. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Gold for gold, its gold and its silver, silver for silver, its gold and its silver, wheat for wheat, a mudd for a mudd, barley for barley, a mudd for a mudd, dates for dates, a mudd for a mudd, and salt for salt, a mudd for a mudd. Whoever increases or adds more has committed usury. There is nothing wrong with selling gold for silver and silver for the majority of them, hand to hand. As for credit, there is no problem. There is nothing wrong with selling wheat for barley and barley for the majority of them, hand to hand. As for credit, there is no problem.” The scholars agreed on the statement based on this Sunnah, and the majority of Muslim jurists agreed on it, except for wheat and barley, for Malik made them one type, so two of them are not permissible for one, and this is the opinion of Al-Layth, Al-Awza’i, and most of the scholars of Medina and Ash-Sham. Malik added to them sult. Al-Layth said: sult, millet, and corn are one type, and Ibn Wahb said the same. I said: If the Sunnah is proven, then there is no other statement with it. And he, peace be upon him, said: If these types differ, then sell them as you wish, if it is hand to hand. His saying, Wheat for wheat and barley for barley is evidence that they are two different types, just as wheat differs from dates, and because their characteristics are different and their names are different, and no consideration is given to the grower and the harvester if the hair is not considered, rather he separates and explains, and this is the doctrine of al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri and the scholars of hadith. Fourth: Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan believed that the prohibition and ban came from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the minted dinar and the minted dirham, not regarding the minted gold and silver bullion, nor regarding the minted jewelry. It has been said that this was only from him regarding the jewelry, until he happened to Ubadah, as Muslim and others reported. He said: We invaded while Muawiyah was the leader of the people and we took many spoils. Among the spoils we took were silver vessels. Muawiyah ordered a man to sell them as gifts to the people. The people disputed about that. report of that reached Ubadah ibn al-Samit, so he stood up and said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) forbid the sale of gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, and salt for salt, except equal for equal, and whoever gives more or more has committed usury. So the people returned what they had taken. report of that reached Muawiyah, so he stood up and gave a sermon and said: What is the matter with the men who narrate hadiths from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) when we used to witness and accompany him but did not hear them from him! Ubadah ibn al-Samit stood up and repeated the story, then said: We will narrate what we heard from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), even if Muawiyah dislikes it - or he said, even if he dislikes it - I do not mind not accompanying him in his army on a dark night. Hammad said this or something similar. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: It has been narrated that this story was about Abu al-Darda’ with Muawiyah. It is possible that this happened to them with him, but the hadith is preserved in the custom for Ubadah, and it is the origin that scholars relied on in the chapter on usury. They did not differ that what Muawiyah did in this was not permissible, and it is not objectionable that Muawiyah was unaware of what Abu Darda and Ubadah knew, for they were two great jurists among the Companions and their elders, and what was found with others who were less than them was unaware of Abu Bakr and Umar, so Muawiyah is more deserving. It is possible that his school of thought was like that of Ibn Abbas, for he was a sea of knowledge and did not see anything wrong with a dirham for two dirhams until Abu Saeed turned him away from that. This story of Muawiyah with Ubadah was during the reign of Umar. Qubaysah ibn Dhu’ayb said: Ubadah objected to something about Muawiyah, so he said: I will not live with you in a land where you are, and he entered Medina. Umar said to him: What brought you here? So he told him. He said: Go back to your place, may God curse a land in which you and your likes are absent! And he wrote to Muawiyah: You have no authority over him. Fifth: The imams narrated, and the wording is from Dar Qutni, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A dinar for a dinar and a dirham for a dirham, there is no difference between them. Whoever needs paper money, let him exchange it for gold. And if he needs gold, let him exchange it for paper money, ha and ha.” The scholars said that his saying, peace be upon him: A dinar for a dinar and a dirham for a dirham, there is no difference between them is an indication of the type of the original coin, as evidenced by his saying: Silver for silver and gold for gold in the hadith. White silver and black silver and red gold and yellow gold, none of that is permissible to sell some of it for others except like for like, equal for equal in every case. This is the view of the group of scholars, as we have explained. The narrations from Malik differed regarding money, so he included it with dirhams in terms of it being a price for things, and he forbade including it once in terms of it not being a price in every country, but rather it is specific to one country and not another. Sixth: There is no consideration for what has been narrated from many of Malik’s companions, and some of them narrate it from Malik, about a merchant who is motivated to go out and has a need for minted dirhams or minted dinars, so he comes to the mint with his silver or gold and says to the minter, “Take this silver or gold of mine and take the amount of your hand’s work and give me minted dinars in my gold or minted dirhams in this silver of mine, because I am motivated to go out and I fear that the one I went out with will miss me,” and that this is permissible due to necessity, and that some people have done it. Ibn al-Arabi narrated it in his Qabas from Malik about someone other than a merchant, and that Malik was lenient in this, so in the image he has sold his silver, which weighed one hundred and five dirhams, and his wages are for one hundred, and this is pure usury. What makes this permissible is that if he said to him: Strike this for me and agree to do so for a fee, and when he struck it, he took it from him and gave him the fee, then what Malik did first is what will be the last, and Malik only looks at the money and applies the ruling of the situation to it, and all the other jurists rejected it. Ibn al-Arabi said: The evidence for Malik in this is clear. Abu Umar, may God have mercy on him, said: This is the very essence of usury which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade when he said: Whoever increases or is increased has committed usury. Ibn Wahb responded to this issue from Malik and denied it. Al-Abhari claimed that this is a matter of kindness in order to seek trade and so as not to miss out on the market, and usury is only for the one who wants to earn usury from among those who intend and seek that. Al-Abhari forgot his origin in cutting off the means, and his statement about someone who sold a garment on credit without intending to buy it back, then finds it being sold in the market: It is not permissible for him to buy it back from him for less than what he sold it for, even if he did not intend to do so or seek it. There are many examples of this. If usury was only for those who intended it, it would not have been forbidden except for the jurists. Umar said: No one trades in our market except one who has acquired knowledge, otherwise he will eat usury. This is clear to those who have been given fairness and inspired with the right path. I said: Malik, may God have mercy on him, went to extremes in preventing excess to the point that he made what is imagined as what is realized. He prevented a dinar and a dirham for a dinar and a dirham in order to block the means and to eliminate suspicions, because if there was no suspicion of excess, they would not have been exchanged. He justified his prevention of that by the impossibility of equivalence when distributing, as that would entail gold and silver for gold. More clearly than that, his prevention is based on moral differentiation, as he prevented a dinar of high-quality gold and a dinar of lower-quality gold in exchange for the higher, and he abolished the lower-quality. This is from his keen insight, may God have mercy on him, so it indicates that that narration from him is reprehensible and not authentic. And God knows best. Seventh: Al-Khattabi said: “Tabr is pieces of gold or silver before they are struck and stamped into dirhams or dinars, the singular of which is tabra. ‘Ayn is the struck dirhams or dinars. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade selling a mithqal of gold for a mithqal or something of unstruck tabar. Likewise, he forbade the difference between struck silver and unstruck silver, and that is the meaning of his saying: Its tabar and its ‘ayn are the same.” Eighth: The scholars agreed that dates are exchanged for dates, and it is not permissible except like for like. They differed about selling one date for two dates, and one grain of wheat for two grains. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Al-Thawri prohibited it, and it is an analogy to the statement of Malik, which is correct, because what usury occurs in is the difference in its large amount, its small amount is included in that, by analogy and consideration. Those who permitted that argued that the consumer of one or two dates is not obligated to pay the value, saying: Because it is neither measured by volume nor weighed, so the difference in it is permissible. Ninth: Know, may God have mercy on you, that the issues of this chapter are many and its branches are widespread. What connects this to you is that you look at what each of the scholars considered as the reason for usury. Abu Hanifa said: The reason for that is that it is a type of measured or weighed. Everything that is subject to measurement or weight, according to him, is of one type. Selling some of it for some with a difference or on credit is not permissible. So he forbade selling some dirt for some with a difference because it is subject to measurement. He permitted bread, one loaf for two loaves, because it was not subject to measurement, which is its origin, so it was removed from the type that usury is subject to and included other than it. Al-Shafi’i said: The reason is that it is a type of food. This is his opinion in the new hadith. According to him, it is not permissible to sell flour for bread, nor to sell bread for bread with a difference or on credit, whether the bread is leavened or unleavened. According to him, it is not permissible to sell an egg for two eggs, nor a pomegranate for two pomegranates, nor a watermelon for two watermelons, neither hand to hand nor on credit, because all of that is edible food. He said in the old days: It is measured or weighed. The expressions of our Maliki companions differed in this regard, and the best of them is that it is usually stored for living, such as wheat, barley, dates, and salt, which are mentioned, and what is similar to it, such as rice, corn, millet, and sesame, and legumes such as beans, lentils, cowpeas, and chickpeas, as well as meat, dairy, vinegars, and oils, and fruits such as grapes, raisins, and olives. There is a difference of opinion regarding figs, and honey and sugar are included with them. All of this is subject to usury from the side of women. It is permissible to differentiate in it, according to the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: If these types differ, then sell them however you wish, if it is hand to hand. There is no usury in fresh fruits that do not last, such as apples, watermelons, pomegranates, pears, gourds, cucumbers, eggplants, and other vegetables. Malik said: It is not permissible to sell eggs for eggs with a difference, because it is something that is stored, and he allows like for like. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam said: It is permissible to exchange one egg for two eggs or more, because it is something that cannot be saved, and this is the opinion of Al-Awza’i. Tenth: Grammarians differed in the pronunciation of riba. The Basrans said: It is one of the words with a waw, because you say in its dual: ribwan, as Sibawayh said. The Kufians said: It is written with a ya’ and its dual with a ya’, because of the kasra at the beginning. Al-Zajjaj said: I have not seen a mistake uglier or more heinous than this! It is not enough for them to make a mistake in writing so that they make a mistake in the dual while they read: And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the wealth of the people. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: Riba was written in the Qur’an with a waw to differentiate it from adultery, and riba was more deserving of a waw than it, because it is from riba yarbu. Eleventh: The Almighty’s saying: They will not rise except as one rises whom Satan has beaten into insanity. The sentence is the predicate of the subject, which is those. The meaning is from their graves, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’, Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd. Some of them said: A devil will be placed with him to strangle him. They all said: He will be resurrected like a madman as a punishment for him and as a source of loathing for all the people of the gathering place. This unanimously agreed upon interpretation is strengthened by the fact that in Ibn Mas’ud’s reading it says: They will not rise on the Day of Resurrection except as one rises. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: As for the wording of the verse, it was possible to liken the state of the one who stands with greed and avarice for worldly trade to the state of the madman standing, because greed and desire provoke him until his limbs become disturbed. This is like what you say to someone who walks quickly and mixes up his movements, whether from fear or otherwise: This one has gone mad! Al-A’sha likened his she-camel in her energy to madness in his saying: And after the night, she becomes as if she has been visited by a group of jinn or possessed. Another said: I swear, I love Asmaa more than anything else But what came in the reading of Ibn Masoud and what the commentators agreed upon weakens this interpretation. And he utters it, he does it, from khabat yakhtabb, as you say: he owns it and worships it. So God made this sign for those who eat usury, and that is that it increased in their bellies and weighed them down, so when they come out of their graves they rise and fall. And it is said: They will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection with their bellies swollen like pregnant women, and whenever they rise they fall and people walk on them. And some scholars said: This is only a sign for them by which they will be known on the Day of Resurrection, then the punishment is behind that, just as the thief will come with what he stole on the Day of Resurrection with fame that he will be known by, then the punishment is behind that. And God the Almighty said: They eat, meaning they earn usury and do it. And He specifically mentioned eating because it is the strongest of man’s intentions in money, and because it indicates greed, which is the most intense greed. It is said: A greedy man between greed and greedy people, as stated in Al-Mujmal. So this part of the consequences of earning is considered to be the same as earning as a whole, so clothing, housing, saving, and spending on one’s family are included in His statement: those who eat. Twelfth: In this verse is evidence of the corruption of the denial of those who denied epilepsy from the side of the jinn, and claimed that it is an action of nature, and that the devil does not enter into man, does not enter into man, and does not cause any possession from him. The response to them has already been mentioned in what preceded this book. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Yusr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate and say: “O God, I seek refuge in You from falling, from being destroyed, from drowning, from being burned. I seek refuge in You from being overcome by Satan at the time of death. I seek refuge in You from dying while turning my back on Your path. I seek refuge in You from dying from being stung.” It was narrated from the hadith of Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Dawud told us, Hammam told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to say: O God, I seek refuge in You from madness, leprosy, vitiligo, and evil diseases. Madness means insanity. It is said: A man was possessed and possessed, so he is possessed and possessed if he is insane. This is a sign of usury in the Hereafter. It was narrated in the hadith of the Night Journey: “Gabriel set out with me and I passed by many men, each one of whom had a belly like a huge house, standing in front of the wayfarers of Pharaoh’s family. Pharaoh’s family were exposed to the Fire morning and evening, coming forward like mad camels, thrashing around the stones and trees, neither hearing nor understanding. When the people of those bellies sensed them, they would stand up and their bellies would move them and they would fall down. Then one of them would stand up and his belly would move him and he would fall down, and they would not be able to move until Pharaoh’s family covered them and trampled them, coming and going. That would be their punishment in the intermediate realm between this world and the Hereafter. Pharaoh’s family would say, ‘O God, never let the Hour come.’ For God Almighty says, ‘And on the Day the Hour comes, admit Pharaoh’s family into the severest punishment. ’” Killing O Gabriel, who are these? He said, “These are those who consume interest. They will not rise except as one rises who is being afflicted by Satan with insanity.” Insanity means madness, as well as alawlaq, alas, and rud. Thirteenth: The Almighty’s saying: That is because they say, ‘Trade is only like usury.’ Its meaning is according to all the interpreters of the unbelievers, and it was said to them: Then he shall have what he has already paid. This is not said to a disobedient believer, rather his sale is annulled and his action is returned, even if he was the one who made it. Therefore, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it will be rejected. But the sinners who engage in usury may be subject to some of the threat in this verse. Fourteenth: The Almighty’s saying: Trade is but like usury, meaning that the increase when the due date comes at the end is like the original price at the beginning of the contract. This is because the Arabs did not know any usury except that, so when their debt became due, they would say to the creditor: Either pay it or increase it, meaning increase the debt. So God, the Almighty, forbade that and responded to their statement with His true saying: God has permitted trade and forbidden usury, and He explained that if the due date comes and he does not have what he can pay, he should look to what is easy to pay. This usury is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, abrogated with his statement on the Day of Arafah when he said: Behold, all usury is abolished, and the first usury that I abolish is our usury, the usury of Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib, for it is all abolished. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began with his uncle and the people closest to him. This is one of the traditions of justice for the imam, that he should bestow justice upon himself and his close associates, and then it will spread to the people. Fifteenth: The Almighty’s saying: God has permitted trade and forbidden usury. This is from the generality of the Qur’an, and the definite article is for the genus, not for the covenant, since no sale mentioned before can be referred to, as the Almighty said: By time, indeed, mankind is in loss. Then He made an exception: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds. If it is proven that the sale is general, then it is specific to what we mentioned of usury and other things that are forbidden and prohibited from being contracted, such as alcohol, dead animals, and the rope of a pregnant woman, and other things that are proven in the Sunnah and the consensus of the Ummah to prohibit them. Similar to it is Kill the polytheists and all the apparent meanings that require generality and are subject to specification, and this is the doctrine of most jurists. Some of them said: It is from the generality of the Qur’an that is explained by what is permissible of trade and what is forbidden, so it cannot be used to permit or prohibit trade unless it is accompanied by a statement from the Sunnah of the Messenger, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, even if it indicates the permissibility of trade in general but not in detail. This is the difference between generality and generality. Generality indicates the permissibility of trade in general and in detail unless it is specified by evidence. The general does not indicate its permissibility in detail unless accompanied by an explanation. The first is more correct. And God knows best. Sixteenth: The word sale in the language is derived from the root word ba’a which means to pay something in return and take something in exchange. It requires a seller, who is the owner or someone who is in his position, a buyer, who is the one who pays the price, and something sold, who is the thing being priced, who is the one who pays the price in exchange for it. Accordingly, the pillars of sale are four: the seller, the buyer, the price, and the thing being priced. Then, the exchange among the Arabs differs according to what is added to it. If one of the two things being exchanged is in exchange for a slave, it is called a sale. If it is in exchange for the benefit of a slave, then if it is the benefit of a woman, it is called marriage. If it is something else, it is called a lease. If it is an item for an item, it is a cash sale, which is the exchange. If it is a deferred debt, it is a salam. Its explanation will come in the verse on debt. The ruling on exchange has already passed, and the ruling on leasing will come in stories and the ruling on the dowry in marriage in women, each in its place, God willing. Seventeenth: The sale is an acceptance and an offer that occurs with the future and past words. The past is real and the future is a metaphor. It occurs with the explicit and the metaphor that is understood from it is the transfer of ownership. So whether he said: I sold you this commodity for ten and he said: I bought it, or the buyer said: I bought it and the seller said: I will sell it to you for ten and the buyer said: I will buy or I have bought. Likewise, if he said: Take it for ten or I gave it to you or take it or may it be blessed for you for ten or I delivered it to you - and they both mean the sale - then all of that is a binding sale. If the seller said: I sold it to you for ten and then he went back before the buyer accepted, then he said: He does not have the right to go back until he hears the buyer’s acceptance or rejection, because he gave that from himself and made it obligatory for her, and he said that to him, because the contract was not completed for him. If the seller said: I was playing, then the narration about him differed. He said once: The sale is binding on him and no attention is paid to his word. He said once: The value of the commodity is considered. If the price is similar to its value, then the sale is binding. If it is different, such as a slave for a dirham and a house for a dinar, then it is known that he did not intend to sell it, but rather he was joking, so it is not binding on him.
2:280: God Almighty says: “But if he is in hardship, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him. But if you remit it by charity, that is better for you, if you only knew.” It contains nine issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And if he is in hardship. When the Almighty ruled that the usurers should be entitled to their principal when they have the money, He ruled that the one in hardship should be given consideration to the state of ease. This is because when Thaqeef demanded their money that they had from Banu al-Mugheerah, they complained of hardship - meaning Banu al-Mugheerah - and said: We have nothing, and they asked for a term until the time of their fruits, so this verse was revealed: And if he is in hardship. Second: The Almighty’s statement: And if he is in hardship along with His statement: And if you repent, then you shall have your capital sums indicates that the creditor has the right to demand payment from the debtor and that it is permissible to take his money without his consent. It indicates that when the creditor refuses to pay the debt when he is able to, he is unjust, because Almighty God says: And you shall have your capital sums and thus He has made it permissible for him to demand his capital sums. So if he has the right to demand, then the debtor must inevitably pay it. Third: Al-Mahdawi said: Some scholars said: This verse abrogates what was done in the pre-Islamic era of selling to someone who was in financial difficulty. Makki narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered it at the beginning of Islam. Ibn Atiyyah said: If the action of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is proven, then it is abrogated, otherwise it is not abrogated. Al-Tahawi said: A free man was sold in debt at the beginning of Islam if he did not have money to pay it off, until God abrogated that, saying: But if he is in hardship, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him. They used as evidence a hadith narrated by Al-Darqutni from the hadith of Muslim bin Khalid Al-Zanjy, who told us Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ibn Al-Baylamani, on the authority of Sarq, who said: A man owed me money - or he said a debt - so he took me to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he did not find any money for me, so he sold me from it, or he sold me to him. Al-Bazzar narrated it with this chain of transmission, with a longer chain of transmission than it. Muslim bin Khalid Al-Zanjy and Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Baylamani are not to be relied upon. A group of scholars said: The Almighty’s statement: then grant respite until it is easy for you is general for all people, so whoever is in difficulty will be granted respite. This is the statement of Abu Hurairah, Al-Hasan and most of the jurists. An-Nahhas said: The best that has been said about this verse is the statement of Ata’, Ad-Dahhak and Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham. He said: It is for every person in difficulty who will be granted respite in interest and in all of his debt. This is a statement that includes all statements, because it is possible that it is a general abrogator that was revealed regarding interest, and the ruling on others is the same as its ruling. Also, because the reading in the nominative case means even if one of the people is in difficulty. If it was specifically for interest, the accusative would have been correct, meaning even if the one who owes the interest is in difficulty. Ibn Abbas and Shuraih said: This is specifically for interest. As for debts and other transactions, there is no respite in them, rather it is paid to their owners or it is withheld until he pays it back. This is the statement of Ibrahim. They used as evidence the statement of God the Almighty: God commands you to render trusts to whom they are due (Al-Anfal 14:10). Ibn Atiyah said: This statement was necessary if there was no extreme poverty. However, in the case of lack and clear poverty, the ruling is to wait out of necessity. Fourth: If a person’s debts are many and his creditors demand their money, then the ruler has the right to release him from all his money and leave him what he needs. Ibn Nafi’ narrated from Malik that he should only be left with what he needs to cover himself. The well-known view is that his usual clothing should be left to him unless there is any surplus in it, and his debt should not be taken away from him even if that would be disgraceful to him. There is a difference of opinion regarding leaving his wife’s clothing and selling his books if he is a scholar. He should not be left with a home, a servant, or a Friday garment unless their value has decreased. In this case, it is forbidden to imprison him. The basic principle in this is the saying of God the Almighty: But if he is in hardship, then let there be postponement until it is easy for him. The imams narrated, and the wording is from Muslim, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, who said: “A man was afflicted during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with fruit that he had bought, and his debts increased. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Give him charity.’ The people gave him charity, but it was not enough to pay off his debt. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to his creditors: ‘Take what you find, and you have nothing else.’” In Musannaf Abi Dawud: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not do anything to his creditors except give them his money. This is explicit, for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not order the man, who was Muadh ibn Jabal, to be imprisoned, as Shuraih said, nor to be confined to his home, contrary to Abu Hanifa, who said: He is confined to his home because it is possible for him to have money, and he is not required to earn it, for the reason we have mentioned. And God is our guide.” Fifth: The bankrupt person is imprisoned according to Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa and others until his insolvency is proven. According to Malik, he is not imprisoned if he is not accused of concealing his money and his stubbornness is not proven. Likewise, he is not imprisoned if his insolvency is proven, as we mentioned. Sixth: If the bankrupt’s money is collected and then lost before it reaches its owners and before it is sold, then the bankrupt must guarantee it, and the creditors’ debt remains in his possession. If the ruler sells his money and collects its price, then the price is lost before the creditors collect it, then they must guarantee it and the bankrupt is absolved of it. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hakam said: The bankrupt’s guarantee of it always reaches the creditors. Seventh: Hardship is the tightness of circumstances due to lack of money. From this comes the word army of hardship. And delay is the postponement. And easiness is a source meaning ease. And Dhu with the perfect kana which means found and happened was raised. This is the saying of Sibawayh, Abu Ali, and others. And Sibawayh recited: I would ransom my she-camel for the Banu Dhuhl ibn Shaiban if it was a day with grey stars. The accusative case is permissible. In the Mushaf of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, it is: And if he is in hardship, meaning: And if the person being asked is in hardship. Al-A'mash read: And if he is in hardship, then a respite. Abu Amr al-Dani said on the authority of Ahmad ibn Musa: And it is also in the Mushaf of Ubayy ibn Ka'b. Al-Nahhas, Makki and al-Naqqash said: According to this, the wording of the verse is specific to the people of usury, and for those who read Dhu it is general for all who have a debt. It was mentioned earlier. Al-Mahdawi narrated that in the Mushaf of Uthman, it is: If he is in hardship. Al-Mu'tamir narrated on the authority of Hajjaj al-Warraq, who said: In the Mushaf of Uthman, And if he is in hardship, it was mentioned by al-Nahhas. The reading of the group is: Nazarah with a kasra on the Dhad. Mujahid, Abu Raja and al-Hasan read Fanzarah with a sukoon on the Dhad, and it is a Tamimi dialect, and they are the ones who say: Fi karmeh Zayd meaning karmeh Zayd, and they say kabd fi kabd. Nafi' alone read Maysarah with a damma on the Seen, and the majority read it with a fatha. An-Nahhas narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Ata’ that it is fa-nazira - on the matter - to Maysarhi with a damma on the seen and a kasra on the ra’ and the addition of the ya’ in the insertion. It was read fa-nazira. Abu Hatim said that fa-nazira is not permissible, it is only in An-Naml because a woman spoke this to herself, from nazra, so she is nazra. What is in Al-Baqarah is from delay, from your saying: I gave you an anzara with the debt, meaning I delayed it for you. And from this is His statement: Then give me respite until the Day they are resurrected. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj permitted this and said: It is from the names of the sources, like the statement of God the Almighty: There is no liar in her occurrence and the statement of God the Almighty: She thinks that He will do to her a great calamity and the traitor of the eyes and others. Eighth: The Almighty’s statement: And that you give charity is the subject and its predicate is it is better: God Almighty encouraged with these words to give charity to the needy and made that better than giving him respite, as stated by Al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and Al-Dahhak. Al-Tabari said: And others said: The meaning of the verse is that giving charity to the rich and the poor is better for you. The first is correct, and there is no mention of the rich. Ninth: Abu Jaafar Al-Tahawi narrated on the authority of Buraidah bin Al-Khasib, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever gives a respite to a debtor in difficulty, he will receive a charity like that for every day. Then I said: For every day, a charity like that. He said: “For every day, a charity, as long as the debt is not due. But if he gives him a respite after it is due, he will receive a charity like that for every day.” Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man from among those who came before you was brought to account, and nothing good was found of him except that he used to mix with people and was wealthy, so he used to order his servants to forgive those who were in difficulty. God Almighty said, ‘We are more deserving of that than he is. Forgive him.’” It was narrated: On the authority of Abu Qatada that he sought out a debtor of his, but he disappeared from him, then he found him and said: I am insolvent. He said: By God? He said: God, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever would like God to save him from the distress of the Day of Resurrection, let him give relief to one in difficulty or forgive him. And in the long hadith of Abu al-Yusr - whose name was Ka`b ibn `Amr - that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever grants respite to a debtor in difficulty or forgives him, God will shelter him in His shade. These hadiths encourage what is explicitly stated in them. The hadith of Abu Qatada indicates that if the creditor knows or suspects the debtor’s difficulty, it is forbidden for him to demand it from him, even if his difficulty has not been proven to the judge. Granting respite to a debtor in difficulty means delaying it until he becomes solvent. Forgiving him means removing the debt from his responsibility. Abu al-Yusr combined the two meanings for his creditor when he erased the document from him and said to him: If you find someone to pay, then pay, otherwise you are absolved.
2:281: It was said: This verse was revealed nine nights before the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then nothing was revealed after that. This was said by Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Jubayr and Muqatil said: Seven nights. It was narrated three nights. It was narrated that it was revealed three hours before his death, and that he, peace be upon him, said: Make it between the verse on usury and the verse on debt. Makki narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Gabriel came to me and said: Make it at the beginning of two hundred and eighty verses. I said: It was narrated on the authority of Abi bin Kaab, Ibn Abbas, and Qatada that the last thing to be revealed was: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves to the end of the verse. The first statement is more well-known, more correct, and more famous. Abu Salih narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The last verse to be revealed from the Qur’an: “And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.” Gabriel said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, place it on the head of two hundred and eighty cows. Abu Bakr al-Anbari mentioned it in his book Al-Radd, and it is the saying of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with him, that it was the last verse to be revealed, and that he, peace be upon him, lived twenty-one days after it, as will be explained at the end of Surat When the Help of God and the Victory Comes, God willing. The verse is a sermon for all people and a command specific to every human being. A Day is the object, not the circumstance. On it you will be returned to God is an attribute of it. Abu Umrah read it with a fatha on the ta’ and a kasra on the jim, like in Indeed, to Us is their return, and taking into consideration Abu’s reading, A Day you will be returned to God, and the rest read it with a damma on the ta’ and a fatha on the jim, like in Then they will be returned to God. And if I am returned to my Lord and considering Abdullah's reading of a day when you will be returned to God, and Al-Hasan read they will return with the letter ya, meaning all people will return. Ibn Jinni said: It is as if God Almighty was lenient with the believers by confronting them with the mention of the return, as it is something that breaks hearts, so He said to them: And fear a Day, then He returned in mentioning the return to the occultation as a kindness to them. The majority of scholars agree that this day warned against is the Day of Resurrection, Reckoning, and Atonement. Some people said: It is death that will last. Ibn Atiyyah said: The first is more correct based on the words in the verse. In His statement to God there is an omitted complement, meaning to the judgment of God and the separation of His judgment. They are a response to the meaning of all, not to the word, except according to Al-Hasan's reading they will return, so his statement they is a response to the collective pronoun in they will return. In this verse there is a text that states that reward and punishment are related to the acquisition of deeds, and it is a response to the Jabriyah, as has been mentioned previously.
2:282: God Almighty said: "O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write it down between you in justice. And let no scribe refuse to write as God has taught him. So let him write, and let the one upon whom the debt is owed dictate. And let him fear God, his Lord, and not withhold from it anything. But if the one upon whom the debt is owed is foolish or weak or cannot dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice. And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men. But if there are not two men, then a man and two women from among those whom you accept as witnesses. So if one of the two errs, the other can remind her. And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called. And do not be weary of writing it down, whether it is small or large, for its term. That is more just in the sight of God and more suitable for testimony and more likely to prevent you from doubting. Unless it is a present trade which you carry on among yourselves, then there is no blame upon you if you do not write it down. And bring to witness when you transact, and let not the scribe or the witness be harmed. But if you do, then indeed, it is an act of disobedience on your part. And fear God, and God teaches you. And God is Knowing of all things." There are fifty-two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt (al-Baqarah 2:170). Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It has reached me that the most recent verse in the Qur’an with regard to the throne is the verse on debt. Ibn Abbas said: This verse was revealed specifically regarding the Salam contract. Its meaning is that the Salam contract of the people of Madinah was the reason for the verse, and it includes all debts unanimously. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: It includes thirty rulings. Some of our scholars have used it as evidence for the permissibility of deferring payments in loans, according to what Malik said, since he did not distinguish between the loan and other contracts in debts. The Shafi’is disagreed on this and said: The verse does not permit deferring payments in all debts, but rather it commands witnesses if it is a deferred debt, and then it is known by other evidence that deferring payments in debt is permissible or not. Second: The Almighty’s saying: with a debt is an emphasis, like His saying: nor a bird that flies with its wings. “So the angels prostrated, all of them together.” The reality of debt is any transaction in which one of the two exchanges is cash and the other is on credit, because the cash among the Arabs is what is present, and the debt is what is absent. The poet said: You promised us two dirhams of paint and grilling, urgently, without debt. Another said: Let fate throw me wherever it wants, if it does not throw me into the two pits. If they light wood and fire, then that is death in cash, not in religion. Third: The Almighty’s saying: for a specified term. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The saying of God, for a specified term, indicates that a loan for an unknown term is not permissible. The Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, indicates a similar meaning to the Book of God Almighty. “It has been proven that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They came to Madinah and they were borrowing dates for two or three years. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever borrows dates should borrow a known measure and a known weight for a known period.” Narrated by Ibn Abbas. Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others. Ibn Umar said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to sell camel meat until the time of the transaction. The time of the transaction is when a female camel gives birth and then becomes pregnant. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade them from doing that. All the scholars who have memorized his words have agreed that the permissible Salam is for a man to give to his companion a specified and described amount of food, from the food of a public land that does not go wrong, by a specified measure, for a specified term, in specified dinars or dirhams. The price of what he gave in Salam is paid before they part ways from the place where they made the transaction, and they name the place where the food will be received. If they do that and it is permissible, then it is a valid Salam. I do not know of any scholar who invalidates it. I said: Our scholars said: The advance payment until the harvest, the harvesting, the Newroz, and the festival is permissible, as it is specific to a specific time and period. Fourth: Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, defined Salam and said: It is a sale of a known thing in the conscience, limited by description to a present thing or something similar to it, for a known period. Restricting it to a known thing in the conscience indicates caution against the unknown, and against Salam in specific things, such as what they used to borrow in Medina when the Prophet, peace be upon him, came to them, for they used to borrow the fruits of palm trees in their entirety, so he forbade them from that because of the uncertainty in it, as those trees might not bear fruit at all. Their saying that it is limited to the description is to exclude what is known in general without detail, as if he surrendered dates, clothes, or whales and did not specify their type or specific description. And their saying: With a present eye, we guard against debt with debt. And their saying: Or what is similar to it, we guard against the two or three days for which it is permissible to delay the capital of the Salam contract to it, then it is permissible to delay it for that amount according to us, with or without a condition due to the proximity of that, and it is not permissible to stipulate it upon it. And neither Al-Shafi’i nor Al-Kufi permitted delaying the capital of the Salam contract after the contract and separation, and they saw that it is like exchange. Our evidence is that the two chapters differ in their most specific descriptions, for the exchange chapter is narrow and the conditions are many in it, unlike the Salam contract, for the impurities of transactions in it are more. And God knows best. Their saying for a known term is a precaution against the current sale, as it is not permissible according to the well-known opinion, which will come. Describing the term as known is a precaution against the unknown term for which they used to make the sale in the pre-Islamic era. Fifth: Salam and advance are two expressions with the same meaning and they came in the hadith, except that the name specific to this chapter is Salam because advance is said for a loan. Salam is a sale from the sales that are permissible by consensus, except from: He (peace be upon him) forbade selling what you do not have. He permitted Salam, because Salam was a sale of something known in the conscience, it was a sale of something absent, which was called for by the necessity of each of the two parties to the sale. The owner of the capital needs to buy the fruit, and the owner of the fruit needs its price before its season to spend on it. So it became clear that Salam sale is one of the urgent interests, and the jurists called it the sale of the needy. If it is permissible immediately, this wisdom is nullified and this interest is removed, and there is no benefit in excluding it from the sale of what you do not have. And God knows best. Sixth: The agreed upon and disputed conditions of Salam, which are nine: six for the Salam fih, and three for the Salam capital. As for the six for the Salam fih: that it be in the dhimmah, that it be described, that it be specified, that it be deferred, that the term be known, and that it be present at the place of the term. As for the three for the Salam capital: that it be of a known type, specified, and cash. These three conditions for the capital are agreed upon except for cash, as mentioned above. Ibn al-Arabi said: As for the first condition, which is that it be in the dhimmah, there is no doubt that what is meant by it is that it be in the dhimmah, because it is a debt, and were it not for that, it would not have been legislated as a debt, and people would not have intended it for profit and ease. And people agreed on that statement. However, Malik said: Salam is not permissible for a specific item except under two conditions: One of them is that it be a safe village, and the second is that it is permissible to take it, such as milk from a sheep or fresh dates from a palm tree, and no one else said that. These two issues are correct in the evidence, because specification is not allowed in the Salam contract for fear of misleading and uncertainty, lest it be impossible at the place. If the place is followed and it is not impossible to find what is in it in most cases, then that is permissible, because the guarantee of the consequences is not certain in the matters of jurisprudence, and there must be the possibility of slight uncertainty, and that is common in the matters of branches, and its enumeration is in the books of the issues. As for the Salam contract in milk and dates with the beginning of taking it, it is a civil matter that the people of Medina agreed upon, and it is based on the principle of interest, because a person needs to take milk and dates daily and it is difficult to take it every day initially, because cash may not be available and because poetry may be disputed, and the owner of the palm trees and milk is in need of cash, because the one who has goods cannot dispose of them. So since they share in need, they are permitted to do this transaction by analogy with loans and other basic needs and interests. The second condition, which is that it be described, is agreed upon, as is the third condition. The estimation is of three types: measure, weight, and number. This is based on custom, which is either the custom of people or the custom of the Shari’ah. As for the fourth condition, which is that it be deferred, there is disagreement about it. Al-Shafi’i said: Immediate salam is permissible, but most scholars forbade it. Ibn al-Arabi said: The Malikis were confused about estimating the term until they returned it to one day, until some of our scholars said: Immediate salam is permissible. The correct view is that a term is necessary for it, because the sold item is of two types: immediate, which is the item, and deferred. If it is immediate and the one to whom it is delivered is not with it, then it is like: selling what you do not have, so a term is necessary until each contract is completed with its description and conditions, and the poetic rulings are given their places. Our scholars define it as a period, and the markets differ in such cases. And the saying of God the Most High: for a specified term and the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): For a known term is enough for anyone to say. I said: What our scholars have permitted of the current salam is that in which countries differ in terms of prices. Salam is permissible in cases where there is a day, two days, or three between them. But in one country, it is not, because its price is the same, and God knows best. As for the fifth condition, which is that the term be known, there is no disagreement among the nation about it, because God the Most High and His Prophet described the term as such. Malik was the only one among the jurists in the countries to permit selling until the harvest and harvest, because he saw it as known. This has been discussed previously in the statement of God the Most High: They ask you about the new moons. As for the sixth condition, which is that it be present at the location, there is no disagreement about it among the nation either. If the sold item is cut off at the location of the term by the command of God the Most High, the contract is annulled according to all scholars. Seventh: It is not a condition of the Salam contract that the recipient owns it, contrary to some of the predecessors, as narrated by Al-Bukhari: On the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi al-Mujalid, who said: Abdullah ibn Shaddad and Abu Burdah sent me to Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa and said: Ask him, did the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) give advance payment for wheat during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? Abdullah said: We used to give advance payment to the people of Ash-Sham for wheat, barley and oil by a known measure for a known period. I said: To whom did the original amount come from? He said: We did not ask them about that. Then he sent me to Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza and I asked him. He said: The companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to give advance payment during the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and we did not ask them whether they had a crop or not. Abu Hanifa stipulated that the Muslim should be present from the time of the contract until the time of the contract, for fear that the Muslim might be sought and not found, which would be a risk. The rest of the jurists disagreed with him and said: Its presence at the time of the contract is considered. The Kufians and al-Thawri stipulated that the place of possession should be mentioned in what has a load and a burden, and they said: The salam contract is invalid if the place of possession is not mentioned. Al-Awza’i said: It is disliked. In our view, if they were silent about it, the contract would not be invalidated, and the place of possession would be specified. Ahmad, Ishaq, and a group of the people of hadith said the same, based on the hadith of Ibn Abbas, for there is no mention of the place where the salam contract is to be possessed. If it were one of its conditions, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have made it clear, just as he made clear the measure, weight, and term. Similar to it is the hadith of Ibn Abi Awfa. Eighth: Abu Dawood narrated on the authority of Saad meaning Al-Ta’i on the authority of Atiyah bin Saad on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever advances something should not spend it on something else. Abu Muhammad Abd al-Haqq said: Atiyah is al-Awfi, and no one can use his hadith as evidence, even though the ajla’ have narrated from him. Malik said: The matter with us regarding someone who advances food at a known price for a specified period, and the period has expired and the buyer does not find the seller to pay what he bought from him, so he releases him, is that he should not take from him anything except his silver or gold or the price that he paid him specifically, and that he should not buy anything from him with that price until he receives it from him. This is because if he takes something other than the price that he paid him or spends it on something other than the food that he bought from him, then it is the food before it is fully paid. Malik said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) forbade the sale of food before it is fully paid. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: Then write it down, meaning the debt and the term. It is said: He ordered writing, but what is meant is writing and witnessing, because writing without witnesses is not evidence. It is said: We were ordered to write so that we would not forget. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd on the authority of Yusuf ibn Mihran on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the words of God the Almighty: When you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down to the end of the verses: “The first person to deny it was Adam, peace be upon him. God showed him his descendants and he saw a man with a shining light. He said, ‘O Lord, who is this?’ He said, ‘Your son David.’ He said, ‘O Lord, how old is he?’ He said, ‘Sixty years.’ He said, ‘O Lord, add to his years.’ He said, ‘There is no god but God that He should add to your lifespan.’ He said, ‘What is my lifespan?’ He said, ‘A thousand years.’ Adam said, ‘I have given him forty years.’ He said, ‘So God wrote a book for him and had His angels bear witness to it. When death approached him, the angels came to him and he said, ‘There are forty years left of my life.’ They said, ‘You have given them to your son David.’ He said, ‘I have not given anything to anyone.’ He said, ‘So God the Almighty brought out the book and had His angels bear witness to it.’” In another narration: And He completed one hundred years for David and one thousand years for Adam. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi as well. In his saying: Then write it down, there is an apparent indication that he should write it down with all of its descriptions that are clear to it and express it, due to the imagined difference between the two parties, which informs the judge of what he should rule upon their being brought before him. And God knows best. Tenth: Some people have said that writing down debts is obligatory for their owners, imposed by this verse, whether it is a sale or a loan, so that forgetfulness or denial does not occur in it, and this is the choice of At-Tabari. Ibn Jurayj said: Whoever lends should write it down, and whoever sells should bear witness. Al-Sha’bi said: They used to think that his saying If he trusts abrogates his command to write down. Ibn Jurayj narrated something similar, and Ibn Zayd said it, and it was narrated from Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri. Al-Rabi’ said that it is obligatory with these words, then God the Most High made it easier by saying: If some of you trust others. The majority said: The command to write down is an encouragement to preserve money and remove doubt. If the debtor is pious, then writing down will not harm him, but if he is not, then writing down is trustworthy in his religion and the need of the owner of the right. Some of them said: If you bear witness, then be firm, and if you are entrusted, then you are absolved and able. Ibn ‘Atiyyah: This is the correct opinion. There is no abrogation in this, because God Almighty has urged the Book regarding what a person can give away and leave behind by consensus, so His recommendation is only for the sake of caution for people. Eleventh: The Almighty’s saying: And let a scribe write between you in justice. Ata’ and others said: It is obligatory for the scribe to write, and Al-Sha’bi said the same, and that is if there is no scribe other than him, then it is obligatory for him to write. Al-Suddi: It is obligatory with the gap. The lam was deleted from the first and confirmed in the second, because the second is absent and the first is for the addressee. It has been confirmed in the addressee, and from that is the Almighty’s saying: So let them rejoice with the ta’. And it is deleted in the absent, and from that: Muhammad, sacrifice yourself every soul if you are afraid of something, take it easy Twelfth: The Almighty’s statement: with justice, meaning with truth and equity, meaning that he does not write for the one who has the right more than what he said or less. And He said between you and did not say one of you, because since the one who has the debt is accused in the book on which the debt is, and vice versa, God Almighty prescribed a scribe other than them who would write with justice, so that there would be no animosity in his heart or pen for one of them over the other. And it was said: Since people used to deal with each other so that none of them would deviate from the deal, and there were those among them who wrote and those who did not, God Almighty commanded that a scribe write between them with justice. Thirteenth: The letter ba in the Almighty’s saying with justice is related to His saying: and to write and is not related to scribe because it was necessary that no one should write a document except someone who is just in himself, and a boy, a slave, or someone who is cautious may write it if they establish its jurisprudence. As for those who are appointed to write it, it is not permissible for the rulers to leave them alone except those who are just and acceptable. Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: No one should write documents between people except someone who is knowledgeable about them, just in himself, and trustworthy, because God Almighty said: And let a scribe write between you with justice. I said: So the ba’ in this case is related to scribe, meaning that a just scribe will write between you, so bi-just is in the position of an adjective. Fourteenth: The Almighty’s statement: And let not a scribe refuse to write. God forbade the scribe from refusing. People differed about the obligation of writing on the writer and witnessing on the witness. Al-Tabari and Al-Rabi’ said: It is obligatory on the writer if he is ordered to write. Al-Hasan said: It is obligatory on him in a situation where he is not able to have another writer, and it harms the religion if he refuses. If that is the case, then it is an obligation. If he is able to have another writer, then he is at liberty if someone else does it. Al-Suddi said: It is obligatory on him when he is free, and this has been mentioned previously. Al-Mahdawi narrated on the authority of Al-Rabi’ and Al-Dahhak that his statement and he shall not refuse was abrogated by his statement and neither the writer nor the witness shall be harmed. I said: This is consistent with the statement of those who saw or thought that it was obligatory at first for whoever the two contracting parties chose to write, and it was not permissible for him to refuse until it was abrogated by the words of God Almighty: And let no scribe or witness be harmed. This is far-fetched, because it has not been proven that it is obligatory for whoever the two contracting parties wanted, whoever he may be. If writing was obligatory, hiring for it would not be valid, because hiring for performing obligations is invalid, and the scholars did not differ about the permissibility of taking a fee for writing a document. Ibn al-Arabi: What is correct is that it is a matter of guidance, so he should not write until he takes his right. Abaa ya’ba is an anomaly, and nothing came except qala yaqala, abaa ya’ba, ghassa yaghsaa, and jaba al-kharaj yajba, and it has been mentioned previously. Fifteenth: The Almighty’s statement: As God has taught him, so let him write. The kaf in kama is related to His statement to write. The meaning is to write as God has taught him. It is possible that it is related to what is in His statement and not refuse of the meaning, that is, as God has blessed him with the knowledge of writing, so let him not refuse and let him excel as God has excelled him. It is possible that the speech on this meaning is complete when He says to write, then as God has taught him is the beginning of a speech, and the kaf is related to His statement so let him write. Sixteenth: The Almighty said: And let him upon whom the right is dictate, meaning the debtor who is wanted, who confesses to himself with his tongue so that he knows what he owes. Dictation and dictation are two languages, amal and amla. Amal is the language of the people of Hijaz and Banu Asad, and Tamim says: I dictated. The Qur’an came in both languages. The Almighty said: So she dictates to him morning and evening. The original is amlalat, and the lam was replaced with a ya’ because it is lighter. So the Almighty commanded the one upon whom the right is to dictate, because testimony is only due to his confession. The Almighty commanded him to be pious in what he dictates, and forbade him from reducing anything of the right, and reducing means deficiency. From this meaning is the Almighty’s saying: And it is not lawful for them to conceal what God has created in their wombs. Seventeenth: The Almighty’s saying: If the one upon whom the right is is a fool or weak. Some people said: meaning young. This is a mistake, because the fool may be old, as will be explained. Or weak meaning old and has no mind. Or unable to dictate. God made the one upon whom the right is of four types: one who is independent and dictates, and three types who do not dictate and their calamities occur at all times, and the right is due to them in two aspects other than transactions such as inheritances if they are divided and other than that, and they are the fool, the weak, and the one who is unable to dictate. The fool is the one who has a weak opinion regarding money and does not know how to take from it for himself or give from it, and is likened to a foolish garment, which is lightly woven. The one with a foul tongue is called a fool, because foulness is rarely found except in ignorant people and those with weak minds. And the horror of the word foolishness refers to weakness of mind sometimes and weakness of body other times. The poet said: We fear that our dreams will be fooled and that time will be ignorant of the dreamer And Dhu al-Rummah said: Walking as spears shake, their tops are blown away by the passing winds That is, he weakened it and made it soft, so he moved it. They said: Weakness is with a damma on the letter Ḍād in the word body and with a fathah on the letter Ḍād in the word opinion. It was said: They are two languages. The first is more correct, because Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “A man was buying during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his mind was weak. His family came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Prophet of God, put so-and-so under guardianship, for he is buying and his mind is weak.’ So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and forbade him from selling. He said: ‘O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I cannot stay away from selling for even an hour.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If you are not going to give up selling, then say ‘Ha, Ha, and do not cheat.’” Abu ‘Isa Muhammad ibn ‘Isa al-Sulami al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Anas, and he said: It is authentic. He said: A man was weak in his mind, and he mentioned the hadith. Al-Bukhari mentioned it in al-Tarikh and said about it: If you sell, say, ‘No cheating.’ You have the option for three nights regarding every item you buy. This man is Hubban bin Munqidh bin Amr al-Ansari, the father of Yahya and Wasi’, the sons of Hubban. It was said that he is Munqidh, the grandfather of Yahya and Wasi’, the two sheikhs of Malik, and his father is Hubban. He lived to be one hundred and thirty years old. He was wounded in one of his campaigns with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by a wound that left him insane and speechless. Al-Darqutni narrated that he said: Hubban bin Munqidh was a weak, blind man who had been scorched on the head by a scorpion. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him the option of choosing what he bought for three days. His tongue had become heavy, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Sell and say: ‘No deception.’ I heard him say: ‘No deception, no deception.’” Narrated by Abu Omar. Deception means trickery. From this is their saying: If you cannot be defeated, then deceive. Eighteenth: The scholars differed regarding someone who is deceived in sales due to his lack of experience and weak mind. Should he be placed under guardianship or not? Ahmad and Ishaq said that he should be placed under guardianship. Others said that he should not be placed under guardianship. The two opinions are in the school of thought, and the first is correct, due to this verse and his saying in the hadith: O Prophet of God, place so-and-so under guardianship. He did not place him under guardianship because he said: O Prophet of God, I cannot resist selling. So he permitted him to sell and made it specific to him, because whoever is deceived in sales should be placed under guardianship, especially if it is due to his mental insanity. What indicates the specificity is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Habban told me, he is my grandfather Munqidh ibn Amr, “and he was a man who had been struck by a stroke on his head that broke his tongue and took away his mind, and he would not give up trading and would continue to be cheated. So he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so he said: When you sell, say: There is no deception, then you have the option for three nights regarding every item you buy. If you are satisfied then keep it, and if you are dissatisfied then return it to its owner.” Omar lived a long life, he lived for one hundred and thirty years, and during the time of Uthman ibn Affan may God be pleased with him when people became widespread and numerous, he would buy goods in the market and return them to his family having been terribly cheated. They would blame him and say to him, Will you buy? He would say, “I have the option. If you are satisfied, I will take it, and if you are dissatisfied, I will return it. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) gave me the option of three days.” He would return the goods to their owner the next day and the day after, and he would say, “By God, I will not accept them. You have taken my goods and given me dirhams.” He would say, “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) gave me the option of three days.” So a man from the companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) would pass by and say to the merchant, “Woe to you! He has spoken the truth. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) gave him the option of three days.” Narrated by Al-Daraqutni. Abu Omar mentioned it in Al-Isti’ab and said: Al-Bukhari mentioned it in Al-Tarikh on the authority of Ayyash ibn Al-Waleed on the authority of Abdul A’la on the authority of Ibn Ishaq. Nineteenth: The Almighty’s saying: or weak. The weak is the one whose mind is impaired, whose nature is deficient, and who is unable to dictate, either due to his inability, his muteness, or his ignorance of how to speak. This person’s guardian may also be a father or a trustee. The one who cannot dictate is the minor, and his guardian is his trustee or his father. The one who is absent from the place of witnessing, either due to illness or some other excuse, and his guardian is his representative. As for the mute, it is permissible for him to be among the weak, and it is more appropriate that he is among those who are unable. These are distinct categories, and their explanation and discussion will come in Women, God willing. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth: The Almighty said: So let his guardian dictate with justice. At-Tabari believed that the pronoun in his guardian refers to the right and attributed this to Al-Rabi’ and Ibn Abbas. It was said: It refers to the one upon whom the right is, which is correct. What was narrated from Ibn Abbas is not correct. How can the witness testify to something and enter money into the conscience of the fool by dictating the one who owes the debt! This is something that is not in the Sharia. Unless the one who said it means that the one who is unable to dictate due to illness or old age, because his tongue is too heavy to dictate or because he is mute, and if that is the case, then the sick person and the one whose tongue is too heavy to dictate or because he is mute are not a guardian according to one of the scholars, like what was proven regarding the boy and the fool according to the one who is under guardianship. If that is the case, then the one with the right should dictate with justice and listen to the one who is unable, and when he completes dictation, he acknowledges it. This is a meaning that the verse did not intend: This is not correct except for the one who is unable to dictate due to illness and the one mentioned with him. Twenty-first: When God Almighty said: And let the one upon whom the right is dictate, this indicates that he is trustworthy in what he brings and issues, and this requires accepting the statement of the pledger with his oath if he and the pledgee disagree about the amount of the debt and the pledge is in effect. So the pledger says, I pledged fifty, and the pledgee claims one hundred, then the statement of the pledger is accepted and the pledge is in effect. This is the doctrine of most of the jurists: Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and the people of opinion. Ibn al-Mundhir chose it, saying: Because the pledgee claims the surplus, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The burden of proof is on the plaintiff and the oath is on the defendant. Malik said: The word of the mortgagee is to be taken as evidence between him and the value of the mortgage, and no more than that is to be believed. It is as if he sees that the mortgage and his oath are witnesses for the mortgagee, and the statement of God the Almighty: And let him upon whom the right is dictate is a refutation of him. The one upon whom the right is is the mortgager. This issue will come. If someone says: God the Almighty made the mortgage a substitute for the testimony and the letter, and the testimony indicates the truthfulness of the one for whom the testimony is given as evidence between him and the value of the mortgage, so if it reaches its value, there is no proof of the increase. It is said to him: The mortgage indicates that its value must be the amount of the debt, because something may be mortgaged for little or much. Yes, the mortgage usually does not fall short of the amount of the debt, but if it matches it, it does not. This speaker says: The mortgagee is to be believed with an oath regarding the amount of the debt until it equals the value of the mortgage. This is not the custom, because perhaps the debt falls short of the mortgage, which is the norm, so their statement is of no consequence. Twenty-second: If it is proven that the guardian is meant, then this is evidence that his approval is permissible for his orphan, because if he dictates it, then his word is implemented against him regarding what he dictated. Twenty-third: The actions of a fool who is under guardianship without the permission of his guardian are unanimously invalid and irrevocable, and do not require a ruling or have any effect. If a fool acts and is not under guardianship, then there is a difference of opinion about it, which will be explained in the chapter on women, God willing. Twenty-fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men. Martyrdom means asking for testimony. People differed as to whether it is obligatory or recommended. The correct view is that it is recommended, as will be explained, God willing. Twenty-fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Two witnesses. God Almighty has ordained testimony in His wisdom in financial and physical rights and the prescribed punishments, and He has made and made in every art two witnesses except in the case of adultery, as will be explained in Surat An-Nisa. And witness is an exaggerated vocative, and in that there is an indication of someone who has testified and has done so repeatedly, so it is as if it is an indication of justice. And God knows best. Twenty-sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Of your men is explicit in rejecting the infidels, children and women. As for slaves, the wording includes them. Mujahid said: What is meant is the free, and Judge Abu Ishaq chose this and elaborated on it. The scholars differed regarding the testimony of slaves. Shuraih, Uthman al-Batti, Ahmad, Ishaq and Abu Thawr said: The testimony of a slave is permissible if he is just, and they preferred the wording of the verse. Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi’i and the majority of scholars said: The testimony of a slave is not permissible, and they preferred the deficiency of slavery, and al-Sha’bi and al-Nakha’i permitted it in a small matter. The correct opinion is that of the majority, because God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt and continued the address to His saying: Of your men, so the apparent address includes those who contract a debt, and slaves do not own that without the permission of their masters. If they say: The specificity of the beginning of the verse does not prevent the connection to the generality of the end of it. It was said to them: This is related to the Almighty’s saying: And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon, as will be explained later.
