And His saying of your men is evidence that the blind man is among those who are eligible for testimony, but if he knows for certain, like what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about testimony, and he said: Do you see this sun? Testify to something like it, or leave it. This indicates that it is a condition for the witness to see what he testifies to, not for someone who testifies based on inference, which may be mistaken. Yes, it is permissible for him to have intercourse with his wife if he recognizes her voice, because proceeding with intercourse is permissible based on a preponderance of opinion. So if a woman is brought to him and he is told: This is your wife, and he does not know her, it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her, and it is permissible for him to accept a gift that came to him based on the words of the Messenger. If someone informs him about Zayd’s confession, sale, slander, or usurpation, it is not permissible for him to testify against the one he was informed about, because the way to testify is certainty, and in other cases it is permissible to use a preponderance of opinion. Therefore, Al-Shafi’i, Ibn Abi Layla, and Abu Yusuf said: If he knew it before he went blind, then testimony is permissible after he went blind, and the blindness that prevents him from the one testified against is like absence or death in the case of the one testified against. This is the doctrine of these people. And what prevents the blind from performing what the sighted person carries has no basis, and his testimony is valid regarding the lineage that is proven by widespread report, as he reports about what was transmitted in a ruling from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And some scholars accepted the testimony of the blind regarding what is transmitted by sound, because he saw that the evidence for that rises to the level of certainty, and he saw that the confusion of sounds is like the confusion of images and colors, and this is weak and necessitates the permissibility of relying on sound for the sighted person. I said: Malik’s school of thought states that the testimony of a blind person regarding a voice is permissible in divorce and other matters if he recognizes the voice. Ibn Qasim said: I said to Malik: What if a man hears his neighbor from behind a wall but does not see him, and hears him divorcing his wife, and he testifies against him even though he recognizes the voice? He said: Malik said: His testimony is permissible. This was said by Ali bin Abi Talib, Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, Shureih Al-Kindi, Al-Sha’bi, Ata bin Abi Rabah, Yahya bin Sa’id, Rabi’ah, Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, Malik, and Al-Layth. Twenty-seventh: The Almighty said: But if there are not two men, then a man and two women. The meaning is: If the claimant does not bring two men, then let him bring a man and two women. This is the opinion of the majority. Man is raised as the subject, and two women is conjoined to it and the predicate is omitted. That is, a man and two women will take their place. The accusative is permissible in places other than the Qur’an, that is, then call to witness a man and two women. Sibawayh narrated: If a dagger, then a dagger. Some people said: Rather, the meaning is: If there are not two men, that is, they are not found, then it is not permissible to call to witness two women except in the absence of men. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is weak, as the wording of the verse did not give it, rather what appears from it is the opinion of the majority, that is, if the one calling to witness is not two men, that is, if the owner of the right neglected that or intended it for some excuse, then let him call to witness a man and two women. God the Almighty made the testimony of two women with a man permissible in the presence of two men in this verse, and He did not mention it in any other verse. So it was permitted in money specifically according to the majority opinion, on the condition that there is a man with them. This was only in money and not in other things, because God has increased the reasons for documenting money due to the many ways of obtaining it and the general affliction with it and its repetition. So He made documentation in it sometimes by writing, sometimes by witnessing, sometimes by mortgaging, and sometimes by guaranteeing. And He included in all of that the testimony of women with men. And no sane person would imagine that the words of God the Almighty: When you contract a debt include the debt of the dowry with sexual intercourse, and the settlement of the blood money for premeditated murder, because that testimony is not testimony on the debt, rather it is testimony on marriage. The scholars permitted their testimony alone in matters that no one else can see due to necessity. Similarly, the testimony of children in injuries between them was permitted due to necessity. Scholars have differed regarding the testimony of children in cases of wounds, which are: Twenty-eighth: Malik permitted it as long as they did not differ or separate. The testimony of less than two of them is not permissible against a minor against an adult and an adult against a minor. Among those who used to rule based on the testimony of children in cases involving wounds between them was Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr. Malik said: This is the agreed upon matter among us. Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa and his companions did not permit their testimony, based on the words of God the Almighty: of your men, “of those whom you approve,” and of just men among you. These characteristics are not present in children.
2:283: It contains twenty-four issues: First: When God Almighty mentioned the encouragement to have witnesses and write for the benefit of preserving money and bodies, He followed that by mentioning the state of excuses that prevent writing, and made a pledge for it, and specified among the states of excuses travel, which is the most common excuse, especially at that time due to the frequency of invasions, and every excuse is included in that meaning. There may be a time when it is difficult for a writer to be present in the city, such as when people are busy and at night, and also the fear of ruining the debtor’s conscience is an excuse that necessitates requesting a pledge. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mortgaged his armor to a Jew who asked him for a loan of barley. He said: Muhammad only wants to steal with my money. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He lied. I am trustworthy on earth and trustworthy in heaven. If he had entrusted me, I would have paid it back. Go to him with my armor. He died and his armor was mortgaged, may God bless him and grant him peace, as will be explained above. Second: The majority of scholars said: The mortgage while traveling is according to the text of the revelation, and while at home it is proven by the Sunnah of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is correct. We have explained its permissibility while at home from the verse in meaning, since excuses may arise in the case of prohibition, and no one has narrated a prohibition while at home except Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and Dawud, who held fast to the verse. There is no proof in it, because even though this statement was made as a condition, what is meant by it is most cases. The fact that the mortgage in the verse is during travel is not something that is prohibited otherwise. In the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Aisha: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, bought food from a Jew on credit and mortgaged his iron armor.” Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died and his armor was mortgaged to a Jew for thirty sa’ of barley for his family. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And you find not a scribe. The majority read scribe meaning a man who writes. Ibn Abbas, Abi, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Ikrimah, and Abu Al-Aaliyah read and you do not find a book. Abu Bakr Al-Anbari said: Mujahid explained it and said: Its meaning is if you do not find ink, meaning in books. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas book. An-Nahhas said: This reading is anomalous and the majority are against it, and rarely does something deviate from the reading of the majority without it being criticized. The speech was organized on the subject of a scribe, as God Almighty said before this: And let a scribe write between you in justice. And a book requires a group. Ibn Atiyah said: A book is good because every case has a scribe, so it was said to the group: And you do not find a book. Al-Mahdawi narrated from Abi Al-Aaliyah that he read kutubu books, and this is the plural of kitab in terms of the different types of cases. As for the reading of Abi and Ibn Abbas kitab, An-Nahhas and Makki said: It is the plural of katib like qa’im and qiyam. Makki: The meaning is even if the inkwell, pen, and paper are not available. The denial of the existence of the writer is due to the absence of any instrument that was agreed upon, and the denial of the book also requires the denial of the book, so both readings are good except with regard to the writing of the Qur’an. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: A bet taken. Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read farhan with a damma on the ra’ and the ha’, and it was narrated from them to soften the ha’. At-Tabari said: Some people interpreted that rahana with a damma on the ra’ and the ha’ is the plural of rahn, so it is the plural of jma’, and Az-Zajjaj narrated it from Al-Farra’. Al-Mahdawi said: Faran is the subject and the predicate is omitted, and the meaning is farhan maqbudhah, which is sufficient from that. An-Nahhas said: Aasim ibn Abi Al-Najud read “farhan with a sukoon on the ha’, and it is narrated from the people of Mecca. The root of this is rahan, just as it is said: baghul and mules, “ram” and rams, and rahan is the plural of rahn, like katab and kutub. It was said: It is the plural of rahn, like saqf and saqf, “halaq” and halaq, “fursh” and fursh, and nashr and nashr, and the like. And rahan with a sukoon on the ha’ is the plural of rahn, like sahab and saqf, “halaq” and farsh, and nashr and nashr, and the like. The first is more appropriate, because the first is not an adjective and this is an adjective. Abu Ali al-Farsi said: I do not know of the breaking of rahn into the smallest number, so if it had come, its measure would have been af’al like kalb and aklab, and it is as if they dispensed with the little instead of the many, just as they dispensed with the construction of the many instead of the little in their saying: three vastness, and they dispensed with the construction of the little instead of the many in rasan and arsan, so rahn is pluralized into two constructions, which are fa’l and fa’al. Al-Akhfash: Fa’l on fa’l is ugly and it is rare and irregular. He said: And rahn may be the plural of bet, as if he pluralizes rahn on rahan, then pluralizes rahn on rahn, like farash and farash. Fifth: The meaning of mortgage: to detain the asset as a document of right in order to recover the right from its price or from the price of its benefits when it is impossible to take it from the creditor. This is how scholars have defined it. In the speech of the Arabs, it means permanence and continuity. Ibn Sidah said: And to mortgage it means to make it last, and from the word rahn meaning to continue, as in the saying of the poet: Bread and meat are theirs, and their coffee is poured freshly Al-Jawhari said: “To mortgage something means to make it last. And I mortgaged food and drink to them, meaning I made it permanent for them, and it is a mortgaged food.” And the mortgaged is the fixed, and the mortgaged is the lean camel or the people. He said: Or do you see my body as a waste, mortgaged with weakness, and the glory of men is not in fatness? Ibn Atiyah said: It is said in the meaning of the pledge, which is the document of the pledge: I pledged a pledge, some of them narrated it. Abu Ali said: I pledged in exaggeration, and as for the loan and sale, I pledged. Abu Zaid said: I pledged in the commodity an mortgage: I exaggerated in it, and it is specifically in the high price. He said: Eidiya in which I pawned dinars. Describing a camel: Al-Eid is a clan of mare and mare camels described as noble. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said about a pledge: I pledged and I pledged, and Ibn Al-A’rabi and Al-Akhfash said the same. Abdullah bin Hammam Al-Saluli said: When I feared their claws, I escaped and gave them Malik as a pledge. Tha'lab said: All the narrators agreed on their mortgage, as it is permissible to mortgage it and I mortgaged it, except for Al-Asma'i, who narrated it and he mortgaged it, as a future verb connected to a past verb, and he likened it to their saying: I stood up and slapped his face, which is a good opinion, because the waw is the waw of state, so he made slap the state of the first verb in the sense of I stood up and slapped his face, meaning I left it staying with them, because it is not said: I mortgaged the thing, but rather it is said: I mortgaged it. And you say: I mortgaged my tongue for such-and-such, and it is not said: I mortgaged it. Ibn Al-Kaseet said: I mortgaged it in the sense of I lent it. The mortgagee is the one who takes the mortgage. The thing is mortgaged and mortgaged, and the female is a hostage. I bet someone on such-and-such a bet. I mapped it. And I mortgaged my children with it as a mortgage: I threatened them with it in danger. And the hostage is the singular of hostages, all from Al-Jawhari. Ibn Atiyah: It is said without dispute in selling and lending: I mortgaged a mortgage, then the thing paid was named after this source. You say: I mortgaged a mortgage, just as you mortgaged a garment. Sixth: Abu Ali said: Since the mortgage means proof and permanence, then the mortgage is void according to the jurists if it leaves the mortgagee’s hand and goes to the pledgor in any way, because it differs from what it was made by the mortgagee’s choice. I said: This is what is accepted by us that when the mortgage is returned to the mortgager by the mortgagee’s choice, the mortgage is void. Abu Hanifa said this, but he said: If it is returned by a loan or a deposit, it is not void. Al-Shafi’i said: Its return to the mortgager’s hand absolutely does not void the ruling of possession that was mentioned above, and our evidence is a mortgage that is in possession. So if it is taken out of the possession of the recipient, this word does not apply to it linguistically, so it does not apply to it legally, and this is clear. Seventh: If he pledged it verbally but did not actually take possession of it, this does not require a ruling, based on the Almighty’s statement: A pledge taken possession of. Al-Shafi’i said: God did not make the ruling except with a pledge described as taking possession of it, so if the description is absent, the ruling must be absent, and this is very clear. The Malikis said: The pledge is binding by the contract and the pledger is forced to pay the pledge so that the pledgee may take possession of it, based on the Almighty’s statement: Fulfill contracts, which is a contract, and His statement: by the covenant, which is a covenant. And the statement of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Believers are bound by their conditions. This is a condition. For us, taking possession is a condition for its complete benefit. And for them, it is a condition for its obligation and validity. Eighth: The Almighty’s statement: received requires the mortgagee to be separated from the mortgage. People are unanimously agreed on the validity of the mortgagee’s receipt, as well as the receipt of his agent. They differed about the receipt of a just person in whose hands the mortgage is placed. Malik, all his companions, and the majority of scholars said: The receipt of a just person is receipt. Ibn Abi Laila, Qatada, Al-Hakam, and Ata’ said: It is not receipt, and it is not received unless it is with the mortgagee, and they saw that as an act of worship. The statement of the majority is more correct in terms of meaning, because if it is with the just person, it becomes received linguistically and literally, because the just person is a representative of the owner of the right and is in the position of an agent, and this is clear. Ninth: If the pledge is placed in the hands of a just person and is lost, neither the pledgee nor the thing in his possession is liable, because the pledgee did not have anything in his possession to guarantee. The thing in his possession is a trustee, and the trustee is not liable. Eleventh: Our scholars permit pledging what is owed, because it is received, contrary to those who forbade it. An example of this is two men who dealt with one another in a debt, so they pledged the debt that was owed to him. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: Every commodity that is permissible to sell is permissible to pledge. For this reason, we permit pledging what is owed, because its sale is permissible, and because it is money that a document can be made with, so it is permissible to pledge it, by analogy with an existing commodity. Those who forbade it said: “Because its receipt is not established, and receipt is a condition for the necessity of the pledge, because the right must be collected from it at the place of issue, and the collection is from its money, not from its substance, and that is not conceivable in the case of debt.” Twelfth: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The back is ridden at its own expense if it is mortgaged, and the milk of the udder is drunk at its own expense if it is mortgaged, and the expense is upon the one who rides and drinks. Narrated by Abu Dawud, who said instead of drinks in both places: milks. Al-Khattabi said: This is ambiguous speech, and the wording itself does not clarify who rides and milks, is it the mortgager, the mortgagee, or the just person in whose hand the mortgage is placed? I said: This has been explained and clarified in two hadiths, and because of them the scholars differed on this. Al-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurairah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If the animal is mortgaged, then the mortgagee is responsible for its feed and the milk it drinks, and the one who drinks it is responsible for its expenses. Narrated by Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Ala’, who narrated to us, Ziyad ibn Ayoub, who narrated to us, Hisham, who narrated to us, Zakariya, from al-Sha’bi, from Abu Hurayrah. This is the opinion of Ahmad and Ishaq: that the mortgagee benefits from the mortgage by milking and riding it in proportion to the expenses. Abu Thawr said: If the mortgager spends on it, the mortgagee does not benefit from it. But if the mortgager does not spend on it and leaves it in the hands of the mortgagee, who spends on it, then he has the right to ride it and employ the slave. This was stated by al-Awza’i and al-Layth. The second hadith was also narrated by al-Daraqutni, and there is an issue in its chain of transmission, which will be explained later - from the hadith of Ismail ibn Ayyash, from Ibn Abi Dhi’b, from al-Zuhri, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The pledge shall not be forfeited, and its owner shall have the benefit and shall bear the loss. This is the opinion of al-Shafi’i, al-Sha’bi, and Ibn Sirin, and it is the opinion of Malik and his companions. Al-Shafi’i said: The benefit of the pledge is for the pledgor, and its expenses are his, and the mortgagee shall not benefit from anything from the pledge except for the preservation of the document. Al-Khattabi said: This is the first and most correct opinion, based on the statement of the Prophet (peace be upon him): The pledge shall not be forfeited from its owner who pledged it to him, and he shall bear the loss. Al-Khattabi said: His statement: from its owner means for its owner. The Arabs use min in place of lam, as in their saying: Is it true that Umm Awfa did not speak? I said: It came explicitly to its owner, so there is no need for interpretation. At-Tahawi said: That was at a time when usury was permissible, and he did not forbid a loan that brought benefit, nor did he forbid taking one thing for another even if they were not equal. Then usury was forbidden after that. The nation agreed that the mortgaged female slave is not permitted to be slept with by the mortgager, so it is also not permitted for him to serve her. Ash-Sha’bi said: He does not benefit from the mortgage at all. This Ash-Sha’bi narrated the hadith and issued a fatwa to the contrary, and in his view that is not permissible except that it is abrogated. Ibn ‘Abd al-Barr said: They agreed that the milk and back of the mortgaged are for the mortgager. It is possible that the mortgagee milked it with the permission of the mortgager or without his permission. If it was without his permission, then in the hadith of Ibn ‘Umar from the Prophet (peace be upon him): No one shall milk another’s cattle except with his permission. This is what is rejected and what is decreed to be abrogated. If it is with his permission, then the agreed upon principles prohibiting the unknown, uncertainty, selling what you do not have, and selling what has not been created also reject this, because that was before the prohibition of usury was revealed. And God knows best. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: If the mortgagee stipulates the benefit of the mortgage, then there are two cases for that: If it is from a loan, it is not permissible, and if it is from a sale or lease, it is permissible, because he becomes a seller of the commodity at the mentioned price and the benefits of the mortgage are for a known period, so it is as if it is a sale and lease. As for the loan, because it becomes a loan that brings benefit, and because the subject of the loan is to be an act of worship, so if benefit enters it, it becomes an increase in the type and that is usury. Thirteenth: It is not permissible to close a mortgage, which is for the mortgagee to stipulate that he has his right if he does not bring it to him at its due date. This was an act of the Jahiliyyah, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nullified it by saying: A mortgage is not closed. This is how we qualified it by raising the qaf as a predicate, meaning the mortgage is not closed. You say: I closed the door, so it is closed. And closing the mortgage is in the hand of its mortgagee if he does not redeem it. The poet said: Our neighbor, whoever gathers will disperse, and whoever is subject to accidents will close. Zuhair said: I left you with a pledge that could not be released on the day of farewell, and the pledge became closed. Fourteenth: Al-Darqutni narrated from the hadith of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, on the authority of Ziyad bin Saad, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The pledge shall not be closed, and he shall bear the loss. Ziyad ibn Sa’d is one of the trustworthy hadith masters, and this is a good chain of transmission. Malik narrated it on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, with a mursal chain of transmission, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The pledge shall not be closed. Abu ‘Umar said: “This is how it was narrated by everyone who narrated al-Muwatta’ on the authority of Malik, as far as I know, except for Ma’n ibn ‘Isa, who connected it, and Ma’n is trustworthy, except that I fear that the mistake in it is from ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid al-Ghadha’iri on the authority of Mujahid ibn Musa on the authority of Ma’n ibn ‘Isa. Abu ‘Abdullah ‘Amrus added to it on the authority of al-Abhari in his chain of transmission: “He shall bear the loss, and he shall bear the loss.” The narrators differed in their attribution of this wording to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abi Dhi’b, Mu’ammar, and others attributed it to the Prophet. Narrated by Ibn Wahb who said: Yunus said: Ibn Shihab said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab used to say: The pledge belongs to the one who pledged it, he has the right to its gain and he is responsible for its loss. Ibn Shihab said that this was said by Saeed and not from the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him. However, Muammar mentioned it from Ibn Shihab with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him. Muammar is the most reliable of people regarding Ibn Shihab. Yahya bin Abi Anisa followed him in narrating it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and Yahya is not strong. The origin of this hadith according to the scholars of transmission is mursal, even though it has been transmitted through many sources, which they attribute to weakness. However, it is a hadith that none of them attribute to the Prophet, even though they differed in its interpretation and meaning. Ad-Darqutni also narrated it on the authority of Ismail bin Ayyash, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Abu Umar said: Ismail did not hear it from Ibn Abi Dhi’b, but he heard it from ‘Ibad bin Kathir, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, and ‘Ibad is weak in their view and cannot be relied upon. Ismail is also not acceptable to them if he narrates from people other than his country. If he narrates from people from the Levant, his narration is sound, but if he narrates from people from Medina and others, his narration contains many errors and confusion. Fifteenth: The growth of the pledge is included with it if it is not distinct, such as fat, or if it is offspring, such as birth and offspring, and similar to it is the offspring of the palm tree, and other than that of yield, fruit, milk and wool, it is not included in it unless it is stipulated. The difference between them is that children follow the mothers in zakat, but the wool, milk and fruit of trees are not like that, because they are not followed by the mothers in zakat, nor are they in their forms or meaning, nor do they stand with them, so they have their own ruling, not the ruling of the origin, unlike the child and offspring. And God knows best about the correctness of that. Sixteenth: A mortgage is permissible for someone whose debt has covered his property, as long as he has not gone bankrupt. The mortgagee has more right to the mortgage than the creditors. This was stated by Malik and a group of people. A different opinion was reported from Malik - and this was stated by Abdul Aziz bin Abi Salamah - that the creditors are included with him in this, but it is nothing, because if someone is not placed under guardianship, his actions are valid in all his circumstances, from buying and selling, and the creditors treat him as if he sells, buys, and pays. Malik’s opinion did not differ in this regard, and so is the mortgage. And God knows best. Seventeenth: The Almighty’s saying: If some of you trust others Al-Anfal 17:1. A condition that links the will of the one who owes the debt to pay and refrain from delaying payment. Meaning, if the one who owes the debt is trustworthy and reliable with the owner of the debt, then let him pay him what he was entrusted with. His saying then let him pay from the word pay has a hamza, and it is the answer to the condition. It is permissible to lighten the hamza, so the hamza is changed to a waw, but it is not changed to an alif, and there is no in-between, because the alif is only preceded by an open letter. It is a matter that means obligation, based on the consensus on the obligation of paying debts, and the confirmation of the judge’s ruling on it and his compulsion of the creditors upon it, and based on the authentic hadiths on the prohibition of the money of others. Eighteenth: The Almighty’s saying: His trust. Trust is a source by which the thing that is in the conscience is named, and He added it to the one who owes the debt in terms of its relation to it, as the Almighty said: And do not give your wealth to the foolish. Nineteenth: The Almighty said: And let him fear God, his Lord, meaning in not concealing any of the truth. His saying: And do not conceal testimony is an explanation of His saying: And do not harm with a kasra on the ‘ayn. The witness was forbidden from being harmed by concealing testimony, and it is a prohibition of obligation with several indications including the threat. The place of the prohibition is where the witness fears the loss of a right. Ibn Abbas said: The witness must testify wherever he is called to testify, and inform wherever he is asked to inform. He said: Do not say, I informed it to the emir, but rather, I informed him of it so that he may return and be reassured. Abu Abd al-Rahman read and do not conceal with a ya’, making it a prohibition for the absent. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth: If there are witnesses to the right, they must perform it sufficiently. If two perform it and the judge suffices with them, the obligation is dropped from the rest. If he does not suffice with them, it is necessary to go to him until proof is established. This is known by the supplication of its owner. If he says to him: I revive my right by performing what you have for me of testimony, then that is obligatory upon him. Twenty-first: The Almighty said: And whoever conceals it, then indeed his heart is sinful. He mentioned the heart specifically since concealment is one of its actions, and since it is the morsel of flesh whose soundness makes the whole body sound, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said. So He expressed the sentence with some, and it was mentioned earlier in the Surah. Al-Kiya said: When he resolved not to perform it and left performing it with his tongue, the sin returned to both aspects. So his saying: his heart is sinful is a metaphor, and it is more emphatic than the truth in indicating the threat, and it is from the wonderful expression and subtle articulation of meanings. It is said: the heart is sinful because of its transformation, and God Almighty, if He transforms a heart, He makes it a hypocrite and seals it, we seek refuge in God from Him, and it was mentioned earlier in the Surah. And his heart is raised with sin, and sin is the predicate of if, and if you wish, you can raise sinful as the subject, and his heart is the subject that fills the place of the predicate, and the sentence is the predicate of if. And if you wish, you can raise sinful as the predicate of the beginning, intending to delay it. If you wish, it could be a substitute for sin or a substitute for part for whole. If you wish, it could be a substitute for the implied pronoun in sin. Three issues were presented here, completing twenty-four. First: Know that what God the Almighty has commanded of witnessing and writing is to take into account the reconciliation of people and to eliminate disputes that lead to corruption of people, lest Satan tempt him to deny the truth and exceed what the Shariah has set, or to leave the amount due, and for this reason the Shariah has forbidden unknown transactions, the habit of which leads to differences and corruption of people and the occurrence of resentment and disparity. Among these is what God has forbidden of gambling, and drinking alcohol, as God the Almighty says: Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through intoxicants and gambling 3:10. Whoever follows the discipline of God in His commands and prohibitions will attain the reconciliation of this world and the hereafter. God the Almighty says: And if they had done what they were instructed to do, it would have been better for them 3:10. Second: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Whoever takes people’s money intending to repay it, God will repay it on his behalf. Whoever takes it intending to waste it, God will waste him.” Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: She borrowed money, and it was said: O Mother of the Believers, you borrow money and you do not have the means to pay it back? She said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever takes on a debt and intends to pay it back, God will help him with it. At-Tahawi, Abu Ja`far al-Tabari, and Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah narrated in his Musnad on the authority of `Uqbah ibn `Amir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not frighten people after they are secure. They said: O Messenger of God, what is that? He said: Religion. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Anas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a supplication he mentioned: O God, I seek refuge in You from worry, grief, helplessness, laziness, cowardice, miserliness, being in debt, and being overpowered by men. Scholars said: Being in debt is when the lender cannot find where to pay him. It is taken from the Arab saying: A heavy load, meaning a heavy animal, and a heavy animal is one that cannot bear the load, said Hishaab al-Ayn. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Religion is the disgrace of religion. It was narrated that he said: Debt is a concern at night and a humiliation during the day. Our scholars said: It is shameful and humiliating because it preoccupies the heart and mind, and the necessary concern in paying it, and humiliating oneself before the debtor when meeting him, and bearing his favor by delaying it until its time. And perhaps he promises to pay it himself and then fails to do so, or the debtor speaks about it and lies about it, or he swears to him and he breaks his oath, and so on. For this reason: “He, peace be upon him, used to seek refuge from sin and debt. So say to him: O Messenger of God, how often do you seek refuge from debt? Qaffal said: If a man is in debt, he speaks and lies and makes a promise and breaks it.” Also, he may have died without paying off the debt, so it becomes a mortgage, as he, peace be upon him, said: The soul of the believer is mortgaged in his grave to his debt until it is paid off. All of these reasons are shameful to the religion, they take away its beauty and diminish its perfection. And God knows best. Third: When God the Almighty commanded writings, witnesses, and taking bets, this was a clear text on observing the preservation and growth of wealth, and a response to the ignorant Sufis and their rabble who do not see this, so they give away all their wealth and do not leave enough for themselves and their children. Then, if he is in need and his children become poor, he either accepts the favors of his brothers or their charity, or takes from the masters of the world and their oppression. This action is reprehensible and forbidden. Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: I am not surprised by the ascetics who did this despite their lack of knowledge. Rather, I am surprised by people who have knowledge and reason, how they urged this and ordered it despite it being contrary to the Shari’ah and reason. Al-Muhasibi mentioned many words about this, and Abu Hamid al-Tusi strengthened and supported it. In my opinion, al-Harith is more excused than Abu Hamid, because Abu Hamid was more knowledgeable, but his entry into Sufism required him to support what he entered into. Al-Muhasibi said in a long statement of his: It has reached me that: When Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf died, some of the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said, We only fear for Abdur-Rahman because of what he left behind. Ka’b said, Glory be to God! What do you fear for Abdur-Rahman? He earned well, spent well, and left behind well. When Abu Dharr heard of that, he went out angrily, seeking Ka’b. He passed by a camel’s jawbone and took it by the hand, then set off looking for Ka’b. It was said to Ka’b, Abu Dharr is looking for you. So he ran away until he entered upon Uthman seeking help and told him the report. Abu Dharr began to trace the trail of Ka’b until he reached Uthman’s house. When he entered, Ka’b stood up and sat behind Uthman, running away from Abu Dharr. Abu Dharr said to him, “O son of the Jewess, do you claim that what Abdur-Rahman left behind is okay? The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) came out one day and said, ‘The majority will be the minority on the Day of Resurrection, except for those who say thus and thus.’” Al-Muhasibi said: This is Abd al-Rahman, with his virtue, who will be stopped in a courtyard on the Day of Resurrection because of what he earned lawfully, for his chastity and good deeds, and he will be prevented from striving to Paradise with the poor, and he will crawl in their footsteps, and so on from his words. Abu Hamid mentioned it, strengthened it, and strengthened it: In the hadith of Tha’laba, that he was given money but refused to pay zakat. Abu Hamid said: Whoever observes the conditions of the prophets and saints and their sayings will not doubt that losing money is better than having it, even if it is spent on good deeds, because the least that is in it is to be preoccupied with improving it rather than remembering God. So the seeker should give up his money until he has nothing left except what is necessary for him, and whatever dirham remains for him to turn to in his heart is hidden from God the Most High. Al-Jawzi said: All of this is contrary to the Shari’ah and reason, and a misunderstanding of what is meant by money, and God has honored it and magnified its value and commanded that it be preserved, since He made it a means of support for mankind, and whatever He made a means of support for the noble man is noble, so God the Most High said: And do not give the foolish your property which God has made a means of support for you. And God the Almighty forbade giving money to someone who is not wise, saying: But if you perceive in them sound judgment, then release their property to them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade wasting money. He said to Sa`d: It is better for you to leave your heirs rich than to leave them poor, begging from people.” He said: The wealth of Kamal Abu Bakr did not benefit me. He said to Amr ibn al-Aas: Yes, good money for the good man. He prayed for Anas, and his last prayer was: O God, increase his wealth and children and be good to him in them. Kaab said: “O Messenger of God, one of my repentances is to give away my wealth as charity to God and His Messenger. He said: Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you.” Al-Jawzi said: These hadiths are included in the Sahihs, and they are contrary to what the Sufis believe, that accumulating wealth is a veil and a punishment, and that withholding it contradicts trust in God. It is not denied that its temptation is feared, and that many people avoid it for fear of that, and that collecting it from its source is difficult, and that the heart’s safety from being tempted by it is reduced, and the heart being occupied with remembrance of the Hereafter while being present is rare, so this is why its temptation is feared. As for earning money, whoever limits himself to earning enough money lawfully, then that is a must. As for whoever intends to collect it and increase it lawfully, then he should consider his intention. If he intends to boast and show off, then that is a bad intention. But if he intends to protect himself and his family, and saves for the events of his time and theirs, and intends to provide for his brothers and enrich the poor and do good deeds, then he will be rewarded for his intention. Collecting it with this intention is better than many acts of obedience. The intentions of many of the Companions in collecting money were sound due to the goodness of their intentions in collecting it, so they were keen on it and asked for an increase in it. "When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) cut off Al-Zubayr, he brought his horse and galloped the horse until he stood up, then he threw his whip and said: Give him wherever his whip reaches." Sa`d ibn `Ubadah used to say in his supplication: O God, be generous to me. And my brother Yusuf said: And we will increase by a camel's load. And Shu`ayb said to Moses: But if you complete ten, it will be from You. And when Ayyub recovered, a man scattered golden locusts on him, so he began to gather them in his garment and ask for more of them. So it was said to him: Have you not had your fill? So he said: O Lord, is a poor man satisfied with Your bounty? This is something that is deeply rooted in human nature. As for the words of Al-Muhasibi, they are mistakes that indicate ignorance of knowledge. And what he mentioned of the hadith of Ka`b and Ubayy is impossible, a fabrication of the ignorant, and its invalidity was hidden from him because of its connection to the people. Some of this has been narrated, although its chain of transmission is not proven, because in its chain of transmission is Ibn Lahi`ah, who is criticized. Yahya said: His hadith cannot be relied upon. The correct history is that Abu Dharr died in the year twenty-five, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf died in the year thirty-two, so he lived seven years after Abu Dharr. Then the wording of what they mentioned of their hadith indicates that their hadith is fabricated. Then how can the companions say: We fear for Abd al-Rahman, or is there no consensus on the permissibility of collecting money from lawful sources, so what is the point of fear when it is permissible? Or does the law permit something and then punish it? This is a deficiency and it is jurisprudence. Then does Abu Dharr deny Abd al-Rahman, and Abd al-Rahman is better than Abu Dharr in a way that is not comparable? Then his attachment to Abd al-Rahman alone is evidence that he did not investigate the conduct of the companions, for Talhah left behind three hundred spices, each spice has three qintars. And a spice is a load. And the wealth of al-Zubayr was fifty thousand and two hundred thousand. And Ibn Mas`ud left behind ninety thousand. Most of the companions earned money and left it behind, and none of them denied it to anyone. As for his saying: Abdul Rahman will crawl on the Day of Resurrection. This is evidence that he did not know the hadith. I seek refuge in God that Abdul Rahman will crawl on the Day of Resurrection. Do you think that someone who preceded and is one of the ten who were promised Paradise and one of the people of Badr and Shura will crawl? Then the hadith is narrated by Ammarah bin Zadhan, and Al-Bukhari said: Perhaps his hadith is confused. Ahmad said: He narrates strange hadiths from Anas, and Abu Hatim Al-Razi said: He cannot be relied upon, and Al-Daraqutni said: He is weak. His statement: Leaving lawful money is better than accumulating it is not like that, and whenever the intention is correct, accumulating it is better without any disagreement among the scholars. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab used to say: There is no good in someone who does not seek money, to pay off his debts and protect his honor, and if he dies, he leaves it as an inheritance for those after him. Ibn Al-Musayyab left behind four hundred dinars, and Sufyan Al-Thawri left behind two hundred, and he used to say: Money in this time is a weapon. The predecessors continued to praise money and collect it for calamities and to help the poor. However, some of them avoided it, preferring to be busy with worship and collecting worries, so they were satisfied with little. If this speaker said: Reducing it is better, the matter would be brought closer, but he would crowd it with the level of sin. I said: What indicates the preservation and care of money is the permissibility of fighting over and without it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr. This will be explained in Al-Ma’idah, God willing.
2:284: The Almighty said: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. The meaning of this has been presented. The Almighty’s saying: And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it. There are two issues in this: First: People differed regarding the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And whether you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it. There are five opinions: The first: that it was abrogated, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, Aisha, Abu Hurairah, Al-Shaabi, Ata’, Muhammad ibn Sirin, Muhammad ibn Ka’b, Musa ibn Ubaydah and a group of the Companions and Followers, and that this obligation remained for a year until God revealed relief by saying: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. This is the statement of Ibn Masoud, Aisha, Ata’, Muhammad ibn Sirin, Muhammad ibn Ka’b and others. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When the verse, And if you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it, was revealed, he said: Something of it entered their hearts that had not entered their hearts before, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Say, ‘We hear, we obey, and we submit.’ He said: So God cast faith into their hearts, and God revealed: “God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have whatever it has earned, and it will bear whatever it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake.” He said: “We have already done so, our Lord. And lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us.” He said: “We have already done so, our Lord. And do not burden us with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.” He said: I have already done so. In one narration, when they did that, God abrogated it, then revealed: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. And it will come. Second: Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Al-Sha’bi, and Mujahid said: It is a special court, and it is in the meaning of the testimony that he forbade concealing. Then he informed in this verse that the one who conceals it and hides what is in his soul will be held accountable. Third: The verse is about what comes to mind of doubt and certainty, and Mujahid also said this. Fourth: It is a general court that has not been abrogated, and God will hold His creation accountable for what they have done and for what they have not done of what is established in their souls and what they concealed, intended and willed. He will forgive the believers and punish the disbelievers and hypocrites for it. At-Tabari mentioned this on the authority of some people, and he included something similar to this on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was narrated on the authority of ‘Ayy ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: It was not abrogated, but when God gathers the creation, He will say: I will inform you of what you concealed within yourselves. As for the believers, He will inform them and then forgive them, and as for the people of doubt and uncertainty, He will inform them of what they concealed of denial. This is His statement: God will bring you to account for it, then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills. This is His statement, the Exalted, the Majestic: But He will punish you for what your hearts have earned of doubt and hypocrisy. Ad-Dahhak said: God will inform him on the Day of Resurrection of what he had concealed so that he may know that it was not hidden from Him. And in the report: God Almighty says on the Day of Resurrection, “This is a day when secrets will be exposed and consciences will be revealed. My scribes have only written what is apparent of your deeds, and I am the One who knows what they have not known about, nor have they been informed of, nor have they written. So I will inform you of that and hold you accountable for it. So I will forgive whomever I will and punish whomever I will. So I will forgive the believers and punish the disbelievers.” This is the most correct statement on this subject, and the hadith of the secret conversation indicates it, as will be explained. It should not be said, as it has been proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God has forgiven my nation for what their souls have thought of, as long as they do not speak of it or act upon it. We say: This applies to worldly rulings, such as divorce, manumission, and sale, the rulings of which are not binding unless they speak of them. What is mentioned in the verse is what the servant will be held accountable for between him and God Almighty in the Hereafter. Al-Hasan said: The verse is decisive and has not been abrogated. Al-Tabari said: Others said something similar to the meaning mentioned by Ibn Abbas, except that they said: The punishment that is a recompense for what crosses the minds and accompanies the thought is only for the calamities, pains, and other hardships of this world. Then he attributed to Aisha something like this meaning, which is the fifth statement: Al-Tabari preferred that the verse is decisive and not abrogated. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is correct, and that is because the Almighty’s saying: And if you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it means what is within your capacity and under your earnings, and that is the continuation of belief and thought, and since the wording was something that could include thoughts, the Companions and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were afraid, so God explained to them what He intended by the other verse, and made it specific and stated His ruling that He does not charge a soul except with what it can bear, and thoughts are not within its capacity, rather they are a predominant matter and are not something that is acquired, so in this explanation there was their relief and the removal of their distress, and the rest of the verse is decisive and there is no abrogation in it: and what refutes the matter of abrogation is that the verse is report and report does not include abrogation, so if someone goes to estimate abrogation, then it is only based on the ruling that befell the Companions when they were frightened by the verse, and that is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Say, ‘We hear and we obey.’ This command comes from it to remain steadfast on this and adhere to it and await God’s kindness in forgiveness. If this ruling is established, then it is correct that it has been abrogated, and the verse then resembles the Almighty’s saying: If there are twenty among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred. This is the wording of the report, but its meaning is adhere to this and remain steadfast on it and be patient according to it. Then it was abrogated after that. And the people agreed, as far as I know, that this verse in jihad was abrogated by the patience of one hundred for two hundred. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: This verse in Al-Baqarah is most similar to it. It was said that there is an implication and restriction in the speech, meaning that God will hold you accountable for it if He wills. Based on this, there is no abrogation. Al-Nahhas said: Among the best things that have been said about the verse and what is most similar to the apparent meaning is the saying of Ibn ‘Abbas: It is general. Then he included the hadith of Ibn ‘Umar in the secret conversation, narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim and others, and the wording is from Muslim, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “On the Day of Resurrection, the believer will be brought near to his Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, until He places His cloak over him and He will make him confess his sins. He will say: ‘Do you know?’ He will say: ‘O Lord, I know.’ He will say: ‘I concealed them from you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.’ Then he will be given his record of good deeds. As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, they will be called out before all creation: ‘These are the ones who lied about God.’” It has been said that it was revealed regarding the religion of those who take the disbelievers as allies among the believers. That is, whether you declare what is in your hearts, O believers, regarding the allegiance to the disbelievers or keep it secret, God will hold you accountable for it. This was stated by Al-Waqidi and Muqatil. They used as evidence the words of God, the Most High, in Al Imran 3:“Say: ‘Whether you conceal what is in your hearts or reveal it’” - regarding the allegiance to the disbelievers - God knows it - which indicates what precedes it, in His words: Believers should not take disbelievers as allies rather than believers. I said: This is far-fetched, because the context of the verse does not require it, but rather it is clear in Al Imran, and God knows best. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: It has reached me that the prophets, peace be upon them, used to come to their people with this verse: “To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it.” God the Almighty said: Then He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read yaghfir and yu’thabdhu in the jussive mood, in apposition to the answer. Ibn ‘Amir and ‘Asim read both in the nominative case, meaning, He forgives and punishes. It was narrated from Ibn ‘Abbas, Al-A’raj, Abu Al-‘Aliyah, and ‘Asim Al-Jahdary in the accusative case, in apposition to the meaning, as in God the Almighty’s statement: Then He multiplies it for him. This has been mentioned before. Apposition to the word is better for consistency, as the poet said: Whenever you say something, he speaks to you wisely. An-Nahhas said: It was narrated on the authority of Talha bin Masraf that God will hold you accountable for it, without the letter fa’, as a substitute. Ibn Atiyyah: And this is how Al-Ja’fi and Khallad read it. It was narrated that it is like this in the Mushaf of Ibn Mas’ud. Ibn Jinni said: It is as a substitute for Man yuhasabukum. It is an interpretation of accountability, and this is like the poet’s saying: Slow down, Bani Shaiban, some of your Eid will meet tomorrow, my horse is on Safwan They met horses that would not deviate from the battlefield if they were in a difficult situation. This is an alternative. The poet repeated the verb because the benefit is in what follows. An-Nahhas said: It is better than the Jazm if it is without the Fa of the nominative case, and it is in the position of the state, as the poet said: When you come to him, you will have dinner by the light of his fire. You will find the best fire with him, the best stove.
2:285: God Almighty said: “The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], ‘We make no distinction between any of His messengers.’ And they say, ‘We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination.’”
2:286: God Almighty says: “God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have whatever it has earned, and it will bear whatever it has committed. Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.” It contains eleven issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak: that this verse was in the story of the Ascension, and this is how it was narrated in some narrations on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Some of them said: The entire Qur’an was revealed by Gabriel, peace be upon him, to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, except for this, for it was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who heard it on the night of the Ascension. Some of them said: that was not in the story of the Ascension, because the night of the Ascension was in Mecca and this entire Surah was Madani. As for the one who said that it was on the night of the Ascension, he said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended and reached a high place in the heavens with Gabriel until he passed Sidrat al-Muntaha, Gabriel said to him: I have not passed this place and no one has been commanded to pass this place except you. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed until he reached the place that God willed. Gabriel indicated to him to greet your Lord, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All compliments, prayers and good things are due to God. God Almighty said: Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of God and His blessings. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted his nation to have a share in peace, so he said: Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God. Gabriel and all the inhabitants of the heavens said: I bear witness that there is no god but God and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. God Almighty said: “The Messenger has believed” in the sense of gratitude, meaning that the Messenger believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted his nation to share in the honor and virtue, so he said: “And the believers - all of them believe in God and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between anyone of them.” His Messengers” meaning they say we believe in all the Messengers and we do not disbelieve in any of them and we do not differentiate between them as the Jews and Christians differentiated. So his Lord said to him: How do they accept the verses that You revealed? Which are His saying: And if you disclose what is in your souls so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “They say, We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the destination” meaning the return. Then God the Most High said at that time: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity meaning its ability and it is said: except less than its capacity. It shall have whatever it has earned of good and it shall bear whatever it has acquired of evil. Then Gabriel said at that time: Ask and you will be given it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget meaning if we are ignorant or make a mistake meaning if we deliberately, and it is said: if we know about forgetfulness and error. So Gabriel said to him: You have been given that, and your nation has been relieved of error and forgetfulness. So he asked something else, and he said: Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden meaning a burden like that which You placed upon those before us, which is that He forbade them from good things because of their injustice, and if they sinned at night they would find that written on their door, and the prayers for them were fifty, so God made it easier for this nation and removed from them after He had imposed fifty prayers. Then he said: Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. He said: Do not burden us with work that we cannot bear, lest You punish us. It is also said: Do not make it difficult for us, because if they were ordered to perform fifty prayers, they would be able to do that, but it is difficult for them and they cannot continue doing it. And pardon us from all of that. And forgive us and overlook us. It is also said: And pardon us from being transformed, And forgive us from being swallowed up, And have mercy on us from being slandered, because some of the past nations were stricken with transformation, some of them were stricken with swallowing up, and some of them were slandered. Then he said: You are our Master meaning our Guardian and Preserver. So give us victory over the disbelieving people. So his supplication was answered. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I was supported by terror for a month’s journey. It is said that when the invaders left their homes with pure intentions and beat drums, terror and awe would fall into the hearts of the infidels for a month’s journey, whether they knew of their departure or not. Then when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned, God revealed these verses to inform his nation of that. This verse has another interpretation. Al-Zajjaj said: When God the Most High mentioned in this Surah the obligation of prayer and zakaah, and explained the rulings of Hajj, the rulings on menstruation, divorce, and ila’, and the stories of the prophets, and explained the ruling on usury, He mentioned His glorification by saying: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Then He mentioned the belief of His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), then He mentioned the belief of the believers in all of that, so He said: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord. That is, the Messenger believed in all of these things that were mentioned, and likewise all the believers believed in God, His angels, His books, and His messengers. It was said that the reason for its revelation was the verse before it, which is: “To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And whether you disclose what is in yourselves or conceal it, God will bring you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills. And God is over all things competent.” For it is: When this was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it was difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then knelt down and said: O Messenger of God, we have been charged with the deeds that we are able to bear: prayer, fasting, jihad, and charity, and God has revealed this verse to you and we are not able to bear it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you want to say as the People of the Book before you said: We hear and we disobey? Rather, say: We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination. They said: We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination. When the people recited it, their tongues became easy to understand, so God revealed after it: “The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in God and His angels and His books and His messengers. We make no distinction between any of His messengers. And they said: We hear and we obey. Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the final destination.” When they did that, God abrogated it, and God the Almighty revealed: “God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. It will have [the consequence of] whatever it has earned, and it will bear [the consequence of] whatever it has committed.” Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we forget or make a mistake. He said: Yes. Our Lord, and lay not upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us. He said: Yes. Our Lord, and burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. He said: Yes. “And pardon us and forgive us and have mercy upon us. You are our Protector, so give us victory over the disbelieving people.” He said: Yes. Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Our scholars said: His saying in the first narration, I have done so, and here he said, Yes, is evidence of transmitting the hadith with the meaning, and it has been mentioned previously. And when the matter was established that they said, We hear and obey, God praised them and commended them in this verse, and removed the hardship in the matter of thoughts from them, and this is the fruit of obedience and devotion to God Almighty, as happened to the Children of Israel in contrast to that, when they were blamed and burdened with hardships of humiliation, poverty, and exile when they said, We hear and disobey, and this is the fruit of disobedience and rebellion against God Almighty. May God protect us from His vengeance by His grace and generosity. And in the hadith, it was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “The house of Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas is illuminated every night with lamps. He said: Perhaps he reads Surat Al-Baqarah. Thabit was asked and said: I read from Surat al-Baqarah 2:‘The Messenger has believed.’ It was revealed when the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were distressed by what God Almighty had promised them of being held accountable for what their souls had concealed. They complained about that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Perhaps you will say, ‘We hear and disobey,’ as the Children of Israel said. They said: ‘Rather, we hear and obey.’ Then God Almighty revealed, praising them: ‘The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord.’ So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And it is right for them to believe.’” The second: The Almighty’s saying: believed means believed, and it has been mentioned before. And that which was revealed is the Qur’an. Ibn Mas’ud read and the believers believed as every believer in God, according to the wording. It is permissible in other than the Qur’an to say believed as meaning. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir and Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr and Ibn Amir read and his books as plural. And they read in At-Tahrim his book as singular. Abu Amr read here and in At-Tahrim and his books as plural. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read and his book as singular in both of them. So whoever pluralized meant the plural of book, and whoever singular meant the source that includes every written word that was revealed from God. It is permissible in the reading of whoever singularized it to mean the plural, the book would be a name for the species, so the two readings are equal. God the Almighty said: So God sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners, and sent down with them the Book. The group read and His messengers with a damma on the seen, and likewise our messengers and your messengers and your messengers, except for Abu Amr, it was narrated from him that he lightened our messengers and your messengers, and it was narrated from him in your messengers with emphasis and emphasis. Abu Ali said: Whoever reads your messengers with emphasis, then that is the root of the word, and whoever lightens it, then it is as it is lightened in the singular, like anq and tanb. And if it is lightened in the singular, then that is more appropriate in the plural which is heavier, and he said that its meaning is Meccan. The majority of people read we do not separate with a nun, and the meaning is they say we do not separate, so the statement was deleted a lot, God Almighty said: “And the angels will enter upon them from every gate * Peace be upon you”: meaning they say “peace be upon you”. And He said: And they ponder the creation of the heavens and the earth, “Our Lord, You did not create this in vain: meaning they say Our Lord, and there is nothing like it. Saeed bin Jubair, Yahya bin Ya’mar, Abu Zur’ah bin Amr bin Jarir, and Ya’qub read we do not separate with a ya, and this is according to the wording of all. Harun said: It is in the letter of Ibn Masoud that they do not differentiate. He said between one in the singular and did not say individuals, because one includes one and all, as God Almighty said: There is not one of you who can prevent it. So barriers is an attribute of one, because its meaning is the plural. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Spoils of war are not permissible for any black-headed person except you. And Ru’bah said: If people's affairs are Dinka, they will not fear anyone other than Dinka. The meaning of this verse is that believers are not like Jews and Christians in that they believe in some and disbelieve in others. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And they said, ‘We hear and obey.’ There is an ellipsis in it, meaning we hear with a hearing that accepts. It was said: Hear means accept, as it is said: God hears whoever praises Him, so there is no ellipsis in it. In short, this saying necessitates praise for the one who says it. Obedience is accepting the command. His saying, Your forgiveness is a verbal noun like disbelief and loss, and the agent in it is an implied verb, the meaning of which is: forgive your forgiveness, as Al-Zajjaj said. And others: We ask or I ask for your forgiveness. And to You is the destination is an acknowledgment of the resurrection and standing before God Almighty. It was narrated: “When this verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Gabriel said to him: God has made it permissible to praise you and your nation, so ask and you will be given. So he asked until the end of the surah.” Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity. Assignment is the command to do what is difficult for it. To undertake a matter means to undertake it, as Al-Jawhari narrated. As-was’ means energy and capacity. This is a definitive report. God the Almighty stated that He has not charged the servants since the revelation of the verse with any act of worship of the heart or limbs except what is within the capacity of the person charged and in accordance with his perception and intention. Thus, the distress was removed from the Muslims in their interpretation of the matter of thoughts. In the meaning of this verse, what Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him narrated: I would not have liked anyone to have given birth to me except Ja’far ibn Abi Talib, for I followed him one day while I was hungry, and when he reached his home, he did not find in it anything but a sack of ghee in which traces of it remained, so he split it in our hands, and we began to lick what was in it of ghee and honey, and he said: God does not charge a soul beyond its capacity, and no hand gives except what it finds. Fifth: People differed about the permissibility of imposing an unbearable burden in worldly rulings, after agreeing that it is not present in the Shariah, and that this verse indicates its absence. Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari and a group of theologians said: Imposing an unbearable burden is permissible rationally, and does not violate any of the beliefs of the Shariah, and it is an indication of the torture of the one who is charged and a definite proof of it. This is seen in imposing a picture-maker to perform a ritual. Those who say it is permissible differed about whether it occurred in the message of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) or not. A group said: It occurred in the case of Abu Lahab, because he charged him with believing in the entire Shariah, including that he would not believe, because he ruled that his hands would be cut off and he would burn in the Fire, and that is an indication that he would not believe, so he charged him with believing that he would not believe. A group said: It never occurred. Consensus has been reported on this. The Almighty's statement: He will burn in the Fire means if he fulfills it, as reported by Ibn 'Atiyyah. The verb wakalaf is transitive and takes two objects, one of which is omitted, meaning worship or something. So God, the Most High, in His kindness and favor upon us, even though He has charged us with what is difficult and burdensome, such as the continuation of one person among ten, and the migration of a person and his departure from his homeland and separation from his family, homeland and customs, yet He has not charged us with burdensome hardships or painful matters, as He charged those before us with killing themselves and cutting off the place of urination from their clothes and skins. Rather, He made it easy and gentle and removed from us the burden and shackles that He placed on those who came before us. So to God belong praise and thanks, grace and blessings. Sixth: The Almighty’s statement: For it is what it has earned, and against it is what it has earned. He means of good deeds and bad deeds. This was stated by Al-Suddi. There is no disagreement among the group of commentators on this, as stated by Ibn Atiyyah. It is similar to His statement: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. “And no soul earns except against itself.” Thoughts and the like are not from the earnings of a person. The phrase in good deeds is for it because they are among the things that a person rejoices in earning and is pleased with, so they are added to his possession. It is stated in bad deeds against it because they are burdens, burdens, and difficult tasks. This is like saying: I have money, but I owe a debt. The verb earn is repeated, so the difference between the conjugation is good for the style of speech, as He said: So give the disbelievers respite, give them respite a little. Ibn Atiyah said: It appears to me in this that good deeds are among those that are acquired without effort, since the one who acquires them is on the right path of God Almighty’s command and the outline of His law, and bad deeds are acquired by means of the construction of exaggeration, since the one who acquires them is forced to pierce the veil of God Almighty’s prohibition in their matter and to go beyond it to them, so it is good in the verse to come with the two forms of derivation to protect against this meaning. Seventh: In this verse is evidence of the validity of the application of Our trust to the actions of the servants, whether they are acquisition or earning. Therefore, they did not apply to that either creation or creator, contrary to those who applied that from the bold innovators. And those who applied that from Our trust to the servant, and that he is the doer, did so purely metaphorically. Al-Mahdawi and others said: It was said that the meaning of the verse is: No one will be held accountable for the sin of another. Ibn Atiyah said: This is correct in itself, but not in this verse. Eighth: Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: The Almighty’s statement: For her is what she has earned, and against her is what she has committed is used as evidence that whoever kills another with a heavy object, strangulation, or drowning must pay for it in retaliation or by hand, contrary to those who make his blood money the responsibility of the agnates. This contradicts the apparent meaning, and indicates that the waiver of retaliation from the father does not necessitate its waiver from his partner. It indicates that the punishment is obligatory on the agnates if they allow a madman to have intercourse with her. Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: Our scholars mentioned this verse that retaliation is obligatory on the father’s partner, contrary to Abu Hanifa, and on the partner of the sinner, contrary to al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa, because each of them has committed the murder. They said: The participation of one who is not obligated to retaliation with one who is obligated to retaliation is not a doubt in warding off a warding off by doubt. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget or make a mistake. The meaning is: Pardon the sin that occurs from us in these two ways or one of them, like his saying, peace be upon him: My nation has been absolved of mistakes, forgetfulness, and what they are forced to do. That is, the sin of that. There is no disagreement about this, that the sin is absolved. Rather, there is disagreement about the rulings related to that. Is that absolved and nothing is required from it, or are the rulings of all of that required? There is disagreement about that. The correct view is that it differs according to the incidents. A category is not absolved by consensus, such as fines, blood money, and obligatory prayers. A category is absolved by consensus, such as retaliation and uttering a word of disbelief. There is a third category, such as someone who ate forgetfully in Ramadan or broke his oath absentmindedly, and what is similar to that which occurs by mistake or forgetfulness. This is known in the branches. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: Our Lord, and do not place upon us a burden, meaning a heavy load. Malik and Al-Rabi’ said: A burden is a difficult and harsh matter. Sa’id bin Jubayr said: A burden is the severity of work, and what was difficult for the Children of Israel, such as urination and the like. Ad-Dahhak said: They were burdened with difficult matters. This is similar to the saying of Malik and Al-Rabi’, and from it is the saying of An-Nabigha: O He who prevents injustice from befalling their leaders and who bears their burdens after they have known Him. Ata’: Al-Isr is the transformation into monkeys and pigs. Ibn Zayd also said this. It was also narrated from him that it is the sin for which there is no repentance or expiation. In the language, Iṣr means a covenant, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: And you took upon you My covenant. Iṣr means distress, sin, and burden. Iṣr is the rope with which loads and the like are tied. It is said: Asr, ya’ṣir, Iṣr, he imprisoned him. Iṣr with a kasra on the hamzah is from this. Al-Jawhari said: The place is Ma’ṣir and Ma’ṣir, and the plural is Ma’āsir, and the common people say Ma’āsir. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: It is possible to use this apparent meaning as evidence for every act of worship that the opponent claims is burdensome, and it is similar to the saying of God Almighty: And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty, and the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Religion is easy, so make it easy and do not make it difficult. O God, make it difficult for those who make it difficult for the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: Al-Kaya al-Tabari said something similar. He said: It is used as evidence to deny hardship and distress, which apparently contradicts the tolerant Hanafi school of thought, and this is clear. Eleventh: The Almighty’s saying: And burden us not with that which we have no ability to bear. Qatada said: Its meaning is do not be harsh on us as You burdened those who came before us. Ad-Dahhak: Do not burden us with actions that we cannot bear. Ibn Zayd said something similar. Ibn Jurayj: Do not transform us into monkeys or pigs. Salam ibn Sabur said: That which we cannot bear: the youth. Al-Naqqash narrated it on the authority of Mujahid and Ata.
