It was narrated that Abu Darda’ used to say in his supplication: And I seek refuge in You from a youth who has no ability. As-Suddi said: It is the severity and shackles that were on the Children of Israel. God the Almighty said: And pardon us meaning our sins. You pardoned his sin if you left him and did not punish him. And forgive us meaning cover our sins. Forgiveness means covering. And have mercy on us meaning favor us with mercy, beginning with you. You are our Master meaning our Guardian and Supporter. This was mentioned as a way of teaching people how to supplicate. It was narrated on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal that when he finished reciting this surah, he would say Amen. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is thought to be narrated on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. If that is the case, then it is perfect. If it is by analogy to Surat Al-Hamd, where there is a supplication and here is a supplication, then it is good. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: I do not think that anyone who has a mind and has attained Islam sleeps until he recites them. I said: Muslim narrated in this meaning on the authority of Abu Masoud Al-Ansari, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites these two verses from the end of Surat Al-Baqarah at night, they will suffice him. It was said: from the night prayer, as narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God revealed to me two verses from the treasures of Paradise with which he concluded Surat Al-Baqarah. The Most Gracious wrote them with His hand a thousand years before He created the creation. Whoever recites them twice after the evening prayer, they will suffice him for the night prayer. The Messenger has believed to the end of Surat Al-Baqarah. It was said: They will suffice him from the evil of Satan, so he will have no power over him. Abu Amr Al-Dani narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Al-Yaman, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Almighty, the Majestic, wrote a book two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth, and He revealed from it these three verses with which He concluded Surat Al-Baqarah. Whoever recites them in his house, Satan will not come near his house for three nights.” It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was given these verses from the end of Surat Al-Baqarah from a treasure beneath the Throne. No prophet before me was given them.” This is correct. The angel descended with them along with Al-Fatihah was mentioned in Al-Fatihah. Praise be to God.
3:1: The Almighty said: “Alif, Lam, Meem. God - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence.” There are five issues: The first: His saying: "Alif, Lam, Mim. God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining." This surah is Madani by consensus. Al-Naqqash narrated that its name in the Torah is Tayyiba. Al-Hasan, Amr ibn Ubayd, Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, and Abu Ja`far al-Rawasi read "Alif, Lam, Mim. God" with the alif of connection cut off, assuming the pause on Alif, Lam, Mim as they assume the pause on the names of numbers such as one, two, three, four, and they are connected. Al-Akhfash Sa`id said: "Alif, Lam, Mim. God" is permissible with the kasra of the meem due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a mistake, and the Arabs do not say it because of its heaviness. Al-Nahhas said: The first reading is the reading of the common people, and the ancient grammarians spoke about it. The doctrine of Sibawayh is that the meem is opened due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, and they chose the opening for it so as not to combine a kasra with a ya and a kasra before it. Al-Kisa’i said: “If you find the letters of spelling with an alif of connection and you delete the alif of connection, you move it with the movement of the alif, so you say: “alif-lam-mam God” and alif-lam-mam “remember,” and alif-lam-mam “approach.” Al-Farra’ said: The original is alif-lam-mam God as al-Ru’asi read, so you find the movement of the hamza on the meem. Umar ibn al-Khattab read al-Hayy al-Qayyim, and Kharijah said: In the copy of Abdullah al-Hayy al-Qayyim. The opinions of the scholars regarding the letters at the beginning of the surahs have been presented at the beginning of al-Baqarah, and from where it came in this surah God, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Sustaining, a sentence that stands on its own, so you can imagine all of those opinions.” Second: Al-Kisa’i narrated that Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, prayed the ‘Isha’ prayer and began with Surat Al-Imran. He recited, God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. So he recited one hundred verses in the first rak’ah and the remaining one hundred in the second. Our scholars said: He should not recite a surah in two rak’ahs. If he does, it will suffice him. Malik said in Al-Majmu’ah: There is nothing wrong with it, and it is not a concern. I said: The correct view is that this is permissible. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Al-A’raf in the Maghrib prayer, dividing it into two rak’ahs. It was also included by Al-Nasa’i and authenticated by Abu Muhammad Abd Al-Haqq, and will come. Third: There are reports and narrations about the virtue of this Surah. Some of them say that it is a protection from snakes, a treasure for the vagabond, that it will plead for its reciter in the Hereafter, and that whoever recites the last part of it in one night will be recorded as having prayed a night in prayer, and so on. Al-Darimi Abu Muhammad mentioned in his Musnad: Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said: Ubaid God Al-Ashja’i told me, he said: Misa’ar told me, he said: Jabir told me before he fell into what he fell into, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: Abdullah said: Surah Al-Imran is a good treasure for the vagabond, he recites it at the end of the night. Muhammad bin Saeed told us, Abdul Salam told us, on the authority of Al-Jariri, on the authority of Abu Al-Saleel, he said: A man was afflicted with blood, he said: So he took refuge in Wadi Majannah: a valley in which no one walks without being struck by a snake, and on the edge of the valley were two monks, and when evening came, one of them said to his companion: By God, the man is dead! He said: So he began to recite Surah Al-Imran. They said: So he recited Surah Tayyiba, perhaps he would be saved. He said: So he woke up safe and sound. And it was narrated on the authority of Makhul who said: Whoever recites Surat Al Imran on Friday, the angels will pray for him until the night. And it was narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Affan who said: Whoever recites the last verses of Surat Al Imran at night, he will be credited with having spent the whole night in prayer. In his chain of transmission is Ibn Lahi’ah and Muslim narrated on the authority of Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an Al-Kalabi who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The Qur’an will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, along with its people who used to act upon it. Surat Al-Baqarah and Al Imran will precede it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave three examples for them that I have not forgotten since. He said: ‘As if they were two black clouds or two shades between which there is a light, or as if they were two flocks of white birds pleading on behalf of their companion.’” It was also narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Recite the Qur’an, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companions. Recite the two lights, Al-Baqarah and Al-Imran, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection like two clouds, or like two canopies, or like two flocks of birds in flight, pleading on behalf of their companions. Recite Al-Baqarah, for taking it is a blessing and abandoning it is a cause of regret, and the sorcerers cannot do it.” Muawiyah said: It has reached me that the sorcerers are the sorcerers. Fourth: Scholars have three opinions regarding naming Al-Baqarah and Al-Imran as the two lights: The first: that they are the two luminaries, taken from the flower and the flower, so either to guide their reader with what blossoms for him from their lights, that is, from their meanings. Or because of the complete light that results from reading them on the Day of Resurrection, which is the second opinion. Third: They were called thus because they associate with what is included in the greatest name of God, as Abu Dawud and others mentioned on the authority of Asma bint Yazid that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The greatest name of God is in these two verses: ‘And your God is one God; there is no god but He, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.’ And the one in Al Imran 3:‘God; there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.’” Ibn Majah also narrated it. And the clouds: the swirling clouds, and it is the shadow if it is close to the head, and it is also the shade, and the meaning: that their readers are in the shade of their reward, as it came: the man is in the shade of his charity. And his saying they argue means that God creates those who argue on his behalf with their reward, angels as it came in some of the hadith. Whoever recites ‘God bears witness that there is no god but He’, God will create seventy angels who will ask forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection. His statement, between them is an east, is qualified by the sukoon or fatha of the ra’, which is an indication of the light, because when he said, two black ones, it might be thought that they were dark, so he negated that by saying, between them is an east. What he meant by their being black is that they are so dense that they prevent those beneath them from the heat of the sun and the intensity of the flames. And God knows best. Fifth: The beginning of this Surah was revealed because of the Najran delegation, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn al-Zubayr: They were Christians who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina with sixty riders, among them were fourteen of their nobles. Of the fourteen, there were three men to whom their affairs were referred: Al-Aqib, the leader of the people and the one with their opinions, whose name was Abdul-Masih; Sayyid Thamal, their master and leader of their community, whose name was Al-Ayham; and Abu Haritha ibn Alqamah, the brother of Banu Bakr ibn Wa’il, their bishop and scholar. They entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after the afternoon prayer, wearing the garments of the nobles, cloaks and robes. The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We have never seen a delegation like them in beauty and majesty. The time for their prayer came, so they stood up and prayed in the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, facing east. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave them. Then they stayed there for days, debating with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Jesus and claiming that he was the son of God, and other heinous and confused statements, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, responded to them with clear proofs while they did not see. The beginning of this surah was revealed about them, up to more than eighty verses, until their matter came to an end when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to the Mubahala, according to what is mentioned in the biography of Ibn Ishaq and others.
3:2: God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.
3:3: The Almighty said: The Book has been sent down to you meaning the Qur'an in truth meaning with honesty, and it was said: with the overwhelming argument. And the Qur'an was sent down in stages: one thing after another, that is why He said sent down and revealed is time after time. And the Torah and the Gospel were sent down all at once, that is why He said sent down. And the ba in His statement in truth is in the position of a state of the Book, and the ba is related to something omitted, the meaning is bringing the truth. And it is not related to sent down, because it has taken two objects, one of them with a preposition, and it does not take a third. And confirming is a confirmed state that is not transferred, because it cannot be non-confirming, that is, non-conforming, this is the opinion of the majority. And some of them estimated the transfer in it, meaning that he is confirming himself and confirming others. God the Almighty said: For what was before it meaning of the revealed books. The Torah means light and radiance, derived from wara al-zand and wara are two languages if its fire comes out. Its origin is tawariyah on the weight of tafa’ala, the ta’ is redundant, and the ya’ was moved and before it was a fatha, so it was changed to an alif. It is possible that it is tafa’ala, so the ra’ was moved from kasra to fatha, as they said in jariyah: jarah, and in nasiyyah: nasiyyah, both from al-Farra’. Al-Khalil said: Its origin is faw’ala, so the origin is wariyah, the first waw was changed to a ta’ as it was changed in tawalaj, and the origin is wulaj faw’ala from walajat, and the ya’ was changed to an alif due to its movement and the openness of what preceded it. The structure of faw’ala is more than tafa’ala, and it was said: the Torah is taken from tawariyah, which is hinting at something and concealing something else, so most of the Torah is hints and allusions without explicitness or clarification, this is the saying of al-Mu’arraj. The majority are of the first opinion, based on the Almighty’s saying: And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light and a reminder for the righteous. Meaning the Torah. The Gospel is an active participle from najl, which is the root, and it is pluralized as anajil, and Taurat as tuwar. The Gospel is the root of knowledge and wisdom, and it is said: May God curse his Najali, meaning his parents, since they were its root. It is also said: It is from najalat which means to extract something, so knowledge and wisdom are extracted from the Gospel, and from it the child and offspring are called najl because of its emergence, as he said: To a group whose grandfather did not pass on meanness to their young ones, and every stallion is their son. And the gospel is the water that comes out of the gush. And the earth became clean, and it has najal if water comes out of it, so the gospel was named after it, because God Almighty brought out through it what was destroyed from the truth, healthy. And it was said: It is from najl in the eye with the movement, which is its width, and its stabbing is najla, meaning wide. He said: Maybe a blow with a polished sword between Basra and a stab from Najla The Gospel was named thus because it is an original text that He brought out for them and made it spacious for them, and a light and radiance. It was said that tanajal means dispute, and it was named the Gospel because people disputed over it. Shammar narrated on the authority of some of them: The Gospel is every written book with many lines. It was said that it is the son of work and making. He said: And I am grateful for that act as I am grateful for it That is, I work and make. It was said: The Torah and the Gospel are from the Syriac language. It was also said: The Gospel in Syriac is Inkilyun, as narrated by Al-Tha’labi. Al-Jawhari said: The Gospel is the book of Jesus, peace be upon him. It is mentioned in both the masculine and feminine forms. When used in the feminine form, it means the scroll, and when used in the masculine form, it means the book. Another said: The Qur’an is also called the Gospel, as narrated in the story of the supplication of Moses, peace be upon him, that he said: O Lord, I see on the tablets people whose Gospels are in their hearts, so make them my nation. So God Almighty said to him: That is the nation of Muhammad, peace be upon him. What he meant by the Gospels is the Qur’an. Al-Hasan read: And the Gospel with the opening of the hamza, and the rest read it with the breaking like the crown, two languages. It is possible, if heard, that it is one of the foreign names that the Arabs Arabized, and there is no example for it in their speech.
3:4: The Almighty said: Before meaning the Qur’an a guidance for the people. Ibn Furak said: The meaning is a guidance for the righteous people. Its evidence is in Surat Al-Baqarah a guidance for the righteous. So he returned this general to that specific one, and guidance is in the accusative case as a state. And the Criterion is the Qur’an. This has been mentioned before.
3:5: The Almighty says: Indeed, nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven. This is report about His knowledge of things in detail, and there are many examples of this in the Qur’an. He is the All-Knowing of what was, what will be, and what will not be. So how can Jesus be a god or the son of a god when all things are hidden from Him?!
3:6: God Almighty says: “It is He who shapes you in the wombs however He wills. There is no god but He, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: It is He who forms you. The Almighty informed us about His forming of human beings in the wombs of mothers. The root of the womb is mercy, because it is something that shows mercy. The derivation of the word image is from to incline meaning to make it inclined, so the image is inclined to a likeness and form. This verse is a glorification of God the Almighty, and within it is a response to the Christians of Najran, and that Jesus is one of the image-makers, and that is something that no sane person would deny. The Almighty referred to the explanation of the image in Surat Al-Hajj and Surat Al-Mu’minoon. Likewise, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) explained it in the hadith of Ibn Mas’ud, as will be explained there, God willing. It also contains a response to the naturalists, as they make it an active and controlling factor. The response to them has already been mentioned in the verse of monotheism and in the Musnad of Ibn Sinjar, whose name is Muhammad ibn Sinjar, the hadith: God the Almighty creates the bones and cartilage of the fetus from the semen of the man and its fat and flesh from the semen of the woman. This is the clearest evidence that a child is created from the semen of a man and a woman, and it is explicit in the words of God Almighty: O mankind, indeed We have created you from a male and a female. And in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Thawban, in which it says: The Jew said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have come to ask you about something that no one on earth knows except a prophet, a man, or two men. He said: Will it benefit you if I tell you? He said: I will listen with my ears. He said: I have come to ask you about a child. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The man’s fluid is white and the woman’s fluid is yellow. So if they come together and the man’s fluid rises above the woman’s fluid, they will produce a boy, God willing. And if the woman’s fluid rises above the man’s fluid, they will produce a girl, God willing. And its explanation will come at the end of the consultation, God willing. Second: The Almighty’s saying: How He wills meaning from good and bad, black and white, tall and short, sound and defective, and other misery and happiness. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibrahim bin Adham that the reciters gathered to him to hear what he had to say of hadiths, so he said to them: I am busy with four things and I do not have time to narrate hadiths. So it was said to him: What is that preoccupation? He said: One of them is that I am thinking about the Day of the Covenant when He said: These are in Paradise and I don’t care, and these are in Hell and I don’t care, so I don’t know which of the two groups I was in at that time. The second group was when I was pictured in the womb, so the angel said, He is in charge of the wombs. Oh God, am I miserable or happy? I don’t know what the answer was at that time. And the third is when the Angel of Death takes my soul and says: O Lord, with disbelief or with faith, I do not know how the answer comes out. The fourth is where He says: And separate yourselves today, O criminals, so I do not know which of the two groups I will be in. Then the Most High said: There is no god but He, meaning there is no creator or fashioner other than Him, and this is evidence of His oneness, so how can Jesus be a fashioned god when He is a fashioner? The Almighty who cannot be defeated, the Wise with wisdom, or the Perfect, and this is more specific to what was mentioned about fashioning.
3:7: It contains nine issues: First: Muslim narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are entirely clear - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are unspecific. As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they will follow that of it that is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation of it. And none knows its interpretation except God and those firmly rooted in knowledge say, ‘We believe in it. All is from our Lord.’ And none will remember except those of understanding.” She said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you see those who follow that which is ambiguous in it, then they are the ones whom God has named, so beware of them. And on the authority of Abu Ghalib, he said: I was walking with my father Abu Umamah while he was on his donkey until he reached the stairs of the Damascus Mosque and saw some heads hanging from the sky. He said: What are these heads? It was said: These are the heads of Khawarij who are being brought from Iraq. Abu Umamah said: The dogs of Hell, the dogs of Hell, the dogs of Hell! The worst of those killed under the sky. Blessed is he who killed them and they were killed. He said it three times and then wept. I said: What makes you weep, Abu Umamah? He said: Out of mercy for them, for they were among the people of Islam and then left it. Then he recited: It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses that are precise until the end of the verses. Then he recited: And be not like those who became divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them. I said: O Abu Umamah, are they these? He said: Yes. I said: Is it something you say in your own opinion or something you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Then I am bold. Then I am bold. Rather, I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, more than once, twice, three times, four times, five times, six times, or seven times. And he put his fingers in his ears. He said: Otherwise, be silent. He said it three times, then he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The Children of Israel split into seventy-one sects, one of which will be in Paradise and the rest of them in Hell. And this nation will increase over them by one, one in Paradise and the rest of them in Hell.” Second: Scholars differed on the clear and ambiguous verses in many opinions. Jabir ibn Abdullah said, and this is what Al-Sha’bi, Sufyan Al-Thawri and others implied: The clear verses of the Qur’an are those whose interpretation is known and whose meaning and explanation are understood. The ambiguous verses are those that no one has a way to know, and which God has kept to Himself, without His creation. Some of them said: This is like the time of the Hour, the emergence of Gog and Magog, the Antichrist, and Jesus, and similar to the disconnected letters at the beginning of the surahs. I said: This is the best that has been said about the ambiguous. We have already mentioned in the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham that God the Most High revealed this Qur’an and kept to Himself the knowledge of whatever He willed from it, the hadith. Abu Uthman said: Al-Muhkam is the opening of the Book without which prayer is not valid. Muhammad bin Al-Fadl said: Surat Al-Ikhlas, because there is nothing in it except monotheism. It has been said: The entire Qur’an is decisive, because God the Most High said: A Book whose verses are perfected. And it has been said: It is all ambiguous, because He said: A Book whose verses are all ambiguous. I said: This has nothing to do with the meaning of the verse, for the Almighty’s statement: A Book whose verses are perfect means in terms of arrangement and arrangement, and that it is the truth from God. The meaning of a Book that is ambiguous is that some of it resembles others and some of it confirms others. What is meant by His statement, Verses that are perfect and others that are ambiguous is not this meaning, but rather the ambiguous in this verse is from the category of possibility and confusion, from His statement, The cows are all alike to us. That is, they are confusing to us, meaning that they could mean many types of cows. What is meant by perfect is what is in contrast to this, that is, what is not ambiguous and can only have one meaning. It was said: Ambiguous is what can have many meanings, then if the meanings are returned to one meaning and the rest are invalidated, then the ambiguous becomes perfect. So the perfect is always the origin to which the branches are returned, and the ambiguous is the branch. Ibn Abbas said: The decisive verses are His statement in Surat Al-An'am: Say, 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you' up to three verses, and His statement regarding the Children of Israel: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment. Ibn Atiyyah said: I have this as an example that he gave regarding the decisive verses. Ibn Abbas also said: The decisive verses are abrogating, and His prohibitions and obligations, and what is believed in and acted upon, and the ambiguous verses are abrogated, and its beginning and end, and its likes and its categories, and what is believed in but not acted upon. Ibn Mas'ud and others said: The decisive verses are abrogating, and the ambiguous verses are abrogated. Qatada, Al-Rabi' and Ad-Dahhak said the same. Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Az-Zubayr said: The decisive verses are those in which there is the proof of the Lord and the protection of the servants and the repelling of opponents and falsehood. They have no transformation or distortion from what they were placed upon. The ambiguous verses have transformation, distortion and interpretation, and God tested the servants with them. This was said by Mujahid and Ibn Ishaq. Ibn Atiyah said: This is the best of the sayings about this verse. An-Nahhas said: The best that has been said about the decisive and ambiguous verses is that the decisive verses are those that exist on their own and do not need to be referred to anything else, such as And there is none comparable to Him and Indeed, I am the Forgiver of whoever repents. As for the ambiguous verses, such as Indeed, God forgives all sins, they refer to the words of God the Almighty: And indeed, I am the Forgiver of whoever repents and to the words of God the Almighty: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him. I said: What An-Nahhas said clarifies what Ibn Atiyah chose, which is the current usage of the tongue, and that is that the decisive verse is a passive participle from ahkam, and al-ihkam and al-muhkam. There is no doubt that what is ambiguous in meaning is not ambiguous or hesitant, it is only like that due to the clarity of its individual words and the perfection of their structure, and whenever one of the two matters is missing, then ambiguousness and confusion result. And God knows best. Ibn Juwaiz Mandad said: There are aspects to the ambiguous verses, and what the scholars differed about is that which verses abrogated the other, such as the statement of Ali and Ibn Abbas about a pregnant woman whose husband died, she must observe the waiting period of the longest of the two periods. Omar, Zaid bin Thabit, Ibn Masoud and others used to say that the pregnancy was terminated, and they used to say that Surat An-Nisa’ abrogated four months and ten days. Ali and Ibn Abbas used to say that it was not abrogated. And like their disagreement about the will for the heir, was it abrogated or not? And like the conflict between two verses, which of them should be given precedence if abrogation is not known and its conditions are not met, like the statement of God the Almighty: And lawful for you are all beyond that which requires bringing together relatives from the right hand, and His statement the Almighty: And that you marry two sisters together, except for what has already occurred prevents that. And from this also is the conflict of reports from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the conflict of analogies, and that is the ambiguous. It is not ambiguous to read the verse in two readings and have the name or all of it. And the two readings are like the two verses, and it is necessary to act according to them both, as was read: And wipe over your heads and your feet. With the fat-ha and the kasra, as will be explained in Al-Ma’idah, God willing. Third: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: A man said to Ibn Abbas: I find in the Qur’an things that I disagree with. He said: What is it? He said: There will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask about one another. He said: And they will turn to one another, asking about one another. He said: And they will not conceal from God a word. He said: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists. They concealed this verse. And in al-Nazi’at 79:Or did He build the heaven? to His saying: He spread it out. So He mentioned the creation of the heaven before the creation of the earth, then He said: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days? to: obedient. So He mentioned in this the creation of the earth before the creation of the heaven. He said: And God is Forgiving and Merciful. “And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” And God is Hearing and Seeing. It was as if it was and then it passed away. Ibn Abbas said: There will be no kinship between them in the first blast, then the trumpet will be blown and all who are in the heavens and on the earth will fall unconscious except whom God wills, so there will be no kinship between them at that time and they will not ask each other, then at the last blast They will turn to each other, asking each other. As for His statement, We were not polytheists, “nor will they conceal from God a word,” God will forgive the sins of the sincere ones, and the polytheists will say, “Come, let us say: We were not polytheists,” so God will seal their mouths and their limbs will speak of their deeds. At that time it will be known that God does not conceal a word, and with Him those who disbelieved will wish that they were Muslims. And God created the earth in two days, then He turned to the heaven and made them seven heavens in two days, then He spread out the earth, that is, He extended it and brought forth from it water and pasture, and He created in it the mountains, trees, hills and what is between them in two other days, so that is His statement, And the earth after that He spread out, so He created the earth and what is in it in four days, and He created the heaven in two days. His saying, And God is Forgiving and Merciful, means Himself, that is, He has always been and will always be like that, for God has never willed anything without bringing about what He willed. Woe to you, so do not let the Qur’an differ with you, for both are from God. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And others similar. “Akhr” was not declined because it was changed from the alif and lam, because its origin is to be an adjective with the alif and lam like big and small, but when it was changed from the course of the alif and lam, it prevented it from being declined. Abu Ubaid: They did not decline it because its singular is not declined in definite or indefinite nouns. Al-Mubarrad denied that and said: According to this, ghadab and attash should not be declined. Al-Kisa’i: It was not declined because it is an adjective. And he said: Labad and Hatama are two adjectives and they are declined. Sibawayh: It is not permissible for Akhr to be changed from the alif and lam, because if it were changed from the alif and lam, it would have been definite. Don’t you see that sihr is definite in all sayings because it would not have been changed from sihr, and ams in the saying of the one who said dahab ams is changed from ams, so if akhr was also changed from the alif and lam, it would have been definite, and God the Almighty described it as indefinite. Fifth: The statement of God the Almighty: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation al-Baqarah 2:177, which is raised by the subject and the predicate, they follow that which is ambiguous in it. Deviation is inclination, and from it the sun deviated, and the eyes deviated. It is said: he deviated, yazigh, zighan if he abandoned the straight path, and from it the statement of God the Almighty: So when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate. This verse includes every group of disbelievers, heretics, ignorant people, and innovators, even though it was referred to at that time by the Christians of Najran. Qatada said in his interpretation of the statement of God the Almighty: But as for those in whose hearts is deviation: If they are not the Kharijites and the various types of Khawarij, then I do not know who they are. I said: This interpretation has been mentioned by Abu Umamah with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, and that is enough for you. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And they follow that of it which is ambiguous, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation. Our Sheikh Abu al-Abbas, may God have mercy on him, said: Those who follow the ambiguous do not fail to follow it and collect it seeking to cast doubt on the Qur’an and mislead the common people, as the heretics and Qarmatians who challenged the Qur’an did, or seeking to believe in the apparent meanings of the ambiguous, as the anthropomorphists did who collected what is in the Book and Sunnah that appears to be corporeal until they believed that the Creator, exalted be He above that, or they follow it in the manner of manifestation, eye, hand, foot, and morning, God, exalted be He above that, or they follow it in the manner of presenting its interpretations and clarifying its meanings, or as Subaih did when he asked Umar many questions about it. So these are four categories: First: There is no doubt about their disbelief, and that God’s ruling regarding them is to kill them without being given the opportunity to repent. Second: The correct view is that they are infidels, as there is no difference between them and worshippers of idols and images. They should be asked to repent, and if they repent, then fine. Otherwise, they should be killed, as is done with those who apostatize. Third: They differed on the permissibility of that based on the difference in the permissibility of interpreting it. It is known that the doctrine of the predecessors was to refrain from discussing it, even though they were certain of the impossibility of its apparent meanings, so they would say, Leave it as it came. Some of them went so far as to express its interpretations and interpret it in a way that is correct to interpret it in the tongue without being certain of the specificity of any ambiguous part of it. Fourth: The ruling on it is eloquent etiquette, as Omar did with Subaygh. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: The imams of the Salaf used to punish whoever asked about the interpretation of the problematic letters in the Qur’an, because if the questioner intended by his question to perpetuate innovation and stir up sedition, then he deserves to be denounced and severely punished. But if that was not his intention, then he deserved to be rebuked for the sin he committed, as he created a way for the hypocritical heretics at that time to aim at weakening the Muslims by casting doubt and misleading them into distorting the Qur’an from the methods of revelation and the truths of interpretation. Among that is what Ismail bin Ishaq al-Qadi told us, Sulayman bin Harf told us, on the authority of Hammad bin Zayd, on the authority of Yazid bin Hazim, on the authority of Sulayman bin Yasar, that Subaygh bin Asal came to Madinah and began to ask about the ambiguous and similar verses of the Qur’an. report of that reached Omar, may God be pleased with him, so he sent for him and brought him, and he had prepared for him clusters of palm clusters. When he arrived, Omar said to him: Who are you? He said: I am Abdullah Subaygh. Omar may God be pleased with him said: I am the servant of Omar. Then he went to him and struck his head with a palm branch, wounding him. Then he continued to strike him until his blood flowed down his face. He said: That is enough, O Commander of the Faithful. By God, what I felt in my head has gone away. There are different accounts of his good manners, and they will be mentioned in Adh-Dhariyat. Then God inspired him to repent and cast it into his heart, so he repented and his repentance was good. The meaning of seeking discord is seeking doubts and confusion for the believers so that they may corrupt their relationship and return people to their deviation. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the people seeking is that they sought an interpretation of their resurrection and revival, so God, the Almighty, informed that the interpretation and time of that is known only to God. He said: The evidence for that is the saying of God, the Almighty: Do they await anything but its interpretation? The Day its interpretation comes? That is, the Day they see what they were promised of resurrection, revival, and punishment. Those who had forgotten it before will say, Indeed, the messengers of our Lord have come with the truth. That is, we have seen the interpretation of what the messengers informed us of. He said: Stopping at the words of God Almighty, And none knows its interpretation except God, means that no one knows when the resurrection will be except God. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And none knows its interpretation except God. It is said: A group of Jews, including Huyayy ibn Akhtab, entered upon the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and said: We have heard that Surat Alif, Lam, Meem, and Alif have been revealed to you. If you are truthful in what you say, then the kingdom of your nation will be seventy-one years, because the Alif in the Abjad numeral system is one, the Lam is thirty, and the Mim is forty. So it was revealed, and none knows its interpretation except God. Interpretation can mean explanation, like when you say: The interpretation of this word is such-and-such. It can also mean what a matter is interpreted by God. Its derivation is from the word ala al-amr ila kada yu’ulihi, meaning it became. And I interpreted it with an interpretation, meaning I made it into something. Some jurists have defined it, saying: It is the expression of a possibility in the word intended by evidence outside of it. Interpretation is the clarification of the word, like saying: There is no doubt about it. That is, there is no suspicion. Its origin is from interpretation, which means clarification. It is said: I interpreted something, lightened, I interpreted it with a kasra, I interpreted it. Interpretation is the clarification of the meaning, like saying: There is no doubt about it among the believers. Or because it is true in itself, so it does not accept doubt, and doubt is only a description of the doubter. And as Ibn Abbas said about the grandfather, he is a father, because he interpreted the words of God Almighty, O children of Adam. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And those firmly rooted in knowledge. The scholars differed as to whether and those firmly rooted in knowledge is the beginning of a statement that is cut off from what precedes it, or is it conjoined to what precedes it, so the waw is for the plural. The majority are of the opinion that it is cut off from what precedes it, and that the statement ends at His saying except God. This is the opinion of Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Aisha, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, and others. It is the opinion of al-Kisa’i, al-Akhfash, al-Farra’, Abu Ubaid, and others. Abu Nahik al-Asadi said: You connect this verse, although it is cut off. The knowledge of the firmly rooted did not end except at their saying, “We believe in it. All of it is from our Lord.” Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz said something similar, and al-Tabari narrated something similar from Yunus from Ashhab from Malik ibn Anas, and they say that this is the report of the firmly rooted. Al-Khattabi said: God the Almighty has divided the verses of His Book, which He has commanded us to believe in and to affirm what is in it, into two types: clear and ambiguous. He the Almighty said: “It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. In it are verses that are clear - they are the foundation of the Book - and others that are ambiguous.” Until His saying: All are from our Lord. So know that God has kept the knowledge of the ambiguous parts of the Book to Himself, and no one knows its interpretation except Him. Then God the Almighty praised those firmly rooted in knowledge for saying, We believe in it. Had it not been for the soundness of their faith, they would not have deserved to be praised. The view of most scholars is that the complete stop at this verse is at the words of God the Almighty: And none knows its interpretation except God. And that what comes after it is a resumption of another statement, which is the words of God the Almighty: And those firmly rooted in knowledge say, “We believe in it. This was narrated from Ibn Mas`ud, Ubayy ibn Ka`b, Ibn Abbas, and Aisha. Rather, it was narrated from Mujahid that he connected the firm rooted in knowledge to what came before it and claimed that they knew it. Some linguists have argued for this, saying: Its meaning is and those firmly rooted in knowledge teach it, saying, We believe. He claimed that the position of they say is in the accusative case as a state. Most linguists reject this and reject it, because the Arabs do not imply the verb and the object together, and they do not mention a state except with the appearance of the verb. So if the verb does not appear, then it is not a state. If that were permissible, then it would be permissible to say: Abdullah is riding, meaning Abdullah came riding. But that is only permissible with the mention of the verb, like his saying: Abdullah speaks and reconciles between people. So he was reconciling as a state for him, like the poet’s saying: Abu Omar recited to me. He said: “Abu al-Abbas Tha’lab recited to us: I sent a cat to Kaka, it walks short and stands tall That is, he shortens it while walking, so the statement of the majority of scholars with the help of the grammarians’ schools of thought is more appropriate than the statement of Mujahid alone. Also, it is not permissible for God, the Exalted, to deny something from creation and affirm it for Himself and then have a partner in that. Do you not see the statement of God, the Exalted: Say: None in the heavens and earth knows the fault except God, and His statement: “None reveals it at its time except Him,” and His statement: Everything will perish except His Face. So all of this is something that God, the Exalted, has kept to Himself in knowledge and no one else shares it with Him. Likewise His statement, the Blessed and Most High: And none knows its interpretation except God. If the and in His statement and those firmly rooted had been for the sake of sequence, then there would have been no benefit in His statement: All is from our Lord. And God knows best. I said: What Al-Khattabi narrated, that no one other than Mujahid said, it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the firm-founded are connected to the name of God Almighty, and that they are included in the knowledge of the ambiguous, and that with their knowledge of it they say we believe in it, and Al-Rabi’ and Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn Al-Zubayr and Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and others said it. And they say on this interpretation we reach the state of the firm-founded, as he said: The wind cries its sorrow and the lightning flashes in the clouds This verse has two possible meanings. It is possible that and the lightning is the subject, and the predicate glitters according to the first interpretation, so it is cut off from what precedes it. It is also possible that it is conjoined with the wind, and glitters is in the place of a state according to the second interpretation, i.e. not together. The proponents of this statement also argued that God Almighty praised them for their firmness in knowledge, so how could He praise them when they are ignorant, and Ibn Abbas said: I am among those who know its interpretation. Mujahid recited this verse and said: I am among those who know its interpretation, as narrated by Imam al-Haramayn Abu al-Ma’ali. I said: Some scholars have attributed this statement to the first statement, saying: The estimation of the completeness of the statement with God is that its meaning is and none knows its interpretation except God, meaning the interpretation of the ambiguous verses, and those firmly rooted in knowledge know some of it, saying, We believe in it, all from our Lord, because of the evidence that He has established in the decisive verses and the ability to return it to God. So if they know the interpretation of some of it and do not know some of it, they say, We believe in all of it, all from our Lord, and whatever our knowledge does not encompass of the hidden things in His righteous law, its knowledge is with our Lord. If someone says: Some of its interpretation was unclear to the firmly rooted ones, to the point that Ibn Abbas said: I do not know what al-Awah is or what ghuslān is, it is said to him: This is not necessary, because Ibn Abbas became knowledgeable after that, so he explained what he came across. A more definitive answer than this is that He, the Glorified, did not say, and every firmly rooted one, so this is necessary, so if no one knows it, the other knows it. Ibn Furak preferred that the firmly rooted ones know the interpretation and elaborated on that, and in his saying, peace be upon him, to Ibn Abbas: O God, give him understanding of the religion and teach him the interpretation that will make that clear to You. That is, teach him the meanings of Your Book. The pause on this is at His statement, and those firmly rooted in knowledge. Our Sheikh Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Umar said: This is correct, for calling them firmly rooted implies that they know more than the decisive, whose knowledge is equal to that of all who understand the speech of the Arabs. And in what is their firmness if they only know what everyone knows? But the ambiguous varies, for some of it is not known at all, such as the matter of the spirit and the Hour, which God has kept to Himself in His unseen, and no one engages in knowledge of this, not Ibn Abbas nor anyone else. So whoever among the skilled scholars said that those firmly rooted do not know the ambiguous, he meant this type. As for what can be understood in terms of language and approaches in the speech of the Arabs, it is interpreted and its correct interpretation is known, and any interpretation that may be incorrect is removed from it, such as His statement about Jesus and a spirit from Him and other than that. No one is called firmly rooted except if he knows a lot of this type according to what is decreed for him. As for those who say: The ambiguous is the abrogated, then it is correct according to his statement to include those firmly rooted in the science of interpretation, but his limiting the ambiguous to this type is incorrect. And firmness: is stability in something, and everything that is firm is firm, and its origin in celestial bodies is that the mountain and tree are firmly rooted in the ground. The poet said: I have a deep-rooted love for Laila in my heart that no sign of her will change. Faith became firmly established in someone’s heart. Some of them said: The water of the pond dried up. This was narrated by Ibn Faris, so it is one of the opposites. Rusakah firm, Rasakah firm, Rasab firm, and Rasab remained all mean that it is established in him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about those who are firmly established in knowledge, so he said: He is the one whose oath is fulfilled, whose tongue is truthful, and whose heart is sincere. If it is said: How could there be ambiguous verses in the Qur’an when God says: And We have sent down to you the message that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them. So how could He not make it all clear? It is said to him: The wisdom in that, and God knows best, is to show the superiority of the scholars, because if it were all clear, the superiority of some of them over others would not be apparent. And this is what is done by those who compile a classification, making some of it clear and some of it ambiguous, and leaving room for ambiguity, because that which is easy to find has little splendor. And God knows best. Ninth: The Almighty’s statement: All is from our Lord. There is a pronoun in it referring to the Book of God Almighty, its clear and ambiguous verses. The meaning is: All is from our Lord. The pronoun was omitted because all indicates it, as it is a word that requires addition. Then he said: None will remember except those of understanding, meaning none will say this, believe, stop where he stops, and abandon following the ambiguous verses except one with a core, which is the mind. The core of everything is its essence, and for this reason the mind is called a core. And core is the plural of with.
3:8: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate. There is an omission in the speech, the meaning of which is they say. This is a narration about those firmly rooted. It is possible that the meaning is Say, O Muhammad. And it is said: The deviation of the heart is corruption and inclination from the religion. So they were afraid, after they had been guided, that God would lead them to corruption. So the answer is that they asked, when God guided them, that He not test them with actions that would be too heavy for them and that they would be unable to do them, such as And if We had decreed upon them, ‘Kill yourselves’ or ‘Leave your homes.’ Ibn Kaysan said: They asked not to deviate, so God would not make their hearts deviate, like: So when they deviated, God made their hearts deviate, meaning, Keep us steadfast in Your guidance as You have guided us, and do not let us deviate, so that we deserve for our hearts to deviate. It was said: It is disconnected from what came before, because when God mentioned the people of deviance, He followed that by teaching His servants to supplicate to Him so that they would not be from the blameworthy group that was mentioned, which are the people of deviance. In Al-Muwatta’, on the authority of Abu Abdullah Al-Sunabhi, he said: I came to Madinah during the caliphate of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, so I prayed Maghrib behind him, so he recited in the first two rak’ahs the Mother of the Qur’an and a short surah from Al-Mufassal, then he stood up in the third, so I came close to him until my clothes almost touched his clothes, and I heard him recite the Mother of the Qur’an and this verse: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate Al-Mufassal. Scholars said: Reciting this verse is a form of Qunut because it contains the matter of the apostates. Qunut is permissible in the Maghrib prayer according to a group of scholars, and in every prayer also if a great matter befalls the Muslims that frightens them and they fear for themselves. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it in the hadith of Shahr ibn Hawsha who said: I said to Umm Salamah: O Mother of the Believers, what was the most frequent supplication of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when he was with you? She said: The most frequent supplication was: O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. I said: O Messenger of God, what is your most frequent supplication: O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. He said: “O Umm Salamah, there is no human being except that his heart is between two of the fingers of God. So whoever He wills, He may stand, and whoever He wills, He may deviate.” Muadh then recited: Our Lord, let not our hearts deviate after You have guided us. He said: A good hadith. This verse is an argument against the Mu’tazilah in their hearts: God does not lead His servants astray. If the deviation had not come from him, it would not have been permissible for him to claim that he should prevent what he is not permitted to do. Abu Waqid read to Jarrah, Do not let our hearts deviate, attributing the action to the hearts, and this is a request to God Almighty. The meaning of the verse according to both readings is that you should not create deviation in it, so that it deviates. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And grant us from Yourself mercy meaning from You and from before You as a favor, not because of any reason or action from us. In this there is surrender and exchange. There are four languages for Ladan: Ladan with a fatha and with a damma on the lam, a jazm on the dal and a fatha on the noon, and with a fatha on the lam, a sukoon on the dal and a fatha on the noon. Perhaps the ignorant Sufis and heretics of the Batiniyyah cling to this verse and others like it and say: Knowledge is what God has granted us from the beginning other than acquisition, and looking at books and papers is a veil. This is refuted by what will be explained in this place. The meaning of the verse is: Grant us a blessing emanating from mercy, because mercy returns to the attribute of the Self, so a gift cannot be imagined in it. It is said: Wahba yahabi, and the original is yuhib with a kasra on the ha’. Whoever says: The original is yuhib with a fatha on the ha’ has made a mistake, because if it were as he said, the waw would not have been deleted, just as the waw was not deleted in yujall. The waw was deleted because it came between a ya and a kasra, then it was opened after it was deleted because it contains a throat letter.
3:9: That is, He who will raise them up and revive them after their dispersion. This is an acknowledgment of the resurrection on the Day of Judgment. Al-Zajjaj said: This is the interpretation that the firmly grounded knew and acknowledged. Those who followed disagreed with what was unclear to them about the matter of resurrection until they denied it. Doubt is suspicion, and its implications have been discussed previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. Al-Mi'ad is a noun derived from al-Wa'ad.
3:10: Its meaning is between, i.e. their wealth and children will not protect them from the punishment of God at all. Al-Salami read lan yaghni with a ya' because the verb came before it and there was a barrier between the noun and the verb. Al-Hasan read yaghni with a ya' and the sukoon of the last ya' for the sake of alleviation, like the poet's saying: Enough despair from Asmaa Kafi and not for her illness, as the cure is long He should have said enough, so he sent the ya. Al-Farra’ added something similar: As if their hands in the bottom of the valley were the hands of slave girls, playing with paper. Qarq and Qarqah are two dialects in Al-Qaa. And min in His saying min God means with, Abu Ubaidah said. Those are the fuel of the Fire. And fuel is a name for firewood, and it was mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Talhah bin Masraf read waqood with a damma on the waw, deleting an added word, which is hatab the fuel of the fire. And it is permissible in Arabic, if the waw is a damma, to say aqwad like aqtat. And waqood with a damma on the waw is the source, and the fire was ignited if it was lit. Ibn Al-Mubarak narrated from the hadith of Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This religion will appear until it crosses the seas and until the seas are crossed by horses in the way of God Almighty. Then there will come people who will recite the Qur’an. When they recite it, they will say, Who among us recites more knowledgeable than us? Then he will turn to his companions and say, Do you see any good in those people? They will say, No. He will say, Those are from you and those are from this nation and those are the fuel of the Fire.
3:11: Persistence is habit and affair. A man's perseverance in his work is perseverance and diligence if he is serious and strives, and I made him persevere. And his camel is persevering if he exerts himself in walking. And the two persevering are night and day. Abu Hatim said: I heard Yaqub mention Kad'ab with the opening of the hamza, and he said to me when I was a young man: On what is Kad'ab permissible? I said to him: I think it is from dai'b yadab daban. He accepted that from me and was amazed at the quality of the estimate for my youth, and I do not know whether it is said or not. An-Nahhas said: This statement is wrong, it is not said at all in dai'b, but rather it is said da'ab yadab da'uban and da'aban, this is how the grammarians narrated it, including Al-Farra' who narrated it in the Book of Sources, as Imru' al-Qais said: As usual, from Umm Al-Huwairith before her and her neighbor Umm Al-Rabab in Masal As for the word da’ab, it is permissible, just as it is said: poetry and poetry, “river” and river, because it contains a throat letter. They differed about the letter kaf. It was said: It is in the nominative case, and its meaning is their habit is like the habit of the people of Pharaoh, meaning the actions of the infidels with you are like the actions of the people of Pharaoh with Moses. Al-Farra’ claimed that the meaning is: The Arabs disbelieved as the people of Pharaoh disbelieved. Al-Nahhas said: It is not permissible for the letter kaf to be related to disbelieved, because disbelieved is included in the relative clause. It was said: It is related to God took them, meaning He took them as He took the people of Pharaoh. It was said: It is related to His statement: Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them, meaning they will not avail them as wealth and children did not avail the people of Pharaoh. This is an answer to someone who stayed behind from jihad and said: Our wealth and families have occupied us. It is correct for an action to be applied to it from the word fuel, and the simile would be in the burning itself. This meaning is supported by “And the people of Pharaoh were overtaken by an evil punishment. The Fire, they will be exposed to it morning and evening. And on the Day the Hour comes, [it will be said], ‘Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment.’” The first statement is more correct, and was chosen by more than one scholar. Ibn Arafa said: Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh meaning like the habit of the people of Pharaoh. He said: These infidels were accustomed to blasphemy and to oppressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, just as the people of Pharaoh were accustomed to oppressing the prophets. Al-Azhari said the same meaning. As for His statement in Surat al-Anfal Like the habit of the people of Pharaoh, the meaning is that these people were punished with killing and captivity just as the people of Pharaoh were punished with drowning and destruction. The Almighty’s saying: By Our signs may mean the recited signs, or it may mean the signs that are in the accusative case to indicate oneness. So God seized them for their sins, and God is severe in penalty.
3:12: Meaning the Jews. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) defeated the Quraysh at Badr and brought all the Jews to Medina, he said: "O group of Jews, beware of God as He befell the Quraysh on the day of Badr before He befalls you with what befell them. You have known that I am a prophet sent by God. You will find that in your book and in God's covenant with you." They said: O Muhammad, do not be deceived by the fact that you fought ignorant people who had no knowledge of war and you took advantage of them. By God, if you had fought us, you would have known that we are the people. So God revealed: Say to those who disbelieve, 'You will be overcome' with the ta' meaning the Jews: i.e. defeated and gathered to Hell in the Hereafter. This is the narration of Ikrimah and Sa'id bin Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas. In the narration of Abu Salih on his authority, when the Jews rejoiced at what befell the Muslims on the day of Uhud, this was revealed. So the meaning according to this is that they will be overcome with the ya' meaning the Quraysh, and gathered with the ya' in both of them, and this is the reading of Nafi'. The Almighty says: And what an evil resting place meaning Hell. This is the apparent meaning of the verse. Mujahid said: The meaning is: What they prepared for themselves is evil. So it is as if the meaning is: What an evil deed they did that led them to Hell.
3:13: The Almighty said: There has certainly been for you a sign meaning a mark. He said (was) and did not say it was because the feminine of sign is not real. It was said: He returned it to the explanation, meaning there has certainly been for you a statement, so he went with the meaning and left the wording, like the saying of Imru' al-Qais: A sudden change in the license of the broken Banah He did not say the broken one, because he meant the penis. Al-Farra’ said: He mentioned it because he distinguished between them with the description. So when the description came between the noun and the verb, he mentioned the verb. This meaning has already passed in Al-Baqarah in the Almighty’s saying: It is prescribed for you, when death approaches any of you, if he leaves goods, that he make a bequest. “In two companies that met” meaning the Muslims and the polytheists on the day of Badr. A company The majority read a company in the nominative case, meaning one of them is a company. Al-Hasan and Mujahid read a company in the accusative case and another is a disbeliever as a substitute. Ibn Abi Ubaidah read both of them in the accusative case. Ahmad ibn Yahya said: The accusative case is permissible as a state, meaning they met, different, believers and disbelievers. Al-Zajjaj said: The accusative case means I mean. A group of people were called a company because they are returned to, i.e. they return to it in times of hardship. Al-Zajjaj said: A company is a division, taken from fawat ra’shu bil-sif and it is said fa’itahu if you split it open. There is no disagreement that the reference to these two companies is to the day of Badr. There is disagreement about who is being addressed by it. It was said: It is possible that it is addressed to the believers, and it is possible that it is addressed to all the disbelievers, and it is possible that it is addressed to the Jews of Medina, and some people have said any of these possibilities. The benefit of addressing the believers is to strengthen and encourage their souls so that they may advance against those like them and their likes, as has happened. God the Almighty said: “They will see them twice as many as they are, with the sight of the eye. And God supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.” Abu Ali said: The vision in this verse is seeing with the eye, and that is why it takes one object. Makki and Al-Mahdawi said: It is indicated by the sight of the eye. Nafi’ read tarunahum with a ta’ and the rest with a ya’. Mithlihim is an accusative in the state of the ha’ and mim in tarunahum. The majority of people are of the opinion that the subject of tarunahum is the believers, and the attached pronoun refers to the disbelievers. Abu Amr denied that tarunahum should be read with a ta’. He said: If that were the case, it would have been mithleekum. An-Nahhas said: This is not necessary, but it is permissible for it to be mithleekum your companions. Makki said tarunahum with a ta’ is an address in lakum, so it is appropriate for the address to be to the Muslims, and the ha’ and mim to the polytheists. It would have been necessary for the one who read with the ta’ to read mithleekum with the kaf, and that is not permissible due to the discrepancy in the script, but the speech went from addressing to speaking in the third person, like the Almighty’s saying: Until, when you were in the ship and it sailed with them and His saying: Then those are the ones who are doubled. So it returned to the third person, so the ha’ and the mim in mithleekum could be referring to the polytheists, meaning you see, O Muslims, the polytheists like me in number, and this is far-fetched in meaning, because God the Almighty did not increase the polytheists in the eyes of the Muslims, but rather informed us that He made them few in the eyes of the believers, so the meaning would be you see, O believers, the polytheists like you in number, and they were three times their number, so God made the polytheists few in the eyes of the Muslims and made them see their number like me so that their souls would be strengthened and boldness would occur, and they knew that one hundred of them would overcome two hundred of the disbelievers, and He made the Muslims few in the eyes of the polytheists so that they would be bold with them and so the judgment of God would be implemented against them. It is possible that the pronoun in their equals refers to the Muslims, meaning you see, O Muslims, that the Muslims are equal to me in number, meaning you see yourselves as equal in number. God did this to them so that they would be able to meet the polytheists. The first interpretation is more appropriate, as indicated by the words of God the Almighty: When God showed them to you in your dream as few and His words: And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: I said to a man next to me: Do you see them as seventy? He said: I think they were a hundred. So when we took the captives, they told us that they were a thousand. At-Tabari narrated on the authority of some people that they said: Rather, God increased the number of the believers in the eyes of the disbelievers until they were twice their number in their eyes. At-Tabari deemed this statement weak. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: And it is also rejected from several angles. Rather, God made the polytheists few in the eyes of the believers, as mentioned above. According to this interpretation, you would see the disbelievers, meaning you see, O disbelievers, the believers twice as many as them, and it is possible that you see twice as many as you, based on what was mentioned above. Al-Farra’ claimed that the meaning is you see them twice as many as three times as many. This is far-fetched and not known in the language. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a chapter on harshness, in which there is an error in all standards, because we only understand the like of something as being equal to it, and we understand twice as much as being equal to it twice. Ibn Kaysan said: Al-Farra’ explained his statement by saying: Just as you say when you have a slave: I need his like, so you need him and his like, and you say: I need his double, so you need three, and the meaning is contrary to what he said and the language. What led Al-Farra’ to this is that the polytheists were three times as many as the believers on the day of Badr, so he thought that it was not possible for them to see them except according to their number, and this is far-fetched and the meaning is not correct. Rather, God showed them other than their number for two reasons: One of them is that He saw the good in that, because the hearts of the believers are strengthened by that. The other is that it is a sign for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Battle of Badr will be mentioned, God willing. As for the reading of the letter ya, Ibn Kaysan said: The ha and the meem in they see them refer to and another disbelieving group and the ha and the meem in multithlihim refer to a group fighting in the way of God. This is from the concealment indicated by the context of the speech, which is His statement: He supports with His victory whom He wills. This indicates that the disbelievers were twice as many as the Muslims in the sight of the eye and three times as many in number. He said: The vision here refers to the Jews. Makki said: The vision refers to the group fighting in the way of God, and the visible is the disbelieving group, meaning the group fighting in the way of God sees the disbelieving group twice as many as the believing group, and the disbelieving group was three times as many as the believing group, so God made them small in their eyes as mentioned above. The address in for you is to the Jews. Ibn Abbas and Talhah read you see them with a damma on the ta, and as-Salami with a damma on the ta for what was not named as an agent. “And God supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.” Its meaning has been presented, and praise be to God.
3:14: It contains eleven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Beautified for people. Zain comes from adornment. People differed about who is the adorner. A group said: God adorned that, and this is the apparent statement of Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him, mentioned by Al-Bukhari. In the revelation: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it. When Omar said: Now, O Lord, when You have adorned it for us, the following verse was revealed: Say, Shall I inform you of something better than that? A group said: The adorner is Satan, and this is the apparent statement of Al-Hasan, for he said: Whoever adorns it, no one is more severe in blaming it than its Creator. So God’s adornment is only by creating and preparing for benefit and creating the nature to incline toward these things. Satan’s adornment is only by whispering, deception, and making it seem good to take it from other than its intended sources. The verse, in both versions, begins with a sermon for all people, and within that is a rebuke to the contemporaries of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from among the Jews and others. The majority read Zain in the passive form of the verb, raising love. Ad-Dahhak and Mujahid read Zain in the active form of the verb, lowering love. The letter ha’ was moved from the word shahāt to differentiate between the noun and the adjective. Shahāwat is the plural of shahwāt, which is well-known. A man is shahwān for something, and something shahī means desired. Following desires leads to ruin and obeying them leads to destruction. In Sahih Muslim: Paradise is surrounded by hardships and Hellfire is surrounded by desires. Narrated by Anas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The benefit of this metaphor is that Paradise can only be attained by crossing the paths of hardships and being patient with them. Hellfire can only be saved from by abandoning desires and weaning the soul from them. It was narrated that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The path to Paradise is rough with a hill, and the path to Hell is smooth with a plain. This is the meaning of his statement, Paradise is surrounded by hardships, and Hell is surrounded by desires. That is, the path to Paradise is difficult to traverse, and it is at the highest point of the hills, while the path to Hell is smooth, neither rough nor rugged. This is the meaning of his statement, Smooth with a plain, with a sukun on the letter s. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Of women. He began with them because of the great longing of souls for them, because they are the snares of Satan and the temptation of men. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have not left behind me any trial more severe for men than women. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. The trial of women is more severe than all things. It is said: There are two trials for women, and there is only one trial for children. As for the two trials for women, one of them is that it leads to severing family ties, because a woman orders her husband to sever ties with his mothers and sisters. The second is the trial of accumulating wealth from lawful and unlawful sources. As for children, there is only one trial for them, which is the trial of accumulating wealth for their sake. Abdullah ibn Masoud narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not let your women live in rooms, nor teach them to write. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, warned them, because letting them live in rooms means that they will look at men, but that does not protect them or conceal them, because they may look down on men, which will cause temptation and calamity. And because they were created from man, so they understood it in man, and man was created with desire and was made a dwelling for him, so neither of them is trustworthy with the other. And in teaching them to write, this meaning is a source of temptation and more severe. And in the book of Ash-Shihab, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Lend women so that they may remain in their chambers. If a person cannot be patient in these times, he should look for a woman of religion so that the religion may be safe for him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You should marry a religious woman, may your hands be covered with dust. Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurairah. And in Sunan Ibn Mahah on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not marry women for their beauty, for perhaps their beauty will destroy them. And do not marry them for their wealth, for perhaps their wealth will make them insolent. But marry them for their religion. And a black, blind slave woman with religion is better. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And the sons is in apposition to what preceded it. One of the sons is a son. God Almighty said, informing about Nuh 71:Indeed, my son is of my family. And you say in the diminutive form bani as Luqman said. In the hadith, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Al-Ash’ath bin Qais: Do you have a son from the daughter of Hamad? He said: Yes, I have a boy from her and I wish I had a bowl of food to feed to whoever is left of Banu Jablah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you say that, then they are the fruit of the hearts and the delight of the eyes, and despite that, they are cowardly, miserly and sad. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And the qintars. Qintars is the plural of qintar, as the Almighty said: And you have given one of them a qintar, which is a large knot of money. It was said: It is the name of the standard by which it is weighed, as is the pound and the quarter. And when that weight is reached, it is said: This is a qintar, meaning it is equal to a qintar. The Arabs say: A man has become qintar if his money has reached the point of being weighed by a qintar. Al-Zajjaj said: Qintar is taken from the knotting of something and its perfection. The Arabs say: I have perfected something if I have perfected it, and from this the qintar was named because of its perfection. Tarafa said: Like the Roman bridge, its Lord swore that it would be surrounded until it was built with bricks. And the knotted bridge, so the qintar is like a knot of money. The scholars differed in defining its limit, as it is in many sayings. Abi bin Kaab narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The qintar is one thousand and two hundred ounces. This was stated by Muadh ibn Jabal, Abdullah ibn Umar, Abu Hurairah and a group of scholars. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is the most correct of the sayings, but the qintar according to this differs in the amount of ounce in different countries. It was also said: It is twelve thousand ounces. Al-Busti included it in his Musnad al-Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A qintar is twelve thousand ounces. An ounce is better than what is between the heavens and the earth. Abu Hurairah also said the same. In Musnad Abi Muhammad al-Darimi, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri, he said: Whoever recites ten verses at night will be recorded among those who remember God, and whoever recites one hundred verses will be recorded among those who are devout, and whoever recites five hundred to a thousand verses will have a qintar of reward in the morning. It was said: What is a qintar? He said: A bull’s worth of musk filled with gold. It was narrated by Abu Nadrah al-Abdi. Ibn Sidah mentioned that it is like this in Syriac. Al-Naqqash said on the authority of Ibn al-Kalbi that this is how it was conveyed to the Romans. Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak and al-Hasan said: One thousand two hundred mithqals of silver, and al-Hasan attributed it to the Prophet. Ibn Abbas said: Twelve thousand dirhams of silver, and one thousand dinars of gold is the blood money for a Muslim man. It was narrated on the authority of al-Hasan and al-Dahhak. Saeed ibn al-Musayyab said: Eighty thousand. Qatadah said: One hundred pounds of gold or eighty thousand dirhams of silver. Abu Hamza al-Thumali said: A qintar in Africa and Andalusia is eight thousand mithqals of gold or silver. As-Suddi: Four thousand mithqals. Mujahid: Seventy thousand mithqals. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar. Makki narrated a saying that a qintar is forty ounces of gold or silver, and Ibn Sidah said in Al-Muhkam, and said: A qintar in the language of the Berbers is a thousand mithqals. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: A qintar is a lot of money, some of it on top of some, and this is what is known among the Arabs, and from it is his saying: And you have given one of them a qintar, meaning a lot of money. And from it is the hadith: Safwan bin Umayya was a qantar in the pre-Islamic era, and his father qantar means he had a qantar of money. On the authority of Al-Hakam: Qantar is the area between the sky and the earth. They differed on the meaning of Al-Muqantara. Al-Tabari and others said: It means double, as if Qantara is three and Al-Muqantara is nine. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Farraa that he said: Qantara is the plural of Qantar, and Al-Muqantara is the plural of plural, so it would be nine qantar.
