Al-Suddi: Al-Muqantara is the multiplied until it became dinars or dirhams. Makki: Al-Muqantara is the completed one, and Al-Harawi narrated it, as it is said: Badr Mubadara, and thousands composed. Some of them said: This is why the building was called Al-Qantara because of the density of the building, one on top of the other. Ibn Kaysan and Al-Farraa: Al-Muqantara should not be less than nine qantar. It was said: Al-Muqantara is a reference to the presence of money and its being ready. In Sahih Al-Busti on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever recites ten verses will not be counted among the heedless. Whoever recites one hundred verses will be counted among the devout. Whoever recites one thousand verses will be counted among the pious. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Of gold and silver Gold is feminine, it is said: it is the good gold, its plural is dhahab and dhahub. It is possible that it is the plural of dhahabah, and its plural is adhhab. So-and-so went a good way. Gold is a measure for the people of Yemen. A man went if he saw a gold mine and was amazed. Silver is well-known, and its plural is silver. So gold is taken from dhahab, and silver is taken from anfadh something, it is scattered, and from it I scattered the people, so they dispersed, meaning I separated them and they dispersed. This derivation indicates their disappearance and lack of permanence as is seen in existence. Among the best things said in this meaning is what some of them said. Fire is the last dinar I spoke with, and worry is the last of this flowing dirham. And the person between them, if he is pious, his heart is tormented between worry and Hellfire. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And horses is feminine. Ibn Kaysan said: I was told on the authority of Abu Ubaidah that he said: The singular of horses is kha’il, like tayr and tayr and wadayn and wadayn, and the horse was named thus because it struts in its gait. Another said: It is a collective noun that has no singular from the same word, the singular is fars, like qawm, “raht,” nisa, “camels,” and the like. And in the report from the hadith of Ali on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God created the horse from the wind, and that is why He made it fly without wings. Wahb ibn Munabbih created it from the south wind. Wahb said: There is no glorification, no magnification, and no declaration of unanimity that its owner makes except that he hears it and responds to it with the same. There will be a mention of horses and their description in Surat Al-Anfal, which is sufficient, God willing. In the hadith: God offered Adam all the beasts, and he was told: Choose one of them, so he chose the horse. He was told: You have chosen your glory, so its name became good from this aspect. It was called a horse because it is marked with glory, so whoever rides it is proud of God’s gift to him and struts with it against the enemies of God Almighty. It was called a horse because it preys over distances in the air like a lion preys and leaps, and it covers them like devouring something with its hands, hitting and grabbing it. It was called an Arab because it was brought after Adam to Ishmael as a reward for raising the foundations of the House, and Ishmael was an Arab, so it had its gift from God Almighty, so it was called an Arab. In the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The devil does not enter a house in which there is an old horse. It was called old because it was freed from the hybridity. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best horses are those that are dark raven, bald-headed, and white-footed. Then those that are bald-footed and have a white spot on their right sides. If they are not dark raven, then they are bay with this feature. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Qatada. In Musnad Al-Daraami on his authority that a man said: O Messenger of God, I want to buy a horse, so which one should I buy? He said: Buy a dark raven, white-footed, and white-footed horse, or a bay with this feature, so you will gain and be safe. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Anas who said: After women, nothing was more beloved to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, than horses. The imams narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Horses are of three types: for a man they bring reward, for a man they provide cover, and for a man they bring sin. The hadith is long, and its fame makes mentioning it unnecessary. The rulings on horses will be mentioned in Al-Anfal and An-Nahl, sufficiently, God willing. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: The one who has been marked: meaning the one who grazes in the meadows and pastures, as Saeed bin Jubair said. It is said: The animal or sheep has been marked if it has been set free to roam, it is then saimat. And I marked it means I left it for that reason, so it is musamāma. And I marked it means taswīm, so it is samūma. In Sunan Ibn Majah, on the authority of Ali, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade fasting before sunrise, and the slaughter of milking animals. Fasting here means grazing. God the Almighty said: You will graze in it. Al-Akhtal said: Like Ibn Buza’ah or someone like him, it is better for you, Ibn Masima Al-Ajmal Ibn Ra’iah meant camels. As-Sawam is every animal that grazes. It was also said: prepared for jihad, as stated by Ibn Zayd. Mujahid like Al-Musawwah Al-Mutahmah Al-Hasan. Ikrimah said: He marked her with Al-Hasan, and An-Nahhas chose it, from their saying: a handsome man. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Al-Musawwah is the one marked with the marks of horses on their faces, from Seema which is the mark. This is the doctrine of Al-Kisa’i and Abu Ubaidah. I said: The wording includes everything mentioned, so it is a well-trained, well-trained she-camel, so that it can be distinguished from others. Abu Zaid said: The origin of that is to put wool or a mark on it that differs from the rest of its body so that it can be distinguished from others in the pasture. Ibn Faris the linguist stated in his book Majmal: The branded, sent one with riders on it. Al-Mu'arraj said: The branded, cauterized one. Al-Mubarrad: The one known in the countries. Ibn Kaysan: The bleak one. And all of them are close in character. Al-Nabigha said: And the arrows are marked with arrows, and they are like jinn-like arrows. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And the livestock. Ibn Kaysan said: If you say yes, it only refers to camels. If you say livestock, it refers to camels. And everything that grazes. Al-Farra’ said: It is masculine and not feminine. They say: This is a blessing that has been brought, and its plural is cattle. Al-Harawi said: The blessing is both masculine and feminine, and the cattle are the livestock such as camels, cows, and sheep. And if it is said: the blessing is camels in particular. Hassan said: And there was still a companion in its meadows, yes and God willing. In Sunan Ibn Majah, on the authority of Urwah al-Barqi, he said: Camels are a source of pride for their owners, sheep are a blessing, and goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sheep is one of the beasts of Paradise. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded the rich to keep sheep, and the poor to keep chickens. He said: When the rich keep chickens, God, the Most High, permits the destruction of the earth. It was narrated on the authority of Umm Hani that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Keep sheep, for there is blessing in them. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Shaiba on the authority of Waki’ on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Umm Hani, with a sound chain of transmission. Ninth: And the Almighty’s saying: And tillage. Here, tillage is the name for everything that is tilled and it is a source named after it. You say: A man plowed tillage if he stirred the earth meaning he farmed. So the name plowing applies to planting grains and gardens and other types of farming. In the hadith: Plow for your world as if you will live forever. It is said: I plowed and I plowed. In the hadith of Abdullah: Plow this Qur’an, meaning search it. Ibn al-A’rabi said: Plowing is inspection. In the hadith: The most truthful name is al-Harith because al-Harith is the earner, and plowing money is its earning, and the plow is the kindling of fire and the plow is the path of the bowstring, and the plural is ahrithah. A man made his camel emaciated. In the hadith of Mu’awiyah: What did your camels do? They said: We plowed them on the day of Badr. Abu Ubaid said: They mean we made them emaciated. It is said: The animal plowed and I plowed it, two languages. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn Umamah Al-Bahili, he said: When he saw a path and some of the tools of cultivation, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: No people enter this house except that humiliation enters it. It was said: The humiliation here is what is required of those who are busy with cultivation from the rights of the land that the imams and sultans demand of them. Al-Muhallab said: The meaning of his statement in this hadith, and God knows best, is: Encouraging the highest conditions and seeking a livelihood from the most honorable of industries. This is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, feared for his nation from being busy with cultivation and neglecting horse riding and jihad in the way of God. Because they were busy with cultivation, the nations who ride horses and make a living from their earnings would overcome them. So he deducted the livelihood from jihad, not from being devoted to cultivating the land and sticking to the profession. Do you not see that Umar said: Be strong, rough, and cut off the knees, and jump the horses so that the camel herders do not overcome you with them. So he ordered them to stick to the horses and exercise their bodies by jumping on them. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no Muslim who plants a tree or sows a seed from which a bird, a person, or an animal eats, but that it is considered a charity for him. Scholars said: God Almighty mentioned four types of money, each type of money is used to finance a class of people. As for gold and silver, it is used to finance merchants, as for branded horses, it is used to finance kings, as for sheep, it is used to finance the people of the desert, and as for crops, it is used to finance the people of the villages. So the trial of each class is from the type that is financed, as for women and children, they are a trial for everyone. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: That is the enjoyment of worldly life, meaning that which is enjoyed in it and then it goes away and does not remain. This is a sign of his asceticism in this world and an encouragement for the Hereafter. Ibn Majah and others narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is only the enjoyment of this world, and there is nothing better than a righteous woman among the enjoyments of this world. In the hadith: Ascetic in this world and God will love you, meaning in its pleasures of prestige and money in excess of what is necessary. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The son of Adam has no right to these qualities: a house in which he lives, a garment to cover his private parts, bread and money.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Uthman ibn Affan. Sahl ibn Abdullah was asked: What makes it easy for a servant to abandon the world and all desires? He said: By occupying himself with what he has been commanded to do. Eleventh: The Almighty’s saying: And God has with Him the best destination. Subject and predicate. The destination is the return, ab means to return, as Imru’ al-Qais said: I have traveled the world until I was satisfied with the spoils of war and returned Another said: Everyone who is absent will return, but the one absent from death will not return. The root of the word ma’ab is ma’ub. The vowel of the waw was changed to a hamza and the waw was replaced with an alif, like maqal. The meaning of the verse is to belittle and despise the world and to encourage a good return to God Almighty in the hereafter.
3:15: The end of the question when he said of that, for those who feared God is an advanced predicate, and gardens is a subject in the nominative case. It was said: its end is with their Lord, and gardens on this is a subject in the nominative case with an implied subject, the meaning of which is that they are gardens. According to this interpretation, it is permissible to say gardens in the accusative case instead of good, but it is not permissible according to the first. Ibn Atiyyah said: This verse and the one before it are similar to his saying, peace be upon him: "A woman is married for four reasons: her wealth, her lineage, her beauty, and her religion. So marry the one who is religious, may your hands be covered with dust." Narrated by Muslim and others. So his saying So marry the one who is religious is an example of this verse. What came before is an example of the first, so God mentioned this as a consolation from the world and strengthening the souls of those who abandon it. The meanings of the words of this verse were previously mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Al-Ridwan is a source of contentment, which is that when the people of Paradise enter Paradise, God Almighty says to them: Do you want something more? They say: O our Lord, what is better than this? He says: My pleasure, so I will never be angry with you after that. Narrated by Muslim. And in the words of God Almighty: And God is Seeing of His servants, there is a promise and a threat.
3:16: Those who instead of those who feared God, and if you wish it could be in the nominative case, meaning they are those, or in the accusative case for praise. Our Lord meaning, O our Lord. Indeed, we have believed meaning we have believed. So forgive us our sins a supplication for forgiveness. And protect us from the punishment of the Fire was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah.
3:17: The patient ones means those who abstain from sins and desires, and it was said: in acts of obedience. And the truthful ones meaning in actions and words. And the obedient ones are the obedient ones. And the spenders meaning in the way of God. These meanings have been presented in full in Surat Al-Baqarah. So God the Almighty explained in this verse the conditions of the righteous who are promised Paradise. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of the Almighty’s statement: And those who seek forgiveness before dawn. Anas bin Malik said: They are those who ask for forgiveness. Qatada said: Those who pray. I said: There is no contradiction, because they pray and seek forgiveness. And he mentioned the pre-dawn hours specifically because it is the time when supplications are accepted and the time when prayers are answered. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his interpretation of the words of God Almighty, informing us about Jacob, peace be upon him, to his sons: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, that he delayed that until the dawn. It was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and will be mentioned later. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel: Which part of the night is most listened to? He said: I do not know, except that the Throne shakes at dawn. It is said sahar and sahar with the ha open or closed. Al-Zajjaj said: Sahar is from the time the night ends until the second dawn appears. Ibn Zayd said: Sahar is the last sixth of the night. I said: More authentic than this is what the imams narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty descends to the lowest heaven every night when the first third of the night has passed and says: ‘I am the King, I am the King. Who is it that calls upon Me, that I may answer him? Who is it that asks Me, that I may give him? Who is it that seeks My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?’ And he continues like this until dawn breaks.” In another narration: until the dawn breaks. The wording of Muslim. There is disagreement over its interpretation. The best that has been said about it is what came in the book of al-Nasa’i, explaining it on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa’id, may God be pleased with them both. They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty gives respite until the thanks of the first night has passed, then He commands a caller to say: ‘Is there a supplicant to be answered? Is there a seeker of forgiveness to be forgiven? Is there a questioner to be given?’” Abu Muhammad ‘Abd al-Haqq authenticated it, and it removes the ambiguity and clarifies every possibility. The first is from the category of deleting the complement, meaning: The King of our Lord descends and says. It has been narrated with a damma on the ya’, and it clarifies what we have mentioned. And God is our guide. We have mentioned it in the most sublime book explaining the beautiful names of God and His sublime attributes. The issue of seeking forgiveness is recommended. God the Almighty praised those who seek forgiveness in this verse and others, saying: And in the hours before dawn they seek forgiveness. Anas bin Malik said: We were commanded to seek forgiveness seventy times before dawn. Sufyan al-Thawri said: It has reached me that when it is the beginning of the night, a caller calls out for the devout to arise, so they rise and pray until dawn. When it is the time of dawn, a caller calls out: Where are those who seek forgiveness? So those seek forgiveness, and others rise and pray and join them. When dawn breaks, a caller calls out: Let the heedless arise, so they rise from their beds like dead people raised from their graves. It was narrated on the authority of Anas that I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “God says: Verily, I am about to punish the people of the earth, but when I look at the people who frequent My houses, at those who love one another in My presence, at those who pray at night, and at those who seek forgiveness in the hours before dawn, I turn away the punishment from them through them.” Makhul said: If there are fifteen men in a nation who seek forgiveness from God twenty-five times every day, God will not hold that nation accountable for the punishment of the general public. Abu Naim mentioned it in his book Al-Hilyah. Nafi’ said: Ibn Umar used to stay up at night and then say, O Nafi’, is it dawn? I would say, No. He would repeat the prayer and then ask, and when I said, Yes, he would sit and seek forgiveness. Ibrahim bin Hattab narrated on the authority of his father, who said: I heard a man in the corner of the mosque at dawn saying, O Lord, You commanded me and I obeyed You, and this is dawn, so forgive me. I looked and saw that it was Ibn Mas’ud. I said: All of this indicates that it is seeking forgiveness with the tongue while the heart is present, not what Ibn Zayd said, that what is meant by those who seek forgiveness are those who pray the dawn prayer in congregation. And God knows best. And Luqman said to his son, O my son, do not let the rooster be more intelligent than you, calling out at dawn while you are asleep. The chosen wording of seeking forgiveness is what Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Shaddad bin Aws, and there is no other version of it in Al-Jami`, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The master of seeking forgiveness is to say: ‘O God, You are my Lord, there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I abide by Your covenant and promise as much as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favor upon me and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You.’ He said: ‘Whoever says it during the day, convinced of it, and dies that day before evening comes, he is among the people of Paradise. Whoever says it at night, convinced of it, and dies that night before morning comes, he is among the people of Paradise.’” Abu Muhammad Abd Al-Ghani bin Sa`id narrated from the hadith of Ibn Lahi`ah on the authority of Abu Sakhr on the authority of Abu Mu`awiyah on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr on the authority of Abu Al-Sahba` Al-Bakri on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the hand of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and then said: ‘Shall I not teach you words that you can say, even if your sins were like the treading of an ant or the crushing of an atom, God would forgive you for you, because you are forgiven: O God, there is no god but You.’” Glory be to You, I have done evil and wronged myself, so forgive me, for no one forgives sins except You.”
3:18: It contains four issues: The first: Saeed bin Jubair said: There were three hundred and sixty idols around the Kaaba, and when this verse was revealed, they fell down in prostration. Al-Kalbi said: When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) appeared in Medina, two rabbis from the rabbis of Ash-Sham came to him. When they saw Medina, one of them said to his companion: How similar this city is to the city of the Prophet who will emerge at the end of time. When they entered upon the Prophet (peace be upon him), they recognized him by description and attribute, and said to him: Are you Muhammad? He said: Yes. They said: And you are Ahmad? He said: Yes. They said: We are asking you about a testimony, if you tell us about it we will believe in you and trust you. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to them: Ask me. They said: Tell us about the greatest testimony in the Book of God. Then God revealed to His Prophet (peace be upon him): {God bears witness that there is no god but He, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - an upholder of justice.} So the two men became Muslims and believed in the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). It has been said that what is meant by those of knowledge are the prophets, peace be upon them. Ibn Kaysan said: The Muhajireen and the Ansar. Muqatil: The believers of the People of the Book. As-Suddi and Al-Kalbi: All believers: All believers. This is more apparent because it is general. Second: In this verse there is evidence of the virtue of knowledge and the honor and virtue of scholars. If there were anyone more honorable than scholars, God would have linked them with His name and the names of His angels, just as He linked the name of scholars. He said about the honor of knowledge to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And say, ‘My Lord, increase me in knowledge.’ If there were anything more honorable than knowledge, God the Most High would have commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask for more of it, just as He commanded him to seek more knowledge. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The scholars are the heirs of the prophets. He also said: Scholars are God’s trustees over His creation. This is a great honor for scholars, and their position in religion is important. Abu Muhammad Abdul Ghani Al-Hafiz narrated from the hadith of Barakah bin Nasheet, who is Ankal bin Hakarik, and his interpretation is Barakah bin Nasheet, and he was a hafiz, he said: Umar bin Al-Mu’ammal narrated to us, Muhammad bin Abi Al-Khasib narrated to us, Ankal narrated to us, Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Scholars are the inheritors of the prophets. The people of heaven love them, and the whales in the sea ask forgiveness for them when they die until the Day of Resurrection.” There is a hadith on this subject on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ narrated by Abu Dawud. Third: Ghalib Al-Qattan narrated: I came to Kufa for business and stayed near Al-A’mash. I used to visit him frequently. When it was night, I wanted to go down to Basra, but he got up and prayed at night and recited this verse: “God bears witness that there is no god but He, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - maintaining justice. There is no god but He, the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam.” Al-A’mash said: I bear witness to what God bears witness to, and I entrust this testimony to God, and it is a trust for me with God, and indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam. He said it repeatedly, so I went to him and bid him farewell, then I said: I heard you recite this verse, so what did you convey in it? I have been with you for a year and you did not tell me about it. He said: By God, I will not tell you about it for a year. He said: So I stayed and wrote on his door that day, and when the year passed I said: O Abu Muhammad, the year passed. He said: Abu Wa’il told me. On the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The one who made it will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and God, the Most High, will say: ‘My servant made a covenant with Me, and I am more deserving of fulfilling it. Admit My servant into Paradise.’” Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: Ghalib al-Qattan, who is Ghalib bin Khattaf al-Qattan, narrates the hadith of Shahada God, which is a defective hadith. Ibn Adi said: The weakness of his hadith is clear. Ahmad bin Hanbal said: Ghalib bin Khattaf al-Qattan is trustworthy, trustworthy. Ibn Ma’in said: Trustworthy. Ibn Hatim said: He is truthful and righteous. I said: It is enough for you of his justice and trustworthiness that Al-Bukhari and Muslim included him in their books, and that is enough for you. It was narrated from the hadith of Anas from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Whoever recites, ‘God bears witness that there is no god but He, and the angels and those of knowledge, upholding justice, there is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise,’ when he sleeps, God will create for him seventy thousand angels who will ask forgiveness for him until the Day of Resurrection.” It is said that whoever acknowledges this testimony with a firm belief in his heart has upheld justice. It was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair that he said: There were three hundred and sixty idols around the Kaaba, and each tribe of the Arabs had one or two idols. When this verse was revealed, the idols fell down in the morning prostrating to God. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying, God has borne witness, meaning He made clear and informed, as one says: So-and-so bore witness before the judge when he made clear and informed to whom the right belongs, or to whom it is. Al-Zajjaj said: The witness is the one who knows and explains something, so God has shown us His Oneness through what He created and made clear. Abu Ubaidah said: God has borne witness means God has decreed, meaning He knows. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is rejected for several reasons. Al-Kisa’i read with the fat-ha on the an in His saying, that there is no god but Him, and His saying, that the religion. Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning is that the religion with God is Islam, that there is no god but Him, then the ba’ was deleted, as he said, I commanded you to do good, meaning to do good. Al-Kisa’i said that he made them both accusative, meaning God bore witness that it is such and such, and that the religion is with God. Ibn Kaysan said: The second is a substitute for the first, because Islam is an interpretation of the meaning, which is monotheism. Ibn Abbas read, as narrated by Al-Kisa’i, God bears witness that it is with a kasra and that the religion is with a fatha. The meaning is: God bears witness that the religion is Islam, then he began and said: There is no god but Him. Abu Al-Muhallab, who was a reciter, read Shahadaa God in the accusative case as a state, and from him Shahadaa God. Shu’bah narrated from Asim from Zur from Abi from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to read that the religion with God is the true religion, not Judaism, nor Christianity, nor Zoroastrianism. Abu Bakr Al-Anbari said: It is not hidden from anyone with discernment that this speech from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is by way of interpretation, and some of those who transmitted the hadith introduced it into the Qur’an. Qa’iman is in the accusative case as a state of emphasis from His name, the Most High, in His statement God bears witness or from His statement except Him. Al-Farra’ said: It is in the accusative case as a severance, its original form was Al-Qa’im, but when the alif and lam were cut off, it was in the accusative case as in His statement And to Him belongs the religion. In the reading of Abdullah, Al-Qa’im is in the qualifier Al-Qust as an adjective, Al-Qust Al-Adl. “There is no god but He, the Almighty, the Wise.” It was repeated because the first took the place of the claim, and the second testimony took the place of the judgment. Jaafar Al-Sadiq said: The first is description and monotheism, and the second is a formality and teaching, meaning say there is no god but God, the Almighty, the Wise.
3:19: The Almighty said: Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam. The religion in this verse is obedience and faith, and Islam means faith and acts of obedience, as Abu Al-Aaliyah said, and the majority of theologians agree with it. The origin of the names faith and Islam is differentiation, as in the hadith of Gabriel. It may also mean synonymy. So each one of them is called by the name of the other, as in the hadith of the delegation of Abd Al-Qays and that he ordered them to believe in God alone. He said: Do you know what faith is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Testifying that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establishing prayer, paying zakat, fasting Ramadan, and giving five from the spoils of war. The hadith, and also his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Faith has seventy-odd branches, the lowest of which is removing harm, and the highest of which is saying, ‘There is no god but God.’ Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. Muslim added: Modesty is a branch of faith. It can also mean overlapping, which is that one of them is used and what is meant by it is its original meaning and what is meant by the other, as in this verse, where belief and deeds are included in it. From this is his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Faith is knowledge in the heart, statement with the tongue, and action with the limbs. Narrated by Ibn Majah, and it has been mentioned above. The truth is that it is the first in terms of position and law, and everything else is a matter of expansion. And God knows best. God the Almighty said: And those who were given the Scripture did not differ. The verse: God the Almighty informed about the difference of the People of the Scripture, that it was due to their knowledge of the truths, and that it was out of transgression and seeking the world. This was said by Ibn Umar and others. There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: And those who were given the Scripture did not differ out of transgression among themselves except after knowledge had come to them, this was said by Al-Akhfash. Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn Al-Zubayr said: What is meant by this verse is the Christians, and it is a rebuke to the Christians of Najran. Al-Rabi` ibn Anas said: What is meant by it is the Jews. The phrase those who were given the Scripture includes the Jews and the Christians, meaning, and those who were given the Scripture did not differ, meaning in the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, except after knowledge had come to them, meaning the clarification of his description and prophethood in their books. It was said: Meaning, and those who were given the Gospel did not differ about the matter of Jesus and divided their words about him except after knowledge had come to them that God is one God, and that Jesus is the servant and Messenger of God. And transgression is the accusative of the object for the sake of it or the state of those, and God the Almighty knows best.
3:20: The Almighty said: But if they argue with you, say, 'I have submitted my face to God, and so have those who follow me.' That is, they argue with you using false statements and fallacies, so entrust your matter to what you are charged with of faith and conveying the message, and upon God is your victory. His saying, my face, means my essence, and from it is the hadith: My face prostrates to Him who created it and shaped it. It has been said that the face here means the intention, as you say: So-and-so went out in such-and-such a face. This meaning has been fully explained in Surat Al-Baqarah, but the first is more appropriate. The face is used to refer to the curtains of the self, as it is the most noble of the person’s organs and the most comprehensive of the senses. He said: I surrender my face to the one to whom the supplies surrender, carrying pure, fresh water. The most skilled theologians have said about the Almighty’s statement: And the Face of your Lord will remain that it refers to the Self, and it has been said: the action intended for His Face. His statement: And whoever follows whom is in the nominative case in apposition to the ta’ in His statement: I have submitted, meaning, whoever follows them has also submitted. It is permissible to attach to the nominative pronoun without emphasising the separation between them. Nafi’, Abu Amr, and Ya’qub confirmed the ya’ of itba’na according to the original, and the others deleted it in imitation of the Qur’an, as it occurred in it without a ya’. The poet said: My wealth does not disappear for a day, but my poverty does disappear for a day. God the Almighty said: “And say to those who were given the Scripture and to the unlettered ones, ‘Have you submitted?’ If they have submitted, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, upon you is only the conveyance. And God is Seeing of His servants.” Meaning the Jews, Christians, and the unlettered ones who have no Scripture, who are the polytheists of the Arabs. Have you submitted is an interrogative that means a statement and includes an order, i.e. submit, as stated by al-Tabari and others. Al-Zajjaj said: Have you submitted is a threat. This is good, because the meaning is have you submitted or not? The phrase in his statement then they have been guided came in the past tense, as an exaggeration in informing about the occurrence of guidance for them and its attainment. Belagh is a verbal noun from balagha with a lightened ayn of the verb, meaning upon you is only to convey. It was said that it was abrogated by jihad. Ibn Atiyyah said: This requires knowing the date of its revelation. As for the apparent revelation of these verses regarding the delegation of Najran, the meaning is that up to you is only to convey what was revealed to you, including fighting and other things.
3:21: It has six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the verses of God and kill the prophets Abu al-Abbas al-Mubarrad said: There were people from the Children of Israel to whom the prophets came calling them to God the Almighty, so they killed them. Then some people from the believers arose after them and ordered them to convert to Islam, so they killed them. This verse was revealed about them. And likewise, Muqal ibn Abi Maskeen said: The prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them, would come to the Children of Israel without a book and kill them. Then some people from among those who followed them would rise up and order justice, meaning fairness, so they would be killed. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “What a bad people are those who kill those who enjoin justice among the people. What a bad people are those who neither enjoin what is right nor forbid what is wrong. What a bad people are those among whom the believer walks in dissimulation.” Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Children of Israel killed forty-three prophets in one hour at the beginning of the day. One hundred and twelve men from the servants of the Children of Israel stood up and enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong. They were all killed at the end of the day. They are the ones mentioned by God in this verse.” Al-Mahdawi and others mentioned this. Shu’bah narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Ubaidah on the authority of Abdullah who said: The Children of Israel used to kill seventy prophets in a day, and then a market would be held to sell them at the end of the day. If someone says: Those who were admonished by this did not kill a prophet, then the answer to this is that they were satisfied with the action of the one who was killed, so they were in his position. Also, they fought the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions and intended to kill them. God the Almighty said: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you or kill you. Second: This verse indicates that enjoining good and forbidding evil was obligatory in the previous nations, and it is the benefit of the message and the succession of the prophethood. Al-Hasan said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever enjoins what is right or forbids what is wrong is the caliph of God on His earth, the caliph of His Messenger, and the caliph of His Book. On the authority of Durrah bint Abi Lahab, she said: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was on the pulpit and said: Who is the best of people, O Messenger of God? He said: He who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong, fears God the most, and maintains ties of kinship. In the Qur’an, it is stated: “The hypocrites, men and women, are of one another. They enjoin what is wrong and forbid what is right.” Then He said: “The believing men and women are allies of one another. They enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.” God the Almighty made enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong a distinction between the believers and the hypocrites. This indicates that the most specific characteristics of the believer are enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, the most important of which is calling to Islam and fighting for it. Moreover, enjoining what is right is not appropriate for everyone, but rather the ruler carries it out, since the implementation of the prescribed punishments is up to him, and the discretionary punishment is up to him, and imprisonment and release are up to him, and exile and banishment are up to him. So he appoints in every town a righteous, strong, knowledgeable, and trustworthy man and orders him to do that, and he carries out the prescribed punishments in their proper manner without adding anything more. God Almighty said: Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer and give zakat, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. Third: It is not a condition for the one who forbids to be just according to the people of the Sunnah, contrary to the innovators who say: Nothing can change it except justice. This is invalid, because justice is limited to a few people, while enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is general for all people. If they cling to the words of God the Most High: Do you enjoin righteousness upon people while you forget yourselves? and His words: It is most hateful to God that you say what you do not do and the like, it will be said to them: The blame here was for committing what was forbidden, not for forbidding what is wrong. There is no doubt that forbidding it from one who does it is worse than one who does not do it, and for this reason it will revolve in Hell as a donkey revolves in a millstone, as we explained in Al-Baqarah when God the Most High said: Do you enjoin righteousness upon people? Fourth: Muslims have unanimously agreed on what Ibn Abd al-Barr mentioned that the evil must be changed by everyone who is able to do so. And that if he is not subject to anything except blame for changing it that does not go beyond harm, then that should not prevent him from changing it. If he is not able to do so, then with his tongue. If he is not able to do so, then with his heart. He is not required to do more than that. If he denounces it with his heart, then he has done what is required of him if he is not able to do anything else. He said: The hadiths from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, emphasizing enjoining good and forbidding evil are very numerous, but they are restricted to ability. Al-Hasan said: Only a believer can speak with hope or an ignorant person can learn. As for the one who puts down his sword or whip and says: Protect me, protect me, then that is none of your business. Ibn Mas`ud said: It is sufficient for a person, if he sees an evil that he is not able to change, that God knows from his heart that he hates it. Ibn Lahi`ah narrated on the authority of al-A`raj on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is not permissible for a believer to humiliate himself. They said: O Messenger of God, what is the reason for humiliating himself? He said: He is exposed to a calamity that he cannot bear. I said: Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Zaid bin Jud’an on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Jundub on the authority of Hudhayfah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and both of them spoke about it. It was narrated on the authority of some of the Companions that he said: “If a man sees an evil and is unable to denounce it, then let him say three times: O God, this is an evil. If he says that, then he has done what is required of him.” Ibn al-Arabi claimed that if someone hopes that it will go away and fears that changing it will result in beating or killing, then it is permissible for him, according to most scholars, to rush into it because of this uncertainty. But if he does not hope that it will go away, then what benefit is there in that? He said: What I have is that if the intention is sincere, then let him rush into it however it is and not care. I said: This is contrary to what Abu Omar mentioned about consensus. This verse indicates the permissibility of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong with fear of being killed. God Almighty said: And enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and be patient over what befalls you. This is an allusion to harm. Fifth: The Imams narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; and if he is not able to do so, then with his tongue; and if he is not able to do so, then with his heart - and that is the weakest of faith.” The scholars said: Enjoining what is right is for the rulers with their hands, and with their tongues is for the scholars, and with their hearts is for the weak, meaning the common people. So if the evil can be removed with the tongue of the one forbidding it, then let him do it. And if he is not able to do so except by punishment or killing, then let him do it. But if it is removed without killing, then killing is not permissible. This is based on the statement of God the Most High: Then fight against those who oppress until they return to the command of God. And upon this the scholars based that if someone repels an aggressor against a person or property from himself or his property or the life of another, then he may do so and nothing is upon him. If Zaid saw Amr intending to get a woman from Bakr, he must repel her if the owner of the money is not able to do so and is not satisfied with it. The scholars even said: If we assume retaliation, and it was said: Every town has four, its people are protected from calamity: a just leader who does not wrong, a scholar on the path of guidance, and sheikhs who command what is right and forbid what is wrong and encourage the pursuit of knowledge and the Qur’an. Their women are covered and do not display themselves like the display of the first days of ignorance. Sixth: Anas bin Malik narrated that it was said: O Messenger of God, when will we abandon enjoining good and forbidding evil? He said: When what appeared among the nations before you appears among you. We said: O Messenger of God, what appeared among the nations before us? He said: Kingship among your young, immorality among your old, and knowledge among your vices. Zaid said: The interpretation of the meaning of the Prophet's statement, and knowledge among your vices, is if knowledge is among the wicked. Narrated by Ibn Majah. This chapter will be further explained in Al-Ma'idah and elsewhere, God willing. The meaning of give them good tidings and it is lost was presented in Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it.
3:22: Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
3:23: There are three issues: First: Ibn Abbas said: This verse was revealed because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered the school house upon a group of Jews and called them to God. Nuaim bin Amr and Al-Harith bin Zaid said to him: What religion are you on, O Muhammad? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am on the religion of Abraham. They said: Abraham was a Jew. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Come to the Torah, for it is between us and you. But they refused, so the verse was revealed. Al-Naqqash mentioned that it was revealed because a group of Jews denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Come to the Torah, for it contains my description. But they refused. The majority read li-hakam and Abu Jaafar Yazid bin Al-Qaqa’ read li-hakam with a damma on the ya. The first reading is better, because God, the Most High, says: This is Our Book that speaks against you with the truth. Second: This verse is evidence that the one who is called must go to the ruler because he has been called to the Book of God. If he does not do so, he is a disobedient person and must be disciplined according to the degree of disobedience and disobedience. This ruling is applicable to us in Andalusia and the Maghreb, not in Egypt. This ruling that we have mentioned is explained in the revelation in Surat An-Nur in the words of God the Almighty: And when they are called to God and His Messenger to judge between them, at once a party of them turn away. to His words: Rather, it is those who are the wrongdoers. Az-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Whoever is called by his opponent to a Muslim ruler and he does not respond, then he is a wrongdoer and has no right. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is a false hadith. As for his saying he is a wrongdoer, this is a sound statement. As for his saying he has no right, this is not sound. It is possible that he means that he is not on the right path. Ibn Khuwayr Mandad Al-Maliki said: It is obligatory upon everyone who is called to the ruler’s council to respond unless he knows that the ruler is immoral, or knows that he is hostile to the plaintiff and the defendant. Third: It is evidence that the laws of those before us are our laws, except for what we know to be an abrogation, and that it is obligatory to rule by the laws of the prophets before us, as will be explained. We do not read the Torah or act according to what is in it because the one who has it in his hand is illiterate and has changed it and altered it. If we knew that nothing in it had changed or been altered, it would be permissible for us to read it. Something similar to this was narrated from Umar, when he said to Ka’b, If you know that it is the Torah that God sent down to Moses, son of Imran, then read it. He, peace be upon him, knew what had not been changed in it, so he called them to it and to rule by it. This will be explained in Al-Ma’idah and the reports that have been reported about it, God willing. It has been said that this verse was revealed about that. And God knows best.
3:24: A reference to turning away and aversion, and their deception in saying: We are the children of God and His beloved. And other than that of their sayings. The meaning of their saying: The Fire will not touch us has already been discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah.
3:25: Addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation, in a way that expresses surprise and amazement, i.e. how will their state be or what will they do when they are gathered on the Day of Resurrection and those adornments that they claimed in this world have vanished from them, and they are punished for what they acquired from their disbelief, their boldness, and their ugly deeds. The lam in His statement for the day means for, as Al-Kisa’i said. The Basrans said the meaning is for the reckoning of the Day. Al-Tabari: for what happens on the Day.
3:26: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God Almighty wanted to reveal the Opening of the Book, the Throne Verse, and God is witness, and Say, O God, Owner of the Kingdom, until His saying, without account, they clung to the Throne, and there was no veil between them and God, and they said, O Lord, bring us down to the abode of sins and upon those who disobey You. Then God Almighty said: By My glory and majesty, no servant reads them after every prescribed prayer except that I will make him dwell in the Sanctuary of Holiness, regardless of what he has done, and unless I look at him with My hidden eye seventy times every day, and unless I fulfill for him seventy needs every day, the least of which is forgiveness, and unless I protect him from every enemy and grant him victory over him, and nothing will prevent him from entering Paradise except that he dies." And the fight against Muadh ibn Jabal: One day I asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for forgiveness and did not pray the Friday prayer with him. He said: O Mu’adh, what prevented you from praying the Friday prayer? I said: O Messenger of God, Yuhanna ibn Bari’ah the Jew had gold on his time and he was watching me at my door, so I was afraid that he would detain me without you. He said: Do you want God to pay off your debt, O Mu’adh? I said: Yes. He said: “Say every day: ‘O God, Possessor of Sovereignty,’ until His saying: ‘Without account, Most Merciful of this world and the Hereafter, and Most Merciful of them. You give from them to whom You will and withhold from them from whom You will. Pay off my debt for me. Even if you had the earth full of gold on you, God would pay it off for you.” Narrated by Abu Nu’aym al-Hafiz, also on the authority of ‘Ata’ al-Khurasani, that Mu’adh ibn Jabal said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) taught me verses from the Qur’an, or words that no Muslim on earth supplicates with while he is distressed, in debt, or in debt, except that God will pay off his debt and relieve his concern. I was deprived from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he mentioned it. It is strange from the hadeeth of ‘Ata’ that he transmitted on the authority of Mu’adh. Ibn ‘Abbas and Anas ibn Malik said: When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) conquered Mecca and promised his nation the kingdom of Persia and Rome, the hypocrites and Jews said: “Far from it! How can Muhammad have the kingdom of Persia when Rome is more powerful and secure than that? Were not Mecca and Medina enough for Muhammad until he coveted the kingdom of Persia and Rome?” Then God revealed this verse. It was said: It was revealed to conclusively refute the falsehood of the Christians of Najran in their saying that Jesus is God. This is because these descriptions make it clear to every person of sound nature that Jesus is not in any of them. Ibn Ishaq said: God the Almighty made known in this verse their stubbornness and disbelief, and that even though God the Almighty gave Jesus (peace be upon him) signs that indicate his prophethood, such as reviving the dead and other things, God the Almighty is the only One who can do these things, from His saying: “You give the kingdom to whom You will and take the kingdom away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and abase whom You will.” And His saying: “You cause the night to enter the day and cause the day to enter the night. You bring the living out of the dead and bring the dead out of the living. And You provide for whom You will without account.” If Jesus was a god, this would have been his, and this would have been a consideration and a clear sign. The Almighty said: “Say: O God.” Grammarians differed in the construction of the word O God after their consensus that it has a damma on the ha’ and a shaddah on the open meem, and that it is a vocative. It came with a light meem in the saying of Al-A’sha: As a call from Abu Rabah, may God hear the great ones Al-Khalil, Sibawayh and all the Basrans said: The original form of Allahumma ya Allah, when the word was used without the vocative letter which is ya, they replaced it with this doubled meem, so they brought two letters, which are the two meems, instead of two letters, which are ya and alif, and the damma in the ha’ is the damma of the singular vocative noun. Al-Farra’ and the Kufians believed that the original form of Allahumma ya Allah is amna bi-khayr, so he deleted and mixed the two words, and that the damma in the ha’ is the damma that was in amna when the hamza was deleted, the movement was transferred. An-Nahhas said: This is a grave mistake according to the Basrans, and the statement about this is what Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said. Al-Zajjaj said: It is impossible to leave the damma, which is evidence of the singular vocative, and to put the damma of am in the name of God, this is blasphemy in the name of God. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is an exaggeration from Al-Zajjaj, and he claimed that he had never heard Ya God am, and the Arabs do not say Ya God. The Kufians said: The letter of vocative may enter God, and they recited on that the saying of Al-Zajir: Forgive or punish, O God last: And you don't have to say every time you glorify or praise God, Oh God, what? Return to us, our Sheikh, as a Muslim, for we will not be deprived of his goodness. last: Whenever I feel pain, I say, Oh God, oh God. They said: If the letter mim was a substitute for the letter of address, they would not have come together. Al-Zajjaj said: This is anomalous and its speaker is not known, and what was in the Book of God and in all the records of the Arabs should not be left to him. Something similar to it was mentioned in his saying: They both blew into my mouth from their mouths, and the barker howled louder. The Kufians said: The light meem is added in the words fam and ibnam, but the double meem is not added. Some grammarians said: What the Kufians said is wrong, because if it were as they said, it would have been necessary to say: O God and limit it to that because it is a supplication. Also, you might say: You are O God, the Provider. If it were as they claimed, then you would have separated the subject and the predicate with two sentences. An-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Whoever says O God has supplicated to God with all of His names. Al-Hasan said: O God, the supplication is combined. The Almighty said: Owner of the Kingdom: Qatada said: It has reached me that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked God Almighty to give his nation the kingdom of Persia, so God revealed this verse. Muqatil said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked God to give him the kingdom of Persia and the kingdom of Rome to his nation, so God Almighty taught him to supplicate with this supplication. Its meaning has been presented previously. Malik is in the accusative case according to Sibawayh as a second vocative, and similarly the saying of God Almighty: Say, O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth. According to him, it is not permissible to describe O God, because the letter meem has been added to it. Muhammad bin Yazid and Ibrahim bin al-Sarri al-Zajjaj disagreed with him and said: Malik in grammar is an attribute of the name of God Almighty, and so is Fater al-Samawat and the earth. Abu Ali said: This is the school of Abu al-Abbas al-Mubarrad, and what Sibawayh said is more correct and clearer, because there is nothing in the described names like O God, because it is a singular noun to which a sound has been added, and sounds are not described, such as ghaaq and the like. The rule of the singular noun is that it is not described, even though they have described it in places. So when what is not described is added here to what the standard is that it is not described, it becomes like a sound added to a sound, such as hayhil, so it is not described. And the kingdom here means prophecy, according to Mujahid. It was said: dominance. It was said: money and slaves. Al-Zajjaj: The meaning is the owner of the servants and what they own. It was said: The meaning is the owner of this world and the hereafter. The meaning of You give the kingdom is faith and Islam. Whom You will means whomever You will to give it to, and likewise what comes after it, and it is necessary to estimate the deletion, meaning and You take the kingdom away from whomever You will to take it away from, then this was deleted, and Sibawayh recited: Is there anyone in this world who can make excuses for people and do whatever he wants to people? Al-Zajjaj said: Whatever He wills to do to people, He does. And His saying: And You honor whomever You will. It is said: Honor if he is high, subdued, and overcomes. And from it, and honor me in speech. And You humiliate whomever You will. He humiliated, he humiliates, he humiliates if he overcomes, is high, and overpowers. Tarafa said: Slow to reveal, quick to betray, humiliated by all men, pampered. In Your Hand is good: meaning in Your Hand is good and evil, so it was deleted, as he said: Garments that protect you from the heat. It was said: Good was specified because it is a place of supplication and desire for its bounty. Al-Naqqash said: In Your Hand is good, meaning victory and spoils. The scholars of allusions said: Abu Jahl had a lot of money, and he fell into Al-Rass on the day of Badr, and the poor Suhaib, Bilal and Khabbab did not have money, and their kingdom was faith. Say: O God, Owner of the Kingdom, You give the kingdom to whom You will. You establish the Messenger, the orphan of Abu Talib, at the head of Al-Rass until he calls out, bodies that have turned to the well: O Utbah, O Shaybah, You honor whom You will and humiliate whom You will. That is, Suhaib, that is, Bilal, do not think that we prevented you from the world because of your hatred. In Your Hand is good. What prevented you from weakness Indeed, You are over all things competent. The bestowal of truth is general and takes care of whomever You will.
3:27: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Al-Suddi said about the meaning of His statement: He inserts the night into the day: the verse, meaning that He inserts what is missing from one into the other, until the day becomes fifteen hours, which is the longest, and the night becomes nine hours, which is the shortest, and likewise He inserts the day into al-Layl 92:this is the statement of Al-Kalbi, and it was narrated from Ibn Masoud. The wording of the verse may include the alternation of night and day, as the disappearance of one of them is the entry into the other. The commentators differed about the meaning of the statement of God the Almighty: And brings forth the living from the dead. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is that He brings forth the believer from the disbeliever and the disbeliever from the believer, and something similar was narrated from Salman Al-Farsi. Muammar narrated from Al-Zuhri that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon his wives and there was a woman with a beautiful appearance. He said: Who is this? They said, One of your aunts. He said, And who is she? They said, She is Khalidah bint al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Glory be to Him Who brings forth the living from the dead. She was a righteous woman and her father was an unbeliever. According to this opinion, what is meant is the death of the heart of the unbeliever and the life of the heart of the believer. Death and life are metaphors. Many scholars have said that life and death in the verse are two realities. Ikrimah said, It is bringing forth a living chicken from a dead egg, and bringing forth a dead egg from a living chicken. Ibn Mas`ud said, It is the sperm that comes out of a man while it is dead and he is alive, and the man comes out of it while it is dead. Ikrimah and al-Suddi said, "It is the seed that comes out of an ear of corn and the ear of corn comes out of the seed, and the pit from the date palm and the date palm comes out of the pit, and life in the date palm and the ear of corn is a simile. Then he said, "And You provide for whom You will without account." That is, without restriction or stinginess, as you say: So-and-so gives without calculation, as if he does not calculate what he gives.
3:28: There are two issues: First: Ibn Abbas said: God forbade the believers to be kind to the infidels and take them as allies, and similarly: Do not take as intimates those other than yourselves. And here comes the explanation of this meaning. And the meaning of He is not from God in anything is that he is not from the party of God nor from His allies in anything, like the village was asked. And Sibawayh narrated: He is from me two farsakhs, meaning from my companions and with me. Then he made an exception, which is: Second: He said: Except that you fear them with a fear. Muadh ibn Jabal and Mujahid said: Taqiyyah was in the beginning of Islam before the Muslims became strong, but today God has made Islam honorable that they fear their enemy. Ibn Abbas said: It is to speak with his tongue while his heart is at peace with faith, and he does not kill or commit any sin. Al-Hasan said: Taqiyyah is permissible for a person until the Day of Resurrection, and there is no taqiyyah in killing. Jabir ibn Zayd, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak read: Except that you fear them with a fear. It was said: If a believer is standing among the disbelievers, he may be gentle with them with his tongue if he fears for himself and his heart is at peace with faith. Taqiyyah is not permissible except with fear of being killed, amputated or greatly harmed. As for the one who is forced to disbelieve, the correct view is that he should be stubborn and not respond to uttering the word of disbelief, rather it is permissible for him as will be explained in An-Nahl, God willing. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i made taqah inflected, while the rest made it fatha. The root of taqah is waqiyah, with the weight of fa’lah, like ta’dah and thahmah. The waw was changed to a ta’ and the ya’ to an alif. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that this verse was revealed about Ubadah ibn As-Samit Al-Ansari, who was a pious Badri man and had an alliance with the Jews. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out on the Day of the Confederates, Ubadah said: O Prophet of God, I have five hundred Jewish men with me, and I have decided that they should go out with me so that I may use them to gain victory over the enemy. So God revealed: Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. The verse. It was said: It was revealed about Ammar bin Yasir when he spoke about some of what the polytheists wanted from him, as will be explained in An-Nahl. God the Almighty said: And God warns you of Himself. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, God warns you of Him. Then they dispensed with that with this and it became the used, God the Almighty said: You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in your soul. So its meaning is You know what I have and what is in my reality, and I do not know what you have or what is in your reality. Another said: The meaning is And God warns you of His punishment, like the village was asked. And he said: You know what is in my soul meaning my unseen, so the soul was made in the place of the implied because it is in it. And to God is the destination meaning and to God’s reward is the destination. And in it is an acknowledgment of the resurrection.
3:29: He is the Knower of what is hidden in the hearts and what they contain, and of what is in the heavens and the earth and what they contain. He is the Knower of the unseen. Not an atom's weight escapes Him, and nothing is hidden from Him. Glory be to Him. There is no god but Him. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed.
3:30: (Day) is an accusative connected to His statement: And God warns you of Himself. It was said that it is connected to His statement: And to God is the destination on the Day you find. It was said that it is connected to His statement: And God is over all things competent on the Day you find. It is permissible for it to be disconnected based on the implication of remember. And similar to it is His statement: Indeed, God is Exalted in Might, the Possessor of Retribution on the Day the earth will be changed and present is a state of the deleted pronoun from the connection of what, the meaning of which is on the Day every soul will find what it has done of good present. This is on the basis that you find from finding what was lost. And what from His statement: And what you have done of evil is in apposition to the first what. And you wish is in the place of the state of the second what. And if you make you find. meaning you learn, then present is the second object, and likewise you wish is in the place of the second object, the meaning of which is on the Day every soul will find the recompense for what it has done present. It is possible that the second ma is a subject in the nominative case, and tawd is in the nominative case because it is the best subject. It is not correct for ma to mean reward, because tawd is in the nominative case. If it were past, it would be possible for it to be a reward, and the meaning of the statement would be: And whatever evil you have done, I wish that there was a long distance between them and it, meaning like the distance between the east and the west. And the future, if you make ma for the condition, is only in the jussive mood, unless you assume that the fa has been deleted, based on the assumption that And whatever evil you have done, she wished. Abu Ali: This is the analogy of Al-Farra’s statement in my opinion, because he said in the verse of God Almighty: And if you obey them, then you are indeed polytheists, meaning that he was defeated previously. Al-Nabigha said: Except for someone like you or someone you are ahead of, the horse will outrun when it seizes the lead. Al-Amad: anger. It is said: Amad Amad if he became very angry.
3:31: Love: affection, and also love with the kasra. Love is also the beloved, like the cheek and the cheeks, it is said I loved him so he is a lover, and his love loves him with the kasra so he is beloved. Al-Jawhari said: This is anomalous, because it does not come in the doubled yaf'al with the kasra. Abu Al-Fath said: The origin of it is habba like a circumstance, so the ba was made quiescent and assimilated in the second. Ibn Al-Dahan Saeed said: In love there are two languages: love and I love, and the origin of love in this structure is habba like a circumstance, as indicated by their saying: I loved N and most of what is mentioned is fa'il from fa'l. Abu Al-Fath said: The indication of love is the Almighty's saying: He loves them and they love him. With the damma of the ya. And follow me, God will love you, and love is used for fa'l because they say habib. And for fa'l like their saying mahboob: The active participle of transitive love was not mentioned, so it is not said: I am love. And the passive participle of af'al was not mentioned except a little, like his saying: I am like a beloved and honored person Abu Zaid said: I loved him, I love him. And he recited: By God, if it weren’t for his dates, I wouldn’t have loved him, nor would he have been lower than Awif and Hashim. And he recited: By your life, I and the students of Egypt are yours, the ones who are increasingly distant from what they love. Al-Asma'i narrated the opening of the letter of the present tense with the letter Ya alone. And love is the Khabiyah, a Persian word that has been Arabized, and the plural is Habbab and Habbah, narrated by Al-Jawhari. The verse was revealed about the delegation of Najran when they claimed that what they claimed about Jesus was love for God Almighty, said Muhammad bin Ja'far bin Al-Zubayr. Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj said: It was revealed about a group of the People of the Book who said: We are the ones who love our Lord. It was narrated that the Muslims said: O Messenger of God, by God, we love our Lord, so God Almighty revealed: "Say: If you love God, then follow me." Ibn Arafa said: Love among the Arabs is the desire for something with intent. Al-Azhari said: The servant's love for God and His Messenger is his obedience to them and following their commands. God Almighty said: "Say: If you love God, then follow me." And God's love for His servants is His blessing them with forgiveness, God Almighty said: Indeed, God does not love the disbelievers. That is, He does not forgive them. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: The sign of loving God is loving the Qur’an, the sign of loving the Qur’an is loving the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the sign of loving the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the sign of loving the Sunnah, the sign of loving God, the Qur’an, the Prophet, and the Sunnah is loving the Hereafter, the sign of loving the Hereafter is to love oneself, the sign of loving oneself, the sign of loving oneself is to hate the world, the sign of hating the world is to take nothing from it except provisions and sustenance. Abu al-Darda’ narrated: On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the Almighty’s saying: “Say: If you love God, then follow me, and God will love you.” He said: On righteousness, piety, humility, and lowliness of soul. Narrated by Abu Abdullah al-Tirmidhi. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever wants God to love him must speak the truth, fulfill his trusts, and not harm his neighbor. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God loves a servant, He calls Gabriel and says, ‘I love so-and-so, so love him.’ Gabriel loves him, then he calls out in the heavens and says, ‘God loves so-and-so, so love him.’ The people of the heavens love him. Then acceptance is placed for him on earth. And when He hates a servant, He calls Gabriel and says, ‘I hate so-and-so, so hate him.’ Gabriel hates him, then he calls out to the people of the heavens, ‘God hates so-and-so, so hate him.’ They hate him, then hatred is placed for him on earth.” More explanation of this will come at the end of Surah Maryam, God willing. Abu Raja’ al-Attardi read, ‘Fat’abuni, with the opening of the ba’, and ‘Yafifiru lakum’ in apposition to ‘Yahibubukum. Mahbub narrated on the authority of Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ that he assimilated the ra’ of ‘min yaghfiru’ into the lam of ‘min lakum.’ An-Nahhas said, ‘Al-Khalil and Sibawayh do not permit assimilating the ra’ into the lam, and Abu Amr is too noble to make a mistake in such a matter, and perhaps he concealed the vowel as he does in many things.
3:32: The Almighty said: Say: Obey God and the Messenger. Its explanation will come in An-Nisa. But if they turn away. is a condition, except that it is a past tense verb that is not parsed. The meaning is: If they turn away in their disbelief and turn away from obeying God and His Messenger, then God does not like the disbelievers, meaning He is not pleased with their actions and does not forgive them, as mentioned above. And he said: then God and did not say then because when the Arabs magnify something, they mention it again. Sibawayh recited: I do not see death preceded by anything that made death bitter to the rich and the poor
3:33: The Almighty said: Indeed, God chose Adam and Noah. Chose means choose, and it was mentioned in Al-Baqarah. The derivation of Adam and his nickname were mentioned in it, and the meaning is that God chose their religion, which is the religion of Islam, so the complement was deleted. Al-Zajjaj said, He chose them for prophethood over the scholars of their time. And Nuh 71:It was said that it is derived from Naah, which is a foreign name, but it was declined because it has three letters, and he is the Sheikh of the Messengers, and the first Messenger whom God sent to the people of the earth after Adam, peace be upon him, by prohibiting daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, maternal aunts, and all other relatives. And whoever said that Idris was before him among the historians, then he made a mistake, as will be explained in Al-A'raf, God willing: God the Almighty said: And the family of Abraham and the family of Imran, over the worlds. The meaning of family and what it is used for is fully explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. In Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The family of Abraham and the family of Imran are the believers from the family of Abraham and the family of Imran and the family of Yasin and the family of Muhammad. God the Almighty says: Indeed, the people who have the closest claim to Abraham are those who followed him and this unlettered Prophet and those who have believed. And God is the ally of the believers. It was said: The family of Abraham are Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob and the Tribes, and that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is from the family of Abraham. It was said: The family of Abraham himself, and so is the family of Imran, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: And a remnant of what the family of Moses and the family of Aaron left behind. And in the hadith: He was given a flute from the Psalms of the House of David, and the poet said: Do not cry over a dead person after a dead person whom Ali, Abbas, and the family of Abu Bakr loved. Another said: He who remembers the family of Layla is met as a healthy person is met by a counter. He meant who remembered Layla herself. It was said: The family of Imran are the family of Abraham, as he said: Some descendants are from each other. It was said: What is meant is Jesus, because his mother is the daughter of Imran. It was said: himself, as we mentioned. Muqatil said: He is Imran, the father of Moses and Aaron, and he is Imran bin Yashar bin Fahath bin Lawi bin Jacob. Al-Kalbi said: He is Imran, the father of Mary, and he is from the descendants of Solomon, peace be upon him. Al-Suhayli narrated: Imran bin Matan, and his wife Hannah with a noon. These were mentioned specifically from among the prophets because the prophets and messengers, all of them, are from their descendants. Imran was not declined because at the end of it there is an extra alif and noon. The meaning of his saying: on the worlds is on the worlds of their time, according to the commentators. Al-Tirmidhi, the wise Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ali, said: All of creation, all of them. It was said: Over the worlds, over all of creation, all of them, until the Day of Judgment. This is because these are messengers and prophets, so they are the elite of creation. As for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his rank exceeded the chosen one because he is beloved and a mercy. God Almighty said: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds. So the messengers were created for mercy, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was created as mercy himself, so he became a security for creation, because when God sent him, creation was safe from torment until the blowing of the trumpet. The rest of the prophets did not occupy this position, so he, peace be upon him, said: I am a mercy sent down, and he chooses that he himself is a mercy to the creation from God. His saying sent down means a gift from God to the creation. It is said that He chose Adam with five things: The first is that He created him with His hand in the best form with His power, the second is that He taught him all the names, the third is that He ordered the angels to prostrate to him, the fourth is that He settled him in Paradise, and the fifth is that He made him the father of mankind. And He chose Noah with five things: The first is that He made him the father of mankind, because all people drowned and his descendants were the ones who remained, the second is that He prolonged his life, and it is said: Blessed is he who lives long and does good deeds. Third, his prayer was answered against the unbelievers and the believers. Fourth, he carried him on the ship. Fifth, he was the first to abrogate the laws, and before that he did not forbid marrying maternal and paternal aunts. And he chose Abraham for five things: First, he made him the father of the prophets, because it was narrated that a thousand prophets came from his loins from his time until the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Second, he took him as a close friend. Third, he saved him from the fire. Fourth, he made him an imam for the people. Fifth, he tested him with words and guided him until he completed them. Then he said: And the family of Imran. If Imran was the father of Moses and Aaron, then he chose them over the worlds when he sent manna and quails to his people, and that was not the case with any of the prophets in the world. And if he was the father of Mary, then he chose Mary for him by giving birth to Jesus without a father, and that was not the case with anyone in the world. And God knows best.
3:34: The meaning of offspring and its derivation are presented in Al-Baqarah. It is an accusative of state, said Al-Akhfash, meaning in the case of some of them being from others, meaning offspring are children of some. The Kufians: on the cut-off.
