Al-Zajjaj: a substitute, meaning He chose offspring, some from others, and the meaning of some from others, meaning in supporting each other in religion, as he said: The hypocrites, men and women, are from each other. Meaning in misguidance, said Al-Hasan and Qatadah. It was said: in selection, choice, and prophethood. And say: what is meant by it is procreation, and this is the weakest of them.
3:35: It contains eight issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: When the wife of Imran said: Abu Ubaidah said: When is redundant. Muhammad bin Yazid said: The meaning is remember when. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is He chose the family of Imran when the wife of Imran said. She is Hannah with a silent ha and a noon, the daughter of Faqud bin Qanbal, the mother of Mary, the grandmother of Jesus, peace be upon him. It is not an Arabic name and Hannah is not known in Arabic as a woman’s name. In Arabic, Hannah is called Abu Habba al-Badri, and it is said about him: Abu Habba with one ba, which is more correct. His name is Amer, and the monastery of Hannah is in the Levant, and there is another monastery also called that. Abu Nuwas said: Oh, Deir Hanna, from the same vineyards, who will tell you about me, for I am not sane? There are many Habbahs among the Arabs, including Abu Habbah al-Ansari, and Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba’kak who is mentioned in the hadith of Subai’ah Habbah. Khannah with the voiced kha’ is not known except as the daughter of Yahya ibn Aktham al-Qadi, and she is the mother of Muhammad ibn Nasr. Jannah with the voiced jim is not known except as Abu Jannah, and he is the maternal uncle of Dhu al-Rummah the poet. All of this is from the book of Ibn Makula. Second: The Almighty’s saying: My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated to Your service. The meaning of vow was mentioned earlier, and that the servant is not bound unless he commits himself to it. It is said that when she became pregnant, she said: If God saves me and I give birth to what is in my womb, I will make it dedicated to Your service. The meaning of to You is for Your worship. The word muharran is in the accusative case as a state, and it was said: It is an adjective for a deleted object, meaning, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, a freed boy. The first is more appropriate in terms of interpretation, context, and syntax. As for syntax, the placement of the adjective in place of the described is not permissible in some places, but it is permissible as a metaphor in others. As for the interpretation, it was said that the reason for what Imran’s wife said was that she was old and could not give birth, and they were a household with a place from God, and that she was under a tree and saw a bird cooing its chicks, so her soul moved because of that, and she called upon her Lord to grant it a son, and she vowed that if she gave birth, she would make her son a muhassir, meaning, freed and devoted to God Almighty, serving the church, confined to it, and devoted to the worship of God Almighty. That was permissible in their law, and their children were required to obey them. So when Mary gave birth, she said: My Lord, I have given birth to a female, meaning that a female is not fit to serve the church. It was said: Because of the menstruation and harm that befalls her. It was also said: She is not fit to mix with men. She hoped it would be a boy, so she was set free. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: There is no disagreement that the wife of Imran is not subject to a vow because she is free. If his wife was his mother, there is no disagreement that a man’s vow regarding his child is not valid, regardless of his circumstances. If the one making the vow is a slave, his word regarding that is not established for him. If he is free, it is not valid for him to be his slave. Likewise, the woman is the same: So what is the point of the vow regarding that? Rather, its meaning, and God knows best, is that a man only wants his child to be familiar with him, to seek support and consolation. So this woman sought the child to be familiar with him and to find peace with him. So when God Almighty bestowed him upon her, she vowed that her share of familiarity with him would be left to him, and he would be suspended for the service of God Almighty. This is the vow of the free and righteous. She meant by him someone who is free from my side, someone who is free from the slavery of the world and its occupations. A Sufi man said to a slave: O slave, leave me to God so that I may worship Him and learn knowledge. She said: Yes. So he walked until she could see, then he returned to her and knocked on the door. She said: Who? He said to her: Your son is so-and-so. She said: We have left you to God and will not return to you. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Freed is taken from freedom, which is the opposite of slavery. From this is the liberation of the book, which is its deliverance from disorder and corruption. Khasif narrated on the authority of Ikrimah and Mujahid: That the one who is freed is purely for God Almighty and is not tainted by anything of worldly affairs. This is well-known in the language that everything that is pure is called: free, and freed in its meaning. Dhu al-Rummah said: The earring is hanging in the free hart of Dhafra, the rope is far from it, so it is trembling Free clay with no sand in it, and so-and-so spent a free night if her husband did not reach her the first night, but if he was able to reach her, then it was a gray night.
3:36: Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And when she delivered her, she said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female.’ Ibn Abbas said: She only said this because vows to males were not accepted, so God accepted Mary. Female is a state, or if you wish, an alternative. It was said: She raised her until she grew up and then sent her out, narrated by Ashab from Malik. It was also said: She wrapped her in her rag and sent her to the mosque, so she fulfilled her vow and disowned her. Perhaps the veil was not with them as it was in the early days of Islam, as in Bukhari and Muslim: A black woman used to clean the mosque during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then she died. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And God knows best what she delivered is according to the reading of those who read wada with a damma on the ta’ as part of her speech, so the speech is connected. It is the reading of Abu Bakr and Ibn Amir, and in it is the meaning of submission to God, obedience and glorification of Him that nothing is hidden from Him. She did not say it as a way of informing because knowledge of everything is established in the soul of the believer, but rather she said it as a way of glorifying and glorifying God the Almighty. According to the readings of the majority, it is from both God the Almighty and Majestic, presented, and its estimation is that it is delayed after And I seek refuge for her in You and her offspring from Satan, the accursed. And God knows best what she delivered, said Al-Mahdawi. Makki said: It is an announcement from God the Almighty to us as a way of confirmation, so He said: And God knows best what Mary’s mother delivered, whether she said it or not. This is strengthened by the fact that if it was from the speech of Mary’s mother, the meaning of the speech would be: And You know best what she delivered, because she called out to Him at the beginning of the speech in her saying: My Lord, I have delivered a female. And it was narrated from Ibn Abbas that what she delivered with a kasra on the ta’, meaning this was said to her. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And the male is not like the female. Some Shafi’is used it as evidence that a woman who consents to her husband having intercourse during the day in Ramadan is not equal to him in the obligation of expiation upon her. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is an oversight on his part, for this is better than the law of those before us, and they do not say it. And this prayer was intended by her words as is attested to by the evidence of his condition and the end of her words, for she vowed to serve the mosque for her child, but when she saw that he was a female who was not fit and that he was an ‘awrah, she apologized to her Lord for his presence for her contrary to what she intended for her. And Maryam was not declined because it is a definite feminine, and it is also foreign, al-Nahhas said. And God knows best. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And indeed, I have named her Mary means servant of the Lord in their language. And indeed, I seek refuge for her with You meaning Mary. And her offspring meaning Jesus. This indicates that offspring may refer specifically to a child. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No child is born except that Satan pokes him and he cries out from the poking of Satan, except the son of Mary and his mother. Then Abu Hurairah said: Read if you wish: And indeed, I seek refuge for her with You and for her offspring from Satan, the accursed. Our scholars said: This hadith indicates that God, the Almighty, answered the supplication of Mary’s mother, for Satan pokes all of Adam’s children, even the prophets and saints, except Mary and her son. Qatada said: Every newborn is stabbed in the side by Satan when he is born, except for Jesus and his mother. A veil was placed between them, and the stab hit the veil and nothing of it reached them. Our scholars said: If that were not the case, then the special relationship between them would be invalidated. This does not necessarily mean that Satan’s stabbing leads the possessed person astray and misleads him, for that is a corrupt assumption. Satan has exposed prophets and saints to various types of corruption and misleading, and despite that, God protected them from what Satan seeks, as He, the Most High, said: Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority. This is despite the fact that each one of the children of Adam has been assigned a companion from the devils, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And Mary and her son, although they were protected from his stabbing, were not protected from his constant presence and company. And God knows best.
3:37: The Almighty said: So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance. The meaning is: He made her follow the path of the happy ones, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Some people said: The meaning of acceptance is taking care of her upbringing and looking after her. Al-Hasan said: The meaning of acceptance is that He did not torment her for a single hour of the night or day. And caused her to grow with good growth means He made her creation perfect, without any increase or decrease, so she would grow in one day what a newborn grows in one year. Acceptance and growth are two sources of different meanings, and the root is acceptance and growth. The poet said: I am ungrateful after death has been turned away from me and after you have given me a hundred thousand dirhams. He wanted to give it to you, but when he said it grew, he indicated it grew, as Imru’ al-Qais said: So we reached the best, and our words were soft and she was satisfied, so she showed difficulty, meaning humiliation. The source of humiliation is humiliation, but he returned it to the meaning of humiliated, and so is everything that comes to you in this chapter. So the meaning of accept and accept is one, so the meaning is that her Lord accepted her with a good acceptance. Similar to it is the saying of Ru’bah: It was folded like a thorn. The snake because the meaning of tawtaywat and tawtaywat are the same, and similar to it is the saying of Al-Qatami: The best thing is what you receive from it, not what you follow. Because you followed and you followed are one. And in the reading of Ibn Masoud, And He sent down the angels a revelation because the meaning of He sent down and He sent down is one. Al-Mufaddal said: Its meaning is And He caused it to grow, so it grew a good growth. And taking the meaning into account is more appropriate, as we mentioned. The original form of acceptance is the damma, because it is a verbal noun like entrance and exit, and the fatha came in a few letters, like wil’u and wazu’, these three and no more, Abu Amr, Al-Kisa’i, and the Imams said. Al-Zajjaj permitted acceptance with the damma of the qaf according to the original form. God the Almighty said: And Zakariya took her under his care. That is, he took her into his care. Abu Ubaidah said: He took care of her. The Kufians read wa-kafalaha with a shaddah, so it is transitive with two objects, and the meaning is wa-kafalaha Rabbi Zakariya, meaning He obligated him to take care of her, decreed that for him, and made it easy for him. In the Mushaf of Abu, it is wa-akfalaha and the hamza is like the shaddah in the transitive, and also if he accepted it, then he accepted it, and caused it to grow, then God informed about Himself what He did with her, so wa-kafalaha came with a shaddah on that, and the rest of them lightened it by attributing the action to Zakariya. So God the Almighty informed that He is the one who took care of her and took care of her, as indicated by His statement: Which of them will take care of Mary? Makki said: This is the preferred choice, because the shaddah goes back to the lightening, because God the Almighty, when Zakariya took care of her, He took care of her by the command of God, and because when Zakariya took care of her, he did the will and power of God, so on that basis the two readings are intertwined. Amr bin Musa narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer and Abu Abdullah Al-Muzani, and Kaffalaha with a kasra on the fa. Al-Akhfash said: It is said kafala yakful and kaffala yakful, but I did not hear kafala, and it has been mentioned. Mujahid read fataqbalha with a sukoon on the lam as a question and request. Rabha with the accusative as a vocative complement. Anbatha with a sukoon on the ta and Kaffalaha with a sukoon on the lam Zakariya with extension and the accusative. Hafs, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read Zakariya without extension or hamza, and the rest extended it and hamzated it. Al-Farra’ said: The people of Hijaz extend Zakariya and shorten it, and the people of Najd delete the alif from it and decline it and say: Zakariya. Al-Akhfash said: There are four languages: extension and shortening, Zakariya with a shaddah on the ya and the decline, and Zakara and I saw Zakariya. Abu Hatim said: Zakariya is not declined because it is foreign, and this is a mistake, because what was in it was like ya like this was declined like kursi and Yahya, and Zakariya was not declined in the long and short form because it has an alif of femininity, foreignness, and definiteness. God Almighty says: Whenever Zechariah entered the sanctuary to her, he found provision with her until His saying: Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication. There are four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Whenever Zakariya entered upon her in the sanctuary. The sanctuary in the language is the most honorable place in the assembly. More clarification will come for it in Surat Maryam. It was mentioned in al-Naba 78:She was in a room that Zakariya used to ascend to by a ladder. Waddah Al-Yaman said: The mihrab of the sanctuary, if I come to her, I will not meet her until I climb the stairs Any mistress of the room. Abu Saleh narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Imran’s wife became pregnant after she had grown old, so she vowed to set what was in her womb free. Imran said to her: Woe to you, what have you done? Have you seen if it is a girl? They were both saddened by that. Imran died and Hannah was pregnant, so she gave birth to a girl, and God accepted her with a good acceptance. Only boys were freed, so the rabbis contributed pens with which they wrote the revelation, as will come. Zachariah took care of her and took a place for her. When she grew old, he made a niche for her that could only be climbed by a ladder. He hired a wet nurse for her and locked the door behind her. No one entered upon her except Zachariah until she grew old. When she menstruated, he would take her out to his house and she would be with her aunt. Her aunt was Zachariah’s wife, according to Al-Kalbi. Muqatil said: Her sister was Zachariah’s wife, and when she purified herself from her menstruation and bathed, he would return her to the niche. Some of them said: She did not menstruate and was pure from menstruation. Whenever Zachariah entered upon her, he would find with her winter fruits in the summer and summer fruits in the winter. He said, O Mary, where did you get this? She said, It is from God. At that point, Zachariah desired a child and said, He who brings this to her is able to provide me with a child. The meaning of from where, Abu Ubaidah said. An-Nahhas said: This is lenient, because from where is a question about places, and from where is a question about doctrine and directions. The meaning is, from which doctrine and from which direction did you get this? Al-Kumait differentiated between them, saying: Where and how can I weep with joy, without passion or doubt? And whenever it is accusative with wajd, meaning every entrance. Indeed, God provides for whomever He wills without account. It was said: It is from the words of Mary, and it is possible that it is a new sentence, so that was the reason for Zachariah’s supplication and his request for a son.
3:38: The second: The Almighty’s saying: There Zakariya called upon his Lord. There is in the accusative case, because it is an adverb used for time and place, and its origin is for place. Al-Mufaddal bin Salamah said: There is in time and there is in place, and this may be made in place of this. And grant me means give me, from You means from You. Good offspring means righteous offspring. Offspring can be one and can be a plural, male and female, and here it is one. This is indicated by His saying: Then grant me from Yourself a protector, and He did not say protectors, but rather He made good feminine because the word offspring is feminine, like His saying: Your father is a caliph born of another, and you are the caliph of that perfection. So his offspring was a female, and he gave birth to the word caliph. It was narrated from the hadith of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Any man who dies and leaves behind good offspring, God will reward him like their deeds and will not diminish anything from their reward. The derivation of offspring has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Good means righteous and blessed. You are the Hearer of supplication means receptive, and from this: God hears whoever praises Him. Third: This verse indicates the desire for a child, which is the way of the Messengers and the Truthful. God the Almighty said: And We have certainly sent messengers before you, and made for them wives and offspring. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, he said: Uthman wanted to be a celibate woman, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade him. If he had permitted him to do so, we would have been singled out. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Aisha that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Marriage is from my Sunnah, so whoever does not act upon my Sunnah is not from me. And marry, for I will outnumber the nations with you. And whoever has the means, let him marry, and whoever does not have the means, let him fast, for it will be a restraint for him.” This is a response to some ignorant Sufis who said: The one who seeks a child is foolish, and he did not know that he is the stupid, foolish one. God the Almighty said, informing us about Abraham the Friend: And grant me a reputation of truth among later generations. And He said: And those who say, ‘Our Lord, grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes.’ Al-Bukhari has included a chapter on seeking a child in this regard. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Abu Talha when he married his son: Did you get married last night? He said: Yes. He said: May God bless you both in the coming night. He said: So I became pregnant. In Al-Bukhari: Sufyan said: A man from the Ansar said: I saw nine children, all of whom had recited the Qur’an. He also included a chapter on supplication for many children with blessings, and he cited the hadith of Anas ibn Malik who said: Umm Sulaym said: O Messenger of God, your servant Anas, supplicate to God for him. He said: O God, increase his wealth and children and bless what You have given him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: O God, forgive Abu Salamah and raise his status among the guided ones, and replace him with his descendants among those who come after. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) also said: Marry a loving child, for I will outnumber the nations through you. Narrated by Abu Dawud. There are many hadiths with this meaning that encourage seeking a child and encourage it, because of the benefit that a person hopes for in his life and after his death. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When one of you dies, his deeds come to an end except for three things. Then he mentioned, or a righteous child who prays for him. If there were only this hadith, it would have been sufficient. Fourth: If this is proven, then it is obligatory for a person to supplicate to his Creator to guide his son and wife by granting them success, guidance, righteousness, chastity, and care, and that they be a help to him in his religion and his worldly life so that his benefit from them will be great in the first and last days. Do you not see the words of Zachariah, And make him, my Lord, pleasing, and he said, Good offspring, and he said, And grant us from among our wives and offspring comfort to our eyes. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, supplicated for Anas, saying: O God, increase his wealth and children and bless him in them. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. That is enough for you.
3:39: The Almighty said: And the angels called him Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read Fanadah with an alif for the masculine, and they pronounce it with a fat-ha because its root is a ya', and because it is the fourth letter. The alif is the reading of Ibn 'Abtas and Ibn Mas'ud, and it is the choice of Abu Ubaid. It was narrated on the authority of Jarir on the authority of Mughirah on the authority of Ibrahim who said: Abdullah used to mention the angels throughout the Qur'an. Abu Ubaidah said: We see that he chose that in opposition to the polytheists because they said: The angels are the daughters of God. An-Nahhas said: This is an argument that does not achieve anything, because the Arabs say: The men said, and the men said, and so do the women. How can one argue against them with the Qur'an? If it were permissible to argue against them with this from the Qur'an, then it would be permissible for them to argue with the Almighty's statement: And when the angels said, but the argument against them is in the Almighty's statement: Bear witness to their creation meaning they did not witness, so how can they say that they are females? It is known that this is conjecture and desire. As for his calling out, it is permissible for the masculine plural and his calling out for the feminine plural. Makki said: The angels are among those who have reason in the broken form, so they are treated in the feminine form as something that does not have reason. You say: she is the men, she is the trunks, she is the camels, and the Bedouins said. This is strengthened by his statement: And when the angels said, and it was mentioned in another place, saying: And the angels stretched out their hands, and this is a consensus. And God Almighty said: And the angels will enter upon them from every gate. The feminine and masculine of this plural are both good. Al-Suddi said: Gabriel alone called him, and this is also the reading of Ibn Mas'ud. In the revelation: He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command, meaning Gabriel, and the Spirit is the revelation. It is permissible in Arabic to describe one person by the plural. It is stated in the revelation: Those to whom the people said, meaning Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud, as will come. It was said: All the angels called him, and this is more apparent. That is, the call came from them. The Almighty said: And he was standing praying in the sanctuary, that God gives you good tidings. "Standing is the subject and predicate of praying" in the nominative case, and if you wish, it is accusative as a state of the implied subject. "Bin God" means that God. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read "Inna" meaning she said that God, so the call means saying. "Bishrishk" with emphasis is the reading of the people of Madinah. Hamzah read "Bishrishk" without emphasis, as did Hamid ibn Al-Qays Al-Makki, except that he broke the shin, added a damma to the ya', and softened the ba'. Al-Akhfash said: They are three languages with one meaning. The evidence for the first is the reading of the group, that what is in the Qur’an of this from a past tense verb or a command is with emphasis, like the Almighty’s saying: So give good tidings to My servants. “So give him good tidings of forgiveness.” So We gave her good tidings of Isaac. “They said, We have given you good tidings of the truth.” As for the second, which is the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud, it is Bishara yubashir, and it is the language of Tihamah, and from it is the saying of the poet: I gave my children good report if you saw a letter from Al-Hajjaj being read. Another said: And if you see those who are looking forward to the dew, their hands are covered with dust in a barren valley. So help them and give them the good report they have been given. And if they are in distress, then come down. The third is from absher yabsher ibsharan which means: O Umm Amr, be glad with the good report, a terrible death and a great locust God the Almighty said: "By Yahya" His name in the first book was Hayy, and the name of Sarah, the wife of Abraham, peace be upon him, was Yasara, and its interpretation in Arabic is that she does not give birth, so when she was given the good report of Isaac, she was told: Sarah, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, named her that. She said: O Abraham, why did we omit a letter from my name? Abraham said that to Gabriel, peace be upon them both, and he said: That letter was added to the name of their son, one of the best of the prophets, whose name was Hayy, and he was named Yahya. Al-Naqqash mentioned it. Qatada said: He was named Yahya because God the Almighty revived him with faith and prophethood. Some of them said: He was named that because God the Almighty revived people with guidance through him. Muqatil said: His name was derived from God's name Hayy, so he was named Yahya. It was also said: Because the womb of a nation was revived through him. "Confirming a word from God" means Jesus according to most commentators. Jesus was called a word because he was by the word of God, which is "Be" and he was, without a father. Abu Al-Samal Al-Adawi read it as a word with a broken kaf and a silent lam throughout the Quran, and it is an eloquent language like shoulder and thigh. It was said: He was called a word because people are guided by him as they are guided by the word of God. Abu Ubaid said: The meaning of "by a word from God" is a book from God. He said: The Arabs say "recite to me a word" meaning a poem, as it was narrated that Al-Huwaidara mentioned Hassan and said: May God curse his word, meaning his poem. Other sayings were said. The first saying is more famous and most scholars agree with it. John was the first to believe in Jesus, peace be upon them, and he believed in him. John was older than Jesus by three years, and it is said by six months. He was the son of a maternal uncle, so when Zakariya heard his testimony, he went to Jesus and hugged him while he was in his rag. Al-Tabari mentioned that when Mary became pregnant with Jesus, her sister also became pregnant with John. Her sister came to visit and said: O Mary, do you know that I am pregnant? Mary said to her: Do you know that I am pregnant? She said to her: And I feel that which is in my womb prostrating to that which is in your womb. And that is because it was narrated that she felt her fetus coming out with its head towards Mary’s womb. Al-Suddi said: That is what he said, Confirming a word from God, and confirming is in the accusative case as a state. And master is the one who rules his people and is the last to his word. Its root is sayyud, it is said: so-and-so, aswad from so-and-so, a noun of action from the word of sovereignty. So it indicates that it is permissible to call a person a master, just as it is permissible to call him a noble or generous person. Likewise, it was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said to Banu Qurayzah: Rise up to your master. In Bukhari and Muslim, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about Al-Hasan: This son of mine is a master, and perhaps God will reconcile two great groups of Muslims through him. And so it was, for when Ali, may God be pleased with him, was killed, more than forty thousand pledged allegiance to him, as did many of those who had stayed behind from his father and who had broken their pledge of allegiance. He remained as caliph in Iraq and the rest of Khorasan for about seven months. Then he marched to Muawiyah with the people of Hijaz and Iraq, and Muawiyah marched to him with the people of Ash-Sham. When the two armies saw each other in a place called Maskan in the land of Sawad in the Anbar region, Al-Hasan hated fighting because he knew that one of the two groups would not prevail until most of the other was destroyed, and the Muslims would perish. So he handed over the matter to Muawiyah on the condition that he would be the master after Muawiyah. Muawiyah committed to all of that, and his words, may God bless him and grant him peace, were true: This son of mine is a master, and there is no one blacker than those whom God Almighty and His Messenger have made black. Qatada said about God Almighty’s statement, and a master, he said: in knowledge and worship. Ibn Jubayr and Ad-Dahhak: in knowledge and piety. Mujahid: the noble master. Ibn Zayd: The one who is not overcome by anger. Al-Zajjaj said: The master is the one who surpasses his peers in every good thing. This is comprehensive. Al-Kisa’i said: The master is the old goat. In the hadith: A two-year-old sheep is better than a master goat. He said: Whether he has a sheep that he has brought close to slaughtering for a guest or a sheep that he has brought to slaughter for a master "Hasuran is derived from the word hasr" which means confinement. Something confined me or imprisoned me if it detained me. Ibn Mayada said: Laila did not abandon you because she was distant from you, nor because she was busy with things. A she-camel with a narrow urethra. A she-camel with a narrow urethra is one who does not come to women as if he is refraining from them, just as it is said: a man with a narrow urethra and a tight urethra if he holds back his provisions and does not bring out what the drinking companions bring out. It is said that the people drank and so-and-so was stingy with them, meaning he was stingy, on the authority of Abu Amr. Al-Akhtal said: And a drinker who wins the cup, make me regret neither the presence nor the bracelet In the revelation: And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers. That is, a confinement. The prison is the property because it is veiled. Labid said: And the garbage has overcome the necks as if they were jinn standing at the door of the mat Yahya, peace be upon him, was chaste. Fa’ul means maf’ul, he does not come to women, as if he was forbidden from what is done to men, according to Ibn Mas’ud and others. Fa’ul means maf’ul frequently in the language, including haluub meaning milked. The poet said: It has forty-two black, milky ewes, as dark as a raven's tail. Ibn Masoud also said, as did Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, Ata, Abu al-Shatha, al-Hasan, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd: He is the one who refrains from women and does not approach them even though he is able to. This is the most correct of the sayings for two reasons: First, it is praise and commendation of him, and praise is usually for an acquired action and not for one’s nature. Second, fa’ul in the language is one of the forms of fa’ilun, as he said: The sword's blade strikes the market with its fat, if they lack provisions, then you are barren. The meaning is that he restrains himself from desires. Perhaps this was his law, but our law is marriage, as mentioned above. It was said: The chaste is the impotent man who has no penis that enables him to have sex and does not ejaculate, also from Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Ad-Dahhak. Abu Salih narrated from Abu Hurairah who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Every son of Adam will meet God with a sin he has committed. He will punish him for it if He wills or have mercy on him, except for John, son of Zakariya, for he was a master, chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous.” Then the Prophet reached with his hand to a speck of earth, picked it up and said: His penis was like this speck. It was said: Its meaning is the one who guards himself from the sins of God Almighty. And a prophet from among the righteous. Az-Zajjaj said: The righteous is the one who fulfills what is required of him and fulfills the rights of the people.
3:40: It was said: The Lord here is Gabriel, meaning he said to Gabriel: Lord, meaning my master, how can I have a boy, meaning a son? This is the saying of Al-Kalbi. Some of them said: His saying Lord means God Almighty. And how means how, and it is in the accusative case as an adverb. There are two meanings for the meaning of this question: The first is that he asked if he would have a child while he and his wife were in the same condition or would they return to the condition of someone who gives birth? The second asked if he would be blessed with a child from his barren wife or from someone else. It was said: The meaning is by what status do I deserve this while I and my wife are in this condition, in a humble manner. It is narrated that there were forty years between his supplication and the time when he would be given the good report, and on the day of the good report he was ninety years old and his wife was close in age to him. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: Bishr was one hundred and twenty years old on the day of his death, and his wife was ninety-eight years old. That is why he said, And my wife is barren, meaning sterile and cannot give birth. It is said: a barren man and a barren woman, whose barrenness is evident. And ‘aqarah’ and ‘aqarah with a damma on the qaf in both of them, ‘ta’aqar ‘aqarah became ‘aqar, like hasanat ‘tahsan ‘hasanah’ from Abu Zaid. And ‘aqara’ also. The active parts of the verb fa’ala are verbal, it is said: ‘azamat’ so she is ‘azaima’, and ‘zarafat’ so she is ‘zarifah’. And it is only said ‘aqarah’ because it is intended to mean one who has ‘aqarah’ by lineage. If it were by action, he would have said: ‘aqarat’ so she is ‘aqira’ as if she has ‘aqarah’, meaning old age that prevents her from having children. ‘aqarah’ is the great sand dune that does not grow anything. ‘aqarah’ is also the dowry of a woman if she steps on a sapling. And the egg of ‘aqar’: they claim it is the egg of a rooster, because it lays one egg in its lifetime until it is long. And the ‘aqarah of fire’ is also its middle and most of it. Aqar al-Hawd: its backside where camels stop when they come in. It is said: Aqar and Aqar, like ‘Usr and ‘Usr, and all of them are Aqar, so it is a common word. The Kaf in his saying likewise is in the accusative case, meaning God does what He wills like that. The boy is derived from the word ghulmah which is the intense desire for marriage. The stallion became agitated with the desire to mate. Layla al-Akhiliya said: He cured her of the incurable disease that a young man had, if he shook the canal he would give her water to drink. The drunk, flighty young man. He is between ghulumah and ghulumiyah, and the plural is ghulamah and ghulman. It is said that ghaylam is a young man and a young girl as well. Ghaylam is the male turtle. Ghail is a place. The sea became turbulent and its waves clashed.
3:41: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: My Lord, make for me a sign. Here, make means make because it takes two objects. For me is in the position of the second object. When he was given the good report of a son and this was not far-fetched to him regarding the power of God, the Almighty, he asked for a sign, that is, a mark by which he would know the truth of this matter and that it was from God, the Almighty. So God punished him by making him silent about people’s speech because he asked for the sign after the angels had spoken to him, as most of the commentators said. They said: And likewise, if it was not due to a disease that made him mute or something similar, then in any case there is a punishment for it. Ibn Zayd said: When Zakariya’s wife became pregnant with John, he was no longer able to speak to anyone, and despite that, he would read the Torah and remember God, the Almighty. But if he wanted to speak to someone, he could not do so. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Except for a sign. In the language, a sign is a gesture with the lips, and it may be used to gesture with the eyebrows, eyes, and hands. Its origin is movement. It was said: The request for that sign is to increase reassurance. The meaning: Complete the blessing by making a sign for me, and that sign is an increase in blessing and honor. So it was said to him: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days, meaning that you will be prevented from speaking for three nights. The evidence for this statement is the Almighty’s saying after the angels gave him the good report: And I created you before, when you were nothing, meaning that I brought you into existence with My power, so I will bring you forth a child. An-Nahhas chose this statement and said: Qatada’s statement that Zachariah was punished by not speaking is undesirable, because God Almighty did not inform us that he had sinned, nor that He forbade him from doing so. The statement in it is that the meaning is to make for me a sign that indicates the existence of a child, since that was hidden from me. And a sign is the accusative of the discontinuous exception, as Al-Akhfash said. Al-Kisa’i said: A symbol symbolizes and a symbol. It is read illa razā with a fathah on the mīm and rāmzā with a damma on the mīm and a damma on the ra’, the singular is rāmzā. Third: This verse is evidence that gestures are considered as speech, and this is found in many of the Sunnahs. The most emphatic of gestures is what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ruled regarding the black woman when he said to her: Where is God? She pointed to the sky, so he said: Free her, for she is a believer. Thus, Islam was permitted by gestures, which is the basis of the religion that protects blood and wealth, and by which one deserves Paradise and is saved from the Fire. He ruled that she is a believer, just as he ruled by the speech of the one who says that. So gestures must be effective in all aspects of the religion, and this is the opinion of most jurists. Ibn al-Qasim narrated from Malik that if a mute gestures with a divorce, then it is binding upon him. Al-Shafi’i said about a man who falls ill and his tongue becomes slurred, then he is like a mute with regard to taking back a wife and divorce. Abu Hanifa said: This is permissible if his gesture is known, but if there is doubt about it, then it is invalid. This is not by analogy, but rather by preference. The analogy in all of this is that it is invalid, because he does not speak and his gesture is not understood. Abu al-Hasan ibn Battaal said: Abu Hanifa was prompted to say this because he did not know the Sunnahs that permitted gestures in various religious rulings. Perhaps al-Bukhari tried to refute him by translating the chapter on gestures in divorce and other matters. Ata’ said: What he meant by his statement not to speak to people was fasting for three days. When they fasted, they would only speak in symbols. This is far-fetched. And God knows best. Fourth: Some of those who permit the abrogation of the Qur’an by the Sunnah said: Zakariya, peace be upon him, was prevented from speaking even though he was able to do so, and that it was abrogated by his saying, peace be upon him: Do not fast one day until night. Most scholars are of the opinion that it was not abrogated, and that Zakariya was only prevented from speaking because of a defect that entered him and prevented him from doing so, and that defect is the inability to speak while being healthy. This is what the commentators said. Many scholars are of the opinion that: Do not fast one day until night only means about the remembrance of God. As for idle talk and what is of no benefit, then silence about that is good. God the Almighty said: And remember your Lord much and glorify Him in the evening and the morning. He ordered him not to abandon remembrance in his soul even if his tongue was tied, according to the first opinion. The meaning of remembrance has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurti said: If anyone were permitted to abandon remembrance, he would have permitted it to Zachariah based on God’s statement: “Do not speak to people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much.” And he would have permitted a man who is in war based on God’s statement: When you meet a company, stand firm and remember God much. At-Tabari mentioned it. And glorify means pray. Prayer was called a glorification because it contains the glorification of God the Almighty from evil. In the evening is the plural of evening, and it was said that it is one. This is from the time the sun declines until it sets, according to Mujahid. In Al-Muwatta’, it is narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad who said: I did not catch people except when they were praying Dhuhr in the evening. And early is from sunrise until the time of forenoon.
3:42: The Almighty said: God has chosen you meaning He has selected you, and it has been mentioned before. And purified you meaning from disbelief, according to Mujahid and Al-Hasan. Al-Zajjaj: from all impurities such as menstruation, postpartum bleeding, and others, and He chose you for the birth of Jesus over the women of the worlds all together until the Day of Judgment, and this is correct according to what we will explain, and it is the saying of Al-Zajjaj and others. And the choice was repeated because the meaning of the first is the selection for his games, and the meaning of the second is for the birth of Jesus. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Musa that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Many men have attained perfection, but none of the women have attained perfection except Mary, daughter of Imran, and Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh. Indeed, the superiority of Aisha over women is like the superiority of tharid over all other foods." Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: Perfection is the ultimate and the complete. It is said in its past tense, kamal with the fatha and damma of the meem, and it is completed in its present tense with the damma. And the perfection of each thing is according to its nature. And absolute perfection is only for God, the Almighty. There is no doubt that the most perfect of human beings are the prophets, followed by the saints from the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. If this is established, it has been said that the perfection mentioned in the hadith means prophethood, and it is necessary for Mary, peace be upon her, and Asiyah to be prophets, and this has been said. The correct view is that Mary is a prophet, because God Almighty revealed to her through the angel as He revealed to all the prophets, as mentioned above and will also be explained in Mary. As for Asiyah, nothing has been reported that clearly indicates her prophethood, but rather that she is a truthful and excellent person, as will be explained in At-Tahrim. It has been narrated through authentic chains of transmission that he, peace be upon him, said, according to what Abu Hurairah narrated from him: “The best women of the worlds are four: Mary, daughter of Imran, Asiya, daughter of Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh, Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid, and Fatima, daughter of Muhammad.” And from the hadith of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The best women of the people of Paradise are Khadija, daughter of Khuwaylid, Fatima, daughter of Muhammad, Mary, daughter of Imran, and Asiya, daughter of Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh. And in another chain of transmission on his authority: The lady of the women of Paradise after Mary is Fatima and Khadija. The apparent meaning of the Qur’an and the hadiths indicates that Mary is better than all the women of the world, from Eve to the last woman upon whom the Hour will come. The angels conveyed to her the revelation from God Almighty with the assignment, the information and the good report, just as they conveyed it to all the prophets. So she is a prophetess, and a prophet is better than a saint, so she is better than all women: the first and the last, absolutely. Then after her in virtue is Fatima, then Khadija, then Asiya. Likewise, Musa ibn Uqbah narrated on the authority of Kurayb on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The master of the women of the worlds is Mary, then Fatima, then Khadija, then Asiya. This is a good hadith that removes the ambiguity. God has given Mary something that He has not given to any other woman, which is that the Holy Spirit spoke to her, appeared to her, blew into her garment, and came near her to blow. This is not the case with any other woman. She believed in the words of her Lord and did not ask for a sign when she was given the good report, as Zachariah, peace be upon him, asked for a sign. Therefore, God called her a truthful woman in His revelation, saying: And his mother was a truthful woman. He also said: And she believed in the words of her Lord and His books, and she was of the devout. So He testified that she was a truthful woman, testified that she believed in the words of the good report, and testified that she was devout. Zachariah was given good report of a boy, but he noticed his old age and the barrenness of his wife’s womb. He said, How can I have a boy when my wife is barren? So he asked for a sign. And Mary was given good report of a boy, but she noticed that she was a virgin and that no man had touched her. So it was said to her, Thus says your Lord. So she was satisfied with that and believed in the words of her Lord and did not ask for a sign from Him who knows the essence of this matter. And who among all the women of the worlds, a daughter of Adam, has such virtues? Therefore, it was narrated that she preceded the predecessors with the messengers to Paradise. It was reported from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that if she had been named, she would have been justified. No one will enter Paradise before the predecessors of my nation except a few dozen men, including Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Moses, Jesus, and Mary, the daughter of Imran. It was right for those who claimed to have knowledge of the apparent and used apparent things as evidence for hidden things to know the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: I am the master of my sons Adam, and I am not boasting, and his saying when he said: “The banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection will be in my hand, and the keys to the honorable ones will be in my hand. I am the first orator, the first intercessor, the first bearer of good tidings, the first and the first.” No one attained this prestige in this world over the messengers except for a great matter in the heart. And the same is the case with Mary, she did not attain God’s testimony in the revelation of truthfulness and confirmation of the words except with a close and near rank. And whoever said that she was not a prophet said: Her vision of the angel was like the vision of Gabriel, peace be upon him, in the description of Dihya al-Kalbi when he was asked about Islam and faith, and the companions were not prophets in that, and the first is more apparent and most agree with it. And God knows best.
3:43: That is, prolong standing in prayer, on the authority of Mujahid. Qatada: Continue obedience. The discussion of Qunut has already been presented. Al-Awza'i said: When the angels said that to her, she stood in prayer until her feet swelled and blood and pus flowed, peace be upon her. And prostrate and bow down. Prostration is mentioned before bowing here because the waw does not require order. The disagreement on this has already been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah when God the Almighty says: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of God. So if you say Zaid and Umar stood up, it is possible that Amr stood up before Zaid, so based on this the meaning would be bow down and prostrate. It has also been said: Their law was to prostrate before bowing. With those who bow down. It has been said: Its meaning is do it, even if you do not pray with them. It has been said: What is meant by it is congregational prayer. It has already been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah.
3:44: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: This is from the report of the unseen, meaning what we mentioned from the story of Zachariah, John, and Mary, peace be upon them, from the report of the unseen. We reveal it to you, so the metaphor is returned to that, and that is why it was mentioned. And revelation here is sending to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Revelation can be inspiration, allusion, or other than that. Its origin in the language is informing in secret, and that is why inspiration became called revelation, and from it And when I inspired the disciples, and His saying, And your Lord inspired the bees, and it was said: The meaning of I inspired the disciples is I commanded them, it is said: he inspired and he inspired, and he threw and he threw with the same meaning. Al-Ajjaj said: The decision inspired her and she settled down. Any matter of the earth with the decision. And in the hadith: Revelation, revelation means speed, and the verb is to inspire, to inspire. Ibn Faris said: Revelation is the sign, writing, message, and everything that you convey to someone else so that he knows how it was. Revelation is the swift revelation. Revelation is the voice, and it is said: We inspired them, meaning we called for their help. He said: Maymouna and the provisions were inspired to her The second: The Almighty’s saying: And you were not with them, meaning, and you, O Muhammad, were not with them, meaning, in their presence and with them, when they cast down their pens. The plural of pen, from qalamuhu, if he cut it. It was said: their arrows and darts. It was also said: their pens with which they wrote the Torah, and this is better, because God forbade arrows, saying: That is wickedness. However, it is possible that they did that in a way other than the way the pre-Islamic era did it. Which of them would take care of Mary, meaning, cradle her? Zachariah said: I have more right to her, her maternal aunt is with me. And with him was Ash’a bint Faqud, the sister of Hannah bint Faqud, the mother of Mary. And the Children of Israel said: We have more right to her, the daughter of our scholar. So they cast lots over her and each one brought his pen, and they agreed to put the pens in the water of my rivers, so whoever stopped his pen and the water did not reach him, he would take care of her. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The pens exploded and the pen of Zechariah rose. It was a sign for him, because he was a prophet through whose hands signs were performed. Others have said otherwise. And which of them will take charge of Mary is the subject and predicate in the accusative case with the implied verb indicated by the speech, the meaning being: They are waiting for which of them will take charge of Mary. The verb does not work in the wording of which because it is a question. Third: Some of our scholars have used this verse as evidence to prove the use of drawing lots, which is a principle in our Sharia for anyone who wants justice in division. It is a Sunnah according to the majority of jurists for those on equal footing in argument, so that justice may be done between them, their hearts may be reassured, and suspicion may be removed from those who are in charge of dividing their property. No one should be favored over another if the property is of the same type, in accordance with the Qur’an and Sunnah. Abu Hanifa and his companions rejected the practice of drawing lots, and they rejected the hadiths that were mentioned about it, and they claimed that it has no meaning and that it is similar to the arrows that God forbade. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated that Abu Hanifa permitted it and said: Drawing lots in analogy is not correct, but we abandoned analogy in that and took the narrations and Sunnah. Abu Ubaid said: Three of the prophets used the practice of drawing lots: Yunus, Zakariya, and our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The use of drawing lots is like the consensus of the scholars regarding what is divided between partners, so there is no meaning to the statement of those who rejected it. Al-Bukhari translated at the end of the Book of Testimonies the chapter on drawing lots in problems and the words of God Almighty when they cast their pens and he cited the hadith of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir: The example of the one who upholds the limits of God and the one who violates them is like the example of people who drew lots to choose a place to live in a ship... the hadith. And it will come in Al-Anfal, God willing, and in Surat Az-Zukhruf also, God willing, and the hadith of Umm Al-Ala, that Uthman bin Maz’un drew their lot for the residence when the Ansar drew lots for the residence of the Muhajireen, the hadith, and the hadith of Aisha, she said: Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to travel, he would cast lots among his wives, and whichever one the lot fell on, he would go out with her. And he mentioned the hadith. The narrations from Malik differed on this. He once said: He should knock for the sake of the hadith. He once said: He should travel with the most suitable of them for him in the journey. And the hadith of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If people knew what is in the call to prayer and the first row, and they could not find anything except drawing lots for it, they would draw lots. There are many hadiths with this meaning. The method of drawing lots is mentioned in the books of jurisprudence and differences. Abu Hanifa argued by saying: The drawing of lots in the case of Zakariya and the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was something that if they had agreed upon it without drawing lots, it would have been permissible. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is weak because the benefit of drawing lots is to extract a hidden ruling in the event of a dispute. As for what is extracted by mutual agreement, that is another matter. It is not correct for anyone to say that drawing lots is done in a place of mutual agreement, because it never happens with mutual agreement, but rather it is done in matters about which people dispute and are miserly. The method of drawing lots according to al-Shafi’i and what is said about it is that small, flat pieces of paper are cut out and the name of the one who has the share is written on each piece, then they are placed in flat clay pellets with no irregularities in them, then they are dried a little, then they are thrown into the garment of a man who was not present and his garment covers them, then he puts his hand in and takes it out. If a man’s name comes out, he is given the part for which he drew lots. Fourth: The verse also indicates that the maternal aunt is more entitled to custody than all other relatives except the grandmother. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled regarding Hamza’s daughter, may God bless her and grant her peace, to Ja’far, and her maternal aunt was with him. He said: The maternal aunt is in the same position as the mother. This issue was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ali who said: Zaid bin Haritha went to Mecca and brought back Hamza’s daughter. Ja’far said: I will take her. I have more right to her. She is my cousin and my maternal aunt is with me. The maternal aunt is my mother. Ali said: I have more right to her. She is my cousin and my daughter is with me. She is the daughter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so she has more right to her. Zaid said: I have more right to her. I went to her and traveled and brought her back. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out and mentioned a hadith in which he said: As for the girl, I rule that she should be with her maternal aunt. The maternal aunt is my mother. Ibn Abi Khaithama mentioned that Zaid bin Haritha was Hamza’s executor. According to this, the maternal aunt is more entitled to custody than the executor. The paternal cousin, if he is a husband who has not severed ties with the maternal aunt, has custody even if he is not a mahram to her.
3:45: Evidence of her prophethood as mentioned above. And when it is related to they dispute and it is possible that it is related to his saying: And you were not with them. With a word from him and Abu al-Samal read with a word from him, and it was mentioned above. His name is the Messiah and he did not say her name because the meaning of the word means born. And the Messiah is a title for Jesus and it means the friend, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said. It is said that it is an Arabized and its origin is the sheen and it is common. Ibn Qaris said: And the Messiah is the vein and the Messiah is the friend, and the Messiah is the satin dirham with no engraving on it. And the wipe is the sexual intercourse, it is said he wiped it, and the asma is the smooth place. And the masha is the firm woman who has no back, and by so-and-so there is a touch of beauty. And the masaih are the good horses, and its singular is masiha. He said: She has false temples in her centers, soft and not weak or delicate There is a difference of opinion about the Messiah, son of Mary, from what he took. It was said: Because he wiped the ground, i.e. went into it and did not hide in it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he would not wipe a person with a defect except that he was healed. So it is as if he was called Messiah for that reason, so in this case he is Fa’il with the meaning of Fa’il. It was also said: He was wiped with the blessed oil that the prophets used to wipe themselves with, it has a pleasant smell, so when he wiped himself with it, it was known that he was a prophet. It was also said: Because his soles were wiped. It was also said: Because camels wiped him, i.e. it affected him and appeared on him. It was also said: He was called that because he was wiped with purity from sins. Abu Al-Haytham said: Messiah is the opposite of Al-Masih. It is said: God wiped him, i.e. created him in a good, blessed way, and distorted him, i.e. created him in a cursed, ugly way. Ibn Al-A’rabi said: Messiah is the truthful one, and Al-Masih is the one-eyed one, and the Antichrist was named after him. Abu Ubaid said: Messiah is originally in Hebrew Mashiha with a shin, so it was Arabized like Musa was Arabized Yamoussa. As for the Antichrist, he was called masih because one of his eyes is anointed. It has been said about the Antichrist masih with a kasra on the m and a shaddah on the s. Some say the same with a dotted kha. Some say masih with a fatha on the m and with a light kha. The first is more famous and most agree with it. He was called this because he will travel around the earth, i.e. he will surround it and enter all its countries except Mecca, Medina, and Jerusalem. So it is a fa’il with the meaning of fa’il. The Antichrist will anoint the earth as a trial, and the son of Mary will anoint it as a gift. And since he has anointed eye, fa’il with the meaning of maf’ul. The poet’s fight: Christ kills the Messiah In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no country that the Antichrist will not tread upon, except Mecca and Medina. The hadith. It was mentioned in the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr: Except the Kaaba and the Holy House. Abu Jaafar al-Tabari mentioned it, and Abu Jaafar al-Tahawi added: And the Mosque of al-Tur. It was narrated from the hadith of Junada bin Abi Umayya on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in the hadith of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah on the authority of Samura bin Jundub on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And that he will appear on the whole earth except for the Haram and the Holy House, and that he will confine the believers to the Holy House. And he mentioned the hadith. And in Sahih Muslim: While he was like that, God sent the Messiah, son of Mary, and he descended at the white minaret east of Damascus between two Mahroudahs, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. When he lowered his head, it dripped, and when he raised it, pearls like pearls poured down from him. No disbeliever can smell the scent of his breath without dying. His breath ends where his gaze ends, seeking it until it catches up with him at the gate of Ludd, where it kills him. The hadith in its entirety has been said: The Messiah is a name for Jesus, not derived, so God named him with it. Based on this, Jesus is a substitute for the Messiah from the substitute that is him. Jesus is a foreign name, so it is not declined, and if you make it Arabic, it is not declined in the definite or indefinite, because it has the feminine alif. It is derived from ‘asa ya’usa, if he ruled him and took charge of him. Wajihan means noble, one who came and had power, and it is in the accusative case, as Al-Akhfash said. And among those brought near to God, the Most High, and it is conjoined with wajihan, meaning and brought near, as Al-Akhfash said. The plural of wajih is wajiha’ and wajiha’.
3:46: And he speaks to the people is in apposition to face, as Al-Akhfash also said. The cradle is the bed of a baby while he is breastfeeding. Made means to prepare and smooth the matter. In the revelation, They prepare for themselves. The thing is raised as the camel's hump is prepared. The old man is between the state of a girl and the state of old age. An old woman. The garden has become old if the light covers it. He says: He speaks to the people in the cradle as a sign, and he speaks to them as an old man with the revelation and the message. Abu Al-Abbas said: He spoke to them in the cradle when he healed his mother and said: I am the servant of God. As for his speech while he was an old man, when God the Most High sent him down from the heaven, He sent him down in the form of a thirty-three-year-old, which is the old man, and he says to them: I am the servant of God as he said in the cradle. So these are two signs and two proofs. Al-Mahdawi said: The benefit of the verse is that he informed them that Jesus, peace be upon him, would speak to them in the cradle and would live until he spoke to them as an adult, since it was the custom that those who spoke in the cradle would not live. Al-Zajjaj said: And an old man means and he speaks to people as an old man. Al-Farra’ and Al-Akhfash said: It is in apposition to wajihan. It was said: The meaning is and he speaks to people as a child and as an adult. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The old man is the forbearing one. Al-Nahhas said: This is not known in the language, but an old man according to the linguists is someone who is close to forty. Some of them said: “He is called a young man until he is sixteen years old. Then he becomes a young man until he is thirty-two. Then he becomes an old man at thirty-three,” as Al-Akhfash said. And of the righteous is in apposition to wajihan, meaning he is one of the righteous servants. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah mentioned that Abdullah bin Idris narrated to us on the authority of Hisin on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaaf. He said: Only three spoke in the cradle: Jesus, the companion of Joseph, and the companion of Jurayj. This is what he said: And the companion of Joseph. It is in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Only three spoke in the cradle: Jesus, son of Mary, the companion of Jurayj, the companion of the tyrant, and a child being breastfed by his mother. He mentioned the hadith in full. It came from the hadith of Suhaib in the story of the trench: A woman was brought to be thrown into the fire for her faith, and with her was a suckling child. In a book other than Muslim’s, she hesitated to fall into it, so the child said, O mother, be patient, for you are on the truth. Ad-Dahhak said: Six spoke in the cradle: the witness of Joseph, the child of the hairdresser of Pharaoh’s wife, Jesus, John, the companion of Gregory, and the companion of the tyrant. He did not mention the trench, so he omitted the companion of the trench, and thus the speakers would be seven. There is no contradiction between this and his saying, peace be upon him: None spoke in the cradle except three exclusively, for he informed what was in his knowledge of what was revealed to him regarding that lawful thing, then after this God Almighty informed him of whatever He willed of that, so he informed about it. I said: As for the companion of Joseph, we will talk about him later. As for the companion of Gregory, the companion of the tyrant, and the companion of the trench, they are in Sahih Muslim. And the story of the trench will come in Surat Al-Buruj, God willing: As for the boy of the hairdresser of Pharaoh’s wife, Al-Bayhaqi mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When I was taken on the Night Journey, I passed by a pleasant fragrance. I said, What is this fragrance? They said, The comb of Pharaoh's daughter and her sons fell from her hand. She said, In the name of God. Pharaoh's daughter said, My father? She said, My Lord, and your Lord, and the Lord of your father is God. Pharaoh then called her and said, Do you have a lord other than me? She said, Yes, my Lord, and your Lord is God. He then ordered a copper gong to be heated and then ordered that it be thrown into it. She said, I have a need of you. He said, What is it? She said, To gather my bones and the bones of my children in one place. He said, That is for you because of the right you have over us. So he ordered that they be thrown in, one by one, until he reached a baby among them. He said, Sit, mother, and do not be lazy, for we are upon the truth. Four spoke while they were young: This one, and the witness of Joseph, and the companion of Gregory, and Jesus, son of Mary.
3:47: God the Almighty said: She said, 'My Lord' meaning, my master. She was addressing Gabriel, peace be upon him, because when he appeared to her, he said to her, I am only a messenger from your Lord to grant you a pure boy. When she heard that from him, she asked about the way the child came about, and she said, How can I have a child when no man has touched me? That is, through marriage, Z in her surah, and I was not unchaste. She mentioned this for emphasis, because her saying, No man has touched me includes what is forbidden and what is permissible. She says: The prevailing custom that God has established among His creation is that a child does not come about except through marriage or fornication. It was said: She did not rule out anything from the power of God the Almighty, but she wanted to know how this child would come about: from a future husband or will God create him from the beginning? It was narrated that when Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to her, Thus does God create what He wills, she said, "Thus says your Lord: It is easy for Me." He blew into the pocket of her armor and her sleeve, as Ibn Jurayj said. Ibn Abbas said: Gabriel took hold of her shirt with his finger and blew into it, and she immediately became pregnant with Jesus. Others have been said, as will be explained in her surah, God willing. Some of them said: Gabriel’s blew into her womb, and she became pregnant as a result. Some of them said: It is not permissible for creation to be from Gabriel’s blew, because the child becomes partly from the angels and partly from humans, but the reason for that is that when God Almighty created Adam and took the covenant from his descendants, He made some of the water in the loins of the fathers and partly in the wombs of the mothers, so when the two waters meet, they become a child. And God Almighty made both waters in Mary, partly in her womb and partly in her loins, so Gabriel blew into it to arouse her desire, because if a woman’s desire is not aroused, she cannot become pregnant. So when her desire was aroused by Gabriel’s blew, the water that was in her loins fell into her womb, and the two waters mixed, and she became pregnant as a result. This is indicated by the words of God Almighty: When He decrees a matter, meaning He wants to create a creation, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. It has been discussed in detail in Surat Al-Baqarah.
3:48: The Almighty said: And He will teach him the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel. Ibn Jurayj said: The Book is writing and calligraphy. It was said: It is a book other than the Torah and the Gospel that God taught Jesus, peace be upon him.
3:49: And a Messenger means, and We make him a Messenger. Or a Messenger will speak to them. It was said: It is conjoined with His statement, a distinguished one. Al-Akhfash said: If you wish, you can make the waw in His statement, and a Messenger an intrusion, and the Messenger is a state of the ha', meaning, and He teaches him the Book as a Messenger. And in the long hadith of Abu Dharr: The first of the prophets of the Children of Israel was Moses and the last of them was Jesus, peace be upon him. I create for you means I form and determine for you from clay like the form of a bird. Al-A'raj and Abu Ja'far read it as Kahyah with emphasis. The rest read it with a hamza. The bird is masculine and feminine. Then I will breathe into it meaning into one of it or from it or into the clay, so it becomes a bird. A bird and a bird are like a merchant and a merchant. Wahb said: It used to fly as long as people were looking at it, but when it disappeared from their sight, it would fall dead so that the act of creation would be distinguished from the act of God Almighty. It was said: He did not create anything other than the bat because it is the most perfect bird in creation to be more eloquent in power because it has breasts, teeth and ears, and it menstruates, purifies itself and gives birth. It is said: They only asked to create a bat because it is more amazing than all other creations, and among its wonders is that it has flesh and blood, flies without feathers, gives birth as an animal gives birth, and does not lay eggs as other birds do, so it has an udder from which milk comes out, and it does not see in the light of day or in the darkness of night, but only sees in two hours: an hour after sunset and an hour after sunrise before it becomes very bright, and it laughs as a human laughs, and menstruates as a woman menstruates. It is said: Their question to him was to be obstinate, so they said: Create for us a bat and put a soul in it if you are truthful in what you say, so they took clay and made a bat from it, then breathed into it and behold, it flies between heaven and earth. The formation of the clay and the breathing were from Jesus, and the creation was from God, just as the breathing was from Gabriel and the creation was from God. And the Almighty’s saying: And I heal the blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by God’s permission. The blind is the one who is born blind, according to Ibn Abbas. And Abu Ubaidah said the same, saying: He is the one who is born blind, and he recited for Ru’bah: He turned back like a blind man Ibn Faris said: Blindness is the blindness that a person is born with, but it may also occur. Suwaid said: His eyes turned white Mujahed: He is the one who sees during the day but not at night. Ikrimah: He is the one who sees during the day but in the language it means blindness. It is said, Kama yaknahu kamha and Kamhatha ana if you blind her. Leprosy is well-known and it is a whiteness that affects the skin, and al-abras is the moon, and Sam is a well-known leper, and its plural is al-abras. These two were mentioned specifically because they are both blind. At the time of Jesus, peace be upon him, medicine was prevalent, so God showed them a miracle of the same kind: And I bring the dead back to life by God’s permission. It was said that He brought back to life four souls: Al-Adhir, who was a friend of his, the son of the old woman, the daughter of the tenth, and Sam bin Noah. God knows best. As for Al-Adhir, he had died a few days before that, so he called upon God and said, By God’s permission, his wood was dripping. So he lived and had a son. As for the son of the old woman, he passed by him being carried on his bed, so he called upon God and got up, put on his clothes, carried the bed on his neck and returned to his family. As for the daughter of the tenth, a night had passed over her, so he called upon God and she lived after that and had a son. When they saw that, they said, You bring back to life one whose death was near, so perhaps they did not die. So they had a stroke, so He brought back to life Sam bin Noah for us, and he said to them, Guide me to his grave. So he went out and the people went out with him until they reached his grave, so he called upon God and came out of his grave with his hair gray. Jesus said to him, How did your head turn gray when there was no gray hair in your time? He said: O Spirit of God, you called me and I heard a voice saying: Answer the Spirit of God, so I thought that the Day of Resurrection had come, and from the horror of that my head turned white. He asked him about the death throes, and he said: O Spirit of God, the bitterness of the death throes has not left my throat, and it has been more than four thousand years since his death, so he said to the al-Nas 114:Believe him, for he is a prophet, so some of them believed in him and some of them denied him and said: This is magic. It was narrated from the hadith of Ismail bin Ayyash who said: Muhammad bin Talhah told me from a man: When Jesus, son of Mary, wanted to revive the dead, he would pray two rak’ahs, reciting in the first: Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and in the second: The revelation of the prostration. When he finished, he would praise God and extol Him, then he would call upon Him by seven names: O Eternal, O Hidden, O Everlasting, O Unique, O One, O Eternal. Al-Yahqi mentioned it and said: Its chain of transmission is not strong. God the Almighty said: “And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.” That is, what you eat and what you store. When He brought the dead back to life for them, they asked Him for another sign and said: Tell us what we eat in our houses and what we store for tomorrow. So He informed them and said: O so-and-so, you ate such-and-such, and you ate such-and-such and stored such-and-such. That is His saying: And I will inform you the verse. Mujahid, Az-Zuhri and Al-Sakhtiyani read and what you store with a light dhal. Saeed bin Jubair and others said: He used to inform the children in the book of what they stored until their fathers prevented them from sitting with him. Qatada said: He informed them of what they ate from the table and what they stored from it secretly.
3:50: And confirming is in apposition to his statement: And a Messenger. It was said that the meaning is: I have come to you confirming. What is before me is what was before me. And to make lawful for you is an ellipsis, meaning: I have come to you to make lawful for you. Some of what was forbidden to you means some of the foods. It was said that Jesus, peace be upon him, only permitted them what was forbidden to them because of their sins and was not in the Torah, such as eating fat and everything with claws. It was also said that he only permitted them things that the rabbis had forbidden to them and were not forbidden to them in the Torah. Abu Ubaidah said: It is possible that some means all. And Labid recited: There are places where I don't like them, or some souls are attached to their bathrooms. This statement is wrong according to the linguists, because some and part do not mean the whole in this context, because Jesus, peace be upon him, only permitted them things that Moses had forbidden them, such as eating fats and other things, but he did not permit them to kill, steal, or commit indecency. The evidence for this is that it was narrated on the authority of Qatadah that he said: Jesus came to them with something softer than what Moses, peace be upon them and our Prophet, came with, because Moses came to them with the prohibition of camels and some fats, so Jesus came to them with the permissibility of some of them. Al-Nakhfi read some of what was forbidden to you, such as generosity, meaning it became forbidden. Some may be put in the sense of the whole if an indication is added to it, as the poet said: Abu Munther, you have perished, so let some of us outlast your kindness. Some evil is less serious than others. He wants some evil to be less than all of it. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord. He only used the singular form and they are signs because they are one type in indicating his message.
3:51: "Indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path."
3:52: The Almighty said: And when Jesus perceived disbelief on their part, meaning on the part of the Children of Israel. The meaning of perceived is knew and found, as Al-Zajjaj said. Abu Ubaidah said: The meaning of perceived is recognized, and the origin of that is the existence of something through the senses. Perceiving is knowledge of something. The Almighty said: Do you perceive anyone among them? Perceiving is killing. The Almighty said: When you were catching them by His permission, and from that is the hadith about the locusts.
