If he feels the cold. From them is disbelief meaning disbelief in God. It was said that he heard the word disbelief from them. Al-Farra’ said: They wanted to kill him. “He said: Who are my helpers for God?” He sought help against them. Al-Suddi, Al-Thawri and others said: The meaning is with God, so to means with, like the saying of God the Almighty: And do not consume their wealth with your wealth meaning with. And God knows best. Al-Hasan said: The meaning is from my helpers on the path to God, because he called them to God the Almighty. It was said: The meaning is whoever adds his support to the support of God the Almighty. So to according to these two sayings is in its proper place, and it is the best. And he sought help to protect himself from his people and to show the call, according to Al-Hasan and Mujahid. This is the way of God with His prophets and saints. And Lot said: If only I had against you strength or could take refuge in a strong support meaning a clan and companions who would support me. “The disciples said: We are the helpers of God” meaning the helpers of His Prophet and His religion. The disciples were the companions of Jesus, peace be upon him, and they were twelve men, as stated by Al-Kalbi and Abu Rawq. There is a difference of opinion about their name. Ibn Abbas said: They were called that because of the whiteness of their clothes, and they were fishermen. Ibn Abi Nujayh and Ibn Artah said: They were tailors, so they were called that because they whitened their clothes. Ata’ said: Mary entrusted Jesus with various jobs, and the last thing she entrusted him with was to the disciples, who were tailors and dyers. Jesus’ teacher wanted to travel, so he said to Jesus: I have many clothes of different colors, and I have taught you how to dye, so dye them. Jesus cooked a single grain and put all the clothes in it and said: Be, by God’s permission, as I want you to be. He brought the disciples and all the clothes into the grain, and when he saw it, he said: I have spoiled it. Jesus took out a single grain and put all the clothes in it and said: Be, by God’s permission, as I want you to be. The disciples and all the clothes were presented in love. When he saw them, he said: I have spoiled them. Jesus brought out a red, yellow, green, and other clothes, and each garment had its dye written on it. The disciples were amazed and knew that this was from God. He called the people to it, so they believed in him. They are the disciples. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak: They were called that because they were the special ones of the prophets. They mean the purity of their hearts. It was said: They were kings. That is because the king made food and invited the people to it, and Jesus was at the plate, and it did not decrease. The king said to him: Who are you? He said: Jesus, son of Mary. He said: I will leave this kingdom of mine and follow you. So he set off with those who followed him. They are the disciples, said Ibn Awn. The origin of the word hour in the language is whiteness. Clothes were made white by their whiteness, and the word houri of food is what was made white, and ahwar is white. The ahwar is the one that is white with a hump. The word ahwari is also the helper. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every prophet has a disciple, and my disciples are Az-Zubayr. And the dialogues: women for their whiteness, and he said: Tell the anecdotes to make others cry, but only barking dogs make us cry.
3:53: The Almighty says: Our Lord, we have believed in what You have revealed. That is, they say, Our Lord, we have believed. “In what You have revealed” meaning in Your Book and what You have revealed of Your rulings. And we followed the Messenger meaning Jesus. So register us among the witnesses meaning the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, the meaning is: Make our names with their names and include us among them. It was also said: The meaning is: Write us down with those who testified to the truthfulness of your prophets.
3:54: God the Almighty said: And they plotted meaning the infidels of the Children of Israel from whom he sensed disbelief, that is, he killed him. That is because when his people expelled Jesus and his mother from among them, he returned to them with the disciples and shouted out the call to them, so they intended to kill him and conspired to kill him, and that was their plot. And God's plot is His enticement of His servants without them knowing, according to Al-Faraas and others. Ibn Abbas said: Whenever they commit a sin, We renew a blessing for them. Al-Zajjaj said: God's plot is His recompense for their plot, so He called the recompense by the name of the beginning, like His saying: God mocks them, And He is deceiving them. This was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. The root of plotting in the language is deception and trickery. And plotting is the deception of the leg. And a woman with enchanted legs. And plotting is a type of clothing. And it is said: Rather, it is the deception, as narrated by Ibn Faris. It was said: And God planned is to cast the likeness of Jesus on someone else and raise Jesus to him. This is because when the Jews gathered to kill Jesus, he entered the house fleeing from them, so Gabriel raised him from the window to the sky. Their king said to a wicked man among them called Judah: Go in and kill him. So he entered the window and did not find Jesus there, and he cast the likeness of Jesus on him. When he came out, they saw him looking like Jesus, so they seized him, killed him, and crucified him. Then they said: “The face of Jesus and his body resemble the body of our companion. If this is our companion, then where is Jesus? And if this is Jesus, then where is our companion.” So a fight broke out between them and they killed each other. This is what God the Almighty said: And they planned, and God planned. Other than this was said as follows. And God is the best of planners is an active participle from makra yamkar to plot. Some scholars have counted it among the names of God the Almighty, so when he supplicates with it, he says: O best of planners, plot for me. And he, peace be upon him, used to say in his supplication: O God, plot for me and do not plot against me. We have mentioned it in the book Al-Asna in explaining the beautiful names of God. God knows best.
3:55: The Almighty's saying: "When God said, O Jesus, indeed I will take you is the agent in when they plotted", or an implied verb. A group of scholars of meaning, including Ad-Dahhak and Al-Farra', said about the Almighty's saying: "Indeed I will take you and raise you to Me" that it is an order of precedence and delay, because the waw does not require rank. The meaning is: Indeed I will raise you to Me and purify you from those who disbelieved and take you after you descend from the sky, like His saying: "And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been an obligation and a specified term" and the meaning is And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord and a specified term, it would have been an obligation. The poet said: O palm tree of the same vein, peace and God’s mercy be upon you Peace be upon you and the mercy of God. Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning of Mutawwafika is He who takes you and raises you to the heavens without death, like Tawwafit Mali min Fulan, meaning He seized it. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: God took Jesus, peace be upon him, for three hours during the day, then raised him to the heavens. This is far-fetched, because it is authentic in the reports from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he will descend and kill the Antichrist, as we have explained in the Book of Remembrance, and in this book according to what came before and will come. Ibn Zayd said: Mutawwafika is He who takes you, and Mutawwafika and Rafika are one and the same, and he has not yet died. Ibn Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas that the meaning of Mutawwafika is He who causes you to die. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: It is a death from sleep. God the Most High said: And it is He who takes you by night, meaning He puts you to sleep, because sleep is the brother of death, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He was asked: Is there sleep in Paradise? He said, "No, sleep is the brother of death, and there is no death in Paradise." Narrated by Al-Dar Qanti. The correct view is that God raised him to the heavens without death or sleep, as Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said, and this is the choice of Al-Tabari, and it is the correct view from Ibn Abbas, and Ad-Dahhak said it. Ad-Dahhak said: The story was that when they wanted to kill Jesus, the disciples gathered in a room, and they were twelve men. Jesus entered upon them from the niche of the room, and Satan informed the gathering of the Jews, so four thousand men rode out of them and took the door of the room. Jesus said to the disciples: Which of you will come out, be killed, and be with me in Paradise? A man said: I will, O Prophet of God. So he threw him a woolen coat and a woolen turban, and gave him his staff and made him look like Jesus, so he went out to the Jews, and they killed him and crucified him. As for Jesus, God freed him from feathers and clothed him with light and cut off from him the pleasure of food and drink, so he flew with the angels. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Muawiyah narrated to us: Al-A’mash narrated to us: Al-Munhal narrated to us: Saeed bin Jubair narrated to us: Ibn Abbas said: When God, the Blessed and Exalted, wanted to raise Jesus to heaven, he came out to his companions, who were twelve men, from a spring in the house, and his head was dripping with water. He said to them: There is one among you who will disbelieve in me twelve times after having believed in me. Then he said: Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him so that he may be killed in my place and be with me in my degree? A young man from the youngest of them stood up and said: I am. Jesus said: Sit down. Then he repeated to them and the young man stood up and said: I am. Jesus said: Sit down. Then he repeated to them and the young man stood up and said: I am. He said: Yes, you are that one. Then God cast the likeness of Jesus, peace be upon him, upon him. He said: God, the Exalted, raised Jesus from a window that was in the house to heaven. He said: The Jews came to demand it, so they took the look-alike and killed him, then crucified him. Some of them disbelieved in him twelve times after having believed in him, so they split into three groups: One group said: God was with us as He willed, then He ascended to heaven, and these are the Jacobites. A group said: The Son of God was among us as long as God willed, then God raised him to Himself, and these are the Nestorians. A group said: The servant of God and His Messenger was among us as long as God willed, then He raised him to Himself, and these are the Muslims. So the two infidels conspired against the Muslim woman and killed her, and Islam remained obliterated until God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were killed, and God Almighty revealed: So a party of the Children of Israel believed and a party disbelieved, and We supported those who believed meaning their fathers believed in the time of Jesus over their enemy by making their religion prevail over the religion of the infidels and they became victorious. And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By God, the son of Mary will descend as a just judge, and they will break the cross, and they will kill the pigs, and they will abolish the jizya, and they will leave the camels alone so that no one will run after them, and rancor, hatred, and envy will go away, and they will call to money but no one will accept it.” And also on his authority, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the son of Mary will surely come to Fakh al-Rawha’, performing Hajj or Umrah, or both. And he will not come down with a new law that will abrogate our law, but rather he will come down renewing what has been forgotten and followed, as in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How will you be when the son of Mary will descend among you and your Imam will be from among you? And in another narration: And your mother will be from among you. Ibn Abi Dhi’b said: Do you know what your mother will be from among you? I said: Tell me. He said: Then your mother will be from the Book of your Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, and the Sunnah of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. We have expanded this chapter in the Book of At-Tadhkirah. Praise be to God. The original word Mutawwafik is Mutawwafik, with the damma omitted due to its being too heavy, and it is the predicate of in. "And He will raise you up is in apposition to it, and so is Your Purifier and so is And He will make those who follow you". It is permissible to say "And He will make those who follow you", which is the original. It was said that the complete time is at His saying: "And He will purify you from those who disbelieve". An-Nahhas said: This is a good statement. "And He will make those who follow you, O Muhammad, above those who disbelieve", meaning with the argument and establishing proof. It was also said that it is with glory and victory. Ad-Dahhak and Muhammad ibn Abaan said: What is meant are the disciples. And God Almighty knows best.
3:56: The Almighty says: As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter. Meaning, by killing, crucifixion, captivity, and jizya, and in the Hereafter by fire.
3:57: "And as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them their reward in full. And God does not like the wrongdoers."
3:58: That we recite to you. That is in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is we recite it. The imperative that is permissible with the subject implied.
3:59: The Almighty's saying: "Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is as the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust." is evidence of the validity of analogy. The likeness is based on the fact that Jesus was created without a father like Adam, not that he was created from dust. One thing may be likened to another, even if there is a big difference between them after they come together in one description. Adam was created from dust, but Jesus was not created from dust, so there was a difference between them in this respect. However, the likeness between them is that they were created without a father, and because the origin of their creation was from dust, because Adam was not created from the dust itself, but rather He made the dust into clay, then made it into clay, then created him from it. Likewise, Jesus was transformed from one state to another, then made him a human being without a father. This verse was revealed because of the delegation of Najran when they denounced the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: “Jesus is the servant of God and His Word, so they said: Show us a servant created without a father. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Adam, who is his father? Are you amazed at Jesus who has no father? Adam, peace be upon him, had neither a father nor a mother.” This is what God the Almighty said: And they do not bring you an example meaning about Jesus except that We bring you the truth about Adam and the best explanation. It was narrated that when he, peace be upon him, called them to Islam, they said: We were Muslims before you. He said: You have lied. Three things prevent you from Islam: your saying that God has taken a son, your eating of pigs, and your prostration to the cross. They said: Who is the father of Jesus? So God the Almighty revealed: “The likeness of Jesus before God is as the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust” until His saying: Then we invoke the curse of God upon the liars. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them, and some of them said to each other: If you do that, the valley will be engulfed in fire upon you. They said: Do you not offer us anything other than this? He said: Islam, the poll tax, or war. So they acknowledged the poll tax as follows. The discussion ended when he said Adam. Then he said: He created him from dust, then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was. That is, and he was. The future can be in the place of the past if the meaning is known.
3:60: Al-Farra' said: The truth is from your Lord is in the nominative case with the implied he. Abu Ubaidah said: It is a new statement and its predicate is in his saying from your Lord. It was said that he is the subject, meaning the truth has come to you. So do not be among those who deny. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation, because he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not doubt the matter of Jesus, peace be upon him.
3:61: There are three issues: The first is the Almighty’s saying: So whoever disputes with you about him meaning, argues with you and disputes with you, O Muhammad, about him, meaning about Jesus, after what has come to you of knowledge that he is the servant and messenger of God. Then say, Come, meaning, Come. It was used for someone who has significance and elevation, then it came into use for everyone who calls for coming, and more clarification will come in Al-An’am. Na’da is in the place of Jazm. Our sons is evidence that the sons of daughters are called sons, and that is: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came with Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein, and Fatima was walking behind him and Ali was behind them, and he was saying to them: If I supplicate, then follow them. The meaning of his saying, Then let us implore is that we implore in supplication, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Kisa’i: We curse. The origin of supplication is striving to supplicate with cursing and other things. Labid said: Among the elders of his people, time looked at them and supplicated. That is, he strove to destroy them. It is said: May God curse him. “Bahl” means to curse. Bahl is a small amount of water. Abhaltuhu means to leave him alone and want him. Bahlahtu also means to destroy him. Abu Ubaidah narrated: May God curse him. Ibn Abbas said: They are the people of Najran: the master, the wise man, and Ibn al-Harith, their leaders. So we place the curse of God on the liars. The second: This verse is one of the signs of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he called them to the Mubahalah, but they refused and accepted the jizyah after their leader, Al-Aqib, informed them that if they challenged him, the valley would be engulfed in fire, for Muhammad is a prophet sent, and you know that he came to you with the final decision regarding the matter of Jesus. So they abandoned the Mubahalah and returned to their country on the condition that they would pay a garment every year in Safar and a thousand garments in Rajab, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with them on that in exchange for Islam. Third: Many scholars said: His saying, peace be upon him, about Al-Hassan and Al-Hussein when they challenged each other to the challenge, We call our sons and your sons, and his saying about Al-Hassan: This son of mine is a special master, with Al-Hassan and Al-Hussain, to be called the sons of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and not others, because of his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Every cause and lineage will be cut off on the Day of Resurrection except my cause and lineage. For this reason, some of Al-Shafi’i’s companions said about someone who made a will for the son of so-and-so, and he did not have a son of his own, but he had a son of a son and a son of a daughter: The will is for the son of the son, not the son of the daughter, and this is the saying of Al-Shafi’i. More clarification of this will come in Al-An’am and Al-Zukhruf, God willing.
3:62: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, this is the true account. The reference in His saying, Indeed, this is is to the Qur'an and what is in it of stories. They are called stories because the meanings follow one another in them. It is from their saying: Do not follow the traces of so-and-so, meaning do not follow him. And there is no god but God, min is an additional word for emphasis, and the meaning is, There is no god but God, the Almighty, meaning the One who cannot be defeated. The Wise, the Possessor of Wisdom. And something similar has come before, and praise be to God.
3:63: But if they turn away, then indeed, God is Knowing of the corrupters.
3:64: There are three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Say, O People of the Scripture. The address in the statement of Al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd and Al-Suddi is to the people of Najran. And in the statement of Qatada, Ibn Jurayj and others is to the Jews of Medina. They were addressed with this because they made their rabbis in their obedience to them like lords. And it was said: It is for the Jews and Christians together. And in the letter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Heraclius: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. From Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to Heraclius, the Great of the Romans. Peace be upon him who follows the guidance. As for what follows, I invite you to the call of Islam. Submit and you will be safe, and submit and God will give you your reward twice. But if you turn away, then upon you is the sin of the Arians. O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we will not worship except God. Until His saying: Then say, Bear witness that we are Muslims. The wording of Muslim. Equity means justice and fairness, as Qatada said. And Zuhair said: Show me a plan that doesn't hurt us and treats us equally. Al-Farraa: It is said in the meaning of justice, sawa and sawa. If you open the seen, it is lengthened, and if it is broken or closed, it is shortened, like the saying of God, a place apart. He said: In the reading of Abdullah to the word justice between us and you, and Qanab read the word with a sukoon on the lam, he threw the movement of the lam on the kaf, as it is said kabad. So the meaning is, answer what you are called to, which is the just and upright word that does not deviate from the truth. It has been explained by the saying of God, that we worship none but God. So the position of an is in the accusative case as a substitute for a word, or in the nominative case as an implied subject, the estimate is that we worship none but God, or it is explanatory and has no position. It is permissible with that in na’bud and what is conjoined to it to raise and to apocopate. The apocopation is based on an being explanatory with the meaning of any, as God, the Almighty, said, that you walk, and la is apocopate. This is the school of thought of Sibawayh. And it is permissible with this to raise na’bud and what comes after it to be a predicate. It is permissible to raise it in the sense that we do not worship, and similarly to that is that he does not return to them with words and he does not possess for them harm or benefit. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said: And we do not associate anything with Him and it is not taken with the jussive mood, on the assumption that there is no an at the beginning of the speech. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And let not some of us take others as lords besides God meaning that we do not follow him in making something permissible or forbidden except in what God has made permissible. This is similar to His saying: They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God meaning that they have placed them in the position of their Lord in accepting their prohibition and permissibility of what God has not prohibited or permitted. This indicates the invalidity of the saying of istihsan and the mere opinion that is not based on a legal proof. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: Such as the istihsan of Abu Hanifa in the estimates that he made without clear evidence. This is a refutation of the Rafidis who say: It is necessary to accept the statement of the Imam without clarifying a legal basis, and that he makes permissible what God has prohibited without clarifying a basis from the Shari’ah. And arbab is the plural of rabbi. And here dun means other. Third: The Almighty’s saying: But if they turn away, meaning, they turn away from what they have been called to. Then say, Bear witness that we are Muslims, meaning, we are characterized by the religion of Islam, submitting to its rulings, acknowledging what God has bestowed upon us in that of favors and blessings, not taking anyone as a lord, not Jesus, nor Ezra, nor the angels, because they are human beings like us, created as we are created, and we do not accept anything from the monks because they forbid us what God has not forbidden us, so we would have taken them as lords. Ikrimah said: The meaning of take is to prostrate. It was previously mentioned that prostration was, until the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a refuge when he wanted to prostrate, as was explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. Anas ibn Malik narrated that he said: We said, O Messenger of God, should we bow to one another? He said, No. We said, Should we embrace one another? He said, No, but shake hands. Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan. This meaning will be further explained in Surat Yusuf, God willing. In reality, touching the Qur’an or part of it while not in a state of purity, God willing.
3:65: The Almighty said: O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham? The original form is lama, so the alif was deleted to differentiate between the question and the report. This verse was revealed because of the claim of each group of Jews and Christians that Abraham was of their religion, so God the Almighty denied them by saying that Judaism and Christianity were only revealed after him, so that is why He said: And the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him. Al-Zajjaj said: This verse is the clearest argument against the Jews and Christians, because the Torah and the Gospel were revealed after him and there is no name for any of the religions in them, and the name Islam is in every book. It is said: There were a thousand years between Abraham and Moses, and between Moses and Jesus also a thousand years. Do you not understand the falsity of your argument and the invalidity of your statement? And God knows best.
3:66: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Here you are, you have argued meaning about the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because they knew him in what they found of his description in their book, so they argued about him with falsehood. So why do you argue about what you have no knowledge of? Meaning their claim that Abraham was a Jew or a Christian. The original form of ha antum is a’antum, so the first hamza was replaced with a ha’ because it is its sister, on the authority of Abu Amr Ibn al-Ala’ and al-Akhfash. Al-Nahhas said: This is a good statement. Qanbal read on the authority of Ibn Kathir ha antum like ha’antum. Better than that is for the ha’ to be a replacement for the hamza, so its original form would be a’antum. It is permissible for the ha’ to be for emphasis, it entered into antum, and the alif was deleted due to frequent use. In these, there are two languages: lengthening and shortening, and some Arabs shorten it. Abu Hatim recited: By your life, we and these allies are in a predicament whose nails have not been cut. These here are in the position of a call, meaning, Oh, these. It is permissible for these to be the predicate of you, on the condition that these means who and what comes after it is related to it. It is also permissible for it to be the predicate of you who argued. This was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. Praise be to God. Second: The verse is evidence of the prohibition of disputing about what one has no knowledge of, and the prohibition of those who do not have verification. God Almighty said: “Here you are, you argue about that of which you have knowledge. Why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge?” The command to argue has been given to those who have knowledge and certainty, as God Almighty said: And argue with them in a way that is best. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that a man came to him who denied his son and said: O Messenger of God, my wife gave birth to a black boy. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you have camels? He said: Yes. He said: What are their colors? He said: Red. He said: Is there any gray among them? He said: Yes. He said: Where is that from? He said: Perhaps a vein has been pulled out. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This boy, perhaps a vein has been pulled out. This is the reality of argument and the end of clarifying the evidence from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
3:67: May God exonerate him from their false claims, and make clear that he was a follower of the Islamic Hanafi school of thought and was not a polytheist. A Hanafi is someone who believes in the Oneness of God, performs Hajj, sacrifices, completes the prayer, and faces the Qiblah. Its derivation has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. A Muslim in the language is someone who is humbled before the command of God Almighty and obeys Him. The meaning of Islam has already been fully explained in Surat Al-Baqarah, and all praise is due to God.
3:68: Ibn Abbas said: The Jewish leaders said: By God, O Muhammad, I know that I am the most deserving of the religion of Abraham from you and from others, for he was a Jew and you are nothing but envy. So God Almighty revealed this verse. The meaning of the word most deserving is the truth. It was said: with help and support, and it was said: with the argument. For those who followed him in his religion and his Sunnah. This prophet was mentioned alone to glorify him, as he said in them: fruits, palm trees, and pomegranates. This meaning was presented in full in Surat Al-Baqarah. This is in the nominative case in apposition to those, and the prophet is an attribute of this or an explanatory apposition. If it were to be in the accusative case, it would be permissible in the speech in apposition to the ha in follow him. And God is the protector of the believers, meaning He is their supporter. And "On the authority of Ibn Mas'ud that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every prophet has guardians from among the prophets, and my guardian among them is my father and the friend of my Lord. Then he recited: The most deserving of Abraham are those who followed him and this prophet."
3:69: It was revealed about Muadh ibn Jabal, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and Ammar ibn Yasir when the Jews of Banu Nadir, Qurayzah and Banu Qaynuqa' invited them to their religion. This verse is similar to the words of God the Almighty: Many of the People of the Scripture wish they could turn you back to disbelief after you have believed, out of envy. According to this statement, min is for partiality. It was also said: all the People of the Scripture, so min is for clarifying the type. The meaning of if they were to mislead you is that they would cause you to commit sin by turning away from the religion of Islam and opposing it. Ibn Jurayj said: They were to mislead you means they would destroy you. From this is the saying of al-Akhtal: I was the speck in a murky, foaming wave, the one who brought it threw it as a gift of misguidance. That is, he perished utterly. They only mislead themselves is a negation and an affirmation. And they do not perceive means they realize that they will not be able to mislead the believers. It was said: And they do not perceive means they do not know that Islam is correct, and it is obligatory for them to know, because the proofs are clear and the arguments are dazzling, and God knows best.
3:70: That is, with the authenticity of the verses that you have in your books, according to Qatada and Al-Suddi. It was said: The meaning is that you bear witness to the likes of them from the verses of the prophets that you acknowledge.
3:71: Confusion: mixing, and it was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. The meaning of this verse and the one before it is the same. You conceal the truth, and you may conceal the answer to the question. And you know a sentence in the place of the circumstance.
3:72: God Almighty said: And a party of the People of the Scripture said, Believe in what was revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day and disbelieve at its end that perhaps they will return. It was revealed about Ka’b between Al-Ashraf and Malik bin Al-Saif and others. They said to the lowly among their al-Nas 114:Believe in what was revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day, meaning its beginning. It was called the beginning because it is the most beautiful part of it, and the first part of it is the beginning. The poet said: And it shines in the face of the day, bright as the sea’s ocean, its system is smooth Another said: Whoever is happy about Malik's death, let him come to our women in broad daylight. It is an accusative of circumstance, as is its last particle. Qatada’s school of thought is that they did that to cast doubt on the Muslims. A group is a community, from tafa yatuwuf, and it may be used for one person in the sense of the same group. The meaning of the verse is that the Jews said to each other: Show belief in Muhammad at the beginning of the day, then disbelieve in him at the end of it, for if you do that, doubts about his religion will appear to those who are aware, so they will return from his religion to your religion, and they will say that the People of the Book know it better than us. It was said that the meaning is: Believe in his prayer at the beginning of the day toward the Holy House, for it is the truth, and disbelieve in his prayer at the end of the day toward the Kaaba, so that they may return to your qiblah, from Ibn Abbas and others. Muqatil said: Its meaning is that they came to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the beginning of the day and returned from him and said to the common al-Nas 114:It is the truth, so follow it. Then they said: Let us look in the Torah. Then they returned at the end of the day and said: We have looked in the Torah, but it is not it. They say it is not true, but they wanted to confuse the lowly and cast doubt on it.
3:73: And the Almighty's saying: "And do not believe except in him who follows your religion": This is a prohibition, and it is from the speech of the Jews to each other, meaning that the leaders said that to the common people. Al-Suddi said: It is from the speech of the Jews of Khaybar to the Jews of Medina. This verse is the most difficult in the surah. It was narrated from Al-Hasan and Mujahid that the meaning of the verse is: And do not believe except in him who follows your religion, and do not believe that they will argue with you before your Lord because they have no argument, for you are more sound than them in religion. And that and argue with you is in the accusative case, meaning that they argue with you, i.e. with their argument, meaning do not believe them in that because they have no argument. That someone should be given like what you were given of the Torah, manna, quails, the parting of the sea, and other signs and virtues. So that it should be given later after or argue with you, and his saying that the guidance is the guidance of God is an interjection between two statements. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is: Do not believe except in the one who follows your religion. Do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you have been given. Do not believe that they will argue with you. He thinks that it is conjoined. It was said: The meaning is: Do not believe except in the one who follows your religion that anyone will be given the like of what you have been given. The extension is also for interrogation to emphasize the denial that they said that no one will be given the like of what they have been given, because the Jewish scholars said to them: Do not believe except in the one who follows your religion that anyone will be given the like of what you have been given. That is, no one will be given the like of what you have been given. So the speech is in the same order. And that is in the nominative case according to the one who raised it in your saying I struck him, and the predicate is omitted, its estimate is that someone will be given what you have been given, you believe or acknowledge, that is, giving something that exists and is believed or acknowledged, that is, do not believe in that. It is permissible for an to be in the accusative case with an implied verb, as is permissible in your saying Azīdā ḍarbūtuhu Is it Zaydān ḍarbūtuhu? This is stronger in Arabic because the interrogative with the verb is more appropriate, and the meaning is Do you acknowledge that it will be brought? or Do you spread that? or Do you remember that? and the like. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, and Hamid read it with the long vowel. Abu Hatim said: An means now, so the lam of the jar was deleted for the sake of lightness and was replaced with a long vowel, like the reading of the one who read an kāna dhī mal meaning now. His saying or they argue with you in this reading refers back to addressing the believers, or or can be in the meaning of an because they are letters of doubt and reward, one of which is placed in place of the other. The meaning of the verse is: And that they argue with you before your Lord, O company of believers. So say: O Muhammad, the guidance is the guidance of God and we are upon it. And whoever reads without the long vowel said: The first negation indicates their denial in their saying Do not believe. The meaning is that the Jewish scholars said to them: Do not believe that anyone will be given what you have been given, meaning they have no faith or proof, so the meaning is connected to knowledge, wisdom, the Book, the proof, manna, quails, the splitting of the sea, and other virtues and honors, meaning that they will only be in you, so do not believe that anyone will be given what you have been given except for those who follow your religion. So the speech has an inversion according to this reading, and the lam is redundant. And whoever excepts is not from the first, otherwise the speech would not be permissible. And ahad was included because the beginning of the speech is a negation, so it was included in the connection of an because it is the object of the negated verb, so an is in the accusative case due to the absence of the preposition. Al-Khalil said: an is in the genitive case with the deleted preposition. It was said: the lam is not redundant, and ta'minu is based on taqriru. Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning is do not believe except for those who follow your religion, hating that anyone will be given what you have been given. It was said: The meaning is do not tell what is in your book about the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, except to those who follow your religion, lest it be a path for idol worshippers to believe in it. Al-Farra’ said: It is possible that the speech of the Jews was cut off at the words of God Almighty, except for those who follow your religion, then He said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say: Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God. That is, the true explanation is the explanation of God Almighty that no one will be given what you have been given, between that no one will be given what you have been given, and there is no implied meaning after that, that is, lest you go astray. Therefore, it is appropriate for one to enter into the speech and or in the meaning of until and except that, as Imru’ al-Qais said: I told him, "Don't cry. We are trying to become king or die and be excused." Another said: If I winked at a people's channel, their heels would break or straighten out. And similar to it is their saying: We will not meet or the Hour will come, meaning until or until, and this is the doctrine of Al-Kisa’i. According to Al-Akhfash, it is a conjunction to Do not believe and it has been mentioned before. That is, they have no faith or argument, so it is a conjunction to the meaning. It is possible that the entire verse is addressed to the believers from God, the Most High, in order to strengthen their hearts and sharpen their insights, so that they do not doubt when the Jews deceive and falsify their religion. The meaning is: O group of believers, do not believe except those who follow your religion, and do not believe that anyone will be given the same as you have been given of virtue and religion, and do not believe that someone who opposes you or is able to do so will argue with you about your religion before your Lord, for guidance is the guidance of God and virtue is in God’s hand. Ad-Dahhak said: The Jews said: We will argue with our Lord about those who oppose us in our religion, so God, the Most High, made it clear that they are the ones who will be refuted and punished, and that the believers are the victors. And their argument is their dispute on the Day of Resurrection. In the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: The Jews and Christians will argue with us before our Lord, saying, You gave us one reward and you gave them two. He will say, Did I wrong you in any of your rights? They will say, No. He will say, Then My bounty is given to whomever I wish. Our scholars said, If they had known that this was from the bounty of God, they would not have argued with us before our Lord. So God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they will argue with you before your Lord on the Day of Resurrection. Then He said, “Say to them now, ‘The bounty is in God’s hand. He gives it to whomever He wishes. God is all-Encompassing and Knowing.’” Ibn Kathir recited an with a long vowel as an interrogative, as Al-A’sha said: If she saw a blind man, struck by the vicissitudes of fate and a time that was torn and crazy The rest read it without extending it as report. Saeed bin Jubair read an yu’ta with a kasra on the hamza, meaning negation, and it is from the speech of God, as Al-Farra’ said. The meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, that guidance is the guidance of God, that someone is given the like of what you have been given or that they argue with you before your Lord. He means the Jews with falsehood and say, We are better than you. And the accusative or that they argue with you means by implying that, and aw is implied after it, an if it means until or an except that. Al-Hasan read an yu’ta with a kasra on the ta’ and an open ya’, meaning that someone is given someone the like of what you have been given, so the object was deleted: God Almighty says: Say: Indeed, the guidance is the guidance of God. There are two opinions: One of them: That guidance to goodness and direction to God the Almighty are in the hand of God the Most High, Who gives it to His prophets, so do not deny that someone other than you is given what you have been given. If they deny that, then tell them that the favor is in the hand of God, Who gives it to whomever He wills. The other statement: Say, Indeed, guidance is the guidance of God which He gave to the believers through belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one else. Some of the scholars of allusions said about this verse: Do not associate with anyone except those who agree with you in your conditions and your way, for whoever does not agree with you will not accompany you, and God knows best.
3:74: That is, through his prophethood and guidance, according to Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and others. Ibn Jurayj: Through Islam and the Qur’an, whoever He wills. Abu Uthman said: The most beautiful statement is to leave with him the hope of the hopeful and the fear of the fearful, And God is the possessor of great bounty.
3:75: It contains eight issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount, will return it to you, such as Abdullah ibn Salam. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you. He is Phinehas ibn Azura the Jew. A man entrusted him with a dinar and he betrayed him. It was also said: Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions. Ibn Wathab and al-Ashhab al-Uqaili read min in yamanhu according to the language of those who read nasta’in, which is the language of Bakr and Tamim. In the version of Abdullah Malik, it is not a good omen for Yusuf, and the rest read it with an alif. Nafi’ and al-Kisa’i read yu’da hi with a ya’ in the inclusion. Abu Ubaid said: Abu Amr, al-A’mash, Asim and Hamzah agreed in the narration of Abu Bakr on stopping the ha’, so they read yu’da ilaika. Al-Nahhas said: With the sukoon of the ha’, it is not permissible except in Ash’ar according to some grammarians, and some of them do not allow it at all and see that it was a mistake from those who read it, that he thought that the jazm falls on the ha’, and Abu Amr is too noble for such a thing to be permissible for him. The correct view is that he used to break the ha’, which is the reading of Yazid ibn al-Qa’qa’. Al-Farra’ said: The doctrine of some of the ‘Abbas is to jazm the ha’ if what precedes it is moved, and they say: I struck him with a severe strike, just as they make the mim of ‘antum wa-qamatum quiescent, and its origin is the nominative, as the poet said: When he saw that he was not satisfied, he went to a palm grove and lay down. It was said: The sukoon of the ha’ in this position is permissible because it occurred in the position of the jazm and it is the missing ya’. Abu al-Mundhir Salam and al-Zuhri read yu’dah with a damma on the ha’ without a waw. Qatada, Hamid and Mujahid read yu’dahhu with a waw in the insertion, the waw was chosen for it from the lip and the ha’ has a distant point of articulation. Sibawayh said: The waw in the masculine is like the alif in the feminine and it is replaced by a ya’ because the ya’ is lighter if it is preceded by a kasra or a ya’, and the ya’ is deleted and the kasra remains because the ya’ was deleted and the verb was raised so it was maintained in its state. Second: The Most High informed that among the People of the Book there is the traitor and the trustworthy, and the believers do not distinguish between them, so all of them should be avoided. He mentioned the People of the Book specifically, even though the believers are like that, because treachery is more common among them, so the statement was based on the most common. And God knows best. The interpretation of the qintar has already been mentioned. As for the dinar, it is twenty-four qirats, and the qirat is three grains of medium barley, so the total is seventy-two grains, and this is agreed upon. And whoever preserves a lot and pays it, the little is more deserving, and whoever betrays or prevents it in a little, then that is more common in a lot. This is the clearest evidence for the statement of the implication of the address. There is much disagreement among the scholars about it, mentioned in the principles of jurisprudence. The Most High mentioned two categories: those who pay and those who do not pay except by persisting in doing so. And there may be among the people those who do not pay even if you persist in doing so. The Most High mentioned the two categories because it is the most common and usual, and the third is rare, so the statement was based on the most common. Talha bin Masraf, Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Salami and others read Damt with a kasra on the dal. These are two dialects, and the kasra is the dialect of Azd Al-Sarat, from Damt Tadam, like Khafat Takhaf. Al-Akhfash narrated Damt Tadum, as an anomaly. Third: Abu Hanifa based his doctrine on the obligation of the debtor to remain with him on the words of God Almighty: Except as long as you stand over him. The rest of the scholars rejected it, and it was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah. Some of our scholars from Baghdad based their evidence on the imprisonment of the two debtors on the words of God Almighty: And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will return it to you unless you stand over him. That is, he faces you, but he fears you and is shy of you, because shyness is in the eyes. Do you not see the saying of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: And do not ask a blind person for a need, because shyness is in the eyes. And if you ask your brother for a need, look at him with your face until he is shy and fulfills it. It is said that he is constantly with him, because if you give him a look, he will deny you. It was said that by standing he meant the continuation of the demand, not the very act of standing. The original word dinar is dinar, but one of the two nuns was replaced with a ya in order to make it easier, due to its frequent use. This is indicated by the fact that the plural form is dinars and the diminutive is dinarinir. Fourth: Trust is of great value in religion, and one of the great things about it is that it and the womb stand on both sides of the Sirat, as in Sahih Muslim. So no one can cross the Gemini except those who preserve them. Muslim narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us about the lifting of trust. He said: A man sleeps a sleep and the trust is taken from his heart. It was mentioned in its entirety at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. Ibn Majah narrated: Muhammad ibn Al-Musaffa told us, Muhammad ibn Harb told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Sinan, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahariyyah, on the authority of Abu Shajarah, many times, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God, the Almighty, wants to destroy a servant, He strips him of his modesty. If He strips him of his modesty, you will find him only as a hated and detestable person. If He strips him of his trustworthiness, you will find him only as a traitor and a betrayer. If He strips him of his mercy, you will find him only as an accursed and cursed person. If He strips him of his mercy, you will find him only as an accursed and cursed person. The meaning of his, peace be upon him, saying, “Fulfill the trust of the one who entrusted you with it, and do not betray the one who betrayed you,” has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. And God knows best. Fifth: This verse does not include any justification for the People of the Book or for some of them, contrary to those who have held this view, because there are some wicked Muslims who fulfill trusts and insure a great deal of money, and they are not therefore just. The path of justice and testimony does not suffice in fulfilling trusts in money in terms of transactions and deposits. Do you not see their saying: We have no responsibility for the illiterate. So how can someone who believes that it is permissible to take our money and our women without any hardship on him be just? If that were sufficient for them to be just, their testimony against the Muslims would have been accepted. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: That is because they said meaning the Jews We have no blame for the unlettered ones. It was said that when the Jews pledged allegiance to the Muslims, they would say: We have no blame for the unlettered ones, meaning that there is no blame on us for their injustice because they oppose us. They claimed that this was in their book, so God, the Almighty, denied them and responded to them, saying: Yes, yes, there is a path of punishment for them because of their lies and their taking the Arabs’ money as permissible. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: The speech was completed, then He said: Whoever fulfills his covenant and fears God. It is said that the Jews had borrowed money from the Arabs, and when the people who had rights converted to Islam, the Jews said: We have nothing against you, because you abandoned your religion, so your debt was dropped from us. They claimed that it was the ruling of the Torah, so God, the Almighty, said: Yes, in response to their saying: We have no blame for the unlettered ones. That is, it is not as you say. Then He resumed and said: Whoever fulfills his covenant and fears polytheism, then he is not one of the liars, but God and His Messenger love him. Seventh: A man said to Ibn Abbas: We take a share of the wealth of the People of the Covenant, a chicken or a sheep, and we say: There is no harm in that. He said to him: This is like what the People of the Book said: There is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered ones. If they pay the jizyah, their wealth is not permissible for you except with their own consent. Abd al-Razzaq mentioned it on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani on the authority of Sa’sa’ah that a man said to Ibn Abbas, and he mentioned it. Eighth: The Almighty’s statement: And they tell lies about God while they know indicates that the unbeliever is not considered worthy of having his testimony accepted, because God the Almighty described him as a liar. It contains a refutation of the unbelievers who forbid and permit other than what God forbade and permitted, and they make that part of the Shari’ah. Ibn al-Arabi said: From this comes the refutation of those who rule by istihsan without evidence, and I do not know of anyone from the people of the Qiblah who said this. In the hadith: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: There is nothing that existed in the days of ignorance that is not under my feet except for trust, for it is given to the righteous and the wicked.
3:76: (Min) is raised by the beginning and it is a condition and Awfa is in the place of Jazm. And itqa is conjoined to it, meaning and he feared God and did not lie and did not consider permissible what was forbidden to him. Indeed, God loves the righteous meaning He loves those. The meaning of God’s love for His friends has been presented. The ha’ in His statement by His covenant refers back to God the Almighty. It has been mentioned in His statement and they say lies about God while they know. It may refer to the one who fulfills his promise, avoids disbelief, betrayal, and breaking a covenant. The covenant is a verbal noun that is added to the subject and the object.
3:77: There are two issues: First: The Imams narrated on the authority of Al-Ash’ath bin Qais, who said: There was a land between me and a Jewish man, and he denied it to me, so I brought him to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Do you have evidence? I said: No. He said to the Jew: Swear. I said: Then he will swear and take my money. Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price. The Imams also narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever usurps the right of a Muslim by falsely taking an oath, God has made Hell obligatory for him and has forbidden Paradise for him. A man said to him: Even if it is something insignificant, O Messenger of God? He said: Even if it is a twig of arak. The meaning of God will not speak to them, nor look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. The second: This verse and the hadiths indicate that the judge’s ruling does not make the hidden money permissible by ruling the apparent if the one in whose favor the ruling is made knows that it is invalid. The imams narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You bring your disputes to me, but I am only a human being, and perhaps some of you are more eloquent in their arguments than others. I only judge between you based on what I hear from you. So whoever I judge in his favor regarding his brother’s right, he should not take it, for I am only giving him a piece of the Fire which he will bring on the Day of Resurrection.” There is no disagreement among the Imams about this. Abu Hanifa contradicted it and went to extremes and said: The ruling of the judge based on invalid testimony makes the vagina permissible for the one who is forbidden to him, as mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. He claimed that if two false witnesses testified against a man that his wife was divorced and the judge ruled based on their testimony, then her vagina would be permissible for the one who married her if he knew that the case was invalid. He was criticized for ignoring this clear and authentic hadith, and for protecting wealth and not considering it permissible based on corrupt rulings, and for not protecting the vagina from that, while the vagina is more deserving of being protected and preserved. The invalidity of his statement will come in the verse of cursing, God willing.
3:78: It means a group of Jews. They twist their tongues with the book. Abu Jaafar and Shaiba read yalawun on the basis of multiplication. If he inclines it, and from it the meaning is they distort the words and deviate from the intended meaning. The origin of li is inclination. He twisted with his hand, and he twisted his head. The Almighty said: Twisting their tongues, meaning stubbornly from the truth and inclining away from it to something else. The meaning of do not twist anyone is do not turn towards him. It is said that he turned towards him if he stopped and stayed. And li is the one who delays. He twisted him with his religion, twisting it, twisting, delaying. He said: I had borrowed Hassan for fear of bankruptcy and misery. It improves the sale of the original and the visible And Dhu al-Rummah said: You want me to come to you while you are full and better, you who wear the scarf, to litigate In the hadith, the one who finds it is permissible to expose and punish him. Tongues is the plural of tongue in the language of the male, and the feminine says tongues.
3:79: It was not means it is not appropriate, as he said: It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. It is not for God to take a son. It is not for us to speak of this. Meaning it is not appropriate. And the word human is used for both singular and plural because it is like a source, and what is meant by it here is Jesus according to Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi. The book: the Quran. The rule: knowledge and understanding. It was also said: rulings. That is, God does not choose a liar for His prophethood, and if a human did that, God would deprive him of the signs and indications of prophethood. And the word then is in the accusative case, as a combination between that He gives him and says, meaning that the coming of prophethood and his saying: Be My servants instead of God do not come together. But be rabbis, meaning but it is permissible for the prophet to say to them: Be rabbis. It was said that this verse was revealed about the Christians of Najran. It was also narrated that the entire Surah up to the words: And when you left your family was revealed because of the Christians of Najran, but the Jews were mixed with them because they committed the act of denial and stubbornness that they did. The rabbis, singular rabbani, is attributed to the Lord. The rabbi is the one who educates people with the small things of knowledge before the big things, as if he follows the example of the Lord Almighty in making things easy. Its meaning was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Some of them said, it was originally rabbi, then the alif and the nun were added for emphasis, just as someone with a thick beard is called lahyani, someone with a thick forehead is called jammani, and someone with a thick neck is called raqbani. Al-Mubarrad said: The rabbis The masters of knowledge, the singular of which is rabban, from their saying rabbah yarbahu, so he is rabban if he managed it and fixed it, so its meaning according to this is they manage the affairs of people and fix them. The alif and the nun are for emphasis as they said rayyan and atshan, then the nisba ya was added to it as it was said lahyani and raqbanani and jamani. The poet said: If I were mortgaged in the atmosphere, He would bring me down from it. Hadith and rabbanani rabbanani, so the meaning of the rabbanani is the one who knows the religion of the Lord who acts according to his knowledge, because if he does not act according to his knowledge, then he is not a scholar. This meaning was mentioned previously in al-Baqarah 2:Abu Razin Al-Rabbani said: He is the knowledgeable and wise. Shu’bah narrated on the authority of Asim on the authority of Zar’an Abdullah bin Mas’ud: But be rabbanin. He said: Wise scholars. Ibn Jubayr: Wise and pious. Ad-Dahhak said: No one should abandon memorizing the Qur’an as much as he can, because God the Almighty says: But be rabbanin. Ibn Zayd said: The rabbanin are the governors, and the rabbanin are the scholars. Mujahed said: The rabbis are above the scholars. An-Nahhas said: It is a good statement, because the scholars are the scholars. The rabbi is the one who combines knowledge with insight into politics. It is taken from the Arab saying: The Lord of the people’s affairs, he raises it if he fixes it and takes care of it, so he is rab and rabbi in the plural. Abu Ubaidah said: I heard a scholar say: The rabbi is the one who knows what is permissible and what is forbidden, the one who commands and forbids, the one who knows the report of the nation and what was and what will be. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said on the day Ibn Abbas died: Today the rabbi of this nation died. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There is no believing man or woman, free or slave, but that God Almighty has a right over him to learn from the Qur’an and understand His religion. Then he recited this verse: But be devout scholars of the Lord. The verse. Narrated by Ibn Abbas. God the Almighty said: Because you taught the books and because you studied. Abu Amr and the people of Medina read it with a light pronunciation from knowledge. Abu Hatim preferred this reading. Abu Amr said: And its confirmation is you study. He did not say you study with a heavy pronunciation from teaching. Ibn Amir and the people of Kufa read it with a heavy pronunciation from teaching, and Abu Ubaid preferred it. He said: Because it combines two meanings: you know and you study. Makki said: The heavy pronunciation is more expressive, because every teacher is a scholar in the sense of teaches, and not everyone who teaches something is a teacher. The heavy pronunciation indicates knowledge and teaching, while the light pronunciation only indicates knowledge. Teaching is more expressive and praiseworthy, while other than it is more blameworthy. Those who preferred the light pronunciation cited as evidence the words of Ibn Masoud. He said: Be rabbis, wise scholars. So it is far-fetched to say: Be jurists, wise scholars, with your teaching. Al-Hasan said: Be wise scholars with your knowledge. Abu Haywah read: You study from I study means I study. Mujahid read you learn with a fatha on the ta and a shaddah on the lam, meaning you learn.
3:80: Ibn Amir, Asim and Hamzah read it in the accusative case, in apposition to that he should give it to him. This is strengthened by the fact that the Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you want us to take you, O Muhammad, as a lord? God Almighty said: It is not for a human being that God should give him the Scripture, wisdom and prophethood - until His saying: nor does he command you. The pronoun in it refers to humans, meaning nor does the human being command you, meaning Jesus and Ezra. The rest read it in the nominative case, as a resumption and a break from the first statement, and the pronoun in it refers to the name of God Almighty, meaning nor does God command you to take. This reading is strengthened by the fact that in the Mushaf of Abdullah it says and he will not command you, which indicates a resumption, and the pronoun also refers to God Almighty, as mentioned by Makki, and Sibawayh and Az-Zajjaj said. Ibn Jurayj and a group said: “nor does Muhammad, peace be upon him, command you”. This is the reading of Abu Amr, Al-Kisa’i and the people of the Two Sanctuaries. That you take them as lords for them. Does He command you to disbelieve after you are Muslims? By way of denial and astonishment, God Almighty forbade the prophets to take people as servants to deify them, but He obligated creation to respect them. It has been proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Let none of you say, My slave or My female slave, but let him say, My boy or My girl. And let none of you say, My Lord, but let him say, My master. And in the revelation: Mention me to your Lord. And there comes an explanation of this meaning, God willing.
3:81: It was said: God took a covenant from the prophets that they would believe in each other and command some of them to believe in each other, so that is the meaning of support through belief. This is the saying of Saeed bin Jubair, Qatada, Tawus, As-Suddi and Al-Hasan, and it is the apparent meaning of the verse. Tawus said: God took a covenant from the first of the prophets to believe in what the last brought. Ibn Masoud read: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture. Al-Kisa'i said: It is possible that And when God took a covenant from the prophets means when God took a covenant from those with the prophets. The Basrans said: If God took a covenant from the prophets, then He took a covenant from those who were with them, because they followed them and believed them. And in His statement lama means who. Sibawayh said: I asked Al-Khalil bin Ahmad about His statement: And when God took a covenant from the prophets, What I have given you of the Book and wisdom," and he said: "lama means who." An-Nahhas said: The meaning is based on Al-Khalil’s statement, to that which I have given you, then the ha’ was deleted due to the length of the name. Which is raised by the beginning and its predicate is of the Book and wisdom. “Min” is for clarifying the genus. This is like the saying of the speaker: Zayd is better than you, and this is the saying of Al-Akhfash that it is the lam of beginning. Al-Mahdawi said: His statement, Then he came to you, and what follows it is a sentence connected to the relative clause, and the pronoun referring back to it is deleted, and the meaning is then a messenger came to you confirming it. God the Almighty said: Then there came to you a Messenger confirming that which is with you, that you must believe in him and support him. The Messenger here is Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, in his statement Ali and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them. Even though the word is indefinite, the reference is to a specific person, like God the Almighty’s statement: “God presents an example: a city that was safe and secure” until His statement: And there had certainly come to them a Messenger from among themselves, but they denied him. So God took a covenant from all the prophets that they would believe in Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and support him if they ever found him, and He commanded them to take that covenant, as it is like a succession. It is as you say in speech: I took your covenant that you will do such and such, as if you said I make you swear, and the separation between the oath and its answer is by the preposition lama in the recitation of Ibn Kathir as will come. And whoever opens it makes it the recipient of the oath, which is taking the covenant. And the lam in that you will believe in him is the answer to an omitted oath, meaning, by God, that you will believe in him. Al-Mubarrad, Al-Kisa’i and Al-Zajjaj said: “It is not a condition that the lam of verification is entered upon it as it is entered upon in, and its meaning is for whatever I have given you, so the position of what is accusative, and the position of what I have given you is jussive, and “then he came to you” is conjoined to it, that you will believe in him. The lam in his statement that you will believe in him is the answer to the condition, like the statement of the Most High: And if We will, We will surely take away and the like. Al-Kisa’i said: that you will believe in him is the basis of the oath, so it is connected to the first statement, and the answer to the condition is his statement: But whoever turns away after that. In this way, it does not need anything except the estimation of a pronoun. The people of Kufa read when I have given you with a kasra on the lam, and it also means who and it is related to taking, meaning that God took His covenant for the sake of what He gave them of the Book and wisdom, then if there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you will believe in him after the covenant: because taking the covenant is in the meaning of swearing as mentioned above. Al-Nahhas said: Abu Ubaidah has a good statement on this. He said: The meaning is, And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, ‘You shall believe in what I have given you of the Torah.’ It was said: There is an ellipsis in the speech, and the meaning is, And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘You shall teach the people what has come to you of the Book and wisdom, and you shall take from the people that they shall believe.’ This ellipsis is indicated by and you have taken upon you My covenant. It was said: The lam in His statement, when in the reading of those who break it means after, meaning after what I have given you of the Book and wisdom, as Al-Nabigha said: I imagined her verses and I knew her for six years and this year is the seventh That is, after six years. Saeed bin Jubair read lama with emphasis, and its meaning is when I came to you. It is possible that its origin is lightening, so min was added according to the doctrine of those who see its addition in the answer, so it became lam ma, and the nun was changed to mim for assimilation, so three mims came together, so the first one was deleted for lightening. The people of Madinah read atainakum for glorification. The rest read atayyakum in the singular form. Then, all the prophets were not given the Book, only some were given it, but the upper hand is for those who were given the Book. What is meant is taking the covenant of all the prophets, so whoever was not given the Book is in the same ruling as whoever was given the Book because he was given the judgment and prophethood. Also, whoever was not given the Book is commanded to take the Book of the one who came before him, so he falls under the description of whoever was given the Book. God the Almighty said: Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourselves My covenant? They said, We have acknowledged. He said, Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses. “Acknowledged” is from acknowledgment. “Isr” and Isr are two languages, and it means a covenant. Isr in the language means heaviness, so the covenant was called Isr because it means prevention and severity. He said, “Then bear witness means know, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Zajjaj: Explain because the witness is the one who confirms the claim of the plaintiff. It was said that the meaning is, Bear witness against yourselves and your followers. “And I am with you among the witnesses” over you and over them. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: God the Almighty said to the angels, Bear witness against them, so it is a metaphor for something not mentioned.
3:82: (of) is a condition. So whoever among the nations of the prophets turned away from the faith after taking the covenant, they are the wicked, meaning those who have departed from the faith. And the wicked is the one who has departed. And it has been mentioned before.
3:83: The Almighty said: Do they seek other than the religion of God? Al-Kalbi said: Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf and his companions argued with the Christians before the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and they said: Which of us has more right to the religion of Abraham? The Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, said: Both groups are innocent of his religion. They said: We are not satisfied with your judgment and we do not accept your religion. Then, Do they seek other than the religion of God? was revealed, meaning they seek. And the subject of ghair was made yabughun, meaning they seek other than the religion of God. Abu Amr alone read yabughun with the ya' as a predicate and to him you return with the ta' as a second person addressee. He said: Because the first is specific and the second is general, so they were distinguished because of their difference in meaning. Hafs and others read yabughun and yaji'un with the ya' in both, because of His statement: Then those are the transgressors. The rest read with the ta' in both as an address, because of His statement: For what I have given you of the Book and wisdom. And God knows best. The Almighty said: And to Him I submit meaning I surrender, submit, obey, and humble myself. Every creature is submissive and obedient, because it is created with something that it cannot escape. Qatada said: The believer submits willingly, and the disbeliever submits unwillingly when he dies, and that does not benefit him, because of His saying: So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment. Mujahid said: The conversion of the infidel to Islam is unwilling because he prostrates to other than God and his shadow prostrates to God. Have they not seen what God has created of things, whose shadows extend to the right and the left, prostrating to God, while they are humbled? “And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, and so do their shadows in the mornings and the evenings.” It was said: The meaning is that God created creation as He wanted from them, so among them are the handsome and the ugly, the tall and the short, the healthy and the sick, and all of them are obedient by necessity. The healthy is obedient and obedient, loving that, and the sick is obedient and submissive, even if he is unwilling. Obedience is submission and following with ease. Unwillingness is that which is with difficulty and refusal from the soul. Willingly and by compulsion are two sources in the place of the state, meaning obedient and compelled. Anas bin Malik narrated that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the Almighty’s words: And to Him submits whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion, he said, The angels obeyed him in the heavens, and the Ansar and Abd al-Qais on the earth. And he, peace be upon him, said: Do not curse my companions, for my companions submitted out of fear of God, and the people submitted out of fear of the sword. Ikrimah said: Willingly is the one who submitted without argument, and unwillingly is the one who was forced by the argument to monotheism. This is indicated by the words of God the Almighty: And if you ask them who created them, they will surely say, ‘God.’ “And if you ask them, who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon, they will surely say, ‘God.’” Al-Hasan said: It is a general meaning with a specific meaning. And from him: All those in the heavens submitted, and the speech was completed. Then he said: And the earth, willingly or unwillingly. He said: The hypocrite who is unwilling will not benefit from his deeds. Willingly or unwillingly are two sources in the place of the state. On the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: If one of your animals finds it difficult or it is a sun, then let him recite in its ear this verse: Is it other than the religion of God that they seek, while to Him submits all who are in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly? to the end of the verse.
3:84: "Say, 'We believe in God and what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Tribes, and what was given to Moses, Jesus, and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him.'"
3:85: (ghair) is the object of (yabtagh), (dinaa) is accusative as an explanation, and it is permissible for dinaa to be accusative with yabtagh, and ghair to be accusative as a state of religion. Mujahid and As-Suddi said: This verse was revealed about Al-Harith bin Suwaid, the brother of Al-Jalas bin Suwaid, and he was one of the Ansar. He and twelve others with him apostatized from Islam and went to Mecca as disbelievers, so this verse was revealed, then he sent to his brother asking for repentance. This was narrated from Ibn Abbas and others. Ibn Abbas said: He converted to Islam after the verses were revealed. And in the Hereafter he will be among the losers. Hisham said: That is, he will be a loser in the Hereafter among the losers. If it were not for this, I would have distinguished between the relative clause and the relative pronoun. Al-Mazini said: The alif and lam are the same in the man. This was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah when He said: And indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous.
3:86: "Ibn Abbas said: A man from the Ansar converted to Islam, then apostatized and joined polytheism, then regretted it. So he sent to his al-Nas 114:Ask the Messenger of God for me, is there any chance for me to repent? So his people came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Is there any chance for him to repent? So the verse was revealed: "How can God guide a people who disbelieved after their belief?" until His saying: "Forgiving, Most Merciful. So he sent to him and he converted to Islam. Narrated by al-Nasa'i. And "In another narration: A man from the Ansar converted to Islam and joined the polytheists, so God revealed: "How can God guide a people who disbelieved?" until His saying: "Except those who repent?" So his people sent it to him, and when it was read to him, he said: By God, my people did not call me a liar on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor did I call the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a liar on the authority of God, and God Almighty is the most truthful of the three. So he returned repentant, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted it from him and left him." Al-Hasan said: It was revealed about the Jews because they were giving good tidings of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and were asking for victory over those who disbelieved. When he was sent, they were stubborn and disbelieved, so God Almighty revealed: The reward of those is that upon them is the curse of God and of the angels and of mankind, all together.
