Then it was said: How is an interrogative word and its meaning is denial, meaning God does not guide. Similar to it is His statement: How can there be a covenant for the polytheists with God and with His Messenger? meaning they will not have a covenant. The poet said: How can I sleep on the bed while the people are in a fierce raid? That is, I have no sleep. And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. It is said: The apparent meaning of the verse is that whoever disbelieves after his conversion to Islam, God will not guide him, and whoever is a wrongdoer, God will not guide him. We have seen many apostates who have converted to Islam and God has guided them, and many wrongdoers have repented from wrongdoing. It is said to him: Its meaning is that God will not guide them as long as they persist in their disbelief and wrongdoing and do not accept Islam. But if they convert to Islam and repent, God has guided them to that. And God knows best.
3:87: That is, if they persist in their disbelief. The meaning of the curse of God and the people has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it.
3:88: Nor do they give respite meaning they do not delay or postpone.
3:89: Then he excluded the repentant ones and said: Except those who repent, that is Al-Harith bin Suwaid as mentioned above. The meaning of the verse includes everyone who returns to Islam and is sincere.
3:90: Qatada, Ata' al-Khurasani and al-Hasan said: It was revealed about the Jews who disbelieved in Jesus and the Gospel, then they increased in disbelief in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Qur'an. Abu al-Aaliyah said: It was revealed about the Jews and Christians who disbelieved in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, after believing in his description and attributes. Then they increased in disbelief by continuing in their disbelief. It was also said: They increased in disbelief by the sins they acquired. This is the choice of al-Tabari, and according to him it refers to the Jews. Their repentance will not be accepted is problematic because of his statement: And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants and pardons misdeeds. It was said that the meaning is that their repentance will not be accepted at death. An-Nahhas said: This is a good statement, as God the Almighty said: And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, Indeed, I have repented now." It was narrated from al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ata'. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "God accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he is not at the point of death." This meaning will be explained in Surat An-Nisa. It was said: Their repentance will not be accepted which they were upon before they disbelieved, because disbelief had nullified it. It was also said: Their repentance will not be accepted if they repent from their disbelief to another disbelief, and their repentance will only be accepted if they repent to Islam. Qatrib said: This verse was revealed about a group of people from Mecca who said: We are waiting for Muhammad to be struck by a calamity of fate, and if we decide to return, we will return to our people. So God revealed: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief, their repentance will never be accepted. That is, their repentance will not be accepted while they persist in disbelief. So He called it an unacceptable repentance because the people did not have a sound resolve, and God, the Almighty, accepts all repentance if the resolve is sound.
3:91: Filling with kasra is the amount that fills something, and filling with fatha is the source of filling something, and it is said: Give me its fullness and its two fullness and three fullness. The waw in and if he ransomed himself with it is said to be an intrusive and redundant letter, meaning: no one will be accepted to fill the earth with gold if he ransomed himself with it. The grammarians who are experts in the field of reasoning said: The waw cannot be intrusive because it indicates a meaning. The meaning of the verse is: no one will be accepted to fill the earth with gold as a donation even if he ransomed himself with it. And gold is in the accusative case for interpretation according to Al-Farra'. Al-Mufaddal said: The condition of interpretation is that the speech be complete and vague, like your saying I have twenty, so the number is known and the counted is vague, so if you say a dirham, you explain. The accusative of the distinguishing is in fact intrusive because it has nothing to lower it or raise it, and the accusative is the lightest of the vowels, so it is made for everything that has no factor. Al-Kisa’i said: It is in the accusative case with the omission of min meaning of gold, like his saying: or equivalent to that in fasting. Meaning, of fasting. In Al-Bukhari and Muslim on the authority of Qatada, “On the authority of Anas bin Malik, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The disbeliever will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to him: Tell me, if you had the earth full of gold, would you ransom yourself with it? He will say: Yes. It will be said to him: You were asked for something easier than that.” The wording of Al-Bukhari. Muslim said: Instead of ‘I was,’ ‘I lied,’ ‘I was asked.’
3:92: There are two issues: First: The imams narrated, and the wording is from Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Anas, who said: When this verse was revealed, You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. Abu Talha said: Our Lord asks us about our wealth, so I bear witness, O Messenger of God, that I have dedicated my land to God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Dedicate it to your relatives, Hassan bin Thabit and Ubayy bin Ka’b. In Al-Muwatta’, the most beloved of his wealth to him was Bayruha’, which faced the mosque. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to enter it and drink from its pure water. And he mentioned the hadith. In this verse, there is evidence of the use of the apparent and general address, for the Companions, may God be pleased with them all, did not understand anything other than that from the meaning of the address when the verse was revealed. Do you not see that when Abu Talha heard, You will never attain righteousness until you spend, he did not need to stop until he explained what God wants His servants to spend from with another verse or a clear Sunnah, for they love many things. And Zaid bin Haritha did the same. He took a horse called Subul from what he loved and said: O God, You know that I have no wealth more beloved to me than this horse of mine. So he brought it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: This is for the sake of God. So he said to Usama bin Zaid, Take it. Zaid seemed to feel bad about that. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has accepted it from you. Asad bin Musa mentioned it. Ibn Umar freed his freed slave Nafi’, and Abdullah bin Ja’far had given him a thousand dinars for him. Safiyya bint Abi Ubaid said: I think he interpreted the words of God, the Almighty: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. Shibl narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari to buy him a slave girl from the captives of Jalula on the day of the conquest of Mada'in Kisra, in the fight against Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. Umar called for her and she pleased him, so he said: God the Almighty says: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. So Umar, may God be pleased with him, freed her. It was narrated on the authority of al-Thawri that he heard that the mother of the slave girl al-Rabi' ibn Khaitham said: When a beggar came to him, he would say to me: O so-and-so, give the beggar some sugar, for al-Rabi' loves sugar. Sufyan said: He interprets the words of God the Almighty: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love. It was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Abdul Aziz that he used to buy quantities of sugar and give it in charity. It was said to him: Why don't you give its value in charity? He said: Because sugar is dearer to me, so I wanted to spend from that which I love. Al-Hassan said: You will not attain what you love except by abandoning what you desire, and you will not attain what you hope for except by being patient with what you hate. Second: They differed in the interpretation of righteousness. It was said that it means Paradise, according to Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Ata, Mujahid, Amr ibn Maymun, and As-Suddi. The meaning is that you will not attain the reward of righteousness until you spend from what you love. And giving is giving, from your saying I gave him a giving. And a favor reached me from so-and-so, meaning it reached me. So the meaning is that you will not reach Paradise and be given it until you spend from what you love. And it was said: Righteousness is righteous action. And in the authentic hadith: You must be truthful, for it leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: It means obedience. Ata’ said: You will not attain the honor of religion and piety until you give in charity while you are healthy and miserly, hoping for a living and fearing poverty. And from Al-Hasan: Until you spend is the obligatory zakat. Mujahid and Al-Kalbi: It is abrogated, abrogated by the verse on zakat. And it was said: The meaning is until you spend from what you love in the way of goodness, whether in charity or other acts of obedience, and this is comprehensive. And An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Sa’sa’ah bin Mu’awiyah, who said: A Muslim slave who spends from all his wealth in the way of God, two pairs will be received by the guardians of Paradise, all of them calling him to what they have. I said: How is that? He said: If it is camels, then two camels, and if it is cows, then two cows. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: This verse showed them the virtue of chivalry. That is, you will not attain My kindness to you except by being kind to your brothers and spending on them from your wealth and status. So if you do that, My kindness and compassion will attain you. Mujahid said: It is like His statement: {And they give food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor. And whatever you spend - indeed, God is Knowing of it.} That is, if He knows, He will reward for it.
3:93: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: lawful meaning lawful, then He made an exception and said: Except what Israel made unlawful for himself. He is Jacob, peace be upon him. In Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell us, what did Israel forbid himself? He said: He lived among the Bedouins and complained of sciatica, and he did not find anything that suited him except camel meat and milk, so he forbade them. They said: You are right. And he mentioned the hadith. And it is said: He vowed that if he recovered from it, he would give up the food and drink he loved most, and the food and drink he loved most were camel meat and milk. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada and Al-Suddi said: Jacob, peace be upon him, came from Harran intending to go to Jerusalem when he fled from his brother Esau. He was a strong and powerful man. A king met him and Jacob thought he was a thief, so he tried to defeat him. The king nudged Jacob’s thigh, peace be upon him. Then the king ascended to heaven while Jacob was looking at him. He suffered from sciatica, which caused him severe suffering. He could not sleep at night because of the pain and would spend the night screaming. Jacob, peace be upon him, swore that if God, the Almighty, healed him, he would not eat a vein or eat food that contained a vein, so he forbade it to himself. After that, his sons would follow the veins and extract them from the flesh. The reason for the king’s nudging of Jacob was that he had vowed that if God gave him twelve sons and he came to Jerusalem healthy, he would slaughter the last one. This was done to fulfill his vow, according to Ad-Dahhak. Second: There is a difference of opinion as to whether the prohibition was imposed by Jacob based on his own efforts or by permission from God Almighty? The first correct opinion is that God the Almighty added the prohibition to it by His saying: Except what He has forbidden. And that if the Prophet’s ijtihad leads him to something, it is a religion that we must follow because God the Almighty has confirmed it for him. And just as it is revealed to him and it is necessary to follow it, likewise he is given permission to exert himself, and the result of his ijtihad is determined if he is able to do so. And if permission had not been given to him to prohibit that, he would not have climbed over the ladder of making it permissible and forbidden. And our Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, prohibited honey according to the authentic narration, or his servant Maria, but God did not approve of his prohibition and revealed: You have not forbidden what God has made lawful for you, as will be explained in the prohibition. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: It can be said: The general meaning of God the Almighty’s saying: You have not forbidden what God has made lawful, requires that it is not specific to Maria. Al-Shafi’i saw that the obligation of expiation in that is not reasonable in meaning, so he made it specific to the place of the text. Abu Hanifa saw that as a principle in the prohibition of everything permissible and treated it as an oath. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Say: Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful. Ibn Abbas said: When Jacob, peace be upon him, was afflicted with sciatica, the doctors prescribed that he avoid camel meat, but he forbade it to himself. The Jews said: We only forbid ourselves camel meat because Jacob forbade it and God revealed its prohibition in the Torah. So God revealed this verse. Ad-Dahhak said: God denied them and responded to them, saying: O Muhammad, “Say: Then bring the Torah and recite it, if you should be truthful.” But they did not.
3:94: Then the Almighty said: But whoever invents a lie against God after that - it is those who are the wrongdoers. Al-Zajjaj said: In this verse is the greatest evidence of the prophethood of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He informed them that it was not in their book, and ordered them to bring the Torah, but they refused, meaning they knew that he said that through revelation. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: It was only forbidden to them because Jacob forbade it to them. That is because Israel said when he was afflicted with sciatica: By God, if God cures me of it, I will not eat it for you or me, and that was not forbidden to them. Al-Kalbi said: God Almighty did not forbid it to them in the Torah, but He forbade it after the Torah because of their injustice and disbelief. When the Children of Israel committed a great sin, God Almighty forbade them good food, or poured upon them a punishment, which is death. This is what God Almighty said: But because of the words of those who were Jews, We forbade them [some] good things that had been lawful to them Al-Anfal 13:10. And His statement: And We forbade those who were Jews every animal with claws. The verse - to His saying: That is how We rewarded them for their transgression, and indeed, We are truthful. Fourth: Ibn Majah included in his Sunan the medicine for sciatica. Hisham bin Ammar and Rashid bin Saeed Al-Ramli told us: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: Hisham bin Hassan told us: Anas bin Sirin told us that he heard Anas bin Malik say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Healing sciatica: Melt the buttocks of an Arabian sheep, then divide it into three parts, then drink one part on an empty stomach every day. Al-Tha’labi also included it in his interpretation from the hadith of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about sciatica: Take the buttocks of an Arabian ram, neither young nor old, and cut them into small pieces, then take out its dung and divide it into three parts, one third on an empty stomach every day. Anas said: So I prescribed it to more than a hundred people and they were cured, God willing. Shu’bah: An old man told me during the time of Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf about sciatica: I swear to you by God the Most High, if you do not stink, I will burn you in fire or shave you with a razor. Shu’bah said: I have tried it, say it and wipe that place.
3:95: That is, say, O Muhammad, God has spoken the truth, that it was not forbidden in the Torah. So follow the religion of Abraham, the upright one. He was commanded to follow his religion. And he was not of the polytheists. He responded to them in their false claim, as mentioned above.
3:96: It has five issues: First: It is proven in Sahih Muslim that Abu Dharr said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the first mosque established on earth. He said: Al-Masjid Al-Haram. I said: Then which? He said: Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa. I said: How much time is between them? He said: Forty years, then the earth is a mosque for you, so wherever the prayer time comes, pray. Mujahid and Qatada said: No house was established in the direction of prayer. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: There were many houses before the house, meaning that it was the first house established for worship. Mujahid said: The Muslims and the Jews boasted, so the Jews said: Jerusalem is better and greater than the Kaaba, because it is the place of migration of the prophets and it is in the Holy Land. The Muslims said: Rather, the Kaaba is better, so God revealed this verse. The construction of the House and the first to build it have already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Mujahid said: God created the location of this House two thousand years before He created anything on earth, and its foundations are in the seventh lowest earth. As for the Al-Aqsa Mosque, it was built by Solomon, peace be upon him, as Al-Nasa’i narrated with a sound chain of transmission from “the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When Solomon, son of David, built the Holy House, he asked God for three things: He asked God Almighty for a rule that would match His rule, and he was given it. He asked God Almighty for a kingdom that no one after him would deserve, and he was given it. And when he finished building the mosque, he asked God Almighty that no one would come to it with nothing but prayer in it, and that He would bring him out of his sin as on the day his mother bore him, and he was given it.” So there is a problem between the two hadiths, because there were long periods between Abraham and Solomon. The historians said: More than a thousand years. It was said: Abraham and Solomon, peace be upon them, only renewed what others had founded. It has been narrated that the first to build the House was Adam, peace be upon him, as mentioned above. So it is possible that someone other than him from his descendants built the Holy House forty years after him, and it is also possible that the angels built it after building the House with God’s permission, and each is possible. And God knows best. Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: God Almighty commanded the angels to build a house on Earth and to circumambulate it. This was before the creation of Adam. Then Adam built what he built and circumambulated it, then the prophets after him, then Abraham, peace be upon him, completed its construction. Second: The Almighty’s saying: For the one at Bakkah is the predicate of in and the lam is for emphasis. And Bakkah is the location of the House, and Mecca is the rest of the country, according to Malik bin Anas. Muhammad bin Shihab said: Bakkah is the mosque, and Mecca is the entire sanctuary, and houses are included in it. Mujahid said: Bakkah is Mecca. So the mīm in this case is replaced by the bā’, as they said: sticky and inseparable clay. Ad-Dahhak and the historian said the same. Then it was said: Bakkah is derived from bak, which means crowding. The people crowded together. It was called Bakkah because of the crowding of people in the place of their circumambulation. And bak means breaking the neck. It was said: It was called that because it used to break the necks of tyrants if they committed injustice there. Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr said: No tyrant ever intended to harm it except that God, the Almighty, punished him. As for Mecca, it was said that it was named thus because of its scarcity of water. It was also said that it was named thus because it sucks the marrow from the bone, which causes difficulty to the one who intends to go there, from their saying: Makakat al-Azm if you extract what is in it. And the young camel sucks its mother’s udder and drinks it if it sucks all the milk in it and drinks it. The poet said: She wrote, but there were no pearls left in her heart. It was said: It was called this because it enables injustice in it, i.e. it destroys and diminishes it. It was also said: It was called this because people used to laugh and make noise in it, from His statement: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands (al-Anfal 8:35), i.e. clapping and whistling. This is not required by the inflection, because <Makkah>is a doubled dual and <Makka>is a defective triliteral. Third: The Almighty’s saying: blessed. He made it blessed because of the multiplication of work in it, so blessing is the abundance of good. It is accusative as a state of the implied in <place>or as an adverb of <Bakkah>, meaning: the one who settled in Bakkah blessed. It is permissible in other than the Qur’an to use <blessed>, as a second predicate, or as a substitute for who, or as an implied subject. And guidance for the worlds is in apposition to it, and it has the meaning of and it is guidance for the worlds. It is permissible in other than the Qur’an to use <blessed>in the accusative as an adjective for the house.
3:97: Fourth: The Almighty's saying: In it are clear signs is raised by the beginning or by the description. The people of Mecca, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Saeed bin Jubair read <a clear sign>as a singular, meaning the Station of Abraham alone. They said: The trace of his feet in the Station is a clear sign. Mujahid interpreted the Station of Abraham as the entire Sanctuary, so he went to the fact that among its signs are Safa and Marwa, the Corner, and the Station. The rest used the plural. They meant the Station of Abraham, the Black Stone, Al-Hateem, Zamzam, and all the sacred sites. Abu Jaafar Al-Nahhas said: Whoever recites clear signs his recitation is clearer, because Safa and Marwa are signs. Among them is that the bird does not fly over the Kaaba while it is healthy. Among them is that the bird of prey seeks prey but when it enters the sanctuary it leaves it. Among them is that when the rain falls towards the Yemeni corner, there is fertility in Yemen, and when it falls towards the Levant, there is fertility in the Levant, and when it covers the Kaaba, there is fertility in all countries. Among them is that the pebbles, whatever is added to them, are seen in the same amount. The station is from their saying: I stood up a station, which is the place where one stands. The station is from your saying: I established a station. This has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah, and the disagreement has also been mentioned in the station and the correct one from it. The station was raised on the subject and the predicate is omitted, and the estimate from it is the station of Abraham, as Al-Akhfash said. It was narrated from Muhammad bin Yazid that he said: Standing instead of Signs and there is a third saying meaning it is the station of Abraham. The saying of Al-Akhfash is well-known in the speech of the Arabs. As Zuhair said: It has its own provisions and helpers who will bring it with them, and when it is emptied it will be crushed. That is, it passed and after its flow. And Abu al-Abbas said: Maqam means Maqamat because it is a source. God Almighty said: God has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing. And the poet said: Eyes that have disease at their edges Yes, at its edges. This is strengthened by the hadith narrated: The entire Hajj is the Station of Abraham. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And whoever enters it shall be safe. Qatada said: This is also one of the signs of the Sacred Sanctuary. An-Nahhas said: It is a good statement, because people were being snatched from around it, and no tyrant could reach it, and it reached the Holy House and was destroyed, but it did not reach the Sacred Sanctuary. God the Almighty said: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the elephant? (al-Fil 105:1). Some of the scholars of meaning said: The form of the verse is a statement and its meaning is a command, its meaning is: And whoever enters it, make him safe, like His saying: There shall be no obscenity nor wickedness nor disputing during Hajj. (al-Baqarah 2:197) meaning do not speak obscenities nor commit wickedness nor argue. For this meaning, the previous Imam An-Nu’man ibn Thabit said: Whoever commits a sin and deserves a punishment for it, then seeks refuge in the Sacred Sanctuary, He will protect him, because of His saying: And whoever enters it shall be safe. So God the Almighty made safety obligatory for whoever enters it. This was narrated from a group of the Salaf, including Ibn Abbas and others. Ibn al-Arabi said: “Whoever said this has made a mistake in two ways: First, he did not understand from the verse that it was report of what had happened in the past, and he did not intend by it to prove a future ruling. Second, he did not know that that security had gone and that killing and fighting had taken place after that in it, and what God says does not happen in a way that is different from what He tells us, so that indicates that this was in the past.” Abu Hanifa contradicted him and said: If someone takes refuge in the Sacred Sanctuary, he is not given food, drink, treatment, or speech until he leaves, so his being forced to leave does not make security valid. It was narrated from him that he said: Retaliation takes place in the outskirts of the Sacred Sanctuary, and there is no security with this either. The majority of scholars agree that the prescribed punishments are carried out in the Sacred Sanctuary. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the killing of Ibn Khatal while he was clinging to the curtains of the Kaaba.” I said: Al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Whoever commits a punishment in the Sacred Sanctuary, it will be carried out on him there. If he commits it outside the Sacred Sanctuary and takes refuge in the Sacred Sanctuary, he will not be spoken to or given allegiance until he leaves the Sacred Sanctuary and the punishment is carried out on him. This is the opinion of Al-Sha’bi. This is the argument of the Kufians, and Ibn Abbas understood that from the meaning of the verse, as he was the scholar and the scholar of the nation. The correct view is that he intended by that to enumerate the blessings upon everyone who was ignorant of it and denied it among the Arabs, as God the Almighty said: Have they not seen that We have made a secure Sanctuary while people are snatched away all around them? (al-Ankabut 29:67). So in the pre-Islamic era, whoever entered it and took refuge in it was safe from raids and killing, as will be explained in <Al-Ma’idah>, God willing. Qatadah said: Whoever entered it in the pre-Islamic era was safe. This is good. It was narrated that some of the atheists said to some scholars: Isn’t it in the Qur’an: And whoever enters it is safe. We entered it and did such and such, and whoever was in it was not safe! He said to him: Are you not from the Arabs? What does the speaker mean when he says, Whoever enters my house is safe? Isn’t he saying to the one who obeys him, He refrained from him, I made him feel safe and I refrained from him? He said, Yes. He said, So is his statement, ‘And whoever enters it is safe.’ Yahya ibn Ja’dah said, The meaning of ‘And whoever enters it is safe’ is from the Fire. I said: This is not general, because in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, there is a long hadith about intercession: By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, there is none among you who will implore God more fervently to exact the truth than the believers on the Day of Resurrection for their brothers who are in the Fire, saying, ‘Our Lord, they used to fast with us, pray, and perform Hajj.’ It will be said to them, ‘Bring out those whom you recognized.’” The hadith. Only he who enters it to perform the rituals, respecting it, recognizing its rights, and drawing closer to God the Most High, will be safe from its punishment. Ja’far Al-Sadiq said: Whoever enters it in purity as the prophets and saints entered it, will be safe from its punishment. This is the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: “Whoever performs Hajj and does not utter obscenities or commit sins will emerge from his sins as on the day his mother bore him. And an accepted Hajj brings no less than Paradise as a reward.” Al-Hasan said: An accepted Hajj is one who returns ascetic in this world and desirous of the Hereafter. He recited: O Kaaba of God, the supplication of the refugee, the supplication of the one who feels the need He said goodbye to his loved ones and his home, and came between fear and hope. If God accepts his generosity in his endeavor, he will be saved, otherwise he will not be saved. You are one of those whose intercession is hoped for, so be kind to Wafid bin Hajjaj. It was said: The meaning is whoever entered it in the year of the Umrah of expiation with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The evidence for this is the Almighty’s statement: You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing, in safety (al-Fath 48:27). It was also said: Whoever here refers to someone who does not have reason, and the verse is about safety for hunting. This is anomalous. In the revelation: And among them are those who walk on their bellies (al-Nur 24:45) the verse. God Almighty says: “And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God - those who can afford the expenses for one’s journey. And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds.” There are nine issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: By God. The Lām in His saying By God is the Lām of affirmation and obligation. Then He confirmed it with His saying: Upon, which is one of the most emphatic expressions of obligation among the Arabs. So when an Arab says: So-and-so owes me such-and-such, he has confirmed it and made it obligatory. So God Almighty mentioned Hajj with the most eloquent expressions of obligation, emphasizing its right and magnifying its sanctity. There is no disagreement about its obligation, and it is one of the foundations of Islam. It is only obligatory once in a lifetime. Some people said: It is obligatory once every five years, and they narrated a hadith about that which they attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The hadith is invalid and not authentic, and the consensus is against them. I said: “And Abd al-Razzaq said: Sufyan al-Thawri told us, on the authority of al-Ala’ ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The Lord, glory be to Him, says: ‘A servant whom I have given abundant provision to and who does not return to Me is deprived every four years.’ It is well-known from the hadith of al-Ala’ ibn al-Musayyab ibn Rafi’ al-Kahili al-Kufi, from the sons of the hadith scholars. More than one person narrated from him, some of whom said: every five years, and some of whom said: on the authority of al-Ala’, on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabab, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, in other differences. The atheist denied the Hajj, saying: It involves stripping off one’s clothes, which contradicts modesty, and running, which contradicts dignity, and throwing pebbles at the wrong target, which contradicts reason. So they concluded that all of these actions are invalid, because they did not know their wisdom or reason, and they were ignorant that it is not a condition of the Master with the servant that he understands the intended meaning of everything he orders him to do, nor that he is aware of the benefit of his assignment. Rather, he must comply, and he must submit without seeking a benefit or asking about an intended meaning. For this reason, peace be upon him, he used to say in his Talbiyah: “Here I am, truly, truly, in worship and submission, here I am, O God of Truth.” The Imams narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed us and said: O people, God has made Hajj obligatory upon you, so perform Hajj. A man said: Every year, O Messenger of God? He was silent until he said it three times. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If I had said yes, it would have been obligatory and you would not have been able to do it. Then he said: Leave me as I have left you, for those who came before you were destroyed because of their excessive questioning and their disagreement with their prophets. So if I command you to do something, do as much of it as you can, and if I forbid you from something, leave it. This hadith shows that when the address is directed to those charged with an obligation, it is sufficient to do it once and does not require repetition, contrary to what Professor Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini and others said. It is proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked by his companions: O Messenger of God, should we perform Hajj this year or forever? He said: No, forever. This is a text in response to those who said: It is obligatory once every five years. Pilgrimage was known and famous among the Arabs, and it was something they desired for its markets, justification, and piety. When Islam came, they were addressed with what they knew and were obligated to do what they knew. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the pilgrimage before the obligatory pilgrimage, and he stood at Arafat and did not change the law of Abraham as they changed it,” when the Quraysh were standing at the sacred monument and saying, We are the people of the sanctuary, so we will not leave it, and we are the Hams, according to what was explained previously in <Al-Baqarah>. I said: “One of the strangest things I have seen is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj twice before the migration, and that the obligation was dropped from him because of that, because he had answered the call of Abraham when it was said to him: ‘And proclaim to the people the Hajj’ (al-Hajj 22:27).” Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: This is far-fetched, because if it is stated in his law: ‘And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind,’ then it must be obligatory upon him by virtue of the address in his law. If it is said: He only addressed those who had not performed Hajj, then this would be arbitrary and specific, for which there is no evidence, and it would be necessary that this address not be obligatory upon those who performed Hajj according to the religion of Abraham, and this is extremely far-fetched. Second: The Qur’an and Sunnah indicate that Hajj is to be performed without delay, not immediately. This is the conclusion of the Maliki school of thought, as stated by Ibn Khuwayz Mandad, and it is the opinion of al-Shafi’i, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Abu Yusuf in a narration from him. Some of the later Malikis from Baghdad held that it is to be performed immediately, and it is not permissible to delay it if one is able to do so. This is the opinion of Dawud. The first is correct, because God the Almighty said in Surat al-Hajj 22:And proclaim to mankind the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on foot. (al-Hajj 22:27), and Surat al-Hajj was revealed in Mecca. God the Almighty also said: And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind. (al-Hajj 22:27) This Surah was revealed in the year of Uhud in Madinah, the third year of the Hijra. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not perform Hajj until the year ten.” As for the year: “The hadith of Dhimam bin Tha’labah al-Sa’di from Banu Sa’d bin Bakr came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about Islam. He mentioned the testimony, prayer, zakat, fasting, and Hajj.” Narrated by Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, and Anas. All of them mention Hajj, and that it was obligatory. The hadith of Anas is the best and most complete in its context. There is disagreement about the time of his arrival. It was said: the year five. It was said: the year seven. It was said: the year nine. Ibn Hisham mentioned it on the authority of Abu Ubaidah al-Waqidi in the year of the Trench after the withdrawal of the Confederates. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: The evidence that Hajj can be delayed is the consensus of scholars on not declaring a person who is able to perform Hajj a sinner if he delays it for a year or two or the like, and that if he performs Hajj after years of being able to do so, then he has performed the Hajj that was obligatory upon him on time. According to all of them, he is not like someone who missed a prayer until its time had passed and then made it up after its time had passed, nor like someone who was unable to fast Ramadan due to illness or travel and made it up, nor like someone who spoiled his Hajj and made it up. Since they agreed that it is not said to someone who performs Hajj after years of being able to do so: You have fulfilled what was obligatory upon you, we know that the time for Hajj is flexible and that it can be delayed, not immediate. Abu Umar said: Everyone who says that it can be delayed does not set a limit for that, except what was narrated from Sahnun, who was asked about a man who finds what he can do for Hajj and delays it for many years despite being able to do so. Is he a sinner by delaying Hajj and is his testimony rejected? He said: No, even if he is sixty years old. If he is over sixty, then he is a sinner and his testimony is rejected. This is a specific ruling, and the limits in Islamic law are only taken from those who have the right to legislate. I said: Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad narrated it on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim. Ibn al-Qasim and others said: If he delays it for sixty years, there is no problem, but if he delays it after sixty, there is a problem, “because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘The lifespans of my ummah will be between sixty and seventy, and few will exceed that.’ So it is as if the speech might be too tight for him in this decade. Abu ‘Umar said: Some people, such as Sahnun, have used as evidence “the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): ‘The battlefield of my ummah will be between sixty and seventy, and few will exceed that.’” There is no proof in it, because it is a statement that came out of the most likely age of his ummah if the hadeeth is authentic. It is evidence for extending it to seventy because it is also the most likely age, and one should not conclude that someone whose justice and trustworthiness are authentic is a sinner based on such a weak interpretation. And God is the Grantor of success. Third: The scholars agreed that the address in the words of God the Almighty: And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by mankind is general for all of them and is extended to all of them. Ibn al-Arabi said: Even though people differed in the absolute generalities, they agreed to apply this verse to all people, male and female, except for the young, who is excluded by consensus from the principles of obligation. Likewise, the slave is not included in it, because he was excluded from the absolute generality by the words of God the Almighty in the end: Whoever can afford it and the slave is not able, because the master prevents him from his rights in this worship. God the Almighty has given precedence to the master’s right over his right out of kindness to the slaves and in their interest. There is no disagreement about this among the nation or among the imams, so we should not speak ill of what we do not know, and there is no evidence for it except consensus. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The majority of the people of knowledge agreed, except for those who are not considered to be disagreeing, that if a boy performs Hajj while he is young, and if a slave performs Hajj while he is a slave, then the boy reaches puberty and the slave is freed, then they are obligated to perform Hajj al-Islam if they find a way to do so. Abu Omar said: Dawud disagreed with a group of jurists of the regions and the imams of the tradition regarding the slave, and that he is addressed with the Hajj, but according to the majority of scholars he is excluded from the general address in the Almighty’s saying: And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by people who can afford the expenses based on the lack of disposal, and that he does not have the right to perform Hajj without his master’s permission, just as he was excluded from the Friday address, which is the Almighty’s saying: O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on Friday (al-Jumuah 62:9) - according to the majority of scholars except for a few exceptions. And just as he was excluded in the address requiring testimony, God the Almighty said: And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called (al-Baqarah 2:282), so the slave was not included in that. And just as it is permissible to exclude the boy from His saying: And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by people (Al Imran 3:97), and he is one of the people based on the fact that the pen has been lifted from him. And the woman was excluded from His saying: O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer and she is one of those included in the name of faith, and likewise the slave was excluded from the aforementioned address. This is the opinion of the jurists of Hijaz, Iraq, Syria and Morocco, and the likes of them are not permitted to distort the interpretation of the Book. If it is said: If he is present in the Sacred Mosque and his master has given him permission, then why is he not obligated to perform Hajj? It is said to him: This is a question based on consensus, and perhaps it cannot be explained, but if this ruling is established based on consensus, we use it as evidence that his Hajj while in slavery is not counted as Hajj al-Islam. “It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Any boy who performs Hajj and then reaches puberty must perform another Hajj. Any Bedouin who performs Hajj and then emigrates must perform another Hajj. Any slave who performs Hajj and then is freed must perform another Hajj.” Ibn al-Arabi said: Some of our scholars were lenient and said: The reason for the slave not being obligated to perform Hajj, even if his master permitted him, is because he was originally a disbeliever and the Hajj of a disbeliever was not considered valid. When he was made a permanent slave, he was not required to perform Hajj. This is invalid for three reasons, so know this: First, that the disbelievers, according to us, are required to perform the branches of the Shari’ah, and there is no disagreement about this in the opinion of Malik. Second, that all acts of worship are obligatory on him, such as prayer and fasting, even though he is a slave. If he did them while he was a disbeliever, they would not be considered valid, so Hajj must be like them. Third, that disbelief was lifted by Islam, so its ruling must be lifted. It is clear that what we have mentioned about the rights of the master being given precedence is what is relied upon. And God is the Grantor of success. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: Whoever can afford a way to it <of>is in the accusative case as a substitute for some of the whole. This is the opinion of most grammarians. Al-Kisa’i permitted <of>to be in the nominative case with <-Hajj>, the estimation being that whoever can afford to perform Hajj to the House. It was said that it is a condition. <and was able>is in the subjunctive mood, and the answer is omitted, meaning whoever can afford to perform Hajj must perform Hajj. Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: It was said, O Messenger of God, is Hajj every year? He said: No, rather Hajj. It was said: What is the way? He said: Provisions and a mount. And it was narrated on the authority of Anas, Ibn Masoud, Ibn Omar, Jabir, Aisha, and Amr bin Shuaib on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather. And on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Pilgrimage to the House is a duty owed to God by people, whoever is able to do so. He was asked about that, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That you find the back of a camel. The hadith of Ibn Omar was also included by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, and Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi in his Jami’, who said: It is a good hadith, and the scholars act upon it that if a man owns provisions and a mount, Hajj is obligatory upon him. Ibrahim bin Yazid is al-Khawzi al-Makki, and some of the scholars of hadith have spoken about him because of his memory. “And they narrated it on the authority of Wakee’ and Ad-Daraqutni on the authority of Sufyan ibn Saeed. They said: Ibrahim ibn Yazid narrated to us on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abbad on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: A man stood up to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what makes Hajj obligatory? He said: Provisions and a mount. He said: O Messenger of God, what is Hajj? He said: Disheveled hair and spitting. Another stood up and said: O Messenger of God, what is Hajj? He said: The hustle and bustle.” Wakee’ said: By hustle he meant the hustle and bustle of the Talbiyah, and the slaughter of the sacrificial animal. This is the wording of Ibn Majah. Among those who said that provisions and a mount are conditions for the obligation of Hajj are: Umar ibn Al-Khattab and his son Abdullah, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Saeed ibn Jubayr, Ata’ and Mujahid. This is the view of Al-Shafi’i, Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah and his companions, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abdul Aziz ibn Abi Salamah and Ibn Habib. Abdus mentioned something similar on the authority of Sahnun. Al-Shafi’i said: “Ability has two aspects: One is that he is physically able and has enough money to perform Hajj. The second is that he is physically disabled and cannot stay on his mount, and he is able to command someone to perform Hajj on his behalf for a fee or without a fee, as will be explained later. As for the one who is physically able, then the obligation of Hajj is obligatory for him according to the Book, as God the Almighty says: “Whoever can afford the expenses of performing Hajj thereto.” As for the one who is financially able, then the obligation of Hajj is obligatory for him according to the Sunnah, as stated in the hadith of al-Khath’amiyyah, as will be explained later. As for the one who is physically able, and he is strong and does not encounter unbearable hardship in riding a mount, if he has the provisions and a mount, then the obligation of Hajj is obligatory for him personally. If he does not have the provisions and a mount, or one of them, then the obligation of Hajj is dropped from him. If he is able to walk and is able to do so and finds the provisions or is able to earn provisions on his way by a craft such as beading, cupping, or the like, then it is recommended for him to perform Hajj on foot, whether he is a man or a woman.” Ash-Shafi’i said: A man has less excuse than a woman because he is stronger. This is recommended, not obligatory, according to them. However, if he is able to obtain provisions by begging people on the road, it is disliked for him to perform Hajj because he becomes a burden on people. Malik ibn Anas may God have mercy on him said: “If he is able to walk and finds provisions, then Hajj is obligatory upon him. If he cannot find a mount and is able to walk, then the obligation of Hajj is obligatory upon him. If he does not own provisions but is able to earn his needs from them on the road, then the obligation of Hajj is also obligatory upon him. If he is one of the honorable people who does not earn his living by himself, then it is not obligatory upon him. If he is one of those who earn his living by trade or industry, then Hajj is obligatory upon him. And likewise, if his habit is to beg people, then Hajj is obligatory upon him. Malik also made Hajj obligatory upon the one who is able to walk, even if he does not have provisions or a mount with him. This is the opinion of Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr, Ash-Sha’bi, and Ikrimah. Ad-Dahhak said: If he is a strong, healthy young man who has no money, then he must hire himself out for his food or his offspring until he completes his Hajj.” Muqatil said to him: Did God command people to walk to the House? He said: If one of them had an inheritance in Mecca, would he abandon it?! Rather, he should go to it even if he had to crawl. Likewise, Hajj is obligatory for him. They used as evidence the words of God the Almighty: And proclaim to mankind the Hajj [pilgrimage]; they will come to you on foot (al-Hajj 22:27), meaning on foot. They said: Because Hajj is one of the acts of worship of the body and one of the individual obligations, it is necessary that provisions and a mount should not be among the conditions for its obligation, like prayer and fasting. They said: Even if the hadith of Al-Khawzi about provisions and a mount were authentic, we would have interpreted it to refer to all people and most of them in distant lands. The general application of speech to most situations is common in the Shariah and in the speech and poetry of the Arabs. Ibn Wahb, Ibn Al-Qasim, and Ashhab narrated from Malik that he was asked about this verse and he said: People in that matter according to their ability, ease, and patience. Ashhab said to Malik: Is it provisions and a mount? He said: No, by God, that is only according to the people’s ability. He may find provisions and a mount but not be able to walk, and another may be able to walk on his feet. Fifth: If he is able and the obligation of Hajj is fulfilled, something may arise that prevents him from doing so, such as a debtor preventing him from going out until he pays off his debt, and there is no disagreement on that. Or he has dependents for whom he is obligated to provide, so Hajj is not obligatory for him until he provides for them during his absence due to his going and returning, because this provision is obligatory immediately, and Hajj is obligatory to be delayed, so giving priority to the dependents is more appropriate. “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘It is enough of a sin for a man to neglect those he provides for.’” Similarly, parents fear being neglected and not being compensated for being kind to them, so he has no way to perform Hajj, because its meaning is because of longing and loneliness, so he should not pay attention to it. A woman is prevented by her husband, and it was said that he does not prevent her. The correct view is that it is forbidden, especially if we say that Hajj is not obligatory immediately. The sea does not prevent the obligation if it is mostly safe - as was explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah - and he knows that he will not be weak. But if it is mostly damaged or weak to the point that he misses the prayer, then it is not. If he cannot find a place to prostrate due to the large number of riders and the narrowness of the place, Malik said: If he cannot bow and prostrate except on his brother’s back, then he should not ride him. Then he said: Should he ride where he cannot pray? Woe to him who abandons prayer! Hajj is dropped if there is an enemy on the road who seeks lives or money unless there is a specific limit or an unjust amount. There is a difference of opinion about its being dropped without unjustification. Al-Shafi’i said: He should not be given a grain and the obligation of Hajj is dropped. It is obligatory for the beggar if that is his habit and he thinks it is most likely that he will find someone to give him. It was said that it is not obligatory, based on what was mentioned above regarding taking ability into consideration. Sixth: If the obstacles are removed and he does not have enough money to perform Hajj with, but he has merchandise, then he must sell some of his merchandise for Hajj, which he can sell for the debt. Ibn al-Qasim was asked about a man who has a sacrifice and nothing else, can he sell it for the obligatory Hajj and leave his children with nothing to live on? He said: Yes, that is upon him, and he should leave his children in charity. The correct opinion is the first, “because the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: It is enough of a sin for a man to neglect those he needs.” This is also the opinion of al-Shafi’i. What appears from his school of thought is that Hajj is not obligatory except for one who has enough money to spend on going and coming back - as he said in al-Imla’ - even if he does not have family or children. Some of them said: Returning is not considered because it is not a great hardship for him to leave his country, because he has no family or children there, and all countries are his homeland. The first is more correct, because a person feels lonely when he is separated from his homeland, just as he feels lonely when he is separated from his home. Do you not see that if a virgin commits adultery, he is flogged and banished from his country, whether he has a family or not? Al-Shafi’i said in Al-Umm: If he has a home and a servant and his family’s expenses are sufficient for his absence, then he is obligated to perform Hajj. The apparent meaning of this is that he considered the money for Hajj to be more than the servant and home, because he gave it precedence over his family’s expenses, so it is as if he said: After all this. His companions said: He is obligated to sell the home and servant and rent a home and a servant for his family. If he has merchandise with which he trades and its profit is sufficient for him and his family on a permanent basis, and whenever he spends from the original merchandise, its profit is lost and is not sufficient for him, is he obligated to perform Hajj from the original merchandise or not? There are two opinions: The first is according to the majority and is the correct and well-known opinion, because there is no disagreement that if he has a property whose yield is sufficient for him, then he is obligated to sell the original property for Hajj, and the same applies to the merchandise. Ibn Shuraih said: He is not obligated to do that, and he should keep the merchandise and not perform Hajj from it, because Hajj is only obligatory upon him for the surplus of his sufficiency. So this discussion is about the ability with the body and money. Seventh: The sick and the bitten, and the bitten is the cutting, and from it the sword was called bitten, and it is as if the one who has reached the point of not being able to hold on to the mount or remain on it is like the one whose limbs have been cut off, as he is not able to do anything. The scholars differed in their ruling after their consensus that they are not obligated to travel to Hajj, because Hajj was only imposed by God on the one who is able by consensus, and the sick and bitten are not able. So Malik said: If he was bitten, the obligation of Hajj is dropped from him originally, whether he was able to have someone perform Hajj on his behalf with money or otherwise, the obligation of Hajj is not obligatory on him even if Hajj was obligatory on him and then he was bitten and the obligation of Hajj was dropped from him, and it is not permissible for Hajj to be performed on his behalf during his lifetime under any circumstances, rather if he bequeathed that Hajj be performed on his behalf after his death, Hajj is performed on his behalf from a third, and it is voluntary, and he provided evidence with the words of God the Almighty: And that man can have nothing but what he strives for (al-Najm 53:39), so He informed that he has nothing but what he strives for. So whoever said that he has the striving of someone else has contradicted the apparent meaning of the verse. And the Almighty said: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God. This is not possible, because Hajj is the intention of the person responsible to go to the House himself, and because it is an act of worship that cannot be performed by a representative if he is unable to do it, like prayer. “And Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, the Almighty, will admit three people into Paradise by means of a single Hajj: the deceased, the one who performs Hajj on his behalf, and the one who carries it out.” Narrated by al-Tabarani Abu al-Qasim Sulayman ibn Ahmad, who said: Amr ibn Husayn al-Sadusi told us, who said: Abu Ma’shar told us on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, and he mentioned it: I said: Abu Ma'shar's name is Najih and he is weak according to them. Al-Shafi'i said: In the case of a sick person who has a bone disease or an old man, he is able to have someone obey him if he orders him to perform Hajj on his behalf, so he is able to some extent. This is of two types: One of them is that he is able to have money with which to hire someone to perform Hajj on his behalf, so he is obligated to perform Hajj. This is the opinion of Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him. It was narrated from him that he said to an old man who had not performed Hajj: Prepare a man to perform Hajj on your behalf. This is the opinion of Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah and his companions, Ibn Al-Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq. The second is that he is able to have someone who will offer him obedience and representation so that he can perform Hajj on his behalf. In this case, Hajj is also obligatory according to Al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Rahawayh. Abu Hanifah said that Hajj is not obligatory if he offers obedience under any circumstances. Al-Shafi’i provided evidence for this with what was narrated by Ibn Abbas: “A woman from Khatham asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, God’s obligation upon His servants in Hajj has come upon my father, who is an old man and cannot stay on his mount. Should I perform Hajj on his behalf? He said: Yes.” This was during the Farewell Pilgrimage. In another narration: He cannot sit upright on the back of his camel. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then perform Hajj on his behalf. Tell me, if your father had a debt, would you pay it off?” She said: Yes. He said: The debt of God is more deserving of being paid off. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made Hajj obligatory upon his daughter’s obedience to him and her offering of herself to him by performing Hajj on his behalf. If this is obligatory upon his daughter’s obedience to him, then it is more appropriate for him to be obligated upon his ability to pay the money with which he is hired. However, if he offers him money without obedience, then the correct view is that he is not obligated to accept it and perform Hajj on his own behalf, and he does not become able to do so by offering him money. Our scholars said: The hadith of Al-Khathamiyyah is not intended to be an affirmation, but rather its purpose is to encourage people to be dutiful to their parents and to look into their interests in this world and in religion and to bring them benefit in nature and in the Shari’ah. When he saw from the woman an apparent reaction and willingness and a sincere desire to be dutiful to her father and a keenness to convey goodness and reward to him, and she regretted that he would miss out on the blessing of Hajj, he agreed to that. He also said to the other who said: My mother vowed to perform Hajj but she did not perform Hajj until she died, so should I perform Hajj on her behalf? He said: “Perform Hajj on her behalf. Do you think that if your mother had a debt, would you have paid it off?” She said: Yes. This indicates that it is a voluntary act and conveying goodness and goodness to the dead. Do you not see that he likened the act of Hajj to a debt? And by consensus, if a person dies and he has a debt, his guardian is not obligated to pay it off from his money, but if he volunteers to do so, the debt is paid on his behalf. And among the evidence that Hajj is not obligatory on her father is what this woman stated explicitly when she said: He is not able to. And whoever is not able is not obligated. This is a statement denying the obligation and preventing the duty. What was denied at the beginning of the hadith is not permissible to be confirmed at the end of it by conjecture. This is confirmed by his statement: The debt of God is more deserving of being paid. There is no consensus on its apparent meaning. The debt of a slave is more deserving of being paid. It begins with it by consensus due to the poverty of man and the independence of God, as stated by Ibn al-Arabi. Abu Omar ibn Abd al-Barr mentioned that the hadith of al-Khath’amiyyah according to Malik and his companions is specific to her. Others said: There is confusion in it. Ibn Wahb and Abu Mus’ab said: It is specifically for the son. Ibn Habib said: The concession came in Hajj on behalf of an old man who has no means of transportation and did not perform Hajj, and on behalf of someone who died and did not perform Hajj, that his son may perform Hajj on his behalf even if he did not leave a will for him, and it is sufficient for him, God willing. This is speaking about the one who was bitten and the like. The hadith of al-Khath’amiyyah was narrated by the imams, and it refutes al-Hasan’s statement that it is not permissible for a woman to perform Hajj on behalf of a man. Eighth: The scholars agreed that if the person responsible does not have enough food to provide himself on the road, he is not obligated to perform Hajj. If a stranger gives him money to perform Hajj with, he is not obligated to accept it, according to consensus, and he is not deemed to be doing so as a favor. If a man gives his father money, Al-Shafi’i said: He is obligated to accept it, because the man’s son is from his earnings and there is no blame on him for that. Malik and Abu Hanifa said: He is not obligated to accept it, because it would nullify the sanctity of fatherhood, since it would be said: He has compensated him and he has fulfilled it. And God knows best. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds. Ibn Abbas and others said: The meaning is whoever disbelieves in the obligation of Hajj and does not see it as obligatory. Al-Hasan al-Basri and others said: Whoever abandons Hajj while he is able to do it is a disbeliever. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Al-Harith on the authority of Ali who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has provisions and a mount to reach the House of God and does not perform Hajj, then it is not upon him to die a Jew or a Christian, because God says in His Book: And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by people, whoever is able to do so. Abu Isa said: This is a strange hadith that we do not know except from this source, and there is talk about its chain of transmission, and Hilal bin Abdullah is unknown, and Al-Harith is considered weak. Similar to it was narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah and Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with them both. And on the authority of Abd Khair bin Yazid on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his sermon: O people, God has made Hajj obligatory upon you for whoever is able to do so, and whoever does not do so, let him die in whatever state he wishes, whether he wishes as a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, unless he has an excuse such as illness or an unjust ruler. He has no share in my intercession or coming to my Pool.” Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has what it takes to perform Hajj but does not perform Hajj, or has wealth on which zakat is due but does not perform Hajj, then he has no share in my intercession or coming to my Pool. He purified him and asked about the return when he was dying. It was said: O Ibn Abbas, we used to consider this for the disbelievers. He said: I will recite to you a Qur’an with it: “O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. And whoever does that - then it is those who are the losers. And spend from what We have provided for you before death approaches one of you and he says, “My Lord, if only You would delay me for a short term so I could give charity and be among the righteous.” (al-Munafiqun 63:9-10), Al-Hasan bin Salih said in his interpretation: So purify yourself and perform Hajj. “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that a man asked him about the verse, and he said: Whoever performs Hajj without hoping for reward or sits without fearing punishment has disbelieved in it.” Qatadah narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: I was thinking of sending men to the provinces to look at whoever had wealth and did not perform Hajj and impose the jizya on him. That is what God, the Most High, said: And whoever disbelieves - then indeed, God is free from need of the worlds. I said: This was taken as a severe warning, and for this reason our scholars said: The verse implies that whoever dies without performing Hajj while he is able, then the threat is directed at him, and it is not sufficient for someone else to perform Hajj on his behalf, because if someone else’s Hajj would relieve him of the obligation, then the threat would be relieved of him. And God knows best. Saeed bin Jubair said: If a wealthy neighbor of mine dies without performing Hajj, then I would not pray over him.
3:98: God Almighty says: Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of God while God is Witness over what you do?’
3:99: The Almighty said: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, why do you avert from the way of God those who believe?' That is, do you turn away from the religion of God those who believe? Al-Hasan read <tasdoon>with a damma on the taa and a kasra on the sad. They are two dialects: sad and asd, like sal al-lahm and asl if it stinks, and kham and akhm also if it changes. tabghinuha 'awjanah means you seek it, so the lam was deleted, like and when you measure them (al-Mutaffifin 83:3). It is said: baghitu lahu kada, meaning you sought it. And abghituhu kada, meaning I helped him. And 'awj' is the inclination and deviation <with a kasra on the 'ayn>in religion, speech, and action and what deviates from the path of straightness. And <with a fatha>in the wall and the wall and every standing person, according to Abu Ubaidah and others. The meaning of the Almighty's saying: They follow the caller, there is no crookedness in him (Ta-Ha 20:108) is they are not able to deviate from his call. And 'awj' in the place and 'awj means he stayed and stood. And the standing one, the poet said: Are you bringing us back so that we may see the courtyards or the traces of the tents? A crooked man: the one with bad manners, and he is between crookedness. The crookedness of horses is the one with a hump in its legs, and the crookedness of horses is attributed to a horse that existed in the pre-Islamic era. It is said: a horse with a hump if it has a wide space between the legs without a hump, and this is praise. It is also said: the hump is a crookedness in the legs. Al-Khalil said that hump is described as severity, and that is not crookedness. The Almighty said: And you are witnesses, meaning rational. It was said: witnesses because it is written in the Torah that the religion of God that no other religion is acceptable is Islam, as it contains a description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
3:100: God Almighty says: O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they will turn you back, after your belief, to disbelief. It was revealed about a Jew who wanted to renew the strife between the Aws and the Khazraj after it had been interrupted by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He sat among them and recited to them a poem that one of the two tribes had said during their war. The other tribe said: Our poet said it on such and such a day. It seemed that something had occurred to them, so they said: Come, let us return the war to its former glory. So these called out: O family of the Aws. And those called out: O family of the Khazraj. So they gathered, took up their weapons, and lined up to fight. Then this verse was revealed. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and stood between the two rows, recited it and raised his voice. When they heard his voice, they listened attentively to him and began to listen. When he finished, they threw down their weapons, embraced one another, and began to weep. Narrated by Ikrimah, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Abbas. The one who did that was Shas bin Qais the Jew. He sent someone to the Aws and Khazraj to remind them of the wars that had taken place between them, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had mentioned them. The people realized that it was a temptation from Satan and a plot from their enemy, so they threw down their weapons, wept, and embraced each other. Then they left with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, listening and obeying. Then God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, meaning the Aws and Khazraj. If you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, meaning Shas and his companions. They will turn you back to disbelief after your belief. Jabir bin Abdullah said: “There was no one more hateful to us than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He gestured to us with his hand, so we stopped, and God Almighty put things right between us. There was no person more beloved to us than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I have never seen a day uglier or more desolate at the beginning and a better end than that day.”
3:101: God the Almighty said: In the form of astonishment, that is, And how can you disbelieve while the verses of God are recited to you meaning the Qur'an. And among you is His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas said: There was fighting and evil between the Aws and the Khazraj in the pre-Islamic era, so they mentioned what had happened between them and some of them attacked each other with swords. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and mentioned that to him, so he went to them, and this verse was revealed: And how can you disbelieve while the verses of God are recited to you and among you is His Messenger - until His saying: And He saved you from it. This verse includes those who did not see the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because what is in them of his Sunnah takes the place of seeing him. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for this address to be specifically to the companions of Muhammad, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was among them and they saw him. It is permissible for this address to be to the entire nation, because his traces and signs and the Qur'an that was given to us are in the place of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, among us, even if we did not see him. Qatada said: In this verse there are two clear signs: the Book of God and the Prophet of God. As for the Prophet of God, he has passed away, and as for the Book of God, God has kept him among them as a mercy and a blessing from Him. In it is what He has made lawful and unlawful, and what He has obeyed and disobeyed. How is in the accusative case, and the fa was opened according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. The opening was chosen for it because what preceded the fa was a ya and it was difficult for them to combine a ya and a kasra. The Almighty said: And whoever holds fast to God means refrains and clings to His religion and obedience to Him. He has been guided means guided and directed to a straight path. Ibn Jurayj said: He holds fast to God believes in Him. It was said: The meaning is whoever holds fast to God means he clings to the rope of God, which is the Qur’an. It is said: he protected himself with it and held fast, and he held fast and held fast if he refrained from it from anything else. I held fast to someone means I prepared for him what he clings to. Everyone who clings to something is protected and holding fast. Everyone who prevents something is a protector. Al-Farazdaq said: I am the son of the two capitals, Banu Tamim. When the two events are great, we will be afflicted. Al-Nabigha said: The sailor remains, fearing his fate, clinging to the bamboo after the distance and the Najd. Another said: So he made a condition for himself while he was in a coma, and he threw his reasons for it and relied on it. And food protected him: it prevented him from hunger. The Arabs say: food protected so-and-so, meaning it prevented him from hunger. So they called the gruel Abu Asim for that reason. Ahmad bin Yahya said: The Arabs called bread Asim and Jabir, and he recited: Do not blame me, blame Jaber, for Jaber has burdened me with the burdens. They call it Amer. And he recited: Abu Malik used to visit me at noon, he would come and leave his luggage at Amer’s. Abu Malik is the nickname of hunger.
3:102: There is one issue: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Mara on the authority of Abdullah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The right to fear Him is that He be obeyed and not disobeyed, that He be remembered and not forgotten, and that He be thanked and not denied. Ibn Abbas said: It is that He not be disobeyed for the blink of an eye. The commentators mentioned that when this verse was revealed, they said: O Messenger of God, who is able to do this? It was difficult for them, so God, the Almighty, revealed: So fear God as much as you are able (al-Taghabun 64:16), and this verse was abrogated, according to Qatada, Ar-Rabi’ and Ibn Zayd. Muqatil said: There is nothing in Al Imran that was abrogated except this verse. It was said: His statement: So fear God as much as you are able is an explanation of this verse. The meaning is: So fear God as He should be feared as much as you are able, and this is more correct, because abrogation only occurs when there is no reunification, and reunification is possible, so it is more appropriate. Ali bin Abi Talha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The statement of God the Almighty, O you who have believed, fear God as He should be feared, has not been abrogated. Rather, the fear of Him as He should be feared means to strive in the cause of God as He should be striven for, and not be deterred by the blame of a blamer for the sake of God, and to stand up for justice even if it is against yourselves and your children. An-Nahhas said: Everything mentioned in the verse is obligatory for Muslims to use and no abrogation has occurred in it. The meaning of the statement of God the Almighty, And do not die except as Muslims, has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah.
3:103: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And hold fast. Protection is fortification, and from this the word badhraqa is called asma. And badhraqa means guarding the caravan, by sending with it someone to protect it from anyone who might harm it. Ibn Khalawayh said: Badhraqa is not an Arabic word, but rather it is a Persian word that the Arabs Arabized. It is said: The sultan sent badhraqa with the caravan. The word rope is a common word, and its origin in the language is the cause by which one reaches a goal or need. The rope is the neck rope. The rope is a rectangle of sand, and from it the hadith: “By God, I did not leave a rope without stopping on it. Is there any Hajj for me?” The rope is the halter. The rope is the covenant. Al-A’sha said: If the ropes of a tribe cross it, it will take its ropes from the other tribe to you. He wants safety. And the rope is tricky. Katheer said: So, do not rush, Ezz, to understand, whether the advice comes from informers or from ropes. And the rope: the hunter’s snare. None of them are intended in the verse except the one with the meaning of the covenant, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Masoud said: The rope of God is the Qur’an. “And Ali and Abu Saeed Al-Khudri narrated it on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and on the authority of Mujahid and Qatadah, similarly. Abu Muawiyah narrated on the authority of Al-Hijri on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This Qur’an is a rope.” And Baqi bin Mukhallad narrated, Yahya bin Abdul Hamid narrated to us, Hisham narrated to us on the authority of Al-Awam bin Hawshab on the authority of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, And hold fast, all together, to the rope of God, and do not be divided, he said: the group. It was narrated on his authority and others from various sources, and the meaning is all close and intertwined, for God the Most High commands harmony and forbids division, for division is destruction, while the group is salvation. May God have mercy on Ibn Al-Mubarak when he said: The community is the rope of God, so hold fast to His firmest handhold for those who are close to Him. Second: The Almighty’s statement: And do not be divided means in your religion as the Jews and Christians were divided in their religions, according to Ibn Mas’ud and others. It is possible that its meaning is and do not be divided, following whims and different purposes, and be brothers in the religion of God, so that this would prevent them from estrangement and discord, and what follows it indicates this, which is the Almighty’s statement: And remember God’s favor upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together and you became, by His favor, brethren.
