There is no evidence in it for the prohibition of differing in branches of knowledge, for that is not a difference, since the difference is that which makes it impossible to unite and bring together. As for the ruling on matters of ijtihad, the difference in them is due to the extraction of obligations and the subtleties of the meanings of the Shari’ah, and the Companions continued to differ in the rulings on incidents, and despite that they were united. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The difference of my nation is a mercy,” and God only forbade a difference that is the cause of corruption. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The Jews split into seventy-one or seventy-two sects, and the Christians are the same, and my nation will split into seventy-three sects. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a saheeh hadith. He also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: What happened to the Children of Israel will happen to my nation, step by step, to the point that if there was one among them who had sexual intercourse with his mother openly, there would be one among my nation who would do that. The Children of Israel will split into seventy-two sects, and my nation will split into seventy-three sects, all of them in the Fire except one sect. They said: Who is it, O Messenger of God? He said: What I and my companions follow. He narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Ziyad Al-Ifriqi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yazid on the authority of Ibn Amr, and he said: This is a hasan gharib hadith, we do not know it except from this source. Abu Omar said: Abdullah Al-Ifriqi is trustworthy, his people trust him and praised him, but others weakened him. “Abu Dawud included it in his Sunan on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He said: Verily, those who came before you from the People of the Book split into seventy-two sects, and this sect will split into seventy-three, seventy-two in Hell and one in Paradise, which is the group. And there will emerge from my nation people who will be traded by those desires as a dog trades with its owner, and there will not remain a vein or joint of him except that it enters it.” And in Sunan Ibn Majah: On the authority of Anas ibn Malik, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever departs this world with sincerity to God alone and worshipping Him with no partner, and establishes prayer and gives zakat, he dies with God pleased with him.” Anas said: It is the religion of God that the Messengers brought and conveyed from their Lord before the chaos of hadiths and the difference of desires, and the confirmation of that is in the Book of God in the last of what was revealed. God says: But if they repent meaning: they give up idols and their worship, and establish prayer and give zakah (al-Tawbah 9:5). And He said in another verse: But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion (al-Tawbah 9:11). Narrated by Nasr bin Ali Al-Jahdhami from Abu Ahmad from Abu Jaafar Al-Razi from Al-Rabi bin Anas from Anas. Abu Al-Faraj Al-Jawzi said: If it is said that these sects are known, then the answer is that we know the division and the origins of the sects and that each group of the sects was divided into sects, even if we do not know the names of those sects and their doctrines, the origins of the sects have become clear to us: the Haruriyyah, the Qadariyyah, the Jahmiyyah, the Murji’ah, the Rafidah, and the Jabriyah. Some scholars said: The origin of the deviant sects is these six sects, and each sect divided into twelve sects, so they became seventy-two sects. The Haruriyyah divided into twelve sects, the first of which was the Azraqiyyah - they said: We do not know anyone who is a believer, and they disbelieved the people of the Qiblah except for those who follow their saying. The Ibadis - they said: Whoever follows our saying is a believer, and whoever turns away from it is a hypocrite. The Tha’labiyyah - they said: God Almighty did not decree or predestine. The Khazimiyyah - they said: We do not know what faith is, and all creation is excused. The Khalfiyyah - they claimed that whoever abandons jihad, whether male or female, is a disbeliever. The Kuziyyah - they said: No one has the right to touch anyone because he does not know what is pure from what is impure, nor to eat with him until he repents and washes himself. The Kanziyyah - they said: No one has the right to give his money to anyone, because he may not deserve it, but he should hoard it in the earth until the people of truth appear. Al-Shamrakhiyyah said: There is nothing wrong with touching foreign women because they are fragrant flowers. Al-Akhnasiyyah said: Neither good nor evil can reach the dead after his death. Al-Hakimiyyah said: Whoever rules over a creature is an infidel. Al-Mu'tazilah said: The matter of Ali and Mu'awiyah was confused for us, so we disavow both groups. Al-Maymuniyyah said: There is no Imam except with the approval of those who love us. The Qadarites were divided into twelve sects: The Ahmarites - who claimed that one of the conditions of justice from God is that He controls His servants’ affairs and prevents them from committing sins. The Dualists - who claimed that good is from God and evil is from Satan. The Mu’tazilites - who said that the Qur’an was created and denied the attributes of Lordship. The Kaysaniites - who said: We do not know whether these actions are from God or from His servants, and we do not know whether people will be rewarded or punished. The Shaytanites - who said: God Almighty did not create Satan. The Shuraikiites - who said: All evil deeds are predestined except for disbelief. The Wahmiyya - who said: The actions and speech of creation have no essence, nor do good and evil have an essence. The Zubarites - who said: Every book that was sent down from God is true to act upon, whether it was abrogating or abrogated. The Mas’udiyya - who claimed that whoever disobeys and then repents, his repentance is not accepted. The Nakithyyah claimed that whoever breaks the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is not sinful. The Qastiyah followed Ibrahim ibn al-Nazzam in his statement: Whoever claims that God is a thing is an infidel. The Jahmites were divided into twelve sects: The Mu’attilah claimed that everything that human imagination falls upon is created, and that whoever claims that God is seen is an infidel. The Marisiyah said: Most of the attributes of God are created. The Multazaqah made the Creator, glory be to Him, in every place. The Waridiyyah said: Whoever knows his Lord will not enter Hell, and whoever enters it will never leave it. The Zanadiqa said: No one has the right to prove a Lord for himself, because proof can only be after perception by the senses, and what cannot be perceived cannot be proven. The Hariqiyah claimed that the infidel is burned by the Fire once and then remains burned forever, never feeling the heat of the Fire. The Makhluqiyah claimed that the Qur’an is created. The Faniyyah claimed that Paradise and Hell will perish, and some of them said that they were not created. The Abdiyyah - they denied the messengers and said: They are only wise men. The Waqifiyah - they said: We do not say that the Qur’an is created or uncreated. The Qabriyyah - they deny the torment of the grave and intercession. The Lafdhiyyah - they said: Our utterance of the Qur’an is created. The Murji'ah were divided into twelve sects: The Tarkiyyah - they said that God Almighty has no obligation upon His creation except belief in Him, so whoever believes in Him can do whatever he wants. The Sa'ibiyyah - they said that God Almighty has left His creation to do whatever they want. The Rajayyah - they said that the obedient is not called obedient nor the disobedient disobedient, because we do not know what he has with God Almighty. The Salibiyyah - they said that obedience is not part of faith. The Bahishiyyah - they said that faith is knowledge, and whoever does not know the truth from falsehood and the lawful from the unlawful is a disbeliever. The 'Amalah - they said that faith is an action. The Manqusiyyah - they said that faith neither increases nor decreases. The Musta'niyyah - they said that exception is from faith. The Mushabbihah - they said that sight is like sight and hand is like hand. The Hashawiyyah - they said that the ruling of all the hadiths is the same, so according to them, the one who abandons the voluntary act is like the one who abandons the obligatory act. The Dhahiriyyah - who denied analogy. The Bid'iyyah - they were the first to innovate these hadiths in this nation. The Rafidah were divided into twelve sects: The Alawites - they said: The message was to Ali and Gabriel made a mistake. The Amariyyah - they said: Ali is Muhammad's partner in his command. The Shiites - they said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, is the successor of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his guardian after him, and the nation has disbelieved by pledging allegiance to anyone other than him. The Ishaqiyyah - they said: The prophethood is continuous until the Day of Resurrection, and everyone who knows the knowledge of the Ahl al-Bayt is a prophet. The Nawusiyyah - they said: Ali is the best of the nation, so whoever prefers anyone other than him has disbelieved. The Imamiyyah - they said: The world cannot exist without an Imam from the descendants of al-Husayn, and the Imam is taught by Gabriel, peace be upon him, and when he dies, someone else is replaced in his place. The Zaidiyyah - they said: The descendants of al-Husayn are all Imams in prayers, so if one of them is found, it is not permissible to pray behind anyone other than them, whether they are righteous or wicked. The Abbasids - they claimed that al-Abbas was more deserving of the caliphate than anyone else. Reincarnationists - they said: Souls reincarnate, so whoever was a good person, his soul leaves and enters another creation that will live happily. Regressive - they claimed that Ali and his companions will return to the world and take revenge on their enemies. Cursing - they curse Uthman, Talha, Al-Zubayr, Muawiyah, Abu Musa, Aisha and others. The lying in wait - they imitate the dress of ascetics and in every era they appoint a man to whom they attribute the matter, they claim that he is the Mahdi of this nation, and when he dies they appoint another. Then the Jabriyah were divided into twelve sects: The Mudariyyah - they said: There is no action for man, rather God does everything. The Af’aliyyah - they said: We have actions but we have no power over them, rather we are like animals led by a rope. The Mufraghiyyah - they said: All things were created, and now nothing is created. The Najjariyah - they claimed that God punishes people for His actions, not their actions. The Mananiyyah - they said: Do what comes to your heart, so do what you think is good. The Kasbiyyah - they said: The servant does not earn reward or punishment. The Sabqiyyah - they said: Whoever wants to do, let him work, and whoever wants to do not, let him not work, for the happy person is not harmed by his sins, and the wretched person is not benefited by his righteousness. The Habibiyyah - they said: Whoever drinks the cup of God’s love, the worship of the pillars is dropped from him. The Khawfiyyah - they said: Whoever loves God, the Most High, cannot fear Him, because the beloved does not fear his beloved. Intellectuals - they said: Whoever increases in knowledge, he will be exempted from the amount of worship that he deserves. Al-Khashabiyyah - They said: The world is equal among the servants, there is no differentiation between them in what their father Adam inherited from them. Al-Manyah - They said: The action is from us and the ability is for us. The statement of the division that increased in this nation will come at the end of Surah Al-An'am, God willing. Ibn Abbas said to Samak Al-Hanafi: O Hanafi, the group, the group!! The nations of the past were destroyed because of their division. Have you not heard God the Almighty say: And hold fast, all together, to the rope of God, and be not divided? And in Sahih Muslim: “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Verily, God is pleased with three things for you and dislikes three things for you. He is pleased with you that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and that you hold fast, all together, to the rope of God, and do not be divided. And He dislikes three things for you: It was said: He said: And excessive questioning and wasting money.” So God the Almighty has made it obligatory upon us to adhere to His Book and the Sunnah of His Prophet and to refer to them when there is a difference of opinion. He has commanded us to unite in holding fast to the Book and the Sunnah in belief and action. This is the reason for the agreement of the word and the organization of the dispersion by which the interests of this world and the religion are completed, and safety from difference. He has commanded unity and forbade the division that occurred to the People of the Two Books. This is the meaning of the verse in full, and it contains evidence of the validity of consensus as mentioned in its place in the principles of jurisprudence, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: “And remember the favor of God upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together so that by His favor you became brethren. And you were on the brink of a pit of Fire and He saved you from it.” God the Almighty commanded us to remember His favors, the greatest of which is Islam and following His Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, for through it enmity and division were removed and love and harmony were established. What is meant are the Aws and the Khazraj, and the verse is general. The meaning of so that by His favor you became brethren is that by the favor of Islam you became brothers in religion. Everything in the Qur’an that is became means you became, like the Almighty’s saying: If your water were to become sunken (al-Mulk 67:30) meaning it became sunken. Ikhwan is the plural of brother, and he was called brother because he seeks the path of his brother, i.e. he intends him. Shafa is everything that is its deviation, and so is its edge, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: On the brink of a crumbling precipice (al-Tawbah 9:109). The rajaz poet said: We dug a record for the pilgrims, a plant growing above her lips And to be on the lookout for something means to be on the lookout for it, and from this comes the word ashfa which means to make a patient on the verge of death. And there is nothing left of it except a little means a little. Ibn al-Sikkit said: It is said of a man when he dies, or of the moon when it is extinguished, or of the sun when it sets: there is nothing left of it except a little means a little. Al-Ajjaj said: And a high rank for those who have been honored by it, whether with or without healing. His saying, Without healing, means the sun has set. Or with healing, and some of it remains. It is one of the words with a ya’, and in language it is from the waw. An-Nahhas said: The root of shafa is shafu, and for this reason it is written with an alif and is not inclined. Al-Akhfash said: Since inclination is not permissible in it, it is known that it is from the waw, and because inclination is between the ya’ and its dual shafwan. Al-Mahdawi said: This is a metaphor that means their exit from disbelief to faith.
3:104: We have already discussed enjoining good and forbidding evil in this surah. The word min in the phrase minkum is for partiality, meaning that those enjoining must be scholars, but not all people are scholars. It has also been said that it is to clarify the type, meaning that you should all be like that. I said: The first statement is more correct, as it indicates that enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is a communal obligation, and God Almighty has specified them in His statement: Those who, if We establish them in the land, will establish prayer (al-Hajj 22:41) and the verse. Not all people are empowered. Ibn al-Zubayr recited: And let there be among you a group inviting to good, enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, and seeking help from God over what befalls them. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: This addition is an interpretation by Ibn al-Zubayr, and some of his words were erroneously included by some of the narrators, who added it to the words of the Qur’an. This indicates the correctness of what I am describing in the hadith that my father told me. Hasan ibn Arfa told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Abu Asim, on the authority of Abu Awn, on the authority of Subaih, who said: I heard Uthman ibn Affan reciting: And enjoining what is right, forbidding what is wrong, and seeking help from God over what befalls them. No sane person would doubt that Uthman did not believe in this addition in the Qur’an, since he did not write it in his copy of the Qur’an, which is the Imam of the Muslims. Rather, he mentioned it as a sermon and confirmation of what preceded it from the words of the Lord of the Worlds, may He be glorified and exalted.
3:105: It means the Jews and Christians according to the majority of commentators. Some of them said: They are the innovators of this nation. Abu Umamah said: They are the Kharijites, and he recited the verse. Jabir ibn Abdullah said: Those who divided and differed after clear proofs had come to them means the Jews and Christians. <came to them>is a masculine plural, and came to them is a group.
3:106: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black. This means on the Day of Resurrection when they are raised from their graves, the faces of the believers will be white and the faces of the disbelievers will be black. It is said that this is when the Book is read. If the believer reads his book and sees his good deeds in it, he will be happy and his face will turn white. If the disbeliever and hypocrite reads his book and sees his bad deeds in it, his face will turn black. It is also said that this is when the scales are weighed. If his good deeds outweigh his bad deeds, his face will turn white. It is also said that this is when the Almighty says: And separate yourselves today, you criminals. (Ya-Sin 36:59) It is also said that when the Day of Resurrection comes, each group will be commanded to gather before their deity. When they reach Him, they will be sad and their faces will turn black. The believers, the People of the Book, and the hypocrites will remain. Then God the Almighty will say to the believers: Who is your Lord? They will say: Our Lord is God the Almighty. Then He will say to them: Do you recognize Him when you see Him? They will say: Glory be to Him! If we see it, we will recognize it. They will see it as God wills. The believers will fall down in prostration to God, and their faces will become white like snow, while the hypocrites and the People of the Book will remain unable to prostrate, so they will be sad and their faces will blacken. This is the saying of God, the Most High: On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black. It is permissible to say <tabyad wa tasawwad>with a kasra on the two ta’s, because you say: abyadt, so you break the ta’ as you break the alif. This is the language of Tamim and Yahya ibn Waththab recited it in this way. Al-Zuhri recited <yawm tabyad wa tasawwad>with a kasra on the ta’ as well. It is permissible to say <yawm yubyadh wa hujhu>with a ya’ as a masculine plural, and it is permissible to say <ajwah>like <aqtat>. The whitening of faces is their radiance with bliss. And their blackening is what burdens them with painful torment. Second: They differed in the designation. Ibn Abbas said: The faces of the people of the Sunnah will be white and the faces of the people of innovation will be black. I said: “This statement of Ibn Abbas was narrated by Malik bin Sulayman al-Harawi, the brother of Ghassan, on the authority of Malik bin Anas, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the statement of God the Most High: “On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black,” he said: He means the faces of the people of the Sunnah will turn white and the faces of the people of innovation will turn black.” Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Ali bin Thabit al-Khatib mentioned it. He said: It is an objectionable hadith of Malik. Ata’ said: The faces of the Muhajireen and the Ansar will turn white and the faces of Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadir will turn black. Abi bin Ka’b said: Those whose faces turned black are the disbelievers, and it was said to them: Did you disbelieve after your belief in your confession when you were brought forth from the loins of Adam like ants? This is the choice of al-Tabari. Al-Hasan: The verse is about the hypocrites. Qatadah: It is about the apostates. Ikrimah: They are a people from the People of the Book who believed in their prophets and believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he was sent, but when he was sent, they disbelieved in him. This is what His statement: Did you disbelieve after your belief? This is the choice of al-Zajjaj. Malik ibn Anas: It is about the people of desires. “Abu Umamah al-Bahili on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is about the Kharijites.” And in another report that “peace be upon him said: It is about the Qadarites.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Ghalib that Umamah said: The dogs of Hell are the worst of those killed under the sky, the best of those killed are those who killed him - then he recited - On the Day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black to the end of the verse. I said to Abu Umamah: Did you hear it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: If I had not heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except once, twice, or three times - until he counted seven - I would not have narrated it to you. He said: This is a good hadith. “And in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will precede you to the Cistern. Whoever passes by me will drink, and whoever drinks will never thirst again. People will come to me whom I know and who will know me, then I will be prevented from them.” Abu Hazim said: Then Nu’man ibn Abi Ayyash heard me and said: Is this how you heard it from Sahl ibn Sa’d? I said: Yes. He said: I bear witness that Abu Saeed Al-Khudri heard him add to it: “Then I will say that they are from me. Then it will be said: You do not know what they innovated after you. Then I will say: Away with those who innovated after me.” And on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he used to narrate that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A group of my companions will come to me at the Cistern on the Day of Resurrection and they will be brought to the Cistern. Then I will say: O Lord, my companions. Then He will say: You have no knowledge of what they innovated after you. They turned back in retreat.” And there are many hadiths with this meaning. Whoever changes, alters, or innovates in the religion of God what God does not approve of and does not permit, he is among those who are expelled from the Cistern, far away from it, with black faces. The most severely expelled and distant of them are those who oppose the community of Muslims and depart from their path, such as the Khawarij with their different sects, the Rawafidh with their different shades, and the Mu'tazilah with their various whims. All of these are changers and innovators, as are the oppressors who are excessive in injustice and oppression, obliterating the truth, killing its people, and humiliating them, and those who openly commit major sins but take their transgressions lightly, and the group of people of deviation, whims, and innovations. Everyone fears that they are meant by the verse and the hadith, as we have explained. No one will remain in the Fire forever except a disbelieving denier who does not have a mustard seed's weight of faith in his heart. Ibn al-Qasim said: There may be someone from those other than the people of whims who is worse than the people of whims. He used to say: The perfection of sincerity is avoiding sins. Third: The Almighty’s statement: As for those whose faces will be blackened, there is an omission in the speech, meaning it will be said to them, Did you disbelieve after your belief? meaning on the day of the covenant when they said, Yes. And it is said: This is for the Jews, and they were believers in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he was sent, but when he was sent, they disbelieved in him. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: This is for the hypocrites, it is said: Did you disbelieve in secret after your admission in public? And the Arab scholars agreed that the letter fa must be used next to amma because the meaning in your statement, As for Zayd, he is leaving, is that whatever happens, Zayd is leaving.
3:107: And the Almighty said: And as for those whose faces will be white, these are the people of obedience to God the Almighty and the faithful to His covenant. In the mercy of God they will abide therein, meaning in His Paradise and the abode of His honor, they will abide therein forever. May God make us among them and keep us away from the paths of innovations and misguidance and guide us to the path of those who believe and do righteous deeds. Amen.
3:108: The Almighty's saying: These are the verses of God is a subject and predicate, meaning the Qur'an. We recite them to you meaning We send Gabriel down to you so he recites them to you. In truth meaning with honesty. Al-Zajjaj said: These are the verses of God mentioned are God's proofs and evidence. It was said: Those means these, but when it ended it became as if it had become distant, so it was said those. It is possible for the verses of God to be a substitute for those and not an adjective, because the vague cannot be described by the adjective. And God does not intend injustice to the worlds meaning that He does not punish them without sin.
3:109: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Al-Mahdawi said: The connection between this and what came before it is that when he mentioned the conditions of the believers and the disbelievers and that he does not want injustice for the worlds, and the connection with the mention of the breadth of his power and his independence from injustice because whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is in his grasp, and it was said: It is the beginning of a speech, in which he explained to his servants that everything in the heavens and whatever is on the earth belongs to him so that they may ask him and worship him and not worship anyone other than him.
3:110: The Almighty’s saying: You are the best nation produced for mankind. There are three issues in it: First: “Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Bahz bin Hakim on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Concerning the words of God the Almighty: “You are the best nation produced for mankind,” he said: You complete seventy nations, you are the best of them and the most honored in the sight of God.” He said: This is a good hadith. Abu Hurairah said: We are the best people for mankind, we drive them in chains to Islam. Ibn Abbas said: They are those who migrated from Mecca to Medina and witnessed Badr and Al-Hudaybiyyah. Umar bin Al-Khattab said: Whoever does what they did will be like them. It was said: They are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning the righteous and virtuous among them. They are the witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection, as mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Mujahid said: You are the best nation produced for mankind according to the conditions mentioned in the verse. It was said: Its meaning is: You were in the Preserved Tablet. It was said: You were the best nation since you believed. It was said: It came to present the good report to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation. The meaning is that when you came from the People of the Book, you were the best nation. Al-Akhfash said: He means the people of a nation, meaning the best people of religion, and he recited: I swore and left no doubt for you. Can a man trust a slave while he is obedient? It was said: It is the perfect kana, and the meaning is: You were created and found to be the best nation. <The best nation>is a state. It was said: Kan is redundant, and the meaning is: You are the best nation. Sibawayh recited: Our neighbors were generous. And similar to it is the saying of God the Almighty: How can We speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? (Maryam 19:29) and His saying: And remember when you were few and He multiplied you (al-A’raf 7:86). And He said in another place: And remember when you were few (al-Anfal 8:26). Sufyan narrated on the authority of Maysarah Al-Ashja’i on the authority of Abu Hazim on the authority of Abu Hurairah: You were the best nation produced for mankind he said: You dragged people in chains to Islam. Al-Nahhas said: The meaning of this is: You were the best nation for mankind. And according to the saying of Mujahid: You were the best nation when you enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong. And it was said: The nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, became the best nation because the Muslims were more numerous among them, and enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong was more widespread among them. So it was said: This is the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, “as he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best people are my generation” meaning those among whom I was sent. Second: If it is proven by the text of the revelation that this nation is the best of nations, “The imams narrated from the hadith of Imran bin Husayn from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The best of people are my generation, then those who come after them, then those who come after them” the hadith. This indicates that the first of this nation are better than those who come after them, and this is what most scholars have adopted, and that whoever accompanied the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and saw him even once in his life is better than those who come after him, and that the virtue of companionship is not equaled by any action. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr has adopted the view that there may be among those who come after the Companions someone better than those who were among the group of Companions, “and that his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: The best of people are my generation” is not general, based on the evidence that the generation includes the virtuous and the inferior. His generation included a group of hypocrites who outwardly showed faith and people who committed major sins, upon whom or some of whom the prescribed punishments were imposed, and he said to them: What do you say about the thief, the drinker, and the adulterer? And he said, facing those who were in my generation: Do not curse my companions. And he said to Khalid bin Al-Walid about Ammar: Do not curse those who are better than you. Abu Umamah narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Blessed is he who has seen me and believed in me, and blessed - seven times - is he who has not seen me and believed in me. In Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Hamid, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar, who said: “I was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘Do you know which of creation has the best faith?’ We said: ‘The angels.’ He said: ‘And they have the right, but others than them.’ We said: ‘The prophets.’ He said: ‘And they have the right, but others than them.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The best of creation in faith are people in the loins of men who believe in me even though they have not seen me. They find paper and know what is in it, so they are the best of creation in faith.’” Salih ibn Jubayr narrated on the authority of Abu Jumah, who said: “We said: ‘O Messenger of God, is there anyone better than us?’ He said: ‘Yes, a people who will come after you and find a book between two covers and believe in what is in it and believe in me even though they have not seen me.’” Abu Omar said: Abu Jumah: He was a companion and his name was Habib bin Saba’ and Salih bin Jubair were trustworthy followers. Abu Tha’labah Al-Khushani narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There are days ahead of you in which the one who is patient in his religion will be like the one holding onto hot coals. The one who works in them will have the reward of fifty men who do the same as him. It was said: O Messenger of God, who are they? He said: Rather, from you. Abu Omar said: This phrase <rather, from you>was not mentioned by some of the hadith scholars and did not mention it. Omar bin Al-Khattab said in his interpretation of the statement: You are the best nation produced for mankind, he said: Whoever does as you do will be like you. There is no contradiction between the hadiths, because the first is specific, and God is the Grantor of success. It has been said in explaining the hadiths of this chapter: His generation was preferred because they were strangers in their faith due to the large number of disbelievers and their patience in the face of their harm and their adherence to their religion. And the last of this nation, when they established the religion and adhered to it and were patient in obeying their Lord at a time when evil, immorality, chaos, sins and major sins appeared, they were also strangers at that time, and their deeds were pure at that time as the deeds of their predecessors were pure. “And what bears witness to this is his saying, peace be upon him: Islam began as something strange and will return as it began, so blessed are the strangers.” And the hadith of Abu Tha’labah also bears witness to it, “And what bears witness to it is his saying, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: My nation is like rain, it is not known whether its beginning or its end is better.” It was mentioned by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and Abu ‘Isa al-Tirmidhi, “And Hisham ibn ‘Ubaydullah al-Razi narrated it on the authority of Malik on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: The example of my nation is like rain, it is not known whether its beginning or its end is better.” It was mentioned by al-Darqutni in Musnad Hadith Malik. Abu Omar said: Hisham bin Ubaidullah is trustworthy and there is no disagreement about that. It was narrated that when Omar bin Abdul Aziz assumed the caliphate, he wrote to Salim bin Abdullah to write for me the biography of Omar bin Al-Khattab so that I may act upon it. Salim wrote to him: If you act upon the biography of Omar, then you are better than Omar because your time is not like the time of Omar, and your men are not like the men of Omar. He wrote to the jurists of his time, and all of them wrote to him similar to what Salim said. Some of the great scholars opposed the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The best of people are my generation, with his statement: The best of people are those who live long and do good deeds, and the worst of people are those who live long and do bad deeds. Abu Omar said: These hadiths, with their numerous chains of transmission and their goodness, require equality between the first of this nation and its last. The meaning of this is what was mentioned above about faith and righteous deeds in a corrupt time in which people of knowledge and religion are removed, and immorality and chaos increase, and the believer remains and the immoral is honored, and religion returns to being strange as it began as strange, and the one who stands in it will be like the one holding hot coals. Then the first of this nation will be equal to the last of it in the virtue of deeds, except for the people of Badr and Al-Hudaybiyyah. And whoever ponders the effects of this chapter will see the truth for him, and God gives His grace to whomever He wills. Third: The Almighty’s saying: You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong is praise for this nation as long as they establish that and are characterized by it. But if they abandon change and conspire to commit evil, the name of praise will be removed from them and the name of blame will be attached to them, and that will be the reason for their destruction. We have already discussed enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong at the beginning of the surah. The Almighty said: And if the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. He informed us that the People of the Scripture’s belief in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is better for them, and He informed us that among them are believers and sinners, and that the sinners are more numerous.
3:111: The Almighty's saying: They will not harm you except a slight harm means their lies, distortions and slander, not that they will prevail, according to Al-Hasan and Qatada, so the exception is connected, and the meaning is they will not harm you except a slight harm, so the harm is used as a source. So the verse is a promise from God to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers, that the People of the Book will not defeat them and that they will be victorious over him, and that they will not be harmed by them except by harm through slander and distortion, and as for the outcome, it will be for the believers. It was said: It is disconnected and the meaning is they will not harm you at all, but they will harm you with what they hear. Muqatil said: The leaders of the Jews, Ka'b, Adi, An-Nu'man, Abu Rafi', Abu Yasir, Kinanah and Ibn Suriya, went to their believers: Abdullah bin Salam and his companions, and harmed them because of their Islam, so God Almighty revealed: They will not harm you except a slight harm meaning with the tongue, and the speech is complete. Then he said: And if they fight you, they will turn their backs to you, meaning defeated, and the speech is complete. Then they will not be aided is a new sentence, and that is why the letter nun was added to it. In this verse is a miracle for the Prophet, peace be upon him, because the Jews who fought him turned their backs to him.
3:112: The Almighty said: Abasement has been imposed upon them meaning the Jews. Wherever they are found meaning they find and encounter, and the discussion is complete. The meaning of abasement has been imposed upon them has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Except by a rope from God is an interrupted exception that is not from the first. That is, but they hold fast to a rope from God. And a rope from the people meaning the covenant that they have. And the people are Muhammad and the believers pay them the tax so they give them security. There is an abbreviation in the speech and the meaning is: Except that they hold fast to a rope from God, so it was deleted. Al-Farra' said: And they incurred the wrath of God meaning they returned. It was said: They endured. Its origin in the language is that it is not binding upon them, and it has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Then he informed why He did that to them, saying: "That is because they disbelieved in the signs of God and killed the prophets without right. That is because they disobeyed and were transgressors." It has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah in full.
3:113: Then he informed and said: They are not equal and the speech was completed. The meaning is: The People of the Book and the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are not equal, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud. It was said: The meaning is: The believers and the disbelievers from the People of the Book are not equal. "Abu Khaithama Zuhair bin Harb mentioned: Hashim bin Al-Qasim narrated to us: Shaiban narrated to us on the authority of Asim on the authority of Zur on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delayed the 'Isha' prayer one night, then he went out to the mosque and saw the people waiting for the prayer, so he said: There is no one from the people of religions who remembers God Almighty at this hour except you." He said: And this verse was revealed: "They are not equal. Among the People of the Book is a community standing" - to His saying: And God is Knowing of the righteous. Ibn Wahb narrated something similar. Ibn Abbas said: The statement of God Almighty: Among the People of the Book is a community standing, reciting the verses of God during the hours of the night and prostrating refers to those who believed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When Abdullah bin Salam, Tha’laba bin Sa’ya, Asid bin Sa’ya, Asid bin Ubayd, and those Jews who converted to Islam, believed and were truthful and desired Islam and were steadfast in it, the rabbis of the Jews and the unbelievers among them said: None believed in Muhammad or followed him except the worst of us, and if they were among our best they would not have abandoned the religion of their fathers and gone to another one. So God, the Almighty, revealed concerning that, His statement: “They are not all alike. Among the People of the Scripture is a community standing, reciting the verses of God during periods of the night and prostrating themselves.” to His statement: And those are among the righteous. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning of among the People of the Scripture is one with a nation, meaning one with a good way. And he recited: Can a man trust a nation while it is obedient? It was said: There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is that among the People of the Book there is a nation that is established and another that is not established, so he left out the other and was satisfied with the first, like the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb: My heart disobeyed me, but I am obedient to its command. I do not know how to guide its seekers. He wanted: did he guide or was he wrong, so he deleted it. Al-Farra’ said: <nation>is raised by <-sawa’a>and the meaning is: A nation of the People of the Book who recite the verses of God and a nation of disbelievers are not equal. Al-Nahhas said: This is a wrong statement for several reasons: One of them is that it raises <nation>by <-sawa’a>so it does not refer to a noun that is nothing, and it raises by what is not running on the verb and it implicitly implies what it does not need, because the mention of the disbeliever has already been made, so there is no basis for implicitly implying this. Abu Ubaidah said: This is like their saying the fleas ate me and your companions left. Al-Nahhas said: This is wrong, because their mention has already been made, and the fleas ate me was not mentioned before. The hours of the night is its hours. Its singular is inna and ana and inna, and it is accusative as an adverb. Yasjudu means they pray, according to Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj, because recitation does not occur in bowing and prostration. Similar to his saying: And to Him they prostrate (al-A’raf 7:206) is that they pray. In al-Furqan 25:And when it is said to them, ‘Prostrate to the Most Gracious,’ (al-Furqan 25:60) and in al-Najm 53:Then prostrate to God and worship (al-Najm 53:62). It was said that it refers specifically to the well-known prostration. The reason for revelation rejects this, and that what is meant is the Isha prayer as we mentioned from Ibn Masoud. The idol worshippers slept when night fell upon them, and the monotheists stood before God in the Isha prayer reciting the verses of God. Do you not see that when he mentioned their standing, he said: And they prostrate. That is, with standing also. Ath-Thawri: It is the prayer between the two Isha prayers. It was said that it is during the night prayer. A man from Banu Shaibah who used to study books said: We find words from the words of the Almighty Lord: Does a camel herder or a sheep herder think that when night falls upon him he will be forsaken like one who stands and prostrates during the hours of the night?
3:114: They believe in God means they acknowledge God and believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And they enjoin what is right It was said: This is general. It was also said that it means the command to follow the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And they forbid what is wrong Forbidding what is wrong means forbidding disobeying it. And they hasten to do good deeds which they do, rushing and not hesitating, because they know the extent of their reward. It was also said: They hasten to do good deeds before they miss out. And those are among the righteous meaning with the righteous, and they are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Paradise.
3:115: And whatever good they do, they will never be denied it. Al-A'mash, Ibn Waththab, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Hafs and Khalaf read both with a ya', describing the existing nation. This is the reading of Ibn Abbas and the choice of Abu Ubaid. The rest read both with a ta' as a direct address, based on the statement of God the Almighty: You are the best nation produced for mankind. This is the choice of Abu Hatim. Abu Amr saw both readings as ya' and ta'. The meaning of the verse is: And whatever good you do, you will never be denied its reward, rather you will be thanked and rewarded for it.
3:116: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieve is the subject of in, and the predicate is neither their wealth nor their children will avail them at all against God. Muqatil said: When God mentioned the believers among the People of the Book, He mentioned their disbelievers, which is His statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve. Al-Kalbi said: He made this a beginning, so He said: Indeed, those who disbelieve, neither their many wealth nor their many children will avail them at all against the punishment of God. He specified the children because they are the closest of their lineage to them. And those are the companions of the Fire is a beginning and a predicate, and so is They will abide therein eternally. All of this has been mentioned before.
3:117: The Almighty said: The likeness of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind in which there is a chill. <ma>can be a source, and it can mean which and the pronoun is omitted, meaning like what they spend. The meaning of like a wind is like a blowing wind. Ibn Abbas said: And the chill is the intense cold. It was said: Its origin is from the creaking which is the sound, so it is the sound of the intense wind. Al-Zajjaj: It is the sound of the flames of the fire that was in that wind. This meaning was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah and in the hadith: He forbade the locusts that were killed by the chill. The meaning of the verse: The likeness of the spending of the disbelievers in its invalidity, loss and lack of benefit is like the likeness of a crop that was struck by a cold wind or fire that burned it and destroyed it, so its owners did not benefit from anything after they had hoped for its benefit and benefit. God the Almighty said: And God did not wrong them in that but they wrong themselves by disbelief, disobedience and withholding the right of God the Almighty. It was said: They wronged themselves by planting at the wrong time or in the wrong place, so God Almighty disciplined them for putting something in the wrong place, as Al-Mahdawi narrated.
3:118: It has six issues: First: God Almighty emphasized the warning against relying on the infidels. It is connected to what came before in His statement: If you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture. The batana is a source, which is used to name both the singular and the plural. The batana of a man are his intimates who conceal his affair, and its origin is from the batin which is the opposite of the back, and the batin of so-and-so with so-and-so, he conceals batun and batana if it is specific to him. The poet said: They are my loyal ones, yes, and my confidants, and they are my defect, without any relative Second: God Almighty forbade the believers in this verse from taking the infidels, Jews, and people of whims as intruders and refuges, negotiating with them about opinions, entrusting their affairs to them, and saying: Whoever is against your doctrine and religion, you should not talk to him. The poet said: Do not ask about a person, but ask about his companion, for every companion follows the example of his companion. In Sunan Abi Dawood, “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A person is upon the religion of his close friend, so let each of you consider whom he takes as a close friend.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he said: Consider people by their brothers. Then God Almighty explained the meaning for which He forbade maintaining relations, saying: They will not spare any corruption for you. He said: Corruption, meaning that they will not spare any effort in corrupting you. That is, even if they do not fight you outwardly, they will not spare any effort in deceiving and tricking you, as will be explained. “It was narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the statement of God Almighty: “O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves, for they will not spare any corruption for you.” He said: They are the Khawarij. It was narrated that Abu Musa al-Ash’ari asked a dhimmi to write a report, so Umar wrote to him, rebuking him and reciting this verse to him. Abu Musa al-Ash’ari presented an account to Umar, may God be pleased with them both, and he sent it to Umar, who was pleased with him. A letter came to Umar and he said to Abu Musa: Where is your scribe to read this letter to the people? He said: He does not enter the mosque. He said: Why! Is he sexually impure? He said: He is a Christian. He rebuked him and said: Do not approach them when God has cast them out, do not honor them when God has humiliated them, and do not trust them when God has betrayed them. On the authority of Omar may God be pleased with him, he said: Do not employ the People of the Book, for they consider bribery permissible. Seek help in your affairs and over your subjects from those who fear God Almighty. It was said to Omar may God be pleased with him: There is a man from the Christians of Al-Hirah here, and no one is more literate than him or writes with a pen. Should he not write for you? He said: I will not take an entourage other than the believers. It is not permissible to appoint the People of the Book as scribes or any other of their dealings in buying and selling or appointing them as representatives. I said: The situation has been reversed in these times with the People of the Book being appointed as scribes and trustees, and thus they prevail among the ignorant and foolish governors and princes. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God did not send a prophet or appoint a successor except that he had two entourages: an entourage that commanded him to do good and urged him to do it, and an entourage that commanded him to do evil and urged him to do it. The one who is protected is he who God Almighty has protected.” Anas bin Malik narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not seek light from the fire of the polytheists, and do not engrave ‘Arabs’ on your rings. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan explained it and said: He, peace be upon him, meant: Do not consult the polytheists in any of your affairs, and do not engrave ‘Muhammad’ on your rings. Al-Hasan said: The confirmation of that is in the Book of God Almighty: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates those other than yourselves (al-Baqarah 2:170). Third: The Almighty’s saying: From without you meaning from other than you. Al-Farra’ said: And they do work less than that (Al-Anbiya’: 82) meaning other than that. It was said: From without you means in conduct and good manners. The meaning of They spare no effort in ruining you is they do not fall short in what causes corruption for you. The position of the attribute for <the retinue from without you>is said: they spare no effort meaning they do not fall short. And I spared no effort means I fell short. Imru’ al-Qais said: As long as the heart of a person is in control of the dangers, he will not be able to Al-Khabal: insanity. Al-Khabal: corruption, and it may be in actions, bodies, and minds. In the hadith: Whoever is afflicted with blood or Khabal meaning a wound that corrupts a limb. Al-Khabal: corruption of the limbs, and a man is Khabal and Mukhtal, and love corrupted him, meaning it spoiled him. Aws said: My sons, you are not a hand but a hand with a weak arm Any corrupted arm. Al-Farra recited: Ibn Saad looked and said, It was a disaster for your companions and the mounts. Any corruption. And <Khabalan>is in the accusative case with the second object, because al-alo takes two objects, and if you wish it is in the infinitive, meaning they drive you crazy, or if you wish by removing the preposition, meaning by the insanity, as they said I beat him painfully. <And>in His statement, And they wished that you had suffered is a source, meaning they wished that you had suffered. That is, what is difficult for you. And hardship is difficulty, and its meaning has already been mentioned in <Al-Baqarah>. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Hatred has already appeared from their mouths. This means that the enmity and denial of you has appeared from their mouths. Hatred is loathing, and it is the opposite of love and hatred. It is a feminine noun. The Almighty mentioned mouths specifically and not tongues, indicating their boasting and chattering in these statements of theirs. They are above the one who conceals himself in whose eyes hatred appears. From this meaning is his (peace be upon him) prohibition of a man from opening his mouth from his brother’s honor. It means that he should open it. It is said: The donkey brayed its mouth with braying, and the mouth itself brayed. The bridle opened the horse’s mouth with braying, and the horses came with their mouths open. This hadith does not indicate that it is permissible for someone to whisper something about his brother’s honor, as this is forbidden by consensus of scholars. In the revelation: Do not backbite one another. (al-Hujurat 49:12) The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your blood, your wealth, and your honor are sacred to you. So the mention of greed is an indication of boasting and exaggeration, so know this. Fifth: This verse is evidence that the testimony of an enemy against his enemy is not permissible. The people of Medina and the people of Hijaz said the same. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hanifa that it is permissible. Ibn Battel narrated on the authority of Ibn Shaban that he said: The scholars agreed that the testimony of an enemy against his enemy is not permissible in anything, even if he is just. Enmity removes justice, so how about the enmity of an unbeliever? Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And what their hearts conceal is greater. This is report and information that they harbor more hatred than they show with their mouths. Abdullah bin Masoud read: Hatred has begun with the verb masculine, since hatred means loathing.
3:119: The Almighty said: Here you are, loving them meaning the hypocrites. The evidence for this is the Almighty's saying: And when they meet you, they say, 'We believe', as stated by Abu Al-Aaliyah and Muqatil. Love here means friendship, meaning that you, O Muslims, are friends with them and they do not be friends with you because of their hypocrisy. It was said: The meaning is that you want Islam for them and they want disbelief for you. It was said: What is meant is the Jews, as stated by most. The Book is a generic noun, Ibn Abbas said: It means in the books. The Jews believe in some, as God the Almighty said: And when it is said to them, 'Believe in what God has revealed,' they say, 'We believe in what was revealed to us,' and they disbelieve in what came after it (al-Baqarah 2:91). And when they meet you, they say, 'We believe' meaning in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And when they are alone among themselves they bite their fingertips meaning the tips of their fingers out of rage and anger at you, and some of them say to one another: Do you not see that these have appeared and multiplied? Biting is an expression of intense anger with the inability to vent it, and from this is the saying of Abu Talib: They bite the back of our necks with their fingers Another said: When they saw me - may God prolong their anger - they became so angry that they became like the tips of their thumbs. It is said: to bite, bite, bite, bite, bite. And bite <with a damma on the ‘ayn>: is the fodder of the animals of the people of the cities, such as the harvest and the crushed pits. It is said from it: the people bite, if their camels eat bite. And a fat camel, as if it is attributed to it. And bite <with a kasra>: is the cunning man and the eloquent cunning. And biting the fingers is done by the angry person who missed something he could not do, or something befell them that he could not change. And this biting is with the teeth, like biting the hand over something that is about to be missed, or like knocking the regretful tooth, and other things like counting pebbles and lines on the ground for the worried. And this bite is written with the dropped Ḍād, and the admonition of time with the emphatic Ḍād, as he said: A sermon of the time, O son of Marwan, left no money except what was wiped out or wasted One of the fingers is called an anmal with a damma on the mim, and it is also said with a fatha, but the damma is more common. When Abu al-Juza’ recited this verse, he would say: They are the Ibadis. Ibn Atiyyah said: This characteristic may be found in many of the people of innovation until the Day of Resurrection. God Almighty said: “Die in your rage. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts.” If it is said: How did they not die when God Almighty says to something: Be, and it is? Two answers have been given: The first - about which Al-Tabari and many of the commentators said - is a supplication against them. That is, say, O Muhammad, may God continue your rage until you die. So based on this, it is appropriate to supplicate against them with this directly or indirectly, unlike the curse. Second: The meaning is that he informed them that they will not attain what they hope for, for death is before that. According to this meaning, the meaning of supplication is removed and the meaning of rebuke and vexation remains. This meaning is consistent with the statement of Musafir ibn Abi Amr: He wishes to make us sick and to poke out the eyes of those who envy him. This meaning is seen in the Almighty’s saying: Whoever thinks that God will not support him in this world and the Hereafter, let him stretch out a rope to the heaven and then cut it off. (al-Hajj 22:15)
3:120: The Almighty said: If good befalls you, it distresses them. As-Salami read it with a ya' and the rest read it with a ta'. The wording is general and includes everything that is good and bad. What the commentators mentioned about fertility and drought, the gathering of the believers and the emergence of division among them, and other sayings are examples and there is no difference. The meaning of the verse is that whoever has this characteristic of intense enmity, hatred, and joy at the befalling of hardships on the believers, is not worthy of being taken as a confidant, especially in this serious matter of jihad, which is the essence of this world and the hereafter. The poet said well when he said: All enmity can be healed, except the enmity of someone who is your enemy out of envy. And if you are patient meaning in the face of their harm and in obedience and loyalty to the believers, and fear God, their plot will not harm you at all. It is said: He harmed him means he harmed him and “he... so the Almighty made the negation of their harm conditional upon patience and fear of God, so that was a consolation for the believers and a strengthening of their souls. I said: The two Haramiyyin and Abu Amr read la yadhirkum from darār yadhir as we mentioned, and from this is his saying la dhir and the ya' was deleted due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, because when you delete the damma from the ra', the ra' remains quiescent and the ya' remains quiescent, so the ya' was deleted, and it was more appropriate to delete it, because before it is what indicates it. Al-Kisa'i narrated that he heard dharahu yadhuruhu and he permitted la yadhirkum and claimed that in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b there is la yadhirkum. The Kufians read la yadhirkum with a damma and a shaddah on the ra' from darār yadhir. It is permissible for them to be raised on the assumption of the omission of the fa', and the meaning is: so do not harm you, and from this is the saying of the poet: Whoever does good deeds, God will reward them. This is what Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said, or it could be raised with the intention of presentation. Sibawayh recited: If your brother is defeated, you will be defeated. That is, it will not harm you if you are patient and fear God. It is permissible for it to be in the jussive mood, and the ra’ was given a damma because of the meeting of two sukoon letters, following the damma. This is also the reading of those who open the ra’, so that the verb is in the jussive mood, and the fatha on <yadhurkum>is due to the meeting of two sukoon letters due to the lightness of the fatha. It was narrated by Abu Zaid on the authority of al-Mufaddal on the authority of Asim, as narrated by al-Mahdawi. Al-Nahhas narrated: Al-Mufaddal al-Dabbi claimed on the authority of Asim <la yadhurkum>with a kasra on the ra’ because of the meeting of two sukoon letters.
3:121: The Almighty said: And when you went forth from your family in the morning. The agent in when is an implied verb, the meaning of which is: remember when you went forth, meaning you went out in the morning. From your family from your home from Aisha. The believers shall take up their positions for battle, and God is Hearing and Knowing. This is Gaza Uhud, and this entire verse was revealed in it. Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: It is the Battle of the Trench. And from Al-Hasan also: The Day of Badr. The majority of scholars agree that it was the Battle of Uhud, as indicated by the words of God the Almighty: When two parties from among you were about to lose heart. This was on the day of Uhud, and the polytheists had headed to Medina with three thousand men to avenge their defeat on the day of Badr. They camped at Uhud on the edge of the valley in a canal opposite Medina on Wednesday, the twelfth of Shawwal in the year three of the Hijra, at the beginning of thirty-one months of the Hijra. They stayed there on Thursday while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in Medina. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw in his dream that there was a notch in his sword, that his cows were being slaughtered, and that he put his hand into the armor of the fortified city. Narrated by Muslim. All of that was according to what is well-known and famous from those battles. The origin of tabawa is to take a home. You have made him live in it, and from this is his saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever lies about me intentionally, let him take his seat in Hellfire meaning, let him take a home in it. The meaning of the believers will take their place is that ranks will be taken for them. Al-Bayhaqi mentioned from the hadith of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (I saw in a dream that I was riding a ram, and the point of my sword was broken. I interpreted it as meaning that I was following the ram of the people, and I interpreted the breaking of the point of my sword as meaning the killing of a man from my family.) So Hamza was killed, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) killed Talha, and Salih was the standard-bearer. Musa bin Uqbah narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab. The standard-bearer of the emigrants was a man from the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and he said: I am, God willing, Asim for what I have. So Salihah bin Uthman, the brother of Saeed bin Uthman Al-Lakhmi, said to him: O Asim, would you like to fight? He said: Yes. So that man rushed to him and struck Talha on the head with his sword until the sword hit his beard and killed him. So the killing of the standard-bearer was a confirmation of the vision of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him): As if I were riding a ram.
3:122: The Almighty said: When two parties among you were about to lose heart, but God was their protector. He said: We are the two parties: Banu Haritha and Banu Salamah, and we do not like it not to be revealed, because God the Almighty said: And God is their protector. It was said: They are Banu Harith, Banu Khazraj, and Banu Nabit, and Nabit is Amr ibn Malik from Banu Aws. Failure is an expression for cowardice, and that is how it is in the language. The concern of the two parties was after the departure when Abdullah ibn Ubayy returned with the hypocrites who were with him, so God preserved their hearts and they did not return, so that is what God the Almighty said: And God is their protector, meaning He preserved their hearts from realizing this concern. It was said: They wanted to retire from the departure, and that was a small thing on their part. It was said: That was a talk of theirs that crossed their minds, so God informed His Prophet, peace be upon him, about it, and they gained insight. That weakness was not theirs, so God protected them, and they blamed each other, and they rose up with the Prophet, peace be upon him, so the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, went until he saw the polytheists, and he left Medina with a thousand, so Abdullah bin Ubay bin Salul returned from him with three hundred men in anger, because his opinion was contradicted when he suggested sitting and fighting in Medina if the enemy rose up against them, and his opinion was in agreement with the opinion of the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, but most of the Ansar refused that, and it will come. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, rose up with the Muslims, and those of them whom God honored with martyrdom were martyred. Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: Four of the Muhajireen were killed on the day of Uhud, and seventy of the Ansar, may God be pleased with them. Seats: the plural of seat, which is a place for sitting, and this is like the word stands, but the word sitting indicates steadfastness, especially since the archers were sitting. This is the meaning of the hadith of the Battle of Uhud in brief, and there will come from its details what is healing. On that day, the polytheists had a horse ridden by Khalid bin Al-Walid, and the Muslims did not have a horse on that day. On that day, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was wounded in the face, and his lower right incisor was broken by a stone, and the egg was smashed from his head (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He rewarded him for his nation and religion with the best reward with which he rewarded any of his prophets for his patience. The one who took charge of that from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was Amr bin Qami’ah Al-Laithi and Utbah bin Abi Waqqas. It has been said that Abdullah bin Shihab, the grandfather of the jurist Muhammad bin Muslim bin Shihab, was the one who wounded the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the forehead. Al-Waqidi said: What is established among us is that the one who threw a stone at the face of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the one who caused his lip to bleed and his incisor to be injured was Utbah bin Abi Waqqas. Al-Waqidi said on the authority of Nafi’ ibn Jubayr who said: I heard a man from the Muhajireen say: I witnessed the Battle of Uhud and I saw arrows coming from every direction and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the middle of them, deflecting all of that from him. I saw Abdullah ibn Shihab al-Zuhri saying on that day: Show me Muhammad, show me Muhammad, for I will not be saved if he is saved. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was beside him with Uhud, then he passed him, and Safwan rebuked him for that, so he said: By God, I did not see him. I swear by God that he is protected from us! We went out, four of us, and we pledged and agreed to kill him, but we did not succeed in that. The stones were heaped on the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) until he fell into a hole that Abu Amir the monk had dug as a plot against the Muslims. He (peace be upon him) fell on his side and Talhah embraced him until he stood up. Malik ibn Sinan, the father of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, sucked the blood from the wound of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). Two rings on the helmet of the Prophet's shield stuck to his face, so Abu Ubaidah ibn Al-Jarrah pulled them out and bit them with his front teeth until they fell. He was worried and his determination adorned him (peace be upon him). In this raid, Hamza (peace be upon him) was killed. He was killed by Wahshi, and Wahshi was a slave of Jubair ibn Mut'im. Jubair had said to him: If you kill Muhammad, we will give you the reins of the horses, and if you kill Ali ibn Abi Talib, we will give you a hundred camels, all of them with black eyes, and if you kill Hamza, you are free. Wahshi said: As for Muhammad, he has a guardian from God who cannot get to him, but as for Ali, no one went out to him except that he killed him. As for Hamza, he is a brave man, and I hope I will meet him and kill him. Whenever Hind would prepare for Wahshi or pass by him, she would say: O Abu Dasma, heal and seek healing. So he lay in ambush for him behind Sakhr. Hamza had attacked the polytheists. When he returned from his attack and passed by Wahshi, he struck him with a lancet and he fell dead. May God have mercy on him and be pleased with him. Ibn Ishaq said: Hind ripped open Hamza’s liver and chewed it, but she could not swallow it, so she spat it out. Then she climbed onto a high rock and screamed at the top of her voice, saying: We rewarded you with the Day of Badr, and war after war has a price. I had no patience with Utbah, nor did my brother, uncle, or Bakri. I healed my soul and fulfilled my vow. I healed my wild beast and the resentment in my chest. Thank you, Wahshi, for my life until my bones are thrown into my grave Hind bint Athatah bin Abbad bin Abdul Muttalib answered her and said: I was disgraced in Badr and after Badr, O daughter of the great valley of disbelief Good morning to you, my beautiful Hashemites, at dawn In every sector, Hossam Yafri Hamza Laithi and Ali Saqri When gray hair appeared and your father betrayed me, the edges of the throat were dyed with it And your vow is an evil vow Abdullah bin Rawahah said, weeping for Hamza, may God be pleased with him: My eyes cried and they had every right to cry, but crying and wailing are of no use. On the lion of God, the next day they said, Ahmaza, that man is dead. All Muslims were affected by it there, and the Messenger was affected by it. O Abu Ya'la, the pillars have guided you, and you are the noble one who attains righteousness. May the peace of your Lord be upon you, in the gardens of eternal bliss. Oh, good Hashemites, be patient, for all your actions are good and beautiful. The Messenger of God is patient and generous, and he speaks by the command of God when he says: Oh Hashem, be patient, for all your deeds are good and beautiful. The Messenger of God is patient and generous, and he speaks by the command of God when he says: Is there anyone who can tell Lu’ay about me? From today onwards, my situation will continue to circulate. Before today, they did not know or taste our events that satisfy their thirst. You forgot to strike us with Qalib Badr the day after the sudden death came to you The day after Abu Jahl was killed, birds were circling around him. Utbah and his son are all destroyed, and the old man is bitten by the polished sword. We left Umayyah Majlab and in Haizoma with Nabil The Banu Rabi'ah tribe asked about it, but there are remnants of it on our swords. Oh Hind, do not gloat over Hamza, for your glory is humiliated. Oh Hind, cry and do not get tired, for you are the foolish Hebrew madman. His sister Safiyya also inherited him, and this is mentioned in the biography, may God be pleased with them all. The Almighty’s saying: And upon God let the believers put their trust. There is one issue in it, which is explaining trust. Trust in the language means showing helplessness and relying on others. Someone was dependent if he wasted his matter relying on others. Scholars differed about the reality of trust. Sahl ibn Abdullah was asked about it and he said: A group said that it is contentment with the guarantee and cutting off greed from the creatures. A group said: Trust is abandoning the causes and relying on the Causer of causes. If the cause distracts him from the Causer, the name of trust is removed from him. Sahl said: Whoever says that trust is achieved by abandoning the cause has attacked the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because God the Almighty says: So eat of what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good (al-Anfal 8:69). So spoils are acquired. God the Almighty also said: Then strike upon the necks and strike from them every fingertip (al-Anfal 8:12). So this is an action. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God loves the professional servant. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to lend money secretly. Another said: This is the opinion of most jurists, and that trust in God is confidence in God and certainty that His judgment will be carried out, and following the Sunnah of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in striving for the necessary means of food and drink, guarding against the enemy, preparing weapons, and using what is required by the usual Sunnah of God Almighty. This is what the Sufi scholars have adopted, but it does not deserve the name of trust in their view with reassurance regarding those means and turning to them in the heart, for they do not bring benefit nor do they repel reassurance regarding those means and turning to them in the heart, for they do not bring benefit nor repel harm, rather the cause and the effect are the action of God Almighty, and everything is from Him and by His will, and whenever the one who trusts relies on those means, he has been stripped of that name. Then the trustful are in two states: The first is the state of the one who is able to trust, so he does not turn to any of those means in his heart, and does not engage in them except by the command of the matter. The second: The state of the one who is not capable, who sometimes turns to the causes, but he repels them from himself by scientific methods, definitive proofs, and current tastes. He remains in this state until God, through His generosity, raises him to the station of the capable, trusting ones, and joins him to the degrees of the knowers.
3:123: God Almighty says: “And God had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak. So fear God that you may be grateful.” It has six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And indeed God helped you at Badr. Badr was on the seventeenth of Ramadan, a Friday, eighteen months after the Hijra. Badr is a body of water there, and the place was named after it. Al-Sha’bi said: That water belonged to a man from Juhayna, and he was called Badr, and the place was named after it. The first is more common. Al-Waqidi and others said: Badr is the name of a place that was not transferred. It will come in the story of Badr in Al-Anfal, God willing. Adh-lah means few, and that is because they were three hundred and thirteen or fourteen men. And their enemy was between nine hundred and a thousand. And Adh-lah is the plural of humiliated. And the word humiliation in this place is borrowed, and they were nothing but honorable in themselves, but their relation to their enemy and to all the infidels in the regions of the earth necessitates upon reflection their humiliation and that they will be defeated. And victory is support, so God granted them victory on the day of Badr, and killed the leaders of the polytheists on it, and on that day Islam was built, and it was the first battle that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fought. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Buraydah, he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) participated in seventeen battles, and fought in eight of them. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq that he said: I met Zaid bin Arqam and asked him: How many battles did the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) participate in? He said: Nineteen battles. I asked: How many battles did you participate in with him? He said: Seventeen battles. I asked: What was the first battle he participated in? He said: Dhat al-Usayr or al-Ushair. All of this is contrary to what the historians and biographers say. Muhammad bin Saad said in his book Al-Tabaqat: The battles of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) were twenty-seven, and his raids were fifty-six, and in another narration forty-six, and the battles in which the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) fought were Badr, Uhud, Al-Muraisi’, Al-Khandaq, Khaybar, Qurayzah, Al-Fath, Hunayn, and At-Ta’if. Ibn Saad said: This is what we have agreed upon. In some narrations, he fought against Banu Nadir, in Wadi Al-Qura on his way back from Khaybar, and in Al-Ghabah. If this is established, then we say: Zaid and Buraydah only reported what he knew or witnessed.
