Zaid’s statement: The first raid he raided was Dhat al-Usayrah also contradicts what the historians and biographers have said. Muhammad ibn Sa’d said: There were three raids before the raid of al-Usayrah, meaning he raided it himself. Ibn Abd al-Barr said in the book al-Durar fi al-Maghazi wa al-Siyar: The first raid that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) raided was the raid of Waddan, which he raided himself in Safar. That is because he arrived in Madinah twelve nights before the end of Rabi’ al-Awwal, and stayed there for the rest of Rabi’ al-Awwal, and the rest of the year until Safar of the year two of the Hijrah. Then he went out in the aforementioned Safar and appointed Sa’d ibn Ubadah over Madinah until he reached Waddan and bid farewell to Banu Damrah. Then he returned to Madinah without encountering any war, and it is called the raid of al-Abwa’. Then he stayed in the city until the month of Rabi` al-Akhir of the aforementioned year, then he left it and appointed Sa`ib ibn Uthman ibn Naz`un over the city until he reached Buwat in the direction of Radwa, then he returned to the city and did not encounter any war, then he stayed there for the rest of Rabi` al-Akhir and some of Jumada al-Ula, then he left as a raider and appointed Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad over the city, and he took the road to Malik to al-`Usayrah. I said: Ibn Ishaq mentioned on the authority of Ammar bin Yasser who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib and I were companions in the expedition of Al-Ushayriyah from Batn Yanbu. When the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) descended upon it, he stayed there for a month, and made peace there with Banu Mudlij and their allies from Banu Damrah. Then Ali ibn Abi Talib said to me: "O Abu Al-Yaqzan, would you like to go to these people? A group of Banu Mudlij are working at a spring of theirs. We are looking at how they work." So we went to them and looked at them for a while, then we fell asleep. We went to a tree of palm trees in a shallow area of land and slept in it. By God, nothing scared us except the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) by his foot. We sat down and were covered in dust from that shallow area. On that day, the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said to Ali: What is the matter with you, O Abu Turab? So he told him what had happened to us. He said: The red one of Thamud who hamstrung the she-camel and the one who will strike you, O Ali, on this - and the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) put his hand on his head - until this is wet from it - and he put his hand on his beard. Abu Omar said: He stayed there for the rest of Jumada al-Ula and some nights of Jumada al-Akhira, and he bid farewell to Banu Mudlij there, then he returned without encountering any war. Then after that came the first Battle of Badr a few days later. This is what the historians and biographers do not doubt, for Zayd ibn Arqam only reported what he had. And God knows best. It is said: Dhat al-Usr with sin and shin, and a ha is added to it and it is said: al-Ushirah. Then came the Battle of Badr al-Kubra, which is the greatest of the battles in virtue of those who witnessed it, and in it God supported His Prophet and the believers with His angels according to the majority of scholars, and the apparent meaning of the verse indicates this, not on the Day of Uhud. And whoever said that it was on the Day of Uhud made the words of God the Almighty: And God had certainly helped you at Badr to His words: give thanks an interjection between the two statements. This is the saying of Amir al-Sha’bi, and the people disagreed with him. Narrations claim that the angels were present on the day of Badr and fought. Among them is the saying of Abu Usaid Malik bin Rabi’ah, who was present at Badr: If I were with you now at Badr and had my sight, I would show you the valley from which the angels came out. I have no doubt or hesitation. Narrated by Aqeel on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Hazim Salamah bin Dinar. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Zuhri is not known to have narrated anything from Abu Hazim other than this one hadith. It is said that Abu Usaid was the last of the people of Badr to die. He was mentioned by Abu Omar in Al-Isti’ab and others. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, he said: On the day of Badr, the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) looked at the polytheists, who were a thousand, and his companions were three hundred and nineteen men. The Prophet of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) faced the qiblah, then stretched out his hands and began to call upon his Lord: (O God, fulfill for me what You promised me. O God, fulfill what You promised me. O God, if You destroy this group of Muslims, You will not be worshipped on earth). He continued to call upon his Lord, stretching out his hands and facing the qiblah, until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr came to him, took his cloak, threw it over his shoulders, then embraced him from behind and said: O Prophet of God, it is enough for you to implore your Lord, for He will fulfill for you what He promised you. Then God the Almighty revealed: When you called upon your Lord, and He answered you, ‘I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another.’ (al-Anfal 8:9) So God the Almighty reinforced him with the angels. Abu Zamil said: Ibn Abbas told me: While a Muslim man was pursuing a polytheist man in front of him that day, he heard a whip strike above him and the voice of a horseman saying: Go forward, Haizum. He looked at the polytheist in front of him and fell down. He looked at him and saw that his nose had been cut off and his face split as if he had been struck by a whip, turning it all green. Then the Ansari came and told the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about that, and he said: You have spoken the truth, from the reinforcements of the third heaven. So they killed seventy that day and took seventy captive. He mentioned the hadith, and its full completion will come at the end of Al-Anfal, God willing. So the Sunnah and the Qur’an agree on what the majority said, and praise be to God. On the authority of Kharijah bin Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Gabriel: “Who among the angels said on the day of Badr: Go forward, Haizum?” Gabriel said: O Muhammad, not all the people of heaven know better. On the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him that he addressed the people and said: While I was drawing water from the well of Badr, a violent wind came, the likes of which I had never seen before, then it went away, then a violent wind came, the likes of which I had never seen before except the one before it. He said: And I think he mentioned: Then a violent wind came, and the first wind was Gabriel, who descended with a thousand angels with the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). The second wind was Michael, who descended with a thousand angels on the right of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), and Abu Bakr was on his right. The third wind was Israfil, who descended with a thousand angels on the left side of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), and I was on the left side. On the authority of Sahl ibn Hunaif may God be pleased with him, he said: I saw us at Badr and one of us would point his sword at the head of a polytheist, but his head would fall off his body before it reached him. On the authority of Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas, he said: On the day of Badr, people would recognize those killed by the angels from those they had killed by striking them above the necks and on the fingers like the mark of fire that had been burned. Al-Bayhaqi may God have mercy on him mentioned all of this. Some of them said: The angels were fighting and the mark of their striking the infidels was clear, because wherever their strike struck, fire ignited in that place, to the extent that Abu Jahl said to Ibn Mas’ud: Did you kill me?! The one who killed me was the one whose spear did not reach the hump of his horse, even if I tried hard. The benefit of the large number of angels was to calm the hearts of the believers, and because God the Almighty made those angels fighters until the Day of Resurrection. So every army that is patient and seeks reward, the angels come to them and fight with them. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: The angels did not fight except on the day of Badr, and in other than that, they witness and do not fight, they are only a number or reinforcements. Some of them said: The benefit of the large number of angels was that they were calling and glorifying God, and increasing the number of those who fought that day. So based on this, the angels did not fight on the day of Badr, but rather they were present to call for steadfastness, and the first is more. Qatada said: This was on the day of Badr, God reinforced them with a thousand, then they became three thousand, then they became five thousand, so that is what God Almighty said: When you called upon your Lord, and He answered you, ‘I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another.’ (al-Anfal 8:9)
3:124: The Almighty said: Will it not suffice you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down? And His saying: Yes, if you are patient and fear God and they come upon you at once, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels with marks. So the believers persisted on the day of Badr and feared God, so God reinforced them with five thousand angels as He promised them. This is all on the day of Badr. Al-Hasan said: These five thousand are a reserve for the believers until the Day of Resurrection. Al-Sha'bi said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were informed on the day of Badr that Kurz bin Jabir Al-Muharibi wanted to reinforce the polytheists, so this upset the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims, so God revealed: Will it not suffice you until His saying: marked. So Kurz was informed of the defeat, but he did not reinforce them and returned, so God did not reinforce them with the five thousand, and they had been reinforced with a thousand. It was said: God promised the believers on the day of Badr that if they were patient in obeying Him and feared His prohibitions, He would also support them in all their wars. They were not patient and did not fear His prohibitions except on the day of the Confederates, so He supported them when they besieged Qurayzah. It was said: This was on the day of Uhud, God promised them support if they were patient, but they were not patient, so He did not support them with a single king, and if they had been supported they would not have been defeated. This was said by Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak. If it is said: It has been proven from Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas that he said: I saw on the right and left of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Badr two men wearing white clothes fighting on his behalf with the fiercest fighting. I have never seen them before or after. It was said to him: Perhaps this is specific to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he was specific to two kings fighting on his behalf, and this is not support for the Companions. And God knows best. Second: The descent of the angels is a reason for victory that the Almighty Lord does not need, but rather the creation needs it, so let the heart attach itself to God and trust in Him, for He is the Victorious with and without a reason, His command, when He intends a thing, is only to say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is (Ya Sin: 82). But He informed of this so that the creation would comply with the reasons He commanded them to do, which had already passed, And you will not find any change in the way of God (al-Ahzab 33:62). This does not undermine trust. It is a response to those who said that reasons were only prescribed for the weak, not the strong, for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions were the strong ones and others were the weak ones, and this is clear. Madd is in evil, and Amd is in good. This was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. Abu Haywah read Mizlin with a kasra over the zay and a light sukoon, meaning sending down victory. Ibn ‘Amir read it with a shaddah over the zay and a fathah for emphasis.
3:125: The Almighty said: Yes and the speech is complete. If you are patient is a condition, meaning in meeting the enemy. And fear is a conjunction to it, as for disobeying Him. The answer is He will support you and the meaning of from their face is from their face. This is from Ikrimah, Qatadah, Al-Hasan, Al-Rabi', Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd. It was said: from their anger, from Mujahid and Al-Dahhak. They had become angry on the day of Uhud because of what they had encountered. The origin of for is to intend something and to take it seriously, and it is from their saying: the pot boiled, boiling, and seething. And fore is boiling. And his anger boiled if it seethed. And its action from fore means before it calms down. And the boiling is what boils from the pot. And in the revelation And the oven boiled (Hud:40) the poet said: Their fate boils over on us, so we drink it Third: The Almighty’s saying: marked with a fat-ha on the waw, a passive participle, and this is the reading of Ibn ‘Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Nafi’. That is, marked with signs. Marked with a kasra on the waw is an active participle, and this is the reading of Abu ‘Amr, Ibn Kathir, and ‘Asim, so the meaning is possible as mentioned above, that is, they informed themselves with a sign, and informed their horses. Al-Tabari and others preferred this reading. Many commentators said: Marked means sending their horses in the raid. Al-Mahdawi mentioned this meaning in masawmeen with a fat-ha on the waw, that is, God sent them against the infidels. Ibn Furak also said the same. According to the first reading, they differed regarding the mark of the angels. It was narrated from Ibn Abi Talib, Ibn ‘Abbas, and others that the angels wore white turbans that they let down between their shoulders. Al-Bayhaqi mentioned it from Ibn ‘Abbas, and Al-Mahdawi narrated it from Al-Zajjaj. Except for Gabriel, who wore a yellow turban like Al-Zubayr ibn Al-‘Awwam, and Ibn Ishaq said the same. Al-Rabi’ said: Their sign was that they were on white horses, on piebald horses between the sky and the earth, marked, killing and capturing. So his saying marked indicates that the piebald horses were not the sign. And God knows best. Mujahid said: Their horses had trimmed tails and manes, and their forelocks and tails were marked with wool and wool. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The angels marked the horses on the day of Badr with white wool on their forelocks and tails. Abbad bin Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, Hisham bin Urwah and Al-Kalbi said: The angels descended in the sign of Az-Zubayr, wearing yellow turbans hanging loosely over their shoulders. Abdullah and Urwah, the sons of Az-Zubayr, said that. Abdullah said: It was a yellow sheet that Az-Zubayr, may God be pleased with him, wore as a turban. I said: The verse indicates: The fourth: on adopting a badge and mark for the tribes and battalions, which the Sultan makes for them, so that each tribe and battalion can be distinguished from the others during war, and on the superiority of the piebald horse because the angels descend upon it. I said: Perhaps it was revealed to her in agreement with Al-Miqdad’s horse, for it was piebald and they had no other horse, so the angels descended on the piebald horses out of respect for Al-Miqdad, just as Gabriel descended wearing a yellow turban like Al-Zubayr. And God knows best. And the verse also indicates... The fifth: On woolen clothing, which was worn by the prophets and righteous people. Abu Dawood and Ibn Majah narrated, and the wording is his, on the authority of Abu Burdah, on the authority of his father, who said: My father said to me: If you had witnessed us while we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the rain struck us, you would have thought that our smell was the smell of sheep. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, wore a Roman robe made of wool with narrow sleeves, as narrated by the imams. And Yunus, peace be upon him, wore it. Narrated by Muslim. This meaning will be further explained in An-Nahl, God willing. Sixth: I said: As for what Mujahid mentioned that their horses had their tails and manes cut off, it is far-fetched, for in the Musannaf of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Utbah ibn Abd al-Salami, he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Do not cut the forelocks, manes, or tails of horses, for their tails are their place of slaughter, their manes are their warmth, and their forelocks contain goodness. So Mujahid’s statement is based on the fact that the horses of the angels were of that nature. And God knows best. The verse indicates the beauty of white and yellow colors because the angels descend with them. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever wears yellow shoes, his need will be fulfilled. And he, peace be upon him, said: Wear white clothes, for it is the best of your clothes, and shroud your dead in it. As for turbans, they are the crowns and clothing of the Arabs. Rukana narrated: He wrestled with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, defeated him - Rukanah said - and I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The difference between us and the polytheists is the turbans over the skullcaps. Narrated by Abu Dawud. Al-Bukhari said: Its chain of transmission is unknown and it is not known that it heard some of it from others.
3:126: The Almighty says: And God has not made it except as good tidings for you. The ha' is for support, which is the angels, or the promise, or the support, and it is indicated by He supports you or for the timing or for the sending down or the number according to the meaning, because five thousand is a number. And that your hearts may be reassured by it. The lam is the lam of ki, meaning that your hearts may be reassured by it, He made it. And victory is only from God meaning the victory of the believers, and that does not include the victory of the disbelievers, because what happened to them of victory is only a respite surrounded by failure, bad consequences, and loss.
3:127: The Almighty said: To cut off a portion of those who disbelieved meaning by killing. The verse was structured as: And God had already given you victory at Badr to cut off. It was said: The meaning is: And victory is only from God to cut off. It is possible that it is related to -provides you, meaning He provides you to cut off. The meaning: Who among the polytheists was killed on the day of Badr, according to Al-Hasan and others. Al-Suddi: He means by it those among the polytheists who were killed on the day of Uhud, and they were eighteen men. The meaning of suppresses them is to grieve them, and the suppressed is the one who is grieved. It was narrated: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Abu Talha and saw his son depressed. He said: ‘What is the matter with him?’ It was said: ‘His camel died.’” Its origin, as some linguists have mentioned, is to afflict them with grief and anger in their livers. The dal was replaced with a ta, just as it was changed in sabt ra’shu and sabdahu, meaning to shave his head. God kabt the enemy, meaning to turn him away and humiliate him, and kabdahu afflicted him in his liver. It is said: Grief has burned his liver, and enmity has burned his liver. The Arabs say about the enemy: black-livered. Al-A’sha said: I did not dare to go to a people who are enemies and have black livers. As if the livers, when burned by the intensity of the enmity, turned black. Abu Majlaz read or yakbadhum with a dal. The loser: the one who has lost hope. Khaab yakhib if he does not get what he asked for. Al-Khayab: the cup that does not light.
3:128: God Almighty says: “You have no part in the matter, whether He forgives them or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers. To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and God is Forgiving and Merciful.” There are three issues: First: It is proven in Sahih Muslim: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had his front tooth broken on the day of Uhud, and his head was wounded. He kept draining the blood and saying: How can a people succeed when they have wounded the head of their Prophet and broken his front tooth while he is calling them to God? Then God revealed: You have no part in the matter. Ad-Dahhak: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wanted to supplicate against the polytheists, so God revealed: You have no part in the matter. It was said that he asked permission to supplicate for their extermination. When this verse was revealed, he knew that some of them would convert to Islam, and many of them did, including Khalid ibn al-Walid, Amr ibn al-Aas, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and others. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) was praying against four men, so God Almighty revealed, You have no part in the matter, so God guided them to Islam. He said: This is a good, strange, and authentic hadith. And God Almighty’s statement, or He will forgive them, it was said: It is connected to to cut off a part, and the meaning is: to kill a group of them, or sadden them with defeat, or to forgive them, or to punish them. And or here may mean until and except that, Imru’ al-Qais said:...or we die and we are excused Our scholars said: His, peace be upon him, saying: How can a people succeed who split the head of their prophet? is a rejection of the success of the one who did that to him. And the Almighty’s saying: You have no part in the matter is an approximation of what he rejected and a hope for their conversion to Islam. And when he hoped for that, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: O God, forgive my people, for they do not know. As in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: It is as if I see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating the story of a prophet who was beaten by his people, and he is wiping the blood from his face and saying: O Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know. Our blind people said: The narrator in the hadith of Ibn Masoud is the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he is the one being narrated from, as evidenced by what has come clearly and explicitly: (When his front tooth was broken and his face was wounded on the day of Uhud, his companions were greatly distressed by that and they said: Why don’t you invoke curses upon them? He said: (I was not sent to curse, but I was sent as a caller and a mercy. O God, forgive my people, for they do not know.) It was as if that was revealed to him before the Uhud incident occurred, and the Prophet did not specify that for him. When that happened to him, it was determined that he was the one meant by that, as evidenced by what we mentioned. It is also explained by what Omar said to him in some of his speech: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God! Noah invoked curses upon his people and said: My Lord, do not leave on the earth a single inhabitant of the disbelievers (Nuh 71:26). If you had invoked the like of it upon us, we would have perished from the last one. Your back and your mother trampled on your face and your front tooth was broken, but you refused to say anything but good, so you said: My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know. And his saying: God’s wrath was intense against a people who broke the front teeth of their Prophet meaning the one who did that directly. We mentioned his name with some differences in that, but we said that it was specific to the one who did it directly, because a group of those who witnessed Uhud converted to Islam and their Islam was good. Second: Some Kufians claimed that this verse abrogates the supplication that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to do after bowing in the last rak’ah of the dawn prayer. He provided evidence: On the authority of Ibn Omar, he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say in the dawn prayer after raising his head from bowing, and he said: (O God, our Lord, to You be praise in the Hereafter - then he said - O God, curse so-and-so, so God the Almighty revealed: You have no part in the matter, whether He forgives them or punishes them the verse. Al-Bukhari narrated it, and Muslim also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, more complete than it. This is not a place for abrogation, but God the Almighty alerted His Prophet that the matter is not up to him, and that he does not know anything of the unseen except what he knows, and that the matter is entirely up to God, He forgives whomever He wills and hastens punishment for whomever He wills. The meaning is: You have no part in the matter, and God has whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, apart from you and apart from them. He forgives whomever He wills and forgives whomever He wills. So there is no abrogation, and God knows best. And He explained by His saying: You have no part in the matter that matters are by the decree and predestination of God, in response to the Qadarites and others. Third: The scholars differed regarding the Qunut in the Fajr prayer and other prayers. The Kufians forbade it in the Fajr prayer and other prayers. This is the view of Al-Layth and Yahya bin Yahya Al-Laythi Al-Andalusi, the companion of Malik, and Al-Sha’bi rejected it. In Al-Muwatta’, on the authority of Ibn Umar: He did not perform the Qunut in any of the prayers. Al-Nasa’i narrated that Qutaybah informed us on the authority of Khalaf on the authority of Abu Malik Al-Ashja’i on the authority of his father, who said: I prayed behind the Prophet (peace be upon him) and he did not pray Qunut, I prayed behind Abu Bakr and he did not pray Qunut, I prayed behind Umar and he did not pray Qunut, I prayed behind Uthman and he did not pray Qunut, I prayed behind Ali and he did not pray Qunut, then he said: O my son, this is an innovation. It was said: Qunut is always said in Fajr and in all prayers if a calamity befalls the Muslims, as stated by Ash-Shafi’i and At-Tabari. It was also said: It is recommended in Fajr prayer, and it was narrated from Ash-Shafi’i. Al-Hasan and Sahnun said: It is a Sunnah. This is implied by the narration of Ali ibn Ziyad from Malik that the one who deliberately neglected the prayer should repeat it. At-Tabari narrated the consensus that neglecting it does not invalidate the prayer. Al-Hasan said: There is prostration of forgetfulness in neglecting it, and this is one of the two opinions of Ash-Shafi’i. Ad-Daraqutni mentioned from Saeed ibn Abdul Aziz regarding the one who attributed Qunut in Fajr prayer, he said: He should perform the two prostrations of forgetfulness. Malik chose before bowing, and this is the opinion of Ishaq. It was also narrated on the authority of Malik after bowing, and it was narrated on the authority of the four caliphs, and it is the opinion of al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq as well. It was narrated on the authority of a group of the Companions that there is a choice in that. Al-Daraqutni narrated with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Anas that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to recite the supplication in the morning prayer until he departed this world. Abu Dawud mentioned in Al-Marasil on the authority of Khalid bin Abi Imran, who said: While the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) was praying against Mudar, Gabriel came to him and motioned to him to be silent, so he remained silent. Then he said: (O Muhammad, God did not send you to insult or curse. Rather, He sent you as a mercy and not as a punishment. You have no part in the matter. Either He will forgive them or punish them, for they are wrongdoers.) He said: Then he taught him this supplication, so he said: (O God, we seek Your help and ask Your forgiveness, and we believe in You and submit to You and abandon and forsake those who disbelieve in You. O God, You alone do we worship, and to You we pray and prostrate, and to You we hasten and we hope for Your mercy and fear Your punishment, for Your punishment will surely overtake the disbelievers.)
3:129: God Almighty says: “To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.”
3:130: God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied. This prohibition of consuming usury is an interjection during the story of Uhud. Ibn Atiyyah said: I have memorized something narrated about that. I said: Mujahid said: They used to sell on credit, and when the time came, they would increase the price in return for delaying it, so God the Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied. I said: He only singled out usury from among all other sins because it is the one for which God has permitted war in His statement: But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger. (al-Baqarah 2:279), and war is permitted by killing, so it is as if He is saying: If you do not avoid usury, you will be defeated and killed. So He ordered them to abandon usury because it was practiced among them. And God knows best. Doubled is an accusative in the state of state, and doubled is its description. It was read muda'fa and its meaning is the usury in which the Arabs used to weaken the debt, so the claimant would say: Do you demand or increase? As mentioned in Al-Baqarah. And muda'fa is an indication of the repetition of the doubling year after year as they used to do, so this emphatic phrase indicates the hideousness and ugliness of their action, and therefore the case of doubling was mentioned in particular. God Almighty says: And fear God meaning regarding usurious money, so do not consume it.
3:132: The Almighty said: And obey God meaning obey God in the obligatory duties and the Messenger in the Sunnah. It was also said: And obey God in prohibiting usury and the Messenger in what has reached you of the prohibition. That you may receive mercy meaning so that God may have mercy on you. This has been mentioned previously.
3:133: God Almighty says: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the righteous. There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And hasten. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir read and hasten without the waw, and this is how it is in the copies of the Qur’an of the people of Medina and the people of Ash-Sham. The remaining seven read and hasten with the waw. Abu ‘Ali said: Both matters are common and correct. Whoever reads with the waw, it is because he connected the sentence to the sentence, and whoever leaves the waw, it is because the second sentence is confused with the first, thus dispensing with the connection with the waw. And hastening means taking the initiative, and it is a reciprocal verb. And in the verse there is an omission, meaning hasten to what necessitates forgiveness, which is obedience. Anas bin Malik and Makhul said in their interpretation of And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord: its meaning is to the opening takbir. Ali bin Abi Talib said: to performing the obligatory duties. ‘Uthman bin ‘Affan: to sincerity. Al-Kalbi: to repentance from usury. And it was said: to steadfastness in battle. And other than this was said. The verse is general in all, and its meaning is the meaning of So hasten to do good deeds (al-Baqarah 2:148). And it was mentioned before. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And a Garden whose width is that of the heavens and the earth. Its meaning is like width, so the complement was deleted, like His saying: He did not create you and resurrect you except as a single soul (Luqman 31:28), meaning except as the creation of a single soul and its resurrection. The poet said: I thought my caravan was an embrace, but it was no embrace other than you He wants the sound of a hug. Its counterpart is in Surat al-Hadid 57:And a garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth (al-Hadid 57:21). Scholars differed in its interpretation. Ibn Abbas said: The heavens and the earth will be joined together as clothes are spread out and joined together. That is the width of Paradise, and no one knows its length except God. This is the opinion of the majority, and it is not denied, because “in the hadith of Abu Dharr on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: (The seven heavens and the seven earths in relation to the Kursi are nothing but a pearl thrown into a desert. The Kursi in relation to the Throne is nothing but a ring thrown into a desert.) These are creations that are much greater than the heavens and the earth, and the power of God is greater than all of that. Al-Kalbi said: There are four gardens: the Garden of Eden, the Garden of Refuge, the Garden of Paradise, and the Garden of Delight. Each garden is as wide as the heavens and the earth if they were connected to each other. Ismail Al-Suddi said: The heavens and the earth would collapse and become mustard seed, so for every mustard seed there is a garden whose width is like the width of the heavens and the earth. In Sahih: (The lowest in status of the people of Paradise is he who wishes and wishes until his hopes run out, then God Almighty says: You have that and ten times more like it.) Narrated by Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, narrated by Muslim and others. Ya`la bin Abi Marra said: Al-Tanukhi, the messenger of Heraclius to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, met him in Homs. He was an old man who said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the letter of Heraclius, so he handed the document to a man on his left. He said: I said: Who is your companion who is reading? They said: Muawiyah. So here is my companion’s letter: You wrote inviting me to a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is the Hellfire? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God! Where is the night when the day comes? And with a similar argument, Al-Faruq used it as evidence against the Jews when they said to him: What do you think of your saying and a Paradise whose width is the heavens and the earth, so where is the Hellfire? They said to him: You have taken what is in the Torah. God Almighty pointed out the width to the length because the length is usually greater than the width, and when length is mentioned it does not indicate the extent of the width. Al-Zuhri said: Rather, he described its width. As for its length, only God knows it. This is like the Almighty’s saying: “Reclining on couches whose linings are of heavy brocade” (Al-Rahman: 54). He described the lining with the best known adornment, since it is known that the outer surfaces are more beautiful and perfect than the linings. The Arabs say: a wide land, and a wide desert, meaning wide. The poet said: As if the lands of God are wide for the fearful and wanted, his hand is full Some people said: The speech is based on the Arabs’ metaphorical passage, so since Paradise is extremely vast and spacious, it is good to express it as the width of the heavens and the earth, as you would say to a man: This is a sea, or to a large animal: This is a mountain. The verse did not intend to specify the width, but rather it meant that it is the widest thing you have seen. The majority of scholars agree that Paradise was created and exists, based on His statement: Prepared for the righteous, which is the text of the hadith of Isra’ and others in the two Sahihs and others. The Mu’tazila said: They were not created in our time, and that when God the Most High folded the heavens and the earth, He began the creation of Paradise and Hell wherever He willed, because they are a house of recompense with reward and punishment. So He created us after the obligation at the time of recompense, so that the house of obligation and the house of recompense would not come together in this world, as they did not come together in the Hereafter. Ibn Furak said: Paradise will be increased on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Atiyo said: This is related to Mundhir ibn Sa’id and others who said that Paradise has not been created yet. Ibn Atiyah said: Ibn Furak’s statement it is added to it is an indication of something that exists, but it needs a chain of transmission that eliminates the excuse for the addition. I said: Ibn Atiyyah may God be pleased with him spoke the truth in what he said. If the seven heavens and the seven earths in relation to the Kursi are like dirhams thrown into a desert, and the Kursi in relation to the Throne is like a ring thrown into a desert, then Paradise now, as it will be in the Hereafter, is as wide as the heavens and the earth, since the Throne is its ceiling, according to what was mentioned in Sahih Muslim. It is known that the ceiling contains what is beneath it and more. If all of creation is like a ring in relation to it, then who can estimate it and know its length and width except God, its Creator, whose power has no end, and whose kingdom has no limit, glory be to Him.
3:134: God Almighty says: Those who spend in prosperity and adversity and who restrain anger and pardon the people - and God loves the doers of good. There are four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Those who spend This is from the description of the righteous for whom Paradise has been prepared. The apparent meaning of the verse is praise for the action of the one who is recommended. As-Sira means ease and As-Sira means hardship - said by Ibn Abbas, Al-Kalbi and Muqatil. Ubaid bin Umair and Ad-Dahhak said: As-Sira and Ad-Sira are ease and hardship. It is said in the state of health and sickness. It was said: In the state of ease in life, and in Ad-Sira means he makes a will after death. It was said: In the state of ease in weddings and banquets, and in Ad-Sira in calamities and funerals. It was said: In the state of ease is the spending that pleases you, such as spending on children and relatives, and Ad-Sira on enemies. It is said: In the state of ease is what a young man is entertained with and given as gifts. And Ad-Sira is what he spends on the needy and gives them in charity. I said: The verse is general. Then God Almighty said: And those who restrain anger, which is the issue: The second: To suppress anger is to return it to the stomach. It is said: He suppressed his anger, meaning he kept quiet about it and did not show it, although he was able to inflict it on his enemy. And he filled the water skin and blocked it. And the kadhamah is what blocks the path of water, and from this comes the word kadham for the strap that blocks the mouth of the water skin and the water skin. And the camel suppressed its jar if it returned it to its stomach. And it is sometimes said that it holds the jar back before sending it to its mouth: kadham, as narrated by al-Zajjaj. It is said: The camel and the female camel suppressed if they did not chew the cud, and from this comes the saying of al-Ra’i: Then they poured out, after their reluctance, a jug of Dhu al-Abraq, when they pastured a field. Al-Haqil: a place. Al-Haqil is a plant. It has been said that it does this when it is frightened or in distress, so it does not chew the cud. A’sha Bahila said, describing a man who slaughters camels, so they are frightened by him: You may choke on the pearls when you see them until the jars cut through your insides. And from this is a man who is kazeem or makzoom if he is filled with grief and sadness. In the Qur’an: And his eyes turned white from grief, so he was “kazeem (Yusuf 12:84) And his face remained dark, and he was “kazeem (al-Nahl 16:58) When he cried out while he was “kazeem (al-Qalam 68:48). Rage is the root of anger, and they often go together, but the difference between them is that rage does not appear in the limbs, unlike anger, which appears in the limbs with an action, and it is inevitable. That is why rage was attributed to God, the Most High, as it refers to His actions towards those who incur wrath. Some people have interpreted rage as anger, but that is not good. And God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And those who pardon people. Pardoning people is the most noble type of good deed, as it is permissible for a person to pardon and where his right is directed. And whoever deserves punishment and it is left to him, he has been pardoned. And there is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of from people. Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Kalbi, and Al-Zajjaj said: And those who pardon people means from kingdoms. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is good as an example, as they are servants, so they sin a lot, and the power over them is easy, and enforcing the punishment is easy, so this is why it is interpreted like this. It was narrated on the authority of Maymun bin Mihran that his slave girl came one day with a plate of hot broth, and he had guests, so she stumbled and poured the broth on him, so Maymun wanted to hit her, but the slave girl said: My master, use the saying of God Almighty: And those who restrain anger. He said to her: I have done so, so she said: Do what comes after it, And those who pardon people. He said: I have pardoned you. The slave girl said: And God loves the doers of good. Maymun said: I have done good to you, so you are free for the sake of God Almighty. It was narrated from Al-Ahnaf bin Qais something similar. Zaid bin Salim said: And those who pardon people for their injustice and wrongdoing. This is general, and it is the apparent meaning of the verse. Muqatil bin Hayyan said about this verse: It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said at that time: Indeed, these are few of my nation, except for those whom God has protected, and they were many among the nations that have passed. So God, the Most High, praised those who forgive when angry and commended them, saying: And when they are angry, they forgive (al-Shura 42:37). And He praised those who restrain their anger by saying: And pardon the people, and He informed us that He loves them for their goodness in that. There are hadiths that have been narrated about restraining anger, forgiving people, and controlling oneself when angry, and that is one of the greatest forms of worship and struggle against one’s self. So He said: The strong man is not the one who wrestles well, but the strong man is the one who controls himself when he is angry. And he, peace be upon him, said: There is no sip that a servant takes that is better for him or greater in reward than a sip of anger for the sake of God. Anas narrated. A man said: O Messenger of God, what is more severe than anything? He said: The wrath of God. He said: What saves from the wrath of God? He said: Do not get angry. Al-Arji said: If you get angry, be dignified and control your anger. Be aware of what you say and hear. It is enough of an honor for you to be patient for an hour in which God will be pleased with you and you will be elevated. Urwa bin Al-Zubayr said about forgiveness: No people will attain glory, even if they are honored, until they are humiliated, even if they are honored by others. They curse and you see the colors shining. There is no forgiveness of humiliation, but forgiveness of honor. Abu Dawood and Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Sahl bin Muadh bin Anas Al-Juhani on the authority of his father on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever suppresses his anger while he is able to vent it, God will call him on the Day of Resurrection in front of all creation and let him choose whichever of the houris he wants. He said: This is a good and strange hadith. Anas narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said::(When the Day of Resurrection comes, a crier will call out, Whoever has his reward from God, let him enter Paradise. It will be said, Who is his reward from God? Then those who pardoned people will stand up and enter Paradise without being brought to account.) Al-Mawardi mentioned it. Ibn al-Mubarak said: I was sitting with al-Mansur when he ordered a man to be killed, so I said, “O Commander of the Faithful, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call out before God, the Almighty, the Majestic, whoever has a hand with God, let him come forward. No one will come forward except he who has pardoned a sin.) So he ordered him to be released. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: “And God loves the doers of good,” meaning He rewards them for their good deeds. Sari al-Saqti said: Good deeds mean doing good when possible, for you cannot do good at all times. The poet said: Do good if you are able to, and good deeds will be prepared. If you can, then do it quickly, being careful not to make it impossible. In Surat Al-Baqarah, we have already discussed the good-doer and doing good, so there is no point in repeating it.
3:135: The Almighty said: And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, God Almighty mentioned in this verse a category, they are below the first category, so He included them with it through His mercy and grace, so these are the ones who repent. Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Ata’: This verse was revealed about Nabhan At-Tammar - his nickname was Abu Muqbil - a beautiful woman came to him and he sold her some dates. He hugged her and kissed her and regretted it. He went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, so this verse was revealed. Abu Dawud At-Tayalisi mentioned in his Musnad on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: Abu Bakr told me - and Abu Bakr spoke the truth - that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (There is no servant who commits a sin, then performs ablution, prays two rak’ahs, and then seeks forgiveness from God, but that He will forgive him - then he recited this verse - And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins - the verse, and the other verse - And whoever does evil or wrongs himself.) At-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: A good hadith. This is general. A verse may have been revealed for a specific reason, then it includes all those who did that or did it more than that. It has been said that the reason for its revelation was: A Thaqafi went out on a raid and left his Ansari companion in charge of his family. He betrayed him by attacking her. She defended herself, but he kissed her hand. He regretted that and went out wandering the earth, regretful and repentant. Then the Thaqafi came and his wife told him about his companion’s action. He went out in search of him and brought him to Abu Bakr and Umar, hoping to find relief with them. They rebuked him. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him about his action. Then this verse was revealed. The general meaning is more appropriate for the hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that the companion said: O Messenger of God, the Children of Israel were more honorable to God than us, because the punishment of the sinner among them was written on the door of his house, and in another narration: the expiation for his sin was written on the threshold of his house: cut off your nose, cut off your ear, do such and such. So God Almighty revealed this verse as an expression of expansion and mercy and as a compensation for that action for the Children of Israel. It is narrated that Iblis cried when this verse was revealed. The word fahsha is used to refer to a sin, and it is often used specifically for adultery, so much so that Jabir ibn Abdullah and As-Suddi interpreted this verse as adultery. The word or in the phrase or wronged themselves is said to mean and, and what is meant is less than major sins. They remembered God means fearing His punishment and being ashamed of Him. Ad-Dahhak: They remembered the greatest presentation to God. It was also said that they thought that God would ask them about it, as stated by Al-Kalbi and Muqatil. Muqatil also said: They remembered God with their tongues when they sinned. Then seek forgiveness for their sins, meaning they asked for forgiveness for their sins. Every supplication that has this meaning or wording is a seeking of forgiveness. The master of seeking forgiveness was mentioned at the beginning of this Surah, and its time is the pre-dawn hours. Seeking forgiveness is great and its reward is immense, so much so that At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever says, I seek forgiveness from God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and I repent to Him, will be forgiven, even if he had fled from battle. Makhul narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: I have not seen anyone who sought forgiveness more than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Makhul said: I have not seen anyone who sought forgiveness more than Abu Hurairah. Makhul used to seek forgiveness a lot. Our scholars said: The required forgiveness is that which loosens the knot of persistence and establishes its meaning in the heart, not uttering it with the tongue. As for the one who says with his tongue: I seek forgiveness from God, but his heart persists in his disobedience, then his seeking forgiveness requires seeking forgiveness, and his minor sin is included among the major sins. It was narrated from Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he said: Our seeking forgiveness requires seeking forgiveness. I said: He said this in his time, so how about in our time when we see a person bent over in injustice! Eager to do it and not giving it up, and the rosary in his hand, claiming that he is seeking forgiveness for his sin, but that is mockery and belittlement on his part. In the Qur’an: And do not take the verses of God in jest (al-Baqarah 2:231). And it has been mentioned before. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And who forgives sins except God? That is, no one forgives sin or removes its punishment except God. And they did not persist That is, they did not persist and resolve to do what they did. Mujahid said: That is, they did not continue. Ma’bad bin Subaih said: I prayed behind Uthman and Ali was next to me, then he turned to us and said: You prayed without ablution, then he went and performed ablution and prayed. And they did not persist in what they did while they knew Insistence is the determination in the heart to do something and not to give it up. From this comes the word to tie up dinars, meaning to tie them up. Al-Hutay’ah said, describing horses: Frowning with disheveled truffles, if they seek their excuse with harvesters, they insist That is, she persisted in her enemy. Qatada said: Persistence is persistence in sins. The poet said: He insists at night, his troubles are not hidden. Woe to all of Egypt, the heart has chosen Sahl ibn Abdullah said: The ignorant is dead, the forgetful is asleep, the sinner is drunk, the persistent is doomed, and persistence is procrastination, and procrastination is saying: I will repent tomorrow, and this is the claim of the soul. How can he repent tomorrow when tomorrow he does not own? Someone other than Sahl said: Persistence is to intend not to repent, but if he intends sincere repentance, he is no longer persisting. Sahl’s statement is better. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no repentance with persistence. Third: Our scholars said: The motive for repentance and the solution to persistence is to continue thinking about the Book of God, the Almighty, the Forgiving, and what God, the Exalted, mentioned of the details of Paradise and promised to the obedient, and what He described of the torment of Hell and threatened the disobedient with, and he continued in that until his fear and hope became strong, so he called upon God, hoping for success in what is right. It has been said: The motive for that is a divine warning that alerts whoever seeks his happiness, to the ugliness of sins and their harm, as they are deadly poisons. I said: This is a difference in wording, not in meaning, because a person does not reflect on the promise and threat of God except by being alerted. So if the servant looks, by the grace of God the Most High, at himself and finds that he is laden with sins he has acquired and evil deeds he has committed, and regret arises from him for what he has neglected, and he abandons what came before for fear of the punishment of God the Most High, then it is true that he has repented. But if he is not like that, then he is persisting in sin and adhering to the causes of destruction. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: The sign of the repentant is that sin preoccupies him with food and drink, like the three who stayed behind. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: And they know has several opinions. It was said: That is, they remember their sins and repent from them. An-Nahhas said: This is a good opinion. It was said: And they know that I will punish for persistence. Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair said: And they know that if they repent, God will accept their repentance. It was said: They know that if they seek forgiveness, He will forgive them. It was said: They know what I have forbidden them, as Ibn Ishaq said. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi said: And they know that persistence is harmful, and that leaving it is better than continuing. Al-Hasan bin Abi Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, said on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, in what he narrated on the authority of his Lord, the Almighty, He said: (A slave committed a sin and said, O God, forgive my sin. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said, “My slave committed a sin and knew that he has a Lord who forgives sins and punishes for sins. Then he sinned again and said, “O God, forgive my sin.” He mentioned the same thing twice, and at the end of it: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.) Narrated by Muslim. This is evidence of the validity of repentance from its deficiency by repeating the sin, because the first repentance was an act of obedience that has expired and become valid. After committing the second sin, he needs another new repentance. Returning to sin is worse than starting it, because it adds to the sin the nullification of repentance. Returning to repentance is better than starting it, because it adds to it the persistence of insistence on the door of the Generous, and that there is no forgiver of sins except Him. His saying at the end of the hadith Do whatever you wish is a command that means honoring according to one of the sayings, so it is similar to his saying: “Enter it in peace” (al-Hijr 15:46). The end of the speech is report about the state of the one being addressed, that his past sins have been forgiven, and he is preserved, God willing, in what he will do in the future. The verse and the hadith indicate the great benefit of acknowledging sin and seeking forgiveness for it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a servant confesses his sin and then repents to God, God will accept his repentance. Narrated by both of them in the two Sahihs. He said: The young man deserves forgiveness if he confesses to the sins he has committed. Another said: Admit your sin and then ask for it to be forgiven. Denial is denial of sin, two sins. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you did not sin, God would replace you with a people who would sin and seek forgiveness, and He would forgive them. This is the benefit of the name of God the Most High, the Forgiving, the Accepter of Repentance, as we explained in the Most Sublime Book explaining the beautiful names of God. Fifth: The sins that one must repent for, whether they are disbelief or other than that. The repentance of the disbeliever is his belief along with his regret for his previous disbelief. Mere belief is not repentance in itself. Other than disbelief, it is either a right of God the Most High or a right of someone else. The right of God the Most High is sufficient for repentance from abandonment. However, there are some in which the Shariah did not suffice with mere abandonment, but rather added to that in some of them a compensation such as prayer and fasting. There are some in which it added expiation such as breaking oaths, li’an, and other than that. As for the rights of people, what is owed to them due to insolvency is hoped for, and His grace is bestowed. How many consequences has He guaranteed and how many bad deeds have He replaced with good ones? More clarification of this meaning will follow. Sixth - If a person does not remember and knows of it, he is not required to repent from it specifically, but if he remembers a sin, he must repent from it. Many people have interpreted what our Sheikh Abu Muhammad Abdul-Muati Al-Iskandarani may God be pleased with him mentioned, that Imam Al-Muhasibi may God have mercy on him believes that repentance from all types of sins is not valid, and that regretting all of them is not enough. Rather, he must repent from every action with his limbs and every resolve in his heart to do so specifically. They assumed that from his statement, but this is not what he meant, nor does his statement require it. Rather, the ruling of the person who is accountable is that if he knows the ruling on his actions, and knows the sin from the other, then his repentance is valid from the whole of what he knows. For if he does not know that his past action is a sin, he cannot repent from it, neither in general nor in detail. An example of this is a man who deals with a type of usury and does not know that it is usury, so if he hears the words of God Almighty: “O you who have believed, fear God and give up what remains of usury, if you should be believers. But if you do not, then be informed of a war from God and His Messenger” (al-Baqarah 2:279-288). This threat was too great for him, and he thought that he was safe from usury. If he now knows the reality of usury, then thinks about his past days and realizes that he has done a lot of it in the past, it is correct for him to regret it now in general, and he is not required to specify its times. And so it is with all the sins and evil deeds that he has committed, such as backbiting, gossiping, and other forbidden things that he did not know were forbidden. If the servant understands and examines what he has said in the past, he will repent from that in general, and regret what he has neglected of the right of God the Most High. And if he seeks forgiveness from the one whom he has wronged, then he seeks forgiveness from him in general, and his soul is content with abandoning his right, it is permissible, because it is a form of giving an unknown gift. This is with the servant’s stinginess and his eagerness to seek his right, so how about the Most Generous of the Generous, who bestows obedience and its causes and pardons sins, both small and great. Our Sheikh, may God have mercy on him, said: This is what the Imam meant, and what his words indicate to those who examine them. What the one who thinks about him thought that regret is not valid except for an action, a movement, and a stillness, specifically, is from the mind of the burden of what is unbearable, which did not occur according to the Sharia, even if it is permissible according to reason. It is necessary for him to know how many sips he took when drinking alcohol, how many movements he made when committing adultery, and how many steps he took to something forbidden. This is something that no one obeys, and repentance cannot be achieved from it in detail. There will come more clarification of the rulings on repentance and its conditions in An-Nisa’ and other things, God willing. Seventh: In the Almighty’s saying: And they did not persist, there is clear evidence and conclusive proof of what the sword of the Sunnah and the tongue of the nation, Judge Abu Bakr bin al-Tayyib, said: A person will be held accountable for what he has resolved in his conscience and resolved in his heart of disobedience. I said: In the revelation: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice - We will make him taste a painful punishment (al-Hajj 22:25) and He said: So it became like a barren field. So they were punished. It was said that their action was based on their intention, and its explanation will come. In Al-Bukhari: If two Muslims meet with their swords, then the killer and the killed will be in Hell. They said: O Messenger of God, this is the killer, but what about the killed? He said: He was eager to kill his companion. So he linked the threat to eagerness, which is determination, and he abolished the display of weapons. The most explicit of this is what Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Abu Kabsha Al-Anmari, and he authenticated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet: (The world is for four types of al-Nas 114:A man whom God has given wealth and knowledge, so he fears his Lord thereby, maintains ties of kinship thereby, and does what God has rightly done. This is the one with the best status. A man whom God has given knowledge but not wealth, so he is sincere in his intention and says, If I had wealth, I would do what so-and-so does. This is his intention, so their reward is equal. A man whom God has given wealth but not knowledge, so he squanders his wealth without knowledge, neither fearing his Lord thereby, nor maintaining ties of kinship thereby, nor does he know what God has rightly done. This is the one with the worst status. A man whom God has given neither wealth nor knowledge, so he says, If I had wealth, I would do what so-and-so does. This is the view of the judge, and it is the view of most of the early Muslims and scholars of jurists, hadith scholars, and theologians. No attention should be paid to the disagreement of those who claim that what a person is concerned with, even if he has decided on it, he is not held accountable for it. He has no proof for his saying, peace be upon him: (Whoever intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, it will not be recorded against him. But if he does it, one bad deed will be recorded against him.) Because the meaning of but does not do it is that he did not resolve to do it, as evidenced by what we have mentioned. The meaning of but if he does it is that he reveals it or resolves to do it, as evidenced by what we have described. And God is our guide.
3:136: God Almighty says: “Their reward is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And excellent is the reward of the workers.” God Almighty, by His grace and generosity, has arranged the forgiveness of sins for those who are sincere in their repentance and do not persist in their sin. This can be connected to the story of someone who fled and then repented and did not persist in his sin, for him is God’s forgiveness.
3:137: God Almighty says: There have already been precedents before you, so travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied. This is a consolation from God Almighty to the believers. Sunnah is the plural of Sunnah, which means the straight path. So-and-so is on the Sunnah, meaning he is on the straight path and does not incline toward any whims. Al-Hudhali said: Do not be upset about a tradition that you have followed, for the first to be satisfied with a tradition is the one who follows it. Sunnah: the imam who is followed. It is said: So-and-so set a good or bad sunnah if he did an action that was followed in it, whether good or bad. Labid said: From a group whose fathers followed the Sunnah for them, but you are a people whose leader is Sunnah. The Sunnah of the nation, and the Sunnahs of nations, on the authority of Al-Mufaddal. And he recited: People have not witnessed any virtue like their virtue, nor have they seen anything like them in the past traditions. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is people of Sunnah, so the noun was omitted. Abu Zaid said: The proverbs of Ata’: laws. Mujahid: The meaning is there have already been Sunnahs before you meaning the destruction of those who denied before you, such as Aad and Thamud. The consequence: the end of the matter, and this was on the Day of Uhud. He says: So I will give them respite and give them time and lead them on until the Book reaches its term, meaning by supporting the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers and destroying their enemies, the disbelievers.
3:138: God Almighty says: This is a statement for the people and a guidance and an admonition for the righteous. Meaning the Qur’an, according to Al-Hasan and others. It was said: This is a reference to His statement: There have already been precedents before you, and admonition is preaching. It has been mentioned previously.
3:139: God Almighty says: And do not weaken and do not grieve, and you will be superior if you are [true] believers. He consoled them and comforted them for what they had suffered on the day of Uhud of killing and wounds, and urged them to fight their enemy and forbade them from weakness and failure, saying: And do not weaken, meaning do not weaken and do not refrain, O companions of Muhammad, from fighting your enemies for what has befallen you. And do not grieve, over their backs, or over what has befallen you of defeat and calamity. And you will be the highest, meaning you will have the final victory and triumph, if you are believers, meaning in the truth of my promise. It was said that if means when. Ibn Abbas said: The companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were defeated on the day of Uhud, and while they were like that, Khalid bin Al-Walid approached with cavalry from the polytheists, wanting to climb the mountain over them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O God, do not let him defeat us. O God, we have no strength except through You. O God, no one worships You in this town except these people.” So God revealed these verses. A group of Muslim archers rose up and climbed the mountain. They threw the horses of the polytheists until they defeated them, so this is what God the Almighty said: And you will be the highest meaning the victors over the enemies after Uhud. So they did not send out an army after that except that they were victorious in every army that was in the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and in every army that was after the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and in which there was one of the Companions, they were victorious. All of these countries were conquered during the time of the Companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), then after their extinction, no country was conquered in the same way as they were conquered at that time. In this verse is a statement of the superiority of this nation, because He addressed them with what He addressed His prophets, because He said to Moses: Indeed, you are the highest (Ta-Ha 20:68) and He said to this nation: And you will be the highest. This word is derived from His Most High name, for He is the Most High, and He said to the believers: And you will be the highest.
3:140: God Almighty says: “If a wound should touch you, a wound similar to it has already touched the [other] people. And these days We alternate among the people so that God may make evident those who believe and take from among you martyrs. And God does not like the wrongdoers.” God the Almighty said: If a wound should touch you. Al-Qarh means a wound. The Dammah and Fatha are two dialects of it according to Al-Kisa’i and Al-Akhfash, like ‘Aqar and ‘Aqar. Al-Farra’ said: With the Fatha it is the wound, and with the Dammah it is its pain. The meaning is: If a wound should touch you on the Day of Uhud, a similar wound touched the people on the Day of Badr. Muhammad bin Al-Sumaiqa’ read Qarh with the Fatha of the Qaf and the Ra’ as a source. And those days We alternate among the people. It was said: This is in war, sometimes for the believers so that God the Almighty may support His religion. And sometimes for the disbelievers if the believers disobey so that He may test them and purify their sins. But if they do not disobey, then the party of God is the victorious. It was said: We alternate among the people from joy and sorrow, health and sickness, wealth and poverty, and the cycle. The poet said: One day for us and one day against us, one day for women and one day for eagles The Almighty’s saying: And that God may make evident those who believe means: This exchange was only to see the believer from the hypocrite and to distinguish some of them from others, as He said: And whatever befell you on the day the two armies met was by permission of God, that He might make evident the believers, and that He might make evident those who were hypocrites (Al Imran 3:166-167). It was said: To make evident the patience of the believers, the knowledge that will be rewarded, just as He knew it unseen before He charged them. This meaning was mentioned previously in Al Baqarah. The Almighty’s saying: And He takes from among you witnesses contains three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And He takes from among you martyrs, meaning He honors you with martyrdom, meaning that a people will be killed and they will be witnesses over the people for their deeds. It was said: This is why he was called a martyr. It was said: He was called a martyr because he was witnessed to in Paradise. It was said: He was called a martyr because their souls were brought to the Abode of Peace, because they are alive with their Lord, and the souls of others do not reach Paradise. So the martyr means the witness, meaning the one present for Paradise. This is the correct view, as will come. The virtue of martyrdom is great, and it is sufficient for you to know its virtue in the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives (al-Tawbah 9:111) and the verse. And His saying: “O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? * You believe in God and His Messenger and strive in the cause of God with your wealth and your lives” (al-Saff 61:10-12). And in Sahih Al-Busti on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The martyr does not feel the pain of death except as one of you feels the pain of an ulcer. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Rashid bin Sa’d on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that a man said: O Messenger of God, why are believers tested in their graves except for the martyr? He said: The flash of swords over his head is enough of a test. And in Bukhari: Those Muslims who were killed on the day of Uhud among them Hamza, Al-Yaman, Anas bin Al-Nadr, and Mus`ab bin Umair. Amr bin Ali told me that Muadh bin Hisham said: My father told me on the authority of Qatada who said: We do not know of any tribe among the Arab tribes that has more martyrs and is more honorable on the Day of Resurrection than the Ansar. Qatada said: Anas bin Malik told us that seventy of them were killed on the day of Uhud, seventy on the day of Bir Ma’unah, and seventy on the day of Yamamah. He said: Bir Ma’unah was during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the day of Yamamah was during the time of Abu Bakr, the day of Musaylimah the Liar. Anas said: Ali bin Abi Talib was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had more than sixty wounds from stab wounds, blows, and arrow wounds. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to wipe them and they healed, by God Almighty’s permission, as if they had never existed. Second: In the words of God Almighty: And He takes from among you martyrs is evidence that the will is not the command as the people of the Sunnah say, for God Almighty forbade the infidels from killing the believers: Hamza and his companions and wanted to kill them, and He forbade Adam from eating from the tree and wanted to do so, so Adam had intercourse with him, and the opposite is that He ordered Satan to prostrate and he did not want to do so, so he refused, and from him the indication occurred in His true words: But God disliked their being sent forth, so He held them back (al-Tawbah 9:46), even though He had ordered all of them to fight, but He created laziness and the causes that prevented them from moving, so they sat back. Third: It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr and said to him: Give your companions the choice regarding the prisoners. If they wish to be killed, they will be ransomed, on the condition that the same number of them will be killed the following year. They said: Ransom, and one of us will be killed. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, who said: A good hadith. So God fulfilled His promise with the martyrdom of His friends after He gave them the choice, and they chose to be killed. And God does not love the wrongdoers, meaning the polytheists, meaning that even if the disbelievers afflict the believers, He does not love them, and even if He inflicts pain on the believers, He loves the believers.
3:141: God Almighty says: And that God may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers. There are three sayings about it: yamhis means to test. The second is to purify, meaning from their sins, so it is with the deletion of an adjective. The meaning is: And that God may purify the sins of those who believe, as Al-Farra’ said. The third is to purify, this is the strangest. Al-Khalil said: It is said that the rope is purified, meaning its fiber is cut off, and from this comes the word O God, purify our sins from us, meaning save us from their punishment. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: I read to Muhammad bin Yazid from Al-Khalil: Purification means to save. It is said: Mahsahu yamhishu muhasan if he purifies him, so the meaning according to him is: To test the believers to reward them and save them from their sins. And destroy the disbelievers means to uproot them by destruction.
3:142: God Almighty says: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while God has not yet made evident those among you who strive and made evident the steadfast? Am means rather. It was said: The meem is redundant. The meaning is: Did you think, O you who were defeated on the day of Uhud, that you would enter Paradise as those who were killed and endured the pain of wounds and killing did without taking their path and being patient as they were? No, until God knows those among you who strive meaning knows the testimony so that the reward will be inflicted upon them. The meaning is: And you did not strive so that He would know that from you, so when means did not. Sibawayh differentiated between lam and lama, and claimed that lama fa’ala negates a verb, and that lama fa’ala negates a verb. And He knows the patient ones is in the accusative case with the implied an, according to Al-Khalil. Al-Hasan and Yahya bin Ya’mar read ya’lam al-saabireen in the jussive mood according to the sequence. It was read in the nominative case according to the cut-off, meaning and He knows. This reading was narrated by Abd al-Warith from Abu Amr. Al-Zajjaj said: The waw here means until, meaning and God does not know those among you who strive until He knows their patience as mentioned earlier.
3:143: The Almighty said: And you used to wish for death meaning martyrdom before you met it. Al-A'mash read before you meet it meaning before being killed. It was said: before you encounter the causes of death, because many of those who did not attend Badr used to wish for a day in which there would be fighting, so when the day of Uhud came, they were defeated, and some of them were so patient that they were killed, including Anas bin An-Nadr, the uncle of Anas bin Malik, for when the Muslims were defeated, he said: O God, I disavow before You what these people have brought, and he directly fought and said: Oh, it is the scent of Paradise! I find it, and he went on until he was martyred. Anas said: We did not recognize him except by his fingertips, and we found on him eighty-some wounds. And about him and similar verses, Men who have been true to what they pledged to God (al-Ahzab 33:23) was revealed. So the verse is a reproach to those who were defeated, especially since some of them forced the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to leave Madinah, and it will come. Wishing for death is attributed to Muslims wishing for martyrdom based on steadfastness and patience in jihad, not to be killed by the infidels, because that is a sin and disbelief and it is not permissible to desire sin. Based on this, Muslims ask God to grant them martyrdom, so they ask for patience in jihad even if it leads to killing. The Almighty said: And you are watching. Al-Akhfash said: It is a repetition with the meaning of emphasis, as He said: You have seen him is like nor a bird flying with its wings (al-An’am 6:38). It was said that its meaning is while you are seeing, there is no defect in your eyes, just as you say: I saw such and such, but there is no defect in your eyes, meaning you saw him with a true vision, and this goes back to the meaning of emphasis. Some of them said: and you are looking at Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. There is an implied meaning in the verse, meaning you saw him while you were looking, so why did you flee?
3:144: It has five issues: The first: It was narrated that it was revealed because of the defeat of the Muslims on the day of Uhud when Satan cried out: Muhammad has been killed. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: Some of the people said: Muhammad has been killed, so give them your hands, for they are your brothers. Some of them said: If Muhammad has been killed, will you not continue with what your Prophet has done until you join him? So God Almighty revealed regarding that: Muhammad is no more than a messenger; messengers have passed away before him until His saying: Then God gave them the reward of this world. And ma is a negative particle, and what follows it is a subject and a predicate, and the function of ma is invalidated. Ibn Abbas read: messengers have passed away before him without the definite article.
