So God Almighty informed in this verse that the messengers will not remain among their people forever, and that it is necessary to adhere to what the messengers brought even if the messenger is lost through death or murder. He honored His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and described him with two names derived from his name: Muhammad and Ahmad. The Arabs say: A praiseworthy man and Muhammad if his praiseworthy qualities are many. The poet said: To the noble, generous, and generous Muhammad This was mentioned in Al-Fatihah, and Abbas bin Murdas said: O Seal of the Prophets, you are sent with goodness. All guidance is your guidance. God built you with love in his creation and named you Muhammad This verse is a continuation of the reproach to the defeated, meaning that they were not to be defeated even if Muhammad was killed, and prophethood does not prevent death, and religions do not disappear with the death of prophets, and God knows best. The second: This verse is the clearest evidence of the courage and boldness of Abu Bakr, for the limit of courage and boldness is the steadfastness of the heart when calamities befall, and there is no calamity greater than the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as was explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. His courage and knowledge were evident to him. The people said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has not died, including Umar, and Uthman was silent, and Ali hid, and the matter was disturbed, so Abu Bakr revealed it with this verse when he came from his residence in As-Sunh. The hadith is thus in Al-Bukhari, and in Sunan Ibn Majah on the authority of Aisha, she said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away, and Abu Bakr was with his wife, the daughter of Kharijah, in Al-Awali, they began to say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, has not died, it is only some of what he used to take when the revelation came, so Abu Bakr came and uncovered his face and kissed him between the eyes and said: You are more honorable to God than for Him to kill you! Twice, by God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died while Umar was in a corner of the mosque saying: By God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has not died, and he will not die until he cuts off the hands and feet of many hypocrites. Abu Bakr stood up and ascended the pulpit and said: Whoever worshipped God, God is alive and has not died, and whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died. “And Muhammad is no more than a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. If he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm God at all, and God will reward the grateful.” Umar said: It is as if I had not read it until that day and he retracted the statement he had made, as mentioned by Al-Wa’ili Abu Nasr Ubaidullah in his book Al-Ibanah: On the authority of Anas bin Malik that he heard Umar bin Al-Khattab when Abu Bakr was pledged allegiance to in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he stood on the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, testifying before Abu Bakr, and he said: As for what follows, I said to you yesterday a statement, and it was not as I said, and by God, I did not find the statement I said to you in a book that God revealed or in a covenant that the Messenger entrusted to me. God’s Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: But I hoped that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would live until he managed us. He wanted to say: Until he is the last of us to die. So God, the Almighty, chose for His Messenger what is with Him over what is with you. This is the Book by which God guided His Messenger, so take it and you will be guided to what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was guided to. Al-Wa’ili Abu Nasr said: The statement that he said and then retracted was: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die and will not die until he cuts off the hands and feet of men.” He said that because of the greatness of what had been brought to him, and he feared the tribulation and the emergence of the hypocrites. So when he saw the strength of the certainty of the greatest friend, Abu Bakr, and his utterance of the statement of God, the Almighty: Every soul will taste death (Al Imran 3:185), and His statement: Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die (al-Zumar 39:30), and what he said that day, he became aware and became certain and said: It is as if I had not heard the verse except from Abu Bakr. The people went out reciting it in the streets of Medina, as if it had never been revealed except that day. And he died, may God bless him and grant him peace, on Monday without disagreement, at the time of his entry into Medina during his migration when the sun was at its highest. He was buried on Tuesday, and it was said on Wednesday night. Safiyya bint Abdul Muttalib said, mourning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Oh Messenger of God, you were our hope, you were kind to us and you were not harsh. You were merciful, a guide and a teacher, so let those who were crying weep for you today. By God, I do not cry for the Prophet because of his loss, but because I fear the coming chaos. As if my heart was reminded of Muhammad, and I did not fear the hardships after the Prophet. O Fatima, may God bless the Lord of Muhammad, my grandmother who spent the night in Yathrib May my mother, my aunt, my uncle, my fathers, myself and my wealth be sacrificed for the Messenger of God I believed and conveyed the message honestly and died with a clear and pure oud If the Lord of mankind had kept our Prophet, we would have been happy, but his matter was already decided. May God's peace and blessings be upon you, and may you be admitted to the Gardens of Eden, satisfied. I see that Hassan orphaned him and left him crying and calling his grandfather today, mourning him. If it is said that it is: Third: Why did the burial of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, be delayed when he said to the people of a household who delayed the burial of their dead: Hurry up to bury your corpses and do not delay them? The answer is from three aspects: First: What we mentioned about their lack of agreement on his death. Second: Because they do not know where to bury him. Some people said in Al-Baqi’, and others said in the mosque. Some people said: He should be detained until he is carried to his father Ibrahim, until the greatest scholar said: I heard him say: No prophet is buried except where he dies. This was mentioned by Ibn Majah, Al-Muwatta’ and others. Third: They were occupied with the disagreement that occurred between the Muhajireen and the Ansar regarding the pledge of allegiance, so they looked into it until the matter was settled and the unity was organized and the situation was secure, and the caliphate was established in its place, so they pledged allegiance to Abu Bakr, then they pledged allegiance to him the next day with a group of them and with their approval, so God removed the distress from the people of apostasy through him, and the religion was established through him, and praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. Then they returned after that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they looked into his burial and washed him and shrouded him, and God knows best.. Fourth: There is a difference of opinion as to whether he was prayed over or not. Some of them said: No one prayed over him, but rather each one stood and supplicated, because he was too noble to be prayed over. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a weak statement, because the Sunnah is to pray over him in the funeral, just as it is to pray over him in supplication, so he says: O God, pray over Muhammad until the Day of Resurrection, and that is a benefit for us. It was said: He was not prayed over, because there was no imam there, and this is weak, because the one who performed the obligatory prayer with them was the one who led them in prayer. It was said: The people prayed over him individually, because he was the last one to see him, so they wanted each one to take his blessing specifically without being a follower of anyone else in it, and God knows best about the correctness of that. I said: Ibn Majah narrated with a chain of transmission, rather a sahih one, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, in which it says: When they finished preparing him on Tuesday, he was placed on his bed in his house, then the people entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in groups to pray over him. When they finished, they brought the women in, and when they finished, they brought the children in. No one led the people in prayer for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated on the authority of Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdhami, who told us that Wahb ibn Jarir told us, who told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Husayn ibn Abdullah told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the hadith in full. Fifth: In the change of the situation after the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Anas, who said: When the day came that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered Medina, everything was illuminated, but the day he died, everything was darkened, and we did not shake our hands from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until our hearts were in denial. Narrated by Ibn Majah, and he said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: We used to avoid speaking and being cheerful with our women during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for fear that the Qur’an would be revealed about us. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, we spoke. And it was narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah bint Abi Umayyah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she said: When the people, during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to pray, their sight would no longer be the place of their feet. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, and Abu Bakr was there, then when the people stood up to pray, their sight would no longer be the place of their forehead. Then Abu Bakr died, and Umar was there, then when the people stood up to pray, their sight would no longer be the place of the qiblah, and Uthman bin Affan, and there was a sedition, so people turned right and left during prayer. God the Almighty said: Then if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? Then if he dies is a condition, or is killed is conjoined with it, and the answer is will you turn back. The interrogative particle entered into the particle of the condition because the condition was formed by it and became one sentence and one piece of report. The meaning is: Will you turn back on your heels if he dies or is killed? Likewise, every interrogative particle entered into a particle of the condition, because it is not in its proper place, and its place is to be before the answer to the condition. His statement will you turn back on your heels is a metaphor, meaning you have turned back as disbelievers after your belief, as stated by Qatada and others. It is said about someone who returns to what he was upon: he turned back on his heels, and from this is he turned back on his heels (al-Anfal 8:48). It was said: what is meant by turning back here is defeat, so it is a reality, not a metaphor. It was also said: the meaning is you did the action of the apostates even if it was not an apostasy. God Almighty says: And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm God at all. Rather, he will harm himself and expose himself to punishment because of the disobedience. God Almighty is neither benefited by obedience nor harmed by disobedience because of His wealth. And God will reward the grateful, meaning those who were patient, struggled, and were martyred. And God will reward the grateful came after His statement: will never harm God at all, so it is a connection between a promise and a threat.
3:145: The Almighty’s saying: And no soul can die except by God’s permission at a predetermined time. This is an exhortation to jihad, and an announcement that death is inevitable and that every person, whether killed or not, dies when he reaches his appointed time, because the meaning of postponed is until a term, and the meaning of by God’s permission is by God’s decree and destiny, and a book is in the accusative case as a source, meaning God has written a predetermined book, and the term of death is the time in which it is known to Him, the Exalted, that the soul of a living person leaves his body, and when a servant is killed, we know that this is his term, and it is not correct to say that if he had not been killed, he would have lived. The evidence for His saying: a predetermined book is: So when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it. (al-A’raf 7:34), Indeed, the term of God is coming. (al-Ankabut 29:5), For every term is a book. (al-Ra’d 13:38), and the Mu’tazilite says: The term advances and delays, and whoever is killed is only destroyed. Before its appointed time, and likewise every animal that was slaughtered was killed before its appointed time, because the killer must guarantee the blood money. God Almighty has made it clear in this verse that no soul shall perish before its appointed time, and more clarification of this will come in Al-A’raf, God willing. And in it is evidence of the books of knowledge and its recording, and its clarification will come in Taha, when He says, He said, ‘The knowledge thereof is with my Lord, in a Record’ (Ta-Ha 20:52), God willing. God the Almighty said: And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him thereof meaning the spoils. It was revealed about those who left the position in search of the spoils. It was said: It is general for everyone who desires this world without the Hereafter, and the meaning is We will give him thereof what was allotted to him. In the revelation: Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whomever We intend (al-Isra’ 17:18). And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him thereof meaning We will give him the reward for his work, as God the Almighty described of doubling the good deeds for whomever He wills. It was said: What is meant by it is Abdullah bin Jubair and those who remained in the position with him until they were killed. And We will reward the grateful meaning We will give them the eternal reward as a reward for them for not retreating, so it is a confirmation of what came before about giving more of the Hereafter. It was said: And We will reward the grateful of the provision in this world so that it is not imagined that the grateful person is deprived of what was allotted to him from what the disbeliever attains.
3:146: God Almighty said: And how many a prophet fought with whom were many pious men. Al-Zuhri said: The devil shouted on the day of UHud 11:Muhammad has been killed, and a group of Muslims were defeated. Ka’b bin Malik said: I was the first to recognize the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I saw his eyes shining from under his helmet, so I called out at the top of my voice: This is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He motioned for me to be silent, so God Almighty revealed: “And how many a prophet fought with whom were many pious men. They did not lose heart for what afflicted them in the cause of God, nor did they weaken” Al-Akhbar. Ka’in means how many. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: It is that the letter kaf of comparison entered it and was built with it, so the meaning of how many came into the speech, and it was represented in the Qur’an as a nun, because it is a word that was transferred from its original form, so its wording changed its meaning. Then its use became widespread, so the Arabs played with it and manipulated it by changing it and deleting it, so languages were read in it. Ibn Kathir read wa-ka’in like wa-ka’in, on the weight of fa’il, and its original form was changed to an alif, just as it was changed in ya’as, so it was said ya’as. The poet said: And there is a friend in the valleys who sees me if I am afflicted, he is the one afflicted Another said: And we have turned away from you a well-armed man who comes before the caravan, wearing a mask. Another said: There are people among the community whose brother is above them and they are honorable. Ibn Muhaisin read wa-ka-in with a hamza and a shortened letter like wa-ka-an, which is from ka-in and its alif was deleted. He also said wa-ka-ayn like wa-ka-ayn, which is the reversed form of ka-ay with a lightened letter. The rest read wa-ka-ayn with a shaddah like ka-ayn, which is the original. The poet said: How many people have their brother above them and they are honorable? Another said: How can we protect ourselves from an enemy with our glory and how can we protect ourselves from the weak and the fearful? So he combined two languages: Ka'in and Ka'in, and a fifth language Ka'in like Ka'in, and it is as if it is a shortened version of Ka'in reversed Ka'in. Al-Jawhari did not mention other than two languages: Ka'in like Ka'in, and Ka'in like Ka'in. You say Ka'in rajul laqat with the accusative of what comes after Ka'in as a distinction, and you also say: Ka'in min rajul laqat, and inserting min after Ka'in is more than the accusative and better. And Bikayn tabi'i hath al-thawb? That is, how much do you sell it for? Dhu al-Rummah said: And our fear of the enemy's wrath and spear is not his country Al-Nahhas said: Abu Amr stopped and like without a nun, because it is a tanween, and this was narrated by Surah Ibn al-Mubarak from al-Kisa’i, and the rest stopped with a nun in accordance with the line of the Mushaf, and the meaning of the verse is to encourage the believers, and to command them to follow the example of those who came before from the best followers of the prophets, meaning many of the prophets were killed with him, many devout men, or many of the prophets were killed and their nations did not apostatize, two sayings: The first is from al-Hasan and Sa’id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan said: No prophet was ever killed in war, and Ibn Jubayr said: We have not heard that a prophet was killed in combat, and the second is from Qatada and Ikrimah, and stopping on this saying, on killed is permissible, and it is the reading of Nafi’, Ibn Jubayr, Abu Amr and Ya’qub, and it is the reading of Ibn Abbas and Abu Hatim chose it, and there are two views on it: One of them is that killed is applied to the prophet alone, and then the completion of the speech is at his saying killed and there is an implication in the speech, meaning and with him are many devout men, as it is said the prince was killed with a great army, meaning and with him is an army, And he went out with me on business, that is, with me, the second aspect is that the killing befell the Prophet and those with him from the riba’is, and the aspect of the speech is the killing of some of those who were with him, the Arabs say: We killed Banu Tamim and Banu Salim, but they killed some of them, and his saying and they did not weaken refers back to those who remained from them, I said: This statement is more similar to the revelation of the verse and more appropriate, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not killed, and a group of his companions were killed with him, and the Kufians and Ibn Amir read Qatil and it is the reading of Ibn Masoud, and Abu Ubaid chose it and said: If God praises the one who fights, then the one who was killed is included in it, and if He praises the one who was killed, no one else is included in it, so Qataal is more general and more praised, and the riba’is with a kasra on the ra’ is the reading of the majority, and the reading of Ali, may God be pleased with him, with a damma on it, and Ibn Abbas with a fatha, three languages, and the riba’is the large groups, from Mujahid, Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, and Ikrimah, and one of them is rabbi with a damma on the ra’ and a kasra, attributed to the rabbah also with a kasra on the ra’ and a damma, and it is the group, and Abdullah Ibn Masoud said, the riba’is thousands Many, and Ibn Zayd said: The followers, and the first is better known in the language, and from it the rag in which the arrows are collected is called: Rabbah and Rabbah, and the Rabab are tribes that gathered, and Abaan bin Tha’lab said: The Rabbi is ten thousand, and Al-Hasan said: They are the patient scholars, Ibn Abbas and Mujahid and Qatada and Al-Rabi’ and Al-Suddi: the large group, Hassan said: And if a group turns away from the truth, We will impose upon them a burden. Al-Zajjaj said: There are two readings here: Rabiyun with a damma on the ra’, and Rabiyun with a kasra on the ra’. As for the rabiyun with a damma: large groups, and it is said: ten thousand. I said: It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas Rabiyun with a fatha on the ra’, attributed to the Lord. Al-Khalil said: The Lord is one of the servants who were patient with the prophets, and they are the Rabbaniyun, attributed to deity, worship, and knowledge of the Lordship of God Almighty, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: And they did not grow weak for what afflicted them in the cause of God. And they grew weak means they were weakened. It has been mentioned before that weakness is the breaking of seriousness due to fear. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Samal read And they grew weak with a kasra on the ha’ and a damma on it, two dialects from Abu Zaid. And the weakness of a thing is weakness, and I weakened it and weakened it, and the weak is: the lowest and shortest of the ribs, and weakness of camels: the dense, and weakness is: an hour that passes of the night and so is the weakening, and we became weak in that hour, meaning they did not grow weak for the killing of their prophet, or for the killing of those who were killed from them, meaning the rest of them did not grow weak, so the added word was deleted, And they did not grow weak meaning from their enemy, and they did not submit meaning for what afflicted them in jihad, and submission is humiliation and submission, and its origin is istakana on ifta’ala, so the fatha of the kaf was made full and an alif was generated from it, and whoever made it from the universe, it is istaf’ala, and the first is more similar in meaning to the verse, and it was read So what And they weakened, but they were not weakened (with a sukoon on the ha’ and the ‘ayn. Al-Kisa’i narrated they weakened with a fatha on the ‘ayn. Then the Almighty informed about them after some of them were killed or their prophet was killed that they were patient and did not flee and prepared themselves for death, and sought forgiveness so that their death would be in repentance from sins if they were granted martyrdom, and they called for steadfastness so that they would not be defeated, and for victory over their enemies, and they singled out the feet for steadfastness over other limbs because they are relied upon. He says: Why did you not do and say the same, O companions of Muhammad? So He answered their call and gave them victory, triumph, and booty in this world and forgiveness in the Hereafter if they reach it. And thus does God with His sincere, repentant, truthful servants who support His religion, who are steadfast when meeting His enemy with His true promise and His truthful word, And God loves the patient, meaning those who are patient in jihad.
3:147: God Almighty says: And their only statement was that they said, ‘Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our transgression in our conduct and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people.’ Some of them read wa ma kan qawlhum in the nominative case, making it the subject of kan, so its meaning is, wa ma kan qawlhum is nothing but their saying: Our Lord, forgive us our sins. And whoever reads in the accusative case, makes the saying the predicate of kan and its subject is illa anna qawl, “Our Lord, forgive us our sins,” meaning the minor sins, and our extravagance, meaning the major sins. Extravagance means going to extremes in something and exceeding the limit. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to supplicate with this supplication: O God, forgive me my sin, my ignorance, and my extravagance in my affairs and what You know better than me,” and he mentioned the hadith. So a person should use what is in the Book of God and the authentic Sunnah of supplication and leave what is other than it, and not say I chose this, for God Almighty has chosen for His Prophet and His saints and taught them how to supplicate.
3:148: The Almighty said: So God gave them meaning He gave them the reward of this world meaning victory and triumph over their enemy and the good reward of the Hereafter meaning Paradise. Al-Jahdary read So God rewarded them from the reward, and God loves the doers of good mentioned above.
3:149: God Almighty says: O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers. When God Almighty commanded us to follow the example of those who came before us from the supporters of the prophets, He warned against obeying the disbelievers, meaning the polytheists of the Arabs: Abu Sufyan and his companions, and it was said: the Jews and Christians. And Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: He means the hypocrites in their saying to the believers when they are defeated: Return to the religion of your fathers. They turn you back on your heels, meaning to disbelief, and you will return as losers, meaning you will hope to be deceived.
3:150: God Almighty says: Rather, God is your protector, and He is the best of helpers. Then he said: Rather, God is your Master, meaning He is the One who will support and protect you if you obey Him. Rather, God was read in the accusative case, on the basis of rather, obey God, your Master.
3:151: God Almighty says: “We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve because they have associated with God that for which He had not sent down any authority. And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers.” Its counterpart: And He cast terror into their hearts. Ibn Amir and Al-Kisa’i read terror with a damma on the ‘ayn, and they are two dialects. Terror is fear. It is said: I terrified him with terror and terror, so he is terrified. It is possible that terror is a source, and terror is a noun, and its origin is from filling. It is said: A terrifying flood fills the valley, and I terrified the pool, I filled it. The meaning is: We will fill the hearts of the polytheists with fear and terror. Al-Sakhtiyani read will cast with a ya’, and the rest with a nun of majesty. Al-Suddi and others said: When Abu Sufyan and the polytheists set out on the day of Uhud, heading to Mecca, they set out until they were part of the way, regretting and saying: What a bad thing we have done! We killed them until there remained of them only the fugitives. We left them. Go back and eradicate them. When they decided to do that, God cast terror into their hearts until they turned back from what they intended to do. Throwing is used literally for bodies. God Almighty said: And he threw down the tablets (al-A’raf 7:150), So they threw down their ropes and their staffs (Ash-Shu’ara’: 44), So Moses threw down his staff (Ash-Shu’ara’: 45). The poet said: She threw down her stick and settled down Then it may be used metaphorically as in this verse and His saying: And I have bestowed upon you love from Me (Ta-Ha 20:39), and He has cast upon you a question. The Almighty’s saying: Because they associated others with God is an explanation, meaning that the reason for casting terror into their hearts was their associating others with God. So because is the source, and it is said: He associated others with Him meaning he made someone else equal to Him in order to make him a partner. The Almighty’s saying: For which He has not sent down any authority is an argument and clarification, an excuse and proof. From this the governor is called a sultan, because he is the argument of God Almighty on earth. It is said that it is taken from the word salit, which is what the lamp is lit with, and it is sesame oil. Imru’ al-Qais said: Amal Al-Sulait with twisted wick The authority is used to illuminate the manifestation of truth and suppress falsehood. It was said that the iron sword is sharpness, and the sword is from the word taslith which means subjugation, and the authority is from that, so the letter nun is redundant, so the origin of the authority is strength, for it is subjugated by it as it is subjugated by the authority, and the sword is the woman who is loud, and the sword is the man who is eloquent in tongue, and the meaning of this is that the worship of idols has not been proven in any of the religions, and no mind has indicated that it is permissible, then the Almighty informed about their fate and their return, saying: And their refuge is the Fire, then He declared His covenant, saying: And evil is the residence of the wrongdoers. The abode is the place where one resides, it is said: thawa yathawi thawaan, and the shelter is every place to which something returns, night or day.
3:152: God Almighty says: “And God has fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them with His permission until, when you lost heart and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love - among you were those who desired this world and among you were those who desired the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them that He might test you. But He has pardoned you, and God is full of bounty to the believers.” Muhammad bin Kaab Al-Qurazi said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to Medina after Uhud and they were wounded, some of them said to one another: How did this happen to us when God promised us victory! This verse was revealed because they killed the standard-bearer of the polytheists and seven men after him on the standard. The Muslims were initially victorious, but they were busy with the spoils. Some of the archers also left their posts in search of the spoils, and that was the reason for the defeat. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib who said: “When the day of Uhud came and we encountered the polytheists, the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) seated some of the archers and put Abdullah bin Jubair in charge of them and said to them: ‘Do not move from your place. If you see us prevailing over them, do not move, and if you see them prevailing over us, do not help us against them.’ He said: When the people met and the Muslims defeated them, we saw the women running hard on the mountain, and they had lifted their legs and their anklets were visible. They began to say: ‘The spoils, the spoils.’ Abdullah said to them: ‘Wait! Did the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) not command you not to move?’ So they set out. When they reached them, God turned their faces away and killed seventy men from the Muslims. Then Abu Sufyan bin A war came to us while he was in a high place and said: Is Muhammad among the people? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not answer him, until he said it three times. Then he said: Is Ibn Abi Quhafah among the people? Three times. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not answer him. Then he turned to his companions and said: As for these, they have been killed. Umar, may God be pleased with him, could not control himself without saying: You lie, O enemy of God! God has left for you someone who will disgrace you with him. He said: Subdue Hubal, twice. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Answer him. They said: What should we say, O Messenger of God? He said: Say: God is Most High and Most Majestic. Abu Sufyan said: We have Al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Answer him. They said: What should we say, O Messenger of God? He said: Say: God is our Master, and you have no Master. Abu Sufyan said: A day for the day of Badr, and war is a contest. You will find mutilation among the people that I did not command and it did not grieve me. In Bukhari and Muslim, on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas: He said: I saw on the right and left of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud two men wearing white clothes fighting for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the most intense fighting. In a narration on the authority of Sa`d: They were wearing white clothes, I have never seen them before or after, meaning Gabriel and Michael. In another narration: They were fighting for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the most intense fighting I have ever seen them before or after that day. And on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The angels did not fight with them on that day, nor before or after it, except on the day of Badr. Al-Bayhaqi said: Mujahid only meant that they were fighting on the day of Uhud for the people when they disobeyed the Messenger and did not have patience with what he commanded them to do. And on the authority of `Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, he said: And God, the Almighty, had promised them, for their patience and piety, that He would support them with five thousand marked angels. And He did so. But when they disobeyed the command of the Messenger and abandoned their ranks and the archers abandoned the covenant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that they should not leave their homes, and they desired the world, the support was lifted from them. The angels, and God Almighty revealed: “And God had fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them with His permission.” So God fulfilled His promise and showed them the victory, but when they disobeyed, He followed them with calamity. On the authority of Umair bin Ishaq, he said: When the day of Uhud came, they turned away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Sa`d was shooting in front of him, and a young man was shooting arrows for him. Whenever an arrow went missing, he would bring it to him. He said: Shoot, Abu Ishaq. When they finished, they looked for the young man. They did not see him and did not recognize him. Muhammad bin Ka`b said: When the standard-bearer of the polytheists was killed and their standard fell, Umrah bint Alqamah Al-Harithiya raised it. Hassan says about that: If it weren't for the Harithiya Brigade, they would be sold in the markets like jalabiyas. You kill them means you kill them and eradicate them. The poet said: We killed them with the sword, and the rest of them were scattered and dispersed. Jarir said: Swords feel them as the fire rises in the harvested thickets Abu Ubaid said: “Al-Has is the eradication by killing. It is said: ‘A locust is felt’ if it is killed by the cold. The cold is a ‘hass’ for plants, meaning it burns them and destroys them. A year of ‘hass’ means a drought that eats everything. Ru’bah said: If we complain of a year of senses that eats away at the dry green Its origin is from the sense, which is perception by the senses. So the meaning of his sense is that he took away his sense of killing. “With His permission” is with His knowledge, or with His judgment and command. Until when you failed means you became weak and shunned. It is said: Fasakal yafshu’, so he is fasakal and fasakal. The answer to until is omitted, meaning until when you failed, you were tested. And something like this is permissible, like His statement: If you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a ladder into the heaven (al-An’am 6:35). Al-Farra’ said: The answer to until is and you disputed and the waw is an intrusive and redundant letter, like His statement: So when they both submitted and he laid him down upon his forehead, * And We called to him meaning We called to him. And Imru’ al-Qais said: When we passed the neighborhood square and he went away That is, he turned away. According to these people, it is permissible to insert the waw from and you disobeyed, meaning until if you failed and disputed, you disobeyed. Based on this, there is an advancement and delay, meaning until if you disputed and disobeyed, you failed. Abu Ali said: It is permissible for the answer to be He turned you away from them and then is redundant, and the meaning is until if you failed and disputed and disobeyed, He turned you away from them. Some grammarians have recited in its redundancy the words of the poet: I see that I did not sleep on passion, then when I woke up I became normal Al-Akhfash allowed it to be redundant, as in the Almighty’s saying: “Until, when the earth, vast as it is, became strait for them, and their souls became strait for them, and they perceived that there is no refuge from God except in Him. Then He turned to them in forgiveness” (al-Tawbah 9:118). It was said: Until means to, and then there is no answer to it, meaning that God fulfilled His promise to you until you failed, meaning that promise was on the condition of steadfastness. The meaning of you disputed is that you differed, meaning the archers when some of them said to each other: We will catch up with the spoils, and some of them said: Rather, we will remain in our place where the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered us to remain. And you disobeyed meaning you disobeyed the Messenger’s command to remain, after He showed you what you love, meaning the victory that the Muslims had on the day of Uhud at the beginning of their affair, and that was when the standard-bearer of the polytheists was struck down, as mentioned above. That is, when he was struck down, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions spread out and became scattered battalions, and they struck the enemy with blows until they were forced to abandon their burdens, and the horses carried The polytheists attacked the Muslims three times, each time advising them with arrows and returning defeated. The Muslims charged and killed them to the ground. When the fifty archers saw that God Almighty had granted victory to their brothers, they said: By God, we will not sit here for anything. God has destroyed the enemy and our brothers are in the camp of the polytheists. Groups of them said: Why should we stand when God has defeated the enemy? They left their homes that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had enjoined upon them not to leave, and they disputed and failed and disobeyed the Messenger, so the horses rushed upon them to kill them. The words of the verse require rebuke to them, and the reason for the rebuke to them is that they saw the beginnings of victory, so it was necessary for them to know that the completion of victory is in steadfastness, not in defeat. Then, I am the reason for the dispute. He said: Among you is he who desires this world, meaning the spoils. Ibn Masoud said: We did not feel that any of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted this world and its glory until the day of Uhud. And among you is he who desires the Hereafter, and they are the ones who remained in their position and did not disobey the command of their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with their leader, Abdullah bin Jubair. Khalid bin Al-Walid and Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl attacked him, and they were disbelievers at that time, so they killed him along with those who remained. May God have mercy on them. The rebuke is with those who fled, not with those who remained, for those who remained will win the reward. This is like when a general punishment befalls a people, then the righteous and the children perish, but what befell them is not a punishment, rather it is a cause. The reward, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: Then He turned you away from them to test you. That is, after you had taken control of them, He turned you away from them by defeating them. This indicates that disobedience is created by God the Almighty. The Mu’tazila said: The meaning is then you turned away. So, attributing it to God the Almighty by removing fear from the hearts of the disbelieving Muslims is a test for them. Al-Qushayri said: This does not benefit them, because removing fear from the hearts of the disbelievers until they make light of the Muslims is ugly and it is not permissible for them to do something ugly from God. So there is no meaning left for His statement: Then He turned you away from them. It was said: The meaning of He turned you away from them is that He did not charge you with seeking them out. The Almighty says: And He has pardoned you, and God is full of bounty to the believers. That is, He did not eradicate you after the disobedience and transgression. It was said that the address is to everyone, and it was said that it is to the archers who disobeyed what they were commanded to do, and Al-Nahhas chose this. Most of the commentators said: Similar to this verse is the Almighty’s saying: Then We pardoned you, “And God is full of bounty to the believers” with pardon and forgiveness. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was never victorious in any situation as he was on the day of Uhud. He said: And we denied that, so Ibn Abbas said: Between me and those who denied that is the Book of God Almighty, that God Almighty says on the day of UHud 11:And God had fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing them by His permission. Ibn Abbas says: The killing is the killing, “Until when you were weak and disputed about the matter and disobeyed after He had shown you what you love, among you were those who desired this world and among you were those who desired the Hereafter. Then He turned you away from them that He might test you. And He has pardoned you, and God is full of bounty to the believers.” What he meant by this were the archers, and that was because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stationed them in a place and then said: Protect our backs, for if you see us being killed, do not help us, and if you see us having captured spoils, do not share them with us. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, captured spoils and they allowed the camp of the polytheists to enter, the archers all retreated and entered the camp to plunder, and the rows of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, met, so they were like this and he interlocked his fingers and they were confused, so when he left The archers, that situation in which they were, entered the horses from that place upon the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they struck each other and became confused, and many of the Muslims were killed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were at the beginning of the day until seven or nine of the standard-bearers of the polytheists were killed, and the Muslims moved towards the mountain, and did not reach where the people say: the cave, but they were under the mortar, and the two devils shouted: Muhammad has been killed, and there was no doubt that it was true, and we remained like that, not doubting that he was killed until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared to us between the two Sa’dains, and we recognized him by his swaying when he walked, he said: So we were so happy that it was as if what had happened to us had not happened, he said: So he advanced towards us and he said: The wrath of God has become intense upon a people who bloodied the face of their Prophet, and Ka’b bin Malik said: I was the first of the Muslims to recognize the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I recognized him by his eyes shining from under the helmet, so I called out at the top of my voice: O group of Muslims! Be glad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has come, and he motioned to me to be silent.
3:153: God Almighty says: “When you were ascending and did not look back at anyone, and the Messenger was calling you from behind you, then He rewarded you with grief for grief, so that you would not grieve over what had escaped you or what had befallen you. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” Idh is related to His saying, And He has pardoned you. The general reading is tas’adun with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the ‘ayn. Abu Raja’ al-Attardi, Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Hasan, and Qatadah read with a fatha on the ta’ and the ‘ayn, meaning you ascend the mountain. Ibn Muhaisin and Shibl read idh yas’adun wa la yalwan with a ya’ in both of them. Al-Hasan read talawun with one waw. Abu Bakr ibn ‘Ayyash narrated from ‘Issam wa la tulwan with a damma on the ta’, and it is an irregular language mentioned by al-Nahhas. Abu Hatim said: As’adat means you proceed in front of your face, and ascended means you climb a mountain or other than it. Ascending means walking on a level ground, valleys, and ravines, and ascending means rising on mountains, roofs, ladders, and stairs. It is possible that their ascension on the mountain was after their ascension in the valley, so the meaning is correct according to the reading tas’adun and tas’adun. Qatadah and al-Rabi’ said: They ascended on the day of Uhud in the valley. And the reading of Abu when you ascend in the valley Ibn Abbas said: They ascended in Uhud fleeing, so both readings are correct: On that day there were among the defeated ascending and rising, and God knows best. Al-Qutbi and Al-Mubarrad said: Ascending means going far and deep in it, so ascending is as if going far into the ground like going far in height. The poet said: Oh you who ask, where have you ascended? For there is an appointment for you in the valley of Yathrib. Al-Farra’ said: Ascending is the beginning of a journey, and descending is the return from it. It is said: We ascended from Baghdad to Mecca and to Khorasan and the like, if we went out to them and began the journey, and we descended if we returned. Abu Ubaidah recited: You were crying over the ascent, but today you went out and the driver shouted Al-Mufaddal said: Ascended, ascended, and ascended have the same meaning. The meaning of twilwun is that you limp and stay, meaning that some of you do not turn to others in order to flee, for the one who ascends to something turns his neck or the reins of his mount to it. On one means Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Kalbi said: And the Messenger calls you in your rear, meaning in your rear. It is said: So-and-so came in the rear of the people, the rear of the people, the rear of the people, and the rear of the people. In Al-Bukhari your rear is the feminine of your rear. Amr bin Khalid told us, Zuhair told us, Abu Ishaq told us, he heard Al-Bara’ bin Azib say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed Abdullah bin Jubair as commander of the infantry on the day of Uhud, and they returned defeated. That was when the Messenger called them in their rear, and there remained with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only twelve men. Ibn Abbas and others said: “The supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was: O servants of God, go back,” and his supplication was to change the evil, and it is impossible for him, peace be upon him, to see the evil while he was Defeat and then not forbid it. I said: This is on the condition that defeat is a sin, and it is not so, as will be explained, God willing. God the Almighty said: So He rewarded you with grief for grief. In the language, grief means covering. I covered something, and a day of grief and a night of grief if they were dark. From this comes the grief of the crescent moon if it is not seen, and the matter grieves me. Mujahid, Qatada and others said: The first grief is the killing and wounds, and the second grief is the rumor of the killing of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when Satan shouted about it. It was said: The first grief is what they missed of victory and booty, and the second is what happened to them of killing and defeat. It was said: The first grief is the defeat, and the second is Abu Sufyan and Khalid looking down on them in the mountain. When the Muslims looked at them, that grieved them, and they thought that they would attack them and kill them, but this made them forget what had happened to them. At that time, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, do not announce it upon us, as mentioned above. The ba in bagham in this way means upon, and it was said: It is in its proper form, and the meaning is that they grieved the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by disobeying him, so He rewarded them with their grief for those who were afflicted among them. Al-Hasan said: So He rewarded you with grief on the day of Uhud with grief on the day of Badr for the polytheists. He called grief a reward just as He called the punishment for sin a sin. It was said: God made them stand on their sin, so they were distracted by that from what had befallen them. His saying: “So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you or what has befallen you. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” The lam is related to His saying: And He has pardoned you. It was said: It is related to His saying: Then He rewarded you with grief for grief. That is, this grief was so that you would not grieve over what had escaped you of the spoils, or what had befallen you of defeat. The first is better. The ma in His saying What befell you is in the accusative case. It was said: La is a conjunction, that is, so that you may grieve over what has escaped you and what has befallen you as a punishment for your disobedience to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is like His saying: What prevented you from not prostrating when I commanded you? (al-A’raf 7:12), that is, from prostrating. His saying: So that the People of the Scripture would not know? (al-Hadid 57:29), that is, so that he would know. This is the saying of al-Mufaddal. It was said: He meant by His saying: Then He rewarded you with grief for grief that is, griefs followed one after the other, so that you would not be preoccupied after this with the spoils. And God is Acquainted with what you do. In it is the meaning of warning and threat.
3:154: The Almighty said: Then He sent down upon you, after the distress, security, drowsiness. Security and safety are the same. It was said: Security is only with causes of fear, and safety is with its absence. It is accusative with anzal and na'asan as a substitute for it. It was said: It is accusative as the object for it, as if he said: He sent down upon you for security drowsiness. Ibn Muhaisin read amna with a sukoon on the meem. God the Almighty favored the believers after these distresses on the day of Uhud with drowsiness until most of them slept. Only he who feels secure slumbers, and the fearful one does not sleep. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Anas that Abu Talha said: Drowsiness overcame us while we were in our ranks on the day of Uhud. He said: My sword kept falling from my hand and I would grab it, and it would fall and I would grab it. Yaghsha was read with a ya' and a ta'. The ya' is for drowsiness, and the ta' is for safety. The group is used for one person and a group. And a group whose souls are concerned means al-Munafiqun 63:Mu'tab bin Qushair and his companions. They had gone out in the hope of the spoils and fear of the believers, but drowsiness did not overcome them and they began to regret their presence and to say sayings. The meaning of their souls had worried them is that they were driven to worry, and worry is what you are concerned with. It is said: The thing worried me meaning it was from my concern, and an important matter is severe. And the matter worried me and made me anxious, and worry melted me. The waw in his saying and a group is the waw of the state meaning when, meaning when a group thought that the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was false and that he would not be victorious. The thought of the Age of Ignorance means the thought of the Age of Ignorance, so it was deleted. "They say: Do we have any part in the matter?" Its wording is a question and its meaning is denial, meaning we have no part in the matter, meaning the matter of going out. We only went out reluctantly, as indicated by the saying of God Almighty, informing us about them: If we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed here. Al-Zubayr said: Sleep was sent upon us that day, and I heard the people of Mu'tab bin Qushair and drowsiness overcame me saying: If We have something to do with the matter that we were killed here. It was said: The meaning is that he says we have nothing to do with the victory that Muhammad promised us, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: “Say: The whole matter is God’s.” Abu Amr and Yaqub read all of it in the nominative case as the subject and its predicate is to God, and the sentence is the predicate of in, and it is like His saying: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about God, their faces will be blackened (al-Zumar 39:60), and the rest in the accusative case, as you say: The whole matter is God’s, so it is an emphasis, and it means all in encompassing and generalizing, and all can only be an emphasis, and it was said that it is an attribute of the matter, and Al-Akhfash said: It is a substitute, meaning victory is in the hand of God, He gives victory to whomever He wills and lets down whomever He wills, and Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: They think about God other than the truth, the thought of the ignorant, meaning the denial of destiny, and that is because they spoke about it, so God the Almighty said: “Say: The whole matter is God’s,” meaning destiny, its good and evil from God, they hide within themselves, meaning of polytheism, disbelief and denial, that which they do not reveal to you, “they reveal,” saying: If we had any part in the matter, we would not have been killed here. What killed our tribes? It was said: The hypocrites said: If we had reason, we would not have gone out to fight the people of Mecca, and our leaders would not have been killed. God responded to them and said: "Say: If you had been in your houses, those upon whom killing was decreed would have gone out" meaning in the Preserved Tablet, to their resting places meaning their places of death. It was said: Death was decreed upon them meaning fighting was decreed upon them, so it was expressed as killing, because it could lead to it. Abu Haywah read labaraz with a damma on the ya and a shaddah on the ra, meaning he would make him go out. It was said: If you, O hypocrites, had stayed behind, you would have gone out to another place other than it, where you would be defeated until God tests what is in the hearts and reveals it to the believers. The waw in His statement and to test is inserted like His statement: and to be among those who are certain (Al-An`am: 75), meaning to be, and the verb with the lam of ki was deleted, and the meaning is: God what is in your hearts and to purify what is in your hearts, and God is Knowing. God imposed fighting and war upon you and He will give you victory on the Day of Uhud to test your patience and to purify your sins if you repent and are sincere. It was said: The meaning of to test is to treat you as someone who tests. It was said: So that you may witness what He knows in secret. It was said: It is with the deletion of an adjective, and the meaning is to test the friends of God Almighty. The meaning of testing has already been presented, with what is in the hearts meaning what is in them of good and evil. It was said: The heart of the heart is the chest, because the heart of the thing is itself.
3:155: God Almighty says: “Indeed, those of you who turned back on the day the two armies met - it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. But God has pardoned them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Forbearing.” God the Almighty said: The devil caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned. This sentence is the predicate of Indeed, those who turned away, and what is meant is those who turned away from the polytheists on the day of Uhud, according to Umar, may God be pleased with him, and others. As-Suddi said: He means those who fled to Medina at the time of their defeat, not those who climbed the mountain. It was said: It was about specific people who stayed behind from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the time of their defeat for three days, then they turned away. The meaning of the devil caused them to slip is that he called for their slipping by reminding them of past sins from them, so they hated to remain steadfast lest they be killed, and this is the meaning of because of some of what they had earned. It was said: He caused them to slip and it is a verb derived from zalah, which is a sin. It was said: Zal and azal have the same meaning. Then it was said: They hated to fight before sincerely repenting, so they turned away for this reason. This is according to the first statement, and according to the second, by their disobedience to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in abandoning the position and inclining toward the spoils. Al-Hasan said: What they had earned is their acceptance of what Satan whispered to them. Al-Kalbi said: Satan made them seem good to them. Their actions, and it was said: The defeat was not a sin, because they wanted to fortify themselves in the city, so that the enemy would cut off his hope for them when they heard that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was killed, and it is permissible to say: They did not hear the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, due to the terror they were in, and it is permissible to say: The number of the enemy more than doubled, because they were seven hundred and the enemy was three thousand, and at this point the defeat is permissible, but the defeat of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a mistake that is not permissible, and perhaps they imagined that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, also took refuge in the mountain, and the first is better, and in general, if the matter is attributed to a proven sin, then God has forgiven it, and if it is attributed to a justified defeat, then the verse is about those who went far in the defeat and exceeded the justified limit, and Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi mentioned Nasr bin Muhammad bin Ibrahim, he said: Al-Khalil bin Ahmad told us, he said Al-Siraj told us, he said Qutaybah told us, he said Abu Bakr bin Ghailan told us on the authority of Jarir: That there was a conversation between Uthman and Abd al-Rahman bin Awf, so Abd al-Rahman bin Awf said to him: Do you curse me when you witnessed Badr and you did not witness it, and He pledged allegiance under the tree but did not pledge allegiance. You were appointed with those who were appointed on the day of assembly, meaning the day of Uhud. Uthman responded to him and said: As for your saying: I witnessed Badr and you did not, I did not miss anything that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, witnessed, except that the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sick and I was with her, tending to her. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave me a share among the shares of the Muslims. As for the pledge of allegiance under the tree, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me as a watchman over the polytheists in Mecca. The watchman is the observer, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck his right hand over his left and said: This is for Uthman, for the right hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his left hand is better for me than my right hand and my left hand. As for the day of assembly, God Almighty said: And God has pardoned them, so I was among those whom God pardoned. So Uthman performed the Hajj with Abd al-Rahman. I said: This meaning is also correct from Ibn Umar, as in Sahih al-Bukhari. He said: Abdun told us, Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Muhab, who said: “A man came to perform Hajj to the House and saw some people sitting, so he said: Who are these people sitting? They said: These are Quraysh. He said: Who is the old man? They said: Ibn Umar. So he came to him and said: I am going to ask you about something that you will tell me. He said: I ask you by the sanctity of this House, do you know that Uthman bin Affan fled on the day of Uhud? He said: Yes. He said: Do you know that he was absent from Badr and did not witness it? He said: Yes. He said: Do you know that he stayed away from the Pledge of Ridwan and did not witness it? He said: Yes. He said: Say Allahu Akbar. Ibn Umar said: Come, so I may tell you and explain to you what you asked me about. As for his fleeing on the day of Uhud, I bear witness that God has pardoned him. As for his absence from Badr, he had the daughter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) under him and she was sick. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: You will have the reward and share of a man who witnessed Badr. As for his absence from the Pledge of Ridwan, if he had been one of the most honorable In the valley of Mecca, from Uthman bin Affan, to send him in his place, so he sent Uthman, and the Pledge of Ridwan was after Uthman went to Mecca, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said with his right hand: This is the hand of Uthman, so he struck his hand with it and said: This is for Uthman, go with this now with you. I said: Similar to this verse is God’s repentance to Adam, peace be upon him, and His saying, peace be upon him: “So Adam and Moses argued,” meaning He defeated him with the argument. This is because Moses, peace be upon him, wanted to rebuke Adam and blame him for expelling himself and his offspring from Paradise because of his eating from the tree, so Adam said to him: Do you blame me for something that God Almighty decreed for me forty years before I was created, and he who repents to him has no sin, and he who has no sin is blamed, and likewise he who God pardons, and this was only because God Almighty informed him of that, and His report is true, and others of the repentant sinners hope for His mercy and fear His punishment, so they are in fear and apprehension that their repentance will not be accepted, and if it is accepted, then the fear is overwhelming them since they do not know about that, so know.
3:156: The Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved meaning the hypocrites, and said to their brothers meaning in hypocrisy or in lineage in the raids that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to Bir Ma'unah, If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed so the Muslims were forbidden to say the same as they said, and His saying if they struck refers to what has passed, that is, when they struck, because in the speech there is a meaning of condition, since those were vague and not timed, so if occurred as the past occurs in the conditional clause in place of the future, and the meaning of struck in the land is that they traveled in it and went for trade or something else and died, or were on a raid raiders and were killed, and the word ghazy is a defective plural that does not change its wording in the nominative and genitive, and its singular is ghazy, like rak'i and rak'u, and sa'im and sawm, and na'im and na'im, and shahed and shahed, and ghayb and ghayb, and in the plural ghazy is permissible, like qada and ghazy. With a long vowel, like darab and sawwam, and it is said: ghazi is the plural of ghazzah. The poet said: Tell the caravans and the invaders when they invade It was narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri that he read it ghazī with a light pronunciation. Al-Maghzīyah is the woman whose husband went on a raid, and a she-camel who gave birth late and then gave birth. A she-camel who was unable to conceive was called a ghazāt. Ghazwī is the intention of something, and al-Maghzā is the destination. It is said in relation to the raid: Ghazwī. The Almighty says: That God may make that a regret in their hearts meaning their assumption and their saying, and the lam is related to His saying they said, meaning that He may make their assumption that if they had not gone out they would not have been killed a regret meaning remorse in their hearts and regret is concern for something that has passed and was not able to be attained. The poet said: Alas, I did not fulfill my desires and did not enjoy the neighborhood and the closeness It was said: It is related to something omitted, and the meaning is: Do not be like them, so that God may make that statement a regret in their hearts because their hypocrisy has become apparent. It was said: The meaning is do not believe them and do not pay attention to them, so that was a regret in their hearts. It was said: so that God may make that a regret in their hearts on the Day of Resurrection because of the shame and regret they are in, and because of the bliss and dignity that the Muslims are in. The Almighty says: And God gives life and causes death. That is, He is able to give life to whoever goes out to fight, and cause death to whoever stays with his family. And God is Seeing of what you do. It was read with the letter ya and the letter ta. Then the Almighty informed us that being killed in the way of God and dying in it is better than the entire world.
3:157: God Almighty says: And if you are killed in the way of God or die - forgiveness from God and mercy are better than what they accumulate. The answer to the penalty is omitted, and it was dispensed with by the answer to the oath in His statement: for forgiveness from God and mercy. It would have been more appropriate to dispense with the answer to the oath, because it is the beginning of the speech, and its meaning is that He will forgive you. The people of Hijaz say: matam, with a kasra on the m, like namattum, from mata yamout, like khafat yakhaf, and the lower Mudar say: matam, with a damma on the m, like samtum, from mata yamout, like you say kan yakun, and qala yaqool, this is the saying of the Kufians and it is good.
3:158: The Almighty said: And if you die or are killed, to God you will be gathered. The Almighty’s saying: To God you will be gathered is an admonition. God admonished them with this statement, meaning do not slacken in fighting and what He has commanded you to do, but rather flee from His punishment and painful torment, for your return is to Him and no one has the power to harm or benefit you except Him, and God Almighty is All-Knowing.
3:159: ma is a conjunction that has the meaning of emphasis, i.e., by mercy, as in His saying: In a little while, "Because they broke their covenant, The army there is defeated," and it is not redundant at all, but rather Sibawayh gave it the meaning of redundancy from the point of view that its function was removed. Ibn Kaysan: ma is indefinite in the position of a genitive with the preposition "ba, and mercy" is a substitute for it. The meaning of the verse is that when he, peace be upon him, was gentle with those who turned away on the day of Uhud and did not reprimand them, the Lord Almighty explained that he did that with the guidance of God Almighty. It was said: ma is an interrogative, and the meaning is: By what mercy from God were you gentle with them? It is an expression of astonishment, and there is some distance in it, because if it were so, fa-ba-ma would have been without an alif. "La-nat is from lan to soften and layan to soften with the fat-ha, and the word vulgar" means rough and harsh. To be rude, to be rude, rudeness, and rudeness, so you are rude. The female is rude, and the plural is rudeness. In describing the Prophet, peace be upon him: He is not rude, nor harsh, nor loud in the markets. Al-Mufaddal recited in the masculine: It is not rude in the lower sense, and the first ones believe in its usefulness, but it is easy. He was careful with his enemies, so they warned him, for his power was deadly and his reward was abundant. Another said about the feminine: I am dying of distress in my home, while others are dying of depression. This world is generous to the ignorant, but harsh to the wise. Hardness of heart is a gloomy face, lack of emotion in desires, and lack of compassion and mercy. This is what the poet said: He cries for us, but we do not cry for anyone else, for we are more cruel than camels. The meaning of lanafadhu is to disperse. I scattered them and they dispersed, meaning I separated them and they dispersed. From this is what Abu al-Najm said, describing camels: The urgent summer months are not stripped of their pebbles, and the stones are shaken off them with the stick. The root of the word fad is kasra, and from it is their saying: May God not break your mouth. The meaning is: O Muhammad, if it were not for your gentleness, modesty and awe would have prevented them from approaching you after what had happened of their turning away. The Almighty’s saying: So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult them in the matter. There are eight issues in it. The first: The scholars said: God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with these commands, which are in a very gradual manner, and that is that He commanded him to forgive them for what he has in his own regard for them of responsibility, and when they reached this level, He commanded him to seek forgiveness for what God has in regard for them of responsibility as well, and when they reached this level, they became worthy of consultation in matters. The linguists said, consultation is taken from the saying of the Arabs: I bought the animal and consulted it if you know its report by running or otherwise, and the place where it runs is called mishwar, and it may be from their saying: I bought the honey and bought it, so it is mashwar and mushtar if you took it from its place. Adi bin Zaid said: In listening, the sheikh gives him permission and a hadith like what is mentioned Second: Ibn Atiyah said: Shura is one of the principles of the Shariah and the firm rulings. Whoever does not consult the people of knowledge and religion, his dismissal is obligatory. There is no disagreement about this. God praised the believers by saying: And their affairs are by consultation among themselves (al-Shura 42:38). An Arab said: I have never been deceived to the point that my people were deceived. It was said: How is that? He said: I do not do anything until I consult them. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: It is obligatory for the rulers to consult the scholars regarding what they do not know, and regarding matters of religion that are unclear to them, and the leaders of the army regarding what is related to war, and the leaders of the people regarding what is related to interests, and the leaders of the scribes, ministers and workers regarding what is related to the interests of the country and its development. It was said: He who consults does not regret it. It was also said: He who is impressed by his own opinion goes astray. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And consult them in the matter indicates the permissibility of ijtihad in matters and taking conjectures with the possibility of revelation, for God permitted His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to do so. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning in which God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to consult his companions. A group said: That is in the plots of war, and when meeting the enemy, and to comfort their souls, and to raise their status, and to reconcile them to their religion, even though God Almighty had made him independent of their opinion through His revelation. This was narrated on the authority of Qatada, al-Rabi’, Ibn Ishaq, and al-Shafi’i. Al-Shafi’i said: It is like His saying: And the virgin is consulted, to comfort her heart, not that it is obligatory. Muqatil, Qatada, and al-Rabi’ said: If the leaders of the Arabs did not consult in the matter, it would be difficult for them, so God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to consult them in the matter, for that is more affectionate to them, removes their grudges, and is better for their souls. So if he consults them, they will know that He honors them. Others said: This is in matters for which no revelation came to him. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Al-Dahhak, who said: God Almighty did not command His Prophet to consult because he needed their opinion, but rather he wanted to teach them the virtue of consultation, and for his nation to follow his example after him. In the reading of Ibn Abbas: And consult them in some of the matter. And the speaker did well: Consult your friend about the hidden problem and accept the advice of a kind advisor. God has recommended this to His Prophet in His saying: Consult them and Trust. Fourth: It was reported in Musannaf Abi Dawud on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The advisor is trustworthy.’ The scholars said: The description of the advisor, if it is in rulings, is that he be knowledgeable and religious, and that rarely happens except in a rational person. Al-Hasan said: ‘A person’s religion is not complete unless his mind is complete. So if someone of this description is consulted and he strives to do good and exerts his best effort and the advice falls into error, then there is no penalty upon him. Al-Khattabi and others said this: Fifth: The description of the advisor in worldly matters is that he should be wise, experienced, and kind to the one he is consulting. He said: Consult your friend about the hidden problem It was presented, and another said: If a matter becomes difficult for you, consult a wise person and do not disobey him. In the verses, and consultation is a blessing, and he, peace be upon him, said: “He who consults does not regret, nor does he who seeks guidance be disappointed,” and Sahl bin Saad Al-Sa’idi narrated: “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: A servant has never been miserable because of consultation, nor has he been happy because of his independent opinion,” and some of them said: Consult someone who has experienced matters, for he will give you from his opinion what he usually agrees upon, and you will take it for free. Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, made the caliphate, which is the greatest of calamities, consultation. Al-Bukhari said: The imams after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would consult trustworthy people from among the people of knowledge in permissible matters in order to take the easiest of them, and Sufyan Al-Thawri said: Let the people of your consultation be people of piety and trustworthiness, and those who fear God Almighty, and Al-Hasan said: By God, no people consult among themselves except that He guides them to the best of what they can bring with them, and it was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no people who had a consultation and someone named Ahmad or Muhammad was present with them, so they included him in their consultation except that it is better for them.” Sixth: Consultation is based on differences of opinion, and the one seeking advice looks into that difference and looks for the statement that is closest to the Book if he is able to. Then if God Almighty guides him to what He wills of it, he resolves to do it and carries it out, relying on Him, because this is the ultimate goal of the required effort, and God Almighty commanded His Prophet with this in this verse. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: So when you have decided, then rely upon God. Qatada said: God Almighty commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, when he decided on a matter, to go ahead with it and rely upon God, not upon consulting them. Determination is the narrated and refined matter, and following an opinion without deliberation is not determination, except for the section of the apostles from the young Arabs, as he said: If they cast their determination between their eyes and neglected to mention the consequences He did not consult anyone but himself regarding his opinion, and he was not satisfied with anyone but the one who had the sword as his companion. Al-Naqqash said: Resolve and firmness are one and the same, and the ‘ha’ is a substitute for the ‘ain. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: “This is a mistake, for firmness is the quality of looking into a matter and purifying it and being careful not to make a mistake in it, and firmness is the intention to carry it out. God Almighty says: “And consult them in the matter, and when you have decided,” so consultation and what is similar to it is firmness. The Arabs say: He has become firm if he has decided. Ja’far al-Sadiq and Jabir ibn Zayd read: So when you have resolved with a damma on the ta’, attributing firmness to Himself, glory be to Him, as He is with His guidance and success, as He said: And you did not throw when you threw, but it was God who threw (al-Anfal 8:17). The meaning of the statement is that I resolved for you and granted you success and guided you. So put your trust in God, and the rest with a fatha on the ta’. Al-Muhallab said: This Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, complied with the command of his Lord, so He said: It is not appropriate for a prophet who wears clothes for his nation to put them down until God decides, meaning it is not appropriate for him, when he has resolved, to leave, because it is a violation of the trust that God Almighty has stipulated. With determination, he dressed for his nation when he advised him to go out on the day of Uhud from those whom God honored with martyrdom in it, and they were the righteous believers who had missed Badr: O Messenger of God, go out with us to our enemy, indicating determination.
