The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had advised sitting, and Abdullah bin Ubay also advised that and said: Stay, O Messenger of God, and do not go out to them with the people, for if they stay, they will stay in an evil council, and if they come to us to Medina, we will fight them in the courtyards and the mouths of the alleys, and the women and children will throw stones at them from the roofs. By God, we have never fought an enemy in Medina except that we defeated him, nor have we gone out from it to an enemy except that we were defeated. Those who mentioned us rejected this opinion, and encouraged the people and called for war. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the Friday prayer, and after his prayer he entered his house and put on his weapons. Those people regretted it and said: We forced the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he went out to them in his righteousness, they said: O Messenger of God, stay if you wish, for we do not want to force you. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We do not want to. When a prophet puts on his weapon, he should put it down until he fights. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: “So rely upon God. Indeed, God loves those who rely [upon Him].” Reliance is dependence on God while showing helplessness. The noun is taklan. It is said from it: I relied on Him in my affair. Its original form is: awtakaltu. The waw was changed to a ya’ because of the kasra of what preceded it, then the ta’ was replaced and assimilated into the ta’ of ifti’al. It is also said: I entrusted him with my affair, tawkilan. The noun is agency, with the waw broken or open. Scholars differed about trust. A group of Sufis said: Only he who does not have fear of anyone other than God in his heart, such as a lion or other, deserves it, and until he abandons the pursuit of sustenance for the guarantee of God Almighty. The majority of jurists said what was mentioned above regarding God Almighty’s statement: And upon God let the believers put their trust, which is correct as we have explained. Moses and Aaron feared, as God Almighty informed us about them in His statement: Do not fear. (Ta-Ha 20:46), and He said: “So Moses felt fear within himself. We said, ‘Do not fear.’” (Ta-Ha 20:67-68), and He informed us about Abraham in His statement: “But when he saw that their hands did not reach him, he was unaware of them and felt fear of them. They said, ‘Do not fear.’” (Hud 11:70) So if Abraham and Moses, the one who spoke to God, feared, and that is enough for you, then others are more deserving, and this meaning will be explained.
3:160: The Almighty said: If God helps you, none can overcome you. That is, put your trust in Him, for if He helps you and protects you from your enemy, you will not be defeated. But if He forsakes you, He abandons you from His aid. Who is there that can help you after Him? That is, no one can help you after Him, that is, after He forsakes you, because He said, And if He forsakes you, and forsake means abandoning aid, and the forsworn is the one who is abandoned and no one cares about him. The wild animal was forsworn, so it stayed with its young in the pasture and abandoned its companions, so it was forsworn. Tarafa said: Take care of the rhubarb with a tent, take the edges of the barren land and wear He also said: I looked at you with the eyes of a slave girl who has let her friends down for the sake of a child. It was said: This is from the reverse, because it is the one that is abandoned if it is left, and his legs are abandoned if they are swayed. He said: And let down the man without sweeping A man who has let him down is someone who will continue to let him down. And God knows best.
3:161: It contains eleven issues: First: When the archers abandoned their positions on the day of Uhud, as mentioned above, for fear that the Muslims would seize the spoils and nothing would be given to them, God Almighty made it clear that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not permitted to divide them, so it was not right for you to accuse him. Ad-Dahhak said: Rather, the reason is that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out scouts in some of his battles and then took spoils before they came, so he divided them for the people and did not divide them for the scouts, so God sent down a rebuke to him: And it is not for a prophet to take spoils of war, and whoever takes spoils of war means dividing for some and leaving others. A similar statement was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas also said, and Ikrimah, Ibn Jubayr, and others said: It was revealed because of a red velvet that was lost in the spoils on the day of Badr, so some of those who were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Perhaps the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it, so the verse was revealed. Abu Dawud and At-Tirmidhi narrated it, and he said: This is a good and strange hadith. Ibn Atiyyah said: It was said that this statement was from believers who did not think that there was any harm in that, and it was said: It was From the hypocrites, and it has been narrated that the missing was a sword, and these sayings come out on the reading yaghl with the opening of the ya and the damma of the ghain, and Abu Sakhr narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab and it was not for a prophet to yaghl he said: you say and it was not for a prophet to conceal anything from the Book of God, and it was said: the lam in it is transferred, meaning and it was not for a prophet to yaghl, like his saying: It was not for God to take a son, glory be to Him meaning it was not for God to take a son, and it was read yaghl with the damma of the ya and the opening of the ghain, and Ibn al-Sikkit said: we did not hear about the spoils except ghal ghululan, and it was read and it was not for a prophet to yaghl and yaghl, he said: so the meaning of yaghl is to betray, and the meaning of yaghl is to betray, and it is possible for two meanings: one of them is to betray, meaning it is taken from his spoils, and the other is to betray that he is attributed to yaghlul: then it was said: whoever yaghl something secretly has yaghl yaghl ghululan, Ibn Arafa said: it is called yaghlul because the hands It is restricted from it, meaning it is forbidden. Abu Ubaid said: Gholul is specifically from spoils of war, and we do not see it as being from treachery or hatred. What makes this clear is that it is said from treachery: aghal yaghl, and from hatred: ghal yaghl with the kasra, and from gholul: ghal yaghl with the damma, and the camel’s ghal is also yaghl if it does not finish its watering, and the man is aghal treachery, Al-Nimr said: May God reward Hamza bint Nawfal on our behalf with the reward of a liar who betrays trust. In the hadith: No iqlal nor islal meaning no betrayal or theft. It is also said: no bribery. Shuraih said: There is no guarantee for the borrower other than the one who has been betrayed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There are three things that a believer’s heart will not be betrayed by. Whoever narrates it with the fat-ha, it is from the word dhughn. “Ghal” is transitive and intransitive. It is said: So-and-so entered the desert, meaning he entered it and entered it. Ghal means he betrayed. Ghal means he betrayed. Ghal means the water flows between the trees if it runs in them. Yaghal with the damma is used in all of that. It was said: Ghalul in the language means taking something from the spoils to hide it from its owners. From this comes the word ghalal meaning it penetrates the trees. Ghalal means the water flowing in the roots of the trees because it is hidden by the trees, as he said: The floods played with it, and its water became a sludge that cut into the roots of the castor bean. And from it is the ghalala for the garment that is worn under the clothes, and ghal: a peaceful land with trees, and the growing places of salam and acacia, it is called ghal, and ghal is also a plant, and the plural is ghalān with dammah, and some people said: the meaning of yaghl is to find ghalān, as you say: I praised the man and found him praiseworthy, so this reading according to this interpretation goes back to the meaning of yaghl with the fathah of the ya and the dammah of the ghain, and the meaning of yaghl according to the majority of scholars is that no one has the right to cheat him, that is, to betray him in the spoils, so the verse is in the meaning of forbidding people from cheating in the spoils, and threatening him with it, and just as it is not permissible to betray the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is not permissible to betray anyone else, but he was mentioned specifically because betrayal with him is more severe and has a greater burden, because sins are magnified in his presence to make him respected, and the rulers are only on the command of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they have their share of respect. And it was said: the meaning of yaghl is that no prophet has ever cheated, The purpose is not to prohibit. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And whoever steals will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection. That is, he will bring it carrying it on his back and neck, tormented by its weight and its burden, terrified by its voice, and rebuked by the display of his treachery in front of all witnesses, as will come. And this disgrace that God Almighty inflicts on the one who steals is similar to the disgrace that befalls the traitor, in that a banner is raised for him at his backside according to the extent of his treachery. And God Almighty made these punishments according to what people know and understand. Do you not see the words of the poet: My name is Waheek, have you heard of the treachery with which the banner was raised for us in the assembly? The Arabs used to raise a banner for the traitor, and the criminal would also be paraded with his crime. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up among us one day and mentioned theft, and he magnified it and magnified its matter, then he said: I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a camel on his neck that roars, saying: O Messenger of God, help me, and I will say: I have no power over you, I have conveyed the message to you. I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a neighing horse on his neck, saying: O Messenger of God, help me, and I will say: I have no power over you, I have conveyed the message to you. I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a bleating sheep on his neck, saying: O Messenger of God, help me, and I will say: I have no power over you, I have conveyed the message to you. I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a soul on his neck that cries, and he says: O Messenger of God, help me, and I will say: I have no power over you, I have conveyed the message to you. I will not find one of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with fluttering papers on his neck, and he says: O Messenger of God, help me, and I will say: I have no power over you, I have conveyed the message to you. “I do not want to find any of you coming on the Day of Resurrection with a mute person on his neck and saying, ‘O Messenger of God, help me,’ and I will say, ‘I do not have anything for you, I have conveyed the message to you.’” Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub who said: “Whenever the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, acquired spoils of war, he would order Bilal to call out to the people and they would bring their spoils and he would take a fifth of it and divide it up. One day after the call, a man came with a rein of hair and said, ‘O Messenger of God, this was part of what we acquired of the spoils of war.’ He said, ‘Did you hear Bilal calling out three times?’ He said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘What prevented you from bringing it?’” So he apologized to him, and he said: No, you will bring it on the Day of Resurrection, and I will not accept it from you. Some scholars said: He meant that he will be burdened with that on the Day of Resurrection, as He said in another verse: “And they will bear their burdens on their backs. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.” (Al-An`am: 31) It was said: The report is based on the fame of the matter, meaning that he will come on the Day of Resurrection with his matter famous, as it would be famous if he carried a camel that was roaring or a horse that was neighing. I said: This is a departure from the truth to metaphor and simile. If the discussion revolves around the truth and metaphor, then the truth is the origin, as in the books of principles. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us of the truth, and there is no perfume after the bride. It is said: Whoever steals something in this world will be presented to him on the Day of Resurrection in the Fire, then it will be said to him: Go down to it and take it. So he will go down to it, and when he reaches it, he will carry it, until when he reaches the door, it will fall from him to the bottom of Hell. So he will return to it and take it, and it will remain like this until God wills. It is said: He will come with what he stole, meaning that that betrayal and theft will bear witness against him on the Day of Resurrection. Third: The scholars said: Stealing is a major sin, as evidenced by this verse and what we mentioned from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: He carries it on his neck. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about Mud’am: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the cloak that was taken from the spoils on the day of Khaybar was not divided up and it would have caught fire on him. He said: When the people heard that, a man came with one or two straps to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: One or two straps of fire. Narrated by Al-Muwatta’. So his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, and his abstention from praying for the one who stole is evidence of the greatness of stealing and the greatness of the sin in it and that it is one of the major sins. It is one of the rights of humans and there must be retribution for it with good and bad deeds, then its owner in the will. His saying: One or two straps of fire, is like his saying: Give back the tailor and the needle. This indicates that it is not permissible to take a small or large amount in a conquest before the division, except for what they agreed upon of eating food in the conquest area and from… Firewood gathering and hunting. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri that he said: Food should not be taken in the land of the enemy except with the permission of the Imam. This has no basis, because the reports contradict it, as follows. Al-Hasan said: When the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered a city or a fortress, they would eat from the gruel, flour, ghee, and honey. Ibrahim said: They would eat food from the land of the enemy in the land of war and feed it before it was given a fifth. Ata’ said: In the raids, they would be in the secret and obtain various types of ghee, honey, and food and eat, and whatever remained they would return to their Imam. This is the view of the group of scholars. Fourth: This hadith is evidence that the thief should not burn his belongings, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not burn the belongings of the man who took the cloak. And I do not burn the belongings of the owner of the beads who did not pray over them. If burning his belongings was obligatory, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would have done so. If he had done so, it would have been mentioned in the hadith. As for what was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him, “On the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: If you find a man who has stolen, burn his belongings and beat him,” Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Za’idah, who is weak and cannot be relied upon. Al-Tirmidhi said: I asked Muhammad, meaning al-Bukhari, about this hadith and he said: This was only narrated by Salih ibn Muhammad, who is Abu Waqid al-Laythi, and he is a fabricator of hadith. Abu Dawud also narrated on his authority that he said: We went on a raid with al-Walid ibn Hisham, and with us were Salim ibn Abdullah ibn Umar and Umar ibn Abdul Aziz. A man stole some belongings, so al-Walid ordered his belongings to be burned and paraded around, but he did not give him his share. Abu Dawud said: This is the more authentic of the two hadiths. It was narrated from the hadith of Amr ibn Shu`ayb on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr and Umar burned the belongings of the usurper and beat him. Abu Dawud said: Ali ibn Bahr added to it on the authority of al-Walid, and I did not hear it from him: and they denied him his share. Abu Umar said: Some of the narrators of this hadith said: and strike his neck and burn his belongings. This hadith is based on Salih ibn Muhammad, and he is not one of those who can be relied upon. It has been proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The blood of a Muslim is not permissible except in one of three cases, and he denies killing in the case of usurpation. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is no amputation for the traitor, the plunderer, or the embezzler. This contradicts the hadith of Salih ibn Muhammad, which is stronger in terms of chain of transmission. The usurper is a traitor in language and Sharia, and if amputation is denied him, then killing is more appropriate. At-Tahawi said: If the hadith of Salih mentioned is authentic, it is possible that it was when the punishments were in the case of wealth, as he said about the one who withheld zakat: We will take it and half of his wealth, a determination from The determination of God Almighty, and as Abu Hurairah said about the lost camel that was concealed: There is a fine for it and a similar amount with it, and as Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas narrated about the hanging fruit: a fine of twice its amount and lashes as punishment. All of this has been abrogated, and God knows best. Fifth: If a man steals from the spoils of war and finds it, it is taken from him, and he is disciplined and punished with discretionary punishment. According to Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifah, their companions, and Al-Layth: His belongings are not to be burned. Al-Shafi’i, Al-Layth, and Dawud said: If he was aware of the prohibition, he is to be punished. Al-Awza’i said: All of the stealer’s belongings are to be burned except for his weapons, the clothes he is wearing, and his saddle. His mount is not to be taken away from him, and the thing he stole is not to be burned. This is the opinion of Ahmad and Ishaq, and Al-Hasan said the same, unless it is an animal or a copy of the Qur’an. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: It was narrated that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with them both, beat the stealer and burned his belongings. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: Among those who said that the stealer’s saddle and belongings are to be burned are Makhul and Sa’id ibn Abd Al-Aziz. The proof of those who held this view is the aforementioned hadith of Salih, which we consider a hadith that does not require violating the sanctity or enforcing a ruling, because of the reports that contradict it that are stronger than it. What Malik and those who followed him held in this matter is more correct from the point of view and the correct report, and God knows best.. Sixth: Malik’s school of thought did not differ regarding the punishment for the body. As for the money, he said regarding a dhimmi who sells wine to a Muslim: The wine is spilled on the Muslim, and the price is taken from the dhimmi as a punishment for him, so that he does not sell wine to Muslims. Based on this, it is permissible to say: The punishment for the money is permissible, and Umar, may God be pleased with him, spilled milk that had been mixed with water. Seventh: The scholars agreed that the one who has stolen the property may return all that he has stolen to the owner of the shares before the people disperse if he finds a way to do so, and that if he does so, it is repentance for him and an exoneration from his sin. They differed about what should be done with it if the people of the army disperse and he does not reach it. A group of scholars said: He should pay the Imam a fifth of it and give the rest in charity. This is the view of Al-Zuhri, Malik, Al-Awza’i, Al-Layth, and Al-Thawri. It was narrated from Ubadah ibn Al-Samit, Mu’awiyah, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri. It is similar to the view of Ibn Mas’ud and Ibn Abbas, because they were of the view that the money whose owner is not known should be given in charity. This is the view of Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Al-Shafi’i said: He does not have the right to give charity with someone else’s money. Abu Omar said: This is in my opinion with regard to what its owner can be found and reached or to his heirs. However, if none of that is the case, Al-Shafi’i does not dislike giving charity in that case, God willing. They agreed on the permissibility of giving charity with regard to lost property after identifying it and its owner being absent, and they made him, if he comes, have the choice between reward and guarantee. The same applies to usurped property. And God is the Grantor of success. In The prohibition of embezzlement is evidence of the participation of the conquerors in the spoils, so it is not permissible for one person to monopolize part of it without the other. Whoever usurps part of it will be disciplined by consensus, as mentioned above. Eighth: If he had intercourse with a female slave or stole a minimum amount, the scholars differed about the punishment to be carried out on him. A group of scholars held that there should be no amputation of his hand. Ninth: Among the embezzlements are the gifts of workers, and the ruling on them in terms of disgrace in the Hereafter is the ruling on the embezzler. Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan and Muslim in his Sahih on the authority of Abu Humayd al-Sa’idi: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, employed a man from Azd called Ibn al-Latibiyyah, Ibn al-Sarh Ibn al-Atbiyyah, to collect the zakat. He came and said: This is for you and this was given to me. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on the pulpit and praised God and thanked Him and said: What is wrong with the worker whom we send and he comes and says: This is for you and this was given to me? Why does he not sit in the house of his mother or father and see whether he is given a gift or not? No one among you will come with anything of that except that he will come with it on the Day of Resurrection. If it is a camel, it will roar, and if it is a cow, it will moo, or a sheep will bleat. Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits, then he said: O God, have I conveyed the message? O God, have I conveyed the message.” Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Buraidah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Whoever we employ in a job and provide for him, and whatever he takes after that is embezzlement.” It was also narrated on the authority of Abu Mas`ud al-Ansari said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me as a messenger and then said: Go, Abu Mas`ud, lest I find you on the Day of Resurrection carrying a camel from the charity camels, roaring and you have stolen it. He said: Then I will not go. He said: Then I will not hate you. These hadiths were also restricted by what Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of al-Mustawrid ibn Shaddad, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever works for us should acquire a wife. If he does not have a servant, then let him acquire a servant. If he does not have a home, then let him acquire a home. Abu Bakr said: I was informed that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever takes anything other than that is a thief and a thief. And God knows best. Tenth: Among the forms of embezzlement is withholding books from their owners, and other things are included in its meaning. Al-Zuhri said: Beware of embezzling books. It was said to him: What is embezzling books? He said: Withholding them from their owners. It has been said in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty: And it is not for a prophet to commit embezzlement that he conceals something from the revelation out of desire, fear, or flattery. This is because they hated what was in the Qur’an of faults in their religion and insults to their gods, so they asked him to conceal that, so God revealed this verse. Muhammad ibn Bashar said this, and what we began with is the opinion of the majority. Eleventh: The Almighty’s saying: Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged. This has been discussed previously.
3:162: God Almighty says: Is he who pursues the pleasure of God meaning by abandoning theft and being patient in jihad like he who incurs the wrath of God meaning by disbelief or theft or turning away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in war, and their refuge is Hell meaning his abode is the Fire, meaning if he does not repent or God forgives him, and wretched is the destination meaning the return, and Ridwan is read with a kasra on the ra’ and a damma on it like ‘adwān and ‘adwān.
3:163: The Almighty said: They are degrees with God meaning that whoever follows the pleasure of God is not like whoever incurs His wrath. It was said: They are degrees are different, meaning that they are of different status with God. For whoever follows His pleasure is honor and great reward, and for whoever incurs His wrath is humiliation and painful torment. The meaning of They are degrees is that they have degrees, or are on degrees, or are in degrees, or have degrees. The people of Hell also have degrees, as He said: I found him in the depths of the Fire, so I brought him out to shallow water. So the believer and the disbeliever are not equal in degree. Then the believers also differ, as some of them are higher in degree than others, and so are the disbelievers. The degree is the rank, and from this comes the ladder: because it is folded up rank after rank. The most famous in the homes of Hell are levels, as He said: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire (An-Nisa’: 145). So for whoever does not exceed the levels, each of them is called a level, and the level is to the bottom. And the stairs up.
3:164: God Almighty explained the greatness of His favor upon them by sending Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. There are several sayings about the meaning of the favor: One of them is that the meaning of from themselves is a human being like them. When he showed the proofs, and he was a human being like them, it was known that this was from God. It was also said: from themselves from them, so they were honored by him, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was the favor. It was also said: from themselves so that they would know his situation and his method would not be hidden from them. If his position among them was like this, they would be more deserving of fighting for him and not being defeated without him. It was read in the exceptions from themselves (with an open fa’) meaning from the most honorable of them, because he is from Banu Hashim, and Banu Hashim are better than Quraysh, and Quraysh are better than the Arabs, and the Arabs are better than others. Then it was said: The word believers is general and its meaning is specific to the Arabs, because there is no tribe from the tribes of the Arabs except that he was born, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they have a lineage in him, except for Banu Taghlib, for they were Christians, so God purified them from the filth of Christianity. And this is an explanation of the interpretation of the words of God the Almighty: It is He who sent among the unlettered a Messenger from among themselves (al-Jumuah 62:2). Abu Muhammad Abd al-Ghani mentioned: Abu Ahmad al-Basri told us: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Sa’id al-Qadi Abu Bakr al-Marwazi told us: Yahya ibn Ma’in told us: Hisham ibn Yusuf told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-Nawfali, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: God has conferred a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves. She said: This is specifically for the Arabs. Others said: He meant all the believers, and the meaning of from among themselves is that he is one of them and a human being like them, and he was only distinguished from them by revelation, and this is the meaning of His words: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. He singled out the believers for mention because they are the ones who benefit from him, so the favor upon them is greater. And the words of God the Almighty: He recites to them recites is in the accusative case as an attribute of Messenger, and its meaning is he reads, and recitation is reading, and teaches them the Book and wisdom were mentioned previously in al-Baqarah. The meaning of and they were before is that they were before in nothing but clear error. And similar to it is And you were before that among those astray, meaning, and you were not before that except among those astray. This is the doctrine of the Kufians, and the meaning of this verse was previously mentioned in Al-Baqarah.
3:165: The alif is for interrogation, and the waw is for conjunction. A calamity means defeat. You have suffered double its [loss] on the day of Badr, by killing seventy of them and taking seventy captive. A captive is considered to be killed, because a captor can kill his captive if he wishes. So you defeated them on the day of Badr and also on the day of Uhud, in the beginning, and you killed close to twenty of them. You killed them in two days, and they took revenge on you on the day of Uhud. You said, ‘How is this?’ That is, from where did this defeat and killing come to us, while we are fighting in the way of God, and we are Muslims, and among us is the Prophet and the revelation, and they are polytheists! “Say: It is from yourselves” meaning opposing the archers. No people obeyed their Prophet in war except that they were victorious, because if they obeyed, they are the party of God, and the party of God is the victorious. Qatada and Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas said: It means that they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to leave after he wanted to stay in Medina, and he interpreted it, in the vision he saw as a strong shield, Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, as their choice of ransom on the day of Badr over killing. It was said to them: If you ransom the prisoners, some of you will be killed according to their number. Al-Bayhaqi narrated: On the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the prisoners on the day of Badr: If you wish, you can kill them, and if you wish, you can ransom them and enjoy the ransom, and some of you will be martyred according to their number.” So the last of the seventy was Thabit bin Qais, who was killed on the day of Yamamah. So the meaning of from yourselves according to the first two opinions is your sins, and according to the last opinion, it is your choice.
3:166: It means the day of Uhud, of killing, wounding and defeat. Then by the permission of God means by His knowledge. It was also said: by His decree and destiny. Al-Qaffal said: That is, by His leaving you alone with them, not that he intended that. This is the interpretation of the Mu'tazila. The letter fa was included in Then by the permission of God because ma means who, meaning that which befell you on the day the two armies met was by the permission of God. So the statement resembles the meaning of a condition, as Sibawayh said: The one who stood up will have a dirham. “And that He may teach the believers.”
3:167: The Almighty said: And that He may know those who are hypocrites meaning to distinguish, and it was said to see, and it was said: to show the faith of the believers by their steadfastness in the battle, and to show the disbelief of the hypocrites by their display of gloating so that they may know that, and the reference in His saying: They were hypocrites and it was said to them is to Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions who turned away with him from supporting the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were three hundred, so Abdullah bin Amr bin Haram Al-Ansari, Abu Jabir bin Abdullah, walked in their footsteps and said to them: Fear God and do not abandon your Prophet, and fight in the way of God or defend yourself, and similar to this of speech, so Ibn Ubayy said to him: I do not see that there will be fighting, and if we knew that there will be fighting we would have been with you, so when Abdullah was so bad from them he said: Go, enemies of God, for God and His Messenger will suffice you, and he went with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and was martyred, may God Almighty have mercy on him. People differed about the meaning of his saying: Or repel. Al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, and others said: Increase our blacks even if you do not fight with us, so that this will be a repelling and suppression of the enemy, because when the blacks are numerous, the enemy is repelled. Anas bin Malik said: On the day of Al-Qadisiyyah, I saw Abdullah bin Umm Maktum, the blind man, wearing a suit of armor whose edges were dragging, and in his hand was a black banner. It was said to him: Has not God revealed your excuse? He said: Yes! But I myself am the most black of the Muslims. It was narrated from him that he said: So how about my presence in the path of God! Abu Aoun Al-Ansari said, the meaning of or defend is to guard, and this is close to the first, and there is no doubt that the guard is a defender, because if it were not for the position of the guards on the borders, the enemy would have come to them. Some of the commentators said that the saying of Abdullah bin Amr or defend is only a call to fight out of zeal, because he called them to fight in the way of God, which is that the word of God is supreme. When he saw that they were not like that, he presented to them the way that would make them feel ashamed and arouse pride, that is, or fight in defense of the estate. Do you not see that Quzman said: By God, I only fought for the sake of my people’s lineage? And do you not see that some of the Ansar said on the day of Uhud when he saw the Quraysh sending their backs to the crops of the canal, Are you grazing the crops of Bani Qaylah, and why should we fight? The meaning is that if you do not fight in the way of God, then fight to defend yourselves and your women. The Almighty says: They will be nearer to disbelief that Day than to faith. That is, they will make their condition clear, tear down their veils, and reveal their hypocrisy to those who thought they were Muslims. Thus, they will appear to be closer to disbelief, even though they are truly disbelievers. The Almighty says: They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts. That is, they will show faith, but conceal disbelief. The mention of the mouths is an emphasis, like His saying: It flies with its two wings (al-An’am 6:38).
3:168: The Almighty’s saying: Those who said to their brothers means for the sake of their brothers, and they are the martyrs who were killed from the Khazraj, and they are brothers of lineage and neighborhood, not brothers of religion, that is, they said to these martyrs: If they had stayed, that is, in Medina, they would not have been killed. It was said: Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions said to their brothers, that is, to their likes from al-Munafiqun 63:If they had obeyed us, these who were killed would not have been killed. His saying: If they had obeyed us means that they would not have gone out to Quraysh. His saying: And they sat means that they said this statement and sat back themselves from jihad, so God responded to them by saying: Say, then repel that is, say to them, O Muhammad: If you are truthful, then repel death from yourselves, and repelling means repelling. He explained with this that caution does not benefit from fate, and that the one who is killed is killed at his appointed time, and what God knows and informs of will inevitably happen. It was said: On the day this was said, seventy hypocrites died. Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi said: I heard some The commentators in Samarkand say: When the verse was revealed: “Say: ‘Then avert death from yourselves,’” seventy hypocrites died that day.
3:169: First: When God Almighty explained that what happened on the day of Uhud was a test to distinguish the hypocrite from the truthful, He explained that whoever was not defeated and killed has honor and life with him, and the verse is about the martyrs of Uhud, and it was said: It was revealed about the martyrs of Bir Ma'unah, and it was said: Rather, it is general for all martyrs, and in the book of Abu Dawud with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When your brothers were afflicted at Uhud, God placed their souls in the bodies of green birds that go to the rivers of Paradise, eat from its fruits, and take refuge in lamps of gold suspended in the shade of the Throne, so that they would not lose interest in jihad or retreat in war. God Almighty said: I will convey to them on your behalf,” he said: So God revealed: And do not think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead to the end of the verses. Baqi bin Mukhallad narrated, “On the authority of Jabir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met me and said: O Jabir, why do I see you downcast and worried? I said: O Messenger of God, my father was martyred and left behind children and a debt. He said: Shall I not give you good report of what God, the Almighty, met your father with? I said: Yes, O Messenger of God. He said: God brought your father back to life and spoke to him directly, and He never spoke to anyone except from behind a veil. He said to him: O My servant, wish and I will give you. He said: O Lord, return me to the world so that I may be killed in Your cause a second time. The Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, said: It has already been decreed by Me that they will not return to it. He said: O Lord, then convey it to those who come after me. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: “And never think that those who were killed in the way of God are dead. Rather, they are alive.” He said: When Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib and Mus`ab bin Umair and they saw what they were given of goodness, they said: If only our brothers knew what goodness has befallen us, they would increase their desire for jihad. God Almighty said: I will convey it to them on your behalf. Then God Almighty revealed: And never think that those who are killed in the way of God are dead until His saying: The reward of the believers will not be lost. Abu al-Dhaha said: This verse was revealed about the people of Uhud in particular, and the first hadith requires the correctness of this statement. Some of them said: It was revealed about the martyrs of Badr, and they were fourteen men, eight from the Ansar and six from the Muhajireen. It was said: It was revealed about the martyrs of Bir Ma’unah, and their story is famous, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others mentioned it. Others said: When the guardians of the martyrs were afflicted with a blessing and joy, they would regret and say: We are in a blessing and joy, and our fathers and brothers are in the graves. So God Almighty revealed this verse to relieve them and inform them about the state of their dead. I said: In short, even if it is possible that the revelation was due to the group, God Almighty informed us in it about the martyrs that they are alive in Paradise and are provided for, and there is no doubt that they died and their bodies are in the dust, and their souls are alive like the souls of all the believers, and they were given preference in provision in Paradise from the time of killing until it was as if the life of this world was permanent for them. Scholars have differed on this meaning. The majority of scholars agree on what we have mentioned, and that the life of the martyrs is certain. Then some of them say: The souls return to them in their graves and they enjoy themselves just as the infidels live in their graves and are tormented. Mujahid said: They are provided with the fruits of Paradise, meaning they find its fragrance but are not in it. Some people have concluded that this is a metaphor, and the meaning is that they are, by the judgment of God, deserving of enjoyment in Paradise. It is like saying: So-and-so did not die, meaning his memory is alive, as it was said: The death of the pious is an eternal life. Some people have died while they were alive among the people. The meaning is that they are granted beautiful praise. Others said: Their souls are in the bellies of green birds and that they are granted provision in Paradise and eat and enjoy themselves. This is the correct statement, because whatever is authentically transmitted is the reality. The hadith of Ibn Abbas is a text that removes the dispute, as is the hadith of Ibn Mas`ud, which was included by Muslim. We have already explained this meaning in the book At-Tadhkirah bi-Ahwal Al-Mawta wa-Amr Al-Akhira. Praise be to God. We have mentioned there how many martyrs there are, and that their condition varies. As for those who interpret the martyrs as being alive, meaning that they will come back to life, this is far-fetched and is rejected by the Qur’an and Sunnah, for the Most High’s statement, Rather, they are alive, is evidence of their life, and that they are provided for, and no one is provided for except the living. It has been said that the reward of a battle is written for them every year, and they share in the reward of every jihad that came after them until the Day of Resurrection, because they established the matter of jihad. Similar to the statement of the Most High, Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul (al-Ma’idah 5:32), as will be explained there, God willing. It has also been said that their souls bow and prostrate under the Throne until the Day of Resurrection, like the souls of the living believers who spent the night in a state of ritual purity. It has also been said that the martyr does not decay in the grave, and the earth does not eat him. We have mentioned this meaning in al-Tadhkirah, and that the earth does not eat the prophets, martyrs, scholars, muezzins who seek reward, and bearers of the Qur’an. Second: If the martyr is alive by law, then he is not prayed over, just like the living by sense. The scholars differed regarding washing the martyrs and praying over them. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, and Al-Thawri went to wash all the martyrs and pray over them, except for those killed in battle while fighting the enemy specifically, based on the hadith of Jabir who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Bury them with their blood,’ meaning the day of Uhud, and he did not wash them. It was narrated by Al-Bukhari. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that the iron and leather be removed from the dead of Uhud and that they be buried with their blood and clothes. This is what Ahmad, Ishaq, Al-Awza’i, Dawud bin Ali, and a group of the jurists of the Ath-Thār and the people of hadith and Ibn Ulayyah said. Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab and Al-Hasan said: They are washed. One of them said: The martyrs of Uhud were not washed because of their large number and the preoccupation with that. Abu Umar said: None of the jurists of the regions said this statement of Sa’id and Al-Hasan except Ubaydullah bin Al-Hasan Al-Anbari, and what they mentioned about being preoccupied with washing the martyrs of Uhud is not what they mentioned about being preoccupied with washing the martyrs of Uhud. A reason, because each one of them had a guardian who would occupy himself with him and take care of his affairs, and the reason for that, and God knows best, is what came in the hadith about their blood: “It will come on the Day of Resurrection like the scent of a path.” So it became clear that the reason is not the occupation as those who said about that said, and this issue has no place in analogy and consideration, but rather it is a matter of following the trace that was transmitted by all regarding those killed at Uhud who were not washed. Some of the later scholars who followed the school of al-Hasan used as evidence his saying, peace be upon him, regarding the martyrs of UHud 11:I am a witness over these on the Day of Resurrection. He said: This indicates their exclusivity and that no one else shares in that with them. Abu Omar said: This resembles an anomaly, and the saying that they should not be washed is more appropriate, because that was proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding those killed at Uhud and others. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: A man was shot with an arrow in his chest or throat and died, so he was wrapped in his clothes as he was. He said: And we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Third: As for praying over them, the scholars differed on that as well. Malik, Al-Layth, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and Dawud were of the opinion that they should not be prayed over, based on the hadith of Jabir who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would gather the two men killed at Uhud in one garment and then say: Which of them knew more of the Qur’an? If one of them was pointed out to him, he would put him forward in the grave and say: I will be a witness over these people on the Day of Resurrection. He ordered that they be buried with their blood and they were not washed and no prayer was said over them.” The jurists of Kufa, Basra and Ash-Sham said: They should be prayed over, and they narrated many reports, most of which were mursal. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over Hamza and all the martyrs of Uhud. Fourth: The scholars agreed that if a martyr is carried alive and does not die in battle and lives and eats, then he should be prayed over, as was done with Omar, may God be pleased with him. They differed about the one who was killed unjustly, such as the one killed by the Khawarij, the highway robbers, and the like. Abu Hanifa and al-Thawri said: Everyone who was killed unjustly is not washed, but he is prayed over, as is the case with every martyr. This is the opinion of all the people of Iraq. They narrated through many authentic chains of transmission on the authority of Zayd ibn Suhan, who was killed on the Day of the Camel: Do not remove my garment and do not wash my blood. It was proven on the authority of Ammar ibn Yasir that he said like the people of Zayd ibn Suhan, and Ammar ibn Yasir was killed at Siffin and Ali did not wash him. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions, one of which is that he is washed like all the dead except those killed by the people of war. This is the opinion of Malik. Malik said: The one who was killed by the infidels and died in battle is not washed. Every person killed other than the one killed in battle, killed by the infidels, is washed and the prayer is prayed over. This is the opinion of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God be pleased with him. The other opinion of al-Shafi’i is that the one killed by the rebels is not washed. The opinion of Malik is more correct, because washing the dead has been proven by consensus and transmitted by all, so washing every dead person is obligatory except… Whoever narrated it based on consensus or an established Sunnah, and success is from God. Fifth: If an enemy attacks people in their home and they do not know about it and kills some of them, is his ruling the same as the ruling of those killed in battle, or the ruling of all the dead? This issue was revealed to us in Cordoba, may God restore it: The enemy, may God break him, attacked on the morning of the third of the great Ramadan in the year six hundred and twenty-seven, while the people were in their huts, unaware, so he killed and took captives. My father, may God have mercy on him, was among those killed. So I asked our Sheikh, the reciter, the teacher Abu Ja`far Ahmad, known as Abu Hujjah, and he said: Wash him and pray over him, because your father was not killed in battle between the two lines. Then I asked our Sheikh Rabi` ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ahmad ibn Rabi` ibn Abi, and he said: His ruling is the ruling of those killed in battle. Then I asked the judge of the group, Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Qatral, and a group of jurists were around him, and they said: Wash him, shroud him, and pray over him. So I did. Then after that I came across the issue in al-Tabsira by Abu al-Hasan al-Lakhmi and others. If that had been before I washed him, I would have buried him with his blood in his clothes. Sixth: This verse indicates the great reward of killing in the way of God and martyrdom in it, to the point that it expiates sins, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Killing in the way of God expiates everything except debt. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said this to me just now.” Our scholars said that mentioning debt is an indication of what is similar to it in terms of rights related to consciences, such as usurpation, taking money unjustly, premeditated murder, wounding, and other consequences. All of this is more deserving of not being forgiven by jihad than by debt, as it is more severe. Retribution in all of these is by good deeds and bad deeds, as stated in the established Sunnah. “Abdullah bin Anas narrated that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God will gather the servants, or he said the people, Hammam doubted, and he pointed with his hand to the Levant, naked, uncircumcised and mute. We said: What is wrong with them? He said: They have nothing with them. Then he will call out to them in a voice that will be heard from near and far: I am the King, I am the Judge. It is not appropriate for anyone from the people of Paradise to enter Paradise while one of the people of Hell seeks him out with a wrong, and it is not appropriate for anyone from the people of Hell to enter Hell while one of the people of Paradise seeks him out with a wrong, even a slap. We said: How is that, when we come to God barefoot, naked and uncircumcised? He said: With good deeds and bad deeds.” Narrated by Al-Harith bin Abi Usamah, and in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know who is bankrupt? They said: The bankrupt among us is the one who has no dirham or property. He said: The bankrupt among my nation is the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection with prayer, fasting and zakat, but he has insulted this one, slandered that one, consumed the wealth of this one, shed the blood of this one and struck this one. So this one will be given from his good deeds and this one from his bad deeds.” His good deeds, but if his good deeds run out before he has paid off his debt, some of their sins will be taken and placed on him, then he will be thrown into the Fire.” And “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if a man were killed in the cause of God, then brought back to life, then killed, then brought back to life, then killed, and he had a debt, he would not enter Paradise until it was paid off for him.” Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘The soul of the believer is suspended as long as he had a debt.’ Ahmad ibn Zuhayr said: Yahya ibn Ma’een was asked about this hadeeth and he said: It is saheeh. If it is said: This indicates that some of the martyrs will not enter Paradise from the time of their killing, and their souls will not be in the bodies of birds as you mentioned, nor will they be in their graves, so where will they be? We say: It has been narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: ‘The souls of the martyrs are on a river at the gate of Paradise called Barq, and their provision comes out to them from Paradise morning and evening. Perhaps they are these.’ And God knows best.” And for this reason Imam Abu Muhammad bin Atiyah said: And these are different classes and conditions, and they are united by the fact that they are provided for. And Imam Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Yazid bin Majah Al-Qazwini narrated in his Sunan, “On the authority of Salim bin Amir, who said: I heard Abu Umamah say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The martyr of the sea is like the martyrs of the land and the one who is drowning in his blood on land, and between the two waves is like the one who crosses the world in obedience to God. And God Almighty has assigned the Angel of Death to take the souls, except for the martyrs of the sea, for He, glory be to Him, takes charge of taking their souls, and forgives the martyr of the land all sins except debt, and forgives the martyr of the sea all sins and debt.” Seventh: The debt that prevents its owner from Paradise, and God knows best, is the debt that he left behind and did not bequeath, or was able to pay but did not pay, or he owed it extravagantly or foolishly and died without paying it. As for the one who owed a debt due to poverty and hardship and died without leaving behind payment, then God will not prevent him from Paradise, God willing, because it is obligatory upon the ruler to pay his debt, either from the charity, or from the share of the debtors, or from the spoils of war that are returned to the Muslims. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever leaves behind a debt or a loss, then it is upon God and His Messenger, and whoever leaves behind wealth, then it is for his heirs.’” We have added more clarification to this topic in the Book of Remembrance, and praise be to God. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: With their Lord they will be provided for. There is an omission in it of an added word, the meaning of which is with the honor of their Lord. And with implies the utmost closeness, so it is like with and therefore it is not made diminutive, so it is said! Stubborn, said Sibawayh, this is with him the dignity, not with him the distance and nearness, and they are provided with provision is the provision known in customs, and whoever said: it is the life of remembrance said: they are provided with beautiful praise, and the first is the truth, and it has been said: the souls perceive in that state in which they roam of the scents of Paradise and its goodness and its bliss and its joy what is appropriate for the souls, from what they are provided with and refreshed by, and as for the physical pleasures, then if those souls are returned to their bodies they will receive from the bliss all that God has prepared for them, and this is a good statement, and if there is a kind of metaphor in it, it is in accordance with what we have chosen, and the one who grants success is God, and Farheen is accusative in the place of the state of the implied in they are provided with provision, and Farheen is permissible in speech as an adjective for the living, and it is from joy in the sense of joy, and the virtue in this verse is the mentioned bliss, and Ibn al-Samiq read Farheen with an alif and they are two languages like farah and farah, and hazar and hadhar, and greed and greed, and miserliness and miserliness, al-Nahhas said: It is permissible to raise it in places other than the Qur’an, as an adjective for living things.
3:170: The Almighty said: And they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them meaning they have not yet joined them in virtue, even though they have virtue, and its origin is from the word bashara good report, because when a person rejoices, the effect of joy appears on his face. Al-Suddi said: The martyr is brought a book in which there is a mention of his brothers who will come to him, so he rejoices as the family of the absent one rejoices at his arrival in this world. Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, Al-Rabi' and others said: Their rejoicing is that they say: Our brothers whom we left behind us in this world are fighting in the way of God with their Prophet, so they are martyred and attain the same honor as we are, so they are happy and rejoice for them because of that. It was said: The reference to the rejoicing is for those who have not yet joined them to all the believers even if they were not killed, but when they witnessed the reward of God, they became certain that the religion of Islam is the truth for which God rewards, so they rejoice for themselves with what God has given them from His grace, rejoicing for the believers that there is no fear for them nor will they grieve. This meaning was adopted by Al-Zajjaj and Ibn Furak.
3:171: That is, with a paradise from God. It is also said: with forgiveness from God. And grace. This is for the sake of further clarification, and grace is included in the blessing, and in it is evidence of its vastness, and that it is not like the blessings of this world. It was said: grace came after the blessing for the sake of emphasis: Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Al-Miqdam bin Ma'dikarib who said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The martyr has six qualities with God." This is how it is in Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, six, "and they are seven in number: he is forgiven at the first moment, he is shown his seat in Paradise, he is protected from the torment of the grave, he is safe from the greatest terror, a crown of dignity is placed on his head, a ruby of which is better than the world and what is in it, he is married to seventy-two wives from the houris, and he intercedes for seventy of his relatives." He said: This is a good, authentic, strange hadith, and this is an explanation of the blessing and the grace, and the narrations in this meaning are many. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: Swords are the keys to Paradise. "It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: God, the Most High, has honored the martyrs with five honors that He has not honored any of the prophets with, not even me: One of them is that the Angel of Death took the souls of all the prophets, and he is the one who will take my soul. As for the martyrs, God is the One who takes their souls with His power as He wills, and the Angel of Death is not empowered over their souls. The second is that all the prophets... They were washed after death, and I am washed after death, and the martyrs are not washed and they have no need for the water of this world. The third is that all the prophets were shrouded, and I am shrouded, and the martyrs are not shrouded, but are buried in their clothes. The fourth is that when the prophets died, they were called dead, and when I die, it is said that he died, and the martyrs are not called dead. The fifth is that the prophets are given intercession on the Day of Resurrection, and my intercession is also on the Day of Resurrection. As for the martyrs, they intercede every day for those for whom they intercede.” The Almighty’s saying: And that God Al-Kisa’i read it with a kasra on the alif, and the rest with the accusative. So whoever reads with the accusative, its meaning is that they are happy with a blessing from God and are happy that God does not waste the reward of the believers. And whoever reads with the kasra, then it is based on the beginning, and its evidence is the reading of Ibn Mas’ud And God does not waste the reward of the believers.
3:172: The Almighty’s saying: Those who is in the nominative case as the subject, and its predicate is after the wounds had afflicted them. It is also possible that it is in the accusative case, in place of the believers, or of those who have not yet joined. “They responded” means they answered, and the sin and the ta’ are extra letters, and from this is His saying: No one responded to him at that time. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, he said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: Your father was among those who responded to God and the Messenger after they were afflicted with a wound. Muslim’s wording is from him on the authority of Aisha: O son of my sister, your parents, meaning al-Zubayr and Abu Bakr, were among those who responded to God and the Messenger after they were afflicted with a wound. She said: When the polytheists returned from Uhud and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions suffered what they suffered, he feared that they would return, so he said: Who will volunteer for these so that they may know that we have strength? Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr volunteered with seventy, so they went out in the footsteps of the people, and they heard about them and returned with a blessing and grace from God. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, referred to what happened in the Battle of Hamra al-Asad, which is about eight miles from Madinah. And when it was Sunday, which was the second day of Uhud, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out to the people to follow the polytheists, and he said: No one should go out with us except those who witnessed it yesterday. So two hundred men of the believers rose up with him, in Bukhari, and he said: Who will go after them? So seventy men volunteered from among them. He said: Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr were among them, as mentioned above, until he reached Hamra al-Asad, terrifying the enemy. And perhaps among them was one who was burdened with wounds and could not walk and could not find a mount, so perhaps he would be carried on the shoulders, and all of that was in compliance with the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a desire for jihad. It was said: The verse was revealed about two men from Banu Abd al-Ashhal who were severely wounded, one of them leaning on the other, and they went out with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they reached Hamra al-Asad, Nu`aym ibn Mas`ud met them and informed them that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those with him from Quraysh had gathered their forces and agreed to come to Medina and exterminate its people. They said what God has told us about them: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. While Quraysh had agreed on that, Ma`bad al-Khuza`i came to them: Khuza'ah were allies of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he advised him. He had seen the condition of the Prophet's companions and what they were like. When he saw the Quraysh's determination to return to exterminate the people of Medina, he was overcome by fear of that, and he sincerely advised the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, but he feared the Quraysh by saying to them: I have left Muhammad and his companions at Hamra' al-Asad with a great army, and those who had stayed behind have gathered around it, and they have burned for you, so escape, escape! For I forbid you from that, and by God, what I saw made me say some verses of poetry about it. He said: What did you say? He said: I said: My camel was almost knocked down by the sounds as the ground was covered with the locusts. Dress up like a noble lion, do not be rude when meeting, nor do you lean towards the isolated ones. I remained an enemy, I think the earth is tilted towards what they called a leader who will not be disappointed I said, Woe to Ibn Harb from meeting you when the plain is covered with horses. I am a warner to the people of valor, a warning to every one of them who has a desire and a sense. From the army of Ahmed, do not be afraid of his bombs, and what you warned about cannot be described in words. He said: This made Abu Sufyan and those with him afraid, and God cast terror into their hearts, and they returned to Mecca in fear and haste, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned with his companions to Medina victorious, as God Almighty said: So they returned with favor and bounty from God, no harm touched them, meaning fighting and terror. Jabir ibn Abdullah asked permission from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to go out with him, and he gave him permission, and God Almighty informed them that a great reward had been obtained for them with this return. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that it was a raid. This is the interpretation of the majority of scholars for this verse. Mujahid and Ikrimah, may God have mercy on them, deviated and said: This verse is from His statement: Those to whom the people said to His statement: Great. It was revealed about the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) going out to Badr al-Sughra, and that was because he went out to meet Abu Sufyan at Uhud, when he said: Our meeting is at Badr next year. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Say yes. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out before Badr, and there was a great market there. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave his companions dirhams, and he approached Badr when Nu’aym ibn Mas’ud al-Ashja’i came to him and informed him that the Quraysh had gathered and were coming to fight him and those who joined them. The Muslims were afraid of that, but they said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. So they persisted until they came to Badr, but they did not find anyone. They found the market and bought leather and merchandise with their dirhams, and they returned without encountering any plot, and they made a profit in their trade. That is what God the Almighty said: And they returned with favor and bounty from God. That is, bounty in those trades, and God knows best.
3:173: There is a difference of opinion regarding the Almighty’s statement: Those to whom the people said, Mujahid, Muqatil, Ikrimah, and Al-Kalbi said: He is Na’im bin Mas’ud Al-Ashja’i, and the wording is general but its meaning is specific, like His statement: Or do they envy the people, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Suddi: He is a Bedouin who was given a reward for that. Ibn Ishaq and a group said: He means by the people the caravan of Abd Al-Qais, who passed by Abu Sufyan and he sent them to the Muslims to discourage them. It was said: The people here are the hypocrites. Al-Suddi said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions prepared to march to Badr Al-Sughra for the appointment with Abu Sufyan. The hypocrites came to them and said: We are your companions who forbade you from going out to them and you disobeyed us, and they fought you in your homes and were victorious, so if you come to them in their homes, then no one among you will return. They said: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Abu Ma’shar said: Some people from Hudhayl from the people of Tihamah entered Medina, so the companions asked them The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, said: They have gathered against you large groups, so fear them, meaning fear them and beware of them, for you will not be able to withstand them. So the people are according to these sayings on the same level of gathering, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: So He increased them in faith meaning, the people’s words increased their faith, meaning belief and certainty in their religion, and steadfastness in supporting them, and strength, courage and readiness. So the increase in faith in this regard is in deeds. The scholars have differed regarding the increase and decrease of faith in statements, and the belief in this is that faith itself, which is a single crown, and a single belief in something, is only an individual meaning, with which no increase enters if it occurs, and nothing remains of it if it disappears. So nothing remains except that the increase and decrease are in its attachments and not its essence. So a group of scholars went to the view that it increases and decreases in terms of the deeds that emanate from it, especially since many scholars apply the name of faith to acts of obedience, based on the saying of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): Faith has seventy-odd chapters, the highest of which is the statement, ‘There is no god but God,’ and the lowest of which is removing something harmful from the road. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi. Muslim added, And modesty is a branch of faith. And in the hadith of Ali may God be pleased with him, faith appears as a white spot in the heart, and whenever faith increases, the spot increases. And his saying ( Al-Asma`i said: Al-Lamza is like a dot and similar whiteness, and from it it is said: a horse of Al-Maz, if there is some whiteness in its hooves, and the modernists say (Lamza) with the fat-ha, but as for the speech of the Arabs, it is with the damma, like Shubah, Dahmah, and Khumrah, and in it is an argument against those who deny that faith increases and decreases, do you not see him say: whenever faith increases, the lamza increases until the whole heart turns white, and likewise hypocrisy appears as a black lamza in the heart whenever hypocrisy increases, the heart turns black until the whole heart turns black, and among them is he who said: faith is an accident, and it does not remain for two times, so it is for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and for the righteous, it is successive, so it increases in consideration of the succession of its likes in the heart of the believer, and in consideration of the continuity of its presence, and it decreases in consideration of the succession of heedlessness in the heart of the believer, Abu Al-Ma`ali indicated this, and this meaning is found in the hadith of intercession, the hadith of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri narrated by Muslim, and in it: “The believers will say, O our Lord, our brothers used to fast, pray, and perform Hajj, and it will be said to them, ‘Come out of You have known that their images are forbidden to the Fire. They will bring out a large number of people, the Fire having taken up half of their legs and up to their knees. Then they will say, “Our Lord, there is no one left in it of those whom You have commanded us to have.” He will say, “Go back. Whoever you find in his heart the weight of a dinar of goodness, bring him out.” They will bring out a large number of people. Then they will say, Our Lord, we have not left in it anyone of those whom You have commanded us. Then He will say, “Go back. Whoever you find in his heart the weight of half a dinar of goodness, bring him out.” They will bring out a large number of people. Then they will say, Our Lord, we have not left in it anyone of those whom You have commanded us. Then He will say, “Go back. Whoever you find in his heart the weight of an atom of goodness, bring him out.” And he mentioned the hadith. It has been said that what is meant by faith in this hadith are the deeds of the heart, such as intention, sincerity, fear, advice, and the like. He called it faith because it is in the place of faith, or he meant faith, according to the custom of the Arabs in naming a thing by its name if it is adjacent to it, or was due to it. Evidence for this interpretation is the statement of the Shafi’is after bringing out whoever had in his heart the weight of an atom of goodness: We have not left in it any good. Although the Almighty will bring out after that large groups. Whoever says there is no god but God, and they are certainly believers, and if they were not believers, He would not have expelled them. Then the non-existence of the first existence upon which the example is based was neither an increase nor a decrease, and that was measured in the movement, for if God, the Exalted, created a single knowledge and created with it its like or its likes with information, then His knowledge has increased. If God annihilated the likes, then it has decreased, meaning the increase has disappeared. Likewise, if He created a movement and created with it its like or its likes. A group of scholars went to the view that the increase and decrease of faith is only through evidence, so the evidence increases according to one, and it is said in that: It is an increase in faith, and in this sense according to one of the opinions, the superiority of the prophets over creation, for they taught it in many ways, more than the ways in which creation taught it. This opinion is outside the meaning of the verse, since it is not conceivable that the increase in it is from the side of evidence. A group went to the view that the increase in faith is only through the revelation of the obligations and report during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in knowledge of them after ignorance for a long time, and this is only an increase in faith, so the statement in it that faith increases is a metaphorical statement, and a decrease in it is not conceivable. This limit, but it is only conceivable in addition to the one who knows, so know. God Almighty says: And they said, ‘God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’ That is, God is sufficient for us. Hasab is derived from ihsab, which means sufficiency. The poet said: Fill our house with cheese and butter, and you are rich enough to satisfy and quench your thirst. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said regarding the Almighty’s statement: Those to whom the people said, ‘The people have gathered against you,’ until His statement: And they said, ‘Sufficient for us is God, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.’ This was said by Abraham, peace be upon him, when he was thrown into the fire, and it was said by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the people said to them, The people have gathered against you, and God knows best.
3:174: Our scholars said: When they entrusted their affairs to Him and relied on Him with their hearts, He gave them four meanings of reward: grace, favor, averting evil, and following contentment, so He pleased them with Him and He was pleased with them.
3:175: Ibn Abbas and others said: The meaning is that He frightens you with His allies, that is, with His allies, or from His allies, so the preposition was deleted and the verb was connected to the noun and was made accusative, as God Almighty said: To warn of a severe punishment, that is, to warn you of a severe punishment, that is, to frighten the believer with the disbeliever. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: The meaning is that He frightens His allies, the hypocrites, so that they refrain from fighting the polytheists. As for God’s allies, they do not fear Him when He frightens them. It has been said that what is meant by this one who frightens you is a devil from among the devils of mankind, either Nu’aym ibn Mas’ud or someone else, based on the disagreement on that as mentioned above. So do not fear them, that is, do not fear the disbelievers mentioned in His statement: Indeed, the people have gathered against you, that is, it refers to the allies. If you say: The meaning is that He frightens with His allies, that is, He frightens you with His allies. God Almighty says: And fearful meaning fearful of abandoning My command if you are to believe in My promise. Fear in the speech of the Arabs means panic. So-and-so made me fear him, meaning I was more afraid of him. Fearful is a desert without water. It is said: a she-camel is fearful, meaning a mangy one. Fear is like a leather bag in which honey is bought. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Some of the truthful ones gathered with Abraham the Friend and said: What is fear? He said: Do not feel safe until you reach safety. Sahl said: Whenever Al-Rabi’ bin Khathim passed by Bakir, he would faint. Ali bin Abi Talib was told about that, so he said: If that happens to him, inform me. So he happened to him, so inform him. He came to him and put his hand in his shirt and found that he was moving a lot, so he said: I bear witness that this is the most fearful of the people of your time. The one who fears God Almighty is the one who fears that He will punish him either in this world or in the Hereafter. For this reason it was said: The one who fears is not the one who cries and wipes his eyes, but the one who fears is the one who leaves what he fears will be punished for. So God Almighty imposed on His servants to fear Him, so He said: And fear, if you are believers. And He said: And fear Me. And He praised the believers for fear, so He said: They fear their Lord above them. (al-Nahl 16:50) And the masters of signs about fear have expressions that refer to what we mentioned. Professor Abu Ali Al-Daqqaq said: I entered upon Abu Bakr bin Furak, may God have mercy on him, to visit him, and when he saw me, his eyes teared up, so I said to him: God May God heal you and cure you. He said to me: Do you think that I fear death? I only fear what is beyond death. In Sunan Ibn Majah, on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I see what you do not see and hear what you do not hear. The heaven groans, and it has every right to groan. There is not in it the space of four fingers but there is an angel prostrating his forehead to God. By God, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much, and you would not take pleasure in women on the beds, and you would go out to the high places, beseeching God. By God, I would wish that I were a tree that is being cut down.’” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, who said: A hasan ghareeb hadith. It is narrated from other sources that Abu Dharr said: I would wish that I were a tree that is being cut down. And God knows best.
3:176: The Almighty said: And let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. These are people who converted to Islam and then apostatized out of fear of the polytheists, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distressed, so God Almighty revealed: And let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. Al-Kalbi said: He meant by it the hypocrites and the leaders of the Jews, they concealed the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Book, so it was revealed.
