It is said: When the People of the Book did not believe, that was difficult for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because people would look at them and say that they were People of the Book, so if it were true they would have followed him, so it was revealed: And let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you. The reading of Nafi' is with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the zay wherever it occurred except in Al-Anbiya': The greatest terror will not grieve them (Al-Anbiya': 103), for it is with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the zay, and Abu Ja'far is the opposite, and Ibn Muhaisin read it all with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the zay, and the rest all with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the zay, and they are two languages: The matter saddened me, it saddened me, and it also saddened me, and it is a rare language, and the first is the more eloquent of the two languages, said Al-Nahhas, and the poet said: In I sadden: My friends have passed away and my home has made me sad The general reading is yusara'un and Talhah read yusara'un fi al-kufr. Ad-Dahhak said: They are the infidels of Quraysh. Another said: They are the hypocrites. It was said: It is what we mentioned before. It was said: It is general for all infidels, and their hastening in disbelief is supporting Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qushayri said: And grief over the disbelief of the infidel is obedience, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was excessive in grief over the disbelief of his people, so he was forbidden from that, as he said: So do not waste your soul over them in regret. And he said: Perhaps you will kill yourself over their traces if they do not believe in this hadith out of grief. “They will never harm God at all,” meaning they will never decrease God’s kingdom and authority at all, meaning that it will never decrease because of their disbelief. As narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he narrated on the authority of God, the Blessed and Exalted, that He said: O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden amongst you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, all of you are astray except for those I have guided, so seek guidance from Me and I will guide you. O My servants, all of you are hungry except for those I have fed, so seek food from Me and I will feed you. O My servants, all of you are naked except for those I have clothed, so seek clothing from Me and I will clothe you. O My servants, you sin by night and by day, and I forgive all sins, so seek forgiveness from Me and I will forgive you. O My servants, you will never attain harm by which you harm Me, nor will you attain benefit by which you benefit Me. O My servants, if the first and last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as pious as the most wicked heart of any man among you, that would not increase My kingdom at all. O My servants, if the first and last of you, your humans and your jinn, were as wicked as the most wicked.” “The heart of one man, that would not decrease My kingdom in the least. O My servants, were the first of you and the last of you, the humans of you and the jinn of you, to stand on one plain and ask of Me, and I were to give each person what he asked for, that would not decrease what I have any more than a needle decreases the sea if put into it. O My servants, it is only your deeds that I count for you and then recompense you for. So whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.” Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, and by al-Tirmidhi and others. It is a great hadith that is too long to be written in its entirety. It was said that the meaning of they will not harm God in the least is that they will not harm the friends of God when they abandon their support, since God, the Almighty and Majestic, is their supporter. God the Almighty says: God intends not to give them any share in the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment. That is, a portion. A portion is a share and a fortune. It is said: So-and-so is more fortunate than so-and-so, and he is fortunate. The plural of fortune is ahaaz, not in analogy. Abu Zayd said: It is said that a man is fortunate, meaning new, if he has a share of sustenance. And I was fortunate in a matter, and the plural of fortune is ahaaz, meaning He does not give them a share in Paradise. This is a text indicating that good and evil are by the will of God the Almighty.
3:177: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who have purchased disbelief in exchange for faith was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah, will never harm God at all was repeated for emphasis. It was said: that is, from his bad management, replacing faith with disbelief and selling it with it, so he does not fear its side or its management. A thing was in the accusative case in both places because it is in the position of a source, as if he said: they will never harm God, a little or a lot of harm. It is permissible to make it in the accusative case if the ba is omitted, as if he said: they will never harm God at all.
3:178: God the Almighty said: And let not those who disbelieve think that Our granting them respite is better for themselves. Granting them respite means a long life and a comfortable life. The meaning is: These people who frighten the Muslims should not think that God is able to destroy them. Rather, He extends their lives so that they commit sins, not because it is better for them. It is said: We grant them respite because of the victory they achieved on the Day of Uhud. That was not good for them, but rather it was so that they would be punished more. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that he said: There is no one, righteous or wicked, except that death is better for him, because if he is righteous, God the Almighty said: And what is with God is better for the righteous. And if he is wicked, God the Almighty said: We grant them respite only so that they may increase in sin. Ibn `Amir and `Asim read and do not think with a ya' and a fat-ha on the seen. Hamza read it with a ta' and a fat-ha on the seen. The rest read it with a ya' and a kasra on the seen. Whoever reads it with a ya', then those who do so are the doers., that is, let not the disbelievers think, that Our granting them respite is better for themselves is a substitute for the two objects, and ma means who, and the pronoun is omitted, and khayr is the predicate of an and it is permissible to estimate ma and the verb as a source, and the estimate is that those who disbelieve should not think that Our granting them respite is better for themselves, and whoever reads with the ta’, then the subject is the one addressed, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and alladhina is in the accusative case as the first object of tahsab, and that and what follows it is a substitute for alladhina, and it replaces the two objects, as it would if it were not a substitute, and it is not appropriate for an and what follows it to be a second object of tahsab, because the second object in this chapter is the first in meaning, because hasab and its sisters are included in the subject and predicate, so the estimate is: and do not think that Our granting them respite is better, this is what al-Zajjaj said. Abu Ali said: If this was correct, he would have said khayr in the accusative case, because an becomes a substitute for alladhina al-disbelievers, so it is as if he said: Do not think that the granting of respite to those They disbelieved in good, so his saying: report is the second object of hasab, so it is not permissible to read la tahsabna with a taa’ unless the kasra in in anma makes khayrān accusative, and this was not narrated from Hamza, and the reading from Hamza is with a taa’, so this reading is not correct, and al-Farra’ and al-Kisa’i said: Hamza’s reading is permissible on repetition, its meaning is do not think those who disbelieve, and do not think that what we extend to them is good, an is corrupted as the place of the two objects of la hasab the second, and it and what it worked as a second object of la hasab the first, al-Qushayri said, and this is close to what al-Zajjaj mentioned in the claim of substitution, and the reading is correct, so Abu Ali intended to mislead al-Zajjaj, al-Nahhas said: Abu Hatim claimed that Hamza’s reading with a taa’ here, and his saying: and do not think those who are stingy is a mistake that is not permissible, and a group followed him in that. I said: This is nothing, because of what was previously explained regarding the grammar, and because of the correctness of the reading and its confirmation by transmission. Yahya bin Waththab read innama namli lihum with a kasra on the inn in both of them. Abu Ja`far said: Yahya’s reading is good, as you say: I thought that Umar, his father Khalid, Abu Hatim said: I heard Al-Akhfash mention the kasra on inn as evidence for the people of destiny, because he was one of them, and he makes it an example of precedence and delay (and let not those who disbelieve think that We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin. We only grant them respite that is better for themselves) He said: And I saw in a copy of the Qur’an in the congregational mosque that they had added a letter to it, so it became innama namli lihum fiman so Ya`qub the reader looked at it and saw the mistake, so he erased it. The verse is a text in the invalidity of the doctrine of the Qadarites, because he informed us that He extends their lives so that they may increase in disbelief by committing sins, and the succession of similar things in the heart, as was previously explained regarding its opposite, which is faith. And from Ibn Abbas, he said: There is no righteousness nor… A wicked person is not to be blamed for his sins, but death is better for him. Then he recited: We only grant them respite so that they may increase in sin. And he recited: What is with God is better for the righteous. Narrated by Razin.
3:179: Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The believers asked to be given a sign by which they could differentiate between a believer and a hypocrite, so God the Almighty revealed: God would never leave the believers in the state you are in, and they differed as to who was addressed by the verse. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Muqatil, Al-Kalbi and most of the commentators said: The address is to the disbelievers and hypocrites, meaning God would never leave the believers in the state you are in of disbelief, hypocrisy and enmity towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Kalbi said: The Quraysh of Mecca said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: A man from among us you claim is in Hell, and if he abandons our religion and follows your religion you say he is from the people of Paradise! So tell us about this, where is he from? And tell us who from among us comes to you? And who does not come to you? God the Almighty revealed: God would not leave the believers in the state you are upon of disbelief and hypocrisy, until He distinguishes the wicked from the good. It was said that this is addressed to the polytheists, and what is meant by the believers in His statement: to leave the believers are those in the loins and wombs who believe, meaning that God would not leave your children whom He has decreed to believe in the state you are upon of polytheism, until He separates you from them. Based on this, and God would not inform you is a new statement, and this is the opinion of Ibn Abbas and most of the commentators. It was said that the address is to the believers, until He distinguishes between you through the trial and the assignment, so that you recognize the wicked hypocrite and the good believer. On the Day of Uhud, He distinguished between the two groups, and this is the opinion of most of the scholars of meanings. and God would not inform you of the unseen, O group of believers, meaning that God would not appoint the hypocrites for you until you recognize them, but He makes that clear to you through the assignment and the trial, and that became clear on the Day of Uhud, for the hypocrites stayed behind and showed gloating, so you did not know this unseen before this, but now it has become clear. God informed Muhammad, peace be upon him, and his companions of that. It was said: The meaning of to inform you is that God would not have informed you of what would happen from them. So his saying: And God would not have informed you of the unseen is connected according to this, and according to the first two sayings it is disconnected. That is because when the infidels said: Why was there no revelation to us? He said: And God would not inform you of the unseen, that is, of those who deserve prophethood, until the revelation is by your choice. But God selects, that is, chooses, from among His messengers to inform of His unseen, whoever He wills. It is said: I looked at such-and-such, and I informed others about it. It is intransitive and transitive. It was read hatta yamayz with a shaddah from maiz, and likewise in al-Anfal, and it is the reading of Hamza. The rest yamayz with a light shaddah from maza yamayz. It is said: I distinguished something some of it from some other, I distinguish it, and I distinguished it with a distinction. Abu Muadh said: I distinguished something, I distinguish it with a distinction, if you separate between two things. If they are things, you say: I distinguished them with a distinction. And similarly, if you make one thing into two things, you say: I separated between them, with a light shaddah, and from this is the parting of poetry. If you make it things, you say: I separated it with a distinction. I said: And from it the people were distinguished, some of them were distinguished from others, and almost distinguished: they were torn apart, and with this the saying of God Almighty was interpreted: You almost burst with rage (al-Mulk 67:8), and in the hadith: Whoever removes something harmful from the road, it is charity for him. God the Almighty says: So believe in God and His Messenger. It is said that when the infidels asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to clarify to them who among them would believe, God revealed: So believe in God and His Messenger. That is, do not occupy yourself with what does not concern you, but occupy yourself with what concerns you, which is belief. So believe, that is, you must believe, not long for knowledge of the unseen. And if you believe and fear God, then for you is a great reward, that is, Paradise. It is mentioned that a man was an astrologer with Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf Al-Thaqafi. Al-Hajjaj took pebbles in his hand, and he knew their number, so he said to the astrologer: How many are in my hand? So he counted and the astrologer got it right. Al-Hajjaj ignored him and took pebbles that he had not counted, so he said to the astrologer: How many are in my hand? So he counted and got it wrong. Then he counted again and got it wrong. So he said: O prince, I think you do not know the number of what is in your hand? He said: No. He said: So what is the difference between them? He said: I counted that and it went beyond the limits of the unseen, so I calculated and was correct. But this, you did not know its number, so it became unseen, and no one knows the unseen except God Almighty. This chapter will come in the livestock, God Almighty willing.
3:180: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And let not those who who is in the nominative case, and the first object is omitted. Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, and Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is that miserliness is good for them, meaning that the misers should not think that miserliness is good for them. It was only omitted because they are miserly indicates miserliness, and it is like his saying: Whoever is truthful, it is better for him, meaning that truthfulness is better for him. And from this is the saying of the poet: If a fool is forbidden, he will run after it and disobey, and the fool will go after disobedience. The meaning is: He led to foolishness, so foolishness indicates foolishness. As for Hamza’s reading with the letter ta’, it is very far-fetched. An-Nahhas said: It is permissible for it to be interpreted as: Do not think that the stinginess of those who are stingy is good for them. Al-Zajjaj said: It is like And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82), and huwa in his saying: huwa khayran lahim is a separator according to the Basrans, and it is the pillar according to the Kufians. An-Nahhas said: It is permissible in Arabic to say huwa khayran lahim as a subject and a predicate. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Rather, it is worse for them is the subject and predicate, meaning miserliness is worse for them, and the seen in saytooqoon is the seen of the threat, meaning they will be surrounded, said Al-Mubarrad, and this verse was revealed about miserliness with money and spending in the way of God, and paying the obligatory zakat, and this is like His saying: And they do not spend it in the way of God, a group of interpreters went to this, including Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas, Abu Wa’il, Abu Malik, Al-Suddi, and Al-Sha’bi, they said: The meaning of they will be surrounded by what they were stingy with is what was mentioned in the hadith on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, he said: Whoever God gives wealth and he does not pay its zakat, it will be likened to him on the Day of Resurrection to a bald-headed snake with two tufts, which will encircle him on the Day of Resurrection, then seize him by the two sides and say, ‘I am your wealth, I am your treasure.’ Then he recited this verse: “And let not those who are miserly think,” narrated by Al-Nasa’i, and narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Ibn Masoud, “on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, he said: There is no one who does not pay “Whoever pays the Zakat of his wealth, he will be given a bald-headed, scorpion-like figure on the Day of Resurrection, until it is placed around his neck.” Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to us the proof of this from the Book of God Almighty: And let not those who are stingy with what God has given them of His bounty think. It was narrated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “There is no relative who comes to his relative and asks him for some of the bounty he has, and he is stingy with it, except that a scorpion will be brought out for him on the Day of Resurrection from the Fire, licking his lips until it encircles him.” Ibn Abbas also said: It was revealed about the People of the Book and their stinginess, explaining what they knew about the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was said by Mujahid and a group of scholars. The meaning of they will be encircled according to this interpretation is that they will bear the punishment for what they were stingy with, so it is from the word capacity as God Almighty said: And upon those who are able to bear it (al-Baqarah 2:184), and it is not from the word encircling. Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: The meaning of they will be encircled is that a collar of fire will be placed for them on the Day of Resurrection. This is consistent with the first interpretation, i.e. the statement of al-Suddi. It was also said: They will be bound by their deeds as The collar is attached to the neck. It is said: So-and-so tied his work to the collar of a dove, meaning he bound his work. God Almighty said: And every man We have fastened his bird to his neck (al-Isra’ 17:13). From this meaning is the saying of Abdullah bin Jahsh to Abu Sufyan: Tell Abu Sufyan about a matter that will lead to regret. I sold your cousin's house to pay the fine on your behalf. Your ally is God, the Lord of mankind, the diligent Qassam Go with her, go with her, I put a dove's necklace around her This is consistent with the second interpretation. Stinginess and miserliness in the language means that a person prevents a right that is due to him. As for the one who prevents what is not due to him, he is not miserly, because he is not blamed for that. The people of Hijaz say: they are miserly, and they were miserly. The rest of the Arabs say: they were miserly, they are miserly. An-Nahhas narrated it. And miserliness means miserliness and miserliness, on the authority of Ibn Faris. Third: In the fruit of miserliness and its benefit, which is what was narrated: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Ansar: Who is your master? They said: Al-Jadd bin Qais, despite his miserliness. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What disease is worse than miserliness? They said: How is that, O Messenger of God? He said: A people settled on the coast of the sea and, due to their miserliness, they hated for guests to stay with them, so they said: Let the men among us stay away from the women, so that the men will apologize to the guests for the distance of the women, and the women will apologize for the distance of the men. So they did and it lasted a long time, so the men were busy with the men and the women with the women.” Al-Mawardi mentioned it in the book Adab al-Dunya wa al-Din, and God knows best. Fourth: There is a difference of opinion regarding miserliness and stinginess, whether they have one meaning or two. It was said: Stinginess is refraining from giving what you have, and stinginess is eagerness to obtain what you do not have. It was also said that stinginess is miserliness with eagerness, and this is correct, because Muslim narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection, and beware of stinginess, for stinginess destroyed those who came before you, for it led them to shed each other’s blood and make permissible what is forbidden. ’ This refutes the statement of those who said: Stinginess prevents what is obligatory, and stinginess prevents what is recommended, because if stinginess prevented what is recommended, it would not have come under this great threat and severe blame that leads to the destruction of this world and the Hereafter. This meaning is supported by what al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, ‘The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The dust of the path of God and the smoke of Hell will never come together in the nostrils of a Muslim man, and stinginess and faith will never come together in the heart of a Muslim man. ’” This indicates that stinginess is more severely blamed than Stinginess, except that what has come indicates their equality, which is his saying: And he was asked: Can a believer be stingy? He said: No. And Al-Mawardi mentioned in the book Adab Al-Dunya Wa Al-Din “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Ansar: Who is your master? They said: Al-Jadd bin Qais, despite his stinginess,” and it has been mentioned before. God the Almighty says: And to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth. God the Almighty informed us of His permanence and the permanence of His kingdom, and that He is eternal as He is in eternity, independent of the worlds. He inherits the earth after His creation perishes and their possessions disappear, so the possessions and wealth remain unclaimed. This is the course of inheritance in the custom of creation, but this is not inheritance in reality, because the inheritor in reality is the one who inherits something that was not his before. God the Almighty is the owner of the heavens and the earth, and what is between them. The heavens and what is in them, and the earth and what is in them, belong to Him. The wealth was a loan to its owners, so when they died, the loan was returned to its owner who originally had it. Similar to this verse is God the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it (Maryam 19:40). The meaning of the two verses is that God the Almighty commanded His servants to spend and not be stingy before they die and to leave that as an inheritance for God the Almighty, and nothing will benefit them except what they spend.
3:181: The Almighty said: God has certainly heard the statement of those who say, 'God is poor and we are rich.' God mentioned the ugly statement of the infidels, especially the Jews. The commentators said, when God revealed, Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? some of the Jews, including Huyayy ibn Akhtab, said, according to Al-Hasan, and Ikrimah and others said: He is Phinehas ibn Azura, "God is poor and we are rich. He borrows from us." They only said this to deceive their weak ones, not because they believe this, because they are People of the Book. Rather, they disbelieved by this statement because they wanted to cast doubt on the weak ones among them and the believers, and to deny the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that he is poor according to what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, because he borrowed from us. We will write down what they said, We will reward them for it, and it was said: We will write it in their records of deeds, meaning We will command the guardians to confirm their statement so that they will read it on the Day of Resurrection in their books that they will be given, so that it will be more conclusive as evidence against them. This is like His statement: And indeed, We are its scribes. It was said: The purpose of writing is to preserve, i.e. We will preserve what they said so that we may reward them. And in His statement what they said is in the accusative case with We will write. Al-A’mash and Hamza read sayyaktub with a ya’, so what is the name of what its agent is not named, and this is considered by the reading of Ibn Mas’ud: And it will be said, Taste the punishment of the burning fire. The Almighty said: And their killing of the prophets without right. That is, We write their killing of the prophets, that is, their approval of the killing, and what is meant is the killing of their prophet ancestors, but since they were satisfied with that, the attribution to them was valid. And a man was considered good by Al-Sha’bi for killing Uthman, may God be pleased with him, so Al-Sha’bi said to him, You have shared in his blood, so he made the approval of the killing a killing, may God be pleased with him. I said: This is a major issue, where being pleased with a sin is a sin. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Al-Aras bin Umaira Al-Kindi, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a sin is committed on earth, then whoever witnesses it, thinks about it and says it once and denies it is like someone who was absent from it, and whoever is absent from it and approves of it is like someone who witnessed it.” This is the text of the Almighty’s statement: Unjustly. The meaning of this was presented in Surat Al-Baqarah. And We will say, ‘Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire.’ That is, it will be said to them in Hell, or at death, or at the reckoning. This is what this statement is from God Almighty, or from the angels. There are two opinions. Ibn Masoud’s reading is and it is said and the burning is the name of the blazing fire, and the fire includes the blazing and the non-blazing.
3:182: The Almighty’s saying: That is because of what your hands have put forth meaning that this punishment is for the sins that have gone before. He specifically mentioned the hands to indicate that they are in charge of the action and are directly involved in it, as the action may be attributed to a person in the sense that he is commanded to do it, like His saying: They slaughter their sons (al-Qasas 28:4). The root of your hands is your hands, so the damma was deleted because of its heaviness, and God knows best.
3:183: The Almighty’s saying: those who is in the accusative case instead of those who in the Almighty’s saying: God has heard the statement of those who said or an attribute of the servants or a predicate of the beginning, meaning they are the ones who said. Al-Kalbi and others said: It was revealed about Ka`b ibn al-Ashraf, Malik ibn al-Sayf, Wahb ibn Judah, Phinehas ibn Azura and a group who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: Do you claim that God sent you to us, and that He sent down to us a book in which He commanded us not to believe in a messenger who claims to be from God until he brings us a sacrifice that is consumed by fire? If you bring it to us, we will believe you. So God revealed this verse. It was said: This was in the Torah, but the full statement was: Until the Messiah and Muhammad come to you. So when they come to you, believe in them without a sacrifice. And it was said: The matter of the sacrifices was established until it was abrogated by the tongue of Jesus, son of Mary. And the prophet among them would slaughter and supplicate, and a white fire would descend with a roar and a rustle without smoke, and it would consume the sacrifice. So this statement was a claim of the Jews, since there was an exception, so they concealed it, or it was abrogated. So they were stubborn in their adherence to it. The miracles of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, are conclusive evidence in invalidating their claim, as are the miracles of Jesus. And whoever must be believed must be believed. Verifying it, then the Almighty said to establish the argument against them: Say O Muhammad, Messengers have come to you O group of Jews: With clear proofs and with what you have said of the sacrifice So why did you kill them if you should be truthful meaning Zachariah, John, and Isaiah, and all of the prophets who were killed, peace be upon them, and you did not believe in them, he meant their ancestors, and this is the verse that was recited by Aamer Al-Sha’bi, may God be pleased with him, so he used it as evidence against the one who approved of the killing of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, as we have explained, and that God Almighty called the Jews killers because of their satisfaction with the actions of their ancestors, even though there were about seven hundred years between them, and the sacrifice is what one draws closer to God Almighty through rituals, charity, and good deeds, and it is a verb from the word qurbah, and it can be a noun and a verbal noun, so an example of the noun is sultan and proof, and the verbal noun is adwan and khusran, and Isa bin Omar used to read bi-qurban with a damma on the ra’ following the damma on the qaf, as was said in the plural of thulmah: thulmah and in hujrah: hujrat.
3:184: God Almighty said, consoling and comforting His Prophet: If they deny you, then messengers before you were denied who came with clear proofs meaning with evidence and the scriptures meaning the written books. The scriptures are the plural of Zabur, which means book, and its origin is from Zabart, which means I wrote, and every Zabur is a book. Imru’ al-Qais said: For whom I saw him, he made me sad like the lines of a psalm on a Yemeni palm branch I know my writing, and it was said: The Psalms are from the word Zabar meaning to warn, and Zabart the man means to rebuke him, and Zabart the well means to cover it with stones, and Ibn Amir read and with the Zabar and with the illuminating book with an addition of ba in both words, and this is how it is in the copies of the Mushafs of the people of Ash-Sham, and the illuminating book means the clear and shining, from your saying: I illuminated the thing, I illuminated it meaning I made it clear, it is said: He lit the thing and He illuminated it and He illuminated it and He illuminated it have the same meaning, and each one of them is intransitive and transitive, and he combined the word Zabar and the book and they have the same meaning because of the difference in their wording, and their origin is as we mentioned.
3:185: It contains seven issues: The first: When God Almighty informed about the misers and their disbelief in their saying: Indeed, God is poor and we are rich, and He commanded the believers to be patient with their harm in His saying You will surely be tested the verse, He made clear that this is something that will pass away and will not last, for the life of this world is near, and the Day of Resurrection is the Day of Judgment, the taste of death is from the taste, and this is something that there is no escape from for man, and no escape from which for an animal. Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: He who does not die in vain will die old. Death is a cup and a person will taste it. Another said: Death is a door and all people enter it. I wonder what the home is after the door. The second: The reading of the common al-Nas 114:the taste of death with the addition, and Al-A’mash, Yahya, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read the taste of death with the tanween and the accusative of death, they said: because she has not tasted it yet, and that is because the active participle is of two types: one of them is that it has the meaning of the past, and the second is the meaning of the future, so if you want the first, then there is nothing in it except the addition to what comes after it, like your saying: this is the striker of Zaid yesterday, and the killer of Bakr yesterday, because it is like a static noun which is a proper noun, like the servant of Zaid, and the companion of Bakr, the poet said: The guardians of the tribe's shame, no one can approach them from behind them. If you want the second, then the accusative and tanween are permissible in this way, and this is the rule, because it runs the course of the present tense verb. If the verb is intransitive, then it is not transitive, like Zayd is standing. If it is transitive, then you make it transitive and accusative with it, so you say: Zayd is hitting ‘Amr, meaning he is hitting ‘Amr. And it is permissible to delete the tanween and the addition for the sake of lightness, as Al-Marar said: Ask the carefree person about all those who give their heads, whether they are successful, mixed with miserable people. A murderer, his neck is hanging from the shoulder of the saddle of the mount, Arandas The tanween was deleted for the sake of brevity. The original is: He raised his head with the tanween and the accusative. An example of this is also in the revelation, the Almighty’s saying: Are they removers of his distress? (al-Zumar 39:38), and what is similar to it. Third: Then know that death has causes and signs. One of the signs of the death of a believer is sweat on the forehead. An-Nasa’i narrated it from “the hadith of Buraydah who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The believer dies with sweat on the forehead.” We have explained it in At-Tadhkirah. So when he is dying, he is taught the Shahada, based on his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Teach your dead ‘There is no god but God’ so that it will be his last words, and he will conclude with the Shahada, and it will not be repeated to him so that he will not become bored. It is recommended to recite Yasin at that time, based on his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Recite Yasin over your dead. Narrated by Abu Dawud. Al-Ajurri mentioned in the Book of Advice from the hadith of Umm Ad-Darda’ that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There is no dead person in whose presence Surat Yasin is recited except that death is made easy for him.’” So when he has passed away and the sight follows the soul, as he, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us in Sahih Muslim, and acts of worship are lifted and obligations are removed, rulings are imposed on the living, including closing his eyes and informing his righteous brothers of his death. Some people disliked it and said: It is from the mourning, but the first is more correct. We have explained it in other places, including preparing it by washing and burying it so that it does not change quickly. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a group of people who delayed burying their dead: ‘Hurry up to bury your corpse.’ And he said: ‘Hurry up with the funeral.’ The hadith, and it will come.” Third: As for washing him, it is a Sunnah for all Muslims, except for the martyr, according to what was mentioned above. It was said that washing him is obligatory, as stated by Judge Abdul Wahhab. The first is the doctrine of the Book, and according to these two statements, the scholars. The reason for the disagreement is his saying, peace be upon him, to Umm Atiyah in washing his daughter Zainab, according to what is in the book of Muslim, and it was said: She is Umm Kulthum, according to what is in the book of Abu Dawud: Wash her three or five times or more than that if you see fit, the hadith, which is the origin according to the scholars in washing the dead. It was said: What is meant by this command is to explain the ruling on washing, so it is obligatory. It was said: What is meant by it is to teach how to wash, so there is nothing in it that indicates obligation. They said: And what is indicated by his saying: If you see that, and this requires excluding the apparent meaning of the command from obligation, because he delegated it to their consideration. It was said to them: There is a distance in this, because your referring If you see to the command is not the first to understanding, rather the first is the return of this condition to the closest mentioned, which is more than that or to the choice in numbers. In general, there is no disagreement that washing the dead is prescribed and practiced in the Sharia. It is not left, and its description is like the description of the ritual bath for major ritual impurity, as is well known, and it does not exceed seven washings in washing the dead by consensus, according to what Abu Omar narrated. If something comes out of him after the seven, he washes the place alone, and his ruling is the ruling of the one in a state of major ritual impurity if he breaks his ablution after his washing. So when he finishes his washing, he is shrouded in his clothes, which are: Fourth: Shrouding is obligatory according to most scholars. If he has money, then it is from his capital, according to most scholars, except for what was narrated from Tawus, who said: From a third, whether the money is little or much. If the deceased is someone whose expenses are obligatory upon someone else during his life, such as a master, whether he is a slave, or a father, or a husband, or whoever, then it is upon the master by consensus, and upon the husband, father, and son, according to differences, then upon the public treasury or upon the group of Muslims, based on sufficiency. What is required from it by specifying the obligation is covering the private parts. If there is excess in it, but it does not include the entire body, then his head and face are covered, to honor his face and to cover what appears of the change in his appearance. The origin of this is the story of Mus`ab ibn `Umair, who left a tiara on the day of Uhud, and if his head was covered, his feet would stick out, and if his feet were covered, his head would stick out. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Put it next to his head and put some idhkhir on his feet. The hadith was narrated by Muslim. The witr is recommended by all scholars in the shroud, and they all agree that there is no limit to it. The recommended type is white. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Wear white from your clothes, for it is the best of your clothes, and shroud your dead in it.’” Narrated by Abu Dawud. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was shrouded in three white, silken garments. A shroud other than white is permissible unless it is made of silk or brocade. If the heirs dispute over the shroud, they are to be ordered to wear the same clothing as he wore on Fridays and holidays. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If one of you shrouds his brother, let him shroud him well.’” Narrated by Muslim, unless he bequeaths less than that. If he bequeaths more than that, it is said that the excess is invalidated. It is said that it is in the third, and the first is more correct, based on the words of God Almighty: And do not be extravagant. Abu Bakr said: It is for the respite. When he is finished washing and shrouding him, he is placed on his bed and the men carry him on their shoulders, which is: Fifth: The ruling is to walk quickly, based on the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): Hurry up with the funeral, for if it is good then you are bringing it forward to goodness, and if it is not then you are removing evil from your necks, not as the ignorant do today by walking slowly, standing with it time after time, and reciting the Qur’an with melodies to what is not permissible and not permitted, as the people of Egypt do with their dead. Al-Nasa’i narrated: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Khalid told us, Uyaynah ibn Abd al-Rahman told us, my father told me: I witnessed the funeral of Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, and Ziyad came out walking in front of the bier, so some men from the family of Abd al-Rahman and their clients began to face the bier and walk on their heels and say: Slowly, slowly, may God bless you! So they crawled, until when we were on some of the road to al-Marbad, Abu Bakra may God be pleased with him caught up with us on a mule. When he saw those who were doing that, he charged at them on his mule and whipped them and said: Leave! By the One Who honored the face of Abu al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, I saw us with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we were almost walking with it at a trot. The people relaxed. Abu Majida narrated, “On the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: We asked our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about walking with the funeral procession, and he said: Less than a trot. If it is good, then hasten to it, and if it is otherwise, then away with the people of the Fire.” The hadith. Abu `Umar said: What the group of scholars agree upon in this is to hasten a little beyond nature, and haste is more beloved to them than slowness, and haste that is difficult for the weak people who follow it is disliked. Ibrahim al-Nakha`i said: Slow down with it a little and do not crawl like the Jews and Christians. Some people have interpreted the haste in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah as hastening the burial, not walking, and that is not a thing for what we have mentioned. And God is the Grantor of success. Sixth: As for praying over him, it is a communal obligation, like jihad. This is the well-known view of the scholars, Malik and others, based on the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the Negus: Stand up and pray over him. Asbagh said: It is a Sunnah, and it was narrated from Malik. This meaning will be further explained in Bara’ah. Seventh: As for burying him in the dirt, covering him up and concealing him, that is obligatory, based on the Almighty’s statement: Then God sent a crow scratching the ground to show him how to conceal the shame of his brother (al-Ma’idah 5:31), and there He mentions building a mosque over him, God willing. This is a set of rulings on the dead and what is required of them by the living. On the authority of Aisha, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Do not dress the dead, for they have already passed away to what they sent forth.’” Narrated by Muslim. In Sunan al-Nasa’i, she also said: “A bad mention was made to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of someone who had died, so he said: ‘Do not mention your dead except in a good way.’” God the Almighty said: And you will only be given your full compensation on the Day of Resurrection. The reward of the believer is a reward, and the reward of the disbeliever is a punishment. The blessing and affliction in this world are not considered as rewards or recompense, because it is the place of destruction. So whoever is removed from the Fire means farther away, and admitted to Paradise has attained he has attained what he hopes for, and escaped what he fears. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abd Rabb al-Ka’bah on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever is pleased to be removed from the Fire and to enter Paradise, let his death come to him while he bears witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and he comes to the people as he would like to be come to.” On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The space of a whip in Paradise is better than the world and everything in it. Read if you wish So whoever is removed from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained.” And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion. That is, it deceives and tricks the believer into thinking that he will live long, while it is fleeting. Enjoyment is that which is enjoyed and benefited from, such as an axe, a pot, or a bowl, then it disappears and its possession is no longer there. This is what most of the commentators have said. Al-Hasan said: Like the greenery of plants and girls’ toys that have no result. Qatada said: It is an abandoned enjoyment that is about to vanish with its people. So a person should take from this enjoyment, by obeying God Almighty, as much as he can. And he who said well: This is the house of harm and filth, the house of destruction and the house of others. If you got it all, you would die without having had your fill of it. Whoever hopes for long life, long life will be harmful to him. If you are old and your youth has passed, there is no good in living after old age And arrogance with the opening of the ghain is the devil, who deceives people with false hopes and promises. Ibn Arafa said: Arrogance is that which you see as having an appearance that you like, but in which there is an interior that is disliked or unknown. And the devil is arrogant, because he leads to what the self loves, and behind that is what is bad. He said: And from this is the sale of uncertainty, which is that which has an appearance of a sale that deceives and an interior that is unknown.
3:186: This address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation, and the meaning is: You will be tested and tried in your wealth by calamities and misfortunes by spending in the way of God and all the obligations of the Shari’ah, and the trials in the souls by death, illnesses, and the loss of loved ones. He began by mentioning wealth because of the many calamities in it. And you will hear. If it is said: Why was the waw established in Latabilun and deleted from Watisa’n, the answer is that the waw in Latabilun was preceded by a fatha, so it was moved due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, and it was made specific, with a damma because it is the waw of the plural, and it was not permissible to delete it because there is nothing before it that indicates it, and it was deleted from Watisa’n because there is nothing before it that indicates it, and it is not permissible to hamza the waw in Latabilun because its movement is incidental, as stated by An-Nahhas and others. It is said for one masculine: Latabilin ya rajul, and for two: Latabilian ya rajulan, and for a group of men: Latabilun, and it was revealed because Abu Bakr May God be pleased with him, he heard a Jew say: God is poor and we are rich, in response to the Qur’an and belittling it when God revealed: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? (al-Baqarah 2:245), so he slapped him, and he complained about him to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was revealed. It was said that the one who said it was Finhas the Jew, on the authority of Ikrimah, Al-Zuhri: He is Ka’b ibn Al-Ashraf, it was revealed because of him, and he was a poet, and he used to satirize the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and incite the infidels of Quraysh against him, and flirt with the women of the Muslims until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Muhammad ibn Maslama and his companions to him, and he killed him in the famous killing in the biography and the authentic report, and other than this was said, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, there were Jews and polytheists in it, so he and his companions used to hear a lot of harm, and in the two Sahihs: “He, peace be upon him, passed by Ibn Abi while he was on a donkey, so he called him to God Almighty, and Ibn Abi said, If what you say is true, then do not harm us with it in our gatherings!” Return to your journey, and whoever comes to you, tell him the story, and he held his nose so that the dust of the donkey would not touch him. Ibn Rawahah said, Yes, O Messenger of God, so entertain us in our gatherings, for we love that. The polytheists who were around Ibn Ubayy and the Muslims reviled him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to calm them down until they calmed down. Then he entered upon Sa`d ibn `Ubadah to visit him while he was sick, and he said, Did you not hear what so-and-so said? Sa`d said, “Forgive him and pardon him, for by the One Who sent down the Book to you, God has brought you the truth that was sent down, and the people of this lake agreed to crown him and tie him with a headband. When God returned that to him with the truth that He gave you, he was pleased with him, and that is what you saw. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgave him, and this verse was revealed.” It was said: This was before the revelation of the battle, and God urged His servants to patience and piety and informed that it was from the determination of matters, and likewise in Bukhari in the context of the hadith, that this was before the revelation of the battle, and it is more apparent that it is not abrogated, for argument is in the best way and moderation is always recommended, and he, peace be upon him, with the command to fight, was friendly with the Jews and moderated them, and forgave the hypocrites, and this is clear, and the meaning of determination of matters is their firmness and solidity, and it has been mentioned previously.
3:187: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture. This is connected to the mention of the Jews, for they were commanded to believe in Muhammad, peace be upon him, and to explain his command, but they concealed his description, so the verse is a rebuke to them, and with that it is general report for them and others. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: It is for everyone who was given knowledge of something from the Scripture, so whoever knows something should teach it, and beware of concealing knowledge, for it is destruction. Muhammad bin Ka’b said: It is not permissible for a scholar to remain silent about his knowledge, nor for an ignorant person to remain silent about his ignorance. God the Almighty said: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, and He said: So ask the people of the message if you do not know. (Al-Anbiya’: 7), and Abu Hurairah said: If it were not for what God took from the People of the Scripture, I would not have told you anything. Then he recited this verse: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture. Al-Hasan bin ‘Ammarah said: I came to Al-Zuhri after he had abandoned hadith, and I found him at his door, so I said: If you see, will you tell me? He said: Do you not know? I left the hadith? I said: Either you tell me or I tell you. He said: Tell me. I said: Al-Hakam bin Utaybah told me on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar who said: I heard Ali bin Abi Talib say: God did not take a duty from the ignorant to learn until He took a duty from the scholars to teach. He said: So he told me forty hadiths. The second: The letter ha’ in his saying: that you may make it clear to the people refers to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, even if he is not mentioned. It was said: it refers to the book, and it includes the explanation of the command of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because it is in the book. He said: and do not conceal it and did not say conceal it because it is in the meaning of the state, meaning that you will make it clear without concealing it. Abu Amr and Asim read in the narration of Abu Bakr and the people of Mecca li-tabayyinnahu with a ta’ as a recitation of the address, and the rest with a ya’ because they are absent. Ibn Abbas read and when God took the covenant of the prophets to make it clear so his saying then they cast it away comes referring to the people to whom the prophets made it clear. In the reading of Ibn Mas’ud li-tabayyinnahu without the heavy nun. Casting is throwing, and its explanation has been presented in Al-Baqarah. Behind their backs is an exaggeration in throwing, and from it and you took it behind your backs and its explanation has also been presented in Al-Baqarah. The meaning of his saying: and they bought with it a small price has been presented in Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. What a bad purchase they are buying. It also came forward, praise be to God.
3:188: That is, because of what they did by sitting back and not participating in the invasion and the excuse they brought. It was reported in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri that when some hypocrites stayed behind during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to fight, they would stay behind and rejoice in their absence from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. But when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, they would apologize to him and swear, and they would like him to praise them for what they did not do. So the verse was revealed: Think not of those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done. It is also in the two Sahihs that Marwan said to his gatekeeper: Go, Rafi’, to Ibn Abbas and say to him: If every man among us who rejoices in what he has been given and loves to be praised for what he has not done is to be punished, then we will all be punished. Ibn Abbas said: What do you have to do with this verse? This verse was only revealed about the People of the Book. Then Ibn Abbas recited: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, ‘You shall make it clear to the people and not conceal it’ and Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done are beyond the pale of Paradise. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked them about something and they concealed it from him and told him something else. So they left and showed him that they had told him what he had asked them about and praised him for that, and were happy with what they had done by concealing it and what he had asked them about. Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi said: It was revealed about the scholars of the Children of Israel who concealed the truth and gave their kings knowledge that agreed with their falsehood, and bought with it a small price, meaning with what the kings gave them of this world. So God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done and love to be praised for what they have not done are beyond the reach of punishment. And for them is a painful punishment.” So He informed that they will have a painful punishment for what they corrupted of the religion for the servants of God, and He said: Ad-Dahhak: The Jews used to say to the kings, We find in our book that God will send a prophet at the end of time who will seal prophethood. So when God sent him, the kings asked them, Is this the one you find in your book? The Jews said, coveting the kings’ wealth: It is not this, so the kings gave them the treasuries, and God Almighty said: Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have given the kings are lying until they take the world’s goods, and the first hadith is contrary to the implication of the second hadith, and it is possible that it was revealed for both reasons because they came together at the same time, so it was an answer to both groups, and God knows best. His saying: And they sought praise for that to Him, meaning they asked to be praised, and Marwan’s saying: If every man of us, etc. is evidence that generality has specific forms, and that those is one of them, and this is certain from whoever understands that from the Qur’an and Sunnah, and God Almighty’s saying: And they love to be praised for what they have not done if the verse is about the People of the Book, not about the hypocrites who stayed behind, because they used to say: We are on the religion of Abraham and they were not on his religion, and they used to say: We are the people of prayer, fasting, and the Book, wanting to be praised for that, and those is the subject of think with the letter ya, and this is the reading of Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and Ibn ‘Amir. Katheer and Abi Amr, that is, the joyful should not think that their joy will save them from the torment. It was said that the first object is omitted, which is themselves, and the second in a desert. The Kufians read tahsabna with a ta’ as addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that is, do not think, O Muhammad, those who are joyful in the desert of torment. His saying: Do not think that they are with a ta’ and a fatha on the ba’ is a reiteration of emphasis, and its first object is the ha’ and the mim, and the second object is omitted, that is, likewise, and the fa’ is a conjunction or an extra particle in place of the second verb from the first. Ad-Dahhak and Isa bin Omar read with a ta’ and a damma on the ba’ do not think that they are, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. Mujahid, Ibn Katheer, Abu Amr, and Yahya bin Ya’mar read with a ya’ and a damma on the ba’ as report about those who are joyful, that is, do not think that they are themselves, in a desert is the second object, and do not think that they are is an emphasis. It was said: those who is the subject of think that they are. Its two objects are omitted because they think they indicate it, as the poet said: In what book or verse do you see their love as a disgrace to me and consider it a sin? The mention of the object of one verb dispensed with the mention of the object of the second, and the second in a desert, which is a substitute for the first verb, so its replacement dispensed with the mention of its two objects, and the fa’ is redundant, and it was said: These verbs may come cancelled but not in the rule of useful sentences, such as the poet’s saying: I did not think that there would remain between us more affection than the two beautiful, intelligent, and intelligent women. Al-Mudhaki: Horses that have been sore for a year or two, the singular is mudhk, like the camel al-mukhalaf, and in the proverb the running of the mudhkiyat is overwhelming, and the musnafat is a passive participle, it is said: Sanfat al-ba’ir asnafhu sanfan if you hold it back with its reins while you are riding it, and asnaf al-ba’il is a dialect for sanfa, and asnaf al-ba’il by itself if it raises its head, transitive and intransitive, and the Arabs used to ride camels and avoid horses, they say: War leaves no affection, and Ka’b ibn Abi Salma said: I hope and wish that her affection will come closer, and I do not think we have any desire from you The majority of the seven reciters and others read atawā with a short alif, meaning with what they brought of lies and concealment. Marwan ibn al-Hakam, al-A’mash, and Ibrahim al-Nakha’i read atawā with a long vowel, meaning they gave. Sa’id ibn Jubayr read atawā without naming its agent, meaning they gave. The desert is the escape, a verbal noun from fazā yafūz if he escaped, meaning they are not winners. The place of fears is called a desert as an expression of optimism, as al-Asma’i said. It was said: Because it is a place of escape and a place of possibility of destruction. The Arabs say: a man is successful if he dies. Tha’lab said: I told Ibn al-A’rabi what al-Asma’i said, and he said he made a mistake. Abu al-Makarim said to me. Ibn al-A’rabi said: Because he is resigned to what has befallen him. It was said: Do not think that they are in a place far from punishment, because success is distancing oneself from the disliked, and God knows best.
3:189: This is an argument against those who said that God is poor and we are rich, and a denial of them. It was said: The meaning is do not think that the happy ones will escape the punishment, for God has everything, and they are in the grip of the Almighty. So it is connected to the first statement, meaning that they will not escape His punishment, He takes them whenever He wills. And God is over all things, meaning possible, Powerful. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah.
3:190: First: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth has been mentioned in the meaning of this verse in Al-Baqarah in more than one place. So the Almighty concluded this surah with the command to look and reason in His verses, since they are not issued except by a Living, Self-Sustaining, Holy, Peaceful One who is independent of the worlds, so that their faith is based on certainty and not on imitation. Signs for those of understanding who use their minds to contemplate the evidence. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: When this verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he stood up to pray, and Bilal came to him to call him to prayer. He saw him crying and said: O Messenger of God, are you crying when God has forgiven you your past and future sins! He said: O Bilal, should I not be a grateful servant, when God revealed to me last night the verse: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding. Then He said: Woe to the one who reads it and does not contemplate it. Second: The scholars said: It is recommended for the one who wakes up from sleep to wipe his face and begin his standing by reciting these ten verses, following the example of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This has been proven in the two Sahihs and others, and it will come. Then he prays what has been written for him, combining contemplation and action, and this is better, as will be explained in this verse after this. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite ten verses from the end of Surat Al Imran every night. It was narrated by Abu Nasr Al-Wa’ili Al-Sijistani Al-Hafiz in the book Al-Ibanah from the hadith of Sulayman bin Musa on the authority of Muzahir bin Aslam Al-Makhzumi on the authority of Al-Maqburi on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and the beginning of the surah was mentioned earlier on the authority of Uthman, who said: Whoever recites Al Imran at night will be credited with the reward of standing in prayer for a night.
3:191: Third: The Almighty said: " Those who remember God while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides. " God mentioned three states that the son of Adam is never without in most of his affairs, as if they limit his time. From this meaning is the saying of Aisha may God be pleased with her: " The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to remember God at all times. " Narrated by Muslim. This includes being in the bathroom or otherwise. The scholars differed on this. Abdullah ibn Amr, Ibn Sirin, and al-Nakha'i permitted it, while Ibn Abbas, Ata', and al-Sha'bi disliked it. The first is more correct due to the generality of the verse and the hadith. al-Nakha'i said: There is nothing wrong with remembering God while in the bathroom, for it ascends. The meaning is: the angels ascend with it written in their scrolls. So the complement was omitted. The evidence for this is the Almighty's saying: " Not a word does he utter but there is a watcher by him ready to record it. " ( Qaf: 18), and He said: " And indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording. " ( Al-Infitar: 10-11) ] And because God Almighty commanded His servants to remember Him in every situation and did not make any exception, so He said: Remember God with much remembrance ( Al-Ahzab: 41), and He said: Then remember Me, and I will remember you ( Al-Baqarah: 152), and He said: Indeed, We do not allow to be lost the reward of one who does good work ( Al-Kahf: 30), so He is general, so remembering God Almighty in all his situations is rewarded, God willing. Abu Nu’aym said: Abu Bakr bin Malik told us, Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal told us, my father told us, Wakee’ told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Marwan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ka’b Al-Ahbar, who said: Moses, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, are You near so that I may commune with You, or are You far so that I may call out to You? He said: O Moses, I am the companion of the one who remembers Me. He said: O Lord, for we are in one state after another, we respect You and magnify You by remembering You. He said: What is it? He said: Major ritual impurity and defecation. He said: O Moses, remember Me in every situation. The dislike of those who dislike that is either to sanctify the remembrance of God Almighty in places where it is desirable not to mention Him, such as the dislike of reciting the Qur’an in the bathroom, or to keep the honorable scribes on the condition that they be placed in a place of filth and impurity to write down what is spoken, and God knows best. Standing and sitting is in the accusative case as a state, and on their sides is in the place of the state, meaning and lying down. Similar to it is the statement of God Almighty: He called us on his side or sitting or standing ( Yunus: 12), on the contrary, meaning he called us lying on his side. A group of commentators, including Al-Hasan and others, said that his statement they remember God to the end is only an expression of prayer, meaning they do not waste it, so in the case of an excuse they pray it sitting or on their sides, and it is like the statement of God Almighty: And when you have completed the prayer, remember God standing, sitting, and lying on your sides ( An-Nisa’: 103), according to the statement of Ibn Mas’ud, as will be explained. And if the verse is in Prayer and its understanding is that a person prays standing, and if he is unable to do so, then sitting, and if he is unable to do so, then on his side, as was proven on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, who said: I had hemorrhoids, so I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about prayer. He said: Pray standing, and if you are unable to do so, then sitting, and if you are unable to do so, then on your side. Narrated by the imams. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray sitting in voluntary prayers a year before his death, according to what is in Sahih Muslim. Al-Nasa’i narrated, “ On the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying while sitting cross-legged. ” Abu Abd al-Rahman said: I do not know of anyone who narrated this hadith other than Abu Dawud al-Hafri, who is trustworthy. I do not think this hadith is anything but a mistake, and God knows best. Fourth: The scholars differed on the manner and form of the prayer of the sick and the one who is sitting. Ibn Abd al-Hakam reported on the authority of Malik that he should sit cross-legged while standing. Al-Buwayti said the same on the authority of al-Shafi’i. Then when he wants to prostrate, he should prepare for prostration to the extent that he is able. He said: The same applies to the one who is performing a voluntary prayer. A similar opinion is that of al-Thawri. Al-Layth, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Ayyusuf, and Muhammad also said the same. Al-Shafi’i said in the narration of al-Muzani: He should sit throughout his prayer like the sitting for the testimony of faith. This was narrated on the authority of Malik and his companions. The first is the well-known opinion and is the apparent meaning of al-Madwa. Abu Hanifa and Zufar said: He should sit like the sitting for the testimony of faith, and likewise he should prepare himself and prostrate. Fifth: He said: If he is unable to sit, he should pray on his side or back, as a choice. This is the view of Al-Mudawwana. Ibn Habib narrated on the authority of Ibn Al-Qasim that he should pray on his back. If he is unable, then on his right side, then on his left side. In the book of Ibn Al-Mawaz, it is the opposite. He should pray on his right side, otherwise on the left, otherwise on his back. Sahnun said: He should pray on his right as he is placed in his grave, otherwise on his back, otherwise on his left. Malik and Abu Hanifah said: If he prays lying down, his feet should be towards the qiblah. Al-Shafi’i and Al-Thawri said: He should pray on his side and his face towards the qiblah. Sixth: If he becomes strong due to a light illness while he is praying, Ibn al-Qasim said: He should stand for the rest of his prayer and continue from what he has gone before. This is the opinion of al-Shafi’i, Zufar, and al-Tabari. Abu Hanifah and his two companions, Ya’qub and Muhammad, said about someone who prays a rak’ah lying down and then it becomes valid: He should start the prayer from the beginning. If he was sitting, bowing and prostrating, then it becomes valid, he should continue according to Abu Hanifah’s opinion, but not according to Muhammad’s opinion. Abu Hanifah and his companions said: If someone begins the prayer standing and then reaches the point of gesturing, he should make it clear. This was narrated from Abu Yusuf. Malik said about a sick person who is unable to bow or prostrate but is able to stand and sit: He should pray standing and nod to bowing, and if he wants to prostrate, he should sit and nod to prostration. This is the opinion of Abu Yusuf and is analogous to the opinion of al-Shafi’i. Abu Hanifah and his companions said: He should pray sitting. Seventh: As for the prayer of one who is lying down, it was narrated in the hadith of Imran bin Husayn an addition that is not found in any other hadith, which is: “ The prayer of one who is lying down is like half the prayer of one who is sitting. ” Abu Omar said: The majority of scholars do not permit the voluntary prayer while lying down. This is a hadith that was only narrated by Husayn al-Mu’allim, namely Husayn bin Dhakwan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Buraidah, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn. There is a difference of opinion regarding Husayn’s chain of transmission and text, a difference that requires us to stop regarding it. Even if it is authentic, I do not know what its basis is. If any of the scholars permitted the voluntary prayer while lying down for those who are able to sit or stand, then his basis is this addition in this hadith, and it is an argument for those who hold that view. If they agreed on the dislike of the voluntary prayer while lying down for those who are able to sit or stand, then this hadith of Husayn is either wrong or abrogated. It was said: What is meant by the verse are those who use the creation of the heavens and the earth as evidence that what changes must have a changer, and that changer must be able to perfect it, and he has the right to send messengers. If he sends a messenger and indicates his truthfulness, With one miracle, no one has any excuse. These are the ones who remember God in every situation, and God knows best. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: “ And they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth. ” We have already explained the meaning of and they reflect, which is either remembrance with the tongue or prayer, its obligatory and voluntary acts. So God, the Almighty, connected another act of worship to one of them with another act of worship, which is reflecting on the power of God, His creations, and the lessons He has spread, so that this would increase their insight. And in everything there is a sign that indicates that it is one. It was said: they disbelieve is in apposition to the state. It was said: it is disjunctive, and the first is more likely. Thought: the heart hesitates about something. It is said: he thought, and a thoughtful man thinks a lot. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) passed by some people who were contemplating God and said: Contemplate the creation but do not contemplate the Creator, for you cannot appreciate His value. Rather, contemplation, consideration and expansion of the mind are in the creation, as He said: and they contemplate the creation of the heavens and the earth. It was narrated that Sufyan al-Thawri may God be pleased with him prayed two rak’ahs behind the Maqam, then he raised his head to the sky. When he saw the stars, he fainted and was urinating blood from the length of his grief and contemplation. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him who said: “ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘ While a man was lying on his bed, he raised his head and looked at the stars and at the sky and said, ‘I bear witness that you have a Lord and a Creator. O God, forgive me.’ So God looked at him and forgave him. ’ ” And he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is no worship like contemplation. It was narrated that he ( peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Contemplation for an hour is better than worship for a year. Ibn al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Malik who said: Umm al-Darda’ was asked: ‘What was Abu al-Darda’s main concern?’ She said: ‘Contemplation was his main concern.’ It was said to him: ‘Do you consider contemplation to be an action?’” He said: Yes, it is certainty. Ibn Al-Musayyab was asked about the prayer between Dhuhr and Asr. He said: This is not worship. Rather, worship is abstaining from what God has forbidden and contemplating the commands of God. Al-Hasan said: Contemplation for an hour is better than standing all night. Ibn Abbas and Abu Al-Darda’ said the same. Al-Hasan said: Contemplation is the mirror of the believer in which he looks at his good and bad deeds. Among the things he contemplates are fears of the Hereafter, such as the gathering and resurrection, Paradise and its delights, and Hell and its torment. It is narrated that Abu Sulayman Al-Darani may God be pleased with him took a cup of water to perform ablution for the night prayer and he had a guest with him. When he put his finger in the ear of the cup, he saw that he remained contemplating until dawn came. He said to him: What is this, O Abu Sulayman? He said: When I put my finger in the ear of the cup, I thought about the words of God Almighty: When the shackles are around their necks and the chains are dragged ( Ghafir: 71). I thought about my condition and how I would receive the shackles if they were placed around my neck on the Day of Resurrection. I continued in that state until morning. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is the ultimate fear, and the best of matters are their middle ground. The scholars of the nation, who are the proof for this method, and reading the knowledge of the Book of God Almighty and the meanings of the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for one who understands and hopes to benefit from it, are not better than this. Ibn al-Arabi said: People differed as to which of the two deeds is better: contemplation or prayer. The Sufis went to the view that contemplation is better, as it produces knowledge and is the best of the legal stations. The jurists went to the view that prayer is better, because of what was mentioned in the hadith about urging it, calling to it, and encouraging it. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he spent the night with his aunt Maymunah, and in it: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and wiped the letter nun from his face, then he recited the ten final verses of Surat Al Imran, and stood up to sing. He performed a light ablution and then prayed thirteen rak’ahs. Look, may God have mercy on you, at his combination of contemplating the creation and then turning to his prayer after that. This is the Sunnah that is relied upon. As for the way of the Sufis, that the sheikh should be among them, thinking for a day, a night, and a month without slackening, then this is a way that is not right for humans, nor does it continue according to the Sunnah. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: My father told me, on the authority of some scholars of the East, he said: I was spending the night in the Mosque of Al-Aqdam in Egypt, and I prayed the Isha prayer. I saw a man lying down in his cloak, covered with his cloak until morning. We prayed that night. When the dawn prayer was called, that man stood up, faced the qibla, and prayed with the people. I was astonished at his boldness in praying without ablution. When the prayer was finished, he went out, so I followed him to admonish him. When I approached him, I heard him recite poetry: The body is lying down, absent, present and alert, the heart is silent and mindful He is contracted in the unseen and expanded, like that of the one who knows and remembers. He spends the night thinking, for he is asleep and awake all night. He said: I knew that he was one of those who worship by thought, so I turned away from him. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: “ Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. ” That is, they say: You did not create it in vain or jest, but rather You created it as evidence of Your power and wisdom. Falsehood is the vanishing and passing away, and from it is the saying of Labid: Verily, everything except God is false, meaning it will perish. And in vain is in the accusative case because it is a deleted verbal noun, meaning a false creation. And it was said: It is in the accusative case because the preposition was removed, meaning I did not create it for falsehood. And it was said: It is in the second object, and creation can mean making. “ Glory be to You. ” An- Nahhas narrated on the authority of Musa ibn Talhah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the meaning of Glory be to God, so he said: “ To sanctify God from evil. ” And its meaning has already been fully presented in Al-Baqarah. Save us from the punishment of the Fire means, Save us from its punishment. And it has already been presented.
