And God knows best. The Almighty said: “Say: The enjoyment of this world is little” beginning and predicate, and so on. And the Hereafter is better for him who fears God meaning sins. We have already discussed this in Al-Baqarah. The enjoyment of this world is its benefit and enjoying its pleasures, and He called it little because it does not last. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My example and the example of the world are like that of a rider who said, A nap under a tree, then left it and departed. This meaning has been fully explained in Surat Al-Baqarah.
4:78: It has four issues The first - the Almighty’s saying: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you is a condition and a reward, and ma is redundant. This address is general, even if what is meant is the hypocrites or the weak believers who said: Why do you not delay us for a short term? That is, until we die at our appointed times. This is more similar to the hypocrites, as we mentioned, because of their saying when the people of Uhud were afflicted, they said: If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed. (Al Imran 3:156) God responded to them: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were in lofty towers. This was said by Ibn Abbas in the narration of Abu Salih from him. One of the towers is a tower, which is a tall building or a great palace. Tarafa said, describing a she-camel. It is like a Roman tower, surrounded by gypsum, bricks and stones. Talha bin Sulayman read yadrakum with the kaf raised and the fa’ omitted, which is rare and only occurs in poetry, such as his saying: Whoever does good deeds, God will reward them. He wanted to thank God. Scholars and commentators differed about what was meant by these towers. Most said, and it is the most correct, that he meant the towers in the fortresses that are built on the earth, because they are the ultimate goal of human beings in fortification and protection, so God gave them an example of them. Qatada said: In fortified palaces. Ibn Jurayj and the majority said: And from this is the saying of Amir ibn Tufayl to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him: Would you like a fortified and protected fortress? Mujahid said: The towers are the palaces. Ibn Abbas: The towers are the fortresses, roofs and castles. The meaning of fortified is elongated, as Al-Zajjaj and Al-Qatabi said. Ikrimah: Decorated with gypsum, which is plaster. Qatada said: Fortified, fortified and fortified and fortified are the same. From this is and a fortified palace (Al-Had: 45) and the emphasis is for emphasis. It was said: fortified is elongated and fortified is covered with gypsum. It is said: He built the building and praised its mention. Al-Suddi said: What is meant by the towers are towers in the lowest heaven that are built. This statement was narrated by Makki on the authority of Malik, who said: Do you not see the words of God Almighty: And the heaven with the mansions (al-Buruj 85:1) He has placed in the heaven mansions (al-Furqan 25:61) And We have certainly placed in the heaven mansions (al-Hijr 15:16). Ibn Al-Arabi also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Al-Qasim on the authority of Malik. Al-Naqqash narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: In lofty towers means in palaces from a hadith. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is what the apparent meaning of the wording gives. The second - This verse responds to the Qadarites regarding the appointed times, because God Almighty said: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were in fortified towers. Thus He informed them that when the appointed times are over, the soul must leave the body, whether that be killing, death, or something else that God has made it customary for it to end. The Mu’tazila said: If the murderer had not killed the one who was killed, he would have lived. The men preceded them in Al Imran and will come, so they agreed with this statement of theirs with the infidels and hypocrites. Third: Taking and building lands to protect money and lives, which is the way of God with His servants. This is the clearest evidence to reject the statement of those who say, trust is abandoning the causes, because taking lands is one of the greatest and most important causes, and we have been commanded to do so, and the prophets took them and dug several trenches around them to increase the protection. It was said to Al-Ahnaf, what is the ruling on the wall? He said, to deter the foolish until the wise man comes and protects him. Fourth: If we go down to the statement of Malik and al-Suddi that they are the constellations of the sky, then the constellations of the heavens are twelve constellations constructed from the rising, and they are the great planets. The planets are called constellations because of their appearance from the constellations that appear and rise, and from this is His saying, And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance (al-Ahzab 33:33). God Almighty created them as mansions for the sun and the moon, and determined them in them and arranged the times upon them, and made them southern and northern as a guide to interests and a sign of the qiblah, and a way to obtain the hours of the night and the hours of the day to know the times of the night prayer and other conditions of livelihood. God the Almighty said: And if good befalls them, they say, ‘This is from God.’ That is, if the hypocrites are afflicted with fertility, they say, This is from God. “But if evil befalls them,” that is, drought and famine, they say, This is from you, that is, it befell us because of your bad luck, your companions. It was said: Good means safety and security, and bad means illnesses and fear. It was also said: Good means wealth and bad means poverty. It was also said: Good means blessing, victory, and booty on the Day of Badr, and bad means affliction, hardship, and killing on the Day of Uhud. It was also said: Good means prosperity, and bad means hardship. These are the sayings of the commentators and scholars of interpretation - Ibn Abbas and others - regarding the verse. And that it was revealed about the Jews and the hypocrites, because when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them in Medina, they said: We have not ceased to know the deficiency in our fruits and farms since this man and his companions came to them. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning of from you is due to your bad management. And it was said: from you due to your bad luck as we mentioned, meaning due to your bad luck that has befallen us. They said it as a way of purification. God Almighty said: “Say: All is from God” meaning hardship and ease, victory and defeat are from God, meaning by God’s decree and destiny. Then what is the matter with these people meaning the hypocrites that they can hardly understand a word meaning what is the matter with them that they do not understand that all is from God.
4:79: The Almighty said: Whatever good befalls you is from God, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself. That is, whatever befell you, O Muhammad bin Khasab, of prosperity, health, and safety, is by God's grace and kindness to you, and whatever befell you of drought and hardship, is because of a sin you committed for which you were punished. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation is meant. That is, whatever befell you, O people, of fertility and abundance of provision, is from God's grace upon you, and whatever befell you of drought and scarcity of provision, is from yourselves, meaning that it befell you because of your sins. This was said by Al-Hasan, Al-Suddi, and others, as the Almighty said: O Prophet, when you divorce women (al-Talaq 65:1). It has also been said that the address is to man, and what is meant by it is the species, as the Almighty said: By time, indeed, mankind is in loss (At-Asr: 1-2), meaning that people are in loss. Do you not see that He made an exception from them, saying: Except those who believe. And an exception is only made from a group or a community. According to this interpretation, His statement, What befell you is a new beginning. It was said: There is an omission in the speech, the meaning of which is they say, and accordingly the speech is connected, and the meaning is: What is the matter with these people that they can hardly understand a statement until they say: Whatever good has befallen you is from God? And it was said: The interrogative alif is implied, and the meaning is: Is it from yourself? And similar to it is the saying of God Almighty: And that is a blessing which You bestow upon me (Ash-Shu’ara’: 22), and the meaning is: Or is that a blessing? And similarly is the saying of God Almighty: And when he saw the moon rising, he said, ‘This is my Lord.’ (al-An’am 6:77) Meaning, Is this my Lord? Abu Khurash Al-Hudhali said: They threw me and said, O Khuwaylid, you did not take heed. I said, and I denied the faces, They are they. He wanted to say more important, so he implied the question mark, which is common and will come. Al-Akhfash said, What means which. It was said: It is a condition. Al-Nahhas said: The correct statement of Al-Akhfash is that it was revealed regarding a specific thing, such as drought, and this is not one of the sins at all. If it were one of them, it would have been whatever bad thing I have suffered. Abd al-Wahhab ibn Mujahid narrated on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ubayy, and Ibn Mas’ud. Whatever good thing befalls you is from God, and whatever bad thing befalls you is from yourself, and I have written it for you. This is a reading of the interpretation. Some of the people of deviation have attributed it to the Qur’an, and the hadith with that on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud and Ubayy is disconnected because Mujahid did not see Abdullah or Ubayy. According to the statement of those who said, The good thing is the conquest and the spoils on the day of Badr, and the bad thing is what befell them on the day of Uhud, they were punished when the archers who the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had ordered to protect his back and not move from their place were defeated. They saw the defeat of the Quraysh and the Muslims taking their money as spoils, so they left their ranks. Khalid ibn al-Walid, who was with the infidels that day, looked and saw the back of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been The archers were exposed, so he took a detachment of horsemen and turned until he was behind the Muslims and attacked them. There was no archer behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except the one with the banner. He kept the will of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he stood until he was martyred in his place, as was explained in Al Imran. Then God Almighty revealed a verse similar to this, which is His statement, the Most High: Or when a disaster struck you meaning the day of Uhud and you had inflicted double its amount meaning the day of Badr you said, ‘From where is this?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves’ (Al Imran 3:165). It is not permissible for the good here to be obedience and the bad to be disobedience as the Qadarites said, because if that were the case, then what I inflicted would be as we have mentioned, since it means action according to them and earnings according to us. Rather, the good and obedience and the bad to be disobedience are in something like His statement: Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof, and whoever brings an evil deed will not be recompensed except the like thereof (Al An’am: 160). As for this verse, it is as we explained it before, of fertility and drought, ease and hardship, in the manner that came. In the verse of Al-A’raf, which is the Almighty’s saying: And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and a loss of fruits that perhaps they might be reminded (al-A’raf 7:130) with years means drought year after year, withholding rain from them, so their fruits decreased and their prices rose. But when good comes to them, they say, ‘This is for us.’ But if evil befalls them, they ascribe an evil omen to Moses and those with him. (al-A’raf 7:131) meaning, they consider them a bad omen and say this is because we follow you and obey you. So God responded to them by saying: Behold, their omen is only with God. (al-A’raf 7:131) meaning that the bird of blessing and the bird of bad omen, whether good or evil, benefit or harm, are from God, the Almighty, and no creature has any control over them. So likewise is the Almighty’s saying in what He informed us about them that they attribute it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, where He said: And if evil befalls them, they say, ‘This is from you.’ Say, ‘All is from God.’ Just as He said: Behold, their omen is only with God. (al-A’raf 7:131) And as God the Almighty said: And whatever befell you on the day the two armies met was by God’s permission. (Aal ‘Imran: 131) 166] That is, by God’s decree, destiny, and knowledge, and the verses of the Book bear witness to one another. Our scholars said: And whoever believes in God and the Last Day does not doubt that everything is by God’s decree, destiny, will, and desire, as God Almighty said: And We test you with evil and with good as trial (Al-Anbiya’: 35) and God Almighty said: And when God intends evil for a people, there is no repelling it, and they have no protector besides Him (al-Ra’d 13:11). Question: Some of the ignorant people of the Sunnah have argued about this verse and used it as evidence, just as the Qadarites have argued about it and used it as evidence. The reason for their argument is that the Qadarites say: The good here is obedience and the bad is disobedience. They said: And disobedience has been attributed in the Almighty’s saying: And whatever evil befalls you is from yourself to man and not to God Almighty. So this is the reason for their attachment to it and the reason for others’ attachment to it is the Almighty’s saying: All is from God. They said: He attributed the good and the bad to himself and not to his creation. This verse is only related to the ignorant from both groups, because they based it on the fact that the bad deed is the sin, and it is not so for what we have explained, and God knows best. And if the Qadarites said: Whatever good befalls you meaning of obedience is from God, then this is not their belief because their belief on which they based their doctrine is that the good deed is the action of the doer of good and the bad deed is upon the wrongdoer. Also, if they had an argument in it, he would have said: Whatever good deed I have attained and whatever bad deed I have attained, because He is the doer of both the good deed and the bad deed, so it is not attributed to Him except by His action for them, not by the action of someone else. This statement was stated explicitly by Imam Abu al-Hasan Shabib ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Haidera in his book called Haz al-Ghalasim fi Ifham al-Mukhasim. The Almighty says: And We have sent you to mankind as a Messenger is a confirmed source, and it is possible that the meaning is having a message. “And sufficient is God as a witness” is an accusative of clarification, and the ba is redundant, meaning sufficient is God as a witness to the truthfulness of the message of His Prophet and that he is truthful.
4:80: God Almighty says: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God, but whoever turns away - then We have not sent you over them as a guardian. God Almighty says: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God. God Almighty knows that obeying the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is obedience to Him. In Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Whoever obeys me has obeyed God, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed God. Whoever obeys the emir has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys the emir has disobeyed me.” In another narration: And whoever obeys my emir, and whoever disobeys my emir. God Almighty says: And whoever turns away meaning turns away We have not sent you over them as a guardian meaning as a guardian and monitor of their actions. You are only responsible for conveying the message. Al-Qutbi said: An accountant. So God abrogated this with the verse of the sword and commanded him to fight whoever disobeys God and His Messenger.
4:81: The Almighty said: "And they say, 'We obey,' but when they go forth from you, a party of them will camp other than what you say. And God records what they plot." That is, our command is obedience. Obedience in the accusative case is permissible, meaning we obey in obedience. This is the reading of Nasr bin Asim, Al-Hasan and Al-Jahdari. This is about the hypocrites according to the opinion of most of the commentators, that is, they say when they are with you: our command is obedience, or we obey in obedience. Their statement is not beneficial because the one who does not believe in obedience is not truly obedient because God Almighty did not realize their obedience with what they showed. If it were obedience without belief in reality, He would have ruled it for them. So it is proven that obedience is by belief with its existence. And when they go forth, that is, they leave, a party of them will camp. So he mentioned the group because it is in the meaning of men. The Kufians assimilated the ta' into the ta' because they are from the same point of articulation. Al-Kisa'i considered this ugly in the verb, but according to the Basrans it is not ugly. The meaning of house is false and deceptive. It was said: other, substitute and distortion. That is, they changed the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he entrusted to them and ordered them to do. The word al-Tabtib means to change, and from this is the saying of the poet: They came to me, and I was not satisfied with what they had planned, and they came to me with something reprehensible. I will marry their orphan, and will a free man marry a free man? last: My verse is that Abdul Malik may God kill him, an ungrateful slave. A man decides a matter at night. God Almighty said: When they plan what is not pleasing to Him (An-Nisa’: 108). The Arabs say: He decided a matter at night, if he decided it. The night was specifically mentioned because it is a time when he is free. The poet said: They decided their plan at night, and when morning came, they started to make noise. From this is the house of fasting and the houses: the water stays at night, and the houses: the matter its owner stays at night concerned about it. Al-Hudhali said: And I make its paragraph a provision if the houses of a difficult matter are afraid And the night and the night is that the enemy comes at night and spends the night doing something if he does it at night, as it is said: he remained during the day and the night of something is estimated. If it is said: then what is the wisdom in starting it by mentioning all of them and then saying the night of a group of them it is said: it only expresses the state of one who knows that he will remain in his disbelief and hypocrisy and forgives one who knows that he will return from that. And it is said: it only expresses the state of one who witnessed and was confused about his matter, as for one who heard and remained silent, he did not mention him, and God knows best. And God writes down what they spend the night meaning He records it in their records of deeds to reward them for it. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is that He sends it down to you in the book. And in this verse is evidence that mere saying does not benefit anything as we mentioned, for they said: obedience and they uttered it, and God did not verify their obedience nor did He rule for them that it is valid because they did not believe in it. So it is proven that the obedient one cannot be obedient except by believing in it with its existence. God the Almighty says: “So turn away from them and rely upon God, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs. Will they not then reflect upon the Qur’an?” God the Almighty says: So turn away from them meaning do not tell Ad-Dahhak by their names, meaning the hypocrites. It was said: Do not punish them. Then He ordered him to rely upon Him and trust in Him for victory over his enemy. It was said: This was abrogated by God the Almighty’s saying: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites (al-Tawbah 9:73). Then He criticized the hypocrites for turning away from reflecting upon the Qur’an and thinking about it and its meanings. To reflect upon something is to think about its consequences. In the hadith: Do not turn your backs on one another means that none of you should turn his back on another. The people turned their backs, and their affair went on until its end. Tadbeer means that a person tadbeer his affair as if he is looking at what his end will be. This verse and the Almighty's saying: Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts? (Muhammad 47:24) indicate the necessity of reflecting upon the Qur'an in order to know its meaning. This was a response to the corruption of the statement of those who said: Nothing is to be taken from its interpretation except what was proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they forbade it from being interpreted in a way that is permissible in the Arabic language. It is evidence of the command to look and reason and invalidate imitation, and it is evidence of establishing analogy. God the Almighty said: And if it had been from other than God, they would have found within it much discrepancy. That is, disparity and contradiction, according to Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, and Ibn Zayd. This does not include the difference in the words of the recitations, the words of the proverbs and the indications, and the lengths of the chapters and verses. Rather, what is meant is the difference of contradiction and disparity. It was said: The meaning is that if what you are reporting was from God, it would be different. It was said: There is no speaker who speaks much except that much discrepancy is found in his speech, either in the description and wording, or in the existence of the meaning, or in contradiction, or in falsehood. So God the Almighty revealed the Qur’an and commanded them to ponder it, because they do not find in it any discrepancy in its arrangement, or any rejection of its meaning, or any contradiction or falsehood in what they report of the unseen and what they conceal.
4:82: God Almighty says: Do they not then consider the Qur’an carefully? Had it been from other than God, they would surely have found therein much discrepancy.
4:83: The Almighty’s saying: And when there comes to them information about security “if” has the meaning of a condition and it is not rewarded with it even if ma is added to it, and fi is rarely used. Sibawayh said: What Ka’b ibn Zuhair said is good: And if you wish, you can send it out from the sunset, active and terrified. It means that the good does not make a definite judgment - if - as it was not made a definite judgment in the verse and it was mentioned at the beginning of Al-Baqarah and the meaning is that if they heard something about matters in which there was security such as the victory of the Muslims and the killing of their enemy or fear which is the opposite of this they would spread it meaning they would divulge it and show it and talk about it before they knew its truth so it was said: This was from the weakness of the Muslims, from Al-Hasan, because they would divulge the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they would think that there was nothing wrong with them in that and Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said: It is about the hypocrites so they were forbidden from that because of what would befall them of lying in spreading rumors. God the Almighty said: And if they had referred it back to the Messenger or to those in authority among them meaning, they would not have spoken of it or divulged it until the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was the one who spoke of it and divulged it. Or those in authority, who are the people of knowledge and jurisprudence, according to Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others. As-Suddi and Ibn Zayd: the governors. And it was said: the commanders of the raiding parties. The ones who extract it among them would have known about it meaning, they would have extracted it. Meaning, they would have known what should be divulged and what should be concealed. Extraction is derived from the verb istanabatat al-ma’ meaning to extract it. The Nabataeans are called Nabataeans because they extract what is in the earth. Extraction in the language means extraction, and it indicates independent reasoning when there is no text or consensus, as mentioned above. The Almighty’s saying: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy is raised by the beginning according to Sibawayh, and it is not permissible for the report to appear according to him. The Kufians say: You would have followed Satan, except for a few is raised in this verse. There are three sayings. Ibn Abbas and others said: The meaning is that they spread it except for a few of them. It was not spread or diffused. A group of grammarians said this: Al-Kisa’i, Al-Akhfash, Abu Ubaid, and Abu Hatim Al-Tabari. And in: The meaning is for his knowledge that they deduce from them except for a few of them, according to Al-Hasan and others. Al-Zajjaj chose it. He said: Because this deduction is known to most, because it is a question of report. Al-Farra’ chose the first. He said: Because the knowledge of the raids, if it appears, its knowledge is derived and others, and the broadcasting is in some and not in others. Al-Kalbi said about him: Therefore, I found the exception from the broadcasting to be good. Al-Nahhas said: These are two sayings based on metaphor, meaning that there is an advancement and delay in the speech. A third saying without metaphor: The meaning is: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, that He sent among you a Messenger who established the proof among you, you would have disbelieved and associated others with God, except for a few of you, because he was monotheist and in it. Fourth statement: Al-Dahhak said: The meaning is that you would have followed Satan except a few, meaning that the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, told themselves about a matter from Satan except a few, meaning those whose hearts God tested for piety. According to this statement, his statement except a few is an exception to his statement you would have followed Satan. Al-Mahdawi said: Most scholars rejected this statement, because if it were not for God’s grace and mercy, all people would have followed Satan.
4:84: The Almighty’s saying: So fight in the cause of God This fa is related to His saying: And whoever fights in the cause of God and is killed or is victorious, We will give him a great reward. “So fight in the cause of God” means for this reason, fight. It was said: It is related to His saying: And what is the matter with you that you do not fight in the cause of God? “So fight” as if this meaning is: Do not abandon jihad against the enemy and seeking victory over them for the weak believers even if you are alone because victory has been guaranteed to him. Ibn Atiyah said: This is the apparent meaning of the wording, except that it has never come in any report that fighting was made obligatory for him but not for the nation for a period of time. So the meaning, and God knows best, is that it is addressed to him in the wording, and it is an example of what is said to each person in particular, meaning you, O Muhammad, and to each one of your nation, the saying to him: So fight in the cause of God, you are only responsible for yourself. For this reason, every believer should strive even if he is alone. Among that is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: By God, I will fight them until my forelock is separated.” And Abu Bakr’s saying at the time of apostasy: If my right hand opposes me, I will fight it with my left. It was said that this verse was revealed during the season of Badr al-Sughra, for when Abu Sufyan returned from Uhud, he made an appointment with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the season of Badr al-Sughra. When the appointed time came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to it with seventy riders, but Abu Sufyan did not attend and no fighting took place. This is in the meaning of what Mujahid said, as mentioned previously in Al Imran. The point of arrangement in this and the connection with what came before is that he described the hypocrites as being confused and spreading rumors, then he ordered the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to turn away from them and to be serious in fighting in the way of God, even if no one helped him in that. The Almighty said: You are not charged except with yourself. “You are charged” is in the nominative case because it is a future tense and it is not in the subjunctive mood because it is not the cause of the first. Al-Akhfash claimed that it is permissible to make it in the subjunctive mood. Except yourself is the predicate of what its agent is not named, and the meaning is that you are not obligated to do the actions of anyone other than yourself and you are not held accountable for them. There are three issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying, And urge the believers, meaning urge them to jihad and fighting. It is said, I urged someone to do something, if you ordered him to do it. And someone urged someone to do something, and he devoted himself to it, and he persevered, have the same meaning. The second - the Almighty’s saying: Perhaps God will restrain the violence of those who disbelieve is a desire, and desire from God Almighty is obligatory, although desire has come in the speech of the Arabs as an obligation, including the Almighty’s saying: And the one I hope will forgive me my sin on the Day of Judgment (Ash-Shu’ara’: 82). And Muqbil said: My opinion of them is that they are in Tanufah, competing for the prizes of proverbs. God Almighty says: And God is more severe in attack meaning in power, greater in authority, and more capable of attacking what He wants. And more severe in punishment meaning in punishment. According to Al-Hasan and others, Ibn Duraid said: God struck him with a punishment, meaning He struck him with something that He punished him with. He said: And I punished the man with a punishment from punishment, and punishment is the thing that is inflicted on a person. He said: And throw a whip at their backs Third: If someone says: We see the infidels in distress and hardship, and you say: If ‘asa means certainty, then where is that promise? It is said to him: This promise has existed, and its existence is not necessarily continuous and permanent. So whenever it exists, even for a moment, for example, then the promise has been fulfilled. So God restrained the infidels’ distress at Badr al-Sughra, and they broke their covenant of war and fighting. And God spared the believers the fighting. (al-Ahzab 33:25) and at al-Hudaybiyah also from what they sought of treachery and seizing the opportunity. So the Muslims became aware of them, so they went out and took them captive. This was while the ambassadors were walking among them in the peace treaty, and this is what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: And it is He who restrained their hands from you. (al-Fath 48:24), as will come. And God cast terror into the hearts of the parties, and they turned away without killing or fighting, as the Almighty said: And God spared the believers the fighting. And the Jews left their homes and their wealth without the believers fighting them. So all of this is distress, and God restrained the believers, even though a large number of Jews and Christians entered under the jizyah, humiliated, and they left the fighting, humiliated. So He restrained… May God protect the believers from their wrath, and praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.
4:85: First - The Almighty's saying: Who will intercede? The root of intercession is shafa'ah and similar words from shafa' which means pair in number. From this comes the word shafi' because he becomes an intercessor with the one in need. From this comes the word shafu' if she brings together two milkings in one milking, and the word shafi' if she brings together a pregnancy and a child that follows her. Shafa' is the joining of one to another. Shafa'ah is the joining of the partner's property to your property. So intercession, if you join someone else to your position and means, then it is in fact a manifestation of the intercessor's status with the intercessor and the delivery of benefit to the one for whom intercession is made. The second - The interpreters differed regarding this verse. Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd and others said that it is about people’s intercession between them regarding their needs. So whoever intercedes to benefit will have a share, and whoever intercedes to harm will have a share. It was said: Good intercession is in righteousness and obedience, and bad intercession is in sins. So whoever intercedes with a good intercession to make things right between two people will deserve the reward, and whoever seeks to gossip and backbite will sin. This is close to the first. It was said: What is meant by good intercession is supplication for the Muslims, and bad intercession is supplication against them. In the Sahih report: Whoever supplicates in absentia, his supplication will be answered, and the angel will say, ‘Amen, and for you the same.’ This is the share, and likewise in evil, rather the evil of his supplication will return to him. The Jews used to supplicate against the Muslims. It was said that the meaning is: whoever intercedes for his companion in jihad will have his share of the reward, and whoever intercedes for another in falsehood will have his share of the burden. And from Al-Hasan also: The good is what is permissible in religion, and the bad is what is not permissible in it. It is as if this statement is comprehensive, and the burden is the sin and the guilt, from Al-Hasan and Qatadah. Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: It is the share and its derivation is from the cloak that the camel rider covers his hump so that it does not fall. It is said: I covered the camel if you put a cloak on its hump and rode on it. It is also said: I covered it because he did not use the whole back, but rather used a portion of the back. It is used for the portion of good and evil. In the Book of God Almighty: He will give you a double portion of His mercy (al-Nahl 16:28). The intercessor is rewarded for what is permissible even if he does not intercede because God Almighty said: Whoever intercedes and did not say intercede. In Sahih Muslim: Intercede and you will be rewarded, and let God decree through the tongue of His Prophet what He loves. Third - The Almighty’s saying: And God is ever, over all things, a Guardian. Guardian means powerful, and from this is the saying of Al-Zubayr ibn Abdul Muttalib: And I held a grudge against him and was hateful of his wrongdoing. That is, powerful: the meaning is that God Almighty gives every person his strength, and from this is his saying, peace be upon him: It is enough of a sin for a person to neglect those he provides for. As for the one who narrated it thus, meaning those who are under his power and in his grasp, such as children and others, Ibn Atiyah mentioned it, saying: I provided for him, I provided for him, I provided for him, so I am a provider and a provider. Al-Kisa’i narrated: I provide for, I provide for. As for the poet’s saying: I am disgusted with the account Al-Tabari said about it: It is not from this previous meaning and it is in the meaning of the suspended. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Muqeet is the preserver. Al-Kisa’i said: Al-Muqeet is the capable. Al-Nahhas said: Abu Ubaidah’s statement is more appropriate because it is derived from the word qut, and qut means the amount that a person preserves. Al-Farra’ said: Al-Muqeet is the one who gives every man his sustenance. It was mentioned in the hadith: It is enough of a sin for a man to waste the one he sustains. Al-Tha’labi mentioned qiyyat, and Ibn Faris narrated in Al-Mujmal: Al-Muqeet is the capable and Al-Muqeet is the preserver and the witness, and he does not have a qiyyat for a night and a qiyyat for a night, and God knows best.
4:86: It contains twelve issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And when you are greeted with a greeting. The greeting is a verb derived from hayyat, the root of which is tahiyyah, like tardiyyah, and tasmiyyah, so they assimilated the ya into the ya. The greeting is as-salaam, and the root of the greeting is supplication for life and greetings to God, meaning peace from calamities. It was also said: the kingdom. Abdullah bin Saleh Al-Ajli said: I asked Al-Kisa’i about his saying greetings are for God, what does it mean? I said: greetings are for God, like blessings, so I said: What is the meaning of blessings? He said: I did not hear anything about it, and I asked Muhammad bin Al-Hasan about it, and he said: It is something with which you worship God. So I went to Kufa and met Abdullah bin Idris, who was killed. I asked Al-Kisa’i and Muhammad about his saying greetings are for God, and they answered me with such and such. Abdullah bin Idris said: They have no knowledge of poetry or of these things. The greeting is the kingdom, and he recited: I, Qaboos, lead it until I kneel to greet him with my soldiers Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad recited: I will take him to Al-Nu'man and I will stop to greet him with my soldiers. He wants to own his kingdom and another said: I have received everything the young man has received, except for greetings. Al-Qatibi said: He said, Greetings are due to God in the plural because there were kings on earth who were greeted with different greetings. It would be said to some of them, May you never be cursed, to others, May you submit and be happy, and to others, May you live a thousand years. So it was said to us, Say, ‘Greetings are due to God,’ meaning the words that indicate the king, and God the Most High is used as a metaphor for him. The point of the arrangement is that he said before: If you go out for jihad as was previously commanded, and you are greeted during your journey with the greeting of Islam, do not say to the one who greets you, You are not a believer, but rather return the greeting, for the rulings of Islam apply to them. Second: The scholars differed regarding the meaning and interpretation of the verse. Ibn Wahb and Ibn al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Malik that this verse is about saying May God bless you to one who sneezes and responding to the one who says May God bless you. This is weak, as there is no indication of that in the speech. As for responding to the one who says May God bless you, it is something that falls under the meaning of returning the greeting, and this is the view of Malik, if it is authentically reported from him, and God knows best. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: It is permissible to interpret this verse as referring to a gift if it is for a reward. So whoever is given a gift for a reward, he has the choice: he may return it, or he may accept it and give him its value. I said: And the companions of Abu Hanifa said something similar to this. They said: The greeting here is the gift, based on the Almighty’s saying: Or return it. And it is not possible to return the greeting in kind, and the apparent meaning of the statement requires performing the greeting in kind, which is the gift, so he ordered compensation if he accepted it or to return it in kind, and this is not possible in the case of greeting. And the ruling on the gift for reward and the present will come in Surat al-Rum when He says: And whatever you give of interest (al-Rum: 39), God willing. And the correct view is that the greeting here is peace, based on the Almighty’s saying: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you (al-Mujadilah 58:8). And al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani said: They greet them with white newborns among them and the cloaks of the Idrij on the hangers. He meant: And he greets them. And on this the group of commentators have agreed. If this is proven and established, then the understanding of the verse is to say: The scholars agreed that initiating the greeting of peace is a recommended Sunnah, and returning it is an obligation, according to the Almighty’s saying: Then greet with something better than it, or return it. And they differed about whether if one of the group responds, is it sufficient or not? Malik and Al-Shafi’i held that it is sufficient and that the Muslim has responded to him like his saying. The Kufians held that returning the greeting of peace is one of the obligatory duties. They said: And peace is the opposite of returning it, because initiating it is voluntary and returning it is an obligation. If someone else responded to the one who greeted them, that would not remove the obligation of returning it from them. This indicates that returning the greeting of peace is obligatory for each person specifically, until Qatada and Al-Hasan said: The one praying responds to the greeting of peace verbally if he greets him, and that does not interrupt his prayer because he did what he was commanded to do, and the people are on the caliphate. The first ones cited as evidence what Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: It is sufficient for a group to pass by if one of them greets them, and it is sufficient for one of them to respond to them while sitting. This is a text in a disputed matter. Abu Omar said: It is a good hadith with no opposition. In its chain of transmission is Sa’id bin Khalid, who is Sa’id bin Khalid al-Khuza’i, a Madani, who is not bad according to some of them. Some of them weakened him, including Abu Zur’ah, Abu Hatim, and Ya’qub bin Shaybah. They considered this hadith of his to be objectionable, because he is the only one who heard it with this chain of transmission, and Abdullah bin al-Fadl did not hear it from Abdullah bin Abi Rafi’, between them al-A’raj in other hadiths, and God knows best. They also used as evidence “his saying, peace be upon him: A few greet many. And since they agreed that one person greets a group and does not need to repeat it to the number of the group, likewise one person responds on behalf of the group and represents the rest as a collective obligation. Malik narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The rider greets the pedestrian, and if one of the people greets, it is sufficient for them. Our scholars said: This indicates that one person is sufficient in response, because it is not said that it is sufficient for them except in what is obligatory, and God knows best. I said: This is how our scholars interpreted this hadith and made it an argument for the permissibility of rejecting one person, and there is concern in it. Third - The Almighty’s saying: “So greet them with something better than it, or return it i.e., the same.” The best response is to add: “Upon you be peace and the mercy of God” to the one who says: “Peace be upon you.” If he says: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of God,” you add in your response: And His blessings. This is the end, so there is no more. God the Almighty said, informing about the Noble House: The mercy of God and His blessings (Hud 11:73), as will be explained, God willing. If the end of the greeting is peace, you add in your response the and at the beginning of your speech and say: “And upon you be peace and the mercy of God and His blessings.” The response in kind is to say to the one who says “Peace be upon you”: “Upon you be peace,” except that the entire greeting should be in the plural form, even if the one being greeted is one person. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, who said: If you greet one person, say: “Peace be upon you,” for the angels are with him. Likewise, the response should be in the plural form. Ibn Abi Zayd said: He says: “Peace be upon you,” and the one who responds says: “Peace be upon you,” or he says: “Peace be upon you,” as it was said to him, and this is the meaning of His saying: Or return it. And do not say in your response: “Peace be upon you.” Fourth - The choice in greeting is polite in presenting the name of God Almighty before the name of the created being. God Almighty said: “Peace be upon the family of Yasin” (al-Saffat 37:130) and He said in the story of Abraham, peace be upon him: The mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house (Hud 11:73) and He said, informing about Abraham, “Peace be upon you.” And in the two Sahihs of Al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty created Adam in His image, his height was sixty cubits. When He created him, He said, “Go and greet those people, who were a group of angels sitting, and listen to how they greet you, for that will be your greeting and the greeting of your descendants.” He said, “So he went and said, ‘Peace be upon you.’ They said, ‘Peace be upon you and the mercy of God.’ He said, “And they added, ‘And the mercy of God.’” He said, So everyone who enters Paradise will be in the image of Adam, and his height will be sixty cubits. And creation has continued to decrease after him until now.” I said: This hadith, despite its authenticity, has gathered seven benefits: First - informing about the description of the creation of Adam. Second - We will enter Paradise through it by his grace. Third - Greeting the few before the many. Fourth - Presenting the name of God Almighty. Fifth - Responding in kind to their saying: Peace be upon you. Sixth - Addition to the response. Seventh - Answering everyone with a response as the Kufians say, and God knows best. Fifth: If he returns the name of the person he greeted, it is not forbidden or disliked, as it was proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said to the man who did not pray properly and he greeted him. And peace be upon you. Go back and pray, for you did not pray.” And Aisha said: And peace and God’s mercy be upon him when he told her that Gabriel sends her his peace. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. In the hadith of Aisha, it is from the jurisprudence that if a man sends a greeting to another man, he must respond as he responds to his sick person when he sees him. “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My father sends you his greetings, so he said: “Peace be upon you and your father.” Al-Nasa’i and Abu Dawud narrated from “the hadith of Jabir bin Salim, who said: I met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: “Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God.” He said: “Do not say ‘peace be upon you,’ for ‘peace be upon you’ is the greeting of the dead. Rather, say ‘peace be upon you.’” This hadith is not proven except that since it was the custom of the Arabs to put the name of the one being cursed first in evil, as in their saying: May God’s curse and wrath be upon him, God said: And upon you is my curse until the Day of Judgment. [p. 78] This was also the custom and habit of poets in greeting the dead, as in their saying: May the peace and mercy of God be upon you, Qais bin Asim, as long as He wishes to have mercy on you. The other, Al-Shamakh, said: Peace be upon you from the prince and may God's hand bless that torn skin He forbade him from doing that, not because that is the prescribed expression for the dead, “because it was proven that he, peace be upon him, greeted the dead as he greeted the living, saying: Peace be upon you, abode of a people of believers, and we, God willing, will join you.” Aisha said: I said, O Messenger of God, what should I say when I enter the graves? He said: Say, “Peace be upon you, O people of the dwellings among the believers.” The hadith will come in Surat Al-Hakam, God willing. I said: It may be possible that the hadith of Aisha and others is about greeting all the people of the graves when he enters them and looks over them, and the hadith of Jabir bin Salim is specific to greeting the passerby intended by the increase, and God knows best. Sixth: It is Sunnah for a rider to greet a pedestrian, a standing person to greet a sitting person, and a small number to greet a large number. This is what came in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The rider should greet.’” He mentioned him, so he began with the rider because of his high status and because that would keep him from being arrogant. The same was said about the pedestrian, like him. It was said: Since the one sitting is in a state of dignity, steadfastness, and stillness, he has an advantage over the one walking, because his state is the opposite of that. As for the small number greeting a large number, it is out of consideration for the honor of the group of Muslims and their majority. Al-Bukhari added to this hadith. And the young greet the old. As for the old greeting the young, Ash’ath narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he did not see the greeting of the young children. He said: Because responding is obligatory and the young child is not obligated to respond, so he should not greet them. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin that he used to greet the young children but he did not hear them. Most scholars said: Greeting them is better than leaving it. It was reported in the two Sahihs on the authority of Sayyara who said: I was walking with Thabit when he passed by some boys and greeted them. He mentioned that he was walking with Anas when he passed by some boys and greeted them. This is from his great character, may God bless him and grant him peace. He passed by and in it is training for the young and urging them to learn the Sunnah and training them in the manners of the Shari’ah in it, so follow the example: Seventh: As for greeting women, it is permissible except for young women, for fear of temptation from speaking to them with the instigation of Satan or a treacherous eye. As for old and weak women, it is good for security, as we have mentioned. This is the opinion of Ata’ and Qatadah, and Malik and a group of scholars agreed with it. The Kufians forbade it if there were no mahrams among them, and they said: Since women are no longer required to perform the call to prayer, the call to prayer, and to recite aloud in prayer, they are no longer required to return the greeting, so they are not to greet them. The first is correct, as narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d, who said: We used to rejoice on Friday. I said: Why? He said: We had an old woman who would send for goods - Ibn Maslama said: palm trees in Madinah - and she would take some of the roots of Swiss chard and throw them in the pot and grind up grains of barley. When we prayed the Friday prayer, we would leave and greet her and she would bring it to us and we would rejoice because of it. We would not take a nap or eat lunch except after Friday. Takrkar means grinding. Al-Qatabi said this. Eighth - The Sunnah in greeting and responding is to say it out loud, and pointing with the finger and palm is not sufficient according to Al-Shafi’i, and according to us it is sufficient if it is far away. Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: Peace is one of the names of God, the Almighty, which God placed on earth, so spread it among you. If a man greets people and they respond to him, he will have a higher degree than them because he mentioned them. If they do not respond to him, someone better and kinder than them will respond to him. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Al-Harith, who said: If a man greets people, he will have a higher degree, but if they do not respond to him, the angels will respond to him and curse them. If a Muslim responds, his response will be heard, because if the Muslim does not hear it, it is not obligatory for him. Do you not see that if a Muslim greets with a greeting that the Muslim does not hear, it is not considered a greeting from him? Likewise, if he responds with an answer that was not heard from him, it is not considered an answer. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you greet, listen. If you respond, listen. If you sit, sit with trust and do not raise one another’s speech.” Ibn Wahb said: Usamah ibn Zayd ibn Nafi’ told me: I was walking with a man from the jurists of Ash-Sham called Abdullah ibn Zakariya, and my mount stopped me urinating. Then I caught up with him and did not greet him because of his weakness. He said: Why don’t you greet him? I said: I was with you just now. He said: Even if it is true, the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to walk with trees separating them. If they met, they would greet one another. Ninth - As for the disbeliever, the ruling on responding to him is to say to him: And upon you. Ibn Abbas and others said: What is meant by the verse: And when you are greeted with a greeting, if it is from a believer, then greet in return with one better than it, and if it is from a disbeliever, then respond according to what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, by saying to them: And upon you. Ata’ said: The verse is specifically about the believers, and whoever is safe from others, it is said to him: And upon you, as came in the hadith. I said: The proof of the waw and its omission came in Sahih Muslim: You should do it without the waw, which is the clear meaning of the narration. As for the proof of the waw, there is a problem with it, because the conjunction waw requires association, so it is necessary that they be included with them in both of them, they called upon us for death or for the poison of our religion. So the interpreters of that differed in sayings: The first of them is to say: The waw is in its place of conjunction, except that we are answered upon them and they are not answered upon us, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said. And it was said that it is redundant, and it was said: for resumption, and the first is better, and the narration of deleting the waw is better in meaning, and its proof is the most correct and famous narration, and most scholars agree with it. Tenth - There is a difference of opinion about returning the greeting of the People of the Covenant, is it obligatory like returning it to Muslims? Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha’bi and Qatadah held this view, adhering to the generality of the verse and the command to return it to them in the authentic Sunnah. Malik held, as narrated by Ashab and Ibn Wahb, that it is not obligatory. If you return it, say: Upon him. Ibn Tawus chose to say in returning it to them: “May peace be upon you,” meaning may it be lifted from you. Some of our scholars chose “peace” with a kasra on the seen, meaning stones. The statement of Malik and others on this is sufficient and comprehensive, as came in the hadith. The statement about initiating the greeting with them will come in Surat Maryam, when God Almighty says, informing us about Abraham in his saying to his father, “Peace be upon you” [Maryam 47]. And in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: You will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not guide you to something that, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread peace among yourselves.” This requires spreading it among Muslims, not polytheists, and God knows best. Eleventh - He should not greet the one who is praying. If he greets him, he has the choice. If he wishes, he can respond by pointing with his finger, or if he wishes, he can hold off until he finishes the prayer and then respond. It is not appropriate to greet the one who is relieving himself. If he does so, he is not obligated to respond to him. A man entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this situation, and he said to him: If you find me or see me in this state, do not greet me, because if you greet me, I will not respond to you. And do not greet someone who is reading and interrupt his reading, and he has the choice: if he wants to respond, he can do so, or if he wants to hold off until he finishes and then responds. And do not greet someone who enters the bathroom while his private parts are uncovered, or who is busy with something that has to do with the bathroom, and whoever is otherwise, greet him. Twelfth - The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God is ever, over all things, a Keeper. It means Guardian. It was said: Sufficient, from their saying: I think that such and such is sufficient for me. And similarly, God is sufficient for you. Qatada said: Accountant, just as it is said: Akil means Muwakil. And it was said: It is a noun from accounting, and this description is good here because the meaning of the verse is that a person increases or decreases or is given the amount he brings. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, who said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a man came and greeted him and said: “Peace be upon you.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, responded to him and said: Ten. Then another man came and greeted him and said: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of God.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, responded to him and said: Twenty. Then he sat down. Then another man came and greeted him and said: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, responded to him and said: Thirty. This hadith has been explained, which is that whoever says to his Muslim brother: “Peace be upon you,” ten good deeds will be written for him. If he says: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of God,” twenty good deeds will be written for him. If he says: “Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings,” thirty good deeds will be written for him. And the same is true for the one who responds, and God knows best.
4:87: The Almighty’s saying: God, there is no god but He is a subject and a predicate. The lam in His saying He will surely gather you is the lam of the oath. It was revealed about those who doubted the resurrection. So God the Almighty swore by Himself and every lam after it is a doubled nun, so it is the lam of the oath. Its meaning is in death and under the earth until the Day of Resurrection. Some of them said: To is a connection in the speech, meaning He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection. The Resurrection was called the Resurrection because people will stand on it before the Lord of the Worlds, may He be glorified and exalted. God the Almighty said: Do they not think that they will be resurrected? For a tremendous Day, the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the Worlds? (al-Mutaffifin 83:4-6). It was said that it was called the Day of Resurrection because people will rise from their graves to it. God the Almighty said: The Day they will emerge from the graves quickly. (al-Ma’arij 70:43) The origin of the Resurrection is the waw. And who is more truthful than God in speech? is in the accusative case for clarification, and the meaning is no one is more truthful than God. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Man Azdaq read it with a zay. The rest read it with a sad, and its origin is the sad except that Because its exit is close, its location is Zay.
4:88: God Almighty said: So what is the matter with you that you are two groups concerning the hypocrites? “Two groups” means two different factions. Muslim narrated “on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Uhud, and some of those who were with him returned, and the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were divided into two groups. Some of them said: Shall we kill them? Some of them said: No. So the following was revealed: “Why are you divided into two groups regarding the hypocrites?” Al-Tirmidhi narrated it, and he added: It is good. He said: It removes the filth as fire removes the impurities of iron. He said: A good and authentic hadith. Al-Bukhari said: It is good and removes the impurities as fire removes the impurities of silver. The meaning of the hypocrites here is Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions who abandoned the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud and returned with their army after they had left, as mentioned in the chapter on Imran. Ibn Abbas said: They are people in Mecca who believed and abandoned the migration. Ad-Dahhak said: They said: If Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, appears, then we will recognize him, and if our people appear, then that is more beloved to us. So the Muslims were divided into two groups, some who support them and some who disavow them. So God Almighty said: Why are you divided into two groups regarding the hypocrites? Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman reported on the authority of his father that it was revealed about a group of people who came to Medina and pretended to be Muslims, but were struck by the epidemic and fever of Medina, so they were overwhelmed and left Medina. A group of the Prophet’s companions met them and said: Why have you returned? They said: The epidemic of Medina struck us and we were overwhelmed. They said: Do you have no example in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? Some of them said: They are hypocrites. Some of them said: They are not hypocrites, they are Muslims. Then God Almighty revealed: So what is the matter with you that you are two parties concerning the hypocrites? And God has driven them back for what they have earned. The verse until they came to Medina claiming that they were emigrants, then they apostatized after that and asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to go to Mecca to bring some of their goods to trade in. The believers differed about them, some saying: They are hypocrites and others saying: They are believers. So God Almighty explained their hypocrisy and revealed this verse and ordered that they be killed. I said: These two statements are supported by the context of the last verse of the Almighty’s saying: Until they emigrate. The first is more authentically transmitted and is the choice of Bukhari and Muslim and Tirmidhi and two groups are accusative in the state as it is said: Malik is standing from Al-Akhfash. The Kufians said: It is the report of what is for you like the report of Kan and I thought and they allowed the insertion of the definite article in it. Al-Farra’ narrated: Arkashum and Rakashum means he returned them to disbelief and reversed them. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl and Al-Kisa’i said: Rakas and Nakas means turning something upside down or returning its beginning to its end and Al-Markoos is the reversed and in the reading of Abdullah and Ubayy, may God be pleased with them, God has Rakashum. Ibn Rawahah said: They were plunged into a dark temptation as black as night, followed by temptations. That is, they relapsed. So-and-so relapsed in a matter from which he had escaped. The Rakusiya are a people among the Christians and the Sabians. The Rakis is the bull in the middle of the threshing floor and the bulls around it when threshing. Do you want to guide one whom God has led astray? That is, direct him to the reward by ruling for them as the believers rule. But you will not find for him a way. That is, a path to guidance and right conduct and seeking proof. This is a refutation of the Qadarites and others who say that their guidance was created, and it has been mentioned previously.
4:89: There are five issues in it, the first is the saying of God the Almighty: They wish that you would disbelieve meaning they wished that you would be like them in disbelief and hypocrisy. The law is the same, so God the Almighty commanded us to disavow them, saying: So do not take from them allies until they emigrate as He the Almighty said: You have no share in their guardianship until they emigrate (al-Anfal 8:72). And migration is of various types, including migration to Madinah to support the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and this was obligatory at the beginning of Islam until he said: There is no migration after the conquest, and likewise the migration of the hypocrites with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the battles, and the migration of those who converted to Islam in the land of war, for it is obligatory. And the migration of a Muslim is from what God has forbidden him, as He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: And the emigrant is the one who emigrates from what God has forbidden him, and these two migrations are established now. And the migration of the people of disobedience until they return is a discipline for them, so do not speak to them or mix with them until they repent, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did with Ka`b and his two companions. But if they turn away, seize them and kill them. He says: If they turn away from monotheism and migration, then release them and kill them. Wherever you find them. It is general in all places, both permissible and forbidden, and God knows best. Then He made an exception, which is:
4:90: The second, he said: Except those who pray meaning they are connected to them and enter into what is between them of neighborliness and alliance, meaning: Do not kill people between whom and those between you and them there is a covenant, for they are bound by their covenant. Then the covenants were abrogated and this was abrogated. This is the saying of Mujahid and Ibn Zayd and others and it is the most correct of what has been said about the meaning of the verse. Abu Ubaid said: They pray and claim kinship, and from this is the saying of Al-A'sha: If she called, she would say to Bakr bin Wael, and Bakr would curse her, and the noses would be downcast. He means if you are related, Al-Mahdawi said, and the scholars denied it, because lineage does not prevent fighting and killing the infidels. An-Nahhas said: This is a great mistake, because it goes to the fact that God Almighty forbade fighting anyone who has a lineage between him and the Muslims, and the polytheists had lineages between them and the first predecessors, and worse than this ignorance is that there was then abrogation, because the people of interpretation agree that the abrogator has a declaration of immunity, and that the declaration of immunity was only revealed after the conquest and after the wars had ended. Al-Tabari said its meaning: I said: Some scholars carried the meaning of they are related to the security, meaning that the one who is related to the people of security is safe if everyone is safe from him, not in the sense of lineage which is in the sense of kinship. And there was a difference of opinion regarding those who had a covenant between them and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it was said that they were Banu Madaj. On the authority of Al-Hasan: There was a contract between them and Quraysh, and there was a covenant between Quraysh and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ikrimah said: It was revealed regarding Bilal ibn Uwaimir, Suraqah ibn Ju’sham, and Khuzaymah ibn Amir ibn Abd Manaf, there was a covenant between them and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And it was said: Khuza’ah. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He meant by the people between whom and you there is a covenant, the Banu Bakr bin Zaid bin Manat, who were in a peace and truce. Third: This verse contains evidence of the establishment of a truce between the people of war and the people of Islam if there is an interest for the Muslims in the truce, as will be explained in Al-Anfal and Bara’ah, God Almighty willing. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: Or they come to you with their chests constricted. That is, they are constricted. Labid said: It became easy and erect like a lofty, barren trunk, its greed confined to it. That is, their chests are constricted by the height of this palm tree. And from this comes the restriction in speech, which is the restriction of speech for the speaker. And the concealment of a secret. Jarir said: And the informers have brought me down, and they have found that the one who confides in you, O Umaym, is stingy with your secret. The meaning of hasarat is hasarat, so I implied qad, as Al-Farra’ said: It is a state of the implied raised noun in ja’ukom, just as you say: so-and-so came and lost his mind, meaning his mind has gone. It was also said: It is a predicate after a predicate, as Al-Zajjaj said. That is, they came to you, then he informed and said: their chests were constrained. Based on this, hasarat is a substitute for they came to you. It was also said: Hasarat is in the accusative case as an attribute of a people. In the letter Abi, except for those who pray to a people between whom and you there is a covenant, their chests were constrained, and there is no or they came to you. It was also said: Its meaning is or they came to you men or people whose chests were constrained, so it is an attribute of a described noun in the accusative case as a state. Al-Hasan read or they came to you with the constraint of their chests in the accusative case as a state, and it is permissible to raise it as a subject and a predicate. And he narrated or they came to you with the constraint of their chests and the nominative case is permissible. Muhammad bin Yazid said: Their chests were constricted is a supplication against them, as you say: May God curse the infidel. Al-Mubarrad said: Some commentators deemed it weak and said: This requires that they not fight their people, and that is invalid because they are infidels and their people are infidels. It was answered that its meaning is correct, so not fighting the Muslims would be a challenge for them and a humiliation for their people. It was said that or has the meaning of and, as if he is saying: To a people between whom and you there is a covenant and they came to you with their hearts constricted from fighting you and fighting with you, so they hated fighting the two groups. It is possible that they had a covenant on that, so it is a type of covenant, or they said we will submit and not fight, so it is possible that this was accepted from them at the beginning of Islam until God opened their hearts to piety and expanded them to Islam. The first is more apparent. And God knows best. Or they fight is in the accusative case, meaning from fighting you. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: And if God had willed, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. God’s giving the polytheists power over the believers is by enabling them to do so and strengthening them, either as punishment and vengeance when evil is spread and sins become apparent, or as a trial and test, as God the Almighty said: And We will surely test you until We make evident those among you who strive [for the cause] and the steadfast, and We will make evident your report. (Muhammad 47:31) Or as a purification of sins, as God the Almighty said: And that God may purify those who believe. (Al Imran 3:141). And God can do whatever He wills and give power to whomever He wills over whomever He wills, if He wills. The point of organization and connection to what came before is that kill the hypocrites over whom you differed, unless they emigrate, unless they connect with those between you and them with whom there is a covenant, then they enter into what they have entered into, then they have their ruling, and except for those who came to you, their hearts are closed from fighting you or fighting their people, so they entered among you, so do not kill them.
4:91: The Almighty's saying, You will find others who desire to be secure from you and secure their people. Its meaning is the meaning of the first verse. Qatada said: It was revealed about a people from Tihamah who sought security from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that they would be secure with him and their people. Mujahid: It is about a people from Mecca. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud, who used to grant security to the Muslims and the polytheists. Al-Hasan said: This is about a people from the hypocrites. It was said: It was revealed about Asad and Ghatafan who came to Medina and converted to Islam, then returned to their homes and declared their disbelief. The Almighty said: Every time they are returned to the trial, they relapse into it. Yahya ibn Waththab and Al-A’mash read it with a kasra on the ra’ because the original is raddaw, so it was assimilated and the kasra was accepted on the ra’. To the trial means disbelief. They relapse into it. It was said: meaning you will find someone who will show you peace so that they will feel safe with you, and if a trial arises for them, they will be with its people against you. The meaning of they relapse into it is they relapsed from their covenant with whom they had made a covenant. It was said: meaning if they are called to polytheism, they return and go back to it.
4:92: It has twenty issues. The first - the Almighty’s saying: And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. This is a verse from the mothers of rulings, and the meaning is that it is not appropriate for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. So His saying and it was not is not a negation, but rather it is a prohibition and a prohibition, like His saying: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God (al-Ahzab 33:53). If it was a negation, then no believer would have ever been found to have killed a believer, because what God has negated is possible for it to exist, as God the Almighty said: It is not for you to cause its trees to grow (al-Naml 27:60). So the servants will never be able to cause its trees to grow. Qatada said the meaning is that he did not have that in the covenant of God. It was said: He did not have that in the past, just as he does not have that now in any way. Then He made an exception that is disconnected, not from the first, and it is the one in which except has the meaning of but, and the meaning is that he did not have to kill him at all, but if he killed him by mistake, then he is subject to such and such. This is the saying of Sibawayh and Az-Zajjaj, may God have mercy on them. And from the disconnected exception is the Almighty’s saying: They have no knowledge of it except the following of conjecture (An-Nisa’: 60). 157] Al-Nabigha said: I stood there in the evening asking her questions, but she couldn't give me an answer, and there was no one in the room Except for the graves, how clear they are, and the intention is like a basin for the oppressed, flogging Since the signs were not of the same kind as anyone in reality, they were not included in his statement. The same is true of his other statement: The disease has become empty, with no companions except wild beasts and the wind passing through the rooms. The other said: A town with no companions except the camels and the wild donkeys The other said: Some men are like a dung beetle, with no fruit or shade, unless they are counted among the palm trees. Sibawayh recited it, and there are many like it. One of the most creative of these is the saying of Jarir: From the whites, she did not travel far, and she did not step on the ground except the tail of a departed camel. As if he said: You did not step on the earth except by stepping on the tail of the cloak. The verse was revealed because of the killing of Ayyash bin Abi Rabi’ah by Al-Harith bin Yazid bin Abi Anisa Al-Amiri due to a quarrel that had occurred between them. When Al-Harith migrated as a Muslim, Ayyash met him and killed him, but he did not know about his conversion to Islam. When he was informed, he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what happened to me and Al-Harith was what you know, and I did not know that he had converted to Islam until I killed him, so the verse was revealed. It was said: It is a connected exception, meaning that it is not for a believer to kill a believer and not have retaliation against him unless it was by mistake, in which case he would not have retaliation against him, but there is such and such in it. Another meaning is that it is understood that it was in the sense of settled and found, as if he said: And it was not found and it was not settled, and it is not permissible for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake, since he is sometimes overcome by it. So the exception comes in these two interpretations without interruption, and in order for the verse to include in this the greatness of intention and the hideousness of its affair, as you say: It was not for you, so-and-so, to speak of this except forgetfully, out of respect for intention and purpose, while speaking of it is absolutely forbidden. It was said: The meaning is and there is no mistake. Al-Nahhas said: It is not permissible for except to have the meaning of and, and that is not known in the speech of the Arabs, and it is not correct in meaning because a mistake is not forbidden, and it is not understood from the evidence of his address that it is permissible to kill the infidel Muslim, since the blood of the Muslim is respected. Rather, he specifically mentioned the believer to emphasize his tenderness, brotherhood, compassion, and belief. Al-A'mash read it as a long khātā' in the three places. The forms of khātā' are countless and are linked by lack of intent, such as shooting at the ranks of polytheists and hitting a Muslim, or someone who deserves to be killed, such as an adulterer, warrior, or apostate, seeking him out to kill him, but he meets someone else and thinks it is him, so he kills him, then that is a khātā', or someone who shoots at a target and hits a person, or something similar. This is something that is not disputed. Khātā' is the name of khātā', and khātā' is the name of khātā', meaning to make a mistake if he did not do it intentionally. Khātā' is the name that takes the place of khātā', and it is said of someone who intended to do something but did something other than that: khātā', and of someone who did something other than what is correct: khātā'.
