Ibn al-Mundhir said: God the Most High said: It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake until His saying: And a blood money to be paid to his family, so God the Most High ruled that a believer killed by mistake is blood money, and the established Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is confirmed on that, and the scholars have agreed to say it. Second - David went to retaliation between the free man and the slave in the soul, and in everything in which retaliation is possible from the limbs, adhering to the words of God Almighty: And We ordained for them therein that a life is for a life until His words Almighty: And for wounds there is retaliation (al-Ma’idah 5:45) and his saying, peace be upon him: The blood of Muslims is equal. He did not differentiate between a free man and a slave. This is the opinion of Ibn Abi Layla. Abu Hanifa and his companions said that there is no retaliation between free men and slaves except in the case of a soul. Thus, a free man is killed for a slave just as a slave is killed for a free man. There is no retaliation between them for any wounds or limbs. The scholars agreed that the words of God Almighty: And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake do not include slaves, but rather it is intended for the free without slaves. Likewise, his words, peace be upon him: The blood of Muslims is equal are intended for the free in particular, and the majority are of the same opinion. If there is no retaliation between slaves and free men in anything less, then the soul is more deserving of that. This was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Third: The Almighty said: Then the freeing of a believing slave, meaning he must free a slave. This is the expiation that God Almighty has made obligatory in the expiation for murder and zihar as well, as will come. The scholars differed about what is sufficient of it. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i, Qatadah and others said: The believing slave is the one who has maintained the ties of faith. The minor does not suffice in this regard, and this is the correct view in this regard. Ata’ bin Abi Rabah said: The minor born among Muslims suffices. A group of them, including Malik and Al-Shafi’i, said: Anyone who has been given a ruling in his favor in praying over him if he dies and buries him suffices. Malik said: And whoever prays and fasts is more beloved to me. According to all scholars, the blind, the crippled, the one with severed hands or feet, or the paralyzed does not suffice, but according to most of them the lame and the one-eyed suffice. Malik said: Unless it is a severe limp, then it is not sufficient according to Malik, al-Shafi’i and most scholars. Amputating one of the hands or one of the feet is sufficient according to Abu Hanifa and his companions, but it is not sufficient according to most of them. It is not sufficient according to Malik for someone who is completely insane, but it is not sufficient according to Malik for someone who goes insane and regains consciousness. It is sufficient according to al-Shafi’i, but it is not sufficient according to Malik for someone who has been freed for years, but it... Malik, al-Awza’i and the people of opinion, and it is sufficient according to al-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr, and Ibn al-Mundhir chose it and said: Malik: It is not valid for someone who freed some of him, because God Almighty said: Then the freeing of a slave. And whoever frees some of him, it is not said that he freed a slave, but rather he freed some of him. They also differed in its meaning. It was said: It required a purification and cleansing of the sin of the killer, and his sin was abandoning caution and care until a man whose blood was protected perished at his hands. And it was said: It required a substitute for suspending the right of God Almighty in the soul of the slain person, because he had a right in himself, which is to enjoy life and to dispose of what He permitted him to do as living people do, and God Almighty had a right in him, which is that he was a slave of His slaves, and he deserves from the name of slavery, whether he was young or old, free or slave, Muslim or dhimmi, what distinguishes him from beasts and animals. And it is hoped that there will be from his descendants someone who worships God and obeys Him, so his killer was not free from missing out on the name that we mentioned and the meaning that we described, so therefore he included the expiation. Whichever of these two meanings it was, it shows that even if the text was raised against the killer by mistake, the killer intentionally is like him, rather he is more deserving of the obligation of the expiation than him, as will be explained. God knows best. Fourth - The Almighty said: And a blood money that is paid. Blood money is what is given in exchange for the blood of the murdered person to his guardian. Passed is paid and paid. God did not specify in His Book what is given in blood money. Rather, the verse stipulates the blood money in general and does not stipulate it on the agnates or the killer. Rather, it was taken from the Sunnah. There is no doubt that stipulating consolation on the agnates is contrary to the analogy of the principles in fines and guaranteeing damages. What is required of the agnates is not required as a punishment, nor is the sin of the killer on them, but rather it is pure consolation. Abu Hanifa believed that it is based on support, so he stipulated it on the people of his office. The reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have been proven that the blood money is one hundred camels. And her valley, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Abdullah bin Sahl, who was killed in Khaybar, to Huwaisa, Mahsiyya, and Abd al-Rahman, and that was a statement on the tongue of his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for the general writing, and the people of knowledge agreed that the people of camels must pay one hundred camels, and they differed about what is required of those other than the people of camels, so a group said: The people of gold must pay one thousand dinars, and they are the people of the Levant, Egypt, and the Maghreb, this is the opinion of Malik, Ahmad, Ishaq, the people of opinion, and al-Shafi’i in one of his two opinions, in the old days, and this was narrated from Umar, Urwah bin al-Zubayr, and Qatadah, and as for the people of silver, it is twelve thousand dirhams, and they are the people of Iraq, Persia, and Khorasan, this is the doctrine of Malik based on what he heard from Umar that he estimated the blood money for the people of the villages, so he made it one thousand dinars for the people of gold and twelve thousand dirhams for the people of silver. Al-Muzani said: Al-Shafi’i said: The blood money is camels. If they are not available, then their value is in dirhams and dinars, according to what ‘Umar valued them, a thousand dinars for those who own gold and twelve thousand dirhams for those who own silver. Abu Hanifa and his companions and Al-Thawri said: The blood money in silver is ten thousand dirhams. Al-Sha’bi narrated from ‘Ubaidah from ‘Umar that he made the blood money for those who own gold a thousand dinars, and for those who own silver ten thousand dirhams, and for those who own cows two hundred cows, and for those who own sheep a thousand sheep, and for those who own camels a hundred camels, and for those who own garments two hundred garments. Abu ‘Umar said in this hadith that which indicates that dinars and dirhams are a type of blood money, not in exchange or value, and this is what is apparent from the hadith from ‘Uthman, ‘Ali and Ibn ‘Abbas. Abu Hanifa disagreed with what he narrated from ‘Umar regarding cows, sheep and garments, and ‘Ata’, Tawus and a group of the Tabi’in said the same, and it is the opinion of the seven Madinan jurists. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: A group said that the blood money for a free Muslim is one hundred camels and no other blood money, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, imposed. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i, and Tawus said the same: Ibn al-Mundhir said: The blood money for a free Muslim is one hundred camels at all times, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, imposed. The narrations from Umar, may God be pleased with him, differed regarding the number of dirhams, and none of them are authentic from him because they are mursals. I have informed you of the doctrine of al-Shafi’i, and we say the same. Fifth - The jurists differed regarding the age of camel blood money. Abu Dawood narrated from the hadith of Amr bin Shuaib on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that whoever is killed by mistake, his blood money is one hundred camels: three young camels, thirty two-year-old camels, thirty one-year-old camels, and ten two-year-old camels.” Al-Khattabi said: I do not know of any jurists who said this hadith. Rather, most scholars said: The blood money by mistake is one-fifth. This is what the People of Opinion and Al-Thawri said, as did Malik, Ibn Sirin, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, except that they differed regarding the categories. The People of Opinion and Ahmad said: Five young camels, five young camels, five two-year-old camels, five three-year-old camels, and five two-year-old camels. This statement was narrated from Ibn Masoud. Malik and Al-Shafi’i said: Five four-year-old camels, five two-year-old camels, five two-year-old camels, and five three-year-old camels. This statement was narrated from Umar ibn Abd Al-Aziz, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Al-Zuhri, Rabi’ah, and Al-Layth ibn Sa’d. Al-Khattabi said: The People of Opinion have an effect on it, except for the narration of Abdullah ibn Khashf ibn Malik, who is unknown and is not known except for this hadith. Al-Shafi’i refrained from saying it because of the defect in the narration we mentioned, and because it includes two-year-old camels, and there is no role for two-year-old camels. A mother-in-law's blood-money in one of the charity camels. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the story of the blood-money quota that he paid the blood-money of the one killed in Khaybar one hundred camels from the charity camels, and there is no mother-in-law's blood-money in the charity camels. Ibn Umar said: Zaid bin Jubayr narrated from Khafs bin Malik from Abdullah bin Masoud that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the blood-money in the case of an accident into fifths. However, this was only transmitted by Khafs bin Malik Al-Kufi Al-Ta'i, who is unknown, because it was only transmitted from him by Zaid bin Jubayr bin Harmal Al-Ta'i Al-Jashmi from Banu Jashm bin Mu'awiyah, one of the trustworthy Kufians. I said: Al-Darqutni mentioned in his Sunan the hadith of Khafs bin Malik, narrated by Hajjaj bin Arta’ah, on the authority of Zaid bin Jubayr, on the authority of Khafs bin Malik, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the blood money for an accident should be one hundred camels, twenty of which were due, twenty were two-year-old camels, twenty were two-year-old camels, twenty were two-year-old camels, and twenty were two-year-old camels.” Al-Daraqutni said: This is a weak hadith that is not proven by those knowledgeable about hadith for several reasons. One of them is that it contradicts what Abu Ubaidah ibn Abdullah ibn Mas’ud narrated on the authority of his father with a sound chain of transmission on his authority that is not subject to criticism or interpretation. Abu Ubaidah was more knowledgeable about his father’s hadith, his school of thought, and his fatwas than Khafs ibn Malik and his peers, and Abdullah ibn Mas’ud was more pious to his Lord and more zealous in his religion than to narrate on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he would rule according to a ruling and issue a fatwa contrary to it. This is not to be imagined from Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said in a matter that was brought to him that he had not heard anything from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he had not been informed of it, his saying: I say it according to my opinion. If it is correct, then it is from God and His Messenger, and if it is wrong, then it is from me. Then it reached him after that that his fatwa on it was in accordance with the ruling of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he greeted him in the same manner, and his companions saw him at that time, and he was extremely happy, as they had never seen him, because his youth agreed with the judgment of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So if someone had this description and this was his condition, how could it be correct for him to narrate something from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and contradict it? Another aspect - which is that the hadith with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, in which he mentioned Bani al-Makhd, we do not know that it was narrated by anyone other than Khafs ibn Malik from Ibn Mas’ud, and he is an unknown man, and no one narrated it from him except Zayd ibn Jubayr ibn Harmal al-Jashmi. And the people of knowledge of hadith do not use as evidence a hadith that is narrated by an unknown man alone. Rather, knowledge is established for them by a hadith if it is narrated by a well-known, just person, or a man from whom the name of ignorance has been lifted, and the lifting of the name of ignorance from him is when two or more men narrate from him. So if this is his description, then the name of ignorance has been lifted from him and he has become known. As for the one from whom only one man narrated a hadith and he is alone in narrating a hadith, it is obligatory to refrain from narrating that hadith until someone else agrees with him, and God knows best. And another aspect - which is that we do not know anyone who narrated the hadith of Khafs ibn Malik from Zayd ibn Jubayr narrated from him, except for al-Hajjaj ibn Arta’ah, and al-Hajjaj was a man who was famous for forgery and for narrating from someone he did not meet or hear from, and he left narrating from him, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, Yahya ibn Sa’id al-Qattan, and Isa ibn Yunus after they sat with him and informed him, and they are enough for you in terms of knowledge of the man and his nobility. Yahya ibn Ma’in said: Hajjaj ibn Arta’ah’s hadith is not to be relied upon. Abdullah ibn Idris said: I heard al-Hajjaj say: A man is not noble until he abandons congregational prayer. Isa ibn Yunus said: I heard al-Hajjaj say: I go out to pray and the porters and grocers crowd me. Jarir said: I heard al-Hajjaj say: The love of money and honor has destroyed me. He mentioned other aspects, including that a group of trustworthy people narrated this hadith on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Arta’, and they differed with him about it, and other things that would take too long to mention. What we mentioned of what they mentioned is sufficient and indicative of the weakness of what the Kufians went to regarding blood money, even though Ibn Al-Mundhir, with his greatness, chose it over what will come. Hammad bin Salamah narrated that Sulayman Al-Taymi told us on the authority of Abu Majlaz on the authority of Abu Ubaydah that Ibn Mas’ud said: The blood money for an accident is five-fifths: twenty of his due, twenty of a two-year-old camel, twenty of a two-year-old camel, twenty of a two-year-old camel, and twenty of a two-year-old male camel. Al-Daraqutni said: This is a good chain of transmission and its narrators are trustworthy. Something similar to this has been narrated on the authority of Alqamah on the authority of Abdullah. I said: This is the doctrine of Malik and al-Shafi’i that the blood money is one-fifth. Al-Khattabi said: It has been narrated from a group of scholars that they said that the blood money for accident is one-fourth, and they are al-Sha’bi, al-Nakha’i, and al-Hasan al-Basri. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh also held the same opinion, except that they said: Twenty-five young camels, twenty-five of his due, twenty-five two-year-old female camels, and twenty-five young female camels. This has been narrated from ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib. Abu ‘Umar said: As for the statement of Malik and al-Shafi’i, it has been narrated from Sulayman ibn Yasar, and there is nothing in it from any companion. The people of Madinah acted on it, as did Huyayy ibn Jurayj from Ibn Shihab. I said: We have mentioned from Ibn Masoud what agrees with what Malik and Al-Shafi’i concluded. Abu Omar said: The teeth of camels in blood money were not taken by analogy or consideration, but rather were taken by following and acceptance. And what was taken by way of tradition has no place in consideration, so everyone says what was confirmed to him from his predecessors, may God be pleased with them all. I said: As for what Al-Khattabi narrated that he does not know who said the hadith of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated it on the authority of Tawus and Mujahid, except that Mujahid replaced the daughter of a young camel with thirty young female camels. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: And with the first statement I say he means the statement of Abdullah and the people of opinion which Al-Daraqutni, Al-Khattabi and Ibn Abd Al-Barr weakened. He said: Because it is the least of what was said. And with a hadith with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which agrees with this statement. I said: How strange is Ibn al-Mundhir? With his criticism and diligence, how could he say a hadith that the critics did not agree with his authenticity? But bewilderment and forgetfulness may befall a person, and perfection is only for the glory of the Majestic. Sixth - It has been confirmed from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the Chosen One, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he ruled that the blood money for an accident should be paid by the agnatic kin, and the scholars have agreed to say this. And the consensus of the scholars that the blood money for an accident should be paid by the agnatic kin is evidence that what was meant by the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying to Abu Ramtha when he entered upon him with his son: He does not commit a crime against you and you do not commit a crime against him, intentionally but not accidentally. They agreed that what exceeds a third of the blood money is on the agnatic group, and they differed regarding the third. The majority of scholars agree that the agnatic group does not bear intentional, confession or settlement, and they do not bear from the blood money of an accident except what exceeds a third, and what is less than a third is from the property of the perpetrator. A group said: The blood money for an accident is on the agnatic group, whether the crime is small or large, because whoever pays the greater pays the less, just as the blood money for intentional, from the property of the perpetrator is small or large. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i. Seventh - Its ruling is that it should be paid by the agnates, and the agnates are the agnates, and the woman’s son if he is not from her agnates is not from the agnates, nor are the brothers from the mother by the agnates of their brothers from the father and mother, so they do not have a blood money for them. Likewise, the diwan is not a blood money according to the majority of the people of Hijaz. The Kufians said: It is a blood money if he is from the people of the diwan, so the blood money is paid by the agnates for three years according to what Omar and Ali decided, because the camels may be pregnant and harm him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to give them at once for purposes: including that he used to give them as a settlement and payment, and that he used to hasten it to reconcile them. When Islam was established, the Companions were able to use this system. Ibn al-Arabi said: Abu Omar said: The scholars, ancient and modern, have agreed that the blood money is not paid by the agnates except after three years and not less than that. They have agreed that it is paid by adult men. The people of biography and knowledge have agreed that the blood money was paid by the agnates in the pre-Islamic period, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, approved it in Islam, and they were… They were rational in support, then Islam came and things went on like that until Omar made the diwan. The jurists agreed on the narration of that and the statement of it and they unanimously agreed that there was no diwan in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor did Abu Bakr adhere to it, and that Omar made the diwan and gathered the people and made the people of each region a hand and made it upon them to fight the enemy who was near them. Eighth - I said: Among the things that fall under this category and are included in its system is killing a fetus in the womb of a slave woman, which is to strike the womb of a slave woman and she delivers it alive and then it dies. All scholars said: In it is the full blood money in the case of accident and in the case of deliberate killing after the oath. It was said: Without the oath. They differed in what determines its life after their agreement that if it starts screaming or suckles or breathes a confirmed breath, it is alive, in it is the full blood money. If it is left, Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa said: Movement indicates its life. Malik said: No, unless it accompanies a long stay. The male and female are the same in the ruling according to all scholars. If she delivers it unless it accompanies a long stay. The male and female are the same in the ruling according to all scholars. If she delivers it dead, then there is a blood money for it: a male or female slave. If she does not deliver it and it dies while it is in her womb and it does not come out, then there is nothing in it. All of this is a consensus with no disagreement. It was narrated from Al-Layth bin Sa’d and Dawud that they said regarding the woman who dies from being struck in her womb and then the fetus comes out dead after her death: In it is the blood money, regardless of whether she threw it before her death. Or after her death, the only thing that counts is the life of his mother at the time of her being struck. The rest of the jurists said: There is nothing wrong with it if he comes out dead from her womb after her death. Al-Tahawi said, arguing for a group of jurists, saying: They agreed, and Al-Layth agreed with them, that if he struck her womb while she was alive and she died and the fetus was in her womb and did not miscarry, then there is nothing wrong with it. The same applies if it miscarries after her death. Ninth - The forelock should only be white. Abu Omar bin Al-Ala’ said in “The saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: In the fetus, the gharrah of a male or female slave. If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had intended the gharrah to mean something, he would have said: In the fetus, a male or female slave. But he meant whiteness, so nothing is accepted in blood money except a white boy or a white girl in whom there is no less black or black. The scholars differed about its value. Malik said: It is worth fifty dinars or six hundred dirhams, half of the tenth of the blood money of a free Muslim man, and tenth of the blood money of a free female slave. This is the opinion of Ibn Shihab, Rabi’ah, and all the people of Medina. The people of opinion said: Its value is five hundred dirhams. Al-Shafi’i said: The age of the gharrah is seven or eight years, and he is not obligated to accept it with a defect. The implication of Malik’s school of thought is that he has a choice between giving a gharrah or ten of the blood money of the mother in gold, twenty dinars if they were gold-bearing people, and six hundred dirhams in silver - if they were silver-bearing people - or one-fifth of the prescribed camels. Malik and his companions said: It is from the offender’s money, which is the opinion of Al-Hasan bin Hayy. Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i, and their companions said: It is on the agnates, and this is more correct, due to the hadith of Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba: It was narrated that two women were married to two men from the Ansar, and they quarrelled, so one of them struck the other with a pole and killed her. The two men disputed before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “A call is made for one who does not cry out, whether he eats or drinks or cries out, so what is the case with that?” He said: A rhyme like the rhyme of the Bedouins? So he ruled that there should be a blood money and that it should be paid by the woman’s blood money group. This is an authentic and sound hadith, a text in a disputed matter that requires a ruling. Since the blood money for the woman who was struck was paid by her blood money group, the fetus was also paid by analogy and consideration. Our scholars cited as evidence the statement of the one against whom he ruled: How should I pay? They said: This indicates that the one against whom the judgment was passed is specific, and he is the perpetrator. If the blood money for the fetus had been passed on the agnates, he would have said: And the one who passed the judgment on them said. And in analogy, every perpetrator’s crime is against him, except for what is proven otherwise by evidence that has no opposition, such as a consensus that cannot be contradicted, that the text of a Sunnah from the perspective of the transmission of just individuals has no opposition to it, so it must be ruled by it. And God Almighty said: And no soul earns except against itself, and no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another (al-An’am 6:164). Tenth - There is no disagreement among scholars that if the fetus is born alive, there is expiation and blood money. They differed about expiation if it is born dead. Malik said that there is a fine and expiation. Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i said: There is a fine and no expiation. They differed about the inheritance of the fine from the fetus. Malik and Al-Shafi’i and their companions said that the fine in the fetus is inherited from the fetus according to the Book of God Almighty because it is blood money. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: The fine is for the mother alone because it is a crime committed against her by cutting off one of her limbs and it is not blood money. And from the evidence that the male and female were not considered in it as is required in blood money, it indicates that it is like a limb. Ibn Hormuz used to say: His blood money is for his parents specifically, for his father two-thirds and for his female slave one-third. Whoever is alive, that is for him. But if one of them has died, it is for the remaining one of them, whether father or mother, and the brothers do not inherit anything. Eleventh - The Almighty’s saying: Except that they give charity. Its original form is that they give charity, so the ta’ was assimilated into the sad. Giving charity means giving, meaning unless the guardians and heirs of the murdered person acquit the killers of what God has obligated them to pay as blood money, so it is an exception that is not from the first. Abu Abd al-Rahman and Nabih read except that they give charity with a light sad and ta’, and Abu Amr read it likewise, except that he stressed the sad. It is permissible according to this reading to delete the second ta’, but it is not permissible to delete it according to the reading of the ya’ and in the letter of Abi and Ibn Mas’ud, except that they give charity. As for the expiation that is for God Almighty, it is not dropped by their acquittal, because he destroyed a person in the worship of God Almighty, so he must give another to worship his Lord. Rather, the blood money that is their right is dropped, and the expiation must be paid from the offender’s money and is not borne. Twelfth - The Almighty’s saying: But if he was from a people who are enemies to you, and he is a believer. This is the issue of a believer who is killed in the land of the infidels or in their wars on the grounds that he is one of the infidels. The meaning according to Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, As-Suddi, Ikrimah, Mujahid, and Al-Nakha’i is: If this killed man was a believing man who believed and remained among his people and they are like a cow, an enemy to you, then there is no blood money in it. Rather, his expiation is freeing a slave, which is the well-known opinion of Malik, and Abu Hanifa said the same. The blood money is dropped for two reasons: One of them is that the guardians of the killed person are infidels, so it is not valid to give it to them so that they may be strengthened by it. The second is that the sanctity of this one who believed but did not emigrate is small, so there is no blood money, according to the Almighty’s saying: And those who believed but did not emigrate - you have no right to their guardianship until they emigrate. (al-Anfal 8:72) A group said: Rather, the reason for dropping the blood money is that the guardians are infidels only. So whether the killing was by mistake among Muslims or among his people and they did not emigrate, or he emigrated and then returned to his people, his expiation is freeing a slave, and there is no blood money in it, so it is not valid to give it to The infidels, and if blood money was obligatory, it would be obligatory for the public treasury, so blood money is not obligatory in this case. And if the killing took place in the lands of Islam, this is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i, and Al-Awza’i, Al-Thawri, and Abu Thawr said the same. According to the first opinion, if a believer is killed in the lands of the Muslims and his people are at war, then blood money is due for the public treasury and expiation. I said: From this chapter is what came in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Usama, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent us on a military expedition and we attacked Al-Harqat of Juhayna early in the morning. I caught up with a man who said: There is no god but God, so I stabbed him. I felt bad about that and mentioned it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did he say there is no god but God and you killed him? I said: O Messenger of God, he only said it out of fear of the weapon. He said: Why didn’t you split open his heart so that you could know whether he said it or not? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not rule that he should be subject to retaliation or blood money. It was narrated on the authority of Usamah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked God’s forgiveness for me after three times and said: “Free a slave,” and he did not rule on retaliation or blood money. Our scholars said: As for the renunciation of retaliation, it is clear, since the killing was not an act of aggression. As for the renunciation of blood money, it is for three reasons: The first is because he was given permission to fight in principle, and thus he killed a respected person by mistake, such as a circumciser or a doctor. The second is because he was an enemy and he did not have a Muslim guardian to whom he owed blood money, according to the Almighty’s saying: But if he is from a people hostile to you, as we mentioned. The third is that Usama confessed to the killing, and no evidence was presented for that, and the tribe did not understand his confession. Perhaps Usama did not have money for which blood money could be paid, and God knows best. Thirteenth - The Almighty’s saying: And if he was from a people between you and whom there is a treaty This is about a dhimmi or a mu’ahid who is killed by mistake, so blood money and expiation are required. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i and Al-Shafi’i. Al-Tabari chose this and said: Except that God, the Most High, made it ambiguous and did not say and he is a believer as He said about the one killed from among the believers and from the people of war. His making it general and what was qualified before indicates that it is the opposite. Al-Hasan, Jabir bin Zaid and Ibrahim also said: The meaning is that if the one killed by mistake was a believer from a people with whom there is a treaty, then their treaty requires that they are more entitled to the blood money of their companion, so his expiation is to free him and pay the blood money. Al-Hasan read it: And if he was from a people between you and whom there is a treaty, and he is a believer. Al-Hasan said: If a Muslim kills a dhimmi, then there is no expiation upon him. Abu Omar said: As for the verse, its meaning according to the people of Hijaz is rejected by His saying: And it is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. Then God, the Most High, said: And if he was from a people meaning that believer. And God knows best. Ibn Al-Arabi said: What I think is that the sentence is interpreted as interpreting the general to the qualified. I said: This is the meaning of what Al-Hasan said and Abu Omar narrated it from the people of Hijaz. His saying, A Muslim ransom in the indefinite form does not require a specific blood money. It was said: This is about the polytheists of the Arabs who had a treaty with the Prophet, peace be upon him, that they would submit or declare war until a specified time. So whoever among them was killed, blood money and expiation were required, then this was abrogated by the saying of God Almighty: A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty (al-Tawbah 9:1). Fourteenth: The scholars agreed that the blood money for a woman is half that of a man. Abu Omar said: Her blood money - and God knows best - is half that of a man because she is entitled to half of a man’s inheritance, and the testimony of two women is equal to the testimony of one man. This is only in the case of accidental killing. As for intentional killing, there is retaliation between men and women, according to the words of God Almighty: A life for a life (al-Ma’idah 5:45), A free man for a free man (al-Baqarah 2:178), as mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. Fifteenth - Al-Darqutni narrated from the hadith of Musa bin Ali bin Rabah Al-Lakhmi, who said: I heard my father say that a blind man used to recite during the Hajj season during the caliphate of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and he said: O people, I have encountered something reprehensible. Can a blind person understand a healthy person who has sight? They both fell apart This is because a blind man was being led by a sighted man and they fell into a well. The blind man fell on the sighted man and the sighted man died. So Umar ruled that the sighted man should be given the blood money of the blind man. The scholars differed concerning a man who falls on another man and one of them dies. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr: The higher man is responsible for the lower man, but the lower man is not responsible for the higher man. This is the opinion of Shuraih, al-Nakha’i, Ahmad and Ishaq. Malik said about two men, one of whom dragged his companion until they both fell and died: The blood money is on the family of the one who pulled him. Abu Omar said: I do not think there is any disagreement about this, and God knows best - except what some of the later scholars of our companions and the companions of al-Shafi’i said: He is liable for half the blood money because he died from his own actions and from the fall of the one who fell on him. Al-Hakam and Ibn Shabrama said: If a man falls on another from the top of a house and one of them dies, they said: He is liable for the living one of them. Al-Shafi’i said about two men, one of whom hits the other and they die: The blood money of the one who is hit is on the family of the one who hits him, and the blood money of the one who hits him is wasted. He said about two horsemen who collide and die: Each one of them is liable for half the blood money of his companion because each one of them died from his own actions and the actions of his companion. This was said by Uthman al-Batti and Zafar. Malik, al-Awza’i, al-Hasan ibn Hayy, Abu Hanifah and his companions said about two horsemen who collide and die: Each one of them is liable for the blood money of the other from his family. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: And likewise with us, two ships collide if the sailor is not the ship and the rider is not the horse. It was narrated on the authority of Malik regarding two ships and two horsemen, each of them must pay the value of what he destroyed to his companion. Sixteenth - The scholars differed on this matter regarding the details of the blood money of the People of the Book. Malik and his companions said: It is half of the blood money of a Muslim. The blood money of a Zoroastrian is eight hundred dirhams, and the blood money of their women is half of that. This statement was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and Amr ibn Shu`ayb. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said the same. This meaning was narrated by Sulayman ibn Bilal on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Ayyash ibn Abi Rabia on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather: The Prophet (peace be upon him) made the blood money for a Jew or a Christian half of the blood money for a Muslim. This Abd al-Rahman was also narrated by al-Thawri. Ibn Abbas, al-Sha’bi and al-Nakha’i said: If a person is killed by mistake among the people of a covenant, do not care whether he is a believer or an unbeliever, according to the covenant of his people, the blood money is like the blood money of a Muslim. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, Uthman al-Batti and al-Hasan ibn Hayy. They made all blood money equal for a Muslim, a Jew, a Christian, a Zoroastrian, a person with whom a covenant has been made, and a dhimmi. This is the opinion of Ata’, al-Zuhri and Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab. Their evidence is the words of God Almighty: a ransom. This requires the full blood money like the blood money of a Muslim. They supported this with what Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Dawud ibn al-Husayn on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the story of Banu Qurayzah and Banu al-Nadir. That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made their blood money equal, a full blood money. Abu Omar said: This is a weak hadith, there is no proof like it. Al-Shafi’i said: The blood money of a Jew or a Christian is one-third of the blood money of a Muslim, and the blood money of a Zoroastrian is eight hundred dirhams. His proof is that this is the least that has been said about that, and the covenant is free except with certainty or proof. This statement was narrated from Omar and Othman, and Ibn al-Musayyab, Ata’, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Amr ibn Dinar, Abu Thawr, and Ishaq said it. Seventeenth - The Almighty said: But whoever cannot find meaning a slave and does not have enough money to buy one, then a fast of two months meaning he must fast two months consecutive even if he breaks his fast one day. This is the opinion of the majority. Makki said on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: Fasting for two months is sufficient for the blood money and manumission for whoever cannot find one. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: This opinion is a mistake because the blood money is on the ‘aqila and not on the killer. Al-Tabari narrated this opinion on the authority of Masruq. Eighteenth - Menstruation does not prevent succession without disagreement, and if she becomes pure and does not delay it and completes the rest of her fast with what came before, then there is nothing upon her other than that unless she is a bird before dawn, then she leaves the fast of that day knowing that she is pure, and if she does so, she starts over according to a group of scholars, Abu Omar said: They differed regarding the sick person who has fasted some of the two consecutive months, according to two opinions, Malik said: No one who is required to fast two consecutive months in the Book of God Almighty has to break his fast except for an excuse or illness or menstruation, and he has no right to travel and break his fast. Among those who said that he should build upon his illness are Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Sulayman bin Yasar, Al-Hasan, Al-Shaabi, Ata’, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Tawus. Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hakam bin Uyaynah, and Ata’ Al-Khurasani said: He should start over his illness, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and his companions, Al-Hasan bin Hayy, and one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. And he has another opinion: that he should build upon it as Malik said. Ibn Shabramah said: He should make up that day alone if there is a major excuse, such as fasting Ramadan. Abu Omar said: The argument of those who said that he should build upon it is that he is excused. In interrupting the sequence due to his illness and he did not intend it, and God has overlooked the unintentional. The argument of those who said that he should start over is because the sequence is an obligation that is not dropped due to an excuse, but rather the sin is dropped by analogy to prayer because it is consecutive rak’ahs, so if he interrupts it due to an excuse, he should start over and it is not built. Nineteenth - The Almighty’s saying: Repentance from God is in the accusative case as a source, and its meaning is a return, or the sinner’s need for repentance is greater because he did not take precautions and it was his right to take precautions. It was said: That is, let him come with fasting as an alleviation from God Almighty for him by accepting fasting instead of the slave. From this is the Almighty’s saying: God knew that you were betraying yourselves, so He turned to you in forgiveness (al-Baqarah 2:187), meaning it was made easy. And the Almighty’s saying: He knew that you would not be able to count it, so He turned to you in forgiveness (al-Muzzammil 73:20) Al-Muwaffiyah Twenty - And God was that is, in His eternity and everlastingness Knowing of all information Wise in what He ruled and decreed.
4:93: It contains seven issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And whoever kills from the condition and its answer his recompense is and it will come. The scholars differed regarding the description of what is relied upon in killing. Ata’, Al-Nakha’i and others said: It is the one who kills with an iron object such as a sword, dagger, spearhead, or the like that is sharpened and prepared for cutting, or with something that is known to cause death, such as heavy stones and the like. The group of those who kill intentionally said: Everyone who kills with an iron object, whether the killing is with a stone, stick, or something else. This is the opinion of the majority. Second: God the Almighty mentioned in His Book intentional and accidental killing but did not mention quasi-intentional killing. Scholars differed in their opinion about it. Ibn al-Mundhir said: Malik denied it and said: There is nothing in God’s Book except intentional killing and accidental killing. Al-Khattabi also mentioned it on the authority of Malik and added: As for quasi-intentional killing, we do not know of it. Abu Omar said: You, Malik and Al-Layth bin Saad, considered quasi-intentional killing. Whoever kills with money, in their opinion, is not usually killed for something similar, such as a bite, a slap, a whip, a stick, or the like, then it is intentional killing and retaliation is due for it. Abu Omar said: A group of the Companions and Followers agreed with their opinion. The jurists of the regions believed that all of this is quasi-intentional killing. It was mentioned on the authority of Malik and Ibn Wahb and a group of the Companions and Followers said it. Ibn al-Mundhir said: Quasi-intentional killing is practiced by us. Among those who have proven intentional killing are Al-Sha’bi, Al-Hakam, Hammad, Al-Nakha’i, Qatadah, Sufyan Al-Thawri, the people of Iraq, and Al-Shafi’i. We have narrated that on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab and Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them. I said: And this is correct, because blood is the most deserving of protection, since the basic principle is to protect it in its state, so it is not permissible except by a clear order that is not problematic. And this is problematic, because since it was uncertain between intentional and accidental, he was judged to have quasi-intentional intent, so the beating was intentional and the killing was not intentional, and it only occurred without intent, so the retaliation is dropped and the blood money is increased. And the Sunnah came with something like this. Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, the blood money for a semi-intentional mistake, whether committed with a whip or a stick, is one hundred camels, forty of which have their young in their bellies.” Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Deliberate killing is punishable by retaliation, and accidental killing is punishable by blood money, and whoever kills blindly with a stone, stick, or whip, he must pay heavy blood money in camels’ teeth.” It was also narrated from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Musa, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The penalty for semi-intentional murder is more severe than premeditated murder, but its perpetrator is not killed. This is a text. Tawus said about a man who is injured by shooting in combat with a stick, whip, or stones, he is to be killed but not executed because he does not know who killed him. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Blindness is the blind command due to partisanship, so you do not know what its direction is. Ishaq said: This is about the quarrelling of people and their killing of one another, so it is as if its origin is from blindness, which is confusion. Al-Darqutni mentioned it. Question: Those who say that it is quasi-intentional differed regarding the increased blood money. Ata’ and Al-Shafi’i said: It is thirty of his right, thirty two-year-old camels, and forty three-year-old camels. This statement was narrated from Umar, Zaid bin Thabit, Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah, and Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari. It is the school of Malik, as he says that it is quasi-intentional. The well-known school of thought is that he did not say it except in the story of Al-Mudlaji and his son, as he struck him with the sword. It was said: It is a quarter of two-year-old camels, a quarter of two-year-old camels, a quarter of two-year-old camels, a quarter of two-year-old camels, and a quarter of two-year-old camels. This is the statement of Al-Nu’man and Ya’qub. Abu Dawud mentioned it on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Asim bin Damrah on the authority of Ali. It was said: It is five-year-old camels, twenty two-year-old camels, twenty two-year-old camels, twenty three-year-old camels, and twenty two-year-old camels. This is the statement of Abu Thawr. It was said: Forty young camels to a young age, thirty to a young age, and thirty two-year-old female camels. It was narrated on the authority of Uthman ibn Affan, and al-Hasan al-Basri, Tawus, and al-Zuhri said the same. It was said: Thirty-four young camels to a young age, thirty-three to a young age, and thirty-three two-year-old female camels. Al-Sha’bi and al-Nakha’i said the same, and Abu Dawud mentioned it on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Asim ibn Damrah on the authority of Ali. Third: They differed about who is obligated to pay the blood money for semi-intentional murder. Al-Harith Al-Akli, Ibn Abi Laila, Ibn Shabrumah, Qatadah, and Abu Thawrak said that it is due from his own money. Al-Sha’bi, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Hakam, Al-Shafi’i, Al-Thawri, Ahmad, Ishaq, and the People of Opinion said: It is due from the agnatic kin. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: Al-Sha’bi’s statement is more authentic, due to the hadith of Abu Hurairah: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the blood money for the fetus the responsibility of the aggressor’s family. Fourth: The scholars agreed that the aqila does not bear the blood money for premeditated murder and that it is from the offender’s money. This was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. They agreed that the unintentional killer must pay expiation, and they differed on it in premeditated murder. Malik and Al-Shafi’i believed that the unintentional killer must pay expiation as in the case of accidental murder. Al-Shafi’i said: If expiation is required for accidental murder, then it is more appropriate that it should be required for premeditated murder. He said: If prostration is prescribed in forgetfulness, then it is more appropriate to prescribe it in intentional killing. What God Almighty mentioned in the expiation for intentional killing does not replace what is required in error. It has been said that the intentional killer is only required to pay expiation if he is pardoned and does not kill. However, if he kills in retaliation, then there is no expiation for him, which should be taken from his money. It has been said that it is required. And whoever kills himself must pay expiation from his money. Al-Thawri, Abu Thawr, and the people of opinion said that expiation is not required except where God Almighty has made it obligatory. Ibn al-Mundhir said: We say the same, because expiation is an act of worship, and it is not permissible to imitate, and it is not permissible for anyone to impose an obligation that is required of the servants of God except by a Book, Sunnah, or consensus. And there is no proof for whoever imposes expiation on the intentional killer from where I mentioned. Fifth - They differed regarding a group of people who kill a man by mistake. A group said: Each one of them must pay expiation. This is what Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Harith Al-Akli, Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr and the People of Opinion said. A group said: All of them must pay one expiation. This is what Abu Thawr said. This was narrated from Al-Awza’i. Al-Zuhri differentiated between freeing a slave and fasting. He said regarding a group of people who throw a catapult and kill a man: All of them must free a slave, and if they cannot find one, then each one of them must fast for two consecutive months. Sixth - Al-Nasa’i narrated: Al-Hasan bin Ishaq Al-Marwazi told us - a trustworthy person - he said: Khalid bin Khidash told us, he said: Hatim bin Ismail told us, on the authority of Bashir bin Al-Muhajir, on the authority of Abdullah bin Buraidah, on the authority of his father, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The killing of a believer is greater in the sight of God than the destruction of the world. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first thing for which a servant will be held accountable is prayer, and the first thing for which judgment will be passed between people is regarding bloodshed. Ismail bin Ishaq bin Nafi bin Jubair bin Mut’im narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas that someone asked him, saying: O Abu al-Abbas, is there repentance for a murderer? Ibn Abbas said to him, as if astonished by his question: What do you say? Two or three times. Then Ibn Abbas said: Woe to you! He has repentance! I heard your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The murdered man comes with his head hanging in one of his hands, his killer being held in his other hand, his veins gushing blood until they both stop. The murdered man says to God Almighty, “Lord, this one killed me.” God Almighty says to the murderer, You are miserable, and takes him to the Fire. “And on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have never disputed with my Lord about anything more than the killing of a believer, and He did not answer me. Seventh - The scholars differed on whether the premeditated murderer has repentance. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: The people of Kufa disagreed about it, so I traveled to Ibn Abbas and asked him about it. He said: This verse was revealed: “And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell.” It was the last to be revealed and nothing abrogated it. Al-Nasa’i narrated on his authority that he said: I asked Ibn Abbas: Is there repentance for someone who intentionally kills a believer? He said: No, and I recited to him the verse in al-Furqan 25:And those who do not invoke with God another deity (al-Furqan 25:68). This is a Meccan verse that was abrogated by a Medinan verse: And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and the wrath of God is upon him. It was narrated from Zaid bin Thabit something similar, and that the verse of An-Nisa’ was revealed six months after the verse of Al-Furqan, and in another narration eight months, both of which were mentioned by An-Nasa’i from Zaid bin Thabit. The Mu’tazilah went to the generality of this verse with the reports from Zaid bin and Ibn Abbas and said: This is a specification of the generality of the Almighty’s statement: And He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. They saw that the threat is inevitably effective for every killer, so they combined the two verses by saying: The estimate is: And He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills, except for the one who kills intentionally. A group of scholars, including Abd bin Umar - and it was also narrated from Zaid and Ibn Abbas - went to the fact that he has repentance. Yazid bin Harun narrated: Abu Malik and Al-Ashja’i told us from Sa’d bin Ubaydah, who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: Is there repentance for the one who kills a believer intentionally? He said: No, except Hellfire. He said: When he left, his companions said to him: Is this how you used to issue fatwas to us? You used to issue fatwas to us that if he did not kill, his repentance would be accepted. He said: I think he was an angry man who wanted to kill a believer. He said: So they sent after him and found him like that. This is the doctrine of the people of the Sunnah and it is correct, and that this verse is specific, and the evidence for specificity is verses and hadiths. They agreed that the verse was revealed about Muqays bin Dabbaba. He and his brother Hisham bin Dabbabah had converted to Islam, and he found Hisham killed among the Banu al-Najjar. He informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he wrote to them to hand over to him his brother’s killer, and he sent with him a man from Banu Fihr. Banu al-Najjar said, By God, we do not know his killer, but we will pay the blood money. So they gave him a hundred camels, then they returned to Medina. Then Muqays attacked al-Fihri and killed him with his brother, took the camels, and returned to Mecca as an apostate and disbeliever. He began to recite: I killed Faher with it and carried his blood money to the Sharia of Banu al-Najjar, the masters of Fare’ I solved my problem and realized my revolution and I was the first to return to the idols The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will not trust him in a place of safety or sanctuary. He ordered that he be killed on the day of the conquest of Mecca while he was clinging to the Kaaba. If this is proven by the transmission of the people of interpretation and religious scholars, then it should not be applied to the Muslims. Then, taking the apparent meaning of the verse is not more appropriate than taking the apparent meaning of His statement: Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds (Hud 11:114) and His statement, And it is He who accepts repentance from His servants (al-Shura 42:25) and His statement: And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. Taking the two apparent meanings is a contradiction, so it is necessary to make a specific distinction. Then, combining the verse of Al-Furqan with this verse is possible, so there is no abrogation or contradiction. That is to apply the general meaning of the verse of An-Nisa to the specific meaning of the verse of Al-Furqan, so that its meaning is that his punishment is such and such except for the one who repents, especially since the reason, which is killing, and the reason, which is the threat of punishment, are the same. As for the reports, they are many, such as the hadith of Ubadah ibn As-Samit, in which he said: “Pledge allegiance to me that you will not associate anything with God, nor commit adultery, nor steal, nor kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. Whoever among you fulfills his pledge, his reward is with God. Whoever commits any of that and is punished for it, it is an expiation for him. Whoever commits any of that and God conceals it, his matter is up to God. If God wills, He will pardon him, and if He wills, He will punish him.” Narrated by the Imams and included in the two Sahihs. And like the hadith of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the one who killed a hundred souls, narrated by Muslim in his Sunan and other authentic hadiths. Then they agreed with us about the man who testifies against him for murder and reads that he killed intentionally and the ruler comes to the guardians and the punishment is carried out on him and he is killed in retaliation, this is not followed in the hereafter and the threat is not enforced on him by consensus based on the requirement of the hadith of Ubadah, so what they relied on from the generality of the Almighty’s saying: And whoever kills a believer by mistake - the freeing of a slave and the entry of the specification with what we mentioned was broken on them, and if that is the case then the face is that this verse is specific as we explained or it is carried on what was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: intentionally meaning he considers his killing permissible, this also says to the thought by consensus and a group said: The killer is in the will whether he repents or does not repent, Abu Hanifa and his companions said it. If it is said: The Almighty’s saying: Then his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and the wrath and the curse of God are upon him is evidence of his disbelief because God the Almighty does not become angry except with a disbeliever who has left the faith, we say: This is a threat and breaking the threat is generosity as he said: Whenever I promise him or promise him, I will break my promise and fulfill my promise. It was presented: A second answer - if He rewards him with that, meaning he is worthy of that and deserving of it because of his great sin. This was stated by Abu Majlaz Lahiq bin Hamid, Abu Salih, and others. Anas bin Malik narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If God promises a reward to a servant, He will fulfill it, and if He threatens him with punishment, then He has the will, if He wills, He will pardon him. And in these two interpretations there is an entry. As for the first, Al-Qushayri said: And there is a consideration in this, because the speech of the Lord does not accept contradiction unless it is intended to specify the general, then it is permissible in speech. As for the second, even if it was narrated that it is elevated, Al-Nahhas said: And this is the wrong aspect in it, and God Almighty said: That is their recompense - Hell for what they disbelieved (al-Kahf 18:106) and no one said: If He recompenses them, and this is a mistake in Arabic because after it is and the wrath of God is upon him, and it is interpreted to mean He recompensed him. And a third answer - then his recompense if he does not repent and persists in the sin until he meets his Lord in disbelief is the evil of sins. Hibat God mentioned in the book of the abrogating and abrogated that this verse was abrogated by the saying of God Almighty: And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he said: This is the consensus of the people except Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar, for they said it is decisive, and in what he said there is a consideration because it is a place of generality and specification, not a place of abrogation. Ibn Atiyah said it. I said: This is good because abrogation does not enter into the report, but rather the meaning is that it is sufficient for him. Al-Nahhas said: In the meanings of the Qur’an for him: The saying about it among the scholars of insight is that it is decisive and that it is sufficient for him if he does not repent. If he repents, then his matter has been made clear by His saying: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents. (Ta-Ha 20:82) So this does not go beyond it, and eternity does not require permanence. God Almighty said: And We have not granted to any human being before you immortality. (al-Anbiya 21:34) And God Almighty said: He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal. (al-Humazah 104:3) And Zuhair said: Nothing is eternal except the mountains All of this indicates that eternity is used in a sense other than eternity, as this disappears with the disappearance of the world. Similarly, the Arabs say: I will make so-and-so eternal in prison. Prison ends and perishes, as does the prisoner. Similar to this is their saying in supplication: May God make his kingdom eternal and his days everlasting. All of this has been presented previously, both in wording and meaning, and praise be to God.
4:94: It contains eleven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, when you go forth in the cause of God, investigate. This is connected to that of killing, jihad, and going forth: traveling on the earth. The Arabs say: I went forth on the earth if I went forth for trade, or for a raid, or something else, coupled with fi. And they say: I went forth on the earth without fi if I intended to relieve myself. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Two men should not go out to relieve themselves, talking, and exposing their private parts, for God hates that. This verse was revealed about a group of Muslims who, on their journey, passed by a man who had a camel and spoils to sell. He greeted the people and said: There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God. One of them attacked him and killed him. When he mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he was upset, and the verse was revealed. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There was a man with his spoils, and the Muslims caught up with him and said: Peace be upon you. They killed him and took his spoils. Then God Almighty revealed this until His saying: The offering of the life of this world. That is the spoils. He said: Ibn Abbas read the peace in a place other than Bukhari, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, carried his blood money to his family and returned his spoils to him. There was a difference of opinion regarding the identification of the killer and the one killed in these places. What is most agreed upon, and it is in the biography of Ibn Ishaq, the Musannaf of Abu Dawud, and Al-Isti’ab by Ibn Abd al-Barr, is that the killer is Muhlim ibn Jaththama and the one killed is Amir ibn al-Adbat. So he, peace be upon him, prayed against Muhlim, and he did not live after that for more than seven days. Then he was buried, but the earth did not accept him. Then he was buried, but it did not accept him. Then he was buried a third time, but it did not accept him. When they saw that the earth would not accept him, they threw him in some of those valleys. And he, peace be upon him, said: The earth accepts those who are worse than him. Al-Hasan said: It holds back those who are worse than him, but he advised the people not to return. In Sunan Ibn Majah, on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent an army of Muslims to the polytheists, and they fought them fiercely until they surrendered their shoulders. Then a man of my flesh attacked a polytheist with a spear. When he covered him, he said: I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I am a Muslim. So he stabbed him and killed him. Then he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I am ruined. What have I done? Once or twice. Then he told him what he had done. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Why didn’t you cut open his stomach so that I could know what was in his front passage? He said: O Messenger of God, if I had cut open his stomach, would I have known what was in his heart? He said: No, neither did you accept what he said nor did you know about it. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent about it. He did not remain steadfast for long until he died. We buried him and he became on the ground. We said: Perhaps an enemy dug him up. So we buried him. Then we ordered our young men to guard him. He became on the ground. We said: Perhaps the young men fell asleep. So we buried him. Then we guarded him ourselves. He became on the ground. We threw him in one of those valleys. It was said that the killer was Usama bin Zaid and the one killed was Mirdas bin Nahik al-Ghatafani, then al-Fazari, from Banu Murrah, from the people of Fadak. Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik: It was said that this Mirdas had converted to Islam that night and informed his family of that. When the matter became difficult for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he swore at that time that he would not fight a man who said: There is no god but God. This has been said before. It was said that the killer was Abu Qatada. It was said that he was Abu al-Darda’. There is no disagreement that the one whom the earth threw out when he died while he was a dream. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to the family of the rich Muslim. And the camel and its blood money were carried on the road of the coalition. And God knows best. Al-Tha’labi mentioned that the commander of that expedition was a man called Ghalib bin Fadala Al-Laithi, and it was said: Al-Miqdad, as Al-Suhayli narrated. The second - the Almighty’s saying: So verify meaning ponder and verify. This is the reading of the group, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. They said: Whoever is commanded to verify has been commanded to ascertain. It is said: I verified the matter and the matter became clear by itself, so it is transitive and intransitive. Hamza read So verify from confirmation with a triple tha’ followed by one ba’. In this, so verify is more emphatic because a person may verify and not ascertain, and in if there is a meaning of condition, so that is why the fa’ was included in his saying so verify and it may be rewarded with it, as he said: If you are in need, be patient. It is good that he is not punished for it, as the poet said: The soul desires if it desires, and if it returns to a little, it is satisfied. Verification and verification of murder is obligatory whether at home or travelling, and there is no disagreement about this. Travel was mentioned specifically because the incident in which the verse was revealed occurred while travelling. Third: The Almighty’s saying: “And do not say to one who offers you peace, ‘You are not a believer.’” As-Salam, As-Salam, and As-Salam are one and the same, as Al-Bukhari said. They were all read with it, and Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam chose As-Salam, but the people of insight disagreed with him and said As-Salam here is more appropriate because it means submission and surrender, as God the Almighty said: “So offer peace. We did not do any evil.” (al-Nahl 16:28) As-Salam means surrender and submission, meaning do not say to one who throws his hand and surrenders to you and declares your call, You are not a believer. It was said: As-Salam means his saying, “Peace be upon you,” and it refers to the first because his greeting with the greeting of Islam is a sign of his obedience and submission, and it is possible that it means turning away and abandoning. Al-Akhfash said: It is said that someone is As-Salam if he does not mix with anyone, and As-Salam with a stressed or broken sin and a silent lam means reconciliation. Fourth - It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ja`far that he read I am not a believer with the opening of the second mim from I am safe if you grant him protection, then he is a believer. Fifth: If a Muslim meets an infidel and he has no covenant with him, it is permissible for him to kill him. If he says: There is no god but God, it is not permissible to kill him, because he has held fast to the protection of Islam that protects his blood, his wealth and his family. If he kills him after that, he is killed for it. The killing is dropped for these people because they were in the early days of Islam and they interpreted it because he said it seeking refuge and fear of weapons, and that protection is saying it with reassurance, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed that he is protected no matter how he said it. Therefore, he said to Usamah: Why didn’t you split open his heart so that you could know whether he said it or not? Muslim narrated that you should look into whether he is telling the truth or lying? That is not possible, so all that remains is to clarify his tongue. In this there is a great chapter of jurisprudence, which is that rulings are based on suspicion and appearances, not on certainty and knowledge of secrets. Sixth: If he says: Peace be upon you, then he should not be killed until he knows what is beyond this, because it is a matter of doubt. Malik said about the infidel who is found and says: I came seeking protection, seeking safety: These are problematic matters, and I think that he should be returned to his place of safety and not be ruled according to the ruling of Islam, because his infidelity has been proven, so it is necessary for him to show what indicates his statement, and it is not sufficient for him to say I am a Muslim or I am a believer, nor to pray until he says the decisive word upon which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the ruling dependent on him in his saying: I was commanded to fight people until they say, There is no god but God. Seventh: If he prays or does an action that is characteristic of Islam, our scholars have differed about it. Ibn al-Arabi said: We believe that he is not a Muslim. As for it being said to him: What is behind this prayer? If he says: The prayer of a Muslim, it is said to him: Say: There is no god but God. If he says it, his truthfulness becomes clear. If he refuses, we know that this is a joke and it is considered apostasy by those who consider his Islam. The correct view is that it is original disbelief and not apostasy. Likewise, the one who said: Peace be upon you is required to say the word. If he says it, his guidance becomes clear. If he refuses, his stubbornness becomes clear and he is killed. This is the meaning of his statement: Then verify meaning the problematic matter or verify and do not rush. The two meanings are the same. If someone kills him, then he has done something forbidden. If it is said: How can the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) harsh treatment of a dreamer and his throwing him out of his grave be explained? We say: Because he knew from his intention that he did not care about his Islam, so he killed him deliberately because of the enmity that existed between them in the days of ignorance. Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: You seek the goods of worldly life meaning you seek to take his money. The goods of this world are called goods because they are fleeting and not permanent. Abu Ubaidah said: It is said that all the goods of worldly life are goods with the opening of the letter ra and from it: The world is a present commodity from which the righteous and the wicked eat. And commodity with a silent ra is everything other than dinars and dirhams. So every commodity is commodity, but not every commodity is commodity. In Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Wealth is not about having a lot of possessions, but rather wealth is the wealth of the soul. Some scholars have taken this meaning and organized it as follows: Be content with what is enough for you and use satisfaction, for you do not know whether you will wake up or go to bed. Wealth does not come from having a lot of money, but rather wealth and poverty come from the self. This corrects the statement of Abu Ubaidah: Money includes everything that is acquired. In the book: The eye of the offering is what is obtained from the world, and from it is the saying of the Most High: “You desire the goods of the world” (al-Anfal 8:67) and its plural is offering. In Al-Mujmal by Ibn Faris: The offering is what befalls a person from illness or the like, and the offering of the world is what is in it of money, little or much, and the offering of furniture is what is not cash, and the offering of something is if it is apparent and possible, and the offering is the opposite of length. Ninth - The Almighty’s saying: So with God are many spoils is a promise from God for what he brings in a way and from what is permissible without committing a forbidden act, meaning do not rush. Thus were you before meaning thus were you hiding your faith from your people out of fear for yourselves until God bestowed His favor upon you by making the religion victorious and the polytheists prevailing. They are now like this, each one of them among his people waiting to reach you, so it is not appropriate for you to kill him when he reaches you until you verify his matter. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is thus were you his disbelief, then God bestowed His favor upon you by you becoming Muslims, so do not deny that he is like this and then becomes Muslim at the moment when he meets you, so you must verify his matter. Tenth - This verse was used as evidence by those who said: Faith is the statement, because God Almighty said: And do not say to one who greets you, ‘You are not a believer.’ They said: And who prevented saying to one who said, There is no god but God, “You are not a believer,” along with those who killed them merely by saying it? And were it not for the faith that is this statement, their statement would not be faulty. We said: The people only doubted in a state that this statement was from him as a means of protection, so they killed him. And God did not make for His servants other than ruling by outward appearance. And “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’” This does not mean that faith is only the acknowledgment. Do you not see that the hypocrites used to say this statement, and they were not believers, according to what was explained in Al-Baqarah? The explanation of this was revealed by “His saying, peace be upon him: ‘Why did you not split open his heart?’” So it was proven that faith is acknowledgment and other things, and that its reality is belief in the heart, but the servant has no way to it except what he heard from him only. And this was also used as evidence by those who said: The repentance of the zindiq is accepted if he shows it. He said: Because God Almighty did not differentiate between the zindiq and others when he shows Islam, and the statement on this has already been made. At the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, there is a response to the Qadarites, for God informed us that He bestowed favors upon the believers from among all creation by singling them out for success. The Qadarites say: He created them all with faith. If it were as they claimed, then there would be no meaning to singling out the believers for favors from among all creation. Eleventh - The Almighty’s saying: Then verify. He repeated the command to verify for emphasis. Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Aware. A warning against disobeying God’s command, meaning, protect yourselves and avoid the error that will lead to your destruction.
4:95: It has five issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home. Ibn Abbas said: Not equal are those who sit at home from Badr and those who go out to it. Then he said: except those who are disabled. Disadvantage is time. The imams narrated, and the wording is from Abu Dawud, on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, who said: I was next to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was overcome by tranquility, so the thigh of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell on my thigh. I felt it heavier than the thigh of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he was relieved and said, Write. So he wrote on his shoulder, Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home, except for those who have a disability, and those who strive and fight in the cause of God, to the end of the verse. Ibn Umm Maktum, who was a blind man, stood up when he heard the virtue of the striving ones, and said, O Messenger of God, what about those of the believers who are unable to strive? When he had finished speaking, tranquility came over the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so his thigh fell on my thigh. I felt as heavy the second time as I had felt the first time. Then he was relieved and said, Read, Zaid. So I read, Not equal are those of the believers who sit at home, except for those who have a disability, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Not equal are those who have a disability, the entire verse. Zaid said: So God revealed it alone, so I attached it. By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is as if I can see its attachment at a crack in the shoulder. In Bukhari, on the authority of Muqsim, the freed slave of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, that he heard Ibn Abbas say: Those of the believers who sit at Badr are not equal to those who go out to Badr. The scholars said that those who are harmed are those who have excuses, since they have been harmed to the point that they were prevented from jihad. It is authentic and proven in the hadith that he, peace be upon him, said - when he returned from one of his battles: “In the city there are men who, if you cross a valley or travel a journey, are with you. They are people who are held back by an excuse.” This requires that the one who has an excuse be given the reward of the warrior.
