It was said: It is possible that his reward is equal, and there is plenty of grace in God’s bounty, and his reward is grace, not entitlement, so what is proven by sincere intention is not proven by action. It was said: His reward is given without doubling, so the warrior is given the doubling for the direct action, and God knows best. I said: The first statement is more correct - God willing - because of the authentic hadith on this subject, There are men in Medina, and because of the hadith of Abu Kabsha al-Anmari, “His saying, peace be upon him: The world is only for four types of people. The hadith was mentioned in Surat Al Imran. This meaning is mentioned in the hadith: If a servant falls ill, God Almighty says: Write down for My servant what he used to do when he was healthy until he recovers or I take him to Me. Second - Some scholars have held fast to this verse that the people of the diwan have a greater reward than the people of voluntary worship, because the people of the diwan, since they were possessed by the gift, and spent in hardships, and were terrified by the missions and orders, were greater than the volunteer because of his calmness and ease of mind in the great summers and the like. Ibn Muhayriz said: The people of the gift are better than the volunteer because of what they are concerned about. Makhul said: The terrors of missions negate the terrors of the Resurrection. Third: It was also related to those who said: Wealth is better than poverty, because God the Almighty mentioned the money that leads to good deeds. People differed on this issue, although they agreed that what is more needy than poverty is disliked and what is more arrogant than wealth is blameworthy. Some people preferred wealth, because the rich is capable and the poor is helpless, and ability is better than helplessness. Al-Mawardi said: This is the doctrine of those who are obsessed with the love of nobility. Others preferred poverty, because the poor is an abandoner and wealth is a garment, and abandoning the world is better than being in it. Al-Mawardi said: This is the doctrine of those who are overcome by the love of safety. Others preferred moderation between two matters by going beyond the limit of poverty to the lowest levels of wealth in order to reach the virtue of the two matters, and to be safe from the blameworthiness of the two states. Al-Mawardi said: This is the doctrine of those who see moderation as preferable and that: The best things are the middle ones, and the wise poet did well when he said: Except for seeking refuge in God from lack of wealth and from ever desiring something that is not desired. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: “except those who are harmed.” The reading of the people of Kufa and Abu Amr is except in the nominative case. Al-Akhfash said: It is an attribute of those who sit because they did not mean by them a specific people, so they became like indefinite nouns, so it was permissible to describe them with except. The meaning is that those who sit are not equal to those who are harmed, meaning that those who sit who are not harmed are not equal, and the meaning is that those who sit who are healthy are not equal, as Al-Zajjaj said. Abu Haywah read except making it an attribute of the believers, meaning from the believers who are not harmed from the healthy believers. The people of the Two Sanctuaries read except in the accusative case as an exception from those who sit or from the believers, meaning except those who are harmed, for they are equal to the mujahideen, or if you like, in the state of those who sit, meaning that those who sit are not equal to the healthy, meaning in their state of health. The state of them is permissible because their wording is the word of the definite noun, and it is like you say: Zaid came to me not sick. What we mentioned about the reason for revelation indicates the meaning of the accusative case, and God knows best. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: God has favored those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit at home by a degree. And after this He said: Degrees from Him and forgiveness and mercy. Some people said: The preference by degree then by degrees is only an exaggeration, clarification and emphasis. It was said: God favored the strivers over those who sit at home who are most harmed by one degree, and God favored the strivers over those who sit at home who are deceived by degrees. This was said by Ibn Jurayj, al-Suddi and others. It was said: The meaning of degree is elevation, meaning He raised their mention and elevated them with praise and commendation and neglect. This is the meaning of degree and degrees, meaning in Paradise. Ibn Muhayriz said: Seventy degrees between every two degrees, the noble horse attended seventy years. Degrees is a substitute for reward, explaining it. It is also permissible to put it in the accusative case based on the circumstance, meaning He favored them by degrees... nominative case, meaning He favored them by degrees. It is permissible to put it in the nominative case, meaning that it is degrees and reward, accusative with favor, and if you wish, it is a source, which is better. It should not be in the accusative case with favor because it has been He fulfilled its two objects, which are his saying the mujahideen and on those who sit, and so is the degree, for the degrees are stations, some of which are higher than others. In the Sahih, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: In Paradise there are one hundred levels that God has prepared for those who strive in His cause. The distance between each level is like the distance between the heaven and the earth. “And to each God has promised goodness.” And to each is in the accusative case with promise, and goodness is Paradise, meaning God has promised goodness to each. Then it was said: What is meant is all the strivers in particular, and it was said: the strivers and those who are harmed, and God knows best.
4:96: God Almighty says: “Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.”
4:97: What is meant by it is a group of people from Mecca who had converted to Islam and showed it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they migrated to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they stayed with their people and a group of them were tempted, so they were tempted. When the matter of Badr happened, a group of infidels left them, so the verse was revealed. It was said: When they underestimated the number of Muslims, doubts about their religion entered them, so they apostatized and were killed for apostasy. The Muslims said: These people of ours were Muslims and were forced to leave, so ask forgiveness for them, so the verse was revealed. The first is more correct. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said: A mission was sent to the people of Medina, so I signed up for it. I met Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, and I informed him. He forbade me from doing so in the strongest terms. Then he said: Ibn Abbas informed me that some Muslims were with the polytheists and they used to increase the number of polytheists during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. An arrow would come and be shot and strike one of them and kill him, or it would strike and kill him. Then God Almighty revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves. The Almighty’s saying: The angels take them may be a past tense verb that is not supported by a feminine marker, since the feminine of the word angels is not real. It may also be a future tense verb with the meaning of take them so one of the two ta’s was deleted. Ibn Furak narrated from Al-Hasan that the meaning is gather them into the Fire. It was said: take their souls, which is more apparent. It was said: The angels are meant to be the Angel of Death, based on the Almighty’s saying: “Say: ‘The Angel of Death who is put in charge of you will take you’” (al-Sajdah 32:11). Those who wrong themselves is an accusative in the state of being wronged, meaning wronging themselves, so the nun was deleted for the sake of belittling and adding, as the Almighty said: A guidance reaching the Ka’bah (al-Ma’idah 5:95). The angels’ saying: In what were you? is a question of rebuke and reproach, meaning were you among the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or were you polytheists? The saying of these al-Nas 114:We were weak in the land, meaning Mecca, is an incorrect apology, since they were able to use tricks and were guided to the path, then the angels stopped them on their religion by saying: Was not the earth of God spacious? This question and answer indicate that they died as Muslims, wronging themselves by not emigrating. Otherwise, if they had died as disbelievers, none of this would have been said to them. Rather, they were not mentioned among the Companions because of the severity of what they had done and because none of them were identified with the faith and it is possible that he would apostatize. And God knows best. Then God the Almighty excluded from them from the pronoun, which is the ha’ and the mim in their refuge, those who were truly weak from the time of men and weak women and children, such as Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, Salamah ibn Hisham, and others for whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Ibn Ayyash said: My mother and I were among those whom God meant by this verse, and that was because he was one of the parents at that time, and a slave woman, who was Umm al-Fadl bint al-Harith, and her name was Lubabah, and she was the sister of Maymuna and her other sister was Lubabah the younger, and they were nine sisters. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about them: The sisters are believers, and among them are Salma, Al-Asmaa, and Hafidah. It is said about Hafidah: Umm Hafid, and her name is Hazila. They are six sisters and three from the same mother, and they are Salma, Salama, and Asma bint Umays Al-Khathamiyyah, the wife of Ja’far ibn Abi Talib, then the wife of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, then the wife of Ali, may God be pleased with them all. The Almighty said: In what were you? It is a question of rebuke, and it has been mentioned previously. The original meaning of then was that the alif was deleted to differentiate between the question and the report, and the pause on it is in it so that the alif and the movement are not deleted. What is meant by His saying: Was not the earth of God spacious? is Medina, meaning were you not able to emigrate and distance yourself from those who oppressed you? In this verse is evidence of abandoning the land in which one commits sins. Saeed bin Jubair said: If one commits sins in a land, then leave it and recite: Was not the earth of God spacious, so that you could emigrate therein? And “It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever flees with his religion from one land to another, even if it is a handspan, deserves Paradise and is a companion of Abraham and Muhammad, peace be upon them.” Then those, their refuge is Hell, meaning their abode is the Fire. Emigration was obligatory on everyone who converted to Islam. And evil is the destination, is in the accusative case for explanation. His saying: They cannot find a way. The way is a general term for the types of means of escape, and the path is the path of Medina, according to what Mujahid al-Suddi and others mentioned. The correct view is that it is general for all paths. His saying: God the Almighty said: Then those - perhaps God will pardon them. This one who has no means to migrate has no sin that he should be pardoned for, but the meaning is that he may imagine that he must endure the utmost hardship in migration, so that whoever does not endure that hardship will be punished. So God removed that illusion, since it is not necessary to endure the utmost hardship, rather it was permissible to abandon migration when one does not have provisions and a mount. So the meaning of the verse is: Those people will not be held fully accountable for it, and for this reason He said: And God is Forgiving and Forgiving. The past and the future are one with regard to Him the Almighty, and this has been mentioned previously.
4:98: God Almighty says: Except for the weak among men, women and children who are unable to devise a plan nor are they shown a way.
16:110: God Almighty says: “Then it is those whom God may pardon. And God is Pardoning and Forgiving.” The Almighty said: Then your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient. This is all about Ammar and the meaning is they were patient in the struggle. An-Nahhas mentioned it. Qatada said: It was revealed about a group of people who emigrated to Medina after the polytheists had persecuted and tortured them. Their mention was mentioned earlier in this surah. It was said: It was revealed about Ibn Abi Sarh who had apostatized and joined the polytheists, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that he be killed on the day of the conquest of Mecca. He sought refuge with Uthman, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, granted him refuge. An-Nasa'i mentioned it on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He said in Surat al-Nahl 16:Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief, except for one who is forced, to His saying: And for them is a punishment. So a great punishment was abrogated, and he made an exception from that and said: "Then your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient. Indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful." He is Abdullah bin Saad bin Abi Sarh who was in charge of Egypt. He wrote to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but Satan made him slip and he joined the infidels. He was ordered to be killed on the day of the conquest, so Uthman ibn Affan sought protection for him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, granted him protection.
4:100: It has five issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God will find a condition and its answer: on the earth [places of refuge]. There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of maraghim. Mujahid said: maraghim is the one who moves. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi’ and others said: maraghim is the one who moves and departs. Ibn Zayd said: maraghim is the one who emigrates. Abu Ubaidah said: An-Nahhas said: These sayings are in agreement in meaning. maraghim is the one who departs and moves in a state of migration. It is the name of the place where one emigrates. It is derived from ragham and raghm anfus meaning to stick to the dirt. Raghmat fulan means to emigrate and be hostile to him, and I did not care if his nose was in rage. It was said: He was called a reluctant emigrant because when a man converted to Islam, he would oppose his people and abandon them, so his departure was called reluctant, and his return to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was called migration. Al-Suddi said: The reluctant is the one seeking a livelihood. Ibn al-Qasim said: I heard Malik say: The reluctant is going on the earth. All of this is an interpretation of the meaning, and all of it is close to each other. As for the specific word, then the reluctant is the place of the reluctant as we mentioned, and it is that each of the disputants humbles the nose of his companion by overpowering him in his desire, so it is as if the infidels of Quraysh humbled the noses of those imprisoned in Mecca, so if one of them had emigrated, he would humble the noses of Quraysh because of his protection from them, so that protection is the place of the reluctant, and this is what al-Nabigha said: Like a mountain, the dear one who is reluctant and the one who escapes seeks refuge in its corners Second: The Almighty’s saying: And abundance meaning in provision. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Al-Rabi’ and Al-Dahhak. Qatada said: The meaning is abundance from misguidance to guidance and from poverty to wealth. Malik said: Abundance is the abundance of the land. This is more similar to the eloquence of the Arabs, for with the vastness of the land and the abundance of fortresses comes abundance in provision, and an expansion of the chest for its worries and thoughts and other aspects of relief. Similar to this meaning is the saying of the poet: And if Khalil was aiming at me, I would find a wide, spacious path behind me. last: I would have a wide turbulent land in length and breadth. Third: Malik said: This verse indicates that no one may reside in a land where he curses the predecessors and acts unjustly. He said: The one who is reluctant to go to the land and the spaciousness is the spaciousness of the country as mentioned above. Some scholars also used this verse as evidence that if the warrior goes out to fight and then dies before the battle, he has his share even if he did not attend the war. It was narrated by Ibn Lahi’ah on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib on the authority of God, the Almighty, in Medina. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: And whoever emigrates from his home to God and His Messenger Al-Madinah 4:17. Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, said: I sought the name of this man for fourteen years until I found him. In this statement of Ikrimah there is evidence of the honor of this knowledge in the past, and that taking care of it is good and knowing it is a virtue. Similar to it is the statement of Ibn Abbas: I spent years wanting to ask Omar about the two women who conspired against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and nothing prevented me except his awe. The one mentioned by Ikrimah is Damrah ibn al-Ays or al-Ays ibn Damrah ibn Zinba’, as narrated by al-Tabari on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr. It is also said about him: Damrah, and it is said Jundub bin Damrah from Banu Laith, and he was one of the weak in Mecca and he was sick, so when he heard what God revealed about the migration, he said: Take me out, so a bed was prepared for him, then he was placed on it and he went out with him, and he died on the way in luxury, so God revealed about him: And whoever emigrates from his home the verse. Abu Omar mentioned that it was said about him: Khalid bin Hizam bin Khuwaylid, the nephew of Khadija, and that he emigrated to the land of Abyssinia, and a snake bit him on the way, so he died before he reached the land of Abyssinia, so the verse was revealed about him, and God knows best. Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi narrated that he was Habib bin Damrah, and it was said: Damrah bin Jundub al-Damri, on the authority of al-Suddi: It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he was Jundub bin Damrah al-Junda’i. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Jaber that he was Damrah bin Bagheeth who was from Banu Laith. Al-Mahdawi narrated that he was Damrah bin Damrah bin Na’im. It was said Damrah bin Khuza’ah, and God knows best. Muammarah narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: When the verse, Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves was revealed, a sick Muslim man said: “By God, I have no excuse. I am a guide on the road and I am well-off, so carry me.” So they carried him, and death overtook him on the road. The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If he had reached us, his reward would have been completed. He died in At-Tan’im, and his sons came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him the story. Then this verse was revealed: And whoever emigrates from his home was revealed. His name was Damrah ibn Jundub, and it is said: Jundub ibn Damrah, as mentioned above. And God is Forgiving for what he committed of polytheism, Most Merciful when He accepted his repentance. Fifth: Ibn Al-Arabi said: The scholars, may God be pleased with them, divided traveling on earth into two categories: fleeing and seeking. The first is divided into six categories: Migration, which is leaving the land of war to the land of Islam. It was obligatory during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This migration will remain obligatory until the Day of Judgment. What was cut off by the conquest is heading to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wherever he was. If he remained in the land of war, he disobeyed, and his situation differs. Second: Leaving the land of innovation. Ibn Al-Qasim said: I heard Malik say: It is not permissible for anyone to reside in a land where the Salaf are reviled. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is correct, because if you are not able to change the evil, then abandon it. God Almighty said: And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until His saying: the wrongdoers (al-An’am 6:68). Third: Leaving a land where the forbidden has become widespread: Seeking the lawful is obligatory upon every Muslim. Fourth - Fleeing from harm to the body, and this is a favor from God that He has permitted. If he fears for himself, God has permitted him to leave it and flee with himself to save himself from that danger. The first person to do this was Abraham, peace be upon him, for when he feared his people, he said: Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord (al-Ankabut 29:26) and he said: Indeed, I am going to my Lord, He will guide me (al-Saffat 37:99). And he said, informing about Moses: So he went out from it, fearing and waiting. (al-Qasas 28:21) Fifth: Fear of illness in a bad country and leaving it for a pleasant land. When the shepherds were sick in the city, they were permitted to go out to the playground and stay there until they recovered. He made an exception for leaving because of the plague, so God, the Most High, forbade it in the authentic hadith from His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Its explanation was presented in Al-Baqarah. However, our scholars said: It is disliked. Sixth: Fleeing for fear of harm to one’s money, for the sanctity of a Muslim’s money is like the sanctity of his blood, and the family is similar and more emphatic. As for the section on medicine, it is divided into two sections: seeking religion and seeking the world. As for seeking religion, it is divided into nine sections according to its types: Traveling for a lesson. God Almighty said: Have they not traveled through the land and observed what was the end of those before them? (al-Rum 30:9), and it is common. It is said that Dhul-Qarnayn only traveled the earth to see its wonders. It was said: to save the truth in it. The second - The journey of Hajj. The first, even if it was recommended, is an obligation. The third - The journey of jihad, and it has its own rules. The fourth - Traveling for a living. A man may find it difficult to earn a living while staying, so he goes out in search of it, not adding to it hunting, woodcutting, or gathering grass, so it is an obligation upon him. The fifth - Traveling for trade and earning more than food, and this is permissible by the grace of God Almighty. God Almighty said: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord (al-Baqarah 2:198) meaning trade, which is a blessing from God during the Hajj journey. So how is it if you are alone? The sixth - in seeking knowledge, which is well-known. The seventh - intending to go to the places. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Travel is not permissible except to three mosques: The eighth - the frontiers to guard them and increase their numbers for sins. The ninth - increasing brothers in God Almighty. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man visited his brother in a village, so God sent an angel to him on his path. He said, Ibn, do you want? He said, I want a brother of mine in this village. He said, Do you have a favor that you would like to bestow upon him? He said, No, except that I loved him for the sake of God Almighty. He said, Then I am the messenger of God to you, informing you that God has loved you as you loved him for His sake. Narrated by Muslim and others.
4:101: It contains ten issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: You have traveled means you have traveled. This has been mentioned before. The scholars differed regarding the ruling on shortening the prayers while traveling. It was narrated from a group that it is obligatory, and this is the saying of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, the Kufians, Judge Ismail, and Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman. They provided evidence with the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: Prayer was made obligatory, two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs. The hadith is not an argument for its contradiction, as it was performed during travel, and that weakens it. The consensus of the jurists of the countries is that it is not a principle to be considered in the prayer of a traveler behind a resident. Others from the Companions, such as Umar, Ibn Abbas, and Jubayr ibn Mut’im, said: Prayer was made obligatory when one is at home, two rak’ahs when travelling, and one rak’ah when one is fearful. Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Then the hadith of Aisha was narrated by Ibn Ajlan on the authority of Salih ibn Kaysan on the authority of Urwah, “On the authority of Aisha, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made prayer two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs.” Al-Awza’i said in it on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Urwah, “On the authority of Aisha, she said: God made prayer obligatory upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs.” This hadith is confused. Then her saying: Prayer was made obligatory is not apparent, as it excludes the Maghrib and Fajr prayers, as Maghrib has not been increased or decreased, and the same applies to Fajr. All of this weakens its text, not its chain of transmission. Ibn al-Jahm narrated that Ashhab narrated on the authority of Malik that shortening is obligatory, and the well-known view of his school of thought, and most of his companions and most of the scholars of the early and later generations, is that shortening is Sunnah, and this is the view of al-Shafi’i, and this is the correct view as will be explained, God willing. The view of most Malikis in Baghdad is that obligation is a matter of choice, and this is the view of the companions of al-Shafi’i. Then they differed about which is better. Some of them said: Shortening is better, which is the opinion of Al-Abhari and others. It was said: Completing is better. It was narrated from Al-Shafi’i and it was narrated from Saeed Al-Farawi Al-Maliki that the correct opinion in the Maliki school of thought is that one has the choice. I said - and this is what appears from the saying of God the Almighty: There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer except that Malik, may God have mercy on him, recommends shortening it, and he also sees that he should repeat it in the time if he completes it. Abu Mus`ab narrated in his Mukhtasar on the authority of Malik and the people of Medina that he said: Shortening the prayer while traveling is a Sunnah for men and women. Abu `Umar said: This is sufficient for you in the school of Malik, although there is no difference in his saying: Whoever completes the prayer while traveling should repeat it as long as he is in the time, and this is recommended according to those who understand it, not obligatory. Al-Shafi`i said: Shortening the prayer when not in fear is according to the Sunnah, but in fear while traveling, it is according to the Qur’an and the Sunnah. And whoever prays four, there is nothing upon him, and I do not like anyone to complete the prayer while traveling out of a desire for the Sunnah. Abu Bakr al-Athram said: I said to Ahmad ibn Hanbal: Can a man pray four while traveling? He said: No, I do not like the Sunnah, two rak`ahs. And in the Muwatta of Malik on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of a man from the family of Khalid ibn Asid, that he asked `Abdullah ibn `Umar and he said: O Abu Abdul Rahman, we find the prayer of fear and the prayer of residence in the Qur’an, but we do not find the prayer of travel. Abdullah bin Omar said: O my nephew, God, the Blessed and Exalted, sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to us and we do not know anything, so we do as we saw him do. In this report, shortening the prayer while traveling without fear is a Sunnah, not an obligation, because it is not mentioned in the Qur’an. Rather, the shortening mentioned in the Qur’an is if there is travel and fear and they come together, so shortening is not permitted in His Book except with these two conditions. And similar to it in the Qur’an: And whoever among you cannot afford to marry (An-Nisa’: 25) the verse was mentioned before, then the Most High said: And when you are secure, establish prayer meaning complete it, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shortened from four to two except for the sunset prayer in all his travels, in safety, fearing none but God Almighty, so that was a prescribed Sunnah from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an addition to the rulings of God Almighty like all other Sunnahs and what is not mentioned in the Qur’an. And his saying: as we saw him do with the hadith of Umar where “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about shortening the prayers while traveling without fear, so he said: This is a charity that God has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity. This indicates that God Almighty may permit something in His Book with a condition, then permit that thing on the tongue of His Prophet in exchange for that condition. Hanzala ibn Umar was asked about the prayer of travel, and he said: Two rak’ahs. I said: So where is the saying of God the Almighty: “If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you” while we are safe? He said: The Sunnah of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him. So Ibn Umar called it a Sunnah, and Ibn Abbas said the same. So where is the doctrine from them? Abu Umar said: Malik did not establish the chain of transmission of this hadith because he did not name the man who asked Ibn Umar and he omitted a man from the chain of transmission. The man whom he did not name is Umayyah ibn Abdullah ibn Khalid ibn Asadi ibn Abi al-Ays ibn Umayyah ibn Abd Shams ibn Abd Manaf, and God knows best. Second: The scholars differed regarding the distance in which the prayer is shortened. Dawud said: It is shortened in every long or short journey, even if it is three miles from where the Friday prayer is performed, adhering to what Muslim narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Yazid al-Hana’i, who said: “I asked Anas bin Malik about shortening the prayer, and he said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) went out for a journey of three miles or three farsakhs - the branch of doubt - he prayed two rak’ahs.” This is not an argument because it is doubtful, and if one of them is assumed, perhaps it is the limit of travel from which shortening began, and it was a long journey in addition to that, and God knows best. Ibn al-Arabi said: Some people have toyed with religion and said: Whoever leaves the city to its outskirts shortens and eats, and the one who says this is a foreigner who does not know how to travel among the Arabs, or he takes religion lightly. If the scholars had not mentioned it, I would not have been satisfied to glance at it with the back of my eye or think about it with the curiosity of my heart. The limit of travel for which shortening occurs is not mentioned in the Qur’an or the Sunnah. Rather, it was like that because it was an Arabic expression whose knowledge was established among the Arabs, whom God the Most High addressed in the Qur’an. We know with certainty that whoever leaves the house for some matter is not a traveler, linguistically or legally, and even if he walks for three days, he is definitely a traveler. Just as we rule that whoever walks for a day and a night is a traveler, “because the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: It is not permissible for a woman who believes in God and the Last Day to travel a day’s journey except with a mahram. This is the correct view because it is a compromise between the two situations, and Malik relied on it, but he did not find this hadith agreed upon. He narrated once: “A day and a night” and once three days. Then he came to Abdullah bin Omar and did what he did, for he used to shorten the prayer to Ra’im, which is four Bards, because Ibn Omar used to follow the example of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: All scholars agree that shortening was only prescribed as a relief, and it is only for a long journey that is often difficult. So Malik, Al-Shafi’i and their companions, Al-Layth, Al-Awza’i, the scholars of Hadith, Ahmad, Ishaq, and others considered a full day. Malik’s statement: A day and a night refers to a full day, because he did not mean by his statement: The pleasure of a day and a night is to travel the entire day and the entire night, but rather he meant to travel a distance in which he spends the night far from his family and cannot return to them. In Al-Bukhari: Ibn Omar and Ibn Abbas used to break their fast and shorten their prayers in four Bards, which is sixteen Farsakhs, and this is the view of Malik. Al-Shafi’i and Al-Tabari said: Forty-six miles. And from Malik in Al-Utaybah regarding someone who goes to his farm at a distance of forty-five miles, he said: He shortens, and this is a close matter. And from Malik in the scattered books: That he shortens in Thirty-six miles, which is close to a day and a night. Yahya bin Omar said: He repeats it forever! Ibn Abd al-Hakam: In time! The Kufians said: He does not shorten it in less than a three-day journey, and this is the opinion of Uthman, Ibn Masoud, and Hudhayfah. In Sahih al-Bukhari, “On the authority of Ibn Omar, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A woman should not travel for three days except with a mahram. Abu Hanifa said: Three days and nights, by camel travel and on foot. Al-Hasan and Al-Zuhri said: The prayer is shortened for a two-day journey. This statement was narrated from Malik and Abu Saeed Al-Khudri narrated it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A woman should not travel for two nights except with a husband or a mahram. Ibn Umar shortened the prayer to thirty miles and Anas to fifteen miles. Al-Awza’i said: The majority of scholars shortened the prayer to a full day, and we take this. Abu Umar said: The reports attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were confused in this regard, as you can see in their wording, and their summary, according to me - and God knows best - was that they came out in response to the questioners, so each one narrated the meaning of what he heard, as if “It was said to him (peace and blessings of God be upon him) at one time: Can a woman travel a day’s journey without a mahram? He said: No. And it was said to him at another time: Can a woman travel two days without a mahram? He said: No. And another said to him: Can a woman travel three days’ journey without a mahram? He said: No.” And likewise the meaning of the night and the post is according to what was narrated, so each one conveyed what he heard according to the meaning, and God knows best. And the meanings of the reports in this regard are gathered - even if their apparent meanings differ - that a woman should not travel a journey in which there is fear of temptation without a mahram, whether it is short or long, and God knows best. Third: They differed on the type of travel in which the prayer is shortened. People agreed on jihad, Hajj, Umrah, and similar travels such as maintaining family ties and reviving a soul. They differed on other matters. The majority are of the opinion that shortening the prayer is permissible in permissible travel such as trade and the like. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he said: Do not shorten the prayer except in Hajj or Jihad. Ata’ said: Do not shorten it except in a journey of obedience and for the sake of goodness. It was also narrated on his authority: It is shortened in all permissible travels, as the majority say. Malik said: If he goes out hunting, not for his livelihood, but for recreation, or he goes out to see a town for recreation and enjoyment, he does not shorten his prayer. The majority of scholars are of the opinion that there is no shortening of the prayer during a journey of disobedience, such as a rebel or a highwayman and those similar to them. It was narrated from Abu Hanifa and Al-Awza’i that shortening is permissible in all of these cases. It was narrated from Malik, and it was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah, and there was a difference of opinion from Ahmad. Once he said that the majority say, and once he said: He does not shorten his prayer except for Hajj or Umrah. What is correct is what the majority said, because shortening was only legislated to make things easier for the traveler, due to the derivatives that follow it and to help him in what he is doing, which is permissible. All journeys are the same in this regard, due to the Almighty’s saying: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you meaning sin for shortening the prayer so it is general. And he, peace be upon him, said: The best of God’s servants are those who shorten their prayers and break their fast when they travel. Al-Sha’bi said: God loves to work with permission just as He loves to work with His commands. As for traveling for disobedience, it is not permissible to shorten the prayer, because that would be helping him to disobey God, and God Almighty says: And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. (al-Ma’idah 5:2) Fourth - They differed on when to shorten the prayer. The majority are of the opinion that the traveler does not shorten the prayer until he leaves the houses of the village, and at that time he is traveling through the land. This is the opinion of Malik in Al-Mudawwana. Malik did not set a limit for proximity. It was narrated from him that if a village gathers its people, its people do not shorten the prayer until they pass it by three miles, and so on for returning. If it does not gather its people, they shorten the prayer when they pass its orchards. It was narrated from Al-Harith bin Abi Rabi’ah that he wanted to travel, so he prayed two rak’ahs with them in his house, and among them was Al-Aswad bin Zaid and more than one of the companions of Ibn Mas’ud. This is what ‘Ata’ bin Abi Rabah and Sulayman bin Musa said. I said: The meaning of the verse according to this is: And when you travel throughout the land, meaning when you intend to travel throughout the land, and God knows best. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: The traveler does not shorten his prayers on the first day until nightfall, and this is anomalous, and it has been proven from the hadith of Anas bin Malik: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the noon prayer in Medina and the afternoon prayer in Dhu al-Hulayfah, two rak’ahs. It was narrated by the imams. The distance between Dhu al-Hulayfah and Medina is about six or seven miles. Fifth: The traveler must intend to shorten the prayer from the time of entering ihram. If he begins the prayer with the intention of shortening it, then decides to stay during his prayer, he makes it a transfer. If that is after he has prayed one rak’ah, he adds another to it and says the salutation, then he prays the prayer of a resident. Al-Abhari and Ibn al-Jalab said: This, and God knows best, is recommended. If he builds on his prayer and completes it, his prayer is sufficient for him. Abu Omar said: In my opinion, it is as they said, because it is a noon prayer, whether it is a traveler’s prayer or a resident’s prayer. The same applies to the rest of the five daily prayers. Sixth - The scholars differed in this regard regarding the duration of stay that if the traveler intends to complete, he should pray it in full. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Al-Layth bin Sa’d, Al-Tabari, and Abu Thawr said: If he intends to stay for four days, he should pray it in full. It was narrated from Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab. Abu Hanifa and his companions and Al-Thawri said: If he intends to stay for fifteen nights, he should pray it in full, even if it is less, he should shorten it. This is the opinion of Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas, and there is no one among the Companions who disagreed with them, as Al-Tahawi mentioned. It was also narrated from Sa’id, and Ahmad said: If the traveler combines a stay of twenty-one obligatory prayers, he should shorten it, and if it is more than that, he should pray it in full. Dawud said the same. What Malik said is correct, based on the hadith of Ibn Al-Hadrami: “It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he made it obligatory for the emigrant to reside in Mecca after completing his rituals for three days, then to depart.” Narrated by al-Tahawi, Ibn Majah, and others. It is known that since emigration was obligatory before the conquest, residing in Mecca was not permissible, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made three days for the emigrant to complete his needs and prepare his circumstances, and he did not rule for it the ruling of the residence or the area of residence, and he left him in it the ruling of the traveler, and prevented him from residing for the fourth time, so he ruled for him the ruling of the resident resident, and this was a principle that was relied upon. And similar to that is what Omar, may God be pleased with him, did when he expelled the Jews based on the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he made a stay for them of three days to settle their affairs. Ibn al-Arabi said: I heard some of the Maliki scholars say: The three days were outside the ruling of residence because God Almighty postponed in them the one upon whom He had sent down punishment and was certain of leaving this world, so God Almighty said: “Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise that will not be denied.” (Hud 11:65) And in the matter there is a statement other than these statements, which is that the traveler shortens the prayer forever until he returns to his homeland, or stops at his homeland. It was narrated on the authority of Anas that he stayed for two years in Nishapur shortening the prayer. Abu Majlaz said: I said to Ibn Umar: I come to Madinah and stay there for seven or eight months seeking a need, so he said: Pray two rak’ahs. Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i said: We stayed in Sijistan and with us were men from the companions of Ibn Mas’ud for two years praying two rak’ahs, and Ibn Umar stayed in Azerbaijan praying two rak’ahs at a time, and the snow stood between them and the return. Abu Umar said: The interpretation of these hadiths in our view is that none of these residents had the intention for this period, but rather something like that is to say: I will go out today, I will go out tomorrow, and if that is the case then there is no determination here to stay. Seventh - Muslim narrated on the authority of Urwa on the authority of Aisha who said: God imposed prayer when He imposed it as two rak'ahs, then completed it in the city and left the prayer of travel as the first obligation. Al-Zuhri said: I said to Urwah, why does Aisha complete it while traveling? He said: She interpreted what Uthman interpreted, and this is not a satisfactory answer. People differed in interpreting the completion of Uthman and Aisha, may God be pleased with them, into statements: Muammar said on the authority of Al-Zuhri: Uthman, may God be pleased with him, prayed four rak'ahs in Mina because he had decided to stay after Hajj. Mughirah narrated on the authority of Ibrahim that Uthman prayed four rak'ahs because he had made it his homeland. Yunus said on the authority of Al-Zuhri: When Uthman acquired wealth in Taif and wanted to stay there, he prayed four. He said: Then the imams after him adopted it. Ayoub said on the authority of Al-Zuhri: Uthman ibn Affan completed the prayer in Mina for the sake of the Bedouins, because they were many at that time, so he led the people in praying four rak'ahs to teach them that prayer is four. Abu Dawud mentioned all of these sayings in his book Al-Manasik in the chapter on prayer in Mina. Abu Omar mentioned in Al-Tamhid that Ibn Jurayj said: It has reached me that Uthman completed it as four rak’ahs in Mina because a Bedouin called out to him in the mosque of Al-Khayf in Mina and said: O Commander of the Faithful, I have not ceased to pray it as two rak’ahs since I saw you in the first year. Uthman feared that the ignorant people would think that the prayer was only two rak’ahs. Ibn Jurayj said: He only completed it. Abu Omar said: As for the interpretations of Aisha completing it, there is nothing narrated from her, but rather they are assumptions and interpretations that are not accompanied by evidence. The weakest thing that has been said about that is that she is the mother of the believers and that the people wherever they are are her sons and their homes are her homes. Was I the mother of the believers, except that she is the wife of the Prophet, the father of the believers, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he is the one who established shortening in his travels and in his battles and his Hajj and Umrah? And in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka’b and the Mushaf of the Prophet, the believers are closer to themselves than their wives are to them and he is a father to them. Mujahid said about the words of God Almighty: These are my daughters; they are purer for you. Hud 11:78] He said: They were not his daughters, but they were the women of his nation, and every prophet is the father of his nation. I said: It has been objected to this that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was a legislator, and she was not like that, so they separated. And weaker than this is the statement of those who said: When she completed it, she was not on a permissible journey, and this is absolutely false, for she was more fearful of God and more pious than to go on a journey that He would not approve of, and this interpretation of it is from the lies and slander of the innovating Shia, glory be to You, this is a great slander, and she only went out, may God be pleased with her, striving and seeking reward, wanting to extinguish the fire of discord, as she is more deserving of being ashamed of, so matters went out of control, and an explanation of this meaning will come, God willing. And it has been said: She completed it because she did not see shortening except in Hajj, Umrah and military campaigns, and this is false, because that was not transmitted from her nor is it known from any school of thought. Then she completed it on her journey to Ali, and the best that has been said about her shortening and completing it is that she took the permission of God to show people that completing it is not difficult even if something else is better. And Ata’ said: Shortening is a Sunnah and a permission, and he is the narrator “on the authority of Aisha: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fasted and broke his fast, completed the prayer, and shortened it while traveling. Narrated by Talha bin Amr on his authority. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did all of that. He fasted and broke his fast, shortened the prayer, and completed it. Al-Nasa’i narrated with a sound chain of transmission: “Aisha performed Umrah with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Medina to Mecca. When she arrived in Mecca, she said: O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you! Did you shorten your prayer and complete it, break your fast and fast? He said: Well done, O Aisha.” And he did not criticize me. This is how it is restricted to opening the first ta’ and closing the second ta’ in both words. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Aisha: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to shorten and complete his prayers while traveling, break his fast, and fast. His chain of transmission says: Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: That you shorten the prayer “that” is in the accusative case, meaning that you shorten it. Abu Ubaid said: There are three languages in it: I shortened the prayer, I shortened it, and I shortened it. The scholars differed in its interpretation. A group of scholars went to the view that it is shortening to two out of four in fear and other than that, based on the hadith of Ya’la bin Umayya, as will come. Others said: It is shortening the two rak’ahs to one rak’ah, and the two rak’ahs in travel are only a completion, as Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: A completion without shortening, and shortening it is that it becomes one rak’ah. Al-Suddi said: If you pray two rak’ahs in travel, then it is a completion, and shortening is not permissible unless you fear. This verse permits each group to pray one rak’ah without adding anything to it, and the imam has two rak’ahs. Something similar was narrated from Ibn Umar, Jabir bin Abdullah, and Ka’b, and Hudhayfah did it in Tabaristan, and the prince Saeed bin Al-Aas asked him about that. Ibn Abbas narrated: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed in the same way during the Battle of Dhi Qarad, one rak’ah for each group, and they did not make it up. Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed like this with his companions on the day of the battle of Khasfa and Banu Tha’laba. Abu Hurairah narrated: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was like that between Dajnan and Usfan: I said: In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God imposed prayer on the tongue of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as four rak’ahs in the city, two rak’ahs in travel, and one rak’ah in fear. This supports and reinforces this statement, except that Judge Abu Bakr Ibn al-Arabi mentioned in his book called al-Qabas: Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: This hadith is rejected by consensus. I said: This is not correct. He and others have mentioned disagreement and dispute, so what they claim of consensus is not correct. And God is the Grantor of success. Abu Bakr al-Razi al-Hanafi narrated in Ahkam al-Qur’an that what is meant by shortening here is shortening the manner of prayer by leaving bowing and prostration to nodding, and by leaving standing to bowing. Others said: This verse permits shortening the limits of prayer and its form when fighting or war is raging, so it is permissible for someone in this state to pray by nodding his head, and to pray one rak’ah when he directs himself to the takbir, as mentioned previously in Surat al-Baqarah. At-Tabari preferred this statement and said: It is equivalent to the statement of God the Almighty: And when you are secure, establish prayer, meaning with its limits and complete form. I said: These three statements are close in meaning, and they are based on the fact that the traveler is required to shorten the prayer and that the prayer for him was only revealed as two rak’ahs, so there is no shortening. It is not said that there is no blame in what is prescribed as two rak’ahs, nor is it said that what was prescribed as two rak’ahs is shortened, just as it is not said about the dawn prayer. And God Almighty mentioned shortening with two conditions, and what is considered in it is the prayer of fear. This is what Abu Bakr al-Razi mentioned in Ahkam al-Qur’an and he used it as evidence, and he responded to it with the hadith of Ya’la ibn Umayyah as will come later, God willing. Ninth - The Almighty’s saying: If you fear. The speech was based on the most common, as fear was most common among Muslims when travelling. For this reason, Ya`la ibn Umayya said: I said to `Umar: Why should we fall short when we are safe? `Umar said: I was amazed by what amazed you, so I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and he said: It is a charity that God has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity. I said: The companions of Al-Shafi’i and others have used as evidence for the Hanafis this hadith of Ya’la bin Umayyah and said: His saying: Why should we shorten it when we are safe is conclusive evidence that the meaning of the verse is shortening the rak’ahs. Al-Kaya Al-Tabari said: The companions of Abu Hanifa did not mention an interpretation of this that is equal to the remembrance. Then the two conditions are not considered in the prayer of fear, because if he did not travel the earth and there was no travel, but the infidels came to us and invaded our country, then the prayer of fear is permissible and the presence of the two conditions is not considered according to what he said. And in the reading of Abu, it is said: Shorten the prayer lest the disbelievers tempt you with a fall if you fear. The meaning according to his reading is: Hatred that the disbelievers tempt you. It is established in the Mushaf of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, if you fear. And a group went to the view that this verse only permits shortening during travel for the one who fears the enemy, so whoever is safe does not have to shorten it. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she used to say while travelling: Complete your prayers. They said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to shorten them. She said: He was at war and was afraid. Are you afraid? Ata’ said: Among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Aisha and Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas used to pray in full, and Uthman used to pray in full, but that is explained by reasons, some of which were mentioned above. A group of people said that God Almighty did not permit shortening in His Book except on two conditions: travel and fear, and other than fear according to the Sunnah, including Al-Shafi’i, who has already mentioned it. Others said that God Almighty’s statement, If you fear, is not connected to what came before it, and that the speech ended at His statement, of prayer, then He began by saying, If you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you, then establish for them, O Muhammad, the prayer of fear. His statement, Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy, is an interjection said by Al-Jarajani, and Al-Mahdawi and others mentioned this statement, and Al-Qushayri and Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi rejected this statement. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: There is great difficulty in carrying this out, even though the man - meaning Al-Jarajani - went into great detail in estimating and giving examples. Ibn Al-Arabi said: All of this was not needed by Amr, nor his son, nor Ya’la Ibn Umayya with them. I said: A hadith has come with what Al-Jurjani said, and it was mentioned by Judge Abu Al-Walid Ibn Rushd in his introductions, and Ibn Atiyah also in his interpretation, on the authority of Ali Ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: A group of merchants asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: We travel the earth, so how do we pray? So God revealed: And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer. Then the conversation was interrupted. After a year, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on an expedition and prayed the noon prayer. The polytheists said: Muhammad and his companions have given you power over them. Why did you not attack them? One of them said: They have another prayer after it. So God revealed between the two prayers: If you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you. to the end of the prayer of fear. If this report is correct, then no one has anything to say about it, and it is evidence for shortening the prayer other than in fear in the Qur’an. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: God’s statement: And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer was revealed regarding prayer while traveling, then If you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you was revealed regarding fear a year later. So the verse, according to this, included two issues and two rulings. His statement: And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer means traveling, and the conversation was completed. Then He began another obligation, so he presented the condition and the estimate: If you fear that those who disbelieve will tempt you, and if you are among them and lead them in prayer, and the waw is redundant, and the answer is: Then let a group of them stand with you. And his saying: Indeed, the disbelievers have been to you a clear enemy. An objection. Some people have said that the mention of fear was abrogated by the Sunnah, which is the hadith of Umar, as it was narrated that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: This is charity that God has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity.” An-Nahhas said: Whoever made the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, shortening of prayers when not in fear and his action in that case abrogating the verse has made a mistake, because the verse does not prohibit shortening in times of safety, but rather it permits shortening in times of fear only. Tenth - The Almighty’s saying: That those who disbelieve may tempt you. Al-Farra’ said: The people of Hijaz say fatanat al-rajul and Rabi’ah, Qays, Asad, and all the people of Najd say aftanat al-rajul. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh differentiated between them and said: fatanathu made a temptation in him like akhaltuhu and aftanatuhu made him a tempter. Al-Asma’i claimed that he did not know aftanathu. “Indeed, the disbelievers were to you a clear enemy.” Enemy here means enemies, and God knows best.
4:102: It contains eleven issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer. Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Ayyash al-Zarqi, who said: We were with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) in Usfan when the polytheists, led by Khalid ibn al-Walid, confronted us, and they were between us and the Qiblah. The Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) led us in the noon prayer. They said: They were in a state that if we had caught them by surprise, they would have been better off. He said: Then they said: Now a prayer will come upon them that is dearer to him than their children and their own lives. He said: So Gabriel (peace be upon him) came down with this verse between noon and afternoon: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer. He mentioned the hadith, and its full details will come, God willing. This was the reason for Khalid’s conversion to Islam, may God be pleased with him. This verse is connected to what was mentioned previously about jihad, and the Lord, may He be blessed and exalted, explained that prayer is not dropped due to the excuse of travel or the excuse of jihad and fighting the enemy, but it contains concessions, as was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah, and this surah explains the difference of opinion among the scholars. This verse is addressed to the Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) and it includes the rulers after him until the Day of Resurrection. Similar to it is the statement of God, the Most High: Take from their wealth a charity (al-Tawbah 9:103). This is the statement of all the scholars. Abu Yusuf and Ismail ibn Ali were an exception, and they said: We do not pray the prayer of fear after the Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), because the address was specific. For him, by the words of God Almighty: And if you are among them, and if he is not among them, then that is not for them because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is not like others in that, and all of them loved to be followed and prayed behind, and no one after him takes his place in virtue, and the people after him are equal in their conditions and are similar, so the imam prays with a group and orders someone to pray with the other group, but as for them praying with one imam, no. The majority said: We have been commanded to follow him and take him as an example in more than one verse and more than one hadith, so God Almighty said: Those who oppose his command, lest a trial befall them or (al-Nur 24:63) and “He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Pray as you have seen me pray.” It is necessary to follow it absolutely until clear evidence indicates the specificity. If what they mentioned was evidence of the specificity, it would be necessary to limit the addresses to those to whom they were directed. In that case, it would be necessary for the Shari’ah to be limited to those to whom it was addressed. Then, the Companions, may God be pleased with them all, rejected the notion of specificity in this prayer and attributed it to other than the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are more knowledgeable about what is said and more aware of the situation. God the Almighty said: And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they engage in another conversation. (al-An’am 6:68) This is addressed to him, and his nation is included in it. There are many like it. God the Almighty said: Take from their wealth a charity. This does not require limiting it to him alone and that those after him take his place in that. The same is true of His statement: And when you are among them. Do you not see that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, in a group of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, fought those who interpreted the zakat as you interpreted the fear prayer? Abu Omar said: There is no taking of the zakat in which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those after him were equal. The caliphs are similar to the prayer of someone who prayed behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and prayed behind someone else, because the benefit of taking zakat is to deliver it to the poor, and there is no merit in it for the giver, as there is merit in prayer for the one praying behind him. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Then let a party of them stand with you meaning a group of them who stand with you in prayer, and let them take their arms meaning those who pray with you, and it is said: and let them take their arms those who are facing the enemy, as will be explained. God Almighty did not mention in the verse for each party except one rak’ah, but it was narrated in the hadiths that they added another to it, as will be explained. The kasrah was deleted from His saying: Then let them stand and So let them be because of its heaviness. Al-Akhfash, Al-Farra’ and Al-Kisa’i narrated that the lam of command, the lam of ki and the lam of negation are opened, and Sibawayh forbids that for a compelling reason, which is the difference between the lam of jar and the lam of emphasis. What is meant by this command is division, meaning the rest of them and the face of the enemy, in anticipation of his attack. The narrations differed regarding the form of the fear prayer, and the scholars differed regarding their differences. Ibn Al-Qassar mentioned that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed it in ten places. Ibn Al-Arabi said: “It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he prayed the fear prayer twenty-four times.” Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, the imam of the people of hadith and the foremost in knowing the reasons for transmitting it, said: I do not know that anything has been narrated regarding the fear prayer except an authentic hadith, and they are all authentic hadiths, so according to whichever hadith the worshipper prays the fear prayer, it will suffice him, God willing. Abu Ja`far Al-Tabari said the same. As for Malik and the rest of his companions except Ashhab, they went in the prayer of fear to the hadith of Sahl ibn Abi Hathma, which is what he narrated in his Muwatta’ on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad on the authority of Salih ibn Khawat Al-Ansari that Sahl ibn Abi Hathma told him that the prayer of fear is that the imam stands with a group of his companions and a group facing the enemy, so the imam bows one rak’ah and prostrates with those with him, then he stands, and when he stands straight he stands, and they complete the remaining rak’ah for themselves, then they say the salutation and leave while the imam is standing, so they are facing the enemy, then the others who have not prayed come forward and say the takbir behind the imam, so he bows with them for the rak’ah and prostrates, then he says the salutation, so they stand and bow for themselves for the remaining rak’ah, then they say the salutation. Ibn Al-Qasim, the companion of Malik, said: The practice according to Malik is based on the hadith of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad on the authority of Salih ibn Khawat. Ibn Al-Qasim said: He used to take the hadith of Yazid ibn Ruman, then he returned to this. Abu Umar said: The hadith of Al-Qasim and the hadith of Yazid ibn Ruman are both on the authority of Salih ibn Khawat, except that There is a separation between them in the greeting of peace. In the hadith of Al-Qasim, the imam greets the second group, then they stand and complete the rak’ah for themselves. In the hadith of Yazid ibn Ruman, he waits for them and greets them. Al-Shafi’i said this and he agreed with him. Al-Shafi’i said: The hadith of Yazid ibn Ruman from Salih ibn Khawat is the most similar of the hadiths in the fear prayer to the apparent meaning of the Book of God, and I say this. Among the arguments of Malik in his choice of the hadith of Al-Qasim is the analogy to other prayers, in that the imam does not have the right to wait for someone who has preceded him in something from it, and that the agreed upon Sunnah is that the followers complete what they have preceded in after the imam’s greeting of peace. Abu Thawr’s statement in this regard is like the statement of Malik, and Ahmad said this is like the statement of Al-Shafi’i in his preferred opinion. He did not find fault with someone who did any of the aspects narrated in the fear prayer. Ashhab, one of Malik’s companions, went to the hadith of Ibn ‘Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the fear prayer with one of the two groups, one rak’ah, and the other group facing the enemy. Then they turned away and stood in place of their companions, facing the enemy. Then those came, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with them. Then these people completed one rak’ah and those people completed one rak’ah. Ibn ‘Umar said: If the fear was greater than that, he prayed while riding or standing, nodding. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Malik, and others narrated it. Al-Awza’i went to this description, and it is what Abu ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Barr approved. He said: Because it has the most authentic chain of transmission, and it was transmitted by the people of Medina, and they are the proof against those who disagreed with them. And because it is more similar to the principles, because the first and second groups did not complete the rak’ah until after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had finished the prayer, which is well-known from his Sunnah, which is agreed upon in all prayers. As for the Kufians: Abu Hanifa and his companions, except for Abu Yusuf al-Qadi Ya’qub, they went to the hadith of ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Darqutni. He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the prayer of fear. They stood in two rows behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, facing the enemy. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with them one rak’ah. The others came and took their place. These people faced the enemy, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with them and then gave the taslim. These people stood up and prayed one rak’ah for themselves, then gave the taslim. Then they went and took the place of those people facing the enemy. Those people returned to their places and prayed one rak’ah for themselves, then gave the taslim. This description and form is the form mentioned in the hadith of Ibn Umar, except that there is a difference between them, which is that the performance of those people in the hadith of Ibn Umar appears to be in one state, and the imam remains like the guard alone. Here their performance is divided according to the manner of their prayer. Some of them interpreted the hadith of Ibn Umar based on what came in the hadith of Ibn Mas’ud. He went to the hadith of Ibn Mas’ud al-Thawri - in one of the three narrations from him - and Ashab bin Abdul Aziz, according to what Abu al-Hasan al-Lakhmi mentioned from him. The first was mentioned by Abu Umar, Ibn Yunus, and Ibn Habib from him. Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Hudhayfah and Abu Hurayrah and Ibn Umar: That he, peace be upon him, prayed with each group one rak`ah and they did not make it up, and this is what is required by the hadith of Ibn `Abbas: “And in fear, one rak`ah.” This is the saying of Ishaq, and we have already mentioned this in Al-Baqarah, and that prayer is more deserving of what is taken care of, and that the hadith of Ibn `Abbas does not constitute evidence. And his saying in the hadith of Hudhayfah and others: They did not make it up means in the knowledge of the one who narrated that, because it has been narrated that they made up a rak`ah in that particular prayer, and the testimony of the one who added is more deserving. And it is possible that what is meant is that they did not make it up, meaning they did not make it up if they felt safe, and the benefit is that the one who is afraid, if he feels safe, does not make up what he prayed in that manner of prayers in fear. Abu `Umar said all of it, and in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Jabir: That he, peace be upon him, prayed two rak’ahs with a group, then they moved back, and he prayed two rak’ahs with the other group. He said: So the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, prayed four rak’ahs and the people prayed two rak’ahs. Abu Dawud and Al-Darqutni narrated it from: Hadith of Al-Hasan on the authority of Abu Bakra, and they mentioned in it that he said the salutation after every two rak’ahs. Ad-Daraqutni also narrated it on the authority of Al-Hasan, “On the authority of Jabir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed two rak’ahs with them, then he said the salutation, then he prayed with the others two rak’ahs, then he said the salutation.” Abu Dawud said: This is what Al-Hasan used to issue fatwas on, and it was narrated on the authority of Al-Shafi’i, and it is used as evidence by all those who permit the difference in intention of the imam and the one being led in prayer. This is the view of Al-Shafi’i, Al-Awza’i, Ibn Ulayyah, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Dawud. They supported this with the hadith of Jabir: that Mu’adh used to pray the ‘Isha’ prayer with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he would come and lead his people in prayer. Al-Tahawi said: This was only in the beginning of Islam, when it was permissible to pray the obligatory prayer twice, then that was abrogated, and God knows best. These are the sayings of the scholars on the prayer of fear. Third: This prayer mentioned in the Qur’an is only needed when the Muslims are facing the Qiblah and the enemy and the Qiblah. This only happened at Dhat ar-Riqa’. As for Usfan and the other place, the Muslims were facing the Qiblah. What we mentioned about the reason for revelation in the story of Khalid ibn al-Walid does not fit with the division of the people into two groups, because in the hadith after his saying So I led them in prayer he said: The time for prayer came and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to take up their weapons and we lined up behind him in two rows. He said: Then he knelt and we all knelt. He said: Then he raised his head and we all raised our heads. He said: Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prostrated in the row next to him. He said: And the others were standing, guarding them. When they prostrated and stood, the others sat down and prostrated in their places. He said: Then these people advanced in the rows of these people and these people came to the rows of these people. He said: Then he knelt and they all knelt down. Then he raised his head and they all rose up. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prostrated and the row next to him, and the others were standing, guarding them. When the others sat down, they prostrated. Then he greeted them. He said: So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed it twice: once in Usfan and once in the land of Banu Salim. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadeeth of Abu Ayyash al-Zarqi and said: It is the opinion of al-Thawri and it is more cautious. Abu ‘Eesa al-Tirmidhi delayed it from the hadeeth of Abu Hurayrah. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, camped between Dajnan and Usfan, the hadith. In it, he, peace be upon him, split them into two parts and prayed with each group one rak’ah, so the people had one rak’ah and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had two rak’ahs.” He said: A good, authentic, strange hadith. There are narrations on this topic from Abd God ibn Mas’ud, Zayd ibn Thabit, Ibn Abbas, Jabir, Abu Ayyash al-Zarqi, whose name was Zayd ibn al-Samit, Ibn Umar, Hudhayfah, Abu Bakr, and Sahl ibn Abi Huthaymah. I said: There is no contradiction between these narrations. Perhaps he prayed with them one prayer as mentioned in the hadith of Abu Ayyash, together, and he prayed with them another prayer separately as mentioned in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and in it there is evidence for those who say that the fear prayer is one rak’ah. Al-Khattabi said: The fear prayer has types that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed on different days and in different forms, in all of which he sought what was most cautious for the prayer and most effective in guarding. Fourth: They differed on how to perform the Maghrib prayer. Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Bakra. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the Maghrib prayer with the people in three rak’ahs, then they left. The others came and he prayed with them in three rak’ahs, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had six and the people had three. Al-Hasan and the majority said the same regarding the Maghrib prayer, contrary to this, which is that he prays two rak’ahs in the first and one rak’ah in the second. It is made up, according to their different principles, when it is before or after the imam’s salutation. This is the opinion of Malik and Abu Hanifa, because it is more appropriate for the form of the prayer. Al-Shafi’i said: He prays one rak’ah in the first because Ali, may God be pleased with him, did it on the night of the Harir. And God Almighty knows best. Fifth: They differed regarding the prayer of fear when war is raging and fighting is intense and it is feared that the time will run out. Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Awza’i, Al-Shafi’i and most of the scholars said: He should pray however he can, based on the statement of Ibn ‘Umar: If the fear is greater than that, he should pray while riding or standing, nodding. He said in Al-Muwatta’: Facing the qiblah or not. The statement of Al-Dahhak and Ishaq was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. Al-Awza’i said: If the conquest is imminent and they are not able to pray, they should pray nodding, each person for himself. If they are not able to nod, they should delay the prayer until the fighting subsides and they are safe, so they should pray two rak’ahs. If they are not able, they should pray one rak’ah and two prostrations. If they are not able, they should say the takbir and delay it until they are safe. Makhul said. I said: Al-Kia al-Tabari narrated it in his Ahkam al-Quran on the authority of Abu Hanifa and his companions. Al-Kia said: If the fear is more severe than that and fighting is ongoing, then the Muslims pray as much as they can, facing the qiblah or turning their backs to it. Abu Hanifa and his three companions agree that they do not pray in this case, but rather delay the prayer. If they fight during the prayer, they say: The prayer is invalid. It was narrated on the authority of al-Shafi’i that if he continues stabbing and striking, his prayer is invalid. I said: This statement indicates the correctness of the statement of Anas: I was present at the battle of the fortress of Tustar at dawn and the fighting became intense, so we were not able to pray until after the sun had risen, so we prayed it while we were with Abu Musa and it was opened for us. Anas said: What would please me with that prayer in this world? What would please me with that prayer in this world and what is in it? Al-Bukhari mentioned it, and our Sheikh, the teacher Abu Ja`far Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Qaysi al-Qurtubi, known as Abu Hujjah, was in agreement with it, and it is the choice of Al-Bukhari, and it appears that he followed it with the hadith of Jabir, who said: Omar came on the day of the Trench and began to curse the infidels of Quraysh and say: O Messenger of God, I did not pray the afternoon prayer until the sun was about to set. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And by God, I did not pray it. He went down to Buthan, performed ablution, and prayed the afternoon prayer after the sun had set, then he prayed the sunset prayer after it. Sixth: They differed regarding the prayer of the seeker and the sought. Malik and a group of his companions said that they are the same, each one of them prays on his mount. Al-Awza’i, Al-Shafi’i, the scholars of Hadith, and Ibn Abd Al-Hakam said: The seeker does not pray except on the ground, and this is correct, because the seeker is voluntary, and the obligatory prayer is to be prayed on the ground wherever that is possible, and a rider does not pray it except in extreme fear, but the seeker is not like that, and God knows best. Seventh: They also differed regarding the army if they saw a blackness and thought it was an enemy and prayed the fear prayer, then it became clear to them that it was nothing. Our scholars have two narrations regarding it: One of them is that they should repeat it, and Abu Hanifa said the same. The second is that they do not have to repeat it, and this is the more apparent of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. The first is that the mistake became clear to them, so they returned to the correct path, like the ruling of the judge.
