The second is that they knew based on their own effort, so it was permissible for them, just as if they had made a mistake in the direction of the qiblah. This is more appropriate because they did what they were commanded to do. It may be said that they should repeat it during the time, but after it has ended, no, and God knows best. Eighth - The Almighty said: And let them take their weapons. And He said: And let them take their precautions and their weapons. This is an exhortation to be cautious and to take weapons so that the enemy does not achieve his hope and realize his opportunity. The weapon is what a person uses to defend himself in war. Antara said: I clothed the curly hair of Bani Aban with my weapon after being naked and disgraced He says, I lent him my weapon so that a slave who is naked may be protected from his weapon. Ibn Abbas said: And let them take their weapons means the group facing the enemy, because the praying group does not fight. Another said: It is the praying group, meaning let those who prayed first take their weapons. This was mentioned by Al-Zajjaj. He said: It is possible that the group who are in prayer were ordered to carry weapons, meaning let a group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons because it is more terrifying to the enemy. An-Nahhas: It is possible that it is for everyone because it is more terrifying to the enemy, and it is possible that it is for the group facing the enemy in particular. Abu Omar said: Most of the scholars recommend that the worshipper take his weapon if he prays in fear and they interpret his statement and let them take their weapons as a recommendation because it is something that if it were not for fear it would not be obligatory to take it, so the command to do so is a recommendation. The people of the apparent meaning said: Taking a weapon in the prayer of fear is obligatory because of the command of God to do so, except for the one who is harmed by rain, because if that is the case then it is permissible for him to put down his weapon. Ibn al-Arabi said: If they pray they take their weapon when they are afraid and al-Shafi’i said the same and it is the text of the Qur’an. Abu Hanifa said: They should not carry it because if it were obligatory for them to carry it then the prayer would be invalidated by leaving it. We said: It is not obligatory for them to carry it for the sake of the prayer, but rather it is obligatory for them to strengthen them and in view of that. Ninth - The Almighty’s saying: So when they prostrate, the pronoun in prostrate refers to the praying group, so let them turn away. This is according to some of the narrated forms. It was said: The meaning is: So when they prostrate in the rak’ah of making up, and this is according to the form of Sahl bin Abi Hathmah. These verses indicate that prostration may be used to refer to the entire prayer, and it is like his saying, peace be upon him: If one of you enters the mosque, let him prostrate twice. That is, let him pray two rak’ahs, and this is in the Sunnah. The pronoun in his statement, let them be, may refer to those who prostrated, or it may refer to the group that stood first, facing the enemy. Tenth - The Almighty said: And those who disbelieved wish meaning the disbelievers wished and loved that you would neglect to take up arms so that they could reach their goal. Thus, God Almighty explained the wisdom behind the command to take up arms and mentioned caution in the second group rather than the first - because it is more appropriate to take caution, because the enemy does not delay his goal past this time because it is the last of the prayer. Also, the enemy says that the weapons have weighed them down and they have eaten. In this verse is the clearest evidence of taking the necessary measures and adopting everything that saves those with understanding, leads to safety, and reaches the abode of honor. The meaning of one inclination is an exaggeration, meaning that it is eradicated and does not require a second. Eleventh - The Almighty’s saying: And there is no blame upon you if you are harmed by rain The verse. The scholars have a statement regarding the obligation of carrying weapons in prayer that we have indicated. If it is not obligatory, then it is recommended to be cautious, then it is permissible to put them down in the rain, because the linings get wet and become heavy and the iron rusts. It was said: It was revealed about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Batn Nakhal, when the polytheists were defeated and the Muslims took booty. It was a rainy day, and “he, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to relieve himself, putting down his weapon. The infidels saw him cut off from his companions, so Ghawrath ibn al-Harith approached him and descended upon him from the mountain with his sword. He said: Who will protect you from me today? He said: God. Then he said: O God, protect me from Ghawrath however You wish. He aimed his sword at the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to strike him, but he fell on his face because of the slipperiness he had caused.” Al-Waqidi mentioned. Gabriel, peace be upon him, pushed him in the chest, as will be mentioned in Al-Ma’idah, and the sword fell from his hand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took it and said: Who can protect you from me, O Ghawrath? He said: No one. He said: Will you testify to the truth for me and I will give you your sword? He said: No, but I testify that I will not fight you after this and will not aid an enemy against you. So he gave him the sword. The verse was revealed as a concession to lay down weapons in the rain. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf fell ill from a wound, as in Sahih al-Bukhari, so God Almighty gave them permission to lay down their weapons and prepare for the enemy, with the excuse of rain. Then He commanded them, saying: And take your precautions, meaning be alert, whether you lay down your weapons or not. This indicates the emphasis on being prepared and cautious of the enemy in all circumstances and not surrendering, because no army has ever been afflicted except through negligence in caution. Ad-Dahhak said about God Almighty’s statement: And take your precautions, meaning, gird yourself with your swords, because that is the way of the invaders.
4:103: It has five issues: The first: You have completed means you have finished the fear prayer. This indicates that the word qada is used in both cases, and it was done at its time. From this is the saying of God Almighty: So when you have completed your rites (al-Baqarah 2:200), which was mentioned previously. The second - the Almighty’s saying: So remember God while standing, sitting, or lying on your sides. The majority of scholars have said that this commanded remembrance is only after the prayer of fear, meaning that when you have finished the prayer, remember God with your heart and tongue, no matter what state you are in, standing, sitting, and lying on your sides. And continue to remember Him by glorifying God, declaring His oneness, and supplicating for victory, especially in times of battle. Similar to this is: When you meet a company, stand firm and remember God much that you may be successful. (al-Anfal 8:45) It is said: So when you have completed the prayer, meaning if you pray in a land of war, then pray on your mounts, or standing, sitting, or lying on your sides if you are unable to stand if you are afraid or sick, as the Almighty said in another verse: But if you fear, then on foot or riding. (al-Baqarah 2:239) And your people said that this verse is similar to the one in Al-Imran. It was narrated that Abdullah bin Masoud saw people making noise in the mosque, so he said: What is this noise? They said: Does not God Almighty say: So remember God while standing, sitting, and lying on your sides. He said: What is meant by this is the obligatory prayer. If you are unable to stand, then sit, and if you are unable to pray, then pray on your side. What is meant is the prayer itself, because prayer is the remembrance of God Almighty, and it includes the obligatory and recommended remembrances. The first statement is more apparent, and God knows best. Third - The Almighty’s saying: So when you are reassured meaning you are secure, and reassurance is the soul being at peace from fear. Then establish prayer meaning perform it with its pillars and in its perfect form when travelling and in its perfect number when at home. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times meaning timed and imposed. Zaid bin Aslam said: Specifically means you perform it in its stars, and the meaning according to the linguists is: imposed for a specific time. It is said: its time, so it is specified. And its time, so it is specified. This is the saying of Zaid bin Aslam, may God be pleased with him, and he said: a book and the source is masculine, so that is why he said: specified.
4:104: Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: And do not weaken meaning do not become weak. It was mentioned previously in Al Imran in pursuit of the people seeking them. It was said: It was revealed in the Battle of Uhud where the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ordered to go out in the tracks of the polytheists and the Muslims had wounds and he was ordered not to go out with him to those who were in the battle as mentioned previously in Al Imran. It was said: This is in every jihad. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: If you are suffering meaning you are suffering from the wounds that have befallen you, then they are also suffering from what befalls them, but the advantage is that you hope for the reward of God while they do not hope for it, and that is because the one who does not believe in God does not hope for anything from God. Similar to this verse is: If a wound should touch you, then a wound similar to it has already touched the people (al-An’am 6:240). It has been mentioned before. Abd al-Rahman al-A’raj read that you are suffering with a fat-ha on the hamza, meaning because. Mansur ibn al-Mu’tamir read that you are suffering with a kasra on the ta’, and it is not permissible according to the Basrans to break the ta’ because of the heaviness of the kasra in it. Then it was said: hope here means fear because the one who hopes for something is not certain of its occurrence, so it is not free from fear of missing out on what he hopes for. Al-Farra’ and al-Zajjaj said: hope is not used to mean fear except with negation, like the Almighty’s saying: What is the matter with you that you do not hope for God with reverence? (Nuh: 23) meaning you do not fear God’s greatness, and the Almighty’s saying: For those who do not hope for the days of God (al-Jathiyah 45:24) meaning they do not… They fear. Al-Qushayri said: It is not far-fetched to mention fear without there being a negation in the speech, but they claimed that this did not exist except with the negation, and God knows best.
4:105: It has four issues: First: In this verse there is an honor for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a respect, glorification, and delegation to him, and also a correction on the right path in judgment, and a reprimand for what was brought to him regarding the matter of Banu Ubayraq: They were three brothers: Bishr, Bashir, and Mubashir, and Aseer bin Urwah, their son, Omar. They dug into the drinking place of Rifa’ah bin Zaid at night and stole his armor and food. It was found and it was said that the thief was Bashir alone, and he was called Abu Ta’mah. He took an armor. It was said that the deterrent was in a bag containing flour, and the flour was scattered from a hole in the bag until it reached his house. Then Rifa’ah’s nephew, whose name was Qatada bin Al-Nu’man, came to complain about them to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Aseer bin Urwah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, these people went to a house that was people of righteousness and religion, and they accused them of theft and accused them of it without evidence. He began to argue on their behalf until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became angry with Qatada and Rifa’ah, so God Almighty revealed: “And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves” (An-Nisa’: 107) and God Almighty revealed: And whoever commits a sin or an offense and then throws it at an innocent person, and the innocent person they accused was… Quickly, Labid bin Sahl, and it was said: Zaid bin Al-Sameen, and it was said: a man from the Ansar: So when God revealed what He revealed, Ibn Abi Raq the thief fled to Mecca and stayed with Salafah bint Saeed bin Shaheed, so Hassan bin Thabit said a house in which he would offer her, and he is And Saad's daughter brought him down and he began to argue with her about the skin of her buttocks and she argued with him You thought that what you had done would be hidden, while among us there was a prophet who had the revelation and who brought it forth. When she heard of it, she said: Hassan’s poetry was given to me as a gift, and I took his saddlebag and threw it outside the house, so he fled to Khaybar and apostatized. Then he dug into a house one night to steal, and the wall fell on him, so he died an apostate. Al-Tirmidhi mentioned this hadith with many of its wordings, and he said: A good and strange hadith. We do not know anyone who narrated it except Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani. Abu al-Layth and al-Tabari mentioned it with different wordings. Yahya ibn Salam mentioned the story of his death in his interpretation, and al-Qushayri also mentioned it, and he added the mention of apostasy. Then it was said: Zayd ibn al-Sameen and Labid ibn Sahl were Jews. It was said: Laid was a Muslim, and al-Mahdawi mentioned him, and Abu Omar included him in his book of the Companions, so this indicated his Islam in his view. Bashir was a hypocrite who satirized the Companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and attributed poetry to others. The Muslims used to say: By God, it is nothing but the poetry of the wicked. So he recited poetry in which he was connected, and from it his saying: Or whenever men recite a poem, it is distorted and they say Ibn Al-Abiraq recited it. Ad-Dahhak said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to cut off his hand, and he was obeyed. Then the Jews came, doubting the weapon, so they took it and fled with it. Then the verse Here you are was revealed, meaning the Jews. God knows best. Second: The Almighty’s saying: By what God has shown you means according to the laws of the Shari’ah, either by revelation and text or by contemplation that follows the laws of revelation. This is a principle in analogy and it indicates that if the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, saw something, he was right, because God, the Almighty, showed it to him, and God, the Almighty, guaranteed infallibility to His prophets. But if one of us sees something with his stomach, then he does not have to cut off what he narrated and he did not mean seeing it with the eye here, because the ruling is not seen with the eye, and there is an implication in the speech, that is, by what God has shown you, and there is another implication in it. And carry out the rulings according to what we have made clear to you, without being deceived by their evidence. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And do not be an advocate for the traitors. This is an active participle, like saying, I sat with him, so I am his companion. The active participle here does not have the meaning of a passive participle, which indicates that. And do not argue. The adversary is the one who argues, and the plural of adversary is adversaries. It was also said: An adversary, an opponent, an adversary is also an active participle. So God Almighty forbade His Messenger from supporting those who accuse others and defending them with what their opponent says of the argument. In this is evidence that representation on behalf of the one who is wrong and the accused in a dispute is not permissible, so it is not permissible for anyone to argue on behalf of anyone except after knowing that he is right. The speech in the Surah proceeded to preserve the money of orphans and people, so it was made clear that the money of the disbeliever is preserved for him just as it is for the Muslim, except in the place that God Almighty permitted it. Fourth issue: The scholars said: If the hypocrisy of a people becomes apparent to the Muslims, it is not appropriate for a group of them to argue with another group on their behalf in order to protect them and defend them, because this happened during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and regarding them the words of God Almighty were revealed: And do not be an advocate for the traitors and And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves and the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by it are those Muslims who used to do it without him for two reasons: The first is that God Almighty made that clear with what He mentioned after in His words: Here you are, you have argued on their behalf in the life of this world and the second is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a judge between them and for this reason he would apologize to him and he would not apologize to anyone else, so this indicates that the intention was for someone else.
4:106: There is one issue: Al-Tabari said that the meaning is, ask forgiveness of God for your sin in your quarrel with the traitors, so he ordered him to ask forgiveness for what he intended to defend against them and the hand of the Jew, and this is a doctrine of those who permit minor sins against the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is not a sin, because the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, only defended on the surface and he believed in their innocence. The meaning is: And ask forgiveness of God for the sinners of your nation and those who quarrel falsely, and your place among the people is to listen to the litigants and judge in the manner you hear and ask forgiveness for the sinner. It was said: It is an order to ask forgiveness in the manner of glorification, like a man who says: I ask forgiveness of God in the manner of glorification without intending repentance from a sin. It was said: The address is to the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and what is meant is the Banu Ubayraq, like the Almighty’s saying: O Prophet, fear God (al-Ahzab 33:1), And if you are in doubt (Yunus 10:94).
4:107: That is, do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. It was revealed about Aseer bin Urwa, as mentioned above. Argumentation is from argument, which means twisting, and from it comes a man with a twisted nature, and from it comes the word ajdal for a falcon. It was said that it comes from jadalah, which means the face of the earth, so each of the two opponents wants to throw his companion on it. Al-Ajjaj said: I may ride case after case and leave the helpless with the argument Forgiving is not impossible The argument is the land, from that they say: I left it argumentative or thrown on the argument. The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God does not love means He is not pleased with him and does not mention whoever is a traitor “a traitor” is more eloquent because it is one of the forms of exaggeration, and that was only because of the great value of that betrayal, and God knows best.
4:108: Ad-Dahhak said: When the shield was stolen, he dug a hole in his house and put the shield under the dirt, so the verse was revealed: They hide themselves from the people, but they do not hide themselves from God. He says: The location of the shield is not hidden from God. And He is with them, meaning He is a watchful guardian over them. It was also said: They hide themselves from the people, meaning they conceal themselves, as God the Almighty said: And whoever hides himself by night (Ar-Ra'd: 10) meaning concealed. It was also said: They are shy from the people. This is because shyness is the reason for concealment, and the meaning of And He is with them means with knowledge, sight, and hearing. This is the saying of the people of the Sunnah. The Jahmites, Qadarites and Mu'tazilites said: He is everywhere, adhering to this verse and what is like it. They said: When He said, And He is with them, it was proven that He is everywhere because He has proven that He is with them. God is exalted above what they say, for this is an attribute of bodies, and God is exalted above that. Have you not seen the debate of a human being regarding the statement of God Almighty: There are not three who confer privately but that He is the fourth of them. (Al-Mujadilah: 7) when he said: He is in His essence in every place, so his opponent said to him: He is in your skullcap, in your stuffing and in the belly of your donkey. God is exalted above what they say! This was narrated by Wakee’, may God be pleased with him. The meaning of they spend the night is they say: Al-Kalbi said it on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas. What is not pleased means what God is not pleased with for the people of His obedience. From the statement means from opinion and belief, like your saying: the school of Malik and Al-Shafi’i. It was said: The statement means what is said because the statement itself does not spend the night.
4:109: The Almighty says: Here you are meaning the people of Bashir the thief when they fled with him and argued on his behalf. Al-Zajjaj said: These means those with whom you argued "disputed" in worldly life. So who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection? "A question that means denial and rebuke. Or who will be their guardian?" The guardian: the one who manages affairs. So God Almighty is responsible for managing His creation. The meaning is: there is no one who will manage their affairs if God takes them with His punishment and throws them into the Fire.
4:110: Ibn Abbas said: God offered repentance to Banu Abiriq with this verse, meaning, And whoever does evil by stealing or wrongs himself by associating partners with God and then seeks forgiveness from God meaning by repenting, for seeking forgiveness with the tongue without repentance is of no benefit, and we have explained this in Al Imran. Ad-Dahhak said: The verse was revealed concerning Wahshi, the killer of Hamza, who associated partners with God and killed Hamza, then he came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, I regret it, so is there any repentance for me? Then he revealed: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself the verse. It was said: What is meant by this verse is generality and inclusiveness for all creation. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Al-Aswad and Alqamah, who said: Abdullah bin Masoud said: Whoever recites these two verses from Surat An-Nisa and then seeks forgiveness from God will be forgiven: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful “And if they had come to you, when they wronged themselves, and asked forgiveness from God and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found God Forgiving and Merciful” It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: When I heard a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God would benefit me with it as He willed, and if I heard it without swearing, Abu Bakr told me and Abu Bakr was truthful: He said: If a servant of God commits a sin, then performs ablution, prays two rak’ahs, and seeks forgiveness from God, He will forgive him. Then he recited this verse: And whoever does evil or wrongs himself but then seeks forgiveness from God will find God Forgiving and Merciful.
4:111: The Almighty said: And whoever earns a sin meaning a crime only earns it against himself meaning its consequences will return to him. Earning is what a person brings to himself in benefit or wards off harm from himself, and for this reason the action of the Almighty Lord is not called earning.
4:112: The Almighty said: And whoever commits a sin or a crime It was said: They have one meaning, repeated for emphasis due to the difference in wording. Al-Tabari said: The difference between a sin and a crime is that a sin can be intentional or unintentional, while a crime can only be intentional. It was said: A sin is something you do not do intentionally, such as killing by mistake. It was said: A minor sin and a major crime. The wording of this verse is general, and includes the Nazis and others. The Almighty said: Then he throws it at an innocent person. The name of the innocent person was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah, and the ha in bih refers to sin or wrongdoing because its meaning is sin, the first of them both. It was said: It refers to earning. He has borne slander and manifest sin. This is a simile, since sins are a burden and a burden, so they are like things that are carried. The Almighty said: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens in addition to their own burdens. (al-Ankabut 29:23) Slander comes from slander, which is that you confront your brother by accusing him of a sin of which he is innocent. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know what backbiting is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: It is mentioning your brother in a way he dislikes. It was said: What if what I say is true in my brother? He said: If what you say is true, then you have backbitten him, and if it is not true, then you have slandered him. This is a clear text: accusing an innocent person of backbiting is slander. It is said: he slandered him, slandered him, or slanderously, if he says about him what he did not do, and he is a slanderer, and the one he is talking to is stunned. It is also said: a man is stunned with a kasra if he is astonished and confused. And stunned with a damma is similar to it, but more eloquent than it is stunned, as God the Most High said: So he who disbelieved was stunned (Al-Baqarah 2:258) because it is said: a stunned man, but it is not said: stunned or stunned. Al-Kisa’i said this.
4:113: The Almighty said: And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy What comes after lawla is raised as a subject according to Sibawayh, and the predicate is omitted and does not appear, and the meaning is And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy by alerting you to the truth, and it was said: by prophecy and infallibility A group of them would have decided to mislead you from the truth because they asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to acquit Ibn Ubayraq of the accusation and attach it to the Jew, so God, the Almighty, favored His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, by alerting him to that and informing him of it And they mislead none but themselves because they know the deeds of the misguided, so its consequences will return to them And they do not harm you at all because you are infallible And God has sent down to you the Book and wisdom This is the beginning of a speech, and it was said: The waw is for the state like your saying: I came to you while the sun was rising, and from this is the saying of Imru' al-Qais: I had lunch while the birds were in their nests The speech is connected, meaning that they will not harm you at all while God has revealed to you the Qur’an, and wisdom is the judgment by revelation, and and taught you what you did not know meaning of the laws and rulings, and you know is in the accusative case because it is the predicate of was, and the damma was deleted from the nun for the sake of the jussive, and the waw was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
4:114: He meant what the people of Banu Abiriq negotiated about in terms of planning, and they mentioned it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Whispering is the secret between two people. You say: I whispered to so-and-so in a whisper and a secret conversation, and they are producing and whispering, and I saved so-and-so, I saved him, meaning I whispered to him, so whispering is derived from najawwat al-shay’ anjuwwa, meaning I saved it and isolated it, and salvation is from the high ground because it is isolated by its height from what is around it. The poet said: He who escapes is like he who is punished, and he who hides is like he who walks on a limb. The secret conversation is a source and a group may be called by it, as it is said: a people of justice and contentment. God Almighty said: And when they were in secret (al-Isra’ 17:47). So according to the first, the command is a command of exception from the genus of the exception, which is the disconnected exception. It was mentioned before and min is in the nominative case, meaning but whoever commands charity or goodness or reform between people and calls for it, then in his secret conversation is good. It is permissible for min to be in the genitive case and the estimate would be: There is no good in much of their secret conversation except the secret conversation of whoever commands charity, then it is deleted. And the second is that the whispering is a name for the group of people who are alone, so min is in the accusative case as a substitute, meaning there is no good in much of their whispering except for the one who commands charity, or it is in the accusative case according to the saying of the one who said: I did not pass by anyone except Zayd. And some of the commentators, including Al-Zajjaj, said: The whispering is the speech of the group of people who are alone or two, whether that is secret or public, and there is a distance in it, and God knows best, and the well-known word includes all righteous deeds. And Muqatil said: The well-known here is the obligation, and the first is more correct, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every good deed is charity, and it is a good deed to meet your brothers with a cheerful face. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The known is as his name is, and the first to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection will be the known and his family. Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: Do not let the disbelief of the one who disbelieves in the known make you lose interest in it, for the grateful may be grateful with many times the ingratitude of the disbeliever. Al-Khatia said: He who does good will not lose his reward. Customs between God and people will not be lost. Al-Rayashi recited: The hand of kindness is a sheep, whether carried by a generous or grateful person. For in the gratitude of the grateful there is a reward, and with God the ungrateful is not ungrateful. Al-Marudi said: “Whoever is able to do a good deed should hasten to do so, fearing that it will be missed, and should hasten to do so for fear of failing. He should know that it is one of the opportunities of his time and the spoils of his ability, and he should not neglect it out of confidence in his ability to do it. How many people have been confident in their ability, but then it was followed by regret, and how many have relied on a position that has been lost, causing shame, as the poet said: I still hear how many confident people were shy until I was tested and became the confident shy one If he had been aware of the vicissitudes of his time and had been cautious of the consequences of his actions, his gains would have been stored up and his losses would have been compensated for. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Whoever has a door of goodness opened for him, let him seize it, for he does not know when it will be closed to him.” It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Everything has a fruit, and the fruit of kindness is forgiveness. It was said to Anushirwan: What is the greatest calamity for you? He said: That you are able to do kindness but do not do it until it is too late. Abdul Hamid said: Whoever delays an opportunity before its time should be confident that it will not be missed. Some poets said: If your winds blow, seize them, for every fluttering wind has a stillness. Do not neglect to do good in it, for you do not know when peace will come. Some of the people of veneration wrote to the governor of the palace to take care of his veneration: The highest path, do you want to take care of my honor or do you want to be rewarded for your generosity? For the benefit of this world, I want you, so pay attention to my needs from the slumber of sleepers Al-Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: A good deed is not complete except with three characteristics: hastening it, minimizing it, and concealing it. If you hasten it, you will congratulate it, if you minimize it, you will magnify it, and if you conceal it, you will complete it. Some poets said: Your kindness to me has increased in importance, for you consider me a lowly and insignificant person. You forget about him as if he never came to you, but he is famous and dangerous among people. One of the conditions of doing good is not to be grateful for it or to be impressed by its action, because that leads to the loss of gratitude and the nullification of reward. This was explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. The Almighty’s saying: or reconciliation between people is general in terms of blood, money, honor, and everything about which there is a dispute or disagreement among Muslims, and in every speech intended for the sake of God Almighty. In the hadith: All the words of the son of Adam are against him, not for him, except for what is an enjoining of good or forbidding of evil or remembrance of God the Most High. As for the one who seeks to show off and assume leadership, he will not attain the reward. Omar wrote to Ibn Musa al-Ash'ari, may God be pleased with him: Send the opponents back until they reconcile, because the passing of judgment creates grudges between them. And in the discussion of what is forbidden in private conversation and what is permissible, God willing, we will come to what is forbidden in private conversation and what is permissible, and on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, he said: Whoever reconciles between two people, God will give him for every word the freeing of a slave. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Ayyub: Shall I not guide you to a charity that God and His Messenger love? It reconciles people when they are at odds and brings them closer together when they are estranged. Al-Awza’i said: There is no step more beloved to God, the Almighty and Majestic, than a plan to reconcile people. Whoever reconciles two people, God will write for him a release from the Fire. Muhammad ibn al-Munkar said: Two men were arguing in a corner of the mosque, so I went to them and continued with them until they reconciled. Abu Hurairah said, while he was watching me: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever reconciles between two people deserves the reward of a martyr. This hadith was mentioned by Abu Mut’i’ Makhul bin al-Mufaddal al-Nasafi in his book Al-Lu’lu’iyyat. I found it in the author’s handwriting on a piece of paper, but he did not indicate its location. May God be pleased with him. Seeking is in the accusative case as the object of the verb.
4:115: There are two issues: The first - the scholars said: These two verses were revealed because of Ibn Ubayraq the thief, when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that his hand should be cut off and he fled to Mecca and apostatized. Saeed bin Jubair said: When he reached Mecca, he dug into a house in Mecca and the polytheists caught up with him and killed him, so God Almighty revealed: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him until His saying: He has certainly strayed far astray. Ad-Dahhak said: A group of Quraysh came to Medina and converted to Islam, then returned to Mecca as apostates, so this verse was revealed: And whoever contradicts the Messenger and contradiction is the return, and even if the verse was revealed about the thief of armor or other things, it is general for everyone who deviates from the path of the Muslims and guidance means right guidance and clarification, and it has been mentioned previously. And God Almighty’s saying: We will give him what he has taken is said to have been revealed about those who apostatized and the meaning is: We will leave him and what he worships. According to Mujahid: That we will entrust him to idols that do not benefit or harm, and Muqatil said the same. Al-Kalbi said: God Almighty’s saying: We will give him what he has taken was revealed about Ibn Ubayraq, when his condition became clear. He stole it and fled to Mecca, then turned back and dug into a wall belonging to a man in Mecca called Hajjaj bin Alat. He remained in the dugout until he was found in the same condition. They expelled him from Mecca, so he went to Mecca, Syria, and stole some of the caravan’s money. They stoned him and killed him. Then the verse was revealed: We will give him what he took and drive him into Hell, and evil is his destination. ‘Asaa, Hamza, and Abu Amr read and he has his handle with the ha’ pronounced with a sukoon, while the rest read it with a kasra. They are two dialects. Second - The scholars said about the Almighty’s saying: And whoever contradicts the Messenger is evidence of the validity of the statement by consensus, and about the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him is a response to the Khawarij, as they claimed that the one who commits a major sin is an unbeliever, and the statement in this meaning has been presented, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: There is no verse in the Qur’an that is more beloved to me than this verse: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. He said: This is a strange hadith. Ibn Furak said: Our companions agreed that there is no eternity except for the disbeliever, and that the immoral person from the people of the Qiblah, if he dies without repenting, then even if he is punished in the Fire, he will inevitably be taken out of it through the intercession of the Messenger, or through the beginning of mercy from God Almighty. Ad-Dahhak said: “Our sheikh from the Bedouins came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I am an old man who is immersed in sins and transgressions, except that I have not associated anything with God since I knew Him and believed in Him, so what is my status with God? So God Almighty revealed: ‘Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills.’”
4:116: God Almighty says: “Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. And whoever associates others with God has certainly strayed far astray.”
4:117: The Almighty’s saying: They invoke besides Him meaning besides God except females was revealed about the people of Mecca when they worshipped idols. In is a negative meaning what, and females are idols meaning Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat. Every tribe had an idol that they worshipped and they would say: The female of the sons of so-and-so. This was said by Al-Hasan and Ibn Abbas. And with every idol came its devil who would appear to the guardians and priests and speak to them. So the speech came out in a state of astonishment because the female of every species is the lowest. This is ignorance from someone who thanks God for an inanimate object and calls it a female or believes it to be a female. It was said: Except females is dead because dead has no soul like wood and stone. And dead is described as it is described about the feminine so as not to diminish the status. You say: Stones please me as you say: Women please me. It was said: Except females are angels because they said: The angels are the daughters of God and they are our intercessors with God, according to Ad-Dahhak. And Ibn Abbas’s reading is except a idol with a fat-ha on the waw. And the letter tha is used to singularize the generic noun. It was also read wathana with the letter tha and the letter waw in the plural of wathan and awthan also as the plural of wathan like asad and asads. An-Nahhas: It was not read with it, as far as I know. I said: Abu Bakr al-Anbari mentioned - my father told us, Nasr ibn Dawud told us, Abu Ubaid told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she used to recite: They invoke not besides Him except idols. Ibn Abbas also recited: Except athana, as if he had made the plural of wathan into wathan, just as you say: jamal and jamal, then he made the plural of wathan into wathan, just as you say: mithal and mithl, then he replaced the waw with a hamza because it was joined, just as God Almighty says: And when the messengers gather (al-Murasilaat: 11) from the time, so thana was the plural of the plural, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Except a female, as the plural of anis, like ghadeer and ghadr, and al-Tabari narrated that it was the plural of inatha, like thamaar and thamar. Abu Umar al-Dani narrated this recitation from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Abu Haywah recited it with it. God the Almighty says: And they invoke none but a rebellious devil. He means Iblis, because if they obeyed him in what he suggested to them, then they worshipped him. Similar in meaning is: They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God. (al-Tawbah 9:31), meaning they obeyed them in what they commanded them to do, not that they worshipped them. The derivation of the word devil and murid has come before: the rebellious and the disobedient. Fa’il from mard, if he rebelled. Al-Azhari said: the rebel is the one who goes out of obedience. A man marrad marudan if he rebelled and went out of obedience, so he is marid, murid, and mutamarrad Ibn Arafa said: He is the one whose evil has become apparent. From this he says: A tree is mardah if its leaves fall and its branches appear. From this, a man is called amrad, meaning one whose hair appears from his cheeks.
4:118: The Almighty’s saying: The curse of God. The root of the word curse is removal, as mentioned above. In common parlance, it means removal coupled with anger and wrath. So the curse of God upon Satan - may God’s curse be upon him - is permissible in particular, and so are all the dead infidels, such as Pharaoh, Haman, and Abu Jahl. As for the living, the discussion of this has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. God Almighty says: And he said, ‘I will surely take from among Your servants a prescribed portion.’ That is, Satan said, and the meaning is: I will extract them through my temptation and lead them astray through my misguidance, and they are the infidels and the disobedient. And in the report, out of every thousand, one belongs to God and the rest belongs to Satan. I said: This is a correct meaning supported by the Almighty’s statement to Adam on the Day of Resurrection: “Send the people of Hellfire. He will say: What are the people of Hellfire? He will say: From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.” Narrated by Muslim. And the people of Hellfire are included with the share of Satan, and God knows best. It was said: Among the share is their obedience to him in things, including that they would strike a nail for the newborn at his birth and walk around with him on the day of his week, saying so that the inhabitants would recognize him.
4:119: It contains nine issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And I will surely mislead them meaning I will divert them from the path of guidance. And I will arouse in them false hopes meaning I will make them wish for a wish. This is not limited to one wish because each person’s oath is according to his desire and the evidence of his situation. It was said: I will arouse in them false hopes for a long life of goodness, repentance, and knowledge with persistence. And I will command them to cut off the ears of cattle. Al-Batak is the cutting. From this comes the word batak meaning I will carry it to cut off the ears of the bahīrah and the ṣa’ibah and the like. It is said: bataka and bataka lightened and stressed. In bataka it means a piece, and the plural is batak. Zuhair said: She flew away with a feather in her hand The second - the Almighty’s saying: And I will command them, and they will change the creation of God. All the lams are for swearing. The scholars differed as to what this change refers to. A group said: It is castration, gouging out the eyes, and cutting off the ears. Its meaning was said by Ibn Abbas, Anas, Ikrimah, and Abu Salih. All of that is torture of the animal, and prohibition and permission by tyranny and saying without proof or evidence. The ears of livestock are beauty and benefit, as are other organs. Therefore, Satan saw that he should change the creation of God Almighty with them. In the hadith of Iyadh ibn Ma’ al-Majashi’i: And I created My servants as monotheists, all of them. However, the devils came to them and led them astray from their religion. I forbade them what I had made lawful for them and commanded them to thank Me for that for which I had not sent down any authority. I commanded them to change My creation. The hadith was reported by Judge Ismail and Muslim as well. Ismail narrated that Abu al-Walid and Sulayman ibn Harb told us that Shu`bah told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas on the authority of his father who said: I came to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) while I was in poor condition. He said: Do you have any wealth? I said: Yes. He said: From what wealth? I said: From all wealth, from horses, camels, slaves - Abu al-Walid said: And sheep - He said: If God gives you wealth, let its effect be seen on you. Then he said: Do the camels of your people give birth with healthy ears, so that you go to a razor and slit their ears and say, This is a sea, and slit their skins and say, This is a harvest, to forbid them to yourself and your family? I said: Yes. He said: Everything that God has given you is permissible, and the razor of God is stronger than your razor, and the arm of God is stronger than your arm. I said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of a man who I visit and he does not accept me, then he visits me again, should I accept him or reward him? He said: Rather, I accept him. Third - Since this is the work and effect of Satan, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us: To examine the eye and the ear, and not to sacrifice an animal with a severed ear, or one with a severed ear, or one with a severed ear, or one with a severed ear, or one with a severed ear, or one with a severed ear. Narrated by Abu Dawud on the authority of Ali, who said: We were commanded, and he mentioned it: The severed ear: the one with the cut end of the ear, and the severed ear: the one with the cut end of the ear, and the severed ear: the one with the cut ear, and the defect in the ear is taken into consideration by the group of scholars. Malik and Al-Layth said: The one with a severed ear or most of the ear is not sufficient, and the one with a severed ear is sufficient, and this is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i and the group of jurists. If it is a severed ear, which is the one created without an ear, then Malik and Al-Shafi’i said: It is not permissible, and if it has a small ear, it is sufficient. Something similar was narrated from Abu Hanifa. Fourth: As for castrating animals, a group of scholars have permitted it if the intention is to benefit from it, either for fat or otherwise. The majority of scholars and their group are of the opinion that there is nothing wrong with sacrificing a castrated animal, and some of them have deemed it acceptable if it is fatter than others. Omar ibn Abdul Aziz permitted castrating horses, and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr castrated a mule of his, and Malik permitted castrating male sheep. This is permissible because the intention is not to make the animal dependent on a religion for an idol that is worshipped or for a god that is worshipped alone, but rather the intention is to make the meat tasty in what is eaten and to strengthen the male if his hope of having a female is lost. Some of them disliked this, “because of the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: They only do that without knowing.” Ibn al-Mundhir chose it and said: Because that is proven from Ibn Umar, and he used to say: It is the growth of God’s creation, and Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan disliked that, and al-Awza’i said: They disliked castrating everything that has offspring, and Ibn al-Mundhir said: And in it is our hadith, one of them from Ibn Umar: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade castrating sheep, cows, camels, and horses.” The other is the hadith of Ibn Abbas: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the immobilization of the soul and the castration of animals.” What is in Al-Muwatta’ from the chapter is what he mentioned on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar that he disliked castration and said: In it is the perfection of creation. Abu Umar said: He means in leaving castration is the perfection of creation, and it was narrated that creation grows. I said: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Ghani narrated it on the authority of Umar ibn Ismail on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Do not single out what God’s creation has created. Narrated by Al-Daraqutni. He said: Abu Abdullah Al-Mu’addal told us. Abbas bin Muhammad told us. Abu Malik Al-Nakha’i told us, on the authority of Omar bin Ismail. He mentioned it. Al-Daraqutni said: Abd Al-Samad bin Al-Nu’man narrated it on the authority of Abu Malik. Fifth - As for castration in humans, it is a calamity, because if he is castrated, his heart and strength are destroyed, unlike animals, and his offspring are cut off, as is commanded in his saying, peace be upon him: Marry and reproduce, for I will multiply your numbers before the nations.” Then there is great pain in it that may lead its owner to destruction, as it involves wasting money and taking a life, and all of that is forbidden. Then this is an example, and: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade mutilation,” and this is correct. A group of Hijazi and Kufi jurists disliked buying eunuchs from the Slavs and others, and they said: If they had not bought from them, they would not have been castrated. They did not differ that castrating the sons of Adam is not permissible and is not permitted, because it is mutilation and changing the creation of God Almighty. Likewise, cutting off the rest of their limbs without a prescribed punishment or retaliation. Abu Omar said: Sixth - If this is decided, then know that the label and notification are excluded from it. His, peace be upon him, prohibition of the devil’s condition, which is what we presented of his prohibition of torturing animals with fire and branding: cauterization with fire, and its origin is the mark. It is said: He branded something, if he marked it with a mark by which it is known, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: Their mark is on their faces (al-Fath 48:29). So the mark is the mark and the brand is the iron, and it is proven in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Anas, he said: I saw in the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the brand, with which he would brand the camels of charity, spoils of war, and other things, so that each wealth would be known and given to its rightful owner, and not be used to others. Seventh: Branding is permissible on all parts of the body except the face, because “Jabir narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade striking the face and branding the face.” Narrated by Muslim. This was only because of its importance to the parts, as it is the seat of beauty and handsomeness, and because it is the basis of the animal’s stature. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by a man striking his slave and said: Fear the face, for God created Adam in His image. That is, He did not create the image of the one who was struck. That is, the face of this one who was struck resembles the face of Adam, so he should be respected for his resemblance. This is the best interpretation that has been said, and God knows best. A group said: The reference to the change is to tattooing and what comes in its place of artificial beauty. This was said by Ibn Masoud, and from that is the authentic hadith on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God curse the tattooers and the tattooed, the pluckers and the plucked, and the filers for the sake of beauty, changing the creation of God. The hadith was narrated by Muslim and will be mentioned in full in Al-Jahsr, God willing. Tattooing is done on the hands, which is to pierce the back of a woman’s palm and wrist with a needle, then fill it with kohl or incense, turning it green. A woman has been tattooed, she is a tattooer, and the one who has that done to her, as Al-Harawi said. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The men of Sicily and Africa do it so that each one of them can show his manhood in his youth. Al-Qadi Iyad said: In Al-Harawi’s narration - one of the narrators of Muslim - instead of “the tattooer and the tattooed woman” is the tattooer and the filer with a ya instead of a mim. It is from washi which means adornment, and the origin of washi is weaving a garment in two colors. A bull with black embroidery on its face and legs, meaning that the woman exposes herself by what she does to herself of plucking, filing, and asher. The pluckers are the plural of mutanamisa and she removes hair from her face with a plucker, which is the one who removes. Hair, and it is called the namisah, Ibn al-Arabi and the people of Egypt pluck the pubic hair and it is from it, because the Sunnah is to shave the pubic hair and pluck the armpits. As for plucking the vulva, it makes it loose and hurts it and nullifies much of its benefit. The Mutafalijahat are the plural of Mutafalijah, which is the one who makes a gap in her teeth, meaning she suffers until the solid teeth return by creation, so the craft of the craft is broken. In a book other than Muslim’s, the Washirat are the plural of Washira, which is the one who makes a mark on her teeth, meaning she makes a mark in them, which are the incisions that are made in the teeth of young men. The old woman does that to imitate the young woman. All of these matters have been attested to by the hadiths cursing the one who does them and that they are among the major sins. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning for which they were forbidden. It was said: Because it is a form of deception. It was said: Because it is a form of changing the creation of God Almighty, as Ibn Masoud said, and it is more correct and it includes the first meaning. Then it was said: This forbidden thing is only in what is permanent, because it is a form of changing the creation of God Almighty. As for what is not permanent, such as kohl and adorning oneself with it for women, the scholars Malik and others permitted that, but Malik disliked it for men. Malik also permitted a woman to dye her hands with henna, and it was narrated on the authority of Umar that he disapproved of that and said: Either she should dye all of her hands or she should leave it. Malik disapproved of this narration on the authority of Umar and do not leave dyeing with henna. “For the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a woman who did not dye her hands and said: Let none of you leave her hand as if it were a man’s hand.” So she continued to dye it and she was over ninety until she died. Judge Iyad said: There is a hadith forbidding the application of henna black, mentioned by the author of Al-Masabih. And she should not neglect it and have a necklace of thread and beads around her neck, for “it is narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said to Aisha, may God be pleased with her: It is not permissible for a woman to be without a necklace, either a string or a belt. Anas said: It is recommended for a woman to hang it around her neck during prayer, even if it is a belt. Abu Ja`far al-Tabari said: In the hadith of Mas`ud there is evidence that it is not permissible to change anything of her nature in which God created her, by adding or subtracting, seeking beauty for a husband or someone else, whether her teeth are gapped or her moustache is missing, or she has an extra tooth and she removed it, or long teeth and she cut off their tips. Likewise, it is not permissible for her to shave her beard, moustache or sideburns if they grow for her, because that would be changing the creation of God. `Iyad said: And it follows from what he mentioned that whoever was created with an extra finger or an extra limb, it is not permissible for him to cut it or remove it, because it is changing the creation of God Almighty, unless this extra tooth causes him pain, in which case there is no problem in removing it, according to Abu Ja`far and others. Eighth - I told you, and from this chapter, “His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: May God curse the one who extends hair and the one who gets it extended, the one who tattoos and the one who gets it tattooed. Narrated by Muslim. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade a woman from extending her hair, which is adding more hair to it to make it thicker. The one who extends hair is the one who does that and the one who gets it extended is the one who calls for someone to do that to her. Muslim narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade a woman from attaching anything to her hair.” It was narrated on the authority of Asma’ bint Abi Bakr, who said: “A woman came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I have a daughter who is engaged to be married and her hair is fertile and her hair is falling out. Should I add it to her hair? He said: May God curse the one who adds it to her hair and the one who asks for it to be added to her hair. This is all explicit evidence that it is forbidden to add hair to her hair. Malik and a group of scholars said the same. They forbade adding anything from wool, rags, or anything else because it is like adding it to hair. Al-Layth ibn Sa`d deviated from the viewpoint of the people of the apparent meaning. Others permitted putting hair on the head and said: The prohibition on adding it to her hair came specifically. This is pure apparent meaning and ignores the meaning. Some people deviated from the viewpoint and permitted adding it to her hair in general, which is a completely false statement that is refuted by the hadiths. It was narrated from `Aisha may God be pleased with her but it is not authentic. It was narrated from Ibn Sirin that a man asked him and said: My mother used to comb women’s hair. Do you think I would eat from her money? He said: If she adds it to her hair, then no. The prohibition does not include what is tied with colored silk threads for the purpose of adornment and beautification. And God knows best. Ninth - A group said: What is meant by changing the creation of God is that God the Most High created the sun, the moon, the stones, fire, and other creatures, to be considered and benefited from, then the infidels changed them by making them gods to be worshipped. Al-Zajjaj said: God the Most High created the livestock to be ridden and eaten, so He forbade them to themselves, and He made the sun, the moon, and the stones subservient to the people, so they made them gods to be worshipped. Thus, they changed what God created. A group of the people of interpretation said: Mujahid, Al-Dahhak, Saeed bin Jubayr, and Qatadah. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “So let them change the creation of God” means the religion of God. Al-Nakha’i said it, and Al-Tabari chose it. He said: If that is its meaning, then it includes doing everything that God has forbidden, such as castration, tattooing, and other sins, because Satan calls to all sins, meaning let them change what God created in His religion. Mujahid also said: So let them change the creation of God means the nature of God upon which people were created, meaning that they were born as Muslims, so Satan ordered them to change it, and this is the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: Every child is born in a state of fitrah, but his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian. So the meaning of creation goes back to what He created in them on the Day of the Atom of belief in Him in the words of God Almighty: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes. (al-A’raf 7:172) Ibn al-Arabi said: It was narrated on the authority of Tawus that he would not attend the marriage of a black woman to a white woman, nor a white woman to a black woman, and he would say that this is from the words of God: So let them change the creation of God. Al-Qadi said: Even if the wording allows it, it is specific to what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, carried out in the marriage of his freed slave Zayd, who was white, to his wet-nurse Barakah al-Habashiyyah, the mother of Usama, who was blacker than white. This was something that was hidden from Tawus despite his knowledge. I said: Then Usama married Fatima bint Qafis, who was white and Quraish, and she was married to Bilal, the sister of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, who was a Zuhri woman. This also applies and was hidden from them. God Almighty says: And whoever takes Satan as a friend instead of God meaning obeys him and abandons God’s command has certainly lost meaning he has diminished his soul and cheated it by giving Satan God Almighty’s right over him and abandoning Him for his sake.
4:120: The Almighty says: He promises them meaning He promises them his falsehoods and nonsense of money, status and leadership, and that there will be no resurrection or punishment, and He makes them think of poverty so that they will not spend in good deeds. And He gives them false hope likewise. And Satan promises them nothing but deception meaning trickery. Ibn Arafa said: Deception is that which you see as having an appearance that you like, while it has an inner aspect that is hated or unknown. Satan is a deceiver, because he leads to what the self loves and behind that is what is bad. Those is the beginning. Their abode is the second beginning. Hell is the predicate of the second, and the sentence is the predicate of the first. A refuge is a shelter, and the verb from it is Haasa Yahis. And who is more truthful than God in statement is the beginning and the predicate. Qayla is for clarification. Qayla is for clarification. Qayla means that no one is more truthful than God. We have already discussed the meanings contained in these verses, and praise be to God.
4:121: God Almighty says: Their refuge is Hell, and they will find no escape from it.
4:122: God Almighty says: “And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide forever. The promise of God is truth. And who is more truthful than God in statement?”
4:123: The Almighty said: It is not according to your desires nor according to the desires of the People of the Book. Abu Ja`far al-Madani read It is not according to your desires nor according to the desires of the People of the Book with a light ya’ in both of them. Among the best narrations about its revelation is what al-Hakam ibn Abaan narrated on the authority of `Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: The Jews and Christians said, None will enter Paradise except those who are from us. The Quraysh said, We will not be resurrected. So God revealed, Not according to your desires, nor according to the desires of the People of the Scripture. Qatada and As-Suddi said: The believers and the People of the Scripture boasted. The People of the Scripture said, Our Prophet came before your Prophet and our Book came before your Book, and we have more right to God than you. The believers said, Our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our Book supersedes all other books. So this verse was revealed. God the Almighty said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. Evil here means polytheism. Al-Hasan said: This verse is about the disbeliever. He recited: Is anyone but the disbeliever recompensed? And from him also: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. He said: This is for those whom God wants to humiliate. As for those whom He wants to honor, God has mentioned a people and said: “Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did and overlook their misdeeds. They are among the companions of Paradise, the true promise which they were promised.” (al-Ahqaf 46:16) Ad-Dahhak said: He means the Jews, Christians, Magians, and the disbelievers of the Arabs. The majority said: The wording of the verse is general, and the disbeliever and the believer are recompensed for their evil deeds. As for the recompense of the disbeliever, it is Hell because his disbelief has destroyed him, and as for the believer, it is the calamities of this world, as Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: When the verse Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it was revealed, it reached a great extent among the Muslims, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They came close and blocked, for in everything that befalls a Muslim there is expiation, even the calamity that befalls him and the thorn that pricks him. And Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim included in Nawadir Al-Usul in the ninety-fifth chapter, Ibrahim bin Al-Mustamir Al-Hudhali told us, he said, Abd Al-Rahman bin Salim bin Hayyan Abu Zaid told us, he said: I heard my father mention on the authority of his father who said: I accompanied Ibn Omar from Mecca to Medina, and he said to Nafi’: Do not pass between the crucified, meaning Ibn al-Zubayr. He said: What surprised him in the middle of the night was that a young camel was struck, so he sat up and wiped his eye and then said: May God have mercy on you, Abu Khabib, if you were and if you were! I heard your father al-Zubayr say: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it in this world or in the Hereafter.” If this is for that, then take it easy. Al-Tirmidhi Abu Abdullah said: As for the revelation, he summarized it and said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper. So it included the righteous and the wicked, the enemy and the friend, the believer and the disbeliever. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, distinguished in this hadith between the two places, “and said: He will be recompensed for it in this world or in the Hereafter.” The recompense is not collected for him in the places. Do you not see that Ibn Umar said: If this is for that, then take it easy. Its meaning is that he fought in the sanctuary of God and caused a great event in it until he burned the House and threw a catapult at the Black Stone, so it cracked until it was covered with silver, and it is still there to this day. Likewise, he heard the house groaning, Ah, ah! When Ibn Umar saw what he had done, then saw him killed and crucified, he remembered the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. Then he said: If this killing is for what he did, then it is better for him, meaning that he was recompensed for that evil, this killing and crucifixion. May God have mercy on him! Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, distinguished between the two groups in another incident. My father, may God have mercy on him, told us, he said: Abu Na’im told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Usamah ibn al-Haad al-Laythi, he said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it was revealed, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, said: This is not lasting. He said: From us, Abu Bakr. The believer will be recompensed for it in this world, and the disbeliever will be recompensed for it on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Jarud told us, he said: Wakee’, Abu Mu’awiyah, and Abda told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Zuhair al-Thaqafi, he said: When the verse, Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it was revealed, Abu Bakr said: How can we be righteous, O Messenger of God, with this? We will be rewarded for everything we have done. He said: May God forgive you, O Abu Bakr. Are you not afflicted, are you not grieved, are you not afflicted with hardships? He said: Yes. He said: This is what you will be rewarded for. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained what the revelation had summarized in its words: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr As-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, that when this was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: As for you, O Abu Bakr, and the believers, you will pass through this in this world until you meet God, and you will have no sins. As for the others, it will be collected for them until they are rewarded for it on the Day of Resurrection. He said: A strange hadith: There is an argument in its chain of transmission. Musa ibn Ubaydah is considered weak in the hadith. Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Qattan and Ahmad ibn Hanbal weakened him. The client of Ibn Saba` is unknown. This has been narrated from Abu Bakr through other chains of transmission, but it also has no sound chain of transmission. There is also a hadith on the same topic from Aisha. I said: It was narrated by Ismail bin Ishaq Al-Qadi. He said: Sulayman bin Harb told us. He said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zayd, on the authority of his mother, that she asked Aisha about this verse: And if you disclose what is in your souls or conceal it (al-Baqarah 2:284) and about this verse: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it. Aisha said: None of us asked me. I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: O Aisha, this is a pledge to God for what befalls him of fever, calamity, and thorns, even the merchandise that he weakens in his sleeve and loses it and is frightened and finds it in his pocket, until the believer emerges from his sins as gold emerges from the bellows. “And a noun is not implied in all of these sayings, and the estimate is: What is from your wealth is not what you wish for, but whoever knows evil will be recompensed for it.” And it was said: The meaning is that God’s reward is not according to your wishes, as it has been mentioned previously: And those who believe and do righteous deeds - We will admit them to gardens. God the Almighty said: And he will not find for himself besides God any protector or helper. He means the polytheists, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. (Ghafir 40:51) It was said: Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, unless he repents. The Friday reading is and he will not find for himself in the subjunctive mood, in apposition to will be recompensed for it. Ibn Bakkar narrated on the authority of Ibn Amir and he will not find for himself in the nominative case, as a new resumption. If the verse is applied to the disbeliever, then tomorrow he will have no protector or helper, and if it is applied to the believer, then he will have no protector or helper besides God.
4:124: The condition of faith is because the polytheists claimed to serve the Kaaba, feed the pilgrims, and host guests, and the People of the Book were the first to say that they were the children of God and His beloved. So God Almighty made it clear that good deeds are not accepted without faith. The two sheikhs, Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir, read they will enter Paradise with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the kha’ on what the doer was not named. The rest read with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the kha’, meaning they will enter Paradise through their deeds. The mention of the naqir, which is the dot on the back of the date pit, has already been mentioned.
4:125: The Almighty said: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to God while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth? The religion of Islam is superior to all other religions. Submits himself to God means that he sincerely devoted his religion to God, submitted to Him, and turned to Him in worship. Ibn Abbas said: He meant Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. Dina is in the accusative case as a statement, and he is good is the subject and predicate in the place of the state, meaning monotheist, so the People of the Book are not included in it, because they abandoned belief in Muhammad, peace be upon him. The religion is the religion and the monotheist is the Muslim, and this has been mentioned previously. God Almighty said: And God took Abraham as a friend. Tha’lab said: The friend was called a friend because his love permeates the heart and leaves no gap in it without filling it. He recited the words of Bashar: The path of the soul has penetrated me, and because of it, Khalil was named Khalil. And Khalil is an active participle in the sense of an agent, like Al-Alim in the sense of the Knower. It was also said that it is in the sense of the passive participle, like Al-Habib in the sense of the beloved. Abraham loved God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was beloved by God. It was also said that Al-Khalil is from the specialization, so God Almighty knows best. Abraham was special in his time for the message, and Al-Nahhas chose this. He said: The evidence for this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God has taken your companion as a friend, who helps himself, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If I were to take a close friend, I would have taken Abu Bakr as a close friend. That is, if I were to single out anyone for something, I would have singled out Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. This is a response to those who claim that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, singled out some of his companions for something of the religion. It was said: The close friend is the one in need, so Abraham is the close friend of God in the sense that he is poor and in need of God Almighty: as if he is the one who is in trouble. Zuhair said, praising Haram bin Sinan: And if a friend comes to him one day in a state of absence, he says, Neither my wealth nor my harem are absent. That is, there is no impermissibility. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of Khalil is the one whose love is free from any defect. It is permissible for him to be called Khalil God because he is the one whom He loved and chose with complete love. It is also permissible for him to be called Khalil God meaning one who is poor before God the Most High, because he did not make his poverty or neediness except for God the Most High, sincere in that, and the defect is poverty. It was narrated that when he threw the catapult and was in the air, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said: Do you have a need? He said: As for you, no. So God the Most High made him a friend of Abraham, supporting him. It was said: He was called that because he went to a friend of his in Egypt, or it was said: Mosul, to buy food from him, but he did not find its owner. So he filled his bags with sand and went with it to his family, so he ate and slept. His family opened it and found it to be flour, so they made him some of it. When they brought it to him, he said: Where did you get this from? They said: Who brought it from your Egyptian friend? He said: It is from my friend, meaning God Almighty, so he was called the friend of God for that. It was said: He hosted the leaders of the infidels and gave them gifts and was kind to them. They said to him: What do you need? He said: My need is that you prostrate once. So they prostrated. He called upon God Almighty and said: O God, I have done what I could, so do, O God, what is worthy of that. So God guided them to Islam, so God took him as a friend for that reason. It was said: When the angels entered upon him in the form of humans, he brought a fattened calf, but they did not eat from it and said: We do not eat anything without a price. So he said to them: Give its price and eat. They said: What is its price? He said: That you say at the beginning: In the name of God and at the end: Praise be to God. So they said among themselves: It is right for God to take him as a friend, so God took him as a friend. Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God took Abraham as a friend because of his feeding and food, his spreading of peace, and his praying at night while people were asleep. Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Gabriel, why did God take Abraham as a friend? He said: To feed him food, O Muhammad. It was said: The meaning of a friend is the one who is loyal for the sake of God and hostile for the sake of God. Friendship between people is derived from the sharing of secrets between close friends. It was said: It is from friendship, so each of the two friends fills the gap between his companion. In the book of Abu Dawud, it was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man is like his friend, so let each one of you look at whom he befriends. And he who said it well: He who does not have a close friend in God, his friend is in danger. last: If you have a friend, do not trust every brother. If you are given a choice between them, stick to those who are rational and modest. The mind has no power if the virtues of the infidels are different. Hassan bin Thabit, may God be pleased with him, said: Men's friends are many, but in adversity they are few. Do not be deceived by the friendship of someone you befriend, for you have no friend with your deputy.
