Every brother says I am loyal but does not do what he says He has a good lineage and religion, so when he says he is the doer
4:126: The Almighty says: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth meaning ownership and creation. The meaning is that He took Abraham as a friend because of his good obedience, not because he needed to befriend him or to increase his number and support him. How could he have anything in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? Rather, he was forced to comply with his command.
4:127: It was revealed because some of the Companions asked about the matter of women and their rulings in inheritance and other matters, so God commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to say to them: God gives you a legal opinion about them, meaning He explains to you the ruling on what you asked about. This verse refers back to what the surah began with regarding the matter of women, and they had rulings that they did not know, so they asked and it was said to them: God gives you a legal opinion about them. Ashhab narrated on the authority of Malik that he said: “The Prophet, peace be upon him, used to ask questions but did not answer until revelation was sent down to him.” This is in the Book of God: “And they ask you about women. Say: God gives you a legal opinion about them.” And they ask you about orphans. (al-Baqarah 2:220) and They ask you about wine and gambling. (al-Baqarah 2:219) and And they ask you about the mountains. (Ta-Ha 20:195). God the Almighty said: And what is recited to you “And what” is in the nominative case in apposition to the name of God the Almighty: The meaning is: And the Qur’an gives you a fatwa concerning them, and it is His saying: Then marry such women as seem good to you (An-Nisa’: 3) and it has been mentioned previously. And God the Almighty said: And you desire to marry them meaning: and you desire not to marry them, then from was deleted. And it was said: and you desire to marry them, then in was deleted. Saeed bin Jubayr and Mujahid said: And he desires to marry her if she is very wealthy. The hadith of Aisha strengthens the deletion of from, because in her hadith: And you desire to marry them is like one of you desires to marry his orphan girl who is in his care when she is little in wealth and beauty. And the beginning of the surah was mentioned previously.
4:128: It contains seven issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And if a woman is raised by an implied verb that is explained by what follows it, and feared means expected. The statement of the one who said: feared was certain is wrong. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: And if a woman feared from her husband the continuation of rebellion, Al-Nahhas said: The difference between rebellion and turning away is that rebellion is distancing, and turning away is that he does not speak to her or feel comfortable with her, and the verse was revealed because of Sawda of the house of Zam’ah. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Sawdah feared that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would divorce her, so she said: Do not divorce me, but keep me and devote my day with you to Aisha. So he did. Then the verse was revealed: There is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best. So whatever they agree upon is permissible. He said: This is a good and strange hadith. Ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab: That Rafi’ bin Khadij was married to Khawlah bint Muhammad bin Maslama, and he was displeased with her situation, either because he grew old or because of someone else, so he wanted to divorce her, but she said: Do not divorce me, and divide for me whatever you wish. So the Sunnah was broken by that, and the verse was revealed: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, and Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, she said: A man has a wife whom he does not like much of and wants to leave her, so she says, I will make you my concern. So this verse was revealed. The general reading is that they should reconcile. Most of the Kufians read that they should reconcile. Al-Jahdary and Uthman al-Batti read that they should reconcile, and the meaning is that they should reconcile. Then it was assimilated. Second: In this verse of jurisprudence there is a response to the foolish ignorant people who believe that if a man takes a woman’s youth and she becomes old, he should not exchange her. Ibn Abi Malekah said: “When Sawdah bint Zam’ah became old, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to divorce her, but she preferred to be with him. So she said to him: Keep me and devote my day to Aisha. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did so, and she died while she was one of his wives.” I said: And the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslama did the same. Malik narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Rafi ibn Khadij that he married the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansariyya, and she remained with him until she grew old, then he married a young girl, and he preferred the young woman over her, so she asked him for a divorce, so he divorced her once, then he neglected her until she was permissible, then he took her back, then he returned and delayed the young woman over her, so she asked him for a divorce, so he divorced her once, then he took her back and preferred the young woman over her, so she asked him for a divorce, so he said: As you wish, only one remains, so if you wish, you can settle for what you see of preference, and if you wish, I will leave you, she said: Rather, I will settle for preference. So he kept her in that state and Rafi did not see any sin when she settled with him on the basis of preference. It was narrated by Muammar from Al-Zuhri with his wording and meaning, and he added: This is the reconciliation that we have been informed about, And if a woman fears from her husband desertion or evasion, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves - and settlement is best. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: His statement, and God knows best: So he preferred the younger woman over her means in his inclination towards her and his enthusiasm for her, not that he preferred her over her in food, clothing and sleeping, because this should not be thought of someone like Rafi, and God knows best. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shabah mentioned: Abu Al-Ahwas told us on the authority of Samak bin Harb on the authority of Khalid bin Arara on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that a man asked him about this verse, and he said: It is a woman who is with a man and his eyes turn away from her because of her ugliness or poverty or old age or bad character and she hates to leave him, so if she gives him something from her dowry, it is permissible for him to take it, and if she gives him some of her days, there is no blame. Ad-Dahhak said: There is nothing wrong with reducing her right if He married a woman who was younger than her and he liked her. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It is a man who has an older woman under him and marries a younger woman. He says to the older woman: I will give you from my money on condition that I divide with this younger woman more than I divide with you during the night and day. The other woman is satisfied with what they agreed upon, but if she refuses to be satisfied, then he must treat them equally in dividing. Third: Our scholars said: In this, all types of reconciliation are permissible in this case, such as the husband giving on condition that she be patient, or she giving on condition that the husband gives preference, or on condition that he gives preference and adheres to the marriage contract, or the reconciliation is based on patience and preference without giving, then all of this is permissible. It may be permissible for one of them to reconcile with her companion for her day with something that she gives her, as the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did, and that is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was angry with Safiyyah, so she said to Aisha: Reconcile between me and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I have given my day to you. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad mentioned this in his rulings, “On the authority of Aisha, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was angry with Safiyyah for something, so Safiyyah said to me: Would you please the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on my behalf, and you will have my day? She said: So I put on a veil that I had that was dyed with raspberries and sprinkled it, then I came and sat beside the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Go away from me, for this is not your day. I said: That is the grace of God, which He gives to whom He wills. I told him the report and he was pleased with her. It indicates that leaving women equal and giving preference to some over others is not permissible except with the permission and approval of the one who is preferred. Fourth: The Kufians read yasaliha and the rest read yansaliha. Al-Jahdari read yasaliha. Whoever read yasaliha, he explained that it is known in the speech of the Arabs that if there is a quarrel between people, it is to say tasaliha al-qawm and not tasaliha al-qawm. If it had been tasaliha, its source would have been islah. Whoever read yasaliha has used something similar to it in quarreling and dispute, as he said, “fa tasaliha bainu” (he made peace between them). He put his saying saliha in the accusative case according to this reading as a maf’ul, and it is a noun like the gift from a’ta’a fa tasaliha sulh like tasaliha amuran. And it is also a maf’ul according to the reading of whoever read yasaliha because tafa’ala came transitive and it is possible that it is a source whose augmentations were deleted. Whoever read yasaliha, the original is yasaliha, then it became yasaliha, then the ta’ was replaced with a sad and the sad was assimilated into it, and the sad was not replaced with a ta’ because of the extension of the sigh. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: And reconciliation is better. This is a general, absolute expression that implies that true reconciliation, which brings peace to souls and removes differences, is absolutely good. This meaning includes everything that a reconciliation takes place between a man and his wife, whether in money, intercourse, or anything else. Better means better than separation, because persistence in differences, enmity, and hatred are the foundations of evil. And he, peace be upon him, said about hatred: It is the shaver, meaning the shaver of religion, not the shaver of hair. Sixth - The Almighty’s saying: And the souls have brought forth greed. This is report that greed is in everyone and that man is bound to be greedy by virtue of his creation and nature until he leads his companion to do some of what he dislikes. It is said: greed, greed with a broken sheen. Ibn Jubayr said: It is the woman’s greed for her husband’s provision and for his dividing her days for her. Ibn Zayd said: Greed here is from him and from her. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is better, because most women are greedy for their share from their husbands, and most husbands are greedy for their share from their wives. Greed is controlling beliefs and will, ambitions, money, and the like. Whatever is excessive in it regarding religion is praiseworthy, and whatever is excessive in it regarding other matters, there is some blame in it, and it is what God said about it: And whoever is protected from the greed of his soul - it is those who will be successful. (al-Hashr 59:9) And whatever reaches the level of preventing legitimate rights or what chivalry requires is miserliness, and it is a vice. And if miserliness leads to these blameworthy morals and vile characteristics, there is no good to be hoped for or any hoped-for improvement.. I said: It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the Ansar: Who is your master? They said: The grandfather is stingy. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What disease is worse than stinginess? They said: How is that, O Messenger of God? He said: A people settled on the coast of the sea and, due to their stinginess, they hated having guests stay with them. So they said: Let the men among us stay away from the women, so that the men will apologize to the guests for the distance of the women and the women will apologize for the distance of the men. So they did and it took a long time for them, so the men were busy with the men and the women with the women. Al-Mawardi mentioned this previously. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: And if you do good and fear God is a condition: Then God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted. The answer: This is addressed to husbands, in that the husband may be stingy and not do good, meaning if you do good and fear God in your dealings with women, then your staying with them, despite your disliking their company and avoiding their injustice, is better for you.
4:129: The Almighty said: "And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so. So do not incline completely towards [some] women." The Almighty informed us of the negation of the ability to be equal between women, and that is in the inclination of nature towards love, intercourse, and the portion of the heart. So God Almighty described the state of humans and that by virtue of creation they do not possess the inclination of their hearts towards some over others, and for this reason "he, peace be upon him, used to say: O God, this is my division of what I own, so do not blame me for what You own and I do not own.” Then he forbade it and said: Do not lean completely. Mujahid said: Do not intentionally do wrong, but rather adhere to equality in division and spending, because this is what is possible. This will be explained in detail in Al-Ahzab, God willing. Qatada narrated on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Anas on the authority of Bashir bin Nahik on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has two wives and does not treat them equally will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side of his body leaning. The Almighty said: Then leave her as if she were suspended, meaning she is neither divorced nor married, as Al-Hasan said. This is a simile for something suspended from something, because it does not settle on the ground nor does it carry what it is suspended on. This is consistent in their saying in the proverb: A land from the compound by suspension, and in the grammarians’ terminology, from the one who suspends the action, and from it in the hadith of Umm Zar’ in the woman’s saying: My husband is a lover, if he sets out he sets out, and if I keep quiet I am suspended. Qatada said: Like a prisoner. And this is how he read fatadharuha ka al-masjunnah. Ibn Masoud read fatadharuha as if she were suspended. The position of fatadharuha is accusative because it is the answer to the prohibition, and the kaf in ka al-mu’allaqa is also in the accusative position.
4:130: The Almighty said: And if they separate, God will enrich each from His abundance. That is, if they do not reconcile, but rather separate, then let them think well of God, for He may provide for the man a wife who will please his eyes, and for the woman someone who will provide for her. It was narrated on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad that a man complained to him about poverty, so he ordered him to marry. The man went and got married, then came to him and complained to him about poverty, so he ordered him to divorce. He was asked about this verse, and he said: I ordered him to marry, perhaps he is one of the people of this verse: If they should be poor, God will enrich them from His bounty. (al-Nur 24:32) So since he was not one of the people of that verse, I ordered him to divorce, and I said: Perhaps he is one of the people of this verse: And if they separate, God will enrich each from His abundance.
4:131: The Almighty said: And We have already enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you meaning the command to fear God was general for all nations and the discussion of fear God has already passed. And you is in apposition to those “that you fear God” in the accusative case. Al-Akhfash said: meaning that you fear God. Some of the scholars said: This verse is the millstone of the verses of the Qur’an because all of it revolves around it.
4:132: The Almighty said: "And if you disbelieve, then to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And God is Free of need and Praiseworthy." "And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs." If someone says: What is the benefit of this repetition, then there are two answers: One is that it was repeated for emphasis so that the servants would be aware and see what is in His kingdom and His dominion and that He is independent of the worlds. The second answer is that it was repeated for benefits: So in the first, He informed that God the Almighty enriches everyone from His vastness because He has whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, so His treasures are inexhaustible. Then He said: We have enjoined upon you and the People of the Book piety. And if you disbelieve, meaning if you disbelieve, then He is sufficient for you because He has whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Then He informed in the third about the preservation of His creation and His management of them by His saying: And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs, because He has whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And He said: What is in the heavens, and He did not say whoever is in the heavens, because he took it as a genus, and in the heavens and the earth there are those who have reason and those who do not.
4:133: God Almighty said: If He wills, He can take you away meaning death O people meaning the polytheists and hypocrites and bring others meaning other than you. And when this verse was revealed, “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, struck Salman on the back and said: They are the people of this "and it was said: The verse is general, that if you disbelieve, He will take you away and bring a creation more obedient to God than you. This is like what He said in another verse: "And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people; then they will not be the likes of you." (Muhammad 47:38) And in the verse there is a warning and a warning to all who have a position of authority, leadership, and leadership but are not just with their subjects, or who are knowledgeable but do not act upon their knowledge or advise people, that He will take them away and bring someone else. "And God is Able to do that." And ability is an eternal attribute, His abilities are infinite, just as His knowledge is infinite. The past and the future in His attributes have one meaning. He only mentioned the past specifically so that it would not be imagined that it occurs in His essence and attributes. Ability is that by which the action occurs, and it is not permissible for inability to exist with it.
4:134: That is, whoever does what God has enjoined upon him, seeking the Hereafter, God will give him that in the Hereafter. And whoever does it seeking the world, God will give him what was written for him in the world, and he will have no reward in the Hereafter, because he worked for someone other than God, as God Almighty said: And he will have no share in the Hereafter (al-Shura 42:20) and God Almighty said: Those are the ones who will have nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire (Hud 11:16). This is based on the fact that what is meant by the verse is the hypocrites and the disbelievers, and this is the choice of At-Tabari. It was narrated that the polytheists did not believe in the Resurrection, but rather sought to draw closer to God Almighty so that He would make things easier for them in this world and remove from them its hardships, so God Almighty revealed: “Whoever desires the reward of this world, then with God is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And God is Hearing and Seeing.” That is, He hears what they say and sees what they conceal.
4:135: It contains ten issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Be steadfast in justice. “Be steadfast” is an exaggerated construction, meaning that you should repeatedly stand up for justice, which is fairness in your testimony against yourselves. A person’s testimony against himself is his acknowledgement of the rights owed to him. Then he mentioned the parents because of the obligation to be dutiful to them and their great status. Then he repeated the words close relatives, since they are the source of affection and fanaticism. So the stranger among the people is more deserving of being held up for justice and testified against. So the speech in the surah came about preserving the rights of people in money. Second: There is no disagreement among scholars regarding the validity of the rulings of this verse, and that the testimony of a child against his parents, the father and mother, is valid, and that does not prevent him from being dutiful to them. Rather, being dutiful to them includes testifying against them and saving them from falsehood, which is the meaning of the Most High’s statement: Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire (al-Tahrim 66:6). If he testifies for them or they testify for him, which is: Third: There has been disagreement about it in the past and present. Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri said: Those who passed away from the righteous predecessors permitted the testimony of parents and brothers, and they interpreted in that the saying of God Almighty: Be upholders of justice, witnesses for God. No one from the righteous predecessors, may God be pleased with them, was accused of that. Then things appeared among the people that led the rulers to accuse them, so the testimony of the one who is accused was abandoned and it became impermissible in the case of a son, father, brother, husband and wife. This is the doctrine of Al-Hasan, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Sha’bi, Shuraih, Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Shafi’i and Ibn Hanbal. Some people permitted the testimony of one another if they were just. It was narrated from ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattab that he permitted it, and it was also narrated from ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd Al-‘Aziz, and Ishaq, Al-Thawri and Al-Muzani said the same. The doctrine of Malik is that the testimony of a brother for his brother is permissible if he is just except in relation to lineage. Ibn Wahb narrated from him that it is not permissible if it is in relation to his dependents or a share of money that he inherits. The Malikis and Abu Hanifa said: The testimony of the husband for his wife is not accepted because of the continuity of the benefits of property between them and it is the subject of the testimony. Al-Shafi’i said: The testimony of the spouses for each other is permissible, because they are strangers and there is only a marriage contract between them, which is subject to termination. The principle is that the testimony is accepted except where it is specified in what is other than the specified, so it remains as the principle. This is weak, because marriage requires tenderness, continuity, intimacy and love, so the accusation is strong and apparent: Abu Dawood narrated from the hadith of Sulayman bin Musa, on the authority of Amr bin Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather. The Messenger of God rejected the testimony of the traitor, male or female, and the one who is ignorant against his brother, and rejected the testimony of the one who is content with the people of the house and permitted it for others. Al-Khattabi said: The one who is ignorant is the one who has apparent enmity with the one who is testified against, so his testimony against him is rejected due to suspicion. Abu Hanifa said: His testimony against the enemy is acceptable if he is just. The one who is content is the one who asks and seeks food, and the origin of the one who is content is the question. It is said about the one who is content: he is the one who is cut off from the people, serves them and takes care of their needs, and this is like the hired hand or the agent and the like. The meaning of rejecting this testimony is the accusation of bringing benefit to himself, because the one who is content with the people of the house benefits from the benefit that comes to them, and whoever brings benefit to himself with testimony, his testimony is rejected, like someone who testifies for a man to buy a house for which he is the pre-emptor, or like someone who is ruled in his favor against a man for a debt while he is bankrupt, so the bankrupt testifies against a man for a debt and the like. Al-Khattabi said: And whoever rejects the testimony of the one who is content with the people of the house because of bringing benefit, then his statement is similar to rejecting the testimony of the husband for his wife, because what is between them of accusation in bringing benefit is greater, and this is what Abu Hanifa went to: And the hadith is an argument against whoever permits the testimony of the father for his son, because he brings benefit through it due to his innate love and inclination towards it, and because he owns his money over it, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You and your wealth belong to your father. Among those whose testimony is rejected by Malik is the Bedouin against the villager. He said: Unless he is in the desert or a village. As for the one who testifies in the city as a Bedouin and leaves his neighbors from the city dwellers, I think he is suspicious. Abu Dawud al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The testimony of a Bedouin against a villager is not permissible. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hakam said: Malik interpreted this hadith to mean that it means testimony regarding rights and property, and testimony regarding blood money and similar matters that people are required to bear is not acceptable. The majority of scholars said: The testimony of a Bedouin, if he is just and establishes the testimony in the proper manner, is permissible, and God knows best. This has been discussed in Al-Baqarah and will be discussed in full in Bara’ah, God willing. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: Witnesses for God is an accusative as an attribute of Qawwamin. If you wish, it can be a predicate after a predicate. An-Nahhas said: And better than these two is that it be an accusative as a state of what is in Qawwamin of mentioning those who believe, because it is the same meaning, that is, be upholders of justice when you testify. Ibn Atiyah said: And the state in it is weak in meaning, because it is a specification of upholding justice to the meaning of testimony. And witnesses is not declined because it has the feminine alif. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: For God means for God’s sake, for His sake, for His pleasure and reward. Even if it is against yourselves is related to witnesses. This is the apparent meaning that people have interpreted it. This testimony mentioned is regarding rights, so he acknowledges them for their people. This is his bearing witness against himself, as God Almighty taught the believers this, as Ibn Abbas said: They were commanded to speak the truth, even if it is against themselves. It is possible that His saying: Witnesses for God means regarding the Oneness of God, and His saying: Even if it is against yourselves is related to maintainers. The first interpretation is clearer. Sixth - The Almighty’s saying: If he is rich or poor, then God is more worthy of them both. There is an implied pronoun in the speech, which is the name of was, meaning that if the plaintiff or the one being testified against is rich, then his wealth is not taken into consideration and he is not feared. And if he is poor, then he is not taken into consideration out of compassion for him. Then God is more worthy of them both, meaning in what He has chosen for them of poverty and wealth. Al-Suddi said: A rich man and a poor man disputed before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sided with the poor man and saw that the poor man should not wrong the rich man. So the verse was revealed. Seventh - The Almighty’s statement: Then God is more worthy of them both. He only said them both and did not say it, even though or only indicates a single acquisition, because the meaning is that God is more worthy of each one of them. Al-Akhfash said: Or cannot be in the sense of and, meaning that he could be rich or poor, so God is more worthy of the two opponents, no matter who they are. This is weak. It was said: He only said them both because they were mentioned before, as God the Almighty said: And if he has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is a sixth. (An-Nisa’: 12) Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: So do not follow desire is a prohibition, for following desire is a destructive outcome. God Almighty said: So judge between people in truth and do not follow desire, for it will lead you astray from the way of God (Sad: 26). So following desire is interpreted as bearing witness to something that is not true, and as injustice in judgment, and so on. Al-Sha’bi said: God Almighty has imposed three things on the rulers: that they not follow desire, that they not fear people and that they fear Him, and that they not exchange His verses for a small price. That you be just is in the accusative case. Ninth - The Almighty’s saying: And if they twist or turn away The reading of and if they twist is from lawwat meaning I pushed someone’s right meaning I pushed him with it. The verb from it is lawwa, and the original form of it is lawwa. The ya was changed to an alif due to its vowel and the vowel of what preceded it. The source is liya, and the original form is lawyaan, and layyanan, and the original form is lawyanan, then the waw was assimilated into the ya. Al-Qatibi said that talawa is from lay in testimony and inclination toward one of the two opponents. Ibn Amir and the Kufians read talawa, meaning you have undertaken the matter and turned away, from your saying: I have assumed the matter. So the meaning of the speech is to rebuke those who turn away from carrying out the matter. It was said that the meaning of talawa is al-‘arād, so the reading with a damma on the lam conveys two meanings: al-wilāyah and al-‘arādah, while the reading with two waws conveys one meaning, which is al-i’rād. Some grammarians claimed that whoever reads talawa made a mistake, because there is no meaning of al-wilāyah here. Al-Nahhas and others said: This is not necessary, but talawa is the meaning of talawa, and that is because its original form is talawa, so the damma on the waw was considered too heavy, followed by another waw, so the vowel was placed on the lam. One of the two waws was deleted due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, which is the reading with the sukoon of the lam and two waws mentioned by Makki. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning according to his reading is and they twisted, then he hamzated the first waw, so it became tal’u, then the hamzah was lightened by placing its vowel on the lam, so it became talawa, and its root is talawa, so the two readings agree on this estimation. Al-Nahhas, Makki, Ibn al-Arabi, and others mentioned it. Ibn Abbas said: It is about the two opponents sitting in front of the judge, and the judge has me and his turning away from one of them to the other. What is like this is prolonging the speech and dragging it until the judgment is passed and its implementation is lost for the one the judge is inclined toward. Ibn Atiyah said: I have seen some judges do that, and God is the judge of all. Ibn Abbas also said, as-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, al-Dahhak, and Mujahid: It is about witnesses, the witness twists the testimony with his tongue and distorts it, so he does not say the truth in it, or he turns away from performing the truth in it. The wording of the verse includes the judgment and testimony, and every person is commanded to be just. In the hadith: He who finds it is permitted to expose his honor and punish him. Ibn al-A'rabi said: His punishment is his imprisonment and his honor is his complaint. Tenth - Some scholars have used this verse as evidence to reject the testimony of a slave, saying: God Almighty made the judge a witness in this verse, and this is the clearest evidence that the slave is not among those who are qualified to testify, because what is intended from him is independence in this important matter if the need arises for him, and this is not possible from the slave at all, so the testimony was rejected.
4:136: The Almighty said: O you who believe, believe. The verse was revealed about all believers, and the meaning is, O you who believe, persist in your belief and remain steadfast in it. And the Book that was sent down to His Messenger, meaning the Qur'an. And the Book that was sent down before, meaning every book sent down to the prophets. Ibn Kathir, Abu Omar, and Ibn Amir read was sent down and was sent down with the dammah, the rest read was sent down and was sent down with the fathah. It was said that it was revealed about those who believed in the prophets who came before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, peace be upon them. It was said that it was addressed to the hypocrites, and the meaning according to this is, O you who believe, in appearance, be sincere to God. It was said that what is meant is the polytheists, and the meaning is, O you who believe in Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Al-Taghut, believe in God, meaning believe in God and His books.
4:137: It was said: The meaning is that they believed in Moses and disbelieved in Ezra, then they believed in Ezra then disbelieved in Jesus, then they increased in disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: Those who believed in Moses then believed in Ezra, then disbelieved after Ezra in the Messiah, and the Christians disbelieved in what Moses brought and believed in Jesus then they increased in disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought of the Qur’an. It was said: God Almighty does not forgive any kind of disbelief, so how did He say: Indeed, those who believed then disbelieved, then believed then disbelieved and then increased in disbelief – never will God forgive them. The answer is that if the disbeliever believes, his disbelief is forgiven, but if he returns and disbelieves, he is not forgiven, and the first disbelief is not forgiven. This is as came in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Some people said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, O Messenger of God, will we be held accountable for what we did in the pre-Islamic era? He said: As for those among you who are good in Islam, they will not be held accountable for it, and those who do evil will be held accountable for their deeds in the pre-Islamic period and in Islam. In another narration: And those who do evil in Islam will be held accountable for the first and the last. The evil here means disbelief, as it is not correct to mean by it committing an evil, as it is necessary for Islam not to destroy what came before it except for those who are protected from all evils except at the time of their death, and that is invalid by consensus. The meaning of Then they increased in disbelief is they persisted in disbelief. God would not forgive them nor guide them “guide them” a path a way to Paradise. It was said: He does not single them out for success as He singles out His friends. In this verse, there is a response to the people of power, as God the Most High has made clear that He does not guide the disbelievers to a path of goodness so that the servant may know that he only attains guidance through God the Most High, and guidance is also denied by the will of God the Most High. The verse also includes the ruling on apostates, and the discussion of them has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah when God the Most High says: And whoever among you turns back from his religion and dies while he is a disbeliever (al-Baqarah 2:217)
4:138: Giving good report is informing about something that has an effect on the skin. Its explanation has been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah and the meaning of hypocrisy.
4:139: The Almighty said: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. “Those” is a description of the hypocrites. This is evidence that whoever commits a sin among the monotheists is not a hypocrite because he does not befriend the disbelievers. It includes the prohibition of befriending the disbeliever and taking helpers in the deeds related to religion. In the Sahih, “On the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that a man from the polytheists caught up with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to him: Go back, for we do not seek help from a polytheist. “Glory” means victory. He gives him victory if he defeats him. For glory belongs to God entirely. That is, victory and power belong to God. Ibn Abbas said: They seek from them meaning from Banu Finqa’, for Ibn Abi was their ally.
4:140: The Almighty’s saying: And it has been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of God, they are disbelieved in and ridiculed. The address is to all who show faith, whether they are ignorant or hypocrites, because if they show faith, then it is necessary for them to comply with the commands of the Book of God. So the revealed saying is the Almighty’s saying: And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses, then turn away from them until they engage in another conversation. (al-An’am 6:68) The hypocrites used to sit with the rabbis of the Jews and ridicule the Qur’an. Asim and Ya’qub read that it was revealed with the opening of the noon and the zay and with its emphasis because the name of God, the Majestic and Sublime, came before it in His Almighty’s saying: For indeed, all honor belongs to God. Hamid read likewise, except that he lightened the zay. The rest of them revealed without the subject being named. That if you hear the verses of God is in place of that if you hear according to the reading of Asim and Ya’qub, it is in the accusative case because the verb falls upon it. In the reading of the rest, it is in the nominative case because it is the name of something whose subject is not named. Disbelieve in it means if you hear disbelief and ridicule of the verses of God, then the hearing falls upon the verses, and what is meant is hearing. Blasphemy and mockery, as you say, I heard Abdullah being blamed, meaning I heard Abdullah being blamed. God the Almighty said: So do not sit with them until they engage in another talk meaning other than disbelief. Indeed, then you would be like them. This indicates the obligation to avoid people who commit sins if they commit an evil act, because whoever does not avoid them has accepted their actions, and acceptance of disbelief is disbelief. God the Almighty said: Indeed, then you would be like them. So whoever sits in a gathering of sin and does not denounce them will be with them in sin, and it is necessary to denounce them if they speak of sin and do it. If he is not able to denounce them, then he should get up and leave them so that he will not be among the people of this verse. It was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may God be pleased with him, that he took some people who were drinking alcohol, and it was said to him about one of those present that he was fasting, so he imposed discipline on him and recited this verse: Indeed, then you would be like them. meaning that acceptance of sin is sin, and for this reason the one who does it and the one who accepts it will be held accountable for the punishment of sins until they are all destroyed. This similarity is not in all the characteristics, but it is an obligation that resembles the apparent ruling of comparison, as he said: Every companion follows the example of the one he is compared to. It has been mentioned before, and if avoiding people who commit sins is proven, as we have explained, then avoiding people of innovations and whims is more appropriate. Al-Kalbi said: The Most High’s statement: So do not sit with them until they engage in a conversation other than that was abrogated by the Most High’s statement: And there is not upon those who fear God any account of their account (al-An’am 6:69). The majority of commentators said: It is decisive. Juwaybir narrated on the authority of Al-Dahhak, who said: This verse includes every innovator in religion until the Day of Resurrection. God the Almighty says: Indeed, God will gather the hypocrites. The original is gatherer with the tanween, but it was deleted for the sake of lightness, as it means to gather. Those who lie in wait for you means the hypocrites, that is, they wait for you to face calamities. If you have a victory from God meaning victory over the Jews and spoils, They will say, ‘Were we not with you?’ meaning, give us from the spoils. And if the disbelievers have a share meaning, triumph, They will say, ‘Did we not gain control over you?’ meaning, did we not gain control over you until the Muslims feared you and we abandoned them from you. It is said: He gained control over something meaning, he overcame it. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: The devil gained control over them (Al-Mujadilah: 19). It was said that the original istihtasad is hawt meaning he surrounded him. This verb came according to the original, and if it was made weak, it would have been alam nastadha and the verb with weak istihdaha yastahyidh, and without weak istihdaha yastahyidh, and we prevent you from the believers meaning by abandoning them from you and separating them from what they want from you. The verse indicates that the hypocrites used to go out in the raids. With the Muslims, and that is why they said: Were we not with you? This indicates that they did not give them the spoils, and that is why they asked for them and said: Were we not with you! It is possible that they meant by their saying Were we not with you to show gratitude to the Muslims, meaning that we informed you of their report and we were your supporters. There are three issues: The first - His Almighty’s saying: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers The scholars have five interpretations of it: The first - what was narrated on the authority of Yasaa’ Al-Hadrami, who said: From Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, a man said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, what do you think of God’s saying: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers How is that when they fight us and sometimes prevail over us? So Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: The meaning of that is on the Day of Resurrection, the Day of Judgment. And Ibn Abbas said the same: That is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Atiyyah said: And this is what all the people of interpretation said. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is weak, because of the lack of benefit of the report of it, and even if the beginning of the speech suggests its meaning, because God Almighty says: So God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, He delayed the judgment until the Day of Resurrection, and made the matter in this world a cycle in which the disbelievers prevail sometimes and are prevailed at other times, based on what He saw of wisdom and the previous word. Then He said: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers, so whoever imagined that the end of the speech goes back to its beginning, and that nullifies its benefit since it is repetition. Second: God will not give them a way to wipe out the state of the believers, erase their traces, and make their property permissible, as stated in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Thawban, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: And I asked my Lord not to destroy them with a general famine and not to send over them an enemy from other than themselves who would violate their honor. And my Lord said, “O Muhammad, when I have decreed a decree, it cannot be rejected. And I have given you a command for your nation that I will not destroy them with a general famine and not send over them an enemy from other than themselves who would violate their honor even if all their regions were to unite against him, until some of them would destroy others and some of them would take others captive.” Third: God Almighty does not give the unbelievers any way to prevail over the believers except that they enjoin falsehood and do not forbid evil, and they delay repentance, so the enemy’s control comes from them, as God Almighty said: And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned (al-Shura 42:30). Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is very valuable. I said: And what is indicated by his saying, peace be upon him, in the hadith of Thawban, until some of them destroy others and take others captive, is that until is an end, and the apparent meaning of the statement requires that their enemy will not be empowered over them and take them captive unless they destroy others and take others captive. And this has been found in these times with the tribulations that have occurred among the Muslims, so the power of the infidels has grown strong and they have taken control of the lands of the Muslims until nothing remains of Islam except a few, so we ask God to help us with His forgiveness, victory, and kindness. Fourth - God Almighty does not give the unbelievers a legitimate way over the believers. If there is one, it is contrary to the law. Fifth: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers. That is, any rational or legal argument that they can use to prove it, except that it is invalidated and refuted. The second - Ibn al-Arabi: Our scholars have taken this verse as evidence that the infidel does not own the Muslim slave, and Ashhab and al-Shafi’i said the same: Because God Almighty denied the infidel the right to own him, and ownership by purchase is a right, so it is not legislated for him nor is it concluded by that. Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik, and it is the saying of Abu Hanifa: The meaning of And God will never give the disbelievers a right over the believers is in the permanence of ownership, because we find that the beginning is for him over him, and that is by inheritance, and its form is that a disbelieving slave is converted into the hand of a disbeliever, so it is necessary to rule on him by selling him, and before the ruling on his sale, he dies, so the Muslim slave inherits from the infidel’s heir, so this is a right that has been established by force, not intention, and that ownership by purchase has been established by the intention of intent, so the disbeliever wanted to own him by his choice, so if he ruled on the contract of his sale and the establishment of his ownership, then his intention has been fulfilled in it and he has been given a right over him. Abu Omar said: The Muslims have agreed that the emancipation of a Muslim slave by a Christian or a Jew is valid and binding on him. They have also agreed that if a disbeliever’s slave converts to Islam and is sold to him, his price is paid to him. This indicates that he is selling his property and emancipation is established for him based on his property, except that there is no unstable ownership because selling it is obligatory on him. And God knows best, because God Almighty says: And God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers. He means enslavement, ownership, and servitude, a stable, permanent ownership. Scholars differed regarding the purchase of a Muslim slave by an infidel slave, with two opinions: One of them is that the sale is void, and the second is that the sale is valid and permissible for the buyer. Third - The scholars also differed on this matter regarding a Christian man who arranged for a Christian slave to convert to Islam. Malik and Al-Shafi’i said in one of his two opinions: He should be separated from the slave and he should be released to his Christian master and he should not be sold to him until his situation is clear. If the Christian dies and he owes a debt, his debt should be paid by the freed slave unless he has enough money to support the freed slave, in which case he should be freed. Al-Shafi’i said in the other opinion: He should be sold to him as soon as he converts to Islam. Al-Muzani chose this, because the freed slave is a testament and it is not permissible to leave a Muslim in the possession of a polytheist who humiliates him and converts him, and he has become an enemy to him through Islam. Al-Layth ibn Sa’d said: A Christian should be sold to a Muslim who frees him and his loyalty goes to the one who bought and freed him and his price should be paid to the Christian. Sufyan and the Kufians said: If the freed slave of a Christian converts to Islam, his value should be assessed and he should work to find his value. If the Christian dies before the freed slave finishes working, the slave should be freed and the work is void.
4:141: God Almighty says: “Those who lie in wait for you - if you have a victory from God, they say, ‘Were we not with you?’ But if the disbelievers have a share, they say, ‘Did we not gain control over you and protect you from the believers?’ So God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and God will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers.”
4:142: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, the hypocrites seek to deceive God, but it is He who deceives them. The meaning of deception and trickery from God has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, as a punishment for their deception of His friends and messengers. Al-Hasan said: Every person, believer and hypocrite, will be given a light on the Day of Resurrection, and the hypocrites will rejoice and think that they have been saved. Then, when they come to the path, the light of every hypocrite will be extinguished. That is what they say: Wait for us so that we may borrow from your light. (al-Hadid 57:13) The Almighty says: And when they stand for prayer, they stand with laziness. That is, they pray out of show, while they are lazy and sluggish, not hoping for a reward, nor believing that there will be consequences for abandoning it. In the Sahih hadith: The most burdensome prayers for the hypocrites are the evening and morning prayers. For the evening comes when they are tired from the work of the day, and it becomes difficult for them to get up for it. But the morning prayer comes when sleep is more beloved to them than joy, and if they were to draw their swords, they would not get up. Hypocrisy: showing off beauty so that people can see it, not to follow God’s command. Its explanation has been presented above. Then he described them as having little remembrance when showing off and when fearful. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, criticizing those who delay prayer: This is the prayer of the hypocrites, three times. One of them sits watching the sun until it is between the horns of Satan or on the horns of Satan. He then stands up and performs four rak’ahs in which he does not mention God except a little. Narrated by Malik and others. It was said that he described them as having little remembrance because they did not mention God by reading or glorifying Him, but rather they mentioned Him by saying Allahu Akbar. It was also said that he described them as having little remembrance because God Almighty does not accept it. It was also said that it is due to the lack of sincerity in it. Here are two issues: First - God Almighty mentioned in this verse the prayer of the hypocrites, and His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned them. So whoever prays as they pray and remembers as they remember will join them in not being accepted, and will be excluded from the requirement of God Almighty’s saying: “Indeed, the believers will succeed. Those who are humble in their prayers.” (al-Mu’minun 23:1-2) And God will come, unless he has an excuse, in which case he should limit himself to a loan, according to what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did to the Bedouin when he saw him neglecting the prayer, so he said to him: “When you stand up for prayer, then complete your prayer, then face the qiblah and say Allahu Akbar, then recite whatever you can of the Qur’an, then bow until you are at ease in bowing, then rise until you are standing straight, then prostrate until you are at ease in prostration, then rise until you are at ease in sitting, then do that throughout the prayer.” Narrated by the imams. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no prayer for one who does not recite the Mother of the Qur’an. He said: A prayer is not valid in which a man does not straighten his back in bowing and prostration. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: A good and authentic hadith. The scholars among the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who came after them acted upon this view. They believe that a man should straighten his back in bowing and prostration. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and Ishaq said: Whoever does not straighten his back in bowing and prostration, his prayer is invalid, because of the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: A prayer is not valid in which a man does not straighten his back in bowing and prostration. Ibn al-Arabi said: Ibn al-Qasim and Abu Hanifah held that tranquility is not obligatory, and it is an Iraqi narration that none of the Malikis should concern themselves with. This meaning has already been mentioned in al-Baqarah. Second - Ibn al-Arabi said: If someone prays a prayer so that people can see him and they will testify to his faith, or he wants to seek status and appear in order to accept testimony and be permitted to lead the prayer, then this is not the ostentation that is forbidden and there is no blame upon him. Rather, the ostentation of sin is to show it off as prey for people and a way to eat, so this is an intention that is not sufficient and he must repeat it. I said: His saying, “And he wanted to seek status and prominence in order to accept the testimony,” is a matter of contemplation, and its explanation has been presented in An-Nisa’, so reflect on it here. This verse indicates that showing off is included in both obligatory and voluntary prayers, because God Almighty said: And when they stand for prayer, they stand. So it is general. Some people said: It only includes voluntary prayers in particular, because obligatory prayers are obligatory on all people, and voluntary prayers are subject to that. And it was said the opposite, because if he did not perform voluntary prayers, he would not be held accountable for them.
4:143: The oscillating: the one who hesitates between two things. Oscillation is disturbance. It is said: I oscillated him and he oscillated. From this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: Or do you see that God has given you a surah that makes every king waver before it? last: Fantasy for Umm Al-Salsabil, and beyond it is a month’s journey for the wavering mail Thus it was narrated with a kasra on the second dhal. Ibn Jinni said: Where is the one who is shaken and anxious who does not stand firm or take his time? These hypocrites are wavering between the believers and the polytheists, neither sincere in their faith nor openly declaring their disbelief. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Ibn Umar, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The hypocrite is like a stray sheep between two flocks, it lends itself to this one once and to that one another time. In another narration, it is “takir” instead of ta’ir. The majority of scholars read mudhdhabiyin with a damma on the meem and a fatha on the dhaaleen. Ibn Abbas read it with a kasra on the second dhaal. In the letter of Abi, it is mudhdhabiyin. Assimilation is permissible in this reading: mudhdhabiyin with the first dhaal and a kasra on the second. According to Al-Hasan, mudhdhabiyin with a fatha on the meem and the dhaaleen.
4:144: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies. Two objects, meaning do not make your close friends and confidants from them. This meaning has already been presented. Do you want to give God clear authority over you? meaning in His tormenting you by establishing His proof against you since He has forbidden you.
4:145: The Almighty’s saying: In the depths The Kufians read the depths with a sukoon on the ra’ and the first is more eloquent because it is said in the plural: adrak like camel and camels, as Al-Nahhas said. Abu Ali said: They are two languages like shama’ and shama’ and the like, and the plural is adarak. It was said: the plural of the depths is adarak like fals and aflas. The fire has seven levels, meaning levels and stations, except that the Arabs use for everything that is low, it is adarak. And when it is high, it is a staircase, so Paradise has a staircase and the fire has adarak. This has been mentioned before. So the hypocrite is in the lowest level, which is the abyss, due to the severity of his disbelief and the abundance of his calamities and his ability to harm the believers. The highest levels are Jahannam, then Laza, then Al-Hutama, then Al-Sa’ir, then Saqar Al-Jahim, then Al-Hayyah. All of them may be called by the name of the first level. May God protect us from its punishment by His grace and generosity. And from Ibn Mas’ud in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: In the lowest level of the Fire he said: coffins: of iron, locked in the fire, locked on them. And Ibn Umar said: Indeed, The three most severe torments in Hell on the Day of Resurrection are: the hypocrites, those who disbelieved among the people of the table, and the people of Pharaoh. This is confirmed in the Book of God Almighty. God Almighty said: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire. And God Almighty said about the people of the table: Then I will punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone in the worlds. (al-Ma’idah 5:115) And He said about the people of Pharaoh: Enter the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment. (Ghafir 40:46)
4:146: An exception for those who are hypocrites, and one of the conditions for someone who repents from hypocrisy is that he should reform his words and actions, and hold fast to God, that is He made it a refuge and a sanctuary and he purifies his religion for God as stated in this verse, otherwise he is not repentant, and for this reason he caused the reward of the believers to fall into procrastination because the hypocrites joined them, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Al-Aswad who said: We were in Abdullah’s circle when he came and stood over us, greeted us, and said: Hypocrisy has descended upon people better than you. Al-Aswad said: Glory be to God, God the Most High says: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire. Abdullah smiled and Hudhayfah sat in a corner of the mosque. Abdullah said: His companions dispersed and he threw pebbles at me, so I came to him. Hudhayfah said: I was amazed at his laughter, for he knew what I had said: Hypocrisy has descended upon people who were better than you, then they repented, so God accepted their repentance. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of those are with the believers is among the believers. Al-Qutbi said: He turned away from their speech out of anger at them, so he said: those are with the believers, and he did not say: They are the believers. The ya was deleted from yu’ta in writing, as it was deleted in pronunciation, because it was still and the lam after it was still. Similar to it is The Day when the crier calls out (Qaf: 41), We will call the guards (al-Alaq 96:18), and The Day when the caller calls out (al-Qamar 54:6). The waw was deleted because of the meeting of two still letters.
4:147: An interrogative meaning to report to the hypocrites the estimation of any benefit for Him in your punishment if you are grateful and believe, so the Almighty pointed out that He does not punish the grateful believer and that His punishment of His servants does not increase His kingdom and His leaving them punished for their actions does not decrease His authority. Makhul said: Four things that are for Him are for Him and three things that are for Him are against Him. The four that are for Him are: gratitude, faith, supplication and seeking forgiveness. God the Almighty said: What would God do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And God the Almighty said: And God would not punish them while you are among them, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness. (al-Anfal 8:33) And God the Almighty said: Say, ‘My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication.’ (al-Furqan 25:77) As for the three that are against Him: evil, transgression and breaking the oath. God the Almighty said: So whoever breaks his oath, he breaks it only to the detriment of himself. (al-Fath 48:10) And God the Almighty said: And the evil plan does not encompass except its own people. (Fatir 35:10) 43] And the Almighty said: Your aggression is only against yourselves (Yunus 10:23) And God is ever Appreciative and Knowing meaning He thanks His servants for their obedience to Him. The meaning of thanks is that He rewards them, so He accepts the little work and gives a great reward for it. This is gratitude from Him for His worship. Gratitude in the language means manifestation. It is said: a grateful animal if it shows more fat than it is given in fodder. This meaning has been presented in full. The Arabs say in the proverb more grateful than a lightning bolt because it is said: it turns green and fresh in the shade of the clouds without rain. And God knows best.
4:148: There are three issues: The first - His Most High’s saying: God does not like that evil should be uttered aloud. The speech was completed, then He, the Majestic and Almighty, said: Except for him who has been wronged. An exception not from the first in the accusative case, meaning, but for him who has been wronged, he may say, So-and-so has wronged me. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case and the meaning would be: God does not like that anyone should utter evil aloud except for him who has been wronged. The majority read Zulam with a damma on the dhal and a kasra on the lam, and it is permissible to make it sukoon. And for him who read Zulam with a fatha on the dhal, The letter Dhad and the opening of the letter Lam, which is Zaid bin Aslam, Ibn Abi Ishaq and others, as follows, so it is not permissible for him to make the letter Lam silent because of the lightness of the opening. According to the first reading, a group said: The meaning is that God does not like anyone to speak ill of the one who has been wronged, so it is not disliked for him to speak ill of the one who has been wronged. Then they differed about how to speak ill of the one who has been wronged and what is permissible of that. Al-Hasan said: It is a man who wrongs another man, so he should not supplicate against him, but he should say: O God, help him against him. O God, extract my right. O God, come between him and what he wants of my wrong. This is the supplication of defense, and it is the least degree of evil. Ibn Abbas and others said: What is permissible for the one who has been wronged is to supplicate against the one who has wronged him, and if he is patient, it is better for him. This is a generalization in the type of supplication against the wrongdoer. He and Al-Suddi also said: There is no problem for the one who has been wronged to seek revenge against the one who has wronged him with the same injustice and speak ill of the one who has been wronged. Ibn Al-Mustanabir said: Except for the one who has been wronged means: Except for the one who is forced to speak ill of the one who has disbelieved or something similar, so that is permissible. The verse according to this is about compulsion. Qatrib said the same: Except for the one who has been wronged means the one who is forced because he is wronged, so that is dropped from him. If he disbelieves, he said: It is permissible for the meaning to be Except for the one who has been wronged as a substitute, as if it were He said: God does not love anyone except the one who has been wronged, meaning He does not love the wrongdoer, so it is as if he is saying: He loves the one who has been wronged, meaning with the reward of the one who has been wronged. The meaning of this statement is: God does not love the one who speaks ill of others except the one who has been wronged, in exchange. Mujahid said: It was revealed regarding hospitality, so he permitted him to speak ill of others. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid: It was revealed regarding a man who hosted a man in a deserted area, but he did not host him, so it was revealed, Except for the one who has been wronged. Ibn Abi Nujayh also narrated it on the authority of Mujahid: He said: This verse, God does not love the public mention of evil except for the one who has been wronged, was revealed regarding a man who passes by a man and does not host him, so He permitted him to say about him: He did not treat him well as a guest. Those who made hospitality obligatory used this verse as evidence. They said: Because injustice is forbidden, so it indicates its obligation. This is the statement of Al-Layth bin Sa’d and the majority, that it is one of the noble morals, and its explanation will come in Hud. What is required by the apparent meaning of the verse is that the wronged person may seek revenge against his oppressor, but with moderation - if he is a believer, as Al-Hasan said: As for responding to slander with slander and the like. No, and it was mentioned in Al-Baqarah. If he is an unbeliever, then send for your people and call for whatever destruction you wish and for every call, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did when he said: O God, intensify your punishment on Mudar and make it a year for them like the years of Joseph.” He said: O God, punish so-and-so and so-and-so, he named them, and if he openly commits injustice, he will pray against him openly and will not spare him a respectable honor, nor a respectable body, nor a respectable wealth. Abu Dawud narrated: On the authority of Aisha, she said: Something of hers was stolen, so she began to pray against it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not pray against him. Do not lighten the punishment for him by praying against him. It was also narrated on the authority of Amr ibn al-Sharid on the authority of Anbih, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If someone is wronged, his honor and punishment are made permissible. Ibn Al-Mubarak said: His honor is made permissible, he is treated harshly, and his punishment is imprisoned. In Sahih Muslim: Delaying payment by a wealthy person is injustice. So if a wealthy person is asked to pay and delays payment, he is being unjust. This makes it permissible for him to say about him: He should not delay payment by people and withhold their rights. This makes it permissible for the imam to discipline and punish him until he stops doing that. Its meaning was narrated on the authority of Sufyan, and it is the meaning of what Ibn al-Mubarak said, may God be pleased with them both. The second - and it is not from this chapter with what occurred in Sahih Muslim from the saying of Al-Abbas about Ali, may God be pleased with them, in the presence of Omar, Othman, Al-Zubayr and Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf: O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this lying, sinful, treacherous, traitorous hadith and not one of them responded to him because it was a government that each one of them believed for himself, until Omar implemented what was obligatory upon them. Ibn Al-Arabi said and our scholars said: This only happens when the positions are equal or close. However, if they are different, then the mob will not be able to overpower the virtuous, but rather it will demand its right by merely claiming without expressing injustice or anger. This is correct and the reports indicate this. The other aspect is that this saying was taken out of Al-Abbas by anger and his reaching the authority of his paternal uncles, because the paternal uncle is like the father, and there is no doubt that if the father uses these words to address his son, this is only taken from him to mean that he intended to be harsh and deter him, exaggerating in disciplining him, not that he is described by those matters. Then it was added to this that they were in a dispute over religious authority, so Al-Abbas believed that opposing him in it is not permissible, and that opposing him in it leads to the opponent being described by those matters, so he used them with the beginnings of Anger at these aspects, and when those present knew that, they did not deny it. Al-Mazari, Judge Iyad, and others pointed to this. Third: As for the one who reads Zulam with a fat-ha on the Dhad and the Lam - which is the reading of Zaid bin Aslam, and he was one of the scholars of the Qur’an in Madinah after Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, and the reading of Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and Ata’ bin As-Sa’ib, the meaning is, except for the one who wronged in action or speech, then speak to him openly with evil speech in the sense of forbidding his action, rebuking him, and responding to him. The meaning is that God does not like it to be said to the one who repents from hypocrisy: Didn’t you become a hypocrite? except for the one who wronged, meaning he persisted in hypocrisy. This is indicated by the statement of God the Most High: Except for those who repent (An-Nisa’: 146, al-Baqarah 2:160). Ibn Zaid said: This is because when God the Most High informed us about the hypocrites that they will be in the lowest level of Hell, this was a public display of evil speech, then He said to them after that: What would God do with your punishment? (An-Nisa’: 147) in the sense of comfort and calling to gratitude and faith, then He said the believers. God does not like that evil be said aloud except by someone who has been wronged in his persistence in hypocrisy. Then it will be said to him: Are you not the disbelieving hypocrite for whom in the Hereafter you will have the lowest level of Hell? And similar statements. Some people said: The meaning of the statement is: God does not like that anyone should speak aloud of evil. Then He made an exception in a disconnected way: that is, but by someone who has been wronged, he speaks aloud of evil out of injustice and aggression, and he is unjust in that. I said: This is the way of many oppressors and their habit, for in addition to their oppression, they use their tongues to attack the honor of their oppressed in a way that is forbidden to them. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that the meaning is except for the one who oppresses and says something bad, for you should take him by the hand, and the exception is not from the first. I said: This is indicated by hadiths, including his saying, peace be upon him: Take your fools by the hand, he said. Support your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. They said: We support him if he is oppressed, but how can we support him if he is an oppressor? He said: To prevent him from oppression. Al-Farra’ said: To the one who oppresses, meaning not to the one who oppresses. God Almighty says: And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing. This is a warning to the oppressor so that he does not oppress and to the oppressed so that he does not exceed the limit in taking revenge.
4:149: Then he followed this with his saying: Whether you disclose good or conceal it or pardon an offense, so he encouraged forgiveness and encouraged it, and forgiveness is an attribute of God Almighty with the ability to take revenge. The virtue of those who pardon people has already been mentioned in Al Imran, so in these simple words there are many meanings for whoever ponders them. It was said that if you pardon, then God will pardon you. Ibn Al Mubarak narrated that he heard someone who heard Al Hassan say: When the nations kneel before the Lord of the Worlds on the Day of Resurrection, it will be called out to those whose reward is with God to stand, and no one will stand except those who pardoned in this world. This hadith is confirmed by the words of God Almighty: But whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with God. (al-Shura 42:40)
4:150: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who disbelieve When He mentioned the polytheists and hypocrites, He mentioned the disbelievers from the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians, because they disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and He explained that disbelief in him is disbelief in all of them, because there is no prophet who did not command his people to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in all of the prophets, may God bless them and grant them peace. The meaning of and they want to differentiate between God and His messengers is between belief in God and His messengers. So the Almighty stated that differentiating between God and His messengers is disbelief, and it was only disbelief because God, may He be glorified, imposed on people that they worship Him according to what He legislated for them through the tongues of the messengers. So if they denied the messengers, they rejected their laws and did not accept them from them, and so they refused to adhere to the servitude that they were commanded to adhere to, so it was like denying the Creator, may He be glorified, and denying the Creator is disbelief because it entails abandoning the obligation of obedience and servitude. Likewise, differentiating between His messengers in belief in them is disbelief, and it is… The second issue - because God Almighty said: And they say, ‘We believe in some and disbelieve in others.’ They are the Jews who believed in Moses and disbelieved in Jesus and Muhammad. This was mentioned previously in their statement in Surat Al-Baqarah. They say to their common people, We do not find mention of Muhammad in our books. “And they want to take a path in between.” That is, they want to take a path between belief and disbelief, that is, an innovated religion between Islam and Judaism. He said: That, and he did not say those two, because that applies to both, and if it were those two it would be permissible.
4:151: Third - The Almighty’s saying: Those are the disbelievers, truly is an emphasis that removes the illusion of their faith when He described them as saying, We believe in some, and that this does not benefit them if they disbelieve in His Messenger, and if they disbelieve in His Messenger, they disbelieve in Him, the Almighty, and they disbelieve in every Messenger who gave good tidings of that Messenger, so they became the disbelievers, truly, and for the disbelievers takes the place of the second object of We have prepared, meaning We have prepared for all their types a humiliating punishment, meaning humiliating.
4:152: He means the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation.
4:153: The Jews asked Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ascend to the heavens while they see him, and to bring down to them a written book in what he claims to be true, all at once, just as Moses brought the Torah out of his stubbornness toward him, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God Almighty informed them that their fathers had stubbornly oppressed Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace, with something greater than this. They said, ‘Show us God openly.’ That is, clearly, and this has been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. Clearly is an adjective for an omitted source, that is, seeing clearly, so they were punished with a thunderbolt because of the enormity of what they had brought of questioning and injustice after what they had seen of miracles. The Almighty said: Then they took the calf. There is an omission in the speech, the meaning of which is: So We revived them, but they did not leave, so they took the calf. This has been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah, and it will be mentioned in Taha, God willing: After the clear proofs had come to them, meaning the evidence, indications, and apparent miracles such as the hand, the staff, the splitting of the sea, and other things, that there is no god but God Almighty. So We pardoned that, meaning what they had been stubborn about. And We gave Moses a clear authority, meaning a clear argument, and these are the signs that he brought, and they were called an authority because the one who brought them is a conqueror with the argument, and they conquer the hearts, in that you know that it is not within the power of human beings to bring something like them.
4:154: The Almighty said: And We raised the Mount above them because of their covenant meaning because of their breaking the covenant that was taken from them, which is to act according to what is in the Torah. The raising of the mountain and their entering the gate have already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Prostrating is in the accusative case as a state, and Warsh read it alone. And We said to them, Do not transgress on the Sabbath with the opening of the 'ayn from 'ada ya'du 'addu 'adwan 'adwan wa 'adwan wa 'adwan, meaning by hunting down whales, as mentioned in Al-Baqarah. The original form of it is ta'tadawwa. The ta' was assimilated into the dal. An-Nahhas said: It is not permissible to make the 'ayn quiescent, lest it be connected to combining two quiescents in this. The one who reads it only seeks error. And We took from them a firm covenant meaning the covenant that was taken from them in the Torah. It was said: A covenant confirmed by an oath, so it was called firm for that reason.
4:155: The Almighty’s saying: So because they broke their covenant So because they broke it is in the genitive case with the preposition ba and ma is an additional emphasis like His saying: So because of the mercy of God (Al Imran 3:159) and it has been mentioned before and the preposition is related to something omitted, the meaning is: So because of their breaking their covenant, We cursed them, according to Qatada and others, and this was omitted because the listener knew.
