Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Hamza al-Kisa’i said: It is related to what preceded it, and the meaning is: So the thunderbolt seized them because of their injustice until His saying: So because of their breaking their covenant He said: So he explained their injustice for which the thunderbolt seized them with what came after it from their breaking the covenant and killing the prophets and all the other things that were mentioned in which they wronged themselves, and al-Tabari and others denied that because those who were seized by the thunderbolt were during the time of Moses and those who killed the prophets and accused Mary of slander were after Moses by a time, so the thunderbolt did not seize those who were seized by their accusation. Al-Mahdawi and others said: This is not necessary because it is permissible to inform On their authority, and what is meant is their fathers, as mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, So because of their breaking their covenant, We forbade them good things that had been made lawful for them. Because this story extends to His statement, Then because of the wrongdoing of those who are Jews, We forbade them (An-Nisa’: 160), and their breaking the covenant is that they were ordered to explain the description of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: The meaning is, So because of their breaking their covenant and their doing such and such, God sealed their hearts. It was said: The meaning is, So because of their breaking, they will not believe except a few. The fa is inserted. And their disbelief is a conjunction, as is and their killing. What is meant by the verses of God is their books that they distorted. Ghalaf is the plural of ghalaf, meaning our hearts are vessels for knowledge, so we have no need for knowledge other than what we have. It was said: It is the plural of aghlaf, which is the one covered by the ghalaf, meaning our hearts are in coverings, so there is no need for what you say, and it is like His statement, Our hearts are in coverings (Fussilat 41:5). This was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah, and their purpose with this was to ward off the argument of the messengers. And the nature is the seal, and it was mentioned in the cow for their disbelief meaning as a punishment for their disbelief, as He said: Rather, God has cursed them for their disbelief, so little do they believe (al-Baqarah 2:88) meaning except a little faith, meaning in some of the prophets, and that is of no benefit to them. Then He repeated for their disbelief to inform that they disbelieved after disbelief. And it was said: The meaning is for their disbelief in the Messiah, so it was deleted because what follows it indicates it, and the factor in for their disbelief is the factor in for their refutation because it is conjoined with it, and it is not permissible for the scholar to have a nature in him, and the great slander is her accusation of Joseph the carpenter, and he was one of the righteous among them, and slander is the excessive lie that is astonished by, and it was mentioned previously, and God Almighty knows best.
4:156: God Almighty says: And because of their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander.
4:157: The Almighty said: And their saying, 'We have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary.' The word in was broken because it is a subject after the word saying. The opening of it is a language. It was previously mentioned in Al Imran that the word messiah was derived as a substitute for if you wish with the meaning of I mean. "And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him. It was rejected for their saying, But it was made to appear to them," meaning that it was made to appear to someone else, as previously mentioned in Al Imran. It was also said that they did not know his person and killed the one they killed while they were doubting him, as the Almighty said: "And those who differed about him are in doubt about it." The reports said that it was from all of them. It was also said that only their common people differed about him. The meaning of their difference was that some of them said that he was a god and some of them that he was the son of God. Al-Hasan said: It was also said that their difference was that their common people said that we killed Jesus, and those who witnessed his ascension to heaven said that we did not kill him. It was also said that their difference was that the Nestorians among the Christians said that Jesus was crucified in relation to his humanity, not in relation to his divinity. The Angelicists said that the crucifixion and killing occurred to the Messiah in his complete humanity and divinity. It was said: Their difference is that they said: If this is our companion, then where is Jesus? And if this is Jesus, then where is our companion? And it was said that their difference is that the Jews said: We killed him because the Jews are the head of the Jews and he is the one who sought to kill him. And a group of Christians said: Rather, we killed him. And a group of them said: Rather, God raised him to the heavens and we were looking at him. They have no knowledge of it is an extra word, and the speech was completed. Then the Almighty said: Except the following of conjecture. An exception not from the first in the accusative case, and it is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a substitute, meaning they have no knowledge of it except the following of conjecture. Sibawayh recited: A town with no companions except the camels and the wild donkeys God the Almighty said: And they did not kill him for certain. Ibn Abbas and As-Suddi said: The meaning is they did not kill them, they thought it was certain, like you say I killed him with certainty, if you knew him with complete knowledge, so the ha’ refers back to the thought. Abu Ubaid said: If the meaning was And they did not kill Jesus for certain, he would have said: And they did not kill him for certain. It was said: The meaning is And they did not kill the one who appeared to them to be Jesus for certain, so the pause on this is for certain. It was said: The meaning is And they did not kill Jesus, and the pause is And they did not kill him, and for certain is an adjective for a deleted source, and there are two interpretations for it: one of them is that they said this with certainty, or God said a certain word. The other interpretation is that the meaning is that they did not know him with certain knowledge. An-Nahhas said: If you interpret the meaning as rather God raised him to Him for certain, then it is a mistake because it does not work with what comes after it, but rather with what comes before it due to its weakness. Ibn Al-Anbari permitted the pause on and they did not kill him so that it would be made accusative with an implied verb that is the answer to the oath, the interpretation being: And you certainly believed them for certain, meaning they believed for certain.
4:158: Rather, God raised him up to Himself is the beginning of a new statement: that is, to the heavens, and God Almighty is above place. The manner of raising him up has already been mentioned in Al Imran. And God was Exalted in Might that is, Strong in taking revenge on the Jews, so He sent Peter, son of Astisanos the Roman, against him, and he killed them in a terrible manner. And Wise He ruled over them with a curse and wrath.
4:159: The Almighty said: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Ikrimah said: The meaning is that he will surely believe in the Messiah before his death, meaning the People of the Book. The first ha refers to Jesus, and the second to the People of the Book. This is because there is no one from the People of the Book, the Jews, and the Christians who will not believe in Jesus, peace be upon him, if he sees the angel, but it is a belief that is of no benefit, because it is a belief at a time of despair and when facing the state of death. The Jew acknowledges at that time that he is the Messenger of God, and the Christian acknowledges that he was the Messenger of God. It was narrated that Al-Hajjaj asked Shahr bin Hawshab about this verse, and he said: I am brought a prisoner from the Jews and Christians, and he orders that his neck be struck, and I look at him at that time and I do not see faith in him. Shahr bin Hawshab said to him: When he sees the matter of the Hereafter, he acknowledges that Jesus is the servant and Messenger of God, so he believes in him, but it does not benefit him. Al-Hajjaj said to him: Where did you get this from? He said: I took it from Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, so al-Hajjaj said to him: I took it from his pure mind. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: There is no one from the People of the Book who does not believe in Jesus before his death. So it was said to him: If he drowns, burns, or is eaten by a wild beast, will he believe in Jesus? He said: Yes! It was said: Both ha’s are for Jesus, peace be upon him, and the meaning is that whoever is alive when he descends on the Day of Resurrection will believe in him. This was said by Qatada, Ibn Zayd, and others, and it was chosen by al-Tabari. Yazid ibn Zurai’ narrated on the authority of a man on the authority of al-Hasan regarding the Almighty’s statement, And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death, he said: Before the death of Jesus. By God, he is alive with God now, but when he descends, they will all believe in him. Something similar was narrated by al-Dahhak and Say’id ibn Jubayr: It was said: He will surely believe in him, meaning in Muhammad, peace be upon him, even if it was not permissible for him to mention it because these stories were revealed to him, and the intended meaning is belief in him, and belief in Jesus is also belief in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, since it is permissible to differentiate between them. It was said: He will surely believe in him, meaning in God Almighty before he dies, and belief will not benefit him when he sees it. The first two interpretations are more apparent. Al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: “Then Abu Hurairah said: And read if you wish: ‘And there is none from the People of the Scripture but will believe in him before his death.’” Abu Hurairah said: Before his death, Jesus repeats it three times. The verse is understood by Sibawayh as: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but will believe in him. The Kufians understand it as: And there is none from the People of the Scripture but will believe in him. There is something ugly in this, because the relative pronoun is omitted, and the relative clause is part of the relative pronoun, so it is as if some of the noun was omitted.
4:160: There are two issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: Then because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a substitute for because of their breaking of the covenant. And the good things are what is stated in the Almighty’s saying: And as for those who were Jews, We have forbidden every animal having claws. (Al-An`am: 146) He mentioned wrongdoing before prohibition because it is the purpose that was intended to inform about it as the reason for the prohibition. And because of their averting [people] from the way of God, meaning because they averted themselves and others from following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
4:161: : And their taking of usury, although they were forbidden from it, and their consuming people's wealth unjustly. All of this is an explanation of the injustice they committed, as well as what preceded it of their breaking the covenant and what came after it. It was mentioned in Al Imran that the scholars differed regarding the reason for the prohibition into three opinions, this is one of them. Second - Ibn al-Arabi said: There is no disagreement in the Maliki school that the infidels are addressed, and God has made clear in this verse that they have been forbidden from usury and consuming wealth unjustly. If that is report of what was revealed to Muhammad in the Qur’an and that they were included in the address, then that is fine and good. If it is report of what God revealed to Moses in the Torah, and that they changed, distorted, disobeyed and contradicted, then is it permissible for us to deal with them when the people have corrupted their wealth in their religion or not? So a group thought that dealing with them is not permissible, because of this corruption in their wealth. The correct view is that it is permissible to deal with them despite their usury and to venture into what God the Almighty has forbidden them, as there is conclusive evidence for that in the Qur’an and Sunnah. God the Almighty said: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you (al-Ma’idah 5:5). This is explicit, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, dealt with the Jews. He died and his armor was mortgaged to a Jew for barley that he took for his family. The decisive factor in the disease of doubt and disagreement is the agreement of the nation on the permissibility of trade with the people of war. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, traveled to them as a merchant, and his travel is a decisive matter on the permissibility of traveling to them and trading with them. If it is said: This was before the prophethood, we say: He was not defiled before the prophethood by anything forbidden, and this was proven by continuous chain of transmission, nor was he excused for it when he was sent, nor was he prevented from it when he was prophesied, nor was any of the companions in his lifetime, nor any of the Muslims after his death, for they used to travel to free prisoners, and that is obligatory, and in peace, as Uthman and others were sent, and it may be obligatory or recommended. As for traveling to them merely for trade, it is permissible.
4:162: The Almighty said: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them He excluded the People of the Book, because the Jews denied it and said: These things were originally forbidden and you permit them and they were not forbidden by their injustice, so it was revealed, But those firmly rooted in knowledge and the firm is the one who is deeply rooted in the knowledge of the Book and is steadfast in it, and firmness is the establishment and it was mentioned in Al Imran and what is meant is Abdullah bin Salam and Kaab Al Ahbar and their peers and the believers meaning from the Muhajireen and Ansar, the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace and those who establish prayer and Al Hassan and Malik bin Dinar and a group read: and those who establish prayer as a conjunction and this is also the case in Abdullah's letter, as for the letter Abi, it is in it and those who establish prayer as in the copies of the Qur'an and there are six opinions differed in its accusative case, the most correct of which is the opinion of Sibawayh that it is accusative of the praise, meaning I mean the residents. Sibawayh said: This is a chapter on what is accusative for glorification and from that and those who establish prayer and he recited: Every nation obeyed the command of their master except Namir, who obeyed the command of her seducer. It is narrated about their guide: Those who depart, but they have not yet departed, and those who say to whoever has knowledge, We will abandon it. And he recited: Do not distance my people, who are the poison of the enemy and the scourge of the islands. Those who enter every arena and are good at the knots of the blue Al-Nahhas said: This is the most correct of what has been said about the residents. Al-Kisa’i said: The residents are connected to what Al-Nahhas said. Al-Akhfash said: This is far-fetched, because the meaning is: And they believe in the residents. Muhammad ibn Jarir narrated that it was said to him: “The residents here are the angels, peace be upon them, because of their constant prayer, glorification, and seeking forgiveness.” He chose this statement, and he narrated that the accusative case of praise is far-fetched, because the praise only comes after the completion of the report, and the report of the firmly rooted in those is: We will give them a great reward. So the residents is not accusative case of praise. Al-Nahhas said: The doctrine of Sibawayh in his statement: And the die is to raise it as a subject. Another said: It is raised with an implied subject, meaning they are the ones who give zakat. It was said: And the residents are in apposition to the kaf in those. It was said: It is in apposition to the ha and the mim, meaning from them and from the residents. These three answers are not permissible because they contain an apparent apposition to an implied lowered subject. The sixth answer is what was narrated that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, was asked about this verse and about His statement: Indeed, these two are magicians (Ta-Ha 20:63) and His statement: And the Sabians (al-Ma’idah 5:69) in Al-Ma’idah. She said to the questioner: O son of my brother, the scribes made a mistake. Aban Uthman said: The scribe was dictated to and he wrote, so he wrote: But those firmly rooted in knowledge among them and the believers. Then he said to him: What should I write? So he was told: Write. And those who establish prayer. Hence this happened. Al-Qushayri said: This approach is invalid because those who compiled the book were role models in language, so it should not be thought that they included in the Qur’an what was not revealed. The most correct of these statements is the statement of Sibawayh, which is the statement of Al-Khalil, and the statement of Al-Kisa’i, which is the choice of Al-Qaffal and Al-Tabari, and God knows best.
4:163: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah. This is connected to His saying: The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from the heaven. (An-Nisa’: 153) So the Almighty informed us that the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is like the matter of the prophets who came before him. Ibn Abbas said, as mentioned by Ibn Ishaq: It was revealed about a group of Jews - among them Sakin and Eid bin Zaid - who said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God has not revealed to anyone after Moses, so God denied them. Revelation is information in secret. It is said: He revealed to him the speech, Yahya, by revelation, and he revealed, by revelation, to Noah. He presented it because he was the first prophet to whom the laws were enunciated. Other than this, it was said that Az-Zubayr bin Bakkar narrated to me that Abu Al-Hasan Ali bin Al-Mughira told me on the authority of Hisham bin Muhammad bin Al-Sa’ib on the authority of his father, who said: The first prophet that God, the Blessed and Exalted, sent to the earth was Idris, and his name was Enoch. Then the messengers stopped until God sent Noah bin Lamak. Ibn Methuselah, son of Enoch, and Sam, son of Noah, was a prophet, then the messengers were cut off until God sent Abraham as a prophet and took him as a friend, and he is Abraham, son of Tarah, and Tarah’s name is Azar, then He sent Ishmael, son of Abraham, and he died in Mecca, then Isaac, son of Abraham, and he died in Syria, then Lot and his uncle Abraham, then Jacob, and he is Israel, son of Isaac, then Joseph, son of Jacob, then Shuaib, son of Job, then Hud, son of Abdullah, then Salih, son of Asf, then Moses and Aaron, son of Imran, then Job, then Al-Khidr, and he is Khadrun, then David, son of Isha, then Solomon, son of David, then Yunus, son of Matta, then Elias, then Dhul-Kifl, and his name is Uwaidna, from the tribe of Judah, son of Jacob. He said: And between Moses, son of Imran, and Mary, daughter of Imran, mother of Jesus, there were one thousand and seven hundred years, and they are not from the tribe, then Muhammad, son of Abdullah, son of Abdul Muttalib, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Zubayr said: Every prophet mentioned in the Qur’an was born to Abraham except Idris, Noah, Lot, Hud, and Salih, and he was not from the Arabs. There are only five prophets: Hud, Salih, Ishmael, Shuaib, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. They were only called Arabs because no one spoke Arabic except them. The Almighty’s saying: And the prophets after him includes all the prophets. Then He said: And We inspired Abraham so He singled out some people for mention to honor them, like the Almighty’s saying: And His angels and His messengers and Gabriel and Michael (al-Baqarah 2:98). Then He said: And Jesus and Job Jesus was mentioned before the people who came before him, because the waw does not require order. Also in it is the specification of Jesus in response to the Jews. In this verse is an indication of the status of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his honor, as He mentioned him before His prophets. Similar to it is the Almighty’s saying: And when We took from the prophets their covenant, and from you and from Noah (al-Ahzab 33:7) The verse. Noah is derived from Noah, and it was mentioned previously in Al-Imran and it was declined. It is a foreign name because it has three letters, so it was lightened. As for Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac, they are foreign and are definite, and so they are not declined. Likewise, Jacob, Jesus, and Moses, except that it is permissible for Jesus and Moses to have the alif for femininity, so they are not declined in definite or indefinite. As for Yunus, And Yusuf narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he read Wa Yunus with a kasra on the nun and likewise Yusuf making them from anas and asif, and based on this they must be declined and hamzated and both of them would be ya’anis and ya’asif. And whoever does not hamzate says: Yunus and Yusuf. Abu Zaid narrated: Yunus and Yusuf with a fatha on the nun and seen. Al-Mahdawi said: It seems that Yunus is originally a verb in the active voice and Yunus fa’li is in the passive voice for the object, so he is called by them. God the Almighty said: And We gave David the Psalms. The Psalms are the book of David and it was one hundred and fifty surahs. It does not contain rulings or what is permissible or forbidden, but rather rulings and sermons. The Psalms are writing. The Psalms mean what is written, like the messenger, riding, and milking. Hamza read Zabur with a damma on the zay, the plural of zabar, like fils and fulus, and zabar means what is written, just as it is said: this dirham is the strike of the prince, meaning it is struck. The origin of the word is documentation. It is said: a well is covered with stones, and the book is called to it by humans, jinn, birds, and wild animals because of its beautiful voice. He was humble and ate from the work of his hand. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated from Hisham bin Urwah from his father, who said: David, peace be upon him, used to address the people and he would hold a basket of palm leaves in his hand, and when he finished, he would hand it to someone next to him to sell it. He used to make shields. In the hadith: Blue eyes are Yemenite, and David was blue.
4:164: The Almighty’s saying: And messengers We have related to you before, meaning in Mecca. And messengers is in the accusative case because of an implied verb, meaning, And We sent messengers, because the meaning of And We inspired Noah is And We sent Noah. It was said: It is in the accusative case because of a verb indicated by We related to them, meaning, And We related to messengers. Similar to it is what Sibawayh recited: I no longer carry a weapon, nor do I own the camel's head if they run away I fear the wolf if I pass by it alone, and I fear the wind and the rain. And I fear the wolf. And in the letter of Abi and the messengers in the nominative case, on the assumption that among them are messengers. Then it was said: When God Almighty stated in His Book some of the names of His prophets, and did not mention the names of others, and for those who mentioned there is preference over those who did not mention, the Jews said: Muhammad mentioned the prophets and did not mention Moses, so And God spoke to Moses directly was revealed. Speaking is a source meaning emphasis, indicating the invalidity of those who say: He created for himself speech in a tree and Moses heard it. Rather, it is the real speech by which the speaker is speaking. Al-Nahhas said: The grammarians agreed that if you emphasise the verb with the source, it is not a metaphor, and that it is not permissible in the saying of the poet: The basin was full and my cotton said To say: He said a word, so when he said speaking, it must be a speech in reality from the speech that is understood. Wahb bin Munabbih said: Moses, peace be upon him, said: O Lord, why did you take me as a speaker? He asked for the work that God made him happy with so that he could do it more, so God Almighty said to him: Do you remember when a kid from your flock called out, so you followed it most of the day and it tired you out, then you took it and kissed it and hugged it to your chest and said to it, you tired me and you tired yourself, and you were not angry with it, so for that reason I took you as a speaker.
4:165: The Almighty’s saying: Messengers, bringing good tidings and warning is an accusative in apposition to Messengers, We have related their stories. It is permissible for it to be an implied verb, or it is permissible for it to be an accusative in apposition, meaning as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him Messengers “so that mankind will have no argument against God after the messengers,” and they will say, You did not send to us a messenger, and You did not send down to us a book. And in the revelation: And We never punish until We have sent a messenger. (al-Isra’ 17:15) And the Almighty’s saying: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, ‘Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could have followed Your signs?’ (Ta-Ha: 134) In all of this is clear evidence that nothing is required from the perspective of reason. It was narrated on the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar that he said: The prophets were two thousand thousand two hundred thousand. Muqatil said: The prophets were one thousand thousand four hundred thousand and one thousand twenty-four thousand. Anas bin Malik narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I was sent after eight thousand prophets, four thousand of whom were from the Children of Israel. This was mentioned by Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi in his interpretation, then he narrated on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Ishaq on the authority of al-Harith al-A’war on the authority of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, how many prophets were there and how many were messengers? He said, The prophets were one hundred thousand and twenty-four thousand prophets and the messengers were three hundred and thirteen. I said: This is the most authentic of what has been narrated on this matter. It was included by Al-Ajurri and Abu Hatim Al-Basti in his authentic document.
4:166: The Almighty said: But God bears witness The subject is raised by the beginning, and if you wish, you can double the nun and make it accusative. There is an omission in the speech that is indicated by the speech, as if the infidels said: We do not bear witness to that, O Muhammad, in what you say, so who will bear witness for you? So He revealed, But God bears witness, and the meaning of He sent it down with His knowledge is that He knows that you are worthy of sending it down to you, and the verse indicates that He, the Almighty, is All-Knowing with knowledge. And the angels bear witness He mentioned the testimony of the angels to counteract the negation of their testimony. And sufficient is God as a witness meaning sufficient is God as a witness, and the ba is redundant.
4:167: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who disbelieved meaning the Jews, that is, they were unjust, and averted from the path of God meaning from following the Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by saying: We do not find his description in our book, and prophethood is only in the children of Aaron and David, and it is in the Torah that the law of Moses is not abrogated, have gone far astray because they disbelieved and despite that they prevented people from Islam.
4:168: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged meaning the Jews, that is, they wronged Muhammad by concealing his description, and themselves when they disbelieved, and the people when they concealed it God will never forgive them this is about those who die in their disbelief and do not repent.
4:169: God Almighty says: “Except the path to Hell, wherein they will abide forever. And that, for God, is easy.”
4:170: The Almighty says: O people This is addressed to everyone The Messenger has come to you meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him with the truth with the Qur’an. It was also said: with the true religion. It was also said: with the testimony that there is no god but God. It was also said: the ba is for transitivity, meaning he came to you with the truth, so it is in the position of a state. The Almighty says: So believe, it is better for you. The speech contains an implied meaning, And do good for you. This is the doctrine of Sibawayh, and according to Al-Farra’, it is an adjective for a deleted source: meaning, a belief that is better for you. According to Abu Ubaidah, it is better for you.
4:171: The Almighty’s saying: O People of the Scripture, do not go to extremes in your religion refers to extremism. Extremism means going beyond the limit, and from this the price went to extremes, and a man went to extremes in a matter, and the flesh and bones of a girl went to extremes if she hastened her youth and exceeded her limits. What is meant by this is what the commentators mentioned, the Jews’ extremism regarding Jesus until they slandered Mary, and the Christians’ extremism regarding him until they made him a god. So, all extremism and negligence are evil and disbelief, and for this reason Mutraf ibn Abdullah said: The good is between two evils, and the poet said: Fulfill your right and do not delay, and shake hands, for no generous person has ever been fully satisfied. Do not go to extremes in anything and be moderate. Both sides of the matter are reprehensible. The other said: You should follow the middle path, for it is a means of salvation, whether you ride a tamed or a difficult path. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on his authority, peace be upon him: Do not praise me as the Christians praised Jesus, but say: He is the servant and messenger of God. The Almighty said: And do not say about God except the truth. That is, do not say that He has a partner or a son. Then the Almighty explained the state and description of Jesus, peace be upon him, saying: There are three issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: The Messiah The Messiah is raised by the beginning and Jesus is a substitute for him, and so is the son of Mary. It is possible that it is the predicate of the beginning and the meaning is: The Messiah is the son of Mary. And he indicated by his saying: Jesus, the son of Mary, that how can someone who is related to his mother be a god, and it is the right of the god to be eternal and not created, and the Messenger of God is a piece of report after a piece of report. Second: God Almighty did not mention a woman and call her by name in His Book, Mary, except for his son Imran, for He mentioned her name in about thirty places for His wisdom, which some of the sheikhs mentioned, for kings and nobles do not mention their free women in public, nor do they vulgarize their names, but rather they refer to the wife as wedding, “family,” children, and the like. If they mentioned female slaves, they did not refer to them and did not protect their names from being mentioned or explicitly stated. So when the Christians said what they said about Mary, and about her son, God explicitly mentioned her name, and did not refer to her as motherhood or servitude, which are attributes of her, and the speech proceeded according to the custom of the Arabs in mentioning their female slaves. Third: The belief that Jesus, peace be upon him, has no father is obligatory. If his name is repeated in relation to the mother, hearts sense what they must believe in terms of denying his father and exonerating the pure mother from the statement of the Jews, may God curse them. And God knows best. God Almighty says: And His Word which He cast into Mary meaning He was created by the word Be and he was a human being without a father. The Arabs call a thing by its name if it comes from it. It was said: His Word was God Almighty’s good report to Mary, peace be upon her, and His message to her through the tongue of Gabriel, peace be upon him, as in His saying: When the angels said, ‘O Mary, indeed God gives you good tidings of a word from Him’ (Al Imran 3:45). It was also said that the word here means the verse. God Almighty said: And she believed in the words of her Lord (Al Harim: 12) and The words of God have not been exhausted (Luqman 31:27). Jesus had four names: the Messiah, Jesus, Word, and Spirit. Others were said that are not in the Qur’an, and the meaning of He cast it into Mary is Mary by it. The Almighty’s saying: And a spirit from Him is what led the Christians astray, so they said: Jesus is a part of Him, so they were ignorant and went astray. There are eight answers to this: The first - Abi bin Ka’b said: God created the spirits of the sons of Adam when He took the covenant from them, then He returned them to the loins of Adam and kept with Him the spirit of Jesus, peace be upon him. Then when He turned His creation around, He sent that spirit to Mary, so Jesus, peace be upon him, was from Him. That is why He said: And a spirit from Him. It was said: This addition is for preference, even though all spirits are from His creation, like His saying: And purify My House for those who perform Tawaf (al-Hajj 22:26). It was said: The one from whom wondrous things appear may be called a spirit and attributed to God Almighty, so it is said: This is a spirit from God, meaning from His creation, just as it is said about a blessing that it is from God. Jesus healed the blind and the leper and brought the dead back to life, so he deserved this name. It was said: He is called a spirit because of the breath of Gabriel, peace be upon him, and the breath is called a spirit because it is a wind that comes out of the spirit. The poet - he is Dhu al-Rummah - said: I said to him, Raise it to you, revive it with your spirit, and buy it for her. It was reported that Gabriel blew into Mary’s armour and she became pregnant by God’s permission. Based on this, and a spirit from Him is connected to the implied word, which is the name of God in He threw her. The meaning is: God and Gabriel threw the word to Mary. It was also said: A spirit from Him, meaning He created her, as He said: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all from Him. (al-Jathiyah 45:13), meaning from His creation. It was also said: A spirit from Him, meaning a mercy from Him. So Jesus was a mercy from God to those who followed him. From this is the saying of God Almighty: And He supported them with a spirit from Him. (Al-Mujadilah: 22), meaning with mercy. It was also read: A spirit and basil (al-Waqi’ah 56:89). It was also said: A spirit from Him and a proof from Him. And Jesus was a proof and an argument against his people, may God bless him and grant him peace. God the Almighty said: So believe in God and His Messengers meaning believe that there is one God, the Creator and Sender of Christ, and believe in His Messengers, including Jesus, so do not make him a god. And do not say, ‘Our gods’ are three. Al-Zajjaj said: Ibn Abbas said: By the Trinity he means God the Almighty, His wife, and His son. Al-Farra’ and Abu Ubaid said: That is, do not say they are three, like God the Almighty’s saying: They will say, ‘Three.’ (al-Kahf 18:22) Abu Ali said: The meaning is, do not say he is the third of three, so the subject and the complement were omitted. The Christians, with their sects, are unanimous on the Trinity and say that God is one essence and has three hypostases. They make each hypostasis a god, and they mean by the hypostases existence, life, and knowledge. They may express the hypostases as the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, meaning by the Father existence, and by the Spirit life, and by the Son Christ, in their speech in which there is confusion in its explanation of the principles of religion. The result of their speech leads to adherence to the fact that Jesus is a god because of the extraordinary events that God the Almighty performed through his hands according to his motives and will. They said: We know that these matters are beyond the power of humans, so the one who is able to do them should be described as divine. It is said to them: If that was within his power and he was independent of it, then saving himself from his enemies and repelling their evil from him would be within his power. This is not the case. If the Christians only acknowledge that, then their statement and claim that he did it independently is invalid. If they do not accept that, then they have no proof either, because they are opposed by Moses, peace be upon him, and the great matters that took place at his hands, such as turning the staff into a snake, splitting the sea, the hand, the egg, the manna, the quails, and other things. Likewise, what took place at the hands of the prophets. If they deny that, then we also deny what they claim about his appearance at the hands of Jesus, peace be upon him. They cannot prove any of that for Jesus, because the way to prove it with us is the texts of the Qur’an, and they deny the Qur’an and lie about whoever brought it. They cannot prove that with the reports of continuous transmission. It has been said: The Christians were on the religion of Islam for eighty-one years after Jesus was raised, praying towards the qiblah and fasting the month of Ramadan, until a war broke out between them and the Jews. There was a brave man among the Jews called Paul, who killed a group of Jesus’ companions. He said, “If the truth is with Jesus, then we have disbelieved and denied, and our destination is Hell. We are deceived if they enter Paradise and we enter Hell, and if he tricks them and leads them astray, they will enter Hell.” He had a horse called Al-Aqab, and he showed remorse and put dirt on its head and said to the Christians, “I am Paul, your horse. I have been called from heaven that there is no repentance for you unless you become a Christian.” So they brought him into a house in the church, and he stayed there for a year, not going out day or night, until he learned the Gospel. He went out and said, I have been called from heaven that God has accepted your repentance, so they believed him and loved him. Then he went to Jerusalem and appointed Nestorius as their successor and taught him that Jesus, son of Mary, was a god. Then he went to the Romans, who were both divine and human, and said, “Jesus was not a human being who became human, nor a body who became flesh, but he was the son of God and taught that to a man called Jacob. Then he called a man called Al-Malik and said to him, ‘God is and will remain, and Jesus will remain.’ When he had control over them, he called these three one by one and said to him, ‘You are my salvation, and I have seen the Messiah. ’” In his sleep and was pleased with him, and he said to each one of them, Tomorrow I will slaughter myself and offer myself as a sacrifice, so invite the people to your sect. Then he entered the slaughterhouse and slaughtered himself. On the third day, each one of them invited the people to his sect, so each one of them followed a group and they fought and differed until this day, so all the Christians are from the three sects. This was the reason for their polytheism, as it is said, and God knows best. This story has been narrated in the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: So We cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection (al-Ma’idah 5:14) and it will come, God willing: The Almighty’s saying: It is better for you to desist. “It is better for you” is in the accusative case according to Sibawayh with the implication of a verb, as if he said: Do what is better for you, because if he forbade them from polytheism, he ordered them to do what is better for them. Sibawayh said: Among the things that are in the accusative case with the implication of a verb that is not shown is: It is better for you to desist, because if you say: Do it, then you are removing it from one matter and including it in another. And he recited: Promise me that you will spend your money or that interest will be easier between them Abu Ubaidah’s doctrine: Stop, and it will be better for you. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: This is a mistake because it implies the condition and its answer, and this does not exist in the speech of the Arabs. Al-Farra’s doctrine is that it is an adjective for a deleted source. Ali ibn Sulayman said: This is a grave mistake, because the meaning would be: Stop, and the end that is better for you. The Almighty said: God is only one God. This is a beginning and a single predicate is a description of Him. It is permissible for God to be a substitute for the name of God Almighty, One, whose predicate is the estimation: The worshipped is only one. Glory be to Him that He should have a son. That is, He is far removed from having a son. When from was dropped, that was in the accusative case by removing the preposition, that is, how could He have a son, and the son of a man is similar to Him and there is no similarity to God Almighty. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He has no partner, and Jesus and Mary are from, and the sum of whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is in them is created. So how could Jesus be a god when he was created? If it is permissible for him, then let children be permissible so that everyone who has a miracle manifested upon him is his son. And sufficient is God as a Disposer of affairs meaning for His friends, as has been mentioned previously.
4:172: The Almighty said: The Messiah will not disdain meaning he will not be proud or ashamed to be a servant of God meaning from being, so it is in the accusative case. Al-Hasan read: that it is with a kasra on the hamza as a negation of it, meaning what, and the meaning is that he will not have a son, and it is necessary to raise it is and the narration did not mention it, nor the angels brought near meaning from the mercy and pleasure of God, so it indicates with this that the angels are better than the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them all, and likewise nor do I say that I am an angel (Hud 11:31) and the reference to this meaning has been presented in Al-Baqarah and whoever disdains meaning disdains from His worship and is arrogant so do not do it He will gather them to Him meaning to the place of assembly all together and each will be rewarded according to what he deserves, as he explained in the verse after this But as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty until His saying: a helper. The root of is disdainful is nakaf so the ya, the sin, and the ta are additions. It is said: nakaft min The thing and I disdained it and I disdained it, meaning I kept it away from what one disdained. From this is the hadith: He was asked about Subhan God, so he said: God is abstaining from all evil means that He is exalted and sanctified from rivals and children. Al-Zajjaj said: He is abstaining means he is not ashamed, taken from nakafat al-da’m if you remove it with your finger from your cheek, and the hadith is from this. The sweat does not stop from his forehead meaning it does not stop. From this, the hadith states: He came with an army whose end will not be cut off, whose end will not be interrupted. It was said: It is from nakaf which means defect. It is said: He has no nakaf or wakaf in this matter, meaning there is no defect: meaning the Messiah will not refrain from nor abstain from slavery, nor will he be cut off from it, nor will he find fault with it.
4:173: God Almighty says: “As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will pay them their reward in full and increase them from His bounty. But as for those who disdain and are arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or helper.”
4:174: The Almighty said: O mankind, there has come to you a proof from your Lord meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to Al-Thawri. He called it a proof because it is accompanied by proof, which is a miracle. Mujahid said: The proof here is the argument, and the meaning is close, for the miracles are his argument, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the revealed light is the Qur’an, according to Al-Hasan. He called it a light because through it the rulings are made clear and one is guided from misguidance, so it is a clear light, meaning clear and evident.
4:175: The Almighty said: But as for those who believed in God and held fast to Him meaning to the Qur’an from His disobedience. And if they held fast to His Book, then they held fast to Him and to His Prophet. It was said: they held fast to Him, meaning to God. Infallibility means abstention. It was mentioned before. And guides them meaning He guides them. So He implied He to indicate that the speech is cut off from what preceded it. To Him meaning to His reward. It was said: To the truth so that they may know it a straight path meaning a straight religion and a path is accusative with an implied verb indicating it and He guides them is the estimate and he knows them a straight path. It was said: It is a second object on the estimate and he guides them to his reward a straight path. It was said: It is a state and the ha in to him is said: It is for the Qur’an. It was said: For grace. It was said: For grace and mercy, because they mean reward. It was said: It is for God Almighty with the deletion of the added as mentioned earlier that the meaning is And He guides them to His reward. Abu Ali: The ha refers back to what was mentioned earlier from the name of God Almighty and the meaning is And He guides them to His path. So if we make a straight path accusative as a state, the state is from this deleted word. And in His saying: And grace is evidence that the Almighty bestows His reward upon His servants, because if it were in exchange for the work, He would not have been preferred. And God knows best.
4:176: It has six issues: First - Al-Bara’ bin Azib said: This is the last verse revealed from the Qur’an. This is in the book of Muslim. It was also said: It was revealed while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was preparing for the Farewell Pilgrimage, and it was revealed because of Jabir. Jabir bin Abdullah said: I fell ill and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr came to visit me while they were walking, and I fainted. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution and poured some of his ablution water over me, and I regained consciousness. I said: O Messenger of God, how should I decide about my wealth? He did not answer me anything until the verse about inheritance was revealed: “They ask you for a legal opinion. Say: God gives you a legal opinion about those who are not related to you.” Narrated by Muslim. He said: The last verse to be revealed was: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. (al-Baqarah 2:281) This has been mentioned before, and the discussion of those who are not related to you has been completed at the beginning of the surah, and that what is meant by brothers here is brothers on the father’s side and the mother’s side or on the father’s side. Jabir had nine sisters. The second - the Almighty’s saying: If a man dies and has no son, meaning he has neither a son nor a father, so He was satisfied with mentioning one of them. Al-Jurjani said: The word son is used for both the son and the one born. The father is called a father because he is a son, and the one born is called a son because he is a son, like the word offspring, which comes from dhara, then it is used for the one born and the father. God Almighty said: And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ark. (Ya-Sin 36:41) Third: The majority of scholars from the Companions and the Followers consider sisters as the daughters’ agnates even if there is no brother with them, except for Ibn Abbas, for he did not consider sisters as the daughters’ agnates. This is what Dawud and a group agreed with, and their proof is the apparent meaning of the statement of God Almighty: If a man dies and leaves no child but has a sister, she shall have half of what he leaves. The sister was not inherited except if the deceased had no child. They said: It is known that the daughter is from the son, so it is necessary that the sister does not inherit if she is present. Ibn al-Zubayr used to say what Ibn Abbas said in this matter until al-Aswad ibn Yazid informed him: Muadh ruled in a case of a daughter and a sister and divided the money between them in half. Fourth - This verse is called the verse of summer, because it was revealed in the summer. “Umar said: By God, I will not leave anything more important to me than the matter of the kalalah. I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he was never harsh with me about anything as he was with me about it, until he stabbed my side or my chest with his finger and then said: O Omar, is not the verse about summer that was revealed at the end of Surat An-Nisa sufficient for you? And on his authority, may God be pleased with him, he said: “There are three things that I would rather have the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, be among than the world and everything in it: kalalah, usury, and the caliphate.” Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan. Fifth - Some of the Rafidis attacked Paul: Omar: By God, I will not stop talking. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: God makes clear to you lest you go astray. Al-Kisa’i said: The meaning is that God makes clear to you lest you go astray. Abu Ubaid said: Al-Kisa’i was told a hadith narrated by Ibn Umar “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Let none of you call upon his son to agree with God’s answer. He approved of it. An-Nahhas said: The meaning according to Abu Ubaid is lest he agree with God’s answer. This statement according to the Basrans is a clear mistake because they do not permit the omission of “la” and the meaning according to them is: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray. Then it was deleted as he said: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82). And likewise the meaning of the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is that he does not like to agree with God’s answer. And God is Knowing of all things. It was mentioned in more than one place, and God knows best.
5:1: By the power and strength of God, it is Madani by consensus, and it was narrated that it was revealed when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) returned from Al-Hudaybiyah. Al-Naqqash mentioned, "On the authority of Abu Salamah, who said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) returned from Al-Hudaybiyah, he said: (O Ali, do you know that Surat Al-Ma'idah was revealed to me, and what a beneficial thing it is?)" Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is a fabricated hadith that is not permissible for a Muslim to accept it. As for us saying: Surat Al-Ma'idah, and what a beneficial thing it is, we do not attribute it to anyone, but it is good speech. Ibn Atiyyah said: In my opinion, this does not resemble the speech of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). "It was narrated on his authority (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that he said: (Surat Al-Ma'idah is called in the Kingdom of God the Savior, and it saves its reciter from the hands of the angels of punishment)". Among these surahs is what was revealed during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and among them is what was revealed in the year of the conquest, which is the Almighty's saying: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from believing in God (Al-Ma'idah 5:10). Everything that was revealed of the Qur’an after the migration of the Prophet (peace be upon him) was revealed in Medina, whether it was revealed in Medina or during a journey. Only what was revealed before the migration is considered Meccan. Abu Maysarah said: Al-Ma’idah is one of the last things to be revealed and there is nothing abrogated in it. It contains eighteen obligations that are not found in any other surah, and they are: And the strangled, the beaten, the fallen, the gored, and that which a wild animal has eaten, “And that which has been slaughtered on stone altars, and that you seek lots with arrows,” And what you have trained of birds of prey to hunt, “And the food of those who were given the Scripture,” And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, and complete purification, When you rise to prayer, “And the male thief, male or female,” Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram, until His saying: Mighty, Possessor of Retribution, and God has not appointed any bahīrah, nor sā’ibah, nor wasīlah, nor Ḥām. And the Almighty said: As a testimony between you when death approaches one of you verse. I said: And the nineteenth obligation is the saying of God the Almighty: And when you call to prayer, the call to prayer is not mentioned in the Qur’an except in this verse. As for what came in Surat Al-Jumu’ah, it is specific to Friday, and in this surah it is general for all prayers. And “It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he recited Surat Al-Ma’idah during the Farewell Pilgrimage and said: (O people, Surat Al-Ma’idah is among the last to be revealed, so make lawful what it makes lawful and forbid what it makes unlawful.)9 And something similar to it, from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, with a chain of transmission ending with her. Jubayr ibn Nufayr said: I entered upon Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and she said: Do you recite Surat Al-Ma’idah? I said: Yes. She said: It is the last to be revealed by God, so whatever you find in it of what is lawful, then make it lawful, and whatever you find in it of what is unlawful, then forbid it.” Al-Sha’bi said: Nothing was abrogated from this surah until His saying: nor the sacred month nor the sacrificial animals, the verse. Some of them said: It was abrogated by or two others from other than you. It has seven issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: O you who believe. Alqamah said: Everything in the Qur’an, O you who believe, is Medinan and O people, is Meccan. This was excluded according to the majority and has been mentioned before. This verse is one of those whose eloquence and abundance of meanings are evident despite the fewness of its words to anyone who has insight into speech, as it includes five rulings: First - The command to fulfill contracts. Second - The permissibility of the animal of livestock. Third - The exception of what follows after that. Fourth - The exception of the state of ihram in what he hunts. Fifth - What the verse requires of permitting hunting for those who are not in ihram. Al-Naqqash narrated that the companions of Al-Kindi said to him: O wise man, make for us something like this Qur’an. He said: Yes! Make something like some of it. So he hid himself for many days, then he came out and said: By God, I am not able and no one can bear this. I opened the Qur’an and Surah Al-Ma’idah came out, so I looked and saw that it spoke of fulfillment and forbade breaking and permitted a general permissibility. Then he made an exception after an exception, then he informed about his ability and wisdom in two lines. No one can do this except in the skins. The second - the Almighty’s saying: Fulfill. It is said: And fulfill and fulfill are two languages! God Almighty said: And who is more faithful to his covenant than God? (al-Tawbah 9:111) and God Almighty said: And Abraham, who fulfilled (al-Najm 53:37) and the poet said: As for Ibn Tawq, he fulfilled his duty as he fulfilled the duty of the camels of the star driver. He combined the two languages with contracts. Contracts are ties, the singular of which is contract. It is said: I tied the covenant and the rope, and I tied the honey. It is used for meanings and bodies. Al-Hutay’ah said: A people who, when they make a contract with their neighbor, tighten the knot and burden him with hardship. So God Almighty commanded the fulfillment of contracts. Al-Hasan said: He means by that the contracts of religion, which are what a person has made for himself, such as buying, selling, renting, leasing, marriage, divorce, farming, reconciliation, ownership, choice, emancipation, management, and other matters, as long as that is not outside of the Shari’ah. Likewise, what he has made for himself for God of acts of obedience, such as Hajj, fasting, seclusion, standing in prayer, vows, and similar acts of obedience of the religion of Islam. As for vowing something permissible, it is not binding by consensus of the nation. Ibn al-Arabi said: Then it was said: The verse was revealed about the People of the Book, because God Almighty said: And when God took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture to make it clear to the people and not to conceal it (Al Imran 3:187). Ibn Jurayj said: It is specific to the People of the Book and it was revealed about them. It was said: It is general and this is correct, because the word believers includes the believers of the People of the Book because there is a contract between them and God to fulfill the trust in what is in their book regarding the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they are commanded to do that in His saying: Fulfill the contracts and in other places. Ibn Abbas said: Fulfill the contracts means with what is permissible and what is forbidden and what is imposed and what is set in all things. Mujahid and others said the same. Ibn Shihab said: I read the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which he wrote to Amr ibn Hazm when he sent him to Najran, and at the beginning of it: This is a clarification for the people from God and His Messenger. O you who believe, fulfill the contracts, so he wrote the verses in it until His saying: Indeed, God is swift in account. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is fulfill the contract. May God be with you and your covenant with one another. All of this goes back to the general statement, which is correct in this chapter. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Believers are bound by their conditions. He said: Every condition that is not in the Book of God is invalid, even if there are a hundred conditions. So he explained that the condition or contract that must be fulfilled is what is in accordance with the Book of God, that is, the religion of God. If something appears in it that contradicts it, it is rejected, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it will be rejected. Ibn Ishaq said: The tribes of Quraysh gathered in the house of Abdullah bin Jud’an because of his honor and lineage. They made a contract and pledged that they would not find anyone in Mecca who had been wronged, whether from its people or others, except that they would stand with him until his grievance was returned to him. Quraysh called that alliance the Alliance of the Virtuous, which is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I witnessed an oath in the house of Abdullah bin Jud’an for which I would not have preferred red camels, and if I had been called upon to do so in Islam, I would have responded. This oath is the intended meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: And whatever oath was made in the pre-Islamic period, Islam only rejected it with severity, “because it is in accordance with the Sharia, as it commands justice against the oppressor. As for what was from their corrupt covenant and their invalid contracts based on injustice and raids, Islam has demolished it, praise be to God. Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Walid bin Utbah attacked Al-Hussein bin Ali regarding his money - due to the authority of Al-Walid: for he was the governor of Medina - so Al-Hussein said to him: I swear by God that you will do justice to me regarding my right, or I will take my sword and stand in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then I will call for the Hilf Al-Fudul. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr said: And I swear by God that if he calls me, I will take my sword and stand with him until he takes justice from his right, or we will all die. And the report reached Al-Miswar bin Makhrama, and he said the same thing, and it reached Abd Al-Rahman bin Uthman bin Ubaidullah Al-Taimi, and he said the same thing. When that report reached Al-Walid, he did justice to him. Third: The Almighty’s saying: “Lawful to you are the beasts of cattle.” The address is to everyone who has committed himself to faith in its entirety and perfection. The Arabs had traditions regarding livestock, such as the bahīrah, the sā’ibah, the wasīlah, and the ḥām, among which are the ḥām. This verse was revealed to remove those imaginary illusions and corrupt and false opinions. There was disagreement about the meaning of the beasts of cattle. The beast is the name of every quadruped, named thus due to its ambiguity, due to its lack of speech and understanding, and its lack of discrimination and intellect. From this comes the word Ṭabmhum meaning closed, and layl ḥīmah, and bahmah for the brave man who does not know where he is brought from. The livestock: camels, cows, and sheep. They were named thus due to their gentle gait. God Almighty said: And the livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and many benefits. (al-Nahl 16:142) meaning large and small. Then He explained them by saying: Eight pairs (An’am: 143) until His saying: Or were you witnesses? (An’am: 244). And God Almighty said: And He has made for you, from the hides of livestock, houses which you find light on the day of your departure and the day of your settlement. “Their wool” (al-Nahl 16:80) means sheep; and their hair (al-Nahl 16:80) means camels; and their hair (al-Nahl 16:80) means goats. These are three pieces of evidence that indicate that the name an’am includes these types: camels, cows, and sheep. This is the statement of Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan. Al-Harawi said: If it is said an’am, then it is specifically camels. Al-Tabari said: Some people said that the beast of livestock is its wild animals, such as gazelles, wild cows, donkeys, and other than that. This was mentioned by others than Al-Tabari on the authority of Al-Suddi, Al-Rabi’, Qatadah, and Al-Dahhak. It is as if he said: The livestock have been made lawful for you, so the type was added to something more specific than it. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is a good statement, because the livestock are the eight pairs, and whatever is added to them from the rest of the animals is called an’am with a group with it. It is as if the predator, such as the lion and every fanged animal, is outside the definition of the livestock. So the beast of livestock is the grazer among the four-legged animals. I said: Accordingly, it includes ungulates because they are grazers and not predators, and it is not like that because God Almighty said: And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and many benefits. Then He linked to them His statement: And horses, mules, and donkeys. (al-Nahl 16:8) He renewed their mention and linked them to the livestock, indicating that they are not from them, and God knows best. It was said: The livestock is what is not game because game is called wild, not animal. This goes back to the first statement. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that he said: The livestock are the fetuses that come out from the wombs of their mothers when slaughtered, so they are eaten without ritual slaughter. Ibn Abbas said the same, and there is some distance in it because God Almighty said: Except what is recited to you. And I do not have an exception for the fetuses. Malik said: The slaughter of the slaughtered animal is the slaughter of its fetus if it was not realized alive and its hair had grown and its creation was complete. If its creation was not complete and its hair had not grown, it is not eaten unless it is realized alive, then it is ritually slaughtered. If they hasten to slaughter it and it dies by itself, it was said: It is ritually slaughtered. It was said: It is not ritually slaughtered, and more clarification will come for this, God willing. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: Except what is recited to you meaning what is recited to you in the Qur’an and Sunnah, from the Almighty’s saying: Forbidden to you are dead animals (al-Ma’idah 5:3) and his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: Every fanged beast of prey is forbidden. If it is said: What is recited to us is not the Sunnah, we say: Every Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is from the Book of God. The evidence for this is two things: One of them is the hadith of Al-Aseef. I will judge your children according to the Book of God. Stoning is not stipulated in the Book of God, the second hadith of Ibn Masoud. Why should I not declare the curse of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when it is in the Book of God and the hadith and will come in Surat al-Hashr and it is possible except for what is recited to you now or what is recited to you in the future on the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that it is evidence of the permissibility of delaying the statement beyond a time when it does not require hastening the need. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: except for the game that is lawful. That is, whatever was game is lawful in the case of ihram but not in the case of ihram, and whatever was not game is lawful in both cases. The grammarians differed on whether except for what is recited is an exception or not? The Basrans said: It is an exception from the cattle and the non-localized game is another exception from it, so both exceptions from his saying: the cattle and it is the exception from it, the estimate is: except what is recited to you except the game and you are in a state of ihram, unlike his saying: Indeed, We were sent to a people of criminals * Except the family of Lot (al-Hijr 15:58-59) as follows. And it was said: It is an exception from what follows it from the exception, so it becomes like the saying of the Almighty: They said, Indeed, we were sent to a people of criminals (al-Hijr 15:58). And if it were like that, then it would be necessary to permit hunting in ihram because it is an exception from the forbidden, since the Almighty’s saying: Except what is recited to you is an exception from permission, and this is a weak view, so its meaning is that the cattle are permissible to you except the local game and you are in a state of ihram except what is recited to you except the game. And it is also permissible for its meaning to be fulfill the contracts except the local game, and the cattle are permissible to you except what is recited to you. Al-Farra’ permitted that except what is recited to you be in the place of raising as a substitute on the condition that it is connected with except It is also connected with la, and the Basrans do not permit it except in the indefinite or what is close to it from the names of the species, such as the people came except Zayd, and the accusative according to him is that the non-local hunting is accusative in the state of what is in awfa. Al-Akhfash said: O you who believe, fulfill the contracts, the non-local hunting. Another said: It is a state of the kaf and the mim in lakum, and the meaning is: I have made lawful for you the beast of cattle, the non-local hunting. Then it was said: It is permissible for the permissibility to return to the people, meaning do not make the hunting permissible during the state of ihram, and it is permissible for it to return to God Almighty, meaning I have made lawful for you the beast except what was hunted during the time of ihram, as you say: I have made lawful for you such and such, but it is not permissible for you on Friday. So if you say it returns to the people, then the meaning is: the hunting is not permissible, so the nun was deleted for ease. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And you are in a state of ihram means entering into ihram for Hajj and Umrah. It is said: A man is in ihram and people are in ihram if they enter into ihram for Hajj. From this comes the saying of the poet: I said to her: Come to me, for I am forbidden, and after that I am intelligent. Any one who wears it is called ihram because of what he who enters it forbids himself from women, perfume, and other things. It is said: he entered the sanctuary, so hunting in the sanctuary is also forbidden. Al-Sahn, Ibrahim, and Yahya bin Waththab read haram with a sukoon on the ra’, and it is a Tamimi dialect. They say in rusul: rusul, and in kutub: kutubu, and the like. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God decrees what He wills is a strengthening of these legal rulings that contradict the customary rulings of the Arabs. That is, you, O Muhammad, who hears the abrogation of those rulings that you have known of them, be aware, for the One who is the Owner of everything decides what He wills “There is no objector to His judgment” (al-Ra’d 13:41), He legislates what He wills as He wills.
5:2: It contains thirteen issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: Do not violate the symbols of God is addressed to the true believers, meaning do not transgress the limits of God in any matter. The symbols are the plural of a symbol on the weight of fa’alih. Ibn Faris said: The singular is called a symbol, which is better. The symbol is the sacrificial animal, and its marking is to cut its hump until blood flows from it, so it is known that it is a sacrificial animal. Notification is informing by way of sensing. It is said: he marked the sacrificial animal, meaning he made a mark for it so that it is known that it is a sacrificial animal. From this comes the symbols, the landmarks, the singular of which is a mark, and they are the places that have been marked with signs. From this comes the poetry because it is where the feeling occurs. From this comes the poet because he senses with his intelligence what no one else senses. From this comes the barley for the hair on his head. So the symbols, according to what is said, are the animals that are marked to be sacrificial to the House of God, and according to what is said about all the rituals of Hajj, Ibn Abbas said. And Mujahid said: Al-Safa and Al-Marwah, the sacrificial animal, and the sacrificial animal, all of that is from the symbols. The poet said: We kill them generation by generation. You see them as ritual sacrifices by which people draw near. The polytheists were performing Hajj, Umrah, and offering sacrifices, so the Muslims wanted to change them, so God Almighty revealed: Do not violate the symbols of God. Ata’ bin Abi Rabah said: The symbols of God are everything that God has commanded and forbidden. Al-Hasan said: The religion of God is all like His saying: “That is it. And whoever honors the symbols of God - indeed, it is from the piety of hearts.” (al-Hajj 22:32) meaning the religion of God. I said: This statement is the most likely one that is preferred over the one that deceives him because of its generality. Scholars have differed regarding the poems of the sacrifice, which are: Second: The majority permitted it, then they differed on which side it should be marked. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Abu Thawr said: It should be on the right side. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, and it was confirmed on the authority of Ibn Abbas. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, marked his camel’s right hump.” Narrated by Muslim and others, and this is the correct view. It was also narrated that he marked his body on the left side. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: This is, in my opinion, a rejected hadith from Ibn Abbas, and the correct view is the hadith of Muslim from Ibn Abbas. He said: There is no other authentic hadith from him. The right hump is its side, and the hump is higher and more visible. A group said: It should be on the left side, which is the view of Malik. He said: There is nothing wrong with it on the right side. Mujahid said: On both sides, sheep. Ahmad said the same in one of his two views. Abu Hanifa forbade all of this and said: It is torture for the animal. The hadith is to be rebutted. Also, this is similar to the branding by which the owner is known, as mentioned above. Ibn al-Arabi went too far in his rebuttal and denial of Abu Hanifa when he did not see the marking, so he said: It is as if he had not heard of this ritual in the Shari’ah, for it is more famous than it is among the scholars. I said: What I saw stated in the books of the Hanafi scholars is that giving a sign is reprehensible according to the opinion of Abu Hanifa, and according to Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, it is neither reprehensible nor a Sunnah, but rather it is permissible because giving a sign was a Sunnah like imitation, and in that it is a wound and its like it was forbidden, so it included the Sunnah and innovation, so it was made permissible. And for Abu Hanifa, giving a sign is like it and it is forbidden in that it is the torture of an animal, so it was reprehensible. And what was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was only in the beginning when the Arabs were plundering all wealth except what was made an offering, and they did not know the offering except by giving a sign, then it disappeared with the disappearance of the enemy. This is how it was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and it was narrated from Sheikh Imam Abu Mansur Al-Maturidi, may God Almighty have mercy on him, that he said: It is possible that Abu Hanifa disliked giving a sign to the people of his time while he was exaggerating in sexual intercourse in a way that he feared spreading it. As for what did not exceed the limit, he did as he did in the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is good. And this is how Abu Ja`far Al-Tahawi mentioned: So this is it. The Hanafi scholars apologized to Abu Hanifa for the hadith mentioned in Al-Ish’ar, as they heard it and it reached them and they knew it. They said: According to the opinion that it is reprehensible, no one should be deemed forbidden by it because doing something reprehensible is not considered one of the rituals. Third: The Almighty’s saying: nor the sacred month is a singular noun that indicates the genus of all the sacred months, which are four: one singular and three consecutive, and their explanation will come in Bara’ah. The meaning is: Do not consider them permissible for fighting or raiding, and do not change them, for changing them is permissible, and that is what they used to do of postponing. Likewise His saying: nor the offerings nor the necklaces means do not consider them permissible, and it is with the deletion of an adjective, meaning nor those with necklaces, the plural of necklace. So the Almighty forbade considering permissible the satire as a whole, then He mentioned the imitator of it as an emphasis and exaggeration in drawing attention to the prohibition of imitation. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: nor the offering nor the necklaces. The offering is what is offered to the House of God Almighty, whether a camel, cow, or sheep. The singular is a gift, a gift, and an offering. So whoever said: He meant by the rituals the rites said: He mentioned the offering as a reminder of its specificity. And whoever said: The rituals are the offering said: The rituals are what are marked, meaning marked by the flow of blood from their humps, and the offering is what is not marked, it is sufficient for it to be adorned. And it was said: The difference is that the rituals are the body of the livestock, and the offering is the cows, sheep, clothes, and everything that is offered. And the majority said: The offering is general in all that is used to draw near to God from sacrifices and charity. And from this is his saying, peace be upon him: The early Friday prayer is like the gift of a camel” until he said: like the gift of an egg so he called it a sacrifice and calling the egg a sacrifice has no place except that he meant by it charity and likewise the scholars said: If he said I made my garment a sacrifice then he must give it in charity except that the generality is directed to one of the three types of camels, cows and sheep and driving them to the sanctuary and slaughtering them there and this is only received by those who know the law in the saying of the Most High: But if you are prevented, then what can be obtained of sacrifice (al-Baqarah 2:196) and he meant by it the sheep and the Most High said: Two just men among you shall judge it as a sacrifice delivered to the Kaaba (al-Ma’idah 5:95) and the Most High said: And whoever enjoys the ‘Umrah until the Hajj, then what can be obtained of sacrifice (al-Baqarah 2:196) and the minimum is a sheep according to the jurists and Malik said: If he said my garment is a sacrifice, its price is put in a sacrifice and the necklaces are what people used to wear as a security for them then it is on the deletion of an added meaning nor the owners of the necklaces then it was abrogated Ibn Abbas said: Two verses were abrogated from Al-Ma’idah The verse of the necklaces and His saying: But if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them (al-Ma’idah 5:42). As for the necklaces, they were abrogated by the command to kill the polytheists wherever they were and in whatever month they were. As for the other, they were abrogated by the saying of God Almighty: And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5:49) as follows. It was said: He meant by the necklaces the necklaces themselves, so it is a prohibition against taking the bark of the trees of the sanctuary to wear it as a garland seeking security. This was said by Mujahid, Ata’, and Mutraf ibn Ash-Shakheer. And God knows best. The reality of the sacrificial animal is everything given for which no compensation is mentioned. The jurists agreed that whoever says: I owe God a sacrificial animal, he sends its price to Mecca.
