As for the necklaces, they are everything that is hung on the humps and necks of the sacrificial animals as a sign that it is for God Almighty, such as a sandal or something else. It is an Abrahamic tradition that remained in the pre-Islamic period and Islam approved it. It is the tradition of cows and sheep. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, once sent sheep to the House as a gift and he put a necklace on them. This was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. A group of scholars agreed with this: Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, and Ibn Habib. Malik and the people of opinion rejected it, and it seems that this hadith about putting a necklace on sheep did not reach them, or it did reach them, but they rejected it because Al-Aswad alone narrated it from Aisha, may God be pleased with her. So the statement with this is more appropriate, and God knows best. As for cows, if they have humps, they are made to feel hair like camels. Ibn Umar said this, and Malik said the same. Al-Shafi’i said: They are put a necklace on and they are made to feel hair absolutely, and they did not differentiate. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: They are put a necklace on and they are not made to feel hair. This statement is more correct, since they do not have humps and they are more like sheep than camels, and God knows best. Fifth - They agreed that whoever imitates a sacrificial animal with the intention of entering ihram and drives it, he becomes in ihram. God Almighty said: Do not violate the rites of God until He said: and hunt. He did not mention entering ihram, but when he mentioned imitating it, it was known that it is in the same position as entering ihram. Sixth: If he sends the sacrificial animal and does not water it himself, then he is not in a state of ihram, according to the hadith of Aisha, who said: I twisted the necklaces of the sacrificial animals of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with my own hands, then he put them on with his own hands, then he sent them with my father. Nothing that God had permitted for him was forbidden to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he slaughtered the sacrificial animals. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. This is the view of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and the majority of scholars. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: He becomes forbidden. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever offers a sacrificial animal, what is forbidden to the pilgrim is forbidden to him until he slaughters the sacrificial animal. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. This is the view of Ibn Umar, Ata’, Mujahid, and Saeed bin Jubayr. Al-Khattabi narrated it from the People of Opinion, and they provided evidence for it with the hadith of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: I was sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had lost his shirt from his pocket, then he took it out from his feet. The people looked at the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: I was ordered to have my body that I was sent with adorned and branded in such and such a place, so I put on my shirt and forgot, so I did not take two shirts out from my head. He had sent his body and stayed in Madinah. In its chain of transmission is Abd al-Rahman ibn Ata’ ibn Abi Laybiyyah, who is weak. If he adorned a sheep and went with it, the Kufians said: He does not become a pilgrim, because adorning a sheep is not recommended nor is it one of the rituals, because a wolf is feared for it, so it does not reach the sanctuary, unlike the body that is left until it reaches the water and grazes the trees and reaches the sanctuary. In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, she said: I wove her necklaces from wool. Wool was dyed wool, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: And the mountains will be like carded wool (al-Qari’ah 101:5). Seventh: It is not permissible to sell or give away the sacrificial animal if it is tied up or marked, because it is obligatory. If the one who made it obligatory dies, it is not inherited from him and is executed for his own sake, unlike the sacrifice, which is not obligatory except by slaughter, especially according to Malik, unless he makes it obligatory by word. If he makes it obligatory by word before slaughtering, and says: I made this sheep a sacrificial animal, it is obligatory upon him. If it is lost and then he finds it during the days of slaughtering or after it, he slaughters it, and it is not permissible for him to sell it. If he bought another sacrificial animal, he slaughters both of them, according to the opinion of Ahmad and Ishaq. Al-Shafi’i said: There is no replacement upon him if it is lost or stolen. The replacement is only for what is obligatory. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: If it is lost, it is sufficient. And whoever dies on the day of sacrifice before he sacrifices, his sacrifice is inherited from him like the rest of his property, unlike the sacrificial animal. Ahmad and Abu Thawr said: It is slaughtered in all cases. Al-Awza’i said: It is slaughtered unless he has a debt that cannot be paid except from that sacrifice, in which case it is sold for his debt. If he dies after slaughtering it, his heirs do not inherit it from him, and they did with it from eating. And the charity is what he had to do with it, and they do not divide its meat by way of inheritance. And whatever defects afflict the sacrifice before slaughtering is upon its owner to replace it, unlike the sacrificial animal. This is the conclusion of the Maliki school of thought. It has been said about the sacrificial animal that its owner must replace it, and the first is more correct, and God knows best. Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: nor those who are in the Sacred House means those who intend to go there, as they say I intended to go there, meaning I intended to go there. Al-A’mash read nor those who are in the Sacred House with the addition like his saying: other than the place of hunting, and the meaning is do not prevent the infidels who intend to go to the Sacred House for the purpose of worship and devotion. Based on this, it was said: What is in these verses of prohibition against a polytheist or observing his sanctity by wearing a necklace or the door of the House, it is all abrogated by the verse of the sword in His saying: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5) and His saying: So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year of theirs (al-Tawbah 9:28). So the polytheist cannot go to Hajj, and he is not safe in the sacred months even if he offers a sacrifice, wears a necklace and performs Hajj. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said it as will be mentioned. Some people said: The verse is decisive and has not been abrogated and it is for Muslims, and God has prohibited frightening those who intend to go to His House from Muslims, and the prohibition is general in the sacred month and other than it, but He specifically mentioned the sacred month as a sign of reverence and preference, and this is consistent with the saying of Ata’, then the meaning is do not violate the signs of God, which are His commands and prohibitions, and what people know, do not violate it. Therefore, Abu Maysarah said: It is decisive. Mujahid said: The necklaces were not abrogated from it, and a man would wear something from the bark of the forbidden, so he would not approach it, so that was abrogated. Ibn Jurayj said: This verse is a prohibition against pilgrims cutting off their spoils. Ibn Zayd said: The verse was revealed in the year of the conquest, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca. Some polytheists came to perform Hajj and Umrah, so the Muslims said: O Messenger of God, these are only polytheists, so we will not leave them alone unless we attack them. So the Qur’an was revealed: And do not protect the Sacred House. It was said: This was due to the matter of Shuraih bin Dhubay’ah al-Bakri - nicknamed al-Hatim - the soldiers of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, captured him while he was performing Umrah, so this verse was revealed, then this ruling was abrogated as we have repeated, and al-Hatim caught up with him and returned to Yamamah, so he was killed as an apostate. It was narrated from his story that he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, and left his horses outside Medina and said: To what do you call people? He said: To testify that there is no god but God, to establish prayer, and to pay zakat. He said: Good, except that I have leaders and I do not decide anything without them, and perhaps I will become Muslim and bring them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said to his companions: A man will enter upon you who speaks with the tongue of Satan, then he left him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He entered with the face of an unbeliever and left with the back of a traitor, and the man is not a Muslim. He passed by the wild animals of Medina and drove them away, and they sought him but were unable to find him. He left, saying: The night has enveloped her with a broken driver who is neither a camel nor a sheep herder. Nor a butcher on the back and the back of the bed, they slept and Ibn Hind did not sleep A young man, with slender legs and flapping feet, is measuring it. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out in the year of the issue, he heard the talbiyah of the pilgrims of Yamamah and said: This is Al-Khatam and his companions. He had given the plundered livestock of Medina as a gift to Mecca, so they set out in search of it, and the verse was revealed: It is not permissible, and I do not feel any piety towards God, even if they are polytheists. Ibn Abbas mentioned this. Ninth - And the verse is decisive. The Almighty’s saying: Do not violate the symbols of God requires completing the rituals. For this reason, the scholars said: If a man enters Hajj and then spoils it, he must perform all the actions of Hajj and it is not permissible for him to leave any of them. If his Hajj is spoiled, then he must make up for it in the year. Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi said: The Almighty’s saying: nor the sacred month is abrogated by His saying: And fight the polytheists altogether (al-Tawbah 9:36). His saying: nor the sacrificial animals nor the garlands is decisive and has not been abrogated. So whoever puts on the sacrificial animals and intends to enter ihram becomes a pilgrim and it is not permissible for him to exit ihram based on the evidence of this verse. So these rulings are connected to each other, some of them are abrogated and some of them are not. Tenth - The Almighty’s saying: They seek bounty from their Lord and His pleasure. The majority of commentators said about it: Its meaning is that they seek bounty and profits in trade and they seek His pleasure in addition to that in their assumption and desire. It was said: Some of them sought trade, and some of them sought the pleasure of God through Hajj, even if they did not attain it. Some of the Arabs believed in a reward after death, and that he would be resurrected, and it is not far-fetched that he would obtain some kind of relief in the Fire. Ibn Atiyyah said: This verse is a reconciliation from God Almighty to the Arabs and kindness to them so that souls would be at ease and people would mix and come to the season and listen to the Qur’an, and faith would enter their hearts and the proof would be established for them as it was. This verse was revealed in the year of the conquest, and God abrogated all of that after the year nine when Abu Bakr performed Hajj and the people were called to Surat Bara’ah. Eleventh - The Almighty’s saying: And when you have completed your ihram, then hunt is a command of permission - by consensus of the people - to lift what was prohibited by ihram. Many scholars have narrated this, but it is not correct. Rather, the formula of do that comes after the prohibition is based on its original obligation, and this is the view of Judge Abu al-Tayyib and others. Because the requirement for obligation is established and the precedence of the prohibition does not serve as a deterrent, its evidence is the Almighty’s saying: And when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists (al-Tawbah 9:5). So this do is based on obligation because what is meant by it is jihad. Rather, permission was understood there, and what is similar to it from His saying: And when the prayer is concluded, then disperse (al-Jumuah 62:10), And when they have purified themselves, then come to them (al-Baqarah 2:222) is from looking at the meaning and consensus, not from the formula of the command, and God knows best. The twelfth - The Almighty’s saying: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from coming to the Sacred Mosque. That is, let it not make you bear it, according to Ibn Abbas and Qatadah, and it is the saying of Al-Kisa’i and Abu Al-Abbas. It takes two objects, and it is said: So-and-so made me bear your hatred, meaning it made me bear it. The poet said: I stabbed Abu Uyaynah with a stab that made Fazara angry after that. Al-Akhfash said: That is, do not let it injure you. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Farra’ said: The meaning of do not let the hatred of a people cause you to transgress from right to wrong, and from justice to injustice. He, peace be upon him, said: Return the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you. The discussion of this and the like of this verse has already passed: So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you. (al-Baqarah 2:194) It has already been fully presented. It is said: So-and-so is the crime of his family, meaning he is their earner. So crime and wrongdoer mean the earner. So-and-so committed a crime, meaning he acquired the sin. From this is the saying of the poet: Nahedh's crime in Ars Nik, you see the bones that did not gather a cross Its meaning is the earner of sustenance, and the cross is the udk, and this is the origin of the construction of the word j-r-m. Ibn Faris said: It is said jaram and ajram, and la-jaram is like your saying la-did-la-ma-ha-wal-ma-ha, and its origin is from jaram, meaning he acquired. He said: Fazara then committed a crime to get angry Another said: O you who complain about Akla and what you have done to the tribes of killing and oppression It is said: Jaram yajriman jarman if he cut off. Al-Rummani Ali bin Isa said: This is the origin, so Jaram means to carry on something to cut it off from something else, and Jaram means to gain because it is cut off to gain, and Jaram means right because the right is cut off from it. Al-Khalil said: There is no doubt that they will have the Fire (al-Nahl 16:62), the punishment has been deserved for them. Al-Sakai said: Jaram and Ajram are two languages with one meaning, meaning he acquired, and Ibn Masoud read yajrimankum with a damma on the ya’, and the meaning is also that they will not gain you, and the Basrans do not know the damma, but they say: Jaram, not ghair, and hatred is resentment, and it was read with a fatha on the noon and a sukoon on it. It is said: I hated the man, I hate him, I hate him, I hate him, and I hate him, and I hate him, and I hate him, and I hate him, all of that if I hated him, meaning that he will not gain you the hatred of a people by preventing you from transgressing, and what is meant is your hatred of a people, so he added the source to the object. Ibn Zayd said: When the Muslims were prevented from the House in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, some polytheists passed by them wanting to perform Umrah, so the Muslims said: We repel them as their companions repelled us, so this verse was revealed, meaning do not transgress against these people, and do not repel them if they repel you their companions, with the opening of the hamza, the object for which, meaning because they repelled you. Abu Omar and Ibn Kathir read with the breaking of the hamza if they repel you, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid. It was narrated from Al-A’mash if they repel you. Ibn Atiyah said: If for the reward, meaning if such an action occurs in the future, and the first reading is more possible in meaning. An-Nahhas said: As for if your chests with the breaking of if, the great scholars of grammar, hadith, and reason forbid reading it with it for several reasons, including that the verse was revealed in the year of the conquest, the eighth year, and the polytheists repelled the Muslims in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah for six years, so the repelling was before the verse, and if it is read with the breaking, it is not permissible for it to be except after it, as you say: Do not give so-and-so anything if he fights you, this is only for the future, and if it is opened, it is for the past, so it is obligatory based on this that it is not permissible except because they repelled you. Also, if this hadith was not authentic, the conquest would have been obligatory because his saying: Do not violate the symbols of God until the end of the verse indicates that Mecca was in their hands, and they would not forbid this unless they were able to prevent people from entering the Sacred House. Therefore, it was necessary to open the door because when it was mentioned, that you transgress is in the accusative case because it is the object, meaning that the hatred of a people should not cause you to transgress. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid denied shan’an with a sukoon on the nun because the sources only come in such cases with a vowel, and others disagreed with them and said: This is not a source, but rather it is an active participle on the weight of kaslan and ghadban. Thirteenth - The Almighty’s saying: And cooperate in righteousness and piety. Al-Akhfash said: It is cut off from the beginning of the speech and it is a command for all creation to cooperate in righteousness and piety, meaning to help each other and urge each other to do what God Almighty has commanded and know it, and refrain from what God has forbidden and abstain from it. This is in agreement with what was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The one who guides to good is like the one who does it. It has also been said: The one who guides to evil is like the one who does it. Then it was said: Righteousness and piety are two words with one meaning and it was repeated with different words for emphasis and exaggeration, since every righteousness is piety and every piety is righteousness. Ibn Atiyah said: In this there is some tolerance, and the custom in the meaning of these two words is that righteousness includes what is obligatory and what is recommended, and piety is observing what is obligatory. If one of them is made in place of the other, then it is an exaggeration. Al-Marudi said: God Almighty urged cooperation in righteousness and linked it with piety for Him because in piety is the pleasure of God Almighty and in righteousness is the pleasure of people. Whoever combines the pleasure of God Almighty and the pleasure of people, his happiness is complete and his blessings are widespread. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said in his rulings: Cooperation in righteousness and piety is In many ways, it is the duty of the scholar to help people with his knowledge, so the rich man teaches them and helps them with his money, and the brave man with his bravery in the way of God, and the Muslims should be united like one hand. The blood of the believers is equal, and the lowest of them is responsible for their protection, and they are one hand against everyone else. It is necessary to turn away from the aggressor and not give him support and to turn him away from what he is doing. Then He forbade and said: And do not cooperate in sin and aggression. This is the subsequent ruling on crimes and aggression, which is oppressing people. Then He led with piety and made a general threat, saying: “And fear God. Indeed, God is severe in penalty.”
5:3: It contains twenty-six issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: He has forbidden you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God. This was discussed previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. Second - The Almighty’s saying: And the strangled is the one who dies by strangulation, which is the confinement of the soul, whether it was done to it by a human being or it happened to it in a rope or between two sticks or something similar. Qatada mentioned that the people of the Age of Ignorance used to strangle a sheep or other things, and when it died they would eat it. Ibn Abbas mentioned something similar. Third - The Almighty’s saying: And the one who is beaten severely. The one who is beaten severely is the one who is pelted with stones or sticks until death without slaughtering, according to Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi. It is said: From it, wa-qadh-yaqdh-wa-qadhan and it is said: wa-qadh-yaqdh-wa-qadhan and wa-qadh is severe beating, and so-and-so is wa-qaidh meaning severely beaten. Qatadah said: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to do that and eat it. Ad-Dahhak said: They used to beat the livestock with wood for their gods until they killed them and then ate them. From it is the one who is killed with a bow of a gun. Al-Farazdaq said: A young camel drives the young camel with its foot, a prey for the young camels In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, she said: I said, O Messenger of God, I am ordered to hunt with a spear and I hit it. He said: If you shoot with a spear and it pierces it, eat it, but if it hits it sideways, do not eat it. In another narration: If it is a stump. Abu Omar said: The scholars differed in the past and present regarding hunting with a gun, stone, and a stump. Whoever said that it is a stump, then it is not permissible for him to hunt with it except what he has slaughtered, according to what was narrated from Ibn Omar, and it is the opinion of Malik, Abu Hanifa and his companions, al-Thawri, and al-Shafi’i. The people of Sham disagreed with them on that. Al-Awza’i said regarding the stump, whether it is pierced or not, Abu al-Darda’, Fadala ibn Ubayd, Abdullah ibn Omar, and Makhul did not see anything wrong with it. Abu Omar said: This is what al-Awza’i mentioned on the authority of Abdullah ibn Omar, and what is well-known on the authority of Ibn Omar is what Malik mentioned on the authority of Nafi’ on his authority. The basis in this matter, and what is known and in it is the proof for those who resort to it, is the hadith of Adi ibn Hatim, in which it says: And whatever it hits sideways, do not eat it, for it is a stump. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: And the one who falls. The one who falls is the one who falls from a high place to a low place and dies, whether that is from a mountain or in a well or something similar. It is derived from the verb radda which means destruction, and it does not matter whether she falls by herself or someone else falls by her. If the arrow hits the prey and it falls from a mountain to the ground, it is also forbidden because it may die from the shock and falling, not from the arrow. From this is the hadith: And if you find it drowned in water, do not eat it, for you do not know whether the water killed it or your arrow. Narrated by Muslim. The people of ignorance used to eat what had fallen and did not believe that it was dead except what died from pain or the like without a known cause. As for these causes, they were, in their view, like slaughter, so the law restricted slaughter to a specific description, as will be explained, and all of these remained dead. All of this is from the agreed-upon decisive texts, as well as the gored animal and the one eaten by a wild animal that has lost its life by goring and eating. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And the goring. The goring is in the sense of its object, and it is a sheep that is gored by another or something else and dies before it is slaughtered. Some people interpreted the goring to mean the goring because two sheep may butt heads and die. It was said: Natiha and did not say Natih. The correct form of fa’il is that the ha’ is not mentioned in it, just as it is said: a dyed palm and a greasy beard. However, the ha’ was mentioned here because the ha’ is only deleted from fa’ilah if it is an attribute of a described word. It is said: a goring sheep and a slain woman. If the described word is not mentioned, the ha’ is retained, so you say: I saw the slain woman of Banu Fulan, and this is the goring of the sheep. Because if you did not mention the ha’ and said: I saw the slain woman of Banu Fulan, it is not known whether he is a man or a woman. Abu Maysarah read: and the one who was gored. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And what the wild beast has eaten means everything that has fangs and claws that has been preyed upon by an animal with fangs and claws, such as a lion, fox, wolf, hyena, and the like. These are all wild beasts. It is said: So-and-so bit so-and-so meaning he bit him with a tooth, and sab’a means he attacked him and fell into him. In the speech there is an implied meaning, and what the wild beast has eaten because what the wild beast has eaten has perished. Some Arabs stop the name of the wild beast at the lion, and if the Arabs took a sheep and then it was freed from it, they would eat it. Likewise, if it ate some of it, as Qatada and others said. Al-Hasan and Abu Haywah read the word sab’a with a silent ba’ and it is a language of the people of Najd. Hassan said about Utbah ibn Abi Lahab: Whoever returns to his family this year, the lion will not eat the one who returns. Ibn Masoud read: And the lions ate it. Abdullah bin Abbas read: And the lions ate it. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: Except what you have slaughtered is an accusative of the connected exception according to the majority of scholars and jurists, and it refers to everything that was slaughtered from the mentioned and in which there is life, because slaughter is effective in it because the right of the exception is to be directed to what came before from the speech, and it is not made disconnected except by evidence that must be accepted. Ibn Uyaynah, Sharik and Jarir narrated on the authority of Al-Rukayn bin Al-Rabi’ on the authority of Abu Talha Al-Asadi, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about a wolf that attacked a sheep and split its belly open until its ribs fell out, and it reached its slaughter and slaughtered it, so he said: Eat, and do not eat what fell out of its ribs. Ishaq bin Rahawayh said: The Sunnah regarding the sheep is as Ibn Abbas described, for even if its intestines come out, it is still alive, and the place of slaughter is safe from it. Rather, it is looked at when slaughtering whether it is alive or dead, and it is not looked at whether it lives like it, and the same is true for the sick. Ishaq said: Whoever contradicts this has contradicted the Sunnah from the majority of the Companions and the majority of scholars. I said: Ibn Habeeba went to this and mentioned on the authority of Asbah Malik, it is the opinion of Ibn Wahb and the most famous of the Shafi’i school of thought. Al-Muzani said: I remember another opinion of Al-Shafi’i that it is not eaten if it reaches seven years of age or falls to a state with no life, and it is the opinion of the Medinans, and the most famous of the Maliki opinion is what Abdul Wahhab mentioned in his Taliqa, and it was narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, Malik mentioned it in his Muwatta’ and Ismail Al-Qadi and a group of Malikis from Baghdad went to it, and the exception to this opinion is disconnected, meaning these things are forbidden to you, but what you slaughtered is what was not forbidden. Ibn Al-Arabi said: Malik’s opinion differed regarding these things, so it was narrated on his authority that nothing is eaten except what was slaughtered with the slaughter of a healthy animal, and what is in the Muwatta’ is that if he slaughtered it and its soul was running and it was agitated, then let it be eaten, and this is the correct opinion of his opinion that he wrote with his own hand and read to the people of every country throughout his life, so it is more appropriate than the rare narrations. Our scholars have stated regarding the sick animal that the doctrine is permissible to slaughter it even if it is on the verge of death if there is some life left in it, and I wonder what is the difference between the rest of life from Illness and the rest of the life of seven if the view is consistent and the thought is free from doubt! Abu Omar said: They have agreed in the case of a sick animal whose life is not expected that slaughtering it is a form of ritual slaughter for it if it was alive at the time of slaughtering it, and this is known from what they mentioned of the movement of its hand, foot, tail, or the like. They have agreed that if it is in the throes of death and does not move a hand or foot, then there is no ritual slaughter for it. And this is how it should be, by analogy, the ruling on the one who has fallen and what was mentioned with it in the verse, and God knows best. Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: You have slaughtered. In the speech of the Arabs, slaughtering means slaughter. This was said by Qatrib. Ibn Sidah said in Al-Muhkam: The Arabs say, The slaughter of the two sides is the slaughter of its mother. Ibn Atiyah said: This is only a hadith, and slaughtering an animal means slaughtering it. From this is the saying of the poet: Stimulated by the style I said: The hadith that I referred to was narrated by Al-Daraqutni on the authority of Abu Saeed, Abu Hurairah, Ali, and Abdullah bin “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The slaughter of the fetus is the slaughter of its mother.” This is what the majority of scholars say, except for what was narrated from Abu Hanifa, who said: If the fetus comes out of its mother’s womb dead, it is not permissible to eat it, because the slaughter of one soul cannot be the slaughter of two souls. Ibn al-Mundhir said: “The saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The slaughter of the fetus is the slaughter of its mother,” is evidence that the fetus is not the mother. He said: If a pregnant slave woman is freed, his emancipation is the emancipation of his mother. This requires that his slaughter is the slaughter of his mother, because if he allows that the emancipation of one person is the emancipation of two, then it is permissible that the slaughter of one person is the slaughter of two, based on the report from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what came from his companions, and what most people agree on, which is sufficient without the opinion of any speaker. The scholars agreed that if the fetus comes out alive, the slaughter of its mother is not its slaughter. They differed if the mother is slaughtered and a fetus is from her womb. Malik and all his companions said that its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother if its creation has been completed and its hair has grown, and this is if it comes out dead or a breath of life has left it. However, it is recommended that he slaughter it if it starts moving, and if it beats them to it, he eats. Ibn Al-Qasim said: I sacrificed a sheep, and when I slaughtered it, its offspring started running in its belly, so I ordered them to leave it until it died in its belly. Then I ordered them to cut open its belly and take it out, so I slaughtered it and blood flowed from it, so I ordered my family to roast it. Abdullah bin Kaab bin Malik said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: If the fetus has hair, then its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: Whoever said its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother and did not mention hair or not hair, Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq. Judge Abu Al-Walid Al-Baji said: It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The slaughter of the fetus is the slaughter of its mother, whether it is hairy or not. However, it is a weak hadith, so the Maliki school of thought is the correct one, which is the opinion of most of the jurists of the countries. And success comes from God. Ninth - The Almighty’s saying: You have slaughtered. The root of slaughter in the language is completion, and from it comes the completion of age and the slaughtered horse that comes after the completion of the sores by a year, and that is the completion of the strength. It is said: Dhaka yadki and the Arabs say: The running of the slaughtered animals is overwhelming, and intelligence is the sharpness of the heart. The poet said: It is preferable if they strive to do so, and he is of full age and of sound mind. Intelligence is quick wit, and the verb from it is dhaka yathki dhakhan, and dhakawah is what you stoke the fire with, and dhakawa war and fire ignited them, and dhaka is the name of the sun, because it stokes like fire, and the morning is the son of dhakaa because it is from its light, so the meaning of dhakatum is that you have realized its slaughtering completely. Dhakatu adh-Dhabiha adhakahu, derived from tatayyib, it is said that the smell of a dhaka, so if an animal’s blood flows, it has become fragrant because it dries quickly, and in the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ali, may God be pleased with them both, The slaughtering of the earth is its dryness, meaning its purification from impurity, so the slaughtering of the slaughtered animal is its purification and permission to eat it, so he made the dryness of the earth after the impurity a purification for it and permission to pray in it like the slaughtering of the slaughtered animal, and it is the saying of the people of Iraq, and if this is established, then know that in the Sharia it is an expression of the flowing of blood and the rupture of the jugular veins in the slaughtered animal and the slaughtering of the slaughtered animal and the hamstringing of the unattainable, coupled with the intention of intending for God and remembering Him over it, as will be explained. Tenth - The scholars differed regarding what constitutes slaughter. The majority of scholars agree that everything that ruptures the jugular vein and causes blood to flow is a tool for slaughter, except for the tooth and bone. This is what the reports have been transmitted and the jurists of the countries have said. The tooth and nail that are forbidden in slaughter are those that are not removed because that would result in strangulation. Ibn Abbas also said: That is strangulation. As for those that are removed, if they rupture the jugular vein, then slaughtering with them is permissible according to them. Some people disliked the tooth, nail, and bone in any case, whether they are removed or not, including Ibrahim, Al-Hasan, Al-Layth bin Saad, and it was narrated on the authority of Al-Shafi’i. Their proof is the apparent hadith of Rafi’ bin Khadij, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, we will meet the enemy tomorrow and we do not have a knife with us, so we slaughter with a stick. In the Muwatta of Malik, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Muadh bin Sa’d or Sa’d bin Muadh. A slave girl of Ka’b ibn Malik was tending his sheep in Sal’a. One of her sheep was injured and hit by a stone. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about that and he said: There is nothing wrong with it, eat it. And in Musannaf Abi Dawud. We slaughter with a marble and a piece of a stick, he said, “Hurry up and make a sound that makes the blood flow and mention the name of God over it. Eat, except for the tooth and the nail. I will tell you. As for the tooth, it is a bone, and as for the nail, it is the edge of the Ethiopian.” The hadith was narrated by Muslim. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab that he said: What is slaughtered with a hilt, a shatir, or a dharr is a stallion that is slaughtered with a hilt, and it is possible to slaughter and slit its throat with it. The shatir is a piece of a stick, and it is possible to slaughter with it because it has a thin side. The dharr is a piece of a stone, and it is possible to slaughter with it, but it is not possible to slit its throat. The opposite is the shazaz, and it is used to slaughter with it because it is like the tip of a spear, but it is not possible to slaughter with it. Eleventh - Malik and a group said: Slaughter is not valid unless the throat and jugular veins are cut. Al-Shafi’i said: It is valid if the throat and esophagus are cut, and the jugular veins are not needed because they are the passages of food and drink, without which there is no life, and this is the purpose of death. Malik and others considered death in a way that makes the meat taste good and separates the permissible - which is the meat - from the forbidden, which is taken out by cutting the jugular veins. This is the school of Abu Hanifa, and the hadith of Rafi’ ibn Khadij indicates this in his statement: That which causes blood to flow. The people of Baghdad reported from Malik that he stipulated cutting four things: the throat, the jugular veins, and the esophagus, which is the opinion of Abu Thawr. The well-known view is what was mentioned above, which is the opinion of Al-Layth. Then our companions differed about cutting one of the jugular veins and the throat, is it considered slaughter or not, according to two opinions. Twelfth - The scholars agreed that the slaughter, whatever it is in the throat below the gill, has completed the slaughter. There is a difference of opinion as to whether if it is slaughtered above it and it passes through to the body, is that slaughter or not, with two opinions: It has been narrated from Malik that it is not eaten. Likewise, if he slaughtered it from the nape and completed the cut and caused the blood to flow and cut the throat and jugular veins, it is not eaten. Al-Shafi’i said: It is eaten because the purpose has been achieved. This is based on a principle, which is that even if the purpose of slaughter is the blood, there is a kind of worship in it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered in the throat and slaughtered in the heart and said: Slaughter is in the throat and the heart. So he explained its location and specified its location and said, explaining its benefit: Whatever blood flows and the name of God is mentioned over it, then eat it. If that is neglected and it is not done with intention, nor is it stipulated or with a specific description, then the share of worship is lost from it, so it is not eaten for that reason, and God knows best. Thirteenth - They differed regarding the one who raised his hand before completing the slaughtering, then returned immediately and completed the slaughtering. It was said: It is sufficient for him, and it was said: It is not sufficient for him. The first is more correct because he wounded her and mentioned her slaughtering after it, and her life was collected in her. Fourteenth - It is recommended that one not slaughter an animal whose condition is satisfactory, or one who is able to do so and who has done it according to his Sunnah, whether male or female, adult or not, it is permissible to slaughter it if it is a Muslim or a person of the People of the Book, and the slaughter of a Muslim is better than the slaughter of a person of the People of the Book, and no one slaughters a sacrificial animal except a Muslim, for if the sacrificial animal is slaughtered by a person of the People of the Book, then there is a difference of opinion about it and it is not permissible in order to obtain the doctrine, and what is more similar has permitted it. Fifteenth - And what is strange among humans, it is not permissible to slaughter it except as is permissible to slaughter it among humans, and according to the statement of Malik and his companions, Rabi’ah, and Al-Layth bin Sa’d, and likewise the one who falls into a well, slaughtering it is not permissible except in what is between the throat and the core according to the Sunnah of slaughter, and some of the people of Medina differed in these two issues and others, and in the chapter there is the hadith of Rafi’ bin Khadij, which was presented and its completion after his statement: And the extent of Abyssinia he said: And we seized a plunder of camels and sheep, and a camel ran away from it, and a man shot it with an arrow and detained it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: These camels have escape routes like wild animals, so if one of them overtakes you, do with it like this - and in another narration - and eat it. Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i said the same. Al-Shafi’i said: The Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, giving him authority to do this action is evidence that it is slaughter, and he provided evidence for what Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Ashra’ on the authority of his father, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, is slaughtering only for the right and the core? He said: If you were to stab it in the thigh, it would suffice for you. Yazid bin Harun said: It is an authentic hadith that Ahmad bin Hanbal liked and narrated it on the authority of Abu Dawud and advised those of the hadith masters who came to him to write it down. Abu Dawud said: This is only valid for the one who falls into a precipice and the wild. Ibn Habib interpreted this hadith as meaning that it fell into a precipice and its slaughter cannot be reached except by stabbing it in a place other than the place of slaughter. This is a statement that he made uniquely from Malik and his companions. Abu Omar said: The statement of Al-Shafi’i is more apparent among the people of knowledge and that it is eaten with what a wild animal is eaten with, according to the hadith of Rafi’ bin Khadij, and it is the statement of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas’ud. From the standpoint of analogy, since if a wild animal is able to be eaten, it is not permissible except with what a human is able to be eaten with, because it has become possible for it to be eaten, so it should be according to analogy if it becomes wild or becomes like a wild animal in terms of being unable to eat, that it is permissible with what a wild animal is permissible for it. I said: Our scholars responded to the hadith of Rafi’ ibn Khadij by saying: The Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) authority was only to imprison him, not to slaughter him, and this is what the hadith requires and is apparent from his saying: So he imprisoned him, and he did not say that the arrow killed him. Also, it is possible to do so in most cases, so the rare cases are not taken into account, and this only happens in hunting. The hadith clearly states that the arrow imprisoned him, and after it became imprisoned, it became possible to do so, so it is not eaten except by slaughtering and slitting the throat. And God knows best. As for the hadith of Abu al-‘Ashra, al-Tirmidhi said about it: It is a strange hadith that we do not know except from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, and we do not know this hadith of Abu al-‘Ashra from his father. They differed about the name of Abu al-‘Ashra. Some of them said: His name is Asman ibn Qahtam, and it is said: His name is Yasar ibn Barz, and it is said: Balz, and it is said - his name is Attarid, attributed to his grandfather. This is an unknown chain of transmission that is not an argument, and even if its authenticity were accepted, as Yazid ibn Harun said, there would be no argument in it, since its implication is the permissibility of slaughtering any organ, absolutely, in what is possible and otherwise, and no one says this about what is possible. Its apparent meaning is definitely not what is intended, and the interpretation of Abu Dawud and Ibn Habib is not agreed upon, so it is not an argument, and God knows best. Abu Omar said: Malik’s argument is that they agreed that if a human being did not call out that he is not slaughtered except with what is slaughtered with what is within his power, then they differed, so it is based on his principle until they agree, and there is no argument in this because their consensus was only based on what is within his power, and this is not within his power. And the completion of this chapter is his saying, peace be upon him: “God has prescribed kindness in all things. So when you kill, kill in the best way, and when you slaughter, slaughter in the best way. Let one of you sharpen his blade and let his slaughtered animal rest.” Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Shaddad ibn Aws, who said: “Two things I have memorized from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: God has prescribed and mentioned them.” Our scholars said: Kindness in slaughtering animals means being gentle with them, not throwing them violently or dragging them from one place to another, sharpening the tool, having the intention of permissibility and offering the sacrifice, directing it towards the Qiblah, finishing it, cutting the jugular vein and the throat, resting it and leaving it until it cools, acknowledging God’s favor, and thanking Him for the blessing that He has subjected to us what if He had willed, He would have made permissible for us what if He had willed, He would have forbidden us. Rabi’ah said: Kindness in slaughtering does not include slaughtering one animal while another is looking at it. It was narrated that Malik permitted it, and the first is better. As for kind killing, it is general in everything from slaughtering, retaliation, prescribed punishments, and others. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the devil’s sash. Ibn Issa added in his hadith: It is the one that is slaughtered, cut, without its jugular veins being slit, then left to die. Seventeenth - The Almighty’s saying: And what was slaughtered on altars. Ibn Faris said: The altar is a stone that was erected to be worshipped and the blood of the sacrifices was poured on it. It is also the altar. The altars are stones that are erected around the edge of a well and are made into pillars and raised, erect dust. It was said: The altar is the plural of one al-Nasab like Himar and Himar. It was said: It is a singular noun and the plural is Ansaab and there were three hundred and sixty stones. Talhah read al-Nasab with the Jazm of the Sad. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar al-Nasab with the Fatha of the Nun and the Jazm of the Sad. Al-Jahdari read the Fatha of the Nun and the Sad and made it a unified noun like the mountain and the camel. The plural is Ansaab like camels and generations. Mujahid said: They are stones that were around Mecca on which they slaughtered. Ibn Jurayj said: The Arabs used to slaughter in Mecca and cook with blood whatever came from the House and they would cut up the meat and place it on the stones. When Islam came, the Muslims said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We are more deserving of honoring this House with these actions. It was as if he, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not dislike that, so God Almighty revealed: Their meat will not reach God, nor will they. Its bloods” (al-Hajj 22:37) and it was revealed: And what was slaughtered on altars meaning: The intention in it is to glorify the altars, not that slaughtering on them is not permissible. Al-A’sha said: And this erected monument, do not inhabit it for the sake of well-being, and worship God. It was said: On means for its sake. Qatrib said: Ibn Zayd said: What is slaughtered on altars and what is dedicated to other than God are one thing. Ibn Atiyah said: What is slaughtered on altars is part of what is dedicated to other than God, but it was specifically mentioned after its kind because of the fame of the matter, the honor of the place, and the reverence of souls for it. Eighteenth - The Almighty’s saying: And that you seek lots by arrows is connected to what precedes it, and that is in the nominative case, meaning that it is forbidden for you to seek lots by arrows, and arrows are the lots of gambling, the singular of which is zalam and zalam. He said: A young man is suffering from it like a man Another said: If Juthayma killed its leaders, its women will strike with arrows. Muhammad bin Jarir mentioned: Ibn Wakee’ told them on the authority of his father on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Abu Haseen on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: that the arrows were white pebbles that they used to play with. Muhammad bin Jarir said: Sufyan bin Wakee’ told us: It is chess. As for the saying of Labid: Her followers slip from the ground They said: He meant the hooves of a wild cow, and the Arabs have three types of arrows. Three of them were taken by each person for himself, one of which he would do and the other one he would not do, and the third was neglected and nothing was due on him, so he would put it in a map with him. So if he wanted to do something, he would put his hand in - and they are similar - and if one of them came out, he would follow the order and finish according to what came out for him. If the arrow that had nothing due on it came out, he would repeat the striking. This is what Suraqa bin Malik bin Ja'sham struck with when he followed the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Abu Bakr at the time of the migration. This action was called istisqa because they used it to cast lots for provisions and what they wanted, just as it is said: istisqa' in calling for water. Similar to what God the Most High has forbidden is the astrologer's saying: Do not go out for the sake of such and such a star, and go out for the sake of such and such a star. God the Almighty said: And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow (Luqman 31:34) and the verse: And a full explanation of this will come, God willing. The second type - seven arrows were with Hubal in the interior of the Kaaba, on which were written the calamities that were going on among the people, each arrow was in a book, in which there was an arrow in it, from the matter of blood money, and in another from you and in another from others, and in another attached, and in the rest of them were the rulings on water and other things, and they were the ones that Abdul Muttalib struck his sons with when he vowed to slaughter one of them when they completed ten, the famous story mentioned by Ibn Ishaq, and these seven were also with every soothsayer of the soothsayers of the Arabs and their rulers, in the same way that they were in the Kaaba with Hubal. The third type is the dice of gambling, which are ten, seven of which have luck, and three are squandered, and they were played with for gambling, amusement and play. Their wise men intended to feed the poor and the needy in the winter and the bitter cold, and it was difficult to make a diversion. Mujahid said: The azlaam are the Persian and Roman dice with which they gamble. Sufyan and Waki’ said: It is chess. So casting lots with all of this is seeking a share and a portion, as we have explained. It is from eating money unjustly, and it is forbidden. And every gamble with pigeons, dice, chess, or other such fodder is casting lots with what is in the meaning of the dice, and it is all forbidden. It is a type of divination and exposing oneself to the claim of knowledge of the unseen. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: For this reason, our companions forbade the things that astrologers do on the roads, such as the arrows they have with them and the omens’ notes and the like. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: God only forbade them with regard to matters of the unseen, because no soul knows what will happen to it tomorrow. So the dice have no definition. The unseen has an effect, so some of the ignorant people inferred from this a response to Al-Shafi’i regarding the casting of lots among the slaves in emancipation. This ignorant person did not know that what Al-Shafi’i said was based on authentic narrations and is not something that can be objected to by prohibiting drawing lots with arrows, because emancipation is a legal ruling, and it is permissible for the law to make the casting of lots a sign of proving the ruling of emancipation to cut off the dispute or for an interest that it sees, and that is not equal to the saying of the one who says: If you do such and such or say such and such, then that will guide you to a matter in the future, so it is not permissible to make the casting of lots a sign of something that will be renewed in the future, and it is permissible to make the casting of lots a sign of emancipation for sure, so the separation of the two matters became apparent. Nineteenth - This chapter does not seek omens. And “may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, he liked to hear ‘O Rashid, O Najih.’” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, who said: Hadith: Authentic Hadith: Strange. He liked the omen because it made the soul happy and felt good about the fulfillment of a need and the attainment of hope. So he had good thoughts about God Almighty. He said: I am as my servant thinks of me. And peace be upon him, he hated superstitions, because they are among the actions of the polytheists and because they bring about bad thoughts about God Almighty. Al-Khattabi said: The difference between a good omen and a superstition is that a good omen is only a way of thinking well of God, while a superstition is only a way of relying on something other than Him. Al-Asma’i said: I asked Ibn ‘Awn about a good omen, and he said: It is that he is sick and hears, O you who are healthy, or he is a seeker and hears, O you who are well. This is the meaning of the hadith of Al-Tirmidhi. And in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no bad omen, and the best of it is a good omen. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is a good omen? He said: A righteous word that one of you hears. The meaning of bad omen will be further explained, God willing. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Darda’, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Knowledge is achieved by learning and patience is achieved by patience. Whoever seeks good will be given it. Whoever avoids evil will be protected from it. Three will not attain the highest degrees: one who practices divination, or casts lots, or returns from a journey based on bad omen. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth - The Almighty’s saying: “That is transgression” is an indication of casting lots with arrows, and transgression is going out. It has been said that it goes back to everything he mentioned about making all of these prohibitions permissible, and everything from them is transgression and has gone from the permissible to the forbidden, and refraining from these prohibitions is from fulfilling contracts, as he said: Fulfill contracts. Twenty-one - The Almighty said: Today those who disbelieved have despaired of [defeating] your religion, meaning that you would return to your religion as disbelievers. Ad-Dahhak said: This verse was revealed when Mecca was conquered, and that was “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca on the eighth of Ramadan in the year nine, and it is said: the year eight, and he entered it and the herald of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out: Whoever says to him ‘There is no god but God’ is safe, and whoever puts down his weapon is safe, and whoever closes his door is safe.” There are two versions of Yaas: Ya’sa, ya’isa, ya’isa, and Aysa, ya’isa, iyas, and iyasa. An-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: So do not fear them, but fear Me, meaning do not fear them, and fear Me, for I am the One who is able to grant you victory. Twenty-second - The Almighty’s saying: This day I have perfected your religion for you. This is because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca, there was only the obligation of prayer alone. When he came to Medina, God revealed what was lawful and what was unlawful until he performed the Hajj. When he performed the Hajj and the religion was complete, this verse was revealed: This day I have perfected your religion for you. The verse, as we will explain, was narrated by the imams on the authority of Tariq bin Shihab, who said: A Jewish man came to Omar and said: O Commander of the Faithful, there is a verse in your book that you recite. If it had been revealed to us Jews, we would have taken that day as a festival. He said: Which verse? He said: This day, I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as your religion. Omar said: I know the day on which it was revealed and the place in which it was revealed. It was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Arafat on a Friday. The wording of Muslim and from al-Nasa’i: a Friday night. It was narrated that “when it was revealed on the day of the greater pilgrimage, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it: What makes you cry? He said: What makes me cry is that we used to have an increase in our religion, but now that it has been completed, nothing that is completed without being decreased. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You have spoken the truth. Mujahid narrated that this verse was revealed on the day of the conquest of Mecca. I said: The first statement is more correct, that it was revealed on a Friday, and it was the Day of Arafah after the afternoon prayer during the Farewell Pilgrimage in the year ten, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing in Arafah on his she-camel Al-Adhba’, and the she-camel’s shoulder almost broke from its weight, so it knelt down. A day can be expressed by part of it as a whole, and likewise a month can be expressed by part of it. You say, “We did such-and-such in such-and-such a month, and such-and-such in such-and-such a year.” It is known that you did not include the month or the year, and this is used in the language of the Arabs and the non-Arabs. Religion is an expression for the laws that were honored and opened up to us, for they were revealed in parts, and the last of them was this verse, and no ruling was revealed after it, as Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi said. The majority said: What is meant is most of the obligations, what is permissible and what is forbidden. They said: Much of the Qur’an was revealed after that, and the verse on usury was revealed, and the verse on kalalah was revealed, and so on. Most of the religion and the matter of Hajj were only completed, because no polytheist circumambulated with them in this year, and no one circumambulated the House naked, and all the people stood at Arafat, and it was said: I have completed your religion for you by destroying your enemy for you and making your religion prevail over all religion, just as you say: We have achieved what we want if you have protected your enemy. Twenty-third - The Almighty’s saying: And I have completed My favor upon you, meaning by completing the laws and rulings and making the religion of Islam flourish, as I promised you when I said: And to complete My favor upon you, which is entering Mecca in safety and security, and other than that, what this pure religion has organized until entering Paradise in the mercy of God Almighty. Twenty-fourth - Perhaps someone will say: The Almighty’s statement: This day I have perfected your religion for you indicates that the religion was once complete, and that requires that all of the Muhajireen and Ansar who died, and those who witnessed Badr and Al-Hudaybiyah and pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) both pledges, and sacrificed themselves for God despite the great trials that befell them, died with an incomplete religion, and that the Messenger of God (may God’s peace and blessings be upon him) was calling people to an incomplete religion. It is known that deficiency is a defect and the religion of God Almighty is upright, as God Almighty said: A straight religion (al-An’am 6:161). The answer is to say to him: Why did you say that every deficiency is a defect, and what is your evidence for that? Then it is said to him: Do you see the deficiency of a month, is it a defect? And the deficiency of the prayer of a traveler, is it a defect for it? And the deficiency of the lifespan that God intended in His statement: And no one lives long, nor does his lifespan decrease (Fatir 35:11) is it a defect for him? And the deficiency of the days of menstruation from what is known, and the deficiency of the days of pregnancy, and the deficiency of wealth due to theft or fire or… Drowning if its owner is not poor, and what you deny is that the deficiency of parts of religion in the Sharia before the remaining parts are completed in the knowledge of God Almighty, this is not ugly or defective, and what you deny is that the meaning of God Almighty’s saying: Today I have perfected your religion for you is taken out in two ways: One of them is that what is meant by his reaching is the maximum limit that he had with me in what I decreed and determined. This does not necessitate that what came before that be deficient in the form of a defect, but it is Joseph with a restricted deficiency, so it is said to him: He was deficient in what he had with God Almighty, that it is attached to him and joined to him, like a man whom God makes reach one hundred years, so it is said: God completed his lifespan. It is not necessary for that to mean that his lifespan when he was sixty was deficient... in the form of a deficiency, shortcoming, and defect. “For the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: Whoever God has given him a life of sixty years has been excused for his lifespan. However, it is permissible to describe him as deficient in a restricted manner, so it is said: He was deficient in what was with God the Most High, that He conveyed it to him and made him live to Him. God has made the noon, afternoon, and evening prayers four rak’ahs. If it is said at that time that He completed them, the statement would be correct, and it is not necessary that when they were two rak’ahs they were deficient, deficient, or flawed. If it is said: They were deficient in what was with God, that He added them to it and added to it, that would be correct. This is how it is in the laws of Islam and what was legislated from them, little by little, until God completed the religion to its end, which was with Him. And God knows best. The other aspect is that he meant by his saying: “Today I have perfected your religion for you” that he guided them to the Hajj, which was the only pillar of religion that remained for them, so they performed the Hajj and thus the religion was fulfilled for them by performing its pillars and fulfilling its obligation, for he, peace be upon him, says: Islam was built on five pillars “The hadith. They had testified, prayed, paid zakat, fasted, fought and performed Umrah, but they had not performed Hajj. When they performed Hajj that day on behalf of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, God Almighty revealed: And while they were standing on the eve of Arafah, “This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you.” He only wanted to eat and put it for them. In that is evidence that all acts of obedience are religion, faith and Islam. Twenty-fifth: The Almighty’s statement: And I have approved for you Islam as a religion. That is, I have informed you of My approval of it for you as a religion, for the Almighty has always been pleased with Islam as a religion. So there is no benefit in the specificity of approval for that day if we take it literally. Religion is an accusative of specification, or if you wish, as a second object. It has been said that the meaning is: And I have approved for you Islam as a religion. That is, I have approved of your Islam that you are upon today, a religion that remains in its entirety until the end of the verse, and I do not abrogate anything from it, and God knows best. And Islam in this verse is that which is in the statement of the Almighty: Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam. (Al Imran 3:19), and it is what is explained in Gabriel’s question to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon them both, and it is faith, deeds, and people. Twenty-sixth - The Almighty’s saying: But whoever is forced by famine means whoever is forced by necessity to eat dead meat and other forbidden things. In this verse, famine is hunger and an empty stomach of food, and emaciation is a shriveled stomach. A man is called khamis and khamisan, and a woman is called khamisa and khamisana. From this comes the word akhmas al-qadam, and it is often used to mean hunger and emaciation. Al-A’sha said: You spend the winter with your stomachs full, while your neighbors go to bed hungry. Those who are hungry have shriveled up stomachs. Al-Nabigha said about the shriveled stomach due to its shriveling up: The belly is soft and round, and the throat is bulging with a firm breast. In the hadith: Those with thin stomachs and light backs. Al-Khamas is the plural of Khamis Al-Batn, which means thin. He said that they are exempt from people’s money, and from this is the hadith: The birds go out hungry in the morning and return with full crops in the evening. The khamīsah is also a garment. Al-Asma’i said: The khamīs are embroidered silk or woolen garments, and they are black and were part of people’s clothing. The meaning of necessity and its ruling were mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. Twenty-seventh - The Almighty’s saying: not inclined to sin meaning not inclined to what is forbidden, and it means not transgressing nor exceeding limits (al-Baqarah 2:173). It has been mentioned before and incline means inclination, and sin is forbidden, and from it is the saying of Omar, may God be pleased with him, We did not incline to sin meaning we did not incline nor did we intentionally while we knew it. And everyone who inclined is inclined and inclined. Al-Nakha’i, Yahya bin Waththab, and Al-Salami read mutajnaff without an alif, and it is more eloquent in meaning, because the emphasis on the ‘ayn requires exaggeration and delving into the meaning and establishing its ruling, and the verb ta’afa’al is to imitate the thing and draw near to it. Do you not see that if you say: the branch swayed, then that requires deliberation and approaching inclination, and if you say: it leans, then the ruling of inclination is established? And likewise the man is protected and protected and rational, so the meaning is not intentionally committing a sin in his goal, as Qatada and Al-Shafi’i said, For God is Forgiving and Merciful meaning for God is Forgiving and Merciful, so he deleted it, and Sibawayh recited: Umm Al-Khayar has come to accuse me of a sin that I have not heeded. He wanted to say I did not make it, but he deleted it. God knows best.
5:4: It contains eighteen issues: First: The Almighty’s saying, They ask you, the verse was revealed because of Adi bin Hatim and Zaid bin Muhalhil, who is Zaid al-Khayl, whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Zaid al-Khair. They said: O Messenger of God, we are a people who hunt dogs and falcons, and dogs take cows, donkeys, and gazelles. Some of them we are able to slaughter, and some of them they kill but we are not able to slaughter. God has forbidden dead animals, so what is permissible for us? So the verse was revealed. The second - the Almighty’s saying: “What is lawful for them? Say: Lawful for you are the good things.” What is in the nominative case as the subject and the predicate is lawful for them. And that is redundant, and if you wish, it can mean which, and the predicate is “Say: Lawful for you are the good things,” which is the lawful, and everything that is forbidden is not good. It was said: What the eater and drinker enjoy and there is no harm in it for him in this world or in the hereafter. It was said: The good things are the slaughtered animals, because they became good through slaughter. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And what you have known meaning and hunting what you have known, so there is an unavoidable implication in the speech, and if it were not for it, the meaning would require that the solution asked about be available to the trained hunting dogs, and that is not the doctrine of Ahmad: for the one who permits the meat of the hunted does not specify the permission for the trained, and what the scholars have said about eating the dog in livestock will come, God willing. Some of those who wrote about the rulings of the Qur’an mentioned that the verse indicates that permission includes what we have known of the hunting dogs, and this includes the dog and all the hunting birds, and that necessitates the permission for all forms of benefit, so it indicates the permissibility of selling the dog and the hunting birds and benefiting from them in all forms of benefit except what the evidence specifies, which is eating from the hunting dogs, meaning the hunting dogs and the wild birds, and Adi had five dogs that he named with proper names, and the names of his dogs were Salhab, Ghaleb, Al-Mukhtalis, and Al-Mutanaas, and Al-Suhayli said, and the fifth, I am not sure about it, he said Akhtab, or he said about it Wathab. Fourth: The nation has agreed that if the dog is not black and a Muslim has taught it, it will run away if it is let off and respond if it is called, and it will be deterred after it has caught the prey if it is deterred, and that it will not eat from the prey it has hunted, and it has caused it injury or a wound, and a Muslim hunts with it and mentions the name of God when sending it, then its prey is valid and may be eaten, there is no disagreement. If one of these conditions is violated, then disagreement enters. If what it hunts with is not a dog, such as a cheetah and the like, or a hawk, a falcon, and similar birds, then the majority of the nation is of the opinion that everything that hunts after being trained is a predatory, earning animal. It is said: So-and-so wounded and earned if he earned, and from this comes the word jarha because it is earned by it, and from it comes the word “jara... evil deeds. Al-A’sha said: This is a mighty man whose mark reminds the wounded of what he has done. In the revelation: “And He knows what you have committed during the day” (al-An’am 6:60), and He said: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they are evil? (al-Jathiyah 45:21). Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: Makleebeen means Makleebeen are the owners of dogs, and he is like the one who disciplines, the one who disciplines. It was said: Its meaning is harmful to the hunted as dogs are harmed. Al-Rumani said: Both sayings are possible, and there is no evidence in Makleebeen that hunting with dogs is only permitted, because it is like his saying: believing, even though he insisted on it by limiting the permission to dogs only. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, in what Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated on his authority, he said: As for what is hunted with falcons and other birds, whatever you find slaughtered, slaughter it and it is permissible for you, otherwise do not feed it. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: Abu Jaafar was asked about the falcon, is its hunting permissible? He said: No, unless you know its slaughter. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said: And what you have trained of birds of prey to hunt refers to dogs in particular. If the dog is black and white, then Al-Hasan, Qatadah and An-Nakha’i disliked hunting it. Ahmad said: I do not know anyone who permitted it if it was white, and Ishaq bin Rahawayh said the same. As for the common people of knowledge in Medina and Kufa, they consider it permissible to hunt any trained dog. As for those who forbade hunting black dogs, “it is because of the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The black dog is a devil. Narrated by Muslim. The majority of scholars have used the generality of the verse as evidence, and they have also used as evidence the permissibility of hunting falcons as evidence for what was mentioned as the reason for revelation and what was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about hunting falcons, and he said: Whatever is held back from you, eat it. In its chain of transmission is Mujalid, and it is not known except from his side, and it is weak. In meaning, everything that comes from a dog comes from a cheetah, for example, so there is no difference except in what has no role in influence. This is the analogy in the meaning of the origin, like the analogy of a sword to a knife and a female slave to a male slave, and it has been mentioned previously. Sixth - If this is established, then know that the hunter must intend, when sending, to slaughter and permit it, and there is no disagreement about this, “because of his saying, peace be upon him: If you send your dog and mention the name of God over it, then eat it. This requires intention and saying the name of God. If he intended to do so for fun, then Malik disliked it and Ibn Abd al-Hakam permitted it. This is the apparent meaning of al-Layth’s statement: “I have never seen a truth more similar to falsehood than it,” meaning hunting. However, if he did it without the intention of slaughtering it, then it is forbidden because it is a form of corruption and killing an animal for no benefit. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade killing an animal except for food.” The majority of scholars have held that saying the name of God is essential when sending it, based on his statement: And mentioning the name of God. If it is not found in any way, then the hunt is not eaten. This is the view of the scholars of the apparent meaning and the group of the people of hadith. A group of our companions and others have held that it is permissible to eat what a Muslim hunts and slaughters even if he intentionally left out saying the name of God. They interpreted the command to say the name of God as recommended. Malik, in the well-known view, held that there is a difference between leaving out the name of God intentionally or by mistake, and said: It is not eaten if done intentionally, but it is eaten if done by mistake. This is the view of the jurists of the regions and one of the two views of al-Shafi’i. This issue will come in the chapter on livestock, God willing. Then it is essential. If the dog is sent out by the right hand, such that he has its reins in his hand, so he releases it and entices it towards it, so it is sent out, or if the hunter is still and sees the prey, so it does not move towards it except by the enticement of the hunter, then this is like someone who has its reins in his hand and releases it enticing it according to one of the two opinions. But if the hunter is sent out of his own accord, without being sent out or enticed, then it is not permissible to hunt it and it is not permissible to eat it according to the majority, Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr and the people of opinion, because he only hunted for himself without being sent out and held on to it, and the hunter had no role in it, so sending him out is not attributed to him, because the Prophet, peace be upon him, is not to be believed in the words: If you send your trained dog out. And Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah and Al-Awza’i said: Its prey is eaten if it was taken out to hunt. Seventh - The majority read I learned with the opening of the ‘ayn and the lam, and Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah with the closing of the ‘ayn and the breaking of the lam, meaning from the matter of the birds of prey and hunting with them, and the birds of prey are the earners, and the human organs are called birds of prey because they earn and act, and it was said: they are called birds of prey because they injure and bleed, so it is taken from the wound, and this is weak and the linguists are against it, and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated it from a group and Mukalibeen the reading of the majority with the opening of the kaf and the emphasis on the lam, and the mukalib is the teacher of dogs and their harm, and it is said to the one who teaches other than the dog: mukalib, because he returns that animal like a dog, some of them narrated it, and the hunter is called mukalib, so on this its meaning is hunters, and it was said: the mukalib is the owner of dogs, it is said: dog, so he is mukalib and dogs, and al-Hasan read mukalibeen with the sukun of the kaf and the softening of the lam, and its meaning is the owners of dogs, it is said: the man walked and his livestock increased, and I became a dog, his dogs increased, and al-Asma’i recited: Every young man, even if he walks, will be enriched by death. Eighth - The Almighty said: You teach them from what God has taught you. The pronoun you is in consideration of the word al-jarih since it is the plural of al-jarih. There is no disagreement among scholars regarding two conditions for teaching, which are: that it obeys when commanded and that it is reprimanded when reprimanded. There is no disagreement regarding these two conditions in dogs and similar beasts of prey. There is disagreement regarding the birds that are hunted with it. The well-known view is that this is a condition for them according to the majority. Ibn Habib mentioned that it is not a condition for them to be reprimanded if reprimanded, because this does not usually happen in them. It is sufficient that they are commanded and obey. Rabi'ah said: What responds from them when called is the trained predator, because most animals by nature run away. Al-Shafi'i and the majority of scholars stipulated in teaching that it be held on its owner, but Malik did not stipulate this in the well-known view from him. Al-Shafi'i said: The trained one is the one who, if he robs it, accompanies it and if he calls it to return, it returns to him. He holds the prey on its owner and does not eat from it. If he does this repeatedly, the people of custom said: He became trained, so he is the teacher. Al-Shafi'i also said: And the Kufians said: Ashli. If he is caught and imprisoned and does that again and again, he will eat his catch the third time. Some scholars said: He should do that three times and his catch will be eaten the fourth time. Some of them said: If he does that once, he is a teacher and his catch will be eaten the second time. Ninth - The Almighty’s saying: So eat of what they catch for you meaning what they have kept for you. The scholars differed in its interpretation. Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Al-Nakha’i, Qatadah, Ibn Jubayr, Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, Ikrimah, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, Al-Nu’man and his companions said: The meaning is that he did not eat, but if he ate, what remained is not eaten, because he caught it for himself and did not catch it for his Lord. The cheetah according to Abu Hanifa and his companions is like the dog, and they did not stipulate this in birds, rather what was eaten from it is eaten.
