Sa’id ibn Abi Waqqas, Abdullah ibn Umar, Salman Al-Farsi and Abu Hurairah also said: The meaning is that if he ate, then if the predator eats, whether it is a dog, a cheetah or a bird, he eats what remains of the hunt, even if only a part remains. This is the opinion of Malik and all his companions, and it is the second opinion of Al-Shafi’i, and it is analogy. There is a hadith in this chapter with the same meaning as what we mentioned, one of them - the hadith of Adi regarding the trained dog: And if he eats, do not eat, for he only held it for himself. Narrated by Muslim II - Hadith of Abu Tha’labah Al-Khushani, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding hunting by a dog: If you send your dog and it mentions the name of God over you, then eat from it, and eat from it whatever your hand returns to you. Narrated by Abu Dawud and narrated on the authority of Adi, but it is not authentic. The correct one on his authority is the hadith of Muslim. When the two narrations contradicted each other, some of our companions and others sought to reconcile them, so they interpreted the hadith of prohibition as meaning abstinence and piety, and the hadith of permission as meaning permissibility. They said: Adi was given plenty of time, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, issued a fatwa to refrain from eating out of piety. Abu Tha’labah was in need, so he issued a fatwa to permit it. And God knows best. The correctness of this interpretation is indicated by his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith of Adi: “For I fear that you only refrained for your own sake.” This is the interpretation of our scholars. Abu Amri said in the book of Al-Istidhkar: This hadith of Adi contradicted the hadith of Abu Tha’labah, and it appears that the hadith of Abu Tha’labah abrogates it. So his saying, “Even if he eats, O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace,” he said, Even if he eats. I said: This is questionable because the date is unknown and combining the two hadiths is better if the date is not known, and God knows best. As for the companions of al-Shafi’i, they said: If the eating was due to extreme hunger from a dog, it should be eaten, otherwise it should not be eaten, because that is due to its poor teaching. It was narrated from a group of the Salaf that they differentiated between what a dog or a cheetah has eaten, so they forbade it, and what a hawk has eaten, so they permitted it. This was said by al-Nakha’i, al-Thawri, the people of opinion, and Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and they said: A dog or a cheetah can be beaten and reprimanded, but that is not possible for a bird. The limit of teaching it is that it should be called, so it must be left alone, so it is not possible for it to do more than that, and beating it will harm it. Tenth - The majority of scholars are of the opinion that if the animal that has a wound drinks the blood of the prey, then the prey may be eaten. Ata’ said: Drinking blood is not eating, and Al-Sha’bi and Sufyan Al-Thawri disliked eating that prey. There is no disagreement among them that the reason for permitting the prey, which is the animal that has wounded it, must be certain and not doubtful. If there is doubt, eating it is not permissible, and it is: Eleventh - If the hunter finds another dog with his dog, it is assumed that it was not sent by another hunter, and that it was only sent out in search of prey by its nature and soul, and there is no difference in this, “because of the saying of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: And if other dogs mix with it, then do not eat it. In one narration, “You named your dog and did not name anyone else.” But if another hunter sends it and the two dogs share in it, then it belongs to the two hunters and they are partners in it. So if one of the dogs kills its fighter and then the other comes, then it belongs to the one who killed its fighter. Likewise, it is not permissible to eat what was shot with an arrow and fell from a mountain or drowned in water, because of what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Adi: If you shoot your arrow, mention the name of God. If he is absent from you for a day and you find nothing but the trace of your arrow, then eat. But if you find someone drowning in the water, do not eat, for you do not know whether the water killed him or your arrow.” This is the text. Twelfth - If the game dies in the mouths of dogs without being bitten, it is not eaten because it died by strangulation, so it is similar to being slaughtered with a sharp knife, so it dies during slaughter before its throat is cut. If it is possible for him to take it from the birds of prey and slaughter it, but he does not do so until it dies, it is not eaten and he is negligent in slaughtering because it has become capable of being slaughtered, and the slaughter of one who is capable of being slaughtered differs from the slaughter of one who is not capable of being slaughtered. If he takes it and it dies before he takes out the knife or takes it while it is with him, it is permissible to eat it. If the knife is not with him and he is busy seeking it, it is not eaten. Al-Shafi’i said: There are two opinions regarding what the birds of prey have taken and it does not bleed. One of them is that it is not eaten until it is wounded, based on the Almighty’s saying: of the birds of prey, which is the opinion of Ibn al-Qasim. The other is that it is permissible, which is the opinion of Ashhab: If someone who has been bitten by a dog dies, it is eaten. Thirteenth - His saying: If he is absent from you for a day and you find nothing but the trace of your arrow, then eat it. And something similar to it is in the hadith of Abu Tha’labah that was included by Abu Dawud, except that he added: Then eat it after three days as long as it does not stink. This contradicts his saying, peace be upon him: Whatever you kill, say goodbye to what you have killed. Deafness is what is killed quickly while you see it. Growth is when you shoot the prey and it disappears from you and dies, and you do not see it. It is said: I have shot the prey and it has grown, if it disappears and then dies. Imru’ al-Qais said: He does not grow his money, nor does he count his enemies. Scholars have differed on eating the game that is absent, with three opinions: It is eaten, whether it was killed by an arrow or a dog. Secondly, nothing of it is eaten if it is absent, based on his saying: Eat what you have killed and leave what you have killed. It is not eaten for fear that something other than the arrow may have helped kill it. Thirdly, the difference between an arrow, which is eaten, and a dog, which is not eaten. The reason for this is that the arrow kills in one direction, so it is not problematic, and the wounding animal in multiple directions, so it is problematic. The three opinions are from our scholars: Malik said in other than Al-Muwatta’: If the game falls at night and then is struck dead by a hawk, dog, or arrow, he does not eat it. Abu Omar said: This indicates to you that if it reaches its destination, it is permissible for him to eat it even if it falls at night, unless he dislikes it if it falls at night, based on what was reported from Ibn Abbas: And if it is absent from you for a night, do not eat it. And something similar from Al-Thawri, who said: If it is absent from you for a day, you dislike eating it. Al-Shafi’i said: The analogy is that he does not eat it if it is absent from him. Al-Awza’i said: If he finds it dead the next day and finds in it If he finds an arrow or a trace from his dog, then let him eat it and the like. Ashhab, Abd al-Malik and Asbagh said: It is permissible to eat the game even if it was hunted overnight if its killing force was used up. His saying in the hadith: As long as it does not stink is an explanation because if it stinks, it is considered to be among the filthy things that nature abhors, so eating it is disliked because it is permissible, as: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ate rancid, foul-smelling food. It was said that this was due to the fear of harm to the eater. According to this reason, eating it is forbidden if the fear is real, and God knows best. Fourteenth - The scholars differed in this regard regarding hunting with a Jewish or Christian dog if it was trained, so Al-Hasan Al-Basri disliked it. As for the dog of a Magian, his hawk and his falcon, hunting with them was disliked by Jabir bin Abdullah, Al-Hasan, Ata’, Mujahid, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Thawri and Ishaq, and hunting with their dogs was permitted by Malik, Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa if the hunter was a Muslim. They said: This is like his blade. As for if the hunter is from the People of the Book, the majority of the nation is on the permissibility of hunting him except Malik, and he differentiated between that and his slaughter, and he recited: O you who have believed, God will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and spears reach (al-Ma’idah 5:94). He said: God did not mention the Jews and Christians in this. Ibn Wahb and Ashab said: The hunting of a Jew or a Christian is permissible as is his slaughter. In the Book of Muhammad: It is not permissible to hunt or slaughter a Sabean, and they are a people between the Jews and Christians and they have no religion. As for if the hunter is a Magian, then Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa and their companions and the majority of people forbade eating him. Abu Thawr said there are two opinions regarding it: One of them is: As these and others say - that the Magians are among the People of the Book and that their hunting is permissible, even if a drunk person hunts or slaughters, his hunting or slaughtering is not eaten, because slaughtering requires intention, and a drunk person has no intention. Fifteenth - The grammarians differed regarding the word min in the Almighty’s saying: From what they have caught for you. Al-Akhfash said: It is redundant like His saying: Eat from its fruit (al-An’am 6:141). The Basrans made a mistake and said: Min is not added in affirmation, but rather is added in negation and interrogation. His saying: From its fruit [and] And He will expiate for you some of your misdeeds (al-Baqarah 2:271) and He will forgive you some of your sins (al-Ahqaf 46:31) is for partialization. He answered and said: He said: He will forgive you some of your sins (al-Ahzab 33:71) by omitting min, which indicates its redundancy in affirmation. It was answered that min here is for partialization because only the meat of the hunted animal is permissible, not the dung and blood. I said: This is not intended nor is it customary in eating, so it would cloud what he said: It is possible that he meant what they caught, that is, what the birds of prey left for you. This is according to the opinion of those who said: If a dog ate the prey, it would not harm. Because of this possibility, scholars differed about the permissibility of eating game if the bird of prey ate from it, as mentioned above. Sixteenth - The verse indicates the permissibility of keeping and owning dogs for hunting, and this is proven in the authentic Sunnah. It also increases cultivation and livestock. The first Islam ordered the killing of dogs, to the point that a wild dog was killed in the desert, followed by it. Muslim narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever keeps a dog, except a hunting dog or a herding dog, will have two qirats deducted from his reward every day. It was also narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever keeps a dog, except a herding dog, a hunting dog, or a farm dog, will have a qirat deducted from his reward every day. Al-Zuhri said: And he mentioned to Ibn Umar the saying of Abu Hurairah, so he said: May God have mercy on Abu Hurairah, he was a farmer, and the Sunnah indicates what we mentioned. And he made the deduction from the reward of whoever keeps it for something other than that of benefit, either to frighten the Muslims and disturb them with its barking - as some of the poets of Basra said when he stayed with Ammar and heard his dogs barking, so he began to say: We went down to Ammar, and he let his dogs loose on us, and we almost got eaten between his two houses. I said to my companions in secret: Is today or the Day of Resurrection longer? Or to prevent angels from entering the house or because it is impure, according to what Al-Shafi’i sees, or to violate the prohibition against keeping something that is of no benefit, and God knows best. And he said in one of the two narrations: two qirats, and in the other one qirat, and this may be for two types of dogs, one of which is more harmful than the other, like the black one, which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, ordered to be killed. He did not include it in the exception when he prohibited killing it, so he said: You should have a black, white animal with two spots, for it is a devil. Narrated by Muslim. It is possible that this is due to the difference in locations, so if one keeps it in Madinah or Makkah, for example, it will decrease two qirats, and elsewhere it will decrease one qirat. And God knows best. As for what is permissible to keep, it will not decrease the reward of the one who keeps it, such as a horse or a cat, and it is permissible to buy or sell it. Sahnun even said: And one can perform Hajj with its price. The dog that is permissible to keep with livestock according to Malik is the one that walks with the livestock, not the one that protects the livestock in the house from thieves. The dog for crops is the one that protects the farm from wild animals at night and during the day, not from thieves. Others than Malik have permitted keeping them for thieves of livestock, crops, and houses in the desert. Seventeenth - In this verse is evidence that the learned has a virtue that the ignorant does not have, because if a dog has knowledge, he has virtue over other dogs. So if a person has knowledge, he is more deserving of virtue over other people, especially if he acts upon what he has learned. This is as narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God honor his face, who said: Everything has its value, and the value of a person is what he does well. Eighteenth - The Almighty’s saying: And mention the name of God over it. It is an order to mention it. It was said: When sending out to hunt. The jurisprudence of hunting and slaughtering in the meaning of naming is one, and its explanation will come in Al-An’am. It was said: What is meant by naming here is naming when eating, and this is more apparent. In Sahih Muslim, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar ibn Abi Salamah: O boy, say Bismillah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you. It was narrated in the hadith of Hudhayfah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The devil considers food permissible unless the name of God is mentioned over it. The hadith: “If he forgets to say the name of God at the beginning of eating, then let him say the name of God at the end.” Al-Nasa’i narrated: “On the authority of Umayyah ibn Makhshi, who was one of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man eating and did not say the name of God. When he was at the last morsel, he said: In the name of God, its beginning and its end. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The devil kept eating with him.” When he said the name of God, he vomited what he had eaten. Nineteenth - The Almighty’s saying: “And fear God. Indeed, God is swift in account.” He commanded piety in general, and the close guidance is what these verses contain of commands. The speed of the account is from the fact that God has encompassed everything in knowledge and has counted everything in number, so there is no need to attempt to count or compute as accounting does. For this reason, He said: And sufficient are We as accountants. (Al-Anbiya’: 47) So He, glory be to Him, will hold the creation to account all at once. It is possible that it is a threat of the Day of Resurrection, as if He said: Indeed, God’s account of you is swift in coming, as the Day of Resurrection is near. It is possible that He means by the account the recompense, as if He threatened in this world with a quick and close recompense if they do not fear God.
5:5: It contains ten issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: Today, all good things have been made lawful for you meaning, Today, I have perfected your religion for you and Today, all good things have been made lawful for you He repeated it for emphasis, meaning, Today, all good things have been made lawful for you which you asked about. The good things were made lawful for the Muslims before this verse was revealed, so this is the answer to their question when they said: What is made lawful for us? It was said: By mentioning the day, he referred to the sustenance of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, just as one says: These are the days of so-and-so, meaning, this is the time of your appearance and the spread of Islam. I have perfected your religion with this and made all good things lawful for you. The mention of good things came before this in the verse. The second - the Almighty’s saying: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you is a subject and a predicate. Food is the name of what is eaten and the sacrifices from it, and here it is specific to the sacrifices according to many of the people of knowledge of interpretation. As for what is forbidden to us from their food, it is not included under the generality of the address. Ibn Abbas said: God Almighty said: And do not eat of that upon which the name of God has not been mentioned (al-An’am 6:121), then he made an exception and said: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, meaning the sacrifice of the Jew and the Christian, even if the Christian says when slaughtering: In the name of the Messiah, and the Jew says: In the name of Ezra, and that is because they slaughter him according to the religion. Ata’ said: Everyone from the sacrifice of the Christian, even if he says in the name of the Messiah, because God Almighty has permitted their sacrifices and He knows what they say. Al-Qasim bin Mukhaymara said everyone from his sacrifice, even if he says in the name of Sarjis, the name of their church, and this is the saying of Al-Zuhri, Rabi’ah, Al-Sha’bi, and Makhul. It was narrated from two companions from Abu Al-Darda’ and Ubadah bin Al-Samit. A group said: If you hear a person of the Book mentioning a name other than that of God Almighty, then do not eat. This was said by Ali from the companions. Aisha and Ibn Omar, and it is the opinion of Tawus and Al-Hasan, adhering to the words of God Almighty: And do not eat of that upon which the name of God has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is grave disobedience. (al-An’am 6:121) Malik said: I dislike that but did not forbid it. I said: It is strange that Al-Kaya Al-Tabari narrated the agreement on the permissibility of the slaughter of the People of the Book, then he began to use that as evidence that naming the slaughtered animal is not a condition, so he said: There is no doubt that they do not name the slaughtered animal except the god who is not truly worshipped, such as Christ and Ezra. If they named the god truly, their naming would not be in the way of worship, but rather in another way. The condition of naming not in the way of worship is not reasonable, and the presence of naming from the disbeliever and its absence is like one if worship is not imagined from him. And because the Christian slaughters in the name of Christ, and God has ruled that their slaughtered animals are absolutely permissible, and in that is evidence that naming is not a condition at all, as Al-Shafi’i says: And what is in this for the scholars will come in Al-An’am, God willing. Third: There is no disagreement among scholars that what does not require ritual slaughter, such as food that is inevitable, such as fruit and wheat, is permissible to eat, since it does not harm anyone to own it. Food in which there is an attempt is of two types: one of them is that which involves an attempt at craftsmanship that has no connection to religion, such as baking flour, squeezing oil, and the like. This should be avoided by a dhimmi, as it is disgusting. The second type is the ritual slaughter that we mentioned is what requires religion and intention. Since the analogy is that their slaughters are not permissible, as we say that they have no prayer or acceptable worship, God Almighty permitted their slaughters for this nation, and the text excluded it from analogy, based on what we mentioned from the statement of Ibn Abbas, and God knows best. Fourth - The scholars also differed regarding what they mentioned, does the ritual slaughtering apply to what was forbidden to them or not? There are two opinions. The majority are of the opinion that it applies to all slaughtered animals, what is permissible for him and what is forbidden to him, because it was slaughtered. A group of scholars said, what is permissible for us from their slaughtered animals is only what is permissible for them because what is not permissible for them is not applied to their ritual slaughtering. So this group forbade the pure fats and lard from the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book and limited the term food to some, and the first group applied it to all that is eaten. This disagreement is found in the Maliki school. Abu Omar said: Malik disliked the fats of the Jews and eating what they slaughtered from camels, and most scholars do not see anything wrong with that. This will come in the chapter on livestock, God willing. Malik, may God have mercy on him, disliked what they slaughtered if he found what a Muslim slaughtered, and he disliked that they had markets in which they sold what they slaughtered. This is from him, may God have mercy on him, abstaining. Fifth: As for the Magians, the scholars are unanimous, except for those who are an exception, that their slaughtered animals are not to be eaten and that one should not marry them because they are not people of the Book, according to what is well-known among the scholars. There is nothing wrong with any food from those who do not have a Book, such as polytheists and their worshippers and idols, as long as it is not from their slaughtered animals and does not require slaughtering, except for cheese, because it contains the rennet of a dead animal. If the father of the boy is a Magian and a woman of the Book, then his ruling is the ruling of his father according to Malik and others. The slaughtered animal of the boy is not to be eaten if one of his parents is one whose slaughtered animal is not to be eaten. Sixth: As for the sacrifice of the Christians of Banu Taghlib and the sacrifices of every intruder into Judaism and Christianity, Ali, may God be pleased with him, used to forbid the sacrifices of Banu Taghlib because they were Arabs and he used to say: They did not adhere to anything of Christianity except drinking alcohol, which is the saying of Al-Shafi’i. Based on this, he does not forbid the sacrifices of the Christians who are true believers among them. The majority of the nation said that the sacrifice of every Christian is permissible, whether he is from Banu Taghlib or not, and the same applies to the Jew. Ibn Abbas used as evidence the words of God Almighty: And whoever among you takes them as allies, then indeed, he is one of them (al-Ma’idah 5:51). If Banu Taghlib were not Christians except through their taking them as allies, then their sacrifices would have been eaten. Seventh: There is nothing wrong with eating, drinking and cooking in the utensils of all the infidels, as long as they are not made of gold, silver or pigskin after they have been washed and boiled, because they do not avoid impurities and eat dead animals, so if they cook in those pots, they become impure, and perhaps the impurities spread to parts of the clay pots, so if they cook in them after that, it is likely that those impure parts will mix with what is cooked in the pot again, so piety requires us to refrain from it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: If the vessel is made of copper or iron, it should be washed, and if it is made of clay, water should be boiled in it and then washed - this is if it is needed - and Malik said this. As for what they use for other than cooking, there is nothing wrong with using it without washing, because of what was narrated by al-Daraqutni on the authority of Umar that he performed ablution in the house of a Christian woman for a Christian woman, and it is authentic and will come in full in al-Furqan. In Sahih Muslim, “From the hadith of Abu Tha’labah al-Khushani, he said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, we are a land of the People of the Book, and we eat from their utensils. We are also a land of game. I hunt with my bow and with my trained dog, and I hunt with my untrained dog. So tell me what is permissible for us in this regard. He said: As for what you mentioned, that you are in the land of a people, you are in the land of a people of the People of the Book, and you eat from their utensils. If you find utensils other than theirs, then do not eat from them. If you do not find any, then wash them and then eat from them. Then he mentioned the hadith. Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: “And your food is lawful for them” is evidence that they are addressed with the details of our law, meaning that if they buy meat from them, the meat is lawful for them and the price taken from them is lawful for us. Ninth - And the Almighty’s saying: And chaste women from among the believers and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you the meaning of the verse has already been presented in Al-Baqarah and An-Nisa’. Praise be to God. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s saying: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture it is regarding the covenant and not the land of war, so it is specific. And another said: It is permissible to marry a dhimmi or a war woman due to the generality of the verse. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The chaste women are the chaste and sensible. Al-Sha’bi said: It is that she guards her private parts, so she does not commit adultery and washes herself from major ritual impurity. Al-Sha’bi read and the chaste women with a kasra on the sad and Al-Kisa’i read it with it. Mujahid said: The chaste women are the free women. Abu Ubaid said: He believes that it is not permissible to marry the female slaves of the People of the Book due to the Almighty’s saying: Then from among those whom your right hands possess of your believing girls (An-Nisa’: 25). This is the statement that most scholars hold. Tenth - The Almighty’s saying: And whoever disbelieves in faith It was said: When the Almighty said: And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture The women of the People of the Scripture said: Had it not been that God the Almighty was pleased with our religion, He would not have permitted you to marry us, so the verse was revealed: And whoever disbelieves in faith meaning in what was revealed to Muhammad. Abu Al-Haytham said: The ba’ is a connection, meaning whoever disbelieves in faith, rejects it. His work has become worthless. Ibn Al-Sameeq read has become worthless with the ba’ open. It was said: When the obligatory duties and rulings were mentioned that must be carried out, the threat was mentioned for violating them because that emphasizes the warning against neglecting them. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid that the meaning is: And whoever disbelieves in his heart. Al-Hasan bin Al-Fadl said: If this narration is correct, then its meaning is the Lord of faith. Sheikh Abu Al-Hasan Al-Ash’ari said: It is not permissible to call God faith, contrary to the Hashawiyyah and Al-Salamiyyah, because faith is a source of trust, which means to believe in faith, and the active participle of it is a believer, and faith is belief, and belief can only be speech, and it is not permissible for the Almighty Creator to be speech.
5:6: It contains thirty-two questions: First - Al-Qushayri and Ibn Atiyyah mentioned that this verse was revealed in the story of Aisha when she lost the necklace in the Battle of Al-Muraisi’, and it is the verse of ablution. Ibn Atiyyah said: But since ablution was established and used by them, it is as if the verse did not add anything to it except its recitation, but rather it gave them the benefit and permission to perform tayammum. We have mentioned in the verse about women the opposite of this, and God knows best, and the meaning of this verse is included in what is commanded regarding fulfilling contracts and the rulings of the Shari’ah, and in what is mentioned regarding completing the blessing, for this permission is from completing the blessings. Second: The scholars differed regarding the intended meaning of his saying: When you rise to prayer, with different opinions. A group said: This is a general expression for every time you rise to prayer, whether the one standing is pure or in a state of minor ritual impurity. When he rises to pray, he should perform ablution. Ali used to do this and recite this verse. Abu Muhammad al-Darimi mentioned it in his Musnad, and he narrated something similar from Ikrimah. Ibn Sirin said: The caliphs used to perform ablution for every prayer. I said: The verse is thus decisive and there is no abrogation in it. A group said: The address is specific to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdullah bin Hanzala bin Abi Amir Al-Ghasil said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded ablution before every prayer, but this was difficult for him, so he commanded the use of the siwak and ablution was not required of him, except for the one who had broken his ablution. Abdullah bin Alqamah bin Al-Fughawa said on the authority of his father, that the Companions, who were the guide of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Tabuk, said: This verse was revealed as a concession to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he would not do any action except while in a state of ablution, and he would not speak to anyone or return a greeting, etc. So God informed him with this verse that ablution is only for standing up for prayer, not for other actions. A group said: What is meant by the verse is ablution for every prayer, seeking virtue, and they interpreted the matter as recommended. Many of the Companions, including Ibn Umar, would perform ablution for every prayer, seeking virtue, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to do that until he combined the five prayers with one ablution on the day of the conquest, intending to make it clear to his nation, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: The apparent meaning of this statement is that ablution for every prayer before the occurrence of the abrogating verse was recommended, not obligatory. This is not the case, because when a command is presented, it implies obligation, especially among the Companions, may God be pleased with them, according to what is known from their conduct. Others said: The obligation for every ablution was for every prayer, then it was abrogated in the conquest of Mecca. This is a mistake, because of the hadith of Anas, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer,” and that his nation was otherwise. This will come in the hadith of Suwaid bin Al-Nu’man: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the afternoon and sunset prayers in Al-Sahba’ with one ablution, and that was during the Battle of Khaybar,” which was in the year six, and it was said: the year seven, and the conquest as in the year eight, and it is an authentic hadith narrated by Malik in his Muwatta’ and transmitted by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. It is clear from these two hadiths that the obligation was not before the conquest for every prayer. If it is said: Muslim narrated “on the authority of Buraydah bin Al-Husaib: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer. When it was the day of the conquest, he performed the prayers with one ablution and wiped over his socks. Then Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Today you did something that you did not do before. He said: Did you do it intentionally, O Umar? Why did Umar ask him and inquire about it? It was said to him: He only asked him because he had gone against his custom of praying in Khaybar, and God knows best. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Anas: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to perform ablution for every prayer, whether he was pure or not. Humayd said: I said to Anas: How did you do it? He said: We used to perform ablution once. He said: A good and authentic hadith. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Ablution upon ablution is light. So peace be upon him, he would perform ablution again for every prayer. A man greeted him while he was urinating, but he did not respond to him until he performed tayammum, then he returned the greeting and said: Al-Daraqutni narrated it. Al-Suddi and Zayd ibn Aslam said: The meaning of the verse is: “When you rise to prayer” meaning from the beds, meaning sleeping. The intention of this interpretation is to include all ritual impurities in mention, especially sleep, which is disputed as to whether it is ritual impurity in itself or not. According to this interpretation, the verse is preceded and delayed. The estimate is: O you who believe, when you rise to prayer from sleep or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women meaning minor contact, so wash yourself. Thus the rulings of the one who has a minor ritual impurity are fulfilled. Then he said: And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, purify yourself. This is the ruling of another type. Then he said both types together. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy or you have touched women and you do not find water, then seek clean earth. Muhammad ibn Maslama, one of the companions of Malik - may God have mercy on him - and others said this interpretation. The majority of scholars said: The meaning of the verse is that you have risen to prayer in a state of ritual impurity. According to this interpretation, there is no precedence and delay in the verse, rather the rulings of the verse are arranged. And the one who finds water until his saying: Then purify yourselves. And minor contact was included in his saying those in a state of minor ritual impurity. Then he mentioned after his saying: And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, then purify yourselves. The ruling for one who lacks water from both types was mentioned, and the contact was intercourse. And the one who has major ritual impurity must mention one who lacks water, just as the one who finds water mentioned. This is the interpretation of al-Shafi’i and others, and upon it come the sayings of the Companions, such as Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, Ibn Abbas, Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, and others. I said: These two interpretations are the best that has been said about the verse, and God knows best. The meaning of if you stand up is if you intend, as God Almighty said: So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge (al-Nahl 16:98), meaning if you intend, because ablution is not possible while standing for prayer. Third - The Almighty’s saying: Wash your faces. The Almighty mentioned four parts: the face, and washing it is obligatory, and the hands are likewise, and the head, and washing it is obligatory by agreement. There is disagreement about the feet, as will come, and nothing else is mentioned. This indicates that everything else is etiquette and Sunnah. And God knows best. In washing the face, it is necessary to transfer water to it and pass the hand over it. This is the reality of washing according to us, and we have explained it in An-Nisa’. And others have said: He only has to run the water and he does not have to rub it with his hand. There is no doubt that if a man immerses himself in the water and immerses his face or hand and does not rub it, it is said that he washed his face and hand. And it is known that nothing is considered in that except obtaining the name, so if it is obtained, it is sufficient. The face in the language is taken from the word mawjah, and it is a bite that includes parts and it has length and width. Its limit in length is from the beginning of the surface of the forehead to the end of the beard and from ear to ear in width. This is in the case of a beardless man. As for the bearded man, if the chin is covered with hair, it is either light or thick. If the first is such that the skin is visible from it, then it is necessary to bring water to it. If it is thick, then the obligation has been transferred to it, like hair. The head, like the hair of the head, then what is more than the chin from the ten and is loose from the beard. Sahnun said on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim: I heard Malik asked: Have you heard some of the people of knowledge say that the beard is part of the face, so water should pass over it? He said: Yes, and combing it during ablution is not something people do, and he criticized that for whoever does it. Ibn al-Qasim also mentioned on the authority of Malik, who said: The person performing ablution should move the outer part of his beard without putting his hand in it. He said: It is like the toes of the feet. Ibn Abd al-Hakam said: Combing the beard is obligatory in ablution and ritual washing. Abu Omar said: It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, combed his beard during ablution, through all weak chains of transmission. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad mentioned that the jurists agreed that combing the beard is not obligatory during ablution, except for one thing that was narrated on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, who said: Why does a man wash his beard before it grows, and when it grows he does not wash it? Why does a beardless man wash his chin while a bearded man does not? Al-Tahawi said: Tayammum is obligatory in which the skin is wiped before the hair grows on the face, then it is dropped after that according to all of them, so the same applies to ablution. Abu `Umar said: Whoever makes washing the entire beard obligatory has made it a face, because the face is taken from facing, and God has commanded washing the face in an absolute manner, and He did not make a bearded man special from a beardless man, so washing it is obligatory according to the apparent meaning of the Qur’an, because it is a substitute for the skin. I said: Ibn al-Arabi chose this statement and said: And I say the same because “It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to wash his beard” was reported by al-Tirmidhi and others, so he specified the possibility with the action. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Ishaq that whoever intentionally left combing his beard must repeat it. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Uthman ibn Affan “That the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to comb his beard.” He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Abu Umar said: And whoever does not require washing what hangs down from the beard went to the fact that the original command to wash it is the skin, so it is obligatory to wash what appears above the skin, and what hangs down from the beard does not have anything underneath it that must be washed, so washing the beard is a substitute for it. They also differed regarding washing what is behind the pubis to the ear. Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik that he said: What is behind the temple that is behind the hair of the beard to the chin is not from the face. Abu Umar said: I do not know of any of the jurists of the regions who said what Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: The whiteness is the brown of the pubis and the ear is from the face, and washing it is obligatory. Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad said something similar: It was said: It is washed. Whiteness is recommended. Ibn al-Arabi said: What is correct in my opinion is that it is not necessary to wash it except for a beardless person, not for someone who has an excuse. I said: This is the choice of Judge Abdul Wahhab, and the reason for the disagreement is whether the confrontation applies to him or not, and God knows best. Because of this possibility, they disagreed as to whether the command to wash the face includes the inside of the nose and mouth or not? Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq and others held that this is obligatory in ablution and ritual washing, except that Ahmad said: He who leaves out inhaling water in his ablution must repeat it, but he who leaves out rinsing his mouth must not repeat it. The majority of jurists said that they are two Sunnahs in ablution and ritual washing, because the command only includes the outward appearance and not the inward appearance, and the Arabs do not name a face except that which is confronted. Then, God did not mention them in His Book, nor did the Muslims make them obligatory, nor did everyone agree on them. The obligatory duties are not established except from these faces. This meaning has already been mentioned in An-Nisa. As for the eyes, all people agree that it is not necessary to wash the inside of the eyes, except for what was narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar that he used to sprinkle water in his eyes, and washing them was dropped because of the harm caused by that and the difficulty caused by it. Ibn Al-Arabi said: And that was when Abdullah ibn Umar went blind, he washed his eyes, because he was not harmed by that. And if the ruling on the face is established, then it is necessary to wash a part of the head with the face without specifying, just as it is necessary, according to the opinion of the obligation of the head in general, to wipe a part of the face with it that cannot be determined. This is based on a principle of the principles of jurisprudence, which is that what is not required to be performed is obligatory like it, and God. Know. Fourth - The majority of scholars agree that ablution requires intention, “based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Actions are judged by intentions. Al-Bukhari said: This includes faith, ablution, prayer, zakat, Hajj, fasting, and rulings. God Almighty said: “Say: ‘Each one acts according to his nature’” (al-Isra’ 17:84), meaning according to his intention. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: But jihad and intention. Many Shafi’is said: There is no need for intention, and this is the opinion of the Hanafis. They said: Intention is not required except in the obligatory acts that are intended for their own sake and are not made a cause for something else. As for what was a condition for the validity of another act, it is not required in it by the occurrence of the command itself except by an indication that accompanies it. Purity is a condition, for the one who does not have to pray is not required to perform the obligation of purity, such as the menstruating woman and the woman in postpartum bleeding. Our scholars and some Shafi’is cited as evidence the words of God the Almighty: When you rise to prayer, wash your faces. So when the act of washing was required, the intention was a condition for the validity of the act, because the obligation is from God the Almighty, so it should be required to do what God commanded. So if we say that the intention is not required of him, then the intention to do what God the Almighty commanded him is not required of him. It is known that the one who washed himself to cool off or for some purpose intended to perform the obligation, and it is authentic in the hadith that ablution is an act of disbelief, so if it was valid without intention, he would not have disbelieved. God the Almighty said: And they were commanded only to worship God, devoting their religion to Him sincerely. [Al-Bayyinah]:5] Fifth - Ibn al-Arabi said: Some of our scholars said: If someone goes to the river with the intention of washing, it is sufficient for him, even if his intention is absent on the way. If he goes to the bathroom and it is absent on the way, the intention is invalidated. Judge Abu Bakr Ibn al-Arabi may God be pleased with him said: The foolish muftis based their opinion on this, that the intention for prayer is subject to both opinions, and they cited a text from someone who does not differentiate between suspicion and certainty, that he said: It is permissible for the intention to precede the takbir. Oh God and oh the people of the worlds, what a nation that wanted to be a mufti and an independent jurist, but God did not guide it or make it right. Know, may God have mercy on you, that the scholars differed about the obligation of the intention in ablution, and Malik’s opinion differed about it. When it was lowered from the level of agreement, it was permitted to advance it in some places. As for prayer, none of the imams differed about it, and it is an intended principle, so how can the intended principle that is agreed upon be interpreted as a subsidiary branch that is disputed? Is this anything but the height of stupidity? As for fasting, the Shari’ah has removed the difficulty in it because it was initiated at a time of negligence by advancing the intention to it: Sixth - The Almighty’s saying: And your hands to the elbows. People differed about whether the elbows are included in the definition. Some people said: Yes, because what comes after to if it is of the same type as what came before it is included in it. This was said by Sibawayh and others, and this has already been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. It was said: The elbows are not included in the washing. The two narrations were narrated from Malik, the second from Ashab, and the first is the opinion of most scholars, and it is correct because of what Al-Daraqutni narrated from Jabir that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When he performed ablution, he would run the water over his elbows. Some of them said: To means with, as they say, the herd to the herd of camels, meaning with the herd. This is not necessary, as we explained in An-Nisa’. Because the hand among the Arabs falls on the tips of the fingers to the shoulder, and likewise the foot falls on the fingers to the base of the thigh, so the elbow is included under the name of the hand. If the meaning were with the elbows, it would not be useful. So what he said: To was deducted from the limit of the elbows from the washing, and the elbows remained washed up to the nail. This is a correct statement that follows the original language and meaning. Ibn Al-Arabi said: No one understood the meaning of the issue except Judge Abu Muhammad, for he said: His saying to the elbows is a limit for the hands that are left out, not for the ones that are washed in them. Therefore, the elbows are included in the washing. I said: Since the hand and the foot are used in the language as we mentioned, “Abu Hurairah would reach his armpit and leg with ablution and say: I heard my friend, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The adornment of the believer reaches where the ablution reaches. “Qadi Iyad said: The people are unanimously agreed to disagree with this and not to exceed the limits of ablution,” because of his saying, peace be upon him: Whoever increases it has transgressed and wronged.” Another said: This action was his doctrine and something that he did alone. He did not narrate it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Rather, he derived it from his saying, peace be upon him: You are the pure ones with veils. And from his saying: The ornament reaches as mentioned. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: And wipe over your heads. It was mentioned in An-Nisa’ that wiping is a common word, and as for the head, it is an expression for the whole thing that people know by necessity, including the face. So when God Almighty mentioned it in ablution and specifically mentioned the face for washing, the rest of it remained for wiping. If He had not mentioned washing, it would have been necessary to wipe all of it, including the hair on the head, the eyes, the nose, and the mouth. Malik indicated in the obligation of wiping the head what we mentioned, because… He was asked about the one who leaves part of his head during ablution, so he said: Tell me if he leaves washing part of his face, would that suffice for him? And it is clear from what we have mentioned that the ears are part of the head and that their ruling is the ruling of the head, contrary to what Al-Zuhri said: They are part of the face and are washed with it, and contrary to what Al-Sha’bi said: What is in front of them is part of the face and their outer part is part of the head, and this is the saying of Al-Hasan and Ishaq, and Ibn Abi Hurairah narrated it from Al-Shafi’i, and their argument will be explained. The head is called a head because of its height and the growth of hair on it, and from this comes the head of the mountain. We said that the head is a name for a group of limbs because of the saying of the poet: If they carry my head, and most of me is in the head, then I will leave at the meeting place, then I will continue Eighth - The scholars differed in estimating his wiping into eleven opinions, three of them for Abu Hanifa, two for Al-Shafi’i and six for our scholars. The correct one is the obligation of generalization for what we mentioned. The scholars agreed that whoever wipes his entire head has done well and done what is required of him. The letter Ba’ is an additional emphasis and is not for partiality. The meaning is: Wipe your heads. It was said: Its inclusion here is like its inclusion in Tayammum in His statement: Then wipe your faces. If its meaning was partiality, it would have indicated it in that place, and this is decisive. It was said: It was only included to restrict a unique meaning, which is that washing in language requires something washed with, and wiping in language does not require something wiped with. If he had said: And wipe your heads, wiping with the hand would have sufficed by passing it over the head without anything. So the letter Ba’ was included to indicate something wiped with, which is water, so it is as if he had said: And wipe your heads with water. This became in language in two ways: either on the heart, as Sibawayh recited: Like the moaning of a dove's feathers on her cheek, she wiped the kohl with the two lashes. The gum is the one wiped with the powder of antimony, so it was changed: and as for the condition, then the verb and equality in its proportion, like the poet’s saying. Like the hyenas, they have reached Najran, or their shame has reached Hajar. This is what our scholars have regarding the meaning of the letter baa. Al-Shafi’i said: The statement of God the Most High: And wipe over your heads may mean some of the head and wiping all of it, so the Sunnah indicates that wiping some of it is sufficient, which is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped his forelock. He said in another place: If it is said that God the Most High said: And wipe over your faces in tayammum, does some of the face suffice in that? It is said to him: Wiping the face in tayammum is a substitute for washing it, so it is necessary to wipe over all of the area of washing, and wiping the head is the origin, so this is a difference that we did not mention. Our scholars answered the hadith by saying: Perhaps the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that for an excuse, especially since this action of his, may God bless him and grant him peace, was while traveling, which is a place where excuses are likely and where there is haste and abbreviation and the deletion of many of the obligatory acts because of derivatives and dangers. Then he did not suffice with the forelock. Even wiping over the turban. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba. If wiping the entire head was not obligatory, he would not have wiped over the turban, and God knows best. Ninth - The majority of scholars agree that wiping it once, completely, is sufficient. Al-Shafi’i said: He should wipe his head three times. It was narrated on the authority of Anas, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Ata’. Ibn Sirin used to wipe it twice. Abu Dawud said: And hadiths. Uthman Al-Sahihah all indicate that wiping the head is done once, as they mentioned ablution three times, in which they said: And he wiped his head, and they did not mention a number. Tenth - They differed on where to start with Samah. Malik said: He starts from the front of his head, then he goes with his hands to the back, then he returns them to the front, according to the hadith of Abdullah bin Zaid, narrated by Muslim. Al-Shafi’i and Ibn Hanbal say the same. Al-Hasan bin Hayy used to say: He starts from the back of the head, according to the hadith of Ar-Rabi’ bint Mu’adh bin Afra’, which is a hadith whose wording differs and it is narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Aqil, who is not a hafiz according to them. It was narrated by Abu Dawud, Bishr bin Al-Mufaddal, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of Ar-Rabi’, and Ibn Ajlan narrated on his authority on the authority of Ar-Rabi’. That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution there, so he wiped the entire head from the crown of the hair, each side according to the position of the hair, without moving the hair from its position. This description was narrated from Ibn Umar, and that he would start from the middle of his head. The most authentic hadith in this regard is the hadith of Abdullah bin Zaid. Whoever permits some of the head, he only sees that some of it is in the front of the head. It was narrated from Ibrahim and Al-Sha’bi that they said: Whichever side of your head you wipe, it is sufficient for you. Ibn Umar wiped the fontanelle, and the consensus is established on the desirability of wiping with both hands together and on the parts if he wipes with one hand. There is disagreement about whoever wipes with one finger until it includes what he sees as sufficient for him from the head. The well-known view is that this is sufficient, and this is the view of Sufyan Al-Thawri. Sufyan said: If he wipes his head with one finger, it is sufficient for him. It was said: That is not sufficient because it is a departure from the Sunnah of wiping, and it is as if he was playing, unless it was due to the necessity of illness, in which case there should be no disagreement about the parts. Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad said: Wiping the head with less than three fingers is not sufficient. They differed about returning the hands to the hair of the head, is it obligatory or a Sunnah - after the consensus. The first wipe is obligatory according to the Qur’an. The majority of scholars believe that it is a Sunnah, and it has been said that it is obligatory. Eleventh - If a person performing ablution washes his head instead of wiping it, Ibn al-Arabi said: We do not know of any disagreement that this is sufficient for him, except what Imam Fakhr al-Islam al-Shashi told us in al-Dars on the authority of Abu al-Abbas Ibn al-Qas, one of their companions, who said: It is not sufficient for him. This is an intrusion into the corrupt doctrine of the Dawudiyah of following the apparent meaning that invalidates the Shari’ah, which God has condemned in His statement: They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world (al-Rum: 7) and the Most High said: Or an outward aspect of speech (al-Ra’d 13:33). Otherwise, this washer has done what he was commanded and more. If it is said: This addition has gone beyond the wording that is used as an act of worship, we say: It has not gone beyond its meaning in conveying the action to the place. Likewise, if he shaved his head and then shaved it, he does not have to repeat the wiping. Twelfth - As for the ears, they are part of the head according to Malik, Ahmad, al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa and others. Then they differed about renewing the water. Malik and Ahmad said: He should start over with new water for them other than the water with which he wiped the head, as Ibn Umar did. This is what al-Shafi’i said about renewing the water. He said: They are a Sunnah as they are, neither from the face nor from the head, because the scholars agree that the hair on them should not be shaved during Hajj. Abu Thawr’s statement on this is like al-Shafi’i’s statement. Al-Thawri and Abu Hanifa said: They should be wiped with the head with one water. A group of the Salaf narrated a similar statement from the Companions and Followers. Dawud said: If he wipes his ears, then it is good. Otherwise, there is nothing wrong with him, since they are not mentioned in the Qur’an. It was said to him: The name of the head and its inclusion are as we have explained. The authentic hadiths came in the book of al-Nasa’i, Abu Dawud and others that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped their back and inside and inserted his fingers into his eardrums. The fact that they were not mentioned in the Book indicates that they are not obligatory like washing the face and hands. The Sunnah of wiping them has been proven by the Sunnah, and the people of knowledge dislike it for the one performing ablution. He left wiping his ears and they consider him to have left a Sunnah of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they do not require him to repeat it, except for Ishaq, who said: If he left wiping his ears, it does not count. Ahmad said: If he left them intentionally, I would like him to repeat it. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Ziyad, one of the companions of Malik, that he said: Whoever leaves a Sunnah of ablution or prayer intentionally must repeat it. This is weak according to the jurists, and its speaker has no predecessors and has no share of consideration. If it were like that, the obligatory duty would not have been known from others, and God knows best. The one who said: They are from the face provided evidence for what was proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to say in his prostration. My face prostrates to the One who created it, shaped it, and fashioned its hearing and sight. So He added hearing to the face, and it was established that they have the same ruling as the face. In the Musannaf of Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Uthman: He washed their bellies and backs once, then he washed his feet and said: Where are those who asked about ablution? This is how I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performing ablution. Those who said: He washes their outer parts with the face and their inner parts, wiping them with the head, argued that God, the Almighty, has commanded washing the face and wiping the head. So whatever of the ears faces you must be washed because it is part of the face, and whatever does not face you must be wiped because it is part of the head. This is refuted by the reports that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to wipe the outer parts of his ears and their inner parts, from the hadith of Ali, Uthman, Ibn Abbas, al-Rabi’ and others. Those who said: They are part of the head, argued that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said from the hadith of al-Nasabiji: When he wipes his head, the sins will leave his head and even his ears. The hadith was narrated by Malik. Thirteenth - The Almighty’s saying: And your feet. Nafi’ ibn Amir and Al-Kisa’i read and your feet in the accusative case. Al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated on the authority of Nafi’ that he read and your feet in the nominative case, which is the reading of Al-Hasan and Al-A’mash Sulayman. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Hamza read and your feet in the genitive case. The Companions and Followers differed according to these readings. Whoever read in the accusative case made the agent wash and built on the fact that the obligation for the feet is washing without wiping. This is the doctrine of the majority and all scholars, and it is proven from the actions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and is necessary from his statement in more than one hadith: He saw some people performing ablution and their camels were visible, so he called out at the top of his voice. “Woe to the heels from the Fire! Perform ablution thoroughly.” Then God defined them and said: to the ankles, just as He said about the hands: to the elbows. This indicates the obligation to wash them, and God knows best. And whoever recites in the genitive case makes the agent the ba’. Ibn al-Arabi said: The scholars agreed on the obligation to wash them, and I do not know of anyone who mentioned that except al-Tabari from the Muslim jurists, and the Rafidah from others, and al-Tabari relied on the genitive reading. I said: It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Ablution is two washings and two wipings. It has been narrated that Al-Hajjaj gave a sermon in Ahwaz and mentioned ablution, saying: Wash your faces and your hands and wipe your heads and your feet, for there is nothing in the son of Adam closer to his filth than his feet, so wash their insides and their backs and their heels. Anas bin Malik heard that and said: God is truthful and Al-Hajjaj is lying. God Almighty said: And wipe over your heads and your feet. He said: And when he wiped his feet, he would wet them. It has also been narrated on the authority of Ibn Anas that he said: The Qur’an was revealed regarding wiping and the Sunnah regarding washing. Ikrimah was regarding wiping his feet, and he said: There is no washing for the feet, rather wiping was revealed for them. Amer Al-Sha’bi said: Gabriel came down with forgiveness. Do you not see that tayammum allows for what was washing and cancels what was wiping? Qatadah said: God has made two washings and two wipings obligatory. Ibn Jarir Al-Tabari went to the view that their obligation is the choice between washing and wiping, and he made the two readings like the two narrations. Al-Nahhas said: And among the best things that have been said about it is that wiping and washing are both obligatory, so wiping is obligatory. According to the reading of those who read with the accusative, washing is obligatory according to the reading of those who read with the nasb, and the two readings are like two verses. Ibn Atiyah said: The opinion of those who read with the kasra went to the fact that wiping the feet is washing. I said: And this is correct, for the word massah is vague, and is used to mean wiping and is used to mean washing. Al-Harawi said: Al-Azhari informed us, Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Uthman bin Saeed Al-Dari informed us, on the authority of Abu Hatim, on the authority of Abu Zaid Al-Ansari, who said: “Massage in the speech of the Arabs can be a washing and it can be a wiping. From this it is said to a man when he performs ablution and washes his limbs, he may wipe and it is said: May God wipe what is on you if He washes you and purifies you from sins.” So if it is proven by transmission from the Arabs that wiping can mean washing, then the statement of those who said that what is meant by the reading of the khuff is washing is preferred, by the reading of the nasb in which there is no possibility and by the abundance of the hadiths that are proven about washing and the threat of not washing it in the authentic hadiths that are countless, many of which were transmitted by the imams. Then wiping the head only entered between what is washed to clarify the order, as it is the object before the feet, the estimate: So wash your faces and your hands to the elbows and your feet to the ankles and wipe your heads. So since the head is the object before the feet, it was presented before them in the recitation, and God knows best - not that they are vague with the head because it precedes them in description. Purification: Asim bin Kulayb narrated on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn, may God have mercy on them, recited - upon and your feet - and Ali heard that and he was judging between the people, so he said: And your feet. This is from the first and last of the speech. Abu Ishaq narrated on the authority of Al-Harith on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Wash the feet up to the ankles. And likewise it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas that they recited and your feet in the accusative. And it was said: The lowering in the feet only came as a restriction to wiping them, but if they were wearing socks, and we received this restriction from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, since it was not authentically reported that he wiped his feet except while wearing socks, so he, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained by his action the situation in which the foot is washed and the situation in which it is permissible. And this is good. So if it is said: Wiping over the socks was abrogated by Surat Al-Ma’idah, and Ibn Abbas said it, and Abu Hurayrah and Aisha rejected wiping, and Malik denied it in a narration from him, then the answer is that whoever denies something and someone else confirms it, then there is no proof for the denier. And wiping over the socks was confirmed by a large number of the Companions and others. And Al-Hasan said: Seventy men from the Companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, told me. May God bless him and grant him peace, that they wiped over their socks. It has been proven by a sound narration on the authority of Hammam, who said: Jarir urinated, then performed ablution and wiped over his socks. Jarir said: And “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urinated, then performed ablution and wiped over his socks.” Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: They liked this hadith because Jarir’s conversion to Islam was after the revelation of the Table. This is a text that refutes what they mentioned and what they used as evidence from the narration of al-Waqidi on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Ja’far on the authority of his father that Jarir converted to Islam on the sixteenth of Ramadan and that the Table was revealed in Dhu al-Hijjah on the day of Arafat. This hadith is not proven without its weakness. Rather, it was revealed on the day of Arafat: Today I have perfected your religion for you, based on what was mentioned above. Ahmad bin Hanbal said: I approve of Jarir’s hadith about wiping over the socks, because his conversion to Islam was after the revelation of the Table. As for what was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah and Aisha, may God be pleased with them, it is not authentic. As for Aisha, she did not have knowledge of that, and therefore she referred the questioner to Ali, may God be pleased with him, and referred him to him. He said: Basket, for he was traveling with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the hadith. As for Malik, what was narrated from him of denial is denounced and not authentic. The correct thing is what he said at his death to Ibn Nafi’, he said: I used to take care of myself in particular with purification and I do not see anyone who wipes as negligent in what is required of him. And on this Ahmad ibn Hanbal carried what Ibn Wahb narrated from him that he said: I do not wipe while at home or traveling. Ahmad said as he narrated from Ibn Umar that he ordered them to wipe their shoes and he took them off and performed ablution and said: I have made ablution beloved to me and similarly from Abu Ayyub. And Ahmad, may God be pleased with him, said: So whoever left that in the manner in which Ibn Umar, Abu Ayyub, and Malik left it, I did not denounce him and we prayed behind him and did not criticize him, unless he left that and did not see it as the people of innovation did, then he should not pray behind him, and God knows best. And it was said: His saying: And your feet is connected to the wording and not the meaning, and this also indicates washing, for the meaning is taken into consideration, not the wording, and it was only lowered for the sake of proximity as the Arabs do, and this came in the Qur’an and elsewhere. God the Most High said: He will send upon you a flame of fire. And copper” (al-Rahman 55:35) in the accusative case because copper is smoke. And he said: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, in a Preserved Tablet (al-Buruj 85:21-22) in the accusative case. He said: Imru’ al-Qais: Big people in Bajad Muzamil So Muzamil was lowered by the neighbor and Muzamil is the man and its parsing is the nominative. Zuhair said: Time played with it and changed it after me, the rivers and the country Abu Hatim said: The face of the word qatr was in the nominative case, but it was made accusative in accordance with the permissibility of the word, as the Arabs said: This is a ruined lizard’s stone, so they made it accusative, but it is in the nominative case. This is the doctrine of Al-Akhfash and Abu Ubaidah. Al-Nahhas responded and said: This statement is a great mistake, because the accusative case cannot be used in speech to be compared to it, but rather it is a mistake, and its counterpart is strengthening. I said: What is conclusive in this chapter that washing is obligatory for both feet is what we have presented and what has been proven from his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: Woe to the heels and the soles of the feet from the Fire. “So our fear by mentioning the Fire is for disobeying the will of God Almighty. It is known that the Fire does not punish with it except for those who abandon an obligation. It is known that wiping is not comprehensive, and there is no disagreement among those who say that wiping the feet is on their backs, not their soles. Thus, this hadith shows the invalidity of the statement of those who say that the Messiah, if he enters, will make their soles permissible, according to them. Rather, that is achieved by washing, not by wiping. Another proof from the aspect of consensus is that they agreed that whoever washes his feet has fulfilled his obligation, and they differed about whoever wipes his feet. What is certain is what they agreed upon, not what they differed about. The majority, in its entirety, transmitted from all of them from their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to wash his feet in his ablution once, twice, and three times until he purified them. This is sufficient as an argument for washing with what we have explained. It is clear and evident that the meaning of the reading of the lowering is washing, not wiping, as we have mentioned. And the factor in His statement: “And your feet” is His statement: So wash. The Arabs may connect one thing to another with a verb that is unique to one of them. You say: I ate bread. And I drank milk, and from this the poet said: I fed her straw and cold water. The other said: I saw your husband in the battlefield, carrying a sword and a spear. The other said: And the gazelles and ostriches were born in the two ignorant places. The other said: Milk, dates and ghee drink The estimation: I fed her straw and gave her water to drink, and he was wearing a sword and carrying a spear, and her gazelles were born in the two ignorant places, and her ostriches hatched, and the ostrich does not hatch, but rather lays eggs, and she had children, and the two ignorant places were by the side of the valley, and she drank milk and ate dates, so his saying, And wipe over your heads and your feet, is an affixation of washing to wiping, based on the meaning, and what is meant is washing, and God knows best. Fourteenth - The Almighty’s saying: to the ankles. Al-Bukhari narrated: Musa told us that Wahbat told us on the authority of Amr - he is Ibn Yahya - on the authority of his father who said: Amr ibn Abi Hassan asked Abdullah ibn Zaid about the ablution of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he called for a bowl of water and performed ablution for them as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did. He poured some water over his hand from the bowl and washed his hands three times. Then he put his hand in the bowl and rinsed his mouth and nose and blew out three handfuls of water. Then he put his hand in and washed his face three times. Then he put his hand in and washed his hands up to the elbows three times. Then he put his hand in and wiped his head, turning them forward and backward once. Then he washed his feet up to the ankles. This hadith is evidence that the letter ba in his statement, and wipe your heads is redundant, because he said, so he wiped his head, not with his head. And wiping the head once has been explained in the book of Muslim from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Zaid in the interpretation of his statement, so he turned and forward and backward, and he began with the front of his head, then he went with them to the back of his neck, then he brought them back until he returned to the place from which he began. The scholars differed regarding the ankles. The majority are of the opinion that they are the two protruding bones on the sides of the foot. Al-Asma’i denied the people’s opinion that the ankle is on the back of the foot. This is stated in the Sahih and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said the same. Ibn Atiyah said: I do not know of anyone who has made the limit of ablution to this, but Abd al-Wahhab in al-Talqin mentioned this in a wording that is confusing and ambiguous. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: I do not know of anyone who disagreed that the two heels are the two bones at the junction of the leg joint. Al-Tabari narrated on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Ashhab on the authority of Malik who said: The two heels towards which ablution is obligatory are the two bones attached to the leg, parallel to the heel, and the heel is not the one that appears on the surface of the foot. I said: This is correct in language and Sunnah, because the heel in the speech of the Arabs is taken from the height, from which the Kaaba was named, and the woman’s heel is when her breasts are swollen, the girl’s heel is her tube, and the tube is what is between every two nodes, the heel, and it may be used in honor and glory as a simile, and from it the hadith: By God, your heel will remain high. As for the Sunnah, it is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Al-Nu’man bin Bashir. By God, you must straighten your rows, or God will cause discord among your hearts. He said: I saw a man sticking his shoulder to his companion’s shoulder, his knee to his companion’s knee, and his heel to his heel. The heel is the back of the foot under the Achilles tendon, and the Achilles tendon is the joint of the shin and foot. From this is the hadith: Woe to the Achilles tendons from the Fire, meaning if they are not washed, as he said: Woe to the heels and the soles of the feet from the Fire. Fifteenth - Ibn Wahb said on the authority of Malik: No one is required to separate the toes of his feet during ablution or ritual washing, and there is no good in being rude or excessive. Ibn Wahb said: Separating the toes of the feet is encouraged, and it is necessary for the fingers of the hands. Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik: Whoever does not separate the toes of his feet, there is nothing wrong with him. Muhammad ibn Khal said on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim on the authority of Malik regarding someone who performs ablution by a river and moves his foot, that it is not sufficient until he washes it with his hands. Ibn al-Qasim said: If he is able to wash one of them with the other, it is sufficient for him. I said: The correct view is that it is not sufficient for him to wash anything except what is between them, like the rest of the foot, since that is part of the foot just as what is between the fingers of the hand is part of the hand. There is no consideration for the separation of the fingers of the hands and the joining of the toes, since a person is commanded to wash the entire foot just as he is commanded to wash the entire hand. It has been narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when he performed ablution, he would rub the toes of his feet with his little finger, along with what has been proven that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, would wash his feet. This requires generality, and Malik, may God have mercy on him, at the end of his life would rub the toes of his feet with his little finger or with some of his fingers, based on a hadith narrated to him by Ibn Wahb, from Ibn Lahi’ah and Al-Layth Ibn Sa’d, from Yazid Ibn Amr Al-Ghafari, from Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Halabi, from Al-Mustawrid Ibn Shaddad Al-Qurashi, who said: I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performing ablution and running his little finger between his toes. Ibn Wahb said: Malik said to me: This is good, and I have never heard it before now. Ibn Wahb said: I heard him asked after that about running his fingers between his toes in ablution, and he ordered it. Hudhayfah narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave the fingers alone so that the fire does not penetrate them. This is a text warning against leaving the fingers alone, so what we have said is confirmed, and God is the Grantor of success. Sixteenth: The wording of the verse requires continuity between the limbs, which is that the person performing ablution follows one action after another without any slack between its parts, nor is it separated by an action that is not part of it. The scholars differed on this. Ibn Abi Salamah and Ibn Wahb said: This is one of the obligations of ablution in remembrance and forgetfulness. So whoever separates the limbs of his ablution intentionally or forgetfully, it is not valid. Ibn Abd al-Hakam said: It is valid for him whether he forgets or intentionally. Malik said in al-Mudawwanah and the book of Muhammad: The continuity is dropped, and al-Shafi’i said the same. Malik and Ibn al-Qasim said: If he separates them intentionally, it is not valid for him, but it is valid for him forgetfully. Malik said in the narration of Ibn Habib: It is valid for the washed, but it is not valid for the wiped. These are five opinions based on two principles: The first - that God the Almighty commanded an absolute command, so he followed or separated, and what is meant is that washing all the limbs is done when standing for prayer. The second - that they are acts of worship with different pillars, so it is obligatory for them to be consecutive, like prayer. This is the most correct, and God knows best.
