Seventeenth - The words of the verse also include the order, and there is disagreement about it. Al-Abhari said: The order is a Sunnah, and the apparent doctrine is that the reverse for the forgetful is sufficient. There is disagreement about the deliberate one, so it was said that it is sufficient and arranged in the future. Abu Bakr al-Qadi and others said: It is not sufficient because he is playing around. This is what al-Shafi’i and all his companions went to, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr said. Abu Mus’ab, the companion of Malik, went to it, and mentioned it in his summary and narrated it from the people of Medina, and Malik is with them that whoever puts his hands forward in ablution over his face and does not perform ablution according to the order of the verse, then he must repeat what he prayed with that ablution. Malik went in most of the narrations from him and the most famous ones that the waw does not require following it nor does it give a rank, and this is what his companions said, and it is the saying of Abu Hanifa and his companions, al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, al-Layth ibn Sa’d, al-Muzani, and Dawud ibn Ali. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: The apparent meaning of the Almighty’s saying: So wash your faces and your hands requires that it be sufficient, whether separated or combined, or in a row, according to what is correct from the doctrine of al-Shafi’i, which is the doctrine of Most scholars said: Abu Omar said: Except that Malik is recommended to start ablution again in the order of what he will do in the prayer, and he does not see that as obligatory for him. This is the conclusion of his school of thought. Ali bin Ziyad narrated from Malik who said: Whoever washes his arms, then his face, then remembers his place, repeats washing his arms, and if he does not remember until he prays, he repeats ablution and prayer. Ali said: Then after that he does not repeat the prayer, and he repeats ablution for what he starts again. The reason for the disagreement is what some of them said: The fa’ necessitates the follow-up in his saying: So wash, because since it was an obligation for the condition, it linked the conditional to it, so it required the order in all of them. It was answered that it only required the beginning in the face, since it is the consequence of the condition and its answer, and it only required the order in all of them if the answer to the condition had one meaning. So if they were sentences, you would have an answer to them, and you would not care which one you started with, since the goal is to obtain it. It was said: The order came from the waw, and it is not like that, because you say: Zaid and Amr fought, and Bakr and Khalid disputed, so they included it in the chapter of mutual interaction, which takes it out of the order. The correct thing to say is that the order is received from four aspects: The first is to start with what God started. As he, peace and blessings be upon him, said when he performed Hajj: We begin with what God began with. The second is from the consensus of the predecessors, for they used to arrange the third - from likening ablution to prayer. The fourth - from the perseverance of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that. Those who permitted that argued with the consensus that there is no order in washing the limbs for major ritual impurity, so likewise washing the limbs for ablution, because the meaning in that is washing, not ritual purification. It was narrated from Ali that he said: I do not care when I complete my ablution with which of my limbs I begin. And from Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: There is nothing wrong with starting with your feet before your hands. Al-Daraqutni said: This is mursal and is not proven. The first is the obligation of order, and God knows best. Eighteenth - If the time for ablution is missed while performing ablution, then he should not perform tayammum according to most scholars. Malik permits tayammum in such a case, because tayammum was originally introduced to preserve the time for prayer. If it were not for that, then it would be necessary to delay the prayer until water is available. The majority of scholars have cited as evidence the words of God Almighty: But if you do not find water, then perform tayammum. This is true: the condition for the validity of tayammum is missing, so he should not perform tayammum. Nineteenth - Some scholars have used this verse as evidence that removing impurity is not obligatory because He said: When you stand up for prayer and did not mention istinja’ but mentioned ablution. If removing it were obligatory, it would have been the first thing to begin with. This is the opinion of the companions of Abu Hanifa and it is the narration of Ashab from Malik. Ibn Wahb said from Malik: Removing it is obligatory in remembrance and forgetfulness. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i. Ibn Al-Qasim said: It is obligatory to remove it with remembrance, and it is dropped with forgetfulness. Abu Hanifa said: It is obligatory to remove impurity if it exceeds the size of a Baghli dirham, meaning the large one that is in the form of a mithqal - by analogy with the mouth of the usual exit that is excused. The correct narration is Ibn Wahb, “Because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the two companions of the two graves: They are being punished, but they are not being punished for a major sin. As for one of them, he used to spread gossip, and as for the other, he did not clean himself after urinating. He is not being punished except for neglecting an obligation. There is no proof in the apparent meaning of the Qur’an, because God Almighty only explained in the verse on ablution the description of ablution specifically and did not address the removal of impurity or anything else. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth - The verse also indicates wiping over the socks as we have explained. Malik has three narrations on this: denial absolutely as the Khawarij say. This narration is rejected and not authentic. The second is wiping while traveling but not while at home because most of the hadiths on wiping are only about traveling. The hadith of the shoe indicates the permissibility of wiping while at home. Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Hudhayfah, who said: I saw myself and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walking, and he came to a people’s courtyard behind a wall, so he stood up as one of you would say, and urinated, so I withdrew from him, and he motioned to me, so I came and stood at a certain place until he finished. He added in another narration: “He performed ablution and wiped over his socks.” Similar to it is the hadith of Shureih ibn Hani’, who said: I came to Aisha to ask her about wiping over the socks, so she said: Go to Ibn Abi Talib and ask him, for he used to travel with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. We asked him and he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made three days and nights for the traveler and one day and night for the resident. This is the third narration - he wipes at home and while traveling, and it has been mentioned previously. Twenty-one - According to Malik, the traveler wipes over the socks without a specific time. This is the opinion of Al-Layth bin Sa`d. Ibn Wahb said: I heard Malik say: There is a time for the people of our country to wipe over them. Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Abi bin `Amara that he said: O Messenger of God, can I wipe over the socks? He said: Yes. He said: One day? He said: One day. He said: And two days? He said: And two days. He said: And three days? He said: Yes, and whatever you wish. In another narration: Yes, and whatever you wish. Abu Dawud said: There is disagreement regarding its chain of transmission, but it is not strong. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, al-Nu’man, and al-Tabari said: The resident is permitted one day and one night, and the traveler is permitted three days, according to the hadith of Shuraih and what is similar to it. It was narrated from Malik in his letter to Harun or some of the caliphs, but his companions rejected it. The twenty-second: And wiping, according to all of them, is for someone who puts on his shoes while in a state of ritual purity, based on the hadith of Al-Mughira bin Al-Shu’ba, who said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night on a journey - the hadith - and in it, and I wanted to take off his socks, but he said: Leave them, for I put them on while they are pure. And he wiped over them. Asbagh saw that this was the purity of tayammum, and this is based on the fact that tayammum removes ritual impurity. Dawud was an exception and said: Dawud’s purity here is purity from impurity only, so if his feet are pure from impurity, then wiping over the socks is permissible. The reason for the disagreement is the sharing in the name of purity. Twenty-third - And it is permissible according to Malik to wipe over the khuff even if there is a slight tear in it: Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: Its meaning is that the tear does not prevent benefiting from it or wearing it, and it is like walking in it. And similar to what Malik said, Al-Layth, Al-Thawri, Al-Shafi’i and Al-Tabari said: It has been narrated from Al-Thawri and Al-Tabari that wiping over a torn khuff is permissible in general. And Al-Awza’i said: It is permissible over the khuff and over what is visible of the foot, and this is the saying of Al-Tabari. And Abu Hanifa said: If what is visible of the foot is less than three fingers, then it is permissible to wipe, and it is not permissible to wipe if three are visible. This is a specification that requires verification. And it is known that the khuffs of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, and others from the Followers, were not free from slight tears, and this is beyond the pale of the majority of them. And it has been narrated from Al-Shafi’i that if there is a tear in the front of the foot, then it is not permissible to wipe over it. And Al-Hasan bin Hayy said: He wipes over the khuff if what is visible of it is covered by the sock, but if part of the foot is visible, then he does not wipe. Abu Omar said: This is according to his school of thought regarding wiping over socks if they are thick, and this is the saying of Al-Thawri, Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, and it is: Twenty-fourth - It is not permissible to wipe over socks according to Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i unless they are leather. This is one of the two opinions of Malik. He has another opinion that it is not permissible to wipe over socks even if they are leather. In the book of Abu Dawud, “On the authority of Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba: Abu Dawud said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi did not narrate this hadith because it is well-known from al-Mughira that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiped over his socks and sandals. This hadith was narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash’ari from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but it is neither strong nor connected. Abu Dawud said: Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Mas’ud, al-Bara’ ibn Azib, Anas ibn Malik, Abu Umamah, Sahl ibn Sa’d, and Amr ibn Harith wiped over their socks. It was narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them all. I said: As for wiping over the shoes, Abu Muhammad al-Darimi narrated in his Musnad, Abu Naim told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Khayr, who said: I saw Ali perform ablution and wipe over his shoes, so he made room for them. He said: If I had not seen the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do as you have seen me do, I would have thought that the soles of the feet are more deserving of wiping than their outer parts. Abu Muhammad al-Darimi, may God have mercy on him, said: This hadith was abrogated by the words of God Almighty: “And wipe over your heads and your feet to the ankles.” I said: And the saying of Ali, may God be pleased with him - I would have seen that the soles of the feet are more deserving of wiping than their outer parts - is similar to what he said about wiping over the socks. Abu Dawud narrated it on his authority: He said: And if religion were based on opinion, the soles of the heels would be more deserving of wiping than their upper parts. And I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiping over the outer parts of his socks. Malik and Ash-Shafi’i said about the one who wipes the tops of his socks but not the insides: That is sufficient for him, except that Malik said: Whoever does that must repeat the time, and whoever wipes the insides of the socks but not the outsides, it is not sufficient for him and he must repeat it during the time and after it. And all of Malik’s companions said the same except for something narrated from Ashhab that he said: The insides of the socks and the outsides are the same, and whoever wipes the insides of them but not the outsides does not repeat it except during the time. And it was narrated from Ash-Shafi’i that he said: It is sufficient for him to wipe the insides of them but not the outsides, and the well-known view of the school is that whoever wipes the insides of them and limits himself to them, it is not sufficient for him and he is not wiping. Abu Hanifah and Ath-Thawri said: He wipes the outsides of the socks but not the insides, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq and a group said the same, and the preferred view according to Malik, Ash-Shafi’i and their companions is wiping the tops and bottoms, and it is the view of Ibn ‘Umar and Ibn Shihab, because Abu Dawud and Ad-Daraqutni narrated from Al-Mughirah ibn Shu’bah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution during the Battle of Tabuk, and he wiped the top and bottom of the shoe. Abu Dawud said: It was narrated that Thawr did not hear this hadith from Raja’ ibn Haywah. Twenty-fifth - They differed regarding the one who took off his socks and wiped over them, with three opinions: The first - he washes his feet in place, and if he delays, he starts the ablution again. This was said by Malik and Al-Layth, and this is what Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa and their companions said, and it was narrated from Al-Awza’i and Al-Nakha’i, but he did not mention its location. The second - he starts the ablution again. This was said by Al-Hasan bin Hayy, and it was narrated from Al-Awza’i and Al-Nakha’i. The third - he does not have to do anything and he prays as he is. This was said by Ibn Abi Laila and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and it is a narration from Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, may God be pleased with them. Twenty-sixth - The Almighty’s saying: And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, then purify yourselves. The meaning of junub and purify yourselves has already been mentioned in the lineage. He ordered washing with water. Therefore, Umar and Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with them, saw that the person in a state of major ritual impurity should not perform tayammum at all, but rather leave the prayer until he finds water. The majority of people said: Rather, this phrase is for the one who finds water. The person in a state of major ritual impurity was mentioned later in the rulings on the one who does not have water by saying: Or you have had contact with women. And contact here means sexual intercourse. It has been authenticated from Umar and Ibn Mas’ud that they returned to what the people are upon, and that the person in a state of major ritual impurity performs tayammum. The hadith of Imran bin Husayn is explicit in that, which is: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man isolated and not praying with the people, so he said: O so-and-so, what prevented you from praying with the people? He said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I was in a state of major ritual impurity and there was no water. He said: Use earth, for it will suffice you. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. Twenty-seventh - The Almighty’s saying: “And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the privy” has been presented in full in An-Nisa’. We will add here a fundamental issue that we have neglected here, which is the specification of the generality to the most common habit, for excrement is a metaphor for events that come out of the two exits, as we explained in An-Nisa’, so it is general, but most of our scholars have specified that to the usual events that come out in the usual manner. So if something unusual comes out, such as pebbles or worms, or something usual comes out in the manner of incontinence or illness, none of that would be a contradiction. Rather, they turned to the word, because no matter how much a word is established for its meaning, it is known that it is predominant in usage, and that predominant precedes the understanding of the listener in the state of generalization, and something else for which the word was created becomes distant from the mind, so it becomes not meaningful for it, and the situation in it becomes like that of an animal, for if it is generalized, the mind will precede it to quadrupeds, and the ant does not occur to the mind of the listener, so it becomes not intended nor meaningful for that word apparently. The opponent says: It does not necessitate from the predominance that the rare is not intended, for the word’s inclusion of them is one in its position, and that indicates the speaker’s awareness of them. Intentionally, the origins are more correct, and its completion is in the books of origins. Twenty-eighth - The Almighty’s saying: Or you have touched women. Ubaidah narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud that he said: Kissing is touching, and everything less than intercourse is touching. Ibn Omar said the same and Muhammad bin Yazid chose it. He said: Because he mentioned at the beginning of the verse what is required of one who has intercourse in His saying: And if you are in a state of major ritual impurity, then purify yourselves. Abdullah bin Abbas said: Touching, touching, and intercourse are intercourse, but He, the Almighty, uses a euphemism. Mujahid said regarding His saying, the Almighty, And when they pass by ill speech, they pass by with dignity (al-Furqan 25:72), he said: If they mention marriage, they use a euphemism for it. The discussion of this chapter has already been completed in women, and praise be to God. Twenty-ninth - The Almighty’s saying: And you did not find water. It was mentioned in An-Nisa’ that its absence results in the present healthy person being imprisoned or tied up, which is what is said about it: If he does not find water or soil and fears the time will run out, the jurists differed in his ruling on four opinions: The first, Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: The correct opinion according to the Maliki school of thought is that he does not pray and nothing is upon him. He said: The Medinans narrated it from Malik, who said: It is the correct opinion of the school of thought. Ibn Al-Qasim said: He prays and repeats it, and this is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i. Ashhab said: He prays and does not repeat it. Asbagh said: He does not pray and does not make up for it. Abu Hanifa said the same. Abu Omar Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: I do not know how Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad proceeded to make the correct opinion of the school of thought what he mentioned, and the majority of the predecessors, the majority of the jurists, and the group of the Malikis are against it. I think he went with the apparent meaning of the hadith of Malik, his saying: And they are not on water - the hadith - and he did not mention that they prayed, and there is no proof in this. Hisham Ibn Urwah mentioned on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha in this hadith that they prayed without ablution and he did not mention repeating it. A group of jurists held this view. Abu Thawr said: It is analogy. I said: Al-Muzani provided evidence for what Al-Kaya Al-Tabari mentioned with what was mentioned in the story of the necklace on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, when it went astray, and that the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom he sent to search for the necklace prayed without dry ablution or ablution and were informed of that, then the verse of dry ablution was revealed and he did not denounce them for doing it without ablution or dry ablution, and dry ablution, when it is not prescribed, then they prayed without purity at all. From this Al-Muzani said: And there is no repetition, and it is a text on the permissibility of prayer without purity absolutely when it is impossible to reach it. Abu Omar said: And it should not be attributed to the unconscious, because his mind is overcome and this is with his mind. Ibn al-Qasim and other scholars said: Prayer is obligatory for him if he is of sound mind. When the impediment is removed, he should perform ablution or dry ablution and pray. There are two narrations from al-Shafi’i: The well-known one from him is that he should pray as he is and repeat it. Al-Muzani said: If he is imprisoned and cannot find clean soil, he should pray and repeat it. This is the opinion of Abu Yusuf, Muhammad, al-Thawri and al-Tabari. Zafar ibn al-Hudhayl said: The imprisoned person in the city does not pray even if he finds clean soil. This is according to his principle, for he does not perform dry ablution in his city as mentioned above. Abu Umar said: Whoever says that he should pray as he is and worship if he is able to purify himself, then they are taking precautions to pray without purification. They said: And his saying, peace be upon him: God does not accept a prayer without purification for the one who is able to purify himself. As for the one who is not able, it is not like that because the time is obligatory and he is able to do it, so he prays as he estimated at the time and then repeats it, so he has taken precaution in terms of time and purification together. Those who said that he does not pray went with the apparent meaning of this hadith, which is the saying of Malik, Ibn Nafi’ and Asbagh. They said: If there is no water or soil, he does not pray and does not make up for it if the time for prayer has passed, because its not being accepted due to the lack of its conditions indicates that he is not addressed by it in the case of the lack of its conditions, so nothing is due from the conscience, so he does not make up for it. This was said by other than Abu Omar. Based on this, purity is one of the conditions of obligation. Al-Muwaffiyah Thirty - The Almighty’s saying: Then perform tayammum with clean earth. The difference of opinion regarding earth has already been mentioned in An-Nisa’, and the hadith of Imran bin Husayn is explicit in what Malik says, since if it had been earth, he would have referred it to the surface of the earth, and God knows best. Then wipe your faces and hands with it. It was mentioned in An-Nisa’ as the discussion of it, so reflect on it there. Thirty-one - If our discussion of the verses ends here, then know that the scholars have spoken about the virtue of ablution and purification, which is the conclusion of the chapter: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Purity is half of faith. Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ash’ari. It was discussed in Surat al-Baqarah. Ibn al-Arabi said: Ablution is the foundation of religion and the purity of Muslims, especially this nation in the worlds. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution and said: This is my ablution, the ablution of the prophets before me, and the ablution of my father Abraham.” This is not correct, someone else said. This does not contradict his saying, peace be upon him: For you are a sign that no one else has. They used to perform ablution. Rather, what He has singled out this nation with is the forelock and the forehead, not the ablution. These are favors from God the Most High, with which He has singled out this nation as an honor for it and for its Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, like all its virtues over all other nations, just as He has given its Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the praiseworthy station and other things over all other prophets. And God knows best. Abu Omar said: It is possible that the prophets performed ablution and thereby acquired honor and forehead, while their followers did not perform ablution, as came “On the authority of Moses, peace be upon him, he said: O Lord, I find a nation all like the prophets, so make it my nation. He said to him: That is the nation of Muhammad.” In a long hadith: Salim bin Abdullah bin Omar narrated on the authority of Ka’b al-Ahbar that he heard a man narrating that he saw a vision in a dream that the people were gathered for the reckoning, then the prophets were called with each prophet his nation, and that he saw for each prophet two lights between which he walked, and for those who followed him from his nation one light with which he walked, until he was called Muhammad, and when the hair of his head and face was all light, everyone could see it. Whoever looks at him, and those who follow him from his nation will see two lights like the lights of the prophets. Ka`b said to him, not realizing that it was a vision: Who told you this hadith and what taught you about it? Tell him that it is a vision. Ka`b recited to him: By God, there is no god but Him, I saw what you say in your dream. He said: Yes, by God, I saw that. Ka`b said: By Him in Whose Hand is my soul, or he said: By Him Who sent Muhammad with the truth, this is a description of Ahmad and his nation and a description of the prophets in the Book of God. It is as if what you say is from the Torah. He attributed it to the book Al-Tamhid. Abu `Umar said: It has been said that all nations used to perform ablution, and God knows best. I do not know of this from a sound source. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a Muslim or believing slave performs ablution and washes his face, every sin he has looked at with his eyes will be removed from his face with the water or with the last drop of water. If he washes his hands, every sin his hands have committed will be removed from his hands with the water or with the last drop of water. If he washes his feet, every sin his feet have walked on will be removed with the water or with the last drop of water, until he comes out pure from sins. The hadith of Malik on the authority of Abdullah al-Sunabhi is more complete. The correct version is Abu Abdullah, not Abdullah. This is one of the things that Malik made a mistake about. His name is Abdul Rahman ibn Usaylah, a great follower from Syria, because he lived during the first part of the caliphate of Abu Bakr. Abu Abdullah al-Sunabhi said: I came as an immigrant to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Yemen. When we reached al-Juhfah, there was a rider. We asked him, What is the report? He said, “We buried the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, three days ago.” These hadiths and similar hadiths from Amr ibn Abasa and others inform you that what is meant by them is that ablution is prescribed as an act of worship to nullify sins, and that requires a legitimate intention because it was prescribed to erase sin and raise ranks with God Almighty. Thirty-second - The Almighty’s saying: God does not want to place any difficulty upon you meaning any hardship in religion. The evidence for this is the Almighty’s saying: He has not placed any difficulty upon you in religion (al-Hajj 22:78) and from the connection meaning to place any difficulty upon you. But He wants to purify you meaning from sins as we mentioned from the hadith of Abu Hurairah and Al-Sunabhi. It was said: from ritual impurity and major ritual impurity. It was said: so that you may deserve the description of purity with which the people of obedience are described. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab read to purify you and the meaning is the same as it is said: He saved him and delivered him. And to complete His favor upon you meaning by permitting tayammum when sick or traveling. It was said: by clarifying the laws. It was said: by forgiving sins. In the hadith: The completion of the blessing is entering Paradise and being saved from Hellfire. “So that you may be grateful.” That is, so that you may be grateful for His blessing and accept His obedience.
5:7: The Almighty said: And remember the favor of God upon you and His covenant with which He bound you. It was said: It is the covenant in the Almighty's saying: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam (al-A’raf 7:172) Mujahid and others, and even if we did not mention it, the Truthful One informed us of it, so it is permissible for us to be ordered to fulfill it. It was said: It is an address to the Jews to preserve what was taken from them in the Torah, and what the majority of commentators, such as Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi, are upon is the covenant and agreement that they made with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to hear and obey in ease and hardship, when they said, We hear and obey, as happened on the night of Al-Aqaba and under the tree. And the Almighty added it to Himself, as He said: They only pledge allegiance to God (al-Fath 48:10), so they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-Aqaba to protect him from what they protect themselves, their women, and their children, and that he and his companions would travel to them. The first to pledge allegiance to him was Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, and on that night he had the praiseworthy position of trust. To the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to tighten the bond of his affair, and he said: By Him who sent you with the truth, we will protect you from what we protect our backs from, so pledge allegiance to us, O Messenger of God, for by God we are the sons of wars and the people of the circle, we inherited it from our forefathers. The famous report is in the biography of Ibn Ishaq, and the mention of the Pledge of Ridwan will come in its place. This is connected to the saying of God Almighty: Fulfill the contracts, so fulfill what they said, may God Almighty reward them for their Prophet and for Islam with good, and may God be pleased with them and satisfy them: And fear God, meaning in disobeying Him, for He is All-Knowing.
5:8: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm. The meaning of the verse was presented in An-Nisa’ and the meaning is: I have completed My favor upon you, so be persistently standing firm for God, that is, for the sake of God’s reward, so stand firm for His right and bear witness to the truth without bias towards your relatives or injustice towards your enemies. And let not the hatred of a people incite you to abandon justice and prefer aggression over the truth. This is evidence of the validity of the enemy’s judgment over his enemy in God Almighty and the validity of his testimony against him because he commanded justice even if he hated him, even if his judgment and testimony against him were not permissible with hatred for him. Since his command to be just in it had a face, the verse also indicated that the disbelief of the disbeliever does not prevent justice against him and that it should be limited to those who deserve fighting and enslavement, and that mutilating them is not permissible even if they killed our women and children and caused us grief, then it is not for us to kill them with mutilation intentionally to cause them grief and sorrow. Abdullah bin Rawahah referred to this by saying in the famous story: This is the meaning of The verse: The meaning of His statement, And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from committing an act. It was also read, And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from committing an act. Al-Kisa’i said that they are two dialects. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from committing an act. It was mentioned at the beginning of this surah: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from committing an act. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from committing an act. It was said: And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from committing an act.
5:9: The meaning of for them is forgiveness and a great reward is that God said about the believers for them is forgiveness and a great reward meaning that the understanding of creation does not know its true nature, as He said: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes (Ya-Sin 36:11). And if God the Most High said: and a great reward (al-Ma’idah 5:9) and a generous reward (Ya-Sin 36:11) and a great reward (Hud 11:11), then who can estimate its value? Since the promise is of the type of speech, it is good to insert the lam in His statement: for them is forgiveness and it is in the accusative case because it is in the position of the promised, meaning that He promised them that they will have forgiveness or He promised them forgiveness, except that the sentence is in the position of the singular, as the poet said: We have found the righteous to have a reward of gardens and springs of water. The position of the sentence is in the accusative case, and therefore it was conjoined with the accusative. It was said: It is in the nominative case, so that what was promised is omitted, based on the estimation that they will have forgiveness and a great reward for what he promised them. This meaning is from Al-Hasan.
5:10: And those who disbelieved was revealed about Banu Nadir. It was also said: about all disbelievers.
5:11: The Almighty said: O you who have believed, remember the favor of God upon you when a people were about to stretch out their hands against you. A group said: It was revealed because of the action of the Bedouin in the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa' when he drew the sword of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Who will protect you from me, O Muhammad? As mentioned in An-Nisa’ and in Al-Bukhari: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the people and they gathered while he was sitting with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he did not punish him. Al-Waqidi and Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned that he converted to Islam and some people mentioned that he hit his head on the trunk of a tree until he died. In Al-Bukhari, in the Battle of Dhat Ar-Riqa’, the man’s name is Ghawrath ibn Al-Harith with a dotted, open ghain and a silent waw followed by a ra and a tha’ with a triangle. Some of them have included the ghain, but the first is more correct. Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Idris Al-Razi and Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Umar Al-Waqidi mentioned that his name was Da’thur ibn Al-Haith and he mentioned that he converted to Islam as mentioned above. Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned that his name was Amr ibn Jahash and he was the brother of Banu An-Nadir. Some of them mentioned that the story of Amr ibn Jahash is in a story other than this one, and God knows best. Qatada, Mujahid and others said: It was revealed about a group of Jews to whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to ask for their help in paying blood money, so they intended to kill him, may God bless him and grant him peace, but God prevented him from doing so. Al-Qushayri said: The verse may be revealed in a story and then its mention is revealed again to remind of what came before. They extend their hands to you (i.e. with evil), so restrain their hands from you (i.e. prevent them).
5:12: It has three issues: God Almighty said: And God had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised up from among them twelve leaders. There are three issues: The first - Ibn Atiyah’s statement: These verses that include the report of their breaking the covenants of God Almighty strengthen that the previous verse about restraining hands was only about Banu Nadir. The people of interpretation differed about how these leaders were sent after the consensus that the leader is the chief of the people who is in charge of their affairs and who investigates them and their interests in them. The leader is the great man who is among the people in this way. From this it was said about Omar, may God be pleased with him: He was a leader. So the leaders are the guarantors, and one of them is a leader, and he is the witness of the people and their guarantor. It is said: He investigated them: and he is of good character, meaning good character. The leader and the leader are the path and in the mountain. It was only said: he investigated because he knows the inner workings of the people’s affairs and knows their virtues, and it is the path to knowing their affairs. A group of people said that the leaders are the trustees over their people. All of this is close to each other. The leader is of a higher position than the overseer. Ata’ ibn Yasar said: The bearers of the Qur’an are the overseers of the people of Paradise. Al-Darimi mentioned this in his Musnad. Qatada, may God have mercy on him, and others said: These leaders are great people from every tribe, each one of them is responsible for his tribe. That they should believe and fear God, and so on. The leaders were on the night of Aqaba, in which seventy men and two women pledged allegiance. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, chose twelve men from the seventy and named them the leaders, following the example of Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Rabi’, Al-Suddi, and others said: The pure ones from the Children of Israel were sent as trustees to investigate the tyrants and to probe their strength and defense. They set out to test the condition of those in it and inform them of what they had discovered there so that they could consider invading them. They discovered from the tyrants a great strength, as will come, and they thought that they would not be able to do so. So they agreed among themselves to hide that from the Children of Israel and to inform Moses, peace be upon him. When they returned to the Children of Israel, ten of them betrayed them, so they knew their kinship and who they had trusted with their secret. The report spread until the situation of the Children of Israel was distorted, so they said: “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here.” (al-Ma’idah 5:24) Second - In the verse there is evidence of accepting the report of one person regarding what a person needs and needs to be informed of regarding his religious and worldly needs, so rulings are based on it and what is permissible and forbidden are connected to it. And something similar to it also came in Islam: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Hawazin: Go back so that your leaders can report your matter to us.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari. Third - It also contains evidence of the use of a spy and spying, and investigation. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a spy to Basbasa. It was narrated by Muslim, and the ruling on the spy will come in Al-Mumtahanah, God willing. As for the names of the leaders of the Children of Israel, Muhammad bin Habib mentioned their names in Al-Muhaber, saying: From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua bin Rakab, from the tribe of Simeon and Shokoth bin Hori, from the tribe of Judah, Caleb bin Yokna, from the tribe of Al-Hasar, Yugol bin Joseph, from the tribe of Ephraim bin Yousef, Joshua bin Al-Nun, from the tribe of Benjamin, Yalza bin Ruqwa, from the tribe of Rabbalon, Karabil bin Soda, from the tribe of Mansha bin Yousef, Kadi bin Sosha, from the tribe of Dan, Amael bin Kesel, from the tribe of Sher-Stor bin Michael, from the tribe of Naphtal, John bin Waqosha, and from the tribe of Kadh-Kawwal bin Mukhi. The believers among them were Joshua and Caleb, and Moses, peace be upon him, called upon the others, so they perished in wrath upon them. Al-Maroudi said: As for the leaders of the night of Aqaba, they are mentioned in the biography of Ibn Ishaq, so let us look there at the words of God Almighty: And God said, ‘I am with you.’ If you establish prayer, the verse. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: He said that to the leaders. Another said: He said that to all the Children of Israel. And he broke in because it is a subject with you, accusative because it is a circumstance, meaning with victory and support. Then he began and said: If you establish prayer, until he said: I will surely remove from you your misdeeds, meaning if you do that, I will surely remove from you. The lam in if is a lam of emphasis and its meaning is an oath, and likewise from you your misdeeds, and it includes another condition for his saying: I will surely remove, meaning if you do that, I will surely remove. And it was said: His saying If you establish prayer is a reward for his saying I am with you and a condition for his saying: I will surely remove. And the ta’zir is: glorification and reverence. Abu Ubaidah recited: How many noble people are generous and there are those who are not excused in the assembly That is, to magnify and honor. Ta’zir is beating without limit and response. You say: I admonished so-and-so if you disciplined him and turned him away from evil. His statement you admonished them means you turned away their enemies from them. And you loaned God a goodly loan meaning charity. He did not say loan. This is one of the things that came from the source, unlike the source, like His statement: And God caused you to grow from the earth a plant (Nuh 71:17) So its Lord accepted it with good acceptance (Al Imran 3:37). It was mentioned before. Then it was said: goodly meaning your souls are good with it. It was said: they seek the face of God with it. It was said: permissible. It was said: loan is a noun, not a source. But whoever among you disbelieves after that meaning after the covenant has certainly strayed from the right path meaning he missed the right path. And God knows best.
5:13: The Almighty’s saying: Because they broke their covenant meaning because they broke their covenant. Ma is redundant for emphasis, according to Qatada and all other scholars, and that is because it emphasizes the speech in the sense that it is firmly established in the mind, both in terms of its good composition and in terms of its being frequent for emphasis, as he said: For something that prevails over what prevails The emphasis with a mark is like the emphasis with repetition. We cursed them. Ibn Abbas said: We punished them with the jizya. Al-Hasan and Muqatil said: By transforming. Ataa: We distanced them. Cursing is distancing and expelling from mercy. And We made their hearts hard, meaning hard, not understanding good or doing it. The harsh and the violent have the same meaning. Al-Kisa’i and Hamza read it as qasiyyah with a shaddah on the ya’ without an alif. This is the reading of Ibn Mas’ud, Al-Nakha’i, and Yahya ibn Waththab. The harsh year is the severe year in which there is no rain. It was said: It is from the qasiyyat dirhams, meaning the corrupt and bad ones. So the meaning of a division based on this is not pure faith, meaning there is spending in it. Al-Nahhas said: This is a good statement, because it is said: A qasi dirham if it is adulterated with copper or something else. It is said: A qasi dirham with a light sin and a shaddah on the ya’ for example, shaqi, meaning fake. Abu Ubaid mentioned this and recited: She has a neighing sound in the deafening silence, like a measure of bows in the hands of the money changers. Al-Asma’i and Abu Ubaid said: Kadram qasiyy as if it is an Arabized qashi. Al-Qushayri said: This is far-fetched because there is nothing in the Qur’an that is not from the language of the Arabs. Rather, the dirham qasiyy also means strength and severity because whatever you say you prick it becomes hard and solid. Al-A’mash read qasiyyah with a light ya’ on the weight of fa’la like ’amiyah and shajayyah from qasi yaqsi not from qasa yaqsu. The rest read it on the weight of fa’ila and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid and they are two languages like al-’aliyah and al-’aliyah and al-zakiyah and al-zakiyah. Abu Ja’far al-Nahhas said: It is more appropriate for it to be qasiyyah in the meaning of harsh, except that fa’ila is more eloquent than fa’ila so the meaning is: We made their hearts hard and averse to faith and success in obeying Me because the people were not described with anything of faith so their hearts would be described as having faith mixed with much like the hard dirhams that were mixed with fraud. The rajaz said: I was cruel and cruel to myself They distort the words from their places meaning they interpret them in a way other than their interpretation, and they throw that to the common people. It was said: Its meaning is they change its letters and distort in the accusative case, meaning we made their hearts hard, distorting them. As-Salami and An-Nakha'i read the words with an alif, and that is because they changed the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse of stoning. And they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of meaning they forgot the covenant of God that the prophets took from them regarding belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and explaining his description. And you will not cease to look meaning and you, O Muhammad, are still standing now on a traitor among them and treachery is betrayal, as Qatadah said. This is permissible in the language and is like their saying: A female speaker meaning a nap. It was said: It is an attribute of something omitted and the estimate is a treacherous group. Treasonous may also be used for one person, as it is said: A man is a genealogist and the sign of his treason is based on this for exaggeration. It is said: A treacherous man if you exaggerate in describing him with treason. The poet said: You told yourself to be loyal and not to be treacherous and to keep your fingers tied Ibn Abbas said: On treachery meaning disobedience. It was also said: lying and immorality. Their treachery was their breaking of the covenant between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their supporting the polytheists in their war against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, like the Day of the Confederates and other than that, of their intention to kill him and insult him. Except a few of them. They did not betray, so it is a connected exception from the ha’ and mim in betrayal from them. “So pardon them and forgive.” There are two opinions on its meaning: So pardon them and forgive as long as there is a covenant between you and them and they are people of the covenant. The other opinion is that it was abrogated by the verse of the sword. It was also said: by the words of God Almighty: But if you fear treachery from a people (al-Anfal 8:58).
5:14: The Almighty said: And of those who said, 'We are Christians,' We took their covenant meaning in monotheism and belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as it is written in the Gospel. So they forgot a portion which is belief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning they did not know what they were commanded to do and made that desire and distortion a reason for disbelief in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. We took their covenant is like saying: I took from Zayd his garment and his dirham. Al-Akhfash said: And he arranged those so that it would come after we took and before the covenant, so the meaning would be: We took from those who said, 'We are Christians, their covenant because ah is in the position of the second object of we took" and its meaning according to the Kufians is: And of those who said, 'We are Christians,' from those who We took their covenant. So the ha and the mim refer to the deleted "and of and according to the first opinion they refer to those and it is not permissible so that it does not precede We took their covenant" from those who said, 'We are Christians' nor the softest of clothes she wore. So that an implied word does not precede an explicit word. In their saying, We are Christians, and not saying from the Christians, there is evidence that they innovated Christianity and called themselves by it. Its meaning was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan. God the Almighty said: So We stirred up among them enmity and hatred meaning We stirred up. It was said: We stuck to them is taken from glue, which is what sticks one thing to another, like gum and the like. It is said: He was enamored with something yaghra bil-shay yaghra he was enamored with it with a fatha over the ghain and a sukoon over the ghain, and ghara he was enamored with it with a kasra over the ghain, extended, if he was passionate about it as if he stuck to it. Al-Rummani said: Ighra means dominating some of them over others. It was said: Ighra means incitement, and its root is glue. It is said: I ghara bil-rajul Ighra, shortened and extended, the first letter is open if I stuck to him. Katheer said: If you say, "Slow down, the eye says, With tears, it is beautiful," and its rims are full of water. And I tempted Zaid with such and such until he tempted him with it. From this comes the word ghara which means to cling to it. So tempting with something means to stick to it by way of domination over it. And I tempted the ram, meaning I made him crazy with hunting. Between them is a circumstance of enmity and hatred. Hatred. He referred with this to the Jews and Christians because they were mentioned previously by Al-Suddi and Qatadah: Some of them are enemies to each other. And it was said: He referred to the division of the Christians in particular. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said that they are the closest mentioned, and that is because they split into the Jacobites, Nestorians, and Melkites, meaning some of them disbelieved in each other. Al-Nahhas said: Among the best things that have been said about the meaning of So We stirred up enmity and hatred among them is that God Almighty commanded enmity and hatred towards the disbelievers. Every group is commanded enmity and hatred towards them because they are disbelievers. And His statement: And God will inform them is a threat to them, meaning they will receive the punishment for breaking the covenant.
5:15: The Almighty said: O People of the Book The Book is a generic noun meaning books, so all of them are addressed. There has come to you Our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, making clear to you much of what you used to conceal of the Book meaning of your books, such as belief in him, the verse of stoning, and the story of the Sabbath-breakers who were transformed into monkeys, for they used to conceal it. And he pardons much meaning he leaves it and does not explain it. Rather, he explains what is in it an argument for his prophethood, and as evidence of truthfulness and testimony to his message, and he leaves what there is no need to explain. It was said: And he pardons much meaning he overlooks much and does not inform you of it. It was mentioned that a man from their rabbis came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him, saying: O man, have you pardoned us? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him and did not clarify. Rather, the Jew wanted to show that his words contradicted them. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not clarify them to him, he got up from him and went and said to his companions: I see that he is truthful in what he says because he found in his book that it did not clarify to him what he asked about. There has come to you from God a light meaning a radiance. It was said: Islam. It was said: Muhammad, peace be upon him, according to Al-Zajjaj. And a clear Book meaning the Qur’an, for it clarifies the rulings and it has been mentioned previously.
5:16: With it God guides whoever follows His pleasure meaning what God is pleased with "the paths of peace" the roads of safety leading to the abode of safety free from every affliction, and safe from every fear, which is Paradise. Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi said: "Peace" is God, the Almighty, so the meaning is the religion of God, which is Islam, as He said: Indeed, the religion in the sight of God is Islam (Al Imran 3:19) And He brings them out from darknesses into the light meaning from the darkness of disbelief and ignorance to the light of Islam and guidance by His permission meaning by His success and will.
5:17: The Almighty’s saying: They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘God is the Messiah, son of Mary.’ This was explained and discussed at the end of An-Nisa’. The Christians’ disbelief in the meaning of this statement was only because they said, God is the Messiah, son of Mary, in terms of their being inferior to Him, because if they had said it in terms of narration, denying Him, they would not have disbelieved. Say, ‘Then who has control over God at all?’ That is, of God’s command. Then owns means has power, from their saying, I have control over so-and-so, that is, I have power over him. So who can prevent anything from that? So God, the Almighty, informed us that if the Messiah were a god, he would have been able to repel what would befall him or someone else, and he caused his mother to die and was not able to repel death from her. So if he were to destroy him as well, who could prevent him from doing that or turn him back? And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them. The Messiah and his mother are two limited and restricted creatures, and what is encompassed by the limit and the end is not suitable for divinity. He said, and what is between them, and did not say, and what is between them, because He meant the two types and halves, as Al-Ra’i said: Ways, those are my worries. The poorest of them are two fertile camels like the bow and the squint. He said: Knock. Then he said: These are my concerns. He creates what He wills. Jesus from a mother without a father is a sign for his worship.
5:18: The Almighty said: And the Jews and the Christians say, 'We are the sons of God and His beloved.' Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, frightened some of the Jews with punishment, but they said: We are not afraid, for we are the sons of God and His beloved. So the verse was revealed. Ibn Ishaq said: Nu'man ibn Ada', Bahri ibn Amr, and Sha's ibn Adi came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they spoke to him and all of them, and he called them to God Almighty and warned them of His vengeance. They said: What do you frighten us with, O Muhammad? We are the sons of God and His beloved, as the Christians say, so God Almighty revealed about them: And the Jews and the Christians say, ‘We are the sons of God and His beloved.’ Say, ‘Then why does He punish you for your sins?’ to the end of the verse. Muadh bin Jabal, Saad bin Ubadah, and Uqbah bin Wahb said to them: O group of Jews, fear Him, for by God, you know that he is the Messenger of God, and you used to mention him to us before his mission and you used to protect him for us by his description. Rafi’ bin Huraymila and Wahb bin Judah said: We did not say this to you, nor did God send down a book after Moses, nor did He send a bearer of good tidings or a warner after him. So God Almighty revealed: O People of the Scripture, there has come to you Our Messenger making clear to you, after a hiatus of messengers. to His saying: And God is over all things competent. Al-Suddi said: The Jews claimed that God Almighty revealed to Israel, peace be upon him, that your son is the firstborn of the offspring. Another one said: And the Christians said, We are the sons of God, because in the Gospel there is a narration about Jesus, Go to my father and your father. It was said that the meaning is: We are the sons of the Messenger of God, so it is an omission of an added word. In short, they saw for themselves. He responded to their statement by saying: Why does He punish you for your sins? They were not without one of two aspects: either they say He punishes us, and it is said to them: Then you are not His children and beloved, for the beloved does not excuse his beloved, and you acknowledge His punishment, so that is evidence of your lie - and this is what the dialecticians call the proof of the contradiction - or they say: He does not punish us, so they deny what is in their books and what their messengers brought, and they permit sins while they acknowledge the punishment of the disobedient among them, and for this reason they adhere to the rulings of their books. It was said: The meaning of He punishes you is He punished you: it is in the sense of the past, so why did He transform you into apes and pigs and did not punish those before you from the Jews and Christians with various types of punishment while they are like you? Because God Almighty does not argue with them with something that has not yet happened, because they may say we will not punish tomorrow, rather He argues with them with what they know. Then He said: Rather, you are human beings from among those He created, meaning like the rest of His creation. He holds you accountable for obedience and disobedience and rewards each according to what he did. He forgives whom He wills, meaning for whoever repents from the Jews. And He punishes whom He wills from what is on it. And to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, so He has no partner who can oppose Him. And to Him is the final destination, meaning the matter of the servants will return to Him in the Hereafter.
5:19: The Almighty said: O People of the Book, there has come to you Our Messenger meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace making clear to you the cessation of their argument so that they will not say tomorrow, No Messenger has come "after a period of silence between the messengers" meaning a lull. It is said that something has stopped and it has been said: "after a period" is the cessation between the prophets from Ibn Ali, a group of scholars narrated it, Al-Rumani said: The origin of it is the cessation of work from what it was in terms of seriousness in it from their saying: He stopped working and stopped working from it. From this, the water stopped when it stopped from being hot to cold. And a woman who is lukewarm in her eyes, meaning she is cut off from the sharpness of her gaze and the lukewarmness of the body is like the lukewarmness of water. The period is what is between the index finger and the thumb if you open it. The meaning is: that is, a period of time passed for the messengers. There is disagreement about the length of that period. Muhammad bin Saad mentioned in the book of classes on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were between Moses bin Ammar and Jesus bin Maryam, peace be upon them, a thousand years and seven hundred years and there was no period between them and that a thousand prophets from the Children of Israel were sent between them in addition to those who were sent from others and there was between The birth of Jesus and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was five hundred and sixty-nine years. In the beginning of it, three prophets were sent, and this is what God Almighty said: When We sent to them two, but they denied them, so We reinforced them with a third. (Ya-Sin 36:14) The one who was reinforced was Simon, who was one of the disciples. The period in which God did not send a messenger was four hundred and thirty-four years. Al-Kalbi mentioned that between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, there were five hundred and sixty-nine years, and between them there were four prophets, one of whom was from the Arabs from Banu Abs, and he was Khalid bin Sinan. Al-Qushayri said: And something like this is not done except with report and truth. Qatada said: There were six hundred years between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them. Muqatil, Al-Dahhak, and Wahb bin Munabbih said the same, except that Wahb added twenty years. Al-Dahhak also said four hundred and thirty-some years. Ibn Saad mentioned on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Between Adam and Noah there were ten centuries, all of them upon Islam. Ibn Saad said: Muhammad bin Omar bin Waqid Al-Aslami informed us on the authority of more than one person, who said: There were ten horns between Adam and Noah, and a horn is one hundred years, and between Noah and Adam there were ten years. And Abraham is ten centuries, and a century is a hundred years, and between Abraham and Moses, son of Imran, there are ten centuries, and a century is a hundred years, so this is what is between Adam and Muhammad, peace be upon them, of centuries and years, and God knows best. That you say means lest or out of hatred that you say, so it is a place of accusative There has not come to us a bearer of good tidings meaning a bearer of good tidings nor a warner meaning a warner, and it is permissible to say nor a bearer of good tidings nor a warner in the place. Ibn Abbas said: Muadh bin Jabal, Saad bin Ubadah, and Uqbah bin Wahb said to the Jews: O group of Jews, fear God, for by God you know that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and you used to mention him to us before his mission and describe him by his description, so they said: God did not send down a book after Moses, nor did He send after him a bearer of good tidings or a warner, so the verse was revealed: And God is over all things competent to send whomever He wills from His creation, and it was said: He is competent to fulfill what He gave good tidings of and warned of.
5:20: God Almighty said: And when Moses said to his people, ‘O my people, remember the favor of God upon you.’ It was made clear from God Almighty that their ancestors rebelled against Moses and disobeyed him, so these are against Muhammad, peace be upon him, as a consolation for him, that is, O you who believe, remember the favor of God upon you, and remember the story of Moses. It was narrated from Abdullah bin Kathir that he read O my people, remember with a damma on the meem, and that is what resembles it, and its meaning is O people, When He made prophets among you, it was not declined because it contains the feminine alif, And made you kings, that is, you control your affairs and no one can overcome you after you were owned by Pharaoh, subdued, so he saved you from him by drowning, so they are kings in this way, and similarly Al-Suddi, Al-Hasan, and others explained it. Al-Suddi said: Each one of them owned himself, his family, and his money. Qatada said: He only said: And made you kings because we used to say that they were the first to serve from the children of Adam. Ibn Atiyah said: This is weak because the Copts used to employ the children of Israel, and the apparent matter of the children of Adam is that some of them used to make others serve since they multiplied and increased, and the nations differed only in the meaning of ownership. It was said: He made you people of houses, and no one enters upon you except with permission. Its meaning was narrated from a group of people of knowledge. Ibn Abbas said: If a man does not have anyone enter his house except with his permission, then he is a king. And from Al-Hasan and Zaid bin Aslam also: Whoever has a house, a wife and a servant, then he is a king. This is the saying of Abdullah bin Amr as in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Halabi, who said: I heard Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas and a man asked him, saying: Are we not among the poor immigrants? Abdullah said to him: Do you have a wife to whom you can take refuge? He said: Yes. He said: Do you have a house to live in? He said: Yes. He said: Then you are among the rich. He said: I have a servant. He said: Then you are one of the kings. Ibn al-Arabi said: The benefit of this is that if a man is required to pay expiation and he owns a house and a servant, he sells them as expiation and fasting is not permissible for him because he is able to free a slave, and kings do not pay expiation by fasting and are not described as incapable of freeing slaves. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: He made them kings with manna and quails and stones and clouds, meaning they are served like kings. And from Ibn Abbas also: He means the servant and the house. And Mujahid, Ikrimah and al-Hakam ibn Uyaynah said it, and they added the wife. And Zayd ibn Aslam said the same, except that he said, as is known - “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever has a house - or he said a home - to which he can take refuge, a wife, and a servant who serves him, then he is a king. This was mentioned by An-Nahhas. It is said: Whoever is independent of others is a king. This is as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever wakes up safe in his home, healthy in his body, and has his daily sustenance, it is as if the entire world has been given to him.” The Almighty said: And He gave you meaning He gave you what He has not given to anyone in the worlds. The address is from Moses to his people according to the majority of commentators, and this is the correct interpretation. Mujahid: What is meant by giving is manna, quails, stones, and clouds. It was also said: the large number of prophets among them and the signs that came to them. It was also said: hearts free from rancor and deceit. It was also said: the permissibility of spoils and benefiting from them. I said: This statement is rejected, because the spoils of war were not permissible for anyone except this nation, according to what was proven in the Sahih, and its explanation will come, God willing. This statement from Moses was to prepare them for it, so that they would be strengthened and take the command to enter the land of the tyrants with force, and to carry out in that the influence of one whom God has honored and raised his status. The meaning of of the worlds is the worldly people of your time, according to Al-Hasan. Ibn Jubayr and Abu Malik said: The address is to the mother of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is a deviation from the apparent meaning of the statement, in a way that is not appropriate. The reports have converged that Damascus is the base of the tyrants.
5:21: The Holy means the purified. Mujahid: blessed and the blessing, purification from drought, hunger and the like. Qatada: it is the Levant. Mujahid: the Tur and what is around it, and Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd: it is Jericho. Al-Zajjaj said: Damascus and Palestine and some: Jordan. Qatada's statement includes all of this. Which God has decreed for you means He has imposed its entry upon you and promised you its entry and its habitation. When the Children of Israel left Egypt, He ordered them to fight the people of Jericho in the land of Palestine. They said: We have no knowledge of those lands. So He sent, by the command of God, twelve leaders from each tribe, a man, to spy on the report as mentioned above. They saw its inhabitants, the giants of the giants, who had enormous bodies. It was even said: Some of them saw these leaders, so he took them in his sleeve with fruit he had carried from his garden and brought them to the king, so he scattered them before him and said: These people want to fight us. The king said to them: Go back to your master and tell him our report as mentioned above. It was said: When they They returned and took a bunch of grapes from that land. It was said that one man carried it, and it was said that he had the twelve captains. I said: This is more likely, because it is said that when they reached the tyrants, they found that two of them were carrying a bunch of grapes in their sleeves, and one of them carried a bunch of grapes on a piece of wood, and if a seed fell, a few or four of them would enter into the pomegranate. I said: There is no contradiction between this and the first, for that tyrant who took them in his sleeve, or it is said in his lap, was Awh ibn Anaq, and he was the tallest of them in stature and the most magnificent of them in character, as will come of his mention, God willing. The height of the rest of them was six and a half cubits, according to Muqatil. Al-Kalbi said: The height of each man among them was eighty cubits, and God knows best. So when they spread the report, except for Joshua and Caleb ibn Yuqana, and the Children of Israel refrained from jihad, they were punished by wandering for forty years until those disobedient ones died and their children grew up and fought the tyrants and defeated them. God Almighty says: And do not turn back meaning do not turn back from obeying Me and what I have commanded you to do of fighting the tyrants. It has been said: Do not turn back from obeying God to disobedience, and the meaning is the same.
5:22: The Almighty said: They said, O Moses, indeed therein are a people of tyrants meaning tall bodies. It was said before: a tyrant palm tree, meaning tall. The tyrant is the one who is haughty and resistant to humiliation and poverty. Al-Zajjaj said: The tyrant of mankind is the arrogant, and he is the one who forces people to do what he wants. Its origin according to this is the compulsion, which is coercion, as he forces others to do what he wants. And he forced him, meaning he forced him. It was said that it is taken from the bone fracture, so the origin of the tyrant according to this is the one who reforms his own affairs. Then it was used for everyone who brought benefit to himself, whether right or wrong. It was said: The bone fracture goes back to the meaning of coercion. Al-Farra' said: I did not hear a verb from the verb and diraka from diraka. Then it was said: These were from the remnants of Aad. It was said: They are from the descendants of Esau, son of Isaac, and they were from the Romans. And with them was Ujj al-A'naq, and his height was three thousand cubits and three hundred and three cubits. Ibn Omar said that he used to pull the clouds, meaning he would pull them with his stick and drink from them, and he would take the fish from the bottom of the sea. He roasted it in the sun by raising it to it and then ate it. He attended the flood of Noah, peace be upon him, and he had not yet reached his knees. He was three thousand six hundred years old. He pulled out a rock the size of Moses’ army to crush them with it, but God sent a bird that pecked at it and it fell on his neck and knocked him down. Moses, peace be upon him, came forward, and his height was ten cubits, and his staff was ten cubits, and he ascended ten cubits into the sky, but he did not hit anything except the Kaaba while he was knocked down, so he killed him. It was also said: Rather, he struck him in the vein under his heel and knocked him down, so he died. He fell on the Nile of Egypt and bridged them for a year. This meaning was mentioned with different wordings by Muhammad ibn Ishaq, al-Tabari, Makki, and others. Al-Kalbi said: Awj was from the children of Harut and Marut when they had intercourse with the woman and she became pregnant, and God knows best. The Almighty said: And indeed, we will never enter it meaning the town of Aelia, and it is said: Jericho: until they leave it meaning until they surrender it to us without fighting. It was said: They said that out of fear of the tyrants and did not intend disobedience, for they said: But if they leave it, then we will enter.
5:23: The Almighty said: Two men from among those who feared said. Ibn Abbas and others said: They are Joshua and Caleb bin Yuqana, and it is said that Ibn Qania, and they were among the twelve leaders. They fear means from the tyrants: Qatada feared God Almighty. Ad-Dahhak said: They are two men who were in the city of the tyrants, following the religion of Moses. So the meaning of they fear according to this is from the giants in terms of nature, lest they find out about their oaths and tempt them, but they trusted in God. And it was said: They feared the weakness and cowardice of the Children of Israel. Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr read they fear with a damma on the ya', and this strengthens that they were not from the people of Moses. God has bestowed His favor upon them, meaning with Islam or with certainty and righteousness. Enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will be victorious. They said to the Children of Israel, Do not be frightened by the size of their bodies, for their hearts were filled with terror of you, for their bodies were large and their hearts were weak. And they had known that if they Entering through that door, they were victorious. It is possible that they said that out of trust in God’s promise. Then they said: And upon God rely, if you are believers, believing in Him, for He will grant you victory. Then it was said, according to the first statement, when they said this, the Children of Israel wanted to stone them and said: We believe you and leave the statement of ten!
5:24: Then they said to Moses: We will never enter it as long as they are in it. This is a single act of stubbornness against fighting, and despair of victory. Then they were ignorant of the description of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, so they said: Then go, you and your Lord. They described Him as going and moving, and God is exalted above that. This indicates that they were anthropomorphists, and this is the meaning of what Al-Hasan said, because he said: It is disbelief on their part in God, and this is the most apparent meaning of this statement. It was said: That is, your Lord's support for you is more deserving of our support, and His fighting with you, if you are His Messenger, is more deserving than fighting us. So on this basis, this is disbelief on their part, because they doubted his message. It was said that the meaning is: Go, you, and fight, and let your Lord help you. It was said: By the Lord, they meant Aaron, and he was older than Moses, and Moses used to obey him. In short, they were corrupt in their statement, because God Almighty said: So do not grieve over the corrupt people, meaning do not grieve over them. Indeed, we are sitting here, meaning we will not leave or fight. Sitting is permissible in the state because the statement has It was done before.
5:25: The Almighty said: He said, 'My Lord, I have no control over anyone but myself and my brother,' because he was obeying him. It was said that the meaning is: I have no control over anyone but myself. Then He began and said: And my brother, meaning that my brother also has no control over anyone but himself. So my brother, according to the first statement, is in the accusative case in apposition to myself, and according to the second statement, it is in the nominative case. If you wish, you can apposition it to the name of in, which is the letter ya, meaning that I and my brother have no control over anyone but ourselves. So separate us from the wicked people. It is said: In what way did he ask him about the difference between him and these people? In it are the answers of the first - which indicates their distance from the truth and their deviation from the right path in what they committed of disobedience, and for this reason they were thrown into the wilderness. The second - by requesting distinction, meaning distinguish us from their group and their whole, and do not include us with them in the punishment. It was said that the meaning is: So judge between us and them by protecting us from the disobedience with which You afflicted them. From this is the Almighty's statement: Therein is distinguished every matter of wisdom. (al-Dukhan 44:4) meaning He judges, and He did when He caused them to die in The wilderness. It was said: What he meant in the end is, make us in Paradise and do not make us with them in Hell. The evidence for the difference that indicates the distance in conditions is the poet’s saying: Oh God, separate him from me as much as you separate two people. Ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Amr bin Dinar on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair that he read: So separate with a kasra on the ra. God Almighty said: “He said: ‘Then it is forbidden to them for forty years, while they wander throughout the land.’” God’s desirability of supplicating to Him and punishing them in the wilderness for forty years. The origin of wandering in the free language is said from it: he wandered, wanders, wanders, wanders, and wanders, if he is confused, and he wandered, wanders, and wanders, with the letter ya and the letter waw, and the letter ya is more common. The land is the wandering in which no transgression is committed, and the land and wandering, and from it he said: I am lost in the misery Another said: In a deserted wilderness, the mounts, like the sad cat, were laying their eggs. They would travel a few farsakhs, and it was said: about six farsakhs, their day and night, so they would go in the morning where they went in the evening and stay in the evening where they went in the morning, so they were wandering and had no rest. There was a difference of opinion as to whether Moses and Aaron were with them, and it was said: No, because the wandering was a punishment, and the years of the wandering were the number of days of the calf, so they were treated as a year for each day, and He said: So separate us from the wicked people. It was said: They were with them, but God made the matter easy for them, just as He makes the fire cool and safe for Abraham.
5:26: The meaning of forbidden is that they are forbidden from entering it, as is said: Your face is forbidden to the fire, and you are forbidden from entering the house. So it is a prohibition of prevention, not a prohibition of legislation, according to most of the people of interpretation, as the poet said: She came to defeat me, so I told her to stop. Where is a man who defeats you? It is forbidden. Yes, he is a knight, so he cannot be defeated. Abu Ali said: It is possible that it is a prohibition of worship. It is said: How is it possible for a large group of rational people to travel for easy leagues and not be guided to get out of it? The answer is that Abu Ali said: It may be that God changes the land they are on when they sleep, returning them to the place they started from. It may be due to other than that, such as confusion and reasons preventing them from getting out of it by way of an unusual miracle. Forty is a time adverb for wandering, according to Al-Hasan and Qatadah. They said: None of them entered it, so the pause on this is on upon them. Al-Rabi’ bin Asan and others said: Forty years is a time adverb for prohibition, so the pause on this is on forty years. According to the first, only their children entered it, as Ibn Abbas said. None of them remained except Joshua and Caleb, so Joshua went out from them with their children to that city and conquered it. According to the second, whoever remained from them worshipped for forty years and entered it. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that Moses and Aaron died in the wilderness. Another said: And God informed Joshua.
