And he ordered him to fight the tyrants, and in it the sun was held back from him until he entered the city, and in it he burned the one who had the spoils of war with him, and a white fire would descend from the sky if they took spoils, and it would consume the spoils, and that was evidence of its acceptance, and if there was spoils of war in it, it would not consume it, and the wild beasts and beasts came and consumed it, so the fire descended and did not consume what they had taken, so he said: There is spoils among you, so let every tribe pledge allegiance to me, so they pledged allegiance to him, and the hand of one of them stuck to his hand, so he said: There is spoils of war among you, so let every man of you pledge allegiance to me, so they pledged allegiance to him, man by man, until the hand of one of them stuck to his hand, so he said: You have the spoils of war, so he took out a gold like the head of a cow, so the fire descended and consumed the spoils, and it was a white fire like silver, it had a rustling sound like the sound of trees and the wing of a bird, according to what they mentioned, so they mentioned that he burned the spoils of war and his belongings in a deep place, oh now a deep place of helplessness, known by the name of the Ghul, and his name was helpless I said: And from this we learn the punishment of the transgressor before us: And his ruling has been presented in our religion, and the clarification of what was unclear about the name of the Prophet and the transgressor in the authentic hadith on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: A prophet of the prophets invaded. The hadith was narrated by Muslim, in which he said: “So he raided and approached the village at the time of the afternoon prayer or close to that, and said to the sun, ‘You are commanded, but as for the commanded, O God, hold it back for me for a while.’ So it held it back for him until God granted him victory.” He said: So they gathered what they had taken as booty, and the fire came to consume it, but it refused to feed it, so he said: ‘There is treachery among you, so let a man from each tribe pledge allegiance to me.’ So they pledged allegiance to him. He said: So his hand stuck to the hand of two or three men, and he said: ‘There is treachery among you.’” He mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above. Our scholars said: The wisdom in holding back the sun for Joshua when he fought the people of Jericho and was looking forward to conquering it on Friday evening, and his fear that the sun would set before the conquest was that if it had not been held back for him, it would have been forbidden for him to fight because of the Sabbath, and their enemy would know about it and use the sword against them and sweep them away. So that was a sign for him that was given to a servant, since his prophethood was established by the report of Moses, peace be upon him, according to what is said. And God knows best. In this hadith, he, peace be upon him, says: The spoils of war were not permissible for anyone before us. It is mentioned that God, the Almighty, saw our weakness and inability, so He made them permissible for us. This refutes the statement of those who said in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And He has given you that which He has not given to anyone in the worlds, that it is the permissibility of the spoils of war and benefiting from them. Among those who said that Moses, peace be upon him, died in the wilderness are Amr bin Maymun and Al-Awdi. He added: And Aaron. They went out in the wilderness to some caves, and Aaron died, so Moses buried him and returned to the Children of Israel. They said: What did Aaron do? He said: He died. They said: You lied, but I killed him because of our love for him, and he was loved by the Children of Israel. So God, the Almighty, revealed to him to go with them to his grave, for He sent him to inform them that he died a death that you did not kill. So he went with them to his grave and called out, O Aaron, and he came out of his grave shaking his head. He said: Did I kill you? He said: No, but I died. He said: Then return to your bed and leave. Al-Hasan said: Moses did not die in the wilderness. Another said: Moses conquered Jericho and Joshua was at the forefront of him, so he fought the giants. Those who were in it, then Moses entered it with the Children of Israel and stayed in it as long as God willed him to stay, then God Almighty took him to Himself and no one from creation knew about his grave. Al-Tha’labi said: And it is the most correct of the sayings. I said that Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: “The Angel of Death was sent to Moses, peace be upon him, and when he came to him, he slapped him and put out his eye. He returned to his Lord and said: You sent me to a servant who does not want to die. God restored his eye to him and said: Go back to him and tell him to place his hand on the back of a bull, and for every hair that his hand covers he will have a year.” He said: O Lord, then what? He said: Then death. He said: Then now. So he asked God to send him from the Holy Land, a stone’s throw away. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: If I were there, I would show you his grave on the side of the road under the red sand dune. So our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, knew his grave and described its location, and he saw him standing there praying, as in the hadith. However, it is possible that God hid it from the creation other than him and did not make it famous among them. Perhaps that was so that he would not be worshipped, and God knows best. By the road he means the road to Jerusalem, and in some narrations it is on the side of the mountain instead of the road. The scholars differed in the interpretation of Moses slapping the Angel of Death in the eye and putting it out, according to some sayings, including: that it was an imaginary eye, not a real one. This is false because it leads to the fact that what the prophets see of the images of angels has no reality.. Among them: that it was a spiritual eye and he only gouged it out with an argument and this is a metaphor not a reality. Among them: that he, peace be upon him, did not know the Angel of Death and that he saw a man enter his house without his permission wanting to kill himself, so he defended himself and slapped his eye and gouged it out. Defense is obligatory in this with everything possible and this is a good view because it is a reality in the eye and the slap. Imam Abu Bakr bin Khuzaymah said it, but he objected to it with what is in the hadith, which is that when the Angel of Death returned to God Almighty, he said: O Lord, You sent me to a servant who does not want death. If Moses did not know him, the statement of the Angel of Death would not be true. Also, his saying in the other narration: Answer your Lord indicates his identification of himself and God knows best. Among them: that Moses, peace be upon him, was quick to anger. If he became angry, smoke would rise from his skullcap and he would raise the hair of his body and his cloak, and the speed of his anger was the reason for the Angel of Death slapping him. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is as you see, for the prophets are infallible and such a thing would not happen from them initially in pleasure and anger. Among them, and this is the correct of these statements: that Moses, peace be upon him, knew the Angel of Death and that he came to take his soul, but he came as one who is certain that he had already He ordered his soul to be taken without choice, and Moses had what our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had stated: God does not take the soul of a prophet until he gives him a choice. So when it came to him in a way that was not known to him, he hastened with his chivalry and strength of soul to discipline him and slapped him and put out his eye as a test for the Angel of Death, since he did not give him a choice. What indicates the correctness of this is that when the Angel of Death returned to him and gave him the choice between the sons of snakes and death, he chose death and submitted, and God is the wisest and most knowledgeable in His unseen. This is the most correct of what has been said about the death of Moses, peace be upon him. The commentators have mentioned stories and reports about this, and God knows best their correctness. In Sahih, there is no need for them. Moses lived one hundred and twenty years. It is narrated that Joshua saw him after his death in a dream and said to him: How did you find death? He said: Like a sheep that is skinned while it is alive. This is the correct meaning of “He said, may God bless him and grant him peace” in the Sahih hadith. Death has its agonies, as we explained in the Book of Remembrance. His saying: So do not grieve over the wicked people means do not be sad. Grief and sadness are sorrow, I despair, sorrow, meaning sadness. He said: They say, Don't perish in grief and bear it.
5:27: There are two issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam in truth The verse The connection between this verse and what preceded it is the warning from God Almighty that the injustice of the Jews and their breaking of covenants and agreements is like the injustice of a son of Adam to his brother The meaning: If these Jews intend to kill you, O Muhammad, they killed the prophets before you and killed Cain and Abel, and evil is ancient, meaning their mention of this story is a true story, unlike the fabricated hadiths. In that is a rebuke to those who oppose Islam and a consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. There is disagreement about the two sons of Adam. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: They were not from his loins, they were two men from the Prophet of Israel, God used them as an example to demonstrate the envy of the Jews, and there was a dispute between them, so they offered two sacrifices, and sacrifices were only made among the children of Israel. Ibn Atiyah said: This is an illusion, and how could one of the children of Israel be ignorant of the form of burial until he followed the example of a raven? The correct view is that they are his sons from his loins. This is the view of the majority of commentators, and Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, and others said the same, and they are Cain and Abel, and Cain’s sacrifice was a bundle of spinach - because he was a farmer. And he chose it from the worst of their crops, then he found in it a good ear of grain, so he rubbed it and ate it. And Abel’s sacrifice was a ram, because he was a shepherd, and he took it from the best of his sheep. It was accepted, so it was raised to Paradise, and it continued to graze it until it was sacrificed to the one who was sacrificed, peace be upon him. This was said by Saeed bin Jubair and others. So when Abel’s sacrifice was accepted, because he was a believer, Cain said to him out of envy, because he was a disbeliever: Do you walk on the earth and people see you as better than me?! I will kill you. It was said: The reason for this sacrifice is that Eve, peace be upon her, used to give birth in every womb to a male and a female - except for Shih, peace be upon him, for she gave birth to him alone instead of Abel, as will come, and his name is Hebat God, because Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to Eve when she gave birth to him, This is a gift from God to you instead of Abel. And Adam, when Seth was born, was one hundred and thirty years old. He used to marry the male from this womb to the female from the other womb, and his twin sister was not permissible for him. So she gave birth to a beautiful sister with Cain, whose name was Aqlimia, and with Abel a sister who was not like that, and he named her to Judah. So when Adam wanted to marry them, Cain said: I have more right to my sister. So Adam ordered him, but he did not obey, and he rebuked him, but he did not refrain. So they agreed on the approximation. This was said by a group of commentators, including Ibn Mas`ud. It was narrated that Adam was present at that, and God knows best. It was narrated in this chapter about Ja`far al-Sadiq: Adam did not marry his daughter to his son, and if Adam had done that, he would not have turned away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor was Adam’s religion anything but the religion of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. God's peace and blessings be upon him, and that when God sent Adam and Eve down to earth and brought them together, Eve gave birth to a daughter and named her Anaq. She rebelled and was the first rebel on the face of the earth, so God empowered someone to kill her. Then she gave birth to Cain for Adam, then she gave birth to Abel. When Cain reached puberty, God revealed to him a jinn from the children of the jinn called Jamalah in human form. God revealed to Adam that he should marry her to Cain, so he married her to him. When Abel reached puberty, God sent down to Adam a houri in human form and created a womb for her, and her name was Zala. When Abel looked at her, he loved her, so God commanded Adam to marry Zala to Abel, so he did. Cain said: O my father, am I not older than my brother? He said: Yes. He said: I was more deserving of what you did to him than he was. Adam said to him: O my son, God has commanded me to do this, and grace is in God's hand, and He gives it to whomever He wills. He said: No, by God, but you preferred him over me. Adam said: So offer an offering, and whichever of you accepts his offering is more deserving of the grace. I said: I do not think this story about Ja'far is correct, and what we have mentioned is that he used to marry the boy of this clan to the girl of that clan, and the evidence for this from the Book is the Almighty’s saying: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. (An-Nisa’: 1) This is like the text, then it was abrogated as was explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah, and all that Eve gave birth to were forty of them, male and female, in twenty clans, the first of them was Qabil and his twin Iqlimā’ and the last of them was Abd Al-Mughīth, then God blessed the offspring of Adam. Ibn Abbas said: Adam did not die until he reached the age of forty thousand, and his children gave birth to forty thousand. And what was narrated from Ja'far from his saying: So she gave birth to a daughter and that she rebelled, it is said: With whom did she rebel? With a jinn begging her? And something like this needs a correct transmission that cuts off the excuse, and that is non-existent, and God knows best. Second - In the statement of Abel: God only accepts from those who fear Him, the words before it are omitted because when Cain said to him: I will kill you, he said to him: Why did you kill me when I have done nothing wrong? Nor is I to blame for what God said about my sacrifice, for I feared Him and was in love with the truth. And God only accepts from those who fear Him. Ibn Atiyyah said: What is meant by piety here is avoiding polytheism by consensus of the people of the Sunnah. So whoever fears Him while he is a monotheist, then his deeds in which his intention is sincere are accepted. As for the one who avoids polytheism and sins, then he has the highest degree of acceptance and the seal with mercy. This is known by the information of God the Most High, not that this is obligatory upon God the Most High in reason. Adi bin Thabit and others said: The sacrifice of the pious of this nation is prayer. I said: This is specific to a type of worship. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: “Whoever shows enmity to a friend of Mine, I declare war against him. My servant does not draw near to Me with anything more beloved to Me than what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues to draw near to Me with voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I am his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him, and if he seeks refuge in Me, I will surely grant him refuge. I do not hesitate about anything I do as I hesitate about the soul of a believer. He hates death, but I hate to hurt him.”
5:28: There are two issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: If you stretch out your hand against me the verse means if you intend to kill me, then I do not intend to kill you, so this is surrender from him. And in the hadith: If there is a trial, then be like the story of the son of Adam. And Abu Dawud narrated: “On the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, he said: I said, O Messenger of God: If he enters my house and shows me directions to kill me? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Be like the best of the sons of Adam, and he recited this verse: “If you should stretch out your hand against me to kill me.” Mujahid said: It was obligatory upon him at that time that no one should draw a sword and that he should not resist whoever wanted to kill him. Our scholars said: This is something that may be mentioned as an act of worship, except that in our law it is permissible to push him away unanimously, and there is a difference of opinion regarding the obligation of that upon him. The most correct opinion is that it is obligatory because it forbids evil. Among the literalists are some who do not permit the one who is being attacked to push him away, and they cited as evidence the hadith of Abu Dharr, and the scholars interpreted it as meaning that fighting should be abandoned in times of strife and refraining from fighting when there is doubt, as we explained in the book of At-Tadhkirah. Abdullah ibn Amr and the majority of people said: Abel was stronger than Cain, but he was cautious. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is what is most apparent, and from here it is strengthened that Cain was a sinner, not a disbeliever, because if he were a disbeliever, there would be no reason for being cautious here. Rather, the reason for being cautious in this is that the one who is cautious refuses to fight a monotheist and is content to be wronged in order to be punished in the Hereafter. And something similar to this is what Uthman may God be pleased with him did. It was said: The meaning is I do not intend to kill you, but I intend to defend myself. Based on this, it was said: He was asleep, then Cain came and smashed his head with a stone, as will come. A person’s defense of someone who wants to oppress him is permissible, even if it comes at the expense of the common man. It was said: If you start by killing me, I will not start by killing. It was said: He meant: If you stretch out your hand against me unjustly, then I am not an oppressor. I fear God, Lord of the Worlds.
5:29: The second - the Almighty’s saying: I want you to bear my sin and your sin. It was said that its meaning is the meaning of “the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.” If two Muslims meet with their swords, then the killing and the killed will go to Hell. It was said: O Messenger of God, this is the killing, so what about the killed? He said: He was keen on killing his companion. “It is as if Abel meant that I am not keen on killing you, so the sin that would have burdened me if I had been keen on killing you, I want you to bear it along with your sin in killing me. It was also said that the meaning is with my sin that is specific to me in what I neglected, meaning that it will be taken from my bad deeds and placed upon you because of your injustice towards me, and you will bear your sin in killing me. This is supported by his saying, peace be upon him: On the Day of Resurrection, the oppressor and the oppressed will be brought, and some of the oppressor’s good deeds will be taken and added to the good deeds of the oppressed until he is avenged. If he has no good deeds, some of the oppressed’s bad deeds will be taken and added to him. This was narrated by Muslim with the same meaning, and it was mentioned earlier. It is supported by the words of God Almighty: “And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens with their own burdens” (al-Ankabut 29:13). This is clear and there is no doubt about it. It was said: The meaning is that I want you not to bear my sin and your sin, as God Almighty said: And He has cast into the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with you (al-Nahl 16:15), meaning lest it should shake with you. God Almighty said: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray (An-Nisa’: 176), meaning lest you go astray, so la was omitted. I said: This is weak, because he, peace be upon him, said: No soul is killed unjustly except that the first son of Adam will bear a share of its blood, because he was the first to institute killing. “This proves that the sin of killing is a sin, and for this reason most scholars said: The meaning is that you will bear the sin of killing me and the sin you committed before killing me.” Al-Tha’labi said: This is the general opinion of most of the commentators. It was said: It is a question, meaning or do I mean in the manner of denial, like the saying of God the Almighty: And that is a blessing (Ash-Shu’ara’: 22) meaning or that is a blessing. This is because the will to kill is a sin. Al-Qushayri narrated it. Al-Hasan bin Kaysan was first asked: How does the believer want to sin and enter the Fire? He said: The will only occurred after he stretched out his hand to kill me, and the meaning is: If you stretched out your hand to kill me, I will refrain from that, desiring the reward. It was said to him: How did he say: With my sin and your sin, and what sin is there for him if he kills? He said: There are three answers, one of which is that you will bear the sin of killing me and the sin of your sin because of which your sacrifice was not accepted. This statement is narrated from Mujahid. The other view is that you will bear the sin of killing me and the sin of Your aggression against him because he may be sinful for the aggression even if he did not kill. The third aspect is that if he extended his hand to him, he would be sinful, so he saw that if he refrained from that, his sin would return to its owner, so this became like your saying: The money is between him and Zayd, meaning the money is between them, so the meaning is that you will bear our sin, and the origin of the ba’a returns to the maba’a, which is the home. And they incurred the wrath of God (al-Baqarah 2:61) meaning they returned, and it has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah in full. The poet said: Will you not stop with us, kings, and protect our sacred places? Blood will not be repaid with blood. That is, blood does not return for blood in retaliation. Then you will be among the companions of the Fire is evidence that at that time they were accountable and the promise and threat had reached them. And evidence was given by the words of Abel to his brother Cain, Then you will be among the companions of the Fire, that he was a disbeliever, because the word companions of the Fire only refers to disbelievers wherever it occurs in the Qur’an. This is refuted here by what we have mentioned from the scholars in interpreting the verse. The meaning of among the companions of the Fire is the duration of your being in it, and God knows best.
5:30: It has four issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: So his soul complied with him meaning his soul made the matter easy for him and encouraged him and made it appear to him that killing his brother was easy for him. It is said: The thing obeyed means it was easy and submissive, and so-and-so complied with it for him meaning he made it easy. Al-Harawi said: It complied and obeyed are one. It is said: He obeyed him if he did it willingly. It was also said: His soul complied with him in killing his brother, so the preposition was removed and it was erected. It was narrated that he did not know how to kill him, so Satan came with a bird - or another animal - and began to smash his head between two stones so that Cain would follow his example, so he did. Ibn Jurayj, Mujahid, and others said. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud said: He found him sleeping, so he smashed his head with a stone. That was in Thawr - a mountain in Mecca - Ibn Abbas said. It was also said: At the Hira Pass, narrated by Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari. Ja’far al-Sadiq said: In Basra, in the location of the Great Mosque, and Abel was twenty years old on the day Cain killed him. It is said: Cain knew how to kill by nature because even if a person did not see killing, he did so. He knew by nature that the soul is mortal and can be destroyed, so he took a stone and killed him in the land of An-Nahd. God knows best. Why did he kill him? He regretted it and sat crying at his head when two crows came and fought, and one of them killed the other. Then he dug a hole for him and buried him. The killer did the same to his brother. The private parts are meant as private parts. It was also said that it is the corpse of the one killed. Then he fled to the land of Aden in Yemen, and Satan came to him and said: The fire ate your brother’s sacrifice because he worshipped fire. So you also set up a fire for yourself and your descendants. So he built a house of fire, and he was the first to worship fire, according to what was said. And God knows best. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that when he killed him and Adam in Mecca, the trees became cramped, the foods changed, the fruits became sour, the waters became salty, and the earth became dusty. Adam, peace be upon him, said: Something has happened on earth. So he went to India and found that Cain had killed Abel. It was said that Cain was the one who turned to Adam. When he reached him, he said to him: Where is Abel? He said: I do not know, as if you had entrusted me with his protection. Adam said to him: Did you do it?! By God, he calls out, O God, curse the land that drank the blood of Abel. It was narrated that since then no land has drunk blood. Then Adam remained for a hundred years without laughing until an angel came to him and said to him, May God give you life, O Adam, and your home. He said, What is your home? He said, It made you laugh. This was said by Mujahid and Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d. When Adam’s life had reached one hundred and thirty years, which was five years after killing Abel, she gave birth to something for him, and its interpretation is God’s gift, meaning a successor from Abel. Muqatil said, Before Cain killed Abel, wild beasts and birds were comforted by Adam, but when Cain killed Abel, they fled, and the birds took to the air and the wild beasts took to the forests. It was narrated that when the situation changed, Adam said: The country and its people have changed, and the face of the earth is dusty and ugly. In many verses mentioned by al-Tha’labi and others, Ibn Atiyyah said: And this is how poetry is with the accusative of bashasha. How is the tanween? Al-Qushayri and others said: Ibn Abbas said: Adam did not say poetry, and Muhammad and all the prophets are equal in prohibiting poetry. But when Abel was killed, Adam mourned him, and he is Syriac, so it is an elegy in the Syriac language, which he recommended to his son Seth and said: You are my successor, so memorize these words from me so that they may be inherited. So I memorized them from him until the time of Ya’rub bin Qahtan, so Ya’rub translated it into Arabic and made it poetry. Second - It was narrated on the authority of Anas who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the third day, and he said: It is the day of blood, on which Eve menstruated and on which the son of Adam killed his brother. It was proven in Sahih Muslim and others on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No soul is killed unjustly, except that the first son of Adam will have a share of its blood, because he was the one who instituted killing. This is a clear explanation of the reasoning, and based on this consideration, Satan will have a share of the sin of everyone who disobeyed by prostrating, because he was the first to disobey by doing so. Likewise: whoever introduces into the religion of God something that is not permissible, such as innovations and whims. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever establishes a bad practice in Islam will bear its burden and the burden of whoever knows of it until the Day of Resurrection.” This is a text in the hadith and the evil. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “What I fear most for my nation are the misguided imams.” All of this is clear and a correct text in the meaning of the verse. This is unless the doer repents from that sin, because Adam, peace be upon him, was the first to disobey in eating what he was forbidden from, and there is no sin upon him from those who disobeyed by eating or drinking what he was forbidden from among those who came after him, by consensus, because Adam repented from that and God accepted his repentance, so he became as if he had not committed a sin. Another aspect is that he ate forgetfully, according to the correct opinion, as we explained in Al-Baqarah, and the forgetful person is not sinful nor held accountable. Third: This verse includes a statement about the state of the envious person, to the point that his envy may lead him to destroy himself by killing the people closest to him in kinship, the closest to him in blood, and the most deserving of compassion and protection from harm. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: So he became one of the losers, meaning one of those who lost his good deeds. Mujahid said: One of the killer’s legs was hung by its shin to its thigh from that day until the Day of Resurrection, and his face was towards the sun wherever it turned. In the summer, there was a fence of fire over him, and in the winter, there was a fence of snow over him. Ibn Atiyyah said: If this is correct, then it is from his loss that is included in the Almighty’s saying: So he became one of the losers, otherwise, loss includes loss in this world and the hereafter. I said: Perhaps this is his punishment for saying that he is a sinner and not an infidel, so the meaning is so he became among the losers, meaning in this world, and God knows best.
5:31: It has five issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: Then God sent a crow scratching the ground. Mujahid said: God sent two crows and they fought until one of them killed the other, then dug up and buried him. This son of Adam was the first to be killed. It was said: The crow scratched the ground for his food to hide it until the time of need for it, because it is the habit of the crow to do that, so Cain was reminded by that of burying his brother. It was narrated that when Cain killed Abel, he put him in a bag and walked with him carrying him around his neck for a hundred years. Mujahid said this. Ibn al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Malik that he carried him for one year, and Ibn Abbas said this. It was said: Until I went back and he did not know what to do with him until he followed the example of the crow, as mentioned above. In the report, “On the authority of Anas, he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God bestowed three blessings upon the son of Adam: the wind after the soul, had it not been that the wind comes after the soul, no intimate friend would have been buried; the worms in the corpse, had it not been that worms come into the corpse, kings would have hoarded it, and you would have been better for them than dirhams and dinars; and death after old age, for a man grows old until he becomes bored with himself and his family, children and relatives become bored with him, so death was more concealing for him. Some people said: Qabil knew how to bury, but he left his brother in the open, belittling him. So God sent a raven to search for dirt for Abel to bury him, and he said at that time: “Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this raven and cover my brother’s shame?” So he became one of the regretful ones. When he saw God’s honoring of Abel by seizing the raven to cover him, that was not the regret of repentance. It was said: His regret was for losing him, not for killing him, and if it was, he did not fulfill his conditions, or he regretted but his regret did not continue. Ibn Abbas said: If his regret was for killing him, then the regret would have been repentance from him. It is said: Adam and Eve came His grave and they cried for days over him. Then, Qabil was on the top of a rope and a bull gored him, so he fell to the bottom and his veins were scattered. It is said that Adam prayed against him and the earth swallowed him up. It is said that Qabil became lonely after killing Abel and stuck to the wilderness. He was not able to eat anything except wild animals. So if he caught one, he would throw it until it died and then eat it. Ibn Abbas said: So the animal that was struck was forbidden from the time of Qabil, son of Adam, and he was the first of the humans to be driven to the Fire. This is what God Almighty said: Our Lord, show us those who led us astray from among the jinn and mankind. (Fussilat 41:29) The verse. So Iblis is the head of the disbelievers among the jinn and Qabil is the head of sin among mankind, as will be explained in Ha Mim Fussilat, God willing. It has been said that regret at that time was not repentance, and God knows best and is wiser about all of that. The apparent meaning of the verse is that Abel was the first of the sons of Adam to die, and for this reason the Sunnah of burial was unknown. Al-Tabari also narrated on the authority of Ibn Ishaq on the authority of some of the people of knowledge regarding what is in the books of the ancients. His saying is that he is searching. It means he searches the dirt with his beak and stirs it up. From this, Surah Bara’ah was named Al-Buhuth because it searched for the hypocrites. From this, the poet said: People covered me, so I covered myself from them, and if they searched me, they would search me. In the proverb, do not be like someone searching for a code. The poet said: She was like a bad goat, she went with her foot to a buried knife, to stir it up. The second - God sent the crow to bury him so that he could show the son of Adam how to bury him, and this is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: Then he caused him to die and buried him (Abasa 80:21). So the crow’s action in burying became a tradition that remains among creation, an obligation upon all people, and whoever among them does it, its obligation is dropped from the rest. The people most specifically affected by it are the closest people who are closest to him, then the neighbors, then the rest of the Muslims. As for the infidels, Abu Dawud narrated. I said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Your uncle the old man has died. He said, Go and bury your father in the dirt, then do not say anything until you come to me. So I went and buried him, then I came to him, and he ordered me to wash myself and pray for me. Third: It is recommended that the grave be spacious and well-maintained, as Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Hisham bin Aamer, may God be pleased with him, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Dig, expand and improve. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Adra’ Al-Salami that he said: One night I came to guard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there was a man reciting the Qur’an loudly. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out and I said: O Messenger of God, this is a hypocrite. He said: So he died in Medina and they finished preparing him and carried his bier. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Be gentle with him, may God be gentle with him, for he loved God and His Messenger. He said: And he attended his grave and said: Make room for him, may God make room for him. Some of his companions said: O Messenger of God, I am sad about him. He said: Yes, he loved God and His Messenger. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Bakr Ibn Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Zayd Ibn Al-Habbab, on the authority of Musa Ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Saeed Ibn Abi Saad. Abu Omar Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: Adra’ Al-Sammali narrated one hadith from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Saeed Ibn Abi Saeed Al-Maqburi narrated from him. As for Hisham Ibn Aarem Ibn Umayyah Ibn Al-Hashas Ibn Aarem Ibn Ghanim Ibn Adi Ibn Al-Najjar Al-Ansari, he was called Shahb in the pre-Islamic era, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, changed his name and named him Hisham. His father Amer was martyred on the day of Uhud. Hisham lived in Basra and died there. This is mentioned in the Book of the Companions. Fourth - Then it was said, the grave is better than the cleft, because it is what God chose for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When he died, there were two men in the city, one of whom was practicing lahd and the other was not. They said: Which of them came or did what he did? So the one who practiced lahd came and dug a lahd for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Malik mentioned this in Al-Muwatta’ on the authority of Hisham ibn Umar on the authority of his father, and Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Anas ibn Malik and Aisha, may God be pleased with them both. The two men were Abu Talha and Abu Ubaidah. Abu Talha used to dig a lahd and Abu Ubaidah used to hoe it. A lahd is to dig a hole in the side of a grave if it is hard soil, and the dead person is placed in it, then bricks are placed on him, then dirt is covered. Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas said in the illness in which he died: Dig a grave for me and set up bricks over me as was done for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Narrated by Muslim. Ibn Majah and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The grave is ours and the crack is for others. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: I attended Ibn Omar’s funeral, and when he placed him in the grave, he said: In the name of God, for the sake of God, and according to the religion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he began to level the bricks on the grave, he said: O God, save her from Satan and from the torment of the grave. O God, make the earth smooth from her sides and let her soul ascend and grant her pleasure from You. I said: O Ibn Umar, did you hear something from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or did you say it on your own? He said: Then I am able to say something, but rather something I heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He prayed over the funeral, then he came to the grave of the dead person and threw stones at him from his head three times. This is what is related to the meaning of the verse from the rulings. The origin of “Oh woe to me, oh woe to me” is then an alif from the ya’. Al-Hasan read it according to the origin with the ya’, and the first is more eloquent, because deleting the ya’ in calling is more common, and it is a word that the Arabs call upon at the time of death. Sibawayh said: Al-Asma’i said: Woe after. Al-Hasan read I am unable with a kasra on the jim. Al-Nahhas said: It is an irregular language. It is only said that a woman is unable if her buttocks are large and she is unable to do something, inability, miracle, and miracle. And God knows best.
5:32: The Almighty says: Because of that meaning as a result of that murderer and his crime. Al-Zajjaj said: Meaning because of his crime. It is said: A man has committed an evil against his people. He is punished for it if he has committed a crime, like he took, he takes, he took. Al-Khanout said: The people of Salih's tent, among whom I was, fought over something urgent that I was postponing. Any of his neighbors. It was said: I am their neighbor. Adi bin Zaid said: Yes, God has favored you over the most pious, the most virtuous. Its origin is the jarr, and from it is the ajal because it is a time to which the first contract is drawn, and from it is the ajal, the opposite of the calf, and it means that a previous matter is drawn to it, and from it is ajal meaning yes because it is submission to what it is drawn to, and from it is the ajal for the herd of wild cows because some of it is drawn to some, as Al-Rumani said, and Yazid bin Al-Qaqa Abu Ja`far read: for the sake of that with a kasra on the noon and the deletion of the hamza, and it is a language, and the origin is for the sake of that, so the kasra of the hamza was placed on the noon and the hamza was deleted, then it was said: It is permissible for his saying: for the sake of that to be related to his saying: of the regretters, so stopping at his saying: for the sake of that, it is permissible for it to be related to what comes after it, which is We wrote, so for the sake of: the beginning of the complete speech of the regretters, and on this most people, meaning from the reason for this calamity We wrote, and the Children of Israel were specifically mentioned, and nations before them preceded them in which killing a soul was forbidden because they were the first nation upon whom the threat of killing souls was written down, and before that it was an absolute statement, so the matter was made severe for the Children of Israel by the book according to Their tyranny and bloodshed. The meaning of without a soul is without killing a soul, in which case he deserves to be killed. God has forbidden killing in all religions except for three reasons: disbelief after faith, adultery after marriage, or killing a soul unjustly and aggressively. or corruption on earth means polytheism. It has also been said: highway robbery. Al-Hasan read or corruption in the accusative case, assuming that a verb was omitted that indicates the beginning of the speech, which is or caused corruption. The evidence for this is his statement: Whoever kills a soul without a soul, because it is one of the greatest forms of corruption. The common people read corruption in the accusative case with the meaning of or without corruption it is as if he had killed all of mankind. The wording of the commentators was confused in the arrangement of this simile because the punishment of one who killed all of mankind is greater than the punishment of one who killed one. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The meaning is that whoever killed a prophet or a just imam is as if he had killed all of mankind. And whoever saved him by strengthening his arm and supporting him is as if he had saved all of mankind. And from him also that he said: The meaning is that whoever killed one soul and violated its sanctity is like one who killed all of mankind. And whoever left killing one soul and protected its sanctity and saved it out of fear of God is like one who saved all of mankind. And from him also the meaning is that it is as if he had killed all of mankind at the time of the one killed. And whoever saved it and rescued it from destruction is as if he had saved all of mankind at the time of the rescuer. And Mujahid said: The meaning is that whoever kills a believing soul intentionally, God will make his punishment Hell and become angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment. He says: If he had killed all of mankind, it would not have increased beyond that. And whoever did not kill, then people were saved from him. And Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is that whoever kills a soul is required to be punished in retaliation and retribution as is required of whoever kills all people. He said: And whoever saves a soul means whoever pardons someone who must be killed. Al-Hasan also said it means pardon after being able to do so. It was said: The meaning is that whoever kills a soul, all the believers are his opponents because he has killed everyone. And whoever saves a soul, it is as if he has saved all people, meaning everyone must thank him. And say: He made the sin of the killer of one the sin of the killer of all, and he has the right to rule as he wishes. And it was said: This was specific to the Children of Israel to make it difficult for them. Ibn Atiyah said: In short, the comparison, as it was said, is all true, and the one who violates one is observed by the same one who violates all. An example of this is two men who circumambulated two trees, so that they would not eat from their fruit. One of them ate one of the fruits of his tree, and the other ate the fruit of his entire tree. They are equal in their perjury. It was said: The meaning is that whoever considers one permissible has considered all permissible because he has denied the law. And in the words of God Almighty: And whoever saves it it is an exaggeration, because it is an expression of abandonment and rescue from destruction. Otherwise, the revival is the reality, which is the invention - but It belongs to God Almighty, and this revival is like the words of the accursed Nimrod, I give life and cause death (al-Baqarah 2:258). So he called abandonment revival, then God informed about the Children of Israel that the messengers came to them with clear proofs, and that most of them transgressed the limit and abandoned God’s command.
5:33: It contains fifteen questions: First: People differed about the reason for the revelation of this verse. The majority are of the opinion that it was revealed about the two Arabs. The imams narrated, and the wording is from Abu Dawud, on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “A group of people from ‘Ukl - or he said from his den - came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they chose Medina. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they be given camels and ordered them to drink from their urine and milk. They set out, and when they recovered, they killed the shepherd of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and drove away the camels. report of them reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, early in the day, so he sent after them. When the day had risen, they were brought to him. He ordered that their hands and feet be cut off, their eyes be nailed, and they were thrown into the lava field to draw water, but they were not given water.” Abu Qilabah said: These were people who stole, killed, and disbelieved after their faith, and fought God and His Messenger. In another narration: So he ordered that nails be heated, and he applied kohl to them, and he cut off their hands and feet, but he did not cauterize them. In another narration: “So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a tracker in pursuit of them, and they were brought to him.” He said: Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed concerning that: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption in the land Al-Ansari 2:170. In another narration, Anas said: I saw one of them hitting the ground with his mouth out of thirst until they died. In Bukhari, Jarir bin Abdullah said in a hadith: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me with a group of Muslims until we caught up with them and they had reached their country. We brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Jarir said: They used to say water and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say fire. The historians and biographers have related that they cut off the shepherd’s hands and feet and stuck thorns in his eyes until he died and was brought to the city dead. His name was Yasar and he was Nubian. This action was done by the apostates in the year six of the Hijra. In some narrations on the authority of Anas: “That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, burned them with fire after killing them.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak: It was revealed because of a group of the People of the Book who had a treaty with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they broke the treaty, cut off the way, and spread corruption on earth. In the Musannaf of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger to His saying is Forgiving and Merciful. This verse was revealed about the polytheists, so whoever takes from them before he is able to do so, that does not prevent him from having the punishment he inflicted on him carried out. Among those who said that the verse was revealed about the polytheists are Ikrimah and al-Hasan, and this is weak and is refuted by the words of God Almighty: Say to those who disbelieve, if they desist, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them. (al-Anfal 8:38) And his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Islam destroys what came before it. Narrated by Muslim, and the first authentic hadith is the one that is authentic in this regard. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, and the people of opinion said: The verse was revealed regarding those who went out from among the Muslims, cutting off the way and spreading corruption in the land. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The statement of Malik is correct. Abu Thawr said, providing evidence for this statement: The verse is evidence that it was revealed regarding other than the people of polytheism, which is the statement of God, the Most High: Except for those who repent before you have them in your power. They agreed that if the people of polytheism fall into our hands and become Muslims, their blood is forbidden. This indicates that the verse was revealed regarding the people of Islam. Al-Tabari narrated from some of the people of knowledge: This verse abrogated the action of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the two thieves, so the matter stopped at these limits. Muhammad bin Sirin narrated: This was before the limits were revealed, meaning the hadith of Anas, mentioned by Abu Dawud. Some of them, including Al-Layth bin Sa’d, said: What the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did with the delegation of ‘Uraynah was abrogated, since it is not permissible to mutilate the apostate. Abu Al-Zinad said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not cut off the hand of those who stole. He vaccinated him and blinded their eyes with fire. God Almighty rebuked him for that, so God Almighty revealed about that: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon earth to cause corruption is that they be killed or crucified. The verse was narrated by Abu Dawud. Abu Al-Zinad said: When he was admonished and forbidden from mutilation, he did not return to it. It was narrated from a group that this verse does not abrogate that action because that occurred to those who had apostatized, especially since it was proven in Sahih Muslim and the book of Al-Nasa’i and others that he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only blinded the eyes of those people because they had blinded the eyes of shepherds, so this was retribution, and this verse is about the believing warrior. I said: This is a good statement and it is the meaning of what Malik and Al-Shafi’i went to. Therefore, God the Almighty said: Except those who repent before you have them in your power. It is known that the rulings on the infidels do not differ in the removal of punishment from them by repentance after being able to do so, just as it is dropped before being able to do so. The apostate deserves to be killed for the same apostasy - without fighting - and he is not exiled, nor is his hand or foot cut off, nor is he released, but rather he is killed if he does not convert to Islam, nor is he crucified either. This indicates that what the verse includes is what the apostate meant. God the Almighty said regarding the infidels: Say to those who disbelieve, if they desist, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them. And He said regarding the fighters: Except those who repent. The verse. This is clear, and based on what we have stated at the beginning of the chapter, there is no problem, no blame, and no reproach, since it is required by the Book. God the Almighty said: But whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you. (al-Baqarah 2:194) So they mutilated them, and they were mutilated. However, it is possible that the reproach, if it is correct, is for the increase in killing, which is by tying their eyes with red-hot nails and leaving them thirsty until they died. And God knows best. Al-Tabari narrated on the authority of Al-Suddi: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not blind the eyes of the two Arabs.” Rather, he intended that, so the verse prohibiting that was revealed. This is very weak, because the established reports about blinding were reported in Sahih Al-Bukhari: So he ordered nails to be heated and he applied kohl to them. There is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that the ruling of this verse applies to those who fight among the people of Islam, even if it was revealed about the apostates or the Jews. In the words of God the Most High: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger there is a metaphor and a figure of speech, because God the Most High does not fight or overcome because of the attributes of perfection that He has and because of the transcendence and peers that are required of Him. The meaning is: They fight the friends of God, so He used His noble self to refer to His friends, in order to magnify their harm, just as He used His self to refer to the poor and weak in His words: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan? (al-Baqarah 2:245), urging compassion for them. And similarly in Sahih Sunnah: I asked you for food but you did not feed me. The hadith was narrated by Muslim, and it was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. The second - and the scholars differed about who deserves the name of the warrior. Malik said: The warrior according to us is the one who attacks people in Egypt or in the wilderness and defies them in terms of themselves and their money without any motive, neither humiliation nor enmity. Ibn al-Mundhir said: There is a difference of opinion regarding Malik on this issue. He affirmed the warrior in the city once and denied it once. A group said: The ruling on that in the city or in the homes and roads and the homes of the people of the desert and the villages is the same and their borders are the same. This is the opinion of al-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This is how it is because the name of the warrior applies to both of them and the book is general and no one has the right to exclude people from the scope of the verse without proof. A group said: The warrior does not occur in the city, but rather outside the city. This is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri, Ishaq and al-Nu’man. The assassin is like the warrior, and he is the one who schemes to kill a person in order to take his money, even if he does not brandish a weapon for the one who enters his house or accompanies him on a journey, so he feeds him poison and kills him, so he is killed as a prescribed punishment, not as retaliation. Third - They differed in the ruling on the bandit. A group said: He is to be punished according to what is due to him. Whoever frightens the way and takes money, his hand and foot are to be cut off from opposite sides. If he takes money and kills, his hand and foot are to be cut off and then crucified. If he kills and does not take money, he is to be killed. If he does not take money and does not kill, he is to be banished. This was said by Ibn Abbas. It was narrated from Abu Majlaz, Al-Nakha’i, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and others. Abu Yusuf said: If he takes money and kills, he is to be crucified and killed on the wood. Al-Layth said: Crucified by freedom. Abu Hanifa said: If he kills, he is to be killed. If he takes money and does not kill, his hand and foot are to be cut off from opposite sides. If he takes money and kills, the ruler has a choice in this matter. If he wishes, he does not cut off, kills him, and crucifies him. Abu Yusuf said: Killing comes for everything, and something similar to what Al-Awza’i said. Al-Shafi’i said: If he takes money, his right hand is to be cut off and his left foot is to be cut off and he is to be released, because this crime is more than theft by banditry. If he kills, he is to be killed. If he takes money and kills, he is to be killed and crucified. It was narrated from him that he said: He is to be crucified for three days. He said: If it is present and widespread and is a deterrent to the enemy, he is to be imprisoned. He said: Ahmad: If he kills, he is killed, and if he takes the money, his hand and foot are cut off, as Al-Shafi’i said. Some people said: He should not be crucified before being killed, so that he is prevented from praying, eating and drinking. It was narrated from Al-Shafi’i: I hate that he be killed while crucified, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade mutilation. Abu Thawr said: The imam has a choice according to the apparent meaning of the verse. Malik said the same, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and it is the saying of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Omar bin Abdul Aziz, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and An-Nakha’i. They all said: The imam has a choice in ruling on the combatants. He rules on them with any of the rulings that God the Most High has made obligatory, such as killing, crucifixion, amputation or exile, according to the apparent meaning of the verse. Ibn Abbas said: Whatever is in the Qur’an or its owner has a choice. This saying is more indicative of the apparent meaning of the verse, because the people of the first saying who said that or is for order - even if they differed - you will find their sayings that they combine two punishments for him, so they say: He is killed and crucified. Some of them say: He is crucified and killed. Some of them say: His hand and foot are cut off and he is exiled. This is not the case with the verse, nor is the meaning of or in the language. An-Nahhas said: The first one argued with what At-Tabari mentioned, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel, peace be upon him, about the ruling on the one who fights, so he said: Whoever frightens people on the road and takes money, cut off his hand for taking it and his foot for frightening people, and whoever kills, kill him, and whoever combines that, crucify him. Ibn Atiyah said: “The banishment remains for the one who frightens only, and the one who frightens is in the ruling on the killer, and despite that, Malik sees in it taking the least punishment and punishment as preferable.” Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: Or they are banished from the land. There is a difference of opinion regarding its meaning. Al-Suddi said: It is that he is constantly sought by horse and foot until he is captured and the punishment of God is carried out on him, or he leaves the abode of Islam fleeing from whoever is seeking him. This was narrated by Ibn Abbas, Anas bin Malik, Malik bin Anas, Al-Hasan, Al-Suddi, Al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, and Al-Zuhri. Al-Rumani narrated it in his books. He narrated from Al-Shafi’i that they are taken from one country to another and sought out so that the punishments are carried out on them. Al-Layth bin Sa’d and Al-Zuhri also said this. Malik also said that the Kufians said that their banishment is their imprisonment, so he is banished from the vastness of the world to its narrowness, so it is as if if he is imprisoned he has been banished from the land except for his place of settlement. They provided evidence for that by the saying of some of the people of the prisons: We left this world while we were its people, so we are neither among the dead nor the living. If the jailer comes to us one day with a need, we are surprised and say, This came from this world. Makhul narrated that Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was the first to be imprisoned. He said, I will imprison him until I know that he has repented, and I will not banish him from one country to another so that he will harm them. It appears that the land in the verse is the land of the calamity, and people in the past avoided the land in which they committed sins. This is evident from the hadith. Those who are far away from us are the land and the sanctuary. And if this warrior is feared and he thinks that he will return to banditry or corruption, the imam should imprison him in the country to which he is exiled. And if he is not feared and he thinks that he will not return to the crime of being released, Ibn Atiyah said: This is the explicit opinion of Malik that he should be exiled and imprisoned when he is exiled. This is most likely because he is feared, and al-Tabari preferred it, and it is clear because his exile from the land to which he descended is the text of the verse, and his imprisonment after removing the fear from him. If he repents and the state of release is understood, he is released. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: Or they are banished from the land. The origin of negation is destruction, and from it comes affirmation and negation. So negation is destruction by annihilation, and from it comes the word nafaya for the return of goods, and from it comes the banishment of what flies from the water from the bucket. Al-Zajer said: As if his back is as far away as the birds on the fine sand. Sixth - Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: The money taken by the bandit is not taken into consideration as it is taken into consideration for the thief. It has been said: The quarter of a dinar is taken into consideration in that. Ibn al-Arabi said: Al-Shafi’i and the people of opinion said: A highway robber is not to be cut off except for the one who takes an amount that would cut off the hand of a thief. Malik said: He is to be judged according to the ruling of the bandit, and this is correct, for God Almighty set on the tongue of His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, cutting off the hand for theft is a quarter of a dinar, and He did not set anything for banditry, but rather He mentioned the punishment of the bandit, so He required that the punishment be paid to them for the war for a grain. Then this analogy is a principle upon a principle, and it is disputed, and the analogy of the higher to the lower and the lower to the lower, and this is the opposite of analogy. How can it be correct to compare the bandit to the leg when he seeks to steal money, so if he senses him, he flees, so that if the thief enters with a weapon seeking money, then if he is prevented from it or shouted at and fought over, then he is a bandit, and he is judged according to the ruling of the bandit? Judge Ibn al-Arabi said: When I was in the days of my judgment among the people, if someone came to me with a thief who had entered the house with a knife, I would hold him against the heart of the owner of the house while he was asleep and his companions were taking the man’s money, I would rule on them according to the ruling of the bandits, so understand. This is the origin of religion, and they rose to the heights of knowledge from the depths of the pit at the bottom of the valley. This is what the linguists said. Seventh - There is no disagreement that in highway robbery the one who killed is killed even if the one killed is not equal to the killer. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions, one of them - that it is considered a reward because he killed, so the reward is considered in it like retaliation. This is weak because the killing here is not for mere killing, but rather it is for general corruption such as intimidation and theft of money. God Almighty said: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to spread corruption in the land is that they will be killed. So God Almighty commanded the implementation of the limits on the highway robber if he combined two things, war and striving to spread corruption in the land, and He did not distinguish between the noble and the lowly, nor the high and the lowly. Eighth - If the warriors go out and fight with the caravan, and some of the warriors are killed and some are not, then all of them are killed. Al-Shafi’i said: Only those who are killed are killed. This is also weak, because those who are present at the battle are partners in the spoils, even if not all of them are killed. We have agreed on killing the vanguard, which is the vanguard, so the warrior is more deserving. Ninth - If the warriors frighten the wayfarer and block the road, it is obligatory for the Imam to fight them without calling them, and it is obligatory for the Muslims to cooperate in killing them and stopping them from harming the Muslims. If they are defeated, no one should be pursued who runs away from them unless he has killed and taken money. If that is the case, he should be pursued to be taken and what is due for his crime should be done to him. No one should be killed from them unless he has killed. If they are taken and money belonging to a specific person is found in their hands, it should be returned to him or to his heirs. If no owner is found for it, it should be placed in the public treasury, and whatever money they destroy of someone else, they should pay him. There is no blood money for those they killed if they are able to do so before repentance. If they repent and come repentant, it is: Tenth - The Imam had no way over them, and what was a limit for God was dropped from them and they took the rights of human beings, so he took revenge from them in terms of life and wounds, and what they destroyed of money and blood was due to his guardians in that, and it is permissible for them to pardon and give a gift like all criminals other than combatants. This is the doctrine of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, and the people of opinion. Rather, what was in their hands of money was taken and they were guaranteed the value of what they consumed because that is usurpation, so it is not permissible for them to own it and it is spent on its owners or the Imam keeps it with him until he knows its owner. A group of the Companions and Followers said: The money is not demanded except for what is found with it, and as for what he consumed, it is not demanded for it. Al-Tabari mentioned that from Malik from the narration of Al-Walid bin Muslim from him, and it is apparent from the action of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, with Haritha bin Badr Al-Ghadani, for he was a combatant and then repented before he was able to overpower him, so he wrote to him a published letter dropping the money and blood from him. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: The narration from Malik differed regarding the combatant if the limit was carried out on him and no money was found for him. Does he buy a debt for what he took or is it dropped from him as it is dropped from the thief and the Muslim? The dhimmi and the non-Muslim are the same in this regard. Eleventh - The scholars agreed that the ruler is the guardian of war. If it is said that he is fighting a man’s brother or father in a state of war, then there is nothing in the matter of the one seeking blood money from the matter of the one fighting, and the pardon of the guardian of the blood is not permissible, and the one who is responsible for that is the imam. They made that like a punishment from the punishments of God Almighty: I said: This is a collection of the rulings of the warriors, all of us have discovered its treasures and brought forth its pearls. Among the strangest things said in its interpretation is: Twelfth - Mujahid’s interpretation of it. Mujahid said: What is meant by fighting in this verse is adultery and theft, and this is not correct, for God Almighty has made clear in His Book and on the tongue of His Prophet that the hand of the thief is to be cut off, and the adulterer is to be flogged and exiled if he is a virgin, and stoned if he is a married woman. The rulings of the one fighting in this verse are contrary to that, unless he wants to frighten people on the road by showing off his weapon with the intention of seizing women. This is the most heinous form of fighting and more hideous than taking money. This has been included in the meaning of God Almighty’s statement, And they strive to cause corruption in the land. Thirteenth - Our scholars said, and the thief is called upon by God Almighty, and if he refrains, he is left alone, and if he refuses, he is fought, and if you kill him, then it is the worst killing, and blood is wasted. Al-Nasa’i narrated, “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, that a man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what do you think if Adi attacks me with his money? He said: Then I call upon God. He said: Then Abu Ali said: Then I call upon God. He said: Then the parents of Ali said: Then I call upon God. He said: Then the parents of Ali said: Then fight. If you are killed, then you will be in Paradise, and if you are killed, then you will be in Hell. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, but it does not mention the call upon God. On the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what do you think if a man comes to take my money? He said: Do not give him your money. He said: What if he fights me? He said: Then fight him. He said: What if he kills me? He said: Then you are a martyr. He said: If you kill him? He is in the Fire. Ibn al-Mundhir said: We have narrated from a group of the people of knowledge that they saw fighting thieves and defending themselves and their money. This is the doctrine of Ibn Umar, al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Qatadah, Malik, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and al-Nu’man. This is what the common people of knowledge say: A man can fight for himself, his family, and his money if he is wanted unjustly, according to the reports that came from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he did not specify a time over a time or a situation over a situation except the ruler, because a group of the people of hadith are like those who agree that whoever is unable to defend himself and his money except by rebelling against the ruler and fighting him, then he should not fight him or rebel against him, according to the reports that indicate from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which include the command to be patient with what comes from them, of injustice and oppression, and to refrain from fighting them and rebelling against them as long as they establish prayer. I said: Our school of thought differs over whether they should give him something light, such as clothing or food, or fight him. This difference is based on the original principle, which is: Is the command to fight them because it is a reprehensible change or is it a means of warding off harm? And on this also is based the difference in calling them before fighting, and God knows best. Fourteenth - The Almighty’s saying: “That is a disgrace for them in this world” is due to the hideousness of the fighting and the great harm it causes. The reason for the great harm of the fighting is because it blocks the path of earning for people, because the most and greatest of the earnings is trade, and its pillar and foundation are traveling throughout the land, as the Almighty said: And others travel throughout the land, seeking from the bounty of God (al-Muzzammil 73:20). So when the road is frightened, people are cut off from traveling and need to stay in their homes, so the door of trade is closed to them and their earnings are cut off, so God has prescribed severe punishments for highwaymen, and that disgrace in this world is to deter them from their evil actions and to open the door of trade that He has permitted for His servants to whomever among them wants, and He has promised great punishment in the Hereafter. This sin is outside of sins and is exempted from the hadith of Ubadah in “The saying of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: And whoever commits any of that and is punished for it in this world, it is an expiation for him. And God knows best. It is possible that the disgrace is for the one who is punished and the torment of the Hereafter is for the one who is safe in this world. This sin is like any other, and no believer will remain in Hell forever, as mentioned above, but his punishment is magnified due to the enormity of the sin. Then he is released either by intercession or by being seized. Then this threat is conditional on rescue by the will of God, as God Almighty says: “And He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.” (An-Nisa’: 48) But fear overcomes them according to the threat and the enormity of the sin. Fifteenth - The Almighty’s saying: Except those who repent before you have power over them. The Almighty and Majestic made an exception for those who repent before they are overpowered and informed of the fall of His right from them by saying: So know that God is Forgiving and Merciful. As for retaliation and the rights of people, they are not dropped. And whoever repents after being overpowered, the apparent meaning of the verse is that repentance is of no benefit and the prescribed punishments are carried out on him as mentioned above. Al-Shafi’i said that every prescribed punishment is dropped by repentance. The correct view of his school of thought is that whatever the right of a person is related to, whether retaliation or otherwise, is dropped by repentance before being overpowered. It was said: He meant by the exception the polytheist if he repents and believes before being overpowered, then the prescribed punishments are dropped from him. This is weak because if he believes after being overpowered, he is not killed either by consensus. It was said: The prescribed punishment is not dropped from the combatants after being overpowered - and God knows best - because they are accused of lying in their repentance and pretending to do so if the hand of the Imam reaches them, or because when they are overpowered, they are exposed to being abused, so their repentance is not accepted, like the one who was afflicted with punishment from the nations before us, or the one who reached the state of gurgling and repented. But if their repentance precedes the power over them, then there is no accusation. It is beneficial, as will be explained in Surat Yunus. As for drinkers, fornicators, and thieves, if they repent and reform and this is known about them, then they are brought before the imam, he should not punish them. But if they are brought before him and say, We have repented, they should not be left alone, and in this case they are like combatants who are defeated. And God knows best.
5:34: "Except for those who repent before you have them in your power. So know that God is Forgiving and Merciful."
5:35: The Almighty said: O you who have believed, fear God and seek the means of approach to Him. The means is the closeness according to Abu Wa’il, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ata’, Al-Suddi, Ibn Zayd, and Abdullah Ibn Kathir. It is a verbal noun from the verb tawassulta ilayhi, meaning to draw near. Antaza said: Men have a way to get you to wear kohl and dye your hair. The plural is means. He said: If the informers are absent-minded, we will return to our connection and the reconciliation between us and the means will return It is said: I asked means I asked, and they were asking each other, meaning each one asks the other. So the origin is the request, and the means is the closeness that should be sought, and the means is the degree of Paradise, and it is what the authentic hadith mentioned in “his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: Whoever asks me for intercession, I will grant him intercession.
5:36: "Indeed, those who disbelieve, if they had all that is in the earth and as much more with it to ransom themselves thereby from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them, and they will have a painful punishment."
5:37: Yazid al-Faqir said: It was said to Jabir ibn Abdullah, O companions of Muhammad, you say that a people will come out of the Fire, and God Almighty says: And they will not come out of it. Jabir said: You make the general specific and the specific general. This is only for the disbelievers in particular. So I read the entire verse from beginning to end, and it was for the disbelievers in particular. And remaining means permanent and fixed, it does not disappear or change. The poet said: For on the Day of the People, you will have from me a permanent torment that will last for you.
5:38: It contains twenty-seven questions: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And the male thief, male thief, cut off their hands The verse When the Almighty mentioned taking money by way of seeking and spreading corruption in the land, He mentioned the ruling on the male thief without a spear, as will be explained during the chapter, and the Almighty began with the male thief before the female thief, unlike adultery, according to His Prophet at the end of the chapter. The male thief was cut off in the pre-Islamic era, and the first one to rule that his hand should be cut off in the pre-Islamic era was Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, so God ordered his hand to be cut off in Islam, so the first thief that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off in Islam from among the men was Al-Khayyar bin Adi bin Nawfal bin Manaf, and from among the women was Murrah bint Sufyan bin Abd Al-Asad bin Bani Makhzum, and Abu Bakr cut off the hand of the Yemeni man who stole the necklace, and Umar cut off the hand of Ibn Samra, the brother of Abd Al-Rahman bin Samra, and there is no disagreement about that, and the apparent meaning of the verse is general for every thief, but that is not the case, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The hand of a thief shall not be cut off except for a quarter of a dinar or more.” So he explained that what he meant by his saying and the male and female thief was some thieves and not others, so the hand of a thief shall not be cut off except for a quarter of a dinar or for something worth a quarter of a dinar. This is the opinion of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Uthman ibn Affan, and Ali, may God be pleased with them. Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, al-Layth, al-Shafi’i, and Abu Thawr said the same. Malik said: The hand shall be cut off for a quarter of a dinar or for three dirhams.
