If he steals two dirhams, which is a quarter of a dinar, because of the low exchange rate, his hand shall not be cut off for them. Merchandise shall not be cut off for them unless it reaches three dirhams, whether the exchange rate is low or high. So Malik made gold and silver each one of them a basis in itself, and he made the valuation of merchandise in dirhams according to the well-known view. Ahmad and Ishaq said: If he steals gold, then a quarter of a dinar, and if he steals something other than gold and silver, then its value is a quarter of a dinar or three dirhams of silver. This is similar to what Malik concluded in the other opinion, and the proof for the first opinion is the hadith of Ibn Umar: A man stole a shield and brought it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who ordered it to be valued at three dirhams. Al-Shafi’i made the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with them both, about a quarter of a dinar a basis to which he referred the valuation of goods, not three dirhams, due to the high cost of gold and its permissibility. He left the hadith of Ibn Umar because he saw - and God knows best - the difference of opinion among the Companions regarding the shield for which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was cut off. Ibn Umar says: Three dirhams, Ibn Abbas says: Ten dirhams, and Anas says: Five dirhams. The hadith of Aisha about a quarter of a dinar is a sound and established hadith in which there is no disagreement about it from Aisha, except that some of them stopped it and raised it from the one whose opinion must be acted upon due to its preservation and justice. This was said by Abu Omar and others. Based on this, if the stolen goods amount to a quarter of a dinar by valuation, its thief is cut off, and this is the opinion of Ishaq. So stop at these two principles, for they are the mainstay of the chapter and they are the most correct of what has been said about it. Abu Hanifa and his two companions and al-Thawri said: The hand of the thief is not cut off except for ten dirhams by measure or a dinar of gold in kind or weight, and it is not cut off until it leaves the man’s possession with the goods. Their proof is the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The people of the shield for which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut off the hand for ten dirhams.” It was narrated by Amr ibn Shu`ayb on the authority of his father, his grandfather, who said: The price of a shield at that time was ten dirhams. Al-Daraqutni and others reported them. There is a fourth opinion on the issue, which is what al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Umar, who said: The fifth is not cut off except for five. Sulayman ibn Yasar, Ibn Abi Layla, and Ibn Shabramah said the same. Anas ibn Malik said: Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, cut off the hand for a shield worth five dirhams. A fifth opinion: That the hand is cut off for four dirhams or more. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa`id al-Khudri. A sixth opinion: That the hand is cut off for a dirham or more. This was said by Uthman al-Batti. Al-Tabari mentioned that Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr cut off the hand for a dirham. A seventh opinion: That the hand is cut off for anything that has a value. This is apparently the opinion of the Khawarij. It was narrated on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri, and it is one of the three narrations on his authority. The second is as narrated on the authority of Umar, and the third was narrated by Qatadah on his authority that he said: We discussed how much the cutting off would be during the time of Ziyadah? So our opinion agreed on two dirhams, and these are equivalent statements, and the correct one is what we have presented to you. If it is said: Al-Bukhari and Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God curses the one who steals an egg, so his hand is cut off, and the one who steals a rope, so his hand is cut off. This is in agreement with the apparent meaning of the verse regarding cutting off the hand for a small or a large amount. The answer is that this was issued as a warning against a small amount of a large amount, as it came in the context of encouraging a small amount of a large amount of a large amount of a large amount of a small... small amount of a large amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of a small amount of a large amount of Whoever builds a mosque for God, even if it is the size of a sparrow’s nest, God will build for him a house in Paradise.” It was said: This is a metaphor from another aspect, and that is that if he was harmed by stealing a little, he would steal a lot, so his hand would be cut off. Better than this is what Al-A’mash said, and Al-Bukhari mentioned it at the end of the hadith as an interpretation. He said: They used to think that it was iron, and the rope, they used to think that it was worth dirhams. I said: Like the ropes of a ship and the like, and God knows best. Second: The majority of people agreed that the cutting off is only for the one who took out from his estimate what he wanted to cut off. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan said: If he gathered the clothes in the house, he should be cut off. Al-Sahn bin Abi Al-Sahn also said in another statement like the statement of the rest of the scholars, so it became a correct agreement, praise be to God. Third: The amulet is what is usually set up to protect people’s money, and it differs in everything according to the situation, as will be explained. Ibn al-Mundhir said: There is no established good in this matter, nor is there any discussion about it from the people of knowledge, but rather it is like the consensus of the people of knowledge, and it was narrated from al-Hasan and the people of the apparent meaning that they do not stipulate the amulet. In al-Muwatta’, “On the authority of Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Husayn al-Makki, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no cutting off for hanging fruit, nor for a mountain guard. So if a stable or a threshing floor shelters it, then cut off for what amounts to the price of a shield.” Abu Omar said: This is a hadith whose meaning is connected to the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr bin al-Aas and others, and this Abdullah is trustworthy according to everyone, and Ahmad praised him. And “On the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was asked about hanging fruit, so he said: Whoever takes from it someone in need, not having taken it as a stash, then nothing is upon him. Whoever takes out with something from it, then his hand is to be cut off. Whoever steals without it, then he is to be fined like the same and the punishment.” In another narration, and lashes of punishment instead of and the punishment. The scholars said: Then the lashing was abrogated and in its place was cut off. Abu Omar said: His saying a fine like the same was abrogated. I do not know of any of the jurists who said it except what came from Omar regarding the flour of Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah, which was reported by Malik and a narration from Ahmad bin Hanbal. And what the people are upon is a fine like the same, based on the saying of God Almighty: But whoever transgresses against you, then transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you (al-Baqarah 2:194). Abu Dawud narrated “On the authority of Safwan bin Umayya, who said: I was sleeping in the mosque on a cloak of mine worth thirty dirhams, and a man came and stole it from me. So the man was seized and brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who ordered him to be cut off. He said: So I came to him and said: Will you cut it off for thirty dirhams? I will sell it and give him its price. He said: Why didn’t you do this before you brought it to me? From the point of view, money was created ready for all of creation to benefit from it, then the original wisdom ruled in it the exclusivity which is ownership according to the law, and desires remained attached to it, and hopes hovered over it, so chivalry and religion prevent it in the least of creation, and protection and safekeeping prevent it from most of them. So if its owner protects it, then the protection and safekeeping which is the ultimate possibility for man have come together in it. So if they are violated, the crime becomes heinous and the punishment is great. And if one of the two protections, which is ownership, is violated, then a guarantee and discipline are required. Fourth: If a group of people gather and participate in extracting a minimum amount from its safekeeping, then either some of them are able to extract it, or they cannot do so except through their cooperation. If it is the first, then our scholars differed on it: There are two opinions: One of them is that the hand is cut off, and the second is that the hand is not cut off. This is what Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i said. They said: The hand is not cut off for theft by those who participate except on the condition that each one must have a minimum amount from his share, based on the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The hand of a thief shall not be cut off except for a quarter of a dinar or more.” And each of these did not steal a minimum amount, so they shall not be cut off. The reason for cutting off in one of the two narrations is that participation in the crime does not cancel its punishment, like participation in murder. Ibn al-Arabi said: “How close is the difference between them, for we only killed a group for one person to protect blood, so that the enemies would not cooperate in shedding it. It is the same with money, especially since al-Shafi’i helped us that if a group participated in cutting off a man’s hand, they shall be cut off and there is no difference between them. If it is the second, which is something that cannot be removed except through cooperation, then all of them shall be cut off by agreement of the scholars, as Ibn al-Arabi mentioned. Fifth: If they participated in the theft, such that one of them broke into the safe and another took out, if they were cooperating, then the hand is to be cut off. If each of them did it alone without agreement between them, such that another came and took it out, then there is no cutting off for either of them. If they cooperated in breaking into the safe and one of them took it out alone, then the hand is to be cut off for him alone. Al-Shafi’i said: There is no cutting off because this one broke into the safe and did not steal, and the other stole from a safe place whose sanctity was violated. Abu Hanifa said: If he participated in breaking into the safe and entered and took, then the hand is to be cut off. It is not a condition of participation in breaking into the safe that one should use a single tool, but rather the alternation of striking results in the partnership. Sixth - If one of them entered and took the goods to the door of the safe, then put his hand in and took it, then he must cut off his hand and the first one must be punished. Ashab said: They must both be cut off, and if he puts it outside the safe, then he must cut off his hand, but not the one who took it. If he puts it in the middle of the hole and the other takes it and their hands meet in the hole, then they must both be cut off. Seventh - The grave and the mosque are a place of protection, so the grave robber is to be cut off according to the majority. Abu Hanifa said: There is no cutting off for him because he stole from an unprotected place money that is exposed to loss and has no owner: because the dead person does not own it. Some of them deny the theft because there is no one living in it. The theft only occurs when eyes are avoided and people are guarded against it. The people of Transoxiana relied on denying the theft. The majority said: He is a thief because he put on a night garment and avoided eyes, and he intended a time when no one would look or pass by him, so it was like if he stole at a time when people were going out for the Eid and the city was empty of all of them. As for their saying: The grave is not a place of protection, it is invalid because the protection of everything is according to the possible state in it. As for their saying: The dead person does not own it, it is also invalid because it is not permissible to leave the dead person naked. So this necessity became decisive that the grave is a place of protection, and God Almighty drew attention to it in His saying: “Have We not made the earth a receptacle * For the living and the dead?” (Al-Murasilaat: 25) so that a living person may live in it and a dead person may be buried in it. As for their saying: It is exposed to loss Everything that a living person wears is also subject to damage and decay due to his wearing it, except that one of the two matters is more urgent than the other. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me and said: How would you be if people were afflicted with death and the house was in the care of the guardian, meaning the grave? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: You should be patient. Hammad said: This is what was said by those who said that the hand of the thief should be cut off because he entered the house of the deceased. As for the mosque, whoever steals its mats should be cut off. This was narrated by Isa from Ibn al-Qasim. Even if the mosque does not have a door and he sees them secured, and if he steals the doors, he should also be cut off. It was also narrated from Ibn al-Qasim that if he stole the mats during the day, he should not be cut off, and if he climbed over them at night, he should be cut off. It was mentioned from Sahnun that if his mats were sewn together, he should be cut off, otherwise he should not be cut off. Asbagh said: The thief of the mosque’s mats, its lamps, and its tiles should be cut off, just as if he had stolen its door secretly, or a piece of wood from its ceiling, or its pillars. Ashhab said in the book of Muhammad: There is no cutting off for anything from the mosque’s mats, its lamps, and its tiles. Eighth - The scholars differed as to whether a fine should be paid with amputation or not. Abu Hanifa said: A fine should not be paid with amputation in any case, because God the Almighty said: And as for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands as a punishment for what they have earned, an exemplary punishment from God and He did not mention a fine. Al-Shafi’i said: He should pay the value of the theft, whether he is wealthy or poor, and it should be a debt on him if he becomes wealthy he should pay it. This is the opinion of Ahmad and Ishaq. As for our scholars, Malik and his companions, they said: If the object is still there, he should return it, and if it is lost, if he is wealthy he should pay it, and if he is poor he should not follow it with a debt and nothing is due on him. Malik narrated something similar from Al-Zuhri. Sheikh Abu Ishaq said: It has been said that it should be followed with a debt with amputation, whether he is wealthy or poor. He said: This is the opinion of more than one of our scholars from the people of Medina, and evidence for its validity was provided by the fact that they are two rights for those entitled to it, so one does not cancel out the other, like blood money and expiation. Then he said: This is what I say, and Judge Abu Al-Hasan provided evidence for the famous opinion by the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): If the punishment is carried out on the thief, he is not liable for compensation. And he supported it in his book. Some of them said: The penalty of following up with a fine is a punishment, and cutting off the hand is a punishment, and the two punishments cannot come together. Judge Abdul Wahhab relied on this, and the correct statement is that of Al-Shafi’i and those who agreed with him. Al-Shafi’i said: The thief is liable for what he stole, whether he was wealthy or poor, whether he cut off his hand or not. Likewise, if he robs the road, he said: The punishment is not dropped for God, what he destroys for the servants. As for what our scholars have used as evidence from the hadith, if he is poor, the Kufians used it as evidence, and it is the statement of Al-Tabari, and there is no evidence in it. It was narrated by Al-Nasa’i and Al-Daraqutni on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Awf. Abu Omar said: This hadith is not a statement and no evidence can be established from it. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This hadith is invalid. Al-Tabari said: The analogy is that he must resolve what he has consumed, but we left that out in accordance with the tradition in that. Abu Omar said: Leaving analogy due to a weak tradition is not permissible, because a weak tradition does not require a ruling. Ninth - There is a difference of opinion regarding cutting off the hand of someone who steals money from the one who stole it. Our scholars said: His hand should be cut off. Al-Shafi’i said: His hand should not be cut off because he stole from someone who did not have an owner and no place of safekeeping. Our scholars said: The sanctity of the owner over him remains and has not been severed from him, and the hand of the thief is cut off, like the usurper who steals usurped money from him. If it is said: Make his safekeeping a whole place of safekeeping, we say: The safekeeping is still in place and the ownership is still in place and the ownership in it has not been nullified, so they say to us: Nullify the safekeeping. Tenth - They differed if the theft is repeated after the amputation of the stolen item. The majority said that the amputation is due. Abu Hanifa said: There is no amputation for him, and the generality of the Qur’an requires amputation for him, and this is what he said. Abu Hanifa also said regarding the thief who owns the stolen item by purchase or gift before amputation: He is not to be amputated, and God Almighty says: And as for the male thief, male thief, cut off their hands. So if amputation is due as a right to God Almighty, nothing cancels it. Eleventh - The majority read al-Sariq in the nominative case. Sibawayh said: The meaning is in what was imposed upon you, the male and female thief. It was said: The nominative case in both of them is on the subject and predicate, cut off their hands. The intention is not to a specific person, because if a specific person was intended, the accusative case would be required. You say: Strike Zaid, rather, terrorize him, like you say: Whoever steals, cut off his hand. Al-Zajjaj said: This is the preferred opinion. The thief was read in the accusative case, so they are both on the assumption of cut off the thief, male and female, and this is the choice of Sibawayh because the verb in the imperative case is more appropriate. Sibawayh, may God have mercy on him, said: The correct way in the speech of the Arabs is the accusative case, as you say: Strike Zaid, but the majority refused except in the nominative case, meaning the majority of Al-Farra’ and most of them, so Sibawayh placed the type of thief in the position of a specific person. Ibn Masoud read al-Sariqun wa al-Sariqun wa al-Sariqun wa al-Sariqunu aymanuhum, and this strengthens the readings of the group. Al-Sarq and al-Sarqah with a kasra on the ra’ in both of them is the name of the stolen thing, and the source of sarq is yasraq with a fatha on the ra’. Al-Jawhari said that the origin of this word is to take something hidden from the eyes, and from it is istaraqahu al-sama’u and staqahu al-nazra. Ibn Arafa said: A thief among the Arabs is someone who comes to a safe place in secret and takes from it what does not belong to him. If he takes from someone who is visible, then he is a thief, a robber, a plunderer, and a thief. If he refuses with what is in his hand, then he is angry. I said: In the hadith, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: The worst theft is the one who steals someone’s prayer. They said: How can he steal someone’s prayer? He said: He does not complete his bowing or prostration. Al-Muwatta’ and others narrated it, and he called him a thief, even though he is not a thief in terms of the derivation, because stealing eyes is not usually involved in it. The twelfth - The Almighty’s saying: “Then cut off.” Cutting off means separation and removal, and it is not obligatory except by combining the characteristics that are considered in the thief and in the stolen thing, and in the place from which it was stolen and in its description. As for what is considered in the thief, there are five characteristics, which are: maturity, reason, that he does not own what was stolen from, and that he does not have authority over it. So the slave is not cut off if he steals from the money of his master, and likewise the master if he takes the money of his slave, there is no cutting off under any circumstances, because the slave and his money belong to his master, and no one has cut off for taking the money of his slave because he is taking his money, and cutting off the hand of the slave was dropped by the consensus of the Companions and by the saying of the Caliph, Your servant stole your goods. Al-Darqutni mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘There is no cutting off for the runaway slave if he steals, nor for the dhimmi.’” He said: No, it was not transmitted by anyone except Fahd bin Sulayman, and the correct view is that it is suspended. Ibn Majah mentioned on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘There is no cutting off for the runaway slave if he steals, nor for the dhimmi.’” If a slave steals, sell him even if it is for a penny. Narrated by Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah. Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Awanah, on the authority of Umar bin Abi Salamah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. Ibn Majah said: Jabara bin Al-Maghlis told us, Hajjaj bin Tamim told us, on the authority of Maymun bin Ma’ran, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. A slave from the slaves of the fifth stole from the fifth, so it was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he did not cut off his hand and said: God’s wealth is stolen from some of it. Jabara bin Al-Maghlis is abandoned and Abu Zur’ah Al-Razi said that there is no cutting off for a child or an insane person, and it is obligatory for a dhimmi, a protected person, or a non-Muslim if he enters with security. As for what is considered in the stolen thing, there are four descriptions, which are: the minimum amount, and the discussion of it has already been mentioned, and that it is something that can be owned and possessed and its sale is permissible, and if it is something that cannot be owned and its sale is not permissible, such as wine and pork, then there is no cutting off for it by consensus, except for a free young man according to Malik and Ibn Al-Qasim. It was said: There is no cutting off for him, and this is what Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa said, because it is not wealth, and our scholars said, and it is one of the greatest wealth, and the thief does not fall into the wealth itself, but rather the cutting off is due to the attachment of souls to it and their attachment to the free man is greater than their attachment to the slave, even if it is something that is permissible to own but not permissible to sell, such as a dog that is permitted to be kept and the meat of sacrificial animals. In that, there is a difference of opinion between Ibn Al-Qasim and Ashab. Ibn Al-Qasim said: The thief of a dog is not cut off, and Ashab said: That is in the forbidden thing to keep. As for what is permitted to be taken, its thief is to be cut off. He said: Whoever steals the meat or skin of a sacrificial animal is to be cut off if its value is three dirhams. Ibn Habib said: Asbagh said: If he steals the sacrificial animal before slaughter, his hand is to be cut off. However, if he steals it after slaughter, his hand is not to be cut off. If it is something whose origin is permissible to take and sell, and something is made from it that is not permissible to use, such as a tambourine, musical instruments such as flutes, ouds, and similar musical instruments, then it is to be looked at. If what remains of it after its form has been corrupted and its intended benefit has been lost, a quarter of a dinar or more is to be cut off. The same applies to gold and silver vessels that are not permissible to use and it is ordered to be broken, as what is in them of gold or silver is to be valued, not its manufacture. Likewise, a cross made of gold or silver. If the value of impure oil, despite its impurity, is a nisab, his hand is to be cut off. The third description: The thief does not own it, like someone who steals what he has mortgaged or rented, nor is there any semblance of ownership. There is a difference of opinion among our scholars and others regarding taking into account any semblance of ownership, like someone who steals from the spoils or from the public treasury, because he has a share in it. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him. On his authority, that a man was brought who had stolen a helmet from the fifth, and he did not see any amputation on it, and he said to him, There is a share in it. And this is the doctrine of the group regarding the public treasury. It was said: He must be amputated, based on the generality of the wording of the verse on theft, and that it should be something whose theft is permissible, such as a young slave or an adult non-Arab, because something whose theft is not permissible, such as an eloquent slave, is not amputated for. As for what is considered in the place from which it was stolen, it is one description, which is the safekeeping of such a stolen thing. The summary of what is said about it is that everything that has a known place, its place is its safekeeping, and everything that has a guardian with it, its guardian is its safekeeping. So houses, homes, and shops are safekeeping, and their people are not absent from them or present. Likewise, the public treasury is a safekeeping for the group of Muslims, and the thief does not deserve anything in it, even if before the theft he was among those whom the Imam may give. Rather, the right of every Muslim is determined by the gift. Do you not see that the Imam may be permitted to spend all the money on a beneficial purpose and not distribute it among the people or distribute it in one country rather than another and prevent some people from it rather than others? So, in the estimation, this thief is among those who have no right to it. Likewise, the spoils of war are not… It is void: that it is designated by division, which is what we mentioned in the treasury, or it is designated by the taking itself of the one who witnessed the incident, so the amount of what was stolen must be taken into consideration. If it is more than his right, then it is cut off, otherwise it is not cut off. Fourteenth - The backs of the beasts are a safeguard for what they carry, and the courtyards of the shops are a safeguard for what is placed in them in the place of sale, even if there is no shop, whether its people are with it or not, it is stolen at night or during the day. Likewise, a sheep is in the market, tied up or not, and the beasts are on their tethers, whether their people are with them or not. If the beast is at the door of the mosque or in the market, it is not a safeguard unless there is a guard with it, and whoever ties it in his courtyard or makes a place to tie up his beasts, then it is a safeguard for it, and the ship is a safeguard for what is in it, whether it is loose or tied. If the beast itself is stolen, then it is like the beast if it is loose, then it is not a safeguard, and if its owner ties it up in a place and moors it there, then tying it up is a safeguard. And so on, if there is someone with it wherever it is, then it is a safeguard like the beast at the door of the mosque with a guard with it, unless they disembark the ship at a place and tie it up, then it is a safeguard for it, whether its owner is with it or not. Fifteenth - There is no disagreement that those who live in one house, such as hotels, where each man lives in his own house, should have his hand cut off if he steals from his neighbor’s house if he takes it and takes it out with his theft to the hall of the house, even if he does not enter his house with it or take it out of the house. There is no disagreement that he should not have his hand cut off if he steals anything from the hall of the house, even if he takes it into his house or takes it out of the house, because its hall is permissible for everyone to buy and sell, unless it is an animal in its tether or something similar to it from the goods. Sixteenth - The parents do not cut off the money of their son because of his saying, peace be upon him: You and your wealth belong to your father” and he was cut off for stealing their wealth because there is no doubt about it. It was said: He is not to be cut off, and this is the opinion of Ibn Wahb and Ashab because the son usually has access to his father’s wealth. Don’t you see that the slave is not to be cut off for his master’s wealth? So it is more appropriate for his son not to be cut off for his wealth? They differed about the grandfather, so Malik and Ibn Al-Qasim said: He is not to be cut off. Ashab said: He is to be cut off, and Malik’s opinion is more correct because he is a father. Malik said: I like that the grandfathers on the father’s and mother’s sides are not to be cut off, even if they are not entitled to maintenance. Ibn Al-Qasim and Ashab said: And the hand of those other than them from the relatives is to be cut off. Ibn Al-Qasim said: And the hand of the one who steals from hunger is not to be cut off. Abu Hanifa said: There is no cutting off for any of the forbidden ones, such as the paternal aunt, maternal aunt, sister, and others, and this is the opinion of Al-Thawri. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq said: The hand of the one who steals from these people is to be cut off. Abu Thawr said: Every thief is to be cut off for what the hand is to be cut off for unless they agree on something, then it is safe, according to the consensus, and God knows best. Seventeenth - They differed about the thief of the Qur’an. Al-Shafi’i, Abu Yusuf, and Abu Thawr said: His hand is cut off, whether its value is such that the hand would be cut off, and Ibn al-Qasim said the same. Al-Nu’man said: He is not to be cut off for stealing a Qur’an. Ibn al-Mundhir said: He is to be cut off for stealing a Qur’an. They differed about the thief who steals the money from the sleeve. A group said: He is to be cut off from the inside or outside of the sleeve. This is the opinion of Malik, al-Awza’i, Abu Thawr, and Ya’qub. Abu Hanifa, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ishaq said: If the dirhams were wrapped in the outside of his sleeve and he broke them and stole them, his hand is not to be cut off. Ibn al-Mundhir said: He is to be cut off from whichever direction he stole. Eighteenth - They differed regarding cutting off the hand during travel and implementing the prescribed punishments in the land of war. Malik and Al-Layth bin Saad said: The prescribed punishments are implemented in the land of war and there is no difference between the land of war and Islam. Al-Awza’i said: Whoever raids with an army, even if he is not the emir of one of the cities, implements the prescribed punishments in his army other than cutting off. Abu Hanifa said: If the army raids a land of war and they have an emir, then he does not implement the prescribed punishments in his army unless he is the imam of Egypt, Syria, Iraq or the like, in which case he implements the prescribed punishments in his army. Al-Awza’i and those who said what he said provided evidence with the hadith of Junada bin Abi Umayya, who said: We were with Busr ibn Artah at sea, and a thief called Masdar was brought to us who had stolen from Bakhita. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Hands are not cut off in battle. Had it not been for that, I would have cut him off. This Busr is said to have been born during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had bad reputations with Ali and his companions. He is the one who slaughtered two children belonging to Ubayd God ibn Abbas, and their mother lost her mind and wandered aimlessly. So Ali, may God be pleased with him, prayed against him that God would prolong his life and cause him to lose his mind, and so it was. Yahya ibn Ma’in said: Busr ibn Artah was a bad man. Those who said that cutting off a hand should be based on the generality of the Qur’an, and this is correct, God willing. The most appropriate argument for those who forbade cutting off a hand on land is war and the prescribed punishments, for fear that this would be considered shirk. And God knows best. Nineteenth - If the hand or foot is cut off, where is it cut off? All of them said: It is cut off from the wrist, and the foot from the joint, and the thief is mutilated if he is cut off. Some of them said: It is cut off to the elbow. It was said: To the shoulder because the name hand includes that. And he, may God be pleased with him, said: The foot is cut off from half the foot and the heel is left for him. Ahmad and Abu Thawr said the same. Ibn al-Mundhir said: We have narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he ordered the cutting off of a man’s hand, and he said: Cut it out. There is an argument about its chain of transmission, and a group of people, including Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, and others, recommended this. This is better, and it is closer to recovery and further from destruction. Al-Muwaffah twentieth - There is no disagreement that the right hand is the one that is cut off first, then they differed if he steals a second time. Malik, the people of Medina, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, and others said: His left foot is cut off, then in the third time his left hand, then in the fourth time his right foot, then if he steals a fifth time he is punished and imprisoned. Abu Mus’ab, one of our scholars, said: He is killed after the fourth time, and he provided evidence with a hadith narrated by Al-Nasa’i, “On the authority of Al-Harith bin Hatib that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought a thief and said: Kill him. They said: O Messenger of God, he is only a market. He said: Kill him. They said: O Messenger of God, he only stole. He said: Cut off his hand. He said: Then he stole and his leg was cut off. Then he stole during the time of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, until all his limbs were cut off. Then he also stole a fifth time. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew this better when he said: Kill him. Then he handed him over to the young men of Quraysh to kill him, among them Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who loved the imamate. He said: Command me over them. So they commanded him over them. So whenever he struck him, they struck him until they killed him. And in the hadith of Jabbar, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded a thief in his fifth year and said: “Kill him.” Jabir said: So we set out with him and killed him, then we dragged him and threw him into a well and threw stones at him. Narrated by Abu Dawud and included by al-Nasa’i, who said: This is a strange hadith, and one of its narrators is not strong, and I do not know of any authentic hadith on this subject. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It is proven from Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, that they cut off the hand after the hand and the foot after the foot. It was said: In the second case, his left foot is cut off, then there is no cutting off in anything else. Then if he repeats, he is punished and imprisoned. It was narrated from Ali ibn Talib, and this is what al-Zuhri, Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said. Al-Zuhri said: Nothing has reached us in the Sunnah except cutting off the hand and foot. Ata’ said: His right hand is cut off in particular, and the cutting does not return to him. Ibn al-Arabi mentioned this and said: As for the statement of Ata’, the Companions said that before him there was a caliphate. Twenty-one - They differed about the ruler who orders the cutting off of the thief’s right hand, then his left hand is cut off. Qatada said: The punishment has been carried out on him and nothing more should be done to it. Malik said the same: If the cutter misses the cut, he has lost his left hand. The people of opinion said the same as they approved. Abu Thawr said: The blood money is due from the one who cut off the left leg because he made a mistake and cut off his right hand unless it is forbidden by consensus. Ibn al-Mundhir said: Cutting off the left leg is not without one of two meanings: either the cutting was intentional, in which case he must pay retaliation, or he made a mistake, in which case his blood money is due from the cutter’s family. Cutting off the right hand of the thief is obligatory, and it is not permissible to remove what God Almighty has made obligatory due to the aggression of an aggressor or the mistake of a mistaken person. Al-Thawri said about the one who is to be retaliated against for his right hand, and he puts his left hand forward and cuts it, his right hand is also cut off. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This is correct. A group said: His right hand is cut off if he recovers, because he is the one who destroyed his left hand, and nothing is due from the cutter according to the opinion of the people of opinion and analogy of the opinion of al-Shafi’i. His right hand is cut off if it recovers. Qatada and al-Sha’bi said: Nothing is due from the cutting off, and what was cut off from him is sufficient. Twenty-two - The thief’s hand being hung around his neck. Abdullah bin Muhairiz said: I asked Fadala about the Sunnah of hanging the thief’s hand around his neck. He said: “A thief was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his hand was cut off. Then he ordered it to be done to his neck.” Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said it was a good, rare hadith, and by Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i. Twenty-third - If the punishment for theft is required and the thief kills a man, Malik said: He is to be killed and amputation is included in that. Al-Shafi’i said: He is to be amputated and killed because they are two rights for two people who deserve them, so it is necessary that each one of them be given his right. This is the correct view, God Almighty willing, and it is the choice of Ibn al-Arabi. Twenty-fourth - The Almighty’s saying: Their hands. Since He said their hands and did not say their two hands, the linguists spoke about that. Ibn al-Arabi said: The jurists followed them in what they mentioned, out of good opinion of them. Al-Khalil bin Ahmad and al-Farra’ said: Everything that exists from the creation of man, when it is attributed to two, is pluralized. You say: I crushed their heads and I filled their bellies. And If you both repent to God, your hearts have indeed become inclined. (al-Tahrim 66:4) For this reason He said, Cut off their hands, and did not say, their hands. What is meant is, Cut off the right of this one and the right of that one. It is permissible in the language to say, Cut off their hands, which is the original. The poet said, combining the two languages: And they are two important ones who throw themselves twice, their backs like the backs of two gears. It was said: He did this because it does not constitute a problem. Sibawayh said: If it is singular, it may be prevented if it is intended to be dual. He narrated from the Arabs: They put down their saddles, meaning the saddles of their two camels. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is based on the fact that the right hand alone is what is cut off, and this is not the case. Rather, the hands and feet are cut off, so his saying their hands refers back to four, and it is a plural for two, and they are dual. So the discussion will come on its eloquence. If he had said: So cut off their hands, it would have been correct, because the male and female thief did not mean two people in particular, but rather they are generic names that encompass an innumerable amount. Twenty-fifth - The Almighty’s saying: A recompense for what they have earned is an object for which it is intended, and if you wish, it can be a source. And so is a punishment from God. It is said: I punished him if you did to him something that would require him to be punished for that action. And God is Exalted in Might and cannot be overcome. Wise in what He does, and this has been mentioned previously.
5:39: Twenty-sixth - The Almighty's saying: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and amends is a condition and its answer is then God will accept his repentance. The meaning of after his wrongdoing is after the theft, then God will forgive him, and cutting off the hand is not dropped by repentance. Ata and a group said: It is dropped by repentance before being able to seize the thief. Some Shafi'is said this and attributed it to Shafi'i as a statement, and they relied on the saying of God the Almighty: Except those who repent before you have power over them. This is an exception from the obligation, so all the punishments must be applied to it. Our scholars said: This is our proof in itself, because when God the Almighty mentioned the punishment for the mujahid, He said: Except those who repent before you have power over them. And He linked to it the punishment for the thief and said about it: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and amends, then God will accept his repentance. If it were similar in ruling, the ruling between them would not have been different. Ibn al-Arabi said: O Shafi'is, glory be to God! Where are the jurisprudential details and legal rulings that you deduce from the obscurities of issues? Haven’t you seen the warrior who is tyrannical, the aggressor with his weapon, with whom the Imam needs to attack horses and riders, how he dropped his punishment in deference to that situation, as he did with the infidel in forgiving all that had happened before in order to unite them on Islam? As for the thief and the adulterer, who are in the hands of the Muslims and under the rule of the Imam, what drops the ruling of what was required of them? Or how can it be said: It is compared to the warrior, when wisdom and situation have distinguished between them? This is not befitting of the likes of you, O group of investigators. And if it is proven that the punishment is not dropped by repentance, then repentance is acceptable and cutting off the hand is an expiation for it. And he improved, that is, just as he repented from stealing, he repented from every sin. And it was said: And he improved, that is, he abandoned the sin completely. As for the one who abandoned theft by fornication or converting to Judaism by becoming a Christian, this is not repentance, and God’s repentance is upon the servant to guide him to repentance. And it was said: To accept his repentance. Twenty-seventh: It is said: God began with the male thief in this verse before the female thief, and with the female thief before the male thief. What is the wisdom behind that? The answer is that since the love of money is more prevalent among men and the desire for pleasure is more prevalent among women, He began with them in both places. This is one of the aspects regarding women, as will be explained in Surat An-Nur, starting with the male thief, God willing. Then God made the punishment for theft the cutting off of the hand for taking money, and He did not make the punishment for adultery the cutting off of the penis along with committing the immoral act with it, for three meanings: First: That the thief has something like his hand that was cut off, so the deterrent with it is compensated for by the second. And the adulterer does not have something like his penis if it is cut off, so it is not compensated for by something else if he is deterred by the second cutting off. The punishment is a deterrent for the one being punished and others, and cutting off the hand in theft is apparent, and cutting off the penis in adultery is implicit. Third: Cutting off the penis nullifies the offspring, but cutting off the hand does not nullify it, and God knows best.
5:40: The Almighty's saying: Do you not know that to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? The verse is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others. That is, there is no kinship between God Almighty and anyone that would necessitate favoritism, so that someone might say: We are the children of God and His beloved. The limits are imposed on everyone who commits a crime that requires a punishment. It was said: That is, he has the right to rule as he wishes, so this is why a distinction is made between the combatant and the non-combatant thief. Similar verses and discussions about them have been presented, so there is no point in repeating them, and God is the Grantor of success. This is what is related to the verse on theft from some of the rulings on theft. And God knows best.
5:41: It contains eight issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: O Messenger, let not the verse grieve you The verse has three sayings about the reason for its revelation: It was said: It was revealed about Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadir. A Qurayzah killed a Nadir. When Banu Nadir killed someone from Banu Qurayzah, they did not handcuff him, but rather paid them blood money, as will be explained. So they brought their case to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ruled that the Qurayzah and the Nadir should be treated equally. This upset them and they did not accept. It was said: It was revealed about Abu Lubabah when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Banu Qurayzah, but he betrayed him when he indicated to them that it was slaughter. It was said: It was revealed about the adultery of the two Jews and the story of stoning, and this is the most correct of the sayings. It was narrated by Imams Malik, Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, and Abu Dawud on the authority of Jabir on the authority of Abdullah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Bring me the two most knowledgeable men among you. So they brought the two sons of Suriya. We asked them by God Almighty, how do you find the matter of these two in the Torah? They said, We find in the Torah that if four testify that they saw his penis in her vagina like the kohl stick in the kohl container, they are to be stoned. He said, What prevents you from stoning them? They said, Our authority has gone and we dislike killing. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called for witnesses and they came and testified that they saw his penis in her vagina like the kohl stick in the kohl container. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they be stoned.” And in a hadith other than the Sahih on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, “on the authority of Jabbar ibn Abdullah, he said: A man from the people of Fadak committed adultery. The people of Fadak wrote to some Jews in Medina to ask Muhammad about it. If he orders you to flog, then take it. If he orders you to stone, then do not take it. So they asked him. He called for Ibn Suriya, who was their scholar and was one-eyed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: I ask you by God, how do you find the punishment for adultery in your book? Ibn Suriya said: As you have asked me by God, we find in the Torah that looking is adultery, embracing is adultery, and kissing is adultery. If four testify that they saw his penis in her vagina like the tip of a kohl container, then stoning is obligatory. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is it. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azim, he said: A Jewish man passed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who had been flogged and blackened, so he called them and said: This is how you find the punishment for adultery in your book. They said: Yes. So he called one of their scholars and said: I ask you by God who sent down the Torah to Moses, is this how you find the punishment for adultery in your book? He said: No, and had you not asked me about this, I would not have told you. We find it stoning, but it has become widespread among our nobles, so if we seized a noble person, we would leave him, and if we seized a weak person, we would carry out the punishment on him. We said: Come, let us agree on something to implement on the noble and the lowly. So we made it flogging and blackening instead of stoning. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, I or whoever revives your command when they kill him, so he ordered him to be stoned. Then God Almighty revealed: “O Messenger, let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you” until His saying: If you are given this, then take it. He said: Go to Muhammad, and if he orders you to flog and blacken, then take it, and if he issues a fatwa for you to stone, then beware. Then God Almighty revealed: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - those are the ones who will be punished. The disbelievers: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wrongdoers, “And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the wicked,” in all of the disbelievers. This is how it was mentioned in this narration by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in the hadith of Ibn Umar: “A Jewish man and a Jewish woman came who had committed adultery. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out until he came to the Jews. He said: What do you find in the Torah about one who commits adultery?” The hadith. In another narration: “The Jews came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a man and a woman who had committed adultery.” In the book of Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Ibn Umar, he said: A group of Jews came and invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the Qaf. He came to them in the school house and they said: O Abu al-Qasim, a man among us has committed adultery with a woman, so judge between us and do not contradict any of this. It is all one story. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah in a good manner, and he said: A Jewish man and a Jewish woman committed adultery. Some of them said to each other: Let us go to this Prophet, for he is a Prophet sent with leniency. If he issues a fatwa less than stoning, we will accept it and argue with it before God and say: The fatwa of one of your prophets. They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the mosque with his companions. They said: O Abu al-Qasim, what do you think of a man and a woman among them who commit adultery? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not speak to them until he came to their schoolhouse. He stood at the door and said: I ask you by God, who sent down the Torah to Moses, what do you find in the Torah for one who commits adultery when he is married? They said: “His face should be washed, his forehead should be covered, and he should be flogged. The flogging is when the adulterers are carried on a donkey, their backs facing each other, and they are paraded around.” A young man among them remained silent. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw him remain silent, he insisted on asking him, and he said: O God, since you have asked us, we find stoning in the Torah. He continued the hadith until he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Then I will rule according to what is in the Torah.’ So he ordered them to be stoned.” The second - and the result of these narrations is that the Jews ruled the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he ruled against them according to what is in the Torah, and he relied on the statement of Ibn Suriya and that he heard the testimony of the Jews and acted upon it, and that Islam is not a condition for chastity. These are four issues. If the People of the Covenant bring a case to the Imam, and if what they brought was unjust, such as murder, aggression, and usurpation, he rules between them and prevents them from it without disagreement. However, if it is not like that, then the Imam has the choice to rule between them and leave it according to Malik and Al-Shafi’i. However, Malik saw that turning away from them is better, because ruling between them is the ruling of Islam. Al-Shafi’i said: He does not rule between them in the limits. Abu Hanifa said: He rules between them in every case, and this is the statement of Al-Zuhri, Umar ibn Abd Al-Aziz, and Al-Hakam. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and it is one of the two statements of Al-Shafi’i, based on the statement of God Almighty: And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5:49), as will be explained later. Malik argued with the statement of God Almighty: But if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them (al-Ma’idah 5:42), which is a text on the choice. Ibn Al-Qasim said: If the bishops come As for the two adulterers, the ruler has a choice because enforcing the ruling is the right of the bishops, and the one who disagrees says: The bishops are not to be considered. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is the most correct, because if a man judged between them, it would be enforced and the ruler’s consent would not be taken into account, so the People of the Book are more deserving of that. Isa said on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim: They were not people of the covenant, rather they were people of war. Ibn al-Arabi said: What Isa said on his authority was only rejected because of what al-Tabari and others narrated: That the adulterers were from the people of Khaybar or Fadak, and they were at war with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the name of the adulterous woman was Busra. They sent to the Jews of Medina saying to them: Ask Muhammad about this, and if he gives you a fatwa other than stoning, then take it from him and accept it, and if he gives you a fatwa about it, then beware of him, the event. Ibn al-Arabi said: If this were true, then their bringing the adulterers and asking them for a covenant and security would have been considered a ruling of restraint and justice towards them. So there is no proof for the narration of Jesus in this, and God Almighty said about them: They are listeners to falsehood, listeners to other people who have not come to you. And when they judged the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the ruling was carried out against them and they had no right to return. So whoever judges a man in religion, which is: Third: Its origin is this verse. Malik said: If a man rules against a man, his ruling is binding, and if it is referred to a judge, he confirms it, unless it is clearly unjust. Sahnun said: He confirms it if he sees it as correct. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is in the case of money and rights that are specific to the plaintiff. As for the limits, no one can rule on them except the sultan and the officer. Every right that is specific to the two parties, arbitration is permissible in it, and the arbitrator’s arbitration is enforceable in it. Its realization is that arbitration between people is only their right, not the right of the ruler. However, continuing with arbitration is a breach of the principle of guardianship and leads to people quarreling like donkeys quarreling. There must be a separator, so the Shari’ah ordered the appointment of a governor to put an end to the principle of quarreling, and permitted arbitration to relieve him and them of the difficulty of litigation, so that both interests are fulfilled and the benefit is obtained. Al-Shafi’i and others said: Arbitration is permissible, but it is only a fatwa. Some scholars said: The Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ruling on the Jews by stoning was to establish the ruling of their Book, since they distorted it, concealed it and abandoned acting upon it. Do you not see that he said: O God, I am the first to revive Your command when they have killed it? And that was when he came to Madinah, and for that reason he sought the two sons of Suriya to verify the ruling of the Torah and made them swear to that. The statements of the infidels regarding the limits and their testimony regarding them are not acceptable by consensus, but he did that in order to oblige them to what they committed themselves to and acted upon. It may be possible that the way of knowledge was obtained through revelation, or what God put in his mind of believing the two sons of Suriya in what they said about that, not their words alone. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) explained to him and informed him of the legitimacy of stoning and its beginning at that time, so what he did was to establish the ruling of the Torah and to clarify that it was the ruling of His Shari’ah and that the Torah is the ruling of God, the Most High, because God, the Most High, said: “Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light. The Prophets who submitted [to God] judged by it.” And he was one of the Prophets, and… Abu Hurairah said about him: I rule according to what is in the Torah. And God knows best. Fourth - The majority of scholars reject the testimony of a dhimmi because he is not one of its people, so it is not accepted against a Muslim or an infidel. A group of the Tabi’in and others accepted their testimony if there was no Muslim, as will be explained at the end of the surah. If it is said: He ruled based on their testimony and stoned the adulterers, then the answer is that he only implemented against them what he knew to be the ruling of the Torah and obligated them to act upon it in the same way that the Children of Israel acted upon it, obligating them to prove it against them and demonstrating their distortion and change. So he was an implementer, not a judge. This is according to the first interpretation and according to what was mentioned of the possibility, so that is specific to that incident, since their testimony in such a matter was not heard before in the early generations, and God knows best. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: Do not let it grieve you. Nafi’ read it with the dammah on the ya’ and the kasrah on the zay, and the rest read it with the fathah on the ya’ and the damma on the zay. Grief and sadness are the opposite of joy, and a man grieved with the kasrah, so he is khazin and hazin, and another grieved him, and his sadness is also like aslaka and salka, and mahzun is built upon it. Al-Yazidi said: Hazin is the language of Quraysh, and ahzan is the language of Tamim, and it has been read with it, and ahzazan and tahzan have the same meaning, and the meaning in the verse is comfort for the Prophet: that is, do not let their haste to disbelief grieve you, for God has promised you victory over them. Sixth - The Almighty’s saying: Of those who said, ‘We believe’ with their mouths, and they are the hypocrites, but their hearts did not believe, meaning they did not conceal faith in their hearts as their tongues uttered it, and of those who were Jews, meaning the Jews of Medina, and this would be the end of the statement. Then He began and said: listeners to falsehood, meaning they are listeners, and similarly, going around among you (al-Nur 24:58). It was said that the beginning is from the Almighty’s saying: and of those who were Jews, meaning, and of those who were Jews, there are people who listen to falsehood, meaning they are receptive to the lies of their leaders from the distortion of the Torah. It was said: that they listen to your words, O Muhammad, in order to lie about you. So among them were those who attended the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then lied about him in front of their common people, and made his image ugly in their eyes, and this is the meaning of His saying: listeners to other people who did not come to you, and among the hypocrites were those who would spit. Al-Farra’ said: listeners and going around are permissible, as He said: cursed wherever they are found (al-Ahzab 33:61), and as He said: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and delight [At-Tur].:17] Then he said: Feasting (al-Dukhan 44:27) Others (al-Dhariyat 51:16) And Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: God Almighty mentioned the spy in the Qur’an by saying: listening to other people who have not come to you and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not address them despite his knowledge of them because at that time the rulings had not been established and Islam had not been established. The ruling on the spy will come in Al-Mumtahanah, God willing. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: They distort words from their [proper] usages. That is, they interpret them in a way other than their interpretation after they understood them from you and knew their usages that God Almighty intended, and He explained His rulings, so they said: His law is to abandon stoning and make forty lashes instead of stoning a married person, changing the ruling of God Almighty. They distort is in the place of the row because He said: listeners. It is not a state of the pronoun in they come to you, because if they did not come, they would not hear, and distortion is only from those who witness and hear, so they distort. The distorters from the Jews are some of them, not all of them. Therefore, the meaning was carried over to and from those who are Jews a group. Speakers is more similar. They say is in the place of the state of the pronoun in they distort. “If you are given this, then take it.” That is, if Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, comes to you with the lashes, then accept it, otherwise not. Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: And whomsoever God intends to test meaning his misguidance in this world and his punishment in the Hereafter you will not possess for him anything from God meaning you will not benefit him those are the ones whose hearts God did not intend to purify is a statement from Him, the Almighty, that He decreed that they would be disbelievers, and the verse indicates that misguidance is by the will of God, the Almighty, in response to those who said otherwise, as mentioned above, meaning God did not intend to purify their hearts from the seal and stamp on them as He purified the hearts of the believers as a reward for them, for them in this world is disgrace It was said: it is their disgrace when they denied stoning, then the Torah was brought and the crime was found in it. It was also said: their disgrace in this world was taking the jizya and humiliation, and God knows best.
5:42: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: listeners to falsehood. He repeated it for emphasis and emphasis, and it has been mentioned before. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Consumers of what is unlawful is an expression of abundance. The root of what is unlawful in the language is destruction and hardship. God Almighty said: Then He will destroy you with a punishment (Ta-Ha 20:61). Al-Farazdaq said: There was a time, O Ibn Marwan, when nothing was left of money except what was wiped out or was left behind. This is the narration, or it is raised in apposition to the meaning because the meaning is that he did not leave, did not remain. It is said to the barber: he eradicated, meaning he uprooted. And the forbidden money was called slander because it makes acts of obedience ashamed, meaning it takes them away and eradicates them. Al-Farra’ said: Its origin is the dog of hunger. It is said that a man has a slandered stomach, meaning he is a glutton, so it is as if the one who asks for a bribe and eats the forbidden from greed for what he is given is like the one who has a slandered stomach from gluttony. And it was said: The forbidden money was called slander because it erases a person’s chivalry. I said: The first statement is more appropriate because with the loss of religion, chivalry is lost, and there is no chivalry for one who has no religion. Ibn Masoud and others said: Bribery is ill-gotten gain. Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: A bribe to a ruler is ill-gotten gain. And on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Every flesh that has grown from ill-gotten gains, the Fire is more deserving of it. They said: O Messenger of God, what is ill-gotten gains? He said: Bribery in judgment. Ibn Mas`ud also said: Illicit gains are when a man fulfills a need of his brother and gives him a gift which he accepts. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: Illicit gains are when a man eats based on his status, such as if he has status with the ruler and someone asks him for something and he does not fulfill it except by taking a bribe. There is no disagreement among the early Muslims that taking a bribe to invalidate a right or something that is not permissible is ill-gotten gains and is forbidden. Abu Hanifa said: If a ruler takes a bribe, he is removed from office immediately, even if he is not removed, and every ruling he makes after that is void. I said: This is not permissible to differ on, God willing, because taking a bribe from him is immorality, and the immoral person’s ruling is not permissible, and God knows best. And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: May God curse the briber and the one who takes the bribe. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Bribery, the fee of a soothsayer, and asking for bribes in a case are ill-gotten gains. It was narrated on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih that he was asked: Is bribery forbidden in everything? He said: No, what is disliked about bribery is that you give a bribe to be given something that is not yours or to pay a right that is due to you. But if you give a bribe to pay for your religion, your blood, and your money, then it is not forbidden. Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi, the jurist, said: And we take this to mean that there is nothing wrong with a man paying for himself and his money with a bribe. This is as narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud: He had two dinars in Abyssinia, and he said: The sin is on the receiver, not the giver. Al-Mahdi said: Whoever considers the earnings of a cupper and those mentioned with him to be ill-gotten gains, then the meaning is that it is desirable for the one who takes it to be honorable. I said: The correct view regarding the cupper’s earnings is that they are good, and whoever takes good earnings will not lose his chivalry nor will his status be lowered. Malik narrated on the authority of Hamid al-Tawil, on the authority of Anas, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was cupped by Abu Tayyiba, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered a sa’ of dates for him and ordered his family to reduce his tax. Ibn ‘Abd al-Barr said: This indicates that the earnings of the cupper are permissible, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, does not make a price, reward, or compensation for anything false. This hadith of Anas abrogates what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade regarding the price of blood and abrogates what he disliked regarding the permission of the cupper. Al-Bukhari and Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was cupped and gave the cupper his wages. If it had been ill-gotten gain, he would not have given it to him. Illicit gain and ill-gotten gain are two languages that are recited in. Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, and Al-Kisa’i read it with two dammahs, and the rest read it with a dammah on the seen alone. Al-Abbas ibn Al-Fadl narrated on the authority of Kharijah ibn Mus’ab on the authority of Nafi’ that they ate ill-gotten gain with a fathah on the seen and a sukoon on the ha’. This is a source of sahtahu. It is said: asahat and sahat, meaning one thing and Al-Zajjaj said: sahtahu took it little by little. God the Almighty said: If they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them. This is a choice from God the Almighty, mentioned by Al-Qushayri, and its meaning was mentioned earlier, that they were people of truce, not people of the covenant, because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Medina, he made a truce with the Jews. We are not required to judge between the infidels if they are not people of the covenant, but it is permissible to judge if we wish. As for the people of the covenant, are we required to judge between them if they bring their case to us? Two opinions by Al-Shafi’i: If the dispute is related to a Muslim, then judgment is obligatory. Al-Mahdawi said: The scholars agreed that the judge must judge between a Muslim and a dhimmi, and they differed regarding the dhimmis. Some of them went to the view that the verse is decisive and that the judge has a choice. This was narrated from Al-Nakha’i, Al-Sha’bi, and others, and it is the school of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, and others, except for what was narrated from Malik regarding not implementing the punishment on the People of the Book for adultery, because if a Muslim commits adultery with a woman of the Book, there is a punishment and there is no punishment on her, but if the two adulterers are dhimmis, there is no punishment on them, and this is the school of Abu Hanifa, Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, and others. It was also narrated from Abu Hanifa that he said: They should be flogged and not stoned. Al-Shafi’i said: Abu Yusuf, Abu Thawr and others: The punishment is upon them if they come satisfied with our ruling. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: The imam does not send to them if some of them seek redress from others, and the opponent does not attend his council unless it is in relation to injustices from which corruption spreads, such as murder, looting of homes and the like. As for debts, divorce and other transactions, he does not rule between them except after mutual consent, and the choice is his not to rule and he returns them to their rulers. If he rules between them, he rules by the ruling of Islam. As for forcing them to rule by the Muslims in matters from which corruption spreads, we have not made a covenant with them on corruption, and it is obligatory to cut off corruption from them, from them and from others, because in that is the preservation of their money and blood, and perhaps in their religion it is permissible to do so, and corruption spreads among us. Therefore, we have forbidden them from selling alcohol openly and from displaying adultery and other filth, so that the foolish Muslims do not corrupt them. As for ruling in matters that are specific to their religion, such as divorce, adultery and other things, he is not obligated to follow our religion, and in ruling between them in that there is harm to their rulers and changing their religion, and it is not like that with debts and transactions because in them there is an aspect of injustice and cutting off corruption, and God knows best. And in the verse: A second statement: It is what was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Abdul Aziz and Al-Nakha’i as well, that the choice mentioned in the verse was abrogated by the Almighty’s saying: And judge between them by what God has revealed (al-Ma’idah 5:49) and that the ruler must judge between them, and this is the doctrine of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Abu Hanifa and his companions and others. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: If they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them was abrogated by another verse: And judge between them by what God has revealed. Mujahid said: Only two verses were abrogated from al-Ma’idah 5:His statement: Then judge between them or turn away from them was abrogated by And judge between them by what God has revealed and His statement: Do not violate the symbols of God (al-Ma’idah 5:2) was abrogated by Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). Al-Zuhri said: The Sunnah has been established that the People of the Book should return their rights and inheritances to the people of their religion, unless they come seeking the judgment of God, then judge between them by the Book of God. Al-Samarqandi said: This statement agrees with the statement of Abu Hanifa that they should not judge between them unless they agree to our judgment. Al-Nahhas said: Regarding the abrogating and abrogated, the statement of God the Most High: If they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them was abrogated because it was revealed or the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina and the Jews were many there at that time, and it was more appropriate for them and more suitable for them to return to their judgments. Then when Islam became strong, God the Almighty revealed: And judge between them by what God has revealed.” This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Zuhri, Omar bin Abdul Aziz, and Al-Suddi, and it is the correct statement of Al-Shafi’i. He said in the Book of Jizya: He has no choice if they refer their case to him, because God Almighty said: Until they pay the jizyah willingly while they are humbled (al-Tawbah 9:29). An-Nahhas said: This is one of the most correct arguments, because if the meaning of his statement, while they are humbled, is that the rulings of Muslims apply to them, then it is obligatory that they not be referred back to their rulings. If this is obligatory, then the verse is abrogated. It is also the saying of the Kufians Abu Hanifa, Zufar, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad. There is no disagreement between them that if the People of the Book bring a case to the Imam, then he is not to turn away from him. However, Abu Hanifa said: If the woman and the husband come, then he must rule between them with justice. If the woman comes alone and the husband is not satisfied, then he does not rule. The rest said: It is ruled, so it is proven that the statement of most scholars is that the verse is abrogated, along with what is proven in it from the transmission of Ibn Abbas, and if the hadith had not come from Ibn Abbas, then consideration would have required that it is abrogated because they have agreed that if the People of the Book refer their case to the Imam, then he has the right to judge between them, and that if he judges between them, he is correct according to the group, otherwise he turns away from them, so according to some scholars he is abandoning an obligation and doing what is not permissible for him and is not permitted to do. An-Nahhas said: And for those who said that it was abrogated from the Kufians, there is another statement from them who says: If the Imam knows of a limit from the limits of God Almighty from the People of the Book, he must implement it even if they do not refer their case to him, and he argues that God Almighty says: And judge between them has two possible meanings: One of them - and that you judge between them if they refer their case to you, and the other - and that you judge between them even if they do not refer their case to you - if you know that from them - they said: So our existence in the Book of God Almighty and the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is what requires establishing the truth upon them even if they do not refer their case to us. As for what is in the Book of God, then His Almighty saying: O you who believe, be persistently standing firm. “In justice, witnesses for God” (An-Nisa’: 135). As for what is in the Sunnah, it is the hadith of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: “A Jew who had been flogged and had been bathed passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Is this the punishment for adultery according to you? They said: Yes. So he called one of their scholars and said: I ask you by God, is this the punishment for adultery among you? He said: No. The hadith has been mentioned previously. An-Nahhas said: They argued that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, judged between them and they did not refer this hadith to him. If someone says: In the hadith of Malik on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is said to him: There is not in the hadith of Malik that the two who committed adultery were satisfied with the judgment and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stoned them. Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr said: If the one who argued with the hadith of al-Baraa had pondered, he would not have argued because in the hadith there is an interpretation of the words of God Almighty: “If you are given this, take it, and if you are not given it, beware.” He says: If he issues a fatwa for flogging and blackening, take it, and if he issues a fatwa for stoning, beware. This is evidence that they judged it, and this is clear in the hadith of Ibn Umar and others. If someone says: There is not in the hadith of Ibn Umar that the two adulterers judged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor were they satisfied with his judgment, it is said to him: The punishment for adultery is a right of God Almighty over the ruler to implement, and it is known that the Jews They had a ruler who judged between them and implemented their limits on them, and he is the one who judged the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: And if you judge, judge between them with justice. An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: “There were Qurayzah and Nadir, and Nadir were more noble than Qurayzah. If a man from Qurayzah killed a man from Nadir, he would be killed in his place, and if a man from Nadir killed a man from Qurayzah, his blood money would be one hundred wasqs of dates. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, a man from Qurayzah was killed and they said: Give him to us so that we may kill him.
