They said: There is between us and you the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then the verse was revealed: “And if you judge, judge between them with justice,” A life for a life, “Is it then that they seek the judgment of the days of ignorance?” (al-Ma’idah 5:50).
5:43: The Almighty said: And how can they judge you while they have the Torah, in which is the judgment of God? Al-Hasan said: It is stoning. Qatada said: It is retaliation. It is said: Does the Almighty's saying: In which is the judgment of God indicate that it was not abrogated? The answer: Abu Ali said: Yes, because if it were abrogated, it would not be called after the abrogation that it is the judgment of God, just as it is not said that the judgment of God is the permissibility of alcohol or the prohibition of the Sabbath. And His saying: And those are not believers means that your judgment is from God. Abu Ali said: Whoever seeks other than the judgment of God from where he is not pleased with it is an unbeliever, and this is the case of the Jews.
5:44: The Almighty said: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, in which was guidance and light meaning clarification, illumination, and definition that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the truth of guidance in the nominative case as a subject, and light is an appositive to it. The prophets who submitted to God judge by it for those who are Jews. It was said: What is meant by the prophets is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he expressed it in the plural form. It was also said: Everyone who was sent after Moses to establish the Torah, and that the Jews said: The prophets were Jews, and the Christians said: They were Christians, so God Almighty revealed their lie. The meaning of submitted is that they believed in the Torah from the time of Moses to the time of Jesus, peace be upon them, and between them were a thousand prophets. It was also said: Four thousand. It was also said: More than that, they judged by what was in the Torah. It was also said: The meaning of submitted is that they submitted and obeyed God's command in what they were sent with. It was also said: That is, the prophets who are on the religion of Abraham, may God bless him and grant him peace, judge by it, and the meaning is one. The meaning of for those who are Jews is over those who are Jews, so the lam Meaning on and it was said: the meaning is that the prophets who submitted to Islam judge by it for those who are Jews and over them, so on them was deleted, and those who submitted here is an adjective with a meaning of praise like in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. They repented, meaning they repented from disbelief. And it was said: there is an advancement and a delay in it, meaning we sent down the Torah in which there is guidance and light for those who are Jews, the prophets, rabbis, and scholars judge by it, meaning the rabbis judge by it, and they are the ones who govern the people with knowledge and raise them with its small things before its large things, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It was mentioned previously in Al Imran. Abu Razin said: the rabbis are the scholars, the wise, and the scholars. Ibn Abbas said: they are the jurists. The scholar and the scholar is the man of knowledge, and it is taken from tahbeer, which is to improve, so they clarify and embellish knowledge, and it is inked in their hearts. Mujahid said: the rabbis are above the scholars, and the alif and lam are for emphasis. Al-Jawhari said: Al-Hibr and Al-Hibr are the same as ‘Ahbar Al-Yahud’ and with the kasra it is more eloquent because it is pluralized as ‘af’al’ rather than ‘fa’ul’. Al-Farra’ said: “It is habr with the kasra. This is said of the scholar.” Al-Thawri said: I asked Al-Farra’ why the ink was called habr? He said: The scholar is called habr and ink, so the meaning is the ink of the ink. Then he deleted it as he said: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82) meaning the people of the town. He said: “So I asked Al-Asma’i and he said: This is nothing. It was only called habr because of its influence.” It is said: On his teeth is ink, meaning yellowness or blackness. Abu al-Abbas said: The ink with which he writes is called ink because he inks with it, meaning he verifies with it. Abu Ubaid said: What I have in one of the inks is the sea with the fat-ha, and its meaning is knowledge of inking speech and knowledge and improving it. He said: And this is how all the hadith scholars narrate it with the fat-ha, and the ink with which he writes and its place is the inkwell with the kasra, and the ink is also the trace and the plural is ink from Ya’qub with what they have preserved of the Book of God meaning what they have entrusted of His knowledge, and the ba’ is related to the rabbis and the inkwells as if he said: and the scholars with what they have preserved or it is related to the rulings, meaning they rule with what they have preserved. And they were witnesses over it meaning over the book that it is from God. Ibn Abbas: Witnesses over the ruling of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that it is in the Torah. So do not fear the people meaning in showing the description of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and showing the stoning. And fear meaning in concealing that, so the address is to the scholars of the Jews. And the meaning may include everyone who concealed a right that was due from him and did not reveal it. The meaning of And do not exchange My verses for a small price was mentioned earlier. Completed God the Almighty said: And whoever does not rule by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. The oppressors and the immoral were all revealed about the disbelievers. This was proven in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Al-Baraa’, and it was mentioned earlier. Based on this, the majority of scholars say that a Muslim is not a disbeliever even if he commits a major sin. It was said that there is an implication in it, meaning that whoever does not rule by what God has revealed in rejection of the Qur’an and in denial of the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a disbeliever. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. The verse is general on this basis. Ibn Mas’ud and Al-Hasan said: It is general for everyone who does not rule by what God has revealed from the Muslims, Jews and disbelievers, meaning believing in that and considering it permissible. As for the one who does that while believing that he is riding in a state of ihram, then he is one of the immoral Muslims and his matter is up to God the Almighty. If He wills, He will punish him, and if He wills, He will forgive him. Ibn Abbas said in a narration: Whoever does not rule by what God has revealed has committed an act that rivals the acts of the disbelievers. It was said that whoever does not rule by all that God has revealed is a disbeliever. As for the one who rules by monotheism and does not rule by some of the laws, then he is not included in this verse. The first is correct, except that Al-Sha’bi said: It is specifically for the Jews. Al-Nahhas chose it and said: Three things indicate this, including that the Jews were mentioned before this in His statement, for those who are Jews, so the pronoun returned to them. Among them is that the context of the speech indicates this. Do you not see that after it... And We prescribed for them This pronoun refers to the Jews by consensus. Also, the Jews are those who denied stoning and retaliation. If someone says: If min is for retribution, then it is general unless there is evidence to specify it, it is said to him: min here means who with what we mentioned of evidence and the estimate: And the Jews who did not rule by what God revealed, then those are the disbelievers. This is one of the best things that have been said about this. It is narrated that Hudhayfah was asked about these verses, are they about the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, they are about them, and you should follow their path step by step. It was said: The disbelievers are for the Muslims, the oppressors are for the Jews, and the immoral are for the Christians. This is the choice of Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi. He said: Because it is apparent in the verses. It is the choice of Ibn Abbas, Jabir ibn Zayd, Ibn Abi Zaydah, Ibn Shabramah, and al-Sha'bi as well. Tawus and others said: It is not disbelief that removes one from the religion, but it is disbelief less than disbelief. This differs if he rules by what he has on the basis that it is from God, then it is a change of it that necessitates disbelief, and if he rules by it out of desire and disobedience, then it is a sin that forgiveness attains according to the principle of the people of the Sunnah in forgiveness for sinners. Al-Qushayri said: And the doctrine of The Khawarij said that whoever takes bribes and rules other than by the rule of God is an infidel. This was attributed to Al-Hasan and Al-Suddi. Al-Hasan also said: God Almighty has imposed three things on the rulers: that they not follow whims, that they not fear people and be afraid of Him, and that they not buy. For his verses a small price.
5:45: It contains thirty issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And We ordained for them therein, ‘A life for a life.’ The Almighty made clear that He made a life equal to a life in the Torah, but they disobeyed that and went astray, so the blood money of the Nadhiri was more, and the Nadhiri would not kill for the Qurayzi, but the Qurayzi would be killed for it. When Islam came, Banu Qurayzah consulted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, so he ruled that it was equal. Banu Nadhir said: You have reduced us, so this verse was revealed, and We wrote means we imposed, as was mentioned previously. Their law was retaliation or forgiveness, and there was no blood money among them, as was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. Abu Hanifa and others relied on this verse and said: A Muslim is killed for a dhimmi because it is a life for a life, and this was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him. He was asked: Did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, single you out for anything? He said: No, except what is in this. Then he took out a book from the hilt of his sword, and in it was... “The blood of the believers is equal, and they are one hand against others. A Muslim shall not be killed for a disbeliever, nor shall a person with a covenant be killed for his covenant.” Also, the verse came to respond to the Jews in their preference between tribes and their taking from one tribe a man for a man and from another tribe a man for two men. The Shafi’is said: This is report about the law of those before us, and the law of those before us is not our law. And enough has been said in the Cow in response to them, so reflect on it there. And a fourth aspect is that God Almighty said: And We ordained for them therein that a life is for a life. And that was written in this Torah, and they were one religion, and they did not have people of protection as the Muslims have people of protection, because the jizyah is booty and spoils that God gave to the believers, and He did not make the booty for anyone before this nation, and no prophet in the past was sent except to his people, so the verse made the ruling obligatory on the Children of Israel since their blood was equal. It is like what one of us says about the blood of other than the Muslims: a life for a life, as he points to a specific people and says: The ruling on these people is that a life from them is for a life. So what is obligatory by the ruling of this verse on the people of the Qur’an It is said to them among themselves in this manner: A life for a life, and there is nothing in the Book of God that indicates that a life for a life despite the difference in religion. Second - The companions of Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa said: If he wounds or cuts off the ear or hand and then kills, then that is done to him because God Almighty said: “And We ordained for them therein: A life for a life, and an eye for an eye.” So what was taken from him is taken and he is treated as he was treated. Our scholars said: If he intended to mutilate him, then he is treated likewise, and if that was during his fight and defense, then he is killed with the sword. They only said that in the case of mutilation, it is obligatory because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, blinded the two Arabs, as was explained in this surah. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And an eye for an eye. Nafi’, Asim, Al-A’mash, and Hamzah read it in the accusative case in all of them as a conjunction. It is permissible to lighten an and raise all of them with the beginning and conjunction. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Abu Amr, and Abu Ja’far read it in the accusative case for all of them except for wounds. Al-Kisa’i and Abu Ubaid used to read eye for eye, nose for nose, ear for ear, tooth for tooth, and wounds in the nominative case in all of them. Abu Ubaid said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Harun on the authority of Ibad bin Kathir on the authority of Uqayl on the authority of Al-Zuhri “on the authority of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, read: And We wrote to them in it that a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and wounds are retaliation.” And the nominative case is from three aspects with the beginning and the report and on the meaning in the place of that the soul because the meaning is we said to them: a life for a life. The third aspect was said by Al-Zajjaj - it is a conjunction to the implied in the soul because the pronoun in the soul is in the nominative case, because the estimate is that the soul is taken by the soul, so the names are conjoined to it. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: And whoever reads in the nominative case made it… This is the beginning of a speech about the ruling on the Muslims, and this is the more correct of the two opinions, and that is that it is the reading of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and an eye for an eye, and so is what comes after it, and the address is to the Muslims, they were commanded to do this, and whoever singles out the wounds for raising, then it is upon the cutting off of what came before it and to start with it, the Muslims were commanded to do this specifically and what came before it they were not confronted with it. Fourth: This verse indicates the application of retaliation in what was mentioned. Ibn Shabramah relied on the generality of his statement, An eye for an eye, that the right hand is gouged out with the left, and vice versa. He applied this to the right and left hands, and said: The incisor is taken by the molar and the molar by the incisor, based on the generality of the statement of God Almighty, And a tooth for a tooth. Those who disagreed with him, and they are the scholars of the nation, said: The right eye is the one taken by the right when it is present, and this does not extend to the left with consent. This shows us that what is meant by his statement, An eye for an eye, is the fulfillment of what is similar to it from the offender, so it is not permissible for him to extend it to someone else, just as it is not extended from the foot to the hand in all cases, and there is no doubt about this. Fifth: The scholars agreed that if both eyes were injured by mistake, then blood money is due for both of them. If one eye is injured by mistake, then half the blood money is due for both. If the eye of a one-eyed person is gouged out, then the full blood money is due. This was narrated on the authority of Umar and Uthman, and Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan, al-Zuhri, Qatadah, Malik, al-Layth ibn Sa`d, Ahmad, and Ishaq said the same. It was said: Half the blood money. This was narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mughaffal, Masruq, and al-Nakha`i. This was also said by al-Thawri, al-Shafi`i, and al-Nu`man. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This is what we say, because in the hadith: In both eyes is the blood money. If this is the case, it is reasonable that in one of them is half the blood money. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is the apparent analogy, but our scholars said: The benefit of the one-eyed person in his sight is like the benefit of the healthy person or close to that, so he is required to pay the same blood money as his. Sixth - They differed regarding the one-eyed man who puts out the eye of a healthy person. It was narrated from Omar, Othman and Ali that there is no retaliation against him and he owes the full blood money. This is what Ata, Saeed Al-Musayyab and Ahmad bin Hanbal said. Malik said: If he wants, he can take retaliation and leave him blind, or he can take the full blood money for the eye of the one-eyed man. Al-Nakha’i said: If he wants, he can take retaliation and he can take half the blood money. Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa and Al-Thawri said: He owes retaliation. This was also narrated from Ali and it is the opinion of Masruq, Ibn Sirin and Ibn Muqal. Ibn Al-Mundhir and Ibn Al-Arabi chose it because God the Almighty said: An eye for an eye and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the blood money for the eyes, so half the blood money for the eye. Retaliation between a healthy person and a one-eyed person is like it is among all people. Ahmad bin Hanbal’s opinion is that in retaliation, he takes all of his sight for some of it, and this is not equal. This is what was narrated from Omar, Othman and Ali regarding this. Malik’s opinion is that when the evidence conflicts, the one who was wronged is better. Ibn Al-Arabi said: Adhering to the generality of the Qur’an is more appropriate because it is safer in the sight of God the Almighty. Seventh - They differed regarding the eye of the one-eyed person with which he cannot see. It was narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit that he said: There is one hundred dinars in it. And on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab that he said: There is one-third of its blood money. And Ishaq said the same. And Mujahid said: There is half of its blood money. And Masruq, Al-Zuhri, Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, and Al-Nu’man said that there is a ruling on it. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: And we say the least of what was said. Eighth - In the case of the loss of sight from both eyes while the pupils remain, the full blood money is paid, and Al-A’mash and Al-Akhfash are equal in this. In the case of the loss of sight from one of them while it remains, the blood money is paid in half. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The best thing that has been said about this is what Ali bin Abi Talib said: He ordered that his healthy eye be covered and a man’s eyeballs be given to him, so he went with it while looking until his sight was gone, then he ordered a line drawn at that point. Then he ordered that his other eye be covered and the healthy eye be opened and a man’s eyeball be given to him, so he went with it while looking until his sight was gone, then he ordered a line drawn at that point. Then he ordered that he be moved to another place and the same was done to him and he found it equal, so he was given what was missing from his sight from the money of the other. This is according to the Shafi’i school of thought and it is the saying of our scholars, and it is: Ninth - There is no disagreement among the scholars that there is no retaliation for some of the sight, since it is not possible to reach it. The method of retaliation for the eye is to heat a mirror, then place cotton on the other eye, then bring the mirror close to the eye until its fibers flow. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, as mentioned by Al-Mahdawi and Ibn Al-Arabi. There was a difference of opinion regarding the eyelid. Zaid bin Thabit said: There is a quarter of the blood money for it, and this is the opinion of Al-Sha’bi, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Hashim, Al-Thawri, Al-Shafi’i and the people of opinion. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi that he said: There is a third of the blood money for the upper eyelid, and there are two thirds of the blood money for the lower eyelid, and Malik said the same. Tenth - The Almighty said: And a nose for a nose. The hadith came "On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: And for the nose if it is completely cut off, the blood money." Ibn al-Mundhir said: And all the people of knowledge who have memorized from him agreed to say this, and retaliation for the nose if the crime was intentional is like retaliation for all other limbs according to the Book of God Almighty, and they differed regarding breaking the nose. Malik saw retaliation in intentional cases, and in accidental cases, diligence. Ibn Nafi' narrated that there is no blood money for the nose until it is cut off from its root. Abu Ishaq al-Tunisi said: This is anomalous, and the first is well-known. If we branch off from what is well-known, then in some of the mortals, the blood money is calculated according to his account from the mortal. Ibn al-Mundhir said: And what is cut off from the nose is its good. This was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and al-Sha'bi, and al-Shafi'i said the same. Abu Umar said: And they differed regarding the mortal if it is cut off and the nose is not cut off. Malik, al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa and their companions went to the view that in that case the full blood money is due, then if something is cut off from it after that, then there is a ruling in it. Malik said: What is due blood money from the nose is to cut off the mortal, which is less than the bone. Ibn Al-Qasim: It is the same whether the rib is cut off from the bone and the nose is removed from the bone from under the eyes, but in the case of blood money, like the glans, in which there is blood money, and in the case of removing the penis, there is blood money. Eleventh: Ibn Al-Qasim said: If the nose is pierced or broken and is healed due to a defect, then there is discretion and no known blood money for it. If it is healed without a defect, then there is nothing in it. He said: If the nose is pierced and is healed without a defect, then it is not like the wound that is healed without a defect, so there is blood money for it, because that is what the Sunnah came with. There is no effect in the piercing of the nose. He said: The nose is a separate bone that does not have a wound. Malik, Al-Shafi’i and their companions agreed that there is no wound in it, and there is no wound in their view except in what is in the cavity. The maran is what is part of the nose. Al-Khalil and others said the same. Abu Omar said: I think that its dung is its maran and its harebah is its tip. It has been said that the hare, the rawtah and the atramah are the tip of the nose. The jurists Malik, Al-Shafi’i, the Kufians and those who followed them agreed on the smell if it is diminished or missing, according to the ruling. Twelfth - The Almighty’s saying: And an ear for an ear. Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said about the one who cuts off a man’s ears: He is subject to a ruling, and he is only liable for the blood money for the hearing, and it is measured in its deficiency as it is measured in sight, and in its nullification from one of them, half the blood money is due, even if he could not hear except with it, unlike the blind eye, in which the blood money is full, as mentioned above. Ashhab said: If the hearing is asked about before, then one of the two ears hears what the other hears, then in my opinion it is like the sight, and if the hearing is in doubt, it is tested by shouting at him from several places, and that is measured, and if they are equal or close, he is given according to the amount of his hearing that he lost, and he swears to that. Ashhab said: And that is applied to him according to the hearing of an average man like him, and if he is tested and his statement differs, he is not entitled to anything. Isa bin Dinar said: If his statement differs, he is compensated for the lesser amount with his oath. Thirteenth - The Almighty’s saying: And a tooth for a tooth. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It was proven “from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he exacted retaliation for a tooth and said: The Book of God is Retaliation. The hadith came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In the tooth, five camels. Ibn al-Mundhir said: According to the apparent meaning of this hadith, we say: There is no preference for the incisors over the canines, molars, and canines, because they are all included in the apparent meaning of the hadith. This is what most of the people of knowledge say, and among those who said according to the apparent meaning of the hadith and did not prefer one of them over the other, are Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Tawus, al-Zuhri, Qatadah, Malik, al-Thawri, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, al-Nu’man, and Ibn al-Hasan. This was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Abbas, and Mu’awiyah. There is a second statement that we narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he ruled for what is in front of the mouth, five obligatory prayers, five obligatory prayers, and that is fifty dinars, the value of each obligatory prayer is ten dinars, and for the molars, one camel, one camel. Ata’ used to say: For the tooth, the two incisors, and the two canines, five, five, and for what is left, two camels, two camels, the upper and lower of the mouth are the same, and the molars are the same. Abu Umar said: As for what Malik narrated in his Muwatta’ on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab: that Umar ruled for the molars, one camel, one camel, the meaning of this is that the molars are twenty. Molars and teeth are twelve: four incisors, four canines and four canines. According to Omar’s statement, the blood money becomes eighty camels for teeth, five by five, and for molars, one camel by one. According to Muawiyah’s statement, for molars and teeth, five camels by five, the blood money becomes sixty and one hundred camels. According to Saeed bin Al-Musayyab’s statement, two camels by two for molars, which are twenty molars, for which forty is due. And for teeth, five camels by five, so that is sixty, which completes one hundred camels, and it is the full blood money in camels. The difference between them is only in the molars, not the teeth. Abu Omar said: The difference of scholars from the Companions and Followers regarding the blood money for teeth and the preference of some over others is very great, and the evidence is established for what the jurists, Malik, Abu Hanifa and Al-Thawri, went to, based on the apparent statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And in the tooth there are five camels, and the molar is one of the teeth. Ibn Abbas narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The fingers are the same, and the teeth are the same, the incisor and the molar are the same, this and that are the same. This is a text narrated by Abu Dawood, and Abu Dawood also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the fingers of the hands and feet equal. Abu Omar said: According to these reports, a group of jurists of the countries and the majority of the people of knowledge say that all fingers are equal in blood money and that all teeth are equal in blood money, the incisors, molars and canines. None of them is preferred over the other, according to what is in the book of Amr ibn Hazm. Al-Thawri mentioned on the authority of Azhar ibn Muharib who said: Two men disputed before Shuraih, one of whom struck the incisor of the other with his molar. Shuraih said: The incisor and its beauty, and the molar and its benefit are a tooth, and the tooth of a people. Abu Omar said: This is the practice today in all countries, and God knows best. Fourteenth - If a tooth is struck and turns black, then its full blood money is due according to Malik and Al-Layth bin Saad. Abu Hanifa said the same and it was narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, and it is the opinion of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Al-Zuhri, Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, and Shuraih. It was narrated on the authority of Amr bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that it is due one-third of its blood money. Ahmad and Ishaq said the same. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr said: This is a ruling. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is a disagreement in my opinion that leads to agreement, because if its blackness has taken away its benefit and only its form remains, like the paralyzed hand of a blind woman, then there is no disagreement about the obligation of blood money. Then if some or all of its benefit remains, then it is not due except to the extent that the benefit is lost, according to the ruling. What was narrated on the authority of Umar, may God be pleased with him, that it is a third of its blood money is not authenticated from him in terms of chain of transmission or jurisprudence. Fifteenth - They differed about the age of the boy being pulled out before he has a full mouth. Malik, Al-Shafi’i and the People of Opinion said: If a boy’s tooth is pulled out and grows back, then there is nothing on the one who pulled it out. However, Malik and Al-Shafi’i said: If it grows back less than the length of the one that is close to it, then he is to be given from its blood money according to the amount of its deficiency. A group said: There is a ruling on it. This was narrated from Al-Sha’bi and Al-Nu’man said the same. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: An orchard has it until the time when the people of knowledge say that it will not grow back. If that is the case, then its full amount is due according to the apparent meaning of the hadith. If it grows back, then the blood money is returned. Most of the people of knowledge who have memorized it say: It is to be waited for a year. This was narrated from Ali, Yazid, Amr ibn Abdul Aziz, Shuraih, Al-Nakha’i, Qatadah, Malik and the People of Opinion. Al-Shafi’i did not specify a specific period for this. Sixteenth: If an adult tooth is pulled out and its blood money is taken, then it grows back, Malik said that what was taken is not returned. The Kufians said: It is returned if it grows back. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions: It is returned and it is not returned because this is a growth that is not common and the ruling is not established by the rare. This is the reasoning of our scholars. The Kufians held that its replacement has grown, so its original tooth is returned. Al-Shafi’i said: If another jinn has committed a crime against it and it has grown back healthy, there is a full blood money for it. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This is the more correct of the two opinions, because each of them is pulling out a tooth, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the compensation for a tooth five camels. Seventeenth - If a man pulls out a man’s tooth and its owner puts it back and it falls down, then according to us, there is nothing wrong with it. Al-Shafi’i said: He does not have the right to put it back because it is impure. Ibn al-Musayyab and Ata’ said the same. If he puts it back, he must repeat every prayer he prayed because it is dead. Likewise, if his ear is cut off and he puts it back because of the heat of the blood and it sticks together, likewise Ata’ said: The ruler forces him to pull it out because it is dead and sticks it together. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a mistake and the one who is unaware of it is ignorant that putting it back and returning it to its original form does not necessitate its being crooked by its ruling because the impurity in it was due to separation and it has returned connected. The rulings of the Shari’ah are not attributes of objects, but rather they are rulings that go back to the statement of God Almighty about it and His information about it. I said: What Ibn al-Arabi narrated on the authority of Ata’ is contrary to what Ibn al-Mundhir narrated on his authority. Ibn al-Mundhir said: They differed about a tooth being pulled out as retaliation and then being put back in its place so that it can grow. Ata al-Khurasani and Ata ibn Abi Rabah said: There is nothing wrong with that. Al-Thawri, Ahmad and Ishaq said: It is pulled out because retaliation is for disfigurement. Al-Shafi’i said: He does not have the right to put it back because it is impure, and the ruler forces him to pull it out. Eighteenth - If he had an extra tooth and it was extracted, then there is a ruling on it, and the jurists of the countries said the same. Zaid bin Thabit said: There is a third of the blood money on it. Ibn al-Arabi said: There is no evidence for the estimation, so the ruling is more just. Ibn al-Mundhir said: What was narrated on the authority of Zaid is not correct. It was narrated on the authority of Ali that he said: If some of the tooth is broken, its owner is given according to what was missing from it, and this is the opinion of Malik, al-Shafi’i, and others. I said: Here ends what God Almighty has specified for him regarding the organs, and He did not mention the lips and the tongue. They are: Nineteenth - The majority said: And for the lips is the blood money, and for each unit is half the blood money, with no preference for the upper lip over the lower. It was narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit, Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, and Al-Zuhri: For the upper lip is a third of the blood money, and for the lower lip is two-thirds of the blood money. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: And I say with the first opinion: for the hadith attributed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: And for the lips is the blood money. And because for the hands is the blood money and their benefits are different, and what is cut off from the lips is calculated accordingly. As for the tongue, the hadith came: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: For the tongue is the blood money.” And the scholars of Madinah, the people of Kufa, the people of hadith, and the people of opinion agreed on saying this. Ibn Al-Mundhir said. The twenty-fifth - and they differed regarding the man who commits a crime on the tongue, cutting off part of the tongue and losing some of his speech. Most of the scholars said: The amount of speech lost from twenty-eight letters should be considered, so he should pay blood money in proportion to the amount of his speech lost. If all of his speech is lost, there is blood money in it, so there is blood money in it. This is the opinion of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and the people of opinion. Malik said: There is no retaliation for the tongue due to the lack of knowledge of how to fully implement retaliation. If it is possible, then retaliation is the original. Twenty-one - They differed about the tongue of a mute person who is to be cut off. Al-Sha’bi, Malik, the people of Medina, Al-Thawri the people of Iraq, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, Al-Nu’man and his two companions said: There is a ruling on it. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: There are two strange sayings. One of them is the saying of Al-Nakha’i that there is blood money for it, and the other is the saying of Qatadah that there is a third of the blood money for it. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The first saying is more correct because it is less than what was said. Ibn Al-Arabi said: God Almighty specified the most important organs and left the rest of them for analogy. So every organ has retaliation if it is possible and there is no fear of death for it. Likewise, every organ whose benefit is no longer effective but its form remains, there is no retaliation and there is blood money for it because retaliation is not possible for it. Twenty-second - The Almighty’s saying: And for wounds there is retaliation meaning set-off. It was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. There is no retaliation in every frightening matter, nor in what does not lead to retaliation, unless the striker made a mistake or increased or decreased the amount. And retaliation is due for intentional wounds if they are something for which retaliation is possible. This is all for intentional wounds. As for the mistake, then the blood money is due. And if the blood money is due for accidental killing, then it is the same for wounds. And in Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Anas: That the sister of Al-Rabi’ - Umm Haritha - injured a person, so they disputed before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Retaliation, retribution.” Umm al-Rabi’ said: O Messenger of God, will retribution be taken from so-and-so? By God, no retribution will be taken from her. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Glory be to God, O Umm al-Rabi’, retribution is the Book of God. She said: No, by God, no retribution will ever be taken from her. So they kept on going until they accepted the blood money. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There are among God’s servants those who, if they swear by God, He will fulfill their oath. I said: The one who was wounded in this hadith is a slave girl, and the wound is the breaking of her two front teeth. Al-Nasa’i also narrated on the authority of Anas that his aunt broke a slave girl’s front tooth, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled for retaliation. Her brother Anas ibn al-Nadr said: Will you break so-and-so’s front tooth? No, by Him who sent you with the truth, her front tooth will not be broken. He said: Before that, they had asked her family for forgiveness and compensation, but when her brother, who was Anas’s uncle - and he was the martyr on the day of Uhud - swore, the people agreed to forgive. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There are some servants of God who, if they swear by God, He will fulfill their oath. Abu Dawud also narrated and said: I heard Ahmad ibn Hanbal being asked: How is retaliation for a tooth taken? He said: It cools down. I said: There is no contradiction between the two hadiths, as it is possible that each of them swore an oath and fulfilled their oath to God. This indicates the miracles of the saints, as will be explained in the story of Al-Khidr, God willing. So we ask God to make us steadfast in our belief in their miracles and to include us in their ranks without trial or temptation. Twenty-third - The scholars agreed that the Almighty’s saying and a tooth for a tooth is in the case of deliberate killing. So whoever intentionally hits someone’s tooth, then retaliation is due according to the hadith of Anas. They differed regarding the rest of the bones of the body if they are broken intentionally. Malik said: All the bones of the body are subject to retaliation except for what is feared such as the thigh, the sacrum, the humerus, the mandible, and the Hashimiyyah, in which case blood money is due. The Kufians said: There is no retaliation for a broken bone except the tooth, according to the Almighty’s saying: and a tooth for a tooth. This is the saying of Al-Layth and Al-Shafi’i. Al-Shafi’i said: A fracture can never be like a fracture, so it is forbidden. Al-Tahawi said: They agreed that there is no retaliation for the bone of the head, and so it is for the rest of the bones. The evidence for Malik is the hadith of Anas regarding the tooth, which is a bone, so it is for the rest of the bones except for a bone, and they agreed that there is no retaliation for it due to the fear of losing the soul from it. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: Whoever says there is no retaliation for a bone is contradicting the hadith. And the hadith is not permissible to consider with the presence of the report. I said: This is also indicated by the Almighty’s statement: So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you (al-Baqarah 2:194), And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were punished (al-Nahl 16:126). What they agreed upon is not included in the verses, and God knows best, and God is the Grantor of success. Twenty-fourth - Abu Ubaid said in the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Al-Muwadahah and what was narrated from others in Al-Shaja’. Al-Asma’i and others said: The lam of some of them entered into some: The first of the Shaja’ - Al-Harisa, which is: the one who tears the skin - meaning the one who splits a little - from it it was said, the shortener hars the garment if he splits it and it is also called Al-Harisa from Al-Ba’idah - which is: the one who splits the flesh and splits it after the skin then Al-Mutalaah - which is: the one who took hold of the skin and did not reach the periosteum and the periosteum is a skin or a thin crust between the flesh and the bone. Al-Waqidi said: With us it is Al-Malta’. And others said: It is Al-Malta’ah. He said: And what is it about which the hadith came: It is decided in the case of a wound with its blood, then the one with a scab or a cut, which is: the one from which that crust is scraped or split until the bone is exposed, then that is the wound. Abu Ubaid said: There is no retaliation for any of the wounds except for the wound specifically, because there is nothing among them that has a limit that ends with it except it. As for other wounds, there is its blood money for it, then the Hashimiyyah, which is that which crushes the bone, then the Manqala, with a kasra on the qaf, as narrated by Al-Jawhari, which is that which moves the bone, i.e. breaks it, until the bone bed comes out with the medicine, then the Ummah, which is called the Ma’amumah, which reaches the mother of the head, meaning the brain. Abu Ubaid said: It is said in his statement: And it is decided in the case of a wound with its blood, that if the wound is cut, he is judged for the one who was wounded for the amount of the wound at the time of the wound, and it is not taken lightly. He said: And with us, all wounds are taken lightly until it is seen what happens to it, then it is judged in it at that time. Abu Ubaid said: And with us, the matter with all wounds and all injuries is that it is taken lightly. Hisham told us on the authority of Hisayn, who said that Umar ibn Abdul Aziz: Scratches below the mawda are permissible and there is a settlement for them. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: There is no retaliation for anything below the mawda. Malik said: Retaliation for anything below the mawda is the smeared, the bloody, the puncture wound and the like. The Kufians said the same and added the periosteum. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated it. Abu Ubaid said: The bloody wound is the one that bleeds without blood flowing from it. The tearful wound is that blood flows from it and there is no retaliation for anything below the mawda. Al-Jawhari said: The bloody wound is the one that bleeds but does not flow. Our scholars said: The bloody wound is the one that bleeds, and there is no retaliation for anything after the mawda. From the Hashimiyyah of the bone and the munqala, there is a difference of opinion about it in particular. The nation is the one that reaches the mother of the head and the damighah that pierces the map of the brain. In the hashima of the body, there is retaliation except for what is feared such as the thigh and the like. As for the hashima of the head, Ibn Al-Qasim said: There is no retaliation for it because it will inevitably return to being a munqala. Ashhab said: There is retaliation for it unless it is moved and becomes a munqala, there is no retaliation for it. As for the extremities, retaliation is required for all the joints except for what is feared. In the meaning of the joints are the parts of the scrotum, the ears and the penis. And the eyelids and lips, because it accepts estimation, and in the tongue there are two narrations, and retaliation in the breaking of bones except what was destroyed such as the bones of the chest, neck, spine, thigh and the like, and in the breaking of the bones of the upper arm there is retaliation, and Abu Bakr bin Muhammad bin Amr bin Hazm ruled in the case of a man who broke that his thigh be broken, and Abdul Aziz Abdullah bin Khalid bin Asid did that in Mecca, and it was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Abdul Aziz that he did it, and this is the doctrine of Malik according to what we mentioned, and he said: It is the matter agreed upon among them and practiced in our country in the case of a man who strikes a man and he protects him with his hand and breaks it, he is retaliated against. Twenty-fifth - The scholars said: The head wounds and the body wounds. The scholars agreed that there is a blood money for wounds less than a wound, as Ibn al-Mundhir mentioned. They differed about that blood money. There are five wounds less than a wound: the bloody wound, the tearful wound, the ruptured wound, the joined wound, and the crushed wound. Malik, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and the people of opinion said: There is a ruling for a wound that is bloody, and there is a ruling for a ruptured wound, and there is a ruling for a joined wound. Abd al-Razzaq mentioned on the authority of Zaid bin Thabit that he said: There is a camel for a wound that is bloody, and there are two camels for a ruptured wound, and there are three camels for a wound that is periosteum, and there are four for a wound that is periosteum, and there are five for a wound that is crushed, and there is fifteen for a wound that is crushed, and there is a third of the blood money for a man who is beaten until he loses his mind, or he is beaten until he sings and does not understand, the full blood money, or until he hoarsely speaks and does not understand, the full blood money. And in the eyelid, there is a quarter of the blood money, and in the nipple of the breast, there is a quarter of the blood money. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It was narrated on the authority of Ali regarding the periosteum, like what Zaid said, and it was narrated on the authority of Umar and Uthman that they said: There is half of a wound. Al-Hasan al-Basri, Umar bin Abdul Aziz, and al-Nakha’i said: There is a ruling for it. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, and Ahmad also said: The scholars do not differ that the penalty for a wound caused by a wound is five camels, according to what is in the hadith of Amr ibn Hazm, which states: And in the wound there are five. The scholars agreed that the wound is in the head and face, and they differed in preferring the wound on the face over the wound on the head. It was narrated from Abu Bakr and Amr that they are equal, and a group of the followers said the same, and Al-Shafi’i and Ishaq said the same. It was narrated from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab that the wound on the face is weaker than the wound on the head. Ahmad said: The wound on the face is more deserving of being added to. Malik said: The wound on the head, the wound on the head, and the wound on the head are only on the head and face, and the wound on the head is only on the head up to the brain. He said: The wound on the skull and below it is from the neck, and there is no wound on it. Malik said: The nose is not from the head, and there is no wound on it, and likewise the lower beard, and there is no wound on it. They differed in the wound on other than the head and face. Ashhab and Ibn Al-Qasim said: There is nothing in the wound on the body, its wound on the head, and its wound on the head except for the effort, and there is no known blood money for it. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: This is the saying of Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq, and we say the same. It was narrated from Ata Al-Khurasani that if the wound is on the human body, there are five. And twenty dinars. Abu Omar said: Malik, Al-Shafi’i and their companions agreed that whoever cuts a man’s nose with two or more wounds, or with three wounds, or with more wounds, in one blow, then the full blood money is due for all of them, even if it is torn and becomes one. As for the broken nose, there is no blood money for it according to us, but rather a ruling. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: I did not find in the books of the Medinans mention of the broken nose, but Malik said about whoever breaks a man’s nose, if it was by mistake, then there is discretion in it. Al-Hasan Al-Basri did not set a time limit for the broken nose. Abu Thawr said: If they differed about it, then there is a ruling in it. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: Consideration indicates this, since there is no Sunnah in it and no consensus. Judge Abu Al-Walid Al-Baji said: What is due for the broken nose is due for it. If it becomes a wound, then fifteen, and if it becomes a wound, then a third of the blood money. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: We found that most of the people of knowledge whom we met and heard from them set ten camels for the broken nose. We narrated this statement from Zaid bin Thabit, and Qatada, Ubaidullah bin Al-Hasan and Al-Shafi’i said the same. Al-Thawri and the people of opinion said: There is a thousand dirhams in it. What they mean is one-tenth of the blood money. As for the one who was taken away, Ibn al-Mundhir said: The hadith came from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: In the place of the transfer, fifteen camels are to be taken. And the scholars agreed to say this. Ibn al-Mundhir said: And everyone who has memorized from him among the scholars said that the place of transfer is the place from which bones are to be taken. And Malik, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and the people of opinion said, and it is the saying of Qatadah and Ibn Shabramah - that there is no retaliation in the place of transfer. And we narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr - and it is not proven from him - that he took retaliation from the place of transfer. Ibn al-Mundhir said: And the first is more appropriate because I do not know of anyone who disagreed with that. And as for the place of the one being followed, Ibn al-Mundhir said: The hadith came from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: In the case of a wound that is caused by a woman who is being led, one-third of the blood money is due. The scholars and all the people of knowledge have agreed on this, and we do not know of anyone who disagreed with that except Makhul, who said: If the wound is caused by a woman who is being led, then two-thirds of the blood money is due, and if it is by mistake, then one-third of the blood money is due. This is an odd statement, and I say the first statement. They differed regarding the retaliation for a wound that is caused by a woman who is being led, and many of the people of knowledge said: There is no retaliation for it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr that he cut off the wound from a woman who is being led, but the people denied that. Ata’ said: We do not know of anyone who took retaliation for it before Ibn al-Zubayr. As for a wound that is caused by a puncture wound, then one-third of the blood money is due, according to the hadith of Amr ibn Hazm. There is no disagreement about that except what was narrated on the authority of Makhul, who said: If it is caused by a woman who is being led, then two-thirds of the blood money is due, and if it is by mistake, then one-third of the blood money is due. A wound is anything that penetrates the body, even if it is the entrance of a needle. If it penetrates from both sides, then according to them it is two wounds, and two-thirds of the blood money is due for it. Ashhab said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, ruled that a wound that penetrates the other side should be the blood money for two wounds. Ata’, Malik, al-Shafi’i, and the people of opinion all said: There is no retaliation for a wound that is caused by a puncture wound. Ibn al-Mundhir: And we say the same. Twenty-sixth - They differed regarding retaliation for a slap and the like. Al-Bukhari mentioned on the authority of Abu Bakr, and on his authority, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Suwaid ibn Muqrin, may God be pleased with them, that they retaliated for a slap and the like. He narrated on the authority of Uthman and Khalid ibn al-Walid something similar to that, and it is the opinion of al-Sha’bi and a group of the people of hadith. Al-Layth said: If the slap is on the eye, there is no retaliation for it, for fear of the eye and the ruler will punish him. If it is on the cheek, then there is retaliation for it. A group said: There is no retaliation for a slap. This was narrated on the authority of al-Hasan and Qatadah, and it is the opinion of Malik, the Kufians, and al-Shafi’i. Malik provided evidence for that, saying: The slap of a weak sick person is not like the slap of a strong person, and a black slave is not slapped like a man with a need and appearance. Rather, in all of that, there is personal opinion, because we do not know the extent of the slap. Twenty-seventh - They differed regarding retaliation for a whip strike. Al-Layth and Al-Hasan said: Retaliation is due for it and more is due for transgression. Ibn Al-Qasim said: Retaliation is due for it and no retaliation is due for it according to the Kufians and Al-Shafi’i unless he is wounded. Al-Shafi’i said that if a whip wound is caused, then there is a ruling on it. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: And whatever is inflicted by a whip, stick or stone and is less than a life is deliberate, and retaliation is due for it. This is the opinion of a group of the companions of Hadith. In Al-Bukhari: Umar retaliated for a blow with a whip, and Ali Ibn Abi Tab retaliated for three lashes, and Shuraih took retaliation for a whip and scratches. Ibn Battel said: The hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is an argument for the people of the house for retaliation in every pain, even if it is not a wound. Twenty-eighth - They differed regarding the blood money for women's wounds. In Al-Muwatta', on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, that he used to say: The blood money of a woman for a man is up to one-third of the blood money of a man: her finger, her tooth is like his tooth, her molar is like his molar, her osteoarthritis is like his osteoarthritis. Ibn Bakir said: Malik said: If it reaches one-third of the blood money of a man, it is half of the blood money of a man. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: We narrated this statement from Umar and Zaid bin Thabit, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Umar bin Abdul Aziz, Uroo bin Al-Zubayr, Al-Zuhri, Qatadah, Ibn Hurmuz, Malik, Ahmad bin Hanbal, and Abdul Malik bin Al-Majishun said the same. A group said: The blood money of a woman is half of the blood money of a man, whether it is little or much. We narrated this statement from Ali bin Abi Talib, and Al-Thawri, Al-Shafi'i, Abu Thawr, Al-Nu'man and his two companions said the same. They argued that since they agreed on the large amount, which is the blood money, the small amount was like it, and we say the same. Twenty-ninth - Judge Abdul Wahhab said: And everything that has beauty separate from any benefit at all, then there is a ruling on it, such as the eyebrows, the loss of hair from the beard and the hair of the head, the breasts of a man and his buttocks. The description of the ruling is that the injured person, if he was a healthy slave, then he stands up with the crime, and whatever is missing from his price is made part of his blood money, no matter how much it is. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated it from everyone from the people of knowledge who he has memorized, he said: And the statement of two trustworthy men from the people of knowledge is accepted in it. And it was said: Rather, the statement of one just man is accepted, and God Almighty knows best. So these are some of the rulings on wounds and limbs that are included in the meaning of this verse, in them there is sufficiency for those who limit themselves to them, and God is the guide to guidance by His grace and generosity. The thirty - The Almighty said: Whoever gives it in charity, it is an expiation for him. A condition and its answer, that is, he gives in charity with retaliation and forgives, so it is an expiation for him, that is, for the one who gave charity. It was said: It is an expiation for the one who injured him, so he will not be held accountable for his crime in the Hereafter because it takes the place of taking the right from him and the reward of the one who gave charity. Ibn Abbas mentioned the two opinions, and most of the Companions and those who came after them were on the first. The second was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid and on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i and al-Sha’bi, with differences from them. The first is more apparent because the one who returns in it returns to the one mentioned, which is from. And on the authority of Abu al-Darda’, “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is no Muslim who is injured in any part of his body and forgives it, except that God raises him a degree because of it and removes a sin from him because of it.” Ibn al-Arabi said: And whoever says that if the injured person forgives him, God will forgive him, has no evidence to support it, so it has no meaning.
5:46: The Almighty said: And We followed in their footsteps with Jesus, the son of Mary meaning We made Jesus follow in their footsteps, meaning the footsteps of the prophets who submitted to Islam, confirming what was before him meaning the Torah, for he saw the Torah as true and saw the necessity of working with it until a nullifier comes, confirming, in the accusative case of the solution from Jesus, in it is guidance in the nominative case as a subject, and light is in apposition to it, and confirming has two aspects, and it is possible that it is for Jesus and its conjunction with the first confirming, and it is possible that it is a state of the Gospel, and the interpretation would be, And We gave him the Gospel, settled in it is guidance and a warning and confirming, and guidance and admonition is in apposition to confirming, meaning a guide and an admonisher, for the righteous and He singled them out because they are the ones who benefit from them, and it is possible to raise them in apposition to His saying, in it is guidance and light.
5:47: The Almighty said: And let the People of the Gospel judge by what God has revealed therein. Al-A'mash and Hamzah read the verb in the accusative case, so that the lam is the lam of ki, and the rest read it in the jussive mood as a command. According to the first, the lam is related to his saying, And We gave him the Gospel, so that his people may judge by what God has revealed therein. And whoever reads it in the imperative mood, it is like his saying, And that you judge between them. It is a renewed obligation that begins with it, meaning that the People of the Gospel may judge, that is, at that time. As for now, it is abrogated. It was said: This is an order to the Christians now to believe in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because in the Gospel there is the obligation to believe in it, and abrogation is only conceivable in the branches, not in the fundamentals. Makki said: The preferred choice is the jussive mood, because the group is upon it, and because what follows it of threats and intimidation indicates that it is an obligation from God Almighty to the People of the Gospel. Al-Nahhas said: The correct view, in my opinion, is that they are two good readings, because God Almighty did not reveal a book except for it to be acted upon and He commanded to act upon what is in it, so they are both correct.
5:48: The Almighty’s saying: And We have sent down to you the Book The address is to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Book is the Qur’an in truth meaning it is the true command confirming a state of what came before it of the Book meaning of the type of books and a guardian over it meaning high and elevated over it. This indicates the interpretation of those who say that it is preferable, meaning in the abundance of reward, based on what was previously indicated in Al-Fatihah, and it is the choice of Ibn Al-Hisar in his book Sharh Al-Sunnah, and he mentioned it in our book Sharh Al-Asma Al-Husna, and praise be to God. Qatada said: The guardian means the witness, and it was said Al-Hafiz. And Al-Hasan said: The guardian, and from it the saying of the poet: The Book is a guardian for our Prophet, and the truth is known to those with understanding. Ibn Abbas said: And Muhaymina alayhi means trustworthy. Saeed bin Jubair said: The Qur’an is trustworthy over the books that came before it. Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan also said: Al-Muhaymin Al-Amin. Al-Mubarrad said: Its origin is Mu’aymin, the hamza was replaced with a ha’ as it was said in raqat al-ma’, haraqat. Al-Zajjaj and Abu Ali also said it. It was declined and it was said: hayman, yahaymin, haymanah, and he is Muhaymin meaning he was trustworthy. Al-Jawhari said: He is the one who made others feel secure from fear. Its origin is a’man, so he is Mu’min with two hamzas. The second hamza was changed to a ya’ because of their reluctance to come together, so it became Mu’aymin, then the first was made a ha’ as they said: haraqa al-ma’ and haraqa. It is said from it: hayman over something, yahaymin, if he is its guardian, so he is Muhaymin, from Abu Ubaid. Mujahid and Ibn Muhaisin read: And Muhaymina alayhi with a fatha on the meem. Mujahid said: That is, Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is trustworthy over the Qur’an. The Almighty’s statement: Then judge between them by what God has revealed requires judgment. It was said: This is an abrogation of the choice in His statement: Then judge between them or turn away from them (al-Ma’idah 5:42). It was said: This is not an obligation, and the meaning is: Judge between them if you wish, since it is not obligatory for us to judge between them if they are not from the People of the Covenant. There is hesitation and the discussion of this has already passed. It was said: He meant: Judge between the creation, so this was obligatory upon him. The Almighty’s saying: And do not follow their desires has two issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And do not follow their desires means do not act according to their desires and their will over what has come to you of the truth, meaning do not abandon the ruling by what God Almighty has explained in the Qur’an of clarifying the truth and clarifying the rulings. Desires is the plural of desire and does not pluralize desires. It was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah, so He forbade him from following them in what they want, and it indicates the invalidity of the statement of the one who said: The wine is due to whoever destroyed it for them because it is not their property, so it is guaranteed by the one who destroyed it, because requiring the one who destroyed it to be guaranteed by the one who destroyed it is a ruling based on the desires of the Jews, and we were commanded otherwise. The meaning of over what came to you is over what came to you. For each of you We prescribed a law and a method indicates the lack of attachment to the laws of the first people. The law and the law are the apparent way by which salvation is reached. The law in the language: the path by which water is reached. The law is what God has prescribed for His servants of religion, and He has prescribed for them a law, meaning a Sunnah. The Lawgiver is the greatest path, and the law is also the odd number, and the plural is law and law and law and law is the plural of the plural according to Abu Ubaidah, so it is shared, and the method is the path. Continuous, which is the approach and method, that is, the clear one. Al-Zajer said: Whoever doubts, this is a clear water canal and a straight path. Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Yazid said: The Shari’ah is the beginning of the path and the method is the continuous path. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and others: Shari’ah and method are a way and a path. The meaning of the verse is that He made the Torah for its people, the Gospel for its people, and the Qur’an for its people. This is in the laws and acts of worship, and the origin is monotheism, there is no difference in it. The meaning of that was narrated on the authority of Qatada. Mujahid said: The Shari’ah and method are the religion of Muhammad, peace be upon him, and it has abrogated everything else. The Almighty said: And if God had willed, He would have made you one nation. That is, He would have made your law one, so you would have been on the truth. So He made clear that by difference He meant the belief of some people and the disbelief of others. But that He may test you in what He has given you. There is an omission in the speech, which is related to the lam of ki, that is, but He made your laws different to test you, and testing is testing. The Almighty said: So hasten to do good deeds meaning, hasten to do acts of obedience. This indicates that doing obligatory duties is better than delaying them. There is no difference of opinion about this in all acts of worship except for praying at the beginning of its time. Abu Hanifa believes that delaying it is better, and the generality of the verse indicates this. Al-Kiya said: And in it is evidence that fasting while traveling is better than breaking the fast. All of this has been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. “To God is your return, all of you. Then He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.” That is, about that over which you differed, and doubts will be removed.
5:49: The Almighty’s saying: And judge between them by what God has revealed. We have already discussed it and that it abrogates the option. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a broad claim, for the conditions for abrogation are four: Among them is knowing the date by obtaining the earlier and later verses. This is unknown from these two verses, so it is forbidden to claim that one of them abrogates the other, and the matter remains as it is. I said: We have mentioned from Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas that this verse was revealed late, so it is abrogating unless it is estimated in the speech, And judge between them by what God has revealed, if you wish, because the mention of the choice for him has preceded, so the choice was deleted from the last speech because the first indicates it, because it is conjoined to it, because it is conjoined to it, so the ruling of the choice is like the ruling of the conjoined to it, so they are partners, and the latter is not disconnected from what preceded it, because there is no meaning to that and it is not correct, so his saying, And judge between them by what God has revealed, must be conjoined to what preceded it from his saying, And if you judge, judge between them with justice (al-Ma`idah: 42) and from his saying, But if they come to you, judge between them or turn away from them (al-Ma`idah: 42). So the meaning of And judge between them by what God has revealed is judge by that if you judge and choose the ruling, so it is all decisive and not abrogated, because the abrogator is not connected to the abrogated conjoined to it, so the choice for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in that is decisive and not abrogated. He said: Makki, may God have mercy on him, said: And judge is in the accusative case, in apposition to the Book, meaning: And We have revealed to you that you judge between them by what God has revealed, meaning by the judgment of God that He revealed to you in His Book. And beware of them lest they tempt you. “And beware of them lest they tempt you.” And beware of them lest they tempt you. “That” is a substitute for the ha’ and the mim in and beware of them, and it is a substitute for inclusion or an object for the sake of it, meaning in order that they tempt you. And on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Abbas said: A group of rabbis, including Ibn Suriya, Ka’b ibn Asad, Ibn Saluba, and Shas ibn Qays, gathered and said: Let us go to Muhammad, perhaps we can tempt him away from his religion, for he is only a human being. So they came and said: You know, O Muhammad, that we are rabbis of the Jews, and if we follow you, no one from the Jews will oppose us. There is a dispute between us and some people, so we will bring them to you for judgment, so decide for us against them until we believe in you. But the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, refused, and this verse was revealed. The origin of the word fitnah is testing, as mentioned above, then its meaning differs. God Almighty’s statement here they tempt you means they turn you away and reject you. Fitnah can mean polytheism, and from this is His statement: And fitnah is greater than killing (al-Baqarah 2:217) and His statement: And fight them until there is no more fitnah (al-Baqarah 2:193). Fitnah can mean a lesson, as in His statement: Do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve (al-Mumtahanah 6:5) and Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people (Yunus 10:85). Fitnah can mean turning away from… The way as in this verse and the repetition of and judge between them by what God has revealed is for emphasis or they are conditions and rulings of his command to judge in each one by what God has revealed and in the verse is evidence of the permissibility of forgetfulness on the part of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he said: lest they tempt you and that only happens out of forgetfulness and not intentionally and it was said: the address is to him and what is meant is someone else, and this will be explained in Al-An’am, God willing. The meaning of about some of what God has revealed to you is about everything that God has revealed to you and some is used to mean all. The poet said: Or some souls are fooling around It is narrated or related that he wanted all the souls and upon it they carried the saying of God Almighty: And that I may make clear to you some of that over which you differ (al-Zukhruf 43:63). Ibn Al-Arabi said: The correct thing is that some is as it is in this verse and that what is meant by it is stoning or the ruling that they wanted and did not intend to tempt him from all and God knows best. God Almighty says: But if they turn away meaning if they reject your judgment and turn away from it. Then know that God only intends to afflict them with some of their sins meaning to punish them with exile, tribute, and killing. And that is how it was. He only said: with some because punishing them with some was sufficient to destroy them. And indeed, many of the people are wicked meaning the Jews.
5:50: It has three issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: Do they then seek the judgment of [the time of] ignorance? “Do they then seek the judgment of [the time of] ignorance?” The meaning is that the people of ignorance used to make the judgment of the noble different from the judgment of the lowly, as was mentioned previously in a place. The Jews used to implement the punishments on the weak and poor, but they did not implement them on the strong and rich, so they lost the ignorance in this action. The second - Sufyan bin Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Tawus who said: When they were asked about a man who prefers some of his children over others, he would recite this verse: Do they then seek the judgment of the days of ignorance? Tawus would say: No one has the right to prefer some of his children over others. If he does so, it will not be implemented and will be annulled. The people of the apparent meaning said the same. It was narrated on the authority of Ahmad bin Hanbal something similar, but Al-Thawri, Ibn Al-Mubarak and Ishaq disliked it. If someone does that, it will be implemented and will not be returned. Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Layth, Al-Shafi’i and the people of opinion permitted it. They used as evidence the action of Abu Bakr in giving birth to Aisha without the rest of his children, and they confirmed it to him, peace be upon him: Return it. And his saying, Then have someone else bear witness to this. The first ones used as evidence “the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him, to Bashir: He said: Do you have a son other than this one? He said: Yes. He said: All of them, and you gave him something like this. He said: No. He said: Then do not make me a witness, for I do not bear witness to injustice. In another narration: “And I do not bear witness except to the truth.” They said: Whatever is permissible and not right is invalid and not permissible. His saying: I bear witness to this other than myself is not permission to bear witness, but rather it is a warning against it, because the Prophet, peace be upon him, called it injustice and refrained from bearing witness to it, so it is not possible for any of the Muslims to bear witness to that in any way. As for the action of Abu Bakr, it does not contradict the statement of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and perhaps he gave his sons gifts equivalent to that. If it is said: The basic principle is that a person disposes of his money in an absolute manner, it is said to him: The general principle and the specific incident that contradicts that principle do not contradict each other, like the general and the specific. In the principles, it is correct to base the general on the specific. Then, from that arises disobedience, which is the greatest of major sins, and that is forbidden. And whatever leads to what is forbidden is forbidden. Therefore, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fear God and be just between your children.” Al-Nu’man said: So my father returned and gave back that charity, and the father does not squeeze charity by spending it. His saying: Then return it is understood to mean Return it. And returning is apparent in the annulment, as he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected, i.e. it is rejected and annulled. All of this is clearly and strongly evident and a clear preference for prohibition. Third: Ibn Waththab and Al-Nakha’i read Afhakam in the nominative case, meaning they seek it, so he deleted the ha as Abu Al-Najm deleted it in his saying: Umm Al-Khayar has come to accuse me of a sin I did not commit. Among those who narrated it all with the nominative case, it is possible that the estimation is that the ruling of the Age of Ignorance is a ruling that they seek, so the described was deleted. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Al-A'raj, and Al-A'mash read it with the accusative of the ha' and the kaf and the fathah of the meem, and it returns to the meaning of the reading of the group, meaning the ruling itself, and what is meant is the ruling, so it is as if he said: So they ruled the ruling of the Jahiliyyah, they seek. The ruling and the judge may be one and the same in the language, and it is as if they mean the soothsayer and the like of the rulers of the Jahiliyyah, so what is meant by the ruling is the commonality and the type, since it does not mean a specific ruler. It is permissible for the added word to be a type, as is permissible in their saying: Egypt prevented its ardab and the like. Ibn 'Amir read it with the ta', and the rest with the ya'. And the Almighty’s saying: And who is better than God in judgment for a people who are certain? This is a question of denial, meaning: No one. This is the subject and predicate, and judgment is in the accusative case for clarification, because of His saying: for a people who are certain, meaning with a people who are certain.
5:51: There are two issues: The first - The Jews and the Christians are allies are the objects of the verb take and this indicates the severing of allegiance according to the Sharia. This was explained in Al Imran. Then it was said: What is meant by it are the hypocrites. The meaning is: O you who believed outwardly and were allies of the polytheists and told them the secrets of the Muslims. It was said: It was revealed about Abu Lubabah on the authority of Ikrimah. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed in the story of the Day of Uhud when the Muslims feared, even a group of them, that they would be allies of the Jews and Christians. It was said: It was revealed about Ubadah ibn al-Samit and Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. Ubadah, may God be pleased with him, disavowed allegiance to the Jews and Ibn Ubayy held fast to it and said: I fear that the tables will turn. Some of them are allies of others is a subject and its predicate and it indicates that the Sharia established allegiance among them until the Jews and Christians inherit from each other. The second - the Almighty’s saying: And whoever among you takes them as allies meaning, supports them against the Muslims, then he is one of them. The Almighty has made clear that his ruling is like their ruling, and he prevents the Muslim from being able to prove the inheritance from the apostate, and whoever took them as allies was the one who refused. Then this ruling will remain until the Day of Resurrection in severing allegiance. The Almighty has said: And do not incline toward those who do wrong, lest the Fire touch you (Hud 11:113). The Almighty has said in Al Imran 3:Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers (Al Imran 3:28). The Almighty has said: Do not take as intimates those other than yourselves (Al Imran 3:118). It has been said that the meaning of some of them are allies of others is in support. And whoever among you takes them as allies, then he is one of them is a condition and its answer is because he has disobeyed God Almighty and His Messenger as they have disobeyed, and his enmity is obligatory as their enmity is obligatory, and the Fire is obligatory for him as it is obligatory for them, so he has become one of them, meaning one of their companions.
5:52: The Almighty said: Then you will see those in whose hearts is disease doubt and hypocrisy, and this was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah, and what is meant is Ibn Abi and his companions hasten to them meaning in their friendship and assistance saying we fear that a calamity will strike us meaning time will turn against me, either with drought so they will not rule over us or that the Jews will gain victory over the Muslims so the matter will not last for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This statement is more similar in meaning as if it is from the verb to turn, meaning we fear that the matter will turn, and this is indicated by the Almighty's statement: Perhaps God will bring about victory and the poet said: The fate that is destined for you and the circles of time turn Meaning the states of time that go from one people to another: And there is disagreement about the meaning of conquest. It was said: Conquest is the decision and judgment, according to Qatada and others. Ibn Abbas said: God brought the conquest, so his fighters killed Banu Qurayzah, their children were taken captive, and Banu Nadir were exiled. Abu Ali said: It is the conquest of the lands of the polytheists over the Muslims. Al-Suddi said: He means by conquest the conquest of Mecca. Or a command from Him. Al-Suddi said: It is the jizya. Al-Hasan: His revealing the matter of the hypocrites and informing of their names and the command to kill them. It was said: Fertility and abundance for the Muslims. So they become, over what they kept secret within themselves, regretful.
