That is, they become regretful for their allegiance to the infidel when they see God’s victory for the believers, and when they witness death, they are given the good report of the punishment.
5:53: The Almighty said: And those who believe say The people of Medina and the people of Ash-Sham read: He says without a waw and Amr ibn Abi Ishaq read: And he says with a waw and the accusative in apposition to that it comes according to most grammarians, so the estimate is: So perhaps God will bring the conquest and that he says: It was said: It is an apposition to the meaning because the meaning of So perhaps God will bring the conquest is and perhaps God will bring the conquest since it is not permissible to say: Perhaps Zaid will come and Amr will stand because the meaning is not correct if you say: And perhaps Zaid will say that Amr will stand, but if you say: Perhaps Zaid will stand and Amr will come, it would be good. So if you estimate the presentation in that it comes next to maybe, it is good because the estimate becomes: Perhaps he will come and perhaps he will stand and it is from the category of his saying: I saw your husband in the battlefield, carrying a sword and a spear. And there is a third statement in it - which is that you give it to him on the conquest, as the poet said: To wear an abaya and please my eyes It is permissible to make the name of God Almighty come instead, so the meaning becomes: Perhaps God will come and those who believe will say. The Kufians read and those who believe will say in the nominative case, in order to separate from the first. Are these referring to the hypocrites? They swore by God they swore and strove in faith as a form of rebuke: Are these the ones who swore by God with their utmost oaths that they would help you against Muhammad? It is possible that it is from the believers, some of them to each other, meaning these who swore that they were believers, so God has torn their veil today. Their deeds have been in vain they have become invalid because of their hypocrisy. So they have become losers meaning losers of reward. It was said: they lost in their friendship with the Jews, so they did not obtain any fruit after killing the Jews and expelling them.
5:54: It has four issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: Whoever among you turns back from his religion is a condition and its answer is soon. The reading of the people of Medina and Ash-Sham is whoever turns back with the two dals, the rest of them are whoever turns back. This is from the miracles of the Qur’an and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, since he informed about their apostasy, and it was not during his time, and it was hidden, so it was as he informed after a period of time. The people of apostasy were after his death, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Ishaq said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away, the Arabs apostatized except for three mosques, the mosque of Medina, the mosque of Mecca, and the mosque of Ju’atha. They were in their apostasy in two groups: a group that rejected the entire Sharia and went out of it, and a group that rejected the obligation of zakat and recognized the obligation of other things. They said, We will fast and pray, but we will not pay zakat. So Abu Bakr fought all of them and sent Khalid bin Al-Walid to them with armies, so he fought them and took them captive, according to what is well-known from their stories. The second - the Almighty’s saying: Then God will bring a people whom He will love and who will love Him in the place of description. Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq and his companions. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed about the Ansar. It was said: It is a reference to a people who were not present at that time and that Abu Bakr fought the apostates with a people who were not present at the time of the revelation of the verse, and they were tribes from Yemen from Kinda, Bajila and Ashja. It was said: It was revealed about the Ash’aris, so in the report it is said that when it was revealed, the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came after that and most of the conquests of Iraq were in the time of Umar, may God be pleased with him, at the hands of the tribes of Yemen. This is the most correct of what was said about its revelation, and God knows best. Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah narrated in Al-Mustadrak with his chain of transmission that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, pointed to Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari when this verse was revealed and said: They are a people. Al-Qushayri said: The followers of Abu al-Hasan are from his people, because in every place where a people are attributed to a prophet, the followers are meant. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Humble toward the believers. Humble is an attribute of a people, and likewise mighty means they are compassionate toward the believers and show them mercy and are gentle with them, as they say: a docile animal, meaning it obeys easily. There is nothing of humiliation in it. They are harsh toward the disbelievers and are hostile toward them. Ibn Abbas said: They are toward the believers as a father is toward his son and a master is toward a slave, and they are harsh toward the disbelievers as a wild animal toward its prey. God Almighty said: Harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves. (al-Fath 48:29) It is permissible to say humble in the accusative case as a state, meaning He loves them and they love Him in this state. The meaning of God Almighty’s love for His servants and their love for Him has already been mentioned. Fourth - The Almighty’s statement: They strive in the cause of God is also in the place of an attribute. And they do not fear the blame of a blamer. Unlike the hypocrites who fear the consequences. This indicates the confirmation of the Imamate of Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali, may God be pleased with them, because they strived in the cause of God, the Almighty, during the life of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and fought the apostates after him. It is known that whoever has these attributes is a friend of God, the Almighty. It was said: The verse is general and includes everyone who strives against the infidels until the Day of Judgment, and God knows best. That is the bounty of God which He bestows upon whom He wills. is a subject and predicate. And God is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing. That is, He is All-Encompassing in bounty and All-Knowing of the interests of His creation.
5:55: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Your guardian is only God and His Messenger. Jabir bin Abdullah said: Abdullah bin Salam said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Our people from Qurayzah and Nadir have deserted us and swore not to sit with us, and we cannot sit with your companions because of the distance between our homes. So this verse was revealed. He said: We are pleased with God and His Messenger and the believers as allies. And those are general for all believers. Abu Ja`far Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Husayn bin Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them, was asked about the meaning of Your ally is only God and His Messenger and those who believe. Is it Ali bin Abi Talib? He said: Ali is from the believers. He goes to the extent that this is for all believers. An-Nahhas said: This is a clear statement because those are for a group. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. He said in another narration: It was revealed about Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Mujahid and As-Suddi said: What led them to do that was the statement of God the Almighty: Those who establish prayer and give zakat, while they bow. The second issue - that. A beggar asked in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one gave him anything. Ali ibn al-Salat was bowing and had a ring on his right hand, so he pointed to the beggar with his hand until he took it. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: This indicates that a small action does not invalidate the prayer, because giving a ring in charity while bowing is an action that was done in the prayer and the prayer is not invalidated by it. His statement, And they give zakat while they are bowing, indicates that voluntary charity is called zakat, because Ali gave his ring in charity while bowing, and it is similar to the statement of God, the Most High, And whatever you give in zakat, desiring the countenance of God - those will receive a multiply [in reward] (al-Rum 30:39). The obligatory and voluntary acts were organized, and the name zakat became for the obligatory and voluntary acts, like the name charity and the name prayer, organizing the two matters. I said: What is meant by zakat in this case is giving a ring in charity, and the word zakat is taken to mean giving a ring in charity after that because zakat does not come except with its specific wording, which is the obligatory zakat, as was explained previously in the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. Also, before that, they establish prayer, and the meaning of establishing prayer is that they perform it at its times with all its rights, and what is meant is the obligatory prayer. Then he said: And they are bowing, meaning the voluntary prayer. It was said: He mentioned bowing alone as an honor. It was said: The believers at the time of the revelation of the verse were between those who completed the prayer and those who were bowing. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: The Almighty’s statement: And they give zakat while they are bowing includes the permissibility of a small act in prayer, because this was brought out as a form of praise, and the least that can be done in the context of praise is that it is permissible. It was narrated that Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, gave something to the beggar while he was praying, and it may be permissible that this is a voluntary prayer, because it is disliked in the obligatory prayer. It is possible that the praise is directed at the combination of two states, as if he described someone who believes in the obligation of prayer and zakat, so he expressed prayer as bowing. And regarding belief in the obligation of action, as you say: Muslims are the ones who pray, and you do not mean that they are praying in that state, and praise is not directed during prayer, but rather it means the one who does this action and believes in it.
5:56: The Almighty said: And whoever takes God and His Messenger and those who believe as allies meaning, he entrusts his affair to God and complies with the command of His Messenger and the believers, then indeed, the party of God will be the victorious. Al-Hasan said: The party of God is the soldiers of God, and another said: The supporters of God. The poet said: How can I shine while Bilal is my party member? Any Nasri and the believers are the party of God, so it is no wonder that they defeated the Jews by captivity, killing, expulsion, and imposing the jizya. The party is a group of people, and its origin is from the word deputy from their saying: Hezbollah so-and-so meaning he attacked him, so it is as if the party-goers are gathered like the people of the deputy gather around her, and the party of a man is his companions, and the party is the rose, and from it is the hadith: So whoever misses his portion of the night The Qur’an has been divided into groups, and the party is the sect, and they gathered together, and the parties are the groups that gather to fight the prophets, and his party is a matter, meaning it has befallen him.
5:57: There are two issues: First - It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that a group of Jews and polytheists laughed at the Muslims during their prostration, so God Almighty revealed: O you who believe! Take not those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement to the end of the verses. The meaning of mockery was presented in al-Baqarah 2:Of those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers as allies. Abu Amr and Al-Kisa’i read it in the accusative case, meaning of the disbelievers. Al-Saka’i said: In the letter of Abu, may God have mercy on him, of the disbelievers and of here is to clarify the type, and the accusative is clearer and more evident. An-Nahhas said. It was said: It is conjoined with the closest factor to it, which is His statement: of those who were given the Scripture. So God forbade them from challenging the Jews and polytheists as allies, and informed them that the two groups took the religion of the believers in ridicule and amusement. of is accusative in conjunction with those the first in His statement: Do not take those who have taken your religion in ridicule and amusement among those who were given the Scripture before you and the disbelievers meaning do not take these and those as allies. So the one described as mocking and playing in these readings is the Jews and no one else, and the one forbidden from Taking the Jews and the polytheists as allies, and both of them in the reading with the accusative are described as mockery and play. Makki said: And if the group had not agreed on the accusative, I would have chosen the accusative because of its strength in grammar, meaning, interpretation, and proximity to the conjoined word. And it was said: The meaning is do not take the polytheists and the hypocrites as allies, as evidenced by their saying: We were only mocking (al-Baqarah 2:14). And all the polytheists are disbelievers, but the word disbelievers is often used to refer to the polytheists, and for this reason the mention of the People of the Book was separated from the disbelievers. Second: Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: This verse is like the Almighty’s saying: “Do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are allies of one another” (al-Ma’idah 5:51) and Do not take as intimates those other than yourselves (Al Imran 3:118), which includes the prohibition of supporting and aiding the polytheists and the like. “Jaber narrated: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to go out to Uhud, some Jews came to him and said: We will go with you. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We do not seek help from the polytheists in our affairs. This is the correct view of the Shafi’i school of thought. Abu Hanifa permitted Muslims to use them to defeat the polytheists, and the Book of God Almighty indicates the opposite of what they said, along with what came in the Sunnah regarding this matter, and God knows best.
5:58: It contains twelve issues: First: Al-Kalbi said: When the muezzin called to prayer and the Muslims stood up for prayer, the Jews would say: They have stood up, they have not stood up. They would laugh when the Muslims bowed and prostrated and would say about the call to prayer: You have innovated something that we have not heard of among the nations before. How did you get a cry like the cry of a donkey? What an ugly sound and what a loathsome matter! It was said: When the muezzin called to prayer, they would laugh among themselves and wink at each other in a foolish and frivolous manner, making people ignorant of its people and repelling people from it and from the one calling to it. It was said: They saw the one calling to it as someone who plays and mocks its actions, out of ignorance of its status. So this verse was revealed and the words of God, the Most High, were revealed: And who is better in speech than one who invites to God and does righteousness? (Fussilat 41:33). The call is the supplication by raising the voice and it may include the supplication and the roaring, and he called him by calling and calling, meaning he shouted with him. And they called each other, meaning they called each other, and they called each other, meaning they sat in the club, and the one sitting in the club called him, and the call to prayer is not mentioned in the Book of God Almighty except in this verse. As for it being mentioned on Friday specifically. Second - The scholars said: The call to prayer was not made in Mecca before the migration, but rather they used to call for congregational prayer. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated and the qiblah was turned toward the Kaaba, he ordered the call to prayer, and congregational prayer remained because the matter was being discussed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was concerned about the call to prayer until he saw Abdullah bin Zaid, Omar bin Al-Khattab, and Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard the call to prayer on the night of the Isra’ in the sky. As for the vision of Abdullah bin Zaid Al-Khazraji Al-Ansari and Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with them, it is well-known and that Abdullah bin Zaid informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that at night and knocked on it, and that Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: When morning comes, I will inform the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Bilal to call the people to prayer today. Bilal added in the morning prayer: Prayer is better than sleep, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, approved of it. It is not what Al-Ansari saw. Ibn Saad mentioned it on the authority of Ibn Umar. Al-Daraqutni, may God have mercy on him, mentioned that Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, saw the call to prayer and that he informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Bilal to make the call to prayer before Al-Ansari informed him. He mentioned it in his book Al-Mudabbaj in the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq and the hadith of Abu Bakr on his authority. Third - The scholars differed about the obligation of the call to prayer and the call to prayer. As for Malik and his companions, the call to prayer, according to them, is only obligatory in mosques for groups where people gather. Malik stated this in his Muwatta. The later scholars among his companions differed on two opinions: The first - a confirmed Sunnah obligatory on the community in the city and the villages that are similar to Egypt. Some of them said: It is an obligation on the community. The companions of Al-Shafi’i differed likewise. Al-Tabari narrated from Malik that he said: If the people of Egypt intentionally omit the call to prayer, they must repeat the prayer. Abu Omar said: I do not know of any difference of opinion about the obligation of the call to prayer as a whole on the people of the city, because the call to prayer is the indicative sign that distinguishes between the abode of Islam and the abode of disbelief. “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a military expedition, he would say to them: If you hear the call to prayer, then stop and refrain, and if you do not hear the call to prayer, then cover up - or he said - and launch a raid. And in Sahih Muslim he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to raid when dawn broke. If he heard the call to prayer, he would stop, otherwise he would raid.” The hadith. Ata’, Mujahid, Al-Awza’i and Dawud said: The call to prayer is obligatory, and they did not say it is sufficient. Al-Tabari said: The call to prayer is a Sunnah and not obligatory. It was reported from Ashhab from Malik that if a traveler intentionally omits the call to prayer, he must repeat the prayer. The Kufians disliked that a traveler prays without the call to prayer or the call to prayer. They said: As for the resident of a city, it is recommended for him to call to prayer and the call to prayer. If he finds the call to prayer and the call to prayer sufficient, that is sufficient for him. Al-Thawri said: The call to prayer suffices for the call to prayer while traveling, and if you wish, you may call to prayer and the call to prayer. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: The traveler calls to prayer according to the hadith of Malik ibn Al-Huwayrith. Dawud said: The call to prayer is obligatory for every traveler in his private life, and the call to prayer is due to the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Malik ibn Al-Huwayrith and his companion: If you are traveling, then call the adhan and the iqama, and let the eldest of you lead you in prayer. Narrated by Al-Bukhari, and it is the opinion of the scholars of the Zahir. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: It is proven that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Malik bin Al-Huwayrith and to his cousin: If you are traveling, then call the adhan and the iqama, and let the eldest of you lead you in prayer.” Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The adhan and the iqama are obligatory for every group, whether resident or traveling, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded the adhan and commanded it to be obligatory. Abu Omar said: Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifah and their companions, Al-Thawri, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr and Al-Tabari agreed that if a traveler omits the adhan intentionally or forgetfully, his prayer is valid. Likewise, if he omits the iqama, according to them, they are more averse to omitting the iqama. Al-Shafi’i argued that the adhan is not obligatory and is not an obligation of the obligatory prayers by the fact that the adhan is dropped for one person when combining prayers at Arafat and Muzdalifah. The conclusion of Malik’s view regarding the adhan while traveling is the same as that of Al-Shafi’i. Fourth - Malik, Al-Shafi’i and their companions agreed that the call to prayer is repeated twice and the call to prayer is repeated once, except that Al-Shafi’i repeats the first takbir four times. This is preserved from the narrations of trustworthy people in: Hadith of Abu Mahdhura and in the hadith of Abdullah bin Zaid he said: It is an addition that must be accepted. Al-Shafi’i claimed that the call to prayer of the people of Mecca remained in the family of Abu Mahdhurah until his time and era. His companions said: And this is how it is now with them. And what Malik went to is also found in the authentic hadiths in the call to prayer of Abu Mahdhurah and in the call to prayer of Abdullah bin Zaid. And the practice among them in Medina is that in the family of Sa’d al-Qurazi until their time. Malik and al-Shafi’i agreed on the tarji’ in the call to prayer, and that is the return of the believer when he says: I bear witness that there is no god but God twice, I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God twice, he returns and extends his voice as much as he can. And there is no disagreement between Malik and al-Shafi’i regarding the iqama except his saying: The prayer has begun, for Malik says it once and al-Shafi’i says it twice, and most of the scholars agree with what al-Shafi’i said, and the reports came with it. Abu Hanifa and his companions, al-Thawri and al-Hasan bin Hayy said: The call to prayer and the iqama are both two by two, and the takbir according to them at the beginning of the call to prayer and the beginning of the iqama is Allahu Akbar four times, and they do not tarji’ in the call to prayer, and their proof for that is the hadith of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila who said: The companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us that Abdullah bin Zaid came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, I saw in a dream as if a man stood wearing two green cloaks on the trunk of a wall, and he stood in pairs, and he stood in pairs, and he sat in pairs, and he stood in pairs, and he stood in pairs. Bilal heard that, so he stood and called the adhan in pairs, and he sat in pairs, and he stood in pairs. It was narrated by Al-A’mash and others on the authority of Amr bin Murrah on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, and it is the opinion of a group of the followers and jurists in Iraq. Abu Ishaq Al-Sabi’i said: The companions of Ali and Abdullah used to make the adhan and the iqamah interchangeable. This is the adhan of the Kufians, and it has been inherited from them from generation to generation, just as the Hijazis inherit it. Their adhan is a quadrupling of the takbir like the Meccans, then the testimony that there is no god but God once, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God once, then the hasten to prayer once, then the hasten to success once, then the muezzin returns and prolongs his voice, saying: I bear witness that there is no god but God - the entire adhan - twice, twice, to the end. Abu Omar said: Ahmad bin Hanbal, Ishaq bin Rahawayh, Dawud bin Ali, and Muhammad bin Jarir al-Tabari permitted saying everything that was narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they interpreted it as permissibility and choice. They said: All of that is permissible because all of that has been proven from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions acted upon it. So whoever wants to say: God is Great twice at the beginning of the call to prayer, and whoever wants to say it four times, and whoever wants to go back to his call to prayer, and whoever wants not to go back, and whoever wants to repeat the call to prayer, and whoever wants to separate it except for his saying: The prayer has begun, because that is twice, twice in every case. Fifth - They differed regarding the second call to prayer for the dawn prayer - which is the muezzin saying: Prayer is better than sleep. Malik, Ath-Thawri and Al-Layth said: The muezzin says in the dawn prayer - after saying: Come to success twice - Prayer is better than sleep twice. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i in Iraq. He said in Egypt: He does not say that. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: He says it after finishing the call to prayer, if he wishes. It has been narrated from them that it is in the call to prayer itself, and people do that in the dawn prayer. Abu Omar said: “It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the hadith of Abu Mahdhurah: He ordered him to say in the dawn call to prayer: “Prayer is better than sleep.” It was also narrated from him, and that is from the hadith of Abdullah bin Zaid. It was narrated from Anas that he said: It is Sunnah to say in Fajr: Prayer is better than sleep. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he used to say this. As for Malik’s statement in Al-Muwatta’ that he was informed that the muezzin came to Umar ibn Al-Khattab to call him to the Fajr prayer and found him asleep, so he said: Prayer is better than sleep. So Umar ordered him to include it in the Fajr call, I do not know that this was narrated on the authority of Umar from a source that can be used as evidence and whose authenticity is known. Rather, it contains the hadith of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of a man called Ismail, so recognize it. Ibn Abi Shaybah mentioned it. Abduh ibn Sulayman told us on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of a man called Ismail, who said: The muezzin came to call Umar to the Fajr prayer and said: Prayer is better than sleep. Umar was impressed by him and said to the muezzin: Confirm it in your call to prayer. Abu Umar said: The meaning of it, in my opinion, is that he said to him: The Fajr call is the place to say it, not here. It is as if he disliked that there should be another call from him at the door of the emir as the emirs did after him. Umar said: What led me to this interpretation, even though the apparent meaning of the report is the opposite, is because the repetition in the Fajr prayer is more famous among the scholars and the common people than to be thought. Omar, may God be pleased with him, was ignorant of something about the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he ordered his muezzins in Medina, Bilal, and in Mecca, Abu Mahdhura, so it is preserved and well-known in the call to prayer of Bilal, and the call to prayer of Abu Mahdhura in the dawn prayer of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is well-known among scholars. Waki’ narrated on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Imran bin Muslim on the authority of Suwaid bin Ghafla that he sent to his muezzin, “When you reach ‘Come to prosperity,’ say: ‘Prayer is better than sleep,’ for it is the call to prayer of Bilal.” It is known that Bilal never called to prayer for Omar, nor did he hear him after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except once in Syria when he entered it. Sixth - The scholars agreed that it is part of the Sunnah not to call the prayer until after its time has begun, except for Fajr, for the call to prayer is made before dawn, according to Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr. Their proof is the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Bilal calls the adhan at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum calls the adhan. Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The adhan for the dawn prayer should not be given until its time has begun, “based on the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Malik ibn al-Huwayrith and his companion: When the time for prayer comes, give the adhan, then make the iqama, and let the eldest of you lead you in prayer.” And by analogy with all other prayers, a group of the people of hadith said: If the mosque has two muezzins, one of them should give the adhan before dawn and the other after dawn. Seventh - They differed regarding the muezzin calling the adhan and the iqamah being performed at his place. Malik, Abu Hanifa, and their companions held that there is nothing wrong with that, based on the hadith of Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Zayd on the authority of his father. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him when he saw the call to prayer in his sleep to deliver it to Bilal. Bilal called the adhan and then ordered Abdullah bin Zaid to perform the iqamah.” Al-Thawri, Al-Layth, and Al-Shafi’i said: Whoever calls the adhan is performing the iqamah, based on the hadith of Abd al-Rahman bin Ziyad bin An’am on the authority of Ziyad bin Na’im, on the authority of Ziyad bin Al-Harith Al-Sada’i, who said: I came to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), and when it was early morning, he ordered me to call the adhan, then he stood up for prayer, and Bilal came to call the iqamah, so the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: The brother of Sada has called the adhan, and whoever calls the adhan is the one who calls the iqamah. Abu Omar said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad is the African, and most of them consider him weak, and no one else narrates this hadith, and the first has a better chain of transmission, God willing. Even if the hadith of the African is authentic, then some scholars consider it trustworthy and praise it, so saying it is more appropriate because it is a text in a matter of disagreement, and it comes after the story of Abd God ibn Zayd with Bilal, and the other, so the other from the command of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) is more appropriate to follow. Despite this, I recommend that if there is only one regular muezzin, he should take charge of the iqamah, and if someone else calls it, then the prayer is valid by consensus, and praise be to God. Eighth - The ruling on the muezzin is that he should be slow in his call to prayer and not be merry in it as many of the ignorant do today. Rather, many people and the common people have taken it beyond the limit of being merry, so they repeat it in repetitions and make many interruptions in it so that what he is saying is not understood, nor what he is saying. Al-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a muezzin who was mesmerizing. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The call to prayer is easy and pleasant. So if your call to prayer is easy and pleasant, otherwise do not call to prayer. And in his call to prayer, he faces the qiblah according to a group of scholars, and turns his head right and left in Come to prayer and Come to success according to many scholars. Ahmad said: He should not turn unless he is in a minaret wanting the people to hear him. And Ishaq said the same. And it is better for him to be in a state of purity. Ninth - It is recommended for the listener of the call to prayer to repeat it until the end of the two testimonies of faith, and if he completes it, it is permissible, according to the hadith of Abu Saeed. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘When the muezzin says God is Great, God is Great, and one of you says God is Great, then he says I bear witness that there is no god but God.’ He says I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. He says I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Then he says Come to prayer. He says There is no power and no strength except with God. Then he says Come to success. He says There is no power and no word except with God. Then he says God is Great, God is Great. He says God is Great, God is Great. Then he says There is no god but God, whoever has his heart will enter Paradise.’” And in it, on the authority of Saad ibn Abi Waqqas, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Whoever says when he hears the call to prayer, “I bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner or associate, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. I am pleased with God and Muhammad as Messenger and with Islam as religion,” his previous sins will be forgiven. Tenth - As for the merit of the call to prayer and the muezzin, there are also authentic narrations about it, including what Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the call to prayer is made, Satan turns away and farts so that he does not hear the call to prayer. The hadith is sufficient for you, as it is a symbol of Islam and a sign of faith, as mentioned above. As for the call to prayer, Muslim narrated, “On the authority of Muawiyah, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The muezzins will have the longest necks on the Day of Resurrection. This is a reference to safety from the terror of that day, and God knows best. The Arabs use the term “long neck” to refer to the nobles and leaders of the people, as one of them said. Throughout the necks and shoulders In Al-Muwatta’, “On the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khurdi, he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: No jinn, human, or anything else hears the voice of the muezzin but that it will testify for him on the Day of Resurrection.” And in Sunan Ibn Majah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever calls to prayer, hoping for reward, for seven years, he will be granted freedom from Hellfire. “And in it” on the authority of Ibn Omar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever calls to prayer for twelve years, Paradise will be guaranteed for him, and he will be credited with sixty good deeds for each call to prayer, and with thirty good deeds for each call to prayer.” Abu Hatim said: This chain of transmission is rejected, but the hadith is authentic. On the authority of Uthman ibn Abi al-Aas, he said: The last thing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded me to do was: Do not appoint a muezzin who takes a fee for his call to prayer. This is an authentic hadith. Eleventh - They differed about taking payment for the call to prayer. Al-Qasim bin Abd al-Rahman and the people of opinion disliked it, while Malik permitted it and said: There is nothing wrong with it. Al-Awza’i said: That is disliked, but there is nothing wrong with taking a living for that from the public treasury. Al-Shafi’i said: The caller to prayer is not provided for except from the fifth of the fifth, the share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It is not permissible to take a living for the call to prayer. Our scholars have provided evidence for taking a living from the hadith of Abu Mahdhurah, and there is a view on it. It was narrated by al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah and others. He said: “I went out with a group of people and we were on some of the way when the muezzin of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) called for prayer in front of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). We heard the muezzin’s voice while we were turning away from him, so we shouted, mocking him. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) heard it and sent some people to us. They made us sit in front of him and said: ‘Which of you heard your voice rise?’ He pointed to all the people and they believed me. So he sent all of them and detained me and said to me: ‘Get up and call to prayer.’ So I got up and there was nothing more hateful to me than the command of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) or what he commanded me to do. So I got up in front of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) gave me the call to prayer himself and said: ‘Say: God is Great, God is Great, God is Great. God is Great. I bear witness that there is no god but God. I bear witness that there is no god but God. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God.’ Then he said: ‘Raise your voice and raise your voice. I bear witness that there is no god but God. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Come to prayer. Come to success. Come to success. God is Great, God is Great. There is no god but God.’ Then he called me when he was I finished the call to prayer and he gave me a purse containing some silver. Then he placed his hand on the forehead of Abu Mahdhurah, then passed it over his face, then over his breasts, then over his liver until the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached the navel of Abu Mahdhurah. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God bless you and bless you. I said: O Messenger of God, command me to call to prayer in Mecca. He said: I have commanded you. So everything that I had hated for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went away and all of that became love for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I went to Atab bin Asid, the agent of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca, and I called to prayer with him on the command of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The wording of Ibn Majah. Twelfth - The Almighty said: “That is because they are a people who do not reason.” That is, they are like someone who has no reason to prevent him from doing evil. It was narrated that a Christian man who was in Medina, when he heard the muezzin say: I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, said: Burn the liar. Then a spark of fire fell into his house while he was sleeping and stuck to the house and burned him with the house, burning him and burning that infidel with him. So it was a lesson for mankind, and the calamity is entrusted to reason. They used to wait with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they asked for help, and they did not delay after that. Ibn al-Arabi mentioned this.
5:59: God Almighty said: Say, ‘O People of the Scripture, do you blame us?’ Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: A group of Jews - among them Abu Yasir ibn Akhtab and Rafi’ ibn Abi Rafi’ - came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about the messengers he believed in. He said: By God and what was revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham and Ishmael until His saying: And we are Muslims to Him. When Jesus, peace be upon him, was mentioned, they denied his prophethood and said: By God, we do not know of people of a religion less fortunate in this world and the hereafter than you, nor a religion worse than your religion. So this verse and the one after it were revealed, and it is connected to what preceded it of their denial of the call to prayer. It is a comprehensive testimony to God’s oneness and to Muhammad’s prophethood. The contradictory thing is the religion of one who divides between God’s prophets, not the religion of one who believes in all of them. It is permissible to assimilate the lam into the ta’ because of its proximity to it. And you criticize means you are angry. It was said: you hate. It was said: you disapprove. The meaning is close. It is said: he criticizes from such-and-such, and he criticizes, and he criticizes, and the first is more, less. Abdullah ibn Qays al-Ruqayyat: They did not resent the Umayyads except that they were patient when they got angry. And in the revelation: And they did not resent them (al-Buruj 85:8). It is said: I resented the man with the kasra, so I am a resentful person if I reproached him. It is said: I did not resent him for kindness. Al-Kisa’i said: I resented with the kasra is a language, and I resented the matter also, and I resented it if I hated it, and God took revenge on him, meaning the consequence, and the noun is from the resentment, and the plural is resentments, and resentment is a word, words, and words, and if you wish, you can make the qaf quiescent and transfer its vowel to the nun and say: resentment, plural naqam, like ni’mah and na’am. Except that we believe in God is in the accusative case with tanqimun and tanqimun meaning you criticize, meaning do you resent us for anything but our belief in God and you know that we are on the truth? And that most of you are wicked meaning in your abandonment of faith and your departure from obeying God’s command, so it was said that it is like the saying of the one who says: Do you resent me for anything but that I am chaste and that you are wicked? And it was said: meaning because most of you are wicked, you resent us for that.
5:60: The Almighty said: "Say: Shall I inform you of something worse than that?" That is, something worse than your vengeance upon us. It was also said: Something worse than what you want for us of the evil. This is the answer to their saying: We do not know of a religion worse than your religion. "Mathwabah" is in the accusative case for clarification. Its original form is maf'ulah, so the vowel of the waw was placed on the tha', so the waw was quiescent and after it was a quiescent waw, so one of them was deleted for that reason. Similar to it are maqūl, mujāzah, and mudafah with the meaning of a source. The poet said: And when my neighbor invited me to a guest house, I would roll up my sleeves until my apron reached half of my shin. It was said: It is a passive participle like your saying: Mukrama and Ma’qala “whoever God has cursed” whoever is in the nominative case as He said: He who curses you is the Fire (al-Hajj 22:72) and the meaning is: He cursed whomever God has cursed. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case meaning: Say: Shall I inform you of someone worse than whom God has cursed? It is permissible for it to be in the genitive case as a substitute for evil and the meaning is: Shall I inform you of someone whom God has cursed? What is meant is the Jews. The statement about the Taghut has already been made, meaning: And He made from among them those who worshipped the Taghut. The relative pronoun is omitted according to Al-Farra’. The Basrans said: It is not permissible to omit the relative pronoun, and the meaning is: whoever God has cursed and worshipped the Taghut Ibn Waththab and Al-Nakha’i read Anbikum with a light pronunciation, and Hamza read Abd Al-Taghut with a damma on the ba’ and a kasra on the ta’, making it a noun on the pattern of fa’l like ‘udhd, so it is a construction for exaggeration and abundance like yaqz, nadas, and hazar, and its origin is the adjective, and from it the saying of Al-Nabigha: From a beast and a jar, his legs are folded, his fate is like the sword of a polisher With the damma of the letter Ra. And he made it an accusative with the verb ja’ala meaning he made them a slave to the tyrant, and he added abd to the tyrant, so he lowered it, and made it with the meaning of created, and the meaning is: and he made from them those who exaggerate in the worship of the tyrant. The rest read it with the opening of the ba and the ta and made it a past tense verb and conjoined it with a past tense verb, which is waghada and la’ana, and the meaning according to them is whoever God curses and whoever worships the tyrant, or it is accusative with the verb ja’ala, meaning he made from them monkeys and pigs and wabd al-tyrant, and he made the pronoun in abd singular based on the word min without its meaning. Abi and Ibn Mas’ud read wa ‘abdaw al-tyrant on the meaning, Ibn Abbas: And the slave of the tyrant, so it is permissible for it to be the plural of abd, as he said: rahn and rahn, and saqf and saqf, and it is permissible for it to be the plural of ibd, as it is said: mithl and mithl, and it is permissible for it to be the plural of abd, as it is said: bazl and bazl, and the meaning is: and he served the tyrant. And from Ibn Abbas also, wabd al-tyrant made it the plural of abd, as it is said: shahed and shahd, and ghayb and ghayb, and from Abu Waqid: And the slaves of the tyrant for exaggeration are also the plural of abd, as in ‘amel. And workers, and striker and striker. Mahboob mentioned that the Basrans read: And the worshippers of the tyrant is the plural of worshipper also like standing and standing. It is possible that it is the plural of slave. Abu Jaafar al-Ru’asi read: And slave of the tyrant is among them. Awn al-Uqayli and Ibn Buraidah read: And slave of the tyrant is singular, and it is performed on the authority of a group. Ibn Mas’ud also read: And slave of the tyrant, and on his authority also, and Abi and slave of the tyrant are feminine as the group as God Almighty said: The Bedouins said (al-Hujurat 49:14). Ubayd ibn Umair read: And slaves of the tyrant are like dog and dogs. So these are twelve aspects. God the Almighty said: Those are in the worst place because their place is the Fire, but as for the believers, there is no evil in their place. Al-Zajjaj said: Those are in the worst place according to what you say. Al-Nahhas said: And among the best things that have been said about it: Those whom God has cursed are in the worst place in the Hereafter than your place in this world because of the evil that has befallen you. And it was said: Those whom God has cursed are in the worst place than those who resented you. And it was said: Those who resented you are in the worst place than those whom God has cursed. And when this verse was revealed, the Muslims said to them: Brothers of the apes and pigs, so they lowered their heads in disgrace. And the poet says about them: May God curse the Jews, for the Jews are brothers of monkeys.
5:61: The Almighty says: And when they come to you, they say, 'We believe.' This verse describes the hypocrites, and the meaning is that they did not benefit from anything they heard, rather they entered as disbelievers and left as disbelievers. And God knows best what they were concealing, that is, their hypocrisy. It was said that what is meant are the Jews who said: Believe in what was revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day when you enter the city, and disbelieve at the end of it when you return to your homes. This is indicated by what precedes it from mentioning them and what follows.
5:62: God Almighty says: And you will see many of them meaning the Jews hastening into sin and aggression meaning racing in sins and injustice “and their consuming of usury. Evil is what they do.”
5:63: The Almighty said: Why do not the rabbis and the scholars forbid them? And Why do not means Why do not the rabbis forbid them? The scholars of the Christians and the rabbis and the scholars of the Jews, said Al-Hasan. It was said: All of them are about the Jews because these verses are about them. Then He rebuked their scholars for abandoning their prohibition, saying: How evil is that which they used to do. Just as He rebuked those who hasten to sin, saying: How evil is that which they used to do. The verse indicated that the one who abandons the prohibition of evil is like the one who commits evil. So the verse is a rebuke to the scholars for abandoning the command to do good and the prohibition of evil. This meaning has already been discussed in Al-Baqarah and Al-Imran. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated: Sufyan ibn Sa`id told me on the authority of Mis`ar, who said: It reached me that a king ordered that a water skin be swallowed up, so he said: O Lord, in it is so-and-so the worshipper. So God Almighty revealed to him: Begin with him, and his face did not frown for an hour. And in Sahih Al-Tirmidhi: If people see the oppressor and do not stop him, God will soon punish them all. And it will come. The word manufacture means work, except that it requires quality. It is said: a sword of good manufacture if its work is good.
5:64: The Almighty said: And the Jews say, 'The hand of God is chained.' Ikrimah said: This was said by Finkhas bin Azar, may God curse him, and his companions, who had wealth. When they disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, their wealth decreased. They said, 'God is stingy, and the hand of God is withheld from us in giving.' So the verse is specific to some of them. It was said: When some people said this and the rest did not deny it, it became as if they all said this. Al-Hasan said: The meaning is, 'The hand of God is withheld from punishing us.' It was said: When they saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in poverty and lack of wealth, and heard, Who is he that would loan God a goodly loan? (al-Baqarah 2:245), and they saw that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sought their help in blood money, they said, 'The God of Muhammad is poor.' And perhaps they said, 'Stingy.' This is the meaning of their saying, 'The hand of God is chained.' It is an example like His saying, 'And do not make your hand chained to your neck.' (Al-Isra': 29) And the miser is called Ja'd. Fingers, clenched fist, pinched fingers, and hand tied. The poet said: Khorasan was a land where Yazid lived and every door of goodness was open. Then his fingers were replaced with curly hair, as if his face had been sprinkled with vinegar. The hand in the speech of the Arabs refers to the limb, as in the saying of God Almighty: And take in your hand a bunch (Surah Sad: 44). This is impossible for God Almighty. It refers to a blessing, as the Arabs say: How many blessings do I have with so-and-so? meaning, How many blessings have I bestowed upon him? It refers to strength, as God Almighty said: And remember Our servant David, the possessor of strength (Surah Sad: 17). It refers to kingship and power, as God Almighty said: “Say: ‘Indeed, bounty is in the hand of God. He gives it to whom He wills.’” (Al Imran 3:73). It also refers to a connection, as God Almighty said: From what our hands have made, livestock (Surah Ya Sin: 71). Meaning, from what we have done. He said: Or will He in whose hand is the marriage contract forgive? (Surah Al Baqarah: 237). Meaning, the one who has the marriage contract. It also refers to support and victory, as in the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: The hand of God is with the judge until he judges and the divider, until he divides. And adding the action to the one being reported is an honor and a tribute to him. God Almighty said: O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? (Surah Sad: 75). It is not permissible to carry it on the limb because the Creator, glory be to Him, is One and it is not permissible to make a distinction for Him, nor on the strength, kingdom, blessing, and connection, because the partnership then occurs between His friend Adam and his promise to Iblis, and what was mentioned about His preference over him is invalidated because the meaning of specialization is invalidated. So there remains nothing but to carry it on two attributes related to the creation of Adam as an honor for him without the creation of Iblis, the ability being related to the possible, not by way of directness or by way of contact. And similar to it is what was narrated that His name is exalted and His glory is exalted, that He wrote the Torah with His hand and planted the house of honor with His hand for the people of Paradise, and other than that the attribute is related to its requirement. The Almighty said: Their hands are chained and they are cursed for what they said. The damma was omitted from the ya’ because of its heaviness, meaning they are chained in the Hereafter. It is possible that it is a supplication against them, and likewise and they are cursed for what they said. The purpose is to teach us, as He said: You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, God willing. (al-Fath 48:27) He taught us the exception, as he taught us the supplication against Abu Lahab with His saying: May the hands of Abu Lahab perish. (al-Masad 111:1) It was said: What is meant is that they are the most miserly of creation, for you will not find a Jew who is not mean. In the discussion of this statement, the waw is implied, meaning they said: The hand of God is chained and their hands are chained. Cursing means exclusion, and this has been mentioned previously. The Almighty’s saying: Rather, His hands are spread out is a subject and a predicate, meaning, rather, His blessings are spread out. So, the hand means the blessing. Some of them said that this is a mistake because he said: Rather, His hands are spread out. So, the blessings of God Almighty are more than can be counted, so how can it be, rather, His two blessings are spread out? And the answer is that it is possible for this to be a dual of a type, not a dual of a single singular, so it would be like his saying, peace be upon him: The hypocrite is like a stray sheep among two flocks. “One of the two genders is the blessing of this world and the other is the blessing of the Hereafter. It has been said that the two blessings of this world are the apparent blessing and the hidden blessing, as He said: “And He has bestowed upon you His blessings, apparent and hidden.” (Luqman 31:20) Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about him: The apparent blessing is what is good in your creation, and the hidden blessing is what He conceals from you of your evil deeds. It was said that His two blessings are rain and vegetation, which are the blessings from them and from them. It was said that the blessing is for exaggeration, like the Arabs’ saying: At your service and at your pleasure, and he does not mean to limit it to two times. And the speaker may say: I have no hand in this matter, meaning strength. Al-Suddi said: The meaning of his saying: His hands are two strengths, with reward and punishment, is contrary to what the Jews said: His hand is closed from punishing them. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: God Almighty said to me, Spend on you, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The right hand of God is full, and neither the abundance of night nor day diminishes it. Have you seen what He has spent since He created the heavens and the earth? Indeed, what is in His right hand has not diminished - he said - and His Throne is over the water, and in His other hand is the grasping, raising and lowering. Sufficiency means abundant pouring, and Yaghidh means decreasing. Similar to this hadith is the saying of the Most High: And God withholds and expands (al-Baqarah 2:245). As for this verse, in the reading of Ibn Mas`ud, rather, His hands are two, as Al-Akhfash narrated, and he said: It is said: The hand of His expansion is that it is extending and spreading. He spends as He wills meaning He provides as He wants. It is possible that the hand in this verse means power, meaning His power is comprehensive, so if He wills, He expands, and if He wills, He withholds. And many of them is an oath lam, What has been revealed to you from your Lord meaning in what was revealed to you in transgression and disbelief meaning if something of the Qur’an is revealed and they disbelieve, their disbelief increases. And We cast among them Mujahid said: meaning between the Jews and Christians because He said before this: Do not take the Jews and Christians as allies. It was said: meaning We cast among the sects of the Jews as He said: You think they are all together, but their hearts are diverse (al-Hashr 59:14), so they hate each other and do not agree, so they are the most hated of God’s creation to al-Nas 114:Whenever they kindle a fire for war means the Jews, and whenever is an adverb, meaning whenever they gather and prepare, God disperses their gathering. It was said: When the Jews corrupted and disobeyed the Book of God - the Torah - God sent Nebuchadnezzar upon them, then they corrupted, so He sent Peter the Roman upon them, then they corrupted, so He sent the Magians upon them, then they corrupted, so God sent the Muslims upon them, so whenever their affairs were set straight, God dispersed them, so whenever they kindled a fire, meaning they stirred up evil and gathered their affairs to fight the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, God extinguished it, and He humbled them and weakened their affairs, so the mention of fire is a metaphor. Qatada said: God Almighty humiliated them, for He sent the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while they were under the hands of the Magians, then He Almighty said: And they strive to cause corruption in the land, meaning they strive to invalidate Islam, that is one of the greatest corruptions, and God knows best. It was said: What is meant by fire here is the fire of anger, meaning that whenever they kindled the fire of anger in themselves and gathered their bodies and the strength of their souls with the raging fire of anger, God extinguished it until they became weak, and that was because of what He made of terror a victory in the presence of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
5:65: The Almighty says: And if the People of the Scripture had believed “had been truthful” and feared God meaning polytheism and sins We would have removed from them “Lam” is the answer to if and we covered has been mentioned previously.
5:66: And the establishment of the Torah and the Gospel, acting in accordance with them and not distorting them. This meaning has been presented in full in Surat Al-Baqarah. And what was sent down to them from their Lord meaning the Qur’an. It was said: the books of their prophets. They would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet. Ibn Abbas and others said: meaning rain and plants. This indicates that they were in a state of drought. It was said: the meaning is that We would have expanded their provisions for them and they would have eaten continuously. Above and below were mentioned to emphasize what is opened up to them in this world. Similar to this verse is: “And whoever fears God - He will make for him a way out. And He will provide for him from where he does not expect.” (al-Talaq 65:302) And if they had remained steadfast on the way, We would have given them abundant water. (al-Jinn 72:16) And if only the people of the cities had believed and feared God, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth. (al-A’raf 7:96) So God made the firm one of the causes of provision as in these verses and promised more for whoever is grateful, saying: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you. (Ibrahim 14:7) Then he informed that among them were those who were moderate, and they were the believers, such as the Negus, Salman, and Abdullah bin Salam - they were moderate, so they did not say about Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, except what was appropriate for them. It was said: He meant by moderation a people who did not believe, but they were not among the mocking callers to prayer, and God knows best. Moderation is moderation in action, and it comes from the word intended, and intended means doing something. You say: I intended it, “I intended it,” and I intended it, meaning: Evil is what they do, meaning evil is what they did. They denied the messengers, distorted the Book, and consumed ill-gotten gains.
5:67: There are two issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. It was said: Its meaning is to make the announcement clear because at the beginning of Islam he used to hide it for fear of the polytheists, then he was ordered to make it clear in this verse and God informed him that He would protect him from the people. Umar, may God be pleased with him, was the first to make his Islam clear and he said: We do not worship God secretly. And in that regard the verse was revealed: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers. (al-Anfal 8:64) So the verse indicates the rejection of the statement of those who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealed something from the matter of religion out of fear and its invalidity, and they are the Rafidis. And it indicates that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, went as far as something from the matter of religion because the meaning is to convey all that was revealed to you openly, and if it were not for this, there would be no benefit in the Almighty’s saying: And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. It was said: Convey what was revealed to you from your Lord regarding the matter of Zainab bint Jahsh al-Asadiyyah, may God be pleased with her. Other than this was said, but the correct view is the general one. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is to convey all that was revealed to you from your Lord, for if you conceal something from it, then you have not conveyed His message. This is a lesson for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a lesson for the bearers of knowledge from his nation not to conceal anything from the matter of His law. God Almighty knew from the matter of His Prophet that he would not conceal anything from His revelation, and in Sahih Muslim from Masruq from Aisha that she said: Whoever told you that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealed some of the revelation has lied, and God Almighty says: “O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message.” And God cursed the Rafidis when they said that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, concealed something of what God revealed to him that the people needed. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And God will protect you from the people is evidence of his prophethood because God Almighty informed us that he is infallible and He, glory be to Him, guaranteed him infallibility. It is not permissible that he left something that God commanded him to do, and the reason for the revelation of this verse. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting under a tree when a Bedouin came and drew his sword and said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Who will protect you from me? He said: God. The Bedouin’s hand was terrified and the sword fell from his hand and he hit the tree with his head until his brain was scattered.” Al-Mahdawi mentioned it and Qadi Iyad mentioned it in the book Al-Shifa’. He said: This story has been narrated in Sahih and that Ghawrath ibn Al-Harith is the one who told the story and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forgave him, so he returned to his people and said: I have come to you from the best of people. We have already discussed this meaning in this surah when he said: When a people were about to stretch out their hands against you (al-Ma’idah 5:11) and also in An-Nisa’ in the mention of the fear prayer and in Sahih Muslim “On the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said: We went on a raid with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before Najd. We caught up with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a valley with many jujube trees. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dismounted under a tree and hung his sword on one of its branches. The people dispersed in the valley, seeking shade from the trees. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man came to me while I was sleeping and took the sword. I woke up and he was standing over my head. I did not notice anything until the sword was drawn in his hand. He said to me: Who can protect you from me? I said: God. Then he said a second time: Who can protect you from me? I said: God. He said: The sword was spread out and here he is sitting. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not turn away. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God sent me His message, I was fed up with it and I knew that some people would lie to me, so God revealed this verse: Abu Talib used to send men from Banu Hashim with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, every day to guard him until the verse “And God will protect you from the people” was revealed. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O uncle, God has protected me from the jinn and mankind, so I do not need anyone to guard me. I said: This requires that this was in Mecca and that the verse is Meccan, but that is not the case. It was previously mentioned that this surah is Medinan by consensus. What indicates that this verse is Medinan is what Muslim narrated in Sahih “On the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed up late at the entrance to Medina one night and said: “If only a righteous man from my companions would guard me tonight.” She said: “While we were like that, they heard the rattling of weapons. He said: ‘Who is this?’ He said: ‘Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘What brought you here?’ He said: ‘I felt fear for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I came to guard him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for him and then slept.” In a hadith other than the Sahih, she said: “While we were like that, I heard the rattling of weapons. He said: ‘Who is this?’ They said: ‘Sa`d and Hudhayfah, we came to guard you.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slept until I heard him snore. Then this verse was revealed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stuck his head out towards a red cloth and said: ‘Go away, O people, for God has protected me.’” The people of Medina read: His messages in the plural, and Abu Amr and the people of Kufa read: His message in the singular. An-Nahhas said: Both readings are good, and the plural is clearer because the revelation was sent down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, little by little, then he would explain it. The singular indicates abundance, so it is like a source, and the source in most speech is not pluralized or dualized because it indicates its type by its wording, like His statement: And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them (Ibrahim 14:34) Indeed, God does not guide the disbelieving people meaning He does not direct them, and it has been mentioned before. It has been said: You convey, but as for guidance, it is up to us, similar to The Messenger has no duty except to convey (al-Ma’idah 5:99), and God knows best.
5:68: It has three issues: First - Ibn Abbas said: A group of Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Do you not acknowledge that the Torah is the truth from God? He said: Yes. They said: We believe in it and do not believe in anything other than it. Then the verse was revealed: “You have no religion until you act according to what is in the two books of belief in Muhammad, peace be upon him, and act according to what is required by them.” Abu Ali said: It is possible that this was an abrogation of them. The second - the Almighty’s saying: And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. That is, they will disbelieve in it and increase in disbelief upon their disbelief. Transgression is exceeding the limit in injustice and exaggerating in it. This is because injustice is sometimes minor and sometimes major. So whoever exceeds the level of a minor sin has transgressed. From this is the Almighty’s saying: No indeed, man transgresses. (al-Alaq 96:6), meaning he exceeds the limit in deviating from the truth. Third - God Almighty says: So do not grieve over the disbelieving people. That is, do not grieve over them with grief. He says: His eyes welled up with grief. This is a consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and not a prohibition against sadness because he is not able to bear it, but it is a consolation and a prohibition against being exposed to sadness. This meaning has already been discussed in detail at the end of Al Imran.
5:69: The discussion of all of this has been presented, so there is no point in repeating it. And those who are Jews is conjoined, and so is and the Sabians conjoined to the implied in the Jews according to the statement of Al-Kisa’i and Al-Akhfash. Al-Nahhas said: I heard Al-Zajjaj say: And the statement of Al-Akhfash and Al-Kisa’i was mentioned to him: This is a mistake from two aspects, one of them is that the implied nominative makes it ugly to conjoin it to confirm it, and the other aspect is that the conjoined is a partner to the conjoined to it, so the meaning becomes that the Sabians entered Judaism, and this is impossible. Al-Farra’ said: The raising of and the Sabians is only permissible because in is weak, so it only affects the noun and not the predicate, and those here does not have a clear i’rab, so both matters proceeded in one direction, so the raising of the Sabians is permissible, returning to the original statement. Al-Zajjaj said: The path of what is clear in i’rab and what is not clear in i’rab is one. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: The raising is based on precedence and delay, and the estimate is: Indeed, those who believe and those who are Jews - whoever believes in God and the Last Day and does righteousness - there is no fear concerning them nor… They grieve, and so do the Sabians and Christians. Sibawayh recited, and it is similar to it: Otherwise, know that you and I are rebels as long as we remain in discord. Dhabi Al-Barjami said: Whoever spends the evening in the city, then I and Qiyar are strangers there It was said: In means yes, so the Sabians is the beginning, and the predicate was deleted because the second indicates its defect, so the conjunction is in this estimation after the completion of the speech and the end of the noun and predicate. Qais al-Ruqayyat said: The firstborn of the blamers in my youth would blame me and I would blame him They say, Grey hair has covered you, and you have grown old. I said, It is... Al-Akhfash said that it means yes, and this ha was inserted for silence.
5:70: The Almighty’s saying: We took a covenant from the Children of Israel and sent to them messengers. The meaning of the covenant, which is that they should not worship except God, and what is connected to it, has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. The meaning in this verse is: Do not grieve over the disbelieving people, for We have already excused them, and We sent messengers, but they broke the covenants. All of this goes back to what the surah began with, which is His saying: Fulfill your contracts. “Whenever there came to them” meaning the Jews a messenger with what their souls did not desire, “that did not agree with their desires,” a group they denied, and a group they killed, meaning they denied a group and killed a group. Those whom they denied were Jesus and those like him from the prophets, and they killed Zachariah, John, and other prophets. He only said: they kill to take into account the beginning of the verse. It was said: He meant a group they denied, a group they killed, and a group they lied and killed. This is their habit and custom, so it was abbreviated. It was said: a group they lied and did not kill them, and a group they killed them, so they lied. They kill is an attribute of a group. God knows best.
5:71: The Almighty said: And they thought that there would be no trial The meaning is that those who were taken the covenant thought that there would be no trial or test from God Almighty with hardships, deceived by their saying: We are the sons of God and His beloved, but they were deceived by the length of the respite. Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read it in the nominative case, and the rest read it in the accusative case. The nominative case is based on the fact that Hasab knew and was certain, and An is lightened from the heavy one, and the entry of La is a substitute for the light one, and the pronoun was deleted because they disliked that the verb should follow it, and it is not in its ruling that it should enter it, so they separated between them with La, and whoever places the accusative case made An the forelock of the verb, and Hasab remained in its category of doubt and other things. Sibawayh said: Hasabt ala yaqool dalikah, meaning I thought that he said that, and if you wish, you can place the accusative case. Al-Nahhas said: The nominative case according to grammarians in Hasab and its sisters is better, as he said: Except that I claimed today that I have grown old and that no one like me will witness amusement. The raising is better because Hasab and its sisters are like a noun because it is something fixed. God the Almighty said: So they became blind meaning from guidance and deaf meaning from hearing the truth, because they did not benefit from what they saw or heard Then God accepted their repentance in the speech there is an implication, meaning the trial befell them and they repented, so God accepted their repentance by removing the famine or by sending Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, informing them that God would accept their repentance if they believed. This is an explanation of God accepted their repentance meaning He would accept their repentance if they believed and were truthful, not that they truly repented Then many of them became blind and deaf meaning many of them became blind and deaf after the truth was made clear to them through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so many was raised as a substitute for the waw. Al-Akhfash Saeed said: Just as you say I saw two-thirds of your people, and if you wish it is an implied subject, meaning the blind and deaf are many of them, and if you wish it is an estimate that the blind and deaf are many of them. The fourth answer is that it is according to the language of the one who said the fleas ate me, and according to this is the saying of the poet: But his father and mother are in Hauran, squeezing his relatives From this meaning is His statement: And those who did wrong conferred secretly (al-Anbiya 21:3). It is often permissible in other than the Qur’an to use the accusative as an adjective for a deleted source.
5:72: God Almighty says: They have certainly disbelieved who say, ‘God is the Messiah, the son of Mary.’ This is the statement of the Jacobites. So God responded to this knowledge with a conclusive argument from what they acknowledge, saying: And the Messiah said, ‘O Children of Israel, worship God, my Lord and your Lord.’ That is, if the Messiah says, O Lord and O God, how does he call upon himself or how does he ask of Him? This is impossible. Who associates partners with God? It was said: This is from the statement of Jesus. It was also said: The beginning of a statement from God Almighty, and association is to believe in a creator with Him. The derivation of the Messiah has already been discussed in Al Imran, so there is no point in repeating it. And the wrongdoers will have no helpers.
5:73: The Almighty said: They have certainly disbelieved who say, 'God is the third of three' meaning one of three and the tanween is not permissible in it, according to Al-Zajjaj and others. The Arabs have another doctrine in it, saying: the fourth of three. Based on this, the accusative and genitive are permissible, because its meaning is that which made the three four by being from them. Likewise, if you say: the third of two, the tanween is permissible. This is the saying of the Christian sects of the Royalists, Nestorians, and Jacobites, because they say, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are one God, and they do not say three gods, which is the meaning of their doctrine. Rather, they refrain from using the expression, which is necessary for them. And what was like this is correct to narrate with the necessary expression, and that is because they say: the Son is a god, the Father is a god, and the Holy Spirit is a god. The statement about this has been presented in An-Nisa’, so God disbelieved them for saying this and said: And there is no god except one God meaning that the god is not multiple, and they are obligated to say three gods as was presented, even if they did not explicitly state that verbally. The meaning of one has been mentioned in Al-Baqarah, and min is redundant, and it is permissible in other than the Qur’an to say one god as an exception. Al-Kisa’i permitted the genitive as a substitute. God Almighty says: And if they do not desist meaning, do not stop saying that there is a trinity, a painful punishment will befall them in this world and the hereafter.
5:74: Will they not repent? is a statement and a rebuke, meaning let them repent to Him and ask Him to cover their sins, and what is meant is the unbelievers among them. The unbelievers were specifically mentioned because they are the ones who say that, not the believers.
5:75: The Almighty said: The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a messenger; messengers have passed away before him. This is a beginning and a predicate, meaning that the Messiah, even if the signs appeared through his hands, only brought them as the messengers brought them. If he is a god, then let every messenger be a god. This is a refutation of their statement and an argument against them.
