Then he went to great lengths in his argument and said: And his mother was a woman of truth. This is an beginning and a predicate. They used to eat food. This means that he was a child who was nurtured, and whoever was born of women and ate food was a created being like all created beings. None of them denied this. So when is it appropriate for a lord to be a lord? And their statement: He used to eat with his humanity, not his divinity, this is a case of them becoming mixed, and it is inconceivable for a god to mix with someone other than a god. If it were permissible for the eternal to mix with the created, then it would be permissible for the eternal to become created. If this were true for Jesus, then it would be true for others, so it would be said: Divinity is mixed with every created thing. Some of the commentators said about his statement: They used to eat food that it is a metaphor for feces and urine. This indicates that they were both human beings. Those who said that Mary, peace be upon her, was not a prophetess used as evidence the words of God Almighty: And his mother was a truthful woman. I said: There is a consideration in this, because it is possible that she was a friend while being a prophet like Idris, peace be upon him. There has already been evidence of this in Al Imran, and God knows best. She was only called a friend because of her frequent belief in the signs of her Lord and her belief in what her son told her about Al Hassan and others, and God knows best. The Almighty says: See how We make clear to them the signs meaning the evidence. Then see how they are turned away meaning how they are turned away from the truth after this explanation. It is said: afkahu ya’fukahu if he turned him away. This is a refutation of the Qadarites and the Mu’tazilites.
5:76: The Almighty said: "Say: Do you worship besides God that which has no power to harm or benefit you?" This is to further clarify and establish an argument against them, meaning that you acknowledge that Jesus was a baby in his mother's womb, and had no power to harm or benefit anyone. And since you acknowledge that Jesus was in a state of being neither hearing nor seeing nor knowing, neither benefiting nor harming, how did you take him as a god? And God is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing. Meaning that He has always been All-Hearing, All-Knowing, and has the power to harm and benefit, and whoever has this description is truly a god, and God knows best.
5:77: The Almighty said: "Say, O People of the Scripture, do not go to extremes in your religion beyond the truth." That is, do not go to extremes as the Jews and Christians went to extremes regarding Jesus. The Jews went to extremes when they said about Jesus, "He is not the son of his right mind. The Christians went to extremes when they said, He is a god." Going to extremes is going beyond the limit, and its explanation was presented in An-Nisa. God Almighty says: And do not follow the inclinations of a people. Inclinations is the plural of hawa, and it was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah. Inclination is called hawa because it causes its owner to fall into the Fire. They went astray before. Mujahid and Al-Hasan said: meaning the Jews. And misled many. That is, they misled many people. And went astray from the right path. That is, from the straight path of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The repetition of went astray means that they went astray before and went astray after. What is meant are the ancestors who established misguidance and practiced it, from the leaders of the Jews and Christians.
5:78: The Almighty’s saying: Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary. There is one issue in this: the permissibility of cursing the disbelievers even if they are from the children of the prophets, and that the honor of lineage does not prevent the issuance of a curse on them. The meaning of by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary is that they were cursed in the Psalms and the Gospel, for the Psalms are the tongue of David and the Gospel is the tongue of Jesus, meaning that God cursed them in the two books. Their derivation has been mentioned previously. Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said: He cursed them by transforming them into apes and pigs. Abu Malik said: Those who were cursed by the tongue of David were transformed into apes, and those who were cursed by the tongue of Jesus were transformed into pigs. Ibn Abbas said: Those who were cursed by the tongue of David were the people of the Sabbath, and those who were cursed by the tongue of Jesus were those who disbelieved in the table after it was revealed. Something similar was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: He cursed the ancestors and descendants of those who disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, by the tongue of David and Jesus because they knew that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a prophet sent, so He cursed those who… He disbelieves in it. The Almighty says: That is because they disobeyed. That is in the nominative case as a subject, meaning that is the curse because they disobeyed, meaning because of their disobedience. It is also possible that it is in the accusative case, meaning that we did that to them because of their disobedience and aggression.
5:79: The Almighty’s saying: They did not forbid each other from the evil they were doing. There are two issues in this. First: The Almighty’s saying: They did not forbid one another meaning they did not forbid one another: How evil was what they were doing is a censure for their abandonment of prohibition. Likewise, whoever worships them is censured for doing what they did. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first thing that came to be deficient among the Children of Israel was a man or what a man would encounter and he would say, “O man, fear God and leave what you are doing, for it is not lawful for you.” Then he would encounter him the next day and that would not prevent him from being his food, drink, and seat. So when they did that, God struck the hearts of some of them against others and then said: “Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressors.” to His saying, wicked. Then he said: “No, by God, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and you must seize the hand of the oppressor and force him to do what is right and force him to do what is right, or God will strike the hearts of some of you against others and curse you as He cursed them.” Al-Tirmidhi also included it. The meaning of to force him is to return him. The second - Ibn Atiyah said: The consensus is that forbidding evil is obligatory for whoever is able to do so and is safe from harm to himself and to the Muslims. If he fears, then he should forbid evil in his heart and abandon the evildoer and not associate with him. The most skilled scholars of knowledge said: It is not a condition of the one forbidding that he be free from sin, rather the sinners should forbid each other. Some of the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence said: It is obligatory for those who share cups to forbid each other. They used this verse as evidence. They said: Because His statement: They did not forbid each other from the evil they did implies their participation in the action and their condemnation for not forbidding. The verse is evidence of the prohibition of sitting with criminals and an order to leave them and forsake them. He emphasized this with His statement in denouncing the Jews: You see many of them befriending those who disbelieved. What is in His statement they did not may be in the accusative case and what follows it is an attribute of it, the estimate being what a bad thing they were doing or it may be in the nominative case and it means that which.
5:80: The Almighty said: You will see many of them meaning of the Jews. It was said: Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf and his companions. Mujahid said: He means the hypocrites. Befriending those who disbelieve meaning the polytheists and are not of their religion. Evil is that which their souls have put forward for them meaning they have made it seem good and attractive. It was said: The meaning is evil is that which they have put forward for themselves and their afterlife. That the wrath of God is upon them "that" is in the nominative case with an implied subject, like you say: "What a bad man Zayd is." It was said: It is a substitute for "what in His statement evil" so that it is what we dislike, so it is also in the nominative case. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case meaning because the wrath of God is upon them: "And in the punishment they will abide eternally" subject and predicate.
5:81: The Almighty’s saying: And if they had believed in God and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. This indicates that whoever takes a disbeliever as an ally is not a believer if he believes in his beliefs and is satisfied with his actions. But many of them are wicked, meaning they have departed from faith in their Prophet due to their distortion, or from faith in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, due to their hypocrisy.
5:82: The Almighty said: You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews. The lam is a lam of oath, and the nun was introduced, according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh, to differentiate between the present and the future. Enmity is accusative for clarification, and so is You will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, 'We are Christians.' This verse was revealed about the Negus and his companions when the Muslims came to them in the first migration, according to what is well-known in the biography of Ibn Ishaq and others, fearing the polytheists and their temptations, and they were numerous. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina after that, but they were not able to reach him. War came between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the Battle of Badr took place, and God killed the leaders of the infidels in it, the infidels of Quraysh said: Your revenge is in the land of Abyssinia, so go to the Negus and send two men from your people of opinion, perhaps he will give you from him, so you can kill them for those of you who were killed at Badr. So the infidels of Quraysh sent Amr ibn al-'As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabia brought gifts, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard about that. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri and wrote with him to the Negus. He went to the Negus and read the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he called Ja`far ibn Abi Talib and the emigrants and sent for the monks and priests and gathered them together. Then he ordered Ja`far to recite the Qur’an to them. He recited Surat Maryam and they stood up with tears in their eyes. They are the ones about whom God revealed: And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, ‘We are Christians.’ Then he recited to the two witnesses. Narrated by Abu Dawud. He said: Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Muradi told us. He said: Ibn Wahb told us. He said: Yunus told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, and on the authority of Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab and on the authority of Awrah ibn al-Zubayr that the first emigration was the emigration of the Muslims to the land of Abyssinia. The thief of the hadith is Batula. Al-Bayhaqi mentioned on the authority of Ibn Ishaq that he said: Twenty men from the Christians came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Mecca or close to that, when report of him from Abyssinia spread, and they found him in the mosque, so they spoke to him and asked him, and men from Quraysh were in their clubs around the Kaaba. When they finished asking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about what they wanted, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to God Almighty and recited the Qur’an to them. When they heard him, their eyes overflowed with tears, then they responded to him and believed in him and confirmed him and recognized from him what was described to them in their book about his affair. When they got up from him, Abu Jahl intercepted them with a group of Quraysh and said: May God disappoint you, from the group that sent you from behind you from the people of your religion, to search for them and bring them report of the man, but your sitting with him did not become apparent until you left your religion and believed him in what he said to you. We do not know of a group more foolish than you, or something like what he said to them. They said: Peace be upon you, we do not ignore you. We have our deeds and you have your deeds. We do not spare ourselves any good. It is said: The Christian group from Najran. It is said that these verses were revealed about them: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it until His saying: We do not seek the ignorant (al-Qasas 28:52-55). It is also said: “Ja’far and his companions came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with seventy men wearing woolen garments, among them sixty-two from Abyssinia and eight from the people of Ash-Sham, and they were Bahira the monk, Idris, Ashraf, Abraha, Thamama, Qatham, Duraid and Ayman. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to them Surat Yasin until the end, and they wept when they heard the Qur’an and believed.” They said: How similar this is to what was revealed to Jesus. So it was revealed about them: “You will surely find the most intense of the people in animosity toward the believers to be the Jews and those who associate others with God. And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers to be those who say, ‘We are Christians.’” That is, the delegation of the Negus, and they were the owners of the monasteries. Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab said: God also revealed about them: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it until His saying: Those will be given their reward twice until the end of the verse. Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: They were forty men from the people of Najran from Banu al-Harith ibn Ka’b, thirty-two from Abyssinia, and sixty-eight from the people of Ash-Sham. Qatada said: It was revealed about people from The People of the Book were on a law of truth that Jesus did not bring. So when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they believed in him, so God praised them. The Almighty said: That is because among them are priests and monks. The singular of priests is qass and qasis, as Qatrub said. The priest is the scholar, and its origin is from qass, which means to follow something and seek it out. The rajaz poet said: They accompany the priests, heedless of the harm. Their voices were divided at night, I heard them gossiping and the priest is also a leader of the leaders of the Christians in religion and knowledge, and its plural is qusus, and likewise qasīs like evil and evil, so the priests are those who follow the scholars and worshippers, and it is said in the plural of qasīs broken: qasāsa, one of the sins was replaced with a waw, and qasāsa also like maḥalaba, and the original is qasāsa, so they replaced one of the sins with a waw because of its abundance, and the word qasīs is either Arabic or it is in the language of the Romans, but the Arabs mixed it with their speech so it became from their language, since there is nothing in the book that is not from the language of the Arabs, as mentioned above. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: My father told us, Nasr ibn Dawud told us, Abu Ubaid told us, he said: I was told by Muawiyah ibn Hisham ibn Nasir al-Ta’i, on the authority of al-Salt, on the authority of Hamiyah ibn Ri’ab, he said: I said to Salman, Among them are priests and monks. He said: Leave the priests in the monasteries and the prayer niches. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught me that among them are truthful ones and monks. And Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: The Christians neglected the Gospel and introduced into it what was not from it. There were four men who changed it: Luqas, Marqus, Yahannes, and Maqbus. The priest remained on the truth and on the straight path. So whoever is on his religion and his guidance is a priest. God Almighty says: And monks. Monks are the plural of monk, like riders and rider. Al-Nabigha said: If it were offered to a disheveled monk, a worshipper of God, a devout believer Rana saw her and spoke well of her, and his uncle saw her as a right choice, even if he did not find guidance. The verb from it is rahaba God yarhabhu, meaning he feared Him with fear, terror, and awe. Monasticism and monasticism are worship in a monastery. Abu Ubaid said: Monasticism may be for the singular and the plural. Al-Farra’ said: Monasticism is pluralized if the singular has rahbanah and rahbain like qurban and qurban. Jarir said about the plural: The monks of Medina, if they saw you, would descend and protect themselves from the passion of the incapable minds. Al-Fader: the old ibex, and it is said: the great one, and the same is true of Al-Fadur, and the plural is Fadr and Fadur, and its place is Al-Maqdara, said Al-Jawhari, and another said in Al-Tawhid: If you saw the monks of a monastery on the mountain, the monks would run down and reach And from prayer and awe on the weight of the cloud is a bone in the chest that protrudes over the abdomen like, and this praise is for those of them who believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, not for those who persisted in their disbelief, and for this reason he said and that they are not arrogant meaning about submitting to the truth.
5:83: The Almighty said: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears. That is, with tears, and it is in the place of the state, and so is they say. And Imru’ al-Qais said: My tears streamed down my throat until my tears soaked my saddle. And a widespread report if it increases and spreads like an overflow of water from abundance, and these are the states of the scholars, they cry but do not faint, they ask but do not cry, they grieve but do not die as God Almighty said, “God has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book, repeated. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver at it, then their skins and their hearts soften at the remembrance of God” (al-Zumar 39:32) and He said, The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful (al-Anfal 8:2) and in Al-Anfal this meaning will be explained, God Almighty willing, and God Almighty explained in these verses that the most rebellious, stubborn, and hostile of the disbelievers toward the Muslims are the Jews, and the polytheists are comparable to them, and He explained that the closest of them in love are the Christians, and God knows best. The Almighty said: Then register us with the witnesses meaning with the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who bear witness to the truth, as the Almighty said: And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over the people (al-Baqarah 2:143) on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj. Al-Hasan said: Those who bear witness to faith. Abu Ali said: Those who bear witness to the truth of your Prophet and your Book. The meaning of then register us is to include us, so it will be in the position of what has been written and recorded.
5:84: The Almighty said: And why should we not believe in God and what has come to us of the truth between their insight into the religion, that is, they say, And why should we not believe?, that is, why are we abandoning faith? So we believe in the accusative case as a state. And we hope that our Lord will admit us with the righteous people, that is, with the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as evidenced by His statement, The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants. (al-Anbiya 21:105) He means the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And in the speech there is an implication, that is, we hope that our Lord will admit us into Paradise. And it was said: With means in, as you mention, and in means with. You say: I was among those who met the prince, that is, with those who met the prince. And greed can be lightened or not lightened. It is said: He greed greed, "greed, and greediness," lightened, so it is greed.
5:85: The Almighty’s saying: So God rewarded them for what they said with gardens. This is evidence of the sincerity of their faith and the truth of their words. God answered their question and fulfilled their desire. Thus, whoever has sincere faith and true certainty will be rewarded with Paradise.
5:86: Then he said: And those who disbelieved from the Jews and Christians and the polytheists and denied Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire. Hellfire is a very blazing fire. It is said: So-and-so blazed the fire, meaning he intensified its blazing. It is also said of the lion’s eye: He blazed it because of its intense blazing. It is also said of war. The poet said: War has no refuge except imagination and fantasy Except for the patient young man in the rescue and the impudent horse
5:89: It has five issues: First: Al-Tabari attributed to Ibn Abbas: The verse was revealed because of a man who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, when I eat meat, I feel dizzy and my desire takes hold of me, so I forbid myself from eating meat. So God revealed this verse. It was said: It was revealed because of a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, including Abu Bakr, Ibn Masoud, Abdullah bin Amr, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, and al-Miqdam bin Maz’un. They agreed to fast during the day, stand in prayer at night, not sleep on mattresses, not eat meat or fat, not approach women or perfume, wear hairy clothes, reject the world, travel the earth, become monks, and cut off the penis. So God Almighty revealed this verse, and there are many reports with this meaning, even if they do not mention the revelation. Second - Muslim narrated on the authority of Anas. A group of the Prophet’s companions, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked the Prophet’s wives, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his secret actions. Some of them said: I will not marry women. Some of them said: I will not eat meat. Some of them said: I will not sleep on the bed. So he praised God and thanked Him and said: What is wrong with people who say such and such? But I pray and sleep, I fast and break my fast, and I marry women. So whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me. Al-Bukhari also narrated it on the authority of Anas, and his wording is: He said: Three men came to the houses of the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking about his worship. When they were informed, they considered it insignificant. They said: Where are we in comparison to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? God has forgiven him his sins, past and future. One of them said: As for me, I will pray all night long. Another said: As for me, I will fast all the time and never break my fast. Another said: As for me, I will stay away from women and never marry. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and said: You are the ones who said such and such. By God, I am the one who fears God the most and is the most pious of you, but I fast, fast, pray, sleep, and marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me. And they narrated from Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: `Uthman ibn Maz`un wanted to urinate, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade him. Had he permitted him to do so, we would have been singled out. Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God be pleased with him, narrated in his Musnad. He said: Abu al-Mughira narrated to us, Ma`an ibn Rafa`ah narrated to us, Ali ibn Yazid narrated to me, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Bahili, may God be pleased with him, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on one of his raids. He said: A man passed by a cave in which there was some water, and he thought to himself that he would stay in that cave and be sustained by the water in it and eat the plants around it, and give up the world. He said: If I go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mention that to him, then if he permits me I will do so, otherwise I will not. So he came to him and said: O Prophet of God, I passed by a cave in which there was water and plants that would sustain me, and I thought to myself that I should stay in it and give up the world. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: I was not sent with Judaism or Christianity, but I was sent with the easy-going Hanafi faith. By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, a morning or evening in the cause of God is better than the world and whatever is in it, and the standing of one of you in the row is better than his prayer of sixty years. Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said about this verse and similar verses and the hadiths that have been narrated in its meaning, a response to the extremists of the ascetics and to the idle Sufis, since each group of them has deviated from its path and deviated from its realization. Al-Tabari said: It is not permissible for any Muslim to forbid himself anything that God has permitted for his believing servants, such as good foods, clothing, and marriages, if he fears that by permitting that, he will cause some hardship and difficulty. For this reason, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rejected celibacy from Ibn Maz’un, and it was proven that there is no virtue in abandoning something that God has permitted for his servants, and that virtue and righteousness are only in doing what He has urged His servants to do, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, acted upon it and prescribed it for his nation, and the rightly-guided imams followed him in his path, since the best guidance is the guidance of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. If this is the case, then the error of the one who prefers to wear hair and wool over cotton and linen if he is able to wear such clothing becomes clear, and the preference for all coarse food and leaving meat and other things is clear, in order to avoid the need for women. Al-Tabari said: If someone thinks that… There is no good in what we have said, because wearing coarse clothing and eating it is a hardship on the soul, and spending the surplus between them of value on the needy has been mistakenly thought, and that is because the first thing a person should do is to improve his soul and help it to obey its Lord, and there is nothing more harmful to the body than bad foods because they corrupt his mind and weaken his tools which God made a means to obey Him. A man came to Al-Hasan Al-Basri and said: I have a neighbor who does not eat Faloodeh. He said: Why? He said: He says he does not give thanks. Al-Hasan said: Should he drink cold water? He said: Yes. He said: Your neighbor is ignorant, for the blessing of God upon him in cold water is greater than His blessing upon him in faloodeh. Ibn al-Arabi said: Our scholars said: This is if religion is established and the money is not forbidden. However, if religion is corrupted among the people and the forbidden is widespread, then celibacy is better and abandoning pleasures is more appropriate. And if what is permissible is found, then the state of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is better and higher. Al-Muhallab said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only forbade celibacy and monasticism because he will outnumber the nations with his nation on the Day of Resurrection, and because in this world they will fight groups of infidels with them, and at the end of time they will fight the Antichrist. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to increase the offspring. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: And do not transgress. It was said: The meaning is do not transgress and make permissible what God has forbidden. So the two prohibitions in this case include both sides, that is, do not be strict and make permissible what is permissible, and do not be lenient and make permissible what is forbidden. This was said by Al-Hasan Al-Basri. It was also said: Its meaning is to emphasize His saying: Forbid. This was said by Al-Suddi, Ikrimah, and others, that is, those who forbid what God has permitted and legislated. The first is more appropriate, and God knows best. Fifth: Whoever forbids himself food, drink, or a female slave, or anything that God has permitted, then there is nothing upon him and no expiation for any of that according to Malik, except that if he intended by forbidding the female slave to free her, then she becomes free and it is forbidden for him to have intercourse with her except through a new marriage after freeing her. Likewise, if he says to his wife, You are forbidden to me, then she is divorced three times. This is because God the Most High has permitted him to forbid his wife to himself by divorce explicitly or implicitly, and forbidden is one of the implicit forms of divorce. What the scholars have said about it will come in Surat At-Tahrim, God willing. Abu Hanifa said: Whoever forbids something, it becomes forbidden to him, and if he consumes it, expiation is required of him. This is far-fetched, and the verse refutes him. Saeed bin Jubayr said: The futility of an oath is the forbidding of what is permissible, and this is the meaning of what Al-Shafi’i said, as will come. It contains forty-seven issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: God will not hold you accountable for what is unintentional in your oaths. The meaning of unintentional oaths was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah, and the meaning of in your oaths is any of your oaths. Oaths are the plural of oath, and it was said: Yamin is a verbal noun from Yaman, which means blessing. God the Almighty called it that because it preserves rights. Yaman is masculine and feminine, and the plural is Ayman and Ayman. Zuhair said: So gather the right ones from us and from you The second - and there is a difference of opinion about the reason for the revelation of this verse. Ibn Abbas said: The reason for its revelation was the people who forbade themselves good things such as food, clothing and marriage. They swore to that effect. When the verse was revealed, Do not forbid the good things which God has made lawful to you, they said: What should we do with our oaths? So this verse was revealed and the meaning according to this statement is that if you swear an oath and then annul it, that is, you drop its ruling by excommunication and disbelieve, then God will not hold you accountable for that. But if He holds you accountable for what you have established, then you have not annulled it, that is, you have not disbelieved. Thus it is clear that the oath does not forbid anything. This is the evidence of Al-Shafi’i that the oath is not related to the prohibition of what is lawful, and that the prohibition of what is lawful is futile, just as the permission of what is forbidden is futile, like the saying of someone: I have permitted drinking alcohol. So the verse concludes according to this statement that God the Most High made the prohibition of what is lawful futile in that it is not forbidden. So He said, God will not hold you accountable for your unintentional oaths, that is, for the prohibition of what is lawful. It was narrated that Abdullah bin Rawahah had orphans and a guest. He returned from his work after an hour of the night and said: Have you given my guest dinner? They said: We were waiting for you. He said: No, by God, I will not eat it tonight. His guest said: I am not the one who eats. His orphans said: We do not eat. When he saw that, he ate and they ate. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He said to him: You obeyed the Most Merciful and disobeyed Satan. So the verse was revealed. Third: Oaths in the Sharia are divided into four categories: two categories in which there is expiation and two categories in which there is no expiation. Ad-Daraqutni narrated in his Sunan, Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz told us, Khalaf bin Hisham told us, Abthar told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Oaths are four: two oaths that require expiation and two oaths that require expiation. The two oaths that require expiation are: a man who swears by God that I will not do such and such, and he does so; and a man who says, by God, I will do such and such, and he does not do so; and the two oaths that do not require expiation are: a man who swears by God that I did not do such and such, and he does so; and a man who swears, by God, I will do such and such, and he does so; and a man who swears, by God, I did do such and such, and he does so; and a man who swears, by God, I did do such and such, and he does not do so. Ibn Abdul Barr said: Sufyan al-Thawri mentioned in Jami`ah, and al-Marwazi also mentioned it from him. Sufyan said: Oaths are four: two oaths that require expiation, which is that a man says, by God, I will not do so, and he does so; or he says, by God, I did do so, and he does not do so; and two oaths that do not require expiation, which is that a man says, by God, I did not do so, and he does so; or he says, by God, I did do so, and he did not do so. Al-Marwazi said: As for the first two oaths, there is no difference among the scholars regarding what Sufyan said. As for the other two oaths, the scholars differed concerning them. If the one who swore swore that he did not do such and such, or that he did such and such in his mind, believing that he was doing what he swore, then there is no sin upon him and he must pay expiation, according to the opinion of Malik, Sufyan, Ath-Thawri, and the People of Opinion. Ahmad and Abu Ubaid also said. Al-Shafi’i said there is no sin upon him and he must pay expiation. Al-Marwazi said: Al-Shafi’i’s statement on this is not correct. He said: If the one who swore that he did not do such and such, and he did it deliberately to lie, then he is sinful and he must pay expiation, according to the majority of scholars: Malik, Sufyan Ath-Thawri, the People of Opinion, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Thawr, and Abu Ubaid. Al-Shafi’i used to say that he must pay expiation. He said: It has been narrated from some of the followers something similar to what Al-Shafi’i said. Al-Marwazi said: I am inclined towards the opinion of Malik and Ahmad. He said: As for the idle oath, which the majority of scholars agreed is idle, it is a man’s saying: No, by God, and yes, by God, in his speech and words, the oath is not binding and he does not intend it. Al-Shafi’i said: This is in cases of obstinacy, anger, and haste. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you make in earnest. The qaf is pronounced with a light sukoon from the word aqd. The qaf is of two types: physical, like the qad of a rope, and legal, like the qad of a sale. The poet said: A people who, when they make a contract with their neighbor, they become stubborn and burden him with hardship. The binding oath is passive of the contract, which is the contract of the heart in the future not to do, so he did or they will do as mentioned above, so this is what is resolved by the exception and expiation as follows. It was read ‘aqaddum with an alif after the ‘ayn in the weight of fa’il, and this only happens with two people in most cases, and the second may be from someone who swore for him in a speech that occurred with him, or the meaning is that ‘aqaddum is the oaths because ‘aqaddum is close in meaning to ‘ahid, so it was transitive with the preposition since it was in the meaning of ahid, and ahid is transitive with two objects, the second of which is with a preposition. God Almighty said: And who fulfills what he has pledged to God? (al-Fath 48:10). This is like ‘anaditum was transitive with ila, and its chapter is to say naditu Zayd “And we called him from the right side of the Mount” (Maryam 19:52). But since it was in the meaning of da’tu, it was transitive with ila, God Almighty said: And who is better in speech than one who calls to God? (Fussilat 41:33). Then it was expanded in God Almighty’s saying ‘aqaddum upon him, so the preposition was deleted, so the verb was connected to the object, so it became ‘aqaddumu, then the ha’ was deleted. It was also deleted from the Almighty’s saying: Then proclaim what you are commanded (al-Hijr 15:94), or it could be a fa’il with the meaning of fa’ala, as the Almighty said: May God fight them (al-Tawbah 9:30), meaning kill them. The mufa’ala may come in the speech of the Arabs from one without the meaning of fa’ilat, as in their saying: I travelled and I declared my intentions, and it was read as ‘aqdtum with a shaddah on the qaf. Mujahid said: Its meaning is you intended, meaning you intended. It was narrated from Ibn ‘Umar that the shaddah requires repetition, so expiation is not obligatory on him unless he repeats it. This is refuted by what was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, God willing, I will not swear an oath and then see something better than it, unless I do what is better and atone for my oath.” He mentioned the obligation of atonement for an oath that is not repeated. Ubayd said: “Emphasis is repetition over and over again. I am not confident that someone who recites in that manner will not be required to atone for a single oath until he repeats it repeatedly. This is a statement that is contrary to consensus. Nafi’ narrated that if Ibn ‘Umar broke his oath without emphasizing the oath, he would feed ten poor people. If he emphasized the oath, he would free a slave. It was said to Nafi’: What is the meaning of emphasizing the oath? He said: That he swears on something repeatedly. Fifth - There is a difference of opinion regarding the false oath: is it a binding oath or not? The majority of scholars agree that it is an oath of deceit, trickery, and lying, so it is not binding and there is no expiation for it. Al-Shafi’i said: It is a binding oath because it is acquired in the heart, binding with information, coupled with the name of God the Most High, and there is expiation for it. The first is correct. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This is the opinion of Malik ibn Anas and those who followed him from the people of Medina, and al-Awza’i and those who agreed with him from the people of Ash-Sham said the same. It is the opinion of al-Thawri and the people of Iraq, and Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, Abu Ubaid, the scholars of hadith, and the scholars of opinion from the people of Kufa said the same. Abu Bakr said: And the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever swears an oath and then sees that something else is better, let him do what is better and expiate for his oath. His statement, “let him expiate for his oath and do what is better,” indicates that expiation is only required for someone who swears to do something in the future and does not do it, or to do something in the future and does it. There is a second opinion on the issue, which is that he should expiate even if he intentionally commits a sin by swearing falsely by God. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i. Abu Bakr said: We do not know of any report that indicates this opinion, and the Book and the Sunnah indicate the first opinion. God the Most High said: “And do not make God an excuse for your oaths, lest you be righteous and fear God and make peace between people.” (al-Baqarah 2:224) Ibn Abbas said: It is the man who swears that he will not maintain ties with his relatives, so God made a way out for him in expiation and ordered him not to use God as an excuse and to think about his oath. The reports indicate that the oath that a man swears to seize unlawful money is too great to be expiated for by what expiates an oath. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The verse was revealed in two categories: vain and binding. It is usually taken as a general rule in people’s oaths, so leave what comes after it as a hundred oaths, as no expiation is required for it. I said: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: “A Bedouin came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what are the major sins? He said: Associating partners with God. He said: Then what? He said: Disobeying one’s parents. He said: Then what? He said: A false oath. I said: What is a false oath? He said: That by which a Muslim’s money is taken while he is lying.” It was narrated by Muslim on the authority of Abu Umamah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever usurps the right of a Muslim by swearing an oath, God has made Hell obligatory for him and has forbidden him Paradise. A man said: Even if it is something insignificant, O Messenger of God? He said: Even if it is a twig of arak. And from the hadith of Abdullah bin Masoud, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath to seize the wealth of a Muslim while he is a sinner, will meet God while He is angry with him. So the verse was revealed: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of God and their oaths for a small price (Al Imran 3:77) to the end of the verse. No expiation was mentioned. If we had required expiation from him, his crime would have been dropped and he would have met God while He was pleased with him and would not have deserved the threat that was imposed upon him. How could that not be the case when this oath-taker combined lying, taking the wealth of others into his own hands, belittling the oath to God, the Most High, and taking it lightly and glorifying the world? So he humiliated what God glorified and glorified what God belittled. That is enough for you. For this reason it was said: The oath that immerses is called immersing because it immerses its owner in the Fire. Sixth: If someone swears not to do something out of righteousness that he did not do, then if he does it, he has broken his oath and the infidel will be obligated to do it because of the violation on his part. Likewise, if he says, If I do it, and if he swears that he will do it, then he is immediately guilty of breaking his oath because of the violation. If he does it, he is righteous. Likewise, if he says, If I did not do it. Seventh: The saying of the one swearing: I will do it, even if I do not, is like a command, and his saying: I will not do it, even if I do, is like a prohibition. In the first case, he is not fulfilled until he does all of what he swore upon. An example of this is: I will eat this loaf, so he eats some of it, he is not fulfilled until he eats all of it, because every part of it is sworn upon. If he says: By God, I will eat absolutely - then he is fulfilled by the smallest part that the name applies to, in order to include the essence of eating in existence. As for the prohibition, then he breaks his oath by the smallest part that the name applies to, because its requirement is that no individual of the individuals of what is prohibited enters into existence. If he swears not to enter a house and then inserts one of his feet, he has broken his oath. The evidence for this is that we found the Lawgiver to be strict in the aspect of prohibition by the beginning of the name in His Most High’s saying: And do not marry those whom your fathers married (An-Nisa’: 22). So whoever contracts a marriage with a woman and does not consummate the marriage with her, she is forbidden to his father and son. And the beginning of the name is not sufficient in the aspect of permissibility, so he said: Don't even taste his honey. Eighth: The one sworn by is God Almighty and His beautiful names, such as the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, the Forbearing, and similar to these of His names and supreme attributes, such as His glory, power, knowledge, will, pride, greatness, covenant, pact, and all the other attributes of His Essence, because it is an oath by an eternal, uncreated being, so the one swearing by it is like swearing by the Essence. Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, and others narrated: Gabriel, peace be upon him, looked at Paradise and returned to God Almighty and said: By Your glory, no one hears of it without entering it. And likewise He said about the Fire: By Your glory, no one hears of it without entering it. They also left and others on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: The Prophet’s oath, may God bless him and grant him peace, was: No, by the Changer of hearts. In another narration: No, by the Disposer of hearts. The scholars agreed that if someone swore and said: By God, by God, or by God, and broke his oath, then he must make expiation. Ibn al-Mundhir said: Malik, al-Shafi’i, Abu Ubaid, Abu Thawr, Ishaq, and the People of Opinion used to say that whoever swears by one of the names of God and breaks his oath, then he must make expiation. This is what we say, and I do not know of any disagreement on that. I said: It was mentioned in the chapter on swearing by the Qur’an, and Ya’qub said: Whoever swears by the Most Merciful and breaks his oath, there is no expiation upon him. I said: The Most Gracious is one of His names, glory be to Him, and there is no disagreement about it. Ninth - They differed regarding By the right of God and By the greatness of God and By the life of God and By the life of God and By the oath of God. Malik said: All of these are oaths for which expiation is required. Al-Shafi’i said: In By the right of God and By the majesty of God and By the greatness of God and By the power of God it is an oath if he intended an oath by it, but if he did not intend an oath then it is not an oath because it is possible. By the right of God is obligatory and By the power of God is valid. He said regarding By the life of God and By the life of God if he did not intend an oath by it then it is not an oath. The people of opinion said: If he said By the greatness of God and By the glory of God and By the majesty of God and By the pride of God and By the trust of God then he broke his oath, then he must make expiation. Al-Hasan said regarding By the right of God: It is not an oath and there is no expiation for it, and this is the opinion of Abu Hanifa, as narrated by Al-Razi. Likewise, By the covenant of God and By the covenant of God and By the trust of God are not. Some of his companions said: It is an oath. Al-Tahawi said: It is not an oath. Likewise, if he said: By the knowledge of God it was not an oath according to Abu Hanifa, and his companion Abu Yusuf disagreed with him and said: It is an oath. Ibn Al-Arabi said: What led him to do that is that knowledge may be applied to the known. He is the narrator So it is not an oath and he is oblivious to the fact that ability is based on the ability. So every statement he has about the ability is our proof for the known. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It is proven that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, he is truly worthy of leadership.” In the story of Zaid and his son Usama. Ibn Abbas used to say: By God, and Ibn Omar said the same. Ishaq said: If he meant by by God an oath, it was an oath by will and the heart’s determination. Tenth - They differed regarding swearing by the Qur’an. Ibn Masoud said: He must swear by every verse. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Ibn Al-Mubarak said the same. Ahmad said: I do not know of anything that would prevent it. Abu Ubaid said: It is a single oath. Abu Hanifa said: There is no expiation for him. Qatada said: He should swear by the Qur’an. Ahmad and Ishaq said: We do not disapprove of that. Eleventh - An oath is not valid except by God Almighty and His names and attributes. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: If he swears by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, his oath is valid because he swore by something without which faith is not complete, so he must make expiation, just as if he swore by God. This is refuted by what was proven in the two Sahihs and others, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he caught up with Umar ibn al-Khattab in a group and Umar was swearing by his father, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called out to them: Indeed, God forbids you to swear by your fathers. So whoever swears, let him swear by God or remain silent.” This is a restriction on not swearing by anything other than God Almighty and His names and attributes, as we mentioned. What confirms this is what Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, and others narrated: “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not swear by your fathers or your mothers or by rivals to God, and do not swear except by God, and do not swear by God unless you are truthful.” Then he is contradicted by the one who said: And Adam and Abraham, for there is no expiation upon him, and he swore by something without which faith is not complete. Twelfth - The imams narrated, and the wording is from Muslim, “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever among you swears and says in his oath by Al-Lat, let him say: There is no god but God. And whoever says to his companion, “Come, let us gamble,” let him give in charity. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Mus’ab bin Sa’d on the authority of his father, who said: We were mentioning something and I was new to the pre-Islamic era, so I swore by al-Lat and al-Uzza. Some of the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me: What a bad thing you have said. In another narration, I said it out of idle talk. So I went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him. He said: “Say: ‘There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He is over all things omnipotent.’ Blow to your left three times and seek refuge in God from Satan, then do not do it again.” The scholars said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered whoever uttered that to say after it: ‘There is no god but God,’ as an expiation for that statement, a reminder from heedlessness, and a completion of the blessing. He mentioned al-Lat specifically because it was the one they used to say most often. The ruling on the other names of their gods is the same as its ruling, as there is no difference between them. Similarly, whoever says to his companion: ‘Come on, let me gamble,’ then let him give charity. The ruling on him is like the ruling on al-Lat, because they were accustomed to gambling, which is a form of consuming wealth unjustly. Thirteenth - Abu Hanifa said about a man who says: He is Jewish or Christian or innocent of Islam or the Prophet or the Qur’an or associates partners with God or disbelieves in God: It is an oath for which expiation is required, but it is not required if he says: Jewishness, Christianity, the Prophet, and the Kaaba, even if it is in the form of oaths and adheres to what Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Nafi’: His mistress wanted to separate him from his wife, so she said: One day she is Jewish and one day she is Christian, and every slave of hers is free, and all her wealth is for the sake of God, and she must walk to the House of God if she does not separate them. So she asked Aisha, Hafsa, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, and Umm Salamah, and they all said to her: Do you want to be like Harut and Mawwarat? And they ordered her to atone for her oath and to leave it, while he also went out from him. He said: My mistress said: I will separate you from your wife, and all her money is in the curtain of the Kaaba. She is a Jew one day, a Christian one day, and a Zoroastrian one day. If I do not separate you from your wife, he said: So go to the mother of the believers Umm Salamah and say: My mistress wants to separate me from my wife. She said: Go to your mistress and tell her: This is not permissible for you. He said: So I returned to her. He said: Then I went to Ibn Umar and told him. He came until he reached the door and said: Here are Harut and Marut. She said: I have placed all my money in the curtain of the Kaaba. He said: So what do you eat? She said: And I said: I am a Jew one day, a Christian one day, and a Zoroastrian one day. He said: If you become a Jew She was killed, and if she became a Christian she was killed, and if she became a Zoroastrian she was killed. She said: What do you command me to do? He said: Make atonement for your oath and bring together your young man and young woman. The scholars agreed that if the one taking the oath said: I swear by God that it is an oath, and they differed if he said: I swear or testify that such and such will happen, but he did not say by God, so it is considered an oath according to Malik if he meant by God, and if he did not mean by God, it is not an oath that requires disbelief. Abu Hanifa, Al-Awza’i, Al-Hasan, and Al-Nakha’i said: It is an oath in both cases. Al-Shafi’i said: It is not considered an oath until the name of God Almighty is mentioned. This is the narration of Al-Muzani from him, and Al-Rabi’ narrated from him something similar to what Malik said. Fourteenth: If he says: I swear to you that you will do it, if he means to ask him, then there is no expiation for it and it is not an oath, and if he means an oath, then it is what we mentioned earlier. Fifteenth - Whoever swears by something attributed to God Almighty that is not an attribute, such as saying: And God created, provided for, and housed Him, then there is nothing against him because it is absolutely impermissible, and he swears by something other than God Almighty. Sixteenth: If an oath is made, it is resolved by expiation or exception. Ibn Al-Majishun said: The exception is a substitute for expiation and is not a resolution for the oath. Ibn Al-Qasim said: It is a resolution for the oath. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is the doctrine of the jurists of the countries and it is correct. Its condition is that it be connected and explicitly stated, according to what Al-Nasa’i and Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If someone swears and makes an exception, he can continue, and if he wishes, he can leave without breaking his oath. If he intended it without speaking or without a part of it without an excuse, it will not benefit him. Muhammad ibn al-Mawaz said: The exception is coupled with the oath, believing it even with the last letter. He said: If he finished it and made an exception, it will not benefit him because the oath was finished without the exception, so they brought it after it, it does not affect it like delay. This is refuted by the hadith: “If someone swears and makes an exception,” and the fa is for succession, and the majority of scholars agree with this. Also, this leads to the oath that was initially concluded not being dissolved, and this is invalid. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: Our companions differed when he made an exception in himself, specifying what he swore upon. Some of our companions said: His exception is valid, and he wronged the one to whom he swore. Some of them said: It is not valid until the one to whom he made the oath hears it. Some of them said: It is valid if he moves his tongue and lips with it, even if the one to whom he swore does not hear it. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: We only said that his exception is valid in himself, because oaths are considered according to intentions, and we only said that it is not valid until he moves his tongue with it. And his lips. If he does not move his tongue and lips with it, he is not speaking. The exception to speech occurs without others. We only said that it is not valid in any case because that is a right for the one to whom the oath is sworn. It only occurs according to what he fulfills for him. The ruler, since the oath was not at the choice of the swearer but was fulfilled by him, it is necessary that he has no ruling on it. Ibn Abbas said: The exception of the oath is realized after a year, and Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Hasan followed in that and it was related to the saying of God Almighty: And those who do not invoke with God another deity (al-Furqan 25:68) the verse, so since it was after a year, Except for those who repent (al-Furqan 25:70) was revealed. Mujahid said: Whoever says after two years, God willing, it is sufficient for him. Saeed bin Jubair said: If he makes an exception after four months, it is sufficient for him. Tawus said: He may make an exception as long as he is in his seat. Qatada said: If he makes an exception before he stands up or speaks, he has two teeth. Ahmad bin Hanbal and Ishaq said: He makes an exception as long as he is in that matter. Ata’ said: He has that for the amount of milking a large camel. Seventeenth - Ibn al-Arabi said: As for what Ibn Abbas related to from the verse, it has no connection to it because the two verses were connected in the knowledge of God Almighty and in His Tablet, and their revelation was delayed for a wisdom that God knew about them. As for the fact that a good branch is built upon them, which is that if the one swearing says, By God, I will not enter the house and you are divorced if you enter the house, and he excepted in his first oath, God willing, in his heart, and he also excepted in his second oath in his heart what is suitable for the exception that lifts the oath for a period or reason or the will of someone, he did not show anything of the exception to terrorize the one sworn to, for that benefits him and the two oaths are not binding on him. This is in divorce unless evidence is present. If evidence is present, his claim of exception is not accepted from him, but it is only beneficial to him if he comes seeking a fatwa. I said: The reason for the exception is that God Almighty revealed the first verse and concealed the second, so is the case if the one who swears an oath to terrorize and conceals the exception, and God knows best. Ibn al-Arabi said: Abu al-Fadl al-Maraghi used to read in the City of Peace, and books would come to him from his country, so he would put them in a box and not read a single one of them for fear that he would find something in them that would disturb him and cut him off from his quest. When five years had passed and he had completed his quest and decided to leave, he packed his bags and brought out his books and took out those letters and read in them what if a Mahna read after his arrival he would not be able to acquire a letter of knowledge after that. So he praised God and traveled on a cloth mount and went out to the door of the arena, the road to Khurasan, and al-Kari preceded him on the mount, and he stayed with a mount to buy his baggage from him. While he was trying to do that with him, he heard him say to another mount: Haven’t you heard the scholar say - meaning the preacher - that Ibn Abbas permits the exception even after a year? This has occupied my mind since I heard it, so I remained thinking about it. If that were true, God Almighty would not have said to Job: “And take your hand and your tongue... “He said: ‘I will strike you with it and do not break my oath.’” [p. 44] What prevents him from saying: Say, ‘God willing?’ When he heard him say that, he said: A country where the Famyis have this share of knowledge and this rank, should I go out to Maragha? I will never do it. He followed the path of the generous man and released him from the rent and stayed there until he died. Eighteenth - The exception only removes the oath by God Almighty if it is a concession from God Almighty and there is no disagreement on this. They differed on the exception in the oath by other than God. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa said: The exception occurs in every oath such as divorce, emancipation, and other than that, such as the oath by God Almighty. Abu Omar said: What they agreed upon is the truth, and the success is only in the exception in the oath by God Almighty and not in other than that? Nineteenth - The Almighty’s saying: Then its expiation. The scholars differed about whether expiation is sufficient before breaking the oath or not - after their consensus that breaking the oath before expiation is permissible and good, and it is better for them - on three opinions: One of them is that it is sufficient absolutely, and this is the doctrine of fourteen of the Companions and the majority of the jurists, and it is the well-known doctrine of Malik. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: It is not sufficient in any way, and this is the narration of Ashab on the authority of Malik. The aspect of permissibility is what Abu Musa al-Ash’ari narrated, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, God willing, I will not swear an oath and then see something better than it, except that I will atone for my oath and do that which is better.” Narrated by Abu Dawud. From the meaning, the oath is the cause of atonement, as God Almighty said: That is the expiation for your oaths when you swear. So He added atonement to the oath, and meanings are added to their causes. Also, atonement is a substitute for righteousness, so it is permissible to bring it forward before breaking the oath. The reason for prohibiting it is what Muslim narrated on the authority of Adi bin Hatim, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, let him do what is better. Al-Nasa’i added, and expiate for his oath. From the meaning, expiation is only to remove the sin, and as long as he does not break his oath, there is nothing to remove it, so there is no point in doing it. The meaning of the Almighty’s statement, If you swear, is if you swear and break your oath. Also, every act of worship performed before it becomes obligatory is not valid, considering the prayers. And other acts of worship. Al-Shafi’i said: It is sufficient to feed, free, and clothe a slave, but it is not sufficient to fast because the work of the body is not performed before its time. In other cases, it is sufficient to estimate the expiation, which is the third opinion. Al-Muwaffiyah 20 - God Almighty mentioned the three options in the expiation, so He gave him a choice in them, and if they are not available, He followed them with fasting, and He began with food because it was the best in the Hijaz due to the great need for it and the lack of people there. There is no disagreement that the expiation for an oath is based on choice. Ibn al-Arabi said: What I have is that it is according to the situation. If you know someone in need, then food is better, because if you free someone, you will not meet their need and you will add an eleventh person in need to them. Likewise, clothing follows it. And when God knew the need, He began with the important introduction. Twenty-first - The Almighty’s saying: Feeding ten poor people. According to us and according to Al-Shafi’i, it is necessary to give the poor people ownership of what is given to them, and to give it to them so that they can own it and dispose of it, based on the Almighty’s saying: And he feeds, but is not fed. (al-An’am 6:14) And in the hadith: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fed the grandmother a sixth.” And because it is one of the two types of expiation, nothing is permissible in it except ownership. Its origin is clothing. Abu Hanifa said that if he gave them breakfast and dinner, it would be permissible, and this is the choice of Ibn Al-Majishun from our scholars. Ibn Al-Majishun said: Giving them access to food is feeding. God Almighty said: And they feed food, in spite of their love for it, to the poor, the orphan, and the captive. [Al-Insan] So in whatever way he fed him, is he included in the verse. Twenty-second - The Almighty’s saying: From the middle of what you feed your families. It was previously mentioned in Al-Baqarah that the middle means the highest and the best, and here it is a position between two positions and a half between two extremes, and from it the hadith. The best of things are those that are in the middle. Ibn Majah narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A man would feed his family with ample food, and a man would feed his family with a difficult food, so this verse was revealed: From the middle of what you feed your families. This indicates that the middle is what we mentioned, which is what is between two things. Twenty-third - Feeding, according to Malik, is one mudd for each of the ten poor people, if it is in the city of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is what Al-Shafi’i and the people of Medina said. Sulayman ibn Yasar said: I knew the people, and when they gave in expiation for an oath, they gave a mudd of wheat, the smallest mudd, and they saw that as sufficient for them. This is the opinion of Ibn ‘Umar, Ibn ‘Abbas, and Zayd ibn Thabit. This is what ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said. There is a difference of opinion if it is elsewhere. Ibn Al-Qasim said: One mudd is sufficient for him in any place. Ibn Al-Mawaz said: Ibn Wahb issued a fatwa in Egypt with one and a half mudds, and Ashab with one and a third mudds. He said: And one and a third mudds are for the average food of the cities for lunch and dinner. Abu Hanifa said: Half a sa’ of wheat is given, and one sa’ of dates and barley, according to the hadith of ‘Abdullah ibn Tha’labah ibn Su’ayr on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and gave a sermon and ordered that the Zakat al-Fitr be given as a sa` of dates, or a sa` of barley from each head, or a sa` of wheat between two people. Sufyan and Ibn al-Mubarak took this view and narrated on the authority of Ali, Amr Ibn Umar and Aisha, may God be pleased with them. Sa`id Ibn al-Musayyab said this, and it is the view of most of the jurists of Iraq, because Ibn Abbas narrated that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disbelieved with a sa` of dates and ordered the people to do the same. Whoever cannot find any, then half a sa` of dates.” From the average of what you feed your families. Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan. Twenty-fourth - It is not permissible to feed a rich person or a relative whose expenses he is obligated to pay. If he is one whose expenses he is not obligated to pay, Malik said: I do not like him to feed him, but if he does and he is poor, it is sufficient for him. If he feeds a rich person who is ignorant of his wealth, then in Al-Mudawwana and other books it says: It is not sufficient. And in Al-Usaydah it is sufficient. Twenty-fifth - A man should give out what he eats. Ibn al-Arabi said: A group of scholars have made a mistake here and said: If he eats barley and people eat wheat, then he should give out what people eat. This is a clear oversight, because if the one who is giving expiation cannot afford anything but barley for himself, then he is not required to give anything else to anyone else. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A sa’ of food, a sa’ of barley. So he mentioned them separately so that each person could give out his share of what he eats. This is something that is not hidden. Twenty-sixth - Malik said: If he feeds ten poor people lunch and dinner, that is sufficient for him. Al-Shafi’i said: It is not permissible to feed them all at once because they differ in eating, but he should give each poor person a mudd. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: It is not sufficient to feed ten people one meal, meaning lunch without dinner, or dinner without lunch, until he feeds them lunch and dinner. Omar said: This is the opinion of the imams of fatwas in the regions. Twenty-seventh - Ibn Habib said: Bread is not sufficient as a desert, but rather he should be given with it a condiment of oil, kashk, kamekh, or whatever is available. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is an addition, I do not see it as obligatory. However, it is recommended for him to eat sugar - yes - and meat with the bread. As for specifying the condiment for the food, there is no way to do that because the wording does not include it. I said: The revelation of the verse in the middle requires bread and oil or vinegar, and what is similar in meaning to it, such as cheese and kishk, as Ibn Habib said, and God knows best. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, vinegar is a condiment. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: If he feeds them bread and meat, or bread and oil once a day until they are full, it is sufficient for him. This is the opinion of Ibn Sirin, Jabir bin Zaid, and Makhul. It was narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik. Twenty-eighth - It is not permissible for us to pay the expiation to one poor person, and this is what Al-Shafi’i and the companions of Abu Hanifa said, forbidding all of it to be given to one person at once, and they differed as to whether all of it was given on one day in different payments. Some of them permitted that, and that if the action is repeated, it is good to say about the second action that it does not prevent the one to whom it was given first, because the name of the poor person includes it. Others said: It is permissible to give it to him in days, even though the number of days takes the place of the number of poor people. Abu Hanifa said: That is sufficient for him because the purpose of the verse is to define the amount of food, so if he gives it in an amount to one person, it is sufficient for him. Our evidence is the text of God Almighty regarding the ten, so it is not permissible to deviate from them. Also, it includes reviving a group of Muslims and sufficing them for one day, so they devote themselves to worshipping God Almighty and supplicating to Him, so the one who gives expiation is forgiven because of that, and God knows best. Twenty-ninth - The Almighty’s saying: “Then his expiation” The pronoun, according to the grammatical construction, refers back to what, and it is possible in this place that it means who, and it is possible that it is a source or it refers back to the sin of urging, even if it is not explicitly mentioned, but the meaning requires it. Al-Muwfiyyah Thirty - The Almighty’s saying: Your families is the plural of family in the name of safety. Ja’far bin Muhammad al-Sadiq read: Your families and this is a broken plural. Abu al-Fath said: Ahal is like Ahal is like layal and its singular is ahlat and laylat. The Arabs say: Ahl and ahla. The poet said: His family and I have disavowed their friendship and I have worn them out in my effort, Hamdi and Nayli He says: I was exposed to their affection, said Ibn Al-Sikkit. Twenty-first - The Almighty’s saying: Or their clothing. Bakr read the kaf and the damma, they are two languages like iswa and aswa. Saeed bin Jubair and Muhammad bin Al-Musayqi’ Al-Yamani read: Or like their clothing like the clothing of your family. Clothing for men is a single garment that covers the entire body. As for women, the least that is sufficient for them to pray in is a shirt and a veil. This is the ruling for children. Ibn Al-Qasim said in Al-Utbiyyah: A small girl is clothed in a large garment, and a small girl is clothed in a large garment, by analogy with food. Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, Al-Thawri, and Al-Awza’i said: The least that the name applies to is one garment. In the narration of Abu Al-Faraj from Malik, and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and Mughirah said the same: What covers the entire body, based on the fact that prayer is not sufficient in less than that. It was narrated from Salman, may God be pleased with him, that he said: A good garment is a turban. At-Tabari attributed it to him. Al-Hakam bin Utaybah said: A turban that is wrapped around his head is sufficient, and this is the saying of Al-Thawri. Ibn Al-Arabi said: I was most eager for it to be said: It is not sufficient. It is sufficient to wear only clothing that covers one from the harm of heat and cold, and he also has food to satisfy his hunger, so I say that. As for saying that he should wear one loincloth, I do not know. May God open up knowledge for me and for you with His help. I said: Some people have taken into consideration the customary customs of clothing and attire, so some of them said: One garment is not sufficient unless it is a combination of what may be worn as adornment, such as a cloak and a garment. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: The clothing for expiation of an oath for every poor person is a garment and a loincloth, or a cloak or a shirt or a robe or a cloak. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari that he ordered that two garments be worn on his behalf, and al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin said the same. This is the meaning of what Ibn al-Arabi chose, and God knows best. Thirty-second - The value is not sufficient for food and clothing. Al-Shafi’i said the same. Abu Hanifa said: It is sufficient. He said: The value is sufficient for zakat, so how about expiation? Ibn al-Arabi said: His main point is that the purpose is to fill the gap and remove the need, so the value is sufficient for that. We said: If you look at filling the gap, where are the servants? And where is the text of the Qur’an on the three entities, and the transition in explanation from one type to another? Thirty-third: If he pays the clothing to a non-Muslim or to a slave, it is not permissible for him. Abu Hanifa said: It is permissible for him because he is a poor person, and the word poor includes him, and the generality of the verse includes him. We said that this is specific to him, as he says that part of the money must be given to the poor, so it is not permissible to pay it to the infidel, its origin is zakat. We have agreed that it is not permissible to pay it to an apostate, so every evidence that specifies it for an apostate is our evidence for the non-Muslim, and the slave is not poor because he is independent of his master’s expenses, so it is not given to him like the rich. Thirty-fourth - The Almighty’s saying: or the freeing of a slave. Freeing means releasing from slavery. It is used in captivity and derivatives, the toil of this world, and the like. From this is the saying of Mary’s mother: Indeed, I have vowed to You what is in my womb to be freed (Al Imran 3:35), meaning from the distractions of this world and the like. From this is the saying of Al Farazdaq bin Ghalib. My son Ghadana, I have freed you and given you to Atiya bin Ja’al. That is, I have freed you from satire, and I have singled out the neck of a human being, since it is the organ in which the shackles and bondage are usually found in animals, so it is the place of ownership, so liberation was added to it. Thirty-fifth - It is not permissible for us to free anything except a believing slave who is complete and who has no partner with anyone else, nor freeing part of it, nor freeing for a specified period, nor writing it down, nor managing it, nor being a mother of a child if it were not for the one who frees him if he owns him, nor having the old age or age that would be used for earning a living, sound and not defective, contrary to Dawud in permitting the freeing of a defective slave. Abu Hanifa said: It is permissible to free a female unbeliever because the absolute wording requires it, and our evidence is that it is an obligatory village, so the unbeliever is not a place for it like zakat. Also, everything that is absolute in the Qur’an from this refers back to the restriction in freeing a slave in the case of accidental killing. Rather, we said: There is no polytheism in it for the sake of God Almighty: Then the freeing of a slave. And some of the slave is not a slave. Rather, we said that there is no contract of emancipation in it, because emancipation requires the beginning of emancipation without the completion of emancipation in advance. Rather, we said: It is sound, because God Almighty said: Then the freeing of a slave. And the generality requires the freeing of a complete slave, and the blind slave is incomplete. And in the Sahih, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is no Muslim who frees a Muslim man except that his release from the Fire is every limb of his for every limb of ours, even the vagina for the vagina. This is a text, and two opinions have been narrated in the doctrine about the one-eyed, and likewise about the deaf and the eunuch. Thirty-sixth: If someone gives money to free a slave as expiation and it is lost, the expiation remains due on him, unlike if someone gives money as zakat to give it to the poor or to buy a slave with it and it is lost, then he is not required to do anything else in order to comply with the command. Thirty-seventh - They differed regarding the expiation if the person who swore dies. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr said: The expiations for oaths are taken from the deceased’s capital. Abu Hanifa said: It is to be taken from a third, and Malik said the same if he bequeathed it. Thirty-eighth - If someone swears an oath while he is wealthy and does not atone until he becomes poor, or breaks his oath while he is poor and does not atone until he becomes wealthy, or breaks his oath while he is a slave and does not atone until he is freed, then the consideration in all of this is the time of atonement, not the time of the breaking of the oath. Thirty-ninth - Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, for one of you to insist on swearing an oath against his wife is a sin before God, rather than giving the expiation that God has imposed. “Insisting on an oath means going along with it, even if that results in hardship and difficulty and abandoning what is of immediate or deferred benefit. If something like that happens, then it is better for him to swear an oath and do the expiation and not use the oath as an excuse, as we mentioned in the words of God Almighty: “And do not make God an object of your oaths” (al-Baqarah 2:224).
