And “He, peace be upon him, said: Whoever swears an oath and then sees something else that is better than it, let him expiate for his oath and do what is better,” meaning what is more good. The forty-year-old - Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The oath is based on the intention of the one taking the oath. The scholars said: Its meaning is that if someone is required to take an oath regarding a right that is required of him and he swears while intending something else, his intention will not benefit him, and he will not be relieved of the sin of that oath. This is the meaning of his statement in the other hadith: Your oath is based on what your companion believes you to be true to. It was also narrated: Your companion believes you to be true to it. Muslim also narrated that Malik said: Whoever swears to his claimant regarding a right he has over him, and makes an exception in his oath or moves his tongue or lips or speaks about it, his exception will not benefit him because the intention is the intention of the one sworn to because the oath is a right of his. Rather, it occurs according to what the judge fulfills for him, not according to the choice of the one swearing because it is fulfilled from him. This is the conclusion of his school of thought. His statement: Forty-one - The Almighty’s saying: But whoever does not find means that he does not find in his possession one of these three, from feeding, clothing, or freeing a slave, by consensus. So if he does not find these three things, he should fast. The lack of money can be either due to the absence of money from him or its nonexistence. The first is that he is in a country other than his own. If he finds someone to lend him money, fasting is not permissible for him. But if he does not find someone to lend him money, then there is a difference of opinion on this. It was said: He should wait until he reaches his country. Ibn al-Arabi said: That is not binding on him, rather he should expiate by fasting, because the obligation has been established in the conscience and the condition of nonexistence has been fulfilled. There is no reason to delay the matter, so let him expiate in its place because of his inability to do the three types, according to the Almighty’s saying: But whoever does not find It was said: Whoever does not have any surplus over his capital with which he lives, he is the one who does not find. It was said: He is the one who has nothing but his daily sustenance and he does not have any surplus to feed him. Al-Shafi’i said this, and al-Tabari chose it, and it is the school of Malik and his companions. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim that whoever has any surplus and his daily expenses, then he does not fast. Ibn al-Arabi said: Al-Qasim in the book of Ibn Muzain: If the perjurer has more than his daily sustenance, he should feed him, unless he fears hunger or is in a country where no one is kind to him. Abu Hanifa said: If he does not have a hardship, then he should be deceived and have enough. Ahmad and Ishaq said: If he has enough sustenance for a day and a night, he should feed him what is left over. Abu Ubaid said: If he has enough sustenance for a day and a night, his dependents, and clothing that is enough for them, and after that he owns enough money for expiation, then according to us he is enough. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The statement of Abu Ubaid is good. Forty-second - The Almighty’s saying: Then a fast of three days. Ibn Masoud read it in succession, restricting it to the absolute, and Abu Hanifa and Al-Thawri said the same, and it is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, and Al-Muzani chose it based on analogy to fasting in the expiation for Zihar and taking into consideration the reading of Abdullah. Malik and Al-Shafi’i said in his other statement: Separation is sufficient for him, because succession is a characteristic that is not required except by a text or by analogy to a text, and they are absent. Forty-third - If someone breaks his fast on a day of fasting out of forgetfulness, Malik said: He must make it up. Al-Shafi’i said: He does not have to make it up, as was explained previously in fasting in Al-Baqarah. Forty-fourth - This expiation that God has stipulated is obligatory for the free Muslim by consensus. They differed as to what is obligatory for the slave if he breaks his oath. Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Shafi’i, and the People of Opinion said: He only has to fast, and nothing else will suffice him. Malik’s statement differed on this, and Ibn Nafi’ reported from him that he said: The slave does not expiate by freeing him, because he does not have loyalty, but he expiates by giving charity if his master gives him permission. The most correct of that is that he fast. Ibn Al-Qasim narrated on his authority that he said: If he feeds or clothes with the permission of the master, then it is not clear, and there is something in my heart about him. Forty-fifth - The Almighty’s saying: That is the expiation for your oaths, meaning covering your oaths. To cover something means to cover it and conceal it. It has been mentioned before and there is no disagreement that this expiation is for swearing by God Almighty. Some of the followers went to the view that the expiation for an oath is doing the good that one swore to leave off. Ibn Majah included in his Sunan the following: Whoever says its expiation is leaving it off. Ali ibn Muhammad told us, Abdullah ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Haritha ibn Abi al-Rijal, on the authority of Umrah, on the authority of Aisha, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears to sever family ties or to do something that is not right, then his oath should not be fulfilled on that basis. It was narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears an oath and then sees something better than it, he should abandon it, for abandoning it is an expiation for it. I said: This is supported by the story of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, when he swore that he would not feed the poor and his wife swore that she would not feed him until he fed him, and the guest - or guests - swore that he would not feed him or that they would not tempt him until he fed him, so Abu Bakr said: This was from the devil, so he called for food and ate and they ate. Al-Bukhari narrated it, and Muslim added: When morning came, he went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O Messenger of God, you have been righteous and I have broken my oath. He said: So he informed him, and he said: Rather, you are the most pious and the best of them.” He said: And I have not been informed of any expiation. Forty-sixth - They differed about the expiation for anything other than an oath by God Almighty. Malik said: Whoever swears by charity, he must give a third of it. Al-Shafi’i said: He must pay the expiation for an oath. This is what Ishaq, Abu Thawr, and it was narrated on the authority of Umar and Aisha, may God be pleased with them, said. Al-Sha’bi, Ata’, and Tawus said: There is nothing on him. As for the oath of walking to Mecca, he must fulfill it according to Malik and Abu Hanifa, and the expiation for an oath is sufficient according to Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Abu Thawr. Ibn Al-Musayyab and Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: There is nothing on him. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: Most of the scholars in Madinah and elsewhere require expiation for walking to Mecca like the expiation for an oath by God Almighty. This is the opinion of a group of the Companions, the Followers, and the majority of Muslim jurists. Ibn Al-Qasim, his son Abd Al-Samad, issued a fatwa on this, and he mentioned to him that it was the opinion of Al-Layth ibn Sa’d. The well-known opinion of Ibn Al-Qasim is that there is no expiation for walking to Mecca except by walking for those who are able to do so, and this is the opinion of Malik. As for the one who swears to free, he must free the one he swore to free according to Malik. Al-Shafi’i and others. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas and Aisha that he should make expiation for an oath and is not required to free a slave. Ata’ said: He should give something in charity. Al-Mahdawi said: All scholars whose words are relied upon agree that divorce is binding on whoever swears an oath and breaks it. Forty-seventh - The Almighty’s saying: And guard your oaths meaning by hastening to do what is required of you in terms of expiation if you break your oath. It was said: meaning by abandoning the oath, because if you do not swear, these obligations will not be imposed on you. Perhaps you will be grateful. The meaning of gratitude and perhaps was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Praise be to God.
5:88: The Almighty’s saying: And eat of what God has provided for you, lawful and good. There is one issue in it: Eating in this verse refers to enjoying eating, drinking, clothing, riding, and the like. Eating was mentioned specifically because it is the greatest goal and the most specific benefit for man. The ruling on eating, drinking, and clothing will come in Al-A’raf, God willing. As for the desire for pleasurable things and the soul’s struggle to seek delicious types, people’s schools of thought regarding enabling the soul to do so differ. Some of them see that diverting the soul from them and subduing it from following its desires is more appropriate for humiliating its leadership and making its stubbornness easy for him. If he gives it what it wants, it becomes a prisoner of its desires and submissive to its submission. It was narrated that Abu Hazim used to pass by fruit and desire it, so he would say: Your appointment is Paradise. Others said: Enabling the soul to enjoy its pleasures is more appropriate because it brings it comfort and activity by realizing its will. Others said: Rather, moderation in that is more appropriate because in giving it that one time and preventing it another time, preventing it another time, there is a combination of the two matters. That half is not bad. The meaning of aggression was presented. And the sustenance is in the cow, and praise be to God.
5:90: It contains seventeen issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed is an address to all believers to abandon these things, as they were desires and customs that they were involved in during the Age of Ignorance and they overcame their souls, so they were denied in the souls of many believers. Ibn Atiyyah said: “From this category is the desire to warn with birds, and taking omens in books and the like of what people do today. As for wine, it had not yet been forbidden, and its prohibition was only revealed in the third year after the Battle of Uhud, and the Battle of Uhud was in Shawwal in the third year of the Hijra, and its derivation was presented. As for gambling, the discussion of it has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. As for the idols, it was said: They are the statues.” It was said that they are dice and chess, and their explanation comes in Surat Yunus when God Almighty says: So what is there after the truth except error? (Yunus 10:32). As for the arrows, they are the lots, and the discussion of them has already been mentioned at the beginning of the Surah. It is said: They were in the house with the custodians of the house and the servants of the idols. A man would come if he wanted something and take something from them. If my Lord had commanded me, he would go out to fulfill his need, whether he liked it or not. The second - the prohibition of alcohol was gradual and due to many incidents, as they were fond of drinking it, and the first thing that was revealed about it was: “They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, ‘In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people.’” (al-Baqarah 2:219), meaning in their trade. When this verse was revealed, some people abandoned it and said: We have no need for something that contains great sin. Some people did not abandon it and said: We take its benefit and leave its sin. So this verse was revealed: Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated. (An-Nisa’: 42), so some people abandoned it and said: We have no need for something that distracts us from prayer. Some people drank it at times other than prayer times, until the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, indeed, wine and gambling and idols and divining arrows are but defilement. So it became forbidden because of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, as he mentioned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the faults of wine and what befalls people because of it, and he supplicated to God to prohibit it and said: O God, make wine clear to us in a satisfactory manner. So these verses were revealed, and Umar said: We have finished, we have finished, and it has already passed in Al-Baqarah and An-Nisa. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated. And “They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, “In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people.” This was abrogated by what is in al-Ma’idah 5:Indeed, wine, gambling, and idolatry are only forbidden. And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, he said: It was revealed in verses of the Qur’an, in which he said: “And I came upon a group of the Ansar, and they said: Come, let us feed you and give you wine to drink. This was before wine was forbidden.” He said: So I came to them in a garden, and there was a roasted camel’s head with them and a wineskin of wine. He said: So I ate and drank with them. He said: “So I mentioned the Ansar and the Muhajireen to them, and I said: The Muhajireen are better than the Ansar.” He said: “So a man took hold of a camel’s jawbone and hit me with it, wounding my nose. In another narration, he split it open. Sa’d’s nose was split open. So I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him, and God Almighty revealed about himself, meaning himself, the matter of wine: “Indeed, wine, gambling, idolatry, and divining arrows are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid them.” Third: These hadiths indicate that drinking alcohol was at that time permissible, practiced and known among them to the point that it was not denounced or changed, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, approved of it. There is no disagreement about this. It is indicated by the verse of An-Nisa’ Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated based on what was mentioned above. Was it permissible for them to drink the amount that would intoxicate? The hadith of Hamza clearly states that when he cut open the flanks of the two she-camels of Ali, may God be pleased with them both, their humps were removed, so Ali informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so Hamza came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said harsh words that contradicted what he should have said in terms of respecting, honoring and punishing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This indicates that Hamza had gone away from him with something that would intoxicate. Therefore, the narrator said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew that he was drunk. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not denounce Hamza or reprimand him, neither while he was drunk nor after that. Rather, he went back to what Hamza had said, Are you not slaves to Abu Ali? and he left him. This is contrary to what the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence said and narrated, for they said: Drunkenness is forbidden in every religion, because the religions are for the benefit of the servants, not for their harm. The origin of benefit is the mind, just as the origin of harm is its loss. Therefore, everything that removes it or distorts it must be prevented. However, the hadith of Hamza is possible, that he did not intend to drink it to get drunk, but he rushed into it and it overcame him, and God knows best. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: Abomination. Ibn Abbas said about this verse: Abomination is wrath. And filth, excrement, and dirt may be called Abomination. And Abomination with the letter Z is punishment and nothing else, and Rikas is nothing else, and Abomination is said for two things, and the meaning of from the work of Satan is by his incitement to it and its beautification. And it was said that it is the one who worked on the principles of these matters himself until he followed his example in them. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: So avoid it means that you should distance it and make it a side, so God Almighty commanded to avoid these matters, and it was coupled with the imperative form with the texts of the hadiths and the consensus of the nation, so avoidance occurred in the direction of prohibition, so with this alcohol was prohibited and there is no disagreement among the scholars of the Muslims that Surat Al-Ma’idah was revealed with the prohibition of alcohol, and it is Medinan and one of the last to be revealed, and the prohibition of dead meat, blood and pork was mentioned in the Almighty’s saying: Say, I do not find (al-An’am 6:145) and other verses as report, and regarding alcohol there is a prohibition and a warning, which is the strongest and most emphatic prohibition. Ibn Abbas narrated that when the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, walked to each other and said, Alcohol is prohibited, and it has been made equal to thanks, meaning that he coupled it with slaughtering for idols, and that is a condition, then he linked it that you may succeed, so he linked success to the command, and that indicates the emphasis of the obligation, and God is All-Knowing. Sixth - The majority understood from the prohibition of alcohol, and the filthiness of the Shari’ah towards it, and the calling of filth upon it and the command to avoid it the ruling of its impurity, and Rabia, Al-Layth bin Sa’d, Al-Muzani, the companion of Al-Shafi’i, and some of the later people of Baghdad and Al-Qarawiyyin disagreed with them in that, and they saw that it was pure and that what was forbidden was only drinking it. Sa’id bin Al-Haddad Al-Qarawi demonstrated its purity by pouring it in the streets of Madinah. He said: If it were impure, the Companions, may God be pleased with them, would not have done that, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have done it, just as he forbade relieving oneself in the streets. The answer is that the Companions did that because they did not have a water closet or wells in which to pour it, since most of their circumstances were that they did not have a toilet in their homes. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: They were disgusted by taking a toilet in their homes, and transporting it outside the city was costly and difficult, and it would require delaying what was required immediately. Also, it is possible to avoid it, since the streets of Madinah were wide and the alcohol was not so abundant that it would become a river that covered the entire road, rather it only flowed. In a few places where it can be avoided - this - with what is obtained from that of the benefit of the fame of spilling it in the streets of the city, to spread the work according to the requirement of its prohibition of its destruction and that it is not beneficial and people followed and agreed on that and God knows best. If it is said: Impurity is a legal ruling and there is no text in it and it is not necessary for something to be prohibited to be impure, so how many prohibited things in the law are not impure? We say: The Almighty’s saying: impurity indicates its impurity, because impurity in the language means impurity. Then if we commit ourselves not to rule with a ruling unless we find a text in it, the law would be suspended, because the texts in it are few, so what text is there on the impurity of urine, excrement, blood, dead bodies and other than that? Rather, they are the apparent meanings, generalities and analogies, and what will come in Surat Al-Hajj will clarify this meaning, God willing. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: So avoid it requires absolute avoidance, which does not benefit from anything in any way, whether by drinking, selling, pickling, treating, or anything else. This is indicated by the hadiths reported in the chapter. Muslim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “A man presented a wineskin to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a gift. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘Do you know that God has forbidden it?’ He said: ‘No.’ So he whispered to a man, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: ‘What did you whisper to him?’ He said: ‘I ordered him to sell it.’ He said: ‘He who has forbidden drinking it has forbidden selling it.’ He opened the wineskin until what was in it was gone.’” This is a hadith that indicates what we have mentioned, because if there had been a permissible benefit in it, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have made it clear, as he said about the dead sheep. Why don’t you take its hide, tan it, and benefit from it? Hadith. Eighth - Muslims have agreed that it is forbidden to sell alcohol and blood, and this is evidence of the prohibition of selling excrement, all impurities, and what is not permissible to eat. And this - and God knows best - is that Malik disliked the sale of animal dung, and Ibn al-Qasim permitted it because of the benefit in it. The analogy is what Malik said, and it is the Shafi’i school of thought, and this hadith is evidence of the authenticity of that. Ninth - The majority of jurists have held that it is not permissible for anyone to ferment wine. If it were permissible to ferment it, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have allowed a man to open the wineskin until what was in it was gone, because vinegar is something that he has forbidden to waste money. No one says that someone who pours wine on a Muslim has lost his money. Uthman ibn Abi al-Aas poured out wine for an orphan, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked for permission to ferment it, so he said: No, and he forbade it. A group of scholars from the people of hadeeth and opinion held this view, and Sahnoon ibn Saeed leaned towards it. Others said: There is nothing wrong with fermenting wine, and there is nothing wrong with eating what has been fermented from it by processing it with a human being or otherwise. This is the view of al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, al-Layth ibn Sa’d, and the Kufians. Abu Hanifa said: If musk and salt are added to it and it becomes jam and changes from the state of wine, it is permissible. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan disagreed with him regarding jam and said: Wine should not be processed without converting it to vinegar alone. Abu Omar said: The Iraqis cited Abu al-Darda’ as evidence for fermenting wine, and he sees on the authority of Abu Idris al-Khawlani on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ from a source that is not strong that he used to eat jam from it and say: The sun and salt tanned it. Umar ibn al-Khattab and Uthman ibn Abi al-Aas disagreed with him regarding fermenting wine, and there is no argument in anyone’s opinion with the Sunnah. And with God is success. It may be possible that the prohibition of fermenting it was at the beginning of Islam when its prohibition was revealed. So that it would not be kept for a long time due to the recent drinking of it, with the intention of breaking the habit of doing so. If that is the case, then there is nothing in the prohibition of letting it go at that time and the command to pour it out that prevents eating it if it is pickled. Ashhab narrated on the authority of Malik, who said: If a Christian makes wine, there is nothing wrong with eating it, and likewise if a Muslim makes wine and asks God for forgiveness. This narration was mentioned by Ibn Abd al-Hakam in his book, and what Malik said in the narration of Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn Wahb is correct, that it is not permissible for a Muslim to treat wine until he turns it into vinegar, nor to sell it, but to pour it out. Tenth - There is no difference of opinion between Malik and his companions that if wine has become vinegar by itself, then eating that vinegar is permissible. This is the opinion of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Qubaysah ibn Shihab, Rabi’ah, and one of the two opinions of al-Shafi’i, and it is the conclusion of his school of thought according to most of his companions. Eleventh - Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad mentioned that it can be owned, and he tended to believe that it can remove choking and extinguish a fire. This is a transmission that is not known to Malik, but rather this is based on the opinion of those who see it as pure. If it were permissible to own it, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have ordered it to be poured out. Also, ownership is a type of benefit and is nullified by pouring it out, praise be to God. Twelfth - This verse indicates the prohibition of playing dice and chess, whether gambling or not, because when God Almighty prohibited the report, He informed of the meaning in it, saying: O you who believe, indeed, intoxicants and gambling 12:10. Then He said: Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred 12:10. So every amusement that invites a few to many and causes enmity and hatred between those devoted to it and turns people away from the remembrance of God and from prayer is like drinking alcohol and requires that it be prohibited like it. If it is said: Drinking alcohol causes intoxication, so it is not possible to pray with it, and there is no such meaning in playing dice and chess, it is said to him: God Almighty has combined intoxicants and gambling in prohibition and described them both as causing enmity and hatred between people, and turning people away from the remembrance of God and from prayer. It is known that if alcohol intoxicates, then gambling does not intoxicate. Then God did not see their difference in that preventing them from being equal in prohibition because of the meanings they share. Also, a small amount of alcohol does not intoxicate, just as playing dice and chess does. It does not intoxicate and then it was forbidden like many things. It is not denied that playing dice and chess is forbidden like wine, even if it does not intoxicate. Also, starting to play causes heedlessness, so that heedlessness that takes over the heart takes the place of intoxication. If wine was only forbidden because it intoxicates and distracts from prayer by intoxication, then playing dice and chess should be forbidden because it causes heedlessness and distraction and thus distracts from prayer. And God knows best. Thirteenth - The narrator is correct in that he had not been informed of the abrogator, and he was adhering to the previously mentioned permissibility, so this was evidence that the ruling is not lifted by the existence of the abrogator - as some of the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence say - but rather by its reaching him, as indicated by this hadith, which is correct, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not rebuke him, but rather explained the ruling to him, and because he was addressed to act according to the first one, such that if he left it, he would have disobeyed without dispute, even though the abrogator had already existed. This is what happened to the people of Quba, when they used to pray toward Jerusalem until the one who came to them informed them of the abrogator, so they turned toward the Kaaba. It was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, and Al-Hamdulillah, and it was mentioned in it about wine, its derivation, and gambling. It was mentioned at the beginning of this Surah about idols and arrows, and Al-Hamdulillah.
5:91: Fourteenth - The Almighty's saying: Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred through wine and gambling verse. God Almighty informed His servants that Satan only wants to cause enmity and hatred between us because of wine and other things, so He warned us against it and forbade us from it. It was narrated that two tribes of the Ansar drank wine and became intoxicated, so some of them sent others, and when they recovered, some of them saw on the faces of others the effects of what they had done, and they were brothers with no grudges in their hearts. Some of them began to say: If my brother had been merciful to me, he would not have done this to me. So grudges arose between them, so God revealed: Satan only wants to cause between you animosity and hatred verse. Fifteenth - The Almighty’s saying: And it averts you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. He says: If you are drunk, you will not remember God and you will not pray, and if you pray, it will confuse you as it did with Ali. It was narrated: with Abd al-Rahman as mentioned previously in An-Nisa. Ubaydullah bin Umar said: Al-Qasim bin Muhammad was asked about chess, is it gambling? And about backgammon, is it gambling? He said: Everything that averts from the remembrance of God and from prayer is gambling. Abu Ubayd said: He interpreted the Almighty’s saying: And it averts you from the remembrance of God and from prayer. Sixteenth - The Almighty’s saying: Will you then desist? When Omar, may God be pleased with him, knew that this was a severe threat in addition to the meaning of desist, he said: We have desisted. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his crier to proclaim in the streets of Medina: Behold, wine has been forbidden. So the jugs were broken, and the wine was poured out until it flowed in the streets of Medina.
5:92: Seventeenth - The Almighty’s saying: And obey God and obey the Messenger and beware is an emphasis on the prohibition and a severe threat and compliance with the command. Refrain from what is prohibited and it is good to connect and obey God since the previous statement meant stop and and obey was repeated in mentioning the Messenger as an emphasis. Then He warned against disobeying the command and threatened whoever turned away with the punishment of the Hereafter, so He said: But if you turn away meaning you disobeyed, upon Our Messenger is only the clear notification in prohibiting what he was commanded to prohibit, and it is upon the sender to punish or confirm according to what is disobeyed or obeyed.
5:93: It contains nine issues: First: Ibn Abbas, Al-Bara’ bin Azib, and Anas bin Malik said that when the prohibition of alcohol was revealed, some of the Companions said: What about those among us who died while drinking it and gambling - and the like - so the verse was revealed. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Anas who said: I was the cupbearer of the people in the house of Abu Talha, and the prohibition of alcohol was revealed. He ordered a crier to call out. Abu Talha said: Go out and see what this voice is. He said: So I went out and said: This is a crier calling out: Alcohol has been prohibited. He said: Go and pour it out - and alcohol was from the Fadikh. He said: It flowed from the streets of Madinah. Some of the people said: People were killed while it was in their stomachs. Then God Almighty revealed: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten Al-Madinah 13:10. The second - This verse and this hadith are similar to their question about someone who died facing the first Qiblah, so the verse was revealed: And God would never let your faith go to waste (al-Baqarah 2:143). And whoever does what is permissible for him until he dies doing it, there is nothing for him or against him, neither sin nor blame nor reward nor praise, because what is permissible is equal between the two sides in relation to the Shari’ah. Based on this, he should not have feared or asked about the condition of someone who died while alcohol was in his stomach at the time when it was permissible. Either the speaker was unaware of the evidence of permissibility and it did not occur to him, or because of his overwhelming fear of God the Most High and his compassion for his believing brothers, he imagined that he would be held accountable and punished for drinking the aforementioned alcohol, so God removed that illusion by saying: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds for what they have eaten (al-Baqarah 2:143). Third: This hadith about the revelation of the verse contains clear evidence that if date wine intoxicates, it is wine. This is a text and it is not permissible to object to it because the Companions, may God have mercy on them, were the people of the language and they understood that their drink was wine, since they had no other drink at that time in Medina. Al-Hakami said: We have wine, not the wine of the vineyard, but the product of the tall trees. Generous ones in the sky have gone long and their fruits have been lost to the hands of the criminals. And the clear evidence for that is what Al-Nasa’i narrated: Al-Qasim bin Zakariya told us, Ubaidullah bin Shaiban told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muharrib bin Dithar, on the authority of Jabir, “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Raisins and dates are wine.” And it was proven by authentic transmission that Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him - and his knowledge of the language and the Sharia is sufficient for you - gave a sermon on the pulpit of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O people, the prohibition of wine was revealed on the day it was revealed, and it is made of five things: grapes, dates, honey, wheat, and barley. Wine is that which intoxicates the mind, and this is the clearest meaning of wine. Omar gave a sermon about it in Medina on the pulpit in the presence of a group of the Companions, who were the people of the language, and they did not understand from wine except what we mentioned. If this is proven, the doctrine of Abu Hanifa and the Kufians who say that wine is only made from grapes is invalidated, and that which is made from something other than grapes is not called wine and does not include the name wine, but is called wine. The poet said: I left wine to the wine people and became an ally to those who criticize it A drink that defiles the young man's honor and opens the doors to evil. Fourth - Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Mazari said: The majority of scholars from the Salaf and others have held that drinking anything that intoxicates is forbidden, whether it is a little or a lot, raw or cooked, and there is no difference between that extracted from grapes or something else. Whoever drinks something of that is subject to a hadd punishment. As for that extracted from raw grapes that intoxicates, it is that which there is consensus on the prohibition of a little or a lot of it, even a drop of it. As for what is other than that, the majority are against it. The Kufians disagreed on the little of what he mentioned, which is that which does not reach intoxication, and on the cooked thing extracted from grapes. Some people from Basra went to limiting the prohibition to grape juice and the infusion of raw raisins. As for that which is cooked from them, and the raw and cooked thing from other than them, it is permissible as long as intoxication does not occur. Abu Hanifa went to limiting the prohibition to that which is pressed from the fruits of palm trees and grapes in detail. He believes that the juice of grapes is forbidden in a little or a lot unless it is cooked until it is reduced by a third, and that the infusion of raisins and dates is permissible in their cooked form even if people touch it a little without considering the hadd punishment. As for the raw of it, It is forbidden, but even though he forbade it, it does not require a punishment. All of this is as long as intoxication does not occur. If intoxication occurs, then everyone is equal. Our Sheikh, the jurist Imam Abu al-Abbas Ahmad, may God be pleased with him, said: I am amazed at those who disagree on this issue, for they said: A small amount of wine squeezed from grapes is forbidden like a large amount, and this is agreed upon. So if it is said to them: Why is a small amount of wine forbidden, and it is not a matter of reason? It must be said: Because it is an invitation to much or to worship, then it is said to them: Everything that you have estimated in a small amount of wine is the same as in a small amount of wine, so it is also forbidden, since there is no difference between them except for the mere name if that is accepted. And this analogy is the highest type of analogy, because the branch in it is equal to the root in all its descriptions. This is like what he says in the analogy of the nation to the slave in the spread of emancipation. Then the wonder of Abu Hanifa and his companions, may God have mercy on them, for they delve into analogy and give it precedence over individual reports, and despite that they have abandoned this clear analogy supported by the Book and the Sunnah and the consensus of the nation’s leaders for hadiths, none of which are authentic according to what the hadith scholars have explained their causes in their books, and there is nothing of it in the Sahihs, and the completion of this issue will come in Surat An-Nahl, God willing. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying, They tasted. The origin of this word is in eating. It is said: he tasted food and drank a drink, but it may be used in this case as an exaggeration, and it is said: I did not eat bread, nor water, nor sleep. The poet said: Ostriches with squinting cheeks, do not eat sleep except fasting The statement about the cow has been presented in the Almighty’s saying: And whoever does not feed him (al-Baqarah 2:249) sufficiently. Sixth: Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: This verse includes the permissible and desires and the benefit from every delicious food, drink and sexual intercourse, even if it is exaggerated and its price is prohibitive. This verse is similar to the Almighty’s saying: Do not prohibit the good things which God has made lawful to you and similar to His saying: “Say: Who has prohibited the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?” (al-A’raf
5:94: It contains eight issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: To test you meaning to try you, and the test is the examination. Hunting was one of the livelihoods of the pure Arabs, and it was common among all of them, and was used a lot, so God tested them with it along with the ihram and the sanctuary, just as He tested the Children of Israel in not transgressing on the Sabbath. It was said: It was revealed in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah, some of the people entered ihram with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of them did not, so if there was game presented, their conditions and actions differed regarding it and its rulings were unclear to them, so God revealed this verse explaining the rulings of their conditions and actions and the prohibitions of their Hajj and Umrah. The second - The scholars differed about who is addressed in this verse in two opinions: The first - that they are those who are in a state of ihram, said Malik. The second - that they are those who are in a state of ihram, said Ibn Abbas. It was related to the Almighty’s saying, That they may test you, for it is a duty, for the duty of abstention by which the test is achieved is with the state of ihram. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is not necessary, for the duty is achieved in the state of ihram by what is stipulated for it from matters of hunting and what is prescribed for it from the description of how to hunt. The correct view is that the address in the verse is to all people, their state of ihram and their state of ihram, because the Almighty said, That God may test you, meaning that He will charge you, and the duty is all a test, even if it varies in quantity and scarcity and varies in weakness and severity. Third: The Almighty’s saying: with some of the game means some of the game, so from is for partiality, which is the game of the land in particular, and it does not include all game, as stated by Al-Tabari and others. And by game he meant the hunted thing, because of His saying: your hands reach it. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: Your hands and spears may reach it is a clarification of the ruling on small and large game. Ibn Waththab and Al-Nakha’i read yanalah with a dotted ya’ from below. Mujahid said: The hands reach the chicks and eggs and what cannot escape, and the spears reach the large game. Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: God Almighty said: O you who have believed, God will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and spears may reach. Everything that a person reaches with his hand or spear or with some of his weapons and kills it is game, as God Almighty said. Fifth: God Almighty mentioned the hands specifically because they are the most important tool in hunting, and in them are included the birds of prey, ropes, and what is made by hand of traps and nets. He mentioned the spears specifically because they are the most important thing with which the prey is wounded, and in them are included the arrow and the like. The discussion of what is hunted with from birds of prey and arrows has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah in a sufficient manner, and praise be to God. Sixth: What falls into a trap or snare belongs to its owner. If someone forced the prey to it, and if it were not for it, he would not have been able to take it, then its owner has a partner in it. What falls into the trap set up on the mountain of flies and bees is like a trap or snare, and the doves of the towers are returned to their owners if I am able to do so. The same applies to the bees of the trap. It was narrated from Malik, and some of his companions said: It is not upon the one who has the doves or bees to return them. If the prey forced the dog to come and enters someone’s house or home, then it belongs to the hunter who sent the dogs, not the owner of the house. If it enters the house without the dogs forcing it, then it belongs to the owner of the house. Seventh: Some people have argued that the catch is for the taker, not the one who provoked it, based on this verse, because the one who provoked it has not yet reached anything with his hand or spear, which is the opinion of Abu Hanifa. Eighth - Malik disliked hunting the People of the Book but did not forbid it because of the Almighty’s saying: Your hands and spears will reach it, meaning the People of the Book, because the Almighty said at the beginning of the verse: O you who believe, so the People of the Book were excluded from them. The majority of scholars disagreed with him because the Almighty said: And the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and it is, according to them, like their slaughtered animals. Our scholars responded that the verse only included eating their food, and hunting is another matter, so it does not fall under the generality of food, nor does it include its absolute wording. I said: This is based on the fact that hunting is not permissible for them, so it is not part of their food, so this obligation is dropped. However, if it is permissible for them in their religion, then we are obligated to eat it, as the word includes it, because it is part of their food, and God knows best.
5:95: It contains thirty issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed. This is a general address to every Muslim, male or female, and this prohibition is the test mentioned in the Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, God will surely test you with something of the game. The verse. It was narrated that Abu Al-Yusr - whose name was Amr bin Malik Al-Ansari - was in a state of ihram in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah for an Umrah, and he killed a wild donkey, so the verse was revealed about him: Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. Second - God Almighty says: Do not kill game. Killing is any action that destroys the soul. It has many types: including slaughtering, slaughtering, strangling, crushing, and the like. God Almighty has forbidden the pilgrim in the state of ihram to hunt any action that destroys the soul. Third: Whoever kills or slaughters game and eats from it, he must pay one penalty for killing it without eating it. This is what Al-Shafi’i said. Abu Hanifa said: He must pay the penalty for what he ate, meaning its value. His two companions disagreed with him and said: He does not have to do anything except seek forgiveness because he ate the dead animal as if he ate another dead animal. Therefore, if another pilgrim eats it, he is only required to seek forgiveness. Abu Hanifa’s argument is that he ate something forbidden during his ihram, because killing it was one of the forbidden things during ihram. It is known that the purpose of killing is eating, so if what is used to reach the purpose - the forbidden thing during his ihram - requires a penalty, then what is the purpose is more appropriate. Fourth: It is not permissible for a person in ihram to slaughter game, because God the Almighty has forbidden the person in ihram from killing it, and Abu Hanifa said the same. Al-Shafi’i said: The person in ihram slaughters game as a ritual slaughter, and he is connected to the fact that he slaughtered the first part of his family, which is the Muslim, added to its place, which is the livestock, so he conveyed his purpose of making it permissible to eat it. Its origin is slaughtering the permissible. We said: Your saying that he slaughtered the first part of his family means that the person in ihram is not qualified to slaughter game, because eligibility is not derived rationally, but rather it is derived by the Shari’ah, which is by his permission to slaughter or by denying it, which is by his prohibition of slaughtering. The person in ihram is forbidden from slaughtering game, because God the Almighty has forbidden the person in ihram to slaughter game, so eligibility is negated by the prohibition. Your saying conveyed his purpose, as we have agreed that if the person in ihram slaughters game, it is not permissible for him to eat it, and others eat from it, according to you. So if the slaughter does not make it permissible for the slaughterer, then it is more appropriate that it does not make it permissible for others, because the branch is subordinate to the root in its rulings, so it is not valid to prove for it what is not proven for its root. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: Hunting is a verbal noun that is treated like nouns, so it refers to the hunted animal. The word hunting here is general for all land and sea hunting, until the Almighty’s saying: And hunting of land is forbidden to you as long as you are in a state of ihram, so He permitted hunting of the sea with absolute permission, as will be explained in the verse after this, God willing. Sixth: The scholars differed regarding the exclusion of wild animals from the game of the land and their specification from it. Malik said: Everything that is not considered wild animals, such as the cat, the fox, the hyena, and the like, the pilgrim should not kill it, and if he kills it, he must pay the blood money. He said: I do not think that the pilgrim should kill young wolves, but if he kills them, he must pay the blood money, and they are like the young crows. There is nothing wrong with killing everything that is considered to be a common enemy of people, such as the lion, the wolf, the tiger, and the leopard. Likewise, there is nothing wrong with him killing snakes, scorpions, mice, crows, and kites. Ismail said: This is because of the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Five wicked animals that are to be killed in the sanctuary and outside the sanctuary. The hadith says: They are wicked and described them by their actions because the wicked one does wickedness and the young ones do not do anything. He described the ram as rabid and its offspring are not rabid and are not included in this description. Judge Ismail said: The rabid dog is one of those that greatly harm people. He said: And from that is the snake and the Arabs because they are feared, and likewise the kite and the crow because they snatch meat from people’s hands. Ibn Bakir said: Permission was given to kill the scorpion because it has a fever, and in the case of the mouse because it nibbles the water-skin and the shoe on which the traveler stands, and in the case of the crow because it lands on the back and burrows for its meat. It was narrated from Malik that he said: The crow and the kite are not to be killed unless they cause harm. Judge Ismail said: There is disagreement about the wasp, some of them likened it to the snake and the scorpion and said: Were it not that the wasp does not initiate it would be harsher towards people than the snake and the scorpion, but it does not have the hostility in its nature as the snake and the scorpion, but the wasp protects itself if it is harmed. He said: So if the wasp is exposed If someone defends himself from it, he is not liable for killing it. It was proven from Umar ibn al-Khattab that killing a wasp is permissible. Malik said: He should feed its killer something. Malik also said about someone who kills a flea, fly, ant, or the like. The people of opinion said: There is nothing for fighting all of these. Abu Hanifa said: The pilgrim is not to kill wild animals except the rabid dog and the wolf in particular, whether they are the first to kill him or he initiated them. If he kills another wild animal, he must pay the ransom. He said: If another wild animal initiates it and kills it, there is nothing on him. He said: There is nothing on him for killing a snake, a crow, or a kite. This is the summary of what Abu Hanifa and his companions said, except for Zafar. Al-Awza’i, al-Thawri, and al-Hasan said the same. They argued that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specified specific animals and permitted the pilgrim to kill them because of their harm. There is no reason to add to them unless they agree on something and it falls under their meaning. I said: It is strange that Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, attributes dirt to land on the grounds of all, and does not attribute wild beasts to dogs on the grounds of immorality and hamstringing, as Malik and Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on them, did. Zafar bin Al-Hudhayl said: Only the wolf alone should be killed, and whoever kills another one while in a state of ihram must pay a ransom, whether he initiated it or not, because it is dumb, so his action is wasted. This is a rejection of the hadith and a contradiction to it. Al-Shafi’i said: Everything whose meat is not eaten, the person in a state of ihram may kill it, and the small and large ones are the same, except for the hyena, which is a cross between the wolf and the hyena. He said: There is nothing in the case of the vulture, beetles, monkeys, baboons, and anything whose meat is not eaten, because this is not from the game, according to the Almighty’s saying: And forbidden to you is the game of land as long as you are in a state of ihram. This indicates that the game that was forbidden to them was what was permissible for them before the state of ihram. Al-Muzani and Al-Rabi’ reported this sentence from him. If it is said: Why is a louse ransomed when it harms and is not eaten? It was said to him: It is not permissible to redeem except for what is permissible to redeem hair and nails and wearing what is not permissible to wear, because in removing the louse, it is removing harm from himself if it is on his head and beard, so it is as if he removed some of his hair. But if it appears and is killed, then it does not cause harm. The statement of Abu Thawr in this matter is like the statement of Al-Shafi’i, as Abu Omar said. Seventh - The Imams narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Five types of animals that a pilgrim is not obliged to kill: the wing of a crow, the kite, the scorpion, the mouse, the dog, and the rabid bird. The wording is from Al-Bukhari, and Ahmad and Ishaq said the same. In the book of Muslim, on the authority of Aisha, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Five types of animals are to be killed in the sacred precincts and outside of it: the snake, the speckled crow, the mouse, the rabid dog, and the kite. A group of scholars said the same. They said: Only the speckled crow is to be killed, because it is an absolute restriction. In the book of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And the crow throws but does not kill it. And this is what Mujahid and the majority of scholars said, according to the hadith of Ibn Umar, and God knows best. And according to Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi: And the wild beast. And this is an indication of the reason: Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: And you are in a state of ihram is general for both types of men and women, free and slaves. It is said: a man is in a state of ihram and a woman is in a state of ihram, and the plural of that is in a state of ihram like their saying: qadhal and qadhal. A man who has entered the sanctuary is in a state of ihram, just as it is said: ashal entered the plain. This expression includes time, place, and the state of ihram by association, not by generality. It is said: a man is in a state of ihram if he has entered during the sacred months or in the sanctuary or is in a state of ihram, except that the prohibition of time is by consensus no longer considered, and the prohibition of place remains in the state of ihram according to the original obligation, as Ibn al-Arabi said. Ninth: The sanctity of a place is two sanctities: the sanctity of Medina and the sanctity of Mecca. Al-Shafi’i added that Taif is not permissible when there is a cut in it, nor is it permissible to hunt its game. Whoever does that, there is no penalty for him. As for the sanctity of Medina, it is not permissible for anyone to hunt in it, nor to cut trees, like the sanctity of Mecca. If he does that, he has sinned, and there is no penalty for him according to Malik, Al-Shafi’i, and their companions. Ibn Abi Tha’lab said: He is subject to penalty. Sa’d said: His penalty is to take his spoils. It was narrated from Al-Shafi’i. Abu Hanifa said: Hunting in Medina is not forbidden, nor is cutting its trees. Some of those who followed his school of thought provided evidence for this with the hadith of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever you find hunting within the boundaries of the city or cutting down its trees, take his spoils.” And Saad took the spoils of whoever did that. He said: The jurists agreed that the spoils of whoever hunts in Medina are not to be taken, so this indicates that it was abrogated. Al-Tahawi also provided evidence for them with the hadith of Anas: What did the bird do? He did not deny its hunting and its capture. All of this is without proof. As for the first hadith, it is not strong. Even if it was authentic, there would not have been any abrogation of taking the spoils that would cancel out what was authentic about the prohibition of the city. How many people in ihram do not have a punishment in this world? As for the second hadith, it is permissible for hunting to be outside the sanctuary. Likewise, the hadith of Aisha: The Messenger of God had a wild animal. Whenever it went out, it would play, run, and advance and retreat. When it saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it would lie down and not squirm, afraid to harm him. Our evidence for them is what Malik narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab, “that Abu Hurairah said: If you saw gazelles grazing in Madinah, you would not frighten them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whatever is between them and their homes is sacred.” So Abu Hurairah’s statement, I would not frighten them, is evidence that it is not permissible to frighten game in the sanctuary of Madinah, just as it is not permissible to frighten it in the sanctuary of Mecca. Likewise, Zaid bin Thabit snatched a bird from the hand of Shurahbil bin Sa’d, who had hunted it in Madinah. This is evidence that the Companions understood the meaning of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in forbidding game in Madinah, so they did not permit hunting there or owning what was hunted. Ibn Abi Dhi’b related: “His statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Sahih: O God, Abraham made Mecca sacred, and I make Medina sacred just as he made Mecca sacred, and the same is with him. He shall not be alone in its open spaces, nor shall he cut its trees, nor shall he scare away its game. And because he made it sacred, he prohibited hunting there, so the penalty is attached to it just as he made Mecca sacred. Judge Abdul Wahhab said: This is a statement that I find more reasonable in our principles, especially since Medina is better than Mecca, according to our companions, and prayer in it is better than prayer in the Sacred Mosque. And from the evidence of Malik and Al-Shafi’i that he shall not be judged with a penalty or take spoils, according to the well-known statement of Al-Shafi’i - the generality of his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Sahih: The city is a sanctuary between ‘Ayr and Thawr. Whoever commits an innovation therein or shelters an innovator, then upon him is the curse of God, the angels, and all of mankind. God will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any ransom or compensation.” So he sent the severe threat and did not mention expiation. As for what was mentioned about Sa’d, that is a doctrine of his that is specific to him, as it was narrated from him in the Sahih: That he rode to his palace in Al-‘Uqayq, and he found a slave cutting down a tree - or striking it - and robbed him. When Sa’d returned, the slave’s family came to him and spoke to him about returning to their slave or to them what he had taken from their slave. He said: God forbid that I should return something that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave me as a gift, and he refused to return it to them. So his saying: We gave it to me as a gift is clearly specific, and God knows best. Tenth - The Almighty’s saying: And whoever among you kills him intentionally God the Almighty mentioned the intentional one and did not mention the mistaken or the forgetful one. The intentional one here is the one who intends something while knowing that he is in ihram. The mistaken one is the one who intends something and hits the game. The forgetful one is the one who intentionally hunts and does not remember his ihram. The scholars differed on that in five statements: The first - what Al-Daraqutni attributed to Ibn Abbas, who said: The expiation is only for the deliberate one, and they only made it more severe in the case of the mistake so that it would not be repeated. The second - that his saying intentionally was based on the most common, so the rare one was included in it, like the principles of the Sharia. The third - that there is nothing on the mistaken or the forgetful one. Al-Tabari and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said this in one of his two narrations. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Saeed ibn Jubayr. Tawus and Abu Thawr said this, and it is the statement of Dawud. Ahmad related that he said: When God the Almighty singled out the intentional one for mention, it indicated that others are different from him. He added by saying: The basic principle is the innocence of the conscience, so whoever claims that it is occupied, then the evidence is upon him. The fourth - that he is judged in the case of deliberate, mistaken, and forgetful. Ibn Abbas said this and it was narrated on the authority of Umar and Tawus. And Al-Hasan, Ibrahim, Al-Zuhri, and Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, and their companions said the same. Al-Zuhri said: The penalty is obligatory for intentional killing according to the Qur’an, and for mistake and forgetfulness according to the Sunnah. Ibn Al-Arabi said: If he meant by the Sunnah the reports that were reported from Ibn Abbas and Umar, then they are excellent and what a good example they are. The fifth: That he kills him intentionally for killing him while forgetting his ihram - and this is the saying of Mujahid - because God Almighty said after that: And whoever returns, God will take vengeance on him. He said: If he had remembered his ihram, then the punishment would have been obligatory for him the first time. He said: This indicates that he meant intentionally for killing him while forgetting his ihram. Mujahid said: If he remembered his ihram, then he has become permissible and has no Hajj because he committed a forbidden act of his ihram, so it is invalid for him, just as if he spoke during the prayer or broke his ablution in it. He said: And whoever made a mistake, that is what suffices him. Our evidence for Mujahid is that God Almighty obligated the penalty and did not mention corruption, and there is no difference between remembering the ihram or forgetting it, and it is not correct to consider Hajj with prayer because they are different. It has been narrated On his authority, he said that there is no judgment against him for killing it intentionally, and he seeks forgiveness from God, and his argument is complete. Ibn Zayd said the same, and we were guided to Dawud, “that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the hyena, and he said: It is game, and he included in it if the pilgrim kills it a ram, and he did not say intentionally or by mistake. Ibn Bakir, one of our scholars, said: His Almighty’s statement: intentionally, did not mean to overlook the mistake, but rather he meant intentionally to clarify that he is not like the son of Adam, for whom killing intentionally is not an expiation, and that hunting is an expiation, and he did not mean to drop the penalty for killing by mistake, and God knows best. Eleventh - If he kills it while in a state of ihram, he is to be punished every time he kills it, according to the opinion of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa and others, based on the statement of God the Most High: “O you who believe! Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. And whoever among you kills it intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from sacrificial animals.” So the prohibition is permanent and continues as long as he is in a state of ihram, so whenever he kills it, the penalty is binding on him for that reason. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: He is not to be punished twice in Islam, and he is not to be punished except once. If he returns a second time, he is not to be punished, and it is said to him: May God take revenge on you, based on the statement of God the Most High: And whoever returns, God will take revenge on him. This is what Al-Hasan, Ibrahim, Mujahid, Shuraih said, and our evidence for them is what we mentioned about the continuation of the prohibition in a state of ihram, and the address directed at him in the religion of Islam. The twelfth - The Almighty’s saying: Then the recompense is like that which was killed from the livestock. There are four readings for it. The recompense is like by raising the recompense and giving it a tanween, and like is on the description and the report is implied, the meaning is that upon him is a recompense similar that is obligatory or necessary from the livestock. This reading requires that the like is the recompense itself. And the recompense is in the nominative without a tanween, and like by addition, meaning upon him is a recompense similar to that which was killed. And like is an intrusion like your saying I honor the like of you, and you mean I honor you. Similar to this is the Almighty’s saying: Or he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one whose like is in darkness? (al-An’am 6:122) the meaning is like one who is in darkness. And His saying: There is nothing like Him (al-Shura 42:11) meaning there is nothing like Him. And this reading requires that the recompense is not like Him, since the thing is not added to itself. Abu Ali said: Rather, the recompense of the one killed is obligatory upon him, not the recompense like the one killed, and the addition requires the recompense similar, not the recompense of the one killed, and this is the saying of Al-Shafi’i as will come. And his saying: From the blessings is an attribute of the reward according to both readings. Al-Hasan read from the blessings with a sukoon on the ‘ayn, which is a language. Abd al-Rahman read fajaza with the nominative and tanween, like in the accusative. Abu al-Fath said, like is accusative by the reward itself, and the meaning is that it is rewarded like what was killed. Ibn Masoud and al-A’mash read fajazuhu like with the ha’ pronounced. It is possible that it refers to the hunted or to the hunted killer. Thirteenth - The penalty is only due for killing the game, not for taking it itself, as God Almighty said in Al-Mudawwana: Whoever hunts a bird, plucks its feathers, then traps it until its feathers fall out and it flies away. He said: There is no penalty upon him. He said: Likewise, if he cuts off the hand or leg of a game animal or one of its limbs and its life is saved and it is healthy and catches up with the game, then there is nothing upon him. It was said: He is required to pay the penalty in proportion to what he lost. And if he went and did not know what he did, then his penalty is upon him. And if he hunted a bird and did not catch up with the game or left it fearing for it, then he is required to pay.” Fourteenth - What is sufficient from hunting, whether it is an animal or a bird? What is of the animals is sufficient with its counterpart in creation and form. So in the ostrich, it is a camel, and in the wild donkey and wild cow, it is a cow, and in the gazelle, it is a sheep. Al-Shafi’i said: The least that is sufficient according to Malik is what is easy from the sacrifice and it is a sacrifice, such as the young sheep and the two-year-old from other than it. And what is not sufficient for that, then there is feeding or fasting. And in the pigeons, all of them are their value except for the pigeons of Mecca, for in the pigeon there is a sheep, following the predecessors in that. And the dabs, the fawakhat, the turtledove, and the ones with collars are all pigeons. Ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated from Malik that in the pigeons of Mecca and their chicks there is a sheep. He said: And likewise the pigeons of the sanctuary. He said: And in the pigeons of the sanctuary, there is a ruling. Abu Hanifa said: The equivalent is considered in value, not the creation, so the hunted animal is valued in dirhams in the place where it was killed, or in the nearest place to it if the hunted animal is not sold in the place where it was killed. So he buys a sacrifice with that value if he wishes, or he buys food with it and feeds the poor, each poor person half a sa’ of wheat or a sa’ of barley. As for Al-Shafi’i, he sees the like in the livestock, then the like is established, as in the destroyed livestock, the like is established, and the value of the like is taken as the value of the thing, because the like is the origin of the obligation, and this is clear, and upon it the reading of the addition is derived, so the recompense of the like Abu Hanifa argued and said: If the resemblance through creation was considered in the ostrich a camel, and in the donkey a cow, and in the gazelle a sheep, he would not have stopped it on two just men to judge by it, because that is known, so it does not need to be thoughtful and considered, and what is needed is the justness and consideration when the situation is formed in it and the viewpoint is disturbed by it, and our evidence for that is the saying of God Almighty: Then the recompense is like that which was killed from the livestock Al-Akhbar, so the like apparently requires the natural, formal like without meaning, then he said: from the livestock, so he explained the type of the like, then he said: Two just men among you shall judge by it, and this is a pronoun referring to the like of the livestock because it was not mentioned before for anything else, the pronoun refers to it, then he said: A sacrificial animal delivered to the Kaaba, and what is conceivable in the sacrificial animal is like the killed livestock, but as for the value, it is not conceivable that it is a sacrificial animal, nor was it mentioned in the same The verse confirms what we have mentioned, praise be to God. Their statement: If suspicion were to be taken into account, it would not have been limited to two just witnesses. The answer is that taking two just witnesses into account is only required to consider the state of prey, whether small or large, and what has no type or type, and to include what has no text with what has a text. Fifteenth - Whoever enters ihram from Mecca and closes the door of his house on young pigeons and they die, he must pay a sheep for each young pigeon. Malik said: And for small game, the same as for large ones, and this is the opinion of Ata’. And according to Malik, nothing is to be ransomed with a she-goat or a young camel. Malik said: And this is like the blood money, the young and the old are the same in it. And according to him, the value of a monitor lizard and a jerboa is food. And among the people of Medina, there are those who disagree with him regarding small game and regarding the consideration of a young and two-year-old pigeon, and he says according to the opinion of Umar: For a rabbit, a she-goat and for a jerboa, a young camel. Malik narrated it as a narration that ends with him. Abu al-Zubayr narrated on the authority of Jabir on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In the case of a hyena if it is attacked by a pilgrim, it is a ram. In the case of a gazelle, it is a sheep. In the case of a rabbit, it is a goat. In the case of a jerboa, it is a grazing goat. In another chain of transmission, I said to Abu al-Zubayr: What is a goat? He said: The one that has been weaned and has grazed. Al-Daraqutni reported it. Al-Shafi’i said: In the case of an ostrich, it is a camel. In its young lamb, it is a young calf. In the case of a wild donkey, it is a cow. In its young lamb, it is a calf, because God Almighty has ruled that the likeness in creation is equal. Smallness and bigness are different, so the small and big must be considered in it like all other destroyed animals. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is correct and it is the choice of our scholars. They said: If the game were one-eyed, lame, or broken, the like would be according to its description, so that likeness would be achieved, so the one who destroyed the animal would not be required to pay more than what he destroyed. Our evidence is the statement of God Almighty: Then the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed of livestock. He did not distinguish between small and big. His statement: an offering requires what the name offering includes, due to the right of divorce, and that requires a complete offering, and God knows best. Sixteenth - Regarding the eggs of a female camel, the price is one-eighth of a camel according to Malik. Regarding the eggs of a Meccan pigeon, he said, it is one-tenth of the price of a sheep. Ibn al-Qasim said: It does not matter whether there is a chick in it or not, as long as the chick does not cry after being broken. If it does cry, then he must pay the full penalty like the penalty for an adult bird. Ibn al-Mawaz said: By the judgment of two just men. Most scholars hold that the value of the eggs of every bird is due. Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Ka`b ibn Ujrah: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled regarding ostrich eggs that a pilgrim had acquired, equal to their price.” Narrated by Al-Darqutni, and he narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: For every ostrich egg, there is a reward for fasting for a day or feeding a poor person. Seventeenth - As for what has no equivalent, such as birds and elephants, the value of its meat or its equivalent in food is less than what is intended for it from purposes, because what is considered in what has an equivalent is the obligation of its equivalent, and if there is no equivalent, then the killing takes its place, such as usurpation and other things. And because people say - that is, according to two schools of thought - that value is considered in all hunting and is limited to what has no equivalent from the blessings, this includes the consensus on considering value in what has no equivalent. As for the elephant, it was said: In it is a camel from the great camels that have two humps and they are Khurasani camels. So if none of these camels are found, then its value as food is considered, and that is what is required of it. And the work in it is to put the elephant in a mount and look at the end of the mount’s descent into the water, then the elephant is taken out and the food is hastened in the mount until it descends to the point where the elephant descended and this is its equivalent in food. As for looking at its value, then it will have a great price because of its bones and tusks, so the food increases and that is harmful. Eighteenth - The Almighty’s saying: It will be judged by two just men among you. Malik narrated on the authority of Abd al-Malik ibn Qurayb on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin that a man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: “I and a friend of mine raced to a pass and we hit a gazelle while we were merciful. What do you think?” Umar said to a man next to him: Come so that I and you can judge. So they judged me with a goat. But the man turned away saying: “This is the affair of the believers. He cannot judge a gazelle until he calls a man to judge with him.” Umar ibn al-Khattab heard the man’s words, so he called him and asked him: Do you read Surat al-Ma’idah? He said: No. He said: Do you know the man who judged with me? He said: No. Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: If you had told me that you read Surat al-Ma’idah, I would have beaten you severely. Then he said: “The Almighty says in His Book: ‘It will be judged by two just men among you, an offering delivered to the Kaaba.’” This is Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. Nineteenth - If the two arbitrators agree, the ruling is binding. Al-Hasan and Al-Shafi’i said the same, and if they disagree, others should be considered. Muhammad bin Al-Mawaz said: He should not take the higher of their two opinions, because it was done without arbitration. Likewise, he should not move from the moral equivalent if they ruled on it to food because it is a binding order. Ibn Sha’ban said: Ibn Al-Qasim said: If he ordered them to rule on the penalty from the equivalent and they did so, and he wanted to move on to food, it is permissible. Ibn Wahb, may God have mercy on him, said in Al-Utaybah: It is from the Sunnah that the two arbitrators give the choice to the one who struck the hand, just as God gave him the choice to bring out an offering that reaches the Kaaba or an expiation for feeding the poor or the equivalent of that in fasting. If he chooses the offering, they rule on it according to what they see as equivalent to what he struck between them and that the equivalent of that is a sheep because it is the lowest offering. If it does not reach a sheep, they rule on it with food, then he has the choice to feed it or fast for each mudd a day. Malik said the same in Al-Mudawwanah. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth - And the ruling is resumed in everything in which a government has passed or not passed, even if the government of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, is sufficient in what they ruled regarding the penalty for hunting, it is good. It has been narrated from Malik that except for the pigeons of Mecca, the wild donkey, the gazelle, and the ostrich, a government is necessary, and in these four it is sufficient to follow the government of those who passed from the predecessors, may God be pleased with them. Twenty-first - It is not permissible for the offender to be one of the two arbitrators. Abu Hanifa said the same, and Al-Shafi’i said in one of his two opinions: The offender must be one of the two arbitrators. This is a tolerance on his part, because it appears that a person’s ruling for himself is not permissible. If that were permissible, he would have been independent of others, because he is a judge between himself and God Almighty. So adding a second to him is evidence of renewing the ruling with two men. Twenty-second - If a group of people in ihram participate in killing game, Malik and Abu Hanifa said that each one must pay a full penalty. Al-Shafi’i said: They must all pay one expiation to make up for the sins of Umar and Abd al-Rahman. Narrated by al-Darqutni. The followers of Ibn al-Zubayr were in ihram when a hyena passed by them, so they hit it with their sticks and hit it, and it affected their souls. They came to Ibn Umar and mentioned it to him, and he said: Upon you all, a ram. They said: Or on each one of us a ram? He said: You are honored by you, upon you all a ram. The linguists said: Upon you is honored by you, meaning You are honored by it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding a group of people who hit a hyena, he said: Upon them is a ram that they exchange among themselves. Our evidence is the statement of the Almighty: And whoever among you kills it intentionally - the penalty is an equivalent of what he killed from livestock. This is addressed to every killer, and every one of the killers of game kills a person in full and completeness, as evidenced by the killing of a group for one person. If it were not for that, retaliation would not have been obligatory upon them, and we have said that it is obligatory by consensus, so what we said is proven. Twenty-third - Abu Hanifa said: If a group kills game in the sanctuary and all of them are in a state of ihram, they are to be punished one way, unlike if the people in a state of ihram kill it in the sanctuary and outside it, then there is no difference. Malik said: Each one of them is to be punished in full, based on the fact that a man is in a state of ihram by entering the sanctuary, just as he is in a state of ihram by declaring ihram, and each of the two actions has given him a characteristic that is subject to a prohibition, so he has violated it in both cases. Abu Hanifa’s argument is what Judge Abu Zaid al-Dabusi mentioned, who said: The secret in it is that the crime in the state of ihram is against worship, and each one of them has committed the prohibition of his ihram.
