If the people in a state of ihram kill game in the sanctuary, then they have destroyed a forbidden animal, just as if a group destroyed an animal, then each one of them killed an animal, and they share in the value. Ibn al-Arabi said: Abu Hanifa is stronger than us, and this is evidence that our scholars take lightly, and it is difficult for us to separate. Twenty-fourth - The Almighty’s saying: A sacrificial animal that reaches the Kaaba. The meaning is that if they rule on the sacrificial animal, then what is done with the sacrificial animal, such as marking and adorning it, is done with it, and it is sent from the sanctuary to Mecca, and it is slaughtered and given in charity there, based on His saying: A sacrificial animal that reaches the Kaaba. He did not mean the Kaaba specifically, because the sacrificial animal does not reach it, since it is in a mosque, but rather he meant the Sacred Sanctuary, and there is no disagreement on this. Al-Shafi’i said: The sacrificial animal does not need to reach the sanctuary, based on the fact that the smallness of the sacrificial animal is required in the case of small hunting, because it is bought in the Sacred Sanctuary and given as a sacrifice there. Twenty-fifth - The Almighty’s saying: Or an expiation by feeding poor people. The expiation is for hunting, not for sacrificial animals. Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: The best thing I have heard about the one who kills game and is judged in it is that he assesses the game he killed and sees how much it is worth in food, so he feeds each poor person a mudd or fasts for a day in place of each mudd. Ibn al-Qasim said about him: If the value of the game is dirhams and then assesses it as food, that is sufficient for him, and the first is correct. Abdullah bin Abdul-Hakam said the same. He said about him: In these three cases, he has the choice, whichever of them he does is sufficient for him, whether he is wealthy or poor. This is what Ata and the majority of jurists said, because or is for choice. Malik said: Everything in the Book of God regarding expiations is such and such, so its owner has the choice in that, whichever of them he likes to do, he does. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: If a pilgrim kills a gazelle or something similar, a sheep is slaughtered in Mecca. If he does not find one, then he must feed six poor people. If he does not find one, then he must fast for three days. If he kills a deer or something similar, then he must have a cow. If he does not find one, then he must feed twenty poor people. If he does not find one, then he must fast for twenty days. If he kills an ostrich or a donkey, he must offer a sacrificial animal. If he cannot find any, he must feed thirty poor people. If he cannot find any, he must fast for thirty days. The food should be a mudd to satisfy their hunger. This was stated by Ibrahim al-Nakha’i and Hammad ibn Salamah. They said: The meaning is or an expiation for food if he cannot find an offering. At-Tabari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: If a pilgrim kills game, he is to be punished for it. If he can find its punishment, he must slaughter it and give it in charity. If he does not have its punishment, his punishment is assessed in dirhams. Then the dirhams are assessed in a Hanza, then he must fast for a day in place of each half sa’. He said: What is meant by food is to clarify the matter of fasting. If he cannot find food, he can find his punishment. He also attributed it to al-Suddi. This statement is challenged by the apparent meaning of the verse, as it contradicts it. Twenty-sixth - The scholars differed on the time when the destroyer is considered responsible. Some said: The day of destruction. Others said: The day of judgment. Still others said: The destroyer is obligated to pay the greater of the two values from the day of destruction to the day of judgment. Ibn al-Arabi said: Our scholars differed as they differed, and the correct view is that he is obligated to pay the value on the day of destruction. The evidence for that is that the existence was a right over the destroyer, and if the destroyer destroys it, he is obligated to provide it with something similar, and that is at the time of nonexistence. Twenty-seventh - As for the sacrificial animal, there is a difference of opinion that it must be from Mecca, based on the Almighty’s saying: A sacrificial animal brought to the Kaaba. As for feeding, Malik’s opinion differed on whether it should be in Mecca or at the place of the strike. Al-Shafi’i went to Mecca, and Ata’ said: Whatever was blood or food, it should be in Mecca, and he fasts wherever he wishes, and this is Malik’s opinion regarding fasting, and there is no difference of opinion on this. Judge Abu Muhammad Abdul Wahhab said: It is not permissible to give anything from the penalty for hunting outside the Haram except fasting. Hammad and Abu Hanifa said: It is sufficient at the place of the strike absolutely. Al-Tabari said: He expiates wherever he wishes absolutely. As for the opinion of Abu Hanifa, it has no basis in consideration and no effect on it. As for the one who said he fasts wherever he wishes, it is because fasting is an act of worship specific to the fasting person, so it is in every place like fasting for all other expiations and others. As for the opinion that the food should be in Mecca, it is because it is a substitute for the sacrificial animal or similar to it, and the sacrificial animal is a right for the poor of Mecca, so it is in Mecca as a substitute or similar to it. As for the one who said that it can be in every place, then every food and ransom is considered, and it is permissible in every place, and God knows best. Twenty-eighth - The Almighty’s saying: Or the equivalent of that in fasting. Justice and adl with the opening of the ya’n and its breaking are two languages and they are the equivalent. Al-Kisa’i said. Al-Farra’ said: The equivalent of something with the opening of the ayn is its equivalent of its kind and with the opening of the ayn is its equivalent of something other than its kind. This statement is attributed to Al-Kisa’i. You say: I have the equivalent of your dirhams in dirhams and I have the equivalent of your dirhams in clothes. The correct view from Al-Kisa’i is that they are two languages and it is the view of the Basrans. It is not correct to compare fasting to food in a way closer than the hoopoe. Malik said: He fasts for each mudd one day even if it exceeds two or three months. Al-Shafi’i said the same. Yahya bin Omar from our companions said: It is only said: How many men are satisfied from this hunt, so the number is known and then it is said: How much food is this number satisfied? If he wants, he can take out that food and if he wants, he can fast the number of its mudds. This is a good precaution in it because the value of the hunt in food may be small, so with this view, feeding is increased. Some of the scholars do not see that fasting for compensation should exceed two months. They said: Because it is the highest of expiations. Ibn Al-Arabi chose it. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said: God fasts for every debtor one day as a ransom for harm. Twenty-ninth - The Almighty’s saying: That he may taste the evil consequences of his deed. Taste here is borrowed, as in the Almighty’s saying: Taste, for you are the mighty, the generous. (al-Dukhan 44:49) And He said: So God made her taste the garment of hunger and fear. (al-Nahl 16:112) The reality of taste is in the sense of the tongue, and in all of this it is borrowed, and from this is the hadith. He who is content with God as his Lord has tasted the sweetness of faith. Hadith: And the calamity is the bad end. And the one who is exposed to the worst is the one who is harmed by it after eating it. And the food is bad if it is heavy. And from this is his saying: The mentality of Sheikh Kalobele Yelande He expressed his command in all his conditions. The thirty - the Almighty’s saying: God has pardoned what is past meaning in your ignorance, you did not hunt, said Ata’ bin Abi Rabah and a group with him. It was said: before the expiation was revealed. And whoever returns meaning to what was forbidden. God will take revenge on him meaning with expiation. It was said that the meaning is God will take revenge on him meaning in the Hereafter if he considered it permissible and expiates according to the apparent ruling. Shuraih and Saeed bin Jubair said: He is judged the first time, but if he returns, he is not judged and he is told: Go, God will take revenge on you, meaning your sin is greater than to be expiated. Just as there is no expiation for a false oath according to most scholars due to the enormity of its sin, and the pious avoid the punishment by thinking. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: He fills his back with a whip until he dies. It was narrated from Zaid bin Abi Al-Mu’alla: A man caught game while he was in a state of ihram and passed it over, then he returned, so God, the Almighty, sent down fire from the sky and burned it. This is a lesson for the nation and a deterrent for the aggressors from disobedience. God Almighty says: And God is Exalted in Might and Possessor of Retribution. Exalted means impregnable in His kingdom and nothing is impossible for Him. He is the Possessor of Retribution against those who disobey Him if He wills.
5:96: It contains thirteen issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: Lawful to you is the game of the sea. This is a ruling that the game of the sea is permissible, which is all the whales that are caught. The game here means the catch and it was added to the sea because it was caused by it. The discussion of the sea has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Praise be to God, and enjoyment is in the accusative case as a source, meaning enjoyment of it as enjoyment. The second - the Almighty’s saying: And his food. Food is a general term that is applied to everything that is eaten and is applied to a specific food such as water alone, wheat alone, dates alone, and milk alone. It may also be applied to sleep as mentioned above, and here it is an expression for what the sea throws up and floats on. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the saying of God Almighty: Lawful to you is game from the sea and its food as provision for you and the travelers (10:13). His game is what is caught and his food is what the sea throws up. A similar statement was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and it is the statement of a large group of the Companions and Followers. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that his food is his dead body, and it is in that meaning. It was narrated on his authority that he said: His food is what is salty from it and remains. A group said the same with him. Some people said: His food is its salt that is made from a hundred and the rest of what is in it from plants and other things. Third - Abu Hanifa said: Floating fish are not to be eaten, and other fish are to be eaten, and nothing from the sea animals is to be eaten except fish, and this is the opinion of al-Thawri in the narration of Abu Ishaq al-Fazari from him, and al-Hasan disliked eating floating fish, and it was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he disliked it, and it was also narrated from him that he disliked running fish, and it was narrated from him that he ate all of that, and this is more correct. Abd al-Razzaq mentioned it from al-Thawri from Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali, who said: Locusts and whales are intelligent, so Ali differed from him in eating floating fish, and he did not differ from Jabir that he disliked it, and this is the opinion of Tawus, Muhammad ibn Sirin, and Jabir ibn Zayd, and they provided evidence with the generality of the Almighty’s saying: Forbidden to you are dead animals, and with what Abu Dawud and al-Darqutni narrated from Jabir ibn Abdullah, “from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Eat what the sea has washed up and what it has cast up, and what you find dead or floating on the surface of the water, do not eat it.” Al-Daraqutni said: It was narrated by Abdul Aziz bin Ubaidullah alone, on the authority of Wahb bin Kaysan, on the authority of Jabir, and Abdul Aziz is weak and cannot be relied upon. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated something similar on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Daraqutni said: No one narrated it on the authority of al-Thawri except Abu Ahmad al-Zubayr, and Wakee’, the two Adnayans, Abdul Razzaq, Muammal, Abu Asim, and others disagreed with him. They narrated it on the authority of al-Thawri as a mursal, and this is correct. Likewise, Ayoub al-Sakhtiyani, Ubaidullah bin Amr, Ibn Jurayj, Zuhair, Hammad bin Salamah, and others narrated it on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr as a mursal. Abu Dawud said: This hadith has been narrated through a weak chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Daraqutni said: It was narrated on the authority of Ismail bin Umayyah and Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr, but it is not authentic. It was narrated on the authority of Yahya bin Salim, on the authority of Ismail bin Umayyah and others stopped it. Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ibn Abi Laila, Al-Awza’i and Al-Thawri said in the narration of Al-Ashja’i: Everything in the sea of fish, animals and all other animals in the sea may be eaten, whether it is caught or found dead. Malik and those who followed him provided evidence with his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, regarding the sea: Its water is pure and its dead are permissible. The most authentic hadith in this regard in terms of chain of transmission is the hadith of Jabir about the whale called ambergris. It is one of the most authentic hadiths. It was included in the two Sahihs, and it says: When we arrived in Medina, we went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him. He said: “It is a provision that God has brought forth for you. Do you have any of its meat that you can feed us?” So we sent to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and he ate it. The wording is Muslim. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: I bear witness that Abu Bakr said: The floating fish is permissible for whoever wants to eat it. He also narrated on his authority that he said: I bear witness that Abu Bakr ate the floating fish on the water. He narrated on the authority of Abu Ayyub that he sailed the sea with a group of his companions and they found a floating fish on the water. They asked him about it and he said: Is it good? They said: Yes. He said: Eat it and save my share of it. He was fasting. He narrated on the authority of Jabalah ibn Atiyah that the companions of Abu Talhah found a floating fish and they asked Abu Talhah about it. He said: Give it to me as a gift. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The whale is intelligent and the locusts are all intelligent. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on his authority. These reports refute the statement of those who disliked it and specify the generality of the verse and it is an argument for the majority, except that Malik disliked the sea pig because of its name and did not forbid it and said: You say pig! Al-Shafi’i said: There is nothing wrong with a captive pig. Al-Layth said: There is nothing wrong with sea animals that have died. He said: And the same applies to the captive dog and the capybara. He said: Neither a captive human nor a capybara may be eaten. Fourth: Scholars differed about the animals that are found on land and in the sea. Is it permissible for a pilgrim to hunt them or not? Malik, Abu Majlaz, Ata’, Sa’id ibn Jubayr and others said: Everything that lives on land and has life in it is game on land. If the pilgrim kills it, he must pay blood money for it. Abu Majlaz added to that frogs, turtles, and crabs. Frogs and their kind are forbidden according to Abu Hanifa. There is no disagreement from Al-Shafi’i that it is not permissible to eat frogs. His opinion differed regarding what resembles land animals that are not eaten, such as pigs, dogs, and others. The correct view is to eat all of that, because he explicitly stated that eating pigs is permissible, and what resembles land animals that are not eaten is not eaten according to him, such as crocodiles, sharks, dolphins, and everything that has fangs, because he, peace be upon him, forbade eating everything that has fangs. Ibn Atiyyah said: And among these are types that do not leave the water, so they are inevitably game on the sea. Based on this, Malik’s answer regarding frogs in Al-Mudawwana came out, as he said: Frogs are game on the sea. It was narrated from Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah that it is different from what we mentioned, which is that he takes into account most of the life of animals. He was asked about the one who lives in the water, is he game on land or game on the sea? He said: Wherever it is more, it is from it, and where it hatches, it is from it. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa. The correct view regarding the son of water is that it is a land game that grazes and eats grain. Ibn al-Arabi said: The correct view regarding the animal that is on land and in the sea is that it is prohibited because it is exposed to two proofs of permission and one of prohibition, so the proof of prohibition prevails as a precaution, and God knows best. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: And for the traveler has two opinions: One of them is for the resident and the traveler, as came in the hadith of Abu Ubaidah that they ate it while they were traveling, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ate it while he was a resident, so God Almighty made it clear that it is permissible for the one who resides, just as He made it permissible for the one who travels. The second - that the traveler is the one who rides it, as came in the hadith of Malik and al-Nasa’i: A man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: We travel by sea and carry a little water with us. If we perform ablution with it, we will become thirsty. Can we perform ablution with sea water? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Its water is pure and its dead are permissible. Ibn al-Arabi said: Our scholars said: If the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had said to him: Yes, it would not have been permissible to perform ablution with it except when there is fear of thirst, because the answer is linked to the question, so it would have been impossible. But the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to establish the rule and explain the law by saying: Its water is pure and its dead are permissible. I said: The answer would have been limited to them and not extended to others, had it not been for what was established by the ruling of the Sharia that its ruling on one is its ruling on all, except for what was specifically stated, such as his saying to Abu Burdah regarding the embrace: Sacrifice it and it will not replace anyone else Sixth - The Almighty’s saying: And forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram. The prohibition is not a description of the objects, but rather relates to the actions. The meaning of His saying: And forbidden to you is the game of the land is the act of hunting, which is the prohibition from hunting, or hunting could mean the hunted in the sense of designating the object of the action as mentioned above, and this is the most apparent due to the consensus of the scholars that it is not permissible for the pilgrim to accept a game that was given to him as a gift, nor is it permissible for him to buy it, nor to hunt, nor to establish its ownership in any way, and there is no disagreement among the scholars of the Muslims regarding this due to the generality of the Almighty’s saying: And forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram, and the hadith of Al-Sa’ib bin Jaththama, as follows. Seventh: The scholars differed regarding what a person in ihram may eat from game. Malik, al-Shafi’i and their companions, Ahmad and it was narrated on the authority of Ishaq, and it is the correct one, on the authority of Uthman ibn Affan, said: There is nothing wrong with a person in ihram eating game if it was not hunted for him or for his sake, based on what al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i and al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Jabir that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abu Isa said: This is the best hadith in this chapter. Al-Nasa’i said: Amr ibn Abi Amr is not strong in hadith, even though Malik narrated from him. If he eats from the game that was hunted for him, he must pay the ransom. Al-Hasan ibn Salih and Al-Awza’i said the same. Malik’s opinion differed regarding what was hunted for a specific pilgrim. The well-known opinion of his school of thought among his companions is that the pilgrim does not eat what was hunted for a specific or unspecified pilgrim. He did not accept the statement of Uthman to his companions when he was brought game meat while he was in a state of ihram: Eat, for you are not like him because it was hunted for me. A group of the people of Madinah said the same. It was narrated from Malik. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: Eating game for the pilgrim is permissible in any case if it was hunted by a permissible person, whether it was hunted for him or not, based on the apparent meaning of the words of God Almighty: Do not kill game while you are in a state of ihram. So hunting and killing it is forbidden for the pilgrim, but not for what others hunted. They used as evidence the hadith of Al-Bahzi, whose name was Zaid ibn Ka’b: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the barren wild donkey, he ordered Abu Bakr to divide it among his companions.” From the hadith of Malik and others, and from the hadith of Abu Qatada, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which it says: It is only a taste that God has fed you. This is the saying of Omar bin Al-Khattab, Othman bin Affan in a narration from him, Abu Hurairah, Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam, Mujahid, Ata’, and Saeed bin Jubair. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, Ibn Abbas and Ibn Omar that it is not permissible for a person in ihram to eat game under any circumstances, whether it was hunted for him or not, due to the generality of the words of God Almighty: “And forbidden to you is game on land as long as you are in a state of ihram.” Ibn Abbas said: It is vague, and Tawus and Jabir bin Zaid Abu Al-Shatha’ said the same. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Thawri, and Ishaq said the same. They cited as evidence the hadith of Al-Sa’b bin Jaththama Al-Laythi. He “presented two wild donkeys to the Messenger of God while he was in Abwa’ or Budan, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned them to him. He said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw what was on my face, he said: We did not return them to you except because we are forbidden.” It was narrated by the imams and the wording is from Malik. Abu Omar said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas from the hadith of Saeed bin Jubair, Muqsim, Ata’ and Tawus on his authority. That Al-Sa’ib bin Jaththama presented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the meat of a wild donkey. Sa’id bin Jubair said in his hadith: The hindquarters of a wild donkey, so he returned it dripping with blood as if it had been hunted at that time. Muqsim said in his hadith: A wild donkey man. Ata’ said in his hadith: The thigh of a hunt was presented to him, but he did not accept it and said: We are in a state of ihram. Tawus said in his hadith: A thigh of the meat of a hunt. Ismail narrated it on the authority of Ali bin Al-Madini, on the authority of Yahya bin Sa’id, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, except that some of them attributed it to Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Zaid bin Arqam. Ismail said: I heard Sulayman bin Harb interpret this hadith as meaning that it was hunted for the sake of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. If that were the case, eating it would have been permissible. Sulayman said: What indicates that it was hunted for the sake of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is their statement in the hadith: He returned it dripping with blood as if it had been hunted at that time. Ismail said: Sulayman interpreted this hadith because it needs interpretation. As for the narration of Malik, it does not need interpretation because it is not permissible for a person in a state of ihram to hold a live hunt. And it does not purify it. Ismail said: According to the interpretation of Sulayman ibn Harb, all the hadiths attributed to the Prophet are not different, God willing. Eighth - If he enters ihram and has game in his possession or in his house with his family, Malik said: If it is in his possession, he must release it, but if it is with his family, he does not have to release it. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. Al-Shafi’i said in one of his two opinions: Whether it is in his possession or in his house, he does not have to release it. Abu Thawr said the same. It was narrated from Mujahid and Abdullah ibn al-Harith, similarly, and it was narrated from Malik. Ibn Abi Laila, al-Thawri, and al-Shafi’i said in the other opinion: He must release it, whether it is in his house or in his possession. If he does not release it, then the argument for releasing it is included in the statement of God Almighty: And game on land is forbidden to you as long as you are in a state of ihram. This is general in all ownership and disposal. The argument for keeping it is that it means that it does not prevent one from beginning ihram, so it does not prevent one from continuing to own it. Its origin is marriage. Ninth: If the lawful hunts it in the permissible and brings it into the sanctuary, it is permissible for him to dispose of it in any way, such as slaughtering it and eating its meat. Abu Hanifa said: It is not permissible. Our evidence is that it is the meaning of what is done in hunting, so it is permissible in the sanctuary for the time being, such as keeping it and buying it, and there is no disagreement about that. Tenth - If a person in ihram guides a lawful person to game and the lawful person kills it, there is a difference of opinion regarding it. Malik, al-Shafi’i, and Abu Thawr said: There is nothing upon him, and this is the opinion of Ibn al-Majishun. The Kufians, Ahmad, Ishaq, and a group of the Companions and Followers said: He must pay the penalty, because the person in ihram committed himself to refraining from attacking others, so he is liable for the guidance, just as the one who entrusts something to someone if he guides a thief to a theft. Eleventh - They differed regarding the pilgrim who guides another pilgrim. The Kufians and Ashab from our companions went to the view that each of them must pay a penalty. Malik, Al-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr said: The penalty is on the pilgrim who kills, based on the Almighty’s saying: And whoever among you kills him intentionally, so he connected the obligation of the penalty to the killing, so he indicated its absence by something else, and because he is a guide, he is not obligated by his guidance to pay a penalty, as if he guided the permissible in the sanctuary to game in the sanctuary. The Kufians and Ashab relied on the saying of the peace be upon him in the hadith of Abu Qatada: Did you point out or help? This indicates that a penalty is required, but the first is more correct, and God knows best. Twelfth: If a tree grows in the open area and its branch is in the sanctuary and the game hunted on it is killed, then there is a penalty for it because it was taken in the sanctuary. But if its root is in the sanctuary and its branch is in the open area, then our scholars differed regarding what was taken for it, with two opinions: the penalty is in consideration of the root, and its denial is in consideration of the branch. Thirteenth - The Almighty’s saying: And fear God, to whom you will be gathered. This is an emphasis and warning following this analysis. Then He mentioned the matter of the gathering and the Resurrection, exaggerating the warning, and God knows best.
5:97: It has five issues: The first - His Almighty’s saying, God made the Kaaba. Here, made means created, and it has been mentioned before. The Kaaba was called a Kaaba because it is square, and most of the houses of the Arabs are round. It was said that it was called a Kaaba because of its protrusion and its prominence. Every protruding, prominent thing is a heel, whether it is round or not. From this comes the heel of the foot, the heels of the canal, and the heel of a woman’s breast if it appears in her chest. The house was called that because it has a roof and a wall, and it is the reality of the house even if there is no resident in it. The Almighty called it a sanctuary because He made it forbidden. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Mecca is sacred to God, but not to people. Most of this has been presented in full, praise be to God. Second - The Almighty’s saying: A standing for the people meaning a good and a livelihood for the security of the people through it. Based on this, standing means they stand by it. It was said: standing means they stand by its laws. Ibn Amir and Asim read Qayyim, they are from the words with the letter waw, so the waw was changed to a ya because of the kasra before it. It has also been said that it is qawam. The scholars said: The wisdom in God the Almighty making these things a basis for people is that God the Almighty created creation with the human nature of envy, competition, estrangement, and hatred, and theft, raiding, killing, and revenge. So there was no alternative in the divine wisdom and the original will to have enough to sustain the situation and a deterrent with which wealth is praised. God the Almighty said: Indeed, I am placing on the earth a vicegerent (al-Baqarah 2:30), so God the Almighty commanded them to the vicegerent and made their affairs to one who would deter them from disputes and compel them to unite from estrangement and repel the oppressor from the oppressed and establish each hand in what it seizes. Ibn Al-Qasim narrated that Malik told us that Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, used to say: What deters the Imam more than what deters the Qur’an. Abu Omar, may God have mercy on him, mentioned this. The injustice of the Sultan for one year is less harmful than the people being in chaos for one moment, so God Almighty created. The Caliph for this benefit to conduct matters according to his opinion, and God prevents the aggression of the public through him, so God Almighty magnified the Sacred House in their hearts and instilled in their souls its awe, and magnified its sanctity among them, so whoever sought refuge in it was protected by it and whoever was persecuted was protected by being in it. God Almighty said: Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary while people are being snatched away all around them? (al-Ankabut 29:67) The scholars said: So since it was a specific place that not every oppressed person could reach and not every frightened person could reach it, God made the sacred month another refuge, which is: The third - which is a generic name, and what is meant are the three months by consensus of the Arabs, so God decided in their hearts that they were sacred, so they did not frighten a group - that is, a soul - nor did they seek blood nor expect revenge in them, so that a man would meet the killer of his father, son or brother and not harm him. They cut off a third of the time in them, and they connected three of them in succession as a space and rest and a place for tourism in security and rest, and they made one of them separate in the middle of the year to attain respect, and it is the month of Rajab al-Asam, and it is called Marr. It was only called Rajab al-Asam because the sound of iron was not heard in it, and it is called Mansel al-Asana, because they used to pull the spears out of it, and it is the month of Quraysh, and Awf ibn al-Ahwas says about it: The month of the Umayyads and the gifts when they are covered in blood The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called it the month of the family of God. The people of the sanctuary were called the family of God. It is possible that he meant the month of God because God made it strong and made it difficult, since many of the Arabs did not see it. The names of the months will come in Bara’ah, God willing. Then inspiration was made easy for them and guidance and necklaces were prescribed on the tongues of the noble messengers, which are: Fourth: If they took a camel, they would mark it with blood, or hang a sandal on it, or the man would do that himself out of imitation, as was explained at the beginning of the surah. No one would be frightened by him wherever he met him, and he was the arbiter between him and whoever sought him or wronged him, until God brought Islam and the truth through Muhammad, peace be upon him. Then the religion was organized in its chain and the truth returned to its place, so the imamate was attributed to him, and its obligation upon creation was built upon him, which is His, the Most High, saying: God has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth. (al-Nur 24:55) The rulings on the imamate have already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: That is so that you may know. That is an indication that God made these matters established, and the meaning is that God did that so that you may know that God knows the details of the affairs of the heavens and the earth and knows your interests, O people, before and after. So look at His kindness to the servants in their state of disbelief.
5:98: The Almighty’s saying: Know that God is severe in penalty is a warning, and that God is Forgiving and Merciful is a hope. This meaning has already been presented.
5:99: The Almighty said: The Messenger is only responsible for conveying the message meaning he is not responsible for guidance, success, or reward, but rather he is responsible for conveying the message. This is a refutation of the Qadarites as mentioned above. The root of balugh is to reach. balugh means to reach. balugh means to reach, and balugh means to reach, and balugh means to convey the meaning to the soul in a beautiful form of speech. A man is balugh if he practices eloquence, but he is not eloquent. This is balugh meaning sufficiency because it conveys the amount needed. And God knows what you reveal means that you reveal. It is said that the secret appeared and its owner revealed it, and what you conceal meaning what you conceal and hide in your hearts of disbelief and hypocrisy.
5:100: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: The bad and the good are not equal.” There are three issues in this: The first - Al-Hasan said: The bad and the good, the lawful and the unlawful. Al-Suddi said: The believer and the disbeliever. It was said: The obedient and the disobedient. It was said: The bad and the good. This is by way of example. The correct view is that the wording is general in all matters, and can be imagined in earnings, deeds, people, knowledge from sciences and other things. The bad of all of this does not succeed, does not give birth, and does not have a good outcome, even if it is abundant. The good, even if it is little, is beneficial and has a beautiful outcome. God Almighty said: “And the good land brings forth its vegetation by permission of its Lord. But that which is bad brings forth nothing but a little.” (al-A’raf 7:58) Similar to this verse is the saying of God Almighty: Or shall We treat those who believe and do righteous deeds like corrupters in the land? Or shall We treat the righteous like the wicked? (Sad: 28) and His saying: Or do those who commit evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believe and do righteous deeds? (al-Jathiyah 45:21). The bad is not equal to the good in quantity, spending, place, or gold. The good is on the right side, and the bad takes the left side. The good is in Paradise and the bad is in Hell. This is Between the truth of straightness is continuity in one direction, and the same is true of straightness and its opposite is crookedness, otherwise this would not have happened, and it is: Second - Some of our scholars said: The invalid sale is annulled and is not validated by a transfer of a load or by a change of body, so it is the same in its validation as the valid sale, rather it is annulled forever and the price is returned to the buyer if he received it, and if it is lost in his hand, he is liable for it because he did not receive it as a trust, or he received it with the suspicion of a contract. It was said: It is not annulled in view of the fact that if the sale is annulled and returned after the loss, there is harm and fraud in it for the seller, so the commodity is worth one hundred and is returned to him while it is worth twenty, and there is no penalty in the money, and the first is the most correct of the verse and “and because of his saying, peace be upon him: Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it will be rejected. If this meaning is followed in the non-equality in the issues of jurisprudence, they will be numerous and numerous. Among these is the angry one, which is: Third: If he built or planted on the usurped land, then he must uproot that building and planting because it is impure and its yield is contrary to Abu Hanifa’s statement: It is not to be uprooted and its owner takes its value. This is rejected by his statement, peace be upon him: An unjust race has no right. Hisham said: An unjust race is when a man plants on the land of another in order to take it back. Malik said: An unjust race is everything that is taken, despised and planted without right. Malik said: Whoever usurps land and cultivates it or rents it, or a house and lives in it or rents it and then its owner takes it back, the usurper must pay the rent for what he lives in and return what he took in rent. His statement differed if he did not live in it or cultivate the land and left it idle. The well-known view of his school of thought is that there is nothing wrong with it. It was narrated from him that he must pay the rent for all of that, and Al-Waqar chose it, and it is the school of thought of Al-Shafi’i, “because of his saying, peace be upon him: An unjust race has no right.” Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr that two men disputed before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. One of them planted palm trees on the land of the other, so he ruled in favor of the owner of the land and ordered the owner of the palm trees to remove his palm trees from it. He said: I saw them and their roots were being struck with an axe until they were removed from them, and they were palm trees of a uncle. This is a text. Ibn Habib said: The ruling in it is that the owner of the land The oppressor has the choice: if he wishes, he can keep it in his land for its value, uprooted, or if he wishes, he can remove it from his land and the wages for removal are on the angry one. Al-Darqutni narrated, “On the authority of Aisha, she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever builds in the land of a people with their permission, he is entitled to the value, and whoever builds without their permission, he is entitled to the cancellation. Our scholars said: He is entitled to the value because he built in a place whose benefit he owns, and this is like someone who built or planted with doubt, so he has the right, if the owner of the money wishes, to pay him its value while it is standing, and if he refuses, it is said to the one who built or planted: Pay him the value of his land in a free space, and if he refuses, they are partners. Ibn Al-Majishun said: The explanation of their partnership is that the land is in a free space and then it is cultivated, so whatever its value increases with cultivation over its value while it is in a free space, the worker is a partner with the owner of the land in it if they like, a division or a retention. Ibn Al-Jahm said: So if the owner of the land pays the value of the construction and takes his land, he is entitled to its rent for the past years. It has been narrated from Ibn Al-Qasim and others that if a man builds on the land of another with his permission, then it is necessary for him to remove it, he is given the value of his building after it has been removed, and the first is more correct, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: “Then he is entitled to the value,” and most of the jurists agree with this. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: Even if the abundance of evil pleases you. It was said that the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation, for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is not pleased with evil. It was also said that what is meant by it is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, himself, and his admiration for it is that he is amazed by what he sees of the abundance of disbelievers and unlawful wealth and the small number of believers and lawful wealth. So fear God, O you of understanding, that you may succeed. Its meaning was presented earlier.
5:101: It contains ten issues: First - Al-Bukhari, Muslim and others narrated - and the wording is Al-Bukhari’s - on the authority of Anas, who said: A man said, O Prophet of God, who is my father? He said, Your father is so-and-so. Then the verse was revealed, O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are shown to you, will distress you. It was also narrated on the authority of Anas, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in it: By God, do not ask me about anything that I will not tell you as long as I am in this position.” A man stood up and said: Where will I enter, O Messenger of God? He said: Hellfire. Abdullah bin Hudhafah stood up and said: Who is my father, O Messenger of God? He said: Your father is Hudhafah. He mentioned the hadith. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: Abdullah bin Hudhafah converted to Islam long ago and migrated to the land of Abyssinia for the second migration. He witnessed Badr and was a joker. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Kisra with the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When he said: Who is my father, O Messenger of God? He said: Your father is Hudhafah. A woman said to him: “I have never heard of a more disobedient son than you. I believe that your mother did what the women of the Age of Ignorance did, disgracing them in the eyes of the people.” He said: By God, if I were to be joined to a black slave, I would join him. Al-Tirmidhi and al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: When this verse was revealed: And Hajj to the House is a duty that mankind owes to God, those who can afford the expenses for one’s expenses (Al Imran 3:97), they said: O Messenger of God, every year? He remained silent. They said: Every year? He said: “No. Even if I had said yes, I would have answered.” Then God revealed: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, may distress you to the end of the verse. The wording is from Ad-Daraqutni. Al-Bukhari was asked about this hadith and he said: It is a good hadith, except that it is a mursal hadith. Abu Al-Bukhtari did not meet Ali, and his name was Saeed. Ad-Daraqutni also narrated it on the authority of Abu Ayyad, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, Hajj has been prescribed for you. A man stood up and said: Every year, O Messenger of God. He turned away from him and said: Every year, O Messenger of God. He said: Who said it? They said: So-and-so. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if I had said yes, it would have been obligatory. And if it were obligatory, you would not have been able to do it. And if you were not able to do it, you would have disbelieved. Then God the Most High revealed: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, will distress you. And the verse. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said about this verse: They asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the matters of ignorance that God has pardoned, and there is no point in asking about what God has pardoned. Mujahid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it was revealed about a people who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the bahīrah, the sa’ibah, the wasīlah, and the Ḥām. This is the statement of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: Do you not see that after it, God has not made any bahīrah, sa’ibah, wasīlah, or Ḥām. I said: It is correct and the chain of transmission is sufficient. It is possible that the verse was revealed in response to all of them, so the question would be close to each other. God is Most High and things are of the weight of af’al and it was not declined because it is similar to hamra’. Al-Kisa’i said: It was said: Its weight is af’ala’ like your saying: hayn and ahunaa’ according to al-Farra’ and al-Akhfash. It is made diminutive and it is said: things. Al-Mazini said: It is necessary to make things diminutive like friends are made diminutive in the feminine form friends and in the masculine form friends. Second - Ibn Awn said: I asked Nafi’ about the Almighty’s saying: Do not ask about things which, if they are made known to you, will distress you. He said: Questions have always been disliked. Muslim narrated on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God has forbidden you to be disobedient to mothers, to bury your children alive, to refuse, and to give, and He dislikes three things: it was said and said, and asking too many questions, and wasting money. Many scholars said: What is meant by His saying and asking too many questions is asking too many questions in matters of jurisprudence, being pedantic and demanding about things that were not revealed, and making mistakes and creating misconceptions. The early Muslims disliked that and considered it an obligation, and they would say: When a calamity befell, the one asked would follow it. Malik said: I found the people of this country and they had no knowledge other than the Book and the Sunnah, so when a calamity befell, the emir would gather for it the scholars present, and whatever they agreed upon, he would implement it. You ask too many questions, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked that. It was said that what is meant by asking too many questions is asking people too much about money and needs, insisting and asking too much. Malik also said: It was said that what is meant by asking too many questions is asking about things that do not concern you from the affairs of people, such that this leads to exposing their faults and learning about their shortcomings. This is like the saying of God, the Most High: “And do not spy, nor backbite one another.” (al-Hujurat 49:12) Ibn ‘Abbas said: Khuwaiz Mandad: That is why some of our companions said that whenever food was presented to him, he would not ask where it was from, or something to buy was offered to him, he would not ask where it was from, and he would assume the affairs of the Muslims were safe and sound. I said: The correct view is to carry the hadith in its generality, so it includes all of those aspects, and God knows best. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: Some of the heedless people believed that asking questions about new issues is forbidden until they occur, based on this verse. This is not the case, because this verse explicitly states that the question that is forbidden is only about something that would cause harm in answering it, and there is no harm in answering the new issues of the time, so they differed. I said: Some of the heedless people thought it was ugly, but it would have been better for him to say: Some people forbade asking questions about new issues, but he continued as he was accustomed to. We said it would have been better for him because some of the early Muslims disliked it, and Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him used to curse whoever asked about something that was not mentioned by al-Darimi in his Musnad. He mentioned on the authority of al-Zuhri that he said: It has reached us that Zayd ibn Thabit al-Ansari used to say when he was asked about a matter: Was this the case? If they said: Yes, then he spoke about it with what he knew. If they said: It was not the case, then leave it until it happens. And it was narrated on the authority of Ammar ibn Yasir that he was asked about a matter and he said: Was this the case yet? They said: No. He said: Leave us until it happens, and when it happens we will make it easy for you. Al-Darimi said: Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abi Shaybah told us, Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Ata bin Abbas, who said: I have never seen a people who were better than the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They only asked him about thirteen issues until he died, all of them in the Qur’an, including: They ask you about the sacred month (Al-Baqarah 2:217), And they ask you about menstruation (Al-Baqarah 2:222) and the like. They only asked about what would benefit them. Fourth - Ibn Abd al-Barr said: Questioning today is not feared to result in prohibition or permission. So whoever asks as a questioner, desiring knowledge and denying ignorance from himself, searching for a meaning that must be understood in religion, then there is no problem with him, for the cure for ignorance is asking. And whoever asks stubbornly, not understanding or learning, then his question is not permissible, whether little or much. Ibn al-Arabi said: What the scholar should be busy with is explaining the evidence and clarifying the paths of contemplation, and obtaining in advance the effort and preparing the tool that helps in deriving, so if a problem is presented, you come from its door, and seek in its appropriate places, and God opens up its correctness. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: And if you ask about it when the Qur’an is being revealed, it will be made clear to you. There is ambiguity in it, and that is what I deny. The beginning of the verse prohibits asking. Then He said: And if you ask about it when the Qur’an is being revealed, it will be made clear to you. So He permitted them. It was said: The meaning is: And if you ask about other things in what there is a need for it, so the complement was deleted, and it is not correct to interpret it in any other way. Al-Jurjani said: The metaphor in about it refers to other things, like the Almighty’s saying: And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay, meaning Adam. Then He said: Then We made him a sperm-drop (al-Mu’minun 23:12-13), meaning the son of Adam, because Adam was not carried as a sperm-drop in a secure place. But when He mentioned the human being, who is Adam, He indicated a human being like him, and that was known by the evidence of the solution. So the meaning is: And if you ask about things when the Qur’an is being revealed, such as permitting or forbidding or ruling, or if you need an explanation, then if you ask, then it will be made clear to you. He permitted this type of question. An example of this is that He explained the waiting period of a divorced woman whose husband has died and the pregnant woman. He did not mention the waiting period of one who is not menstruating or pregnant, so they asked him, so He revealed: And those who have despaired of menstruation (al-Talaq 65:4). So the prohibition is if it is something that they do not need to ask about, but as for what they need, then it is not. Sixth - The Almighty’s saying: God has pardoned it] about the question that they had asked about previously. It was said about the things that they asked about from the matters of ignorance and what came after it. It was said: Pardon means leaving it, meaning leaving it and not knowing about it in what is permissible or forbidden, so it is pardoned, so do not search for it, for perhaps if its ruling becomes clear to you, it will upset you. Ubayd ibn Umair used to say: God has made permissible and forbidden, so what He has made permissible has been made permissible, so consider it permissible, and what He has forbidden, so avoid it. And He has left in between things that He has not made permissible or forbidden, so that is pardon from God. Then he recites this verse. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Tha’labah al-Khushani, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty has imposed obligations, so do not neglect them. He has forbidden sacred things, so do not violate them. He has set limits, so do not transgress them. He has remained silent about things, not out of forgetfulness, so do not search for them. The speech in this estimation includes an advancement and a delay, meaning do not ask about things that God has pardoned, if they are revealed to you they will upset you, meaning He has refrained from mentioning them and has not imposed a ruling on them. It has been said: There is no advancement or delay, but rather the meaning is that God has pardoned your previous question, even if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked it, so do not transgress to similar things. His saying: about it, meaning about the question or the questions, as we mentioned:
5:102: Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: A people before you asked for it, then they became disbelievers in it. The Almighty informed us that a people before us asked for signs like it, then when they were given them and imposed upon them, they disbelieved in them and said: It is not from God. This is like the people of Salih asking for the she-camel, and the companions of Jesus asking for the table. This is a clarification of what previous nations fell into, and God knows best. Eighth - If someone says: What you mentioned about the dislike of asking and the prohibition of it contradicts the words of God Almighty: So ask the people of the message if you do not know (al-Nahl 16:43 and An-Anbiya: 7), then the answer is that what God has commanded His servants to do is what has been established and proven to be obligatory, which must be worked for, and what came in the prohibition is what God did not command His servants to do, and He did not mention it in His Book, and God knows best. Ninth - Muslim narrated on the authority of Amer bin Saad on the authority of his father who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The greatest sinner among Muslims is the one who asks about something that is not forbidden to Muslims, and it is forbidden to them because of his question. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: Why did Al-Ajlani not ask about adultery when cursing was established? Abu Al-Faraj Al-Jawzi said: This is attributed to the one who asks about something in vain and in frivolity, and is punished with a surah whose intention is to prohibit what he asked about, and the prohibition is general. Tenth - Our scholars said: The Qadarites have no connection to this hadith that God Almighty does something for the sake of something and because of it. God is exalted above that, for God is capable of everything, and He is All-Knowing of everything. Rather, the reason and motive for doing what He does is the fate and destiny that preceded the thing that was asked about if the question was asked about it, not that the question is a reason for the prohibition and a cause for it. And there are many similar examples: “He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned” (Al-Anbiya’: 23).
5:103: It contains seven issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: What God has made here means named as God Almighty said: Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur’an (al-Zukhruf 43:3), meaning We named it. The meaning in this verse is that God did not name it, nor did He establish it as a ruling, nor did He worship it as a law, but rather He decreed it with knowledge and brought it into existence with His power and will as a creation, for God is the Creator of everything: good and evil, benefit and harm, obedience and disobedience. The second - the Almighty’s saying: From a bahīrah nor a sā’ibah from is redundant and bahīrah is in the sense of maf’ūlah, and it is on the weight of an-naṭihah and an-ḍhībah. In the Sahih on the authority of Sa’d ibn al-Musayyab: bahīrah is the one whose milk is forbidden to the tyrants, so no one among the people milks it. As for sā’ibah, it is the one that they used to leave for their gods. It was said: bahīrah in language is the she-camel with a split ear. It is said: bahīrah the she-camel’s ear is split, meaning he split it wide. The she-camel is bahīrah and mubahūrah, and the sea was a sign of being set free. Ibn Sidah said: It is said that bahīrah is the one that was left without a shepherd, and the abundant she-camel is called bahīrah. Ibn Ishaq said: bahīrah is the daughter of sā’ibah, and sā’ibah is the she-camel that has been followed by ten females, and there is no male among them who did not ride her back, cut her hair, or drink her milk except a guest. So after that, no female produced a slit ear and was set free with her mother, so no one rode her back, cut her hair, or drink her milk except a guest, as was done with her mother, so she is bahīrah, the daughter of sā’ibah. He said: Al-Shafi’i: If a female camel gives birth to five female offspring, her ear is pierced and she is forbidden. He said: It is forbidden for people to eat its meat, and we are not in any way like the lakes. Ibn Aziz said: The bahīra is a she-camel that has given birth to five offspring. If the fifth is a male, they slaughter it and men and women eat it. If the fifth is a female, they slit its ear. Its meat and milk are forbidden to women. This was said by Ikrimah. If it dies, it is permissible for women and the camel that is set free is let loose by a vow that a man must make if God saves him from illness or he attains a high position to do so. It is not prevented from grazing or watering and no one is allowed to ride it. Abu Ubaid said: The poet said: And a free woman, may God bless her, grows, thank God, whether she is healthy or hungry. They may also leave behind other than the female camel. If they leave behind a slave, he is not to be held accountable. It has been said that the freed slave is the one who has no chains attached to him, and no shepherd for him. The subject is the object, like A life of contentment (al-Haqqah 69:21), meaning pleasing, from the snake that let loose and flowed. The poet said: You have hamstrung a she-camel that belonged to my Lord and was free, so stand up for the punishment. As for the wasilah and the ham, Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: The people of the Jahiliyyah used to free camels and sheep and let them go. As for the ham from the camels, when the male finished his estrus, they would put peacock feathers on him and let him go. As for the wasilah from the sheep, when a female was born after a female, they would let her go. Ibn Aziz said: The wasilah in the sheep, he said: When a sheep gave birth to seven wombs, they would look, and if the seventh was a male, it would be slaughtered and the men and women would eat from it. If it was a female, it would be left among the sheep. If it was a male and a female, they would say it joined its brother, so it was not slaughtered because of its location, and its meat was forbidden to women, and the milk of the female was forbidden to women unless one of them died, in which case the men and women would eat it. The ham is the male when he rode his offspring. He said: Abu Qaboos protected her during the glory of his reign, just as he protected his grandchildren’s grandchildren. It is said: If ten wombs are produced from his loins, they say: He has protected his back, so he is not ridden, nor is he prevented from pasture or water. Ibn Ishaq said: The wasila is the ewe that gives birth to ten females in succession in five wombs, with no male among them, they say: She has given birth, and what she gives birth to after that is male for the males among them, not the females, unless one of them dies, in which case the males and females share in eating it. Third: Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw Amr ibn Amir Al-Khuza’i dragging a reed in the fire, and he was the first to set the stray animals free. And in the narration of Amr ibn Luhay ibn Qama’ah ibn Khandaf, the brother of these Banu Ka’b, dragging a reed in the fire. Abu Hurairah narrated that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say to Aktham ibn Lajun: I saw Amr ibn Luhay ibn Qama’ah ibn Khandaf dragging his reed in the Fire, and I have never seen a man more similar to another man than you, nor to another man than you. Aktham said: I fear that his resemblance will harm me, O Messenger of God. He said: No, you are a believer and he is an unbeliever. He was the first to change the religion of Ismail, the Bahirah Sea, the Saibah Sea, and the Hama al-Hami. And in another narration: I saw him as a short, hairy man with a thick beard, dragging his reed in the Fire. And in the narration of Ibn al-Qasim and others on the authority of Malik on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: It harms the people of Hell with its smell. It was mentioned by Ibn al-Arabi: It was said that the first one to innovate that was Junada bin Awf, and God knows best. In Sahih Kifaya, Ibn Ishaq narrated: The reason for setting up idols and changing the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him, was Amr bin Luhay, who left Mecca for Syria. When he arrived in Ma’ab in the land of Balqa, where at that time the Amalekites were, the sons of Amalek - and it is said Amalek - bin Lawdh bin Sam bin Noah, he saw them worshipping idols and said to them: What are these idols that I see you worshipping? They said: These are idols that we ask for rain from, and we receive rain, and we ask for victory from, and we are victorious. He said to them: Why don’t you give me an idol from them so that I can travel to the land of the Arabs and worship it? So they gave him an idol called Hubal, and he arrived in Mecca with it, set it up, and the people began to worship and glorify it. When God sent Muhammad, God revealed to him: “God has not appointed any Bahira, or Sa’iba, or Wasila, or Ham.” But those who disbelieve meaning from Quraysh, Khuza’a, and the polytheists of the Arabs invent lies about God. By saying: God has ordered its prohibition and they claim that they do it to please their Lord in obedience to God, you only know from His statement and they did not have from God that statement, so that is what they fabricate against God and they said: What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males (al-An’am 6:139) meaning of children and milk and forbidden to our wives even if it is dead meaning if she gave birth to it dead, the man and the women share in it, so that is what God the Almighty said: “They are partners in it. He will recompense them for their description” meaning for their lie with the punishment in the Hereafter He is Wise and Knowing (al-An’am 6:139) meaning of prohibition and permissibility, and He revealed to him: “Say: Have you seen what God has sent down to you of provision, then you made some of it unlawful and some of it lawful? Say: Has God permitted you, or do you invent a lie against God?” (Yunus 10:59) and He revealed to him: Eight pairs (al-An’am 6:143) the verse and He revealed to him: And livestock over which they do not mention the name of God, inventing a lie against Him (al-An’am
5:104: God Almighty says: And when it is said to them, ‘Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger,’ they say, ‘Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers.’ The meaning of the verse was presented and discussed in Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it.
5:105: It has four issues: First: Our scholars said: The connection between this verse and what preceded it is to warn against what one must beware of, which is the state of the one whose description was mentioned above, who relied in his religion on the imitation of his fathers and ancestors. The apparent meaning of this verse indicates that enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is not an obligation if the person is upright, and that no one will be held accountable for the sin of another, were it not for what was mentioned in its interpretation in the Sunnah and the sayings of the Companions and Followers, as we will mention, God Almighty willing. The second - the Almighty’s saying: Upon you yourselves means protect yourselves from sins. You say upon you Zaid meaning stick to Zaid, and it is not permissible to say upon him Zaid rather this is sufficient from addressing in three words: upon you Zaid meaning take Zaid, and with you is Amr meaning he is present, and behind you is Zaid meaning he is close to you, and he recited: Oh, you who pour water, pour your bucket without me As for his saying: A man who is not me is upon him, it is anomalous. Third: Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and others narrated on the authority of Qais who said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, addressed us and said: You recite this verse and interpret it in a way other than its interpretation. O you who believe, upon you is yourselves. He who goes astray will not harm you if you are guided. And I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If people see an oppressor and do not stop him, God will soon afflict them all with a punishment from Him. Abu ‘Eisa said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Ishaq ibn Ibrahim said: I heard ‘Amr ibn ‘Ali say: I heard Wakee’ say: Not a single hadith is authentic from Abu Bakr from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: Not even Ismail from Qays. He said: Ismail narrated from Qays with a chain of transmission ending with him. Al-Naqqash said: This is an exaggeration on the part of Wakee’. Shu’bah narrated it from Sufyan and Ishaq from Ismail with a chain of transmission ending with the Prophet. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and others narrated it from Abu Umayyah al-Sha’bani, who said: I came to Abu Tha'labah Al-Khushani and said to him: How do you deal with this verse? He said: Which verse? I said: The words of God the Almighty: {O you who have believed, upon you is yourselves. He who strays will not harm you if you are guided.} He said: By God, I asked about it in Khaybar. I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: Rather, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, until when you see greed being obeyed, desire being followed, the world being preferred, and every person with an opinion being impressed by his opinion, then you should mind your own self and leave the affairs of the masses, for there are days ahead of you in which patience will be like holding hot coals. The one who works in them will have the reward of fifty men who work like you.} In another narration: It was said: O Messenger of God, the reward of fifty of us or of them? He said: By wetness, the reward of fifty of you.} Isa said: This is a good and strange hadith. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: His statement: Rather of you, this phrase was not mentioned by some of the narrators and they did not mention it. It was mentioned earlier. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You are in a time when whoever among you abandons a tenth of what he was commanded to do will perish. Then a time will come when whoever among you does a tenth of what he was commanded to do will be saved.” He said: This is a strange hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that he said: This is for me in a time of this verse: Speak the truth that has been accepted from you, but when it is rejected from you, then be gentle. And it was said to Ibn `Umar during some times of tribulations: If you left the speech these days, why would you not command or forbid? He said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: ‘Let the witness inform the absent,’ and we have witnessed, so it is incumbent upon us to inform you. A time will come when if the truth is said, it will not be accepted.” In a narration from Ibn Umar after his saying: Let the witness inform the absent, we were the witnesses and you were the absent. However, this verse is for people who will come after us. If they say, it will not be accepted from them. Ibn al-Mubarak said that the Almighty’s statement, Upon you yourselves, is addressed to all believers, meaning, upon you are the people of your religion, like the Almighty’s statement, And do not kill yourselves, so it is as if He said: Let some of you command others and be gentle with others. This is evidence of the obligation of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and the misguidance of the polytheists, hypocrites, and People of the Book will not harm you. This is because enjoining what is right is done with Muslims who are disobedient, as mentioned above. The meaning of this was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair. Saeed bin al-Musayyab said: The meaning of the verse is that those who go astray will not harm you if you are guided after enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: The verse includes a person’s preoccupation with his own self and his abandonment of it. Expose people’s faults and search for their conditions, for they do not ask about their condition, so do not ask about their condition. This is like the Almighty’s saying: Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned (al-Muddaththir 74:38), And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another (al-An’am 6:164 and Fatir 35:18), and the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Be a guardian of your home and take care of yourself in particular.” It is possible that what is meant by it is the time when it is difficult to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, so he forbids it in his heart and is busy with reforming himself. I said: The hadith is strange. It was narrated by Ibn Lahi’ah. He said: Bakr bin Sawadah Al-Judhami told us on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If it is two hundred, then do not command what is right and do not forbid what is wrong, and you should take care of yourselves in particular. Our scholars said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) only said that because of the change in time, the corruption of conditions, and the scarcity of those who helped him. Jabir bin Zaid said: The meaning of the verse is, “O you who believe, from the descendants of those who sailed the sea and set free the wandering animals, take care of yourselves in the straight path, for those who will not be harmed by the error of Islam if you are guided.” He said: And when a man converted to Islam, the infidels would say to him: You have made your fathers foolish and led them astray, and you did this and that. So God revealed the verse because of that. It was said: The verse is about the people of desires who are not benefited by preaching, so if you know that a people will not accept, but rather hide and appear, then be silent about them. It was said: It was revealed about the prisoners whom the polytheists tortured until some of them apostatized, so it was said to those who remained in Islam: Take care of yourselves, the apostasy of your companions will not harm you. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is about the People of the Book. Mujahid said: It is about the Jews and Christians and those like them, they go to the meaning that disbelief will not harm you. The People of the Book if they pay the jizya. It was said: It was abrogated by the command to do good and forbid evil. Al-Mahdawi said: Ibn Atiyah said: This is weak and its speaker is not known. I said: It was reported on the authority of Ibn Abi Ubaid al-Qasim Ibn Salam that he said: There is no verse in the Book of God Almighty that combines the abrogating and the abrogated except this verse. Someone else said: The abrogating verse among them is His statement: If you are guided. Guidance here is enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and God knows best. Fourth: Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is a pleasure whenever there is hope of acceptance or there is hope of repelling the oppressor, even if it is violent, unless the one enjoining fears harm that will befall him personally, or a trial that he will bring upon the Muslims, either by disobeying God or by harm that will befall a group of people. If this is feared, then You are responsible for yourselves is a decisive statement that must be adhered to, and it is not a condition for the one forbidding to be just, as mentioned above. And this is what the group of scholars say, so be aware of it.
5:106: It contains twenty-seven issues: First: Makki said, may God have mercy on him: These three verses, according to the people of meaning, are among the most difficult in the Qur’an in terms of grammar, meaning, and ruling. Ibn Atiyah said: These are the words of someone who has no idea about their interpretation, and this is clear from his book, may God have mercy on him. I said: What Makki - may God have mercy on him - mentioned was also mentioned by Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas before him, and I do not know of any disagreement that these verses were revealed because of Tamim al-Dari and `Adi ibn Bad`. Al-Bukhari, al-Darqutni, and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Tamim ad-Dari and Adi ibn Bad’ used to travel to Mecca. A young man from Banu Sahm went out with them and died in a land where there were no Muslims. He left a will to them, so they gave his estate to his family and kept a silver cup decorated with gold. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made them swear that they had not concealed anything from him nor had they found out. Then the cup was found in Mecca and they said: We bought it from Adi and Tamim. Two men from the heirs of al-Sahmi came and swore that this cup belonged to al-Sahmi, and that our testimony was more valid than their testimony and that we had not transgressed. He said: So they took the cup, and this verse was revealed about them. Wording by al-Daraqutni. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Tamim ad-Dari regarding this verse. O you who believe! A testimony between you The people are innocent of it except for me and Adi bin Bada’ - they were Christians who used to go to Ash-Sham before Islam. They came to Ash-Sham with their trade, and a client of Banu Sahm called Badil bin Maryam came to them with a trade, and with him was a silver cup with which he wanted to take the king, and his trade was great. He fell ill and made a will to them and ordered them to deliver what his family had left. Tamim said: When he died, we took the cup and sold it for a thousand dirhams, then we divided it, me and Adi bin Bada’. When we returned to his family, we gave him what we had with us, and they lost the cup. They asked us about it, and we said: He left nothing but this, and he did not give us anything else. Tamim said: When I converted to Islam after the arrival of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Medina, I felt guilty about that, so I went to his family and told them the report, and I paid them five hundred dirhams, and I told them that my companion had the same amount. They brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he asked them for evidence, but they did not find any, so he ordered them to swear by what would be decisive for the people of his religion. So he swore, and God the Almighty revealed: O you who believe! A testimony between you until His saying: After their belief. So Amr ibn al-‘As and another man from them stood up and swore, and the five hundred were taken from the hands of ‘Adi ibn Bad’. Abu ‘Eisa said: This is a strange hadith, and its chain of transmission is not sound. Al-Waqidi mentioned that the three verses were revealed about Tamim and his brother ‘Adi, and they were Christians. Their trade was to Mecca. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, Ibn Abi Maryam, the freed slave of ‘Amr ibn al-‘As, came to Medina intending to trade with Syria. He went out with Tamim and his brother ‘Adi, and he mentioned the hadith. Al-Naqqash said: It was revealed about Badil ibn Abi Maryam, the freed slave of al-‘Aas ibn Wa’il al-Sahmi. He had gone on a journey by sea to the land of the Negus, and with him were two Christian men, one of whom was called Tamim and was from Lakhm, and ‘Adi ibn Bad’. Badil died while they were on the ship, so he was thrown into the sea. He had written his will and then put it in the luggage, saying: Deliver this luggage to my family. When Badil died, they took the money and took from it what they liked, and it was among what they took. A silver vessel containing three hundred mithqals, engraved and gilded. He mentioned the hadith and Sunayd mentioned it. He said: When they arrived in the Levant, Badil became ill, and he was a Muslim. The second - the Almighty’s saying: A testimony between you. Testimony is mentioned in the Book of God the Almighty in different types: including His saying the Almighty: And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men (al-Baqarah 2:282). It was said that its meaning is bring. And from it is the word witness meaning he decided, i.e. he knew, said Abu Ubaidah, like His saying the Almighty: God bears witness that there is no god but Him (Al Imran 3:18). And from it is the word witness meaning he acknowledged, like His saying the Almighty: And the angels bear witness (An-Nisa’: 166). And from it is the word witness meaning he judged, God the Almighty said: And a witness from her family testified (Yusuf 12:26). Testimony means he swore, as in the case of cursing, and testified means he bequeathed, as in His saying the Almighty: O you who believe, a testimony between you. And it was said that its meaning here is attending the will. It is said: I witnessed the will of so-and-so, i.e. I attended it.
