The majority disagree with this, then they differed, and the majority are of the opinion that it is permissible for palm trees and grapes, based on the hadith of ‘Atab bin Asid: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him and ordered him to estimate the value of grapes as he estimates palm trees, and to take its zakat in the form of raisins as the zakat of palm trees is taken in the form of dates.” Narrated by Abu Dawud. Dawud ibn Ali said: Estimating the value of zakat is permissible for palm trees, but not for grapes. He rejected the hadith of Atab ibn Asid because it is disconnected and not connected via a sound chain of transmission, as Abu Muhammad Abd al-Haqq said. Ninth: The method of estimation is to estimate how much is on his date palms that is wet and estimate what would be missing if it were to ripen, then he takes into account what remains after the loss and adds some of that to some until the wall is complete, and likewise with grapes in every vine. Tenth: It is sufficient in the case of a single estimate, as in the case of a judge. If there is more in the dates than what was estimated, the owner of the wall is not required to give it, because it is a ruling that has been executed, as stated by Abdul Wahhab. Likewise, if there is less, the zakat is not less. Al-Hasan said: The Muslims used to estimate it for themselves, and then it was taken from them based on that estimate. Eleventh: If the owner of the property considers the estimation too much, the tax collector shall give him the choice of giving him what he estimated and taking his estimation. Abd al-Razzaq mentioned that Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr that he heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: Ibn Rawahah estimated forty thousand wasqs, and he claimed that when the Jews were given the choice, they took the dates and gave him twenty thousand wasqs. Ibn Jurayj said: So I said to Ata’: Is it right for the tax collector, if the master of the property considers the estimation too much, to give him the choice as Ibn Rawahah gave the Jews the choice? He said: Yes, by my life! And what sunnah is better than the sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? Twelfth: The estimation should not be done except after the perfume, according to the hadith of Aisha, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to send Ibn Rawahah to the Jews to estimate the dates of the palm trees when the first dates were ripe, before they were eaten. Then he would give the Jews the choice of taking them according to that estimate or giving them to him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the estimation so that the zakat could be calculated before the fruits were eaten and distributed.” Narrated by Ad-Daraqutni from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj, from Az-Zuhri, from Urwah, from Aishah. He said: It was narrated by Salih ibn Abi Al-Akhdar, from Az-Zuhri, from Ibn Al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, and Malik, Muammar, and Uqayl transmitted it from Az-Zuhri, from Saeed, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Thirteenth: If the assessor estimates, he should deduct a certain amount from his estimate, based on what Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Busti narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: “When you estimate, take and leave a third. If you do not leave a third, leave a quarter.” The wording of Al-Tirmidhi. Abu Dawud said: The assessor leaves a third for the harvest. Yahya Al-Qattan said the same. Abu Hatim Al-Busti said: This hadith has two characteristics: One is that he leaves a third or a quarter of the tenth, and the second is that he leaves that from the dates themselves before they are tithed, if that is a large wall that can bear it. Al-Kharfah with a damma on the kha’: what is picked from the palm trees when their fruit is ripe, i.e. it is picked. It is said: Dates are the harvest of the fasting person, based on Al-Jawhari and Al-Harawi. The well-known view of the Maliki school is that the assessor does not leave anything from the dates of the palm trees and grapes when he estimates them except his estimate. Some of the Medinans narrated that the estimate is made lighter and is left for the loans, the gift, and the like. Fourteenth: If a disaster befalls the fruit after estimation and before harvesting, then zakat is waived on it by consensus of the people of knowledge, unless what remains of it is five wasqs or more. Fifteenth: There is no zakat on less than five awsuq. This is what was explained from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is general in the Book. God Almighty said: O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned and from that which We have produced for you from the earth (al-Baqarah 2:267) and God Almighty said: And give its due. Then the explanation was made of one-tenth and half-tenth. Then since the amount at which the due is taken if the money reaches it is general, He also explained it and said: There is no zakat on less than five wasqs of dates or grains. This negates zakat on vegetables, as they are not considered wasqs. So whoever has five wasqs in his share of dates or grains, zakat is due on him, and the same applies to raisins, which is called the nisab by scholars. It is said: wasq and wasq with a kasra or fatha on the waw, which is sixty sa’s, and a sa’ is four imdads, and a mudd is a pound and a third according to Baghdadi. The amount of five wasqs of imdads is one thousand and two hundred mudds, which is one thousand and six hundred pounds by weight. Sixteenth: If a person has five wasqs of dates and raisins together, zakat is not obligatory on him by consensus, because they are two different types. They also agreed that dates are not to be added to wheat, nor wheat to raisins, nor camels to cows, nor cows to sheep. Sheep are to be added to goats by consensus. They differed about adding wheat to barley and sult, which are: Seventeenth: Malik permitted it in these three in particular only, because they are in the meaning of one type due to their closeness in benefit and their commonality in the place of growth and harvest, and their separation in name does not necessitate their separation in ruling, such as buffalo and cows, goats and sheep. Al-Shafi’i and others said: They should not be combined, because they are different types, their characteristics are different, their names are different, and their taste is different, and that necessitates their separation. And God knows best. Malik said: Legumes are all one type, and some of them are combined with others. Al-Shafi’i said: A grain known by a separate name without its companion, and it is different in creation and taste from others, should not be combined with others. And each type is combined with others, its bad with its good, such as dates and their types, raisins, black and red, and wheat and its types, brown and others. This is the opinion of Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah, his two companions Abu Yusuf, Muhammad and Abu Thawr. Al-Layth said: All grains, legumes and others, are combined with each other in zakat. Ahmad ibn Hanbal was reluctant to combine gold with silver, and combine grains with each other, but at the end of his life he used to say what al-Shafi’i said about it. Eighteenth: Malik said: And what its owner consumed after it had become ripe or after it was crushed, it is counted against him. And what its owner gave him from it in its harvest and pruning, and from the olives in its picking, he investigated that and it is counted against him. Most of the jurists disagree with him in that, and they do not require zakat except for what he obtained in his hand after threshing. Al-Layth said about the zakat of grains: He begins with it before the expenditure, and what he and his family ate of the crushed grain is not counted against him, like the fresh dates that are left for the people of the garden to eat, so he is not keen on them. Al-Shafi’i said: The tax collector leaves for the owner of the garden what he and his family eat fresh, he does not estimate it for them. And what he ate while it was fresh is not counted against him. Abu Omar said: Al-Shafi’i and those who agreed with him cited as evidence the statement of God Almighty: Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit and give its due on the day of its harvest. And they cited as evidence that what was eaten before the harvest is not counted with this verse. And they cited as evidence the statement of the Prophet, peace be upon him: “If you estimate, leave a third. If you do not leave a third, leave a quarter.” And whatever the animals and cows eat from it when threshing is not counted against its owner, according to Malik and others. Nineteenth: What is sold of green beans, chickpeas, and fennel, the amount of that is dry should be determined and its zakat should be paid as grain. Likewise, what is sold of green fruit should be considered and determined and its zakat should be paid as raisins and dates based on that estimate. It was said: It should be paid from its price. Twenty: As for the fruit of the palm tree that does not turn into dates or into raisins from grapes, such as the grapes and dates of Egypt, as well as its olives that are not pressed, Malik said: Its zakat is taken from its price, and its owner is not required to pay anything else, and its price does not reach twenty mithqals or two hundred dirhams, but rather what is considered to reach five wasqs or more is taken into consideration. Al-Shafi’i said: A tenth or half a tenth of it is taken from its middle as dates if its family eats it fresh or feeds it to them. Twenty-one: Abu Dawood narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “In what is watered by the sky, rivers and springs or is rain-fed, the tenth, and in what is watered by waterwheels or by a sprinkler, half of the tenth, and likewise if it is drunk by a runoff, in which there is a tenth.” Which is the running water on the surface of the ground, said Ibn al-Sikkit. The word runoff is mentioned in the hadith, narrated by al-Nasa’i. If it is drunk by a runoff, but the owner of the land does not own the water but rather rents it for him, then it is like the rain, according to the well-known view of the school. Abu al-Hasan al-Lakhmi saw it as being like the sprinkler, so if it is watered once by rain water and once by a bucket, Malik said: It is looked at what the crops were made to grow and were more, then the ruling is based on it. This is the narration of Ibn al-Qasim from him. Ibn Wahb narrated from him: If it is watered for half a year by springs then it stops and he waters the rest of the year by a sprinkler, then he must pay half of its zakat as a tenth, and the other half as a half of the tenth. He said once: Its zakat is according to what completed its life. Al-Shafi’i said: Each one of them is zakat according to its calculation. An example of this is if it is watered for two months by a sprinkler and four by the sky, then two-thirds of the tenth is for the rain water and one-sixth of the tenth is for the sprinkler! Thus, what increases and decreases is calculated. This is how Bakkar ibn Qutaybah issued his fatwa. Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf said: The majority is considered and zakat is given, and no attention is paid to anything else. It was narrated from al-Shafi’i. Al-Tahawi said: Everyone has agreed that if he watered it with rainwater for a day or two, it is not taken into account and no share is given to it. This indicates that the majority is taken into account, and God knows best. I said: This is a summary of the rulings of this verse, and perhaps others will provide more than that based on what God opens up for them. A summary of the meaning of this verse has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, and praise be to God. Twenty-second: As for his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is no charity in love or dates. Narrated by al-Nasa’i. Hamzah al-Kinani said: No one mentioned in this hadith about love other than Ismail ibn Umayyah, who was a trustworthy Qurayshite from the descendants of Sa’id ibn al-’As. He said: This Sunnah was not narrated by any of the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) except Abu Sa’id al-Khudri. Abu ‘Umar said: It is as Hamzah said, and this is a great Sunnah that everyone accepted, and no one narrated it from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from a proven and preserved source except Abu Sa’id. Jabir narrated something similar from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but it is strange. We found it from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah with a good chain of transmission. Twenty-third: The Almighty’s saying: And do not be extravagant. Extravagance in the language is a mistake. An Arab said, referring to some al-Nas 114:I sought you out and wasted you, meaning I missed your place. The poet said: And their speaker said, while the horses were beating them, You have been extravagant. So we replied, We have been extravagant. Extravagance in spending: wastefulness. Musraf is the nickname of Muslim bin Uqbah al-Murri, the owner of the Battle of al-Harrah, because he was extravagant in it. Ali bin Abdullah bin Abbas said: They prevented my dhimmi when the battalions of Masraf and Bani Al-Lakea came The intended meaning of the verse: Do not take something unjustly and then put it in a place other than its rightful place. This was said by Asbagh bin Al-Faraj. Similar to this is the statement of Iyas bin Muawiyah: Whatever you do in excess of God’s command is extravagance and wastefulness. Ibn Zayd said: This is addressed to the rulers, saying: Do not take more than your right and what is not obligatory on the people. Both meanings are possible in his statement, peace be upon him: He who transgresses in charity is like he who withholds it. Mujahid said: If Abu Qubays were gold belonging to a man and he spent it in obedience to God, he would not be extravagant. But if he spent a dirham or a mudd in disobedience to God, he would be extravagant. In this sense, it was said to Hatim: There is no good in extravagance, so he said: There is no extravagance in goodness. I said: This is weak. It is refuted by what Ibn Abbas narrated that Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas went to five hundred palm trees and cut them down, then divided them up in one day and did not leave anything for his family. So the verse: And be not extravagant was revealed, meaning: do not give all of it. Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: Muadh bin Jabal cut down his palm trees and did not stop giving charity until nothing was left of them. So the verse: And be not extravagant was revealed. Al-Suddi said: And be not extravagant means: do not give your money and become poor. It was narrated on the authority of Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan that he was asked about the statement of God the Almighty: And be not extravagant, and he said: Extravagance is when you fall short of the right of God the Almighty. I said: According to this, giving charity with all of one’s money and preventing the giving of the rights of the poor are included in the ruling on extravagance, and justice is the opposite of this, so one gives charity and keeps as he, peace be upon him, said: The best charity is that given from surplus wealth. Unless one is strong-willed, rich in God, trusting in Him, and has no dependents, then he may give all of his money in charity. He may also give the zakat due from him and the specific rights of money that are necessary in some cases. Abdurrahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: Extravagance is that which one cannot return to goodness. Extravagance is that which one can return to goodness. An-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Extravagance is wastefulness and excess, and extravagance is heedlessness and ignorance. Jarir said: They gave Hanida eight hundred dirhams, and there was no extravagance in their giving. Any neglect, and it is said: a mistake. And a man who is careless of heart, meaning he is mistaken of heart and negligent. Tarafa said: A man who is extravagant in heart sees honey in the water of a cloud of insults.
6:142: The Almighty's saying: And among the livestock are loads and furnishings is in apposition to what came before. That is, He created loads and furnishings from the livestock. Scholars have three opinions regarding livestock: The first: That livestock are camels in particular, and this will be explained in An-Nahl. The second: That livestock are camels alone, and if there are cows and sheep with them, then they are also livestock. The third: And it is the most correct, said by Ahmad bin Yahya: Livestock are all animals that God the Almighty has made lawful. The correctness of this is indicated by the Almighty's saying: Lawful to you are the beasts of grazing livestock, except what is recited to you (al-Ma’idah 5:1), and it was mentioned before. Loads are what can carry and work, according to Ibn Mas'ud and others. Then it was said: The expression is specific to camels. It was said: Everything that a living animal can carry, whether a donkey, mule, or camel, according to Abu Zaid, whether it has loads on it or not. Antara said: What surprised me was the load of its people in the middle of the country, pouring out the seeds of the hammam Fa'ulah with the opening of the fa' if it means the doer, the feminine and masculine are the same, like when you say: a man who is foruqah and a woman who is foruqah for a coward or a fearful person. A man who is foruqah and a woman who is foruqah if he does not perform Hajj, and there is no plural for it. If it means the passive participle, the masculine and feminine are differentiated by the ha' like haluba and rikuba. Hamulah with the damma of the ha': loads. As for hamul with the damma of the ha': they are the camels that carry the howdahs, whether there are women on them or not, according to Abu Zaid. And farashan, Ad-Dahhak said: Hamulah from camels and cows. Farash: sheep. Ibn Abbas said: Hamulah is everything that is carried from camels, cows, horses, mules and donkeys. Farash: sheep. Ibn Zaid said: Hamulah is what is ridden, and farash is what its meat is eaten and milked, like sheep, foals and ajajil. They are called farash because of the strength of their bodies and their proximity to farash, which is the flat ground that people tread on. The rajaz poet said: He left me a load and a mattress that I walk on every day. Another said: We have provided you with the furniture from your livestock, the loads, and the partridges. Al-Asma'i said: I have not heard of a plural for it. He said: It is possible that it is a source named after it, from their saying: God spread it out, meaning he spread it out. The furnishings are the furnishings of the house. The furnishings are the plants when they are spread out. The furnishings are the wide open spaces. The furnishings on the camel's leg: a little expansion, which is praiseworthy. And the thing was spread out, so it is a common word. The Almighty's saying: And furnishings may refer to this. An-Nahhas said: And among the best things that have been said about them is that the load is harnessed and tamed for the load. And the furnishings are what God Almighty created from skins and wool for sitting and relaxing on. The rest of the verse has been mentioned previously.
6:143: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: eight pairs. Eight is in the accusative case as a result of an implied verb, meaning, He created eight pairs, according to Al-Kisa’i. Al-Akhfash Saeed said: It is in the accusative case as a substitute for ḥamūlā and Šarshā. Al-Akhfash Ali bin Sulaiman said: It is accusative with eat meaning eat the meat of eight pairs. It is permissible for it to be accusative as a substitute for what in place. It is permissible for it to be accusative with the meaning eat what is permissible, eight pairs of sheep, two. The verse was revealed about Malik bin Awf and his companions when they said: What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives. So God, the Almighty, alerted His Prophet and the believers with this verse to what He has permitted them, lest they be in the position of someone who has forbidden what God, the Almighty, has permitted. A pair is the opposite of an individual. It is said: a pair or an individual. Just as it is said: loss or zaka, even or odd. So his saying: eight pairs means eight individuals. And every individual among the Arabs needs another called a pair. So a male is called a pair and a female is called a pair. The word pair is used for one and two. It is said: they are two pairs, and they are a pair, just as it is said: they are the same and they are equal. And you say: I bought my pair of pigeons. And you mean a male and a female. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Of the sheep two meaning the male and the female. Sheep: are those with wool from the sheep, and it is the plural of Dha’in. The female is Dha’inah, and the plural is Dhawa’in. It was said: it is a plural that has no singular. It was said in its plural: Dha’in, like ‘Abd and ‘Ubaid. And it is said in it: Dha’in. Just as it is said in Dha’ir: barley, the Dhad was broken in imitation. Talha bin Masraf read from the sheep two with the opening of the hamza, and it is a language heard by the Basrans. It is consistent with the Kufians in everything that has a throat letter as the second letter. Likewise the opening and the sukun in the goats. Aban bin Othman read from the sheep two and from the goats two in the nominative case with the beginning. And in the letter Abi. And from the goats two, and it is the reading of the majority. Ibn ‘Amir and Abu ‘Amr read with the opening. An-Nahhas said: The majority in the speech of the Arabs are goats and sheep with the sukun. This is indicated by their saying in the plural: Mu’iz, so this is the plural of Mu’iz. Just as it is said: ‘Abd and ‘Ubaid. Imru’ al-Qais said: And the Banu Shamji bin Jarim give it to them, their goat, your compassion, the compassionate one. The same applies to two sheep and two lambs. The goat is the opposite of the lamb, and it is the one with hair and short tails. It is a generic name, as are the goats, the goats, the amooz, and the goat. The singular of the goat is a goat, like sahib and sahab and tajar and tajar. The female is a goat, which is a female goat, and the plural is mawaiz. The maaz of the people is the one whose goats are many. The maaz is the owner of the goats. Abu Muhammad al-Faqasi said, describing camels with a lot of milk and preferring them to sheep in times of hardship: They measure not to be annihilated, if the goats are content to lick. Al-Mu'izz is the hardness of the earth. Al-Ama'iz is the hard place with many pebbles, and also Al-Mu'aza. The man is serious about his matter: he is serious. Say, 'Are the two males?' is in the accusative case with Haram. "Umm al-Anthayyin" is in apposition to it. And so is "Amma Ashtamal." And a long vowel was added with the alif of connection to differentiate between the question and the report. And it is permissible to delete the hamza because "Umm" indicates a question. As he said: Do you leave the neighborhood or innovate? Third: The scholars said: The verse is an argument against the polytheists regarding the matter of the bahīrah and what was mentioned with it. And their saying: What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives. So it indicates the establishment of debate in knowledge, because God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to debate them and show them the corruption of their saying. And in it is the establishment of the saying by contemplation and analogy. And in it is evidence that if analogy is presented to a text, then the saying by it is invalid. And it is narrated: If it is refuted, because God the Almighty commanded them to use correct comparison, and commanded them to expel their excuse. The meaning is: Tell them that if the males are forbidden, then every male is forbidden. And if the females are forbidden, then every female is forbidden. And if what the wombs of the two females contain is forbidden, meaning of sheep and goats, then every newborn is forbidden, whether male or female. All of them are born, so all of them are forbidden because the cause is present in them. So, between the invalidity of their cause and the corruption of their statement, God Almighty informed us that what they did was a slander against Him. Inform Me with knowledge, meaning with knowledge, if you have it, where did this prohibition that you fabricated come from? And they have no knowledge, because they do not read books.
6:144: And the statement in: And of the camels two and what follows it is as mentioned previously, Or were you witnesses? meaning, did you witness God forbidding this? And when the proof became necessary for them, they began to fabricate and said: This is what God has commanded. So God Almighty said: Then who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God to lead people astray without knowledge? He made it clear that they lied, as they said what there was no evidence for.
6:145: The Almighty said: "Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden." In this verse, God the Almighty knows what is forbidden. The meaning is: Say, O Muhammad, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden except these things, not what you forbid with your desires. The verse was revealed in Mecca. There were no forbidden things in the Sharia at that time except these things. Then Surah Al-Ma'idah was revealed in Medina. And more were added to the forbidden things, such as strangled animals, animals beaten to death, animals that have fallen from a fall, animals that have been gored, alcohol, and others. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade in Medina the eating of all fanged beasts of prey and all talons of birds. Scholars have differed on the ruling of this verse and its interpretation in several opinions: The first: What we have indicated, that this verse is Meccan, and every forbidden thing that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade or that came in the Book and is included in it, is an additional ruling from God the Almighty on the tongue of His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This is the opinion of most scholars of contemplation, jurisprudence and tradition. Similar to it is the marriage of a woman to her paternal aunt and maternal aunt with His statement: And all beyond that is lawful for you (An-Nisa’: 24) and His ruling on the oath with a witness with His statement: But if there are not two men, then a man and two women (al-Baqarah 2:282), which has been mentioned previously. It has been said that it was abrogated by His statement (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Eating all fanged beasts of prey is forbidden. Narrated by Malik, and it is an authentic hadith. It was said that the verse is decisive and only what is in it is forbidden. This is a statement narrated from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar and Aisha, and it was narrated from them to be different. Malik said: There is nothing clearly forbidden except what is mentioned in this verse. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: This verse includes the permissibility of everything from animals and others except what is excluded in the verse from dead animals, spilled blood and pork. For this reason we said: The meat of beasts of prey and all other animals except humans and pigs is permissible. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: Al-Shafi’i based his permissibility of everything that is not mentioned, taking it from this verse, except what is indicated by evidence. It was said that the verse is an answer to someone who asked about a specific thing, so the answer was specific. This is the view of Al-Shafi’i. Al-Shafi’i narrated from Sa’id ibn Jubayr that he said: In this verse there are things that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) asked about, and he answered them about the forbidden things among those things. It was said: That is, I do not find in what was revealed to me, that is, in this case, the case of the revelation and the time of its descent, then it is not impossible for a revelation to occur after that prohibiting other things. Ibn al-Arabi claimed that this verse is Medinan, but it is Meccan according to the majority. It was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day This day I have perfected for you your religion (al-Ma’idah 5:3) was revealed to him, and no abrogator was revealed after it, so it is decisive, and there is nothing forbidden except what is in it, and I am inclined to that. I said: This is what I saw others say. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr mentioned the consensus that Surat Al-Aam is Meccan except for the words of God Almighty: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you” (al-Ma’idah 5:10). Much of the Qur’an and many Sunnahs were revealed after them. The prohibition of alcohol was revealed in Medina in Al-Ma’idah. They agreed that his prohibition of eating all fanged beasts of prey was only in Medina. Ismail bin Ishaq said: All of this indicates that it was a command that was in Medina after the words “Say: I do not find in what was revealed to me” were revealed because that was Meccan. I said: This is the source of disagreement among scholars. A group of scholars have deviated from the apparent meaning of the hadiths that prohibit eating all fanged beasts of prey, because they came after them and the limitation to them is apparent, so taking them is more appropriate, because they either abrogate what came before them or outweigh those hadiths. As for those who say it is forbidden, it has become clear to them and proven to them that Surat Al-An'am is Meccan, revealed before the Hijrah, and that this verse was intended to refute the Jahiliyyah in forbidding the bahīrah, the sā'ibah, the wasīlah, and the Ḥāmī. Then after that, many things were forbidden, such as domesticated donkeys, the meat of mules, and others, and all fanged beasts of prey and all birds with talons. Abu 'Umar said: According to the opinion of those who say: There is nothing forbidden except what is in it, that what is not intentionally mentioned in the name of God is not forbidden, and the forbidden wine is considered permissible according to the group of Muslims. The consensus of Muslims on the prohibition of grape wine is clear evidence that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, found in what was revealed to him something forbidden other than what was in Surat Al-An'am from what was revealed after it in the Qur'an. The narrations from Malik differed regarding the meat of wild animals, donkeys and mules. He said once: It is forbidden, because of what was reported from his (peace be upon him) prohibition of that, and this is the correct statement according to what is in Al-Muwatta. He said once: It is disliked, and this is the apparent meaning of Al-Mudawwana, because of the apparent meaning of the verse, and because of what was reported from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar and Aisha about the permissibility of eating it, and this is the statement of Al-Awza’i. Al-Bukhari narrated from the narration of Amr ibn Dinar who said: I said to Jabir ibn Zayd: They claim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the meat of domesticated donkeys. He said: Al-Hakam bin Amr Al-Ghifari used to say that in our place in Basra, but Al-Bahr bin Abbas refused that and recited: Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar that he was asked about the meat of wild animals and he said: There is nothing wrong with it. He was asked: The hadith of Abu Tha’labah Al-Khushani, so he said: We do not abandon the Book of God, our Lord, for the sake of a Bedouin who urinates on his legs. Al-Sha’bi was asked about the meat of elephants and lions, so he recited this verse. Al-Qasim said: Aisha used to say when she heard people saying that all fanged beasts of prey are forbidden: That is permissible, and she would recite this verse: “Say: I do not find within what has been revealed to me anything forbidden.” Then she said: If the pot’s water is yellow from blood and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sees it, he does not forbid it. What is correct in this matter is what we began by mentioning, and that what is mentioned about the forbidden things after the verse is included in it and conjoined with it. Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi referred to this in his book Al-Qabas, contrary to what was mentioned in his Ahkam. He said: It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that this verse was among the last to be revealed, so the people of Baghdad among our companions said: Everything other than it is permissible, but eating beasts of prey is disliked. According to the jurists of the countries, including Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, and Abdul Malik, eating all fanged beasts of prey is forbidden. It is not impossible for the addition to occur after his saying: “Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden,” based on the evidence for it, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The blood of a Muslim man shall not be shed except for one of three reasons, and he mentioned disbelief, adultery, and murder. Then our scholars said: The reasons for murder are ten according to the evidence that has been reported, since the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only informs of what he has attained of knowledge from the Almighty Creator, and He erases what He wills, confirms, abrogates, and decrees. It has been proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Eating all fanged beasts of prey is forbidden. It has been narrated that he forbade eating all fanged beasts of prey and all talons of birds. Muslim narrated on the authority of Ma'n on the authority of Malik: He forbade eating all talons of birds. The first is more correct, and the prohibition of all fanged beasts of prey is the explicit doctrine, and Malik translated it in Al-Muwatta' when he said: The prohibition of eating all fanged beasts of prey. Then he mentioned the hadith and followed it by saying: And this is the matter with us. So he informed that the action is consistent with the effect. Al-Qushayri said: Malik's saying that this verse was among the last to be revealed does not prevent us from saying: The prohibition of some of these things was proven after this verse, and God has permitted good things and forbidden bad things, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade eating all fanged beasts of prey, and eating all talons of birds, and he forbade the meat of domestic donkeys in the year of Khaybar. What indicates the correctness of this interpretation is the consensus on the prohibition of excrement, urine, disgusting insects, and red things that are not mentioned in this verse. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Forbidden. Ibn Atiyyah said: When the word prohibition is mentioned by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then it is suitable to end with the mentioned thing, the ultimate prohibition and prevention, and it is also suitable according to the language to stop short of the ultimate in dislike and the like. So whatever is coupled with an indication of submission from the interpreting companions and all of them agreed upon it and the wording of the hadiths is not confused, then it is obligatory by the Shari’ah that its prohibition has reached the ultimate in prohibition and prevention, and is included with pigs, dead animals and blood, and this is the description of the prohibition of wine. And whatever is coupled with an indication of confusion in the wording of the hadiths and the imams differed about it despite their knowledge of the hadiths, such as his saying, peace be upon him: Eating all fanged beasts of prey is forbidden. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade eating all fanged beasts of prey. Then the Companions and those who came after them differed about the prohibition of that. It is permissible for those who consider these aspects to interpret the wording of the prohibition to mean the prohibition, which is dislike and the like. And what is accompanied by an indication of interpretation, such as his (peace be upon him) prohibition of the meat of domesticated donkeys, some of the companions who were present interpreted that because it is impure, and some of them interpreted it so that people would not lose faith, and some of them interpreted it as pure prohibition. And it is proven in the nation that there is disagreement about the prohibition of its meat, so it is permissible for those scholars who consider the wording of the prohibition to mean the prohibition, which is dislike and the like, according to their own efforts and analogy. I said: This is a good contract in this chapter and in the reason for the disagreement on what was mentioned above. It has been said: The donkey is not to be eaten, because it showed its evil nature when it mated with a male and committed sodomy, so it was called filth. Muhammad ibn Sirin said: There is no animal that does the work of the people of Lot except the pig and the donkey. Al-Tirmidhi mentioned it in Nawader al-Usul. Third: Amr bin Dinar narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Shatha’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to eat some things and leave others. Then God sent His Prophet, peace be upon him, and revealed His Book and made lawful what He made lawful and forbade what He made unlawful. So whatever He made lawful is lawful, whatever He forbade is unlawful, and whatever He was silent about is pardoned. Then he recited this verse: “Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden.” Meaning, whatever is not clearly forbidden is permissible according to the apparent meaning of this verse. Al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of Ubaydullah bin Abdullah bin Abbas that he recited: “Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden.” He said: The only thing forbidden from dead animals is what is eaten from them, which is the meat. As for the skin, bones, wool, and hair, they are permissible. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Mulqam bin Talb on the authority of his father who said: I accompanied the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I did not hear any prohibition against eating any insect on earth. Insects: small creatures of the earth, such as lizards, lizards, hedgehogs, and the like. The poet said: We ate usury, O Umm Amr, and whoever is a stranger to you eats insects. Anything that creeps and crawls. Rabbah is the plural of Rabbah, which is a mouse. Al-Khattabi said: His statement, I have not heard of it being forbidden, does not indicate that it is permissible, because it is possible that someone else may have heard it. People differed regarding the jerboa, the fur, the plural, and similar insects. Urwah, Ata, Al-Shafi’i, and Abu Thawr permitted the jerboa. Al-Shafi’i said: There is nothing wrong with the fur, but Ibn Sirin, Al-Hakam, Hammad, and the People of Opinion disliked it. The People of Opinion disliked the hedgehog. Malik ibn Anas was asked about it, and he said: I do not know. Abu Amr narrated: Malik said: There is nothing wrong with eating the hedgehog. Abu Thawr did not see anything wrong with it, and he narrated it from Al-Shafi’i. Ibn Umar was asked about it, so he recited, “Say: I do not find in that which has been revealed to me anything forbidden” Al-Akhbar 2:13. An old man in his presence said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: It was mentioned to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said: It is an evil of evils. Ibn ‘Umar said: “If the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said this, then it is as he said.” Narrated by Abu Dawood. Malik said: There is nothing wrong with eating the lizard, jerboa and monitor lizard, and he said that eating snakes is permissible if they are slaughtered. This is the opinion of Ibn Abi Layla and al-Awza’i, as well as snakes, scorpions, mice, lizards, hedgehogs and frogs. Ibn al-Qasim said: There is nothing wrong with eating the vermin of the earth, its scorpions and its worms according to Malik, because he said that its death in wealth does not spoil it. Malik said: There is nothing wrong with eating bee chicks, cheese worms, dates and the like. The evidence for this is the hadeeth of Mulqam ibn Talab, the opinion of Ibn ‘Abbaas and Abu al-Darda’: What God has made permissible is permissible, what God has forbidden is forbidden, and what He has remained silent about is forgiven. Aisha said about the mouse: It is not forbidden, and she recited: “Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden.” Among the scholars of Madinah are a group who do not permit eating all the vermin of the earth and its insects, such as snakes, lizards, mice and the like. Everything that is permissible is…” Killing it is not permissible for them to eat it, and they do not perform ritual slaughter on it. This is the opinion of Ibn Shihab, Urwah, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifah and his companions and others. According to Malik and his companions, none of the wild beasts of prey are to be eaten, nor the domestic cat nor the wild one, because they are beasts of prey. He said: The hyena and the fox are not to be eaten, and there is nothing wrong with eating all the wild birds of prey, the vulture, the eagle, the hawk, and others, whether they eat carcasses or not. Al-Awza’i said that it is all permissible, except that they dislike the vulture. Malik’s argument is that he did not find any of the people of knowledge who disliked eating the wild birds of prey, and he rejected the hadith “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He forbade eating any bird with talons. It was narrated on the authority of Ashhab that he said: There is no harm in eating an elephant if it is slaughtered. This is the opinion of Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Shafi’i forbade it. Al-Nu’man and his companions disliked eating hyenas and foxes. Al-Shafi’i permitted that, and it was narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas that he used to eat hyenas. Malik’s argument is the general prohibition against eating any wild animal with fangs, and he did not specify seven out of seven. The hadith of the hyena that was narrated by al-Nasa’i permitting its eating is not something that contradicts the hadith of prohibition, because it is a hadith that was narrated only by Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Ammar, and he is not well-known for transmitting knowledge, nor is he one of those who can be used as evidence if someone more reliable than him contradicts it. Abu Omar said: The prohibition of eating any fanged beast of prey has been narrated through many chains of narration. This was narrated by a group of trustworthy and reliable imams, and it is impossible for them to contradict it with something like the hadith of Ibn Abi Ammar. Abu Omar said: The Muslims are unanimously agreed that it is not permissible to eat monkeys because the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) forbade eating them, and it is not permissible to sell them because there is no benefit in them. He said: I do not know of anyone who permitted eating them, except what Abd al-Razzaq mentioned on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Ayyub: Mujahid was asked about eating monkeys, and he said: They are not from the livestock. I said: Ibn al-Mundhir mentioned that he said: We narrated on the authority of Ata that he was asked about a monkey killed in the sanctuary, so he said: It is judged by two just men. He said: According to the doctrine of Ata, it is permissible to eat its meat, because the penalty is not due on the one who kills something other than game. In Bahr al-Madhhab by al-Ruwayani, according to the doctrine of Imam al-Shafi’i: Al-Shafi’i said that it is permissible to sell a monkey because it is known and used to protect goods. Al-Kashfli narrated on the authority of Ibn Shuraih that it is permissible to sell it because it is used. He was asked: What is the point of benefiting from it? He said: It makes children happy. Abu Omar said: The dog, the elephant, and the fanged animal are all like the monkey in my opinion. The evidence is in the statement of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, not in the statement of anyone else. Some people have claimed that there were no Arabs who ate dog meat except a people from Faqas. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar that he said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) forbade eating jallalah and its milk. In another narration: Regarding jallalah in camels, that one should ride them or drink their milk. Al-Halaimi Abu Abdullah said: As for jallalah, it is that which eats dung from animals, chickens and dung beetles. The Prophet (peace be upon him) forbade their meat. The scholars said: Anything that has the smell of dung in its meat or taste is forbidden, and whatever does not appear is permissible. Al-Khattabi said: This is a prohibition to purify and clean it, because if it feeds on jalla, which is dung, its stench is found in its meat, and this is if its fodder is absent from it. However, if it grazes on grass and eats grain and also gets some jalla, then it is not jallalah, but rather it is like dung beetle chickens and similar animals that may get some from it and most of its food and fodder is from something else, so eating it is not disliked. The scholars of opinion, Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad said: It should not be eaten until it is kept for a few days and fed other fodder. Then, if its meat tastes good, it should be eaten. It was narrated in a hadith: The cows are fed for forty days and then their meat is eaten. Ibn Umar used to keep the chickens locked up for three days and then slaughter them. Ishaq said: There is nothing wrong with eating them after washing their meat well. Al-Hasan did not see anything wrong with eating the meat of a camel, and so did Malik ibn Anas. From this perspective, it was forbidden to throw dung on the ground. It was narrated from one of them that he said: "We used to rent the land of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and we would stipulate that whoever rented it would not throw dung on it." It was narrated from Ibn Umar that he used to rent his land and stipulated that it would not be covered with dung. It was narrated that a man used to cultivate his land with dung, so Umar said to him: You are the one who feeds people what comes out of them. They differed about eating horses, so Al-Shafi'i permitted it, which is the correct view, and Malik disliked it. As for the mule, it is a cross between a donkey and a horse, one of which is permissible or disliked, which is the horse, and the other is forbidden, which is the donkey, so the ruling of prohibition prevails, because if permissibility and prohibition are combined in one thing, the ruling of prohibition prevails. This issue will be explained in An-Nahl, God willing, in a more comprehensive manner. The ruling on locusts will be mentioned in Al-A’raf. The majority of predecessors and successors are of the opinion that it is permissible to eat rabbits. It has been reported that Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Al-Aas forbade it. Ibn Abi Laila disliked it. Abdullah ibn Amr said: It was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while I was sitting, but he did not eat it and did not forbid eating it. He claimed that it causes menstruation.” Narrated by Abu Dawud. An-Nasa’i narrated it in a mursal form on the authority of Musa ibn Talhah, who said: A man brought the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a rabbit that had been roasted and said: O Messenger of God, I saw blood on it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left it and did not eat it, and said to those with him: Eat it, for if I desired it, I would eat it. I said: There is nothing in this that indicates its prohibition, but rather it is something similar to what he, peace be upon him, said: It was not in my people’s land, so I find it disgusting. Muslim narrated in his Sahih, “On the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: We passed by Marr Adh-Dhahran and we came across a rabbit. We ran after it and lost it. He said: “So I ran until I caught up with it, then I brought it to Abu Talha, who slaughtered it. He sent its hip and thigh to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he kissed it.” Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: On a eater who feeds him meaning an eater who eats him. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Amir that he read awha with the opening of the hamza. Ali bin Abi Talib read yata’mu with a heavy ta’, meaning he wanted to eat him, so it was assimilated. Aisha and Muhammad bin al-Hanafiyyah read on a eater who tastes him with a past tense verb except that it is a dead body read with the ya’ and the ta’, meaning unless the eye, body, or soul is dead. It was read with the ya’ dead in the nominative case meaning that it occurs and causes death. Al-Masfooh is the flowing that flows, which is forbidden. Other than that, it is excused. Al-Mawardi narrated that if the blood that is not shed has veins that it congeals on, such as the liver and spleen, then it is permissible, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Two dead animals and two types of blood have been made lawful for us. The hadith says. And if it does not have veins that can be frozen on it, but rather is with the meat, then there are two opinions regarding its prohibition: One of them is that it is prohibited, because it is part of the spilled meat or some of it. And the spilled meat was mentioned to exclude the liver and spleen from it. The second is that it is not prohibited, because the prohibition is specific to the spilled meat. I said: This is correct. Imran bin Jadir said: I asked Abu Majlaz about the flesh that is stained with blood, and about the pot that is covered with redness from blood, so he said: There is nothing wrong with it, God only forbade that which is spilled. Aisha and others said something similar, and the scholars agree on this. Ikrimah said: If it were not for this verse, the Muslims would have followed from the veins what the Jews followed. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: There is nothing wrong with blood in a vein or marrow. This and the ruling of the one in need have been mentioned previously in the case of the cow, and God knows best.
6:146: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And We have forbidden to those who are Jews all animals having claws. When God the Almighty mentioned what He had forbidden to the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, He followed that by mentioning what He had forbidden to the Jews, because that would be a denial of their saying: God did not forbid us anything, but we forbade ourselves what Israel had forbidden to himself. The meaning of they were Jews has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. This prohibition on those who are Jews is a command to test and punish. The first thing mentioned of the prohibitions on them is all animals having claws. Al-Hasan read dhafar with a sukoon on the fa’. Abu Al-Samal read dhafar with a kasra on the dha’ and a sukoon on the fa’. Abu Hatim denied the kasra on the dha’ and a sukoon on the fa’, and did not mention this reading, which is a language. And dhafar with a kasra on both of them. The plural is adhfar nails, adhfur nails, and athafir nails, as Al-Jawhari said. An-Nahhas added on the authority of Al-Farra’ adhāfir nails and athafir nails. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: It is said that a man has long nails, just as it is said that a man has long hair. Mujahid and Qatada said: Those with claws are those among the animals and birds that do not have separate digits, such as camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks. Ibn Zayd said: Only camels. Ibn Abbas said: Those with claws are the camels and ostriches, because the ostrich has claws like camels. It was said: It means every bird with claws and an animal with hooves. The hoof is called a nail as a metaphor. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim said: The hoof is a nail, and the claw is a nail, except that this is according to its capacity, and that is according to its capacity, and there is no metaphor here. Do you not see that both are cut and taken from, and both are the same type: soft, loose bone. Its origin is from food that grows, so it is cut like a human nail. It is called a digger because it digs the ground by stepping on it. It is called a claw because it licks birds with the heads of those needles. It is called a nail because it takes things with its nail, meaning that humans and birds grab it. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And of the cattle and the sheep We have forbidden them their fat. Qatada said: He means the thorub and the fat of the kidneys, and Al-Suddi said the same. The thorub is the plural of thrab, which is the thin fat that is on the stomach. Ibn Jurayj said: He forbade them all fat that is not mixed with a bone or on a bone, and He permitted them the fat of the side and the buttocks, because it is on the coccyx. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Except what their backs carry is in the accusative case as an exception, their backs are raised by carried. Or the entrails is in the nominative case as an apposition to the backs, meaning or their entrails carry. The alif and lam are a substitute for the addition. Accordingly, the entrails are among what is permissible. Or what is mixed with bone is in the accusative case as an apposition to what it carries. This is the most correct statement about it. It is the statement of Al-Kisa’i, Al-Farra’, and Ahmad bin Yahya. Consideration requires that a thing be conjoined with what follows it, unless its meaning is correct or evidence indicates otherwise. It was said: The exception in the permissibility is only what the backs carry in particular, and His saying: Or the entrails or what is mixed with bone is conjoined with what is forbidden. The meaning is: Their fat or the entrails or what is mixed with bone are forbidden to them, except what the backs carry, for it is not forbidden. Al-Shafi’i used this verse as evidence that whoever swears not to eat fat has broken his oath by eating the fat of the backs, because God Almighty has excluded what is on their backs from the category of fat. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: or the containers: Al-Hawaya: are the camels, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It is the plural of Mub’ar, and it was named that because dung gathered in it. It is manure. The singular of Al-Hawaya is Hawiya, like Qasa’a and Qawasi’. It was also said: Hawiya like Daraba and Dawareb. It was also said: Hawiya like Safina and Safwan. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Hawaya is what is contained in the stomach, meaning it is round. It is curved, meaning round. It was also said: Al-Hawaya are the milk treasuries, and it is connected to the camels, which are the intestines. It was also said: Al-Hawaya are the intestines on which the fat is. Al-Hawaya in other places: a cloak that is wrapped around the camel’s hump. Imru’ al-Qais said: They made the Hawaiya and sat down and lightened the ornate Iraqi ruling Then God the Almighty informed us that He had written for them this prohibition in the Torah in response to their lie. The text of it is: Forbidden to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, every animal that does not have a split hoof, and every fish that does not have a white spot. Then God abrogated all of that with the law of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He permitted them what was forbidden to them from animals, and removed the hardship with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and obligated the creation of the religion of Islam to permit and prohibit, command and prohibit. Fifth: If they slaughtered their livestock and ate what God permitted for them in the Torah and left what He prohibited for them, is it permissible for us? Malik said in the Book of Muhammad: It is forbidden. He said in Sama’ al-Mabsoot: It is permissible, and Ibn Nafi’ said the same. Ibn al-Qasim said: I dislike it. The first reason is that they believe in its prohibition and do not intend it when slaughtering, so it is forbidden like blood. The second reason, which is correct, is that God the Almighty lifted that prohibition with Islam, and their belief in it has no effect, because it is a corrupt belief, as Ibn al-Arabi said. I say: And what indicates its correctness is what the two Sahihs narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mughaffal, who said: “We were besieging the palace of Khaybar, and a man threw a bag of fat, so I jumped to take it, but I turned around and saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and I felt shy of him.” Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim. “Abdullah ibn Mughaffal said: I found a bag of fat on the day of Khaybar, so I grabbed it and said: I will not give anyone anything of this today. I turned around and saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) smiling.” Our scholars said: His (peace be upon him) smiled because he saw how eager Ibn Mughaffal was to take the bag and how he was stingy with it, and he did not order him to throw it away or forbid him. The view of Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi’i and most scholars is that it is permissible to eat it, except that Malik disliked it due to the difference of opinion on it. Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from Malik that it was forbidden, and the leading companions of Malik agreed with him. Their basis is what was mentioned above, and the hadith is an argument against them. If they slaughtered every animal with claws, Asbagh said: Whatever of their slaughtered animals was forbidden in the Book of God, it is not permissible to eat it, because they are religious. By forbidding it. Ashab and Ibn Al-Qasim said this, and Ibn Wahb permitted it. Ibn Habib said: What was forbidden to them, and we learned that from our book, is not permissible for us from their slaughtered animals. And what we do not know to be forbidden except from their sayings and their own efforts, is not forbidden for us from their slaughtered animals. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: That meaning that is the prohibition. So that is in the nominative case, meaning that is the matter. We recompensed them for their transgression meaning for their injustice, as a punishment for them for killing the prophets and preventing people from the path of God, and taking usury and making people’s money lawful unjustly. This is evidence that the prohibition only occurs for a sin, because it is a restriction and one does not deviate from the spaciousness to it except when held accountable. And indeed, We are truthful in our telling of these Jews what We prohibited them of meat and fat.
6:147: The Almighty’s saying: But if they deny you is a condition, and the answer is Then say, ‘Your Lord is full of vast mercy’ meaning, from the vastness of His mercy, He is forbearing towards you, so He does not punish you in this world. Then He informed them of the punishment He has prepared for them in the Hereafter, saying: And His punishment will not be averted from the criminal people. It was said that the meaning is that His punishment will not be averted from the criminal people if He intends it to happen in this world.
6:148: God the Almighty said: Those who associate others with God will say Mujahid said: meaning the infidels of Quraysh. They said: If God had willed, we would not have associated others with God, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything meaning the bahīrah, the sā'ibah, and the wasīlah. God the Almighty informed of the unseen of what they would say, and they thought that this would be a basis for them because the argument was binding on them and they were certain of the falsehood of what they were doing. The meaning is: If God had willed, He would have sent a messenger to our fathers who would have forbidden them from associating others with God and from forbidding what He had made lawful for them, so that they would desist, and we would have followed them in that. God responded to that and said: Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us? meaning, do you have evidence that this is such and such? You follow nothing but conjecture in this statement. And you are only guessing to make your weak ones think that you have an argument. His saying, nor our fathers is in apposition to the nun in we associated, and he did not say we nor our fathers, because his saying nor takes the place of emphasizing the implied, and for this reason it is appropriate to say: Neither Zayd nor I stood up.
6:149: The Almighty said: "Say: To God belongs the conclusive argument" meaning that which cuts off the excuse of the one being argued, and removes the doubt of the one who looks into it. His conclusive argument according to this is His clarification that He is the One, and His sending of messengers and prophets. He clarified monotheism by looking into the creation, and supported the messengers with miracles, and His command is binding on every accountable person. As for His knowledge, will, and speech, they are unseen and the servant does not know them, except for the messenger He is pleased with. It is sufficient for the account to be such that if the servant wanted to do what he was commanded to do, he would be able to. The Mu'tazila confused His statement: If God had willed, we would not have associated others with Him, and they said: God has condemned those who made their association of others out of His will. Their reliance on that is invalid, because God the Almighty only condemned them for abandoning their efforts in seeking the truth. They only said that in mockery and play. Similar to it is: And they said, 'If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them' (al-Zukhruf 43:20). If they had said it out of respect, reverence and recognition of Him, He would not have criticized them, because God Almighty says: And if God had willed, they would not have associated others with Him (al-An’am 6:107). They would not have believed unless God willed (al-An’am 6:111). And if He had willed, He could have guided you all (al-Nahl 16:9). And there are many like it. So the believers say it so that they may be among them in God Almighty.
6:150: God the Almighty said: "Say: 'Bring your witnesses'" meaning say to these polytheists: Bring your witnesses that God has forbidden what you have forbidden. Halam is a word that is an invitation to something, and it is the same for the people of Hijaz, whether singular or plural, male or female, except in the dialect of Najd, where they say: Halma Halmu Halmi, bringing the sign as it is in all other verbs. The Quran was written in the dialect of the people of Hijaz, God the Almighty said: And those who say to their brothers, 'Come to us' (al-Ahzab 33:18) He says: Halma means come or come near. And Halmat al-ta'am means bring the food. The meaning here is: Bring your witnesses. The meem is opened because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as you say: Return, oh this one. It is not permissible to add a damma or kasra to it. According to Al-Khalil, the original form is ha, with lam added to it, then the alif was deleted due to frequent use. Another said: The original form is hal, with lam added to it. It was said: It is, as it is pronounced, denoting the meaning of bring. In the book Al-Ain by Al-Khalil: Its origin is hal a’um, meaning do I intend to come to you, then they used it more and more until the intended meaning of saying it became attend, just as ta’al originally meant that the arrogant person would say it to the lowly person, so they used it more and more until the lowly person would say to the arrogant person ta’al. God Almighty says: If they testify, meaning if some of them testify to others, then do not testify with them, meaning do not believe that they gave testimony except from a book or on the tongue of a prophet, and they do not have anything of that with them.
6:151: It contains fourteen issues: First: The Almighty said: “Say: Come, I will recite.” That is, come forward and recite the truth and certainty as my Lord has revealed to me, not assumption or lie as you have claimed. Then He explained that and said: Do not associate anything with Him. It is said to a man: Come, meaning come forward, and to a woman: Come, and to two women: Come, and to a group of men: Come, and to a group of women: Come. God Almighty said: Then come, I will provide for you. (al-Ahzab 33:28). They made coming forward a consequence of being exalted and elevated, because the one commanded to come forward in the original formulation of this action is as if he was sitting and it was said to him: Come, meaning raise yourself by standing and coming forward, and they expanded on it until they made it for the one standing and the one walking, as Ibn Al-Shajari said. Second: The Almighty’s saying: What He has forbidden The face of what is that it is a report item in the accusative case with atala and the meaning is: Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden to you. If you connect it to haram then that is the correct view, because it is the closest and is the choice of the Basrans. If you connect it to atala then that is good because it is the first and is the choice of the Kufians. So the meaning in this statement is I recite to you what your Lord has forbidden. “That you do not associate” is in the accusative case with the estimation of a verb from the wording of the first, meaning I recite to you that you do not associate, meaning I recite to you the prohibition of associating, and it is possible that it is accusative due to what is in alaimah of enticement, and alaimah is disconnected from what precedes it, meaning you must abandon associating, and you must be kind to your parents, and you must not kill your children and you must not approach immoralities. Just as you say: Your concern is your concern, meaning stick to your concern. And as he said: Your concern is yourselves (al-Ma’idah 5:105) Ibn Al-Shajari said all of it. Al-Nahhas said: It is permissible for an to be in the accusative case instead of ma, meaning I recite to you the prohibition of polytheism. Al-Farra’ preferred that la be for prohibition, because after it is wa la. Third: This verse is a command from God Almighty to His Prophet, peace be upon him, to call all creation to listen to the recitation of what God has forbidden. And thus it is incumbent upon the scholars who come after him to inform the people and explain to them what God has forbidden them from what He has permitted. God Almighty said: You must make it clear to the people and do not conceal it (Al Imran 3:187). Ibn Al Mubarak mentioned: Isa bin Omar told us on the authority of Amr bin Murrah that he told them that Rabi bin Khaitham said to a companion of his: Would you like to be given a scroll from the Prophet, peace be upon him, whose seal was not broken? He said: Yes. He said: Then read: “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you.” So he recited until the end of the three verses. Kaab Al Ahbar said: This verse is the opening of the Torah: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. “Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you.” Ibn Abbas said: These decisive verses that God mentioned in Surat Al Imran were agreed upon by the laws of creation, and they were never abrogated in any religion. It was said: They are the ten words revealed to Moses. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And to parents, do good. Doing good to parents means being dutiful to them, protecting them, preserving them, obeying their commands, removing slavery from them, and leaving authority over them. And doing good is in the accusative case as a source, and its subject is an implied verb from its wording, meaning, and do good to parents, do good. Fifth: The Almighty said: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. Poverty means: do not bury your daughters alive for fear of poverty, for I will provide for you and for them. Some of them did that with females and males for fear of poverty, as is apparent in the verse. To become poor means to become poor. And to make him poor means to make him poor, so it is intransitive and transitive. Al-Naqqash narrated from a historian that he said: Poverty is hunger in the language of Lakhm. Mundhir bin Saeed mentioned that poverty is spending, it is said: he made his money poor meaning he spent it. He mentioned that Ali, may God be pleased with him, said to his wife: Spend from your money as you wish. A man who is a flatterer speaks with his tongue what is not in his heart. So flattery is a common word that will be explained in its place. Sixth - This may be used as evidence by those who forbid coitus interruptus, because infanticide removes the existing and the offspring, and coitus interruptus prevents the origin of the offspring, so they are similar, except that killing a soul is a greater sin and a more heinous act, and for this reason some of our scholars said that it is understood from his saying, peace be upon him, regarding coitus interruptus: That hidden infanticide means dislike, not prohibition. A group of the Companions and others said this. A group of the Companions, Followers, and jurists also said it was permissible, based on the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): There is no blame upon you for not doing it, for it is fate. That is, there is no blame upon you for not doing it. Al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna understood from it the prohibition and warning against coitus interruptus. The first interpretation is more appropriate, based on the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): And if God wills to create something, nothing can prevent Him. Malik and al-Shafi’i said: It is not permissible to withdraw from a free woman except with her permission. It seems that they saw ejaculation as part of her pleasure and her right to a child, and they did not see that in the case of a woman who has been penetrated by her right hand, since he may withdraw from her without her permission, since she has no right to any of what was mentioned. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed is similar to the saying: And leave the outward of sin and what is hidden (al-An’am 6:120). His saying: what is apparent is a prohibition against all types of immoralities, which are the transgressions. And what is hidden is what the heart has resolved to do in terms of disobedience. Apparent and hidden are two states that fulfill the categories of what they were made for from things. What is apparent is an accusative in place of immoralities, and what is hidden is in apposition to it. Eighth - The Almighty said: And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. The alif and lam in al-nafs are to define the type, as in their saying: People were destroyed by the love of the dirham and the dinar. And similar to it is: Indeed, man was created anxious. (al-Ma’arij 70:19) Do you not see His Almighty saying: Except those who pray? And likewise His saying: By time, indeed, man is in loss. (Al-‘Asr: 1-2) because He said: Except those who believe. And this verse is a prohibition against killing a forbidden soul, whether it is a believer or a covenanted person, except by right that necessitates killing it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ So whoever says, ‘There is no god but God,’ his wealth and his life are protected, except for what is due, and their reckoning is with God.” This right includes several things, including withholding zakat and abandoning prayer. Abu Bakr fought those who withheld zakat, and in the Qur’an, But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakat, let them go on their way. (al-Tawbah 9:5) This is clear. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “The blood of a Muslim is not permissible except in three cases: the married person who commits adultery, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community.” And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If allegiance is given to two caliphs, kill the latter of them. Narrated by Muslim. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever you find doing the work of the people of Lot, kill the one who does it and the one to whom it is done. This will be explained in Al-A’raf. In the Qur’an, it is stated: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive to cause corruption upon earth is that they be killed. (al-Ma’idah 5:33) The verse. And He said: And if two parties among the believers should fight. (al-Hujurat 49:9) The verse. Likewise, whoever splits the unity of the Muslims, opposes the leader of their group, divides their word, and strives to cause corruption upon earth by plundering families and wealth, and transgressing against the ruler and refusing his rule, he shall be killed. This is the meaning of His statement: except by right. He, peace be upon him, said: “The blood of the believers is equal, and the lowest of them is responsible for their protection. A Muslim is not to be killed for an unbeliever, nor is a person with a covenant killed for his covenant, and people of two religions are not to inherit from each other.” Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever kills a protected person without justification, God will forbid him Paradise. And in another narration by Abu Dawud: Whoever kills a man from the People of the Covenant will not smell the fragrance of Paradise, although its fragrance can be smelled from a distance of seventy years. In Bukhari in this hadith: Its scent can be detected from a distance of forty years. Narrated by Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: That refers to these prohibitions. The kaf and the mim are for addressing, and note their syntax. He enjoined it upon you The enjoinment is the confirmed and possible command. The kaf and the mim are in the accusative case because they are pronouns for addressing. In wasi there is a subject pronoun referring back to God. Matar al-Warraq narrated on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar that “Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, looked over his companions and said: Why do you kill me? I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The blood of a Muslim man is not permissible except in one of three cases: a man who commits adultery after being married, in which case he is to be stoned; or he kills intentionally, in which case he is to be killed; or he apostatizes after becoming a Muslim, in which case he is to be killed. By God, I did not commit adultery during the pre-Islamic period or during Islam, nor did I kill anyone to be held accountable for it, nor have I apostatized since I became a Muslim. I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. This is what I have mentioned to you, and He has enjoined upon you that you may understand!
6:152: Tenth - The Almighty said: And do not approach the orphan's property except in a way that is best meaning in a way that benefits him and makes him grow, by preserving his roots and making his branches grow. This is the best of the sayings on this, as it is comprehensive. Mujahid said: And do not approach the orphan's property except in a way that is best by trading with it, and do not buy from it or borrow from it. Eleventh - The Almighty said: Until he reaches maturity meaning his strength, and it may be in the body or in knowledge through experience, and both aspects must be obtained, for maturity here is absolute. The description of the orphan's condition came in Surat An-Nisa' with a restriction, as He said: "And test the orphans until they reach the age of marriage. If you perceive in them sound judgment" (An-Nisa': 6), so He combined the strength of the body, which is the age of marriage, with the strength of knowledge, which is the perception of sound judgment. If the orphan were given access to his money before he attained knowledge and after he attained strength, he would be lost in his desires and would remain a vagabond with no money. The orphan was singled out with this condition because people are heedless of him and fathers miss their sons, so it was more appropriate to take advantage of the loss of a father. Reaching maturity does not permit approaching his money in an unfavorable way, because the sanctity is established for an adult. The orphan was singled out for mention because his opponent is God. The meaning is: Do not approach the orphan's money except in a way that is best forever until he reaches maturity. There is an ellipsis in the speech. So when he reaches maturity and you feel that he is mature, then give him his money. The scholars differed about the maturity of an orphan. Ibn Zayd said: His maturity. The people of Medina said: His maturity and his maturity. According to Abu Hanifa: Twenty-five years. Ibn al-Arabi said: I am amazed at Abu Hanifa, for he believes that the predetermined things are not proven by analogy or consideration, but rather they are proven by transmission, and he proves them with weak hadiths. However, he lived in the mint, so many forgers were found in his opinion. If he had lived in the mine, as God had decreed for Malik, he would not have issued anything except the brilliance of religion. It has been said: The end of middle age is when the maturity is complete, as Suhaim ibn Wathil said: Brother of fifty community, Ashdi and Najdni rotating affairs Najdni narrates with the letter dal and the letter dhal. Ashd is singular and has no plural, like ank, which is lead. It has been said: its singular is shadd, like fals and aflas. Its origin is from shadd an-nahar, meaning it rose. It is said: I came to him at shadd an-nahar and mad an-nahar. Muhammad ibn Muhammad ad-Dhabi used to recite the verse of Antarah: I remember him during the day, as if he had dyed his head with frankincense and his hair with bone. Another said: A tall, pure-handed, pure-bred woman walks around him all day long. Sibawayh used to say: Its singular is shaddah. Al-Jawhari said: It is good in meaning, because it is said: The boy reached his strength. However, fa’lah is not pluralized as af’al, and as for an’am, it is the plural of na’am, from their saying: a day of misery and a day of na’am. As for the saying of those who said: Its singular is shadd, like kalb and akleeb, and shadd like thi’b and thi’ub, it is only an analogy. Just as they say for the singular of ababil: ibul, by analogy with ajul, and it is not something heard from the Arabs. Abu Zaid said: Shaddah afflicted me on fa’li, meaning severity. And a man is more severe if he has a strong animal with him.
