Twelfth - The Almighty said: And give full measure and weight in justice meaning with moderation in taking and giving when buying and selling. Justice means fairness. We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity meaning its ability to give full measure and weight. This requires that these commands are only in what is within the ability of humans in terms of caution and freedom. And what cannot be guarded against, such as the difference between the two measures, and is not within the ability of humans, is excused. It was said: The measure means the measure. It is said: This is such and such a measure, and for this reason He connected it with the balance. Some scholars said: Since God, the Almighty, knows that many of His servants are too narrow-minded to give others what they are not obligated to, He ordered the giver to give to the owner of the right his right that is his, and He did not charge him with more, because more would cause him to feel distressed by it. And He ordered the owner of the right to take his right and did not charge him with being satisfied with less than it, because less would cause him to feel distressed by it. In Muwatta Malik, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, it was reported to him on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas that he said: “Theft has never appeared among a people except that God cast terror into their hearts. Fornication has never spread among a people except that death has increased among them. A people have never reduced the measure and weight except that their livelihood has been cut off. A people have never ruled unjustly except that bloodshed has spread among them. A people have never broken a covenant except that God has given power over them to the enemy.” Ibn Abbas also said: “You, the non-Arabs, have been entrusted with two matters by which those who came before you were destroyed: the measure and the weight.” Thirteenth - The Almighty’s saying: And when you speak, be just includes rulings and testimonies. Even if it is a relative meaning even if the right is against your relatives, as mentioned in An-Nisa. And fulfill the covenant of God is general in all that God has covenanted with His servants. It is possible that it refers to all that is concluded between two people. That covenant was attributed to God in that He commanded that it be preserved and fulfilled that you may remember so that you may be admonished.
6:153: Fourteenth - The Almighty said: And that this is My path, which is straight, so follow it. This is a great verse that is connected to what came before, for when He forbade and commanded, He warned here against following a path other than His, so He commanded in it to follow His path as we will explain with the authentic hadiths and sayings of the Salaf. And that is in the accusative case, meaning, And recite that this is My path, according to Al-Farra' and Al-Kisa'i. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for it to be in the genitive case, meaning, He commanded you to do it and that this is My path. And its interpretation according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh is: And because this is My path, as He said: And that the mosques are for God (al-Jinn 72:18). Al-A'mash, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read that this with a kasra on the hamza as a new sentence, meaning that which is mentioned in these verses is My path, which is straight. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ya'qub read that this with a lightened that. The lightened that is like the stressed that, except that it contains the pronoun of the story and the matter, meaning, that this is. So it is in the nominative case. And the accusative case is permissible. It may be redundant for emphasis, as God Almighty said: So when the bearer of good tidings came (Yusuf 12:96). The path is the path that is the religion of Islam. Straight is in the accusative case as a state, and its meaning is straight and upright, with no crookedness in it. So he ordered following his path that he had established through the tongue of his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his law, and its end is Paradise. And paths branched out from it, so whoever takes the straight path will be saved, and whoever goes out to those paths, they will lead him to the Fire. God Almighty said: And do not follow paths, for they will separate you from His path, meaning they will deviate. Al-Darimi Abu Muhammad narrated in his Musnad with a sound chain of transmission: Affan told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, Asim bin Bahdalah told us, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: One day, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drew a line for us, then he said: This is the path of God. Then he drew lines to its right and lines to its left, then he said: These are paths, on each path of which is a devil calling to it. Then he recited this verse. And Ibn Majah included it in his Sunan, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: We were with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he drew a line, then drew two lines to its right, and drew two lines to its left. Then he placed his hand in the middle line and said: This is the path of God - then he recited this verse - And indeed, this is My path, which is straight, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths, for they will separate you from His path. These paths include Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, and all other religions and people of innovations and misguidance from the people of whims and deviation in branches, and others who delve deeply into argument and delve into speech. All of these are susceptible to error and are a source of bad belief, as Ibn Atiyyah said. I said: This is correct. At-Tabari mentioned in the book of Etiquette of Souls: Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la Al-San’ani told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Aban, that a man said to Ibn Mas’ud: What is the straight path? He said: We left Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, at its lowest point and end in Paradise, and on his right is a horse and on his left is a horse, and there are men calling whoever passes by them, whoever takes that horse will end up in Hell, and whoever takes the path will end up in Paradise. Then Ibn Mas’ud recited: And that this is My straight path (al-An’am 6:159). Abdullah bin Mas’ud said: Learn knowledge before it is taken away, and its taking away is that its people go away. Beware of extremism, delving too deeply into it, and innovations, and stick to the old. Narrated by Ad-Darimi. Mujahid said about His statement: And do not follow other paths he said: Innovations. Ibn Shihab said: This is like the statement of God, the Most High: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects (al-An’am 6:159) and the verse. So escape, escape, and salvation, salvation! And adherence to the straight path and the right Sunnah, which the righteous predecessors followed, and in it is the profitable trade. The imams narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whatever I command you to do, take it, and whatever I forbid you to do, refrain from it. Ibn Majah and others narrated on the authority of Al-Arbadh bin Sariyah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, preached to us a sermon that brought tears to our eyes and made our hearts fearful. We said: O Messenger of God, this is a farewell sermon, so what do you enjoin upon us? He said: You have left behind you on the straight path, its night is like its day, and none will deviate from it after me except the doomed. Whoever among you lives will see much difference, so adhere to what you have known of my Sunnah and the Sunnah of the Rightly-Guided Caliphs after me. Cling to it with your molars and beware of newly invented matters, for every innovation is misguidance. And adhere to obedience, even if it is an Ethiopian slave, for the believer is like a nosed camel, wherever it is led it obeys. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi with the same meaning and authenticated by Abu Dawud. He said: Ibn Kathir told us, Sufyan told us: A man wrote to Umar ibn Abdul Aziz asking him about predestination, so he wrote to him: As for what comes after, I advise you to fear God and be moderate in His commands and follow the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and leave what the innovators have innovated after his Sunnah has been established, and spare them its burden. So adhere to the group, for it is a protection for you, by God’s permission. Then know that people have not innovated an innovation except that what preceded it has passed that which is evidence for it or a lesson in it, for the Sunnah was only established by one who knew what error and slippage, foolishness and delving into the depths of its contradiction. So, accept for yourself what the people accepted for themselves, for they stood firm on knowledge, and were restrained by penetrating insight, and they were stronger in revealing matters, and were more deserving of the superiority of what they were in. If the guidance is what you are upon, then you have preceded them to it. And if you say that it only happened after them, then it was only those who followed a path other than theirs and disliked them, then they are the forerunners. They have spoken about it sufficiently and described what satisfies. There is no one below them who fell short, and no one above them who exceeded them. Some people fell short and were harsh, and some people aspired to do so, and despite that, they are on the straight path. And he mentioned the hadith. And Sahl ibn Abdullah al-Sitri said: You should follow the trace and the Sunnah, for I fear that a time will come in a short while when a person mentions the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and follows his example in all his circumstances, they will criticize him, turn away from him, disown him, humiliate him, and degrade him. Sahl said: Innovation appeared at the hands of the people of the Sunnah because they supported them and spoke to them, so their sayings appeared and spread among the common people and those who did not hear them heard them. If they had left them and not spoken to them, each one of them would have died with what was in his heart and nothing of it would have appeared and he would have carried it with him to his grave. Sahl said: No one of you introduces an innovation until Satan introduces to him an act of worship and he worships with it, then introduces an innovation to him. If he speaks the innovation and calls people to it, that service is taken away from him. Sahl said: I do not know of a hadith that came about the innovators that is more severe than this hadith: God has withheld Paradise from the innovator. He said: Then the Jew and the Christian are more hopeful than them. Sahl said: Whoever wants to honor his religion should not enter upon the ruler, should not be alone with women, and should not argue with the people of whims. He also said: Follow and do not innovate, for you have been sufficed. In Musnad al-Darimi: Abu Musa al-Ash’ari came to Abdullah ibn Mas’ud and said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, I saw something in the mosque just now that I disapproved of, but I have seen, praise be to God, nothing but good! He said: What was it? He said: If you live, you will see it. He said: “I saw in the mosque people sitting in circles waiting for the prayer. In each circle there was a man holding pebbles. He would say to them: ‘Say Allahu Akbar’ one hundred times, and they would say Allahu Akbar one hundred times. He would say: ‘Say ‘Allahu Akbar’ one hundred times, and they would say ‘Allahu Akbar’ one hundred times. He would say: ‘Glorify God’ one hundred times, and they would say ‘Glorify God’ one hundred times.” He said: What did you say to them? He said: I did not say anything to them, but I was waiting for your opinion and your command. He said: Did you not order them to count their bad deeds and guarantee that none of their good deeds would be lost? Then he went and we went with him until he came to one of those circles. He stopped at them and said: What is this that I see you doing? They said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, pebbles with which we count the takbeer, tahleel, and tasbeeh. He said: Count your bad deeds and I guarantee that none of your good deeds will be lost. Woe to you, O nation of Muhammad! How quickly you perish. Or are you opening the door to misguidance? They said: By God, O Abu Abd al-Rahman, we only wanted good. He said: How many a person who wants good will never attain it. And on the authority of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, a man asked him about something from the people of whims and innovations, so he said: Stick to the religion of the Bedouins and the boy in the book, and ignore everything else. Al-Awza’i said: Iblis said to his followers: From what do you approach the children of Adam? They said: From everything. He said: Do you approach them before seeking forgiveness? They said: No way! That is something linked to monotheism. He said: I will spread among them something for which they will not seek forgiveness from God. He said: So he spread desires among them. Mujahid said: I do not know which of the two blessings upon me is greater: that He guided me to Islam, or that He spared me from these desires. Al-Sha’bi said: They are called the people of desires because they fall into the Fire. All of this is from Al-Darimi. Sahl ibn ‘Abdullah was asked about praying behind the Mu’tazila, marrying them, and giving them in marriage. He said: No, and no honor! They are disbelievers. How can someone believe who says: The Qur’an is created, nor is Paradise created, nor is Hell created, nor is there a path for God, nor intercession, nor any of the believers will enter Hell, nor will any of the sinners of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, come out of Hell, nor will there be punishment in the grave, nor will there be Munkar, nor Nakir, nor will there be a vision of our Lord in the Hereafter, nor anything more, and that the knowledge of God is created, nor will they see the ruler or the Friday prayer, and they declare as a disbeliever whoever believes in this. Al-Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad said: Whoever loves a person of innovation, God will nullify his deeds and remove the light of Islam from his heart. This and more have been mentioned in his words. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Innovation is more beloved to Satan than sin. Sin can be repented from, but innovation cannot be repented from. Ibn Abbas said: Looking at a man from the people of the Sunnah who calls to the Sunnah and forbids innovation is an act of worship. Abu al-Aaliyah said: Stick to the first way they were before they split. Asim al-Ahwal said: So I told al-Hasan about it and he said: By God, he has advised you and told you the truth. The meaning of his saying, peace be upon him, has already passed in Al Imran: The Children of Israel split into seventy-two sects, and this nation will split into seventy-three. Hadith. Some knowledgeable scholars have said: This sect that has increased in the sects of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, are people who are hostile to scholars and hate jurists, and this was never the case among previous nations. Rafi’ ibn Khadij narrated that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There will be people in my nation who will disbelieve in God and the Qur’an without realizing it, just as the Jews and Christians disbelieved. I said: May I be your ransom, O Messenger of God! How is that? He said: They acknowledge some and disbelieve in others. I said: May I be your ransom, O Messenger of God! How do they say that? He said: They make Satan equal to God in His creation, power and provision, and they say good is from God and evil is from Satan. He said: So they disbelieve in God and then they read the Book of God, and they disbelieve in the Qur’an after believing and knowing it. He said: What my nation will encounter from them of enmity, hatred and argumentation? Those are the heretics of this nation.” He mentioned the hadith. He continued in An-Nisa and this Surah, the prohibition of sitting with the people of innovation and whims, and that whoever sits with them will be judged by their judgement, so he said: And when you see those who engage in [offensive] discourse concerning Our verses (al-An’am 6:68) the verse. Then he explained in Surah An-Nisa, which is Madani, the punishment for whoever does that and disobeys what God has commanded, so he said: And it has already been revealed to you in the Book (Al-Nisa: 14) the verse. So whoever sits with them is included with them. A group of the imams of this nation have adopted this view and ruled according to these verses in the council of the people of innovation regarding companionship and mixing, including Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Al-Awza’i and Ibn Al-Mubarak, for they said about a man whose habit is to sit with the people of innovation: He is forbidden from sitting with them, and if he stops, then fine, otherwise he is included with them, meaning in the ruling. And Umar ibn Abdul Aziz applied the punishment to the councils of drinking alcohol, and he recited Indeed, if you were like them (An-Nisa’: 140). It was said to him: So he says that I sit with them to show them my opposition and respond to them? He said: He is forbidden from sitting with them, and if he does not stop, he is included with them.
6:154: The Almighty said: Then We gave Moses the Scripture two objects. Completely is an object for it or a source. Upon the one who does good is read in the accusative and nominative. Whoever raises it - which is the reading of Yahya bin Ya'mar and Ibn Abi Ishaq - then it is assumed: Completely on the one who is better. Al-Mahdawi said: And in it is a distance because of the deletion of the subject referring to the one who. Sibawayh narrated on the authority of Al-Khalil that he heard I am not the one who says anything to you. Whoever places the accusative then upon is a past verb included in the relative clause, this is the opinion of the Basrans. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' permitted it to be a noun describing the one who. And they permitted I passed by the one who is your brother describing the one who with the definite article and what is close to it. Al-Nahhas said: This is impossible according to the Basrans, because it is a description of the noun before it is completed, and the meaning according to them is: On the one who does good. Mujahid said: Completely on the believing doer. Al-Hasan said regarding the meaning of his statement: Completly on there were among them doers of good and non-doers, so God sent down the Scripture completely on the doers of good. The evidence for the correctness of this statement is that Ibn Masoud read: Completely for those who do good. It was said: The meaning is: We gave Moses the Torah in addition to what Moses did well, which God taught him before the Torah was revealed to him. Muhammad bin Yazid said: The meaning is: Completely for those who did well, meaning: Completely for what God Almighty did well to Moses, peace be upon him, from the message and other things. Abdullah bin Zaid said: Its meaning is for the goodness of God Almighty to His prophets, peace be upon them [from the message and other things]. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: Completely for the goodness of Moses from his obedience to God Almighty, and Al-Farra’ said the same. Then it was said: Then indicates that the second comes after the first, and the story of Moses, peace be upon him, and his being given the Book came before this, so it was said: Then in the sense of and, meaning We gave Moses the Book, because they are conjunctions. It was said: The meaning of the statement is: Then we had given Moses the Book before We revealed the Qur’an to Muhammad, peace be upon him. It was said: The meaning is: Say: Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you, then recite what We gave Moses, completely. And in detail is conjunction to it. And so is guidance and mercy.
6:155: The Almighty said: And this is a Book subject and predicate. We have sent it down as blessed is an adjective, meaning full of good things. It is permissible in other than the Qur'an to say blessed as a state. So follow it meaning act according to what is in it. And fear meaning fear its distortion. That you may receive mercy meaning that you may hope for mercy and not be punished.
6:156: The Almighty said: That you may not say in the accusative case. The Kufians said: So that you may not say. The Basrans said: We revealed it out of aversion that you may say. Al-Farra' and Al-Kisa'i said: The meaning is, beware of saying, O people of Mecca. The Book was only revealed meaning the Torah and the Gospel. Upon two groups before us meaning the Jews and Christians, and no book was revealed to us. And we were unaware of their study meaning the recitation of their books and their languages. He did not say upon their study because each group is a community.
6:157: Or you say is in apposition to that you say "then there has come to you a clear proof from your Lord" meaning the excuse has been removed by the coming of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Clear proof and explanation are one and the same, and what is meant is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, whom God Almighty called clear proof. "And guidance and mercy" meaning for those who follow him. Then He said: "Then who is more unjust" meaning if you lie, then no one is more unjust than you. "And turn away" is turning away. And "turn away" is turning away. And it has been mentioned before.
6:158: The Almighty's saying: Do they wait? means: I have established the proof against them and sent down the Book to them, but they did not believe, so what are they waiting for? Do they wait except that the angels should come to them? meaning at death to take their souls. Or your Lord should come? Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: Your Lord's command concerning them is to kill them or something else. The complement may be mentioned and what is meant by it is the complement, like the Almighty's saying: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82) meaning the people of the town. And His saying: And they have drunk into their hearts the calf (al-Baqarah 2:93) meaning the love of the calf. Likewise here: The command of your Lord will come, meaning the punishment of your Lord and the torment of your Lord. It is said: This is from the ambiguous verses whose interpretation is known only to God. A similar statement has been made in Al-Baqarah and other verses. Or some of the signs of your Lord should come. It was said: It is the rising of the sun from the west. This clarifies that they are given respite in this world, but when the Hour appears, there will be no respite. It was said: The coming of God Almighty is His coming to decide the judgment between His creation on the Day of Resurrection, as God Almighty said: And your Lord will come with angels, rank upon rank. (al-Fajr 89:22). His coming is not movement, nor transition, nor disappearance, because that only happens when the one who comes is a body or substance. What the majority of the Imams of Ahl al-Sunnah are upon is that they say: He comes, descends, and comes. They do not describe how, because there is nothing like Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. (al-Shura 42:11). In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three things that, if they appear, will not benefit a soul from its faith if it did not believe before or earned any good through its faith: the rising of the sun from the west, the Antichrist, and the beast of the earth.” On the authority of Safwan ibn Assal al-Muradi, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: In the Maghreb there is a door open for repentance, a distance of seventy years’ journey, that will not be closed until the sun rises from it. Narrated by al-Darqutni [al-Darimi] and al-Tirmidhi, who said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Sufyan said: Before al-Sham, God created it on the day He created the heavens and the earth. Open, meaning for repentance, that will not be closed until the sun rises from it. He said: A good and authentic hadith. I said: The Khawarij and the Mu'tazilah denied all of this, as mentioned above. Ibn Abbas narrated: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: O people, do not be deceived about stoning. The sign of that is that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) stoned, and Abu Bakr stoned, and we stoned after them. There will be people from this nation who will lie about stoning, and they will lie about the Antichrist, and they will lie about the rising of the sun from the west, and they will lie about the torment of the grave, and they will lie about intercession, and they will lie about people who will come out of the Fire after they have been burned. Abu Umar mentioned it. Al-Tha'labi mentioned in a long hadith on the authority of Abu Hurairah, "On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, what means: The sun will be held back from the people - sins will increase on earth, and good will disappear so no one will command it, and evil will spread so no one will forbid it - for the amount of a night under the Throne. Every time it prostrates and asks permission from its Lord, the Most High, from where it rises, no answer will come to it until the moon meets it and prostrates with it, and asks permission from where it rises, but no answer will come to them until they are held back for the amount of three nights for the sun and two nights for the moon. No one will know the length of that night except those who pray at night on earth, and they will be a small group in every town of the Muslims. When the amount of three nights has been completed for them, God Almighty will send Gabriel, peace be upon him, to them and say: The Lord, glory be to Him, commands you to return to your places of setting and rise from them, and that there is no light for you with us and no light. So they will rise from their places of setting black, with no light for the sun and no light for the moon, like them in their eclipses before that. That is what God Almighty said: "And He joined the sun and the moon." (al-Qiyamah 75:9) And His statement: When the sun is wrapped up (al-Takwir 81:1), so they rise like two horned camels. Then, when the sun and the moon reach the navel of the sky, which is its middle, Gabriel, peace be upon him, comes to them and takes them by their horns and returns them to the west. He does not set them from their west, but sets them from the door of repentance. Then he returns the two leaves, then what is between them is joined together and it becomes as if there was never a crack between them. So, when the door of repentance is closed, no repentance of a servant will be accepted after that, and no good deed he does will benefit him after that, except for he who was a doer of good before that, for what he was doing before that day will continue upon him. That is what God Almighty said: The Day some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earned any good through its faith. Then the sun and the moon will be clothed after that with light and radiance, then they will rise and set upon the people as they used to rise and set before that.” The scholars said: “The reason a soul’s faith will not benefit from its rising from the west is because such fear has entered their hearts that every desire of the soul is extinguished and every strength of the body is weakened. So all people, because of their certainty of the approach of the Resurrection, will be in the state of someone who is at the mercy of death, with the motives for various types of sins being cut off from them and their being nullified from their bodies. So whoever repents in such a state, his repentance will not be accepted, just as the repentance of someone at the mercy of death will not be accepted.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not yet reached the gurgling point, meaning his soul has not yet reached the top of his throat. This is the time of witnessing when he sees his seat in Paradise or his seat in Hell. The one who witnesses the sun rising from the West is like him. Based on this, the repentance of everyone who witnesses that or is like the one who witnesses it should be rejected as long as he lives, because his knowledge of God, the Most High, His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and His promise has become a necessity. If the days of this world extend until people forget what happened of this great matter and only speak about it a little, then the report about it becomes specific and the continuous transmission of it ceases, then whoever converts to Islam or repents at that time will be accepted. And God knows best. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Abdullah who said: I memorized a hadith from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that I have not forgotten since. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The first of the signs to appear will be the rising of the sun from the west and the emergence of the beast among the people at noon. Whichever of the two is before the other, the other will follow soon after it. And in it, “On the authority of Hudhayfah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in a room and we were below him, so he looked out at us and said: What do you remember? We said: The Hour. He said: The Hour will not come until ten signs occur: A sinking in the east, a sinking in the west, a sinking in the Arabian Peninsula, the smoke, the Antichrist, the beast of the earth, Gog and Magog, the rising of the sun from the west, and a fire that emerges from the depths of Aden that will displace people. Shu'bah said: Abdul Aziz bin Rafi' narrated to me on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl on the authority of Abu Sariha something similar, without mentioning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. One of them said in the tenth: The descent of Jesus, son of Mary, may God bless him and grant him peace. The other said: A wind that will throw people into the sea. I said: This is a well-crafted hadith in the arrangement of signs. Some of them, namely eclipses, have occurred, as Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi mentioned, in Iraq and the Maghreb, and many people have perished because of them. He mentioned this in the book Fahum al-Athar and others. The mention of the beast comes in An-Naml, and Gog and Magog in Al-Kahf. It is said that the signs follow one another like strings on a thread, year after year. It is said that the wisdom in the sun rising from the west is that Abraham, peace be upon him, said to Nimrod: “God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west.” So the disbelievers were confounded. (al-Baqarah 2:258) And the atheists and astrologers, one after the other, deny this and say: It will not happen. So God, the Most High, will cause them to rise one day from the west to show the deniers of His power that the sun is in His dominion. If He wills, He will bring it from the east, and if He wills, He will bring it from the west. Based on this, it is possible that the rejection of repentance and faith is for those who believed and repented from those who denied that and rejected the report of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the rising of the sun. As for those who believed in that, their repentance is accepted and their faith before that will benefit them. It was narrated from Abdullah ibn Abbas that he said: No deeds or repentance are accepted from a disbeliever if he becomes Muslim when he sees it, except for one who was young at that time, because if he became Muslim after that, that will be accepted from him. And whoever was a believing sinner and repented from his sin, it will be accepted from him. It was narrated from Imran ibn Husayn that he said: His repentance is not accepted at the time of sunrise when there is a shout in which many people perish. So whoever becomes Muslim or repents at that time and perishes, his repentance is not accepted, but whoever repents after that, his repentance is accepted. Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi mentioned this in his interpretation. Abdullah ibn Umar said: People will remain after the rising of the sun from the west for one hundred and twenty years until they plant palm trees. And God knows best about His unseen. Ibn Omar and Ibn Al-Zubayr read Yawm Yati with a ta’, like Some car picks him up. And some of his fingers are gone. Jarir said: When the report of Al-Zubayr came, the city walls and the mountains were humbled. Al-Mubarrad said: The feminization is due to proximity to a feminine, not according to the original. Ibn Sirin read la tanfa` with a ta’. Abu Hatim said: They mention that this is a mistake by Ibn Sirin. Al-Nahhas said: There is something subtle in grammar in this that Sibawayh mentioned, and that is that faith and the soul each include the other, so faith was made feminine since it is from the soul and with it. Sibawayh recited: Walking as spears shake, their tops are blown away by the passing winds Al-Mahdawi said: They often feminize the masculine noun phrase if it is added to a feminine noun, and the noun is part of the noun it is added to, from it, or with it. This is what Dhu al-Rummah said: Walk... home So, the word mar is feminine because it is added to the winds, which are feminine, since mar is from the winds. An-Nahhas said: There is another saying about it, which is that faith is feminine because it is a source, just as the feminine source is mentioned, like: So whoever receives an admonition from his Lord (al-Baqarah 2:275), and as he said: You have excused us from his companions In one of the sayings, the excuse is feminine because it means an apology. Say, ‘Wait, we are waiting’ for you to be punished.
6:159: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who have divided their religion Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it as faraqu with an alif, and it is the reading of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, from mufaraqa and al-faraq. Meaning that they abandoned their religion and left it. Ali used to say: By God, they did not divide it, but they departed from it. The rest read it with emphasis, except for Al-Nakha'i, who read faraqu without emphasis, meaning they believed in some and disbelieved in others. What is meant is the Jews and Christians according to Mujahid, Qatadah, As-Suddi and Ad-Dahhak. They were described as being divided, God the Almighty said: And those who were given the Scripture did not become divided except after there came to them clear proof (al-Bayyinah 98:4). He also said: And they want to separate between God and His messengers (An-Nisa': 150). It was said: He meant the polytheists, some of whom worshipped idols and some of whom worshipped angels. It was said: The verse is general for all disbelievers. Whoever innovates and brings something that God Almighty did not command has divided his religion. Abu Hurairah narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this verse: Indeed, those who have divided their religion. They are the people of innovations and doubts, and the people of misguidance from this nation.” And Baqiyah bin Al-Walid narrated: Shu’bah bin Al-Hajjaj told us: Mujalid told us: Al-Sha’bi told us: Shuraih told us: Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Aisha: Those who divided their religion and became sects are the people of innovations, the people of whims and the people of misguidance from this nation. O Aisha, every sinner has repentance, except for the people of innovations and the people of whims. There is no repentance for them, and I am innocent of them and they are innocent of us. Laith bin Abi Salim narrated on the authority of Tawus on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: “Those who have departed from their religion.” The meaning of sects is groups and parties. Every people whose affair is one, some of them follow the opinion of others, so they are sects. You are not from them in anything made it necessary to disavow them, and it is like his saying, peace be upon him: He who deceives us is not from us, meaning we are innocent of him. The poet said: If you try to commit adultery with a lion, then I am not from you and you are not from me That is, I am innocent of you. The place of in something (may God bless him and grant him peace) is in the accusative case as a state of the implied word in the report, as Abu Ali said. Al-Farra’ said: It is on the deletion of an added word, meaning you are not to be punished in anything, and you are only to warn. Their affair is only with God is a consolation to the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace).
6:160: The Almighty said: Whoever brings a good deed is the beginning, and it is a condition, and the answer is he will have ten like it meaning he will have ten good deeds like it, so the good deeds were deleted and the likes that are its description were used in its place, the plural of like. Sibawayh said: I have ten genealogists, meaning I have ten men who are genealogists. Abu Ali said: The feminization of ten like it is good because the likes are added to a feminine, and the addition to the feminine if it is the same in meaning is good in it, like some caravan picks him up. And some of his fingers are lost. Al-Hasan, Saeed bin Jubayr, and Al-A'mash read he will have ten like it. The meaning is: he will have ten good deeds like it, meaning he will have ten times the reward of what is due to him. It is permissible for him to have like, and the like is multiplied so it becomes ten. The good deed here is faith. Meaning whoever comes with the testimony that there is no god but God, he will have for every good deed he did in this world ten times the reward. And whoever brings evil meaning polytheism will not be recompensed except with the like thereof which is eternity in the Fire, because polytheism is the greatest of sins, and the Fire is the greatest of punishments. This is what God Almighty says: A recompense according to the deed (An-Naba’: 26) meaning a recompense according to the deed. As for the good deed, it is the opposite of that, because God Almighty explicitly states that. And in the report: “A good deed is rewarded tenfold and more, and a bad deed is rewarded only once, and I forgive. Woe to him whose one-tenths outweigh his one-tenths.” Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Abu Salih who said: A good deed is There is no god but God and a bad deed is associating partners with God. “And they will not be wronged” means the reward for their deeds will not be diminished. This verse has already been explained in Al-Baqarah. It is contrary to spending in the way of God, and for this reason some scholars said: A tenth is for all other good deeds, and seven hundred is for spending in the way of God, and the elite and the common people are equal in this. Some of them said: For the common people it is ten and for the elite it is seven hundred and more, and so on, and this requires a revelation. The first is more correct, due to the hadith of Khuraim ibn Fatik from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which it says: “As for a good deed, it is worth ten, so whoever does a good deed will have ten like it. As for a good deed worth seven hundred, it is spending in the way of God.”
6:161: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: My Lord has guided me to a straight path.” When the Almighty explained that the disbelievers were divided, that God guided him to the straight religion, which is the religion of Abraham, a religion is in the accusative case as a state, according to Qutrub. It was said: It is in the accusative case with guided me according to Al-Akhfash. Someone else said: It is in the accusative case based on the meaning, because the meaning of guided me is made me know a religion. It is permissible for it to be a substitute for the path, meaning He guided me to a straight path, a religion. It was said: It is in the accusative case with an implied verb, as if he said: Follow a religion, and know a religion. Early was read by the Kufians and Ibn Amir with a kasra on the qaf and a light sukoon and a fatha on the ya’, a verbal noun like shabi’ah so it was described with it. The rest read it with a fatha on the qaf and a kasra on the ya’ and a shaddah on it, and they are two dialects. The root of the ya’ is waw qayyum, then the waw was assimilated into the ya’ like mayt. Its meaning is a straight religion with no crookedness in it. The religion of Abraham is in the place of hanif. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a state of Abraham. Ali bin Suleiman said: It is accusative with the implied meaning I mean.
6:162: Second: The Almighty said: "Say: Verily, my prayer and my sacrifice" The word prayer was previously derived. It was said that what is meant by it here is the night prayer. It was also said: the Eid prayer. And the sacrifice is the plural of Nasikah, which is the sacrifice, and this is what Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Saeed bin Jubair and others said. The meaning is: My sacrifice in Hajj and Umrah. Al-Hasan said: My sacrifice is my religion. Al-Zajjaj said: My worship, and from it is the ascetic who draws closer to God through worship. Some people said: The sacrifice in this verse is all the acts of righteousness and obedience, from your saying Nasaka so-and-so is a ascetic, if he worships. And my life means what I do in my life. And my death means what I bequeath after my death. For God, Lord of the worlds means I single it out for drawing closer to Him. It was also said: And my life and death are for God meaning my life and death are for Him. Al-Hasan read: Nasikah with a sukoon on the seen. The people of Madinah read it with a sukoon on the ya in the inclusion. The general public reads it with a fatha because two sukoon letters come together. An-Nahhas said: None of the grammarians permitted it except Yunus, and he only permitted it because there was an alif before it, and the alif is the long vowel that takes the place of a vowel. Yunus permitted Adrabaan Zayd, but the grammarians forbade this because it combined two quiescent letters and there is no assimilation in the second. Whoever recites according to the recitation of the people of Medina and wants to avoid making mistakes stops at Muhayya, and he is not making a mistake according to all grammarians. Ibn Abi Ishaq, Isa bin Omar, Asim al-Jahdari, and Muhyi recited with a shaddah on the second ya without an alif, and it is the language of the people of Mudar, who say: Qaffa and Asi. The linguists recited: They preceded my passion and embraced their passion It has been presented. Third: Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: The Almighty’s statement: “Say: My Lord has guided me to a straight path” to His statement: “Say: My prayer, my sacrifice, my life, and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds.” Al-Shafi’i used it as evidence for beginning the prayer with this remembrance, for God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and revealed it in His book. Then he mentioned the hadith of Ali, may God be pleased with him: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began the prayer, he would say: I have directed my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with God. Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds - until His saying - and I am of the Muslims. I said: Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that when he stood up to pray, he would say: I have directed my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with God. Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds. No partner has He. This I have been commanded, and I am the first of those who submit. O God, You are the King, there is no god but You. You are my Lord, and I am Your servant. I have wronged myself and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me all my sins, for no one forgives sins except You. Guide me to the best of morals, for no one guides to the best of morals except You. And avert from me the evil of morals, for no one averts the evil of morals except You. I am at Your service and at Your pleasure, and all good is in Your hands, and evil does not come from You. Blessed and exalted are You. I seek Your forgiveness and I repent to You.” The hadith. Ad-Daraqutni narrated it and said at the end of it: It has reached us from An-Nadr ibn Shumayl, who was one of the scholars of language and other things, who said: The meaning of the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, And evil is not from You. Evil is not something that can be brought near to You. Malik said: Direction in prayer is not obligatory upon people, and what is obligatory upon them is to say Allahu Akbar and then recite. Ibn al-Qasim said: Malik did not see what people say before reciting: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. In Mukhtasar ma not fi al-Mukhtasar: Malik used to say it to himself, because of the authenticity of the hadith, but he did not show it to people for fear that they would believe that it was obligatory. Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: I used to pray behind our Sheikh Abu Bakr al-Daynuri, the jurist, during my youth, and he saw me doing this once and said: “O my son, the jurists have differed about the obligation of reciting al-Fatihah behind the imam, and they did not differ that the opening is a Sunnah, so busy yourself with what is obligatory and leave the Sunnah.” The evidence for Malik is “the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the Bedouin whom he taught the prayer: If you stand up for prayer, say Allahu Akbar and then recite. He did not say to him, “Subhan God” as Abu Hanifa says, nor say, Wajit Wajihi as al-Shafi’i says. He said to my father, How do you recite when you begin the prayer? He said, I say Allahu Akbar, al-Hamdulillah Rabb al-‘Alamin. So he did not mention guidance or glorification. If it is said, “Ali has reported that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say it.” We say, It is possible that he said it before the takbir and then said it, and that is good according to us. If it is said, “An-Nasa’i and Ad-Daraqutni narrated that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began the prayer, he would say Allahu Akbar and then say: My prayer and my rituals.” We said: We carry this to mean the voluntary prayer at night, as it came in the book of al-Nasa’i on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began the prayer at night, he would say: Glory be to You, God, and praise be to You. Blessed is Your name and exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god but You.” Or in the voluntary prayer in general, because the voluntary prayer is lighter than the obligatory prayer, because it is permissible to pray it standing, sitting, riding, and facing the qiblah or otherwise while traveling, so its matter is easier. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Maslama that “when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood to pray a voluntary prayer, he would say: God is the Greatest. I have directed my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with God. Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner. This I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims. O God, You are the King, there is no god but You. Glory be to You and praise be to You. Then he recites. This is a text about voluntary prayer, not obligatory prayer. If it is true that this was in the obligatory prayer after the takbir, then it is understood as permissible and recommended. As for the recommended prayer, the recitation is after the takbir, and God knows the truth of matters. Then if he says it, he should not say: And I am the first of the Muslims. It is: Fourth: None of them is the first of them except Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. If it is said: Were not Abraham and the prophets before him? We say three answers about him: The first: He is the first of creation in all meanings, as in the hadith of Abu Hurairah from his saying, peace be upon him: “We are the last but the first on the Day of Resurrection and we are the first to enter Paradise.” In the hadith of Hudhayfah: We are the last of the people of this world and the first on the Day of Resurrection, and the judgment will be for them before all creation. The second: He is the first of them because he was created before them. God Almighty said: And when We took a covenant from the prophets and from you and from Noah (al-Ahzab 33:7). Qatada said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was the first of the prophets in creation and the last of them in the mission. This was mentioned here before Noah and others. The third: The first of the Muslims from his religion, said Ibn al-Arabi, and it is the saying of Qatada and others. The narrations differed regarding the first, some of them are confirmed and some are not, as we mentioned. Imran bin Husayn narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O Fatima, stand up and witness your sacrifice, for every sin you have committed will be forgiven for you at the first drop of its blood. Then say: ‘Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my life and my death are for God, Lord of the worlds. He has no partner, and this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.’ Imran said: ‘O Messenger of God, is this for you and your family specifically or for all Muslims?’ He said: ‘Rather, for all Muslims.’”
6:163: God Almighty says: He has no partner, and this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.
6:164: The Almighty said: "Say: Shall I seek other than God as a lord while He is the Lord of all things?" That is, their Owner. It was narrated that the infidels said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Return, O Muhammad, to our religion, worship our gods, and abandon what you are doing, and we will take care of every consequence you expect in this world and the hereafter. So the verse was revealed. It is a question that requires confirmation and rebuke. The accusative case of I seek and lord is a specification. The Almighty’s saying: And no soul earns except against itself has two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And no soul earns except against itself, meaning that it does not benefit me to seek a lord other than God that you are like that, since no soul earns except against itself, meaning that it will not be held accountable for the sin it has committed or the wrongdoing it has committed besides it. Second: Some scholars who oppose this verse have used this verse as evidence that the sale of a meddler is invalid, which is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i. Our scholars said: What is meant by the verse is bearing the reward and punishment without worldly rulings, as evidenced by the words of God the Almighty: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another as will be mentioned. And the sale of a meddler, in our view, is subject to the owner’s approval. If he approves it, it is valid. This is ‘Urwah Al-Barqi, who sold to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), bought, and disposed of without his permission, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) approved it, and Abu Hanifa said the same. Al-Bukhari and Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of ‘Urwah ibn Abi Al-Ja’d, who said: “A camel was presented to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he gave me a dinar and said: ‘O Urwah, go to the camel and buy us a sheep with this dinar. ’ So I went to the camel and bargained and bought two sheep for a dinar. I came to drive them - or he said, to lead them - and a man met me on the road and bargained with me, so I sold him one of the sheep for a dinar, and I came with the other sheep and a dinar. I said: ‘O Messenger of God, this is the sheep and this is your dinar. ’ He said: ‘How did you do it? ’ So I told him the story. He said: ‘O God, bless him in his right-hand deal. ’ He said: ‘I saw myself standing in the garbage dump of Kufa and I made a profit of forty thousand before I reached my family. ’” This is the wording of Ad-Daraqutni. ‘Umar said: This is a good hadith, and it confirms the authenticity of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for the two sheep. Had it not been for that, he would not have taken the dinar from him nor would he have concluded the sale with him. It is evidence of the permissibility of agency, and there is no disagreement among scholars about it. If the principal says to his agent: Buy such and such, and he buys more than what he was authorized to buy, is that action binding or not? Like a man who says to another: Buy a pound of meat with this dirham, of such and such description, and he buys him four pounds of such and such description with that dirham. What Malik and his companions say is that he is bound by everything if it matches the description and is of the same type, because he is doing good. This is the opinion of Abu Yusuf and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan. Abu Hanifa said: The extra is for the buyer. This hadith is an argument against him. God the Almighty says: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another meaning no bearer of the burden of another, meaning no soul shall be taken for the sin of another, rather every soul shall be taken for its crime and punished for its sin. The root of the word wazr is heavy, and from it God the Almighty says: And We have removed from you your burden (al-Isra’ 17:2). Here it means the sin, as God the Almighty says: And they shall bear their burdens on their backs (al-An’am 6:31). It may also be stated. Al-Akhfash said: It is said wazr yu’zur, wazr yuzur, and wazr yu’zur and wazr yu’zur and it is permissible to say izran, just as it is said isada. The verse was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah, he used to say Follow my path, I will bear your burdens, mentioned by Ibn Abbas. It was said that it was revealed in response to the Arabs in the pre-Islamic era of holding a man accountable for his father, his son, and the crime of his ally. I said: It is possible that what is meant by this verse is in the Hereafter, as well as the one before it. As for what is in this world, some of them may be held accountable for the determination of others, especially if the obedient do not stop the disobedient, as was mentioned in the hadith of Abu Bakr in his statement: Upon yourselves (al-Ma’idah 5:105). And God Almighty said: And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively (al-Anfal 8:25). Indeed, God will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves (al-Ra’d 13:11). And Zainab bint Jajsh said: O Messenger of God, will we perish while there are righteous people among us? He said: Yes, if evil increases.” The scholars said: It means the children of fornication. And evil with the first letter of the word ba open is the name for fornication. So God the Almighty made it obligatory through the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pay the blood money for an accident on the agnates so that the blood of a free Muslim would not be shed, out of respect for blood. The scholars agreed on this without any disagreement among them, so it indicates what we have said. It may be possible that this is in this world, in that Zaid will not be held accountable for the actions of Amr, and that everyone who directly commits a crime will bear its consequences. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Ramtha who said: “I set out with my father towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then the Prophet said to my father: Is this your son? He said: Yes, by the Lord of the Kaaba. He said: Truly. He said: I bear witness to it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled, laughing at the confirmation of my resemblance to my father, and to my father’s successor Ali. Then he said: He will not harm you nor will you harm him.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. What we said at first does not contradict His statement: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens in addition to their burdens (al-Ankabut 29:13), for this is explained in the other verse: That they will bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and some of the burdens of those whom they led astray without knowledge (al-Nahl: 25). So whoever was a leader in misguidance and called to it and was followed in it, then he will bear the burden of the one who led him astray without anything being diminished from the burden of the one who led astray, as will be explained, God willing.
6:165: The Almighty said: And it is He who has made you successors on the earth. Successors is the plural of successor, like karim is the plural of karimah. And everyone who came after those who have passed away is a successor. That is, He made you successors to past nations and previous centuries. Al-Shamakh said: Fate befalls them and I miss them, and I am left behind in one region after another. And He has raised some of you above others in creation, provision, strength, abundance, grace and knowledge. Degrees is in the accusative case by dropping the preposition, meaning to degrees. To test you is in the accusative case with the lam of ki. And testing is testing, meaning to show from you that which will have the ultimate goal of reward and punishment. And He has always been rich in His knowledge, so He tested the wealthy with wealth and asked him to be grateful, and tested the poor with poverty and asked him to be patient. It is said: To test you meaning some of you by others. As He said: And We have made some of you a trial for others (al-Furqan 25:20) as will be explained. Then He frightened them and said: Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment for those who disobey Him. And indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful for those who obey Him. And He said: He is swift in punishment despite His description of respite, and despite the fact that the punishment of the Fire is in the Hereafter, because everything that comes is near, so He is swift in this regard. As God the Almighty said: And the matter of the Hour is not but as the twinkling of an eye or even nearer (al-Nahl 16:77). He said: They see it far away, but We see it near. (al-Ma’arij 70:5-7). He will also be quick to punish those who deserve it in this world, so it will be a warning to those who commit sins in this regard. And God knows best.
7:1: It is a Meccan surah, except for eight verses, which are the words of God Almighty: And ask them about the city (al-A’raf 7:63) until His words: And when We lifted the mountain above them (al-A’raf 7:171). Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Aisha that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited Surat Al-A’raf in the Maghrib prayer, dividing it into two rak’ahs.” Abu Muhammad Abdul Haqq authenticated it. The Almighty’s saying: Alif, Lam, Meem was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah, and its position is raised as a subject.
7:2: And book is its predicate. It is as if he said: The letters of book revealed to you are the letters of book revealed to you. Al-Kisa'i said: meaning this is a book. The Almighty’s saying: So let there not be in your breast any discomfort therefrom has two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: hardship means tightness, meaning do not let your chest become tight with the notification, because “it was narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: I fear that they will cut off my head and call it a loaf of bread. Narrated by Muslim. Al-Kaya said: Its apparent meaning is a prohibition, but its meaning is to negate any difficulty in it, i.e., do not feel distressed by their not believing in it, for your duty is only to convey the message, and you are only responsible for warning about it from some aspect of their belief or disbelief. Similar to this is the statement of God the Almighty: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe (al-Kahf 18:6). And He said: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe (Ash-Shu'ara: 3). The view of Mujahid and Qatadah is that the difficulty here is doubt, and this is not doubt of disbelief, but rather doubt of distress. Likewise is the statement of God the Almighty: And We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say (al-Hijr 15:97). It was said: The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation. There is more to it. The ha in minhu is for the Qur'an. It was said to indicate warning, i.e., the Book was sent down to you so that you may warn with it, so that there is no difficulty in your chest from it. So the statement contains an inversion. It was said to indicate the denial that gives it the strength of the statement. So do not let there be any distress in your chest because of the denial of those who deny Him. Second: The Almighty’s saying: “And a reminder” may be in the nominative, accusative, or genitive cases. The rejection is from two aspects. The Basrans said: It is a nominative case with an implied subject. Al-Kisa’i said: It is in apposition to Book. The accusative case is from two aspects, based on the source, meaning, and He reminded with it as a reminder, as the Basrans said. Al-Kisa’i said: It is in apposition to the ha in We sent it down. The genitive case is based on the position of to warn with it. The warning is for the disbelievers, and the reminder is for the believers, because they are the ones who benefit from it.
7:3: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord, meaning the Book and the Sunnah. God the Almighty said: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. (al-Hashr 59:7). A group said: This is an order that applies to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation. It appears that it is an order for all people, apart from him. That is, follow the religion of Islam and the Qur’an, make lawful what it makes lawful and forbid what it makes unlawful, obey its commands, and avoid what it forbids. The verse indicates that following opinions should not be followed when there is a text. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And do not follow other protectors besides Him from other than Him. The ha refers to the Lord, glory be to Him, and the meaning is: Do not worship other than Him, and do not take as a protector those who deviate from the religion of God. And whoever is satisfied with a doctrine, then the people of that doctrine are his protectors. It was narrated from Malik bin Dinar that he read Do not seek protectors besides Him meaning do not ask. And protectors was not declined because it contains the feminine alif. It was said: It refers to what from His saying: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord. You rarely remember “what” is redundant. It was said: It can be a verbal noun with the verb.
7:4: The Almighty said: And how many a town have We destroyed "Kam is for emphasis, just as Rabb" is for emphasis. It is in the nominative case as a subject, and "Ahlaka" is the predicate. That is, of the towns - which are places where people gather - We destroyed. The accusative case is permissible by implying a verb after it, and it is not possible to put it before it, because what precedes it does not work on the interrogative. The first is strengthened by His statement: "And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah" (Al-Isra': 17). If "Ahlaka had not been occupied by the pronoun, it would have been in the accusative case in place of Kam". It is also permissible for "Ahlaka to be an attribute of the town, and Kam in meaning is the town, so if you describe the town, it is as if you have described Kam". This is indicated by the Almighty's statement: "And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing" (al-Najm 53:26). So the pronoun returns to "Kam" in meaning, since the angels were in meaning. So, according to this estimation, it is not correct for "Kam" to be in the accusative case by implying a verb after it. "Our punishment came upon it is problematic because of the conjunction with fa". Al-Farra' said: "Fa has the meaning of waw", so the order is not necessary. It was also said: "How many a town We intended to destroy, but Our punishment came upon it?" Like His statement: "So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed." (al-Nahl 16:98). It was also said: "The destruction will befall some of the people, so the meaning would be: How many a town We have destroyed, some of which Our punishment came upon, so We destroyed all of them." It was also said: "The meaning is: How many a town We have destroyed by Our command, but Our punishment came upon it." It was also said: "We destroyed it by sending angels of punishment to it, so Our punishment came upon it, which is extermination. Bas" is the torment that befalls the soul. It was also said: "The meaning is: We destroyed it, so Our destruction of them was at such and such a time. So the coming of bas" in this case means destruction. It was also said: "Bas" is not destruction, as we mentioned. Al-Farra’ also said that if the meaning of the two verbs is the same or almost the same, you can put whichever you want first, so the meaning will be: How many a town did Our punishment come to and we destroyed it, like dana he approached and qarabb he approached and qarab he approached and shatamni he insulted me and asa’i he insulted me because insulting and cursing are one and the same thing. Similarly, His statement: The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split (al-Qamar 54:1). The meaning - and God knows best - is that the moon has split and the Hour has drawn near. The meaning is the same. Bayata night means night, and from it comes bayt the house, because one spends the night in it. It is said: bata yabitan he spent the night and bayat. “or hum qa’ilun” or they are saying means or they are saying, but they found it too heavy and deleted the waw, as Al-Farra’ said. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a mistake, if the masculine is repeated, the waw is dispensed with. You say: Zayd came to me riding or he is walking, and the waw is not needed. Al-Mahdawi said: He did not say bayat or they are saying because in the sentence there is a pronoun that refers to the first, so the waw is dispensed with. This is the meaning of what Al-Zajjaj said, whether it is the same, and the waw is not for doubt but for detail, like your saying: I will honor you whether you are fair to me or unjust. This waw is called by grammarians the waw of time. Some say that it is from the qaylah, which is the nap, which is sleeping in the middle of the day. It was said: Resting in the middle of the day if the heat is intense even if there is no sleep with it. The meaning is: Our punishment came to them while they were heedless, either at night or during the day.
7:5: And the claim is the supplication, and from it is His saying: And the last of their supplication (Yunus 10:10). And the grammarians have said: O God, let us share in the righteous supplication of the one who supplicated You. And the claim may mean the claim. And the meaning is: They were not saved at the time of destruction except by admitting that they were wrongdoers. And their supplication is in the accusative case as the predicate of was, and its subject is except that they said. Similar to it is So the answer of his people was only that they said (al-Ankabut 29:29). And it is permissible for the claim to be in the nominative case, and that they said in the accusative case, like the saying of God the Almighty: It is not righteousness that you turn away (al-Baqarah 2:177) by raising the righteousness and His saying: Then the end of those who did evil was the worst, because they denied (al-Rum 30:10) by raising the end.
7:6: The Almighty's saying: Then We will surely question those to whom We sent messengers is evidence that the disbelievers will be held accountable. In the Qur'an, it is said: Then We will surely bring them to account (al-Ghashiyah 88:26). In Surat Al-Qasas, it is said: The criminals will be asked about their sins (al-Qasas 28:78) meaning when they are settled in the punishment. The Hereafter has two places: a place where they will be asked for accountability, and a place where they will not be asked. Their question is a question of confirmation, rebuke, and exposure. The question of the messengers is a question of testifying to them and revealing, i.e. about the people's answer to them. This is the meaning of His saying: That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness (al-Ahzab 33:8) as follows. It was said: The meaning is: Then We will surely question those to whom We sent messengers meaning the prophets and We will surely question the messengers meaning the angels who were sent to them. The lam in Falansa'alan is the lam of an oath, and its true meaning is emphasis.
7:7: And likewise, We will narrate to them with knowledge. Ibn Abbas said: He will speak for them. And We were not absent means We were witness to their deeds. The verse indicates that God Almighty is All-Knowing with knowledge.
7:8: The Almighty's saying: And the weighing on that Day will be the truth is the subject and predicate. It is possible that the truth is its attribute, and the predicate is that Day. It is also possible to put the truth in the accusative case as a source. What is meant by weighing is weighing the deeds of the servants on the scale. Ibn Omar said: The records of the deeds of the servants will be weighed. This is the correct view, and it is what the report mentioned as follows. It was said: The scale is the book in which are the deeds of creation. Mujahid said: The scale is the good and bad deeds in their entirety. It was also narrated from him, Ad-Dahhak, and Al-A'mash: Weight and scale mean justice and judgment, and mentioning weight is an example, as you say: This speech is in the weight of this and in its weight, meaning it is equivalent to it and equal to it even if there is no weight. Az-Zajjaj said: This is permissible from the point of view of the tongue, and it is better to follow what came in the authentic chains of transmission regarding mentioning the scale. Al-Qushayri said: He did well in what he said, because if the scales were to be based on this, then the path would be based on the true religion, Paradise and Hell would be based on what applies to the souls rather than the bodies, the devils and jinn would be based on blameworthy morals, and the angels would be based on praiseworthy powers. The nation in the early days agreed to take these apparent meanings without interpretation. If they agreed to prevent interpretation, then it is necessary to take the apparent meanings, and these apparent meanings became texts. Ibn Furak said: The Mu'tazila denied the scales based on the fact that it is impossible to weigh accidents, since they do not stand on their own. Some theologians say: God Almighty turns accidents into bodies and weighs them on the Day of Resurrection. This is not correct according to us, and the correct view is that the scales are weighed by the books in which the deeds are written, and they are lightened by them. A report has been narrated that confirms this, which is that it was narrated: The scale of some of the children of Adam almost becomes light with good deeds, so a piece of paper is placed on which is written ‘There is no god but God’ and it becomes heavy. It is known that this is due to the weight of the deeds written on it, not the deeds themselves, and that God, the Exalted, lightens the scale when He wills, and makes it heavy when He wills with what is placed on its two pans of scrolls containing deeds. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Safwan ibn Mahraz, he said, “A man said to Ibn Umar: How did you hear the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) say about secret conversation? He said: I heard him say: The believer will be brought near to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection until He covers him with His cloak and makes him confess his sins. He will say: Do you know? He will say: O Lord, I know. He will say: I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today. He will be given his record of good deeds. As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, they will be called out before all of creation: These are the ones who lied about God. His statement: “He will be given his record of good deeds” is evidence that deeds are written in records and weighed. Ibn Majah narrated from Abdullah ibn Amr that the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: “A man from my nation will be called out on the Day of Resurrection in front of all creation, and ninety-nine scrolls will be spread out before him, each scroll extending as far as the eye can see. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, will say, ‘Do you deny any of this? ’ He will say, ‘No, O Lord. ’ He will say, ‘Did the Preservers wrong you? ’ He will say, ‘No. ’ Then He will say, ‘Do you have an excuse? Do you have a good deed? ’ The man will be afraid and say, ‘No. ’ He will say, ‘Yes, indeed, you have good deeds with Us, and there will be no injustice against you today. ’ Then a card will be brought out for him on which will be written, ‘I bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger. ’ He will say, ‘O Lord, what is this card compared to these scrolls? ’ He will say, ‘You will not be wronged. ’ The scrolls will be placed on one side of the scale and the card on the other. The scrolls will fly away and the card will be heavy.” Al-Tirmidhi added, Nothing is heavier than the name of God. He said, This is a hasan ghareeb hadith. More explanation of this topic will come in Al-Kahf and Al-Anbiyyah, God willing.
7:9: The Almighty said: "But those whose scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful. And those whose scales are light - it is they who have lost themselves because they used to wrong Our signs." Mizanui is the plural of Mizan, and its root is Mawazin. The waw was changed to Ya because of the Kasra before it. It was said: It is possible that there are scales for one worker, and each scale weighs a type of his deeds. It could be one scale expressed in the plural form, as you say: So-and-so went to Mecca on mules, and he went to Basra on ships. And in the revelation: "Say, 'My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication. You have denied, so it will be a binding one.'" (Ash-Shu'ara': 105) 'Aad denied the messengers. (Ash-Shu'ara': 123), but it is only one messenger in one of the two interpretations. It was said: Mizan is the plural of Muzain, not Mizan. He meant by Mizan the weighed deeds. And those whose scales are light is the same. Ibn Abbas said: Good deeds and bad deeds are weighed on a scale that has a tongue and two pans. As for the believer, his deeds will be brought in the best form and placed on one pan of the scale, so his good deeds will outweigh his bad deeds. This is what God said: But those whose scales are heavy - it is they who will be the successful ones. And the deeds of the disbeliever will be brought in the ugliest form and placed on the other pan of the scale, so their weight will be light until they fall into the Fire. What Ibn Abbas indicated is close to what was said: God the Almighty creates every part of the deeds of the servants as a substance, so the weight falls on those substances. Ibn Furuk and others rejected this. In the report: “If the good deeds of the believer diminish, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will take out a card the size of a fingertip and throw it into the right side of the scale, which contains his good deeds. The good deeds will outweigh the bad deeds, and that believing servant will say to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), ‘May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! How beautiful your face is and how beautiful your character is! Who are you?’ He will say, ‘I am Muhammad, your Prophet, and these are your prayers that you used to pray for me. I have fulfilled them when you were most in need of them.’” Al-Qushayri mentioned this in his interpretation. He mentioned that the card with a kasra on the ba is a piece of paper with the number of the merchandise in the language of the people of Egypt. Ibn Majah said: Muhammad ibn Yahya said: The card is the piece of paper, and the people of Egypt call the piece of paper a card. Hudhayfah said: The owner of the scales on the Day of Resurrection will be Gabriel (peace be upon him). God the Most High will say: ‘O Gabriel, weigh them and divide some by others. ’ He said: ‘There will be no gold or silver there. If the oppressor has good deeds, some of his good deeds will be taken and divided by the oppressed. If he has no good deeds, some of the oppressed’s bad deeds will be taken and loaded onto the oppressor, and the man will return with a mountain on him. It was narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “God Almighty will say on the Day of Resurrection, ‘O Adam, come out to the side of the Throne at the scale and see what deeds of your children are brought to you. Whoever outweighs his good by the weight of a grain will have Paradise, and whoever outweighs his evil by the weight of a grain will have Hellfire, until you know that I do not punish anyone except the wrongdoer.”
7:10: That is, We have made it a resting place and a cradle for you, and We have prepared for you in it the means of living. And livelihoods are the plural of livelihood, meaning that which one lives by, such as food and drink, and that which sustains life. It is said: he lived, he lives, a living, and a living, and a living, and a living. Al-Zajjaj said: livelihood is that by which one reaches a living. And livelihood according to Al-Akhfash and many grammarians is a verbal noun. Al-A'raj read: Ma'aish with a hamza. Kharijah bin Mus'ab narrated this from Nafi'. Al-Nahhas said: The hamza is a mistake that is not permissible, because the singular form is livelihood, and its root is livelihood, so the alif of connection was added, and it is silent, and the ya' is silent, so it is necessary to move it, since there is no way to delete, and the alif is not moved, so the ya' was moved as it should have been in the singular form.
