And similar to it from the waw are minara and manawaar, and maqam and muqawim: as the poet said: I am a strong and resistant force that neither Jarir nor Jarir’s client could have resisted. And also calamity and calamities. This is good, and calamities is an irregular language. Al-Akhfash said: Calamities is permissible because the singular is defective. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a mistake that requires him to say maqaim. But the saying is that it is like pillow and pillow. It was said: The hamza is not permissible in ma'aish because livelihood is mufa'il, so the ya' is original. It is only hamzated if the ya' is extra like in madinah and mada'in, sahifah and sahifah, karimah and karayem, wazifa and wazifa', and the like.
7:11: The Almighty said: And We have certainly created you, then We formed you. When He mentioned His blessings, He mentioned the beginning of His creation. The meaning of creation has already been mentioned in more than one place. Then We formed you, meaning We created you from sperm, then We formed you. Then We inform you that We said to the angels, Prostrate to Adam. And from Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak and others: The meaning is We created Adam, then We formed you on his back. Al-Akhfash said: Then means and. And it was said: The meaning is, We have certainly created you, meaning Adam, peace be upon him, then We said to the angels, Prostrate to Adam, then We formed you, in the order of precedence and delay. And it was said: And We have certainly created you, meaning Adam, mentioned in the plural form because he is the father of mankind. Then We formed you also refers to him. Just as it is said: We killed you, meaning We killed your master. Then We said to the angels, Prostrate to Adam." And based on this, there is no precedence or delay, also from Ibn Abbas. It was said: The meaning is, And We created you, meaning Adam and Eve. Adam was from dust and Eve was from one of his ribs, then the formation occurred after that. So the meaning is: And We created your parents, then formed them, said Al-Hasan. It was said: The meaning is, We created you in Adam’s back, then formed you when We took the covenant from you. This is the saying of Mujahid, narrated by Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Nujayh. An-Nahhas said: This is the best of the sayings. Mujahid believes that He created them in Adam’s back, then formed them when He took the covenant from them, then prostration occurred after that. This is strengthened by And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants (al-A’raf 7:172). And the hadith. He brought them out like ants and took a covenant from them. It was said: Then is for information, meaning, and We created you, meaning in the back of Adam, peace be upon him, then We formed you, meaning in the wombs. An-Nahhas said: This is authentic from Ibn Abbas. I said: All of these sayings are possible, and the correct one is what is supported by the revelation. God the Almighty said: And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay (al-Mu’minun 23:12) meaning Adam. And He said: And created from it its mate (An-Nisa’: 1) then He said: We made him meaning We made his offspring and descendants a sperm-drop in a firm lodging (al-Mu’minun 23:13) the verse. So Adam was created from clay then he was shaped and honored by prostration, and his descendants were shaped in the wombs of their mothers after they were created in them and in the loins of their fathers. It was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-An’am that every human being is created from sperm and soil, so reflect on that. And He said here: We created you, then We shaped you and He said at the end of al-Hashr 59:He is God, the Creator, the Maker, the Fashioner (al-Hashr 59:24) so He mentioned fashioning after innocence. And an explanation of that will come, God willing. And it was said: The meaning of And We have certainly created you is that We created the spirits first then shaped the ghosts last. The Almighty’s saying: Except Iblis, he was not among those who prostrated is an exception from a different species. It was also said: from the species. Scholars differed as to whether he was among the angels or not, as was previously explained in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:12: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: What prevented you? Ma is in the nominative case as a subject, meaning what prevented you? This is a question of rebuke. That you do not prostrate is in the accusative case, meaning that you prostrate. La is redundant. In Sad: What prevented you from prostrating? (Sad: 75) and the poet said: My father is generous, not stingy, so I hastened it. Yes, from a young man who does not prevent generosity from what he receives. Abu Judeh wanted to be stingy, so he added la and it was said that it is not redundant, because the prevention has a part of the statement and the supplication, so it is as if he said: Who told you not to prostrate? Or who called you not to prostrate? As you say: I told you not to do such and such. It was said: There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: What prevented you from obedience and made you need not to prostrate? The scholars said: What made him need to leave prostration is arrogance and envy: and he concealed that in himself when he was commanded to do so. And his command was before the creation of Adam, God Almighty says: “Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay. So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My [created] soul, then fall down to him in prostration” (Sad: 71-72), so it is as if a great matter entered him from his saying then fall down to him in prostration. For in the occurrence there is the humiliation of the reality and an honor for the one to whom it occurred, so he concealed in himself not to prostrate when he was commanded at that time. When the spirit was breathed into him, the angels fell down in prostration, and he remained standing among them. By standing and not prostrating, he revealed what was in his heart. Then God Almighty said: What prevented you from prostrating? That is, what prevented you from submitting to My command? So He revealed the secret of his heart and said: I am better than him. Second: The Almighty’s saying: When I commanded you indicates what the jurists say, that the command requires obligation in its absolute sense without any evidence, because the blame is attached to abandoning the absolute command, which is the Almighty’s saying to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, and this is clear. Third: The Almighty said: He said, ‘I am better than him.’ That is, my superiority over him prevented me from prostrating. This is from Iblis an answer to the meaning. Just as you say: Who owns this house? The one being addressed says: Its owner is Zayd. This is not the exact answer, but rather it is a statement that goes back to the meaning of the answer. You created me from fire and created him from clay. So he saw that fire is more noble than clay, because of its height, ascent, and lightness, and because it is a luminous substance. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Ibn Sirin said: The first one to make an analogy was Iblis, but he made a mistake in the analogy. Whoever compares religion with his opinion, God will associate him with Iblis. Ibn Sirin said: The sun and moon were not worshipped except by analogies. The wise men said: The enemy of God made a mistake in the superiority of fire over clay, even though they are on the same level in that they are created inanimate objects. Clay is better than fire in four ways: One of them is that the essence of clay is sobriety, calmness, dignity, calmness, forbearance, modesty, and patience. This is what prompted Adam, peace be upon him, after the happiness that preceded him, to repent, be humble, and supplicate, so He granted him forgiveness, selection, and guidance. And from the essence of fire are lightness, rashness, sharpness, haughtiness, and turmoil. This is what prompted Satan, after the misery that preceded him, to be arrogant and persistent, so He granted him destruction, torment, curse, and misery, as Al-Qaffal said. Second: The report states that the dust of Paradise is the most fragrant musk, but the report does not state that there is fire in Paradise and that there is dust in Hell. Third: Fire is the cause of torment, and it is God’s torment for His enemies, and dust is not the cause of torment. Fourth: Clay does not need fire, and fire needs a place, and its place is the earth. I said: A fifth opinion is possible, which is that the earth is a place of worship and purification, as mentioned in the authentic hadith. And the fire is intimidation and torment, as God the Almighty said: Thus God frightens His servants (al-Zumar 39:16). Ibn Abbas said: Obedience was more appropriate for Iblis than analogy, so he disobeyed his Lord, and he was the first to use analogy based on his opinion. Analogy in contradiction to the text is rejected. Fourth: People differed regarding analogy, some of whom said it and some of whom rejected it. As for those who said it, they are the Companions, the Followers, and the majority of those who came after them, and that worshipping with it is permissible rationally and legally, and this is correct. Al-Qaffal from the Shafi’is and Abu al-Husayn al-Basri held that it is obligatory to worship with it rationally. Al-Nazzam held that it is impossible to worship with it rationally and legally, and some of the people of the apparent meaning rejected it. The first is correct. Al-Bukhari said in the book of holding fast to the Book and the Sunnah: The meaning is that no one is infallible except in the Book of God or the Sunnah of His Prophet or in the consensus of the scholars if the ruling is found in them, and if it is not found, then analogy. He titled this Chapter on comparing a known principle to a clear principle whose ruling God has made clear so that the questioner may understand. He titled after this Chapter on the rulings that are known by evidence and how the meaning of evidence is and its interpretation. Al-Tabari said: Ijtihad and deduction from the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the consensus of the nation is the obligatory truth and the necessary duty for the people of knowledge. And thus came the report from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from the group of the Companions and the Followers. Abu Tammam Al-Maliki said: The nation agreed on analogy, and among that they agreed on analogy of gold and silver in zakat. Abu Bakr said: Release me from my pledge of allegiance. Ali said: By God, we will not release you nor will we ask you to resign. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with you for our religion, so should we not be pleased with you for our worldly life? So he compared the Imamate to prayer. Abu Bakr compared zakat to prayer and said: By God, I do not differentiate between what God has united. Ali stated the analogy in the case of a drinker of alcohol in the presence of the Companions and said: If he gets drunk he raves, and if he raves he fabricates, so his punishment is the punishment of a slanderer. Omar wrote a letter to Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari in which he said: Understanding is understanding in what is in your heart that has not reached you in the Book and the Sunnah. Know the examples and similarities, then compare matters accordingly, and go for what is most beloved to God Almighty and most similar to the truth, as you see. The hadith in full was mentioned by Al-Daraqutni. Abu Ubaidah said to Umar may God be pleased with them in the hadith of the epidemic, when Umar returned from Sargh: Did you flee from the decree of God? Umar said: Yes! Flee from the decree of God to the decree of God. Then Umar said to him: Have you seen... So he compared and debated him with what resembles his question in the presence of the Muhajireen and Ansar, and that is enough for you. As for the narrations and verses of the Qur’an in this meaning, they are many. It indicates that analogy is a principle of the principles of religion, and a protection from the protection of Muslims, to which the mujtahids refer, and the working scholars resort to it, and they derive rulings from it. This is the opinion of the group who are the proof, and no attention should be paid to those who deviate from it. As for the reprehensible opinion and the forced analogy that is forbidden, it is that which is not based on these principles mentioned, because that is conjecture and a temptation from Satan. God the Almighty said: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge (al-Isra’ 17:36). And all the weak hadiths and flimsy reports that the opponent cites in denouncing analogy are attributed to this type of reprehensible analogy, which has no known basis in the Shari’ah. This chapter is completed in the books of principles.
7:13: God the Almighty said: He said, 'Then descend from it' meaning from the sky. For it is not for you to be arrogant therein because its inhabitants are the humble angels. Then get out, for you are among the debased meaning among the humiliated. This indicates that whoever disobeys his Lord is humiliated. Abu Rawq and Al-Bajali said: Then descend from it meaning from the form you are in, because he boasted that he was from the fire, so his form was distorted by the darkness and the disappearance of his radiance. It was said: Then descend from it meaning move from the earth to the islands of the seas, as one says: We descended to such and such a land, meaning we moved to it from another place, so it is as if he was taken out from the earth to the islands of the seas, so his authority is there, and he does not enter the earth except like a thief who fears it until he leaves it. The first statement is more apparent. It was mentioned earlier in Al-Baqarah.
7:14: He asked for a look and a respite until the Day of Resurrection and Judgment. He asked not to die because there is no death after the Day of Resurrection.
7:15: Then God the Almighty said: Indeed, you are among those granted respite. Ibn Abbas, Al-Suddi and others said: He granted him respite until the first blast when all of creation will die. He asked for respite until the second blast when people will stand before the Lord of the Worlds, but God refused him that. He said: Until the Day they are resurrected, and he did not mention who will be resurrected before, because the story is about Adam and his descendants, so the context indicates that they are the ones who will be resurrected.
7:16: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Because You have misled me. Misleading means causing error in the heart, meaning because You have caused error, stubbornness, and arrogance in my heart. This is because the disbelief of Iblis is not the disbelief of ignorance, but rather it is the disbelief of stubbornness and arrogance. This has been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. It has been said that the meaning of the statement is an oath, meaning because You have misled me, I will sit for them on Your path, or in Your path, but it was omitted. The evidence for this statement is His saying in (Sad): By Your might, I will mislead them all (Sad: 82). It is as if Iblis magnified the status of God’s misleading him because of what it entails of power over the servants, so He swore by it to magnify his status with Him. It has been said that the letter ba’ has the meaning of lam, as if he said: Because of Your misleading me. It has also been said that it has the meaning of with, and the meaning is because of Your misleading me. It has also been said that it is a question, as if he asked by what means did He mislead him? In this case, it should have been: By what did You mislead me? It was said: The meaning is: Because You have destroyed me by cursing me. And al-ghawa means destruction. God Almighty said: Then they will meet with error (Maryam 19:59) meaning destruction. And it was said: Because You have led me astray. And al-ghawa means misguidance and distancing, as Ibn Abbas said. And it was said: You have disappointed me in Your mercy, and from this is the saying of the poet: And whoever goes astray will not be without someone to blame him for his error. Any one who is deceived. Ibn al-A'rabi said: It is said that a man has gone astray, if his affair has been corrupted for him, or he has become corrupt in himself. This is one of the meanings of the Almighty's saying: And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray (Ta-Ha 20:124), meaning his life in Paradise was corrupted. It is also said that a young camel has gone astray if it does not produce its mother's milk. Second: The doctrine of the Sunnis is that God the Almighty led him astray and created in him disbelief, and therefore he attributed the seduction in this to God the Almighty. And this is the truth, for there is nothing in existence except that it was created by Him, emanating from His will the Almighty. The Imamis, the Qadarites, and others disagreed with their sheikh, Iblis, whom they obeyed in everything he made attractive to them, but they did not obey him in this issue and they say: Iblis made a mistake, and he is capable of making mistakes when he attributed the seduction to his Lord, God is exalted above that. So it is said to them: Even if Iblis is capable of making mistakes, what do you do with an honored and infallible prophet? He is Noah, peace be upon him, when he said to his al-Nas 114:“And my advice will not benefit you, if I wanted to advise you. If God wants to mislead you, He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.” (Hud 11:34) It was narrated that a man came to Tawus in the Sacred Mosque, and he was interested in predestination, and he was one of the great jurists, so he sat down with him and Tawus said to him: Will you stand up or be made to stand up? So it was said to Tawus: You say this to a jurist! He said: Satan is more knowledgeable than him. Satan says: O Lord, because You have led me astray. And this one says: I am leading myself astray. Third: The Almighty’s saying: I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path, meaning by turning them away from it and beautifying falsehood until they perish as he perished, or go astray as he went astray, or fail as he failed, according to what was mentioned previously from the three meanings of you led me astray. The straight path is the road that leads to Paradise, and your path is in the accusative case due to the deletion of on or in from His saying: your straight path, as Sibawayh narrated that Zayd struck his back and stomach. And he recited: When he shakes his hand, his back becomes honeyed, just as the fox swallows honey on the road.
7:17: And among the best things that have been said in the interpretation of: Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left meaning I will turn them away from the truth, and make them desire this world, and make them doubt the Hereafter. And this is the ultimate in misguidance. As He said: And I will mislead them (al-Nisa 4:119) according to what was mentioned above. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah who said: From before them from their worldly life. And from behind them from their Hereafter. And from their right means their good deeds. And from their left means their bad deeds. An-Nahhas said: This is a good statement and its explanation is that the meaning of then I will come to them from before them from their worldly life, until they deny what is in it of signs and report of the previous nations, and from behind them from their Hereafter until they deny it. And from their right of their good deeds and matters of their religion. This is indicated by His statement: Indeed, you used to come to us from the right (al-Saffat 37:28). And from their left means their bad deeds, that is, they follow desires, because He makes them seem attractive to them. And you will not find most of them grateful that is, monotheists, obedient, and showing gratitude.
7:18: God the Almighty said: He said, 'Get out of it' meaning from Paradise. Disgraced and banished. Disgraced means blameworthy. And blame is the defect, with a lightened meem. Ibn Zayd said: Disgraced and blameworthy are the same. It is said: I blamed him, I blamed him, and I blamed him, with the same meaning. Al-A'mash read Madhmoon. The meaning is the same, except that he lightened the hamza. Mujahid said: The blameworthy is the one who is banished. The two meanings are close. And the banished is the one who is banished, according to Mujahid and others. Its original meaning is repelling. For whoever follows you among them, I will surely fill Hell with you all The lam is the lam of an oath, and the response is to I will fill Hell. It was said: For whoever follows you, it is a lam of emphasis. I will fill it is a lam of an oath. The evidence for this is that in other readings it is permissible to delete the first lam, but it is not permissible to delete the second. There is a sense of condition and recompense in the speech, meaning whoever follows you, I will punish him. If you said: Whoever follows you, I will punish him, it would not be permissible, unless you mean I will punish him. Asim read from the narration of Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, Whoever follows you from among them, with a kasra on the lam. Some grammarians rejected this. An-Nahhas said: And its meaning - and God knows best - is for the sake of whoever follows you. Just as it is said: I honored so-and-so for you. The meaning could be: To repel whoever follows you. The meaning of from among you all is from you and from the children of Adam, because their mention has already occurred when He said: And We have certainly created you, addressing the children of Adam.
7:19: He said to Adam after Iblis was expelled from his place in heaven: Dwell, you and Eve, in Paradise. The meaning of dwelling has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no need to repeat it. The meaning of And do not approach this tree (al-Baqarah 2:35) has already been mentioned there. Praise be to God.
7:20: The Almighty said: Then Satan whispered to them meaning to them. It was said: inside Paradise by the snake entering him. It was said: from outside, by the authority that was given to him. This has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. And the whisper: is the low voice. And the whisper: is the talk of the soul, it is said: his soul whispered to him a whisper and a whisper with a kasra on the waw. And the whisper with a fatha: is a noun, like an earthquake. And the whispering of the hunter and dogs and the sounds of jewelry are called: a whisper. Al-A'sha said: You hear the whispering of jewelry when you turn away, as if you were helped by the scent of a young camel. And the whisperer: is the name of the devil, God Almighty said: From the evil of the retreating whisperer (al-Nas 114:4) to reveal to them meaning to appear to them. And the lam is the lam of consequence, as He said: to be to them an enemy and a grief and it was said: the lam of ki. And to be hidden means to cover and conceal from them. And it is permissible in other than the Qur'an to be hidden, like to be killed and from their private parts from her private parts and the private parts were called private parts because revealing them makes its owner feel bad. And this indicates the ugliness of revealing them, so it was said: their private parts were revealed to them and not to others, there was a light on them so their private parts could not be seen, then the light disappeared, and it was said: a garment, so it fell apart and God knows best. Except that you two are angels "that is in the accusative case, meaning except, out of dislike of that", so the complement was deleted, this is the saying of the Basrans. And the Kufians say: so that you two are not. And it was said: meaning except that you two are angels who know good and evil. It was said: Adam desired immortality because he knew that the angels would not die until the Day of Resurrection. An-Nahhas said: God the Almighty has mentioned the superiority of the angels over all creation in more than one place in the Qur’an, including this, unless you are two angels. And from it: nor do I say that I am an angel (Hud 11:31). And from it: nor the angels brought near (An-Nisa’: 172). Al-Hasan said: God preferred the angels with images, wings, and honor. Another said: He preferred them, glory be to Him, with obedience and refraining from disobedience, so preference occurs in everything. Ibn Furak said: There is no proof in this verse, because it is possible that he meant two angels in that they have no desire for food. The choice of Ibn Abbas, Az-Zajjaj, and many scholars is to prefer the believers over the angels, and this has been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Al-Kalbi said: They are preferred over all creation, except for a group of angels: Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death, because they are among the messengers of God. Each group held to the apparent meanings of the Shariah, and the grace is in the hand of God. Ibn Abbas read two angels with a kasra on the lam, which is the reading of Yahya bin Abi Katheer and Ad-Dahhak. Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ rejected the kasra on the lam and said: There was no king before Adam, peace be upon him, so they would become two kings. An-Nahhas said: According to this reading, it is permissible to make the lam sukoon, but it is not permissible according to the first reading due to the lightness of the fatha. Ibn Abbas said: The cursed one came to them from the direction of the king, and for this reason he said: I will guide you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will not decay (Ta-Ha 20:120). Abu Ubaid claimed that Yahya bin Abi Katheer’s argument with his saying: and a kingdom that will not decay is a clear argument, but people are inclined to abandon it, so this is why we abandoned it. An-Nahhas said: Unless you are two kings is an anomalous reading. Abu Ubaid was criticized for this statement, and considered it a grave mistake. Is it permissible for Adam, peace be upon him, to imagine that he would attain more than the kingdom of Paradise, which is the ultimate goal of seekers? Rather, the meaning of and a kingdom that will not decay is the status of the kingdom of Paradise, and eternity in it.
7:21: The Almighty said: And he swore to them meaning he made an oath to them. It is said: he swore an oath, meaning he made an oath. The poet said: I swear by God that I will do my best for you, for you are sweeter than quails when they are raised. The word fa'ilat came from one word. This is a response to those who said that the word mufa'ala can only come from two people. It was mentioned before in Al-Ma'idah. Indeed, I am to you both among the sincere advisers. Lakumā is not included in the relative clause. The meaning is: I am to you both among the sincere advisers, said Hisham Al-Nahwi. Something similar was mentioned before in Al-Baqarah. The meaning of the statement is: Follow me, I will guide you both, as mentioned by Qatada.
7:22: The Almighty said: And he led them astray with deception He caused them to fall into destruction. Ibn Abbas said: He deceived them with an oath. Adam thought that no one would swear falsely by God, so he deceived them with his whisperings and his oath to them. Qatada said: He swore to them by God until he deceived them. And the believer may be deceived by God. Some scholars used to say: He who deceives us by God, we will be deceived. And in the hadith about him, may God bless him and grant him peace: The believer is a generous and arrogant person, while the wicked person is a vile and mean person. Naftawayh recited: If you want to deceive a generous person, you can deceive him. But you will see that the mean person is experienced and cannot be deceived. He let them go means he sent it out. And he let it go: he brought it out. And it was said: he let them go, meaning he spoiled them, from the word daala which means part. That is, he made them bold to commit the sin, so they left Paradise. The Almighty’s saying: “So when they tasted of the tree, their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise.” There are three issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: So when they tasted of the tree, meaning they ate from it. The disagreement over this tree and how Adam ate from it has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Their private parts became apparent to them, Eve ate first and nothing affected her. When Adam ate, the punishment was imposed, because the prohibition was imposed on them, as mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Ibn Abbas said: The light that was their clothing shrank and became nails on the hands and feet. The second - the Almighty’s saying: And they began and it is permissible to make the fa’ sukoon. Al-Akhfash narrated tafaqa yatfaqa, like daraba yadhuru. It is said: tafaqa, meaning he began to do the action. Yakhtasifaan and Al-Hasan read it with a kasra on the kha’ and a shaddah on the sad. The original is yachthafaan, so it was assimilated, and the kha’ was broken because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Ibn Buraidah and Ya’qub read it with a fatha on the kha’, they dropped the vowel of the ta’ on it. It is permissible to yachthafaan with a damma on the ya’, from khasaf yasif. Al-Zuhri read yachthafaan from akhsaf. Both are transmitted with a hamza or doubling and the meaning is: they cut the paper and stick it together to cover themselves with it, and from this comes the khasaf of the sandal, and the khasaf that is patched, and the perforated mukhassaf. Ibn Abbas said: It is the fig leaf. It is narrated that when Adam, peace be upon him, became exposed and his private parts became apparent, he went around the trees of Paradise pulling out a leaf to cover his private parts, so the trees of Paradise rebuked him until the fig tree took pity on him and gave him a leaf. So they, meaning Adam and Eve, began to sew together for themselves from the leaves of Paradise. So God rewarded them by making its exterior and interior equal in sweetness and benefit, and gave them two fruits in one year, twice. Third: The verse contains evidence of the ugliness of revealing the private parts, and that God has made it obligatory for them to cover them, and therefore they hastened to cover them. It is not impossible that they were commanded to do so in Paradise, as it was said to them, Do not approach this tree. The author of Al-Bayan narrated on the authority of Al-Shafi’i that whoever does not find anything to cover his private parts with except tree leaves must cover himself with that, because it is an apparent covering that he can cover himself with, as Adam did in Paradise. And God knows best. God Almighty says: And their Lord called to them, ‘Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?’ That is, He said to them: Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?
7:23: They said, 'Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers.' They said, Our Lord is a vocative complement. The original is O our Lord. It was said that O is omitted, indicating glorification. So they confessed their sin and repented, may God bless them and grant them peace. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:24: The meaning of his saying, He said, ‘Go down,’ also came before the end of the verse.
7:25: All the pronouns refer to the earth. The waw was not mentioned in qala, but if it had been mentioned it would have also been permissible. It is like saying: Zaid said to Amr such-and-such. He said to him such-and-such.
7:26: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts. Many scholars said: This verse is evidence of the obligation to cover one’s private parts, because He said: to conceal your private parts. Some people said: It does not contain evidence for what they mentioned, but rather it only indicates a blessing. I said: The first statement is more correct. Among the blessings is covering the private parts, so He made clear that He, the Most High, made for His offspring something with which to cover their private parts, and He indicated the command to cover them. There is no disagreement among scholars about the obligation to cover the private parts from the eyes of people. They differed about what the private parts are. Ibn Abi Dhi’b said: It is the private parts of a man, the front and back, and nothing else. This is the statement of Dawud, the people of the apparent meaning, Ibn Abi Ubla, and al-Tabari, because God Almighty said: A garment to conceal your private parts, “Their private parts became apparent to them,” To show them their private parts. And in al-Bukhari on the authority of Anas: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ran through the alley of Khaybar - and in it - then he pulled up his garment from his thigh until I could see the whiteness of the thigh of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Malik said: The navel is not private, and I dislike for a man to uncover his thigh in the presence of his wife. Abu Hanifa said: The knee is private. This is the opinion of Ata’. Al-Shafi’i said: The navel and the knees are not private according to the correct view. Abu Hamid al-Tirmidhi narrated that al-Shafi’i had two opinions regarding the navel. Malik’s evidence is his saying, peace be upon him, to Jarhad: Cover your thigh, for the thigh is private.” Al-Bukhari included it in a suspended chain of transmission and said: The hadith of Anas is more authentic, and the hadith of Jarhad is more cautious so as to avoid their differences. This hadith of Jarhad indicates the opposite of what Abu Hanifa said. It was narrated that Abu Hurairah kissed the navel of al-Hasan ibn Ali and said: I accept from you what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have accepted from you.” If the navel were an ‘awrah, Abu Hurairah would not have kissed it, nor would Al-Hasan have allowed him to touch it. As for the free woman, her entire body is ‘awrah except for the face and hands. This is the view of most scholars. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wants to marry a woman should look at her face and hands. Because it is obligatory to uncover it during ihram. Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham said: Everything about a woman is ‘awrah, even her fingernails. Something similar was narrated from Ahmad ibn Hanbal. As for the mother of a child, al-Athram said: I heard him - meaning Ahmad ibn Hanbal - being asked about the mother of a child, how should she pray? He said: She should cover her head and feet, because she is not sold, and she should pray as a free woman prays. As for the female slave, her ‘awrah is what is under her breasts. She may show her head and wrists. It was said: Her ruling is the ruling on her as on a man. It was said: It is disliked for her to uncover her head and chest. ‘Umar may God be pleased with him used to beat female slaves for covering their heads and say: Do not resemble free women. Asbagh said: If her thigh is exposed, she should repeat the prayer during its time. Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham said: Everything about the female slave is ‘awrah, even her fingernails. This is outside the sayings of the jurists, because they unanimously agreed that a free woman may pray the obligatory prayer with her hands and face uncovered, all of that, touching the ground with it. The slave woman is more deserving, and the mother of the child is in a worse state than the slave woman. The private parts of the young boy are not sacred. So when the girl reaches an age where the eye takes hold of her and she is desired, her private parts are covered. The evidence of Abu Bakr bin Abd al-Rahman is the saying of God the Almighty: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments (al-Ahzab 33:59). And the hadith of Umm Salamah that she was asked: What clothes should a woman pray in? She said: She should pray in a long shirt and veil that covers the tops of her feet. It has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Those who traced it back to Umm Salamah are more numerous and have better memory, including Malik, Ibn Ishaq and others. Abu Dawud said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd God ibn Dinar narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the authority of Muhammad ibn Zayd on the authority of his mother on the authority of Umm Salamah that she asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu ‘Umar said: This Abd al-Rahman is weak according to them, except that al-Bukhari included some of his hadeeths. The consensus on this matter is stronger than the hadeeth. Second: The Almighty’s statement: We have sent down upon you clothing meaning the rain that grows cotton and flax, and sustains the animals from which wool, fur and hair are produced. It is a metaphor like And He has sent down for you from the livestock eight mates (al-Zumar 39:6) as will come. It was said: This sending down is the sending down of some clothing with Adam and Eve, to be an example for others. Saeed bin Jubair said: We sent down upon you meaning We created for you, like His statement: And He has sent down for you from the livestock eight mates meaning He created. As will come. It was said: We inspired you with how to make it. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And feathers. Abu Abd al-Rahman, al-Hasan, and Asim read from the narration of al-Mufassal al-Dabbi, and Abu Amr from the narration of al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Ja’fi: and feathers. Abu Ubaidah did not narrate it except from al-Hasan, and he did not explain its meaning. It is the plural of feathers. It is what is from money and clothing. Al-Farra’ said: feathers and feathers, as it is said: clothes and clothing. The feathers of a bird are what God covers it with. It was said: it is fertility and a comfortable life. What most linguists agree on is that feathers are what covers from clothing or livelihood. Sibawayh recited: Freshi is from you and my hobby is with you, even if your visit is for my mother Abu Hatim narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah: He gave him a beast with its feathers, meaning with its fur and whatever clothing it had on. And rough clothing, which is what one wears to humble oneself before God Almighty and worship Him, is better than anything else. And Zaid bin Ali said: Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And the clothing of righteousness - that is best. He explained that righteousness is the best clothing, as He said: If a person does not wear clothes of piety, he will be naked even if he is clothed. The best clothing for a person is obedience to his Lord, and there is no good in one who disobeys God. Qasim bin Malik bin Auf narrated on the authority of Ma’bad Al-Juhani, who said: The garment of piety is modesty. Ibn Abbas said: The clothing of piety is righteous deeds. It was also narrated from him: The good appearance on the face. It was said: What the Almighty taught and guided by. It was said: The clothing of piety is wearing wool and rough clothes, which is what one humbles oneself with before God the Almighty and worships Him better than anything else. Zaid bin Ali said: The clothing of piety is the armor, helmet, forearms, and legs, with which one protects oneself in war. Urwah bin Az-Zubayr said: It is the fear of God. It was said: It is the sense of piety towards God the Almighty in what He has commanded and forbidden. I said: This is correct, and the sayings of Ibn Abbas and Urwah go back to it. The saying of Zaid bin Ali is good, because he urged people to fight. Ibn Zaid said: It is covering the private parts. This is repetitive, because he said first: We have sent down upon you clothing to conceal your private parts. And whoever said: It is wearing rough clothing, because it is closer to modesty and avoiding recklessness, then it is a claim, because the virtuous scholars used to wear fine clothing while achieving piety, as will be explained later, God willing. The people of Medina and Al-Kisa’i read clothes in the accusative case in apposition to the first clothes. It was said: It is in the accusative case with an implied verb, meaning, and We sent down the clothing of piety. The rest read it in the nominative case as the subject. This is its description and the best predicate of the subject. The meaning is: And the clothing of piety referred to, which you have learned, is better for you than wearing the clothing that conceals your private parts, and than the finery that We have sent down to you, so wear it. It was said: It is in the nominative case with the implied it, meaning, and it is the clothing of piety, meaning, it is covering the private parts. And based on this, the statement of Ibn Zayd is derived. It was said: The meaning is: The clothing of piety is good, so that means it. The first parsing is the best that has been said about it. Al-A’mash read: The clothing of piety is good, but he did not read that. This is contrary to the Qur’an. That is from the signs of God meaning that it indicates that He has a Creator. This is in the nominative case as an attribute, or as a substitute, or as an explanatory apposition.
7:27: There are two issues: First: The Almighty said: Let not Satan tempt you meaning let not Satan divert you from the religion, as he tempted your parents by expelling them from Paradise. Ab is for the masculine, and Aba is for the feminine. Based on this, it is said: two parents. He strips them of their clothing is in the accusative case as a state. It is a new sentence, so it is stopped at from Paradise. "To show them is accusative with the lam of ki. Indeed, he and his tribe see you. The original is to see you", then the hamza was lightened. "His tribe" is in apposition to the pronoun and is an emphasis to make the apposition better, like His statement: "You and your wife are Paradise" (al-Baqarah 2:35). This indicates that it is ugly to see you and Amr, and that the pronoun is like the apparent. This is also evidence of the obligation to cover the private parts, because He said: "He strips them of their clothing." Others said: It is only a warning against the loss of blessings, as it was revealed to Adam, peace be upon him. This is because if it were proven that the law of Adam is binding on us, and the matter is otherwise. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, he and his tribe see you, the tribe of his soldiers. Mujahid said: He means the jinn and the devils. Ibn Zayd: His tribe is his offspring. It was also said: His generation. From where you do not see them, some scholars said: This is evidence that the jinn are not seen, because He said: From where you do not see them. It was also said: It is permissible for them to see because when God the Almighty wants to see them, He reveals their bodies so that you can see them. An-Nahhas said: From where you do not see them indicates that the jinn are not seen except at the time of a prophet, so that this would be evidence of his prophethood, because God the Almighty created them in a way in which they are not seen, and they are only seen when they are transferred from their forms. This is one of the miracles that only occur at the time of the prophets, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them. Al-Qushayri said: God has made it a habit for the children of Adam not to see the devils today. And in the hadith: Satan runs through the son of Adam as blood runs. And God Almighty said: He who whispers in the hearts of mankind (al-Nas 114:5). And he, peace be upon him, said: “The king has a touch and the devil has a touch - that is, in the heart - as for the touch of the king, it is a promise of good and belief in the truth, and as for the touch of the devil, it is a promise of evil and denial of the truth.” It was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah. There are authentic narrations about their vision. Al-Bukhari narrated “on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entrusted me with guarding the Ramadan zakat, and he mentioned a long story in which he mentioned that he captured the jinn who was taking the dates, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “What did your prisoner do last night?” It was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. In Sahih Muslim, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, if it were not for the supplication of my brother Solomon, he would have become chained up and played with by the children of the city” - about the demon that had escaped from him. And it will come in S, God willing. Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe meaning to increase their punishment and make them equal in straying from the truth.
7:28: The immorality here, according to most commentators, is their circumambulating the House naked. Al-Hasan said: It is polytheism and disbelief. They argued for that by imitating their ancestors, and by saying that God commanded them to do it. Al-Hasan said: And God commanded us to do it. They said: If God hated what we are doing, He would have moved away from it. “Say: God does not command immorality.” It is clear that they are arbitrary, and they have no evidence that God commanded them to do what they claimed. The condemnation of imitation and many of their ignorances have already been condemned. This is one of them.
7:29: The Almighty said: "Say: My Lord has commanded justice." Ibn Abbas said: There is no god but God. It was said: Justice is fairness, meaning He commanded justice, so obey Him. There is an ellipsis in the speech. And turn your faces toward Him meaning face the qiblah in every prayer. At every mosque meaning in any mosque you are. And call upon Him, devoting your religion to Him alone meaning worship Him alone and do not associate partners with Him. As He began you, you will return is similar to And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time (al-An’am 6:94) and it has been mentioned before. The kaf is in the accusative case, meaning you will return as He began you, meaning as He created you the first time, He will return you. Al-Zajjaj said: It is related to what came before it. Meaning, from it you will emerge as He began you, you will return.
7:30: A group He guided A group is in the accusative case as a state of the implied word in You return, meaning you return as two groups: happy and miserable. This is strengthened by the reading of Abu Ta'udun as two groups, a group He guided and a group upon whom error is due, on the authority of Al-Kisa'i. Muhammad bin Ka'b Al-Qurazi said about the verse of God the Almighty: A group He guided and a group upon whom error is due He said: Whoever God began his creation for misguidance, He will make him misguided, even if he does the deeds of the people of guidance. And whoever God began his creation for guidance, He will make him guided, even if he does the deeds of the people of misguidance. God began the creation of Iblis for misguidance, and he did the deeds of happiness with the angels, then God returned him to what He began his creation for. He said: And he was of the disbelievers (Sad: 74). This is a clear response to the Qadarites and those who follow them. It was said: A group used the word guidance in the accusative case, and the second group used the word guidance in the accusative case with an implied verb, meaning, and led a group astray. Sibawayh recited: I no longer carry a weapon nor do I own the camel's head if it strikes I fear the wolf if I pass by it alone, and I fear the wind and the rain. Al-Farra’ said: If it were in the nominative case, it would have been permissible. Indeed, they have taken the devils as allies instead of God. And Isa ibn Umar read: that they with the opening of the hamza, meaning because they.
7:31: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O children of Adam is addressed to the entire world, even if what is meant by it is those Arabs who circumambulate the House naked, then it is general for every mosque for prayer. Because the point is the generality, not the reason. Some scholars denied that what is meant by it is circumambulation, because circumambulation is only done in one mosque, and what is general for every mosque is prayer. This is the statement of someone who is unaware of the objectives of the Shari’ah. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: A woman would walk around the Kaaba naked and say: Who will lend me a walking stick? She would put it on her vagina and say: Today some or all of it appears, and whatever appears of it I do not permit. Then this verse was revealed: Take your adornment at every mosque. Tawaf with a kasra on the ta’. This woman is Duba’ah bint Amir ibn Qart, as stated by Judge Iyad. And in Sahih Muslim also on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah on the authority of his father, he said: The Arabs used to circumambulate the House naked, except for the Hums. The Hums were Quraysh and what they gave birth to. They used to circumambulate the House naked unless the Hums gave them clothes, so the men would give the men and the women the women. The Hums would not leave Muzdalifah, and all the people would stand at Arafat. In a hadith other than Muslim: They say, We are the people of the sanctuary, so no Arab should circumambulate except in our clothes, and when he enters our land, he should not eat except from our food. So whoever did not have an Arab friend in Mecca to lend him a garment or money to hire one with, was faced with one of two choices: Either circumambulate the House naked, or circumambulate in his clothes. When he finished his circumambulation, he would throw his garment off him and no one would touch it. That garment was called al-Laqee. An Arab said: Enough of his grief, he looks like he has found a harem in the hands of the circumambulators. They remained in that ignorance, innovation and misguidance until God sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then God Almighty revealed: O children of Adam, take your adornment verse. And the muezzin of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, announced: No one should circumambulate the House naked. I said: And whoever said that what is meant is prayer, then its adornment is sandals, because of what Karz bin Wabra narrated on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said one day: Take the adornment of prayer. It was said: What is the adornment of prayer? He said: Put on your shoes and pray in them. Second: The verse indicates the obligation to cover the private parts, as mentioned above. The majority of scholars are of the view that it is an obligation of prayer. Al-Abhari said that it is an obligation in general, and a person must cover it from the eyes of people during prayer and otherwise. This is correct, based on the statement of the Prophet, peace be upon him, to Al-Miswar bin Makhramah: “Return to your garment and take it and do not walk naked.” Narrated by Muslim. Ismail Al-Qadi said that covering the private parts is one of the Sunnahs of prayer, and he argued that if it were an obligation in prayer, then the naked person would not be permitted to pray, because every obligation in prayer must be performed if one is able to do it, or its replacement if one is not able to do it, or the prayer is dropped altogether, and this is not the case. Ibn Al-Arabi said: If we say that covering the private parts is an obligation in prayer, and the garment of an imam falls and his anus is exposed while he is bowing, so he raises his head and covers it, that is sufficient for him, as stated by Ibn Al-Qasim. Sahnoon said: And whoever among the followers looks at him must repeat it. It was also narrated from Sahnoon that he repeats it and they repeat it, because covering the private parts is a condition of prayer, so if it is exposed, the prayer is invalidated - its basic principle is purity - Al-Qadi Ibn Al-Arabi said: As for those who said that their prayer is not invalidated, they did not miss a condition, and as for those who said that if he takes it in its place, his prayer is valid and the prayer of whoever looks at it is invalidated, then it is a document that must be erased and it is not permissible to engage in it. In Bukhari and Al-Nisa’i, “On the authority of Amr bin Salamah, he said: When my people returned from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, they said: He said: Let the one among you who recites the most Qur’an lead you in prayer. He said: So leave me alone and teach me how to bow and prostrate, and I led them in prayer while I was wearing a torn cloak. They used to say to my father: Why don’t you cover your son’s anus from us? The wording of al-Nasa’i. It was proven on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d that he said: “The men were tying their belts around their necks because of the tightness of the belts behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during prayer, like children. Then someone said: O women, do not raise your heads until the men raise them.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Al-Nasa’i and Abu Dawud. Third: They differed about whether he saw his own private parts. Al-Shafi’i said: If the garment is tight, he should button it or sew it together with something so that the shirt does not stick out and the private parts are seen from the pocket. If he does not do that and sees his own private parts, he should repeat the prayer. This is the opinion of Ahmad. Malik permitted praying in an unbuttoned shirt, without trousers. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and Abu Thawr. Salim used to pray with the buttons unbuttoned. Dawud al-Ta’i said: If he has a large beard, there is nothing wrong with it. Al-Athram narrated the same meaning from Ahmad. If he is an imam, he should not pray except in his cloak, because it is an adornment. It was also said: Among the adornments of prayer is praying in shoes. It was narrated by Anas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but it is not authentic. It was said: The adornment of prayer is raising the hands during bowing and rising from it. Abu Omar said: Everything has an adornment, and the adornment of prayer is glorifying God and raising the hands. Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: If God has given you plenty, then give yourselves plenty. A man gathered his clothes together and prayed in a lower garment and a rida’, in a lower garment and a shirt, in a lower garment and a cloak, in trousers and a rida’, in trousers and a shirt, in trousers and a cloak - and I think he said: in a pair of pants and a shirt - in a pair of pants and a rida’, in a pair of pants and a cloak. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Al-Darqutni. Fourth: The Almighty said: And eat and drink, but be not excessive. Ibn Abbas said: In this verse, God permitted eating and drinking as long as it is not excessive or fanciful. As for what is necessary, which is what satisfies hunger and quenches thirst, it is recommended by reason and law, because it preserves the soul and guards the senses. Therefore, law came with the prohibition of continuous eating, because it weakens the body and kills the soul, and weakens one from worship, and law prohibits this and reason repels it. And whoever deprives himself of what is necessary has no share of righteousness or asceticism, because what deprives him of doing acts of obedience due to inability and weakness is more rewarding and greater in recompense. There are two opinions regarding what exceeds what is necessary: Some say it is forbidden, and some say it is disliked. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is correct, because the amount of satiety differs according to countries, times, ages, and foods. Then it was said: In eating less there are many benefits, including that a man is healthier physically, has a better memory, is more intelligent, sleeps less, and has a lighter breath. Eating too much causes stomach upset and the stench of overeating, and various diseases arise from it. Therefore, it requires more treatment than eating too little. Some wise men said: The best medicine is to estimate the food. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained this meaning in a clear statement that makes the words of doctors unnecessary. He said: “No vessel of Adam fills worse than his stomach. A few mouthfuls are sufficient for the son of Adam to straighten his back. If he must, then a third for his food, a third for his drink, and a third for his breath.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Al-Miqdam bin Ma’di Karib. Our scholars said: If Hippocrates had heard this division, he would have been amazed at this wisdom. It is mentioned that Al-Rashid had a skilled Christian doctor, so he said to Ali bin Al-Hussein: There is nothing in your book about medicine, and knowledge is of two types: the knowledge of religions and the knowledge of bodies. Ali said to him: God has gathered all of medicine in half a verse of our book. He said to him: What is it? He said: The Almighty’s saying: And eat and drink, but be not excessive. The Christian said: Nothing about medicine has been transmitted from your Messenger. Ali said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered medicine in a few words. He said: What are they? He said: “The stomach is the home of disease, and diet is the head of every medicine. Give every body what it is accustomed to.” The Christian said: Your book and your prophet did not leave any medicine for Galen. I said: It is said that treating a sick person is two halves: half medicine and half diet. If they come together, then it is as if the sick person has recovered and become healthy. Otherwise, diet is more appropriate for him, since medicine is of no use if diet is not followed. However, diet is of no use if medicine is not followed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The origin of all medicine is diet. What is meant by this - and God knows best - is that it replaces all other medicine. Therefore it is said that the main treatment of the Indians is diet. The patient abstains from eating, drinking, and speaking for several days, then he recovers and becomes healthy. Fifth: Muslim narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The unbeliever eats with seven intestines, while the believer eats with one intestine.” This is an exhortation from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to reduce worldly affairs, to be ascetic in them, and to be content with what is sufficient. The Arabs used to praise eating little and criticize eating too much. As one of them said: A piece of liver is enough for him if he suffers from it from grilling, and a drink of water quenches his thirst. Umm Zar’ said about Ibn Abi Zar’: He will be satisfied with the arm of a jufrah. Hatim al-Ta’i said, criticizing overeating: If you give your stomach what it asks for and your private parts what they want, they will all be blamed. Al-Khattabi said: The meaning of his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: The believer eats in one intestine is that he eats without being full, and he gives preference to himself and keeps some of his food for others, so what he eats is satisfied. The first interpretation is better, and God knows best. It was said that his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: The disbeliever eats in seven intestines is not general, because observation disproves it, as there may be a disbeliever who eats less than a believer, and the disbeliever converts to Islam, so his food does not decrease or increase. It was said: It is a reference to a specific person. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, hosted a disbeliever guest, and it was said: He was Al-Jahjah Al-Ghifari. It was also said: Thamama bin Aththal. It was also said: Nadlah bin Amr Al-Ghifari. It was also said: Basrah bin Abi Basrah Al-Ghifari. He drank the milk of seven sheep, then he became a Muslim in the morning and drank the milk of one sheep but did not finish it, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that. It is as if he said: This is the disbeliever. And God knows best. It was said: When the heart was enlightened by the light of monotheism, it looked at food with the eye of piety in obedience, so it took from it as much as it needed. When it was darkened by disbelief, it ate it like an animal grazing until it was full. There is a difference of opinion about these intestines, are they real or not? It was said: They are real, and they have names known to those who know medicine and anatomy. It was also said: They are metaphors for seven reasons for which the glutton eats: He eats out of need, report, smell, sight, touch, and taste, and he increases his self-sufficiency. It was also said: The meaning is that he eats like someone who has seven intestines. The believer, with his light eating, eats like someone who has only one intestine, so he shares with the unbeliever a part of his food, and the unbeliever exceeds him by seven times. The intestine in this hadith is the stomach. Sixth: If this is established, then know that it is recommended for a person to wash his hands before and after eating, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Ablution before and after eating is a blessing. And so it is in the Torah. It was narrated by Zadan on the authority of Salman. Malik disliked washing clean hands. Following the hadith is better. He should not eat food until he knows whether it is hot or cold? Because if it is hot, he may be harmed. It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Cool your food, for hot food is not blessed. This is an authentic hadith. It was mentioned earlier in Al-Baqarah. He should not smell it, for that is the work of animals. Rather, if he likes it, he should eat it, and if he dislikes it, he should leave it. He should make the bite small and chew it frequently so that it is not considered evil. He should mention God at the beginning and praise Him at the end. He should not raise his voice in praise unless his companions have finished eating, because raising the voice prevents them from eating. There are many etiquettes for eating, this is a summary of them. Some of them will come in Surah Hud, God willing. There are also well-known etiquettes for drinking, which we have not mentioned because they are well-known. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Umar, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you eats, let him eat with his right hand, and if he drinks, let him drink with his right hand, for Satan eats with his left hand and drinks with his left hand. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: And do not be excessive meaning in eating a lot, and from this it means drinking a lot, and that weighs down the stomach, and discourages a person from serving his Lord, and taking his share of the voluntary good deeds. If he goes beyond that to what is above that which prevents him from fulfilling what is obligatory upon him, then it is forbidden for him, and he has been excessive in his food and drink. Asad bin Musa narrated from the hadith of “Awn bin Abi Juhaifa from his father who said: I ate a stew with fatty meat, and I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while I was belching. He said: “Stop your belching, Abu Juhaifa, for the people who are most satiated in this world will be the hungriest on the Day of Resurrection.” Abu Juhaifa did not eat to his full stomach until he departed this world. When he ate lunch, he did not eat dinner, and when he ate dinner, he did not eat lunch. I said: This may be the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: The believer eats with one intestine, meaning the one with complete faith, because the one who is a good Muslim and whose faith is complete, like Abu Juhayfah, thinks about what will happen to him regarding death and what comes after it, so fear and compassion for those horrors prevent him from fulfilling his desires. And God knows best. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning of and do not be extravagant is that you do not eat what is forbidden. It was also said: It is extravagance to eat whatever you desire. Narrated by Anas ibn Malik from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and included by Ibn Majah in his Sunan. It has also been said that it is extravagance to eat after being full. This is also forbidden. Luqman said to his son: O my son, do not eat full on top of full, for it is better to give it to a dog than to eat it. Samurah ibn Jundub asked about his son, what did he do? They said: He smelled it last night. He said: He smelled it! They said: Yes. He said: If he had died, I would not have prayed over him. It has been said: The Arabs in the pre-Islamic era did not eat fatty foods during their pilgrimage, and were content with a small amount of food, and they would go around naked. So it was said to them: Take your adornments at every mosque, and eat and drink, but do not be extravagant, meaning do not be extravagant in forbidding what has not been forbidden to you.
7:32: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God?” He explained that they forbade of their own accord what God had not forbidden them. Adornment here is good clothing, if its owner is able to afford it. It was said: All clothing, as narrated from Omar: If God is generous to you, then be generous. It was mentioned earlier. It was narrated from Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Ali bin Abi Talib, the sheikh of Malik, may God be pleased with them, that he used to wear a silk cloak worth fifty dinars, which he would wear in the winter, and if it was summer he would give it in charity, or sell it and give its price in charity. In the summer he would wear two Egyptian garments with stripes on them and say: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?” Second: If this is the case, then the verse indicates wearing fine clothes and adorning oneself with them on Fridays and holidays, and when meeting people and visiting brothers. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: When Muslims visited each other, they adorned themselves. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated from Umar ibn Al-Khattab that he saw a silken garment being sold at the door of the mosque, so he said: O Messenger of God, why don’t you buy it for Friday and for the delegations when they come to you? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Only he who has no share in the Hereafter wears this. He did not object to him mentioning beautification, but he objected to him being a garment. Tamim al-Dari bought a robe for a thousand dirhams in which he prayed. Malik ibn Dinar used to wear fine Adeni clothes. Ahmad ibn Hanbal's robe was bought for about a dinar. Where is this from someone who dislikes it and prefers coarse linen and woolen clothes, and says: The clothing of piety is better, far from it! Do you think that those we mentioned abandoned the clothing of piety? No, by God! Rather, they are the people of piety and the possessors of knowledge and reason, and others are people of claims, and their hearts are empty of piety. Khalid ibn Shu'dhab said: I witnessed al-Hasan and Farqad came to him, so al-Hasan took hold of his cloak and extended it to him and said: O Farqad, O son of Umm Farqad, righteousness is not in this cloak, rather righteousness is what is firmly established in the heart and confirmed by action. Abu Muhammad, the nephew of Maruf al-Karkhi, entered upon Abu al-Hasan ibn Yasar wearing a woolen cloak, so Abu al-Hasan said to him: O Abu Muhammad, have you softened your heart or have you softened it? Your body? Wool your heart and wear coffee on coffee. A man said to Al-Shabli: A group of your friends have arrived and they are in the mosque. He went and saw them wearing patched clothes and towels, so he began to say: As for the tents, they are like their tents, and I see that the women of the neighborhood are not like his women. Abu al-Faraj ibn al-Jawzi may God have mercy on him said: I dislike wearing patched clothes and cloaks for four reasons: First, it is not the dress of the Salaf, but they used to patch it out of necessity. Second, it implies a claim of poverty, and man has been commanded to show the effect of God’s blessings upon him. Third, it shows asceticism, and we have been commanded to cover it. Fourth, it is an imitation of those who deviate from the Shariah. Whoever imitates a people is one of them. At-Tabari said: He has certainly made a mistake who prefers to wear hair and wool over cotton and linen, even though there is a way to do so through its permissibility. He who eats beans and lentils and chooses them over wheat bread. He who refrains from eating meat for fear of the temptation of women has sinned. Bishr ibn al-Harith was asked about wearing wool, and he was upset with him and the dislike was clear on his face. Then he said: Wearing silk and saffron is more beloved to me than wearing wool in the cities. Abu al-Faraj said: The early Muslims used to wear average clothes, neither high nor low, and they would choose the best of them for Friday prayers, Eid prayers, and for meeting brothers. Choosing the best of them was not considered ugly by them. As for clothing that disgraces its wearer, it includes showing asceticism and showing poverty, and it is as if it is a tongue of complaint to God Almighty, and it requires the wearer to be despised, and all of that is disliked and forbidden. If someone says: Impeccable clothing is a desire of the soul, and we have been commanded to struggle against it, and adorning oneself for people, and we have been commanded that our actions should be for God, not for people. The answer is that not everything that the soul desires is blameworthy, and not everything that one adorns oneself with for people is disliked. Rather, it is forbidden if the Shariah has forbidden it or for the sake of showing off in matters of religion. A person should be seen as beautiful. That is a share of the soul, and he should not be blamed for it. For this reason, he combs his hair, looks in the mirror, straightens his turban, and wears the rough lining of his garment on the inside and its beautiful outer layer on the outside. There is nothing in any of this that is disliked or blameworthy. Makhul narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: A group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were waiting for him at the door. He went out to meet them, and in the house there was a bowl of water. He began to look into the water and smooth his beard and hair. So I said: O Messenger of God, and you do that? He said: Yes, if a man goes out to his brothers, let him prepare himself, for God is beautiful and loves beauty. And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Ibn Masoud, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: He who has an atom’s weight of arrogance in his heart will not enter Paradise. A man said: A man likes his clothes to be nice and his shoes to be nice. He said: God is beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people. There are many hadiths with this meaning, all of which indicate cleanliness and good appearance. Muhammad ibn Sa’d narrated: Al-Fadl ibn Dukayn told us: Mandal told us, on the authority of Thawr, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to travel with a comb, a mirror, oil, a tooth stick, and kohl.” Ibn Jurayj narrated: An ivory comb with which he combed his hair. Ibn Sa’d said: Qubaysah ibn Uqbah told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Rabi’ ibn Subayh, on the authority of Yazid al-Ruqashi, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to oil his head a lot and comb his beard with water.” Yazid bin Harun told us, Ibad bin Mansour told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a kohl container with which he would apply kohl three times in each eye before going to sleep. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And the good things of provision. Good things are a general name for what is good to earn and eat. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: What is meant by good things of provision are what the people of ignorance were forbidden from, such as bahā’ir, sawa’ib, wasā’il, and hawāmi. It was said: It is every delicious food. There is a difference of opinion regarding abandoning good things and turning away from pleasures. Some people said: This is not an act of worship, and doing and abstaining from it are the same in permissible things. Others said: It is not an act of worship in itself, but rather it is a path to asceticism in this world, shortening one’s hope in it, and abandoning effort for its sake. This is recommended, and what is recommended is an act of worship. Others said: It was narrated from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb may God be pleased with him that he said: If we wanted, we could have taken salā’, salā’iq, and sanāb, but I heard God the Almighty criticize some people, saying: You have used up your good things in your worldly life. (al-Ahqaf 46:20). It is also narrated as sāriq with a ra’, and they are both jirdaq. Sala’iq with a lam is what sticks together from meat and vegetables. Sala with a broken sad and a long mad: barbecue. Sanab: mustard with raisins. Others differentiated between attending all of that with or without expense. Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn al-Mufaddal al-Maqdisi, the sheikh of our sheikhs, said: This is correct, God willing, because it was not reported that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, abstained from any food because of its taste. Rather, he used to eat sweets, honey, watermelon, and dates. He only disliked the expense because it distracted him from the important matters of the afterlife with worldly desires. And God knows best. I said: Some Sufis disliked eating good things, and cited as evidence the saying of Omar may God be pleased with him: Beware of meat, for it is as harmful as wine. The answer is that this is a saying of Omar that was issued against those who feared that it would lead to preferring worldly pleasures, persisting in desires, curing the soul of pleasures, forgetting the Hereafter and turning to worldly things. Therefore, Omar used to write to his workers: Beware of luxury and the dress of the Persians, and be rough. He may God be pleased with him did not intend to forbid something that God had permitted, nor to prohibit what God, the Blessed and Exalted, had permitted. The saying of God, the Almighty, is more deserving of compliance and reliance. God, the Almighty, said: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?” And he (peace be upon him) said: The best condiment of this world and the hereafter is meat. Hisham bin Urwa narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to eat cooked meat with dates and say: The heat of this breaks the cold of this and the cold of this breaks the heat of this. Cooking is a language for watermelon, and it is from the reversed. The response to those who prefer to eat rough food has already passed in Al-Ma’idah. This verse responds to him and others: Praise be to God. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: It is for those who believe in the life of this world.” He means by its right to the oneness of God Almighty and belief in Him, for God bestows blessings and provides, so if the one bestowed blessings monotheism and believes in Him, then he has fulfilled the right of the blessing, and if he disbelieves, then Satan has been given power over himself. And in the authentic hadith: “No one is more patient with harm than God. He heals them and provides for them while they call upon Him for a wife and a child.” The discussion continued with regard to worldly life. Then he said, Pure in the nominative case, which is the reading of Ibn Abbas and Nafi’. Pure on the Day of Resurrection means that God will purely give the good things in the Hereafter to those who believe, and the polytheists will not have any of them, just as they had in this world of sharing them. The metaphor of the verse is: Say, They are for those who believe, shared in this world with others, and they are pure for the believers on the Day of Resurrection. So, Pure is a new sentence based on an implied subject. This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, As-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd. It was said that the meaning is that these good things that exist in this world are pure on the Day of Resurrection, for the believers in this world, and their purity is that they will not be punished for them or tormented, so he said, in this worldly life is related to believed. This is what Saeed bin Jubair’s interpretation refers to. The rest read it in the accusative case, as a state and separation, because the speech was completed without it. It is not permissible to stop at this reading on the world, because what follows it is related to His statement: for those who believe, as a state of it, with the estimation of Say: It is fixed for those who believe in the worldly life in the state of its purity for them on the Day of Resurrection, said Abu Ali. And the predicate of the beginning is for those who believe. And the factor in the state is what is in the lam of the meaning of the verb in His statement: for those, and Sibawayh chose the accusative because of the precedence of the circumstance. Thus do We detail the verses meaning, just as I have detailed for you the lawful and the unlawful, I will detail for you what you need.
7:33: There is one issue: Al-Kalbi said: When the Muslims put on their clothes and circumambulated the House, the polytheists mocked them, so this verse was revealed. And the obscenities are the extremely ugly actions, what is apparent of them and what is hidden. Ruh ibn Abbad narrated on the authority of Zakariya ibn Ishaq on the authority of Abu Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, who said: What is apparent of them is the marriage of mothers in the pre-Islamic era, and what is hidden is adultery. Qatada said: Its secret and its public. This is questionable, because he mentioned sin and transgression, which indicates that what is meant by the obscenities is some of them. If that is the case, then the apparent obscenities are adultery. And God knows best. Al-Hasan said: And the sin means wine. The poet said: I drank sin until my mind went astray, so sin takes away the mind Another said: We drink sin openly, and you see musk borrowed among us. And transgression is injustice and exceeding the limit in it. It was mentioned before.
