Tha'lab said: Transgression is when a man attacks another man and speaks about him, and transgresses against him unjustly, unless he takes revenge on him with justice. He excluded sin and transgression from the indecencies and they are from it because of their greatness and indecency, so he mentioned them explicitly to emphasize their matter and with the intention of deterring from them. And likewise and that you associate and and that you say and they are in the accusative case in apposition to what came before. A group denied that sin means wine. Al-Farra' said that sin is less than the limit and transgression against people. Al-Nahhas said: As for sin being wine, this is not known, and the reality of sin is all sins, as the poet said: I found the matter to be guided by the fear of God and its evil is sin. I said: Ibn al-Arabi also denied it and said: There is no proof in the verse, because if he had said: I drank the sin or I drank the burden, it would have been like that, and his statement did not require that sin and burden be names of wine, just as sin is. What required speaking with such ignorance of the language and the path of evidence in meanings. I said: We mentioned it on the authority of Al-Hasan. Al-Jawhari said in Al-Sahah: Wine is sometimes called a sin, and he recited: I drank the sin....home Al-Harawi recited it in his two Gharibs, that wine is a sin. So it is not far-fetched that sin applies to all transgressions and to wine as well in language, so there is no contradiction. And transgression: exceeding in injustice, and it was said: corruption.
7:34: There is one issue: God the Almighty says: And for every nation is a term meaning a specific time. So when their term has come meaning the time known to God the Almighty. Ibn Sirin read their terms have come in the plural. They will not delay it by an hour or less than an hour, except that the hour was mentioned specifically because it is the shortest of all names for times, and it is a time adverb. Nor will they advance This indicates that the one who is killed will be killed at his appointed time. The appointed time for death is the time of death, just as the appointed time for a debt is the time of its due date. Everything that has a set time for something has a set term for it. The appointed time for a person is the time when God knows that the living person will inevitably die. It is a time that it is not permissible to delay his death from, not because it is not possible to delay it. Many of the Mu'tazila, except for those who deviated from them, said: The one who was killed died at a time other than the appointed time that was set for him, and that if he had not been killed, he would have come back to life. This is wrong, because the one who was killed did not die because someone else killed him, but because of what God did in taking his life when He set it for him. If it is said: If he died at his appointed time, why do you kill his assailant and take retaliation from him? It was said to him: We kill him for his transgression and his actions in matters he had no right to, not for his death and the death of his soul, as that was not his doing. If people were left to transgress without retaliation, that would lead to corruption and the destruction of the servants. This is clear.
7:35: The Almighty said: O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among you is a condition. The letter nun was added to emphasize the introduction of ma. It was said: ma is a connection, meaning if there comes to you. He informed that He will send messengers from among them to them so that their response will be closer. Stories are the following of one speech to another. My verses means My obligations and My rulings. So whoever fears God and amends is a condition, and what follows it is its answer, which is the answer to the first. That is, whoever among you amends what is between Me and him. There will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve. This is evidence that the believers on the Day of Resurrection will neither fear nor grieve, nor will terror or panic overtake them. It has been said that the terrors of the Day of Resurrection may overtake them, but their final destination will be security. It has been said that the answer to If there comes to you is what the words indicate, that is, obey them. So whoever fears God and amends The first statement is the statement of Al-Zajjaj.
7:36: God Almighty says: And those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
7:37: God the Almighty says: So who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God or denies His signs? The meaning is any injustice more heinous than inventing a lie against God the Almighty and denying His signs. Then He said: Those will receive their share of the Book meaning what was written for them of provision, life span, and deeds, according to Ibn Zayd. Ibn Jubayr: of misery and happiness. Ibn Abbas: of good and evil. Al-Hasan and Abu Salih: of punishment according to their disbelief. Al-Tabari chose the meaning to be: what was written for them, meaning what was destined for them of good and evil, provision, deeds, and life span, according to what was mentioned previously from Ibn Zayd, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Jubayr. He said: Do you not see that he followed that with his saying: Until when Our messengers come to them, they take their souls meaning the messengers of the Angel of Death. It was said: The Book here is the Qur'an, because the punishment of the disbelievers is mentioned in it. It was also said: The Book is the Preserved Tablet. Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Halwani said: Ali bin Al-Madini dictated to me: I asked Abdul Rahman bin Mahdi about destiny, and he said to me: Everything is by destiny, and obedience and disobedience are by destiny, and the one who said: Disobedience is not by destiny has greatly slandered me. Ali said: Abdul Rahman bin Mahdi said to me: Knowledge, destiny, and the Book are the same. Then I presented the words of Abdul Rahman bin Mahdi to Yahya bin Saeed, and he said: There is nothing left after this, little or much. Yahya bin Ma’in narrated: Marwan Al-Fazari narrated to us: Ismail bin Sami’ narrated to us, from Bakir Al-Tawil, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas: Those will receive their share of the Book. He said: People who do deeds that they must do. And until is not an end, rather it is the beginning of a report about them. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: Until, or, and not to be inflected because they are letters, so they are distinguished from nouns, such as pregnant and drunk. Al-Zajjaj said: It is written until with a ya’ because it resembles drunk, and if it was written alla with a ya’, it would resemble ila. And it is not written Ima with a ya’ because if it is added to it, what. “They said: Where are those you used to call upon besides God?” It is a question of rebuke. The meaning of you call is you worship. “They said, ‘They have gone astray from us,’” meaning they have become useless and gone. It was said that this will happen in the afterlife. And they testified against themselves that they were disbelievers, meaning they admitted to disbelief against themselves.
7:38: The Almighty said: "He said, 'Enter among nations that have passed on before you of jinn and mankind in the Fire.'" That is, with nations, so fi means with. This is not impossible, because when you say: Zaid is in the people, that is, with the people. It was also said: It is in its proper form. That is, enter among them. And the speaker, it was said: It is God, the Almighty, that is, God said, 'Enter.' It was also said: It is Malik, the keeper of the Fire. "Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister," that is, the one who preceded it to the Fire, and she is its sister in religion and faith. "Until, when they all overtake therein," that is, they gather. Al-A'mash read tadārakū, which is the original, then assimilation occurred, so an alif of connection was needed. Al-Mahdawi narrated it from Ibn Mas'ud. Al-Nahhas said: Ibn Mas'ud read Ḍattā idhārakū, that is, some of them overtook each other. And Asmah from Abu Amr Ḍattā idhā idhārakū, by proving the alif to combine two quiescent letters. And he narrated: These two are servants of God. And he gets two-thirds of the money. And on the authority of Abu Amr also: If they catch up, cut off the alif of connection, as if he paused on if to remember, then when his pause was prolonged, cut off the alif of connection as if starting with it. And in poetry, cutting off the alif of connection has come, such as his saying: O soul, be patient, for every living thing will meet another, and every two will have to part. On the authority of Mujahid and Hamid bin Qais, until when they overtook, with the deletion of the alif if due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the deletion of the alif after the dal. All of them are in the accusative case in the state. The last of them said to the first of them, meaning the last of them to enter, and they are the followers, to the first of them, and they are the leaders. Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment in the Fire. The lam in the first of them is a lam of precedence, because they did not address the first of them, but they said regarding the first of them, Our Lord, these led us astray. Weakness is the like that is added to its like once or times. On the authority of Ibn Masoud, the weakness here is snakes and serpents. The equivalent of this verse is Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse. (al-Ahzab 33:68). There, the mention of weakness will come in a more complete manner than this and the rulings that result from it, God willing. He said to each double, meaning to the follower and the one being led. But they do not know according to the reading of those who read with the letter ya, meaning that neither group knows what is in the other group, because if some of those in the fire knew that the punishment of one of them was greater than his punishment, it would be a kind of consolation for them. It was said that the meaning is but you do not know with the letter ta, meaning but you do not know, O those addressed, what punishment they are experiencing. It is possible that the meaning is but you do not know, O people of this world, the extent of the punishment they are in.
7:39: And the first of them will say to the last of them, 'You had no superiority over us.' That is, you disbelieved and did as we did, so you do not deserve a reduction in the punishment. So taste the punishment for what you used to earn.
7:40: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who deny Our signs and are arrogant toward them - the gates of heaven will not be opened for them meaning for their souls. This is mentioned in authentic hadiths that we mentioned in the Book of Remembrance. Among them is the hadith of Al-Bara' bin Azib, in which he said about the taking of the soul of the disbeliever: And there comes out of it a stench like the foulest of a corpse found on the face of the earth. They ascend with it and do not pass by a group of angels except that they say: What is this evil spirit? They say: So-and-so, son of so-and-so, using the worst names he was called by in the world, until they reach the lowest heaven and ask permission but it is not opened for them. Then the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited: The gates of heaven will not be opened for them (al-Baqarah 2:17). It was said: The gates of heaven will not be opened for them if they call upon God, as Mujahid and al-Nakha’i said. It was also said: The meaning is that the gates of Paradise will not be opened for them because Paradise is in the heaven. This is indicated by His statement: And they will not enter Paradise until a camel passes through the eye of a needle. And the camel passes through, so they will not enter it at all. This is conclusive evidence that it is not permissible to forgive them. And on this the Muslims, who are not allowed to make mistakes, are unanimously agreed that God, the Most High, will not forgive them or any of them. Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Tayyib said: If someone were to say: How can this be a consensus of the Ummah? Some theologians have claimed that those who imitate Jews, Christians, and other infidels are not in Hell. It was said to him: These are people who denied that the imitator is an infidel due to a doubt that entered them, and they did not claim that the imitator is an infidel and that he is not in Hell. The way to know whether the imitator is an infidel or not is through observation, not through revelation and report. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with a fathah with a dammah on the ya’ as a masculine plural. The rest read it with a ta’ as a feminine plural, as he said: The doors are opened for them [p. 50], so he made it feminine. Since the femininity in the doors is not real, it is permissible to make the masculine plural. This is the reading of Ibn Abbas with a ya’. Abu Amr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i made it light, meaning that lightening is for little and much, and emphasis is for much and repetition time after time and nothing else, and emphasis here is more appropriate because it is more indicative of much. And the camel is from the camels. Al-Farra’ said: The camel is the husband of the female camel. And Abdullah bin Masoud said the same when he was asked about the camel, he said: It is the female camel's mate, as if he was ignorant of the one who asked him about what all people know. The plural is Jamal, Ajmal, Jamalat, and Jama'il. It is only called a camel if it has four. And in Abdullah's reading: Until the yellow camel passes through the eye of a needle. Abu Bakr al-Anbari mentioned it, my father told us, Nasr bin Dawud told us, Abu Ubaid told us, Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Kathir, on the authority of Mujahid, he said in Abdullah's reading..., and he mentioned it. And Ibn Abbas read the camel with a damma on the jim and a fatha on the mim and a shaddah on it. It is the ship's rope which is called al-Qals, and it is ropes gathered together, the plural of Jamla, said Ahmad bin Yahya Tha'lab. And it was said: The thick rope of hemp. And it was said: The rope that is used to climb palm trees. And it was also narrated from him and from Saeed bin Jubair: The camel with a damma on the jim and a light mim is also al-Qals and the rope, as we mentioned earlier. And it was also narrated from him: al-Jamal with two dhammahs, the plural of Jamal, like Asad and Asad, and al-Jamal is like Asad and Asad. On the authority of Abu al-Samal al-Jamal with the opening of the jim and the sukoon of the mim, and the lightening of jaml. The piercing of the tailor: the eye of the needle, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and others. Every small hole in the body is called poison and poison, and the plural is poisons. The plural of deadly poison is poison. Ibn Sirin read in sam with the damma of the seen. The tailor: that which is sewn with, it is said: a tailor and a tailor, like an izar and a mi’zar and a qana’ and a muqanna’.
7:41: Al-Mahad: the mattress. Ghawash is the plural of Ghashia, meaning fires that cover them. And thus do We recompense the wrongdoers meaning the disbelievers. And God knows best.
7:42: The Almighty's statement: We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity is an interjection. That is, those who believe and do righteous deeds - those are the companions of Paradise, where they will abide eternally. The meaning of We do not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity is that He did not charge anyone with regard to the expenses of his wives except what he found and was able to do, not what he could not reach. He did not intend to prove the ability before the action, as Ibn al-Tayyib said. Similar to it is God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity (al-Talaq 65:7).
7:43: God the Almighty mentioned among the blessings He will bestow upon the people of Paradise, removing rancor from their hearts. Removal means extraction. Rancor is the hidden hatred in the chest. The plural is ghalal. That is, We will remove in Paradise whatever rancor was in their hearts in this world. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Reverence at the gates of Paradise is like the resentment of a camel. God has removed it from the hearts of the believers.” It was narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him that he said: I hope that I, Uthman, Talhah, and Az-Zubayr will be among those about whom God the Almighty said: And We will remove whatever is in their hearts of resentment. It was said: Removing resentment in Paradise means that they will not envy each other for the superiority of their status. It was said that this is because of the drink of Paradise, and for this reason He said: And their Lord will give them a pure drink (al-Insan 76:21) meaning He will cleanse the impurities from their hearts, as will be explained in Surat Al-Insan and Surat Az-Zumar, God willing. And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, Who has guided us to this’ meaning to this reward, by guiding us and creating guidance for us. This is a refutation of the Qadarites. And we would not have been is the reading of Ibn Amir by dropping the waw. The rest confirm it. We would not have been guided is the lam of ki. Had God not guided us is in the nominative case. And they were called is its original form. They were called "that in the accusative case, lightened from the heavy one, meaning that that is Paradise." It may be an explanation of what they were called to, because the call is a statement, so it has no place. That is, it was said to them: That is Paradise because they were promised it in this world, that is, it was said to them: This is that Paradise that you were promised, or it was said to them before entering when they saw it from a later time. It was said: That is in the meaning of this. The meaning of "you inherited it because of what you used to do" is that you inherited its dwellings because of your deeds, and your entry into it is by the mercy and grace of God. As He said, "That is the grace from God" (An-Nisa': 70) and He said, "Then He will admit them to mercy from Him and grace" (An-Nisa': 175). And in Sahih Muslim: None of you will enter Paradise because of his deeds. They said: Not even you, O Messenger of God? He said: Not even me, unless God covers me with His mercy and grace. In other than Sahih Muslim: “There is no disbeliever or believer but that he has a home in Paradise and Hell. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, Paradise will be raised up for the people of Hell so that they may look at their homes therein. It will be said to them: These are your homes if you had acted in obedience to God. Then it will be said: O people of Paradise, lament them for what you used to do. Then their homes will be divided among the people of Paradise.” I said: In Sahih Muslim: No Muslim man dies except that God places in his place a Jew or a Christian in the Fire. This is also an inheritance. He grants by His grace whomever He wills and punishes by His justice whomever He wills. In short, Paradise and its dwellings are not attained except by His mercy. So if they enter it through their deeds, then they have inherited it by His mercy, and they have entered it by His mercy, since their deeds are a mercy from Him to them and a favor to them. It is read awrathutumuha without assimilation. It is read by assimilation of the ta’ into the tha’.
7:44: The Almighty said: And the companions of Paradise will call out This is a question of reproach and reproach. That we have found is like that that is Paradise, meaning that we have found. It was said: It is the same call. Then a crier will announce among them meaning he will announce and make a voice, meaning from the angels. Between them is a circumstance, as you say: I know their midst. Al-Kisa'i and Na'am read it with a kasra on the 'ayn. It is permissible in this language to make the 'ayn sukun. Makki said: Whoever says Na'am with a kasra on the 'ayn wanted to differentiate between Na'am which is a response and Na'am which is a name for camels, cows and sheep. It was narrated from Omar that he denied Na'am by opening the 'ayn in the response, and he said: Say Na'am. Na'am and Na'am are two languages that mean the number and confirmation. The number is when you ask about an affirmative, such as when you say: Is Zaid standing? He will say: Yes. And confirmation is when you tell about what happened, you say: Such and such happened, he will say: Yes. So when you ask about something negated, the answer is yes, such as when you say: Did I not honor you? He will say: Yes. Yes, for the answer to the question that comes after the affirmative as in this verse. And yes, for the answer to the question that comes after the negation, as God the Almighty said: Am I not your Lord? They said: Yes. (al-A’raf 7:172) Al-Bazzi, Ibn ‘Amir, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read that the curse of God is the original. The rest read it with a light an and raising the la’natullah as a subject. An is in the accusative case in both readings by dropping the preposition. It is permissible for the lightened an to not have a syntactic position. It is explanatory as mentioned above. It was narrated from Al-A’mash that he read in the curse of God with a kasrah on the hamzah, so this is based on the implication of the statement as the Kufians read The angels called out to him while he was standing praying in the prayer niche that God It is narrated that Tawus entered upon Hisham ibn ‘Abd al-Malik and said to him: Fear God and beware of the Day of the Call to Prayer. He said: What is the Day of the Call to Prayer? He said: The Almighty’s saying: “Then a crier proclaimed among them: ‘The curse of God is upon the wrongdoers.’” So Hisham was struck dumb. Tawus said: This is the humiliation of description, so how about the humiliation of witnessing?
7:45: The Almighty's saying: Those who hinder [people] from the way of God is in the accusative case for the wrongdoers as an attribute. It is permissible to raise or lower the subject with the omission of them or I mean. That is, those who used to hinder people from Islam in this world. It is from the word sadd which means prevention. Or they themselves hinder from the way of God, that is, they turn away. This is from the word sudud. And they seek to make it crooked they seek to make it crooked and they criticize it so they do not believe in it. This meaning has already passed. And they are disbelievers in the Hereafter that is, and they were disbelievers in it. So it was omitted, and this is common in speech.
7:46: The Almighty said: And between them is a veil meaning between the Fire and Paradise - because they were mentioned - a barrier, meaning a wall. It is the wall that God mentioned in His statement: And He will set up between them a wall (al-Hadid 57:13). And on the heights are men meaning on the heights of the wall, which is its upper part. From this comes the mane of a horse and the mane of a rooster. Abdullah bin Abi Yazid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Al-A'raf is a high place. Mujahid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Al-A'raf is a wall with a mane like a rooster's mane. Al-A'raf in the language means a high place, the plural of 'arf. Yahya bin Adam said: I asked Al-Kisa'i about the singular of Al-A'raf and he remained silent, so I said: Israel narrated to us on the authority of Jabir on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Al-A'raf is a wall with a mane like a rooster's mane. He said: Yes, by God, its singular means, and its plural is A'raf, boy, bring the paper, so he wrote it. This statement was made as a compliment, as he said about it: Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God (al-Nur 24:37). The scholars have spoken about the people of Al-A’raf in ten ways: Abdullah bin Masoud, Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman, Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Dahhak, and Ibn Jubayr said: They are people whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal. Ibn Atiyyah said: In the Musnad of Khaithama bin Sulayman at the end of the fifteenth volume there is a hadith on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the Day of Resurrection, the scales will be placed and the good deeds and bad deeds will be weighed. Whoever’s good deeds outweigh his bad deeds by the weight of a hump will enter Paradise, and whoever’s bad deeds outweigh his good deeds by the weight of a hump will enter Hell. It was said, ‘O Messenger of God, what about those whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal? ’ He said, ‘Those are the people of A’raf who will not enter it, and they will hope to do so. ’” Mujahid said: They are righteous, learned jurists. It was also said: They are the martyrs, as mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. Al-Qushayri said: “It was also said: “They are the virtuous believers and martyrs who have finished their own business and devoted themselves to studying the condition of the people. When they see the people of Hell, they will seek refuge in God from being sent back to Hell, for everything is in God’s power, and anything contrary to what is known is possible.” When they see the people of Paradise who have not yet entered it, they will hope to enter it. Shurahbil ibn Sa’d said: They are the martyrs in the cause of God who went out disobediently for the sake of their fathers. Al-Tabari mentioned a hadith on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this regard: And that their disobedience and their martyrdom are equal. Al-Tha’labi mentioned with his chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God Almighty: And on the heights are men, he said: Al-A’raf is a high place on the Sirat, on which are Al-Abbas, Hamza, Ali bin Abi Talib, and Ja’far Dhu al-Janahain, may God be pleased with them. They know their lovers by the whiteness of their faces and their haters by the blackness of their faces. Al-Zahrawi narrated that they are the just ones on the Day of Resurrection who testify against people about their deeds, and they are in every nation. Al-Nahhas chose this statement and said: It is one of the best things said about it, for they are on the wall between Paradise and Hell. Al-Zajjaj said: They are a people of prophets. It was also said: They are a people who had minor sins that were not expiated by pain and calamities in this world, and they did not have major sins, so they are prevented from Paradise so that they may be afflicted with grief that falls in return for their minor sins. Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, wished to be among the people of Al-A’raf, because his doctrine is that they are sinners. It was also said: They are the children of fornication, as Al-Qushayri mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said: They are angels assigned to this Surah, distinguishing the unbelievers from the believers before they enter Paradise and Hell. This was mentioned by Abu Majlaz. It was said to him: Angels are not called men? He said: They are males and not females, so it is not far-fetched to apply the word men to them - as it was applied to the jinn in His statement: And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn (al-Jinn 72:6). So these angels know the believers by their signs and the unbelievers by their signs, so they give good tidings to the believers before they enter Paradise, even though they have not yet entered it and so they hope for it. And when they see the people of Hell, they pray for themselves to be safe from punishment. Ibn Atiyyah said: What is necessary from the verse is that on Al-A’raf there are men from the people of Paradise whose entry is delayed and what was described of consideration occurs to them in both groups. And they know each by their mark meaning by their marks, which are the whiteness and beauty of the faces of the people of Paradise, and the blackness and ugliness of the faces of the people of Hell, in addition to other things of knowing the place of these and the place of those. I said: He stopped specifying because of the confusion of the trace and the details, and God is All-Knowing of the truths of matters. Then it was said: Al-A'raf is the plural of 'Araf, which is everything high and elevated, because by its appearance it is more known than the low. Ibn Abbas said: Al-A'raf is the honor of the path. And it was said: It is Mount Uhud, which is placed there. Ibn 'Atiyyah said: Al-Zahrawi mentioned a hadith that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, a mountain loves us and we love it. On the Day of Resurrection, it will be placed between Heaven and Hell. People will be detained before it, each of whom will be known by his features. They will be, God willing, among the people of Heaven.” He mentioned another hadith on the authority of Safwan bin Salim that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: One is on a corner of Paradise. I said: Abu Omar mentioned on the authority of Anas bin Malik that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A mountain loves us and we love it, and it is on a canal of the canals of Paradise. God the Almighty said: And the companions of Paradise will call out, meaning the companions of A’raf will call out to the companions of Paradise. “Peace be upon you,” meaning they will say to them, “Peace be upon you.” It was also said that the meaning is: You have been saved from punishment. They have not yet entered it, while they were hoping. That is, the companions of A’raf will not enter Paradise, meaning they have not yet entered it. And they are hoping, according to this interpretation, means they know that they will enter it. This is well-known in the language that hope means knowledge, as mentioned by An-Nahhas: This is the statement of Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, and others, that what is meant are the companions of A’raf. Abu Majlaz said: They are the people of Paradise, meaning the companions of A’raf will say to them, “Peace be upon you,” and the people of Paradise have not yet entered Paradise, while they are hoping to enter it, for the believers passing by the companions of A’raf. The pause is on the statement: Peace be upon you. And on the statement: They have not entered it. Then he begins, They are hoping, meaning they are hoping to enter it. It is permissible for that to be a state, and the meaning is: the believers passing by the companions of A’raf will not enter it hoping, but they entered it not hoping to enter it, so he does not pause on they have not entered it.
7:47: The Almighty said: And when their sight is turned toward the companions of the Fire meaning the direction of meeting, which is the direction of confrontation. The source of the word Tafa'al did not come except for two letters: Talaqa and Tabyan. The rest are with the fatha, such as Tasyaar, Tihamam and Tidhkar. As for the noun with the kasra, it is common, such as Taqsar and Mustathal. They said meaning the companions of Al-A'raf said. Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people they asked God not to place them with them, and they knew that He would not place them with them. This is by way of humility, as the people of Paradise say: Our Lord, perfect for us our light (al-Tahrim 66:8) and they say: Praise be to God by way of thanking God Almighty. And they will enjoy that.
7:48: God Almighty says: And the companions of the heights will call out to men whom they will recognize by their mark, meaning from the people of Hell. They will say, ‘Your multitude and your arrogance have not availed you.’ Meaning, for the world and their arrogance about faith.
7:49: Are these the ones referring to a group of poor believers, such as Bilal, Salman, Khabbab and others. You swore in this world. God will not reach them in the Hereafter. With mercy they are rebuked for that. And their grief and regret were increased by them being told Enter Paradise. Ikrimah read They entered Paradise without an alif and the dal is open. Talhah ibn Musarraf read They entered Paradise with a kasra on the kha as a past tense verb. The verse indicates that the people of A'raf are angels or prophets. Their statement is a report from God the Almighty and whoever made the people of A'raf the sinners, their last statement to the people of Hell will be, And you were not arrogant. And these are the ones who until the end of the verse from God the Almighty's statement to the people of Hell, rebuking them for what they said in this world. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and the first from Al-Hasan. It was said: It is from the speech of the angels assigned to the people of A'raf, for the people of Hell swear that the people of A'raf will enter Hell with them, so the angels will say to the people of A'raf, Enter Paradise, no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve.
7:50: The Almighty’s saying: And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, ‘Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you.’ There are three issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And he will call out It was said: When the people of A’raf reach Paradise, the people of Hell will be greedy and say: O our Lord, we have relatives in Paradise, so give us permission so that we may see them and speak to them. The people of Paradise will not recognize them because of the blackness of their faces, so they will say: Pour upon us some water or from whatever God has provided you. So it was made clear that the son of Adam cannot do without food and drink even if he is in torment. “They will say: God has forbidden them to the disbelievers.” Meaning the food and drink of Paradise. Pour out means expansion. It is said: He poured out His blessings upon him. Second: This verse is evidence that providing water is one of the best deeds. Ibn Abbas was asked: Which charity is best? He said: Water. Didn’t you see the people of Hell when they called out to the people of Paradise to pour out water on us or from what God has provided for you? Abu Dawud narrated that Sa`d came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Which charity do you like best? He said: Water. In another narration: So he dug a well and said: This is for Umm Saad. And on the authority of Anas, he said: Saad said: O Messenger of God, Umm Saad loved charity, would it benefit her if I gave charity on her behalf? He said: Yes, and you should give water. In another narration: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Saad bin Ubadah to provide water for her. This indicates that providing water is one of the greatest acts of worship to God. Some of the Tabi’un said: Whoever has many sins should provide water. God has forgiven the sins of the one who gave water to a dog, so how about the one who gave water to a believing monotheist and brought him back to life? Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: While a man was walking on a road, he became very thirsty. He went down to a well and drank from it. Then he came out and saw a dog eating dirt because of thirst. He said, This dog has become as thirsty as I have become. So he filled his shoe, held it in his mouth, climbed up and gave the dog water to drink. God thanked him for that and forgave him. They said, O Messenger of God, do we have a reward for treating animals? He said, There is a reward for treating animals with a moist liver. The opposite of this is what Muslim narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A woman was tortured because of a cat she imprisoned until it died, so she entered Hell because of it. She did not feed it or give it water when she imprisoned it, nor did she let it eat from the vermin of the earth. In the hadith of Aisha, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Whoever gives a Muslim a drink of water where there is water, it is as if he has freed a slave. Whoever gives a Muslim a drink of water where there is no water, it is as if he has saved his life.” Narrated by Ibn Majah in Sunan. Third: This verse was used as evidence by those who said: The owner of the pool and the water skin has more right to its water, and that he has the right to prevent it from whoever wants it, because the meaning of the words of the people of Paradise: God has forbidden them to the disbelievers is that you have no right to them. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, wrote a chapter on this meaning: (Chapter on whoever sees that the owner of the pool and the water skin has more right to its water) and he included in the chapter on the authority of Abu Hurayrah “on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, who said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I will drive away men from my pool just as a strange camel is driven away from a pool.” Al-Muhallab said: There is no dispute that the owner of the pool has more right to its water, because of his saying, peace be upon him: I will drive away men from my pool.
7:51: The Almighty said: Those who is in the accusative case as an attribute of the disbelievers. It may be in the nominative or accusative case with an implied pronoun. It was said: It is from the saying of the people of Paradise. So today We will forget them meaning We will leave them in the Fire. Just as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs meaning they abandoned working in it and denied it. Ma is a source, meaning We swept them away. And they did not deny Our signs is in apposition to it, meaning and their denial.
7:52: The Almighty said: And We have certainly brought them a Book meaning the Qur'an. We have explained it in detail meaning We have clarified it so that whoever ponders it will know it. It was also said: We have explained it means We revealed it in parts. With knowledge of guidance from Us, in which there was no oversight or mistake. Guidance and mercy Al-Zajjaj said: meaning a guide and one with mercy, so he made it a state of the ha in Fussalnahu. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible to say guidance and mercy, meaning it is guidance and mercy. It was also said: It is permissible to say guidance and mercy in the accusative case as a substitute for Book. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: It is permissible to say guidance and mercy in the accusative case as an attribute of Book. Al-Farra' said: And this is a blessed Book We have revealed (al-An’am 6:92 and 155). For a people who believe He specified the believers because they are the ones who benefit from it.
7:53: The Almighty said: Do they await anything but its interpretation? with a hamza, from al. The people of Medina lighten the hamza. Looking means waiting, meaning do they await anything but what they were promised in the Quran of punishment and accountability? It was said: They look from looking to the Day of Resurrection. So the metaphor in its interpretation refers to the Book. And the consequence of the Book is what God promised in it of resurrection and accountability. Mujahid said: Its interpretation is its recompense, meaning the recompense for their denial of the Book. Qatada said: Its interpretation is its consequence. The meanings are close. The Day its interpretation comes meaning its consequences will appear on the Day of Resurrection. And the Day is in the accusative case with says, meaning those who forgot it before will say the Day of its interpretation. The messengers of our Lord have come with the truth, so are there for us any intercessors? An interrogative with the meaning of a wish. So they will intercede is in the accusative case because it is the answer to the interrogative. For us or we are returned Al-Farra' said: The meaning is or are we returned. So we will do something other than what we were doing. Al-Zajjaj said: We will be returned is in apposition to the meaning, meaning will anyone intercede for us or will we be returned? Ibn Ishaq read or we will be returned, so we will do half of both. The meaning is unless we are returned, as he said: I told him, "Don't cry. We are trying to become king or die and be excused." Al-Hasan read, or we return and we work, raising both of them. They have lost themselves, meaning they did not benefit from them, and whoever does not benefit from himself has lost himself. It was said: they lost the blessings and their share of them. And what they used to invent has vanished from them, meaning what they used to say that there is another god with God has been invalidated.
7:54: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days indicates that He is the only One with the power of creation, so He is the One who must be worshipped. The root of six is six, so they wanted to assimilate the dal into the seen, but they met at the point of articulation of the ta' and it prevailed over them. If you wish, you can say: replace one of the two seens with a ta' and assimilate it into the dal, because you say in its diminutive form: sadisa, and in the plural asdas, and the plural and diminutive return the names to their origins. And they say: So-and-so came as-sadasa, sadata, and satata, so whoever says sadata replaces the seen with a ta'. And the day: from sunrise to sunset. If there is no sun, then there is no day, as Al-Qushayri said. He said: The meaning of in six days is from the days of the Hereafter, each day is a thousand years, to magnify the creation of the heavens and the earth. It was said: from the days of this world. Mujahid and others said: the first of them is Sunday and the last of them is Friday. He mentioned this period, and if He had wanted to create it in a moment, He would have done so, since He is able to say to it, Be, and it would be. But He wanted to teach His servants gentleness and deliberation in matters, and for His power to be revealed to the angels little by little. This is according to those who say: He created the angels before He created the heavens and the earth. Another wisdom is that He created it in six days because everything has a term with Him. And with this He showed that He did not hasten to punish the disobedient, because everything has a term with Him. This is like His saying: “And We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us. So be patient over what they say” (Qaf: 38-39). After He said: And how many generations before them have We destroyed who were mightier than they in strike. God the Almighty said: Then He rose over the Throne. This is the issue of ascension, and the scholars have spoken and conducted about it. We have explained the statements of the scholars about it in the book Al-Asna fi Sharh Asma God Al-Husna wa Attributihi Al-Ala, and we have mentioned fourteen statements about it there. Most of the early and later scholars are of the opinion that if it is necessary to transcend the Creator, glory be to Him, from direction and location, then it is a necessity and necessary consequence for most of the early scholars and their later leaders to transcend Him, glory be to Him, from direction. He is not in a direction above them, because that necessitates, according to them, when He is specific to a direction, that He be in a place or space, and movement and stillness, change and occurrence are required for the localized person, and for the place and space, movement and stillness, change and occurrence are required. This is the opinion of the theologians. The early predecessors, may God be pleased with them, did not deny direction nor did they speak about it. Rather, they and all spoke about affirming it for God the Almighty, as His Book spoke and His Messengers informed. None of the righteous predecessors denied that He rose over His Throne in reality. He made the Throne specific to it because it is the greatest of His creations, but they were ignorant of the manner of ascension, because its reality is not known. Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: Istiwaa is known - meaning in the language - but the manner is unknown, and asking about this is an innovation. Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, said the same. This amount is sufficient, and whoever wants more than that can refer to it in its place in the books of scholars. Istiwaa in the speech of the Arabs means elevation and stability. Al-Jawhari said: And he istiwaa from crookedness, and he istiwaa on the back of his mount, meaning he settled. And he istiwaa to the sky, meaning he intended. And he istiwaa means he took control and appeared. He said: Bashar has taken control of Iraq without sword or bloodshed. The man became straight, meaning his youth ended. And the thing became straight when it became balanced. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah regarding the Almighty’s saying: The Most Gracious established Himself firmly on the Throne (Ta-Ha 20:5), he said: He rose. And the poet said: So I brought them water in a deserted place, and the Yemeni star had risen and settled. That is, it rose and ascended. I said: The action and elevation of God Almighty is an expression of the elevation of His glory, attributes, and kingdom. That is, there is no one above Him in the meanings of majesty that are due to Him, nor is there anyone with Him who shares elevation with Him, but He is the Most High absolutely, glory be to Him. The Almighty’s saying: On the Throne is a common expression that refers to more than one person. Al-Jawhari and others said: The throne is the king’s bed. In the Qur’an: They denied her throne (al-Naml 27:41), And he raised his parents on the throne (Yusuf 12:100). The throne is the roof of the house. The throne of the foot: what protrudes from its back and contains the fingers. The throne of the fish: four small planets below the howling, it is said: they are the lion’s rump. The throne of the well: covering it with wood, after covering its bottom with stones to the extent of a stature, so that wood is the throne, and the plural is thrones. The throne is the name of Mecca. The throne is the king and the sultan. It is said: the throne of so-and-so is gone if his kingdom, sultanate, and glory are gone. Zuhair said: You have both caught up with Abs, whose throne has been shattered, and with Dhubyan, whose sandals have been humiliated by her feet. The throne in the verse may be interpreted to mean the kingdom, meaning that the kingdom is not established except for Him, the Almighty and Majestic. This is a good statement, but there is some consideration in it, and we have explained it in a group of statements in our book. Praise be to God. God the Almighty says: The night covers the day meaning it makes it like a veil, meaning the light of the day disappears so that the foundation of life in this world is completed with the coming of night. So the night is for stillness, and the day is for livelihood. It was read yaghshy with a shaddah, and the same is in ar-Ra'd. This is the reading of Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i. The rest read it lightly. They are two dialects: aghsha and ghashā. They agreed on fa-ghashāha ma ghashā (al-Najm 53:54) with a shaddah. They agreed on fa-aghshinahum (Ya-Sin 36:9), so the two readings are equal. In the shaddah there is a meaning of repetition and multiplication. And taghshyya and i-ghashā means to clothe something with something. The entry of day into night is not mentioned in this verse, so one of them is sufficient instead of the other, like garments that protect you from the heat (al-Nahl 16:81). In Your hand is all good (AAl Imran 3:26). Humayd ibn Qays read Yaghshy al-layl al-nahar meaning that the day covers the night He seeks it quickly meaning He seeks it constantly without slackening. Yaghshy al-layl al-nahar is in the accusative case as a state. The meaning is: He established Himself on the throne, covering the night with the day. And likewise Yaghshy al-layl is a state of the night, meaning He seeks the night with the day, seeking it. It is possible that the sentence is a resumption and not a state. Hastily is a substitute for the understood seeker or an attribute of it, or an attribute of a deleted source, meaning He seeks it quickly. Hast means to hasten and speed. And he turned away hastily means quickly. And the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Al-Akhfash said: It is conjoined with the heavens, meaning and the creation of the sun. It was narrated from Abdullah ibn Amir with the nominative in all of them as the beginning and the report. The Almighty’s saying: Is not His the creation and the command? There are two issues in this: First: God is truthful in His statement, for His is creation and His is the command. He created them and commanded them as He liked. This command requires prohibition. Ibn Uyaynah said: There is a difference between creation and command, so whoever combines them has disbelieved. So creation is the created, and command is His speech which is not created, which is His saying: Be. His command is only when He intends a thing that He says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. (Ya-Sin 36:82). And in His distinction between creation and command is clear evidence of the corruption of the statement of those who say that the Qur’an is created, for if His speech, which is a command, were created, He would have said: Is not creation and creation His? This is a defective, reprehensible and deserving of help in speech. God is exalted above speaking about what is useless. This is indicated by His statement, the Most High: And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. (al-Rum 30:25) And the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. So God, the Most High, informed us that the creatures stand by His command, for if the command were created, it would need another command to stand by it, and that command would need another command to infinity. This is impossible. It has been proven that His command, which is His speech, is ancient, eternal, and uncreated, so that it is correct for creatures to exist through it. This is also indicated by the words of God the Almighty: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except with truth (al-Hijr 15:85). God the Almighty informed us that He created them with truth, meaning the word, which is His saying to the created beings: Be. If the truth were created, it would not be correct for creatures to be created through it, because creation is not created by creation. This is indicated by And Our word has already gone forth for Our servants, the messengers (al-Saffat 37:171) Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it (Al-Anbiya’: 101) But the word from Me will come into effect (al-Sajdah 32:13). All of this is an indication of the precedence in speech in eternity, and that necessitates eternity in existence. This point is sufficient to refute them. They have verses that they use as evidence for their doctrine, such as the words of God the Almighty: And there comes to them no reminder from the Most Merciful, new (Al-Anbiya’: 2). And like the saying of God the Almighty: And the command of God was a decreed predestined (al-Ahzab 33:38). And acted (al-Ahzab 33:37) and what is like it. Judge Abu Bakr said: The meaning of Whatever comes to them of a reminder (Al-Anbiya’: 2) is any admonition, promise or threat from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except that they listen to it while they are playing because the admonition of the Messengers, may God bless them and grant them peace, and their warning is a reminder. God the Almighty said: So remind, for you are only a reminder (al-Ghashiyah 88:21). And it is said: So-and-so is in a gathering of remembrance. And the meaning of And the command of God was a decreed predestined is acted meaning that He, the Almighty, meant His punishment and vengeance against the disbelievers and His victory for the believers and what He ruled and decreed of His actions. And from that is the saying of God the Almighty: Until, when Our command came (Hud 11:40) and He the Almighty said: And Pharaoh’s command was not right (Hud 11:97) meaning by it his affair, actions and ways. The poet said: She has her own command, until when she has set her hooves on a pasture, she sets her own bed. Second: If this is established, then know that the command has nothing to do with the will. The Mu'tazila say: The command is the will itself. This is not correct, rather He commands what He does not will and forbids what He wills. Do you not see that He commanded Abraham to slaughter his son and did not want him to do so? And He commanded His Prophet to pray fifty prayers with his nation, and did not want him to do so except five prayers? And He wanted the martyrdom of Hamza when He says: And He takes from among you martyrs (Al Imran 3:140), and He forbade the infidels from killing him but did not command them to do so. This is correct and valuable in its regard, so ponder it. The Almighty said: Blessed be God, Lord of the worlds. Tabarak is a verb derived from barakah, which means abundance and vastness. It is said: something was blessed and blessed in it, as Ibn Arafa said. Al-Azhari said: He was blessed, exalted and exalted. It was also said that in His name one seeks blessings and good fortune. The meaning of Lord of the worlds has already been mentioned in Al-Fatihah.
7:55: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Call upon your Lord. This is a command to supplicate and worship Him. Then the Almighty, the Majestic, linked to the command qualities that are good with it, which are humility, submission, and supplication. The meaning of secretly is secretly in the soul to distance oneself from hypocrisy. Thus, He praised His Prophet Zachariah, peace be upon him, when He said, informing about him: When he called upon his Lord a secret call (Maryam 19:3). Similar to this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The best remembrance is that which is kept quiet, and the best provision is that which suffices. The Shariah has established that secretly reciting righteous deeds that are not interrupted is of greater reward than reciting them aloud. This meaning was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan said: We have known people who did not have any work on earth that they could keep secret, but it was always done aloud. The Muslims used to strive hard in supplication, but their voices were not heard, and it was nothing but whispers between them and their Lord. This is because God the Almighty says: Call upon your Lord in humility and in secret. He mentioned a righteous servant whose action was pleasing to Him, saying: When he called upon his Lord a call in secret (Maryam 19:3). The companions of Abu Hanifa used this as evidence that concealing Ameen is better than reciting it aloud, because it is a supplication. This was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Fatihah. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Musa that he said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey - and in another narration, during a military campaign - and the people began to recite the takbir aloud - and in another narration, every time a man climbed a hill he would say: There is no god but God - so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O people, be gentle with yourselves, for you are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent, but rather you are calling upon one who hears and is near, and He is with you.” The hadith. Second: The scholars differed regarding raising the hands in supplication. A group of them disliked it, including Jubayr ibn Mut’im, Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr. Shuraih saw a man raising his hands and said: Whoever supplicates with them, may you have no mother! Masruq said to some people who raised their hands: May God cut them off. They chose to point with their index fingers when supplicating to God in need. They would say: That is sincerity. Qatada would point with his finger and not raise his hands. Ata’, Tawus, Mujahid, and others disliked raising the hands. It was narrated that it is permissible to raise the hands from a group of the Companions and Followers. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as mentioned by al-Bukhari. Abu Musa al-Ash’ari said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, supplicated, then raised his hands and I saw the whiteness of his armpits. And the same was narrated by Anas. Ibn Umar said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands and said: O God, I disavow before You what Khalid did. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, he said: “When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at the polytheists, who were one thousand, and his companions were three hundred and nineteen men. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced the qiblah, stretching out his hands, and began to call out to his Lord,” and he mentioned the hadith. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on his authority that he said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, he would not lower them until he wiped his face with them.” He said: This is a strange, authentic hadith. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Salman, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Your Lord is living and generous. He is too shy for His servant to raise his hands to Him and return them empty, or he said, disappointed.” The first ones cited as evidence what Muslim narrated on the authority of Ammarah ibn Ruwaybah, who saw Bishr ibn Marwan on the pulpit raising his hands, so he said: May God make these two hands ugly. I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do nothing more than say with his hand like this, and he pointed with his index finger.” And as narrated by Saeed bin Abi Arubah on the authority of Qatada, “that Anas bin Malik told him: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not raise his hands in any supplication except when praying for rain, for he would raise them until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen. The first is more authentic and more proven than the hadith of Saeed bin Abi Arubah, for Saeed’s mind had changed towards the end of his life. Shu’bah disagreed with him in his narration on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Anas bin Malik, and he said about it: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would raise his hands until the whiteness of his armpits could be seen. It has been said that when a calamity befell the Muslims, raising them at that time was beautiful and good, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did when praying for rain and on the day of Badr. I said: Supplication is good, whatever is possible. It is what is required of a person to show his poverty and need for God, the Almighty, and to humble himself and submit to Him. If he wishes, he may face the Qiblah and raise his hands, that is good, but if he wishes, he may not. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did that, as mentioned in the hadiths. God, the Almighty, said: “Call upon your Lord in humility and in secret.” He did not mention a description of raising the hands or anything else. He said: Those who remember God, standing and sitting (Al Imran 3:191), so he praised them and did not stipulate a condition other than what was mentioned. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, supplicated in his Friday sermon while he was not facing the Qiblah. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, He does not love transgressors means in supplication, even though the wording is general, this is the indication. The transgressor is the one who transgresses the limit and commits the prohibition. He may be differentiated according to what he transgressed in. It was narrated “from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There will be people who transgress in supplication.” Narrated by Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah. Affan told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, Saeed al-Jariry told us “on the authority of Abu Naamah that Abdullah ibn Mughaffal heard his son say: O God, I ask You for the white palace on the right of Paradise when I enter it. He said: O my son, ask God for Paradise and protect him from the Fire, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There will be people who transgress in supplication. Transgression in supplication has many forms: including loud shouting and shouting, as mentioned above. It includes a person supplicating to have the status of a prophet, or supplicating in an impossible manner, and similar excesses. It includes supplicating seeking disobedience and other things. It includes supplicating with what is not in the Book and Sunnah, so he chooses impoverished expressions and rhyming words that he has found in notebooks that have no basis and cannot be relied upon, so he makes them his slogan and abandons what his Messenger, peace be upon him, supplicated with. All of this prevents the supplication from being answered, as was explained in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:56: The Almighty's saying: And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation contains one issue - that He, the Almighty, forbade all corruption, little or much, after its reformation, little or much. So it is general according to the correct sayings. Ad-Dahhak said: Its meaning is do not damage the flowing water, and do not cut down fruitful trees to cause harm. It has been reported: Cutting down dinars is corruption on the earth. It has been said: The trade of rulers is corruption on the earth. Al-Qushayri said: What is meant is do not associate partners, so it is a prohibition against association, bloodshed and chaos on the earth, and an order to adhere to the laws after their reformation, after God reformed it by sending the messengers, establishing the laws and making the religion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, clear. Ibn Atiyyah said: The one who said this statement intended the greatest corruption after the greatest reformation, so he mentioned it specifically. I said: As for what Ad-Dahhak mentioned, it is not general, but rather that is if it causes harm to the believer. As for what causes harm to the polytheists, that is permissible, for “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, damaged the water of the well of Badr and cut down the trees of the disbelievers.” And we will discuss cutting down dinars in Hud, God willing. And call upon Him in fear and hope. He commanded that man should be in a state of anticipation, fear, and hope for God Almighty, so that hope and fear are for man like the two wings of a bird, carrying him on the path of righteousness. If one of them is isolated, man will perish. God Almighty said: "Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful. And that it is My punishment that is the painful punishment." (al-Hijr 15:49-50). So hope and fear. Man calls upon Him out of fear of His punishment and hope for His reward. God Almighty said: And they call upon Us in hope and fear. (al-Anbiya 21:90). And we will discuss this later. Fear is the discomfort of what is not guaranteed from harm. Hope is the expectation of the beloved, as stated by Al-Qushayri. Some scholars said: Fear and hope should prevail throughout life, and when death comes, hope prevails. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let none of you die except while having good thoughts about God. Sahih narrated by Muslim. God the Almighty said: Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good. He did not say near. There are seven aspects to this: The first is that mercy and womb are one, and they mean forgiveness and pardon, as stated by Al-Zajjaj and chosen by Al-Nahhas. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Mercy is a verbal noun, and the right verbal noun to be masculine is masculine, like His statement: So whoever receives an admonition (al-Baqarah 2:275). This is close to what Al-Zajjaj said, because admonition means preaching. It was said: He meant by mercy goodness, and because what is not truly feminine can be made masculine, as stated by Al-Jawhari. It was said: He meant by mercy here rain, as stated by Al-Akhfash. He said: It is permissible to make it masculine as some feminine are made masculine. And he recited: There is no rain and its rain and its rain and its rain and its land is green and its greenery Abu Ubaidah said: The word qarib is mentioned as a masculine noun for place, meaning a close place. Ali bin Sulaiman said: This is a mistake. If it were as he said, qarib would be in the accusative case in the Qur’an, as you say: Verily Zayd is close to you. It was also said: It was mentioned as a relative noun, as if he said: Verily, the mercy of God is close, as you say: A divorced and menstruating woman. Al-Farra’ said: If qarib is used in the sense of distance, it is masculine and feminine, but if it is used in the sense of kinship, it is feminine, without any difference between them. You say: This woman is my relative, meaning she is my kin. Al-Jawhari mentioned this. Others mentioned from Al-Farra’: It is said in relation to kinship that so-and-so is close to us, and other than kinship, it is permissible to make it masculine or feminine. It is said: Your house is close to us, and So-and-so is close to us. God the Almighty said: And what do you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. (al-Ahzab 33:63) The one who provided evidence for him said: This is how the Arabs speak, as Imru’ al-Qais said: Woe to him if he spends the night without Umm Hashim near him or Basbasa, the daughter of Yashkur. Al-Zajjaj said: This is wrong, because the way for the masculine and feminine is to follow their actions.
7:57: The Almighty's saying: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy is in apposition to His saying: He covers the night with the day. He mentioned another of His blessings, and indicated His oneness and the proof of His divinity. The discussion of the wind has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Riyaah is the plural of much, and arwah is the plural of little. The root of rih is ruh. Those who say that the plural of little is arih made a mistake. Bishr has seven readings: The people of the two sanctuaries and Abu Amr read nashra with a damma on the nun and shin, the plural of nashir in the sense of kinship, meaning one who spreads, so it is like shahid and shahad. It is permissible for it to be the plural of nashur like rasool and rusul. It is said: the wind of the resurrection if it comes from here and there. And nashur means manshur, like rukub means the one who is ridden. That is, He is the One who sends the winds as a spreader. Al-Hasan and Qatadah read nashra with a damma on the nun and a sukoon on the shin, lightened from nashr, as one says katab and rusul. Al-A'mash and Hamzah read Nashr with a fatha on the noon and a sukoon on the sheen as a verbal noun, applying the meaning of what preceded it, as if he said: And He is the One Who spreads the winds Nashr. Nashr something was spread, so it was as if it was folded and then spread when it blew. It is permissible for it to be a verbal noun in the place of the state of the winds, as if he said He sends the winds spreading, meaning reviving, from Anshr God the dead, so he spread, just as you say he came to us running, meaning running. It has been said that Nashr (with a fatha) is from Nashr which is the opposite of folding, as we mentioned. It is as if the wind in its stillness is like something folded, then it is sent from its folding so it becomes like something open. Abu Ubaid interpreted it as meaning scattered in its faces, meaning He spreads it here and there. Asim read Bashir with a ba’ and a sukoon on the sheen and the tanween, the plural of Bashir, meaning the winds herald rain. And the evidence for that is His statement: And among His signs is that He sends the winds as good tidings (ar-Rum 30:46). The root of the word shin is damma, but it was made sukoon for ease, like rusul and rusul. And Bishr narrated from him with a fatha on the ba. An-Nahhas said: Bishr and “bashar are read as a source of bashara meaning give him good report. So these are five readings. Muhammad Al-Yamani read bashra with the weight of habla. And the seventh reading is bashra with a damma on the ba and shin. God the Almighty said: Until, when it carried heavy clouds. Clouds are both masculine and feminine. So is every plural between them and their singular is ha’. It is permissible to describe it with one, so you say: heavy clouds and heavy ones. The meaning is: the wind carried heavy clouds with water, i.e. it made heavy with its load. It is said: so-and-so carried nothing, i.e. he carried it. We drove it means the clouds. To a dead land means it has no vegetation. It is said: I drove it to such-and-such a country and to such-and-such a country. It is also said: for a dead land, so the lam is the lam of ajal. A country is every place on earth, inhabited or uninhabited, deserted or inhabited. A town and a country are the singular of countries and countries. A country is the trace, and its plural is ablaad. The poet said: After the destruction of her country al-Balad 90:The most humble of ostriches. It is said: He is more humble than the egg of the country, meaning than the egg of the ostrich that he leaves. Al-Balad is the land, it is said: This is our town, just as it is said: Our sea. Al-Balad is one of the mansions of the moon, and it is six stars of Sagittarius that the sun descends on the shortest day of the year. Al-Balad is the chest, it is said: So-and-so is spacious in town, meaning spacious in chest. The poet said: It was raised and threw a town upon a town, with few sounds except its clouds. He says: The she-camel knelt down and threw her chest on the ground. The town with the first letter of the word baladah open or closed: the purity between the eyebrows, so they are common words. So We sent down water with it meaning in the town. It was said: We sent down water with the clouds, because the clouds are a tool for sending down water. It is possible that the meaning is So We sent down water from it, like His statement: The servants of God drink from it (al-Insan 76:6) meaning from it. “So We brought forth with it from every kind of fruit. Thus do We bring forth the dead that you may remember.” The kaf is in the accusative case. That is, like that bringing forth, We bring the dead back to life. Al-Bayhaqi and others narrated on the authority of Abu Razin al-Uqayli who said: I said, O Messenger of God, how does God revive creation, and what is the sign of that in His creation? He said, Did you not pass by a barren valley of your people, then pass by it shaking with greenery? He said, Yes. He said, That is the sign of God in His creation. It was said: The point of comparison is that their revival from their graves will be by rain that God sends upon their graves, so the graves will split open and their souls will return to them. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then God sends - or he said God sends down - rain like dew, and people’s bodies grow from it. Then it is said, “O people, come to your Lord and stop them, for they will be questioned.” And he mentioned the hadith. We have mentioned it in full in the Book of Remembrance, and praise be to God. So it indicates resurrection and revival, and to God all matters return.
7:58: The Almighty said: "And the good land - its vegetation comes forth by permission of its Lord. But that which is bad brings forth nothing but scum." That is, the good soil. And the bad is that in whose soil there are stones or thorns, according to Al-Hasan. It was said: Its meaning is a simile. The Almighty likened the one who is quick to understand to the good land, and the dull one to the one who is bad, according to An-Nahhas. It was said: This is a metaphor for hearts. A heart that accepts admonition and remembrance, and a wicked heart that turns away from that, according to Al-Hasan as well. Qatada said: A metaphor for the believer who works voluntarily, hoping for reward, and the hypocrite who does not hope for reward. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of them knew that he would find a fat bone or two good arrows, he would attend the evening meal. Nakkad is in the accusative case as a state, and it is the difficulty that prevents giving good things. This is an example. Mujahid said: It means that among the children of Adam there is good and bad. Talhah read except nakkad without the kasra because of its heaviness. Ibn al-Qaqa’ read nakkad with the fatha on the kaf, so it is a source meaning that nakkad. As he said: It is only an advance and a retreat It was said: Nakada with the accusative and genitive of the kaf with the same meaning, like danaf and danaf, two languages. Thus do We diversify the verses meaning just as We diversified the verses, which are the arguments and evidence, in invalidating polytheism, thus We diversify the verses in everything that people need. For a people who are grateful and He specified the grateful because they are the ones who benefit from that.
7:59: The Almighty said: We sent Noah to his people, and he said, 'O my people, worship God.' When He explained that He is the Creator, capable of perfection, He mentioned the stories of the nations and what they contain of warnings against the infidels. The lam in la qad is for emphasis, alerting to the oath. The fa' indicates that the second comes after the first. O my people is an added address. It is also permissible to say, O my people, according to the original. Noah was the first of the messengers whom God sent to the people of the earth after Adam, peace be upon them, to forbid daughters, sisters, paternal aunts, and maternal aunts. An-Nahhas said: It was declined because it has three letters. It may be permissible to derive it from naah, and this meaning and others have been mentioned in Al-Imran, so there is no need to repeat them. Ibn al-Arabi said: Whoever says that Idris was among the historians before him has made a mistake. The evidence for the correctness of his mistake is the authentic hadith in the Night Journey, when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, met Adam and Idris, and Adam said to him: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous son. And Idris said to him: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous brother. If Idris was Noah’s father, he would have said welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous son. So when he said to him and the righteous brother, this indicates that he will meet with him in Noah, may the peace of God be upon them all. And no fair-minded person can say anything after this. Judge Iyad said: The answer of the fathers here came like Noah, Abraham and Adam, welcome to the righteous son. And he said about Idris the righteous brother as he mentioned about Moses, Jesus, Joseph, Aaron and John who were not the fathers of the Prophet, peace be upon him, by agreement. Al-Mazari said: Historians have mentioned that Idris was the grandfather of Noah, peace be upon them. If evidence is established that Idris was also sent, then the genealogists’ statement that he was before Noah is not correct, because of what the peace be upon him reported from Adam’s statement that Noah was the first messenger sent. And if evidence is not established, what they said is permissible: and it is correct to assume that Idris was a prophet who was not sent. Judge Iyad said: This can be combined by saying: Noah’s mission was specific to all the people of the earth - as he said in the hadith - like our prophet, peace be upon him. And Idris was for his people like Moses, Hud, Salih, Lot, and others. Some have provided evidence for this with the words of God Almighty: “And indeed, Elias was among the messengers. When he said to his people, ‘Will you not fear God?’” (37:123-124). It has been said that Elias is Idris. And peace was read to Idrasin. Judge Iyad said: I have seen Abu al-Hasan ibn Battaal say that Adam was not a messenger, to be safe from this objection. And the long hadith of Abu Dharr: The long hadith of Abu Dharr: It indicates that Adam and Idris were messengers. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is combined in that the mission of Noah is famous for reforming people and forcing them to believe through torment and destruction. What is meant is that he was the first prophet sent in this capacity. And God knows best. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Noah, peace be upon him, was sent when he was forty years old. Al-Kalbi said: Eight hundred years after Adam. Ibn Abbas said: He remained among his people calling them for a thousand years minus fifty years, as the revelation informed. Then he lived sixty years after the flood until people increased and became widespread. Wahb said: Noah was sent when he was fifty years old. Awn ibn Shaddad said: Noah was sent when he was three hundred and fifty years old. In many books of hadith, such as Al-Tirmidhi and others, it is stated that all of creation now is from the descendants of Noah, peace be upon him. Al-Naqqash mentioned on the authority of Sulayman ibn Arqam on the authority of Al-Zuhri: The Arabs, Persians, Romans, the people of Ash-Sham, and the people of Yemen are from the descendants of Sam, son of Noah. The Sindh, the Indians, the Zanj, the Abyssinians, the Zutt, the Nubians, and every black skinned person is descended from Ham, the son of Noah. The Turks, the Berbers, the Trans-China, Gog and Magog, and the Slavs are all descended from Japheth, the son of Noah. All creation is the offspring of Noah. The Almighty said: You have no god other than Him. Nafi’, Abu Amr, Asim and Hamzah read ghayr in the nominative case. That is, you have no god other than Him. An adjective for the position. It was said: ghayr means except, that is, you have no god other than God. Abu Amr said: I do not know the accusative or genitive. Al-Kisa’i read it in the genitive case for the position. The accusative is permissible for the exception, but it is not common, except that Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ permitted the accusative of ghayr in every position where it is appropriate, unless the speech is complete or not. So they permitted: No one came to me except you. Al-Farra’ said: It is the language of some of Banu Asad and Quda’ah. And he recited: Nothing prevented drinking from it except the cooing of a dove in the middle of the night. Al-Kisa’i said: It is not permissible to say ‘someone other than you came to me’ in the affirmative, because ‘illa’ does not occur here. An-Nahhas said: “According to the Basrans, it is not permissible to put ‘ghair’ in the accusative case if the statement is not complete. This is, in their view, one of the worst mistakes in grammar.”
