7:60: The elite are the nobles and leaders of the people. This has been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. Misguidance and error: deviating from the path of truth and departing from it. That is, we see you in our call to one God in misguidance from the truth.
7:61: God Almighty said: He said, ‘O my people, there is no error in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.’
7:62: I inform you with emphasis from the word tabligh, and with emphasis from the word tabligh. It was said: They are two languages with the same meaning, like karamahu and akramahu. And I advise you Advice: sincerity of intention from impurities of corruption in dealing, unlike cheating. It is said: I advised him and I advised him with advice, advice, and advice. It is with the letter lam which is more spacious. God the Almighty said: And I advise you, and the noun is advice. And the sincere is the sincere, and a sincere people. And a man with a sincere pocket means pure of heart. Al-Asma'i said: The sincere is the one who is pure of honey and other things. Like the spotless. And everything that is pure has been sincere. And someone was sincere, he accepted advice. It is said: Advise me, I am your sincere advisor. And the sincere is the tailor. And the sincere is the thread with which it is sewn. And the sincere ones also mean the skins. Al-A'sha said: You see, drinking is all intoxication, just like the advice of profit. Profit is a language that refers to a quarter, which is a small group. Profit is also a bird. This will have an additional meaning in Bara’ah, God willing.
7:63: The Almighty said: Or did you wonder? The waw was opened because it is a waw of conjunction, and the alif of interrogation was added to it for confirmation. The way of the waw is to be added to interrogative letters except the alif because of its strength. That there came to you a reminder meaning an admonition from your Lord. Upon a man from among you meaning on the tongue of a man. It was said: Upon means with, meaning with a man. It was said: The meaning is that there came to you a reminder from your Lord sent down upon a man from among you, meaning you know his lineage. Meaning upon a man from your kind. If he were a king, then perhaps there would be a discord in the difference of kind.
7:64: The universe can be singular or plural. It was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah. And blind means ignorant of the truth, as Qatada said. It was also said: about the knowledge of God Almighty and His power. It is said: a man is blind to such-and-such, meaning ignorant.
7:65: The Almighty said: And to 'Ad We sent their brother Hud meaning, and We sent to 'Ad their brother Hud. Ibn Abbas said: meaning, the son of their father. It was also said: their brother in the tribe. It was also said: meaning, a human being from the descendants of their father Adam. In Musannaf Abi Dawud, it is mentioned that their brother Hud means their companion. And 'Ad is from the descendants of Sam bin Noah. Ibn Ishaq said: And 'Ad is the son of 'Aws bin Iram bin Shalih bin Arfakhshad bin Sam bin Noah, peace be upon him. And Hud is Hood bin Abdullah bin Rabah bin Al-Jaloud bin 'Ad bin 'Aws bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah. God sent him as a prophet to 'Ad. He was from the most noble of them in lineage and the best of them in ancestry. And 'Ad, whoever does not decline it, makes it the name of the tribe, and whoever declines it makes it the name of the tribe. Abu Hatim said: And in the letter of Abi and Ibn Mas'ud, the first 'Ad without an alif. And Hud is foreign, and it was declined because of its lightness, because it has three letters. It may be possible that it is Arabic, derived from Had Yahud. The accusative is for substitution. There were seven opinions between Hud and Noah, as mentioned by the commentators. And Ad, as narrated, were thirteen tribes, who inhabited the sands, the sands of Alij. They were people of orchards, crops, and buildings, and their lands were the most fertile lands, so God was angry with them and made them deserts. It was narrated that they were in the regions of Hadhramaut to Yemen, and they worshipped idols. When his people were destroyed, Hud and those who believed with him joined him in Mecca, and they remained there until they died.
7:66: We see you in foolishness meaning in foolishness and frivolity. He said: Walking as spears shake, their tops are blown away by the passing winds This meaning was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. It was said that vision here and in the story of Noah is from seeing with the eyes. It was also said that it may mean opinion, which is the most likely opinion.
7:67: God Almighty said: He said, ‘O my people, there is no madness in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.’
7:68: God Almighty says: I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am to you a trustworthy adviser.
7:69: The Almighty said: And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah. Successors is the plural of successor in the masculine and the meaning, and successors in the wording. He bestowed upon them a favor by making them inhabitants of the earth after the people of Noah. And He increased you in creation abundantly. It is permissible to expand you with a sad because it is followed by a ta, meaning height in creation and greatness of body. Ibn Abbas said: The tallest of them was one hundred cubits, and the shortest was sixty cubits. This increase was over the creation of their fathers. It was said: Over the creation of the people of Noah. Wahb said: The head of one of them was like a great dome, and the eye of the man was such that wild beasts could hatch in it, as were their nostrils. Shahr bin Hawshab narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: If a man from the people of Aad would make two doors from stones, if five hundred men of this nation gathered around it, they would not be able to do it, and if one of them would push his foot into the ground, it would enter it. So remember the favors of God, meaning the blessings of God, the singular of which is ila, ili, ilu, and ila. Like vessels, its singular is I, I, I, Ino, and I. So that you may succeed.
7:70: They asked for the punishment that he had frightened them with and warned them against.
7:71: He said to them: It has befallen you. The meaning of became is became obligatory. It is said: The word and the judgment befell meaning became obligatory. And similar to it is: And when the punishment befell them (al-A’raf 7:134). That is, it descended upon them. And when the word befell them, We brought forth for them a beast from the earth (al-Naml 27:82). The filth is the torment. It was said: what is meant by filth is rust on the heart due to increased disbelief. Do you argue with me about names? meaning the idols that they worshipped, and they had different names. God has sent down for them no authority meaning no proof for you in worshipping them. So the name here means the named. Similar to it is: You worship not besides Him except names which you have named. (Yusuf 12:40) and these names are like Al-Uzza from Al-'Izz and Al-'Azz and Al-Lat, and they do not have anything of Al-'Izz and Al-Lat, and they do not have anything of Al-Izz and Al-Divinity.
7:72: Daber is the last. It was mentioned before. That is, they have no remnants left.
7:73: He is Thamud bin Aad bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah. He is the brother of Judays. They were living a comfortable life, but they disobeyed God's command and worshipped other than Him, and they spread corruption on earth. So God sent to them Salih as a prophet, and he is Salih bin Ubaid bin Asif bin Kashih bin Ubaid bin Hathir bin Thamud. They were an Arab people. Salih was from the most noble of them in lineage and the best of them in status. He called them to God Almighty until they became weak, and only a few of them followed him who were weak. Thamud was not declined because it was made a name for the tribe. Abu Hatim said: It was not declined because it is a foreign name. An-Nahhas said: This is a mistake, because it is derived from thamad, which means little water. The reciters read Unquestionably, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord (Hud 11:68) as the name of the tribe. The dwellings of Thamud were in Al-Hijr between Al-Hijaz and Ash-Sham to Wadi Al-Qura. They are from the descendants of Sam bin Noah. They were called Thamud because of the scarcity of its water. Its explanation will come in Al-Hijr, God willing. This is the she-camel of God, a sign for you. He brought out the she-camel from solid rock when they asked Him. She had a day in which she would drink all the water of the valley, and she would give them milk to drink like it, the sweetest and most delicious of which they had never drunk. It was according to their need, despite their large number. God the Almighty said: For her is a drink, and for you is a drink on a known day (Ash-Shu’ara’: 155). The she-camel was attributed to God the Almighty in the sense of attributing creation to the Creator. It contains the meaning of honor and specialization. Leave her to eat in God's land, and do not meaning you are not responsible for her sustenance and maintenance.
7:74: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And He settled you in the land in it is an omission, meaning He settled you in the land in homes. You take palaces from its plains meaning you build palaces in every place. And you carve out homes in the mountains they took homes in the mountains because of their long lives, as the roofs and buildings would wear out before their lives ended. Al-Hasan read it with the opening of the ha’, which is a language. It contains a throat letter, and that is why it came in the form of fa’il yaf’al. Second: This verse was used as evidence by those who permitted tall buildings such as palaces and the like, and by His statement: “Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?” (al-A’raf 7:32). It was mentioned that a son of Muhammad ibn Sirin built a house and spent a lot of money on it, so he mentioned that to Muhammad ibn Sirin and he said: I see no harm in a man building a building that benefits him. It was narrated that he, peace be upon him, said: If God bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see the effect of the blessing upon him. Among the effects of the blessing are good construction and good clothes. Don’t you see that if he bought a beautiful slave girl with a great deal of money, it is permissible and may be sufficient for him without that, so the same applies to the construction. Others disliked that, including Al-Hasan Al-Basri and others. They cited as evidence the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: If God wants evil for a servant, He destroys his wealth in mud and bricks. In another report from him, peace be upon him, he said: Whoever builds more than he needs will come on the Day of Resurrection carrying it on his neck. I said: I say this, because of his saying, peace be upon him: Whatever a believer spends, he will leave it with God, the Almighty, except for what is spent on building or disobedience. Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah and included by al-Darqutni. And his saying, peace be upon him: “The son of Adam has no right to anything other than these qualities: a house to live in, a garment to cover his nakedness, and a piece of bread and water.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. Third: The Almighty’s saying: So remember the favors of God, meaning His blessings. This indicates that the disbelievers are blessed. This was mentioned in Al Imran. And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption, was mentioned in Al Baqarah. Al ‘Uthy and Al ‘Uthw are two dialects. Al A’mash read Ta’athu with a kasrah on the ta’, taking it from ‘Uthy Ya’tha, not from ‘Uthy Ya’thw.
7:75: The Almighty said: The eminent ones among his people who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed among them, ‘To those who believed.’ The second is a substitute for the first, because the oppressed are the believers. It is a substitute for some of the whole.
7:76: God Almighty said: Those who were arrogant said, ‘Indeed, we disbelieve in that in which you have believed.’
7:77: The Almighty said: So they hamstrung the she-camel. Hamstringing is a wound. It was said: cutting off a limb that affects the soul. And the horse was hamstrung: if its legs were struck with a sword. And horses were hamstrung. And the back of the animal was hamstrung: if it turned away. Imru' al-Qais said: She said, as the foolish one leaned towards us both: You have hamstrung my camel, O Imru’ al-Qais, so get down. That is, you wounded it and caused it to turn its back. Al-Qushayri said: Hammering is the uncovering of the camel’s hock, then it was said in grammar that it is hamstringed, because hamstringing is usually the cause of slaughter. There are different opinions about the hamstring of a female camel. The most correct of them is what is in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abdullah bin Zama’ah who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) gave a sermon and mentioned the she-camel and the one who had hamstrung her. He said: When the most wretched of them arose, a mighty, powerful man, like Abu Zam`ah, arose for her. He mentioned the hadith. It was said that his name was Qidar ibn Salaf. It was said that their kingdom belonged to a woman called Malki, so she envied Salih because of the people’s inclination towards him. She said to two women who had two lovers whom they loved: Do not obey them, and ask them to hamstring the she-camel. So they did. The two men went out and forced the she-camel into a narrow passage, and one of them shot her with an arrow and killed her. Al-Saqb, which was her offspring, came to the rock from which the she-camel had emerged. They emptied it three times and the rock burst open and he entered it. It is said that it is the beast that will emerge at the end of time upon the people, as will be explained in An-Naml. Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Saqb was followed by four men who had hamstrung the she-camel: Musad` and his brother Dhu`ab. Then Musaddaq shot him with an arrow, which broke his heart. Then he dragged him by his foot and brought him to his mother, and they ate him with her. The first is more correct, for Salih said to them: There are only three days left of your life, and that is why he roared three times. It was also said: The one who hamstrung her hamstrung her, and with him were eight men, and they are the ones about whom God said: And there were in the city nine men (al-Naml 27:48), as will be explained in An-Naml. This is the meaning of His statement: So they called their companion, and he seized her and hamstrung her (al-Qamar 54:29). They were drinking, but they did not have enough water to mix their drink. It was the day of the camel’s milk, so one of them stood up and watched the women and said: I will relieve the people of her, so he hamstrung her. The Almighty said: And they were insolent toward the command of their Lord. That is, they were arrogant. Ata means to be arrogant. Ta’ta means to disobey. The harsh night means intense darkness, according to Al-Khalil. They said, O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with. That is, the punishment.
7:78: So the earthquake seized them meaning a severe earthquake. It was said: It was a severe shout that shook their hearts, as in the story of Thamud in Surah Hud in the story of Thamud, so the shout seized them. It is said: the thing trembled, trembling and shaking. And the wind shook the trees, its movement. Its origin is movement with sound, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: The Day the earthquake will shake (An-Nazi'at: 6) The poet said: When I saw that the time for Hajj had come and the people’s mounts were shaking with the people So they became in their home meaning their country. It was said: It is singular in the way of the genus, and the meaning is: in their homes. And he said in another place: in their homes (Hud 11:67 and 94) meaning in their homes. Couched down meaning stuck to the ground on their knees and faces, as a bird crouches. That is, they became motionless from the severity of the torment. The origin of jathum is for the rabbit and the like, and the place is mujtham. Zuhair said: The spring and the Aram walk behind it, and its young ones rise from every perch. It was said: They were burned by lightning and became dead, except for one man who was in the sanctuary of God. When he left the sanctuary, what happened to his people happened to him.
7:79: So he turned away from them meaning when he despaired of them. And he said, 'O my people, I have conveyed to you the message of my Lord and given you good advice.' It is possible that he said that before their death. It is possible that he said it after their death, like his saying, peace be upon him, to those killed in Badr: Have you found what your Lord promised to be true? It was said: Do these corpses speak? He said: You are not better at hearing than they, but they are not able to answer. The first is more apparent. It is indicated by but you do not like advisers, meaning you did not accept my advice.
7:80: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And Lot, when he said to his people. Al-Farra’ said: Lut is derived from their saying: This is alite with my heart, meaning it stuck. An-Nahhas said: Al-Zajjaj said that some grammarians - meaning Al-Farra’ - claimed that Lut may be derived from Lattat Al-Hawd meaning I smeared the basin with clay. He said: This is wrong, because foreign names are not derived like Isaac, so it is not said that it is from sahaq which means distance. Lut was declined because of its lightness because it has three letters and the middle letter is silent. Al-Naqqash said: Lut is one of the foreign names and not from Arabic. As for Lattat Al-Hawd, and This is alite with my heart from this, it is correct. But the name is foreign like Ibrahim and Isaac. Sibawayh said: Noah and Lut are foreign names, except that they are light, which is why they were declined. God sent him to a nation called Sodom, and he was the nephew of Abraham. Its accusative is either with Arsalna which precedes it, in which case it is conjoined. It is permissible for it to be accusative with the meaning of and remember. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Do you commit immorality? meaning intercourse with males. God mentioned it by the name of immorality to clarify that it is adultery, as the Almighty said: “And do not come near to adultery. Indeed, it is an immorality.” (al-Isra’
7:81: The Almighty said: You Nafi' and Hafs read it as a predicate with one broken hamza, explaining the aforementioned obscenity, so it was not good to introduce a question into it because it cuts off what comes after it from what precedes it. The rest read it with two hamzas as a question word meaning rebuke, and that is good because what comes before and after it is an independent statement. Abu Ubaid, Al-Kisa'i and others chose the first, and they argued with the Almighty's saying: Then if I die, will they be the immortals? (al-Anbiya 21:34) and He did not say I understand. And He said: Then if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? (Al Imran 3:144) and He did not say you turned back. This is one of the worst mistakes because they likened two things to something that is not similar, because the condition and its answer are like one thing like the subject and predicate, so it is not permissible for there to be two questions in them. It is not permissible to say: If I die, will I understand? Just as it is not permissible to say: Is Zaid leaving? The story of Lot, peace be upon him, contains two sentences, so you can ask about each one of them. This is the opinion of Al-Khalil and Sibawayh, and it was chosen by An-Nahhas, Makki and others. Desire is an accusative of the verbal noun, meaning you desire them with desire. It is also permissible for it to be a verbal noun in the place of the circumstance. Rather, you are a transgressing people is similar to Rather, you are a transgressing people (Ash-Shu’ara’: 166) in your gathering together with polytheism, this abomination.
7:82: The Almighty said: And the answer of his people was only that they said, 'Drive them out' meaning Lot and his followers. The meaning of purify themselves is from coming in this context. It is said: A man purifies himself, meaning he is free from sin. Qatada said: By God, they criticized them without any fault.
7:83: From those who remain means those who remain in God's punishment, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Qatada. Ghabbar means something that has passed, and ghabbar means it remains. It is one of the opposites. Some people said: The past is transitive with an unvoiced 'ayn. And the remaining is ghabir with an voiced ghayn. Ibn Faris narrated it in Al-Mujmal. Al-Zajjaj said: From those who remain, meaning from those absent from salvation, and it was said, because of its long life. Al-Nahhas said: Abu Ubaidah believes that the meaning is from the long-lived, meaning that it has become old. It is most common in the language for ghabir to be the remaining, as the rajaz poet said: Muhammad has not slept since God forgave him for his past and future sins.
7:84: Lot and his family traveled as God described, during parts of the night (Hud 11:81 and al-Hijr 15:65). Then he ordered Gabriel, peace be upon him, to put his wing under their cities, uproot them, and raise them until the people of the sky heard the crowing of roosters and the barking of dogs. Then he turned their tops into their bottoms, and stones of baked clay rained down on them. It was said: on those of them who were absent. And he caught up with Lot's wife, and he had a stone with him, so he killed her. And it was mentioned that there were four cities. And it was said: five, in which there were four hundred thousand. And the story of Lot will come in Surah Hud more clearly than this, God willing.
7:85: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And to Madyan. It was said about Madyan: the name of a country and a region. It was also said: the name of a tribe, as is said: Bakr and Tamim. It was also said: they are from the descendants of Madyan, son of Abraham, peace be upon him. Whoever sees that Madyan is the name of a man, does not decline it because it is a foreign proper noun. Whoever sees it as the name of a tribe or a land, it is more appropriate not to decline it. Al-Mahdawi said: It is narrated that he was the son of Lot’s daughter. Makki said: He was the husband of Lot’s daughter. There is disagreement about his lineage. Ata’, Ibn Ishaq, and others said: Shu’ayb is the son of Mikail Ibn Yashjar Ibn Madyan Ibn Abraham, peace be upon him. His name in Syriac was Beirut. His mother was Mikail, the daughter of Lot. Al-Sharqi Ibn Al-Qatami claimed that Shu’ayb was the son of Aifa’ Ibn Yoobib Ibn Madyan Ibn Abraham. Ibn Sam’an claimed that Shu’ayb was the son of Juzi Ibn Yashjar Ibn Lawi Ibn Ya’qub Ibn Ishaq Ibn Abraham. Shu’ayb is the diminutive of Shu’ab or Shu’ab. Qatada said: He is Shu’ayb Ibn Yoobib. It was said: Shuaib bin Safwan bin Aifa bin Thabit bin Madyan bin Ibrahim. And God knows best. He was blind, and that is why his people said: And indeed, we see you weak among us (Hud 11:91). He was called: the orator of the prophets because of his good arguments with his people. His people were people who disbelieved in God and cheated with the measure and the weight. There has come to you a clear proof from your Lord, meaning a statement, which is the coming of Shu’ayb with the message. No miracle of his is mentioned in the Qur’an. It was said: His miracle is what Al-Kisa’i mentioned in Stories of the Prophets. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And do not deprive people of their due rights. Deficiency is deficiency. It occurs in goods by describing them as defective or underestimating them, or by deceiving them about their value, or by trickery in increasing or decreasing the measure. All of that is consuming wealth unjustly, and it was forbidden by the previous and ancient nations on the tongues of the Messengers, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all. God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And do not cause corruption on the earth after its reformation is in apposition to and do not deprive. This is a term that includes both minor and major corruption. Ibn Abbas said: Before God sent Shuaib as a messenger, the earth was committing sins, making permissible what is forbidden, and shedding blood. He said: That was its corruption. Then when God sent Shuaib and he called them to God, the earth was reformed. And every prophet sent to his people is their reformer.
7:86: Fourth - The Almighty's saying: And do not sit on every path He forbade them from sitting on the roads and turning people away from the path that leads to obedience to God, and they used to threaten punishment to those who believed. The scholars differed about the meaning of their sitting on the roads in three meanings. Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Mujahid, and Al-Suddi said: They used to sit on the roads leading to Shu'ayb and threaten whoever wanted to come to him and turn him away and say: He is a liar, so do not go to him, as the Quraysh used to do with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the apparent meaning of the verse. Abu Hurairah said: This is a prohibition against cutting off the road and taking the spoils, and that was among their actions. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: On the night of my Isra’, I saw a piece of wood on the road, and no garment would pass through it without it tearing it, nor anything else without it tearing it. I said, What is this, O Gabriel? He said, This is a parable for a group of your nation who sit on the road and cut it off. Then he recited, And do not sit on every road, threatening [anything]. The discussion of thieves and warriors has already been mentioned, and praise be to God. Al-Suddi also said, “They were tax collectors who accepted it, and their example today is these tax collectors who take from people what is not required of them by the Sharia of financial duties by force and coercion, so they guarantee money whose origin is permissible to guarantee from zakat, inheritances, and entertainment. And those who are arranged on the roads and other things that have become widespread in existence and practiced in all countries. It is one of the greatest, most serious and most heinous sins, for it is usurpation, injustice, and oppression of people, and the dissemination of evil, practicing it, continuing it, and approving it. The greatest of them is the inclusion of the Sharia and the ruling in the judiciary. So, we belong to God and to Him we shall return! Nothing remains of Islam except its form, and nothing of the religion except its name.” This interpretation is supported by the previous prohibition. Concerning money, in scales, measures and misappropriation. The Almighty’s saying: Whoever believes in Him The pronoun in He may refer to the name of God Almighty, or to Shu’aib according to the opinion of those who saw sitting on the road as a barrier, or to the path. Crooked Abu Ubaid and Al-Zajjaj said: The ‘ayn is broken in meanings. And its opening is in bodies. The Almighty says: And remember when you were few and He made you many. That is, He made you many, or made you many through wealth after poverty. That is, you were poor and He made you rich. So be patient. This is not an order to remain in disbelief, but rather a warning and a threat.
7:87: He said: And if there was a group of you, so he mentioned it according to the meaning, and if he had considered the wording, he would have said: it was.
7:88: God the Almighty said: The eminent ones among his people who were arrogant said, 'We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who have believed with you from our city, or you must return to our religion.' The meaning of or you must return to our religion is that you must become our religion. It was said: Shu'ayb's followers were disbelievers before believing in him, meaning you must return to us as you were before. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that return means initiation. It is said: Something bad has come back to me from so-and-so, meaning it happened, even if nothing bad had happened before that, meaning it happened to me from him. Shu'ayb said to them: Or even if we were reluctant, meaning even if we were reluctant, you would force us to do it, meaning to leave our homeland or return to your religion. That is, if you did this, you would have done something terrible.
7:89: We would have fabricated a lie against God if we returned to your religion after God has saved us from it despairing of returning to their religion. And it is not for us to return to it except if God, our Lord, wills Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: meaning except by the will of God, the Almighty. He said: This is the saying of the people of the Sunnah, meaning and the return to disbelief does not occur until God wills it. So the exception is discontinuous. It was said: The exception here is in the form of submission to God, the Almighty, as He said: And my success is not except with God (Hud 11:88). The evidence for this is that after it "Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. In God we rely" It was said: It is like you saying I will not speak to you until the crow lays eggs, and until the camel passes through the eye of a needle. The crow never lays eggs, and the camel never passes through the eye of a needle. The Almighty said: Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. That is, He knows what was and what will be. Knowledge is an accusative of specification. It was said that the meaning is and it is not for us to return to it that is, to the village after you hated to be our neighbors. Rather, we would leave your village, migrating to another one. Unless God wills He returns us to it. There is some error in this, because it is said: He returned to the village, but it is not said: He returned in the village. God the Almighty said: Upon God we have put our trust meaning we have relied. This has been mentioned before in more than one place. Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth. Qatada said: God sent him to two nations: the people of Madyan and the people of the thicket. Ibn Abbas said: Shuaib prayed a lot, but when his people persisted in their disbelief and error for a long time, and he despaired of their reform, he invoked God against them and said: Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth, for You are the best of judges. So God answered his prayer and destroyed them with the earthquake.
7:90: God Almighty says: And the eminent ones who disbelieved among his people said, meaning they said to those below them. If you follow Shu`ayb, then you will surely be losers, meaning doomed.
7:91: Then the earthquake seized them. It was also said: the shout. The people of the thicket were destroyed by the shadow, as will come.
7:92: The Almighty said: Those who denied Shu'aib - it is as if they had never lived therein. Al-Jurjani said: It was said that this is a new statement, meaning those who denied Shu'aib became as if they had never ceased to be dead. And sing means to reside. It is said: I sang in a place if I resided in it. And the people sang in their home, meaning their stay in it was long. The place is the home, and the plural is the places. Labid said: I sang six songs before the Dahis River, if only the stubborn soul had immortality. Hatim Tay said: We were rich for a time in vagabondage and wealth, just as time is in its days of hardship and ease. The vicissitudes of time have made us soft and hard, and time has given us to drink from its cup. Our enmity towards our relatives has not increased our wealth, nor has poverty diminished our lineage. Those who denied Shu`ayb were the losers. This is the beginning of a speech, which is an exaggeration of blame and rebuke and a reiteration of the matter’s magnification and glorification. And when they said: Whoever follows Shu`ayb is a loser, God said: The losers are those who said this statement.
7:93: How can I grieve over a disbelieving people? That is, sorrows. I grieve over something, I grieve, and I am grieving.
7:94: The Almighty’s saying: And We did not send to any city a prophet contains an implied meaning, which is that its people denied it, except that We seized them with poverty and hardship that perhaps they might humble themselves. This was discussed previously.
7:95: Then We replaced the bad with good meaning We replaced the drought with fertility. Until they multiplied meaning they increased in number, according to Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zayd said: Their wealth and children multiplied. Afa is one of the opposites. Afa means to increase. Afa means to be destroyed. God the Almighty knows that He seized them with hardship and ease, but they did not deter or give thanks. And they said, 'Our fathers were touched by hardship and ease', so we are like them. Then We seized them suddenly meaning suddenly so that the regret would be greater.
7:96: The Almighty said: And if the people of the towns had only believed A city is called a town because people gather in it. From the root word qarya, which means to gather water. This has already been fully explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. We would have opened upon them blessings from the sky and the earth meaning rain and plants. This is specifically for some people who have been mentioned. Believers may be tested by hardship in life, and it will be an expiation for their sins. Do you not see that He informed us about Noah when he said to his people, "Seek forgiveness from your Lord. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving. He will send down upon you abundant rain." (Nuh 71:10-11) And about Hud, Then repent to Him, and He will send down upon you abundant rain. (Hud 11:52). So He promised them rain and fertility specifically. This is indicated by But they denied, so We seized them for what they used to earn. That is, they denied the messengers. The believers were truthful and did not lie.
7:97: The Almighty says: Then did the people of the towns feel secure? The question is for denial, and the fa is for conjunction. Similar to it is: Then did the judgement of the time of ignorance? (al-Ma’idah 5:50). What is meant by the towns is Mecca and what is around it, because they denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: It is general for all the towns. That Our punishment would not come to them means Our torment. By night means while they were asleep.
7:98: Or do the people of the towns feel secure against Our punishment coming upon them? Al-Haramiyan and Ibn Amir read it with a sukoon on the waw for conjunction, meaning permission, like And do not obey among them a sinner or an ingrate (al-Insan 76:24). He sat with Al-Hasan or Ibn Sirin. The meaning is: Or do they feel secure from these types of punishment. That is, if you feel secure from one type of punishment, you will not feel secure from the other. It is permissible for or to refer to one of the two things, like saying: I struck Zaid or Amr. The rest read it with a fatha on it with a hamza after it. He made it a waw of conjunction with the alif of interrogation entered into it, similar to or whenever they make a covenant (al-Baqarah 2:100). The meaning of in the morning while they are playing is that they are in something that is of no benefit to them. It is said to everyone who is playing in something that is of no benefit to him, as mentioned by Al-Nahhas. In Al-Sahah: Playing is well-known, and playing is like it. He played, he plays. And he played: he played time after time. A man who plays a lot: he plays a lot, and playing with the fatha is the source. And a playful maid.
7:99: The Almighty says: Do they then feel secure against the plan of God? That is, His punishment and recompense for their plan. It was said: His plan is to lure them with blessings and health.
7:100: God Almighty says: Has He not guided meaning made clear. Those who inherit the earth meaning the disbelievers of Mecca and those around them. We afflicted them meaning We seized them for their sins meaning for their disbelief and denial. And We stamp meaning We stamp, so it is a new sentence. It was said: It is conjoined with We afflicted meaning their share and We stamp, so the past tense took the place of the future.
7:101: The Almighty said: Those towns meaning these towns that We destroyed, and they are the towns of Noah, Aad, Lot, Hud, and Shuaib mentioned above. We relate meaning We recite to you some of their report meaning some of their stories. It is a consolation for the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the Muslims. But they were not to believe meaning those disbelievers were not to believe after their destruction if We had brought them back to life, said Mujahid. Similar to it is And if they were returned, they would have returned (al-An’am 6:28). Ibn Abbas and Al-Rabi' said: It was in the knowledge of God Almighty on the day He took the covenant from them that they would not believe in the messengers. Because they denied before meaning on the day of the covenant when He brought them out from the back of Adam and they believed reluctantly, not willingly. Al-Suddi said: They believed on the day He took the covenant from them reluctantly, so they would not believe now in reality. It was said: They asked for miracles, but when they saw them, they would not believe in what they denied before seeing the miracle. Its counterpart is just as they did not believe in him the first time (al-An’am 6:110). Thus does God set a seal upon the hearts of the disbelievers, meaning just as He set a seal upon the hearts of those mentioned, so does God set a seal upon the hearts of those who disbelieve in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
7:102: God Almighty says: And We did not find for most of them any covenant. Min is redundant and indicates the meaning of the genus. If it were not for min, it would be possible to imagine that it is one in meaning. Ibn Abbas said: He means the covenant taken from them at the time of the atom, and whoever breaks the covenant is said to have no covenant, meaning as if he did not make a covenant. Al-Hasan said: The covenant that was made to them with the prophets is that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. It was said: He meant that the disbelievers are divided, so most of them are those who have no trustworthiness or loyalty, and some of them have trustworthiness despite their disbelief, even if they are few. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah.
7:103: The Almighty says: Then We sent after them meaning after Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shuaib. Moses meaning Moses, son of Imran. With Our signs meaning with Our miracles. But they wronged them meaning they disbelieved and did not believe in the signs. Insult is putting something in the wrong place. God Almighty says: Then see how was the end of the corrupters. That is, what was the end of their affair.
7:104: God Almighty said: And Moses said, ‘O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.’
7:105: It is obligatory meaning it is obligatory. Whoever reads only as not then the meaning is he is keen that I not say. In Abdullah's reading, it is it is obligatory by omitting on. It was said that only means with, meaning it is obligatory that I not say. And the same is in the reading of Abu and Al-A'mash as not to say. Just as you say: I shot with the bow and on the bow. So it is obligatory in this sense means obligatory and the meaning of send with me the Children of Israel is keep them. And he used to use them in hard work.
7:106: God Almighty said: He said, ‘If you have come with a sign, then produce it, if you should be of the truthful.’
7:107: So he threw down his staff is used for objects and meanings. It has been mentioned before. The snake is the large male snake, and it is the largest of the snakes. Mubeen means a snake that is not ambiguous.
7:108: And he took out his hand meaning he took it out and showed it. It was said: from his pocket or from his wing, as in the revelation And put your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without disease (al-Naml 27:12) meaning without leprosy. Moses was very dark-skinned, then he put his hand back into his bosom and it returned to its original color. Ibn Abbas said: His hand had a bright light that illuminated what was between the sky and the earth. It was said: His hand would come out white like snow, shining. But when he put it back, it would return to being like the rest of his body.
7:110: From your land meaning from your king, you Copts, by his giving precedence to the Children of Israel over you. So what do you command? meaning he said to Pharaoh: So what do you command. It was said: it is from the saying of the leaders, meaning they said to Pharaoh alone: So what do you command. Just as the tyrants and leaders are addressed: What do you see in such-and-such. It is possible that they said to him and his companions. And ma is in the nominative case, on the basis that dha means who. And in the accusative case, on the basis that ma and dha are one and the same thing.
7:111: They said, 'Arja' The people of Medina, Asim, and Al-Kisa'i read it without a hamza, except that Warsh and Al-Kisa'i made the kasra of the ha' full, and Abu Amr read it with a silent hamza and a damma on the ha'. These are two dialects. It is said: I postponed it and I postponed it. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, and Hisham read it like this, except that they made the damma on the ha' full, and the rest of the people of Kufa read Arja' with a sukun on the ha'. Al-Farra' said: It is a dialect of the Arabs, they stop on the ha' implied in the connection if what precedes it moves, and likewise this is Talha who has come. The Basrans denied this. Qatada said: The meaning of Arja' is to detain him. Ibn Abbas said: He delayed him. It was said: Arja' is taken from Raja yarju, meaning he made him hopeful and left him hoping, as Al-Nahhas narrated from Muhammad bin Yazid. The kasra on the ha' is a tradition. It is permissible to make it a damma on the original. And its sukoon is a mistake that is not permissible except in anomalous poetry. And his brother is in apposition to the ha’. Gatherers is in the accusative case as a state.
7:112: They come to you is in the subjunctive mood because it is the answer to a command, and that is why the letter nun was deleted from it. The people of Kufa, except for Asim, read kull sahar, and the rest of the people read sahar, and they are close, except that fa'alan is more exaggerated.
7:113: The Almighty said: "And the magicians came to Pharaoh" and the mention of sending was omitted for the listener's knowledge. Ibn Abd al-Hakam said: They were twelve chiefs, with each chief twenty overseers, under the hand of each overseer a thousand magicians. Their leader was Shimon according to Muqatil ibn Sulayman. Ibn Jurayj said: They were nine hundred from Arish, Fayoum and Alexandria in threes. Ibn Ishaq said: They were fifteen thousand magicians, and it was narrated from Wahb. It was said: They were twelve thousand. Ibn al-Munkadir said eighty thousand. It was said: Fourteen thousand. It was said: They were three hundred thousand magicians from the countryside, three hundred thousand magicians from Upper Egypt, and three hundred thousand magicians from Fayoum and its environs. It was said: They were seventy men. It was said: Seventy-three, and God knows best. And with them, according to what was narrated, were ropes and sticks carried by three hundred camels. Then the snake swallowed all of that. Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi said: When she opened her mouth, her jaw would be eighty cubits long, placing her lower jaw on the ground and her upper jaw on the palace wall. It was also said that her mouth was forty cubits wide, and God knows best. She headed towards Pharaoh to swallow him, so he jumped from his bed and fled from her and called for help from Moses, who took it and found that it was a staff as it was. Wahb said: Twenty-five thousand died from fear of the staff. They said, ‘Indeed, we have a reward,’ meaning a prize and money. He did not say they said with the letter fa, because he meant when they came, they said. It was read indeed, we have as a report. This is the reading of Nafi’ and Ibn Kathir. They forced Pharaoh to give them money if they were defeated.
7:114: Then Pharaoh said to them: Yes, and indeed you are among those brought near meaning among the people of high status with us, so he gave them more than what they asked for. It was said: They had decided that for themselves in their judgment if they were defeated. That is, they said: We deserve the reward if we are defeated. The rest read it with the interrogative form as a way of asking. They asked Pharaoh: Would he give them a reward if they were defeated or not? They did not decide that with Pharaoh: Rather, they asked him whether he would do that, so he said to them: Yes, for you is the reward and nearness if you are defeated.
7:115: They behaved with Moses, peace be upon him, and that was the reason for their faith. And that is in the accusative case according to Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra', meaning either that you do the throwing. Similar to it is the saying of the poet: They said riding, so we said that is our custom.
7:116: He said, 'Throw.' Al-Farra' said: There is an omission in the speech. The meaning is: Moses said to them, 'You will never defeat your Lord, nor will you invalidate His signs.' This is one of the miracles of the Qur'an, the likes of which does not occur in the speech of people, nor are they able to do it. The simple wording comes with many meanings. It was said: It is a threat. That is, begin by throwing, and you will see what will happen to you of disgrace, since it is not permissible for Moses to order them to practice magic. It was said: He ordered them to do that to show their lies and deception. So when they threw, that is, the ropes and sticks. They bewitched the eyes of the people, that is, they made them imagine and turned them away from their correct perception, with what is imagined from the deception that is like sorcery and sleight of hand, as was explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. The meaning of great is in their eyes, because it was a lot and not great in reality.
7:117: Ibn Zayd said: The meeting was in Alexandria and the snake's tail reached beyond the lake. Another said: It opened its mouth and began to slurp up - that is, swallow - what they threw of their ropes and sticks. It was said: What they threw were ropes of leather with mercury in them, so they moved and they said, These are snakes. Hafs read talaqafa with a sukoon on the lam and a light sukoon on the lam. He made it the future of laqaf yalqaf. An-Nahhas said: According to this reading, it is permissible to talaqafa because it is from laqaf. The rest read it with a shaddah and a fathah on the lam, and they made it the future of talaqafa, so it is talaqafa. It is said: I caught something and swallowed it if you took it or swallowed it. Talaqafa, talaqam, and talham have the same meaning. Abu Hatim said: I was informed in some readings that it is talaqam with a shaddah on the meem. The poet said: You are the staff of Moses that never ceases to feed the magician what he fabricates. It is narrated: He caught it. What they are fabricating means what they are lying about, because they brought ropes and put mercury in them until they moved.
7:118: God Almighty said: Then the truth came to pass. Mujahid said: The truth appeared.
7:119: And they turned back in humiliation is an accusative of state. The verb is derived from it and it becomes smaller, saghran, saghran, and sagharaan. That is, the people of Pharaoh and Pharaoh with them turned back in humiliation, subjugated, and defeated. As for the magicians, they believed.
7:120: God Almighty said: And the magicians fell down prostrating.
7:121: God Almighty said: They said, ‘We believe in the Lord of the worlds.’
7:122: God Almighty said: Lord of Moses and Aaron.
7:123: The Almighty said: Pharaoh said, 'You believed in him before I gave you permission.' This was a denial from him to them. This is indeed a plot you plotted in the city to expel its people from it. That is, there was a conspiracy between you and him in this in order to seize control of Egypt. That is, this was done by you in the city of Egypt before you went out into this desert. So you will soon know. This was a threat to them.
7:124: Ibn Abbas said: Pharaoh was the first to be crucified, and the hands and feet were cut off from opposite sides, the right foot and the left hand, and the right hand and the left foot, on the authority of Al-Hasan.
7:125: God Almighty said: They said, ‘Indeed, to our Lord we will return.’
7:126: And you do not resent us except that we have believed in the signs of our Lord. Al-Hasan read it with the qaf open. Al-Akhfash said that it is a language that is said: naqmat al-amr and naqmatuhu means denying it, meaning you do not resent us except that we have believed in God, which is the truth. When His signs and clear proofs came to us. "Our Lord, pour out upon us patience." Pouring out means pouring, meaning pour it upon us when cutting and crucifying. "And let us die as Muslims." It was said that Pharaoh took the magicians and cut them up on the bank of the river, and that he believed in Moses when the magicians believed, six hundred thousand.
7:127: God the Almighty said: And the chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, 'Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land?' That is, to cause division and disperse the people. And leave you with the accusative of the ra' is the answer to the question, and the waw is a substitute for the fa'. And your gods Al-Hasan said: Pharaoh used to worship idols, so he used to worship and be worshipped. Sulayman Al-Taymi said: I heard that Pharaoh used to worship cows. Al-Taymi said: So I said to Al-Hasan: Did Pharaoh worship anything? He said: Yes, he used to worship something that he had put around his neck. It was said: The meaning of and your gods is and your obedience, as was said in the Almighty's saying: They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides God (al-Tawbah 9:31), that they did not worship them but obeyed them, so it became a metaphor. Na'im bin Maysarah read and leave you with the nominative case, assuming that he was leaving you. Al-Ashhab Al-Uqayli read Wa-Yadhrik in the subjunctive mood, with the light Yadhrik pronounced because of the heaviness of the damma. Anas bin Malik read Wa-Yadhrik in the nominative case and with the letter Nun. They informed about themselves that they would abandon His worship if He left Moses alive. Ali bin Abi Talib, Ibn Abbas, and Al-Dahhak read Wa-Ilahatik which means Wa-Ibadatik. According to this reading, He was worshipped and not worshipped, meaning he abandons his worship of you. Abu Bakr Al-Anbari said: Among the doctrines of the proponents of this reading is that when Pharaoh said: I am your highest lord (al-Nazi’at 79:24) and I have not known of any god for you other than me (al-Qasas 28:38), he denied that he had a lord or a god. So it was said to him: Wa-Yadhrik meaning Wa-Yadhrik and Wa-Ilahatik meaning He abandons you and the worship of people to you. The reading of the common people is Wa-Ilahatik as mentioned above, and it is based on the fact that Pharaoh claimed divinity in appearance and he knew that he was being raised. The evidence for this is his statement when he came to the bathhouse: I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believed (Yunus 10:90). This statement was not accepted from him because he came after the door of repentance was closed. Before this state, he had a god whom he worshipped secretly instead of the Lord of the Worlds, may He be glorified and exalted, as stated by Al-Hasan and others. In the letter of Abi, Do you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land while they have abandoned you from worshipping you? It was said: And your gods. It was said: He used to worship a cow, and if he liked a cow, he would order its worship, and he said: I am your lord and the lord of this one. That is why he said: Then he brought out for them a calf with a body (Ta-Ha 20:18). It was mentioned by Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi. Al-Zajjaj said: He had small idols that his people used to worship to draw closer to him, so they were attributed to him, that is why he said: I am your highest lord. Ismail bin Ishaq said: Pharaoh’s statement: I am your highest lord indicates that they used to worship something other than him. It was said: What is meant by the gods according to the reading of Ibn Abbas is the cow that he used to worship. It was said: They meant the sun and they used to worship it. The poet said: We hastened the goddess to return Then he felt comfortable with his people and said: We will kill their sons with a light pronunciation, as Nafi’ and Ibn Kathir read. The rest use a heavy pronunciation for emphasis. And keep their women alive meaning do not fear them. And indeed, We are over them, dominating. He comforted them with this speech. He did not say We will kill Moses because he knew that he would not be able to defeat him. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Pharaoh was filled with terror of Moses, so whenever he saw him, he would urinate like a donkey.
7:128: When the people of Moses heard about Pharaoh, Moses said to them: "Seek help from God and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to God. He causes whom He wills to inherit it." He made them hope that God would give them the land of Egypt. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous. That is, Paradise is for those who fear God, and the outcome of everything is its end. But when it is said in general terms: The outcome is for so-and-so, then it is understood in common parlance to mean good.
7:129: God the Almighty said: They said, 'We were harmed before you came to us' meaning at the beginning of your birth by killing your sons and enslaving your women. And after you have come to us meaning now that is repeated to us, meaning the threat that came from Pharaoh. It was said: The harm before: their subjection of the Children of Israel to their work until noon, and sending them the rest of the day to earn for themselves. The harm after: their subjection all day without food or drink, said Juwaybir. Al-Hasan said: The harm before and after are the same, which is taking the jizya. He said, 'Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land' Perhaps is obligatory from God. He renewed the promise to them and fulfilled it. They were made successors in Egypt during the time of David and Solomon, peace be upon them, and they conquered Jerusalem with Joshua bin Nun, as mentioned above. It was narrated that they said that when Moses went out with them and Pharaoh followed them, so he was behind them and the sea was in front of them, so God fulfilled the threat by drowning Pharaoh and his people and saving them. He sees how you do provides similar examples. That is, He sees the work for which the reward is due, because God does not reward them for what they do, but rather He rewards them for what they do.
7:130: The Almighty said: And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years meaning drought. This is well-known in the language. It is said: A year struck them, meaning drought. And its meaning is a drought for a year. And in the hadith: O God, make them years like the years of Joseph. Some Arabs use the letter nun in years. Al-Farra’ recited: I see the passing years taking from me as secrets are taken from the crescent moon Al-Nahhas said: Sibawayh recited this verse with the opening of the letter nun, but he recited in this what is not permissible otherwise, which is his saying: I have passed forty Al-Farra’ narrated on the authority of Banu Amir that they say: I stayed with him for years, O man, in the accusative case. He said: Banu Tamim do not inflect and say: Years have passed for him, O man. “Sanin” is the plural of sanah, and sanah here means drought, not a year. And from this, asnat al-qawm means they suffered drought. Abdullah bin al-Zubayri said: Amr Al-Ala broke the tharid for his people, and the men of Mecca were lean and old. Perhaps they will remember meaning that they will be admonished and their hearts will soften.
7:131: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: So when good comes to them, meaning fertility and abundance, they say, ‘This is for Us,’ meaning we were given it by right. But if evil befalls them, meaning drought and disease, which is the issue: Second: They take Moses as an ill omen. Similar to this is And if a misfortune befalls them, they say, ‘This is from you.’ (An-Nisa’: 78). The original is they take bad omen. The ta was assimilated into the ta. Talhah read they took bad omen as a past tense verb. The origin of this is from superstition and the warning of birds. Then their use became widespread until everyone who takes bad omen was called tatiyar. The Arabs used to take good omen from the saneh, which comes from the right. They used to take bad omen from the bareh, which comes from the left. They also used to take bad omen from the sound of the crow, interpreting it as the obvious. They used to infer things from the responses of birds to each other, and from their sounds at times other than their usual times. The same applies to gazelles when they pass by in the morning or in the evening. They would say when they depart: Who will bring me the “saneh after the bareh? However, the strongest thing they had was in all birds, so they called them all superstitions from this aspect. The Persians have bad omens when they see a boy being taken to the teacher in the morning, and they consider seeing a boy returning home from the teacher a good omen, and they consider seeing a water skin on the back of a full, tied skin, and they consider seeing an empty water skin with its skin open, and they consider a porter who is laden with a load, and a dignified animal, and they consider a porter who has put down his load, and an animal whose weight has been removed from it. Islam came with the prohibition of bad omens and bad omens from what is heard from the sound of any bird, whatever it is, and in whatever condition it is, as the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: Leave the birds in their nests. This is because many of the people of the pre-Islamic era, when they wanted to relieve themselves, would go to the birds in their nests and scare them away. If they took the right, they would go on to relieve themselves. This is what they considered to be the saneh. If they took the left, they would go back. This is what they considered to be the barah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade this by saying: Leave the birds in their nests. This is how it is in the hadith. The Arabs say wa-na-tha its nests. Imru' al-Qais said: I had lunch while the birds were in their nests Al-Wakna: is the name for every den and nest. Al-Wakn: is the place where the bird lays eggs and hatches them, and it is a hole in the walls and trees. It is said: The bird was kan yakun wa kanan if it incubated its eggs. There were also some Arabs who did not consider superstition to be a thing, and they praised those who denied it. Al-Muraqqash said: I went out, and I never went out, to Waq and Hatim So the unlucky ones are like the fortunate ones, and the fortunate ones are like the unlucky ones. Ikrimah said: I was with Ibn Abbas when a bird passed by, crowing. A man from the people said: Good, good. Ibn Abbas said: There is neither good nor evil in this. Our scholars said: As for the words of birds, they have no connection to what they are used to indicate, nor do they have knowledge of what is to come, let alone the future, to inform about it. There is no one among the people who knows the language of birds, except what God, the Most High, had given to Solomon, peace be upon him, of that. So superstition is included among the falsehoods. And God knows best. And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: He is not one of us who dreams, speculates, or is prevented from travelling by superstition. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Superstition is polytheism - three times - and there is none of us who does not - but God removes it by trusting in Him.” Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas narrated “on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever is prevented from doing something because of a bad omen has committed shirk. It was said: What is the expiation for that, O Messenger of God? He said: That one of them should say: O God, there is no omen except Your omen, and there is no good except Your good, and there is no god but You, then he goes about his business.” In another report: “If any of you finds that, let him say: ‘O God, none brings good deeds except You, and none takes away evil deeds except You. There is no power nor strength except with You.’” Then he goes, trusting in God, for God will suffice him in whatever he finds in himself of that, and God will suffice him in whatever concerns him. The difference between an omen and a bad omen has already been mentioned in Al-Ma’idah. Indeed, their bad omen is only with God. Al-Hasan read their bad omen, the plural of bad omen, meaning what was decreed for them and against them. But most of them do not know that the famine and hardships that befell them were from God, the Almighty, because of their sins, not from Moses and his people.
7:132: God the Almighty said: And they said, 'Whatever sign you bring us' meaning the people of Pharaoh said to Moses, Whatever. Al-Khalil said: The root is ma, ma, the first is for the condition, and the second is an additional word to emphasize the reward, as it is added to all other letters, such as ima, haytama, aynama, and kayfa. They disliked two letters with the same pronunciation, so they replaced the first alif with a ha and said mahamma. Al-Kisa'i said: Its root is mah, meaning stop, whatever sign you bring us. It was said: It is a single word, which is used as a reward to make what comes after it in the jussive mood, based on the estimation of in. The answer is we are not believers in you. To bewitch us to divert us from what we are doing. The explanation of this word has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. It was said: Moses remained among the Copts after the magicians prostrated for twenty years, showing them signs until God drowned Pharaoh, so this was what they said.
7:133: It has five issues: First: Israel narrated on the authority of Samak on the authority of Nawf al-Shami who said: Moses, peace be upon him, stayed with the people of Pharaoh after he defeated the magicians for forty years. Muhammad bin Uthman bin Abi Shaybah said on the authority of Munjab: Twenty years, showing them signs: locusts, lice, frogs, and blood. Second: The Almighty said: The Flood meaning heavy rain until they drowned in it. Mujahid and Ata’ said: The Flood is death. Al-Akhfash said: Its singular is Tufanah. It was said: It is a source like ar-Rajahan and an-Nasa’an, so no singular is sought for it. An-Nahhas said: The Flood in the language is what is fatal from death or a flood, meaning what surrounds them and destroys them. Al-Suddi said: Not a drop of water reached the Children of Israel, but it entered the homes of the Copts until they stood in the water up to their collarbones, and it lasted for them for seven days. It was said: Forty days. They said: Call upon your Lord to remove it from us so that we may believe in you. So he called upon his Lord and He lifted the flood from them, but they did not believe. So God caused to grow for them in that year what He had not caused to grow before of grass and crops. They said: That water was a blessing. So God sent upon them locusts, which are the well-known animals, the plural of locust in the masculine and feminine. If you wanted to separate the description, you would say, I saw a male locust, and it ate their crops and fruits until it ate the roofs and doors until their homes collapsed. None of it entered the homes of the Children of Israel. Third: Scholars differed about killing locusts if they settle in a land and cause damage. Some said: They should not be killed. All scholars of jurisprudence said: They should be killed. The first argued that it is a great creation of God’s creation that eats from God’s provision and the pen does not write about it. And what was narrated: Do not kill locusts, for they are the greatest soldiers of God. The majority argued that leaving them would lead to the corruption of wealth, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) permitted fighting a Muslim if he wanted to seize his wealth. So if locusts wanted to corrupt wealth, it would be more appropriate to allow killing them. Don’t you see that they agreed that it is permissible to kill snakes and scorpions? Because they harm people, so too do locusts. Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Jabir and Anas ibn Malik that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prayed against locusts, he would say: O God, destroy its adults, kill its children, spoil its eggs, cut off its roots, and seize our livelihoods and provisions by its mouths. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplications. A man said: O Messenger of God, how can you supplicate against one of God’s soldiers to cut off its roots? He said: Locusts are the scatter of fish in the sea. Fourth: It was proven in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, who said: We participated with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) in seven battles, and we used to eat locusts with him. The scholars did not differ about eating it in general, and that if it is taken alive and its head is cut off, it is permissible by consensus. And that it is considered a form of ritual slaughter. Rather, they differed as to whether it needs a reason to die if it is hunted or not. Most of them are of the opinion that it does not need that, and it is eaten however it dies. Its ruling according to them is the ruling on whales, and Ibn Nafi' and Mutraf held this view. Malik held that it must have a reason to die, such as cutting off its head, legs, or wings if it dies from that, or boiling it or throwing it in the fire, because in his view it is a land animal, so its death is forbidden. Al-Layth disliked eating dead locusts, except for what is taken alive and then dies, for it is ritual slaughter. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab held this view. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn 'Umar that the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: Two dead animals are lawful for us: fish and locusts, and the blood of the liver and spleen.” Ibn Majah said: Ahmad ibn Mani’ told us, Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, “On the authority of Abu Sa’id, he heard Anas ibn Malik say: The wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to give each other locusts on plates.” Ibn al-Mundhir also mentioned this. Fifth: Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God the Almighty created a thousand nations, six hundred of them in the sea and four hundred on land. The first destruction of these nations will be the locusts. When the locusts are destroyed, the nations will follow one another like a thread when it breaks.” Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim mentioned this in Nawadir al-Usul and said: The locusts became the first of these nations to be destroyed because they were created from the clay that was left over from the clay of Adam. Nations are destroyed because of the destruction of humans because they are made subservient to them. We return to the story of the Copts - they made a covenant with Moses that they would believe if the locusts were removed from them, so he called and they were removed and some of their crops remained, so they said: What remains is enough for us, and they did not believe, so God sent upon them lice, which are small locusts, said Qatada. The locusts are locusts before they fly, the singular is dabat. And the land is tarred if the locusts eat its plants. Ibn Abbas said: The lice are the weevils that are in the wheat. Ibn Zayd said: The fleas. Al-Hasan said: Small black insects. Abu Ubaidah said: The hamnan, which is a type of tick, the singular of which is hamnanah. So it ate their animals and crops, and stuck to their skins as if it were smallpox on them, and prevented them from sleeping and resting. Habib bin Abi Thabit said: The lice are the dung beetles. And lice, according to the linguists, are a type of monkey. Abu al-Hasan al-A'rabi al-Adawi said: The lice are small insects from the genus of monkeys, except that they are smaller than them, the singular of which is locust. Al-Nahhas said: This does not contradict what the commentators said, because it is possible that all of these things were sent upon them, and that they all combined in that they harmed them. Some commentators mentioned that there was a sand dune in Ain Shams, and Moses struck it with his staff and it became lice. The singular of lice is lumah. It was also said that lice are lice, as stated by Ata’ al-Khurasani. In the reading of al-Hasan and al-Qaml, the qaf is pronounced with a fathah and the mim is silent. So they supplicated, but when it was removed from them, they did not believe, so God sent upon them frogs, the plural of ḍafd’, which is the well-known thing that is found in water. There is one issue in this, which is that the prohibition was reported against killing them. It was narrated by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah with a sound chain of transmission. It was narrated by Abu Dawud on the authority of Ahmad ibn Hanbal on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn Majah on the authority of Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Naysaburi al-Dahli on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the killing of shrikes, frogs, ants, and hoopoes. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Uthman: A doctor mentioned a frog in a medicine for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade him from killing it. Abu Muhammad Abdul Haq authenticated it. Abu Hurairah said: The shrike was the first bird to fast. When Abraham, peace be upon him, went out from Syria to the sanctuary to build the House, the Sakina was with him and the shrike, so the shrike was his guide to the place, and the Sakina was its size. When he reached the spot, the Sakina fell on the place of the House and called out: Build, O Abraham, the size of my shadow. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade killing the shrike because it was Abraham’s guide to the House, and the frog because it used to pour water on Abraham’s fire. When it gained power over Pharaoh, it came and took all the places, and when it reached the oven and settled in it while it was a blazing fire, in obedience to God, God made its croaking a glorification. It is said that it glorifies the most of the animals. Abdullah bin Amr said: Do not kill the frog, for its croaking that you hear is glorification. It was narrated that it filled their bedding, their vessels, their food, and their drink. The man would sit up to his chin among the frogs, and when he spoke, the frog would jump into his mouth. They complained to Moses and said: We repent. So God revealed that to them, but they returned to their disbelief. So God sent blood upon them, and the Nile flowed upon them as blood. The Israelite would scoop up water from it, and the Copt would scoop up blood. The Israelite would pour water into the Copt’s mouth and it would become blood, and the Copt would pour blood into the Israelite’s mouth and it would become clear water. Detailed verses means clear and evident, according to Mujahid. Al-Zajjaj said: Detailed verses is an accusative of state. It is narrated that there were eight days between one verse and the next. It was also said: forty days. It was also said: a month, that is why he said detailed. “Then they were arrogant” means they were too proud to believe in God Almighty.
7:134: The Almighty said: And when the punishment fell upon them meaning the torment. It was read with a damma on the ra', two languages. Ibn Jubayr said: It was a plague that killed seventy thousand Copts in one day. It was said: What is meant by the punishment is what was mentioned previously from the verses. By what He has entrusted to you what means what, meaning by what He has entrusted to you of knowledge, or by what He has chosen for you and informed you. It was said: This is an oath, meaning by His covenant with you except what you pray for us, so what is the connection. If you remove the punishment from us meaning by your prayer to your God until He removes it from us. We will believe in you meaning we will believe in what you have brought. And we will send with you the Children of Israel and they used them, as mentioned above.
7:135: Until a term they will reach meaning the term they were given for drowning. When they break their promise meaning they break what they have pledged to themselves.
7:136: So We took retribution from them and drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them. The sea is the ocean. And they were heedless of them meaning the retribution. So We took retribution indicates it. It was said: about the signs, meaning they did not consider them until they became heedless of them.
7:137: The Almighty said: And We gave inheritance to the people meaning the Children of Israel. Who were oppressed meaning humiliated by service. The easts and wests of the earth Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' claimed that the original form of the easts and wests of the earth was then dropped and the word fi was made accusative. It appears that they inherited the land of the Copts. They are both accusatives as direct objects. It is said: I inherited the money and I made him inherit the money. When the verb is transitive with a hamza, two objects are made accusative. The land is the land of Ash-Sham and Egypt. Its easts and wests are the eastern and western directions of it, so the land is specific, according to Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others. It was said: He meant all of the land, because among the Children of Israel were David and Solomon, and they owned the land. Which We blessed meaning by bringing forth crops, fruits and rivers. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel is His saying: And We intended to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land and make them leaders and make them inheritors (al-Qasas 28:5). Because they were patient meaning, because they were patient in the face of Pharaoh’s harm and in the face of God’s command after they believed in Moses. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had made and what they had built. It is said: Arsh means to build. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: meaning what they had built of palaces and other things. Al-Hasan said: it is the trellise of the grapevine. Ibn Amir and Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim, ya’rshūn with a damma on the ra’. Al-Kisa’i said: it is the language of Tamim. Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubla read ya’rshūn with a shaddah on the ra’ and a damma on the ya’.
7:138: The Almighty said: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people who were devoted to their idols. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it with a kasra on the kaf, and the rest read it with a damma. It is said: ʿakfā yaʿkif and yaʿkif mean to stay on something and stick to it. The source of both is faʿūl. Qatada said: Those people were from Lakhm, and they settled in Ar-Raqqah. It was said: Their idols were statues of cows, and that is why the Samaritan brought out a calf for them. They said, 'O Moses, make for us a god as they have gods.' He said: "Its equivalent is the saying of the ignorant Bedouins when they saw a green tree of the infidels called Dhat Anwat, which they venerated one day every year: O Messenger of God, make for us a Dhat Anwat as they have a Dhat Anwat. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God is the Greatest. You said, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, as the people of Moses said: Make for us a god as they have gods. He said: Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. You will follow the ways of those before you, step by step, to the point that if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it. This was during his journey to Hunayn, as will be explained in Bara’ah, God willing.
7:139: The Almighty said: Indeed, what they are doing will be ruined. That is, destroyed. And ruin means destruction. And every broken vessel will be ruined. And a matter will be ruined. That is, the worshipper and the worshipped will be ruined. And His saying: And in vain means gone and vanished. What they were doing was an additional clause.
7:140: "He said: Shall I seek for you a god other than God?" That is, shall I seek for you a god other than God Almighty. It is said: I sought him and I sought for him. And He has favored you over the worlds that is, over the worlds of your time. It was said: He favored them by destroying their enemy, and by the signs with which He distinguished them.
7:141: He mentioned them as a source. It was said: This is addressed to the Jews of the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. That is, remember when We saved your ancestors, as was explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:142: God Almighty says: And We appointed for Moses thirty nights and completed them with ten, so the term of his Lord was completed as forty nights. There are three issues: First: The Almighty said: And We appointed for Moses thirty nights. He mentioned that among the things with which God honored Moses, peace be upon him, was this. His promise to have intimate conversation was an honor to him. And We completed them with ten. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Masruq, may God be pleased with them, said: They are Dhul-Qa’dah and ten days of Dhul-Hijjah. He ordered him to fast the month and to be alone in worship during it. When he fasted, he found the bad smell from his mouth unpleasant, so he used a toothpick. It was said: With a carob stick. The angels said: We used to smell the scent of musk from your mouth, but you spoiled it with the toothpick. So ten nights of Dhul-Hijjah were added to it. It was said: “God revealed to him when he used a toothpick: O Moses, I will not speak to you until your mouth returns to what it was before. Did you not know that the scent of one who is fasting is more beloved to me than the scent of musk.” And He ordered him to fast ten days. God Almighty spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, on the morning of the sacrifice when he ransomed Ishmael from being slaughtered, and completed the Hajj for Muhammad, peace be upon him. The letter ha’ was deleted from ‘ashar’ because the counted word is feminine. The benefit of his statement: So the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights, is that it is known that thirty and ten are forty, lest it be thought that what is meant is that we completed the thirty with ten of them, so he explained that the ten is more than thirty. If it is said: He said forty in Surat Al-Baqarah and here he said thirty, so would that be from badā’?
