It is said: It is not like that, because he said: And we completed it with ten and forty, and thirty and ten are one statement and not different. Rather, he said the two statements in detail and composition, he said forty in the statement of one author, and he said thirty, meaning a consecutive month and ten. And all of that is forty, as the poet said: Ten and four.... It means fourteen, the night of the full moon. This is permissible in Arabic speech. Second: Our scholars said: This verse indicates that setting a deadline for appointments is an established tradition, and an ancient meaning that God established in matters, and He ruled with it for nations, and He made them aware of the amounts of deliberation in actions. The first deadline that God set was the six days in which He created all creatures, And We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and there touched Us no weariness (Qaf: 38). We have explained its meaning previously in this surah from His statement: Indeed, your Lord is God, Who created the heavens and the earth in six days (al-A’raf 7:54). Ibn Al-Arabi said: If a deadline is set for a reason in which an attempt is made to obtain what is deferred, and the deadline comes and it is not possible, it is increased as an insight and an excuse. God explained this to Moses, peace be upon him, so He set a deadline for him of thirty days, then He increased it by ten to complete forty. Moses, peace be upon him, was slow in these ten days for his people, so they did not understand the permissibility of deliberation and delay until they said: Moses has gone astray or forgotten. They broke his covenant and changed after him, and worshipped a god other than God. Ibn Abbas said: Moses said to his al-Nas 114:My Lord promised me thirty nights that I would meet Him, and He would replace Aaron among you. So when Moses departed to his Lord, God increased him by ten. Their trial was in the ten that God increased by what they did of worshipping the calf, as will be explained. Then the increase that is to the term is determined, just as the term is determined. And it does not happen except by the effort of the ruler after considering the meanings related to the matter: time, condition, and action, so it is like a third of the previous period, just as God granted Moses. If the ruler sees fit to combine the original term and the increase in one period, it is permissible, but it is necessary to wait after that because of the excuse that arises for people, as Ibn al-Arabi said. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: May God excuse a man whose lifespan is delayed until he reaches the age of sixty. I said: This is also the basis for the rulers’ excuses to the one being judged over and over again. This was a kindness to creation, and to enforce the right upon them. It is said: He excused in a matter, meaning he went to extremes in it, meaning he excused the utmost excuse after which there is no excuse. The greatest excuse to the children of Adam is sending messengers to them so that His proof against them would be complete, And We never punish until We have sent a messenger (al-Isra’ 17:15). And He said: And a warner has come to you (Fatir 35:37). It was said: They are the messengers. Ibn Abbas: It is gray hair. Because it comes at the age of maturity, it is a sign of leaving the age of youth. And he made sixty the utmost excuse because sixty is close to the arena of the servants, and it is the age of repentance, humility, and submission to God, and awaiting death and meeting God, so in it there is excuse after excuse. The first is with the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the second is with gray hair, which is when he completes forty, God Almighty said: “And he reached forty years of age. He said, “My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor” (al-Ahqaf 46:15). So God Almighty mentioned that whoever reaches the age of forty, it is time for him to know the extent of God’s blessings upon him and his parents and to be grateful for them. Malik said: I met the people of knowledge in our country, and they would seek the world and mix with people until one of them reached the age of forty, and when that age came upon them, they would isolate themselves from people. Third: The verse also indicates that the date is calculated by nights, not days, as God the Almighty says: thirty nights because the nights are the beginnings of the months. And this is how the Companions, may God be pleased with them, used to tell about the days, until it was narrated that she used to say: We fasted five with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The non-Arabs differ in this, and they calculate by days because they rely on the sun. Ibn al-Arabi: The calculation of the sun is for benefits, and the calculation of the moon is for rituals, and for this reason he said: And We appointed for Moses thirty nights. So it is said: I dated a date and I dated a date; two languages. God Almighty said: And Moses said to his brother Aaron, ‘Take my place among my people and do good.’ The meaning is: When Moses wanted to go on to the intimate conversation and be absent from it, he said to his brother Aaron: Be my successor. This indicates representation. In Sahih Muslim, “On the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say to Ali when he took his place in one of his campaigns: Are you not satisfied to be to me as Aaron was to Moses, except that there is no prophet after me?” The Rafidis, the Imamis, and all the Shiite sects used this as evidence that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed Ali as his successor over the entire nation, to the point that the Imami Companions - may God curse them - were considered infidels because they abandoned the action that is the text on appointing Ali as his successor and appointed someone else as his successor based on their own ijtihad. Some of them considered Ali an infidel because he did not demand his right. There is no doubt about the infidelity of these people and the infidelity of those who followed them in their statement, and they did not know that this was an appointment during life like the agency that ends with the dismissal of the principal or his death, and it does not require that it continues after his death, so what the Imamis and others have relied on is invalidated on this. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, appointed Ibn Umm Maktum and others as his successors in Medina, but this does not necessarily mean that he would always be his successor by consensus. However, Aaron was a partner with Moses in the original message, so they would not have any evidence for what they sought in him. And God is the guide to success. The Almighty’s saying: And reform is an order to reform. Ibn Jurayj said: It was part of reform to rebuke the Samaritan and attack him. It was also said: That is, be gentle with them, reform their affairs, and reform yourself, that is, be a reformer. And do not follow the way of the corrupters that is, do not take the way of the disobedient, and do not be an aid to the oppressors.
7:143: God the Almighty said: And when Moses came to Our appointed time meaning at the promised time. And his Lord spoke to him meaning He made him hear His words without an intermediary. He said, 'My Lord, show me, that I may look at You' He asked to look at Him, and he longed to see Him because He made him hear His words. In it, He said, 'You will never see Me' meaning in this world. It is not permissible to interpret it as meaning: Show me a great sign so that I may look at Your power, because He said to You and He said, 'You will never see Me'. If he had asked for a sign, God would have given him what he asked for, just as He gave him all the other signs. In it, Moses, peace be upon him, had enough to dissuade him from asking for another sign, so this interpretation is invalidated. But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me He gave it an example of something stronger than its structure and more stable. Meaning, if the mountain remains stable and still, then you will see Me, and if it does not remain still, then you will not be able to see Me, just as the mountain cannot be able to see Me. Judge Iyad mentioned on the authority of Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Tayyib what means: Moses, peace be upon him, saw God, and for that reason he fell unconscious. And that the mountain saw its Lord and became leveled by the perception of God’s creation of it. And he derived that from His saying: But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place, then you will see Me. Then He said: But when his Lord revealed Himself to the mountain, He made it level, and Moses fell unconscious. The meaning of manifested is appeared, from your saying: I exposed the bride, meaning you brought her out. And I exposed the sword means you brought it out from rust, polishing in both. And the thing became clear: it was revealed. And it was said: His command and power became clear, as stated by Qatrub and others. And the reading of the people of Medina and Basra is dakan, which indicates its correctness the earth was pounded to dust (al-Fajr 89:21) and that the mountain is masculine. The people of Kufa read dakka, meaning He made it like the ground of daka’, which is the protruding ground that does not reach the level of being a mountain. The masculine is adak, and the plural of dakka’at is dakkawat and dakka, like hamrawat and hamr. Al-Kisa’i said: Dakka of mountains means the wide, and its singular is adak. Other: Al-Dakawat is the plural of Dakaa: mounds of clay that are not very thick. Al-Dakadak is also from sand: what is scattered on the ground but does not rise. A she-camel that has no hump. In the interpretation: The mountain sank into the ground, and it continues to sink into it until now. Ibn Abbas said: He made it dust. Atiyah Al-Awfi: Huge sand. And Moses fell unconscious meaning unconscious, according to Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan and Qatada. It was said: dead, the man was unconscious, so he was unconscious. And he was unconscious, so he was unconscious. Qatada and Al-Kalbi said: Moses fell unconscious on Thursday, the Day of Arafah, and he was given the Torah on Friday, the Day of Sacrifice. And when he regained consciousness, he said, ‘Glory be to You! I repent to You.’ Mujahid said: From the issue of seeing Him in this world. It was said: He asked without permission, and that is why he repented. It was said: He said it as a way of turning to God and humbling himself before Him when the signs appear. The nation agreed that this repentance was not for a sin, because the prophets are infallible. Also, according to the Sunnis, seeing God is permissible. According to the innovators, he asked for the sake of the people to show them that it is not permissible. This does not require repentance. It was said: I repent to You for killing the Copt, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri. It was previously stated in Al-An’am that seeing God is permissible. Ali bin Mahdi Al-Tabari said: If Moses’ question was impossible, he would not have done it despite his knowledge of God, just as it was not permissible for him to say to Him, ‘O Lord, do you have a wife and children?’ The Mu’tazilite doctrine and the response to them will come in the Day of Judgment, God willing. The Almighty said: And I am the first of the believers. It was said: From my people. It was said: From the Children of Israel in this era. It was said: That you will not see in this world because of your previous promise in that. And in the authentic hadith from the hadith of Abu Hurairah and others, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not choose between the prophets, for people will be struck dumb on the Day of Resurrection. I will raise my head and see Moses holding one of the pillars of the Throne. I do not know whether he was struck dumb among those who were struck dumb and then regained consciousness before me, or whether he was held accountable in the first instance.” Or he said, His first strike sufficed him. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Ka’b, who said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, divided His speech and vision between Muhammad and Moses, may God bless them both, so Moses spoke to Him twice, and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Him twice.
7:144: The Almighty said: He said, 'O Moses, indeed I have chosen you over mankind with My messages and with My speech.' Selection means choosing, meaning I have favored you. He did not say over creation, because part of this selection is that He spoke to him and He spoke to the angels, and sent him and sent others. So what is meant is over the people to whom He was sent. Nafi' and Ibn Kathir read with my message in the singular. The rest read it in the plural. The message is a source, so it is permissible to make it singular. And whoever pluralizes it on the basis that he was sent with different types of messages, then he pluralizes the source because of the different types, as he said: Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys. (Luqman 31:19). So he pluralized it because of the different types of sounds and the different voicers. He made the singular in his statement of a voice because he meant by it one type of sounds. This indicates that his people did not share in speaking with him, not even one of the seventy, as we explained in Al-Baqarah. The Almighty said: Then take what I have given you referring to contentment, meaning be content with what I have given you. And be among the grateful meaning among those who show My kindness and favor to you. It is said: A grateful animal if it has fat on it in addition to the fodder it is given. And the grateful person is willing to receive more, as He said: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you (Ibrahim 14:7). It is narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, remained for forty nights after God Almighty spoke to him, and no one saw him except that he died from the light of God Almighty.
7:145: The Almighty said: And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things meaning the Torah. It was narrated in the hadith that Gabriel, peace be upon him, seized him with his wing and passed him in the heights until he brought him close until he heard the creaking of the pen when God wrote the tablets for him, mentioned by Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim. Mujahid said: The tablets were of green emerald. Ibn Jubayr: Of red ruby. Abu Al-Aaliyah: Of chrysolite. Al-Hasan: Of wood, descended from the sky. It was said: From a solid rock, which God softened for Moses, peace be upon him, so he cut it with his hand and then split it with his fingers, so it obeyed him like iron for David. Muqatil said: That is, We wrote for him on the tablets like the engraving of a ring: Al-Rabi' bin Anas: The Torah was revealed and it was seventy camel loads. He added the writing to himself as an honor, since it was written by his command, Gabriel wrote it with the pen with which he wrote the remembrance. And he drew from the River of Light. It was said: It is a writing that God revealed and created on the tablets. The root of the word lawh is lawh with the first letter lām open. God the Almighty said: Rather, it is a glorious Qur’an, in a Preserved Tablet (al-Buruj 85:21-22). It is as if the meanings are revealed in the tablet. It is narrated that it is two tablets, and the plural is used because two is a plural. It is said: A man with great tablets is one whose hands and feet are large. Ibn Abbas said: The tablets were broken when he threw them down, and they were lifted up except for a sixth of them. It was also said: A seventh of them remained, and six sevenths of them were lifted up. So in what was lifted were the details of everything, and in what remained were guidance and mercy. Abu Na’im Al-Hafiz narrated: “On the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I was informed that Moses ibn Imran, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fasted for forty nights. When he threw down the tablets, they were broken, so he fasted the same number of nights, and they were returned to him.” The meaning of from everything is that which he needs in his religion of rulings and clarifying what is permissible and forbidden, on the authority of Al-Thawri and others. It was also said: It is a word that is mentioned for emphasis and is not intended to be general. You say: I went to the market and bought everything. So-and-so has everything. Destroy everything (al-Ahqaf 46:25). And you have been given of everything (al-Naml 27:23). It has been mentioned before. An admonition and a detailed explanation of everything meaning for everything they were commanded to do of the rulings, for they did not have any independent reasoning, but rather this was specific to the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Take it with strength is an omission in the speech, meaning so we said to him: Take it with strength, meaning with diligence and energy. Similar to Take what We have given you with strength has been mentioned before. And command your people to take the best of it meaning to act upon the commands and leave the prohibitions, and to ponder the examples and admonitions. Similar to And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord (al-Zumar 39:55). And He said: And they will follow the best of it (al-Zumar 39:18). Forgiveness is better than retaliation. Patience is better than victory. It has been said: The best of it is the obligatory and voluntary acts, and the least of it is the permissible. I will show you the abode of the wicked. Al-Kalbi said: The abode of the wicked is what they passed by when they traveled from the dwellings of Aad and Thamud, and the generations that were destroyed. It was said: It is Hell, according to Al-Hasan and Mujahid. That is, let it be of remembrance to you, so beware of being among them. It was also said: He meant Egypt by it, that is, I will show you the dwellings of the Copts and the dwellings of Pharaoh, empty of them, according to Ibn Jubayr. Qatada: The meaning is I will show you the dwellings of the infidels who inhabited them before you, from the tyrants and giants, so that you may take heed from them, meaning the Levant. These two statements are indicated by And We gave inheritance to the people (al-A’raf 7:137) the verse. And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land (al-Qasas 28:5) the verse, and it has been mentioned previously. Ibn Abbas and Qasama bin Zuhair read: I will give you inheritance from those who inherited. This is clear. It was also said: The abode is destruction, and its plural is adwar. This is because when God Almighty drowned Pharaoh, He inspired the sea to throw their bodies onto the shore. He said: So it did. Then the Children of Israel looked at them and saw the destruction of the wicked.
7:146: The Almighty said: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right. Qatada said: I will prevent them from understanding My Book. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said the same. It was also said: I will turn them away from believing in it. It was also said: I will turn them away from benefiting from it, and that is a punishment for their arrogance. Similar to it is: But when they deviated, God caused their hearts to deviate. (al-Saff 61:5). The signs are based on these miracles or revealed books. It was also said: The creation of the heavens and the earth. That is, He turned them away from considering them. They are arrogant they see that they are the best of creation. This is a false assumption, that is why He said: without right so they do not follow a prophet nor listen to him because of their arrogance. God the Almighty said: “And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. And if they see the path of right guidance, they will not take it as a way. And if they see the path of error, they will take it as a way.” He means these arrogant ones. He informed about them that they abandon the path of right guidance and follow the path of error and misguidance, i.e. disbelief, they take it as a religion. Then He gave a reason by saying: That is because they denied Our signs, i.e. that action which I did to them by denying them. And they were heedless of them, i.e. they were in their abandonment of contemplating the truth like the heedless. It is possible that they were heedless of what they were being punished for, as it is said: So-and-so did not neglect what was intended for him. Malik bin Dinar read and if they see with a damma on the ya’ in both letters, meaning that is done to them. The people of Medina and Basra read the path of right guidance with a damma on the ra’ and a sukoon on the sheen. The people of Kufa, except for Asim, read right guidance with a fatha on the ra’ and the sheen. Abu Ubaid said: Abu Amr differentiated between right guidance and right guidance, saying: Right guidance is in righteousness, and right guidance is in religion. An-Nahhas said: Sibawayh believes that rashd and rashd are like sakht and ghath, and Al-Kisa’i said the same. The correct version from Abu Amr is different from what Abu Ubaid said. Ismail bin Ishaq said: Nasr bin Ali told us from his father from Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ who said: If rashd is in the middle of the verse, then it is a sukun, and if it is at the beginning of the verse, then it is a sukun. An-Nahhas said: He means by the beginning of the verse something like And prepare for us from our affair right guidance (al-Kahf 18:10). So in his view they are two languages with the same meaning, except that he opened this to make the verses agree. It is said: rashd yurshid, and rashd yurshid. Sibawayh narrated rashd yurshid. The true meaning of rashd and rashd in the language is that a person gets what he wants. It is the opposite of disappointment.
7:147: God Almighty says: “And those who deny Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter - their deeds have become worthless. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?”
7:148: The Almighty said: And the people of Moses took after him meaning after his exit to the Mount. Of their ornaments This is the reading of the people of Medina and Basra. The people of Kufa except for Asim read of their ornaments with a kasra on the hal. Yaqub read of their ornaments with a fatha on the ha and a light tafsir. An-Nahhas said: The plural of halli is halli and halli, like thadi and thadi and thadi. The original is halawi, then the waw was assimilated into the ya and the lam was kasra because of its proximity to the ya, and the ha was kasra because of the kasra of the lam. And its damma is according to the original. Ajlan is a passive participle. Jasdan is an adjective or a substitute. Lahu khawar is raised by the beginning. It is said: khaar yakhwar khawaran if he shouted. Likewise, jaar yajar jawaran. It is also said: khawar yakhwar khawaran if he became cowardly and weak. It was narrated in the stories of the calf: that the Samaritan, whose name is Musa bin Thafar, is attributed to a village called Samarra. He was born in the year of the killing of the sons, and his mother hid him in a mountain cave. Gabriel fed him and recognized him for that, so when he crossed the sea on a narrow horse to precede Pharaoh in the sea, he took a handful from the footprint of the horse’s hoof. This is the meaning of His saying, So I took a handful from the footprint of the Messenger (Ta-Ha 20:96). Moses had promised his people thirty days, but when he was delayed in the extra ten days and thirty nights had passed, he said to the Children of Israel, and he was obeyed by them: You have with you jewelry from the jewelry of the people of Pharaoh, and they had a festival in which they adorned themselves and borrowed jewelry from the Copts, so they borrowed it for that day. When God brought them out of Egypt and the Copts were drowned, that jewelry remained in their hands, so the Samaritan said to them: It is forbidden for you, so bring what you have and we will burn it. It was said: This jewelry is what the Children of Israel took from the people of Pharaoh after the drowning, and that Aaron said to them: The jewelry is spoils, and it is not permissible for you, so he gathered it in a hole he dug and the Samaritan took it. It was said: They borrowed the jewelry on the night they wanted to leave Egypt, and they made the Copts think that they were having a wedding or a gathering. The Samaritan heard their saying, Make for us a god as they have gods (al-A’raf 7:138). Those gods were in the form of cows, so he fashioned for them a calf with a body, that is, solid, but they heard it mooing. It was also said: God turned it into flesh and blood. It was also said: When he threw that handful of dirt into the fire on the jewelry, it became a calf that mooed. It mooed once and did not repeat, then it said to the people, This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot (Ta-Ha 20:88) meaning: He forgot it here and went looking for it, which was left over from him - so let us remove this calf. Then God said to Moses while He was speaking to him, Indeed, We have tried your people after you, and the Samaritan has led them astray (Ta-Ha 20:85). Moses said: O Lord, this Samaritan brought out for them a calf from their jewelry, so who gave it a body? - He wants flesh and blood - and who made it bellow? God the Almighty said: I. He said: By Your glory and majesty, none led them astray except You. He said: You have spoken the truth, O Wise of the wise. This is the meaning of His saying: It is nothing but your trial (al-A’raf 7:155). Al-Qaffal said: The Samaritan had a trick by taking the calf’s belly and facing it towards the wind, until something like a bellow came from it, and he made them think that it only happened like that because of the dust that he had taken from the feet of Gabriel’s horse that was thrown into the body. This is a statement that is incoherent, as Al-Qushayri said. The Almighty said: Have they not seen that He does not speak to them? He explained that the worshipped one must be described as speaking. Nor does He guide them to a way meaning a path to an argument. They took him meaning a god. And they were wrongdoers meaning to themselves in what they did in taking him. It was said: And they became wrongdoers meaning polytheists because they made the calf a god.
7:149: God the Almighty said: And when it fell into their hands meaning after Moses returned from the appointed time. It is said of the regretful and confused person: it fell into his hand. Al-Akhfash said, it is said it fell into his hand, and he dropped. And whoever said: it fell into their hands according to the active participle, then the meaning according to him is: regret fell, as said by Al-Azhari, Al-Nahhas and others. Regret is in the heart, but he mentioned the hand because it is said to someone who has obtained something: such-and-such has fallen into his hand, because doing things is usually done by hand, God the Almighty said: That is because of what your hands have put forth (al-Hajj 22:10). Also: Regret, even if it settles in the heart, its effect appears in the body, because the regretful person bites his hand, and strikes one hand against the other, God the Almighty said: So he began to wring his hands over what he had spent on it (al-Kahf 18:42) meaning regret. And the Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands (al-Furqan 25:27) meaning from regret. The regretful person puts his chin in his hand. It was said: Its origin is from captivity, which is that a man strikes a man or wrestles him down, then throws him from his hands to the ground to capture him or tie him up, so the one who is thrown falls into the hand of the one who falls. And they saw that they had gone astray, meaning that they had turned back by disobeying God. They said, ‘If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.’ They began to acknowledge servitude and seek forgiveness. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers. With the ta’ of addressing, it has the meaning of seeking help, supplication, and entreaty in asking and praying. Our Lord is in the accusative case, deleting the vocative. It is also more expressive in supplication and submission. Their reading is more expressive in submission and humility, so it is more appropriate.
7:150: The Almighty said: And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. Ghadhban was not declined because its feminine form is ghadaban, and because the alif and nun in it are like the alifs of femininity in the word hamra'a. It is accusative as a state. And sadly is very angry. Abu Darda' said: Sadness is more severe than anger. It is asf and asif and asfan and asoof. Asif is also the sad. Ibn Abbas and As-Suddi: He returned sad because of what his people did. Al-Tabari said: God the Almighty informed him before his return that they had been tempted by the calf, so he returned angry. Ibn Al-Arabi: Moses, peace be upon him, was one of the angriest people, but he was quick to calm down, so this is like that. Ibn Al-Qasim said: I heard Malik say: When Moses, peace be upon him, became angry, smoke would rise from his skullcap, and the hair of his body would lift his cloak. This is because anger is a burning ember in the heart. Because of this, the Prophet, peace be upon him, ordered the one who became angry to lie down. If his anger does not go away, he should perform ablution: lying down will quench it and bathing will put it out. His quick anger was the reason why the Angel of Death struck him and put out his eye. The scholars have already mentioned in Al-Ma’idah what they said about this. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim said: Moses, peace be upon him, only permitted this because he was the one who spoke to God, as if he saw that whoever dared to harm him or extended a hand to him, then the matter was grave. Do you not see that he argued with him and said: From where will you extract my soul? From my mouth, when I have spoken to my Lord in private with it? Or from my hearing, when I have heard the words of my Lord with it? Or from my hand, when I have grasped the tablets from it? Or from my feet, when I stood before Him and spoke to Him at the Mount? Or from my eyes, when my face had shone with its light. So he returned to his Lord humiliated. In Musannaf Abi Dawud, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: If one of you becomes angry while standing, let him sit down. If the anger goes away, then fine. Otherwise, let him lie down.” It was also narrated on the authority of Abu Wa’il al-Qass, who said: We entered upon Urwah ibn Muhammad al-Sa’di and a man spoke to him and made him angry. He stood up and then returned after performing ablution. He said: My father told me on the authority of my grandfather Atiyah, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Anger comes from Satan, and Satan was created from fire. Fire is extinguished only with water, so if one of you becomes angry, let him perform ablution. God the Almighty said: How evil is that which you have succeeded me after me. This is a reproach from Him to them, meaning how evil is the deed you have done after me. It is said: He succeeded him, with what he dislikes. It is also said about good. It is said: He succeeded him with good or evil for his family and people after his departure. You hastened the command of your Lord meaning you preceded Him. Haste means doing something before its time, and it is reprehensible. Speed means doing something at its first time, and it is praiseworthy. Yaqub said: It is said: I hastened something, I preceded it. And I hastened a man, I made him hasten, meaning I made him hasten. The meaning of the command of your Lord is the appointment of your Lord, meaning the promise of forty nights. And it was said: You hastened the wrath of your Lord. And it was said: You hastened to worship the calf before the command of your Lord came to you. The Almighty’s saying: And he threw down the tablets has two issues: First: The Almighty said: And he threw down the tablets meaning because of the anger and sorrow that overcame him when he saw his people worshipping the calf, and because of his brother neglecting their matter, Saeed bin Jubair said. This is why it was said: Reporting is not like seeing it. Nor should we pay attention to what was narrated from Qatadah if it is authentic from him. It is not authentic: that his throwing down the tablets was only because he saw in them the virtue of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that was not for his nation. This is a bad statement that should not be attributed to Moses, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was previously narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, that the tablets were broken, and that the details were removed from them, but guidance and mercy remained in them. Second: Some ignorant Sufis have used this as evidence for the permissibility of throwing clothes if they are very excited by the music. Some of them throw them whole, and some tear them and then throw them away. He said: These people are in a state of occultation and are not to be blamed. When Moses, peace be upon him, was overcome by grief over his people worshipping the calf, he threw the tablets and broke them, and he did not know what he did. Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: Who can confirm that Moses, peace be upon him, threw them like a breaker? And what is mentioned in the Qur’an is that he threw them, so how do we know that they broke? Then if it is said: They broke, then how do we know that he intended to break them? Then if we confirm that about him, we would say that he was in a state of occultation, so that if there was a sea of fire in front of him, he would have waded into it. And who can confirm that these people are in a state of occultation when they know the music from other things, and they are wary of a well if they had one? Then how can the conditions of the prophets be compared to the conditions of these fools? Ibn Aqil was asked about their presence and the tearing of their clothes. He said: It is wrong and forbidden. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the wasting of money. Someone said to him: They do not understand what they are doing. He said: If they attend these places knowing that the ecstasy will overcome them and take away their minds, they have sinned by what they have brought upon themselves of tearing and other things that they have corrupted. The address of the Shari’ah does not fall from them, because they were addressed before their presence to avoid this place that leads to that. Just as they are forbidden from drinking intoxicants, so is this ecstasy that the Sufis call ecstasy. If they believe that it contains intoxication by nature, and if they lie, they have corrupted themselves while being sober, so there is no safety in it in either case. Avoiding suspicious places is obligatory. God Almighty says: And he seized his brother by the head, dragging him towards him, meaning by his beard and forelock. Aaron was three years older than Moses - may God’s prayers and peace be upon them both - and more beloved to the Children of Israel than Moses, because he was soft-tempered. Scholars have four interpretations of Moses taking his brother’s head: First: That was common among them, as the Arabs used to do when a man would grab the beard of his brother or friend as an act of respect and greatness, so it was not done as a way of humiliation. Second: That was only to make the revelation of the tablets secret to him, because they were revealed to him in this intimate conversation and he wanted to hide them from the Children of Israel before the Torah. So Aaron said to him: Do not seize my beard or my head, lest his secret be confused with the Children of Israel by his humiliation. Third: He did that to him because it occurred to him that Aaron was inclined towards the Children of Israel in what they did regarding the matter of the calf. And something like this is not permissible for the prophets. Fourth: He brought his brother to him to know what he had, but Aaron hated that lest the Children of Israel think that he had humiliated him. His brother explained to him that they had weakened him, meaning the worshippers of the calf, and they almost killed him, i.e. they came close. So when he heard his excuse, he said, My Lord, forgive me and my brother, meaning forgive me for the anger for which the tablets were thrown, and my brother because he thought he had fallen short in denouncing them even though he had not fallen short, i.e. forgive my brother if he had fallen short. Al-Hasan said: All of them worshipped the calf except Aaron, because if there had been a believer other than Moses and Aaron, he would not have limited himself to saying, My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and he would have prayed for that believer as well. It was said: He asked forgiveness for himself for what he did to his brother, he did that out of his resentment towards him, because he did not catch up with him and inform him of what had happened so that he could return and make amends with them. For this reason, he said, O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following them? (Ta-Ha: 92-93) the verse. Aaron explained that he only stayed there for fear of being killed. The verse indicates that whoever fears being killed when changing an evil should remain silent. This has been explained previously in Al Imran. Ibn al-Arabi: This is evidence that anger does not change rulings as some people have claimed. Moses’ anger did not change any of his actions, but rather they continued in their course, from throwing down the tablet, to rebuking his brother, and issuing a royal decree. Al-Mahdawi: Because his anger was for the sake of God, the Almighty, and his silence about the Children of Israel was out of fear that they would fight and disperse. God the Almighty said: He said, ‘Ibn Umm’ and he was the son of his mother and father. But it is a word of softness and sympathy. Al-Zajjaj said: It was said that Aaron was the brother of Moses from his mother, not from his father. It was read with the fatha on the meem and with the kasra. Whoever read it with the fatha made Ibn Umm a single name like Khamsin five, so it became like saying: O fifteen, come. Whoever read it with the kasra on the meem made it an addition to the pronoun of the speaker, then deleted the ya of addition, because the structure of the vocative is based on deletion, and the kasra was kept in the meem to indicate addition, like his saying: O servants (al-Zumar 39:10). It indicates the reading of Ibn Al-Sumaiqa’ Ya Ibn Ummi by proving the ya according to the original. Al-Kisa’i, Al-Farra’ and Abu Ubaid said: Ya Ibn Umm with the fatha, meaning Ya Ibn Ummah. The Basrans said: This statement is wrong, because the alif is light and is not deleted, but the two names were made a single name. Al-Akhfash and Abu Hatim said: Ya Ibn Umm with the kasra as you say: Ya Ghalam Ghalam Aqbil, and it is an irregular language and reading it with it is far-fetched. This is only in what is added to you. As for what is added to what is added to you, the correct way is to say: Ya boy, my boy, and Ya son of my brother. They allowed Ya son of mother, Ya son of uncle, because of its frequency in speech. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Nahhas said: But it has a good and beautiful way, which makes the son with the mother and the uncle one name, like you say: O fifteen, come, so the Ya was deleted as it was deleted from Ya boy. Indeed the people are weakening me They humiliated me and considered me weak. And they almost means they came close. They are killing me with two Noons, because it is a future verb. Assimilation is permissible in places other than the Qur’an. So do not rejoice over me, my enemies means do not make them happy. And rejoicing is the pleasure of what befalls your brother of calamities in religion and the world. It is forbidden and prohibited. In the hadith, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not gloat over your brother, lest God cure him and test you.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek refuge from it and say: O God, I seek refuge in You from evil judgment, the attainment of misery, and the gloating of enemies.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and others. The poet said: If time brings its scourge upon some people, it will bring down its scourge upon the rest of us. So tell those who gloat over us to wake up. Those who gloat will meet what we met. Mujahid and Malik ibn Dinar read tashamtuhu with the accusative in the ta’ and the fatha on the meem, the enemies in the nominative. The meaning is: Do not do to me what the enemies rejoice over, i.e. do not do that to them because of an action that you do to me. Mujahid also said tashamtuhu with the fatha on both of them, the enemies in the accusative. Ibn Jinni said: The meaning is: Do not rejoice over me, O Lord. This is permissible as he said: God mocks them (al-Baqarah 2:15) and similar to it. Then he returned to the intended meaning and implied a verb with which he made the enemies accusative, as if he said: Do not rejoice over me, the enemies. Abu Ubaid said: It was narrated from Humayd: Do not rejoice over me with the kasra on the meem. An-Nahhas said: There is no basis for this reading, because if it is from shamtuhu, then it is necessary to say tashamtuhu. And if it is from ashmat, then it is necessary to say tashamtuhu. And his statement: And do not place me with the wrongdoing people, Mujahid said: He means those who worshipped the calf.
7:151: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.' Go forward.
7:152: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who took the calf - upon them will be overtaken by wrath from their Lord wrath from God is punishment. And humiliation in the life of this world because they were ordered to kill each other. It was said: humiliation is the jizya. And there is some distance in it, because the jizya was not taken from them, but rather from their descendants. Then it was said: This is from the completion of the words of Moses, peace be upon him, God Almighty informed about it from him, and the speech was complete. Then God Almighty said: And thus do We recompense the slanderers. This statement was from Moses, peace be upon him, before the people repented by killing themselves, for when they repented and God forgave them after the great killing had occurred - as was explained previously in Al-Baqarah - He informed them that whoever among them died as a martyr is a martyr, and whoever remained alive is forgiven. It was said: There was a group who had imbibed the calf in their hearts, meaning its love, and they did not repent, so they are the ones meant by His saying: Indeed, those who took the calf. It was said that he meant those among them who died before Moses returned from the appointed time. It was said: He meant their children. This is what happened to Qurayzah and Nadir, meaning their children will be affected. And God knows best. And thus do We recompense the innovators meaning as We did to these, We will do to the innovators. Malik bin Anas, may God have mercy on him, said: There is no innovator except that you will find humiliation on his head, then he recited: Indeed, those who took the calf - wrath from their Lord will overtake them - until he said - And thus do We recompense the innovators meaning the innovators. It was said: Moses ordered the slaughter of the calf, so blood flowed from it and he cooled it with a cooler and threw it with the blood into the sea and ordered them to drink from that water, so whoever worshipped that calf and drank it, it appeared on the edges of his mouth, and by that the worshippers of the calf were known. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, then God the Most High informed us that God accepts the repentance of the one who repents from polytheism and other things. This has already been mentioned in more than one place.
7:153: And those who have committed evil deeds meaning disbelief and sins. Then repented after that meaning after committing them. And believed - indeed, your Lord, after that meaning after repentance, is Forgiving and Merciful.
7:154: The Almighty said: And when Moses' anger subsided meaning it calmed down. Muawiyah bin Qurra read it this way, with a sukun with a noon. The root of sukun is stillness and abstinence. It is said: The valley flowed three times then calmed down, meaning it stopped flowing. Ikrimah said: Moses was still from his anger, so it is from the inverted. Like you say: I put my finger in the ring, and I put the ring in the finger. And I put the cap on my head, and I put my head in the cap. He took the tablets that he threw down. And in its copy is guidance and mercy meaning guidance from misguidance, and mercy, meaning from torment. Abrogation is the transfer of what is in a book to another book. The original from which it was written is called a copy, and the branch is called a copy. It was said: When the tablets were broken, Moses fasted for forty days, then they were returned to him and those tablets were given back to him in two tablets, and he did not lose anything from them, as mentioned by Ibn Abbas. Al-Qushayri said: According to this, and in its copy means in what was copied from the broken tablets and transferred to the new tablets, guidance and mercy. Ata’ said: And in what remained of it. That is because only a seventh of it remained, and six-sevenths of it were lost. However, nothing of the limits and rulings was lost. It was said: The meaning is in its copy, meaning in what was copied for him from the Preserved Tablet, guidance. It was said: The meaning is in what was written for him in it, guidance and mercy, so there is no need for an original to be copied from. This is like saying: Copy what so-and-so says, meaning write it down in your book. God the Almighty said: For those who fear their Lord meaning they are afraid. There are three opinions about the lam: The Kufians say that it is redundant. Al-Kisa’i said: Someone who heard Al-Farazdaq say: I paid her a hundred dirhams, meaning I paid them. It was also said: It is a lam of ajal, meaning: And those who fear their Lord, not for show or reputation, from Al-Akhfash. Muhammad bin Yazid said: It is related to a source, meaning: For those whose fear is for their Lord. It was also said: When the object came before, it was good to include the lam, like His statement: If you interpret dreams (Yusuf 12:43). When the object came before, which is the object, the action of the verb was weakened and it became like an intransitive verb.
7:155: The Almighty’s saying: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time. Two objects, one of which has min deleted, and Sibawayh recited: Among us are those who were chosen as men of generosity and righteousness when the stormy winds blow. The shepherd said, praising a man: People chose you when their character was ruined and those who had hope in you were disillusioned. He wants: I chose you from among people. The root of I chose is I chose, but when the ya moved and before it was a fatha, it was changed to an alif, like said and ba’a. God Almighty says: So when the earthquake seized them meaning they died. In the language, earthquake means a severe earthquake. It is narrated that they were shaken until they died. God the Almighty said: “He said: ‘My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and me’” meaning, their nation, as God the Almighty said: If a man were to perish (An-Nisa’: 176). And and me is an appositive. The meaning is: If You had willed, You could have destroyed us before we went out to the appointed time in the presence of the Children of Israel so that they would not accuse me. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah: Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan narrated to us from Sufyan from Abu Ishaq from Ammarah bin Abd from Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Moses and Aaron, peace be upon them, set out, and Shibr and Shabir - they are the sons of Aaron - set out, and they came to a mountain in which there was a bed, and Aaron stood on it and took his soul. Moses returned to his people, and they said: You killed him, you envied us for his gentleness and his character, or a word to that effect. The doubt was from Sufyan, so he said: How can I kill him when I have his two sons with me! He said: Then choose whomever you wish, and they chose ten from each tribe. He said: That is what He said: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointed time. So they came to him and said: Who killed you, O Aaron? He said: No one killed me, but God caused me to die. They said: O Moses, you do not disobey. So the earthquake seized them, and they went back and forth to the right and to the left, and he said: “If You had willed, You could have destroyed them and me before. Will You destroy us for what the fools among us have done? This is nothing but Your trial.” He said: So he called upon God, and He revived them and made them all prophets. It was said: The earthquake seized them because they said: Show us God openly, as God the Most High said: And when you said, ‘O Moses, we will not believe in you until we see God openly,’ then the thunderbolt seized you. (al-Baqarah 2:55) As explained previously in Al-Baqarah. Ibn Abbas said: The earthquake seized them because they did not stop worshipping the calf, and were not satisfied with worshipping it. It was said: These seventy are not the ones who said: Show us God openly. Wahb said: They did not die, but the trembling took them from awe until their joints were almost revealed, and Moses feared death for them. It was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah on the authority of Wahb that they died in a day and a night. Other than this was said about the meaning of the reason for the trembling. And God knows best about the correctness of that. The intended question in His statement: Will denial destroy us? means that you will not do that. This is common in the speech of the Arabs. And if it is a negation, it has the meaning of an affirmation, as he said: Aren't you the best of those who ride mounts and the most generous of the worlds in terms of bellies? It was said: Its meaning is supplication and request, i.e. do not destroy us, and he added to himself. What is meant are the people who died from the earthquake. Al-Mubarrad said: What is meant is a question of greatness, as if he is saying: do not destroy us, and Moses knew that God does not destroy anyone for the sin of someone other than him, but it is like the saying of Jesus: If You punish them, they are Your servants (al-Ma’idah 5:118). It was said: What is meant by the seventy fools. The meaning is: Will You destroy the Children of Israel for what these fools did in their saying: Show us God openly? “It is only your trial” meaning this is nothing but your test and examination. And he added the trial to God Almighty and did not add it to himself, as Abraham said: And when I am ill, it is He who cures me (Ash-Shu’ara’: 80), so he added the illness to himself and the healing to God Almighty. And Joshua said: And none made him forget except Satan (al-Kahf 18:63). Moses, peace be upon him, benefited from the Almighty’s saying to him: Indeed, We have tried your people after you (Ta-Ha 20:85). So when he returned to his people and saw the calf set up for worship and it was lowing, he said: It is only your trial by which you mislead meaning by the trial. Whom You will and guide whom You will. This is a refutation of the Qadarites.
7:156: The Almighty said: And decree for us in this world [that which is] good. That is, guide us to righteous deeds for which good deeds will be decreed for us. And in the Hereafter, that is, a reward for them. Indeed, we have been guided to You, that is, we have repented, as stated by Mujahid, Abu al-Aaliyah, and Qatadah. And guidance means repentance, and it was mentioned previously in Surat al-Baqarah. God Almighty said: He said, ‘My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will’ meaning those who deserve it. That is, this tremor and thunderbolt is a punishment from Me that I afflict with whom I will. It was said: The meaning is, whoever I will, meaning, whoever I will to misguide. His saying: And My mercy encompasses all things is general, meaning it has no end, meaning whoever enters it, it is not unable to do so. It was said: It encompasses all things of creation, even the beast has mercy and compassion for its offspring. Some of the commentators said: Everything coveted this verse, even Satan, so he said: I am a thing, so God the Most High said: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear God, so the Jews and Christians said: We are fearing God, so God the Most High said: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, the verse. So the verse is no longer general, praise be to God. Hammad bin Salamah narrated on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God the Almighty wrote it for this nation.
7:157: It contains ten issues: First: Yahya bin Abi Katheer narrated on the authority of Nawf Al-Bakali Al-Himyari: When Moses chose seventy men from his people for the meeting with his Lord, God Almighty said to Moses: I have made the earth a place of prostration and purification for you, so you may pray wherever the prayer overtakes you, except near a toilet, a bathroom, or a grave. And I will put tranquility in your hearts, and I will make you read the Torah from memory, read by the man among you, the woman, the free man, the slave, the young and the old. Moses said that to his people, but they said: We do not want to pray except in churches, and we cannot carry tranquility in our hearts, and we want it to be as it was in the Ark, and we cannot read the Torah from memory, and we do not want to read it except by sight. So God Almighty said: Then I will write it down for those who fear God - until His saying - the successful ones. So He made it for this nation, so Moses said: O Lord, make me their prophet. He said: Their prophet is from them. He said: O Lord, make me from them. He said: You will never reach them. Moses said: O Lord, I have come to you with a delegation from the Children of Israel, and you have made our delegation for others. Then God revealed: And among the people of Moses was a community guiding with the truth and doing justice thereby (al-A’raf 7:159). Moses was pleased. Nawf said: So praise God who made the delegation of the Children of Israel for you. Abu Nu’aym also mentioned this story from the hadith of Al-Awza’i, who said: Yahya bin Abi Amr Al-Saybani told us that Nawf Al-Bakali told me that when he began a sermon, he would say: Do you not praise your Lord who preserved your absence and took your share for you after your share and made the delegation of the people for you? That is because Moses, peace be upon him, came with the Children of Israel and God said to them: I have made the earth a place of prostration for you. Wherever you pray in it, your prayer will be accepted, except in three places. Whoever prays in them, I will not accept his prayer: the graveyard, the bathroom, and the toilet. They said: No, except in the church. He said: And I have made the earth a means of purification for you if you cannot find water. They said: No, except with water. He said: And I have made wherever a man prays and he is alone, his prayer will be accepted. They said: No, except in a group. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet. These words, as we mentioned, excluded the Jews and Christians from the commonality that appears in His saying: Then I will prescribe it for those who fear Me. This number was restricted to the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, and others. And they follow means in his law and religion and what he brought. The Messenger and the Prophet are two names for two meanings, for the Messenger is more specific than the Prophet. The Messenger was given priority out of concern for the meaning of the message, otherwise the meaning of prophethood is the one that comes first, and therefore “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, responded to Al-Bara’ when he said: And in Your Messenger whom You have sent. He said to him: Say, I believe in Your Prophet whom You have sent. It was included in Sahih. Also, in His statement: “And in Your Messenger whom You have sent” there is a repetition of the message, which has one meaning, so it is like a filler that is useless. Unlike His statement: And Your Prophet whom You have sent, there is no repetition in them. Based on this, every Messenger is a Prophet, but not every Prophet is a Messenger, because the Messenger and the Prophet share a general matter, which is the report, and differ in a specific matter, which is the message. So if you say: Muhammad is a Messenger from God, this includes that he is a Prophet and the Messenger of God. And likewise with the other Prophets, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them. Third: The Almighty’s saying: the illiterate is attributed to the illiterate nation, which is as it was born. It did not learn to write or read, as Ibn Aziz said. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was illiterate. He did not write, read, or calculate. God Almighty said: And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand (al-Ankabut 29:48). It was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Ibn Omar, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: We are an illiterate nation; we neither write nor calculate.” The hadith. It was said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was traced back to Mecca, the mother of villages, as mentioned by Al-Nahhas. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Which they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. Al-Bukhari narrated: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, Falih told us, Hilal told us, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar: I met Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas. I said: Tell me about the description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Torah. He said: Yes, by God, he is described in the Torah with some of his description in the Qur’an: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner (al-Ahzab 33:45) and a protection for the illiterate. You are My servant and Messenger, I have named you Al-Mutawakkil. He is not rude nor harsh nor a companion in the markets. He does not repel evil with evil, but he pardons and forgives. God will not take him until He establishes through him the crooked religion by which they say, There is no god but God, and He opens through it blind eyes, deaf ears, and sealed hearts. -In other than Al-Bukhari- Ata said: Then I met Ka'b and asked him about that, and they did not differ on a single word, except that Ka'b said in his language: quloob ghuluf, adhaan samum, and a'yun umm. Ibn Atiyyah said: I think this is a mistake or a foreign language. It has been narrated from Ka'b that he said: quloob ghuluf, adhaan samum, and a'yun umm. Al-Tabari said: It is a Himyarite language. Ka'b added in describing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: His birth was in Mecca, his migration was to Tabah, his rule was in Ash-Sham, and his nation is the praisers, they praise God in every situation and in every home, they perform ablution for their limbs and wear their izars to the middle of their shins, they are shepherds of the sun, they perform the prayers wherever it catches them even on the back of a sweeper, their rows in battle are like their rows in prayer. Then he recited: Indeed, God loves those who fight in His cause in rows as if they were a solid structure (al-Saff 61:4). Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: He enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong. Ata’ said: He enjoins upon them what is right by abandoning rivals, having good morals, and maintaining family ties. And forbids them what is wrong by worshipping idols and severing family ties. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And lawful for them are the good things. Malik’s school of thought is that the good things are the permissible things, so it is as if he described them as good, since it is a word that includes praise and honor. According to this, we say about the filthy things: they are the forbidden things, and for this reason Ibn Abbas said: The filthy things are pork, usury, and other things. Based on this, Malik permitted the filthy things such as snakes, scorpions, beetles, and the like. Al-Shafi’i’s school of thought, may God have mercy on him, is that the good things are from the aspect of taste, except that the word is not general in his view, because its generality in this aspect of taste necessitates the permissibility of wine and pork, rather he sees it as specific to what the Shari’ah has permitted. He sees the filthy things as a general word for the forbidden things by the Shari’ah and the filthy things, so he forbids scorpions, beetles, geckos, and what is similar to this. People are of these two opinions, and this meaning was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And He will remove from them their burden. “Heaviness” means heaviness, as stated by Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ibn Jubayr. Heaviness also means a covenant, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and Al-Hasan. This verse combines both meanings, for the Children of Israel had taken a covenant from them that they would perform heavy deeds, but that covenant and the burden of those deeds were removed from them by Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, such as washing away urine, making spoils permissible, sitting with menstruating women, eating with them, and sleeping with them. If urine got on one of them’s clothes, he would cut it off. It was also narrated that he would flog one of them. And if they gathered the spoils, fire would descend from the sky and consume them, and if a woman menstruated, they would not go near her, and other things that have been proven in the authentic hadith and others. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And the shackles which were upon them. The shackles are a metaphor for those burdens. Among the burdens is leaving work on the Sabbath, as it is narrated that Moses, peace be upon him, saw a man carrying a reed on the Sabbath, so he struck his neck. This is the opinion of the majority of commentators. There was no blood money for them, but rather retaliation. They were ordered to kill themselves as a sign of their repentance, and so on. So this was likened to shackles, as the poet said: This house is not like it used to be, O Umm Malik, but chains have surrounded necks. The young man returned like an old man, saying nothing but justice, so the critics were relieved. He likened the limits of Islam and its prohibitions against transgressing into prohibitions to chains surrounding necks. From this meaning is what Abu Ahmad bin Jahsh said to Abu Sufyan: Go with her, go with her, I put a dove's necklace around her That is, you are bound by its shame. It is said: So-and-so was bound by such-and-such if it is binding on him. Ninth: If it is said: How did you connect the shackles, which is plural, to the burden, which is singular? The answer is that the burden is a verbal noun that refers to many. Ibn Amir read their burdens in the plural: like their deeds. He made it plural because of the different types of sins. The rest read it in the singular, because it is a verbal noun that refers to little and many of the same type with its wording being singular. They agreed on the singular in His statement: And do not place a burden upon us (Al-Baqarah 2:286). And so on whenever you are presented with this meaning, such as and upon their hearing (Al-Baqarah 2:7). Their glance will not return to them [Ibrahim 43]. And from a hidden glance (Ash-Shura 42:45). All of them mean plural. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: So those who believed in him and honored him meaning, honored him and supported him. Al-Akhfash said: Al-Jahdary and Isa read and honored him with a light pronunciation. And likewise and you honored them (al-Ma’idah 5:12). It is said: Azrahu ya’zuruhu and yu’zuruhu. The light is the Qur’an and success: achieving what is desired. This has been mentioned previously.
7:158: He mentioned that Moses gave the good report about him, and that Jesus gave the good report about him. Then he ordered him to say himself, I am the Messenger of God to you all. And his words are the words of God Almighty, which He wrote from the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an.
7:159: God Almighty says: And among the people of Moses was a community who guided with the truth and did justice thereby. That is, they call people to guidance. They are just means in judgment. In the interpretation: These are a people from beyond China, from beyond the river of sand, they worship God with truth and justice, they believed in Muhammad and abandoned the Sabbath, they face our Qiblah, none of them can reach us, nor can anyone from us reach them. It was narrated that when the disagreement occurred after Moses, there was a nation among them who guided with the truth, and they were not able to be among the Children of Israel until God brought them out to a part of His land isolated from creation, so a path was created for them in the land, so they walked in it for a year and a half until they came out beyond China, so they are on the truth until now. And between the people and them is a sea that cannot be reached because of it. Gabriel took the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them on the night of the Ascension, so they believed in him and he taught them surahs from the Qur’an. He said to them: Do you have a measure and a balance? They said: No. He said: So where is your livelihood? They said: We go out to the wilderness and plant, and when we harvest we put it there, so if one of us needs it he takes what he needs. He said: Then where are your women? They said: In one of our corners, so if one of us needs his wife, he goes to her in the time of need. He said: Does one of you lie in his speech? They said: If one of us did that, a blazing fire would seize him, for the fire descends and burns him. He said: Why are your houses level? They said: So that we do not rise above one another. He said: Why are your graves at your doors? They said: So that we do not forget to remember death. Then when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to the world on the night of the Isra’, the following was revealed to him: And among those We have created is a nation who guide with the truth and do justice thereby (al-A’raf 7:181) meaning the nation of Muhammad, peace be upon them. It teaches him that what was given to Moses in his people, I have given to you in your nation. It was said: They are those who believed in our Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, from the People of the Book. It was said: They are a people from the Children of Israel who held fast to the law of Moses before it was abrogated, and they did not change or kill the prophets.
7:160: The Almighty's saying: And We divided them into twelve tribes, nations. He enumerated His blessings upon the Children of Israel, and made them into tribes so that the matter of each tribe would be known from the perspective of their leader, and the matter would be easy for Moses. In the revelation: And We raised up from among them twelve leaders. (al-Ma’idah 5:12), and it has been mentioned before. And His saying: twelve and the tribe is masculine because after it are nations, so the feminization went to the nations. And if he had said: twelve to masculine the tribe, it would have been permissible, according to Al-Farra'. And it was said: He meant by the tribes the tribes and groups, and that is why He feminized the number. The poet said: The Quraysh are made up of ten clans, and you are innocent of their ten tribes. So he went with the belly to the tribe and faction, and therefore he made it feminine. And the belly is masculine, just as the tribes are a masculine plural. Al-Zajjaj: The meaning is that we divided them into twelve groups. Asbat instead of twelve. Nations is an adjective for the tribes. Al-Mufaddal narrated on the authority of Asim. And we divided them in a lightened form. Asbatan The tribes in the children of Isaac are like the tribes in the children of Ishmael, peace be upon them. And the tribes are taken from the sabt, which is a tree that camels feed on. It has already been fully discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:161: God Almighty said: And when it was said to them, ‘Dwell in this city and eat from it wherever you wish and say, “Forgive us, and enter the gate in prostration. We will forgive you your sins. We will increase the doers of good.”
7:162: And Muammar narrated on the authority of Hammam bin Munabbih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, "On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the words of God Almighty: "But those who did wrong among them substituted a statement other than that which was said to them," they said: A grain in a hair. And it was said to them: "And enter the gate prostrating," so they entered leaning on their backsides. "Because they were wronging" is in the nominative case, because it is a future verb and its position is in the accusative case. And "what" is in the sense of a source, meaning because of their wrongdoing. The meanings and rulings in this verse have already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. And praise be to God.
7:163: The Almighty said: And ask them about the city meaning about the people of the city. He referred to them by it because it was their settlement or the reason for their gathering. Similar to it is: And ask the city in which we were (Yusuf 12:82). And his saying, peace be upon him: The throne shook at the death of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh meaning the people of the throne from the angels, rejoicing and rejoicing at his arrival, may God be pleased with him. That is, ask the Jews who are your neighbors about the report of their ancestors and what God transformed from them into apes and pigs. This is a question of confirmation and rebuke. This was a sign of the truthfulness of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as God informed him of these matters without him learning. They used to say: We are the sons of God and His beloved, because we are from the tribe of His friend Abraham, and from the tribe of Israel, who are the firstborn of God, and from the tribe of Moses, who spoke to God, and from the tribe of his son Uzair, so we are from their children. So God, the Almighty, said to His Prophet: Ask them, O Muhammad, about the town, did you not punish them for their sins? This was by changing a branch of the Shari`ah. There was a difference of opinion about the identity of this village. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and Al-Suddi said: It is Ayla. Ibn Abbas also said that it is Madyan between Ayla and At-Tur. Az-Zuhri: Tiberias. Qatada and Zaid bin Aslam: It is a coast of the Levant, between Madyan and Ainun, called: Maqanat. The Jews concealed this story because of the slander it contained against them. Which was present on the sea means it was near the sea. You say: I was in the presence of the house, meaning near it. When they transgressed on the Sabbath meaning they hunted whales, and they were forbidden from doing so. It is said: The Jews sabbat, they left work on their Sabbath. The man sabbat for the passive participle, a sleep that overcame him, like muteness. And asabat means he remained still and did not move. And the people became on the Sabbath. And the Jews entered on the Sabbath, which is the well-known day. It is from rest and cessation. The plural is asbat, sabat and asbat. And in the hadith: “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever is cupped on Saturday and gets leprosy, he should blame no one but himself. Our scholars said: This is because the blood clots on Saturday, so if you stretch it out to extract it, it will not flow and it will become leprosy. The reading of the group is ya’dun. Abu Nahik read ya’dun with a damma on the ya’, a kasra on the ‘ayn, and a shaddah on the dal. The first is from aggression and the second is from enemies, meaning they prepare the tool to take it. Ibn al-Samiq read in al-asbat on the plural of sabbath: “When their fish come to them on their Sabbath day.” It was read as their sabbaths. Shar’a means many visible streets on the water. Al-Layth said: Whales Shar’a raised their heads. It was said: Its meaning is that the whales of the sea used to come on Saturday, a neck from the sea, and they would jostle a deer. God Almighty inspired them that they should not be hunted on Saturday, because He Almighty forbade the Jews from hunting them. It was said: They used to set out at their doors, like white rams, raising their heads. Some of the later scholars narrated it, so they attacked and took them on Saturday, said al-Hasan. It was said: Sunday, and this is the most correct according to what will come. His statement. And a day when they do not observe the Sabbath meaning they do not do the Sabbath. It is said: Sabbat yasbat if the Sabbath is great. Al-Hasan read yasbatun with a damma on the ya’, meaning they enter the Sabbath, just as it is said: ajma’na, zahrana, and aashharna, meaning we entered the Friday, noon, and month. La yatayyhum meaning their fish. Thus do We test them meaning We make worship difficult for them and test them. The kaf is in the accusative case. Because of what they used to do meaning because of their sin. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl was asked: Do you find in the Book of God that what is lawful comes to you only as sustenance, and what is unlawful comes to you in small groups? He said: Yes, in the story of David and Aylah When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day as a law, and on the day when they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them. It was narrated in the stories of this verse that it was in the time of David, peace be upon him, and that Satan inspired them and said: You were only forbidden from taking it on the Sabbath, so they made pools, and they would drive the whales to it on Friday so that they would remain in it, and they could not get out of it because of the lack of water, so they would take them on Sunday. Ashab narrated on the authority of Malik who said: Ibn Ruman claimed that a man would take a thread and put a stake in it, and he would throw it into the tail of the whale, and at the other end of the thread a peg and leave it like that until Sunday, then the people turned away when they saw that whoever did this would not be afflicted until the whale was hunted in abundance, and he walked with it in the markets, and the wicked announced his hunt, so a group of the Children of Israel stood up and forbade, and they openly forbade and isolated themselves. It was said: Those who forbade said: We will not live with you, so they divided the village with a wall. One day, those who forbade the aggressors were sitting in their councils, and none of the aggressors came out. They said, The people have something to do with it. They went to the wall and looked, and saw that they were apes. They opened the door and entered. The apes recognized their lineage from humans, but the humans did not recognize their lineage from monkeys. The apes would come to their human relatives, smell their clothes, and cry. He would say, Did we not forbid you? They would nod, Yes. Qatada said, “The young men became apes and the old men became pigs. Only those who forbade the aggressors were saved, and the rest perished.” According to this statement, the Children of Israel were only divided into two groups.
7:164: The meaning of the Almighty's saying: And when a group of them said, 'Why do you preach to a people whom God is about to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?' That is, the perpetrators said to the preachers when they preached to them: If you know that God is going to destroy us, why do you preach to us? So God transformed them into monkeys. They said, 'An excuse before your Lord, and perhaps they will fear God.' That is, the preachers said: Our preaching to you is an excuse before your Lord, meaning that it is only obligatory for us to preach to you so that you may fear God. At-Tabari attributed this statement to Ibn al-Kalbi. The majority of commentators said: The Children of Israel split into three groups, which is apparent from the pronouns in the verse. A group disobeyed and persecuted, and they were about seventy thousand. A group forbade and withdrew, and they were twelve thousand. A group withdrew and did not forbid or disobey, and this group said to the forbidding one: Why do you preach to a people - meaning the disobedient one - whom God will destroy or punish, based on the preponderance of opinion, and what is known of God’s actions at that time with disobedient nations? So the forbidding one said: Our preaching is an excuse to God, so that they may fear God. If they had been two groups, the forbidding one would have said to the disobedient one: So that you may fear God, with the letter Kaf. Then after this, they differed, and a group said: The group that did not forbid or disobey was destroyed with the disobedient one as punishment for abandoning the prohibition, as Ibn Abbas said. He also said: I do not know what was done to them, and this is what is apparent from the verse. Ikrimah said: I said to Ibn Abbas when he said I do not know what was done to them: Do you not see that they hated what they were doing and opposed them, so they said: Why do you preach to a people whom God will destroy? So I kept on at him until I knew that they had been saved, so he clothed me with a garment. This is the view of Al-Hasan. What indicates that only the ordinary group was destroyed is His statement: And We seized those who did wrong. And His statement: And you have certainly known those among you who transgressed on the Sabbath (al-Baqarah 2:65) and the verse. Isa and Talhah read excuse in the accusative case. Al-Kisa’i has two ways of making it accusative: One of them is as a source. The second is based on the assumption that we did that as an excuse. This is the reading of Hafs from Asim. The rest read it in the nominative case, which is the preferred choice, because they did not want to apologize for a new apology for a matter for which they were blamed, but it was said to them: Why do you preach? So they said: Our preaching is an excuse. If a man said to another man: Apology to God and to you for such and such, meaning an apology, he would put it in the accusative case. This is the statement of Sibawayh. The verse indicates the statement of blocking the means. It has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. And the discussion of the transformed person, whether he will be a descendant or not, has been mentioned in it, clearly. Praise be to God. And the command to do good and forbid evil has been mentioned in Al-Imran and Al-Ma’idah.
