He went on to say about women that they should avoid and avoid corrupt people, and that whoever sits with them is like them, so there is no point in repeating it.
7:165: Forgetting is used for the forgetful. The deliberate is the one who abandons, as God the Almighty said: So when they forgot that by which they had been reminded meaning they abandoned it intentionally, and from this: They forgot God, so He made them forget (al-Tawbah 9:67). The meaning of with a terrible punishment is severe. There are eleven readings for it: The first - the reading of Abu Amr, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i with Ba'ees on the weight of Fa'il. The second - the reading of the people of Mecca with Ba'ees with a kasra on the Ba' and the weight is the same. The third - the reading of the people of Medina with Ba'ees with a kasra after it a silent ya followed by a broken seen with a tanween, and there are two opinions on it. Al-Kisa'i said: The original is Ba'ees with a light hamza, then two ya's met, so one of them was deleted and the first letter was broken, as is said: ragheef and shaheed. It was said: He meant Ba'ees on the weight of fa'al, so he broke the first letter and lightened the hamza and deleted the kasra, as is said: rahm and rahm. Fourth: Al-Hasan’s reading, with a kasra followed by a silent hamza followed by an open seen. Fifth: Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Muqri’ read Ba’ees with a fatha on the ba’ and a kasra on the hamza and a kasra on the seen with a tanween. Sixth: Ya’qub Al-Qari’ said: It was narrated from some of the reciters with the word tha’ab bi’ees with a fatha on the ba’ and a kasra on the hamza and a fatha on the seen. Seventh: Al-A’mash’s reading with ya’ees on the weight of fa’il. It was narrated from him with ya’ees on the weight of fa’il. It was narrated from him with ya’ees with an open ba’ and a shaddah on the hamza, and the seen in all of them is broken and tanween, I mean the reading of Al-A’mash. Tenth: Nasr Bin Asim’s reading with tha’ab bi’ees with a fatha on the ba’ and a shaddah on the ya’ without a hamza. Ya’qub Al-Qari’ said: It was narrated from some of the reciters with ya’ees with a kasra followed by a silent hamza followed by an open ya’. These are eleven readings mentioned by An-Nahhas. Ali Bin Sulayman said: The Arabs say he came with the daughters of bays meaning he brought something bad. So the meaning of ba’athab bi’ees is a bad punishment. As for Al-Hasan’s reading, Abu Hatim claimed that it has no basis. He said: Because you do not say, I passed by a wretched man, until you say, Wretched is the man, or Wretched is a man. An-Nahhas said: This is rejected from Abu Hatim’s words. The grammarians reported: If you did such-and-such, then well done. They mean well done and the characteristic is good. The interpretation according to Al-Hasan’s reading is: With a punishment, wretched is the punishment.
7:166: The Almighty said: But when they transgressed that which they were forbidden. That is, when they exceeded in disobeying God. We said to them, 'Be apes, despised.' It is said: I humiliated him, so he was despised, meaning I distanced him and expelled him. This was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. It indicates that sins are the cause of vengeance, and there is no ambiguity in this. So it was said: He said that to them in words that can be heard, and they were like that. It was also said: The meaning is that we made them apes.
7:167: That is, their ancestors knew that if they changed and did not believe in the unlettered prophet, God would send upon them someone who would punish them. Abu Ali said: Adhan with a long vowel means to inform. Adhan with a shaddah means to call. Some people said: Adhan and Adhan mean to inform, just as one says: aqiqaan and tayqaan. Zuhair said: I said, You know that prey has a prey, so if you do not lose it, you will kill it. Another said: Learn that the worst people are the ones who call out in their slogan: Left I know. The meaning of He will make them taste is He will make them taste, and this has been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. It was said that what is meant is Nebuchadnezzar. It was also said that it means the Arabs. It was also said that it means the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is more apparent, for they are the ones who will remain until the Day of Resurrection. And God knows best. Ibn Abbas said: The evil of the torment here means taking the jizya. If it is said that they were transformed, so how can the jizya be taken from them? The answer is that it is taken from their sons and children, and they are the most humiliated people, and they are the Jews. And on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, the evil of the torment said: The tax, and no prophet ever collected the tax, except for Moses, peace be upon him, who was the first to impose the tax, so he collected it for thirteen years, then he stopped, and our Prophet, peace be upon him.
7:168: The Almighty said: And We dispersed them throughout the earth into nations. That is, We scattered them throughout the lands. He meant by this to scatter their affairs, so that they did not have a unified word. Among them are the righteous. The subject is the one who believed in Muhammad, peace be upon him, and those who did not change among them and died before the law of Moses was abrogated. Or they are those beyond China, as mentioned previously. And among them are those who are less than that. The subject is the accusative of circumstance. An-Nahhas said: We do not know of anyone who raised it. What is meant are the disbelievers among them. And We tested them. That is, We examined them. With good things that is, with fertility and well-being. And with evil things that is, drought and hardships. Perhaps they will return to return from their disbelief.
7:169: The Almighty said: Then there came after them a posterity meaning the children of those whom they dispersed throughout the land. Abu Hatim said: The posterity with a sukoon on the lam: the children, the singular and the plural are the same. The posterity with a fatha on the lam is the substitute, whether a child or a stranger. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The posterity with a fatha is the good, and the posterity with a jazm is the bad. Labid said: Those who lived in their care are gone, and I am left behind like the skin of a mangy dog. Hence, the bad speech is called khalaf. And from this comes the popular proverb, “He paused for an alif and then said ‘khalaf.’ So ‘khalaf’ is used in condemnation with a sukoon, and ‘khalaf’ is used with a fatha in praise. This is the well-known usage. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This knowledge is carried by the just ones of every generation.” Each of them may be used in place of the other. Hassan bin Thabit said: We are the first to come to you and we are behind you in the obedience of God. Follow Another said: We have found a successor, a wretched successor, who closed his door on us and then swore No one enters the gate except he who knows a slave who, when he is unable to carry his load, stops. It is narrated: Khadaf, meaning to fill up. The intended meaning of the verse is to criticize. They inherited the Book. The commentators said: They are the Jews. They inherited the Book of God, so they read it and taught it, and they disobeyed its rulings and committed its prohibitions while studying it. So this was a rebuke and a rebuke to them. They take the goods of this world. Then He informed about them that they take whatever is offered to them from the worldly pleasures due to their intense greed and gluttony. And they say, ‘We will be forgiven.’ And they do not repent. This indicates that they do not repent. God the Almighty said: And if there comes to them an offer like it, they seize it. Offering means worldly goods, with the letter ra pronounced with a fat-ha. With a sukun, it is any money other than dirhams and dinars. The reference in this verse is to bribery and wicked earnings. Then He blamed them for being deceived in their saying, He will forgive us, and that they were in a state that if they had the opportunity to do it again, they would commit it. They were deceived by their forgiveness while they persisted. He only says, He will forgive us for the one who stopped and regretted it. I said: This description that God the Almighty has condemned these people with is found in us. Al-Darimi Abu Muhammad narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Mubarak told us, Sadaqah ibn Khalid told us, on the authority of Ibn Jabir, on the authority of a sheikh known as Abu Amr, on the authority of Muadh ibn Jabal, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Qur’an will wear out in the hearts of some people as a garment wears out and falls apart. They will recite it but will not find any desire or pleasure in it. They will wear sheepskins over the hearts of wolves. Their actions are greed without fear. If they fall short, they will say, We will attain it. And if they do wrong, they will say, “He will forgive us. Indeed, we do not associate anything with God.” It was said: The pronoun in will come to them refers to the Jews of Medina, meaning that if the Jews of Yathrib, who were at the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were offered something similar, they would take it as their predecessors had taken it. God Almighty says: “Was not a covenant taken from them in the Book that they would not say about God except the truth? And they studied what was in it. And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God. So will you not reason?” There are two issues in it. First: The Almighty’s saying: Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them? meaning the Torah. This is an emphasis on the necessity of speaking the truth in the Sharia and rulings, and that the rulers should not be inclined towards falsehood through bribery. I said: This which is binding on these people and which they have taken a covenant with to speak the truth, is binding on us on the tongue of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in the Book of our Lord, as was explained previously in An-Nisa. And there is no disagreement about it in all the laws, and praise be to God. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And they studied what is in it meaning they read it, and they were close to it. Abu Abd al-Rahman read and they studied what is in it and assimilated the ta’ into the dal. Ibn Zayd said: The one who was right would come to them with a bribe, so they would bring out the Book of God for him and rule in his favor. When the one who was wrong came, they would take the bribe from him and bring out their book that they had written with their own hands and rule in his favor. Ibn Abbas said: And do not say about God except the truth and they said falsehood in the forgiveness of their sins that they require and are certain of. Ibn Zayd said it means in the rulings that they rule by, as we mentioned. Some scholars said: The meaning of and they studied what is in it is to erase it by abandoning acting upon it and understanding it, from your saying: the wind erased the traces, if it wiped them out. And a line is a daris and a quarter is a daris, if its trace was erased and obliterated. This meaning is consistent with the Almighty’s saying: A party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of God behind their backs Al-Anfal 2:13. (al-Baqarah 2:101) And His saying: So they threw him behind their backs (Al Imran 3:187) is according to what was explained previously in Al-Baqarah.
7:170: The Almighty said: And those who hold fast to the Book meaning the Torah, meaning by acting upon it. It is said: he held fast to it and adhered to it, meaning he held fast to it. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Asim read in the narration of Abu Bakr yamsak with a lightened form of amsaka yamsak. The first reading is better, because it contains the meaning of repetition and abundance of holding fast to the Book of God Almighty and His religion, and for that they are praised. Holding fast to the Book of God and the religion requires consistency and repetition to do so. Ka'b bin Zuhair said: You do not hold fast to the covenant you claimed except as a sieve holds water. He came with it in his nature, criticizing the frequent breaking of covenants.
7:171: The Almighty said: And when We lifted the mountain up. Lifting up means we raised it. This was explained previously in Al-Baqarah. As if it were a canopy meaning that due to its height it was as if it were a shade-giving cloud. Take what We have given you with strength meaning with diligence. This was mentioned in Al-Baqarah until the end of the verse.
7:172: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And when your Lord took meaning, remind them, along with what came before from reminding of the covenants in their book, what I took of covenants from the servants on the Day of the Atom. This is a problematic verse, and scholars have spoken about its interpretation and rulings, so we will mention what they mentioned about it according to what we have come across. Some people said: The meaning of the verse is that God, the Almighty, brought forth from the loins of the children of Adam some of them from others. They said: The meaning of And made them testify of themselves, ‘Am I not your Lord?’ is He guided them through His creation to His Oneness, because every adult necessarily knows that he has one Lord. Am I not your Lord? meaning, He said: So this took the place of calling them to witness and acknowledging, as God, the Almighty, said in the heavens and the earth: They said, ‘We have come in obedience.’ (Fussilat 41:11) Al-Qaffal went with this and elaborated. It was said that He, the Almighty, brought forth the souls before creating the bodies, and that He placed in them such knowledge that they knew what He was addressing them with. I said: And in the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, there are other than these two statements, and that God Almighty brought forth the ghosts in which there are souls from the back of Adam, peace be upon him. And Malik narrated in his Muwatta’ that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was asked about this verse: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes, we testify.’ (7:17) So Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, being asked about it. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God the Almighty created Adam, then wiped his back with His right hand and extracted from him offspring. He said, I created these for Paradise, and they will do the deeds of the people of Paradise. Then He wiped his back and extracted from him offspring. He said, I created these for Hell, and they will do the deeds of the people of Hell. A man said, So what is the purpose of working? He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God creates a servant for Paradise, He employs him in the work of the people of Paradise until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Paradise and enters him into Paradise. And when He creates a servant for Hell, He employs him in the work of the people of Hell until he dies doing one of the deeds of the people of Hell and God enters him into Hell. Abu Omar said: This is a hadith with an interrupted chain of transmission, because Muslim bin Yasar did not meet Omar. Yahya bin Ma’in said about it: Muslim bin Yasar is not known, between him and Omar was Nu’aym bin Rabi’ah, as mentioned by al-Nasa’i, and Nu’aym was not known for carrying knowledge. However, the meaning of this hadith has been authenticated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, through many reliable chains of transmission from the hadith of Omar bin al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, Abdullah bin Mas’ud, Ali bin Abi Talib, Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with them all, and others. At-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God created Adam, He wiped his back and from his back fell every soul that He would create from his offspring until the Day of Resurrection. He placed between the eyes of each man of them a gleam of light. Then He showed them to Adam and said, O Lord, who are these? He said, These are your offspring. He saw a man among them and the gleam between his eyes pleased him. He said, O Lord, who is this? He said, This is a man from the last of the nations from your offspring called David. He said, O Lord, how long have you made his lifespan? He said, Sixty years. He said, O Lord, add forty years to my lifespan. When Adam’s lifespan came to an end, the Angel of Death came to him and said, Are there not forty years left of my lifespan? He said, Have you not given them to your son David? He said, Adam denied, so his offspring denied, and Adam forgot, so his offspring forgot. In a narration other than at-Tirmidhi: Then He ordered the writing and witnesses. In another narration: “He saw among them the weak, the rich, the poor, the humiliated, the afflicted, and the healthy. Adam said to Him, “O Lord, what is this? Why did you not make them equal?” He said, I wanted to be grateful. And Abdullah ibn Amr narrated, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: They took from his back as a comb is taken from the head. God gave them minds like the ant of Solomon. He took a covenant from them that He is their Lord and that there is no god but Him. They acknowledged that and committed to it, and He informed them that He would send messengers to them, so some of them testified against others. Abi bin Kaab said: And the seven heavens testified against them, so no one is born until the Day of Resurrection except that a covenant has been taken from him. There are four different opinions about the place where the covenant was taken when they were expelled. Ibn Abbas said: In Batn Na'man, a valley next to Arafat. It was narrated from him that it was in Rahab - a land in India - where Adam, peace be upon him, descended. Yahya bin Salam said: Ibn Abbas said about this verse: God sent Adam down in India, then He wiped his back and brought out from him every soul that He will create until the Day of Resurrection, then He said: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes, we bear witness." Yahya said: Al-Hasan said: Then He returned them to the loins of Adam, peace be upon him. Al-Kalbi said: Between Mecca and Taif. Al-Suddi said: In the lowest heaven when he was sent down from Paradise to it, He wiped his back and brought out from the right side of his back white offspring like pearls, and He said to them: Enter Paradise through My mercy. And He brought out from the left side of his back black offspring and He said to them: Enter the Fire and I do not care. Ibn Jurayj said: Every soul created for Paradise came out white, and every soul created for the Fire was black. Second: Ibn al-Arabi may God have mercy on him said: If it is said, how is it permissible for Him to torment creation when they have not sinned, or punish them for what He wanted from them and wrote for them and led them to, we say: How can that be prevented, rationally or legally? If it is said: Because the Most Merciful, Most Wise among us cannot do that. We say: Because above Him is a commander who commands him and a forbidder who forbids him, and our Lord, the Most High, is not questioned about what He does while they are questioned, and it is not permissible for creation to be compared to the Creator. Nor should the actions of the servants be attributed to the actions of God, and in truth all actions belong to God, the Most High, and all creation belongs to Him. He directs them as He wills and judges between them as He wills. What a human being finds is motivated by a soft nature, compassion for his nature, and a love of praise and commendation, because of the benefit he expects from that, and the Creator, the Most High, is sanctified above all of that, so it is not permissible to consider it. Third: There is a difference of opinion regarding this verse, is it specific or general? It was said: The verse is specific, because God the Almighty said: “Of the children of Adam, from their loins,” so this hadith excludes those who were from the children of Adam through his loins. And He the Almighty said: Or you say, ‘Our fathers were polytheists before,’ so everyone who did not have polytheist fathers was excluded from it. It was said: It is specific to those from whom a covenant was taken by the prophets. It was said: Rather, it is general for all people, because everyone knows that he was a child who was nourished and raised, and that he has a manager and creator. This is the meaning of And He made them witness against themselves. The meaning of They said, ‘Yes,’ is that this is obligatory upon them. So when the creation acknowledged God the Almighty that He is the Lord, then they forgot about Him, He reminded them of His prophets and concluded the remembrance with the best of His chosen ones so that His proof would be established against them, so He said to him: “Then remind. You are only a reminder. You are not a controller over them.” (al-Ghashiyah 88:21-22) Then He enabled him to control, gave him authority, and established His religion on earth. Al-Tartushi said: This covenant is binding on people even if they do not remember it in this life, just as divorce is binding on someone who has witnessed it and forgotten it. Fourth: This verse was used as evidence by those who said: Whoever dies young will enter Paradise because of his confirmation in the first covenant. And whoever reaches the age of reason, the first covenant will not suffice him. This speaker says: The children of the polytheists will be in Paradise, and this is the correct view in this matter. There is disagreement about this issue due to the different reports, and what we have mentioned is correct. We will discuss this in Ar-Rum, God willing. We have already discussed it in the Book of Remembrance, and praise be to God. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: from their loins is a substitute for inclusion in His saying: from the children of Adam. The wording of the verse requires that the taking was from the children of Adam, and Adam is not mentioned in the verse according to the wording. The basis of the system is this: And when your Lord took from the loins of the children of Adam their descendants. The back of Adam was not mentioned because it is known that they are all his children, and that they were brought out on the Day of the Covenant from his loins. So He dispensed with mentioning it because He said: from the children of Adam. The Kufians and Ibn Kathir read their descendants with the singular and the fat-ha on the ta’, and it occurs for the singular and the plural. God Almighty said: Grant me from Yourself good offspring (Al Imran 3:38) so this is for the singular, because he only asked for the gift of a son and was given the good report of John. The reciters agreed on the singular in His saying: from the offspring of Adam (Maryam 19:58) and there is nothing more than the offspring of Adam. And He said: And we were descendants after them so this is for the plural. The rest read their offspring in the plural, because since offspring refers to one person, a word was used that does not refer to one person, so it was pluralized so that the word could be summarized in its intended meaning, without anything sharing it, which is the plural, because the appearance of the children of Adam produced from them many proportionate offspring, descendants after descendants, whose number is known only to God, so it was pluralized for this meaning. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Yes. This was discussed in detail in Surat Al-Baqarah when He said: Yes, whoever earns evil (al-Baqarah 2:81), so ponder it there. That they say and or fight Abu Amr read with the letter ya in both of them. He responded to the repeated third-person utterance before it, which is His saying: Of the children of Adam, from their loins, are their descendants and He made them bear witness over themselves. His saying: They said, “Yes is also a third-person utterance. Likewise, And we were descendants after them and perhaps so he applied it to what came before it and what came after it from the third-person utterance. The rest read with the letter ta in both of them, and they responded to the previous third-person utterance in His saying: Am I not your Lord? They said, Yes. And We bore witness is from His saying the angels. When they said, Yes, the angels said, We bear witness lest you say “or say,” meaning lest you say. It was said that the meaning of this is that when they said, Yes, and acknowledged His Lordship, God Almighty said to the angels, Bear witness. They said, We bear witness to your acknowledgment lest you say “or say.” This is the saying of Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi. Ibn Abbas and Ubayy ibn Ka’b said: His statement, We bear witness is from the statement of the children of Adam. The meaning is: We bear witness that You are our Lord and God. Ibn Abbas said: He made some of them bear witness to others. So the meaning according to this is that they said, Yes, some of us bear witness to others. So if this is from the statement of the angels, then it is stopped at Yes, and it is not appropriate to stop at it if it is from the statement of the children of Adam, because an is related to what precedes Yes, from His statement, And He made them bear witness to themselves, lest they say. Mujahid narrated on the authority of Ibn Amr that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants, as a comb is taken from the head. Then He said to them, Am I not your Lord? They said, Yes. The angels said, We bear witness, lest you say. That is, We bear witness against you to the acknowledgement of Lordship, lest you say. This indicates the ta’. Makki said: This is the preferred choice because its meaning is correct, and because the group is on it. It has been said that His statement, We bear witness is from the statement of God Almighty and the angels. The meaning is: So we bear witness to your acknowledgement, as Abu Malik said, and it was also narrated from al-Suddi.
7:173: And we were descendants after them meaning we followed their example. Will You then destroy us for what the falsifiers did? meaning: You will not do this. And there is no excuse for the imitator in monotheism.
7:174: God Almighty says: And thus do We detail the verses that perhaps they will return.
7:175: The People of the Book mentioned a story that they knew in the Torah. There was a difference of opinion about who was given the signs. Ibn Masoud and Ibn Abbas said: He is Balaam bin Ba'oura, and it is said Na'am, from the Children of Israel in the time of Moses, peace be upon him. He was such that when he looked he saw the throne. He is the one meant by the saying: And recite to them the report of him to whom We gave Our signs, and he did not say a sign. In his council there were twelve thousand inkwells for the students who wrote from him. Then he became such that he was the first to compile a book about the fact that the world has no maker. Malik bin Dinar said: Balaam bin Ba'oura was sent to the king of Midian to call him to faith, so he gave him a gift and granted him a share, so he followed his religion and left the religion of Moses, and about him these verses were revealed. Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulayman narrated on the authority of his father that he said: Balaam had been given prophecy and his prayers were answered. When Moses came with the Children of Israel to fight the tyrants, the tyrants asked Balaam bin Ba'oura to pray against Moses. He stood up to pray, but his tongue began to pray against his companions. He was asked about that, and he said: I am not able to do more than what you hear, and his tongue stuck out on his chest. He said: Now the world and the hereafter have gone from me, and nothing remains but deceit, trickery and ruse. I will plot against you, and I think that you should send your girls to them, for God hates adultery. If they fall into it, they will perish. So they did, and the Children of Israel fell into adultery, and God sent a plague upon them, and seventy thousand of them died. This story was mentioned in full by Al-Tha'labi and others. It was narrated that Balaam bin Ba'oura prayed that Moses would not enter the city of the tyrants, and his prayer was answered, but he remained in the wilderness. Moses said: O Lord, for what sin did we remain in the wilderness? He said: Because of the prayer of Balaam. He said: Just as you heard his supplication against me, hear my supplication against him. So Moses supplicated that God remove the Greatest Name from him, so God stripped him of what he was upon. Abu Hamid said at the end of his book Minhaaj al-Arifin: I heard some of the gnostics say that some of the prophets asked God about the matter of Balaam and his expulsion after those signs and miracles, so God said: He never thanked Me for what I gave him, and if he had thanked Me for that once, I would not have taken it from him. And Ikrimah said: Balaam was a prophet and was given a book. And Mujahid said: He was given prophethood, so his people bribed him to be silent, so he did and left them as they were. Al-Mawardi said: This is not correct, because God does not choose for His prophethood anyone except one who He knows will not go out of His obedience to what He gives him. Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas and Zaid bin Aslam said: It was revealed about Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt Al-Thaqafi, who had read the books and knew that God would send a messenger at that time, and he wished that he would be that messenger. But when God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, he envied him and disbelieved in him. He is the one about whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: His hair believed but his heart disbelieved. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It was revealed about Abu Amir bin Saifi, who used to wear hair-scarves during the pre-Islamic era, and he disbelieved in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He "entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina and said: O Muhammad, what is this that you have brought? He said: I have brought the Hanafi faith, the religion of Abraham. He said: Then I am upon it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am not upon it because you have introduced into it what is not from it. Abu Amir said: May God kill the liar among us, banished and alone. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, may God kill the liar among us in this way. He only said this to attack the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he left Mecca. So Abu Amir went to Ash-Sham and passed by Caesar and wrote to al-Munafiqun 63:Prepare yourself, for I am coming to you from Caesar with an army to expel Muhammad from Medina. So he died in Ash-Sham alone." And about him was revealed: And as an ambush for those who fought against God and His Messenger before (al-Tawbah 9:107) and it will come in Bara'ah. Ibn Abbas said in a narration: It was revealed about a man who had three supplications that were answered for him. He had a wife called Al-Basoos and he had a son from her. She said: Make me one supplication from her. He said: You have one. What do you command? She said: Ask God to make me the most beautiful woman among the Children of Israel. When she knew that there was no one like her among them, she turned away from him. So he asked God to make her a barking dog. So two supplications were lost. Her sons came and said: We cannot bear this. Our mother has become a dog that people taunt us about. Ask God to return her to how she was. So he asked God and she returned to what she was, and the supplications were lost. The first opinion is more famous and is the most accepted. Ubadah ibn As-Samit said: It was revealed about Quraysh. God gave them His signs that He sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they withdrew from them and did not accept them. Ibn Abbas said: Balaam was from the city of the tyrants. It was also said that he was from Yemen. So he withdrew from it means from the knowledge of God, meaning the knowledge that he had was taken away from him. In the hadith, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Knowledge is of two types: knowledge in the heart, which is beneficial knowledge, and knowledge on the tongue, which is God’s proof against the son of Adam.” This is like the knowledge of Balaam and others like him. We seek refuge in God from it, and we ask Him for success and a true death. Shedding means coming out. It is said: The snake shed its skin, meaning it came out of it. It is also said: This is from the inverted form, meaning the verses shed themselves from it. Then Satan pursued him, meaning he caught up with him. It is said: I followed the people, meaning I caught up with them. It is also said: It was revealed about the Jews and Christians. They awaited the emergence of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they disbelieved in him.
7:176: The Almighty said: And if We willed, We could have raised him up meaning Balaam. That is, if We willed, We could have killed him before he disobeyed, so We raised him up to Paradise. With it means by working with it. But he clung to the earth meaning he leaned on it, according to Ibn Jubayr and Al-Suddi. Mujahid: He settled in it, meaning he settled in its pleasures. The root of ikhlaad is adherence. It is said: So-and-so settled in a place if he resided in it and stuck to it. Zuhair said: Whose home is it that you covered with gharqad like a revelation in the stone of the eternal stream? Meaning the resident, so the meaning is that he adhered to the pleasures of the earth, so he expressed it as the earth, because the pleasures of this world are on the face of the earth. And he followed his desires meaning what Satan made attractive to him. It was also said: He was with the disbelievers. It was also said: He followed the pleasure of his wife, and she desired money until she made him pray against Moses. His example is like that of a dog is subject and predicate. If you attack him, he pants is a condition and its answer. It is in the place of the state, meaning his example is like that of a dog, panting. The meaning is: He is on one thing and does not desist from disobedience, like a dog that is in this state, so the meaning is: He is panting in every case, whether you chase him or not. Ibn Jurayj said: The dog is cut off from his heart, he has no heart, if you attack him, he pants or leave him, he pants, likewise the one who abandons guidance has no heart, his heart is cut off. Al-Qatibi said: Everything that pants only pants from exhaustion or thirst, except the dog, which pants when tired, at rest, sick, healthy, quenched, or thirsty. So God made an example of one who denies His signs, saying: If you admonish him, he goes astray, and if you leave him, he goes astray. So he is like a dog: if you leave him, he pants, and if you chase him, he pants, as God says: “And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is all the same to you whether you invite them or whether you are silent” (al-A’raf 7:193). Al-Jawhari said: The dog pants with the fat-ha panting or panting with the damma if he sticks out his tongue from exhaustion or thirst, and the same applies to a man when he becomes exhausted. And His statement: If you attack him, he pants is because if you attack a dog, he barks and turns away, fleeing, and if you leave him, he attacks you and barks, tiring himself out facing you and turning away from you, and he is afflicted by what afflicts him when he is thirsty, sticking out his tongue. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim said in Nawader Al-Usul: He likened it to a dog among wild beasts because the dog has a dead heart, and its panting is because its heart is dead. All other wild beasts are not like that, so they do not pant. The dog became like that because when Adam (peace be upon him) came down to earth, the enemy rejoiced at him, so he went to the wild beasts and paralyzed them on Adam, so the dog was the most aggressive of them. Then Gabriel came down with the staff that was given to Moses in Madyan and made it a sign for him to Pharaoh and his people, and he put great authority in it and it was from the myrtle of Paradise, so he gave it to Adam (peace be upon him) on that day to drive away the wild beasts from himself, and he ordered him, as was narrated, to come close to the dog and put his hand on its head, so the dog became accustomed to it and its heart died from it because of the power of the staff, and it became accustomed to it and its children until this day, because of putting his hand on its head and it became a guard among the guards of his children. And if he is disciplined and taught to hunt, he will be disciplined and accept teaching, and that is what He said: You will learn them from what God has taught you (al-Ma’idah 5:5). As-Suddi: Balaam after that was panting like a dog. This example, according to many scholars of interpretation, is general for everyone who was given the Qur’an but did not act upon it. It was also said that it is for every hypocrite. The first is more correct. Mujahid said about the verse: “His example is that of a dog: if you attack him, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants.” That is, if you chase him with your mount or foot, he pants, or if you leave him, he pants. The same is true for someone who reads the Book and does not act upon what is in it. Another said: This is the worst example, because his example is that his desires have overcome him until he no longer has the power to harm or benefit himself, like a panting dog, whether he attacks him or not, he does not have the power to stop panting. It was also said that one of the characteristics of a dog is to fall upon someone who does not fear him, starting with rudeness, then his recklessness calms down by obtaining every vile reward. God made him an example of someone who accepts bribes in religion until he is stripped of the signs of his Lord. The verse indicates to those who ponder it that no one should be deceived by his actions or knowledge, because no one knows what will happen to him. It indicates the prohibition of taking bribes to nullify or change a right. This has been explained in Al-Ma’idah. It also indicates the prohibition of imitating a scholar except with a clear argument, because God the Most High informed us that He gave this one His signs and then he withdrew from them, so it is necessary to fear the same for others and not accept them except with a proof. God Almighty says: “That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the story that perhaps they will give thought.” That is, it is the example of all the disbelievers.
7:177: God Almighty says: Evil is the example of the people who deny Our signs and were wronging themselves. His saying: The example of the people is bad It is said: The thing is bad, ugly, so it is intransitive, and it is bad, it is bad, so it is transitive, meaning their example is bad. And its meaning is: Bad example like the people, so the added word was deleted, and like is made accusative as a specification. Al-Akhfash said: So he made the example of the people a metaphor. And the people is raised by the beginning or by the implication of the subject. The meaning is: Bad example is like the people. Abu Ali estimated it: Bad example like the people. Asim Al-Jahdary and Al-A'mash read Bad like the people, raising like with bad.
7:178: Its meaning has been presented in more than one place. This verse responds to the Qadarites as mentioned above, and responds to those who say that God Almighty has guided all those who are accountable and that it is not permissible for Him to lead anyone astray.
7:179: God the Almighty informed us that He created people for Hell with His justice, then He described them and said: They have hearts with which they do not understand meaning they are like those who do not understand, because they do not benefit from them, nor do they understand reward or fear punishment. Eyes with which they do not see means guidance. Ears with which they do not hear means sermons. The purpose is not to deny their senses perceptions altogether, as we explained in Al-Baqarah. Those are like livestock, nay, they are more astray because they are not guided to reward. They are like livestock, meaning their concern is eating and drinking, and they are more astray because livestock see their benefits and harms and follow their Owner, while they are the opposite. Ata' said: Livestock know God, while the disbeliever does not know Him. It was said: Livestock are obedient to God the Almighty, while the disbeliever is disobedient. Those are the heedless meaning they abandoned contemplation and turned away from Paradise and Hell.
7:180: The Almighty’s saying: And to God belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. There are six issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: And to God belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. This is a command to sincerely worship God and to avoid polytheists and atheists. Muqatil and other commentators said: The verse was revealed about a Muslim man who used to say in his prayer: O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful. A polytheist from Mecca said: Didn’t Muhammad and his companions claim that they worshipped one Lord, so why does this man invoke two Lords? Then God the Almighty revealed: And to God belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. Second: It was mentioned in the book of Al-Tirmidhi, Sunan Ibn Majah and others, a hadith “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which he stated: God has ninety-nine names, one of which has what is not in the other.” We have explained that in the book Al-Asna fi Sharh Asma God Al-Husna. Ibn Atiyyah said - and mentioned the hadith of Al-Tirmidhi - that hadith is not mutawatir, even though Abu Eisa said about it: This is a strange hadith that we do not know except from the hadith of Safwan bin Salih, and he is trustworthy according to the people of hadith. What is mutawatir from it is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise.” The meaning of enumerate is to count and memorize them. Others have been said, which we have explained in our book. We mentioned there the authenticity of the hadith of al-Tirmidhi, and we mentioned the names that were agreed upon and those that were disputed, which we have come across in the books of our Imams, which number more than two hundred names. Before specifying them, we mentioned in the introduction to the book thirty-two chapters regarding their rulings, so whoever wants them can find them there and in other books written on this subject. And God is the Guide to what is right, there is no Lord but Him. Third: The scholars differed in this regard regarding the name and the named. We have mentioned what the scholars have said about this in the book Al-Asna. Ibn Al-Hisar said: In this verse, the name is used for the named and it is used for the designation. His saying, And to God is used for the named, and his saying, the names is the plural of a name used for the designations. Evidence of the correctness of what we have said is his saying, So call upon Him by them. The ha in his saying, So call upon Him refers to the named, glory be to Him, so He is the one called upon. The ha in his saying, by them refers to the names, which are the designations by which He is called upon, and not by anything else. This is what the Arabic language requires. Similar to that is the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have five names, I am Muhammad and Ahmad. The hadith. Something of this was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. What the people of truth believe is that the name is the named, or an attribute of it related to it, and that it is not the name. Ibn Al-Arabi said when discussing the Almighty’s statement, And to God belong the best names: There are three opinions on this. Some of our scholars said: This is evidence that the name is the named, because if it were other than Him, then the names would have to be for other than God Almighty. Second: Others said: What is meant by it are the names, because He, glory be to Him, is One and the names are plural. I said: Ibn Atiyah mentioned in his interpretation that the names in the verse mean the designations, unanimously agreed upon by the interpreters, and nothing else is permissible. Judge Abu Bakr said in the book Al-Tamhid: The interpretation of the Prophet’s statement, may God bless him and grant him peace: God has ninety-nine names, whoever counts them will enter Paradise means that He has ninety-nine designations without dispute, and they are expressions about God Almighty having various descriptions, some of which He deserves for Himself and some of which He deserves for a description related to Him, and His names that refer to Himself are Him, and what is related to a description of Him are His names. Some of them are descriptions of His essence. Some of them are descriptions of actions. This is the interpretation of the statement of God Almighty: And to God belong the best names, so invoke Him by them meaning the best designations. Third: Others among them said: And to God belong the attributes. Fourth: God Almighty called His names the Most Beautiful because they are beautiful to the ears and hearts, as they indicate His Oneness, Generosity, Goodness, Mercy and Bounty. The Most Beautiful is a source of description. It is permissible to estimate the Most Beautiful as the feminine of the best, like the greatest is the feminine of the greatest, and the plural is the greatest and the best. According to the first, it is singular as the description of what is not rational is singular, as God Almighty said: Other purposes (Ta-Ha: 18) and O mountains, echo with him (Saba’: 10). Fifth: The Almighty said: So call upon Him by them, meaning ask Him by His names, and ask for each name what is appropriate for Him. You say: O Most Merciful, have mercy on me, O Most Wise, judge for me, O Provider, provide for me, O Guide, guide me, O Opener, open for me, O Accepter of Repentance, accept my repentance, like this. If you call upon Him by a general name, you say: O Owner, have mercy on me, O Mighty, judge for me, O Kind, provide for me. If you call upon Him by the most general and greatest name, you say: O God, then it includes every name. Do not say: O Provider, guide me, unless you mean: O Provider, provide me with good. Ibn al-Arabi said: And thus, arrange your supplication and you will be among the sincere. The conditions of supplication were mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah, and in this Surah as well. Praise be to God. Sixth - Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi included several names among His names, such as the Perfecter of His Light, the Best of Inheritors, the Best of the Deceivers, the Fourth of Three, the Sixth of Five, the Good, the Teacher, and the like. Ibn Al-Hisar said: He followed Ibn Burjan in this, as he mentioned among the names the Cleanser and other things that were not mentioned in the Book or the Sunnah. I said: As for what was mentioned of his saying that was not mentioned in the Book or the Sunnah, it came in Sahih Muslim at-Tayyib. And at-Tirmidhi at-Tirmidhi narrated it. And he narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say in his supplication: O Lord, help me and do not help against me, support me and do not support against me, and plot for me and do not plot against me.” The hadith. He said about it: A good and authentic hadith. Based on this, it is permissible to say: O best of plotters, plot for me and do not plot against me. And God knows best. We have mentioned the good and the clean in our book and other than it, which was mentioned in the report, and from the good predecessors, and what is permissible to be called and claimed, and what is permissible to be called and not claimed, and what is not permissible to be called and not claimed, according to what Sheikh Abu al-Hasan al-Ash’ari mentioned. And there it will become clear to you, God willing. The Almighty’s saying: “And leave those who blaspheme concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do.” There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty said: They blaspheme. Blasphemy means inclination and abandoning the right path. It is said: A man blasphemed in religion. And blasphemy means he deviated. And from this comes the grave's grave, because it is on its side. And blasphemy is read in two languages, and blasphemy can be in three ways: The first is by changing it as the polytheists did, and that is because they deviated from it from what it was and named their idols with it, so they derived Al-Lat from God, Al-Uzza from Al-Aziz, and Manat from Al-Mannan, as Ibn Abbas and Qatada said. The second is by adding to it. The third is by subtracting from it, as the ignorant do who invent supplications in which they call God Almighty by names other than His, and mention Him by actions other than those mentioned, and other things that are not befitting of Him. Ibn Al-Arabi said: So beware of it, and do not call upon any of you except with what is in the Book of God and the five books, which are Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawud, and Al-Nasa'i. These are the books that Islam revolves around, and what is in Al-Muwatta’, which is the origin of the books, has been included in them. Leave aside everything else, and let none of you say, I have chosen such-and-such a supplication, for God has chosen for him and sent His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to creation with that. Second: The meaning of addition to the names is likening, and the meaning of reduction is nullification. The anthropomorphists described Him with what He did not permit, and the nullifiers deprived Him of what He was described with. Therefore, the people of truth said: Our religion is a path between two paths, neither by likening nor by nullification. Sheikh Abu al-Hasan al-Bushanji was asked about monotheism and he said: Affirming an essence that is not likened to essences, nor is it nullified from the attributes. It has been said that the meaning of the Almighty’s statement: And leave those who blaspheme is leave them, do not argue with them, and do not confront them. So, according to this, the verse was abrogated by fighting, as Ibn Zayd said. It has been said that its meaning is a threat, like the Almighty’s statement: Leave Me and he whom I created alone (al-Muddathir: 11) and His statement: Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves (al-Hijr 15:3). This is what is apparent from the verse, because the Almighty said: They will be recompensed for what they used to do. And God knows best.
7:181: In the hadith, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are this nation.” It was narrated that he said: This is for you, and God has given the like of it to the people of Moses. And he recited this verse and said: There will be people from my nation who will follow the truth until Jesus, son of Mary, descends. The verse indicates that God Almighty will never leave the world without a caller to the truth at any time.
7:182: God the Almighty informed about those who denied His signs that He will lead them astray. Ibn Abbas said: They are the people of Mecca. And leading is taking gradually, one station after another. And the ladder: to wrap something, it is said: I led it and its level. And from this the dead is led in his shrouds. And it was said: It is from the degree, so leading is to descend one step after another to the intended goal. Ad-Dahhak said: Whenever they renew their disobedience to Us, We renew their blessings. And it was said to Dhul-Nun: What is the most deceiving thing with which a servant can be deceived? He said: With kindnesses and generosity, so God the Almighty said: We will lead them astray from where they do not know We bestow blessings upon them and make them forget to thank Him, and they recited: You had good thoughts about the days when they were good and you did not fear the bad things that fate would bring. The nights were safe for you, so you were deceived by them, and when the nights are clear, trouble occurs.
7:183: The Almighty said: And I will grant them respite meaning I will extend their period of time, give them time, and delay their punishment. Indeed, My plan means I am deceitful. Strong means very strong. Its origin is from the word matn, which is the thick flesh on the side of the back. It was said: It was revealed about the mockers from Quraysh, whom God killed in one night after He granted them time. Similar to it is Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly (Al-An'am: 44). It has been mentioned before.
7:184: The Almighty said: Have they not thought meaning what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought to them. Stopping at they think is good. Then He said: There is no madness in their companion in response to their saying: O you to whom the message has been sent down, indeed you are mad (al-Hijr 15:6). It was also said: It was revealed because “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood one night on Al-Safa, calling the Quraysh, one tribe after another, saying: O sons of so-and-so, warning them of God’s wrath and punishment. Then one of them said: This companion of theirs is mad, he kept making noise until morning.”
7:185: The Almighty’s saying: Have they not considered the dominion of the heavens and the earth? contains four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Have they not looked? It is a wonder that they turned away from looking at His signs, to know the perfection of His power, according to what we explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. The word malakut is one of the structures of exaggeration, and its meaning is the great king. It was mentioned previously. Second: This verse - and what is similar to it - was used as evidence by those who said that it is obligatory to look at His signs and consider His creations. They said: In the censure of God Almighty of those who do not look, and He deprives them of the benefit of their senses, He said: They have hearts with which they do not understand (Qaf: 6) and His saying: Do they not look at the sky above them, how We have constructed it? (al-Ghashiyah 88:17) and His saying: And in yourselves, so will you not see? (al-Dhariyat 51:21). Scholars have differed on the first duty: is it contemplation and reasoning, or faith, which is the belief that occurs in the heart, the validity of which is not conditional on knowledge? Al-Qadi and others have held that the first duty is contemplation and reasoning, because God, the Blessed and Exalted, does not know by necessity, but rather He knows by contemplation and reasoning through the evidence that He has established for His knowledge. Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, went to this, where he titled his book (Chapter: Knowledge before speech and action, based on the statement of God, the Almighty: So know that there is no god but God (Muhammad 47:19). Al-Qadi said: Whoever is not knowledgeable about God is ignorant, and the ignorant of Him is a disbeliever. Ibn Rushd said in his introductions: This is not clear, because faith is valid with the certainty that may be obtained by the one whom God has guided through imitation, and at first glance from considering what God has guided to consider in more than one verse. He said: Al-Baji has provided evidence for those who said that contemplation and reasoning are the first duties with the consensus of Muslims in all ages on calling the common people and the imitators believers. He said: If what they went to was correct, it would not be correct to call a believer except the one who has knowledge through contemplation and reasoning. He said: Also, if faith was not valid except after contemplation and reasoning, it would be permissible for the disbelievers, if the Muslims prevailed over them, to say to them: It is not permissible for you to kill us, because it is part of your religion that faith is not valid except after contemplation and reasoning, so delay us until we contemplate and reason. He said: This leads to leaving them on Their disbelief, and that they should not be killed until they have seen and proven. I said: This is the correct view in this chapter. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was ordered to fight people until they say there is no god but God and believe in me and what I have brought. If they do that, their blood and wealth are protected from me except for what is rightfully due, and their reckoning is with God.” Ibn al-Mundhir translated in his book al-Ashraf (mentioning the description of the perfection of faith) that all the people of knowledge who have memorized from him agreed that if a disbeliever says: I bear witness that there is no god but God and I bear witness that Muhammad is His slave and Messenger, and that everything that Muhammad brought is true, and I absolve myself from every religion that contradicts the religion of Islam - and he is an adult of sound mind - then he is a Muslim. If he returns after that and shows disbelief, then he is an apostate and what is required of an apostate is obligatory upon him. Abu Hafs al-Zanjani said: Our Sheikh, the judge Abu Ja`far Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Samnani, used to say: The first of the obligations is belief in God and in His Messenger and in all that he brought, then contemplation and reasoning that lead to knowledge of God the Most High. So the obligation of belief in God the Most High takes precedence in his view over knowledge of God. He said: This is closer to the truth and easier for people, because most of them do not know the reality of knowledge, contemplation and reasoning. So if we say: The first of the obligations is Knowing God would lead to the excommunication of many and many, and that only a few people would enter Paradise. This is unlikely, because the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, has stated that the majority of the people of Paradise are his nation, and that the nations of all the prophets are one row, while his nation is eighty rows. This is clear and there is no doubt about it. Praise be to God. Third: Some of the later and earlier theologians went to the view that whoever does not know God Almighty through the methods they have used and the research they have written, his faith is not valid and he is an unbeliever. Accordingly, it is necessary to declare most Muslims unbelievers, and the first to start declaring them unbelievers are their fathers, ancestors and neighbors. Some of them were criticized for this and said: Do not criticize me for the large number of people in Hell. Or something like that. I said: This statement can only be made by someone who is ignorant of the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Prophet, because he has restricted the vast mercy of God to a small group of theologians, and they have rushed to declare the general Muslims infidels. Where is this in comparison to the statement of the Bedouin who uncovered his private parts to urinate, and the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rebuked him: O God, have mercy on me and Muhammad, and do not have mercy on anyone with us. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have restricted what is vast. Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Al-Tirmidhi, and other imams. Do you see that this Bedouin knew God through evidence, proof, argument, and explanation? And that His mercy encompasses everything, and how many like him are judged to have faith. Rather, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was satisfied with many of those who converted to Islam by uttering the two testimonies of faith, and he even was satisfied with a gesture in that. Do you not see when he said to the black woman: Where is God? She said: In the sky. He said: Who am I? She said: You are the Messenger of God. He said: Free her, for she is a believer. There was no contemplation or reasoning, rather he judged their faith from the first glance, even though there was some negligence regarding contemplation and knowledge. And God knows best. Fourth: Looking and contemplating should also not be done at the beautiful faces of beardless men and women. Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: Abu al-Tayyib Tahir ibn Abdullah al-Tabari said: I have been informed about this group that listens to hearsay that they add to it looking at the face of a beardless man, and perhaps they adorn it with jewelry and dyed clothes, and they claim that they intend by it to increase faith through looking and contemplating and deducing the craftsmanship from the Creator. This is the ultimate in following desires, deceiving the mind and contradicting knowledge. Abu al-Faraj said: Imam Abu al-Wafa ibn Aqil said: God did not permit looking except at a form that the soul has no inclination towards, nor does desire have a share in it, but rather a lesson that is not mixed with desire, nor does it include pleasure. For this reason, God Almighty did not send a woman as a messenger, nor did He make her a judge, nor an imam, nor a muezzin, all because she is a place of desire and temptation. So whoever says: I find lessons in beautiful images, we call him a liar. And whoever distinguishes himself with a nature that takes him out of our nature, we call him a liar, and these are only the tricks of Satan for the claimants. Some wise men said: Everything in the macrocosm has a counterpart in the microcosm. That is why God Almighty said: Indeed, We created man in the best of stature (al-Tin 95:4) and said: And in yourselves - then will you not see? (al-Dhariyat 51:21). We have already explained the analogy at the beginning of Al-An’am. So the wise man should look at himself and reflect on his creation from the perspective of his being gushing water to his being a sound creation, aided by nourishment, raised by kindness, and preserved by milk until he gains strength and reaches maturity. And if he says: I, I, and forgets that when a period of time came upon him, he was nothing worth mentioning, and he will return buried, then woe to him if he is regretful. God the Almighty said: “And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a secure lodging” - until His saying - You will be resurrected (al-Mu’minun 23:12-16). So he sees that he is a servant who is being cared for and charged with responsibility, frightened with punishment if he falls short, and hoping for reward if he obeys. So he is less devoted to worshipping his Master, for even though he does not see Him, He does not fear people, and God is more deserving of being feared, and not even one of God’s servants is arrogant, for he is composed of destinies, loaded with filth, destined for Paradise if he obeys, or to Hell. Ibn al-Arabi said: Our sheikhs liked for a person to look at the wise verses that gathered these scientific descriptions: How can he be proud of his return, his companion forever? He is from him, to him, his brother and his foster son. He invites him to the Hashish while he is young, and he obeys him. God the Almighty said: And God has not created anything is in apposition to what preceded it, meaning in what God created of things. And that perhaps their term has drawn near meaning in their terms that may have drawn near, so it is in the accusative case in apposition to what preceded it. Ibn Abbas said: What he meant by the approaching of the term was the Day of Badr and the Day of Uhud. Then in what statement after it will they believe? meaning in what Qur’an other than what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought will they believe? It was said: The ha is for the term, meaning in what statement after the term will they believe when belief will be of no benefit, because the Hereafter is not a place of obligation.
7:186: He explained that their turning away was because God led them astray. This is a refutation of the Qadarites. And leaves them in their transgression in the nominative case as a resumption. It was also read in the jussive case based on the position of the fa’ and what follows it. They are blind means they are confused. It was also said: they are hesitating. This has already been fully discussed at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah.
7:187: God Almighty says: “They ask you about the Hour: when will it come?” When is a question about time, like when. The rajaz poet said: When will my need be met? When? Don't you see that it is time for her to succeed? The Jews used to say to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: If you are a prophet, then tell us about the Hour, when will it occur? It was narrated that the polytheists said that out of extreme denial. And its anchorage is in the nominative case according to Sibawayh, and the predicate is when. It is a circumstance built on the fat-ha, built because it has the meaning of interrogation. And its anchorage with the damma on the meem, from God has established it, meaning He has made it firm, meaning when will it occur. And with the fat-ha on the meem, from Rasta, meaning it has become firm and stopped, and from it and firm pots (Saba’: 13). Qatada said: meaning firm. Say, ‘The knowledge thereof is only with my Lord,’ subject and predicate, meaning He has not made it clear to anyone, so that the servant is always on guard. He does not reveal it, meaning He does not make it apparent. Lawwaqtuha, meaning at its time, except Him. And manifestation means making something apparent. It is said: So-and-so revealed the report to me if he revealed it and made it clear. The meaning of Its knowledge is heavy in the heavens and the earth is that its knowledge is hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth. And everything whose knowledge is hidden is heavy on the heart. It was said: Its coming is too great for the people of the heavens and the earth, according to Al-Hasan and others. Ibn Jurayj and Al-Suddi: Its description is too great for the people of the heavens and the earth. Qatada and others said: The meaning is that the heavens and the earth cannot bear it because of its greatness: because the sky is split, the stars are scattered, and the seas are dried up. It was said: The meaning is that the question is too heavy for it. It will not come to you except suddenly meaning suddenly, a source in the place of a state. They ask you as if you are knowledgeable about it meaning knowledgeable about it and ask a lot about it. Ibn Faris said: Al-Hafi is the one who knows something. And Al-Hafi is the one who investigates the question. Al-A’sha said: If you ask about me, then, O Lord, ask me about Al-A’sha, where he ascended. It is said: He is afḥā in the question and in the request, so he is ḥaḥf and ḥaḥfī in the form of multiplication, like ḥaḥb and ḥaḥfī. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: The meaning is that they ask you as if you are afḥā in the question about it, i.e. urgent. He believes that there is no precedence or delay in the speech. Ibn Abbas and others said: It is a precedence or delay, and the meaning is: They ask you about it as if you are afḥā with them, i.e. eager to be kind to them and happy with their question. This is because they said: There is kinship between us and you, so tell us the time of the Hour. “Say: Its knowledge is only with God, but most people do not know.” This is not a repetition, but one of the two knowledges is for its occurrence and the other is for its absence.
7:188: The Almighty said: "Say: I do not possess for myself any benefit or harm." That is, I do not possess the ability to bring good to myself or ward off evil from myself, so how can I possess knowledge of the Hour? It was also said: I do not possess for myself guidance or misguidance. Except what God wills is in the accusative case as an exception. The meaning is: Except what God wills to possess me and enable me to do. Sibawayh recited: He does whatever he wants to people And if I had known the unseen, I would have increased in goodness. The meaning is, if I had known what God Almighty wanted from me before He made it known to me, I would have done it. It was also said: If I had known when I would be victorious in war, I would have fought and not been defeated. Ibn Abbas said: If I had known the year of famine, I would have prepared enough for it in the time of abundance. It was also said: The meaning is, if I had known the trade that would be profitable, I would have bought it when it was in decline. It was also said: The meaning is, if I had known when I would die, I would have increased in good deeds, according to Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj. It was also said: The meaning is, if I had known the unseen, I would have answered all those asked about. All of this is intended, and God knows best. "And no harm has touched me. I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings to a people who believe." This is a new statement, meaning I am not mad, because they attributed it to madness. It was also said: It is connected, and the meaning is, if I had known the unseen, no harm would have touched me and I would have been cautious. This is indicated by the Almighty's statement: I am only a warner and a bringer of good tidings.
7:189: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: It is He who created you from one soul. The majority of commentators said: What is meant by the one soul is Adam. And made from it its mate meaning Eve. That he might dwell in tranquility with her so that he might be comforted and reassured by her, and all of this was in Paradise. Then He began with another state in this world after their descent, saying: So when he had covered her as a metaphor for intercourse. She bore a light burden Everything that is in the belly or on the top of a tree is a burden with the fat-ha. And if it is on the back or on the head, it is a burden with the kasra. Yaqub narrated the kasra regarding the burden of the palm tree. Abu Saeed al-Sirafi said: It is said about a woman’s pregnancy, pregnancy and pregnancy, sometimes likening it to a woman’s pregnancy because of its internalization, and sometimes because of its emergence and appearance to the pregnancy of an animal. Pregnancy is also a source of pregnancy meaning to carry meaning to carry if it is strong. So she passed by it meaning the semen, meaning she continued with that light burden. He says: She stands and sits and turns over, and does not care about its burden until it becomes heavy, from al-Hasan, Mujahid and others. It was said: The meaning is that the pregnancy continued with her, so it is from the inverted form, as you say: I put the cap on my head. Abdullah bin Omar read: Fa-mara-ta-bih with an alif and with a light pronunciation, from mar-ya-mur if he went and came and moved around. Ibn Abbas and Yahya bin Ya’mar read: Fa-mara-ta-bih with a light pronunciation from al-mariyah, meaning she doubted what had happened to her, whether it was pregnancy or illness, or something like that. Second: The Almighty’s saying: So when it became heavy means it became heavy, as you say: the palm tree bore fruit. It was also said: it entered into the heavy, as you say: it became morning and evening. They called upon God, their Lord The pronoun in called upon refers to Adam and Eve. According to this saying, what was narrated in the stories of this verse is that when Eve became pregnant for the first time, she did not know what it was. This strengthens the reading of the one who read so she passed by it with the lightening. So she was alarmed by that, and Satan found a way to her. Al-Kalbi said: Satan came to Eve in the form of a man when she became heavily pregnant in the first place, and he said: What is this that is in your belly? She said: I do not know! He said: I am afraid that it is an animal. So she said that to Adam, peace be upon him. They were always worried about that. Then he returned to her and said: It is from God in a position, so if I call upon God and she gives birth to a human, will you name him after me? She said: Yes. He said: Then I will call upon God. So he came to her after she had given birth and said: Name him after me. She said: What is your name? He said: Al-Harith - if he had named himself to her, she would have known him - so she named him Abd al-Harith. Something similar to this is mentioned in the weak hadith, in al-Tirmidhi and others. And in the Israelite stories there are many that are not reliable, so no one with a heart should rely on them, because Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, even if the deceiver deceived them about God, the believer is not stung by the same stone twice, although it was written and recorded. He said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He deceived them twice, he deceived them in heaven and deceived them on earth.” This was supported by Al-Salami’s reading of Atishrikoon with the letter ta. The meaning of righteous is a healthy child.
7:190: So when He gave them a good child, they attributed to Him partners in what He had given them. Scholars differed in the interpretation of the polytheism attributed to Adam and Eve, which is: Third: The commentators said: It was polytheism in the name and description, not in worship and lordship. The scholars of meanings said: They did not go to the point that Al-Harith was their Lord by naming their son Abd Al-Harith, but they intended that Al-Harith was the reason for the son’s salvation, so they named him thus as a man names himself the servant of his guest out of submission to him, not that the guest is his Lord, as Hatim said: I am the guest's slave as long as he is staying, and there is nothing in me but that from the nature of the slave Some people said: This refers to the gender of the humans and the clarification of the state of the polytheists from the descendants of Adam, peace be upon him, which is what is relied upon. So his saying: They made for him means the male and female disbelievers, and he means both genders. And the evidence for this is So exalted is God above what they associate with Him and he did not say they associate with Him. This is a good statement. And it was said: The meaning is He is the One who created you from one soul from one form and one shape And made from it its mate meaning from its gender And when he covered her meaning the two genders. According to this statement, there is no mention of Adam and Eve in the verse, so if He gave them a child who was good, sound and perfect as they wanted him, they turned him away from the fitrah to polytheism, and this is the action of the polytheists. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: There is no newborn except that he is born upon the fitrah - in a narration on this religion - his parents make him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian. Ikrimah said: It was not specific to Adam, but rather made it general for all creation after Adam. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: This is more surprising to the people of insight, because of the great things in the first statement regarding the Prophet of God, Adam. The people of Medina and Asim read shirk on the basis of monotheism. Abu Amr and the rest of the people of Kufa read it in the plural, like fa’la’, the plural of partner. Al-Akhfash Sa’id rejected the first reading, which is correct with the deletion of the genitive, meaning they made him a partner, like And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82), so the meaning goes back to that they made partners for him. Fourth: The verse indicates that pregnancy is a disease. Ibn Al-Qasim and Yahya narrated on the authority of Malik who said: The beginning of pregnancy is ease and joy, and its end is a disease. What Malik said, that it is a disease, is given by the apparent meaning of his statement: They called upon God, their Lord. This state is seen in pregnant women, because of the seriousness of the matter and the severity of the situation. He made her death a martyrdom, as mentioned in the hadith: If this is proven from the apparent meaning of the verse, then the pregnant woman is like the sick person in his actions. There is no disagreement among the scholars of the countries that the actions of the sick person in what he gives and favors are in his third. Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i said: This only applies to the pregnant woman in the case of labor, but not before that. They argued that pregnancy is a normal condition and most often it is safe. We said: Likewise, most illnesses are mostly safe, and someone who is not sick may die. Fifth: Malik said: If a pregnant woman has been pregnant for six months, she is not permitted to make up for her wealth except for one-third. And whoever divorces his wife while she is pregnant with an irrevocable divorce, and when six months have passed, he wants to take her back, he is not permitted to do so, because she is sick and the marriage of a sick woman is not valid. Sixth: Yahya said: I heard Malik say about a man who attends combat: If he marches in the ranks to fight, he is not permitted to spend anything on his money except a third, and he is like a pregnant woman or a sick person who is in fear of being in that condition. And the one imprisoned for killing is included in this in retaliation. Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i and others disagreed on this. Ibn Al-Arabi said: If you look closely, you will not find that the one imprisoned for killing is in a worse condition than the sick person, and denying that is a negligence in looking, because the cause of death is present in both of them, just as sickness is the cause of death. God the Almighty said: “And you were wishing for death before you met it. But now you have seen it while you are looking.” Ruwaished Al-Ta’i said: O rider, mixing your mount, ask the Banu Asad, what is this sound? And tell them to hasten to make an excuse and seek a word that will acquit you, for I am death. What indicates this is the saying of God the Almighty: When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes turned away and the hearts reached to the throats (al-Ahzab 33:10). So how can Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa say that the severe situation is only a duel, when God the Almighty has informed us about resisting the enemy and the two parties coming together in this great situation of hearts reaching to the throats, and of bad thoughts about God, and of the hearts shaking and turmoil, is this a situation that is seen in the sick person or not? This is something that is undoubtedly fair, and this is for the one who is steadfast in his belief, and strives in the way of God with the right striving, and witnesses the Messenger and his signs, so what about us? Seventh - Our scholars have differed regarding the one who rides the sea during times of fear, is his ruling the same as the ruling of the healthy or the pregnant person? Ibn Al-Qasim said: His ruling is the same as the ruling of the healthy person. Ibn Wahb and Ashab said: His ruling is the same as the ruling of the pregnant woman if she reaches the age of six months.
