Judge Abu Muhammad said: Their statement is more reasonable, because it is a state of fear for the soul, like the burden of pregnancy. Ibn Al-Arabi said: Ibn Al-Qasim did not ride the sea, nor did he see a worm on a stick. Whoever wants to be certain that God alone is the doer, with no doer with Him, and that causes are weak and have no connection to the one who is certain of them, and to realize trust and delegation, then let him ride the sea.
7:191: The Almighty said: Do they associate with Him that which creates nothing? That is, do they worship that which is not capable of creating anything? And they themselves are created That is, the idols are created. He said: They create with the waw and the nun because they believed that idols can harm and benefit, so it was treated like people, like His saying: In an orbit they float (al-Anbiya 21:33). And His saying: O ants, enter your dwellings (Al-Naml: 18).
7:192: And they cannot help them, nor can they help themselves. That is, the idols cannot help nor are they victorious.
7:193: The Almighty said: And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you. Al-Akhfash said: That is, if you call idols to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you call them or are silent. Ahmad bin Yahya said: Because it is the beginning of a verse. He meant that he said: Or are you silent? and he did not say or have you been silent. Silent and silent according to Sibawayh are the same. It was said: What is meant is that whoever has already been known by God will not believe. It was read La ta'aba'ukum with a shaddah and a lightened one, two languages with the same meaning. Some linguists said: Itaabahu - with a lightened one - if he went behind him and did not catch up with him. And Itaabahu - with a shaddah - if he went behind him and caught up with him.
7:194: The Almighty said: Indeed, those you invoke besides God are servants like you. He argued with them about the worship of idols. You invoke and worship. It was said: You invoke them as gods besides God meaning other than God. Idols are called servants because they are owned and subjugated by God. Al-Hasan: The meaning is that idols are created like you. And when the polytheists believed that idols can harm and benefit, He treated them like people, so He said: So invoke them and did not say So invoke them. He said: Servants, and He said: Indeed, those and did not say that which. The meaning of So invoke them is so ask them for benefit and harm. Then let them respond to you, if you should be truthful that worshipping idols benefits. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning of So invoke them is so worship them. Then God rebuked them and belittled their minds, so He said: Do they have feet with which to walk, or do they have hands with which to strike, or do they have eyes with which to see, or do they have ears with which to hear? The verse. That is, you are better than them, so how do you worship them? The purpose is to demonstrate their ignorance, because the worshipped is characterized by limbs. Saeed bin Jubair read: Indeed, those you call upon besides God are servants like you by softening in and breaking it due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, and accusative abbadan with tanween, amthalakum with accusative. The meaning is: What are those you call upon besides God as servants like you? That is, they are stones and wood, so you worship what you are more noble than. An-Nahhas said: This reading should not be read with for three reasons: First, it is contrary to the majority. Second, Sibawayh chooses to raise the predicate of in if it has the meaning of what, so he says: Indeed, Zaid is leaving, because the action of what is weak, and in in its meaning is weaker than it. Third, Al-Kisa'i claimed that in hardly comes in the speech of the Arabs with the meaning of what, except when it is followed by an affirmation, as God Almighty said: The disbelievers are only in delusion. (al-Mulk 67:20) So let them respond to you The original is for the lam to be broken, so the kasra was deleted due to its weight. Then it was said: There is an omission in the speech, the meaning is: So call them to follow you, so let them respond to you if you are truthful that they are gods.
7:195: Abu Ja`far and Shaiba read Or do they have hands with which they strike? with a damma on the ta’, which is a language. The hand, the foot, and the ear are feminine and are made diminutive with a ha’. A ya’ is added to the hand in the diminutive, and it is returned to its original form and is said: yadiyah with a shaddah because of the two ya’s coming together. God Almighty says: “Say: Call upon your partners,” meaning the idols. Then plot, you and them. Do not delay, meaning do not delay. The original is kayduni, the ya was deleted because the kasra indicates it. And so is do not delay. And kayd is deceit. And kayd is war. It is said: he went on a raid but did not encounter any plot.
7:196: My protector is God, who revealed the Book meaning the one who takes care of my support and my protection is God. The protector of something is the one who protects it and prevents harm from it. The Book is the Qur’an. And He takes care of the righteous meaning He protects them. In Sahih Muslim, "On the authority of Amr ibn al-'As, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say openly, not secretly: “Behold, the family of my father - meaning so-and-so - are not my guardians. My guardian is God and the righteous believers.” Al-Akhfash said: It was read: The guardian of God is the one who revealed the Book meaning Gabriel. An-Nahhas. This is the reading of Asim al-Jahdari. The first reading is clearer, because of his saying: And He is the guardian of the righteous.
7:197: God Almighty said: And those whom you call upon besides Him. He repeated it to show that what they worship neither benefits nor harms.
7:198: And if you call them to guidance is a condition, and the answer is they do not hear. "And you see them" is a new sentence. "Looking at you" is in the place of the state. It means the idols. The meaning of looking is opening the eyes to the one being looked at, that is, and you see them as if they are looking at you. And the report about them is with the waw, and they are inanimate objects that do not see, because the report is based on the action of someone who has a mind. And it was said: They had eyes made of manufactured jewels, and that is why He said: "And you see them looking." And it was said: What is meant by that are the polytheists, He informed about them that they do not see when they did not benefit from their sight.
7:199: It has three issues: First: This verse consists of three words, which include the principles of the Sharia regarding commands and prohibitions. His statement, Take what is easy, includes maintaining ties with those who have severed ties, forgiving sinners, being kind to believers, and other morals of the obedient. His statement, And enjoin what is right, includes maintaining ties of kinship, fearing God in what is permissible and what is forbidden, lowering the gaze, and preparing for the eternal home. His statement, And turn away from the ignorant, encourages people to cling to knowledge, turn away from the people of injustice, and refrain from arguing with fools. He equates the ignorant with the stupid, and other praiseworthy morals and wise actions. I said: These qualities need to be expanded upon, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered them for Jabir bin Salim. Jabir bin Salim Abu Jari said: I got on my camel and came to Mecca and sought the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). I dismounted at the door of the mosque and they directed me to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace). He was sitting wearing a woollen cloak with red stripes. I said: Peace be upon you, O Messenger of God. He said: And upon you be peace. I said: We, the Bedouins, are harsh people, so teach me a few words by which God will benefit me. He said: Come closer three times. So I came closer and he said: Repeat to me. So I repeated it to him and he said: Fear God and do not belittle any good deed. Meet your brother with a cheerful face and empty your bucket into the vessel of the one who is asking for water. If someone insults you with something he does not know about you, do not insult him with something you know about, for God will reward you and make him bear a burden. Do not insult anything that God has given you. Abu Jari said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, I did not insult a sheep or a camel after that.” Abu Bakr al-Bazzar included it in his Musnad with the same meaning. Abu Saeed al-Maqburi narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: You cannot satisfy people with your wealth, but you can satisfy them with a cheerful face and good character.” Ibn al-Zubayr said: God did not reveal this verse except regarding people’s morals. Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Hisham bin Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Abdullah bin al-Zubayr regarding his statement: Show forgiveness and enjoin what is right. He said: God did not reveal this verse except regarding people’s morals. Sufyan bin Uyaynah narrated on the authority of al-Sha’bi that he said: “Gabriel came down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: I do not know until I ask the scholar. In another narration: I do not know until I ask my Lord. So he went and stayed for an hour, then returned and said: God Almighty commands you to forgive those who wronged you, give to those who deprived you, and connect with those who cut you off.” Some poets composed it and said: Noble morals are in three, whoever has them is perfect, then that is the young man Give to those you deprive, connect to those you cut off, and forgive those who transgress. Jaafar al-Sadiq said: God commanded His Prophet to have good morals in this verse, and there is no verse in the Qur’an that is more comprehensive of good morals than this verse. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was sent to perfect good morals. The poet said: All things will pass away and end except for praise, for it will remain with you. Even if I were to choose every virtue, I would choose none but good morals. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: God spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai. He was asked: What did He command you? He said: Nine things: Fear in secret and in public, speaking the truth in pleasure and anger, moderation in poverty and wealth, and He commanded me to connect with those who cut me off, to give to those who deprived me, to forgive those who wronged me, and for my speech to be remembrance, my silence to be contemplation, and my gaze to be a lesson. I said: It was narrated on the authority of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: My Lord has commanded me to be sincere in secret and in public, to be just in pleasure and anger, to be moderate in wealth and poverty, to forgive those who wrong me, to connect with those who cut me off, to give to those who deprive me, and for my speech to be a reminder, my silence to be a reflection, and my gaze to be a lesson. It has been said that what is meant by his saying: Take what is forgiven is the zakat, because it is a small part of a lot. There is some distance in this, because it is from ‘afā if it is studied. It may also be said: Take what is forgiven from him, meaning do not reduce it for him and forgive him. The reason for the revelation is to reject it, and God knows best. For when He commanded him to argue with the polytheists, He guided him to noble morals, because they are the reason for drawing the polytheists to faith. That is, accept from people what they forgive you of their morals and make it easy. You say: I took my right easily and simply. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And enjoin what is right meaning what is right. Isa bin Omar read al-‘urf with two dammahs, like al-ḥilm, and they are two languages. Al-‘urf, al-‘arūf, and al-‘arfah: every good characteristic that the mind approves of and the souls are reassured by. The poet said: He who does good will not lose his reward. Customs between God and people will not be lost. Ata’ said: And turn away from the ignorant, meaning There is no god but God. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And turn away from the ignorant. That is, if you establish proof against them and command them to do good and they act ignorantly towards you, then turn away from them, to protect Him from them and to raise His status above their response. Although this was addressed to His Prophet, peace be upon him, it is a discipline for all of His creation. Ibn Zayd and Ata’ said: It was abrogated by the verse of the sword. Mujahid and Qatadah said: It is decisive, and this is the correct one, as narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, who said: Uyaynah bin Hisn bin Hudhayfah bin Badr came and stayed with his nephew Al-Hur bin Qays bin Hisn, and he was one of the men whom Umar brought close to him, and the reciters were the companions of Umar’s gatherings and consultations, whether they were old or young. Uyaynah said to his nephew: O my nephew, do you have a position with this ruler, so that you may ask permission for me to see him? He said: I will ask permission for you to see him, so he asked permission for Uyaynah. When he entered, he said: O son of Al-Khattab, by God, you do not give us enough, nor do you judge between us with justice! Umar became so angry that he was about to attack him. Al-Hurr said: O Commander of the Faithful, God said to His Prophet, peace be upon him: Show forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant, and this is one of the ignorant. By God, Omar did not go beyond it when he recited it to him, and he was a reverent adherent of the Book of God Almighty. I said: The use of this verse by Omar, may God be pleased with him, and the use of it by al-Hurr indicates that it is decisive and not abrogated. Likewise, al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them both, used it, as will be explained. If the rudeness towards the ruler was deliberate and disregarded his rights, then he may punish him. But if it was otherwise, then he may turn away, forgive, and pardon, as the just caliph did.
7:200: There are two issues: First: “When the Almighty’s words were revealed: ‘Take what is easy,’ he, peace be upon him, said: How, Lord, and anger? Then it was revealed: And if he tempts you". The temptation of the devil: his whispers. There are two languages for it, nazgh and naghz, it is said: Beware of nazagh and naghaz, and they are the ones who incite. Al-Zajjaj: Nazgh is the slightest movement that can occur, and from the devil the slightest whisper. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: I witnessed Uthman and Ali, and there was a temptation between them from the devil, and neither of them left anything for the other, then they did not leave until each of them sought forgiveness for the other. The meaning of nazghnak is: it befalls you and presents to you when angry with a temptation that is not permissible. Seek refuge in God means seek salvation from that in God. So God commanded that the temptation be repelled by resorting to Him and seeking refuge in Him, and God is the highest example. One should not seek refuge from dogs except with the Lord of dogs. It was narrated from one of the predecessors that he said to his student: What do you do with the devil if he tempts you to sin? He said: I will fight him. He said: What if he returns? He said: I will fight him. He said: What if he returns? He said: I will fight him. He said: This takes a long time. Have you seen if You passed by sheep and their dog barked at you and prevented you from crossing. What should you do? He said: I will struggle with it and try my best to repel it. He said: This will take a long time, but seek help from the owner of the sheep and he will stop him from doing so. Second: Nazg, Nazg, Hamz and Waswasah are the same. God the Almighty said: “And say: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils” (al-Mu’minun 23:97) and He said: From the evil of the retreating whisperer (al-Nas 114:4). The root of Nazg is corruption. It is said: Nazgha bainaina, meaning he corrupted. And from this is His statement: Satan has incited between me and my brothers (Yusuf 12:100) meaning he corrupted. It is said: Nazg is seduction and temptation, and the meanings are close. I said: Similar to this verse is what is in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The devil comes to one of you and says to him, “Who created such and such?” until he says to him, Who created your Lord? When he reaches the point, let him seek refuge in God and stop. And in it, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about whisperings. He said: That is pure faith. In the hadith of Abu Hurairah: That is clear faith. And the clear and pure. This is not to be taken literally, because it is not correct for whisperings themselves to be faith, because faith is certainty. Rather, the reference is to the fear they found from God, the Most High, that they would be punished for what they did. It is as if he said that your anxiety about this is pure faith and its sincerity, because of the soundness of your faith and your knowledge of its corruption. So he called whisperings faith because repelling them, turning away from them, rejecting them, not accepting them, and being anxious about them all stem from faith. As for his command to seek refuge with God, it is because those whisperings are the effects of Satan. As for the command to stop, it is to refrain from relying on them and turning towards them. So whoever has sound faith and does what his Lord and Prophet have commanded him to do, it will benefit him and he will benefit from it. As for the one who is overcome by doubt and his senses are overwhelmed and he is unable to separate from it, then it is necessary to address him directly with rational evidence, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the one who was overcome by doubt about the mangy camels when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, There is no contagion. An Arab said: What is the matter with camels that are in the sand like gazelles, and when a mangy camel enters them, it makes them mangy? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Who infected the first one? Thus, he uprooted the doubt from its roots. When Satan despaired of tempting and misleading the companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he began to disturb their time with those whispers. And whispers are: outings, so their hearts were repelled by them and they found their occurrence difficult, so they came - as in the Sahih - and said: O Messenger of God! We find in ourselves that which one of us would be too ashamed to speak of. He said: Have you found it? They said: Yes. He said: That is clear faith, in spite of Satan, according to what the Qur’an says in His saying: Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority. (al-Hijr 15:42). Thoughts that are not settled and are not brought about by doubt are what are repelled by turning away from them, and the name of whispering is applied to such thoughts. And God knows best. This meaning has already been mentioned at the end of Surat Al-Baqarah, and praise be to God.
7:201: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who fear God meaning polytheism and sins. When an impulse from Satan touches them This is the reading of the people of Basra and Mecca, and the reading of the people of Medina and Kufa is Ta’if. It was narrated on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr Tayf with a shaddah on the ya. An-Nahhas said: The speech of the Arabs in such a case is Tayf with a light ya, as a source from tafa yatif. Al-Kisa’i said: It is a light tayf like mayt and mayt. An-Nahhas said: The meaning of tayf in the language is what is imagined in the heart or seen in a dream, and this is the meaning of ta’if. Abu Hatim said: I asked Al-Asma’i about tayf, and he said: There is no fa’il in the sources. An-Nahhas said: It is not a source, but it can mean ta’if. The meaning is: Indeed, those who fear sins, when something befalls them, they reflect on the power of God Almighty and His blessings upon them, so they abandon sin. It was said: Tayf and ta’if have two different meanings. The first is imagination. The second is Satan himself. The first is a source of the verb tāfa al-khayal yatuwwaf tayfan, and they did not say ta’if in the active participle from this. Al-Suhayli said that it is because it is an imagination and not a reality. As for his statement: And a company from your Lord circulated over them (al-Qalam 68:19), it is not said about it: tayf, because it is a real active participle, and it is said that it is Gabriel. Al-Zajjaj said: I circulated over them, I circulate, and I circulated the imagination, I circulate. Hassan said: So leave this but it is nice to keep me awake when dinner is over Mujahed: The spectre is anger. Madness, anger, and whispering are called spectres, because they are a gathering of the devil similar to the gathering of imagination. So when they see, meaning they are finished. It was also said: So when they are on insight. Saeed bin Jubair read: Then they remember, with emphasis on the letter dhal. It has no basis in Arabic, as mentioned by Al-Nahhas. Second: Issam bin Al-Mustaliq said: I entered the city and saw Al-Hassan bin Ali, peace be upon them, and I was impressed by his appearance and his good looks, so the envy that my heart had for his father stirred up in me, so I said: Are you the son of Abu Talib? He said: Yes. So I exaggerated in cursing him and cursing his father, so he looked at me with a compassionate and merciful look, then he said: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan, in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, Accept forgiveness, enjoin what is right, and turn away from the ignorant, then he recited until His saying: Then behold, they will see, then he said to me: Take it easy, I ask God for forgiveness for myself and you, for if you had sought our help, we would have helped you, and if you had sought our assistance, we would have supported you, and if you had sought our guidance, we would have guided you. So he saw in me regret for what I had neglected, so he said: “No blame upon you this Day. God will forgive you, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.” (Yusuf 12:92) Are you from the people of Ash-Sham? I said: Yes. So he said: I know a song from Akhzam May God keep you safe, healthy and well. Come to us with your needs and whatever comes your way, and you will find us up to your expectations, God willing. Issam said: The earth, despite its vastness, became too narrow for me, and I wished it would swallow me up. Then I slipped away from it seeking refuge, and there was no one on the face of the earth more beloved to me than him and his father.
7:202: The Almighty says: And their brothers extend them in error and then do not stop. It was said: The meaning is the brothers of the devils, who are the wicked among the misguided people, the devils extend them in error. It was said: The wicked are brothers of the devils because they accept from them. The devil was mentioned before in this verse. This is the best that was said about it, and it is the saying of Qatada, Al-Hasan and Ad-Dahhak. The meaning of they do not stop is they do not repent or return. Al-Zajjaj said: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: And those whom you call upon besides Him cannot help you nor can they help themselves, and their brothers extend them in error, because the disbelievers are brothers of the devils. The meaning of the verse is: If a believer is touched by a phantom from the devil, he is awakened from nearness, but as for the polytheists, the devil extends them. And they do not stop. It was said: It refers to the disbelievers according to both opinions. It was said: It is permissible for it to refer to the devil. Qatada said: The meaning is then they do not stop with them and do not have mercy on them. And the shortening: is to refrain from something, i.e. the devils do not shorten their support of the infidels with error. His saying: in error may be connected to his saying: they support them, and it may be connected to the brothers. And error: ignorance. Nafi’ read they support them with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the meem. The rest read it with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the meem. They are two languages: madd and amd. Madd is more, without the alif, as Makki said. An-Nahhas: A group of Arab scholars reject the reading of the people of Medina, including Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid. Abu Hatim said: I do not know of a reason for it, except that the meaning is that they increase them in error. A group of linguists, including Abu Ubaid, narrated that it is said that if something increases something by itself, it is madd, and if it increases it by something else, it is said amd, like your Lord supports you with five thousand marked angels (Al Imran 3:125). It was narrated from Muhammad bin Yazid that he provided evidence for the reading of the people of Medina, saying: It is said I supported him in such-and-such, meaning I made it attractive to him and called him to do it. And I supported him in such and such, meaning I helped him with an opinion or something else. Makki said: The preferred form is the fat-ha, because it is said: I supported him in evil, and I supported him in good. God the Almighty said: And He extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly (al-Baqarah 2:15). This indicates the strength of the fat-ha in this letter, because it is in evil, and ghayy is evil, and because the group is upon it. Asim Al-Jahdari read yamadunahum fi al-ghayy. Isa bin Omar read yaqasirun with a fat-ha on the ya, a damma on the sad, and a light qaf. The rest read yaqasirun with its opposite. They are two languages. Imru’ Al-Qais said: I miss you so much after it was short
7:203: God the Almighty says: And if you do not bring them a sign meaning, do not recite it to them. They say, 'Why did you not select it?' Lawla means Why not. And nothing follows it in this meaning except the verb, explicit or implicit, and we have already discussed it in detail in Surat Al-Baqarah. The meaning of I selected it is that you invented it from yourself. So inform them that the signs are from God the Almighty, and that He does not recite to them except what He revealed to Him. It is said: I selected the speech meaning you improvised it and made it up, and invented it if you brought it from yourself. Say, 'I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord' meaning from God, not from myself. These are insights from your Lord meaning the Qur'an, the plural of insight, which is evidence and a lesson. That is, what I have shown you that God the Almighty is One is insights, meaning insight is gained through them. Al-Zajjaj said: insights means paths, and insights are paths of religion. Al-Ja'fi said: They carried their insight on their shoulders, but they used my insight to count. Guidance means clear guidance. Mercy means blessing.
7:204: There are two issues: First: The Almighty said: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent. It was said that this was revealed about prayer. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, Abu Hurairah, Jabir, Az-Zuhri, Ubaid ibn Umair, Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, and Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab. Sa’id said: The polytheists would come to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when he prayed, and some of them would say to each other in Mecca: Do not listen to this Qur’an and make noise during it. (Fussilat 41:26) So God, the Almighty, revealed in response to them: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent. It was said that it was revealed about the sermon. This was said by Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Ata’, Amr ibn Dinar, Zayd ibn Aslam, Al-Qasim ibn Muhaymrah, Muslim ibn Yasar, Shahr ibn Hawshab, and Abdullah ibn Al-Mubarak. This is weak, because there is little Qur’an in it, and listening is obligatory in all of them, as Ibn Al-Arabi said. Al-Naqqash: The verse was revealed in Mecca, and there was no sermon or Friday prayer in Mecca. Al-Tabari also mentioned on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that this is in listening on the day of Eid al-Adha, the day of Eid al-Fitr, and Friday, and in what the imam recites out loud, it is general. This is correct because it includes all that this verse and other Sunnahs have required in listening. Al-Naqqash said: The people of interpretation agreed that this listening is in the obligatory and non-obligatory prayers. Al-Nahhas: In the language, it must be in everything, unless there is evidence indicating a specific thing. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for it to be: So listen to it and be silent, act according to it and do not exceed it. And listening is silence for listening, paying attention, and observing. Ansata is the subject of listening, and also naṣat, the poet said: The Imam said: Your master's command is upon you, so we did not disobey him and he listened to us as they said. It is said: Listen to him and listen to him. The poet said: If Hadham says something, listen to her, because what Hadham says is true. Some of them said about his saying, So listen to him and be silent: This was specifically for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that his companions would understand it. I said: This is far-fetched, and the correct view is the generality, because of His statement: Perhaps you will receive mercy. And specificity requires evidence. Abdul-Jabbar bin Ahmad said in his Fawa’id al-Quran: The polytheists used to make a lot of noise and disturbance out of stubbornness and obstinacy, as God related from them: And those who disbelieved said, ‘Do not listen to this Qur’an, and speak noisily during it that you may overcome.’ So God commanded the Muslims when receiving revelation to be in the opposite state and to listen, and He praised the jinn for that, saying: And when We directed towards you a company of the jinn, listening to the Qur’an (al-Ahqaf 46:29) and the verse. Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi said: “When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited in prayer, those behind him would respond to him, if he said: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, they would say the same, until he finished the opening of the Book and the surah. So he remained like that for as long as God willed, then the verse was revealed: “And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy.” So they listened.” This indicates that the meaning of listening is to refrain from speaking out loud as they used to do in response to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Qatada said about this verse: A man would come while they were praying and ask them how much they had prayed, how much was left, so God revealed: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent. Also narrated by Mujahid: They used to speak during the prayer about their needs, so God revealed: That you may receive mercy. The difference in the recitation of the follower behind the imam has already been mentioned in Al-Fatihah. The ruling on the sermon will come in Friday, God willing.
7:205: The Almighty’s saying: And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and fear is similar to Call upon your Lord in humility and secretly (al-A’raf 7:55), which has already been mentioned. Abu Ja’far Al-Nahhas said: There is no disagreement regarding the meaning of And remember your Lord within yourself that it is in supplication. I said: It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas that he meant by remembrance the recitation in prayer. It has been said: The meaning is read the Quran with contemplation and reflection. Supplication is a source, and it may be in the position of a state. And fear is conjoined with it. The plural of fear is fear, because it means fear, as mentioned by An-Nahhas. The root of fear is fear, the waw was changed to a ya because of the kasra of what precedes it. The man feared, he fears fear, fear and fearfulness, so he is fearful, and people fear according to the root, and fear is according to the word. Al-Farra’ narrated that it is also said in the plural of fear, khayf. Al-Jawhari said: Fear is fear, and the plural is khayf, and its root is waw. And without raising the voice means without raising the voice. That is, let yourself hear, as He said: And seek a way between that (al-Isra’ 17:110), meaning between raising the voice and lowering it. This indicates that raising the voice in remembrance is forbidden, as mentioned previously in more than one place. In the mornings and the evenings Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: The evenings are the evenings. And ghadw is the plural of ghadwah. Abu Majlaz read al-ghadu and al-isal, which is the source of asalna, meaning we entered in the evening. Al-asal is the plural of asl, like tanab and atnab, so it is the plural of jam’, and the singular is asil, plural of asl, according to al-Zajjaj. Al-Akhfash: Al-asal is the plural of asil, like yameen and ayman. Al-Farra’: Asl is the plural of asil, and it may be one asl, as the poet said: And there is nothing better than it when the origin is near Al-Jawhari: Asil is the time after the afternoon prayer until sunset. Its plural is asl, asals, and asa’il, as if it were the plural of asila. The poet said: By my life, you are the home whose people are most honored, and I sit in its shade in the evenings. It is also pluralized as aslan, like ba’ir and ba’ran. Then they made the plural smaller and said asilan. Then they replaced the nun with a lam and said asilal. From this is the saying of al-Nabigha: I stood there in the evening asking her questions, but she couldn’t give me an answer, and there was no one in the room Al-Lahiani said: I met him in the evening. And do not be among those who are heedless meaning of the remembrance.
7:206: It contains eight issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who are with your Lord means the angels by consensus. And He said with your Lord and God Almighty is in every place because they are close to His mercy, and everyone who is close to the mercy of God Almighty is with Him, according to Al-Zajjaj. And another said: Because they are in a place where nothing but God’s rule is implemented. And it was said: Because they are the messengers of God, just as it is said: There is a large army with the caliph. And it was said: This is to honor them, and that they are in an honored place, so it is an expression of their closeness in honor, not in distance. And they glorify Him meaning they magnify Him and declare Him free from all evil. And to Him they prostrate It was said: They pray. And it was said: They humble themselves, unlike the people of sin. Second: The majority of scholars believe that this is a place of prostration for the reciter. They differed on the number of prostrations in the Qur’an. The most that has been said is fifteen. The first is the end of Al-A’raf, and the last is the end of Al-Alaq. This is the opinion of Ibn Habib, Ibn Wahb - in one narration - and Ishaq. Some scholars added the prostration of Al-Hijr to the verse of God the Almighty: And be among those who prostrate (al-Hijr 15:98), as will be explained, God willing. Based on this, it would be sixteen. It was also said: fourteen, as Ibn Wahb said in the other narration from him. So he dropped the Hajj again. This is the opinion of the people of opinion, and the correct opinion is that it is dropped, because the hadith is not authentically proven. It was narrated by Ibn Majah and Abu Dawud in their Sunans on the authority of Abdullah bin Manin from Banu Abd Kulal, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Aas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited fifteen prostrations in the Qur’an, three of which are in the Mufassal, and two in the Hajj. And Abdullah bin Manin is not to be relied upon, said Abu Muhammad Abdul Haq. Abu Dawud also mentioned from the hadith of “Uqbah bin Amir, he said: I said: O Messenger of God, are there two prostrations in Surat Al-Hajj? He said: Yes, and whoever does not prostrate in them should not recite them. In its chain of transmission is Abdullah bin Lahi’ah, and he is very weak. Al-Shafi’i confirmed them and omitted the prostration of Sad. It was said: Eleven prostrations, and he omitted the last one of Al-Hajj and the third of Al-Mufassal. This is the well-known Maliki school of thought. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and others. In Sunan Ibn Majah, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’ who said: I prostrated with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, eleven prostrations in which there was nothing from the Mufassal: Al-A'raf, Ar-Ra'd, An-Nahl, Bani Israel, Maryam, Al-Hajj, Al-Furqan, Solomon, Surat An-Naml, Al-Sajdah, Sad, and the prostration of the Ha-Meem. It was said that there were ten, and he omitted the last one, Al-Hajj, Sad, and three of the Mufassal, as mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said that there were four, the prostration of Alif, Lam, Meem, Tanzeel, An-Najm, and Al-Alaq. The reason for the disagreement is the difference in transmission in the hadiths and practice, and their disagreement over the simple command to prostrate in the Qur'an. Does it mean the prostration of recitation or the prostration of obligation in prayer? Third: They differed about the obligation of prostration of recitation. Malik and Al-Shafi’i said: It is not obligatory. Abu Hanifa said: It is obligatory. He related that the absolute command to prostrate is obligatory, and to his saying, peace be upon him: “When the son of Adam recites a prostration and prostrates, Satan withdraws and weeps, saying, ‘Woe to me.’” And in the narration of Abu Kurayb, Woe to me. And in his saying, peace be upon him, informing about Satan - may God curse him: The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate, so he prostrated, so Paradise is for him. I was commanded to prostrate, but I refused, so Hell is for me.” Narrated by Muslim. And because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to do it regularly. Our scholars relied on the authentic hadith of Umar - narrated by al-Bukhari - “that he recited a verse of prostration on the pulpit, then he came down and prostrated, and the people prostrated with him. Then he recited it on the next Friday, and the people prepared to prostrate, so he said: O people, take your time! God did not prescribe it for us unless we wished.” This was in the presence of the Companions, may God be pleased with them all, from the Ansar and the Muhajireen. No one objected to him, so the consensus was established on this. As for his statement: The son of Adam was commanded to prostrate, it is a report about obligatory prostration. The Prophet’s regularity indicates that it is recommended! And God knows best. Fourth: There is no disagreement that prostration during the Qur’an requires what prayer requires, such as purity from ritual impurity and impurity, intention, facing the qiblah, and time. Except for what Al-Bukhari mentioned on the authority of Ibn Umar, that he used to prostrate without purity. And Ibn Al-Mundhir mentioned it on the authority of Al-Sha’bi. According to the majority of scholars, does it require the declaration of faith, raising the hands, saying Allahu Akbar, and saying tasleem? They differed on that. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq were of the view that he says Allahu Akbar and raises his hands to say Allahu Akbar for it. And it was narrated in the hadith on the authority of Ibn Umar. “When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prostrated, he would say ‘Allahu Akbar’, and when he raised his head, he would say ‘Allahu Akbar’.” The well-known Maliki school of thought is that he says ‘Allahu Akbar’ for it when lowering and raising the head in prayer. There is a difference of opinion regarding ‘Allahu Akbar’ for it outside of prayer. The majority of jurists said that ‘Allahu Akbar’ is permissible, and the majority of scholars said that there is no ‘Salam’ for it. A group of the Salaf and Ishaq said that he says ‘Salam’ for it. According to this school of thought, it is confirmed that ‘Allahu Akbar’ at the beginning of it is for the ihram. According to the opinion of those who do not say ‘Salam’, it is only for prostration. The first is more appropriate, because he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The key to prayer is purification, its prohibition is takbir, and its permission is taslim. This is an act of worship that requires takbir, so it was permitted like the funeral prayer, or rather more so, because it is an action and the funeral prayer is a statement. This is the choice of Ibn al-Arabi. Fifth: As for its time, it was said: He prostrates at all times absolutely, because it is a prayer for a reason, and this is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i and the group. It was also said: Until dawn breaks, or until the sun turns yellow after the afternoon prayer. It was also said: He does not prostrate after the dawn prayer or after the afternoon prayer. It was also said: He prostrates after the dawn prayer but does not prostrate after the afternoon prayer. These three opinions are in our school of thought. The reason for the disagreement is the opposition to what the reason for reciting the prostration requires of the prostration ordered upon it, due to the general prohibition of praying after the afternoon prayer and after the dawn prayer. Their disagreement is about the meaning for which prayer at these two times is prohibited, and God knows best. Sixth: When he prostrates, he says in his prostration: O God, remove from me a burden through it, write for me a reward through it, and make it a treasure for me with You. Narrated by Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned by Ibn Majah. Seventh: If he recites it in a prayer, if it is a voluntary prayer, he prostrates whether he is alone or in a group and there is no risk of confusion in it. If he is in a group where there is no risk of confusion in it, then the text states that it is permissible. It was said: He does not prostrate. As for the obligatory prayer, the well-known view from Malik is that he forbade it in it, whether it is a prayer recited silently or aloud, in a group or individually. It is explained by it being an increase in the number of prostrations in the obligatory prayer. It was said: It is explained by fear of confusion for the group, and this is more likely. Based on this, it is not prohibited for individuals or for a group where there is no risk of confusion in it. Eighth - Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Rafi’ who said: I prayed the Isha prayer with Abu Hurairah, and he recited When the sky is split and prostrated. I said: What is this? He said: I prostrated with it behind Abu al-Qasim, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I will not stop prostrating with it until I meet him. He is the only one who narrated it. It also includes: It was said to Imran bin Husain: A man hears the prostration and does not sit for it? He said: What do you think if he sat for it! As if it is not obligatory for him. Salman said: Why did we go out? Uthman said: Prostration is only for the one who hears it. Al-Zuhri said: One does not prostrate unless he is pure. So if you prostrate while you are in a state of ritual purity, then face the qiblah. If you are riding, it does not matter where your face is. Al-Sa’ib did not prostrate for the prostration of the one who is narrating, and God knows best.
8:1: It was a Medinan battle according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Jabir, and Ata. Ibn Abbas said: It was a Medinan battle except for seven verses, from the Almighty’s saying: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you [al-Anfal 8:30] to the end of the seven verses. It has seven issues: First: Ubadah bin Al-Samit narrated that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Badr and they encountered the enemy. When God defeated them, a group of Muslims followed them and killed them. One group surrounded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and another group seized the army and the loot. When God banished the enemy and those who sought them returned, they said: ‘The spoils are ours. We are the ones who sought the enemy and God banished and defeated them.’ Those who surrounded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘You have no more right to it than we do. Rather, it is ours. We surrounded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lest the enemy take him by surprise.’ Those who seized the army and the loot said: ‘You have no more right to it than we do. It is ours. We have taken it and seized it.’ Then God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: ‘The spoils belong to God and the Messenger. So fear God and amend that which is between you and obey God and His Messenger, if you are believers.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among them.” Abu Omar said: The scholars of Arabic said: They say: Astalwa, atafu, and hawata. It is said: Death is seized upon the servants. And His statement: He divided it into fawaq means quickly. They said: Fawaq is what is between the two milkings of a camel. It is said: He waited for him for the fawaq of a camel, meaning this amount. And they say it with dammah and fathah: fawaq and fawaq. And this was before the verse: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God (al-Anfal 8:41) was revealed. And it seems that the meaning according to the scholars is: To God and to the Messenger is the judgment and action in it in a way that brings one closer to God Almighty. Muhammad bin Ishaq mentioned: Abd al-Rahman bin al-Harith and others of our companions told me on the authority of Sulayman bin Musa al-Ashdaq on the authority of Makhul on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Bahili who said: I asked Ubadah bin al-Samit about the spoils of war and he said: It was revealed about us, the companions of Badr, when we differed about the voluntary charity and our morals deteriorated, so God took it away from our hands and gave it to the Messenger, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it up on the basis of bawa’. He said: Equally. This was the fear of God, obedience to His Messenger, and reconciliation between people. It was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) seized a great booty, and among them was a sword. I took it and brought it to the Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) and said: Give me this sword as a gift, for I know its condition. He said: Return it from where you took it. I went until I was about to throw it into the hands of the people. My soul blamed me, so I returned to him and said: Give it to me. He said: Return it from where you took it, so... God revealed: {They ask you about the spoils of war.} [Muslim]. There are many narrations, but what we have mentioned is sufficient, and God is the guide to success. The second: Al-Anfal, singular: Nafl, with a fat-ha on the Fa. He said: Indeed, fearing our Lord is the best voluntary act, and God willing, it is my inheritor and my reward. Any good booty. And the nafl is the oath, and from it the hadith: The Jews will acquit you with the nafl of fifty of them. And the nafl is the negation, and from it the hadith: Then take a nafl from her offspring. And the nafl is a well-known plant. And the nafl is the increase over the obligatory, and it is voluntary. And the offspring of a child is nafl, because it is an increase over the child. And the spoils are nafl, because it is an increase in what God has made permissible for this nation of what was forbidden to others. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was given preference over the prophets in six things - and among them - and the spoils were made lawful for me.” And the spoils are the spoils themselves. Antara said: When the battle rages, we quench our thirst with spears and protect ourselves at the spoils-of-war. Any spoils. Third: Scholars differed on the place of spoils of war into four opinions: First: Its place is in what the infidels deviated from to the Muslims or was taken without war. Second: Its place is the fifth. Third: One-fifth of the fifth. Fourth: The head of the spoils of war, according to what the Imam sees. The doctrine of Malik, may God have mercy on him, is that the spoils of war are gifts of the Imam from the fifth, according to what he sees from the effort, and there is no voluntary charity in the four fifths, and he did not see the voluntary charity from the head of the spoils of war because its people are specified and they are the ones who are in distress, and the division of the fifth is returned to the effort of the Imam. And its people are not specified. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have nothing of what God has bestowed upon you except the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you. So after this it is not possible that the voluntary gift is the right of anyone, but rather it is the right of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is the fifth. This is what is known from his school of thought, and it has been narrated from him that it is from the fifth of the fifth. This is the opinion of Ibn al-Musayyab, al-Shafi’i, and Abu Hanifa. The reason for the disagreement is the hadith of Ibn Umar, narrated by Malik, who said: “The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) sent a raiding party before Najd and they captured many camels. Their shares were twelve camels or eleven camels, and they gave each camel as a gift.” This is how Malik narrated it with doubt in the narration of Yahya from him, and a group of the narrators of Al-Muwatta’ agreed with him on this except Al-Walid bin Muslim, who narrated it from Malik bin Nafi’ from Ibn Umar, and he said in it: Their shares were twelve camels, and they gave each camel as a gift. And he did not doubt. Al-Walid bin Muslim and Al-Hakam bin Nafi’ mentioned from Shu’aib bin Abi Hamza from Nafi’ “from Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) sent us with an army before Najd - in the narration of Al-Walid: four thousand - and a raiding party from the army went out - in the narration of Al-Walid: I was among those who went out with it - so the shares of the army were twelve camels, twelve camels, and the people of the raiding party gave each camel as a gift, so their shares were thirteen camels.” Abu Dawud mentioned this as evidence for those who say that the gift is only part of the fifth. The explanation is that if this expedition had been carried out on the basis that its people were ten, for example, and they had captured one hundred and fifty in their spoils, from which one-fifth was taken thirty, and they had one hundred and twenty, and it was divided by ten, each one was entitled to twelve camels, twelve camels, then the people were given one camel each from the one-fifth, because the one-fifth of thirty does not have ten camels. So if you know what is for ten, you know what is for one hundred and a thousand and more. And the one who said that it was from the one-fifth of the one-fifth argued that it is permissible for there to be clothes sold and goods other than camels, so he gave the one who did not receive the camel the value of a camel from those goods. What supports this is what Muslim narrated in some versions of this hadith: So we captured camels and sheep, the hadith. Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned in this hadith that the prince gave them a gift before the division, and this requires that the gift be from the head of the spoils, and this is contrary to the statement of Malik. And the statement of the one who narrated the opposite is more appropriate because they are memorizers, as Abu Omar, may God have mercy on him, said. Makhool and Al-Awza’i said: A voluntary prayer should not exceed more than one-third, which is the opinion of the majority of scholars. Al-Awza’i said: If they exceed it, then it should be given to them and made part of the fifth. Al-Shafi’i said: There is no limit for a voluntary prayer that the imam should not exceed. Fourth: The hadith of Ibn Umar indicates that the Imam says before fighting: Whoever demolishes such-and-such a fortress will have such-and-such, and whoever reaches such-and-such a place will have such-and-such, and whoever brings a head will have such-and-such, and whoever brings a prisoner will have such-and-such, harming them. It was narrated on the authority of Malik that he disliked it. He said: It is fighting for the sake of the world. He did not permit it. Al-Thawri said: That is permissible and there is nothing wrong with it. I said: This meaning was transmitted from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: “When the day of Badr came, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever kills someone will have such-and-such, and whoever takes a prisoner will have such-and-such.” The hadith in its entirety. In the narration of Ikrimah from him, “From the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever does such-and-such and comes to such-and-such a place will have such-and-such.” So the young men hastened and the elders stood firm with the banners. When they were granted victory, the young men came asking for what had been given to them, but the elders said to them: Do not go with him without us, for we have been a support for you. So God Almighty revealed: And reconcile your differences. Ismail bin Ishaq also mentioned this. It was narrated from Omar bin Al-Khattab that he said to Jarir bin Abdullah Al-Bajali when he came to him with his people while he was intending to go to Ash-Sham: Would you like to go to Kufa and have a third after the fifth from every land and captives? This was said by a group of the jurists of Ash-Sham: Al-Awza’i, Makhul, Ibn Haywah, and others. They saw the fifth as part of the spoils, and the voluntary charity after the fifth, then the spoils among the people of the army. This was said by Ishaq, Ahmad, and Abu Ubaid. Abu Ubaid said: Today, people are of the opinion that there is no voluntary charity from the spoils until one-fifth is taken. Malik said: It is not permissible to say: The Imam said to a group of soldiers: Whatever you take, you have one-third of it. Sahnun said: He meant the beginning. If it decreases, it continues, and they have their shares in the remainder. Sahnun said: If the Imam said to a group of soldiers: Whatever you take, you do not have to pay one-fifth of it, then this is not permissible. If it decreases, you return it, because this is an unusual ruling that is not permissible and does not continue. Sixth: Malik, may God have mercy on him, recommended that the imam not give voluntary gifts except for what is apparent, such as a turban, horse, or sword. Some scholars forbade the imam from giving voluntary gifts of gold, silver, pearls, or the like. Some of them said: A voluntary gift is permissible of anything. This is correct, based on the statement of Umar and the implication of the verse, and God knows best. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: So fear God and amend that which is between you. This is a command to fear God and amend, meaning, be united on the command of God in supplication: O God, amend that which is between you, meaning the state in which the meeting occurs. This indicates the explicit statement that there is a dispute between them, or that the souls are inclined to quarrel, as stated in the hadith. The meaning of fear was mentioned earlier, meaning fear God in your words and actions, and amend that which is between you. And obey God and His Messenger in the spoils of war and the like. If you are believers meaning that the way of the believer is to comply with what we mentioned. It was said that if means when.
8:2: God Almighty says: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith; and upon their Lord they rely. There are three issues: First: The scholars said: This verse is an incitement to the obligation of obeying the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what he ordered regarding the division of the spoils. And fear means fear. And in its future tense there are four languages: wa-jal yu-jil, ya-jil, ya-jil, and ya-jil, as Sibawayh narrated. And the source is wa-jal, wa-jalla, and muwajjalan, with the fat-ha. And this is muwajjala with the kasra for the place and the name. So whoever said: ya-jil in the future tense made the waw an alif because of the fat-ha of what preceded it. And the language of the Qur’an is the waw They said, do not delay (al-Hijr 15:53). And whoever said: ya-jil with the kasra of the ya, it is in the language of Banu Asad, as they say: ana iya-jil, and we are Najil, and you are tai-jil, all with the kasra. And whoever said: ya-jil based it on this language, but he opened the ya as they opened it in ya-il-m, and the ya-l-m was not broken because they found the kasra on the ya-m too heavy. And it was broken in ya-jil to strengthen one of the two ya-s with the other. And the imperative from it is ya-jil, the waw became a ya-m because of the kasra of what preceded it. And she says: I am truly afraid of him. And it is not said in the feminine: wajala, but wajala. And Sufyan narrated on the authority of al-Suddi regarding the words of God Almighty: Those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, he said: If he wanted to wrong someone, he was told: Fear God, so he refrained and his heart became fearful. Second: God the Almighty described the believers in this verse as fearful and apprehensive when He is mentioned. This is due to the strength of their faith and their observance of their Lord, as if they were before Him. Similar to this verse is: And give good tidings to the humble * Who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful (al-Hajj 22:34-35). He also said: And their hearts are reassured by the remembrance of God (al-Ra’d 13:28). This goes back to the perfection of knowledge and the confidence of the heart. And apprehension is the fear of God’s punishment, so there is no contradiction. God combined the two meanings in His statement: “God has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book, repeated [in verses]. From it the skins of those who fear their Lord shiver. Then their skins and their hearts soften at the remembrance of God” (al-Zumar 39:23), meaning their souls are at peace with certainty in God, even if they fear God. This is the state of those who know God, who are afraid of His wrath and punishment, not as the ignorant common people and the innovating rabble do with their screaming, roaring, and braying that resembles the braying of donkeys. It is said to the one who does that and claims that it is piety and reverence: You have not reached the level of the state of the Messenger or the state of his companions in knowledge of God, fear of Him, and glorification of His Majesty. However, their state when they were admonished was understanding about God and crying out of fear of God. Therefore, God described the states of the people of knowledge when they hear His remembrance and the recitation of His Book, saying: “And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.’” (al-Ma’idah 5:83) This is a description of their state and an account of their words. Whoever is not like that is not on their guidance or their path. Whoever follows their example, let him follow his example. Whoever follows the state of the insane and madness is among the worst of them in state, and madness has many types. Muslim narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik that the people asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they overwhelmed him with questions. One day, he went out and ascended the pulpit and said: Ask me, do not ask me about anything but I will explain it to you as long as I am in this position. When the people heard that, they were afraid that something was about to happen before me. Anas said: I started looking right and left, and every person had his head wrapped in his garment and was crying. He mentioned the hadith. Al-Tirmidhi narrated and authenticated it on the authority of Al-Arbadh bin Sariyah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, preached to us an eloquent sermon that brought tears to our eyes and made our hearts tremble.” The hadith. He did not say: we shouted, nor danced, nor marched, nor stood up. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith, meaning belief. For the faith of this hour is an increase over the faith of yesterday, so whoever believes a second and third time, this is an increase in belief in relation to what came before. It was said: It is an increase in the expansion of the chest due to the abundance of verses and evidence, and this meaning was mentioned in Al Imran. And upon their Lord they rely, the meaning of reliance was mentioned in Al Imran as well.
8:3: Those who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them. This was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah.
8:4: Those are the true believers meaning those whose outward and inward faith are equal. This indicates that every truth has a reality, and "peace be upon him" said to Haritha: Every truth has a reality, so what is the reality of your faith?” The hadith. A man asked Al-Hasan, saying: O Abu Saeed, are you a believer? He said to him: Faith is of two types. If you are asking me about faith in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, Paradise, Hell, resurrection, and accountability, then I believe in them. But if you are asking me about the statement of God Almighty: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful - until His statement - Those are the true believers, then by God I do not know if I am one of them or not. Abu Bakr Al-Wasiti said: Whoever says I am a true believer in God, it is said to him: Truth refers to supervision, knowledge, and encompassment, so whoever lacks it, his claim about it is invalid. He means by that what the Sunnis say: The true believer is the one who is destined for Paradise, so whoever does not know that from the secret of His wisdom, then his claim that he is a true believer is incorrect.
8:5: God the Almighty said: As your Lord brought you out from your home with truth. Al-Zajjaj said: The Kaf is in the accusative case, meaning the spoils are fixed for you as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth. That is, like your Lord bringing you out from your home with truth. The meaning is: Go about your business with the spoils and give spoils to whomever you wish, even if they dislike it, because some of the Companions said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when he made something for everyone who brought a prisoner: Most people will remain without anything. So the position of the Kaf in Kama is in the accusative case as we mentioned. Al-Farra' also said the same. Abu Ubaidah said: It is an oath, meaning the one who brought you out, so the Kaf means the waw, and ma means the one who. Saeed bin Mas'adah said: The meaning is those are the true believers as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth. He said: Some scholars said: As your Lord brought you out from your home with truth, so fear God and reconcile your differences. Ikrimah said: The meaning is obey God and His Messenger as He brought you out. It was said: As He brought you out is related to His saying to them are degrees, meaning: They will have degrees with their Lord, forgiveness, and generous provision. That is, this promise to the believers is true in the Hereafter, just as your Lord brought you out of your home with the right due to Him, so He fulfilled His promise to you and made you victorious over your enemy and fulfilled it for you, because He, the Almighty, said: And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours. So just as He fulfilled this promise in this world, so He will fulfill for you what He promised you in the Hereafter. This is a good statement mentioned by Al-Nahhas and he chose it. It was said: The kaf in kama is the kaf of comparison, and its source is by way of recompense, like the saying of the one who says to his servant: As I directed you to My enemies and they weakened you, and you asked for support and I supported you and strengthened you and removed your illness, so take them now and punish them with such and such. And as I clothed you and provided you with provision, so do such and such. And as I was good to you, thank Me for it. He said: Just as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth and covered you with drowsiness as security from Him - meaning him and those with him - and sent down water from the sky to purify them with it, and sent down upon you from the sky angels in succession, so strike above the necks and strike from them every fingertip. It is as if he is saying: I have removed your illnesses and reinforced you with angels, so strike from them these places, which are the places of killing, to achieve the will of God in establishing the truth and invalidating falsehood. And God knows best. And indeed, a party of the believers are averse meaning they are averse to leaving Mecca and leaving their wealth and homes.
8:6: God the Almighty said: They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear. Their argument: their saying when he summoned them to the caravan and the caravan passed away and ordered them to fight and they did not have much equipment with them, that was difficult for them and they said: If you had told us about the fight, we would have taken the necessary measures. The meaning of in the truth is in the fight. After it became clear to them that you do not order anything except by God's permission. It was said: After it became clear to them that God promised them either victory over the caravan or the people of Mecca, and since the caravan passed away, then the people of Mecca and their victory were inevitable. So the meaning of the statement is to deny their argument. As if they were being driven to death out of aversion to meeting the people. And they are looking on meaning they know that this will happen to them. God the Almighty said: On the Day a man will see what his hands have put forth (An-Naba': 40) meaning he will know.
8:7: The Almighty said: And when God promised you one of the two parties that it would be yours One is in the accusative case as a second object. It is yours is also in the accusative case instead of one. And you would like means you love. That the one without the thorn would be yours Abu Ubaidah said: meaning the one without the edge. Thorn is the weapon. Thorn is the plant that has an edge. From this comes the word a man with a thorny weapon, meaning an iron weapon. Then it is reversed and it is said: a thorny weapon. Meaning you would like to defeat the group that has no weapon and no war in it, from Al-Zajjaj. And God intends to establish the truth with His words meaning to make Islam prevail. The truth is always true, but making it prevail is a realization of it in that if it does not appear, it is more like falsehood. With His words meaning with His promise, for He promised His Prophet that in Surat Ad-Dukhan and said: "The Day We shall strike with the greatest strike. Indeed, We will take retribution" (al-Dukhan 44:16) meaning from Abu Jahl and his companions. He said: That He may make it prevail over all religions (al-Tawbah 9:33 and al-Fath 48:28). It was said: With His words, meaning with His command. Beware of fighting them. And to cut off the root of the disbelievers meaning to eradicate them through destruction.
8:8: That the truth may be established meaning that the religion of Islam may be made manifest and glorified. And that falsehood may be nullified meaning disbelief. Nullifying it means eliminating it, just as establishing the truth means making it manifest. Rather, We cast the truth upon falsehood, and it destroys it, and at once it departs (al-Anbiya 21:18). Even though the criminals dislike it.
8:9: The Almighty said: When you called upon your Lord. Seeking help: asking for relief and victory. The man's help said: Oh, help him. The noun is ghawth, ghawath, and ghawath. And so-and-so sought help from me, so I helped him. The noun is ghayath, according to al-Jawhari. Muslim narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, who said: “When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at the polytheists, who were one thousand, and his companions were three hundred and seventeen men. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced the qiblah, then stretched out his hands and began to call upon his Lord: O God, fulfill for me what You promised me. O God, give me what You promised me. O God, if You destroy this group of Muslims, You will not be worshipped on earth. He continued to call upon his Lord, stretching out his hands and facing the qiblah, until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr came to him, took his cloak, threw it over his shoulders, then embraced him from behind and said: O Prophet of God, your supplication to your Lord is sufficient for you, for He will fulfill for you what He promised you. So God, the Most High, revealed: ‘When you called upon your Lord, and He answered you, “I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another.” So God reinforced him with the angels.” He mentioned the hadith. Following one another with the fatha on the dal is the reading of Nafi’. The rest with the kasra is an active participle, meaning one group comes after another, and that is more awe-inspiring in the eyes. And muraddif with the fatha on the dal for that which does not have a doer, because the people who fought on the day of Badr were followed by a thousand angels, meaning they were sent down to them to help them against the infidels. So muraddif with the fatha on the dal is an adjective for alif. It was said: It is a state of the accusative pronoun in mmaddikum. That is, mmaddikum in the state of following you with a thousand angels, and this is the doctrine of Mujahid. Abu Ubaidah narrated that radfani and ardafni are one and the same. Abu Ubaidah denied that ardaf means radf, he said because of the saying of God the Almighty: The one who follows it will follow it (An-Nazi'at: 7) and He did not say al-muraddifah. An-Nahhas, Makki and others said: The reading with the kasra on the dal is more appropriate, because the people of interpretation interpret this reading. That is, they followed one another, and because it has the meaning of fatha according to what Abu Ubaidah narrated, and because most of the reciters are like that. Sibawayh said: Some of them read muraddif with the fatha on the ra and the shaddah on the dal. Some of them read muraddif with the kasra on the ra. Some of them read muraddif with the damma on the ra. The letter dal is broken and stressed in all three readings. According to Sibawayh, the first reading is understood as mutaradayfin two consecutive letters, then the ta’ was assimilated into the dal, and its vowel was placed on the ra’ so that two consonants would not meet. In the second reading, the ra’ was broken because of the meeting of two consonants. The ra’ was given a damma in the third reading, following the damma of the meem, as you say: rad, ward, ward, ya hada. Ja’far ibn Muhammad and Asim al-Jahdary read it with an alif, plural of alif, like fals and aflas. It was also reported from them with an alif.
8:10: The descent of the angels, their marks, and their fighting have already been mentioned in Al Imran. The meaning of His statement, And God made it not but good tidings (Al Imran 3:126) has already been mentioned. What is meant is support. It is also possible that it is a second meaning. And victory comes only from God indicates that victory comes from Him, the Almighty, the Majestic, not from the angels. That is, if it were not for His victory, the angels would not have benefited from the large number. Victory from God comes with the sword and with the argument.
8:11: The Almighty's saying: When drowsiness overtakes you has two objects. This is the reading of the people of Medina, and it is good because the verb is attributed to God, the Almighty, because He was mentioned before in His saying: And victory is not but from God and because after it is and descends upon you, so the verb is attributed to God, the Almighty. Likewise, the overpowering is attributed to God, the Almighty, to make the speech consistent. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read the overpowering of drowsiness by attributing the verb to the overpowering. His evidence is security, a slumber that overwhelms (Al Imran 3:154) in the reading of those who read with the letter ya or the letter ta, so they attributed the verb to the overpowering or to the security. The security is the sleepiness, so they informed that it is the sleep that overwhelms the people. The rest read overpowering you with a fatha on the ghain and a shaddah on the shin. Nausea in the accusative case according to the reading of Nafi’, two languages meaning ghashā and aghashā. God the Almighty said: So we covered them (Ya-Sin 36:9) and He said: So that which covered them covered them (al-Najm 53:54). And He said: As if their faces had been covered (Yunus 10:27). Makki said: The choice is to add the ya’ and the shaddah and to put the na’as in the accusative case, because after it is a security from Him and the ha’ in from Him belongs to God, so He is the one who covers them with sleep, and because it is mostly from Him. It was said: security from the enemy. And security is an object for which or a source, it is said: aman amanah and amanana and amanan, they are all the same. Drowsiness is the state of one who is safe and not afraid. And this drowsiness was on the night when the fighting was to take place the next day, so sleep was strange with what was ahead of them of the important matter, but God controlled their nerves. And “On the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, he said: There was no knight among us on the day of Badr except for Muqdad on a piebald horse. I saw us and there was none among us except the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sleeping under a tree praying and weeping until morning,” mentioned by Al-Bayhaqi. Al-Marudi: There are two aspects to God’s blessing them with sleep that night: One is that He strengthened them by resting for the battle the next day. The second is that He reassured them by removing fear from their hearts, as it is said: Security is a sleeper, and fear is a watcher. It was said: He covered them when the two lines met. Something similar happened on the day of Uhud in Al Imran. God the Almighty said: And He sends down upon you from the sky water to purify you thereby and remove from you the defilement of Satan and to strengthen your hearts and make firm thereby your feet. The apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates that drowsiness came before the rain. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: The rain came before drowsiness. Al-Zajjaj narrated: The infidels on the day of Badr preceded the believers to the water of Badr and they camped there, and the believers were left with no water, so their souls became anxious and they became thirsty and impure and prayed like that. Some of them said to themselves because of Satan’s suggestion to them: We claim that we are the friends of God and His Messenger is among us, and this is our situation while the polytheists are on the water. So God sent down rain on the night of Badr, the seventeenth of Ramadan, until the valleys flowed, so they drank and purified themselves and watered their backs, and the salt marsh that was between them and the polytheists became covered so that the Muslims’ feet could be firmly planted in it during the battle. It has been said that these conditions were before they reached Badr, and this is more correct, and it is what Ibn Ishaq mentioned in his biography and others. This is its sumMaryam 19:Ibn Abbas said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed that Abu Sufyan was coming from the Levant, he called upon the Muslims to come to them and said: ‘This is the caravan of Quraysh, in which there is wealth, so go out to them, perhaps God will grant you its spoils.’ He said: ‘So those who were light set out with him, and some were heavy and disliked going out. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, hurried, not looking back on those who were unable to do so, nor waiting for those who were absent. He set out with three hundred and thirteen of his companions, from the Muhajireen and Ansar.’” And in Bukhari on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, he said: The number of Muhajireen on the day of Badr was more than eighty, and the number of Ansar was more than forty and two hundred. It was also narrated from him that he said: We used to say that the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were three hundred and some ten, the same number as the companions of Talut who crossed the river with him, and none crossed with him except a believer. Al-Bayhaqi mentioned on the authority of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari who said: So we went out - meaning to Badr - and when we had traveled for a day or two, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered us to return, so we did so and we were three hundred and thirteen men. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us of our number, and he was pleased with that and praised God and said: The number of the companions of Talut. Ibn Ishaq said: The people all thought that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not encounter war, so they did not increase their preparations. When Abu Sufyan approached the Hijaz, he was spying on the report and asking whomever he met from the riders, fearing for the people’s wealth, until he received report from some of the riders that Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had mobilized the people against you. So he was cautious and hired Damdam bin Amr al-Ghifari and sent him to Mecca, and ordered him to go to the Quraysh and mobilize them for their wealth and inform them that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, had attacked it with his companions, so Damdam did so.
