So the people of Mecca went out with a thousand men or so, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with his companions, and the report came to him from the Quraysh that they had gone out to protect them. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) consulted the people. Abu Bakr stood up and spoke well. Umar stood up and spoke well. Then Al-Miqdad bin Amr stood up and said: O Messenger of God, go as God has commanded you, for we are with you. By God, we will not say as the Children of Israel said: “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here.” (al-Ma’idah 5:24) Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are with you, fighting. By the One Who sent you with the truth, if you were to march to Bark Al-Ghimad - meaning the city of Abyssinia - we would fight with you and not with him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was pleased with that and prayed for his well-being. Then he said: Advise me, O people, meaning the Ansar. That is because they were the number of people, and when they pledged allegiance to him at Al-Aqabah, they said: O Messenger of God, we are free from your protection until you reach our homes. When you reach us, then you are under our protection. We will protect you as we protect ourselves, our children, and our women. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was afraid that the Ansar would not see that they should support him except in Medina, and that he should not march with them to an enemy outside their country. When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said that, Sa`d ibn Mu`adh spoke to him - and it was said that it was Sa`d ibn `Ubadah, and it is possible that they both spoke on that day - and said: O Messenger of God, it seems that you mean us, the Ansar? The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: Yes. He said: We have believed in you and followed you, so go ahead of what God has commanded you, and by the One Who sent you with the truth, if you were to parade us across this sea and cross it, we would cross it with you. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: Go ahead with God’s blessing, for it is as if I can see where the people will fall. So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) went ahead of the Quraysh to the water of Badr. A heavy rain that God sent down upon them prevented the Quraysh from reaching it ahead of him, and the Muslims only got what made the trampling of the valley easier for them and helped them on their way. Trampling is soft sand in which the feet sink. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) descended to the nearest water source from the waters of Badr to Medina. Al-Hubab bin Al-Mundhir bin Amr bin Al-Jamuh advised him otherwise and said to him: O Messenger of God, what do you think of this place? Is it a place where God has sent you so that we cannot advance or lag behind it, or is it opinion, war and deceit? He (peace be upon him) said: Rather, it is opinion, war and deceit. He said: O Messenger of God, this is not a place for you, so let us go to the nearest water source to the people and descend there and explore the heart behind it, then build a cistern by it and fill it so that we can drink and they do not drink. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) approved of that from his opinion and did it. Then they met and God granted victory to His Prophet and the Muslims. He killed seventy of the polytheists and took seventy captive, and took revenge on them for the believers, and God healed the hearts of His Messenger (peace be upon him) and his companions from their anger. Hassan says about that: Zainab's home was known as the dune, like the line of revelation on the lush paper. The winds circulate it, and every swarm of the Wasmi pours down like a scoop. A quarter of it became ruined and it became desolate after its beloved inhabitant So leave the remembrance every day and respond to the heat of the gloomy chest And tell the truth about what is flawless, unlike the telling of a liar. What did God do on the day after Badr, we have a share among the polytheists? The morning, as if their gathering was Hira, whose pillars appeared at sunset. We met them with a group like the lions of the jungle, both beardless and gray. In front of Muhammad, they supported him against the enemies in the heat of wars. In their hands are sharp swords, and every experienced one is a treader of the heels. Banu Aws Al-Ghatarif and Banu Al-Najjar supported them in the cross religion Abu Jahl left us dead, and Utba left us in the mountains. And Shaiba has left us among the men of noble lineage, if they are called to account. The Messenger of God called them when we threw them like a weeping camel into the well. Did you not find my words were true and that God’s command takes hold of hearts? They did not speak, and if they had spoken, they would have said, You were right and you had a sound opinion. Here are three issues: First: Malik said: It has reached me that “Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: How are the people of Badr among you? He said: The best of us. He said: You are like that among us.” This indicates that the honor of creation is not in their essence, but rather in their actions. The angels have their honorable actions of constant glorification. And we have our actions of sincerity in obedience. And acts of obedience are differentiated by the preference given to them by the Shari’ah, and the best of them is jihad, and the best jihad is the day of Badr, because Islam was built upon it. Second: The Prophet’s (peace be upon him) going out to meet the caravan indicates the permissibility of going out for spoils because it is lawful earnings. This refutes what Malik disliked about that, as he said: That is fighting for the world, and what was reported that whoever fights so that the word of God is supreme is in the way of God, unlike whoever fights for spoils, is intended by it if his intention is alone and religion has no share in it. And Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: They said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he had finished with Badr: Take the caravan, there is nothing better than it. Al-Abbas called out to him while he was among the captives: This is not right. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Why? He said: Because God promised you one of the two groups, and God has given you what He promised you. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have spoken the truth. Al-Abbas knew the hadith of the Prophet’s companions, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what had happened at Badr, so he heard that during the conversation. Third: Muslim narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left the dead of Badr for three days, then he stood over them and called out to them, saying: O Abu Jahl bin Hisham, O Umayyah bin Khalaf, O Utbah bin Rabi’ah, O Shaibah bin Rabi’ah! Have you not found what your Lord promised to be true? I have found what my Lord promised me to be true. Umar heard the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, how do they hear and how can they respond when they have become corpses? He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you are not more able to hear what I say than they are, but they are not able to respond. Then he ordered them to be dragged and thrown into the well, the well of Badr. Jafawa with the opening of the jim and the ya’, and its meaning is that they stink and have become corpses. Umar’s words: They hear are an exclusion based on what is customary. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) answered him that they hear as the living hear. This indicates that death is not pure nonexistence or annihilation, but rather it is the severing of the connection of the soul to the body and its separation, a barrier between them, a change of state and a transition from one abode to another. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: When the dead person is placed in his grave and his companions turn away from him, he can hear the sound of their sandals. Hadith. Narrated by Sahih. The Almighty says: And thereby makes the feet firm. The pronoun in thereby refers to the water that crushed the valley, as mentioned above. It was said that it refers to connecting the hearts, so making the feet firm is an expression of victory and assistance in a place of war.
8:12: The Almighty said: When your Lord revealed to the angels, 'I am with you' The agent in when, establishes, i.e. establishes the feet at that time. It was said: The agent is to bind, i.e. to bind, when it inspires. The estimation may be: Remember when your Lord revealed to the angels, 'I am with you' in the accusative case, and the meaning is: that I am with you, i.e. with victory and support. With you with the opening of the 'ayn is a circumstance, and whoever makes it quiescent, it is a letter for him. So strengthen those who believe i.e. give them good tidings of victory or fighting with them or being with them without fighting, so the angel would walk in front of the row in the form of a man and say: Go, for God is your supporter. The Muslims would think that he was one of them, and it was mentioned in Al Imran that the angels fought that day. They would see heads falling from the necks without anyone they could see. Some of them heard a speaker who heard his words but did not see his person: Go forward, Haizum. It was said: This confirmation was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reminding the believers of the angels' descent as reinforcements. The Almighty said: I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve. This was explained in Al Imran. Then strike above the necks. This is a command to the angels. It was also said: to the believers, meaning strike the necks. Above is redundant, as stated by Al Akhfash, Ad-Dahhak, and Atiyah. Al Mas’udi narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was not sent to punish with the punishment of God, but I was sent to strike necks and tighten bonds.” Muhammad ibn Yazid said: This is a mistake, because above conveys a meaning, so it is not permissible to add it, but the meaning is that they were permitted to strike the faces and what is close to them. Ibn Abbas said: Every head and skull. It was said: That is, what is above the necks, which is the heads, said Ikrimah. Striking the head is more eloquent, because the smallest thing affects the brain. Something of this meaning has already been mentioned in An-Nisa’, and that above is not redundant, when he said: above two (An-Nisa’: 11). And strike from them every fingertip. Az-Zajjaj said: The singular of banan is banana, and here it refers to the fingers and other limbs. Banan is derived from their saying that a man resides in a place if he stays there. The banan is used for residence and life. It was said: What is meant by banan here is the tips of the fingers of the hands and feet. It refers to steadfastness in war and the place of striking, so if the fingertip is struck, the one being struck is prevented from fighting, unlike the rest of the limbs. Antara said: The young man of Al-Haija used to protect her honor and strike every finger in times of distress. And what was mentioned that the fingers are the fingers is what Antarah also said: Death is at my disposal if I reach my fingertips with the Hindu It is common in Arabic poetry. Banan: fingers. Ibn Faris said: Banan are fingers, and it is said: extremities. Some of them mentioned that it was called Banan because it improves the conditions by which a person settles and builds. Al-Dahhak said: Banan is every joint.
8:13: The Almighty said: That is because they opposed God. That is in the nominative case as a subject, and the meaning is: that matter, or that matter. They opposed God means His friends. And discord is that each one becomes in a split. And it has been mentioned before.
8:14: That is you, so taste it, and indeed for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire. Al-Zajjaj said: That is you, so taste it. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with taste it, like saying: Zaidan, so beat him. The meaning of the statement is a rebuke to the disbelievers. And that is in the nominative case in apposition to that is you. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with the meaning of and that for the disbelievers. He said: It is permissible for it to be implied and know that. Al-Zajjaj said: If it were permissible to imply and know, then Zaid is leaving and Amr is sitting would be permissible. Rather, it would be permissible in the beginning to say Zaid is leaving, because the informant is a teacher, and none of the grammarians say this.
8:15: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty said: Crawling. Crawling means drawing near little by little. Its origin is rushing on the buttocks, then every walker in war towards another was called a crawler. Crawling means drawing near and getting close. It is said: He crawled towards the enemy crawling. And the people walked towards each other. And from it is the poetry of zahaaf, which is that a letter falls between two letters and one crawls towards the other. He says: If you draw near and see each other, do not flee from them and do not turn your backs to them. God forbade that to the believers when He imposed upon them jihad and fighting the infidels. Ibn Atiyah said: The backs are the plural of dabar. And the phrase dabar in this verse is very eloquent, because it is ugly to the fleeing one and condemns him. Second: God the Almighty commanded in this verse that the believers should not turn their backs before the infidels. This command is restricted by the condition stipulated in the double of the believers. If a group of believers encounters a group of polytheists who are twice the believers, then it is obligatory for them not to flee before them. Whoever flees from two is a deserter from the battle. Whoever flees from three is not a deserter from the battle, and no threat is directed against him. Fleeing is a major sin according to the apparent meaning of the Qur’an and the consensus of most of the imams. A group of them, including Ibn al-Majishun, said in al-Wadiha: Weakness, strength, and equipment should be taken into consideration. According to their opinion, it is permissible for one hundred horsemen to flee from one hundred horsemen if they know that the polytheists have twice as much courage and bravery as they do. As for the majority opinion, it is not permissible for one hundred to flee except for what is more than two hundred. So if there are more than two Muslims facing each other, it is permissible to flee, and patience is better. The army of Mu’tah, which was three thousand, stood facing two hundred thousand, of whom one hundred thousand were Romans, and one hundred thousand were Arabized from Lakhm and Judham. I said: It was mentioned in the history of the conquest of Andalusia that Tariq, the client of Musa ibn Nusayr, marched with one thousand seven hundred men to Andalusia, and that was in Rajab of the year ninety-three of the Hijra. He met the king of Andalusia, Roderic, who had seventy thousand reins. Tariq advanced towards him and endured for him, so God defeated the tyrant Roderic, and the conquest occurred. Ibn Wahb said: I heard Malik being asked about people who encounter the enemy or are in a guard post, guarding, and the enemy comes to them while they are advancing. Should they fight or turn back and give their companions permission? He said: If they are strong enough to fight them, then they should fight them, otherwise they should turn back to their companions and give them permission. Third: People differed as to whether fleeing on the day of the battle is specific to the day of Badr or general for all battles until the Day of Resurrection. It was narrated from Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that it is specific to the day of Badr, and this is what Nafi’, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Yazid bin Abi Habib, and Ad-Dahhak said, and this is what Abu Hanifa said. And that it is specific to the people of Badr, so they did not have to withdraw, and if they had withdrawn, they would have withdrawn to the polytheists, and there were no Muslims on earth at that time other than them, and the Muslims did not have a group except the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for after that, some of them were a group for others. Al-Kia said: This is questionable, because there were many Ansar in Madinah who were not ordered by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to go out and they did not think that it was fighting, but they thought that it was the caravan, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with those who had fled with him. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas and other scholars that the verse remains until the Day of Resurrection. The first ones cited as evidence what we have mentioned, and the Almighty’s saying: On that Day, and they said: It is a reference to the day of Badr, and that the ruling of the verse was abrogated by the verse of weakness. The ruling on fleeing from the battlefield remains that it is not a major sin. The people fled on the day of Uhud, so God forgave them, and God said about them on the day of Hunayn, Then you turned back, fleeing (al-Tawbah 9:25), and no reprimand was issued for that. The majority of scholars said: This is only a reference to the day of the battle, which is included in the words of God the Almighty: When you meet. The ruling of the verse remains until the Day of Resurrection, on the condition of weakness, which God the Almighty explained in another verse, and there is no abrogation in the verse. The evidence for that is that the verse was revealed after the fighting, the end of the war, and the passing of the day and everything in it. This is what Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, and most scholars agreed with. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Avoid the seven deadly sins - and in it - and flee on the day of battle. This is a text on the issue. As for the day of Uhud, the people fled because of more than their weakness, and despite that they were oppressed. As for the day of Hunayn, likewise whoever fled was only exposed to the large number, as will be explained.
8:16: Fourth: Ibn Al-Qasim said: The testimony of one who fled from the battle is not permissible, and it is not permissible for them to flee even if their leader fled, because of the words of God Almighty: And whoever turns his back to them that day (al-An’am 2:10). He said: It is permissible for more than twice their number to flee, and this is as long as the number of Muslims does not reach twelve thousand. If it reaches twelve thousand, it is not permissible for them to flee even if the number of polytheists exceeds double, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And twelve thousand will not be defeated due to their small number. Most scholars have specified this number in this hadith from the general meaning of the verse. I said: It was narrated by Abu Bishr and Abu Salamah Al-Amili, who is Al-Hakam bin Abdullah bin Khattaf, and he is rejected. They said: Al-Zuhri told us on the authority of Anas bin Malik, “on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: O Aktham ibn al-Jun, go out to fight with people other than your own, improve your character and be generous to your companions. O Aktham ibn al-Jun, the best companions are four, the best vanguards are forty, the best raiding parties are four hundred, and the best armies are four thousand. Twelve thousand will not be defeated due to a small number.” And it was narrated from Malik what indicates this from his school of thought, which is his statement to al-Amri al-Abid when he asked him, Do you have the freedom to abandon jihad other than the rulings and replace them? He said, If you have twelve thousand with you, then you have no freedom to do so. Fifth: If he fled, then let him seek forgiveness from God Almighty. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Bilal bin Yasar bin Zaid, who said: My father told me on the authority of my grandfather, who heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever says, I seek forgiveness from God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, and I repent to Him, God will forgive him, even if he had fled from the battlefield.” He said: This is a strange hadith that we do not know except from this source. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Except when turning aside for the sake of fighting or withdrawing to a company. Turning aside means moving away from the straight path. So the one who turns from one side to another for the sake of war is not defeated, and likewise the one who withdraws if he intends to withdraw to a company of Muslims to seek their help, so he returns to the battle not defeated either. Abu Dawud narrated “on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that he was in one of the companies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: The people surrounded him, and I was among those surrounded. He said: When we came out, we said: What should we do, since we have fled from the battle and have been afflicted with the wrath? We said: We will enter the city and establish ourselves there and go away, and no one will see us. He said: So we entered and said: Let us present ourselves to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). If we have repentance, we will stay, and if not, we will go. He said: So we sat with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before the dawn prayer, and when he came out, we stood up to him and said: We are the ones who fled. He came to us and said: No, you are the ones who are disturbing us. He said: So we came close and kissed his hand. He said: I am the group of Muslims. Tha’lab said: The ‘Akkaroon are the ‘Atafoon. Another said: The man who turns away during war and then returns is called ‘Akar and ‘I’tkar. Jarir narrated from Mansur from Ibrahim who said: A man from Al-Qadisiyah was defeated and came to Madinah to ‘Umar and said: O Commander of the Faithful, I am lost! I fled from the battle. ‘Umar said: I am your group. Muhammad bin Sirin said: When Abu ‘Ubaidah was killed, the report came to ‘Umar and he said: If he had turned to me, I would have been his group, so I am the group of every Muslim. According to these hadiths, fleeing is not a major sin, because the group here is Madinah, the Imam, and the group of Muslims wherever they are. According to the other opinion, it is a major sin, because the group there is the group of people present for the war. This is according to the opinion of the majority that fleeing from the battle is a major sin. They said: Rather, that statement was made by the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and ‘Umar as a precaution for the believers, since at that time they were steadfast against their weakest many times. And God knows best. And in his saying and turning away on the day of the battle is sufficient. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: “He has incurred the wrath of God” meaning he deserved the wrath. The root of baa is rajaa he returned, and this has been mentioned previously. And his abode is Hell meaning his place of residence. This does not indicate eternity, as has been mentioned previously in more than one place. The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: Whoever says, ‘I seek forgiveness from God, there is no god but He, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining,’ he will be forgiven, even if he had fled from battle.
8:17: The Almighty said: You did not kill them, but God killed them meaning on the day of Badr. It was narrated that when the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) returned from Badr, each one of them mentioned what he had done: I killed such and such, I did such and such, and from that came boasting and the like. So the verse was revealed to inform that God is the One Who causes death and determines all things, and that the servant only participates through his earnings and intentions. This verse responds to those who say that the actions of the servants were created for them. It was said: The meaning is: You did not kill them, but God killed them by driving them to you until He had power over you. It was also said: But God killed them with the angels He provided you with. And you did not throw when you threw is similar, but God threw. The scholars differed regarding this throwing into four opinions: First: This throwing was done at the Messenger of God’s (peace be upon him) pebbles on the day of Hunayn. It was narrated by Ibn Wahb on the authority of Malik. Malik said: There was no one left on that day who was not affected by that. Ibn al-Qasim also narrated the same on his authority. Second: This was on the day of Uhud when Abi bin Khalaf threw a spear at his neck. Abi thought in defeat. The polytheists said to him: By God, there is nothing wrong with you. He said: By God, if he had spat on me, he would have killed me. Didn’t he say: Rather, I will kill him? Abi had threatened the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with being killed in Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Rather, I will kill you. So the enemy of God died from the blow of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on his way back to Mecca, in a place called Sarif. Musa bin Uqbah said on the authority of Ibn Shihab: On the day of Uhud, my father came, covered in iron, on his horse, saying: I will not be saved if Muhammad is saved. So he charged at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intending to kill him. Musa bin Uqbah said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Some of the believers intercepted him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to clear his way. Then Mus`ab bin `Umair met him to protect the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he killed Mus`ab bin `Umair. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the collarbone of Abu bin Khalaf through a gap between the white cloth and the armor, so he stabbed him with his spear, so my father fell from his horse, and no blood came out of his stab wound. Saeed said: He broke one of his ribs. He said: It was about that that the verse was revealed: And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw. This is weak, because the verse was revealed after Badr. Third: What is meant is the arrow that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shot in the fortress of Khaybar, which traveled through the air until it hit Ibn Abi al-Haqiq while he was on his bed. This is also invalid, and Khaybar and its conquest are much further away than Uhud. The correct version of the killing of Ibn Abi al-Haqiq is different from this. Fourth: It was on the day of Badr, as stated by Ibn Ishaq. And it is more correct, because the surah is from Badr, and that is because “Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Take a handful of dirt, so he took a handful of dirt and threw it at their faces, and there was not one of the polytheists except that dirt from that handful struck his eyes, nostrils and mouth.” Ibn Abbas said it, and it will come. Tha’lab said: The meaning is And you did not throw the fear and terror in their hearts when you threw the pebbles and they were defeated but God threw meaning He helped you and made you victorious. The Arabs say: God threw for you, meaning He helped you and made you victorious and made for you. This was narrated by Abu Ubaidah in the book of metaphors. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: And you did not throw with your strength when you threw, but you threw with the strength of God. And that He might test the believers from Him with a good test here the test is the blessing. And the lam is related to something omitted, meaning and that He might test the believers He did that.
8:18: That is it, and that God weakens the plot of the disbelievers. The reading of the people of the Haramain and Abu Amr. The reading of the people of Kufa is weaken the plot of the disbelievers. The emphasis has the meaning of exaggeration. It was narrated from Al-Hasan weaken the plot of the disbelievers with addition and alleviation. The meaning is that God, the Almighty, casts terror into their hearts until they scatter and their assembly disperses and they become weak. And plotting means deceit. It has been mentioned before.
8:19: The Almighty's saying: If you ask for victory, victory has already come to you. This is a condition and its answer. There are three opinions on this: It is addressed to the disbelievers, because they asked for victory and said: O God, we have severed the ties of kinship and wronged its owner, so grant him victory over him. This was said by Al-Hasan, Mujahid and others. This statement was made by them when they went out to support the caravan. It was also said that Abu Jahl said it during the fighting. Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith said: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. He was one of those killed at Badr. The opening is the acceptance of victory, meaning that victory has come to you, but it was for the Muslims against you. That is, what has become clear of the matter has come to you, and the truth has been revealed to you. And if you desist meaning from disbelief it is better for you. "And if you return" meaning to this statement and fighting Muhammad. "We will return" to supporting the believers. "And your faction meaning your group will not avail you at all. Even if they are many" meaning in number. The second: It is addressed to the believers, meaning if you seek help, then victory has come to you. And if you desist meaning from what you did of taking spoils and prisoners before permission, it is better for you. “But if you return” meaning to such a thing, we will return to rebuking you. As He said: Had it not been for a previous decree from God (al-Anfal 8:68) and the verse. The third opinion: That If you seek victory, victory has already come to you is addressed to the believers, and what comes after it is to the disbelievers. That is, if you return to fighting, we will return to something like the Battle of Badr. Al-Qushayri: The correct view is that it is addressed to the disbelievers, for when they set out to support the caravan, they clung to the curtains of the Kaaba and said: O God, support the more guided of the two groups, and the best of the two religions. Al-Mahdawi: It was narrated that the polytheists went out with them to the curtains of the Kaaba seeking victory by them, that is, seeking victory. I said: There is no contradiction because it is possible that they did both. And that God is with the believers with the kasra on the alif as a new sentence, and with the fatha on it, it is in apposition to his statement: And that God weakens the plot of the disbelievers. Or to his statement: I am with you. The meaning is: And because God, and the estimate is because of their large number and that God. That is, whoever God is in his support, no group will overcome him, no matter how large it is.
8:20: The Almighty's saying: O you who have believed, obey God and His Messenger is addressed to the believing believers. He addressed them alone, not the hypocrites, out of respect for them. God renewed the command to obey God and the Messenger, and forbade them from turning away from Him. This is the opinion of the majority. A group said: The address in this verse is only to the hypocrites. The meaning is: O you who believed with your tongues only. Ibn Atiyyah said: Although this is a remote possibility, it is very weak, because God described the one He addressed in this verse as having faith. Faith is belief, and the hypocrites are not described by any belief in anything. Even more distant than this is the one who said: The address is to the Children of Israel, because this is foreign to the verse. The Almighty said: And do not turn away from him. Turning away means turning away. He said about him and did not say about them both because obeying the Messenger is obeying him. It is like the Almighty’s saying: And God and His Messenger are more worthy for them to please (al-Tawbah 9:62). And you are listening is a subject and predicate in the place of a circumstantial. The meaning is: And you are listening to what is recited to you of the arguments and proofs in the Qur’an.
8:21: God the Almighty says: And do not be like those who said, 'We hear' meaning like the Jews, hypocrites, or polytheists. It is from hearing with the ear. And they do not hear meaning they do not ponder what they hear, nor do they think about it, so they are like those who did not hear and turned away from the truth. He forbade the believers from being like them. The verse indicates that the believer's saying, I hear and obey is of no benefit unless the effect of that is apparent in him through his compliance with his actions. So if he falls short in the commands and does not do them, and relies on the prohibitions and rushes into them, then what hearing and obedience does he have? He will then be like the hypocrite who shows faith but conceals disbelief, and that is what is meant by His statement: And do not be like those who say, 'We hear' while they do not hear. He means by that the hypocrites, or the Jews, or the polytheists, as mentioned above.
8:22: Then the Almighty informed us that the infidels are the worst of what creeps on the earth. In Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, The worst of living creatures in the sight of God are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason. He said: They are a group of Banu Abd al-Dar. The original is ashr, the hamza was deleted due to frequent use. And so is khayr, the original is akhyr.
8:23: The Almighty said: And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. It was said: The arguments and evidence, hearing and understanding. But His knowledge of their misery preceded. And if He had made them hear meaning if He had made them understand, they would not have believed after His eternal knowledge of their disbelief. It was said that the meaning is that He would have made them hear the speech of the dead who asked to be revived, because they asked to revive Qusayy ibn Kilab and others so that they would bear witness to the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Zajjaj: He would have made them hear the answer to everything they asked about. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were averse because He had previously known that they would not believe.
8:24: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, respond to God and the Messenger. This address is to the believing believers without dispute. And the response: the answer: and He wills you its original is He wills you, the damma was removed from the ya’ because of its heaviness. And assimilation is not permissible. Abu Ubaidah said: The meaning of respond is answer, but it is known in speech that respond is transitive with lam, and ajaba is transitive without lam. God the Almighty said: O our people, respond to the caller of God (al-Ahqaf 46:31). And respond can be transitive without lam, and the evidence for that is the saying of the poet: Farewell, he called, O He who answers to the generosity, but no one answered him at that time. You say: He answered him and responded to his question. The source is the answer. The noun is the answer, like energy and obedience. You say: He heard badly, so he answered badly. This is how he speaks with this letter. The answer and the response: dialogue. And you say: It is for a good response with a kasra meaning the answer. When He revives you is related to His saying: Respond. The meaning: Respond to what He revives you if He calls you. It was said: The lam means to, meaning to what He revives you, meaning He revives your religion and teaches you. And it was said: meaning to what He revives your hearts with, so you unify Him, and this is a borrowed revival, because it is from the death of disbelief and ignorance. Mujahid and the majority said: The meaning is to respond to obedience and what the Qur’an includes of commands and prohibitions, for in it is eternal life and everlasting blessing. It was said: What is meant by his saying what gives you life is jihad, for it is the cause of life in appearance, because if the enemy does not invade, he invades, and in his invasion there is death, and death in jihad is eternal life. God Almighty said: “And never think of those who are killed in the way of God as dead. Rather, they are alive” (Al Imran 3:169). The correct view is the generality, as the majority said. Second: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed bin Al-Mualla, who said: I was praying in the mosque, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me, but I did not answer him. Then I came to him and said: O Messenger of God, I was praying. He said: Did not God the Almighty say, Respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life, and mentioned the hadith. It was mentioned earlier in Al-Fatihah. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: This is evidence that if an obligatory action or obligatory statement is performed during prayer, it does not invalidate it, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to respond even if it is during prayer. I said: It contains evidence for the statement of Al-Awza’i: If a man is praying and sees a boy about to fall into a well, and he shouts at him, turns to him, and rebukes him, there is nothing wrong with that. And God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And know that God intervenes between a man and his heart. It was said: The text from Him requires that He Almighty created disbelief and faith, so He intervenes between a disbelieving man and the faith that He commanded him to have, so he does not acquire it if He does not enable him to do so, rather He enables him to do its opposite, which is disbelief. And thus the believer is intervened between himself and disbelief. So it became clear from this text that He Almighty is the Creator of all the acquisitions of the servants, their good and their evil. And this is the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: No, and the Changer of hearts. And God's action was just with regard to those whom He led astray and forsook, as He did not prevent them from a right that was due to Him, so that the attribute of justice would be removed. Rather, He prevented you from what He should have bestowed upon them, not what was due to them. Al-Suddi said: He comes between a person and his heart, so he cannot believe except by His permission, nor disbelieve except by His permission, that is, by His will. The heart is the seat of thought. Its explanation was presented in Al-Baqarah. It is in God's hand, whenever He wills, He prevents the servant from it with illness or affliction so that he does not understand. That is, hasten to respond before you are unable to do so due to the loss of reason. Mujahid said: The meaning is that He comes between a person and his mind so that he does not know what he is doing. And in the Qur'an: Indeed in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart (Qaf: 37), that is, reason. And it was said: He comes between him and it with death, so he cannot make up for what he missed. It was said: The Muslims feared the large number of the enemy on the day of Badr, so God informed them that He stands between a person and his heart by replacing fear with security, and replacing their enemy with fear from security. It was said: The meaning is that He turns things from one state to another, and this is comprehensive. Al-Tabari chose that this be a statement from God, the Almighty, that He has more control over the hearts of His servants than they do, and that He stands between them and them if He wills, so that a person does not attain anything except by the will of God, the Almighty. And to Him you will be gathered is an appositive. Al-Farra’ said: If it had been repeated, it would have been broken, and that was correct.
8:25: There are two issues: First: Ibn Abbas said: God commanded the believers not to tolerate evil among themselves, lest the punishment should afflict them all. Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam interpreted it in the same way, for he said on the Day of the Camel, which was in the year thirty-six: I did not know that we meant by this verse except today, and I did not think it was except for those who were addressed at that time. Al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Suddi and others interpreted it in the same way. Al-Suddi said: The verse was revealed specifically about the people of Badr: Then the trial afflicted them on the Day of the Camel, so they fought. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: This verse was revealed about the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: God commanded the believers not to tolerate evil among themselves, lest the punishment afflict them all. And on the authority of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There will be a trial among some of my companions, which God will forgive them for their association with me, and people will follow them in it, and God will cause them to enter the Fire because of it.” I said: These interpretations are supported by the authentic hadiths. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Zainab bint Jahsh that she asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to him: O Messenger of God, will we perish while there are righteous people among us? He said: Yes, if evil increases.” And in Sahih al-Tirmidhi: If people see an oppressor and do not stop him, God will soon inflict a punishment on them all. These hadiths have been mentioned above. In Sahih al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of al-Nu’man ibn Bashir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “The example of the one who upholds the limits of God and the one who transgresses them is like the example of people who drew lots to board a ship. Some of them got the upper part and some the lower part. When those on the lower part wanted water, they passed by those on the upper part and said, ‘If we could make a hole in our share and not harm those on the upper part,’ and if they leave them to do what they want, they will all perish. But if they take them by the hand, they will all be saved.” In this hadith is the punishment of the common people for the sins of the elite. It also includes the deserving of punishment for abandoning enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. Our scholars said: If fitnah occurs, everyone perishes. This is when sins appear and evil spreads and no change is made. If no change is made, then the believers who reject it in their hearts must abandon that city and flee from it. This was the ruling with the nations before us, as in the story of the Sabbath when they abandoned the sinners and said, ‘We will not live with you.’ This is what the early Muslims may God be pleased with them said. Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik that he said: A land in which evil is committed openly should be abandoned and no one should settle in it. He cited as evidence the actions of Abu Darda’ in leaving Muawiyah’s land when he declared usury, so he permitted the sale of a gold watering can for more than its weight. It was included in Sahih Al-Bukhari. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If God sends down a punishment upon a people, the punishment will afflict everyone among them, and then they will be resurrected according to their deeds.” This indicates that general destruction may be a purification for the believers and a punishment for the wicked. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was fooling around in his sleep, so I said: O Messenger of God, did you do something in your sleep that you did not do before? He said: It is strange, some people from my nation come to this House with a man from Quraysh who has taken refuge in the House, until when they are in the desert, the earth swallows them up. We said: O Messenger of God, the road may gather people. He said: Yes, among them are the one who has insight, the one who is forced, and the wayfarer, who all perish in one death and come from different sources. God Almighty will resurrect them according to their intentions. If it is said: God Almighty said: And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another (Al-An`am: 164). Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned (al-Muddaththir 74:38). It shall have what it has earned, and it shall bear what it has earned (al-Baqarah 2:286). This necessitates that no one be held accountable for the sin of another, but rather the punishment is related to the one who committed the sin. The answer is that if people openly commit evil, then it is obligatory for everyone who sees it to change it, and if he remains silent about it, then all of them are sinners. This one by his action and this one by his approval. God has made in His judgment and wisdom the one who is satisfied in the position of the one who acts, so he is included in the punishment, as Ibn Al-`Arabi said: And it is the meaning of the hadiths as we mentioned. The meaning of the verse is: And fear a trial that will extend beyond the oppressor, and will affect the righteous and the wicked. Second: Grammarians differed about the inclusion of the letter nun inل سيبن. Al-Farra’ said: It is like saying: Get down from the animal, lest it smite you. It is the answer to a command in the form of a prohibition, meaning if you get down from it, it will not smite you. Similar to this is the saying of God the Almighty: Enter your dwellings, lest they crush you (al-Naml 27:18). Meaning if you enter, they will not crush you. The letter nun was included because of the meaning of recompense in it. It was said: Because it came out in the form of an oath, and the letter nun is only included with a verb of prohibition or the answer to an oath. Abu al-Abbas al-Mubarrad said: It is a prohibition after a command, and the meaning is the prohibition for the oppressors, meaning do not come near oppression. Sibawayh narrated:ل عرنك هوناI do not want you to be here, meaning do not be here, for whoever is here, I will see him. Al-Jurjani said: The meaning is, fear a trial that will specifically afflict the oppressors. So his sayingل سيبنis a prohibition in the place of a description of an indefinite noun, and its interpretation is informing that it will afflict the oppressors. Ali, Zaid bin Thabit, Ubayy and Ibn Masoud read latasiban without an alif. Al-Mahdawi said: Whoever reads “latasiban it is possible that it is shortened from la tasibiban and the alif is deleted just as it is deleted from ma which is the sister of la in the phrase umm wa allahi laaf’alan and the like. It is also possible that it is different from the reading of the group, so the meaning is that it afflicts the oppressor in particular.”
8:26: The Almighty said: And remember when you were few. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about the Muhajireen, meaning describing their condition before the migration and at the beginning of Islam. Weakened is an adjective. On the land meaning the land of Mecca. Fearing is an adjective. That He might snatch you away is in the accusative case. Snatching means taking quickly. The people is in the nominative case as the subject. Qatada and Ikrimah: They are the polytheists of Quraysh. Wahb ibn Munabbih: Persians and Romans. So He sheltered you Ibn Abbas said: To the Ansar. As-Suddi: To Madinah, and the meaning is the same. He sheltered him with a long vowel: He joined him. He sheltered him with a short vowel: He joined him. And supported you He strengthened you. With His victory meaning with His help. It was also said: With the Ansar. It was also said: With the angels on the day of Badr. And He provided you with good things meaning the spoils. That you might be grateful its meaning has already been mentioned.
8:27: It was narrated that it was revealed about Abu Lubaba bin Abdul Mundhir when he indicated to Banu Qurayza to slaughter. Abu Lubaba said: By God, my feet did not move until I knew that I had betrayed God and His Messenger, and this verse was revealed. When it was revealed, he tied himself to one of the pillars of the mosque and said: By God, I will not taste food or drink until I die or God accepts my repentance. The report is well-known. On the authority of Ikrimah, he said: When the affair of Qurayzah happened, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali, may God be pleased with him, with those people who were with him. When he reached them, they attacked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, came on a piebald horse. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: It is as if I see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wiping the dust from the face of Gabriel, peace be upon them both. I said: Is this Dihya, O Messenger of God? He said: This is Gabriel, peace be upon him. He said: O Messenger of God, what prevents you from going to them from Banu Qurayzah? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How can I protect them? Gabriel said: I will bring this horse of mine to them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode a horse with a thorn, and when Ali, may God be pleased with him, saw it, he said: O Messenger of God, do not worry if you do not go to them, for they will revile you. He said: No, it will be a greeting. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them and said: O brothers of apes and pigs. They said: O Abu al-Qasim, you were not vulgar! They said: We will not submit to the judgment of Muhammad, but we will submit to the judgment of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh. So he submitted. He ruled that their fighters should be killed and their children should be taken captive. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The angel approached me at dawn and revealed about them: O you who have believed, do not betray God and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know. It was revealed about Abu Lubabah, he pointed to Banu Qurayzah when they said: We will submit to the judgment of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh. Do not do that, for it is slaughter, and he pointed to his throat. It was said: The verse was revealed about them that they used to hear something from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and then they would throw it to the polytheists and spread it. It was also said: The meaning is the spoils of war. It is attributed to God, because He is the One who ordered its division. And to the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him), because he is the one who conveys it on behalf of God the Almighty and takes care of it. And betrayal means treachery and concealing something, and from it: He knows the treachery of the eyes (Ghafir 40:19) and “He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: O God, I seek refuge in You from hunger, for it is a wretched bedfellow, and from betrayal, for it is a wretched lining.” Narrated by An-Nasa’i on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say…, and he mentioned it. And betray your trusts is in the accusative case, in accordance with the first. It may also be in the answer, as is said: Do not eat fish and drink milk. Trusts are the deeds that God has entrusted to His servants. It is called a trust because it provides security from the prevention of the right, taken from security. The discussion of fulfilling trusts and deposits and other things has already been presented in An-Nisa’. And you know means what ugliness and shame there is in betrayal. It was also said: You know that it is a trust.
8:28: The Almighty said: And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial. Abu Lubabah had wealth and children among Banu Qurayzah, which led him to be gentle with them, so this is an indication of that. Trial means a test, with which He tested them. And that with God is a great reward. So prefer His right over your right.
8:29: The meaning of piety has already been mentioned. And God knew whether they would be pious or not. So He mentioned it in the form of a condition, because He addressed His servants in the same way that they address one another. So if the servant fears his Lord - by following His commands and avoiding His prohibitions - and leaves doubtful matters for fear of falling into forbidden things, and fills his heart with pure intention, and his limbs with righteous deeds, and guards himself from the impurities of hidden and apparent polytheism by considering other than God in his deeds, and relying on this world by refraining from wealth, He will make for him a criterion between truth and falsehood, and will provide him with the possibility of whatever good he wants. Ibn Wahb said: I asked Malik about the statement of God, the Most High: If you fear God, He will make for you a criterion. He said: A way out. Then he recited: And whoever fears God, He will make for him a way out. (al-Talaq 65:2) Ibn Al-Qasim and Ashhab narrated something similar from Malik, and Mujahid said it before him. The poet said: Malik, from the length of the sorrow, Farqan after the two cats left and disappeared Another said: How can I hope for immortality when death is seeking me, and I have no choice but to separate myself from the cup of death? Ibn Ishaq: A Criterion that separates truth from falsehood. Ibn Zayd said the same. Al-Suddi: Salvation. Al-Farra: Conquest and victory. It was said: He will admit you to Paradise and admit the infidels to Hell.
8:30: This is a report of what the polytheists agreed upon to plot against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Dar al-Nadwa. They agreed to kill him, so they plotted against him and lay in wait for him at the door of his house all night to kill him if he came out. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Ali ibn Abi Talib to sleep on his bed and asked God Almighty to blind them from his traces, but God blinded their sight. He came out while they were asleep, and he put dirt on their heads and got up. When morning came, Ali came out to them and told them that there was no one in the house, so they knew that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had passed away and escaped. This report is well-known in the biography and elsewhere. The meaning of li-thabatuk is li-habasuk to imprison you. It is said: abtabahu to imprison him. Qatada said: li-habasuk to bind you. It was also narrated from him and Abdullah ibn Kathir: li-habasuk to imprison you. Abaan ibn Taghlib and Abu Hatim said: li-habasuk to inflict severe wounds and beatings. The poet said: I said, Woe to you, what is in your newspaper? They said, The Caliph has been afflicted with pain and suffering. Or they kill you or expel you is a conjunction. And they plan is a new sentence. Planning is planning a matter in secret. And God is the best of planners is a subject and predicate. And planning from God is their punishment for their planning without them realizing it.
8:31: It was revealed about Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, who had gone to Al-Hirah to trade and had bought stories of Kalila and Dimna, and Kisra and Caesar. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, related the stories of those who had passed, Al-Nadr said: If I wanted, I could have said something like this. This was impudence and a lie. It was said that they imagined that they could come up with something like it, just as the magicians of Moses imagined, then they tried to do so but failed and said out of stubbornness: This is nothing but legends of the ancients. This has been mentioned previously.
8:32: Readers are on the accusative of truth as report of kana. And huwa was entered for separation. And huwa al-haqq is permissible in the nominative case. From You Al-Zajjaj said: I do not know anyone who read it with it, and there is no difference between grammarians in permitting it, but the reading is a Sunnah, and it is not read in it except with a satisfactory reading. And there is a difference of opinion about who said this statement, so Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr said: The one who said this is Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith. Anas bin Malik: The one who said it is Abu Jahl, narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. Then it is permissible to say: They said it because of a doubt that was in their hearts, or as a way of stubbornness and ambiguity to the people that they were on insight, then what they asked about happened to them on the day of Badr. It was narrated that a Jewish man met Ibn Abbas, and the Jew said: Who are you? He said: From Quraysh. So he said: You are from the people who said: O God, if this is the truth from You the verse. So why should they not say: If this is the truth from You, then guide us to it! These are ignorant people. Ibn Abbas said: And you, O Israelite, are among the people whose feet did not dry from the wetness of the sea in which Pharaoh and his people were drowned, and Moses and his people were saved, until they said: Make for us a god as they have gods. Moses said to them: Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. (al-A’raf 7:138) So the Jew lowered his head in utter confusion. Then it rained rained in torment. And it rained in mercy, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah. It has been mentioned previously.
8:33: When Abu Jahl said: O God, if this is the truth from You the verse was revealed: And God would not punish them while you are among them This is in Sahih Muslim. Ibn Abbas said: The people of a town were not punished until the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the believers left it and joined where they were commanded. And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness Ibn Abbas: They used to say during the circumambulation: Your forgiveness. And seeking forgiveness, even if it is done by the wicked, repels a kind of evil and harm. It was said: Seeking forgiveness refers to the Muslims who are among them. That is, God would not punish them while there are those among them who seek forgiveness from the Muslims. So when they left, God punished them on the Day of Badr and other days. This was said by Ad-Dahhak and others. It was said: Seeking forgiveness here refers to Islam. That is, And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness meaning they submit, as Mujahid and Ikrimah said. It was said: And while they seek forgiveness, meaning in their loins there is someone who seeks forgiveness from God. This was also narrated from Mujahid. It was said: The meaning of they seek forgiveness is if they sought forgiveness. That is, if they sought forgiveness, they would not have been punished. He called them to seek forgiveness, as stated by Qatada and Ibn Zayd. Al-Madaini said on the authority of some scholars: There was a man from the Arabs during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was extravagant with himself. He did not hesitate, but when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, he put on wool and returned from what he had been doing, and he displayed religion and asceticism. So it was said to him: If you had done this while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was alive, he would have been happy with you. He said: I had two guarantees, one of which has passed and the other remains. God Almighty said: And God would not punish them while you are among them. This is a guarantee. The second is: And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness.
8:34: The Almighty said: And what is it that God should not punish them? The meaning is: What prevents them from being punished? That is, they deserve punishment for the ugly deeds and reasons they committed, but for every person there is a set term. So God punished them with the sword after the departure of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And regarding that, the verse was revealed: A questioner asked about a punishment to come (Al-Ma'arij: 1). Al-Akhfash said: An is redundant. An-Nahhas said: If it were as he said, He would have raised He punishes them. "But most of them do not know" meaning that the righteous are His friends.
8:35: Ibn Abbas said: The Quraysh used to circumambulate the House naked, clapping and whistling, and they thought that was an act of worship. And whistling is whistling. And clapping is applauding, as stated by Mujahid, Al-Suddi and Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them. And from it is the saying of Antarah: And the wife of a prostitute left a braid, and she was bitten by its prey, like the cheek of a wise man. That is, it makes a sound. And from it, the animal makes a meowing sound when it blows with wind. Al-Suddi said: The meowing is the whistle, in the tune of a white bird in the Hijaz called the meowing. The poet said: If the cawing chirps outside a meadow, woe to the people of sheep and donkeys. Qatada: Al-Makka is striking with the hands, and Al-Tasdiyya is shouting. According to both interpretations, it is a refutation of the ignorant Sufis who dance, clap, and shock. All of that is reprehensible, and the rational person is above such things, and the one who does it is like the polytheists in what they used to do at the House. Ibn Jurayj and Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he said: Al-Makka is their putting their fingers in their mouths. And Al-Tasdiyya is whistling, they want to distract Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, from prayer. Al-Nahhas said: What is well-known in the language is what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar. Abu Ubaid and others narrated that it is said: Makka yamku makwan and Makka if he whistles. And Sada yasda tasdiyya if he claps, and from this is the saying of Umar ibn Al-Atnabah: They all made a cacophony of noise at home. That is, by clapping. Saeed bin Jubair and Ibn Zayd: The meaning of tasddiyya is to prevent them from entering the House, so the original form according to this is tasaddada, so one of the two dals was replaced with a ya.
8:36: God Almighty says: “Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God. So they will spend it; then it will be for them a cause of regret; then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered to Hell.”God
8:37: The meaning of so that God may distinguish the wicked from the good is the believer from the disbeliever. It has also been said that it is general in all things, including deeds, expenditures, and other things.God
8:38: It contains five issues:God First: The Almighty’s statement: Say to those who disbelieve. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to say this meaning to the disbelievers, whether he said it in this phrase or another. Ibn Atiyyah said: If it had been as Al-Kisa’i mentioned, that it was in the copy of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, Say to those who disbelieve, if you desist, you will be forgiven, then the message would not have been conveyed except with those exact words. This is according to what the words require. Second: The Almighty’s statement, If they desist, meaning from disbelief. Ibn Atiyyah said: “It is inevitable, and the reason for that is the answer to the condition that they will be forgiven for what has passed, and forgiveness for what has passed can only come about if one desists from disbelief.” Abu Saeed Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Zubayri said well: The young man deserves forgiveness if he confesses and then stops what he did and committed. Because God Almighty said about the one who confesses: If they cease, what has occurred will be forgiven them. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Shamasah al-Mahri, who said: We were present with Amr ibn al-As while he was being led to death, crying for a long time. The hadith states: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Didn't you know that Islam destroys what came before it, that migration destroys what came before it, and that Hajj destroys what came before it? The hadith. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a kindness from God, the Most High, that He bestowed upon creation, because the disbelievers plunge into disbelief and crimes, and commit sins and transgressions. If that were to require them to be held accountable, they would never have repented, nor would they have received forgiveness. So God, the Most High, made it easy for them to accept their repentance when they returned, and to offer forgiveness through Islam, and to destroy all of what came before, so that this would be closer to their entering the religion, and more likely to lead to their acceptance of the word of the Muslims. If they knew that they would be held accountable, they would not have repented or submitted. In Sahih Muslim: “Among those who came before you, a man killed ninety-nine people and then asked if there was any chance for him to repent. A worshipper came and asked him if there was any chance for him to repent. He said, ‘There is no chance for you to repent.’ So he killed him, and thus he completed one hundred.” The hadith. So, look at the worshipper’s words, There is no chance for you to repent. When he knew that killing him had made him despair, he did the action of one who despaired of mercy. Scare away corruption of creation, while making things easy is in their best interest. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him that whenever a man who had not killed came to him and he asked him, Is there any chance for the killer to repent? he would say, There is no chance for repentance, to frighten and warn. When someone who had killed came to him and he asked him, Is there any chance for the killer to repent? he would say, You have repentance, to make things easy and to reconcile. This has already been mentioned. Third: Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn Wahb said on the authority of Malik that if someone divorced while a polytheist and then converted to Islam, there is no divorce for him. Similarly, if someone swore and then converted to Islam, there is no breach of it on his part. Similarly, if someone is obligated to do these things, he is forgiven. As for someone who slanders a Muslim and then converts to Islam, or steals and then converts to Islam, the prescribed punishment for slander and theft is carried out on him. If he commits adultery and converts to Islam, or rapes a Muslim woman and then converts to Islam, the prescribed punishment is waived for him. Ashab narrated on the authority of Malik that he said: God the Almighty only means what happened before Islam, of wealth, blood, or anything else. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is correct, based on what we have presented of the generality of His statement: Say to those who disbelieve, if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them, and His statement: Islam abolishes what came before it, and the meaning we have explained of facilitation and not alienation. I said: As for the infidel at war, there is no disagreement about dropping what he did while he was an infidel in the land of war. However, if he entered our country with security and slandered a Muslim, he is to be punished with the prescribed punishment, and if he stole, his hand is to be cut off. The same applies to the dhimmi who slanders with the prescribed punishment of eighty, and if he stole, his hand is to be cut off, and if he killed, he is to be killed. Islam does not drop this punishment for him because he broke the covenant while he was an infidel, according to the narration of Ibn al-Qasim and others. Ibn al-Mundhir said: They differed about a Christian who commits adultery and then converts to Islam, and a witness from the Muslims testifies against him. It was narrated from al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him that while he was in Iraq, there is no prescribed punishment for him or banishment, because God the Almighty said: Say to those who have disbelieved, if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them. Ibn al-Mundhir said: This is in agreement with what was narrated from Malik. Abu Thawr said: If he confesses, while he is a Muslim, that he committed adultery while an infidel, the prescribed punishment is to be carried out on him. It was narrated from al-Kufi that he said: He is not to be punished with the prescribed punishment. Fourth: As for the apostate who converts to Islam and has missed prayers, committed crimes, or destroyed property, it was said: He is ruled by the original disbeliever if he converts to Islam; he is not held accountable for anything he did during his apostasy. Al-Shafi'i said in one of his two opinions: He is bound by every right of God Almighty and of humans, based on the fact that the rights of humans are binding on him, so the rights of God Almighty must be binding on him. Abu Hanifa said: What is for God is dropped, but what is for humans is not dropped. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is the opinion of our scholars, because God Almighty is independent of His rights, while humans are in need of Him. Don't you see that the rights of God Almighty are not binding on a child, but the rights of humans are binding on him? They said: God's statement, Say to those who have disbelieved, if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them is general in its application of the rights of God Almighty. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: And if they return means to fighting, because the word return when it comes in an absolute sense implies a return to a state that a person was in and then moved from. Ibn Atiyyah said: We do not find in this verse for these disbelievers a state similar to what we mentioned except fighting. It is not permissible to interpret it as referring to disbelief, because they did not separate from it. We only said that about return when it is in an absolute sense because it can come in the speech of the Arabs as included in the subject and predicate, so its meaning is the meaning of became, as you say: Zayd returned as a king, meaning he became. And from this is the saying of Umayyah ibn Abi Salt: These are the noble deeds that do not make a woman urinate again after shedding milk from her father with water. This does not include a return to a state to which the referent had previously been linked. It is restricted by its predicate and cannot be limited to anything less than it. Its ruling is the ruling of became. The Almighty’s saying: The way of the ancients has passed. This phrase combines the threat, intimidation, and example of those nations that perished in the past by the punishment of God.
8:39: God Almighty says: And fight them until there is no more persecution meaning disbelief. To the end of the verse. Its meaning and explanation of its words have been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah and elsewhere. Praise be to God.God
8:40: God Almighty says: “But if you turn away, then know that God is your Protector. What an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper.” The seventh part of Al-Qurtubi’s interpretation has been completed, and it will be followed, God willing, by the eighth part. It begins with the Almighty’s saying: And know that whatever you obtain of anything…
8:41: The Almighty said: And know that whatever you gain, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, if you should believe in God. It contains twenty-six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils. Spoils in the language are what a man or group obtains through effort, and from that is the saying of the poet: I have traveled the world until I was satisfied with the spoils of war and returned Another said: The sheep are fed on the day of the sheep, wherever you go, and the deprived are deprived. The spoils of war and the booty have the same meaning. It is said: the people took spoils of war. Know that there is agreement that what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: You have taken spoils of something is the money of the infidels if the Muslims seize it by force and coercion. The language does not require this specification, as we have explained, but the Shari’ah has defined the wording with this type. The Shari’ah has named the money that reaches us from the infidels by two names: booty and fay’. So what the Muslims obtain from their enemy by striving and frightening the horses and riders is called booty. This name has stuck to this meaning until it became a common usage. The booty is derived from the word fa’a yaf’u if it returns, and it is any money that enters the Muslims without war or coercion. Such as the land tax, the skull tax, and the fifth of the spoils of war. Sufyan al-Thawri and Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib said something similar. It was said that they are one and the same, and they include the fifth, as stated by Qatada. It was said that the booty refers to all the money that the Muslims obtain without force. The meanings are similar. Second: This verse abrogates the beginning of the surah, according to the majority. Ibn Abd al-Barr claimed that there was consensus that this verse was revealed after His statement: They ask you about the spoils of war, and that four-fifths of the spoils of war were divided among the conquerors, as will be explained later. And His statement: They ask you about the spoils of war, was revealed when the people of Badr quarrelled over the spoils of war, as mentioned in the beginning of the surah. I said: What indicates the correctness of this is what Ismail bin Ishaq mentioned. He said: Muhammad bin Katheer told us. Sufyan told us. Muhammad bin Al-Sa’ib told me on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas. He said: “On the day of Badr, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever kills someone will have such-and-such, and whoever takes a prisoner captive will have such-and-such.’ They killed seventy and took seventy captive. Abu al-Yusr ibn Amr came with two prisoners and said: ‘O Messenger of God, you promised us that whoever kills someone will have such-and-such, and you have brought two prisoners.’ Sa`d stood up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, we were not prevented by an increase in reward or cowardice toward the enemy, but we stood here fearing that the polytheists would turn their backs. If you give to these, nothing will remain for your companions.’ He said: ‘And these kept saying, and those kept saying,’ and so was revealed: ‘They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger. So fear God and amend that which is between you.’ So they handed the spoils over to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then was revealed: ‘And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it belongs to God.’” It has been said: It is a firm and not abrogated, and that the spoils belong to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and are not divided among the conquerors, and likewise for the Imams who came after him. This is what Al-Mazari narrated from many of our companions, may God be pleased with them, and that the Imam has the right to take it away from them. They cited as evidence the conquest of Mecca and the story of Hunayn. Abu Ubaid used to say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, conquered Mecca by force and attacked its people, then returned it to them and did not divide it or make it spoils for them. Some people saw that this was permissible for the Imams after him. I said: And on this basis the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it belongs to God and the four-fifths are for the Imam, if he wishes he may keep it and if he wishes he may divide it among the conquerors. This is nothing, for what we have mentioned, and because God the Almighty attributed the spoils to the conquerors, saying: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils then specified the fifth to whomever He named in His Book, and was silent about the four-fifths, just as He was silent about the two-thirds in His saying: And his parents inherit him, then his mother shall have a third (An-Nisa’: 11), so the father has two-thirds by consensus. And likewise the four-fifths belong to the conquerors by consensus, as Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abd al-Barr, al-Dawudi, al-Mazari also, Qadi Iyadh and Ibn al-Arabi mentioned. The narrations with this meaning are consistent, and some of them will come. And the meaning of His saying: They ask you about the spoils the verse, is what the Imam gives as a gift to whomever he wishes for what he sees as in the interest before the division. Ata and Al-Hasan said: It is specific to what has escaped from the polytheists to the Muslims, from a male or female slave or animal, and the Imam decides regarding it as he pleases. It was said: What is meant by it are the spoils of war, i.e. their booty, if the Imam wishes, he may give a fifth of it, and if he wishes, he may give it all as a gift. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said about the Imam who sends out a military expedition and they seize the spoils: If the Imam wishes, he may give it all as a gift, and if he wishes, he may give a fifth of it. Abu Omar narrated it from Makhul and Ata. Ali bin Thabit said: I asked Makhul and Ata about the Imam giving the people what they seize as a gift, he said: That is for them. Abu Omar said: Whoever holds this opinion has interpreted the statement of God the Almighty: {They ask you about the spoils. Say, The spoils belong to God and the Messenger} that this is for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to place it wherever he wishes. He did not see that this verse was abrogated by the statement of God the Almighty: {And know that whatever you obtain of spoils - indeed, God has a fifth of it}. It was said: Other than this, which we have already mentioned in the book Al-Qabas in explanation of the Muwatta of Malik bin Anas. None of the scholars, as far as I know, have said that the Almighty’s statement: They ask you about the spoils of war al-Anfal 2:17 abrogates His statement: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it belongs to God. Rather, the majority said, based on what we have mentioned, that His statement: Whatever you obtain of spoils of war abrogates it, and they are the ones who are not permitted to distort or change the Book of God Almighty. As for the story of the conquest of Mecca, there is no proof in it due to the scholars’ disagreement about its conquest. Abu Ubaid said: We do not know of any country in Mecca that resembles it in two respects: One of them is that God had singled out the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) from the spoils of war that He did not give to anyone else, due to His statement: They ask you about the spoils of war al-Anfal 2:17, so we see that this was specific to him.
