The other aspect is that he established laws for Mecca that were not for any other country. As for the story of Hunayn, he compensated the Ansar when they said: He will give the spoils to the Quraysh and leave us while our swords are dripping with their blood! So he said to them: Are you not pleased that people return with this world and you return with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to your homes? Narrated by Muslim and others. No one else has the right to say this, although it is specific to him according to what some of our scholars have said. And God knows best. Third: The scholars did not differ that his statement: And know that whatever you gain of spoils is not general. And that it is included in the specificity, so what they specified by consensus is that they said: The spoils of the murdered go to his murderer if the imam calls for it. And the same applies to slaves, I mean the prisoners, the choice in them is up to the imam without dispute, as will be explained. And what he also specified is the land. The meaning is: Whatever you gain of gold, silver, other goods, and captives. As for the land, it is not included in the generality of this verse, because Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: If it were not for the last of the people, I would not have conquered a village without dividing it as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided Khaybar. And what confirms this doctrine is what was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Iraq withheld its qafiz and dirham, and Syria withheld its mudd and dinar.” The hadith. At-Tahawi said: It was withheld means it will be withheld, so this indicates that it is not for the conquerors, because what the conquerors own does not have a qafiz or dirham, and if the land were divided, nothing would remain for those who came after the conquerors. And God Almighty says: And those who came after them (al-Hashr 59:10) in conjunction with His statement: for the poor emigrants. He said: Rather, what is transferred from one place to another is divided. Al-Shafi’i said: Everything that is obtained from the spoils of war from the people of the land of war, whether little or much, such as a house, land, goods, or other than that, is divided, except for adult men, for the imam has the choice among them to grant a gift, kill, or take captive. The way of what is taken from them and the captives is the way of the spoils. He argued with the generality of the verse. He said: And the land is inevitably spoils, so it must be divided like all other spoils. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided what was conquered by force in Khaybar. They said: Even if it is permissible to claim exclusivity in the land It is permissible to claim something other than the land, thus invalidating the ruling of the verse. As for the verse of the gathering, there is no proof in it, because that only applies to the spoils of war, not the booty. His statement, and those who came after them is a resumption of speech with a supplication for those who preceded them in faith, and nothing else. They said: The action of Omar in stopping the land is not without one of two aspects: Either it was spoils that pleased its people, and they were pleased with that, so he stopped it. Likewise, Jarir narrated that Omar was pleased with its people. Likewise, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) did with the captives of Hawazin, when they came to him, his companions were pleased with what was in their hands. Or what Omar stopped was booty, so he did not need to please anyone. The Kufians went to the option of giving the Imam the choice to divide it or approve it and impose a tax on it. And it becomes their property like the land of peace. Our Sheikh Abu al-Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It seems that this combined the two proofs and mediated between the two schools of thought, and this is what Umar, may God be pleased with him, understood with certainty, and therefore he said: If it were not for the last of the people, then he did not inform about the abrogation of the action of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor about its specificity to them, except that the Kufians added to what Umar did, for Umar only endowed it for the interests of the Muslims and did not give it to the people of peace, and they are the ones who told the Imam to give it to the people of peace. Fourth: Malik, Abu Hanifa and Al-Thawri held that the spoils are not for the killer, and that their ruling is the ruling of spoils, unless the emir says: Whoever kills a person, his spoils are his, in which case they are his. Al-Layth, Al-Awza’i, Al-Shafi’i, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, Abu Ubaid, Al-Tabari and Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The spoils are for the killer in every case, whether the imam said it or not. However, Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, said: The spoils are for the killer only if he killed a person facing him, but not if he killed him turning away from him. Abu Al-Abbas Ibn Surayj, one of Al-Shafi’i’s companions, said: The hadith is not: Whoever kills a person, his spoils are his in general, because of the consensus of scholars that whoever kills a prisoner, a woman, or an old man, he is not entitled to the spoils of any of them. The same applies to whoever attacks a wounded person, and whoever kills someone whose hands and feet have been cut off. He said: Likewise, the one who flees does not refrain from fleeing, and he is like one who has been bound. He said: Thus, it is known that the hadith only made the spoils for the one whose killing has an additional meaning, or for the one whose killing is a virtue, and he is the one who kills on the advance, because of the expense involved. As for the one who inflicts a great loss, then no. At-Tabari said: The spoils are for the killer, whether he is facing his killer or retreating, fleeing or fighting him, if he is in battle. This is refuted by what Abd al-Razzaq and Muhammad ibn Bakr mentioned on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: I heard Nafi`, the freed slave of Ibn `Umar, say: We have not ceased to hear that if Muslims and infidels meet and a Muslim man kills a non-Muslim man, his spoils are his, unless it is in the midst of battle, because in that case it is not known who killed whom. This apparently refutes the statement of al-Tabari, as he stipulated that the spoils of war should be killed in battle in particular. Abu Thawr and Ibn al-Mundhir said: The spoils of war belong to the killer in battle or otherwise, whether he advances or retreats, flees or revolts, in all cases, due to the generality of the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever kills a person, his spoils belong to him. I said: Muslim narrated on the authority of Salamah bin Al-Akwa’ who said: We went on an expedition with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) against Hawazin. While we were sacrificing with the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), a man came on a red camel and made it kneel. Then he took a rope from its saddle and tied the camel with it. Then he went forward to eat lunch with the people and kept looking. Among us were some who were weak and thin in the back, and some of us were on foot. Then he went out running fast, came to his camel, released its rope, made it kneel, sat on it and aroused it, so the camel ran fast with him. A man followed him on a thin camel. Salamah said: I went out running fast and was at the hip of the camel, then I advanced until I was at the hip of the camel, then I advanced until I took hold of the camel's reins and made it kneel. When it put its knee on the ground, I drew my sword and struck the man's head and he flew away. Then I came leading the camel, on which was its saddle and weapons. The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) met me while the people were with him. He said: Who killed this man? They said: Ibn al-Akwa'. He said: He has all his spoils. This is Salamah, whom he killed while fleeing and not returning, and he gave him his spoils. In it is an argument for Malik that the killer does not deserve the spoils except with the permission of the Imam, because if it was due to him by the killing itself, he would not have needed to repeat this statement. Another of his arguments is what Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah mentioned, who said: Abu al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Qays, on the authority of Bishr ibn Alqamah, who said: I fought a man on the day of al-Qadisiyyah and killed him and took his spoils. I went to Sa`d, and Sa`d addressed his companions and said: This is the spoils of Bishr ibn Alqamah, and it is better than twelve thousand dirhams, and we have given it to him as a gift. If the spoils were for the killer by decree of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, there would be no need for them to attribute it to themselves by their own efforts, and the killer would have taken it without their order. And God knows best. In the Sahih, “Mu`adh ibn `Amr ibn al-Jamuh and Mu`adh ibn `Afra struck Abu Jahl with their swords until they killed him. They came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Which of you killed him? Each of them said: I killed him. He looked at their swords and said: Both of you killed him. He ruled that his spoils should go to Muadh ibn Amr ibn al-Jamuh. This is explicit that the spoils do not belong to the killer, because if they were his, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have divided them between them. It is also in Sahih on the authority of Awf ibn Malik who said: I went out with those who went out with Zaid bin Haritha in the Battle of Mu'tah, and my reinforcements from Yemen accompanied me. He narrated the hadith, in which it says: Awf said: O Khalid, did you not know that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ruled that the spoils go to the killer? He said: Yes, but I thought it was too much. Abu Bakr and Al-Barqani narrated it with the same chain of transmission as Muslim, and he added to it a statement that Awf bin Malik said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not take a fifth of the spoils, and a reinforcement was their companion in the Battle of Mu'tah in a corner of Syria. He said: A Roman from among them began to attack the Muslims while he was on a blond horse with a golden saddle, a stained belt, and a sword decorated with gold. He said: He incited them. He said: The reinforcement was gentle with him until he passed by him, and he struck the hock of his horse and he fell, and he attacked him with his sword and killed him and took his weapon. He said: So Khalid bin Al-Walid gave it to him and kept it from him. Awf said: I said to him: Give it all. Did you not hear the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: The spoils go to the killer! He said: Yes, but I thought it was too much. Awf said: There was some talk between us, so I said to him: I will tell the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). Awf said: When we gathered with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), Awf mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), so he said to Khalid: Why did you not give it to him? He said: I thought it was too much. He said: Give it to him. I said to him: Do you hope that I will fulfill what I promised you? He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) became angry and said: O Khalid, do not give it to him. Are you leaving my commanders to me? This clearly indicates that the spoils are not due to the killer on the basis of the killing itself, but rather by the opinion and consideration of the imam. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: The spoils are not due to the killer except in a duel specifically. Fifth: Scholars differed about dividing the spoils into fifths. Al-Shafi’i said: It is not to be divided into fifths. Ishaq said: If the spoils are small, they are for the killer, and if they are large, they are divided into fifths. Omar bin Al-Khattab did this with Al-Bara’ bin Malik when he fought the Marzban and killed him. The value of his belt and his pillars was thirty thousand, so he divided that into fifths. Anas narrated from Al-Bara’ bin Malik that he killed one hundred polytheists, except for one man, in a duel. When they invaded Al-Zara, the peasant of Al-Zara came out and said: A man and a man. Al-Bara’ came out and they fought with their swords, then they embraced each other. Al-Bara’ left him and sat on his liver. Then he took the sword and slaughtered him, took his weapon and belt and brought it to Omar. He gave him the weapon and valued the belt at thirty thousand, so he divided it into fifths, and said: It is money. Al-Awza’i and Makhul said: The spoils are spoils and there is a fifth in them. Something similar was narrated from Omar bin Al-Khattab. The argument for Al-Shafi’i is what Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Awf bin Malik Al-Ashja’i and Khalid bin Al-Walid, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the spoils belong to the killer and did not take a fifth of the spoils.” Sixth: The majority of scholars are of the opinion that the spoils are not given to the killer unless he establishes evidence of his killing. Most of them said: One witness is sufficient, according to the hadith of Abu Qatada. It was also said: Two witnesses or one witness and an oath. Al-Awza’i said: It is given to him merely on the basis of his claim, and evidence is not a condition for entitlement. Rather, if that happens, it is preferable to prevent dispute. Do you not see that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave Abu Qatada the spoils of his murdered person without testimony or an oath? The testimony of one person is not sufficient, and a ruling cannot be based on it alone. Al-Layth ibn Sa’d said the same. I said: I heard our Sheikh, the Hafiz Al-Mundhiri Al-Shafi’i, Abu Muhammad Abdul-Azim say: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him the spoils based on the testimony of Al-Aswad bin Khuza’i and Abdullah bin Unais. Based on this, the dispute is resolved, the problem is removed, and the ruling is valid. As for the Malikis, their statement is that the Imam does not need evidence for it, because it is a gift from the Imam from the beginning. The condition of testimony was for him, and if he did not stipulate it, it is permissible for him to give it to him without testimony. Seventh: They differed about what the spoils are. As for the weapon and everything needed for fighting, there is no disagreement that it is from the spoils, and his horse if he fought on it and was killed off. Ahmad said about the horse: It is not from the spoils. Likewise if there are dinars or jewels in his purse or belt or something like that, there is no disagreement that it is not from the spoils. They differed about what he adorns himself with for war. Al-Awza’i said: All of that is from the spoils. A group said: It is not from the spoils. This is narrated from Sahnun, may God have mercy on him, except for the belt, which according to him is from the spoils. Ibn Habib said in Al-Wadihah: The bracelets are from the spoils. Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: Then a fifth of it belongs to God. Abu Ubaid said: This abrogates the Almighty’s saying at the beginning of the Surah: “Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not take a fifth of the spoils of Badr, so his ruling on not taking a fifth was abrogated by this. Unless it appears from the saying of Ali, may God be pleased with him, in Sahih Muslim: I had a portion of my share of the spoils on the day of Badr, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had given me a portion of the fifth on that day. The hadith says that it was a fifth. If this is the case, then the statement of Abu Ubaid is rejected. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is possible that the fifth that was mentioned on me was from one of the battles that took place between Badr and Uhud, for there were the battles of Banu Sulaym, Banu al-Mustaliq, Dhi Amr, and Bahran, and no fighting was recorded in them, but it is possible that spoils were taken. And God knows best. I said: This interpretation is refuted by what Ali said on that day, which was a reference to the day the spoils of Badr were divided. However, it is possible that it was from the fifth, if there was no fifth in Badr, from the fifth of the company of Abdullah bin Jahsh, because it was the first spoils taken in Islam, and the first fifth was in Islam. Then the Qur’an was revealed: And know that whatever you obtain of anything - indeed, a fifth of it is for God. This is more appropriate than the first interpretation. And God knows best. Ninth: What is in His statement: what you have gained means that, and the letter ha is omitted, meaning that which you have gained. The letter fa was added because the speech has the meaning of reward. The second is an emphasis on the first, and it is permissible to break it. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr. Al-Hasan said: This is the key to the speech, the world and the hereafter belong to God, mentioned by Al-Nasa’i. And God Almighty began the speech about the spoils of war and the fifth by mentioning Himself, because they are the most honorable earnings, and He did not attribute charity to Him because it is the filth of people. Tenth - Scholars differed on how to divide the fifth into six opinions: First: A group said: The fifth is divided into six, so the sixth is given to the Kaaba, which is for God. The second is for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The third is for relatives. The fourth is for orphans. The fifth is for the poor. The sixth is for wayfarers. Some of the proponents of this opinion said: The share that is for God is returned to those in need. Second: Abu Al-Aaliyah and Al-Rabi’ said: The spoils of war are divided into five, one share is set aside from it, and the four are divided among the people. Then he strikes with his hand the share that he set aside, and whatever he takes of it he gives to the Kaaba. Then he divides the rest of the share that he set aside into five: a share for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a share for the relatives, a share for the orphans, a share for the poor, and a share for the wayfarer. Third: Al-Munhal bin Amr said: I asked Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hussein about the fifth, and he said: It is for us. I said to Ali: God Almighty says: And the orphans, the needy, and the traveler (al-Baqarah 2:177), and he said: Our orphans and our needy. Fourth: Al-Shafi’i said: It is divided into five. He saw that the share of God and His Messenger is one, and that it is spent on the interests of the believers, and the four-fifths are divided into the four categories mentioned in the verse. Fifth - Abu Hanifa said: It is divided among three: orphans, the poor, and the wayfarer. In his view, the ruling on the kinship of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was lifted upon his death, just as the ruling on his share was lifted. They said: And one begins with the fifth by repairing bridges, building mosques, and the salaries of judges and soldiers. Something similar to this was also narrated from Al-Shafi’i. Sixth - Malik said: It is entrusted to the Imam’s consideration and effort, so he takes from it without estimation, and gives from it to relatives based on his effort, and spends the rest in the interests of the Muslims. The four caliphs said this, and they acted on it. This is indicated by his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have nothing of what God has bestowed upon you except one-fifth, and one-fifth is returned to you. He did not divide it into fifths or thirds, but rather he mentioned those mentioned in the verse to alert them, because they are among the most important to whom it is given. Al-Zajjaj said, citing Malik’s evidence: God the Almighty said: “They ask you, what they should spend. Say, ‘Whatever you spend of good is for parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveler.’” (al-Baqarah 2:215) And it is permissible for a man, by consensus, to spend on these categories if he sees fit. Al-Nasa’i reported on the authority of Ata’ who said: The one-fifth of God and the one-fifth of His Messenger are one. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would carry some of it, give some of it, put it wherever he wanted, and do with it as he wanted. Eleventh - The Almighty’s saying: And to the near of kin. The lam is not to indicate entitlement and ownership, but rather it is to indicate the expenditure and location. The evidence for this is what Muslim narrated: “Al-Fadl ibn Abbas and Rabi’ah ibn Abd al-Muttalib came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and one of them spoke and said: O Messenger of God, you are the most pious of people, and the most loyal of people. We have reached the age of marriage, so we have come to command you to take charge of some of this charity, so that we may pay it to you as people pay it, and we may receive it as they receive it. He remained silent for a long time until we wanted to speak to him. He said: Zainab kept glaring at us from behind the curtain, not to speak to him. He said: Then he said: Charity is not permissible for the family of Muhammad, rather it is the filth of people. Call for me Muhamiyah - who was in charge of the fifth - and Nawfal bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib. He said: So they came to him and said to Muhamiyah: Marry this boy to your daughter - to Al-Fadl bin Abbas - so he married him. He said to Nawfal bin Al-Harith: Marry this boy to your daughter, meaning Rabi’ah bin Abdul Muttalib. He said to Muhamiyah: Give them such and such a dowry from the fifth. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I have nothing from what God has bestowed upon you except the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you. He gave all of it and some of it, and he gave it to those whose hearts were to be reconciled, and he is not among those whom God mentioned in the division, so this indicates what we mentioned, and God is the Grantor of success. Twelfth - The scholars differed regarding the relatives in three opinions: All of Quraysh, as some of the predecessors said, because “when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended Al-Safa, he began to shout: O sons of so-and-so, O sons of Abd Manaf, O sons of Abd al-Muttalib, O sons of Ka’b, O sons of Murrah, O sons of Abd Shams, save yourselves from the Fire.” The hadith will come in Ash-Shu’ara’. Ash-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Abu Thawr, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and Muslim ibn Khalid said: Banu Hashim and Banu Abd al-Muttalib, and because “when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the share of the relatives between Banu Hashim and Banu Abd al-Muttalib, he said: They did not leave me in ignorance or Islam. Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib are one thing, and he interlaced his fingers.” Narrated by al-Nasa’i and al-Bukhari. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Layth said: Yunus told me, and he added: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not divide anything between Banu Abd Shams and Banu Nawfal. Ibn Ishaq said: Abd Shams, Hashim and al-Muttalib are brothers on their mother’s side, and their mother is ‘Atika bint Murrah. Nawfal was their brother on their father’s side. Al-Nasa’i said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the shares for the relatives, who are Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, among them the rich and the poor. It has been said that it is for the poor among them and not the rich, such as orphans and wayfarers - and this is the most correct of the two opinions in my opinion. - And God knows best - and the young and the old, the male and the female are equal, because God the Most High made that for them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among them. There is no mention in the hadith that he preferred some of them over others. Third: Banu Hashim in particular, as stated by Mujahid and Ali bin Al-Hussein. It is also the statement of Malik, Al-Thawri, Al-Awza’i and others. Thirteenth - When God Almighty explained the ruling on the fifth and was silent about the four fifths, this indicates that it belongs to the conquerors. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained this by saying: And any sacrifice that disobeys God and His Messenger, then its fifth is for God and His Messenger, and then it is yours. There is no disagreement about this among the nation or among the imams, as Ibn al-Arabi narrated in his Ahkam and others. However, if the imam sees fit to grant the captives a favor by releasing them, he does so, and the rights of the conquerors over them are nullified, as “the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did with Thamamah ibn Aththal and others, and he said: If Al-Mut'am bin Adi were alive and spoke to me about these stinking ones - meaning the prisoners of Badr - I would have left them for him. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. As a reward for his action in the matter of breaking the document. He has the right to kill all of them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ayt from among the prisoners, and he killed Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith with Al-Safra', and there is no disagreement about this. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a share like the share of the spoils of war, whether he was present or absent. The share of the chosen one, he chose a sword or an arrow or a servant or an animal. Safiyyah bint Huyayy was from the chosen one from the spoils of Khaybar. Dhu Al-Fiqar was also from the chosen one. It was cut off with his death, except for Abu Thawr, who saw it remaining for the Imam, so he made it the same as the share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The wisdom behind that was that the people of ignorance considered the leader to have a quarter of the spoils. Their poet said: You have the square, the pure, your wisdom, the active and the curious. Another said: He is one of the quarters of the armies, twenty of his crucifixions, and he is counted among the living. It is said: A quarter of the army is a quarter of it if he takes a quarter of the spoils. Al-Asma'i said: A quarter in the pre-Islamic era and a fifth in Islam. So he would take a quarter of the spoils without law or religion, and he would select from it. Then he would control whatever he wanted after the selection, and we would take whatever was left over from it and whatever was left over from the spoils and goods for him. So God the Almighty made the religion firm by saying: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God. And He kept the share of the selected for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and dropped the rule of the pre-Islamic era. Amer Al-Sha'bi said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a share called Al-Safi. If he wanted, he could give him a male or female slave or a horse, which he could choose before the fifth.” Narrated by Abu Dawud. In the hadith of Abu Hurairah, he said: “The slave will be met and will say: ‘O so-and-so! Did I not honour you, make you a leader, give you a wife, make horses and camels subservient to you, and let you rule and reign supreme?’” Narrated by Muslim. Tarabaa’ with a unified ba’ underneath means taking a quarter, i.e. a quarter of what your people obtain from spoils and earnings. Some of the companions of al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him said that one-fifth of the fifth was for the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him), and he would spend it on providing for his children and wives, and save from that for his year’s sustenance, and spend the rest on horses and weapons. This is refuted by what ‘Umar narrated, who said: “The wealth of Banu Nadir was among the spoils of war that God bestowed upon His Messenger, for which the Muslims had not fought with horses or camels. It was exclusively for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He would spend from it on himself a year’s sustenance, and whatever remained he would put into mounts and weapons, equipment in the way of God.” Narrated by Muslim. He said: And the fifth is returned to you. Fourteenth - There is no indication in the Book of God that the rider is superior to the foot soldier, rather it states that they are equal, because God the Almighty made the four-fifths for them and did not distinguish the foot soldier from the rider. If it were not for the reports transmitted from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the rider would be like the foot soldier, the slave would be like the free man, and the child would be like the adult. Scholars have differed in the division of the four-fifths. What most scholars agree on, as mentioned by Ibn al-Mundhir, is that the rider is given two shares and the foot soldier is given one share. Among those who said this are Malik ibn Anas and those who followed him from the people of Medina. Al-Awza’i and those who agreed with him from the people of Ash-Sham said the same. Al-Thawri and those who agreed with him from the people of Iraq said the same. It is the opinion of Al-Layth ibn Sa’d and those who followed him from the people of Egypt. Al-Shafi’i and his companions said the same. Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, Ya’qub and Muhammad said the same. Ibn al-Mundhir said: We do not know of anyone who disagreed with this except Al-Nu’man, for he disagreed with the Sunnah and what most scholars of old and new agreed upon. He said: The rider is not given more than one share. I said: Perhaps he likened it to the hadith of Ibn Omar: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave two shares to the horseman and one share to the foot soldier.” Ad-Daraqutni reported it and said: Ar-Ramadi said: Ibn Numayr said so. An-Naysaburi told us: In my opinion, this is a mistake on the part of Ibn Abi Shaybah or Ar-Ramadi, because Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr, and others narrated it on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them, contrary to this, which is: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave three shares to the man and his horse, one share for him and two shares for his horse.” This is how Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr narrated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Numayr, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Umar, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, and he mentioned the hadith. And in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Umar: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave the horse two shares and its owner one share.” This is the text. Al-Daraqutni narrated, “On the authority of Al-Zubayr, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave me four shares on the day of Badr: two shares for my horse, one share for me, and one share for my mother from among the relatives. And in another narration: and one share for his mother, the share of the relatives. And it was narrated on the authority of Bashir bin Amr bin Muhsin, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave four shares to my horse, and one share to me, so I took five shares.” It was said that this was up to the Imam’s discretion, so he would implement what he saw fit. And God knows best. Fifteenth - There is no difference between a rider and a foot soldier with more than one horse, and this is what Al-Shafi’i said. Abu Hanifa said: He shares more than one horse, because it is more difficult and more beneficial, and this is what Ibn Al-Jahm of our companions said, and Sahnun narrated it from Ibn Wahb. Our evidence is that there is no narration from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he shares more than one horse, and the same is the case with the Imams after him, and because the enemy cannot fight except on one horse, and anything more than that is luxury and extra equipment, and this does not affect the increase in the two shares, like the one who has extra swords or spears, and the third and fourth are considered. It was narrated from Sulayman bin Musa that he shares for whoever has horses, one share for each horse. Sixteenth - Only free-range horses are to be given a share, because of their ability to charge and retreat, and mules and camels are like them in that regard. And what is not like that is not to be given a share. It was said: If the Imam permits it, he is to be given a share, because the benefit from it differs according to the place. Camels and mules are suitable for rugged places such as valleys and mountains, and free-range horses are suitable for places where charge and retreat are possible, so that was related to the opinion of the Imam. Free-range horses are the horses of the Arabs. Camels and mules are the horses of the Romans. Seventeenth - Our scholars differed regarding the weak horse. Ashhab and Ibn Nafi said: He is not entitled to a share, because it is not possible to fight on it, so it is similar to the broken one. It was said: He is entitled to a share because it is hoped that he will recover. He is not entitled to a share for the emaciated if he is in a place where he is not useful, just as he is not entitled to a share for the broken one. As for the one who is slightly ill, such as a horse with a crippling illness, or something similar that does not prevent him from obtaining the intended benefit, he is entitled to a share. The borrowed or rented horse is given, as is the one that is usurped, and its share goes to its owner. The share is due to the horses even if they are on ships and the spoils fall at sea, because they are prepared to go to land. Eighteenth - There is no right to the spoils for the rank and file, such as the workers and craftsmen who accompany the army for a living, because they did not intend to fight nor did they go out to fight. It was said: They are entitled to a share, based on the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The spoils are for those who witnessed the battle. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. This is not an argument because it came as a statement for those who directly engaged in war and went out to it, and it is sufficient for God the Almighty to explain the fighters and the earners of livelihood from the Muslims, as He made them two distinct groups, each one of them has its own situation in its ruling, as He said: He knows that there will be among you sick and others traveling throughout the land seeking from the bounty of God and others fighting in the cause of God (al-Muzzammil 73:20). However, if these people fight, it does not harm them that they are earning their livelihood, because the reason for entitlement has been found in them. Ashhab said: None of them deserves it even if he fights, and Ibn Al-Qassar said the same about the hired worker: He does not get a share even if he fights. This is refuted by the hadith of Salamah bin Al-Akwa’ who said: I was a follower of Talha ibn Ubayd God, watering his horse, grooming it, serving it, and eating from his food. The hadith says: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave me two shares, the share of the horseman and the share of the foot soldier, and he combined them for me. Narrated by Muslim. Ibn al-Qassar and those who said his opinion used as evidence the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, mentioned by Abd al-Razzaq, in which it says: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abd al-Rahman: These three dinars are his fortune and share of his conquest in the affairs of this world and the hereafter.” Nineteenth - As for slaves and women, the doctrine of the Book is that they are not to be given shares or given a share. It was said: They are to be given a share, and this is what the majority of scholars said. Al-Awza’i said: If a woman fights, she is to be given shares. He claimed that “the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave shares to the women in Khaybar.” He said: And the Muslims adopted that from us. And Ibn Habib from our companions inclined to this opinion. Muslim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he had in his letter to Najdah: You ask me, did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, go to war with women? He did go to war with them, and they treated the wounded and took from the spoils. As for a share, no share was given to them. As for boys, if they are able to fight, then we have three opinions: giving them a share or denying them until they reach adulthood, based on the hadith of Ibn Umar, and Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi’i said the same. The difference is between fighting and receiving a share, or not fighting and not receiving a share. The first is correct. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the Banu Qurayzah to kill those who had hair and to leave those who had not. This was in consideration of the ability to fight, not of puberty. Abu Omar narrated in Al-Isti’ab, “On the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be presented with the young men of the Ansar, and he would include those of them who had reached maturity. One year I was presented with him, and he included a young man and turned me back. I said: O Messenger of God, you included him and you turned me back. If he wrestled with me, I would defeat him. He said: So wrestle with me and I defeated him, so include me. As for the slaves, they are not given a share either, and they are given a share. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth - If the infidel attends with the permission of the Imam and fights, then in our view there are three opinions regarding his share: the share and its denial, and Malik and Ibn Al-Qasim said this. Ibn Habib added: And they have no share. And in the third - and it is from Sahnoon - there is a distinction between the Muslims being independent on their own, so he does not receive a share, or not being independent and needing his assistance, so he receives a share. If he does not fight, he is not entitled to anything. And the same applies to slaves with free people. Al-Thawri and Al-Awza’i said: If help is sought from the People of the Covenant, he receives a share for them. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: He does not receive a share for them, but he is given a share. Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, said: The Imam hires them from money that has no specific owner. If he does not do so, he gives them the share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he said in another place: He is given a share for the polytheists if they fight with the Muslims. Abu Omar said: Everyone agreed that if the slave, who is one of those whose security is permissible, fights, he is not given a share for him, but he is given a share, so the infidel is more deserving of not receiving a share for him. Twenty-one - If a slave or a dhimmi went out as thieves and took the property of the people of war, it is theirs and is not subject to one-fifth, because none of them or women are included in the generality of the words of God Almighty: “And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God.” As for the infidels, they have no role, without dispute. Sahnun said: What a slave takes is not subject to one-fifth. Ibn al-Qasim said: It is subject to one-fifth, because it is permissible for his master to permit him to fight and fight for the sake of religion, unlike the infidel. Ashab said in the book of Muhammad: If a slave or a dhimmi goes out with the army and takes spoils, the spoils are for the army and not them. Twenty-second: The reason for deserving the share is the witnesses of the battle for the victory of the Muslims, as mentioned above. If he witnessed the end of the battle, he is entitled to it. If he was present after the end of the fighting, then he is not. If he was absent due to defeat, then the same applies. If he intended to join a group, then his entitlement is not dropped. Al-Bukhari and Abu Dawud narrated: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abaan bin Saeed to lead a raiding party from Medina to Najd. Abaan bin Saeed and his companions came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Khaybar after he had conquered it, and their horses were packed with palm fibres. Abaan said: ‘Distribute to us, O Messenger of God.’ Abu Hurairah said: ‘I said: ‘Do not distribute to them, O Messenger of God.’ Abaan said: ‘You are in it, O wool, descending upon us from a stray head.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Sit down, O Abaan.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not distribute to them.” Twenty-third - The scholars differed regarding the one who went out to witness the battle and was prevented from doing so by an excuse such as illness. There are three opinions regarding the confirmation of his share and its denial: A distinction is made in the third, which is the well-known, so it is confirmed if the error occurred before the battle and after the escape, which is the most correct, as stated by Ibn al-Arabi. And it is denied if it occurred before that. And like the one whom the emir sent to the army on a matter in the interest of the army and that distracted him from witnessing the battle, then he is given a share, as stated by Ibn al-Mawaz, and narrated by Ibn Wahb and Ibn Nafi’ from Malik. And it was narrated that he is not given a share, but rather he is given a share due to the lack of a reason for which he deserves a share, and God knows best. Ashab said: A share is given to the prisoner even if he is in chains. The correct opinion is that he is not given a share, because he is a property that is deserved by the battle, so the one who is absent or present while sick is like the one who did not attend. Twenty-fourth: The absolutely absent person is not given a share. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) never gave a share to an absent person except on the day of Khaybar, when he gave a share to the people of Hudaybiyyah, those who were present and those who were absent, based on the words of God the Almighty: God has promised you abundant spoils which you will take (al-Fath 48:20), as stated by Musa bin Uqbah. This was narrated from a group of the Salaf. The day of Badr was divided among Uthman, Saeed bin Zaid, and Talhah, and they were absent, so they are as if they were present, God willing. As for Uthman, he stayed behind to visit Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), by his order, because of her illness. So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) assigned him his share and reward, so he was as if he had been present. As for Talhah bin Ubaidullah, he was in Ash-Sham on business, so the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) assigned him his share and reward, so he is counted among the people of Badr. As for Saeed bin Zaid, he was also absent in Ash-Sham, so the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) assigned him his share and reward. So he is counted among the people of Badr. Ibn al-Arabi said: As for the people of al-Hudaybiyyah, it was an appointment from God that was reserved for those people, and no one else would share in it with them. As for Uthman, Sa`id, and Talhah, it is possible that they had shares of the fifth, because the nation is unanimous that whoever remains due to an excuse should not have a share. I said: It appears that this was specific to Uthman, Talha and Saeed, and no one else could be compared to them. And their share was from the spoils of war like everyone else who was present, not from the fifth. This is what appears from the hadiths, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: When Uthman was absent from Badr, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with him and she was sick. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You will have the reward and share of a man who witnessed Badr. Twenty-fifth - The Almighty’s statement: If you have believed in God. Al-Zajjaj from a group said: The meaning is, then know that God is your Master, if you are. So, if is related to this promise. A group said: If is related to His statement: And know that whatever you have taken as spoils. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is the correct view, because His statement: And know includes the command to submit and surrender to God’s command regarding the spoils, so he connected if to His statement: And know according to this meaning, that is, if you are believers in God, then submit and surrender to God’s command regarding what He has informed you of regarding the division of the spoils. God Almighty says: And We did not send down to Our Servant on the Day of Criterion - water in the accusative case, in apposition to the name of God - the Day of Criterion meaning the day on which truth was distinguished from falsehood, which was the Day of Badr. The day the two armies met - the party of God and the party of Satan - and God has power over all things.
8:42: The Almighty said: When you were on the lower side of the valley and they were on the farthest side. That is, We sent down when you were in this condition. Or the meaning could be: And remember when you were. The side of the valley is the valley side. It is read with the damma and kasra of the 'ayn, so with the damma the plural is 'Adi, and with the kasra 'Adi, like Lihyah and Lahyan, Fariyah and Faryan. The lower world is the feminine of the lower. The farthest is the feminine of the farthest. From dana yadnu, and qasa yaqusu. It is also said: al-Qasiya. The original is waw, and it is the language of the people of Hijaz, qaswa. So the lower world was next to Madinah, and al-Qaswa is next to Makkah. That is, when you are descending to the edge of the valley on the lower side to Madinah, and your enemy is on the farthest side. And the caravan is lower than you means the caravan of Abu Sufyan and others. They were in a place lower than them to the seashore in the luggage. It was said: They are the camels that were carrying their luggage, and they were in a place where they were safe, as a blessing from God the Almighty to them, so He mentioned His blessings upon them. The riders are initially lower than you, an adverb in the position of the predicate. That is, a place lower than you. Al-Akhfash, Al-Kisa’i, and Al-Farra’ permitted that the riders are lower than you, meaning they are lower than you. The riders are the plural of rider. The Arabs do not say: riders except for a group of camel riders. Ibn Al-Sikkit and most linguists reported that rider and riders are not said except for the one on camels, and it is not said for someone who is on a horse or other than it. The riders, the riders, the riders, and the riders are only on camels, from Ibn Faris. And if you had made an appointment, you would have differed in the appointment meaning that the agreement would not have happened due to their large number and your small number, because if you had known their large number, you would have been late, so God the Almighty granted you success. That God may accomplish a matter that is to be accomplished from the victory of the believers and the manifestation of the religion. The lam in that God may accomplish is related to something omitted. Meaning: He gathered them so that God might decide. Then he repeated it and said: So that he may perish, meaning he gathered them there to decide a matter. So that he may perish who perishes “from” is in the nominative case. And he lives is in the accusative case in apposition to so that he may perish. And the proof is the establishment of the argument and evidence. That is, so that he who dies may die after seeing the proof and seeing the lesson. So the proof was established against him. And the same applies to the life of he who lives. Ibn Ishaq said: So that he who disbelieves may disbelieve after a proof was established against him and his excuse was cut off, and he who believes may believe based on that. And it was read from hayya with two ba’s according to the original, and with one double ya’. The first is the reading of the people of Madinah, Al-Bazzi, and Abu Bakr. The second is the reading of the rest. And it is the choice of Abu Ubaid, because it is like that in the Mushaf.
8:43: Mujahid said: The Prophet (peace be upon him) saw them in his sleep a little, so he told his companions about it, and God made them steadfast with that. It was said: By sleep he meant the place of sleep, which is the eye, meaning in the place of your sleep, so it was deleted, according to Al-Hasan. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a good opinion. However, the first is more permissible in Arabic, because it came: And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes, and made you as few in their eyes. This indicated that this was a vision of meeting, and that was a vision of sleep. The meaning of you would have failed is you would have been cowardly from war. And you would have disputed in the matter would have differed. But God saved means He saved you from disobedience. Ibn Abbas: From failure. It is possible from both of them. It was said: Saved means He completed the matter of the Muslims with victory.
8:44: The Almighty said: And when He showed them to you, when you met, as few in your eyes. This was while awake. It is permissible to carry the first to be awake as well if you say: The dream is the place of sleep, which is the eye, so the first in this case is specific to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is for everyone. Ibn Masoud said: I said to a man who was next to me on the day of Badr: Do you see them as seventy? He said: They are about a hundred. So we captured a man and said: How many were you? He said: We were a thousand. And He made you few in their eyes. This was at the beginning of the fighting until Abu Jahl said on that day: They are only cannibals, take them by force and tie them up with ropes. When they began fighting, the Muslims became great in their eyes and became numerous, as He said: They will see them twice their number, with the sight of their eyes (Al Imran 3:13), according to what was explained in Al Imran. That God may accomplish a matter which was to be done. This was repeated, because the meaning in the first is the encounter, and in the second is the killing of the polytheists and the glorification of the religion, which is the completion of the blessing upon the Muslims. And to God return all matters, meaning their destiny and return to Him.
8:45: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, when you meet a company meaning a group then stand firm is an order to stand firm when fighting the infidels, just as in the verse before it, which forbade fleeing from them. So the order and the prohibition met in the same way. This is an emphasis on standing firm against the enemy and being patient with him. God the Almighty says: And remember God often that you may succeed. Scholars have three opinions regarding this remembrance: First: Remember God when your hearts are anxious, for remembering Him helps you to be steadfast in times of hardship. Second: Be steadfast in your hearts and remember Him with your tongues, for the heart does not rest when meeting God and the tongue is disturbed. So He commanded remembrance so that the heart may be steadfast in certainty and the tongue may be steadfast in remembrance, and say what the companions of Saul said: Our Lord, pour out upon us patience and plant firmly our feet and give us victory over the disbelieving people. (al-Baqarah 2:250). This state can only come about through the strength of knowledge and the ignition of insight, which is the praiseworthy courage in people. Third: Remember what you have of God’s promise to you in His purchase of your souls and His trust in you. I said: It is more apparent that it is a mention of the tongue that is in harmony with the heart. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: If anyone had been permitted to omit remembrance, he would have permitted Zachariah. God the Almighty says: “Do not speak to people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much.” (Al Imran 3:41). And a man would have been permitted to do so in war. God the Almighty says: When you meet a company, stand firm and remember God much. Qatada said: God the Almighty has made His remembrance obligatory upon His servants, when they are busy fighting with swords. The ruling on this remembrance is that it should be kept quiet, because raising one’s voice in a place of battle is bad and disliked if the one remembering is one. But if it is done by all of them during an attack, then it is good, because it weakens the enemy’s resolve. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Qays ibn Ibad who said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked making noise during combat. Abu Burdah narrated something similar on the authority of his father on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas said: Covering one’s face during combat is disliked. Ibn Atiyyah said: And with this - and God knows best - the Murabitun followed the example of removing it during combat to protect themselves with it.
8:46: The Almighty said: And obey God and His Messenger and do not dispute This is a continuation of the command to them, and taking them by the hand in their differences in the matter of Badr and their dispute. Fatafhashlū is in the accusative case with the letter fa' in response to the prohibition. Sibawayh does not permit the deletion of the letter fa' and the jussive, but al-Kisa'i permitted it. It was read tafhashlū with the kasra of the sheen. This is not known. Wa dhahab rayhkum means your strength and victory, as you say: the wind belongs to so-and-so, if he is dominant in the matter. The poet said: If your winds blow, seize them, for every fluttering wind has a stillness. Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: There was never victory except with a wind that blew and struck the faces of the infidels. And from this is his saying, peace be upon him: I was aided by the north wind and destroyed by the south wind. Al-Hakam said: And your wind will go away, meaning the north wind, because with it Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and his nation were aided. Mujahid said: “And the wind of the companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, went away when they disputed with him on the day of Uhud.” The Almighty says: “And be patient. Indeed, God is with the patient.” He commands patience, which is praiseworthy in all situations, especially in times of war, as He says: If you meet a group, then stand firm.
8:47: That is, Abu Jahl and his companions who went out on the day of Badr to support the caravan. They went out with singing girls, female singers and musical instruments. When they reached Al-Juhfah, Khafaf Al-Kinani - who was a friend of Abu Jahl - sent gifts to him from his son, and said: If you wish, I will support you with myself and whoever of my people has fled. Abu Jahl said: If we are fighting God as Muhammad claims, then by God we have no power over God, and if we are fighting people, then by God we have power over people. By God, we will not stop fighting Muhammad until we reach Badr and drink alcohol there, and the female singers play for us, for Badr is a season of the seasons of the Arabs and a market of their markets, until the Arabs hear of our departure and fear us for the rest of time. So they went to Badr, but what happened happened of their destruction. In the language, arrogance means strengthening with the blessings of God Almighty and what He has clothed in well-being over sins. It is a source in the place of a state. That is, they went out arrogantly, hypocritically and denouncing. And they were prevented from misleading people.
8:48: It was narrated that Satan appeared to them on that day in the form of Suraqa bin Malik bin Ja'sham, who was from Banu Bakr bin Kinanah. The Quraysh were afraid that Banu Bakr would come to them from behind, because they had killed a man from among them. So when he appeared to them, he said what God had told him about. Ad-Dahhak said: Satan came to them on the day of Badr with his banner and his soldiers. He cast into their hearts the idea that they would never be defeated while they were fighting for the religion of their fathers. And Ibn Abbas said: God supported his Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a thousand angels. Gabriel, peace be upon him, was with five hundred angels on his side, and Michael was with five hundred angels on his side. Iblis came with an army of devils, carrying a banner in the form of men from Banu Mudlij, and Satan was in the form of Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju’sham. Satan said to the polytheists: No one among the people can defeat you today, and I am your protector. When the people lined up, Abu Jahl said: O God, give us the right, so support it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hand and said: O Lord, if you destroy this group, you will never be worshipped on earth again. Gabriel said: Take a handful of dirt. So he took a handful of dirt and threw it in their faces, and there was not one of the polytheists who did not get his eyes, nostrils, and mouth. So they turned back, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to Satan. When he saw him, his hand was in the hand of a polytheist. Satan pulled his hand away and turned back, along with his followers. The man said to him: O Suraqa, did you not claim that you were our protector? He said: I am innocent of you, for I see what you do not see. Al-Bayhaqi and others mentioned it. In the Muwatta of Malik, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abi Ubla, on the authority of Talhah bin Ubayd God bin Kurayz, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Satan has never seen himself smaller, more insignificant, more defeated, or more angry than on the Day of Arafah. This is only because he saw the descent of mercy and the forgiveness of great sins by God, except for what he saw on the Day of Badr. It was said: What did he see on the Day of Badr, O Messenger of God? He said: He saw Gabriel dispersing the angels. The meaning of nakas is to return in the language of Sulaym, according to a historian and others. The poet said: Turning back is not an honor, but honor is taking the initiative. Another said: The regression of those who come later will not benefit them, nor will the progress of those who come before them harm them. There is no retreat here, but rather an escape, as he said: If he hears the call to prayer, he turns away and farts. “I fear God.” It was said: Satan feared that the day of Badr was the day I was looking at. It was also said: Satan lied when he said: I fear God, but he knew that he had no power. The plural of jar is ajwar and jiran, and in rare cases it is jirah.
8:49: It was said: The hypocrites are those who show faith and conceal disbelief. And those in whose hearts is disease are the doubters, and they are less than the hypocrites, because they are new to Islam, and among them is some weakness of intention. They said when going out to fight and when the two ranks met: Their religion has deceived them. It was said: They are one, and this is more appropriate. Do you not see the saying of God the Almighty: Those who believe in the unseen (al-Baqarah 2:3), then He said: And those who believe in what has been revealed to you (al-Baqarah 2:4), and they are one.
8:50: It was said: He meant those who remained and were not killed on the day of Badr. It was also said: It refers to those who were killed at Badr. The answer to if is omitted, meaning: You would have seen a great matter. They strike is in the place of the state. Their faces and their backs means their backs, he referred to it as the backs, as Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair said. Al-Hasan: Their backs, and he said: A man said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Messenger of God, I saw something like a shoelace on Abu Jahl’s back. He said: That is the beating of the angels. It was said that this beating will be at death. It may also be on the Day of Resurrection when they will be taken to Hell. And taste the punishment of the burning fire. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is, And they will say, ‘Taste,’ but it was omitted. Al-Hasan said: This is on the Day of Resurrection, when the keepers of Hell will say to them: Taste the punishment of the burning fire. It was narrated that some of the commentaries said: There were iron clubs with the angels, and whenever they struck, fire would flare up in the wounds. That is why God said: And taste the punishment of the burning fire. Taste can be both tangible and in meaning. It may be used as a test or trial, for example: Ride this horse and taste it. Look at so-and-so and taste what he has. Al-Shamakh said, describing a horse: So he tasted it and she gave him enough softness to drown the arrow. Its origin is from the taste in the mouth.
8:51: That is in the nominative case, meaning that is the matter. Or that is your reward. Because of what your hands have put forth meaning what you have acquired of sins. And that God is not unjust to the servants since He has made the way clear and sent the messengers, so why did you disobey? And that is in the accusative case in apposition to what, and if you wish, you can put it in the accusative case, meaning and that, and delete the ba, or meaning: and that is because God. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case in conjunction with that.
8:52: Habit is custom. It was mentioned earlier in Al Imran. That is, the custom of torturing them when taking souls and in the graves is like the custom of the people of Pharaoh. It was said: The meaning is that these people were punished with killing and captivity just as the people of Pharaoh were punished with separation, that is, their habit is like the habit of the people of Pharaoh.
8:53: Explanation. That is, this punishment, because they changed and altered, and God's blessing upon the Quraysh was fertility and abundance, security and well-being. Do they not see that We have made a secure sanctuary while people are being snatched away all around them? (al-Ankabut 29:67) The verse. Al-Suddi said that God's blessing upon them was Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but they disbelieved in him, so he was transferred to Medina and the punishment befell the polytheists.
8:54: This is not a repetition, because the first is a custom in denying, and the second is a custom in changing, and the rest of the verse is clear.
8:55: The Almighty says: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God meaning those who crawl on the face of the earth in the knowledge and judgment of God. Those who disbelieve - they will not believe is similar to the deaf and dumb who do not use reason (al-Anfal 8:22).
8:56: Then he described them and said: Those among them with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear God. That is, they do not fear revenge. And the word from among them in his saying from them is for partiality, because the covenant was only made with their nobles, then they broke it. What is meant by them are Qurayzah and Nadir, according to Mujahid and others. They broke the covenant and aided the polytheists of Mecca with weapons, then they apologized and said: We forgot. So he made a covenant with them again, but they broke it on the day of the Trench.
8:57: Condition and its answer. The letter nun was added to emphasize what ma was added to, this is what the Basrans said. The Kufians said: The heavy and light nun are added with ma in mujazat to differentiate between mujazat and khayyir. The meaning of thaqafananhum is that you capture them and put them in a state of weakness, in which you are able to overcome them and defeat them. This is necessary from the wording, as he said in war. Some people said: You encounter them and meet them. It is said: I thaqafatuhu thaqfan, meaning I found him. So-and-so is thaqafa laqf, meaning he is quick to find what he tries and seeks. Thaqaf laqf. A woman is thaqaf. The first statement is more appropriate, because of its connection to the verse as we have explained. The one who encounters may be overcome, so it is possible to be displaced by it, or it may not be overcome. Thaqaf in the language: what is used to tie a canal and the like. From this is what An-Nabigha said: She calls us Qaina, and the iron bites her like a culture bites the deafness of pipes. He scattered them from behind them. Saeed bin Jubair said: The meaning is he warned those behind them about them. Abu Ubaid said: It is the language of the Quraysh 106:he scattered them, he heard about them. Ad-Dahhak said: he tortured them. Az-Zajjaj: He did to them an act of killing by which those behind them were scattered. Dispersion in the language means: scattering and dispersing. It is said: I scattered the sons of so-and-so, I uprooted them from their places and expelled them from them until they left them. And the same is the case for the singular, you say: I left him scattered from his homeland and his family. A poet from Hudhayl said: I roam the valleys every day for fear that a wise man will lead me astray. And from it is the word sharad al-ba’ir the camel or animal if it separates from its owner. And min means who, as Al-Kisa’i said: It was narrated from Ibn Mas’ud sharadh with the voiced dhal, and they are two languages. Qatrib said: sharadh with the voiced dhal means tormenting. And with the silent dhal it means separation, as Al-Tha’labi narrated. Al-Mahdawi said: sharadh has no basis, unless it is a substitute for the silent dhal because of their similarity, and sharadh is not known in the language. And it was read min khalfahum with a kasra on the meem and the fa. La’allahum dhikrūn means they remember your promise to them. And it was said: This refers to those behind them, because the one who was killed does not remember, meaning those behind them who did the same as them were scattered.
8:58: It has three issues: First: The Almighty said: And if you fear treachery from a people meaning deceit and a breach of covenant. Then throw back to them on equal terms. This verse was revealed regarding Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadir. At-Tabari narrated it on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Atiyyah said: What appears from the wording of the Qur’an is that the matter of Banu Qurayzah ended when He said: Then he scattered with them those behind them. Then the Almighty began in this verse with His command regarding what He would do in the future with those from whom He feared treachery, so this verse was applied to them. Banu Qurayzah were not among those whose treachery was feared, but rather their treachery was apparent and well-known. Second: Ibn al-Arabi said: If it is said, how is it permissible to break a covenant with fear of betrayal, and fear is suspicion without certainty, so how can the certainty of a covenant be dropped with suspicion of betrayal? The answer is from two aspects: First: Fear may come with the meaning of certainty, just as hope may come with the meaning of knowledge. God the Almighty said: What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God? (Nuh: 13). Second: If the signs of betrayal appear and its evidence is proven, it is obligatory to abandon the covenant so that persistence in it does not lead to destruction, and it is permissible to abandon certainty here out of necessity. However, if certainty is known, then there is no need to abandon the covenant with them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went to the people of Mecca in the year of the conquest, when it became well-known that they broke the covenant, without abandoning their covenant with them. Rejection is throwing and rejecting. Al-Azhari said: Its meaning is that if you make a covenant with a people and you know that they have broken the covenant, do not rush to break it until you tell them that you have broken the covenant and the truce, so that they are equal in knowledge of the breach, then attack them. An-Nahhas said: This is one of the miracles of the Qur’an, the likes of which cannot be found in speech, despite its brevity and many meanings. The meaning is: But if you fear treachery from a people between you and them, then throw away the covenant to them, that is, say to them, I have thrown away your covenant with you, and I will fight you, so that they may know that and be with you in knowledge. Do not fight them while there is a covenant between you and them and they trust you, for that would be treachery and betrayal. Then he explained this by saying: Indeed, God does not love the traitors. I said: What Al-Azhari and Al-Nahhas mentioned about breaking the covenant with knowledge of its breach is refuted by the action of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the conquest of Mecca. When they broke it, he did not address them, but rather said: O God, cut off our report of them and their invasion. This is also the meaning of the verse, because in cutting off the covenant with them and breaking it with knowledge of it, there is a breach of their covenant and equality with them. As for without knowledge of their breach of the covenant, it is not permissible and is not permitted. Al-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Salim bin Amir, who said: “There was a treaty between Muawiyah and the Romans, and he was marching towards their country to get closer, and when the treaty expired he would attack them. Then a man came to him on a horse or a mule saying: ‘God is Great, God is Great, loyalty, no treachery.’ They looked and saw that he was Amr ibn Abasa. Muawiyah sent for him and asked him. He said: ‘I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever has a treaty with a people should not tighten the knot or loosen it until its term expires or he denies it to them on equal terms.’ So Muawiyah returned with the people.” Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Equality means equality and moderation. The rajaz poet said: Strike the faces of your treacherous enemies until they respond to you in the same way. Al-Kisa’i said: Al-Sawa’a means justice. It may also mean the middle, as in the Almighty’s saying: In the middle of Hellfire (al-Saffat 37:55). And from this is the saying of Hassan: Woe to the companions of the Prophet and his family after sunset in the midst of the atheists Al-Farra: It is said, So throw it to them equally, openly, not secretly. Third: Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every traitor will have a banner raised for him on the Day of Resurrection, according to the extent of his treachery. Beware, there is no traitor more treacherous than a general leader.” Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: Treachery towards the Imam is greater and more heinous than towards others, because of the corruption in that. If they betray and that is known about them, and they do not break the covenant, the enemy will not trust them with a covenant or peace treaty, so their power will increase and their harm will increase, and that will repel people from entering the religion, and will cause the leaders of the Muslims to be censured. But if the enemy has no covenant, then every trick should be used against him, and every deception should be resorted to. This is what the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is based on: War is deception. Scholars have differed on whether one should fight alongside a treacherous imam, with two opinions. Most of them said that one should not fight alongside him, unlike the traitor and the immoral. Some of them said that one should fight alongside him. Both opinions are in our school of thought.
8:59: The Almighty said: And let not those who disbelieve think that they will outstrip meaning whoever escaped the battle of Badr was the first to live. Then He resumed and said: Indeed, they will not escape meaning in this world until God gives you victory over them. It was said: He means in the Hereafter. This is the saying of Al-Hasan. Ibn Amir, Hafs and Hamzah read yaḥsabna with a ya' and the rest with a ta', so that the verb has a subject pronoun. And those who disbelieved is the first object. And sabakwa is the second object. As for the reading with a ya', a group of grammarians including Abu Hatim claimed that this is a mistake and it is not permissible to read it with it, and it does not accommodate someone who knows grammar or has understood it. Abu Hatim said: Because yaḥsabna did not come with an object and it needs two objects. Al-Nahhas said: This is a severe bias, and the reading is permissible and the meaning is: And let not those who disbelieved behind them think that they will outstrip, so the pronoun would refer to what came before, except that reading with a ta' is clearer. Al-Mahdawi: Whoever reads with the letter ya may have the pronoun of the Prophet (peace be upon him) in the verb, and those who disbelieved have preceded would be the two objects. It is possible that those who disbelieved are the subject, and the first object is omitted, meaning: And let not those who disbelieved think that they have preceded. Makki: It is possible to omit with preceded that, so it fills the place of the two objects, and the estimate is: And let not those who disbelieved think that they have preceded, so it is like Do people think that they will be left alone (al-Ankabut 29:2) in filling the place of the two objects. Ibn Amir read that they are not helpless with the opening of the hamza. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid ruled out this reading. Abu Ubaid said: It is only permissible if the meaning is: And let not those who disbelieved think that they will not be helpless. Al-Nahhas said: What Abu Ubaid mentioned is not permissible according to the Basran grammarians, it is not permissible to think that Zaid is outside, except with the kasra of the alif, and it is not permissible because it is in the place of the subject, as you say: I thought that Zaid’s father was outside, and if it was opened, the meaning would be I thought that Zaid was outside. This is impossible, and it also includes the remoteness of the fact that there is no basis for what he said to have a correct meaning, unless he makes la redundant, and there is no basis for directing a letter in the Book of God the Almighty to lengthening without an argument that must be accepted. The reading is good as long as the meaning is: because they are not unable. Makki: The meaning is that the disbelievers should not think that they have missed because they are not unable, meaning they will not miss. For an is in the accusative case by deleting the lam, or in the genitive case by applying the lam due to its frequent deletion with an, and this is narrated from Al-Khalil and Al-Kisa’i. The rest read it with a kasra on in to resume and cut off from what came before it, and this is the choice, because it contains a meaning of emphasis, and because the group is on it. It was narrated from Ibn Muhaisin that he read they do not fail with emphasis and a kasra on the noon. An-Nahhas: This is wrong for two reasons: First - that the meaning of his inability is his weakness and the weakness of his command. Second - that it should have been with two noons. The meaning of his inability is that his death preceded him until he was unable to do so.
8:60: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And prepare against them. God, the Exalted, commanded the believers to prepare strength for the enemies after He emphasized the importance of piety. If God, the Exalted, had willed, He could have defeated them with words, spitting in their faces, and a handful of dirt, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did. But He wanted to test some people with others through His prior knowledge and His effective judgment. Whatever you prepare for your friend of good or your enemy of evil is included in your preparation. Ibn Abbas said: Strength here means weapons and bows. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on the pulpit, say: “And prepare against them whatever you are able of power. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery.” This is a text narrated by Uqbah Abu Ali Thamamah bin Shafi al-Hamadani, and there is no other version of it in Sahih. And there is another hadith on archery also from Uqbah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Lands will be opened to you, and God will suffice you. None of you will be unable to play with his arrows.” And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Everything that a man does for fun is false except shooting with his bow, training his horse, and playing with his family, for these are all true. The meaning of this, and God knows best, is that everything that a man does for fun that does not benefit him in this life or the hereafter is false, and it is better to ignore it. Although he does these three things to amuse himself and to be active, they are true because they are connected to something that may be beneficial, for shooting with the bow and training his horse are both aids in fighting. Playing with family may lead to a child who will worship God alone and become one, so these three are true. In the Sunan of Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God will admit three people into Paradise because of a single aral-Saff 61:the maker who seeks good in making it, the shooter, and the one who shoots it.” The virtue of archery is great and its benefits are immense for Muslims, but its punishment is severe for the unbelievers. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O sons of Ishmael, shoot, for your father was an archer. Learning horsemanship and the use of weapons is a communal obligation. It may also be obligatory. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And from the tethering of horses. Al-Hasan, Amr ibn Dinar, and Abu Haywah read and from the tethering of horses with a damma on the ra’ and the ba’, the plural of ribat, like kitab and kutubu. Abu Hatim said on the authority of Ibn Zayd: The ribat of horses is five or more, and its plural is ribat. It is that which is tied, it is said from it: he tied, he ribats, a ribat. And he tied, he irtabat, irtabatan. And the tethering of horses and their tethering is their tethering in front of the enemy. The poet said: God ordered to tie it to his enemy in war. God is the best guide. Makhool bin Abdullah said: Blame for tying up and locking up horses, which God recommended to the Prophet Muhammad Horse tethering is a great virtue and a noble status. Urwah al-Barqi had seventy horses prepared for jihad. The preferred ones among them are females, as stated by Ikrimah and a group.
