This is correct, for the belly of a female is a treasure and her back is glory, and Gabriel’s horse was female. The imams narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Horses are of three types: for a man they are a reward, for a man they are a cover, and for a man they are a burden.” The hadith does not specify a male or a female. The best of them is the one with the greatest reward and the most benefit. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Which slaves are best? He said: The most expensive in price and the most precious to their owners.” Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Wahb al-Jashmi - who was a companion of the Prophet - that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Name yourselves with the names of the prophets, and the most beloved names to God the Almighty are Abdullah and Abd al-Rahman. Tie up horses and stroke their forelocks and rumps, and put garlands on them, but do not put garlands on them. And you should have every bay horse with a white spot on its forehead, or blond horse with a white spot on its forehead, or black horse with a white spot on its forehead.” Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Qatada that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The best horses are those that is dark raven, with a white spot on the right, then those that are dark raven and have a clear right hand. If they are not dark raven, then they are bay with this feature.” Al-Darimi also narrated it on the authority of Abu Qatada, “A man said: O Messenger of God, I want to buy a horse, so which one should I buy? He said: Buy a dark raven, with a white spot on the right, or a bay with this feature, and you will gain and be safe.” The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) disliked horses with white spots. White spots are when a horse has white spots on its right leg and on its left hand, or on its right hand and left leg. Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him. It is mentioned that the horse on which Al-Hussein bin Ali may God be pleased with them both was killed was white. Third: If it is said: His statement, And prepare against them whatever you are able of power, would have been sufficient, so why did He specifically mention archery and horses? It is said to him: Since horses are the origin of wars and their burdens, in whose forelocks goodness is tied, and they are the strongest of power and the most powerful of equipment and the fortresses of knights, and with them one roams the field, He specifically mentioned them as an honor, and swore by their dust as an honor. So He said: And the charging steeds, panting (al-Adiyat 100:1) and the verse. Since arrows are among the most effective things used in wars and in striking the enemy and the closest to reaching lives, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically mentioned them and drew attention to them. Similar to this in the verse of at-Tazil, Gabriel and Michael (al-Baqarah 2:98) and there are many like it. Fourth: Some of our scholars have used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of endowing horses and weapons, and making treasuries and storehouses for them as equipment for enemies. Scholars have differed regarding the permissibility of endowing animals such as horses and camels with two opinions: prohibition, which is what Abu Hanifa said; and validity, which is what Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, said. It is more correct, due to this verse, and the hadith of Ibn ‘Umar about the horse that was carried in the path of God, and his saying, peace be upon him, regarding Khalid: As for Khalid, you are wronging Khalid, for he has withheld his armor and provisions for the sake of God. The hadith. And what was narrated “that a woman gave a camel for the sake of God, and her husband wanted to perform Hajj, so she asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Give it to him so that he may perform Hajj on it, for Hajj is for the sake of God.” And because it is wealth that is used for the sake of worship, it is permissible to endow it like a four-wheeled camel. Al-Suhayli mentioned in this verse the names of the horses of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his war equipment. Whoever wants it will find it in the book of Al-A’lam. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: And you terrify thereby the enemy of God and your enemy, meaning you frighten thereby the enemy of God and your enemy from among the Jews, Quraysh, and the infidel Arabs. And others besides them, meaning the Persians and the Romans, as al-Suddi said. It was also said: the jinn. This is the choice of al-Tabari. It was also said: What is meant by this is everyone whose enmity is not known. Al-Suhayli said: It was said: They are Qurayzah. It was also said: They are from the jinn. Others were also said. Nothing should be said about them, because God the Almighty said: And others besides them whom you do not know, God knows them, so how can anyone claim to have knowledge of them, unless there is an authentic hadith that came in this regard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is his statement in this verse: They are the jinn. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The devil does not drive anyone crazy in a house in which there is an old horse. It was called old because it had been freed from the hybrids. This hadith was narrated by Al-Harith bin Abi Usamah on the authority of Ibn Al-Maliki on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He narrated: The jinn do not come near a house in which there is a horse, and they are repelled by the neighing of horses. Sixth - The Almighty said: And whatever you spend meaning give in charity. It was also said: spend it on yourselves or your horses, in the way of God, it will be fully repaid to you in the Hereafter, the good deed is rewarded tenfold to seven hundredfold, to many times over. And you will not be wronged.
8:61: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: “And if they incline to peace, then incline to it.” He said to it because peace is feminine. It is possible for the feminine to be for the action. And inclination is leaning. He says: If they incline - meaning those to whom he has abandoned their covenant - to peace, meaning reconciliation, then incline to it. And a man inclined to another: he leaned towards him, and from this the ribs were called jawaneh sides, because they leaned towards the filling. And camels inclined: if their necks leaned while walking. And Dhu al-Rummah said: If he dies on a saddle, his soul is revived by your memory, and the sent camels are at their zenith. Al-Nabigha said: Jawah has become certain that if the two armies meet, his tribe will be the first to prevail. It means the bird. And the night falls when it approaches and lowers its ropes to the ground. And peace and peace are reconciliation. Al-A'mash, Abu Bakr, Ibn Muhaisin and Al-Mufaddal read Al-Salam with a kasra on the seen. The rest read it with a fatha. The meaning of that has been fully explained in Al-Baqarah. And peace may be from submission. The majority read Fajanah with a fatha on the noon, and it is the language of Tamim. And Al-Ashab Al-Uqaili read Fajanah with a damma on the noon, and it is the language of Qais. Ibn Jinni said: And this language is the analogy. Second: There is a difference of opinion regarding this verse, whether it is abrogated or not. Qatada and Ikrimah said: It was abrogated by Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). And fight the polytheists altogether (al-Tawbah 9:36). They said: It abrogated every truce, until they say there is no god but God. Ibn Abbas said: The abrogating verse is “So do not weaken and call for peace” (Muhammad 47:35). It was said: It is not abrogated, rather he meant accepting the jizyah from those who pay the jizyah. The companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made peace with many non-Arab countries during the time of Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and the imams who came after him, in many of the lands of the Persians, on what they took from them, and they left them as they were, although they were able to eradicate them. Likewise, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made peace with many of the people of the lands on the basis of money that they pay, including Khaybar, whose people were returned to it after they were defeated on the condition that they work and pay half. Ibn Ishaq said: Mujahid said: This verse refers to Qurayzah, because the jizya is accepted from them, but nothing is accepted from the polytheists. Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd said: The meaning of the verse is: If they invite you to peace, then respond to them. And there is no abrogation in it. Ibn al-Arabi said: And this is how the answer to it differs, and God the Almighty said: “So do not weaken and call for peace while you are superior, and God is with you” (Muhammad 47:35). So if the Muslims are in a state of honor, strength, and protection, and a large group, and severe hardship, then there is no peace, as He said: There is no peace until horses stab spears and skulls are struck with thin white bullets. If the Muslims have an interest in making peace, for a benefit they can bring or a harm they can prevent, then there is nothing wrong with the Muslims initiating it if they need it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made peace with the people of Khaybar on conditions that they broke, so he broke their peace. Ad-Damri and Ukaydir made peace with Dumah and the people of Najran, and he made a truce with the Quraysh for ten years until they broke his covenant. The caliphs and companions continued to follow this path that we have legislated, and they worked in the ways that we have explained. Al-Qushayri said: If the Muslims are in power, then the truce should not last for more than one year. If the infidels are in power, then it is permissible to make a truce with them for ten years, but it is not permissible to extend it beyond that. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made a truce with the people of Makkah for ten years. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The scholars differed regarding the period of time that was between the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the people of Makkah in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah. Urwah said: It was four years. Ibn Jurayj said: It was three years. Ibn Ishaq said: It was ten years. Ash-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him said: It is not permissible to make a truce with the polytheists for more than ten years, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did in the year of Hudaybiyyah. If the polytheists make a truce for more than that, it will be broken, because the original ruling is to fight the polytheists until they believe or pay the jizyah. Ibn Habib said on the authority of Malik may God be pleased with him: It is permissible to make a truce with the polytheists for one, two, or three years, and for an extended period. Al-Muhallab said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) only brought this case against them, which appears to be weak for the Muslims, “because God prevented the she-camel of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from going to Mecca when he went there and it knelt down. He said: He who prevented the elephant prevented her.” According to what Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Al-Miswar bin Makhramah. It indicates the permissibility of making peace with the polytheists and making a truce with them without taking money from them, if the Imam sees fit. When there is a need, it is permissible for the Muslims to conclude a peace treaty with money that they give to the enemy: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a truce with Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari and al-Harith ibn Awf al-Murri on the day of the Confederates, on the condition that he would give them a third of the produce of Medina, and that they would leave with those with them from Ghatafan and abandon Quraysh, and that they would return with their people from them. This statement was a bargain and not a contract. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw that they had repented and were satisfied, he consulted Sa`d ibn Mu`adh and Sa`d ibn `Ubadah, and they said: O Messenger of God, is this something you like so that we may do for you, or something that God has commanded you to do so that we may listen to it and obey, or something that you may do for us? He said: Rather, it is something that I will do for you, for the Arabs have shot you with one bow. Sa`d ibn Mu`adh said to him: O Messenger of God, by God, we and these people were upon polytheism and idol worship, we did not worship God nor did we know Him, and they never hoped to obtain a fruit from us, except by purchase or hospitality, so when God honored us with Islam, and guided us to it and made us victorious through you, should we give them our money! By God, no.” We will give them nothing but the sword, until God judges between us and them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with that and said: You have that. He said to Uyaynah and Al-Harith: Go back, for you have nothing with us but the sword. Sa`d took the scroll, and it did not contain the testimony that there is no god but God, so he erased it.
8:62: The Almighty said: And if they intend to deceive you meaning by appearing peaceful to you, but concealing treachery and betrayal, then avoid them, for their corrupt intentions do not concern you. Then God is sufficient for you God will suffice you, meaning He will take care of your sufficiency and protection. The poet said: If there is a battle and the stick splits, then you and Al-Dahhak are enough, the sword of Engineer Enough with you and enough with the laughing Saif. God Almighty says: It is He who supported you with His victory meaning He strengthened you with His victory. He means the day of Badr. And with the believers An-Nu’man ibn Bashir said: It was revealed about the Ansar.
8:63: And He united their hearts meaning He brought together the hearts of the Aws and Khazraj. Bringing hearts together despite the intense tribalism among the Arabs was one of the signs and miracles of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because one of them would slap his face and fight for it until he got it back. They were the most zealous of God's creation, so God united them through faith, until a man would fight his father and brother because of religion. It was said: He meant bringing together the Muhajireen and the Ansar. The meanings are similar.
8:64: This is not a repetition, as he said previously: And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is God and this is a specific sufficiency. In his saying: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God he intended to generalize, meaning God is sufficient for you in every situation. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about the conversion of Umar, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had thirty-three men and six women convert to Islam with him, then Umar converted to Islam and they became forty. The verse is Meccan, and was written by the order of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a Medinan surah, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri. I said: What he mentioned about the conversion of Omar, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the opposite occurred in the biography. On the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: We were not able to pray at the Kaaba until Omar converted to Islam. When he converted to Islam, he fought the Quraysh until he prayed at the Kaaba and we prayed with him. Omar converted to Islam after those of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had left for Abyssinia. Ibn Ishaq said: All of those who reached the land of Abyssinia and migrated to it from the Muslims, except for their children who left with them as children or were born there, were eighty-three men, if Ammar bin Yasir was among them. And he doubts that. Al-Kalbi said: The verse was revealed in Al-Baida’ in the Battle of Badr before the fighting. The Almighty said: And whoever follows you of the believers. It was said: The meaning is: God is sufficient for you, and sufficient for you are the Muhajireen and Ansar. It was also said: The meaning is: God is sufficient for you, and sufficient for whoever follows you. This was said by Al-Sha’bi and Ibn Zayd. The first is from Al-Hasan. Al-Nahhas and others chose it. So, according to the first statement, who is in the nominative case, in apposition to the name of God the Almighty. According to the meaning: Then sufficient for you is God and those who follow you of the believers. According to the second, it is implied. Similar to it is the statement of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: God and the sons of Qaylah will suffice him. It was said: It is possible that the meaning is and those who follow you of the believers, God is sufficient for them, so the predicate is implied. It is possible that who is in the accusative case, meaning: God will suffice you and those who follow you.
8:65: The Almighty said: "O Prophet, urge the believers to fight" meaning urge and exhort them. It is said: haraḍ ‘ala al-amr, waṣib, wasab, and ikb all mean the same thing. The one who is on the verge of destruction is the one who is close to destruction, and from this is the Almighty’s saying: "Until you become a patient person" (Yusuf 12:85) meaning you melt away from grief, so you are close to destruction and are among those who perish. "If there are twenty among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred" is a statement that includes a promise with a condition, because its meaning is that if twenty among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred. Twenty, thirty, and forty are each a noun placed in the form of the plural for this number. This noun is used in the same way as Palestine. If someone says: Why did he break the first twenty and open the first thirty and what comes after it up to eighty except sixty? The answer according to Sibawayh is that twenty from ten is like two from one, so he broke the first twenty like he broke two. The evidence for this is their saying: Sixty and ninety, just as it was said: Six and nine. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: If there are twenty among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred, was revealed, and this was difficult for the Muslims, when God imposed on them that not one out of ten should flee.
8:66: Then came the alleviation and said: Now God has lightened your burden. Abu Tobah read until His saying: One hundred patient ones will overcome two hundred. He said: So when God lightened their number, He reduced their patience by the amount He had lightened their burden. Ibn al-Arabi said: Some people said that this was on the day of Badr and it was abrogated. This is a mistake on the part of the one who said it. It has never been reported that the polytheists lined up with the Muslims on it, but God, the Almighty, imposed that on them first, and made it conditional on you understanding what you are fighting for, which is the reward. And they do not know what they are fighting for. I said: The hadith of Ibn Abbas indicates that this was an obligation. Then, when this was difficult for them, the obligation was reduced to the proof of one for two, so it was made easier for them and it was written for them that one hundred should not flee from two hundred. According to this statement, it is an alleviation, not an abrogation. And this is good. Judge Ibn al-Tayyib mentioned that if some of the ruling or some of its descriptions are abrogated, or its number is changed, then it is permissible to say that it was abrogated, because in that case it is not the first, but rather it is different. He mentioned a difference of opinion on this.
8:67: It has five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Prisoners is the plural of prisoner, like killed and killed and wounded and wounded. The plural of prisoner is also said: prisoners with a damma on the hamza and prisoners with a fatha on it, and it is not high. They used to tie the prisoner with a chain, which is the chain, so every prisoner who was taken prisoner was called a prisoner, even if he was not taken prisoner. Al-A’sha said: Poetry tied me to its house as captors tie donkeys This was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Abu Amr bin Al-Ala said: The prisoners are those who are not bound when they are taken, and the prisoners are those who are bound. Abu Hatim narrated that he heard this from the Arabs. Second: This verse was revealed on the day of Badr, as a rebuke from God the Almighty to the companions of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning is: You should not have done this act that required the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be taken captive before the slaughter. And they have this information in His saying, You want the worldly goods. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not order the men to be spared during the war, nor did he ever want the worldly goods, but rather the majority of those directly involved in the war did so. So the rebuke and rebuke were directed because of those who advised the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to take the ransom. This is the opinion of most of the commentators, and it is the only correct opinion. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was mentioned in the verse when he did not forbid it when he saw it from the hut and when Sa`d ibn Mu`adh, `Umar ibn al-Khattab, and `Abdullah ibn Rawahah disliked it, but he, peace be upon him, was preoccupied with the suddenness of the matter and the coming of victory, so he left the prohibition of sparing, and that is why he and Abu Bakr cried when the verses were revealed. And God knows best. Muslim narrated from the hadith of `Umar ibn al-Khattab, and the beginning of it was presented in Al-`Imran, and this is its completion. Abu Zamil said: Ibn Abbas said: “When the prisoners were taken prisoner, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr and Umar: What do you think about these prisoners? Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, they are cousins and relatives. I think that you should take a ransom from them, so that we may have strength against the infidels, and perhaps God will guide them to Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you think, O Ibn al-Khattab? I said: No, by God, O Messenger of God, I do not think what Abu Bakr thought, but I think that you should give us power and strike their necks. Give Ali power over Uqayl and strike his neck, and give me power over so-and-so a relative of Umar and strike his neck, for these are the leaders of infidelity and its leaders. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, liked what Abu Bakr said, but he did not like what I said. The next day I came and found the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr sitting and crying. I said: Even if I cannot find the means to cry, I will pretend to cry because of your crying. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I cry for what your companions offered me by taking the ransom. I have been offered their punishment.” Lower than this tree (a tree that was close to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace). And God Almighty revealed, It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a slaughter on the land, until His Almighty saying, So eat of what you have taken as lawful and good spoils, so God made the spoils lawful for them. And Yazid bin Harun narrated, saying: Yahya told us, saying: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “On the day of Badr, the prisoners were brought, including Al-Abbas. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you think about these prisoners? Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, they are your people and your family, spare them so that God may accept their repentance. Umar said: They lied to you and expelled you and fought you, bring them forward and strike their necks. Abdullah bin Rawahah said: Look for a valley with plenty of firewood and set it on them. Al-Abbas said while he was listening: You have severed your ties of kinship. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered and did not respond to them at all. Some people said: He will accept the opinion of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. Others said: He will accept the opinion of Umar. Others said: He will accept the opinion of Abdullah bin Rawahah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out and said: God softens the hearts of men in it until they are softer than milk and hardens the hearts of men in it until they are harder than stones. Your example, O Abu Bakr, is like that of Ibrahim. Some people said: He will accept the opinion of Umar. Others said: He will accept the opinion of Abdullah bin Rawahah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out and said: God softens the hearts of men in it until they are softer than milk. It is softer than milk and hardens the hearts of men in it until they are harder than stones. You, Abu Bakr, are like Abraham when he said, “So whoever follows me - indeed, he is of me; and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are Forgiving and Merciful.” (Ibrahim 14:36) And you, Abu Bakr, are like Jesus when he said, If You should punish them - indeed, they are Your servants; but if You forgive them - indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. (al-Ma’idah 5:118) And you, Umar, are like Moses when he said, Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment. (Yunus 10:88) You are a burden, so no one will escape except by ransom or by striking his neck. Then Abdullah said, Except for Suhayl ibn Bayda, for I heard him mention Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent. He said, I have never seen anyone more afraid of stones falling from the sky on me than I was on that day. Then God, the Almighty, revealed, It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has made slaughter in the land. to the end of the two verses. In a narration, the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) said: A punishment was about to befall us because of the opposition of Ibn al-Khattab, and if a punishment had been sent down, none would have escaped except 'Umar. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of 'Umar who said: When the day of Badr came and he - meaning the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) - took the ransom, God the Almighty revealed: It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a slaughter on the land until His saying: A great punishment has befallen you for what you have taken - of the ransom - ". Then He made the spoils permissible." Al-Qushayri mentioned that Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: O Messenger of God, this was our first battle with the polytheists, so the slaughter was dearer to me. The slaughter is the large number of killings, according to Mujahid and others. That is, he exaggerates in killing the polytheists. The Arabs say: So-and-so has inflicted a slaughter in this matter, meaning he has gone to extremes. Some of them said: until he is defeated and killed. Al-Mufaddal recited: She prays Duha prayer all her life in worship, and she has made Pharaoh suffer greatly in his disbelief. It was said: Until he inflicts heavy casualties. It was also said: Inflicting heavy casualties means strength and intensity. So God the Almighty informed that killing the prisoners who were ransomed at Badr was more appropriate than ransoming them. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: This was the day of Badr and the Muslims at that time were few, but when they became numerous and their power became strong, God the Almighty revealed after this about the prisoners: Then either a favor from us afterwards or ransom (Muhammad 47:4) as will be explained in Surat Al-Qital, God willing. It was said: They were only rebuked because the incident of Badr was of great importance and had a great impact on the leaders of Quraysh, their nobles, their leaders and their money by killing, enslaving and owning them. All of that had a great impact, so it was their right to wait for the revelation and not to rush, but when they rushed and did not wait, what happened to them happened. And God knows best. Third: Al-Tabari and others narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the people: “If you wish, you may take ransom for the prisoners and seventy of you will be killed in the war, according to their number. Or if you wish, they will be killed and you will be safe.” They said: We will take ransom and seventy of us will be martyred. Abd bin Hamid mentioned in his chain of transmission that Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the choice of the people in this way. This has already been discussed in Al Imran. Ubaidah Al Salmani said: They asked for both options, and seventy of them were killed on the day of Uhud. A problem arises here, which is: Fourth: It can be said: If there was a choice, then how did the rebuke occur with His saying, He touched you? The answer is that the rebuke occurred first because of their eagerness to take the ransom, then the choice occurred after that. What indicates this is that when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered the killing of Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt, Al-Miqdad said: My prisoner, O Messenger of God. And Mus’ab ibn Umair said to the one who took his brother prisoner: Tighten your hand on him, for he has a wealthy mother. And other stories of their eagerness to take the ransom. So when the prisoners were gathered and taken to Madinah and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) executed Al-Nadr, Uqbah, and others and began to consider the rest of them, the choice was revealed from God, the Almighty. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) consulted his companions at that time, so Umar chose the first banner in the killing, and Abu Bakr saw the interest in strengthening the Muslims with the ransom money. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) leaned towards Abu Bakr’s opinion. Both opinions are an effort after a choice. So nothing of hardship was revealed after this. And God knows best. Fifth: Ibn Wahb said: Malik said that there were polytheist prisoners at Badr, so God revealed: It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a slaughter on the land. They were polytheists at that time, and they ransomed themselves and returned. Had they been Muslims, they would have stayed and not returned. The number of those killed among them was forty-four men, and the same number were taken captive. The martyrs were few. Amr ibn al-Ala’ said: The dead were seventy, and the captives were the same. Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Musayyab and others said the same. This is correct as in Sahih Muslim. They killed seventy on that day and took seventy captive. Al-Bayhaqi mentioned: They said: The captives were brought, and over them was Shuqran, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and they were forty-nine men who were counted, and they were seventy in the original, this is agreed upon without doubt. Ibn al-Arabi said: Malik only said that they were polytheists because the commentators narrated that al-Abbas said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: I am a Muslim. In another narration, the captives said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: We believe in you. All of this was weakened by Malik, and he argued for its invalidity with what he mentioned about their return and in addition to that they attacked him at Uhud. Omar bin Abdul Barr said: They differed about the time of Al-Abbas’ conversion to Islam, and it was said that he converted to Islam before the day of Badr, and for that reason the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever meets Al-Abbas should not kill him, for he was only expelled against his will. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Badr: “Some people from Banu Hashim and others have been forced out. They have no need to fight us. Whoever among you meets someone from Banu Hashim, do not kill him. Whoever meets Abu al-Bukhtari, do not kill him. Whoever meets al-Abbas, do not kill him, for he was only forced out.” He mentioned the hadith. He mentioned that he converted to Islam when he was taken prisoner on the day of Badr. He mentioned that he converted to Islam in the year of Khaybar, “and he used to write to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the report of the polytheists. He wanted to emigrate, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to him: Stay in Mecca, for your stay there is more beneficial for you.”
8:68: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Had it not been for a previous decree from God, that He will not punish a people until He makes clear to them what they should avoid. People differed regarding the previous decree from God, and the most correct of them is what preceded regarding the permissibility of spoils, as they were forbidden to those before us. When the day of Badr came, people rushed to the spoils, so God, the Almighty, revealed: Had it not been for a previous decree from God, meaning regarding the permissibility of spoils. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated in his Musnad: Salam told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “When the day of Badr came, people rushed to the spoils and took them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The spoils are not permissible for any black-headed person except you.” So when the Prophet and his companions captured the spoils, they would collect them and a fire would descend from the sky and consume them. Then God the Almighty revealed: Had it not been for a previous decree from God, to the end of the two verses. At-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: A good and authentic hadith. Mujahid and Al-Hasan also said the same. And from them and Saeed bin Jubair also: The previous decree is God’s forgiveness for the people of Badr, for their past and future sins. A group said: The previous decree is God’s pardon for them in this sin, specifically. The general is more correct, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar about the people of Badr: “And how do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.” Narrated by Muslim. It was said: The previous book is that He would not punish them while Muhammad, peace be upon him, was among them. It was said: The previous book is that He would not punish anyone for a sin he committed out of ignorance until he came forward to Him. A group said: The previous book is what God decreed regarding the erasure of minor sins by avoiding major ones. Al-Tabari believed that all of these meanings are included in the wording and that it includes them, and he refrained from specifying one meaning over another. Second: Ibn al-Arabi: The verse is evidence that if a servant commits what he believes to be forbidden, while in the knowledge of God it is permissible for him, there is no punishment for him, like a fasting person who says: This is my period day, so break his fast now. Or a woman says: This is my period day, so break his fast, and they both do that, and the period and menstruation are what cause breaking the fast. In the well-known view of the school, there is expiation for it, and al-Shafi’i said the same. Abu Hanifa said: There is no expiation for him, and this is the other narration. The basis of the first narration is that the occurrence of permissibility does not constitute an excuse for the punishment of prohibition in the event of a violation, as if he had intercourse with a woman and then married her. The basis of the second narration is that the sanctity of the day is void before God, the Almighty, and his violation occurred in a place that has no sanctity in the knowledge of God, so it is like if he intended to have intercourse with a woman who had been brought to him while he believed that she was not his wife. This is more correct. The first explanation is not necessary, because the knowledge of God Almighty and our knowledge are equal in the issue of prohibition, and in our issue our knowledge and God’s knowledge differ, so the reliance is on God’s knowledge. As He said: Had it not been for a previous decree from God, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you took.
8:69: Its appearance requires that all the spoils belong to the conquerors, and that they share in it equally, except that the Almighty’s saying: And know that whatever you obtain of anything - a fifth of it belongs to God makes clear the obligation to take out a fifth of it and spend it on the aforementioned purposes. We have already discussed this in full.
8:70: It has three issues: First: The Almighty said: O Prophet, say to those who are in your hands of the captives. It was said: The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. And it was said: To him alone. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The captives in this verse are Abbas and his companions. They said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We believe in what you have brought, and we bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. We will advise you regarding your people. So this verse was revealed. The invalidity of this statement by Malik has been mentioned previously. In Musannaf Abi Dawud, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made the ransom of the people of the pre-Islamic era on the day of Badr four hundred. And on the authority of Ibn Ishaq: "The Quraysh sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ransom their prisoners, so each tribe ransomed its prisoner for whatever they were pleased with. Al-Abbas said: O Messenger of God, I was a Muslim. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God knows best about your Islam, so if it is as you say, then God will reward you for that. As for the outward appearance of your affair, it is upon us. Ransom yourself, your two nephews Nawfal ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Aqil ibn Abi Talib, and your ally Utbah ibn Amr, the brother of Banu al-Harith ibn Fihr. He said: I do not have that, O Messenger of God. He said: Where is the money that you and Umm al-Fadl buried, and you said to her: If I find it on this journey, then this money is for Banu al-Fadl, Abd God and Qatham? He said: O Messenger of God, I do not know that you are the Messenger of God. This is something that no one but me and Umm al-Fadl know. So calculate for me, O Messenger of God, what you have taken from me is twenty ounces of money that I had with me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No. That is something that God has given us from you." So he ransomed himself, his two nephews and his ally, and God revealed about him: "O Messenger of God, O Prophet, say to those prisoners in your hands... the verse. Ibn Ishaq said: The prisoner who ransomed the most was Al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib, because he was a wealthy man, so he ransomed himself with one hundred ounces of gold. In Al-Bukhari: Musa ibn Uqbah said: Ibn Shihab said: Anas ibn Malik told me. “Some men from the Ansar asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, give us permission to leave the ransom for our nephew Abbas. He said: No, by God, you will not leave a single dirham.” Al-Naqqash and others mentioned: “The ransom of each of the captives was forty ounces, except for Al-Abbas, for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Double the ransom for Al-Abbas, and he ordered him to ransom his two brothers’ sons, Aqil ibn Abi Talib and Nawfal ibn Al-Harith, so he paid eight ounces for them, and eighty ounces for himself, and twenty ounces were taken from him during the war. This was because he was one of the ten who guaranteed feeding the people of Badr, and the turn came to him on the day of Badr, and they fought before he could feed them, and the twenty remained with him, so they were taken from him during the war, so he took from him that day one hundred and eighty ounces. Al-Abbas said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You left me as long as I lived asking the Quraysh for my hand. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Where is the gold that you left with your wife, Umm Al-Fadl? Al-Abbas said: What gold? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You said to her: I do not know what will happen to me on this face of mine, so if something happens to me, it is for you and your son. He said: O son of my brother, who told you this? He said: God told me. Al-Abbas said: I bear witness that you are truthful. I never knew that you were the Messenger of God until today, and I knew that none revealed this to you except the Knower of secrets. I bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are His servant and Messenger, and I disbelieve in everything other than Him. And he ordered his two nephews to become Muslims, and it was about them that the verse was revealed: “O Prophet, tell those who are in your hands of the captives.” The one who took Al-Abbas prisoner was Abu Al-Yusr Ka’b bin Amr, the brother of Banu Salamah, and he was a short man, while Al-Abbas was a tall, large man. When he brought him to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said to him: An angel has helped you against him. Second: The Almighty’s saying: If God knows in your hearts goodness, meaning Islam. He will give you better than what was taken from you, meaning the ransom. It was said in this world. And it was said in the hereafter. In Sahih Muslim: “When money from Bahrain was brought to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Al-Abbas said to him: I have ransomed myself and I have ransomed Aqeel. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Take it. So he spread out his garment and took what he could carry.” Abridged. In a hadith other than Sahih: Al-Abbas said to him: This is better than what was taken from me, and I still hope that God will forgive me. Al-Abbas said: And he gave me Zamzam, and I would not like to have all the money of the people of Mecca in return. At-Tabari attributed to Al-Abbas that he said: “It was revealed when I informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of my conversion to Islam, and I asked him to settle the score with me for the twenty ounces that were taken from me before the ransom, but he refused and said: That is spoils of war. So God replaced it with twenty slaves, all of whom traded with my money.” In the Musannaf of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: “When the people of Mecca sent to ransom their captives, Zainab sent money to ransom Abu al-‘As, and she sent a jurist with a necklace of hers that Khadija had, and she brought it to Abu al-‘As. She said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw her, he felt very sorry for her and said: If you see fit to release her captive and return to her what is hers? They said: Yes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had taken from him or promised him that he would release Zainab to him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Zaid bin Haritha and a man from the Ansar and said: Stay in Batn Ya’jij until Zainab passes by you, and keep her company until you bring her back.” Ibn Ishaq said: This was a month after Badr. Abdullah bin Abi Bakr said: I was told on the authority of Zainab, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she said: When Abu al-‘As came to Mecca, he said to me: Get ready, and join your father. She said: So I went out to get ready, and Hind bint Utbah met me and said: O daughter of Muhammad, did I not hear that you want to join your father? I said to her: I did not want that. She said: O cousin, do not do that. I am a wealthy woman and I have goods for your needs. If you want a good, I will sell it to you, or a loan from my expenses, I will lend you, because what is between men does not apply between women. She said: By God, I do not think she said that except to do it, so I feared her and concealed it and said: I do not want that. When Zainab finished preparing her, she departed and her father-in-law went out with her, led by Kinanah ibn al-Rabi’ during the day. The people of Mecca heard about that, and Hubbar ibn al-Aswad and Nafi’ ibn Abd al-Qais al-Fihri went out in search of her. Hubbar was the first to reach her with a spear while she was in her litter. Kinanah knelt down and scattered his arrows, then took his bow and said: By God, no man will come near me except that I will place an arrow in him. Abu Sufyan came with the nobles of Quraysh and said: O man, hold back your arrows until we speak to you. Abu Sufyan stopped him and said: You have done nothing. You have gone out with the woman in front of the people, and you know about our disaster that befell us at Badr, so the Arabs think and say that this is weakness on our part and your going out to him with his daughter in front of the people from among us is weak. Go back with the woman and stay with her for a few days, then ask her gently at night and send her back to her father, for by my life we have no need to keep her away from her father, and we have no resentment for what has befallen us now. So he did. When two or three days had passed, he asked her, and she set out until she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They mentioned that she had miscarried - because of the fright she had suffered when Hubbar ibn Umm Dirham had frightened her - what was in her stomach.
8:71: Thirdly - Ibn al-Arabi said: When some of the polytheists were taken captive, some of them spoke about Islam but did not act resolutely in it nor did they acknowledge it with a firm acknowledgment. It seems that they wanted to get closer to the Muslims and not distance themselves from the polytheists. Our scholars said: If a disbeliever speaks about faith in his heart and with his tongue but does not act resolutely in it, then he is not a believer. And if he finds such a thing in a believer, then he is a disbeliever, except for what is from the whisperings that he is not able to repel, then God has pardoned and dropped it. God explained the truth to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, when He said: And if they intend to betray you, meaning if these people are from them in treachery and deceit, they have already betrayed God before by their disbelief, deceit, and fighting you. And if this statement from them is good and God knows it, then He will accept it from them and compensate them with something better than what they have done and forgive them for what came before of their disbelief, treachery, and deceit. The plural of treason is khayyan, and it should have been said khawāyin because it is one of the words with the letter waw, but they differentiated between it and the plural of khaynah. It is also said khayyān, khwān, khwāyān, and khānah.
8:72: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who believed He concluded the Surah by mentioning allegiance so that each group would know its guardian whom it seeks help from. The meaning of migration and jihad has already been mentioned in terms of language and meaning. And those who gave shelter and aided is conjoined to it. They are the Ansar who settled in the home and the faith before them, and the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and the Muhajireen joined them. Those is the subject in the nominative case. Some of them is a second subject. Allies of some is its predicate, and all are the predicates of that. Ibn Abbas said: Allies of some in inheritance, so they would inherit through migration, and those who believed and did not migrate did not inherit from those who migrated, so God abrogated that by saying: And those of kinship al-Arham. Narrated by Abu Dawud. And the inheritance became for those of kinship among the believers. And the people of two religions do not inherit anything. Then came his saying, peace be upon him: Attach the obligatory shares to their people as was previously explained in the verse on inheritance. It was said: There is no abrogation here, but rather its meaning is in support and assistance, as was previously mentioned in An-Nisa. And those who believe is the subject and the predicate you have no part in their guardianship Yahya bin Waththab, Al-A’mash and Hamzah read from their guardianship with a kasra on the waw. It was said: It is a dialect. It was said: It is from walayat something, it is said: wali bain al-wilayah. And wali bain al-wilayah. The fat-ha in this is clearer and better, because it means support and lineage. Guardianship and guardianship may also be used to mean emirate. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And if they seek your help in religion means that if these believers who did not migrate from the land of war call upon you for help with a mobilization or money to rescue them, then help them, for that is obligatory upon you, so do not let them down. Except if they seek your help against a people of unbelievers between you and them is a covenant, then do not support them against them, and do not break the covenant until its term is completed. Ibn al-Arabi: Except if they are weak captives, then the guardianship is with them and the support for them is obligatory, until not a single eye remains from us that blinks until it goes out to rescue them if our numbers can bear that, or we spend all our money to extract them until no one has a dirham left. This is what Malik and all the scholars said, We belong to God and to Him we shall return, regarding what happened to the creation when they left their brothers in the captivity of the enemy while they had in their hands treasures of money, and surplus conditions, ability, number, strength, and endurance. Al-Zajjaj: It is permissible to say upon you is victory in the accusative case as an inducement.
8:73: Third - The Almighty said: And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. God cut off the alliance between the disbelievers and the believers, so He made the believers allies of one another, and the disbelievers allies of one another, supporting each other with their religion and dealing with each other with their beliefs. Our scholars said that a disbeliever who has a Muslim brother should not marry her, as there is no alliance between them, and the people of her religion should marry her. Just as a Muslim woman cannot be married except by a Muslim, so too a disbeliever cannot be married except by a disbeliever who is a relative of hers, or a bishop, even if she is a Muslim, unless she is a freedwoman. If a marriage contract is made with someone other than a freedwoman, it is annulled if it is for a Muslim, but it is not valid for a Christian. Asbagh said: It is not annulled, a Muslim marriage is more appropriate and preferable. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: If you do not do it, the pronoun refers to inheritance and its commitment. The meaning is: If you do not leave them to inherit as they used to inherit, said Ibn Zayd. It was said: It refers to mutual support, assistance, assistance, and joining hands. Ibn Jurayj and others: If this is not done, then strife will occur from him soon, so it is more certain than the first. Al-Tirmidhi mentioned on the authority of Abdullah bin Muslim bin Hormuz on the authority of Muhammad and Saad bin Ubayd on the authority of Abu Hatim Al-Muzani who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "If there comes to you one with whose religion and character you are pleased, then marry your wife to him. If you do not do so, there will be tribulation on the earth and great corruption." They said: O Messenger of God, even if that is in him? He said: If there comes to you one with whose religion and character you are pleased, then marry your wife to him." Three times. He said: A strange hadith. It was said: It refers to keeping the covenant and pact included in His statement: "Except for a people between you and whom there is a treaty." This, even if he does not do so, is tribulation itself. It was said: It refers to victory for the Muslims in religion. This is the meaning of the second statement. Ibn Ishaq said: God made the Muhajireen and Ansar the people of His authority in religion, to the exclusion of others, and He made the disbelievers allies of one another. Then He said: "Unless you do so," which means that the believer will be an ally of the disbeliever, to the exclusion of the believers. "There will be a trial," meaning a trial through war, and what comes with it of raids, exile, and captivity. And great corruption: the emergence of polytheism. Al-Kisa'i said: The accusative case is permissible in His statement: "There will be a trial," meaning there will be your actions and great corruption. "Truly" is a source, meaning they fulfilled their faith by migration and victory.
8:74: And God fulfilled their faith in the good report of His saying: For them is forgiveness and noble provision, meaning a great reward in Paradise.
8:75: Fifth - The Almighty's saying: And those who believed after that and emigrated meaning after the Haybiyah and the Pledge of Ridwan. This is because the emigration after that was of a lower rank than the first emigration. The second emigration is the one in which the peace treaty was made, and the war laid down its burdens for about two years, then came the conquest of Mecca. For this reason, he, peace be upon him, said: There is no migration after the conquest. So he explained that whoever believed and migrated after that would join them. The meaning of from you is like you in victory and loyalty. Sixth: The Almighty said: And those of kinship as a beginning. The singular is dhu, and womb is feminine, and the plural is wombs. What is meant by it here are the agnates, not the one born through the womb. What makes it clear that what is meant by haram are the agnates is the saying of the Arabs: And your womb has connected you. They do not mean the maternal kinship. Qatilah bint al-Harith said - the sister of al-Nadr ibn al-Harith - thus said Ibn Hisham. Al-Suhayli said: The correct view is that she is the daughter of al-Nadr, not his sister. This is what was stated in the Book of Evidences - in which she mourns her father when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed him with patience - in al-Safra’: O rider, the noble one is expected to rise at five in the morning, and you will be successful. Inform the dead of the greeting that the noble horses continue to flutter with From me to you, a tear is shed, and another is choking Does Al-Nadr hear me if I call him, or how can a dead person who does not speak hear? O Muhammad, the best of the noble ones among his people, and the stallion is a well-bred stallion What would it have hurt you if you had been ungrateful, perhaps from the young man who is the one who is annoying and enraging? If I were able to pay a ransom, I would pay it with the most precious thing that can be paid. Al-Nadr is the closest of relatives to the family and the most deserving of manumission. The swords of his father's sons continued to attack him, but God has wombs there that have been torn. Patience leads to death, tired and chained, while suffering and bound Seventh: The predecessors and those who came after them differed regarding the inheritance of the uterine relatives - who have no share in the Book - from the relatives of the deceased and are not agnates, such as the children of daughters, the children of sisters, the daughters of the brother, the paternal aunt and maternal aunt, the paternal uncle who is the brother of the mother’s father, the maternal grandfather, the maternal grandmother, and those related by them. Some people said: The uterine relatives who do not have a share do not inherit. It was narrated from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, Zaid bin Thabit, and Ibn Umar, and a narration from Ali, and it is the opinion of the people of Medina. It was narrated from Makhul and al-Awza’i, and al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him said the same. The following said that they inherit: Umar bin al-Khattab, Ibn Mas’ud, Mu’adh, Abu al-Darda’, Aisha, and Ali in a narration from him, and it is the opinion of the people of Kufa, Ahmad, and Ishaq. They cited the verse as evidence and said: Two reasons have come together in the uterine relatives: kinship and Islam, so they are more deserving than those who have one reason, which is Islam. The first responded and said: This is a general and comprehensive verse, and it appears that every kinship is close or distant, and the verses of inheritance are explanatory and the explanatory judges and explains the general. They said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made loyalty a fixed cause, and he established the master in it in the place of the agnatic kin, so he said: Loyalty to the one who freed. He forbade the sale of loyalty and its gift. Others cited as evidence what Abu Dawud and Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Al-Miqdam, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever leaves behind all of this, it is to me - or perhaps he said, to God and His Messenger - and whoever leaves behind wealth, it is to his heirs. I am the heir of one who has no heir, I am responsible for his maintenance and I inherit from him, and the maternal uncle is the heir of one who has no heir, I am responsible for his maintenance and I inherit from him.” Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Tawus that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: God is the protector of he who has no protector, and the maternal uncle is the heir of he who has no heir. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The maternal uncle is an heir. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked about the inheritance of the paternal aunt and maternal aunt. He said, I do not know until Gabriel comes to me. Then he said, Where is the one who asked about the inheritance of the paternal aunt and maternal aunt? He said, The man came and said, ‘Gabriel whispered to me that they have nothing.’ Ad-Daraqutni said, “No one narrated it on the authority of anyone except Mus’adah on the authority of Muhammad ibn ‘Amr, and he is weak. The correct version is mursal.” It was narrated on the authority of Ash-Sha’bi that Ziyad ibn Abi Sufyan said to his companion, Do you know how ‘Umar ruled regarding the paternal aunt and maternal aunt? He said, No. He said, “I know best how ‘Umar ruled regarding them. He made the maternal aunt like the mother and the paternal aunt like the father.”
9:1: It has five issues: First - in its names. Saeed bin Jubair said: I asked Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, about Surat Bara’ah, and he said: That is the scandalizer. The verses and from them and from them kept being revealed until we feared that it would not leave anyone. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahman said: This surah was revealed during the Battle of Tabuk, and it was revealed after that. At the beginning of it, the covenants of the infidels were renounced to them. In this surah, the secrets of the hypocrites were revealed. It is called Al-Fadihah and Al-Buhuth because it searches for the secrets of the hypocrites. It is called Al-Mubthara and Al-Batharah: the search. Second: The scholars differed about the reason for the omission of the Basmalah from the beginning of this Surah, with five opinions: The first - It was said: It was the custom of the Arabs in their time in the pre-Islamic era, if there was a covenant between them and a people, then if they wanted to break it, they would write a letter to them and not write the Basmalah in it. So when Surah Bara’ah was revealed about the breaking of the covenant that was between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent it to Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, so he recited it to them during the season, and he did not say the Basmalah in that, as was their custom in breaking the covenant by omitting the Basmalah. A second statement: “An-Nasa’i narrated that Ahmad narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated that Yahya ibn Sa’id narrated that Awf narrated that Yazid al-Farsi narrated that Ibn Abbas said: I said to Uthman, ‘What made you choose al-Anfal, which is from the Mathani, and Bara’ah, which is from the Mi’in, and you combined them together, and you did not write the line ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful’, and you placed them in the seven long ones? What made you do that? Uthman said: When something was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would call one of those who wrote for him and say: ‘Put this in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’ And the verses would be revealed to him and he would say: ‘Put these verses in the surah in which such and such is mentioned.’ Al-Anfal was among the first of what was revealed, and Bara’ah was among the last of the Qur’an, and its story was similar to its story. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away without explaining to us that it was from it, so I thought that it was from it, and that is why I combined them together and did not write the line ‘In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful’ between them.” Abu ‘Isa al-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: This is a good hadith. A third statement - also narrated from Uthman. Malik said, as narrated by Ibn Wahb, Ibn al-Qasim, and Ibn Abd al-Hakam: When the beginning of it was dropped, Bismillah al-Rahman al-Raheem was dropped with it. It was narrated from Ibn Ajlan that he heard that Surah Bara’ah was equal to Surah al-Baqarah or close to it, so it was dropped from it, and that is why Bismillah al-Rahman al-Raheem was not written between them. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: It was like Surah al-Baqarah. A fourth statement - said by Kharijah, Abu ‘Usmah, and others - said: When they wrote the Qur’an during the caliphate of Uthman, the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) differed. Some of them said: Bara’ah and al-Anfal are one Surah. Some of them said: They are two Surahs. So I left a space between them for the opinion of those who said that they are two Surahs, and I left Bismillah al-Rahman al-Raheem for the opinion of those who said that they are one Surah, so both groups were satisfied, and their evidence was established in the Qur’an. A fifth statement - Abdullah ibn Abbas said: I asked Ali ibn Abi Talib why Bismillah al-Rahman al-Raheem was not written in Bara’ah? He said: Because Bismillah Al-Rahman Al-Raheem is a protection, and Bara’ah was revealed with the sword, and there is no protection in it. And its meaning was narrated from Al-Mubarrad, who said: That is why they were not combined, because Bismillah Al-Rahman Al-Raheem is mercy, and Bara’ah was revealed with wrath. And something similar was narrated from Sufyan. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: The reason why Bismillah Al-Rahman Al-Raheem was not written at the beginning of this surah is because the name is mercy, and mercy is protection, and this surah was revealed about the hypocrites and with the sword, and there is no protection for the hypocrites. The correct view is that the name was not written, because Gabriel, peace be upon him, did not reveal it in this surah, Al-Qushayri said. And in the statement of Uthman: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed away without explaining to us that it was part of it, is evidence that all the surahs were organized by his statement and explanation, and that Bara’ah alone was added to Al-Anfal without a covenant from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of the death that hastened him before he explained that. And they were called Al-Qarinatain, so it was necessary to combine them and add one to the other, because of the description that required them from being paired while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was alive. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: This is evidence that analogy is a fundamental principle in religion. Do you not see how Uthman and the prominent companions resorted to analogy of similarity in the absence of a text, and saw that the story of Bara’ah was similar to the story of al-Anfal, so they included it in it? If God Almighty has made clear the entry of analogy into the composition of the Qur’an, then what do you think of the rest of the rulings? Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Bara’ah means: I am innocent of something, I am innocent of it, so I am innocent of it, if you remove it from yourself and cut off the reason between you and it. Bara’ah is in the nominative case as a predicate of an implied subject, meaning this is bara’ah. It is correct to raise it as a subject. The predicate in His saying: to those. It is permissible to begin with an indefinite noun because it is described, so it is defined with some definition, and it is permissible to report about it. Isa bin Omar read Bara’ah in the accusative case, on the assumption that they committed themselves to bara’ah, so it has the meaning of enticement. It is a source on fa’ala, like hatred and baseness. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: To those of the polytheists with whom you have made a treaty. Meaning, to those with whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a treaty, because he was the one in charge of the contracts, and all of his companions were satisfied with that, so it was as if they had made a contract and made a treaty, so the contract was attributed to them. Likewise, what the leaders of disbelief made with their people is attributed to them and counted against them, and they will be held accountable for it, since it is not possible to do otherwise, since obtaining the satisfaction of everyone is impossible. So if the leader makes a contract for what he sees as being in the interest of something, it is binding on all of the subjects.
9:2: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: So travel freely returns from the report to the address, meaning tell them to travel freely, meaning travel freely in the land, coming and going, safe and not fearing any of the Muslims with war, looting, killing, or captivity. It is said, so-and-so traveled freely in the land, traveling freely, and from this comes the word traveling in flowing, flat water, and from this comes the saying of Tarafa bin al-Abd: If I was afraid of this from you, you wouldn't have gotten to me until you saw horses galloping in front of me. Second: The scholars differed about the manner of this postponement, and about those whom God and His Messenger disavowed. Muhammad bin Ishaq and others said: They are two types of polytheists, one of whom had a covenant of less than four months to search for himself. Then he is at war with God, His Messenger, and the believers, killed wherever he is found and taken prisoner unless he repents. The beginning of this period is the day of the greater pilgrimage, and its end is until the tenth of the month of Rabi` al-Akhir. As for those who did not have a covenant, their term is the expiration of the four sacred months. That is fifty days: twenty of Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram. Al-Kalbi said: The four months were only for those who had a covenant between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, less than four months, and whoever had a covenant of more than four months, then he is the one whom God commanded to complete his covenant with by His saying: So fulfill their covenant with them until their term. This is the choice of al-Tabari and others. Muhammad bin Ishaq, Mujahid, and others mentioned that this verse was revealed about the people of Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with the Quraysh in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, on the condition that they would stop fighting for ten years, during which people would be safe and refrain from harming one another. Then Khuza’ah entered into the covenant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Banu Bakr entered into the covenant of the Quraysh, and Banu Bakr attacked Khuza’ah and broke their covenant. The reason for this was the blood of Banu Bakr that had been shed by Khuza’ah before Islam for a period of time. When the truce concluded on the day of Hudaybiyyah came, the people felt safe with each other. Banu al-Dayl of Banu Bakr - who were the ones who had the blood - took advantage of that opportunity and the negligence of Khuza’ah, and wanted to avenge Banu al-Aswad ibn Razan, whom Khuza’ah had killed. So Nawfal ibn Mu’awiyah al-Dayli went out with those who obeyed him from Banu Bakr ibn Abd Manat, until they attacked Khuza’ah at night and fought. Quraysh helped Banu Bakr with weapons, and some of Quraysh helped them with their own people, so Khuza’ah fled to the sanctuary, as is well-known and written. This was a breach of the peace treaty concluded on the day of Hudaybiyyah. So Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza’i, Badil ibn Warqa’ al-Khuza’i, and some of Khuza’ah went out and came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, seeking his help for what Banu Bakr and Quraysh had afflicted them with. Amr ibn Salim recited to him, saying: Oh God, I implore Muhammad by the oath of our father and his father, the Atlda You were a father to us and you were a son, then we surrendered and did not withdraw our hand So support him, may God guide you, with a strong support, and call upon the servants of God to come as reinforcements. Among them is the Messenger of God, stripped naked, white like the sun, growing upward. If he is humiliated, his face will be covered with dust, like the foaming sea running. The Quraysh broke their promise to you and violated your firm covenant. They claimed that you do not call anyone, and they are more humiliated and fewer in number. They made us spend the night in the open air and killed us while we were kneeling and prostrating. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: I will not be victorious unless I support Banu Ka'b. Then he looked at a cloud and said: It is crying out for the victory of Banu Ka'b, meaning Khuza'ah. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said to Badil ibn Warqa' and those with him: "Abu Sufyan will come to strengthen the bond and extend the peace treaty, and he will leave without need." The Quraysh regretted what they had done, so Abu Sufyan went to Medina to continue the bond and extend the peace treaty, but he returned without need, as the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) had informed them, based on what is known about his story. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) prepared for Mecca, and God conquered it, and that was in the eighth year of the Hijra. When Hawazin heard of the conquest of Mecca, Malik ibn Auf al-Nasri gathered them, based on what is well-known and famous from the campaign of Hunayn. Some of it will come. The Muslims were victorious and triumphant over the disbelievers. The Battle of Hawazin took place on the day of Hunayn in the first of Shawwal in the eighth year of the Hijra. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left the division of the spoils of wealth and women, and did not divide them until he reached Taif. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) besieged them for twenty-some nights, and it was said otherwise. He set up a catapult against them and threw it at them, as is well-known from those raids. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned to Al-Juhfah and divided the spoils of Hunayn, as is well-known from its matter and story. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned and they dispersed, and Atab bin Asid performed Hajj for the people in that year. He was the first leader to perform Hajj in Islam. The polytheists performed Hajj at their sacred sites. Atab bin Asid was a good, virtuous and pious man. Ka`b bin Zuhair bin Abi Salma came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and praised him, and recited over his head his poem, which began: Happiness has appeared, and my heart is filled with joy today And he recited it to the end, and mentioned the immigrants in it and praised them - and before that he had memorized a satire of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - and he criticized the Ansar for not mentioning them, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a poem in which he praised the Ansar and said: Whoever is pleased with the generosity of life will remain among the righteous Ansar. They inherited the virtues from their ancestors. The best are the sons of the best. The forced ones are Samhari, with arms like the lower Indian ones, not short. And those who look with red eyes like embers, their eyes not dull And the sellers of their souls to their prophet for death on the day of embracing and repeating They purify themselves by seeing it as a ritual for them with the blood of the infidels they have killed. Train as I trained with a hidden belly, the necks of the fierce lions were defeated If you decide to prevent them from you, you will be at the strongholds of the Forgiver. They struck Ali on the day of Badr with a blow that would have overwhelmed all of Nizar. If people knew all my knowledge about them, those who argue would believe me. People who, when the stars fade, are the destinations of the incoming and outgoing visitors. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed in Medina after his return from Taif in Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, Safar, Rabi’ al-Awwal, Rabi’ al-Akhir, Jumada al-Awwal, and Jumada al-Akhira. In Rajab of the year nine, he set out with the Muslims to wage a campaign against the Romans, the campaign of Tabuk. It was the last campaign he waged. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned from Tabuk, he wanted to perform Hajj, but he said: There are naked polytheists coming to the House, circumambulating the House, and I do not want to perform Hajj until that does not happen. So he sent Abu Bakr as a leader for Hajj, and he sent with him forty verses from the beginning of Surah Bara’ah to recite to the people of the season. When he left, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called Ali and said: Bring out this story from the beginning of Surah Bara’ah, and announce that to the people when they gather. Ali went out on the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) she-camel, Al-Adhba’, until he reached Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with them both at Dhu’l-Hulayfah. When Abu Bakr saw him, he said to him: Are you a leader or someone commanded? He said: No, I am commanded. Then they got up, and Abu Bakr led the people in Hajj according to their stations in the pre-Islamic period. In the book of Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Jabir: “And Ali recited Surah Bara’ah to the people until he finished it one day before the Day of Tarwiyah, and on the Day of Arafah and on the Day of Sacrifice after Abu Bakr’s sermon had ended, on the three days.” When the first day of the march came, Abu Bakr stood up and addressed the people, telling them how to march and how to throw stones, teaching them their rituals. When he finished, Ali stood up and recited to the people the Declaration of Innocence until he finished it. Sulayman ibn Musa said: When Abu Bakr gave the sermon at Arafat, he said: Stand up, Ali, and deliver the message of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So Ali stood up and did so. He said: Then it occurred to me that not all the people had witnessed Abu Bakr’s sermon, so I began to look for the tents on the Day of Sacrifice. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Yathi’ who said: I asked Ali, What did I send for during the Hajj? He said: “I was sent with four things: that no one should circumambulate the House naked, and whoever had a treaty with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, his term is until its expiration, and whoever did not have a treaty, his term is four months, and none shall enter Paradise except a believing soul, and the Muslims and polytheists shall not meet after this year of theirs.” He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. An-Nasa’i also narrated it and said: I kept calling until my voice became hoarse. Abu Omar said: Ali was sent to renew his covenant with everyone who had a treaty, and to covenant with them that no polytheist should perform Hajj after that year, and that no one should circumambulate the House naked. And the Hajj was performed in that year in the ninth year of Abu Bakr. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed Hajj the following year, the Hajj that he had not performed before from Medina, and his Hajj took place in Dhul-Hijjah. So he said: Time has come full circle is the hadith, as will be explained in the verse of forgetfulness. And the Hajj was established in Dhul-Hijjah until the Day of Judgment. Mujahid mentioned that Abu Bakr performed Hajj in Dhul-Qi’dah of the year nine. Ibn al-Arabi: The wisdom in giving the certificate of innocence to Ali was that the certificate of innocence included the breaking of the covenant that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made. And it was the custom of the Arabs that no contract was broken except by the one who made it, or a man from his household. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to cut off the tongues of the Arabs with the argument, and he sent his Hashemite cousin from his household to break the covenant, until no one remained for them to speak. Al-Zajjaj said its meaning. Third: The scholars said: The verse includes the permissibility of severing the covenant between us and the polytheists.
