There are two cases for this: The case in which the period between us and them expires, so we declare war on them. Declaring war is optional. The second: That we fear treachery from them, so we renounce our covenant with them as mentioned above. Ibn Abbas: The verse is abrogated, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a covenant, then renounced the covenant when he was ordered to fight.
9:3: It has three issues: First: The Almighty said: And the call to prayer. The call to prayer means notification in language without dispute. It is a plural of taf on bara’ah. “To the people” here means all of creation. The greater day of Hajj is a circumstance, and the agent in it is the call to prayer. Even if it was described by saying: from God, the scent of the verb remains in it, and it is an agent in circumstances. It was said: The agent in it is shameful. The action of the call to prayer is not valid, because it was described and thus it was removed from the ruling of the verb. Second: The scholars differed regarding the greater Hajj. Some said: The Day of Arafah. It was narrated on the authority of Umar, Uthman, Ibn Abbas, Tawus, and Mujahid. This is the view of Abu Hanifa, and it was also said by Al-Shafi’i. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abi Awfa, and Al-Mughira bin Shu’bah: It is the Day of Sacrifice. This was chosen by Al-Tabari. Ibn Umar narrated: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood on the Day of Sacrifice during the Hajj in which he performed Hajj and said: ‘Which day is this?’ They said: ‘The Day of Sacrifice.’ He said: ‘This is the day of the greater Hajj.’” Narrated by Abu Dawud. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him sent me to announce on the Day of Sacrifice in Mina: No polytheist shall perform Hajj after this year, and no naked person shall circumambulate the House. The greater day of Hajj is the Day of Sacrifice. It was called the greater because people said: the lesser Hajj. Abu Bakr announced it to the people that year, and no polytheist performed Hajj in the year of the Farewell Pilgrimage in which the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) performed Hajj. Ibn Abi Awfa said: The Day of Sacrifice is the greater day of Hajj, in which blood is shed, hair is placed, turban is thrown away, and the Sacred Sanctuary is made permissible on it. This is the Maliki school of thought, because the entire Hajj is on the Day of Sacrifice, because the standing is on the night of the day, and the stoning, the sacrifice, shaving, and circumambulation are on the morning. The first scholars cited as evidence the hadith of Mukhramah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The greatest day of Hajj is the Day of Arafah. Narrated by Ismail Al-Qadi. Al-Thawri and Ibn Jurayj said: The greatest Hajj is all the days of Mina. This is like saying: the Day of Siffin, the Day of the Camel, and the Day of Bu'ath, meaning the time and place, not the day itself. It was narrated from Mujahid: The greatest Hajj is the Qiran, and the lesser Hajj is the Ifrad. This has nothing to do with the verse. It was narrated from him and Ata': The greatest Hajj is the one in which there is standing at Arafah, and the lesser Hajj is the Umrah. It was also narrated from Mujahid: All the days of Hajj. Al-Hasan and Abdullah bin Al-Harith bin Nawfal said: It was called the greatest day of Hajj because Muslims and polytheists performed Hajj that year, and the festivals of the religions: the Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians coincided on that day. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is weak that God, the Almighty, would describe it in His Book as the greatest for this reason. It was also narrated from Al-Hasan: It was called the greatest because Abu Bakr performed Hajj on it and the covenants were abandoned on it. This is similar to Al-Hasan's view. Ibn Sirin said: The greatest day of Hajj is the year in which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed the Farewell Hajj, and the nations performed Hajj with him on it. Third: The Almighty’s saying: God is free from the polytheists and so is His Messenger. “An” with the fat-ha is in the accusative case. The meaning is that God. And whoever reads with the kasra estimated it to mean he said that God is free. Bare is the predicate of an. And His Messenger is in apposition to the place, or if you wish, to the implied raised pronoun in bare. Both are good, because the speech has become long. And if you wish, it is on the subject and the predicate is omitted, the meaning is: And His Messenger is free from them. And whoever reads And His Messenger with the accusative - which is al-Hasan and others - it is in apposition to the name of God, the Almighty, on the word. And in the anomalies, And His Messenger with the genitive case is on the oath, meaning and the right of His Messenger, and it was narrated from al-Hasan. The story of Omar in it was presented at the beginning of the book. So if you repent meaning from polytheism. Then it is better for you meaning more beneficial for you. But if you turn away meaning from faith. Then know that you will not escape God meaning you will escape Him, for He encompasses you and will send down His punishment upon you.
9:4: The Almighty's saying: Except those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty is in the accusative case as a connected exception, meaning: God is innocent of the polytheists except those with whom you made a treaty during the period of their treaty. It was said: The exception is disconnected, meaning that God is innocent of them, but those with whom you made a treaty and remained steadfast in the treaty, so fulfill your treaty with them. His saying: Then they did not fail you indicates that there were among the people of the treaty those who broke their treaty and among them were those who remained faithful, so God, the Almighty, permitted His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to break the treaty of those who failed, and He commanded to fulfill the treaty for those who remained faithful to their treaty until its term. The meaning of they did not fail you is any of the conditions of the treaty. And they did not aid is they did not help. Ikrimah and Ata' ibn Yasar read Then they did not fail you with a voiced ḍād with the omission of an adjective, the meaning being: Then they did not break their treaty. It is said: This is specific and is intended for Banu Damrah in particular. Then he said: Then fulfill their covenant with them until their term, meaning even if it was more than four months.
9:5: It contains six issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: So when the sacred months have passed - meaning they have left. And you leave the month if you are in its last days, you leave it by peeling it and by salukha meaning you have exited from it. And the poet said: If I finish the month and start the month before it, it is enough to kill me by finishing the months and starting them. The month has passed and the day has passed from the coming night. The woman has removed her armor. In the Qur’an: “And a sign for them is the night. We remove from it the day.” (Ya-Sin 36:37) And a palm tree that has been stripped, which is the one whose green fruit is scattered. As for the sacred months, the scholars have two opinions: It was said that they are the well-known months, three in succession and one on its own. Al-Asamm said: It means those polytheists who do not have a covenant, so he is required to refrain from fighting them until the sanctuary is removed, which is a period of fifty days according to what Ibn Abbas mentioned, because the call to do so was on the Day of Sacrifice. This has been mentioned before. It was said: The months of the covenant are four, as stated by Mujahid, Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Zayd, and Amr ibn Shuaib. It was said that they are sacred because God forbade the believers in them to shed the blood of polytheists and to attack them except for the sake of good. Second: The Almighty’s statement: Then kill the polytheists is general for every polytheist, but the Sunnah has specified from it what was previously explained in Surat Al-Baqarah, such as women, monks, children, and others. And God the Almighty said about the People of the Book: Until they pay the jizyah (al-Tawbah 9:29). However, it is possible that the word polytheists does not include the People of the Book, and this requires prohibiting taking the jizyah from idol worshippers and others, as will be explained. And know that the generality of His statement: Then kill the polytheists requires the permissibility of killing them in any way, except that the reports came prohibiting mutilation. Despite this, it is possible that when Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him killed the apostates by burning them with fire, stones, throwing them from mountaintops, and throwing them into wells, he was referring to the generality of the verse. Likewise, the burning of some apostates by Ali may God be pleased with him may have been an inclination toward this school of thought, and reliance on the generality of the wording. And God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Wherever you find them is general in every place. Abu Hanifa, may God be pleased with him, specified the Sacred Mosque, as mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah, then they differed. Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl said: This abrogated every verse in the Qur’an that mentions turning away and being patient with the harm of enemies. Ad-Dahhak, As-Suddi and Ata’ said: It was abrogated by His saying: Then either a favor from us afterwards or a ransom (Muhammad 47:4). And that a prisoner is not killed in a state of patience, either he is shown a favor or he is ransomed. Mujahid and Qatadah said: Rather, it abrogates the Almighty’s saying: Then either a favor from us afterwards or a ransom and that nothing is permissible with regard to the prisoners of the polytheists except killing. Ibn Zayd said: The two verses are decisive. This is correct, because favor, killing and ransom were always part of the ruling of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding them from the first war he fought against them, which was the Day of Badr, as mentioned previously. His saying: And take them indicates this. Taking is captivity. Captivity is only for killing, ransom, or favor, according to what the Imam sees fit. The meaning of and confine them is to prevent them from moving into your country or entering you, unless you give them permission to enter you safely. Fourth - The Almighty’s saying: And lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. The ambush: is the place where the enemy is watched. It is said: I lay in wait for so-and-so, meaning I watched him. That is, lie in wait for them in places of surprise where they lie in wait. Amer bin Tufail said: I knew, and I do not think you have forgotten, that death is for the young man at the watchtower. Adi said: O critics, ignorance is a pleasure for youth, and death is an ambush for souls. This is evidence of the permissibility of assassinating them before the call. The accusative of all is based on circumstance, which is the choice of Al-Zajjaj. It is said: I went a road and I went every road. Or by dropping the preposition, the estimate: in every observation post and on every observation post, so the observation post is made the name of the road. Abu Ali Al-Zajjaj made a mistake in making the road a circumstance and said: The road is a specific place like a house or a mosque, so it is not permissible to delete the preposition from it except in what has been mentioned in deletion by hearing, as Sibawayh narrated: I entered Syria and I entered the house, and as it was said: As the fox road honey Fifth - The Almighty said: If they repent meaning from polytheism. And establish prayer and give zakat, then let them go on their way. This verse requires contemplation, because Almighty God made killing conditional on polytheism, then He said: If they repent. The basic principle is that killing, whenever it is for polytheism, is removed by its removal, and that necessitates the removal of killing by mere repentance, regardless of establishing prayer and giving zakat. Therefore, killing is dropped by mere repentance before the time of prayer and zakat. This is clear in this meaning, except that Almighty God mentioned repentance and mentioned two other conditions with it, so there is no way to cancel them. Similar to this is the saying of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: “I have been commanded to fight people until they say, ‘There is no god but God,’ establish prayer, and pay zakat. If they do that, their blood and wealth are protected from me, except for what is due, and their reckoning is with God.” Abu Bakr al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him said: By God, I will kill whoever differentiates between prayer and zakat, for zakat is due on wealth. Ibn Abbas said: May God have mercy on Abu Bakr, how knowledgeable he was. Ibn al-Arabi said: The Qur’an and Sunnah are in harmony and consistent. There is no disagreement among Muslims that whoever abandons prayer and other obligatory acts, considering them permissible, is an infidel, and whoever abandons the Sunnah acts, being careless, is a sinner, and whoever abandons voluntary acts is not a heretic, unless he denies their virtue, in which case he becomes an infidel, because he is rejecting what the Messenger (peace be upon him) brought and conveyed. They differed concerning whoever abandons prayer without denying it or considering it permissible. Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la narrated: I heard Ibn Wahb say: Malik said: Whoever believes in God and believes in the Messengers and refuses to pray is to be killed. Abu Thawr and all the companions of al-Shafi’i said the same. This is the opinion of Hammad bin Zaid, Makhul and Waki’. Abu Hanifa said: He should be imprisoned and beaten, but not killed. This is the opinion of Ibn Shihab, and Dawud bin Ali says the same. Among their proofs is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have been commanded to fight people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ If they say that, then their blood and property are protected from me, except for a right. They said: “The right to it is the three things that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The blood of a Muslim is not permissible to be shed except in one of three cases: disbelief after faith, adultery after marriage, or killing a soul without a soul.” A group of the Companions and Followers said that whoever intentionally neglects a single prayer until its time has passed without an excuse, and refuses to perform it or make it up and says I will not pray, then he is a disbeliever, and his blood and wealth are permissible, and his Muslim heirs do not inherit from him. He should be asked to repent, and if he repents, otherwise he should be killed, and the ruling on his wealth is like the ruling on the wealth of an apostate, and this is the opinion of Ishaq. Ishaq said: This was the opinion of the scholars from the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until our time. Ibn Khuwayzmandad said: Our companions differed on when the one who neglects prayer should be killed. Some of them said at the end of the preferred time, and some of them said at the end of the necessary time, and this is the correct view. That is, four rak’ahs remain from the time of the ‘Asr prayer until sunset, and four rak’ahs from the night until the time of the ‘Isha’ prayer, and two rak’ahs from the Fajr prayer before sunrise. Ishaq said: The passing of the time means delaying the Dhuhr prayer until sunset, and the Maghrib prayer until the break of dawn. Sixth: This verse indicates that whoever says, I have repented, his statement is not sufficient unless he adds to it his actions that establish repentance, because God Almighty has stipulated here with repentance establishing prayer and paying zakat in order to establish repentance with them. He said in the verse on usury: But if you repent, you shall have your capital sums (al-Baqarah 2:279). He also said: Except for those who repent, amend, and declare [the truth]. The meaning of this has already been presented in Surat Al-Baqarah.
9:6: It has four issues: First: The Almighty said: And if any of the polytheists meaning of those whom I have commanded you to fight. Seeks your protection meaning asks for your protection, that is, your safety and covenant, so give it to him so that he may listen to the Qur’an, that is, understand its rulings, commands and prohibitions. If he accepts an order, then that is good, and if he refuses, then return him to his place of safety. There is no disagreement about this, and God knows best. Malik said: If a combatant is found on the road to a Muslim country and says: I have come seeking protection. Malik said: These are ambiguous matters, and I think that he should be returned to his place of safety. Ibn al-Qasim said: Likewise, if someone is found and has settled as a merchant on our coast and says: I thought that you would not interfere with someone who has come as a merchant so that he may sell. The apparent meaning of the verse is only for someone who wants to listen to the Qur’an and consider Islam. As for hiring for anything other than that, it is only for the benefit of the Muslims and considering what will benefit them. Second: There is no disagreement among all scholars that the Sultan’s security is permissible, because he is the first priority for consideration and interest, and is a deputy for everyone in bringing benefits and repelling harm. They differed regarding the security of someone other than the Caliph. The security of a free man is valid according to all scholars. However, Ibn Habib said: The Imam looks into him. As for the slave, he has security according to the well-known school of thought, and this is what Al-Shafi’i and his companions, Ahmad, Ishaq, Al-Awza’i, Al-Thawri, Abu Thawr, Dawud, and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said. Abu Hanifa said: He has no security, and this is the second opinion of our scholars. The first is more correct, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The blood of Muslims is equal and their protection is sought by the lowest of them. They said: When he said the lowest of them, the protection of a slave is permissible, and the free woman is more deserving of that, and no consideration is given to a reason that does not give him a share. Abdul Malik bin Al-Majishun said: The protection of a woman is not permissible unless the Imam approves it, so his statement differed from the majority. As for the boy, if he is able to fight, his protection is permissible, because he is among the fighters and is included in the group that protects. Ad-Dahhak and As-Suddi said that this verse was abrogated by the statement: Then kill the polytheists. Al-Hasan said: It is a ruling for one year until the Day of Resurrection, and Mujahid said the same. It was said: The ruling of this verse only remained for the period of four months that were set for them as a deadline, and it is nothing. Saeed bin Jubair said: A polytheist came to Ali bin Abi Talib and said: If a man from us wants to come to Muhammad after the four months have passed and hear the words of God or come to him with a need, he should be killed! Ali ibn Abi Talib said: No, because God Almighty says: If any of the polytheists seeks your protection, grant him protection so that he may hear the word of God. This is correct. The verse is decisive. Third - The Almighty’s saying: And if anyone “any” is raised by an implied verb like the one after it. This is good in in and bad in its sisters. Sibawayh’s school of thought regarding the difference between in and its sisters is that since it is the mother of conditional letters, it was singled out for this, and because it does not occur in anything else. Muhammad bin Yazid said: As for his saying: because it does not occur in anything else, this is a mistake, because it can have the meaning of what and is lightened from the heavy one, but it is ambiguous, and this is not the case with others. Sibawayh recited: Do not be sad if you have lost someone, and if you are lost, then be sad. Fourth: The scholars said: In the words of God the Almighty: until he hears the word of God is evidence that the word of God the Almighty is heard when the reciter recites. Sheikh Abu al-Hasan, Judge Abu Bakr, Abu al-Abbas al-Asqalani, Ibn Mujahid, Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini and others said, because God the Almighty said: until he hears the word of God. So he stated that His word is heard when the reciter recites His words. This is indicated by the consensus of the Muslims that when the reciter recites the Opening of the Book or a Surah, they say: We heard the word of God. They differentiated between reciting the word of God the Almighty and reciting the poetry of Imru’ al-Qais. The meaning of the word of God the Almighty has already been explained in Surat al-Baqarah, and that it is neither a letter nor a sound, and praise be to God.
9:7: The Almighty says: How can there be a treaty with God and with His Messenger, except for those with whom you made a treaty at al-Masjid al-Haram? The word how here is used to express astonishment, just as you would say: How can so-and-so outstrip me? That is, he should not outstrip me. And a treaty is a noun that means to be. And in the verse there is an implication, that is, how can there be a treaty with the polytheists while concealing treachery, as He said: You told me that death is only in the villages, so how about when there is a plateau and a dune? The estimate, so how did he die, on the authority of Al-Zajjaj. It was said: The meaning is how can the polytheists have a covenant with God that will make them feel safe from His punishment tomorrow, and how can they have a covenant with His Messenger that will make them feel safe from the punishment of this world? Then he made an exception and said: Except those with whom you made a covenant at Al-Masjid Al-Haram. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: They are Banu Bakr, meaning the covenant is only for those who did not break it or violate it. God Almighty says: So as long as they remain upright with you, remain upright with them. That is, as long as they remain faithful to your covenant, remain upright with them in the same way. Ibn Zayd: So they did not remain upright, so He set a term of four months for them. As for the one with whom we have not made a covenant, fight him wherever you find him, unless he repents.
9:8: The Almighty’s saying: How can it be, even if they gain the upper hand over you? He repeated the astonishment that they could have a covenant with the evil of their actions, meaning, how can they have a covenant, even if they gain the upper hand over you, not observing any pact or covenant with you? It is said: I gained the upper hand over someone, meaning I overcame him. The word gazd means I overcame in the house, and from this is they were not able to gain the upper hand over him (al-Kahf 18:97) meaning they could not gain the upper hand over him. God the Almighty said: They do not observe among you kinship or covenant. They observe, they guard. And the guard is the preserver. It has been mentioned before. Except a covenant, on the authority of Mujahid and Ibn Zayd. And on the authority of Mujahid also: It is one of the names of God the Almighty. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak: Kinship. Al-Hasan: Neighborhood. Qatada: An oath, and a covenant. Abu Ubaidah: An oath. And on his authority also: Except a covenant, and a covenant is a pledge. Al-Azhari: The name of God in Hebrew, and its origin is from Alil, which is the brilliance. It is said that its color is Al-Yu’l Ala, meaning it became clear and shiny. And it was said: Its origin is from sharpness, and from it is the tool for the spear, and from it is a sharpened ear, meaning sharpened. And from it is the saying of Tarafa bin Al-Abd describing the ears of his she-camel as sharp and erect: Two instruments in which the emancipation is known, such as the hearing of a sheep with a single lamb If it is said about the covenant, neighborhood, and kinship, il, it means that the permission is directed to that direction, i.e. it is specified for it. The covenant is called il because of its clarity and appearance. The plural is alal in rare cases, and ilal in large cases. Al-Jawhari and others said: il in the kasra is God Almighty, and il also means the covenant and kinship. Hassan said: By your life, you are to the Quraysh like the head of an ostrich is to the neck of an ostrich. The Almighty said: nor a covenant meaning a pledge. It is every sacred thing that you are bound to commit a sin if you neglect it. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: The covenant is the pledge. Whoever makes the covenant the pledge, then the repetition is due to the difference in the two words. Abu Ubaidah Muammar said: The covenant is the pledge. Abu Ubaid said: The covenant is the security in his saying, peace be upon him: And the lowest of them will strive to protect their covenant. The plural of covenant is dhimmah. A well is a dhimmah with the first letter of the letter dhal open with little water, and its plural is dhimam. Dhu ar-Rummah said: On donkeys whose eyes are like the dams of the wells, and the winds have pricked them If you push her, her water will go away. The People of the Covenant are the people of the covenant. God Almighty says: They please you with their mouths meaning they say with their tongues what is outwardly pleasing. But their hearts refuse, and most of them are wicked meaning they break the covenant. Every disbeliever is wicked, but here He meant those who openly commit shameful acts and break the covenant.
9:9: It means the polytheists in their breaking of the covenant with a meal that Abu Sufyan fed them, said Mujahid. It was said: They exchanged the Qur’an for worldly pleasures. So they turned away from His path means they turned away, from turning away. Or they prevented from the path of God, from the path of sidd.
9:10: An-Nahhas said: This is not a repetition, but the first is for all polytheists and the second is for the Jews in particular. The evidence for this is They have purchased with the verses of God a small price meaning the Jews, they sold the proofs of God the Almighty and His explanation in order to seek leadership and covet something. And those are the transgressors meaning those who transgress from what is lawful to what is unlawful by breaking the covenant.
9:11: The Almighty said: If they repent meaning from polytheism and adhere to the rulings of Islam. Then they are your brothers meaning they are your brothers in religion. Ibn Abbas said: The blood of the people of the Qiblah is forbidden. This meaning has been mentioned previously. Ibn Zayd said: God has made prayer and zakat obligatory and refused to separate between them, and refused to accept prayer without zakat. Ibn Masoud said: You have been commanded to pray and zakat, so whoever does not pay zakat has no prayer. And in the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Whoever differentiates between three things, God will differentiate between him and His mercy on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Whoever says, ‘I obey God’ but I do not obey the Messenger,’ while God the Almighty says, ‘Obey God and obey the Messenger’ (An-Nisa’: 59). Whoever says, ‘I establish prayer’ but I do not pay zakat,’ while God the Almighty says, ‘And establish prayer and give zakat’ (al-Baqarah 2:43). Whoever differentiates between thanking God and thanking his parents, while God the Almighty says, ‘Be grateful to Me and to your parents’ (Luqman 31:14).” God Almighty says: And We detail the verses meaning We explain them. For a people who know. He specified them because they are the ones who will benefit from them. And God knows best.
9:12: It contains seven issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And if they break their oath. Breaking means breaking, and its origin is in what was twisted and then dissolved. So it is borrowed from oaths and covenants. He said: If she swears that staying away will not break her covenant, then the one with dyed fingers has no oath. Any covenant. And his saying: And they attacked your religion meaning by sabotaging and war and other things that the polytheist does. It is said that he stabbed him with a spear and stabbed with bad words about him, with the damma of the ‘ayn in both. And it was said: he stabbed with a spear with the damma and he stabbed with words with the fatha. And here it is a metaphor, and from it is “the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when he ordered Usama: If you attack his leadership, then you attacked the leadership of his father before, and by God, he is worthy of leadership.” Narrated by Sahih. Second: Some scholars have used this verse as evidence for the obligation to kill anyone who criticizes the religion, as he is an unbeliever. Criticism is to attribute to it what is not appropriate for it, or to make light of what is part of the religion, due to the proven conclusive evidence of the soundness of its principles and the rectitude of its branches. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The majority of scholars agree that whoever insults the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, must be killed. Among those who said this are Malik, al-Layth, Ahmad, and Ishaq, and it is the school of thought of al-Shafi’i. It was narrated from al-Nu’man that he said: Whoever insults the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the People of the Covenant should not be killed, as will be mentioned. It was narrated that a man said in the assembly of Ali: Ka’b ibn al-Ashraf was killed only treacherously, so Ali ordered that his neck be struck off. Another said this in the assembly of Mu’awiyah, so Muhammad ibn Maslama stood up and said: Is this said in your assembly and you remain silent? By God, I will never live under a roof with you, and if I am alone with him, I will kill him. Our scholars said: This person should be killed and not given a chance to repent if he attributes treachery to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is what Ali and Muhammad ibn Salamah may God be pleased with them understood from the one who said that, because that is heresy. As for attributing it to those who directly killed him, so that he says: They gave him security and then betrayed him, then this attribution would be a complete lie, because there is nothing in their conversation with him that indicates that they gave him security, nor did they explicitly state that to him. If they had done that, it would not have been security, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) only directed them to kill him, not to give him security, and he gave permission to Muhammad ibn Maslamah to say that. Based on this, there is consideration and hesitation in killing those who attributed that to them. And his insulting him, does it necessitate that he attributes treachery to them, because he approved of their action and was pleased with it, so it necessitates that he was pleased with the treachery, and the one who explicitly stated that was killed? Or does it not necessitate that he attribute treachery to them, so he is not killed, so it is necessary to torture the one who said it and punish him with imprisonment, severe beating, and great humiliation. Third: As for the dhimmi, if he slanders the religion, his covenant is broken according to the well-known opinion of the Maliki school, because of his saying: And if they break their oaths verse. So he ordered that they be killed and fought. This is the opinion of al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him. Abu Hanifa said about this: He should be asked to repent, and that merely slandering does not nullify the covenant except with the presence of the slander, because God, the Almighty, only ordered that they be killed under two conditions: one of them is that they broke the covenant, and the second is that they slandered the religion. We said: If they did something that contradicted the covenant, their covenant is broken, and mentioning the two matters does not necessitate that fighting him be contingent upon their presence, because the slander makes it permissible for them to do so on its own, rationally and legally. The interpretation of the verse according to us is: If they break their covenant, fighting them is permissible, and if they do not break their covenant, but rather slander the religion while fulfilling the covenant, fighting them is permissible. It was narrated that a dhimmi was brought to ‘Umar who had gored an animal on which a Muslim woman was riding, and it speared it and caused it to fall, exposing some of its private parts, so he ordered that he be crucified in the same place. Fourth: If a dhimmi fights, his covenant is broken and his wealth and children are spoils of war with him. Muhammad ibn Maslama said: His children will not be held accountable for it, because he broke it alone. He said: As for his wealth, it will be taken. This is a contradiction that does not resemble the position of Muhammad ibn Maslama, because his covenant is what protected his wealth and children, so if his wealth is taken away from him, his children are taken away from him. Ashhab said: If a dhimmi breaks his covenant, he is bound by his covenant and will never return to slavery. This is strange, as if he saw the covenant as a tangible meaning. Rather, the covenant is a ruling required by reason, and Muslims are committed to it, so if he breaks it, it is broken like all other contracts. Fifth: Most scholars agree that whoever among the People of the Covenant curses the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), or denigrates or belittles his status, or describes him in a manner other than that in which he disbelieved, then he is to be killed, because we did not give him the covenant or the pact for this. Except for Abu Hanifa, Al-Thawri and their followers from the people of Kufa, who said: He is not to be killed, because what he is doing of polytheism is greater. But he is to be disciplined and punished. The evidence for this is the saying of God the Almighty: And if they break their covenant (Al-Anbiya’ 4:10). Some of them used as evidence for this the command of God the Almighty the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to kill Ka’b ibn Al-Ashraf, who had a covenant. Abu Bakr became angry with one of his companions, so Abu Barzah said: Shall I not strike his neck? He said: This was not the case for anyone after the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “A blind man had a slave girl, and he had two sons from her who were like two pearls. She used to curse the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and insult him. He would forbid her, but she would not stop, and he would reprimand her, but she would not desist. One night, she mentioned the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but her master could not bear it. He got a pickaxe and put it in her stomach, then leaned on her until he pierced it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Will you not bear witness that her blood is shed?’” And in a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “So he killed her. When morning came, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was told about that. The blind man got up and said: ‘O Messenger of God, I am her companion. She used to curse you and insult you. I forbade her, but she would not desist. I reprimanded her, but she would not desist. I had two sons from her who were like two pearls. She was my companion. Last night, she used to curse you and insult you, so I killed her. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Will you not bear witness that her blood is shed?’” Sixth: They differed if he insulted him and then converted to Islam to avoid being killed. It was said: His conversion to Islam cancels his killing, and this is the well-known opinion of the school of thought, because Islam cancels what came before it. Unlike the Muslim if he insulted him and then repented, God the Almighty said: Say to those who disbelieve, if they cease, what has previously occurred will be forgiven them (al-Anfal 8:38). It was said: Islam does not cancel his killing, as stated in Al-Utbiyya because it is a right of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that is required due to his violation of his sanctity and his intention to cause him shortcomings and disgrace, so his return to Islam was not what cancels it, and he is not in a better state than the Muslim. Seventh: The Almighty said: Fight the leaders of disbelief. Leaders is the plural of leader, and what is meant are the leaders of Quraysh - according to some scholars - such as Abu Jahl, Utbah, Shaibah, and Umayyah ibn Khalaf. This is far-fetched, because the verse is in Surah Bara'ah, and when it was revealed and recited to the people, God had eradicated the influence of Quraysh, and none remained except Muslims or peaceful people. It is possible that what is meant is Fight the leaders of disbelief. That is, whoever breaks the covenant and attacks the religion is the root and head of disbelief, so he is one of the leaders of disbelief according to this. It is possible that what is meant by it are the predecessors and leaders among them, and that fighting them is fighting their followers and that they have no sanctity. The original is ummah like mithal and amthalath, then the mim was assimilated into the mim and the vowel was reversed on the hamza, so two hamzas came together, and the second was replaced with a ya. Al-Akhfash claimed that you say: this is ayyam min this, with a ya. Al-Mazini said: Awm min this, with a waw. Hamza read a'immah. Most grammarians believe that this is a mistake, because he combined two hamzas in one word. Indeed, they have no oaths means they have no covenants, meaning their covenants are not true and they do not fulfill them. Ibn Amir read They have no faith with a kasra on the hamza from faith, meaning they have no Islam. It is possible that the source of I trusted him is faith, from security, the opposite of which is fear, meaning they do not believe, from I trusted him meaning I granted him protection, so he said: Fight the leaders of disbelief, for they have no oaths, perhaps they will desist meaning from polytheism. Al-Kalbi said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made peace with the people of Mecca for a year while he was at Al-Hudaybiyyah, so they prevented him from entering the House, then they made peace with him on the condition that he would return, and they stayed as long as God willed. Then the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Khuza'ah fought the allies of Banu Umayyah from Kinanah, so Banu Umayyah provided their allies with weapons and food. Khuza'ah sought help from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so this verse was revealed and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ordered to help his allies as mentioned above. In Bukhari, on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, he said: We were with Hudhayfah and he said: There are only three people left from the companions of this verse - meaning, Fight the leaders of disbelief, for indeed, there are no oaths for them - and there are only four hypocrites left. A Bedouin said: You are the companions of Muhammad, and you tell stories that we do not know what they are! You claim that there are only four hypocrites, so what about these who destroy our homes and steal our belongings? He said: Those are the wicked ones. Indeed, there are only four of them left, one of them is an old man who, if he drank cold water, would not find it cold. The Almighty says: Perhaps they will desist meaning from their disbelief, falsehood, and harm to the Muslims. This requires that the purpose of fighting them be to prevent their harm so that they will desist from fighting us and enter our religion.
9:13: The Almighty's saying: Will you not fight a people who broke their oaths? is a rebuke and contains the meaning of incitement. It was revealed about the infidels of Mecca, as we mentioned earlier. And they intended to expel the Messenger meaning that they were the reason for the expulsion, so the expulsion was attributed to them. It was said: They expelled the Messenger, peace be upon him, from Medina to fight the people of Mecca for the breach of the covenant that they had committed, according to Al-Hasan. And they initiated the fighting against you with the fighting. The first time meaning they broke the covenant and helped Banu Bakr against Khuza'ah. It was said: They initiated the fighting against you on the day of Badr, because the Prophet, peace be upon him, went out with the caravan and when they secured others, they could have left, but they refused except to reach Badr and drink wine there, as mentioned above. So God is more deserving that you fear Him meaning that you fear His punishment for not fighting them, than that you fear that something bad will happen to you in fighting them. It was said: Their expulsion of the Messenger was their preventing him from performing Hajj, Umrah, and Tawaf, and this was their initiation. God knows best.
9:14: The Almighty's saying: Fight them is a command. God will punish them is its answer. It is a jussive mood meaning retribution. The meaning is: If you fight them, God will punish them by your hands, disgrace them, give you victory over them, and heal the hearts of a believing people. And remove the anger of their hearts is evidence that their anger had become intense. Mujahid said: He means Khuza'ah, the allies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. All of it is an conjunction, and all of it is permissible to put it in the nominative case based on the separation from the first. It is permissible to put it in the accusative case based on the omission of an, which is the inflection according to the Kufians, as he said: If Abu Qaboos perishes, the spring of the people and the sacred month will perish. And we take after him the tail of a life that has a back that has no hump If you wish, you can raise it and we take, and if you wish, you can lower it. What is meant by His statement: And heals the hearts of a believing people is Banu Khuza’ah, according to what we mentioned from Mujahid. “The Quraysh aided Banu Bakr against them, and Khuza’ah were allies of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. A man from Banu Bakr recited a satire of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of the Khuza’ah said to him: If you repeat it, I will break your mouth. So he repeated it and his mouth was broken, and a fight broke out between them, and they killed some of the Khuza’is. Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza’i went out with a group of people to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him about what happened. He entered the house of Maymunah and said: Pour me some water. So he began to wash himself, saying: I will not be victorious if I do not support Banu Ka’b. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to prepare and go out to Mecca, and the conquest occurred.”
9:15: The Almighty said: And God accepts the repentance of whom He wills The reading is in the nominative case as a resumption, because it is not of the same type as the first. That is why He did not say and repents in the accusative case, because fighting does not require them to repent from God, the Almighty and Majestic. It requires them to be tormented and disgraced, and to heal the hearts of the believers and remove the anger from their hearts. Similar to it is: But if God wills, He will seal your heart (al-Shura 42:24). The speech is complete. Then He said: And God erases falsehood and those whom God accepted their repentance, such as Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl, and Sulaym bin Abi Amr, because they converted to Islam. Ibn Abi Ishaq read and repents in the accusative case. This is also narrated from Isa Al-Thaqafi and Al-A'raj, and based on this, repentance is included in the answer to the condition, because the meaning is: If you fight them, God will punish them. And so is what is conjoined to it. Then He said: And God accepts the repentance meaning if you fight them. So He combined their torment at your hands, their healing, the anger from your hearts, and your repentance. And raising it is better, because repentance is not caused by fighting, as it may occur without fighting for whomever God wills to repent in any case.
9:16: The Almighty said: Or did you think to go from one thing to another. That you would be left is in the place of the two objects according to Sibawayh. According to Al-Mubarrad, the second object has been deleted. The meaning of the statement: Or did you think that you would be left without being tested by what the believer and the hypocrite appear with, the appearance by which they deserve reward and punishment? This meaning has been presented in more than one place. And when he knows is made jussive by when, even though what is redundant, then according to Sibawayh it is an answer to your saying: He did, as mentioned above. And the meem was broken due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. Walijah is a lining and an intervention, from al-wuluj which means to enter, and from it the kabas in which the wild beasts enter is called tawlij. And walaj means to enter. The meaning is: an intruder of affection without God and His Messenger. Abu Ubaidah said: Everything that you introduce into something that is not from it is a walijah, and a man who is among the people but is not from them is a walijah. Ibn Zayd said: The walija is the intruder, and the walija is the intruder. So the walija of a man is the one who is exclusively involved in his affair without the others. You say: He is my walija and they are my walija, the singular and plural are the same. Abaan ibn Taghlib, may God have mercy on him, said: What a bad refuge for fugitives, aggressors, and suspicious people. It was said: Walijah is a confidant, and the meaning is the same, similar to Do not take confidants from among yourselves (Al Imran 3:118). Al Farra’ said: Walijah is a confidant from among the polytheists whom they take as confidants and reveal their secrets to them and teach them their affairs.
9:17: The Almighty said: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God. The phrase to maintain is in the nominative case as the subject of was. Witnesses to the state. Scholars differed in the interpretation of this verse. Some said: He meant that they were not allowed to perform Hajj after they were banned from entering the Sacred Mosque. The affairs of the House, such as custodianship, watering, and providing food, were left to the polytheists. So He made it clear that they were not worthy of that, but rather its people were the believers. It was said: When Abbas was taken prisoner and was reproached for his disbelief and severing family ties, he said: You mention our faults but do not mention our virtues. Ali said: Do you have virtues? He said: Yes, we maintain the Sacred Mosque, we screen the Kaaba, we provide water to the pilgrims, and we free the captives. So this verse was revealed in response to him. So it is obligatory for Muslims to take charge of the rulings of the mosques and prevent the polytheists from entering them. The common reading is ya'mur with a fat-ha on the ya' and a damma on the meem, from umar ya'mur. Ibn al-Sumaiq' read it with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the meem, meaning they make it inhabited or help in its construction. Masjid God was read in the singular, meaning the Sacred Mosque. This is the reading of Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Muhaisin, and Ya'qub. The rest read it as masajid in the general sense. This is the choice of Abu Ubaid, because it is more general and the specific is included in the general. It may be possible that the plural reading refers to the Sacred Mosque in particular. This is permissible in the case of generic nouns, as it is said: So-and-so rides horses even though he only rides a horse. The reading masajid is more correct because it includes both meanings. They agreed to read the statement, Only the mosques of God are to be maintained in the plural, as al-Nahhas said. Al-Hasan said: He only said masajid and it refers to the Sacred Mosque because it is the qiblah of all mosques and their imam. God the Almighty said: Witnesses. It was said: He meant and they are witnesses, but when he dropped and they he put it in the accusative case. Ibn Abbas said: Their testimony against themselves of disbelief is their prostration to their idols and their acknowledgment that they are created. Al-Suddi said: Their testimony of disbelief is that you say to a Christian, What is your religion? and he says, Christian, and to a Jew, Jewish, and to a Sabean, Sabian, and it is said to a polytheist, What is your religion? and he says, Polytheist. “Their deeds have become worthless, and they are in the Fire.” The meaning of this was presented earlier.
9:18: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: Only those who maintain the mosques of God is evidence that testifying to the belief of those who maintain mosques is correct, because God, the Almighty, linked it to them and informed us about their commitment to them. Some of the Salaf said: If you see a man maintaining a mosque, then think well of him. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you see a man frequenting the mosque, then bear witness to his faith. God the Almighty said: The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day. In another narration: He frequents the mosque. He said: A good, strange hadith. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is in the apparent correctness, not in the sections of testimonies, for testimonies have states with those who know them. Some of them are intelligent, perceptive, and have acquired what they know in belief and information, and some of them are fools, and each one is placed according to his status and is able to describe it. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And he feared none but God. If it is said: There is no believer who does not fear other than God, and the believers and prophets have always feared enemies other than themselves. It is said to him: The meaning is: And he did not fear other than God from what he worshipped, because the polytheists used to worship idols and fear them and hope in them. Second answer: That is, he did not fear in the matter of religion other than God. Third: If it is said: Faith has been established in the verse for those who maintain mosques by praying in them, cleaning them, and repairing what is weak in them, and who believe in God. And faith in the Messenger is not mentioned in it, nor is faith for those who do not believe in the Messenger. It is said to him: What is mentioned about establishing prayer and other things indicates the Messenger, because it is what he brought. Establishing prayer and paying zakat are only valid for those who believe in the Messenger, so this is why He did not mention them individually. And perhaps from God is obligatory, according to Ibn Abbas and others. And it was said: Perhaps means it is appropriate, meaning it is appropriate that they be among the guided.
9:19: First - The Almighty's saying: Have you made the pilgrims' watering? The estimation in Arabic is: Have you made the pilgrims' watering companions, or the people who water the pilgrims, like the one who believed in God and fought in His cause. It is correct to estimate the deletion in the one who believed, meaning have you made the work of watering the pilgrims like the work of the one who believed. It was said: The estimation is like the faith of the one who believed. And watering is a source like striving and protection. So the noun was made in the place of the source since its meaning is known, like the generosity is Hatim, and the poetry is Zuhair. And the construction of the Sacred Mosque is like And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82). Abu Wijza read: Have you made the pilgrims' watering companions? And the pilgrimage to the Sacred Mosque is the plural of saq and the root is saqiyah on the basis of fa'lah, thus the defective word from this is pluralized, like qadi and qudat and nas and nasah. If it is not defective, it is pluralized on the basis of fa'lah like nas'i and nas'ah, for those who used to postpone the months. Ibn al-Zubayr and Sa`id ibn Jubayr read it as saqāt and `Umrah, except that Ibn Jubayr put the masjid in the accusative case, intending the tanween in `Umrah. Ad-Dahhak said: saqāt with a damma on the seen, and it is a language. Hajj is the name of the genus of pilgrims. Maintaining the Sacred Mosque means making treaties with it and taking care of its interests. The apparent meaning of this verse is that it invalidates the statement of those polytheists who boasted about providing water to the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque, as mentioned by As-Suddi. He said: Abbas boasted about providing water to the pilgrims, Shaibah about maintaining it, and `Ali about Islam and jihad. So God confirmed `Ali and denied them both, and He informed that maintaining it is not done by disbelief, but rather by faith, worship, and performing acts of obedience. This is clear and beyond doubt. It is said that the polytheists asked the Jews and said: We are the ones who provide water to the pilgrims and maintain the Sacred Mosque, so are we better than Muhammad and his companions? The Jews said to them, out of defiance of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): You are better. A problem has arisen here, which is what came in Sahih Muslim on the authority of An-Nu`man ibn Bashir, who said: 3309 I was at the pulpit of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) when a man said: I do not care if I do not do any work after Islam except providing water to the pilgrims. Another said: I do not care if I do not do any work after Islam except maintaining the Sacred Mosque. Another said: Jihad in the way of God is better than what you have said. Umar rebuked them and said: Do not raise your voices at the pulpit of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) - and it is a Friday - but when you have prayed the Friday prayer, go in and ask him about what you disagreed about. Then God the Almighty revealed: Do you consider providing water to the pilgrims and maintaining the Sacred Mosque equal to one who believes in God and the Last Day? until the end of the verse. This context requires that it was revealed when the Muslims disagreed about which of these works is better. Then it is not appropriate to say to them at the end of the verse: And God does not guide the wrongdoing people. So the problem is cleared up. It can be removed by saying: Some of the narrators were lenient in what they said, so God revealed the verse. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited the verse to Umar when he asked him, so the narrator thought that it was revealed at that time, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used it as evidence that jihad is better than what those whom Umar heard said, so he asked them for a fatwa and recited to him what had been revealed to him, not that it was revealed about them. And God knows best. If it is said: Accordingly, it is permissible to use what was revealed about the disbelievers as evidence for the Muslims, and it is known that their rulings are different. It is said to him: It is not unlikely that rulings befitting the Muslims could be derived from what God revealed about the polytheists. Umar said: If we wanted, we could have made stews and roasted meats, and one side would be cleared and another would be raised, but we heard the statement of God the Most High: You have exhausted your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them (al-Ahqaf 46:20). This verse is explicit about the disbelievers, and with that, Umar understood from it a warning against what suits their conditions to some extent, and none of the companions objected to him. So this verse could be of this type. This is valuable and removes the confusion and ambiguity. And God knows best.
9:20: The Almighty's saying: Those who believe is in the nominative case as a subject. Its predicate is greater in degree with God. And degree is in the accusative case as a clarification, meaning than those who boasted about watering and building. And the disbelievers do not have a degree with God so that it can be said: The believer has a greater degree. What is meant is that they estimated for themselves a degree in building and watering, so He addressed them according to what they estimated in themselves even if the estimation was wrong, like the Almighty's saying: The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be the best place to settle (al-Furqan 25:24). It was said: Greater in degree than anyone with a degree, meaning they will have the advantage and the highest position. And those are the successful ones by that.
9:21: The Almighty says: Their Lord gives them good tidings meaning He informs them in this world of the great reward and everlasting bliss they will have in the Hereafter. Bliss means a comfortable and luxurious life.
9:22: The Almighty’s saying: “Immortal” is in the accusative case as a state. Immortality is residence. Indeed, God has with Him a great reward meaning He has prepared for them in His house of honor that reward.
9:23: This verse appears to be addressed to all believers, and it will remain in effect until the Day of Judgment in severing allegiance between believers and unbelievers. A group reported that this verse was revealed to urge emigration and reject the lands of the unbelievers. Thus, the addressee in this case is to the believers who were in Mecca and other Arab lands. They were told not to befriend their fathers and brothers, lest they follow them in residing in the lands of unbelief. If they like means if they like, as it is said: He responded means He answered. That is, do not obey them and do not single them out. God the Almighty singled out fathers and brothers, as there is no closer kinship than them. So He denied allegiance between them, just as He denied it between people, by saying: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies (al-Ma’idah 5:51) to show that closeness is closeness of religions, not closeness of bodies. In a similar manner, the Sufis chant: They tell me the home of the beloved is near, and you are like a sand dune. This is truly amazing. I said: What good are close homes if there is no closeness between the hearts? How many a distant home has achieved what it wanted, while another neighbor nearby has died like a sand dune? Children are not mentioned in this verse, as most people believe that children are subordinate to their fathers. Kindness and gifts are excluded from guardianship. 3310 Asma’ said: O Messenger of God, my mother came to me seeking help, and she is a polytheist. Should I maintain ties of kinship with her? He said: Maintain ties of kinship with your mother. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. God Almighty says: And whoever among you takes them as allies - it is those who are the wrongdoers. Ibn Abbas said: He is a polytheist like them, because whoever is satisfied with polytheism is a polytheist. God Almighty says: “Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your kindred, the wealth that you have acquired, the commerce in which you fear decline, and the dwellings in which you delight are dearer to you than God and His Messenger and striving in His cause, then wait until God brings about His decision. And God does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.”
9:24: When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) ordered the migration from Mecca to Medina, a man would say to his father, a father to his son, a brother to his brother, and a man to his wife: We have been ordered to migrate. Some of them hastened to do so, and some of them refused to migrate, saying: By God, if you do not go to the abode of migration, I will never benefit you or spend on you at all. Some of them would have their wives and children cling to them and say to them: I ask you by God not to go, so that we may be lost after you. Some of them would feel compassion and abandon migration and stay with them, so the verse was revealed: O you who have believed, do not take your fathers and your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over belief. He said: If they chose to stay in disbelief in Mecca over belief in God and migrate to Medina. And whoever among you takes them as allies after the verse was revealed, then it is they who are the wrongdoers. Then it was revealed about those who stayed behind and did not migrate: “Say: If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your kindred” which is the group that goes back to one contract like a contract of ten or more, and from it comes cohabitation which is meeting on something. And wealth that you have acquired he says: you acquired it in Mecca. The origin of iqtiraaf is separating something from its place to another. And commerce in which you fear decline Ibn al-Mubarak said: It is the daughters and sisters who, if they decline in the house, cannot find a suitor for them. The poet said: They were poor among their people, and my presence made them even more poor. And dwellings that please you means: and homes that you find pleasant to live in. Better to you than for you to migrate to God and His Messenger in Medina. Better is the predicate of was. It is permissible in places other than the Qur’an to raise better as the subject and predicate, and the subject of was is implied in it. Sibawayh recited: If I die, people will be of two types: those who gloat and those who praise what I did. And he recited: It is the cure for my illness if I obtain it, but there is no cure for the illness that is available from it. This verse is evidence of the obligation to love God and His Messenger, and there is no disagreement about this among the Ummah, and that this takes precedence over everything beloved. The meaning of loving God and loving His Messenger has already been mentioned in Al Imran. And jihad in His cause, so wait is in the form of a command and its meaning is a threat. He says: Wait. Until God brings about His command meaning by fighting and conquering Mecca, according to Mujahid. Al Hasan: with a punishment, whether immediate or delayed. In His statement: And jihad in His cause is evidence of the virtue of jihad and preferring it over the comfort of the soul and its relationships with family and money. The virtue of jihad will come at the end of the surah. The rulings on women’s migration have already been mentioned sufficiently, praise be to God. In the authentic hadith: 3311 “The devil sits in wait for the son of Adam in three places: he sits in wait for him on the path of Islam and says: Why do you abandon your religion and the religion of your fathers? So he disobeyed him and became Muslim. He sits in wait for him on the path of migration and says: Are you abandoning your wealth and your family? So he disobeyed him and migrated. Then he sits in wait for him on the path of jihad and says: You will fight jihad and be killed, so your family will be married and your wealth will be divided. So he disobeyed him and fought jihad, so it is incumbent upon God to admit him to Paradise.” An-Nasa’i narrated it from the hadith of Sabrah ibn Abi Fakih who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The devil... and he mentioned him. Al-Bukhari said: Ibn al-Fakih, and he did not mention any difference in it. Ibn Abi ‘Uday said: It is said Ibn al-Fakih and Ibn Abi al-Fakih. End quote.
9:25: It contains eight issues: First: The Almighty said: God has already helped you in many battles. When Hawazin heard of the conquest of Mecca, Malik bin Auf Al-Nasri from Banu Nasr bin Malik gathered them together, and he was in charge of the entire army. He brought with him the infidels' wealth, livestock, women and children, and he claimed that this would protect them and strengthen their power in the battle. They were eight thousand, according to Al-Hasan and Mujahid. It was also said that they were four thousand from Hawazin and Thaqif. Malik bin Auf was in charge of Hawazin, and Kinanah bin Abd was in charge of Thaqif, so they camped in Awtas. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Abdullah bin Abi Hadrad Al-Aslami as a spy, so he came to him and informed him of what he had seen from them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, resolved to target them, and borrowed armor from Safwan bin Umayyah bin Khalaf Al-Jumahi. It was said that it was one hundred armors. It was also said that it was four hundred armors. He borrowed thirty or forty thousand from Rabi'ah Al-Makhzumi, and when he arrived, he paid him back. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “May God bless you in your family and your wealth. The reward for a loan is loyalty and praise.” Narrated by Ibn Majah in Sunan. 3312 The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with twelve thousand Muslims, ten thousand of whom accompanied him from Medina, and two thousand of the Muslims of the conquest, who were the freedmen, in addition to those who joined him from the Bedouins, from Sulaym, Banu Kalb, Abs, and Dhubyan. He appointed Atab ibn Asid over Mecca. On this departure, the ignorant Bedouins saw a green tree. They had a well-known tree in the pre-Islamic period called Dhat Anwat, and the infidels would go out to it on a specific day of the year, venerating it. They said: O Messenger of God, make for us a Dhat Anwat as they have a Dhat Anwat. So he, peace be upon him, said: "God is Great! You said - by Him in Whose Hand is my soul - as the people of Moses said: 'Make for us a god as they have gods.' He said: 'Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly. You will follow the ways of those before you, step by step, to the point that if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it.'" So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rose and came to the valley of Hunayn, which is one of the valleys of Tihamah. Hawazin had ambushed the sides of the valley, and that was in the dimness of dawn, so they attacked the Muslims as one man. The majority of the Muslims were defeated and no one looked back at the other. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood firm, and with him stood firm, Abu Bakr and Umar, and from his family Ali, Al-Abbas, Abu Sufyan ibn Al-Harith ibn Abdul Muttalib and his son Ja'far, Usama ibn Zaid, Ayman ibn Ubayd - who is Ayman ibn Umm Ayman, who was killed that day at Hunayn - Rabi'ah ibn Al-Harith, Al-Fadl ibn Abbas, and it was said in the place of Ja'far ibn Abi Sufyan: Qatham ibn Abbas. So these were ten men, and that is why Al-Abbas said: The Messenger of God helped us in the war nine times, and those who fled from him fled and were terrified. And he who lives with us encounters death himself, and what touches him for the sake of God does not suffer. Umm Sulaym stood firm with a group of those who stood firm, holding a camel belonging to Abu Talha and holding a dagger in her hand. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and none of them were defeated. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on his grey mule, whose name was Daldul. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas: 3313. Abbas said: I was holding the reins of the tongue of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) and restraining it so that it would not go too fast, and Abu Sufyan was holding the stirrup of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), so the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: O Abbas, call the people of the tamarisk tree. Abbas said - and he was a man with a loud voice. It is narrated that due to the intensity of his voice, he once raided Mecca and called out, Oh, morning! and every pregnant woman who heard his voice miscarried her fetus. So I said at the top of my voice: Where are the people of the tamarisk tree? He said: By God, when they heard my voice, their turning was like the turning of a cow to her young. They said: Here I am, here I am. He said: So they fought, and the infidels... The hadith. And in it: “He said: Then the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) took pebbles and threw them in the faces of the infidels.” Then he said: They are defeated, by the Lord of Muhammad. He said: So I went to look and saw the fighting as I had seen it. He said: By God, it was no sooner that he threw his pebbles at them than I could see their edge weakened and their matter running away. Abu Omar said: We have narrated from various sources on the authority of some of the polytheists who had witnessed Hunayn who had converted to Islam. He said - when he was asked about the day of Hunayn -: We met the Muslims and soon defeated them and pursued them until we reached a man riding on a white mule. When he saw us, he rebuked us and scolded us. He took pebbles and dirt in his hand and threw them and said: I saw the faces and there was not a single eye that did not get into it. We could not control ourselves but turned back on our heels. Saeed bin Jubair said: A man who was one of the polytheists told us on the day of Hunayn. He said: When we met the companions of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), they did not stop to milk a sheep for us. When we reached the owner of the gray mule - meaning the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) - we were met by men with white faces and handsome faces. They said to us: May your faces be disfigured, go back. So we went back and they mounted our shoulders and it was like that. He meant the angels. I said: There is no contradiction, because it is possible that the faces of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were distorted together, and it indicates that the angels fought on the day of Hunayn. And God knows best. And Ali may God be pleased with him killed forty men with his own hand on the day of Hunayn. And the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took four thousand heads as captives. And it was said: six thousand, and twelve thousand camels, in addition to what is not known of the spoils. Second: The scholars said about this raid: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever kills a person and has evidence against him, he is entitled to his spoils. This was explained in Al-Anfal. Ibn Al-Arabi said: For this reason and others, the legal scholars included this verse in the legal rulings. I said: It also includes the permissibility of borrowing weapons and the permissibility of enjoying what was borrowed if it is according to the customary practice of borrowing something similar to it, and the permissibility of the imam borrowing money when there is a need for that and returning it to its owner. The hadith of Safwan is the basis for this chapter. And in this raid: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) commanded: Do not have intercourse with a pregnant woman until she gives birth, nor with a menstruating woman until she menstruates. This indicates that captivity breaks the bond of kinship. This has been fully explained in Surat An-Nisa. In the hadith of Malik, Safwan went out with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) while he was a disbeliever, and he witnessed Hunayn and At-Ta’if, and his wife was a Muslim. The hadith. Malik said: This was not by the command of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and I do not see that polytheists should be helped unless they are servants or nannies. Abu Hanifa, Ash-Shafi’i, Ath-Thawri, and Al-Awza’i said: There is nothing wrong with that if the ruling of Islam is the predominant one, but it is disliked to seek their help if the ruling of polytheism is the predominant one. We have already discussed giving them shares in the spoils of war. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And the day of Hunayn. Hunayn is a valley between Mecca and Taif, and it was declined because it is a masculine noun, and this is the language of the Qur’an. Some Arabs do not decline it, making it the name of a place. And he recited: They supported their prophet and strengthened his resolve with Hanin on the day when heroes were helpless. And the word day is an adverb, and it is in the accusative case here to mean: And We gave you victory on the day of Hunayn. Al-Farra’ said: Mawātīn is not declined because it has no equivalent in the singular and it has no plural, except that the poet may be forced to do so and use the plural, and not everything that is permissible in speech is permissible in poetry. He recited: They chew on her iron Al-Nahhas said: I saw Abu Ishaq astonished by this. He said: He took Al-Khalil’s statement and made a mistake in it, because Al-Khalil says about it: It is not declined because it is a plural that has no equivalent in the singular, and it is not pluralized in the broken plural, but with the alif and the ta’ it is not impossible. Fourth: The Almighty said: When your great number pleased you. It was said: They were twelve thousand. It was said: Eleven thousand five hundred. It was said: Sixteen thousand. Some of them said: We will not be defeated today due to fewness. So they entrusted this word, and what we mentioned about the defeat in the beginning happened until they retreated, so victory and triumph were for the Muslims by the blessing of the Master of Messengers, may God bless him and grant him peace. So God Almighty made clear in this verse that victory is only by God’s victory, not by numbers. He said: And if He should forsake you, who is there that can support you after Him? (Al Imran 3:160). Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And the earth, vast as it is, has become strait for you, meaning from fear, as He said: As if the lands of God, which are wide, are for the fearful and wanted, a rope's scale. Al-Rahb with a damma on the ra’ means spaciousness. You say from it: So-and-so is spacious. Al-Rahb with a fatha: wide. You say from it: a spacious country, and a spacious land. And it was welcomed, welcomes, spaciousness and breadth. It was said that the ba’ means with, meaning with its spaciousness. It was also said that it means on, meaning on its spaciousness. It was also said that the meaning is with its spaciousness, so ma is a source. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Then you turned back, retreating. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq, who said: 3316 A man came to Al-Bara’ and said: Did you turn back on the day of Hunayn, O Abu ‘Ammarah? He said: I bear witness that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not turn back, but he went away hidden from the people and retreated to this tribe of Hawazin. They were a people of archers, so they shot them with a volley of arrows that looked like locusts, so they fled. The people came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Sufyan was leading his mule. He got down, supplicated and asked for help, saying: I am the Prophet, no lie. I am the son of ‘Abd al-Muttalib. O God, Your help has come down. Al-Bara’ said: By God, when the battle became fierce, we would seek protection from him, and the bravest of us was the one who stood next to him, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
9:26: Seventh - The Almighty said: Then God sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers meaning He sent down upon them what would calm them down and remove their fear, until they dared to fight the polytheists after they had turned away. And He sent down soldiers you did not see meaning the angels, who strengthen the believers with what they instill in their hearts of thoughts and confirmation, and weaken the disbelievers by cowardly approaching them from where they do not see them and without fighting, because the angels did not fight except on the day of Badr. It was narrated that "a man from Banu Nasr said to the believers after the fighting: Where are the piebald horses and the white men who were riding them? We were among them like a mole, and we were killed only by their hands. They informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, and he said: Those are the angels." And He punished those who disbelieved meaning with your swords. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
9:27: Then after that God wills to forgive whomever He wills meaning whoever was defeated and guides him to Islam, such as Malik ibn Auf al-Nasri, the chief of Hunayn, and those of his people who converted to Islam with him. Eighth - When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the spoils of war in Al-Juranah, a delegation of Hawazin came to him as Muslims, desiring to be kind to them and do good to them, and they said: "O Messenger of God, you are the best of people and the most pious of people, and you have taken our children, women and wealth. He said to them: I have been patient with you and the divisions have been made and I have those whom you see, and the best of words is the most truthful, so choose either your children or your wealth. They said: We will not be fair in anything to lineage. So he stood up and delivered a sermon and said: These people have come as Muslims and we have given them a choice, but they did not be fair in lineage, so they agreed to return the children, and what was mine and that of Banu Abd al-Muttalib and Banu Hashim is theirs. The Muhajirun and Ansar said: As for what was ours, it is for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Aqra’ bin Habis and Uyaynah bin Hisn among their people refused to return to them anything of what was in their shares. Al-Abbas bin Mirdas al-Sulami also refused, and hoped that his people would help him as Al-Aqra’ and Uyaynah had helped their people. Banu Sulaym refused and said: Rather, what was ours is for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever among you is stingy with what is in his hands, we will compensate him for it." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned their women and children to them, and compensated those who were not content to give up their share with compensations that they were satisfied with. Qatada said: “He told us about the wet-nurse of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who breastfed him from Banu Sa’d. She came to him on the day of Hunayn and asked him about the captives of Hunayn. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not own anything except what I get from them, but come to me tomorrow and ask me while the people are with me. When I give you my share, the people will give you. So she came the next day, so he spread out his garment for her and made her sit on it. Then she asked him and he gave her his share.
