When the people saw that, they gave her their shares. The number of the captives of Hawazin, according to Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, was six thousand heads. It was also said: four thousand. Abu ‘Umar said: Among them was al-Shima’, the foster sister of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was the daughter of al-Harith ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza from Banu Sa’d ibn Bakr and the daughter of Halima al-Sa’diyya. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, honored her and gave her and treated her well, and she returned to her country, happy with her religion and what God had bestowed upon her.” Ibn ‘Abbas said: “On the day of Awtas, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a woman running and screaming and not staying still. He asked about her and was told: She had lost a son of hers. Then he saw her find her son and kiss him and embrace him. He called her and said to his companions: Is this woman throwing her child into the fire? They said: No. He said: Why? They said: Because of her compassion. He said: God is more merciful to you than she is.” Muslim narrated it with the same meaning, and praise be to God.
9:28: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, indeed, the polytheists are unclean is a subject and a predicate. Scholars differed about the meaning of describing the polytheist as unclean. Qatada, Muammar ibn Rashid and others said: Because he is in a state of major ritual impurity, since washing him from major ritual impurity is not a ritual bath. Ibn Abbas and others said: Rather, the meaning of polytheism is that which makes him impure. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Whoever shakes hands with a polytheist should perform ablution. The entire school of thought is that a kafir must perform ablution if he converts to Islam, except Ibn Abd al-Hakam, who said: It is not obligatory, because Islam destroys what came before it. Abu Thawr and Ahmad said that a ritual bath is obligatory for him. Al-Shafi’i omitted it and said: I prefer that he perform a ritual bath. Ibn al-Qasim said something similar. Malik said: He does not know how to perform a ritual bath, as narrated by Ibn Wahb and Ibn Abi Uways. The hadith of Thamamah and Qays ibn Asim refutes these statements. They were narrated by Abu Hatim al-Busti in his Sahih Musnad: “And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Thamamah one day and he converted to Islam. So he sent him to the garden of Abu Talha and ordered him to bathe. So he bathed and prayed two rak’ahs. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your companion’s conversion to Islam has been good.” Muslim narrated it with the same meaning. And in it: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, bestowed his favor upon Thamamah, he went to a palm grove near the mosque and bathed. Qais ibn Asim was ordered to wash himself with water and lotus. If he converted to Islam before his wet dream, then washing himself is recommended. When he converted to Islam after reaching puberty, he must intend to wash himself with ritual impurity. This is the opinion of our scholars, and it is the conclusion of the school of thought. Ibn al-Qasim permitted the infidel to wash himself before declaring the testimony of faith with his tongue, if he believes in Islam in his heart. This is a weak opinion in view and contradicts the hadith. This is because no one becomes a Muslim by intention without speech. This is the opinion of the group of Ahl al-Sunnah regarding faith: it is speech with the tongue and belief in the heart, and it is purified by action. God the Almighty said: To Him ascends good words, and righteous action raises it. (Fatir
9:29: It contains fifteen issues: First: The Almighty said: Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day. When God Almighty forbade the infidels from approaching the Sacred Mosque, the Muslims felt in themselves because of what was cut off from them from the trade that the polytheists used to bring. God Almighty said: And if you fear poverty Al-Masjid Al-Haram, 19:10. As mentioned above. Then in this verse, He made the jizyah permissible, although it had not been taken before, so He made it a substitute for what prevented them from bringing their trade to the polytheists. God Almighty said: Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day Al-Masjid Al-Haram, 19:10. So God, the Almighty, commanded fighting all the infidels because they agreed to this description, and He mentioned the People of the Book specifically to honor their Book, and because they are knowledgeable about monotheism, the Messengers, the laws, and the religions, and especially to mention Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, his religion, and his nation. When they denied it, the argument was confirmed against them and the crime was great from them, so He pointed out their position and then made the fighting an end, which is to give the jizyah instead of killing. And this is correct. Ibn Arabi said: I heard Abu al-Wafa Ali ibn Aqil in a session of consideration reciting it and citing it as evidence. He said: Fight, which is an order for punishment. Then he said: Those who do not believe, which is a statement of the sin that necessitated the punishment. His statement: nor the Last Day, is an emphasis on the sin in terms of belief. Then he said: nor do they forbid what God and His Messenger have forbidden, an increase in the sin of violating actions. Then he said: nor do they follow the religion of truth, an indication of emphasis on the sin of deviation, obstinacy, and disdain for submission. Then he said: of those who were given the Scripture, as an emphasis on the argument, because they found it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. Then he said: until they pay the jizyah willingly, so he explained the extent to which the punishment extends, and specified the substitute by which it is lifted. Second: The scholars differed regarding who the jizya should be taken from. Al-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him said: The jizya is not accepted except from the People of the Book in particular, whether they are Arabs or non-Arabs, based on this verse. They are the ones who were specifically mentioned, so the ruling is directed towards them and not others, based on the words of God the Almighty: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). He did not say: until they pay the jizya, as He said about the People of the Book. He said: It is accepted from the Magians according to the Sunnah, and Ahmad and Abu Thawr said the same. It is the school of thought of Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa and his companions. Al-Awza’i said: The jizya is taken from every worshipper of idols or fire, or denier or disbeliever. The same is the school of thought of Malik, who saw that the jizya is taken from all types of polytheists and deniers, Arabs or non-Arabs, Taghlibis or Qurayshites, whoever they may be, except the apostate. Ibn Al-Qasim, Ashab and Sahnun said: The jizya is taken from the Magians of the Arabs and all nations. As for the idol worshippers among the Arabs, God did not establish a jizya for them, and none of them will remain on earth. Rather, they are entitled to fight or to convert to Islam. Ibn al-Qasim said: The jizya is taken from them, as Malik says. This is in the branching of Ibn al-Jalab, and it is a possibility, not a text. Ibn Wahb said: The jizya is not accepted from the Magians of the Arabs, but from others. He said: Because there is no Magian among the Arabs who did not all convert to Islam, so whoever is found among them to be contrary to Islam is an apostate, and is killed in all cases if he does not convert to Islam. The jizya is not accepted from them. Ibn al-Jahm said: The jizya is accepted from everyone who professes a religion other than Islam, except for those who are unanimously agreed upon by the infidels of Quraysh. He mentioned in explaining that it is an honor for them from humiliation and degradation, because of their status with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Another said: That is because they all converted to Islam on the day of the conquest of Mecca. And God knows best. Third: As for the Magians, Ibn al-Mundhir said: I do not know of any disagreement that the jizya should be taken from them. In al-Muwatta’: Malik, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father: “That Umar ibn al-Khattab mentioned the matter of the Magians and said: I do not know what to do with them. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Abu Omar said: He means in the jizya specifically. And in the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Treat them as the people of the Book do,” is evidence that they are not people of the Book. And the majority of jurists agree with this. It was narrated from Al-Shafi’i that they were people of the Book and then changed. And I think that he went in that to something narrated from Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, from a weak source, which revolves around Abu Sa’id Al-Baqal, mentioned by Abd Al-Razzaq and others. Ibn Atiyyah said: It was narrated that a prophet named Zoroaster was sent among the Magians. And God knows best. Fourth: God Almighty did not mention in His Book the amount of the jizya taken from them. Scholars differed regarding the amount of the jizya taken from them. Ata bin Abi Rabah said: There is no time limit for it, but it is based on what they agreed upon. Yahya bin Adam, Abu Ubaid, and al-Tabari said the same, except that al-Tabari said: The minimum is a dinar, and there is no limit to more. They cited as evidence what the people of Sahih narrated on the authority of Amr bin Awf: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made peace with the people of Bahrain regarding the jizya. Al-Shafi’i said: A dinar for the rich and the poor from among the free adults, without any reduction from it. He cited as evidence what was narrated by Abu Dawud and others on the authority of Muadh: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) sent him to Yemen and ordered him to take a dinar from every adult as a tribute. Ash-Shafi'i said: This is the clear meaning of God Almighty. It is the saying of Abu Thawr. Ash-Shafi'i said: If they reach an agreement on more than one dinar, it is permissible, and if they increase and are happy with that, it is accepted from them. If they reach an agreement on hospitality for three days, it is permissible, if the hospitality is known in bread, barley, straw and condiments, and he mentioned what is required of the average person and what is required of the wealthy person, and he mentioned the place of descent and protection from cold and heat. Malik said, as narrated by Ibn al-Qasim, Ashab and Muhammad ibn al-Harith ibn Zanjawayh: It is four dinars for the people of gold and forty dirhams for the people of silver, the rich and the poor alike, even if he is a Zoroastrian. It is not to be increased or decreased from what 'Umar imposed, and nothing more is to be taken from them. It has been said: The weak person is to be relieved according to what the Imam sees fit. Ibn al-Qasim said: Nothing is to be decreased from 'Umar's imposed due to hardship, nor is it to be increased due to wealth. Abu Omar said: It is taken from their poor what they can bear, even if it is one dirham. Malik adopted this view. Abu Hanifa and his companions, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: Twelve, twenty-four, and forty. Al-Thawri said: There are different taxes reported from Omar ibn al-Khattab regarding this, so the governor can take whichever he wants, if they are people of the covenant. As for the people of peace, they are to take whatever they have agreed upon and nothing more. Fifth: Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: What the Qur’an indicates is that the jizya is taken from male fighters, because God the Almighty said: Fight those until His saying - until they give the jizya. This necessitates that it is obligatory on those who fight. It also indicates that it is not on slaves, even if they are fighters, because they do not have money, and because God the Almighty said: until they give. It is not said of those who do not own property until they give. This is a consensus among scholars that the jizya is only imposed on the skulls of free adult men, who are those who fight, excluding women, children, slaves, the insane who are mentally unstable, and the elderly. There is a difference of opinion regarding monks. Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik that it is not taken from them. Mutraf and Ibn al-Majishun said: This is if he did not become a monk after it was made obligatory. If it was made obligatory and then he became a monk, his monasticism does not cancel it. Sixth: If the people of the jizyah pay the jizyah, nothing is taken from them of their fruits, trade, or crops, unless they trade in a country other than the country in which they settled and reached a settlement. If they leave the country in which they settled to another as traders, a tenth is taken from them if they sell and the price of that is paid by their hands, even if it is done several times a year, except in the case of their carrying food, wheat, and oil to Madinah and Makkah in particular, then a tenth is taken from the people of the dhimmah on their trade except once a year, like what is taken from the Muslims. This is the doctrine of Omar bin Abdul Aziz and a group of the Imams of the jurists. The first is the opinion of Malik and his companions. Seventh: If the people of the jizyah pay the jizyah that was imposed on them or they reach a settlement over it, they are left with all their wealth, and with their vineyards and their presses, as long as they cover their wines and do not announce their sale to a Muslim, and they are prevented from displaying wine and pork in the markets of the Muslims. If they display any of that, the wine is poured out on them, and whoever displays the pork is disciplined. If a Muslim pours it out without displaying it, he has transgressed, and he must guarantee it. It was said: It is not obligatory, and if he usurps it, he must return it. They are not to be interfered with in their rulings or in their trade among themselves by usury. If they refer it to the judge, the judge has a choice. If he wishes, he may rule between them according to what God has revealed, or he may turn away from it. It was said: He may rule between them in injustices in any case, and some of their food is taken for the weak, because it is a way of defending them. The imam must fight their enemy on their behalf and seek their help in fighting them. They have no share in the spoils of war, and they did not increase what they agreed upon of the churches, and they were not prevented from repairing what was damaged in them, and they have no way to create others. They take from the clothing and appearance what distinguishes them from the Muslims, and they are forbidden from resembling the people of Islam. There is no harm in buying the children of the enemy from them if they do not have a covenant with them. And whoever is stubborn in paying his jizya will be disciplined for his stubbornness and it will be taken from him humiliated. Eighth - The scholars differed about what the jizya is obligatory for. The Maliki scholars said: It is obligatory in lieu of killing due to disbelief. Al-Shafi’i said: It is obligatory in lieu of blood and residence in the house. The benefit of the disagreement is that if we say it is obligatory in lieu of killing and he converts to Islam, the jizya is dropped for what has passed. If he converts to Islam one day before the year is complete or after it, according to Malik. According to Al-Shafi’i, it is a debt that is established in the conscience and Islam does not drop it, like the rent of a house. Some Hanafis agreed with our opinion. Some of them said: It is obligatory in lieu of victory and jihad. Judge Abu Zaid chose this and claimed that it was the secret of God in the matter. Malik’s opinion is more correct, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There is no jizyah on a Muslim. Sufyan said: Its meaning is that if a dhimmi converts to Islam after the jizyah has become obligatory on him, it is no longer obligatory on him. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud. Our scholars said: This is indicated by the words of God the Almighty: until they pay the jizyah willingly while they are subdued, because this meaning disappears with Islam. There is no disagreement that if they convert to Islam, they do not pay the jizyah willingly while they are subdued. Al-Shafi’i does not take it after Islam in the manner that God the Almighty said. Rather, he says: The jizyah is a debt, which was made obligatory on him for a previous reason, which is housing or avoiding the evil of being killed, so it became like all debts. Ninth: If the Imam made a covenant with the people of a town or fortress, then they broke their covenant and refused to pay the jizya and other things that were required of them, and refused the rule of Islam without being wronged, and the Imam was not unjust to them, then it is obligatory for the Muslims to invade them and fight them with their Imam. If they fight and are victorious, then the ruling on them is the same as the ruling in the land of war. It has been said: They and their women are spoils of war and there is no fifth on them, and this is a school of thought. Tenth: If they go out stealthily and highway robbers, they are in the same position as Muslim combatants if they do not refuse to pay the jizya. If they go out complaining, their case will be looked into and they will be returned to the covenant and treated fairly by their oppressor. None of them will be enslaved and they will be free. If some of them break the covenant but not others, then whoever does not break it is bound by his covenant, and no one will be held accountable for the breach of another. Their remaining in the covenant will be known by their denunciation of the breakers. Eleventh - The jizya is of the same weight as fa`lah, from the root jaza yajzi, meaning to repay for what was given to him. So it is as if they gave it as a reward for the security they were granted, and it is like sitting and sitting. And from this meaning is the saying of the poet: He rewards you or praises you. Whoever praises you for what you have done is like someone who has rewarded you. Twelfth - Muslim narrated on the authority of Hisham bin Hakim bin Hizam, who passed by some Nabataeans in the Levant who had been made to stand in the sun - in one narration: and oil had been poured on their heads - and he said: What is the matter with them? He said: They are being held back for the jizya. Hisham said: I bear witness that I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God punishes those who punish people in this world. In another narration: Their emir at that time was Umair bin Saad in Palestine. He entered upon him and spoke to him, so he ordered them to be released. Our scholars said: As for punishing them if they refuse to pay it with empowerment, then it is permissible. However, if their inability is proven, then punishing them is not permissible, because whoever is unable to pay the jizya is exempted from it. And the rich are not required to pay it on behalf of the poor. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Safwan bin Salim on the authority of several of the sons of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of their fathers that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wrongs a covenantor, or diminishes his rights, or burdens him beyond his capacity, or takes something from him against his will, I will be his opponent on the Day of Resurrection. Thirteenth - The Almighty said: By hand. Ibn Abbas said: He pays it himself without appointing anyone to do so. Abu Al-Bukhtari narrated on the authority of Salman who said: Blameworthy. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: By force. It was said: By hand, by a favor from you to them, because if you take the jizyah from them, then you have bestowed that favor upon them. Ikrimah: He pays it while standing and the taker is sitting. Saeed bin Jubair said the same. Ibn Arabi: This is not from his saying: By hand, but rather it is from his saying: and they are humbled. Fourteenth - The Imams narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The upper hand is better than the lower hand. The upper hand is the one that gives and the lower hand is the one that takes.” It was also narrated, The upper hand is the one that gives. So He made the hand of the giver in charity upper, and He made the hand of the giver in jizyah lower. And the hand of the taker is upper, because He is the One who raises and lowers. He raises whomever He wills and lowers whomever He wills. There is no god but Him. Fifteenth - On the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, he said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: The people of the land are unable to pay the tax. Should I cultivate it, farm it, and pay its tax? He said: No. Another man came to him and said that to him. He said: No, and he recited the words of God the Almighty: Fight those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day until His saying: and they are humiliated. Would any of you deliberately humiliate someone by snatching him and putting him around his neck? Kulayb bin Wa’il said: I said to Ibn Omar: I bought land. He said: The purchase is good. I said: I give for every yard of land a dirham and a bushel of food. He said: Do not put humiliation around your neck. Maymun bin Mihran narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with them both, that he said: I would not be pleased to have the entire land for a tax of five dirhams, in which I acknowledge humiliation upon myself.
9:30: It contains seven issues: First: Asim and Al-Kisa’i read ‘Uzair ibn God with the tanween of ‘Uzair. The meaning is that ‘ibn’ according to this is the predicate of ‘Uzair, and ‘Uzair is declined whether it is a foreign or Arabic word. Ibn Kathir, Nafi’, Abu ‘Amr and Ibn ‘Amir read ‘Uzair ibn without the tanween because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. This is the reading of those who read “Say: He is God, the One * God, the Self-Sufficient” (al-Ikhla 112:1-2). Abu ‘Ali said: It is common in poetry. Al-Tabari recited in this regard: You will find me on the ground with the prince and trampled on by the canal If the peaceful one is covered, he will flee Second: The Almighty’s statement: And the Jews said This is a statement that is general in meaning but its meaning is specific, because not all Jews said that. This is similar to the statement of the Almighty: Those to whom the people said (Al Imran 3:173), and not all people said that. It was said: The one who said what was narrated about the Jews was Salam bin Mishkam, Nu’man bin Abi Awfa, Shas bin Qais, and Malik bin Al-Saif, they said it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Naqqash said: There is no Jew left who said it, rather they became extinct, so if one person said it, then it is appropriate for the group to be bound by the heinousness of the statement, because of the nobility of the one who said it about them. The statements of the noble are always famous among the people and are used as evidence. From here it is correct for the group to say the statement of its prophet. And God knows best. It has been narrated that the reason for that statement is that the Jews killed the prophets after Moses, peace be upon him, so God lifted the Torah from them and erased it from their hearts, so Ezra went out wandering in the earth, and Gabriel came to him and said: Where are you going? He said: I seek knowledge, so he taught him the entire Torah, so Ezra brought the Torah to the Children of Israel and taught them. It was said: Rather, God preserved it for Ezra as an honor from Him, so he said to the Children of Israel: God has preserved the Torah for me, so they began to study it from Him. The Torah was buried, their scholars had buried it when they were afflicted with tribulations, exile and disease, and Nebuchadnezzar killed them. Then the buried Torah was found and it was equal to what Ezra was studying, so they went astray at that and said, this was not prepared for Ezra except that he is the son of God, narrated by Al-Tabari. The apparent statement of the Christians that the Messiah is the son of God, they only meant the sonship of the lineage, as the Arabs said about the angels. This is also required by the statement of Ad-Dahhak, At-Tabari and others. This is the most heinous disbelief. Abu Al-Ma’ali said: The Christians agreed that the Messiah is a god and that he is the son of a god. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is said that some of them believe it is a sonship of compassion and mercy. This meaning also does not allow for the sonship to be attributed to him, and this is blasphemy. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: This is evidence from the words of our Lord, the Blessed and Most High, that whoever reports the disbelief of another, which no one is permitted to initiate, there is no blame upon him, because he only speaks about it in the sense of reverence for it and refuting it, and if our Lord had willed, no one would have spoken about it. So if He has enabled tongues to speak about it, then He has permitted reporting about it, in the sense of denying it with the heart and tongue, and refuting it with argument and proof. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: That is what they say with their mouths. It was said: Its meaning is emphasis, as the Almighty said: They write the Book with their hands (al-Baqarah 2:79) and His statement: Nor a bird that flies with its wings (al-An’am 6:38) and His statement: Then when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast (al-Haqqah 69:13) and the like. It was said: The meaning is that since it is the statement of a simpleton with no clarification or proof, but rather it is a statement by the mouth, a mere claim with no meaning behind it, it is correct, because they acknowledge that God Almighty has not taken a wife, so how can they claim that He has a son? It is a lie and a statement of the tongue only, unlike the correct statements that are refuted by evidence and supported by proof. The scholars of meaning said: God Almighty did not mention a statement that was accompanied by mouths and tongues except that it was a false statement, such as His statement: They say with their mouths what is not in their hearts (Al Imran 3:167) and “A grave word is it that comes out of their mouths. They say nothing but a lie” (Al Kahf: 5) and They say with their tongues what is not in their hearts (Al Fath: 11). Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: They imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before. They imitate, they resemble, and from this comes the saying of the Arabs: a woman who does not menstruate or who has no breasts, as if she resembles men. And the scholars have three sayings regarding the saying of those who disbelieved: The first: the saying of the idol worshippers: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza, and Manat, the third other. The second: the saying of the infidels: the angels are daughters of God. The third: the saying of their ancestors, so they imitated them in falsehood and followed them in disbelief, as He informed us about them in His saying, the Almighty: Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion (al-Zukhruf 43:22). Sixth - Scholars differed on whether to pronounce the word Dhya’a in the long vowel or not. Ibn Walad said: A woman who does not menstruate is a woman who is not menstruating, with a hamza but not a long vowel. Some of them pronounce it in the long vowel, and this is Sibawayh, who makes it in the form of fa’laa with a long vowel, and the hamza in it is extra, because they say nisa’a Dhya, and they delete the hamza. Abu al-Hasan said: An-Najirmi told me: Dhya’a with a long vowel and the ha’. It combines two signs of femininity, as he narrated from Ibn Amr al-Shaibani in al-Nawadir. He recited: Barren or inanimate Ibn Atiyah: Whoever says: They imitate is taken from their saying: A woman with a radiant complexion, then his statement is wrong, Abu Ali said, because the hamza in dahā’ is original, and in dahā’ it is extra like hamra’. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: May God curse them, how they are deluded. That is, may God curse them, meaning the Jews and Christians, because the cursed is like the killed. Ibn Jurayj said: May God curse them means astonishment. Ibn Abbas said: Everything in the Qur’an that is killed is a curse, and from this is the saying of Aban ibn Taghlib: May God kill her, she insulted me, and she knew that I was the one who corrupted and reformed myself. Al-Naqqash narrated that the origin of Qatal God is supplication, then they used it so much that they said it to express astonishment about good and evil, and they did not mean supplication. Al-Asma’i recited: Oh God, kill Laila. How can I please you while I tell people that I don’t care about her?
9:31: The Almighty said: They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah, the son of Mary. Ahbar is the plural of habbar, which is the one who speaks well, organizes it, and perfects it with good expression. And from this comes the word thawb muhbar, meaning the plural of adornment. It has been said about one of the ahbar: habbar with a kasra on the ha. The commentators say it with a fatha, and the linguists say it with a kasra. Yunus said: I have not heard it except with a kasra on the ha, and the evidence for that is that they said: madad habbar, meaning the ink of a scholar, then the usage became widespread until they said for the ink habbar. Al-Farraa said: kasra and fatha are two languages. Ibn al-Sikkit said: habbar with a kasra is ink, and habbar with a fatha is the scholar. And monks are the plural of monk, taken from awe, which is the one who fears God Almighty to be sincere in intention to Him without people, and to devote his time to Him, his work to Him, and his enjoyment with Him. The Almighty said: Lords besides God. The scholars of meaning said: They made their rabbis and monks like lords since they obeyed them in everything. From this is the Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘Blow,’ until when he had made it a fire (al-Kahf 18:96) meaning like fire. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Did anyone corrupt the religion except the kings, the bad rabbis, and the monks? Al-A'mash and Sufyan narrated on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari who said: Hudhayfah was asked about the statement of God Almighty: They have taken their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God. Did they worship them? He said: No, but they made lawful for them what was unlawful so they made it lawful, and they made unlawful for them what was lawful so they made it unlawful. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Adi bin Hatim who said: “I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I had a cross of gold around my neck. He said: What is this, O Adi? Throw away this idol. I heard him recite in Surat Bara’ah: They have taken their rabbis and monks as lords besides God, and the Messiah, son of Mary. Then he said: They did not worship them, but when they made something lawful for them, they considered it lawful, and when they made something unlawful for them, they considered it unlawful.” He said: This is a strange hadith that is only known through the hadith of Abd al-Salam ibn Harb. Ghutayf ibn A’yan is not well-known in hadith. The Almighty’s saying: And the Messiah, the son of Mary. The discussion of its derivation has already been mentioned in Al Imran. Messiah is the sweat flowing from the forehead. Some of the later scholars did well and said: Be happy, for you will be familiar with sorrows when you witness the resurrection and the scales. And Christ flowed from your forehead like flowing streams. And he continued in the women the meaning of adding it to his mother Mary.
9:32: The Almighty said: They want to extinguish the light of God meaning His evidence and proofs of His Oneness. He made the proofs like light because of the clarity they contain. It was said: The meaning is the light of Islam, meaning that they extinguish the religion of God by their denial. With their mouths is the plural of fuwwah according to the original, because the original in mouth is fuwwah, like hawd and hawds. And God refuses except to perfect His light It is said: How did you enter except when there is no particle of negation in the speech, and it is not permissible to hit except Zayd. Al-Farra' claimed that except only entered because there is an end of denial in the speech. Al-Zajjaj said: Denial and verification do not have ends. The tools of denial are: ma, la, in, and laysa, and these do not have ends that are pronounced with them, and if the matter was as he wanted, it would have been permissible to hate except Zayd, but the answer is that the Arabs delete with abi. The meaning is: And God refuses everything except to perfect His light. Ali bin Suleiman said: This is permissible in the case of ‘Abi’ because it is a prohibition or refusal, so it is similar to negation. Al-Nahhas said: This is good, as the poet said: And do I have another mother if I leave her? God wills that I be her only son.
9:33: The Almighty said: It is He who has sent His Messenger meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. With guidance meaning with the Criterion. And the religion of truth that He may make it prevail over all religion meaning with argument and proofs. And He made it prevail over the laws of religion so that nothing of it would be hidden from Him, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It was said: To make it prevail means to make the religion of Islam prevail over all religions. Abu Hurairah and Ad-Dahhak said: This is when Jesus, peace be upon him, descends. As-Suddi said: That is when the Mahdi emerges, no one will remain who has not entered Islam or paid the jizyah. It was said: The Mahdi is Jesus only, and this is incorrect, because the authentic narrations have been transmitted in succession that the Mahdi is from the family of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it is not permissible to apply it to Jesus. The hadith that was reported in which he said: There is no Mahdi except Jesus is not correct. Al-Bayhaqi said in the book of Baath and Resurrection. Because its narrator is Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Jundi, who is unknown. He narrates on the authority of Abaan ibn Abi Ayyash - who is rejected - on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is disconnected. The hadiths before it that explicitly state the emergence of the Mahdi, and in them is a statement that the Mahdi is from the family of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have more authentic chains of transmission. I said: We have mentioned this and added more clarification in our book The Book of Remembrance and we have mentioned the report of the Mahdi in full, praise be to God. It was said that he meant to make him prevail over all religions in the Arabian Peninsula, and he did so.
9:34: It contains eleven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: To devour the wealth of people unjustly. The lam is used on the verb yaf’ala and does not enter on the verb fa’ala because it is similar to the nouns yaf’ala. The rabbis are the scholars of the Jews. The monks are the Christians who strive hard in worship. It was said that they used to take taxes and duties from the wealth of their followers in the name of churches and churches and other things, which they would make them believe that spending on it is from the Sharia and to curry favor with God the Almighty. During that, they would withhold that wealth, like what Salman al-Farsi mentioned about the monk who extracted his treasure, mentioned by Ibn Ishaq in al-Seer. It was also said that they used to take taxes from their crops and wealth in the name of protecting the religion and implementing the Sharia. It was also said that they used to accept bribes in rulings, as many governors and rulers do today. His saying: unjustly includes all of that. And they hinder [people] from the path of God means they prevent the people of their religion from entering the religion of Islam and following Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And those who hoard gold and silver. The root of the word treasure in the language is to gather and to pluralize, and it is not limited to gold and silver. Do you not see his saying, peace be upon him: “Shall I not tell you of the best thing a man can treasure: a righteous woman.” That is, by adding it to himself and gathering it together. He said: And she was not provided with all the treasure except threads and thread of rags. Another said: I don't know if I feed their hungry ones even if I have stored up wheat Qarf al-Hati is the barley gruel. He says: He stayed with a people and his hospitality was to them, the barley gruel, which is al-Hati. When they stayed with him, he said: May you not have a pearl... the house. Gold and silver were mentioned specifically because they are not seen, unlike other wealth. Al-Tabari said: A treasure is anything that is gathered together, whether in the depths of the earth or on its surface. Gold was called gold because it disappears, and silver because it is shaken and dispersed, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: They dispersed to it (al-Jumuah 62:11) - They would have dispersed from around you (Al Imran 3:159). This meaning was mentioned in Al-Imran. Third: The companions differed about what was meant by this verse. Muawiyah thought that it meant the People of the Book, and Al-Asamm thought the same, because his statement: And those who hoard is mentioned after his statement: Indeed, many of the rabbis and monks devour the wealth of people unjustly. Abu Dharr and others said: What is meant by it are the People of the Book and other Muslims. This is correct, because if he had meant the People of the Book specifically, he would have said: and hoard, without and those. So when he said: and those, he started a new meaning that clarifies that he connected one sentence to another. So those who hoard is a new statement, and it is raised as a subject. Al-Suddi said: He meant the people of the Qiblah. So these are three opinions. According to the statement of the companions, it is evidence that the infidels are addressed in their view with the branches of the Shari’ah. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Wahb, who said: I passed by Ar-Rabdhah and there I met Abu Dharr and said to him: What brought you to this place? He said: I was in Ash-Sham and Muawiyah and I differed about {And those who hoard gold and silver and spend it not in the way of God}. Muawiyah said: It was revealed about the People of the Scripture. I said: It was revealed about us and them, and there was a dispute between me and him about that. He wrote to Uthman complaining about me, so Uthman wrote to me to go to Madinah, so I went and the people crowded around me as if they had never seen me before. I mentioned that to Uthman and he said: If you wish I can move away and be close, and that is what brought me to this place, and if they had appointed an Abyssinian over me I would have listened and obeyed. Fourth: Ibn Khuwayzmandad said: This verse includes zakat on money, and it is obligatory with four conditions: freedom, Islam, a year, and a minimum amount of money free from debt. The minimum amount is two hundred dirhams or twenty dinars. Or the minimum amount of one of them is completed by the other. A quarter of a tenth is taken from this and a quarter of a tenth is taken from this. We said that freedom is a condition because the slave lacks ownership. We said that Islam is a condition because zakat is a purification and the infidel is not purified, and because God the Almighty said: And establish prayer and give zakat (al-Baqarah 2:43), so the one who was addressed with prayer was addressed with zakat. We said that a year is polytheism because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no zakat on wealth until a year has passed. We only said that the minimum amount is a condition because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no zakat on less than two hundred dirhams, and there is no zakat on less than twenty dinars. The completion of the nisab is not taken into consideration at the beginning of the year, but rather it is taken into consideration at the end of the year, because they agreed that the profit is subject to the ruling of the original. Evidence for this is that if someone has two hundred dirhams and trades with them, and at the end of the year it becomes a thousand, he must pay zakat on the thousand, and he does not start a new year for the profit. If this is the case, the ruling on the profit does not differ, whether it was issued from the nisab or less. They also agreed that if he had forty sheep, and they gave birth at the beginning of the year, then the mothers died except for one of them, and the young goats were the completion of the nisab, then zakat is paid from them. Fifth: Scholars differed about the money whose zakat has been paid, is it called a treasure or not? Some people said: Yes. Abu Ad-Dhaha narrated it on the authority of Jahda bin Hubayrah on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him. Ali said: Four thousand or less is a provision, and whatever is more is a treasure even if its zakat has been paid, but this is not correct. Some people said: Whatever its zakat has been paid from it or from someone else on its behalf is not a treasure. Ibn Omar said: Whatever its zakat has been paid is not a treasure even if it is under seven earths, and everything whose zakat has not been paid is a treasure even if it is above the earth. The same was narrated on the authority of Jabir, and this is correct. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever God gives wealth to, and he does not pay its zakat, it will be presented to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald-headed serpent with two tufts of hair. It will encircle him on the Day of Resurrection, then seize him by his two jaws and say, ‘I am your wealth, I am your treasure.’” Then he recited, And let not those who are stingy think (Al Imran 3:180), the verse. And in it also on the authority of Abu Dharr, he said: I went to him - meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - and he said: “By Him in Whose Hand is my soul - or by Him besides Whom there is no god - or as he swore - no man who has camels, cows or sheep and does not pay their dues will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with them as big and fat as they can be, trampling him with their lightest ones and butting him with their horns. Whenever the last one passes, the first one returns to him until judgment is passed between the people.” The evidence of the discourse of these two hadiths indicates the correctness of what we have mentioned. Ibn Umar explained this meaning in Sahih al-Bukhari. A Bedouin said to him: Tell me about the statement of God the Most High: And those who hoard gold and silver. Ibn Umar said: Whoever hoards it and does not pay its zakat, woe to him. This was before zakat was revealed, but when it was revealed, God made it a purification for wealth. It was also said: Hoarding is what is in excess of need. It was narrated from Abu Dharr, and it is among what was transmitted from his school of thought, and it is among his most severe and what he alone narrated, may God be pleased with him. I said: It is possible that the summary of what was narrated from Abu Dharr in this regard is that the verse was revealed at a time of great need, weakness of the emigrants, and the inability of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to provide for them, and there was not enough in the treasury for them, and the years of calamities were attacking them, so they were forbidden to keep anything of the money except what was needed, and it is not permissible to save gold and silver at such a time. So when God opened up to the Muslims and made things easy for them, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made it obligatory for them to give five dirhams for two hundred dirhams, and half a dinar for twenty dinars, and he did not make it obligatory for all of them, and he considered the period of masturbation, so that was a clarification from him (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It was said: Treasure is that from which urgent rights have not been paid, such as freeing a prisoner, feeding the hungry, and other things. It was said: Treasure in language is the sum of the two currencies, and other money is applied to them by analogy. It was said: The sum of them is that which is not jewelry, because jewelry is permitted to be taken and there is no right to it. What is correct is what we began by mentioning, and that all of that is called treasure in language and in Sharia. And God knows best. Sixth: Scholars differed regarding the zakat on jewelry. Malik and his companions, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, and Abu Ubaid held that there is no zakat on it. This is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i in Iraq, and he later stopped in Egypt and said: I seek God’s guidance regarding it. Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa and his companions, and Al-Awza’i said: There is zakat on all of that. The first scholars argued and said: The intention of growth requires zakat on merchandise, which is not the subject of zakat. Abu Hanifa argued with the generality of the words regarding the obligation of zakat on both types of cash, and he did not differentiate between jewelry and other things. Al-Layth ibn Sa’d made a distinction and required zakat on what was made into jewelry to avoid zakat, and he dropped it on what was worn or loaned. There are details regarding jewelry in the doctrine, which are explained in the books of branches. Seventh: Abu Dawood narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: And those who hoard gold and silver, he said: This was hard on the Muslims. Umar said: I will relieve you. He went and said: O Prophet of God, this verse was hard on your companions. He said: God did not impose zakat except to purify what remains of your wealth, and He only imposed inheritances - and he mentioned one word - to be for those who come after you. Umar said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Shall I not tell you of the best thing that a man hoards? A righteous woman, when he looks at her she pleases him, when he commands her she obeys him, and when he is away from her she guards him. At-Tirmidhi and others narrated on the authority of Thawban that the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God the Almighty has condemned gold and silver. If only we knew which money is best, we would earn it. Omar said: I will ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for you. So he asked him and he said: A tongue that remembers God, a heart that is grateful, and a wife who helps a man in his religion. He said: A good hadith. Eighth - The Almighty's saying: And they do not spend it in the way of God and did not say they spend them both, so there are six answers to this: First - Ibn Al-Anbari said: He meant the most common and general, which is silver. Similar to this is His saying: And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult (al-Baqarah 2:45) He returned the metaphor to prayer because it is more general. Similar to this is: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it (Al-Jumu'ah: 11) He returned the ha to the transaction because it is more important, and left amusement, as many commentators said. Some of them rejected it and said: It does not resemble it, because or has separated the transaction from amusement, so it is good to return the pronoun to one of them. Second - The opposite, which is that they spend it for the gold and the second is conjoined to it. The Arabs feminize gold, they say: it is red gold. It can be masculine, but the feminine is more common. Third - That the pronoun refers to the treasures. Fourth - To the treasured money. Fifth - To the zakat, the meaning is and they do not spend the zakat of the treasured money. Sixth: Sufficiency with the pronoun of one instead of the pronoun of the other if the meaning is understood. This is common in the speech of the Arabs. Sibawayh recited: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs Radwan did not say. Another said: He accused me of something that my father and I were innocent of, and for the sake of the long term he accused me of it He did not say innocent. Similar to this is the statement of Hassan bin Thabit, may God be pleased with him: The crack of youth and black hair, unless disobeyed, is madness. He did not say disobedient. Ninth: If it is said: Whoever does not hoard and does not spend in the way of God, but spends in sins, is his ruling in terms of the threat the same as the ruling of someone who hoards and does not spend in the way of God? It is said to him: That is more severe, because whoever squanders his money in sins has disobeyed in two ways: by spending and consuming, such as buying and drinking alcohol. Rather, in two ways if the sin is one that is transgressed, such as someone who helps in oppressing a Muslim by killing him or taking his money or something else. The hoarder has disobeyed in two ways, which are by withholding zakat and withholding the money, nothing more. And withholding the money may not be taken into consideration, and God knows best. Tenth - The Almighty’s saying: Then give them tidings of a painful punishment. The meaning of this has already been presented. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained this punishment by saying: The hoarders will be given glad tidings of a weeping on their backs that will come out of their sides, and a weeping on the nape of their necks that will come out of their foreheads. Narrated by Muslim. Narrated by Abu Dharr in one narration: “The hoarders will be given glad tidings of a hot coal that will be placed on the top of one’s breast until it comes out of the crease of his shoulder, and it will be placed on the crease of his shoulder until it comes out of the nipple of his breast, and he will shake.” Our scholars said: The coming out of the coal from the nipple of his breast to the crease of his shoulder is to torment his heart and his stomach when he is filled with joy at the abundance of wealth and happiness in this world, so he will be punished in the Hereafter with worry and torment. Eleventh - Our scholars said: The apparent meaning of the verse is that the threat is attached to the one who hoards and does not spend in the way of God, and exposes himself to the obligatory and other things. However, the description of the hoard should not be taken into consideration, for the one who does not hoard and prevents spending in the way of God must be like that. However, the one who hides under the ground is the one who prevents spending it on obligatory things according to custom, and therefore the threat was specifically directed at him. And God knows best.
9:35: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell. Day is a circumstantial phrase, and the meaning is they will be tormented on the Day when it will be heated. It is not correct to say: So give them good tidings on the Day when it will be heated, because good tidings will not be given then. It is said: The iron was heated in the fire, meaning it was lit, and it is said: I heated it, but it is not said: I heated it. Here he said on it, because he made on the meaning of heating, and the meaning of heating is ignition. That is, it is lit and cauterized. Cauterization: sticking hot iron or fire to a limb until the skin burns. The foreheads are the plural of forehead, and it is the level between the eyebrow and the forelock. I faced someone with such-and-such, meaning I faced him with it and struck his forehead. The junub is the plural of janub. Cauterization is more famous and more hideous in the face, and in the flank and back it is more painful and hurtful, so he mentioned them specifically from among the other limbs. The Sufi scholars said: When they sought wealth and prestige, God disfigured their faces. When they turned away from the poor when they sat with them, He blackened their sides. When they leaned their backs on their wealth, trusting in it and relying on it, He blackened their backs. The scholars of the apparent meaning said: These parts were singled out because when the rich saw the poor, he lowered his eyes and shriveled his face. As He said: Yazid turns a blind eye to me as if he saw the cupping between his eyes Do not let what is hidden appear before your eyes, and do not meet me except with your nose downcast. If he asks him, he folds his flank, and if he asks him too much, he turns his back. So God has ordained punishment for the state of disobedience. Second: The narrations differed regarding the method of cauterization. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Abu Dharr, there is what we mentioned about the mention of the cauterization. And in it, from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, he said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no owner of gold or silver who does not pay its dues, but that on the Day of Resurrection, plates of fire will be beaten out for him and heated in the fire of Hell and his sides, forehead and back will be branded with them. Whenever they cool, they will be given to him in a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the servants and he will see his path, either to Paradise or to Hell.” The hadith. In Bukhari: That his treasure will be presented to him as a bald-headed snake. It was previously mentioned in other than Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud that he said: Whoever has wealth and does not pay its zakat, on the Day of Resurrection, a bald-headed snake will be hung around his neck, pecking at its head. I said: Perhaps this occurs in some situations: one situation in which money is represented as a snake, another situation in which it is plates, and another situation in which it is bruises. So the characteristics change but the physicality is the same, so the brave man is a body and money is a body. This representation is true, unlike his saying: Death will be brought as if it were a white ram, for that is another way, and God, the Most High, can do whatever He wills. He specifically mentioned the brave because he is the second enemy of creation. The brave among snakes is the male snake that jumps on the rider and the foot, and stands on its tail and may reach the rider, and is found in the deserts. It was also said that it is the serpent. Al-Lahiani said: The snake is called brave, and three brave, then brave. The bald among snakes is the one whose head is swollen and white from the poison. In Al-Muwatta: It has two bulging dots in its cheeks like foam. This happens in a person's cheeks if he gets angry and talks a lot. Umm Ghiran bint Jarir said: I may have recited to my father until my cheeks become bulging. He gave an example of the brave whose poison is abundant, so money is likened to this animal and its owner meets him angry. Ibn Duraid said: Two black dots above its eyes. In another narration: It was likened to him a brave man who follows him and forces him, so he gives him his hand and he bites it like a stallion. Ibn Masoud said: By God, God will not punish anyone for a treasure that touches dirham by dirham or dinar by dinar, but rather He will expand its bulk until each dirham and dinar are placed separately. This is only valid for the disbeliever - as mentioned in the hadith - not for the believer. And God knows best. Third: Al-Tabari attributed to Abu Umamah Al-Bahili, who said: “A man from the people of the Suffah died and a dinar was found in his cloak. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Cauterization.’ Then another man died and two dinars were found on his cloak. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Two cauteries.’” This is either because they were living off charity and had gold, or because this was in the early days of Islam, and then the Shari’ah decided to control money and pay its due. If controlling money was forbidden, then it would have been his right to pay it all, and there is no one in the Ummah who is obligated to do this. The situation of the Companions and their wealth is sufficient for you, may God be pleased with them. As for what was mentioned about Abu Dharr, it is his school of thought, may God be pleased with him. Musa bin Ubaidah narrated from Imran bin Abi Anas from Malik bin Aws bin Al-Hadathan from Abu Dharr from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever collects a dinar, a dirham, gold, or silver and does not give it to a creditor or spend it in the way of God, it is a treasure with which he will be branded on the Day of Resurrection. I said: This is what befits Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, to say, and that what is left over from need is not a treasure if it is prepared for the sake of God. Abu Umamah said: Whoever leaves behind eggs or yellow and branded them with them, he will be forgiven or not forgiven. Indeed, the adornment of the sword is from that. Thawban narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no man who dies while he has a red or white garment, except that God will make for him for every carat a plate with which to cauterize from his forehead to his feet, and he will be forgiven after that or punished.” I said: This is based on what is paid in zakat, as evidenced by what we mentioned in the verse before this. So the meaning would be: And if there is a red or white person who does not pay his zakat. Likewise, what was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him: Whoever leaves behind ten thousand, they will be made into plates with which their owner will be punished on the Day of Resurrection. That is, if he does not pay its zakat, so that the hadiths do not contradict each other. And God knows best. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: This is what you hoarded for yourselves, meaning it will be said to them: This is what you hoarded, but it was omitted. Then taste what you used to hoard, meaning the punishment for what you used to hoard.
9:36: God Almighty says: “Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve [lunar] months in the register of God [from] the day He created the heavens and the earth; of these, four are sacred. That is the right religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them.” In eight issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: The number of months is the plural of month. So if a man says to his brother: I will not speak to you for months, and he swears on that, then he will not speak to him for a year, some scholars said. It was said: He will never speak to him. Ibn al-Arabi: I think that if he did not intend that, it would require three months, because it is the least plural required by the formula fa’ul in the plural of fa’l. The meaning of with God is in the judgment of God and in what is written in the Preserved Tablet. Twelve months Ahmad parsed twelve months, unlike its counterparts, because it contains the letter of parsing and its evidence. The general public read ashar with a fatha on the ‘ayn and the shin. Abu Ja’far read ashar with a jazm on the shin. In the Book of God means the Preserved Tablet. He repeated it after saying with God because many things are described as being with God, but it is not said that they are written in the Book of God, like His saying: Indeed, with God is knowledge of the Hour (Luqman 31:34). The second - God the Almighty said: On the Day He created the heavens and the earth. He only said On the Day He created the heavens and the earth to clarify that His judgment and decree was before that, and that He, glory be to Him, established these months and named them with their names according to what He arranged them on the Day He created the heavens and the earth, and revealed that to His prophets in His revealed books. This is the meaning of His Almighty saying: Indeed, the number of months with God is twelve months. And their ruling remains as they were, and their order was not changed by the polytheists changing their names and presenting the first in the name. The purpose of that is to follow God's command in it and reject what the people of ignorance did of delaying the names of the months and presenting them, and basing the rulings on the names they arranged for them. Therefore, "he, peace be upon him, said in his sermon during the Farewell Pilgrimage: O people, time has returned to its state on the Day God created the heavens and the earth," as will be explained. And what the people of ignorance did of making Muharram Safar and Safar Muharram does not change what God the Almighty described. The agent in the word day is the source that is in the Book of God, and it does not mean by it one of the books, because entities do not work in circumstances. The estimate is: in what God wrote on the day He created the heavens and the earth. And when is related to the source that is the number, and it is the agent in it. And in from his saying: in the Book of God is related to something omitted, which is an attribute of his saying: twelve, and the estimate is: twelve months counted or written in the Book of God. And it is not permissible for it to be related to a number because of what it contains of differentiation between the connection and what is connected by the report of if. Third: This verse indicates that it is obligatory to suspend the rulings of worship and other things, and that it should be based on the months and years that the Arabs know, not the months that the Persians, Romans, and Copts consider, even if they do not exceed twelve months, because they differ in number, some of which exceed thirty and some of which are less, and the months of the Arabs do not exceed thirty, even if some of them are less, and the month that is less is not specified for it, but rather their difference in decrease and completion is according to the difference in the moon’s course in the zodiac. Fourth: The Almighty said: Of them, four are sacred. The sacred months mentioned in this verse are Dhul-Qi’dah, Dhul-Hijjah, Muharram, and Rajab, which is between Jumada al-Akhira and Sha’ban. It is Rajab Mudar, and it was called Rajab Mudar because Rabi’ah ibn Nizar used to forbid the month of Ramadan and call it Rajab. Mudar used to forbid Rajab itself, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said about it: The one between Jumada and Sha’ban, and he removed the confusion that occurred in its name by explaining it. The Arabs also used to call it Mansel al-Asna. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Raja’ al-Attardi - whose name was Imran ibn Milhan, or it was said Imran ibn Taym - who said: We used to worship stones, so if we found a stone that was better than it, we would throw it away and take another one. If we did not find a stone, we would gather a handful of dirt, then bring sheep, milk them, and circumambulate them. When the month of Rajab began, we would say Mansel al-Asna, and we did not leave a spear with an iron tip or an arrow with an iron tip except that we would pull it out and throw it away. Fifth - The Almighty said: That is the right religion, meaning the correct reckoning and the complete number. Ali bin Abi Talha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That religion means that is the judgment. Muqatil: the truth. Ibn Atiyah: What is more correct in my opinion is that the religion here is according to its most famous aspects, meaning that is the law and obedience. Al-Qayyim means the upright and straight one, from qama yaqoom. Like master, from saada yasud. Its root is qayyum. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: So wrong not yourselves therein according to Ibn Abbas refers to all the months. According to some of them, it refers to the sacred months in particular, because it is closer to them and has the advantage of magnifying injustice. The Almighty’s saying: There shall be no obscenity, nor wickedness, nor disputing during Hajj (al-Baqarah 2:197) does not mean that injustice is permissible on days other than these, as we will explain. Then it was said: There are two opinions regarding injustice: One of them: Do not wrong yourselves therein by fighting, then it was abrogated by permitting fighting in all the months, as stated by Qatada, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Al-Zuhri, and Sufyan Al-Thawri. Ibn Jurayj said: Ata’ bin Abi Rabah swore by God that it is not permissible for people to wage war in the Haram or in the sacred months unless they fight in them, and it was not abrogated. The first is correct, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, waged war against Hawazin at Hunayn and Thaqeef at At-Ta’if, and besieged them in Shawwal and some of Dhul-Qa’dah. This meaning was mentioned earlier in Al-Baqarah. Second: Do not wrong yourselves by committing sins, because if God the Almighty glorifies something in one respect, it becomes one sanctity, and if He glorifies it in two or more respects, its sanctity becomes multiple, so the punishment for bad deeds is doubled just as the reward for good deeds is doubled. For whoever obeys God in the sacred month in the sacred land, his reward is not the same as the reward of whoever obeys Him in the lawful month in the sacred land. And whoever obeys Him in the lawful month in the sacred land, his reward is not the same as the reward of whoever obeys Him in a lawful month in a lawful land. God the Almighty has indicated this in His saying: O wives of the Prophet! Whoever of you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her, twofold. (al-Ahzab 33:30) Seventh: Scholars have differed on this meaning regarding someone who is killed by mistake in the sacred month, whether the blood money is increased or not. Al-Awza’i said: The blood money is increased according to what we have been informed about when killing in the sacred month, and in the sacred city, so it is one blood money and a third. And it is increased in the case of semi-intentional killing of camels. Al-Shafi’i said: The blood money is increased for a soul and wounds in the sacred month, in the sacred land, and among relatives. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, Salim bin Abdullah, Ibn Shihab, and Aban bin Othman: Whoever is killed in the sacred month or in the sacred city, his blood money is increased by a third. This was also narrated on the authority of Othman bin Affan. Malik, Abu Hanifa, their companions, and Ibn Abi Laila said: Killing in the sacred city and outside of it is the same, and in the sacred month and outside of it is the same. This is the opinion of a group of the followers. And it is correct, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, established blood money and did not mention the sacred city or the sacred month. They agreed that the expiation for someone who kills by mistake in the sacred month and outside of it is the same. So the analogy is that the blood money should be the same. And God knows best. Eighth - God the Almighty mentioned the four sacred months specifically, and forbade injustice during them as an honor to them, even though it is forbidden at all times. As He said: There shall be no obscenity, nor wickedness, nor disputing during Hajj (al-Baqarah 2:197). This is the opinion of most of the commentators. That is, do not wrong yourselves during the four months. Hammad bin Salamah narrated on the authority of Ali bin Zaid on the authority of Yusuf bin Mihran on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Do not wrong yourselves during the twelve months. Qais bin Muslim narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah who said: During all of them. If it is said according to the first opinion: Why did He say in them and not in them? That is because the Arabs say for what is between three and ten: hunna and hadith, and when they exceed ten they say: hi and hadith, wanting to distinguish the little from the much. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Kisa’i that he said: I am amazed at this action of the Arabs. Likewise, they say for nights less than ten: khalon, and for nights above that: khalat. It is not said: How did He make some times more sacred than others? We say: The Almighty Creator can do whatever He wills. He bestows virtue upon whomever He wills. There is no cause for His knowledge and no restriction upon it. Rather, He does what He wills by His wisdom, and wisdom may appear in it or it may be hidden. The Almighty’s saying: And fight the polytheists altogether contains one issue: God the Almighty said: Fight is an order to fight. And all of it means all together, and it is a verbal noun in the position of a state. That is, surrounding them and gathered together. Al-Zajjaj said: A verbal noun like this is: May God grant him wellness and punish him with a good punishment. It is not dual or plural, and so are general and specific. Some scholars said: The purpose of this verse was directed at individuals, then that was abrogated and made a communal obligation. Ibn Atiyyah said: What he said was never known from the law of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he obligated the entire nation to go out. Rather, the meaning of this verse is to urge fighting them, forming parties against them, and uniting the word. Then he qualified it by saying: as they fight you all together, so according to their fighting and gathering against us, our gathering against them is obligatory. And God knows best.
9:37: The Almighty said: The postponement is only an increase in disbelief. This is how most of the Imams read it. An-Nahhas said: No one narrated from Nafi' as far as we know that the word Nasa'i is without a hamza except Warsh alone. It is derived from Nasa'ahu and Ansa'ahu meaning to bring him out. Al-Kisa'i narrated both languages. Al-Jawhari: An-Nasa'i is a fa'il with the meaning of maf'ul, from your saying: I postponed something so it is Manso'u if you delay it. Then Manso'u is changed to Nasa'i just as Maqtool is changed to Maqtool. A man is Nasa'i and a people are Nasa'a, like Fasiq and Fasqa. At-Tabari said: An-Nasa'i with a hamza means an increase. It is said: Nasa' yansa'u if he increases. He said: The hamza is not omitted except from forgetfulness, as God Almighty said: They forgot God, so He forgot them (al-Tawbah 9:67). He responded to Nafi’s reading, and provided evidence by saying: It is transitive with a preposition. It is said: May God prolong your lifespan, just as you say: May God increase your lifespan. And from this is his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: Whoever wants his provision to be expanded and his lifespan to be extended, let him maintain kinship ties. Al-Azhari said: “Ansa’at al-shay’ to postpone something is a noun that is used in place of the real source. They used to forbid fighting in Muharram, but if they needed to, they would forbid it in Safar instead and fight in Muharram. The reason for that was that the Arabs were people of wars and raids, so it was difficult for them to remain for three consecutive months without changing them, and they said: If three consecutive months pass without us gaining anything, we will perish. So when they left Mina, a man from Banu Kinanah would stand up, then from Banu Fuqim from them called Al-Qalmas, and he would say: I am the one whose decree cannot be rejected. They would say: Delay us for a month, meaning postpone the sanctity of Muharram for us and make it in Safar, so Muharram would be permissible for them. They continued like that month after month until the prohibition covered the entire year. Then Islam came and Muharram returned to the place in which God had placed it. This is the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: “Time has come full circle as it was on the day God created the heavens and the earth.” Mujahid said: The polytheists used to perform Hajj every month for two years. They performed Hajj in Dhul-Hijjah for two years, then in Muharram for two years, then in Safar for two years, and so on in all the months until Abu Bakr’s Hajj, which he performed before the Farewell Pilgrimage, coincided with Dhul-Qi’dah of the ninth year. Then the Prophet, peace be upon him, performed the Farewell Pilgrimage the following year, and it coincided with Dhul-Hijjah. That is what he said in his sermon: Time has come full circle, the hadith. He meant by that that the months of Hajj returned to their places, Hajj returned to Dhul-Hijjah, and the postponement was abolished. And a third saying. Ayyas bin Muawiyah said: The polytheists used to count the year as twelve months and fifteen days, so the Hajj would be in Ramadan and in Dhul-Qi'dah, and in every month of the year, according to the month's rotation, with an additional fifteen days. Abu Bakr performed Hajj in the ninth year of Dhul-Qi'dah, according to the rotation, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not perform Hajj. When it was the following year, Hajj coincided with Dhul-Hijjah in the ten days, and that coincided with the new moons. This statement is similar to the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Time has come full circle. That is, the time of Hajj has returned to its original time, which God appointed on the day He created the heavens and the earth, according to the original legitimacy that He knew beforehand, and by which He implemented His judgment. Then he said: The year is twelve months. This negates the addition that they added to the year - which is the fifteen days - by their arbitrariness, so the original time was determined and the ignorant arbitrariness was invalidated. Imam Al-Mazari narrated on the authority of Al-Khawarizmi that he said: The first thing that God created was the sun, He made it move in the sign of Aries, and the time that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, indicated coincided with the setting of the sun in the sign of Aries. This requires a stop, as it can only be reached by transmission from the prophets, and there is no authentic transmission from them regarding that, and whoever claims it should support it. Then the mind allows the opposite of what he said, which is that God created the sun before the zodiac signs, and it is possible that He created all of that at once. Then the scholars of ta’dil have tested that and found the sun in the sign of Pisces at the time of his saying, peace be upon him: Time has turned round, between it and Aries there are twenty degrees. Some of them said ten degrees. And God knows best. The people of interpretation differed about the first to postpone, so Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said: Banu Malik bin Kinanah, and they were three, and Juwaybir narrated from Ad-Dahhak from Ibn Abbas: The first to do that was Amr bin Luhay bin Qama’ah bin Khandaf. Al-Kalbi said: The first to do that was a man from Banu Kinanah called Nu’aym bin Tha’labah, then after him there was a man called Junada bin Auf, and he is the one whom the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, met. Al-Zuhri said: A tribe from Banu Kinanah, then from Banu Faqim, among them was a man called Al-Qalmas, whose name was Hudhayfah ibn Ubayd. In another narration: Malik ibn Kinanah. The one who was in charge of the intercalation would seize leadership because the Arabs had made him their leader. And their poet says about that: And we forget the pen month Al-Kumait said: Aren't we the ones who forget the months of permissibility and make them forbidden? The Almighty’s saying: An increase in disbelief is a statement of what the Arabs did by collecting all kinds of disbelief. They denied the existence of the Almighty Creator, so they said: And what is the Most Gracious? in the most correct way. They denied the resurrection, so they said: Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed? (Ya-Sin 36:78). They denied the mission of the messengers, so they said: A human being from among us whom we should follow? (al-Qamar 54:24). They claimed that the lawful and unlawful were up to them, so they innovated it from themselves, following their desires, so they made lawful what God made unlawful. And there is no changer of His words, even if the polytheists hate it. God the Almighty said: “He misleads thereby those who disbelieve, making it lawful one year and forbidding it another year, that they may conform to the number of what God has forbidden, and they make lawful what God has forbidden. God does not guide the disbelieving people.” There are three readings for this. The people of the Two Sanctuaries and Abu Omar read yudalil and the Kufians read yudalil as a passive verb. Al-Hasan and Abu Raja read yudalil. Each of the three readings conveys a meaning, except that the object was deleted from the third reading. The meaning is: And those who disbelieved mislead thereby those who accept it from them. Those is in the nominative case. It is possible for the pronoun to refer to God the Almighty. The meaning is: God misleads thereby those who disbelieve, as God the Almighty said: He misleads whom He wills (al-Ra`d: 27), and as He said at the end of the verse: And God does not guide the disbelieving people. The second reading is He misleads thereby those who disbelieve meaning what is attributed to them, and Abu Ubaid chose this reading, because God the Almighty said: Their evil deeds have been made pleasing to them. The first reading was chosen by Abu Hatim, because they were astray by it, that is, by the postponement, because they thought it was and went astray by it. The ha’ in yahluhunu refers to the postponement. It was narrated from Abu Raja’ yadhil with the opening of the ya’ and the dad. It is a dialect, it is said: dalalta adhal, and dalalta adhal. Liwata’u is the accusative with the lam of ki, meaning to agree. The people agreed upon such and such, meaning they did not make a month permissible without making a month sacred so that the sacred months would remain four. This is the correct one, not what is mentioned that they made the months five. Qatadah said: They deliberately took Safar and added it to the sacred months, and linked it to Muharram in the prohibition, and Qatrab and al-Tabari said the same about him. Accordingly, the postponement means the increase. And God knows best.
9:38: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: What is the matter with you? “What” is an interrogative particle that means confirmation and rebuke. The meaning is: What is preventing you from such-and-such, as you say: Why are you turning away from so-and-so?
