There is no dispute that this verse was revealed as a rebuke for those who stayed behind from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. It was in the ninth year of the Hijra, one year after the conquest, and it will be mentioned at the end of the surah, God willing. And Nafar is moving quickly from one place to another for something that happens. It is said about the son of Adam: Nafar to the matter, he flees, aversion. And a people are aversion, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: And they turned back in aversion (al-Isra’ 17:46). And it is said about an animal: Nafarat Tanfaz with a damma or kasra on the fa Nafaran and Nafour. It is said about an animal: Nafar, which is a name like Al-Harran. And the pilgrim fled from Mina in aversion. Second: The Almighty’s saying: You were weighed down to the earth. The commentators said: Its meaning is you were weighed down to the pleasures of the earth, or to residing on the earth. It is a rebuke for abandoning jihad and a reproach for retiring from taking the initiative to go out, and it is similar to someone who is attached to the earth. Its original form is tathaqaltum, the ta’ was assimilated to the tha’ because of its proximity to it, and it needed the alif of connection to reach the pronunciation of the consonant, and similar to it are idaraku and idara’tum “atayirna” and wazaynat. Al-Kisa’i recited: She takes over the bed if he finds her waist sweet-tasting if he follows the kiss Al-A'mash read tathaqaltum based on the original. Al-Mahdawi narrated it. Tabuk - and he called the people to it - was in the heat of the summer, with good fruits and cool shade - as mentioned in the authentic hadith as follows - so laziness overcame the people, so they retired and were slow. So God rebuked them with this statement, and the preference for this world over the Hereafter was absent from them. The meaning of are you satisfied with the life of this world rather than the Hereafter is instead, the estimate is: are you satisfied with the pleasures of this world instead of the pleasures of the Hereafter. So min includes the meaning of a substitute, like the Almighty's saying: And if We willed, We could have made you angels on the earth, succeeding you (al-Zukhruf 43:60), meaning instead of you. The poet said: I wish we had a cold drink of Zamzam water that was cooked the night before. It is narrated from the water of Hamnan. He meant: If only we had a cold drink instead of Zamzam water. And the tahyan is a stick that is erected in the corner of the house for air, and water is hung on it until it cools. God rebuked them for preferring comfort in this world over comfort in the Hereafter, as the comfort of the Hereafter is not attained except through the hardship of this world. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Aisha when she was performing the circumambulation while riding. Your reward is according to your effort. Narrated by Al-Bukhari.
9:39: There is one issue - which is that the Almighty's saying: If you do not go forth is a condition, and therefore the letter nun was deleted from it. The answer is He will punish you, and replace you with another people and this is a severe threat and a confirmed warning against abandoning the mobilization. Ibn al-Arabi said: Among the established principles is that when a command is given, its occurrence does not exceed the requirement of the action. As for the punishment when it is abandoned, it is not taken from the command itself nor is it required by the requirement, but rather the punishment is by the report about it, like His saying: If you do not do such and such, I will punish you with such and such, as mentioned in this verse. So, according to it, it is obligatory to go forth for jihad and go out to fight the infidels so that the word of God is supreme. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment and It was not for the people of Madinah - to His saying - to work [At-Tawbah 121] was abrogated by the verse that follows it: And it was not for the believers to go forth all together. This is the saying of Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan and Ikrimah. He punishes you. Ibn Abbas said: It means withholding rain from them. Ibn Al-Arabi said: If this is authentically reported from him, then he is more knowledgeable about where he said it. Otherwise, the painful punishment is in this world with the enemy’s control and in the fire in the hereafter. I said: The statement of Ibn Abbas was included by Imam Abu Dawud in his Sunan on the authority of Ibn Nafi’ who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about this verse: If you do not go forth, He will punish you with a painful punishment. He said: So He withheld the rain from them, and that was their punishment. Imam Abu Muhammad Ibn Atiyyah mentioned it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called a tribe to battle, but they stayed back, so God withheld the rain from them and punished them with it. Painful means painful, meaning hurtful. It has been mentioned before. And He will replace you with another people. He threatened to replace His Messenger with a people who will not stay back when he calls them to battle. It was said: The sons of Persia. It was also said: The people of Yemen. And will not harm Him at all is a conjunction. The letter ha was said to refer to God Almighty, and it was said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Being reluctant to engage in jihad while showing dislike is forbidden for everyone. As for those who are not disliked, then the one whom the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) specified is forbidden to be reluctant, and if he is safe from them, then the obligation is a communal obligation. Al-Qushayri mentioned it. It has been said that what is meant by this verse is the obligation to mobilize when there is a need and the disbelievers appear and their power grows. The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that this is in the form of a summons, so based on this, it is not appropriate to apply it to the time of the appearance of the polytheists, because the obligation of that is not specific to the summons, because it is specified. If that is proven, then it is unlikely that the summons and mobilization would be a requirement for something that was not previously required, except that if the Imam appoints a people and urges them to jihad, they should not be reluctant when appointing, and his appointment becomes an obligation on the one he appoints, not for the purpose of jihad, but for the obedience of the Imam. And God knows best.
9:40: It contains eleven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: If you do not support him, meaning: help him by accompanying the men in the Battle of Tabuk. God rebuked them after his Prophet (peace be upon him) left Tabuk. Al-Naqqash said: This is the first verse to be revealed in Surat Bara’ah. The meaning is: If you abandon his support, God will take care of it, as God has already supported him in times of scarcity and made him victorious and mighty over his enemy. It was said: God supported him with his companion in the cave by making him feel comfortable and carrying him on his neck, and by his loyalty and protecting him with himself and comforting him with his money. Al-Layth ibn Sa’d said: No one accompanied the prophets (peace be upon them) like Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Abu Bakr was excluded by this verse from the rebuke in His saying: If you do not support him. Second: The Almighty’s saying: When those who disbelieved drove him out. He went out by himself, fleeing, but because they forced him to do so until he did it, so he attributed the action to them and imposed the ruling on them. For this reason, the one who was forced to kill is killed and the property destroyed by force is liable, because he forced the killer and the destroyer to kill and destroy. Third: The Almighty’s saying: The second of two meaning one of two. This is like the third of three and the fourth of four. So if the wording is different, and you say the fourth of three and the fifth of four, the meaning is that he made the three four by himself and the four five. It is in the accusative case as a state, meaning they expelled him alone from all the people except Abu Bakr. The factor in it is God aided him meaning He aided him alone and aided him one of two. Ali bin Sulayman said: The meaning is so he expelled the second of two, like And God caused you to grow from the earth a plant (Nuh 71:17). The majority of people read thani with the accusative of the ya’. Abu Hatim said: Nothing is known other than this. A group read thani with the sukoon of the ya’. Ibn Jinni said: Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ narrated it, and his reason is that he sukoon the ya’ to resemble it with the alif. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is like the reading of Al-Hasan [what remains of usury] and like the saying of Jarir: He is the Caliph, so impose what you are satisfied with. The past of determination is not in his rule. Fourth: The Almighty said: When they were in the cave. The cave is a hole in the mountain, meaning the Cave of Thawr. When the Quraysh saw that the Muslims had reached Medina, they said: This is an unbearable and preoccupying evil. So they decided to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They plotted against him and lay in wait for him at the door of a house all night to kill him if he came out. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Ali ibn Abi Talib to sleep on his bed and asked God to blind them from his tracks, but God blinded their sight. He came out while they were asleep. He put dirt on their heads and got up. When morning came, Ali, may God be pleased with him, came out to them and told them that there was no one in the house. They knew that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had escaped. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made an appointment with Abu Bakr al-Siddiq to emigrate, so they gave their two mounts to Abdullah ibn Arqat. It is said that he was Ibn Arqat, and he was an unbeliever, but they trusted him. He was a guide on the roads, so they hired him to guide them to Medina. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) came out from a hole in the back of Abu Bakr's house in Bani Jumah and they headed towards the cave in Mount Thawr. Abu Bakr ordered his son Abdullah to listen to what the people were saying, and he ordered his servant Amir bin Fuhaira to tend his sheep and let them rest for them at night so that he could take what they needed from them. Then they got up and entered the cave. Asma bint Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq used to bring them food and Abdullah bin Abu Bakr would bring them report. Amir bin Fuhaira would follow them with the sheep and erase their tracks. When the Quraysh missed him, they began to look for him through a well-known tracker who tracks tracks, until he stopped at the cave and said: Here the tracks are cut off. They looked and saw that a spider had woven a web at the mouth of the cave immediately. This is why the Prophet (peace be upon him) forbade killing it. When they saw the spider's web, they were certain that there was no one in it, so they returned and offered the Prophet (peace be upon him) a hundred camels for whoever returned him to them. This story is well-known, and the story of Suraqah bin Malik bin Ju'sham in this regard is mentioned. It was narrated from the hadith of Abu al-Darda’ and Thawban, may God be pleased with them: God Almighty commanded a dove to lay eggs on a spider’s web and sit on its eggs. When the infidels saw it, it turned them away from the cave. Fifth - “Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr hired a man from Banu al-Dayl as a guide and a guide, and he followed the religion of the infidels of Quraysh. They gave him their two camels and made an appointment with him at the Cave of Thawr after three nights. He came to them with their two camels on the morning of the third, and they set out, and Amer bin Fuhayrah and the guide al-Dayl set out with them, and he took them by the coastal route.” Al-Muhallab said: It includes jurisprudence regarding trusting the polytheists with one’s secret and money if one knows that they are loyal and honorable, just as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entrusted this polytheist with his secret in leaving Makkah and with his two camels. Ibn al-Mundhir said: It includes hiring the Muslims from the infidels to guide people on the way. Al-Bukhari said in his biography: Chapter on hiring the polytheists in times of necessity or if the Muslims are not found. Ibn Battaal said: Al-Bukhari only said in his biography or if the Muslims are not found because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) only hired the people of Khaybar to work in their land, since there were no Muslims to replace them in working the land, until Islam became strong and ‘Umar did not need them, and they were expelled. Most of the jurists permit hiring them in times of necessity and other times. It includes: two men hiring one man for one job for them. It includes: evidence of the permissibility of fleeing with one’s religion out of fear of the enemy, and hiding in caves and other places, and that one should not throw oneself into the hands of the enemy, relying on God and submitting to Him. And if your Lord had willed, He could have protected him, even though he was with them. But this is the way of God with the prophets and others, and you will not find any change in the way of God. This is the clearest evidence of the corruption of those who forbade that and said: Whoever fears other than God, that is a deficiency in his trust, and he does not believe in destiny. All of this is in the meaning of the verse, and praise and guidance be to God. Sixth - The Almighty said: When he said to his companion, ‘Do not grieve; indeed God is with us.’ This verse includes the virtues of the Truthful One, may God be pleased with him. Asbagh and Abu Zaid narrated on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim on the authority of Malik, The second of the two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion, ‘Do not grieve; indeed God is with us.’ He is the Truthful One. So God, the Almighty, fulfilled His words to him with His words and described the companionship in His Book. Some scholars said: Whoever denies that Umar and Uthman or any of the companions were companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a liar and an innovator. Whoever denies that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was a companion of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is an infidel, because he rejected the text of the Qur’an. The meaning of God is with us is with victory, care, protection, and guardianship. Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Harith bin Abi Usamah narrated: Affan told us, Hammam told us, Thabit told us, on the authority of Anas, that Abu Bakr told him, saying: “I said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while we were in al-Kahf 18:If one of them were to look at his feet, he would see us under his feet. He said: O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two people with God as their third?” Al-Muhasibi said: He meant with them in victory and defense, not in the sense that he made it general to all creatures, for he said: There is not a secret conversation between three but that He is their fourth (Al-Mujadilah: 7). So its general meaning is that He hears and sees both the disbelievers and the believers. Seventh - Ibn al-Arabi said: The Imamis - may God curse them - said: Abu Bakr's sadness in the cave is evidence of his ignorance and deficiency, and the weakness and weakness of his heart. Our scholars responded to that by saying that attributing sadness to him is not a deficiency, just as it was not a deficiency in Abraham when he said about him: "He disliked them and felt fear of them. They said, "Fear not." (Hud 11:70). And it was not a deficiency in Moses when he said: "So Moses felt fear within himself. We said, Fear not. (Ta-Ha 20:67-68). And in Lot: "And do not grieve. Indeed, We will save you and your family." (al-Ankabut 29:33). These great men, may God's prayers be upon them, were found to be taqiyya explicitly, and that was not a slander against them or a description of them as deficient, and the same is true of Abu Bakr. Then it is a possibility according to Abu Bakr, for he said: If one of them looked under his feet, he would see us. Second answer: The sadness of the friend was due to fear that harm would come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not infallible at that time, but rather the verse And God will protect you from the people (al-Ma’idah 5:67) was revealed to him in Medina. Eighth - Ibn al-Arabi said: Abu al-Fada’il al-Adl told us: Jamal al-Islam Abu al-Qasim told us: Moses, peace be upon him, said: No indeed, my Lord is with me; He will guide me (al-Shu’ara’: 62) and he said about Muhammad, peace be upon him: Do not grieve, indeed God is with us. There is no doubt that when God was with Moses alone, his companions turned away after him, so he returned from his Lord and found them worshipping the calf. And when he said about Muhammad, peace be upon him, Do not grieve, indeed God is with us, Abu Bakr remained guided, a monotheist, knowledgeable, decisive, and upholding the command, and no confusion came to him. Ninth: Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Nabit bin Sharit on the authority of Salim bin Ubaid - who was a companion - who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fainted..., the hadith. And in it: The immigrants gathered to consult and said: Let us go to our brothers from the Ansar and include them with us in this matter. The Ansar said: One of us is a leader and one of you is a leader. So Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: Who has three like these The second of the two when they were in the cave and he said to his companion, Do not grieve, indeed God is with us." Who are they? He said: Then he extended his hand and pledged allegiance to him and the people pledged allegiance to him with a good and beautiful pledge. I said: This is why some scholars said: In the words of God the Almighty: The second of the two when they were in the cave there is evidence that the caliph after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq - may God be pleased with him - because the caliph can never be anything but second. I heard our Sheikh, Imam Abu al-Abbas Ahmad bin Omar say: Al-Siddiq deserved to be called the second of the two because he took up the matter after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, just as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took up the matter first. This is because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, all of the Arabs apostatized, and Islam remained only in Medina, Mecca, and Jawatha. So Abu Bakr rose up calling the people to Islam and fighting them to enter the religion as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did. So from this perspective he deserved to be called the second of the two. I said: There are authentic hadiths in the Sunnah, the apparent meaning of which indicates that he is the caliph after him, and consensus has been reached on that and no one has disagreed with him. The one who casts doubt on his caliphate is certain to be mistaken and immoral. Whether he is an unbeliever or not is disputed, but the most apparent is that he is an unbeliever. This meaning will be further explained in Surat Al-Fath, God willing. What is certain from the Book, the Sunnah, and the sayings of the scholars of this Ummah, and what hearts and minds must believe in, is the superiority of Abu Bakr over all the companions. There is no concern with the sayings of the Shiites or the people of innovation, for they are between an unbeliever whose neck is struck, and an innovator and immoral whose word is not accepted. Then after Abu Bakr, Umar Al-Faruq, then after him Uthman. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: We used to choose between people during the time of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), so we would choose Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Uthman. The imams of the early Muslims differed regarding Uthman and Ali, and the majority of them were of the opinion that Uthman should be given precedence. It was narrated from Malik that he hesitated about that. It was also narrated from him that he returned to what the majority were of the opinion. And this is the most correct, God willing. Tenth - The Almighty’s saying: So God sent down His tranquility upon him There are two opinions on this: One of them is on the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The second is on Abu Bakr. Ibn al-Arabi: Our scholars said, and this is the stronger opinion, because he feared for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the people, so God sent down His tranquility upon him by ensuring the safety of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So his anxiety subsided and his fear went away and he attained security. God, the Exalted, caused a dove to grow in the nest there, and sent a spider that wove a web over him. How weak these soldiers are in the outward appearance of the senses and how strong they are in the inner meaning! And this is the meaning that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar when he took a risk with Abu Bakr: Will you leave my companion for me? All the people said, ‘You lied,’ and Abu Bakr said, ‘You told the truth.’ Narrated by Abu al-Darda’. Eleventh - The Almighty said: "And He supported him with soldiers you did not see" meaning of the angels. The metaphor in His statement "And He supported him" refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The two pronouns differ, and this is common in the Qur’an and in the speech of the Arabs. "And He made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest" meaning the word of polytheism. "And the word of God is the highest" It was said: There is no god but God. And it was said: He promised victory. Al-A'mash and Ya'qub read "and the word of God" in the accusative case based on making. The rest read it in the nominative case as a new sentence. Al-Farra' claimed that the accusative reading is far-fetched. He said: Because you say, "So-and-so freed his father's slave, and you do not say, the slave of so-and-so's father." Abu Hatim said something similar. He said: It should have been said, "and His word is the highest." Al-Nahhas said: What Al-Farra' mentioned does not resemble the verse, but what Sibawayh recited resembles it: I do not see death preceded by anything that made death bitter to the rich and the poor This is good and excellent, there is no problem with it. In fact, the clever grammarians say: There is a benefit in repeating the mention in such a case, which is that it contains the meaning of glorification. God the Most High said: When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake, And the earth discharges its burdens (al-Zalzalah 99:1-2). There is no problem with this. The plural of the word is kalam. Tamim says: it is a word with a kasra on the kaf. Al-Farra’ narrated three languages for it: kalimah, kalimah, and kalimah, like kabd, kabd, and kabd, and waraq, waraq, and waraq. The word is also the poem in its entirety, as Al-Jawhari said.
9:41: It contains seven issues: First: Sufyan narrated on the authority of Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ghifari who said: The first part of Surat Bara’ah to be revealed was: Go forth, whether light or heavy. Abu al-Dhaha also said the same. He said: Then the beginning and the end of it were revealed. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Go forth, whether light or heavy. It is in the accusative case as a state, and there are ten sayings about it: First: It is mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Go forth in companies or (An-Nisa’: 71): scattered raiding parties. Second: It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah: active and inactive. Third: light: the rich, and heavy: the poor, said by Mujahid. Fourth: light: the young, and heavy: the old, said by Al-Hasan. Fifth: busy and not busy, said by Zaid bin Ali and Al-Hakam bin Utaybah. Sixth: heavy: the one who has children, and light: the one who has no children, said by Zaid bin Aslam. Seventh: heavy: the one who has an estate that he hates to abandon, and light: the one who has no estate, said by Ibn Zaid. Eighth: light: men, and heavy: horsemen, said by Al-Awza’i. Ninth: light: those who precede to war like the vanguard, which is the front of the army, and heavy: the entire army. The tenth: light: the brave, and heavy: the coward, narrated by Al-Naqqash. The correct meaning of the verse is that the people were ordered all at once, meaning go forth, whether the movement is easy or heavy for you. It was narrated that Ibn Umm Maktum came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: Should I flee? He said: Yes, until God Almighty revealed: There is no blame upon the blind (al-Nur 24:61). These sayings are in the sense of an example of heaviness and lightness. Third: There is a difference of opinion regarding this verse. Some say that it was abrogated by the words of God the Almighty: There is no blame upon the weak or upon the ill (al-Tawbah 9:91). It was also said that what abrogated it was His words: Why should not a party from every division of them go forth (al-Tawbah 9:122). The correct view is that it is not abrogated. Ibn Abbas narrated on the authority of Abu Talhah regarding the words of God the Almighty: Go forth, whether light or heavy, he said: young and old. God did not listen to anyone’s excuse. So he went out to Ash-Sham and fought until he died, may God be pleased with him. Hammad narrated on the authority of Thabit and Ali bin Zaid on the authority of Anas that Abu Talhah recited Surah Bara’ah and came to this verse: Go forth, whether light or heavy, so he said: O my son, prepare me, prepare me. His sons said: May God have mercy on you! I fought with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) until he died, and with Abu Bakr until he died, and with Umar until he died, so we will fight on your behalf. He said: No, prepare me. He went on a sea expedition and died at sea. They could not find an island to bury him on for seven days, so they buried him there. He did not change, may God be pleased with him. At-Tabari narrated from someone who saw Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad in Homs on the coffin of a money changer, and some of his fat was left over from the coffin while he was preparing for the expedition. He was told: God has excused you. He said: Surat Al-Ba’uth came to us: Go forth, whether light or heavy. Al-Zuhri said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab went out to the expedition and one of his eyes had gone. He was told: You are ill. He said: God has mobilized the light and the heavy. If I am not able to fight, the blacks will increase and the provisions will be preserved. It was narrated that some people saw a man during the expeditions of the Levant with his eyebrows over his eyes due to old age. He said to him: O uncle, God has excused you. He said: O my nephew, we have been commanded to go forth, whether light or heavy. Ibn Umm Maktum may God be pleased with him - whose name was Amr - said on the day of UHud 11:I am a blind man, so hand me the standard, for if the standard-bearer is defeated, the army will be defeated, and I do not know who is aiming his sword at me, so I will not move. So Mus`ab ibn `Umair took the standard that day, as was explained in Al Imran. For this reason and what was similar to it that was narrated from the Companions and the Followers, we said: Abrogation is not valid. And there may be a situation in which everyone must be mobilized, which is: Fourth: If jihad becomes necessary due to the enemy’s dominance over a region, or his presence in the heartland, then if that happens, then it is obligatory upon all the people of that country to set out and go out to it, light and heavy, young and old, each according to his ability, those who have a father without his permission and those who do not have a father. No one who is able to go out should stay behind, whether he is a fighter or a large number. If the people of that town are unable to confront their enemy, then it is obligatory upon those who are close to them and live near them to go out according to what is obligatory upon the people of that town, until they know that they have the ability to confront them and defend them. Likewise, everyone who knows that they are weak in the face of their enemy and knows that he can overtake them and can aid them, then it is obligatory upon him to go out to them, for all Muslims are one hand against everyone else, until the people of the region that the enemy has descended upon and occupied stand up to repel the enemy, then the obligation is dropped from the others. If the enemy approaches the land of Islam but does not enter it, then it is also obligatory upon them to go out to it, until the religion of God prevails, the integrity is protected, the domain is preserved, and the enemy is disgraced. There is no disagreement on this. A second part of the duty of jihad - it is also obligatory for the Imam to send a group to attack the enemy once a year, he goes out with them himself, or sends someone he trusts to call them to Islam and encourage them, and to stop their harm and make the religion of God prevail over them, until they enter Islam or pay the jizyah willingly. There is also a voluntary jihad, which is the Imam sending out a group after a group, sending out raiding parties at times of surprise and when there is a possibility of an opportunity, lying in wait for them by guarding them in a place of fear, and showing strength. If it is said: What should one do if everyone falls short, and it is: Fifth: It was said to him: He should go to one prisoner and ransom him, because if he ransomes one, he has paid more for one person than he would have paid for the group, because if the rich divided the ransom of the prisoners, each one of them would not pay more than less than a dirham. And he should go on a raid himself if he is able, otherwise he should equip a raider. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever equips a warrior has indeed fought, and whoever leaves behind a family of his own has indeed fought. Narrated by Sahih. This is because his position is not sufficient and his wealth is not sufficient. Sixth: It was narrated that some kings made a covenant with the infidels that they would not hold a prisoner captive. A Muslim man entered their country and passed by a closed house. A woman called out to him, I am a prisoner, so tell your friend about me. When he met with him and asked him for food and they exchanged some talk, the report reached this tormented woman. He had hardly finished talking when the prince stood up and went out fighting immediately. He walked to the border until he brought out the prisoner and took control of the place, may God be pleased with him. Ibn al-Arabi mentioned him and said: The enemy descended upon us - may God break him - in the year 527 AH. He raided our lands and took our best people captive and entered our country in numbers that terrified the people. They were many, even if they did not reach what they had specified. So I said to the governor and his client: This is the enemy of God who has entered into polytheism and the net, so let there be a blessing among you, and let there be a movement from you to support the religion that is required of you. Let all the people go out to him until not one of them remains in all the regions and surround him, for he will inevitably perish if God makes it easy for you to do so. Sins prevailed, hearts trembled with transgressions, and every person became a fox who takes refuge with his neighbor even if he sees a plot against his neighbor. To God we belong and to Him we shall return. God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And strive is a command to strive, which is derived from effort, with your wealth and your lives. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Fight the polytheists with your wealth, your lives and your tongues. This is a description of the most perfect and beneficial jihad in the sight of God Almighty. He urged perfection of descriptions, and mentioned wealth first, as it is the first expenditure at the time of preparation. He arranged the matter as it is in itself.
9:42: When the Prophet (peace be upon him) returned from the Battle of Tabuk, God revealed the hypocrisy of some people. The word present means what is offered of worldly benefits. The meaning is close spoils. He informed about them that if they were invited to a spoil, they would follow him. A present is the predicate of was. "Nearby" is its description. "And a short journey" is in apposition to it. The name of "was" was omitted because the speech indicates it. The meaning is: If what was invited to was a short present and a short journey - that is, easy and with known routes - they would have followed you. This is a metaphor for the hypocrites, as we mentioned, because they are included in a group of those who were addressed with the call to arms. This is found in the speech of the Arabs, they mention the group and then use the omission referring back to some of it, as was said in the words of God the Almighty: "And there is not one of you but will pass over it" (Maryam 19:71) that it is the Resurrection. Then He, the Almighty, the Majestic, said: Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees. (Maryam 19:72) meaning Hell. Similar in meaning to this verse from the Sunnah is the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: If one of them knew that he would find a fat bone or two good arrows, he would attend the evening prayer. He says: If one of them knew that he would find something ready and quickly to take it, he would come to the mosque for its time. But the distance was too far for them. Abu Ubaidah and others narrated that the distance is a journey to a distant land. It is said: A difficult distance. What is meant by all of this is the Battle of Tabuk. Al-Kisa’i narrated that it is said: A difficult distance and a difficult journey. Al-Jawhari said: A difficult journey with the dammah is from clothing. A difficult journey also means a long journey, and they may have said it with the kasrah. A difficult journey is a splinter that breaks off a board or piece of wood. It is said about an angry person: he became angry and a splinter flew from him, with the kasrah. And they will swear by God, ‘If we were able,’ meaning if we had the means to travel and have money. We would have gone out with you, similar to it. And Hajj to the House is a duty owed to God by those who can afford the expenses. (Aal ‘Imran: 97) The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained it by saying: provisions and a mount, as has been mentioned previously. They destroy themselves, meaning with lies and hypocrisy. And God knows that they are liars, in their illness.
9:43: The Almighty's saying: May God forgive you for giving them permission. It was said: It is the opening of a speech, as you say, May God guide you, honor you, and have mercy on you! It was such and such. According to this interpretation, it is appropriate to stop at his saying: May God forgive you, as narrated by Makki, Al-Mahdawi, and Al-Nahhas. And he informed him of the forgiveness before the sin, lest his heart fly with fear. It was said: The meaning is, God forgives you for what was your sin in giving them permission, so it is not appropriate to stop at his saying: May God forgive you, according to this estimation. Al-Mahdawi narrated it and Al-Nahhas chose it. Then it was said: There are two opinions regarding permission: The first - Why did you give them permission to go out with you, and in their going out without a number and a sincere intention, it is corruption. The second - Why did you give them permission to stay when they made excuses, mentioned by Al-Qushayri, who said: This is a gentle reproach, as he said: May God forgive you. And peace be upon him, he gave permission without any revelation that came down to him. Qatada and Umar ibn Maymun said: There were two things that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did, but he was not commanded to do: his permission for a group of hypocrites to stay behind him, although he was not allowed to do anything except by revelation, and his taking ransom from the prisoners, so God rebuked him as you hear. Some scholars said that he only left out the first, so God presented forgiveness to him rather than addressing him in the form of rebuke. God the Almighty said: Until it becomes clear to you who are truthful and you know the liars meaning, so that it becomes clear to you who is truthful and who is a hypocrite. Ibn Abbas said: This is because the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) did not know the hypocrites at that time, but he only knew them after the revelation of Surat At-Tawbah. Mujahid said: These are people who said: We will ask permission to sit, if we are given permission we will sit, and if we are not given permission we will sit. Qatada said: This verse was abrogated by the statement in Surat al-Nur 24:So when they ask your permission for some matter of theirs, give permission to whomever you wish among them (al-Nur 24:62). An-Nahhas mentioned this in his book Ma’ani Al-Quran.
9:44: The Almighty says: Those who believe in God and the Last Day do not ask your permission meaning to stay or go out. Rather, if you command something, they rush to do it. So asking permission at that time was one of the signs of hypocrisy without an excuse.
9:45: That is why He said: Only those ask your permission who do not believe in God and the Last Day and whose hearts are in doubt, so in their doubt they waver. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Those who believe in God do not ask your permission is abrogated by the one in al-Nur 24:The believers are only those who have believed in God and His Messenger - to His saying - Forgiving and Merciful (al-Nur 24:62) to strive in the accusative case with an implied in, on the authority of Al-Zajjaj. It was said that the meaning is their dislike of striving, like His saying: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray (al-Nisa 4:176). And their hearts are in doubt doubted the religion. So in their doubt they waver meaning in their doubt they go and come back.
9:46: God the Almighty says: And if they had intended to go forth, they would have prepared for it some equipment. That is, if they had intended to fight, they would have prepared themselves as if they were travelling. Their failure to prepare is evidence of their intention to stay behind. But God disliked their going forth, that is, their going forth with you. So He held them back, that is, He kept them back from you and let them down. Because they said: If we are not given permission to stay, we will corrupt and incite against the believers. This is indicated by the fact that after it, If they had gone forth with you, they would not have increased you except in confusion. "And it was said, 'Sit with those who sit still.'" It was said: This is from what some of them said to each other. It was also said: This is from what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, and this is the permission mentioned above. It was said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said it in anger, so they took his literal wording and said: We have been given permission. It was also said: This is an expression of letting down, that is, God put sitting still in their hearts. The meaning of "with those who sit still" is with those who are disabled, the blind, the lame, the women, and the children.
9:47: The Almighty's saying: If they had gone forth with you, they would not have increased you except in confusion is a consolation for the believers for the hypocrites' failure to follow them. Confusion means corruption, backbiting, causing discord and rumors. This is an intermittent exception, meaning they did not increase your strength but sought confusion. It was said that the meaning is they would not increase you in what they waver in opinion except confusion, so the exception is not intermittent. The Almighty says: And they would have hastened to spread corruption among you. The meaning is that they would have hastened to spread corruption among you. And spreading is the speed of movement. The rajaz poet said: I wish I was a tree trunk in it, so I could hide and put it there It is said: The camel ran when it ran, it runs quickly. And I put it down, I carried it on the enemy. It was said: Al-Idaa’ is a pace like the trot. And the gap between two things, and the plural is Al-Khalal, meaning the gaps that are between the rows. That is, they put you in between by gossiping and spoiling the relationship between people. They seek discord among you is a second object. The meaning is they seek discord for you, meaning corruption and incitement. It is said: I sought him so-and-so, I helped him in seeking it. And I sought him so-and-so, I sought it for him. It was said: Discord here is polytheism. And among you are those who listen to them meaning they have spies who convey report from you to them. Qatada: And among you are those who accept their words and obey them. An-Nahhas: The first statement is more appropriate, because the most common of its two meanings is that the meaning of listening is hearing the speech, and similar to it is: listeners to lies (al-Ma’idah 5:42). And the second statement - it is hardly said about it except a listener, like a speaker.
9:48: The Almighty said: They had sought discord before meaning they sought to cause corruption and ruin before their affair became apparent, and the revelation came down regarding what they had concealed and what they would do. Ibn Jurayj said: He meant twelve hypocrites who stood at Thaniyat al-Wada' on the night of al-Aqabah to attack the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And they turned matters upside down for you meaning they diverted them and thought about invalidating what you had come for. Until the truth came and the command of God became apparent meaning His religion while they were averse.
9:49: God the Almighty said: And among them is he who says, 'Permit me' from adhan yadhan. If you give an order, you add a broken hamza followed by a hamza, which is the fa of the verb, and two hamzas cannot come together, so you replace the second with a ya because of the kasra before it, so you say idhan. If you connect, the reason for combining two hamzas is removed, then you add a hamza, so you say: And among them is he who says idhan li. Warsh narrated from Nafi': And among them is he who says awdhan li, lightening the hamza. An-Nahhas said: It is said idhan lifulan then idhan lahu, the spelling of the first and second is the same with an alif and a ya before the dhal in writing. If you say idhan lifulan and idhan ghayrli, the second would be without a ya, and the same with the fa. The difference between thumma and waw is that thumma is stopped on and is separated, while waw and fa are not stopped on and are not separated. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Al-Jadd bin Qais, the brother of Ibn Salamah, when he wanted to go out to Tabuk: O Jadd, would you like to fight the yellow people and take from them concubines and slave girls? Al-Jadd said: My people know that I am fond of women, and I fear that if I see the yellow people I will not be able to stay away from them, so do not tempt me and give me permission to stay and I will help you with my money. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him and said: I have given you permission. So this verse was revealed. That is, do not tempt me with the brightness of their faces. He had no fault except hypocrisy. Al-Mahdawi said: Al-Asfar was a man from Abyssinia who had daughters who were the most beautiful in their time, and he was in the land of the Romans. It was said that they were called that because the Abyssinians defeated the Romans, and daughters were born to them who took from the whiteness of the Romans and the blackness of the Abyssinians, so they were yellow for honey. Ibn Atiyyah said: In Ibn Ishaq’s statement there is weakness. Al-Tabari attributed that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Go out and capture the daughters of the yellow ones. Then his grandfather said to him: Give us permission and do not tempt us with women. This is a different approach from the first, and it is more like hypocrisy and hostility. When it was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Banu Salamah - and al-Jadd ibn Qays was one of them: Who is your master, O Banu Salamah? They said: Jadd ibn Qays, but he is a miserly coward. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What disease is more deadly than miserliness? Your master is the white young man, Bishr ibn al-Bara’ ibn Ma’rur. Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari said about him: And Bishr bin Al-Baraa was blackened for his generosity, and Bishr bin Al-Baraa deserved to be blackened If the delegation came to him, he would take his money and say, Take it, I will be back tomorrow. “Indeed, they have fallen into temptation.” That is, they have fallen into sin and disobedience, which is hypocrisy and falling behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers. That is, their path to the Fire. It surrounds them.
9:50: The Almighty's saying: If good befalls you, it distresses them is a condition and a reward, and likewise But if a disaster befalls you, they say, We had taken our precaution beforehand, and they turn away is in apposition to it. The good is the spoils and victory. The disaster is defeat. The meaning of their saying: We took our precaution beforehand is that we took precautions for ourselves and were determined, so we did not go out to fight. And they turn away means from faith. And they are happy, meaning they are pleased with that.
9:51: The Almighty said: Say, 'Nothing will ever happen to us except what God has decreed for us.' It was said: In the Preserved Tablet. It was also said: What He informed us of in the Book of Who I am. Either we are victorious, and victory is a good thing for us, or we are killed, and martyrdom is a greater good thing for us. The meaning is that everything is by fate and destiny. It was mentioned in Al-A'raf that knowledge, destiny, and the Book are the same. He is our Master means our Supporter. And trust is entrusting the matter to Him. The majority read yasabana with the accusative of lan. Abu Ubaidah narrated that some Arabs use it with certainty. Talhah ibn Masraf read hal yasabana. It was narrated from A'yan, the judge of Rayy, that he read Say, 'Nothing will ever happen to us except what God has decreed for us' with a doubled nun. This is a mistake, as the nun does not emphasize what was a predicate. If this was in Talhah's reading, it would have been permissible. God the Almighty said: Will his plot ever remove that which enrages him? (al-Hajj 22:15).
9:52: The Almighty says: "Say: Do you wait for us?" The Kufians assimilate the lam into the ta'. As for the lam of the definite article, it is not permissible except to assimilate, as God the Almighty said: The repentant (al-Tawbah 9:112) due to the frequency of the lam of the definite article in their speech. And assimilation is not permissible in His statement: "Say: Come" (Al-An'am: 151) because qul is a weak word, so they did not combine two defects on it. And awaiting is waiting. It is said: tarabbas bi al-ta'am, meaning he waited for it until the price increases. And al-husna is the feminine of al-ahsan. The singular of al-husnayyin is husna, and the plural of al-husna, and it is not permissible to pronounce it except as a definite article. It is not said: I saw a woman who is husna. What is meant by al-husnayyin is booty and martyrdom, according to Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others. The word is an interrogative and the meaning is a rebuke. And we are waiting for you that God will afflict you with a punishment from Him meaning a punishment that will destroy you, as He afflicted the nations before you. Or by our hands meaning we are given permission to fight you. Then wait is a threat and warning. That is, wait for the appointments of Satan, for we are waiting for the appointments of God.
9:53: It has four issues: First: Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Al-Jadd bin Qais when he said: Give me permission to sit down, and this is what I have to help you with. The word spend is a command, and its meaning is a condition and a reward. This is how the Arabs use it in such cases, they use or, as the poet said: Treat us well or badly, we are not to be blamed or criticized if you are harsh. The meaning is whether you did wrong or good, we are as you know. The meaning of the verse is: whether you spend willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you. Then the Almighty explained why it will not be accepted from them, saying: And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they disbelieved in God and His Messenger. So in this there is the clearest evidence, which is: Second: If the actions of the disbeliever are righteous, such as maintaining kinship ties, mending the brokenhearted, and helping the needy, he will not be rewarded for them or benefit from them in the Hereafter, but he will be fed with them in this world. The evidence for this is what Muslim narrated on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, Ibn Jud’an used to maintain kinship ties and feed the poor during the pre-Islamic period. Will that benefit him? He said: It will not benefit him, for he never said, O Lord, forgive my sin on the Day of Judgment. Anas narrated that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “God does not wrong a believer for a good deed he is given in this world and is rewarded for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed with the good deeds he did for God in this world, until when he reaches the Hereafter, he will have no good deed for which he can be rewarded.” This is the text. Then it was said: Is it necessary, by virtue of this true promise, that the unbeliever be fed and given for his good deeds in this world, or is that restricted to the will of God mentioned in His saying: We hasten for him therein whatever We will for whomever We intend (al-Isra’ 17:18)? This is the correct of the two opinions, and God knows best. Calling what the unbeliever does a good deed is only according to the unbeliever’s opinion, otherwise it is not a valid act of worship from him, due to the lack of its validating condition, which is faith. Or it is called a good deed because it outwardly resembles the image of the believer’s good deed. There are also two opinions. Third: If it is said: Muslim narrated on the authority of Hakim bin Hizam that he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Messenger of God, do you think that there is a reward for the things that I used to do in the pre-Islamic era, such as charity, freeing slaves, or maintaining family ties? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have become Muslim, despite the good I have already done. We say: His statement: I have become Muslim, despite the good I have already done, appears to contradict the fundamental principles, because it is not valid for a disbeliever to draw near to God Almighty and be rewarded for his obedience, because one of the conditions of the one drawing near to God is that he should know the one to whom he is drawing near, so if the condition is not met, the validity of the condition is negated. So the meaning of the hadith is: You acquired beautiful characteristics in the pre-Islamic era that gave you beautiful habits in Islam. That is because Hakim, may God be pleased with him, lived for one hundred and twenty years, sixty in Islam and sixty in the pre-Islamic era, so he freed one hundred slaves in the pre-Islamic era and carried one hundred camels? And he did the same in Islam. This is clear. It has been said: It is not far-fetched in God’s generosity to reward him for doing that with Islam, just as He forgives him for the sins he committed while he was a disbeliever. Rather, he is not rewarded for the one who did not convert to Islam or repent, and died a disbeliever. This is the apparent meaning of the hadith. And it is correct, God willing. The absence of a condition of faith in the absence of reward for the good he does, then converts to Islam and dies a Muslim, is not a mental condition that does not change. And God is too generous to waste his work if his Islam is good. Al-Harbi interpreted the hadith in this sense and said: I converted to Islam on the basis of what I have done before, meaning whatever good you have done before, that is for you. Just as you say: I converted to Islam on the basis of a thousand dirhams, meaning on the basis that I will keep them for myself. And God knows best. Fourth - If it is said: Muslim narrated "on the authority of Al-Abbas who said: I said, O Messenger of God, Abu Talib used to protect you and support you, did that benefit him? He said: Yes, I found him in the depths of the Fire so I took him out to the shallows." It was said to him: It is not far-fetched that the disbeliever will be relieved of some of the punishment because of the good he did, but with the addition of intercession, as came in the case of Abu Talib. As for others, the revelation informed us in His saying: So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them (al-Muddaththir 74:48). And He said, informing us about the disbelievers: So we have no intercessors * Nor a close friend (Ash-Shu'ara: 101). Muslim narrated "on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned his uncle Abu Talib in his presence and said: Perhaps my intercession will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection, so he will be placed in the shallows of the Fire up to his ankles, and his brain will boil from it." From the hadith of Al-Abbas - may God be pleased with him -: And were it not for me, he would have been in the lowest level of the Fire. God Almighty says: Indeed, you were a wicked people, meaning disbelievers.
9:54: It has three issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except that they The first an is in the accusative case, and the second is in the nominative case. The meaning is: And nothing prevented their expenditures from being accepted from them except their disbelief. The Kufians read anhu with a ya because expenditures and spending are one and the same. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And they do not come to prayer except lazily. Ibn Abbas said: If he is in a group, he prays, and if he is alone, he does not pray. He is the one who does not hope for reward for prayer, nor fear punishment for abandoning it. So hypocrisy inevitably leads to laziness in worship. We have already discussed all of this in the chapter on women. We have already mentioned the hadith of Al-Ala’ there, with emphasis. Praise be to God. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And they do not spend except reluctantly, because they consider it a loss and withholding it a gain. If this is the case, then it is not accepted and there is no reward for it, according to what was mentioned above.
9:55: That is, do not approve of what We have given them and do not incline towards it, for it is a lure. God only intends to punish them thereby. Al-Hasan said: The meaning is by giving zakat and spending in the way of God. This is the choice of Al-Tabari. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: There is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is do not be impressed by their wealth or their children in this worldly life, for God only intends to punish them with it in the Hereafter. This is the opinion of most Arab scholars, as mentioned by Al-Nahhas. It was said: He punishes them by the fatigue of gathering. According to this interpretation and the opinion of Al-Hasan, there is no inversion in it, and it is good. It was said: The meaning is do not be impressed by their wealth or their children, for God only intends to punish them with it in this world because they are hypocrites, so they spend reluctantly and are punished for what they spend. And their souls will perish while they are disbelievers. This is a text indicating that God intends for them to die as disbelievers, and the decree has preceded that.
9:56: And they swear by God that they are of you. He explained that one of the characteristics of the hypocrites is swearing that they are believers. Similar to this is When the hypocrites come to you, they say, 'We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God.' (al-Munafiqun 63:1) the verse. The difference is fear, meaning that they fear revealing what they are and being killed.
9:57: The Almighty said: If they could find refuge This is how the pause is. And in the script with two alifs: the first is a hamza, and the second is a replacement for the tanween, and this is how I saw part of it. And refuge is the fortress, according to Qatada and others. Ibn Abbas: the amulet, and they are the same. It is said: I sought refuge in him, he sought refuge with the movement and refuge and I sought refuge in him have the same meaning. And the place is also refuge and refuge. And seeking refuge is compulsion. And I forced him to do something, I compelled him to it. And I sought refuge in my affair to God, I entrusted it. And Amr ibn Laja' al-Tamimi the poet, according to al-Jawhari. Or caves is the plural of cave, from ghar yaghir. Al-Akhfash said: And it is permissible for it to be from aghar yaghir, as the poet said: Praise be to God, good evening and good morning Ibn Abbas said: Caves are caves and tunnels, and they are the places where one hides, and from this comes the cave of water and the cave of the spring. Or entrance is a passive participle from the entrance, meaning a path in which we hide by entering, and he repeated it because of the difference in pronunciation. An-Nahhas said: The original is madakhil. The taa was changed to dal, because the dal is abandoned and the taa is voiced and they are from the same point of articulation. It was said: The original is mutadakhil on mutafa'il, as in Abi's reading: aw mutadakhilan, and its meaning is entering after entering, meaning people who enter with them. Al-Mahdawi: mutadakhilan from tadakhul like tafa'ala if he takes the trouble to enter. And from Abi also: mandakhilan from indakhul, and it is anomalous, because its triliteral is not accepted by Sibawayh and his companions. Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ibn Muhaisin read: aw madakhilan with a fatha on the meem and a sukoon on the dal. Al-Zajjaj said: It is read aw madakhilan with a damma on the meem and a sukoon on the dal. The first is from dakhala yadhuqul. The second is from adhaqa yadhuqul. Thus is the source, place and time, as Sibawayh recited: Ibn Hammam cave on the Khath'ama neighborhood It was narrated on the authority of Qatada, Isa and Al-A’mash, or Madkhal, with emphasis on the dal and kha. The majority use emphasis on the dal alone, meaning a place where they put themselves. So these are six readings. They turned back to it means they returned to it. While they were running fast means they were hurrying, nothing could stop their faces. From the word jamah the horse ran fast if the bridle could not stop it. The poet said: Swimming wildly and bringing it like a commotion of burning palm fronds Meaning: If they found any of these mentioned things, they would have quickly fled to it, escaping from the Muslims.
9:58: The Almighty said: And among them is he who slanders you concerning the charities meaning he criticizes you, on the authority of Qatada. Al-Hasan: He finds fault with you. Mujahid said: He finds fault with you and asks you. Al-Nahhas: The opinion of the linguists is the opinion of Qatada and Al-Hasan. It is said: Lamazah yalmazah if he finds fault with him. Lamzah in the language is a fault in secret. Al-Jawhari said: Lamzah is a fault, and its origin is a gesture with the eye and the like, and Lamzah yalmazah and yalmazah and it was read with them And among them is he who slanders you concerning the charities. A man is a lamaz and lamzah meaning a faultfinder. It is also said: Lamzah yalmazah if he pushed him and hit him. The hamzah is like the lamzah. The hamzah and the hammaz are the faultfinders, and the hamzah is like it. It is said: a man is a hamzah and a woman is also a hamzah. And hamzah means pushing him and hitting him. Then it was said: slander is to the face, and slander is behind the back. God described a group of hypocrites who criticized the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for distributing charity, and claimed that they were poor so he would give them some. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri said: “While the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) was distributing wealth, Harqoos ibn Zuhair - the origin of the Khawarij - who was called Dhu al-Huwaysira al-Tamimi came to him and said: ‘Be just, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘Woe to you! Who will be just if I am not just?’ Then the verse was revealed.” A sahih hadith narrated by Muslim with the same meaning. “At that point, ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him said: ‘Leave me, O Messenger of God, so I can kill this hypocrite.’ He said: ‘God forbid that people should say that I kill my companions. This man and his companions recite the Qur’an, but it does not go near their throats. They pass through it as an arrow passes through its target.”
9:59: The Almighty’s saying: And if they had been satisfied with what God had given them, the answer to if is omitted, the meaning being that it would have been better for them.
9:60: It contains thirty issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Zakat is only for the poor. God Almighty has given some people wealth over others as a blessing from Him upon them, and He has made their gratitude for that by giving a share to those who have no wealth, on His behalf, the Almighty, in what He included in His saying: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision. (Hud 11:6) Second: The Almighty’s saying: For the poor clarifies the recipients of the charity and the place, so that it does not go beyond them, then the choice is up to whom to divide it. This is the saying of Malik, Abu Hanifa and their companions. Just as it is said: The saddle is for the beast and the door is for the house. Al-Shafi’i said: The lam is the lam of ownership, like when you say: The money is for Zaid, Amr and Bakr, so there must be equality between the two mentioned. Al-Shafi’i and his companions said: This is as if he bequeathed it to specific categories or to specific people. They argued with his wording that it requires restricting the charity to the eight categories, and they supported this with Al-Bukhari: “The hadith of Ziyad bin Al-Harith Al-Sada’i, who said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sending an army to my people, so I said: O Messenger of God, hold back your army, for I am yours with their Islam and obedience, and I wrote to my people and their Islam and obedience came. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O brother of Sada’, the one obeyed by his people. I said: Rather, God has bestowed His favor upon them and guided them. He said: Then a man came to him asking him about charity, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: God was not pleased with the ruling of a prophet or anyone else in charity until He divided it into eight parts, so if you are one of those parts, I will give you.” Narrated by Abu Dawud and Al-Daraqutni. The wording is from Al-Daraqutni. It was narrated from Zaid Al-Abidin that he said: God, the Most High, knew the amount of zakat to be paid and what would suffice for these categories, and He made it a right for all of them, so whoever prevents them from that is unjust to them and their provision. Our scholars adhered to the words of God Almighty: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good, but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you (al-Baqarah 2:271). Whenever charity is mentioned in the Qur’an, it is an obligatory charity. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have been commanded to take alms from your rich and give them to your poor. This is a text mentioning one of the eight categories in the Qur’an and Sunnah, and it is the opinion of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ali, Ibn Abbas, and Hudhayfah. A group of the Tabi’un said the same. They said: It is permissible to give it to the eight categories, and to whichever category it is given, it is permissible. Al-Munhal ibn Amr narrated on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish on the authority of Hudhayfah regarding his statement: Alms are only for the poor and the needy, he said: God only mentioned these alms so that you would know, and whichever category you give them to, it will suffice you. Saeed ibn Jubayr narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Alms are only for the poor and the needy, he said: Whichever category you give them to, it will suffice you. This is the opinion of al-Hasan, Ibrahim, and others. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: Malik even claimed consensus on this. I said: He means the consensus of the Companions, for it is not known that they disagreed with what Abu Omar said, and God knows best. Ibn al-Arabi: What we have made a criterion between us and them is that the nation agreed that if each category was given its share, it would not be necessary to generalize it, so the generalization of categories is the same. And God knows best. Third: Linguists and jurists differed on the difference between the poor and the needy in nine opinions. Yaqub bin Al-Sikkit, Al-Qatabi and Yunus bin Habib went to the view that the poor is in a better situation than the needy. They said: The poor is the one who has some of what is sufficient for him and sustains him, and the needy is the one who has nothing, and they argued with the saying of Al-Ra’i: As for the poor man whose milk was according to the children, he was not left with a slave. This was the opinion of some linguists and hadith scholars, including Abu Hanifa and Judge Abdul Wahhab. Al-Wafaq is the agreement between two things, like the union. It is said: Habatuhu wafaqa ‘alayhi wa ‘ayyalihi meaning that it has milk sufficient for them, with no surplus, according to Al-Jawhari. Others said the opposite, making the poor person better off than the needy. They cited as evidence the words of God the Almighty: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea (al-Kahf 18:79). So He informed that they had a ship from the ships of the sea. And it may be worth a sum of money. They supported this with what was narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he sought refuge from poverty. It was narrated from him that he said: O God, let me live as a poor person and let me die as a poor person. If the poor person was in a worse state than the poor person, then the two reports would contradict each other, as it is impossible for him to seek refuge from poverty and then ask for something worse off than it, and God answered his prayer and took him while he had money from what God had bestowed upon him, but he did not have enough to cover his expenses, and that is why he mortgaged his armor. They said: As for the shepherd’s house, there is no proof in it, because it was only mentioned that the poor man had a milking cow in a certain condition. They said: The meaning of the poor man in the speech of the Arabs is the destitute whose back has been torn from his back due to extreme poverty, and there is no condition more severe than this. And God has informed us about them in His saying: They are not able to move about in the land (al-Baqarah 2:273). And they cited as evidence the saying of the poet: When Labad saw the light, he flew up and raised his flag like a helpless pauper. That is, he could not fly, so he became like someone whose backbone had been severed and stuck to the ground. This was the opinion of Al-Asma'i and others, and Al-Tahawi narrated it from the Kufians. It is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi'i and most of his companions. Al-Shafi'i has another opinion: that the poor and the needy are the same, there is no difference between them in meaning even if they differ in name, and this is the third opinion. This is the opinion of Ibn Al-Qasim and the rest of the companions of Malik, and Abu Yusuf said the same. I said: The apparent meaning of the wording indicates that the needy is not the poor, and that they are two categories, except that one category is in greater need than the other. From this perspective, the statement of those who make them one category is close, and God knows best. There is no proof in the statement of those who use as proof the statement of God the Almighty: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people (al-Kahf 18:79). Because it is possible that it was rented to them, just as it is said: This is the house of so-and-so if he lives in it, even if it belongs to someone else. God the Almighty said in describing the people of Hell: And for them are maces of iron (al-Hajj 22:21), so He attributed it to them. God the Almighty also said: And do not give your property to the foolish (An-Nisa’: 5). And the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Once he sold a slave and he had money. It is very common for something to be attributed to him but not to him. From this is their saying: the door of the house, the saddle of the animal, the saddle of the horse, and the like. It is permissible to call them poor people as a sign of mercy and sympathy, as someone who is tested by a calamity or is driven into a disaster is called poor. In the hadith: Poor people of Hell and the poet said: Poor people of love, even their graves are covered with the dust of humiliation among the graves. As for what he interpreted from his saying, peace be upon him: O God, let me live poor, the hadith narrated by Anas, it is not like that. Rather, the meaning here is: humility before God in which there is no arrogance, pride, haughtiness, arrogance, or evil. Abu al-Atahiya did well when he said: If you want the most honorable person in the nation, look at a king dressed as a pauper. He who has great desire for God and he is fit for this world and for religion He is not a questioner, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked asking questions and forbade them, and he said about a black woman who refused to move out of the way for him. Leave her, for she is a tyrant. As for the Almighty’s saying: For the poor who are restricted in the cause of God, unable to move about in the land, it is not impossible that they have something. And God knows best. And what the companions of Malik and al-Shafi’i went to, that they are equal, is good. Close to it is what Malik said in the book of Ibn Sahnoon, he said: The poor is the needy who is self-sufficient, and the destitute is the beggar, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas and al-Zuhri said it, and Ibn Sha’ban chose it and it is the fourth opinion. And a fifth opinion - Muhammad ibn Maslama said: The poor is the one who has a home and a servant to someone lower than that. And the destitute is the one who has no money. I said: This statement is the opposite of what was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, and a man asked him and said: Are we not from the poor immigrants? Abdullah said to him: Do you have a wife to whom you can take refuge? He said: Yes. He said: Do you have a home to live in? He said: Yes. He said: Then you are from the rich. He said: Then I have a servant. He said: Then you are from the kings. A sixth statement - narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The poor are from the immigrants, and the needy are from the Bedouins who did not immigrate, and Ad-Dahhak said it. A seventh statement - which is that the needy is the one who is humble and submissive even if he does not ask. And the poor is the one who endures and accepts something secretly and does not humble himself, said Ubaidullah bin Al-Hasan. An eighth statement was said by Mujahid, Ikrimah and Az-Zuhri - the poor are the wanderers, and the poor are the poor Muslims. A ninth statement was also said by Ikrimah - that the poor are the poor Muslims, and the needy are the poor People of the Book. And it will come. Fourth: The benefit of the disagreement over the poor and needy, whether they are one category or more, appears in the case of someone who bequeaths a third of his wealth to so-and-so and to the poor and needy. So whoever says they are one category says: So-and-so gets half of the third and the poor and needy get half of the second third. And whoever says they are two categories, the third is divided between them into thirds. Fifth: Scholars have differed on the limit of poverty in which it is permissible to take - after the consensus of most of the scholars who have memorized it - that whoever has a house and a servant that he cannot do without may take from the zakat, and the giver may give to him. Malik used to say: If there is no surplus in the price of the house and the servant from what he needs from them, then it is permissible for him to take, otherwise it is not permissible, as mentioned by Ibn al-Mundhir. Al-Nakha’i and al-Thawri said the same as Malik. Abu Hanifa said: Whoever has twenty dinars or two hundred dirhams should not take from the zakat. The nisab was considered based on the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): I was commanded to take charity from your rich and give it to your poor. This is clear, and al-Mughirah narrated it from Malik. Al-Thawri, Ahmad, Ishaq and others said: Whoever has fifty dirhams or its equivalent in gold should not take, and he should not be given more than fifty dirhams from it unless he is in debt, as stated by Ahmad and Ishaq. The evidence for this statement is what al-Daraqutni narrated from Abdullah ibn Mas’ud from the Prophet (peace be upon him), who said: Charity is not permissible for a man who has fifty dirhams. In its chain of transmission is Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, who is weak, and from him is Bakr ibn Khunais, who is also weak. Hakim ibn Jubayr narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly, and he said: Fifty dirhams. Hakim ibn Jubayr is weak, and Shu’bah and others abandoned it. This was stated by al-Daraqutni, may God have mercy on him. Abu Omar said: This hadith is attributed to Hakim ibn Jubayr, and he is rejected. It was narrated on the authority of Ali and Abdullah, who said: Charity is not permissible for a man who has fifty dirhams or their value in gold. This was mentioned by al-Daraqutni. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: He who has forty dirhams should not take it. Al-Waqidi narrated it on the authority of Malik. The evidence for this statement is what al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever asks people for something while he is rich will come on the Day of Resurrection with bruises and scratches on his face. It was said, ‘O Messenger of God, what is his wealth?’ He said, ‘Forty dirhams.’” And in the hadith of Malik, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasa’, on the authority of a man from Banu Asad, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever among you asks while he has an ounce or its equivalent, he has asked insistently. An ounce is forty dirhams. The well-known report from Malik is what Al-Qasim narrated from him that he was asked: Is zakat given to someone who has forty dirhams? He said: Yes. Abu Omar said: It is possible that the first is someone who is strong enough to earn and manage his affairs well. The second is weak enough to earn, or someone who has children. And God knows best. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr said: Whoever is strong enough to earn and work, with a strong body and good management, to the point that he is independent of people, then giving him charity is forbidden. He cited as evidence the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Charity is not permissible for the rich or the wealthy. Narrated by Abdullah bin Omar, and included by Abu Dawood, Al-Tirmidhi, and Al-Darqutni. Jabir narrated that he said: “A charity came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the people took it from him. He said: It is not suitable for the rich, the healthy, or the worker.” Narrated by Ad-Daraqutni. Abu Dawud narrated: “On the authority of Ubaydullah bin Adi bin Al-Khayyar, who said: Two men informed me that they came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) during the Farewell Pilgrimage while he was distributing the charity and asked him for some of it. He looked up and down and saw that we were both strong. He said: If you wish, I will give it to you. There is no share in it for the rich or the strong, earning person.” Because he had become rich through his earnings, just as others are rich with their money, so each of them became independent of asking. Ibn Khuwayzmand said the same, and he narrated it from the school of thought. This should not be relied upon, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to give it to the poor, and its being suspended over time is invalid. Abu ‘Eisa At-Tirmidhi said in his Jami’: If a man is strong and in need and has nothing, and he gives him charity, it is sufficient for the one giving charity according to the scholars. The interpretation of the hadith according to some scholars is based on the issue. Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: The apparent meaning indicates that this is permissible, because he is poor despite his strength and physical health. Abu Hanifa and his companions said the same. Ubaydullah ibn al-Hasan said: Whoever does not have enough to sustain him for a year should be given zakat.
