His evidence is what Ibn Shihab narrated on the authority of Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to save from what God had bestowed upon him a year’s sustenance, then he would spend what was beyond that on grazing animals and weapons, in accordance with the words of God, the Most High: And He found you poor and made you rich (al-Duha 93:8). Some scholars said: Everyone can take from the zakat what he needs. Some people said: Whoever has dinner for a night is rich. This was narrated on the authority of Ali. They used as evidence the hadith of Ali on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever asks a question out of apparent wealth will gain a great deal of Hellfire. They said: O Messenger of God, what is apparent wealth? He said: A night’s dinner. Narrated by Al-Daraqutni, who said: In its chain of transmission is Amr ibn Khalid, who is rejected. Narrated by Abu Dawud on the authority of Sahl ibn Al-Hanzaliyyah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in it: Whoever asks while he has enough to satisfy him, he only asks for more from the Fire. Al-Nufaili said in another place: From the embers of Hellfire. They said: O Messenger of God, what will satisfy him? Al-Nufaili said in another place: What is the wealth that does not require asking? He said: The amount that will feed him breakfast and dinner. Al-Nufaili said in another place: That he has enough to eat for a day and a night, or a night and a day. I said: This is what came in explaining the poverty in which taking is permissible. The general term poor does not mean that it is specific to Muslims without the People of the Covenant, but the hadiths have agreed that alms are taken from the rich Muslims and given to their poor. Ikrimah said: The poor are the poor Muslims, and the needy are the poor of the People of the Book. Abu Bakr Al-Eisa said: Omar bin Al-Khattab saw a blind dhimmi thrown at the gate of the city, so Omar said to him: What is the matter with you? He said: They hired me for this jizya, until when my sight went away, they left me and I have no one to return anything to me. Omar said: Then you are not fair, so he ordered that he be given his food and what would be good for him. Then he said: This is one of those about whom God Almighty said: Zakat is only for the poor and the needy (Al-Anfal 2:10). They are the people of the Book at the time. When God Almighty said: Zakat is only for the poor and the needy verse, and compared the sentence with the sentence, which is the sentence of charity, with the sentence of the disbursement, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained that, so “he said to Muadh when he sent him to the right: Tell them that God has imposed upon them charity, which is taken from their rich and given to their poor.” So the people of each country were given the zakat of their country. Abu Dawud narrated: “Ziyad or some of the princes sent Imran bin Husayn to collect the alms tax. When he returned, he said to Imran: Where is the money? He said: You sent me for the money! We took it from where we used to take it during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we put it where we used to put it during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Ad-Daraqutni and At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Awn bin Abi Juhayfah on the authority of his father who said: The tax collector of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us and took the alms tax from our rich and distributed it to our poor. I was an orphan boy and he gave me a camel from it. At-Tirmidhi said: There is a good hadith on this topic on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Sixth - Scholars have differed regarding the transfer of zakat from its place, with three opinions: It is not to be transferred, as stated by Sahnoon and Ibn al-Qasim, and this is the correct opinion based on what we have mentioned. Ibn al-Qasim also said: If some of it is transferred due to necessity, I see it as correct. It was narrated from Sahnoon that he said: If the imam is informed that there is a great need in some country, it is permissible for him to transfer some of the charity due to someone else to it, because if need arises, it must be given precedence over someone who is not in need. "A Muslim is a brother to a Muslim. He does not hand him over or wrong him." The second opinion: It is transferred. Malik also said this. The evidence for this opinion is what was narrated that Muadh said to the people of Yemen: Bring me a fifth or not, so that I may take it from you instead of corn and barley in zakat, for it is easier for you and more beneficial for the emigrants in Madinah. It was narrated by Al-Daraqutni and others. The fifth is a common word, and here it refers to a garment five cubits long. It is said that it was named thus because the first one to do it was a king of the kings of Yemen, as Ibn Faris mentioned in Al-Mujmal and Al-Jawhari also. There are two proofs in this hadith: The first is what we mentioned about transferring the zakat from Yemen to Madinah, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would take charge of distributing it. This is supported by the Almighty’s saying: Zakat is only for the poor, and He did not differentiate between the poor of one country and the poor of another. And God knows best. The second is taking the value in zakat. There are different narrations from Malik about taking the value in zakat, as he permitted it once and prohibited it another time, so the basis for the permissibility - which is the opinion of Abu Hanifa - is this hadith. It was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari from the hadith of Anas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever has a camel whose zakat is a young camel, but he does not have a young camel, but he has a ḥaqqah, then it is taken from him as much as we can of two sheep or twenty dirhams. The hadith. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Make them independent of asking on this day, meaning the day of Eid al-Fitr. Rather, he meant that they should be independent of what satisfies their needs, so anything that satisfies their needs is permissible. God the Almighty said: Take from their wealth a charity (al-Tawbah 9:103) and did not specify anything from anything. According to Abu Hanifa, one should not pay a house instead of zakat, such as if he owes five dirhams and he houses a poor person in it for a month, because that is not permissible. He said: Because housing is not wealth. The reason for his statement: The guardian is not sufficient - which is the apparent meaning of the doctrine - is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: For five camels, a sheep, and for forty sheep, a sheep. So he specified the sheep, so if he does not do it, he has not done what was commanded, and if he does not do what was commanded, then the command remains upon him. The third statement: The share of the poor and needy is divided in the place, and the rest of the shares are transferred according to the Imam’s discretion. The first statement is more correct. And God knows best. Seventh: Is the place of the money considered at the time the year is complete and the charity is distributed in it, or the place of the owner since he is the one addressed? There are two opinions. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Khuwayzmandad chose the second in his rulings. He said: Because the person is the one addressed to give it, so the money becomes dependent on him, so the ruling on it must be according to the addressee. Like the wayfarer, who may be rich in his country but poor in another country, so the ruling is for him where he is. Question: There are different narrations from Malik regarding someone who gave to a poor Muslim and then it became clear later that he gave to a slave, an infidel, or a rich person. He said once: It is sufficient for him, and once: It is not sufficient for him. The reason for its permissibility - and it is the most correct - is what Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man said: I will give charity tonight. So he went out with his charity and put it in the hand of an adulteress. In the morning they were talking about giving charity tonight to an adulteress. He said: “O God, praise be to You for an adulteress. I will give charity.” So he went out with his charity and put it in the hand of a rich man. In the morning they were talking about giving charity to a rich man. He said: “O God, praise be to You for a rich man. I will give charity.” So he went out with his charity and put it in the hand of a thief. In the morning they were talking about giving charity to a thief. He said: O God, praise be to You for an adulteress, a rich man, and a thief. So he was brought and it was said to him: “As for your charity, it has been accepted. As for the adulteress, perhaps she will abstain from her adultery with it, and perhaps the rich man will take heed and spend from what God has given him, and perhaps the thief will abstain from stealing with it.” It was narrated that “A man took out the zakat of his wealth and gave it to his father. When morning came, he learned about that and asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said to him: “The reward for your zakat and the reward for maintaining family ties have been written for you, so you have two rewards.” In terms of meaning, it permitted him to exert effort in what he gave. If he makes an effort and gives to someone he thinks is worthy of it, then he has done what is required of him. The reason for his statement: It does not suffice. He did not put it in its rightful place, so it is similar to intentional killing. And because intentional killing and error in guaranteeing money are the same, it is necessary that he guarantee what he destroyed for the poor until he delivers it to them. Eighth: If he pays the zakat when it is due and it is lost without negligence, he is not liable, because he is an agent for the poor. If he pays it after a period of time and it is lost, he is liable, because he delayed it from its due date and it became his responsibility, so he is liable. And God knows best. Ninth: If the Imam is fair in taking and spending, it is not permissible for the owner to take charge of spending himself on the mature or otherwise. It has been said that the zakat on the mature is on its owners. Ibn Al-Majishun said: This is if the spending is for the poor and needy in particular. If it is necessary to spend it on other categories, then no one should distribute it to them except the Imam. There are many branches of this chapter, and these are the most important of them. Tenth - The Almighty’s saying: And those who work on it means the messengers and collectors whom the Imam sends to collect the zakat by appointing someone to do so. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hamid Al-Sa’idi who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) employed a man from the tribe of Asad, called Ibn al-Lutbiyyah, to collect the alms of Banu Salim. When he came, he calculated his account. The scholars differed about the amount they should take, and there are three opinions: Mujahid and al-Shafi’i said: It is the eighth. Ibn ‘Umar and Malik said: They should be given the equivalent of their work as wages, which is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and his companions. They said: Because he has devoted himself to the benefit of the poor, so his sustenance and the sustenance of his helpers are from their money, like a woman who devotes herself to the benefit of her husband, her expenses and the expenses of her followers, whether a servant or two, are on her husband. They are not measured by the price, rather, the sustenance is considered, whether it is an eighth or more, like the judge’s salary. The sustenance of the helpers is not considered in our time, because it is pure extravagance. The third opinion: They should be given from the public treasury. Ibn al-‘Arabi said: This is a correct opinion from Malik ibn Anas, narrated by Ibn Abi Uways and Dawud ibn Sa’id ibn Zanbu’ah, and it is weak in evidence, because God, the Exalted, has explicitly informed us of their share in it, so how can they differ from it based on induction and investigation? The correct opinion is to make an independent judgment about the amount of the wage, because The statement regarding the enumeration of categories was only for the place, not for the beneficiary, as mentioned above. They differed about the worker if he was a Hashemite, so Abu Hanifa forbade him because of his saying, peace be upon him: Charity is not permissible for the family of Muhammad, it is only the filth of the people. This is charity in one respect, because it is part of charity, so it is included in charity in every respect, as an honor and to purify the kinship of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the filth of the people. Malik and Al-Shafi’i permitted his work, and he is given the wage for his work, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali bin Abi Talib as a tax collector, and he sent him as a worker to Yemen to collect zakat, and he appointed a group of Banu Hashim and appointed the caliphs after him as well. And because he was hired for permissible work, it is necessary that the Hashimite and others be equal in it, considering all other industries. The Hanafis said: The hadith of Ali does not state that he was obligated to receive charity, but if he was obligated to receive something else, it is permissible. It was narrated from Malik. Eleventh - The Almighty’s statement: and those who work on it indicates that everything that is from the communal obligations such as the messenger, the writer, the sharer, the tithe-giver, and others, the one who performs it is permitted to take wages for it. This includes the imamate, for although the prayer is directed to all of creation, if some of them precede them from the communal obligations, then there is no doubt that it is permissible to take wages for it. This is the origin of the chapter, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, referred to it when he said: Whatever I leave behind after the expenses of my wives and the maintenance of my workers is charity, said Ibn al-Arabi. Twelfth - The Almighty said: And those whose hearts are to be reconciled. There is no mention of those whose hearts are to be reconciled in the revelation except in the section on charity. They are people who were in the early days of Islam and who were outwardly Muslim. They were reconciled by giving them a share of charity due to their weak faith. Al-Zuhri said: Those whose hearts are to be reconciled are those who converted to Islam from a Jew or a Christian, even if he was rich. Some of the later scholars said: Their description is disputed. It was said: They are a group of disbelievers who bite to reconcile them to Islam. They did not convert to Islam by force or the sword, but rather converted to Islam by giving and kindness. It was said: They are people who converted to Islam outwardly but their hearts were not certain, so they give so that Islam would take root in their hearts. It was said: They are a group of the great polytheists who have followers and give so that their followers would be reconciled to Islam. He said: These statements are similar, and the intention of all of them is to give to those whose Islam cannot be truly taken root except by giving, so it is as if it is a type of jihad. The polytheists are of three types: a type that returns by establishing proof. A type by force. A type by kindness. The Imam who oversees the Muslims uses with each group what he sees as a reason for its salvation and deliverance from disbelief. In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Anas, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said - I mean to the Ansar: I give to men who have recently converted from disbelief, so that I may win them over. The hadith. Ibn Ishaq said: He gave them so that he could win them over and win over their people. They were nobles, so he gave Abu Sufyan ibn Harb one hundred camels, and he gave his son one hundred camels, and he gave Hakim ibn Hizam one hundred camels, and he gave Al-Harith ibn Hisham one hundred camels, and he gave Suhayl ibn Amr one hundred camels, and he gave Huwaytib ibn Abd Al-Uzza one hundred camels, and he gave Safwan ibn Umayya one hundred camels. He also gave Malik ibn Awf and Al-Ala ibn Jariyah. He said: These are the people with the hundreds. He gave men from Quraysh less than one hundred, including Mukhramah ibn Nawfal Al-Zuhri, Umair ibn Wahb Al-Jumahi, and Hisham ibn Amr Al-Amri. Ibn Ishaq said: I do not know what he gave them. He gave Saeed ibn Yarbu’ fifty camels, and he gave Abbas ibn Murdas As-Sulami a few camels, but he was dissatisfied with them. So he said about that: It was a plunder that I saved early on the dowry in Al-Ajra' And I wake people up to sleep, when people are asleep, I do not sleep So my plunder and the plunder of the slaves became between Uyaynah and Al-Aqra’ I was in the war, but I did not give anything and I did not prevent anything. Except for the ones I gave him the number of his four legs There was no fortress or prison that surpassed Mardas in the assembly. I was not lower than either of them, and whoever is lowered today will not be raised. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: Go and cut off his tongue for me. So they gave it to him until he was satisfied, and that was how his tongue was cut off. Abu Omar said: Among those whose hearts were to be reconciled was mentioned Nadir bin Al-Harith bin Alqamah bin Kalda, the brother of Nadir bin Al-Harith who was killed by patience at Badr. Others mentioned that he was among those who migrated to Abyssinia, so if he was one of them, then it is impossible that he was among those whose hearts were to be reconciled. Whoever migrated to the land of Abyssinia was among the first emigrants, those whose faith was firmly rooted in their hearts and fought for it, and not among those who could be reconciled. Abu Omar said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) appointed Malik bin Awf bin Saad bin Yarbu’ Al-Nasri over those of his people from the tribes of Qais who had converted to Islam, and he ordered him to attack Thaqeef, so he did so and made things difficult for them. His Islam and the Islam of those whose hearts were to be reconciled were good, except for Uyaynah bin Hisn, for he was not forgotten. The rest of those who are to be reconciled are distinguished, among them is the good and distinguished one who is united by his virtue, such as Al-Harith ibn Hisham, Hakim ibn Hizam, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Suhayl ibn Amr, and among them are those who are less than these. And God has given preference to the prophets and all of His believing servants, some of them over others, and He knows them best. Malik said: It has reached me that Hakim ibn Hizam took out what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had given him for those whose hearts were to be reconciled, and he gave it in charity after that. I said: Hakim bin Hizam and Huwaytib bin Abdul Uzza each lived for one hundred and twenty years, sixty in Islam and sixty in the pre-Islamic era. I heard our Imam, Sheikh, and Hafiz Abu Muhammad Abdul Azim say: Two people from the Companions lived for sixty years in the pre-Islamic era and sixty years in Islam, and they died in Madinah in the year fifty-four. One of them was Hakim bin Hizam, and he was born inside the Kaaba thirteen years before the Year of the Elephant. The second was Hassan bin Thabit bin Al-Mundhir bin Haram Al-Ansari. This was also mentioned by Abu Omar and Uthman Al-Shahrazuri in his book, Knowing the Types of Hadith Science, and they did not mention anyone else. Huwaytib was mentioned by Abu Al-Faraj Al-Jawzi in his book, Al-Wafa fi Sharaf Al-Mustafa. Abu Omar mentioned him in his book, The Companions, that he witnessed Islam when he was sixty years old, and he died when he was one hundred and twenty years old. He also mentioned Humn bin Awf, the brother of Abdul Rahman bin Awf, that he lived for sixty years in Islam and sixty years in the pre-Islamic era. Muawiyah and his father Abu Sufyan bin Harb were counted among those whose hearts were to be reconciled. As for Muawiyah, it is far-fetched that he was one of them. How could he be one of them when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entrusted him with God’s revelation, its recitation, and his mixing of it himself? As for his situation during the days of Abu Bakr, it is more famous and more apparent than this. As for his father, there is no doubt that he was one of them. There is a difference in their number, and in summary, all of them were believers and there was no disbeliever among them, as mentioned above. And God knows best and is wisest. Thirteenth - The scholars differed about their remaining. Omar, Al-Hassan, Al-Shaabi and others said: This category was cut off with the glory and appearance of Islam. This is well-known from the Maliki school of thought and the people of opinion. Some Hanafi scholars said: When God glorified Islam and its people and cut off the roots of the infidels - may God curse them - the Companions, may God be pleased with them all, agreed during the caliphate of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, that their share should be dropped. A group of scholars said: They will remain, because the Imam may need to win over Islam. Omar only cut them off because he saw the glory of the religion. Yunus said: I asked Al-Zuhri about them and he said: I do not know of any abrogation in that. Abu Jaafar Al-Nahhas said: This ruling is established regarding them. If someone needs to win over Islam and fears that he will harm the Muslims, or it is hoped that his Islam will improve after he is given to him, then he should be given from the charity. Judge Abdul-Wahhab said: If they are needed at some times, they should be given from the charity. Judge Ibn Al-Arabi said: What I have is that if Islam is strong, they should be removed, and if they are needed, they should be given their share as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to give them, because in the Sahih: Islam began as something strange and will return to being strange. Fourteenth - If we conclude that their share is not returned to them, then it is returned to the rest of the categories or what the Imam sees fit. Al-Zuhri said: Half of their share is given to the mosque builders. This is what shows you that the eight categories are not entitled to equal status, and if they were entitled, their share would be dropped with their dropping and would not be returned to others, just as if he made a will for specific people and one of them died, his share would not be returned to the rest of them. And God knows best. Fifteenth - The Almighty said: And for freeing slaves meaning for freeing slaves, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Ibn Omar, and it is the doctrine of Malik and others. It is permissible for the Imam to buy slaves from the money of charity and free them on behalf of the Muslims, and their loyalty will be to the group of Muslims. If the person who pays zakat buys them and frees them, it is permissible. This is the conclusion of the Malikite doctrine, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan, and it was stated by Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Ubaid. Abu Thawr said: The person who pays zakat should not buy a soul from it and free it by virtue of loyalty, and this is the opinion of Al-Shafi'i and the people of opinion and a narration from Malik. The first is correct, because God the Almighty said: And for freeing slaves, so if the slaves have a share of charity, he may buy a slave and free it. There is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that a man may buy a horse and ride it in the way of God. So if he is able to buy a horse with the full amount from zakat, it is permissible for him to buy a slave with the full amount, there is no difference between that. And God knows best. Sixteenth - The Almighty’s saying: And for the necks is the basis for loyalty. Malik said: It is the neck that is freed and its loyalty is to the Muslims, and likewise if the imam frees it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the sale of loyalty and its gift. He, peace be upon him, said: “Loyalty is a bond like the bond of kinship. It cannot be sold or given away.” And he, peace be upon him, said: Loyalty is to the one who freed. Women do not inherit anything from the loyalty, as the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: Women do not inherit anything from the wala’ except what they free or free those whom they freed. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, inherited half from the daughter of Hamza from her freed slave and half from his daughter. If the freed slave leaves male and female children, the wala’ goes to the males of his children and not the females. This is the consensus of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. The wala’ is only inherited by pure agnatic kinship, and women are not agnatic kinship, so they do not inherit anything from the wala’, so understand and you will inherit. Seventeenth - There is a difference of opinion as to whether the freed slave is to be helped by it, and it was said: No. This was narrated from Malik, because when God the Almighty mentioned the slave, it indicated that He meant complete emancipation. As for the freed slave, he is included in the word of the debtors due to the debt of the writing, so he is not included in the slaves. And God knows best. It was narrated from Malik from the narration of the Medinans and Ziyad from him: that the freed slave is to be helped by it at the end of his writing due to what he emancipates. And this is the majority of scholars in interpreting the statement of God the Almighty: And for the slaves. Ibn Wahb, Al-Shafi'i, Al-Layth, Al-Nakha'i and others said the same. Ali bin Musa Al-Qummi Al-Hanafi narrated in his rulings: that they agreed that the freed slave is meant. They differed regarding the emancipation of slaves. Al-Kaya Al-Tabari said and mentioned a clear reason for preventing this, saying: Emancipation is the annulment of ownership and not the transfer of ownership, and what is given to the freed slave is ownership, and it is the right of charity that it is not valid unless ownership is given in it. This is strengthened by the fact that if zakat is paid on behalf of the debtor in his debt without his order, it is not valid because he did not own it, so it is more appropriate that it is not valid in emancipation. He mentioned that in emancipation, loyalty is drawn to herself, and this does not happen when it is paid to a slave who has been paid a contract. He mentioned that if the price of a slave is paid to a slave, the slave does not own him, but if he pays it to his master, then emancipation has become his property. If he pays it after the purchase and emancipation, then he has paid a debt, and this does not count towards zakat. I said: A hadith has been reported that clearly states the meaning of what we mentioned about the permissibility of freeing a slave and helping a freed slave together. It was narrated by Al-Daraqutni on the authority of Al-Baraa’ who said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Guide me to an act that will bring me closer to Paradise and distance me from Hell. He said: If I have shortened the sermon, then the question has become obsolete: freeing a soul and freeing a slave. He said: O Messenger of God, are they not the same? He said: No. Freeing a soul means that you free it alone, and freeing a slave means that you help with its price. And he mentioned the hadith. Eighteenth - They differed about freeing the captives from it. Asbagh said: It is not permissible. This is the opinion of Ibn Al-Qasim. Ibn Habib said: It is permissible, because it is a slave owned by the ownership of slavery, so it goes from slavery to emancipation, and that is more deserving and more appropriate than freeing the slaves that are in our hands, because if freeing a Muslim from the slavery of a Muslim is an act of worship and permissible than charity, then it is more deserving and more appropriate that it be in freeing a Muslim from the slavery and humiliation of an infidel. Nineteenth - The Almighty said: And the debtors are those who are burdened with debt and cannot pay it back, and there is no disagreement about this. Except for the one who calls to prayer foolishly, for he will not be given from it or from anything else unless he repents. And he who has money and a debt that surrounds him with money to pay off his debt will be given from it. If he has no money and a debt, then he is poor and in debt, so he will be given according to both descriptions. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: “A man was struck by a calamity during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the fruits he bought, and his debts increased. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Give him charity. The people gave him charity, but it was not enough to pay off his debt. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to his creditors: Take what you find, and you have nothing but that.” Twenty- It is permissible for someone who is likely to be righteous and virtuous to be given from charity what he can bear if it is obligatory upon him, even if he is rich, if that would be depriving him of his money, like a debtor. This is the opinion of al-Shafi’i and his companions, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others. Those who hold this opinion have cited as evidence the hadith of Qubaysah ibn Mukhariq, who said: “I took on a burden and came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask him about it. He said: ‘Stay until the charity comes to us, and we will order it for you. ’ Then he said: ‘O Qubaysah, begging is not permissible except for one of three: A man who took on a burden, so begging is permissible for him until he obtains it, then he stops; a man who is afflicted with a need that has overwhelmed his wealth, so begging is permissible for him until he obtains a livelihood – or he said, a full livelihood – and a man who is afflicted with poverty until three wise men from his people stand up and say: ‘Poverty has afflicted so begging is permissible for him until he obtains a livelihood – or he said, a full livelihood – so begging other than them, O Qubaysah, is ill-gotten gain that its owner eats ill-gotten. ’” So his saying: ‘Then he stops’ is evidence that he is rich, because the poor person is not required to stop. And God knows best. It was narrated from him, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Begging is not permissible except for one of three: one who is extremely poor, one who has a terrible debt, or one who has a painful blood money.” It was narrated from him, peace be upon him: Charity is not permissible for a rich person except for the five. The hadith will come. Twenty-one - They differed as to whether the debt of the deceased should be paid from it or not. Abu Hanifa said: The debt of the deceased should not be paid from charity. This is the opinion of Ibn Al-Mawaz. Abu Hanifa said: And it should not be given to someone who owes expiation or anything similar from the rights of God Almighty. Rather, the debtor is the one who owes a debt and is imprisoned for it. Our scholars and others said: The debt of the deceased should be paid from it because he is one of the debtors. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have more right over every believer than he has over himself. Whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his family, and whoever leaves behind debt or loss, it is up to me and upon me.” Twenty-second - The Almighty said: And in the way of God and they are the warriors and the place of ribat, they are given what they spend in their war, whether they are rich or poor. This is the opinion of most scholars, and it is the conclusion of the school of Malik, may God have mercy on him. Ibn Omar said: The pilgrims and the worshippers. It is reported from Ahmad and Ishaq, may God have mercy on them, that they said: The way of God is Hajj. In Bukhari: It is mentioned from Abu Las: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, carried us on the camels of charity for Hajj. It is mentioned from Ibn Abbas: He frees from the zakat of his money and gives for Hajj. Abu Muhammad Abdul Ghani Al-Hafiz narrated: Muhammad bin Muhammad Al-Khayash narrated to us, Abu Ghassan Malik bin Yahya narrated to us, Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, Mahdi bin Maymun narrated to us, from Muhammad bin Abi Yaqub, from Abdul Rahman bin Abi Naam, whose nickname is Abu Al-Hakam, who said: I was sitting with Abdullah bin Omar when a woman came to him and said to him: O Abu Abdul Rahman, my husband has bequeathed his money for the way of God. Ibn Omar said: So it is as he said, in the way of God. I said to him: What you asked about has only increased her sorrow. He said: So what do you command me, O son of Abi? Yes, I command her to give it to these armies who go out and spread corruption in the land and block the way! He said: I said: So what do you command her? He said: I command her to give it to righteous people, to the pilgrims to the Sacred House of God. They are the delegation of the Most Gracious. They are the delegation of the Most Gracious. They are the delegation of the Most Gracious. They are not like the delegation of Satan. He said it three times. I said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, and what is the delegation of Satan? He said: People who enter upon these leaders and spread gossip to them, and spread lies among the Muslims, so they are rewarded and given gifts. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hakam said: And from the charity is given for the mounts and weapons and what is needed of war equipment, and to keep the enemy away from the estate, because it is all from the path of conquest and its benefit. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave one hundred camels in the incident of Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah to extinguish the rebellion. I said: Abu Dawud narrated this hadith on the authority of Bashir bin Yasar, that a man from the Ansar called Sahl bin Abi Hathmah told him. “The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) paid him a hundred camels of charity, meaning the blood money of the Ansari who was killed in Khaybar.” Isa bin Dinar said: Charity is permissible for a warrior in the cause of God, who is in need during his battle and whose wealth and delegation are absent from him. He said: It is not permissible for a warrior who has his own wealth with him, but it is permissible for one whose wealth is absent from him. This is the view of al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq and the majority of scholars. Abu Hanifa and his two companions said: The warrior is not given anything unless he is poor and stranded. This is an addition to the text, and in his view, an addition to the text is abrogation, and abrogation can only be by the Qur’an or a mutawatir report, and that is absent here. Rather, in the authentic Sunnah there is the opposite of that from his (peace be upon him) saying: “Charity is not permissible for a rich person except for five: a fighter in the cause of God, or a worker for it, or a debtor, or a man who bought it with his own money, or a man who has a poor neighbor and gives charity to the poor person, and the poor person gives a gift to the rich person.” Narrated by Malik in a mursal form on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar. And Ma’mar narrated it on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So this hadith explains the meaning of the verse, and that it is permissible for some of the rich to take it, and explains the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Charity is not permissible for the rich or the one who has a sound financial position, because his statement is general and not general, as evidenced by the five rich mentioned. Ibn al-Qasim used to say: It is not permissible for the rich to take from charity what will help him in jihad and spend it in the way of God, but it is only permissible for the poor. He said: Likewise, it is not permissible for the debtor to take from charity what will protect his wealth and pay off his debt, even if he is independent of it. He said: If the fighter is in need of charity during his raid and he is wealthy and has money that is absent from him, he does not take anything from charity and borrows, and when he reaches his country, he pays it from his money. All of this was mentioned by Ibn Habib from Ibn al-Qasim, and he claimed that Ibn Nafi’ and others disagreed with him on that. Abu Zaid and others narrated from Ibn al-Qasim that he said: The fighter is given from zakat even if he has enough money with him during his raids and he is wealthy in his country. This is the correct view, based on the apparent meaning of the hadith: Charity is not permissible for the rich except for five. Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik that it is given to the fighters and the places of ribat, whether they are poor or wealthy. Twenty-third - The Almighty’s saying: And the wayfarer. The way is the road, and the traveler is attributed to it because he is constantly on it and passes through it, as the poet said: If you ask me about love, then I am love, the son of love, the brother of love, and its father. What is meant is that the one who has lost all means of support while traveling from his country, his hometown, and his wealth, is given from it even if he is rich in his country, and he is not obligated to occupy his conscience with a loan. Malik said in the book of Ibn Sahnoon: If he finds someone to lend him, he is not given. The first is more correct, because he is not obligated to be under the favor of anyone, and he has found the favor of God Almighty. If he has what makes him rich, then there are two narrations regarding the permissibility of taking it for him because he is a wayfarer: The well-known is that he is not given, and if he takes it, he is not obligated to return it when he reaches his country or expel it. Twenty-fourth: If he comes and claims one of the attributes, will his statement be accepted or not and will he be told to prove what he says? As for religion, he must prove it, and as for the rest of the attributes, the apparent situation testifies in his favor and is sufficient in them. The evidence for that is two authentic hadiths narrated by the people of authenticity, and it is the apparent meaning of the Qur’an. Muslim narrated on the authority of Jarir who said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the middle of the day. He said: Then came to him a group of barefoot, naked people, wearing leopard prints or cloaks, and carrying swords, most of them from Mudar, in fact all of them from Mudar. The face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became red when he saw their poverty. So he entered and then came out and ordered Bilal to call the adhan and the iqamah and prayed. Then he delivered a sermon and said: O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you (An-Nisa’: 1) and the verse in al-Hashr 59:And let a soul look to what it has put forth for tomorrow (al-Hashr 59:18). A man gave in charity from his dinar, from his dirham, from his garment, from a sa’ of wheat - until he said - even half a date. He said: Then came a man from the Ansar with a bag that was almost too big for him, rather it was too big for him. He said: Then the people followed one another until I saw two piles of food and clothing, until I saw the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, beaming as if it were gilded. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he (peace be upon him) said: “Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam will have its reward and the reward of those who act upon it after him, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. And whoever establishes a bad practice in Islam will bear its burden and the burden of those who act upon it after him, without that detracting from their burden in the slightest.” So the Prophet (peace be upon him) was satisfied with their apparent condition and urged them to give charity, and he did not ask them for proof, nor did he investigate whether they had money or not. Similar to it is the hadith of a leper, a bald man, and a blind man, narrated by Muslim and others. This is its wording: On the authority of Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) say: “There were three among the Children of Israel: a leper, a bald man, and a blind man. God wanted to test them, so He sent an angel to them. He came to the leper and said, ‘What would you like best?’ He said, ‘Good color and good skin, and that which people have made unclean of me will go away.’ He rubbed him and his uncleanness went away and he was given a good color and good skin. He said, ‘Which wealth would you like best?’ He said, ‘Camels’ - or he said, ‘cows’ - Isaac was uncertain - except that the leper or the bald man said, ‘camels’ and the other said, ‘cows’. He said, ‘So he was given a ten-year-old female camel.’ He said, ‘May God bless you in it.’ He came to the bald man and said, ‘What would you like best?’ He said, ‘Good hair, and that which people have made unclean of me will go away.’ He rubbed him and that went away. He said, ‘So he was given good hair.’ He said, ‘Which wealth would you like best?’ He said, ‘Cows’. He was given a pregnant cow. He said, ‘May God bless you in it.’ He came to the blind man and said, ‘What would you like best?’ He said, ‘For God to restore my sight so that I may see people through him.’ He rubbed him and God restored his sight. He said, ‘Which wealth would you like best?’ He said, ‘Sheep.’ He was given a male ewe, and these two produced offspring and this one gave birth. So this one had a valley of camels, this one had a valley of cows, and this one had a valley of The sheep. He said: Then he came to the leper in his form and appearance. A poor man said: My ropes have been cut off in my journey. I have no means today except by God. I ask you by Him who gave you a beautiful color, beautiful skin, and wealth for a camel to support me on my journey. He said: The rights are many. He said to him: It is as if I know you. Weren’t you a leper whom people despised and a poor man whom God gave you? He said: I inherited this wealth from my grandfather. He said: If you are lying, may God make you what you were. He said: And he came to the bald man in his form and said to him the same as he said to this one and replied to him the same as he replied to this one. He said: If you are lying, may God make you what you were. He said: And he came to the blind man in his form and appearance and a poor man and a wayfarer said: My ropes have been cut off in my journey. I have no means today except by God. I ask you by Him who restored your sight to you for a sheep to support me on my journey. He said: I was blind. God restored my sight to me, so take what you want and leave what you want. By God, I will not burden you today with anything that I took for God. He said: Keep your wealth. If you are tested, He is pleased with you. And he was angry with your two companions.” And in this is the clearest evidence that whoever claims that he has children or other things in addition to his poverty is not to be exposed, contrary to the one who said that he is to be exposed if he is able, because in the hadith, a poor man and a wayfarer said, I ask you for a sheep, and he was not required to prove the journey. As for the one who is being freed from slavery, he is required to prove the writing because slavery is the origin until freedom is proven. Twenty-fifth - It is not permissible to give zakat to those whose expenses are obligatory, namely the parents, children and wife. If the imam gives a man’s charity to his son, father and wife, it is permissible. However, he may not take it himself, because it removes an obligation from him. Abu Hanifa said: It is not permissible to give it to his son’s son or daughter’s son, nor to his freed slave, nor to his freed slave, nor to the mother of his child, nor to a slave who has been freed half of his slave’s wealth, because he is commanded to give and distribute it to God Almighty through the hand of the poor, and the benefits of the property are shared between him and these people, and for this reason the testimony of some of them for others is not accepted. He said: The freed slave is a slave as long as he owes a dirham, and perhaps he becomes unable to do so, so the earnings become his. According to Abu Hanifa, the freed slave is like the freed slave. According to his two companions Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, he is like a free man who has a debt, so it is permissible to pay it to him. Twenty-sixth: If he gives it to those for whom he is not obligated to support, then there is a difference of opinion regarding it. Some of them permit it and some of them dislike it. Malik said: Fear of praise. And Mutraf narrated that he said: I saw Malik giving his zakat to his relatives. And Al-Waqidi said: Malik said: The best people to whom you can put your zakat are your relatives whom you do not support. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the wife of Abdullah bin Masoud: You will have two rewards, the reward of kinship and the reward of charity. And they differed regarding a woman giving her zakat to her husband. It was reported from Ibn Habib that he used to help support her with what she gave him. Abu Hanifa said: It is not permissible, and his two companions disagreed with him and said: It is permissible. And this is the most correct view, as it was proven: “Zainab, the wife of Abdullah, came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and said: I want to give charity on behalf of my husband. Will he reward me? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, you will have two rewards: the reward of charity and the reward of kinship.” The absolute charity is zakat, and because the husband does not have to spend on her, he is like a stranger. Abu Hanifa argued that the benefits of the property are shared between them, so the testimony of one of them on behalf of the other is not accepted. The hadith is to be understood as voluntary. Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr, and Ashhab permitted that, if he does not spend it on her for what is required of her, but rather he spends what he takes from her on his own expenses and clothing, and he spends on her from his own money. Twenty-seventh - They also differed regarding the amount given. The debtor is given the amount of his debt, and the poor and needy are given what is sufficient for them and their dependents. There is a difference of opinion regarding the permissibility of giving the nisab or less than it, based on the previous difference of opinion regarding the limit of poverty at which taking is permissible. Ali bin Ziyad and Ibn Nafi’ narrated: There is no limit for that, but it is up to the discretion of the governor. The poor may be few and the charity may be many, so the poor may be given a year’s sustenance. Al-Mughira narrated: He is given less than the nisab but it does not reach it. Some of the later scholars said: If there are two zakats in the country, cash and crops, he should take what reaches the other. Ibn al-Arabi said: What I see is that he should be given the nisab, and if there are two zakats in the country or more, the purpose is to enrich the poor until he becomes rich. If he takes that, and the other zakat is present and he has enough for him, someone else should take it. I said: This is the doctrine of the people of opinion regarding giving the nisab. Abu Hanifa disliked it although it was permissible, and Abu Yusuf permitted it. He said: Because some of it is due to his need and is occupied with the present, so the surplus from his present need is less than two hundred. If he gives him more than two hundred dirhams in total, the surplus from his present need is the amount of two hundred, so it is not permissible. Among the later Hanafis, there are those who said: This is if he does not have dependents and his dependents are not in debt. If he has a debt, there is no problem in giving him two hundred dirhams or more, an amount that if it were to pay off his debt, would remain for him less than two hundred. If he is a dependent, there is no problem in giving him an amount that if it were distributed among his dependents, each one of them would receive less than two hundred, because giving him charity in the sense of giving him charity and his dependents. This is a good statement. Twenty-eighth - Know that the Almighty’s saying: for the poor is absolute and does not contain any conditions or restrictions. Rather, it indicates the permissibility of spending on all the poor, whether they are from Banu Hashim or others. However, the Sunnah came with conditions in mind: Among them is that they should not be from Banu Hashim and that they should not be among those whose expenses the giver of charity is obligated to pay. There is no disagreement about this. A third condition is that he should not be able to earn a living, because he, peace be upon him, said: Charity is not permissible for the rich or the one who has a good reputation. This has been stated above. There is no disagreement among Muslim scholars that obligatory charity is not permissible for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor for Banu Hashim, nor for their clients. It has been narrated on the authority of Abu Yusuf that it is permissible for a Hashimite to give charity to another Hashimite, as reported by al-Kaya al-Tabari. Some scholars have deviated and said that no charity is forbidden to the clients of Banu Hashim. This is contrary to what is proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said to his client Abu Rafi’: The client of the people is one of them. Twenty-ninth - They differed about the permissibility of voluntary charity for Banu Hashim. The majority of scholars agree - and it is correct - that voluntary charity is permissible for Banu Hashim and their clients, because Ali, Abbas and Fatimah, may God be pleased with them, gave charity and endowed endowments to a group of Banu Hashim, and their endowed charity is well-known and famous. Ibn al-Majishun, Mutraf, Asbagh and Ibn Habib said: Banu Hashim are not given from the obligatory charity or from the voluntary charity. Ibn al-Qasim said: Banu Hashim are given from the voluntary charity. Ibn al-Qasim said: The hadith that was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Charity is not permissible for the family of Muhammad. This is only in zakat, not in voluntary charity. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad chose this opinion, and Abu Yusuf and Muhammad said the same. Ibn al-Qasim said: Their clients are given from the two charities. Malik said in al-Wadiha: The family of Muhammad is not given from voluntary charity. Ibn al-Qasim said - he was asked, meaning Malik - what about their clients? He said: I do not know what a client is. So I argued with him with the words of the Prophet, peace be upon him: The client of a people from among them. He said: He said: The nephew of the people is one of them. Asbagh said: This is in terms of righteousness and sanctity. Al-Muwfiyyah Thirty - The Almighty’s saying: A duty from God is in the accusative case as a source according to Sibawayh. That is, God has made charity a duty. And it is permissible to put it in the nominative case as a definite noun according to Al-Kisa’i, that is, they are a duty. Al-Zajjaj said: I do not know that it was read in this way. I said: Ibrahim bin Abi Ubla read it as a noun, making it a predicate, just as you say: Zaid is only outside.
9:61: God the Almighty made it clear that among the hypocrites there were those who would spread their tongues to harm the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and would say: If he reproaches me, I will swear to him that I did not say that, so he would accept it, for he is a listening ear. Al-Jawhari said: A man is called an ear if he listens to what everyone says, whether it is one person or a group. Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: He is an ear, he said: He listens and accepts. This verse was revealed about Atab bin Qushair, who said: Muhammad is an ear that accepts everything that is said to him. It was said: He is Nabtal bin Al-Harith, as Ibn Ishaq said. Nabtal was a large man with disheveled hair and beard, dark-skinned, red-eyed, dark-skinned, and deformed in appearance. He is the one about whom the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever wants to look at the devil, let him look at Nabtal ibn al-Harith. As-Saf'ah with dammah: blackness mixed with redness. According to al-Jawhari, a man is asfa', and it is read with dammah and sukoon on the dhal. Say, 'Adhan khair lakum' means he is an ear of goodness, not an ear of evil, meaning he hears goodness and does not hear evil. Al-Hasan and Asim read Qul 'Adhan khair lakum with the nominative and tanween, in the narration of Abu Bakr. The rest read it with the addition, and Hamzah and Rahmah with the genitive. The rest read it with the nominative in apposition to Adhan, and the meaning is: Say, he is an ear of goodness and he is mercy, meaning he is a listener of goodness, not a listener of evil, meaning he is a listener of what he loves to hear, and he is mercy. And whoever lowers it, then it is in apposition to Khair. An-Nahhas said: This is far-fetched according to the Arabs, because there is a distance between the two nouns, and this is ugly in the genitive. Al-Mahdawi: And whoever makes mercy a genitive, then it is in apposition to Khair, and the meaning is a listener of goodness and a listener of mercy, because mercy is from goodness. And it is not correct to connect mercy to the believers, because the meaning is to believe in God and to believe in the believers, so the lam is redundant according to the Kufians. And similar to it is they fear their Lord (al-A’raf 7:154) meaning they fear their Lord. Abu Ali said: Like His statement He has followed you (al-Naml 27:72), and according to Al-Mubarrad it is related to a source indicated by the verb, the meaning is: his belief for the believers, meaning his confirmation for the believers, not for the disbelievers. Or it could be carried on the meaning, because the meaning of believe is to confirm, so it is transitive with the preposition lam as it is transitive in His statement: Confirming what was before it (al-Baqarah 2:97).
9:62: It has three issues: First: It was narrated that a group of hypocrites gathered, among them Al-Jalas bin Suwaid and Wadiah bin Thabit, and among them was a young man from the Ansar called Aamer bin Qais. They belittled him and spoke and said: If what Muhammad says is true, then we are worse than donkeys. The young man became angry and said: By God, what he says is true and you are worse than donkeys. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was informed of what they said, and they swore that Aamer was lying. Aamer said: They are the liars, and he swore to that effect and said: O God, do not separate us until the truth of the truthful one is proven and the lie of the liar is proven. Then God revealed this verse, which says: They swear to you by God to please you. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And God and His Messenger are more deserving that they should be pleased with Him. It is a subject and a predicate. Sibawayh’s school of thought is that the meaning is: And God is more deserving that they should be pleased with Him and His Messenger is more deserving that they should be pleased with Him, then it was deleted, as some of them said: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs Muhammad bin Yazid said: There is nothing omitted in the speech, and the meaning is, and God is more deserving that they should be pleased with Him and His Messenger, on the basis of precedence and delay. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is, and His Messenger is more deserving that they should be pleased with Him, and God is the opening of a speech, as you say: What God and you willed. Al-Nahhas said: The statement of Sibawayh is more appropriate, because it has been authenticated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he forbade saying: What God wills and you will, and nothing can be advanced or delayed, and its meaning is correct. I said: It was said that God Almighty made His pleasure in His pleasure. Don’t you see that He said: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed God (An-Nisa’: 80). And whenever Ar-Rabi’ bin Khaitham passed by this verse, he would stop and then say: A letter and any letter, He has delegated it to him, so he does not command us except with good. Third: Our scholars said: This verse includes the acceptance of the oath of the one taking the oath, even if the one to whom the oath is taken is not obligated to consent. The oath is a right of the claimant. It includes that the oath should be by God Almighty, as mentioned above. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever swears, let him swear by God or remain silent, and whoever swears to Him, let him tell the truth. The discussion of oaths and the exceptions thereto has already been completed in Al-Ma’idah.
9:63: The Almighty said: Did they not know? meaning the hypocrites. Ibn Hormuz and Al-Hasan read they learned with the ta' as a direct address. That is in the accusative case as they learned, and the ha' is a metaphor for the hadith. Who is arguing with God? is in the nominative case as a subject. Arguing is the occurrence of this person in a certain limit and that person in a certain limit, like quarreling. It is said: So-and-so arguing with so-and-so means he became in a limit other than his limit. Then for him is the fire of Hell. It is said: What comes after the fa' in the condition is a subject, so it should have been then with the kasra of the hamza. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh permitted then for him is the fire of Hell with the kasra. Sibawayh said: It is good and he recited: And my knowledge of the waters of Asdam, the camels of challenge have not ceased to be on the way of the vanguards And if my mounts become bored with its atmosphere, then I am unruly in my share of the matter However, the reading of the general public is fa'an with the opening of the hamza. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh also said: the second an is a replacement for the first. Al-Mubarrad claimed that this statement is rejected, and that what Al-Jarmi said is correct, he said: the second an is repeated for emphasis because the speech is long, and similar to it is And they, in the Hereafter, are the greatest losers (al-Naml 27:5). And also So the consequence of them is that they will be in the Fire, abiding eternally therein (al-Hashr 59:17). Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is that the Fire is obligatory for him. Al-Mubarrad denied it and said: This is a mistake because the open shaddah an is not used as a beginning and the predicate is implied. Ali bin Sulayman said: The meaning is that it is obligatory for him to have the Fire of Hell, because the second an is the predicate of a deleted beginning. It was said: The estimate is that for him is that he has the Fire of Hell. Fan is raised by the stability of the implication of the genitive between the fa' and an.
9:64: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: The hypocrites should beware is a statement, not a command. What indicates that it is a statement is that what follows it is Indeed, God will bring out that which you fear because they disbelieved out of stubbornness. Al-Suddi said: Some of the hypocrites said: By God, I wish I had come forward and flogged a hundred people so that nothing would be revealed concerning us that would disgrace us. So the verse was revealed: Beware meaning be on your guard. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is to beware, so it is a command, just as one says: He does that. Second: The Almighty’s saying: that you may descend upon them “that” is in the accusative case, meaning from that you may descend. And it is permissible, according to Sibawayh, for it to be in the genitive case by deleting from and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as the object of to warn, because Sibawayh permitted: I warned Zayd, and he recited: Beware of things that do not harm you and be safe from things that do not save you from fate. Al-Mubarrad did not permit it, because caution is something in form. The meaning of upon them is upon the believers is a Surah concerning the hypocrites, informing them of their shameful deeds, faults, and shortcomings. That is why it was called Al-Fadihah, “Al-Muthira,” and Al-Mubathara, as mentioned at the beginning of the Surah. Al-Hasan said: The Muslims used to call this Surah Al-Haffara because it excavated what was in the hearts of the hypocrites and revealed it. Third: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: ‘Mock!’” This is a command of threat and intimidation. Indeed, God will bring out meaning, reveal what you fear. Its manifestation. Ibn Abbas said: God revealed the names of the hypocrites, and they were seventy men, then He abrogated those names from the Qur’an out of His compassion and mercy, because their children were Muslims and people would taunt one another. So, based on this, God fulfilled His promise to reveal that when He said: Indeed, God will bring out what you fear. It was said: God’s bringing out is that He informed His Prophet, peace be upon him, of their conditions and names, not that they were revealed in the Qur’an. God, the Almighty, said: And you will surely recognize them by the tone of their speech (Muhammad 47:30), which is a type of inspiration. And among the hypocrites were those who hesitated and were not certain of the denial of Muhammad, peace be upon him, or his truthfulness. And among them were those who knew his truthfulness but were stubborn.
9:65: It has three issues: First: This verse was revealed during the Battle of Tabuk. Al-Tabari and others said on the authority of Qatada: “While the Prophet (peace be upon him) was marching in the Battle of Tabuk, and a group of hypocrites were walking in front of him, they said: Look, this one is conquering the palaces of Ash-Sham and taking the fortresses of the yellow people! So God, the Exalted, showed him what was in their hearts and what they were talking about, so he said: Detain the group for me - then he came to them and said - You said such and such, so they swore: We were only joking and playing, meaning we were not serious.” At-Tabari mentioned on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar that he said: I saw the one who said this statement, Wadi’ah bin Thabit, clinging to the saddle of the she-camel of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), walking with the stones hitting him and he was saying: We were only joking and playing. And the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Was it God, His verses, and His Messenger that you were mocking? Al-Naqqash mentioned that the one who was hanging on was Abdullah bin Abi Salul. Al-Qushayri also mentioned on the authority of Ibn Omar. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is a mistake, because he did not witness Tabuk. Al-Qushayri said: It was said that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said this to Wadi’ah bin Thabit, who was one of the hypocrites and was in the Battle of Tabuk. Wading: entering water, then it was used for any entry that involves pollution and harm. Second: Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: What they said was either serious or joking, and in any case it is kufr, because joking about kufr is kufr, and there is no disagreement about it among the nation. Verification is the brother of knowledge and truth, and joking is the brother of falsehood and ignorance. Our scholars said: Look at His statement: Do you take us in jest? He said: I seek refuge in God from being among the ignorant. (al-Baqarah 2:67) Third: Scholars differed regarding joking in all other rulings such as selling, marriage and divorce, with three opinions: It is not binding absolutely. It is binding absolutely. The distinction between selling and other things. It is binding in marriage and divorce, and this is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i regarding divorce as one opinion. It is not binding in selling. Malik said in the book of Muhammad: The marriage of a joker is binding. Abu Zaid said on the authority of Ibn Al-Qasim in Al-Utbiyyah: It is not binding. Ali bin Ziyad said: It is annulled before and after. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions regarding the sale of a joker. Likewise, the two opinions are derived from the opinion of our scholars. Ibn Al-Mundhir narrated the consensus that the seriousness of divorce and its joking are the same. Some of our later companions said: If they agree on joking in marriage and selling, it is not binding, and if they disagree, seriousness prevails over joking. Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three things which are serious even if done in jest: marriage, divorce, and taking back a wife.” Al-Tirmidhi said: A good and rare hadith. This is what the scholars among the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and others acted upon. I said: This is how it is in the hadith and the return. In the Muwatta of Malik, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, he said: There are three things in which there is no play: marriage, divorce, and manumission. And this was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, Abdullah bin Masoud, and Abu Al-Darda, all of them said: There are three things in which there is no play and no return, and the one who plays in them is serious: marriage, divorce, and manumission. And on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Omar, he said: Four things are permissible for everyone: manumission, divorce, marriage, and vows. And on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said: There are three things in which there is no play: marriage, divorce, and vows.
9:66: The Almighty’s saying: “Make no excuses. You have disbelieved after your belief” is a form of rebuke, as if He is saying: Do not do what is of no benefit, then He ruled that they were disbelievers and did not apologize for their sin. And apologized means excused, meaning he had an excuse. Labid said: And whoever cries for a whole year has apologized Apology: erasing the trace of resentment. It is said: I apologized for the houses that were destroyed. Apology is the lessons. The poet said: Or did you know the verses that made the ruins of your love apologize with intelligence? Ibn al-A'rabi said: Its origin is to cut. And I apologized to him, meaning I cut off what was in his heart of resentment. And from it comes the word adhra a young boy's pubic hair, which is what is cut off during circumcision. And from it comes the word adhra a young girl's pubic hair, because the ring of her virginity is cut off. God the Almighty said: If We pardon a party of you, We will punish a party because they were criminals. It was said: They were three men, two mocked and one laughed, so the pardoned one is the one who laughed and did not speak. A party is a group, and it is said to one person in the same sense as a group. Ibn al-Anbari said: The plural form is used for one person, like when you say: So-and-so went out on mules. He said: It is permissible for the group to be a group if it is meant for one person, and the ha is for emphasis. There are different opinions about the name of this man who was pardoned. It was said: Mahshi bin Himyar, as Ibn Ishaq said. Ibn Hisham said: It is also said that he is Ibn Makhshi. Khalifa bin Khayyat said in his history: His name is Makhashin bin Himyar. Ibn Abd al-Barr mentioned Makhashin al-Himyari and al-Suhayli mentioned Makhashin bin Khumayr. They all said that he was martyred in Yamamah, and he had repented and was called Abd al-Rahman, so he prayed to God to be killed as a martyr and his grave would not be known. There is a difference of opinion as to whether he was a hypocrite or a Muslim. It was said: He was a hypocrite, then he repented sincerely. It was also said: He was a Muslim, except that he heard the hypocrites and laughed at them and did not denounce them.
9:67: The Almighty said: The hypocrites, men and women is the beginning. Some of them is the second beginning. It is permissible for it to be a substitute, and for the predicate to be from some, and the meaning of some of them from some is that they are like one thing in deviating from the religion. Al-Zajjaj said: This is connected to his saying: And they swear by God that they are of you, but they are not of you meaning that they are not of the believers, but some of them are of one another, meaning they are similar in enjoining evil and forbidding good. And closing their hands is an expression for abandoning jihad, and in what is required of them of rights. Forgetting: abandonment here, meaning they abandoned what God commanded them to do, so He left them in doubt. It was said: They abandoned His command until it became like something forgotten, so He made them like someone who was forgotten in His reward. Qatada said: He forgot them, meaning of the good, but as for the evil, He did not forget them. And immorality: is abandoning obedience and religion. It was mentioned before.
9:68: The Almighty said: God has promised the hypocrites It is said: God promised good as a promise. And He promised evil as a threat. Immortal is in the accusative case as a state and the agent is omitted, meaning they will pray it immortal. It is sufficient for them is subject and predicate, meaning it is sufficient and fulfills the reward for their deeds. And the curse: distance, meaning from God's mercy: and it has been mentioned before. And for them is a lasting punishment meaning constant and permanent.
9:69: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Like those before you. Al-Zajjaj said: The kaf is in the accusative case, meaning that God promised the disbelievers the fire of Hell as He promised those before them. It was said: The meaning is that you did as those before you did in commanding evil and forbidding good, so the complement was deleted. It was said: That is, you are like those before you, so the kaf is in the nominative case because it is the predicate of a deleted subject. Ashdh was not declined because Af’al is an adjective. Its original form is ashdhd, meaning they were stronger than you in strength, but it was not possible for them nor was it possible for them to lift the punishment of God, the Almighty. Second: Saeed narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You will take as the nations before you took, cubit by cubit, span by span, and armspan by armspan, to the extent that if one of them entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it. Abu Hurairah said: If you wish, recite the Qur’an: “Like those before you who were stronger than you in strength and more abundant in wealth and children. So enjoy your share as those before you enjoyed their share,” until he finished the verse. They said: O Prophet of God, what did the Jews and Christians do? He said: And people are none other than them. And in the Sahih from him on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You will follow the ways of those before you, inch by inch and cubit by cubit, to the point that if they entered the hole of a lizard, you would enter it too. They said: O Messenger of God, do you mean the Jews and Christians? He said: Then who else? Ibn Abbas said: How similar tonight is to last night! These are the Children of Israel, and we likened them to them. And something similar was narrated by Ibn Mas`ud. Third: The Almighty said: So enjoy their portion meaning benefit from their share of religion as those before them did. And you plunged is a transition from the third person to the second person. Like those who plunged meaning like their plunge. So the kaf is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted source, meaning and you plunged in a plunge like those who plunged. And who is an incomplete noun like who, which is used to express the singular and the plural. It has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. It is said: I plunged into the water, I plunged into it, wading and plural. The place is a ford, which is what people pass through on foot and on horseback. Its plural is makhadd and makhawwad also, on the authority of Abu Zaid. And I plunged my beast into the water. And the people plunged, meaning their horses plunged. And I plunged into the ghamrat: I stormed into it. It is also said: He plunged into it with the sword, meaning he moved his sword in the well. And he plunged into its filth is stressed for emphasis. And the one who plunges into a drink is like the one who immerses in gruel, it is said from it: I plunged into the drink. The people engaged in conversation and negotiated about it. The meaning is: you engaged in worldly matters with amusement and play. It was also said: in the matter of Muhammad’s denial. Those are in vain became invalid. It was mentioned earlier. Their deeds are their good deeds. And those are the losers was also mentioned earlier.
9:70: The Almighty says: Did there not come to them the report meaning report of those before them? The alif is for confirmation and warning, meaning did they not hear Our destruction of the disbelievers before? The people of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud instead of those. And the people of Abraham meaning Nimrod bin Canaan and his people. And the people of Midian Midian is the name of the country in which Shu'aib was. They were destroyed by the punishment of the Day of Shadow. And the overturned It was said that it refers to the people of Lot, because their land was overturned with them, meaning it was turned upside down, as Qatada said. It was also said that the overturned refers to everyone who was destroyed, just as it is said: the world was turned upside down on them. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs meaning all the prophets. It was also said that the messengers came to the people of the overturned, so according to this, their messenger was Lot alone, but he sent a messenger to every village, and there were three villages, and it was said four. And the Almighty’s saying in another place: And the overturned ones (al-Najm 53:53) is in the way of the genus. And it was said: He meant by the messengers one, like His saying: O messengers, eat from the good things (al-Mu’minun 23:51) and there was no one else in his time. I said - and this is questionable, due to the authentic hadith from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: God addressed the believers with what He commanded the Messengers. The hadith. It was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah. What is meant is all the Messengers, and God knows best. God Almighty says: God would not wrong them meaning He would not destroy them until He sent prophets to them. But they were wronging themselves but they wronged themselves after the proof was established against them.
9:71: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Some of them are allies of others, meaning their hearts are united in affection, love, and compassion. Some hypocrites said, Some of them are from others, because their hearts are different, but they are joined to each other in judgment. Second: The Almighty’s saying: They enjoin what is right meaning the worship of God Almighty and His Oneness, and everything that follows that. And they forbid what is wrong meaning the worship of idols and everything that follows that. At-Tabari mentioned on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah that he said: Everything that God mentioned in the Qur’an about enjoining what is right [enjoining what is right is a call from polytheism to Islam] and forbidding what is wrong is the prohibition of the worship of idols and devils. We have already discussed enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong in Surat Al-Ma’idah and Surat Al-Imran, and praise be to God. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And establish prayer. This was discussed at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. Ibn Abbas said: It is the five daily prayers, and according to this, the obligatory zakat here is considered. Ibn Atiyyah: In my opinion, praise for voluntary prayers is more eloquent, since the one who establishes voluntary prayers is more deserving of establishing the obligatory prayers. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And they obey God in the obligatory duties and His Messenger in what He has prescribed for them. And the seen in His saying: God will have mercy on them is inserted into the promise as a respite so that souls may enjoy His hope, and His Almighty grace is the leader in fulfillment.
9:72: The Almighty said: God has promised the believing men and believing women gardens meaning orchards underneath which rivers flow meaning beneath its trees and chambers rivers. It was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah that it flows in a controlled manner by power without a groove. They will abide therein and in pleasant dwellings palaces of emerald, pearl and ruby whose fragrance wafts from a distance of five hundred years. In Gardens of Eden meaning in a permanent abode. It is said: Aden in a place if one resides there, and from this comes the word mine. Ata' Al-Khurasani said: The Gardens of Eden are the reed of Paradise, and its ceiling is the Throne of the Most Merciful, the Almighty. Ibn Mas'ud said: They are the two valleys of Paradise, meaning its middle. Al-Hasan said: They are a palace of gold that none shall enter except a prophet, a friend, a martyr, or a just judge, and something similar was narrated by Ad-Dahhak. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: Aden is the highest level in Paradise, and in it is the Spring of Tasnim, and the gardens surround it, and it has been covered from the day God created it until the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, the righteous, and whomever God wills descend upon it. And the pleasure of God is greater meaning greater than that. That is the great attainment.
9:73: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation after him is included in it. It was said: What is meant is to strive against the disbelievers with the believers. Ibn Abbas said: He ordered to strive against the disbelievers with the sword, and against the hypocrites with the tongue and severe warning and harshness. It was narrated from Ibn Masoud that he said: Strive against the hypocrites with your hand, and if you cannot, then with your tongue, and if you cannot, then restrain yourself from slandering them.
