Al-Hasan said: Strive against the hypocrites by establishing the prescribed punishments against them with the tongue - and Qatada chose this - and they were the ones who most frequently applied the prescribed punishments. Ibn Al-Arabi Abu Bakr: As for establishing proof with the tongue, it was permanent, and as for the prescribed punishments, because most of the times they applied the prescribed punishments, it was a claim without proof. The sinner is not a hypocrite, but rather the hypocrite is the one who has hypocrisy hidden in his heart, not the one who is apparent with his limbs, and the accounts of those who were punished testify that they were not hypocrites. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And be harsh with them. Harshness is the opposite of compassion, and it is the severity of the heart in imposing a command on its owner. It is not in the tongue, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of your female slaves commits adultery, let him flog her with the prescribed lashes, and let him not reproach her. And from this is the saying of God the Almighty: And if you had been rude [in speech] and harsh in heart, they would have disbanded from around you. (Al Imran 3:159). And from this is the saying of the women to Omar: You are ruder and harsher than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The meaning of harshness is roughness of the side. It is the opposite of the saying of God the Almighty: And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers. (Ash-Shu’ara’: 215) And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy. (al-Isra’ 17:24). This verse abrogated everything from forgiveness, reconciliation, and pardon.
9:74: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty said: They swear by God that they did not say it. It was narrated that this verse was revealed about Al-Jalas bin Suwaid bin Al-Samit and Wadi’ah bin Thabit. They spoke ill of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: By God, if Muhammad is truthful about our brothers who are our leaders and best, then we are worse than donkeys. Amir bin Qais said to him: Yes! By God, Muhammad is truthful and believed, and you are worse than a drunkard. Amir informed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, of that. Al-Jalas came and swore by God at the pulpit of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that Amir is a liar. Amir swore that he had said it, and said: O God, reveal something to Your truthful Prophet. So it was revealed. It was said that it was Asim bin Adi who heard it. It was also said that it was Hudhayfah. It was also said that it was heard by his wife’s son, whose name was Umair bin Saad, according to what Ibn Ishaq said. Another said that his name was Mus’ab. Al-Jalas intended to kill him so that he would not tell the truth about him, so it was revealed about him: And they intended what they did not attain. Mujahid said: When his companion told Al-Jalas that he would tell the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) what you said, he intended to kill him, but he did not do so, he was unable to do so. He said, this is the indication in his saying, and they intended what they could not achieve. It was said that it was revealed about Abdullah bin Ubayy, he saw a man from Ghifar fighting with a man from Juhayna, and Juhayna were allies of the Ansar, so Al-Ghifari Al-Juhayni attacked him. Ibn Ubayy said: O sons of Aws and Khazraj, support your brother! By God, our example and that of Muhammad are like the saying of the one who said: Fatten your dog and it will eat you, and if we return to Medina, the more honorable will expel therefrom the more abject. So he informed the Prophet (peace be upon him) of that, and Abdullah bin Ubayy came to him and swore that he did not say it. Qatadah said: A third opinion is that it was the saying of all the hypocrites, as Al-Hasan said. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is correct, because of the generality of the statement and the presence of meaning in it and among them, and the sum of that is their belief that he was not a prophet. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And they have certainly said the word of disbelief. Al-Naqqash said: Their denial of what God had promised of victory. It was also said: The word of disbelief is the saying of Al-Jalas: If what Muhammad brought is true, then we are worse than donkeys. And the saying of Abdullah bin Ubay: If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble. Al-Qushayri said: The word of disbelief is cursing the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and attacking Islam. And they disbelieved after their Islam meaning after the ruling that they were Muslims. This indicates that the hypocrites are disbelievers, and in the Almighty’s saying: That is because they believed and then disbelieved (al-Munafiqun 63:3) there is conclusive evidence. The verse also indicates that disbelief is anything that contradicts belief and knowledge, even though faith is only in There is no god but God without any other words or actions except in prayer. Ishaq bin Rahawayh said: They agreed on something in prayer that they did not agree on in all other religions, because they all said: Whoever is known to be a disbeliever and then they see him praying the prayer on time until he has prayed many prayers, and they did not know him to acknowledge it verbally, he is judged to be a believer, and they did not judge him in fasting and zakat, which is an example of that. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And they intended that which they could not attain, meaning the hypocrites who killed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of Aqaba in the Battle of Tabuk, and they were twelve men. Hudhayfah said: "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, named them until he had counted them all. I said: Why don't you send for them and kill them? He said: I hate for the Arabs to say that when he defeated his companions he began to kill them (then said: O God, shoot them) with the dabilah. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is the dabilah? He said: A meteor from Hell that he places on the strings of one of their hearts until his soul is taken." And so it was. Muslim narrated it with the same meaning. It was said that they intended to tie the crown on the head of Ibn Abi Abi so that they could gather around him. The statement of Mujahid on this has been mentioned above. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And they did not resent anything except that God and His Messenger enriched them from His bounty. That is, they did not resent anything, as Al-Nabigha said: There is no fault in them except that their swords have dents from the clashing of the battalions. It is said: Naqam yanqam, and Naqam yanqam. The poet said in the kasr: They did not resent the Umayyads except that they were patient when they got angry. Zuhair said: It is either delayed and placed in a book and stored for the Day of Judgment, or it is hastened and taken revenge. It is chanted with the kasra or fatha of the qaf. Al-Sha’bi said: They used to ask for blood money and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) would rule in their favor, but they were content. Ikrimah mentioned that it was twelve thousand. The murdered man was the freed slave of Al-Jalas. Al-Kalbi said: Before the arrival of the Prophet (peace be upon him), they were living in hardship, they did not ride horses and did not acquire spoils of war. When the Prophet (peace be upon him) arrived, they were content with the spoils of war. This proverb is well-known: Beware the evil of those you have done good to. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: It was said to Al-Bajali: Do you find in the Book of God the Most High: Beware the evil of those you have done good to? He said: Yes, And they did not resent it except because God and His Messenger had enriched them from His bounty. Fifth: The Almighty said: If they repent, it will be better for them. It was narrated that Al-Jalas stood up when the verse was revealed, asked for forgiveness, and repented. This indicates the repentance of the disbeliever who conceals disbelief and shows faith, and he is the one whom the jurists call the zindiq. Scholars differed on this. Al-Shafi’i said: His repentance is accepted. Malik said: The repentance of the zindiq is not known, because he used to show faith and conceal disbelief, and his faith is not known except by his words. And this is what he does now at all times. He says: I am a believer, but he conceals the opposite of what he shows. So if he is found and says: I repent, his condition does not change from what it was. So if he comes to us repenting of his own accord before we are found, his repentance is accepted, and this is what is meant by the verse. And God knows best. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: And if they turn away meaning they turn away from faith and repentance, God will punish them with a painful punishment in this world by killing, and in the Hereafter by fire. And they will have on earth no protector meaning no one to prevent them, nor helper meaning no supporter. This has been mentioned previously.
9:75: It contains eight issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And among them are those who made a covenant with God. Qatada said: This is a man from the Ansar who said: If God provides me with something, I will pay its due and give in charity. So when God gave him that, he did what He has commanded you to do. So beware of lying, for it leads to immorality. And Ali bin Yazid narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili: “That Tha’laba bin Hatib Al-Ansari he named him said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ask God to grant me wealth. So he, peace be upon him, said: Woe to you, Tha’laba! A little that you can thank for is better than a lot that you cannot bear. Then he repeated it a second time and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Are you not satisfied to be like the Prophet of God? If I wished for the mountains to move with me in gold, they would move. So he said: By the One Who sent you with the truth, if I ask God and He grants me wealth, I will give everyone his due. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for him, and he took sheep, and they grew like worms grow, and the city became too small for him, so he moved away from it and went down to one of its valleys until he began to pray the noon and afternoon prayers in congregation, and he left everything else. Then they grew and increased until he stopped praying except the Friday prayer, and they continued to grow until he stopped the Friday prayer as well. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to Tha’laba three times. Then he revealed: Take from their wealth a charity. So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent two men to collect the charity, and he said to them: Pass by Tha’laba by so-and-so. - A man from Banu Salim - took their alms. They went to Tha'laba and read him the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: This is nothing but a sister of the jizya! Go until you are done and then return. The hadith, which is well-known. It was said: The reason for Tha'laba's wealth was that he inherited a cousin of his. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: It was said that Tha'laba ibn Hattab was the one about whom the verse And among them are those who made a covenant with God was revealed, as they withheld the zakat, and God knows best. What was said about those who witnessed Badr contradicts the statement of God in the verse: Then He caused hypocrisy to follow them in their hearts the verse. I said: It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the reason for the revelation of the verse that Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah was delayed in receiving his money in Ash-Sham, so he swore in a gathering of the Ansar: If he handed it over, I would give some of it in charity and I would give some of it as charity. But when he handed it over, he was stingy with it, so this verse was revealed. I said: Tha’laba was a Badri Ansari and one of those to whom God and His Messenger testified to his faith, as will be explained at the beginning of Al-Mumtahanah. So what was narrated about him is not correct. Abu Omar said: Perhaps the statement of those who said about Tha’laba that he was the one who withheld the zakat and about whom the verse was revealed is not correct, and God knows best. Ad-Dahhak said: The verse was revealed about some hypocrites, Nabtal ibn Al-Harith, Jad ibn Qays, and Mu’tab ibn Qushayr. I said: This is more similar to the revelation of the verse about them, except that his saying, “Then He made hypocrisy follow them,” indicates that the one who made a covenant with God was not a hypocrite before, unless the meaning is: He increased their hypocrisy and they remained in it until death, which is the saying of God Almighty: Until the Day they meet Him, as will come. Second: Our scholars said: When God the Almighty said: And among them is he who made a covenant with God, it is possible that he made a covenant with God with his tongue but did not believe it in his heart. It is possible that he made a covenant with God with both of them and then a bad end overtook him, because actions are judged by their endings and days are judged by their consequences. And whoever raises the subject and the predicate in the genitive case. The word oath was mentioned in the hadith and there is no oath in the apparent meaning of the Qur’an except by mere connection and commitment. As for it being in the form of an oath in meaning, the lam indicates it, and he brought two lams, the first for the oath and the second for the lam of the answer, and both are for emphasis. And some of them said: They are lams of the oath, and the first is more apparent, and God knows best. Third: The covenant, divorce, and every ruling that a person makes on his own and does not need anyone else for it, then he is bound by what he intends to do with it, even if he does not utter it, as our scholars have said. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa said: No one is bound by a ruling unless he utters it, and this is the other opinion of our scholars. Ibn al-Arabi: The evidence for the correctness of what we have stated is what Ashab narrated from Malik, and he was asked: If a man intends divorce in his heart but does not utter it with his tongue, then he said: It is binding on him, just as he is a believer in his heart and a disbeliever in his heart. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a wonderful principle, and its clarification is to say: A contract in which a person does not need anyone else to commit to it, so it is concluded with intention. Its origin is faith and disbelief. I said: The evidence for the second statement is what Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has forgiven my nation for what their souls have thought of, as long as they do not act upon it or speak about it.” Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: A good and authentic hadith. The scholars act upon this, that if a man thinks of divorce in his heart, it is nothing until he speaks about it. Abu Umar said: Whoever believes in divorce in his heart but does not utter it with his tongue, it is nothing. This is the most famous view from Malik. It has been narrated from him that divorce is binding on him if he intends it in his heart, just as he disbelieves in his heart even if he does not utter it with his tongue. The first view is more correct in terms of opinion and the path of the hadith, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has forgiven my nation for what their souls whisper to them, as long as the tongue does not utter it or the hand does it. Fourth: If it was a vow, then fulfilling the vow is obligatory without dispute, and leaving it is a sin. If it was an oath, then fulfilling the oath is not obligatory by consensus. However, the meaning here is that if a man is poor and does not have to pay zakat, then he asks God for something for which zakat is not obligatory and pays what is obligatory for him, then when God gives him what He wills of that, he leaves what he committed to from what would have been obligatory for him in the original religion if he had not committed to it, but dealing with asking for money to fulfill rights is what got him into trouble, since his request from God Almighty was without a pure intention, or an intention but the beginning in which misery was written for him preceded it. We seek refuge in God from that. I said: And from this meaning, peace be upon him: If one of you makes a wish, let him consider what he wishes for, for he does not know what has been written for him in the unseen of God, the Almighty and Majestic, of his wish. That is, its consequences. Many a wish may lead to temptation or arrogance, and it may be a cause of destruction in this world and the next, because worldly matters are ambiguous and their consequences are dangerous and disastrous. As for wishing for matters of religion and the next, wishing for them has a praiseworthy outcome, is encouraged, and is recommended. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: If He gave us from His bounty, we would surely give in charity is evidence that whoever says: If I own such and such, it is charity, then it is obligatory for him. Abu Hanifa said the same. Ash-Shafi’i said: He is not obligated. The dispute over divorce is similar, and the same applies to emancipation. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: He is obligated to do so in emancipation, but he is not obligated in divorce, because emancipation is an act of worship and is in the conscience by vow, unlike divorce, which is a disposition in a place, and it is not established in the conscience. Ash-Shafi’i provided evidence for what was narrated by Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi, and others on the authority of Amr ibn Shu’ayb on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no vow for the son of Adam regarding what he does not own, nor is he allowed to free what he does not own, nor is he allowed to divorce what he does not own. This is the wording of Al-Tirmidhi. He said: There is a hadith on this topic from Ali, Muadh, Jabir, Ibn Abbas, and Aisha, a hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, a good hadith, and it is the best thing narrated on this topic, and it is the opinion of most of the scholars from the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and others. Ibn Al-Arabi: The companions of Al-Shafi’i narrated many hadiths on this topic, none of which are authentic, so they cannot be relied upon, and all that remains is the apparent meaning of the verse.
9:76: Sixth - The Almighty said: But when He gave them of His bounty, meaning He gave them. They were stingy with it, meaning in giving charity and spending money on good deeds, and in fulfilling what they had promised and committed to. Stinginess has already been mentioned in Al Imran. And they turned away, meaning from obeying God, while they were averse, meaning in Islam, meaning they showed aversion to it.
9:77: Seventh - The Almighty's saying: So He made hypocrisy their consequence is two objects, meaning that God made hypocrisy their consequence in their hearts. It was said: meaning that He made miserliness their consequence, and that is why He said: They were miserly with it. "Until the Day they meet Him" is in the accusative case, meaning that they meet Him with their miserliness, meaning the reward for their miserliness, as one says: You will meet your deeds tomorrow. It was said: "Until the Day they meet Him" meaning that they will meet God. In this there is evidence that he died a hypocrite. It is unlikely that the house contained Tha'laba or Hatib, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar: And how do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said, Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you. And Tha’laba and Hatib were among those who attended Badr and witnessed it. Because they broke their promise to God and because they used to lie. Their lie was their breaking of the covenant and their failure to fulfill what they had committed to. Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: Hypocrisy. Hypocrisy, if it is in the heart, is disbelief. But if it is in the actions, it is a sin. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are four characteristics, whoever has them is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has one characteristic of hypocrisy until he gives it up: when he is entrusted, he betrays; when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a promise, he breaks it; and when he quarrels, he behaves indecently.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari. The derivation of this word has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. People differed in the interpretation of this hadith. A group said: This only refers to the one who narrates a hadith that he knows is a lie, and makes a promise that he does not believe will be fulfilled, and waits for a trust in order to betray it. They relied on a hadith with a weak chain of transmission. And that Ali bin Abi Talib may God be pleased with him met Abu Bakr and Umar may God be pleased with them leaving the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and they were both heavy. So Ali said: Why do I see you both so heavy? They said: A hadith we heard from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) about the characteristics of al-Munafiqun 63:when they speak they lie, when they promise they break, when they are entrusted they betray, and when they promise they break their promise. So Ali said: Why didn’t you ask him? They said: We feared the Messenger of God (peace be upon him). He said: But I will ask him. So he entered upon the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, Abu Bakr and Umar left and they were both heavy. Then he mentioned what they said and said: I told them and I did not put it in the position they put it. But when a hypocrite speaks and thinks to himself he lies, and when he promises and thinks to himself he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted and thinks to himself he betrays. Ibn al-Arabi: Clear evidence has been established that the one who deliberately has these characteristics is not a disbeliever, but rather he is a disbeliever because of a belief that is due to ignorance of God and His attributes or denial of Him. God is exalted and sanctified above the belief of the ignorant and the deviation of the deviants. A group said: This was specific to the hypocrites at the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They relied on what Muqatil bin Hayyan narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Omar and Ibn Abbas, who said: We came to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) with some of his companions and said: O Messenger of God, you said that whoever has three things in him is a hypocrite, even if he fasts and prays and claims to be a believer: if he speaks he lies, if he promises he breaks his promise, and if he is entrusted with something he betrays. And whoever has one of these three characteristics has a third of hypocrisy. We thought that we were not free from them or from some of them, but many people are not free from them. He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) laughed and said: What do you have to do with them? They were only used specifically for the hypocrites, just as God has used them specifically in His Book. As for my saying that if he speaks he lies, this is what God the Almighty said: When the hypocrites come to you (al-Munafiqun 63:1) - the verse - are you like that? We said: No. He said: It does not matter, you are innocent of that. As for my saying that if he promises he breaks his promise, this is according to what God revealed to me: “And among them are those who made a covenant with God, ‘If He should give us from His bounty’ - the three verses - are you like that? We said: No, by God, if we made a covenant with God about something, we would fulfill it. He said: It is not your concern, you are innocent of that. As for my saying, “If someone is entrusted with something, he betrays it,” that is in what God revealed to me: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains (al-Ahzab 33:72) - the verse - so every person is entrusted with his religion. The believer performs ritual ablution from major ritual impurity in secret and in public, but the hypocrite does that only in public. Are you like that? We said: No. He said: It is not your concern, you are innocent of that. Many of the followers and imams agreed to this. A group said: This is for those who are mostly characterized by these traits. It appears from the doctrine of Al-Bukhari and other scholars: that these reprehensible characteristics are a hypocrite who is characterized by them until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Al-Arabi said: What I have is that if sins were mostly in him, he would not be a disbeliever because of them as long as they did not affect belief. Our scholars said: The brothers of Joseph, peace be upon him, made a covenant with their father and broke it, and they spoke to him and lied to him, and he entrusted them with Joseph and they betrayed him, and they were not hypocrites. Ata’ bin Abi Rabah said: The brothers of Joseph did these characteristics, and they were not hypocrites, but they were prophets. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Hypocrisy is of two types: hypocrisy of lying and hypocrisy of action. As for the hypocrisy of lying, it was during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and as for the hypocrisy of action, it will not cease until the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bukhari narrated from Hudhayfah: Hypocrisy was during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and as for Today it is only disbelief after faith.
9:78: The Almighty says: Do they not know that God knows their secrets and their private conversations? This is a rebuke, and if He is All-Knowing, then He will punish them.
9:79: The Almighty said: Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity This is also one of the characteristics of the hypocrites. Qatada said: They criticize and find fault. He said: That is because Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf gave away half of his wealth in charity. He had eight thousand, so he gave away four thousand of it. Some people said: How great is his hypocrisy! So God revealed: Those who criticize the believers who give voluntary charity. A man from the Ansar brought half a heap of his dates. They said: God does not need this! So God revealed: And those who find nothing but their effort the verse. Muslim came out to Abu Mas'ud and said: We were ordered to give charity. He said: We used to carry, in another narration: on our backs - he said: Abu Aqil gave half a Sa' in charity. He said: A man came with something larger than him, and the hypocrites said: God is independent of this person's charity, and this other did nothing but show off. So the verse was revealed: Those who criticize those among the believers who give voluntarily concerning the charity and those who find nothing except their effort. He meant Abu Aqil. His name was Al-Habhab. Effort: a small amount by which the poor live. Effort and effort have the same meaning. It has been mentioned before. And you criticize them, they find fault. It has been mentioned before. And the volunteers originally mean the volunteers, the ta' was assimilated into the ta', and they are those who do something voluntarily without it being obligatory for them. And those in the accusative case are in apposition to the believers. It is not permissible for it to be in apposition to the noun before its completion. And they mock is in apposition to they criticize. "God mocked them" is the predicate of the subject, and it is a supplication against them. Ibn Abbas said: It is a predicate, meaning He mocked them as they ended up in the Fire. The meaning of God mocked is their punishment for their mockery. It was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah.
9:80: The Almighty’s saying: Ask forgiveness for them comes in His saying: And never pray over any of them who dies.
9:81: The Almighty said: Those who stayed behind rejoiced in their sitting. That is, in their sitting. He sat down, sitting down, meaning he sat down. And someone else made him sit down, according to al-Jawhari. And those who stayed behind are those who were left behind, meaning God left them behind and discouraged them, or the Messenger of God and the believers left them behind when they knew their reluctance to fight, two opinions, and this was in the Battle of Tabuk. Opposite the Messenger of God is an object for which, and if you wish it can be a source, and disagreement is opposition. And whoever reads behind the Messenger of God means delaying from fighting. And they said, Do not go forth in the heat. That is, some of them said that to each other. Say, 'The fire of Hell.' That is, say to them, O Muhammad, the fire of Hell. More intense in heat, if they only understood. Subject and predicate. Heat is an accusative of explanation, meaning whoever abandons the command of God will be exposed to that fire.
9:82: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: So let them laugh a little is a command, meaning a threat, not an order to laugh. The original is that the lam is broken, but the kasra was deleted because of its heaviness. Al-Hasan said: So let them laugh a little: in this world, and let them weep much in Hell. It was said: It is a command in the sense of report, meaning that they will laugh a little and weep much. Jazā’ is an object for the sake of it, meaning for the reward. Second: There are people who do not laugh because they care about themselves and their state of corruption in their beliefs due to intense fear, even if they are righteous servants. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By God, if you knew what I know, you would laugh little and cry much, and you would go out to the high places, beseeching God Almighty. I wish I were a tree being cut down.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. Al-Hasan Al-Basri, may God be pleased with him, was one of those who was overcome by sadness, so he did not laugh. Ibn Sirin used to laugh and argue with Al-Hasan, saying: God made him laugh and cry. The companions used to laugh, but doing it too much and constantly until it overwhelms one is reprehensible and forbidden, and it is the action of fools and idleness. In the hadith: Its abundance kills the heart. As for crying out of fear of God, His punishment and the severity of His chastisement, it is praiseworthy. He, peace be upon him, said: “Weep, and if you cannot weep, then pretend to weep, for the people of Hell will weep until their tears run down their faces like streams, until the tears stop and blood flows and the eyes become sore that if ships were to sail through them, they would sail.” Narrated by Ibn al-Mubarak on the authority of Anas, and by Ibn Majah as well.
9:83: The Almighty said: Then if God returns you to a party of them meaning the hypocrites. He only said: to a party because all those who stayed in the city were not hypocrites, but there were those among them who had an excuse and those who had no excuse, then He pardoned them and accepted their repentance, like the three who stayed behind. And it will come. And they asked your permission to go out, then say, You will never go out with me" meaning, punish them by never accompanying them. And it is as He said in Surat al-Fath 48:"Say, You will never follow us (al-Fath 48:15). The successors is the plural of khalaf, as if they stayed behind those who went out. Ibn Abbas said: The successors are those who stayed behind from the hypocrites. Al-Hasan said: With the women and weak men, so the masculine was predominant. It was said: The meaning is, then sit with the wicked, from their saying, So-and-so is the successor of his family if he is corrupt among them, from the odor of the mouth of a fasting person. From your saying: The milk has spoiled meaning it has spoiled due to staying in the water skin for a long time. Based on this, it means stay with the spoiled ones. This indicates that taking the spoiled one with you on military expeditions is not permissible.
9:84: It contains eleven issues: First: It was narrated that this verse was revealed regarding Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) prayer over him. This was confirmed in the two Sahihs and others. The narrations clearly state that the Prophet (peace be upon him) prayed over him and that the verse was revealed after that. It was narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik that when the Prophet (peace be upon him) went forward to pray over him, Gabriel came to him and pulled his garment and recited to him, And never pray over any of them if he dies, and the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) turned away and did not pray over him. The confirmed verses contradict this. In Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him, then he left. He did not stay long until the two verses of Bara’ah were revealed: And never pray over any of them who dies. And something similar was narrated by Ibn Umar, narrated by Muslim. Ibn Umar said: “When Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul died, his son Abdullah came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him to give him his shirt to shroud his father in. He gave it to him, then asked him to pray over him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to pray over him. Umar stood up and took hold of the Messenger of God’s garment, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, will you pray over him when God has forbidden you to pray over him? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty has given me a choice and said: ‘Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them, if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times,’ and I will add to seventy.” He said: He is a hypocrite. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him, and God, the Almighty, revealed, And never pray over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave, so he stopped praying over them. Some scholars said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, only prayed over Abdullah bin Ubayy based on the apparent meaning of his conversion to Islam. However, he did not do that because he was forbidden from doing so. Second: If someone were to say: How could Omar say: Do you pray for him when God has forbidden you to pray for him, and there was no previous prohibition against praying for them? It would be said to him: It is possible that this occurred to him, and it was from the type of inspiration and speech that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) testified to, and the Qur’an was revealed according to his intention, as he said: I agreed with my Lord in three things. And it came: in four things. And it was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. So this is from that. And it is possible that he understood that from the words of God the Almighty: Whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them (al-Baqarah 2:20). Not that there was a previous prohibition as indicated by the hadith of Al-Bukhari and Muslim. And God knows best. I said: It is possible that it was understood from the Almighty’s saying: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists (al-Tawbah 9:113) because it was revealed in Mecca. And we will discuss it later. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Ask forgiveness for them verse. The Almighty made it clear that even if he asks forgiveness for them, it will not benefit them, even if he asks forgiveness a lot. Al-Qushayri said: What is narrated that he said: I will add to seventy has not been proven. I said: This is contrary to what was proven in the hadith of Ibn Umar, And I will add more than seventy, and in the hadith of Ibn Abbas, If I knew that if I added more than seventy they would be forgiven, I would add more. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over him. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. Fourth: The scholars differed in the interpretation of his saying: Ask forgiveness for them whether it is despair or a choice. A group said: What is meant by it is despair based on the saying of God Almighty: God will never forgive them. And mentioning the seventy is a common occurrence, or it is their custom in expressing abundance and annoyance. So if one of them says: I will not speak to him for seventy years, it becomes to them like saying: I will never speak to him. Similar to it in annoyance is the saying of God Almighty: In a chain whose length is seventy cubits (al-Haqqah 69:32), and the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Whoever fasts one day for the sake of God, God will distance his face from the Fire for a distance of seventy years. A group said: It is a choice - including Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Urwah - if you wish, you may ask forgiveness for them, and if you wish, you may not ask forgiveness. “That is why when he wanted to pray for Ibn Abi, Umar said: Will you pray for the enemy of God, who said on such and such a day such and such? He said: I was given a choice and I chose.” They said: Then this was abrogated when the verse was revealed: It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness (al-Munafiqun 63:6). That is because they disbelieved meaning that God will not forgive them for their disbelief. Fifth: The Almighty said: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists (al-Tawbah 9:113) and the verse. This verse was revealed in Mecca upon the death of Abu Talib, as will be explained. This is understood to mean the prohibition of asking forgiveness for someone who died as a disbeliever. It precedes this verse from which it is understood that it is a choice, as He said: God has only given me a choice. This is problematic. It was said: Asking forgiveness for the hypocrites in which he was given a choice is a verbal request that is of no benefit, and its purpose is to please the hearts of some of the living relatives of the one for whom forgiveness is sought. And God knows best. Sixth: There is a difference of opinion about the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) giving his shirt to ‘Abdullah. It was said: He gave it to him because ‘Abdullah had given his shirt to the Prophet’s uncle, al-‘Abbas, on the day of Badr. When al-‘Abbas was taken prisoner on the day of Badr - as mentioned above - and his garment was stolen, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw him like that and felt sorry for him. He asked for a shirt for him, but he could not find a shirt that was as big as ‘Abdullah’s shirt, because they were similar in height. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wanted by giving him the shirt to remove his hand from him in this world, so that he would not meet him in the Hereafter while he had a hand in repaying him. It was also said: He gave him the shirt to honour his son, to help him in his request and to comfort his heart. The first is more correct. Al-Bukhari narrated it on the authority of Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, who said: When the day of Badr came, the prisoners were brought and Al-Abbas was brought and he was not wearing any clothes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked for a shirt for him and they found the shirt of Abdullah bin Ubayy that he could afford, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave it to him. For this reason, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took off the shirt that he had put on him. In the hadith, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My shirt will not avail him anything against God, and I hope that a thousand men from my people will submit to my action. This is how it is in some narrations: from my people meaning from the hypocrites of the Arabs. The correct version is that he said: men from his people. It is stated in the Battles of Ibn Ishaq and in some books of interpretation: “A thousand men from the Khazraj submitted to and repented for this action of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Seventh: When God the Almighty said: And never pray for any of them who dies, our scholars said: This is a text prohibiting praying for the infidels, and there is no evidence in it for praying for the believers. There is a difference of opinion as to whether it is taken from its meaning that prayer for the believers is obligatory, according to two opinions. It is taken because he explained the prohibition of praying for the infidels due to their disbelief, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, they disbelieved in God and His Messenger, so if disbelief is removed, prayer becomes obligatory. This is similar to His saying: No indeed, from their Lord that Day they will be veiled (al-Mutaffifin 83:15), meaning the infidels, so it indicates that other than the infidels, namely the believers, will see Him, so that is the same. And God knows best. Or prayer is taken from evidence outside the verse, which is the hadiths that were reported on this topic, and the consensus. The origin of the difference of opinion is the saying of the evidence of the address and leaving it. Muslim narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: A brother of yours has died, so stand up and pray over him. He said: So we stood up and lined up in two rows, meaning the Negus. And on the authority of Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, announced to the people the death of the Negus on the day he died. He took them out to the prayer place and said the four takbirs. The Muslims are unanimously agreed that it is not permissible to omit the funeral prayer for Muslims, whether they committed major sins or were righteous, as is inherited from their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in word and deed. Praise be to God. The scholars are unanimous on this except for the martyr, as mentioned above, and for the people of innovation and rebels. Eighth - The majority of scholars say that the takbir is four. Ibn Sirin said: The takbir used to be three, then they added one. A group said: He should say takbir five times. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud and Zaid bin Arqam. And on the authority of Ali: six takbirs. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Anas bin Malik, and Jabir bin Zaid: three takbirs, and what is relied upon is four. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The angels prayed for Adam and said four Takbirs over him, and said: This is your tradition, O children of Adam. Ninth: There is no recitation in this prayer according to the well-known Maliki school of thought, as well as Abu Hanifa and Al-Thawri, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you pray for the dead, then make your supplication sincere for him. Narrated by Abu Dawud from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Muhammad ibn Maslama, Ashhab from our scholars, and Dawud were of the opinion that he should recite Al-Fatihah, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: There is no prayer without the Opening of the Book based on its generality. And what Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who prayed over a funeral and recited the Opening of the Book and said: So that you may know that it is a Sunnah. And Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: The Sunnah in the funeral prayer is to recite the Mother of the Qur’an in a low voice in the first takbir, then say the takbir three times, and then say the taslim at the end. Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi also mentioned on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: The Sunnah in the funeral prayer is to say Allahu Akbar, recite the Opening Chapter of the Qur’an, then send blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), then devote your supplication to the deceased. One should only recite the first Takbeer, then say the Tasleem. Our Sheikh Abu al-Abbas said: These two hadeeths are authentic, and according to the scholars of Usul al-Fiqh, they are included in the Musnad. It is more appropriate to act upon the hadeeth of Abu Umaamah, as it combines the statement of Allaahu Akbar, There is no prayer, and the supplication devoted to the deceased. Reciting al-Fatihah in it is only an opening supplication. And God knows best. Tenth - It is the Sunnah of the Imam to stand at the head of a man and the buttocks of a woman, based on what Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Anas. He prayed over a funeral and Al-Ala’ bin Ziyad said to him: O Abu Hamza, is this how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed over the dead, as you pray? He would say four takbirs and stand at the head and buttocks of the woman. He said, Yes. Muslim narrated it on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub, who said: I prayed behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he prayed over Umm Ka’b, who died while she was giving birth. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to pray over her in the middle of her. Eleventh - God Almighty said: And do not stand at his grave. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, buried the dead, he would stand at his grave and pray for him to be steadfast, as we explained in At-Tadhkirah and Al-Hamd, may God bless him and grant him peace.
9:85: Repeat it for emphasis. This has been discussed above.
9:86: The believers volunteered to answer, and the hypocrites made excuses. The command is for the believers to continue believing, and for the hypocrites to begin believing. That is in the accusative case, meaning that they believed. Length means wealth, and it has been mentioned before. He mentioned them specifically because the one who does not have wealth does not need permission because he is excused. And they said, 'Leave us to be with those who sit back' meaning those who are unable to go out.
9:87: The Almighty said: They were pleased to be with the ones who stayed behind. Al-Khawalif is the plural of Khalafah, meaning with women, children, and men who have excuses. A man may also be called Khalafah or Khalaf if he is not noble, as mentioned above. It is said: So-and-so is Khalafah of his family if he is below them. Al-Nahhas said: Its origin is from Khalaf al-Laban left if it turns sour from sitting for a long time. And Khalaf Fumm al-Sa'im fasting person if its smell changes, and from it so-and-so is Khalaf Su'u bad, except that Fawa'il is the plural of Fa'ilah. The fa'il of an adjective is not pluralized as Fawa'il except in poetry, except for two letters, which are Faris knight and Halak perished.
9:88: And the Almighty's saying in describing the mujahideen: And for them are the good things It was said: The beautiful women, on the authority of Al-Hasan. The evidence for this is the Almighty's saying: In them are good and beautiful things (al-Rahman 55:70). It is also said: She is the best of women. The original is khayra, but it was shortened, like hayna and hayna. It was also said: The plural of khayr. So the meaning is that for them are the benefits of both worlds. The meaning of success has already been mentioned.
9:89: And the gardens: the orchards. It has also been mentioned before.
9:90: The Almighty said: And the excuse-makers from among the bedouins came Al-A'raj and Al-Dahhak read the excused with a lightened form. Abu Kurayb narrated it from Abu Bakr from Asim, and the people of readings narrated it from Ibn Abbas. Al-Jawhari said: Ibn Abbas used to read the excuse-makers came with a lightened form, from a'dhar. And he would say: By God, this is how it was revealed. Al-Nahhas said: Except that it is based on Al-Kalbi, and it is from a'dhar, and from it qad a'dhar from andhar, meaning he who came to you and warned you went to extremes in his excuse. As for al-mu'dhar with a shaddah, there are two opinions: One of them is that it is the one who is right, so it is in the meaning of the one who apologizes, because he has an excuse. So, the excuse-makers according to this is originally al-mutadharoon, but the ta' was changed to a dhal and was assimilated into it and its vowel was placed on the 'ayn, just as yakhsamoon (Ya-Sin 36:49) was read with a fatha on the kha'. The excuse-makers are allowed to break the 'ayn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. And it is permissible to add a damma to follow the mim. Al-Jawhari and Al-Nahhas mentioned it. However, Al-Nahhas narrated it on the authority of Al-Akhfash, Al-Farra, Abu Hatim, and Abu Ubaid. It is possible that the original was Al-Muta’diroon, then the ta’ was assimilated into the dhal, and they would be those who have an excuse. Labid said: Until the year, then peace be upon you both. Whoever cries for a full year has apologized. The other opinion is that the one who excuses may not be justified, and he is the one who apologizes but has no excuse. Al-Jawhari said, so he is the one who excuses on the basis of the verb, because he is the one who is sick and negligent and apologizes without an excuse. Another said, it is said that someone excused himself in such and such a matter, meaning he was negligent and did not exaggerate in it. The meaning is that they apologized with a lie. Al-Jawhari said: Ibn Abbas used to say: May God curse those who excuse themselves. It seems that the matter with him is that the one who excuses with emphasis is the one who shows an excuse, as a defect without any reality in the excuse. Al-Nahhas: Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Yazid said: It is not permissible for the original to be the one who apologizes, and it is not permissible to assimilate it, so that confusion occurs. Ismail bin Ishaq mentioned that assimilation is avoided according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh, however the context of the speech indicates that they are blameworthy and have no excuse. He said: Because they came to be given permission, and if they were among the weak and sick and those who do not find what to spend, they would not have needed to ask permission. An-Nahhas said: The origin of the words excuse, “excuse,” and excuse are from one thing, which is difficult and impossible. The Arabs say: Who can excuse me from so-and-so? It means that he has done something great that I deserve to punish him for, but the people did not know about it. So who will excuse me if I punish him? According to the light reading, Ibn Abbas said: They are those who stayed behind with an excuse, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them permission. It was said: They are the people of Amir ibn At-Tufayl, who said: O Messenger of God, if we went out to fight with you, the Bedouins of Tayy would raid our wives, children, and livestock. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, excused them. According to the heavy reading in the second statement, they are a people from Ghifar who apologized, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not excuse them, because he knew that they were not right. And God knows best. And a people sat back without an excuse, which they showed out of audacity towards the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They are those about whom God Almighty spoke when He said: And those who denied God and His Messenger sat back, and what is meant by their lie is their saying, We are believers. And to call to prayer is the monument of Balam Ki.
9:91: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: There is no blame upon the weak Al-Baqarah 2:286. This is a principle in the exemption of the incapable from obligation. Whoever is incapable of doing something is exempted from it. Sometimes he is given a substitute, which is an action, and sometimes he is given a substitute, which is a loss. There is no difference between incapacity due to strength or incapacity due to money. Similar to this verse is the Almighty’s saying: God does not charge a soul except [with that within] its capacity Al-Baqarah 2:286 and His saying: There is no blame upon the blind or upon the lame or upon the ill An-Nur 24:61. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Anas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have left behind in Medina people who did not travel, nor spend, nor cross a valley except that they were with you in it. They said: O Messenger of God, how can they be with us while they are in Medina? He said: An excuse has kept them back. This verse, along with what we have mentioned of similar verses, makes clear that there is no blame on those who have an excuse, and they are people whose excuse is known, such as the people of old age, old age, blindness, and lameness, and people who do not find anything to spend. He said: There is no blame on these people. If they are sincere to God and His Messenger if they know the truth and love His friends and hate His enemies, the scholars said: So the Truth, glory be to Him, excused those who have excuses, and hearts were not patient, so Ibn Umm Maktum went out to Uhud and asked to be given the banner, so Mus'ab bin Umair took it, then a disbeliever came and struck his hand that had the banner and cut it off, so he held it with the other hand and struck the other hand and held it to his chest and recited And Muhammad is no more than a messenger, and messengers have passed away before him (Al Imran 3:144). These are the determinations of the people. And the Truth says: There is no blame upon the blind and it is in the beginning. And there is no blame upon the lame "And Amr bin Al Jamuh, one of the leaders of the Ansar, was lame and he was in the first army. The Messenger, peace be upon him, said to him: God has excused you, so he said: By God, I will dig with my lameness in Paradise." And their likes according to what was mentioned in this Surah, may God be pleased with them. And Abd God bin Mas'ud said: And a man would be brought, supported between two men until he was made to stand in the row. Second: The Almighty’s saying: If they are sincere. Sincerity means doing one’s work sincerely and free from deception. From this comes sincere repentance. Naftawayh said: To be sincere about something means to be sincere. To be sincere about speech means to be sincere about it. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Tamim al-Dari, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Religion is advice three times. We said: To whom? He said: To God, His Book, His Messenger, and the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk.” The scholars said: Advice to God is to sincerely believe in His Oneness, describe Him with the attributes of divinity, purify Him from contradictions, and desire to love and avoid what displeases Him. Advice to His Messenger is to believe in His prophethood, adhere to obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions, befriend those who befriend him and oppose those who oppose him, respect him, love him and love his family, glorify him and glorify his Sunnah, and revive it after his death by searching for it, understanding it, defending it, spreading it, and calling people to it, and adopting his noble morals, may God bless him and grant him peace. Likewise, advice to the Book of God is to read it, understand it, defend it, teach it, honor it, and adopt it. Advice to the leaders of the Muslims is to refrain from rebelling against them, to guide them to the truth, and to alert them to the affairs of the Muslims that they have neglected, and to adhere to their obedience and fulfill their duty towards them. Advice to the public: to abandon hostility towards them, guide them, love the righteous among them, pray for all of them, and wish good for all of them. In the authentic hadith: “The believers in their mutual love, mercy and compassion are like one body: if one part of it is ill, the rest of the body feels pain and fever.” Third: The Almighty said: There is no way against the doers of good. “No way” is in the nominative case, meaning there is no path to punishment. This verse is a basis for lifting punishment from every doer of good. That is why our scholars said about the one who takes revenge on someone who cut off his hand, and that leads to his death in the process: He is not entitled to blood money, because he is doing good in taking revenge on the one who attacked him. Abu Hanifa said: He is obligated to pay blood money. Likewise, if a stallion attacks a man and kills him while defending himself, he is not liable, and this is what Al-Shafi’i said. Abu Hanifa said: He is obligated to pay his owner the value. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The same applies to all matters of Sharia.
9:92: Fourth - The Almighty said: And there is no blame upon those who, when they come to you that you may carry them. It was narrated that the verse was revealed about Arabadh bin Sariyah. It was also said that it was revealed about Aaidh bin Amr. It was also said that it was revealed about Banu Muqrin - and this is the opinion of the majority of commentators - and they were seven brothers, all of whom accompanied the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. There were no other seven brothers among the Companions besides them, and they are: Al-Nu'man, Mu'qil, Uqayl, Suwaid, Sinan, and a seventh who was not named. Banu Muqrin Al-Muzaniyyun are seven brothers who migrated and accompanied the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one else shared with them - according to what Ibn Abd Al-Barr and a group mentioned - in this honor. It was also said that they all witnessed the Battle of the Trench. It was said: It was revealed about seven men from different clans, and they are the weepers who came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk to carry them, but he did not find anything to carry them on, so they turned back with tears streaming from their eyes, grieving that they could not find anything to spend. So they were called the weepers. They are Salim bin Umair from Banu Amr bin Auf, and Alba bin Zaid, the brother of Banu Haritha, and Abu Laila Abd al-Rahman bin Kaab from Banu Mazen bin al-Najjar, and Amr bin al-Hamam from Banu Salamah, and Abdullah bin al-Mughaffal al-Muzani, and it was said: Rather, he is Abdullah bin Amr al-Muzani, and Harmi bin Abdullah, the brother of Banu Waqif, and Arabadh bin Sariyah al-Fazari, this is how Abu Omar named them in his book al-Durar. There is a difference of opinion about them. Al-Qushayri said: Ma'qil ibn Yasar, Sakhr ibn Khansa', Abdullah ibn Ka'b al-Ansari, Salim ibn Umair, Tha'laba ibn Ghanmah, Abdullah ibn Mughaffal and another. They said: O Prophet of God, you have summoned us to go out with you, so carry us on raised sandals and woven sandals so that we may fight with you. He said: I cannot find anything to carry you on, so they turned away crying. Ibn Abbas said: They asked him to carry them on beasts of burden, and a man needed two camels, one to ride and one to carry his water and provisions because of the long road. Al-Hasan said: It was revealed about Abu Musa and his companions who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to carry them, and he was angry at that, so he said: By God, I cannot carry you and I cannot find anything to carry you on, so they turned away crying. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them and gave them a herd of sheep. Abu Musa said: Didn't you swear, O Messenger of God? He said: If God wills, I will not swear an oath and then see something better than it, except that I will do what is better and atone. On my right. I said: This is an authentic hadith narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim with its wording and meaning. In Muslim: He called for us and ordered for us five purebred camels... the hadith. And at the end of it: So go, for God has carried you. Al-Hasan and Bakr bin Abdullah also said: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Mughaffal Al-Muzani, who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him to carry him. Al-Jurjani said: The meaning is, nor upon those who, when they come to you to ask you to carry them and you say, I cannot find. So it is a subject conjoined to what preceded it without a waw, and the answer is, they turned away. And their eyes overflow with tears The sentence is in the accusative case as a state. Sadly is a verbal noun. That they do not find is in the accusative case with that. Al-Nahhas said: Al-Farra’ said, it is permissible for they do not find to make not mean not. And according to the Basrans, it means that they do not find. Fifth: The majority of scholars agree that if someone does not find what he can spend on his military campaign, then it is not obligatory for him. Our scholars said: If his habit is to beg, then it is obligatory for him, just as for the Hajj, and he goes out according to his habit, because if his condition does not change, then the obligation is imposed on him as it is imposed on someone who has money. And God knows best. Sixth: In the words of God the Almighty: And their eyes overflowed with tears there is evidence for circumstantial evidence. Some of them provide necessary knowledge, and some of them are open to hesitation. The first is like someone passing by a house in which the announcement of death has been made, cheeks have been scratched, hair has been shaved, voices have been raised, pockets have been torn, and they have called out for the owner of the house to perish, so he knows that he has died. As for the second, it is like the tears of orphans at the doors of rulers. God the Almighty said, informing about the brothers of Joseph, peace be upon him: And they came to their father at night, weeping (Yusuf 12:16). They are the liars. God the Almighty said, informing about them: And they brought his shirt with false blood (Yusuf 12:18). Despite this, they are circumstantial evidence that is often used as evidence, and testimonies are built on them based on the appearance of circumstances and most of them. The poet said: If tears run down your cheeks, you will know who is crying and who is pretending to cry. This meaning will come in full in Yusuf, God willing.
9:93: The Almighty said: The way meaning the punishment and sin is only against those who ask your permission while they are rich meaning the hypocrites. He mentioned them repeatedly to emphasize the warning against their evil actions.
9:94: The Almighty says: They apologize to you meaning the hypocrites. We will not believe you meaning we will not believe you. God has already informed us of your report meaning He has informed us of your secrets. And God will see your deeds in what you will resume. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do meaning He will reward you for your deeds. All of this has already been fully discussed.
9:95: The Almighty said: They will swear to you by God when you return to them meaning from Tabuk. The thing sworn upon is omitted, meaning they swear that they were not able to leave. To turn away from them meaning to overlook their blame. Ibn Abbas said: meaning do not speak to them. And in the report, it is said that "he, peace be upon him, said when he returned from Tabuk: Do not sit with them and do not speak to them." They are unclean meaning their work is unclean, and the meaning is: they are unclean, meaning their work is ugly. And their refuge is Hell meaning their home and place. Al-Jawhari said: Refuge is any place to which something takes refuge at night or during the day. So-and-so took refuge in his home, ya'wi owyan, on fa'ul, and iwa'. From this is the Almighty's saying: I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water (Hud 11:43). And I took him refuge. And I took him refuge if I brought him down to you, I did and I did, with the same meaning, on the authority of Abu Yazid. The camel shelter with a kasra on the waw is a language that refers to the camel shelter in particular, and it is anomalous.
9:96: Abdullah bin Ubayy swore that he would not stay away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, after that and asked him to be pleased with him.
9:97: The Almighty’s saying: The desert Arabs are more severe in disbelief and hypocrisy contains two issues: First: When God, the Almighty, mentioned the conditions of the hypocrites in Medina, He mentioned those who were outside of it and far from it from the Bedouins, so He said that their disbelief is more severe. Qatada said: Because they are further from knowing the Sunnah. It was also said: Because they are more hard-hearted, harsher in speech, coarse in nature, and further from hearing the revelation. Therefore, God, the Almighty, said about them: And more deserving meaning more likely. That they should not know “that” is in the accusative case with the deletion of the baa. You say: You are deserving of doing and that you do. If you delete the baa only Al-Bukhari is suitable, and if you bring the baa then Al-Bukhari and others are suitable. You say: You are deserving of standing, and deserving of standing. If you said: You are deserving of standing, it would be wrong. Rather, it is suitable with that because that indicates the future, so it is as if it is a replacement for what was deleted. The limits of what God has revealed meaning the obligations of the Shari’ah. It was also said: God’s proofs in the Lordship and the sending of the Messengers are due to their lack of foresight. Second: Since this was the case and indicated their deficiency and their lowering from the full rank of others, three rulings were based on this: First: They have no right to the spoils of war, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Buraidah, in which it says: “Then invite them to move from their home to the home of the immigrants and tell them that if they do so, they will have what the immigrants have and will be subject to what the immigrants are subject to. If they refuse to move from it, then tell them that they will be like the Bedouin Muslims, and the ruling of God that applies to the believers will apply to them and they will have nothing in the spoils and booty unless they fight alongside the Muslims.” The second: disregarding the testimony of the Bedouins about the city dwellers, because that would confirm the accusation. Abu Hanifa permitted it, saying: Because it does not take into account every accusation, and all Muslims are just in his view. Al-Shafi’i permitted it if he is just and acceptable, and this is correct, as we explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. God the Almighty described the Bedouins here with three descriptions: The first - as disbelievers and hypocrites. The second - as someone who takes what he spends as a loss and awaits disaster for you. The third - as someone who believes in God and the Last Day and takes what he spends as an act of devotion to God and the prayers of the Messenger. So whoever has this description, it is unlikely that his testimony will not be accepted, and he will be included with the second and the first, and that is invalid. We have already discussed this in An-Nisa’. Third: Their leading the people of the city in prayer is forbidden due to their ignorance of the Sunnah and their abandonment of Friday prayers. Abu Majlaz disliked the leading of the Bedouin. Malik said: He should not lead the prayer even if he approves of them. Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Shafi’i, Ishaq and the people of opinion said: Prayer behind the Bedouin is permissible. Ibn al-Mundhir chose this if he fulfilled the limits of prayer. The Almighty said: More severe its origin is more severe, and it has been mentioned before. Kufr is an accusative of explanation. And hypocrisy is in apposition to it. And more worthy is in apposition to more severe, and its meaning is more appropriate. It is said: So-and-so is worthy of such-and-such, meaning he is worthy of it, and you are worthy of doing such-and-such, and the plural is jadra’ and jadayrun. Its origin is from jadar al-ha’it, which means raising it with a building. So his saying: he is more worthy of such-and-such, means he is closer to it and more deserving of it. That they do not know means that they do not know. The Arabs: a generation of people, and the nisba to them is Arab among Arabs, and they are the people of the cities. The Bedouins among them are the inhabitants of the desert in particular. It came in classical poetry as ‘a’arib. The nisba to the Bedouins is ‘a’rabi because it does not have a singular, and ‘a’raab is not a plural for Arabs as the Nabataeans were a plural for Nabataeans, but rather ‘arab is a generic name. The pure Arabs are the pure ones among them, and it was taken from its wording and lied about it, like you say: there is no night. And they may say: the Arab Arabs. And ta’arab means resembling the Arabs. And ta’arab after his migration means he became a Bedouin. The Arabized Arabs are those who are not pure, and so are the Arabized, and Arabic is this language. Ya'rub bin Qahtan was the first to speak Arabic, and he is the father of all Yemenites. The Arabs and the Arabs are one: like the Persians and the Ajams. The Arab is the diminutive of the Arabs, as the poet said: Fog is the food of the Arabs, but the souls of the non-Arabs do not desire it. Rather, he made them small out of respect, as he said: I am its smooth trunk, and its generous cluster, all from Al-Jawhari. Al-Qushayri narrated that the plural of Arab is Arabs, and the plural of Bedouin is Arabs and Aaraib. When a Bedouin is told, O Arab, he is happy, and when an Arab is told, A Bedouin, he becomes angry. The Muhajireen and Ansar are Arabs, not Bedouins. The Arabs were called Arabs because the children of Ishmael originated from Araba, which is from Tihama, so they were named after it. The Quraysh settled in Araba, which is Mecca, and the rest of the Arabs spread out in its peninsula.
9:98: God the Almighty said: And among the bedouins are those who takeمنin the nominative case as a subject. What they spend is a loss are two objects, and the meaning is that they spend it, so the ha' was deleted due to the length of the noun. Maghramaan means loss and deprivation, and its origin is the necessity of something, and from it: Indeed, its punishment is a loss (al-Furqan 25:65) meaning necessary, that is, they see what they spend in jihad and charity as a loss and do not expect a reward for it. And he awaits for you the evils awaiting and waiting, and it was mentioned before. The circles are the plural of circle, and it is the state that changes from blessing to calamity, that is, they gather with ignorance of spending the evil of the income and the evil of the heart. Upon them is the circle of evil Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a damma on the seen here and in the fatha and the rest with a fatha. They agreed on the fatha on the seen in His statement: Your father was not a bad man (Maryam 19:28). The difference between them is that evil with a damma is the disliked. Al-Akhfash said: That is, upon them is the circle of defeat and evil. Al-Farra’ said: That is, upon them is the circle of torment and affliction. They said: It is not permissible to say ‘a man of evil’ with the dammah, just as you do not say ‘he is a man of torment or evil.’ It was narrated from Muhammad ibn Yazid that he said: Su’ with the fathah is badness. Sibawayh said: I passed by a man of truth, meaning a man of righteousness. It is not from truthfulness of the tongue, and if it were from truthfulness of the tongue, you would not have said: I passed by a garment of truth. And I passed by a man of evil is not from his evil, but rather its meaning is I passed by a man of corruption. Al-Farra’ said: Su’ with the fathah is the source of ‘his evil,’ ‘saw’an,’ ‘mis’a’ah,’ and ‘saw’iyah. Someone else said: The verb from it is ‘sa’a yusu’u. Su’ with the dammah is a noun, not a source, and it is like saying: Upon them is the circle of affliction and misfortune.
9:99: The Almighty said: And among the desert Arabs are those who believe in God meaning they believed. What is meant is Banu Muqrin from Muzaynah, as mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. Qurbat is the plural of qurbah, which is what one draws near to God Almighty with. The plural is qurbah, qurbat, and qurbat, as narrated by An-Nahhas. Qurbah with a dammah is what one draws near to God Almighty with. You say: I drew near to God an offering. Qurbah with a kasrah on the qaf is what water is drawn from. The plural for the smallest number is qurbat, qurbat, and qurbat, and for many there is qurbah. Likewise, the plural of everything that is in the form fa'lah, such as sidrat and faqrah. You can open the 'ayn, break it, or sukun it, as narrated by Al-Jawhari. Nafi' read in the narration of Warsh qurbah with a dammah on the ra', which is the original. The rest read it with a sukun for ease, such as kutub and rusul. There is no disagreement about qurbah. Ibn Sa'dan narrated that Yazid ibn Al-Qa'qa' read Ala innahu qurbah lahum. The meaning of and the prayers of the Messenger is his seeking forgiveness and supplication. Prayer is of various types. Prayer from God, the Almighty, is mercy, goodness, and blessing. God the Almighty said: It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels do (al-Ahzab 33:43). Prayer from the angels is supplication, and it is also from the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, as he said: “And pray for them. Indeed, your prayer is a reassurance for them.” That is, your supplication is a confirmation and reassurance for them. Indeed, it is a means of drawing near to them. That is, it brings them closer to God’s mercy, meaning their expenses.
9:100: It contains seven issues: First: When God, the Almighty, mentioned the types of Arabs, He mentioned the Muhajireen and the Ansar, and explained that among them were those who were the first to migrate and those who were the Followers, and praised them. There is disagreement about the number of their classes and types. We will mention a part of that to clarify the purpose of it, God willing. Omar bin Al-Khattab narrated that he read and the Ansar in the nominative case in apposition to the first. Al-Akhfash said: The genitive case in the Ansar is correct, because the first are among them. The Ansar is an Islamic name. Anas bin Malik was asked: “What do you think of people saying to you: The Ansar, is it a name that God named you with or were you called by it in the pre-Islamic period?” He said: Rather, it is a name that God named us with in the Qur’an. Abu Omar mentioned it in Al-Istidhkar. Second: The text of the Qur’an gives preference to the first of the Muhajireen and Ansar, who are those who prayed towards the two Qiblahs, according to Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and a group. According to the companions of Al-Shafi’i, they are those who witnessed the Pledge of Ridwan, which is the Pledge of Hudaybiyyah, and Al-Sha’bi said the same. And on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b and Ata’ bin Yasar: They are the people of Badr. And they agreed that whoever migrated before the change of the Qiblah is from the first Muhajireen, without any disagreement among them. As for the best of them, they are: Third: Abu Mansur al-Baghdadi al-Tamimi said: Our companions agree that the best of them are the four caliphs, then the remaining six until the ten are complete, then the Badris, then the companions of Uhud, then the people of the Pledge of Ridwan at al-Hudaybiyah. Fourth - As for the first of them to convert to Islam, Mujalid narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas, Who were the first people to convert to Islam? He said, Abu Bakr, or did you not hear Hassan say: If you remember a sorrow from a trusted brother, then remind your brother Abu Bakr of what they did. The best of creation is the most pious, the most just after the Prophet, and the most faithful to his duties. The second next is the praiseworthy scene and the first of them to believe in the messengers Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi narrated on the authority of Yusuf ibn Yaqub ibn al-Majshun that he said: I met my father, our Sheikh Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, Rabia ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman, Salih ibn Kaysan, Sa`d ibn Ibrahim, and Uthman ibn Muhammad al-Akhnasi, and they had no doubt that the first of the people to embrace Islam was Abu Bakr. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Hassan, and Asma bint Abi Bakr, and Ibrahim al-Nakha`i also said the same. It was also said that the first to embrace Islam was Ali. This was narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Arqam, Abu Dharr, al-Miqdad, and others. Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah said: I do not know of any disagreement among historians that Ali was the first of them to embrace Islam. It was also said that the first to embrace Islam was Zayd ibn Haritha. Mu`mar mentioned something similar on the authority of al-Zuhri. This is the opinion of Sulayman ibn Yasar, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and Imran ibn Abi Anas. It was also said that the first to embrace Islam was Khadija, the mother of the believers. This was narrated from al-Zuhri through various sources, and this is the opinion of Qatadah, Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, and a group of others. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Tha'labi, the commentator, claimed that scholars agreed that the first to convert to Islam was Khadija, and that their disagreement was only about those who converted to Islam after her. Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Rahawayh Al-Hanthali combined these reports, and he used to say: The first man to convert to Islam was Abu Bakr, and the first woman to convert to Islam was Khadija, and the first boy to convert to Islam was Ali, and the first slave to convert to Islam was Zaid bin Haritha, and the first slave to convert to Islam was Bilal. And God knows best. Muhammad bin Saad said: Mus'ab bin Thabit told me, and Abu Al-Aswad Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman bin Nawfal told me: Al-Zubayr converted to Islam after Abu Bakr, and he was the fourth or fifth. Al-Layth bin Saad said: Abu Al-Aswad told me: Al-Zubayr converted to Islam when he was eight years old. It was narrated that Ali converted to Islam when he was seven years old. It was also said: He was ten years old. Fifth: It is well known from the method of the people of hadith that every Muslim who saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is one of his companions. Al-Bukhari said in his Sahih: Whoever accompanied the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or saw him from the Muslims is one of his companions. It was narrated from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab that he did not count as a companion except one who stayed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a year or two, and participated in one or two battles with him. If this statement is true from Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, then it is necessary that Jarir bin Abdullah Al-Bajali or anyone who shared with him the apparent lack of what he stipulated for them, from those we do not know of any disagreement regarding counting as companions, should not be counted as a companion.
