Sixth: There is no dispute that the first of the emigrants was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. Ibn al-Arabi said: Precedence is achieved by three things: the attribute, which is faith, the time, and the place. The best of these aspects is the precedence of attributes, and the evidence for that is the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Sahih: “We are the last ones, but they were given the Scripture before us, and we were given it after them. This is their day in which they differed, and God has guided us to it. So the Jews will be tomorrow, and the Christians the day after tomorrow.” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed us that those nations who preceded us in time, we preceded them in faith and compliance with the command of God Almighty and submission to Him, and surrender to His command and contentment with His duties and tolerance of His tasks. We do not object to Him, nor do we choose with Him, nor do we change His law based on our opinion as the People of the Scripture did, and that is by God’s success in what He has decreed, His facilitation of what pleases Him, and we would not have been guided had God not guided us. Seventh - Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: This verse includes the preference of those who were first in every virtue of the virtues of the Sharia, in knowledge, religion, courage, or other, from giving money and rank in honor. There is a difference of opinion on this issue between Abu Bakr and Omar, may God be pleased with them. The scholars differed on the preference of those who were first in giving over others. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, that he did not prefer people in giving over others according to their precedence. Omar used to say to him: Do you treat those who were first like those who had no precedence? Abu Bakr said: They only worked for God and their reward is for it. Omar used to prefer those who were first in his caliphate, then he said upon his death: If I live until tomorrow, I will join the lowest of people with the highest of them, so he died that night. The caliphate to this day is based on this difference of opinion. The Almighty’s saying: And those who followed them with goodness contains two issues: First: Omar and the Ansar read it in the nominative case. Those who omitted the waw as a description of the Ansar, so Zaid bin Thabit reviewed it, so Omar asked Ubayy bin Kaab and he believed Zaid, so Omar returned to him and said: We only thought that we were raised to a level that no one else with us would attain. So my father said: I find proof of that in the Book of God at the beginning of Surah Al-Jumu'ah: And others among them have not yet joined them (Al-Jumu'ah: 3) and in Surah al-Hashr 59:And those who came after them say, Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith" (al-Hashr 59:10). And in Surah Al-Anfal with His saying: "And those who believed afterward and emigrated and fought with you - those are from you" (al-Anfal 8:75). So the reading with the waw was confirmed. And God explained with His saying: "With goodness" what they are followed in from their actions and words, not in what they committed of slips and mistakes, since they were not infallible, may God be pleased with them. Second: The scholars differed regarding the followers and their ranks. Al-Khatib Al-Hafiz said: A follower is one who accompanied a companion, and one of them is called a follower and a follower. The words of Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah and others indicate that it is sufficient for him to hear from the companion or meet him even if there is no customary companionship. It has been said: The name of the followers is given to those who converted to Islam after Al-Hudaybiyyah, such as Khalid bin Al-Walid and Amr bin Al-Aas and those who were close to them from the Muslims of the conquest, because it was proven that Abd Al-Rahman bin Awf complained to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Khalid bin Al-Walid, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Khalid: “Leave my companions alone, for by Him in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend every day the equivalent of Mount Uhud in gold, it would not reach the level of one of them, nor even half of it.” It is surprising that Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah Al-Na’ma’ and Suwaidan, the sons of Muqrin Al-Muzni, were counted among the Tabi’un when he mentioned the brothers among the Tabi’un, although they are two well-known companions who are mentioned among the companions, and they witnessed the Battle of the Trench as mentioned above. And God knows best. The greatest of the Tabi’un were the seven jurists from the people of Madinah, and they are: Sa’id bin Al-Musayyab, Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, Kharijah bin Zaid, Abu Salamah bin Abd Al-Rahman, Abdullah bin Utbah bin Mas’ud, and Sulayman bin Yasar. Some of the great scholars composed them in one verse, saying: Their thigh is Obaid God, Urwa, Qasim, Saeed Abu Bakr, Suleiman, Kharijah Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: The best of the Tabi'un is Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. He was told: Alqamah and al-Aswad. He said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Alqamah and al-Aswad. It was also narrated from him that he said: The best of the Tabi'un are Qais, Abu Uthman, Alqamah and Masruq. These were virtuous and from the elite of the Tabi'un. He also said: Ata' was the Mufti of Mecca and al-Hasan was the Mufti of Basra. These are the two people who speak the most about them, and the most unknown. It was narrated from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud who said: The two leaders of the Tabi'un among women are Hafsah bint Sirin and Umrah bint Abd al-Rahman, and the third of them - and they are not like them - is Umm al-Darda'. It was narrated from al-Hakim Abu Abdullah who said: There is a class that is counted among the Tabi'un, but it is not authentic that any of them heard from the Companions. Among them are Ibrahim ibn Suwaid al-Nakha'i, who is not Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Nakha'i the jurist. Bakir ibn Abi ibn Abi al-Sumait, and Bakir ibn Abdullah al-Ashja'. He mentioned others and said: Their class is counted among the followers of the Tabi’un, and they met the Companions, among them Abu al-Zinad Abdullah bin Dhakwan, who met Abdullah bin Omar and Anas. Hisham bin Urwah, who was introduced to Abdullah bin Omar, Jabir bin Abdullah and Musa bin Uqbah, who met Anas bin Malik, and Umm Khalid bint Khalid bin Saeed. Among the Tabi’un is a class called the Mukhadrameen, who are those who lived during the pre-Islamic era and during the lifetime of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) and converted to Islam without having any companionship. One of them is Mukhadram with the first letter of the letter Raa’ open, as if he is Khadram, meaning he was cut off from his peers who lived during the Companions and other times. Muslim mentioned them and counted them as twenty people, among them Abu Amr al-Shaibani, Suwaid bin Ghafla al-Kindi, Amr bin Maymun al-Awdi, Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, Abd al-Khair bin Yazid al-Khairani with the first letter of the letter Khaa’ open, a clan from Hamdan, Abd al-Rahman bin Mal, and Abu al-Halal al-Atki Rabi’ah bin Zararah. Among those who were not mentioned by Muslim are: Abu Muslim Al-Khawlani Abdullah bin Thaub, and Al-Ahnaf bin Qais. This is a brief overview of the knowledge of the Companions and Followers whose virtues were spoken of in the Holy Quran, may God be pleased with them all. And it is sufficient for us to have the words of God the Almighty: You are the best nation produced for mankind (Al Imran 3:110) based on what was mentioned above. And the words of God the Almighty: And thus We have made you a just community (al-Baqarah 2:143) and the verse. And the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: I wish we could see our brothers… Hadith. So he made us his brothers. If we fear God and follow his footsteps, God will gather us in his group and not deviate us from his path and religion, for the sake of Muhammad and his family.
9:101: The Almighty said: And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites subject and predicate. That is, a people of hypocrites, meaning Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam, Ghifar, and Ashja'. And among the people of Madinah are those who are stubborn in hypocrisy that is, a people who are stubborn in hypocrisy. It was said: stubborn is from the description of the hypocrites, so there is an inversion in the speech, meaning. And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites who are stubborn in hypocrisy, and among the people of Madinah is the same. The meaning of stubborn is that they stayed and did not repent, according to Ibn Zayd. Another said: they persisted in it and refused anything else, and the meaning is close. The root of the word is from softness, touching, and detachment, so it is as if they were devoted to hypocrisy. From this comes the word mardah a sand dune with no vegetation in it, and a branch with no leaves on it, and a horse with no hair on its two sides, and a young man with no beard between beardless, and it is not said: a young girl with no beard. The smoothing of a building is its smoothing. This is evident in His statement: A smoothed structure (al-Naml 27:44). The smoothing of a branch is its stripping of its leaves. It is said: marda, murada, marwadan, and muradah. The Almighty’s saying: You do not know them, We know them is like His saying: You do not know them, God knows them (al-Anfal 8:60) based on what was mentioned above. It was said: The meaning is that you do not know, O Muhammad, the outcome of their affairs, and we are the only ones who know them. This prevents anyone from being judged to be in Heaven or Hell. God the Almighty says: We will punish them twice; then they will be returned to a great punishment. Ibn Abbas said: With diseases in this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. The illness of the believer is expiation, and the illness of the disbeliever is a punishment. It was said that the first punishment is the disgrace when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) finds out about them, as will be explained in the case of the hypocrites. The second punishment is the punishment of the grave. Al-Hasan and Qatadah: The punishment of this world and the punishment of the grave. Ibn Zayd: The first is the calamities in their wealth and children, and the second is the punishment of the grave. Mujahid: Hunger and killing. Al-Farra: Killing and the punishment of the grave. It was said: Captivity and killing. It was said: The first is taking zakat from their wealth and implementing the prescribed punishments on them, and the second is the punishment of the grave. It was said: One of the two punishments is what God the Almighty said: So do not let their wealth impress you - to His saying - God only intends to punish them with it in the life of this world. The purpose of the verse is to follow the punishment, or to double the punishment for them.
9:102: That is, among the people of Medina and those around you are people who have acknowledged their sins, and others are waiting for the command of God to judge them as He wills. The first group may have been hypocrites who were not stubborn in hypocrisy, and it may have been that they were believers. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about ten who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk, so seven of them tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque. Qatada said something similar and said: It was revealed about them: Take from their wealth a charity, mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. Zaid bin Aslam said: They were eight. It was said: They were six. It was said: Five. Mujahid said: The verse was revealed about Abu Lubaba Al-Ansari specifically in his case with Banu Qurayzah, and that is because they spoke to him about submitting to the judgment of God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he pointed to his throat for them. He wanted the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to slaughter them if they descended. When he was disgraced, he repented and regretted it and tied himself to one of the pillars of the mosque. He swore that he would neither eat nor drink until God forgave him or he died. He remained like that until God forgave him, and this verse was revealed. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to be released. Al-Tabari mentioned it on the authority of Mujahid, and Ibn Ishaq mentioned it in the Seerah more comprehensively than this. Ashhab said on the authority of Malik: And others was revealed concerning Abu Lubaba and his companions. “And he said when he committed the sin: O Messenger of God, shall I seek your protection and be deprived of my wealth?” He said: A third of that will suffice you. And God Almighty said: Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and sanctify them. And Ibn al-Qasim narrated it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ibn Wahb from Malik. And the majority of scholars say that the verse was revealed concerning those who stayed behind from the Battle of Tabuk, “and they had tied themselves up as Abu Lubabah had done, and they had pledged to God that they would not release themselves until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was the one who released them and was pleased with them. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I swear by God that I will not release them nor excuse them until I am ordered to release them. They refused to leave me and stayed behind from the conquest with the Muslims. Then God revealed this verse. When it was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to them and released them and excused them. When they were released, they said: O Messenger of God, this is our wealth that you left behind us, so give it in charity on our behalf, purify us and ask forgiveness for us. He said: “I was not commanded to take anything from your wealth.” So God revealed: Take from their wealth a charity al-Masjid an-Nabawi. Ibn Abbas said: They were ten people, including Abu Lubabah, so he took a third of their wealth and it was an expiation for the sins they committed. So their bad deed was staying behind, according to the consensus of the people of this article. They differed about what was good. Al-Tabari and others said: Confession, repentance and regret. It was said: Their good deed that they did was that they joined the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and tied themselves to the pillars of the mosque and said: We will not approach our family or children until God grants us an excuse. A group said: Rather, the good deed was their raiding what preceded the raiding of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Although this verse was revealed about Bedouins, it is general until the Day of Resurrection for those who have good and bad deeds, so it is hoped for. Al-Tabari mentioned on the authority of Hajjaj bin Abi Zainab that he heard Abu Uthman say: There is no verse in the Qur’an that I hope for this nation more than the Almighty’s saying: “And others have acknowledged their sins. They mixed a good deed with another bad one.” And in Al-Bukhari on the authority of Samurah bin Jund said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to us: “Two men came to me tonight and sent me to go to a city built of bricks of gold and bricks of silver. We were met by men, half of them as handsome as you have ever seen and half as ugly as you have ever seen. They said to them: ‘Go and fall into that river.’ So they fell into it and then returned to us with that evil gone from them and they were in the best of appearances. They said to me: ‘This is the Garden of Eden and that is your home.’ They said: ‘As for the people who were half handsome and half ugly, they mixed good deeds with bad deeds. God has pardoned them.’” Al-Bayhaqi mentioned in the hadith of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the hadith of the Night Journey, in which he said: Then he ascended with me to the heavens… Then he mentioned the hadith until he mentioned his ascension to the seventh heaven. They said: “May God give him life, brother and successor. What a brother, what a successor, and what a good arrival he was. He came and there was a man with gray hair sitting on a chair at the gate of Paradise. With him were people with fair faces and people with black faces, but their colors were slightly different. They came to a river and washed in it, and they came out of it with some of their colors gone. Then they came to another river and washed in it, and they came out of it with some of their colors gone. Then they entered the third river, and they came out of it with their colors gone like the colors of their companions. They sat with their companions, and he said: O Gabriel, who are these with white faces and those with some of their colors? They entered the river with their colors gone. He said: This is your father Abraham, he was the first gray-haired man on the face of the earth. These people with white faces are people who did not mix their faith with injustice - he said - and as for those with some of their colors, they mixed a good deed with another bad one, so they repented, so God accepted their repentance. As for the first river, it is the mercy of God. As for the second, it is the grace of God. As for the third river, And their Lord gave them a pure drink to drink.” And he mentioned the hadith. And the waw in his saying: And another evil is said to mean: it is in the sense of the ba’, and it is said: it is in the sense of with, like you say: the water and the wood are equal. The Kufians denied that and said: because the wood cannot be presented before the water, and the last in the verse can be presented before the first, so it is like mixing the water with the milk.
9:103: It has eight issues. First: The Almighty’s saying: Take from their wealth a charity. There is a difference of opinion regarding this commanded charity. It was said: It is the obligatory charity, as Juwaybir said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is the saying of Ikrimah as mentioned by Al-Qushayri. It was said: It is specific to those about whom it was revealed, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a third of their wealth from them, and this is not part of the obligatory zakat at all. For this reason, Malik said: If a man gives all of his wealth in charity, it is sufficient for him to give a third, adhering to the hadith of Abu Lubabah. According to the first opinion, it is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its apparent meaning indicates that it is limited to him, so no one else takes the charity. According to this, it is dropped when he drops it and is removed by his death. And on this basis, those who refused to pay zakat relied on Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and said: He used to give us instead of it purification, sanctification, and prayers for us, and we did not have them from anyone else. Their poet composed a poem about this, saying: We obeyed the Messenger of God as long as there was no conflict between us. What is strange about Abu Bakr’s reign? And those who asked you and you refused were like dates or sweeter to them than dates. We will prevent them as long as there are still honorable people among us who can bear the affliction, in hardship and ease. This is a type of those who stood up for Abu Bakr, the best of them in their method. Abu Bakr said about him: By God, I will fight whoever separates prayer from zakat. Ibn al-Arabi: As for their saying that this is the address of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one else can join him, this is the speech of someone ignorant of the Qur’an, heedless of the source of the Shari’ah, and toying with religion. The address in the Qur’an did not come in one chapter, but its sources differed in different ways. Some of them are addresses directed to the entire nation, such as His saying: O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer (al-Ma’idah 5:6) and His saying: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting (al-Baqarah 2:183) and the like. Some of them are addresses that are specific to him and no one else shares in it, in wording or meaning, such as His saying: And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you (al-Isra’ 17:79) and His saying: Purely for you (al-Ahzab 33:50). And from it is an address that is specific to it in wording and shared by the entire nation in meaning and action, such as His saying: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun (al-Isra’ 17:78) and His saying: So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge in God (al-Nahl 16:98) and His saying: And when you are among them and lead them in prayer (An-Nisa’: 102). So everyone upon whom the sun declines is addressed with prayer. Likewise everyone who recites the Qur’an is addressed with seeking refuge. Likewise everyone who fears establishes prayer in that manner. And of this type is the saying of God the Most High: Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and sanctify them. And in this meaning came His saying the Most High: O Prophet, fear God (al-Ahzab 33:1) and O Prophet, when you divorce women (al-Talaq 65:1). Second: The Almighty’s saying: Of their wealth. Some Arabs, namely the tribe of Dos, said that wealth is clothing, goods, and merchandise. The physical object is not called wealth. This meaning came in the established Sunnah from the narration of Malik from Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dailami from Abu al-Ghaith Salim, the freed slave of Ibn Mut’i’ from Abu Hurayrah, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Khaybar, and we did not take gold or silver as booty, except for wealth, clothing, and goods. The hadith. Others said that silent wealth is gold and silver. It was said: Camels specifically, and from this their saying: Money is camels. It was said: All livestock. Ibn al-Anbari mentioned from Ahmad ibn Yahya - Tha’lab - the grammarian, who said: Whatever falls short of what is due for zakat of gold and silver is not wealth, and he recited: By God, I have never been given livestock, camels, or money that is subject to zakat. Abu Omar said: It is well known from the speech of the Arabs that everything that is financed and owned is money, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The son of Adam says, ‘My wealth, my wealth.’ But he only has of his wealth what he ate and finished, or wore and wore out, or gave in charity and spent. Abu Qatada said: “So he gave me the shield and I bought a sheep-drawer with it among Banu Salamah. It was the first property I acquired in Islam.” So whoever swears to give all his wealth in charity, that applies to every type of his wealth, whether it is something on which zakat is due or not, unless he intended something specific, in which case it applies to what he intended. It has been said that it applies to zakat money. Knowledge encompasses everything and the tongue bears witness that what you own is called wealth. And God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Take from their wealth a charity is absolute and not restricted by a condition regarding what is taken and what is taken from it, nor does it specify the amount of what is taken and what is taken from it. Rather, the explanation of that is in the Sunnah and the consensus, according to what you mentioned. So zakat is taken from all wealth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made zakat obligatory on livestock, grains, and cash, and there is no disagreement about this. They differed on other things, such as horses and other goods. We will mention horses and honey in bees, God willing. The imams narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There is no zakat on less than five wasqs of dates, no zakat on less than five ounces of silver, and no zakat on less than five herds of camels. We have already discussed the livestock in the zakat on grains and what the earth grows in detail. In minerals, in the cow, and in jewelry in this surah. The scholars have agreed that an ounce is forty dirhams. So if a free Muslim owns two hundred dirhams of minted silver - which are the five ounces mentioned in the hadith - for a full year, then he must pay zakat on it, which is a quarter of a tenth of it, five dirhams. The condition of a year is due to the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: There is no zakat on wealth until a year has passed. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. And whatever is in excess of two hundred dirhams of silver, then according to that calculation, a quarter of a tenth of it is due on each piece of it, whether little or much. This is the opinion of Malik, Al-Layth, Al-Shafi’i, most of the companions of Abu Hanifa, Ibn Abi Laila, Al-Thawri, Al-Awza’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, Abu Thawr, Ishaq, and Abu Ubaid. This was narrated from Ali and Ibn Umar. A group said: There is no zakat on anything in excess of two hundred dirhams until the excess reaches forty dirhams. When it reaches that, then one dirham is due on it, which is a quarter of a tenth. This is the opinion of Sa’id ibn Al-Musayyab, Al-Hasan, Ata’, Tawus, Al-Sha’bi, Al-Zuhri, Makhul, Amr ibn Dinar, and Abu Hanifa. Fourth: As for the zakat on gold, the majority of scholars agree that if the gold is twenty dinars, the value of which is two hundred dirhams or more, then zakat is obligatory on it, based on the hadith of Ali, narrated by al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Damrah and al-Harith on the authority of Ali. Al-Tirmidhi said: I asked Muhammad ibn Ismail about this hadith and he said: I think they are both sahih on the authority of Abu Ishaq, and it is possible that it was narrated on the authority of both of them. Al-Baji said in al-Muntaqa: This hadith does not have a chain of transmission there, but the fact that the scholars agree on accepting it is evidence of the validity of its ruling, and God knows best. It was narrated on the authority of al-Hasan and al-Thawri, and some of the companions of Dawud ibn Ali tended towards it, that there is no zakat on gold until it reaches forty dinars. This is refuted by the hadith of Ali and the hadith of Ibn Umar and Aisha that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to take half a dinar from every twenty dinars, and one dinar from forty dinars. This is the view of the majority of scholars except those mentioned. Fifth: The Ummah agreed that there is no zakat on less than five camels. If they reach five, then a sheep is due on them. A sheep refers to one sheep, and a sheep includes both sheep and goats. This is also an agreement among scholars that there is only one sheep in five, and that is its obligatory duty. The zakat on livestock is explained in the book that Abu Bakr wrote to Anas when he sent him to Bahrain. It was narrated by Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, Al-Daraqutni, Al-Nasa’i, Ibn Majah, and others, and all of them are agreed upon. The disagreement on it is in two places, one of them is in the zakat on camels, which is when they reach one hundred and twenty-one. Malik said: The one who gives zakat has the choice: if he wants to take three one-year-old female camels, or if he wants to take two. Ibn Al-Qasim said: Ibn Shihab said: There are three one-year-old female camels until they reach one hundred and thirty, then his right is in them, and two one-year-old female camels. Ibn Al-Qasim said: My opinion is with the opinion of Ibn Shihab. Ibn Habib mentioned that Abdul Aziz bin Abi Salamah, Abdul Aziz bin Abi Hazim, and Ibn Dinar say the opinion of Malik. The second issue is regarding the charity of sheep, which is if it exceeds three hundred and one sheep, then Al-Hasan bin Saleh bin Hayy said: There are four sheep in it, and if it is four hundred and one sheep then there are five sheep in it, and so on whenever it increases, for every hundred sheep, and a similar report was narrated from Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i. The majority said: There are three sheep in it for two hundred and one sheep, then there is nothing in it until four hundred, so there are four sheep in it, then whenever it increases to one hundred then there is one sheep in it, unanimously and in agreement. Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: This is an issue in which Ibn Al-Mundhir made a mistake. He reported mistakes in it from the scholars, and he mixed up and made most of the mistakes. Sixth: Al-Bukhari and Muslim did not mention in their Sahihs the details of the zakat of cows. It was included by Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i, Al-Darqutni and Malik in his Muwatta’, and it is mursal, maqtu’ and mawquf. Abu Omar said: Some people narrated it from Tawus from Muadh, except that those who mursal it are more reliable than those who attributed it. Among those who attributed it is Baqiyya from Al-Mas’udi from Al-Hakam from Tawus. They differed about what Baqiyya narrated alone from trustworthy people. Al-Hasan bin ‘Amara narrated it from Al-Hakam, as Baqiyya narrated it from Al-Mas’udi from Al-Hakam, and Al-Hasan is unanimous in its weakness. This hadith was narrated with a connected, authentic, and proven chain of transmission, other than the narration of Tawus. ‘Abd Al-Razzaq mentioned it, saying: Mu’ammar and Al-Thawri told us, from Al-A’mash, from Abu Wa’il, from Masruq, from Muadh bin Jabal, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) sent me to Yemen and ordered him to take from every thirty cows a male or female offspring, and from every forty a mature cow, and from every adult a dinar or its equivalent in gold. This was mentioned by Ad-Daraqutni and Abu Isa At-Tirmidhi who authenticated it. Abu Omar said: There is no disagreement among the scholars that the zakat on cows from the Prophet (peace be upon him) and his companions is what Muadh ibn Jabal said: on thirty mature cows, and on forty mature cows, except for something narrated from Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, Abu Qilabah, Az-Zuhri and Qatadah, who require a sheep for every five cows up to thirty. This is a summary of the details of zakat with its principles and branches in the books of jurisprudence. The mixture will be mentioned in Surat Sad, God willing. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: Charity is taken from truthfulness, as it is evidence of the soundness of his faith and the truthfulness of his inner self with his outer self, and that he is not one of the hypocrites who criticize the voluntary believers in giving charity. Purify them and sanctify them with it are two states of the addressee, the meaning is: Take it as a purifier for them and a sanctifier for them with it. It is permissible to make it two attributes of charity, i.e. a charity that purifies and sanctifies them, and the subject of purifies them is the addressee, and the pronoun in it refers to the described indefinite noun. An-Nahhas and Makki narrated that purifying them from the attribute of charity and sanctifying them with it is a state of the pronoun in Take, which is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is possible that it is a state of charity, but that is weak because it is a state of an indefinite noun. Al-Zajjaj said: It is better to address the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that you purify them and sanctify them with it, with certainty and renewal. It is permissible to use the jussive mood as an answer to the command, and the meaning is: that you take from their money charity that purifies them and sanctifies them, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: Stop and let us weep over the memory of a beloved and a home Al-Hasan read tatahāruhum with a sukūn on the ta’, and it is transferred with a hamza from tahāru and atahārutuhu, like dahar and aḥāṭah. Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: And pray for them. The basic principle in the action of every imam who takes charity is to pray for blessings for the one who gives charity. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa who said: “Whenever people came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with their charity, he would say: O God, pray for them. So Ibn Abi Awfa came to him with his charity and he said: O God, pray for the family of Abi Awfa.” Some people held this view, while others held that this was abrogated by the words of God the Almighty: And never pray for any of them who dies. They said: It is not permissible to pray for anyone except the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) alone, because he was singled out for that. They provided evidence for this with the words of God the Almighty: Do not make the calling of the Messenger among you like the calling of one of you to another (al-Nur 24:63) and the verse. And that Abdullah ibn Abbas used to say: No one should pray for anyone except the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The first is more correct, because the address is not limited to him, as mentioned above, and it will come in the verse after this. So we must follow the example of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and take him as an example, because he used to comply with his words: And pray for them, for your prayer is a comfort to them. That is, if you pray for them when they come with their charity, it will comfort their hearts and they will be happy with it. Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated that he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to me, so I said to my wife: Do not ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for anything. She said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will leave us and we will not ask him for anything! She said: O Messenger of God, pray for my husband. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: May God pray for you and your husband. Prayer here means mercy and compassion. An-Nahhas said: All linguists have reported, as far as we know, that prayer in the speech of the Arabs means supplication, and from that comes the prayer for the dead. Hafs, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read Inna salatuk with the singular form. The rest read it in the plural. Likewise, there is a difference in your prayer commands you (Hud 11:87). It was read as sakun with a sukun on the kaf. Qatada said: Its meaning is dignity for them. And sakun is that by which the souls are calmed and the hearts are reassured.
9:104: There are two issues: First: It was said: Those who did not repent from those who stayed behind said: These were with us yesterday, they did not speak or sit with us, so what is wrong with them now? And what is this special thing that they were given that we were not given? So the verse was revealed: Did they not know? The pronoun in they knew refers to those who did not repent from those who stayed behind. Ibn Zayd said its meaning. It is possible that it refers to those who repented and bound themselves. And the Almighty’s saying: He is an emphasis on the uniqueness of God, the Most High, in these matters. The realization of that is that if he said: that God accepts repentance, it would be possible that the acceptance of His Messenger is acceptance from Him, so the verse clarifies that this is something that neither the Prophet of God nor the angel can attain. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And takes the alms. This is an explicit text that God the Almighty is the one who takes them and rewards them, and that the right belongs to Him, the Almighty, and the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, is an intermediary. If he dies, then his agent is the intermediary after him, and God the Almighty is alive and does not die. This shows that the Almighty’s saying: Take from their wealth alms is not limited to the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “God accepts the flour and takes it in His right hand and nurtures it for one of you as one of you nurtures a foal, until the morsel becomes like a mountain. Confirmation of that is in the Book of God: ‘He accepts repentance from His servants and takes the charities’ and ‘God destroys interest and gives increase for charities’ (al-Baqarah 2:276).” He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. In Sahih Muslim: “No one gives in charity a date from lawful earnings except that God takes it in His right hand - in one narration - and it grows in the hand of the Most Merciful until it becomes larger than a mountain.” The hadith. And it was narrated. “Charity falls into the hand of the Most Merciful before it falls into the hand of the beggar. He nurtures it as one of you nurtures his colt or young camel. And God multiplies for whomever He wills.” Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said in their interpretation of these hadiths: This is a metaphor for acceptance and reward for it, just as He, the noble and holy, referred to the sick person with His own compassion, saying: O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit me. This meaning was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. He mentioned the right hand and the palm specifically, because everything that is capable of something takes it with its palm and right hand, or it is placed in it, so it is excluded from what they know, and God Almighty is exalted above the limb. The right hand came in the speech of the Arabs without the meaning of the limb, as the poet said: If a banner is raised for glory, Araba will receive it with her right hand. That is, he is qualified for glory and honor, and it does not mean an oath of a wound, because glory is a meaning, so the oath with which you receive his banner is a meaning. And so is the oath with regard to God Almighty. It has been said that the meaning of grows in the palm of the Most Gracious is an expression for the pan of the scale in which deeds are weighed, so it is a case of deleting the complement, as if he said: So the pan of the scale of the Most Gracious grows. It was narrated from Malik, Ath-Thawri, and Ibn Al-Mubarak that they said in interpreting these hadiths and similar ones: They passed it on without how, as At-Tirmidhi and others said. And this is what the scholars of the Sunnah and the Community say.
9:105: The Almighty says: And say, ‘Work.’ This is addressed to everyone. Then God will see your work, and so will His Messenger and the believers. That is, by making them aware of your work. And in the hadith: If a man worked in a rock that had no door or window, his work would be revealed to the people, whoever they may be.
9:106: It was revealed about the three who were forgiven: Ka'b bin Malik, Hilal bin Umayya from Banu Waqif, Murarah bin Ar-Rabi', and it was said: Ibn Rib'i Al-'Umari, mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. They had stayed behind from Tabuk and were Maysar, as will be mentioned about them. The meaning is: And among them are others who are delayed, from arja'tuhu, meaning I delayed it. And from this it was said: Murji'ah, because they delayed the work. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read marjoon without a hamza, so it was said: It is from arjatuhu, meaning I delayed it. Al-Mubarrad said: It is not said arjatuhu in the sense of I delayed it, but it is from hope. Either He punishes them or He forgives them in Arabic either means one of two things, and God Almighty knows the fate of things, but the address is to the servants according to what they know, meaning let their matter with you be based on hope because there is nothing more for the servants than this.
9:107: It contains ten issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And those who have taken a mosque is conjoined, meaning, among them are those who have taken a mosque, conjoining a sentence to a sentence. It is possible for it to be nominative by the beginning and the predicate is omitted, as if they are being punished or something similar. And whoever reads those who without waw which is the reading of the Medinans, then in his opinion it is nominative by the beginning, and the predicate is Do not stand the estimate: those who have taken a mosque, do not stand in it ever, meaning do not stand in their mosque, said Al-Kisa’i. Al-Nahhas said: The predicate of the beginning is Their building which they have built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts. And it was said: The predicate is They are being punished as mentioned above. And the verse was revealed according to what was narrated about Abu Amir the monk, because he had gone out to Caesar and converted to Christianity and Caesar promised them that he would come to them, so they built the Mosque of Harm, waiting for his arrival in it, said Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others, and his story was mentioned in Al-A’raf and the commentators said: “The Banu Amr ibn Awf built the Quba Mosque and sent to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to come to them. He came to them and prayed in it. Their brothers, the Banu Ghanim ibn Awf, envied them and said: We will build a mosque and send to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to come to us and pray for us as he prayed in the mosque of our brothers, and Abu Amir will pray in it when he comes from Syria. They came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was preparing for Tabuk and said: O Messenger of God, we have built a mosque for those in need, illness and rainy nights, and we would like you to pray for us in it and ask for blessings. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am on a journey and busy, so if we come back we will come to you and pray for you in it. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from Tabuk, they came to him and they had finished with him and prayed on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. He called for his shirt to wear and come to them. Then the Qur’an was revealed to him with the report of the Mosque of Harm. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Malik ibn al-Dukhshum, Ma’n ibn ‘Adi, ‘Amir ibn al-Sakn and Wahshi, the killer of Hamza, and said: They set out to this mosque, whose people were unjust, and demolished and burned it. They left quickly, and Malik bin Al-Dakhshum brought out a torch of fire from his house, and they rose up and burned the mosque and demolished it. The ones who built it were twelve men: Khadham bin Khalid from Banu Ubaid bin Zaid, one of Banu Amr bin Auf, and from his house he brought out the Mosque of Harm, and Mu’tab bin Qushair, and Abu Habeeba bin Al-Az’ar, and Abbad bin Haneef, the brother of Sahl bin Haneef from Banu Amr bin Auf, and Jariyah bin Aamer, and his two sons Mujammi’ and Zaid, the sons of Jariyah, and Nabtal bin Al-Harith, and Bahzaj, and Bajad bin Othman, and Wadi’ah bin Thabit, and Tha’laba bin Hattab is mentioned among them. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: There is a problem with it, because he witnessed Badr. Ikrimah said: Omar bin Al-Khattab asked one of them, “What did you help with in this mosque?” He said: I helped with a pillar. He said: Be happy with it! A pillar around your neck from the fire of Hell. Second: The Almighty’s saying: harm is a verbal noun of action for which purpose. And disbelief and division among the believers and ambush is all in apposition. The people of interpretation said: Harm is to the mosque, but the mosque does not cause harm, rather it is to its people. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There should be neither harm nor reciprocating harm. Whoever causes harm, God will cause harm to him. Whoever causes hardship, God will cause hardship to him.” Some scholars said: Harm is that which benefits you but harms your neighbor. Harm is that which does not benefit you but harms your neighbor. It has been said that they have the same meaning, and both of them were mentioned for emphasis. Third: Our scholars said: It is not permissible to build a mosque next to another mosque, and it must be demolished and its construction must be prohibited lest the people of the first mosque leave and it remain empty, unless the neighborhood is large and one mosque is not sufficient for its people, in which case it should be built. They also said: Two or three mosques should not be built in one city, and the second must be prohibited, and whoever prays Jumu’ah in it is not valid. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) prohibited the Masjid al-Dhirar and demolished it. At-Tabari narrated on the authority of Shaqiq that he came to pray in the Masjid of Banu ‘Amir and found that he had missed the prayer, so it was said to him: He has not prayed in the Masjid of Banu So-and-so yet, so he said: I do not like to pray in it, because it was built for harm. Our scholars said: Every mosque that is built for harm or showing off and reputation is considered a Masjid al-Dhirar and it is not permissible to pray in it. Al-Naqqash said: This necessitates that one should not pray in a church or the like, because it was built for evil. I said: This is not necessary, because the church was not built with the intention of harming others, even though it was originally built for evil. Rather, the Christians took the church and the Jews the synagogue as a place where they worshipped, as they claimed, like a mosque for us, and so they parted ways. The scholars have agreed that whoever prays in a church or synagogue in a clean place, his prayer is valid and permissible. Al-Bukhari mentioned that Ibn Abbas used to pray in a synagogue if there were no statues in it. Abu Dawud mentioned on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi al-Aas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to make the mosque of Taif where their idols were. Fourth: The scholars said: If someone is an imam for an oppressor, no one should pray behind him unless he makes an excuse or repents. The Banu Amr ibn Awf who built the Quba Mosque asked Umar ibn al-Khattab during his caliphate to allow Mujammi ibn Jariyah to lead them in prayer in their mosque. He said: No, not even the blessing of the eye! Isn’t he the imam of the Mosque of Harm? Mujammi said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, do not rush me, for by God I prayed in it without knowing what they had hidden in mind. If I had known, I would not have prayed with them in it. I would have been a young boy who had read the Qur’an, and they were old men who had lived in their ignorance and did not read anything from the Qur’an. So I prayed, not considering what I had done a sin, nor did I know what was in their hearts. Umar may God be pleased with them both excused him, believed him, and ordered him to pray in the Quba Mosque. Fifth: Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: If the mosque is used for worship and the Sharia urges its construction, then it says: Whoever builds a mosque for God, even if it is the size of a sparrow’s nest, God will build for him a house in Paradise. It should be demolished and removed if it causes harm to others, so what do you think of anything else? Rather, it is more deserving of being removed and demolished so that no harm is caused to the oldest. This is like someone who builds an oven or a mill or digs a well or anything else that causes harm to others. The rule in this chapter is that whoever causes harm to his brother should be prevented. If he causes harm to his brother by doing something he should have done with his money and that harms his neighbor or someone other than his neighbor, then that action should be looked at. If leaving it causes greater harm than the harm caused to the doer, then the greater of the two harms should be cut off and the one that is more forbidden in the fundamentals should be forbidden. An example of this is: A man opened a window in his house from which he could look into his brother’s house, where his family and relatives were. It is the custom of women in their homes to throw off some of their clothes and go about their business. It is known that looking into private parts is forbidden, and a prohibition has been reported regarding this. Due to the sanctity of looking into private parts, the scholars saw that they should close the door or window that which is not beneficial or comfortable for the one who opened it, and closing it would cause harm to him, because they intended to cut off the greater of the two harms, since there was no alternative but to cut off one of them. This is the ruling in this matter, contrary to what Al-Shafi’i and those who said the same. The companions of Al-Shafi’i said: If a man dug a well in his property and another dug a well in his property to steal the water from the first well, it is permissible, because each of them dug in his property, so there is no reason to prevent that. An example of this according to them is: If a man dug a toilet next to his neighbor’s well that would spoil it for him, he would not have the right to prevent him, because he was disposing of his property. The Qur’an and Sunnah refute this statement. And God is the Grantor of success. From this chapter is another type of harm that scholars have forbidden, such as the smoke of the oven and the bathroom, and the dust of dung and the worms generated from the manure spread out in the open. And whatever is like this, then what is clearly harmful and feared to continue is cut off. As for what is for a short time, such as shaking clothes and mats at the door, then this is something that people cannot do without, and it is not something that deserves anything, so negating the harm in forbidding such a thing is greater and more important than being patient with it for a short time. And the neighbor has the right to be patient with his neighbor according to the evidence of the Sunnah, as much as he can, just as he should not harm him and be kind to him. Sixth: Among the things that fall under this category is an issue mentioned by Ismail bin Abi Uways on the authority of Malik, who was asked about a woman who was possessed by a jinn, and if her husband had intercourse with her and she became impure or came close to her, this would become more severe for her. Malik said: I do not think he should come close to her, and I think the ruler should stand between him and her. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: And disbelief. Since they believed that there was no sanctity for the Quba Mosque or the Prophet’s Mosque, may God bless him and grant him peace, they disbelieved in this belief, as stated by Ibn al-Arabi. It was also said: And disbelief, meaning in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he brought, as stated by al-Qushayri and others. Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: And to cause division among the believers meaning that they would divide their community so that some people would stay away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This shows you that the greater purpose and most apparent goal of establishing the community is to unite hearts and words in obedience and to establish covenants and sanctity through the act of religion so that familiarity occurs through mixing, and hearts are purified from grudges. Ninth - Malik, may God have mercy on him, realized this verse and said: Two congregations should not pray in one mosque with two imams, contrary to the rest of the scholars. It was narrated from Al-Shafi’i that he forbade it, as it would cause confusion and invalidate this wisdom and provide a pretext for us to say: Whoever wants to separate from the congregation has an excuse, so he should establish his congregation and lead his imamate, and this would cause disagreement and invalidate the system, and this was hidden from them. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This was his way with them, and he was more steadfast than them in wisdom and more knowledgeable about the sections of the Shari’ah. Tenth - The Almighty said: And an ambush for him who fights God and His Messenger meaning Abu Amir the monk, and he was called that because he used to worship and seek knowledge and died as an unbeliever in Qinnasrin by the call of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he had said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I will not find a people who will fight you except that I will fight you with them, so he continued to fight him until the day of Hunayn. When Hawazin was defeated, he went to the Romans to seek help, and he sent to the hypocrites and said: Prepare whatever force and weapons you can, and build a mosque, for I am going to Caesar and bring an army of Romans to expel Muhammad from Medina, so they built the Mosque of Harm. This Abu Amir is the father of Hanzala, who was washed by the angels. Observation means waiting, you say: I have prepared something if you have prepared it, waiting for it. Abu Zaid said: It is said I have monitored him and I have monitored him in good, and I have monitored him in evil. Ibn al-A'rabi said: It is not said except I have monitored, and its meaning is I have watched. And the Almighty’s saying: before meaning before the construction of the Mosque of Harm. And they will swear, ‘We intended nothing but good’ meaning, we intended nothing by building it but good deeds, which is kindness to the Muslims as they mentioned for those with a disease or need. This indicates that actions differ according to the intended meaning and intentions, and therefore He said: “And they will swear, ‘We intended nothing but good’. And God bears witness that they are liars” meaning, He knows the evil of their consciences and their lies in what they swear.
9:108: It contains eleven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Never stand therein means the Mosque of Harm, meaning do not stand there to pray. Prayer may also be expressed by standing, it is said: So-and-so stands at night, meaning he prays, and from this is the authentic hadith: Whoever stands in prayer during Ramadan out of faith and in the hope of reward, will be forgiven for his previous sins. Narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: …, and he mentioned it. It has been narrated that when this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not pass by the road in which the mosque was located, and he ordered that a sweeping place be set up in its place where carcasses, filth, and garbage would be thrown. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Forever. Forever is a time adverb. Time adverbs are of two types: an implied adverb such as today, and an indefinite adverb such as now and time. Forever is from this type, as is time. A fundamental issue arises here, which is that even if al-abd is a vague circumstance that does not contain generality, but if it is connected to the negative la it indicates generality. So if he said: Do not stand up, it would suffice for absolute withdrawal. So if he said: al-abd it is as if he said at some time or at any time. As for the indefinite noun in the affirmative, if it is report about a reality, it does not become general. The people of language understood this and the jurists of Islam ruled on it, saying: If a man says to his wife You are divorced forever, she is divorced once. Third: The Almighty’s saying: For a mosque founded on righteousness. That is, its walls were built and its foundations were raised. The foundation is the root of the building, as is the basis. Foundations is a shortened form of it. The plural of foundation is isasas, like ‘asa’ and ‘asas. The plural of foundation is asas, like qadhal and qadhal. The plural of foundations is asas, like sabab and asbab. And the building was founded by a foundation. And their saying: That was on the foundation of time, and the foundation of time, and the foundation of time, are three languages, meaning on the eve of time and the face of time. And the lam in His saying for a mosque is the lam of an oath. And it was said that it is the lam of beginning, as you say: for Zaid the best of people in action, and it requires emphasis. Found on piety is an attribute of a mosque. Ahq is the predicate of the beginning, which is for a mosque. And the meaning of piety here is the qualities by which punishment is protected, and it is the action of whomever is protected, and this has been mentioned before. Fourth: The scholars differed regarding the mosque that was founded on piety. A group said: It is the Quba Mosque, as narrated by Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and Al-Hasan. They relied on his saying: From the first day, and the Quba Mosque was founded in Medina or one day, as it was built before the Prophet’s Mosque, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was said by Ibn Omar, Ibn Al-Musayyab, and Malik, as narrated by Ibn Wahb, Ashab, and Ibn Al-Qasim. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri: “Two men disputed about the mosque that was founded on piety from the first day. One man said, ‘It is the mosque of Quba’, and another said, ‘It is the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘It is this mosque of mine.’” He said, It is a sound hadith. The first statement is more appropriate to the story, because he said, In it, and the adverbial pronoun indicates the purified men, so it is the mosque of Quba’. The evidence for that is the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said, “This verse was revealed about the people of Quba’: ‘In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves.’” He said, They used to clean themselves with water, so this verse was revealed about them. Al-Sha’bi said, They are the people of the mosque of Quba’, God revealed this about them. Qatadah said, “When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to the people of Quba’: “God, the Exalted, has praised you for purifying yourself, so what do you do? They said: We wash away traces of feces and urine with water.” Narrated by Abu Dawud. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Talhah ibn Nafi’ who said: Abu Ayyub, Jabir ibn Abdullah and Anas ibn Malik al-Ansariyyin told me on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this verse: In it are men who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves. He said: "O Ansar, God has praised you for your purification. What is this purification of yours?" They said: O Messenger of God, we perform ablution for prayer and we perform ghusl after sexual impurity. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is there anything else? They said: "Nothing else. When one of us comes out of the bathroom, he likes to clean himself with water." He said: That is it, so you should do it. This hadith implies that the mosque mentioned in the verse is the Quba Mosque, except that the hadith of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri states that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stated that it was his mosque, so there is no looking around with it. Abu Kuraib narrated: He told us, or Usama, he said: Salih bin Hayyan told us, he said: Abdullah bin Buraidah told us, regarding the words of God Almighty: In houses which God has permitted to be raised and that His name be mentioned therein (al-Nur 24:36), he said: They are only four mosques that were not built except by a prophet: The Kaaba, which was built by Abraham and Ishmael, peace be upon them; the House of Jericho, the Holy House, which was built by David and Solomon, peace be upon them; the Mosque of Medina and the Mosque of Quba, which were founded on piety, and were built by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Fifth: From the first day according to grammarians is the opposite of since, so since in time is like min in place. It was said that its meaning here is the meaning of since, and the estimate is: from the first day its construction began. It was said that the meaning is from the founding of the first days, so it entered into the source of the verb which is asasa, as he said: Whose home is Qannah al-Hajar? Stronger than Hajj and Era That is, from the passage of time and from the passage of time. The reason for this is that one of the principles of grammarians is that man does not attract times, but rather attracts times with mandhu. You say I have not seen you since a month or a year or a day, but you do not say from a month or a year or a day. So if it occurs in speech and is followed by a time, then an implied noun is assumed that is appropriate to attract man, as we mentioned in the estimation of the verse. Ibn Atiyah. I think it is better to dispense with the estimation in this verse, and for man to attract the word first because it means the beginning, as if he said: from the beginning of the days. Sixth: The Almighty’s statement: It is more deserving that you stand therein meaning that you stand, so it is in the accusative case. It is more deserving is more effective than truth, and truth is only used between two things in common, one of which has an advantage over the other in the meaning they share. So the Mosque of Harm, even if it is false and has no truth, they share the truth from the perspective of the belief of its builder, or from the perspective of the belief of the one who thought that standing therein was permissible for the mosque-goer, but one of the two beliefs is false inwardly before God, and the other is true inwardly and outwardly. An example of this is the statement of God the Almighty: The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in settlement and better in resting place (al-Furqan 25:24). It is known that goodness is removed from the Fire, but it is based on the belief of each group that they are on good and that their destination is better, since each party rejoices in what they have. This is not like saying: Honey is sweeter than vinegar, for honey! Even if it is sweet, then everything that is suitable is sweet. Do you not see that some people prefer vinegar to honey, whether it is alone or added to something else with an added meaning. Seventh - The Almighty’s saying: In it whoever said: The mosque refers to the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then the ha in more deserving that you stand in it refers back to him. And in it are men also refers to him. And whoever said: It is the mosque of Quba, then the pronoun in in it refers back to him according to the previous disagreement. Eighth - In this verse, God the Almighty praised those who love purity and prefer cleanliness, which is a human virtue and a religious duty. In Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: Tell your husbands to clean themselves with water, for I feel shy of them. He said: A sound hadith. It has been proven that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to carry water with him when cleaning himself, so he used stones for ease and water for purification. Ibn Al-Arabi: The scholars of Kairouan used to use stones in their ablution areas in the dirt to clean themselves with, then clean themselves with water. Ninth: The impurity of the anus must be mitigated, and the impurity of the rest of the body and clothing must be purified. This is a concession from God for His servants in the presence of water or not, and this is what most scholars have said. Ibn Habib was an exception and said: One should not clean oneself with stones except when there is no water. The established hadiths about cleaning oneself with stones when water is available refute this. Tenth - Scholars differed in this regard regarding removing impurity from bodies and clothes, after their consensus on overlooking and pardoning the blood of fleas as long as it is not excessive, according to three opinions: First - It is an obligatory duty, and the prayer of someone who prays in an impure garment is not valid, whether he knows that or is absent-minded. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Ibn Sirin, and it is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, and Abu Thawr. It was narrated by Ibn Wahb from Malik, and it is the opinion of Abu Al-Faraj Al-Maliki and Al-Tabari, except that Al-Tabari said: If the impurity is the size of a dirham, he must repeat the prayer. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf regarding observing the size of a dirham, by analogy with the anal ring. A group said: Removing impurity is obligatory by the Sunnah from clothes and bodies, it is a Sunnah obligation and not an obligation. They said: Whoever prays in an impure garment must repeat the prayer during the time, but if the time runs out, nothing is required of him. This is the opinion of Malik and his companions except Abu Al-Faraj, and the narration of Ibn Wahb from him. Malik said about a small amount of blood, the prayer is not repeated during the time or after it, but it is repeated for a small amount of urine or feces, and all of this is similar to the Maliki school of thought, the statement of Al-Layth. Ibn Al-Qasim said about it: It is obligatory to remove it in the case of remembrance but not forgetfulness, and it is one of his singular statements. The first statement is more correct, God willing, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by two graves and said: “They are being punished, but they are not being punished for a major sin. As for one of them, he used to go about spreading gossip, and as for the other, he did not protect himself from his urine.” The hadith was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, and that is enough for you. It will come in Surat Al-Subhan. They said: A person is not punished except for neglecting an obligation, and this is clear. Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The most severe punishment in the grave is from urine. Others argued that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took off his shoes during prayer when Gabriel (peace be upon him) informed him that they contained filth and harm... the hadeeth. It was narrated by Abu Dawood and others on the authority of Abu Sa’eed al-Khudri, and will be mentioned in Surah Taha, God willing. They said: Since he did not repeat what he prayed, this indicates that removing them is a Sunnah and his prayer is valid, and he should repeat it as long as he is within the time in order to achieve perfection. And God knows best. Eleventh - Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: As for the difference between the little and the much, according to the size of the Baghli dirham - meaning the large dirhams that are the size of the roundness of the dinar - by analogy to the masrabah, it is corrupt from two aspects, the first - that the estimated amounts are not proven by analogy, so this estimation is not accepted. The second - that what was made lighter in the masrabah is a concession due to necessity, and need and concessions are not used as an analogy, because they are outside the analogy and do not return to it.
9:109: It contains five issues: First: The Almighty said: Is he who founded meaning origin, and it is a question that means confirmation. And who means who, and it is in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is good. Nafi', Ibn Amir and a group read He founded his building in the passive form asas and raised building in both. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i and a group read He founded his building in the active form asas and lowered building in both, and it is the choice of Abu Ubaid due to the large number of those who read it, and that the subject was named in it. Nasr bin Asim bin Ali read Is he who founded his building in the nominative form asas and in the genitive form. And from him also the foundation of his building and from him it is Is he who founded his building Al-Nahhas said: This is the plural of as, as it is said: khaf and akhfaf, and the common isas like khafaf. The poet said: The king became fixed in the Bahalil of the Abbasids Second: The Almighty’s saying: On piety from God. The reading of Isa bin Omar - according to what Sibawayh narrated - is with the tanween, and the alif is an alif of addition like the alif of Tatra in what is nun, and the poet said: It is hung in a ball and in a ball Sibawayh denied the tanween and said: I do not know what its reason is. On the Edge means the letter and the limit, and it has already been fully explained in Al Imran. Jarf was read with the ra' raised, and Abu Bakr and Hamza with it being silent, like Shaghl and Shaghl, and Ar-Rusul and Ar-Rusul, meaning a jaraf that has no origin. Jarf is what is swept away by floods of medicines, and its sides are dug with water, and its origin is from Jaraf and Ijtraf, which is the uprooting of something from its origin. Haar is fallen, it is said: the building fell if it fell, and its origin is Ha'ir, so it is from the inverted and its ya is delayed, so it is said: Ha'ir and Ha'ir, said Al-Zajjaj. The same is the case with Laath of a thing with it if it revolves, so it is Laath meaning Laith. And as they said: Shaki Al-Salah and Shaki Al-Salah. Al-Ajjaj said: He is a Hebrew and a Hebrew Ashaa is the palm tree, and in Hebrew it is called Sidr which is on the banks of rivers, and the meaning of laath is to surround it. Abu Hatim claimed that the origin of it is hawar, then it is said ha’ir like sa’im, then it is reversed and it is said har. Al-Kisa’i claimed that it is from the ones with waw and the ones with ya’, and that it is said tahawar and tahir. I said: That is why it is inclined and opened. Third: The Almighty’s saying: So it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell. The subject of the cliff collapsed is as if he said: So the cliff collapsed with the building into the fire, because the cliff is masculine. It is possible that the pronoun in it refers to who which is the builder, and the meaning is so it collapsed from the one who founded his building on polytheism and hypocrisy. He explained that the building of the disbeliever is like a building on the cliff of Hell, rushing with his people into it. And shifa is the edge. And ashfa on something means he came close to it. Fourth: This verse is evidence that everything that begins with the intention of fearing God Almighty and intending His noble face is what remains and makes its doer happy and ascends to God and is raised to Him. He tells about it in His statement: And the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor, will remain (al-Rahman 55:27) in one of the two ways. He also tells about it in His statement: And the lasting good deeds (al-Kahf 18:46) as will be explained, God willing. Fifth: Scholars differed regarding the Almighty’s statement: Then it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell. Is this literal or metaphorical? There are two opinions: The first is that it is literal and that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent to them and demolished it, smoke was seen coming out of it, according to the narration of Saeed ibn Jubayr. Some of them said: A man would put a palm frond into it and take it out black and burnt. The commentators mentioned that he would dig the place that collapsed and smoke would come out. Asim ibn Abi al-Najud narrated on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that he said: Hell is on the earth, then he recited Then it collapsed with him into the fire of Hell. Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah said: I saw smoke coming out of it during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The second opinion is that it is metaphorical, and the meaning is: The building was in the fire of Hell, as if it collapsed into it and he fell into it. This is like the Almighty’s statement: Then his mother is an abyss (al-Qari’ah 101:9). The first is more apparent, as there is no absurdity in that. And God knows best.
9:110: The Almighty said: Their building which they built will not cease to exist meaning the Mosque of Harm. Doubt meaning doubt in their hearts and hypocrisy, as Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said. An-Nabigha said: I swore, I did not leave you any doubt, and there is no way for a person to go beyond God. Al-Kalbi said: Regret and remorse, because they regretted building it. Al-Suddi, Habib and Al-Mubarrad said: Doubt, meaning resentment and anger. Unless their hearts are cut off Ibn Abbas said: meaning their hearts are cracked and they die, like His statement: We would have cut off his aorta (al-Haqqah 69:46) because life ends with the cutting off of the aorta. Qatada, Ad-Dahhak and Mujahid said the same. Sufyan said: Unless they repent. Ikrimah: Unless their hearts are cut off in their graves. The companions of Abdullah bin Masoud used to recite it: Doubt in their hearts, even if their hearts were cut off. Al-Hasan, Yaqub, Abu Hatim and Abu Hatim recited until you cut off as a literal meaning they will remain in doubt about it until they die and become certain and clear. The reciters differed in his statement cut off. The majority of reciters said cut off with a damma on the ta’, a fatha on the qaf and a shaddah on the ta’ as a passive verb. Ibn Amir, Hamza, Hafs and Yaqub recited it likewise, except that they opened the ta’. It was narrated on the authority of Yaqub and Abu Abd al-Rahman that it is cut off with a passive verb with a light qaf. It was narrated on the authority of Shibl and Ibn Kathir that it is cut off with a light qaf with their hearts in the accusative case, meaning you do that to them. We have already mentioned the reading of the companions of Abdullah, And God is All-Knowing, All-Wise, above.
9:111: It contains eight issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives. It was said: This is a metaphor, like the Almighty’s saying: Those are the ones who have purchased error in exchange for guidance. (al-Baqarah 2:16). The verse was revealed regarding the second pledge, which was the pledge of Al-‘Aqabah Al-Kubra, in which the men of the Ansar exceeded seventy, and the youngest of them was ‘Aqbah ibn ‘Amr. This was because they gathered to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, at Al-‘Aqabah, and ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Set whatever conditions you wish for your Lord and for yourself. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect yourselves and your wealth from. They said: If we do that, what will we have? He said: Paradise. They said: A profitable transaction. We do not take a break or resign.” Then the verse was revealed: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for that they will have Paradise Al-Baqarah 2:17. Then it is general for every mujahid in the way of God from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the Day of Resurrection. Second: This verse is evidence of the permissibility of the master’s dealings with his slave, even if everything belongs to the master. However, if he owns it, he treats him according to what he has assigned to him. What is permissible between the master and his slave is not permissible between him and anyone else, because his money belongs to him and he may take it. Third: The origin of buying and selling among people is that they should compensate for what they have lost with something that is more beneficial to them or similar in benefit to what they have lost. So God, the Exalted, bought from His servants the destruction of their souls and wealth in His obedience, and their squandering in His pleasure, and He, the Exalted, gave them Paradise in exchange for it if they did that. It is a great compensation that cannot be compared to or measured by the compensation. So He made that a metaphor for what they know in buying and selling. From the servant is the surrender of his soul and wealth, and from God is the reward and bounty. So this is called buying. Al-Hasan narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is a greater righteousness than every good deed, until a servant sheds his blood. If he does that, there is no greater righteousness than that.” The poet said about the meaning of righteousness: Generosity with water is a noble act, and generosity with one’s soul is the ultimate act of generosity. Al-Asma’i recited for Ja’far al-Sadiq, may God be pleased with him: I value my precious soul with my Lord, and there is no price for it among all creation. With it you can buy gardens. If I sell it for anything other than that, that would be a great loss. If my soul is lost in this world, I will get it. My soul is lost and the price is lost. Al-Hassan said: “An Arab passed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reciting this verse: ‘Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives.’ He said: ‘Whose words are these?’ He said: ‘The words of God.’ He said: ‘A sale, by God, that is profitable. We will not change it or ask for its cancellation.’ So he went out to fight and was martyred.” Fourth: The scholars said: Just as He bought from the adult believers who are accountable, He also bought from the children and caused them pain and sickness, because of the benefit and consideration for the adults in that, for they are not more righteous and less corrupt than when children are in pain, and because of the reward that the foster parents receive for the worries that they suffer and the upbringing and fostering that they receive. Then He, the Almighty, compensates these children with compensation when they come to Him. An example of this in the evidence is that you hire a worker to build and move dirt, and in all of that there is pain and harm for him, but that is permissible because of the benefit in his work and the reward that he receives. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: They fight in the way of God is an explanation of what they fight for and against, and it has been mentioned previously. They kill and are killed An-Nakha’i, Al-A’mash, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Khalaf read it by placing the object before the subject, and from this is the saying of Imru’ Al-Qais: If you kill us, we will kill you... That is, if you kill some of them, some of us will kill you. The rest read it by placing the subject before the object. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: A true promise binding upon Him in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur’an. This is information from God Almighty that this was in these books, and that jihad and resistance to enemies originated from the time of Moses, peace be upon him. Promise and truth are two confirmed sources. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And who is more faithful to his covenant than God? meaning, no one is more faithful to his covenant than God. It includes fulfilling the promise and the threat. It does not include the Creator’s fulfillment of all, as His promise is for everyone, and as for His threat, it is specific to some sinners, some transgressions, and in some circumstances. This meaning has been fully explained above. Eighth - The Almighty said: So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. That is, show joy over it. And the good report is showing joy in the glad tidings. It was mentioned before. And Al-Hasan said: By God, there is no believer on earth who does not enter into this transaction.
