And that is the great attainment. That is, the attainment of Paradise and eternity in it.
9:112: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Those who repent and worship. The repentant are those who return from the blameworthy state of disobeying God to the praiseworthy state of obeying God. The repentant is the one who returns. The one who returns to obedience is better than the one who returns from disobedience because it combines the two matters. The worshippers are those who are obedient and who intend God, the Most High, with their obedience. The praisers are those who are satisfied with His decree and spend His blessings in His obedience, who praise God in every situation. The travelers are those who fast, according to Ibn Masoud, Ibn Abbas and others. From this is the saying of God, the Most High: Worshippers, travelers (al-Tahrim 66:5). Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: The one who fasts is called a traveler because he abandons all pleasures of food, drink and sex. Abu Talib said: And the tourists do not taste a drop of their Lord and the memories are factors Another said: He prays day and night, constantly remembering God and traveling. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: The tourism of this nation is fasting. It was narrated by Al-Tabari. Abu Hurairah narrated it on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The tourism of my nation is fasting. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Hasan’s doctrine is that they are those who fast the obligatory fast. It has also been said that they are those who fast continuously. Ata’ said: The travelers are the mujahidin. Abu Umamah narrated that a man asked permission from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to travel, so he said: The tourism of my nation is jihad in the way of God. Abu Muhammad Abdul Haqq authenticated it. It was also said: The immigrant travelers, said Abdul Rahman bin Zaid. It was also said: They are those who travel in search of hadith and knowledge, said Ikrimah. It was also said: They are those who travel with their thoughts on the oneness of their Lord and His kingdom, and what He created of lessons and signs indicating His oneness and glorification, narrated by Al-Naqqash. It was narrated that some of the worshippers took a cup to perform ablution for the night prayer, so he put his finger in the cup’s ear and sat thinking until dawn came. He was asked about that, so he said: I put my finger in the cup’s ear and remembered the saying of God the Most High: When the shackles are on their necks and the chains (Ghafir 40:71), and I remembered how I would receive the shackles, and I spent my whole night in that. I said: The word s-y-h indicates the correctness of these statements, because the origin of tourism is to go on the surface of the earth as water flows. The fasting person continues in obedience in leaving what he leaves of food and other things, so he is like a traveler. And the hearts of the thinkers wander in what they mentioned. And in the hadith: God has angels who wander and walk in the horizons, conveying to me the prayers of my nation. It is also narrated as Sayyahin with a sad, from shouting. Those who bow and prostrate means in the obligatory prayers and others. Those who enjoin what is right means the Sunnah. It was also said: faith. And those who forbid what is wrong it was said: innovation. It was also said: disbelief. It was also said: it is general in all that is right and wrong. And those who preserve the limits of God meaning those who carry out what He has commanded and refrain from what He has forbidden. Second - The people of interpretation differed regarding this verse, is it connected to what came before it or separate? A group said: The first verse is independent in itself, and every monotheist who fights in the way of God so that the word of God is supreme falls under that pledge, even if he does not have these qualities in this second verse or most of them. A group said: These descriptions came as a condition, and the two verses are connected, so only the believers who have these descriptions and sacrifice themselves in the way of God fall under the pledge, said Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Atiyyah said: This statement is embarrassing and restrictive, and the meaning of the verse, according to what the statements of the scholars and the Shariah require, is that it is the descriptions of the perfect believers, God mentioned it so that the people of monotheism would race to it so that they would be in the highest rank. Az-Zajjaj said: What I have is that His statement: The repentant, the worshippers is raised by the beginning and its predicate is implied, meaning the repentant, the worshippers - until the end of the verse - also have Paradise even if they do not fight, if there is no stubbornness from them and no intention to abandon the fight, because some Muslims suffice for others in the fight. Al-Qushayri chose this statement and said: This is good, if it was a description of the believers mentioned in His statement: He purchased from the believers, then the promise would be specific to the mujahideen. And in the Mushaf of Abdullah: the repentant, the worshippers, and so on. And for this there are two aspects: One of them is the description of the believers as a following. And the second is the accusative as a praise. Third: The scholars differed regarding the waw in His statement: and those who forbid evil. It was said: It was included in the description of those who forbid, just as it was included in His statement: “Ha Meem. The revelation of the Book is from God, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing. Forgiver of sin and Accepter of repentance.” (Ghafir 40:3) So some of them were mentioned with the waw and some without it. This is permissible and common in speech, and no wisdom or reason is sought for it. It was said: It was included to accompany the one who forbids evil and the one who enjoins good, so one of them is hardly mentioned alone. Likewise, His statement: married women and virgins (al-Tahrim 66:5). It was included in His statement: and the guardians because of its proximity to the conjoined. It was said that it is redundant, but this is weak and meaningless. It was said: It is the waw of eight because seven, according to the Arabs, is a complete, whole number. They said the same about His statement: married women and virgins. And His saying in the gates of Paradise: And its gates are opened (al-Zumar 39:73) and His saying: And they say, ‘Seven,’ and the eighth of them is their dog (al-Kahf 18:22). Ibn Khalawayh mentioned it in his debate with Abu Ali Al-Farsi regarding the meaning of His saying: And its gates are opened, and Abu Ali denied it. Ibn Atiyyah said, and my father, may God be pleased with him, told me on the authority of the grammarian Abu Abdullah Al-Kafi Al-Maliki, who was one of those who settled in Granada and taught there during the time of Ibn Habus, that he said: It is the eloquent language of some Arabs, it is their custom to say when counting: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nineteen, and this is their language. And whenever the word eight comes in their speech, they insert the letter waw. I said: It is the language of the Quraysh. Its explanation and refutation will come in Surat Al-Kahf, God willing, and in Az-Zumar also, God willing.
9:113: It has three issues: First: Muslim narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab on the authority of his father who said: “When Abu Talib was about to die, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and found Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah bin Al-Mughira with him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘O uncle, say: There is no god but God, a word that I will bear witness for you before God.’ Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Umayyah said: ‘O Abu Talib, do you reject the religion of Abdul Muttalib?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept repeating that statement to him until Abu Talib said the last thing he said to them: ‘I am on the religion of Abdul Muttalib,’ and he refused to say: There is no god but God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘By God, I will seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so.’ Then God, the Almighty, revealed: ‘It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire.’” And God revealed about Abu Talib, saying to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills. And He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.” (al-Qasas 28:56) According to this, the verse abrogates the Prophet’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) seeking forgiveness for his uncle, as he sought forgiveness for him after his death, according to what was narrated in other than Sahih books. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: This is far-fetched, because the surah was among the last to be revealed of the Qur’an, and Abu Talib died in the prime of Islam while the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was in Mecca. Second: This verse includes severing allegiance to the infidels, living and dead, for God did not allow the believers to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, so seeking forgiveness for the polytheists is not permissible. If it is said: “It is authentic that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Uhud when they broke his front tooth and split his face: O God, forgive my people for they do not know.” So how can this be reconciled with God Almighty’s prohibition of His Messenger and the believers from seeking forgiveness for the polytheists? It is said to him: That statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was only by way of narration from the prophets who came before him, and the evidence for that is what Muslim narrated on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “It is as if I see the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrating a story about a prophet who was beaten by his people, and he was wiping the blood from his face and saying: ‘O God, forgive my people, for they do not know.’” In Bukhari, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned a prophet before him who was beaten by his people, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to narrate about him, saying: O God, forgive my people, for they do not know. I said: This is explicit in the narration of the one before him, not that he said it about himself as some of them thought. And God knows best. And the prophet that Noah narrated, peace be upon him, as will be explained in Surah Hud, God willing. It was said: What is meant by seeking forgiveness in the verse is prayer. Some of them said: I would not abandon praying for any of the people of the Qiblah, even if she were an Ethiopian woman who was pregnant from fornication, because I have not heard God prohibit prayer except for the polytheists in His saying: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists (al-Anfal 2:10). Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said: The verse prohibits praying for the polytheists, and seeking forgiveness here means prayer. A third answer: It is permissible to seek forgiveness for the living, because it is hoped that they will believe, and it is possible to win them over with kind words and encourage them to the religion. Many scholars have said: There is nothing wrong with a man supplicating for his disbelieving parents and seeking forgiveness for them as long as they are alive. As for the one who has died, hope has been cut off from him, so he should not supplicate for him. Ibn Abbas said: They used to seek forgiveness for their dead, so it was revealed. They refrained from seeking forgiveness, but it did not forbid them from seeking forgiveness for the living until they died. Third: The scholars of meanings said: What was in the Qur’an comes in two ways: in negation, such as His statement: “It was not for you to cause its trees to grow. Is there a god?” (al-Naml 27:60), And it is not for a soul to die except by permission of God (AAl Imran 3:145). And the other in the sense of prohibition, such as His statement: And it was not for you to harm the Messenger of God (al-Ahzab 33:53), and It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists.
19:47: It has three issues: First: Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard a man asking forgiveness for his parents, even though they were polytheists. I said: Do you ask forgiveness for them while they were polytheists? He said: Did not Abraham, peace be upon him, ask forgiveness for his father? So I went to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and mentioned that to him, and this verse was revealed: And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. The meaning is: You, O believers, have no argument in Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father, for that was only because of a promise. Ibn Abbas said: Abraham’s father had promised Abraham that he would believe in God and renounce rivals to Him. When he died as a disbeliever, he knew that he was an enemy of God, so he stopped praying for him. The metaphor in His statement: It shall return to Abraham, is that the one who made the promise was his father. It was also said that the one who made the promise was Abraham, meaning that Abraham promised his father that he would ask forgiveness for him, but when he died as a polytheist, he disowned him. This promise is indicated by His statement: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord Maryam 19:47. Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, relied on God Almighty’s saying in seeking forgiveness for Abu Talib: I will seek forgiveness for you from my Lord. God Almighty informed us that Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father was a promise before his disbelief became clear to him. When his disbelief became clear to him, he disavowed him. So how can you seek forgiveness for your uncle, O Muhammad, when you witnessed his death as a disbeliever? Second: A person’s apparent state at death is judged by it. If he dies as a believer, he is judged by it. If he dies as a disbeliever, he is judged by it. And your Lord knows best his inner state. However, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Al-Abbas: O Messenger of God, have I benefited your uncle in any way? He said: Yes. This is intercession to alleviate the punishment, not to escape from the Fire, as we explained in the Book of Remembrance. Third: The Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing. Scholars differed regarding Al-Awah in fifteen opinions: The first: It is the supplicant who supplicates frequently, said by Ibn Masoud and Ubaid bin Umair. The second: It is the Merciful to the servants of God, said by Al-Hasan and Qatadah, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud. The first has a more authentic chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Masoud, said by Al-Nahhas. The third: It is the one who is certain, said by Ata and Ikrimah, and narrated by Abu Dhibyan on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The fourth: It is the believer in the language of Abyssinia, said by Ibn Abbas as well. The fifth: It is the one who glorifies God and remembers God in a barren and desolate land, said by Al-Kalbi and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab. The sixth: It is the one who remembers God the Almighty a lot, said by Uqbah bin Amir, “A man who glorifies and glorifies God a lot was mentioned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said: He is the most devout. Seventh: He is the one who recites the Qur’an frequently. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. I said: These statements are intertwined and the recitation of the Qur’an brings them together. The eighth - that he is the one who groans, Abu Dharr said that Abraham, peace be upon him, used to say: “Ah from the fire before it is of no benefit, ah.” Abu Dharr said: “There was a man who used to frequently circumambulate the House and say in his supplication: “Oh, oh.” Abu Dharr complained about him to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Leave him, for he is a groaner. So I went out one night and saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, burying that man at night with a lamp. The ninth - that he is the jurist, Mujahid and Al-Nakha’i said. The tenth - that he is the one who supplicates and is humble, narrated by Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Haad from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Anas said: “A woman said something in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he disliked, so Umar forbade her, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave it, for it is a waah. It was said: O Messenger of God, what is the waah? He said: The humble one. The eleventh - That he is the one who seeks forgiveness for his sins when he remembers them, said Abu Ayoub. The twelfth - That he is the one who groans a lot because of his sins, said Al-Farraa. The thirteenth - That he is the teacher of good, said Saeed bin Jubair. The fourteenth - That he is the compassionate, said Abdul Aziz bin Yahya. Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, was called the waah because of his compassion and mercy. The fifteenth - That he is the one who turns away from everything that God hates, said Ataa. Its origin is from the groaning, which is that the chest hears the sound of a sigh. Kaab said: When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, mentioned the fire, he groaned. Al-Jawhari said: Their saying when complaining, “Oh from such-and-such” with a silent waw is only pain. The poet said: Oh, how I remember her when I remember her, and after that there is land and sky between us They may change the waw to an alif and say: Ah min kada. They may also stress the waw and break it and sukun the ha’ and say: Oh min kada. They may also delete the ha’ with the stress and say: Aw min kada, without elongation. Some of them say: Awah, with elongation and stress and opening the waw and sukun the ha’ to lengthen the sound with the complaint. They may also insert the ta’ and say: Awtah, which is elongated and not elongated. A man may ewe tawwayhan and sigh tawhan if he says oh, and the noun from it is the sigh with elongation. Al-Muthaqab al-Abdi said: If I leave her at night, she groans like a sad man Al-Haleem: the one who is very forbearing, who forgives sins and is patient with harm. It was said: the one who never punished anyone except for the sake of God and never took revenge for anyone except for God. Abraham, peace be upon him, was like that, and when he stood up to pray, his heartbeat could be heard two miles away. God the Almighty said: "He said, 'Peace be upon you.'" Abraham, peace be upon him, did not respond badly to him, because he was not commanded to fight him for his disbelief. The majority of scholars agree that what is meant by his peace is the peacefulness that is leaving, not the greeting. At-Tabari said: It means security from me to you. Based on this, the disbeliever should not initiate the peace. Al-Naqqash said: A forbearing person addresses a fool, as He said: "And when the ignorant address them, they say, 'Peace.'" (al-Furqan 25:63). Some of them said about the meaning of his peace: It is a greeting of separation, and it is permissible to greet the disbeliever and to initiate it. It was said to Ibn Uyaynah: Is it permissible to greet the disbeliever? He said: Yes, God the Almighty said: "God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, God loves those who act justly." (al-Mumtahanah 60:8). He said: There has certainly been for you a good example in Abraham (al-Mumtahanah 60:4), and Abraham said to his father: “Peace be upon you.” I said: What is most apparent from the verse is what Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said, and there are two authentic hadiths on this topic: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not initiate greetings to Jews and Christians. If you meet one of them on the road, force him to the narrowest part of it.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, rode a donkey with a saddle and a Fadak quilt underneath it, and Usama bin Zaid was riding behind him, while he was visiting Sa`d bin `Ubadah in Banu al-Harith bin al-Khazraj, and that was before the Battle of Badr, until he passed by a gathering in which there was a mixture of Muslims, idolaters, and Jews, and among them was `Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul, and in the gathering was `Abdullah bin Rawahah. When the gathering was covered by the dust of the beast, `Abdullah bin Ubayy covered his nose with his cloak, then he said: Do not dust us, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, greeted them,” the hadith. The first indicates that one should not greet them in the first place, because that is an honor, and the infidel is not worthy of that. The second hadith permits that. At-Tabari said: What Usama narrated does not contradict the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, because there is no disagreement between them in one of them, and that is because the hadith of Abu Hurayrah is general, and the report of Usama shows that its meaning is specific. Al-Nakha'i said: If you have a need with a Jew or a Christian, then greet him first. This shows that the hadith of Abu Hurairah, Do not greet them first is valid if there is no reason that calls for you to greet them first, such as fulfilling a covenant or a need that you have before them, or the right of companionship, neighborliness, or travel. Al-Tabari said: It has been narrated from the Salaf that they used to greet the People of the Book. Ibn Mas'ud did this with a peasant who accompanied him on his way. Alqamah said: I said to him, O Abu Abd al-Rahman, is it not disliked for them to greet first?! He said: Yes, but it is the right of companionship. When Abu Usamah returned to his house, he would not pass by a Muslim or a Christian, young or old, without greeting him. He was asked about that, and he said: We were commanded to spread the greeting of peace. Al-Awza'i was asked about a Muslim who passed by a disbeliever and greeted him, so he said: If you greet him, the righteous before you have greeted, and if you leave him, the righteous before you have left him. It was narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: If you pass by a gathering in which there are Muslims and disbelievers, greet them. I said: The people of the first article argued that peace, which means greeting, was only given to this nation, based on the hadith of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty has given my nation three things that He has not given to anyone before them: peace, which is the greeting of the people of Paradise.” The hadith was mentioned by Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim, and it has already been mentioned in Al-Fatihah with his chain of transmission. The discussion of the meaning of his saying: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord has already been mentioned. Peace is raised by beginning, and that is permissible with its indefinite noun because it is an indefinite noun that is specific, so it is linked to the definite noun. God Almighty says: Indeed, he was ever gracious to me. Al-Hafi is extremely kind and gentle. It is said: He was kind to me or He was gracious to me. Al-Kisa’i said: “It is said: “He was kind to me” or He was gracious to me. Al-Farra’ said: Indeed, he was ever gracious to me means knowledgeable and gentle, who would answer me when I called upon him.
9:115: God Almighty says: And God would not lead a people astray after He has guided them. That is, God would not cause misguidance to fall into their hearts after guidance until He made clear to them what they should avoid and they did not avoid it, and then they would deserve to be led astray. I said: In this is the clearest evidence that if sins are committed and their veil is violated, they are a cause of misguidance and ruin, and a ladder to abandoning guidance and righteousness. We ask God for success, guidance and righteousness by His grace. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ may God have mercy on him said about His statement: until He makes clear to them: meaning until He uses His command to argue with them, as He said: And when We desire to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones, but they defiantly disobey therein (al-Isra’ 17:16). Mujahid said: until He makes clear to them, meaning the command of Abraham, that they should not ask forgiveness for the polytheists in particular, and that He makes clear to them obedience and disobedience in general. It was narrated that when the prohibition of alcohol was revealed and was made strict, they asked the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about someone who died while drinking it, so God revealed: And God would never lead a people astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they should avoid (al-Isra’ 17:16). This verse is a refutation of the Mu’tazilah and others who say that their guidance and faith are created, as mentioned above. God Almighty says: Indeed, God is Knowing of all things.
9:116: "Indeed, to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death. And you have not besides God any protector or helper." Its meaning has been mentioned more than once.
9:117: Al-Tirmidhi narrated: Abd bin Hamid told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Kaab bin Malik, on the authority of his father, who said: “I did not stay behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in any battle he fought until the Battle of Tabuk, except Badr. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not rebuke anyone who stayed behind from Badr. Rather, he went out to help the caravan, and the Quraysh went out to help their caravan, and they met without an appointment, as God Almighty said. By my life, the most honorable of the Prophet’s battles among the people was Badr, and I would not have liked to have witnessed it instead of my pledge of allegiance on the night of Al-Aqabah when we pledged to Islam. Then I did not stay behind after that from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until the Battle of Tabuk, which was the last battle he fought, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave permission to depart. He mentioned the hadith in full. He said: So I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was sitting in the mosque with the Muslims around him, and he was shining like the moon. When he was pleased with something, he would shine. So I came and sat in front of him, and he said: Be glad, O Ka’b ibn Malik, for the best day that has come upon you since your mother gave birth to you. I said: O Prophet of God, is it from God or from you? He said: Rather, it is from God.” Then he recited this verse: God has forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship. Until he reached: God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful. He said: “And it was also revealed about us: ‘Fear God and be with the truthful.’” And he mentioned the hadith. It will come in its entirety from Sahih Muslim in the story of the three, God willing. Scholars differed regarding this repentance that God bestowed upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the Muhajireen and the Ansar. Ibn Abbas said: The repentance was upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) because he gave permission to the hypocrites to stay behind, as evidenced by his statement: God has pardoned you for giving them permission (al-Tawbah 9:43), and upon the believers because some of their hearts tended to stay behind him. It was said: God’s repentance upon them was to rescue them from severe hardship. It was said: To deliver them from the enemy’s affliction. He referred to this as repentance, even though it was outside its usual meaning, due to the presence of the meaning of repentance in it, which is returning to the previous state. The scholars of meaning said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was mentioned in the repentance because he was the reason for their repentance, so he was mentioned with them, like his statement: Then a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger (al-Anfal 8:41). God the Almighty said: Those who followed him in the hour of hardship meaning in the time of hardship, and what is meant is all the times of that battle and not a specific hour. It was said: The hour of hardship was the most difficult hour that they went through in that battle. Hardship is the difficulty of the matter. Jabir said: The hardship of the afternoon, the hardship of provisions, and the hardship of water all came together for them. Al-Hasan said: The hardship of the Muslims would go out on a camel, taking it in turns among them, and their provisions were rotten dates, spoiled barley, and stinking oil. The group would take out what they had with them - except the dates - among themselves, and if one of them became hungry, he would take a date and chew it until he could taste it, then he would give it to his companion so that he could drink a sip of water with it, and so on until the last of them had passed, and nothing remained of the date except the seed, so they went with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with their truthfulness and certainty, may God be pleased with them. Omar, may God be pleased with him, said when he was asked about the hour of hardship: “We went out in intense heat and stopped at a place where we were afflicted with intense thirst, to the point that we thought our necks would break from thirst, and a man would slaughter his camel, squeeze out its dung and drink it, and put what was left on his liver. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, God has accustomed you to goodness in supplication, so supplicate for us. He said: Do you like that? He said: Yes. So he raised his hands and did not bring them back until the sky shaded the place, then it poured and they filled what they had with them. Then we went to look, but we did not find it had passed the camp.” Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa`id narrated that: “We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the Battle of Tabuk. The people were afflicted with famine and said: O Messenger of God, if you give us permission, we can slaughter our camels and eat and use oil. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do so. Then Umar came and said: O Messenger of God, if they do so, the noon prayer will be short, but invite them with their surplus provisions and pray to God to bless them, perhaps God will make that a blessing. He said: Yes. Then he called for a mat and spread it out, then he called for the surplus provisions. One man would bring a handful of corn, another would bring a handful of dates, and another would bring a piece of bread, until a small amount of it had gathered on the mat. Abu Hurairah said: I estimated it and it was the size of a goat’s rump. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed for blessing. Then he said: Take it in your vessels. So they took it in their vessels until - by Him besides Whom there is no god - there was not a vessel left in the camp except that they filled it. The people ate until they were full, and there was some left over. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I bear witness that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God.” God will not let a servant meet God with them without doubting them, and he will be prevented from entering Paradise.” Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih with its wording and meaning, and praise be to God. Ibn Arafah said: The Tabuk Army was called the Army of Difficulty because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, urged the people to go on a military expedition in the heat of anger, and he was harsh and difficult with them, and it was during the purchase of fruit. He said: The example of the Army of Difficulty was given because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had never gone on a military expedition before with a similar number, because his companions on the Day of Badr were three hundred and a few, and on the Day of Uhud seven hundred, and on the Day of Khaybar one thousand and five hundred, and on the Day of the Conquest ten thousand, and on the Day of Hunayn twelve thousand, and his army in the Battle of Tabuk was thirty thousand and more, and it was the last of his military expeditions, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out in Rajab and stayed in Tabuk during Sha’ban and some days of Ramadan, and he sent out his raiding parties and made peace with some people on the basis of the jizyah. During this raid, he left Ali in charge of Medina, so the hypocrites said: He left him behind out of hatred for him. So he went out behind the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and informed him, so he, peace be upon him, said: Are you not satisfied to be to me as Aaron was to Moses?” He explained that his sitting by his command, peace be upon him, is equivalent in reward to his going out with him, because the matter depends on the command of the Lawgiver. “It was called the Battle of Tabuk because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, saw some of his companions crying the “hasi” of Tabuk, meaning they put a cup in it and moved it to bring out water, so he said: You have not ceased crying over it So that battle was called Tabuk. The hasi with a kasra is what the earth dries up from the sand, and when it becomes hard, it holds it, so the sand is dug up from it and extracted, which is drinking, as al-Jawhari said. God the Almighty said: After the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated hearts are raised by tzigh according to Sibawayh. In the hadith, kat is implied, similar to kana, because the predicate is binding on it just as kana is binding. If you wish, you can raise it by kada, and the meaning would be: after the hearts of a party of them had almost deviated. Al-A'mash, Hamza and Hafs read yazigh with a ya', and Abu Hatim claimed that whoever reads yazigh with a ya' is not permitted to raise hearts by kada. An-Nahhas said: What he did not permit is permitted by others, based on the masculine gender of all. Al-Farra' narrated: Rahbah al-bilad and arhabat, and rahbah is the language of the people of Hijaz. There is disagreement over the meaning of tzigh. It was said: it is destroyed by effort, hardship and severity. Ibn Abbas said: it deviates - i.e. it turns away - from the truth in resistance and support. It was said: after a party of them intended to stay behind and disobey, then they caught up with it. It was said: they intended to return, but God accepted their repentance and commanded them to do so. The Almighty said: Then He turned to them in forgiveness. It was said: His turning to them in forgiveness was that He reconciled their hearts so that they did not deviate. And this is the way of the Truth with His friends: when they are on the verge of destruction and prepare themselves for ruin, He rains down upon them clouds of generosity and revives their hearts. And he recites: I hope from you, but I do not know of a Lord from whom I can hope for some of what I hope from you. And when hardships become severe on earth for people, they cry out for help and cry out. And the servants were afflicted with fear and hunger, and they persisted in sins and sought refuge. I had no refuge but you, my Lord, so I was certain that I would be saved through you He said about the three: Then He turned to them in repentance so that they might repent. It was said: The meaning of Then He turned to them in repentance is that He guided them to repentance so that they might repent. It was also said: The meaning is He turned to them in repentance, meaning He made things easy for them and did not punish them so that they might repent. It was also said: He turned to them in repentance so that they might remain steadfast in repentance. It was also said: The meaning is He turned to them in repentance so that they might return to a state of contentment with them. In short, if it were not for what preceded in their knowledge that He had decreed for them repentance, they would not have repented. The evidence for this is his saying, peace be upon him: Work, for everyone is facilitated for what he was created for.
9:118: The Almighty said: And concerning the three who stayed behind It was said: About repentance, on the authority of Mujahid and Abu Malik. Qatada said: About the Battle of Tabuk. It was reported on the authority of Muhammad bin Zaid that the meaning of they stayed behind is they left behind, because the meaning of I left behind so-and-so is I left him and departed from him sitting on what I had set out to do. Ikrimah bin Khalid read they stayed behind meaning they stayed behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was reported on the authority of Ja'far bin Muhammad that he read they differed and it was said: they were left behind meaning they were postponed and delayed from the hypocrites, so nothing was decided regarding them. This is because the repentance of the hypocrites was not accepted, and some people apologized, so their excuse was accepted, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, delayed these three until the Qur'an was revealed regarding them. This is the correct view, as narrated by Muslim, Al-Bukhari and others. The wording is from Muslim. Ka`b said: We, the three, were left behind regarding the matter of those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted from them when they swore an oath to him, so he pledged allegiance to them and asked forgiveness for them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, postponed our matter until God decided on it. Therefore, God, the Almighty, said: And concerning the three who stayed behind. What God mentioned regarding what we stayed behind was not our staying behind from the battle, but rather it was His leaving us behind and postponing our matter regarding those who swore an oath and apologized to him, so he accepted it from them. This hadith is long, and this is the end of it. The three who stayed behind were: Ka’b ibn Malik, Murarah ibn Rabi’ah al-Amiri, and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqfi, and all of them were from the Ansar. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated their hadith. Muslim said on the authority of Ka’b ibn Malik that he said: “I did not stay behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in any campaign he led except the campaign of Tabuk. However, I did stay behind in the campaign of Badr, and he did not rebuke anyone who stayed behind. Rather, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims went out seeking the caravan of Quraysh, until God gathered them and their enemy without an appointment. I witnessed with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the night of Al-Aqabah when we pledged to Islam, and I would not like to have the sight of Badr in it, even though Badr is more famous among the people than it. My story when I stayed behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the campaign of Tabuk was that I was never stronger or faster than when I stayed behind him in that campaign. By God, I had never gathered two camels before that until I gathered them in that campaign. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out in intense heat, and faced a long journey and a wilderness, and faced a large enemy. He made clear to the Muslims their situation so that they could prepare for their campaign, and he informed them of his destination, and the Muslims were with the Messenger of God. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was many, and they were not gathered in a book of Hafiz - meaning the diwan - Kaab said: Say a man wants to be absent, thinking that this will be hidden from him unless a revelation from God the Most High has been sent down about it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went on that expedition when the fruits and shade were good, so I was heading towards it, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims with him passed by, and I began to go out in the morning to prepare with them, then I returned without having completed anything, and I said to myself: I am able to do that if I wanted to! This continued to happen to me until the people continued to be serious, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) became a warrior and the Muslims were with him, and I did not have completed anything of my preparation, then I went out and returned without having completed anything, and this continued to happen to me until they hastened and the expedition was over, so I intended to set out and catch up with them, so I wish I had done so! Then that was not destined for me, so whenever I went out among the people after the departure of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), it saddened me that I did not see for myself a role model except a man who was accused of hypocrisy, or a man from among the weak whom God had excused. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) did not mention me until he reached Tabuk. He said while he was sitting among the people in Tabuk: What happened to Ka`b ibn Malik? A man from Banu Salamah said: O Messenger of God, his cloak and looking at his shoulders are enough for him. Mu`adh ibn Jabal said: What a bad thing you said! By God, O Messenger of God, we know nothing but good about him. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) remained silent. While he was like that, he saw a white man who was fading like a mirage. The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: Be Abu Khaithama. He was Abu Khaithama al-Ansari, and he was the one who gave away a sa` of dates in charity until the hypocrites slandered him. Ka'b ibn Malik said: When I heard that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had set out on his way back from Tabuk, my grief overcame me, so I began to remember the lie and say: How will I escape his wrath tomorrow? I sought help in that from every wise man among my family. When I was told: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is about to arrive, falsehood was removed from me until I knew that I would never be saved from it at all. I decided to believe him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, arrived in the morning. When he returned from a journey, he would start at the mosque and bow in it two rak'ahs, then he would sit for the people. When he had done that, those who had stayed behind came to him and began to apologize to him and swear to him. They were about eighty-odd men. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted their outward expressions, pledged allegiance to them, asked forgiveness for them, and entrusted their secrets to God, until I came. When I had finished, he smiled the smile of someone angry, then he said: Come. So I came walking until I sat in front of him. He said to me: What kept you back? Didn't you buy your back? He said: I said, O Messenger of God, by God, if I had sat with anyone other than you from the people of this world, I would have thought that I would escape his wrath with an excuse, and I have been given an argument, but by God, I know that if I told you today a lie that would please you, God would soon make you angry with me, and if I told you a truthful statement that you would find against me, I would have hoped for the reward of God in the Hereafter. By God, I had no excuse, and by God, I was neither stronger nor more able than I was when I stayed behind from you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As for this, he has told the truth, so get up until God decides about you. So I got up and some men from Banu Salma rose up and followed me and said to me: By God, we do not know that you have committed a sin before this! You were unable to apologize to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with what those who stayed behind apologized to him, so it would have been sufficient for you for your sin that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had asked forgiveness for you! He said: By God, they continued to rebuke me until I wanted to go back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and lie about myself. He said: Then I said to them, has anyone else experienced this with me? They said: Yes! Two men met him and said the same as you said, and they were told the same as you were told. I said: Who are they? They said: Murarah ibn Rabi'ah al-'Amiri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqfi. He said: They mentioned to me two righteous men who had witnessed Badr and in whom there is an example. He said: So I went when they mentioned them to me. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade the Muslims from speaking to us, O three, from among those who stayed behind. He said: So the people avoided us, and he said: And they changed towards us, until the land became strange to me in my mind, and it was not the land that I know. We remained in that state for fifty nights. As for my two companions, they submitted and sat in their houses weeping, but as for me, I was the youngest and most patient of the people. I would go out and attend the prayer and go around the markets and no one would speak to me, and I would come to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and greet him while he was sitting after the prayer, and I would say to myself: Did he move his lips in return for the greeting or not? Then I would pray close to him and steal glances at him. When I turned to pray, he would look at me, and when I turned toward him, he would turn away from me. When this coldness of the Muslims had become too long for me, I walked until I climbed over the wall of Abu Qatada, who was my cousin and the dearest person to me. I greeted him, but by God, he did not return my greeting. I said to him, “O Abu Qatada, I ask you by God! Do you know that I love God and His Messenger?” He remained silent. I returned and implored him, but he remained silent. I returned and implored him, but he said, God and His Messenger know best. My eyes welled up with tears, and I turned away until I climbed over the wall. While I was walking in the market of the city, a Nabataean from the people of Ash-Sham, who had brought food to sell in the city, said, Who can point out Ka’b ibn Malik? The people began to point me out to him until he came to me and gave me a letter from the King of Ghassan, and I was a scribe. I read it and it said, As for what follows! We have been informed that your companion has been cold towards you, and God has not placed you in a house of humiliation or loss, so join us and we will console you. He said: So I said when I read it: This is also a trial! So I took it to the oven and lit it with it, until forty of the fifty had passed and the revelation was delayed, behold, the messenger of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to me and said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) orders you to separate from your wife. I said: Should I divorce her or what should I do? He said: No, rather separate from her and do not come near her. He said: So he sent to my companion with the same. I said to my wife: Go back to your family and stay with them until God decides on this matter. He said: The wife of Hilal ibn Umayya came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said to him: O Messenger of God, Hilal ibn Umayya is an old man who has lost his way and has no servant. Do you mind if I serve him? He said: No, but he should not come near you. She said: By God, he has no desire for anything! By God, he has not stopped crying since what happened to him until this day. He said: Some of my family said: Why don’t you ask permission from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) about your wife, for he gave permission to the wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah to serve him. I said: I will not ask permission from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), and how do I know what the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) will say if I ask his permission about her, and I am a young man! He said: So he remained like that for ten nights, and fifty nights were completed for us from the time he forbade us from speaking. He said: Then I prayed the dawn prayer on the morning of the fifty nights on the roof of one of our houses, and while I was sitting in the state that God mentioned about us, my soul was constricted and the earth was constricted for me despite its vastness, I heard the voice of a caller, most of whom was on the mountain of Sal’, saying at the top of his voice: O Ka’b ibn Malik, be of good cheer. He said: So I fell down in prostration, and I knew that relief had come. He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) announced to the people that God had accepted our repentance when he had prayed the dawn prayer. The people went to give us good report, but some went before my companion to give us good report. A man ran towards me on a horse, and a horseman from Aslam ran before me and up the mountain, but the voice was faster than the horse. When the one whose voice I heard giving me good report came to me, I took off my garment and dressed him in it as a sign of his good report. By God, I did not own anything else that day. I borrowed two garments and put them on, then I set off following the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The people met me in groups, congratulating me on my repentance and saying: May God’s repentance be upon you. Then I entered the mosque, and there was the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sitting in the mosque with people around him. Talhah ibn Ubaydullah stood up and ran until he shook my hand and congratulated me. By God, no man from the Muhajireen stood up except him. He said: Ka’b would never forget that for Talhah. Ka'b said: When I greeted the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), he said while his face was shining with joy, Receive good tidings for the best day that has passed for you since your mother bore you. I said, Is it trustworthy with God, O Messenger of God? Is it from you? He said, No, rather from God. When the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) was happy, his face would light up until it was like a piece of the moon. We used to know that. When I sat in front of him, I said, O Messenger of God, part of God's repentance for me is that I give up my wealth in charity to God and His Messenger. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said, Keep some of your wealth for yourself, for it is better for you. I said, Then I will keep my share in Khaybar. I said, O Messenger of God, God has only saved me because of truthfulness, and part of my repentance is that I will only speak the truth as long as I live. He said: By God, I have not known anyone among the Muslims whom God has blessed with truthfulness since I mentioned that to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) until this day better than He has blessed me with it. By God, I have not deliberately told a lie since I said that to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) until this day, and I hope that God will protect me in what remains.” So God, the Almighty, revealed: God has indeed forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him in the hour of hardship - until he reached - He is to them Kind and Merciful * And to the three who were left behind until, when the earth became strait for them with all its spaciousness, and their souls became strait for them - until he reached - Fear God and be with the truthful. Ka’b said: By God, God has never bestowed upon me a greater blessing after God guided me to Islam than my truthfulness to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), so that I would not lie about him and thus perish as those who lied perished. God said to those who lied when He sent down the revelation the worst thing He has ever said to anyone, and God, the Almighty, said: They will swear to you by God when you return to them that you will turn away from them, so turn away from them. Ka'b said: We, the three of us, were left behind regarding the matter of those whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, accepted when they swore to him, so he pledged allegiance to them and asked forgiveness for them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, postponed our matter until God decided on it. Therefore, God, the Almighty, said: And upon the three, and what God mentioned regarding what we were left behind is not our staying behind from the conquest, but rather it is His leaving us behind and postponing our matter regarding those who swore to him and apologized to him and he accepted from them. The Almighty says: The earth, despite its vastness, became too narrow for them. That is, despite its vastness. It is said: a spacious home, spacious, and spacious. Ma is a source, meaning the earth, despite its vastness, became too narrow for them, because they were abandoned, not treated or spoken to. This is evidence of abandoning the people of sin until they repent. God the Almighty said: And their souls became straitened for them meaning their chests became straitened with worry and loneliness, and with the coldness they encountered from the Companions. And they thought that there was no refuge from God except to Him meaning they were certain that there was no refuge to which they could turn for forgiveness and acceptance of their repentance except to Him. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: Sincere repentance is when the earth becomes straitened for the repentant person despite its vastness, and his soul becomes straitened for him, like the repentance of Ka’b and his two Companions. God the Almighty said: “Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent. Indeed, God is the Accepter of Repentance, the Most Merciful.” So he began with repentance from Him. Abu Zaid said: I made four mistakes: In beginning with God the Almighty, I thought that I loved Him, but He loved me. God the Almighty said: He loves them and they love Him (al-Ma’idah 5:54). I thought that I was pleased with Him, but He was pleased with me. God the Almighty said: God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him (al-Ma’idah 5:119). I thought that I was remembering Him, but He was remembering me. God the Almighty said: And the remembrance of God is greater (al-Ankabut 29:45). I thought that I was repenting, but He was repenting to me. God the Almighty said: Then He turned to them in forgiveness that they might repent. It was said: The meaning is, then He repented to them so that they would remain steadfast in repentance, as God Almighty said: O you who have believed (An-Nisa’: 136). It was also said: That is, He made things easy for them and did not hasten their punishment as He did with others. God Almighty said: Then because of wrongdoing on the part of the Jews, We prohibited to them [certain] good things which had been lawful to them (An-Nisa’: 160).
9:119: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And be with the truthful. This command to be with the truthful is good after the story of the three when truthfulness benefited them and took them away from the ranks of the hypocrites. Mutraf said: I heard Malik bin Anas say: Rarely was a truthful man who did not lie except that he enjoyed his mind and was not afflicted with what afflicts others of old age and senility. There is a difference of opinion about what is meant here by the believers and the truthful. It was said: It is addressed to those who believed from the People of the Book. It was said: It is addressed to all believers, meaning, avoid disobeying the command of God. And be with the truthful, meaning with those who went out with the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, not with the hypocrites. That is, be on the path and way of the truthful. It was said: They are the prophets, meaning, be with them through righteous deeds in Paradise. It was said: They are what is meant by His statement: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces - the verse until His statement - Those are the ones who have been truthful (al-Baqarah 2:177). It was said: They are those who fulfill their covenant, because of the Almighty’s saying: Men who have been true to what they pledged to God (al-Ahzab 33:23). It was also said: They are the emigrants, because of the saying of Abu Bakr on the day of Saqifah, “God called us the truthful ones, so He said: ‘For the poor emigrants’ (al-Hashr 59:8), then He called you the successful ones, so He said: ‘And those who have settled in the home and faith’ (al-Hashr 59:9). It was also said: They are those whose outward appearance and inward appearance are equal. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This statement is the truth and the ultimate goal to which all ends, because this quality removes hypocrisy in belief and opposition in action, and its owner is called the truthful, like Abu Bakr, Omar, Othman and those below them in their ranks and times. As for the one who said: They are what is meant by the verse of Al-Baqarah, then it is most of the truthfulness followed by the less, and it is the meaning of the verse of Al-Ahzab. As for the interpretation of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, it is the one that includes all the statements, because all the qualities are present in them. Second: The right of one who understands and comprehends about God is to adhere to truthfulness in words, sincerity in actions, and purity in conditions. Whoever is like this will join the righteous and attain the pleasure of the Forgiving. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Be truthful, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to be truthful and seeks to be truthful until he is recorded with God as truthful.” Lying is the opposite of that. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Beware of lying, for lying leads to immorality, and immorality leads to the Fire. A man continues to lie and seeks to lie until he is recorded with God as a liar.” Narrated by Muslim. Lying is shameful and its people are stripped of their testimony. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) rejected the testimony of a man who told a lie. Muammar said: I do not know whether he lied about God or about His Messenger or about one of the people. Sharik ibn Abdullah was asked: O Abu Abdullah, if I hear a man lying deliberately, can I pray behind him? He said: No. On the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said: Lying is not appropriate in seriousness or jest, nor is it appropriate for one of you to promise something and then not fulfill it. Read if you wish, O you who believe, fear God and be with those who are truthful. Do you see any dispensation in lying? Malik said: The report of a liar is not accepted in the speech of the people, even if he is truthful in the hadith of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Another said: His hadith is accepted. The correct view is that the testimony and report of a liar are not accepted for the reason we have mentioned, for acceptance is a great rank and a noble position that is only for those whose characteristics are perfect, and there is no characteristic worse than lying, for it removes positions and invalidates testimonies.
9:120: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: It was not for the people of Madinah and those around them of the bedouins to stay behind the Messenger of God appears to be a statement but its meaning is a command, like His statement: And it was not for you to harm the Messenger of God (al-Ahzab 33:53), which has been mentioned before. To stay behind is in the nominative case as the subject of was. This is a rebuke to the believers from the people of Yathrib and the neighboring Arab tribes, such as Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ashja’, Ghifar, and Aslam, for staying behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Battle of Tabuk. The meaning is: It was not for these mentioned people to stay behind, because the call to arms was for them, unlike others, who were not called to arms, according to some of them. It is possible that the call to arms was for every Muslim, and these were singled out for rebuke because of their closeness and proximity, and that they were more deserving of it than others. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And let them not desire themselves over himself meaning they should not be satisfied for themselves with humiliation and ease while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is in hardship. It is said: I desired something, meaning I was above it. Third: The Almighty said: That is because they are not afflicted with thirst meaning thirst. Ubayd ibn Umair read thamaa with a long vowel. They are two dialects like khata’ and khita’. Nor nasb is an atf, meaning fatigue, and Nor is redundant for emphasis. And so is Nor mukhmasa meaning famine. Its origin is the shrinkage of the abdomen, and from it is a man with a slender body and a woman with a slender body. It has been mentioned before. In the way of God meaning in His obedience. Nor do they tread on a path meaning a land. That enrages the disbelievers meaning by their treading on it, and it is in the accusative case because it is an adjective to the path, meaning enraging. Nor do they gain from the enemy a hit meaning killing and defeat. Its origin is from nalta meaning I attained something, meaning I hit it. Al-Kisa’i said: It is from their saying something that is gained from it, and it is not from al-ta’al, rather al-ta’al is from naltatu meaning a gift. Another said: I attained anul from the gift, from the letter waw, and anil from the letter ya. You say: I attained it, so I am anil, meaning I attained it.
9:121: nor do they cross a valley The Arabs say: valley and valleys, not according to the norm. An-Nahhas said: As far as I know, no fa'il and af'ala are known other than it, and the norm is to pluralize wawdi, so they found the combination of two waws heavy, although they might find one heavy, so they said: aqtat in waqtat. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh narrated in the diminutive of Wasil the name of a man or yasul, so they do not say anything else. Al-Farra narrated in the plural of wawd awda. I said: And he collected his blood money. Jarir said: I knew Barqa Al-Awdah, a strange drawing, your time has been long, from the drawings Except that a good deed will be recorded for them. Ibn Abbas said: For every great deed they will receive seventy thousand good deeds in the way of God. And in Sahih: “Horses are three - and in it - as for the one that is for him a reward, a man ties it up in the way of God for the people of Islam in a meadow or garden, and it does not eat from that meadow or garden except that he is written down as many good deeds as it ate, and he is written down as many good deeds as its dung and urine.” The hadith. This is when it is in its places, so how about if he trains it? Fourth: Some scholars have used this verse as evidence that the spoils are deserved if they are brought back and are in enemy territory. If he dies after that, he gets his share. This is the opinion of Ashhab and Abdul Malik, and one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. Malik and Ibn Al-Qasim said: He gets nothing, because God Almighty only mentioned the reward in this verse and did not mention the share. I said: The first is more correct because God Almighty made treading on the lands of the infidels equivalent to seizing their wealth and expelling them from their lands, which angers them and brings humiliation upon them. It is like seizing spoils, killing and taking them captive. If that is the case, then spoils are deserved by taking them, not by possession. Therefore, Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: No people tread on the lands of their own lands except that they are humiliated. And God knows best. Fifth: This verse was abrogated by the Almighty’s saying: It is not for the believers to go forth all together. Its ruling was when the Muslims were few in number, but when they increased in number, it was abrogated and God permitted whoever wished to stay behind, as stated by Ibn Zayd. Mujahid said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent some people to the desert to teach the people, and when this verse was revealed, they were afraid and returned, so God revealed: It is not for the believers to go forth all together. Qatada said: This was specific to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he went out on a military expedition himself, no one had the right to stay behind him except for an excuse. As for other imams and governors, whoever wished to stay behind him from the Muslims had the right to stay behind him if the people did not need him or were in need of him. A third opinion: It is decisive. Al-Walid ibn Muslim said: I heard Al-Awza’i, Ibn Al-Mubarak, Al-Fazari, Al-Subai’i, and Sa’id ibn Abdul Aziz say about this verse that it is for the beginning and the end of this nation. I said: Qatada’s statement is good, as evidenced by the Battle of Tabuk, and God knows best. Sixth: Abu Dawood narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You have left behind in Medina people who, whenever you travelled, spent money or crossed a valley, were with you in it. They said: O Messenger of God, how can they be with us when they are in Medina? He said: An excuse has kept them back. Narrated by Muslim on the authority of Jabir, who said: “We were with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) on a military expedition and he said: ‘Indeed there are men in Madinah who, whenever you set out on a journey or cross a valley, were with you and were held back by illness.’” So the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) gave the one who had an excused reward the same as he gave to the strong, hard worker. Some people have said: The reward is only for the one who has an excused reward, not doubled, and is doubled for the one who works directly. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a judgment on God the Almighty and a restriction of the breadth of His mercy. Some people have criticized him and said: They give the reward doubled for certain, but we do not confirm the doubling in any place, as it is based on the amount of intentions, and this is an unknown matter. What is confirmed is that there is doubling, and your Lord knows best who deserves it. I said: What appears from the hadiths and verses is equality in reward, including his saying, peace be upon him: Whoever guides to something good will have a reward similar to that of the one who does it. And his saying: Whoever performs ablution and goes out to pray and finds that the people have prayed, God will give him a reward like that of the one who prayed and attended. This is apparent from the words of God the Almighty: And whoever emigrates for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become incumbent upon God. And the evidence for this is that the sincere intention is the basis of actions, so if it is sound in performing an act of obedience and its owner is unable to do it due to an obstacle that prevents him, then there is no reason for the reward of the one who is unable to be equal to the reward of the one who is able to do it and even more, because of his saying, peace be upon him: The intention of the believer is better than his action. And God knows best.
9:122: It contains six issues: The first - the Almighty’s saying: And the believers which means that jihad is not for individuals but rather it is a communal obligation as mentioned above, because if everyone went out, the dependents left behind would be lost. So let a group of them go out for jihad and let a group stay and learn about the religion and protect the sacred, until when the ones who went out return, the ones who stayed will teach them what they learned of the rulings of the Shari’ah and what was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This verse abrogates the Almighty’s saying: If you do not go out (al-Tawbah 9:39) and the verse before it, according to the saying of Mujahid and Ibn Zayd. Second: This verse is the basis for the obligation to seek knowledge, because the meaning is, the believers would not go forth all at once while the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was staying and not going forth, so they would leave him alone. Why should they not go forth after they knew that going forth would not be enough for all of them? From every division of them a party and the rest would remain with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to carry out the religion on his behalf and gain understanding. When the people who went forth returned to them, they would tell him what they had heard and learned. This is an obligation to gain understanding of the Qur’an and Sunnah, and that it is for the sufficiency of the people, not for individuals. This is also indicated by the words of God Almighty: So ask the people of the message if you do not know (al-Nahl 16:43) (Al-Anbiya’: 7). So this includes those who do not know the Qur’an and Sunnah. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Why did they not go forth? Al-Akhfash said: meaning, why did they not go forth? From every division of them a party. In the language, the word party means a group, and it may refer to less than that, up to two men, and for one, it means a group. It was previously mentioned that what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: If We pardon a party of you, We will punish a party (al-Tawbah 9:66) is one man. There is no doubt that what is meant here is a group for two reasons, one of them is rational, and the other is linguistic. As for the rational, this is because knowledge is not usually acquired by one person, and as for the language, His saying: That they may gain understanding in the religion and warn their people, came with the pronoun for the group. Ibn Al-Arabi said: Judge Abu Bakr and Sheikh Abu Al-Hasan before him see that the group here is one, and they support this with the evidence of the obligation to act on the report of one person, and this is correct, not because the word party refers to one person, but because the report of one person or persons is one report, and its opposite, which is continuous transmission, is not limited. I said: The most explicit evidence that one person is called a group is the Almighty’s statement: And if two parties among the believers should fight (al-Hujurat 49:9) meaning two people. Its evidence is the Almighty’s statement: Then make settlement between your two brothers (al-Hujurat 49:10), so it came in the dual form, and the pronoun in they fought is even if it is the pronoun for a group, then the minimum for a group is two according to one of the two opinions of the scholars. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: That they may understand The pronoun in that they may understand and that they may warn refers to those who stayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Qatada and Mujahid said. Al-Hasan said: They are for the rebellious group, and this was chosen by Al-Tabari. The meaning of that they may understand the religion is that they may see and be certain of what God shows them of victory over the polytheists and support for the religion. And that they may warn their people from the disbelievers. When they return to them from jihad, so they may inform them of God Almighty’s support for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers, and that they will not be able to fight them and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so what happened to their companions from the disbelievers happened to them. I said: The statement of Mujahid and Qatadah is clearer, that is, so that the later group may understand with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the aversion to the raids. This requires urging and encouraging the pursuit of knowledge, without obligation and compulsion, since that is not in the strength of speech, but rather the pursuit of knowledge is required by its evidence, as Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said. Fifth: Seeking knowledge is divided into two parts: an obligation on individuals, such as prayer, zakat, and fasting. I said - and in this meaning came the narrated hadith: Seeking knowledge is an obligation. Abdul Quddus bin Habib narrated: Abu Saeed Al-Wahhazi on the authority of Hammad bin Abi Sulayman on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, he said: I heard Anas bin Malik say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Seeking knowledge is an obligation upon every Muslim. Ibrahim said: I did not hear from Anas bin Malik except this hadith. It is a collective obligation, such as obtaining rights, establishing limits, and adjudicating between opponents, etc., since it is not appropriate for all people to learn it, lest their conditions and the conditions of their families be lost, and their livelihoods be diminished or nullified. So it is determined between the two situations that some should carry it out without specifying, and that is according to what God has made easy for His servants and divided among them from His mercy and wisdom by His previous power and word. Sixth: Seeking knowledge is a great virtue and a noble rank that no action can match. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Whoever takes a path in search of knowledge, God will make a path for him to Paradise. The angels lower their wings in satisfaction with the seeker of knowledge. The scholar is asked for forgiveness by all those in the heavens and on the earth and by the fish in the depths of the water. The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like the superiority of the moon on the night of the full moon over all the other planets. The scholars are the heirs of the prophets. The prophets did not leave behind dinars or dirhams, but rather they left behind knowledge. So whoever takes it has taken an abundant portion.” Al-Darimi Abu Muhammad narrated in his Musnad. He said: Abu Al-Mughira told us. Al-Awza’i told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about two men among the Children of Israel. One of them was a scholar who prayed the obligatory prayers and then sat and taught people good. The other fasted during the day and prayed at night. Which of them was better? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The superiority of this scholar who prays the obligatory prayers and then sits and teaches people good over the worshipper who fasts during the day and prays at night is like my superiority over the lowest of you. Abu Omar narrated it in his book Bayan al-Ilm on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Khudri who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like my superiority over my nation. Ibn Abbas said: The best jihad is that of one who builds a mosque in which he teaches the Qur’an, jurisprudence, and Sunnah. It was narrated by Sharik on the authority of Laith ibn Abi Salim on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer on the authority of Ali al-Azdi who said: I wanted to engage in jihad, but Ibn Abbas said to me: Shall I not guide you to something that is better for you than jihad? You go to a mosque and recite the Qur’an and learn jurisprudence there. Al-Rabi’ said: I heard al-Shafi’i say: Seeking knowledge is more obligatory than voluntary prayer. And the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: The angels spread their wings This hadith has two possible meanings: One is that they show compassion and mercy towards him, as God the Almighty said in what He commanded children to do good to their parents, saying: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy (al-Isra’ 17:24), meaning be humble towards them. The other meaning is that what is meant by spreading the wings is spreading them, because in some narrations: And the angels spread their wings meaning that if the angels see a seeker of knowledge seeking knowledge from his direction seeking the pleasure of God and all his other circumstances are compatible with seeking knowledge, they spread their wings for him on his journey and carry him on it, so from there he is safe and does not become barefoot if he is walking and does not get tired, and the long road is made easy for him and he is not afflicted with the types of harm that afflict a traveler such as illness, loss of wealth, and losing his way. Something of this meaning has already passed in Al Imran when God the Almighty said: God is witness (Al Imran 3:18), the verse. Imran bin Husayn narrated that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: A group of my nation will continue to be victorious over the truth until the Hour comes. Yazid bin Harun said: If they are not the people of hadith, then I do not know who they are? I said: This is what Abd al-Razzaq said in interpreting the verse, that they are the people of hadith, as mentioned by al-Tha’labi. I heard our Sheikh, the professor, reciter, grammarian and hadith scholar Abu Ja’far ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Qaysi al-Qurtubi, known as Ibn Abi Hujjah, may God have mercy on him, say in interpreting the words of peace be upon him: The people of the West will continue to be victorious over the truth until the Hour comes. They are the scholars. He said: This is because the word west is a common term that refers to a large bucket and the setting sun, and it refers to a stream of tears. So the meaning of the people of the West will continue is that the people of the stream of tears out of fear of God, out of knowledge of Him and His rulings, will continue to be victorious, the hadith. God the Almighty said: Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge. (Fatir 35:28) I said: This interpretation is supported by what he, peace be upon him, said in Sahih Muslim: “Whoever God wants good for, He gives him understanding of the religion. And a group of Muslims will continue to fight for the truth, victorious over those who oppose them, until the Day of Resurrection.” The apparent meaning of this passage is that its beginning is connected to its end. And God knows best.
