9:123: There is one issue - that God, the Almighty, taught them how to wage jihad and that they should start with the closest enemy first, and that is why the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, started with the Arabs, and when he finished, he headed towards the Romans, who were in Ash-Sham. Al-Hasan said: It was revealed before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ordered to fight the polytheists, so it is part of the gradualism that was before Islam. Ibn Zayd said: What was meant by this verse at the time of its revelation was the Arabs, and when he finished with them, it was revealed about the Romans and others: Fight those who do not believe in God (al-Tawbah 9:29). It was narrated from Ibn Umar that what was meant by this was the Daylamites. It was narrated from him that he was asked who should start with the Romans or the Daylamites? He said: The Romans. Al-Hasan said: It is fighting the Daylamites, the Turks, and the Romans. Qatada said: The verse is general in fighting the closest, then the closest, and the nearest, then the nearest. I said: Qatada’s statement is the apparent meaning of the verse, and Ibn al-Arabi chose to begin with the Romans before the Daylamites, based on what Ibn Umar said, for three reasons. First: They are People of the Book, so the argument against them is stronger and more compelling. Second: They are closer to us, I mean the people of Medina. Third: Our land has more prophets in its land, so rescuing it from them is more obligatory. And God knows best. And that they may find in you harshness meaning severity, strength and zeal. Al-Fadl narrated on the authority of Al-A'mash and Asim, ghaltha with a fatha on the ghain and a sukoon on the lam. Al-Farra' said: The language of the people of Al-Hijaz and Banu Asad is with a kasra on the ghain, and the language of Banu Tamim is ghaltha with a damma on the ghain.
9:124: What is the connection, and what is meant are the hypocrites. Which of you has this increased in faith? The increase and decrease of faith has been discussed in Surah Al Imran. The meaning of the Surah has been discussed in the introduction to the book, so there is no point in repeating it. Al-Hasan wrote to Omar bin Abdul Aziz that faith has laws and obligations, whoever completes them has completed faith, and whoever does not complete them has not completed faith. Omar bin Abdul Aziz said: If I live, I will explain them to you, and if I die, I am not keen on your company. Al-Bukhari mentioned it. Ibn Al-Mubarak said: I found no alternative but to say that faith increases, otherwise I will reject the Qur’an.
9:125: The Almighty said: And as for those in whose hearts is disease, meaning doubt, suspicion, and hypocrisy. This has been mentioned before. It will increase their filth upon their filth, meaning doubt upon their doubt and disbelief upon their disbelief. Muqatil said: sin upon sin, and the meaning is close.
9:126: The Almighty said: Or do they not see that they are tested every year once or twice? The general reading is with a ya', reporting the hypocrites. Hamza and Ya'qub read with a ta' reporting them and addressing the believers. Al-A'mash read or they did not see. Talhah ibn Musarraf read or you do not see, which is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, addressing the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. They are tested, according to At-Tabari, means they are tested. Mujahid said: with famine and hardship. Atiyyah said: with diseases and pains, which are the harbingers of death. Qatada, Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: with conquest and jihad with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they see what God has promised of victory then they do not repent for that nor do they remember.
9:127: The Almighty’s saying: And when a surah is revealed, they look at one another. What is the connection, and what is meant are the hypocrites, that is, if they attend the Messenger while he is reciting a Qur’an in which their disgrace or the disgrace of one of them has been revealed, they start looking at one another with a look of fear as a way of confirming, saying: Does anyone see you when you say this so that he can convey it to Muhammad? This is out of their ignorance of his prophethood, peace be upon him, and that God informs him of whatever He wills of His unseen. It was said: that looking in this verse means informing. Al-Tabari narrated from some of them that he said: looking in this verse is a place where he said. God the Almighty says: Then they turned away meaning they turned away from the path of guidance. This is because when He revealed to them their secrets and informed them of the hidden matters of their affairs, they inevitably felt amazement, pause and contemplation. If they had been guided, that time would have been a time when they believed. So when they persisted in disbelief and became confused about it, it was as if they had turned away from that state which was a time when they would have believed in the right way and been guided. They did not hear the recitation of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as someone who contemplates it and contemplates its verses: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason. (al-Anfal 8:22) Do they not then reflect upon the Qur’an, or are there locks upon their hearts? (Muhammad 47:24) God Almighty said: God turned their hearts away. There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: God has turned their hearts away is a supplication against them, meaning say this to them. It is also possible that it is report about turning them away from goodness as a reward for their actions. It is a word that is invoked, like His saying: May God fight them (al-Tawbah 9:30). The ba in His saying: that they are is a connection to turned away. Second: Ibn Abbas said: It is disliked to say we have turned away from the prayer, because some people turned away and God turned their hearts away. Rather, say we have completed the prayer. At-Tabari narrated it from him. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is questionable and I do not think it is correct, because the system of speech is to say: No one should say we have turned away from the prayer, because it was said about some al-Nas 114:Then they turned away and God turned their hearts away. Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik al-Qaysi al-Wa’iz informed us, and Abu al-Fadl al-Jawhari heard him say: We were at a funeral and al-Mundhir said: Turn away, may God have mercy on you! He said: No one should say they have turned away, because God the Most High said about a people He condemned: Then they turned away and God turned their hearts away. Rather, say: They have returned, may God have mercy on you, because God the Most High said about a people He praised: “So they returned with favor and bounty from God. No harm had touched them.” (AAl Imran 3:174) Third: God Almighty informed in this verse that He is the One Who directs and controls hearts, and the One Who molds and turns them, in response to the Qadarites who believe that the hearts of creation are in their hands and their limbs are under their control, acting according to their will and ruling according to their will and choice. Therefore, Malik said, as narrated by Ashab: “How clear is this in response to the Qadarites: ‘The structure they have built will not cease to be a source of doubt in their hearts unless their hearts are cut out.’” And God Almighty said to Nuh 71:None of your people will believe except those who have already believed (Hud 11:36). This will never happen, will not return, and will not disappear.
9:128: These two verses, according to Abu, are the closest Quran to the heavens in time. And according to Saeed bin Jubair: The last of the Quran to be revealed is And fear a Day when you will be returned to God (al-Baqarah 2:281) based on what was mentioned above. It is possible that Abu’s statement: The closest Quran to the heavens in time comes after his statement: And fear a Day when you will be returned to God. And God knows best. The address is to the Arabs according to the majority of scholars, and this is in order to enumerate the blessings upon them in that, as it came in their language and in what they understand, and they were honored by it in the past. Al-Zajjaj said: It is addressed to the entire world, and the meaning is: A Messenger from among mankind has come to you, and the first is more correct. Ibn Abbas said: There is no tribe of Arabs who did not give birth to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so it is as if he said: O Arabs, a Messenger from among the children of Ishmael has come to you. The second statement is more convincing for the argument, meaning he is a human being like you so that you understand him and follow his example. The Almighty’s saying: From among yourselves implies praise for the lineage of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he is from the core and purest of the Arabs. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa’, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God chose Kinanah from the descendants of Ishmael, and chose Quraysh from Kinanah, and chose Quraysh from Banu Hashim, and chose me from Banu Hashim. It was narrated that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am from marriage and not from fornication. This means that his lineage, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Adam, peace be upon him, was not due to any offspring except marriage, and there was no fornication in it. Abdullah bin Qusayt Al-Makki read it as from yourselves with a fat-ha on the fa from preciousness, and it was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from Fatima, may God be pleased with her, meaning a messenger has come to you from the most noble and excellent of you, from your saying: something precious if it is desired. It was also said: from yourselves, meaning the most obedient of you. God the Almighty said: Hard for Him is what you suffer meaning He finds your hardship hard. Hardship is from the saying: A hill is a difficult place, if it is a difficult and deadly place. Ibn al-Anbari said: The root of hardship is to intensify. So when the Arabs say: So-and-so is being harsh with so-and-so, what they mean is to intensify and force him to do something that is difficult for him to do. This has been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. And what is in what you suffer is a source, and it is the subject, and dear is the predicate that comes before. It is permissible for what you suffer to be the subject of dear, and dear is an attribute of the Messenger, and this is more correct. Likewise, keen on you, and kind and merciful is raised as an attribute. Al-Farraa said: If it had been read as dear to him what you suffer, keen, kind, merciful, in the accusative case as a state, it would have been permissible. Abu Jaafar Al-Nahhas said: The best thing that has been said about its meaning, which agrees with the speech of the Arabs, is what Ahmad bin Muhammad Al-Azdi told us: Abdullah bin Muhammad Al-Khuza’i told us: I heard Amr bin Ali say: I heard Abdullah bin Dawud Al-Khuraibi say about the words of God Almighty: “There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. Grievous to him is what you suffer,” meaning that you should enter the Fire. He is anxious over you, meaning that you should enter Paradise. It was also said: He is anxious for you to believe. Al-Farra’ said: He is stingy that you should enter the Fire. And being anxious about something means being stingy with it so that it is lost and destroyed. To the believers, Most Kind, Most Merciful. The most kind is the one who is extremely compassionate and merciful. The meaning of Most Kind, Most Merciful has already been fully explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. Al-Husayn bin Al-Fadl said: God did not combine two of His names for any of the prophets except for the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for He said: To the believers, Most Kind, Most Merciful, and He said: Indeed, God is to the people Most Kind and Merciful. (al-Baqarah 2:143) Abdul Aziz bin Yahya said: The structure of the verse: “There has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves, exalted in honor, concerned for the believers, kind and merciful. Grievous to him is what you suffer. He is concerned only with your affairs, and he is the one who will intercede for you, so do not be concerned about what you suffer as long as you adhere to his Sunnah, for nothing pleases him except your entry into Paradise.”
9:129: The Almighty said: But if they turn away, then say, 'God is sufficient for me' meaning, if the disbelievers turn away, O Muhammad, after these blessings that God has bestowed upon them, then say, God is sufficient for me meaning, God is sufficient for me. "There is no god but He. Upon Him I have relied" meaning, I have depended, and to Him I have entrusted all my affairs. And He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne He specified the Throne because He is the greatest of creations, so everything below it is included in it if He mentions it. The general reading is with the accusative of the great as a description of the Throne. It was read with the nominative as a description of the Lord, and it was narrated from Ibn Kathir, and it is the reading of Ibn Muhaysin. In the book of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Abu al-Darda', he said: “Whoever says in the morning and evening, ‘God is sufficient for me. There is no god but He. In Him I have put my trust, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne’ seven times, God will suffice him in whatever concerns him, whether he is telling the truth or lying.” In Nawader al-Usul, on the authority of Buraydah, he said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says ten words after every prayer, God will find them sufficient and rewarding: five for this world and five for the Hereafter: God is sufficient for my religion, God is sufficient for my world, God is sufficient for what concerns me, God is sufficient for him who wrongs me, God is sufficient for him who envies me, God is sufficient for him who plots against me with evil, God is sufficient for me at death, God is sufficient for me when questioned in the grave, God is sufficient for me at the scale, God is sufficient for me at the bridge, God is sufficient for me, there is no god but He. In Him I rely, and to Him I turn.” Al-Naqqash narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b that he said: The two verses of the Qur’an closest to God Almighty are these two verses: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves to the end of the surah, and we have explained it. Yusuf ibn Mihran narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the last verse to be revealed of the Qur’an was There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves and this verse. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. We have mentioned a different verse from Ibn Abbas, as we mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, and it is more correct. Muqatil said: It was revealed in Mecca beforehand. This is far-fetched, because the surah was revealed in Medina, and God knows best. Yahya bin Ja'dah said: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him would not confirm a verse in the Qur'an until two men testified to it. Then a man from the Ansar came to him with the two verses from the end of Surat Bara'ah: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves. 'Umar said: "By God, I do not ask you for proof for them. That is how the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was." So he confirmed them. Our scholars said: The man is Khuzaymah bin Thabit, and 'Umar may God be pleased with him confirmed them based on his testimony alone because the evidence for their authenticity was established in the description of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It is a sign that makes it unnecessary to ask for another witness, unlike the verse of Al-Ahzab the Confederates: Men who have been true to what they pledged to God (al-Ahzab 33:23), which was confirmed based on the testimony of Zayd and Khuzaymah because they heard it from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This meaning was mentioned in the introduction to the book. Praise be to God.
10:1: Surah Yunus, peace be upon him, is Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir. Ibn Abbas said: Except for three verses from the words of God the Almighty: If you are in doubt (Yunus 10:94) to the end. Muqatil said: Except for two verses, which are His words: If you are in doubt, which were revealed in Medina. Al-Kalbi said: It is Meccan except for the words: And among them are those who believe in it and among them are those who do not believe in it (Yunus 10:40), which were revealed in Medina about the Jews. A group said: About forty verses from the beginning of it were revealed in Mecca and the rest in Medina. God Almighty says: “Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the Wise Book.” God the Almighty said: Alif, Lam, Ra. An-Nahhas said: It was read to Abu Ja`far Ahmad ibn Shu`ayb ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Harith. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us on the authority of his father on the authority of Yazid that Ikrimah told him on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Alif, Lam, and Nun are the letters of the Most Gracious, separated. So I told it to al-A`mash and he said: You have similar things to this and you do not tell me about it? And on the authority of Ibn Abbas also, he said: The meaning of Alif, Lam, Ra is that I see God. An-Nahhas said: I saw Abu Ishaq leaning towards this statement, because Sibawayh had narrated something similar on the authority of the Arabs and recited: I do good things, and if I do evil things, I do not want evil unless you wish it. Al-Hasan and Ikrimah said: Al-Ra is a section. Saeed said on the authority of Qatada: Al-Ra is the name of the Surah. He said: And so is every spelling in the Qur’an. Mujahid said: They are the openings of the Surahs. Muhammad bin Yazid said: They are an alert, and so are the letters of spelling. Al-Ra was read without inclination. And it was read with inclination so that it would not resemble the letters ma and la. The Almighty’s saying: These are the verses of the Wise Book is a subject and predicate, meaning those that were mentioned are verses of the Wise Book. Mujahid and Qatadah said: He meant the Torah, the Gospel, and the previous books, because those are a reference to an absent feminine. It was said: those have the same meaning as these, meaning these are the verses of the Wise Book. And from this is the saying of Al-A’sha: These are my horses from him and these are my riders, their young ones are as yellow as raisins This is my horse. What is meant is the Qur’an, and it is more correct, because the previous books were not mentioned, and because al-Hakim is one of the attributes of the Qur’an. The evidence for this is the statement of God the Almighty: “Alif, Lam, Ra. A Book whose verses are perfected” (Hud 11:1). This meaning was mentioned at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah. Al-Hakim is the one who rules on what is permissible and what is forbidden, the limits and the rulings, as stated by Abu Ubaidah and others. It was also said that al-Hakim means the judge, meaning that he rules on what is permissible and what is forbidden, and judges between people with truth, so fa’il means fa’il. The evidence for this is the statement of God the Almighty: And He sent down with them the Book in truth to judge between people concerning that wherein they differed (al-Baqarah 2:213). It was also said that al-Hakim means the one judged, meaning that God ruled in it with justice, kindness and giving to relatives, and ruled in it by forbidding indecency and wrongdoing, and by Paradise for those who obey Him and Hell for those who disobey Him, so it is fa’il in the sense of the passive participle, as stated by al-Hasan and others. Muqatil said: Al-Hakim means the one who is decisive from falsehood, with no lies or differences in it. Fa’il means maf’il, like the saying of Al-A’sha, mentioning his poem that he said: Strangely, the kings come, wise. I said it so that it might be said, Who said it?
10:2: The Almighty said: Was it a wonder to the people? A question that means confirmation and rebuke. Amazing is the predicate of was, and its subject is that We inspired and it is in the nominative case, meaning Our inspiration was a wonder to the people. In Abdullah's reading, it is amazed as the subject of was. The predicate is that We inspired. To a man among them Man was read with a sukoon on the jim. The reason for revelation, according to what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, is that the disbelievers said when Muhammad was sent: God is too great for His Messenger to be a human being. They said: God did not find anyone to send him except the orphan of Abu Talib. So the verse: Was it a wonder to the people meaning the people of Mecca was revealed. It was said: They were amazed by the mention of the resurrection. The Almighty’s saying: Warn the people and give good tidings to those who believe is in the accusative case by dropping the preposition, meaning that I warn the people, and likewise that they will have a sure footing. The meaning of warning and good tidings and other words of the verse have already been mentioned. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of a sure footing. Ibn Abbas said: a sure footing, a sure abode, the evidence for which is the Almighty’s saying: And say, My Lord, let me enter a sure entrance (al-Isra’ 17:80). And it was also narrated from him: a good reward for what they have done of their deeds. And it was also narrated from him: a sure footing preceded happiness in the first mention, and Mujahid said it. Al-Zajjaj: a high degree. Dhu al-Rummah said: You have a foot that people do not deny that, with its high lineage, it has floated on the sea. Qatada: A true predecessor. Al-Rabi’: A reward for truth. Ata’: A station of truth. Yaman: A true faith. It was said: The call of the angels. It was said: A righteous son whom they presented. Al-Mawardi: That the truth of obedience matches the truth of reward. Al-Hasan and Qatada also said: He is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he is an intercessor who is obeyed and precedes them, as he said: I will be your predecessor at the Cistern. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked and said: It is my intercession, you seek my intercession with your Lord through me. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim said: He presented him, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the praised station. And also from Al-Hasan: Their affliction in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And Abdul Aziz bin Yahya said: The most truthful is the saying of God Almighty: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it (al-Anbiya 21:101). And Muqatil said: Deeds they presented, and Al-Tabari chose it. Al-Waddah said: Pray to the Lord of the Throne and take a step that will save you on the day of stumbling and error. It was said: It is God’s advancement of this nation in the resurrection from the grave and in entering Paradise. As He said: We are the last ones who will be the first on the Day of Resurrection, and the judgment will be made for us before all creation. The truth is that it is a metaphor for striving in good deeds, so it is used as a metaphor for it, just as it is used to refer to giving a gift with the hand and praising with the tongue. Hassan recited: We have the upper hand over you and we are behind you in the obedience of God. Follow us. He means precedence in sincere obedience, and God knows best. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Kisa’i said: Every precedence in good or evil is, according to the Arabs, precedence. It is said: So-and-so has precedence in Islam, he has with me a precedence of truth, a precedence of evil, and a precedence of good. It is feminine and can be masculine. It is said: a precedence of goodness and a precedence of righteousness. Ibn Al-A’rabi said: precedence is advancement in honor. Al-Ajjaj said: The Banu Awam tribe slipped away from the ruling family and left the kingdom to a king with a foot In Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “I have five names. I am Muhammad, Ahmad, and I am the annihilator through whom God annihilates disbelief. I am the gatherer who will gather people at my feet, and I am the last of the prophets,” meaning the last of the prophets, as God Almighty said: and the seal of the prophets (al-Ahzab 33:40). The Almighty said: The disbelievers said, ‘Indeed, this is an obvious magician.’ Ibn Muhaysin, Ibn Kathir, and the Kufians Asim, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Khalaf, and Al-A’mash read magician as a description of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The rest read magic as a description of the Qur’an. The meaning of magic was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah.
10:3: The Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself on the Throne. It was mentioned in Al-A'raf. He directs the affair. Mujahid said: He alone decrees and determines it. Ibn Abbas said: No one shares with Him in directing His creation. It was also said: He sends the affair. It was also said: He descends with it. It was also said: He orders it and carries it out, and the meanings are close. So Gabriel is for revelation, Michael is for rain, Israfil is for the trumpet, and Azrael is for seizing. Its reality is to send down matters in their ranks according to the rulings of their consequences, and its derivation is from the word dabar. The command is a name for the type of matters. There is no intercessor is in the nominative case, and the meaning is there is no intercessor except after His permission. The meaning of intercession was mentioned in Al-Baqarah. No prophet or anyone else can intercede except with His permission, glory be to Him. This is a response to the infidels’ statement regarding what they worshipped besides God: These are our intercessors with God (Yunus 10:18). So God informed them that no one can intercede for anyone except with His permission, so how about the intercession of idols that do not understand? God Almighty says: That is God, your Lord, so worship Him. That is, the One who did these things, creating the heavens and the earth, is your Lord, you have no other Lord but Him. So worship Him that is, make Him One and devote your worship to Him. Will you not remember? That is, these are His creations, so that you may use them as evidence of Him.
10:4: The Almighty’s saying: To Him is your return is in the nominative case. All together is in the accusative case as a state. The meaning of returning to God is returning to His reward. God’s promise is true is two sources, meaning God promised that promise and fulfilled it truly and honestly, without breaking it. Ibrahim bin Abi Ubla read God’s promise is true as a new sentence. God the Almighty said: He begins creation meaning from dust. Then He returns it to it. Mujahid: He creates it, then causes it to die, then brings it to life for resurrection, or He creates it from water, then returns it from one state to another. Yazid ibn al-Qa’qa’ read that He begins creation, so that an is in the accusative case, meaning He promised you that He begins creation. It is permissible for the estimation to be because He begins creation, as one says: Here I am, for all praise and blessings are Yours, and the kasra is better. Al-Farra’ permitted an to be in the nominative case, so it would be a noun. Ahmad ibn Yahya said: The estimation would be truly His beginning of creation. God the Almighty says: That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds with justice. That is, with fairness. And those who disbelieve will have a drink of scalding water. That is, hot water that has reached its peak. The scalding water is the same. It is said: I made the water scalding hot, so it is scalding water, meaning scalding hot. Fa’il means maf’ul. And everything that is scalded among the Arabs is scalding water. And a painful torment, that is, painful, whose pain reaches their hearts. Because they used to disbelieve, that is, because of their disbelief. Most of the Quraysh acknowledged that God was their Creator, so he argued with them by saying: He who is able to begin is able to repeat after annihilation or after the parts are separated.
10:5: The Almighty said: It is He who made the sun a radiance two objects, meaning bright, and it is not feminine because it is a source, or having radiance, and the moon a light is a conjunction, meaning illuminating, or having light, so radiance is that which illuminates things, and light is that which reveals and conceals, because it is from fire from the same root. And radiance is the plural of light, like whips and basins are the plural of whip and basin. Qanbal read from Ibn Kathir dia'a with a hamza on the ya', but there is no basis for this, because its ya' was an open waw and it is the 'ayn of the verb, its root is dawa', so it was changed and made a ya' as it was made in fasting and standing. Al-Mahdawi said: Whoever reads dia'a with a hamza, it is inverted, the hamza that comes after the alif was brought forward so it came before the alif so it became dhay'aya, then the ya' was changed to a hamza because it came after an extra alif. Likewise, if you consider that the Ya’ when it is delayed returns to the Waw from which it was changed, then it is also changed to a Hamza, so its weight is Fala’, changed from Fa’al. It is said: The sun and the moon shine their faces for the people of the seven heavens and their backs for the people of the seven earths. The Almighty said: And He has destined for him mansions. That is, he has mansions, or He has destined for him mansions. Then it was said: The meaning is He has destined for them both, so He made it singular for brevity and abbreviation, as He said: And when they see a transaction or amusement, they disperse to it (al-Jumuah 62:11). And as He said: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs It was said: The information is about the moon alone, since it is used to count the months upon which transactions and the like are done, as mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. And in Surat Ya-Sin 36:And the moon - We have measured for it phases (Ya-Sin 36:39) meaning according to the number of the month, which is twenty-eight phases. And two days for the waning and the new moon, and there its explanation will come. God Almighty says: That you may know the number of years and the reckoning. Ibn Abbas said: If He made two suns, one during the day and one during the night, in which there is neither darkness nor night, He would not know the number of years and the reckoning of months. The singular of years is sanah, and some Arabs say sanawat in the plural. Some of them say sanhat. The diminutive is saniyah and saniyah. God Almighty says: God did not create this except in truth. That is, God Almighty did not intend by creating this except wisdom and correctness, and to demonstrate His creation and wisdom, and to indicate His power and knowledge, and so that every soul may be rewarded for what it has earned. This is the truth. The Almighty says: He details the verses for a people who know. The detailing of the verses is their clarification to prove His Almighty power, because the night is distinguished by its darkness and the day by its light without them being entitled to it or obligatory, so this is evidence for them that it is by the will of the one who wills. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hafs, and Yaqub read yafasil with a ya, and Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it, because of what was said before it: God did not create this except with truth and after it and what God created in the heavens and the earth, so it follows it. Ibn al-Sumaiqa’ read tafasil with a damma on the ta’ and a fatha on the sad as a passive verb, and ayat as a nominative. The rest read nafasil with a noon as a sign of glorification.
10:6: Its meaning was presented in Al-Baqarah and elsewhere, and praise be to God. It has been said that the reason for its revelation was that the people of Mecca asked for a sign, so He directed them to contemplate and consider His creations, as Ibn Abbas said. For a people who fear meaning polytheism. As for the one who associates partners with God and does not provide evidence, then the verse is not a sign for him.
10:7: The Almighty says: Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us hope and fear, and from this the poet said: If a bee stings him, he does not want to be stung by it and he stays in a house full of honey bees. It was said that they hope and desire, and from it is the saying of another: I hope that the Banu Marwan will listen to me and obey me, and my people Tamim and the desert will follow me. Hope can mean fear and greed, meaning they do not fear punishment nor hope for reward. And making the encounter of punishment and reward a encounter with God is an exaltation of them. It was said: The encounter is taken literally, which is seeing, meaning they do not hope to see us. Some scholars said: Hope does not mean fear except with denial, like the Almighty’s saying: What is the matter with you that you do not have reverence for God? (Nuh 71:13). Some of them said: Rather, it occurs with its meaning in every place where the meaning indicates it. The Almighty said: And were content with the life of this world meaning they were content with it in exchange for the Hereafter, so they worked for it. And were reassured by it meaning they were happy with it and were content with it. The root of itmaana is itmaana rest assured, so its mim was brought forward and a nun and an alif were added, as mentioned by Al-Gharnawi. And those who are heedless of Our signs meaning of Our evidence and do not consider or reflect.
10:8: Their abode means their place of residence and their abode. The Fire is for what they used to earn meaning disbelief and denial.
10:9: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who have believed meaning have been truthful. And done righteous deeds - their Lord will guide them because of their faith meaning He will increase their guidance, as He said: And those who are guided - He will increase them in guidance (Muhammad 47:17). It was said: Their Lord will guide them because of their faith to a place beneath which rivers flow. Abu Rawq said: Their Lord will guide them because of their faith to Paradise. Atiyah said: He will guide them, reward them and recompense them. Mujahid said: Their Lord will guide them with light on the path to Paradise, He will make for them a light by which they walk. It is narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, what strengthens this, that he said: “The believer receives his deeds in the best possible way, so they comfort him and guide him. The unbeliever receives his deeds in the worst possible way, so they alienate him and lead him astray.” This is the meaning of the hadith. Ibn Jurayj said: He makes their deeds a guide for them. Al-Hasan: He guides them and has mercy on them. The Almighty says: Underneath which rivers flow. It was said: There is an omitted waw in the speech, meaning: and it flows beneath them, meaning beneath their gardens. It was also said: beneath their beds, and this is better for recreation and entertainment.
10:10: The Almighty said: "Their supplication therein will be: Glory be to You, O God." Their supplication: meaning their prayer. The supplication is a verbal noun from the verb to call, just as the complaint is a verbal noun from the verb to complain, meaning their supplication in Paradise is to say: Glory be to You, O God. It was said: If they wanted to ask for something, they would express their request with the wording of glorification and conclude with praise. It was said: Their calling to the servants to bring them whatever they wanted, then they would glorify God. It was said: The supplication here means a wish. God the Almighty said: And for you therein is whatever you ask for (Fussilat 41:31) meaning whatever you wish. And God knows best. God Almighty says: “And their greeting therein will be, ‘Peace.’” That is, God’s greeting to them, or the King’s greeting, or the greeting of some of them to others: “Peace.” The meaning of greeting has already been fully discussed in Surat An-Nisa. Praise be to God. The Almighty’s saying: And their final call will be, ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.’ There are four issues in this: First: It was said: When the birds pass by the people of Paradise and they desire it, they say: Glory be to You, O God. Then the angel brings what they desire, and when they eat, they praise God, so their question is with the wording of glorification and the conclusion is with the wording of praise. Abu Ubaid did not narrate anything except the lightening of an and the raising of what comes after it. He said: Rather, we see that they chose this and distinguished between it and the saying of the Almighty: That the curse of God (al-Nur 24:7) and That the wrath of God (al-Nur 24:9) because they wanted to narrate when it is said Praise be to God. An-Nahhas said: The doctrine of Al-Khalil and Sibawayh is that this an is lightened from the heavy, and the meaning is that it is praise be to God. Muhammad bin Yazid said: It is permissible that Praise be to God makes it light, and it makes it heavy, and raising is more appropriate. An-Nahhas said: Abu Hatim narrated that Bilal bin Abi Burdah recited and the end of their supplication is that Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. I said: It is the reading of Ibn Muhaisin, as narrated by Al-Gharnawi because he narrated it from him. Second: Glorification, praise, and declaration of God’s oneness may be called supplication. Muslim and Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say when in distress: “There is no god but God, the Great, the Forbearing. There is no god but God, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no god but God, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of the Noble Throne.” At-Tabari said: The early Muslims used to supplicate with this supplication and called it the supplication of distress. Ibn Uyaynah was asked about this and said: Do you not know that “God the Most High says: If my servant is distracted by his praise from asking Me, I will give him the best of what I give to those who ask.” What ends the dispute and that this is called supplication even though it has nothing of the meaning of supplication, but rather it is glorification of God the Most High and praise of Him is what An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The supplication of Jonah when he supplicated in the belly of the whale: “There is no god but You, glory be to Him. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.” No Muslim supplicates with it for anything but that it will be answered for him. Third: It is Sunnah for the one who begins eating to mention the name of God when he eats and drinks and to praise Him when he finishes, following the example of the people of Paradise. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God is pleased with the servant who eats a meal and praises Him for it, or drinks a drink and praises Him for it. Fourth: It is recommended for the supplicant to say at the end of his supplication as the people of Paradise said: And their final supplication is: Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. And it is good to recite at the end Surat As-Saffat, for they combine the glorification of the Creator, the Most High, from what is attributed to Him, and the greetings to the Messengers, and the conclusion with praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.
10:11: God Almighty says: And if God were to hasten for people the evil as they hasten for good, their term would have been ended for them. There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And if God were to hasten the evil for the people, it was said: Its meaning is, if God were to hasten the punishment for the people as they hasten the reward and good, they would die, because they were created weak in this world, and they will not be like that on the Day of Resurrection, because on the Day of Resurrection they will be created to remain. It was also said: The meaning is, if God were to do with the people in responding to their dislike as they want to do with them in responding to their good, He would destroy them, and this is the meaning of their term would be fulfilled for them. It was also said: It is specific to the disbeliever, meaning, if God were to hasten the punishment for the disbeliever for his disbelief as He hastened for him the good of this world of wealth and children, He would hasten the fulfillment of his term for him so that he would hasten the punishment of the Hereafter, said Ibn Ishaq. Muqatil: It is the saying of Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky, for if this were to be hastened for them, they would perish. Mujahid said: It was revealed about a man who invokes God against himself, his wealth, or his children when he becomes angry: O God, destroy him, O God, do not bless him in him, and curse him, or something like that. If that were answered from him as good is answered, their time would have been cut short. So the verse was revealed to condemn a reprehensible characteristic that some people have: they supplicate for good and want to hasten the response, but sometimes their bad character leads them to supplicate for evil. If it were hastened for them, they would perish. Second: There is a difference of opinion regarding the answer to this supplication. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I asked God, the Almighty, not to answer the supplication of a lover against his beloved. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: I read in some books that God, the Almighty, says to the angels assigned to the servant: Do not write anything against My servant when he is upset, as a kindness from God, the Almighty, to him. Some of them said: That supplication may be answered, and they cited as evidence the hadith of Jabir, which Muslim narrated in his Sahih at the end of the book. Jabir said: “We went with the Messenger of God in the Battle of Batn Buwat, and he was seeking Al-Majdi bin Amr Al-Juhani, and the camel driver was following him, five, six, and seven of us. A man from the Ansar came around on his camel, so he dismounted it and mounted it. Then he sent it and it gave him a little milk, and he said to it: ‘May God curse you!’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Who is this who cursed his camel?’ He said: ‘I did, O Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘Get off it, and do not accompany us with a cursed one. Do not curse yourselves, your children, or your wealth. Do not coincide with a time when God is asked for a gift and He responds to you.’” In a book other than Muslim’s, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on a journey and a man cursed his camel. He said: Where is the one who cursed his camel? The man said: I am he, O Messenger of God. He said: Keep her away from you, for you have responded to her.” Al-Halimi mentioned it in Minhaaj ad-Din. Sha’ is narrated with a sin and a sheen, and it is a warning to a camel, meaning a secret. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And if God were to hasten it. The scholars said: Hastening is from God, and hastening is from the servant. Abu Ali said: They are both from God, and there is an omission in the speech, meaning, and if God were to hasten evil for the people, just as they hasten good, then he omitted hasten and used its description in its place, then he omitted its description and used the complement to it in its place. This is the school of thought of Al-Khalil and Sibawayh. And according to the saying of Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra’, like their hastening, then the kaf was omitted and made accusative. Al-Farra’ said: Just as you say, I hit Zayd, I hit you, meaning like you hit me. Ibn Amir read, He would have completed their term for them. It is a good reading, because it is connected to His saying: And if God were to hasten evil for the people. The Almighty said: Then warn those who do not expect the meeting with Us. That is, do not hasten evil for them, for perhaps one of them will repent, or a believer will emerge from their loins. In their transgression they wander blindly. That is, they are confused. Transgression means elevation and loftiness, and this was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. It has been said that what is meant by this verse is the people of Mecca, and that it was revealed when they said: O God, if this is the truth from You (al-Anfal 8:32), the verse, as mentioned previously, and God knows best.
10:12: The Almighty said: And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side. It was said that what is meant by man here is the disbeliever. It was said that he is Abu Hudhayfah ibn al-Mughira, the polytheist, who is afflicted with hardship, distress and effort. He calls upon Us, lying on his side means lying on his side. Or sitting or standing. Rather, He meant all of his states, because man does not go beyond one of these three states. Some of them said that He began with the one lying down because harm is most severe in most cases, so he calls upon Us more, and his effort is more intense, then the one sitting, then the one standing. But when We removed his harm from him, he passed on means he continued in his disbelief and did not give thanks or learn a lesson. I said: This is the characteristic of many of the monotheists who mix. If they are granted well-being, they continue with their sins. So the verse includes the disbeliever and others. As if he had not called us. Al-Akhfash said: It is as if the heavy as if was lightened, and the meaning is as if. And he recited: And as if he who has a lineage loves, and he who is poor lives a life of hardship. Likewise He has made beautiful meaning just as this supplication has been made beautiful during times of calamity and turning away during times of prosperity. He has made beautiful for the extravagant meaning for the polytheists their actions of disbelief and sins. This beautification may be from God, or it may be from Satan, and his misguidance is his call to disbelief.
10:13: God the Almighty says: And We have destroyed generations before you when they committed injustice meaning the past nations before the people of Mecca. We destroyed them. When they committed injustice meaning they disbelieved and associated partners with God. And their messengers came to them with clear proofs meaning with clear miracles and bright evidence. And they were not to believe meaning We destroyed them because We knew that they would not believe. The disbelievers of Mecca are frightened by the punishment of the past nations, meaning We are able to destroy these people because they denied Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, but We give them respite because We know that among them are those who believe, or that from their loins will come those who believe. This verse responds to the people of misguidance who say that guidance and faith are created. It was said: The meaning of they were not to believe is that He punished them for their disbelief by sealing their hearts, and this is indicated by His saying: Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
10:14: The Almighty said: Then We made you successors two objects. Successors is the plural of successor, and the last of the cattle has already been mentioned, meaning We made you inhabitants on the earth. After them means after the destroyed generations. La nazar is in the accusative case with the lam of ki, and its counterparts and likes have already been mentioned, meaning that what will happen from you will be what you deserve reward and punishment for, and He will never cease to know it from the unseen. It was said: He will treat you as someone who is testing, to show justice. It was said: The looking refers to the messengers, meaning that Our messengers and our friends will see how your deeds are. And how is in the accusative case with the word: you do because the question is at the beginning of the sentence, so what precedes it does not apply to it.
10:15: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And when Our verses are recited to them, recited means read, and clear is an accusative of state, meaning clear, without ambiguity or confusion. Those who do not expect to meet Us say, meaning they do not fear the Day of Resurrection and Reckoning, nor do they expect the reward. Qatada said: He means the polytheists of Mecca. Bring a Qur’an other than this or change it, and the difference between changing it and bringing something else is that changing it cannot be with it, while bringing something else may be with it. There are three aspects to their saying that: One of them is that they asked him to turn a promise into a threat and a threat into a promise, and what is permissible into what is forbidden and what is forbidden into what is permissible. This was said by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari. Second: They asked him to remove what was in the Qur’an of faults in their gods and belittling their dreams, as Ibn Issa said. Third: They asked him to omit what it contained of mentioning resurrection and revival, as Al-Zajjaj said. Second: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: It is not for me” meaning say, O Muhammad, what was mine. That I should change it of my own accord from myself, just as I do not have the right to reject it and deny it. I only follow what is revealed to me meaning I only follow what I recite to you of promise and threat, prohibition and permissibility, command and prohibition. This may be used as evidence by those who forbid the abrogation of the Book by the Sunnah, because the Almighty said: “Say: It is not for me to change it of my own accord” and this is far-fetched, because the verse was revealed regarding the polytheists’ request for a structure similar to the Qur’an, and the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not able to do that, and they did not ask him to change the ruling without the wording, and because what the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, says, if it is revelation, it is not from his own accord, but rather from God Almighty. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, meaning if I disobey Him in changing or altering Him or in abandoning working with Him. The punishment of a terrible Day, meaning the Day of Resurrection.
10:16: The Almighty said: "Say: If God had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made it known to you." That is, if God had willed, He would not have sent me to you to recite the Qur'an to you, nor would God have taught you or informed you of it. It is said: I knew something and God made me know it, and I knew it and knew it. In knowledge there is the meaning of deception, and from it I knew the man, meaning I deceived him. For this reason, the word dari is not used in reference to God Almighty, and also there is no stopping in it. Ibn Kathir read: and I would have made you know it without an alif between the lam and the hamza, and the meaning is: If He had willed, He would have made you know it without reciting it to you, so it is the lam of emphasis that entered on the alif of af'al. Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan read and I would not have made you know it by changing the ya' to an alif, in the language of Banu Uqayl. The poet said: By God, I do not fear vagrancy as long as there are Qaisis on earth driving camels. Another said: Did you not warn the people of Yamamah, Tayyi, of a war like the famous white-haired ones? Abu Hatim said: I heard Al-Asma'i say: I asked Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala: Is there any basis for reading Al-Hasan and I did not know you about it? He said: No. Abu Ubaid said: There is no basis for reading Al-Hasan and I did not know you about it except for a mistake. Al-Nahhas said: The meaning of Abu Ubaid's statement: There is no basis, God willing, is for a mistake, because it is said: Darayt means I worked, and Darayt ghayri, and it is said: Dar'at means I pushed away, so the mistake occurs between Darayt and Dar'at. Abu Hatim said: I think he meant Al-Hasan and I did not know you about it, so he replaced the Ya' with an Alif according to the language of Banu Al-Harith ibn Ka'b, they replace the Ya' with an Alif if what precedes it is a Fatha, like in the verse: Indeed, these two are magicians (Ta-Ha 20:63). Al-Mahdawi said: Whoever reads adra’tukum means that the root of the hamza is a ya’, so its root is adra’tukum and the ya’ was changed to an alif even if it was silent, as he said: yābis in yās and ta’ī in tayy, then the alif was changed to a hamza according to the language of those who say al-‘alam in al-‘alam and al-khatām in al-khatām. An-Nahhas said: This is a mistake, and the narration from Al-Hasan is walā adra’tukum with the hamza, and Abu Hatim and others said that it is without a hamza, and it is possible that it is from dar’at meaning daf’at, meaning nor did I command you to pay so that you would abandon disbelief in the Qur’an. God the Almighty said: I have remained among you a lifetime is an adverb, meaning a specified period of time, which is forty years. Before it means before the Qur’an. You know me as truthful and trustworthy. I neither read nor write, then I came to you with miracles. Do you not understand? that this can only be from God, not from me. It was said: The meaning of I have remained among you a lifetime is I have remained among you for the duration of my youth, not disobeying God. Do you want me now that I have reached forty years to disobey God’s command and change what He sends down to me? Qatada said: He remained among them for forty years, and for two years he saw the visions of the prophets. He died, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the age of sixty-two.
10:17: This is a question that means denial, i.e. who is more unjust than he who invents lies about God, changes His words, and adds something to them that He did not reveal. Likewise, no one is more unjust than you if you deny the Qur'an and invent lies about God, and say that this is not His word. This is what the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to say to them. It was said: It is from the words of God from the beginning. It was said: The infidel is the polytheist, and the one who denies the verses is the People of the Book. Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.
10:18: The Almighty said: And they worship besides God that which can neither harm them nor benefit them meaning idols. And they say, 'These are our intercessors with God' This is the height of their ignorance, as they await intercession in the end from someone who can neither benefit nor harm them at the moment. It was said: Our intercessors means intercede for us with God to improve our lives in this world. Say, 'Do you inform God of that which He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?' The general reading is tanbi'un with emphasis. Abu al-Samal al-Adawi read atnabi'un God with a lightened vowel. From anba'a yanbi'. The common reading of naba’ yanbi’ is tanbi’ah, and they have the same meaning, and they are combined in the statement of God the Almighty: “Who informed you of this? He said: The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me.” (al-Tahrim 66:3), meaning: Do you inform God that He has a partner in His kingdom or an intercessor without His permission, while God does not know of a partner for Himself in the heavens or on the earth, because He has no partner, so He does not know him. Similar to this is His statement: Or do you inform Him of that which He does not know on the earth? (Ar-Ra’d: 33) Then He purified and sanctified Himself from polytheism and said: Glory be to Him, and exalted above what they associate with Him. Meaning: He is greater than to have a partner. It was said: The meaning is that they worship that which does not hear, see, or distinguish. “And they say: These are our intercessors with God,” so they lie. And is it possible for you to inform Him of that which He does not know? Glory be to Him, and exalted be He above what they associate with Him! Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read tashirkuun with a ta’, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid, the rest with a ya’.
10:19: It was presented in the cow, so there is no point in repeating it. Al-Zajjaj said: They were the Arabs who were polytheists. It was said: Every newborn is born in a state of fitrah, but they differed upon reaching puberty. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them concerning that over which they differed referring to fate and destiny, meaning had it not been for what preceded in His ruling that He would not judge between them concerning that over which they differed with regard to reward and punishment before the Day of Resurrection, He would have judged between them in this world, so He would have admitted the believers to Paradise due to their deeds and the disbelievers to Hell due to their disbelief, but the term had preceded from God, with His knowledge of their actions, so He made their appointment the Day of Resurrection, said Al-Hasan. Abu Rawq said: It would have been judged between them to establish the Hour upon them. It was said: He would have finished destroying them. Al-Kalbi said: The word is that God delayed this nation so that He would not destroy them with punishment in this world until the Day of Resurrection, so had it not been for this delay, He would have judged between them by sending down the punishment or establishing the Hour. The verse is a consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in delaying the punishment for those who disbelieved in Him. It was said: The previous word is that He does not take anyone except with an argument, which is sending messengers, as He said: And We never punish until We have sent a messenger (al-Isra’ 17:15). It was said: The word is His statement: My mercy has preceded My wrath, and were it not for that, He would not have delayed the sinners until they repented. And Jesus read He would have judged with the opening.
10:20: The people of Mecca wanted to say, why doesn't He send down to him a sign, a miracle other than this one, so that He may turn the mountains into gold for us, and have a house of gold for him, and revive for us those of our fathers who died. Ad-Dahhak said: A staff like the staff of Moses. Say, 'The unseen belongs only to God.' That is, say, O Muhammad, that the revelation of the sign is unseen. Then wait, that is, watch. I am with you among those who wait, for its revelation. It was said: Wait for God's judgment between us to show the truthful over the false.
10:21: He means the infidels of Mecca. Mercy after a hardship that has befallen them. It was said: prosperity after hardship, and fertility after drought. Then they have a plan concerning Our signs. That is, mockery and denial. The answer to His statement: And when We make them taste, according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh. Say, God is swifter. Subject and predicate. Planning is for clarification, that is, He hastens the punishment for their plotting, that is, what comes to them of punishment is faster in destroying them than what they have done of plotting. Indeed, Our messengers write down what you plot. He means by messengers the guardians. The general reading is plotting with the ta' as an address. Ya'qub read in the narration of Ruways and Abu Amr in the narration of Harun Al-'Atki plotting with the ya', because of His statement: Then they have a plan concerning Our signs. It was said: Abu Sufyan said, We have been afflicted with drought because of your supplication, so if you give us drink, we will believe you. So they were given drink by his supplication to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but they did not believe, so this is their plotting.
10:22: The Almighty says: It is He who travels you on land and sea until, when you are in ships and they sail with them meaning, He carries you on land on beasts and in the sea on ships. Al-Kalbi said: He protects you while traveling. The verse includes an enumeration of blessings in the way people ride beasts and the sea. We have already discussed seafaring in Al-Baqarah. Yusriyyakum is the reading of the common people. Ibn Amir yansharkum with the letter noon and the letter sheen, meaning He spreads you out and disperses you. The word al-Falak is used for both singular and plural, and is masculine and feminine, and we have already discussed it. His saying: and they sail with them is a transition from addressing to absent, and it is found in the Qur'an and Arab poetry a lot. Al-Nabigha said: Oh, house of Mayya, in the high places, the Sind is strong and the past has been long upon it Ibn al-Anbari said: It is permissible in the language to return from the third-person address to the direct address. God Almighty said: “And their Lord will give them a pure drink. Indeed, this is your reward, and your effort is appreciated.” (al-Insan 76:22) So the kaf was replaced with the ha. The Almighty said: A pleasant wind, and they rejoiced in it. This was discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah. A stormy wind came upon it. The pronoun in came upon it refers to the ship. It was also said to refer to a pleasant wind. And a strong storm, it is said: the wind blew and blew, so it is stormy, stormy, and stormy, meaning strong. The poet said: Even if a disturbing wind blows in it, and its sound thunders, it roars Asif said in the masculine form because the word wind is masculine, and it is also the storm. Tayyiba is neither stormy nor slow. And the waves came upon them from every side and the wave is what rises from the water and they thought that is, they were certain that they were surrounded that is, the calamity surrounded them. It is said to someone who fell into a calamity: he has been surrounded, as if the calamity has surrounded him, and the origin of this is that if the enemy surrounds a place, its people perish. They called upon God, sincere to Him in religion that is, they called upon Him alone and left what they used to worship. This is evidence that people were created to turn to God in times of hardship, and that the call of the one in need is answered even if he is an unbeliever, because the causes have been cut off and he turns to the One, Lord of Lords, as will be explained in An-Naml, God willing. Some of the commentators said: They said in their call, Ahya Sharahiyya, meaning, O Living, O Self-Sustaining. This is the language of the Persians. Question: This verse indicates riding the sea in general, and from the Sunnah is the hadith of Abu Hurairah, which includes: We ride the sea and carry with us a little water. The hadith of Anas in the story of Umm Haram indicates the permissibility of riding it in war. This meaning has been fully discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah, praise be to God. The ruling on riding the sea when it is turbulent and boiling has been mentioned at the end of Al-A’raf. Is his ruling the same as the ruling on a healthy person or a sick person who is under quarantine? Reflect on it there. God Almighty says: If You save us from this meaning from these hardships and horrors. Al-Kalbi said: from this wind. We will surely be among the grateful meaning among those who work in Your obedience for the blessing of salvation.
10:23: When He delivered them meaning He saved them and rescued them. They were transgressing in the land without right meaning they were committing corruption and sins on the land. Transgression means corruption and polytheism, from the root word bagha which means to become corrupt, and its root is to seek, meaning they seek by arrogance and corruption. Without right meaning by lying, and from this the woman bagha means she sought someone other than her husband. God the Almighty said: O mankind, indeed your transgression is only against yourselves meaning, its consequences will return to you. The speech was completed, then He began and said: The enjoyment of worldly life meaning, it is the enjoyment of worldly life, and it will not last. An-Nahhas said: Your transgression is raised by the beginning and its predicate is the enjoyment of worldly life and against yourselves is the object of the meaning of the verb of transgression. It is possible that its predicate is against yourselves and an implied subject is implied, meaning, that is, the enjoyment of worldly life, or it is the enjoyment of worldly life, and between the two meanings is a subtle letter. If you raise enjoyment as the predicate of your transgression, then the meaning is that some of you transgressed against one another, like: So greet yourselves (al-Nur 24:61) and likewise: Indeed there has come to you a Messenger from among yourselves (al-Tawbah 9:128). If the predicate is against yourselves, then the meaning is that your corruption will return to you, like: And if you do evil, it is against you (al-Isra’ 17:7). It was narrated on the authority of Sufyan ibn Uyaynah that he said: He meant that transgression is the enjoyment of worldly life, meaning its punishment is hastened for its perpetrator in this world, as it is said: transgression is a fatal outcome. Ibn Abi Ishaq read mataa’ in the accusative case as a verbal noun, meaning you enjoy the enjoyment of worldly life. Or by removing the preposition, meaning for enjoyment, or a verbal noun, meaning the object in the state, meaning enjoying. Or it is accusative as a circumstance, meaning in the enjoyment of worldly life, and the object of the circumstance, preposition and state is the meaning of the verb in transgression. And upon yourselves is the object of that meaning.
10:24: The Almighty said: The example of the life of this world is like water which We send down from the sky. The meaning of the verse is comparison and representation, meaning the description of the life of this world in its transience, disappearance, little danger and refuge in it is like water, meaning like water, so the Kaf is in the nominative case. This comparison will be further explained in Al-Kahf, God willing. We sent it down from the sky is an adjective for water. So it mixed. It was narrated on the authority of Nafi' that he stopped at So it mixed, meaning the water mixed with the earth, then the plants of the earth began with it, meaning the plants of the earth with water, so it produced various types of plants, so it grew according to this beginning, and according to the doctrine of those who did not stop at So it mixed. It is nominative with mixed, meaning the plants mixed with the rain, meaning they drank from it and became dewy, beautiful and green. Mixing is the intermingling of one thing with another. God the Almighty said: From what people eat of grains, fruits and legumes. And livestock of pasture, straw and barley. Until the earth takes on its adornment meaning its beauty and ornamentation. Ornament is the perfection of the beauty of something, and from it gold is called zakhruf. And was adorned meaning with grains, fruits and flowers. The original form is tazaynatu. The ta’ was assimilated into the za’ and the alif of connection was used because the assimilated letter takes the place of two letters, the first of which is silent and it is not possible to begin with a silent letter. Ibn Mas’ud and Ubayy ibn Ka’b read wa tazaynatu according to the original form. Al-Hasan, Al-A’raj and Abu Al-Aaliyah read wa azaynatu meaning it brought adornment upon it, meaning the crops and plants. The verb came according to its original form, and if he had made it sound, he would have said wa zaynatu. Awf ibn Abi Jamila Al-A’rabi said: Our elders read wa zayanatu, and its weight is aswadat. In Al-Muqaddami’s narration wa zaynatu, and its original form is tazaynatu, and its weight is taqa’ast, then it was assimilated. Al-Sha’bi and Qatadah read wa zaynatu like af’alat. Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi read wazaynat like af’alat, and he also said wazayanat like af’alat, and it was narrated from him azyayant with a hamza, three readings. God the Almighty said: And its people thought meaning they were certain. That they were able to do it meaning to harvest it and benefit from it. He spoke about the land and the meaning is the plant if it is understood and it is from it. It was said: It was returned to the yield, and it was said: To the adornment. Our command came to it meaning Our punishment, or Our command to destroy it. By night or by day are two adverbs. So We made it a harvest are two objects, meaning harvested and cut off with nothing in it. He said harvested and did not feminize because it is fa’il with the meaning of maf’ul. Abu Ubaid said: The harvest is the uprooted. As if it had not flourished yesterday meaning it was not inhabited, from ghanī if he resided in it and inhabited it. Al-Maghānī in the language: the houses that people inhabit. Qatadah said: As if it had not enjoyed. Labid said: I sang a Saturday before the Dahis River, if only the stubborn soul had immortality. The general reading is taghanna with a ta to feminize the earth. Qatada read yaghnan with a ya, referring to the ornament, meaning just as this crop perishes, so does the world. We explain the verses means we clarify them for a people who reflect on the verses of God.
10:25: The Almighty said: "And God invites to the abode of peace" When He mentioned the description of this abode, which is the abode of this world and the description of the Hereafter, He said: Indeed, God does not invite you to the accumulation of this world, but rather He invites you to obedience so that you may reach the abode of peace, meaning Paradise. Qatada and Al-Hasan said: Peace is God and the abode of Paradise, and Paradise was called the abode of peace because whoever enters it is safe from harm. And among His names, glory be to Him, is Peace, and we have explained it in The Most Sublime Book in Explaining the Beautiful Names of God. And it will come in Surat Al-Hashr, God willing. And it was said: The meaning is that God invites to the abode of safety. And peace and safety have the same meaning as breastfeeding and suckling, as Al-Zajjaj said. The poet said: Greetings, Umm Bakr. Do you have any peace after your people? It was said: He meant that God calls to the abode of greeting, because its people receive greetings and peace from God, as well as from the angels. Al-Hasan said: Peace is never cut off from the people of Paradise, and it is their greeting, as He said: “And their greeting therein is peace.” Yahya bin Muadh said: O son of Adam, God has called you to the abode of peace, so look from where you respond to Him, for if you respond to Him from your worldly life, you will enter it, and if you respond to Him from your grave, you will be denied it. Ibn Abbas said: Paradise is seven: the abode of glory, the abode of peace, the Garden of Eden, the Garden of Refuge, the Garden of Eternity, the Garden of Paradise, and the Garden of Bliss. The Almighty’s saying: And He guides whom He wills to a straight path. He included the call in order to demonstrate His proof, and He specified guidance in order to be independent of His creation. The straight path, it was said, is the Book of God. It was narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The straight path is the Book of God Almighty. It was said: Islam, narrated by Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: The truth, said by Qatada and Mujahid. It was also said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his two companions after him, Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them. Jabir bin Abdullah narrated: “One day, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and said, ‘I saw in a dream that Gabriel was at my head and Michael was at my feet.’ One of them said to the other, ‘Give him an example.’ He said to him, ‘Listen, your ears have heard and understand, your heart understands. Your example and that of your nation is like that of a king who took a house, built a house in it, held a banquet in it, then sent a messenger inviting people to his food. Some of them responded to the messenger and some of them left him. So God is the King, the house is Islam, the house is Paradise, and you, O Muhammad, are the Messenger. Whoever responds to you enters Islam, and whoever enters Islam enters Paradise, and whoever enters Paradise eats from what is in it.’” Then he recited, meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, And guides whom He wills to a straight path. Then Qatada and Mujahid recited, “And God invites to the abode of peace.” This verse is a clear argument in refuting the Qadarites, because they said, ‘God has guided all of creation to a straight path,’ and God said, ‘And guides whom He wills to a straight path.’ So they rejected the texts of the Qur’an against God.
10:26: The Almighty said: For those who do good is the best and more. It was narrated from the hadith of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the words of God the Almighty: And an addition. He said: For those who do good deeds in this world will have the best, which is Paradise, and an addition is the sight of the Noble Face of God. This is the saying of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Ali ibn Abi Talib in one narration, and Hudhayfah, Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Ka’b ibn Ujrah, Abu Musa, Suhayb and Ibn Abbas in one narration, and it is the saying of a group of the Followers, and it is the correct view on this topic. Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Suhayb on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, God Almighty will say: Do you want something more? They will say: Did You not make our faces white? Did You not admit us into Paradise and save us from the Fire? He will say: Then the veil will be lifted, and they will not be given anything more beloved to them than looking at their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. And in another narration, then he recited: For those who do good is the best and more.” An-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Suhaib, who said: It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: This verse: For those who do good is the best and more. He said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, a caller will call out: O people of Paradise, you have an appointment with God that He wants to fulfill for you. They will say: Have You not made our faces white and our scales heavy and saved us from the Fire? He will say: “Then the veil will be lifted and they will look at Him. By God, He has not given them anything more beloved to them than looking at Him, nor anything more soothing to their eyes.” Ibn al-Mubarak included it in his Raqa’iq on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, as a chain of transmission ending with him. We have mentioned it in the Book of Remembrance. We mentioned there the meaning of lifting the veil, and praise be to God. At-Tirmidhi al-Hakim Abu Abdullah, may God have mercy on him, included it: Ali ibn Hajar told us, al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Abu al-A’aliyah, on the authority of Abu ibn Ka’b, who said: “I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the two additions in the Book of God, in His statement: “For those who do good is the best and more,” he said: Looking at the face of the Most Gracious, and about His statement: And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more (37:147) he said: Twenty thousand.” It has been said that the addition is that the good deed is multiplied by ten good deeds or more than that, as narrated from Ibn Abbas. It was narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: The addition is a room made of a single pearl with four thousand doors. Mujahid said: The best is a good deed like a good deed, and the addition is forgiveness from God and His pleasure. Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: The best is Paradise, and the addition is what God gave them in this world from His grace, for which He will not hold them accountable on the Day of Resurrection. Abdur-Rahman ibn Sabit said: The best is good report, and the addition is looking at the face of God the Generous, God the Most High said: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord (37:22-23). Yazid bin Shajarah said: The increase is that the cloud passes by the people of Paradise and rains upon them all the rare things that they have not seen, and says: O people of Paradise, what do you want me to rain upon you? They do not want anything except that it rains upon them. It was said: The increase is that not even the length of a day of the days of this world passes by them except that seventy thousand angels surround the home of one of them, with each angel gifts from God that are not with his companion. They have never seen the likes of those gifts. So glory be to the Vast, the All-Knowing, the Rich, the Praiseworthy, the Most High, the Great, the Mighty, the Powerful, the Righteous, the Merciful, the Planner, the Wise, the Kind, the Generous, Whose powers are limitless. It was said: Treat people well, and the good is their intercession, and the increase is God’s permission and acceptance of it. The Almighty said: nor does it overwhelm. It was said that its meaning is to catch up, and from this it was said: a teenage boy if he catches up with the men. It was also said: to rise. It was also said: to cover, and the meanings are close. Qatar is dust. Nor humiliation means disgrace, as the people of Hell will catch up with, meaning that dust will not catch up with them when they are gathered before God, nor will humiliation cover them. Abu Ubaidah recited for Al-Farazdaq: Crowned with the king's robe, followed by waves above which you can see the banners and the qitra Al-Hasan read qatr with a sukoon on the ta’. Al-Qatar, Al-Qatrah and Al-Qatrah have the same meaning, as Al-Nahhas said. The singular of qatr is qatra, and from this comes the saying of God the Almighty: A darkness will cover it (Abasa 80:41), meaning it will be covered by dust. It was also said: qatr means depression and eclipse. Ibn Abbas: qatr means the blackness of faces. Ibn Bahr: smoke of fire, and from this comes qatar al-qadr. Ibn Abi Layla said: it is the distance of their sight of their Lord, the Almighty and Majestic. I said: This is questionable, because God the Almighty says: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it - until His saying - The greatest terror will not grieve them (al-Anbiya 21:101-103) and He said in more than one verse: And there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve (al-Baqarah 2:62) and He said: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God’ and then remain on a right course - the angels will descend upon them, [saying], ‘Do not fear and do not grieve’ (Fussilat 41:30) and the verse.
