This is general, because by the grace of God, the face of the doer of good will not change in any place, neither before nor after the vision, to blackness from gloom or sadness, nor will any of the smoke of Hell or anything else rise above it. But as for those whose faces will turn white, they will be in the mercy of God; they will abide therein eternally (Al Imran 3:107).
10:27: The Almighty said: And those who have earned evil deeds meaning they have committed sins. It was also said: polytheism. The recompense of an evil deed is its like recompense is raised by the subject, and its predicate is its like. Ibn Kaysan said: The ba' is redundant, and the meaning is the recompense of an evil deed is its like. It was also said: The ba' with what follows it is the predicate, and it is related to an omitted word that it takes its place, and the meaning is: the recompense of an evil deed is its like, like your saying: I am only with you, meaning I am only with you. It is permissible for it to be related to recompense, the estimation: the recompense of an evil deed is its like, so the predicate of the subject was omitted. It is permissible for recompense to be raised on the estimation of they will have the recompense of an evil deed, so it would be like His saying: Then a number of other days (al-Baqarah 2:184) meaning they will have a number, and the like, and the ba' in this estimation is related to an omitted word, as if he said to them the recompense of an evil deed is established by its like, or it could be emphatic or redundant. The meaning of this likeness is that this punishment is similar to their sins, i.e. they are not wronged, and the action of the Lord - may His power and glory be exalted - is not justified by a cause. And humiliation will overwhelm them i.e. Hawazin and Khazin will overwhelm them. They will have no protector from God i.e. from the punishment of God. No protector i.e. anyone who can prevent them from it. As if I had covered i.e. been clothed. Their faces were covered in pieces plural of piece, and based on this, dark is a state of the night, i.e. their faces were covered in pieces of the night when it was dark. Al-Kisa’i and Ibn Kathir read cutting with a sukoon on the ta’, so dark is a description based on this, and it is possible that it is a state of the night. Cutting is the name of what was cut off and then dropped. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: Cutting is a section of the night, and this will come in Hud, God willing.
10:28: The Almighty said: And the Day We shall gather them together meaning We shall assemble them, and gathering is the plural. All together is a state. Then We shall say to those who associated others with God meaning they took a partner with God. Your place meaning stick to it and remain in your place, stop where you are. You and your partners and this is a threat. Then We shall remove from them meaning We shall separate and cut off the communication that was between them in this world. It is said: I removed it so it is removed, meaning I separated it so it was separated, and it is the verb fa'ala because you say in its source tazeeelan, and if it were not fa'alat you would have said zaylaan. And zayala is separation. It is said: God removed it muzayala and ziyalan if He left him. And zayala is contrast. Al-Farra' said: Some of them read fazayala among them, it is said: I will not remove so-and-so, meaning I will not separate from him. If you say: I will not separate him, then it has another meaning, meaning I will not associate with him. And their partners said he meant by partners the angels. It was said: The devils, and it was said: The idols, so God Almighty makes them speak and this dialogue takes place between them. That is because they claimed that the devils whom they obeyed and the idols whom they worshipped ordered them to worship them and they said: We did not worship you until you ordered us. Mujahid said: God makes the idols speak and they say: We did not know that you worshipped us, and we did not order you to worship us. If the partners are attributed to the devils, then the meaning is that they say that out of astonishment, or they say it as a lie and a trick to escape, and this was exemplified tomorrow, even though knowledge has become necessary.
10:29: The Almighty says: Then sufficient is God as a witness between us and you. Witness is the object, meaning God is sufficient as a witness, or distinction, meaning He is sufficient as a witness between us and you if we have commanded you to do this or were pleased with it from you. If we were meaning we were unaware of your worship except that we were unaware, neither hearing nor seeing nor understanding, because we were inanimate and had no soul within us.
10:30: The Almighty said: There is in the accusative case as an adverb. Tablawu means at that time. Tabalu means taste. Al-Kalbi said: Learn. Mujahid: Test. Every soul shall have what it has sent forth meaning the reward for what it has done and presented. It was also said: Tasallam, meaning it hands over what it owes of rights to its owners without its choosing. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read tatlu, meaning every soul reads its book that was written for it. It was also said: Tatlu follows, meaning every soul follows what it has sent forth in this world, as Al-Suddi said. And from this is the saying of the poet: The suspicious follows the suspicious, just as you have seen a wolf following a wolf. God the Almighty said: And they will be returned to God, their true Master in the accusative case as a substitute or description. It is permissible to put the truth in the accusative case in three ways. The meaning would be: And they will be returned truly, then the definite article was brought. It is permissible to put their true Master not what they worship besides Him. The third way is to be praise, i.e. I mean the truth. It is permissible to raise the truth, and the meaning would be their true Master - as a subject and predicate, and a break from what came before - not what they associate with Him. And He described Himself, glory be to Him, with the truth because the truth is from Him, just as He described Himself with justice because justice is from Him, i.e. all justice and truth are from before Him. Ibn Abbas said: Their true Master means the one who rewards them with the truth. And lost from them means invalidated. What they used to invent invents in the nominative case and it means the source, i.e. their invention. If it is said: How did He say And they will be returned to God, their true Master when He informed us that the disbelievers have no Master? It is said: He is not their Master in victory and assistance, but He is their Master in provision and the abundance of blessings.
10:31: The purpose of this speech is to respond to the polytheists and establish the proof against them. Whoever among them acknowledges it, the proof is clear to them, and whoever does not acknowledge it, it is established against him that these heavens and earth must have a Creator, and no rational person would dispute this. This is close to the level of necessity. From the sky meaning by the rain. And the earth by the plants. Who owns hearing and sight meaning who made them and created them for you. And who brings forth the living from the dead meaning the plant from the earth, and man from the sperm, and the ear of corn from the grain, and the bird from the egg, and the believer from the disbeliever. And who manages the affair meaning determines and decrees it. They will say, ‘God’ because they believed that the Creator is God, or they will say, ‘God’ if they think and are fair. Then say to them, O Muhammad, Do you not fear God? meaning do you not fear His punishment and vengeance in this world and the Hereafter.
10:32: The Almighty’s saying: “That is God, your Lord, the Truth. So what is there after the truth except error?” There are eight issues in it: First: The Almighty’s saying: That is God, your true Lord meaning, this One who does these things is your true Lord, not what you associate with Him. What comes after the truth is related, meaning, what comes after worshipping the true God, God, is misguidance, because the beginning of it is That is God, your true Lord and the end of it is What comes after the truth except misguidance? This is in faith and disbelief, not in deeds. Some of them said: Disbelief is covering up the truth, and everything other than the truth follows this path, so what is forbidden is misguidance and what is permissible is guidance, because God is the One who permits and forbids. The first is correct, because before it is Say, ‘Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?’ then He said: That is God, your true Lord meaning, this is the One who provided for you, and all of this is His doing. Your true Lord meaning, the One to whom divinity is due and who deserves worship, and if that is the case, then associating others with Him is misguidance and not right. Second: Our scholars said: This verse ruled that there is no third position between truth and falsehood in this issue, which is the monotheism of God Almighty, and the same is the case in its counterparts, which are the fundamental issues in which the truth is one party, because the discussion in them is only about the enumeration of the existence of an entity and how it is, and that is in contrast to the issues of branches in which God Almighty said: For each of you We prescribed a law and a method (al-Ma’idah 5:48), and his saying, peace be upon him: What is lawful is clear and what is unlawful is clear, and between them are matters of similarity. Discussion of branches is only about rulings that arise from the existence of an established entity in which there is no difference, but rather the difference is in the rulings related to it. Third: It was proven on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up to pray in the middle of the night, he would say: O God, to You is all praise is the hadith. And in it is “You are the Truth, Your promise is the Truth, Your word is the Truth, and meeting You is the Truth, Paradise is the Truth, Hell is the Truth, the Hour is the Truth, the Prophets are the Truth, and Muhammad is the Truth” is the hadith. So his saying: You are the Truth means the Necessary Existent, and its origin is from the truth of something, meaning it is established and necessary. This description of God the Most High is true, since His existence for Himself was not preceded by nonexistence, nor is nonexistence attached to it. And what is other than Him of which this name is said is preceded by nonexistence, and it is permissible for it to be attached to nonexistence, and its existence is from its Creator, not from itself. And considering this meaning, the most truthful word spoken by the poet was the word of Labid: Everything except God is false This is indicated by the Almighty’s saying: “Everything will perish except His Face. To Him belongs all judgement, and to Him you will be returned.” (al-Qasas
10:33: The Almighty said: Thus has the word of your Lord come into effect meaning His judgment, decree, and previous knowledge. Upon those who disobey meaning they disbelieved and lied. That they will not believe meaning they will not believe. This is the most complete evidence of Qadariyah. Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read here and at the end of it Thus has the word of your Lord come into effect and in Surah Ghafir in the plural in all three. The rest read it in the singular and that is in the accusative case, meaning that they or because they. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a substitute for words. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for it to be in the kasra as a new sentence.
10:34: The Almighty said: “Say: Is there among your partners” meaning your gods and objects of worship one who initiates creation and then repeats it meaning, say to them, O Muhammad, that as a way of rebuke and confirmation. If they answer you, then fine, otherwise “Say: God initiates creation and then repeats it” and no one else does that. Then how are you deluded? meaning, how do you turn and turn away from the truth to falsehood?
10:35: The Almighty says: "Say: Is there among your partners any who guides to the truth?" It is said: He guided him to the path and to the path have the same meaning, and it has been mentioned before. That is, is there among your partners any who guides to the religion of Islam? If they say no and there is no alternative to it, then say to them: God guides to the truth. Then say to them, rebuking and reassuring them: Is he who guides? That is, guides. to the truth? And He is God, the Most High. More deserving to be followed than he who guides not unless he is guided. He means the idols that do not guide anyone, and do not walk unless they are carried, and do not move from their place unless they are moved. The poet said: A boy has a mind that lives where his leg guides his foot. It was said: What is meant are the leaders and the misguiders who do not guide themselves to guidance unless they are guided. And he guides to six readings: First: The people of Medina, except Warsh, read yahdi with a fatha on the ya’, a sukoon on the ha’, and a shaddah on the dal. They combined two sukoon letters in their reading, as they did in His statement, La ‘addu Do not add and in His statement, Yakhasamoon They will deduct (Ya-Sin 36:49). An-Nahhas said: No one can pronounce combining two sukoon letters. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: Whoever seeks something like this must move a light movement to a kasra, and Sibawayh calls this stealing a movement. Second: Abu Amr and Qalun read in a narration between the opening and the sukoon, according to his doctrine of concealment and embezzlement. Third: Ibn Amir, Ibn Kathir, Warsh and Ibn Muhaisin read yahdi with the opening of the ya and ha and the shaddah of the dal. An-Nahhas said: This reading is clear in Arabic, and the original in it is yahtadi, the ta was assimilated into the dal and its vowel was changed to the ha. Fourth: Hafs, Yaqub, and Al-A’mash read on the authority of Abu Bakr like the reading of Ibn Kathir, except that they broke the ha’. They said: Because if the Jazm is forced to move it, it is moved to the kasra. Abu Hatim said: It is the language of the lower Mudar. Fifth: Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim yahudi with a kasra on the ya’ and the ha’ and a shaddah on the dal, all of that is because the kasra follows the kasra as mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah in yakhtafi (al-Baqarah 2:20). It was said: It is the language of those who read nasta’in and lan tamsana al-nar (Al Imran 3:24) and the like. Sibawayh does not permit yahudi but permits tahdi and nahdi and ihdi and he said: Because the kasra on the ya’ is heavy. Sixth: Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Khalaf, Yahya bin Waththab, and Al-A’mash read yahudi with a fatha on the ya’, a sukoon on the ha’, and a soft dal, from hada yahudi. An-Nahhas said: This reading has two faces in Arabic, even though it is far-fetched. One of the two faces is that Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said: yahudi means yahtadi. Abu Al-Abbas said: This is not known, but the meaning is amman la yahudi ghayruhu, the speech is complete. Then he said: Except that he is guided, he resumed from the beginning, meaning, but he needs to be guided, so it is a discontinuous exception, just as you say: So-and-so does not hear others except that he hears,... hear. Abu Ishaq said: So what is the matter with you? is a complete statement, and the meaning is: So what do you have to do with worshipping idols? Then it was said to them: How do you judge meaning for yourselves and decide with this blatant falsehood, worshipping gods who do not benefit themselves in anything except that something is done to them, and God does what He wills, so you abandon His worship, so the place of how is the subject of you judge.
10:36: The Almighty says: And most of them follow nothing but conjecture meaning the leaders among them, meaning they follow nothing but guesswork and conjecture that they are gods and that they intercede, and they have no proof with them. As for their followers, they follow them out of imitation. Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth meaning against the punishment of God, for the truth is God. It was said that the truth here is certainty, meaning conjecture is not like certainty. And in this verse is evidence that conjecture is not sufficient in matters of belief. Indeed, God is Knowing of what they do of disbelief and denial, it was presented in the form of a threat.
10:37: The Almighty said: And this Qur'an could not have been invented by other than God. "An with Yaftara" is a source, and the meaning is: And this Qur'an could not have been invented, as you say: So-and-so loves to ride, meaning he loves to ride, as Al-Kisa'i said. Al-Farra' said: The meaning is: And this Qur'an should not have been invented, as in His saying: "And it is not for a prophet to take spoils" (Al Imran 3:161), "And it is not for the believers to go forth all together" (al-Tawbah 9:122). It was said: "An has the meaning of Lam", meaning: And this Qur'an could not have been invented. It was also said: It has the meaning of "No", meaning it is not invented. It was also said: The meaning is: It was not possible for anyone to come with the like of this Qur'an from other than God and then attribute it to God Almighty for its miraculousness, description, meanings, and composition. "But a confirmation of what was before it" Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farra', and Muhammad ibn Sa'dan said: The meaning is: But it was a confirmation, and they allow the nominative case to mean: But it is a confirmation. "Which was before it" meaning from the Torah, the Gospel, and other books, for they had been given glad tidings of it, so it came to confirm it in that glad tidings, and in the call to monotheism and belief in the Resurrection. It was said: The meaning is but the confirmation of the Prophet who was before the Qur’an, which is Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, because they saw him before they heard the Qur’an from him. And the explanation is in the accusative and nominative cases in the two ways mentioned in confirmation. And the explanation is clarification, meaning it clarifies what is in the previous books of God. And the book is the generic name. And it was said: What he meant by the explanation of the book is what is explained in the Qur’an of rulings. "There is no doubt in it" the ha’ refers back to the Qur’an, meaning there is no doubt in it, that is, in its revelation from God Almighty.
10:38: The Almighty said: Or do they say, 'He has invented it'? Am here is in the place of the interrogative alif because it is connected to what precedes it. It was said: It is the disconnected Am that is estimated to mean but and the hamza, like the Almighty's saying: "Alif, Lam, Meem. The revelation of the Book, about which there is no doubt, is from the Lord of the worlds. Or do they say, 'He has invented it'?" (al-Sajdah 32:1-3) meaning, rather, do they say, 'He has invented it'? Abu Ubaidah said: Am has the meaning of waw, and its metaphor is: And they say, 'He has invented it'. It was said: The meem is a connection, and the meaning is: Do they say, 'He has invented it'? That is, Muhammad invented the Qur'an on his own, so it is an interrogative meaning a rebuke. Say, 'Bring a surah like it' The meaning of the statement is an argument, for the first verse indicated that the Qur'an is from God, because it confirms the books that came before it and agrees with them without Muhammad, peace be upon him, learning from anyone. This verse obligates them to bring a surah like it if it was invented. The miracle of the Qur’an was mentioned in the introduction to the book, and praise be to God.
10:39: God the Almighty said: Rather, they denied that of which they had no knowledge. That is, they denied the Qur'an while they were ignorant of its meanings and interpretation, and they must know that by asking, so this indicates that the interpretation must be looked into. And His statement: And its interpretation has not yet come to them means, and the true consequence of the denial of the punishment that will descend upon them has not yet come to them. Or they denied what is in the Qur'an of the mention of resurrection, Paradise, and Hell, and its interpretation has not come to them, meaning the true nature of what they were promised in the Book, as Ad-Dahhak said. And it was said to Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl: Do you find in the Qur'an Whoever is ignorant of a thing opposes it? He said yes, in two places: Rather, they denied that of which they had no knowledge. And His statement: And when they are not guided by it, they will say, 'This is an ancient falsehood.' (al-Ahqaf 46:11). Thus did those before them deny means the nations that had passed away, meaning that was their way. And the kaf is in the accusative case. Then see how was the end of the wrongdoers, meaning that they were subjected to destruction and torment.
10:40: The Almighty said: And among them are those who believe in it. It was said: What is meant are the people of Mecca, meaning that among them are those who believe in it in the future, even if they have denied it for a long time, because of His previous knowledge of them that they are among the fortunate. Man is raised by the subject and the predicate is in the genitive case. And so on. And among them are those who do not believe in it. The meaning is that among them are those who persist in their disbelief until they die, like Abu Talib and Abu Lahab and the like. It was said: What is meant are the People of the Book. It was said: It is general for all disbelievers, and this is correct. It was said: The pronoun in bih refers to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God Almighty informed that He only delayed the punishment because among them are those who will believe. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters, meaning those who persist in their disbelief, and this is a threat to them.
10:41: The Almighty said: And if they deny you, then say, 'To me is my work.' The subject is raised, and the meaning is: To me is the reward for my work in conveying, warning, and obeying God the Almighty. And to you is your work, meaning its reward from polytheism. You are innocent of what I do, and I am innocent of what you do, similarly, meaning no one will be held accountable for the sin of another. This verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword, according to Mujahid, Al-Kalbi, Muqatil, and Ibn Zayd.
10:42: The Almighty says: And among them are those who listen to you meaning with their outward appearances, and their hearts do not comprehend anything of what he says of the truth and recites from the Qur’an. For this reason, He said: Then can you make the deaf hear even if they do not understand? meaning you do not hear, so its outward appearance is a question but its meaning is negation, and He made them like the deaf because of the seal on their hearts and the imprint on them, meaning you are not able to guide those whom God has made deaf from hearing guidance.
10:43: And the same meaning is in: "And among them are those who look at you. Can you guide the blind even though they do not see?" God the Almighty informed us that no one believes except through His guidance and success. This and what is similar to it was a response to the Qadarites' statement, as mentioned earlier in more than one place. He said: They listen in the sense of who and looks in the wording, and what is meant is to console the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, that is, just as you cannot make someone who has been deprived of hearing hear, nor can you create for the blind sight by which he can be guided, so too you cannot guide these people to faith, and God has decreed that they will not believe. The meaning of looks at you is that he keeps looking at you, as He said: They look at you, their eyes rolling like one who is in a faint from death (al-Ahzab 33:19). It was said that it was revealed about the mockers, and God knows best.
10:44: When he mentioned the people of misery, he mentioned that he did not wrong them, and that the decree of misery upon them and the deprivation of the heart's hearing and sight is not injustice from him, because he disposed of his kingdom as he wished, and he is just in all his actions. But people wrong themselves by disbelief, disobedience, and disobeying the command of their Creator. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read but with a lightened people in the nominative case. An-Nahhas said: A group of grammarians, including Al-Farra', claimed that when the Arabs say but with a waw, they prefer to emphasize it, and if they delete the waw, they prefer to lighten it. He argued for that and said: Because if it is without a waw, it resembles bal, so they lightened it so that what comes after it is like after bal. And if they use a waw, it differs from bal, so they stress it and put it in the accusative case, because if a lam and a kaf are added to it, it becomes one letter. And he recited: But I love her for the dean So he used the letter lam because it is in.
10:45: The Almighty said: And on the Day He will gather them as if they had not remained meaning as if they had not remained in their graves. Except for an hour of the day meaning about an hour, meaning that they considered the length of their stay in the graves short due to the horror of what they would see of the resurrection, as evidenced by their saying: We remained a day or part of a day (al-Kahf 18:19). It was said: The length of their stay in this world was shortened due to the horror of what they would face, not the length of their time in the grave. Ibn Abbas said: They saw that the length of their lives in comparison to eternity was like an hour. They will recognize one another is in the accusative case as a state of the ha' and mim in He will gather them. It is permissible for it to be disconnected, as if he said, They will recognize one another. Al-Kalbi said: They will know each other as they knew each other in this world when they emerge from their graves. This acquaintance is an acquaintance of reproach and disgrace. Some of them will say to each other: You led me astray, seduced me, and led me to disbelief. It is not an acquaintance of compassion, mercy, and sympathy. Then the acquaintance will be cut off when they witness the horrors of the Day of Resurrection, as God says: And no intimate friend will ask another intimate friend (al-Ma’arij 70:10). It was said: The acquaintance of reproach will remain, and this is correct, because God the Almighty says: And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are made to stand - to His saying - And We have put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved (Saba’: 33) and His saying: Whenever a nation enters, it curses its sister (al-A’raf 7:38) and His saying: Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries (al-Ahzab 33:67) and the verse. As for his statement: And no intimate friend will ask about his intimate friend, and his statement: So when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship between them (al-Mu’minun 23:101), its meaning is that he will not ask him a question of mercy and compassion, and God knows best. It was said: The Day of Resurrection is the place of resurrection. It was also said: The meaning of they will know each other is they will ask each other how long you stayed, as He said: And they will turn to each other, asking each other (al-Saffat 37:27). This is good. Ad-Dahhak said: That is the acquaintance and compassion of the believers, and there will be no compassion for the disbelievers, as He said: they will have no kinship between them. The first is more apparent, and God knows best. The Almighty said: Those who deny the meeting with God have certainly lost out. That is, the presentation to God. Then it was said: It is possible that this is information from God, the Almighty, after He indicated the resurrection and revival, that is, they lost the reward of Paradise. And it was said: They lost out in the state of meeting God, because loss is only in that state in which there is no hope of forgiveness and no repentance is of any benefit. An-Nahhas said: It is possible that the meaning is that they get to know each other, they say this. And they were not guided, meaning in the knowledge of God.
10:46: The Almighty said: And if We show you is a condition. Some of what We promise them meaning of showing your religion during your life. The commentators said: The part that We promised them was killing those who were killed and taking captive those who were taken captive at Badr. Or We cause you to die is in apposition to We show you meaning We cause you to die before that. Then to Us is their return is the answer to either. What is meant is that if We do not take revenge on them soon, We will take revenge on them later. Then God is Witness meaning a witness who does not need a witness. Of what they do of fighting you and denying you. If it was said: Then God is Witness meaning there, it would be permissible.
10:47: And for every nation is a messenger, so when their messenger comes, the matter will be judged between them with justice. The meaning is: For every nation is a messenger who is a witness over them, so when their messenger comes on the Day of Resurrection, the matter will be judged between them, like: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness? (al-Nisa 4:41). Ibn Abbas said: The disbelievers will deny tomorrow that the messengers have come to them, so the messenger will be brought and say: I have conveyed the message to you, and then the punishment will be decreed against them. The evidence for this is the statement of: And the Messenger will be a witness over you. (al-Baqarah 2:143). It is possible that the meaning is that they will not be punished in this world until a messenger is sent to them, so whoever believes will succeed and be saved, and whoever does not believe will perish and be punished. The evidence for this is the statement of God the Almighty: And We never punish until We have sent a messenger. (al-Isra’ 17:15). Justice means fairness. And they will not be wronged meaning they will not be punished without sin and they will not be held accountable without proof.
10:48: The infidels of Mecca, due to their extreme denial and hastening of the punishment, mean when will be the punishment or when will be the resurrection that Muhammad promises us. It was said: It is general for every nation that denied its Messenger.
10:49: God the Almighty said: "Say: I do not possess for myself any harm or benefit." When they hastened the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) with the punishment, God said to him: Say to them, O Muhammad, I do not possess any harm or benefit for myself, meaning that is not for me or for anyone else. Except what God wills that I possess and have power over, so how can I possess what you have hastened? Do not hasten. For every nation there is a term meaning their destruction and punishment have a known time in His knowledge, glory be to Him. When their term comes meaning the time of the expiration of their term. They will not delay an hour nor will they advance it meaning they cannot delay an hour while remaining in this world nor advance it so that they are delayed.
10:50: The Almighty's saying: "Say: Have you considered: if His punishment should come upon you at night or during the day?" are two circumstances, and it is an answer to their saying: When is this promise? and a dispelling of their opinions in hastening the punishment, meaning if the punishment comes upon you, what benefit will it bring you, and faith will not benefit you then. What are the criminals hastening from it? is a question that means intimidation and glorification, meaning how great is what they are hastening for, as it is said to someone who seeks something whose consequences he finds unpleasant: What are you bringing upon yourself! The pronoun in from it is said to refer to the punishment, and it is said to refer to God, the Most High. An-Nahhas said: If you make the ha in from it refer to the punishment, then you have two interpretations for what: One of them is that what is in the nominative case as the subject, and that means which, and it is the predicate of what and the pronoun is omitted. Another estimation is that what is one name in the nominative case as a subject, and the predicate is in the sentence. Al-Zajjaj said: If you make the ha’ in from it refer to the name of God Almighty, you make what and that one thing, and it is in the accusative case of Al-Bukhari’s he hastens, and the meaning is: what thing do the criminals hasten from God Almighty?
10:51: The Almighty said: Then when it comes, will you believe in it now? There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: Do you feel secure that the punishment will not descend upon you and then it will be said to you when it comes: Now have you believed in it? It was said: It is from the words of the angels mocking them. It was said: It is from the words of God Almighty, and the interrogative alif was added to then, and the meaning is: confirmation and rebuke, and to indicate that the meaning of the second sentence comes after the first. It was said: That then here means: then with the opening of the tha, so it is an adverb, and the meaning is: is there, and this is the doctrine of al-Tabari, and then it does not have the meaning of interrogation. Now it was said: Its origin is a verb built like haan, and the alif and lam to transform it into a noun. Al-Khalil: It was built for the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the alif and lam are for the covenant and the indication of the time, and it is the limit of two times. And you were hastening it meaning the punishment.
10:52: God Almighty says: Then it will be said to those who did wrong, meaning the keepers of Hell will say to them, Taste the eternal punishment, meaning that which will never end. Are you recompensed except for what you used to earn? meaning the recompense for your disbelief.
10:53: The Almighty said: And they ask you meaning they ask you, O Muhammad, about the punishment and the coming of the Hour. More deserving is the subject. He as-Suddi replaces the predicate, and this is the opinion of Sibawayh. It is possible that He is the subject, and more deserving is its predicate. "Say: Yes" is a word of confirmation, affirmation, and confirmation meaning yes. And my Lord is an oath. Indeed, it is the truth is its answer, meaning it will happen without doubt. And you will not escape meaning you will not escape His punishment and recompense.
10:54: The Almighty said: And if every soul that has wronged that is, associated partners with God and disbelieved, had whatever is on the earth that is, a kingdom. It would ransom itself with it that is, from the punishment of God, meaning it would not be accepted from it, as He said: Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - never will the earth full of gold be accepted from one of them, even if he were to ransom himself with it (Al Imran 3:91). And it has been mentioned before. God the Almighty said: And they concealed their regret meaning they hid it, meaning their leaders, meaning they concealed their regret from their followers. When they saw the punishment This was before the burning in the fire, so when they fell into the fire, the fire distracted them from pretending, as evidenced by their saying: Our Lord, our misery has overcome us (al-Mu’minun 23:106). So it is clear that they do not hide what is in them. It was said: they concealed it, and the word is from opposites, and it is indicated by the fact that the Hereafter is not a place of sternness and patience. It was said: they found the pain of regret in their hearts, because regret cannot be revealed. Katheer said: So I felt remorse when the caller called for the cold beauty of Ghadir Al-Mubarrad mentioned a third aspect: that their faces showed signs of regret, which are wrinkles on the forehead, and the singular is sirar. Regret is sorrow for the occurrence of something or the loss of something, and its origin is adherence, and from it comes the companion because he adheres to gatherings. So-and-so is regretful and remorseful. Sadm is the obsession with something. To regret and regret something means to be concerned about it. Al-Jawhari said: Sadm with a fat-ha is regret and sadness, and sadm with kasra means to be concerned and sad, and a regretful man is sadm, and two regretful ones are two sadmans, and it was said: it is following. And he has no worries or sadm except that. It was said: Regret is the reverse of dung, and dung is adherence, and from it comes someone who is addicted to alcohol. Damn is what accumulates in the house and clumps in urine and dung, it was named thus for its adherence. Damnah: the hatred that adheres to the chest, and the plural is daman. Their hearts were damant with kasra, it is said: I harbored a grudge against so-and-so, meaning I held a grudge. And it was judged between them with justice meaning between the leaders and the lower ones with fairness. And they will not be wronged.
10:55: Is there not a word of warning to the listener that is added at the beginning of the speech, that is, pay attention to what I am saying to you: “Indeed, to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Unquestionably, the promise of God is truth.” To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no obstacle that prevents Him from fulfilling what He promised. But most of them do not know. That.
10:56: God Almighty says: It is He who gives life and causes death, and to Him you will be returned. Between the meaning, and it has been presented.
10:57: The Almighty says: O mankind meaning Quraysh. There has come to you instruction meaning admonition. From your Lord meaning the Qur'an, which contains admonitions and wisdom. And healing for what is in the hearts meaning doubt, hypocrisy, disagreement and discord. And guidance meaning right direction for those who follow it. And mercy meaning blessing, for the believers He singled them out because they are the ones who benefit from faith, and all are attributes of the Qur'an, and the conjunction is to emphasize the praise. The poet said: To the venerable king, the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded place
10:58: God the Almighty said: "Say: By the grace of God and His mercy." Abu Saeed Al-Khudri and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, said: God's grace is the Qur'an, and His mercy is Islam. And it was also narrated from them: God's grace is the Qur'an, and His mercy is that He made you among its people. And from Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid, and Qatadah: God's grace is faith, and His mercy is the Qur'an, the opposite of the first statement. And it was said: other than this. So in that let them rejoice refers to the grace and mercy, and the Arabs use this for the singular, dual, and plural. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he recited So rejoice in that with the letter ta, and this is the reading of Yazid ibn al-Qa’qa’, Ya’qub, and others. In the hadith: To take your ranks. Joy is a delight in the heart by realizing the beloved. Joy has been condemned in places, such as His saying: “Do not rejoice. Indeed, God does not love those who rejoice” (al-Qasas 28:76) and His saying: Indeed, it is a boastful joy (Hud 11:10). But it is absolute. So if joy is restricted, it is not condemned, because of His saying: Rejoicing in what God has given them of His bounty (Al Imran 3:170). Here, the Most High said: So in that let them rejoice meaning in the Qur’an and Islam, so let them rejoice, so it is restricted. Harun said: And in the letter of Abi, So in that, rejoice. An-Nahhas said: The way of the command is to be with the lam so that it is accompanied by a decisive letter, just as there is a letter with the prohibition, except that they delete from the command to the addressee, sufficing with addressing him, and they may bring it according to the original, from it So in that, let them rejoice. “It is better than what they accumulate” meaning in this world. The general reading is with the letter ya in both verbs. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Amir that he read fa-li-fa-rahu with the letter ya and ya-jma’u with the letter ta, addressing the disbelievers. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he read with the letter ta in the first, and ya-jma’u with the letter ya in the opposite way. Abaan narrated on the authority of Anas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever God guides to Islam and teaches him the Qur’an, then complains of poverty, God will write poverty between his eyes until the Day he meets Him. Then he recited: “Say: ‘In the bounty of God and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice. It is better than what they accumulate.’”
10:59: God Almighty says: “Say: Have you considered what God has sent down to you of provision, and you have made some of it lawful and some unlawful?” There are two issues: First: The Almighty said: Say, Have you considered? He is addressing the infidels of Mecca. What God has sent down to you of provision is in the accusative case with Have you considered? Al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative case with Anzala. And Anzala means created, as He said: And He sent down for you from the livestock eight mates (al-Zumar 39:6). And We sent down iron, wherein is great force (al-Hadid 57:25). It is permissible to express creation as Inzala, because what is on earth of provision is what comes down from the sky as rain. Then you made of it lawful and unlawful Mujahid said: It is what they ruled by prohibiting the bahīrah, the sā’ibah, the wasīlah, and the Ḥām. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the statement of God the Almighty: And they assigned to God a share of what He created of crops and livestock (al-An’am 6:136). Say, ‘Has God permitted you?’ That is, to permit and prohibit. Or against God? “Umm” means rather. You fabricate is their saying that God commanded us to do it. Second: He used this verse as evidence to deny analogy, and this is far-fetched, because analogy is the evidence of God Almighty, so the permissibility and prohibition are from God Almighty when there is evidence that God Almighty has established for the ruling. If he disagrees with the fact that analogy is the evidence of God Almighty, then he is departing from this purpose and returning to something else.
10:60: The Almighty said: And what do those who invent lies about God think on the Day of Resurrection? Day is an adverbial phrase, or a presumption, like what do you think, Zayd? The meaning is: Do they think that God will not hold them accountable for it? Indeed, God is full of bounty to mankind. That is, in delay and respite. It was said: He meant the people of Mecca when He placed them in a secure sanctuary. But most of them, meaning the disbelievers, do not thank God for His blessings or for delaying the punishment from them. It was said: They do not thank, they do not believe in the Oneness of God.
10:61: God the Almighty says: And you are not engaged in any affair Ma is for denial, meaning you are not engaged in any affair, meaning in worship or other than that, except that the Lord is aware of you. The affair is the matter, and the plural is affairs. Al-Akhfash said: The Arabs say Ma shana shana, meaning you did not do his work. And you do not recite from it any Qur'an Al-Farra' and Al-Zajjaj said: The ha' in minhu refers to the affair, meaning that an affair occurs and the Qur'an is recited for it, so he knows how to rule it, or the Qur'an is revealed for it and it is recited. Al-Tabari said: Minhu means from the Book of God the Almighty. Of the Qur'an is repeated for emphasis, like His saying: Indeed, I am God (al-Qasas 28:30). And you do not do any work is addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the nation. His saying: And you are not engaged in any affair is addressing him, and what is meant is him and his nation, and it may be addressing the Messenger, and what is meant is him and his followers. It was said that what is meant is the infidels of Quraysh. Except that We were witnesses over you meaning, we know it. Similar to it is There is no secret conversation between three but that He is the fourth of them (Al-Mujadilah: 7). As you indulge in it, meaning you engage in it, and the ha refers back to the action. It is said: So-and-so indulged in talk and action if he was immersed in it. Al-Ra’i said: Then they poured out, after their repression, a jug of water from the valleys, when they were pasturing a field. Ibn Abbas: You overflow in it, you do it. Al-Akhfash: You speak. Ibn Zayd: You engage in conversation. Ibn Kaysan: You spread the saying. Ad-Dahhak said: The ha’ refers back to the Qur’an, meaning: When you spread lies in the Qur’an. And your Lord does not hide from you. Ibn Abbas said: It disappears. Abu Rawq said: It is distant. Ibn Kaysan said: It goes. Al-Kisa’i read ya’zub with a kasra on the zay wherever it occurs, and the rest read it with a damma, and they are two eloquent languages, like ya’rsh and ya’rsh. From mithqal is from a connection, meaning and your Lord does not hide from you the mithqal of a dhartha, meaning the weight of a dhartha, meaning a small red ant, and it was mentioned before in An-Nisa. On the earth nor in the heaven nor smaller than that nor larger is in apposition to the word mithqal, or if you wish, to dhartha. Ya’qub and Hamzah read it with a dhammah on the ra’ in both of them in apposition to the position of mithqal because from is redundant for emphasis. Az-Zajjaj said: It is permissible to raise the ra’ in the beginning. And its predicate is except in a clear book meaning the Preserved Tablet with God’s knowledge of it. Al-Jurjani said: Except has the meaning of the conjunction and, meaning it is in a clear book, like the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, no messengers fear in My presence * Except for he who does wrong (al-Naml 27:10-11) meaning and he who does wrong. And His saying: So that mankind will have no argument against you, except for those who do wrong among them (al-Baqarah 2:150) meaning and those who do wrong among them, so except has the meaning of the conjunction and, and He is implied after it, like His saying: And say, ‘Forgive us’ (al-Baqarah 2:58) meaning it is a forgiveness. And His saying: And do not say, ‘Three’ (An-Nisa’: 171) meaning they are three. Similar to what we are discussing is: “And not a leaf falls but He knows it. And no grain is there in the darknesses of the earth and no moist or dry thing but that it is in a clear book” (al-An’am 6:59) and it is in a clear book.
10:62: The Almighty said: Behold, for the allies of God there is no fear concerning them meaning in the Hereafter. Nor shall they grieve for the loss of this world. It was also said: There is no fear concerning them, nor shall they grieve meaning whoever God Almighty has taken care of, protected, and is pleased with, will not fear the Day of Resurrection nor grieve. God Almighty said: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those are removed from it - meaning from Hell - far away - to His saying - The greatest terror will not grieve them (al-Anbiya 21:103). Saeed bin Jubair narrated: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Who are the friends of God? He said: Those whom God is remembered by seeing.” And “Umar ibn al-Khattab said regarding this verse: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Among the servants of God are those who are neither prophets nor martyrs, and the prophets and martyrs will envy them on the Day of Resurrection because of their status with God. It was said: O Messenger of God, tell us who they are and what their deeds are, so that we may love them. He said: They are people who love one another for the sake of God, without any kinship ties between them or money that they exchange. By God, their faces are radiant and they are on pulpits of light. They do not fear when people fear, nor do they grieve when people grieve. Then he recited: “Unquestionably, for the friends of God there is no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.” Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: The friends of God are people with yellow faces from staying up late, blind eyes from tears, empty bellies from hunger, and dry lips from withering away. It was said: They have no fear for their offspring, because God is their Guardian. Nor will they grieve for their worldly life, because God will compensate them in their children and the Hereafter, because He is their Guardian and Master.
10:63: This is the description of the friends of God Almighty, so: who is in the accusative case as a substitute for the name of in which is friends. Or if you like, on I mean. It was said: It is the beginning, and its predicate is: For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, so it is cut off from what precedes it. That is, they avoid polytheism and sins.
10:64: God Almighty said: For them is good tidings in the life of this world. “On the authority of Abu al-Darda’, he said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: No one has asked me about it except you since it was revealed. It is the good vision that a Muslim sees or that is seen for him. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi in his Jami`. Al-Zuhri, Ata` and Qatadah said: It is the good report that the angels give to the believer in this world at the time of death. On the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b Al-Qurazi, he said: When the soul of a believing slave is filled with sorrow, the Angel of Death comes to him and says: Peace be upon you, O friend of God. God sends you peace. Then he recites this verse: “Those whom the angels take in death, [while] good, saying, ‘Peace be upon you.’” (al-Nahl 16:32), as mentioned by Ibn Al-Mubarak. Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said: It is that he knows where he is before he dies. Al-Hasan said: It is what God the Most High gives them good report of His Book of His Paradise and His generous reward, as He says: Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Him and approval (al-Tawbah 9:21), and His saying: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds that they will have gardens (al-Baqarah 2:25). And His saying: And receive good tidings of the Paradise which you were promised (Fussilat 41:16). 30] That is why he said: There is no change in the words of God, meaning there is no breach of His promises, because His promises are in His words. And in the Hereafter, it was said: in Paradise when they emerge from their graves. It was also said: when the soul emerges, it is given the good report of God’s pleasure. Abu Ishaq al-Tha’labi said: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Jawzaqi say: I saw Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz in a dream riding a mule wearing a cloak and a turban, so I greeted him and said to him: Welcome, we will not cease to remember you and your good qualities, so he said: And we will not cease to remember you and your good qualities, God the Most High said: For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, good praise, and he pointed with his hand. There is no change in the words of God, meaning there is no breach of His promise. It was also said: There is no change in His report, meaning He does not abrogate it with anything, and it will not be except as He said: That is the great attainment, meaning that which His friends attain, so it is the great attainment.
10:65: The Almighty said: And let not their statement grieve you The speech is complete, meaning do not be grieved by their fabrications and their denial of you, then He began by saying: Indeed, honor belongs to God meaning complete power, comprehensive victory, and complete ability belong to God alone, for He is your supporter, helper, and protector. All together is an accusative of state, and this does not contradict His saying: And to God belongs honor and to His Messenger and to the believers (al-Munafiqun 63:8), for all honor belongs to God, and all honor belongs to God. God the Almighty said: Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Honor, above what they describe (al-Saffat 37:180). He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing He hears their words and voices, and He knows their deeds and actions and all their movements.
10:66: The Almighty says: Indeed, to God belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth. That is, He rules over them as He wills, and does with them whatever He wills, glory be to Him! The Almighty said: And those they invoke other than God do not follow partners. “What” is for negation, meaning they do not follow partners in reality, but rather they think that they will intercede or benefit. It was said: What is an interrogative, meaning what do those they invoke other than God follow, criticizing their actions? Then he answered and said: They follow nothing but assumption, and they do nothing but guess. That is, they guess and lie, and this has been mentioned before.
10:67: The Almighty said: It is He who made the night for you that you may rest therein. He made clear that it is obligatory to worship the One who is able to create the night and the day, not to worship the One who is not able to do anything. That you may rest therein meaning with your wives and children, so that fatigue and exhaustion may go away from you. And stillness means calmness from disturbance. The Almighty said: And the day is seeing meaning shining so that you may be guided by it in your needs. The one who sees is the one who sees, and the day is seen in. He said: seeing is a metaphor and expansion based on the Arabs’ custom in saying: a standing night, and a fasting day. Jarir said: You blamed us, O Umm Ghilan, in the night, and you slept, while the night of the mounts was not asleep. Qatrib said: It is said that the night became dark, meaning it became full of darkness, and the day became harmful and visible, meaning it became full of light and sight. God Almighty says: Indeed in that are signs meaning signs and indications. For a people who listen meaning listening for consideration.
10:68: The Almighty said: They said, 'God has taken a son' meaning the disbelievers. This has been mentioned before. Glory be to Him He has cleared Himself of having a wife, children, partners, and equals. He is the Rich; to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth Then He informed of His absolute richness, and that He owns whatever is in the heavens and the earth, as ownership, creation, and servant. There is none in the heavens and the earth but comes to the Most Merciful as a servant (Maryam 19:93). You have no authority for this meaning you have no proof for this. Do you say about God that which you do not know? of affirming that He has a son? A son requires similarity and resemblance, and God, the Most High, is not similar to anything nor does He resemble anything.
10:69: God Almighty says: “Say: ‘Indeed, those who invent lies against God will not succeed,’” meaning they will not win and will not feel safe. And the speech is complete.
10:70: Enjoyment in this world meaning that is enjoyment, or it is enjoyment in this world, as Al-Kisa'i said. Al-Akhfash said: They have enjoyment in this world. Abu Ishaq said: The accusative is permissible in places other than the Qur'an to mean they enjoy enjoyment. Then to Us is their return meaning their return. Then We will make them taste the severe punishment meaning the harsh one. Because they used to disbelieve meaning because of their disbelief.
10:71: The Almighty said: And recite to them the report of Noah He ordered him, peace be upon him, to remind them of the stories of those who came before, and to frighten them with the painful punishment for their disbelief. The waw was omitted from recite because it is a command, meaning, read to them the report of Noah. When he said to his people When is in the accusative case. O my people, if it is too great for you meaning, it is great and heavy for you. My position The position with a fatha on the meem: the place in which one stands. The position with a damma is the residence. It was not recited, as far as I know, meaning, if my stay among you is prolonged. And my reminder you, and my frightening you. With the signs of God and you resolved to kill me and expel me. So upon God I have relied meaning, I have relied. This is the answer to the condition, and he, peace be upon him, continued to rely on God in every situation, but he made it clear that he relied on this in particular so that his people would know that God would suffice him in their matter, meaning if you do not support me, then I will rely on someone who will support me. God the Almighty said: So decide upon your plan, you and your partners. The general reading is fa-jma’u, with the alif sukun sukun. Asim al-Jahdari read fa-jma’u by connecting the alif and opening the meem, from jamaa’ yajma’u. sukun. Al-Hasan, Ibn Ishaq, and Ya’qub read fa-jma’u by cutting off the alif sukun sukun. As for the first reading, it is from ajma’ ‘ala al-shay’ if he is determined upon it. Al-Farra’ said: ajma’ al-shay’ is a thing that he prepared. The historian said: I have decided upon the matter, which is more eloquent than ajma’a ‘alayhi. And he recited: Oh, how I wish, and hopes are of no avail. Will I ever become one day when my affair is settled? An-Nahhas said: There are three aspects to the accusative case of partners in this reading. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ said: It means call upon your partners to support you, and it is accusative according to them because this verb is implied. Muhammad bin Yazid said: It is conjoined to the meaning, as he said: I wish your husband was in the battlefield, carrying a sword and a spear. The spear is not girdled, but it is carried like a sword. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is with your partners in your support, as it is said: water and wood met. The second reading is from the plural, considering the Almighty’s saying: So he gathered his plan and then came (Ta-Ha 20:60). Abu Muadh said: It is possible that the plural of ajma’ has one meaning, and your partners according to this reading is in apposition to your affair, or in the meaning of so gather your affair and gather your partners, or if you wish in the meaning of with. Abu Ja’far al-Nahhas said: I heard Abu Ishaq permitting Zayd and Amr to stand. The third reading is that the partners are in apposition to the implied raised noun in ajma’u, and the goodness of that speech has been prolonged. Al-Nahhas and others said: This reading is far-fetched, because if it were in the nominative case, it would have been necessary to write it with a waw, and no waw was seen in the copies of the Qur’an in his saying and your partners, and also their partners are the idols, and the idols do not make anything and do not do anything until they gather. Al-Mahdawi said: It is permissible for the partners to be raised by the beginning and the predicate is omitted, meaning and your partners to gather their affair, and this was attributed to the partners and they do not hear nor see nor distinguish as a way of rebuking those who worship them. The Almighty said: Then let not your affair be a burden for you. The noun yakan and its predicate. Ghammah and gham are the same, and their meanings are covering, from their saying: the crescent moon is covered if it is hidden, meaning let your affair be apparent and revealed so that you can do what you want, not like someone whose affair is hidden and is not able to do what he wants. Tarafa said: By your life, my day is not sad, nor my night is eternal. Al-Zajjaj: A person who is sad is sad. Sadness and grief are like distress and anxiety. It was said that sadness is the distress of a matter that causes sadness, so its owner does not know the source of his matter so that what is saddening him can be relieved. In Al-Sahah: Sadness is distress. Al-Ajjaj said: Rather, if you witnessed people when they were filled with grief, their grief would not have been relieved. It is said: a matter of gloom, meaning vague and ambiguous. God Almighty said: Then let not your affair be a gloom for you. Abu Ubaidah said: Its metaphor is darkness and narrowness. Gloom is also: the bottom of a palm tree and other places. Someone else said: The origin of all of this is derived from the cloud. God the Almighty said: Then pass it on to me and do not give me respite. The alif of iqda is an alif of connection, from qada yaqdi. Al-Akhfash and Al-Kisa’i said: It is a proverb. And We passed it on to him (al-Hijr 15:66), meaning We finished it for him and conveyed it to him. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then pass it on to me and do not give me respite. He said: Go to me and do not delay. An-Nahhas said: This is a correct statement in the language, and from it: the dead person passed away, meaning he went away. And he informed them of this that they would not reach him, and this is from the evidence of prophethood. Al-Farra’ narrated on the authority of some of the reciters: Then go to me with the letter fa and the severing of the alif, meaning they headed towards him. It is said: the caliphate has passed on to so-and-so, and the pain has passed on to me. This is a statement from God the Almighty about His Prophet Noah, peace be upon him, that he was confident in God’s victory, and not afraid of their plot, knowing that they and their gods can neither benefit nor harm. It is a consolation to His Prophet, peace be upon him, and a strengthening of his heart.
10:72: The Almighty said: But if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward. That is, if you turn away from what I have brought you, it is not because I have asked you for a reward that would burden you with my reward. My reward is only from God in conveying His message. And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims that is, those who believe in the Oneness of God the Almighty. The people of Medina, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Hafs opened the ya' of ajra wherever it occurred, and the rest made it quiescent.
10:73: The Almighty says: But they denied him meaning Noah. So We saved him and those with him meaning the believers. In the ark meaning the ship, and we will mention it later. And We made them successors meaning the inhabitants of the earth and successors to those who drowned. Then see how was the end of those who were warned meaning the final fate of those whom the messengers warned but did not believe.
10:74: The Almighty said: Then We sent after him meaning after Noah. Messengers to their people such as Hud, Salih, Abraham, Lot, Shuaib and others. And they came to them with clear proofs meaning miracles. But they were not to believe in what they had denied before The meaning is: what Noah's people had denied before. It was said: what they had denied before, meaning before the Day of the Atom, because there were those among them who denied in their hearts, even though all of them said: Yes. An-Nahhas said: And among the best things that have been said about this for a people who are specific, such as: Whether you warn them or do you not warn them, they will not believe (al-Baqarah 2:6). Thus do We set a seal meaning We seal the hearts of the transgressors meaning those who exceed the limit in disbelief and denial, so they will not believe. This refutes the statement of the Qadarites as mentioned above.
10:75: The Almighty says: Then We sent after them meaning after the messengers and nations. Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs meaning the nobles of his people. With Our signs meaning the nine signs, which have been mentioned above. But they were arrogant meaning about the truth. And they were a criminal people meaning polytheists.
10:76: The Almighty says: So when the truth came to them from Us, meaning Pharaoh and his people. They said, ‘This is clearly magic.’ They attributed miracles to magic.
10:77: Moses said to them: Do you say about the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' It was said: There is an omission in the speech, the meaning is: Do you say about the truth, this is magic? So do you say denial, and their statement is omitted, meaning this is magic, then he resumed another denial from before it and said: Is this magic! So he omitted their first statement, sufficing with the second of their statement, denying Pharaoh and his people. Al-Akhfash said: It is from their statement, and the alif was entered to narrate their statement, because they said, Is this magic? So it was said to them: Do you say about the truth when it has come to you, 'Is this magic?' It was narrated from Al-Hasan. And magicians will not succeed meaning whoever brings it will not succeed.
10:78: The Almighty said: They said, ‘Have you come to us to distract us?’ That is, to turn us around and divert us. It is said: He turned him around if he twisted him and diverted him. The poet said: I looked around the neighborhood until I saw myself getting sick from listening to the noise and the deception And from this turning is only a deviation from the direction before it. From what we found our fathers doing meaning the worship of idols. And you will have pride meaning greatness, kingship and authority. On the land meaning the land of Egypt. And the king is called pride because it is the greatest thing sought in the world. And we will not believe you Ibn Masoud, Al-Hasan and others read it with the letter ya because it is a non-real feminine and they were separated. Sibawayh narrated: Two women attended the judge today.
10:79: He only said it when he saw the stick and the white hand and believed that they were magic. Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Ibn Waththab, and Al-A’mash read magician. The discussion of them has already been presented in Al-A’raf.
10:80: That is, throw down to the ground whatever ropes and sticks you have with you. This has been discussed in detail in Al-A'raf.
10:81: The Almighty said: "So when they threw, Moses said: What you have brought is magic." Ma is in the nominative case as a subject, and the predicate is you have brought it and the meaning is: what thing have you brought, as a rebuke and diminution of what they brought of magic. Abu Amr's reading of magic is as an interrogative with an implied subject and the meaning is is it magic? It is permissible for it to be a subject and the predicate is omitted, the meaning is: the magic you brought it. Ma is not according to the reading of the one who asked for it in the meaning of who, since it has no predicate. The rest read magic as a predicate, and the evidence for this reading is the reading of Ibn Masoud: What you have brought is magic. Abu's reading: What you have brought is magic, in it is in the meaning of who, and you have brought it is the relative clause, and the position of what is raised as a subject, and magic is the predicate of the subject. Ma is not accusative if you make it in the meaning of who because the relative clause does not work on the relative. Al-Farra' permitted the accusative of magic with you have brought it, and what is for the condition, and you have brought it is in the place of the jussive with what and the fa is omitted, the meaning is: then God will invalidate it. It is permissible to make magic the source, meaning what you have brought is magic, then the alif and lam are added, so in this estimation there is no need to delete the fa. Al-Nahhas chose this statement, and said: The deletion of the fa in the recompense is not permitted by many grammarians except in poetic necessity, as he said: Whoever does good deeds, God will reward them. Rather, some of them may have said: It is not permissible at all. I heard Ali bin Sulayman say: Muhammad bin Yazid told me, Al-Mazini told me, I heard Al-Asma’i say: The grammarians changed this verse, and the narration is: Whoever does good, the Most Merciful will thank him. I heard Ali bin Sulaiman say: The deletion of the letter fa in mujazaah is permissible. He said: The evidence for that is And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned (al-Shura 42:30) And whatever strikes you of disaster - it is for what your hands have earned are two famous and well-known readings. Indeed, God will not amend the work of corrupters means magic. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever goes to bed at night and then recites this verse: “What you have brought is magic - indeed, God will nullify it. Indeed, God will not amend the work of corrupters” - no magician’s trick will harm him. And do not write on a person who has been bewitched except that God will repel the magic from him.
10:82: God Almighty says: And God will establish the truth meaning He will make it clear and explain it. With His words meaning with His words, arguments and proofs. It was said: With His promises of victory. Even though the criminals dislike it from the people of Pharaoh.
10:83: The Almighty said: None believed in Moses except the offspring of his people. The ha' refers to Moses. Mujahid said: That is, none of them believed, but rather the children of those to whom Moses was sent from the Children of Israel believed. Due to the length of time, the fathers perished and the children remained and believed. This is the choice of al-Tabari. Offspring are the descendants of a person, and they may increase. It was said that he meant by offspring the believers of the Children of Israel. Ibn Abbas said: They were six hundred thousand, because Jacob, peace be upon him, entered Egypt with seventy-two people and they multiplied in Egypt until they reached six hundred thousand. Ibn Abbas also said: Of his people, meaning from the people of Pharaoh, among them the believer of Pharaoh's family, Pharaoh's treasurer and his wife, his daughter's hairdresser, and his treasurer's wife. It was said: They are people whose fathers were Copts and whose mothers were from the Children of Israel, so they were called descendants just as the children of the Persians who were born in Yemen and the lands of the Arabs were called Banaa, because their mothers were not from the same race as their fathers. Al-Farra’ said: Based on this, the metaphor in his people goes back to Moses due to kinship on the mothers’ side, and to Pharaoh if they were from the Copts. God the Almighty said: For fear of Pharaoh because he was a tyrant over them. And their chiefs and did not say and his chiefs, and there are six answers from him: The first - that since Pharaoh was a tyrant, he spoke about him by the action of all. The second - that when Pharaoh was mentioned, he knew that there was someone else with him, so the pronoun returned to him and to them, and this is one of the two opinions of Al-Farraa. The third - that the group was named Pharaoh like Thamud. The fourth - that the estimate is: for fear of the people of Pharaoh, so it is from the category of deleting the added like: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82) and this is the second opinion of Al-Farraa. This answer according to the doctrine of Sibawayh and Al-Khalil is wrong, it is not permissible for them to say Hind stood up, and you mean her slave. The fifth - the doctrine of Al-Akhfash Saeed: that the pronoun refers to the offspring, meaning the chiefs of the offspring, and this is the choice of Al-Tabari. The sixth - that the pronoun refers to his people. Al-Nahhas said: This answer seems to be the most eloquent. To tempt them is a singular verb used to describe Pharaoh, meaning to divert them from their religion with punishments. It is in the accusative case as a substitute for inclusion. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case as in Bukhari’s fear. Pharaoh was not declined because it is a foreign name and it is a definite noun. And indeed, Pharaoh was haughty in the land meaning, arrogant and haughty. And indeed, he was among the transgressors meaning, those who exceeded the limit in disbelief, because he was a slave and claimed divinity.
10:84: God Almighty said: And Moses said, ‘O my people, if you have believed’ meaning you have confirmed. In God, then rely on Him meaning you have depended. If you are Muslims He repeated the condition for emphasis, and explained that the perfection of faith is in entrusting the matter to God.
10:85: They said, 'Upon God we have put our trust' meaning we have submitted our affairs to Him, and we are satisfied with His judgment and destiny, and we have submitted to His command. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people meaning do not give them victory over us, so that this would be a trial for us from the religion, or do not test us by punishing us at their hands. Mujahid said: The meaning is do not destroy us at the hands of our enemies, and do not punish us with a punishment from You, so that our enemies say, If they were right, we would not have been given power over them, and they will be tempted. Abu Majlaz and Abu Ad-Dahha said: It means do not give them victory over us, so that they see that they are better than us, and so they increase in their transgression.
10:86: The Almighty said: And save us by Your mercy meaning save us. From the disbelieving people meaning from Pharaoh and his people, because they used to force them to do hard work.
10:87: The Almighty’s saying: And We inspired Moses and his brother, saying, ‘Provide houses for your people in Egypt.’ There are five issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: And We inspired Moses and his brother, ‘Take homes for your people in Egypt.’ It is said: I took a place for Zaid, and I took a place for Zaid. The place of residence is the one that is required, and from this comes the phrase God took him a home, meaning He made him stay in it and settled him, and from this comes the hadith: Whoever deliberately lies about me, let him take his seat in Hellfire. The rajaz poet said: We are the sons of Adnan, there is no doubt that glory and kingship are ours. And Egypt in this verse is Alexandria, according to Mujahid. And Ad-Dahhak said: It is the country called Egypt, and Egypt is what is between the sea and Aswan, and Alexandria is part of the land of Egypt. Second: The Almighty said: And make your houses a Qiblah. Most of the commentators said: The Children of Israel did not pray except in their mosques and churches, and they were apparent. When Moses was sent, Pharaoh ordered the mosques of the Children of Israel to be destroyed and they were prevented from praying. So God inspired Moses and Aaron to take and choose for the Children of Israel houses in Egypt, meaning mosques, and He did not mean inhabited houses. This is the saying of Ibrahim, Ibn Zayd, Al-Rabi’, Abu Malik, Ibn Abbas and others. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Saeed bin Jubair that the meaning is: And make your houses facing each other. The first saying is more correct, meaning make your mosques towards the Qiblah. It was said: Jerusalem, and it is the Qiblah of the Jews to this day, as Ibn Bahr said. It was also said: the Kaaba. Ibn Abbas said: The Kaaba was the Qiblah of Moses and those with him. This indicates that the Qiblah in prayer was a law for Moses, peace be upon him, and the prayer did not lack the condition of purity, covering the private parts and facing the Qiblah, because that is more effective in the obligation and more abundant in worship. It was said: What is meant is to pray in your homes secretly so that you may be safe. This was when Pharaoh frightened them, so they were ordered to be patient and to build mosques in their homes, and to go ahead with prayer and supplication until God fulfilled His promise. This is what is meant by His saying: Moses said to his people, ‘Seek help from God and be patient.’ (al-A’raf 7:128) The verse. It was part of their religion that they would not pray except in churches and synagogues as long as they were safe. If they were afraid, they were permitted to pray in their homes. Ibn al-Arabi said: The first is the more apparent of the two opinions, because the second is a claim. I said: His statement: A correct claim, because in the authentic hadith he, peace be upon him, said: The earth has been made for me a place of prostration and purification. This is something that He has been given exclusively, not the prophets. Praise be to God, we pray in mosques and homes, and wherever we are able to pray. However, voluntary prayers performed at home are better than voluntary prayers performed in mosques, even bowing before and after Friday prayers, and before and after the obligatory prayers, because voluntary prayers involve showing off, while obligatory prayers do not. The more a deed is free from showing off, the more weighty and closer it is to God, the Most High. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shafiq who said: I asked Aisha about the voluntary prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: “He used to pray four rak’ahs in my house before noon, then he would go out and lead the people in prayer, then he would come back and pray two rak’ahs. He used to pray the Maghrib prayer with the people, then he would come back and pray two rak’ahs, then he would pray the ‘Isha’ prayer with the people, and he would come back to my house and pray two rak’ahs…” The hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar that he said: I prayed with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) two prostrations before noon, two prostrations after it, and two prostrations after sunset. As for the Maghrib, ‘Isha’, and Jumu’ah prayers, I prayed with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in his house. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah that “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to the mosque of Banu al-Ashhal and prayed the Maghrib prayer there. When they had finished their prayer, he saw them glorifying God after it, so he said: This is the prayer at home.” Third: Scholars differed on this matter regarding the standing of Ramadan. Is it better to perform it at home or in the mosque? Malik was of the opinion that it is better to perform it at home for those who are able to do so, and Abu Yusuf and some of the companions of al-Shafi’i said the same. Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Ahmad and some of the companions of al-Shafi’i were of the opinion that attending it in congregation is better. Al-Layth said: If people stand in their homes and no one stands in the mosque, they should not go out to it. The evidence for Malik and those who said the same is the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the hadeeth of Zayd ibn Thabit: So pray in your homes, for the best prayer of a person is in his home, except for the obligatory prayer. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. The opponent argued that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed it in congregation in the mosque, then he informed of the reason that prevented him from doing so all the time, which was fear that it would be made obligatory upon them. Therefore, he said to them: So pray in your homes. Then the companions used to pray it in the mosque in separate groups, until Umar gathered them behind one reciter, and the matter settled on that and it became a Sunnah. Fourth - If we assume that it was permissible for them to pray in their homes if they feared for themselves, then this is evidence that someone who is excused due to fear or otherwise is permitted to leave the congregation and Friday prayers.
