The excuse that permits him to do so is such as a confining illness, or fear of its worsening, or fear of the ruler’s injustice in money or otherwise without ruling against him justly. Heavy rain with mud is an excuse if it does not stop, and someone who has a close friend who is about to die and there is no one to nurse him, and Ibn Umar did that. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And give good tidings to the believers. It was said that the address was to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said that it was to Moses, peace be upon him, and this is more apparent, meaning that he gave the Children of Israel good tidings that God would make them victorious over their enemy.
10:88: God Almighty said: And Moses said, ‘Our Lord, You have given Pharaoh and his chiefs’ “You have given” means you have given. “adornment and wealth in the life of this world” meaning worldly wealth. They had mountains from Fustat in Egypt to the land of Abyssinia in which were mines of gold, silver, peridot, emerald, and ruby. The Almighty’s saying: Our Lord, that they may go astray from Your path. There is a difference of opinion regarding this lam, and the most correct thing to say about it - and this is the saying of Al-Khalil and Sibawayh - is that it is the lam of consequence and becoming. In the report: God has an angel who calls out every day, ‘Build for death and build for destruction.’ That is, the outcome of their affair was misguidance, so it was as if He had given it to them so that they would go astray. It was also said that it is not ki, meaning that He gave it to them so that they would go astray, become arrogant and haughty. It was also said that it is lam ajl, meaning that He gave it to them because they turned away from You, so they did not fear that You would turn away from them. Some people claimed that the meaning is: I gave them that so that they would not go astray, so la was deleted, as God the Almighty said: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray (An-Nisa’: 176). The meaning is: so that you do not go astray. An-Nahhas said: The apparent meaning of this answer is good, except that the Arabs do not delete la except with an, so the author of this answer clarified it by saying, so that you go astray. It was also said that the lam is for supplication, meaning, test them with straying from Your path, because after it is: Destroy their wealth and make it severe. It was said: The verb means the source, i.e. misleading them, like the Almighty’s saying: So that you may turn away from them (al-Tawbah 9:95). The Kufians read: li-yidalu with a damma on the ya’ of misleading, and the rest read it with a fatha. God the Almighty said: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth meaning punish them for their disbelief by destroying their wealth. Al-Zajjaj said: Obliterating something means removing its original form. Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: Their wealth and dirhams became engraved stones in their original form, in hectares, thirds, and halves. They did not have any mine that God did not obliterate, so that no one benefited from it after that. Qatada said: We were informed that their wealth and crops became stones. Mujahid and Atiyah said: He destroyed them until they could not be seen. It is said: an obliterated eye, and the place is obliterated if it is erased and destroyed. Ibn Zayd said: Their dinars, dirhams, furniture, and everything they had became stones. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: A man among them would be with his family in his bed and they would have become two stones. He said: Umar ibn Abdul Aziz asked me, so I mentioned that to him, so he called for a map that had been found in Egypt and took out from it fruits, dirhams, and dinars, and they were stones. Al-Suddi said: It was one of the nine signs. And harden their hearts. Ibn Abbas said: That is, prevent them from believing. It was also said: Measure them and seal them so that they do not open up to believing, and the meaning is the same. So that they do not believe. It was said: It is an appositive to His statement: So that they may go astray, meaning, I gave them blessings so that they may go astray and not believe. This was stated by Al-Zajjaj and Al-Mubarrad. Based on this, there is nothing in it of the meaning of supplication. His statement: Our Lord, obliterate and harden is an interjection. Al-Farra’, Al-Kisa’i and Abu Ubaidah said: It is a supplication, so it is in the position of the jussive according to them, meaning, O God, so that they do not believe, meaning, so that they do not believe. And from this is the statement of Al-A’sha: Do not let what is hidden appear before your eyes, and do not meet me except with your nose downcast. That is, do not relax. And whoever says, Let them go astray - that is, test them with misguidance - he said: It is connected to it, so they will not believe. And it was said: It is in the accusative case because it is the answer to the command, that is, and make their hearts hard, so they will not believe. This is the saying of Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra’ also, and Al-Farra’ recited: Oh camel, go with a broad neck to Solomon, so that we may rest. Therefore, the letter nun was deleted because it is in the accusative case. Until they see the painful punishment. Ibn Abbas said: It is drowning. Some people have found this verse difficult to understand, saying: How can he invoke curses upon them when the Messengers ruled that their people should believe? The answer is that it is not permissible for a prophet to invoke curses upon his people except with God’s permission, and to inform them that there is no one among them who will believe and no one who will come from their loins who will believe. The evidence for this is His statement to Noah, peace be upon him: None of your people will believe except those who have already believed. (Hud 11:36) At that point, he said: My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller. (Nuh 71:26) and the verse. And God knows best.
10:89: The Almighty said: He said, 'Your prayer has been answered.' Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Moses prayed and Aaron said Amen, so Aaron was called a supplicant after he said Amen to the prayer. Saying Amen to a prayer is to say Amen, so your saying Amen is a prayer, meaning O Lord, answer me. It was said: Aaron prayed with Moses as well. The scholars of meaning said: The Arabs sometimes address one person as two people. The poet said: I said to my friend, Do not rush us to remove its roots. So he cut down the wormwood. This is based on the fact that Amen is a supplication, and that Aaron did not supplicate. An-Nahhas said: I heard Ali bin Sulayman say: The evidence that the supplication is for them is the saying of Moses, peace be upon him, Our Lord, and he did not say Lord. Ali and As-Salami read your supplications in the plural. Ibn As-Sameeq read I have answered your supplication as report from God the Most High, and he put a supplication in the accusative case after it. The discussion of Amen at the end of Al-Fatihah has been presented in full. It is one of the things that was specific to our Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, Aaron, and Moses, peace be upon them. Anas bin Malik narrated that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: “God has given my nation three things that He has not given to anyone before them: peace, which is the greeting of the people of Paradise and the rows of angels, and amen, except for what was said by Moses and Aaron.” Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim mentioned this in Nawader al-Usul. It was mentioned earlier in Al-Fatihah. God the Almighty says: So be upright. Al-Farra' and others said: It is an order to be upright in their matter and to remain steadfast in it from the call of Pharaoh and his people to faith, until the interpretation of the answer comes to them. Muhammad bin Ali and Ibn Jurayj said: Pharaoh and his people remained forty years after this answer, then they were destroyed. It was said: Be upright means to call, and steadfastness in call is to leave haste in achieving the goal, and haste does not fall from the heart except by the uprightness of tranquility, in it, and that tranquility does not come except by the satisfaction of the good for all that appears from the unseen. And do not follow the path of those who do not know with a shaddah on the noon in the place of the jussive of prohibition, and the noon is for emphasis and it was moved due to the meeting of two quiescent letters and the kasra was chosen for it because it resembles the noon of the dual. Ibn Dhakwan read it with a light noon for negation. It was said: It is a state of be upright, meaning be upright without following, and the meaning is: Do not follow the path of those who do not know the reality of My promise and My threat.
10:90: The Almighty said: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea This was discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah in His statement: And when We parted the sea for you (al-Baqarah 2:50). Al-Hasan read and We crossed and they are two dialects. Then Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them It is said: taba'a and itaba'a have the same meaning, if he caught up with him and overtook him. And ibta'a with emphasis means walking behind him. Al-Asma'i said: atabahu with a severing of the alif in the matter means he followed him. And atabahu with a severing of the alif in good or evil, this is the saying of Abu Amr. It has been said that they have the same meaning. So Moses went out with the Children of Israel and they were six hundred thousand and twenty thousand, and Pharaoh followed him in the morning with two thousand thousand and six hundred thousand. This was mentioned previously. Baghya is an accusative of state. A'adwa is conjoined to it, meaning in a state of aggression, transgression and oppression. It is said: 'Ada he accuses, ya'du he accuses, like ghazaa he invades, ghazwa he invades. Al-Hasan read wa’adu with a damma on the ‘ayn and the dal and a shaddah on the waw, like ‘ala ya’luwu ‘alwan. The commentators said: baghyan means seeking superiority without right in speech, and ‘adwun in action, so they are both accusative as a direct object. Until when drowning overtook him means it reached him and reached him. He said, ‘I believe’ means I have believed. That means that he is. There is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believed. So when the preposition was deleted, the verb became transitive and was accusative. It was read with a kasra, meaning I became a believer and then resumed. Abu Hatim claimed that the saying was deleted, meaning I believed, so I said that he is, and faith is of no benefit at that time, and repentance is accepted before seeing the hardship, but after that and after mixing, it is not accepted, according to what was explained previously in An-Nisa’. It is said that Pharaoh was afraid to enter the sea, and he was riding a black horse, and there was no female horse among Pharaoh’s horses. Then Gabriel came on a thin horse - that is, a delicious horse - in the form of Haman and said to him: Go forward. Then he entered the sea, and Pharaoh’s horse followed it, and Michael led them, and none of them strayed. When they were the last of them in the sea and they were the first to emerge, the sea closed over them, and Pharaoh was drowning, and he said: I believe in that in which the Children of Israel believe. So Gabriel put a spear in his mouth while the sea was still. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God drowned Pharaoh, he said, ‘I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believe.’ Gabriel said, ‘O Muhammad, if you could see me taking some of the mud from the sea and putting it in his mouth, fearing that mercy might reach him.’” Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a good hadith. Mud from the sea: the black mud that is found on its land, as the linguists said. On the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: Gabriel kept putting mud in Pharaoh’s mouth for fear that he would say ‘There is no god but God’ and God would have mercy on him, or for fear that God would have mercy on him. This hadith is hasan gharib sahih. Awn ibn Abdullah said: It has reached me that Gabriel said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: No child of Satan is more hateful to me than Pharaoh. When he was about to drown, he said: ‘I believe in the verse.’ I was afraid that he would say it and God would have mercy on him, so I took some soil or mud and stuffed it in his mouth. It was said: He did this to him as a punishment for the greatness of what he had done. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: God stopped the Nile of Egypt from flowing during his time, so the Copts said to him: If you are our Lord, then make water flow for us. So he rode and ordered his soldiers, one by one, and they stood on their steps. He jumped where they could not see him, got down from his mount, put on other clothes, prostrated, and supplicated to God Almighty, so God made water flow for him. Then Gabriel came to him while he was alone in the form of someone asking a question and said: What does the prince say about a man who has a slave who grew up in his blessings and has no support other than him, but he was ungrateful for his blessings, denied his rights, and claimed sovereignty over him? So Pharaoh wrote, saying that Abu al-Abbas al-Walid ibn Mus'ab ibn al-Rayyan said that his punishment is to be drowned in the sea. So Gabriel took him and passed by, and when he was about to drown, Gabriel, peace be upon him, handed him his writing. This has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'As and Ibn Abbas with a chain of transmission. This was on the Day of Ashura, as was explained previously in Surat al-Baqarah as well, so there is no point in repeating it. God Almighty says: And I am one of the Muslims, meaning one of the monotheists who submit to God in obedience and submission.
10:91: It was said: It is from the words of God the Most High. It was said: It is from the words of Gabriel. It was said: Michael, may God's prayers be upon them, or other angels, may God's prayers be upon them. It was said: It is from the words of Pharaoh in his soul, and there was no speech on the tongue, but rather it occurred in his heart, so he said to himself what he said: since regret did not benefit him, and similar to it. We feed you only for the sake of God (al-Insan 76:9) The Lord praised them for what was in their hearts, not that they said it verbally, and true speech is the speech of the heart.
10:92: The Almighty said: So today We will save you with your body meaning We will cast you onto a high place on the earth. This is because the Children of Israel did not believe that Pharaoh had drowned, and they said: It is more serious than that, so God cast him onto a high place on the earth, meaning a high place on the sea, so that they could see him. Aws bin Hajar said, describing rain: He who is saved by his punishment is like he who is saved by his salvation, and he who is hidden is like he who walks on a treadmill. Al-Yazidi and Ibn Al-Sameeq read it as nanhika with a ha from tanhiyya, and Alqamah narrated it from Ibn Masoud, meaning to be on one side of the sea. Ibn Jurayj said: So he threw him at the sea magician until the Children of Israel saw him. He was short and red like a bull. Alqamah narrated from Abdullah that he read it as bindaika from nida. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: It is not contrary to the spelling of our Mushaf, since its way is to write it with a Ya and a Kaf after the Dal, because the Alif is dropped from your vocative in the order of the Mushaf’s script, just as it was dropped from the darkness and the heavens. So if it is deleted, the spelling of your body and your vocative are equal. However, this reading is not recommended due to its anomaly and its contradiction with what most Muslims do. The reading is a Sunnah that others adopt from others, and its meaning is deficient in the interpretation of our reading, since it does not mention the armor, which is what the reports have continued, that the Children of Israel differed about the drowning of Pharaoh, and they asked God Almighty to show them him drowned, so they threw him on a high place on the ground with his body, which is his armor that he wears in wars. Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: His armor was made of strung pearls. It was said: Of gold, and he was known by it. It was said: Of iron, Abu Sakhr said: And the body is the short armor. Abu Ubaidah recited for al-A’sha: And white as a veil, decorated with a bow above the body’s pocket He also recited for Amr bin Ma’dikarib: Their women went on with all their might, arguing, and with their bodies. Kaab bin Malik said: You see the bodies therein covered with heroes and the strong cores. By bodies he meant armor, and by yalba he meant Yemeni armor, which was made of hides, some of which were sewn together, and it is a generic name, the singular being yalba. Amr ibn Kulthum said: We have eggs and Yemeni milk and swords that stand and bow to us It was said: With your body with a body without a soul, Mujahid said: Al-Akhfash said: As for the saying of the one who said with your armor, it is nothing. Abu Bakr said: Because when they supplicated to God asking Him to see Pharaoh drowned, He showed him to them and they saw a body without a soul, so when the Children of Israel saw him, they said: Yes! O Moses, this is Pharaoh and he has drowned, so doubt left their hearts and the sea swallowed Pharaoh as he was. So based on this, We will save you with your body has two meanings: One of them is - We will cast you to a place of safety on the land. The second is - We will show your body that has no soul. The anomalous reading of calling you returns in meaning to the meaning of the group reading, because calling has two interpretations, one of them is - We will cast you with your shouting of the word of repentance, and your saying after its door was closed and the time for its acceptance had passed: I believe that there is no god except the one in whom the Children of Israel believed, and I am of the Muslims in a high position. And the other - today we isolate you from the mysterious sea by your call when you said I am your highest Lord, so his saving with the body was a punishment from the Lord of the Worlds for what he had neglected of his disbelief, from which came his call in which he fabricated and slandered, and claimed the ability and command which he knows he is lying about and incapable of and unworthy of. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: So our recitation includes what is in the anomalous recitation of meanings and adds to them. The Almighty says: That you may be a sign to those who come after you meaning for the Children of Israel and for those who remained from the people of Pharaoh who were not overtaken by the drowning and who did not receive this report. And indeed, many of the people, of Our signs, are heedless meaning they turn away from contemplating and reflecting on Our signs. It was read to those who come after you with a fat-ha on the lam, meaning for those who remain after you and succeed you on your land. Ali ibn Abi Talib read to those who created you with a qaf, meaning that you will be a sign to your Creator.
10:93: The Almighty said: And We had already settled the Children of Israel in a place of truth meaning a place of truth, praised and chosen, meaning Egypt. It was also said: Jordan and Palestine. Ad-Dahhak said: It is Egypt and Ash-Sham. And We provided for them of the good things meaning fruits and other things. Ibn Abbas said: meaning Qurayzah, An-Nadir and the people of the Prophet's time from the Children of Israel, because they believed in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and were waiting for his emergence, then when he emerged they envied him, and for this reason He said: And they did not differ meaning in the matter of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Until knowledge came to them meaning the Qur'an and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Knowledge means what is known, because they knew it before his emergence, as Ibn Jarir At-Tabari said. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them meaning He will rule between them and separate. On the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ in this world, so He will reward the obedient and punish the disobedient.
10:94: The Almighty's saying: If you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but what is meant is someone else, i.e. you are not in doubt but not in doubt. Abu Omar Muhammad bin Abdul Wahid Al-Zahid said: I heard the two Imams Tha'lab and Al-Mubarrad say: The meaning of If you are in doubt is say, O Muhammad, to the disbeliever, if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you. Then ask those who read the Scripture before you i.e. O idol worshipper, if you are in doubt about the Qur'an, then ask those who converted to Islam from the Jews, meaning Abdullah bin Salam and his likes, because the idol worshippers used to acknowledge that the Jews were more knowledgeable than them because they were people of the Scripture, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called them to ask those who acknowledged that they were more knowledgeable than them, whether God would send a messenger after Moses. Al-Qutbi said: This is addressed to those who were not certain of denying or believing Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, but rather were in doubt. It was said: What is meant by the address is the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and no one else. The meaning is: If you were to be in doubt about what We have informed you of, and you asked the People of the Book, they would remove your doubt. It was also said: Doubt is a tightness of the chest, meaning if your chest is tight due to the disbelief of these people, then be patient, and ask those who read the Book before you to tell you about the patience of the prophets before you in the face of the harm of their people and how their affair ended. Doubt in the language is originally tightness. It is said: He tightened the garment with a knot until it becomes like a vessel. Likewise, the ties of a traveller’s table are stretched until they contract, so doubt tightens the chest and tightens it until it becomes tight. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl Abu Bakr said: The letter fa with the conditional letters does not require the action nor does it confirm it, and the evidence for that is what was narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him: He said when this verse was revealed: By God, I do not doubt - then he resumed speaking and said - The truth has come to you from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters meaning the doubters and skeptics.
10:95: And do not be among those who deny the signs of God, lest you be among the losers. The address in these two verses is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others are meant.
10:96: The Almighty says: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe. This was discussed in this surah. Qatada said: That is, those upon whom the wrath and anger of God has come into effect because of their disobedience will not believe.
10:97: Even if every sign came to them The feminine form of every is used to mean, even if every sign came to them. Until they see the painful punishment then they will believe and it will not benefit them.
10:98: The Almighty said: Why was there not a city that believed? Al-Akhfash and Al-Kisa'i said: meaning why not. In the Mushaf of Abi and Ibn Mas'ud, why not. The root of lawla in speech is to incite or indicate the prevention of something because of the existence of something else. The meaning of the verse is understood to negate the belief of the people of the cities, then He excepted the people of Yunus, so according to the wording it is a discontinuous exception, and according to the meaning it is connected, because its meaning is that the people of the city did not believe except the people of Yunus. The accusative in people is the correct way, and Sibawayh also included it in the chapter on what is only accusative. An-Nahhas said: Except the people of Yunus is accusative because it is an exception that is not from the first, meaning but the people of Yunus, this is the saying of Al-Kisa'i, Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra'. It is permissible. Except the people of Yunus is in the nominative case, and among the best things said about the nominative case is what Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is other than the people of Yunus, so when he came with except, he parsed the noun that comes after it with the parsing of other than as he said: Every brother who leaves his brother, by your father's life, except Al-Farqadhan It was narrated in the story of the people of Yunus from a group of commentators: That the people of Yunus were in Nineveh in the land of Mosul and they used to worship idols, so God sent Yunus, peace be upon him, to them calling them to Islam and to abandon what they were doing, but they refused. It was said: He stayed calling them for nine years and despaired of their faith, so it was said to him: Tell them that the punishment will come to them in the morning in three days, so he did, and they said: He is a man who does not lie, so watch him, if he stays with you and among you, then there is no harm upon you, but if he departs from you, then the punishment will undoubtedly descend. So when night came, Yunus prepared provisions and left them, but in the morning they did not find him, so they repented and called upon God and put on hairdressers and separated mothers and children from people and animals, and they returned the grievances in that state. Ibn Masoud said: A man would come to a stone on which the foundation of his building had been placed, and he would uproot it and return it, and the punishment from them, according to what was narrated from Ibn Abbas, was two-thirds of a mile. And it was narrated that it was a mile. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, that they were covered by a shade that was red and it kept getting closer until they felt its heat between their shoulders. Ibn Jubayr said: The punishment covered them as a garment covers a grave. When their repentance was valid, God lifted the punishment from them. Al-Tabari said: The people of Yunus were singled out from among all the nations in that He accepted their repentance after they witnessed the punishment. This was mentioned by a group of commentators. Al-Zajjaj said: The punishment did not befall them, but they saw the sign that indicated the punishment. If they had seen the punishment itself, faith would not have benefited them. Killing: Al-Zajjaj’s statement is good: Because the witnessing that does not benefit repentance with it is being afflicted with punishment like the story of Pharaoh. That is why he brought the story of Jonah on the same level as the story of Pharaoh because he was faithful when he saw the punishment and it did not benefit him, and the people of Jonah repented to that. This is supported by his statement, peace be upon him: God accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not seen the gargle. The gargle is the death rattle, and that is the state of being possessed by death, but not before that. And God knows best. The meaning of what we have said has been narrated from Ibn Mas’ud, that when [the people of Yunus] were promised the punishment for three days, it departed from them, and in the morning they did not find it, so they repented and separated their mothers and children. This indicates that their repentance was before they saw the sign of the punishment. And it will come with a clear chain of transmission in Surat As-Saffat, God willing. And the meaning of We removed from them the punishment of disgrace is that the punishment that Yunus promised them would befall them, not that they saw it with their own eyes or by illusion. Based on this, there is no problem, contradiction, or particularity, and God knows best. In short, the people of Nineveh were among the fortunate in their foreknowledge. It has been narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Caution does not avert fate, but supplication averts fate. This is because God Almighty says: Except the people of Yunus, when they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: That is the day of Ashura. God Almighty says: And We gave them enjoyment for a time. It was said: until their appointed time, as Al-Suddi said. It was also said: until they go to Paradise or to Hell, as Ibn Abbas said.
10:99: The Almighty said: And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together. That is, He would have forced them to Him. All of them is an emphasis on whoever. According to Sibawayh, all of them is in the accusative case as a state. Al-Akhfash said: He used the phrase all of them after all as an emphasis, like His saying: Do not take two gods (al-Nahl 16:51). God the Almighty said: Would you then compel mankind until they become believers? Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was keen on the faith of all people, so God the Almighty informed him that no one would believe except he who was destined for happiness in the first mention, and no one would go astray except he who was destined for misery in the first mention. It was said: What is meant by the people here is Abu Talib, and this is also from Ibn Abbas.
10:100: The Almighty said: And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of God what is negated, meaning that a soul should not believe except by His judgment, destiny, will and desire. And He places the impurity Al-Hasan, Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal read it and we place it with the letter noon for emphasis. Impurity means torment, with the letter ra with the damma and the letter ra with the kasra are two dialects. Upon those who do not reason is the command and prohibition of God Almighty.
10:101: The Almighty said: "Say: Look at what is in the heavens and the earth." This is a command to the unbelievers to consider and look at the creations that indicate the Creator and the One capable of perfection. This meaning has been discussed in more than one place in detail. And what avails is negated, meaning it will not avail. It was said: it is interrogative, the meaning is what does it avail? The verses mean the evidence. And the warnings mean the messengers, the plural of warner, which is the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. From a people who do not believe meaning from those who were previously known by God that they would not believe.
10:102: The Almighty says: Do they then await anything but the like of the days of those who passed on before them? The days here mean events. It is said: So-and-so is knowledgeable about the days of the Arabs, meaning their events. Qatada said: He means the events of God with the people of Noah, Aad, Thamud, and others. The Arabs call punishment days and blessings days, like the Almighty's saying: And remind them of the days of God (Ibrahim 14:5). Everything that has passed for you of good or evil is days. Then wait means wait, and this is a threat and a warning. Indeed, I am with you among those who wait meaning those who wait for the appointment of my Lord.
10:103: The Almighty said: Then We will save Our messengers and those who believe meaning, according to Our way, if We send down a punishment upon a people, We will extract from among them the messengers and believers. The meaning of then is, then know that We will save Our messengers. Thus is it incumbent upon Us meaning, it is obligatory upon Us, because He has informed and there is no contradiction in His information. Ya'qub read: Then We will save with a lightened pronunciation. Al-Kisa'i, Hafs, and Ya'qub read: We will save the believers with a lightened pronunciation, while the rest stressed it. They are two eloquent languages: Anja yanji, inja', and Naja yanji, tanjiyyah with one meaning.
10:104: God Almighty says: "Say, 'O mankind,' meaning the infidels of Mecca. 'If you are in doubt about my religion,' meaning in doubt about the religion of Islam, I call you to it. 'Then I do not worship those you worship besides God,' of idols that do not have reason. 'But I worship God, who takes your souls,' meaning He causes you to die and takes your souls. 'And I have been commanded to be among the believers,' meaning those who believe in the verses of their Lord.
10:105: The Almighty said: And that you set your face upright "that is in apposition to that I be", meaning it was said to me: "Be among the believers and set your face upright". Ibn Abbas said: "Your work", and it was said: "Your soul", meaning: "Be steadfast by turning to what you have been commanded to do of the religion". "Hanif" means upright in it, inclined away from every religion. Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib, may God be pleased with him, said: I thanked God when He guided my heart from polytheism to the true religion. Its derivation has already been mentioned in Al-An’am, and praise be to God. And do not be among those who associate others with God. That is, it was said to me, Do not associate others with God. The address was to him, but someone else was meant.
10:106: And also His saying: And do not invoke meaning do not worship besides God that which will not benefit you if you worship it, nor harm you if you disobey it. But if you do meaning worship other than God, then you will be among the wrongdoers meaning those who place worship in the wrong place.
10:107: God Almighty says: And if God should touch you with adversity meaning, He afflicts you with it. There is no remover meaning, there is no repeller “of it except Him. And if He intends for you good” meaning, He afflicts you with ease and blessings, “there is no repeller of His favor. He causes it to fall” meaning, with whatever He intends of good and evil. “Whomsoever He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving” of the sins and errors of His servants, the Most Merciful to His friends in the Hereafter.
10:108: The Almighty said: Say, 'O mankind, the truth has come to you' meaning the Qur'an. It was also said: the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. "From your Lord. So whoever is guided" meaning believes in Muhammad and has faith in what he brought. He is only guided for [the benefit of] himself meaning for his own salvation. And whoever goes astray meaning abandons the Messenger and the Qur'an and follows idols and statues. He only goes astray to his own detriment meaning that the consequences of that are upon himself. And I am not a guardian over you meaning a guardian who will preserve your deeds. I am only a messenger. Ibn Abbas said: The verse of the sword abrogated it.
10:109: The Almighty said: And follow what is revealed to you and be patient. It was said: It was abrogated by the verse on fighting. It was also said: It was not abrogated, and its meaning is: Be patient in obedience and avoid disobedience. Ibn Abbas said: When this was revealed, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered the Ansar and did not gather anyone else with them and said: You will find after me self-interest, so be patient until you meet me at the Cistern. And Anas said something similar. Then Anas said: But they were not patient, so he commanded them to be patient as God Almighty commanded him. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Hassan says about that: Shall I not tell Muawiyah bin Harb, the Commander of the Faithful, my words? We are patient and we will give you respite until the Day of Mutual Loss and Dispute. Until God judges, and He is the best of judges. This is a subject and a predicate, because He, the Almighty, judges only with the truth. Surah Yunus has been completed, and all praise is due to God alone.
11:1: It was narrated in Makkah according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: Except for one verse, which is the verse: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day (Hu: 114). Abu Muhammad Al-Darimi narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Ka'b that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Recite Surat Hud on Friday. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, I have grown old! He said: Hud, Al-Waqi'ah, Al-Mursalat, 'Amma Yatas'alun, and Idha Ash-Shams Kuwwirat have made my hair turn gray. He said: This is a hasan ghareeb hadith, and some of this has been narrated as mursal. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah included it in Nawader Al-Usul: Sufyan bin Wakee' narrated to us that Muhammad bin Bishr narrated to us on the authority of Ali bin Salih on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Abu Juhaifa who said: "They said: O Messenger of God, we see that you have grown old!" He said: Hud and its sisters have made my hair turn gray. Abu Abdullah said: Fear causes gray hair because fear stuns the soul and dries up the moisture of the body. Under every hair there is a spring, and from it sweats. When fear dries up its moisture, the springs dry up, so the hair dries up and turns white, just as you see green plants with their watering place. When their watering is gone, they dry up and turn white. The hair of an old man turns white because its moisture is gone and his skin dries up. The soul is stunned by the threat of God and the horrors of what the report from God has brought, so it withers, and its water dries up because of that threat and horror that it has brought, and because of that it turns gray. God the Most High said: A Day when He will make children gray-haired (al-Muzzammil 73:17). They turned gray because of fear. As for Surah Hud, when it mentioned the nations and what befell them of the immediate wrath of God the Most High, when the people of certainty recite it, their hearts will see His kingdom, His authority, and His moments of smiting His enemies. If they died from fear, it would be right for them, but God, Blessed and Exalted be His name, is gentle with them at those times until they read His words. As for its sisters, there are similar surahs, such as Al-Haqqah, Sa’ala Sa’il, Idha Ash-Shams Kuwwirat, and Al-Qari’ah. In reciting these surahs, there is that which reveals to the hearts of those who know His power and might, so that souls are amazed by it and heads turn gray. I said, and it has been said that what turned the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) gray in Surah Hud was His saying, So stand firm as you are commanded (Hud 11:112), as will be explained, God willing. And “Yazid ibn Abaan said: I saw the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) in my dream, so I recited to him Surah Hud, and when I finished it, he said: O Zaid, this is the recitation, so where is the weeping?” Our scholars said, Abu Ja’far An-Nahhas said: It is said, “This is Hud, so know that without a tanween, as it is the name of the surah, because if you named Yazid’s wife, it would not be declined. This is the saying of Al-Khalil and Sibawayh.” And Isa bin Omar says: This is Hud with the tanween as the name of the surah, and likewise if he named a woman Zayd, because when it was quiescent in the middle it became light and was declined, and if you wanted to delete it, you declined according to what everyone said, so you said: This is Hud and you mean Surat Hud, Sibawayh said: The evidence for this is that you say this is Ar-Rahman, and if you did not mean this Surat Ar-Rahman you would not have said this. God the Almighty said: Alif, Lam, Ra. This has been discussed previously. He wrote means this is a book. He made His verses perfect is in the nominative case as an attribute of the book. The best that has been said about the meaning of He made His verses perfect is the statement of Qatada, meaning He made them all perfect, with no fault or falsehood in them. Perfection prevents speech from corruption, meaning they are organized in a perfect system that is not affected by contradiction or fault. Ibn Abbas said: meaning no book abrogated them, unlike the Torah and the Gospel. Based on this, the meaning is: He made some of His verses perfect by making an abrogator not abrogated. This has been discussed previously. The generic noun may also refer to the type, so it is said: I ate Zayd’s food, meaning some of his food. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: He made His verses perfect with commands and prohibitions. Then He made them detailed with promises and threats, rewards and punishments. Qatada said: God made them perfect from falsehood, then He made them detailed with what is lawful and what is unlawful. Mujahid: He made them perfect as a whole, then He explained by mentioning verse by verse all that is needed of evidence for monotheism, prophethood, resurrection, and other things. It was said: It was collected in the Preserved Tablet, then detailed in the revelation. It was said: Fussilat was revealed star by star for you to contemplate. Ikrimah read Fussilat in a lightened form, meaning I ruled with truth. Min ladan means from Alaikum means Wise means He who rules over matters. Aware of everything that is and is not.
11:2: The Almighty said: That you worship none but God. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: That is, with not, that is, it was made clear and then detailed that you worship none but God. Al-Zajjaj said: So that, that is, it was made clear and then detailed that you worship none but God. It was said: He ordered His Messenger to tell the people not to worship except God. Indeed, I am from Him to you, that is, from God. A warner, that is, one who frightens with His punishment and His power for those who disobey Him. And a bearer of good tidings of pleasure and Paradise for those who obey Him. It was said: It is from the statement of God first and last, that is, worship none but God. Indeed, I am from Him to you a warner", that is, God is a warner to you against worshipping other than Him, as He said: "And God warns you of Himself" (Al Imran 3:28).
11:3: The Almighty's saying: And seek forgiveness from your Lord is in apposition to the first. Then repent to Him meaning return to Him with obedience and worship. Al-Farra' said: Then here has the meaning of and, meaning and repent to Him, because seeking forgiveness is repentance, and repentance is seeking forgiveness. It was said: Seek forgiveness from Him for your past sins, and repent to Him for the new one whenever you commit them. Some of the righteous said: Seeking forgiveness without ceasing is the repentance of liars. This meaning was presented in full in Al-Imran. And in Al-Baqarah when He said: And do not take the verses of God in jest. It was said: The mention of seeking forgiveness was presented first because forgiveness is the desired goal, and repentance is the reason for it, so forgiveness comes first in what is desired and last in the reason. It is possible that the meaning is seek forgiveness from Him for minor sins, and repent to Him for major sins. He will grant you good enjoyment. This is the fruit of seeking forgiveness and repentance, meaning He will grant you benefits from abundant provision and a comfortable life, and He will not uproot you with torment as He did to those who were destroyed before you. It was also said: He will grant you good enjoyment, and the root of enjoyment is to prolong, and from it is the word God granted you enjoyment and He granted you enjoyment. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Good enjoyment is abandoning creation and turning to the truth. It was also said: It is contentment with what exists and abandoning grief over what is lost. Until a specified term. It was said: It is death. It was also said: The Resurrection. It was also said: Entering Paradise. According to this, good enjoyment is protection from every evil and feared matter, from what will happen in the grave and other terrors and distress of the Resurrection. The first is more apparent, because of His statement in this Surah: "And, O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in [continuing] showers and add you strength to your strength." (Hud 11:52). This ends with death, which is the specified term. And God knows best. Muqatil said: They refused, so the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) invoked God against them, and they were afflicted with famine for seven years until they ate burnt bones, filthy carcasses, and dogs. And every possessor of virtue will be given his virtue meaning every one who does good deeds will be given the reward for his deeds. It was also said: And every one whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds will be given his virtue meaning Paradise, which is God’s virtue, so the metaphor in His statement: His virtue refers to God the Most High. Mujahid said: It is what a person expects from words he says with his tongue, or work he does with his hand or foot, or what he volunteers from his money, it is God’s virtue. He gives it to him if he believes, and He does not accept it from him if he is a disbeliever. But if they turn away, then indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great Day meaning the Day of Resurrection, which is great because of the horrors in it. It was also said: The great day is the day of Badr and others. And turn away may be in the past tense and the meaning is: And if they turn away, then say to them, indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great Day. It may be a future tense from which one of the two ta’s has been deleted, and the meaning is: Tell them that if you turn away, then I fear for you.
11:4: God Almighty says: To God is your return meaning after death. And He is over all things competent of reward and punishment.
11:5: The Almighty said: Indeed, they turn away their breasts to hide from Him. He informed us about the enmity of the polytheists towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers, and they thought that their conditions were hidden from God. They turn away their breasts means they conceal their enmity towards the Muslims, so this is the deletion. Ibn Abbas said: They conceal what is in their breasts of rancor and enmity, and they show the opposite. It was revealed about Al-Akhns bin Shuraik, who was a man of sweet speech and sweet talk. He would meet the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with what he liked, but would conceal from him what would displease him. Mujahid said: They turn away their breasts out of doubt and suspicion. Al-Hasan said: They turn away what is in them of disbelief. It was said: It was revealed about some hypocrites. When he passed by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would turn his chest and back, lower his head and cover his face, so that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not see him and call him to faith. Its meaning was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad, so the letter ha in minhu refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: The hypocrites said: If we close our doors, cover ourselves with our clothes, and turn our chests in enmity towards Muhammad, then who will know about us? So the verse was revealed. It was also said: Some Muslims used to cover their bodies and not expose them to the sky, so God, the Most High, explained that the act of worship is what their hearts contain of belief and what they show in word and deed. Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Ibad bin Ja’far that he heard Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, say: Indeed, they turn their chests to hide from Him He said: They did not have intercourse with women, nor did they go to the toilet while they were facing the sky, so this verse was revealed. Other than Muhammad ibn Abbad narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, they bend their chests without a nun after the waw, in the weight of tantu, and the meaning of tathnawi and the other two readings are close, because it is not tanwa until they bend it. It was said: Some of them would bend to the left of others in slandering the Muslims, and their ignorance reached the point that they thought that this was hidden from God Almighty. Li-yashfifu means to hide from Him, meaning from Muhammad or from God. Except when they cover themselves with their garments meaning they cover their heads with their garments. Qatada said: The most hidden thing a servant can be is when he bends his back, covers himself with his garment, and conceals his concern within himself.
11:6: The Almighty said: And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision. Ma is a negation, Min is redundant, and Dabbah is in the nominative case. The meaning is: And there is no creature. But upon God is its provision. Upon means Min, meaning from God is its provision. This is indicated by the statement of Mujahid: Everything that comes to it of provision is from God. It was said: Upon God meaning as a favor, not an obligation. It was said: A promise from Him that is true. This meaning was explained previously in An-Nisa and that nothing is obligatory upon Him, the Almighty. Rizqah is in the nominative case as a subject, and according to the Kufians as an adjective. The apparent meaning of the verse is general but its meaning is specific, because many of the creatures perish before they are provided with provision. It was said: It is general for every animal: And for you, an animal that has not been provided with sustenance to live, has been provided with its soul. The point of organization with what came before: That He, the Almighty, informed about the sustenance of everyone, and that He does not neglect to nurture it, so how could your conditions be hidden from Him, O group of disbelievers, while He provides for you?! And the animal is every animal that moves. And sustenance in reality is that which the living being is nourished by, and in it is the survival of its soul and the growth of its body. And sustenance cannot mean ownership, because animals are provided with sustenance and it is not correct to describe them as owning their fodder, and likewise children are provided with milk and it cannot be said: The milk in the breast belongs to the child. And God Almighty said: And in the heaven is your provision (al-Dhariyat 51:22) and we do not have ownership in the heaven, and because if sustenance were ownership, then if a person ate from the property of someone else, he would have eaten from the sustenance of someone else, and that is impossible, because the servant only eats his own sustenance. This meaning was mentioned in Al-Baqarah, and praise be to God. And it was said to some of them: Where do you eat from? He said: He who created the millstone brings it flour, and He who split the jaws is the Creator of provisions. Abu Usaid was asked: Where do you eat from? He said: Glory be to God, and God is the greatest! God provides for the dog, so will He not provide for Abu Usaid? Hatim al-Asamm was asked: Where do you eat from? He said: From God. He was asked: God sends down to you dinars and dirhams from the sky? He said: As if he has nothing but the sky! O man, the earth is his and the sky is his. If he does not give me my provision from the sky, He will bring it to me from the earth. And he recited: How can I fear poverty when God is my provider and the provider of this creation in hardship and ease? He provides sustenance for all creation, for the lizard in the desert, and for the whale in the sea. Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim mentioned in Nawadir al-Usul on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: When the Ash'aris, Abu Musa, Abu Malik, and Abu Amir, migrated and came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were widowed from provisions, they sent a man from them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him. When he reached the door of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he heard him reciting this verse: “And there is no creature on earth but that upon God is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage. All is in a clear register.” The man said: The Ash'aris are not the least of the creatures to God. So he returned and did not enter upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said to his companions: Be glad, relief has come to you. They thought nothing but that he had spoken to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and promised him. While they were like that, two men came to them carrying a bowl between them filled with bread and meat. They ate from it as much as they wanted, then some of them said to each other: If only we could return this food to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that he may fulfill his need. They said: The two men said: Take this food to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for we have already had our fill of it. Then they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, we have never seen food more abundant or tastier than the food you have sent. He said: I have not sent you any food. They told him that they had sent their companion. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him and he told him what he had done and what he had said to them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is something that God has provided for you. God the Almighty says: And He knows its place of rest meaning in the earth where it will take refuge. And its place of deposit meaning the place where it will die and be buried. This was said by Muqsim on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: Its place of rest is in the womb, and its place of deposit is in the loins. It was also said: He knows its place of rest in Paradise or in Hell. And its place of deposit is in the grave, as indicated by God the Almighty’s statement describing the people of Paradise and the people of Hell: An excellent place to settle and to stay Al-Furqan 25:76. Evil is the place to settle and to stay Al-Furqan 25:66. All is in a clear register meaning in the Preserved Tablet.
11:7: The Almighty said: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days. This was explained in Al-A'raf, and praise be to God. And His Throne was over the water. He explained that He created the Throne and the water before He created the earth and the heaven. Ka'b said: God created a green ruby and looked at it with awe, so it became water that trembles in fear of God Almighty. That is why the water trembles until now, even though it was still. Then He created the wind and made the water on its surface, then He placed the Throne on the water. Sa'id bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He was asked about the Almighty's saying: And His Throne was over the water, so he said: On what was the water? He said: On the surface of the wind. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Imran bin Husayn. He said: “I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a group of Banu Tamim came to him, and he said: ‘Accept the good report, O Banu Tamim.’ They said: ‘You have given us good report, so give us twice.’ Then some people from Yemen entered, and he said: ‘Accept the good report, O people of Yemen, since Banu Tamim did not accept it.’ They said: ‘We accept it. We came to learn about the religion, and to ask you about this matter, what was it?’ He said: ‘God was and there was nothing other than Him, and His throne was over the water. Then He created the heavens and the earth and wrote everything in the remembrance. Then a man came to me and said: ‘O Imran, catch your she-camel, for she has gone.’ So I went looking for her, and suddenly a mirage was crossing her path. By God, I gave birth to her and she had gone and I had not yet risen.” God the Almighty said: That He may test you as to which of you is best in deed. That is, He created this to test His servants by considering and deducing evidence of the perfection of His power and the Resurrection. Qatada said: The meaning of Which of you is best in deed (Hud 11:11) is which of you is most perfect in mind. Al-Hasan and Sufyan al-Thawri said: Which of you is most ascetic in this world. “It was mentioned that Jesus, peace be upon him, passed by a sleeping man and said: O sleeper, get up and worship. He said: O spirit of God, you have worshipped. He said: And what did you worship? He said: I have left this world for its people. He said: Sleep, for you have surpassed the worshippers.” Ad-Dahhak: Which of you is most grateful? Muqatil: Which of you is most pious to God? Ibn Abbas: Which of you works most in obeying God the Almighty. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Which of you is best in deed? He said: Which of you is best in mind, most wary of the prohibitions of God, and most quick to obey God. So he gathered all the sayings, and this will also come in Al-Kahf, God willing. The meaning of the test has already been presented. And if you say, ‘You will be resurrected,’ meaning, if you were to indicate, O Muhammad, the resurrection, after death, and you mentioned that to the polytheists, they would say: This is magic. And in was broken because it is a subject after the saying. Sibawayh narrated the opening. Those who disbelieve will surely say, the opening of the lam is because it is an advanced verb with no pronoun in it, and after it they will say, because it has a pronoun in it. And magic means false deception, because magic is false according to them. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read This is nothing but a clear magician as a metaphor for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
11:8: The Almighty said: And if We postponed the punishment from them for a specified term The lam in لإنis for swearing, and the answer isلقولنا. The meaning of to a term is to a specified term and a known time, so the term here is the period, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and the majority of commentators. The root of the term ummah is the group, so the time and years were expressed by the term ummah because the ummah is in it. It was said: It is with the deletion of the complement, and the meaning is until the coming of a nation in which there are no believers, so they deserve destruction. Or the extinction of a nation in which there are believers, so no one remains after its extinction. The term ummah is a common noun that is said in eight ways: The ummah is the group, as in the Almighty's saying: And he found upon him a nation of mankind (al-Qasas 28:23). The ummah is also the followers of the prophets, peace be upon them. The ummah is the man who gathers goodness and is followed, as in the Almighty's saying: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth (al-Nahl 16:120). The nation is the religion and creed, as in the saying of God the Almighty: Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion (al-Zukhruf 43:23). The nation is the time and place, as in the saying of God the Almighty: And if We should delay the punishment from them for a specified term (al-Zukhruf 43:23). And also in His saying: And remember after a term (Yusuf 12:45). The nation is the stature, which is the height and height of a person. It is said from that: So-and-so has a good nation, meaning stature. The nation is the man who is alone in his religion and no one shares it with him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl will be sent as a single nation. And the mother nation, it is said: This is the nation of Zayd, meaning the mother of Zayd. He will say, ‘What is holding it back?’ meaning the punishment. And they said this either as a denial of the punishment because it was delayed from them, or in hastening it and mocking it, meaning what is holding it back from us: Behold, the day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them. It was said: It is the killing of the polytheists at Badr, and Gabriel’s killing of the mockers, as will come. And what they used to mock befell them means it descended and encompassed them. That which they used to mock means the recompense for what they used to mock, and the complement is omitted.
11:9: The Almighty said: And if We let man taste mercy from Us Man is a common name for the species in all disbelievers. It is said that man here is Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and it was revealed about him. It was also said about Abdullah bin Abi Umayya Al-Makhzumi. Mercy means a blessing. Then We took it away from him means We deprived him of it. Indeed, he despairs means he despairs of mercy. Ungrateful for blessings, he is ungrateful for them, Ibn Al-A'rabi said. An-Nahhas: Li'awus from Ya'isa and Ya'as, and Sibawayh narrated Ya'isa ya'as on the basis of the verb yaf'al, and its equivalent is Hasab yahusub and Na'am yan'am, and Ya'as ya'as, and some of them say Ya'as ya'as, and in Arabic speech only these four letters are known from the sound ones that came on the basis of the verb yaf'al, and there is a difference in one of them. It is Ya'as and Yawus on the basis of abundance like Fakhur for exaggeration.
11:10: The Almighty said: And if We let him taste [good] blessings meaning health, prosperity, and abundance in provision. After a hardship has befallen him meaning after distress, poverty, and hardship. He will surely say, 'The evil deeds have departed from me' meaning the sins that harm their doer such as distress and poverty. Indeed, he is exultant and boastful meaning he rejoices and boasts about the abundance he has attained and forgets to thank God for it. It is said: a proud man if he boasts - and fakhkur is for exaggeration - Yaqub al-Qari' said: Some of the people of Madinah read l-farah with a damma on the ra' as they say: a man who is clever, cautious, and sneaky. In both languages, it is permissible to use the sukoon because of the weight of the damma and kasra.
11:11: The Almighty said: Except those who are patient meaning the believers, He praised them for their patience in adversity. It is in the accusative case. Al-Akhfash said: It is an exception not from the first, meaning but those who are patient and do righteous deeds in the states of blessing and adversity. Al-Farraa said: It is an exception from And if We let him taste it meaning from man, for man means people, and people includes the disbeliever and the believer, so it is a connected exception and it is good. For those is forgiveness is subject and predicate. And a reward is conjoined. Great is an adjective.
11:12: The Almighty said: Perhaps you will abandon some of what is revealed to you meaning perhaps because of the greatness of what you see from them of disbelief and denial you imagine that they will remove you from some of what you are upon. It was said: When they said Why was not a treasure sent down to him or an angel brought with him? they intended to stop cursing their gods, so this verse was revealed. The meaning of the speech is a question, meaning are you going to stop what contains cursing their gods as they asked you? And the command to convey was emphasized to him, like His saying: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord (al-Ma’idah 5:5). It was said: The meaning of the speech is negation with exclusion, meaning that you will not do that, but rather convey to them everything that was revealed to you, and that is because the polytheists of Mecca said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If we bring a book that does not contain cursing of our gods, we will follow you, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, intended to stop cursing their gods, so this verse was revealed. God the Almighty said: And your breast is constricted by it is in apposition to abandoning and your breast is raised by it, and the ha in by it refers back to what or to some, or to conveying, or to denying. He said constricted and did not say constricted to resemble abandoning which preceded it, and because constriction is an accident, and constriction is more necessary than it. That they say is in the accusative case, meaning that they hate to say, or lest they say, like His statement: God makes clear to you, lest you go astray (An-Nisa’: 4), meaning lest you go astray. Or lest they say. Why means why was a treasure sent down to him or an angel come with him to confirm him, said Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah bin Al-Mughirah Al-Makhzumi, so God the Almighty said: O Muhammad, You are only a warner you are only required to warn them, not to bring them what they suggest of signs. And God is Disposer of affairs meaning Guardian and Witness.
11:13: The Almighty said: Or do they say, ‘He invented it’? ‘Or’ means ‘rather,’ and it was mentioned before in Yunus, meaning, you have removed their excuse and their doubt about your prophethood with this Qur’an, and you have provided them with an argument with it. If they say, ‘You invented it’ - meaning, you made it up - then let them produce something similar to it, invented according to their claim. And call upon whomever you can besides God, meaning, of the priests and helpers.
11:14: The Almighty said: If they do not respond to you meaning in the exchange and it was not prepared for them, then the proof has been established against them, since they are the eloquent tongues and the owners of the most eloquent tongues. Then know that it has been revealed with the knowledge of God and know the truth of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and know and that there is no god but Him, so are you Muslims? An interrogative meaning a command. The meaning of this verse has been discussed previously, and that the Qur'an is miraculous in the introduction to the book. Praise be to God. And He said: Say, then bring and after it. If they do not respond to you and He did not say to you, so it was said: It is to change the address from the individual to the plural for the sake of glorification and magnification, and the leader may be addressed in the same way as the group. It was said: The pronoun in for you and in so know refers to everyone, meaning let everyone know that it was revealed with the knowledge of God, as Mujahid said. It was also said: The pronoun in for you and in so know refers to the polytheists, and the meaning is: If the one you call to help does not respond to you, and you are not prepared to exchange, then know that it was revealed with the knowledge of God. It was also said: The pronoun in for you refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to the believers, and in so know refers to the polytheists.
11:15: It has three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Whoever was “was” is redundant, and for this reason He made the answer definite and said: We will call them as Al-Farra’ said. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever was is in the place of the definite with the condition, and its answer is We will call them meaning whoever is meant, and the first in the wording is past and the second is future, as Zuhair said: Whoever fears the causes of death will meet them, even if he seeks the causes of heaven with a ladder. Scholars differed in the interpretation of this verse. It was said: It was revealed about the disbelievers. Ad-Dahhak said this, and An-Nahhas chose this, based on the evidence of the verse that follows it: Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire. That is, whoever among them does kinship or charity, We will reward him for it in this world, with physical health and abundant provision, but he will have no good deed in the Hereafter. This meaning was presented in full in Bara’ah. It was also said: What is meant by the verse are the believers, that is, whoever intends the reward of this world through his work, the reward will be hastened for him and nothing will be diminished in this world, and he will have the punishment in the Hereafter because he intended only this world. This is like what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Actions are but by intentions. The servant is only given according to his intention and according to his conscience. This is something agreed upon among nations and religions. It was also said: It is for the hypocrites. In the hadith, it is said to al-Munafiqun 63:You fasted, prayed, gave charity, struggled, and read so that it might be said, and it has been said. Then he said: These are the first to be set on fire by the Fire. Narrated by Abu Hurairah, then he cried bitterly and said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke the truth. God the Almighty said: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments and he recited the two verses. Muslim included it in his Sahih with the same meaning, and so did At-Tirmidhi. It was said: The verse is general in all those who intend by their actions other than God the Almighty, whether they have a basis in faith or not. This was said by Mujahid and Maymun ibn Mihran, and Muawiyah may God have mercy on him agreed with him. Maymun ibn Mihran said: No one does a good deed except that he will be rewarded for it. If he is a sincere Muslim, he will be rewarded in this world and the Hereafter, and if he is a disbeliever, he will be rewarded in this world. It was said: Whoever desires the worldly life by going on a campaign with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and in it, meaning in the reward of the campaigners and it will not be diminished from it. This is specific, but the correct view is general. Second: Some scholars said: The meaning of this verse is the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Actions are but by intentions. This verse indicates that whoever fasts in Ramadan, not for Ramadan, it does not count for Ramadan, and it indicates that whoever performs ablution to cool down and clean himself does not count as an act of worship other than prayer, and so on with everything that is similar in meaning. Third: Most scholars have said that this verse is absolute, as is the verse in al-Shura 42:“Whoever desires the harvest of the Hereafter, We increase for him his harvest. And whoever desires the harvest of this world, We give him thereof.” (al-Shura 42:42) The verse. Likewise, Whoever desires the reward of this world, We give him thereof. (Aal ‘Imran: 145) The verse in Subhan has restricted and explained it: Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend. (al-Isra’ 17:18) to His saying prohibited. So the Almighty informed that the servant intends and desires, and God Almighty decrees what he desires. Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding His statement: Whoever desires the life of this world, that it was abrogated by His statement: Whoever desires the immediate. What we have mentioned is correct, and that it is a matter of generality and restriction. Similar to it is His statement: “And when My servants ask you concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me” (al-Baqarah 2:186). This appears to be a report about always answering every supplicant in every situation, but it is not so, because the Most High said: Then He will remove that to which you call, if He wills (al-An’am 6:41). Abrogation in reports is not permissible, because it is impossible for rational obligations to change, and because it is impossible to lie about God the Most High. As for reports about legal rulings, it is permissible to abrogate them with a difference of opinion about them, as mentioned in the fundamentals, and its explanation will come in An-Nahl, God willing.
11:16: The Almighty's saying: Those are the ones who will have nothing in the Hereafter except the Fire refers to eternity, and the believer will not remain eternal, because the Almighty said: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that (al-Nisa 4:116) the verse. It is interpreted as if this hypocrite had met with disbelief. It was said: The meaning is that they will have nothing but the Fire for a specified number of days, then he will be taken out, either by intercession or by being seized. The verse requires a threat of taking away faith, and in the previous hadith he means disbelief and especially hypocrisy, since it is polytheism as was explained previously in An-Nisa and will come at the end of Al-Kahf. And in vain is what they used to do is subject and predicate. Abu Hatim said: And the ha' was deleted. An-Nahhas said: This does not need to be deleted, because it is in the sense of a source, meaning and in vain is his work. In the wording of Abu and Abdullah: And in vain is what they used to do and ma is redundant, meaning and they used to do vain.
11:17: The Almighty's saying: Is he who has clear evidence from his Lord is the beginning and the predicate is omitted, meaning is he who has clear evidence from his Lord in following the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and who has with him the virtue that makes him clear like others who desire the life of this world and its adornments?! On the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein and Al-Hassan bin Abi Al-Hassan. Ibn Zayd also said: The one who has clear evidence is he who follows the Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And a witness from Him follows him from God, and he is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that what is meant by His saying: Is he who has clear evidence from his Lord is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the statement refers back to His saying: And your breast is constrained by it, meaning is he who has with him a statement from God, and a miracle like the Qur'an, and with him a witness like Gabriel - as will come - and the previous books gave glad tidings of him, his breast is constrained by the delivery, and he knows that God will not deliver him. The ha in his Lord refers back to him, and His saying: And a witness from Him follows him. And Ikrimah narrated from Ibn Abbas that it is Gabriel, and this is the opinion of Mujahid and Al-Nakha’i. The ha in from him is God, the Almighty, meaning that a witness from God the Almighty recites the explanation and proof. Mujahid said: The witness is the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hanafiyyah said: I said to my father, are you the witness? He said: I wish I was him, but it is the tongue of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And it was said: He is Ali bin Abi Talib. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: He is Ali bin Abi Talib. And it was narrated from Ali that he said: There is no man from Quraysh except that a verse or two verses were revealed about him, so a man said to him: What was revealed about you? Ali said: And a witness from him recites it. And it was said: The witness is the image of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his face and appearance, because whoever has virtue and intelligence and looks at the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knows that he is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So the ha in this case refers back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to the opinion of Ibn Zayd and others. It was said that the witness is the Qur’an in its organization and eloquence, and the many meanings of it in one word, said Al-Husayn bin Al-Fadl, so the ha in minhu is for the Qur’an. Al-Farra’ said that some of them said: And a witness from it follows it the Gospel, and if it was before it, then it follows the Qur’an in belief, and the ha in minhu is for God the Almighty. It was said: The evidence is the knowledge of God for which the hearts are enlightened, and the witness that it follows is the mind that was implanted in his brain and his chest was enlightened by its light. And before it means before the Gospel. The Book of Moses is raised by the beginning, Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is and the Book of Moses follows it before it, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is described in the Book of Moses They find it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel in the accusative, and Al-Mahdawi narrated it from Al-Kalbi, it is conjoined with the ha in yataluhu and the meaning is: And the Book of Moses is recited by Gabriel, peace be upon him, and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said the meaning is before it Gabriel recited the Book of Moses to Moses. It is also permissible, according to what Ibn Abbas mentioned from this statement, to raise book so that the meaning is: and before it the book of Moses as well, meaning Gabriel recited it to Moses as he recited the Qur’an to Muhammad. Imam is in the accusative case as a state. And mercy is conjoined. Those believe in it refers to the Children of Israel, meaning they believe in what is in the Torah of good tidings about you, and only those who came later disbelieved in you, so they are the ones whose appointment is the Fire, as narrated by Al-Qushayri. The ha in in it may be the Qur’an, or it may be for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And whoever disbelieves in it meaning the Qur’an or the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Of the parties means of all religions, according to Qatadah. And Saeed bin Jubair said the same: the parties are the people of all religions, because they form parties. And it was said: Quraysh and their allies. Then the Fire is his appointment meaning he is from the people of the Fire. And Hassan recited: You brought her to the pools of death, she is a victim, so the fire is her destination and death will meet her. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Yunus on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, no one of this nation, Jew or Christian, hears of me and then dies without believing in that with which I was sent, but that he will be among the companions of the Fire.” So be not in doubt means in doubt. About it means about the Qur’an. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord meaning the Qur’an from God, as Muqatil said. Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is, so be not in doubt that the disbeliever is in the Fire. Indeed, it is the truth means the true statement that will be, and the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is all those who are accountable.
11:18: God the Almighty said: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God? That is, no one is more unjust to themselves than they are because they invent a lie against God, so they attributed His words to someone other than Him, and they claimed that He had a partner and a son, and they said about the idols, These are our intercessors with God. "Those will be presented before their Lord," that is, He will hold them accountable for their deeds. "And the witnesses will say," meaning the guardian angels, according to Mujahid and others. Sufyan said: I asked Al-A'mash about the witnesses, and he said: the angels. Ad-Dahhak: They are the prophets and messengers, his evidence is his statement: "How will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these?"
