(An-Nisa': 41). It was said: the angels, prophets, and scholars who conveyed the messages. Qatada said: He meant all of creation. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Safwan bin Mahraz, on the authority of Ibn Omar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in which he said: “As for the disbelievers and hypocrites, they will be called out in front of all creation: These are the ones who lied about God.” The curse of God be upon the wrongdoers, meaning His distance, His wrath, and His exclusion from His mercy upon those who put worship in the wrong place.
11:19: The Almighty’s saying: Those who hinder [people] from the way of God It is possible that (those) is in the accusative case as a description of the wrongdoers, and it is possible that it is in the nominative case, meaning they are those. It was said: It is the beginning of a speech from God the Almighty, meaning they are those who disbelieve themselves and others about faith and obedience. And they seek to make it crooked meaning they divert people from it to sins and polytheism. And they are disbelievers in the Hereafter He repeated the word they for emphasis.
11:20: The Almighty said: Those were not able to escape on earth meaning they could not escape the punishment of God. Ibn Abbas said: They were not able to command the earth so that it would swallow them up. And they had no protectors besides God meaning helpers, and min is redundant. It was said: ma means who, and its meaning is: Those were not able to escape, neither they nor those who had protectors besides God, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. The punishment will be doubled for them meaning according to the extent of their disbelief and sins. They were not able to hear ma is in the accusative case so that the meaning is: because they were able to hear. And they did not see and they did not use that in hearing and seeing the truth. The Arabs say: I rewarded him for what he did and for what he did, so they delete the ba' once and keep it another time, and Sibawayh recited: I have commanded you to do good, so do what I have commanded you to do, for I have left you with wealth and lineage. It is possible that ma is an adverb, and the meaning is: It will be doubled for them forever, meaning the time they are able to hear and see, and God, the Most High, will make them in Hell able to do that forever. It is possible that ma is a negative that has no place, since the speech was completed before it, and stopping at the punishment is sufficient, and the meaning is: They were not able in this world to hear with a hearing that would negate them, nor to see with a guided sight. Al-Farra’ said: They were not able to hear, because God led them astray in the Preserved Tablet. Al-Zajjaj said: Because of their hatred for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and their enmity towards him, they were not able to hear from him nor understand from him. Al-Nahhas said: This is well-known in the speech of the Arabs. It is said: So-and-so cannot look at so-and-so if that is too much for him.
11:21: The Almighty’s saying: Those are the ones who have lost their souls is a subject and predicate. And what they used to invent has been lost to them meaning their inventions have been lost to them and have been destroyed.
11:22: The Almighty’s saying: La Jarm The scholars have different opinions about it. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: La Jarm means right, so La and Jarm are one word for them, and An is in the nominative case for them, and this is the opinion of Al-Farra and Muhammad bin Yazid, narrated by Al-Nahhas. Al-Mahdawi said: Al-Khalil also said that its meaning is inevitably and inevitably, and this is also the opinion of Al-Farra, mentioned by Al-Tha’labi. Al-Zajjaj said: La here is a negation and it is a response to their saying: The idols benefit them, as if the meaning is that it does not benefit them, and Jarm means earned, that is, that action earned them loss, and the subject of Kas is implied, and An is in the accusative case with Jarm, as you say: Your harshness earned Zayd his anger towards you, and the poet said: We set his head on a bee stump for what his hands had done and what we had transgressed against him. That is, by what you have earned. Al-Kisa’i said: The meaning of la jaram is no turning away or preventing them. It was said: The meaning is no cutting off a cutter, so the subject was omitted when it was used frequently. Jaram is cutting. He cut the palm tree and harvested it, meaning he cut it, so he is a jarim. A people of Jaram and Jaram, and this is the age of Jaram and Jaram. Jarmat the wool of the sheep means I cut it, and I took from it, like Jalamt al-shay’ Jalaman means I cut, and Jalamt al-juzur means I ajlamha Jalam if you take the meat from its bones, and Akhdhat al-shay’ bi-jalamtu - with a sukoon on the lam - if you take it all, and this is Jalamt al-juzur - with a fat-ha - meaning I gathered its meat, as al-Jawhari said. Al-Nahhas said: Al-Kisa’i claimed that it has four languages: La Jaram, La ‘an Dha Jaram, La An Dha Jaram. He said: Some people from Fazara say: La Jar annahu without a mim. Al-Farra’ narrated two other languages for it. He said: Banu Amir say: La dha Jarm. He said: And some Arabs say: La Jarm, with a damma on the jim.
11:23: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who have believed who is the noun of in and believed is a relative clause, meaning they have been truthful. And done righteous deeds and humbled themselves before their Lord is in apposition to the relative clause. Ibn Abbas said: They humbled themselves, repented. Mujahid: They obeyed. Qatadah: They were humble and submissive. Muqatil: They were sincere. Al-Hasan: Humility is humility due to the fear that is fixed in the heart, and the origin of humility is leveling, from khabt which is the flat and wide land. So humility is humility and reassurance, or continuous repentance to God Almighty on a level basis. To their Lord Al-Farra' said: To their Lord, and their Lord is one, and the meaning may be: They directed their humility to their Lord. Those is the predicate of in.
11:24: The Almighty said: The likeness of the two parties is the beginning, and the predicate is like the blind and what follows. Al-Akhfash said: That is, like the blind. An-Nahhas: The meaning is like the party of the disbeliever is like the blind and the deaf, and like the party of the believer is like the hearing and the seeing, and for this reason he said: Are they equal? So he returned to the two parties, and they are two, its meaning was narrated from Qatada and others. Ad-Dahhak said: The blind and the deaf are like the disbeliever, the hearing and the seeing are like the believer. It was said: The meaning is: Are the blind and the seeing equal, and are the deaf and the hearing equal? Likewise is in the accusative case as a specification. Do you not remember in the two descriptions and consider.
11:25: The Almighty said: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people. The Almighty mentioned the stories of the prophets, peace be upon them, to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to alert him to the need to be patient in the face of the harm of the disbelievers until God relieves him of their matter. I means he said: I, because sending has the meaning of saying. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Al-Kisa'i read ani with the opening of the hamza, meaning We sent him saying that I am to you a clear warner. He did not say that because he returned from the absence to addressing Noah to his people, as He said: And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things then He said: So take it with strength (al-A’raf 7:145).
11:26: The Almighty said: That you worship none but God meaning leave the idols and do not worship them, and obey God alone. Whoever reads inni with the kasra makes it an interjection in the speech, and the meaning is that We sent him to not worship anyone but God. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day.
11:27: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Then the chiefs said. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: The chiefs are the leaders, meaning they are full of what they say. This has been mentioned previously in al-Baqarah and others. We see you as nothing but a human being. “Like us” is in the accusative case as a state. And like us is added to a definite noun and it is indefinite and the tanween is estimated in it, as the poet said: Oh God, there is someone like you who is jealous of women Second: The Almighty’s saying: And we do not see that you were followed by anyone except the lowest of us. Arazel is the plural of ardhall and ardhall is the plural of radhal, like kalb dog, akalab dogs, and akalib dogs. It was said: aradhal is the plural of ardhall, like aswad is the plural of aswad black among snakes. And ardhall is the vile, they meant that our lowest, downtrodden, and base people followed you. Al-Zajjaj said: They attributed them to weaving, and they did not know that industries have no effect on religion. Al-Nahhas said: the lowest are the poor, those who have no lineage, and the lowly in industries. In the hadith: They were weavers and cuppers. This was out of ignorance on their part, because they criticized the Prophet of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) for something that was not faulty, because the prophets (blessings and peace of God be upon them) are only required to come with proofs and signs, they are not required to change images and forms, and they are sent to all people, so if a lowly person among them converts to Islam, they will not be deprived of that, because they are required to accept the Islam of everyone among them who converts to Islam. I said: The lowly here are the poor and the weak, as Heraclius said to Abu Sufyan: Did the nobles of the people follow him or the weak? He said: Rather, the weak. He said: They are the followers of the messengers. Our scholars said: This was only because the leadership took control of the nobles, and the difficulty of separating from it, and their disdain to submit to others, and the poor are free from those obstacles, so he is quick to respond and submit. This is the most common condition of the people of this world. Third: Scholars differed in identifying the lowly ones. Ibn al-Mubarak reported on the authority of Sufyan that the lowly ones are those who go to the doors of judges and rulers asking for testimonies. Tha’lab reported on the authority of Ibn al-A’rabi: The lowly ones are those who eat the world with their religion. He was asked: Who is the lowly ones? He said: The one who improves the worldly life of others by corrupting his religion. Ali, may God be pleased with him, was asked about the lowly ones. He said: Those who, when they gather, are victorious, and when they disperse, are not recognized. Malik ibn Anas, may God be pleased with him, was asked: Who are the lowly ones? He said: The one who curses the Companions. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: The lowest ones are the weavers and the cuppers. Yahya ibn Aktham: The tanner and the sweeper if he is not from the Arabs. Fourth: If a woman says to her husband: You lowlife, and he says: If you are one of them, then you are divorced. Al-Naqqash narrated that a man came to Al-Tirmidhi and said: My wife said to me: You lowlife, and I said: If you are lowlife, then you are divorced. Al-Tirmidhi said: What is your profession? He said: Your name. He said: Lowlife, by God, lowlife, by God lowlife. I said: According to what Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned on the authority of Sufyan, she is not divorced, and likewise according to the statement of Malik and Ibn al-A’rabi, nothing is required of him. The Almighty said: The outward appearance of opinion. That is, the apparent opinion, but their inner self is the opposite of that. It is said: bada badawan if it appears, as He said: Today, when there is no sight The wilderness is called badi' because of its appearance. It appeared to me that I should do such-and-such, meaning that a different opinion appeared to me. Al-Azhari said: Its meaning is in what appears to us of opinion. It is possible that badi' al-ra'y is from bada'a yada' and the hamza was deleted. Abu Amr emphasized the hamza and read: badi' al-ra'y or awwal al-ra'y, meaning they followed you when they began to look, and if they had looked and thought deeply they would not have followed you. The meaning does not differ here with the hamza and without the hamza. It is in the accusative case with the deletion of fi as God Almighty said: And Moses chose his people. (al-A’raf 7:7) And we see no superiority for you over us meaning in following him, and this is a denial from them of his turn, may God bless him and grant him peace. Rather, we think you are liars the address is to Nahaj and those who believed with him.
11:28: God the Almighty said: He said, 'O my people, have you considered, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord?' meaning, upon certainty, said Abu Imran Al-Joni. It was also said: upon a miracle, and this meaning was mentioned previously in Al-An'am. And He has given me mercy from Himself, meaning, prophecy and a message, according to Ibn Abbas, and it is a mercy to creation. It was also said: guidance to God through proof. It was also said: through faith and Islam. So it was blinded to you meaning, the message and guidance were blinded to you, so you did not understand them. It is said: I was blinded to such-and-such, and such-and-such was blinded to me, meaning, I did not understand it. The meaning is: So mercy was blinded, and it was said: it is reversed, because mercy is not blinded, rather one is blinded to it, so it is like saying: I put my head in the skullcap, and the shoe entered my foot. Al-A'mash, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it Fa'mait with a damma on the 'ayn and a shaddah on the meem for what the agent is not named, meaning God blinded you to it. This is also in Abu's reading Fa'maaha, mentioned by Al-Mawardi. Analzamkumuha It was said: the testimony that there is no god but God. It was also said: the ha' refers to mercy. It was also said: to the evidence, meaning: Shall I force you to accept it, and make it obligatory upon you?! It is a question with the meaning of denial, meaning I cannot force you to know it. Noah, peace be upon him, intended by this statement to respond to them. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' narrated Analzamkumuha with a sukoon on the first meem for ease. Sibawayh permitted such a thing, and he recited: Today I drink without deserving any sin from God nor being excessive. An-Nahhas said: It is permissible, according to what Yunus said, in a sentence other than the Qur’an, to say, We will force you to do it, and the pronoun is used in the same way as the explicit, just as you say, We will force you to do that. “And you are averse to it,” meaning it is not correct for you to accept it while you are averse to it. Qatada said: By God, if the Prophet of God, Noah, peace be upon him, had the power, he would have forced his people to do it, but he did not have the power to do that.
11:29: The Almighty said: And O my people, I do not ask of you for it meaning for conveying, calling to God, and believing in Him any reward, meaning money that would be too heavy for you. My reward is only from God meaning my reward for conveying the message. And I will not drive away those who believe They asked him to drive away the lowly ones who believed in him, just as the Quraysh asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to drive away the clients and the poor, according to what was explained in Al-An'am, so he answered them by saying: And I will not drive away those who believe, for they are to meet their Lord It is possible that he said this in order to show them respect for meeting God, the Almighty, and it is possible that he said it in order to argue, meaning if I did that, they would argue with me before God, so He would reward them for their faith, and reward those who drove them away. But I see you as a people behaving ignorantly in your despising them and asking them to drive them away.
11:30: The Almighty said: And O my people, who will protect me from God? Al-Farra’ said: meaning, will prevent me from His punishment. If I drive them out meaning because of their faith. Will you not remember? The ta’ was assimilated into the dhal. It is permissible to delete it, so you say: you remember.
11:31: The Almighty said: And I do not tell you that I have the treasures of God, nor that I know the unseen. He informed of his humility and humbleness before God the Almighty, and that he does not claim what he does not have from the treasures of God, which are His blessings upon whomever He wills of His servants, and that he does not know the unseen, because no one knows the unseen except God the Almighty. And I do not say that I am an angel means I do not say that my status among the people is the status of the angels. The scholars have said: The benefit of the statement is to indicate that the angels are better than the prophets, because of their constant obedience, and their continuous worship until the Day of Judgment, may the prayers of God be upon them all. This meaning was previously mentioned in Al-Baqarah. And I do not say to those whose eyes despise them meaning that your eyes find them heavy and despise them, and the original is tazdihim, the ha and mim were deleted due to the length of the name. The letter dal is replaced by a ta’, because the original form of tazdari is taztari, but the ta’ is replaced after the zay with a dal, because the zay is voiced and the ta’ is unvoiced, so the ta’ was replaced by a voiced letter from its point of articulation. It is said: azrayt alayhi if you criticize him. And zarayt alayhi if you belittle him. Al-Farra’ recited: His friend distances him, his wife despises him, and his little one scolds him. God will not give them any good meaning, your contempt for them will not invalidate their rewards or reduce their recompense. God knows best what is within their souls so He will reward them for it and hold them accountable for it. Indeed, then I would be among the wrongdoers meaning, if I said what was mentioned above. And then is omitted because it is in the middle.
11:32: God the Almighty said: They said, 'O Noah, you have disputed with us and prolonged your dispute with us' meaning you have argued with us and prolonged your dispute with us and exaggerated it. Argument in the speech of the Arabs means exaggeration in dispute, derived from the word jadal which means intense killing, and the falcon is also called ajrad due to its intensity in flying, and this meaning has been mentioned in (Al-An'am) more fully than this. Ibn Abbas read fa-ha-jadalna as mentioned by Al-Nahhas. Argument in religion is praiseworthy, and for this reason Noah and the prophets argued with their people until the truth appears, so whoever accepts it is successful and prosperous, and whoever rejects it is disappointed and loses. As for arguing for other than the right until falsehood appears in the guise of truth, it is reprehensible, and its companion is blameworthy in both worlds. Then bring us what you promise us meaning of punishment. If you should be of the truthful in your statement.
11:33: The Almighty said: He said, ‘God will only bring it to you if He wills.’ That is, if He wanted to destroy you, He would punish you. And you will not escape. That is, you will not escape. It was said: you will be victorious because of your great numbers, because they were amazed by that. They filled the earth with plains and mountains, as will come.
11:34: The Almighty said: And my advice will not benefit you meaning my informing you and my striving to make you believe. If I wanted to give you good advice meaning because you do not accept advice. The meaning of advice in language has already been mentioned in Bara'ah. If God wants to mislead you meaning to lead you astray. This is one of the things that proves the invalidity of the doctrine of the Mu'tazilah and the Qadarites and those who agree with them, since they claimed that God does not want the sinner to disobey, nor to declare the disbeliever to be an infidel, nor to mislead the misguided, and that He does that, and God does not want that. So God responded to them by saying: If God wants to mislead you. This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-Fathah and it is misleading. They have belied their accursed Sheikh Iblis, as we have explained in Al-A'raf regarding God's seduction of him, where he said: Then because You have put me in error (al-A’raf 7:16). They have no escape from the words of Noah, peace be upon him: If God wants to lead you astray, so he attributed their seduction to God, the Most High, since He is the Guide and the Misleader, glory be to Him above what the deniers and wrongdoers say, far above. It was said: To lead you astray means to destroy you, because misguidance leads to destruction. At-Tabari: To lead you astray means to destroy you with His punishment. It was narrated from Tayy: So-and-so became misguided, meaning sick, and I led him astray and destroyed him. From this, So they will meet with error (Maryam 19:59). He is your Lord, so to Him is the seduction, and to Him is the guidance. And to Him you will be returned is a threat and a warning.
11:35: The Almighty said: Or do they say, 'He has fabricated it'? They mean the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He has fabricated it means he invented the Qur'an himself, and what he told about Noah and his people, as Muqatil said. Ibn Abbas said: It is from Noah's dialogue with his people, and it is more evident, because there is nothing before or after it except the mention of Noah and his people, so the address is from them and to them. Say, 'If I have fabricated it' means I have invented it and fabricated it, meaning the revelation and the message. Then upon me is my crime meaning the punishment of my crime, and if I am right in what I say, then upon you is the punishment of my denial. I have committed a sin is the source of ajram, which is committing a bad deed. It was said that the meaning is: the punishment of my crime and my earnings. Jarram and ajam have the same meaning, according to An-Nahhas and others. He said: An outcast from the clan and a hostage, I am certain of what my hands have committed and my tongue has reaped. Whoever reads Ajrami with the opening of the hamza, it is the plural of Jarm, and An-Nahhas also mentioned it. And I am innocent of what you commit, meaning of disbelief and denial.
11:36: The Almighty said: And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed. That is in the nominative case as a noun for which the agent has not been named. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, and the meaning would be that. And believed is in the accusative case with believes. The meaning of the statement is despair of their belief and the continuation of their disbelief, in order to fulfill the threat that was sent down to them. Ad-Dahhak said: So he invoked against them when he was informed of this and said: My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dwelling. (Nuh 71:26) the two verses. It was said: A man from the people of Noah carried his son on his shoulder, and when the boy saw Noah he said to his father: Give me a stone, so he gave him a stone and threw it at Noah, peace be upon him, and it made him bleed, so God Almighty revealed to him: None of your people will believe except those who have already believed. So do not be sad about what they used to do. That is, do not be sad about their destruction to the point that you become miserable, i.e. sad. Misery is sadness, and from this the poet said: How many a friend or intimate friend I have lost, but I did not feel sad, even though the loss was great. It is said: A man became sad if he heard something he disliked. Sadness is a feeling of resignation.
11:37: The Almighty said: And construct the ark under Our eyes and with Our inspiration. That is, construct the ship so that you and those who believe with you can ride it. Under Our eyes That is, in Our sight and where We see you. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: By Our protection of you, the protection of those who see you. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: By Our protection, and the meaning is the same, so He expressed the vision with the eyes, because vision is through them. And all the eyes are for greatness, not for multiplication, as God the Almighty said: How excellent are We in power! (al-Mursalat 77:23) How excellent are We in preparing! (al-Dhariyat 51:48) And indeed, We are indeed exalted. (al-Dhariyat 51:48). The meaning of eyes in this verse and others may go back to the meaning of eye, as He said: And that you may construct it under My eyes. (Ta-Ha 20:39) All of this is an expression of perception and comprehension, and He, the Almighty, is free from senses, likening, and conditioning, and there is no Lord but Him. It was said: The meaning with Our eyes is with the eyes of Our angels whom We made eyes to protect and assist you, so the plural is in this case of multiplication. It was said: with Our eyes meaning with Our knowledge, as Muqatil said. Ad-Dahhak and Sufyan said: with Our eyes with Our command. It was said: with Our revelation. It was said: with Our assistance to you in making it. and Our revelation meaning about what We revealed to you about making it. “And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged. Indeed, they are to be drowned.” That is, do not ask for respite for them, for I am to drown them.
11:38: The Almighty said: And he made the ark meaning he began to make. Zaid bin Aslam said: Noah, peace be upon him, spent a hundred years planting trees, cutting them down and drying them, and a hundred years working on them. Ibn Al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Ibn Ashras on the authority of Malik who said: I was informed that Noah's people filled the earth, until they filled the plains and mountains, and these people could not descend to those, nor could those people ascend to those. Noah spent a hundred years planting trees to build the ark, then he gathered them and dried them for a hundred years, and his people mocked him, and that was because they saw him doing that, until what happened was from the decree of God concerning them. It was narrated on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith who said: Noah built his ark in the areas of Damascus, and cut its wood from Mount Lebanon. Judge Abu Bakr bin Al-Arabi said: When God, the Almighty, rescued the believers in the loins and wombs, God revealed to him. (None of your people will believe except he who has already believed. So build the ark.) He said: O Lord, I am not a carpenter. He said: (Yes, I do. That is with my own eyes.) So he took the axe and put it in his hand, and his hand did not miss. So they passed by him and said: This one who claims to be a prophet has become a carpenter, so he built it in forty. Al-Tha'labi and Abu Nasr Al-Qushayri narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Noah built the ark in two years. Al-Tha'labi added: This is because he did not know how to make the ark, so God revealed to him that he made it like the rook of a bird. Ka'b said: He built it in thirty years, and God knows best. Al-Mahdawi: It was reported that the angels taught him how to make it. They differed regarding its length and width. According to Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, its length was three hundred cubits, its width was fifty, and its thickness was thirty cubits, and it was made of teak wood. Al-Kalbi, Qatadah, and Ikrimah said the same: Its length was three hundred cubits, and the cubit reached the shoulder. Salman Al-Farsi said: Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The length of the ark was one thousand two hundred cubits, and its width was six hundred cubits. Al-Tha'labi narrated it in the book of brides. Ali bin Zaid narrated on the authority of Yousef bin Mahran on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The disciples said to Jesus, peace be upon him: If you would send us a man who witnessed the ark and tell us about it. So he set off with them until he reached a mound of dirt and took a handful of that dirt. He said: Do you know what this is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: This is Ka’b Ham bin Noah. He struck the mound with his staff and said: Rise by God’s permission. He found him standing, shaking the dirt from his head, and he had turned gray. Jesus said to him: Is this how you perished? He said: No, I died when I was young, but I thought it was the messenger and that is why I grew gray. He said: Tell us about Noah’s ark? He said: Its length was one thousand two hundred cubits, and its width was six hundred cubits. It had three layers, one layer had beasts and wild animals, one layer had humans, and one layer had birds. He mentioned the rest of the story as will be mentioned, God willing. Al-Kalbi said about it, as narrated by Al-Naqqash: Water entered it four cubits, and it had three doors, one door had beasts and birds, one door had wild animals, and one door had men and women. Ibn Abbas made it three bellies, the lower bellies for beasts, predators and animals, the middle bellies for food and drink, and he rode in the upper bellies, and carried with him the body of Adam, peace be upon him, between the men and women, then buried him later in the Holy House, and Satan was with them in the sack. It was said: The snake and the scorpion came to enter the ship, and Noah said: I will not carry you, because you are the cause of harm and affliction, so they said: Carry us, and we guarantee that we will not harm anyone who mentions you, so whoever recites when he fears their harm, “Peace be upon Noah among the worlds” 37:79, they will not harm him, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri and others. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in his history, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: “Whoever says in the evening, ‘May God’s peace be upon Noah and upon Noah, peace’, will not be stung by a scorpion that night.” God the Almighty said: And whenever is an adverb. A group of his people passed by him, they mocked him. Al-Akhfash and Al-Kisa’i said: It is said: I mocked him and from him. There are two opinions about their mockery of him: One of them is that they saw him building his ship on land, so they mocked him and ridiculed him and said: O Noah, you have become a carpenter after becoming a prophet. The second is that when they saw him building the ship and they had never seen a ship built before, they said: O Noah, what are you doing? He said: I am building a house that walks on water. They were amazed by what he said and mocked him, and the waters of the seas were the remainder of the flood. “He said: If you mock us” meaning what we did today when building the ship. We will mock you tomorrow when the flood occurs. What is meant by mockery here is to make you foolish, and its meaning is that if you make us foolish, then we will make you foolish just as you make us foolish.
11:39: The Almighty said: And you will know who will be afflicted with a punishment that will disgrace him. It is a threat, and man is connected to sawfa'alamoon, and ya'alamoon here is from the category of transitive to an object, meaning you will know who will be afflicted with the punishment. It is possible for man to be an interrogative, meaning who will be afflicted with the punishment? It was said: man is in the nominative case as a subject and ya'alamoon is the predicate, and ya'alamoon is an attribute of -'adhab. Al-Kisa'i narrated: Some people from the people of Hijaz say: saw ta'alamoon, and whoever said: sat'alamoon dropped both the waw and the fa. The Kufians narrated: saf ta'alamoon, and the Basrans do not know except saffa'al, and sat'al are two languages, neither of them is from the other. And it is obligatory upon him means it is obligatory upon him and descends upon him. Permanent torment means permanent, meaning the torment of the Hereafter.
11:40: The Almighty said: Until, when Our command came, and the oven overflowed. There are seven different opinions about the oven: The first - that it is the surface of the earth, and the Arabs call the surface of the earth an oven, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Al-Zuhri and Ibn Uyaynah, and that is because it was said to him: If you see water on the surface of the earth, then embark, you and those with you. The second - that it is the oven for bread in which it is baked, and it was an oven made of stones, and it was for Eve until it became for Noah, and it was said to him: If you see water overflowing from the oven, then embark, you and your companions. And God caused water to gush forth from the oven, and his wife knew about it and said: O Noah, the water overflowed from the oven, and he said: The promise of my Lord has come true. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan, and Mujahid and Atiyah said it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The third - that it is the place where water gathers in the ship, also on the authority of Al-Hasan. The fourth - that it is the rising of dawn, and the light of morning, from their saying: The light of dawn is illumination, as stated by Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Fifth - It is the mosque of Kufa. Ali bin Abi Talib also said this, and Mujahid said this. Mujahid said: It was near the oven in Kufa. He said: Noah built the ark in the interior of the mosque of Kufa, and the oven was to the right of the one entering, facing Kinda. The gushing of water from it was a sign for Noah, and evidence of the destruction of his people. The poet, who was Umayyad, said: Their oven boiled and the water rose above the mountains until it reached them. Sixth: It is the highlands of the earth and the elevated places on it, as stated by Qatada. Seventh: It is the spring in the island Ain Al Warda narrated by Ikrimah. Muqatil said: That was Adam’s oven, but it was in the Levant in a place called Ain Warda. Ibn Abbas also said: Adam’s oven boiled in India. An-Nahhas said: These statements are not contradictory, because God the Almighty informed us that water came from the sky and the earth, He said: So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water * And We caused springs to gush forth from the earth (al-Qamar 54:11). These statements agree that this was a sign. Boiling is boiling. The oven is a foreign name that the Arabs Arabized, and it is based on the structure of a verb, because its original structure is tanar, and there is no nun before a ra’ in the speech of the Arabs. It was said: The meaning of the oven boiled is a representation of the presence of torment, like their saying: the battle heated up when the war intensified. The oven is the furnace. It is also said: the people’s pot boiled when their war intensified. Their poet said: You left your destiny with nothing in it, and the destiny of the people is boiling hot God the Almighty said: We said, ‘Load therein of every pair two’ meaning a male and a female, because the original offspring remained after the flood. Hafs read: of every pair two with the tanween of all meaning of every thing two pairs. Both readings go back to one meaning: something with another that cannot be dispensed with. The two are called: they are two pairs, in every two neither of them can do without the other, as the Arabs call each one of them a pair. It is said: he has a pair of sandals if he has two sandals. Likewise, he has a pair of pigeons, and he has a pair of chains. God the Almighty said: And that He created the two mates, the male and the female (al-Najm 53:45). The woman is called the man’s wife, and the man is called her husband. The two may be called a pair, and the two pairs may mean the two types, and the two kinds, and each kind is called a pair. God the Almighty said: And it brought forth from every beautiful pair (al-Hajj 22:5), meaning from every color and kind. Al-A’sha said: And every pair of brocade worn by Abu Qudamah is loved by both of them. He wanted every type and color. And of every pair is in the accusative case with carry. And two is an emphasis. And your family meaning, carry your family. Except for those who precede. Of is in the accusative case with the exception. Upon him is the saying from them, meaning, of destruction, and he is his son Canaan and his wife Wa’ilah, they were disbelievers. And whoever believed Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj said: meaning, carry whoever believed in me, meaning whoever believed you, so of is in the accusative case with carry. And none believed with him except a few Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Eighty people from his people believed, including three of his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and three of his daughters-in-law. And when they got out of the ship, they built a village which is today called the village of the eighty near Mosul. It was reported in the hadith that there were eight people on the ship: Noah and his wife, other than the one who was punished, and his three sons and their wives. This is the opinion of Qatada, Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, Ibn Jurayj, and Muhammad bin Ka’b. Ham had intercourse with his wife on the ship, so Noah asked God to change his sperm and he came up with a black man. Ata’ said: Noah asked Ham not to have his children’s hair grow beyond their ears, and that wherever his children were, they would be slaves to the sons of Shem and Japheth. Al-A’mash said: They were seven: Noah, his three daughters-in-law, and three sons, and he miscarried Noah’s wife. Ibn Ishaq said: They were ten, in addition to their wives: Noah, his sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and six people who believed in him, and all of their wives. And little is raised by believed, and it is not permissible to put it in the accusative case as an exception, because the speech before it was not complete, except that the benefit of including except and what is that if you said: So-and-so and so-and-so believed with him, it is possible that others have believed, so if you bring what and except, you require what comes after except and negate others.
11:41: The Almighty said: And He said, Embark therein. It is an order to ride, and it is possible that it is from God Almighty, or it is possible that it is from Noah to his people. Riding is going up on the back of something. It is said: The debt rode him. There is an omission in the speech, meaning ride the water in the ship. It was said: The meaning is ride it. And in is for emphasis, like the Almighty's saying: If you interpret dreams (Yusuf 12:43). The benefit of in is that they were ordered to be inside it, not on its back. Ikrimah said: Noah, peace be upon him, rode in the ark on the tenth of Rajab, and it came to rest on Al-Judi on the tenth of Muharram, so that is six months. Fatada said the same and added: It is the day of Ashura, so he said to those who were with him: Whoever is fasting, let him complete his fast, and whoever is not fasting, let him fast it. Al-Tabari mentioned a hadith about this. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Noah boarded the ship on the first day of Rajab and fasted the entire month. The ship sailed with them until the day of Ashura, on which day it was sent to Judi, and Noah and those with him fasted. At-Tabari mentioned on the authority of Ibn Ishaq what indicates that it stayed on the water for about a year, and it passed by the Kaaba and circled it seven times, and God raised it from drowning so it did not drown. Then it continued to the right and returned to Judi and settled on it. God the Almighty said: In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. The people of the Two Holy Mosques and the people of Basra read it with a damma on the meem in both of them, except for those who deviate, meaning in the name of God is its course and its anchorage. So its course and its anchorage are in the nominative case as a subject, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, and the meaning would be: In the name of God at the time of its course, then time was deleted and its course was established in its place. Al-A'mash, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read: In the name of God is its course with a fatha on the meem and its anchorage with a damma on the meem. Yahya bin Isa narrated from Al-A'mash from Yahya bin Waththab In the name of God is its course and its anchorage with a fatha on the meem in both of them, on the source of jarat tajri jaran wa majra, and warstaw raswan and marsa if it is fixed. Mujahid, Sulayman bin Jundub, Asim Al-Jahdari and Abu Raja Al-Attardi read: In the name of God is its course and its anchorage as an attribute of God the Almighty in the genitive case. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case with an implied subject, meaning He is its course and its anchorage. It is permissible to put it in the accusative case as a state. Ad-Dahhak said: When Noah, peace be upon him, said, In the name of God is its course, it would course, and when he said, In the name of God is its anchorage, it would anchor. Marwan bin Salim narrated on the authority of Talha bin Ubaidullah bin Kurayz, on the authority of Al-Hussein bin Ali, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is safety for my nation from drowning if they board the ship, in the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. “And they have not appraised God with true appraisal, while the earth entirely will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand. Glory be to Him and He is far above what they associate with Him.” (al-Zumar 39:67) “In the name of God is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.” This verse is evidence of mentioning the Basmalah at the beginning of every action, as we explained in the Basmalah, and praise be to God. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning to the people of the ship. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When the dung and filth increased, God inspired Noah to touch the elephant’s tail, and a male and female pig fell out of it and they approached the dung. Noah said: Why don’t you touch the tail of this pig! So he did, and a male and female mouse came out of it. When they fell, they approached the ship and its ropes, gnawing at it, and gnawing at the luggage and provisions until they feared for the ship’s ropes. Then God inspired Noah to wipe the lion’s forehead, so he wiped it, and two cats came out of it and ate the mouse. When the lion was loaded onto the ship, he said: O Lord, what shall I feed him? He said: I will keep him busy. So a fever seized him, and he has been feverish for all eternity. Ibn Abbas said: The first of the animals that Noah loaded onto the ark was a goose, and the last of what he loaded was a donkey. He said: Satan clung to its tail, and his hands had entered the ship, and his feet were still outside, so the donkey began to tremble and could not enter. So Noah shouted at it: Enter, woe to you! So he began to tremble, and said: Enter, woe to you! And if the devil is with you, a word slipped from his tongue, so he entered and the devil jumped and entered. Then Noah saw him singing in the ship, so he said to him: O cursed one, what brought you into my house?! He said: You gave me permission, so he mentioned it to him, so he said to him: Get up and go out. He said: You have no choice but to take me with you, so it was, as they claim, on the back of the ship. And Noah, peace be upon him, had two luminous beads with him, one in place of the sun, and the other in place of the moon. Ibn Abbas said: One of them was white as the whiteness of the day, and the other was black as the blackness of the night, so he knew the times of the prayers by them, so when they reached the evening the blackness of this one overcame the whiteness of this one, and when they reached the morning the whiteness of this one overcame the blackness of this one, according to the hours. God the Almighty said, informing us: Woe to me! (Hud 11:72) And as the poet said:
11:42: The Almighty said: And it sailed with them in waves like mountains. Wave is the plural of wave, and it is what rises from a large amount of water when the wind is strong. The kaf is for comparison, and it is in the accusative case as an adjective for the wave. It was mentioned in the interpretation that the water exceeded everything by fifteen cubits. And Noah called to his son. It was said: He was an unbeliever and his name was Canaan. It was also said: Yam. And it is permissible according to Sibawayh: And Noah called to his son by deleting the waw from his son in the wording, and he recited: He has a high-pitched voice As for And Noah called to his son, and he was this is an irregular reading, and it is narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and Urwah bin Az-Zubayr. Abu Hatim claimed that it is permissible, as he meant her son, so he deleted the alif, as you say: his son, so you delete the waw. An-Nahhas said: What Abu Hatim said is not permissible according to the doctrine of Sibawayh, because the alif is light and cannot be deleted, and the waw is heavy and can be deleted. And he was apart means from his father’s religion. It was said: from the ship. It was said: that Noah did not know that his son was a disbeliever, and that he thought he was a believer, and that is why he said to him: And do not be with the disbelievers and it will come. This call was before the people were certain of drowning, and before they saw despair, rather it was when the oven first boiled and the sign appeared to Noah. Asim read: O my son, embark with us with a fatha on the ya’, and the rest with a kasra on it. The root of ya bini is that it has three ya’s: the ya’ of diminutive, the ya’ of verb, and the ya’ of addition. The ya’ of diminutive was assimilated into the lam of verb, and the lam of verb was kasra for the ya’ of addition. The ya’ of addition was deleted because it takes the place of tanween, or because it is quiescent and the ra’ is quiescent in this position. This is the root of the reading of those who kasra the ya’, and it is also the root of the reading of those who open it, because the ya’ of addition was changed to an alif because the alif is light, then the alif was deleted because it is a replacement for a letter that is deleted, or because it is quiescent and the ra’ is quiescent. An-Nahhas said: As for the reading of Asim, it is problematic. Abu Hatim said: He means ya biniyyah, then he deletes. An-Nahhas said: I saw Ali bin Sulayman who said that this is not permissible, because the alif is light. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: I do not know of any grammarian who permitted speaking about this except Abu Ishaq, for he claimed that the fat-ha is from two directions, and the kasra is from two directions. The fat-ha is based on the fact that the ya’ is replaced by an alif. God Almighty said, informing us: Woe to me! (Hud 11:72), and as the poet said: Oh, how amazing is her enduring journey! He wants, O my son, then the alif is deleted due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, as you say: Abdullah came to me in the dual. The other way is to delete the alif, because the vocative is a place for deletion. The kasra is to delete the ya for the vocative. The other way is to delete it due to the meeting of two quiescent letters.
11:43: The Almighty said: "He said, 'I will return and join.' To a mountain that will protect me.' That is, prevent me.' From the water,' so that I will not drown. 'He said, 'There is no protector today from the command of God.' That is, there is no protector, for it is a day when the punishment will be justified upon the disbelievers.' 'Asim is in the accusative case for exoneration. It is permissible for there is no protector today to have 'La in the sense of 'is not.' 'Except for whom God has mercy' in the accusative case as an exception not from the first, that is, but whom God has mercy upon, He will protect him, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case, on the basis that 'Asim means protected, like: 'Gushing water' (Al-Tariq: 6) meaning gushing forth, so the exception in this case is connected. The poet said: Slow to get up, soft-spoken, my heart has become captivated by him That is, fascinated. Another said: Let the noble deeds not rise for their desire and sit, for you are the one who feeds and clothes. Any food that is covered. An-Nahhas said: The best thing that has been said about it is that min is in the nominative case, meaning that none can protect from the command of God today except the Merciful, meaning except God. This is the choice of At-Tabari. What makes this good is that you did not make a protector in the sense of infallible, so you would take it out of its context, nor illa in the sense of lakin. And the waves came between them means between Noah and his son. And he was among those who were drowned It was said that he was riding a horse that had become arrogant and proud of himself, so when he saw the water, he came and said: O my father, the oven has boiled, so his father said to him: O my son, ride with us. He had not finished reviewing when a great wave came and swallowed him and his horse, and a barrier was placed between him and Noah, so he drowned. It was said that he made a house for himself made of glass to protect himself from the water, so when the oven boiled, he entered it and locked it from the inside, and he continued to defecate and urinate in it until he drowned thereby. It was said that the mountain he took refuge in was Mount Sinai.
11:44: The Almighty said: And it was said, 'O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain]' This is a metaphor because it is dead. It was also said: What distinguishes it was made in it. The one who said that it is a metaphor said: If one searched the speech of the Arabs and non-Arabs, he would not find anything like this verse in its beautiful arrangement, eloquent arrangement, and comprehensive meanings. In the hadith: God the Almighty does not leave the earth without rain in a year or two, and that no water ever descends from the sky except under the protection of an angel assigned to it, except for the water of the flood, for what came out of it was not preserved by the angel. This is the Almighty's saying: Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the moving ship (al-Haqqah 69:11). The ship sailed with them until the matter was over, then God ordered the water pouring from the sky to be held back, and God ordered the earth to swallow it. It is said:ٱلَم البَماء یْبُهlikeَناَم ينبَمنمand ٱلَم یْبُهlikeحَد یحَد, two languages narrated by Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra'. The drain is the place where water is drunk. Ibn al-Arabi said: The two waters met in a predestined manner, what was on the earth and what came down from the sky. So God commanded what came down from the sky to stop, so the earth did not absorb a single drop, and He commanded the earth to swallow only what came out of it. This is what God Almighty said: And it was said, ‘O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain],’ and the water subsided. It was also said: God distinguished between the two waters, so what was from the earth’s water He commanded it to swallow, and the sky’s water became seas. God the Almighty said: And the water subsided meaning decreased. It is said: something subsided and I subsided it, just as it is said: it decreased by itself and someone else decreased it. Ghayd with a damma on the ghayn is permissible. And the matter was decided meaning it was decreed and completed, meaning that the people of Noah were destroyed completely and properly. It is said that God the Almighty made their wombs sterile, meaning the wombs of their women, forty years before the drowning, so there were no children among those who perished. The correct view is that He destroyed the children in the flood, just as the birds and wild animals perished, and the drowning was not a punishment for the children, animals, and birds, rather they died at their appointed times. It was narrated that when the water increased in the streets, the mother of a boy feared for him, and she loved him very much, so she went out with him to the mountain, until she reached a third of it, and when the water reached her neck, she raised her hands with her son until the water carried him away. If God had mercy on any of them, He would have had mercy on the mother of the boy. God the Almighty said: And it came to rest on al-Judi, and it was said, ‘Away with the wrongdoing people!’ That is, destruction for them. Al-Judi is a mountain near Mosul. It came to rest on it on the tenth of Muharram, the day of Ashura. Noah fasted on it and ordered all those with him from people, beasts, birds, animals, and others to fast on it, in gratitude to God the Almighty. This meaning has been mentioned previously. It was also said that it was on a Friday. It was narrated that God the Almighty revealed to the mountains that the ship would come to rest on one of them, so they became tall, and al-Judi remained untouched out of humility to God, so the ship came to rest on it, and its branches remained on it. In the hadith, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Some of it remained that the early generations of this nation had attained. Mujahid said: The mountains became tall and untouched so that they would not be drowned, so the water rose above them fifteen cubits, and al-Judi became humble and humbled itself to the command of God the Almighty and did not drown, and the ship came to rest on it. It was also said that al-Judi is the name of every mountain, and from this is the saying of Zaid bin Amr bin Nufail: Glory be to Him, then glory be to Him. It returns to Him, and before us, glory be to Al-Judi and Al-Jamad. It is said that Judi is one of the mountains of Paradise, and that is why it settled on it. It is also said that God honored three mountains with three al-Nas 114:Judi with Noah, Mount Sinai with Moses, and Hira with Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all. Question: When Al-Judi humbled himself and submitted, he became honorable, and when others rose up and were exalted, he became superior. This is God’s way with His creation. He raises up those who are humble, and He lowers those who are exalted. The one who said it well said: If the necks are humbled in reverence to you, then their glory lies in their humiliation. In Sahih Al-Bukhari and Muslim, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a she-camel called Al-Adhbaa, and it was not outrun. Then a Bedouin came on his camel and outran it. The Muslims were very upset about that and said: Al-Adhbaa has outrun it! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is God’s right that He does not raise anything in this world without lowering it.” Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Charity does not decrease wealth, and God does not increase a servant’s forgiveness except in honor. No one humbles himself before God except that God raises him up.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has revealed to me that you should be humble so that no one transgresses against another and no one boasts over another. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. Question: We mention in it the story of Noah and his people and some mention of the ship. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in his history on the authority of Al-Hasan: that Noah was the first messenger sent by God to the people of the Earth, and that is what God Almighty said: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years (al-Ankabut 29:14). And: sins had increased among them, and the tyrants had increased and they had become very arrogant, and Noah would call upon them night and day, secretly and openly, and he was patient and forbearing, and no prophet encountered anything more severe than what Noah encountered, so they would enter upon him and strangle him until he was left as a dead body, and they would beat him in the gatherings and he would be expelled, and he would not call down curses on those who did this to him, but he would call upon them and say: My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know, and this would only make them flee from him, to the point that he would speak to a man among them and wrap his head with his garment and put his fingers in his ears so that he would not hear anything of his words, and that is what God the Almighty said: And whenever I called them that You might forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their garments (Nuh 71:7). Mujahid and Ubayd ibn Umair said: They would beat him until he fainted, and when he regained consciousness he would say: My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know. Ibn Abbas said: Noah was beaten and then wrapped in felt and thrown into his house so that they would think he had died. Then he would go out and call them, until he despaired of the faith of his people. A man came to him with his son leaning on a stick and said: O my son, look at this old man, do not let him deceive you. He said: O my father, give me the stick. So he gave him the stick and took it and said: Put me on the ground. So he put him down. Then he walked towards him with the stick and struck him and wounded him in the head with a clear wound, and blood flowed. Noah said: (My Lord, you see what your servants do to me. If there is any good in your servants, then guide them; but if it is otherwise, then give me patience until you judge, for you are the best of judges.) So God revealed to him and made him despair of the faith of his people, and informed him that there remained in the loins of men or in the wombs of women a believer. He said: And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be sad over what they have been doing. That is, do not be sad for them. And construct the ark under Our eyes and with Our inspiration. He said: O Lord, where is the wood? He said: Plant the trees. He said: So he planted the teak tree for twenty years, and he stopped supplicating, and they stopped mocking him, and they used to mock him, and when the trees reached maturity, his Lord commanded him to cut them down and dry them, and he said: O Lord, how do I make this house? He said: Make it in three forms, its head like the head of a rooster, its roost like the roost of a bird, and its tail like the tail of a rooster, and make it closed and make doors for it on its side, and fasten it with nails, meaning iron nails. And God sent Gabriel and taught him the making of the ship, and made his hand not to miss. Ibn Abbas said: The house of Noah, peace be upon him, was Damascus, and he built his ship from the wood of Lebanon between Zamzam and the corner and the station, and when it was completed, he loaded the wild beasts and animals in it in the first door, and he placed the wild beasts and birds in the second door, and closed them, and he placed the sons of Adam, forty men and forty women, in the upper door and closed them, and he placed the ants with him in the upper door because of their weakness so that the animals would not tread on them. Al-Zuhri said: God the Almighty sent a wind that brought to him two of each pair, from the beasts of prey, birds, wild animals and cattle. Jaafar bin Muhammad said: God sent Gabriel and gathered them together. He began to strike the pairs with his hands, and his right hand would fall on the male and his left hand on the female, and he would enter the ship. Zaid bin Thabit said: The goat found it difficult for Noah to enter the ship, so he pushed it with his hand by its tail, and then its tail broke and became crooked and its shyness became apparent. The ewe continued until she entered, and he stroked her tail, covering her modesty. Ishaq said: A man of knowledge told us that Noah carried the people of the ship, and put in it two of each kind, and he carried two of the hoopoes. The hoopoe died in the ship before the earth appeared, so the hoopoe carried her and traveled around the world with her trying to find a place for her, but he did not find any clay or soil, so his Lord had mercy on him and dug a grave for her on his back and buried her in it. Those protruding feathers on the hoopoe’s back are the place of the grave, and that is why the backs of the hoopoes protrude. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Noah carried with him on the ship from all kinds of trees, and the ‘ajwa dates from Paradise were with Noah on the ship. The author of Kitab al-Aroos and others mentioned: When Noah, peace be upon him, wanted to send someone to bring him report of the land, the chicken said: I am. So he took it and sealed its wing and said to it: You are sealed with my seal, never fly away. My nation will benefit from you. So he sent the crow and it found a carcass and landed on it and was detained, so he cursed it. That is why it is killed in the sacred precincts and outside. He called for fear against it, and that is why it does not live in houses. He sent the dove, but it did not find a resting place, so it landed on a tree in the land of Sinai and carried an olive leaf and returned to Noah. He knew that it had not settled on the land. Then he sent it after that and it flew until it landed in the valley of the sanctuary, and behold, the water had dried up from the places of the Kaaba, and its clay was red, so its feet were dyed. Then it came to Noah, peace be upon him, and said: I give you good report that you give me a necklace around my neck and dye on my feet, and I live in the sanctuary. So he wiped his hand over its neck and necklace, and gave it redness on its feet, and prayed for blessings for it and its offspring. Al-Tha’labi mentioned that after the crow he sent the pheasant, which was a type of chicken, and said: Beware of apologizing. So it found the greenery and the open space, but it did not return, and he took his children with him as a hostage until the Day of Resurrection.
11:45: It has five issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And Noah called upon his Lord meaning he called upon Him. “And he said: ‘My Lord, indeed my son is of my family’” meaning of my family whom You promised to save from drowning, so there is an omission in the speech. And Your promise is the truth meaning the truth. Our scholars said: Noah asked his Lord for his son because He said: (and your family) and left out His saying: except for those against whom the word has already passed. So when he was with his family, he said: My Lord, indeed my son is of my family. This is indicated by His saying: And do not be with the disbelievers meaning do not be among those who are not from them, because he was a believer in his opinion, and Noah did not say to his Lord: Indeed my son is of my family except that this was the case in his opinion, since it is impossible for him to ask for the destruction of the disbelievers, then ask for the salvation of some of them, and his son was secretly disbelieving and outwardly believing, so God informed Noah of what He alone possessed of knowledge of the unseen, meaning He knew about the state of your son what you did not know. Al-Hasan said: He was a hypocrite, and for that reason Noah considered it permissible to call upon him. And also on his authority: He was his wife’s son. His evidence is Ali’s reading And Noah called to her son. And You are the most just of judges is subject and predicate. That is, You ruled that some people would be saved, and some people would be drowned.
11:46: Second: The Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘O Noah, indeed he is not of your family’ meaning, he is not of your family whom you promised to save, said Saeed bin Jubair. The majority said: He is not of your family, your religion or yours, so it is with the deletion of an adjective, and this indicates that the rule of agreement in religion is stronger than the rule of lineage. Indeed, he is an unrighteous deed Ibn Abbas, Urwah, Ikrimah, Ya’qub, and Al-Kisa’i read indeed, he is an unrighteous deed meaning from disbelief and denial, and Abu Ubaid chose it. The rest read work meaning, your son is of unrighteous deed, so the adjective was deleted, said Al-Zajjaj and others. He said: It grazes as it grazes until it remembers, then it is only coming and going Yes, of coming and going. This statement and the one before it go back to one meaning. It is possible that the ha’ is for the question, meaning that your asking me to save him is an evil deed. Qatada said. Al-Hasan said: The meaning of an evil deed is that he was born on his bed and he was not his son. He was not of sound mind. Mujahid also said this. Qatada said: I asked Al-Hasan about him and he said: By God, he was not his son. I said: God informed us about Noah that he said: Indeed, my son is of my family, so he said: He did not say from me, and this is an indication that he was the son of his wife from another husband. I said to him: God narrated about him that he said: Indeed, my son is of my family (And Noah called to his son), and the people of the two books do not differ that he was his son. Al-Hasan said: And who takes his religion from the people of the book! They are liars. And he recited: So they betrayed them both (al-Tahrim 66:10). Ibn Jurayj said: He called to him while he thought that he was his son, and he was born on his bed, and his wife had betrayed him in it, and that is why he said: So they betrayed them both. Ibn Abbas said: No prophet's wife ever rebelled against him, and that he was his son. Ad-Dahhak, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubair, Maymun bin Mihran and others said the same, and that he was his son. It was said to Saeed bin Jubair that Noah said: Indeed, my son is of my family. Was he of his family? Was he his son? So he glorified God for a long time and then said: There is no god but God! God tells Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that he is his son, and you say that he is not his son! Yes, he was his son, but he differed in intention, action and religion. That is why God the Most High said: Indeed, he is not of your family. This is the correct view in this matter, God willing, due to the majesty of the one who said it. His saying: Indeed, he is not of your family does not negate that he is his son. His saying: And they betrayed them means in religion, not in bed. This is because this woman used to tell people that he was crazy, and that she said to him: Will your Lord not support you? He said to her: Yes. She said: Then when? He said: When the oven boils, she goes out and says to her al-Nas 114:O people, by God, he is crazy, he claims that his Lord will not help him unless the oven boils. This is her betrayal. The other betrayal is that she used to guide the guests to what will come, God willing. And God knows best. It was said: A child may be called a deed just as it is called an earnings, as in the hadith: Your children are from your earnings. Al-Qushayri mentioned it. Third: In this verse there is consolation for the creation for the corruption of their children, even if they were righteous. It was narrated that Ibn Malik ibn Anas came down from above with a dove that had covered him. He said: Malik knew that the people had understood him, so Malik said: Manners are the manners of God, not the manners of fathers and mothers, and goodness is the goodness of God, not the goodness of fathers and mothers. It also contains evidence that the son is from the family, linguistically and legally, and from the people of the house. So whoever makes a will for his family, his son is included in that, and whoever is included in his home, and he is among his dependents. And God the Almighty said in another verse: “And indeed Noah called upon Us, and excellent is the respondent. And We saved him and his family from the great distress.” (al-Saffat 37:75-76) So He named all those who were included in his home from his family. Fourth: The verse indicates the statement of Al-Hasan, Mujahid and others: that the child belongs to the bed, and that is why Noah said what he said, taking the apparent meaning of the bed. Sufyan bin Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Amr bin Dinar that he heard Ubayd bin Umair say: We see that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only ruled that the child belongs to the bed because of the son of Noah, peace be upon him. Abu Omar mentioned it in the book Al-Tamhid. And in the authentic hadith on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: The child belongs to the bed, and the adulterer gets the stone, meaning disappointment. It was said: stoning with stones. Urwah bin Al-Zubayr read: And Noah called to her son meaning his wife’s son, and it is an interpretation of the reading mentioned above from him and from Ali, may God be pleased with him, and it is an argument for Al-Hasan and Mujahid, except that it is an anomalous reading, so we do not abandon the agreed upon reading for it. And God knows best. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: Indeed, I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant. That is, I forbid you from this question, and I warn you lest you be, or I hate that you be among the ignorant, meaning the sinners. And from this is the statement of the Almighty: God admonishes you that you never return to the like of it. (al-Nur 24:17) That is, God warns you and forbids you. It was said: The meaning is I raise you from being among the ignorant. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is an addition from God and an admonition by which He raises Noah from the station of the ignorant, and elevates him to the station of the scholars and the knowers.
11:47: Then Noah said: My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You for that of which I have no knowledge. The verse. These are the sins of the prophets, peace be upon them. So he thanked God for his humility and modesty. And unless You forgive me for what he neglected in asking. And have mercy on me meaning through repentance. I will be among the losers meaning in deeds. So he said: "O Noah, disembark in peace from Us."
11:48: The Almighty said: "It was said, 'O Noah, descend with peace from Us.'" That is, the angels said to him, or God said to him: Descend from the ship to the earth, or from the mountain to the earth, for it has swallowed the water and dried up. "With peace from Us." That is, with safety and security. It was also said: with a greeting. And blessings upon you. That is, lasting blessings, derived from the word brook brooking of a camel, which means its stability and standing. And from it comes the word barakah blessing for the stability of water in it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: Noah is the younger Adam, so all of creation now is from his descendants, and there were no men or women with him in the ship except those who were from his descendants, according to the saying of Qatada and others, as mentioned above. And in the revelation: And We made his descendants the survivors. (al-Saffat 37:77). And upon nations from among those with you. It was said: This includes every believer until the Day of Resurrection. And included in His statement: And nations We will grant enjoyment, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us is every disbeliever until the Day of Resurrection. This was narrated from Muhammad bin Ka'b. The meaning of this is: And upon the offspring of nations from among those with you, and the offspring of nations We will grant enjoyment. It was said: from is for partiality, and it is to clarify the type. And nations We will grant enjoyment (and nations) is raised in the meaning and it is nations. Al-Akhfash Saeed said: It is like you say: I spoke to Zaid and Amr was sitting. Al-Farraa permitted in other readings and nations, and its meaning is: And We will grant enjoyment to nations. on was repeated with nations because it is conjoined with the kaf of upon you, which is a genitive pronoun, and it is not conjoined with a genitive pronoun except by repeating the preposition according to the statement of Sibawayh and others. This was explained in detail in An-Nisa in His statement: And fear God, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs (al-Nisa 4:1) in the accusative. And the ba' in His statement: (in peace) is related to something omitted, because it is in the position of a state, meaning descend in peace upon you. From us is in the accusative case related to an omitted word, because it is an adjective for blessings. And upon nations is related to what upon you is related to, because it was repeated for the sake of what is conjoined with the kaf. From in His statement: From those with you is related to an omitted word, because it is in the accusative case as an adjective for nations. With you is related to an omitted verb, because it is the relative clause of whoever meaning from those who settled with you, or believed with you, or rode with you.
11:49: The Almighty said: This is from the report of the unseen (Hud 11:49) meaning that report, and in another place that meaning that report and stories from the report of what is hidden from you. We reveal it to you meaning for you to understand it. You did not know it, nor did your people meaning they were unaware of the matter of the flood, and the Magians now deny it. Before this is report meaning unknown to you and your people. So be patient with the hardships of the message and the harm of the people as Noah was patient. It was said: He meant their ignorance of the story of Noah's son, even if they heard about the flood, then it is general. So be patient meaning be patient, O Muhammad, in carrying out the command of God and conveying His message, and in the harm you encounter from the infidel Arabs, as Noah was patient with the harm of his people. Indeed, the outcome in this world is victory, and in the hereafter is success. For the righteous from polytheism and sins.
11:50: The Almighty said: And to 'Aad We sent their brother Hud meaning, We sent him, so it is conjoined with We sent Noah. He was called their brother because he was from them, and the tribe was their gathering, as you say: O brother of Tamim. It was said: He was called their brother because he was from the children of Adam, just as they were from the children of Adam, and this was mentioned previously in Al-A'raf and they were idol worshippers. It was said: They are two 'Aad, the first 'Aad and the other 'Aad, so these are the first, and what is the other is Shaddad and Luqman mentioned in the Almighty's saying: Iram, who had lofty pillars (al-Fajr 89:7). 'Aad is the name of a man, then it continued for a people who were attributed to him. He said, 'O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him' in the accusative case according to the wording, and other than Him in the nominative case according to the position, and other than Him in the accusative case as an exception. You are nothing but fabricators meaning, you are not in your taking of a god other than Him except lying about Him, may He be glorified and exalted.
11:51: The Almighty said: “O my people, I do not ask of you for this any reward. My reward is only from He who created me.” Its meaning was presented earlier. And nature is the beginning of creation. Do you not understand? What happened to the people of Noah when they denied the messengers.
11:52: The Almighty said: And O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. It was mentioned at the beginning of the Surah. He sends the sky is in the subjunctive mood because it is a response and it has the meaning of recompense. Upon you in abundance is in the accusative case as a state, and it has the meaning of multiplying, meaning He sends the sky with rain in succession, one after the other. The Arabs delete the ha' in Mif'al as a relative pronoun, and Mif'al most often comes from Af'al, and it came here from Fa'l, because it is fromدْماْمة السَاء َمِظْه ومدظْب َمومِظْب َمَما َمدظْرا. The people of Hud - I mean 'Aad - were people of gardens, crops, and buildings, and their dwellings were in the sands between Ash-Sham and Yemen as mentioned in Al-A'raf. And increases you is in apposition toيهْبسهوم.قوة إلى قوقَةMujahid said: Severity upon your severity. Ad-Dahhak: Fertility to your fertility. Ali ibn 'Isa: Glory upon your glory. Ikrimah: A son to your son. It was said: God withheld rain from them and made their wombs barren for three years, so no children were born to them. So Hud said to them: If you believe, God will revive your land and provide you with wealth and children, and that is the strength. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that He will increase your strength in blessings. And do not turn away, criminals, meaning do not turn away from what I call you to, and persist in disbelief.
11:53: God Almighty said: They said, ‘O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof.’ That is, a clear argument. And we will not believe you, out of their insistence on disbelief.
11:54: The Almighty said: We say nothing but that you have been afflicted with meaning that you have been afflicted with some of our gods meaning our idols. With evil meaning madness for cursing them, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It is said: the matter afflicted him and afflicted him if it befell him. And from this is And feed the contented and the needy (al-Hajj 22:36). He said, Indeed, I call God to witness" meaning upon myself. "And bear witness meaning and I make you bear witness, not that they were worthy of witness, but it is the end of the statement, meaning so that you may know that I am innocent of what you associate meaning of the worship of the idols that you worship.
11:55: So plot against me all together meaning you and your idols in your enmity and harm towards me. Then do not wait meaning do not delay. This statement, despite the large number of enemies, indicates complete confidence in the victory of God Almighty. It is one of the signs of prophethood, that the Messenger alone would say to his al-Nas 114:So plot against me all together and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said the same to the Quraysh. And Noah, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then decide your plan, you and your partners (Yunus 10:71) the verse.
11:56: The Almighty said: Indeed, I have put my trust in God, my Lord and your Lord. That is, I am satisfied with His judgment and trust in His victory. There is no creature that is a soul that crawls on the earth, and it is in the nominative case as a subject. But He has control over its forelock. That is, He directs it as He wills and prevents it from what He wills, that is, you will not come to harm. And everything that has a soul is called a beast or a beast, and the ha is for emphasis. Al-Farra' said: Its owner and the one who is able to do it. Al-Qutbi said: Its conqueror, because whoever you take by the forelock, you have conquered. Ad-Dahhak said: He brings it to life and then causes it to die, and the meanings are close. The forelock is the hair cut at the front of the head. And we stretch a man's forelock, meaning I stretched his forelock. Ibn Jurayj said: He only mentioned the forelock because the Arabs use that when describing a person as humble and submissive, so they would say: The forelock of so-and-so is in the hand of so-and-so, meaning that he is obedient to him and he directs him as he wishes.
