And when they captured a prisoner and wanted to release him and show him favor, they would cut his forelock to be known for that as a sign of pride over him, so he addressed them in a way that they recognized in their speech. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim said in Nawader Al-Usul: The meaning of the verse of God the Almighty: There is no creature but that He holds its forelock, according to us is that God the Almighty has determined the measures of the deeds of His servants, then looked at them, then created His creation, and His sight had penetrated all that they were doing before He created them, so when He created them, He placed the light of that look in their forelocks, so that light holds their forelocks, directing them to their deeds that were determined for them on the Day of Judgment. God created the measures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. Narrated by Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God determined the measures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. That is why the Messengers were strengthened and became among the most determined because they noticed the light of the forelocks, and they were certain that all of His creation were led by that light to the deeds that His sight penetrated into them. The one who had the greatest share of observation was the one who had the strongest resolve. That is why the Prophet Hud, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not strong enough to say: Then plot against me all together and do not give me respite. “Indeed, I have put my trust in God, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock.” It was called a forelock because the actions were specified and emerged from the unseen of the unseen, so they became specified in the destinies. The sight of the Creator penetrated all the movements of creation with power, then the movements of every living creature that crawled on the earth were placed on his forehead between his eyes, so that place was called a forelock because it specified the movements of the servants according to what was destined, so the forelock is taken by the specified movements that God the Most High looked at before He created it. And he described the forelock of Abu Jahl by saying: A lying, sinful forelock (al-Alaq 96:16), informing that the forelocks in it are lying and sinful, so according to what they interpreted, it is impossible for the forelock to be attributed to lying and error. And God knows best. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path. An-Nahhas said: The path in the language is the clear path, and the meaning is that even if God, the Most High, has power over everything, He does not take them except with the truth. And it was said: Its meaning is that there is no flaw in His management, and no disparity in His creation, glory be to Him.
11:57: The Almighty said: If you turn away in the accusative case, therefore the letter nun was deleted from it. The original is tatawalawu, so the letter ta was deleted because two tas came together. I have conveyed to you what I was sent with means I have made it clear to you. And my Lord will replace you with a people other than you meaning He will destroy you and create someone more obedient to Him than you, who will make Him One and worship Him. And He will replace you is cut off from what precedes it, therefore it is raised, or it is conjoined with what is required after the letter fa in His statement: I have conveyed to you. It was narrated on the authority of Hafs on the authority of Asim And He will replace you in the accusative case based on the position of the letter fa and what comes after it, like: And He will leave them in their transgression wandering blindly (al-A’raf 7:186). God Almighty says: And you will not harm Him at all meaning by turning away and ignoring Him. Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things meaning He is the Guardian of all things. Over means to in the sense of lam, so He protects me from you harming me.
11:58: God the Almighty said: And when Our command came meaning Our punishment by destroying the tribe of Aad. We saved Hud and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us because no one is saved except by the mercy of God the Almighty, even if he has good deeds. In Sahih Muslim, Al-Bukhari and others, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: None of you will be saved by his deeds. They said: Not even you, O Messenger of God? He said: Not even me, unless God covers me with mercy from Him. It was said: The meaning of by a mercy from Us is that We showed them the guidance that is mercy. And they were four thousand. It was also said: Three thousand. And We saved them from a severe punishment meaning the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. It was said: It is the barren wind as God mentioned in Al-Dhariyat and others, and it will come. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: And the punishment that the Prophet threatens his nation with, when it comes, God will save the Prophet and the believers with him from it, yes! It is not unlikely that God would test a prophet and his people by afflicting them with a calamity that would be a punishment for the unbelievers and a test for the believers, if it was not something that the prophet had threatened them with.
11:59: The Almighty said: And those were 'Aad is a subject and predicate. Al-Kisa'i narrated that some Arabs do not decline 'Aad and make it a name for the tribe. They denied the signs of their Lord meaning they belied the miracles and rejected them. And they disobeyed His messengers meaning Hud alone, because no messenger was sent to them other than him. Similar to this is the Almighty's saying: O messengers, eat of the good things (Al-Mu'minun: 51) meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, alone, because there was no messenger in his time other than him. The plural is here because whoever denies one messenger has disbelieved in all the messengers. It was said: They disobeyed Hud and the messengers before him, and they were such that if a thousand messengers were sent to them, they would have denied them all. And they followed the command of every stubborn tyrant meaning their fallen ones followed their leaders. The tyrant is the arrogant one. The stubborn, tyrannical one is the one who does not accept the truth nor submit to it. Abu Ubaid said: The stubborn, obstinate, and obstinate is the one who opposes with disagreement. From this, the vein that bursts with blood is called ‘Aanad. The rajaz poet said: I am too old to stand stubbornness
11:60: The Almighty said: And they were pursued in this world by a curse meaning they were pursued by it. And on the Day of Resurrection meaning they were pursued on the Day of Resurrection by something similar, so the completion is on His saying: And on the Day of Resurrection. Behold, indeed, the 'Aad people disbelieved in their Lord Al-Farra' said: meaning they disbelieved in the blessing of their Lord. He said: It is said I disbelieved in him and I disbelieved in him, like I thanked him and I thanked him. Behold, away with 'Aad, the people of Hud meaning they are still far from the mercy of God. Distance means destruction. Distance means distancing from good. It is said: ba'd means delayed and distant. And ba'd means perishing. He said: Do not distance my people, who are the poison of the enemy and the scourge of the islands. Al-Nabigha said: Do not be far away, for death is a source of strength, and every person will one day perish.
11:61: It has five issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And to Thamud meaning We sent to Thamud a righteous man meaning in lineage. And to Yahya bin Waththab read and to Thamud with tanween throughout the Qur’an, and this is how it was narrated from Al-Hasan. The rest of the reciters differed on it, so they declined it in some places and did not decline it in others. Abu Ubaidah claimed that if it had not been for the contradiction of the majority, the correct way would have been to leave it indeclinable, since the feminine was more prevalent in it. An-Nahhas said: What Abu Ubaidah - may God have mercy on him - said, that the feminine is more prevalent in it is a rejected statement, because Thamud is called a neighborhood, and it is called a tribe, and the tribe is not more prevalent in it, rather the matter is the opposite of what he said according to Sibawayh. And the best according to Sibawayh in what Banu so-and-so did not say indeclination, such as Quraysh and Thaqeef and the like, and likewise Thamud, and the reason for that is that since the masculine was the original, and it could have both masculine and feminine, the lighter original was more appropriate. And the feminine is good and excellent. Sibawayh recited about the feminine: Al-Walid was overcome by forgiveness and was spared the difficulties of the Quraysh and ruled them. The second: The Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him.’ It was mentioned above. He produced you from the earth. That is, He began your creation from the earth, and that is because Adam was created from the earth as mentioned above in Al-Baqarah and Al-An’am, and they are from Him. It was also said: He created you on the earth. It is not permissible to assimilate the ha’ of ghairuhu into the ha’ of huwa except in the language of deleting the waw in Al-Adraj. And He made you its inhabitants and its residents. Mujahid said: The meaning of istama’km is He made you its inhabitants from His saying: So-and-so made so-and-so his home, so it is his for my life. Qatada said: He made you live in it. According to these two sayings, istaf’ala has the meaning of af’ala, like istajabah has the meaning of ajabah. Ad-Dahhak said: He prolonged your lives, and their lives were from three hundred to one thousand. Ibn Abbas: He made you live in it. Zayd ibn Aslam: He ordered you to build what you need in it from building houses and planting trees. It was said: The meaning is He inspired you to build it from tillage, planting, digging rivers, and other things. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: Some Shafi’i scholars said: Colonization is the request for development, and the absolute request from God Almighty is obligatory. Judge Abu Bakr said: The word istaf’ala comes in the Arabic language with meanings: including istaf’ala with the meaning of requesting an action, like his saying: I asked him to carry it, and with the meaning of believing, like their saying: I found this matter easy, I thought it was easy, or I found it easy, and istaz’atmuhu, meaning I thought it was great and I found it, and from it istaf’ala with the meaning of I hit, like their saying: I found it good, I hit it. And from it is in the meaning of action, like his saying: He settled in the place and settled down, and they said, and his saying: They mock and They ridicule him, so the saying of the Most High: He made you inhabit it He created you to inhabit it, not in the sense of finding it new and easy, meaning I found it good and easy, and this is impossible for the Creator, so it goes back to the fact that He created, because of the benefit, and something may be expressed by its benefit metaphorically, and it is not correct to say: He asked God Almighty to inhabit it, because the word is not permissible in his right, but it is correct to say: He called for its inhabit, because he came with the word istaf’ala, which is calling for the action by speech from someone lower than him if it is a command, and a request for the action if it is from the lower to the higher desire. I said: He did not mention istaf’ala in the sense of af’ala, like his saying istawwad in the sense of awqad, and we have mentioned it, and it is: Fourth: It contains evidence of housing and life estate. The discussion of Al-Baqarah regarding housing and ownership has already been mentioned. As for life estate, scholars differed and it is of three opinions: The first: It is ownership of the benefits of the property during the life of the owner for the duration of his life. If he does not mention any descendants and the owner dies, it returns to the one who gave it or to his heirs. This is the opinion of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, Yazid bin Qusayt, and Al-Layth bin Saad. It is the well-known opinion of Malik and one of the opinions of Al-Shafi’i. The evidence for this opinion has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. The second: It is ownership of the property and its benefits and it is a pure gift. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i and their companions, Al-Thawri, Al-Hasan bin Hayy, Ahmad bin Hanbal, Ibn Shabramah, and Abu Ubaid. They said: Whoever gives a man something during his life, it belongs to him during his life, and after his death it belongs to his heirs, because he has owned its property, and the condition of the giver for life and life is invalid, because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Life estate is permissible. And Life estate is for the one to whom it was given. Third: If he said your lifespan and did not mention the descendants, it is like the first statement. If he said for your descendants, it is like the second statement. Al-Zuhri, Abu Thawr, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, and Ibn Abi Dhi’b said the same. It has been narrated from Malik, and it is the apparent statement of his in Al-Muwatta’. What is known from him and his companions is that it returns to the one who has a long lifespan if the descendants of the one who has a long lifespan are extinct, if the one who has a long lifespan is alive. Otherwise, it returns to whoever is alive from his heirs and the people who are most deserving of his inheritance. The one who has a long lifespan does not own the neck of anything according to the word lifespan, according to Malik and his companions. Rather, he owns the benefit without the neck according to the word lifespan. Malik also said about confinement: If it is confined to a man and his descendants, it does not return to him. If it is confined to a specific man for his life, it returns to him. The same applies to lifespan by analogy, and it is the apparent statement of Al-Muwatta’. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If a man grants a man a life estate for him and his descendants and says, ‘I have given it to you and your descendants as long as anyone among you lives,’ then it belongs to the one to whom it is given and it does not revert to its owner because he gave a gift that is subject to inheritance.” And on his authority, he said: The life estate that came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was to say: ‘It is for you and your descendants,’ but if he said: ‘Do you have it as long as I live?’ then it reverts to its owner. Muammar said: And this is what Al-Zuhri used to issue fatwas about. I said: The meaning of the Qur’an is consistent with the second opinion, because God the Almighty said: And He made you inhabited meaning He made you live, so He made the righteous man live in it for the duration of his life with righteous deeds, and after his death with good remembrance and good praise, and vice versa for the proud man, so the world is a container for them, life and death. It may be said: Good praise flows in the course of the offspring. In the revelation: And grant me a reputation of truth among later generations (Ash-Shu’ara’: 84), meaning good praise. It was said: He is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. He also said: And We made his descendants the survivors (Saffat: 77), and He also said: And We blessed him and Isaac, and among their descendants are doers of good and those who clearly wrong themselves (Saffat: 113). Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: So seek His forgiveness meaning ask Him for forgiveness for worshipping idols. Then repent to Him meaning return to worshipping Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive meaning He is near to answering whoever calls upon Him. The discussion of this has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah when He said: Indeed, I am near and respond to the call of the caller.
11:62: The Almighty said: They said, 'O Salih, you were among us a source of hope before this' meaning, we hoped that you would be a master among us before this, that is, before your call to prophethood. It was said: Salih used to criticize their gods and hate them, and they used to hope that he would return to their religion, but when he called them to God, they said: Our hope in you has been cut off. Are you forbidding us is an interrogative that means denial. To worship means from worshipping. What our fathers worshipped "Fan" is in the accusative case by dropping the preposition. "And indeed, we are in doubt in Surah Ibrahim and Inna and the original is Inna, so he found three nuns" heavy so he dropped the third. "From what you call us is addressed to Salih, and in Surah Ibrahim it is You call us" because the address is to the messengers, may God's prayers and peace be upon them. "To him is doubtful from arabatuhu Fan aaribuhu" if you did something to him that would cause him doubt. Al-Hudhali said: If I came to him from the unseen, he would smell my affection and pluck my clothes. As if I had made him suspicious
11:63: The Almighty said: "He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has given me mercy from Himself?'" Its meaning was presented in the words of Noah. Who can protect me from God if I disobey Him? is a question that means negation, meaning no one can protect me from Him if I disobey Him. Then you do not increase me except in loss, meaning misguidance and distancing from good, said Al-Farra'. The loss is for them, not for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, as if he said: except in loss for you, not for me. It was said: The meaning is you do not increase me by your argument with the religion of your fathers except in insight into your loss, on the authority of Ibn Abbas.
11:64: The Almighty said: And O my people, this is the she-camel of God is a subject and predicate. A sign for you is in the accusative case as a state, and the agent has the meaning of indication or warning in this. It was only said: The she-camel of God, because He brought her out for them from a mountain - as they requested - on the condition that they would believe. It was also said: He brought her out from a solid rock isolated in the corner of the stone called Al-Kathbah, and when the she-camel came out - as they requested - the Prophet of God Salih said to them: This is the she-camel of God for you, a sign. "So leave her to eat" is an imperative imperative, and the nun was deleted from So leave her because it is an imperative. It is not said: Wadhra or Wadhra except as an anomaly. The grammarians have two opinions on it. Sibawayh said: They dispensed with it by leaving it out. Another said: Since the waw was heavy and there was a verb in the speech with its meaning without a waw in it, they omitted it. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible to raise ta'akul as a state and a new sentence. "And do not touch it" is a jussive with a prohibition. Badly Al-Farra’ said: By hamstringing. Then you will be seized is the answer to the prohibition. A near torment meaning close to hamstringing it.
11:65: The Almighty’s saying: “So they hamstrung her. He said, ‘Enjoy yourselves in your home for three days.’” There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: So they hamstrung her. Some of them hamstrung her, and it was attributed to all of them because it was with the consent of the rest. We have already discussed hamstringing her in Al-A’raf. It will also come. And he said, ‘Enjoy yourselves.’ That is, Salih said to them, Enjoy yourselves, that is, with the blessings of God, the Almighty, before the punishment. In your homes, that is, in your country. If He had meant the home, He would have said, In your homes. It was said: That is, each one of you enjoys his home and dwelling, like His saying: He brings you forth as a child (Ghafir 40:67), that is, each one as a child. He expressed enjoyment of life because the dead do not enjoy or take pleasure in anything. So she was hamstrung on Wednesday, so they stayed on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, and the punishment came to them on Sunday. They only stayed for three days because the young camel bellowed three times, as was previously mentioned in Al-A’raf, so their colors turned yellow on the first day, then red on the second, then black on the third, and they perished on the fourth. This was previously mentioned in Al-A’raf. Second: Our scholars have used as evidence that God postponed the punishment of the people of Salih for three days, that if the traveler does not agree to stay for four short nights, then the three days are outside the ruling of staying. What the scholars have said about this has been presented in An-Nisa’. The Almighty says: That is a promise that will not be denied. That is, it is not a lie. It was also said: It is not a lie in it.
11:66: The Almighty said: So when Our command came meaning Our punishment. We saved Salih and those who believed with him by mercy from Us previously mentioned. And from the disgrace of that Day meaning and We saved them from the disgrace of that Day, meaning from his disgrace and humiliation. It was said: The waw is redundant, meaning We saved them from the disgrace of that Day. It is not permissible to add it according to Sibawayh and the people of Basra, and according to the Kufians it is permissible to add it with lama and hatta only. Nafi' and Al-Kisa'i read yawmi'idh in the accusative. The rest read it with the kasra, adding yawm to idh. Abu Hatim said: Abu Zaid told us on the authority of Abu Amr that he read and from the disgrace of that Day assimilating the ya' into the ya', adding, and breaking the meem in yawmi'idh. Al-Nahhas said: What grammarians narrate - such as Sibawayh and those close to him on the authority of Abu Amr in such a case - is concealment. As for assimilation, it is not permissible, because two consonants meet, and it is not permissible to break the zay.
11:67: The Almighty said: And the shriek seized those who did wrong meaning on the fourth day they were shouted at and died. It was mentioned because the shriek and the screaming are one and the same. It was said: Gabriel's shriek. It was also said: A shriek from the sky in which there was the sound of every thunderbolt and the sound of everything on earth, so their hearts were torn apart and they died. And He said here: And the shriek seized those who did wrong and He said in Al-A'raf So the earthquake seized them (al-A’raf 7:78) and its explanation was presented there. And in the interpretation: When they were certain of the punishment, some of them said to each other: What is your position, that the matter should come upon you suddenly?! They said: What should we do? So they took their swords and spears and their number, and they were said to be twelve thousand tribes, in each tribe twelve thousand fighters, and they stood on the roads and paths, they claimed to be tortured, so God Almighty inspired the angel in charge of the sun to torture them with its heat, so he brought it close to their heads and their hands were severed, and their tongues hung on their chests from thirst, and all the animals that were with them died. And the water began to gush forth from those springs from its boiling until it reached the sky, and it did not fall on anything without destroying it from the intensity of its heat, and they remained like that, and God inspired the Angel of Death not to take their souls as torture for them until the sun set, then he shouted at them and they were destroyed. So they became in their homes, prostrated meaning fallen on their faces, stuck to the dust like a bird when it perches.
11:68: "Indeed, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord. So away with Thamud!" Its meaning was presented above.
11:69: God the Almighty said: And Our messengers had already come to Abraham with good tidings. This is the story of Lot, peace be upon him, who was Abraham's cousin, peace be upon him. The villages of Lot were in the Levant, and Abraham was in Palestine. When God sent down the angels with the punishment of the people of Lot, they passed by Abraham and stayed with him. Everyone who stayed with him treated him well. They passed by with the good tidings of Abraham, so he thought they were guests. They were Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil, peace be upon them. Ibn Abbas said: Ad-Dahhak: They were nine. As-Suddi: Eleven angels in the form of handsome young boys, with radiance and outstanding beauty. With the good tidings It was said: With a child. It was also said: With the destruction of the people of Lot. It was also said: They gave him the good tidings that they were messengers of God the Almighty, and that he had nothing to fear. "They said, 'Peace'" is in the accusative case because the verb is placed upon it, as you say: They said good. This is the choice of At-Tabari. As for his saying: They will say three (al-Kahf 18:22), the three is a noun other than saying that is said. If they were all raised or all lowered, “They said peace, he said peace” would be permissible in Arabic. It was said: It was lowered as a source. It was said: (They said peace) meaning they initiated him with the correct saying. As he said: “And when the ignorant address them, they say peace” (al-Furqan 25:63), meaning correctly. So peace is the meaning of their saying, not its wording. Ibn Al-Arabi said its meaning and chose it. He said: Do you not see that when God the Most High wanted to mention the word, He said it specifically, so He said, informing about the angels: “Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured” (al-Ra’d 13:24), “Peace be upon you, you have done well” (al-Zumar 39:73). It was said: They prayed for him, and the meaning is I gave you peace. “He said peace” has two aspects in raising it: One of them: by implying a subject, meaning it is peace, and my command is peace. The other means peace be upon you if it is made in the sense of greeting, so the predicate is implied. Salam was permissible in the indefinite form due to its frequent use, so the alif and lam were deleted as they were deleted from la ham in the phrase Allahumma. And it was read as Salam. Al-Farra’ said: “Peace and safety have the same meaning, like solution and lawful.” The Almighty’s saying: And he did not delay in bringing a roasted calf. There are fourteen issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: So he did not stay until he came an means until, as the great grammarians said, Ibn al-Arabi narrated: The meaning is: So he did not stay until he came. It was said: an is in the accusative case due to the omission of the preposition, the meaning is: So he did not stay until he came, meaning he did not delay in coming quickly, so when the preposition was deleted, an remained in the accusative case. In labath there is a pronoun for the name of Ibrahim. And ma is negative, as Sibawayh said. Al-Farra’ said: So he did not stay in his coming, meaning he did not delay in coming, so an is in the nominative case, and there is no pronoun in labath, and ma is negative, and it is correct for ma to mean who, and in labath there is a pronoun for Ibrahim and an ja’a is the predicate of ma, meaning that what Ibrahim stayed was his coming with a roasted calf. And haneeth is grilled. It was said: it is grilled with a sea of stones without being touched by fire. It is said that a sheep was roasted, and hot stones were placed on it to cook it, so it is called Haneeth. A horse was roasted, which is to prepare it for a lap or two, then to expose it to the sun to make it sweat, so it is called Mahnooz and Haneeth. If it does not sweat, it is called Kaba. Haneeth is a place near Madinah. It is also said that Haneeth is Sameet. Ibn Abbas and others said: Haneeth is cooked. Haneeth means Mahnooz, and he brought a calf because cows were the most common of his property. Second: In this verse, it is part of the etiquette of a guest to hasten his hospitality, to offer what is available and easy immediately, then follow it with something else if he has a new one, and not to make any effort that will harm him. Hospitality is one of the noble morals, and one of the manners of Islam, and one of the characteristics of the prophets and righteous people. Abraham was the first to add to what was mentioned in Al-Baqarah, but it is not obligatory according to most scholars, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Hospitality is for three days and its reward is a day and a night, and whatever is beyond that is charity. The reward is the gift and the relationship that is originally recommended. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his neighbour, and whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honor his guest. Honoring the neighbour is not obligatory by consensus, so hospitality is the same. And God knows best. Al-Layth went to its obligation, adhering to the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The night of the guest is a right and other hadeeths. What we have indicated is sufficient, and God is the guide. Ibn al-Arabi said: Some people said that hospitality was obligatory at the beginning of Islam and then it was abrogated. This is weak, because the obligation was not proven and the abrogating factor did not come. He mentioned the hadith of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, which was narrated by the imams, and in it: So we asked them for hospitality but they refused to host us, and the chief of that tribe bit him. He said: This is clear that if hospitality had been a right, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would have taken care of the people who refused and would have made that clear to them. Third: The scholars differed as to who is addressed by it. Al-Shafi’i and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hakam were of the opinion that it is addressed to the people of cities and the desert. Malik said: There is no hospitality for the people of cities. Sahnun said: Hospitality is for the people of villages, and as for the city, it is the hotel where the traveler stays. The two languages were narrated by the author of Al-Ain and others. They cited as evidence the hadith of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hospitality is for the people of the hair and not for the people of the city. This is an invalid hadith, and Ibrahim, the nephew of Abd al-Razzaq, is a rejected hadith attributed to lying. This is one of the things he narrated alone and attributed to his fabrication, as stated by Abu Umar ibn Abd al-Barr. Ibn al-Arabi said: Hospitality is truly a communal obligation. Some people said that it is obligatory in villages where there is no food or shelter, unlike the cities which are filled with shelter and provisions. There is no doubt that the guest is honorable and hospitality is an honor, but if he is a stranger then it is an obligation. Fourth: Ibn al-Arabi said: Some of our scholars said: Abraham’s hospitality was small, so the beloved thanked the beloved for it. This is a judgment based on conjecture in place of certainty, and on analogy in place of transmission. How did he know that it was small?! Rather, the commentators have transmitted that the angels were three, Gabriel, Michael, and Israfil, peace be upon him, and the calf was great for three. So what is this interpretation of the Book of God based on opinion?! This, by God’s trust, is the reprehensible interpretation, so avoid it, for you have known it.
11:70: Fifth: The Sunnah is that if food is offered to a guest, the one who is offered it should hasten to eat, because it is an honor for a guest to hasten to serve it, and an honor for the host to hasten to accept. When they withdrew their hands, Ibrahim disliked them, because they had gone beyond the norm and violated the Sunnah, and he feared that their appearance was something disliked that they intended. It was narrated that they were poking the meat with sticks that were in their hands, but their hands did not reach the meat. When he saw that from them, he disliked them and had a fear of them, meaning he concealed it. It was also said: he sensed, and al-wajoos means entering. The poet said: The mail came with a piece of paper, and my heart was afraid of the paper. Fear Fear, meaning fright. And if they saw the guest not eating, they thought evil of him, so the angels said, Do not fear, we have been sent to the people of Lot. Sixth: It is part of table manners that the host should look at his guest to see if he is eating or not. This should be done by looking around and stealing, not by looking intently. It was narrated that a Bedouin ate with Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik. Sulayman saw a hair in the Bedouin’s mouthful of food, so he said to him: Remove the hair from your mouthful. Sulayman said to him: Are you looking at someone who sees a hair in my mouthful of food? By God, I will not eat with you. I said: It has been mentioned that this story was with Hisham bin Abdul Malik, not with Sulayman, and that the Bedouin left him saying: Death is better than visiting a miser who deliberately notices the edges of his food. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: But when he saw that their hands did not reach him, he disapproved of them. He says: He disapproved of them. You say: I disapproved of you, I disapproved of you, and I disapproved of you if you found him not as you were used to. The poet said: You denied me, but the only thing you denied of the events was gray hair and baldness. So he combined the two languages. It is said: You disapproved of what you see with your eyes. And you disapproved of what you see with your heart.
11:71: Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And his wife standing is a subject and predicate, meaning standing so that the angels could see. It was said: She was behind the curtain. It was also said: She was serving the angels while he was sitting. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Standing praying. In the reading of Abdullah ibn Masoud: And his wife standing while he was sitting. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: So she laughed. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: She menstruated, and she was in despair, to confirm the good report. And the linguists recited on that: I come to the wedding when she is purified, and I leave her one day if she is laughing. Another said: The laughter of the rabbits on the rock is like the blood of the belly on the day of the encounter. The Arabs say: The rabbit laughed when it menstruated. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Ikrimah, that they took it from their saying: The camphora laughed - which is the peel of the date palm - when it split. Some linguists denied that there is in the speech of the Arabs laughing in the meaning of menstruated. The majority said: It is the well-known laughter, and they differed about it. It was said: It is the laughter of amazement. Abu Dhu’ayb said: He came up with a joke that people had never seen the like of, which is laughter, except that it is the work of bees. Muqatil said: She laughed out of fear of Ibrahim, and his trembling from three men, and Ibrahim was with his servants and his entourage, and Ibrahim alone was standing with a hundred men. Al-Dahhak said: Menstruation is not correct in the language. Abu Ubaid and Al-Farra’ denied that, Al-Farra’ said: I did not hear it from a trustworthy person, but it is a metaphor. It was narrated that the angels wiped the calf, so it rose from its place and joined its mother, so Sarah laughed at that, so they gave her the good report of Isaac. It is said: When Ibrahim, peace be upon him, wanted to have guests, he would have Sarah serve them, so that is his saying: And his wife standing meaning standing in their service. It is said: standing due to Ibrahim’s fear so she laughed because of their saying: Do not fear in joy at the security. Al-Farra’ said: There is an inversion in it, the meaning is: So we gave her the good report of Isaac. There are sayings about it: The best of them is that when they did not eat, he denied them and feared them, but when they said, Do not fear, and informed him that they were messengers of God, he was happy with that, so his wife laughed in joy at his joy. It was said: She said to him: I think that these people will be punished, so I will bring Lot to you. So when the messengers came with what she said, I was pleased with it and laughed. An-Nahhas said: If its chain of transmission is sound, then it is good. Laughter is the exposure of the teeth. It is also possible that laughter is the radiance of the face. You say: I saw so-and-so laughing, meaning radiant. And I came upon a meadow that was laughing, meaning radiant. And in the hadith: God, the Exalted, sends the clouds and they laugh the most beautiful laugh. He made its clearing from the lightning laughter, and this is borrowed speech. It was narrated from a man from the readers of Mecca called Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-A’rabi. Fadhahkat with the opening of the ha’, Al-Mahdawi said: The opening of the ha’ of Fadhahkat is not known. And laughter, laughing, laughing, and laughing, four languages. And laughter is a single time, and from it is the saying of Kathir: His laughter closed the necks of money Al-Jawhari said it. Tenth: Muslim narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa`d who said: Abu Usaid al-Sa`idi invited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to his wedding, and his wife was their servant at that time, and she was the bride. Sahl said: Do you know what I gave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to drink? I soaked dates in a bowl for him at night, and when he had eaten, I gave them to him to drink. Al-Bukhari included it and entitled it Chapter on a woman standing over men at a wedding and serving them herself. Our scholars said: It includes the permissibility of a bride serving her husband and his companions at her wedding. It includes that there is nothing wrong with a man presenting his family to his righteous brothers and employing them for them. It is possible that this was before the revelation of the veil. And God knows best. Eleventh: Al-Tabari mentioned that when Abraham, peace be upon him, presented the calf, they said: We will not eat food except for a price. He said to them: Its price is that you remember God at the beginning and praise Him at the end. Gabriel said to his companions: God has rightly taken this as a friend. Our scholars said: And they did not eat because angels do not eat. It was permissible, just as God made it easy for the angels to doubt the human body and appearance, to make it easy for them to eat the food. However, according to the scholars, He sent them in the form of a human and Abraham, peace be upon him, took it upon himself to provide hospitality until he saw the delay and fear, then the good report came to him suddenly. Twelfth: This indicates that saying Bismillah at the beginning of a meal and praising God at the end were prescribed by the nations before us. It was reported in the Isra’iliyyat that Abraham, peace be upon him, would not eat alone. When his meal was ready, he would send for someone to eat with him. One day, he met a man. When he sat down to eat with him, and when he came out, Gabriel came down to him and said to him: God says that He will provide for him despite his disbelief for the rest of his life, and you were stingy with him in giving him a morsel. Abraham went out frightened, dragging his cloak, and said: Go back. He said: I will not go back until you tell me why you sent me back for no reason. So he told him the matter. This is a generous Lord. I have believed. He entered, said Bismillah, and ate as a believer. Thirteenth: The Almighty’s saying: So We gave her good tidings of Isaac. When Ishmael was born to Abraham from Hagar, Sarah wished to have a son, and despaired due to her advanced age. So she was given good tidings of a son who would be a prophet and give birth to a prophet. This was good tidings for her that she would see her son’s son. Fourteenth: The Almighty’s saying: And after Isaac, Jacob. Hamza and Abdullah bin Aamer read Jacob in the accusative case. The rest read Jacob in the nominative case. The nominative case means: And after Isaac, Jacob will happen to her. It is permissible for the verb that acts on from to be in the nominative case, as if the meaning is: And after Isaac, Jacob was established for her. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case, and it is in the position of a state, i.e., We gave her good tidings of Isaac, opposite to him, Jacob. The accusative case means: And We gave her good tidings of Jacob after Isaac. Al-Kisa’i, Al-Akhfash, and Abu Hatim permitted Jacob to be in the genitive case, meaning: And after Isaac, We gave her good tidings of Jacob. Al-Farra’ said: The genitive case is not permissible except by repeating the preposition. Sibawayh said: And if you said: I passed by Zaid the day before yesterday, and yesterday Amr, it would be ugly and vile, because you distinguished between the genitive and what it shares, which is the waw, just as you differentiate between the preposition and the genitive, because the preposition is not separated from the genitive, nor from the waw.
11:72: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Oh woe to me! Al-Zajjaj said: Its original form is Oh woe to me, but the ya’ was replaced with an alif because it is lighter than the ya’ and the kasra, and it did not refer to a supplication for woe upon herself, but it is a word that is easy for women to say when something happens to them that they are surprised by, and they are surprised by her giving birth and by her husband being an old man because it is unusual, and what is unusual is strange and reprehensible. Shall I give birth? is an interrogative that means astonishment. And I am an old woman means an old woman. And she has become old, and she has become old, and she has become old, meaning she has advanced in age. It may also be said: an old woman. A woman is old with a kasra on the jim, her buttocks have become large, and her buttocks have become large, with a damma and fatha on the ‘ayn. Mujahid said: She was ninety-nine years old. Ibn Ishaq said: She was ninety years old. Other than this has been said. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And this is my husband meaning my husband. Old man is in the accusative case as a state, and the agent in it is warning or indication. And this is my husband is the subject and the predicate. Al-Akhfash said: In the reading of Ibn Masoud and Abi And this is my husband is old An-Nahhas said: Just as you say this Zaid is standing, so Zaid is a substitute for this, and standing is the predicate of the subject. It is permissible for this to be the subject and Zaid is standing to be two predicates. Sibawayh narrated: This is sweet and sour. It was said: Abraham was one hundred and twenty years old. It was said: He was one hundred, so he was one year older than that according to Mujahid. It was said: She objected by her saying: And this is my husband is old meaning about his not having intercourse with her. And this Sarah is the wife of Abraham, the daughter of Haran bin Nahor bin Sharu’ bin Arghu bin Faligh, and she is the cousin of Abraham. This is an amazing thing meaning that what you gave me the good report of is an amazing thing.
11:73: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: They said, ‘Do you wonder at the command of God?’ When she said: And I am an old woman and my husband is an old man, and she was amazed, the angels denied her amazement at the command of God, that is, at His decree and destiny, that is, there is no wonder that God would grant you a son, who is Isaac. And with this verse, many scholars have used as evidence that the one to be sacrificed was Ishmael, and that he was older than Isaac, because it gave the good report that Isaac would live until Jacob was born to him. We will discuss this and explain it in As-Saffat, God willing. Second: The Almighty’s saying: The mercy of God and His blessings is the subject, and the predicate is upon you. Sibawayh narrated upon you with a kasra on the kaf because it is adjacent to the ya. Is it a predicate or a supplication? Its being a predicate is more honorable, because that necessitates the attainment of mercy and blessings for them, meaning: May God bestow His mercy and blessings upon you, O people of the household. Its being a supplication only necessitates that it is something that is hoped for and has not yet been attained. The accusative of people of the household is for specificity, and this is the doctrine of Sibawayh. It was also said: for calling. Third: This verse indicates that a man’s wife is from the people of the house, so this indicates that the wives of the prophets are from the people of the house. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and others are from the people of the house of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about whom God said: And purifies you with a thorough purification, and it will come. Fourth: The verse also indicates that the ultimate goal of peace and His blessings as God informed us about the righteous of His servants may the mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, O people of the House. Blessing is growth and increase, and among those blessings is that all the prophets and messengers were in the children of Abraham and Sarah. Malik narrated on the authority of Wahb bin Kaysan Abi Nu`aym on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr bin Ata’ who said: I was sitting with Abdullah bin Abbas when a man from Yemen entered upon him and said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings, then he added something to that, so Ibn Abbas said - and his eyesight had gone that day - who is this? They said: The Yemeni who covers you, so they recognized him, and he said: Peace has ended with blessing. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: I entered the mosque and saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a group of his companions. I said: Peace be upon you. He said: And upon you be peace and the mercy of God, twenty for me and ten for you. He said: I entered a second time and said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God. He said: And upon you be peace and the mercy of God and His blessings, thirty for me and twenty for you. I entered a third time and said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings. He said: And upon you be peace and the mercy of God and His blessings, thirty for me and thirty for you. You and I are equal in peace. He is Praiseworthy and Glorious means Praised and Glorious. We have explained them in The Beautiful Names.
11:74: The Almighty said: So when the terror had departed from Abraham, meaning the fear. It is said: he was terrified of something if he was afraid. Al-Nabigha said: He was terrified by the sound of dogs, so he was subject to the evil eye out of fear and fear of the scorpions. And the good tidings came to him meaning of Isaac and Jacob. Qatada said: They gave him the good tidings that they had only brought the punishment to the people of Lot, and that he would not fear. He argues with Us meaning he argues with Our messengers, and he attributed it to himself, because they had come down at his command. This argument was narrated by Humayd ibn Hilal on the authority of Jundub on the authority of Hudhayfah, and that is because when they said: Indeed, We will destroy the people of this city Al-Ankabut 29:31, he said to them: Tell me, if there were fifty Muslims in it, would you destroy them? They said: No. He said: Then forty? They said: No. He said: Then thirty? They said: No. He said: Then twenty? They said: No. He said: If there were ten in it - or five, Humayd was unsure - they said: No. Qatada said something similar, he said, he meant Ibrahim: A people who do not have ten Muslims, there is no good in them. It was said that Ibrahim said: Tell me, if there was a Muslim man in it, would you destroy it? They said: No. Then Abraham said: "Indeed, within it is Lot. They said, 'We know best who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is among those who remain behind.'" (al-Ankabut 29:32). Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah said: They were four hundred thousand. Ibn Jurayj. And in the villages of the people of Lot were four thousand thousand. The view of al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i is that yujadilna is in place of jadilna. An-Nahhas said: Since the answer to lama must be in the past, the future was made in its place, just as the condition must be in the future, so the past was made in its place. And there is another answer - that yujadilna is in place of the state, meaning he came to argue with us, and this is the view of al-Farra'.
11:75: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, grieving, and turning back [to God]. The meaning of gracious and forbearing was mentioned in (al-Tawbah 9:114). The one who turns back is the one who returns. It is said: he turned back if he returned. Abraham, peace be upon him, used to turn back to God Almighty in all his affairs. It was said: the one who turns back is the one who groans in sorrow for what the people of Lot had lost of faith.
11:76: God Almighty says: O Abraham, turn away from this, meaning, stop arguing about the people of Lot. Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, meaning, His punishment of them. And indeed, there will come upon them, meaning, it will descend upon them. A punishment that cannot be averted, meaning, it will not be averted from them or repelled.
11:77: God Almighty says: And when Our messengers came to Lot, they were distressed because of them. When the angels left Abraham, and there were four farsakhs between Abraham and Lot's village, Lot's two daughters - who were standing straight - saw the angels and saw a good appearance, so they said: What is the matter with you? And where did you come from? They said: From such and such a place, we want this village. They said: Its people are people of immorality. They said: Is there anyone who will host us? They said: Yes! This old man, and they pointed to Lot. When Lot saw your appearance, his people feared for them. Sa'i bihum means he was upset by their coming. It is said: sa'a yusu'u, which is intransitive, and sa'ahu yusu'u, which is also transitive. If you wish, you can add a damma to the seen, because its original form is damma, and the original form is su'i bihum from su'. The vowel of the waw is changed to the seen, so it becomes a ya'. If you lighten the hamza, you put its vowel on the ya', so you say: si bihum lightened, and an irregular language with a shaddah. wa-da-qadda bihum dhur'an means his chest was constricted by their coming and he hated it. It was also said: his capacity and energy were constricted. Its origin is that the camel walks with its hands, an arm's length according to the width of a step, but if it is loaded with more than its shoulders, it becomes constricted from that, and weakens and stretches its neck, so the narrowness of the arm is an expression for the narrowness of the capacity. It was also said: it is from dhara'ahu al-qay', meaning it overcame him, meaning he was constricted from being held back, which was disliked in his soul. He was constricted by them because of what he saw of their beauty, and what he knew of the immorality of his people. "And he said, 'This is a difficult day,' meaning a day of great evil. And the poet said: And unless you are satisfied with Bakr bin Wael, you will have a difficult day in Iraq. Another said: A tough day that makes the heroes nervous, the strong ones get nervous, the tall ones get nervous It is said: ‘Asib and ‘Asab in the form of a group, meaning a group of people who are hated and evil has gathered and has become ‘asab, meaning he has gathered his group with evil, and from this it is said: ‘Asaba and ‘Asaba, meaning those who have gathered the word, meaning they are gathered in themselves. And the ‘Asaba of a man is those who are gathered with him in lineage, and I became a group for so-and-so, I became like his ‘Asaba, and a man is ‘Asab, meaning he has gathered in creation.
11:78: The Almighty said: And his people came running to him in the place of the circumstantial. They rushed means they hastened. Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farra' and other linguists said: Hastening can only be hastening with trembling. It is said: The man rushed hastening, meaning he hurried in a trembling from cold or anger or fever, and he is rushing. Muhalhil said: They came running, prisoners of their money, in spite of their noses. Another said: With acceleration towards him, I rush This is an example of: So-and-so was passionate about the matter, Zaid thundered, and so-and-so was proud. It comes and is only used in this way. It was said: He rushed, meaning his eagerness made him rush, and based on this they rush means they urge him on. And whoever said the first said: He did not hear anything except the man rush, meaning he hurried, in the form of what its agent was not named. Ibn al-Qutiyya said: The person rushed, and he rushed: he was driven and hurried. Al-Harawi said: It is said: The man rushed and rushed, meaning he urged. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, and al-Suddi said: they rush they run. Ad-Dahhak: they run. Ibn Uyaynah: As if they are pushing. Shammar ibn Atiyya said: It is a walk between a trot and a jog. Al-Hasan said: A walk between two walks, and the meaning is close. The reason for their haste was that it was narrated that when the unbelieving wife of Lot saw the guests, their beauty and their appearance, she went out until she reached the gatherings of her people, and she said to them: Lot hosted tonight young men, the likes of whom had never been seen before in beauty, and so on and so forth, so they came running to him. It is mentioned that when the messengers arrived at the land of Lot, they found Lot in his field. It was said: They found his daughter drawing water from the River of Sodom, so they asked her to indicate who was hosting them, and she saw their appearance and feared for them from the people of Lot, and she said to them: Stay where you are! She went to her father and told him, so he came out to them, and they said: We want you to host us tonight, so he said to them: Haven't you heard of the work of these people? They said: What is their work? He said, I bear witness by God that they are the worst people on earth. God Almighty had said to His angels, Do not punish them until Lot bears witness against them four times. When Lot said this, Gabriel said to his companions, This is one thing. The statement was repeated among them until Lot repeated the testimony four times, then he entered the city with them. God the Almighty said: And before meaning before the coming of the messengers. It was also said: before Lot. They used to do evil deeds meaning it was their custom to have intercourse with men. So when they came to Lot and intended to be his guests, Lot stood up to them, defending himself, and said: These are my daughters as a subject and a predicate. There is a difference of opinion regarding his statement: These are my daughters. It was said: He had three daughters from his loins. It was also said: Two daughters, Zayta and Za’ura. It was also said: They had two obedient masters, so he wanted to marry his two daughters to them. It was also said: He urged them in this situation to marry, and their custom was to permit a disbeliever to marry a believing woman. This was permissible at the beginning of Islam, then it was abrogated. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married one of his daughters to Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, and the other to Abu al-‘As ibn al-Rabi’ before the revelation, and they were both disbelievers. A group - including Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair - said that he referred by his statement: my daughters to women as a whole, since the Prophet of the people was a father to them. This is strengthened by the fact that in Ibn Masoud’s reading: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and his wives are their mothers, and he is a father to them. A group said: The speech was only to defend against it and he did not intend to confirm it. This statement was narrated from Abu Ubaidah, just as it is said to someone who forbids eating the property of others: Pork is lawful for you than this. And Ikrimah said: He did not show them his daughters or the daughters of his female slave, but rather he said this to them so that they would turn away. God the Almighty said: They are purer for you is a subject and a predicate, meaning I will marry them to you, so it is purer for you than what you want, meaning more permissible. Purification is abstaining from what is not permissible. Ibn Abbas said: Their leaders had proposed to his daughters but he did not answer them, and on that day he wanted to ransom his guests with his daughters. The alif in athar is not for comparison so that it would be thought that there is purity in a man’s marriage, rather it is like saying: God is greater, higher and more majestic, even if it is not a comparison, and this is permissible and common in the speech of the Arabs, and no one would be stubborn with God the Almighty so that God the Almighty would be greater than him. Abu Sufyan ibn Harb said on the day of UHud 11:High is Hubal, high is Hubal, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Umar: Say God is higher and more majestic. Hubal was never high or majestic. The general public read it by raising the ra’. Al-Hasan and Isa ibn Amr read hunna athar in the accusative case as a state. And hunna is a pillar. Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, and Al-Akhfash do not allow hun here to be a pillar. Rather, it is a pillar in what the sentence is not complete without what comes after it, such as Zayd was your brother, to indicate that brother is not an adjective. Al-Zajjaj said: It indicates that kan needs a predicate. Another said: It indicates that the predicate is definite or what accompanies it. God Almighty says: So fear God and do not disgrace me regarding my guest. That is, do not humiliate me or degrade me. And from this is the saying of Hassan: May God disgrace you, O Atib bin Malik, and may you meet one of the thunderbolts before death. I extended my right hand to the Prophet deliberately and made his mouth bleed. I cut it with lightning. It may be from khazayah, which means shyness and modesty. Dhu al-Rummah said: Shame overtook him after his round of the rope mixed with anger. Another said: She will not be ashamed if the wind sticks to her cloak or the jewelry is removed from her neck. The word guest is used for both persons and all in the singular form, because it is originally a verbal noun. The poet said: Never fail to provide the butcher's knife for the guest, and the guest is the most deserving visitor. It is permissible to use the dual and plural forms, and the first is more common, like when you say: men of fasting, breaking the fast, and lying. A man was disgraced, meaning he was ashamed, like he was humiliated and disgraced. And he was disgraced, if he was disgraced, he is disgraced in both of them. Then he rebuked them by saying: Is there not among you a man of sound mind? meaning a strong man who enjoins what is right and forbids what is wrong. It was said: Rashīd means one who is sound. Or it means one who is rightly guided or guided, meaning righteous or reformer. Ibn Abbas: a believer. Abu Malik: He forbade evil. It was said: Rasheed means guidance, and guidance and rightness are guidance and righteousness. It is permissible for it to mean a guide, like the wise means the judge.
11:79: The Almighty said: They said, 'You have certainly known that we have no right to your daughters.' It was narrated that the people of Lot proposed to his daughters but he rejected them. It was their custom that whoever rejected a woman's proposal was never permissible for him. This is what the Almighty said: They said, 'You have certainly known that we have no right to your daughters.' And after this characteristic does not exist. The point of the speech is that we have no connection to your daughters, nor are they our intention, nor is it our custom to ask for that. And indeed, you know what we want, referring to the guests.
11:80: The Almighty said: He said, 'If only I had power over you' When he saw their persistence in others, and he was weak against them, and was unable to repel them, he wished he had found help to repel them, so he said in a manner of grief and submission: (If only I had power over you) meaning supporters and helpers. Ibn Abbas said: He meant a child. And that is in the nominative case with an implied verb, the meaning of which is: If it happened or occurred. This is consistent with that that follows if. The answer to if is omitted, meaning I would have returned the people of corruption, and stood between them and what they want. Or I take refuge in a strong support meaning I seek refuge and gather. Or I take refuge was read in the accusative case in apposition to strength as if he said: If only I had power over you or shelter in a strong support, meaning if I take refuge, so it is accusative with the implied that. What Lot meant by the support was the clan, and the abundance. Their ugly actions led them to say this, even though he knew what was with God. It is narrated that the angels were angry with him when he said these words, and they said: Your refuge is indeed strong. In Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on Lot, for he used to take refuge in a strong refuge. The hadith was mentioned earlier in Al-Baqarah. Al-Tirmidhi included it and added: God did not send a prophet after him except in a wealthy family of his people. Muhammad ibn Amr said: Wealth is abundance and strength, a good hadith. It is narrated that when Lot’s people defeated him, and they intended to break down the door while he was holding it, the messengers said to him: Move away from the door. So he moved away and the door opened, but Gabriel struck them with his wing and blinded their eyes, and they turned back on their heels saying: Save us. God, the Most High, said: And they certainly sought to seduce him from his guest, but We blinded their eyes. (al-Qamar 54:37) Ibn Abbas and the commentators said: Lot closed his door and the angels were with him in the house, and he was debating with his people and imploring them from behind the door, while they were trying to climb over the wall. When the angels saw the effort, distress and fatigue he had endured because of them, they said: O Lot, your support is severe, and there will come to them a punishment that cannot be averted, and we are messengers of your Lord, so open the door and leave us and them. So he opened the door and Gabriel struck them with his wing as mentioned above. It was said: Gabriel took a handful of dirt and threw it in their faces, so God reached the eyes of those far away and those near that dirt and blinded their eyes, so they did not know the way, nor were they guided to their homes, and they kept saying: Escape, escape! For in the house of Lot there are people who are the most magicians on the face of the earth, and they have bewitched us and blinded our sight. And they kept saying: O Lot, stay where you are until morning, and you will see, threatening him.
11:81: The Almighty said: They said, 'O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord.' When the angels saw his grief, turmoil and defense, they recognized him by themselves. When he knew that they were messengers, he allowed his people to enter. Then he ordered Gabriel, peace be upon him, to cover their eyes, so they became blind, and their hands, so they dried up. They will not reach you meaning with harm. So travel by night with your family. The word Fasir was read with the alif connected and disconnected, two dialects, so they are clear. God Almighty said: And the night when it departs (al-Fajr 89:4) and He said: Glory be to Him Who sent you by night (al-Isra’ 17:1). Al-Nabigha said, combining the two dialects: A strong wind from Gemini blew over him, bringing freezing cold to the north. Another said: Al-Nadira neighborhood, the mistress of the chamber has whispered to you, but she was not in a hurry It has been said: Fasir with a sukoon if he walked from the beginning of the night, and Sara if he walked from the end of it, and it is not said during the day except Sara. Labid said: If a person is taken prisoner at night, he thinks he has done a good deed, but a person is a worker as long as he lives. Abdullah bin Rawaha said: When the morning comes, people praise the secret and the darkness of sleep disappears from them. The Almighty’s saying: of the night nor Ibn Abbas said: in a part of the night. Ad-Dahhak: in the remainder of the night. Qatada: after the middle of the night has passed. Al-Akhfash: after the darkness of the night. Ibn Al-A’rabi: in an hour of the night. It was also said: in the darkness of the night. It was also said: after a lull in the night. It was also said: a part of the night. They are all close together. It was also said: it is the middle of the night, taken from cutting it in half, and from this is the saying of the poet: A mourner wails through the night for a man in the middle of Upper Egypt If it is said: The night journey only takes place at night, then what is the meaning of in a part of the night? The answer is: If he had not said: in a part of the night, it would have been permissible for it to be the beginning. And let none of you turn back meaning, let none of you look behind him, as Mujahid said. Ibn Abbas: None of you should stay behind. Ali bin Isa: None of you should be occupied with what he leaves behind of money or belongings. Except your wife in the accusative case, which is the clear reading with an obvious meaning, meaning, so travel with your family except your wife. And likewise in the reading of Ibn Masoud so travel with your family except your wife, so he is an exception from the family. Based on this, he did not take her with him. And God the Almighty said: She was among those who remained behind Al-Ankabut 29:32, meaning among those who remained. Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read: Except your wife in the nominative case as a substitute for one. A group of people, including Abu Ubaid, denied this reading, and said: It is not correct except by raising yaltafi and it is an adjective, because the meaning becomes - if it is replaced and made jussive - that the woman is permitted to turn around, and the meaning is not like that. An-Nahhas said: This interpretation by Abu Ubaid and others on the likes of Abu Amr, despite its greatness and its place in Arabic, is not necessary, and raising it as a substitute has a correct meaning, and the interpretation of it is according to what Muhammad bin Al-Walid narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid that a man says to his chamberlain: So-and-so should not go out, so the wording of the prohibition is for so-and-so and its meaning is for the addressee, i.e. do not let him go out, and similar to it is your saying: No one should stand except Zaid, its meaning is: forbid them from standing except Zaid, and likewise the prohibition is for Lot and its wording is for someone else, as if he said: forbid them, no one should turn around from them except your wife. It may be an exception to the prohibition of turning around because it is a complete statement, meaning, none of you should turn around except your wife, for she will turn around and perish. Lot went out with her, and he forbade those who were taken with him from turning around, but none of them turned around except his wife. When she heard the roar of the torment, she turned around and said, Oh my people! Then a stone overtook her and killed her. It will befall her means from the torment. The metaphor in it refers to the matter and the affair, meaning that the matter, the affair, and the story. “It will befall them what will befall them. Their appointed time is the morning.” When the angels said, Indeed, we will destroy the people of this city Al-Ankabut 29:31, Lot said, Now, now. He hastened the torment for them out of his anger at his people, so they said, Is not the morning near? Isa bin Omar read Is not the morning with a damma on the ba’, which is a language. It is possible that he made the morning the appointed time for their destruction, because souls are more trustworthy in it, and people are united in it. Some of the commentators said: Lot went out with his two daughters, and no one else was with him, at dawn, and the angels said to him: God has appointed for you in this town angels with the sound of thunder, lightning flashes, and great thunderbolts. We have mentioned to them that Lot will go out, so do not harm him. His sign is that he will not look back, and his two daughters will not look back, so do not be alarmed by what you see. So Lot went out, and God rolled up the earth for him in his time until he was saved and reached Abraham.
11:82: The Almighty said: So when Our command came meaning Our punishment. We turned it upside down This is because Gabriel, peace be upon him, put his wing under the villages of the people of Lot, and they were five: Sodom - which is the largest village - Gomorrah, and Dadoma. They put it down and raised it from the edges of the earth until it was closest to the sky with everything in it, until the people of the sky heard the braying of their donkeys and the crowing of their roosters. Not a single jar was turned over for them, nor was a single vessel broken for them. Then they were thrown down on their heads, and God followed them with stones. Muqatil: Four were killed, and Da'wah was saved. Others were said, and God knows best. The Almighty’s saying: And We rained down upon them stones of baked clay is evidence that the one who did what they did was stoning, and this has been mentioned previously in Al-A’raf. In the interpretation: We rained in punishment, and We rained in mercy. As for the speech of the Arabs, it is said: The sky rained and it rained, as narrated by Al-Harawi. There is a difference of opinion regarding Sijil. Al-Nahhas said: Sijil is severe and plentiful, and Sijil and Sijjin, the lam and the nun, are sisters. Abu Ubaidah said: Sijil is severe, and he recited: A beating that the heroes recommended to be done to a prisoner An-Nahhas said: Abdullah bin Muslim responded to him and said: This is a prison and that is a book, so how can he be cited as evidence?! An-Nahhas said: This response is not necessary, because Abu Ubaidah believed that the letter lam is replaced by the letter nun due to the proximity of one to the other, and Abu Ubaidah’s statement is rejected from another angle, which is that if it were according to his statement, it would have been stones of sijil, because it is not said: stones of shadid, because shadid is an adjective. Abu Ubaidah narrated from Al-Farra’ that millstones are sometimes called sijil. Muhammad bin Al-Jahm narrated from him that sijil is clay that is cooked until it becomes like millstones. A group of them, including Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair and Ibn Ishaq, said: Sijil is a non-Arabic word that was Arabized, its origin is sanj and jil. It is also said: sanak wakil, with a kaf in place of the jim, and in Persian they are stone and clay that the Arabs Arabized and made them one name. It was said: it is from the language of the Arabs. Qatada and Ikrimah said: As-Sajil is clay, as evidenced by His statement: That We may send upon them stones of clay (al-Dhariyat 51:33). Al-Hasan said: The origin of stones was clay, but they were hardened. As-Sajil among the Arabs means anything hard and solid. Ad-Dahhak said: It means bricks. Ibn Zayd said: Clay that has been baked until it is like bricks. It was narrated from him that As-Sajil is the name of the lowest heaven. This was mentioned by Al-Mahdawi, and Al-Tha’labi narrated it from Abu Al-Aaliyah. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is weak and is refuted by its description as manḥudūd. It was narrated from Ikrimah: It is a sea suspended in the air between the heaven and the earth, from which the stones descended. It was said: They are mountains in the sky, and they are what God referred to in His statement: And He sends down from the sky, from mountains, wherein is hail (al-Nur 24:43). It was said: It is from what was recorded for them, meaning He wrote for them that it would befall them, so it is in the meaning of Sijjīn prison. God the Almighty said: And what will make you know what is Sijjīn? It is a book inscribed (al-Mutaffifin 83:8-9). This was said by Az-Zajjaj and he chose it. It was said: It is a verbal noun from the verb asjalltuhu, meaning I sent it, so it is as if it was sent upon them. It was also said: It is from asjalltuhu, meaning I gave it, so it is as if it were a punishment they gave it. He said: Whoever debates with me debates with a noble man who fills the bucket to the limit of distress The people of meaning said: Sijjil and Sijjin are severe stones and beatings. Ibn Muqbil said: And a man beats the whites of the suburb with a beating that the heroes commanded the prisoner to do Manḍūd Ibn Abbas said: successive. Qatada said: He arranged some of them on top of each other. Al-Rabi' said: He arranged some of them on top of each other until they became one body. Ikrimah said: arranged. Some of them said: arranged, and the meaning is close. It is said: you arranged the goods and the milk if you put some of them on top of each other, so it is manḍūd, naḍīd, and naḍūd. He said: And I raised it to the two curtains and the table
11:83: Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali said: Ma'add, meaning it is among what God has prepared for His oppressive enemies. Marked means marked, from the word seema which means a mark, meaning it had something like rings on it. It was said: Written on each stone was the name of the person who was thrown at it, and it was unlike the stones of the earth. Al-Farra' said: They claimed that it was striped with red and black on white, and that was its marking. Ka'b said: It was marked with white and red, and the poet said: A young man whom God has blessed with beauty, with a features that are not difficult for the eye to see. Marked is an adjective for stones. Arranged is an adjective for Sijjil. In His statement, with your Lord, there is evidence that it is not from the stones of the earth, as Al-Hasan said. And it is not far from the wrongdoers, meaning the people of Lot, meaning it did not miss them. Mujahid said: It terrifies the Quraysh, meaning: The stones are not far from the wrongdoers of your people, O Muhammad. Qatada and Ikrimah said: It means the wrongdoers of this nation, and by God, God has not protected a wrongdoer from them yet. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “There will be in the last days of my nation a people whose men will be content with men and whose women will be content with women. When that happens, then await the punishment of the people of Lot, that God will send upon them stones of baked clay.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: And it is not far from the wrongdoers. In a narration from him, peace be upon him: “The nights and days will not pass until this nation considers the backsides of men permissible as they considered the backsides of women permissible, and groups of this nation will be struck by stones from your Lord.” It was said: The meaning is that these villages are not far from the oppressors, and they are between Ash-Sham and Madinah. And far came in the masculine form meaning a far place. And regarding the stones that rained, there are two sayings: One of them: That they rained on the cities when Gabriel raised them. The second: That they rained on those of the people who were not in the cities and were outside of them.
11:84: The Almighty said: And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb. That is, We sent to Madyan, and Madyan is the people of Shu'ayb. There are two opinions about their name: One of them is that they are the sons of Madyan, son of Abraham. It was said: Madyan, meaning the sons of Madyan. Just as it was said: Mudar, meaning the sons of Mudar. The second opinion is that it is the name of their city, so they were attributed to it. An-Nahhas said: Madyan is not declined because it is the name of a city. This meaning and more were mentioned in Al-A'raf. He said, O my people, worship God; you have no deity other than Him. It was mentioned. And do not reduce the measure or the weight. They were, along with their disbelief, people of shortcoming and cheating. When a seller came to them with food, they would take an extra measure and take as much as they could and be unjust. When a buyer came to them with food, they would sell it for a lesser measure and be stingy with as much as they could. So they were commanded to believe in order to refrain from polytheism, and to fulfill as a prohibition against cheating. I see you in good health, meaning in abundance of provision and many blessings. Al-Hasan said: Their price was cheap. And I fear for you the punishment of a comprehensive Day. He described the day as encompassing, and he meant to describe that day as encompassing them, because when the day of punishment encompasses them, then the punishment has encompassed them, and it is like saying: a severe day, meaning a day of intense heat. There is a difference of opinion about that punishment. It was said: it is the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter. It was said: it is the punishment of extermination in this world. It was said: it is the high price, its meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas. In the hadith from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: A people do not show cheating in measuring and weighing except that God afflicts them with famine and high prices. And it was mentioned earlier.
11:85: The Almighty said: And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice. He ordered giving full measure and weight in justice after forbidding cheating for emphasis. Giving full means completing. In justice meaning with justice and truth. The intended meaning is that everyone who has a share should receive his share. He does not mean giving full measure and weight because He did not say: Give full measure and weight. Rather, He meant that you should not reduce the size of the customary measure, and the same applies to cymbals. And do not deprive people of their dues meaning do not deprive them of anything they are entitled to. And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption. He explained that treachery in measuring and weighing is an exaggeration in corruption on the earth. More on this has already been mentioned in Al-A'raf, and praise be to God.
11:86: The Almighty said: What remains from God is better for you meaning what God leaves for you after fulfilling rights in justice is more blessed and has a better outcome than what you leave for yourselves of the excess of cheating through arrogance and injustice. Al-Tabari and others said its meaning. Mujahid said: What remains from God is better for you meaning obeying Him. Al-Rabi' said: God's commandment. Al-Farra' said: God's observation.
