Ibn Zayd: God's mercy. Qatada and Al-Hasan: Your portion from your Lord is better for you. Ibn Abbas said: God's provision is better for you. If you are believers is a condition for this because they only know the truth of this if they are believers. It was said: It is possible that they were acknowledging that God is their Creator, so He addressed them with this. And I am not a guardian over you meaning a watcher who watches you when you measure and weigh, meaning I cannot witness every transaction that you do until I hold you accountable for fulfilling your right. It was said: It is not possible for me to protect you from removing God's blessings upon you due to your disobedience.
11:87: The Almighty said: They said, 'O Shu'ayb, your prayer' It was read your prayers without the plural. Does it command you that we should abandon what our fathers worshipped? An is in the accusative case. Al-Kisa'i said: Its position is in the genitive case because of the omission of the ba'. It was narrated that Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, prayed a lot, and was consistent in worship, both obligatory and voluntary. He used to say: Prayer prevents indecency and wrongdoing. So when he commanded and forbade them, they taunted him for what they saw him doing frequently in prayer, and they mocked him and said: What did God inform about them? It was said: Prayer here means reading. Sufyan said it on the authority of Al-A'mash, meaning your reading commands you, and this indicates that they were disbelievers. Al-Hasan said: God did not send a prophet except that He imposed upon him prayer and zakat. Or that we do with our wealth as we wish Al-Farra' claimed that the meaning is: Or do you forbid us from doing with our wealth as we wish. Al-Salami and Al-Dahhak bin Qais read or that you do with our wealth as you wish with the letter taa in both verbs, and the meaning is: whatever you wish, O Shuaib. Al-Nahhas said: or that in this reading is connected to the first an. It was narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam that he said: Among the things he forbade them from was the deletion of the dirhams. It was also said that the meaning of or that we do with our wealth as we wish is if we agreed to a covenant between us for less, then why did you prevent us from it?! Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided they mean in your opinion, and the same is in the description of Abu Jahl: Taste, indeed, you are the mighty, the generous (al-Dukhan 44:49), meaning in your opinion, in your opinion. It was also said that they said it in a mocking and derisive manner, as Qatada said. And from this is their saying to the Abyssinian: Abu Al-Baydaa, and to the white one: Abu Al-Jun, and from this is the saying of the guards of Hell to Abu Jahl: Taste, indeed, you are the mighty, the generous. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: The Arabs describe a thing by its opposite for superstition and optimism, as they say that a stray dog is salim and that a desert is mafsah. It was also said: It is an insinuation that they intended to insult, and better than all of this, and what precedes it indicates its correctness, meaning that you are truly the forbearing and wise, so how do you order us to abandon what our fathers worshipped! And what follows indicates it. Your prayers order you to abandon what our fathers worshipped. They denied it when they saw his frequent prayers and worship, and that he is forbearing and wise in order to order them to abandon what their fathers used to avoid, and what follows also indicates it.
11:88: He said, 'O my people, have you considered, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me from Himself with a good provision?' That is, should I not forbid you from going astray?! All of this indicates that they said it in a true sense, and that it was their belief in it. This meaning is similar to what the Jews of Banu Qurayzah said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he said to them, O brothers of the monkeys! They said, O Muhammad, we did not know you to be ignorant! Question: The commentators said: One of the things that they were forbidden from doing, and for which they were punished, was cutting up dinars and dirhams. They would lend from the edges of the correct coins so that the loan would be better for them. They would deal with the correct coins by counting, and with the loaned coins by weight, and they would cheat in the weight. Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: They would break the dinars and dirhams, and a group of the earlier commentators said the same, such as Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Zaid bin Aslam and others. Breaking them is a great sin. In the book of Abu Dawud, on the authority of Alqamah bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade breaking the coins of the Muslims that are permissible among them except for a reason.” Because if they are correct, their meaning is established and their benefit becomes apparent, and if they are broken, they become a commodity and their benefit is nullified, and that harms the people, and for this reason it is forbidden. It has been said in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: And there were in the city nine men who spread corruption in the land and did not reform (al-Naml 27:48) that they used to break dirhams, as Zaid bin Aslam said. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: They claimed that there was no one in the city more knowledgeable about the interpretation of the Qur’an than Zaid bin Aslam after Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi. Question: Asbagh said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim ibn Khalid ibn Janadah, the client of Zayd ibn al-Harith al-Ataqi, said: Whoever breaks it, his testimony is not accepted, and if he excuses himself with ignorance, he is not excused, and this is not a place for an excuse. Ibn al-Arabi said: As for his saying: His testimony is not accepted, it is because he committed a major sin, and major sins negate justice but not minor ones. As for his saying: His excuse with ignorance is not accepted in this, it is because it is a clear matter that is not hidden from anyone, and the excuse is only accepted if the truthfulness in it is apparent, or the aspect of truthfulness in it is hidden, and God knows it better than the servant, as Malik said. Question: If this is a sin and corruption for which testimony is rejected, then the one who did it will be punished. Ibn al-Musayyab passed by a man who had been flogged and said: What is this? A man said: He is cutting off dinars and dirhams. Ibn al-Musayyab said: This is corruption on earth, and he did not disapprove of his flogging. A similar statement was reported from Sufyan. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Najibi said: I was sitting with Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who was the governor of Medina at that time, and a man was brought who was cutting off dirhams and he had testified against him. He flogged him and shaved his head, and ordered him to be paraded around, and ordered him to say: This is the punishment for one who cuts off dirhams. Then he ordered him to be returned to him. He said: Nothing prevented me from cutting off your hand except that I had not done so before today, and I have done so, so whoever wants to cut off may do so. Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: As for disciplining him with a whip, there is no question about it. As for shaving it, Omar did it. During my days of judging between people, I used to beat and shave. I only did that for those who saw their hair as an aid to their sin and a way to beautify themselves with it in corruption. This is what is required in every way of sin, that it should be cut off if it does not affect the body. As for cutting off his hand, Omar took that from the chapter on theft, because lending dirhams is not breaking them. Breaking is a corruption of the description, and lending is a reduction in the value. It is taking money for the purpose of concealment. If it is said: Is not protection the basis for cutting off? We say: It is possible that Omar saw that preparing it for judging between people, whether a dinar or a dirham, was a protection for it, and the protection of everything is according to its condition. Ibn Al-Zubayr implemented that, and cut off a man’s hand for cutting off dinars and dirhams. Our Maliki scholars said: Dinars and dirhams are the seals of God with His name on them. If, according to the people of interpretation, someone who breaks a seal of God is worthy of that, or someone who breaks a seal of a ruler with His name on it is disciplined, and the seal of God is what fulfills needs, so they are not equal in punishment. Ibn al-Arabi said: I think that the hand should be cut off for lending it but not for breaking it. I used to do that during my rule, except that I was surrounded by ignorant people, so I did not respond because of the words of the envious and misguided. So whoever among the people of truth is able to do it one day, let him do it for the sake of God the Most High. God the Almighty said: He said, ‘O my people, have you considered, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord?’ It was mentioned above. And has provided me from it a good provision. That is, ample and lawful. Shu’aib, peace be upon him, had a lot of money, as Ibn Abbas and others said. It was said: He meant by it guidance and success, knowledge and understanding, and there is an omission in the speech, which is what we mentioned, that is, should I not forbid you from going astray! It was said: The meaning is Have you considered, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord should I follow misguidance? It was said: The meaning is Have you considered, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord would you order me to disobey in reducing and defrauding, while God has made me independent of that? And I do not want to disobey you is in the accusative case with I want. To what He forbade you from that is, I do not forbid you from something and commit it, just as I do not abandon what I have commanded you to do. I only desire reform as much as I am able means I only desire to do good, that is, to reform your worldly life with justice, and your afterlife with worship. He said: as much as I am able because ability is a condition of action, not will. And what is a source, meaning I only desire reform according to my effort and ability. And my success means my guidance, and success is guidance. Except in God, upon Him I have relied means I have depended. And to Him I turn means I return regarding all the misfortunes that befall me. It was said: To Him I turn in the afterlife. It was said: Repentance is supplication, and its meaning is and to Him I supplicate.
11:89: The Almighty said: "And O my people, do not let my hostility lead you to abandon faith, so that what befell the disbelievers before you befalls you, said Al-Hasan and Qatadah. It was said: Do not let my hostility lead you to suffer the punishment, as it befell those who came before you, said Al-Zajjaj. The meaning of leads you to it was mentioned earlier in Al-Ma'idah and discord in Al-Baqarah, and here it means enmity, said Al-Suddi. From this is the saying of Al-Akhtal: Is there anyone who can convey my message to me? How can you find the taste of discord? Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: It is harmful. Qatada said: My separation. And the people of Lot are not far from you, because they had recently experienced the destruction of the people of Lot. It was said: And the dwellings of the people of Lot are not far from you, meaning in a distant place, and that is why the word far was used alone. Al-Kisa’i said: It means their homes are in your homes.
11:90: The Almighty said: And, O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord and then repent to Him. It was mentioned above. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving. These are two of His names, glory be to Him, and we have explained them in the book Al-Asna fi Sharh Al-Asmaa Al-Husna. Al-Jawhari said: I loved a man, I loved him, and Al-Wadood is the lover, and Al-Wad, Al-Wad, Al-Wadda, and Al-Mawaddah are love. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "that whenever he mentioned Shu'aib, he would say: That is the orator of the prophets."
11:91: God the Almighty said: They said, 'O Shu'aib, we do not understand much of what you say.' That is, we do not understand, because you burden us with matters that are not known to us, such as the resurrection and the Hereafter, and you preach to us with things that we have never known before. It was also said that they said that out of aversion to listening to him and disdain for his speech. It is said: Faqah yafqhu means he understood. Al-Kisa'i narrated: Faqah faqhan wa fiqhan means he became a jurist. "And indeed, we see you weak among us." It was said: He was afflicted with a vision problem. This was said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah. It was also said: He had weak eyesight. This was said by Al-Thawri and An-Nahhas narrated from him something similar to what Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said. An-Nahhas said: The linguists narrated that Himyar says to a blind person: "Da'if," meaning he has weakened due to the loss of his eyesight, just as they say to him: "Blind," meaning he has been harmed by the loss of his eyesight, just as they say to him: "Makfoof," meaning he has been prevented from seeing due to the loss of his eyesight. Al-Hasan said: Its meaning is humiliated. It was said: The meaning is weak in body, as narrated by Ali bin Issa. Al-Suddi said: Alone, you do not have soldiers or helpers with which you can oppose us. It was said: He has little knowledge of the interests of this world and the politics of its people. Weak is in the accusative case as a state. And were it not for your people is raised as a subject, and a man’s people are his clan whom he relies on and is strengthened by. From this comes the word rahatā’ for the jerboa’s hole, because it trusts itself in it and hides its children in it. The meaning of l-rajmanak is l-slay you by stoning, and if they killed a person, they would stone him with stones, and his people were from their religion. It was said: The meaning of l-rajmanak is l-swear you, and from this comes the saying of Al-Ja’di: Our translations are so bitter that we become like a racehorse Stoning also means cursing, and from it comes the accursed Satan. And you are not powerful over us meaning you are not victorious, dominant, or immune to us.
11:92: The Almighty said: He said, 'O my people, throw away my burdens' 'Arha'ti is raised by the beginning, and the meaning is throw away my burdens in your hearts more precious to you than God and greater and more majestic and He owns you. And you took it behind your backs meaning you took what I brought you from the command of God behind your backs, meaning you put it behind your backs, and you refrained from killing me for fear of my people. It is said: I put his command behind me if you fell short in it, and it has been mentioned in Al-Baqarah, Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do meaning of disbelief and disobedience. Encompassing meaning Knowing. And it was said: Preserver.
11:93: The Almighty said: "And O my people, work according to your position. Indeed, I am working. You will soon come to know." A threat and a warning, and it was mentioned before in Al-An'am. Whoever is visited by a punishment that will disgrace him means that it will destroy him. And who is in the accusative case, like He will know the corrupter from the reformer. (al-Baqarah 2:220) And whoever is a liar is in apposition to it. It was said: That is, you will soon know who among us is a liar. It was said: It is in the nominative case, meaning: And He will disgrace whoever is a liar. It was said: Its meaning is: And whoever is a liar will know his lie and taste the consequences of his action. Al-Farra' claimed that they only used huwa in and whoever is a liar because they do not say who is standing, rather they say: whoever stands, and whoever stands, and whoever is standing, so they added huwa so that it would be a sentence that takes the place of a verb and does. An-Nahhas said: The opposite of this is indicated by his saying: From my messenger to Thuraya that I am fed up with her and the book And wait, for I am with you, watching. That is, wait for the punishment and wrath, for I am waiting for victory and mercy.
11:94: The Almighty said: And when Our command came It was said: Gabriel shouted at them a shout and their souls left their bodies We saved Shu'aib and those who believed with him by mercy from Us, and the shout seized those who did wrong That is, Gabriel's shout. And you are the verb in the form of the shout, and he said in the story of Salih: And the shout seized those who did wrong (Hud 11:67) So it was mentioned in the meaning of the shout. Ibn Abbas said: God did not destroy two nations with one punishment except the people of Salih and the people of Shu'aib. God destroyed them with the shout, except that the people of Salih were seized by the shout from beneath them, and the people of Shu'aib were seized by the shout from above them. So they became in their homes, prostrated.
11:95: "As if they had never sung therein. Except away with Madyan, as Thamud were destroyed." Its meaning was presented. Al-Kisa'i narrated that Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read as Thamud was destroyed with a damma on the 'ayn. Al-Nahhas said: What is known in the language is that it is only said after he perishes after he perishes. Al-Mahdawi said: From the damma on the 'ayn of ba'dat, it is a language used for good and evil, and its source is distance, and after it is used for evil in particular, it is said: after he perishes after he perishes, so after according to the reading of the group means a curse, and the meaning of the two languages may come together due to their closeness in meaning, so it is from what came its source in a different form due to the closeness of the meanings.
11:96: The Almighty said: And We sent Moses with Our signs He explained that he followed the prophet to establish the proof and remove every defect with Our signs meaning with the Torah. It was said: with miracles. And a clear authority meaning a clear argument, meaning the staff. The meaning of authority and its derivation have already been mentioned in Al Imran, so there is no point in repeating it.
11:97: "To Pharaoh and his people. So they followed the command of Pharaoh," meaning his affair and condition, until they took him as a god and disobeyed the command of God Almighty. And Pharaoh's command was not sound, meaning sound and leading to what is right. It was said: Sound meaning guiding to good.
11:98: The Almighty says: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection meaning that he will precede them to the Fire, as he is their leader. It is said: He preceded them, if he preceded them. He brought them into the Fire means he entered them into it. It is mentioned in the past tense, and the meaning is he will bring them into the Fire. Whatever is realized is as if it is going to happen, so this is why the future is expressed in the past. And an evil place to be brought in means an evil entrance to be entered. He did not say evil because the speech refers to the place to which one is brought in, which is like you say: What an excellent home is your home, and What an excellent home is your home. The place to which one is brought in is the water to which one is brought in, and it is in the sense of the action.
11:99: The Almighty said: And they will be pursued in this worldly life with a curse meaning in this world. And on the Day of Resurrection meaning and the curse of the Day of Resurrection, and this meaning has already been mentioned. What an evil provision is that which is provided Al-Kisa'i and Abu Ubaidah narrated: I supported him, I supported him, meaning I helped him and gave him. The name of the gift is rafd, meaning what an evil gift and assistance. Rafd also means a huge cup, said Al-Jawhari, and the interpretation is: What an evil provision is the provision of the one who is provided. Al-Mawardi mentioned: Rafd with the fat-ha of the cup, and rafd with the kasra of it is what is in the cup of drink, this was narrated from Al-Asma'i, so it is as if he was criticizing what they are given to drink in the fire. It was said: Rafd is the increase, meaning what an evil provision they are given after drowning in the fire, said Al-Kalbi.
11:100: The Almighty said: "That is from the report of the towns. We relate it to you." That is in the nominative case with an implied subject, meaning the matter is that. And if you wish, with the subject, and the meaning is: That is the previous report from the report of the towns. Among them are standing and harvested. Qatada said: Standing is what was empty on its trellises, and harvested is what has no trace. It was said: Standing is inhabited, and harvested is ruined, Ibn Abbas said: Mujahid said: Standing empty on its trellises, and harvested is uprooted, meaning harvested like the crop when it is harvested. The poet said: People are divided among themselves like crops, some of which are standing and some of which are harvested. Another said: We are like raw seed, when the time comes for its harvest Al-Akhfash Saeed said: Haseed means harvested, and its plural is hasadi and hasad like marad and marad. He said: It is for someone who has a harvest, like qatila and qatala.
11:101: And We did not wrong them The root of injustice in the language is putting something in the wrong place, and it was mentioned in detail in Al-Baqarah. But they wronged themselves by disbelief and sins. Sibawayh narrated that it is said: He wronged him. So their gods which they called upon besides God did not avail them at all There is an omission in the speech, meaning which they used to worship, meaning call upon. When the command of your Lord came, and they did not increase them except in destruction meaning except in loss, as Mujahid and Qatadah said. Labid said: I have been afflicted, and every man of innovation will return to affliction, and that is the end of the world. And destruction is loss and ruin, and there is an implication in it, meaning that their worship of idols increased them, so the complement was deleted, meaning that their worship of them had caused them to lose the reward of the Hereafter.
11:102: The Almighty said: And thus did your Lord seize when He seized the towns meaning, just as He seized these towns that belonged to Noah, Aad, and Thamud, He seized all the unjust towns. Asim Al-Jahdari and Talha bin Masraf read And thus did your Lord seize when He seized the towns and also from Al-Jahdari And thus did your Lord seize like the group When He seized the towns. Al-Mahdawi said that whoever reads: And thus did your Lord seize when He seized then it is a report of what was customary in destroying the previous nations, and the meaning is: And thus did your Lord seize those He took from the destroyed nations when He seized them. The group read it as a source, and the meaning is: And thus did your Lord seize whomever He wanted to destroy when He seized them, so when for the past, meaning when He seized the towns, and if for the future, and it was unjust meaning and its people were unjust, so the complement was deleted like and ask the town (Yusuf 12:82) Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe meaning His punishment for the polytheists is painful and severe. In Sahih Muslim and Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Abu Musa, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty gives the wrongdoer respite until, when He seizes him, He does not let him go. Then he recited: And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes towns Al-Tirmidhi 10:10. Abu Isa said: This is a good, sound, strange hadith.
11:103: The Almighty said: Indeed in that is a sign meaning a lesson and an admonition. For him who fears the punishment of the Hereafter "That is a Day" is a subject and predicate. "Gathered" is from its description. "For Him are the people" is a noun for what its agent is not named, and for this reason He did not say gathered. If you assume that the people is raised by the subject, and the predicate is gathered for Him, then He did not say gathered on this estimation, because For Him takes the place of the agent. The plural is hashre, meaning they will be gathered for that day. "And that is a witnessed Day" meaning that the righteous and the wicked will witness it, and the people of heaven will witness it. We have mentioned these two names with other names of the Resurrection in the Book of Remembrance and explained them, and praise be to God. The words of God the Almighty: And a witness and what is witnessed. There is a difference of opinion regarding them. Ali, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with them said: The witness is Friday, and what is witnessed is the Day of Arafah. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan. Abu Hurairah narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: (The promised day is the Day of Resurrection, the witnessed day is the Day of Arafah, and the witness is Friday...) Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi included it in his Jami', and he said: This is a hasan gharib hadith. We do not know it except from the hadith of Musa ibn Ubaidah, and Musa ibn Ubaidah is considered weak in hadith. Yahya ibn Sa'id and others weakened him. Shu'bah, Sufyan Ath-Thawri, and more than one of the imams narrated it from him. Al-Qushayri said: Friday is a witness against every worker for what he did on it. I said: And so it is for all the other days and nights, for every day is a witness, and so is every night. The evidence for this is what Abu Nu`aym al-Hafiz narrated on the authority of Mu`awiyah ibn Qurrah, on the authority of Ma`qil ibn Yasar, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is not a day that comes upon the servant except that it is called out in it: O son of Adam, I am a new creation. I am a witness to what you do, so do good for me and I will bear witness for it for you tomorrow, for if I were to pass away, you would never see me again. And the night says the same.” This is a strange hadith from the hadith of Mu`awiyah, narrated only by Zayd al-`Ami, and I do not know of it as being traced back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except with this chain of transmission. Al-Qushayri narrated on the authority of Ibn `Umar and Ibn al-Zubayr that the witness is the Day of Eid al-Adha. Sa`id ibn al-Musayyab said: The witness is al-Tarwiyah, and the witnessed is the Day of `Arafah. Israel narrated on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of `Ali, may God be pleased with him: The witness is the Day of `Arafah, and the witnessed is the Day of Sacrifice. An-Nakha`i said the same. `Ali also said: The witnessed is the Day of `Arafah. Ibn Abbas and Al-Hussein bin Ali, may God be pleased with them, said: The Day of Resurrection will be witnessed, as God Almighty said: That is a Day when the people will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day (Hud 11:103). I said: And based on this, the scholars’ statements differed regarding the witness. It was said: God Almighty, according to Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Saeed bin Jubayr. Its explanation is: And sufficient is God as a witness (An-Nisa’: 79). Say, ‘What is the greatest testimony?’ Say, ‘God is Witness between me and you.’ It was also said that it was Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas as well as Al-Hussein bin Ali. Ibn Abbas read, How will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? (An-Nisa’: 41), and Al-Hussein read, O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner. (al-Ahzab 33:45) I said: And I recite: And the Messenger will be a witness over you (al-Baqarah 2:143). It was said: The prophets bear witness over their nations, based on the Almighty’s saying: How will it be when We bring from every nation a witness? (An-Nisa’: 41). It was also said: Adam. It was also said: Jesus, son of Mary, based on His saying: And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them (al-Ma’idah 5:117). The witnessed: his nation. Also from Ibn Abbas and Muhammad ibn Ka’b: The witness is the human being, evidence for which is: Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as accountant (al-Isra’ 17:14). Muqatil: his limbs, al-Sharh 94:The Day their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do (al-Nur 24:24). Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: The witness is this nation, and the witnessed is all other nations, al-Sharh 94:And thus We have made you a just community that you will be witnesses over mankind (al-Baqarah 2:143). It was also said: The witness: the guardians, and the witnessed: the children of Adam. It was also said: the nights and the days. We have already explained it. I said: Money may testify against its owner, and the land may testify against what he did on it. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “This wealth is green and sweet, and the best companion of the Muslim is he who gives from it to the poor, the orphan, and the wayfarer - or something to that effect from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) - and whoever takes it unlawfully is like one who eats and is never satisfied, and it will be a witness against him on the Day of Resurrection.” In Tirmidhi, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited this verse: On that Day it will tell of its report [Al-Zalzalah 4] and said: Do you know what its report is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: ((Its report is that it will bear witness against every male and female slave regarding what they did on its back. It will say, ‘He did such and such on such and such a day.’ He said: So this is its report.)) He said: A good, strange, and authentic hadith. It was said: The witness is the creation. They testified to God the Almighty’s Oneness. The One to whom the testimony of Oneness is given is God the Almighty. It was said: The witnessed day is Friday, as Abu al-Darda’ narrated that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: (Increase your prayers upon me on Friday, for it is a witnessed day that the angels witness…) and he mentioned the hadith. It was narrated by Ibn Majah and others. I said: So, the Day of Arafah is witnessed, because the angels witness it and descend on it with mercy. And the same is true for the Day of Sacrifice, God willing. Abu Bakr Al-Attar said: The witness is the Black Stone, which testifies for whoever touches it with sincerity, devotion, and certainty. And the witnessed is the pilgrim. And it was said: The witness is the prophets, and the witnessed is Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Its explanation is: And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘What I have given you of the Book and wisdom’ - to His saying: And I am with you among the witnesses (Al Imran 3:81).
11:104: The Almighty said: And We do not delay it meaning We do not delay that day. Except for a predetermined term meaning for a term that Our judgment has already determined, and it is predetermined with Us. The Day that comes and it was read the Day that comes because the ya' is deleted if it is preceded by a kasra, as you say: I do not know, Al-Qushayri mentioned it. Al-Nahhas said: The people of Madinah, Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i read it with the ya' in the insertion, and deleting it in the pause, and it was narrated that Abi and Ibn Mas'ud read the Day that comes with the ya' in the pause and connection. Al-A'mash and Hamzah readيوم ياَقيwithout a ya' in both pause and connection. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: The correct view in this is that it should not be paused on, and that it should be connected with a ya', because a group of grammarians said: The ya' is not deleted, and something is not made jussive without a jussive. As for pausing without a ya', there is the opinion of al-Kisa'i, who said: Because a sound verb is paused on like a jussive verb, so the ya' was deleted, just as the damma is deleted. As for the reading of Hamzah, Abu Ubaid provided evidence for the deletion of the ya' in both pause and connection with two arguments. One of them is that he claimed that he saw it in the imam who said that it is the Mushaf of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, without a ya'. The other argument is that he narrated that it is the language of Hudhayl, they say: Ma adra. Al-Nahhas said: As for his argument with the Mushaf of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, it was said to me that it is gone. As for his argument with their saying:َا َمدمْم, there is no argument in it, because this deletion was narrated by the ancient grammarians, they mentioned its reason, and that it cannot be used as an analogy. Al-Farra recited the following verse about the deletion of the letter ya: Enough, a hand that does not befit a generous dirham and another that gives blood with the sword That is, to give. Sibawayh and Al-Khalil have narrated that the Arabs say: I do not know, and they delete the ya and make do with the kasra, except that they claim that this is due to frequent use. Al-Zajjaj said: The best thing in grammar is to prove the “ya. He said: What I see is following the Qur’an and the consensus of the reciters, because reading is a Sunnah, and something similar has occurred in the speech of the Arabs.
11:105: No soul shall speak except with His permission. The original is tatakallam, one of the two ta's was deleted for ease. It contains an implication, that is, no soul shall speak except with the permitted good speech, because they are forced to leave the ugly. It was said: The meaning is: Do not speak with an argument or intercession except with His permission. It was said: They have a time in the gathering when they are prevented from speaking except with His permission. This verse is the one that the people of heresy in religion ask about the most. They say: Why did He say: No soul shall speak except with His permission and This is a Day when they will not speak, nor will they be permitted to make excuses (al-Mursalat 77:35-36)? And He said in a place when mentioning the al-Qiyamah 75:And some of them will turn to others, questioning each other (al-Saffat 37:27). And He said: On the Day when every soul will come, pleading for itself (al-Nahl 16:16). And He said: Stop them, for they will be questioned (al-Saffat 37:24). And He said: On that Day, neither man nor jinn will be asked about his sin (al-Rahman 55:39). The answer is what we have mentioned, that they will not speak with an argument that is required of them, but rather they will speak by acknowledging their sins, blaming each other, and placing sins on each other. As for speaking and uttering an argument for them, then no. This is like saying to someone who speaks to you a lot, and his speech is empty of argument: I did not speak anything, and I did not utter anything. So the one who speaks without an argument for him is called a non-speaker. And some people said: That day is long, and it has places and situations in some of which they are prevented from speaking, and in some of which they are permitted to speak. This indicates that no soul speaks except with His permission. And among them are the wretched and the blessed meaning from among the souls, or from among the people, and He mentioned them in His statement: On a Day when all people will be gathered together. And the wretched is the one upon whom misery is decreed. And the blessed is the one upon whom happiness is decreed. Labid said: Some of them are happy and take their share, and some of them are miserable and content with life. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab who said: “When this verse was revealed: ‘Some of them are wretched and some are happy,’ I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Prophet of God, then what should we work on? On something that has already been completed, or on something that has not yet been completed? He said: Rather, on something that has already been completed and the pens have written about it, O Umar, but everyone is facilitated for what he was created for.” He said: This is a good and strange hadith from this source. We do not know it except from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, and it was mentioned previously in al-A’raf.
11:106: The Almighty said: But as for those who are wretched is the beginning. In the Fire is in the place of the report, and likewise for them therein is sighing and sobbing. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: Sighing is from the chest, and sobbing is from the throat, and the opposite is also reported from him. Al-Zajjaj said: Sighing is from intense groaning, and sobbing is from very loud groaning. He said: The linguists from Kufa and Basra claimed that sighing is like the beginning of the sound of donkeys in braying, and sobbing is like the end of the sound of a donkey in braying. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said the opposite, he said: Sighing is the intense sound, and sobbing is the weak sound. Ad-Dahhak and Muqatil said: Sighing is like the beginning of a donkey's braying, and sobbing is like the end of it when it finishes its sound. The poet said: He made a gasp in his stomach, or he gasped, until it was said that he brayed, but he did not bray. It was said: Zafar is the expulsion of the soul, which is when the stomach is filled with grief and it is expelled with the soul, and inhalation is the return of the soul. It was also said: Zafar is the repetition of the soul from the intensity of sadness, taken from zafar which is the load on the back due to its intensity, and inhalation is the long, extended breath, taken from their saying: a towering mountain, meaning tall. Zafar and inhalation are among the sounds of the sad.
11:107: The Almighty said: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure as long as they endure is in the accusative case as an adverb, meaning the permanence of the heavens and the earth, and the meaning is: the time of that. There is a difference of opinion in the interpretation of this, so a group of them, including Ad-Dahhak, said: The meaning is as long as the heavens of Paradise and Hell and their earth endure, and the sky is everything that is above you and shades you, and the earth is what your foot rests on. And in the revelation: And We have inherited the earth, that we may settle in Paradise wherever we will (al-Zumar 39:74). And it was said: He meant the heaven and earth that are known in this world, and this was done according to the custom of the Arabs in informing about the permanence of something and its confirmation, like their saying: I will not come to you as long as night falls, or a flood flows, and as long as night and day differ, and as long as the doves moan, and as long as the heavens and the earth endure, and the like of this, by which they mean a length without end, so God made them understand the permanence of the disbelievers with that. Even though He had informed of the disappearance of the heavens and the earth. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, that all created things originate from the light of the Throne, and that the heavens and the earth in the Hereafter will return to the light from which they were taken, so they will remain forever in the light of the Throne. The Almighty’s statement: Except what your Lord wills is in the accusative case, because it is an exception that is not from the first, and there are ten different opinions about it: The first: It is an exception from His statement: Then in the Fire, as if He said: Except what your Lord wills of delaying a people from that, and this is a statement narrated by Abu Nadrah on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri and Jabir, may God be pleased with them both. And He did not say whoever He wills, because what is meant is the number and not the people, like His statement: Whatever is good for you (An-Nisa’: 3). And on the authority of Abu Nadrah on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Except whom He wills that He not admit them, even though they are wretched in their disobedience. The second: The exception is only for the disobedient believers in taking them out of the Fire after a period, and based on this, His statement: As for those who are wretched is general for the disbelievers and disobedient, and the exception is from abiding eternally, as stated by Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Sinan and others. In the Sahih, from the hadith of Anas bin Malik, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: People will enter Hell until they become like hot coals, then they will be taken out of it and entered Paradise, and it will be said, ‘These are the people of Hell.’ This meaning has been mentioned previously in An-Nisa’ and elsewhere. Third: The exception is from the sighing and breathing in, meaning that they will have sighing and breathing in there, except for what your Lord wills of the types of torment that He did not mention. Likewise, for the people of Paradise, there is what was mentioned and what was not mentioned of bliss. Narrated by Ibn Al-Anbari. Fourth: Ibn Mas’ud said: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure they will not die in it, nor will they be taken out of it except what your Lord wills, which is that He will command the fire to consume them and annihilate them, then He will renew their creation. I said: This statement is specific to the infidel, and the exception is for him in eating and renewing creation. Fifth: That except means except as you say in speech: I have no man with me except Zaid, and I have a thousand upon you, return them except for the thousand that I have upon you. It was said: The meaning is as long as the heavens and the earth endure except for what your Lord wills of eternity. Sixth: It is an exception from expulsion, and He does not want to expel them from it. As you say in speech: I wanted to do that except that I willed something else, and you are continuing with that action, so the meaning is that if He wanted to expel them, He would have expelled them, but He has informed them that they will remain in it eternally. Al-Zajjaj mentioned these two sayings from the linguists, he said: And the people of meanings have two other sayings, one of the sayings: Eternal therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure except for what your Lord wills from the amount of their standing at the head of their graves, and for the accounting, and the amount of their stay in this world, and the intermediate realm, and standing for the accounting. The other saying: The exception occurs in the increase in bliss and torment, and its meaning is: Eternal therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure except for what your Lord wills from the increase in bliss for the people of bliss, and the increase in torment for the people of Hell. I said: The exception is in the increase in eternity over the duration of the heavens and the earth known in this world, and this was chosen by Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ali, meaning they will be eternal in it for the duration of the heavens and the earth, and that is the duration of the world, and the heavens and the earth have a time in which they will change, and that is the saying of the Most High: The Day the earth will be replaced by another earth (Ibrahim 14:48). So God the Most High created the humans and dealt with them, and bought from them their souls and their wealth in exchange for Paradise, and based on that He pledged to them on the Day of the Covenant, so whoever fulfilled that covenant will have Paradise, and whoever lost his neck will remain eternally in the Fire for the duration of the heavens and the earth, for they only lasted for the purpose of dealing, and likewise the people of Paradise will remain eternally in Paradise for the duration of that, so when this dealing is completed, everyone will fall into the will of God, God the Most High said: “And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play. We did not create them except in truth” (al-Dukhan 44:38-39). So the people of the two abodes will remain eternal for the duration of their duration for the truth of Oneness, so whoever meets Him as a monotheist for His Oneness will remain in his home forever, and whoever meets Him as a polytheist By His Oneness as a god who remained in prison forever, God informed the servants of the extent of eternity, then He said: except what your Lord wills of the increase in the period that the hearts are unable to comprehend because it has no end, so by belief their eternity in both worlds will last forever. It has been said: that except has the meaning of the letter waw, as Al-Farra’ and some of the people of insight said, and it is (the eighth - and the meaning: and what your Lord wills of the increase in eternity over the duration of the heavens and the earth in this world. It has been said in His Almighty’s saying: Except those who have wronged (al-Baqarah 2:150) meaning nor those who have wronged. And the poet said: Every brother who leaves his brother, by your father's life, except Al-Farqadhan That is, the two Farqand. Abu Muhammad Makki said: This is a far-fetched statement according to the Basrans that except has the meaning of and, and its explanation has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. It was said: Its meaning is as your Lord willed, like His Most High’s saying: And do not marry those women whom your fathers married, except what has already occurred (An-Nisa’: 22), meaning as has already occurred. And it is - the ninth, the tenth - that His Most High’s saying: Except what your Lord wills is only by way of an exception that the Shari’ah has encouraged its use in every speech, so it is like His Most High’s saying: You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in safety (al-Fath 48:27), so it is an exception in an obligation, and this exception is likewise in the ruling of a condition, as if he said: If your Lord wills, so it is not described as connected or disconnected, and it is supported and strengthened by His Most High’s saying: A gift uninterrupted and similarly from Abu Ubaid, who said: The determination of the will of God Almighty preceded in the eternity of the two groups in the two abodes, so the word of exception occurred, and the determination had preceded in eternity. He said: This is like His Most High’s saying: You shall surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in safety (al-Fath 48:27), and it is known that they will enter it inevitably, so He did not require the exception in The two places are an option, since the will has preceded the determination to remain eternally in both worlds and to enter the Sacred Mosque, and something similar from Al-Farra. And the eleventh statement is that the wretched are the happy, and the happy are the wretched, and no one else, and the exception in the two places refers to them, and its explanation is that what means whom God Almighty excepted from those who enter the Fire and remain eternally in it those who come out of it from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with what they have of faith, and He excepted from those who enter Paradise and remain eternally in it those who enter the Fire because of their sins before entering Paradise, then come out of it to Paradise. They are the ones upon whom the second exception falls, as if God Almighty said: But as for those who are wretched, they will be in the Fire for them therein sighing and sobbing, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. That He will not make them abide therein, and they are those who are expelled from it from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, through their faith and the intercession of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So by entering the Fire they are called the wretched, and by entering Paradise they are called the happy, as Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas when he said: Those who are happy were wretched by entering the Fire, then they were happy by exiting from it and entering Paradise.
11:108: Al-A'mash, Hafs, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i readوماَمدظنب دهوما with a damma on the seen. Abu Amr said: The evidence that it is sa'daw is that the first one is shaqaw and he did not say ashaqu. Al-Nahhas said: I saw Ali bin Sulayman expressing astonishment at Al-Kisa'i's readingس'ādaw despite his knowledge of Arabic! This was an incorrect reading, because it is only said: Sa'ad so-and-so and may God make him happy, and as'ad is like amrad. Al-Kisa'i only used as evidence their saying: Mas'ūd, but he has no evidence for it, because it is said: in place of Mas'ūd in it, then it is deleted and he is called by it. Al-Mahdawi said: And whoever uses a damma on the seen inس'ādaw is based on their saying: Mas'ūd, and this is anomalous and rare, because it is not said: May God make him happy, rather it is said: May God make him happy. Al-Tha'labi said: Sa'daw with a damma on the seen means they were granted happiness. It is said: Sa'd and As'ad have the same meaning. The rest read Sa'daw with a fatha on the seen by analogy with Shaqwa. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose this. Al-Jawhari said: Happiness is the opposite of misery. You say: From it, the man was happy with a kasra, so he is happy, like he was safe, so he is safe, and he was happy, so he is Mas'ud. It is not said about him: Mas'ud, as if they dispensed with it by Mas'ud. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahim said: It was reported: May God make him happy, so he is Mas'ud, and may God make him happy, so he is Mas'ud. This strengthens the statement of the Kufians. Sibawayh said: It is not said that someone was happy, just as it is not said that someone was miserable, because it is from the intransitive verbs. Ata' is not cut off meaning not severed, from Jadhah, meaning he cut it off. Al-Nabigha said: You find the double-weave Saluki and the fire of the humpbacks ignites with its sheets.
11:109: The Almighty's saying: So be not is a definite prohibition, and the letter nun was omitted due to frequent use. In doubt means in doubt. Of what these people worship of the gods that they are false. Better than this: that is, say, O Muhammad, to everyone who doubts do not be in doubt of what these people worship that God Almighty did not command them to do it, and they only worship them as their fathers used to do, imitating them. And We will surely give them their share, undiminished There are three opinions on this: The first: Their share of provision, said by Abu Al-Aaliyah. The second: Their share of punishment, said by Ibn Zayd. The third: What they were promised of good or evil, said by Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both.
11:110: The Almighty's saying: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord The word: that God the Almighty has decreed that He would delay them until the Day of Resurrection because He knew that there was goodness in that, and had it not been for that, their term would have been decided between them by rewarding the believer and punishing the disbeliever. It was said: What is meant is between those who differed regarding the Book of Moses, for they were between those who believed in it and those who denied it. And it was said: between these who differed regarding you, O Muhammad, by hastening the punishment, but the decree had preceded to delay the punishment for this nation until the Day of Resurrection. And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it If it is applied to the people of Moses, meaning they are in doubt about the Book of Moses, so they are in doubt about the Qur'an.
11:111: The Almighty said: "And indeed, each one of them will be fully repaid for their deeds. Indeed, He is Acquainted with what they do." That is, each of the nations that we have enumerated will see the reward for their deeds, and so will your people, O Muhammad. The reciters differed in the reading of and indeed, each one of them will see, so the people of the Two Sanctuaries - Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu Bakr with them - read and indeed, each one of them will see with a lightened in, on the basis that it is in the lightened from the heavy in and the one that is used. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh mentioned this. Sibawayh said: We were told by someone I trust that he heard the Arabs say: Indeed, Zaid is leaving, and he recited the words of the poet: As if a gazelle gives to the one who leaves the ladder He meant as if it were a gazelle, so he lightened the accusative of what came after it. The Basrans allow lightening the doubled in with their actions, and Al-Kisa’i denied that and said: I do not know on what basis and that both was read! Al-Farra’ claimed that he made both the accusative in the reading of those who lightened it by saying: li-yuwaifunhum, meaning that they will make them both, and all the grammarians denied that and said: This is a big mistake, no one allows Zayd to strike him. The rest stressed in and made both the accusative with it according to its origin. Asim, Hamza, and Ibn ‘Amir read lama with the emphasis. The rest lightened it with the meaning: and that both of them will make them both, they made ma a connection. It was said: It entered to separate between the two lams that receive the oath, and both of them are open, so he separated them with -ma. Al-Zajjaj said: The lam of l-ma is the lam of in and ma is redundant and emphatic. You say: Indeed, Zaid is departing. If requires that a lam be added to its predicate or its subject, as in your saying: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, and His statement: Indeed, in that is a reminder (al-Zumar 39:21). The lam in li-yuwaifinhum is that with which an oath is received, and it is added to the verb and the double or light nun is required for it. When the two lams come together, they are separated by -ma and ma is redundant and emphatic. Al-Farra’ said: ma has the meaning of min as in His statement: And indeed, among you are those who are slow to fulfill (An-Nisa’: 72), meaning, indeed, each of them will fulfill their promise. The lam in li-yuwaifinhum is for an oath, and this meaning goes back to what Al-Zajjaj said, except that ma according to Al-Zajjaj is redundant and according to Al-Farra’ a noun meaning min. It was said: It is not redundant, but rather it is a noun that has a lam of emphasis added to it, and it is the predicate of in and li-yuwaifinhum is the answer to the oath, the meaning is: And indeed each one was created for your Lord to pay them their deeds. And it was said: ma has the meaning of min like His saying: Then marry such women as seem good to you (An-Nisa’: 3), meaning of, and all of this is the same saying of Al-Farra’. As for the one who stressed lama and read wa-in kula-lama with the stress in both of them - and he is Hamza and those who agreed with him - it was said: It is a mistake. It was narrated from Muhammad bin Yazid that this is not permissible, and it is not said: Indeed Zaid except for I will strike him, nor for me for I will strike him. Al-Kisa’i said: God knows best about this reading, and I do not know its face. He and Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: The stress in both of them is problematic. Al-Nahhas and others said: The grammarians have different opinions on this matter: The first: Its origin is li-man ma, then the nun accepted a mim, and three mims came together, so the middle one was deleted, so lama and ma became, according to this opinion, with the meaning of min, the estimate being: And indeed both of them are for those who, like their saying: When I issued the order to him, he was exhausted by the path of its sources. Al-Zajjaj falsified this statement and said:َنis a noun with two letters, so it is not permissible to delete it. The second is that the original form ofلَنisَا, so the broken meem was deleted because of the meeting of the meems, and the meaning is: And indeed, each one of them is created to pay them in full. It was said:لمis a source ofلمand it came without a tanween to carry the connection to the pause, so on this it is like his saying: And you consume the inheritance, devouring what (al-Fajr 89:19), meaning collecting the eaten money, so the meaning on this is: And indeed, each one of them, your Lord will pay them in full for their deeds, a fulfillment of what, meaning gathering their deeds together, so it is like your saying:َقيَان لقوَن. Al-Zuhri readلمwith emphasis and a tanween for this meaning. Third: That lama means illa. The linguists have said: I ask you by God for what you did, meaning except for what you did. Similar to this is the saying of the Most High: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it (Al-Tariq: 4), meaning except for it. So the meaning of the verse is: There is no one of them except that He will fulfill their obligation. Al-Qushayri said: Al-Zajjaj refuted this statement by saying: And indeed, both of them are not so that illa can be estimated and it is not said: The people went when Zaid was given. Fourth: Abu Uthman Al-Mazini said: The original is And indeed, both of them are not with a light lama then it was made heavy like his saying. I was afraid that we would see a drought in our year after it was so fertile. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: This is a mistake! The heavy word is only made light, and the light word is not made heavy. Fifth: Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam said: It is possible that the emphasis is from their saying: I gathered the thing, I gathered it, then from it the word fa’la is built, as it was read Then We sent Our messengers one after the other (al-Mu’minun 23:44) without a tanween and with a tanween. The alif in this case is for feminization, and it is inclined to this statement of the proponents of inclination. Abu Ishaq said: The statement that is not permissible other than me is that it is lightened from the heavy, and it has the meaning of ma like: Indeed, every soul has a guardian over it (Al-Tariq: 4). And also it is stressed in its original form, and it has the meaning of ma and lama has the meaning of illa. This was narrated by Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, and all the Basrans. And that lama is used in the meaning of illa. I said: This is the statement that Al-Zajjaj approved, Al-Nahhas and others narrated it from him, and something similar to it and Al-Zajjaj weakened it, except that the correct statement is in in it as a negative, and here it is lightened from the heavy, so they differed and two readings remained. Abu Hatim said: And in the letter of Abu: And in every soul there is a guardian over it and it was narrated from Al-A’mash And in every soul there is a guardian over it with lama lightened and lama raised. Al-Nahhas said: These readings that are contrary to the generality have in in the meaning of ma and nothing else, and they are for interpretation, because it is not permissible to read with what is contrary to the generality except in this manner. Indeed, He is All-Aware of what they do is a threat and a warning.
11:112: The Almighty's saying: So stand firm as you have been commanded. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to others. It was said: to him, and what is meant is his nation, as al-Suddi said. It was also said: stand firm seek to remain on the religion from God and ask Him for that. So the seen is the seen of the question, as you say: I seek forgiveness from God, I ask forgiveness from Him. And steadfastness is continuing in one direction without taking to the right or the left, so stand firm in obeying God's command. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Abdullah al-Thaqafi, he said: I said, O Messenger of God, tell me something about Islam that I will not ask anyone about after you! He said: Say, I believe in God, then stand firm. Al-Darimi Abu Muhammad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Uthman ibn Hadir al-Azdi, he said: I entered upon Ibn Abbas and said, Advise me! He said: Yes! You must fear God and be steadfast, follow and do not innovate. And those who repent with you meaning, stand firm, you and they, meaning his companions who repented from polytheism and those who followed him from his nation after him. Ibn Abbas said: No verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that was more difficult or harsher than this verse. That is why he said to his companions when they said to him: Your hair has turned gray quickly! He said: Hud and its sisters have turned my hair gray. This was mentioned earlier in the surah. “It was narrated on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami who said: I heard Abu Ali al-Sarri say: I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a dream and I said: O Messenger of God! It was narrated on the authority of you that you said: Hud has turned my hair gray. He said: Yes. I said to him: What has turned your hair gray from it? Stories of the prophets and the destruction of nations! He said: No, but His statement: So stand firm as you have been commanded. “And do not transgress” is a prohibition against transgression and exceeding the limit. From this is: When the water overflows (al-Haqqah 69:11). It was said: That is, do not act tyrannically towards anyone.
11:113: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And do not incline. Inclination is the true meaning of relying, trusting, and being content with something and being satisfied with it. Qatada said: Its meaning is do not love them or obey them. Ibn Jurayj: Do not incline toward them. Abu Al-Aaliyah: Do not be satisfied with their actions, and all of them are close. Ibn Zayd said: Inclination here means to belittle them, and that is not to denounce their disbelief. Second: The majority read: tarkanawa with the kaf open. Abu Amr said: It is the language of the people of Hijaz. Talha bin Masraf, Qatadah and others read: tarkanawa with the kaf closed. Al-Farra’ said: It is the language of Tamim and Qais. Some people permitted rakna yarkan like mana’ yanma’. Third: The Almighty’s saying: To those who have wronged. It was said: The polytheists. It was said: It is general for them and for the disobedient, similar to the Almighty’s saying: And when you see those who engage in discourse about Our verses (al-An’am 6:68) and the verse. It was mentioned earlier. This is the correct meaning of the verse, and that it indicates abandoning the people of disbelief and disobedience from the people of innovations and others, because their company is disbelief or disobedience, since company is only based on love. A wise man said: Do not ask about a person, but ask about his companion, for every companion follows the example of his companion. If the companionship is out of necessity and taqiyya, then the discussion of this has already been mentioned in Al Imran and Al Ma’idah. And the companionship of the oppressor out of taqiyya is an exception to the prohibition in the case of necessity. And God knows best. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Then the Fire will touch you, meaning it will burn you, by mixing with them, keeping company with them, and conspiring with them in their disobedience and agreeing with them in their affairs.
11:114: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day. None of the people of interpretation differed that the prayer in this verse refers to the obligatory prayers, and He mentioned it specifically because it is the second part of faith, and to it one turns in times of calamity. Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distressed by a matter, he would turn to prayer. The Sufi sheikhs said: What is meant by this verse is the utilization of time in worship, obligatory and voluntary. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is weak, because the command did not include that except as obligatory, not voluntary. The litanies are known, and the times of the voluntary acts that are encouraged are limited, and other times are extended to the encouragement as a substitute, not as a generality, and that is not within the power of a human being. Second: The Almighty’s saying, The two ends of the day. Mujahid said, The first end is the dawn prayer, and the second end is the noon and afternoon prayers. Ibn Atiyyah chose this. It was also said, The two ends are the dawn and sunset. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan. Al-Hasan also said, The second end is the afternoon prayer alone. This was said by Qatada and Ad-Dahhak. It was also said, The two ends are the noon and afternoon prayers. The two ends are the sunset, the evening, and the dawn. It is as if this speaker took into consideration the loudness of the recitation. Al-Mawardi narrated that the first end is the dawn prayer by consensus. I said: This agreement is lacking in the previous statement. Al-Tabari preferred that the two ends are Fajr and Maghrib, and that is apparent. Ibn Atiyyah said: It was responded to him that Maghrib is not included in it because it is part of the night prayer. Ibn al-Arabi said: It is strange that al-Tabari sees that the two ends of the day are Fajr and Maghrib, and they are the two ends of the night! So he turned the bow into a ruku’ and deviated from the Burjas into a ghalwa. Al-Tabari said: The evidence for this is the consensus of all that one of the two ends is Fajr, which indicates that the other end is Maghrib, and no one agreed with him on that. I said: This is an exaggeration from Ibn al-Arabi in his response, and no one agreed with him on that. We mentioned from Mujahid that the first party is the dawn prayer, and it was agreed upon - except for those who deviated - that whoever eats or has intercourse after dawn intentionally, that his day is a day of breaking the fast, and he must make up for it and make expiation. And that is only what comes after dawn during the day, so it indicates the correctness of what al-Tabari said about the dawn, and what remains for him is the sunset prayer, and the response to him is what was mentioned above. And God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And in the vicinity of the night meaning in the vicinity of the night. Az-Zulf is the hours that are close to each other, and from this Muzdalifah was named, because it is a place after Arafat near Mecca. Ibn Al-Qa’qa’, Ibn Abi Ishaq and others read and Zulf with a damma on the lam, the plural of zaleef, because it was pronounced as zaleef, and it is possible that its singular is Zalfah in a language, like Basra and Bisr, in a language of those who have a damma on the seen. Ibn Muhaysin read and Zulfan of the night with a sukoon on the lam, and the singular is Zalfah, which gathers the plural of the types that are individuals, such as Durrah and Durrah, and Wool and Wool. Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin also read Zulf like Qurba. The rest read and Zulf with a fatha on the lam, like Ghurfah and Ghurfah. Ibn Al-A’rabi said: Az-Zulf is the hours, and its singular is Zalfah. Some people said: Az-Zulfah is the first hour of the night after sunset, so based on this, what is meant by Az-Zulf Al-Layl is the Isha prayer, as Ibn Abbas said. Al-Hasan said: Maghrib and Isha. It was said: Maghrib and Isha are the morning prayers, and it was mentioned before. Al-Akhfash said: He means the night prayer, but he did not specify. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. The majority of interpreters from the Companions and Followers, may God be pleased with them all, said that the good deeds here are the five daily prayers. Mujahid said: The good deeds are a man saying: Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, and God is Greatest. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is an example of good deeds, and what appears is that the wording is general for good deeds and specific for misdeeds, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: As long as you avoid major sins. I said: The reason for revelation supports the majority’s statement. It was revealed about a man from the Ansar. It was said: He was Abu Al-Yusr bin Amr. It was said: His name was Ibad. He was alone with a woman, kissed her, and enjoyed herself with her except for intercourse. "At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah who said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I have been intimate with a woman at the far end of the city and I have had intercourse with her without touching her, so I am here, so decide in what you wish. Umar said to him: God has covered you! If only you had covered yourself, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not answer him at all. The man went away and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, followed him with a man and called him. He recited to him: “Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.” to the end of the verse. A man from the people said: Is this specific to him? He said: No, rather it is for all people. At-Tirmidhi said: A good and authentic hadith. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud that a man kissed a woman in an unlawful manner, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about her expiation, so the following was revealed: “Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds.” The man said: Is this for me, O Messenger of God? He said: For you and for those of my nation who do it.” At-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and authentic hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Abu al-Yusr that he said: A woman came to me to buy dates, so I said: There are dates in the house that are better than these. So she entered the house with me, so I was drawn to her and kissed her. Then I went to Abu Bakr and mentioned that to him, and he said: Conceal it for yourself and repent and do not tell anyone. But I could not be patient. Then I went to Umar and mentioned that to him, and he said: Conceal it for yourself and repent and do not tell anyone. But I could not be patient. Then I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that to him, and he said: You left behind a fighter in the way of God in his family with something like this. He wished that he had not converted to Islam until that moment, until he thought that he was one of the people of Hell. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lowered his head until God revealed to him: Establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember. Abu al-Yusr said: So I went to him and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited it to me, and his companions said: O Messenger of God! Is it for this specifically or for all people? He said: Rather, it is for all people. Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a good and strange hadith, and Qays ibn al-Rabi’ declared it weak. And Wakee’ and others, and “it was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him, and the ‘Asr prayer was established. When he finished, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down to him with the verse and called him and said to him: Did you witness the prayer with us? He said: Yes. He said: Go, for it is an expiation for what you did.” And “it was narrated that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse to him, he said to him: Get up and pray four rak’ahs.” And God knows best. And Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim included in Nawader Al-Usul a hadith from Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “I have not seen anything better sought or faster attained than a new good deed for an old sin, ‘Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.’” Fifth: The verse and these hadiths indicate that there is no punishment for a forbidden kiss or forbidden touch. It may be used as evidence that there is no punishment or discipline for a man and a woman even if they are found wearing the same garment. This is the choice of Ibn al-Mundhir, because when he mentioned the scholars’ disagreement on this issue, he mentioned this hadith indicating that nothing is required of them. What the scholars have to say about this will come in Noor, God willing. Sixth: God the Almighty mentioned in His Book the prayer with its bowing, prostration, standing, recitation and its names. He said: Establish prayer (al-Isra’ 17:78). He said: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun (al-Isra’ 17:78). He said: “So glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning. To Him is praise in the heavens and the earth, and in the afternoon and when you reach the noon” (Al-Rum: 17-18). He said: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting (Ta-Ha 20:130). He said: Bow and prostrate (al-Hajj 22:77). He said: And stand before God, devoutly obedient (al-Baqarah 2:238). He said: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent (al-A’raf 7:204) based on what was mentioned above. And He said: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice (al-Isra’ 17:110), meaning in your recitation. All of this is a summary that He summarized in His Book, and He referred to His Prophet in His explanation, so He, the Most High, said: And We have sent down to you the message that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them (al-Nahl 16:44). So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained the times of prayer, the number of rak’ahs and prostrations, the description of all prayers, their obligations and Sunnahs, and what the prayer is not valid without from the obligations and what is recommended in it from Sunnahs and virtues. So he said in Sahih Al-Bukhari: Pray as you have seen me pray. And everyone transmitted this from him from everyone, as is well known, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die until he explained everything that the people needed, so the religion was completed and the path was made clear. God, the Most High, said: This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion (al-Ma’idah 5:3). The Almighty says: That is a reminder for those who remember. That is, the Qur’an is an admonition and repentance for those who take heed and remember. He specifically mentioned those who remember because they are the ones who benefit from the reminder. Remembrance is a verbal noun that begins with the feminine alif.
11:115: The Almighty said: And be patient meaning with the prayer, as He said: And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant therein (Ta-Ha 20:132). It was said: The meaning is: Be patient, O Muhammad, with whatever harm you encounter. For God does not allow to be lost the reward of those who do good meaning those who pray.
11:116: The Almighty says: Then why were there not meaning why were there not. Of the generations before you meaning of the nations before you. Of those who had remnants meaning people of obedience, religion, reason and insight. Forbidding their people from corruption on the earth because God Almighty gave them reason and showed them signs, and this is a rebuke to the disbelievers. It was said: Why were there not here is for negation, meaning what was before you, like His statement: Then why was there not a city that believed (Yunus 10:98), meaning it was not. Except a few is an intermittent exception, meaning but a few. Of those We saved from them they forbade corruption on the earth. It was said: They are the people of Yunus, because of His statement: Except the people of Yunus (Yunus 10:98). It was also said: They are the followers of the prophets and the people of truth. And those who did wrong followed meaning they associated partners with God and disobeyed. They indulged in luxury meaning, being preoccupied with money and pleasures, and preferring that over the Hereafter. And they were criminals.
11:117: God the Almighty says: And your Lord would not destroy the cities meaning the people of the cities. With injustice meaning with polytheism and disbelief. And their people were righteous meaning with regard to their dealings with rights, meaning He would not destroy them with disbelief alone until corruption was added to it, as He destroyed the people of Shu'ayb for cheating in measure and weight, and the people of Lot for sodomy. This indicates that sins are closer to the punishment of extermination in this world than polytheism, even though the punishment of polytheism in the Hereafter is more severe. In Sahih Al-Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him, he said: If people see an oppressor and do not stop him, God will soon afflict them with a punishment from Himself. This has been mentioned previously. It has been said that the meaning is: And your Lord would not destroy the cities with injustice while their people were Muslims, for that would be injustice to them and a deficiency in their rights, meaning He would not destroy a people except after giving them an excuse and warning. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that the meaning is that your Lord would not destroy anyone while he was wronging him, even if he was the ultimate in righteousness, because He is disposing of His kingdom, and the evidence for that is His statement: Indeed, God does not wrong the people at all (Yunus 10:4). It was said: The meaning is that God would not destroy them for their sins while they were righteous, meaning sincere in their faith. So injustice is sins according to this.
11:118: The Almighty said: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made mankind one community. Saeed bin Jubair said: On the religion of Islam alone. Ad-Dahhak said: People of one religion, people of misguidance or people of guidance. And they will not cease to differ meaning on different religions, as Mujahid and Qatadah said.
11:119: Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy is an interrupted exception, meaning for those upon whom your Lord has mercy, through faith and guidance, they do not differ. It was said: They differ in provision, this one is rich and this one is poor. Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy through contentment, said Al-Hasan. And for that He created them said Al-Hasan, Muqatil, Ata' and Yaman: The reference is to the difference, meaning for that He created them. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said: And for His mercy He created them, and He only said: and for that and did not say: and for that, and mercy is feminine because it is a source, and also the femininity of mercy is not real, so it was carried to mean grace.
