It was said: The reference to this is to difference and mercy, and that may refer to two opposite things, like the Almighty’s saying: Neither a fattened male nor a virgin, between those two (Ar-Raqra: 68) and He did not say between those two or those two, and He said: And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly, but are between those two moderate (al-Furqan 25:67) and He said: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice therein, but seek a way between those (al-Isra’ 17:110) and likewise His saying: Say, ‘In the bounty of God and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice’ (Yunus 10:58) and this is the best of the sayings, God willing, because it is general, that is, when He mentioned their creation, and to this Malik, may God have mercy on him, referred in what Ashhab narrated from him. Ashhab said: I asked Malik about this verse, and he said: He created them so that a group would be in Paradise and a group in the Blaze, that is, He created the people of difference for difference, and the people of mercy for mercy. It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: He created them into two groups, a group that He will have mercy on and a group that He will not have mercy on. Al-Mahdawi said: There is an inversion in the discussion of this estimation, the meaning is: And they will not cease to differ except for whom your Lord has mercy, and the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: I will fill Hell with jinn and people all together, and for that He created them. It was said: It is related to His statement: That is a Day when mankind will be gathered together, and that is a witnessed Day (Hud 11:103), and the meaning is: And to witness that Day He created them. It was said: It is related to His statement: And among them are the wretched and the happy, meaning He created them for happiness and wretchedness. The Almighty said: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled. The meaning of fulfilled is that it was established as He informed and decreed in His eternity. The perfection of a word is its inability to accept change and alteration. I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together. “Of” is to clarify the type, meaning from the type of jinn and the type of people. All together is to emphasize. Just as He informed that He will fill His Hell, so He informed on the tongue of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He will fill His Paradise by saying: And for each of you is her fill. Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, which was mentioned earlier.
11:120: The Almighty said: And We relate to you both both is in the accusative case with -نمصmeaning: And everything you need from the report of the messengers, We relate to you. Al-Akhfash said: Both is an introductory state, like you say: Both, I struck the people. From the report of the messengers meaning from their report and their patience with the harm of their people. That by which We strengthen your heart meaning in carrying out the message, and in being patient with the harm that befalls you in it. It was said: We increase your confirmation and certainty with it. Ibn Abbas said: That by which your heart is urged. Ibn Jurayj said: We make your heart patient so that you do not grieve. The scholars of meanings said: We are pleased, and the meaning is close: And ma is a substitute for both meaning: We relate to you from the report of the messengers that by which We strengthen your heart. And there has come to you in this truth meaning in this surah, according to Ibn Abbas, Abu Musa, and others. This surah was singled out because it contains report of the prophets, Paradise, and Hell. It was said: He mentioned it specifically for emphasis, even though the truth is in the entire Qur’an. Qatada and Al-Hasan said: The meaning is in this world, meaning prophethood. And an admonition and a reminder for the believers. The admonition is what is admonished by the destruction of past nations and the past generations that denied. This is an honor for this surah, because the truth, admonition, and reminder have come in other surahs, and He did not say in them what He said in this one specifically. And a reminder for the believers meaning they remember what happened to those who perished and repent. He specified the believers because they are the ones who are admonished when they hear the stories of the prophets.
11:121: The Almighty said: And say to those who do not believe, ‘Work according to your position.’ A threat and warning. Indeed, we are working.
11:122: And wait, for we are waiting. Another threat, the meaning of which has been mentioned previously.
11:123: The Almighty said: And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth meaning their unseen and their testimony, so it was deleted to indicate the meaning. Ibn Abbas said: The treasuries of the heavens and the earth. Ad-Dahhak said: Everything that is hidden from the servants in them. The rest said: The unseen of the heavens and the earth is the descent of punishment from the sky and its rise from the earth. Abu Ali Al-Farisi said: And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth meaning He knows what is hidden in them. He added the unseen, which is added to the object, as an extension, because he deleted the preposition. You say: I was hidden in the earth and I was hidden in such-and-such a country. And to Him will return the matter in its entirety meaning on the Day of Resurrection, since no creature has a command except by His permission. Nafi' and Hafs readيْجعwith a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the jim, meaning it will be returned. So worship Him and put your trust in Him meaning resort to Him and trust in Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do meaning He will reward each one according to his deeds. The people of Medina, Ash-Sham, and Hafs read it with a ta' for addressing. The rest read it with a ya' for the report. Al-Akhfash Saeed said: they work if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not address them. He said: some of them. And he said: you work with the ta’ because he addressed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Say to them and your Lord is not unaware of what you do. Ka’b al-Ahbar said: The conclusion of the Torah is the conclusion of Hud from His saying: And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth to the end of the surah. Surah Hud is completed and Surah Yusuf, peace be upon him, follows it.
12:1: It is all Meccan. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: Except for four verses of it. It was narrated that the Jews asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the story of Joseph, so the Surah was revealed, and it will come. And "Saad bin Abi Waqqas said: The Qur'an was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited it to them for a period of time, and they said: If you were to tell us a story, then it was revealed: "We narrate to you", so he recited it to them for a period of time, and they said: If you were to tell us, then it was revealed: "God has sent down the best statement" (al-Zumar 39:23)" The scholars said: God mentioned the stories of the prophets in the Qur'an and repeated them with one meaning in different ways, with different words according to the degrees of eloquence, and He mentioned the story of Joseph and did not repeat it, so no opponent was able to oppose what was repeated, nor to oppose what was not repeated, and the miracle is for those who contemplate. The Almighty’s saying: Alif, Lam, Ra. It was previously mentioned, and the meaning here is: These are the verses of the Book, as a subject and a predicate. It was said: Alif, Lam, Ra is the name of the surah, meaning this surah called Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book, meaning by the clear Book, that is, the one that clarifies its lawful and unlawful, its limits, its rulings, its guidance, and its blessings. It was said: That is, these are the verses that you were promised in the Torah.
12:2: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an. It is possible that the meaning is: We have sent down the Qur'an in Arabic. The accusative of Quran is in the state of being, meaning all together. And Arabic is an adjective for His saying Quran. It is also possible that it is an introduction to the state, as you say: I passed by Zaid, a righteous man, and Arabic is in the state of being, meaning he recites in your language, O Arabs. Express between, and from it: The married woman expresses herself. "Perhaps you will understand" means so that you may know its meanings and understand what is in it. And some Arabs use "an with perhaps as a likeness to asa." And the lam in perhaps is redundant for emphasis, as the poet said: Oh my father, may you always be well It was said: Perhaps you will understand meaning that you will be hopeful of contemplating it, so the meaning of doubt returns to them, not to the Book, nor to God Almighty. It was said: The meaning of We sent it down is that We sent down the report of Joseph. An-Nahhas said: This is more similar to the meaning, because it is narrated that the Jews said: Ask him why the family of Jacob moved from Ash-Sham to Egypt? And about the report of Joseph, so God Almighty sent this down in Mecca in agreement with what is in the Torah, and in it there is an addition that they do not have. So this was for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - since he informed them and he had never read a book nor was he in the place of a book - like the resurrection of the dead Jesus, peace be upon him, according to what will come in it.
12:3: The Almighty said: We relate to you subject and predicate. The best stories means the source, and the meaning is: We narrated the best stories. The origin of stories is to follow something, and from it the Almighty said: And she said to her sister, 'Follow him' (al-Qasas 28:11), meaning follow his traces, so the narrator follows the traces and tells them. And good refers to the stories, not the story. It is said: So-and-so is a good narrator of the hadith, meaning he is good at narrating it. It was said: Stories is not a source, but rather it is in the meaning of a noun, as it is said: God is our hope, meaning we are hoped for, so the meaning according to this is: We inform you of the best report. With what We have revealed to you meaning with Our revelation, so -ma with the verb is like a source. This Qur'an The Qur'an is in the accusative case as an attribute of this, or a substitute for it, or an explanatory apposition. Al-Farra' permitted the accusative, he said: on repetition, and according to the Basrans it is on the substitute for -ma. Abu Ishaq permitted the nominative case with an implied subject, as if someone asked him about the revelation and he was told: It is this Qur’an. And you were, before it, among the unaware, meaning among those unaware of what We have made you aware of. Question: Scholars differed as to why this Surah was called the best of stories among all the stories. It was said: Because there is no story in the Qur’an that includes as many lessons and wisdom as this story does, and this is explained by His statement at the end of it: Indeed in their stories is a lesson for those of understanding (Yusuf 12:111). It was also said: It was called the best of stories because of the beauty of Yusuf’s tolerance of his brothers, his patience with their harm, and his forgiveness of them - after meeting them - without mentioning what they did, and his generosity in forgiving them, until he said: No blame will there be upon you today (Yusuf 12:92). It was also said: Because it mentions the prophets, the righteous, the angels, the devils, the jinn, mankind, livestock, and birds, the biographies of kings and kingdoms, merchants, scholars, and ignorant people, men and women, their tricks and deceit, and it mentions monotheism, jurisprudence, biographies, dream interpretation, politics, social interaction, and managing one’s livelihood, and a number of benefits that are good for religion and the world. It was said: Because it mentions the beloved and the beloved and their lives. It was also said: best here means most amazing. Some of the scholars of meaning said: It was the best of stories because everyone mentioned in it ended up in happiness. Look at Joseph, his father, his brothers, and the wife of the Aziz. It was said: The king also converted to Islam through Joseph and his conversion was good, and the interpreter of dreams was the cupbearer, and the witness, as they say, so the matter of everyone was nothing but good.
12:4: The Almighty said: When Joseph said when is in the accusative case as an adverb, meaning, remind them when Joseph said. The general reading is with a damma on the seen. Talha bin Masraf read yu'saf with a hamza and a kasra on the seen. Abu Zaid narrated yu'saf with a hamza and a fatha on the seen. It was not declined because it is foreign, and it was said: it is Arabic. Abu al-Hasan al-Aqta' - and he was a wise man - was asked about Yusuf and he said: Sorrow in the language means sadness, and aseef means two slaves, and they have met in Yusuf, and that is why he was named Yusuf. To his father, O father with a kasra on the taa is the reading of Abu Amr, Asim, Nafi, Hamza and Al-Kisa'i. According to the Basrans, it is a sign of femininity introduced to father in the vocative case in particular instead of the yaa of addition. The sign of femininity may be introduced to the masculine, so it is said: a man of marriage and mockery. An-Nahhas said: If you say O father with a kasra on the taa, then the taa according to Sibawayh is a substitute for the yaa of addition, and according to his statement, stopping is not permissible except with the haa. He has evidence for his statement, including that your saying: O his father conveys the meaning of O my father, and that O father is not said except in the definite article, and it is not said: My father came to me, and the Arabs do not use this except in the vocative case in particular, and it is not said: O my father because the taa is a substitute for the yaa, so they cannot be combined. Al-Farra’ claimed that if he said: O my father with a kasra, it indicates the ya’ and nothing else, because the ya’ is in the intention. Abu Ishaq claimed that this is a mistake, and the truth is what he said. How can the ya’ be in the intention and not say: O my father?! Abu Ja’far, Al-A’raj, and Abdullah bin Aamer read O my father with a fatha on the ta’. The Basrans said: They meant O my father with a ya’, then the ya’ was replaced with an alif, so it became O my father, so the alif was deleted and the fatha remained on the ta’. It was said: The original is the kasra, then the kasra was replaced with a fatha, just as the ya’ is replaced with an alif, so it is said: O young man, come. Al-Farra’ permitted O my father with a damma on the ta’. Indeed I saw eleven stars There is no disagreement among grammarians that it is said: Eleven came to me, and I saw and passed by eleven, and likewise thirteen and nineteen and what is between them. They made the two names one name and parsed them with the lightest vowels. Al-Suhayli said: The names of these stars were mentioned with a chain of transmission, narrated by Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah said: “Bustanah - and he was a man of the People of the Book - came and asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the eleven stars that Joseph saw. He said: Al-Harith, Al-Tariq, Al-Dhiyal, Qabis, Al-Musabbih, Al-Dharuh, Dhu Al-Kanafat, Dhu Al-Qar’, Al-Faliq, Waththab, and Al-Amudan. Joseph, peace be upon him, saw them prostrating to him.” Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: The stars are his brothers, the sun is his mother, and the moon is his father. Qatadah also said: The sun is his maternal aunt, because his mother had died, and his maternal aunt was under his father. I saw them is an emphasis. He said: I saw them prostrating to me, so it came in the masculine form. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said that when he spoke about these things with obedience and prostration, which are actions of rational beings, he spoke about them as he spoke about someone with reason. This meaning was mentioned previously in His statement: And you will see them looking at you. (al-A’raf 7:198) The Arabs pluralize what is not rational with the plural of rational if they put it in its place, even if it is outside the original.
12:5: It contains eleven issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: So they will plot against you a plot, meaning they will conspire to destroy you, because its interpretation is clear, and perhaps Satan will lead them to intend evil for you at that time. The lam in laka is for emphasis, like His saying: If you interpret dreams (Yusuf 12:43). Second: The vision is a noble state and a high status. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: After me, there is nothing left of the good tidings except the righteous and true vision that a righteous man sees or that is seen for him. He also said: The most truthful of you in vision is the most truthful of you in speech. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ruled that it is a part of forty-six parts of prophecy. It was narrated: of seventy parts of prophecy. It was narrated from the hadeeth of Ibn ‘Abbaas may God be pleased with him a part of forty parts of prophecy. It was narrated from the hadeeth of Ibn ‘Amr a part of forty-nine parts. It was narrated from the hadeeth of al-‘Abbaas a part of fifty parts of prophecy. It was narrated from the hadeeth of Anas of twenty-six. On the authority of Ubadah ibn al-Samit: Of the forty-four of the prophethood. The correct one of them is the hadith of the forty-six, and the hadith of the seventy follows it in authenticity. Muslim did not include in his Sahih other than these two hadiths. As for the rest of them, they are from the hadiths of the sheikhs, as Ibn Battel said. Abu Abdullah al-Maziri said: The most common and most correct one according to the people of hadith is Of the forty-six. Al-Tabari said: The correct thing to say is that most of these hadiths, or most of them, are authentic, and each hadith has a reasonable explanation. As for his statement: It is a part of seventy parts of prophethood, then that is a general statement regarding every true and righteous vision, and for every Muslim who sees it in his sleep, regardless of his condition. As for his statement: It is from forty - or - forty-six, then he means by that whoever is in the condition that was mentioned about the friend - may God be pleased with him - that he was in. So whoever is one of those who perform ablution perfectly in the cold, and are patient for the sake of God in the face of the disliked, and wait for the prayer after the prayer, then his righteous vision - God willing - is a part of forty parts of prophethood. And whoever is in a state between that, then his true vision is between two parts, between forty and sixty, not less than seventy, and more than forty. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr referred to this meaning and said: The difference of the narrations in this chapter regarding the number of parts of the vision is not, in my opinion, a contradictory and conflicting difference - and God knows best - because it is possible that it is The righteous vision of some of those who see it depends on the truthfulness of their speech, the fulfillment of their trust, the firm religion, and the goodness of their certainty. So according to the degree of difference between people in what we have described, the vision of them will be in different parts in number. So whoever has sincere intentions in worshipping his Lord, his certainty, and the truthfulness of his speech, his vision will be more truthful, and closer to prophethood: just as the prophets are distinguished, God Almighty said: And We have certainly preferred some prophets over others (al-Isra’ 17:55). I said: This interpretation gathers the scattered hadiths, and it is better than interpreting some of them without others and rejecting them. Abu Saeed Al-Asfaqi mentioned it on the authority of some of the people of knowledge. He said: The meaning of his saying: A part of forty-six parts of prophethood is that God Almighty revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in prophethood for twenty-three years - according to what Ikrimah and Amr bin Dinar narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both - so if we attribute six months of twenty-three years, we find that it is a part of forty-six parts. Al-Maziri referred to this statement in his book Al-Mu’allim and Al-Ghaznawi chose it in his interpretation of Surah Yunus when God Almighty said: For them is good tidings in the life of this world (Yunus 10:64). It is invalid from two aspects: The first is what Abu Salamah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Aisha that the duration of revelation was twenty years, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent at the beginning of forty, and he stayed in Mecca for ten years. This is the statement of Urwah, Al-Sha’bi, Ibn Shihab, Al-Hasan, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, and Sa’id Ibn Al-Musayyab, with differences from him. It is the narration of Rabi’ah and Abu Ghalib on the authority of Anas. If this hadith is proven, this interpretation is invalidated. The second is that the rest of the hadiths in the different parts remain without meaning. Third: The vision is part of prophecy because it contains what is impossible and impossible, such as flying, changing things, and knowing something of the knowledge of the unseen, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: There remains of the good tidings of prophecy only the true vision in sleep hadith. In short, the true vision is from God, and it is from prophecy. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: The vision is from God and the dream is from Satan and believing in it is true, and it has a good interpretation, and some of it may suffice without interpretation, and it contains from the wonders of God and His kindness what increases the believer’s faith, and there is no disagreement on this among the people of religion and truth from the people of opinion and tradition, and no one denies the vision except the people of atheism and a group of the Mu’tazila. Fourth: If it is said: If a true vision is part of prophecy, then how can an unbeliever, a liar, or a confused person be worthy of it? Some of the infidels and others whose religion is not acceptable have had true and correct dreams, such as the dream of the king who saw seven cows, the dream of the two young men in prison, the dream of Nebuchadnezzar, which Daniel interpreted as the end of his kingdom, the dream of Khosrau about the appearance of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the dream of Atikah, the aunt of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about his affair, and she was an infidel. Al-Bukhari translated Chapter on the Dreams of the People of Prison - so the answer is that the dream of the infidel, the wicked, the immoral, and the liar, even if their dream is true at some times, is not from revelation or from prophecy, because not everyone who is truthful in a hadith about the unseen, his report of that is prophecy. It was mentioned in Al-An`am that the soothsayer and others may tell a word of truth and it is believed, but that is rare and few, so the same is the case with the dream of these people. Al-Muhallab said: Al-Bukhari translated this because it is possible for the dream of the polytheists to be a true dream, just as the dream of the two young men was true, except that it is not permissible for it to be added to prophecy. The believer’s vision of it, because not every vision that can be interpreted is truly part of prophecy. Fifth: The vision attributed to God the Most High is that which is free from illusions and delusions, and its interpretation is in accordance with what is in the Preserved Tablet, and that which is from the report of illusions is the dream, and it is attributed to Satan, and it is called a dream because it contains contradictory things, as Al-Muhallab said. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided the vision into sections that suffice for the words of every speaker. Awf bin Malik narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The vision is of three types: the terrors of Satan to grieve the son of Adam, and some of them are what he is concerned about while awake and sees in his sleep, and some of them are a part of forty-six parts of prophecy.” He said: I said: Did you hear this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: Yes! I heard it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Sixth: The Almighty said: He said, ‘O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers’ Al-Ma’idah 6:10. Vision is a verbal noun derived from the verb to see in a dream. Vision is of the form fa’la, like saqya and bushra, and its alif is for the feminine, which is why it is not declined. Scholars have differed about the reality of vision. It was said: It is a perception in parts that have not been affected by a defect, such as deep sleep and others. This is why visions are most often seen at the end of the night due to the lack of sleep, so God Almighty creates for the dreamer an emerging knowledge, and creates for him what he sees based on what he sees, so that perception is correct. Ibn al-Arabi said: He does not see in a dream except what is correct to perceive while awake. This is why he does not see in a dream a person standing or sitting in any case, but rather he sees the usual permissible things. It was said: God is an angel who displays the visible things to the place of perception of the sleeper, and represents to him tangible images. Sometimes those images are examples that correspond to what occurs in existence, and sometimes they are for rational, non-tangible meanings. In both cases, they are good report or warnings. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere: I saw a black woman with disheveled hair coming out of the city to a place of turmoil, so I interpreted it as fever. “I saw my sword with its chest cut off and cows being slaughtered, so I interpreted them as a man from my family being killed, and the cows as a group of my companions being killed.” I saw that I put my hand into a strong shield, so I interpreted it as the city. “I saw two bracelets on my hand, so I interpreted them as liars who would emerge after me.” And other examples have been given for which examples are given, some of which appear in meaning from time to time, and some of which do not appear except after contemplation. In the time of Joseph, peace be upon him, a sleeper saw cows, so he interpreted them as Joseph’s years. He saw eleven stars, the sun, and the moon, so he interpreted them as his brothers and parents. Seventh: If it is said: Joseph, peace be upon him, was young at the time of his vision, and the actions of a young person are not valid, so how could he have a vision that had validity so that his father would say to him: Do not relate your vision to your brothers? The answer is that the vision is a real perception based on what we have presented, so it is from a young person just as it is from him the real perception when awake, and if he tells what he saw, he is truthful, and likewise if he tells what he sees in a dream, and God Almighty has told about his vision and that it came to pass as he saw, so there is no objection. It was narrated that Joseph, peace be upon him, was twelve years old. Eighth: This verse is a principle that dreams should not be told to anyone who is not compassionate or sincere, nor to someone who is not good at interpreting them. Abu Razin Al-Uqayli narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A dream is one of forty parts of prophecy, and “A dream is suspended by a flying leg as long as its owner does not tell it to him. When he tells it to him, it will come true. So do not tell it to anyone except a wise person, a lover, or a sincere advisor.” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, who said: A good and authentic hadith. Abu Razin’s name is Laqeet bin Amir. It was said to Malik: Does anyone interpret dreams? He said: Is prophecy a game? Malik said: Only those who are good at it can interpret dreams. If they see something good, they will tell us about it, and if they see something bad, they should say something good or remain silent. It was said: Can a person interpret a dream as good even though it is bad according to the opinion of those who say that it is as they interpret it? He said: No! Then he said: A dream is a part of prophecy, so prophecy should not be toyed with. Ninth: This verse is evidence that it is permissible for a Muslim to warn his Muslim brother of someone he fears will harm him, and it is not included in the meaning of backbiting, because Jacob, peace be upon him, warned Joseph not to tell his brothers about his dream, lest they plot against him. It also indicates the permissibility of not showing favors to someone whose evil is feared out of envy and plotting. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Seek help in achieving your needs by keeping them secret, for every person who has a blessing is envied. It also contains clear evidence that Jacob, peace be upon him, knew the interpretation of dreams, as he knew from its interpretation that they would be exposed to them, and he did not care about that for himself, because a man would like his son to be better than him, but a brother would not like that for his brother. It also indicates that Jacob, peace be upon him, felt more envy and hatred for Joseph than his sons, so he forbade him from telling them visions for fear that this would make their hearts bridle at that time. It was mentioned in the book of al-Tabari by Ibn Zayd that they were prophets, and this is refuted by the certainty of the infallibility of prophets from worldly envy, disobedience to parents, exposing a believer to destruction, and conspiring to kill him. No attention should be paid to the statement of those who said that they were prophets, and it is not impossible in reason for a prophet to slip, except that this slip combined types of major sins, and the Muslims agreed on their infallibility from them, but they differed only on minor sins as mentioned above and what will come. Tenth: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Nothing remains of prophecy except the good tidings. They said: What are the good tidings? He said: The righteous vision. This hadith, on its face, indicates that the vision is good tidings in general, but that is not the case. Rather, the true vision may be a warning from God the Almighty that does not please the one who sees it. Rather, God the Almighty shows it to the believer as kindness and mercy, so that he may prepare for the calamity before it occurs. If he realizes it, he interprets it himself, otherwise he asks someone who is qualified to do so. Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, saw a vision of Ahmad ibn Hanbal while he was in Egypt that indicated his ordeal, so he wrote to him about it so that he may prepare for it. It was mentioned previously in Yunus in the interpretation of the words of God the Almighty: For them is good tidings in the life of this world (Yunus 10:64) that it is the righteous vision. This and the hadith of Al-Bukhari are most likely transmitted, and God knows best. Eleventh: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Salamah who said: “I used to see a dream that would make me sick until I heard Abu Qatada say: And I used to see a dream that would make me sick until I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: ‘A good dream is from God. So if one of you sees something he likes, let him not tell it to anyone except the one he loves. And if he sees something he dislikes, let him seek refuge with God from its evil and spit three times and let him not tell it to anyone, for it will not harm him.’” Our scholars said: So God made seeking refuge with it one of the things that removes its harm. Do you not see the statement of Abu Qatada: ‘I used to see a dream that was heavier on me than a mountain, but when I heard this hadith, I did not consider it anything.’ Muslim added from the narration of Jabir on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: ‘If one of you sees a dream that he dislikes, let him spit to his left three times and seek refuge with God from Satan three times and turn over from the side he was on.’” And in the hadith of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said: ‘If one of you sees something he dislikes, let him stand up and pray.’” Our scholars said: All of this is not contradictory, but rather this command to turn and pray is an addition, so the dreamer must do all of them, and standing up for prayer includes all of them, because if he prays, his action for prayer includes all of those matters, because if he stands up for prayer, he turns on his side, and if he rinses his mouth, he spits and spit, and if he stands up for prayer, he seeks refuge and supplicates and beseeches God Almighty to spare him its evil in a state that is the closest state to being answered, and that is the magic of the night.
12:6: The Almighty said: And thus will your Lord choose you. The Kaf is in the accusative case, because it is an adjective for a deleted source, and so is the Kaf in His statement: As He completed it for your parents before. And ma is a genitive. It was said: And thus meaning just as He honored you with the vision, so will He choose you, and be good to you by fulfilling the vision. Muqatil said: By prostrating to you. Al-Hasan: By prophecy. And choosing is choosing the most important matters for the chosen one, and its origin is from the word jabayt meaning to obtain it, and from it the word jabayt the water in the basin, said Al-Nahhas. This is the praise of God Almighty for Joseph, peace be upon him, and an enumeration of what He enumerated for him of the blessings that God Almighty gave him, from empowerment in the land, and teaching the interpretation of hadiths, and they agreed that this was in the interpretation of the vision. Abdullah bin Shaddad bin Al-Haad said: The interpretation of Joseph's vision, peace be upon him, was after forty years, and that was the end of the vision. By hadiths he meant what people see in their dreams, and it is a miracle for him, as he did not make a mistake in it. Joseph, peace be upon him, was the most knowledgeable person about its interpretation, and our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was similar to that, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, was one of the most knowledgeable people about it, and Ibn Sirin achieved great progress, nature and goodness in it, and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab was similar or close to him, according to what they mentioned. It has been said in the interpretation of his statement: And teaches you the interpretation of hadiths meaning the hadiths of nations and books and evidence of monotheism, so it is a reference to prophethood, and that is what is meant by his statement: And completes His favor upon you meaning with prophethood. It has been said: By bringing your brothers to you, and it has been said: By saving you from every harm. As He completed it upon your fathers before Abraham with friendship, and saving him from the fire. And Isaac with prophethood. It has been said: From the slaughter, said by Ikrimah. And God Almighty informed him with his statement: And upon the family of Jacob that He would give prophethood to all the children of Jacob, said a group of commentators. Your Lord is All-Knowing of what He gives you. Wise in what He does to you.
12:7: The Almighty said: There were certainly in Joseph and his brothers signs for those who ask meaning whoever asks about their story. The people of Mecca read sign in the singular, and Abu Ubaid chose signs in the plural, he said: because it is a great good. An-Nahhas said: And sign here is a good reading, meaning there was certainly a sign for those who asked about the story of Joseph in what they were told, because they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Mecca and said: Tell us about a man from the prophets who was in Ash-Sham who sent his son to Egypt, and he cried over him until he went blind? - and there was no one from the People of the Book in Mecca, nor anyone who knew the story of the prophets, but the Jews from Medina were directed to them to ask him about this - so God Almighty revealed Surah Joseph in one sentence, in which there is everything in the Torah of report and more, so it was a sign for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, like the revival of the dead Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. Signs is a sermon, and it was said: a lesson. It was narrated that in some copies of the Qur’an it is a lesson. It was said: Insight. It was also said: Wonder, you say so-and-so is a sign of knowledge and beauty, meaning wonder. Al-Tha'labi said in his interpretation: When the vision reached Joseph's brothers, they envied him. Ibn Zayd said: They were prophets, and they said: He is not pleased for his brothers to prostrate to him until his parents prostrate to him! So they sought enmity towards him, and the refutation of this statement has been presented. God Almighty said: There was certainly concerning Joseph and his brothers and their names were: Reuben, who was the eldest of them, and Simeon, Levi, Judah, Zealon, and Ishgar, and their mother was Leah, daughter of Layan, and she was the daughter of Jacob's maternal uncle, and he had four sons from two concubines: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. Then Leah died, and Jacob married her sister Rachel, and she bore him Joseph and Benjamin, and Jacob's sons were twelve men. Al-Suhayli said: Jacob's mother's name was Rebecca, and Rachel died while giving birth to Benjamin, and Layan, son of Naher, son of Azar, is Jacob's maternal uncle. It was said: In the names of the two slave girls, Leah and Talta, one of them belonged to Rachel, and the other to her sister Leah, and they had been given to Jacob as a gift, and Jacob had brought them together, and it was not permissible for anyone after him, because God Almighty said: And that you should bring two sisters together, except for what has already occurred. (An-Nisa’: 23). The response to what Ibn Zayd said has already been presented, and praise be to God.
12:8: The Almighty said: When they said to Joseph Joseph is raised by the beginning, and the lam is for emphasis, and it is the one with which the oath is received, meaning, by God, for Joseph. And his brother is in apposition to it. Better to our father than us is its predicate, and it is not dual or plural because it means a verb, and they only said this because the report of the dream reached them, so they conspired to plot against him. And we are a group meaning a group, and they were ten. A group is between one and ten, and it was said: to fifteen. It was said: between forty and ten, and it does not have a singular from its wording like a group and a group. Indeed, our father is in manifest error They did not mean the error of religion, because if they had meant that, they would have been disbelievers, but they meant that he was in a deviation from the path of management, in preferring two over ten while being equal in their affiliation to him. It was said: in a clear error in his preferring Joseph and his brother over us.
12:9: The Almighty said: Kill Joseph There is an omission in the speech, meaning one of them said: Kill Joseph to make the matter more decisive. Or throw him into the ground meaning into the ground, so the preposition was dropped and the ground was made in the accusative case. Sibawayh recited what was omitted from it in: When he shakes his hand, his back becomes honeyed, just as the fox swallows honey on the road. An-Nahhas said: However, there is much good in the verse, because it takes two objects, one of them with a preposition, so if you delete the preposition the verb takes it. It was said that the speaker is Shimon, as Wahb ibn Munabbih said. Kaab al-Ahbar said: Dan. Muqatil said: Reuben, and God knows best. The meaning is a land far from his father, so this omission is necessary because he was with his father in a land. Yakhal is in the subjunctive mood because it is the answer to the command, meaning: he is purified and clear. For you is the face of your father so he turns to you completely. And you will be after him meaning after the sin, and it was said: after Joseph. A righteous people meaning repentant, meaning speak of repentance after that and God will accept it from you, and in this is evidence that the repentance of the killer is acceptable, because God Almighty did not deny this statement from them. It was said: Righteous meaning your affairs will be put right with your father without favoritism or preference.
12:10: It contains thirteen issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: A speaker among them said The speaker was Judah, the eldest son of Jacob, as Ibn Abbas said. It was also said: Reuben, his maternal cousin, and he is the one who said: I will never leave the land the verse. It was also said: Simeon. And they cast him into the bottom of the well The people of Mecca, Basra, and Kufa read in the bottom of the well. The people of Medina read in the depths of the well. Abu Ubaid chose the singular, because it is in one place where they threw him, and he denied the plural for this reason. An-Nahhas said: This is a restriction in the language, and depths in the plural is permissible from two aspects: Sibawayh narrated that he walked on it in the evenings and in the evenings, meaning in the evening and in the evening, so he made each time of it an evening and an evening, and thus he made each place of what is hidden its absence. The other - that there are depths in the well a group. It is said: Ghaab yaghiban and ghaybah and ghayban, as the poet said: I will stay for two months or a half or three months, and I will be here as you have left me in absentia Al-Harawi said: Al-Ghayaba is like a hole or a niche in a well above the water, it hides something from the eye. Ibn Aziz said: Everything that hides something from you is ghayaba. I said: And from this the grave is called ghayaba. The poet said: If one day I am absent, then follow my path among the clan and family. A well is a well that has not been covered. If it is covered, it is a well. Al-A’sha said: If you were in a well eighty fathoms high and climbed the paths of heaven with a ladder It was called a well because it was cut into the ground. The plural of well is jibbah, jibab, and ajbab. He combined ghaybah and jibb because he meant they threw him in a dark place in the well so that the eyes of onlookers would not catch sight of him. It was said: It is a well in Jerusalem, and it was said: It is in Jordan, as said by Wahb ibn Munabbih. Muqatil: It is three farsakhs from the home of Jacob. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Some caravan picks it up is a subjunctive in response to the command. Mujahid, Abu Raja’, Al-Hasan and Qatadah read: will pick it up with a ta’, and this is based on the meaning, because some caravans are cars. Sibawayh said: Some of his fingers fell off, and he recited: And shine with the words that you have broadcasted as the chest of the canal shines with blood Another said: I see the years passing by, taking from me as secrets are taken from the crescent moon. He did not say east or took. The car is the group that travels on the road for travel. The speaker only said this so that they would not need to carry him to a distant place and the purpose would be achieved, because the one who picked him up from the car would carry him to a distant place. This was a way of planning so that they would not need to move by themselves, because their father might not give them permission, and he might find out about their intention. Third: This indicates that Joseph’s brothers were not prophets, neither from the beginning nor the end, because prophets do not plot to kill a Muslim, rather they were Muslims, then they committed a sin and then repented. It was said: They were prophets, and it is not impossible for reason to make a mistake by a prophet, so this was a mistake on their part. This is refuted by the fact that prophets are infallible from major sins, as we have stated. It was said: They were not prophets at that time, then God informed them, and this is more likely, and God knows best. Fourth: Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: Joseph was thrown into the well while he was a boy, and Ibn al-Qasim narrated the same from him, meaning that he was young. The evidence for the Almighty’s statement: Do not kill Joseph, but throw him into the bottom of the well, for some traveler to pick him up, he said: Only a young person picks him up. And His statement: And I fear that a wolf will eat him, that is a matter that is specific to young people, and their statement: Send him with us tomorrow to frolic and play, and indeed, We will be his guardians. Fifth: Picking up is taking something from the road, including foundlings and lost property. We will mention from its rulings what is indicated by the verse and the Sunnah, and what the scholars and linguists have said about it. Ibn Arafa said: Picking up is finding something without seeking it, including the Almighty’s saying: Some wayfarer picks it up meaning he finds it without expecting it. The scholars differed about the foundling. It was said: Its origin is freedom because free people are more likely to be slaves. It was narrated from Al-Hasan bin Ali that he ruled that the foundling is free, and he recited: And they sold him for a cheap price for a few dirhams. This is what Ashab, the companion of Malik, went for, and it is the saying of Omar bin Al-Khattab. It was also narrated from Ali and a group. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: If he intended to enslave him, then he is a slave, and if he intended to seek reward, then he is free. Malik said in his Muwatta: The matter according to us regarding the abandoned person is that he is free, and his allegiance is to the Muslim community; they inherit from him and pay blood money for him. Al-Shafi’i said the same, and he cited as evidence the words of the Prophet (peace be upon him): The allegiance is only for the one who freed him. He said: So he denied allegiance to anyone other than the freedman. Malik, Al-Shafi’i and their companions agreed that the foundling does not have a loyal relationship with anyone, and no one inherits from him through loyalty. Abu Hanifa and his companions and most of the Kufians said: The foundling has a loyal relationship with whomever he wants, so whoever has a loyal relationship with him inherits from him and pays blood money for him. According to Abu Hanifa, he has the right to transfer his loyalty wherever he wants, as long as the one who found him has not paid blood money for him. If he has a crime against him, he has no right to transfer his loyalty from him ever. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah reported on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him: The abandoned person is free. If he likes to be loyal to the one who found him, he should be loyal to him, and if he likes to be loyal to someone else, he should be loyal to him. Ata’ said something similar, and it is the opinion of Ibn Shihab and a group of the people of Medina, and he is free. Ibn al-Arabi said: The foundling was originally free because the free people predominated over the slaves, so the ruling was based on the majority, just as he was ruled to be a Muslim, taking into account the majority. If he was in a village in which there were Christians and Muslims, Ibn al-Qasim said: The ruling is based on the majority. If he was found to be wearing Jewish clothing, then he is Jewish, and if he was found to be wearing Christian clothing, then he is Christian. Otherwise, he is a Muslim, unless the majority of the people of the village were not Muslims. Another said: If there was only one Muslim in it, the foundling would be ruled to be a Muslim, giving priority to the ruling of Islam, which is supreme and cannot be overridden. This is what Ashhab said. Ashhab said: He is a Muslim forever, because I consider him a Muslim in every case, just as I consider him free in every case. The jurists differed regarding the outcast whose evidence indicates that he is a slave. A group of the people of Medina said: Their statement is not accepted in that regard. Ashhab went with this, based on the statement of Umar: He is free, and if he is judged to be free, the evidence is not accepted that he is a slave. Ibn al-Qasim said: The evidence is accepted in that regard, and this is the statement of al-Shafi’i and al-Kufi. Sixth: Malik said about the foundling: If the finder spends on him and then a man establishes evidence that he is his son, then the finder has recourse to the father if he threw him away intentionally. If he did not throw him away but he strayed from him, then the father is not liable for anything, and the finder is a volunteer in providing support. Abu Hanifa said: If he spends on the foundling, then he is a volunteer, unless the judge orders him to. Al-Awza’i said: Whoever spends on someone who is not obligated to provide support has recourse to what he spent. Al-Shafi’i said: If the foundling does not have money, then his support must be paid from the public treasury. If he does not have money, then there are two opinions: One of them is that a loan is taken from him on his behalf. The second is that it is given in installments to the Muslims without compensation. Seventh: As for lost property and lost items, scholars have differed regarding their ruling. A group of scholars said: Lost property and lost items are the same in meaning, and the ruling regarding them is the same. Abu Ja`far al-Tahawi held this view, and he rejected the statement of Abu `Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam - that lost property is only an animal, and lost property is something other than an animal - and he said this is a mistake, and he cited as evidence the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith of the slander to the Muslims: Your mother lost her necklace, so he applied this to the necklace. Eighth: The scholars agreed that if the lost item is not trivial and insignificant or something that will not last, then it is known for a full year. They agreed that if its owner comes, he has more right to it than the one who found it if it is proven to him that he is its owner. They agreed that if the one who found it eats it after a year and its owner wants to guarantee it, then that is his right. If he gives it in charity, then its owner has the choice between guaranteeing it or giving it as a reward. Whichever of the two he chooses, that is according to consensus. The one who found it does not have the right to give it in charity, nor does it spend it before a year. They agreed that he may eat the lost sheep that he fears for. Ninth: The jurists differed about what is better, leaving it or taking it. One of them is that the hadith is evidence of the permissibility of picking up lost property and taking stray property as long as it is not a camel. He said about the sheep: For you, for your brother, or for the wolf, urging him to take it, and he did not say about anything, leave it until it is lost or its owner comes to it. If leaving the lost property was better, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have ordered it, as he said about lost camels, and God knows best. The summary of the Maliki school of thought is that he has the flexibility to take it if he wants, or leave it if he wants. This is the opinion of Ismail bin Ishaq, may God have mercy on him. Al-Muzani said on the authority of Al-Shafi’i: I do not like anyone to leave the lost property if he finds it if he is trustworthy with it. He said: And the lost property is the same whether it is small or large. Tenth: Imams Malik and others narrated on the authority of Zaid bin Khalid Al-Juhani who said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about lost property. He said: “Know its container and its strap, then announce it for a year. If its owner comes back, then do as you please with it.” He said: What about lost sheep, O Messenger of God? He said: For you, your brother, or the wolf. He said: What about lost camels? He said: “What is it to you? It has its watering place and its shoes. It reaches the water and eats the trees until its owner finds it.” In the hadith of Abu, he said: “Keep its number, container and wrapper, and if its owner comes, then fine. Otherwise, enjoy it.” In this hadith there is an increase in the number. It was narrated by Muslim and others. The scholars agreed that the bag and the wrapper of the lost item are one of its signs and evidence. If the owner of the lost item comes with all its descriptions, it is given to him. Ibn al-Qasim said: He is forced to give it. If someone who is entitled to it comes and claims it with proof that it was his, the finder is not liable for anything. Should he swear with the descriptions or not? There are two opinions: the first is from Ashab, and the second is from Ibn al-Qasim. He is not required to give evidence according to Malik and his companions and Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others. Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi’i said: It is not given to him unless he provides evidence that it is his. This is contrary to the text of the hadith. If proof were a condition for giving, there would be no meaning to mentioning the bag, the wrapper and the number, as he is entitled to it with proof in any case. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would not have been allowed to remain silent about that, as it is delaying the statement from the time of need. And God knows best. Eleventh: The text of the hadith refers to camels and sheep and explains their ruling, but it is silent about other animals. Our scholars differed on whether cows are considered to be like camels or sheep. There are two opinions. Likewise, our imams differed on picking up horses, mules, and donkeys. The apparent opinion of Ibn al-Qasim is that they are to be picked up. Ashhab and Ibn Kinanah said: They are not to be picked up. The opinion of Ibn al-Qasim is more correct, because of the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: Guard your believing brother’s lost property. Twelfth: The scholars differed regarding spending on lost animals. Malik said, as Ibn al-Qasim reported: If the finder spends on animals, camels, etc., he has the right to claim the spending from their owner, whether he spent on them by order of the ruler or otherwise. He said: He has the right to withhold what he spent on the spending, and he has more right to it, like a pledge. Al-Shafi’i said: If the one who finds them spends on lost animals, then he is a volunteer. Al-Rabi’ narrated this from him. Al-Muzani said: If the judge orders him to spend, then it is a debt, and what he claims is accepted from him if it is similar to what he intended. Abu Hanifa said: If he spends on lost animals and camels without order of the judge, then he is a volunteer. If he spends by order of the judge, then it is a debt on its owner when he comes, and he has the right to withhold it when its owner comes, and the spending on it is for three days or so, until the judge orders the sale of the sheep or the like and decides on the spending. Thirteenth: There is nothing in his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding lost property after announcing it: Enjoy it or Do whatever you want with it or It is yours or Spend it or Then eat it or It is the property of God, He gives it to whom He wills as is in Sahih Muslim and other books, that indicates ownership and the removal of the liability from the finder if its owner comes, because in the hadith of Zaid bin Khalid Al-Juhani from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “If you do not know it, then spend it and let it be a trust with you. If its owner comes one day, then return it to him.” In another narration: (Then eat it. If its owner comes, then return it to him.) Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim. The scholars agreed that when its owner comes, he has more right to it, except for what Dawud went to, that the finder owns the lost property after announcing it, for those apparent meanings, and no attention should be paid to his statement, because of the people’s disagreement, and because of his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then return it to him.
12:11: The Almighty said: They said, 'O our father, what is the matter with you that you do not trust us with Joseph?' It was said to Al-Hasan: Does he envy the believer? He said: How can I forget you with the sons of Jacob! That is why it was said: The father is a thief and the brother is a swindler. At that point, they agreed to separate him from his son by a kind of trickery. They said to Jacob: O our father, what is the matter with you that you do not trust us with Joseph? It was said: When they negotiated and differed on the opinion of the second speaker, they returned to Jacob, peace be upon him, and said this statement. And in it is evidence that they had asked him before that to take Joseph with them, but he refused, as follows. Yazid bin Al-Qa'qa', Amr bin Ubaid, and Al-Zuhri read La Ta'amna with idgham, and without ishmām, which is the norm, because the way of what is assimilated is to be quiescent. Talhah bin Masraf read La Ta'amna with two apparent noons, according to the original. Yahya bin Waththab and Abu Razin - and it was narrated from Al-A'mash - read la timana with a kasra on the ta', and it is the language of Tamim, they say: you strike, and it has been mentioned before. The rest of the people read with idgham and ishmām to indicate the state of the letter before its idgham. And indeed, we are his sincere advisers meaning in his protection and care until we return him to you. Muqatil said: There is an inversion in the speech, and that is because Joseph's brothers said to their father: Send him with us tomorrow the verse, then their father said: Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him so they said then in response to his saying: What is the matter with you that you do not trust us with Joseph the verse.
12:12: Send him with us tomorrow to the desert. To graze and play tomorrow is an adverb, and the original according to Sibawayh is ghadu, and he pronounced it according to the original. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: What is between dawn and the morning prayer is called ghadwa, and so is bukra. We graze and play with the letter noon and the letter 'ayn is sukoon, the reading of the people of Basra. What is known from the reading of the people of Mecca is We graze with the letter noon and the letter 'ayn is kasra. The reading of the people of Kufa. He grazes and plays with the letter ya and the letter 'ayn is sukoon. The reading of the people of Medina is with the letter ya and the letter 'ayn is kasra, the first reading from the Arabs' saying rat'a a person and a camel graze if they eat as they wish, and the meaning is: We enjoy the fertility, and everything fertile is grazing. He said: The pasture is not there Another said: You will enjoy what you neglect until you remember, for it is only coming and going. Another said: I am an infidel after death has been turned away from me and after you have given me a hundred thousand dirhams. That is, the pasture due to the abundance of pasture. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatada tarta’a meaning to strive. An-Nahhas said: He took it from his saying: Indeed, we went racing because the meaning is: We race in running to a specific destination. And likewise yatra’a with a sukoon on the ‘ayn, except that it is for Joseph alone, peace be upon him. And yatra’a with a kasra on the ‘ayn is from herding sheep, meaning to train and dismount thereby, so sometimes he grazes and sometimes he plays because of his young age. Al-Qutbi said natra’a we guard and take care, and we graze each other, from your saying: May God protect you, meaning He preserves you. And we play is from playing. It was said to Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’: How did they say and we play when they were prophets? He said: They were not prophets at that time. It was said: What is meant by permissible play is relaxation, not forbidden play which is against the truth, and for this reason Jacob did not reject their saying and we play. And from this is his saying, peace be upon him: Why not a young camel that you play with and she plays with you? Mujahid and Qatadah read: Yartaa meaning his mount grazes, so the object was deleted, Wa Yala’ab in the nominative case as a new sentence, and the meaning is: he is one of those who play. And We will surely guard him from everything you fear for him. Then it is possible that they were going out riding, and it is possible that they were on foot. It has been reported that they carried Joseph on their shoulders as long as Jacob could see them, then when they were out of his sight they threw him down to run with them to harm him.
12:13: The Almighty said: He said, 'Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him away' in the nominative case, meaning that you should take him away. He informed about his grief for his absence. And I fear that a wolf will eat him because he saw in his dream that a wolf attacked Joseph, so he feared for him, said Al-Kalbi. It was said: He saw in his dream as if he was on the top of a mountain, and as if Joseph was in the valley, and then ten wolves surrounded him, wanting to eat him, but one of them fended him off, then the earth split open and Joseph hid in it for three days, so the ten were his brothers, when they conspired to kill him, and the one who defended him was his older brother Judah, and his hiding in the earth was his stay in the well for three days. It was said: He only said that out of fear for them for him, and that he meant them by the wolf, so his fear was only from their killing him, so he referred to them by the wolf as a metaphor for them, as a cover for them. Ibn Abbas said: So he called them wolves. It was said: He did not fear them for him, and if he had feared them, he would not have sent him with them. Rather, he feared the wolf, because it is the most common feared thing in the desert. The wolf is derived from the word tadha’abat ar-rih, meaning it comes from every direction. This is what Ahmad ibn Yahya said. He said: The wolf is hamzated because it comes from every direction. Warsh narrated from Nafi’ al-dheeb without a hamzah, because the hamzah was silent and before it was a kasrah, so he lightened it and it became a ya’. And you are heedless of it means busy with grazing.
12:14: The Almighty said: They said, ‘If the wolf had eaten him while we were a company,’ meaning a group that saw the wolf and did not repel it from him. Then we would surely be losers, meaning in protecting our sheep, meaning if we were unable to repel the wolf from our brother, then we would be even more unable to repel it from our sheep. It was said: Then we would surely be losers because they were ignorant of his right. It was also said: Then we would surely be incapable.
12:15: The Almighty said: So when they took him away and decided to put him that is in the accusative case, meaning that they would put him in the bottom of the well. It was said in the story: When Jacob, peace be upon him, sent him with them, he took a strong covenant from them to protect him, and he handed him over to Reuben and said: O Reuben! He is young, and know, my son, my compassion for him. If he is hungry, feed him, and if he is thirsty, give him something to drink, and if he is tired, carry him and then hurry back to me. He said: So they began to carry him on their shoulders, not one putting him down until another lifted him up, and Jacob accompanied them for a mile and then returned. When their father lost sight of them, the one who was carrying him threw him to the ground until he almost broke. So he took refuge with another and found in each one of them more angry and oppressive than the other. So he called out to Reuben and said: You are the eldest of my brothers, and the successor after my father Ali, and the closest of the brothers to me, so have mercy on me and have mercy on my weakness. So he slapped him hard and said: There is no kinship between me and you, so call the eleven stars to save you from us. So he knew that their hatred was because of his vision, so he clung to his brother Judah and said: O my brother! Have mercy on my weakness, my helplessness and my young age, and have mercy on the heart of your father Jacob, for how quickly you forgot his commandment and broke his covenant. So Judah’s heart softened and he said: By God, they will never reach you as long as I am alive. Then he said: O my brothers! Killing a soul that God has forbidden is one of the greatest sins. So they returned this boy to his father, and promised him that he would never tell his father anything about what had happened. His brothers said to him: By God, you only want to have a position with Jacob. By God, if you do not leave him alone, we will kill you with him. He said: If you insist on anything else, then here is this desolate, barren pit, which is a shelter for snakes and vermin. Throw him in it. If he is afflicted with any of that, then that is what is meant, and you will be relieved of his blood. If he escapes into the hands of caravans who take him to another land, then that is what is meant. They agreed on that, and it is the saying of God Almighty: So when they took him away and decided to put him in the bottom of the pit. The answer to when is omitted, meaning when they took him away and decided to throw him in the pit, their trial became great. It was said that the answer to when is their saying: They said, ‘O our father, we went racing.’ It was said: The meaning is that when they took him from their father and agreed to put him in the bottom of the well, they put him in it. This is according to the Basrans’ school of thought. As for the Kufians’ opinion, the answer is: We inspired and the waw is inserted, and the waw, according to them, is added with lama and hatta. God Almighty said: Until, when they came to it and its gates were opened (al-Zumar 39:73), meaning it was opened. And His statement: Until, when Our command came and the oven overflowed (Hud 11:40), meaning it overflowed. Imru’ al-Qais said: When we passed the neighborhood square and he went away That is, he withdrew, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: So when they had both submitted and he laid him down upon his forehead, We called to him, meaning We called to him. And in His saying: And We revealed to him is evidence of his prophethood at that time. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah said: God gave him prophethood while he was in the well on a rock high above the water. Al-Kalbi said: He was thrown into the well when he was eighteen years old, so he was not a child. And whoever says he was a child, it is not far-fetched in reason that a child would prophesy and receive revelation. It was said: It was a revelation of inspiration like His saying: And your Lord inspired to the bees (al-Nahl 16:68). It was said: It was a dream, and the first is more apparent - and God knows best - and that Gabriel came to him with the revelation. God the Almighty said: You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs. There are two interpretations of this: The first is that it was revealed to him that he would meet them and rebuke them for what they had done. Based on this, the revelation after he was thrown into the well was to strengthen his heart and give him good report of safety. The second is that it was revealed to him about what they were doing to him. Based on this, the revelation before he was thrown into the well was to warn him. And they do not perceive that you are Joseph, because God the Almighty commanded him when the matter was entrusted to him in Egypt not to inform his father and brothers of his location. It was said: by God the Almighty's revelation of prophecy, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. It was said: the ha is for Jacob, God the Almighty revealed to him what they had done to Joseph, and that he would inform them of his affair, and they did not perceive what God had revealed to him, and God knows best. Among what was mentioned of his story when he was thrown into the well - as mentioned by Al-Suddi and others - is that when his brothers began to lower him into the well, he clung to the edge of the well, so they tied his hands and tore off his shirt, so he said: O my brothers! They returned my shirt to me so that I may hide myself in this well. If I die, it will be my shroud, and if I live, I will cover my nakedness with it. They said, Call upon the sun, the moon, and the eleven stars to keep you company and clothe you. He said, I did not see anything. So they lowered him into the well, and when he reached halfway down, they threw him in, hoping that he would fall and die. There was water in the well, so he fell into it. Then he took refuge near a rock and spoke on it. It was said that it was Simon who cut the rope, hoping that it would crumble on the rock. Gabriel was under the leg of the Throne, so God revealed to him, Catch up with My servant. Gabriel said, So I hurried and descended until I came between throwing him and falling, and I made him sit on the rock, safe and sound. That well was a shelter for vermin, so he stood on the rock and began to cry. They called out to him, and he thought that it was mercy upon him that had come to them, so he answered them. They wanted to throw him with the rock, but Judah prevented them. Judah used to bring him food, but when he fell naked, Gabriel came down to him. When Abraham was thrown into the fire naked, Gabriel brought him a shirt of silk from Paradise and dressed him in it. That remained with Abraham, then Isaac inherited it, then Jacob inherited it. When Joseph grew up, Jacob made that shirt into a talisman and put it around his neck, so it would not leave him. When he was thrown into the well naked, Gabriel took out that shirt and dressed him in it. Wahb said: When he stood on the rock, he said: O my brothers! Every dead person has a will, so listen to my will. They said: What is it? He said: When you all gather and befriend one another, remember my loneliness. When you eat, remember my hunger. When you drink, remember my thirst. When you see a stranger, remember my loneliness. When you see a young man, remember my youth. Gabriel said to him: O Joseph! Stop this and occupy yourself with supplication, for supplication has a place with God. Then he taught him and said: Say: O God, O Companion of every stranger, O Friend of every lonely person, O Refuge of every fearful person, O Reliever of every distress, O Knower of every secret conversation, O End of every complaint, O Present of every assembly, O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining! I ask You to cast Your hope into my heart, so that I have no concern or preoccupation other than You, and to make for me a way out and relief from my situation, for You are able to do all things. The angels said: Our God! We hear a voice and a supplication. The voice is the voice of a boy, and the supplication is the supplication of a prophet. Ad-Dahhak said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down to Joseph while he was in the well and said to him: Shall I not teach you some words that, if you say them, God will hasten your release from this well? He said: Yes! Then he said to him: Say: O Maker of all that is made, O Mender of all that is broken, O Witness to your secret conversations, O Present of all gatherings, O Reliever of all distress, O Companion of all strangers, O Comforter of all who are alone, bring me relief and hope, and cast Your hope into my heart so that I will not hope in anyone but You. Joseph repeated them several times that night, and God brought him out of the well that morning.
12:16: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And they came to their father at night, meaning at night, and it is a circumstance that takes the place of a state. They came at night so that they would be more able to apologize in the darkness. That is why it was said: Do not ask for a need at night, for modesty is in the eyes, and do not apologize during the day for a sin and then falter in your apology. It was narrated that when Jacob, peace be upon him, heard their crying, he said: What is the matter with you? Did something happen to the sheep? They said: No. He said: Where is Joseph? They said: We went racing and the wolf ate him, so he cried out and said: Where is his shirt? As will be explained, God willing. Al-Suddi and Ibn Hibban said: When they said the wolf ate him, he fell unconscious, so they poured water on him but he did not move, and they called him but he did not answer. Wahb said: Judah placed his hand over Jacob’s breathing passages but he did not feel any breath, and no vein moved in him, so Judah said to them: Woe to us from the Judge on the Day of Judgment! We lost our brother and killed our father. Jacob did not regain consciousness until the cold of dawn. He regained consciousness with his head in Reuben's lap. He said: O Reuben! Did I not entrust my son to you? Did I not make a covenant with you? He said: O my father! Stop weeping for me and I will tell you. So Jacob stopped weeping and said: O my father, we went racing and left Joseph with our belongings and a wolf ate him. Second: Our scholars said: This verse is evidence that a person’s crying does not indicate the sincerity of his words, because it may be artificial. Some of the righteous are able to do that, and some of them are not. It has been said: Artificial tears are not hidden, as a wise man said: If tears run down your cheeks, you will know who is crying and who is pretending to cry.
12:17: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: We race Nafta’ala, from the word musabah. It was said: meaning we compete, and this is how Abdullah reads: We went to compete and it is a type of competition, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. Al-Azhari said: Struggle is in arrows, and betting is in horses, and the competition combines them. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: We race means in archery, or on horses, or on foot, and the purpose of racing on foot is to train the soul to run, because it is the tool in fighting the enemy, and repelling wolves from sheep. Al-Suddi and Ibn Hayyan said: We race we run fast to see who is faster. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The competition is a law in the Sharia, and a wonderful characteristic, and an aid in war, and “the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) did it with himself and his horse, and he raced Aisha may God be pleased with her on foot and he won, and when the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) grew old, he raced her and she won, so he said to her: This for that.” I said: Salamah bin Al-Akwa’ raced a man when they returned from Dhi Qard to Medina, and Salamah beat him. Narrated by Muslim. Second: Malik narrated on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar: “The son of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raced between horses that had been trained from Al-Hafiya’ and the distance was Thaniyat Al-Wada’, and he raced between horses that had not been trained from Thaniyat to the mosque of Bani Zuraiq, and Abdullah Ibn Umar was among those who raced with them.” This hadith, despite its authenticity in this regard, includes three conditions, and the race is not permissible without them, which are: The distance must be known. The second - That the horses be of equal condition? The third - That the trained horse not race with the non-trained horse in the same period and the same destination. The horses that must be trained and raced on, and this Sunnah is established for them, are the horses prepared for jihad against the enemy, not for fighting the Muslims in tribulations. Third: As for racing with arrows and camels, Muslim narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, who said: “We traveled with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we stopped at a place, some of us were fixing our tents, and some of us were using fresh water,” and he mentioned the hadith. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no racing except with an arrow, a hoofed animal, or a camel. The mention of an arrow was confirmed in the hadith of Ibn Abi Dhi’b on the authority of Nafi’ bin Abi Nafi’ on the authority of Abu Hurairah, which was mentioned by Al-Nasa’i, and the jurists of Hijaz and Iraq say the same. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a she-camel called Al-Adhba’ that could not outrun – Humayd said: or could hardly outrun – and a Bedouin came on a camel and outran it, and that upset the Muslims until they recognized him and said: ‘It is the right of God that nothing in this world should be raised except that He lowers it.’” Fourth: Muslims unanimously agree that racing is not permissible as a bet except on the hoof, the blade, and the spear. Al-Shafi’i said: Apart from these three, racing is gambling. Abu al-Bukhtari al-Qadi added in the hadith on the hoof, the blade, and the spear or wing, which is a word he made up for al-Rashid, so the scholars abandoned his hadith for that reason and for other fabrications, so the scholars do not write down his hadith under any circumstances. It was narrated from Malik that he said: There is no racing except on horses and archery, because it is a strength for those at war. He said: And racing on horses is more beloved to us than racing on archery. The apparent meaning of the hadith equates racing on noble horses with racing on horses. Some scholars have prohibited betting on everything except horses, because they were the ones that the Arabs used to bet on. It was narrated from Ata’ that betting on everything is permissible, and his statement may be interpreted, because applying it to the general meaning of everything leads to permitting gambling, which is forbidden by consensus. Fifth: It is not permissible to race horses and camels except at a known destination and a known time, as we have mentioned. Likewise, the race in archery is not permissible except at a known destination and a known shot, and a type of hit, whether it is a loss or an unconditional hit. There are three types of races: a race that the governor or a man other than the governor gives from his money voluntarily, giving the winner a known amount, and whoever wins takes it. A race that one of the competitors gives without his partner, so if his partner wins it, he takes it, and if he wins his partner takes it, and it is good for him to spend it in the way he gave it, and he does not return it to his money. There is no disagreement about this. The third race - there is disagreement about it, which is that each of them gives something like what his partner gives, so whoever wins secures his race and his partner’s race.
