This way is not permissible until a muhallil enters between them and they are not sure that he will beat them. If the muhallil wins, he secures both races and takes them alone. If one of the competitors wins, he secures his race and takes his partner’s race, and the muhallil does not get anything in it, and there is nothing against him. If the second of them outran the third, it is as if neither of them outran. Abu Ali ibn Khairan, one of the companions of al-Shafi’i, said: The ruling on a horse that is in a state of ihram is that its race is unknown, and it is called a state of ihram because it makes the race permissible for the two competitors to race at the beginning. The scholars agreed that if there is no state of ihram between them and each of the competitors stipulates that if he wins, he will take his race and his companion will win, then this is gambling, and it is not permissible. In Sunan Abi Dawud, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, he said: Whoever enters a horse between two horses and is not sure that it will win, this is not gambling, and whoever enters it and is sure that it will win, this is gambling. In al-Muwatta’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, he said: There is no harm in betting on horses if a state of ihram enters them, if he wins, he takes the race, and if he wins, he does not have to do anything. This is what al-Shafi’i and the majority of scholars said. Malik’s opinion differed on this, and he said once that a state of ihram is not obligatory in horses, and we do not accept the opinion of Sa’id in this regard. Then he said: It is not permissible except with a state of ihram, and this is better than his opinion. Sixth: No one may ride horses or camels in a race except a person who has reached puberty, and if their owners ride them, that is better. It was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he said: No one may ride horses in a race except their owners. Al-Shafi’i said: The minimum for a race is to race with a guide or part of him, or with a hump or part of him. The race of the archers is like this in his opinion, and the statement of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan in this regard is similar to the statement of al-Shafi’i. Seventh: “It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he raced Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, won, and Abu Bakr prayed a third of Umar’s distance.” The meaning of Abu Bakr prayed is that the head of his horse was at the hump of the Messenger of God’s horse, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the hump is the place of the rump. God the Almighty said: And We left Joseph by our belongings meaning by our clothes and fabrics, guarding them. And the wolf devoured him This is because when they heard their father say: And I fear that the wolf will eat him they took it from his mouth and forbade him, because it was the most obvious fear for him. And you will not believe us meaning you will not believe. And if we meaning even if we were, as Al-Mubarrad and Ibn Ishaq said, truthful in what we said, and Jacob did not believe them because of the strength of the accusation and the abundance of evidence that contradicted what they said, as will be explained. It was said: And if we were truthful meaning even if we were among the people of trust and honesty in your view, you would not have believed us, and you would have accused us in this case, because of the intensity of your love for Joseph. Its meaning was said by Al-Tabari, Al-Zajjaj and others.
12:18: God Almighty said: And they brought his shirt with false blood. There are three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: With false blood. Mujahid said: It was the blood of a young goat or a young kid that they slaughtered. Qatada said: It was the blame of a gazelle, meaning they came upon his shirt with false blood on it. So he described the blood with the infinitive, so it was estimated: With the blood of a lie, like: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82). The subject and the object may be called by the infinitive, it is said: This is the prince’s strike, meaning his strike, and poured water means poured, and sunken water means sunken, and a just man means just. Al-Hasan and Aisha read: with fresh blood with the unvoiced dāl, meaning fresh blood. Fresh blood is called kadhb. It was narrated that it is the changed one, as Al-Sha’bi said. Kadhb is also the whiteness that appears in the nails of young people, so it is possible that the blood on the shirt is likened to the whiteness that appears in the nails due to the difference in the two colours. Second: Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: When they wanted to make the blood a sign of their truthfulness, God coupled this sign with a sign that contradicts it, which is the shirt being free from reproach, since it is not possible for a wolf to prey on Joseph while he was wearing the shirt and the shirt being free from being torn. When Jacob, peace be upon him, examined the shirt and did not find any tear or mark in it, he used that as evidence of their lie, and said to them: When was this wolf wise to eat Joseph and not tear the shirt! Ibn Abbas and others said this. Israel narrated on the authority of Samak bin Harb on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The blood was the blood of a young goat. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Samak on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When he looked at it, he said: You have lied. If the wolf had eaten him, the shirt would have been torn. Al-Mawardi narrated that there are three signs in the shirt: When they came upon him with the blood of a liar, when his shirt was torn from the back, and when it was thrown on his father’s face and he regained his sight. I said: This is rejected, because the shirt that they brought with the blood is not the same shirt that was torn, and not the shirt that the bearer of good tidings brought him. It has been said that the story that was torn is the one that he brought, so he regained his sight, as will be explained at the end of the surah, God willing. It was narrated that they said to him: Rather, the thieves killed him, so their statements differed, so he accused them, and Jacob said to them: You claim that the wolf ate him, and if he had, it would have torn his shirt before it reached his skin, and I do not see any tear in the shirt, and you claim that the thieves killed him, and if they had killed him, they would have taken his shirt. Do they want anything but his clothes?! So they said at that time: And you will not believe us, even if we were truthful from Al-Hasan and others, meaning if we were described as truthful, you would have accused us. Third: The jurists used this verse as evidence in applying the signs in matters of jurisprudence such as the oath and others, and they agreed that Jacob, peace be upon him, used the authenticity of the shirt as evidence of their lie. Thus, the observer must consider the signs and indications if they conflict, and whichever of them is more likely, he should rule on the side of the more likely, which is the strength of the accusation, and there is no disagreement in ruling on it, as Ibn al-Arabi said. God Almighty said: He said, ‘Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, so patience is most fitting.’ There are three issues: First: It was narrated that when they said to Jacob: Then the wolf ate him, he said to them: Didn’t the wolf leave a limb for you to bring me to enjoy it?! Didn’t he leave me a garment so I could smell his scent? They said: Yes! This is his shirt stained with his blood. This is what God Almighty said: And they brought his shirt with false blood (Yusuf 12:18). Jacob wept at that and said to his sons: Show me his shirt. So they showed it to him, and he smelled it and kissed it. Then he turned it over and did not see any rips or tears in it. He said: By God, there is no god but Him, I have never seen a wolf more wise than him today. He ate my son and snatched him from his shirt and did not tear it on him. He knew that the matter was not as they said, and that the wolf did not eat him. So he turned away from them as if he was angry, crying and sad and said: O my sons! Guide me to my son. If he is alive, I will return him to me, and if he is dead, I will shroud him and bury him. It was said that they said at that time: Didn’t you see how our father lied to us in our statement! Come, let us take him out of the pit and cut him up limb by limb, and bring our father one of his limbs so that he may believe us and end his despair. Then Judah said, By God, if you do this, I will be your enemy as long as I live, and I will tell your father about your evil deed. They said, If you prevent us from this, then come, let us hunt a wolf for him. He said: So they hunted a wolf, smeared it with blood, and tied it up with ropes, then they brought it to Jacob and said, O our father! This is the wolf that comes to our sheep and preys on them, and perhaps it is the one who caused us the loss of our brother, we do not doubt it, and this is his blood on it. Jacob said, Let him go. So they let him go, and the wolf wriggled at him, and he approached him and Jacob said to him, Come closer, come closer, until his cheek was pressed to his cheek. Jacob said to him, O wolf! Why have you caused me such a loss of my son and caused me such a long time of grief?! Then he said, O God, make him speak. So God Almighty made him speak. He said, “By Him Who chose you as a prophet, I have not eaten his flesh, nor torn his skin, nor plucked a single hair from his hairs. By God, I have no covenant with your son. I am only a strange wolf that came from the outskirts of Egypt in search of a brother of mine who was lost. I do not know whether he is alive or dead. Your sons hunted me down and tied me up. The flesh of prophets is forbidden to us and to all wild animals. By God, I will not stay in a country where the sons of prophets lie to wild animals.” So Jacob released him and said, “By God, you have brought proof against yourselves. This is a wild wolf that came out following the covenant of his brother, and you have lost your brother. I know that the wolf is innocent of what you have brought. “Rather, your souls have made something seem good to you,” other than what you describe and mention. Then he said, preparing himself, So patience is most fitting. It is: Second: Al-Zajjaj said: That is, my affair and what I believe is beautiful patience. Qatrib said: That is, my patience is beautiful patience. It was said: That is, beautiful patience is more appropriate for me, so fa is the subject and its predicate is omitted. It is narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about beautiful patience and he said: It is that with which there is no complaint. More clarification will come at the end of the surah, God willing. Abu Hatim said: Isa bin Omar recited, according to what Sahl bin Yusuf claimed, fa sabraan jameelan and he said: And this is how Al-Ashhab Al-Uqaili recited it, and he said: And this is how it is in the Mushaf of Anas and Abu Salih. Al-Mubarrad said: fa sabraan jameelan in the nominative is more appropriate than the accusative, because the meaning is: He said, My Lord, I have beautiful patience. He said: And the accusative is for the source, meaning, so I will be patient with beautiful patience. He said: He complained to my camel about the long journey. Be patient, for we are both afflicted. And beautiful patience is that in which there is no impatience or complaint. It was said: The meaning is I do not live with you with a gloomy face and a scowling forehead, rather I live with you as I was with you, and in this there is what indicates that he pardoned their punishment. On the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit that Jacob’s eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, so he used to raise them with a rag, so it was said to him: What is this? He said: The length of time and the abundance of sorrows, so God revealed to him: Do you complain about me, O Jacob? He said: O Lord! I committed a sin, so forgive me. And God is the one sought for help is the subject and predicate. For what you describe means for the possibility of what you describe of lies. Third: Ibn Abi Rafa’ah said: People of opinion should question their opinion when they think that Jacob, peace be upon him, was a prophet, when his sons said to him: We went racing and left Joseph with our belongings, and a wolf ate him (Yusuf 12:17). He said: Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, so have patience and be gracious. So he was right here. Then they said to him: Your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew, and we were not guardians of the unseen. (Yusuf 12:81). He said: Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something, so he was wrong. First: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you. “A group” is the predicate of indeed. It is permissible to put it in the accusative case as a state, and the predicate would be For each one of them is what he has earned of sin. The reason for its revelation is what the imams narrated from the long hadith of the slander in the story of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and it is a well-known, authentic hadith, the fame of which makes it unnecessary to mention it, and it will come in an abbreviated form. Al-Bukhari included it as a suspended hadith, and his hadith is more complete. He said: Abu Usamah said on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha, and he also included it on the authority of Muhammad bin Kathir on the authority of his brother Sulayman on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Umm Ruman, the mother of Aisha, that she said: When Aisha was accused, she fell unconscious. And on the authority of Musa bin Ismail on the authority of Abu Wa’il, he said: Masruq ibn al-Ajda’ narrated to me: Umm Ruman, the mother of Aisha, narrated to me: While Aisha and I were sitting, a woman from the Ansar came in and said: May God do such-and-such to such-and-such! Umm Ruman said: What is that? She said: My son, who narrated the hadith? She said: What is that? She said: So-and-so. Aisha said: Did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, hear it? She said: Yes. She said: And Abu Bakr? She said: Yes. So she fell unconscious, and she did not regain consciousness until she was struck by a fever with chills. I threw her clothes over her and covered her. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and said: What is the matter with her? I said: O Messenger of God, she has a fever with chills. He said: Perhaps she is talking about a hadith she is talking about? She said: Yes. Aisha sat up and said: By God, if I swear, you will not believe me! And if I tell you, you will not excuse me! My example and your example are like that of Jacob and his sons, and God is the One sought for help against what you describe. She said: And he left without saying anything, and God revealed her excuse. She said: Praise be to God, not to anyone else, nor to you. Abu Abdullah Al-Humaidi said: “Some of the Baghdadi hadith masters we met used to say that the mursal in this hadith is clearer, and they used as evidence for that the fact that Umm Ruman died during the lifetime of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and Masruq did not see the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) without dispute.” Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Ubaydullah bin Abdullah bin Abi Malekah that Aisha used to recite when you receive it with your tongues and say: Walaq means falsehood. Ibn Abi Malekah said: She was more knowledgeable about that than others because it was revealed about her. Al-Bukhari said: “Muammar bin Rashid said on the authority of Al-Zuhri: The hadith of the slander took place during the Battle of Al-Murays’i’.” Ibn Ishaq said: That was in the sixth year. Musa bin Uqbah said: In the fourth year. Al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Muammar on the authority of Al-Zuhri, who said: “Al-Walid bin Abdul Malik said to me: Has it reached you that Ali was among those who slandered?” He said: I said: No, but two men from your people, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, informed me that Aisha said to them: Ali was a Muslim regarding her affair. Abu Bakr al-Ismaili included it in his book Al-Mukhraj ala al-Sahih from another chain of transmission on the authority of Muammar on the authority of al-Zuhri, in which it says: He said: I was with al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik and he said: The one who bore the greatest burden among them was Ali ibn Abi Talib? I said: No, Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, Urwah, Alqama and Ubaydullah ibn Abd God ibn Utbah all narrated to me saying: I heard Aisha say: The one who bore the greatest burden was Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Al-Bukhari also included it on the authority of al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha: The one who bore the greatest burden among them was Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Second: The Almighty’s saying: By slander. Slander is lying. A group is three men, as Ibn Abbas said. It was also narrated from him, from three to ten. Ibn Uyaynah: Forty men. Mujahid: From ten to fifteen. Its root in the language and speech of the Arabs is a group who are fanatical about one another. The true meaning of good is that which brings more benefit than harm. Evil is that which brings more harm than benefit. Good with no evil in it is Paradise. Evil with no good in it is Hell. As for the affliction that befalls the saints, it is good, because its harm of pain is small in this world, and its good is the great reward in the hereafter. So God the Almighty alerted Aisha, her family, and Safwan, as the address to them in His saying: Do not think it is evil for you; rather, it is good for you, is because the benefit and goodness outweigh the evil. Third: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, set out with Aisha with him on the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq, which was the expedition of al-Marisi’, and returned and approached Madinah, the call to depart was made one night. She got up when the call to depart was made and walked until she passed the army. When she had finished her business, she went to the saddlebags and touched her chest. There was a necklace of Dhofar agate that had broken. She went back and looked for it, but her search for it delayed her. She found it and turned back, but she did not find anyone. She was a young woman with little flesh. The men lifted her litter and did not notice her being removed from it. When she did not find anyone, she lay down in her place, hoping that she would be missed and that he would return to her. She slept in the place, and nothing woke her up except the words of Safwan ibn al-Mu’attal: To God we belong and to Him we shall return. This was because he had stayed behind the army to guard the rearguard. It was said: She woke up to retrieve him, and he got off his camel and moved away from it until Aisha mounted, and he began to lead her until he reached the army at noon, so the people of the slander fell into their words, and the one who gathered around him about it and sought his help and ignited it was Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul the hypocrite, and he is the one who saw Safwan holding the reins of Aisha’s camel and said: By God, she did not escape from him and he did not escape from her, and he said: The wife of your Prophet spent the night with a man. And among those who said it were Hassan bin Thabit, Mastah bin Athatah and Hamna bint Jahsh. This is an abbreviation of the hadith, and it is in full and perfect in Bukhari and Muslim, and it is more complete in Muslim. When Safwan heard Hassan’s words about the slander, he came and struck him with the sword once on the head and said: Receive the flies of the sword from me, for I am a young man who, when provoked, is not a poet. So Hassan's group took him, wrapped him in a cloak, and brought him to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, overlooked Hassan's wound and asked him for it as a gift. This indicates that Hassan was one of those who took on the role of arrogance, as will be mentioned later, and God knows best. This Safwan was the rearguard of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) during his battles due to his bravery, and he was one of the best of the Companions. It was said that he was chaste and did not have intercourse with women. This was mentioned by Ibn Ishaq on the authority of Aisha. It was also said that he had two sons, as indicated by his hadith narrated with his wife, “And the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about his two sons: ‘They resemble him more than a crow resembles a crow.’” And his saying in the hadith: By God, I have never uncovered a woman’s private parts, meaning committing adultery. He was killed as a martyr, may God be pleased with him, in the Battle of Armenia in the year nineteen during the time of Umar, and it was said: in the land of the Romans in the year fifty-eight during the time of Muawiyah. Fourth: The Almighty said: For every person among them is what he has earned of sin, meaning from those who spoke the slander. He did not name from the people of the slander except Hassan, Mastah, Hamna, and Abdullah, and others were ignorant, as stated by Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan asked him about that and he said: Except that they were a group, as God the Almighty said. And in the copy of the Qur’an of Hafsah it says a group of four. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And he who took upon himself the greater part of it among them. Humayd al-A’raj and Ya’qub read his greater part with a damma on the kaf. Al-Farra’ said: This is a good interpretation, because the Arabs say: So-and-so took upon himself the greater part of such-and-such, meaning he took upon himself the greater part. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha that he was Hassan, and that she said when he went blind: Perhaps the great punishment that God has threatened him with is the loss of his sight. Masruq narrated it on her authority. It was narrated on her authority that he was Abdullah ibn Ubayy, and this is the correct view, and Ibn Abbas said the same. Abu Omar ibn Abdul Barr narrated that Aisha exonerated Hassan of the slander, and said: He did not say anything. Hassan denied that he had said anything of that in his saying: Hassan Razan does not weigh with suspicion and becomes hungry from the meat of the ignorant The wife of the best of people in religion and character, the Prophet of guidance and the most generous of women Aqila is a tribe from Luay ibn Ghalib, whose noble endeavors are eternal. A well-mannered woman whose tents God has made beautiful and purified from all ugliness and falsehood If what I said is true, I will not raise my whip to my fingers. How I wish as long as I live and my support for the family of the Messenger of God is the adornment of gatherings He has high ranks over people, the virtue of which is beyond compare. Surah Al-Mutawa’il It was narrated that when he recited to her: A noble horse, she said to him: “You are not like that. You mean that you have fallen into negligence.” This is a contradiction, but it can be reconciled by saying: Hassan did not say that explicitly and explicitly, and he might have suggested that and hinted at it, so it was attributed to him. And God knows best. People differed about whether he was involved in the slander or not, and whether he was flogged or not. God knows which one it was, and that is the issue. Sixth: The fur of Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) flogged two men and a woman for slander: Mistah, Hassan, and Hamna.” This was mentioned by al-Tirmidhi. Al-Qushayri narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) flogged Ibn Ubayy eighty times, and in the Hereafter he will have the punishment of Hellfire.” Al-Qushayri said: “What is proven in the reports is that he flogged Ibn Ubayy and flogged Hassan and Hamna. As for Mistah, no explicit slander has been proven against him, but he would hear and spread the word without stating it explicitly.” Al-Mawardi and others said: “They differed over whether the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) punished the slanderers. There are two opinions: One of them is that he did not punish any of the slanderers, because the prescribed punishments are only carried out by confession or by evidence, and God did not require him to carry them out by informing him of them, just as He did not require him to kill the hypocrites, although He had informed him of their disbelief.” I said: This is corrupt and contradicts the text of the Qur’an, for God Almighty says: And those who accuse chaste women and do not produce four witnesses meaning that their statement is true: Then flog them with eighty lashes. The second statement: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, punished the people of slander, Abdullah bin Ubayy, Mastah bin Athatah, Hassan bin Thabit, and Hamna bint Jahsh. A Muslim poet said about that: Hassan tasted that which his family and Hamna had when they said, Hijra and Mastah. Ibn Salul tasted the shame of the punishment, as he indulged in slanderous speech that is clear. They treated the wife of their prophet with stoning and anger at the Lord of the Noble Throne, so they became wicked. They harmed the Messenger of God in it, so they committed shameful acts that will remain, and they disgraced them. Then he poured down upon them rains as if they were showers of rain falling from the peaks of the clouds. I said: The well-known report and what is known among scholars is that the one who punished Hassan, Mastah, and Hamna, and he did not hear of any punishment for Abdullah bin Ubayy. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: When my excuse came up, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood up and mentioned that, and recited the Qur’an. When he came down from the pulpit, he ordered the two men and the woman to be flogged, and he named them: Hassan ibn Thabit, Mastah ibn Athatah, and Hamna bint Jahsh. In the book of al-Tahawi, it says: Eighty by eighty. Our scholars said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy was not flogged because God, the Most High, had prepared for him a great punishment in the Hereafter. If he had been flogged in this world, it would have been a reduction in his punishment in the Hereafter and a mitigation for him, even though God, the Most High, had testified to the innocence of Aisha may God be pleased with her and to the falsehood of everyone who accused her. The benefit of the flogging was achieved, since its purpose was to demonstrate the lie of the slanderer and the innocence of the slandered, as God, the Most High, said: But if they do not produce witnesses, then it is they who are liars in the sight of God. These Muslims were flogged to expiate for them the sin of the slander they committed, so that they would not be held responsible for it in the Hereafter. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said about the prescribed punishments: It is an expiation for the one against whom it was carried out,” as in the hadith of Ubadah ibn al-Samit. It may also be said that the punishment of Ibn Abi was left out of a desire to win over his people, out of respect for his son, and to extinguish the fire of discord expected from that, the principles of which had appeared from Sa`d ibn Ubadah and his people, as in Sahih Muslim. And God knows best.
12:19: The Almighty said: And a car came meaning a group of passersby walking from Ash-Sham to Egypt, so they lost their way and wandered until they came down close to the well. The well was in a desert far from civilization, it was only for shepherds and passersby, and its water was salty and sweet when Joseph was thrown into it. So they sent their water-drawer It was mentioned in the meaning, and if he had said: So she sent her water-drawer, it would have been in the wording, like and she came. The water-drawer is the one who brings water to draw for the people, and his name - according to what the commentators mentioned - was Malik bin Da'r, from the pure Arabs. So he lowered his bucket meaning he sent it, it is said: he lowered his bucket if he sent it to fill it, and he lowered it meaning he took it out: from Al-Asma'i and others. And he lowered - from the same waw - he pulled and brought out, and likewise he lowered if he sent, so when it became heavy they returned it to the ya' because it is lighter than the waw, as the Kufians said. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: When it exceeds three letters, it returns to the letter Ya, following the future tense. The plural of Dalu in the smallest number is Adal, but when it increases, you say Dalī and Dālī, so the Wāw is changed to Ya, except that the plural is subject to change, and to differentiate between the singular and the plural, and also Dalā’. So Yusuf clung to the rope, and when he came out, there was a boy like the moon on a full moon night, the most beautiful of boys. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in the hadith of the Isra’ in Sahih Muslim: And then I saw Yusuf, and he had been given half of beauty. Ka’b al-Ahbar said: Yusuf had a handsome face, curly hair, large eyes, even build, white in color, thick forearms and upper arms, a thin belly, and a small navel. When he smiled, you saw the light from his molars, and when he spoke, you saw in his speech the rays of the sun from his teeth. No one can describe him, and his beauty was like the light of day at night, and he resembled Adam (peace be upon him) on the day God created him and breathed into him from His spirit before he committed the sin. It was said: He inherited this beauty from his grandmother Sarah, and she had been given one-sixth of beauty. When Malik bin Da’r saw him, he said: O my good report, this is a boy. This is the reading of the people of Medina and Basra, except for Ibn Abi Ishaq, who read O my good report, this is a boy and changed the alif to a ya’, because this ya’ breaks what precedes it, so since it is not permissible to break the alif, it was changed as a substitute. The people of Kufa read O my good report without an addition, and there are two opinions about its meaning: One of them is the name of the boy, and the second means: O you who have good report, this is your time and your time. Qatada and al-Suddi said: When the one who was pouring water lowered his bucket, Yusuf clung to it and said: O my good report, this is a boy. Qatada said: He gave his companions good report that he had found a slave. Al-Suddi said: He called a man whose name was Bushra. Al-Nahhas said: Qatada’s statement is more appropriate, because the Qur’an does not mention anyone by name except rarely, and it only comes by euphemism, as God the Almighty said: And the Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands Al-Furqan 27, and he is Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt, and after that: Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend Al-Furqan 28, and he is Umayyah ibn Khalaf, said Al-Nahhas. The meaning of the call to good report is to give good report to those who are present, and it is more emphatic than saying I was given good report, as you say: Oh, how amazing! meaning, Oh, how amazing! This is one of your days and signs, so attend. This is the view of Sibawayh, and Al-Suhayli said the same. It was also said: It is like you say: Oh, how happy! Al-Bushra is a source of good report, and this is more correct, because if it were a proper noun, it would not be added to the pronoun of the speaker. According to this, Bushra would be in the accusative case, because it is a vocative with an addition, and the meaning of the vocative here is to alert, i.e. pay attention to my joy and happiness. According to Al-Suddi, it would be in the nominative case, as you say: O Zaid, this is a boy. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, as you say: O man! And His statement: O regret for the servants (Ya-Sin 36:30). However, Bushra was not given a nunation because it is not declined. And they confided in him merchandise. The ha’ is a metaphor for Joseph, peace be upon him, while the waw is a metaphor for his brothers. It was said: about the merchants who bought him, and it was said: about the newcomer and his companions. Merchandise is in the accusative case as a state. Mujahid said: Malik bin Da'r and his companions, the merchants who were with them in the company, captured him and said to them: He is merchandise that we have taken from some of the people of Ash-Sham or the people of this water to Egypt. They only said this out of fear of partnership. Ibn Abbas said: Joseph's brothers captured him as merchandise when he was extracted from the well. They came and said: What a bad thing you have done! This is a runaway slave of ours. They said to Joseph in Hebrew: Either you acknowledge your slavery to us and we will sell you to these people, or we will take you and kill you. He said: I acknowledge your slavery to you. So he acknowledged it to them and they sold him to them. It was said: Judah advised his brother Joseph in their language: Acknowledge your slavery to your brothers, for I fear that if you do not, they will kill you. So God will make a way out for you and you will escape from being killed. Joseph concealed his affair for fear that his brothers would kill him. Malik said: By God, this is not the characteristic of slaves! They said: He was raised in our lap, and he adopted our morals and was disciplined according to our manners. He said: What do you say, boy? He said: They are right! I was raised in their lap and acquired their morals. Malik said: If you sell it to me, I will buy it from you. So they sold it to him. That is:
12:20: It contains six issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And they sold it. It is said: I bought means I purchased, and I sold means I sold in language. The poet said: I bought a cold one, I wish I was important after the cold one I sold. Another said: When he bought it, his eyes welled up with tears and his chest filled with blame. Hamiz At a low price means a decrease, and here it is a source that is used in place of the noun, meaning they sold him at a low price, meaning a decrease. His brothers did not intend to benefit from his price, but rather they intended to benefit from their father's absence from him. It was said: Judah saw from afar that Joseph was taken out of the well, so he informed his brothers, so they came and sold him to the incoming party. It was also said: No! Rather, they returned to the well after three days to find out the report, and they saw the tracks of the caravan, so they followed them and said: This is our slave who has run away from us, so they sold him to them. Qatada said: Bakhs is injustice. Ad-Dahhak, Muqatil, As-Suddi, and Ibn Ata' said: Bakhs is forbidden. Ibn al-Arabi said: There is no basis for this. Rather, the indication in it is that he did not receive his price at its value, because if his brothers sold him, their intention was not to benefit from his price, but rather their intention was to benefit from their father’s absence from him. And if those who sold him the incoming goods hid it as a deduction, or they said to their companions: Send us merchandise, and they saw that they did not pay a price for it and that what they took from it was all profit. I said: His statement and the indication in it is that he did not receive its price at its value indicates that if they had taken its full value, that would have been permissible, but it is not so. So it indicates the correctness of what al-Suddi and others said, because they made the sale on a person that it is not permissible to sell, so its price was not permissible for them. Ikrimah and al-Sha’bi said: Little. Ibn Hayyan said: False. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas’ud, they sold it for twenty dirhams, each of his brothers took two dirhams, and they were ten. And Qatadah and al-Suddi said the same. And Abu al-Aaliyah and Muqatil said: Twenty-two dirhams, and they were eleven, each of them took two dirhams. And Mujahid said the same. Ikrimah said: Forty dirhams, and what was narrated from the Companions is more appropriate. Andخسis an attribute ofَِن. Dirhams is a substitute and an explanation for it. It is said: dirhams, as the plural of dirham, and it may be a collective noun according to Sibawayh, and it may also be according to him as the extension of the kasra so that it becomes a ya, and this is not like the extension of the maqsur, because the extension of the intended is not permissible according to the Basrans in poetry or otherwise. The grammarians recited: Her hands sweep away the pebbles at every noon, sweeping away the dirhams, and the money changers are led astray. Counted is an adjective, and this indicates that prices were counted and not weighted. It was said: It is an expression of the smallness of the price, because they were dirhams that were not enough to be weighed due to their smallness, and that is because they did not weigh anything that was less than an ounce, which is forty dirhams. Second: Judge Ibn al-Arabi said: The origin of the two currencies is weight. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not sell gold for gold or silver for silver except weight for weight. Whoever increases or is increased has committed usury.” Weight has no benefit except the amount. As for its essence, there is no benefit in it, but counting was done to make it easier for people due to the large number of transactions. Weight is difficult, even if mithqals or dirhams were struck, it would be permissible to sell some of them for others by count if there was no deficiency or preponderance in them. If they decreased, the matter reverted to weight. For this reason, breaking or cutting them is a form of corruption on earth, as mentioned above. Third: The scholars differed on whether dirhams and dinars are designated or not. The narrations on this matter differed from Malik: Ashhab said that it is not designated, which is the apparent meaning of Malik’s statement, and Abu Hanifa said the same. Ibn al-Qasim said that it is designated, and it was narrated from al-Karkhi, and al-Shafi’i said the same. The benefit of the disagreement is that if we say it is not designated, then if he says: I sold you these dinars for these dirhams, the dinars are attached to the responsibility of their owner, and the dirhams are attached to the responsibility of their owner. If they are designated and then lost, nothing is attached to their responsibility, and the contract is void, like the sale of goods and other things. Fourth: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hassan bin Ali, may God be pleased with them both, that he ruled regarding the foundling that he was free, and he recited: And they sold him for a cheap price, for a few dirhams and the statement about it has already been mentioned. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: And they were among those who were ascetic in it. It was said: What is meant are his brothers. It was also said: The travelers. It was also said: The ones who came. In any case, he was not considered stupid by them, not by the brothers, because the aim was his departure from his father, not his money, nor by the travelers because the brothers said that he was a runaway slave from us - and asceticism is a lack of desire - nor by the ones who came because they feared that their companions would share with them, and they saw that a small amount of his price in isolation was better. Sixth: In this verse there is clear evidence of the permissibility of buying a valuable thing for a small price, and the sale is binding. For this reason, Malik said: If he sold a pearl of great value for a dirham and then said, I did not know that it was a pearl and I thought it was a pearl, the sale is binding on him and he did not pay attention to his statement. It was said: And they were among the ascetics of it, meaning of his beauty, because even though God Almighty gave Joseph half of his beauty, He diverted the people’s desires to it from him out of honor for him. It was said: And they were among the ascetics of it, they did not know his status with God Almighty. Sibawayh and Al-Kisa’i narrated: Zahdt and Zahdt with the kasra and fatha of the ha’.
12:21: The Almighty said: And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife, 'Make his stay comfortable.' It was said that buying here means exchanging, since it was not a contract, like: Those are the ones who have purchased error for guidance. (al-Baqarah 2:16). It was also said that they thought it was a purchase, so this wording was used according to the apparent assumption. Ad-Dahhak said: This is the one who was bought by the king of Egypt, and his nickname is Al-Aziz. Al-Suhayli: His name is Qutfir. Ibn Ishaq said: Itfir bin Ruwaihab bought him for his wife Ra'il, mentioned by Al-Mawardi. It was also said that her name was Zulaykha. God had placed the love of Joseph in the heart of Al-Aziz, so he recommended him to his family, mentioned by Al-Qushayri. Al-Tha'labi and others mentioned the two opinions about her name. Ibn Abbas said: Qutfir, the minister of the king of Egypt, bought him, and he is Al-Rayyan bin Al-Walid. It was also said: Al-Walid bin Al-Rayyan, and he is a man from the giants. It was said: He is the Pharaoh of Moses, because Moses said: And Joseph had already come to you with clear proofs (Ghafir 40:34) and that he lived for four hundred years. It was also said: The Pharaoh of Moses was from the sons of the Pharaoh of Joseph, as will be explained in Ghafir. This was the Aziz who bought Joseph from the king’s treasuries, and he bought Joseph from Malik bin Da’ar for twenty dinars, and he added a robe and two sandals to him. It was also said: He bought him from the people of the company. It was also said: They increased his price, and it reached many times his weight in musk, amber, silk, silver, gold, pearls and jewels, the value of which is known only to God, so Qutfir bought him from Malik for this price, as stated by Wahb bin Munabbih. Wahb also said and others: When Malik bin Da’ar bought Joseph from his brothers, he wrote a document between them and him: This is what Malik bin Da’ar bought from the sons of Jacob, who are so-and-so and so-and-so, a slave of theirs for twenty dirhams, and they stipulated that he was a runaway, and that he would not return with him except chained and bound, and he gave them a covenant from God on that. He said: Then Joseph bade them farewell, and began to say: May God protect you, even if you neglect me, and may God help you, and if you abandon me, may God have mercy on you, even if you do not have mercy on me. They said: So the sheep vomited what was in their bellies as fresh blood because of the severity of this farewell, and they carried him on a saddle-saddle without a cover or a cushion, chained, shackled and chained. He passed by the cemetery of the Canaanites and saw his mother’s grave - and lions had been assigned to guard it, but the lions were distracted - so Joseph threw himself on his mother’s grave and began to roll around, embrace the grave and tremble, saying: O mother! Raise your head and you will see your son chained, shackled, chained and shackled. Separate me from my father, so ask God to unite us in the abode of His mercy, for He is the Most Merciful of the merciful. The lions on the camel looked for him but did not see him, so he followed his trace and saw a white spot on a grave. He looked at it and saw that it was him, so he kicked it with his foot in the dirt and rolled it around and beat it severely. The lions said to him: Do not do that! By God, I did not run away nor did I stay, but I passed by my mother's grave and wanted to say goodbye to her, and I will not return to what you hate. Al-Aswad said: By God, you are a bad servant, calling your father one time and your mother another! Why don't your masters do this? He raised his hands to the sky and said: O God, if I have committed a sin with You that has disfigured my face, then I ask You by the right of my fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob to forgive me and have mercy on me. The angels in the sky made a commotion, and Gabriel came down and said to him: O Joseph! Lower your voice, for you have made the angels of the sky cry! Do you want me to turn the earth upside down and turn it upside down? He said: Be steadfast, Gabriel, for God is Forbearing and does not rush. So he struck the earth with his wing and it became dark, the dust rose, the sun was eclipsed, and the caravan remained, not recognizing one another. The leader of the caravan said: Who among you has done something wrong? - I have been traveling for so-and-so and nothing like this has ever happened to me - Al-Aswad said: I slapped that Hebrew boy and he raised his hand to the sky and spoke words I do not know, and I have no doubt that he cursed us, so he said to him: You only wanted our destruction! Bring him to us, so he brought him to him, and he said to him: Boy! He slapped you and what you saw happened to us, so if you want to take revenge, then take revenge on whomever you want, and if you want to forgive, then that is what is expected of you, he said: I have forgiven in the hope that God will forgive me, so the dust cleared, and the sun appeared, and he illuminated the east and west of the earth, and the merchant visited him morning and evening and honored him, until he reached Egypt and washed himself in its Nile and God removed from him the gloom of travel and returned his camels to him, and he entered the city with him during the day and his light shone on the walls, and they put him up for sale and Qutfir, the king’s minister, bought him, as Ibn Abbas said as mentioned above. It was said: This king did not die until he believed and followed Joseph in his religion. Then the king died and Joseph was in charge of the treasuries of the land at that time. Qabus became king after him, and he was an unbeliever. Joseph called him to Islam, but he refused. Honor his abode meaning his home and residence with good food and fine clothing. It is derived from the verb thawa meaning to reside in a place. This has been mentioned previously in Al Imran and elsewhere. Perhaps he will benefit us meaning he will suffice us in some important matters when he reaches maturity. Or we will adopt him as a son Ibn Abbas said: He was chaste and had no children. Ibn Ishaq said the same: Qutayfir did not approach women and had no children. If it is said: How did he say or we will adopt him as a son when he was his property, and sonship and slavery contradict each other? It is said: He frees him and then adopts him as a son through adoption. Adoption was known among nations, and it was the same in the early days of Islam, as will be explained in Al Ahzab, God willing. Abdullah bin Masoud said: The three people with the best insight are the Aziz when he discerned Joseph and said: Perhaps he will benefit us or we will adopt him as a son, and the daughter of Shu'ayb when she said to her father about Moses: Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy (Al Qasas: 26), and Abu Bakr when he appointed Umar as his successor. Ibn al-Arabi said: It is amazing that the commentators agreed on bringing this report! And physiognomy is a strange science, as will be explained in Surat al-Hijr, and it is not so in what they have transmitted, because Abu Bakr appointed Umar as his successor due to his experience in deeds, his constant and long companionship, and his knowledge of what he had witnessed of knowledge and grace from him, and this is not by way of physiognomy. As for the daughter of Shu`ayb, she had with her the clear sign, as will be explained in Al-Qasas. As for the matter of al-`Aziz, it can be considered physiognomy, because he did not have an apparent sign. And God knows best. God the Almighty says: And thus We established Joseph in the land. The Kaf is in the accusative case, meaning, just as We saved him from his brothers and from the well, so also We established him, meaning, We turned the heart of the king who bought him toward him until he was able to command and forbid in the country that the king controlled. And that We might teach him the interpretation of dreams. That is, We did that in confirmation of the words of Jacob: And that He might teach you the interpretation of dreams. (Yusuf 12:6). It was said: The meaning is, We established him so that We might reveal to him words from Us, and teach him their interpretation and explanation, and the interpretation of dreams, and the speech was completed. And God is predominant over His affair. The Ha refers to God the Almighty, meaning, nothing can overcome God, rather He is predominant over His own affair in what He wants to say to it: Be, and it is. It was said: It refers to Yusuf, meaning, God is predominant over Yusuf’s affair, He manages it and protects it and does not leave it to anyone else, so that the plot of a plotter cannot reach it. But most people do not know. That is, they do not know his secret. It was said: What is meant by the majority is everyone, because no one knows the unseen. It was said: It is taken literally, because someone may be informed of some of His unseen. It was said: The meaning but most people do not know is that God is predominant over His affair, and they are the polytheists and those who do not believe in destiny. The wise men said about this verse: And God is predominant over His affair, as Jacob ordered him not to tell his brothers about his dream, but God’s affair prevailed until he told, then his brothers wanted to kill him, but God’s affair prevailed until he became a king and they prostrated before him, then the brothers wanted to leave their father alone, but God’s affair prevailed until their father’s heart became distressed with them, and he remembered them after seventy or eighty years, so he said: Oh, my grief for Joseph (Yusuf 12:84). Then they planned to be righteous people after him, meaning repentant, but God’s affair prevailed until they forgot the sin and persisted in it until they finally confessed before Joseph after seventy years, and they said to their father: Indeed, we were sinners. Then they wanted to deceive their father with crying and the shirt, but God’s affair prevailed so he was not deceived, and he said: Rather, your souls have enticed you to do something then they plotted to remove his love from their father’s heart, but God’s affair prevailed so love and longing increased in his heart, then a woman plotted Aziz said that if she spoke to him, she would overpower him, so God’s command prevailed until Aziz said: “And ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you were among the sinners.” (Yusuf 12:29). Then Yusuf planned to escape from prison by mentioning the cupbearer, but God’s command prevailed and he forgot the cupbearer, and Yusuf remained in prison for several years.
12:22: The Almighty said: And when he reached his prime Ashdahu according to Sibawayh is a plural, singular is shaddah. Al-Kisa’i said: singular is shadd, as the poet said: I remember him during the day, as if he had dyed his head with frankincense and his hair with bone. Abu Ubaid claimed that it has no singular form of the same word among the Arabs, and its meaning is the completion of strength followed by a decrease. Mujahid and Qatadah said: The most severe is thirty-three years. Rabi’ah, Zaid bin Aslam and Malik bin Anas said: The most severe is reaching puberty, and the scholars’ statements on this have already been fully discussed in Surat An-Nisa’ and Surat Al-An’am. We gave him wisdom and knowledge. It was said: We made him the one in control of the ruling, so he ruled in the kingdom’s authority, meaning, We gave him knowledge of the ruling. Mujahid said: The mind is understanding and prophethood. It was also said: Wisdom is prophethood, and knowledge is the knowledge of religion. It was also said: The knowledge of dreams. Whoever said: Prophethood was given to him as a boy said: When he reached his maturity, We increased his understanding and knowledge. Thus do We reward the doers of good. It was said: Those who are patient in adversity, as Joseph was patient, as Ad-Dahhak said. Al-Tabari said: Even though its source is apparent for every doer of good, what is meant by it is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty says: Just as I did this to Joseph after he suffered what he suffered and then gave him what I gave him, thus I will save you from the polytheists of your people who intend to be hostile to you, and I will establish you in the land.
12:23: The Almighty said: And she in whose house he was sought to seduce him She is the wife of Al-Aziz, she asked him to have intercourse with her. The root of seduction is to desire and ask gently and softly. Rawad and riyad are seeking pastures, and it is said that it is from rawid, it is said: So-and-so walks slowly, meaning gently, so seduction is gentleness in seeking, it is said about a man: he sought her for herself, and about a woman she sought him for herself. Rawd is to be patient, it is said: he sought me, give me time. And the doors were closed Closing is for many, and it is not said: the door was closed, and closed is for many and few, as Al-Farazdaq said about Abu Amr bin Al-Ala: I kept closing and opening doors until I came to Abu Amr bin Ammar It is said: It had seven doors that she closed and then invited him to herself. And she said, ‘Heet laka’ meaning, come, approach, and come back. It has no source or inflection. An-Nahhas said: It has seven readings, and the most important of what is in it and the most authentic in chain of transmission is what Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Abu Wa’il who said: I heard Abdullah bin Masoud reciting Heet laka. He said: I said: Some people recite it Heet laka. He said: I only recite as I learned. Abu Ja’far said: And some of them say on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that is not far-fetched, because his saying: I only recite as I learned indicates that it is elevated, and this reading with the opening of the ta’ and the ha’ is the correct reading of Ibn Abbas, Sa’id bin Jubayr, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Ikrimah, and Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’, Asim, Al-A’mash, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i recited it. Abdullah bin Masoud said: Do not interrupt in the Qur’an, for it is like one of you saying: Come and come. Ibn Abi Ishaq the grammarian read qalat hait laka with a fatha on the ha’ and a kasra on the ta’. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami and Ibn Kathir read hayt laka with a fatha on the ha’ and a damma on the ta’. Tarafa said: My people are not the farthest away if a caller from the tribe says: Hit These are three readings with the ha’ open. Abu Ja’far, Shaiba and Nafi’ readومقماَم َمَظت لكwith a kasra on the ha’ and a fatha on the ta’. Yahya ibn Waththab read ومقماَم َمَظت لكwith a kasra on the ha’ followed by a silent ya’ and a damma on the ta’. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ikrimah:ومقماَم ُهتم لكwith a kasra on the ha’ followed by a silent hamza and a damma on the ta’. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Amir and the people of Ash-Sham:ومقماَم ُهتمwith a kasra on the ha’ and a hamza and a fatha on the ta’. Abu Ja’far said:ومقماَم ُهتم لكwith a fatha on the ta’ due to the meeting of two sukoon letters, because it is a sound like mah and sah that should not be declined. The fatha is light because before the ta’ is a ya’ like ayna and kayfa. Whoever breaks the ta’ does so because the original is kasra, because if a sukoon is moved to kasra, and whoever makes a damma it does so because it has the meaning of purpose, i.e. she said: My supplication is for you, so when the addition is deleted, it is based on the damma, like haythu and ba’d. The reading of the people of Medina has two opinions: One of them is that the fat-ha is due to the meeting of two quiescent letters as mentioned above. The other is that it is a verb from the ha’ of yahi’a like ja’a yaji’u, so the meaning in hay’at is that your appearance has improved, and lika is from another statement, as you say: laka ‘ani. And whoever pronounces the hamza and damma on the ta’, it is a verb meaning taihay’at laka, and the same is true for whoever recites hay’at laka. Abu ‘Amr rejected this reading. Abu ‘Ubaidah - Mu’ammar ibn al-Muthanna - said: Abu ‘Amr was asked about the reading of whoever recites with a kasra on the ha’ and a damma on the ta’ with a hamza, so Abu ‘Amr said: It is invalid, he made it from taihay’at! Go and review the Arabs until you reach Yemen. Do you know anyone who says this?! Al-Kisa’i also said: taihay’ has not been narrated from the Arabs. ‘Ikrimah said: taihay’at laka means taihay’at laka, adorned and improved, and it is an unacceptable reading because it was not heard in Arabic. An-Nahhas said: It is good according to the Basrans, because it is said: The ha’ of a man is ha’ and he prepares a form, so the ha’ of yahi’i is like ja’a yaji’ and hay’at is like ja’at. The kasra of the ha’ in hayt is a dialect of some people who prefer the kasra of the ha’ to the fatha of it. Az-Zajjaj said: The best reading is hayt with the fatha of the ha’ and the ta’. Tarafa said: My people are not the farthest away if a caller from the tribe says: Hit With the opening of the ha and the ta. The poet said about Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him: Tell the Commander of the Faithful, the brother of Iraq, if you come Iraq and its people are in your hands, so come on, come on Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said: Hait is a Syriac word that invites him to itself. Al-Suddi said: Its meaning in Coptic is Come to you. Abu Ubaid said: Al-Kisa’i used to say: It is a language of the people of Hawran that was transmitted to the people of Hijaz and means Come. Abu Ubaid said: So I asked a learned sheikh from Hawran and he mentioned that it is their language, and Ikrimah said the same. Mujahid and others said: It is an Arabic language that invites him to itself, and it is a word of urging and turning to things. Al-Jawhari said: It is said Hawat bih or Hayt bih if one shouts at him and calls him. He said: It surprised me that Al-Kari would have been silent if he had been concerned with her. He shouted, and another said: Every young man is motivated by it God the Almighty said: He said, ‘God forbid’ meaning, I seek refuge in God and I seek protection in Him from what you are calling me to. It is a verbal noun, meaning, I seek refuge in God as a refuge. The object is deleted and the verbal noun is made accusative by the deleted verb, and the verbal noun is added to the name of God just as the verbal noun is added to the object, as you say: I passed by Zayd as Amr passes by, meaning as I pass by Amr. He is my Lord means her husband, meaning, he is my master who honored me, so I will not betray him. This was said by Mujahid, Ibn Ishaq, and As-Suddi. Az-Zajjaj said: meaning, God is my Lord who has taken care of me with His kindness, so I will not commit what He has forbidden. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed. In the report, she said to him: O Joseph! How beautiful is the image of your face! He said: In the womb, my Lord shaped me. She said: O Joseph, how beautiful is your hair! He said: It is the first thing to wear out of me in my grave. She said: O Joseph! How beautiful are your eyes? He said: With them I look at my Lord. She said: O Joseph! Lift your eyes and look at my face. He said: I fear blindness in my afterlife. She said: O Joseph! I come near you and you distance yourself from me?! He said: I want to be close to my Lord by that. She said: O Joseph! I have spread out the silk bedding, so come in with me. He said: The cotton does not cover me from my Lord. She said: O Joseph! I have spread out the silk bedding for you, get up and fulfill my need. He said: Then my share of Paradise will be gone, and other words of hers while he was going back to her, until he was about to do something to her. Some of them mentioned that women continued to have lustful inclinations towards Joseph until God informed him, and bestowed upon him the awe of prophethood, so his awe distracted everyone who saw him from his beauty. Scholars differed about his intention, but there is no disagreement that her intention was to disobey, but Joseph was about her.
12:24: Had he not seen the proof of his Lord But when he saw the proof, they would not have intended it, and this is because infallibility is obligatory for the prophets. God the Almighty said: "Thus did We turn away from him evil and immorality. Indeed, he was one of Our chosen servants." So there is an inversion in the speech, meaning had he not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have intended it. Abu Hatim said: I was reading the strange verses of the Qur'an to Abu Ubaidah, and when I came to His statement: And indeed, she intended it and he intended it the verse, Abu Ubaidah said: This is an inversion, meaning that Zulaykha intended to commit the sin but was persistent, and Joseph intended it but did not do what he intended to do, so there is a difference between the two inversions. Al-Harawi mentioned these two statements in his book. Jamil said: I thought of them from Buthaina, if it appeared, it would cure the burning passion in my heart last: I intended to do it but did not, and I almost did. I wish I had left Uthman's wives crying over him. This is all a thought without determination. It was said: He intended to marry her. It was also said: He intended to hit her, meaning to beat her and repel her from himself, and the proof is his refraining from hitting her, because if he had hit her, he would have thought that he intended to do something forbidden to her, so she refused, so he hit her. It was said: Joseph’s intention was a sin, and that he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, and this is what most of the commentators and their general public agreed with, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr, Ibn Al-Anbari, Al-Nahhas, Al-Mawardi and others. Ibn Abbas said: He untied the belt and sat with her as a circumcised person would. And from him: She lay on her back and he sat between her legs, taking off his clothes. Saeed bin Jubair said: He loosened the button of his trousers. Mujahid said: He untied his trousers until he reached the buttocks, and he sat with her as a man sits with his wife. Ibn Abbas said: When he said: That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret (Yusuf 12:52), Gabriel said to him: Not even when you intended to do it, O Joseph? Then he said: And I do not acquit myself (Yusuf 12:53). They said: And turning away in such a situation indicates sincerity, and is greater for the reward. I said: This was the reason for God’s praise of Dhul-Kifl, as will be explained in S~, God willing. The answer to if only is omitted, meaning if only he had not seen the proof of his Lord, he would have carried out what he intended to do. Similar to it is: No! If only you knew with certainty (al-Takathur 102:5). The answer to it is: Why do you compete? Ibn Atiyyah said: This statement was narrated from Ibn Abbas and a group of the Salaf, and they said: The wisdom in that is to be an example for sinners so that they may see that their repentance returns to the pardon of God Almighty, as it returned to those who were better than them, and were not destroyed by closeness to sin. All of this is based on the fact that Joseph’s intention reached, according to what this group narrated, that he sat between Zulaykha’s feet and began to untie his clothes and his cloak and the like, and she had lied down for him, as At-Tabari narrated. Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam said: Ibn Abbas and those after him do not differ that he intended it, and they are more knowledgeable about God and the interpretation of His Book, and they have greater respect for the prophets than to speak about them without knowledge. Al-Hasan said: God the Almighty did not mention the sins of the prophets to reproach them for them, but He mentioned them so that you would not despair of the error. Al-Ghaznawi said: Although the slip of the prophets has a ruling: increased fear, intense shyness with shame, abandonment of the wonder of work, enjoyment of the blessing of forgiveness after hope, and their being leaders of hope for those who make mistakes. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: Some people said that a worry occurred to Joseph, and that worry was a natural movement without determination to decide on the action, and what was of this kind is not held against the servant, and it may occur to a person’s heart while he is fasting to drink cold water, and eat delicious food, but if he does not eat or drink, and does not make up his mind to eat and drink, he is not held accountable for what crossed his mind, and the proof is that he diverted him from this worry until it did not become a determined resolve. I said: This is a good statement, and among those who said it is Al-Hasan: Ibn Atiyyah said: What I say about this verse is that it is not correct that Joseph was a prophet at the time of this calamity, nor is it supported by any narration. If that is the case, then he is a believer who has been given wisdom and knowledge, and it is permissible for him to have a worry, which is wanting something without doing it, and to have a bad thought, despite the sin in that. If we assume that he was a prophet at that time, then in my opinion, nothing is permissible for him except a worry, which is a thought, and nothing of what was mentioned about solving his problem and the like is correct for him, because infallibility is with prophethood. And what was narrated that it was said to him: You will be in the register of prophets and you will do the deeds of fools then its meaning is the promise of prophethood later. I said: What he mentioned of this detail is correct, but the Almighty’s saying: And We revealed to him indicates that he was a prophet according to what we mentioned, and it is the saying of a group of scholars. If he was a prophet, then all that remains is that the concern he had was something that crossed the mind and did not remain in the chest, and it is that for which God lifted the accountability from the creation, since the one charged with it has no ability to repel it. And his saying: And I do not acquit myself - if it was from the words of Joseph - means from this concern, or it was from him by way of humility and admission, because the soul contradicted what he was purified with before and was innocent. And God the Almighty informed about the state of Joseph from the time of his maturity, saying: And when he reached his full strength, We gave him wisdom and knowledge according to what was explained above, and the report of God the Almighty is true, and His description is correct, and His words are true, for Joseph acted according to what God taught him of the prohibition of adultery and its preliminaries, and the betrayal of the master, neighbor, and stranger in his family, so he did not approach the wife of the Aziz, nor did he respond to the advances, but rather he turned away from her and fled from her, a wisdom that was specific to him, and an action in accordance with what God taught him. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The angels said: ‘O Lord, this is your servant who intends to do a bad deed, and You are All-Knowing about him. ’ He said: ‘Watch him. If he does it, write it down for him as a similar one. But if he refrains from it, write it down as a good deed for him. He only refrained from it because of My sake. ’” And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, informing about his Lord: If My servant intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, it is written down as a good deed. So if what the servant intends to do is a bad deed, it is written down for him as a good deed for refraining from it, so there is no sin. And in Sahih Muslim: God has forgiven my nation for what their souls have thought of, as long as they do not do it or speak of it. And it has been mentioned before. Ibn al-Arabi said: In the City of Peace, there was an imam from the imams of Sufism - and what an imam - known as Ibn Ata! He spoke one day about Yusuf and his story, until he mentioned his innocence from what was attributed to him of evil. Then a man stood up from the back of his gathering, and he was full of people from every sect, and said: O Sheikh! O our master! So, what did Yusuf intend and what happened? He said: Yes! Because care is from there. Look at the sweetness of the scholar and the learner, and look at the astuteness of the layman in his question, and the answer of the scholar in its brevity and completeness. Therefore, the Sufi scholars said: The benefit of His saying: And when he reached his full strength, We gave him wisdom and knowledge is that He gave him that during the period of the dominance of desire so that it would be a reason for him to be protected. I said: If his infallibility and innocence are established by the praise of God the Almighty for him, then what Mus`ab bin `Uthman said is not correct: Sulayman bin Yasar was one of the most handsome people in appearance, and a woman longed for him and tempted him, but he refused her and mentioned it to her, so she said: If you do not do it, I will make you famous. So he went out and left her, and he saw in his dream Joseph the Truthful, peace be upon him, sitting, and he said: Are you Joseph? He said: I am Joseph who was tempted, and you are Solomon who was not tempted?! This requires that the degree of sainthood be higher than the degree of prophethood, and this is impossible. If we assumed that Joseph was not a prophet, then his degree would be sainthood, and he would be preserved as he was. If the doors were closed to Solomon, and he was reviewed in the speech and address, and the talk and answer with a long companionship, then he would fear temptation and a great trial, and God knows best. God the Almighty says: Had he not seen the proof of his Lord that is in the nominative case, meaning had he not seen the proof of his Lord, and the answer is omitted for the listener’s knowledge, meaning that what happened would have happened. This proof is not mentioned in the Qur’an. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that Zulaykha went to an idol crowned with pearls and rubies in the corner of the house and covered it with a garment. He said: What are you doing? She said: I am ashamed before my God that He sees me in this form. Joseph said: I am more deserving of being ashamed before God. This is the best thing that has been said about it, because it establishes evidence. It was also said: He saw written on the ceiling of the house: “And do not come near to adultery. Indeed, it is ever an immorality and an evil way.” (al-Isra’ 17:32). Ibn Abbas said: A hand appeared on which was written: And indeed, over you are guardians. (al-Infitar 82:10). Some people said: Remember God’s covenant and pledge. It was also said: He was called, O Joseph! You are written in the register of the prophets and you are doing the work of fools?! It was said: He saw the image of Jacob on the walls, biting his fingertip threatening him, so he calmed down, and his lust came out of his fingers. This was said by Qatada, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Salih, and Saeed bin Jubair. Al-A’mash narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: He untied his trousers, and Jacob appeared to him, and said to him: O Joseph! So he turned and fled. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: Jacob appeared to him, so he struck his chest, and his lust came out of his fingers. Mujahid said: So each of Jacob’s sons had twelve male children, except for Joseph, who had only two boys, and his children were reduced because of that lust. Other than this was said. In short: This proof is a sign from the signs of God that God showed Joseph until his faith was strengthened and he refrained from sinning. God the Almighty says: Thus did We turn away from him evil and immorality. The kaf of thus may be in the nominative case, so that it is the predicate of a deleted subject, the meaning is: the proofs are like this, and it may be an adjective for a deleted source, meaning We showed him the proofs by seeing them like this. Evil is lust, and immorality is direct contact. It was said: evil is bad praise, and immorality is adultery. It was said: evil is the betrayal of its owner, and immorality is committing an immorality. It was said: evil is the punishment of the Almighty King. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read al-Mukhlisin with a kasra on the lam, and its interpretation is those who were sincere in obeying God. The rest read with a fatha on the lam, and its interpretation is: those whom God made sincere to His message. Joseph, peace be upon him, had these two qualities, because he was sincere in obeying God the Almighty, sincere in the message of God the Almighty.
12:25: God Almighty said: And they raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back. There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And they raced to the door. The scholars said: This is from the abbreviation of the miraculous Qur’an in which meanings come together. That is because when he saw the proof of his Lord, he fled from her and they fought one another. She was to bring him back to herself, and he was to flee from her. So she caught up with him before he came out. And she tore his shirt from behind. That is, from behind. She grabbed the top of his shirt and tore the shirt at the collar, and the tear went down to the bottom of the shirt. Racing is seeking to be the first to something, and from it comes the word sabaqa. And qad means cutting, and it is most often used for something that is long. Al-Nabigha said: The double-weave Saluki advances and the fire of the hummingbirds is kindled in the sheets. The word qat with a ta is used for something that is incidental. Al-Mufaddal ibn Harb said: I read in Musahaq Fal-ma’a shar’uhu qamis tu’ta min dabar meaning it was torn. Ya’qub said: At is a tear in intact skin or intact clothing. The alif was deleted from istabqa in pronunciation because it is sukun and the lam after it is sukun, as you say: ja’ani ‘Abdullah in the dual. Some Arabs say: ja’ani ‘Abdullah with an alif without a hamza, combining two sukun because the second is assimilated and the first is a long and soft letter. Some of them say: Abdullah with an alif and a hamza, as you say when stopping. Second: The verse contains evidence of analogy and consideration, and working according to custom and habit, because it mentions that the shirt is torn from the front and the back, and this is something that the Malikis have mentioned alone in their books, and that is that if the shirt is pulled from behind, it is torn from that side, and if it is pulled from the front, it is torn from that side, and this is the most common. God the Almighty said: And they found her master at the door. That is, they found the noble one at the door. By master, he meant the husband, and the Copts call the husband master. It is said: he found him, he encountered him, he got him into trouble, he got into trouble, and he got into trouble, all of which have the same meaning. So when she saw her husband, she sought a way to trick him and almost did so. “She said: What is the recompense for one who intended evil for your family?” That is, adultery. Except that he be imprisoned or a painful punishment. She says: He is beaten a painful beating. What is the recompense is the subject, and its predicate is that he be imprisoned. “Or punishment” is in apposition to the position of that he be imprisoned because the meaning is: except imprisonment. And it is permissible to say or a painful punishment meaning: or he is punished painfully, as Al-Kisa’i said.
12:26: God Almighty said: He said, ‘She sought to seduce me,’ and a witness from among her family testified. There are three issues: First: The scholars said: When she cleared herself, and she was not sincere in her love for him - because it is the nature of the lover to prefer the beloved - he said: She tried to seduce me. Joseph spoke the truth in response to her slander and lie to him. Nawf al-Shami and others said: It is as if Joseph, peace be upon him, did not reveal the matter, so when it reached him, he became angry and said the truth. The second: And a witness from among her people testified, because when they disagreed in their statement, the king needed a witness to know who was telling the truth and who was lying. So a witness from among her people testified, that is, a judge from among her people ruled, because it was a ruling from him and not a testimony. There are four opinions regarding this witness: The first: that he was a child in the cradle who spoke. Al-Suhayli said: This is correct, because of the hadith reported about it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is his saying: None spoke in the cradle except three, and he mentioned among them the witness of Joseph. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: It was said about him: He was a child in the cradle in the house and he was her maternal cousin. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Four spoke when they were young, and he mentioned among them the witness of Joseph. This is an opinion. The second: That the witness is the shirt, narrated by Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, and it is a correct metaphor from the linguistic perspective, because the language of action is more eloquent than the language of speech, and the Arabs sometimes attribute speech to inanimate objects and describe them with their attributes, and that is common in their poetry and speech, and among the sweetest of it is the saying of some of them: A wall said to the peg, why did you split me? It said to him: Ask someone who will crush me. However, the saying of God the Most High after of its people invalidates the possibility that it is the shirt. The third: That it is a creation of God the Most High, not of a human or a jinn, as Mujahid also said, and this is refuted by the saying of God the Most High: of its people. Fourth: He was a wise and intelligent man whom the minister consulted in his affairs. He was among the woman’s people and was with her husband. He said: I heard the turning away and the commotion from behind the door, and the tearing of the shirt. It is not known which of you was in front of the other. If the tearing of the shirt was from the front, then you are telling the truth, and if it was from behind, then he is telling the truth. So they looked at the shirt and saw that it was torn from the back. This is the statement of Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid, and As-Suddi. As-Suddi said: He was her cousin. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and it is the correct statement in this regard, and God knows best.
