It was narrated from Ibn Abbas - narrated from him by Isra’il from Samak from Ikrimah - that he said: He was a man with a beard. Sufyan said from Jabir from Ibn Abi Malekah from Ibn Abbas that he said: He was one of the king’s special people. Ikrimah said: He was not a boy, but he was a wise man. Sufyan narrated from Mansour from Mujahid that he said: He was a man. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: What is more likely to be the meaning - and God knows best - is that he was a wise, rational man whom the king consulted and he came up with this evidence. If he had been a child, his testimony for Joseph, peace be upon him, would have sufficed for him to come up with evidence from custom, because the speech of a child is a miraculous sign, so it would have been clearer than reasoning from custom. This is not contrary to the hadith Four spoke while they were young, including Joseph’s companion. The meaning would be: young, not old. There is another evidence for this, which is that Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, narrated the hadith from the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the narration from him has been transmitted in succession that Joseph’s companion was not a boy. I said: It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Ibn Jubayr, Hilal bin Yasaaf, and Ad-Dahhak that he was a boy in the cradle. However, if he had been a boy who spoke, the evidence would have been his own words, without the need to use the shirt as evidence. That would have been a breach of custom and a type of miracle, and God is more general. And we will come to those boys who spoke in the cradle in Surat Al-Buruj, God willing. Third: If we assume that the witness is a young child, then there is no indication in that to act on signs as we mentioned. If he is a man, then it is valid for him to be an argument for ruling by the sign in the case of lost property and many other situations. Malik even said about thieves: If you find goods with them and people come and claim them, and they do not have evidence, then the ruler will blame them for that. If no one else comes, then he will give it to them. Muhammad said about household goods if a man and a woman disagree about them: What is for the men is for the man, what is for the women is for the woman, and what is for the man and the woman is for the man. Shuraih and Iyas bin Muawiyah used to work on signs in governments, and the origin of that is this verse, and God knows best.
12:27: The Almighty’s saying: If his shirt was torn from before “was” is in the position of a conditional imperative, and there is something grammatically problematic about it, because the letters of the condition refer the past to the future, and this is not the case with was. So Al-Mubarrad Muhammad bin Yazid said: This is due to the strength of was, and that it expresses all actions. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is if it was, that is, if he knew, and knowledge did not occur, and so does being because it conveys knowledge. Was torn from before is a predicate of was with the past tense verb, as Zuhair said: He had turned his back on the one who was hiding, but he neither showed her nor advanced her. Yahya bin Ya'mar and Ibn Abi Ishaq read min qabl with a damma on the qaf, the ba' and the lam, and likewise dabar. Al-Zajjaj said: He makes them two ends like qabl and ba'd, as if it were wa-'ad, as if he said: min qabluhu wa min dabarhu. So when the noun was deleted - which is what is intended - the noun became its end after the noun was its end. It is permissible to read min qabl and min dabar with a fatha on the ra' and the lam, likening it to something that is not declined, because it is definite and has been removed from its category. Mahbub narrated on the authority of Abu Amr min qabl and min dabar as light and genitive.
12:28: The Almighty said: And when he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said, 'Indeed, it is from your plot.' It was said that the noble one said that to her when she said: What is the reward of one who intended evil for your family? And it was said that the witness said it to her. Plotting means deceit and trickery, and it was mentioned previously in Al-Anfal. Indeed, your plot is great. And he said great because of the greatness of their temptation and their trickery in escaping their predicament. Muqatil said on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The plotting of women is greater than the plotting of Satan because God, the Almighty, says: "Indeed, the plot of Satan has ever been weak." (al-Nisa 4:76) And He said: Indeed, your plotting is great."
12:29: The Almighty said: Joseph, turn away from this The one who said this is the witness. And Joseph is a singular address, meaning O Joseph, so it was deleted. Turn away from this meaning do not mention it to anyone and keep it secret. Then he turned to her and said: And you And ask forgiveness for your sin He said: Ask forgiveness for your husband for your sin so that he does not punish you. Indeed, you were among the sinners He did not say among the sinful women because he intended to inform about the masculine and feminine, so the masculine prevailed, and the meaning is: among the sinful people, or among the sinful people, like: Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people (al-Naml 27:43) And she was among the obedient (al-Tahrim 66:12). It was said: The one who said to Joseph turn away and to her ask forgiveness was her husband, the king, and there are two opinions on this: One of them: He was not jealous, so he was calm. And the lack of jealousy is found in many of the people of Egypt. Second: God Almighty took away his jealousy and he was kind to Joseph until he was relieved of his anger and forgave her.
12:30: The Almighty said: And women in the city said It is said: women with a damma on the noon, and this is the reading of Al-A'mash, Al-Mufaddal and Al-Salami, and the plural is women. It is also permissible to say: And women said, and women said, like the Bedouins said and the Bedouins said, and that is because the story spread among the people of Egypt and the women talked. It was said: The wife of the cupbearer of the Aziz, and the wife of his baker, and the wife of the owner of his animals, and the wife of the owner of his prison. It was said: The wife of the chamberlain, on the authority of Ibn Abbas and others. She seduced her young man The young man in the speech of the Arabs is the young man, and the woman is a young girl. He has overcome her with love It was said: He has overcome her. It was said: His love has entered her pericardium, on the authority of Mujahid and others. Amr bin Dinar narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: He entered under her pericardium. Al-Hasan said: Passion is the interior of the heart. Al-Suddi and Abu Ubaid: The pericardium of the heart is its covering, and it is its skin. It was said: It is the middle of the heart, and the meaning in these sayings is close, and the meaning is: His love reached her core and overcame it. Al-Nabigha said: They prevented it from entering the pericardium, which the fingers sought. It has been said that pericarditis is a disease, and Al-Asma’i recited the following verse by the rajaz poet: He follows her and she is passionate about him Abu Jaafar bin Muhammad, Ibn Muhaisin and Al-Hasan read Shafaha with an unvoiced ‘ayn. Ibn Al-A’rabi said: Its meaning is that his love burned her heart. He said: The first is the action. Al-Jawhari said: Love made him sick. Abu Zaid said: It made him sick. He was madly in love with such-and-such, so he is madly in love. Al-Hasan read Qad Shafaha and said: Her stomach is filled with love. Al-Nahhas said: Its meaning according to most linguists is that he has gone astray with it, because the tops of mountains are their heights, and he was madly infatuated with that with a sukoon on the ghayn, except that Abu Ubaidah recited the verse of Imru’ Al-Qais: To kill me, and her heart was filled with passion, as a happy woman is filled with passion for a handsome man He said: So the pain of love and its essence were likened to that. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Sha’bi that he said: Al-Shaghaf with the voiced ghayn is love, and Al-Sha’af with the unvoiced ‘ayn is madness. Al-Nahhas said: It was narrated qad shaghafaha with the kasra of the ghayn, and nothing is known in the speech of the Arabs except shaghafaha with the fatha of the ghayn, and likewise sha’faha meaning he left her ardent. Saeed bin Abi Arubah said on the authority of Al-Hasan: The pericardium is the veil of the heart, and the sha’af is the blackness of the heart, so if love reached the sha’af, she would die. Al-Hasan said: It is said that the pericardium is the skin attached to the heart that cannot be seen, and it is the white skin, so his love stuck to her heart like the skin sticks to the heart. God the Almighty said: Indeed, we see her in manifest error, meaning in this action. Qatada said: Her young man is her husband’s young man, because Joseph was considered a slave among them, and he would carry out her orders regarding him. Muqatil said on the authority of Abu Uthman al-Nahdi on the authority of Salman al-Farsi, who said: The wife of al-Aziz asked her husband Joseph for a gift, so he gave him to her and said: What will you do with him? She said: Should I take him as a son? He said: He is yours. So she raised him until he reached maturity, and she felt for him what she felt for herself. She would uncover herself for him, adorn herself, and call upon him out of kindness, but God protected him.
12:31: The Almighty said: So when she heard of their plot meaning their backbiting of her and their trickery in slandering her. It was said: She informed them and sought their trust, so they divulged her secret, so this was called a plot. His saying: She sent to them is an omission in the speech, meaning she sent to them inviting them to a feast to make them fall into what she had fallen into. Mujahid said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The wife of Al-Aziz said to her husband: I want to prepare food and invite these women, so he said to her: Do so, so she prepared food, then she furnished the houses for them, Najdat means decorated, and Najd is what a house is furnished with from furnishings, meaning it is decorated, and the plural is Najood on the authority of Abu Ubaid, and tanjid is decoration, and she sent to them to bring her food, and that none of you from those whom she had named should stay behind. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: They were forty women and they came against their will, and Umayyah ibn Abi Al-Salt said about them: Until they came to her by force and she prepared for them tables and kebabs. It is narrated: Patterns. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: So they came and took their seats. And I prepared for them a reclining place meaning I prepared for them seats for them to recline on. Ibn Jubayr said: In every seat there was a cup of honey, a citron, and a sharp knife. Mujahid and Saeed ibn Jubayr read: a reclining place without a hamza, and the citron is the mutak in the Coptic language, and Mujahid interpreted it in the same way. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid who said: The reclining place is the food, and the mutak without a hamza is the citron, and the poet said: We drink sin openly, and you see the incense among us borrowed. Azd Shanu'a may say: the citron is the matka. Al-Jawhari said: the matka is what the circumciser leaves. The origin of the matka is the zamāward. And the matka is for women who did not circumcise. Al-Farra' said: A sheikh from the trustworthy people of Basra told me that the matka is shortened to the zamāward. Some of them said: it is the citron, as narrated by Al-Akhfash. Ibn Zayd: citron and honey that is eaten with it, the poet said: We remained in comfort, reclined, and drank lawful water from its wells. We ate. An-Nahhas: The Almighty said: And I prepared in the equipment, which is everything that you make as a preparation for something. A recliner The most correct thing that has been said about it is what Ali bin Abi Talha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A sitting place. As for the statement of a group of the people of interpretation that it is food, it is permissible on the assumption: food for a recliner, like: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82), and the evidence for this deletion is And each one of them was brought a knife because the presence of women with knives with them is only for food that is cut with knives, this is what he said in his book I’rab al-Quran. And he said in his book Ma’ani al-Quran: And Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatada, who said: The recliner is food. And it was said: The recliner is everything that one reclines on when eating, drinking, or talking, and this is what is known among the people of language, except that the narrations have been authenticated with that. Al-Qatabi narrated that it is said: We reclined at so-and-so’s place, meaning we ate. The root of reclined is reclined. The same applies to balanced and transitive, because it is from wazana, “wa’adat,” and waka’at. It is also said: reclined, “reclined,” reclined, “reclined.” Every one of them is a knife, are two objects. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ narrated that the knife is masculine and feminine. Al-Farra’ recited: He stabbed the hump the next day with a sharp knife. Al-Jawhari: It is mostly used in the masculine form. He said: He seems to be an advisor, but when he is alone, he is a sharp knife to the throat. Al-Asma'i: The word knife is only known as a masculine form. God the Almighty said: And she said, ‘Go out to them’ with a damma on the ta’ because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, because the kasra is heavy if it is followed by a damma, and the ta’ was broken according to the original. It was said that she said to them: Do not cut or eat until I teach you, then she said to her servant: If I tell you to call for me El, call for Joseph. El was an idol that they used to worship, and Joseph, peace be upon him, was working in clay, and he had tied his apron and rolled up his sleeves, so she said to the servant: Call for me El, meaning call for the Lord, and El in Hebrew means the Lord. He said: The women were amazed and said: How can he come! So the servant went up and called for Joseph, and when he came down she said to them: Cut up what you have with you. And when they saw him, they glorified him and cut their hands with knives until the knives reached the bone, said Wahb ibn Munabbih. Sa`id ibn Jubayr: He did not come out to them until he had adorned himself. Then he came out to them suddenly, and they were astonished at him and were perplexed by the beauty of his face and his adornment and what was on him. So they began to cut their hands, and they thought that they were cutting citrons. There is a difference of opinion about the meaning of akbarnahu. Juwaybir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas: they venerated him and feared him. And also on his authority, they were secure and amazed from astonishment. And the poet said: If they see the stallion from above the continent, they neigh and exaggerate the gushing semen. Ibn Sam'an said on the authority of several of his companions: They said, We were infatuated with him, and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: We loved him until ten of them died in that gathering from astonishment, bewilderment, and passion for Joseph. It was said: Its meaning is an embrace of astonishment, as said by Qatada, Muqatil, and al-Suddi. The poet said: We come to women when they are pure, but we do not come to women when they are very old. Abu Ubaidah and others denied this and said: That is not in the speech of the Arabs, but it is possible that it is a hug from the intensity of their reverence for it, and a woman may be frightened and miscarry her child or menstruate. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said akbarnahu but not hadnahu so ikbar does not mean menstruation. Al-Azhari responded by saying: It is possible that akbartu means hadat, because when a woman menstruates at the beginning, she moves from the realm of childhood to adulthood. He said: The ha in akbarnahu may be the ha of stopping and not the ha of pronoun, and this is false, because the ha of stopping is dropped in the description. More exemplary than that is the statement of Ibn al-Anbari: The ha is a pronoun for the source of the verb, meaning akbarna ikbaran, meaning hadan of menstruation. According to the first statement of Ibn Abbas, the ha refers back to Joseph, meaning they revered Joseph and honored him. God the Almighty said: And cut off their hands. Mujahid said: They cut them off until they threw them away. It was also said: They scratched them. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: A cut with a knife. An-Nahhas said: Mujahid means that it is not a cut from which the hand is revealed, rather it is a scratch and a cut, and this is well-known in the language that it is said that if a person scratches his companion’s hand, he cuts off his hand. Ikrimah said: Their hands are their sleeves, and there is some ambiguity in this. It was also said: Their fingers, meaning they did not feel pain in the cutting and wounding, meaning because their hearts were occupied with Joseph, and the cutting refers to the large number, so the large number could be attributed to one person whose hand was wounded in several places, or it could be attributed to their number. God the Almighty said: And they said, ‘God forbid’ meaning, God forbid. Al-Asma’i narrated on the authority of Nafi’ that he read as Abu Omar bin Al-Ala’ read: And they said, ‘God forbid’ with the alif, which is the original. Whoever deletes it replaces the lam in God. There are four languages for it. It is said: Hashaka except for you, “Hasha la... and “Hasha Zayd” except for Zayd. Al-Nahhas said: I heard Ali bin Sulayman say, ‘I heard Muhammad bin Yazid say,’ the accusative is more appropriate, because it has been confirmed that it is a verb for their saying “Hasha la Zayd except for Zayd, and the letter is not deleted from it. Al-Nabigha said: I do not spare anyone from the people Some of them said: Haash is a letter, and ahashi is a verb. The fact that hasha is a verb is indicated by the occurrence of a preposition after it. Abu Zaid narrated from an Arab: O God, forgive me and whoever hears, hasha al-Shaytan and Abu al-Asbagh, so he put it in the accusative case. Al-Hasan read And they said hasha lillah with a sukoon on the shin, and from him also haash al-ilah. Ibn Masoud and Abi: haash God without lam, and from it is the saying of the poet: Except for Abu Thawban, he is reluctant to be rude or insulting. Al-Zajjaj said: The origin of the word is from the margin, and the margin means the side. You say: We were in the margin of so-and-so, meaning on his side. So your saying: Zaid's distance from this means Zaid moved away from this and stayed away from it. The exception is the exclusion and distancing from the group mentioned. Abu Ali said: It is an active participle from the margin, meaning Joseph was excluded and he became on the margin and side of what he was disgusted by, or from being a human being. So, in the exception, the letter of preposition is Haasha according to Sibawayh, and according to what Al-Mubarrad and Abu Ali said, it is a verb. God the Almighty said: Ma hada basharan Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: ma is like laysa, you say: Laisa Zaid is not standing, and ma hada basharan and ma hunna umahum their mothers (Al-Mujadilah: 2). The Kufians said: When the ba’ was deleted, it was placed in the accusative case. The explanation of this - according to what Ahmad ibn Yahya said - is that if you say: Ma Zaid is not departing, then the position of the ba’ is in the accusative case, and so are all the letters of genitive case. When the ba’ was deleted, it was placed in the accusative case to indicate its position. He said: This is what Al-Farraa said. He said: ma did not work at all, so the Basrans forced them to say: Zaid is the moon, because the meaning is like the moon! Ahmad ibn Yahya responded by saying: The ba’ is more included in the letters of genitive case than the kaf, because the kaf can be a noun. Al-Nahhas said: Only the statement of the Basrans is correct, and this statement contradicts itself, because Al-Farraa explicitly permitted Ma bi bnalaq Zaid, and he recited: By God, if you were free, you would not be free, nor would you be a free man. The text forbade the accusative case, and we do not know of any difference of opinion among grammarians that it is permissible: Ma fika Raghib Zayd, wa ma ilaika bi-qasid Amr, then they delete the ba’ and raise it. The Basrans and Kufians reported that Ma Zayd is leaving in the nominative case, and the Basrans reported that it is the language of Tamim, and they recited: You make me a rival, while I have no rival to one of noble lineage. Al-Nad, Al-Nadeed, and Al-Nadeeda are the same as the equivalent and the counterpart. Al-Kisa’i said that it is the language of Tihama and Najd. Al-Farra’ claimed that the nominative case is the stronger of the two forms. Abu Ishaq said: This is wrong. The Book of God Almighty and the language of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are stronger and more appropriate. I said: In the Mushaf of Hafsa may God be pleased with her it is this is not a human being mentioned by Al-Ghaznawi. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: The women mentioned that the form of Joseph is more beautiful than the form of humans, rather he is in the form of an angel, and God the Most High said: Indeed, We created man in the best of stature (al-Tin 95:4). The combination between the two verses is that their saying: God forbid is an acquittal of Joseph from what the wife of Al-Aziz accused him of in terms of seduction, meaning that Joseph was far from this, and their saying: for God means for fear of Him, meaning God is innocent of this, meaning that Joseph was saved from that, so this has nothing to do with the form, and the meaning is that it is like the angels in acquittal from sins, so based on this there is no contradiction. It was said: What is meant is his being exonerated from resembling humans in form, due to his extreme beauty. His saying: for God is an emphasis on this meaning, so based on this meaning the women said that thinking that the form of the angel is more beautiful, and they did not hear the saying of God the Most High: Indeed, We created man in the best of stature (al-Tin 95:4), for it is from Our Book. Some of the weak people thought that if this statement was a false assumption on their part, then it would be obligatory for God to respond to them and expose their lie. This is false, because there is no obligation on God Almighty, and not everything that God Almighty informs about the disbelief of the disbelievers and the lies of the liars must be accompanied by a response. Also, people of custom may say about the ugly, It is as if he were a devil, and about the beautiful, It is as if he were an angel, meaning that no one has seen the like of him, because people do not see angels. So it is based on a suspicion that the image of the angel is better, or on the report of the purity of his morals and his distance from accusations. This is nothing but an angel, meaning this is nothing but an angel. The poet said: I am not for my people, but for an angel who descends from the sky and aims It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan: Ma hatha bashara with a kasra on the ba’ and the shin, meaning this is not a purchased slave, meaning something like this should not be sold, so the source was placed in the place of the passive participle, as he said: Lawful to you is the game of the sea (al-Ma’idah 5:96), meaning its catch, and there are many similar examples. It is possible that the meaning is: this is not a price, meaning something like it is not priced or valued, so what is meant by buying at this price is the price at which it was bought. Like your saying: this is not for a thousand if you negate the statement of the speaker: this is for a thousand. So the ba’ in this case is related to something omitted which is the predicate, as if he said: this is not estimated to be bought. The reading of the common people is more similar, because after it this is nothing but a noble angel is an exaggeration in his superiority in the genus of angels, magnifying his status, and because something like bashara is written in the Qur’an with a ya’.
12:32: The Almighty said: She said, 'That is what you blamed me for.' When she saw their infatuation with Joseph, she showed her excuse by saying: You blamed me for it, meaning with his love, and that means this, and this is the choice of Al-Tabari. It was said: The ha' is for love, and that is in its place, and the meaning is: That is the love for which you blamed me, meaning this love is that love. And blame is the description of something ugly. Then she confessed and said: And I did try to seduce him, but he held fast, meaning he refused. And protection is called protection because it prevents one from committing a sin. It was said: held fast means he resisted, and the meaning is the same. And if he does not do what I command him, he will be imprisoned. She tried to seduce him again in the presence of them, and she tore off the veil of modesty, and promised to imprison him if he did not do it. She only did this when she did not fear blame or a statement contrary to her first command, since it was between him and her. And that they may be among the humiliated meaning the humiliated. The Mushaf writesواليهوًراwith an alif and it is read with a light noon for emphasis. The noon of emphasis is heavy and light. The pause is on his sayingلجسجنننwith a noon because it is heavy, and on لُهوًراwith an alif because it is light. It is similar to the noon of i'rab in your saying: I saw a man, Zaid, and Amr. And similar to it is his saying: We will seize by the forelock (Al-'Alaq: 15) and similar to it. The pause is on it with an alif, like the saying of Al-A'sha: Do not worship Satan, but worship God. That is, he wanted to worship, so when he stopped at it, the stop was with the alif.
12:33: The Almighty said: He said, 'My Lord, prison is more to my liking than that to which they invite me.' That is, entering prison, so the complement was omitted, as stated by Al-Zajjaj and Al-Nahhas. (More to my liking) means easier and lighter for me than standing in sin, not that entering prison is something that is truly loved. It was narrated that when Joseph, peace be upon him, said: Prison is more to my liking, God revealed to him O Joseph! You have imprisoned yourself since you said prison is more to my liking, and if you had said well-being is more to my liking, I would have been well. Abu Hatim narrated that Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, read: prison with the opening of the seen, and he narrated that this was the reading of Ibn Abi Ishaq, Abd Al-Rahman Al-A'raj, and Ya'qub, and it is the source of his imprisonment as a prison. And if You do not turn away from me their plotting That is, the plotting of women. It was said: The plotting of the women who saw him? For they ordered him to obey the wife of Al-Aziz, and they said to him: She is wronged and you have wronged her. It was said: Each one asked to be alone with him to advise him about the wife of Al-Aziz, and the intention behind that was to reproach him for her right, and order him to help her, so that perhaps he would respond. So each one of them was alone with him and she said to him: O Joseph! Fulfill my need for me, for I am better than your mistress. Each one called him for herself and tried to seduce him, so he said: O Lord, she was one, but they became a group. It was said: The trick of the wife of Al-Aziz in what she called him to of immorality, and he referred to her by addressing the group either to magnify her status in the address, or to change from being explicit to insinuating. And trickery is deceit and effort, and for this reason war was called trickery because of people’s trickery in it. Omar bin Luja said: She appeared to plot against you, O mother of human beings, and plotting with her beauty is not plotting I yearn for them is the answer to the condition, meaning I long for them, from the word saba yasbu - if he inclines and longs - sabawan and sabawwa. He said: To Hind my heart yearns, and Hind like her it yearns That is, if you do not treat me kindly in avoiding sin, I will fall into it. And I will be among the ignorant, that is, among those who commit sin and deserve blame, or among those who do the work of the ignorant. This indicates that no one refrains from disobeying God except with God’s help, and it also indicates the ugliness of ignorance and the blameworthiness of its owner.
12:34: The Almighty's saying: So his Lord responded to him when he said. And if You do not turn away their plot from me refers to the supplication, and it is as if he said: O God, turn away their plot from me, so He responded to his supplication, and was kind to him and protected him from falling into adultery. Their plot It was said: Because they are a group who tried to seduce him. It was also said: It means the plot of women. It was also said: It means the plot of the wife of Al-Aziz, as mentioned in the verse before, and the generality is more appropriate.
12:35: It has four issues The first: The Almighty’s saying: Then it appeared to them meaning it appeared to Al-Aziz and his advisors after they saw the signs, meaning the signs of Joseph’s innocence - the cutting of the shirt from the back, the witness’s testimony, the cutting of the hands, and their lack of patience in not meeting Joseph - to imprison him to conceal the story so that it would not spread among the public, and to prevent him from it. It was said: They are the blessings that were opened up to them as long as Joseph was among them, and the first is more correct. Muqatil said on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: Then it appeared to them after they had seen the signs he said: The shirt is one of the signs, the witness’ testimony is one of the signs, the cutting of the hands is one of the signs, and the women’s glorification of him is one of the signs. It was said: Shyness from people and fear of despair forced her to accept the veil instead of fear of going, so that she would be healed if she was prevented from seeing him. He said: The passion of one who longs for a meeting with the hope of meeting is not like the passion of one who longs without hope. Or he almost got tired of his imprisonment and sacrificed himself. Second: The Almighty’s saying: to imprison him yusajannahu is in the position of the subject, meaning it appeared to them that they should imprison him. This is the saying of Sibawayh. Al-Mubarrad said: This is a mistake, the subject is not a sentence, but rather what is indicated by bada which is a verbal noun, meaning it appeared to them with a bada’, so it was deleted because the verb indicates it, as the poet said: It is right for the one whose father is Abu Musa to be guided by the One who set up the mountains. Yes, by the truth of the truth, so it was deleted. It was said: The meaning is: Then an opinion occurred to them that they did not know, and this was deleted because there is evidence for it in the speech, and the saying was also deleted, meaning they said: They will surely imprison him, and the lam is the answer to an implied oath, said Al-Farra’, and it is a masculine verb, not a feminine verb, and if it were a feminine verb it would have been they will imprison him, and this is indicated by his saying to them and not to them, so it is as if he was informing about the women and their helpers, so the masculine prevailed, said Abu Ali. Al-Suddi said: The reason for Yusuf’s imprisonment was that the wife of Al-Aziz complained to him that he had defamed her and spread her report, so the pronoun in to them in this case refers to the king. Third: The Almighty’s saying: until a time meaning for an unknown period of time, as many commentators have said. Ibn Abbas said: until what was widespread in the city stopped. Saeed bin Jubair said: until six months. Al-Kia narrated that he meant thirteen months. Ikrimah: nine years. Al-Kalbi: five years. Muqatil: seven. The discussion of the time and the rulings related to it has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Wahb said: He stayed in prison for twelve years. And until means until, like His saying: until the break of dawn (al-Qadr 97:5). And God made imprisonment a purification for Joseph, peace be upon him, from his desire for the woman. It is as if the Aziz, even though he knew Joseph’s innocence, obeyed the woman in imprisoning Joseph. Ibn Abbas said: Joseph stumbled three times: when he desired her and was imprisoned, when he said to the young man: Remember me to your Lord so he remained in prison for several years, and when he said to his brothers: You are indeed thieves so they said: If he steals, a brother of his stole before. Fourth: Joseph, peace be upon him, was forced to commit adultery by imprisonment, and he remained there for five years, and he did not accept that because of his great status and noble standing. If a man was forced to commit adultery by imprisonment, it would not be permissible for him by consensus. If he was forced by beating, then the scholars differed on this, and the correct view is that if it was serious, then the sin of adultery alone is dropped from him. Some of our scholars said that the punishment is not dropped from him, and this is weak, because God Almighty does not combine two punishments for His servant, nor does He divert him between two trials, because that is one of the greatest hardships in religion. And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty (al-Hajj 22:78). This will be explained in Al-Nahl, God willing. And Joseph was made, and he sought refuge in Him from the plot, so He responded to him as mentioned above.
12:36: The Almighty said: And there entered the prison with him young men Fityan is the dual form of fata, and it is one of the words with the letter ya, and their saying: fatwa is anomalous. Wahb and others said: Joseph was carried to the prison chained on a donkey, and he was paraded around This is the reward of he who disobeys his mistress while he was saying: This is easier than the fires of fire, the garments of tar, the drink of boiling water, and the eating of Zaqqum. When Joseph reached the prison, he found people whose hope had been cut off and whose affliction had become severe, so he began to say to them: Be patient and be happy, and you will be rewarded. They said to him: O young man! How good your speech is! We have been blessed in your protection. Who are you, O young man? He said: I am Joseph, son of the chosen one of God, Jacob, son of the sacrificed one of God, Isaac, son of the friend of God, Abraham. Ibn Abbas said: When the woman said to her husband, This Hebrew slave has disgraced me, and I want you to imprison him, he imprisoned him in prison. He would console the sad, visit the sick, treat the wounded, pray all night, and cry until the walls, roofs, and doors of the houses would cry with him. The prison was purified by him, and the people of the prison were comforted by him. Whenever a man was released from prison, he would return and sit in the prison with Joseph. The keeper of the prison loved him and made it spacious for him. Then he said to him, O Joseph! I have loved you with a love I have never loved anything as much as you. He said, I seek refuge in God from loving you. He said, Why is that? He said: My father loved me, so my brothers did to me what they did, and my mistress loved me, so what you see happened to me. So he was in prison until the king became angry with his baker and his drinker, so he named them both. So the baker and my father, the drinker, responded, so the drinker went and told the king about that, so the king ordered them to be imprisoned. So he sought comfort from Joseph, and that is why he said: And two young men entered the prison with him. It was said that the baker put poison in the food, so when the food was ready, the cupbearer said: O king! Do not eat, for the food is poisoned. The baker said: O king, do not drink, for the drink is poisoned. So the king said to the cupbearer: Drink! So he drank and it did not harm him, and he said to the baker: Eat, but he refused. So the food was tested on an animal, and it died on the spot, so he imprisoned them for a year, and they remained in prison for that period with Joseph. The cupbearer's name was Manja, and the other Mujalth, as al-Tha'labi mentioned from Ka'b. Al-Naqqash said: The name of one of them was Sharrhum, and the other was Sirrum, the first with a voiced shin, and the other with a silent seen. Al-Tabari said: The one who saw that he was pressing wine was Nabu. Al-Suhayli said: He mentioned the name of the other, but I did not specify it. He said two young men because they were two slaves, and a slave is called a young man, whether he was young or old. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. Al-Qushayri said: Perhaps a young man was a name for a slave in their language, and this is why he said: She sought to seduce her young man. It is possible that a young man was a name for a servant, even if he was not a slave. It is possible that their imprisonment was with the imprisonment of Joseph, or after it, or before it, except that they entered the house in which he was. One of them said, Indeed, I see myself pressing wine meaning grapes. Joseph had said to the people of the prison: I interpret dreams. So one of the young men said to his companion: Come, let us test this Hebrew slave. So they asked him without having seen anything, as Ibn Masoud said. Al-Tabari narrated that they asked him about his knowledge, and he said: I interpret dreams. So they asked him about their dreams. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: It was a true vision that they saw and asked him about, and therefore its interpretation was true. In Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The most truthful of you in vision is the most truthful of you in speech. It was said: It was a false vision that they asked him about as a test, and this is the statement of Ibn Masoud and Al-Suddi. It was said: The one who was crucified of them was a liar, and the other was truthful, as stated by Abu Majlaz. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever tells a false dream will be asked on the Day of Resurrection to tie two barley grains together, but he will not be able to tie them together. Abu Eisa said: This is a good and authentic hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Ali on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever lies in his dream will be asked on the Day of Resurrection to tie a grain of barley together. He said: A good hadith. Ibn Abbas said: When they saw their dreams, they became distressed, and Yusuf said to them: Why do I see you both distressed? They said: O our master! We saw what we disliked. He said: So they told me, and he told him, and they said: Inform us of the interpretation of what we saw. This indicates that it was a dream. Indeed, we see that you are among the doers of good. His goodness was that he used to visit the sick and treat them, and console the grieving. Ad-Dahhak said: If a man from the prison was sick, he would take care of him, and if he hosted him, he would make room for him, and if he needed something, he would gather for him and ask for it. It was said: Of the doers of good meaning the scholars who excelled in knowledge, as Al-Farra’ said. Ibn Ishaq said: Of the doers of good for us, if you interpret it, as he says: Do such and such and you are a doer of good. He said: So what did you see? The baker said: I saw as if I baked bread in three ovens, and put it in three baskets, and placed it on my head, and a bird came and ate from it. Another said: I saw myself taking three bunches of white grapes, squeezing them in three vessels, then filtering them and giving them to the king to drink as I usually did in the past. This is what he said: Indeed, I see myself squeezing wine, meaning grapes, in the language of Oman, as Ad-Dahhak said. Ibn Masoud read: Indeed, I see myself squeezing grapes. Al-Asma’i said: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told me that he met a Bedouin who had grapes with him, so he said to him: What do you have with you? He said: Wine. It was said: The meaning of squeezing wine is grapes is wine, so the noun was omitted. It is also said: wine, wine, and wines, like date, dates, and dates.
12:37: Joseph said to them: No food will come to you that you are provided with meaning no food will come to you tomorrow from your home except that I will inform you of its interpretation so that you may know that I know the interpretation of your visions, so they said: Do it! So he said to them: Such and such will come to you, and it was as he said, and this was from the knowledge of the unseen that was given to Joseph alone. And he explained that God gave him this knowledge because he left the religion of a people who did not believe in God, meaning the religion of the king. The meaning of the statement in my opinion is: knowledge of the interpretation of your visions, knowledge of what will come to you of your food, and knowledge of the religion of God, so listen first to what is related to religion so that you may be guided, and for this reason he did not interpret it for them until he called them to Islam, so he said: O my companions of prison, are separate lords better or God, the One, the Prevailing * What you worship? The entire verse is as follows. And it was said: He knew that one of them would be killed, so he called them to Islam so that they would be happy with him. It was said that Joseph was reluctant to explain to them what they asked him for he knew that it would be unpleasant for one of them, so he ignored their question and started something else. He said: No food will come to you that you will be provided with in a dream except that I will inform you of its interpretation when you are awake. Al-Suddi said that. They said to him: This is from the actions of fortune-tellers and soothsayers. Joseph, peace be upon him, said to them: I am not a soothsayer, but rather that is what my Lord has taught me. I am not informing you of it as a divination or astrology, but rather it is by revelation from God, the Almighty. Ibn Jurayj said: When the king wanted to kill someone, he would prepare a well-known meal for him and send it to him. The meaning is: No food will come to you that you will be provided with while you are awake. According to this, you will be provided with it means that it will come to you from the king or someone else. It is possible that God will provide for you. Al-Hasan said: He would inform them of what was unseen, like Jesus, peace be upon him. It was said that he called them to Islam with that, and made the miracle that they would use as evidence to inform them of the unseen.
12:38: The Almighty said: And I have followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they were prophets of truth. It was not means it was not appropriate. For us to associate anything with God (of) is for emphasis, like saying: No one came to me. And the Almighty said: That is from the grace of God upon us is a reference to His protection from adultery. And upon mankind meaning upon the believers whom God protected from polytheism. It was said: That is from the grace of God upon us since He made us prophets, and upon mankind if He made messengers to them. But most people are not grateful for the blessing of monotheism and faith.
12:39: The Almighty said: O my two companions of the prison meaning O residents of the prison, and the companionship was mentioned because of the length of their stay in it, like saying: the companions of Paradise and the companions of Hell. Are there separate lords? meaning in smallness, largeness, and averageness, or are they separated in number. Better or God, the One, the Prevailing? It was said: The address was to them and to the people of the prison, and they had idols in front of them that they worshipped instead of God, so He said that to make the argument binding, meaning various gods that neither harm nor benefit. Better or God, the One, the Prevailing Who has subdued everything. Similar to it is: Is God better or what they associate with Him? (al-Naml 27:59) It was said: He indicated by the separation that if the gods were multiple, they would be separated in will and some would rise above others, and he explained that if they were separated, they would not be gods.
12:40: The Almighty said: What you worship besides Him are only names. He showed the weakness and inability of idols, saying: What you worship besides Him meaning besides God is only those with names that have no meanings. You named them of your own accord. It was said: By names He meant the named things, meaning what you worship are only idols that have nothing of divinity except the name, because they are inanimate. He said: What you worship and he began by addressing two people, because he intended all those who are in the same state of polytheism as them. Except names you have named, you and your fathers. So the second object was omitted for the sake of indication, and the meaning is: you named them gods from yourselves. God has not sent down that in a book. Saeed bin Jubair said: Of authority meaning of proof. The judgment is only for God who is the Creator of everything. He has commanded that you worship none but Him. "That is the right religion meaning the upright but most people do not know."
12:41: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: As for one of you, he will give his Lord wine to drink. That is, He said to the cupbearer: You will be returned to your work that you were doing in giving the king wine to drink after three days. And He said to the other: As for you, you will be summoned for three days and crucified, and the birds will eat from your head. He said: By God, you did not see anything. He said: You saw or did you not see. The matter about which you are asking has been decided. The linguists have related that saqā and asqā are two languages with one meaning, as the poet said: He watered my people, Bani Majd, and watered Namir and the tribes from Hilal. Al-Nahhas said: What most linguists agree on is that the meaning of saqahu is nawa’ilu give him water to drink, or poured water into his throat, and the meaning of asqahu is give him a drink. God Almighty said: And We gave you to drink sweet water (al-Mursalat 77:27). Second: Our scholars said: If it is said that someone lied in his dream and the interpreter interpreted it for him, is he bound by its ruling? We say: He is not bound by it, and that was in the case of Joseph because he was a prophet, and the interpretation of a prophet is a ruling, and he said: It will be such and such, so God Almighty brought into being what he had informed as he said, to confirm his prophethood. If it is said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah who said: A man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: I saw in a dream that I had greenery, then it became barren, then it became barren, then Umar said to him: You are a man who believes then disbelieves, then believes then disbelieves, then dies a disbeliever, so the man said: You did not see anything, so Umar said to him: What was decreed for you was decreed for the companion of Joseph, we say: It is not for anyone after Umar, because Umar was inspired, and if he had a suspicion, it was true, and if he spoke about it, it would happen, according to what was reported in his reports, and they are many, including - that a man entered upon him and he said to him: I think you are a soothsayer, and it was as he thought, narrated by al-Bukhari. Among them - he asked a man about his name, so he told him that it contains all the names of Hellfire. He said to him: Save your family, for they have been burned. And it was as he said. It was reported by Al-Muwatta. More explanation of this will come in Surat Al-Hijr, God willing.
12:42: It has five issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And he said to the one who thought thought here means he was certain, according to the majority of commentators. Qatada interpreted it as a thought, which is the opposite of certainty. He said: Joseph thought he would be saved because a passerby thinks, and your Lord creates what He wills. The first is more correct and more similar to the state of the prophets, and that what he said to the young men in interpreting the dream was from revelation. It is only a thought in the judgment of people, but as for the right of the prophets, their judgment is true no matter how it occurs. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Remember me with your Lord, meaning your master. This is known in the language to say Lord to a master. Al-A’sha said: My Lord is generous and does not spoil a blessing. If you are asked to sing in the middle of the night, I will sing. That is, mention what you saw, and what I am like in the dream to the angel, and tell him that I am wronged and imprisoned without sin. In Sahih Muslim and others, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Let none of you say, ‘Give your Lord to drink,’ ‘Eat your Lord to drink,’ and ‘Show your Lord to drink.’ Let none of you say, ‘My Lord,’ but say, ‘My Master,’ and let none of you say, ‘My slave, my female slave.’ But say, ‘My boy,’ ‘My girl,’ ‘My servant.’” And in the Qur’an: Mention me to your Lord. To your Lord He is my Lord, the best place for me to stay. meaning my companion, meaning the Mighty One. And it is said to everyone who repairs and completes something: He has made it his Lord, so he is its Lord. Scholars said that his peace be upon him saying: None of you should say (and let him say) is a guide to using the name of the first, not that using the name of the first, not that using that name is forbidden, and because it was reported from him peace be upon him: That the female slave should give birth to her master meaning her owner and her master, this is in agreement with the Qur'an in using that word, so the place of prohibition in this regard was that we should not make these names a habit and leave the first and best. It has been said: A man's saying my slave and my female slave combines two meanings: One of them: That servitude in reality is only for God the Most High, so in one of the people saying to his slave my slave and my female slave is glorification of him, and adding him to himself with what God the Most High added him to himself, and that is not permissible. The second: That the slave enters into something of that in belittling him with that name, so that leads him to disobey badly. Ibn Sha'ban said in Al-Zahi: The master does not say my slave and my female slave, and the slave does not say my Lord or my mistress. This is based on what we mentioned. It was said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The servant should not say ‘My Lord’ but rather say ‘My Master’ because Lord is one of the names of God the Most High that are used by consensus. There is a difference of opinion as to whether ‘Master’ is one of the names of God the Most High or not. If we say that it is not one of the names of God, then the difference is clear, as there is no ambiguity or doubt. If we say that it is one of His names, then it is not as well-known or used as the word ‘Lord’, so there is a difference. Ibn al-Arabi said: It is possible that this was permissible in the law of Joseph, peace be upon him. Third: The Almighty’s saying: But Satan made him forget the remembrance of his Lord. The pronoun in and made him forget has two interpretations: One of them: It refers to Joseph, peace be upon him, meaning Satan made him forget the remembrance of God Almighty. This is because when Joseph said to the cupbearer of the king - when he knew that he would be saved and return to his former state with the king - Remember me to your Lord, he forgot at that time to complain to God and seek help from Him, and he inclined to cling to a creature, so he was punished by staying. Abdul Aziz bin Umair Al-Kindi said: Gabriel entered upon the Prophet Joseph, peace be upon him, in prison, and Joseph recognized him, so he said: O brother of the warners! Why do I see you among the sinners? Gabriel, peace be upon him, said: O pure son of the pure! The Lord of the worlds sends you his greetings and says: Were you not ashamed when you sought help from humans? By My glory! I will keep you in prison for a few years. He said: O Gabriel! Is He pleased with me? He said: Yes! He said: I do not care about the hour. It was narrated that Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and rebuked him about God Almighty for that and the length of his imprisonment, and said to him: O Joseph! Who saved you from being killed by your brothers?! He said: God Almighty. He said: Then who brought you out of the well? He said: God Almighty. He said: Then who protected you from immorality? He said: God Almighty. He said: Then who averted from you the plots of women? He said: God Almighty. He said: How did you trust in a creature and leave your Lord and do not ask Him? He said: O Lord, a word that slipped from me! I ask You, O God of Abraham, Isaac, and Sheikh Jacob, peace be upon them, to have mercy on me. Gabriel said to him: Your punishment is that you remain in prison for a few years. Abu Salamah narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on Joseph, had it not been for the word he said: ‘Remember me to your Lord,’ he would not have remained in prison for a few years.” Ibn Abbas said: Joseph was punished by a long imprisonment for a few years because he said to the one who was saved from him: ‘Remember me to your Lord.’ If Joseph had remembered his Lord, He would have saved him. Ismail bin Ibrahim narrated on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Al-Hasan who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Had it not been for the word of Joseph - meaning his saying: ‘Remember me to your Lord’ - he would not have remained in prison as long as he remained.” Then Al-Hasan wept and said: We are the ones who are brought down by the matter and we complain to the people. It was said: The ha’ refers to the one who is saved, so he is the forgetful one, meaning that Satan made the cupbearer forget to mention Joseph to his Lord, meaning to his master, and there is an omission in it, meaning that Satan made him forget to mention him to his Lord. Some scholars have preferred this statement and said: Had it not been for Satan making Joseph forget to mention God, he would not have deserved the punishment of remaining in prison, since the forgetful one is not held accountable. The people of the first opinion responded that forgetfulness may mean abandonment, so when he abandoned the remembrance of God and Satan called him to do so, he was punished. The people of the second opinion responded to them with the words of God the Almighty: And the one who escaped from the two of them said, ‘And remember after a time.’ This indicates that the one who forgot was the cupbearer, not Joseph, with the words of God the Almighty: Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority. (al-Hijr 15:42). So how can his forgetfulness be attributed to Satan, since he does not have authority over the prophets?! It was said: As for forgetfulness, the prophets are not infallible from it except in one way, which is the report from God the Almighty in what they convey, for they are infallible in it, and if they forget where it is permissible for it to happen, then it is attributed to Satan absolutely, and that only happens in what God informed about them, and it is not permissible for us to do so with them. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Adam forgot, so his descendants forgot. And he said: I am only a human being who forgets as you forget. And this has been mentioned before. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: So he remained in prison for a number of years. The word ba’d is a part of time. Ya’qub said on the authority of Abu Zayd: It is said ba’d and ba’d with the opening of the ba and its breaking. Most of them said: It is not said ba’d and hundred, but rather it is up to ninety. Al-Harawi said: The Arabs use ba’d for what is between three and nine. Ba’d and ba’d are one and the same, and they mean a piece of a number. Abu Ubaidah narrated that he said: Ba’d is less than half a decade, meaning what is between one and four, and this is nothing. In the hadith, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him: And how much is a ba’d? He said: Between three and seven. He said: Go, it is extra in danger. Most of the commentators agree with this, that ba’d is seven, as narrated by al-Tha’labi. Al-Mawardi said: It is the saying of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, and Qutrub. Mujahid said: From three to nine, and al-Asma’i said the same. Ibn Abbas: From three to ten. Al-Zajjaj narrated that it is between three and five. Al-Farra’ said: Al-Bad’ is only mentioned with ten, twenty, and ninety, and is not mentioned after one hundred. There are three sayings about the period that Joseph remained in prison: The first: Seven years, said by Ibn Jurayj, Qatadah, and Wahb ibn Munabbih. Wahb said: Job remained in the affliction for seven years, and Joseph remained in prison for seven years. The second: Twelve years, said by Ibn Abbas. The third: Fourteen years, said by Ad-Dahhak. Muqatil said on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Joseph remained in prison for five and a few years. Its derivation is from ba’dat which means to cut something, so it is a piece of a number. So God punished Joseph by imprisoning him for seven or nine years after the five that had passed, so the ba’d is the period of punishment, not the entire period of imprisonment. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Joseph was imprisoned for seven years, Job remained in the affliction for seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar was tortured by being transformed for seven years. Abdullah ibn Rashid Al-Basri said on the authority of Saeed ibn Abi Aruba: The ba’d is between five and twelve years. Fifth: In this verse there is evidence of the permissibility of relying on causes, even if certainty is obtained, for matters are in the hand of their causer, but He made them a chain, and put some of them on top of others, so their movement is a law, and reliance on the end is certainty. What indicates the permissibility of that is attributing what happened of forgetfulness to Satan, as happened to Moses when he met Al-Khidr, and this is clear, so reflect on it.
12:43: The Almighty said: And the king said, 'Indeed, I see seven fat cows.' When the relief of Joseph, peace be upon him, approached, the king saw his vision, so Gabriel came down and greeted Joseph and gave him good report of relief and said: God will bring you out of your prison and establish you in the land, subjugate its kings to you, and make its tyrants obey you, and give you the upper hand over your brothers. This is because of a vision that the king saw, which was such and such, and its interpretation is such and such. When he remained in prison for more than the king saw the vision until he came out, God made the vision first for Joseph a calamity and hardship, and made it last good report and mercy. This is because the greatest king, Rayyan bin Al-Walid, saw in his sleep as if seven fat cows had emerged from a dry river, followed by seven lean ones - meaning emaciated ones - and the lean ones had approached the fat ones and seized their ears and eaten them, except for the two horns, and the head of seven green ears of corn that seven Dry ones, so they ate them until they had finished them off and nothing remained of them while they were dry. Likewise, the cows were lean and nothing had increased in them from eating them, so the vision terrified him, so he sent to the people and the people of knowledge among them and those who had insight into divination, astrology, fortune-telling and magic, and the nobles of his people, and said: O assembly, give me your legal opinion regarding my vision. So he told them, and the people said: Confused dreams. Ibn Jurayj said: Ata’ told me: False, mistaken confused dreams are among the visions. Jubair said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Some visions are true, and some are confused dreams, meaning false dreams. Al-Harawi said: The Almighty’s statement: Confused dreams means mixed dreams. In the language, a bundle of something is a bundle of something like herbs, pastures and the like, meaning they said: Your vision is not clear, and dreams are mixed visions. Mujahid said: Confused dreams are its horrors. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Adghādah is a vision that has no interpretation. God the Almighty said: seven fat cows. The ha’ was deleted from seven to differentiate between the masculine and feminine fat as an adjective for cows. It is permissible in other than the Qur’an to say seven fat cows as an adjective for seven, and so is green. Al-Farra’ said: And similar to it is: seven heavens in layers (al-Mulk 67:3). Its derivation and meaning have already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: When goats and cows enter a city, if they are fat, then they are years of plenty, and if they are lean, then they are strong, and if the city is a sea city and during a journey, ships will come according to their number and condition, otherwise they will be successive tribulations, as if they are the faces of cows, as in the hadith some resemble others. In another hadith about tribulations: As if they were the hooves of cows meaning because of their similarity, except that they are all yellow, for they are diseases that enter people, even if they are of different colors, hideous in their horns and people are repelled by them, or as if fire and smoke are coming out of their mouths, for it is an army or a raid, or an enemy who strikes them and descends upon their courtyard. The cow may also indicate a wife, a servant, crops and a year, because of what is in it of children, crops and plants. They are eaten by seven lean years from ajaf ya’jif, on the weight of ‘azm ya’zim, and it was narrated ajaf ya’jif on the weight of hamd yahamd. The Almighty said: O eminent ones, give me your opinion concerning my vision. The plural of vision is ru’ya meaning, tell me the ruling on this vision. If you interpret visions. The word ‘abat is derived from crossing the river, so the meaning of I crossed the river is I reached its shore, so across the vision means interpreting what it leads to. The lam in for the vision is for clarification, meaning, if you interpret it. Then he explained and said: for the vision, as Al-Zajjaj said.
12:44: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Confused dreams. Al-Farra’ said: Confused dreams is also permissible. An-Nahhas said: The accusative is far-fetched, because the meaning is: You did not see anything that has an interpretation. Rather, they are confused dreams, meaning mixtures. The singular of confused dreams is daghth, and every mixture of herbs, grass, or other things is called daghth. The poet said: Like a dream that was deceived by its dreamer And we are not knowledgeable about the interpretation of dreams. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of interpreting mixed dreams is that they denied themselves knowledge of what has no interpretation, not that they denied themselves knowledge of interpretation. It was also said: They denied themselves knowledge of interpretation. And the dreams according to this group are visions, some of which are true and some of which are false. For this reason, the cupbearer said: I will inform you of its interpretation, so it was known that the people were unable to interpret, not that they claimed that it has no interpretation. It was also said: They did not intend interpretation, but rather wanted to erase it from the king’s mind so that it would not occupy his mind. Based on this also, they have knowledge. And dreams is the plural of dream, and a dream with a dammah is what a sleeper sees. You say from it: he dreamed with a fathah and he had a wet dream, and you say: I dreamed of such-and-such and I had a dream about it. He said: I dreamt it, and Banu Rufaidah were not far from it, and her dream was not far from me. Its origin is patience, and from it comes the word dream which is the opposite of rashness. So, what is seen in a dream is called a dream, because sleep is a state of patience, stillness, and tranquility. Second: In the verse there is evidence of the invalidity of the statement of those who say: The vision is based on the first interpretation, because the people said: Confused dreams and it did not happen like that, for Joseph interpreted it according to the years of drought and fertility, and it was as he interpreted it, and in it there is evidence of the corruption of the vision being about a flying man, so if it is interpreted it will happen.
12:45: The Almighty said: And he who was saved from the two of them said, meaning the king's cupbearer. And remember after a time, meaning after a while, according to Ibn Abbas and others. From this, to a numbered nation (Hud 11:8). Its origin is the phrase from the time. Ibn Durastawayh said: The nation does not come to be the time except by deleting the noun and placing the noun in its place, as if he said - and God knows best -: And remember after a time a nation, or after a time a nation, and the like. The nation is a large group of people. Al-Akhfash said: It is one in wording, but plural in meaning, and every type of animal is a nation. In the hadith: If dogs were not a nation among the nations, I would have ordered their killing. The Almighty said: And remember meaning remember the need of Joseph, which is his saying: Remember me to your Lord. Ibn Abbas read - according to what Affan narrated on the authority of Hammam on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Ikrimah on his authority - And remember after a nation. An-Nahhas: What is known from the reading of Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak is And remember after a nation, with the opening of the hamza and the softening of the meem, meaning after forgetting. The poet said: I died and I will never forget a conversation. Time destroys minds. On the authority of Shabil bin Azra Al-Dab’i: ba’d ummah with the opening of the alif and the sukoon of the meem and a pure ha’, and it is like ummah, and they are two languages, and their meanings are forgetfulness, and it is said: ummah ya’mahu if he forgot, so on this basis wa’dkar ba’d ummah, Al-Nahhas mentioned it, and a man whose mother is insane. Al-Jawhari said: As for what is in the hadith of Al-Zuhri ummah meaning he acknowledged and confessed, it is an unpopular language. Al-Ashhab Al-Uqaili read - ba’d ummah meaning after a blessing, meaning after God bestowed upon him salvation. Then it was said: The young man Yusuf forgot God’s decree in remaining in prison for a period. It was said: He did not forget, but he feared that the king would remember the sin for which he and the baker were imprisoned, so his saying: wa’dkar means he remembered and informed. Al-Nahhas said: The root of idkar is idhtakkar, and the dhal is close to the point of articulation of the ta’, and it is not permissible to assimilate it into it because the dhal is voiced and the ta’ is unvoiced. If they had assimilate, the voicedness would have been lost, so they replaced the ta’ with a voiced letter, which is the dal, and it was better than the ta’ because the ta’ is closed, so it became idhdkar. So they assimilated the dhal into the dal because of the softness and smoothness of the dal. Then he said: Ana anbikm bi-ta’wilhu meaning I will inform you. Al-Hasan read Ana at’ikum bi-ta’wilhu and said: How can the foreigner inform them?! Al-Nahhas said: The meaning of anbikm is correct and good, meaning I will inform you if you ask. Farsalun is addressing the king but with a word of respect, or he addressed the king and the people of his assembly.
12:46: Yusuf is a singular address, and so is the truthful meaning the one who is very honest. Give us your opinion meaning send him, so he came to Yusuf and said: O truthful one! And he asked him about the king's dream. Perhaps I may return to the people meaning to the king and his companions. Perhaps they will know is the expression, or perhaps they will know) your place of virtue and knowledge so that you may leave. It is possible that he means by the people the king alone, out of respect for him.
12:47: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘You will cultivate.’ When he informed him of the vision, he began to interpret it for him, saying: The seven fat cows and green ears of corn are seven fertile years, and as for the lean cows and dry ears of corn, they are seven barren years. That is why His saying: You will cultivate seven years continuously, meaning consecutively and in succession. It is a source other than a source, because the meaning of you will cultivate is you will be persistent as you are accustomed to in agriculture for seven years. It was said: It is a state, meaning persistent. It was said: It is an attribute of seven years, meaning persistent. Abu Hatim narrated from Ya’qub dā’ban with a fat-ha on the hamzah, and Hafs narrated the same from Asim, and they are two dialects, and there are two opinions about it. The saying of Abu Hatim: It is from dai’b. Al-Nahhas said: The people of language do not know anything except da’b. The other statement: It is a vowel because it contains throat letters. Al-Farra’ said: And likewise every letter whose first letter is open and whose second letter is silent, then its emphasis is permissible if its second letter is a hamza, or a ha’, or an ‘ayn, or a ghayn, or a ha’, or a kha’, and its origin is custom. He said: As usual from Umm Al-Huwairith before her It was mentioned in Al Imran. So whatever you harvest, leave it in its spike. It was said: so that it does not rot, and so that it will last longer. This is how it was in the lands of Egypt. Except a little of what you eat. That is, extract what you need according to need. This statement is a command, and the first is report. It is possible that the first is also a command, although the more apparent of it is report, so the meaning of you plant is plant. Second: This verse is the basis for the statement of the legitimate interests, which are the preservation of religions, souls, minds, lineages, and wealth. Everything that includes the attainment of something of these matters is an interest, and everything that misses something of them is corruption, and preventing it is an interest. There is no disagreement that the purpose of the laws is to guide people to their worldly interests, so that they may be able to know God Almighty and worship Him, which leads to happiness in the Hereafter. Taking this into consideration is a favor from God Almighty and a mercy with which He has shown mercy to His servants, without it being obligatory upon Him or due. This is the doctrine of all the scholars of the Sunnah, and it is explained in the principles of jurisprudence.
12:48: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: Seven difficult years meaning the barren years. They eat is a metaphor, and the meaning is that their families eat. What you have put in advance for them meaning what you have saved for them. Similar to this is the statement of the speaker: Your day, you arrogant one, is full of negligence and heedlessness, your night is full of sleep, and destruction is inevitable for you. The day does not neglect, and the night does not sleep. Rather, it neglects during the day and sleeps at night. Zaid bin Aslam narrated on the authority of his father: Joseph used to set the food for two people and bring it to one man, who would eat some of it, until the day came when he brought it to him and he ate it all. Then Joseph said: This is the first day of the seven severe days. Except a little is in the accusative case as an exception. Of what you store means of what you keep back to plant, because preserving the seeds protects the provisions. Abu Ubaidah said: You protect. Qatada said: You store means you hoard, and the meaning is the same, and it indicates the permissibility of hoarding food until the time of need. Second: This verse is the basis for the validity of the vision of the unbeliever, and that it comes out according to what he saw, especially if it is related to a believer, so how is it if it is a sign for a prophet, a miracle for a messenger, confirmation of the Chosen One for conveying the message, and an argument for the intermediary between God - may He be glorified and exalted - and His servants.
12:49: The Almighty said: Then there will come after that a year. This is report from Joseph, peace be upon him, about what was not in the king's dream, but it is from the knowledge of the unseen that God gave him. Qatada said: God increased his knowledge of a year that they did not ask him about, to demonstrate His grace and to inform him of his place in knowledge and his knowledge. In it people are helped from relief or relief. The man's relief said, Oh, his relief. The noun is relief, ghawth, and ghawth. So-and-so sought help from me, so I helped him. The noun is ghayath, the waw became a ya because of the kasrah before it. And rain is the rain, and rain has fallen on the earth, meaning it has struck it. God has given rain to the land, and the land is given rain, so it is a land that is given rain and is given rain. So the meaning of people are given rain is they receive rain. And in it they squeeze. Ibn Abbas said: They squeeze the necks and the oil. Al-Bukhari mentioned it. Hajjaj narrated on the authority of Ibn Jurayj who said: They squeeze the grapes to make wine, the sesame to make oil, and the olives to make oil. It was said: He meant milking the milk because of its abundance, and this indicates the abundance of plants. It was said: They squeeze means they escape, and it is from the word press, which means salvation. Abu Ubaidah said: Asr with a fat-ha is the refuge and the salvation, and so is press. Abu Zubaydah said: Sadiq, crying for help, but no one helped him. He was the one who was helped. Al-Manjud means fear. I took refuge in someone and I took refuge in him. Abu al-Ghauth said: yasiroun they exploit, and it is from squeezing grapes. I squeezed his money, meaning I extracted it from his hand. Isa read ta’siroun with a damma on the ta’ and a fatha on the sad, and its meaning is you rain, from the saying of God: And We sent down from the pressed clouds abundant water (An-Naba’: 14). And the meaning of ta’siroun with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the sad is the same for those who read it like that.
12:50: God Almighty says: And the king said, ‘Bring him to me.’ That is, the messenger went and informed the king, who said, Bring him to me. “So when the messenger came to him,” that is, ordering him to go out, he said, Return to your Lord and ask Him what is the matter with the women, that is, the condition of the women. Who cut their hands. But he refused to go out unless his innocence was proven to the king regarding what he had accused him of, and that he had been imprisoned and even committed a crime. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The generous son of the generous son of the generous son of the generous Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham - he said - and if I had remained in prison as long as he did and then the messenger came to me, I would have answered - then he recited - “So when the messenger came to him, he said, ‘Return to your Lord and ask Him what was the matter with the women who cut their hands’ - he said - and may God have mercy on Lot, for he used to take refuge in a strong support when he said, ‘He said, “If only I had power over you, or could take refuge in a strong support” (Hud 11:80). God did not send a prophet after him except at the peak of his people.” Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on Lot, for he used to take refuge in a strong support. If I had remained in prison as long as Joseph, I would have answered the caller, and we are more deserving than Abraham when he said to him, ‘Do you not believe?’ He said, ‘Yes, but so that my heart may be reassured.’” (al-Baqarah 2:260) It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: May God have mercy on my brother Joseph. He was patient and forbearing, and if I had remained in prison as long as he did, I would have answered the caller and not sought an excuse.” A similar hadith was narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, the companion of Malik, in the Book of Interpretation of Sahih al-Bukhari, and Ibn al-Qasim has no other hadith in the Diwan. In the narration of al-Tabari: “May God have mercy on Yusuf. If I were the one imprisoned and then a message was sent to me, I would have left quickly, for he was forbearing and patient.” And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was amazed by Yusuf, his patience and generosity, and may God forgive him, when he was asked about the cows. If I were in his place, I would not have told them until I stipulated that they release me. I was amazed at him when the messenger came to him. If I were in his place, I would have rushed to the door.” Ibn Atiyah said: This action of Joseph, peace be upon him, was patience and forbearance, and a search for innocence, because - according to what was narrated - he feared that he would go out and attain a position from the king and remain silent about his sin, forgiving him, and people would see him with that eye forever and say: This is the one who tried to seduce his master’s wife. So Joseph, peace be upon him, wanted to prove his innocence and confirm his position of chastity and goodness, and then he would go out to gain favor and status, so he said to the Messenger: Go back to your Lord and tell him what is the matter with the women, and the purpose of Joseph, peace be upon him, was only: And tell him to investigate my sin, and look into my case, whether I was imprisoned rightly or unjustly, and to treat the wife of the Aziz well, and to respect the covenant of the Aziz King towards him. If it is said: How did the Prophet, peace be upon him, praise Joseph for his patience and forbearance and not taking the initiative to go out, then he himself goes away from a state for which he had praised others? The reason for this is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took for himself another aspect of opinion, which also has an aspect of goodness.
