He says: If it were me, I would have rushed to leave, then I tried to explain my excuse after that. This is because these stories and calamities are subject to people following their example until the Day of Resurrection. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to urge people to do more prudent things. This is because abandoning prudence in such a calamity, abandoning the opportunity to leave such a prison, may result in him remaining in his prison, and the soul of his release turning away from him. Although Joseph, peace be upon him, was safe from that with his knowledge from God, others are not safe from that. The state to which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went himself was a state of prudence, and what Joseph, peace be upon him, did was great patience and endurance. The Almighty said: So ask him what is the matter with the women. He mentioned the women as a whole so that the wife of Al-Aziz would be included in them in a general manner by allusion so that she would not be explicitly mentioned. This is good treatment and etiquette. There is something omitted in the speech, meaning, so ask him to find out what is the matter with the women. Ibn Abbas said: So the king sent to the women and to the wife of Al-Aziz - and Al-Aziz had died.
12:51: So he called them and said, What is the matter with you? meaning, what is your affair? When you sought to seduce Joseph from himself? That is, each one of them spoke to Joseph about herself, as mentioned above, or he meant that each one said that she had wronged the wife of Al-Aziz, so that was a seduce from them. They said, God forbid. meaning, God forbid. We do not know of any evil on his part. meaning, adultery. The wife of Al-Aziz said, Now the truth has become clear." When she saw their acknowledgment of Joseph's innocence, and the truth has become clear means it has become apparent and evident, and its origin is hasas, so it was said: hashas, as he said: kabkabwa in kabbawa, and kafafat in kaf, as Al-Zajjaj and others said. The origin of hash is to uproot something, it is said: he hash his hair if he uprooted it in parts, Abu Al-Qays Ibn Al-Aslat said: The egg has been planted in my head, so I do not eat sleep except for a nap A barren year, meaning a year without any good in it. Jarir said: He takes refuge in you without favor or denial, driven by the year of siege and the wolf. It is as if he wanted to say: and the hyena, which is the barren year, so he put the wolf in its place for the sake of the rhyme, so the meaning of the truth has become clear is that it has been cut off from falsehood by its appearance and its stability. He said: Except for someone who tells lies about me, he is a liar and unjust when the truth is revealed. It was said: It is derived from the share, so the meaning is that the share of truth is distinct from the share of falsehood. Mujahid and Qatadah said: Its origin is taken from their saying, Has his hair if he uprooted it, or cut it, and from it the share of the earth if it is cut from it. And hashas with a kasra is dirt and stones, mentioned by Al-Jawhari. I seduce him, and indeed, he is among the truthful. This statement from her - even if he did not ask about it - is a manifestation of her repentance and a confirmation of the truthfulness of Joseph and his honor, because an admission against himself is stronger than testimony against him, so God combined testimony and admission for Joseph to demonstrate his truthfulness, so that no suspicion would cross his mind, nor doubt would mix with it. The nun was stressed in khatabakun and rawadtun because it is like the mim and waw in the masculine.
12:52: The Almighty's saying: That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret. There is a difference of opinion about who said it. It was said: It is from the words of the wife of Al-Aziz, and it is connected to her words: Now the truth has become clear. That is, I have acknowledged the truth so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret, that is, by lying to him, and I did not speak ill of him while he was absent. Rather, I told the truth and refrained from betrayal. Then she said: And I do not acquit myself. Rather, I tried to seduce him. Based on this, she was acknowledging the Creator, and for this reason she said: Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful. It was said: It is from the words of Joseph, that is, Joseph said: That which I did, of rejecting the messenger so that Al-Aziz may know that I did not betray him in secret. This was said by Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others. The meaning of in secret is when he was absent. Joseph only said that in the presence of the king, and he said: so that he may know in the absence of the king out of respect for the king. It was said: He said it when the Messenger returned to him while he was still in prison. Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger came to Joseph, peace be upon him, with the report and Gabriel was with him talking to him. Joseph said: That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret and that God does not guide the plot of the traitors. That is, I have not betrayed my master in secret. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to him: O Joseph! Not even when you untied your garment and sat in the place where a man sits with a woman?! Joseph said: And I do not acquit myself. The verse. Al-Suddi said: The wife of Al-Aziz only said to him: Not even when you untied your trousers, O Joseph?! Joseph said: And I do not acquit myself. It was said: That is so that he may know from the words of Al-Aziz, that is, that is so that Joseph may know that I have not betrayed him in secret and that I have not neglected to reward him for his trustworthiness. And that God does not guide the plot of the traitors. This means that God does not guide the plot of the traitors with their plot.
12:53: The Almighty’s saying: And I do not acquit myself. It was said: It is from the woman’s words. Al-Qushayri said: It appears that his saying: That is so that he may know and his saying: And I do not acquit myself are from the words of Joseph. I said: If it is possible that it was said by the woman, then it is more appropriate to say so, so that we may acquit Joseph of untying the izar and trousers. If we assume that it was said by Joseph, then it is what crossed his mind, based on what we have presented from the preferred statement in his statement: and he intended her. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Some people say: That is so that he may know that I did not betray him in secret to his statement: Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful from the words of the wife of al-Aziz, because it is connected to her statement: I sought to seduce him, and indeed, he is of the truthful. This is the doctrine of those who deny the intention from Joseph, peace be upon him. Whoever builds on their statement says: From his statement: The wife of al-Aziz said to his statement: Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful are statements connected to each other, and there is no complete stopping at the truth in them, and we do not choose this statement nor do we go towards it. Al-Hasan said: When Joseph said: That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret, the Prophet of God was reluctant to praise himself, so he said: And I do not acquit myself, because praising oneself is reprehensible. God Almighty said: So do not claim yourselves to be pure (al-Najm 53:32), and we have explained this in An-Nisa. It was said: It is from the words of Al-Aziz, meaning: I do not acquit myself of having bad thoughts about Joseph. Indeed, the soul is prone to evil meaning it desires it. Except for those upon whom my Lord has mercy is in the accusative case as an exception, and ma means from, meaning except for those upon whom my Lord has mercy and protected, and ma means many. God Almighty said: Then marry such women as seem good to you (An-Nisa’: 3), and it is an interrupted exception, because it is an exception of the one whom protection has been shown to him from the soul that commands evil. In the report from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “What do you say about a companion of yours? If you honor him, feed him, and clothe him, he will lead you to the worst end, but if you humiliate him, strip him naked, and starve him, he will lead you to the best end.” They said: O Messenger of God! This is the worst companion on earth. He said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they are your souls that are between your sides.”
12:54: The Almighty said: And the king said, 'Bring him to me, that I may take him as my own person.' When the king's innocence was proven to him, and his trustworthiness was confirmed in the story, and he also understood his patience and endurance, his status with him was great, and his good character was confirmed, he said: Bring him to me, that I may take him as my own person. So look at the king's statement first - when his knowledge was confirmed - Bring him to me only, then when Joseph did what he did, the second time he said: Bring him to me, that I may take him as my own person. It was narrated on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: When Joseph was called, he stood at the door and said: My Lord is sufficient for me against His creation, mighty is His protection, and great is His praise, and there is no god but Him. Then he entered, and when the king looked at him, he got down from his bed and fell down prostrating to him, then the king seated him with him on his bed and said: Indeed, you are today with us, established and trustworthy. Joseph said to him: (Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I am a guardian) of the storehouses Knowing of the aspects of their dealings. It was said: He is a keeper of accounts, knowledgeable of languages. And in the hadith: “May God have mercy on my brother Joseph. If he had not said, ‘Put me in charge of the storehouses of the land,’ He would have appointed him immediately, but He delayed that for a year.” It was said that his kingship was delayed for a year because he did not say, God willing. It was said in this story that when Joseph, peace be upon him, entered upon the king, he said, O God, I ask You for the best of His goodness, and I seek refuge in You from His evil and the evil of others. Then he greeted the king in Arabic and said, What is this language? He said, This is the language of my uncle Ishmael. Then he prayed for him in Hebrew and said, What is this language? He said, The language of my fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. The king spoke in seventy languages, and whenever the king spoke in one language, Joseph would answer him in that language. The king was amazed by his matter, and Joseph was thirty years old at that time. Then he sat him on his bed and said, I would like to hear my vision from you. Joseph said, Yes, O King! I saw seven fat, shining, beautiful cows. The Nile revealed them to you, and they appeared to you from its bank, their offspring gushing forth like wine. While you were looking at them and marveling at their beauty, the Nile dried up, its water subsided, and its base became apparent. Then came out of its mire and mud seven thin, disheveled, dusty cows with shrunken bellies. They had neither udders nor offspring, but fangs and molars, and paws like the paws of dogs and trunks like the trunks of wild beasts. They mingled with the fat cows, and they devoured them like wild beasts, eating their flesh, tearing their skins, crushing their bones, and chewing out their marrow. While you were looking and marveling at how they had defeated them while they were so emaciated! Then no fatness or increase appeared from them after they had been eaten! Behold, there were seven green ears of grain, soft and tender, full of grain and water, and beside them seven dry ones, in which there was neither water nor greenery, in one place, their roots in the soil and water. While you were saying to yourself: What is this?! These are green and fruitful, and those are black and dry, and the place of origin is the same, and their roots are in the water, then a wind blew and scattered the black dry leaves upon the green and fruitful ones, and set them on fire and burned them, and they became black and dusty. I awoke terrified, O king, and the king said: By God, what is the matter with this vision, even though it is more amazing than what I heard from you! What do you see in my vision, O friend? Then Joseph said: I think that you should gather food and plant a lot of crops in these fertile years, for if you were to plant on a stone or a silt, it would grow, and God would show growth and blessing. Then you raise the crops in their reeds and ears and build large storehouses for them, so that the reeds and ears would be fodder for the animals and beloved by the people. And you order the people to raise some of their food to your five granaries, so that the food that you have gathered for the people of Egypt and those around it will suffice you, and people will come to you from all directions to buy from you, and you will gather treasures that no one before you had gathered. The king said: Who will manage these matters? Even if you gathered all the people of Egypt, they would not be able to do so, and they would not be trustworthy. Then Joseph, peace be upon him, said: Make me in charge of the storehouses of the land, meaning in charge of the storehouses of your land, which is the plural of treasury, and the definite article was added instead of the addition, like the saying of Al-Nabigha: They have a quality that God has not given to anyone else, such as generosity and dreams that are not false. The Almighty’s saying: I have chosen him for myself is in the subjunctive mood because it is the answer to a command. This indicates that his saying: That is so that he may know that I have not betrayed him in secret took place in prison. It is possible that it took place with the king, then he said in another session: Bring him to me as emphasis. I will choose him for myself means I will make him purely for myself, I will entrust the matter of my kingdom to him. So they went and brought him. This is indicated by So when he spoke to him meaning the king spoke to Joseph and asked him about the dream, and Joseph answered. So the king said: Indeed, you are today with us, established and trustworthy meaning established and your word is effective, trustworthy not fearing treachery.
12:55: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘Appoint me over the storehouses of the land.’ Saeed bin Mansour said: I heard Malik bin Anas say: Egypt is the storehouse of the land. Have you not heard the words: Appoint me over the storehouses of the land, meaning over its preservation, so the complement was omitted. Indeed, I am a guardian of what I was appointed, Knowing of His command. In the interpretation: Indeed, I am a bookkeeper and a scribe, and that he was the first to write on papers. It was said: A guardian for estimating provisions, Knowing of years of famine. Jubair said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on my brother Joseph. If he had not said, ‘Appoint me over the storehouses of the land,’ He would have appointed him immediately, but he delayed that from him for a year.” Ibn Abbas said: When the year had passed since the day he asked for the emirate, the king summoned him, so he went and dressed him with his sword, and set for him a bed of gold, crowned with pearls and rubies, and put on it a robe of brocade. The bed was thirty cubits long and ten cubits wide, and on it were thirty mattresses and sixty elbows. Then he ordered him to come out, so he came out crowned, his color like snow, and his face like the moon, so that the onlooker would see a face of clarity if it were his face. He sat on the bed and the kings submitted to him, and the king entered his house with his wives, and he entrusted him with the affairs of Egypt, and dismissed Qutfir from what he was in charge of and put Joseph in his place. Ibn Zayd said: Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, had many treasures other than food, so he entrusted all his authority to him, and Qutfir died that night, so the king married Joseph to Rachel, the wife of Al-Aziz. When he entered upon her, he said: Is this not better than what you wanted?! She said: O friend, do not blame me, for I was a beautiful and soft woman as you see, and my companion did not come to women, and I was as God made you of beauty, but my soul overcame me. Then Joseph found her to be a virgin, so he had intercourse with her, and she bore him two men: Ephraim bin Joseph, and Manasseh bin Joseph. Wahb bin Munabbih said: His marriage to Zulaykha, the wife of Al-Aziz, was between the two marriages of the brothers. That was because Zulaykha's husband died while Joseph was in prison, and her wealth was gone and she became blind from weeping over Joseph. So she began to beg from people, some of whom had mercy on her and some of whom did not. Joseph would ride once a week in a procession of about a hundred thousand of the nobles of his people. It was said to him: If you approach him, perhaps he will help you with something. Then it was said to her: Do not do that, for perhaps he will mention some of your advances and imprisonment and he will mistreat you. She said: I know my beloved's character better than you do. Then she left him until he had ridden in his procession, and she stood up and called out at the top of her voice: Glory be to Him who made kings slaves through their disobedience, and made slaves kings through their obedience. Joseph said: What is this? So they brought her, and she said: I am the one who used to serve you on the soles of my feet, and the feet of your head with my hand, and you were brought up in my house, and I honored your abode, but my excessive ignorance and stubbornness made me taste the consequences of my situation, so my wealth was lost, my support weakened, my humiliation lasted a long time, and my sight became blind. After I was the envied one of the people of Egypt, I became the one they had mercy on, begging from people, some of whom had mercy on me, and some of whom did not, and this is the reward of the corruptors. So Joseph wept bitterly, and then he said to her: Do you still find anything of what was in your soul of love for me? She said: By God, a glance at your face is dearer to me than the whole world, but hand me the top of your whip. So he handed it to her and she placed it on her chest. He felt the whip in his hand trembling and shaking from the beating of her heart, so he cried and went to his house and sent a messenger to her: If you are a widow we will marry you, and if you have a husband we will make you rich. She said to the messenger: I seek refuge in God that the king should mock me! He did not want me in the days of my youth, wealth, and pride, so does he want me today when I am an old, blind, and poor man?! So the messenger informed him of her words, and when he rode off in the second week she confronted him, so he said to her: Did the messenger not deliver the message to you? She said: I have told you that one look at your face is dearer to me than the world and everything in it. So he ordered that her condition be fixed and prepared, then she was brought to him. Joseph stood up to pray and supplicate to God, and she stood behind him. He asked God Almighty to restore her youth, beauty and sight. God restored her youth, beauty and sight until she returned to the best she had been on the day he visited her, as an honor to Joseph, peace be upon him, for abstaining from God’s prohibitions. So he had intercourse with her and she was a virgin. He asked her, and she said: O Prophet of God, my husband was impotent and did not come to women, and you were of indescribable beauty and loveliness. He said: So they lived in ease, and every day God renewed for them good, and she bore him two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh. And in what was narrated, God Almighty put in Joseph’s heart many times more love for her than what was in her heart, so he said to her: What is the matter with you that you do not love me as you did the first time? She said to him: When I tasted the love of God Almighty, that occupied me from everything else. Second: Some scholars said: This verse permits a virtuous man to work for an immoral man or an infidel ruler, on condition that he knows that he is entrusted with an action that he does not oppose, so he may correct whatever he wants. However, if his work is according to the choice, desires, and immorality of the immoral person, then this is not permissible. Some people said: This was specifically for Joseph, and this is not permissible today. The first is more appropriate if it is on the condition that we mentioned. And God knows best. Al-Mawardi said: If the one who has a guardianship is unjust, then people have differed about the permissibility of guardianship on his part, with two opinions: The first: Its permissibility if he acts according to what he has been entrusted with, because Joseph was entrusted with guardianship on behalf of Pharaoh, and because the consideration in his right is based on his action, not the action of someone else. The second: That this is not permissible, because it involves taking over the guardianship of the oppressors by helping them, and purifying them by taking over their actions. Those who adopted this school of thought responded to Joseph’s guardianship on behalf of Pharaoh with two answers: The first: That Joseph’s Pharaoh was righteous, and the tyrant was Moses’ Pharaoh. Second: He looked into his property without his actions, so he was not responsible for it. Al-Mawardi said: The most correct of these two statements is to separate what he takes over from the oppressor into three categories: First: What its people are permitted to do without exerting effort in implementing it, such as charity and zakat. It is permissible to take it over from the oppressor, because the text of who deserves it has made it unnecessary to exert effort in it, and the permissibility of its owners being alone with it has made it unnecessary to follow the example. The second category: What it is not permissible for them to do it alone and requires effort in its disbursement, such as the money of spoils. It is not permissible to take it over from the oppressor, because he is acting without right and exerting effort in what he is not entitled to. The third category: What it is permissible to take over from its people, and exerting effort in it has an influence, such as cases and rulings. The contract of following is permissible. If the consideration is to implement the ruling between two consenting parties, and mediation between two who are forced, then it is permissible. If it is a compulsion, then it is not permissible. Third: The verse also indicates that it is permissible for a person to propose a job for which he is qualified. If it is said: Muslim narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: O Abd al-Rahman, do not ask for leadership, for if you are given it after asking, you will be left to it, and if you are given it without asking, you will be helped in it. On the authority of Abu Burdah, he said: Abu Musa said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and with me were two men from the Ash’ariyyin, one on my right and the other on my left, and both of them asked for work, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was using a miswak, so he said: What do you say, O Abu Musa - or O Abdullah bin Qais? He said: I said: By the One Who sent you with the truth, they did not tell me what was in their hearts, and I did not sense that they were asking for work. He said: It was as if I could see his miswak under his lip and it had been trimmed. He said: We will not - or - we will not employ anyone who wants it in our work.” He mentioned the hadith, narrated by Muslim as well as others. The answer is: First: Joseph, peace be upon him, only asked for leadership because he knew that no one could take his place in justice, reform, and delivering the rights of the poor, so he saw that this was an obligation imposed on him, since there was no one else. This is how the ruling is today. If a person knew from himself that he would carry out the right in judging or in hisbah, and there was no one who was suitable or could take his place, then this would be an obligation upon him, and it would be obligatory for him to take charge of it and ask for that, and he should inform of his qualities that he deserves from knowledge. And sufficiency and other than that, as Joseph, peace be upon him, said. But if there is someone who can do it and is fit for it and knows that, then it is better not to ask, because of his saying, peace be upon him, to Abd al-Rahman: Do not ask for leadership. Also, asking for it and being keen on it while knowing the abundance of its harms and the difficulty of getting rid of it is evidence that he is asking for it for himself and for his purposes. And whoever is like this is likely to be overcome by his self and perish. This is the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: And entrust it to her. And whoever rejects it because of his knowledge of its harms and his fear of falling short in its rights, he flees from it. Then if he is afflicted with it, then it is hoped that he will get rid of it, and this is the meaning of his saying: I will help her. The second: He did not say: I am considered noble, even if it is as the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: The noble son of the noble son of the noble son of the noble Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham. Nor did he say: I am handsome and good-looking. Rather, he said: I am Guardian, All-Knowing. So he asked for it through guardianship and knowledge, not through lineage and beauty. Third: He only said that to someone who did not know him, so he wanted to introduce himself, and that became an exception to the Almighty’s saying: So do not claim yourselves to be pure (al-Najm 53:32). Fourth: He saw that as an obligation imposed on him, because there was no one else, and this is more apparent, and God knows best. Fourth: The verse also indicates that it is permissible for a person to describe himself with the knowledge and virtue that he has. Al-Mawardi said: This is not absolute in all attributes, but it is specific to what is coupled with its connection, or related to an apparent gain, and it is forbidden in other than that, because of what is in it of self-praise and hypocrisy. If he had distinguished the one who is more virtuous from him, it would have been more appropriate for his virtue, because necessity called Joseph to it because of his previous condition, and because he hoped to conquer his family.
12:56: The Almighty said: And thus We established Joseph in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed. That is, and like this favor that We bestowed upon him in bringing him close to the king's heart, and saving him from prison, We established him in the land, that is, We enabled him to do whatever he wanted. Al-Kiya al-Tabari said: The Almighty's statement: And thus We established Joseph in the land is evidence of the permissibility of trickery in reaching what is permissible, and what contains happiness and goodness, and extracting rights. Similar to it is the statement of the Almighty: And take in your hand a bunch and strike with it and do not break your oath. (Surah Sad: 44) and the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri about the governor of Khaybar, who gave dates to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what he said. I said: This is refuted by what follows. It is said: We established him and We established him. God the Almighty said: We established them in the land as We did not establish you. (Surah al-An'am: 6). Al-Tabari said: The great king Al-Walid bin Al-Rayyan appointed Joseph as his successor in the affairs of Itafir and dismissed him. Mujahid said: He converted to Islam at his hands. Ibn Abbas said: He became king after a year and a half. Muqatil narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If Joseph had said, ‘Indeed, I am a guardian and a knower,’ if God should be displeased, he would have become king in his time. Then Itafir died, so Al-Walid married him to Itafir’s wife, Ra’il. Joseph consummated the marriage with her and found her to be a virgin. She bore him two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, the sons of Joseph. Whoever claims that she was Zulaykha said: Joseph did not marry her, and that when she saw him in his procession, she cried, then said: Praise be to God who made kings slaves through disobedience, and praise be to God who made slaves kings through obedience. So he took her to himself, and she was one of his dependents until she died with him, and he did not marry her. Al-Mawardi mentioned this, and it is contrary to what was mentioned previously from Wahb, and Al-Tha’labi mentioned it, and God knows best. When the king entrusted the affairs of Egypt to Joseph, he was kind to the people and called them to Islam until they believed in him. He established justice among them, and men and women loved him. Wahb, Al-Suddi, Ibn Abbas, and others said: Then the fertile years came, so Joseph ordered the farms to be repaired and ordered them to expand their agriculture. When the crops were ripe, he ordered them to be collected, then he built granaries for them, and in that year they collected a crop that the storehouses could not handle because of its abundance. Then he collected the crops of every year in the same way, until when the seven fertile years had passed and the barren years came, Gabriel came down and said: O people of Egypt, starve, for God has sent famine upon you for seven years. Some of the wise men said: Hunger and famine have two signs: One of them is that the soul loves food more than usual, and hunger rushes to it, unlike what it was before, and it takes more food than is sufficient. The second is that food is lost and is not found at all and is extremely scarce. These two signs came together during the time of Joseph, so men, women, and children woke up calling out, Hunger, hunger! And they eat and are not satisfied, and the king wakes up, calling out, Hunger, Hunger!! He said: So Joseph prayed for him and God cured him of that, then in the morning Joseph called out throughout the land of Egypt, O people! No one should plant a crop or the seed will be lost and nothing will grow. And those years brought great terror that cannot be described, Ibn Abbas said: When the drought began while the king was in the middle of the night, hunger struck him in the middle of the night, so the king cried out, O Joseph! Hunger, hunger!! Then Joseph said: This is the time of famine. When the first year of the famine came, everything they had prepared in the fertile years perished. The people of Egypt began to buy food from Joseph. He sold them the first year for money, until there was not a dinar or a dirham left in Egypt except a handful. In the second year he sold them for jewelry and jewels, until there was nothing left in the people’s hands. In the third year he sold them for livestock and beasts, until he had taken possession of them all. In the fourth year he sold them for male and female slaves, until he had taken possession of them all. In the fifth year he sold them for real estate and farms, until he owned them all. In the sixth year he sold them for their children and women, enslaving them all. In the seventh year he sold them for their necks, until in the seventh year there was not a free man or slave left in Egypt except that he became his slave. The people said: By God, we have never seen a king more magnificent or greater than this. Joseph said to the king of Egypt: How do you see the work of my Lord in what He has given me? Now all this is yours, so what do you think of it? He said: I have entrusted the matter to you, so do as you wish. We are your followers, and I am not one who would disdain your worship and obedience, nor am I except one of your slaves and a subordinate of yours. Joseph, peace be upon him, said: I did not free them from hunger to distance them, nor did I save them from calamity to be a calamity for them. I call God and you to witness that I freed the people of Egypt to the last one, and I returned their money and property to them, and I returned your kingdom to you on the condition that you follow my Sunnah. It is narrated that Joseph, peace be upon him, was never satisfied with food in those years, so it was said to him: Are you hungry while you have the treasures of the earth in your hand? He said: I fear that if I am satisfied I will forget the hungry. Joseph ordered the king’s cook to make his food at noon, so that the king would taste hunger and not forget the hungry. That is why the kings made their food at noon. God the Almighty says: We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will. That is, with Our goodness. Mercy is grace and goodness. And We do not allow to be lost the reward of the doers of good. That is, their recompense. Ibn Abbas and Wahb said: He means the patient ones, for his patience in the well, in slavery, and in prison, and his patience from the prohibitions of God when the woman called him to do. Al-Mawardi said: There are two opinions regarding what Joseph was given in this state: One of them is that it was a reward from God the Almighty for what He tested him with. The second is that God bestowed this upon him as a favor from Him, and his reward will remain the same in the Hereafter.
12:57: The Almighty says: And the reward of the Hereafter is better meaning that what we are given in the Hereafter is better and more than what we were given in this world, because the reward of the Hereafter is permanent, while the reward of this world is cut off. The apparent meaning of the verse is general for every believing, pious person. They recited: Is not the Messenger of God, Joseph, an example for someone like you, imprisoned for injustice and slander? Jamil al-Sabr stayed in prison for a while, then Jamil al-Sabr led him to the king. Some of them wrote to a friend of his: Behind the strait of fear is the vastness of security, and the first joy is the last of sorrow. Do not despair, for God has given Joseph His treasures after his release from prison. Some of them recited: If the incidents reached the limit and the souls almost melted for them The calamity has come and consolation has diminished, for at the end comes relief. There is a lot of poetry in this sense.
12:58: The Almighty said: And the brothers of Joseph came meaning they came to Egypt when they were afflicted with famine to buy provisions. This is from the abbreviation of the miraculous Qur'an. Ibn Abbas and others said: When the people were afflicted with famine and hardship, and that descended upon the land of Canaan, Jacob, peace be upon him, sent his son to provide provisions, and the story of Joseph, peace be upon him, spread far and wide, due to his gentleness, closeness, mercy, compassion, justice, and conduct. When the hardship descended upon the people, Joseph, peace be upon him, would sit with the people at the sale himself, and give them food according to the number of their heads, a wasq for each head. And the brothers of Joseph came and entered upon him, and Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him because they left him as a boy, and they did not imagine that after slavery he would reach that state of kingdom, despite the long period, which was forty years. It was said: They denied him because they believed that he was an infidel king. It was said: They saw him wearing silk, with a gold necklace around his neck, and a crown on his head, and he was dressed in the garb of the Pharaoh of Egypt, and Joseph saw them in their usual clothing and adornment. It is possible that they saw him covered and did not recognize him. It was said: They denied him because of a supernatural matter, a test with which God tested Jacob.
12:59: The Almighty said: And when he had furnished them with their trousseau It is said that he furnished the people with their trousseau, meaning he took care of their trousseau for the journey, and the trousseau of the bride is what is needed when giving it to the husband, and some of the Kufians permitted the trousseau with a kasra on the jim, and the trousseau in this verse is the food that they bought from him. Al-Suddi said: And with Joseph's brothers were eleven camels, and they were ten, so they said to Joseph: We have a brother who stayed behind from us, and his camel is with us, so he asked them why it stayed behind? They said: Because of his father's love for him, and they mentioned to him that he had an older brother who went out to the wilderness and died, so he said to them: I wanted to see this brother of yours whom you mentioned, to know the reason for your father's love for him, and to know your truthfulness, and it is narrated that they left Simeon with him as a hostage, until they brought his brother Benjamin. Ibn Abbas said: Joseph said to the interpreter: Tell them: Your language is different from our language, and your dress is different from our dress, so perhaps you are spies. They said: By God! We are not spies, but we are the sons of one father, who is an old and truthful man. He said: How many are you? They said: Like twelve. One of our brothers went to the desert and died there. He said: Where is the other? They said: With our father. He said: Who knows your truthfulness? They said: No one here knows us, and we have made you aware of our lineage, so how can you feel at ease with us? Joseph said: Bring me a brother of yours from your father if you are truthful, for I am satisfied with that. Do you not see that I give full measure? That is, I complete it and do not withhold it, and I give you an extra camel load for your brother. But if you do not bring him to me, then you will have no measure with me. He threatened them that he would not sell them food if they did not bring him. The Almighty’s statement: Do you not see that I give full measure? has two possible interpretations: One is that He granted them a discount on the price, so it became an increase in the measure. The second is that He measured for them with a full measure. And I am the best of hosts has two possible interpretations: One is that He is the best of hosts, because He treated them well, as Mujahid said. The second is possible, meaning the best of those you have stayed with from those who are trustworthy. According to the first interpretation, it is taken from nuzul which means food, and according to the second, from manzar which means a house.
12:60: The Almighty said: But if you do not bring him to me, then you will have no measure with me meaning, I will not sell you anything afterward, because he has already given them their measure in this case. And do not come near meaning, I will not treat you as a relative with me. He did not mean that they will be far from him or return to him, because he urged them to return. Al-Suddi said: And he asked them for a hostage until they return, so Shimon took a hostage with him. Al-Kalbi said: He chose Shimon from them because he was the most beautiful of them in speech on the day of the well, and the best of them in opinion. And taqribun is in the position of a jazm of prohibition, so the nun was deleted from it and the ya was deleted, because it is the beginning of a verse. If it were a predicate, taqribun would have been with a fatha on the nun.
12:61: God Almighty says: They said, ‘We will seek him out from his father.’ That is, we will ask him and ask him to send him with us. And indeed, we will do so. That is, we will guarantee to bring him, and we will scheme to do so. Question: If it is said: How did Joseph seek refuge in bringing grief to his father by asking for his brother? It is said to him: There are four answers to this: The first: It is possible that God Almighty commanded him to do that as a test for Jacob, to increase his reward, so he followed His command in it. The second: It is possible that he wanted to alert Jacob to the condition of Joseph, peace be upon them. The third: To multiply Jacob’s joy at the return of his two sons to him. The fourth: To give precedence to his brother’s joy at being reunited with him before his brothers, due to his inclination towards him, and the first is more apparent, and God knows best.
12:62: The Almighty said: "And he said to his young men" This is the reading of the people of Medina, Abu Amr and Asim, and it is the choice of Abu Hatim, Al-Nahhas and others. The rest of the Kufians read li-fitanihi and it is the choice of Abu Ubaid, and he said: It is also in Abdullah's copy of the Qur'an. Al-Tha'labi said: They are two good languages, like al-sibyan and al-sabiya. Al-Nahhas said: li-fitanihi is contrary to the vast majority, because in al-sawwad there is no alif or nun, and the majority that is agreed upon is not abandoned due to this broken chain of transmission. Also, fatiha is more similar to fityan, because fatiha among the Arabs is for the smallest number, and the few are more similar to putting the merchandise in the saddlebags. These young men were preparing their equipment, and for this reason they were able to put their merchandise in their saddlebags. It is possible that they were free, and they were his helpers, and their merchandise was the price of what they bought of food. It was said: It was dirhams and dinars. Ibn Abbas said: Sandals, leather, and the traveler's belongings, and it is called a saddle. Ibn al-Anbari said: A container is called a saddle, and a house is called a saddle. He said: "Perhaps they will recognize it" because it is permissible not to hand it over on the road. It was said: He did that so that they would return if they found that, because he knew that they would not accept food except for its price. It was said: So that they would be helped by that to return to buy food. It was said: He thought it ugly to take the price of the food from his father and brothers. It was said: So that they would see his virtue and desire to return to him.
12:63: The Almighty said: So when they returned to their father, they said, 'O our father, we have been denied measure.' Because he said to them: If you do not bring him to me, you will have no measure with me. And they informed him of what had happened to them and his honoring them, and that Simon was held hostage until he knew the truth of what they said. Then send our brother with us, and we will measure. That is, they said at that time: Then send our brother with us, and we will measure. The original is naktal, so the damma was deleted from the lam for the jussive, and the alif was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The people of the two sanctuaries, Abu Amr, and Asim read naktal with a noon, and the rest of the Kufians read yaktal with a ya, and the first is the choice of Abu Ubaid, so that they would all be included in those who measure. He claimed that if it was with a ya, it would be for the brother alone. An-Nahhas said: This is not necessary, because the speech is not devoid of one of two aspects: that the meaning is: So send our brother to measure with us, in which case it is for everyone, or that the estimation is not based on the advancement and delay, in which case there is evidence in the speech for everyone, because of his saying: But if you do not bring him to me, then you will have no measure with me. And indeed, We will guard him from harm befalling him.
12:64: The Almighty said: He said, 'Shall I trust you with him except as I trusted you with his brother before?' That is, you had been careless with Joseph, so how could he trust you with his brother?! Then God is the best guardian. The accusative is an explanatory word, and this is the reading of the people of Medina, Abu Amr, and Asim. The rest of the Kufians read Hafizan as a state. Al-Zajjaj said: It is an explanatory word, and in this is evidence that he responded to their request to send him with them, and the meaning of the verse is: God's protection of him is better than your protection of him. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: When Jacob said: Then God is the best guardian, God the Almighty said: By My glory and majesty, I will surely return to you both your sons after you have put your trust in Me.
12:65: The Almighty's saying: "And when they opened their baggage" The verse does not contain any problematic meaning. "What do we seek?" Ma is an interrogative in the accusative case, and the meaning is: What do we seek beyond this?! He gave us full measure and returned the price to us, they wanted to please their father. It was said: It is negative, meaning we do not seek from you dirhams or merchandise, rather our merchandise that was returned to us is sufficient for us. It was narrated from Alqamah Radt ilaina with a kasra on the ra, because the original is raddat, but when it was assimilated, the vowel of the dal was changed to the ra. And his saying: "And we provide food for our people" means we bring them food. The poet said: I sent you as a guide, but you stayed for a year. When will your help come? Al-Salami read it with a damma on the letter nun, meaning we help them with provisions. And we will give them an additional camel load, that is an easy load, meaning a camel load for Benjamin.
12:66: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: You will give me meaning you will give me. A pledge from God Al-Suddi said: They swore by God that He would return him to Him and not hand him over, and the lam in that you will give me is the lam of an oath. Unless you are surrounded Mujahid said: Unless you perish or die. Qatada said: Unless you overcome him. Al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative case. So when they gave him their pledge, He said, ‘God is Witness over what we say’ meaning He keeps the oath. It was said: He keeps the covenant, upholding management and justice. Second: This verse is the basis for the permissibility of bearing a person’s body and a document for a soul. Scholars have differed on this. Malik, all his companions, and most scholars said: It is permissible if the one bearing it is money. Al-Shafi’i weakened bearing a person’s body in money, and he had a statement similar to Malik’s. Uthman al-Batti said: If he guarantees a person in retaliation or wounds, then if he does not bring it, he is obligated to pay the blood money and compensation for the wounds, and it is his from the offender’s money, since there is no retaliation for the guarantor. So these are three statements on bearing a person’s body in money. The correct view is Malik’s distinction in this, and that it is in money, and not in a prescribed punishment or discretionary punishment, as will be explained.
12:67: It contains seven issues: First: When they decided to leave, he feared the evil eye for them, so he ordered them not to enter Egypt through one gate, and Egypt had four gates. He only feared the evil eye for them because they were eleven men for one man, and they were people of beauty, perfection, and abundance, as Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, and others said. Second: If this is the meaning of the verse, then it is evidence of guarding against the evil eye, and the evil eye is real. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The evil eye can cause a man to enter the grave and a camel to enter the cooking pot. And in his supplication, may God bless him and grant him peace: I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from every devil and pest and from every evil eye, there is evidence of that. Malik narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf that he heard his father say: “My father Sahl ibn Hunayf performed ablution in Al-Kharar and took off the cloak he was wearing, and ‘Amir ibn Rabi’ah was watching. He said: Sahl was a white man with good skin. ‘Amir ibn Rabi’ah said to him: ‘I have never seen anything like today, nor the skin of a virgin!’ Sahl fell ill in his place and his illness became severe. He went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and was informed that Sahl had fallen ill and that he would not go with you, O Messenger of God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and Sahl told him what had happened to ‘Amir. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Why would one of you kill his brother? Why don’t you bless him? The evil eye is real. Perform ablution for him.’ So ‘Amir performed ablution, and Sahl went with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there was nothing wrong with him. In another narration: ‘He performed ablution,’ and ‘Amir washed his face, hands, elbows, knees, and the tips of his feet, and inside his lower garment in a cup, then poured water over him. So Sahl went with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there was nothing wrong with him.” “One day, Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas rode and a woman looked at him and said: Your emir knows that he has lost both sides. He returned to his house and fell down. He heard what the woman had said, so he sent for her and she washed him.” In these two hadiths, it is clear that the evil eye is real and that it kills, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said. This is the opinion of the scholars of the ummah and the doctrine of the people of the Sunnah. It has been denied by groups of innovators, who are refuted by the Sunnah and the consensus of the scholars of this ummah, and by what is seen in existence. How many men have been put in the grave by the evil eye, and how many camels have been put in the grave by fate. But that is by the will of God Almighty, as He said: And they can not harm anyone thereby except by God’s permission. (al-Baqarah 2:102). Al-Asma`i said: I saw a man with eyes who heard a cow being milked and its bleating pleased him, so he said: Which one is this? They said: So-and-so belongs to another cow that they are covering up for, so they both perished, the one being milked and the one being covered up. Al-Asma`i said: I heard him say: When I see something that pleases me, I feel heat coming out of my eye. Third: It is obligatory for every Muslim who likes something to offer blessings, because if he asks for blessings, the forbidden thing will inevitably be averted. Do you not see his saying, peace be upon him, to Amer: Why did you not offer blessings? This indicates that the evil eye does not harm or spread if the one who casts the evil eye offers blessings, and that it only spreads if he does not offer blessings. Blessing is to say: Blessed be God, the best of creators! May God bless him. Fourth: If the one who cast the evil eye is not blessed, then he is ordered to perform ablution, and he is forced to do so if he refuses, because the order is obligatory, especially this, as there is fear that the one who was cast the evil eye will perish, and no one should prevent his brother from something that benefits his brother and does not harm him, especially if it was because of him and he was the one who wronged him. Fifth: Whoever is known to have been afflicted by the evil eye is prevented from interacting with people to ward off harm. Some scholars have said: The Imam orders him to stay at home, and if he is poor, he provides him with what he needs to do, and he refrains from harming people. It has also been said: He is banished, and the hadith of Malik that we mentioned refutes these statements, for he, peace be upon him, did not order that Aamer be imprisoned or banished. Rather, a righteous man may be afflicted by the evil eye, and he is not to be denounced or accused of immorality. Whoever says: He is to be imprisoned and ordered to stay at home, this is a precaution and to ward off harm, and God knows best. Sixth: Malik narrated on the authority of Humayd ibn Qays al-Makki that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon the sons of Ja`far ibn Abi Talib and said to their wet nurse: ‘Why do I see them begging? ’ Their wet nurse said: ‘O Messenger of God! The evil eye hastens to them, and nothing prevented us from performing ruqyah for them except that we do not know what would suit you. ’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Perform ruqyah for them, for if anything precedes destiny, it is the evil eye. ’” This hadith is disconnected, but it is preserved on the authority of Asma’ bint Umays al-Khath’amiyyah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, through authentic, connected, authentic chains of transmission. It states that ruqyah is one of the ways to ward off calamity, and that the evil eye affects a person and makes him humble, i.e., weakens him and makes him weak, and that is by the decree and predestination of God Almighty. It is said that the evil eye is quicker to affect children than it is to affect adults, and God knows best. Seventh: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered in the hadith of Abu Umamah the one who cast the evil eye to perform ablution for the one who was afflicted, and here he ordered the use of ruqyah. Our scholars said: Ruqyah is only used for the evil eye if the one who cast the evil eye is not known. However, if the one who cast the evil eye is known, then he is ordered to perform ablution according to the hadith of Abu Umamah. God knows best. God Almighty says: And I cannot avail you at all against God meaning at all that I warn you against, meaning caution is of no use with destiny. The judgment meaning the command and decree. “is only for God. Upon Him I have relied” meaning I have depended and trusted. And upon Him let the reliant rely.
12:68: The Almighty said: And when they entered from where their father had commanded them meaning from various gates. It could not have availed them against God at all if He had intended to bring about harm to them. Except for a need is an exception not from the first. In the soul of Jacob He fulfilled it meaning a thought that crossed his heart, which was his command that they should disperse. Mujahid said: Fear of the evil eye, and this has been discussed previously. It was said: So that the king would not see their number and strength and strike them out of envy or caution. This was said by some of the later scholars, and An-Nahhas chose it, and said: There is no meaning to the evil eye here. This verse indicates that a Muslim must warn his brother of what he fears for him, and guide him to what is the path to safety and salvation, because religion is advice, and a Muslim is a brother of a Muslim. God Almighty says: And indeed he meaning Jacob. was possessed of knowledge because of what We taught him meaning of his religion. But most of the people do not know meaning they do not know what Jacob, peace be upon him, knew about his religion. It was said: possessed of knowledge meaning action, because knowledge is the first cause of action, so it was named for what it is because of.
12:69: The Almighty said: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother into his care. Qatada said: He took him into his care and made him stay with him. It was said: He ordered that every two people stay in a house, so his brother remained alone, so he took him into his care and said: I feared for him from being alone, and he said to him secretly from his brothers: Indeed, I am your brother, so do not be sad meaning do not be grieved for what they used to do.
12:70: The Almighty said: So when he had furnished them with their provisions, he put the drinking cup in his brother's saddlebag. When Benjamin knew that he was Joseph, he said to him: Do not return me to them. He said: I know Jacob's grief over me, and his grief will increase. Benjamin refused to go out, and Joseph said: You cannot be detained unless I attribute to you something that is not appropriate for you. He said: I do not care! So he slipped the measure into his saddlebag, either himself, where no one knew about it, or he ordered one of his confidants to do so. Preparation means releasing and completing a matter. From this comes the phrase finished the wounded, meaning he killed him and completed his matter. The drinking cup and the measure are one thing, a vessel with two heads in the middle of which is a handle. The king used to drink from one head, and the food was measured with the other head. Al-Naqqash said this on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Everything that is drunk from is a measure. He recited: We drink wine by the cup openly There is a difference of opinion about its type. Shu’bah narrated on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The king’s sa’ was something made of silver that resembled a shuttle, made of silver studded with jewels, and it was placed on the head. Al-Abbas had one in the pre-Islamic era. Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq asked him what the sa’ was. He said: The vessel. Al-A’sha said about it: He has a dirham on his head, a drinker, a pot, a cooker, a saa' and a daisaq. Akrima said: It was made of silver. Abdurrahman bin Zaid said: It was made of gold, and their food was measured with it to exaggerate their honor. It was also said: It was measured with it because food was precious. The Saa' is both masculine and feminine. Whoever feminizes it says: Aswa', like Adour, and whoever masculines it says Aswa', like Athwaab. Mujahid and Abu Salih said: The Saa' is Tarjhala in the language of Himyar. There are readings for it: Sawa' is the reading of the common people, and Sawgh with the emphatic ghain, which is the reading of Yahya bin Ya'mar. He said: It was a golden vessel. Saw' with the unvoiced 'ayn, which is the reading of Abu Raja. Saw' with a damma on the 'sad' and a silent 'w and an unvoiced 'ayn, which is the reading of Abu. Wsi' with a ya' between the 'sad' and the 'alif, which is the reading of Sa'id bin Jubayr. Wsi' with an alif between the 'sad' and the 'ayn, which is the reading of Abu Hurayrah. God the Almighty said: “Then a crier proclaimed: ‘O caravan, you are indeed thieves.’” That is, a crier called out and informed. And proclaimed is for emphasis, as if he called repeatedly: O caravan. A caravan is a group of donkeys, camels, and mules that are ridden. Mujahid said: Their caravan was a group of donkeys. Abu Ubaidah said: The caravan is the ridden camels, and the meaning is: O owners of the caravan, like His statement: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82) and O horses of God, ride meaning: O owners of the horses of God, and it will come. Here are two objections: The first - if it is said: How did Benjamin accept to sit voluntarily, while it is disobedient to his father by increasing his grief, and Joseph agreed with him on that? And how did Joseph attribute the theft to his brothers when they were innocent, and he - the second - the answer to the first: That grief had overcome Jacob to the point that the loss of Benjamin did not affect him at all, or you did not see that when he lost him, he said: Oh my grief for Joseph and did not mention Benjamin, and perhaps Joseph agreed with him on sitting by revelation, so there is no objection. As for Joseph’s attribution of theft to his brothers, the answer is: The people had stolen him from his father, thrown him into the well, then sold him, and thus they deserved this name for that action, so it is true that they were called that. Another answer is that he meant, O caravan, your condition is that of thieves, meaning: Something that belongs to someone other than you has come to you without the king’s consent or knowledge. Another answer is that this was a ruse to reunite him with his brother and separate him from them to him. This is based on the fact that Benjamin did not know about the stash of the measure in his saddlebag, nor did he tell him about it himself. It has been said that the meaning of the statement is a question, meaning, Or are you thieves? Like his saying, And that is a blessing (Ash-Shu’ara’: 22), meaning, Or is that a blessing that you bestow upon me? The purpose is not to attribute lying to Joseph, peace be upon him.
12:71: It contains seven issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And whoever brings it will have a camel-load, and I will be its guarantor. The camel here is the male camel according to most commentators. It was said that it is the donkey, and it is the language of some Arabs, as Mujahid said and chose. Mujahid said: The leader is the muezzin who said: O caravan. The leader, the guarantor, the loader, the guarantor, and the tribe are all the same, and the leader is the chief. He said: I swear that if I return as a kingdom, you will see the Franks turning away. Laila Al-Akhiliya said, mourning her brother: And his shirt is torn, you would think he is sick on the day of the meeting because of shyness. Even if the banner is raised, you will see him under the banner on Thursday, a leader. Second: If it is said: How did he guarantee the camel’s load when it is unknown, and guaranteeing the unknown is not valid? It is said to him: The camel’s load was specific and known to them like a wasq, so guaranteeing it is valid, except that it was in exchange for money for the thief, and that is not permissible for the thief, so perhaps it was valid according to their law or this was a reward, and money was given to whoever was searching and seeking. Third: Some scholars said: In this verse there are two proofs: The first is the permissibility of the reward, and it was permitted due to necessity, because ignorance is permitted in it that is not permitted in other cases. So if a man says: Whoever does such-and-such will have such-and-such, it is valid. The nature of the reward is that one of the two parties is known and the other is unknown due to necessity for it, unlike the lease, in which the compensation and the thing being compensated are determined from both sides. It is one of the permissible contracts that one of them may cancel, except that the one to whom the reward is made may cancel it before and after starting, if he agrees to drop his right, and the one who makes the reward is not allowed to cancel it if the one to whom the reward is made starts the work. The presence of the contracting parties is not a condition in the contract of reward, like other contracts.
12:72: Because he said: And whoever brings it shall have a camel load. And all of this was said by Al-Shafi’i. Fourth: When a person says, Whoever brings my runaway slave will have a dinar, he is obligated to pay what he put in it if he brings him. But if he brings him without guarantee, he is obligated to pay if he brings him seeking payment. This is because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever brings a runaway slave will have forty dirhams, and he did not differentiate between who brought him with a guarantee or without a contract. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said, “This is why our companions said: Whoever does to a person what he should do himself for his own interests, he is obligated to do so, and he will have a reward similar to that if he is one of those who do that for payment.” I said: Al-Shafi’i disagreed with us on all of this. Fifth: - The second evidence - The permissibility of the guarantee for a man, because the muezzin who is the guarantor is not Joseph, peace be upon him. Our scholars said: If a man says: I have taken on responsibility or I have guaranteed or I have made surety or I am your guardian or a leader or a guarantor or a guarantor or a tribe, or it is yours with me or against me or to me or before me, then all of that is a binding burden. The jurists differed about the one who guarantees the life or the face, is he obligated to guarantee the money or not? The Kufians said: Whoever guarantees the life of a man is not obligated to the right that is on the wanted person if he dies, and this is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i in the well-known opinion from him. Malik, Al-Layth and Al-Awza’i said: If he guarantees himself and he has money, then if he does not bring it, he is liable for the money and can recover it from the wanted person. If he stipulates the guarantee of his life or face and says: I do not guarantee the money, then he is not obligated to pay anything from the money. The evidence for those who require the guarantee of the money is that the guarantor knows that the guaranteed face is not demanded by blood money, but rather it is demanded by money, so if he guarantees it for him and he does not bring it, then it is as if he missed it and was unable to do so, so the money is obligatory for him. Al-Tahawi argued for the Kufians, saying: As for guaranteeing the money in the event of the death of the person guaranteed, it has no meaning, because he only guaranteed the life and did not guarantee the money, so it is impossible for him to be obligated to do something that he did not guarantee. Sixth: The scholars differed if a man guarantees money on behalf of another man, can the claimant take from whomever he wants from them? Al-Thawri, the Kufians, Al-Awza’i, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and Ishaq said: He may take from whomever he wants until he gets his right. This was the opinion of Malik, then he changed his mind and said: The guarantor is not to be taken unless the creditor goes bankrupt or disappears, because it is more appropriate to give in return the one who owes him the right, unless he is destitute, in which case it is taken from the one who is responsible, because he is excused for taking it in this case. This is a good opinion. The analogy is that the man has the right to demand whichever of the two men he wants. Ibn Abi Laila said: If a man guarantees money on behalf of his friend, it is transferred to the guarantor and the owner of the original is released, unless the one for whom the guarantee is made stipulates that he may take whichever he wants. He argued that the deceased is released from the debt by the guarantee of Abu Qatada, and Abu Thawr said something similar. Seventh: Leadership is only in rights in which representation is permissible, such as those related to the conscience of money, and which are fixed and stable. Therefore, the burden in writing is not valid because it is not a fixed and stable debt, because if the slave is unable to become a slave and the writing is annulled. As for every right that no one can carry out for another, such as the prescribed punishments, there is no guarantee in it, and the defendant who is accused of the prescribed punishment is imprisoned until his case is considered. Abu Yusuf and Muhammad differed and permitted bail in cases of prescribed punishments and retaliation. They said: If the slandered person or the claimant of retaliation says: My evidence is present, his bail is for three days. Al-Tahawi provided evidence for them with what Hamza bin Amr narrated on the authority of Umar, Ibn Masoud, Jarir bin Abdullah, and Al-Ash’ath, that they ruled on bail for the person in the presence of the Companions.
12:73: The Almighty said: They said, 'By God, you know that we have not come to cause corruption in the land.' It is narrated that they did not attack anyone unjustly, nor did they tend anyone's crops, and that they gathered their camels on the mouths of the hill so that they would not spoil people's crops. Then He said: And we were not thieves. It is narrated that they returned the merchandise that was in their saddlebags, meaning that whoever returns what he finds, how can he be a thief?!
12:74: God Almighty said: They said, ‘What is his penalty, if you are liars?’ Meaning: What is the penalty of the doer if your lie is revealed? So Joseph’s brothers answered:
12:75: His punishment is he in whose saddlebag it is found, that is his punishment meaning he will be excluded and enslaved. (His punishment) is the subject, and he in whose saddlebag it is found is its predicate, and the meaning is: his punishment is the exclusion of he in whose saddlebag it is found, so it is a metaphor for exclusion, and the sentence has the meaning of emphasis, as you say: the punishment of he who steals is to be cut off, so this is his punishment. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers meaning thus do We do to the wrongdoers if they steal, that they be enslaved, and this was from the religion of Jacob, peace be upon him, and his ruling. Their saying this is the saying of one who did not suspect himself, because they committed to enslaving he in whose saddlebag it was found, and the ruling of the thief among the people of Egypt was that he should pay double what he took, as stated by Al-Hasan, Al-Suddi, and others. Question: It was mentioned in Surat Al-Ma’idah that cutting off the hand for theft abrogates what was mentioned in the previous laws, or what was in the law of Jacob regarding enslaving the thief, and God knows best.
12:76: The Almighty said: So he began with their vessels before his brother's vessel. Joseph began with their luggage to remove suspicion and doubt from their hearts if he began with his brother's vessel. The vessel is said with a damma or a kasra on the waw, two languages, and it is what the goods are kept in and preserved. Then he extracted it from his brother's vessel, meaning Benjamin, meaning he extracted the water-skin or the cup when it is feminine, and he said: And for whoever brings it when it is masculine. When his brothers saw that, they lowered their heads and suspected all sorts of things, and they turned to him and said: Woe to you, Benjamin! We have never seen anything like today, your mother Rachel gave birth to two thief brothers! Their brother said to them: By God, I did not steal it, and I do not know who put it in my luggage. It is narrated that they said to him: O Benjamin! Did you steal? He said: No, by God. They said: Who put the cup in your luggage? He said: The one who put the merchandise in your luggage. It is said that when the inspector finished with a man’s saddle, he would seek forgiveness from God Almighty, repenting for his action. The apparent words of Qatada and others are that the one seeking forgiveness was Joseph, because he was searching them and knowing where the cup was until he finished with them. He reached Benjamin’s saddle and said: I do not think this young man was satisfied with this or took anything. His brothers said to him: By God, we will not leave until you search it, for it is better for you and for us. So he searched and brought out the water-skin. This search by Joseph necessitates that the muezzin stole them on his own initiative. It is said that all of that was by the command of God Almighty, and this is strengthened by His Almighty’s saying: Thus did We plan for Joseph. God Almighty says: Thus did We plan for Joseph. There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: We almost means we made, according to Ibn Abbas. Al-Qatabi: We planned. Ibn Al-Anbari: We intended. The poet said: Almost, almost, and that is the best will if what has passed from the time of youth were to return It includes the permissibility of achieving goals through tricks if they do not contradict the Sharia or destroy the foundation, in contrast to Abu Hanifa who permits tricks even if they contradict the foundations and violate the permissibility. Second: The scholars agreed that a man has the right to dispose of his money by selling or giving it away before the year ends if he does not intend to escape from paying zakat. They also agreed that if the year ends and the collector is present, he is not permitted to use trickery or to reduce it, or to separate what is combined or to bring together what is separated. Malik said: If he misses something from his money with the intention of escaping zakat before the year by a month or so, then zakat is obligatory upon him upon the year, based on the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): For fear of zakat. Abu Hanifa said: If he intends by distributing it to escape zakat before the year by a day, it does not harm him, because zakat is not obligatory until the year is complete, and the meaning of his saying: For fear of zakat does not apply to him except at that time. Ibn al-Arabi said: I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Fihri and others say: Our sheikh, the chief justice Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Ali al-Damaghani, had tens of thousands of dinars of wealth. When the year came, he would call his sons and say to them: I have grown old and my strength has weakened, and this money I do not need, so it is yours. Then he would take it out and the men would carry it on their necks to his sons’ homes. When the year came, he would call his sons for some reason and they would say: O our father! We only hope for your life, but as for the money, what desire do we have for it as long as you are alive? You and your wealth are ours, so take it to you. And the men would walk with it until they put it in front of him, and he would return it to its place. By changing ownership, he meant to drop the zakat according to the opinion of Abu Hanifa in separating what is common and bringing together what is dispersed. This is a great matter. Al-Bukhari, may God be pleased with him, wrote a specific book in his collection, which he called: The Book of Tricks. I said: And he translated into it chapters, including: Chapter on zakat and not separating between those who are united nor bringing together those who are separated for fear of charity. And he included in it the hadith of Anas bin Malik, and that Abu Bakr wrote for him the obligatory charity, and the hadith of Talha bin Ubaidullah that a Bedouin came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with unkempt hair. The hadith, and at the end of it: He will succeed if he is truthful or he will enter Paradise if he is truthful. Some people said: There are two haqahs for one hundred and twenty camels. If he intentionally destroys them, gives them away, or uses a trick to avoid zakat, then there is nothing wrong with him. Then he added the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The treasure of one of you on the Day of Resurrection will be a bald-headed, two-horned horse that says, ‘I am your treasure.’ Al-Muhallab said: Al-Bukhari intended in this chapter to inform you that every trick that someone uses to avoid zakat is sinful for him, because when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade gathering and distributing sheep for fear of zakat, this meaning was understood from him. And he understood from his saying: He who is truthful will succeed, that whoever seeks to violate one of God’s obligations by a trick he uses will not succeed, and his excuse before God will not be valid. What the jurists permitted of the owner of the wealth disposing of his wealth close to the end of the year is only what he did not intend to avoid zakat. Whoever intended that, then the sin is not dropped from him, and God is his judge, and he is like one who fled from… Fasting Ramadan a day before the crescent moon is sighted, and he uses a journey that he does not need, desiring to avoid the obligation that God has prescribed for the believers, then the threat is directed at him. Do you not see the punishment of the one who deliberately withholds Zakat on the Day of Resurrection in any way? How the camels trample him, and his wealth appears to him as a bald-headed snake!? This indicates that fleeing from Zakat is not permissible, and he will be required to do so in the Hereafter. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: Some Shafi’i scholars said about the Almighty’s statement: Thus did We plan for Joseph; he would not have taken his brother. It is evidence of a trick to the permissible and extract rights, and this is a great delusion. And the Almighty’s statement: Thus did We establish Joseph in the land. It was said about it: Just as We established Joseph’s control over his wife, We established him in the land over the Aziz, or something similar that does not resemble what he mentioned. Al-Shafi’i said: And similar to it is the statement of the Almighty: And take in your hand a bunch and strike with it and do not break your oath. (Surah Sad: 44). This is not a trick, but rather it is an interpretation of the oath on the words or on the intentions. Al-Shafi’i said: And similar to it is the hadith of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri about the governor of Khaybar that he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with dates of Janib, the hadith, and the Shafi’i intended from this hadith that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to sell a group and buy Janib from the one from whom he sold the group or from someone else. The Malikis said: Its meaning is from someone else, so that it would not be a sin by collecting, and the dirhams are usury, as Ibn Abbas said: A crime for a crime and the dirhams are usury. The Almighty said: In the king’s religion meaning his authority, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Isa: His customs, meaning he oppresses without justification. Mujahid: In his judgment, which is the enslavement of thieves. Except that God wills meaning unless God wills to make the water container in his bag a pretext and excuse for him. Qatada said: Rather, the king’s judgment was to flog and fine him double, but God willed that the judgment of the Children of Israel should be on their tongues, as mentioned above. God the Almighty says: We raise by degrees whom We will meaning by knowledge and faith. It was read We raise by degrees whom We will meaning: We raise by degrees whom We will. This has already been mentioned in Al-An’am. His statement: And above every possessor of knowledge is One who is All-Knowing Israel narrated on the authority of Samak on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: There will be one who is more knowledgeable than another and that one who is more knowledgeable than another, and God is above every scholar. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Abd Al-A’la on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: We were with Ibn Abbas, may God have mercy on him, and he spoke a hadith and a man was amazed by it and said: Glory be to God! And above every possessor of knowledge is One who is All-Knowing. Ibn Abbas said: What you have said is bad. God is the All-Knowing and He is above every scholar.
12:77: The Almighty said: "They said: If he steals, a brother of his stole before him." The meaning is: He followed his brother's example, and if he followed our example, he would not have stolen. They only said that to absolve themselves of his action, because he is not from their mother, and that if he steals, then the blood of his thieving brother has drawn him, because sharing lineages is similar to sharing morals. They differed regarding the theft that they attributed to Joseph. It was narrated from Mujahid and others that Joseph's aunt, the daughter of Isaac, was older than Jacob, and Isaac's belt was given to her because of her age, because they used to inherit by age. This is one of the things that our law abrogated, and whoever stole was excluded. Joseph's aunt took him in and loved him very much. When he grew up, Jacob said to her: Give Joseph to me, for I cannot bear for him to be away from me for an hour. She fell in love with him and feared being separated from him, so she said to him: Leave him with me for a few days so that I may look at him.
