When Jacob left her, she went to Isaac's belt and tied it around Joseph from under his clothes. Then she said: I have lost Isaac's belt, so see who took it and who took it. She looked and said: Examine the people of the house. They examined and found it with Joseph. She said: By God, it is mine, and I can do with it as I wish. Then Jacob came to her and she told him the report. He said to her: "You and that. If he did that, then it is yours." She kept him until she died. For that, his brothers taunted him by saying: If he steals, a brother of his stole before. From here, Joseph learned to put the water-skin in his brother's saddlebag, as his aunt had done. Saeed bin Jubair said: I ordered him to steal an idol that belonged to his maternal grandfather, so he stole it, broke it and threw it on the road. That was their way of changing the wrong, so they accused him of stealing and taunted him for it. Qatada said the same. In the book of Al-Zajjaj: It was a golden idol. Atiyah Al-Awfi said: He was with his brothers at a meal and he looked at a vein and hid it, so they taunted him for that. It was said: He used to steal food from the table of the poor, as narrated by Ibn Isa. It was also said: They lied about him and attributed it to him, as Al-Hasan said. God Almighty says: So Joseph kept it secret within himself and did not reveal it to them. That is, he kept their words to himself: If he steals, his brother had stolen before. This was said by Ibn Shajarah and Ibn Isa. It was also said that he kept his words to himself: You are in the worst position. Then he said out loud: And God knows best what you describe. Ibn Abbas said: That is, you are in a worse position than those whom you have attributed this theft to. The meaning of his statement And God knows best what you describe is that God knows best that what you said is a lie, even if it was pleasing to God. It has been said that Joseph’s brothers at that time were not prophets.
12:78: The Almighty said: They said, 'O Aziz! Indeed, he has an old father, so take one of us in his place.' They addressed him by the name Aziz, since at that moment the first one was about to be removed or killed. And their saying: Indeed, he has an old father means of great stature, and they did not mean old age, because that is well known from the state of the old man. So take one of us in his place meaning a slave in his place. It has been said that this is a metaphor, because they know that it is not correct to take a free man to be enslaved in place of someone whose slavery has been established by their tradition. Rather, this is like saying to someone whose actions you dislike: Kill me and do not do such and such, and you do not want him to kill you, but you are exaggerating in making him descend. It is possible that their saying: Take one of us in his place is true, and it is far-fetched for them, as prophets, to see the enslavement of a free man, so there is nothing left but that they intended by that the way of the porter, i.e. take one of us in his place until your companion returns to you, and their aim by that is for Benjamin to reach his father, and for Jacob to know the truth of the matter, so Joseph, peace be upon him, was prevented from that, since the porter in the limits and the like - meaning bringing the guaranteed only - is permissible with mutual consent, and is not binding if the claimant refuses. As for the porter in such a case on the condition that the porter is obligated to do what the guaranteed was obligated to do in terms of punishment, it is not permissible by consensus. In Al-Wadiha: Porterage in the face only in all limits is permissible, except in the life. The majority of jurists are of the opinion that bail in the life is permissible. There is a difference of opinion regarding Al-Shafi’i, as sometimes he weakened it, and sometimes he permitted it. The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, we see you among the doers of good. It is possible that they meant to describe him with what they saw of his goodness in all his actions with them, and it is possible that they meant: Indeed, we see that you have done good to us in this hand if you extend it to us, and this is the interpretation of Ibn Ishaq.
12:79: The Almighty said: He said, ‘God forbid’ is a verbal noun. That we should take is in the accusative case, meaning that we should not take. Except for whom we find is in the accusative case with -we take. Our goods are with Him meaning God forbid that we should take the innocent for the criminal, and go against what we agreed upon. Indeed, then we would be wrongdoers meaning that we would take other than him.
12:80: The Almighty said: So when they despaired of him meaning they lost hope, like ajab and istajab, sakharah and istasakharah. Khalasu meaning they were alone and he was not with them. Najiyan is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in Khalasu and it is singular and leads to a plural, as in this verse, and it occurs for a singular like the Almighty's saying: And We brought him near for a private conversation (Maryam 19:52) and its plural is anjiya. The poet said: If the people were to save him and the people were disturbed, the bribe would be disturbed There is a recommendation for me and not for him Ibn Kathir read:اَُتْيُسوا(واَت َتْتُْس) َُتْيَإنه(َُتَتم َتْي) with an alif without a hamza due to the change, the hamza was brought forward and the ya’ was delayed, then the hamza was changed to an alif because it was preceded by a fatha. The original reading of the group, because the source only came with the ya’ brought forward - ya’san - and iyaas is not the source of iyaas, rather it is the source of astah awsan and iyaas, meaning I gave him. Some people said: iyaas and iyaas are two dialects, meaning when they despaired of returning their brother to them, they consulted among themselves, and no one else mixed with them from the people, they whispered about what had happened to them. And an-Naji is a fa’il word meaning one who whispers. God the Almighty said: Their eldest said. Qatada said: He is Reuben, he was the eldest of them in age. Mujahid said: He is Simeon, he was the eldest of them in opinion. Al-Kalbi said: Judah, he was the wisest of them. Muhammad bin Ka’b and Ibn Ishaq said: He is Levi, he is the father of the prophets. Did you not know that your father took a covenant from you from God? That is, a covenant from God to protect his son and return him to him. And before that, you neglected Joseph. Ma is in the accusative case in apposition to An, and the meaning is: Did you not know that your father took a covenant from you from God, and you learned your neglect of Joseph? This was mentioned by Al-Nahhas and others. Min in His statement: And before is related to -you learned. It is possible that Ma is redundant, so the two circumstances, which are from before and in Joseph, are related to the verb, which is you neglected. It is possible that ma and the verb are a source, and min qabl is related to an implied verb, the estimate: your negligence with Joseph happened before, so ma and the verb are in the nominative case as a subject, and the predicate is the implied verb to which min qabl is related. I will not leave the land meaning I will stick to it, nor will I leave residing in it. It is said: he left, he left, meaning he disappeared. If the negation enters, it becomes positive. Until my father gives me permission to return, for I am ashamed of him. Or God rules for me to pass with my brother, so I go with him to my father. It was said: The meaning is, or God rules for me with the sword, so I fight and take my brother, or I am unable, so I turn away with an excuse, and that is because Jacob said: Bring him to me unless you are surrounded, and whoever fights and is unable has been surrounded. Ibn Abbas said: And when Judah became angry and took the sword, he would not turn away a hundred thousand, his hair would stand on his chest like a thread and penetrate his clothes. It was reported that Judah said to his brothers - and he was the most angry of them -: Either you spare me the king and those with him, and I will spare you the people of Egypt, or you spare me the people of Egypt, and I will spare you the king and those with him. They said: Rather, we spare the king and those with him, and we will spare you the people of Egypt. So he sent one of his brothers, and they counted the markets of Egypt and found nine markets in them, and each one of them took a market. Then Judah entered upon Joseph and said: O king! If you do not leave our brother with us, I will cry out a cry that will not leave a pregnant woman in your city without her miscarrying what is in her womb. This was especially the case with them when they were angry. Joseph angered him and made him hear a word. Judah became angry and his wrath became intense, and his hairs stood out. This was the case with every one of the sons of Jacob. When he became angry, his skin would shudder, his body would swell, and the hairs on his back would appear from under his garment, until a drop of blood would drip from each hair. When he struck the ground with his foot, it would shake and the building would collapse. If he cried out a cry, not a pregnant woman, animal, or bird would hear him without her miscarrying what is in her womb, completely or not completely. His anger would not subside unless he shed blood or a hand from the descendants of Jacob seized him. When Joseph knew that his brother Judah’s anger was complete and perfect, he spoke to a young son of his in Coptic and ordered him to put his hand between Judah’s shoulders where he could not see him. He did so and his anger subsided and he threw down the sword. He looked right and left. Perhaps he would see one of his brothers, but he did not see him. So he ran out to his brothers and said, Has anyone of you attended to me? They said, No. He said, Where did Simeon go? They said, He went to the mountain. So he went out and met him, and he had carried a huge boulder. He said, What are you doing with this? He said, I will go to the market that is my lot and smash the heads of everyone in it with it. He said, “Then go back and bring it back, or throw it into the sea, and do not make a mistake. By Him who took Abraham as a friend, a hand from the descendants of Jacob has touched me.” Then they went in to Joseph, and Joseph was the most violent of them all. He said, O company of Hebrews! Do you think that there is no one stronger than you? Then he took a large millstone and kicked it with his foot, throwing it behind the wall - kicking means striking with one foot, and he kicked it, said Al-Jawhari - then Judah grabbed one of his hands and threw him to his side, and said: Bring the blacksmiths, I will cut off their hands and feet and strike off their necks. Then he climbed onto his bed, sat on his mattress, and ordered his measure to be placed between his hands, then tapped it once and it made a ringing sound. He turned to them and said: Do you know what he is saying? They said: No! He said: He says: There is no worry, grief, or distress on the heart of these fathers except because of them. Then he tapped a second time and said: He tells me that these people took their young brother and envied him and took him away from their father and then destroyed him. They said: O Aziz! Cover us as God covered you, and bestow upon us the favor of God upon you. Then he pecked him a third time and said: He says: These people threw their young one into the well, then sold him as a slave for a low price, and they claimed to their father that a wolf had eaten him. Then he pecked him a fourth time and said: He tells me that you committed a sin eighty years ago for which you did not ask God’s forgiveness, nor did you repent to Him. Then he pecked him a fifth time and said: He says: Their brother whom they claimed had perished, the days will not pass before he returns and tells the people what they did. Then he pecked him a sixth time and said: He says: If you were prophets or sons of prophets, you would not have lied, nor would you have been disobedient to your father. I would have made you an example to the worlds. Bring me the blacksmiths so that I may cut off their hands and feet. They begged and wept and showed repentance and said: If we had harmed our brother Joseph while he was alive, we would surely be at his disposal and dust for him to trample under his foot. When Joseph saw this from his brothers, he wept and said to them: Get away from me! I have let you go out of my sight for the sake of your father, and had it not been for him, I would have made you an example.
12:81: The Almighty said: Return to your father He said: I will not leave the land. Then say, 'O our father, your son has stolen' Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak, and Abu Razin read your son has stolen. An-Nahhas: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Umar told me, Ibn Shadhan told us, Ahmad ibn Abi Surayj Al-Baghdadi told us: I heard Al-Kisa'i read: O our father, your son has stolen with a damma on the seen and a shaddah on the ra' with a kasrah, on what the doer is not named, meaning he was accused of theft and was accused of it, like you betrayed him, sinned, and depraved him if you attribute these characteristics. Al-Zajjaj said: Sarqa has two possible meanings: one of them is that he learned theft, and the other is that he was accused of theft. Al-Jawhari said: Sarqa and sarqa with a kasrah on the ra' in both of them is the name of the stolen thing, and the source is saraqa yusriq sarqan with a fatha. God Almighty says: And we testify only to what we know. It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And we did not testify except to what we knew means we never testified except to what we knew, but now we testified to what is apparent and we do not know the unseen, as if they were accused of what Benjamin said: He slipped this into my saddlebag like he slipped your merchandise into your saddlebags, Ibn Ishaq said its meaning. It was said that the meaning is: We did not testify to Joseph that the thief would steal except with what we knew of your religion, Ibn Zayd said. And we were not guardians of the unseen meaning you did not know when we took him from you that he would steal, so we would not seize him. Mujahid and Qatadah said: We did not know that your son would steal and our matter would come to this, but we said: We will protect our brother as much as we can. Ibn Abbas said: They mean that he stole at night while they were asleep, and the unseen is the night in the language of Himyar, and from him: We did not know what he did during the night and day and his going and coming. It was said: As long as he was in our sight, no fault occurred, but when he was absent from us, his conditions were hidden from us. It was said that its meaning is: The theft was taken from his saddlebag, and we took it out and looked at it, and we have no knowledge of the unseen, so perhaps they stole it and he did not steal. Second: This verse includes the permissibility of testimony in any way that knowledge is obtained, as testimony is linked to knowledge rationally and legally, so it is not heard except from those who know, and is not accepted except from them, and this is the origin of testimonies, and for this reason our companions said: The testimony of the blind is permissible, and the testimony of the listener is permissible, and the testimony of the mute if he understands is permissible, and likewise the testimony on the handwriting - if he is certain that it is his handwriting or the handwriting of so-and-so - is valid, so whoever has acquired knowledge of something is permitted to testify to it even if the one testified against does not testify to it, God Almighty said: Except for those who testify to the truth while they know (al-Zukhruf 43:86) and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not tell you about the best of witnesses? The best of witnesses is the one who gives his testimony before he is asked for it and this has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Third: Malik’s opinion differed regarding the testimony of passing by, which is that he says: I passed by so-and-so and I heard him say such-and-such. If he fully comprehends the statement, he testifies to one of his two statements, and in the other opinion, he does not testify until he witnesses both of them. The correct view is to give testimony when fully comprehensible, and this is what the group of scholars said, and it is the truth, because the desired has been achieved, and it is necessary for him to give knowledge, so the best of witnesses is the one who informs the one for whom the testimony is given, and the worst of witnesses is the one who conceals it, and God knows best. Fourth: If a man claims a testimony that his age cannot bear, it will be rejected, because he made a false claim and what was clearly proven to be false.
12:82: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And ask the town where we were and the caravan. They verified their testimony before Him, and removed the accusation from themselves so that He would not accuse them. So their saying: And ask the town means its people, so it was deleted, and they mean by the town Egypt. It was said: A town from its towns where they settled and settled from. It was said that the meaning is: And ask the town even if it was inanimate, then you are the Prophet of God, and He makes the inanimate speak to you, and based on this there is no need to omit. Sibawayh said: It is not permissible to say Speak to Hind and you mean Hind’s boy, because this is problematic. And the saying about the caravan is the same as the saying about the town. And we are truthful in our saying. Second: In this verse there is an understanding of the jurisprudence that whoever is right, and knows that he may be suspected or imagined to be wrong, should remove the accusation and all doubt from himself, and state the truth that he is right, so that no one remains to speak. Our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, did this when he said to the two men who passed by while he was leaving the mosque with Safiyyah, turning her over: Take it easy, she is Safiyyah bint Huyayy. He said: Glory be to God! and he was angry with them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The devil reaches a person as blood reaches him, and I feared that he might cast something into your hearts. Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim.
12:83: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘Rather, yourselves have been made attractive to you’ meaning, yourselves have been made attractive to you that my son stole and he did not steal, but rather that was for a matter that God wanted. So patience is most fitting meaning, my affair is most fitting patience, or most fitting patience is more fitting for me, as mentioned at the beginning of the surah. Second: It is the duty of every Muslim, if he is afflicted with a misfortune in himself, his children or his wealth, to receive it with beautiful patience, contentment and submission to what will happen to him, for He is the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, and to follow the example of the Prophet of God, Jacob, and all the other prophets, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all. Saeed bin Abi Arubah said on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: There are no two sips that a servant swallows that are more beloved to God than a sip of misfortune that the servant swallows with good patience and good consolation, and a sip of anger that the servant swallows with forbearance and forgiveness. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God, the Most High: So have beautiful patience, meaning that I do not complain about that to anyone. Muqatil bin Sulayman narrated on the authority of Ata bin Abi Riyah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, who said: He who persists will not be patient. It was mentioned in Al-Baqarah that patience is at the beginning of the shock, and the reward of the one who remembers his misfortune and seeks refuge in God, even if it has passed long ago. Juwaybir said on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Jacob was given the reward of one hundred martyrs for Joseph, and likewise whoever from this nation is patient in his misfortune will have the same reward as Jacob, peace be upon him. God Almighty said: Perhaps God will bring them all to me, because he knew that Joseph, peace be upon him, had not died, but rather that he had not heard of him, because Joseph was carried while he was a slave who did not own anything for himself, then the king bought him and he was in his house not appearing to the people, then he was imprisoned. When he was able to do so, he plotted to let his father know about him, and he did not send a messenger because he did not want his brothers to know that, so he would not let the messenger reach him. He said: about them because they were three, Joseph and his brother, and the one who stayed behind for the sake of his brother, and he is the one who said: I will not leave the land. “Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing” of my condition. The Wise in what He decrees.
12:84: It has three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And he turned away from them meaning he turned away from them. This is because when Jacob heard the report of Benjamin, his grief was complete and he reached his limit, and God renewed His calamity for him in Joseph, so he said: Oh, my grief over Joseph! and he forgot his son Benjamin and did not mention him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Saeed bin Jubair said: Jacob did not have what is in our book about seeking refuge, and if he had, he would not have said: Oh, my grief over Joseph. Qatada and Al-Hasan said: The meaning is: Oh, my grief! Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: Oh, my grief! Kathir said: Oh, how sad for the heart, how it turned away, and for the soul, when it was consoled, it was consoled. Regret is intense sadness over what has passed. The vocative is in the sense of: Come, O regret, for it is one of your times. Al-Zajjaj said: The original is O my regret, but the ya was replaced with an alif because of the lightness of the fat-ha. And his eyes turned white from sadness. It was said: He did not see with them for six years, and that he went blind, as Muqatil said. It was also said: The eye may turn white but some vision remains, and God knows best about the condition of Jacob. His eyes turned white from crying, but the cause of the crying was sadness, so that is why he said: from sadness. It was said: Jacob was praying, and Joseph was sleeping, sitting in front of him. He dozed off, so Jacob turned to him. Then he dozed off a second time, so he turned to him. Then he dozed off a third time, so he turned to him, happy with him and his snoring. Then God Almighty revealed to His angels: (Look at My chosen one and the son of My intimate friend standing in communion with Me, turning to someone other than Me. By My glory and majesty! I will remove the two pupils with which he turned, and I will separate him from the one he turned to by eighty years, so that the workers may know that whoever stands before Me must watch My gaze.) Second: This indicates that looking around during prayer - even if it does not invalidate it - indicates punishment for it and a deficiency in it. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about looking around during prayer, and he said: It is a theft that Satan steals from the prayer of the servant. The scholars’ statement on this will come at the beginning of Surat Al-Mu’minoon, in full, God willing. Third: An-Nahhas said: If some people ask about the meaning of the intense grief of Jacob - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him and our Prophet - then the scholars have three answers to this: One of them is that when Jacob - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - knew that Joseph - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - was alive, he feared for his religion, so his grief was intense because of that. It was said that he was only sad because he handed him over to them when he was young, so he regretted that. The third answer - and it is the clearest - is that grief is not forbidden, but what is forbidden is wailing, tearing clothes, and speaking inappropriately. The Prophet - may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - said: The eyes shed tears and the heart grieves, but we do not say what angers the Lord. God Almighty explained this by saying: So he is suppressed, meaning suppressed, filled with grief, holding it in and not expressing it. From this comes the word suppressing which means hiding anger, so the suppressed is the one whose path to grief is blocked. God Almighty said: When he cried out, suppressed (al-Qalam 68:48), meaning filled with distress. It is possible that al-Makzum means al-Kazim, which means the one who suppresses his sadness. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: al-Kazim is the one who suppresses his sorrow. The poet said: If I am holding back the affliction of Shas, then today my tongue is loose Juraij said on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: His eyes went out from grief so he is suppressing grief. He said: He is distressed. Muqatil bin Sulayman said on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: so he is suppressing grief he said: He is grieved, he says: He knows that Joseph is alive, but he does not know where he is, so he is grieved from that. Al-Jawhari said: Grief is the suppressed grief, you say from it the man is suppressed, so he is grieved and suppressed. An-Nahhas. It is said that someone is suppressing grief and suppressing grief, meaning he is sad and does not complain about his grief. The poet said: So I urged my people and held back their fight, while the people were holding back their fear of death.
12:85: The Almighty said: They said, ‘By God, you do not cease to remember Joseph.’ That is, his son said to him: By God, you do not cease to remember Joseph. Al-Kisa’i said: I did not cease and I did not cease means I did not stop. Al-Farra’ claimed that la is implied, meaning do not cease. He recited: I said, By God, I will stay seated even if they cut off my head and limbs. That is, I will not leave. An-Nahhas said: What he said is good and correct. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh claimed that la is implied in the oath, because there is no problem with it. If it were obligatory, it would have been with the lam and the nun. They only said that to him because they knew for certain that he would persist in that. It is said: he continued to do such-and-such. And he continued to do such-and-such, and they are two dialects, and they are only used with denial. The poet said: It did not stop until its dust was like a canopy on a windy day. That is, it has not stopped, and it will continue to stop. Ibn Abbas said: It will continue. Until it becomes severe meaning it will be destroyed. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: It is close to illness, which is less than death. The poet said: My worries crept in and made me sick, and my illness increased. Likewise, love before the day causes passion. Qatada said: old. Ad-Dahhak: worn out and decrepit. Muhammad ibn Ishaq: corrupt, without mind. Al-Farra: Al-Haridh is the one with a corrupt body and mind, and so is Al-Haridh. Ibn Zaid: Al-Haridh is the one who has reached the lowest age. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas: dry skin on the bones. Al-March: melting from worry. Al-Akhfash said: going. Ibn Al-Anbari: perishing, and they are all close. The origin of Al-Haridh is corruption in the body or mind from sadness, love, or old age, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah and others. Al-Arji said: I am a man who has love in him, so he urged me on until I became weak and sick. An-Nahhas said: It is said that he was infirm and sick, and a man is Haridh and Haradh, except that Haradh is neither dual nor plural, and the same applies to Qaman and Hari, which are neither dual nor plural. Al-Tha’labi: Some Arabs say Haridh for the masculine, and the feminine is Haridhah, so if he is described with this word, it is dual, plural and feminine. It is said: Haridh, yahridh haradhatan, so he is Haridh and Haradh. It is also said: a man is Muharidh, and it is recited: The horses wanted him for a whole day, and if they had trained him, he would have become an instigator. Imru Al-Qais said: I see the man with the horses becoming an instigator like the instigation of a sick young camel in the country An-Nahhas said: The linguists have said that worry made him sick, and a man is a fool. Anas read: Hardhan with a damma on the ha and a sukoon on the ra, meaning like a lichen stick. Al-Hasan read it with a damma on the ha and the ra. Al-Jawhari said: Al-Hardh and Al-Hardh are lichen. Or you will be among the perishing meaning the dead, and this is the saying of everyone, and their purpose was to prevent Jacob from crying and grieving out of pity for him, even though they were the cause of that.
12:86: The Almighty said: He said, ‘I only complain of my suffering.’ The true meaning of bath in the language is what befalls a person of destructive things that he is not prepared to hide. It is from baththatuhu which means to separate him. So the calamity was called bath metaphorically. Dhu al-Rummah said: I stopped at a quarter of my camel’s hump and kept crying and talking to him. I watered it until its stones and playgrounds almost spoke to me. Ibn Abbas said: Bathi is my concern. Al-Hasan: my need. It was said: the most intense sadness, and its reality is what we mentioned. And my sadness is to God is conjoined to it, he repeated it with a different wording. And I know from God that which you do not know meaning I know that Joseph’s vision is true, and that I will prostrate to him. Ibn Abbas said it. Qatada: I know from God’s kindness to me what necessitates my good opinion of Him. It was said: Jacob said to the Angel of Death, Have you taken Joseph’s soul? He said: No, so this confirmed his hope. Al-Suddi said: I know that Joseph is alive, and that is because when his son told him about the king’s conduct, justice, and character, Jacob’s soul sensed that he was his son, so he hoped, and said: Perhaps he is Joseph. He said: There is no friend on earth except a prophet. It was said: I know from the answer to the supplication of the needy what you do not know.
12:87: The Almighty's saying: O my sons, go and inquire about Joseph and his brother. This indicates that he was certain of his life, either by a vision, or by God Almighty making the wolf speak as in the beginning of the story, or by the Angel of Death informing him that he had not taken his soul, which is more apparent. Inquiry is seeking something through the senses, so it is a verb from the verb sense, meaning go to the one who asked you for your brother, and tricked you into taking him, so ask about him and his religion. It is narrated that the Angel of Death said to him: Seek him from here! And he pointed to the direction of Egypt. It was said: Jacob alerted Joseph to the return of the merchandise, the detention of his brother, and the manifestation of honor, so he directed them to the direction of Egypt and not elsewhere. And do not despair of the mercy of God meaning do not lose hope in God's relief, said Ibn Zayd, meaning that the believer hopes for God's relief, and the disbeliever loses hope in hardship. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak said: From God's mercy. None despairs of relief from God except the disbelieving people. This is evidence that despair is one of the major sins, and it is hopelessness. Its explanation will come in Az-Zumar, God willing.
12:88: God Almighty said: So when they entered upon him, they said, ‘O you who are powerful.’ That is, the one who is powerful. Affliction has befallen us and our family. This is the third time they returned to Egypt. There is an omission in the statement, meaning they went out to Egypt. When they entered upon Joseph, they said: Affliction has befallen us and our family, meaning hunger and need. This is evidence of the permissibility of complaining when in distress, meaning hunger. Rather, it is obligatory for him, if he fears harm for himself from poverty or otherwise, to disclose his condition to someone from whom he hopes to benefit, just as it is obligatory for him to complain about his pain to a doctor to treat him. This is not a criticism of trust. This is as long as the complaint is not in the form of discontent. Patience and endurance in calamities are better, and refraining from asking is better. The best speech in complaint is to ask the Master to remove the affliction. This is the statement of Jacob: “I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God. And I know from God that which you do not know.” That is, of His beautiful creation, His strange kindness, and His return to His servants. As for complaining without doubt, it is foolishness, unless it is in the form of consolation and consolation, as Ibn Duraid said: Do not think, oh time, that I am afflicted with a calamity that will make me sweat like the sweat of eternity I practiced it, even if the heavens fell on him from the sides of the atmosphere, he would not complain But it is a sigh of relief when a mine of grief rises from its sides. God Almighty says: And We brought merchandise. Merchandise is a piece of money intended to buy something. You say: I sold the thing and I bought it, meaning I made it merchandise. And in the proverb: Like someone who bought dates to Hajar. God the Almighty says: Mzja'ah is an attribute of merchandise, and the market is driven by pushing, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: Have you not seen that God drives the clouds? (al-Nur 24:43). The meaning is that it is merchandise that is pushed, and not everyone accepts it. Tha'lab said: The merchandise that is mixed is the incomplete, imperfect one. There is a difference of opinion about its specification here. It was said: It was dried meat and hays, mentioned by Al-Waqidi on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. It was said: He created the ghara'ir and ropes, narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said: The goods of the Bedouins are wool and ghee, said by Abdullah bin Al-Harith. It was said: The green seed and the pine, which is the pistachio, the seed of a tree in the Levant, is eaten and oil is squeezed from it for the manufacture of soap, said by Abu Saleh. So they sold it for dirhams that are not spent on food, and are spent among people, so they said: Take it from us according to the account of the good ones that are spent on food. It was said: Bad dirhams, also said by Ibn Abbas. It was said: It did not have the image of Joseph, and the dirhams of Egypt had the image of Joseph. Ad-Dahhak said: The sandals and the leather. And from him: It was sifted gruel. And God knows best. God Almighty says: So give us full measure and be charitable to us. It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Then give us full measure and be charitable to us. They mean just as you sell good things for dirhams, you do not diminish us by the price of our dirhams. This is the saying of most of the commentators. Ibn Jurayj said: Then give us full measure means the measure that he had given to their brother. And be charitable to us means favor us with something between the price of good things and bad things. Said bin Jubayr, Al-Suddi and Al-Hasan said: Because charity is forbidden to the prophets. It was said that the meaning is: Give us charity by increasing our right, said Sufyan bin Uyaynah. Mujahid said: Charity was not forbidden except to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning is: Give us charity by returning our brother to us. Ibn Shajarah said: Give us charity is used to refer to us, and he cited as evidence the words of the poet: Be charitable to us, O Ibn Affan, and be patient, and appoint Al-Ash'ari as our leader for the nights. Indeed, God rewards the charitable meaning in the Hereafter. It is said: This is an indirect speech, because they did not think that he was of their religion, so they did not say: Indeed, God rewards you for your charity. So they said a word that suggests that they meant it, and it is correct for them to interpret it. Al-Naqqash said it. And in the hadith: Indeed, in indirect speech there is an alternative to lying. Second: Malik and other scholars have argued that the measurer’s fee is on the seller. Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn Nafi’ said: Malik said: They said to Yusuf Give us full measure, so Yusuf was the one who gave the measure, and so was the weigher, the counter, and others, because if a man sells a known number of his food, and the contract is imposed on him, he must present it and distinguish the buyer’s right from his right, unless he sells a specific amount of it - a heap or money in which there is no right to fulfill it - so he leaves it between him and it, so whatever is done with the sold item is on the buyer, and this is not the case with what has a right to fulfill it in terms of measure or weight. Do you not see that the seller is not entitled to the price except after fulfilling it, and if it is lost, it is from him before fulfilling it? Third: As for the cash fee, it is also on the seller, because the buyer who pays his dirhams says: They are good, so you are the one who claims the bad, so look at yourself. Also, the benefit falls to him, so the fee is on him. Likewise, it is not on the one who is obligated to retaliate, because he is not obligated to cut off his own hand, unless he is able to do so willingly. Do you not see that it is obligatory for him to ransom his hand, and to make peace if the retaliator asks him to do so? So the fee for cutting off the hand is on the retaliator. Al-Shafi’i said, in the well-known report from him: It is on the one who is retaliated against, like the seller. Fourth: It is disliked for a man to say in his supplication: O God, give me charity, because charity is only given by one who seeks reward, and God Almighty is generous with reward for all blessings, there is no god but Him. Al-Hasan heard a man saying: O God, give me charity, so Al-Hasan said: “O man! God does not give charity, only those who seek reward give charity. Haven’t you heard the saying of God Almighty: ‘Indeed, God rewards the charitable.’ Say: O God, give me and be generous to me.”
12:89: The Almighty said: He said, 'Have you known what you did with Joseph and his brother?' This is a question that means reminding and rebuking, and it is what God said: You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs. (Yusuf 12:15) The verse. When you were ignorant is evidence that they were young at the time they took Joseph, not prophets, because no one is described as ignorant except someone who has this characteristic. It also indicates that their situation is good now, meaning you did that when you were young and ignorant. Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said its meaning. And their saying: And we were indeed sinners is based on this, because they grew up and did not tell their father what they did out of shyness and fear of him. It was said: ignorant of the consequences. And God knows best.
12:90: The Almighty said: They said, 'Are you indeed Joseph?' When they entered upon him and said, Harm has afflicted us and our family, they submitted to him and were humble. He took pity on them and introduced himself to them, saying, Do you know what you did with Joseph and his brother? They were alerted and said, Are you indeed Joseph? Ibn Ishaq said this. It was said that Joseph smiled, so they likened him to Joseph and inquired. Ibn Abbas said that when he said to them, Do you know what you did with Joseph? the verse, then Joseph smiled - and when he smiled his teeth were like strung pearls - so they likened him to Joseph, and they said to him in a questioning manner, Are you indeed Joseph? On the authority of Ibn Abbas also: His brothers did not recognize him until the crown was removed from him, and there was a mark on his horn, and Jacob had a similar mole-like mark. When he said to them: Do you know what you have done to Joseph? He removed the crown from him and they recognized him, and they said: Are you Joseph? Ibn Abbas said: Jacob wrote to him asking for the return of his son, and in the letter: From Jacob, the chosen one of God, the son of Isaac, the sacrifice of God, the son of Abraham, the friend of God, to the Aziz of Egypt - As for what follows - We are a family of trials and tribulations. God tested my grandfather Abraham with Nimrod and his fire, then He tested my father Isaac with slaughter, then He tested me with a son who was the most beloved of my sons to me until my eyesight went blind from crying, and I did not steal and I did not give birth to a thief, peace be upon him. When Joseph read the letter, his joints trembled, his skin shuddered, and he lowered his eyes from crying, and his patience was exhausted so he revealed the secret. Ibn Kathir read innaka as a statement, and it is possible that this reading is a question like his saying: And that is a blessing (Ash-Shu'ara: 26). "He said, 'I am Joseph,' meaning I am the wronged one who was intended to be killed. He did not say 'I am him,' out of respect for the story. 'God has bestowed His favor upon us,' meaning salvation and kingship. 'Indeed, he who fears God and is patient,' meaning fears God and is patient in the face of calamities and in avoiding sins. 'Indeed, God does not allow to be lost the reward of the righteous,' meaning those who are patient in His trials and who obey Him. Ibn Kathir read: 'Indeed, he who fears God,' with the addition of the ya', and reading it with this is permissible, provided that 'min' means 'who,' and 'yattaqi' is included in the relative clause, so the ya' is added and nothing else, and 'wasabir' is raised. It may be permissible to make 'wasabir' in the jussive mood, making 'yattaqi' in the jussive mood and 'min' for the condition, and the ya' is added, and the sign of the jussive mood is the deletion of the damma that was in the ya' according to the original, as he said: Then he called out, When you enter Damascus, O Zaid bin Khalid bin Yazid. Another said: Didn't the report come to you about what happened to the camels of Bani Ziyad? The reading of the group is clear, and the letter ha in that is a metaphor for the hadith, and the sentence is the report.
12:91: The Almighty said: They said, 'By God, God has favored you over us.' The original is two hamzas, the second of which was lightened, and it is not permissible to make it pronounced with emphasis. The active participle is mudathir, and the source is ithar. It is also said: I influenced the dust, itharatan, so I am mudathir, and it is also in the form af'al, then a'la, and the original is athir, the movement of the ya' was transferred to the tha', so the ya' became an alif, then it was deleted due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. I influenced the hadith on fa'alt, so I am athir, and the meaning is: God has favored you over us, and has chosen you with knowledge, patience, wisdom, reason, and kingship. And if we were indeed sinners meaning guilty of a mistake, one makes a mistake if he commits a sin, and within this is the question of forgiveness. It was said to Ibn Abbas: How did they say: And if we were indeed sinners when they did so intentionally? He said: Even if they did so intentionally, they did not do so intentionally until they missed the truth, and likewise everyone who commits a sin has transgressed the path that he is on from the truth, until he falls into doubt and disobedience.
12:92: The Almighty said: No reproach upon you today meaning Joseph - who was forbearing and successful - said: (No reproach upon you today) and the speech is complete. The meaning of today is time. And reproach is reproach and rebuke, meaning there is no reproach, rebuke or blame upon you today, as Sufyan al-Thawri and others said. From this is his saying, peace be upon him: If the female slave of one of you commits adultery, let him flog her the prescribed punishment and let him not reproach her meaning let him not reproach her. And Bishr said: So I pardoned them with a pardon that was not blasphemous, and left them to the punishment of the Everlasting Day. Al-Asma'i said: I rebuked him and Arabized him means if I criticized his actions. Al-Zajjaj said: "The meaning is, there is no spoiling of the sanctity between me and you, and the right of brotherhood, and you have my pardon and forgiveness. The root of "thathrib is spoiling", and it is the language of the people of Hijaz. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took hold of the doorposts on the day of the conquest of Mecca, and the people had taken refuge in the House, so he said: "Praise be to God, who fulfilled His promise and aided His servant and defeated the confederates alone." Then he said: "What do you think, O people of Quraysh?" They said: "Good, a noble brother, and the son of a noble brother, and I have power." He said: "And I say as my brother Joseph said: 'No reproach upon you today.'" Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: "I felt a sweat of shame at what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, because I had said to them when we entered Mecca: Today we will take revenge on you and do something. But when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said what he said, I felt ashamed of my saying. May God forgive you" is a future meaning of supplication, he asked God to cover them and have mercy on them. Al-Akhfash permitted stopping at upon you, and the first is the one used, because stopping at upon you and beginning with today God will forgive you confirms forgiveness on the day, and that only happens through revelation, and this is clear. Ata Al-Khurasani said: Asking for needs from the youth is easier than from the elderly. Have you not seen the words of Joseph: (There is no blame upon you today. God will forgive you) and Jacob said: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord.
12:93: The Almighty’s saying: Go with this shirt of mine is an adjective for the shirt, and the shirt is masculine. As for the poet’s saying: Hawazin invites and the shirt is loose over the belt and is fastened with buttons Its meaning: The shirt is a loose coat of mail. Al-Nahhas said it. Ibn Al-Suddi said on the authority of his father on the authority of Mujahid: Joseph said to them: Go with this shirt of mine and throw it on my father’s face, and he will regain his sight. He said: Joseph knew God better than to know that his shirt would restore Jacob’s sight, but that was the shirt of Abraham that God made him wear in the fire from the silk of Paradise, and Isaac had clothed him, and Isaac had clothed him with it, and Jacob had put that shirt in a reed of silver and hung it around Joseph’s neck, because he feared the evil eye for him, and Gabriel told him to send your shirt, for in it is the scent of Paradise, and the scent of Paradise does not fall on the sick or afflicted except by its fragrance. Al-Hasan said: If God Almighty had not informed Joseph of that, he would not have known that his sight would return to him. The one who carried his shirt was Judah, who said to Joseph: I am the one who carried your shirt with false blood, and you saddened him, and I am the one who carries it now to capture him and restore his sight. So he carried it. Al-Suddi narrated it. And bring me your family, all of them, so that you may take Egypt as a home. Masruq said: They were ninety-three, including men and women. It has been said that the shirt he sent was the shirt that was torn from his back, so that Jacob would know that he was protected from adultery. The first statement is more correct, and it has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the hadith of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Qushayri mentioned it, and God knows best.
12:94: The Almighty said: And when the caravan departed meaning it set out from Egypt to Syria. It is said: He departed several times, and I departed him a separation, so it is intransitive and transitive. Their father said meaning he said to those of his relatives who were present but did not go to Egypt, and they were his grandsons: Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph. It may be possible that some of his sons went out, so he said to those who remained: Indeed, I smell the scent of Joseph, unless you think it is false. Ibn Abbas said: A wind blew and carried the scent of Joseph's shirt to him, and between them was a journey of eight nights. Al-Hasan said: A journey of ten nights, and it was also narrated from him a journey of a month. Malik bin Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: He only conveyed its scent from the one who conveyed the throne of Bilqis before it blinked at Solomon, peace be upon him. Mujahid said: A wind blew and slapped the shirt, and the scents of Paradise wafted into the world and reached Jacob. He found the scent of Paradise and knew that there was no scent of Paradise in the world except what was from that shirt. Then he said: Indeed, I find meaning I smell, so it is a presence through the sense of smell. If only you would be refuted Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: If only you would be foolish. And from the sayings of Al-Nabigha: Except for Solomon, when the king said to him, Go into the wilderness and determine its location. That is, about foolishness. Saeed bin Jubair and Ad-Dahhak said: If you did not lie. And Al-Fand is lying. He lied, and from it is the saying of the poet: Is there anyone who would like to be proud of the generous, or is there anyone who would refute the words of al-Saduq? Any lie. It was said: If you did not find fault, Abu Amr said it. Refutation means defamation. The poet said: My friend, stop blaming and refuting me, for what has passed of my affair will not be returned. Ibn al-A'rabi said: If it were not for you to refute if it were not for you to weaken my opinion, and Ibn Ishaq said the same. The weakness of opinion comes from arrogance. A fourth saying: you go astray, said by Abu Ubaidah. Al-Akhfash said: you blame me, and refutation is blame and weakening of opinion. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Mujahid also said: you become old, and all of them are close in meaning, and it refers to the incapacity and weakening of opinion. It is said: he refuted him if he made him incapable, as he said: He ruined me with blame and refutation. It is said: afand if he spoke incorrectly. afand is a mistake in speech and opinion, as Al-Nabigha said:..... So specify it from the hotel That is, prevent it from corrupting the mind. Hence it was said: Blame is refutation. The poet said: Oh, you who criticize me, blame has come and gone. Love has been long and you have prolonged the refutation. It is said: Time ruined someone, and from this is the saying of Ibn Muqbil: Let time do what it wants, for if it is tasked with destroying people, it will destroy them.
12:95: God the Almighty said: "They said: By God, you are indeed in your old error." That is, you are still straying from the right path. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said: In your past mistake of loving Joseph, do not forget it. Saeed bin Jubair said: In your old madness. Al-Hasan said: This is disobedience. Qatada and Sufyan said: In your old love. It was said: They said this because, according to them, Joseph had died. It was said: The one who told him that was his remaining son, and they did not know the report. It was said: The one who was with him from his family and relatives told him that. It was said: His grandsons, and they were young, but God knows best.
12:96: The Almighty said: So when the bearer of good report came, he threw it on his face meaning on his eyes. And he regained his sight an is redundant, and it was said that the bearer of good report is Simeon. It was also said that Judah said: I will go with the shirt today as I went with it, stained with blood, said Ibn Abbas. And on the authority of Al-Suddi that he said to his brothers: You know that I went to him with the shirt of sorrow, so let me go to him with the shirt of joy. And Yahya bin Yaman said on the authority of Sufyan: When the bearer of good report came to Jacob, he said to him: On what religion did you leave Joseph? He said: On Islam. He said: Now the blessing is complete. And Al-Hasan said: When the bearer of good report came to Jacob, he did not find anything with him to reward him with, he said: By God, you did not find anything with us, and we have not baked anything for seven nights, but God made the throes of death easy for you. I said: This supplication is one of the greatest rewards, and the best gifts and treasures. This verse indicates the permissibility of giving and offering gifts when receiving good report. In this regard, there is the long hadith of Ka’b ibn Malik, in which he says: When the one whose voice I heard giving me good report came to me, I took off my garment and covered them with it as a sign of his good report. He mentioned the hadith, and it was presented in full in the story of the three who were left behind. Ka’b’s covering of his two garments for the one who brought good report, even though he had no other, is evidence of the permissibility of such a thing if he hopes to obtain what he is happy about, and it is evidence of the permissibility of showing joy after the disappearance of sorrow and grief. From this regard is the permissibility of children’s cleverness and feeding people in it. Omar slaughtered a camel after memorizing Surah Al-Baqarah. And God knows best. God Almighty said: He said, ‘Did I not tell you that I know from God that which you do not know?’ He reminded them of His statement: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God, and I know from God that which you do not know.
12:97: The Almighty said: "They said, 'O our father, ask forgiveness for our sins. Indeed, we were sinners.'" There is an omission in the speech, the meaning is: So when they returned from Egypt, they said, 'O our father.' This indicates that the one who said to him, 'By God, you are indeed in your old error,' was his grandchildren or others from his relatives and family, not his children, for they were absent, and that would have been an increase in disobedience. And God knows best. They only asked him for forgiveness because they brought upon him such pain and grief that he could not be relieved of it except by making it lawful. I said: This ruling is established for one who wrongs a Muslim in his person, his money, or anything else, unjustly. He must seek forgiveness for him and inform him of the wrong and its extent. Does an absolute forgiveness benefit him or not? There is a difference of opinion on this, and the correct view is that it does not benefit, because if he were to inform him of a wrong that is significant and disastrous, the wronged person may not be content to seek forgiveness for it. And God knows best. In Sahih al-Bukhari and others, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever has wronged his brother in his honor or anything else, let him forgive him today before there will be neither dinar nor dirham. If he has good deeds, they will be taken from him according to the extent of his wrong, and if he has no good deeds, some of his companion’s bad deeds will be taken and loaded on him.” Al-Muhallab said: So his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, He will be taken from him according to the extent of his wrong, means that the wrong must be of known extent, indicated, and explained. And God knows best.
12:98: God the Almighty said: He said, 'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord.' Ibn Abbas said: He delayed his supplication until dawn. Al-Muthanna bin Al-Sabah said on the authority of Tawus that he said: The dawn of Friday night, and that coincided with the night of Ashura. In the supplication of preservation - from the book of Al-Tirmidhi - on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: While we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Ali bin Abi Talib - may God be pleased with him - came to him and said: - may my father and mother be sacrificed for you - this Qur'an has slipped from my chest, and I do not find myself able to do it, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Shall I not teach you words by which God will benefit you and benefit those you teach them and will make firm what you have learned in your chest? He said: Yes, O Messenger of God! So teach me. He said: If it is Friday night, if you are able to get up in the last third of the night, then it is a witnessed hour and supplication in it is answered. My brother Jacob said to his sons, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, meaning until Friday night comes. And he mentioned the hadith. Ayyub bin Abi Tamima Al-Sakhtiyani said on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair who said: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord on the white nights, on the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth, for supplications are answered on them. And on the authority of Amer Al-Shaabi who said: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord meaning I will ask Joseph if He forgives you, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Sanid bin Dawud mentioned: Hisham told us, Abdul Rahman bin Ishaq told us on the authority of Muharib bin Dithar on the authority of his uncle who said: I used to come to the mosque at dawn and I would pass by the house of Ibn Masoud and I would hear him saying: O God, You commanded me and I obeyed, and You called upon me and I answered, and this is dawn, so forgive me. So I met Ibn Masoud and I said: What words do I hear you say at dawn? He said: Jacob delayed his sons until dawn by saying: I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord.
12:99: The Almighty said: So when they entered upon Joseph meaning a palace that he had there. He took his parents into his care. It was said that Joseph sent two hundred camels and equipment with the bearer of good report, and asked Jacob to bring him his family and all his children. So when they entered upon him, he took his parents into his care, meaning he took them in. By his parents, he meant his father and his aunt. His mother had died in giving birth to his brother Benjamin. It was said that God revived his mother in fulfillment of the vision, so that she prostrated to him. This was said by Al-Hasan. It was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah that God Almighty revived the father and mother of His Prophet, peace be upon him, so they believed in him. God the Almighty said: Enter Egypt, if God wills, in safety. Ibn Jurayj said: That is, I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, if God wills. He said: This is from the Qur’an’s bringing it forward and delaying it. An-Nahhas said: Ibn Jurayj believes that they had entered Egypt, so how can he say: Enter Egypt, if God wills. It was said: He only said: If God wills as a blessing and as a confirmation. Safe from famine, or from Pharaoh, and they would not enter it except with his permission.
12:100: The Almighty said: And raised his parents on the throne. Qatada said: He means the bed, and its meanings have been mentioned before. The throne may also be used to refer to the king and the king himself, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani: Thrones were sacrificed after glory and security It has been presented. God Almighty said: And they fell down before him in prostration. There are three issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And they fell down before him in prostration. It was said that the ha in they fell down before him refers back to God the Almighty, meaning: And they fell down in prostration in gratitude to God, and Yusuf is like a qiblah for the fulfillment of his vision. It was narrated from Al-Hasan. Al-Naqqash said: This is a mistake, and the ha refers back to Yusuf because God the Almighty said at the beginning of the surah: I saw them prostrating to me. And their greeting was that the lowly would prostrate to the noble, and the young to the old. Jacob, his aunt, and his brothers prostrated to Yusuf, peace be upon him, and his skin shuddered and he said: This is the interpretation of my vision from before. And between Yusuf’s vision and its interpretation were twenty-two years. Salman Al-Farsi and Abdullah bin Shaddad said: Forty years. Abdullah bin Shaddad said: And that is the last time a vision takes time. Qatadah said: Thirty-five years. Al-Suddi, Saeed bin Jubayr, and Ikrimah said: Thirty-six years. Al-Hasan, Jisr bin Farqad, and Fadil bin Ayyad said: Eighty years. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Joseph was thrown into the well when he was seventeen years old, and he was absent from his father for eighty years. He lived twenty-three years after he met his father, and he died when he was one hundred and twenty years old. In the Torah, it says one hundred and twenty-six years. Joseph had Ephraim, Manasseh, and Rahmah, the wife of Job, from the wife of Al-Aziz. There were four hundred years between Joseph and Moses. It was said that Jacob stayed with Joseph for twenty years, then he died, peace be upon him. It was also said that he stayed with him for eighteen years. Some of the hadith scholars said: forty-odd years, and there were thirty-three years between Jacob and Joseph until God brought them together. Ibn Ishaq said: eighteen years, and God knows best. Second: Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Al-Hasan - regarding his statement: And they fell down before him in prostration - he said: It was not prostration, but it was a Sunnah that was among them, they would nod their heads, and that was their greeting. Al-Thawri, Ad-Dahhak and others said: It was a prostration like the prostration that is customary among us, and that was their greeting. It was said: It was a bowing like bowing, and it was not falling to the ground, and that is how their greeting was by covering their faces and bowing, and God abrogated all of that in our law, and made speech a substitute for bowing. The commentators agreed that that prostration, whatever its form, was a greeting, not an act of worship. Qatada said: This was the greeting of kings among them, and God gave this nation peace, the greeting of the people of Paradise. I said: This bowing and shrugging which was abrogated from us has become a custom in Egypt and among the Persians, as well as their standing up for one another, to the point that if one of them does not stand up for him he feels as if he is not paid attention to and that he has no value. Likewise, when they meet, they bow to one another, a continuing custom and a stable inheritance, especially when princes and leaders meet. They have deviated from the Sunnah and turned away from the Sunnah. Anas bin Malik narrated that he said: We said, O Messenger of God! Should we bow to one another when we meet? He said: No. We said: Should we embrace one another? He said: No. We said: Should we shake hands with one another? He said: Yes. Abu Omar narrated it in Al-Tamhid. If it is said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Stand up for your master and best among you’ - meaning Sa`d ibn Mu`adh - we say: That was specific to Sa`d because the specific situation required it. It was also said: Their standing was only to get him down from the donkey. Also, it is permissible for an old man to do so if it does not affect him, but if it affects him and he is pleased with it and sees a share for himself, it is not permissible to help him in that, because the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Whoever is pleased for people to stand up for him, let him take his seat in Hellfire.’ It was narrated from the Companions may God be pleased with them all that there was no face more honorable to them than the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and they did not stand up for him when they saw him, because they knew that he disliked that. Third: If it is said: What do you say about pointing with the finger? It is said to him: That is permissible if he is far from you, to specify the time for the greeting, but if he is close, then no. It has been said that it is forbidden in both closeness and distance, because of what was reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Whoever imitates others is not one of us.” And he said: Do not greet as the Jews and Christians greet, because the Jews greet with the palms and the Christians greet with the gesture. And if he greets, then he does not bow, nor does he kiss his hand with the greeting, because bowing in the sense of humility is only appropriate for God. As for kissing the hand, then it is from the actions of the non-Arabs, and they should not be followed in their actions that they innovated out of respect for their leaders. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not stand at my head as the non-Arabs stand at the heads of their kings. This is similar. There is nothing wrong with shaking hands, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) shook hands with Ja’far ibn Abi Talib when he returned from Abyssinia, and he commanded it and encouraged it, and said: Shake hands, and rancor will go away. Ghalib al-Tammar narrated on the authority of al-Sha’bi that the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would shake hands when they met, and when they returned from a journey, they would embrace. If it is said: So Malik disliked shaking hands? We say: Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Malik that he disliked shaking hands and hugging, and Sahnun and others of our companions held this view. It has been narrated on the authority of Malik that it is contrary to that, that shaking hands is permissible, and this is what is indicated by the meaning of what is in al-Muwatta’. The majority of scholars from the early and later generations agreed on the permissibility of shaking hands. Ibn al-Arabi said: Malik disliked shaking hands because he did not see it as a general matter in the religion, nor as a transmitted transmission of greetings, and if it had been from him, it would have been the same. I said: There is a hadith about shaking hands that indicates the encouragement of shaking hands, and the persistence and preservation of it. It is what was narrated by Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: “I met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he took my hand. I said: O Messenger of God! I used to think that shaking hands was for non-Arabs. He said: We are more deserving of shaking hands than they are. There are no two Muslims who meet and one of them takes the hand of the other out of affection and sincere advice between them, except that their sins are cast between them.” God Almighty said: And He was kind to me when He brought me out of prison. He did not say from the well as a use of generosity, so that his brothers would not remember their actions after he forgave them by saying: There is no blame upon you. I said: This is the origin of the Sufi sheikhs: mentioning harshness at the time of purity is harshness, and it is a correct statement indicated by the Book. It was said: because his entering the prison was by his choice, as he said: The Lord of prison is more beloved to me than what they are calling me to, and he was in the well by the will of God Almighty for him. It was said: because he was in prison with the thieves and sinners, and in the well with God Almighty, and also the blessing of being saved from prison was greater, because he entered it because of a matter he intended to do, and also he entered it by his choice as he said: The Lord of prison is more beloved to me, so the distress in it was greater, and he also said in it: Remember me with your Lord, so he was punished in it. And He brought you from the desert It is narrated that Jacob’s dwelling was in the land of Canaan, and they were people of livestock and wilderness, and it was said: Jacob moved to the desert and lived there, and that God did not send a prophet from the people of the desert. It was said: he went out to Bada, which is a place, and Jamil meant it in his saying: You are the one who made me love the trouble that appeared to me and made me settle in other countries And Jacob had a mosque in this place under a mountain. It is said: The people came in a bada if they came in a bada, just as it is said: they went to a ghor, meaning they came to the ghor, and the meaning is: And he brought you from a place where he came in a bada, mentioned by Al-Qushayri, and Al-Mawardi narrated it on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas. After Satan had sown dissension between me and my brothers by causing envy, said Ibn Abbas. It was also said: He corrupted what was between me and my brothers, he attributed their sin to Satan out of his generosity. Indeed, my Lord is Kind to whom He wills meaning He is gentle with His servants. Al-Khattabi said: The Kind is the one who is kind to His servants, who is kind to them from where they do not know, and brings about their interests from where they do not expect, like His saying: “God is Kind to His servants. He provides for whom He wills” (al-Shura 42:19). It was also said: The Kind is the one who knows the details of things, and what is meant here is honor and kindness. Qatada said: He was kind to Joseph by releasing him from prison, and brought him his family from the desert, and removed from his heart the whisperings of Satan. It is narrated that when Jacob arrived with his family and children and approached the land of Egypt, and Joseph heard of this, he asked Pharaoh - whose name was Rayyan - for permission to meet his father Jacob, and he informed him of his arrival, so he gave him permission and ordered the nobles from his companions to ride with him. So Joseph went out and the king with him with four thousand princes with every prince that God created, and the people of Egypt rode with them to meet Jacob. Jacob was walking leaning on Judah’s hand, so Jacob looked at the horses, the people and the armies and said: O Judah! Is this the Pharaoh of Egypt? He said: No, this is your son Joseph. When each of them approached the other, Joseph went to greet him first, but he was prevented from doing so, and Jacob was more deserving of that than him and better, so Jacob began with the greeting and said: Peace be upon you, O remover of sorrows, and he cried and Joseph cried with him, so Jacob cried out of joy, and Joseph cried when he saw his father’s sadness. Ibn Abbas said: There are four types of crying: crying out of fear. And crying from grief, crying from joy, and crying out of hypocrisy. Then Jacob said: Praise be to God who comforted my eyes after worries and sorrows, and he entered Egypt with eighty-two of his family, and they did not leave Egypt until they reached six hundred thousand and more than a thousand, and they crossed the sea with Moses, peace be upon him, narrated by Ikrimah from Ibn Abbas. Ibn Masoud narrated that they entered Egypt and they were ninety-three people, between men and women, and they left with Moses and they were six hundred thousand and seventy thousand. Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham said: They entered it and they were seventy-two thousand, and they left with Moses and they were six hundred thousand. Wahb bin Munabbih said: Jacob and his sons entered Egypt and they were ninety people, between men, women, and children, and they left it with Moses fleeing from Pharaoh, and they were six hundred thousand and five hundred and seventy-some fighting men, in addition to the offspring, the old and the weak, and the offspring were one thousand thousand and two hundred thousand in addition to the fighting men. Historians said: Jacob stayed in Egypt for twenty-four years in the most blessed state and comfort, and he died in Egypt, and he ordered his son Joseph to carry his body until he buried it with his father Isaac in Syria, and he did, then he returned to Egypt. Saeed bin Jubair said: Jacob, peace be upon him, was transferred in a teak coffin to Jerusalem, and that coincided with the day Esau died, so they were buried in one grave, and from then on the Jews and their dead were transferred to Jerusalem, whoever among them did that, and Jacob and Esau were born in one womb, and they were buried in one grave, and their ages were one hundred and forty-seven years.
12:101: The Almighty said: My Lord, You have given me of the kingdom and taught me of the interpretation of dreams. Qatada said: No one wished for death, prophet or otherwise, except Joseph, peace be upon him, when the blessings were complete for him and his family was gathered together, longing to meet his Lord, the Almighty. It was said: Joseph did not wish for death, but rather he wished to die in Islam, meaning when my time comes, let me die as a Muslim, and this is the opinion of the majority. Sahl bin Abdullah al-Tustari said: No one wishes for death except three: a man who is ignorant of what comes after death, or a man who flees from the decrees of God, the Almighty, upon him, or one who longs and loves to meet God, the Almighty. It was proven in Sahih on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Let none of you wish for death because of a calamity that has befallen him. If he must wish for it, then let him say: O God, keep me alive as long as life is good for me, and let me die if death is good for me." Narrated by Muslim. And in it, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let none of you wish for death or supplicate for it before it comes to him, for when one of you dies, his deeds come to an end, and it only increases the believer in goodness. If this is proven, then how can it be said that Joseph, peace be upon him, wished for death, departure from this world, and the end of his deeds? This is far-fetched! Unless it is said that this was permissible in his law. As for it being permissible to wish for death and supplicate for it when tribulations appear and prevail, and one fears the loss of one’s religion, as we have explained in the Book of Remembrance, and the min in his saying: min al-mulk is for partiality, and likewise his saying: And You taught me of the interpretation of dreams because the kingship of Egypt was not all kingship, and the science of interpretation was not all sciences. It was said: min is for the genus, like his saying: So avoid the uncleanness of idols (al-Hajj 22:30). It was said: for emphasis, meaning You gave me the kingdom and taught me the interpretation of dreams. The Almighty’s saying: The Originator of the heavens and the earth is an adjective for calling, and He is Lord, and it is a calling with an addition, and the meaning is: O Lord! It is permissible for it to be a second calling. And the Originator is the Creator, so He, glory be to Him, is the Originator of all beings, meaning their Creator, their Originator, their Maker, and their Inventor absolutely from nothing, and no previous example, and this meaning was presented in full in Al-Baqarah, when He said: The Originator of the heavens and the earth, and we added an explanation of it in the Most Sublime Book in explaining the Most Beautiful Names of God. You are my Guardian meaning my Supporter and the One who takes care of my affairs in this world and the Hereafter. Let me die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous. He meant his three fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. God took him - pure and good, may God bless him and grant him peace - in Egypt, and he was buried in the Nile in a marble box. This is because when he died, the people argued over him, each one wanting to be buried in their own neighborhood, because of what they hoped for from his blessing. They agreed on that until they wanted to fight. They decided to bury him in the Nile from where the water splits in Egypt, so that the water would pass over him and then spread throughout all of Egypt, so that they would be in it by law. So they did. When Moses left with the Children of Israel, he took him out of the Nile and transferred his coffin after four hundred years to Jerusalem, so they buried him with his fathers because of his supplication: And join me with the righteous. He was one hundred and seven years old. On the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Joseph was thrown into the well when he was seventeen years old, and he was in slavery, prison, and kingship for eighty years, then his family was reunited and he lived after that for twenty-three years, and he had children Ephraim, Manasseh, and Rahmah, the wife of Job, according to Abu Lahi’ah. Al-Zuhri said: Ephraim - son of Joseph - had a son, Nun son of Ephraim, and Joshua was a son to Nun, so he is Joshua son of Nun, and he is the youth of Moses who was with him as his master, and God gave him prophecy in the time of Moses, peace be upon him, so he was a prophet after him, and he is the one who conquered Jericho, and killed the giants who were in it, and the sun stopped for him according to what was mentioned in Al-Ma’idah. And Moses son of Manasseh was born to Manasseh son of Joseph, before Moses son of Imran. The people of the Torah claim that he is the one who sought the scholar to learn from him until he caught up with him, and the scholar is the one who breached the ship, killed the boy, and built the wall, and Moses son of Manasseh was with him until he reached where he reached, and Ibn Abbas denied that, and what Ibn Abbas said is true, and so is in the Qur’an. Then there were nations and generations between Joseph and Moses, and between them was Shu`ayb, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them all.
12:102: The Almighty said: That is from the report of the unseen is a subject and a predicate. We reveal it to you is a second predicate. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that that means that, We reveal it to you is its predicate, that is, that which from the report of the unseen We reveal to you, meaning it is what We related to you, O Muhammad, from the report of the unseen We reveal it to you that is, We inform you of this revelation to you. And you were not with them that is, with Joseph's brothers when they decided their plan to throw Joseph into the well. And they were plotting that is, against Joseph to throw him into the well. It was said: They were plotting against Jacob when they brought him the shirt stained with blood, that is, you did not witness those conditions, but God informed you of them.
12:103: The Almighty said: And most of the people, even if you were eager, would not believe. He thought that when the Arabs asked him about this story and he told them, they would believe, but they did not believe. So the verse was revealed as a consolation to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning that you are not able to guide whomever you want to guide. You say: haras yaharis, like daraba yadhurub. And in a weak language, haras yaharis, like hamada yahamd. And harass is seeking something by choice.
