12:104: The Almighty says: And you do not ask them for any reward for it. From is a relative clause, meaning you do not ask them for any reward. It is meaning what it is, meaning the Qur’an and the revelation. Except a reminder meaning a lesson and a reminder for the worlds.
12:105: The Almighty said: And how many a sign is there in the heavens and the earth. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: It i.e. the kaf of comparison entered it and was built with it, so the meaning of how much came into the speech. The discussion of it has already been completed in Al Imran. The discussion of the verse the heavens and the earth has already been completed in Al Baqarah. It has been said: The signs are the effects of the punishments of the previous nations, i.e. they are heedless and turn away from contemplating them. Ikrimah and Amr ibn Faid read and the earth in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is they pass over it. Al-Suddi read and the earth in the accusative case with an implied verb, and the pause on these two readings is on the heavens. Ibn Masoud read: they walk over it.
12:106: The Almighty's saying: And most of them do not believe in God except while they associate others with Him. It was revealed about a people who acknowledged God as their Creator and the Creator of all things, yet they worship idols. This was stated by Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Amir Al-Sha'bi, and most of the commentators. Ikrimah said that it is His saying: And if you ask them, who created them, they will surely say, 'God' (al-Zukhruf 43:87). Then they describe Him with other than His description and attribute rivals to Him. Al-Hasan also said: They are People of the Book who have both polytheism and faith. They believed in God and disbelieved in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. So their faith is not valid. This was narrated by Ibn Al-Anbari. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about the Talbiyah of the polytheists of the Arabs: "Here I am, You have no partner except a partner who is Yours. You own him and what he owns." It was also narrated from him that they are the Christians. It was also narrated from him that they are the anthropomorphists, who believed in general terms and associated others with God in detail. It was said: It was revealed about the hypocrites, meaning: And most of them do not believe in God that is, with their tongues, except that they are disbelievers in their hearts. Al-Mawardi also mentioned this on the authority of Al-Hasan. Ata’ said: This is about supplication, because the disbelievers forget their Lord in times of ease, but when afflicted they are sincere in supplication. Its explanation is: And they think that they are surrounded (Yunus 10:22). And His statement: And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us at his side (Yunus 10:12). And in another verse: And when evil touches him, he is one of fervent supplication (Fussilat 41:51). It was said: Its meaning is that they call upon God to save them from destruction, and when He saves them, one of them says: If it were not for so-and-so, we would not have been saved, and if it were not for the dog, the thief would have entered upon us,” and so on, so they attribute the blessing of God to so-and-so, and His protection to the dog. I said: Many ordinary Muslims may fall into this statement and the one before it, and there is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Almighty. It was said: This verse was revealed in the story of the smoke, and that is because when the people of Mecca were covered by smoke during the years of famine, they said: Our Lord, remove the punishment from us, indeed we are believers (al-Dukhan 44:12). So that was their faith, and their polytheism was their return to disbelief after the punishment was removed, as explained by His statement: Indeed, you will return (al-Dukhan 44:15). And returning only occurs after beginning, so the meaning of: except while they are polytheists is except while they are returning to polytheism, and God knows best.
12:107: The Almighty said: Do they then feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from God? Ibn Abbas said: A great punishment. Mujahid said: A torment that will overwhelm them, similar to it. The Day the punishment will overwhelm them from above them and from beneath their feet. (al-Ankabut 29:55). Qatada said: A calamity that will befall them. Ad-Dahhak said: It means thunderbolts and calamities. "Or the Hour will come upon them?" meaning the Resurrection. "Suddenly" is an accusative of state, and its original form is a verbal noun. Al-Mubarrad said: The Arabs came with a state after an indefinite noun, which is their saying: "A matter happened suddenly." An-Nahhas said: "The meaning of 'suddenly' is an unexpected blow. And they do not perceive," and it is an emphasis. And his saying: "Suddenly," Ibn Abbas said: "The blast will call out to the people while they are in their markets and places, as He said: It will seize them while they are disputing. (Yasin~: 49) as will come.
12:108: The Almighty said: Say, 'This is my way.' is a subject and predicate, meaning say, O Muhammad, this is my way, my Sunnah, and my method, as Ibn Zayd said. Al-Rabi' said: My call. Muqatil: My religion, and the meaning is the same, meaning that which I am upon and call to leads to Paradise. On insight means on certainty and truth, and from it: So-and-so is insightful about this. I is an emphasis. And whoever follows me is in apposition to the pronoun. And glory be to God means say, O Muhammad: And glory be to God. And I am not of the polytheists who take rivals besides God.
12:109: The Almighty said: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns. This is a response to those who say: Why was an angel not sent down to him? (Al-An'am: 8), meaning We sent men among whom there was no woman, jinn, or angel. This refutes what is narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: "Among women there are four prophetesses: Eve, Asiya, the mother of Moses, and Mary." Something of this has already been mentioned in Al-Imran. Of the towns means cities. God did not send a prophet from the desert because of the prevalence of harshness and cruelty among the people of the desert, and because the origin of the cities is more rational, patient, better, and more knowledgeable. Al-Hasan said: God never sent a prophet from the desert, nor from women, nor from the jinn. Qatada said: Of the towns meaning from the people of the cities, because they are more knowledgeable and patient. The scholars said: One of the conditions of the Messenger is that he be a human, civilized man. They only said human as a precaution, based on His statement: They seek refuge with men from among the jinn (al-Jinn 72:6). And God knows best. God Almighty says: Have they not traveled through the land and observed the fates of the nations who denied their prophets so that they might take heed. And the home of the Hereafter is better is a subject and predicate. Al-Farra’ claimed that the home is the Hereafter, and the thing was attributed to itself because of the difference in wording, like Thursday and the first night. The poet said: Even if the land of Abs could overpower you, you would know humiliation with certainty. That is, with certainty of knowledge. Al-Kisa’i used as evidence their saying: the first prayer. Al-Akhfash used as evidence the mosque of the congregation. Al-Nahhas said: “Adding something to itself is impossible, because something is only added to something else to be recognized by it. The best is the first prayer. Whoever says the first prayer means: at the first obligatory prayer. It was called the first because it was the first prayer when prayer was made obligatory, and the first to be revealed. That is why it was also called the noon prayer. The meaning is: and the abode of the hereafter is better. This is the saying of the Basrans. What is meant by this abode is Paradise, meaning it is better for the righteous. It was read: “and the abode of the hereafter.” Nafi’, Asim, Ya’qub, and others read Do you not understand? with a ta’ as an address. The rest read it with a ya’ as a statement.
12:110: The Almighty said: Until when the messengers despaired The reading of it and its meaning has been presented. And they thought that they had been denied This verse contains the exoneration of the prophets and their infallibility from what is not befitting of them. This chapter is important, and its danger is grave, and it should be stopped at so that a person does not slip and end up in the midst of Hell. The meaning is: We did not send before you, O Muhammad, except men, and then We did not punish their nations with torment. Until when the messengers despaired meaning they despaired of the belief of their people. And they thought that they had been denied with emphasis, meaning they were certain that their people denied them. It was said that the meaning is: They thought that those of their people who believed in them denied them, not that the people denied them, but the prophets thought and thought that they were denying them, meaning they feared that doubt would enter the hearts of their followers, so and they thought is in its context in this interpretation. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masoud, Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Sulami, Abu Jaafar bin Al-Qaqa, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Abu Raja Al-Attardi, Asim, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, Yahya bin Wathab, Al-A’mash and Khalaf read kadhdhba with a light pronunciation, meaning the people thought that the messengers lied to them about what they told them about the punishment, and they did not believe them. It was said that the meaning is that the nations thought that the messengers lied about what they promised them of victory. In the narration of Ibn Abbas, the messengers thought that God had broken His promise to them. It was said that this narration is not authentic, because such a thought is not thought of the messengers, and whoever thinks such a thought does not deserve consideration, so how could he say: Our victory came to them?! Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: It is not far-fetched, if the narration is authentic, that what is meant is that this occurred to the hearts of the messengers without them realizing it in their souls. In the hadith: God the Almighty has forgiven my nation for what their souls have thought about as long as they have not uttered it or acted upon it. It is permissible to say: they came close to that thought, like you say: I reached the home, meaning I came close to it. Al-Tha'labi and Al-Nahhas reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: They were human beings who became weak due to the length of the affliction, and they forgot and thought that they had failed, then he recited: Until the Messenger and those who believed with him say, 'When is the victory of God?' (al-Baqarah 2:214). Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim said: The reason for it in our view is that the messengers were afraid after God had promised victory, not because of suspicion of God's promise, but because of suspicion in their souls that they had done something that would break that condition and covenant that was entrusted to them, so if the period was prolonged, despair and suspicions entered them from this aspect. Al-Mahdawi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The messengers thought that they had failed in what befalls humans, and he cited as evidence the words of Abraham, peace be upon him: My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead (al-Baqarah 2:260) and the verse. The first reading is better. Mujahid and Hamid read - Qad qaddabu with the opening of the kaf and the dhal, with a lightened meaning: And the people of the messengers thought that the messengers had been forgotten, when they saw the favor of God, the Almighty, in delaying the punishment. It is possible that the meaning is: When the messengers were certain that their people had lied about God through their disbelief, the messengers came with Our victory. In Bukhari, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, she said to him while he was asking her about the statement of God, the Almighty: Until when the messengers despaired, he said: I said: Did they lie or were they lied to? Aisha said: They lied: They were certain that their people had lied to them, so what is it by conjecture? She said: Yes! By my life! They were certain of that, so I said to her: And they thought that they had been lied to She said: God forbid! The messengers did not think that about their Lord. I said: What is this verse? She said: They are the followers of the messengers who believed in their Lord and believed them, so the affliction was prolonged for them, and victory was delayed from them until when the messengers despaired of those from their people who had lied to them, and the messengers thought that their followers had lied to them, then Our victory came to them at that time. And concerning the words of God the Almighty: Our victory came to them there are two sayings: One of them: The Messengers came with God's victory, said by Mujahid. The second: The punishment of God came to their people, said by Ibn Abbas. Then We will save whom We will it was said: The prophets and those who believed with them. It was narrated from Asim Then We will save whom We will with one noon and an open yaa, and of is in the nominative case, a noun whose agent is not named, and Abu Ubaid chose this reading because it is in the Mushaf of Uthman and all the Mushafs of the countries with one noon. Ibn Muhaysin read Then We willed as a past tense verb, and of is in the nominative case because it is the agent, and according to the reading of the rest it is in the accusative case as the object. And Our punishment is not repelled meaning Our punishment. From the criminal people meaning the disbelieving polytheists.
12:111: The Almighty said: There was certainly in their stories meaning in the story of Joseph, his father and his brothers, or in the stories of the nations. A lesson meaning an idea, reminder and sermon. For those of understanding meaning the intellects. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Al-Harith At-Taymi: Jacob lived one hundred and forty-seven years, and his brother Esau died with him on the same day, and they were buried in the same grave, so His statement: There was certainly in their stories a lesson for those of understanding to the end of the surah. It was not a fabricated story meaning the Qur'an was not a fabricated story, or this story was not a fabricated story. But a confirmation of that which was before it meaning but it was a confirmation, and it is permissible to raise it in the meaning of but it is the confirmation of that which was before it, meaning what was before it of the Torah and the Gospel and the rest of the Books of God Almighty, and this is the interpretation of those who claim that it is the Qur'an. And a detailed account of everything that the servants need of what is permissible and what is forbidden, and the laws and rulings. And guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
13:1: It was revealed in Mecca according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir, and Medinan according to Al-Kalbi and Muqatil. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: It was revealed in Medinan except for two verses that were revealed in Mecca, which are the words of God Almighty: And if there were a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved (Ar-Ra'd: 31) and so on. God the Almighty said: These are the verses of the Book. We have already discussed them. And that which has been revealed to you means this is the Qur’an that has been revealed to you. From your Lord is the truth not as the polytheists say: You bring it of your own accord, so hold fast to it and act according to what is in it. Muqatil said: It was revealed when the polytheists said: Muhammad brought the Qur’an of his own accord. And that is in the nominative case in apposition to verses or to the subject, and the truth is its predicate. It is permissible for its position to be in the genitive case based on the estimation: and the verses of that which has been revealed to you, and the nominative case of the truth based on this is based on the implication of a subject, the estimation of which is: that truth, like God the Almighty’s saying: And they know the truth means that truth. Al-Farra’ said: If you wish, you can make that in the genitive case as an attribute of the Book, even if it contains the letter and as it is said: This book came to us from Abu Hafs and Al-Faruq, and from this is the saying of the poet: To the venerable king, the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded place He wants: To the king, Al-Qarm bin Al-Hammam, the lion of the battalion. But most people do not believe.
13:2: The Almighty said: God is He Who raised the heavens without pillars that you can see the verse. When the Almighty explained that the Qur'an is true, He explained that the One who sent it down is capable of perfection, so look at His creations to know the perfection of His power, and this meaning has been presented. And in His saying: without pillars that you can see there are two opinions: The first: that it was raised without pillars that you can see, said by Qatada, Iyas bin Muawiyah and others. The second: it has pillars, but we do not see it, Ibn Abbas said: it has pillars on Mount Qaf, and it can be said according to this opinion: the pillars are His power with which He holds the heavens and the earth, and they are not visible to us, mentioned by Al-Zajjaj. Ibn Abbas also said: it is the monotheism of the believer. He raised the pillars of the sky when it was about to burst from the disbelief of the disbeliever, mentioned by Al-Ghaznawi. And the pillar is any column, Al-Nabigha said: The jinn are despicable. I have given them permission to build Palmyra with stones and columns. Then He established Himself on the Throne has been discussed above. And He subjected the sun and the moon meaning He made them subservient to the benefit of His creation and the interests of His servants, and every creation is subservient to the Creator. Each runs for a specified term meaning until a known time, which is the passing of this world and the establishment of the Hour at which the sun will be rolled up, the moon will be eclipsed, the stars will be extinguished, and the planets will be scattered. Ibn Abbas said: By the specified term He meant their degrees and stations which they will reach and will not exceed. It was said: The meaning of the specified term is that the moon completes its orbit in a month, and the sun in a year. He directs the affair meaning He directs it as He wills. He details the signs meaning He explains them, meaning He who has power over these things has power over the return, and for this reason He said: Perhaps you will be certain of the meeting with your Lord.
13:3: The Almighty said: And it is He who spread out the earth because He distinguished the signs of the heavens from the signs of the earth, meaning He spread out the earth in length and breadth. And placed therein firm mountains meaning fixed mountains, the singular of which is raasiya, because the earth is fixed by them, meaning it is established, and fixing is stability. Antara said: So I was patient, knowing that, and I am free to anchor if the coward's soul rises Jamil said: I love her and he who established its foundations with love if its verses appear hidden Ibn Abbas and Ata said: The first mountain placed on the earth was Abu Qubais. Question: This verse is a response to those who claim that the Earth is like a ball, and a response to those who claim that the Earth's gates fall upon it. Ibn al-Rawandi claimed that under the Earth there is an ascending body like the ascending wind, and it is descending, so the descending and ascending bodies are equal in mass and strength and they agree. Others claimed that the Earth is composed of two bodies, one of which is descending and the other ascending, so they are equal, and that is why it stopped. What the Muslims and the People of the Book agree upon is the statement that the Earth stops, is still and extends, and that its movement usually occurs through an earthquake that strikes it. And the Almighty's statement: And rivers means running waters in the Earth, in which are the benefits of creation. And of all the fruits He has made therein two mates meaning two types. Abu Ubaidah said: The mates are one, and they can be two. Al-Farra' said: What is meant by the mates here is the male and female, and this is contrary to the text. It was said: The meaning of mates is two types, like sweet and sour, moist and dry, white and black, small and large. Indeed in that are signs meaning indications and indications for a people who give thought.
13:4: It has five issues: The first: The Almighty’s statement: And on the earth are adjacent tracts. There is an omission in the speech, meaning: And on the earth are adjacent tracts and non-adjacent tracts, as He said: Garments to protect you from the heat (al-Nahl 16:81), and the meaning is and protect you from the cold, then it was omitted for the listener’s knowledge. Adjacent tracts are cities and what is inhabited, and non-adjacent tracts are deserts and what is not inhabited. The second: The Almighty’s saying: neighboring villages meaning villages close together, their soil is the same, their water is the same, and they have crops and gardens, then they differ in fruits and dates, so some are sweet, and some are sour, and the fruit of one branch of a tree may differ in small and large, in color and taste, even if the sun and moon spread out over all of them in the same order, and in this is the clearest evidence of His Oneness and the greatness of His Eternal Self, and guidance for those who have strayed from knowing Him, for He, the Almighty, alerted with His saying: watered with one water that all of that is only by His will and desire, and that it is possible with His powers, and this is the clearest evidence of the invalidity of the statement of nature, because if that were by water and soil and nature was the agent for it, then the difference would not have occurred. It was said: The point of the argument is that he established the difference between the places, so some have fresh soil, and some have salty soil despite their being adjacent, and this is also from the indications as You have estimated, glory and majesty be to Him above what the wrongdoers and deniers say, far above. Third: The infidels - may God curse them - believed that every event occurs by itself, not from a maker. They claimed this about the fruits that come out of trees. They acknowledged their occurrence, denied their originator, and denied the symptoms. A group said: The fruits occur not from a maker, and they attributed an agent to the symptoms. The evidence that an event must have a originator is that it occurs at a time, and what is of its kind occurs at another time. If its occurrence at its time was due to its being specific to it, then everything of its kind would have to occur at its time. Since its being specific to its time is invalidated, it is correct that its being specific to it is due to a specific reason that He specified it with. If He had not specified it with it, its occurrence at its time would not have been more appropriate than its occurrence before or after that. The completion of this is in the science of theology. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And gardens of grapes. Al-Hasan read and gardens with a kasra on the ta’, on the assumption: And He placed therein gardens, so it is based on His saying: And placed therein firm mountains. It is permissible for it to be in the genitive case based on all, on the assumption: And of all fruits, and of gardens. The rest: gardens in the nominative case based on the assumption: And between them are gardens. And crops and palm trees, two in pairs and not two in pairs in the nominative case. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Hafs in apposition to the gardens, that is, on the assumption: And in the earth are crops and palm trees. The rest lowered it in sequence to the grapes, so the crops and palm trees are from the gardens, and it is permissible for it to be in apposition to all according to what was mentioned in and gardens. Mujahid, Al-Salami and others read Sanwan with a damma on the sad, and the rest read it with a kasra. They are two dialects, and they are the plural of Sanw, which is the palm trees and the two palm trees, they are gathered by one root, and heads branch out from it to become palm trees, similar to it is Qanawan, the singular of which is Qanw. Abu Ishaq narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa, who said: The Sunwan is the one that is gathered, and other than the Sunwan is the one that is scattered. An-Nahhas said: And it is the same in the language. A palm tree is called if there is another palm tree or more in it, Sunwan. And the Sun is the example, and from it is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: A man’s paternal uncle is his father’s twin. There is no difference in it between the dual and the plural, nor in the inflection, so the plural nun is inflected, and the dual nun is broken. The poet said: Knowledge and patience are two things that make a person generous and beautiful when they come together. Two things that cannot be completed without combining them together. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: They are watered with one water, like the righteous and the wicked of the children of Adam, their father is one, as stated by An-Nahhas and Al-Bukhari. Asim and Ibn Amir read: is watered with a ya’, meaning they are all watered. The rest read it with a ta’, because of His saying: gardens, and Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaidah chose it. Abu Amr said: The feminine is better, because of His saying: And We favor some of them over others in eating, and He did not say some of it. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i and others read and He favors with a ya’ in response to His saying: He directs the matter, and He separates and He covers the rest with a noon meaning: And We favor. Jabir bin Abdullah narrated: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say to Ali, may God be pleased with him: People are from different trees, and you and I are from one tree, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, read: And on the earth are neighboring plots, until he reached His saying: is watered with one water and eating is the fruit. Ibn Abbas said: It means sweet and sour, Persian and date palm. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the words of God the Almighty: And We excel some of them over others in taste, he said: Persian and date palm, sweet and sour. Al-Tha’labi mentioned it. Al-Hasan said: What is meant by this verse is a parable that God the Almighty gave for the children of Adam, their origin is one, yet they differ in good and evil, faith and disbelief, like the difference between fruits that are watered with the same water. From this is the saying of the poet: People are like plants, and plants have different colors, including sandalwood, camphor, and eucalyptus. And there is a tree from which tar ripens for a long time. Indeed in that are signs for a people who understand. That is, signs for whoever has a heart that understands from God Almighty:
13:5: God the Almighty said: And if you are amazed, then their statement is amazed meaning if you are amazed, O Muhammad, at their denial of you after you were, in their view, the truthful and trustworthy, then their denial of the resurrection is amazed at you. God the Almighty is not amazed, and it is not permissible for Him to be amazed, because the soul changes with hidden causes. Rather, He mentioned that so that His Prophet and the believers would be amazed at it. It was said that the meaning is: if you are amazed, O Muhammad, at their denial of the resurrection while they acknowledge that I am the Creator of the heavens and the earth and the different fruits from the same earth, then their statement is a wonder that the creation is amazed at, because the return is in the meaning of the beginning. It was said: The verse is about those who deny the Creator, meaning if you are amazed at their denial of the Creator with the clear evidence that the changeable must have a changer, then this is the place of amazement, and the structure of the verse indicates the first and second, because He said: If we are dust meaning will we be resurrected if we are dust?! Will we indeed be in a new creation? And it was read inna. Shackles is the plural of ghal, which is a collar that the hand is tied with to the neck, meaning that they will be shackled on the Day of Resurrection, as evidenced by His statement: When the shackles are around their necks (Ghafir 40:71) until His statement: Then in the Fire they will be burned (Ghafir 40:72). It was said that the shackles are their evil deeds that are binding on them.
13:6: The Almighty said: And they urge you to hasten the evil before the good meaning, due to their extreme denial and rejection, they seek punishment. It was said that it is their saying: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky (al-Anfal 8:32). Qatada said: They sought punishment before well-being, and God, the Almighty, has ruled to delay the punishment for this nation until the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: Before the good meaning before the faith through which security and good deeds are hoped for. And the examples are the punishments, the singular of which is the example. It was narrated from Al-A'mash that he read the examples with a damma on the meem and a sukoon on the tha', and this is the plural of example. It is permissible for the examples to be replaced by a fatha from the damma because of its heaviness. It was also said that the fatha is brought instead of the ha'. It was narrated from Al-A'mash that he read the examples with a fatha on the meem and a sukoon on the tha', and this is the plural of example, then the damma was deleted because of its heaviness. Al-Nahhas, may God have mercy on him, mentioned all of them. And the reading of the group is one example, such as sadaqa and sadaqa, and Tamim adds both tha and meem, its singular in their language is mithala, with damma on the meem and jazm on the tha, such as ghurfa and ghurafaat, and the verb from it is mithalta bih amathal, with fatha on the meem and sukoon on the tha. And indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness meaning He is the One who overlooks the polytheists if they believe, and the sinners if they repent. Ibn Abbas said: The most hopeful verse in the Book of God is “And indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing. And indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty” if they persist in disbelief. Hammad bin Salamah narrated on the authority of Ali bin Zaid on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab who said: “When the verse was revealed: “And indeed, your Lord is the Possessor of forgiveness for the people despite their wrongdoing. And indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty,” the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Were it not for God’s forgiveness, mercy, and overlooking, no one would enjoy life, and were it not for His punishment, threat, and torment, everyone would be tired.”
13:7: God Almighty said: And those who disbelieve say, ‘Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?’ When they proposed the signs and asked for them, God Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You are only a warner, meaning a teacher. And for every people there is a guide, meaning a prophet who calls them to God. It was said: The guide is God, meaning you are responsible for warning, and God is the guide of every people if He wants to guide them.
13:8: It contains eight issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: God knows what every female bears, meaning male and female, good and bad, righteous and wicked. It was mentioned in Surat Al-An’am that God, the Exalted, is the only One with knowledge of the unseen, with no partner. We mentioned there the hadith of Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The keys of the unseen are five. The hadith states: No one knows what the wombs conceal or increase except God. The scholars differed in the interpretation of His saying: And what the wombs conceal or increase. Qatada said: The meaning is what is lost before nine months, and what is increased after nine. Ibn Abbas said the same. Mujahid said: If a woman menstruates during her pregnancy, that is a deficiency in her child. If it exceeds nine months, it is complete, not a deficiency. It was narrated from him: Ghayd is what the wombs conceal of blood, and augmentation is what is increased from it. It was said: Ghayd and augmentation refer to the child, such as the deficiency of a finger or something else, or the increase of a finger or something else. It was said: Ghayd is the cessation of menstrual blood. And what is increased by postpartum blood after giving birth. Second: In this verse is evidence that a pregnant woman menstruates, and this is the doctrine of Malik and Al-Shafi’i in one of his two opinions. Ata’, Al-Sha’bi and others said: She does not menstruate, and Abu Hanifa said the same, and his evidence is the verse. Ibn Abbas said in its interpretation: It is the menstruation of pregnant women, and this is what was narrated from Ikrimah and Mujahid, and it is the opinion of Aisha, and that she used to issue a fatwa to pregnant women when they menstruated that they should stop praying, and the companions at that time were abundant, and none of them objected to her, so it became like a consensus, said Ibn Al-Qassar. It was mentioned that two men disputed over a child, so they took him to Umar, may God be pleased with him, so he showed him to the fortune teller, and the fortune teller attributed him to them, so Umar hit him with a whip, and asked some women of Quraysh and said: Look, what is the matter with this child? They said: The first one was alone with her and he was alone with her, so she menstruated while pregnant, and she thought that her waiting period had ended, so the second one entered her, and the child was revived by the water of the second one, so Umar said: God is Great! He included it with the first, and he did not say that a pregnant woman does not menstruate, nor did any of the companions say that, so it indicates that it is a consensus, and God knows best. The opponent argued by saying that if a pregnant woman menstruated, and what the woman sees of blood is menstruation, then it would not be valid for a slave woman to purify herself with menstruation, and this is a consensus. And it was narrated from Malik in the book of Muhammad what indicates that it is not menstruation. Third: This verse is evidence that a pregnant woman may give birth after less than nine months or more. Scholars agree that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, and that Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan was born after six months. Fourth: These six months are based on the crescent moons, like all the other months of the Shari’ah. Therefore, it has been narrated in the school of thought from some of the companions of Malik, and I think it is in the book of Ibn Harith, that if three days are less than the six months, then the child is attributed to the reason for the deficiency and excess of the months, as narrated by Ibn Atiyyah. Fifth: Scholars differed regarding the maximum period of pregnancy. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Jamila bint Saad on the authority of Aisha who said: Pregnancy does not last more than two years, the length of time it takes for the shadow of a spindle to turn. This was mentioned by Al-Daraqutni. Jamila bint Saad - the sister of Ubayd bin Saad - said, and on the authority of Al-Layth bin Saad - that the maximum period is three years. Al-Shafi’i narrated on the authority of four years. It was narrated on the authority of Malik in one of his two narrations, and the well-known opinion from him is five years. It was narrated on his authority that there is no limit to it, even if it exceeds ten years, and this is the third narration from him. Al-Zuhri narrated on the authority of six and seven. Abu Omar said: Some of the Companions extend it to seven. Al-Shafi’i said: The maximum period of it is four years. The people of Kufa say: Two years and no more. Muhammad bin Abdul-Hakam says: One year and no more. Dawud says: Nine months, and he does not have a pregnancy longer than that. Abu Omar said: This is an issue that has no basis except independent reasoning, and referring back to what is known about women. And God is the Grantor of success. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim who said: I said to Malik bin Anas that I was told on the authority of Aisha that she said: A woman’s pregnancy does not exceed two years, the length of the shadow of a spindle. He said: Glory be to God! Who says this?! This is our neighbor, the wife of Muhammad bin Ajlan. She gets pregnant and gives birth in four years. A woman of truth, and her husband is a man of truth. She got pregnant three times in twelve years, each pregnancy lasting four years. And he mentioned it on the authority of Al-Mubarak bin Mujahid who said: It is well-known among us that the wife of Muhammad bin Ajlan gets pregnant and gives birth in four years, and she was called the elephant carrier. It was also narrated that Malik bin Dinar was sitting one day when a man came to him and said: O Abu Yahya! Pray for a woman who has been pregnant for four years and has become in great distress. Malik became angry and closed the Qur’an and said: These people do not see us as anyone but prophets! Then he recited, then he supplicated, then he said: O God, if there is wind in this woman’s belly, then remove it from her at once, and if there is a girl in her belly, then replace her with a boy, for You erase what You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book. Malik raised his hand, and the people raised their hands, and the Messenger came to the man and said: Save your wife. The man went, and Malik had not lowered his hand before the man came out of the door of the mosque with a curly-haired boy, four years old, on his neck, his teeth were straight, and his navel had not been cut. It was also narrated that a man came to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: O Commander of the Faithful! I was absent from my wife for two years and came back pregnant, so Umar consulted the people about stoning her, and Muadh ibn Jabal said: O Commander of the Faithful! If you have a right to her, then you have no right to what is in her belly, so leave her until she gives birth. So he left her, and she gave birth to a boy whose two front teeth had come out, and the man recognized the resemblance and said: My son, by the Lord of the Kaaba! Umar said: Women are unable to give birth to the likes of Muadh, were it not for Muadh, Umar would have perished. Ad-Dahhak said: My mother gave birth to me after carrying me in her womb for two years, and she gave birth to me after my tooth had come out. It is mentioned on the authority of Malik that he was carried in his mother’s womb for two years, and it was said: three years. It is said: Muhammad ibn Ajlan remained in his mother’s womb for three years, and she died while he was trembling violently, so her womb was cut open and he was taken out with his teeth still growing. Hammad ibn Salamah said: Harim ibn Hayyan was called Harim because he remained in his mother’s womb for four years. Al-Ghaznawi mentioned that Ad-Dahhak was born at the age of two, and his tooth had already come out, so he was called Ad-Dahhak. Ibad ibn Al-Awwam: A neighbor of ours gave birth to a boy at the age of four years, whose hair reached his shoulders, and a bird passed by him and said: Kash. Sixth: Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: The minimum and maximum of menstruation and postpartum bleeding and the minimum and maximum of pregnancy are taken from the path of ijtihad, because knowledge of that is kept to God alone, so it is not permissible to rule on anything of it except to the extent that He has revealed to us, and it is found apparent in women, rarely or usually, and when we found a woman who had been pregnant for four years or five years, we ruled accordingly, and as for postpartum bleeding and menstruation, since we did not find a settled matter in them, we returned to what is found in the rare ones among them. Seventh: Ibn al-Arabi said: Some of the lenient Malikis have reported that the longest period of pregnancy is nine months, and this has never been said except by Halki, and they are the naturalists who claim that the management of pregnancy in the womb is the seven planets, taking it month by month, and the fourth month is for the sun, and therefore it moves and turbulent, and if the rotation between the seven planets is complete in the seven months, it returns in the eighth month to Saturn, which receives it with its coldness. I wish I could debate or fight them! Why is it that the reference after the completion of the cycle is to Saturn and not to any other? Did God inform you of this, or are you lying about God?! And if it is permissible for it to return to two of them, why is it not permissible for the management to return to three or four, or to return to all of them twice or three times?! What is this control of false assumptions over internal matters?! Eighth: The Almighty’s statement: And everything with Him is by measure. That is, of decrease and increase. It is said: by measure is the amount of time a child leaves his mother’s womb, and the amount of time he stays in her womb until he leaves. Qatada said: in provision and life span. The measure is the amount, and the generality of the verse includes all of that, and God Almighty knows best.
13:9: I said: This verse praises God, the Most High, by saying that He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, meaning He knows what is hidden from creation and what they have witnessed. The unseen is the source of the absent. The witnessed is a source meaning the witness, so God, the Most High, pointed out His uniqueness in knowledge of the unseen and the encompassing of the inner that is hidden from creation, so it is not permissible for anyone to share that with Him. As for the doctors who deduce evidence from signs and indications, if they are certain of that, then it is disbelief, and if they say that it is an experiment, then they leave what they are doing, and that does not detract from the one being praised, because custom can be broken, and knowledge cannot be changed. And the Great is the One to whom everything is below. The Most High is above what the polytheists say, and He is supreme over everything with His power and might. We have mentioned them both in detail in the explanation of the names, and praise be to God.
13:10: The Almighty says: Whether you conceal your speech or declare it aloud is the same among you. Concealed speech is what a person says to himself, and speaking aloud is what he says to others. What is meant by this is that God, the Exalted, knows what a person conceals of good and evil, just as He knows what he declares of good and evil. Of you may be related to equal in the sense: equal among you, like when you say: I passed by Zayd. It may also be understood as: whoever among you conceals his speech, and whoever among you declares it aloud. It may also be understood as: equally among you, whether he conceals his speech or declares it aloud, like when you say: Zayd and Amr are just, meaning both are just. It was said: equal means equal, so there is no need to estimate the deletion of an adjective. And whoever hides by night and travels by day meaning that in God's knowledge, the secret and the open are equal, the one who appears on the roads and the one who hides in the darkness. Al-Akhfash and Qatrib said: The one who hides at night is the one who appears. From this comes the word khafayt which means I revealed something, and akhfayt which means I extracted something. From this comes the word al-Nabhas which means the hidden one. Imru’ al-Qais said: Their secrets are hidden from their tunnels, as if their secrets were hidden and thin from the evening brought And the hidden thief, meaning the one who enters in a swarm, and from this their saying: The wild animal swarmed when it entered its lair. Ibn Abbas said: Mustakhfi is hidden, Wasrab is apparent. Mujahid: Mustakhfi of sins, Wasrab is apparent. It was said: The meaning of Sarab is going. Al-Kisa’i said: Sarrab yasraban saruban if he went, and the poet said: There are people who have come close to untying their stallion, but we have taken off his fetters and he is on the run. Any one who goes. Abu Raja said: The wanderer is the one who goes on his face on the earth. The poet said: I have been a thief, but I have not been a thief Al-Qatabi said: Sarab bi-an-Nahar means he goes about his business quickly, from their saying, the water flowed. Al-Asma’i said: Khall Sarbah means his way.
13:11: The Almighty said: For Him are angels who follow one another meaning that God has angels who follow one another by night and by day. When the angels of the night ascend, the angels of the day follow them. He said: following angels and angels are masculine because it is the plural of follower, it is said: a follower angel, and follower angels, then follower angels is the plural of the plural. Some of them read - For Him are followers before him and behind him. And follower angels are the plural of follower, and it was said that the angels are follower in the word angels. It was said: It is feminine because of the abundance of that from them, like genealogist, scholar, and narrator, as said by Al-Jawhari and others. Follow-up is the return after the beginning, God the Almighty said: And he turned back and did not follow (al-Naml 27:10) meaning he did not return, and in the hadith: following angels, the one who says them - or - does them will not be disappointed so he mentioned glorifying, praising, and magnifying. Abu Al-Haitham said: They are called Mu'aqabat because they return time after time. The verb of the one who does an action and then returns to it has been followed. The Mu'aqabat are the camels that stand at the haunches of the camels that are fighting at the water tank. When a she-camel turns away, another one takes its place. His statement, from before him means the one who hides at night and the one who walks during the day. They guard him by the command of God There is a difference of opinion about this guarding. It was said: It is possible that the angels' entrusting them with guarding them from wild animals, vermin, and harmful things is a kindness from Him to him. So when the decree comes, they leave him alone with it. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them. Abu Majlaz said: A man from Murad came to Ali and said: Beware, for some people from Murad want to kill you. He said: With every man there are two angels who guard him as long as he is not destined. When the decree comes, they leave him alone with the decree of God. The appointed time is a strong fortress. Based on this, they guard him by the command of God means by the command of God and by His permission. So -min means ba, and the letters of the attributes take the place of each other. It was also said: min means an, meaning ba, and the letters of the attributes take the place of each other. It was also said min means an, meaning they guard him by the command of God. This is close to the first, meaning they guard him by the command of God, not from themselves. This is the saying of Al-Hasan. You say: I clothed him from nakedness and from nakedness. From this is the saying of the Almighty: And feed them from hunger (Quraysh 106:4), meaning from hunger. It was said: They protect him from the angels of punishment, so that no punishment will befall him, because God does not change the blessings and well-being of a people until they change what is in themselves by persisting in disbelief. If they persist, the appointed time will come and the punishment will descend upon them, and the guardian angels will be removed from them. It was said: They protect him from the jinn. Ka`b said: If God had not assigned angels to you to defend you in your food, drink, and private parts, the jinn would have snatched you away. The angels of punishment are from the command of God, and He singled them out by saying: from the command of God because they are not seen, as He said: “Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord” (al-Isra’ 17:85), meaning it is not from what you see. Al-Farra’ said: There is an inversion in the speech, meaning, he has guardian angels from the command of God from before him and from behind him who protect him, and this was narrated from Mujahid, Ibn Jurayj, and Al-Nakha’i, and that the angels of punishment and the jinn are from the command of God, there is no inversion in it, and Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning is that they protect his work, so the complement was omitted. Qatada said: They write down his words and actions. It is permissible, if the angels are the guardian angels, that the ha’ in for him refers to God, the Almighty, as we mentioned. It is also permissible for it to refer to the one who hides, and this is one opinion. It was said: He has guardian angels before him and behind him meaning the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, meaning that the angels protect him from his enemies. The Messenger was mentioned in His statement: Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord? You are only a warner meaning, whether you conceal your speech or declare it openly, it does not harm the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, rather he has guardian angels who protect him, peace be upon him. It is permissible that this refers to all the Messengers, because He said: And for every people is a guide meaning they protect the guide before him and behind him. This is a fourth opinion: that what is meant by the verse are the sultans and princes who have people before them and behind them who protect them, so when the command of God comes, they will not avail them against God at all. Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah said this. Ad-Dahhak also said: He is the sultan who is cautious of the command of God, the polytheist. It has been said: In the speech on this interpretation there is an omitted negation, the estimation of which is: They do not protect him from the command of God, the Most High, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. Al-Mahdawi said: And whoever made the successors the guards, the meaning is: They protect him from the command of God, according to his assumption and claim. And it has been said: Whether he keeps his speech secret or he speaks it openly, he has guards and helpers who take turns over him, so they urge him to commit sins, and they protect him from being preached to effectively. Al-Qushayri said: This does not prevent the Lord from granting him respite until the punishment is due, and if this sinner changes what is in himself through long persistence, then that becomes a reason for the punishment, so it is as if he is the one who brings about the punishment himself, so his statement: They protect him from the command of God means from obeying the command of God. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: The successors are what takes turns from the command of God and His judgment on His servants. Al-Mawardi said: And whoever said this statement, then there are two interpretations of his statement: They protect from the command of God: One of them: They protect him from death as long as his term has not come, as Ad-Dahhak said. Second: They protect him from the jinn and harmful vermin, unless the decree comes - said Abu Umamah and Ka'b al-Ahbar - but when the decree comes, they leave him alone. The correct view is that the angels who follow one another are the angels, and this is what al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Jurayj said. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and al-Nahhas chose it, and he provided evidence for it with the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Angels succeed one another among you by night and angels by day, the hadith, narrated by the imams. The imams narrated on the authority of Amr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who recited - Angels succeed one another before him and guardians behind him by the command of God, guarding him. This clarifies the meaning. Kinanah al-Adawi said: Uthman, may God be pleased with him, entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God! Tell me about the servant, how many angels are with him? He said: An angel on your right writes down the good deeds and another on your left writes down the bad deeds. The one on the right is the commander of the one on the left. So if you do a good deed, ten are written down. And if you do a bad deed, the one on the left says to the one on the right: Should I write? He says: No, perhaps he will seek forgiveness from God Almighty or repent. So if he says it three times, he says: Yes, write. May God Almighty relieve us of him. What a bad companion he is. How little he watches God Almighty and how little he is ashamed of us. God Almighty says: Not a word does he utter but there is a watcher by him ready to record it. (Qaf: 18). And two angels before you and behind you. God Almighty says: He has guardians before him and behind him who guard him by the command of God. And an angel holding your forelock. So if you humble yourself before God, He will raise you up, and if you are arrogant towards God, He will break you. And two angels on your lips, and they do not guard over you except the prayers upon Muhammad and his family. And an angel standing over your mouth, not allowing a snake to enter your mouth. And two angels over your eyes. So these are ten angels over every human being, rotating between the angels of the night and the angels of the day, because the angels of the night are not the angels of the day. So these are… Twenty angels over every human being, and Iblis is with the son of Adam during the day and his son during the night. This was mentioned by Al-Tha'labi. Al-Hasan said: The successors are four angels who gather at the time of the dawn prayer. Al-Tabari's choice is that the successors are the processions in front of the princes and behind them, and the ha in lahu refers to them, as mentioned above. The scholars, may God be pleased with them, said: God, the Exalted, made His commands in two ways: One of them: He decreed its occurrence and coming to pass with its owner, so no one can prevent or change that. The other: He decreed its coming, but He did not decree its occurrence and coming to pass, rather He decreed its removal by repentance, supplication, charity, and preservation. God the Almighty says: Indeed, God will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. God the Almighty informs us in this verse that He will not change the condition of a people until they change something, either from themselves or from the one overseeing them, or from someone who is from them because of it, just as God changed the condition of those who were defeated on the Day of Uhud because the archers changed themselves, and other examples of the Shari’ah. So the meaning of the verse is not that no punishment is sent down to anyone unless he commits a sin, rather calamities may befall them because of the sins of others, as the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said when he was asked: Will we be destroyed even though there are righteous people among us? He said: Yes, if evil increases. And God knows best. God the Almighty says: And when God intends evil for a people meaning destruction and punishment, there is no averting it. It was said: If He intends to afflict them with diseases and illnesses, there is no averting His affliction. It was also said: If God intends evil for a people, He blinds their sight until they choose what is afflicting and do it, so they walk to their destruction with their feet, until one of them searches for his fate with his hand, and strives with his foot to shed his blood. And they have no protector besides Him meaning refuge, and this is the meaning of al-Suddi’s statement. It was also said: No supporter to prevent them from His punishment. The poet said: There is no guardian in the heavens except the Most Gracious And Wali and Wali are able and powerful.
13:12: The Almighty says: It is He who shows you lightning, [causing] fear and hope, and produces the heavy clouds. That is, with rain. And clouds is plural, and the singular is cloud, and clouds and clouds are also in the plural.
13:13: "And the thunder exalts Him with praise, and the angels as well, for fear of Him. And He sends down thunderbolts." Thunder, lightning, and thunderbolts have already been discussed in Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. The purpose of the verse is to clarify the perfection of His power, and that delaying punishment is not due to inability. That is, He shows you the lightning in the sky as a fear for the traveler, for he fears its harm because of the rain, terror, and thunderbolts that befall him. God the Most High said: Harm from rain (An-Nisa’: 102) and in the hope that the one who is present will be followed by rain and fertility. Qatada, Mujahid, and others said this meaning. Al-Hasan said: Out of fear of thunderbolts and in hope of His rain that removes drought. And He produces the heavy clouds Mujahid said: meaning with water. The thunder glorifies Him with praise Whoever says that thunder is the sound of the clouds, then it is permissible for thunder to glorify an angel based on the creation of life in it. The evidence for the correctness of this statement is his statement: And the angels for fear of Him. If thunder were an angel, then it would be included among the angels. Whoever says that it is an angel said: The meaning of for fear of Him is fear of God, as stated by al-Tabari and others. Ibn Abbas said: The angels fear God, but not like the fear of the son of Adam. One of them does not know who is on his right and who is on his left. Neither food nor drink distracts them from the worship of God. And from him he said: Thunder is an angel who drives the clouds, and the water vapor is in the hollow of his thumb, and that he is entrusted with the clouds, directing them where he is commanded, and that he glorifies God. So when the thunder glorifies, there is no angel in the heaven who does not raise his voice in glorification, and then the rain descends. And from him also, when he heard the sound of thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him to Whom it glorifies. Malik narrated on the authority of Aamir ibn Abdullah on the authority of his father that whenever he heard the sound of thunder he would say: Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and so do the angels for fear of Him. Then he would say: This is a severe threat to the people of the earth. It was said that it was an angel sitting on a throne between the heaven and the earth, and on his right were seventy thousand angels, and on his left the same number. So if he turned to his right and glorified God, they all glorified God for fear of God, and if he turned to his left and glorified God, they all glorified God for fear of God. And He sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills. Al-Mawardi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ali ibn Abi Talib and Mujahid: “It was revealed about a Jew who said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell me! What is your Lord made of? Pearls or rubies? So a thunderbolt came and burned him.” It was said: “It was revealed about some of the infidel Arabs. Al-Hasan said: There was a man from the tyrants of the Arabs. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a group of people to call him to God, His Messenger, and Islam. He said to them: Tell me about the Lord of Muhammad, what is He, and from whom is He? Is He silver, iron, or copper? The people thought his words were too great, so he said: Should I answer Muhammad to a Lord whom he does not know? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to him repeatedly, saying the same thing. While the group were arguing with him and calling him, a cloud rose and was above their heads, so it thundered and flashed and threw a thunderbolt, burning the infidel and them. They returned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and some of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met them and said: Your companion was burned. They said: How did you know? They said: God revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And He sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills.” Al-Tha’labi mentioned it on the authority of Al-Hasan, and Al-Qushayri with a similar meaning on the authority of Anas, and it will come. It was said: “The verse was revealed about Arbad bin Rabi’ah, the brother of Labid bin Rabi’ah, and about Aamer bin At-Tufayl. Ibn Abbas said: Aamer bin At-Tufayl and Arbad bin Rabi’ah, the two Aamers, came towards the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was sitting in the mosque with a group of his companions. They entered the mosque, and the people were amazed at the beauty of Aamer, who was one-eyed and one of the most handsome people. A man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Messenger of God, this is Aamer bin At-Tufayl coming towards you. He said: Leave him, for God wills good for him, He will guide him. So he came until he stood over him and said: O Muhammad, what will I have if I become Muslim? He said: You have what the Muslims have and you are responsible for what the Muslims are responsible for. Will you make me the ruler after you? He said: That is not up to me, it is up to God to make it as He wills. He said: Will you make me on the land and you on the dirt? He said: No. He said: What will you make for me? He said: I will make you the reins of the horses so that you may fight in the way of God. He said: Do I not have the reins of the horses today? Come with me so that I may talk to you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood with him, and Aamer He motioned to Arbad: If you see me talking to him, then go behind him and strike him with the sword. So he began to argue with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to argue with him. Arbad drew a span of his sword, then God detained him, and he was unable to draw it, and his hand on his sword dried up. God sent a thunderbolt upon him on a summer day, and he cried out and burned him. Amer turned and fled, saying: O Muhammad! I called upon your Lord against Arbad until I killed him, and by God I will fill it against you with bare horses and beardless youths, so he, peace be upon him, said: May God and the sons of Qaylah prevent you from that, meaning the Aws and Khazraj, so Amer went down to the house of a Saluli woman, and in the morning he was saying: By God, if Muhammad and his companion - meaning the Angel of Death - come to me in the morning, I will pierce them with my spear, so God sent an angel who slapped him with his wings and scattered him in the dust, and a great wound came out of his knee at that time, so he returned to the house of the Saluli woman saying: A wound like a camel’s wound, and death in the house of the Saluli woman, then he rode on his horse and died on its back. Labid bin Rabi’ah mourned his brother Arbad and said: Oh eye, why did you not cry for Arbad when we and our opponents rose up in grief? I fear death for Arbad, but I do not fear the star of the fish or the lion Thunder and lightning struck me with the Persians on the day of the great battle of Najd And he said in it: There is no greater calamity than the loss of a brother, like the light of a star. Oh, the generous and kind Arbad, its ancestors singled me out, so I walk with a horn that is angry Labid converted to Islam after that, may God be pleased with him. Question: Narrated Abaan from Anas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not be struck by lightning while remembering God the Almighty.” And Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him said: Whenever the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard the sound of thunder, he would say: Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and so do the angels out of fear of Him, and He is over all things competent. If a thunderbolt strikes him, then I am responsible for his blood money. Al-Khatib mentioned from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas from his father from his grandfather who said: As when we were with Umar on a journey, thunder and hail struck us, so Ka’b said to us: Whoever says when he hears thunder: ‘Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise, and the angels out of fear of Him,’ three times, will be spared from what happens in that thunder. So we did that and were spared. Then I met Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and a cloak had struck his nose and left a mark on it, so I said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is this? He said: A cloak hit my nose and left a mark, so I said: When Ka'b heard the thunder, he said to us: Whoever says when he hears the thunder: Glory be to Him whom the thunder glorifies with His praise and the angels out of fear of Him, three times, will be spared from what happens in that thunder. So we said it and were spared. Then Umar said: Why didn't you tell us so that we could say it? This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. God the Almighty said: And they dispute about God meaning the argument of the Jew when he asked about God the Almighty: What is He made of? Mujahid said it. Ibn Jurayj said: Arbad's argument was about what he intended to do to kill the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is possible that and they dispute about God is a state, or it is possible that it is disconnected. Anas narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent to a great polytheist to call him to God the Almighty, so he said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell me about this god of yours! Is it made of silver, gold, or copper? He found that very difficult, so he returned to him and informed him, so he said: Go back to him and call upon Him. He returned to him and a thunderbolt had struck him, and he returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the following had been revealed: And they dispute about God. And He is severe in penalty. Ibn al-A'rabi said: The penalty is deceit, and deceit from God the Almighty is planning with truth. Copper: Deceit from God is bringing harm to the one who deserves it without him realizing it. Ibn Al-Yazidi narrated on the authority of Abu Zaid He is very severe in punishment, meaning vengeance. Al-Azhari said: Al-Mahal means strength and severity. Al-Mahal is severity, the meem is original, and I did not solve someone’s problem, meaning I forced him until it became clear which of us was more severe. Abu Ubaid said: Al-Mahal is punishment and misfortune. Ibn Arafa said: Al-Mahal is argument, it is said: He did not solve his matter, meaning he argued. Al-Qutaybi said: meaning very scheming, and its origin is from trickery, making its meem like the meem of place, and its origin is from the word kawn, then it is said: I was tamkanat. Al-Azhari said: Ibn Qutaybah made a mistake by saying that the meem in it is extra, rather it is original, and if you see a letter on the example of Fa’al that begins with a broken meem, then it is original, like: Mahad, Malaak, Muras, and other letters. And Mufa`il if it is from the daughters of the three, then it comes with the appearance of the waw like: Mizwad, Muhawwal, and Mahwar, and other letters. He said: Al-A`raj read - and He is very strong in difficulty with the opening of the meem, and its interpretation came on this reading from Ibn Abbas that it is the year. Abu Ubaid Al-Harawi mentioned all of this, except what we mentioned first from Ibn Al-A`rabi, and the sayings of the Companions and Followers with its meaning, and they are eight: The first: very strong in enmity, said by Ibn Abbas. The second: very strong in year, said by Ibn Abbas also. The third: very strong in taking, said by Ali bin Abi Talib. The fourth: very strong in hatred, said by Ibn Abbas. The fifth: very strong in strength, said by Mujahid. The sixth: very strong in anger, said by Wahb bin Munabbih. The seventh: very strong in destruction by the place, which is drought, said by Al-Hasan also. The eighth: very strong in trickery, said by Qatadah. Abu Ubaidah Muammar said: The place and the struggle are deceit and overpowering, and he recited for Al-A`sha: A branch of a spring shakes in the branch of glory, abundant in dew and very difficult Another said: He was confused among people, and everyone had their own problems and difficulties prepared for him. Abdul Muttalib said: Don't worry, if a person is prevented from traveling, then prevent your lawful money. Their cross will not defeat them, nor will they be defeated by their enemy, your enemies.
13:14: The Almighty said: His is the call of truth meaning, to God is the call of truth. Ibn Abbas, Qatadah and others said: There is no god but God. Al-Hasan said: God is the Truth, so His call is the call of truth. It was said: Sincerity in supplication is the call of truth, as some of the later scholars said. It was said: The call of truth is his supplication at times of fear, for no one is called upon except Him in it, as He said: Wandered are those you call upon other than Him (al-Isra’ 17:67). Al-Mawardi said: This is more similar to the context of the verse, because He said: And those they call upon besides Him meaning idols and statues. They do not respond to them at all meaning, they do not respond to their call, nor do they hear their call. Except like one who extends his hands toward water to reach his mouth, but he will not reach it God the Almighty used water as an example to show their despair of having their supplication answered, because the Arabs use the example of someone who strives for something he cannot attain as holding water in his hand. He said: So, in the love that was between us, I became like someone holding water in his hand. There are three meanings to this proverb: The first is that the one who calls upon a god other than God is like a thirsty man who calls upon water to his mouth from afar, wanting to take it but is unable to do so with his tongue, and he points to it with his hand, but it never comes to him, because the water does not respond and the water will not reach him, as stated by Mujahid. The second is that he is like a thirsty man who sees his shadow in the water and has extended his hand into it to reach his mouth, but it will not reach him, because his assumption is false and his imagination is corrupt, as stated by Ibn Abbas. The third is that he is like someone who extends his hand to the water to grasp it, but nothing of it freezes in his hand. Al-Farra’ claimed that what is meant by water here is the well, because it is a source of water, and that the proverb is like someone who extends his hand to the well without a bribe, and the evidence for this is the saying of the poet: The water is the water of my father and grandfather, and my well is the one I dug and the one I folded. Ali may God be pleased with him said: He is like a thirsty person on the edge of a well, he cannot reach the bottom of the well, nor does the water rise to him. The meaning of except as one who spreads out his hands is except like the response of one who spreads out his hands to the water. The source is added to the spreader, then the added particle is deleted, and the subject of the added source is intended in the meaning, which is water. The meaning is: except like the response of one who spreads out his hands to the water. The lam in his statement: so that it reaches his mouth is related to spreading, and his statement: and it will not reach it is a metaphor for the water, meaning the water will not reach his mouth. It is permissible for it to be a metaphor for the mouth, meaning the mouth will not reach the water. And the invocation of the disbelievers is only in error meaning the worship of idols by the disbelievers is only in error, because it is polytheism. It was said: Except in error, meaning that the supplication is lost to them, and they find no way to it, as He said: Where are those you used to call upon besides God? They said, ‘They have gone astray from us.’ (al-A’raf 7:37) Ibn Abbas said: meaning that the voices of the disbelievers are veiled from God, so He does not hear their supplication.
13:15: The Almighty said: And to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion. Al-Hasan, Qatada and others said: The believer prostrates willingly, and the disbeliever prostrates by compulsion with the sword. And from Qatada also: The disbeliever prostrates by compulsion when faith does not benefit him. Al-Zajjaj said: The prostration of the disbeliever by compulsion is what it contains of submission and the effect of craftsmanship. Ibn Zayd said: Willingly is the one who entered Islam willingly, and by compulsion is the one who entered it out of fear with the sword. It was said: Willingly is the one who has been a Muslim for a long time and has become accustomed to prostration, and by compulsion is the one who compels himself to God Almighty, so the verse is about the believers, and based on this the meaning of and the earth is some of those on the earth. Al-Qushayri said: There are two approaches to this verse: The first is that it is general and what is meant by it is specificity. The believer prostrates willingly, and some of the disbelievers prostrate under compulsion and fear, like the hypocrites. So the verse is applied to these people, as mentioned by Al-Farra. It was said according to this statement: The verse is about the believers, some of them prostrate willingly and prostration is not difficult for them, and some of them are difficult for them, because adhering to the obligation is hardship, but they bear the hardship out of sincerity and faith, until they become accustomed to the truth and are trained in it. The second approach - which is correct - is to apply the verse to generalization. Based on this, there are two paths: The first is that the believer prostrates willingly, while the disbeliever is commanded to prostrate and is held accountable for it. The second - and it is the truth - is that the believer prostrates with his body willingly, and every creature, believer and disbeliever, prostrates insofar as it is a creation, prostrating as a sign and need to the Creator. This is like His saying: There is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise (al-Isra’ 17:44), which is a glorification of signification, not a glorification of worship. And their shadows in the mornings and the evenings (al-Ra’d 13:15), meaning the shadows of creation prostrate to God Almighty in the mornings and the evenings, because they appear at these two times, and they incline from one side to the other, and that is God’s control of them as He wills. It is like His saying: Have they not seen what God has created of things? Their shadows turn to the right and the left, prostrating to God, and they are humbled? (Al-Nahl: 48), as Ibn Abbas and others said. Mujahid said: The shadow of the believer prostrates willingly and obediently, and the shadow of the disbeliever prostrates unwillingly and reluctantly. Ibn Al-Anbari said: He gives the shadows minds with which they prostrate and humble themselves, just as He gave the mountains understandings so that they may… I addressed and was addressed. Al-Qushayri said: There is a consideration in this, because the mountain is an eye, so it is possible for it to have a mind on condition that life is estimated, and as for shadows, they are effects and accidents, and it is not conceivable that life is estimated for them, and prostration means inclination, so the prostration of shadows is their inclination from side to side, it is said: the palm tree prostrated, meaning it leaned. And al-asal is the plural of origin, and origin is the plural of asil, and it is between the afternoon and sunset, then asa’il is the plural of plural, Abu Dhu’ayb al-Hudhali said: By my life, you are the home whose people are most honored, and I sit in its shade in the evenings. And their shadows may be conjoined with from and it may be raised by the beginning and the predicate is omitted, the estimate: and their shadows prostrated in the morning and the evenings and in the morning may be a source, and it may be the plural of morning, strengthening its being a plural by contrasting the plural which is the evenings with it.
13:16: The Almighty said: "Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?" God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to the polytheists: (Say: Who is the Lord of the heavens and the earth?) Then He commanded him to say to them: He is God, to oblige the argument if they did not say that and were ignorant of who He is. "Say: Have you taken besides Him protectors?" This indicates their admission that God is the Creator, otherwise there would be no meaning to the argument with His saying: "Say: Have you taken besides Him protectors?" The evidence for this is His saying: "And if you ask them who created the heavens and the earth, they will surely say: God." (al-Zumar 39:38) That is, if you admit it, then why do you worship other than Him?! And that other than Him neither benefits nor harms, and this is a correct obligation. Then He gave them an example and said: "Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal?" Likewise, the believer who sees the truth is not equal to the polytheist who does not see the truth. It was said: The blind man is like what they worshipped instead of God, and the seeing man is like God the Most High: Or are darkness and light equal? That is, polytheism and faith. Ibn Muhaysin, Abu Bakr, Al-A’mash, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read istawwa with a ya’ because the verb came before it, and because the feminine of darkness is not real. The rest read it with a ta’, and Abu Ubaid chose it. He said: Because there was no barrier between the feminine and the verb. Darkness and light are like faith and disbelief, and we do not know how that is. Or have they attributed to God partners who created like His creation so that the creation became indistinguishable to them? This is part of the proof, that is, He created other than God like His creation so that the creation became indistinguishable to them, so they do not know the creation of God from the creation of their gods. “Say: God is the Creator of all things.” That is, say to them, O Muhammad: God is the Creator of all things, so it is necessary for everything to worship Him. The verse is a response to the polytheists and the Qadarites who claimed that they were created as God created. And He is the One before everything. Al-Qahhar is the One who overcomes everything, who overcomes in His will every one who wills.
