Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: It is not far-fetched that the verse was revealed about those who do not acknowledge the Creator, i.e. ask them about the Creator of the heavens and the earth, for it is easy to establish the argument for Him against them, and it brings the matter close to necessity, for the inability of inanimate objects and every created being to create the heavens and the earth is known, and if this is established and it becomes clear that the Creator is God, then how is it permissible for a partner to transgress against Him?! And he explained during the speech that if the world had two makers, creation would be confused, and the action of this would not be distinguished from the action of that, so how do you know that the action is from two?!
13:17: The Almighty said: "He sends down water from the sky, and the valleys flow according to their capacity, and the torrent carries a swelling foam." He gave an example of truth and falsehood, and likened disbelief to the foam that rises above the water, for it disappears and sticks to the sides of the valleys, and the winds blow it away. So disbelief disappears and disappears, as we will explain. Mujahid said: And the valleys flow according to their capacity he said: according to how full they are. Ibn Jurayj said: according to how small or large they are. Al-Ashab Al-Uqaili and Al-Hasan read according to their capacity with a silent dal, and the meaning is the same. It was said: its meaning is according to what was decreed for them. And valleys is the plural of valley, and it was called a valley because of its emergence and flow, so the valley according to this is the name of running water. Abu Ali said: And the valleys flowed is an expansion, meaning its water flowed, so he deleted. He said: The meaning of according to their capacity is according to the amount of their water, because the valleys flowed according to their capacity. And the flood carried a rising foam meaning rising high above the water, and the speech was complete, as Mujahid said. Then he said: And from that which they kindle in the fire and it is the second example. Seeking adornment meaning adornment of gold and silver. Or goods of foam like it Mujahid said: Iron, copper, and lead. And his saying: Foam like it meaning foam rises above these things as the flood rises, and the flood only carried the foam because the water was mixed with the dirt of the earth so that it became foam, likewise what is kindled on the fire of jewels and gold and silver from what is dispersed in the earth of minerals has been mixed with dirt, so it is kindled on it so that it melts and the dirt of the earth separates from it. And his saying: “Thus does God present truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes as scum” Mujahid said: Solid. Abu Ubaidah said: Abu Umar ibn al-Ala’ said: The pot has become suffocated if it boils until its foam pours out, and if it solidifies at the bottom of it. Al-Jafa’ is what the valley threw away, i.e. it threw it. Abu Ubaidah narrated that he heard Ru’bah recite jafalan. Abu Ubaidah said: It is said that the pot threw up its foam, and the wind broke the clouds when it cut them. But that which benefits people remains on the earth. Mujahid said: It is pure, clear water. It was also said: Water and what is pure of gold, silver, iron, copper and lead. This is because God gave the two examples for the truth in its steadfastness, and falsehood in its decay. Falsehood, even if it rises in some cases, it decays like the decay of foam and impurity. It was also said: What is meant is the example that God gave for the Qur’an and what enters the hearts from it. He likened the Qur’an to rain for the generality of its goodness and the continuity of its benefit, and He likened the hearts to valleys, and the same amount of the Qur’an enters them as enters the valleys according to their width and narrowness. Ibn Abbas said: He sends down water from the sky He said: The Qur’an, And the valleys flow according to their capacity He said: The valleys are the hearts of the servants. The author of Souq Al-Arous said: If this interpretation is correct, then the meaning is that God, the Almighty, likened the Qur’an to water, and likened hearts to valleys, and likened the decisive to the pure, and likened the similar to foam. It was said: Foam is the features of the soul and the temptations of doubt that rise from where they are and are disturbed by the authority that swallows them, just as the water of a flood flows purely and raises whatever it finds in the valley, remaining. As for the adornment of gold and silver, it is like the noble conditions and the pure morals, by which men are beautiful and righteous deeds are established, just as gold and silver are the adornment of women, and by them things are valued. Hamid, Ibn Muhaisin, Yahya, Al-A’mash, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read yuqdunu with a ya’, and Abu Ubaid chose it, because of his saying: benefits people, so he informed, and there is no addressing here. The rest read with a ta’ because of his saying at the beginning of the speech: Have you taken protectors besides Him? the verse. And his saying: in the fire is related to something omitted, and it is in the position of a state, and the possessor of the state is the ha’ in upon it, the estimate is: and from what you kindle fixed in the fire or existing. And in his saying: in the fire there is a raised pronoun referring back to the ha’ which is the name of the possessor of the state, and it is not right for in the fire to be related to they kindle from the point of view that it is not right to kindle it in the fire, because the one who kindles it is in the fire, so his saying: in the fire becomes useless. And his saying: seeking adornment is an object for it. Foam like it is a subject and predicate, meaning foam like the foam of a torrent. And it was said: The predicate of foam is his saying: in the fire Al-Kisa’i: Foam is a subject, and like it is an attribute of it, and the predicate is in the sentence before it, which is from what they kindle. Thus does God present examples meaning just as He has shown you these examples, so He also presents them as clear proofs. The speech is complete.
13:18: Then he said: For those who responded to their Lord, meaning they answered, and responded means answered. He said: No one responded to him at that time. It has been presented, that is, he responded to what God called him to of monotheism and prophethood. The best because it is the ultimate in goodness. It has been said: Among the best is victory in this world, and eternal bliss tomorrow. And those who did not respond to him that is, did not respond to belief in him. If they had all that is in the earth that is, of wealth. And the like of it with it that they possess. They would ransom themselves with it from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. Similar to it in Al Imran 3:Indeed, those who disbelieve will never benefit them at all from God in the least (Al Imran 3:10), Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers - never will the earth full of gold be accepted from one of them, even if he were to ransom himself with it (Al Imran 3:91) as was explained there. Those will have an evil reckoning that is, no good deed will be accepted from them, and no bad deed will be overlooked. Farqad al-Sabkhi said that Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said to me: O Farqad! Do you know what an evil reckoning is? I said: No! He said: That a man is held accountable for all his sins, and nothing of them will be lost. And their abode means their dwelling and place of residence. Hell, and wretched is the resting place meaning the bed they have prepared for themselves.
13:19: The Almighty said: Is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind? This is a parable that God gave for the believer and the disbeliever. It was narrated that it was revealed about Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib, may God be pleased with him, and Abu Jahl, may God curse him. What is meant by blindness is blindness of the heart, and the one who is ignorant of religion is blind of heart. Only those with understanding will remember.
13:20: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: Those who fulfill the covenant of God This is a description of those with understanding, meaning that only those with understanding who fulfill their covenant with God will remember. Covenant is a name for the genus, meaning all of God’s covenants, which are His commands and prohibitions that He commanded His servants to follow, and these words include adhering to all obligations and avoiding all sins. His statement: And they do not break the covenant may mean the genus of covenants, meaning if they make a covenant in obedience to God, they do not break it. Qatada said: God preceded His servants in breaking the covenant and forbade it in twenty-some verses, and it may be that He refers to a specific covenant, which is what God took from His servants when He brought them forth from the loins of their father Adam. Al-Qaffal said: It is what is embedded in their minds of the evidence of monotheism and prophethood. Second: Abu Dawud and others narrated on the authority of Awf bin Malik who said: We were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, seven, eight, or nine, and he said: “Will you not pledge allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace?” We had recently pledged allegiance, so we said: We have already pledged allegiance to you, until he said it three times. So we stretched out our hands and pledged allegiance to him. Someone said: O Messenger of God, we have already pledged allegiance to you, so on what should we pledge allegiance to you? He said: That you worship God and do not thank Him for anything, and perform the five daily prayers, and listen and obey - and he whispered a word - Do not ask people for anything. He said: Some of those people would drop their whips and would not ask anyone to hand it to them. Ibn al-Arabi said: One of the greatest covenants in remembrance is not to ask anyone other than Him. Abu Hamza al-Khurasani was one of the great worshippers. He heard that some people pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, not to ask anyone for anything, the hadith. Abu Hamza said: O Lord! These people made a covenant with your Prophet when they saw him, and I covenant with you that I will not ask anyone anything. He said: A pilgrim went out from Syria intending to go to Mecca. While he was walking on the road at night, he was left behind by his companions for an excuse, then he followed them. While he was walking towards them, he fell into a well on the side of the road. When he reached the bottom, he said: I seek help, perhaps someone will hear me. Then he said: The one I made a covenant with sees me and hears me. By God, I did not utter a word to people. Then, he had not been there long when a group of people passed by that well. When they saw him on the side of the road, they said: This well should be blocked. Then they cut wood and set it up over the mouth of the well and covered it with dirt. When Abu Hamza saw that, he said: This is a disaster. Then he wanted to seek help from them, but he said: By God, I will never leave it. Then he came back to himself and said: Didn’t you make a covenant with me? So he remained silent and put his trust in God. Then he leaned against the bottom of the well, thinking about his situation. Suddenly, dirt fell on him and the wood was lifted off him. During that, he heard someone say: Give me your hand! He said: So I gave him my hand and he carried me all at once to the mouth of the well. I went out and did not see anyone. Then I heard someone saying: How did you see the fruit of trust in God? And he recited: My shyness towards you prevented me from revealing my love, but with your knowledge you made me independent of revealing it. I was gentle in my affair, so I showed my witness to my absent one, and gentleness is attained by gentleness. You appeared to me with knowledge, as if you were telling me of the unseen that you are in the palm of your hand. I see myself and I feel lonely because of my awe of you, so you comfort me with your kindness and compassion And you revive a lover who is dying in love, and you wonder how life is with death Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a man who made a covenant with God and found that he was faithful to it completely and perfectly, so follow his example, God willing, and you will be guided. Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: This man’s silence in this situation regarding trust in God, claiming that it is a means of helping himself, is not permissible. If he had understood the meaning of trust in God, he would have known that it does not contradict his calling for help in that situation, just as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not depart from trust in God by concealing his departure from Mecca, hiring a guide, keeping that matter a secret, hiding in the cave, and saying to Suraqa: Hide from us. Praiseworthy trust is not achieved by doing something forbidden, and keeping silent about this person in the well is forbidden for him. The explanation for that is that God the Almighty has created for man a tool with which to ward off harm and a tool with which to bring benefit. If he neglects it, claiming to trust, that is ignorance of trust and a rejection of the wisdom of humility, because trust is the heart’s reliance on God the Almighty, and it is not necessary to cut off the causes. If a person were to become hungry and not ask until he died, he would enter the Fire, as Sufyan al-Thawri and others have said, because it has shown the way to safety, so if he refrains from it, he helps himself. Abu al-Faraj said: And do not pay attention to the saying of Abu Hamza: Then a lion came and pulled me out, because if that is true, then something similar may happen by chance, and it may be a kindness from God the Almighty to the ignorant servant. It is not denied that God the Almighty was kind to him, but what is denied is his action, which is his acquisition, which is his helping himself, which is a trust of God the Almighty with him, and He has commanded him to protect it.
13:21: The Almighty's saying: And those who maintain what God has ordered to be maintained is apparent in maintaining family ties, and this is the opinion of Qatada and most of the commentators, and it also includes all acts of obedience. And fear their Lord It was said: in severing family ties. And it was said: in all acts of disobedience. And fear the evil of the reckoning. The evil of the reckoning is the investigation and discussion thereof, and whoever is discussed in the reckoning will be punished. Ibn Abbas and Saeed bin Jubair said: The meaning of They maintain what God has ordered is belief in all the books and all the messengers. Al-Hasan: It is maintaining the relationship with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And it is possible, fourthly: that they maintain faith with righteous deeds, And fear their Lord in what He has ordered them to maintain, And fear the evil of the reckoning in abandoning it, and the first opinion includes these opinions as we mentioned, and God is our guide.
13:22: The Almighty said: And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord. It was said: those who is a new sentence, because they are patient is past, so it cannot be linked to they fulfill. It was also said: It is from the description of what came before, and the description is permissible sometimes in the past tense, and sometimes in the future tense, because the meaning is whoever does such-and-such will have such-and-such. And since those who includes the condition, and the past tense in the condition is like the future tense, this is permissible. That is why He said: those who are patient, then He said: and those who are patient, then He linked it to it and said: and avert evil with good, Ibn Zayd said: They were patient in obeying God, and were patient in avoiding disobeying God. Ata' said: They were patient in calamities and misfortunes, accidents and misfortunes. Abu Imran al-Joni said: They were patient in their religion seeking the countenance of God. And they established prayer they performed it with its obligatory duties and humility at its appointed times. And spend from what We have provided for them, secretly and publicly, meaning the obligatory zakat, according to Ibn Abbas. This has been discussed in Surah Al-Baqarah and others. And they repel evil with good, meaning they repel bad deeds with righteous deeds, as Ibn Abbas said. Ibn Zayd: They repel evil with good. Saeed bin Jubayr: They repel evil with good. Ad-Dahhak: They repel obscenity with peace. Juwaybir: They repel injustice with forgiveness. Ibn Shajarah: They repel sin with repentance. Al-Qutbi: They repel the foolishness of the ignorant with patience, so foolishness is evil and patience is good. It was said: If they intend to do evil, they turn back from it and seek forgiveness. It was said: They repel polytheism with the testimony that there is no god but God. These are nine sayings, all of which have similar meanings, and the first includes them in general, and its counterpart. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds (Hud 11:114). And from this is his saying, peace be upon him, to Muadh: And follow up the bad with a good one, and it will erase it, and treat people with good character. The Almighty says: For them is the final home meaning the final home of the Hereafter, which is Paradise instead of Hellfire. And the home tomorrow will be two homes: Paradise for the obedient, and Hellfire for the disobedient. So when He mentioned the description of the obedient, their home will inevitably be Paradise. And it was said: He meant by the home the home of this world, meaning that they will have the reward for what they did of acts of obedience in this world.
13:23: The Almighty said: Gardens of Eden which they shall enter meaning they shall have Gardens of Eden, so -Gardens of Eden is a substitute for the Hereafter and it is possible that it is an explanation of -the Hereafter of the Home meaning they shall enter Gardens of Eden, because -the Hereafter of the Home is an event and Gardens of Eden is a specific particle, and the event is only explained by an event like it, so the deleted source is added to the object. It is possible that Gardens of Eden is the predicate of a deleted subject. And Gardens of Eden is the middle of Paradise and its reed, and its roof is the Throne of the Most Gracious, as stated by Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr Abdul Malik. And in Sahih Al-Bukhari: "If you ask God, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Gracious, and from it flow the rivers of Paradise." So it is possible that Gardens is like that, if it is correct, then that is the predicate. Abdullah bin Amr said: In Paradise there is a palace called Aden, surrounded by meadows and winds, in it there are a thousand doors, on each door there are five thousand inkwells, none shall enter it except a prophet, a friend, or a martyr. Aden is taken from the word ‘Aden’ in place if one resides in it, as will be explained in Surat Al-Kahf, God willing: And whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants It is permissible for it to be conjoined with those, meaning: Those and whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants, for them is the final home. It is permissible for it to be conjoined with the raised pronoun in: they enter it, and the connection is good because the accusative pronoun came between them. It is permissible for the meaning to be: They enter it and whoever is righteous among their fathers enters it, meaning whoever is righteous, they do not enter it by lineage. It is permissible for the position of who to be accusative on the basis of: They enter it with whoever is righteous among their fathers, even if he does not do the same deeds as them, God will join him with them as an honor to them. Ibn Abbas said: This righteousness is belief in God and the Messenger. If they had other acts of obedience along with belief, they would have entered it through their obedience, not as a secondary matter. Al-Qushayri said: There is a consideration in this, because belief is necessary, so the statement regarding the condition of righteous deeds is like the statement regarding the condition of faith. So it is more apparent that this righteousness is in the aggregate of deeds, and the meaning is: that the blessing will be completed for them tomorrow by making them gathered with their relatives in Paradise, even if each person enters it through his own deeds, but rather through the mercy of God the Most High. God Almighty says: And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, meaning with gifts and presents from God as an honor to them.
13:24: "Peace be upon you" means they say: Peace be upon you, so he implied the statement, meaning you have been saved from calamities and trials. It was said: It is a prayer for them to remain safe, and if they are safe, meaning may God keep you safe, so it is a report that means a prayer, and includes an acknowledgment of servitude. Because you have been patient means with your patience, so -ma with the verb means a source, and the ba in -ma is related to the meaning. (Peace be upon you) and it is permissible for it to be related to something omitted, meaning this honor is with your patience, meaning with the command and prohibition of God Almighty, said Saeed bin Jubair. It was said: With poverty in this world, said Abu Imran Al-Joni. It was said: For jihad in the way of God, as narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know who will be the first of God’s creation to enter Paradise? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: “The mujahideen who block the gaps and protect against hardships, and one of them dies while he has a need in himself that he cannot fulfill, so the angels come to them and enter upon them from every door, saying: ‘Peace be upon you for what you endured, and excellent is the final home.’” Muhammad bin Ibrahim said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would come to the graves of the martyrs at the beginning of each year and say: ‘Peace be upon you for what you endured, and excellent is the final home.’” Likewise Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman. Al-Bayhaqi mentioned it on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would come to the martyrs, and when he came to the place of the ravine, he would say: ‘Peace be upon you for what you endured, and excellent is the final home.’” Then Abu Bakr used to do it after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Umar used to do it after Abu Bakr, and Uthman used to do it after Umar. Al-Hasan al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, said: For what you endured on the authority of Fadl. The world. It was said: Because you were patient in adhering to obedience and avoiding disobedience. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said its meaning. Ibn Zayd: Because you were patient about what you love if you lose it. And it is possible seventhly: Because you were patient about following desires. And on the authority of Abdullah ibn Salam and Ali ibn al-Husayn, may God be pleased with them, that they said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a caller will call for the people of patience to stand, and some people will stand and it will be said to them: Go to Paradise. The angels will meet them and say: To where? They will say: To Paradise. They will say: Before the reckoning? They will say: Yes! They will say: Who are you? They will say: We are the people of patience. They will say: What was your patience? They will say: We were patient with ourselves in obeying God, and we were patient with ourselves in avoiding the disobedience of God, and we were patient with the trials and tribulations in the world. Ali ibn al-Husayn said: Then the angels will say to them: Enter Paradise, for excellent is the reward of the workers. And Ibn Salam said: Then the angels will say to them: (Peace be upon you for what you were patient). Then excellent is the final home meaning excellent is the final home in which you were, you did what led to what you are in, so the final home in this sense is a noun, and the home is the world. Abu Imran al-Joni said: Then excellent is the final home Paradise instead of Hell. And from him: Then excellent is the final home Paradise instead of the world.
13:25: The Almighty said: And those who break the covenant of God after ratifying it When He mentioned those who fulfill His covenant and continue to obey His command, and mentioned their wealth, He mentioned their opposite. Breaking the covenant: abandoning His command. It was said: neglecting their minds, so they do not contemplate with them to know God the Almighty. And sever what God has ordered to be joined meaning of the wombs. And belief in all the prophets. And they spread corruption on the earth meaning through disbelief and committing sins. For those is the curse meaning expulsion and banishment from mercy. And for them is the evil home meaning the evil destination, which is Hell. Saad bin Abi Waqqas said: By God, there is no god but Him! They are the Kharijites.
13:26: The Almighty says: God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it. When He mentioned the outcome of the believer and the outcome of the polytheist, He explained that He is the One Who expands provision and restricts it in this world, because it is a place of testing. Expanding provision for the disbeliever does not indicate His honor, and restricting it for some believers does not indicate their humiliation. And restricts means He restricts, and from it. And he whose provision is restricted (al-Talaq 65:7) meaning restricts. It was said: Restricts gives according to what is sufficient. And they rejoice in the life of this world meaning the polytheists of Mecca, they rejoiced in this world and did not know anything else, and they were ignorant of what is with God, and it is conjoined with and they spread corruption on the earth. In the verse there is an inversion, the meaning is: And those who break the covenant of God after its ratification and sever what God has ordered to be joined and spread corruption on the earth and rejoice in the life of this world. And the life of this world is not compared to the Hereafter meaning in its aspect. But the life of this world is nothing but enjoyment meaning enjoyment of goods, such as a bowl and a sugar bowl. Mujahid said: A small, fleeting thing, from the pleasures of the day when it rises, it must disappear. Ibn Abbas: He increased like the shepherd’s provisions. It was said: The pleasures of this worldly life are what is enjoyed from it. It was said: What is provided for the hereafter from piety and righteous deeds. And for them is the worst home then the beginning. God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it meaning He expands and restricts.
13:27: The Almighty said: And those who disbelieve say, 'Why was a sign not sent down to him from his Lord?' It is clear in several places that suggesting signs to the messengers is ignorance, after they saw a single sign that indicated the truth, and the one who said this was Abdullah bin Abi Umayya and his companions when they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for signs. Say, 'Indeed, God Almighty misguides whom He wills.' That is, just as He misguided you after He sent down signs and forbade you from using them as evidence, He will misguide you when others are sent down. And He guides to Himself whoever turns back. That is, whoever returns. The ha in to Him refers to the truth, or to Islam, or to God Almighty, on the assumption: And He guides to His religion and obedience whoever returns to Him with his heart. It was said: It refers to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
13:28: The Almighty said: Those who believe those is in the accusative case, because it is the object, meaning God guides those who believe. It was said that it is a substitute for His saying: whoever turns back, so it is also in the accusative case. And their hearts are reassured by the remembrance of God meaning they are calmed and comforted by the One and Only God, so they are reassured. He said: meaning their hearts are reassured constantly by the remembrance of God with their tongues, said Qatada. Mujahid, Qatada and others said: by the Qur'an. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: by His command. Muqatil: by His promise. Ibn Abbas: by swearing by His name, that you are reassured by the remembrance of His grace and favor, as you are reassured by the remembrance of His justice, vengeance and judgment. It was said: by the remembrance of God meaning they remember God and contemplate His signs, so they know the perfection of His power with insight. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of God hearts are reassured meaning the hearts of the believers. Ibn Abbas said: This is about the oath, so if his opponent swears by God, his heart is reassured. It was said: By the remembrance of God meaning by obeying God. It was said: By the reward of God. It was said: By the promise of God. Mujahid said: They are the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
13:29: The Almighty’s saying: Those who believe and do righteous deeds - for them is bliss. It is the subject and predicate. It was said that its meaning is bliss, so blessed is raised as a subject, and it is permissible for its position to be accusative on the assumption: He made for them bliss, and and a good return is conjoined to it in the two mentioned ways, so it is raised or accusative. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer on the authority of Amr bin Abi Yazid Al-Bakali on the authority of Utbah bin Abdul Salami who said: “A Bedouin came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about Paradise and mentioned the Pool. He said: Is there fruit in it? He said: Yes, a tree called Tuba. He said: O Messenger of God! Which tree of our land does it resemble? He said: It does not resemble any of the trees of your land. Have you been to Syria? There is a tree called Al-Jawza that grows on a stem and its top is spread out. He said: O Messenger of God! How great is its root! He said: If a young camel from your family were to set out, it would not reach its root until its collarbone would break from old age.” He mentioned the hadith, and we have written it in full in the chapters of Paradise in the book of At-Tadhkirah. Ibn Al-Mubarak said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Ash'ath, on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: In Paradise there is a tree called Tuba. God the Almighty says to it: Open for My servant whatever he wishes. So it opens for him a horse with its saddle, bridle and appearance as he wishes, and opens for a mount with its saddle, reins and appearance as he wishes, and for fine camels and clothes. Ibn Wahb mentioned from the hadith of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Abu Umamah Al-Bahili, who said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise, there is no house in it except that it has a branch of it, and no beautiful bird except that it is in it, and no fruit except that it is from it. It has been said that its root is in the palace of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Paradise, then its branches divide into the most sublime houses of Paradise, just as knowledge and faith spread from it to all the people of the world. Ibn Abbas said: Tuba for them means joy and delight for them. It was also narrated from him that Tuba is the name of Paradise in Ethiopian. Saeed bin Jubair said: Al-Rabi’ bin Anas: It is the garden in the language of India. Al-Qushayri said: If this is correct, then it is in agreement between the two languages. Qatada said: Tooba for them is good for them. Ikrimah: Blessings for them. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i: It is better for them, and it was also narrated from him: It is an honor from God for them. Ad-Dahhak: It is a blessing for them. An-Nahhas: These sayings are close, because Tooba is a noun from the root of good, meaning a good life for them, and these things go back to the good thing. Al-Zajjaj said: Tooba is a noun from the root of good, and it is the state that is pleasant for them, and the root is Tayyibi, so the Ya became a Waw because of its sukoon and the Damma of what precedes it, as they said: Mawser and Muwqin. I said: The correct view is that it is a tree, based on the hadith that we mentioned, and it is authentic according to what Al-Suhayli mentioned. Abu Omar mentioned it in Al-Tamhid, and we transmitted it from him. Al-Tha’labi also mentioned it in his interpretation, and Al-Mahdawi and Al-Qushayri also mentioned on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Qurrah on the authority of his father that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Tuba is a tree in Paradise that God planted with His hand and breathed into it of His spirit. It grows ornaments and fine garments, and its branches can be seen from beyond the wall of Paradise.” Whoever wants more information on these reports, let him read Al-Tha’labi. Ibn Abbas said: Tuba is a tree in Paradise, its root is in the house of Ali, and in the house of every believer there is a branch of it. Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Ali said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the words of God Almighty: Blessings for them and a good place of return. He said: A tree whose root is in my house and its branches are in Paradise. Then he was asked about it again and he said: A tree whose root is in the house of `Ali and its branches are in Paradise. So it was said to him: O Messenger of God! I was asked about it and I said: Its root is in my house and its branches are in Paradise. Then I was asked about it and I said: Its root is in the house of `Ali and its branches are in Paradise. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My house and the house of `Ali will be in Paradise tomorrow, one in one place. And from him, may God bless him and grant him peace: Its root is in my house and there is no house of yours but a branch of it hangs down in it. “And a good place of return” means to return. It was said: The meaning of the statement is those who believe and whose hearts are reassured by the remembrance of God and who do righteous deeds, blessed are they.”
13:30: The Almighty said: Thus have We sent you to a nation before which there have been nations. That is, We sent you as We sent the prophets before you, as Al-Hasan said. It was said: The favor bestowed upon the one to whom Muhammad, peace be upon him, was sent was likened to the favor bestowed upon the prophets before him. That you may recite to them that which We have revealed to you, meaning the Qur’an. And they disbelieve in the Most Gracious. Muqatil and Ibn Jurayj said: "It was revealed regarding the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah when they wanted to write the treaty document. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali: Write, 'In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.' Suhayl ibn Amr and the polytheists said: 'We do not know the Most Gracious except for the companion of Yamamah,' meaning Musaylimah the Liar. Write, 'In Your name, O God.' This is how the people of the Jahiliyyah used to write. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali: Write, 'This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed upon.' The polytheists of Quraysh said: 'If you were the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we fought you and turned you away, then we have wronged you. But write, 'This is what Muhammad ibn Abdullah has agreed upon.' The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: 'Let us fight them.' He said: 'No, but write what they want.' So it was revealed." Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed regarding the polytheists of Quraysh when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: 'Prostrate to the Most Gracious.' (al-Furqan 25:60). They said, 'And what is the Most Gracious?' So it was revealed: 'Say,' to them, O Muhammad: 'That which you have denied.' He is my Lord, there is no god but Him, and there is no god but Him. He is One in His essence, even if the names of His attributes differ. In Him I have relied, and I have believed and put my trust. And to Him is my return meaning my return tomorrow, and today also I have relied on Him and put my trust, content with His judgment and submitting to His command. It was said: Abu Jahl heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calling upon God in the Black Stone and saying: O God, O Most Merciful. He said: Muhammad used to forbid us from worshipping gods, but he was calling upon two gods. So this verse was revealed, and the following was revealed: “Say: Call upon God or call upon the Most Merciful” (al-Isra’ 17:110).
13:31: The Almighty’s saying: And if only a Qur’an with which the mountains could be moved This is connected to His saying: Why had not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord? (Ar-Ra’d: 27). “A group of the polytheists of Mecca, including Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Abi Umayya Al-Makhzoumi, sat behind the Kaaba, then they sent for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he came to them. Abdullah said to him: If you want us to follow you, then move the mountains of Mecca for us with the Qur’an, and remove them from us until they collapse, for it is a narrow land, and make for us springs and rivers in it, so that we may plant and cultivate. You are not, as you claimed, more insignificant to your Lord than David when He subjected the mountains to him to move with him, and subjected the wind to us so that we could ride it to the Levant to provide for our provisions and needs, then we would return the same day. The wind was subjected to Solomon, as you claimed, so you are not more insignificant to your Lord than Solomon, son of David. And revive for us Qusayy, your grandfather, or whomever you wish of our dead, so that we may ask him, is what you say true or false? For Jesus used to revive the dead, and I am not more insignificant to God than him. So God Almighty revealed: And if a Qur’an were to move the mountains the verse.” He said: Its meaning is Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam, Mujahid, Qatadah and Al-Dahhak, and the answer is omitted, meaning: This would have been the Qur’an, but it was omitted for brevity, because of what is apparent in the speech of the indication of it, as Imru’ Al-Qais said: If it were a soul, it would all be torn apart, but it is a soul that sheds souls. Meaning, it is easy for me, this is the meaning of Qatada’s statement, he said: If a Qur’an had done this before your Qur’an, your Qur’an would have done it. It was said: The answer came before, and there is an inversion in the speech, meaning, and they disbelieve in the Most Gracious, if We had sent down the Qur’an and done to them what they suggested. Al-Farra’: It is possible that the answer is if this were done to them, they would have disbelieved in the Most Gracious. Al-Zajjaj: And if We had sent down to them angels to His saying: the dead they would not have believed, and the implied answer here is what is made clear in His saying: And if We had sent down to them angels to His saying: They would not have believed unless God willed (Al-An’am 6:111). Rather, to God belongs the command entirely meaning, He is the owner of all matters, the doer of whatever He wills of them, so what you seek is not what is by the Qur’an, rather it is by the command of God. God Almighty said: Have not those who have believed despaired? Al-Farra’ said: Al-Kalbi said: Despaired means knows, in the language of the Nakha’, and Al-Qushayri narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, meaning have they not known? Al-Jawhari said it in Al-Sahah. It was said: It is the language of Hawazin, meaning did they not know, according to Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Al-Hasan. Abu Ubaidah said: Did they not know that they would find out? Abu Ubaidah recited in this regard for Malik bin Auf Al-Nasri: I say to them, by the people, when they make me happy, have you not despaired that I am the son of a knight who has asceticism? They make me easy in gambling, and it was mentioned in Al-Baqarah and it is narrated that they take me captive from captivity. Rabah bin Adi said: Have not the people despaired that I am his son, even though I am far from the land of the tribe? In the book of response, I am his son, and this is how Al-Ghaznawi mentioned it: Did he not know? The meaning according to this: Did not those who believed know that if God had willed, He would have guided all people without them seeing the signs? It was said: It is from the well-known despair, meaning did not those who believed despair of the belief of these infidels, because they knew that if God had willed to guide them, He would have guided them, because the believers wished for the revelation of the signs in the hope that the infidels would believe. Ali and Ibn Abbas read: Have not those who believed become clear from the statement. Al-Qushayri said: It was said to Ibn Abbas that it was written Have they not despaired He said: I think the writer wrote it while he was asleep, meaning he added some letters until it became despaired. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh that he recited: Have not those who believe made clear? And it was used as evidence by those who claimed that it was correct in recitation, and it is false on the authority of Ibn Abbas, because Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair narrated the wording on the authority of Ibn Abbas, as it is in the Mushaf with the recitation of Abu Amr and his narration on the authority of Mujahid and Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Then its meaning is: Have not it made clear? If what God meant under the wording with which they contradicted the consensus, then our recitation applies to it and comes with its interpretation. If God intended the other meaning in which despair is not from the path of knowledge, then it was omitted from what they mentioned. As for its omission, it invalidates the Qur’an and leads its companions to slander. If God willed an is a lightened form of the heavy form, meaning that if God willed He would have guided all mankind. This is a response to the Qadarites and others. The Almighty says: “And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by what they have done, a calamity will strike them suddenly because of their disbelief and their rebellion. It is said: “The calamity of a matter” if it befalls it, and the plural is calamities, and the root of calamity is strike. He said: My children were wasted and I did not collect the sticks of the cuckoos that beat the mouths of the pitchers. That is, the disbelievers will continue to be struck by a devastating calamity, such as a thunderbolt as struck Arbad, or by killing, captivity, drought, or other torments and affliction, as befell the mockers, who were the leaders of the polytheists. Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The calamity is the disaster. Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah also said: The calamity is the signs and mirages that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would send to them. Or it befalls meaning the calamity. Near their home said Qatadah and Al-Hasan. Ibn Abbas said: Or you befall near their home. It was said: The verse was revealed in Madinah, that is, the calamities will continue to befall them, descending in their courtyards or near them, such as the villages of Madinah and Makkah. Until the promise of God comes to pass in the conquest of Makkah, said Mujahid and Qatadah. It was said: It was revealed in Mecca, meaning that calamities will strike them, and you will leave them for Medina, O Muhammad, and you will be near their home, or you will besiege them, and this siege will be for the people of Taif, and for the fortresses of Khaybar, and God’s promise will come with permission for you to fight them and conquer them. Al-Hasan said: God’s promise on the Day of Resurrection.
13:32: The Almighty said: And messengers before you were mocked, but I granted respite to those who disbelieved; then I seized them. The meaning of mockery was presented in Al-Baqarah and the meaning of respite was presented in Al-Imran, meaning I mocked them and made them miserable, so I gave the disbelievers respite for a period of time so that whoever I knew would believe among them would believe would believe. Then when the judgment came, I seized them with punishment. How was My punishment? meaning how did you see what I did to them? So I will do the same to the polytheists of your people.
13:33: The Almighty’s saying: Is he who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned? This in charge is not the in charge which is the opposite of sitting, but rather it means taking charge of the affairs of creation, as one says: So-and-so has undertaken such-and-such work. He is in charge of every soul for what it has earned, meaning He enables it to earn, creates it, provides for it, protects it, and rewards it for its work. So the meaning is: He is a guardian who is not negligent, and the answer is omitted, and the meaning is: Is he who is a guardian who is not negligent like one who is negligent? It was said: Is he who is in charge meaning knowledgeable, as Al-A’mash said. The poet said: If it were not for the honorable men of Quraish, you would have stolen the clothes of the House, while God is standing. Any Knower, for God knows what every soul has earned. It was said: What is meant by that are the angels who are assigned to the children of Adam, according to Ad-Dahhak. They made is a state, meaning or they have made, or it is in apposition to mocking, meaning they mocked and made, meaning they named for God partners, meaning idols that they made gods. “Say: Name them”, meaning say to them, O Muhammad: Name them, meaning state their names, as a threat, meaning they only name: Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, Manat and Hubal. Or do you inform Him of what He does not know on earth? Or is a question of rebuke, meaning do you inform Him, and it is in fact in apposition to an earlier question in meaning, because His saying: Name them means: He inspired the names of the creators. Or do you inform Him of what He does not know on earth. It was said: The meaning is: Say to them: Do you inform God of an inward thing that He does not know? Or of an outward statement that He knows? If they say: With an inner meaning that He does not know, they have deviated. If they say: With an outer meaning that He knows, then say to them: Name them. If they name them Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, then say to them: God does not know of a partner for Himself. It was said: Or do you inform Him of what He does not know? That is, you are calling upon a partner for God, and God does not know of a partner for Himself. So do you inform Him of a partner for Him on the earth that He does not know? He specifically denied the partner for the earth, even though He has no partner other than the earth, because they claimed that He had partners for Him on the earth. The meaning of: Or with an outer meaning of the statement is that which God revealed to His prophets. Qatada said: Its meaning is with a false statement, and from this is the saying of the poet: She lent us her milk and meat, and that is shameful, O son of Rayta. Any falsehood. Ad-Dahhak said: By a lie in speech. Fifthly, it is possible that the apparent meaning of the speech is an argument that they show by their speech, and the meaning of the speech is: Do you inform him of that while witnessing it, or do you say it while arguing? Rather, their plotting has been made attractive to those who disbelieve meaning leave this! Rather, their plotting has been made attractive to those who disbelieve. It was said: It is a correction in this way, meaning that God has no partner, but He has made their plotting attractive to those who disbelieve. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid read: Rather, their plotting has been made attractive to those who disbelieve as the name of the subject, and according to the reading of the group, the one who made their plotting attractive to the disbelievers is God, and it was said: Satan. It is permissible to call disbelief a plot, because their plotting against the Messenger was disbelief. And they turned away from the path meaning God turned them away, and this is the reading of Hamza and Al-Kisa’i. The rest with the fat-ha, meaning they turned others away, and Abu Hatim chose it, considering his saying: And they turn away from the way of God (al-Anfal 8:47) and his saying: They are the ones who disbelieved and turned you away from the Sacred Mosque (al-Fath 48:25). The damma reading is also good in Zain and Sadawa because it is known that God is the doer of that in the doctrine of the people of the Sunnah, so it establishes the destiny, and it is the choice of Abu Ubaid. Yahya bin Waththab and Alqamah read - and they turned away with the kasra of the sad, and likewise. This is our merchandise returned to us (Yusuf 12:65) with the kasra of the ra’ also for what its doer is not named, and its original form is Sadawa and Raddat, but when the first dal was assimilated into the second, its vowel was transferred to what preceded it, so it was kasra. And whomever God leaves astray by abandoning him. For him there is no guide meaning successful, and in this is confirmation of the reading of the Kufians and those who followed them, for his saying: And whomever God leaves astray, so likewise his saying: and they turned away. Most of the readers stop on the dal without the ya’, and the same applies to wal and waq, because you say about a man: this is a judge, a guardian, and a huwadi, so the ya’ is deleted because it is sukoon and meets with the tanween. And ma lahu min hadi, wali and waqi are read with the ya’, and this is according to the language of those who say: this is a da’i, wali, and waqi with the ya’, because the ya’ is deleted in the connected state because it meets with the tanween, and we have secured this in the pause, so the ya’ is restored and it becomes hadi, wali, and waqi. Al-Khalil said about calling a judge: O judge, by confirming the ya’, because there is no tanween with the calling, just as there is no tanween in the words da’i and muta’ali.
13:34: The Almighty says: For them is a punishment in the life of this world meaning for the polytheists who pervert, by killing, captivity, imprisonment, and other ailments and calamities. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe meaning more severe, than saying: It is difficult for me to do so. “And they will have no protector from God” meaning no one who can prevent them from His punishment or repel them. The word min is redundant.
13:35: The Almighty said: The example of Paradise which the righteous are promised. Grammarians differed about raising like. Sibawayh said: It is raised by the beginning and the predicate is omitted, and the estimate is: And in what is recited to you is the example of Paradise. Al-Khalil said: It is raised by the subject and its predicate underneath which rivers flow meaning the description of the Paradise that the righteous are promised, under which rivers flow, like your saying: Say Zaid stands, so my saying is the subject and Zaid stands is its predicate, and the example in the sense of the description is present, God Almighty said: That is their example in the Torah and their example in the Gospel (al-Fath 48:29) and He said: And to God belongs the highest example (Al-Nahl: 60), meaning the highest description, and Abu Ali denied it and said: The example has not been heard in the sense of the description, rather its meaning is resemblance, do you not see it running its course in its places and its interactions, like their saying: I passed by a man like you, as you say: I passed by a man who resembles you, he said: It is also corrupted from the meaning, because if the example has the meaning of a description, the meaning of the statement is: the description of the Paradise in which there are rivers, and that is not correct, because the rivers are in Paradise itself and not its description. Al-Zajjaj said: God the Almighty likened to us what is hidden from us with what we see, and the meaning is: Like Paradise is a Paradise with rivers flowing beneath it. Abu Ali denied this and said: The likeness, according to his statement, is either an attribute or a resemblance, and in both cases what he said is not correct, because if it means an attribute, it is not correct, because if you say: The attribute of Paradise is Paradise, then you make Paradise a predicate, that is not correct, because Paradise cannot be an attribute. Likewise, likening Paradise to Paradise, do you not see that the resemblance is an expression of the similarity between similar things, and it is an event, and Paradise is not an event, so the first cannot be the second. Al-Farra’ said: The likeness is inserted for emphasis, and the meaning is: The Paradise that the righteous have been promised has rivers flowing beneath it, and the Arabs often do that with likenesses, like His statement: There is nothing like Him (al-Shura 42:11), meaning He is not like anything. It was said that the meaning is: The attribute of Paradise that the righteous have been promised in beauty, blessings, and eternity is like the likeness of Hell in torment, severity, and eternity, as Muqatil said. Its fruit is continuous does not stop. In the hadith: If you take a fruit, another will take its place. We have explained this in At-Tadhkirah. And its shade means and its shade is like that, so it was deleted, meaning its fruit does not stop, and its shade does not disappear. This is a response to the Jahmites in their claim that the pleasures of Paradise disappear and perish. That is the consequence of those who feared God, and the consequence of the disbelievers is the Fire meaning the consequence of the affair of the deniers and their end is the Fire, they will enter it.
13:36: The Almighty said: And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you. That is, some of those who were given the Scripture rejoice in the Qur'an, such as Ibn Salam and Salman, and those who came from Abyssinia. The wording is general, but what is meant is specific. Qatada said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who rejoice in the light of the Qur'an. This was also said by Mujahid and Ibn Zayd. Mujahid also said that they are the believers among the People of the Book. It was said: They are a group of the People of the Book from among the Jews and Christians who rejoice in the revelation of the Qur'an because it confirms their books. Most scholars said: The mention of the Most Gracious in the Qur’an was little when it was first revealed. When Abdullah bin Salam and his companions converted to Islam, they were upset by the little mention of the Most Gracious in the Qur’an, despite the frequent mention of Him in the Torah. They asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about that, and God Almighty revealed: “Say, ‘Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious. Whichever you call upon, He has the best names.’” (al-Isra’ 17:110). Quraysh said: What is wrong with Muhammad who calls upon one God, but today he calls upon two gods, God and the Most Gracious? By God, we do not know the Most Gracious except the Most Gracious of Yamamah, meaning Musaylimah the Liar. So the following was revealed: And they are disbelievers in the mention of the Most Gracious. (Al-Anbiya’: 36) and And they disbelieve in the Most Gracious. (al-Ra’d 13:30). The believers among the People of the Book rejoiced at the mention of the Most Gracious, so God Almighty revealed: And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you. “And of the parties” means the polytheists of Mecca, and those who did not believe from among the Jews, Christians, and Zoroastrians. It was said that they were the Arabs who formed parties against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: Among the enemies of the Muslims are those who deny some of what is in the Qur’an, because among them are those who acknowledged some of the prophets, and among them are those who acknowledged that God is the Creator of the heavens and the earth. Say, ‘I have only been commanded to worship God and not to associate anything with Him.’ The group read it in the accusative case in apposition to I worship. Abu Khalid read it in the nominative case as a resumption, meaning I single Him out for worship alone, with no partner for Him, and I disavow the polytheists, and whoever said: The Messiah is the son of God and Ezra is the son of God, and whoever believed in likening like the Jews. To Him I invite, meaning I invite people to His worship. And to Him is my return meaning I return in all my affairs.
13:37: The Almighty said: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic judgment. That is, just as We sent down the Qur'an to you, and some of the parties denied it, so too have We sent it down as an Arabic judgment. He described it thus because He sent it down to Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, who was an Arab, so the parties denied this judgment as well. It was said that the structure of the verse is: And just as We sent down the Books to the Messengers in their languages, so too have We sent down to you the Qur'an as an Arabic judgment, meaning in the tongue of the Arabs. And by the judgment, He means the judgments in it. And it was said: He meant by the Arabic judgment the entire Qur'an, because it distinguishes between right and wrong and rules. And if you follow their desires that is, the desires of the polytheists in worshipping other than God, and in directing to other than the Kaaba. After what has come to you of knowledge, you will have no protector against God that is, a helper to support you. And no protector to prevent you from His punishment, and the address is to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and what is meant is the nation.
13:38: There are two issues: First: It was said: The Jews criticized the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for his wives, and they expressed this by saying: We do not see this man’s concern except for women and marriage, and if he were a prophet, the matter of prophethood would have occupied him from women. So God revealed this verse, and reminded them of the matter of David and Solomon, and said: And We had certainly sent messengers before you and made for them wives and offspring. That is, We made them human beings who fulfilled what God had permitted of worldly desires, and the specification is in the revelation. Second: This verse indicates the encouragement and urging of marriage, and forbids celibacy, which is the abandonment of marriage. This is the Sunnah of the Messengers, as stated in this verse, and the Sunnah has been transmitted with its meaning. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Marry, for I will be proud of your great numbers before the nations. This was mentioned previously in Al Imran and he said: Whoever marries has completed half of his religion, so let him fear God in the second half. The meaning of this is that marriage keeps one from adultery, and chastity is one of the two characteristics for which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) guaranteed Paradise, as he said: Whoever God protects from the evil of two things will enter Paradise between his jaws and between his legs. This was reported by Al Muwatta’ and others. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Anas, he said: “Three men came to the houses of the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking about the worship of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When they were informed, they seemed to be ashamed: Where are we in comparison to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? God has forgiven him his past and future sins. One of them said: As for me, I will pray all night long. Another said: I will fast all the time and never break my fast. Another said: I will stay away from women and never marry. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them and said: You are the ones who said such and such. By God, I am the one who fears God the most and is most pious towards Him, but I fast and break my fast, pray and sleep, and marry women. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me.” Muslim narrated it with the same meaning, and this is clearer. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, he said: Uthman wanted to be a celibate person, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade him. If he had permitted him to do so, we would have been singled out. The urging of seeking children and the refutation of those who are ignorant of that have already been mentioned in Al Imran. It was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he used to say: I marry a woman even though I have no need for her, and I have intercourse with her even though I do not desire her. It was said to him: What makes you do that, O Commander of the Faithful? He said: “I love that God will bring forth from me someone with whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, will outnumber the other prophets on the Day of Resurrection. I heard him say: ‘You should marry virgins, for they have sweeter mouths, better character, and have more pure wombs, and I will outnumber the nations with you on the Day of Resurrection.’” He meant by his saying: more pure wombs those who are more likely to give birth. A woman who has many children is called a natiq, because she is known to give birth. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Muqal bin Yasar that he said: “A man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘I have found a woman who is beautiful and lovely, but she does not give birth. Should I marry her?’ He said: ‘No.’ Then he came to him a second time and he forbade him. Then he came to him a third time and he said: ‘Marry the fertile and loving woman, for I will outnumber the nations with you.’” It was authenticated by Abu Muhammad Abdul Haqq, and that is enough for you. God the Almighty says: And it is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by God’s permission. The speech returns to the signs they proposed - what was mentioned previously in the Surah - so God revealed that about them. The apparent meaning of the speech is prohibition, but its meaning is negation, because no one is prohibited from doing what he is not able to do. For every term is a book meaning for every matter that God has decreed there is a book with God, as Al-Hasan said. It was said: There is an advancement and a delay in it, meaning: for every book there is a term, as Al-Farra’ and Ad-Dahhak said, meaning for every matter that God has written there is a specific term and a known time, similar to it. For every report there is a fixed time (al-An’am 6:67), it was made clear that what is meant is not the suggestion of the nations in the descent of the punishment, but rather for every term there is a book. It was said: The meaning is for every period there is a written book and a predestined matter that the angels do not know. At-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim mentioned in Nawad Al-Usul on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: When Moses, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, ascended Mount Sinai, the Almighty saw a ring on his finger, so he said: O Moses, what is this? And He knows best about it. He said: It is one of the men’s jewelry. He said: Is there any of my names or words written on it? He said: No. He said: Then write on it For every term there is a book.
13:39: The Almighty says: God blots out what He wills and confirms. That is, He blots out from that book whatever He wills to inflict on its people and brings it. And confirms whatever He wills, that is, He delays it until its time. It is said: I erased the book, meaning I removed its trace. And confirms that is, He confirms it, like His statement: And the men and women who remember God often (Al-Azab: 35), that is, the women who remember God. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Asim read and establishes with a light pronunciation, while the rest stressed it. This is in the reading of Abu Abbas, and the choice of Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid due to the large number of those who read it with it, because of His statement: God confirms those who believe (Ibrahim 14:27). Ibn Umar said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: God erases whatever He wills and establishes, except for happiness, misery and death. Ibn Abbas said: God erases whatever He wills and establishes, except for a few things: creation and creation, life span, provision, happiness and misery. It was narrated from him: They are two books other than the Mother of the Book, God erases from them whatever He wills and establishes. And with Him is the Mother of the Book in which nothing changes. Al-Qushayri said: It was said that happiness and misery, creation and provision do not change, so the verse is about other than these things, and in this statement there is a kind of arbitrariness. I said: Such a thing is not understood by opinion and effort, but rather it is taken by revelation. If it is correct, then it is obligatory to say it and stop at it. Otherwise, the verse is general in all things, and this is the most apparent, and God knows best. This meaning is narrated from Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him, Ibn Masoud, Abu Wa’il, Ka’b Al-Ahbar, and others, and it is the saying of Al-Kalbi. Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi reported that Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him used to circumambulate the House while crying and saying: O God, if You have written me among the people of happiness, then confirm me among them. If You have written me among the people of misery and sin, then erase me and confirm me among the people of happiness and forgiveness, for You erase what You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book. Ibn Masoud said: O God, if You have written me among the happy, then confirm me among them. If You have written me among the wretched, then erase me from the wretched and write me among the happy, for You erase what You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book. Abu Wa'il used to supplicate frequently: "O God, if You have written us as miserable, then erase it and write us as happy, and if You have written us as happy, then confirm us, for You erase whatever You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book." Ka'b said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: If there were no verse in the Book of God, I would have informed you of what will happen until the Day of Resurrection. God erases whatever He wills and confirms, and with You is the Mother of the Book. Malik ibn Dinar said about the woman for whom he supplicated: O God, if there is a girl in her womb, then replace her with a boy, for You erase whatever You will and confirm, and with You is the Mother of the Book. It was mentioned earlier in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: "I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: 'Whoever is pleased for his provision to be expanded and his life to be extended, let him maintain the ties of kinship.'" Anas ibn Maal said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever loves, so he mentioned it in the same wording, and there are two interpretations for it: One of them is semantic, which is what remains after him of beautiful praise and good mention, and repeated reward, so it is as if he did not die. The other: He delays his lifespan, which is written in the Preserved Tablet, and which is in the knowledge of God is fixed and cannot be changed, as He said: God blots out what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. It was said to Ibn Abbas when he narrated the authentic hadith on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever loves that God should extend his lifespan and expand his provision, let him fear God and maintain the ties of kinship. How can his lifespan and lifespan be increased? He said: God, the Almighty, said: It is He who created you from clay and then decreed a term, and a specified term is with Him. (Al-An`am: 2) The first term is the term of the servant from the time of his birth until the time of his death, and the second term - meaning the one appointed by him - is from the time of his death until the day he meets him in the intermediate realm, which none knows except God. So if the servant fears his Lord and maintains kinship ties, God will increase his first term of life for the intermediate realm as much as He wills. And if he disobeys and severs kinship ties, God will decrease his life in this world as much as He wills, so He will increase his term in the intermediate realm. So if the term is determined in His foreknowledge, then increase and decrease are forbidden, due to the statement of God the Most High: And when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it (Yunus 10:61). So the report and the verse agree, and this is an increase in the lifespan itself and the term itself according to the apparent meaning of the wording, according to the choice of the scholar of the nation, and God knows best. And Mujahid said: God decides the matter of the year in Ramadan, so He erases what He wills and confirms what He wills, except for life and death, misery and happiness, and the statement about this has already been made. Ad-Dahhak said: God erases whatever He wills from the register of the recorders that which contains neither reward nor punishment, and confirms what contains reward and punishment. Abu Salih narrated its meaning from Ibn Abbas. Al-Kalbi said: He erases from the provision and increases it, and He erases from the life span and increases it. He narrated it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then Al-Kalbi was asked about this verse and he said: He writes down all the speech, until on Thursday, everything that does not contain reward or punishment is removed from it, such as your saying: I ate and drank and entered and exited and the like, and it is true, and He confirms what contains reward and punishment. Qatada, Ibn Zayd, and Saeed bin Jubair said: God blots out whatever He wills of the obligatory and voluntary acts, abrogates and replaces them, and confirms whatever He wills and does not abrogate them. The abrogating and abrogated verses are with Him in the Mother of the Book. An-Nahhas and Al-Mahdawi mentioned something similar on the authority of Ibn Abbas. An-Nahhas said: Bakr bin Sahl told us, he said: Abu Salih told us, and on the authority of Muawiyah bin Salih, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, God blots out whatever He wills meaning: God replaces whatever He wills of the Qur’an and abrogates it, and confirms whatever He wills and does not replace it, and with Him is the Mother of the Book meaning: the sum of that is with Him in the Mother of the Book, the abrogating and abrogated. Saeed bin Jubair also said: He forgives whatever He wills - meaning - of the sins of His servants, and leaves whatever He wills and does not forgive it. Ikrimah said: He blots out whatever He wills - meaning by repentance - all sins and confirms in place of sins good deeds. God the Almighty said: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous work Al-Furqan 25:70 Al-Hasan said: God blots out whatever He wills of those whose time has come, and confirms of those whose time has not come. Al-Hasan said: He blots out the fathers and confirms the sons. It was also narrated from him: He forgets the guardians of sins and does not forget. Al-Suddi said: God blots out whatever He wills meaning the moon, and confirms meaning the sun, as explained by His statement: So We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible (al-Isra’ 17:12). Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: This is regarding souls during sleep, He takes them when sleeping, then if He wants their sudden death, He holds them, and whoever He wants to keep, He confirms them and returns them to their owner, as explained by His statement: God takes the souls at the time of their death (al-Zumar 39:42) the verse. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: God erases whatever He wills of the generations, as He says: Have they not seen how many generations We destroyed before them? (Ya-Sin 36:31) and He confirms whatever He wills of them, as He says: Then We brought forth after them another generation (al-Mu’minun 23:31). So He erases a generation and confirms another generation. It was said: It is the man who works for a long time in obedience to God, then works in disobedience to God and dies in his misguidance, so he is the one who erases, and the one who confirms: The man who works in disobedience to God for a long time then repents, so God erases him from the register of bad deeds and confirms him in the register of good deeds. This was mentioned by Al-Tha’labi and Al-Mawardi on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It was said: God erases whatever He wills - meaning this world - and confirms the Hereafter. Qais ibn Abbad said about the tenth day of Rajab: It is the day on which God erases whatever He wills and confirms whatever He wills. It was previously reported from Mujahid that this will be in Ramadan. Ibn Abbas said: God has a Preserved Tablet, a journey of five hundred years, made of white pearl, with two covers of red ruby. God looks every day for three hundred and sixty times. He confirms what He wills and erases what He wills. Abu Darda narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Almighty, opens the Book in the three hours remaining of the night. He looks in the Book that no one else looks at, and He confirms what He wills and erases what He wills.” The belief is that there is no change in the decree of God. This erasure and confirmation are among the things that were previously decreed. It was previously mentioned that some decrees are inevitable and are confirmed, and some are averted by causes, and that is the erased. And God knows best. Al-Ghaznawi: I believe that what is in the Tablet is beyond the unseen due to the knowledge of some of the angels, so it is possible to change it, because it is impossible for creation to comprehend all of God’s knowledge, and what is in His knowledge of the estimation of things cannot be changed. And with Him is the Mother of the Book meaning the origin of what was written of terms and other things. It was said: The Mother of the Book is the Preserved Tablet that cannot be changed or altered. It was also said that change occurs in it. It was said: It only occurs in the other scriptures. Ibn Abbas was asked about the Mother of the Book, so he said: God knows what He is creating. And what He created, they do. So he said about His knowledge: Be a book, and there is no change in the knowledge of God. And from him it is the remembrance, and his evidence is the saying of God Almighty: And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance (al-Anbiya 21:105). And this goes back in meaning to the first, and it is the meaning of Ka’b’s saying. Ka’b Al-Ahbar said: The Mother of the Book is God Almighty’s knowledge of what He created and what He will create.
13:40: The Almighty says: And We only show you some of what ma is redundant, and the meaning is: And if We show you some of what We promise them, meaning of the punishment, because He says: For them is a punishment in the life of this world and His saying: And those who disbelieve will continue to be struck by what they have done meaning if We show you what We promised them or We take you in death, then upon you is only the notification so there is nothing upon you except the notification, meaning the notification, and upon Us is the reckoning meaning the reward and punishment. God the Almighty said: Have they not seen meaning the people of Mecca, that We come to the land meaning that We intend to visit it. We reduce it from its borders is disputed. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: We reduce it from its borders means the death of its scholars and righteous people. Al-Qushayri said: According to this, the borders are the nobles. Ibn al-A’rabi said: The border and the border are the noble man, but this statement is far-fetched, because the intended meaning of the verse is: We showed them the deficiency in their affairs, so that they may know that delaying the punishment from them is not due to inability, unless the statement of Ibn Abbas is interpreted to mean the death of the rabbis of the Jews and Christians. Mujahid also said, Qatadah and al-Hasan: It is what the Muslims are most likely to do from what is in the hands of the polytheists, and this was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and from him also it is the devastation of the land until the inhabited area is in one part of it, and from Mujahid: Its deficiency is its devastation and the death of its people. Waki’ ibn al-Jarrah mentioned on the authority of Talhah ibn Umair on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah regarding God the Almighty’s statement:
13:41: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? He said: The departure of its jurists and the best of its people. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: The statement of Ata' in interpreting the verse is very good, and the people of knowledge accepted it. I said: Al-Mahdawi narrated it on the authority of Mujahid and Ibn Umar, and this is the text of the first statement itself. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid, We reduce it from its edges he said: The death of the jurists and scholars, and it is known in the language that the edge is the noble part of everything, and this is contrary to what Abu Nasr Abdul Rahim bin Abdul Karim accepted from the statement of Ibn Abbas. Ikrimah and Al-Shaabi said: It is the decrease and the taking of souls. One of them said: If the earth were to decrease, your place would be too narrow for you. The other said: A place where you defecate would be too narrow for you. It was said: What is meant by it is the destruction of those nations that perished before Quraysh and the destruction of their land after them, and the meaning is: Did Quraysh not see the destruction of those before them, and the devastation of their land after them? Do they not fear that the same will happen to them? This was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas also that it is that the blessings of the earth, its fruits and its people were decreased. It was said: It was decreased by the injustice of its rulers. I said: This is correct in meaning, because injustice and oppression destroy the country, by killing its people and their expulsion from it, and the blessing is removed from the land, and God knows best.
