God Almighty says: And God judges, and there is no adjuster of His judgment. That is, no one can adjust His judgment by reducing or changing it. And He is swift in account. That is, in taking revenge on the disbelievers, and swift in rewarding the believer. It has been said: He does not require the sight of the heart or the contraction of the fingers in His account, as was explained previously in Al-Baqarah.
13:42: The Almighty says: And those before them plotted meaning before the polytheists of Mecca, they plotted against the messengers and conspired against them and disbelieved in them. But to God belongs all plotting meaning that He is the creator of the plotters, so He does not harm except with His permission. It was said: So to God belongs the best plotting, meaning He will reward them for it. He knows what every soul earns of good and evil, so He will reward for it. And He will know the disbelievers This is how Nafi', Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it. The rest: the disbelievers in the plural. It was said: He meant Abu Jahl. For whom is the final home meaning the final home of this world, reward and punishment, or for whom is the reward and punishment in the Hereafter, and this is a threat and a warning.
13:43: The Almighty said: And those who disbelieve say, 'You are not a messenger.' Qatada said: They are the polytheists of the Arabs, meaning you are not a prophet or a messenger, but you are just making up, meaning when he did not bring them what they suggested, they said that. Say, 'God is sufficient.' That is, say to them, O Muhammad: God is sufficient.' That is, God is sufficient as a witness between me and you regarding my truthfulness and your lies. And he who has knowledge of the Book. This is an argument against the polytheists of the Arabs because they used to refer to the People of the Book - those of them who believed - in the interpretations. It was said: Their testimony was decisive for the words of the opponents, and they were the believers of the People of the Book such as Abdullah bin Salam, Salman al-Farsi, Tamim al-Dari, al-Najashi and his companions. Qatada and Saeed bin Jubayr said. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam's nephew who said: When they wanted to kill Uthman, Abdullah bin Salam came and Uthman said to him: What brought you? He said: I have come to support you. He said: Go out to the people and drive them away from me, for going out is better for me than going inside. So Abdullah bin Salam went out to the people and said: O people! My name in the pre-Islamic era was so-and-so, but the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, named me Abdullah. And it was revealed in verses of the Book of God. It was revealed in: “And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness to the like of it, and he believed, while you were arrogant. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.” (al-Ahqaf 46:10) And it was revealed in: “Say: God is sufficient as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book.” The hadith. We have written it in full in the book of At-Tadhkirah. Abu Isa said about it: This is a good and strange hadith. His name in the pre-Islamic era was Hasin, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, named him Abdullah. Abu Bishr said: I said to Saeed bin Jubair: And whoever has knowledge of the Book? He said: He is Abdullah bin Salam. I said: How can it be Abdullah ibn Salam, while this Surah is Meccan and Ibn Salam only converted to Islam in Medina?! Al-Tha’labi mentioned this. Al-Qushayri said: Ibn Jubayr said: The Surah is Meccan and Ibn Salam converted to Islam in Medina after this Surah, so it is not permissible to attribute this verse to Ibn Salam, for the one with the knowledge of the Book is Gabriel, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: It is God, the Most High, and they used to recite And with Him is the knowledge of the Book and they would denounce those who said: It is Abdullah ibn Salam and Salman, because they see that the Surah is Meccan, and these people converted to Islam in Medina. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he recited: And with Him is the knowledge of the Book, although there is weakness in the narration. This was narrated by Sulayman ibn Arqam from Az-Zuhri from Salim from his father from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mahbub narrated from Ismail ibn Muhammad Al-Yamani that he recited it likewise - And with Him with a kasra on the meem and ‘ayn and the dal The knowledge of the Book with a damma on the ‘ayn and raising the Book. Abdullah bin Ata said: I said to Abu Jaafar bin Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them, they claimed that the one who has knowledge of the Book is Abdullah bin Salam, so he said: It is Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah said the same. It was also said: All the believers, and God knows best. Judge Abu Bakr bin Al-Arabi said: As for the one who said that it is Ali, he did so in one of two ways: Either because he believes that he is the most knowledgeable of the believers, but that is not the case, rather Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman are more knowledgeable than him. And because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the city of knowledge and Ali is its gate, which is a false hadith. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a city of knowledge and his companions are its gates, so some of them have the wide gate, and some of them are the middle one, according to their levels of knowledge. As for the one who said that they are all the believers, he is telling the truth, because every believer knows the Book, understands the aspect of its miracle, and bears witness to the truthfulness of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: According to this, the Book is the Qur’an. As for the one who said it was Abdullah bin Salam, he relied on the hadith of At-Tirmidhi. It is not impossible that something was revealed about Abdullah bin Salam and that it includes all the believers verbally. This is supported by the fact that the Almighty said: And those who disbelieved say meaning Quraysh. So those who have knowledge of the Book are the believers from among the Jews and Christians, who are closer to knowing the Prophethood and the Book than the idol worshippers. An-Nahhas said: The statement of the one who said it was Abdullah bin Salam and others is also possible, because if the proofs are correct and are known by those who read the books that were revealed before the Qur’an, then it is a confirmed matter, and God knows the truth of that.
14:1: All of it is Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah and Jabir. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: Except for two verses of it, which are Medinan. It was also said: Three. It was revealed about those who fought God and His Messenger, and it is the statement of God the Most High: Have you not considered those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? (Ibrahim 14:28) until His statement: Then your destination is the Fire (Ibrahim 14:30). God the Almighty said: “[Alif, Lam, Ra. This is a Book which We have revealed to you].” Its meaning was presented. That you may bring mankind out meaning by the Book, which is the Qur’an, meaning by calling you to it. From darknesses into the light meaning from the darkness of disbelief, misguidance, and ignorance to the light of faith and knowledge. This is an example, because disbelief is like darkness, and Islam is like light. It was also said: From innovation to the Sunnah, and from doubt to certainty, and the meaning is close. By the permission of their Lord meaning by His guidance and kindness to them. The ba in by the permission of their Lord is related to bring forth and the verb was attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) because he is the caller, warner, and guide. To the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy is like saying: I went out to Zayd the wise and virtuous without the waw, because they are one thing, and God is the Almighty who has no equal or likeness. It was also said: The Almighty is the one who cannot be defeated. It was also said: The Almighty is the one who is impregnable in his kingdom and authority. The Praiseworthy means the one who is praised in every tongue, and glorified in every place in every situation. Muqsim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: There were people who believed in Jesus, son of Mary, and people who disbelieved in him. When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, those who disbelieved in Jesus believed in him, and those who believed in Jesus disbelieved, so this verse was revealed. Al-Mawardi mentioned this.
14:2: The Almighty said: God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth meaning ownership, servants, invention and creation. Nafi', Ibn Amir and others read: God in the nominative case as a subject who is its predicate. It was said: who is an adjective, and the predicate is implied, meaning God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, is capable of everything. The rest read in the accusative case as a description of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, so the adjective precedes the described, like your saying: I passed by the elegant Zaid. It was said: as a substitute for the Praiseworthy and not an adjective, because the name of God has become like a proper noun, so it is not Joseph, just as it is not described by Zaid and Amr, rather it is permissible to describe it in terms of meaning, because its meaning is that He is the One who is unique in the ability to create. Abu Amr said: The accusative case is for advancement and delay, its meaning: to the path of God, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. When Jacob stopped at the Praiseworthy, he raised it, and when he connected it, he lowered it as an adjective. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Whoever lowers the word, stops at and what is on earth. The Almighty says: And woe to the disbelievers from a severe punishment. The meaning of woe has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a word that is said for torment and destruction. From a severe punishment meaning in Hell.
14:3: Those who prefer the life of this world means they choose it over the Hereafter, and the disbelievers do that. So those is in the accusative case as a description of them. It was said: It is in the nominative case as the predicate of an implied subject, meaning they are those. It was said: Those who prefer is the subject and its predicate. Those. And whoever prefers the world and its adornments, and prefers remaining in its pleasures over the pleasures of the Hereafter, and turns people away from the path of God - meaning he turns people away from it, which is the religion of God, which the Messengers brought, according to Ibn Abbas and others - is included in this verse. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The thing I fear most for my nation is the misguiding imams and it is an authentic hadith. And how many of them are there in these times, and God is the source of help. It was said: They prefer means they seek the world in a way other than its intended meaning, because the blessing of God is not sought except through obedience to Him and not disobedience to Him. And they seek to make it crooked meaning they seek to make it crooked and inclined to suit their whims, and to fulfill their needs and purposes. The path is both masculine and feminine. Crookedness is pronounced with a kasra on the 'ayn in religion, command, and earth, and in everything that is not straight. The 'ayn is pronounced with a fatha in everything that is straight, such as a wall, a spear, and the like. This has been mentioned previously in Al Imran and other verses. Those are in far astray meaning they have strayed far from the truth.
14:4: The Almighty said: And We did not send any Messenger that is, before you, O Muhammad except with the language of his people that is, their language, to explain to them the matter of their religion. The word language was used alone, even though it was attributed to the people, because what is meant is language, as it is a generic noun that applies to both little and much. There is no argument for the non-Arabs and others in this verse, because whoever translates for him what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought in a translation that he understands, the argument is binding on him. God Almighty said: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner to all mankind (Saba': 28). The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Every prophet was sent to his nation in its language, and God sent me to every red and black among His creation. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no one from this nation, Jew or Christian, hears of me and does not believe in that with which I was sent, but he will be among the companions of the Fire. Narrated by Muslim, and it has been mentioned previously. God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills. This is a response to the Qadarites regarding the influence of the will. It is a new sentence and is not conjoined with li-yabīn because the sending occurred for the purpose of clarification, not for misguidance. The accusative case is permissible in yudhālid because the sending became a cause of misguidance, so it is like His statement: So that he may be for them an enemy and a grief (al-Qasas 28:8). The sending became a cause of misguidance because they disbelieved in it when it came to them, so it became as if it was a cause of their disbelief. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Its meaning was presented earlier.
14:5: The Almighty said: And We had certainly sent Moses with Our signs meaning with Our arguments and proofs, meaning with the miracles indicating his truthfulness. Mujahid said: They are the nine signs. That you bring your people out of darkness into the light is similar to the Almighty's statement to our Prophet, peace be upon him, at the beginning of the surah: That you may bring mankind out of darkness into the light. It was said: That here means that, like the Almighty's statement: And the eminent ones among them set out, saying, 'Walk' (Sad~: 6), meaning walk. The Almighty said: And remind them of the days of God. That is, say to them a word that will remind them of the days of God. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: By the blessings of God upon them. And Ubayy ibn Ka’b said the same, and he narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, that is, by the blessings that God bestowed upon them of salvation from Pharaoh and the wilderness, among other blessings. And blessings are sometimes called days, and from this is the saying of Amr ibn Kulthum: And our days are long On the authority of Ibn Abbas and Muqatil: With the events of God among the past nations. It is said: So-and-so is knowledgeable about the days of the Arabs, meaning their events. Ibn Zayd said: He means the days in which He took revenge on the past nations. Ibn Wahb also narrated on the authority of Malik, who said: His trial. Al-Tabari said: He admonished them about what had happened in the past days for them, meaning what was in the days of God of blessings and tribulations, and they were humiliated slaves, and he was satisfied with mentioning the days about him because they were known to them. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b who said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: While Moses, peace be upon him, was among his people, he reminded them of the days of God, and the days of God are His trials and blessings.” He mentioned the hadith of Al-Khidr, and this indicates the permissibility of admonition that softens hearts, strengthens certainty, is free from all innovation, and is free from all misguidance and doubt. Indeed in that meaning in reminding about the days of God are signs meaning evidence. For every patient meaning very patient in obeying God and avoiding His disobedience. Thankful for God's blessings. Qatada said: It is the servant who, when given, is thankful, and when tested, is patient. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Faith is of two halves, half patience and half gratitude - then he recited this verse - Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful." And something similar was narrated from Al-Sha'bi, without a chain of transmission. Al-Hasan Al-Basri disappeared from Al-Hajjaj for seven years, and when he heard of his death, he said: O God, You have caused him to die, so cause his year to die, and he prostrated in gratitude, and recited: "Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful." He only specified the verses for every patient and grateful person because he considers them and does not neglect them, as He said: "You are only a warner for those who fear it" (An-Nazi'at: 45), even though he was a warner for everyone.
14:6: God Almighty says: “And when Moses said to his people, ‘Remember the favor of God upon you when He delivered you from the people of Pharaoh, who were afflicting you with terrible torment and slaughtering your sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.’” It was presented in full in Al-Baqarah, and praise be to God.
14:7: The Almighty said: And when your Lord proclaimed It was said: It is from the words of Moses to his people. And it was said: It is from the words of God, meaning, and remember, O Muhammad, when your Lord said such-and-such. And promise and promulgate mean to inform, like to threaten and to warn. The meaning of that was narrated from Al-Hasan and others. And from it is the call to prayer, because it is an announcement. The poet said: We did not feel the light of dawn until we heard the call to prayer in our gatherings. Ibn Masoud used to recite And when your Lord said and the meaning is the same. If you are grateful, I will surely increase you meaning if you are grateful for My blessings, I will surely increase you from My bounty. Al-Hasan: If you are grateful for My blessings, I will surely increase you from My obedience. Ibn Abbas: If you are united and obey, I will surely increase you from the reward. The meaning is close in these sayings, and the verse is a clear statement that gratitude is the reason for more. What the scholars have said about the meaning of gratitude has been presented in Al-Baqarah. Some of the righteous were asked about gratitude to God, and he said: Do you not gain strength from His blessings to disobey Him? It was narrated from David, peace be upon him, that he said: O Lord, how can I thank You, when my gratitude to You is a renewed blessing from You to me? He said: O David, now you have thanked me. I said: The true meaning of gratitude is this recognition of the blessing of the Benefactor, and not spending it in anything other than His obedience. Al-Hadi recited while he was eating: I give you His sustenance so that you may obey Him and be grateful for some of His rights. You did not thank Him for His blessings, but you were strengthened to disobey Him because of His provision. He choked on the morsel, and his tears choked him. Ja'far al-Sadiq said: If you hear the blessing of gratitude, then prepare for more. But if you deny, then indeed, My punishment is severe. That is, you denied My right. It was said: My blessings, and He promised punishment for disbelief, just as He promised increase for gratitude. The fa in the answer to the condition was deleted from in for fame.
14:8: God Almighty says: And Moses said, ‘If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, God is Free of need and Praiseworthy.’ That is, He is not deficient in that, rather He is the Free of need. Al-Hamid means the Praiseworthy.
14:9: The Almighty said: Has there not come to you the report of those before you - the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud? report is the report, and the plural is report. He said: Didn't the report come to you? Then it was said: It is from the words of Moses. It was said: It is from the words of God, meaning, remember, O Muhammad, when your Lord said such-and-such. It was said: It is the beginning of a speech from God the Most High. The story of the people of Noah, Aad, and Thamud is well-known, as God narrated in His Book. And His saying: And those after them, none knows them but God means, none can count their number but God, and none knows their lineage but God. And the genealogists, even if they attribute themselves to Adam, do not claim to have counted all nations, but they attribute some and withhold the lineage of others. And “It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he heard the genealogists attribute themselves to Ma’ad bin Adnan, then they added more, he said: The genealogists lied, for God says: ‘None knows them but God.’” And it was narrated from Urwah bin Az-Zubayr that he said: We did not find anyone who knows what is between Adnan and Ismail. Ibn Abbas said: Between Adnan and Ismail there are thirty fathers who are not known. And Ibn Mas’ud used to say when he recited: None knows them but God: The genealogists lied. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs meaning with arguments and evidence. "They put their hands in their mouths" meaning those people put their own hands in their mouths to bite them out of rage at what the messengers had brought, since it was a disgrace to their beloved ones and a reviling of their idols. This was said by Ibn Mas`ud, and something similar was said by `Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd, who recited: "They bit their fingertips in rage" (Al Imran 3:119). Ibn `Abbas said: When they heard the Book of God, they were amazed and put their hands back to their mouths. Abu Salih said: When their prophet said to them, "I am the Messenger of God to you, they pointed with their fingers to their mouths, If you are silent," denying him and rejecting his words. These three statements are close in meaning. The two pronouns refer to the disbelievers, and the first statement is the most authentic in chain of transmission. Abu `Ubaid said: `Abdur-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of `Abdullah, regarding the words of God the Almighty: "They put their hands in their mouths" he said: They bit them out of rage. The poet said: If Salma saw my cheekbones and the fineness in my leg and hand bones After my family and the coldness of my heart, I bit my hand with longing This meaning has already been mentioned in Al Imran with emphasis, and praise be to God. Mujahid and Qatadah said: They rejected the words of the messengers and denied them with their mouths. The first pronoun refers to the messengers and the second refers to the disbelievers. Al Hasan and others said: They put their hands in the mouths of the messengers in rejection of their words. The first pronoun in this case refers to the disbelievers and the second refers to the messengers. It was also said that its meaning is: They signaled to the messengers to be silent. Muqatil said: They took the hands of the messengers and put them on the mouths of the messengers to silence them and cut off their speech. It was also said: The messengers returned the hands of the people to their mouths. It was also said that the hands here are the blessings, meaning they rejected the blessings of the messengers with their mouths, meaning with speech and denial, and the messengers bringing the laws is blessings, and the meaning is: They denied with their mouths what the messengers brought. Fi has the meaning of Baa, it is said: I sat in the house and by the house, and the letters of the attributes are used in place of each other. Abu Ubaidah said: It is a proverb, meaning they did not believe and did not answer. The Arabs say to a man who refrains from answering and is silent: He put his hand in his mouth. Al-Akhfash also said the same. Al-Taqbi said: We have not heard any of the Arabs say: He put his hand in his mouth if he left what he was commanded to do. Rather, the meaning is: They bit their hands in anger and rage, as the poet said: You want to deceive the envious until he bites his hands It means that they annoy the envious person until he bites his fingers and hands. Another said: He has wasted his fingers in a crisis and has become bitten by the job And they said: meaning - the nations to the messengers - Indeed, we have disbelieved in that with which you have been sent meaning in the sending according to your claim, because they acknowledged that they were sent. And indeed, we are in doubt meaning in my Lord and in doubt. About what you call us to of monotheism. Suspicious meaning causing suspicion. It is said: I made him suspicious if you did something that caused suspicion and doubt, meaning we think that you are seeking the kingdom and the world.
14:10: The Almighty said: Their messengers said, 'Is there any doubt about God?' This is a question that means denial, meaning there is no doubt about God, meaning in His Oneness, as Qatada said. It was also said: in obeying Him. A third interpretation is possible: Is there any doubt about God's power?! Because they agree on it and differ in everything else, as indicated by His statement: The Originator of the heavens and the earth, their Creator, Inventor, Maker, and Originator after nonexistence, to draw attention to His power, so worship is not permissible except for Him. He calls you, meaning to His obedience through messengers and books. That He may forgive you some of your sins. Abu Ubaid said: Min is redundant. Sibawayh said: It is for partialization, and it is permissible to mention some and mean all of them. It was also said: Min is for substitution and is not redundant nor partial, meaning that forgiveness is a substitute for sins. And He will delay you for a specified term, meaning death, so He will not punish you in this world. They said, 'If you are,' meaning what you are. Except for human beings like us in form and appearance, you eat what we eat, and drink what we drink, and you are not angels. Do you want to turn us away from what our fathers used to worship of idols and statues? Then bring us a clear authority meaning a clear argument. This was impossible for them, for the messengers were not called except with miracles.
14:11: The Almighty said: Their messengers said to them, 'We are only human beings like you.' That is, in form and appearance as you said. But God bestows favor upon whomever He wills of His servants. That is, He favors him with prophethood. It was also said, with success, wisdom, knowledge, and guidance. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: By reciting the Qur'an and understanding what is in it. I said: This is a good statement. At-Tabari narrated from the hadith of Ibn Umar who said: I said to Abu Dharr: O uncle, advise me. He said: "I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as you asked me, and he said: There is no day, night, or hour in which God does not bestow charity upon whomever He wills of His servants. And God, the Most High, has not bestowed favors upon His servants like that of inspiring them to remember Him." And it was not for us to bring you an authority, that is, an argument or a sign. Except by the permission of God meaning by His will, and that is not within our power, meaning we cannot come up with an argument as you are asking except by His command and power. So its wording is the wording of a statement, but its meaning is negation, because no one is forbidden what he is not able to do. And in God let the believers put their trust its meaning was presented earlier.
14:12: The Almighty said: And why should we not put our trust in God? Ma is an interrogative in the nominative case as a subject, and lana is the predicate, and what follows it is in the case of a state, the meaning is: What is there for us in abandoning our trust in God? And He has guided us to our ways meaning the path that leads to His mercy and saves from His wrath and punishment. And we will surely be patient is an oath lam, its meaning is: By God, we will surely be patient with what you have harmed us with meaning the humiliation, beating, denial and killing, trusting in God that He will suffice us and reward us. And in God let the trustful put their trust.
14:13: The Almighty said: And those who disbelieved said to their messengers, 'We will surely expel you from our land.' The lam is a lam of oath, meaning, By God, we will expel you. "Or you must return." That is, until you return or unless you return, as stated by Al-Tabari and others. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This estimation is not required, because (or) is in its proper form of choice. The disbelievers gave the messengers the choice between returning to their religion or expelling them from their land. This is the way of God Almighty with His messengers and servants. Do you not see His saying: "And indeed, they almost tempted you to leave the land to expel you from it. But then they would not remain behind you except for a little while. The way of those of Our messengers We had sent before you." (al-Isra’ 17:76) This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-A'raf and other books. "In our religion means to our religion, so their Lord inspired to them, 'We will surely destroy the wrongdoers.'"
14:14: And We will surely inhabit you in the land after them. The Almighty said: That is for him who fears standing before Me and fears My threat. That is, his standing before the Day of Resurrection. The infinitive was added to the subject. The position is a source like standing. It is said: he stood before standing and standing. This was added to it because it is specific to it. The position with the opening of the meem is the place of residence, and with the damma is the action of residence. That is for him who fears standing before Me that is, My standing over him and My watching him. God the Almighty said: Then is he who stands over every soul for what it has earned? (Ar-Ra'd: 33). Al-Akhfash said: That is for him who fears standing before Me that is, My punishment, and fears My threat that is, the Qur'an and its prohibitions. It was said: It is the punishment. The threat is the name of the promise.
14:15: The Almighty said: And they sought victory meaning they sought help, meaning the messengers were permitted to seek help against their people and pray for their destruction, as Ibn Abbas and others said, and it has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. And from it is the hadith: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek help from the vagabonds of the emigrants, meaning he sought help. Ibn Zayd said: The nations sought help with supplication as the Quraysh said: O God, if this is the truth from You (al-Anfal 8:32) and the verse. And it was narrated from Ibn Abbas. And it was said: The Messenger said: They have denied me, so grant victory between me and them. And the nations said: If these are truthful, then punish us, from Ibn Abbas also, similar to it: Bring us the punishment of God, if you should be of the truthful (al-Ankabut 29:29) Bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the messengers (al-A’raf 7:77). And every stubborn tyrant will fail the arrogant tyrant who does not see anyone having any right over him, this is how it is according to the linguists, as mentioned by Al-Nahhas. The stubborn one is the one who opposes the truth and deviates from it, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It is said: He turned away from his people, meaning he distanced himself from them. It was also said: It is from and, which means the side. So-and-so was stubborn, meaning he took a side, turning away. The poet said: If you come down, make me the middle one, for I am old and cannot bear to be stubborn. Al-Harawi said: The Almighty said: Jabbar An’id meaning deviating from the goal, and he is the stubborn, obstinate and obstinate. In the hadith of Ibn Abbas, he was asked about the woman with istihadah, so he said: It is an obstinate vein. Abu Ubaid said: It is the one who is stubborn and rebellious like a person, so this vein is in its position in the abundance of what comes out of it. Shammar said: The obstinate is the one who does not stop. Omar said, mentioning his biography: The most stubborn. Al-Layth said: The stubborn among camels is the one who does not mix with them, but rather is always on one side, he meant the one who intended to disagree or separate from the group, so he turned towards it. Muqatil said: The stubborn is the arrogant. Ibn Kaysan said: He is the one who holds his nose high. It was said: The stubborn and obstinate is the one who is arrogant towards the messengers and goes astray from the path of truth and does not follow it. The Arabs say: The worst of camels is the obstinate one who goes astray. It was also said: The obstinate is the disobedient. Qatada said: The obstinate is the one who refused to say there is no god but God. I said: The tyrant and the stubborn in the verse have the same meaning, even though the wording is different. Everyone who deviates from the truth is tyrant and stubborn, meaning arrogant. It was said that what is meant by it in the verse is Abu Jahl, as mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. Al-Mawardi narrated in the book Adab Al-Dunya Wal-Din that Al-Walid bin Yazid bin Abdul Malik was one day looking for good omens from the Qur’an, and he found out the words of God Almighty: And they sought victory, but every tyrant and stubborn was disappointed. So he tore up the Qur’an and began to say: I threaten every stubborn tyrant, for I am that stubborn tyrant. If you come to your Lord on the Day of Resurrection, say, O Lord, Al-Walid tore me apart. He did not live long until he was killed in the worst way, and his head was crucified on his palace, then on the wall of his city.
14:16: The Almighty says: Behind him is Hell meaning behind that disbeliever is Hell, meaning after his destruction. And behind means after. Al-Nabigha said: I swore, I did not leave you any doubt, and there is no way for a person to go beyond God. That is, after God Almighty, and likewise His Almighty saying: And behind it is a severe punishment (Ibrahim 14:17), that is, after it, and His Almighty saying: And they disbelieve in what is behind it (al-Baqarah 2:91), that is, in what is other than it, as Al-Farra’ said. Abu Ubaid said: what is after it. It was said: Behind it means in front of it, and from this is the saying of the poet: And from your vision, a day when you will reach it, there is no present that is impossible for you, nor is there any apparent one. Another said: Do you expect the Banu Marwan to listen to me and obey me, while my people Tamim and the desert are behind me? Labid said: Is there not behind me, if my death is delayed, the necessity of the stick upon which the fingers bend? He wants in front of me. In the revelation: And behind them was a king (al-Kahf 18:79), meaning in front of them. This is what Abu Ubaidah, Abu Ali Qatrib and others agreed with. Al-Akhfash said: It is like saying this matter is behind you, meaning it will come to you, and I am behind so-and-so, meaning in pursuit of him and I will reach him. Al-Nahhas said: In his saying behind him is Hell, meaning in front of him, and it is not from the opposites, but rather from tawara, meaning concealed. Al-Azhari said: That behind can mean behind and in front, so it is from the opposites, and Abu Ubaidah also said it. Its derivation is from what is hidden and concealed, so Hell is hidden and does not appear, so it came from rawa’ because it cannot be seen, as narrated by Ibn Al-Anbari and it is good. God the Almighty said: And he will be given to drink from a purulent water. That is, from water like pus, as a brave man is called a lion, that is, like a lion. This is a metaphor and simile. It was said: It is what flows from the bodies of the people of Hell from pus and blood. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi and al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: It is the one who washes the people of Hell, and that is water that flows from the private parts of the adulterers and adulteresses. It was said: It is from water that you hate and turn away from, so pus is taken from turning away. Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned that Sufyan ibn Amr told us on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Busr on the authority of Abu Umamah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement: And he will be given to drink from a purulent water.
14:17: He gulps it down (Ibrahim 14:16) He said: He brings it close to his mouth and he hates it. When he brings it close to him, it burns his face and his scalp falls off. When he drinks it, it cuts his intestines until they come out of his anus. God says: And they are given to drink scalding water, which will sever their intestines. (Muhammad 47:15) And God says: "And if they call for relief, they will be given water like murky oil, which will scald their faces. What an evil drink!" (al-Kahf 18:29) Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, who said: It is a strange hadith. Ubaidullah bin Busr, from whom Safwan bin Amr narrated the hadith of Abu Umamah, may have been the brother of Abdullah bin Busr. He gulps it down means he takes it in sips, not all at once, because of its bitterness and heat. And he can hardly swallow it down means he swallows it. It is said: he gulps water down, he gulps it down, and he gulps it down, meaning he swallows it down. The drink goes down the throat, if it is smooth and easy, and God made it go down easily. And (almost is a conjunction, meaning that He swallows it after a delay. God the Most High said: And they almost did not do it Al-Baqarah 2:71, meaning they did it after a delay. That is why He said: That which was in their bellies and their skins would melt thereby Al-Hajj 22:20. This indicates swallowing. Ibn Abbas said: He allows it and does not pass by it. And death will come to him from every side Al-Hajj 22:20. Ibn Abbas said: That is, the causes of death will come to him from every direction, from his right and his left, from above and below him, from in front of him and behind him, like His statement: Above them are shades of fire, and beneath them are shades Az-Zumar 39:16. Ibrahim At-Taymi said: It will come to him from every part of his body, even from the ends of his hair, because of the pains in every part of his body. Ad-Dahhak said: Death will come to him from every side and place, even from the big toes of his feet. Al-Akhfash said: He means the afflictions that befall the disbeliever in the Fire, which he called death, and it is one of the greatest deaths. It was said: There is not a limb of his that is not subjected to some kind of torment. If he died seventy times, it would be easier for him than any of them in a single moment, whether a snake biting him, or a scorpion possessing him, or a fire scorching him, or shackles on his feet, or chains around his neck, or a chain with which he is brought near, or a coffin in which he is, or Zaqqum or scalding water, or other than that kind of torment. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: If the disbeliever in Hell calls for a drink and sees it, he will die several deaths. When he approaches it, he will die several deaths. When he drinks from it, he will die several deaths. This is what is meant by His statement: And death will come to him from every side, and he will not die. Ad-Dahhak said: He will not die and find rest. Ibn Jurayj said: His soul will cling to his throat and will not exit his mouth, so he will die, nor will it return to its place in his body, so that life will benefit him. Similar to this is His statement: He will neither die therein nor will he live (Ta-Ha: 74). It was said: God will create pains in his body, each one of which is like the pain of death. It was said: And he is not dead because the hardships of death are prolonged for him, and his agonies are prolonged, so that this will be an increase in his torment. I said: It appears from this that he will die, but this is not the case, because God Almighty said: They will not be put to death so that they die, nor will their punishment be lightened for them (Fatir 35:36). The Sunnah has mentioned this, so the states of the disbelievers are the states of those who are always overcome by the throes of death, and God knows best. And behind it means in front of it. A severe punishment means severe, continuous pain without easing. From this is His statement: And that they may find in you harshness (al-Tawbah 9:123), meaning severity and strength. Fudayl ibn ‘Iyad said about God Almighty’s statement: And behind it is a severe punishment he said: Holding one’s breath.
14:18: The Almighty said: The parable of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are as ashes. Grammarians differed in raising like. Sibawayh said: It was raised by the beginning and the predicate is implied, the estimate: And in what is recited to you or narrated the parable of those who disbelieve in their Lord then he began and said: their deeds are as ashes meaning like ashes that the wind blew fiercely. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, the parable of those who disbelieved in what is recited to you is their deeds as ashes, and according to Al-Farraa it is on the cancellation of the parable, the estimate: And those who disbelieved in their Lord, their deeds are as ashes. And from him also that it is on the deletion of an added word, the estimate: Like the deeds of those who disbelieved in their Lord are as ashes, and the first was mentioned by Al-Mahdawi, and the second by Al-Qushayri and Al-Tha'labi, and it is permissible for it to be a subject as it is said: The description of so-and-so is dark, so like means a description. And in speech it is permissible to make their deeds accusative as a substitute for inclusion from those and this is connected to his saying: And every stubborn tyrant will fail and the meaning is: Their deeds will be nullified and not accepted. Ashes are what remains after something has been burned. So God made this verse an example of the deeds of the disbelievers in that He destroys them just as a strong wind destroys ashes on a stormy day. As-saf is a strong wind, and that was because they associated partners with God in it. There are three sayings about describing the day as as-saf: The first is that even though as-saf refers to the wind, the day can also be described by it because the wind is in it, so it is permissible to say: a stormy day, just as one says: a hot day and a cold day, and the cold and the heat are in both. The second is that he means on a stormy day the wind, because it was mentioned at the beginning of the word, as the poet said: If a dark day comes, the sun is eclipsed He wants to eclipse the sun, but he deleted it because it was mentioned before, as mentioned by Al-Harawi. The third - that it is from the description of the wind, but when it came after the day, its i'rab was followed as it was said: a ruined lizard's hole, mentioned by Al-Tha'labi and Al-Mawardi. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ibrahim bin Abi Bakr read on a stormy day. They are not able meaning the disbelievers. Of what they have earned meaning in the Hereafter, meaning of the reward for what they did of righteousness in this world, because it was nullified by disbelief. That is the farthest error meaning the great loss, and he only made it great and far away because it was not possible to recover it through death.
14:19: The Almighty says: Have you not seen that God created the heavens and the earth in truth? The vision here is the vision of the heart, because the meaning is: Has not your knowledge reached Him? Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read - He created the heavens and the earth. The meaning of in truth is to prove His power. If He wills, He can take you away O people, meaning He is able to annihilate just as He was able to create things, so do not disobey Him, for if you disobey Him, He will take you away and bring forth a new creation better and more obedient than you, because if they were like the first ones, then there would be no benefit in replacing them.
14:20: And that is not difficult for God meaning it is impossible.
14:21: The Almighty said: And they will all appear before God meaning they will emerge from their graves, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Prominence is appearance. Baraz is a wide place for one to appear, and from this comes a woman who appears to people, so the meaning of prominent is they will appear from their graves. It came in the past tense and its meaning is the future, and this is connected to His saying: And every obstinate tyrant will be disappointed meaning they approached when they asked for victory and were destroyed, then they were resurrected for the reckoning and they all appeared before God, with no one to conceal them from Him. To God because of God's command for them to appear. The weak ones said meaning the followers to those who were arrogant and they are the leaders. Indeed, we were your followers it is possible that taba'a is a source, the estimate is: those who follow. It is possible that it is the plural of taba'a, like haris and haris, khadim and khuddam, rasid and rasad, and baqir and baqar. Are you able to protect us from the punishment of God from anything? “Anything?” From is a relative clause. It is said: He protected him from harm or He made him rich if he brought him benefit. “They said: “If God had guided us, we would have guided you.” That is, if God had guided us to faith, we would have guided you to it. It was also said: If God had guided us to the path of Paradise, we would have guided you to it. It was also said: If God had saved us from the punishment, we would have saved you from it. “It is the same for us.” This is the beginning of its predicate ajza’ana, that is: “It is the same for us whether we are impatient or patient. We have no escape.” That is, no place of refuge or shelter. It is permissible for it to have the meaning of a source, and the meaning of a noun. It is said: So-and-so fled from such-and-such, that is, he fled and deviated, he deviated, he deviated, he deviated, he deviated, and the meaning is: we have no way to distance ourselves from the Fire. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the torment becomes severe for the people of Hell, they will say: ‘Come, let us be patient.’ So they will be patient for five hundred years. When they see that this will not benefit them, they will say: ‘Come, let us be impatient.’ So they will be impatient and cry out for five hundred years. When they see that this will not benefit them, they will say: ‘It is the same to us whether we are impatient or patient. We have no escape.’” Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi said: It was mentioned to us that the people of Hell will say to one another: O people! You have been afflicted with the calamity and torment that you see, so come and let us be patient, perhaps patience will benefit us as the people of obedience were patient in obeying God, and patience benefited them when they were patient. So they agreed to be patient and were patient, but their patience was prolonged, so they became impatient and called out: It is the same for us whether we are impatient or patient, there is no escape for us meaning, a place of escape. Then Satan stood up and said: “God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you and broke my promise, and I had no authority over you except that I called you and you responded to me, so do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you.” He said: I cannot help you at all. “And you cannot help me. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with Him before.” The hadith in full, and we have written it in its entirety in the Book of Remembrance.
14:22: The Almighty said: And Satan said, when the matter has been decided. Al-Hasan said: Satan will stand on the Day of Resurrection as a preacher in Hell on a pulpit of fire that all of creation will hear. The meaning of: when the matter has been decided is that the people of Paradise will be in Paradise and the people of Hell will be in Hell, as will be explained in Mary, peace be upon her. Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, meaning resurrection, Paradise, Hell, the reward of the obedient and the punishment of the disobedient, so He fulfilled His promise to you. And I promised you that there would be no resurrection, no Paradise, no Hell, no reward, and no punishment, but I broke my promise to you. Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith of intercession, he said: “Then Jesus will say, ‘Shall I guide you to the unlettered Prophet? ’ So they will come and God will permit me to stand up, and my seat will be filled with the most fragrant scent anyone has ever smelled, until I come to my Lord, and He will intercede for me and will make for me a light from the hair of my head to the nails of my feet. Then the disbelievers will say, ‘The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so who will intercede for us? ’ They will say, ‘It is none other than Iblis, he is the one who led us astray. ’ So they will come to him and say, ‘The believers have found someone to intercede for them, so intercede for us, for you have led us astray. ’ His seat will be filled with the most foul scent anyone has ever smelled. Then their wailing will increase and he will say at that time, ‘Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. ’” The promise of truth is the addition of a thing to its description, like their saying, ‘the mosque of the congregation. ’ Al-Farra’ said, the Basrans said, ‘And the promise of truth has befallen you today, or He promised you the promise of truth, and He fulfilled it for you. ’ So the source was omitted to indicate the state. And I had no authority over you meaning, no argument or explanation, meaning, I did not show you any argument for what I promised you and made attractive to you in this world, except that I invited you and you responded to me meaning, I led you astray and you followed me. It was also said: I did not force you to do what I invited you to do. Except that I invited you is an interrupted exception, meaning, but I invited you with whispers and you responded to me of your own choice, so do not blame me but blame yourselves. It was also said: And I had no authority over you meaning, over your hearts and the place of your faith, but I invited you and you responded to me. This is because he addressed the disobedient believer and the disbelieving denier, and there is a consideration in it, because of his statement: when the matter was decided as it indicates that he addressed the disbelievers and not the disobedient monotheists, and God knows best. So do not blame me but blame yourselves if you come to me without an argument. I will not be your helper meaning, your savior. And you will not be my savior meaning, my helper. The one who cries and seeks help is the one who seeks victory and assistance, and the one who cries is the one who helps. Salamah bin Jandal said: Whenever a frightened person came to us, the screaming sounded like the banging of pipes. Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt said: Do not be afraid, for I am not a cry to you, and you have no help or support from me. It is said: So-and-so screamed, meaning he cried out, screaming, and shouting. And screaming means shouting. And screaming is the effort of screaming. And the screamer is the helper, and the one who seeks help is the one who seeks help. You say from it: He asked for help from me, so I cried out to him. And screaming is the sound of one who seeks help. And screaming is also the screamer, and he is the helper and the one who seeks help, and it is from the opposites, said Al-Jawhari. The common reading is bi-m-sarhi with the fat-ha on the ya. Al-A'mash and Hamza read bi-m-sarhi with the kasra on the ya. The original is bi-m-sarhiyyin, so the nun was removed for the addition, and the ya of the group was assimilated into the ya of addition. So whoever puts it in the accusative case, it is for the sake of doubling, and because if the ya of addition is sukun, it must be in it like in the words: hawai and asai. So if the word before it is moved, the fat-ha or sukun are permissible, like in the words: ghulami and ghulamati. And whoever puts it in the kasra, because of the meeting of two sukun, it is moved to the kasra, because the ya is the sister of the kasra. Al-Farra' said: Hamza's reading was mistaken, and few of them were free from error. Al-Zajjaj said: This is a bad reading and there is no basis for it except a weak one. Qatrib said: This is the language of Banu Yarbu’; they add a ya’ to the ya’ of addition. Al-Qushayri said: What suffices for this is that what is proven by continuous transmission from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, cannot be said to be wrong, ugly or bad. Rather, it is eloquent in the Qur’an, and there is what is more eloquent than it. Perhaps these people meant that what Hamza recited was more eloquent. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated before means I have disbelieved in your associating Me with God Almighty, so -ma is in the sense of a source. Ibn Jurayj said: Today I have disbelieved in what you used to call for in this world of associating partners with God Almighty. Qatadah said: I disobeyed God. Ath-Thawri said: I have disbelieved in your obedience to Me in this world. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment. In these verses there is a response to the Qadarites, the Mu'tazilites, the Imams and those who follow their path. Look at the statement of those who were followed: If God had guided us, we would have guided you and the statement of Satan: Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth. How did they acknowledge the truth in the attributes of God Almighty while they were in the depths of Hell, as He said in another place: Whenever a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them (al-Mulk 67:8) until His statement: So they acknowledged their sin. Their acknowledgment in the depths of the Blaze of truth is not beneficial, but rather the acknowledgment benefits its owner in this world. God Almighty said: "And others acknowledged their sins. They mixed a good deed with another bad one. Perhaps God will turn to them in forgiveness" (al-Tawbah 9:102). And perhaps from God is obligatory.
14:23: The Almighty said: And admit those who believed and did righteous deeds to gardens meaning into gardens because entered is intransitive, just as its opposite, exited, is intransitive, and it cannot be used as an analogy, as Al-Mahdawi said. And when God the Almighty informed about the state of the people of Hell, He also informed about the state of the people of Paradise. The reading of the group is enter as a passive verb. Al-Hasan read and enter as a future and resumption. With the permission of their Lord meaning with His command. It was said: with His will and facilitation. And He said: with the permission of their Lord and did not say: with my permission, out of respect and glorification. "Their greeting therein is, 'Peace'" was mentioned earlier in Yunus. And praise be to God.
14:24: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Have you not seen how God sets forth a parable? When God mentioned the parable of the deeds of the disbelievers, that they are like ashes that the wind blows violently on a stormy day, He mentioned the parable of the sayings of the believers and other things, then He explained that parable and said: A good word is the fruit, so He deleted it because the words indicate it. Ibn Abbas said: The good word is There is no god but God, and the good tree is the believer. Mujahid and Ibn Jurayj said: The good word is faith. Atiyah Al-Awfi and Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: It is the believer himself. Mujahid and Ikrimah also said: The tree is the palm tree, so it is possible that the meaning is: The root of the word in the heart of the believer - which is faith - He likened it to the palm tree in its origin, and He likened the rise of his deeds in the sky to the rise of the palm tree’s branches, and God’s reward for him is the fruit. It was narrated from the hadith of Anas from the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that he said: “The parable of faith is like that of a tree whose roots are firm: faith is its foundation, prayer is its foundation, zakat is its branches, fasting is its twigs, harming oneself for the sake of God is its growth, good character is its leaves, and refraining from what God has forbidden is its fruit.” It is possible that the meaning is: The root of the palm tree is firmly fixed in the ground, meaning its roots drink from the ground and the sky waters it from above, so it is pure and growing. At-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Anas bin Malik who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought a veil containing dates, and he said: The example of a good word is like a good tree whose root is firmly fixed and whose branches are in the sky, yielding its fruit at all times by permission of its Lord - he said - it is the palm tree. And the example of a bad word is like a bad tree uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability - he said - it is the colocynth.” And his statement was narrated from Anas and he said: And it is more correct. Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘God sets forth a parable: a good word is like a good tree, whose root is firm.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Do you know what it is?’ It occurred to me that it was the palm tree.” Al-Suhayli said: What was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, that it was the coconut, is not correct. Since it is authentically reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the hadith of Ibn Umar: “There is a tree whose leaves do not fall and it is like the believer. Tell me what it is - then he said - it is the palm tree.” Malik included it in Al-Muwatta’ from the narration of Ibn Al-Qasim and others except Yahya, who omitted it from his narration. The people of Sahih included it and Al-Harith bin Usamah added to it an addition equal to a journey, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: It is the palm tree; not even a fingertip of it falls, and likewise the believer, his supplication is not dropped. So he explained the meaning of the hadith and the similarity. I said: Al-Ghaznawi mentioned from him, peace be upon him: “The example of the believer is like the palm tree; if you befriend him, he will benefit you; if you sit with him, he will benefit you; if you consult him, he will benefit you. He is like the palm tree; everything in it is beneficial.” He said: Eat from your turban, meaning that the palm tree was created from the surplus clay of Adam, peace be upon him. Likewise, it remains with its head, lives with its heart, and its fruit is the mixture of male and female. It has been said that since it is the most similar tree to man, it was likened to him. This is because if the head of every tree is cut off, branches branch out from its sides, and if the head of the palm tree is cut off, it dries up and its roots are lost. And because it is similar to man and all other animals in pollination, because it does not bear fruit until it is pollinated, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: The best wealth is a well-trodden path and a trained mare. And pollination is the well, and its explanation will come in Surat Al-Hijr. And because it is from the surplus clay of Adam. And it is said that when God, the Almighty, formed Adam from clay, a piece of clay remained, so He formed it with His hand and planted it in the Garden of Eden. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:
14:25: "Honor your paternal aunt. They said: Who is our paternal aunt, O Messenger of God? He said: The palm tree. "It yields its fruit at all times." Al-Rabi' said: Every time morning and evening. Likewise, the work of the believer ascends at the beginning and end of the day. Ibn Abbas said the same. And from him: "It yields its fruit at all times." He said: It is the coconut tree that does not cease to produce fruit. It bears fruit every month. He likened the work of the believer for God Almighty at all times to the palm tree that yields its fruit at different times. Ad-Dahhak said: Every hour of the night or day, winter and summer, is eaten at all times. Likewise, the believer is not without goodness at all times. An-Nahhas said: These sayings are close and not contradictory, because the word "now" according to all linguists except for those who deviated from it means time and it applies to a short or long time. Al-Asma'i recited the verse of An-Nabigha: The exorcists are afraid of its poison, which they release sometimes and sometimes they withdraw. This shows you that now means time, so faith is fixed in the heart of the believer, and his actions, words and glorification are high and elevated in the sky as high as the branches of a palm tree, and what he gains from the blessing of faith and its reward is like what he gets from the fruit of the palm tree at all times of the year, from fresh dates, unripe dates, dates, blossoms, dates and pollen. In a narration from Ibn Abbas: The tree is a tree in Paradise that bears fruit at all times. And for example is the object of strike, word is a substitute for it, and the kaf in his saying: like a tree is in the accusative case as a state of word, the meaning is: a good word likened to a good tree. Second: The Almighty’s statement: It yields its fruit at all times. Since trees yield their fruit once a year, this clarifies the ruling on the time. For this reason, we said: Whoever swears that he will not speak to so-and-so for a while, or say such-and-such for a while, then the time is a year. The word time was mentioned in another place, meaning more than that, as the Almighty said: Has there not come upon man a period of time? It was said in the interpretation: forty years. And Ikrimah narrated that a man said: If I do such-and-such for a while, then his slave is free. So he came to Umar ibn Abdul Aziz and asked him, so he asked me about it, and I said: Indeed, the time is a period that is not attained. His statement: And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time. (Al-Anbiya’: 111) So I think that you should hold back the time between the harvest of the palm tree and its bearing, as if he liked it, and it is the statement of Abu Hanifa regarding the time, that it is six months, following Ikrimah and others. What the scholars have said regarding the time has already been completed in Al-Baqarah, and praise be to God. And God presents examples meaning similarities for the people that perhaps they will remember and take heed. This has been mentioned previously.
14:26: The Almighty said: And the parable of a bad word is that of a bad tree. The bad word is the word of disbelief. It was said: the disbeliever himself. The bad tree is the colocynth tree as in the hadith of Anas, and it is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: that it is a tree that was not created on earth. It was also said: it is the garlic tree, narrated from Ibn Abbas as well. It was also said: truffles and algae. It was also said: kashoot, which is a tree that has no leaves or roots in the earth. The poet said: They are nothing but a bunch of idiots, neither root nor paper. Uprooted from the surface of the earth means uprooted from its roots, as Ibn Abbas said, and from this is the saying of Laqit: It is the expulsion that uproots your origin. Whoever has ever seen something like this, and whoever has heard of it… The historian said: He took her body and it is the same, and the body is the person sitting or standing. The body of his uprooted, and he uprooted it from above the ground, meaning it has no firm root that drinks with its roots from the ground. It has no stability meaning no root in the ground. It was said: from firmness, so likewise the disbeliever has no argument, no stability, and no good in him, and no good word or good deed ascends to him. Muawiyah bin Saleh narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha regarding the Almighty’s saying: “God sets forth an example: a good word” he said: There is no god but God like a good tree he said: the believer, its root is firm there is no god but God is firm in the heart of the believer, and the example of a bad word he said: polytheism, like a bad tree he said: the polytheist, uprooted from above the earth, it has no stability meaning the polytheist has no root to work on. It was said: The example goes back to the call to faith, and the call to polytheism, because the word is understood from the saying and the call to something.
14:27: God Almighty says: God confirms those who believe with the firm word. Ibn Abbas said: It is There is no god but God. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God will make firm those who believe, with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. This was revealed regarding the torment of the grave. It will be said to him: Who is your Lord? He will say: My Lord is God and my religion is the religion of Muhammad. This is what He said: God will make firm those who believe, with the firm word, in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. I said: It came thus, suspended in some of the paths of Muslim on the authority of Al-Baraa’, that it is his saying, and the correct one in it is the elevation as in Sahih Muslim and the book of Al-Nasa’i and Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah and others, on the authority of Al-Baraa’ on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Al-Bukhari mentioned, Ja’far bin Umar told us, he said, Shu’bah told us on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad on the authority of Sa’d bin Ubaydah on the authority of Al-Baraa bin Azib on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “When the believer is seated in his grave, someone comes to him and he testifies that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and that is his saying God confirms those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. We have explained this chapter in the Book of Remembrance and we have explained there those who will be tested in their graves and will be questioned, so whoever wants to stand on it should contemplate it there. Sahl bin Ammar said: I saw Yazid bin Harun in a dream after his death, so I said to him: What did God do with you? He said: Two rough, harsh angels came to me in my grave, and they said: What is your religion, and who is your Lord and who is your Prophet? So I took hold of my white beard and said: Is this said to someone like me?” And people have known your answer for eighty years?! So they went and said: Did you write from Hariz bin Othman? I said yes! They said: He hated Ali, so God hated him. It was said: The meaning of may God make them steadfast is that God keeps them on the steadfast word, and from this is the saying of Abdullah bin Rawahah: God confirms what He has given you of the good confirmation of Moses and a victory like the victory He gave you. It was said: He establishes them in both abodes as a reward for their firm statement. Al-Qaffal and a group said: In the life of this world meaning in the grave, because the dead are in this world until they are resurrected, and in the Hereafter meaning at the reckoning. Al-Mawardi narrated it from Al-Baraa’ who said: What is meant by the life of this world is the questioning in the grave, and by the Hereafter is the questioning on the Day of Resurrection. And God misleads the wrongdoers meaning from their argument in their graves just as they went astray in this world because of their disbelief, so He does not teach them the word of truth. So when they are asked in their graves, they say: We do not know. He says: You neither knew nor did you recite. At that point, He is beaten with whips according to what is proven in the reports. We have mentioned that in the Book of Remembrance. It was said: He gives them respite until they increase in misguidance in this world. And God does what He wills of punishing a people and misleading another people. It was said: The reason for the revelation of this verse is what was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he described the questioning of Munkar and Nakir and what the dead person would answer. Umar said: O Messenger of God, do I have my mind? He said: Yes. He said: Then I am sufficient. Then God Almighty revealed this verse.
14:28: The Almighty said: Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of God for disbelief? That is, they exchanged the favor of God upon them for disbelief in their denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when God sent him from among them and among them, so they disbelieved. What is meant are the polytheists of Quraysh and that the verse was revealed about them, according to Ibn Abbas, Ali and others. It was said: It was revealed about the polytheists who fought the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr. Abu al-Tufayl said: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: They are the Quraysh who slaughtered on the day of Badr. It was said: It was revealed about the two wicked ones from Quraysh, Banu Makhzum and Banu Umayyah. As for Banu Umayyah, they were granted respite for a time, and as for Banu Makhzum, they were destroyed on the day of Badr. This was said by Ali ibn Abi Talib and Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with them. A fourth statement: They converted to Christianity from the Arabs Jabalah ibn al-Ayham and his companions when he slapped his face, so Umar ordered him to be punished in the same manner, but he was not satisfied and refused, so he converted to Christianity and joined the Romans with a group of his people, according to Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. When he reached the land of the Romans, he regretted it and said: The nobles were saved from the shame of a slap, and there would have been no harm in it if they had been patient. She protected me from her stubbornness and pride, and I sold her my healthy eye in need. I wish I was nursing the mothers in a town and did not deny what Omar said Al-Hasan said: It is general for all polytheists. And they made their people settle means they made them descend. Ibn Abbas said: They are the leaders of the polytheists on the day of Badr. They made their people settle means those who followed them. The abode of destruction It was said: Hell, said Ibn Zayd. It was said: On the day of Badr, said Ali ibn Abi Talib and Mujahid. And destruction is perdition, and from it the saying of the poet: I have never seen heroes like them in war on the day after the war when destruction was feared.
14:29: Hell they will burn in it It is clear that the abode of destruction is Hell, as Ibn Zayd said. Based on this, it is not permissible to stop at the abode of destruction because Hell is in the accusative case as a translation of the abode of destruction. If someone raised it with an implied pronoun, meaning: it is Hell, or with what came back from the pronoun in they will burn in it, it would be good to stop at the abode of destruction. And an evil settlement means the settled place.
14:30: The Almighty said: And they have set up rivals for God meaning idols that they worshipped, and this has been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. To lead astray from His path meaning from His religion. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read it with a fatha on the ya', and likewise in Al-Hajj To lead astray from the path of God (al-Hajj 22:9) and similarly in Luqman and Az-Zumar, and the rest read it with a damma on it meaning to lead people astray from His path. As for those who open it, it means that they are the ones who are necessarily led astray from the path of God, meaning their end will be misguidance and error, so this is the lam of the end. Say, 'Enjoy yourselves' is a warning to them, and it is an indication of the smallness of the pleasures of this world that they are in, as it is cut off. Indeed, your destination is the Fire meaning your return and recourse is to the torment of Hell.
14:31: The Almighty said: Say to My servants who have believed meaning that the people of Mecca exchanged the blessing of God for disbelief, so say to those who believed and fulfilled their servitude to Him to establish prayer meaning the five daily prayers, meaning tell them to establish, and the command with it is an implied condition, you say: Obey God and He will admit you into Paradise, meaning if you obey Him He will admit you into Paradise, this is what Al-Farraa said. Al-Zajjaj said: Yaqimu is in the subjunctive mood with the meaning of the lam, meaning that they should establish, so the lam was dropped because the command indicated the absent with -say. He said: It is possible to say: Yaqimu is the answer to an omitted command, meaning tell them to establish prayer and they should establish prayer. And spend from what We have provided for them secretly and publicly meaning zakat, according to Ibn Abbas and others. The majority said: The secret is what is hidden and the public is what is apparent. Al-Qasim bin Yahya said: The secret is voluntary and the public is obligatory. This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah with emphasis when he said: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good (al-Baqarah 2:271). Before a Day comes in which there will be neither trading nor friendship has also been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. And Khalal is the plural of khallah like qallah and qilal. He said: I am not a frying pan, nor a frying pan
14:32: The Almighty says: It is God who created the heavens and the earth meaning He created them and invented them without a previous example. And sent down from the sky meaning from the clouds water and brought forth thereby fruits meaning from the trees as provision for you. “And He has subjected to you the ships that they may sail through the sea by His command” its meaning was presented in Al-Baqarah. And He has subjected to you the rivers meaning the fresh seas for you to drink from and water yourselves and plant your crops, and the salty seas for the different benefits from the directions.
14:33: And He has subjected to you the sun and the moon, constantly pursuing their courses. That is, in improving the plants and other things that they improve. Constant is the process of something working according to a regular pattern. It was also said: constantly moving in compliance with God's command, and the meaning is that they will continue until the Day of Resurrection without stopping. Its meaning was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And He has subjected to you the night and the day. That is, so that you may rest at night and seek His bounty during the day, as He said: And out of His mercy He has made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty. (al-Qasas 28:73).
14:34: The Almighty said: And He gave you of all that you asked Him for meaning He gave you of every responsible thing that you asked Him for, so it was deleted, according to Al-Akhfash. It was said: The meaning is: And He gave you of everything that you asked Him for, and of everything that you did not ask Him for, so it was deleted, so we did not ask Him for the sun or the moon or many of His blessings that we began with. This is like what He said: Garments to protect you from the heat (al-Nahl 16:81) as will come. It was said: of is redundant, meaning He gave you everything that you asked for. Ibn Abbas, Ad-Dahhak and others read And He gave you of everything with the tanween what you asked for. This reading was narrated from Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak and Qatadah, it is in the negative, meaning from everything that you did not ask for, like the sun, the moon and others. It was said: From everything that you asked Him for, meaning that which you did not ask for. And if you count the favor of God meaning the favors of God. You cannot count them and you cannot enumerate them, and you cannot limit them because of their multitude, such as hearing, sight, straightening the image, and other well-being and provision. Blessings are countless and these blessings are from God, so why would you exchange God’s blessing for disbelief?! Why did you not use them to help you obey?! Indeed, mankind is most unjust and ungrateful Human is a general term and what is meant by it is specific. Ibn Abbas said: He meant Abu Jahl. It was said: All disbelievers.
14:35: The Almighty said: And when Abraham said, 'My Lord, make this city secure' meaning Mecca, and it has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols meaning keep me away from worshipping them, and by his saying: my sons he meant his sons from his loins and they were eight, and none of them worshipped an idol. It was said: It is a supplication for whomever God wanted to supplicate for. Al-Jahdary and Isa read and keep me away with the alif cut off and the meaning is the same, it is said: I kept that matter away, and I kept it away and kept it away from him, so he avoided it and avoided it meaning he left it. And Ibrahim Al-Taymi used to say in his al-Qasas 28:Who is safe from affliction after Al-Khalil when he said: And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols as my father and my people worshipped them.
14:36: The Almighty said: My Lord, indeed they have led astray many of the people. Since they were a cause of misguidance, He attributed the action to them metaphorically, for idols are inanimate and do not act. So whoever follows me in monotheism. Then he is of me meaning of my religion. And whoever disobeys me meaning persists in polytheism. Then you are Forgiving and Merciful. It was said: He said this before God made him know that God does not forgive association with Him. It was also said: Forgiving and Merciful because he repented from his disobedience before death. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: And whoever disobeys me in what is less than polytheism.
14:37: It contains six issues: First: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The first time women used narration was before the mother of Ismail. She used narration to cover her traces on Sarah. Then Ibrahim brought her and her son Ismail while she was breastfeeding him, until he placed them near the House, near a tree above Zamzam at the top of the mosque. There was no one in Mecca at that time, and there was no water there. So he placed them there, and placed near them a bag of dates, and gave him water to drink from it. Then Ibrahim turned and went away, and the mother of Ismail followed him and said: O Ibrahim! Where are you going, leaving us in this valley where there is no people or anything? She said that to him repeatedly, but he did not pay attention to her. She said to him: Did God command you to do this? He said: Yes. She said: Then He will not let us down.
