Then she returned, and Abraham set out until he was at the pass where they could not see him. He faced the House and then supplicated with these supplications, and raised his hands and said: My Lord, indeed I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without cultivation until he reached they give thanks. And the mother of Ismail began to suckle Ismail and drink from that water, until what was in the water skin was used up, she became thirsty and her son became thirsty, and she began to look at him writhing - or he said, floundering - so she set out, hating to look at him, and she found Safa to be the nearest mountain on earth to her, so she stood on it, then she faced the valley to see if she could see anyone, but she did not see anyone, so she descended from Safa until she reached the valley, she raised the edge of her armor, then she walked as a person struggles, then she crossed the valley, then she came to Marwa and stood on it, and she looked to see if she could see anyone, but she did not see anyone, so she did that seven times. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That was the walking of people between them, and when she came to Marwa, she heard a voice. She said: Shhh! meaning herself, then she listened and heard again and said: I have heard if you have help! Then she saw the king at the place of Zamzam, so he searched with his heel - or he said with his wing - until the water appeared, so she began to scoop it up and say with her hand like this, and she began to scoop from the water into her water skin and it would bubble up after she scooped.” Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on the mother of Ismail, if she had left Zamzam - or he said: if she had not scooped from the water - Zamzam would have been a flowing spring.” He said: So she drank and breastfed her son, so the king said to her: Do not fear being lost, for here is the House of God that this boy and his father are building, and God does not forsake His people. And he mentioned the hadith in full. Question: It is not permissible for anyone to rely on this in throwing his son and children in a wasteland, relying on the Almighty, the Most Merciful, and following the action of Abraham, the friend of God, as the extremist Sufis say about the reality of trust, because Abraham did that by the command of God, as he said in the hadith: God commanded you to do this? He said: Yes. It has been narrated that when Sarah became jealous of Hagar after she gave birth to Ishmael, Abraham, peace be upon him, went out with her to Mecca. It has been narrated that he, Hagar, and the child rode Al-Buraq and came in one day from Ash-Sham to the heart of Mecca, and he left his son and his maid there and rode back that same day. All of that was by revelation from God Almighty, and when he turned away, he called upon God in accordance with this verse. Second: When God wanted to establish the situation, prepare the place, and outline the location for the honored house and the sacred country, He sent the angel to search for water and establish it as food. In the correct one. Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, sufficed with it for thirty days and nights. Abu Dharr said: I had no food except Zamzam water, so I became fat until my bones broke, and I did not feel any hunger in my liver, and he mentioned the hadith. Ad-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Zamzam water is for whatever it is drunk for. If you drink it to heal yourself, God will heal you. If you drink it to satiate your hunger, God will satiate your hunger. If you drink it to quench your thirst, God will quench it. It is the defeat of Gabriel and the drink God gave to Ishmael.” It was also narrated on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: When Ibn Abbas drank from Zamzam, he would say: O God, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision, and healing from every illness. Ibn al-Arabi said: This will remain in it until the Day of Resurrection for whoever has a pure intention, a safe heart, does not deny it, and does not drink it to be tested, for God is with those who trust in Him, and He exposes those who test themselves. Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ali al-Tirmidhi said: My father, may God have mercy on him, told me: I entered the circumambulation on a dark night and I was so preoccupied with urine that I started urinating until it hurt me. I was afraid that if I left the mosque I would step on some of those feet. This was during the days of Hajj. So I remembered this hadith, so I entered Zamzam and filled myself with it, and it left me until morning. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr: There is a spring in Zamzam in Paradise, opposite the corner. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And of my descendants. The word of in the Almighty’s saying: of my descendants was ancient, according to what was narrated, before the flood. This meaning has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. He added the verse to it because no one else owns it, and he described it as forbidden, meaning that what is permissible in other places, such as sexual intercourse and making lawful, is forbidden in it. It was said: It is forbidden to tyrants, even if its sanctity is violated and its right is treated lightly. This was said by Qatada and others. This has already been mentioned in Al-Ma’idah. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: Our Lord, that they may establish prayer. He singled it out from the religion because of its virtue in it and its place in it, and it is God’s covenant with His servants. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Five prayers have been prescribed by God for His servants. The hadith. The lam in li-yaqimu al-salah is a lam of ki, this is what appears in it and it is related to -askanat and it is correct for it to be a lam of command, as if he asked God to entrust them and to guide them to establish prayer. Sixth: This verse includes that prayer in Mecca is better than prayer elsewhere, because the meaning of Our Lord, that they may establish prayer is that You have settled them near Your sacred House so that they may establish prayer there. Scholars have differed as to whether prayer in Mecca is better or in the Prophet’s Mosque, may God bless him and grant him peace. Most of the people of hadith have said that prayer in the Sacred Mosque is better than prayer in the Prophet’s Mosque, may God bless him and grant him peace, by one hundred prayers, and they have cited as evidence the hadith of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque except the Sacred Mosque, and a prayer in the Sacred Mosque is better than a prayer in this mosque of mine by one hundred prayers.” Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Omar said: This hadith was attributed to Habib Al-Mu’allim on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, and it is authentic, and he did not mix up its wording or meaning, and he was trustworthy. Ibn Abi Khaithama said: I heard Yahya bin Ma’in say: Habib Al-Mu’allim is trustworthy. Abdullah bin Ahmad mentioned it and said: I heard my father say: Habib Al-Mu’allim is trustworthy. How authentic is his hadith! Abu Zur’ah Al-Razi was asked about Habib Al-Mu’allim, and he said: He is from Basra, trustworthy. I said: - This hadith of Habib al-Mu'allim was narrated by al-Hafiz Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hatim al-Tamimi al-Basti in his Musnad al-Sahih, so the hadith is authentic and it is the proof in the event of dispute or disagreement. Praise be to God. Abu Omar said: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, like the hadith of Ibn al-Zubayr. It was narrated by Musa al-Juhani on the authority of Nafi' on the authority of Ibn Omar, and Musa al-Juhani al-Kufi is trustworthy. Al-Qattan, Ahmad, Yahya and their group praised him. He narrated on the authority of Shu'bah, al-Thawri and Yahya ibn Sa'id. Hakim ibn Sayf narrated, Abdullah ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Ata ibn Abi Rabah, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque except the Sacred Mosque, and a prayer in the Sacred Mosque is better than a hundred thousand in any other mosque." This Hakim bin Saif is a sheikh from the people of Raqqa. Abu Zur’ah al-Razi narrated from him, and Ibn Wadah took from him. They consider him a trustworthy sheikh who is not bad. If he has memorized them, then they are two hadiths. Otherwise, the word of Habib al-Mu’allim is to be accepted. Muhammad bin Wadah narrated: Yusuf bin Adi narrated to us from Umar bin Ubayd from Abdul Malik from Ata’ from Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other mosque except the Sacred Mosque, for prayer in it is better. Abu Umar said: All of this is a clear statement in a matter of disagreement, decisive for those who have been inspired by their right path and are not influenced by their fanaticism. Ibn Habib mentioned from Mutraf and from Asbagh from Ibn Wahb that they both used to prefer prayer in the Sacred Mosque over prayer in the Prophet’s Mosque (blessings and peace of God be upon him) based on what is in this chapter. Malik and all the scholars agreed that the two Eid prayers are to be offered in every country except Makkah, for they are to be offered in the Sacred Mosque. Umar, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Abu Darda and Jabir preferred Mecca and its mosque, and they were more deserving of imitation than those who came after them. This is what Al-Shafi’i held, and it is the opinion of Ata’, the Meccans and Kufians. A similar opinion was narrated from Malik. Ibn Wahb mentioned in his Jami’ from Malik that when Adam, peace be upon him, was sent down to Earth, he said: O Lord, is this the place you would like to be worshipped in? He said: Rather, Mecca. What is well-known from him and the people of Medina is that Medina is preferred. The people of Basra and Baghdad differed on this, with one group saying Mecca, and another group saying Medina. The Almighty says: So make the hearts of the people incline toward them. Hearts is the plural of fu’ad, which means hearts. The heart may also be referred to as fu’ad, as the poet said: A heart that led me with longing for you throughout the long distance is patient It was said: It is the plural of delegation, and the original is awfada, so the fa was brought forward and the waw was changed to a ya as it is, so it is as if he said: And make delegations from the distance that incline towards them, meaning they pull away, it is said: he leaned towards him if he leaned, and the she-camel fell, she fell, she is a hole if she ran a strong gallop as if she was in the air of a well, and his saying: incline towards them is taken from it. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: If he had said the hearts of the people, the Persians, the Romans, the Turks, the Indians, the Jews, the Christians and the Magians would have crowded around him, but he said: of the people so they are the Muslims, so his saying: incline towards them means it yearns for them, and yearns to visit the House. Mujahid read incline towards them meaning it yearns for them and respects them. And provide them with fruits that they may be grateful So God answered his prayer, and caused all the trees to grow for them in Taif, and what is brought to them from the cities. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, there is a long hadith, some of which we have mentioned: “After Ishmael married, Abraham came to look at his estate, but he did not find Ishmael. He asked his wife about him, and she said: He went out seeking for us. Then he asked them about their livelihood and their condition, and she said: We are human beings, we are in hardship and difficulty. So she complained to him. He said: When your husband comes, greet him and tell him to change the threshold of his door. When Ishmael came, it was as if he sensed something, so he said: Has anyone come to you? She said: Yes, an old man of such and such came to us and asked me about you, so I told him. He asked me how we lived, so I told him that we were in difficulty and difficulty. He said: Did he advise you about anything? She said: He ordered me to greet you and tell you to change the threshold of your door. He said: That was my father, and he ordered me to leave you and go back to your family. So he divorced her and married another of them. Abraham stayed away from them for as long as God willed, then he came to them after a while and did not find him. He entered upon his wife and asked her about him, and she said: He went out seeking for us. He said: How are you? He asked her about their livelihood and their condition, and she said: We are well and comfortable, and she praised God. He said: What is your food? She said: Meat. He said: What is your drink? She said: Water. He said: O God, bless them in meat and water. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: They did not have grain at that time, and if they had, he would have prayed for them to do so. He said: No one would be alone with them except in Mecca except that they would not agree with him, and he mentioned the hadith. Ibn Abbas said: The words of Abraham, Then make the hearts of some people yearn toward them he asked that God make people yearn to live in Mecca, so that it would become a sacred house, and all of that happened, praise be to God. The first to live in it were Jurhum. In Bukhari - after his saying: And indeed, God does not forsake His people - the house was elevated from the ground like a hill, and the floods would come to it and take it from its right and from its left, and so on until a group of Jurhum passed by them returning from the road of Kada, so they stopped at the bottom of Mecca, and they saw a bird flying around, so they said: This bird is circling around water! We knew this valley and it did not have water, so they sent a runner or two and they found water, so he informed them of the water and they came. He said: And the mother of Ishmael was at the water, so they said: Do you give us permission to camp with you? She said: Yes, but you have no right to the water. They said: Yes. Ibn Abbas said: And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So he found that the mother of Ishmael loved company, so they camped and sent for their people and they camped with them until there were households of them there, the boy grew up and the mother of Ishmael died, so Abraham came after Ishmael married to look at his inheritance, the hadith.
14:38: The Almighty said: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare. That is, nothing of our conditions is hidden from You. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: You know everything that I conceal and what I declare of my longing for Ishmael and his mother when we settled in a barren valley. And nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven. It was said: This is from the words of Abraham. It was said: This is from the words of God the Almighty when he said to Abraham: Our Lord, indeed You know what we conceal and what we declare. God said: And nothing is hidden from God on earth or in heaven.
14:39: Praise be to God who has granted me in my old age meaning in my old age and the age of my wife. Ibn Abbas said: Ishmael was born to him when he was ninety-nine years old, and Isaac when he was one hundred and twelve years old. Saeed bin Jubair said: Abraham was given the good report of Isaac after one hundred and ten years. Indeed, my Lord is the Hearer of supplication.
14:40: The Almighty said: My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer meaning, one of those who are steadfast in Islam and adhere to its rulings. And from my descendants meaning, make from my descendants those who establish it. Our Lord, and accept my supplication meaning, my worship, as He said: And your Lord says, ‘Call upon Me; I will respond to you’ (Ghafir 40:60). And the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: Supplication is the core of worship and this was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah.
14:41: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers. It was said: Abraham asked forgiveness for his parents before it was proven to him that they were enemies of God. Al-Qushayri said: It is not far-fetched that his mother was a Muslim because God mentioned his excuse for asking forgiveness for his father but not his mother. I said: And this is the reading of Saeed bin Jubair, My Lord, forgive me and my parents, meaning his father. It was said: He asked forgiveness for them in the hope that they would believe. It was also said: He asked forgiveness for them on the condition that they would become Muslims. It was also said: He meant Adam and Eve. It was narrated that if a servant says: O God, forgive me and my parents, and his parents had died as disbelievers, then forgiveness will be granted to Adam and Eve because they are the parents of all creation. It was also said: He meant his two sons, Ishmael and Isaac. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i used to read: And for my two sons, meaning his two sons, and Yahya bin Ya’mar read this as well, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi and Al-Nahhas. And for the believers, Ibn Abbas said: From the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was also said: For the believers all of them, and this is more apparent. The Day the Reckoning is established, meaning the Day when people stand for the reckoning.
14:42: The Almighty said: And never think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. This is a consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after he was amazed by the actions of the polytheists and their opposition to the religion of Abraham, meaning, be patient as Abraham was patient, and inform the polytheists that delaying the punishment is not to please them, but rather it is God's way to give the disobedient a period of time. Maymun ibn Mihran said: This is a threat to the oppressor and a consolation to the oppressed. He only delays them means the polytheists of Mecca, He gives them a respite and delays their punishment. The common reading is yu'akhirhum with a ya' and Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it for His statement: And never think that God. Al-Hasan and Al-Salami read, and it was narrated from Abu Amr also nu'akhirhum with a noon for emphasis. For a Day when eyes will stare in horror meaning they will not close from the horror of what they see on that day, as Al-Farra' said. It is said: a man's eyes stare and the eyes stare in horror, meaning they are raised and ascend from the horror of what they see. Ibn Abbas said: On that day, the eyes of the creatures will stare into the air out of extreme confusion, and they will not blink.
14:43: Muhta'een means rushing, as stated by Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Saeed bin Jubayr. It is derived from the verb ahta'a yahta'a ehta'an, meaning to hasten. And from this is the saying of God Almighty: Muhta'een ila al-Da'i The Caller (al-Qamar 54:8), meaning rushing. The poet said: Their home is in the Tigris, and I saw them rushing to the Tigris to listen. It was said: Al-Muhta'een are those who look at that with humility, meaning looking without blinking, said Ibn Abbas. Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said: Muhta'een means looking for a long time. An-Nahhas said: It is known in the language that it is said: Ahta'a if he hastens, Abu Ubaid said: Both meanings may be used together, meaning to hasten while continuing to look. Ibn Zayd said: Al-Muhta'een is the one who does not raise his head. Muqni'i ra'suhum means raising their heads, looking at that. And iqna' al-ra's is raising it, said Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. Ibn Arafa, Al-Qutbi and others said: Al-Muqni' is the one who raises his head and directs his gaze to what is in front of him, and from it is iqna' in prayer and iqna' his voice if he raises it. Al-Hasan said: The faces of the people on that day will be towards the sky, no one will look at anyone. It was said: Nakis their heads, Al-Mahdawi said: It is said iqna' if he raises his head, and iqna' if he lowers his head in humility and submission, and the verse is open to both meanings, said Al-Mubarrad, and the first saying is better known in the language, said Al-Rajjaz: He lowered his head towards me and looked at me as if he had seen something greedy. Al-Shamakh said, describing camels: They attack the bitches with their molars covered like a falling camel. Meaning: with heads raised to it to take them. And from this it was said: veiled for its height. And from this the man qana’ if he is satisfied, meaning he raised his head from the question. And qana’ if he asked, meaning he came with what he could veil himself from, about copper. And the mouth of qana’ means his teeth are bent inward. And a man qana’ with emphasis, meaning he has an egg on him, said Al-Jawhari. Their glance does not return to them meaning their eyes do not return to them from the intensity of the look, so they are staring. It is said: A man’s glance is a glance if he closes his eyelid to the other, so the look is called a glance because it is through it. And the path is the eye. Antara said: I lower my gaze as long as my neighbor appears to me, until my neighbor hides her shelter. Jamil said: I shorten my limbs without a camel, out of respect for a camel and for the limb that I am short of. And their hearts are empty meaning they are of no use due to the intensity of fear. Ibn Abbas: Empty of all good. Al-Suddi: Their hearts came out of their chests and stuck in their throats. Mujahid, Marra, and Ibn Zayd said: Empty, ruined, and torn apart, with no good or reason in them, like what you say about a house that has nothing in it: It is only air. Ibn Abbas said the same. Air in the language means hollow and empty, and from it is the saying of Hassan: Tell Abu Sufyan about me, for you are hollow and empty of air Zuhair said, describing a camel with a small head: As if the man was on a mountain of darkness, his forehead was covered with air Empty, meaning empty. In the Qur’an: And the heart of Moses’ mother became empty (al-Qasas 28:10), meaning from everything except the concern of Moses. It was said: There is an implication in the speech, meaning empty and empty.
14:44: The Almighty said: And warn the people Ibn Abbas said: He meant the people of Mecca. On the Day when the punishment will come to them which is the Day of Resurrection, meaning frighten them on that day. And He only mentioned the Day of Punishment for them even though it is the Day of Reward, because the speech was uttered as a threat to the sinner. Then those who did wrong will say that is on that day Our Lord, give us respite that is, give us respite. For a near term they asked Him to return to the world when the truth appeared in the Hereafter. We will answer Your call that is, to Islam. And we will follow the messengers. They will be answered: Did you not swear before that is, in the worldly abode. You will not perish Mujahid said: It is the oath of the Quraysh that they will not be resurrected. Ibn Jurayj: It is what he narrated from them in His statement: And they swore by God their most solemn oaths that God will not resurrect anyone who dies (al-Nahl 16:38). You will not pass away has two interpretations: One of them is that you will not move from this world to the Hereafter, meaning you will not be resurrected or gathered together. This is the opinion of Mujahid. The second is that you will not pass away meaning you will not be punished. Al-Bayhaqi reported on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: The people of Hell will have five supplications, and God will answer them in four of them. When it is the fifth, they will never speak again. They will say: "Our Lord, You caused us to die twice and brought us to life twice. So we acknowledge our sins, so is there any way out?" (Ghafir 40:11). Then God will answer them, "That is because when God alone is called upon, you disbelieve; but if partners are associated with Him, you believe. So the judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Grand." (Ghafir 40:12). Then they will say: “Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will do righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain.” (al-Sajdah 32:12) God Almighty will answer them: “So taste [the punishment] for having forgotten the meeting of this Day of yours. Indeed, We have forgotten you. And taste the punishment of eternity for what you used to do.” (al-Sajdah 32:14) Then they will say: Our Lord, delay us for a near term; we will answer Your call and follow the messengers. God Almighty will answer them: Did you not swear before that you would not perish? (Ibrahim 14:44) Then they will say: Our Lord, bring us out; we will do righteousness other than what we used to do? (Fatir 35:37) God Almighty will answer them: Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember, and a warner came to you? So taste [it]; for there is no helper for the wrongdoers. (Fatir 35:37) And they will say: Our Lord, our misery has overcome us, and we were a people astray (al-Mu’minun 23:106). So God Almighty will answer them: Be gone into it, disgraced and do not speak (al-Mu’minun 23:108). So they will never speak after that. Ibn Al-Mubarak included it in his Raqa’iq at a longer length than this - and we have written it in the book Al-Tadhkirah - and he added to the hadith: “And you will dwell in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it will become clear to you how We dealt with them, and We have presented to you examples. And they plotted their plot, and with God is their plot, although their plot was such that mountains would move.” He said this the third time, and he mentioned the hadith and added after his saying: Be gone into it, disgraced and do not speak (al-Mu’minun 23:108). At that point, the supplication and hope stopped, and some of them turned to others, barking in the face of one another, and they were overwhelmed. He said: Al-Azhar bin Abi Al-Azhar told me that he mentioned to him that that was His saying: This is a Day on which they will not speak, nor will permission be given to them to make excuses (al-Mursalat 77:35-36).
14:45: The Almighty said: And you dwelt in the dwellings of those who wronged themselves, and it became clear to you how We dealt with them and We presented to you examples. That is, in the land of Thamud and the like. So why don't you consider their dwellings, after it became clear to you what We did to them, and after We presented to you examples in the Qur'an. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read and We will make clear to you with a noon and the jussive, as if it is a future tense and its meaning is the past, and to suit His statement: how We dealt with them. The reading of the group is and it becomes clear, and it is similar in meaning, because that will not become clear to them except by God making it clear to them.
14:46: The Almighty said: And they plotted their plot meaning by associating partners with God, denying the Messengers, and being stubborn, according to Ibn Abbas and others. And with God is their plot, even though their plot was such that mountains would move from it In means what, meaning their plot was such that mountains would not move from it due to its weakness and frailty, And means what in the Qur'an in five places: One of them is this. The second - So if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you (Yunus 10:94). The third - If We had intended to take a diversion, We would have taken it from Ourself, if We were (al-Anbiya 21:17), meaning we were not. The fourth - Say, 'If the Most Gracious had a son' (al-Zukhruf 43:81). The fifth: And We have certainly established them in that in which We have established you (al-Ahqaf 46:26). The group read And if it was with a noon. Amr ibn Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, and Abi read And if it was akad with a dal. The general opinion is that the lam in letzul is broken because it is the lam of the limits and the second lam is opened in the accusative case. Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Jurayj and Al-Kisa’i read to be removed with the first lam open as if it were the lam of initiation and the second raised and lightened from the heavy one, and the meaning of this reading is the enormity of their plot, meaning, and their plot was so great that the mountains almost moved because of it, Al-Tabari said: The preferred reading is the first reading, because if it had moved it would not have been established, Abu Al-Anbari said: There is no proof against the Mushaf of the Muslims in the hadith that Ahmad bin Al-Hussein told us: Uthman bin Abi Shaybah told us, Waki’ bin Al-Jarrah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Danil, who said: I heard Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, say: A tyrant among the tyrants said, I will not stop until I know who is in the heavens, so he went to the chicks of eagles and ordered that they be fed meat, until they grew strong and muscular and hastened, he ordered that a coffin be made in which two men could fit, and that a stick be placed in it with very red meat on its head, and that the legs of the eagles be secured with pegs, and they be tied to the pillars of the coffin, then he and a companion of his sat in the coffin and stirred up the eagles, so when they saw The meat I asked for, so I started raising the coffin until I reached what God willed, then the tyrant said to his companion: Open the door and see what you see? He said: I see the mountains as if they were flies, so he said: Close the door, then I ascended with the coffin as God willed it to ascend, then the tyrant said to his companion: Open the door and see what you see? He said: I see nothing but the sky and it only increases from us in distance, so he said: He turned the staff upside down, so the eagles swooped down. When the coffin fell to the ground, I heard a crash from it that almost moved the mountains from their ranks, he said: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, recite And indeed their plot was bound to vanish with the first lam of to vanish open and the second dammah. Al-Tha'labi mentioned this story with its meaning, and that the tyrant is Nimrod who argued with Abraham about his Lord, and Ikrimah said: There was with him in the coffin a beardless boy, and he carried the bow and arrows and shot them and came back covered in blood and said: You have spared yourself from the God of the heavens. Akrima said: It was stained with the blood of a fish from the sky, and it threw itself into a sea suspended in the air. It was also said: A bird was hit by an arrow, then Nimrod ordered his companion to strike the stick and to turn the meat, so the eagles descended with the ark. The mountains heard the rustling of the ark and the eagles were frightened, and thought that something had happened to them from the sky, and that the Hour had come. So is that what He said: And if their plot had been such that the mountains would have moved away? Al-Qushayri said: This is permissible, given the estimation of the creation of life in the mountains. Al-Mawardi mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Nimrod bin Kanaan built the palace in the village of Al-Rass in the plains of Kufa, and made its length five thousand and fifty cubits, and its width three thousand and twenty-five cubits, and he ascended from it with the eagles, and when he knew that he had no way to the sky, he made it a fortress, and gathered his family and children to fortify himself in it, but God destroyed his building from the foundations, and the palace collapsed on them and they all perished. This is the meaning of And they plotted their plot against God and regarding the mountains that he meant to be removed by their plot, there are two aspects: One of them is the mountains of the earth. The second is Islam and the Qur’an, because it is firm and solid like mountains. Al-Qushayri said: And with God is their plot meaning He knows that and will punish them, or with God is the reward for their plot, so the complement was omitted. And if their plot was to remove mountains with a kasra on the lam, meaning that their plot was a plot that would have an effect and danger with God Almighty, so the mountains are an example of the command of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: And if their plot was in their estimation to move mountains from it and to have an effect in invalidating Islam. It was read to move mountains from it with the first lam open and the second damma, meaning it was a great plot from which mountains would move, but God protected the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is like the saying of God Almighty: And they plotted a great plot (Nuh 71:22) and mountains do not move, but the expression about the greatness of something is like this.
14:47: The Almighty’s saying: So do not think that God will fail to fulfill His promise to His messengers. The name of God Almighty and failure are the objects of think, and His messengers are the objects of His promise, which is broad, and the meaning is: He will fail to fulfill His promise to His messengers. The poet said: You see the bull in it, its head and the rest of it are exposed to the sun. Al-Qutbi said: It is from the advanced which is clarified by the delay, and the delayed which is clarified by the advancement, and it is the same in your saying: Mukhalaf wa’dahu rusuluhu, and Mukhalaf rusuluhu wa’dahu. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Possessor of Retribution, meaning from His enemies. And among His names is al-Muntaqim, and we have explained it in the Most Sublime Book in Explaining the Beautiful Names of God.
14:48: The Almighty said: The Day the earth will be replaced with another earth meaning, mention the Day the earth will be replaced, so it will be related to what came before it. It was said: It is a description of His saying: The Day the reckoning will be established. There is a difference of opinion about how the earth will be replaced. Many people said: The replacement of the earth is an expression of the change in its characteristics, the leveling of its hills, the blowing away of its mountains, and the spreading out of its land. It was narrated by Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, and it was included by Ibn Majah in his Sunan, and Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned it from the hadith of Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Ibn Abbas told me: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be spread out as a hide is spread out, and its width will be increased by such and such, and he mentioned the hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The earth will be replaced by another earth, and He will spread it out and extend it like the spreading of a rough hide. You will not see any crookedness or unevenness in it. Then God will warn the creation with a warning, and in the second place they will be in the same places as the first. Whoever was in its belly will be in its belly, and whoever was on its back will be on its back.” This was mentioned by Al-Ghaznawi. The changing of the sky will be the rolling up of its sun and moon, and the scattering of its stars, as stated by Ibn Abbas. It was also said: its conditions will differ, sometimes like molten metal and sometimes like oil, as narrated by Ibn Al-Anbari. We have already mentioned this chapter clearly in the Book of Remembrance, and we have mentioned what the scholars have said about it, and that the correct view is that this earth will be removed according to what has been proven from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muslim narrated on the authority of Thawban, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “I was standing with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a Jewish rabbi came to him and said: ‘Peace be upon you.’ He mentioned the hadith, in which it says: ‘The Jew said: Where will the people be on the Day when the earth is changed to another earth and the heavens as well?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘In the darkness beyond the bridge.’” He mentioned the hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about His statement: ‘On the Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well], where will the people be on that Day?’ He said: ‘On the Bridge.’” It was narrated by Ibn Majah with the same chain of transmission as Muslim, and by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Aisha that she was the questioner. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. These hadiths state that the heavens and the earth will be replaced and removed, and God will create another earth for the people to be on after they were on the Bridge. In Sahih Muslim, it was narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection on a white, pure land like a pure loaf of bread, in which no one has knowledge.’” Jabir said: I asked Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali about the statement of God, the Almighty: ‘On the Day when the earth will be replaced by another earth.’ He said: It will be replaced by a loaf of bread from which the creation will eat on the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: ‘And We did not make them bodies that did not eat food.’ (Al-Anbiya’: 8). Ibn Mas’ud said: It will be replaced by another earth, white like silver, on which no sin was committed. Ibn Abbas said: It will be replaced by a land of silver. White. And Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: On that day, the earth will be replaced with silver and the sky with gold. This is a replacement for the eye, and that is enough for you. And they will emerge before God, the One, the Prevailing, meaning from their graves, and this has been mentioned before.
14:49: The Almighty said: And you will see the criminals who are the polytheists. On that Day meaning the Day of Resurrection. Binded together meaning bound in shackles which are the chains and fetters, the singular of which is safad and safad. It is said: I safadtuhu safadan meaning I bound him, and the noun is safad, so if you want to make it more numerous you say: I safadtuhu safadan. Amr ibn Kulthum said: They returned with the loot and the captives, and our sons with the kings in chains. Our chained ones. Hassan said: Every prisoner is chained up by a falcon that, when faced with calamity, will be victorious. That is, I fettered him, and I gave him shackles. It was said: I fettered him and I gave him shackles, both of which are used in the chain and the giving. Al-Nabigha said: I did not show up, I swear to God The chain is the gift, because it binds and enslaves. Abu al-Tayyib said: I bound myself to your arms out of love, and whoever finds kindness as a bond will be bound. It was said: Every infidel is paired with a devil in chains. This is explained by His statement: Gather together those who did wrong and their companions (al-Saffat 37:22), meaning their companions from the devil. It was also said: They are the infidels who are gathered together in chains just as they were gathered together in this world for sins.
14:50: Their garments are of tar meaning their shirts, according to Ibn Duraid and others. The singular form is sirbal, and the verb is tarbalat and sarbalat ghayri. Ka'b ibn Malik said: They meet you with a nerve around the Prophet, who has garments woven by David in battle. From tar meaning the tar of camels that they enjoy, said Al-Hasan. This is more eloquent because of the fire burning in them. In the Sahih: If the mourning woman does not repent before her death, she will be raised on the Day of Resurrection wearing a garment of tar and a coat of scabies. It was narrated on the authority of Hammad that they said: It is copper. Isa bin Omar read: tar with the qaf open and the ta’ silent. There is a third reading: with the qaf broken and the ta’ jazm, and from this is the saying of Abu Al-Najm: John, as if the sweat had covered him with tar and sackcloth. A fourth reading: from qatrān narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah, Ikrimah, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, and Ya`qub. Qatr is molten copper and brass, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: Bring me molten copper (al-Kahf 18:96). And now: that which has reached its heat, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: And between scalding water (Al-Rahman: 44). And the fire will cover (i.e. strike) their faces and cover them.
14:51: That God may reward every soul for what it has earned. That is, for what it has earned. Indeed, God is swift in account. This has been mentioned above.
14:52: The Almighty said: This is a message for mankind meaning this that We have revealed to you is a message, meaning a message and a sermon. And that they may warn with it meaning that they may fear the punishment of God Almighty, and it was read. And that they may warn with the opening of the ya and the dhal, it is said: I vowed to warn with something if you knew about it and prepared for it, and they did not use a source from it as they did not use from 'asa and laysa, and it is as if they dispensed with an and the verb like your saying: I was pleased that I vowed with something. And that they may know that He is only one God meaning and that they may know the oneness of God through what He established of arguments and proofs. And that those of understanding may remember meaning and that those of reason may be admonished. These lams in and that they may warn, and that they may know, and that they may remember are related to something omitted, the estimate: and for this reason We revealed it. Yaman bin Ri'ab narrated that this verse was revealed about Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him. Some of them were asked: Does the Book of God have a title? He said: Yes. It was said: Even if it is? He said: The Almighty’s saying: This is a message to mankind and that they may be warned thereby to the end. The interpretation of Surah Ibrahim, peace be upon him, has been completed, and praise be to God.
15:1: Its meaning was presented. And the Book it was said about it: It is a name for the type of books that preceded it from the Torah and the Gospel, then he linked them to the clear Book. And it was said: The Book is the Qur’an, combining the two names for it.
15:2: Rabb does not enter the verb, but if ma is added to it, it prepares it to enter the verb. You say: perhaps Zayd stood up, perhaps Zayd stands up. It is possible for ma to be indefinite meaning something, and yudd to be an attribute of it, meaning perhaps something yudd the disbeliever. Nafi and Asim read rabb with a light ba. The rest read it with a shaddah, and they are two dialects. Abu Hatim said: The people of Hijaz lighten rabb. The poet said: Maybe a blow with a polished sword between Basra and a stab from Najla Tamim, Qais and Rabi’ah use it heavily. It has been reported that: perhaps and perhaps, and perhaps and perhaps, with the ba’ being lightened and also with the ba’ being stressed. Its origin is that it is used for little and it may be used for much, meaning that the infidels often wish that they were Muslims, as the Kufians said. And from this is the saying of the poet: Perhaps the eye has given you a glance that is the most complete of all, but it is of no use to you. Some of them said: It is for belittling in this place, because they said that in some places but not in all, because they were preoccupied with the punishment, and God knows best. He said: Perhaps he will wish and it is only for what happened, because the promise is true as if it had happened clearly. At-Tabarani Abu al-Qasim narrated from the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Some people from my nation will enter the Fire because of their sins and will be in the Fire as long as God wills them to be, then the polytheists will taunt them and say: We do not see that what you used to oppose us in, of your belief and faith, has benefited you. So there will not remain a monotheist except that God will take him out of the Fire.” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish that they were Muslims. Al-Hasan said: When the polytheists see the Muslims who have entered Paradise and their abode is in the Fire, they will wish that they were Muslims. Ad-Dahhak said: This wish is only when they see it in this world when guidance is made clear to them from misguidance. It was said: On the Day of Resurrection when they see the honor of the believers and that of the disbelievers.
15:3: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves is a threat to them. And let hope distract them means it preoccupies them from obedience. It is said: He distracted him from such-and-such meaning he occupied him. And he distracted means he is distracted from something. Then they will know when they see the Resurrection and taste the consequences of what they did. This verse was abrogated by the sword. Second: In Musnad Al-Bazzar, on the authority of Anas, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Four things are misery: dullness of the eye, hardness of the heart, long hope, and greed for the worldly life.” Long hope is an incurable disease and a chronic illness. When it takes hold of the heart, its temperament becomes corrupt and its treatment becomes difficult. No disease leaves it and no medicine is effective for it. Rather, it exhausts doctors and makes wise men and scholars despair of its cure. The reality of hope is greed for the worldly life and devotion to it, love for it, and turning away from the Hereafter. It was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The first of this nation was saved by certainty and asceticism, and its last will perish by miserliness and hope. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, that he stood on the steps of the mosque of Damascus and said: O people of Damascus, will you not listen to your sincere brother? Those who came before you used to gather much, build lofty buildings, and hope far away, but their gatherings became waste, their buildings became graves, and their hopes became delusions. These are the people of Ad who have filled the country with people, money, horses and men. So whoever will buy from me today, I have left them for two dirhams! And he recited: O you who has hopes, even if they are far from you, and claims to have attained the farthest of them How can you achieve what you hope for when you are no longer confident of achieving even the smallest of things? Al-Hasan said: A servant who prolongs hope will do bad deeds. And he spoke the truth, may God be pleased with him! Hope makes one lazy in work, leads to laziness and indolence, leads to preoccupation and idleness, and leads to attachment to the earth and inclination towards desires. This is something that has been seen with the naked eye, so it does not need explanation, nor does its owner seek proof. Just as short-lived hope motivates one to work, leads to initiative, and urges one to compete.
15:4: That is, a temporary term written for them in the Preserved Tablet.
15:5: from is a relative clause, as in saying: No one came to me. That is, it does not exceed its term, nor does it precede it. Similar to this is the saying of God Almighty: And when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it. (al-A’raf 7:34).
15:6: The infidels of Quraysh said this to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mockery, and then they asked him to bring the angels to prove his truthfulness.
15:7: And law ma is an incitement to the verb kulula and hala. Al-Farra' said: The m in law ma is a substitute for the lām in lawla. And similarly, he took control of something and was overwhelmed by it, and similarly, he khalmathu and khallatahu, so he is my friend and my companion, meaning my friend. Based on this, law ma can be used in the sense of report, so you say: If Zaid had not hit Amr. Al-Kisa'i said: Lawla and lawma are the same in report and interrogation. Ibn Muqbil said: If it weren't for modesty and religion, I would have blamed you for some of what is in you, since you blamed my nakedness. He wants to say, If it weren’t for shame. People have said, loma, “lawla,” and hala are one and the same. Linguists have recited the following about this: You consider the sterility of the camel to be your greatest glory, Bani Dhutri, if it were not for the masked Kumi. Do you consider the convincing quantity?
15:8: Hafs, Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read We do not send down the angels except with the truth and Abu Ubaid chose it. Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal read the angels do not descend, the rest the angels do not descend and its meaning is: what they descend with two ta's, one of which was deleted for ease, and Al-Bazzi stressed the ta', and Abu Hatim chose it based on his saying: The angels and the Spirit descend (al-Qadr 97:4). The meaning of except with the truth is except with the Qur'an. It was said with the message, according to Mujahid. Al-Hasan said: except with the punishment if they do not believe. And they would not then be given respite meaning if the angels had descended to destroy them, they would not have been given respite nor would their repentance have been accepted. It was said: the meaning is if the angels had descended to bear witness for you, then they would have disbelieved after that for those who were given respite. The origin of if is because - and its meaning is then - so they added to it that, and they found the hamza heavy so they deleted it.
15:9: The Almighty said: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur'an meaning the Qur'an. And indeed, We will be its guardian from anything being added to it or taken away from it. Qatada and Thabit al-Bunani said: God protected it from the devils adding falsehood to it or taking away truth from it, so He, glory be to Him, took charge of its preservation and it has remained preserved. And He said in other verses: Because they were entrusted with preservation (al-Ma’idah 5:44), so He entrusted its preservation to them, so they changed and altered. Sheikh, jurist, imam Abu al-Qasim Abdullah informed us on the authority of his father, Sheikh, jurist, imam, and hadith scholar Abu al-Hasan Ali bin Khalaf bin Ma’zouz al-Komi al-Tilimsani, who said: It was recited to the learned sheikha, Fakhr al-Nisa, Shahada bint Abi Nasr Ahmad bin al-Faraj al-Daynuri, at her home in Dar al-Salam at the end of Jumada al-Akhira in the year 564 AH. It was said to her: The venerable, active sheikh, the leader of leaders, Abu al-Fawaris Tarrad bin Muhammad al-Zainabi, told you that it was recited to you and you were listening in the year 490 AH. Ali bin Abdullah bin Ibrahim informed us. Abu Ali Isa bin Muhammad bin Ahmad bin Umar bin Abdul Malik bin Abdul Aziz bin Jurayj, known as al-Tumari, informed us. Al-Husayn bin Fahm said: I heard Yahya bin Aktham say: Al-Ma’mun - who was the emir at that time - had a session to consider, and a Jewish man with handsome clothes, handsome face, and pleasant scent entered among the people. He said: He spoke and spoke well and expressed himself well. He said: When the session ended, al-Ma’mun called him and said: An Israelite? He said: Yes. He said to him: Convert to Islam so that I may do and do with you, and he promised him. He said: My religion and the religion of my fathers! And he left. He said: After a year, he came to us as a Muslim. He said: He spoke about jurisprudence and spoke well. When the meeting ended, Al-Ma'mun called him and said: Were you not our companion from yesterday? He said to him: Yes. He said: What was the reason for your conversion to Islam? He said: I left your presence and wanted to test these religions, and you see that I have good handwriting, so I went to the Torah and wrote three copies, adding and subtracting from them, and I brought them into the church and they bought them from me. I went to the Gospel and wrote three copies, adding and subtracting from them, and I brought them into the church and they bought them from me. I went to the Qur'an and made three copies, adding and subtracting from them, and I brought them to the copyists to look through them. When they found additions and subtractions in them, they threw them away and did not buy them. I knew that this was a preserved book, and this was the reason for my conversion to Islam. Yahya bin Aktham said: So I performed Hajj that year and met Sufyan bin Uyaynah and mentioned the story to him. He said to me: The proof of this is in the Book of God, the Almighty. I said: In what place? He said: In the words of God, the Blessed and Exalted, in the Torah and the Gospel: Because of what they were entrusted with of the Book of God (al-Ma’idah 5:44). He left its preservation to them and it was lost. And God, the Almighty, said: Indeed, it is We who sent down the Qur’an and indeed, We will be its guardian. So God, the Almighty, preserved it for us and it was not lost. And it was said: And indeed, We will be its guardian, meaning for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from being falsely attributed to us or us being falsely attributed to him. Or Indeed, We will be its guardian from being nearly killed. Similar to it is: And God will protect you from the people (al-Ma’idah 5:67). And We may be in the nominative case as a subject and We sent down is the predicate. The sentence is the predicate of indeed. It is possible that we is an emphasis on the noun that in the accusative case, and it is not a separator because what follows it is not a definite noun but rather a sentence, and sentences are attributes of indefinite nouns, so their rule is the rule of indefinite nouns.
15:10: Meaning: And We have sent messengers before you, so it was deleted. And Shia is the plural of Shia, which is the nation, meaning among their nations, as Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said. Al-Hasan: Among their groups. And Shia is the group and sect of people who are united and in agreement. So Shia is the sect, and from it is the saying of God the Almighty: Or He may confuse you into sects (Al-An'am: 65). Its origin is taken from Shia, which is the small firewood that is used to light the big ones - as mentioned previously in Al-An'am. Al-Kalbi said: The Shia here are the villages.
15:11: Consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that just as these polytheists did to you, so too did they do to the messengers who came before you.
15:12: The Almighty said: Thus do We cause it to enter meaning misguidance, disbelief, mockery and polytheism. Into the hearts of the criminals of your people, according to Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others. That is, just as We caused it to enter into the hearts of those who came before from the sects of the first ones, so do We cause it to enter into the hearts of the polytheists of your people so that they will not believe in you, just as those before them did not believe in their messengers. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: We cause it to enter denial. And the path is to insert something into something like inserting a thread into a needle. It is said: he made it enter, he made it enter, he made it enter, and the thing into something else is like it, and the thing is like that, and the spear, and the thread in the substance, all of them are actions and actions. Adi bin Zaid said: They took you on a difficult day The silk with a kasra is the thread. This verse is a response to the Qadarites and the Mu'tazilites. It was said: The meaning is that we thread the Qur'an into their hearts so they deny it. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and Qatadah said the opinion that most of the commentators agree with, and it is the most binding argument against the Mu'tazilites. Al-Hasan also said: We thread the remembrance to bind the argument, as mentioned by Al-Ghaznawi.
15:13: And the way of the ancients has passed meaning that the way of God has passed with the destruction of the disbelievers, so how close these people are to destruction. It was said: The way of the ancients has passed with what these people did of denial and disbelief, so they are following their example.
15:14: It is said: He kept doing such and such, meaning he did it during the day. The source is shadows. That is, if they were answered with the verses they suggested, they would persist in disbelief and make excuses with illusions, as they said about the miraculous Qur’an: It is magic. They ascend from to ascend. And the ascents are the elevators. That is, if they ascended to the heavens and saw the kingdom and the angels, they would persist in disbelief, according to Al-Hasan and others. It was said: The pronoun in upon them refers to the polytheists. And in they remained refers to the angels, they go and come. That is, if it were revealed to these people so that they could see doors in the heavens through which the angels ascend and descend, they would say: We saw with our eyes what has no reality, according to Ibn Abbas and Qatadah.
15:15: The meaning of sakrat is to be blocked by magic, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak. Al-Hasan said: I was bewitched. Al-Kalbi: Our eyes were covered, and also from him: I was blinded. Qatada: I was taken. The historian said: It was dizzy with us from the spinning, meaning our eyes became intoxicated. Juwaybir: I was deceived. Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala said: sakrat I was covered and covered. And from it the saying of the poet: The sun rose with a helmet on it and made the eyes of the heat intoxicate Mujahed said: Sakrat was imprisoned. And from this is the saying of Aws bin Hajar: So I spent a sleepless night, neither awake nor drunk I said: These are similar sayings that are gathered by your saying: Man'at. Ibn Aziz said: Sakarat absarana blocked our sight, it is from your saying: Sakarta al-Nahr if you blocked it. It is said: It is from the drunkenness of drink, as if the eye is affected by what affects the drinker when he is drunk. Ibn Kathir read Sakarat with a light pronunciation. The rest read with a heavy pronunciation. Ibn al-A'rabi said: Sakarta was filled. Al-Mahdawi said: The lightening and the heavy pronunciation in Sakarat are apparent, the heavy pronunciation is for multiplication and the lightening conveys its meaning. It is known that Sakarat is intransitive. Abu Ali said: It is possible that hearing is transitive in sight. And whoever reads Sakarat then he likened what happened to their sight to the state of the drunk, as if it ran the course of the drunk due to not attaining it. It has been said: It is with a light pronunciation from the drunkenness of drink, and with a heavy pronunciation it was taken, Al-Mawardi mentioned them. Al-Nahhas said: What is known from the reading of Mujahid and Al-Hasan is Sakarat with a light pronunciation. Al-Hasan said: That is, it bewitched. Abu Ubaid narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah that it is said: They were covered by smoke if they were covered by smoke so that they could not see. Al-Farra’ said: Whoever recites sakarat takes it from the sukoon of the wind. An-Nahhas said: “These sayings are similar. The origin of them is what Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ may God have mercy on him said: It is from being drunk in a drink. This is a good saying, meaning that what covered their sight covered them, just as a drunk person is covered by what covers his mind. The sukoon of the wind is its stillness and lethargy, so it goes back to the meaning of bewilderment.”
15:16: When He mentioned the disbelief of the disbelievers and the inability of their idols, He mentioned the perfection of His power to prove His Oneness. The zodiac signs are the palaces and mansions. Ibn Abbas said: That is, We made in the sky the zodiac signs of the sun and the moon, that is, their mansions. The names of these zodiac signs are: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, and Pisces. The Arabs consider knowledge of the positions of the stars and their gates to be one of the most important sciences, and they use them to prove roads, times, fertility, and drought. They said: The universe is twelve zodiac signs, each sign is one and a half declinations. The origin of the zodiac signs is appearance, and from it a woman displays her adornment. This meaning was mentioned previously in Women. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: The zodiac signs are the stars, and they were named thus because of their appearance and height. It was said: The great planets, said Abu Saleh, meaning the seven moving ones. Some people said: zodiac signs, that is, palaces and houses in which there are guards, created by God in the sky. And God knows best. And its adornment means the sky, as He said in Surat al-Mulk 67:And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps (al-Mulk 67:5). For those who observe means those who consider and reflect.
15:17: That is, stoned. Stoning is throwing stones. It has been said that stoning is cursing and expulsion. This has been mentioned before. Al-Kisa'i said: Every cursed thing in the Qur'an means cursing. Al-Kalbi claimed that all the heavens were not protected from the devils until the time of Jesus, so when God Almighty sent Jesus, He protected three heavens from them until the mission of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He protected all of them after his mission and guarded them from them with meteors. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said the same. Ibn Abbas said: The devils were not prevented from the heavens, so they would enter them and tell their report to the soothsayers, adding nine to them and telling them to the people of the earth, the word is true and the nine is false, so if they saw something of what they said, they believed them in what they came with, so when Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon them, was born, they were prevented from three heavens, and when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was born, they were prevented from all the heavens, so none of them wanted to eavesdrop except that he was pelted with a meteor, as will come.
15:18: That is, but whoever eavesdrops, that is, a small snatch, then it is a disconnected exception. It was said that it is connected, that is, except for whoever eavesdrops. That is, We have preserved the heaven from the devils from hearing anything of the revelation or other things, except for whoever eavesdrops, for We have not preserved it from hearing report from the heavens other than the revelation. As for the revelation, then it does not hear anything from it, due to His statement: Indeed, they are removed from hearing (Ash-Shu'ara: 212). And if the devils listen to something that is not revelation, then they throw it to the priests faster than the blink of an eye, then meteors follow them and kill them or confuse them, as mentioned by Al-Hasan and Ibn Abbas. The statement of God the Almighty: Then a clear meteor pursued him pursued him: caught up with him and overtook him. A meteor: a shining planet. And also a piercing meteor. And His statement: with a blazing meteor (al-Naml 27:7) with a flame of fire on the head of a stick, as Ibn Uzair said. And Dhu ar-Rummah said: As if he were a planet following a poisoned demon in the blackness of the night The planet was called a meteor because of its brilliance, which resembles fire. It was said: A meteor is a flame of fire, a spark for the people of the earth, burning them and not returning if it burns, just as if fire burns it does not return, unlike a planet, which if it burns, returns to its place. Ibn Abbas said: The devils ascend in groups, eavesdropping, and the rebellious one among them is isolated and rises, and the meteor is thrown, and it hits his forehead or nose or whatever he wants, and it ignites, and his companions come while it is ignited and he says: It was such and such, so those people go to their brothers among the priests and add nine to it, and they tell the people of the earth about it, the word is true and the nine is false. So when they see something of what they said, they believe them in all the lies they brought. This meaning will come in the raised form in Surah Saba, God willing. There is a difference of opinion about the meteor, whether it is to be killed or not. Ibn Abbas said: The meteor wounds, burns and incapacitates, but it does not kill. Al-Hasan and a group said: It is to be killed. Based on this opinion, there are two opinions about killing them with meteors before they transmit what they have eavesdropped on to the jinn: The first is that they are killed before transmitting what they have eavesdropped on to others, so based on this, report from heaven does not reach anyone other than the prophets, and therefore divination has been cut off. The second is that they are killed after transmitting what they have eavesdropped on to others from the jinn, and therefore they do not return to transmitting it, and if it had not reached them, the eavesdropping and burning would have been cut off, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. I said: The first statement is more correct, as will be explained in As-Saffat. There is a difference of opinion as to whether meteors were thrown before the mission. Most of them said yes. It was also said no, but that was after the mission. This issue will be explained in Surat Al-Jinn, God willing. And also in As-Saffat. Al-Zajjaj said: Throwing meteors is one of the signs of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that happened after his birth, because the poets in ancient times did not mention it in their poems, and they did not liken a fast thing to it as they likened it to lightning and a flood. It is not far-fetched to say: The falling of the stars happened in ancient times, but they were not pelting the devils, then they became pelting when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was born. The scholars said: We see the falling of the stars, so it is possible that it is as we see, then it becomes fire when the devil overtakes it. It is also possible to say: They are thrown with a torch of fire from the air, so it seems to us that it is a moving star. And the word meteor in the language means a shining fire. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Amer Al-Shaabi who said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent, the devils were stoned with stars that had not been stoned with before. They came to Abd Yalil bin Amr Al-Thaqafi and said: The people have been frightened and have freed their slaves and let their livestock go because of what they saw in the stars. He said to them - and he was a blind man -: Do not be hasty, and look. If they are the stars that you know, then they will be when people die, and if they are not known, then they are from an innovation. So they looked and saw that they were stars that were not known, so they said: This is from an innovation. They did not stay long until they heard about the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him).
15:19: The Almighty’s saying: And the earth We have spread out. This is also one of His blessings, and one of the things that indicate the perfection of His power. Ibn Abbas said: We spread it out on the surface of the water, as He said: And the earth after that He spread it out. (al-Nazi’at 79:30) meaning He spread it out. He also said: And the earth We have spread out, and excellent are the spreaders. (al-Dhariyat 51:48). This is a response to those who claim that it is like a ball. It has been mentioned before. And We cast therein firm mountains stable mountains so that it would not move with its inhabitants. And We caused to grow therein of every well-balanced thing meaning measured and known, as Ibn Abbas and Saeed bin Jubayr said. He only said weighted because weight is used to determine the amount of something. The poet said: Before I met you, I had a balance for every opponent. Qatada said: Weighed means divided. Mujahid said: Weighed and counted. It is said: This is a weighed speech, meaning organized and not scattered. So based on this, we caused to grow in the earth what is weighed of gems, animals and minerals. God the Almighty said about animals: And caused it to grow a good growth (Al Imran 3:37). What is meant by growing is creation and bringing into existence. It was also said: And caused to grow in it meaning in the mountains of every weighed thing of gold, silver, copper, lead and tin, even arsenic and kohl, all of which is weighed by weight. Its meaning was narrated from Al Hasan and Ibn Zayd. It was also said: We caused to grow in the earth fruits that are measured and weighed. It was also said: what prices are weighed in because it is more valuable and more beneficial than what has no price.
15:20: And We have made for you therein means of livelihood meaning the restaurants and drinks from which they live, the singular of which is ma'ishah with a sukoon on the yaa. And from this is the saying of Jarir: The cost of living for the Al-Zaid family is on me, and who will provide me with the thinner and the sling? The root is ma'ishah on maf'ala with a sukoon on the ya'. It was mentioned in Al-A'raf. It was said that it refers to clothing, as Al-Hasan said. It was also said that it refers to the means of livelihood for the duration of life. Al-Mawardi said: This is what is apparent. And those for whom you are not providers means the beasts and cattle, as Mujahid said. He also said that they are the slaves and children about whom God said: We provide for them and for you (Al-Isra': 31). The word min can include slaves and beasts if they are gathered together, because if rational and irrational people are gathered together, the rational person will prevail. That is, We made for you in it livelihoods, male and female slaves, beasts and children whom We provide for and you do not provide for. So min according to this interpretation is in the accusative case, as Mujahid and others said its meaning. It was said that he meant the wild animals. Sa'id said: Mansour read to us and those for whom you are not providers and he said: the wild animals. So -man according to this is used for irrational things, like And among them is he who walks on his belly (al-Nur 24:45) and the verse. It is in the accusative case in apposition to the kaf and the mim in His statement: for you. And there is something ugly in this according to the Basrans, because it is not permissible for them to apposition the apparent to the implicit except by repeating the preposition, like I passed by him and Zayd. And it is not permissible to pass by him and Zayd except in poetry, as he said: Today you are about to insult and curse us, so go away, what is wrong with you and the days? This meaning has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah and Surat An-Nisa.
15:21: God the Almighty says: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasures. That is, there is not a thing of the provisions and benefits of creation but that with Us are its treasures, meaning the rain sent down from the sky, because everything grows with it. Al-Hasan said: Rain is the treasures of everything. It was also said: The treasures are the keys, meaning in the sky are the keys to provisions, as Al-Kalbi said. The meaning is the same. And We do not send it down except according to a known measure. That is, but We do not send it down except according to Our will and according to the need of creation for it, as He said: And if God were to extend provision to His servants, they would transgress throughout the earth, but He sends down according to what He wills. (al-Shura 42:27). It was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, Al-Hakam ibn 'Uyaynah, and others that there is no year with more rain than another year, but God distributes it as He wills, so He rains on some people and deprives others. And sometimes the rain is in the seas and deserts. The treasures is the plural of khazana, which is the place where a person hides his money. The treasury is also the source of khazana, which means to store. Whatever is in a person's treasury is prepared for him. Likewise, whatever the Lord has ordained is as if it is prepared with Him. Al-Qushayri said. Ja`far ibn Muhammad narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather that he said: In the Throne is an example of everything that God created on land and sea. This is the interpretation of the words of God Almighty: And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories. And sending down means creating and bringing into existence, like His words: And We have sent down for you from the grazing livestock eight mates (al-Zumar 39:6) and His words: And We sent down iron, wherein is great might (al-Hadid 57:25). It was said that sending down means giving, and He called it sending down because the rulings of God are sent down from the sky.
15:22: It has five issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And We sent the winds. The common reading is winds in the plural. Hamza read it in the singular, because the meaning of wind is also plural even though its wording is the wording of the singular. Just as it is said: The wind came from every side. Just as it is said: A land of sababas and a garment of akhlaq. And the Arabs do the same with everything that is wide. As for the reason for the common reading, it is because God Almighty described it as lawāqih which is plural. And the meaning of lawāqih is pregnant, because it carries water, soil, clouds, goodness and benefit. Al-Azhari said: And He made the wind laqīh because it carries the clouds, that is, it carries them and directs them, then passes them and turns them, that is, it brings them down. God Almighty said: Until, when it has carried heavy clouds (al-A’raf 7:57), meaning it has become pregnant. And a female camel is laqīh and female camels are lawāqih if they carry fetuses in their bellies. And it was said: lawāqih means fertilized, which is the original, but it does not fertilize except when it is fertilized in itself, as if the wind fertilized with goodness. It was said that they are fertile, and all of that is correct, meaning that some of them pollinate the tree, like their saying: A satisfied life, meaning that there is contentment in it, and a sleeping night, meaning that there is sleep in it. And some of them bring clouds. It is said: The she-camel was fertilized in the kasra fertile and fertile in the fatha so she is fertile. And the stallion impregnated her, meaning that she threw water to her and she carried it, so the winds are like the stallion for the clouds. Al-Jawhari said: And winds are fertile and it is not said fertile, and it is from the rare ones. Al-Mahdawi narrated from Abu Ubaidah: fertile means fertile, he went to the plural of fertile and fertile, then its extra letters were deleted. And it was said: It is the plural of fertile and fertile, on the meaning of having pollination according to the lineage. And it is possible that the meaning of fertile is pregnant. The Arabs say for the south: fertile and pregnant, and for the north: barren and sterile. Ubaid bin Umair said: God sends the good report so the earth rises up, then He sends the stirrer so it stirs the clouds, then He sends the reconciler so it reconciles, then He sends the fertile so it reconciles, then He sends the fertile so it pollinates the tree. It was said: The fertilizing wind that carries the dew and scatters it in the clouds, and when it gathers in them it becomes rain. On the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The south wind is from Paradise and it is the fertilizing wind that God mentioned in His Book and in it are benefits for people. It was narrated on his authority, peace be upon him, that he said: No south wind blows except that God causes a gushing spring to spring forth from it. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash said: Not a drop drips from the clouds except after the four winds work in it, so the north wind stirs it, the south wind fertilizes it, the south wind produces it, and the north wind scatters it. Second: Ibn Wahb, Ibn al-Qasim, Ashab and Ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated on the authority of Malik - and the wording is from Ashab - Malik said: God the Almighty said: And We sent the winds as pollinators So the pollination of wheat, in my opinion, is that it kernels and spikes, and I do not know what dries in its sleeves, but it kernels until it dries then, and the latter does not spoil. And the pollination of all trees is that they bear fruit, then some of it falls and some of it remains, and that is not that it is brought forth. Ibn al-Arabi said: Malik relied in this interpretation on the likening of the pollination of trees to the pollination of a fetus, and that when the child is tied and created and the soul is breathed into it, it is like the kernelization of the fruit and its spike, because it is called by a name that every bearer shares, which is pollination, and based on this came the hadith: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the sale of grain until it is strong.” Ibn Abd al-Barr said: The pollination, according to the scholars, in palm trees is pollination, which is that something is taken from the pollen of the male palm tree and inserted between the pollen of the female palm tree. The meaning of this in all fruits is the emergence of the fruit of the fig and others until the fruit is visible and seen. What is considered by Malik and his companions in what is mentioned of fruits is the male, and in what is not mentioned, what is established from its blossoms is established and falls. The limit of that in crops is its emergence from the ground, said Malik. It was narrated from him that its fruiting is that it becomes grainy. The scholars did not differ that if the wall splits and its females emerge, so it delays its fruiting and another one in the same condition has fruited, that its ruling is the ruling of what has fruited, because the time of fruiting has come upon it and its fruit is apparent after it has disappeared in the grain. If some of the wall has fruited, then what has not been fruited is dependent on it. Likewise, if the wall is clearly ripe, then the rest of the wall is dependent on that ripeness in the permissibility of selling it. Third: All the Imams narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “Whoever buys a palm tree after it has been pollinated, its fruit belongs to the one who sold it, unless the buyer stipulates it. Whoever buys a slave, his money belongs to the one who sold him, unless the buyer stipulates it.” Our scholars said: The pollinated fruit is not included with the roots in the sale except by stipulation, because it is an existing entity surrounded by security from its falling, usually.
