This is unlike the one that has not been pollinated, since its falling is not secure, so its existence has not been confirmed, so it is not permissible for the seller to stipulate it or make an exception for it, because it is like a fetus. This is the well-known view of the Maliki school of thought. It was said: It is permissible to make an exception for it, and this is the view of Al-Shafi’i. Fourth: If the palm trees are purchased and the fruit remains with the seller, it is permissible for the buyer of the original to buy the fruit before it ripens, according to the well-known opinion of Malik. He sees that it is subject to the ruling of a subsidiary even if it is singled out in the contract. And from him in a narration: It is not permissible. This is what Al-Shafi’i, Abu Hanifa, Al-Thawri, the people of the apparent meaning and the jurists of Hadith said. And it is the most apparent of the Hadiths prohibiting the sale of fruit before it ripens. Fifth: What is related to this chapter is the prohibition of selling fertilized camels, and fertilized camels are the male camels, the singular is malqaḥ. The malqaḥ also refers to the female camels that have their offspring in their wombs, the singular is malqaḥwith the qaf open. The malqaḥare the fetuses in the wombs of female camels, the singular is malqaḥ, from their saying: qaḥt, like the feverish from fever, and the mad from jinn. The prohibition came in this. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that: “He prohibited the sale of the fetuses of females. And he prohibited the madamāmin and malqaḥ.” Abu Ubaid said: The madamāmin are the fetuses in the wombs. And the malqaḥare the ones in the loins of the male camels. This is the opinion of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab and others. It was said the opposite: The madamāmin are the ones on the backs of camels, and the malqaḥare the ones in the wombs of females. This is the opinion of Abu Habīt and others. Whichever of the two cases it is, the Muslim scholars are in agreement that it is not permissible. Al-Muzani mentioned from Ibn Hisham a witness that the malqaḥare the ones in the wombs of some Bedouins: My sperm is fertilized in the womb and results from fertilization after a long time Al-Jawhari mentioned as evidence of this the words of the rajaz poet: We found that driving away the pests is better than procrastination and questions. And the year and the next year, inseminated in the belly of the Hail fang God the Almighty says: And We sent down from the sky meaning from the clouds. Everything that rises above you and shades you is called sky. It was also said: from the direction of the sky. Water meaning rain. Then We made it rain for you to drink meaning We made that rain for your watering and for your livestock and your land to drink. It was also said: Saqa and Asqa mean the same thing. It was also said with the difference, and it was mentioned before. And you are not its keepers meaning we are not its keepers with you, meaning we are the keepers of this water, we send it down when we wish and we hold it back when we wish. And similar to it is And We sent down from the sky pure water (al-Furqan 25:48), And We sent down from the sky water in a measured amount and settled it in the earth, and indeed, We are Able to take it away (al-Mu’minun 23:18). Sufyan said: You will not prevent the rain.
15:23: That is, the earth and whoever is on it, and nothing will remain except Us. Similar to it: Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned. (Maryam 19:40). So the ownership of everything belongs to God Almighty. But He owns His servants as possessions, and when they die, the claims are cut off, so God is the inheritor from this aspect. It was said: The revival in this verse is the revival of the sperm in the wombs. As for the resurrection, He mentioned it after this in His statement: And indeed, your Lord will gather them.
15:24: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And We have certainly known those among you who went ahead, and We have certainly known those who remained behind. There are eight interpretations of this: First: those who went ahead in creation until today, and not those who remained behind, who have not yet been created, as stated by Qatada, Ikrimah, and others. Second: those who went ahead are the dead, and those who remained behind are the living, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak. Third: those who went ahead are those who came before the nation of Muhammad, and those who remained behind are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, as stated by Mujahid. Fourth: those who went ahead in obedience and goodness, and those who remained behind in disobedience and evil, as stated by Al-Hasan and Qatada as well. Fifth: those who went ahead in the ranks of war, and those who remained behind in it, as stated by Saeed bin Al-Musayyab. Sixth: those who went ahead are those who were killed in jihad, and those who remained behind are those who were not killed, as stated by Al-Qurazi. Seventh: those who went ahead are the first of creation, and those who remained behind are the last of creation, as stated by Al-Sha’bi. Eighth: those who go forward in the prayer rows, and those who stay behind because of women. All of this is known to God, the Most High, for He knows everything that exists and does not exist, and He knows who He created and what He will create until the Day of Resurrection. However, the eighth statement is the reason for the revelation of the verse, because of what was narrated by Al-Nasa’i and Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “There was a woman who prayed behind the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was beautiful, one of the most beautiful people. Some of the people would move forward until they were in the first row so that he would not see her, and some of them would move back until they were in the last row. When he bowed, he would look from under his armpit, so God, the Most High, warned: ‘And We have certainly known those among you who go forward, and We have certainly known those who stay behind. ’” It was narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Jawza’ without mentioning Ibn Abbas. This is more authentic. Second: This indicates the virtue of the first time of prayer and the virtue of the first row. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If people knew the reward of the call to prayer and the first row, and they could not find any other way to do so except by drawing lots, they would draw lots. So if a man comes at noon and gets down in the first row next to the imam, he will have three levels of virtue: the first time, the first row, and being next to the imam. If he comes at noon and gets down in the other row or in a row lower than the first row, he will have gained the virtue of the first time and missed out on the virtue of the first row and being next to the imam. If the time of noon comes and he gets down in the first row but not next to the imam, he will have gained the virtue of the first time and the first row, and he will have missed out on being next to the imam. If he comes after noon and gets down in the first row, he will have missed out on the virtue of the first time and will have gained the virtue of the first row and being next to the imam. And so on. Being next to the imam is not for everyone, but rather it is as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Let those among you who are wise and intelligent be closest to me. The position next to the imam should be for someone who has this description. If someone else takes it, he should be delayed and he should advance to the place, because it is his right by the command of the owner of the law, just as the mihrab is the place of the imam, whether he advances or delays, said Ibn al-Arabi. I said: And this is what is meant by the statement of Omar may God be pleased with him: Stand back, so-and-so, go forward, so-and-so, then go forward and say Allahu Akbar. It has been narrated from Ka’b that a man from this nation will fall down in prostration and those behind him will be forgiven. Ka’b used to choose the last row of the mosque hoping for that, and he mentions that he found it like that in the Torah. Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim mentioned it in Nawadir al-Usul. Further clarification of this matter will come in Surah as-Saffat, God willing. Third: Just as this verse indicates the virtue of the first row in prayer, it also indicates the virtue of the first row in battle. Standing to slaughter the enemy and selling oneself to God the Almighty is unmatched by any other deed, so advancing towards him is better, and there is no disagreement or concealment about it. No one would advance in battle in front of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he was the bravest of people. Al-Bara’ said: By God, when the battle became fierce, we would protect ourselves with him, and the brave man is not like the one who stands next to him, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.
15:25: The Almighty said: And indeed, your Lord will gather them together meaning for the reckoning and reward. He is Wise and Knowing has been mentioned above.
15:26: The Almighty said: And We have certainly created man meaning Adam, peace be upon him. From clay meaning from dry mud, according to Ibn Abbas and others. Clay is the free clay mixed with sand, so it becomes clinking when it dries. When it is cooked with fire, it is pottery, according to Abu Ubaidah. This is the opinion of most commentators. The linguists recited: Mobile phone enemy Mujahid said: It is stinking mud, and Al-Kisa’i chose it. He said: It is from the Arabs’ saying: The meat became stinking and rotten if it became rotten - whether cooked or raw - it rotted. Al-Hutay’ah said: That's a boy who does his best, and his meat is not spoiled by his sword. Clay is Salal and Musalal, meaning it makes a sound when you tap it like iron makes a sound. It was first dust, meaning scattered parts, then it got wet and became clay, then it was left until it stunk and became aged mud, meaning changed, then it dried and became salsal, according to the majority. This has been explained in Al-Baqarah. Hama is black clay, as is sukoon, you say from it: the well became hama with sukoon if you removed its mud. And the well became hama with a fat-ha its mud became plentiful. And I heated it with ahmaa, Ihmaa, I threw mud into it, according to Ibn Al-Sikkit. Abu Ubaidah said: Hama with a sukoon on the meem is like truffles. The plural is Hama, like Tamra and Tamr. Hama is a source, like panic and alarm, then it was named after it. And sukoon is the changed. Ibn Abbas said: It is the wet, stinking dirt, then it was made into salsal like pottery. Similar to it is the statement of Mujahid and Qatadah, who said: The putrid is the changed, from their saying: The water has become stagnant if it has changed, and from it is yatasannahu (The Cow: 259) and water that is not stagnant (Muhammad 47:15). And from it is the statement of Abu Qais bin Al-Aslat: I watered my echo with a nectar without teeth, like musk, and I poured it on the water of the clusters. Al-Farra’ said: It is the variable, and its origin is from their saying: I rubbed the stone on the stone, if I rubbed it with it. And what comes out of the two stones is called the sinana and the sinin, and from it the word masn is derived. The poet said: Then her waist to the red dome walking on sharpened marble Any smooth, polished hair. It is said that Yazid bin Muawiyah said to his father: Don’t you see Abd al-Rahman bin Hassan flirting with your daughter? Muawiyah said: What did he say? He said: He said: She is a flower like a pearl of the sea, distinguished from a hidden essence Muawiyah said: He is right! Yazid said: He says: If you attribute it, you will not find it in the splendor of generosity. He said: He is right! He said: Where is his saying: Then I poured it... the house? Muawiyah said: He lied. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Masnun is the poured, and it is from the Arabs’ saying: I poured water and other things on the face if I poured it. And al-San is pouring. Ali bin Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: Al-Masnun is the wet, and this means poured, because it is not poured except when it is wet. An-Nahhas: This is a good saying, because it is said: I poured something, meaning I poured it. Abu Amr bin Al-Ala said: And from it is the trace narrated from Omar that he used to pour water on the face and not sprinkle it. And sprinkle with sh is to separate the water, and with the silent sin it is to pour it without separating it. Sibawayh said: Al-Masnun is the pictured. It is taken from the sunnat of the face, which is its image. Dhu al-Rummah said: You will see a smooth, flawless face with no blemishes or scars. Al-Akhfash said: “Al-Masnun is the erect, from their saying: a long face.” It has been said: Al-Salsal is finely ground dirt, as narrated by Al-Mahdawi. Whoever says: Al-Salsal is the stinking one, then its root is Salal, so one of the two lām was replaced with sād. And Min hama is an explanation of the type of Al-Salsal, like your saying: I took this from an Arab man.
15:27: The Almighty said: And the jinn We created before meaning before the creation of Adam. Al-Hasan said: He means Iblis, God Almighty created him before Adam, peace be upon him. He was called a jinn because he was hidden from sight. In Sahih Muslim, from a hadith narrated by Thabit from Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When God Almighty created Adam, peace be upon him, in Paradise, He left him as long as God willed to leave him, so Iblis began to circle around him to see what he was like. When he saw that he was hollow, he knew that he had been created with a creation that could not control itself." From the poisonous fire Ibn Masoud said: The poisonous fire from which God created the jinn is one part of seventy parts of the fire of Hell. Ibn Abbas said: The poisonous is the hot wind that kills. And from him: It is a fire that has no smoke, and lightning comes from it, and it is a fire that is between the sky and the veil. So when God brings about something, it breaks through the veil and the lightning falls to what it was commanded. So the thunderbolt that you hear is the breaking of that veil. Al-Hasan said: The fire of the poisonous wind is a fire that is veiled, and what you hear from the falling of the clouds is its sound. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas also, he said: Iblis was from a tribe of the angels called the jinn, who were created from the fire of the poisonous wind from among the angels. He said: And the jinn who were mentioned in the Qur’an were created from a smokeless flame of fire. I said: This is questionable, as it needs a chain of transmission that eliminates the excuse, as something like this cannot be said from the standpoint of opinion. Muslim narrated from the hadith of Urwah on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The angels were created from light, the jinn were created from a smokeless flame of fire, and Adam was created from that which has been described to you. So his statement: The angels were created from light implies generality. And God knows best. Al-Jawhari said: A smokeless flame of fire from which the jinn were created. The samūm hot wind is feminine, and it is said from it: Our day is poisoned, so it is a poisonous day, and the plural is sama’im. Abu Ubaidah said: The poisons occur during the day and may occur at night, and the heat occurs during the night and may occur during the day. Al-Qushayri said: The hot wind is called samūm because it enters the pores of the body.
15:28: The Almighty said: And when your Lord said to the angels It was mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Indeed, I am creating a human being from clay from clay.
15:29: So when I have proportioned him means I have proportioned his creation and his form. And breathed into him of My spirit Blowing is the flow of wind into something. The spirit is a subtle body. God has made it a habit to create life in the body along with that body. Its reality is adding a creation to a Creator, so the spirit is a creation from His creation. He added it to Himself as an honor and a glorification, like His saying: My earth and my heaven and my house and the she-camel of God and the month of God. And similarly, And a spirit from Him (An-Nisa': 171). This was previously explained in An-Nisa'. We mentioned in the book of At-Tadhkirah the hadiths that indicate that the spirit is a subtle body, and that the soul and the spirit are two names for one thing. This will come, God willing. And whoever said that the spirit is life said that he meant: So when life is installed in him. Then fall down to him in prostration means fall down to him in prostration. It is a prostration of greeting and honor, not a prostration of worship. And God may give preference to whomever He wishes, so He gave preference to the prophets over the angels. This meaning was previously explained in Al-Baqarah. Al-Qaffal said: They were better than Adam, and He tested them by prostrating to him, exposing them to a great reward. This is the doctrine of the Mu'tazila. It was said: They were ordered to prostrate to God in front of Adam, and Adam was their qibla.
15:30: The Almighty’s saying: So the angels prostrated, all of them together, except Iblis. There are two issues in this: First: There is no doubt that Iblis was commanded to prostrate, because God says: What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you? (al-A’raf 7:12). Rather, what prevented him from doing so was arrogance and haughtiness, as was explained in Al-Baqarah. Then it was said: He was one of the angels, so it is an exception from the genus. Some people said: He was not one of the angels, so it is a discontinuous exception. All of this has been explained in Al-Baqarah in full. Ibn Abbas said: The jinn are the fathers of the jinn and they are not devils. The devils are the sons of Iblis, they do not die except with Iblis. The jinn die, and among them are the believers and the disbelievers. So Adam is the father of mankind. The jinn are the fathers of the jinn. Iblis is the father of the devils, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. What was mentioned in Al-Baqarah is the opposite of this, so reflect on it there. Second: Exception of a type other than the type is valid according to Al-Shafi’i, even if he said: I owe someone a dinar except a garment, or ten garments except a bushel of wheat, and what is similar to that is acceptable, and the value of the garment and the wheat is dropped from the amount. Measured, weighed, and estimated items are the same in this regard. Malik and Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with them said: Excluding the measured from the weighed and the weighed from the measured is permissible, even if he previously excluded dirhams from wheat and wheat from dirhams. However, if he excluded the components from the measured or weighed items, and the measured from the components, such as saying: I owe ten dinars except a garment, or ten garments except a dinar, the exception is not valid, and the one who acknowledged is liable for the entire amount. Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: Exception of something other than the type is not valid, and the one who acknowledged is liable for all of what he acknowledged. The evidence for Al-Shafi’i’s statement is that the word exception is used for both genders. God Almighty said: “Therein they will hear no ill speech or sinful talk, but only the word, ‘Peace, peace!’” (al-Waqi’ah 56:25-26)
15:31: So he excluded peace from the category of idle talk. And similar to it is So the angels prostrated, all of them together, except Iblis, and Iblis is not among the angels. God Almighty said: “Except Iblis. He was one of the jinn and disobeyed the command of his Lord” (al-Kahf 18:50). And the poet said: A town with no companions except the camels and the wild donkeys He excluded the male gazelles, and the white camels, from the Anis. Similar to this is the saying of Al-Nabigha:
15:32: The Almighty said: He said, ‘O Iblis, what is the matter with you?’ meaning what is preventing you. from being with those who prostrate meaning from not being.
15:33: He said, 'I would not prostrate to a human being whom You created from clay from altered black mud.' This was due to his arrogance and envy, and that he was better than him, since he was made of fire and fire consumes clay, as was previously explained in Al-A'raf.
15:34: He said, 'Then get out of it' meaning from the heavens, or from the Garden of Eden, or from among the angels. For you are expelled meaning stoned by meteors. It was also said: cursed and ill-fated. All of this has been discussed in detail in Surat Al-Baqarah and Surat Al-A'raf.
15:35: And upon you is the curse meaning my curse, as in Surat Sad~.
15:36: The Almighty said: He said, 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected.' This question from Iblis was not out of his confidence in his status with God Almighty, and that he is worthy of having his supplication answered, but he asked for his punishment to be delayed as an increase in his affliction, like the action of one who despairs of safety. And what he meant by his question of reprieve until the Day they are resurrected was that he would not die, because there is no death on the Day of Resurrection or after it.
15:37: God Almighty said: Then you are among those who are given respite meaning among those who are deferred.
15:38: Until the Day of the Appointed Time. Ibn Abbas said: He meant the first blast, that is, when all creation dies. It was also said: The appointed time that God has kept knowledge of to Himself, and Satan is ignorant of it. Satan dies and then is resurrected. God the Almighty said: Everything on it will perish. (al-Rahman 55:26). There are two opinions about the speech of God the Almighty: One of them: He spoke to him through the tongue of His Messenger. The second: He spoke to him as a severe threat, not as an honor or a way to draw near.
15:39: God the Almighty said: He said, 'My Lord, because You have put me in error, I will surely make [evil] attractive to them on earth.' The meaning of misleading and beautification was mentioned earlier in Al-A'raf. Adorning here can be done in two ways: either by committing sins, or by keeping them busy with the adornments of this world instead of doing acts of obedience. The meaning of and I will surely mislead them all is that I will mislead them from the path of guidance. Ibn Lahi'ah Abdullah narrated on the authority of Diraj Abi Al-Samh on the authority of Abi Al-Haitham on the authority of Abi Saeed Al-Khudri who said that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "Satan said, 'O Lord, by Your glory and majesty, I will continue to mislead the children of Adam as long as their souls are in their bodies.' The Lord said, 'By My glory and majesty, I will continue to forgive them as long as they ask My forgiveness.'"
15:40: The people of Medina and Kufa read it with a fatha on the lam, meaning those whom You have chosen and purified. The rest read it with a kasra on the lam, meaning those who have devoted their worship to You without corruption or hypocrisy. Abu Thamama narrated that the disciples asked Jesus, peace be upon him, about those who are sincere to God, and he said: Those who work and do not like people to praise them.
15:41: Omar bin Al-Khattab said: Its meaning is this is a path that its follower will be straightened until he attacks Paradise. Al-Hasan: Ali means to me. Mujahid and Al-Kisa'i: This is a threat and a warning, like when you say to someone you threaten: Your path is to me and your fate is to me. And like His saying: Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful (al-Fajr 89:14). So the meaning of the statement is: This is a path that returns to me, so I reward everyone according to his deeds, meaning the path of servitude. It was said: The meaning is to guide me to the straight path with clarification and proof. It was also said: with success and guidance. Ibn Sirin, Qatadah, Al-Hasan, Qays bin Abbad, Abu Raja, Hamid and Ya'qub read This is the path of Ali, straight with the raising of Ali and its tanween, and its meaning is high and straight, meaning high in religion and truth. It was said: High to attain, straight to deviate.
15:42: First: The Almighty’s saying: “Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority.” The scholars said: It means over their hearts. Ibn Uyaynah said: It means that He throws them into a sin that prevents them from My forgiveness and makes it difficult for them. And these are the ones whom God has guided, chosen, selected, and chosen. I said: Perhaps someone will say: God has informed us about the description of Adam and Eve, peace be upon them, by saying: Then Satan caused them to slip (al-Baqarah 2:36), and about a group of the companions of His Prophet, by saying: Satan only caused them to slip because of some of what they had earned (Al Imran 3:155). The answer is what was mentioned, which is an illusion, that he has no power over their hearts, nor is he the subject of their faith, nor does he throw them into a sin that leads to its non-acceptance, rather repentance removes it and return erases it. And Adam’s expulsion was not a punishment for what he had committed, as was explained in Al-Baqarah. As for the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, the statement about them has already been made in Al-Imran. Then His saying, the Most High: You have no authority over them may be specific to those whom God has protected, or it may be in most times and circumstances, and his authority may be to relieve distress and remove worry, as He did with Bilal, when he came to guide him as a child is guided until he fell asleep, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions slept and did not wake up until the sun rose, and they were frightened and said: What is the expiation for what we did by being negligent in our prayer? So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: There is no negligence in sleep, so he relieved them. Except for those who follow you of the deviators, meaning the misguided polytheists. That is, His authority over these people, as evidenced by His authority is only over those who take him as a friend and those who associate others with Him. (al-Nahl 16:100) Second: This verse and the one before it are evidence of the permissibility of excluding a little from a lot and a lot from a little, such as saying: Ten minus a dirham. Or saying: Ten minus nine. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said: It is not permissible to except more than half or less. As for excluding more from the whole, it is not valid. Our evidence is this verse, for it excludes the misguided from the servants and the servants from the misguided, and that indicates that excluding less from the whole and excluding more from the whole are permissible.
15:43: The Almighty said: And indeed, Hell is the promised place for them all meaning Iblis and those who follow him. It has seven gates meaning layers, layer upon layer for each gate meaning each layer of them is a portion assigned meaning a known portion. Ibn al-Mubarak said: Ibrahim Abu Harun al-Ghanawi told us: I heard Hattan bin Abdullah al-Raqashi say: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: Do you know how the gates of Hell are? We said: They are like our gates. He said: No, they are like this, one above the other - al-Tha'labi added: and he placed one hand on the other - and that God placed the heavens on the earth, and the fires, one above the other, so the lowest of them is Hell, and above it is al-Hutama, and above it is Saqar, and above it is Jahannam, and above it is Laza', and above it is al-Sa'ir, and above it is al-Hawwa, and each gate is seventy times hotter than the one before it. I said: This is how this interpretation was made. What most scholars agree on is that Hell is the highest level, and it is reserved for the sinners from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is the level where its people are emptied and the winds blow its gates. Then Laza, then Al-Hutama, then Sa’eer, then Saqar, then Jaheem, then Al-Haweeya. Ad-Dahhak said: In the highest level are the Muhammadans, in the second are the Christians, in the third are the Jews, in the fourth are the Sabians, in the fifth are the Magians, in the sixth are the polytheists of the Arabs, and in the seventh are the hypocrites and the people of Pharaoh and those who disbelieved from the people of Al-Ma’idah. God Almighty said: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire (An-Nisa’: 145) - and it was mentioned earlier in An-Nisa’ - and He said: Enter the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment (Ghafir 40:46), and He said: But whoever disbelieves after that among you - I will punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone in the worlds (al-Ma’idah 5:115). Muadh ibn Jabal may God be pleased with him divided the bad scholars of this nation into those gates, which we mentioned in the book At-Tadhkirah. At-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Ibn Umar who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Hell has seven gates, one of which is for the one who draws his sword against my nation. He said: A strange hadith. Ka’b said: Hell has seven gates, one of which is for the Kharijites. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Between every two gates is a journey of seventy years, each gate is two seventy times hotter than the one above it. We mentioned all of this in the book At-Tadhkirah. Salam At-Tawil narrated from Abu Sufyan from Anas ibn Malik from the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) regarding the words of God the Almighty:
15:44: It has seven gates, each gate has a portion assigned to it: a portion in which they associated partners with God, a portion in which they doubted God, a portion in which they were heedless of God, a portion in which they preferred their desires over God, a portion in which they satisfied their anger with God's anger, a portion in which they turned their desire into their portion from God, and a portion in which they rebelled against God. Al-Halimi Abu Abdullah Al-Hussein bin Al-Hasan mentioned it in his book Minhaaj Al-Din, and he said: If it is proven, then those who associate partners with God are the dualists. The doubters are those who do not know whether they have a god or not, and they doubt whether His law is from Him or not. The heedless of God are those who deny Him entirely and do not affirm Him, and they are the materialists. And those who prefer their desires over God are those who are consumed with sins, because they deny the Messengers of God, His commands, and His prohibitions. Those who satisfy their anger with the wrath of God are those who kill the prophets of God and all those who call to Him, and who torment those who advise them or go against their path. Those who make their desires permissible with their share from God are those who deny the resurrection and the judgment, so they worship what they desire, and they will have all their share from God Almighty. Those who rebel against God are those who do not care whether what they are doing is right or wrong, so they do not think, consider, or seek evidence. And God knows best what His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, intended if the hadith is proven. It is narrated that Salman al-Farsi, may God be pleased with him, when he heard this verse, And indeed, Hell is their promised meeting place, all together, fled for three days because he was unable to reason. He was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he asked him, saying: O Messenger of God, was this verse revealed, And indeed, Hell is their promised meeting place, all together? By the One Who sent you with the truth, it broke my heart. Then God, the Most High, revealed, Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs. Bilal said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying alone in the mosque of Medina, when a Bedouin woman passed by him and prayed behind him, and he did not know about her. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse, It has seven gates, for each of them is a portion allotted. The Bedouin woman fell unconscious, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard her groaning, so he turned away and called for water and poured it on her face until she came to and sat up. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O woman, what is the matter with you? She said: Is this part of the revealed Book of God, or are you saying it on your own? He said: O Bedouin woman, rather it is from the revealed Book of God, the Most High. She said: All Which of my limbs is being tormented at each of its gates? He said: O Bedouin woman, each of their gates has a portion assigned to it, and the people of each one of them are being tormented according to their deeds. She said: By God, I am a poor woman. I have no money, and I have only seven slaves. I bear witness, O Messenger of God, that each slave of them is free for the sake of God Almighty for each of the gates of Hell. Gabriel came to him and said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, give the Bedouin woman the good report that God has forbidden her all the gates of Hell and has opened for her all the gates of Paradise.
15:45: The Almighty said: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs. That is, those who feared immorality and polytheism. In gardens that is, orchards. And springs are the four rivers: water, wine, milk, and honey. As for the springs mentioned in Surat al-Insan 76:Al-Kafur, Al-Zajbil, and Al-Salsabil, and in al-Mutaffifin 83:At-Tasnim, they and their people will be mentioned, God willing. The ayn of ayn is pronounced with a damma according to the original, and the kasra is to take into account the yaa, and both were recited with it.
15:46: "Enter it in peace, secure." The general reading is enter it with the alif connected and the kha's damma, from dakhala yakhul, in the imperative mood. Its meaning is: it was said enter it. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah and Ruways from Yaqub read enter it with the tanween damma and the alif connected and the kha's kasra as a passive verb, from akhlaqa. That is, God let them enter it. Their doctrine is to break the tanween in the example of Enter Paradise with mercy (al-A’raf 7:49) and similar words, except that here they put the hamza movement on the tanween, since it is an alif of separation, but in it there is a transition from kasra to damma and then from damma to kasra, so it becomes heavy on the tongue. "In peace" means in safety from every disease and affliction. It was also said: with a greeting from God to them. Safe means from death, torment, isolation and disappearance.
15:47: Ibn Abbas said: The first thing the people of Paradise will see is two springs. They will drink from one of the springs, and God will remove any rancor in their hearts. Then they will enter the other spring and wash themselves in it, and their colors will shine and their faces will be clear, and the freshness of bliss will flow upon them. And something similar was narrated from Ali, may God be pleased with him. And Ali bin Al-Hussein said: It was revealed about Abu Bakr, Omar, Ali, and the Companions, meaning what was between them in the pre-Islamic era of rancor. The first statement is more apparent, as indicated by the context of the verse. And Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: I hope that Talhah, Al-Zubayr, and I will be among these. Rancor means hatred and enmity. It is said from it: ghul yaghl. And it is said from ghulul, which is theft from spoils: ghul yaghl. And it is said from treachery: aghal yaghl. As he said: May God reward Hamza bint Nawfal on our behalf with the reward of a liar who betrays trust. This has already been mentioned in Al Imran. Brothers on thrones facing each other meaning they do not look at each other’s backs out of love and affection, according to Mujahid and others. It has also been said that the family rotates as they wish, so no one sees the other’s backs. It has also been said that facing each other means that the spouses have come to them and they have come to them with affection. Surur is the plural of bed, like jadeed and jadeed. It has also been said that it is from surur, so it is as if it is a high place prepared for pleasure. The first is more apparent. Ibn Abbas said: On thrones crowned with rubies, emeralds and pearls, the bed is between Sana’a and Jabiyah and between Aden and Ayla. And brothers is an accusative in the state of the righteous or of the pronoun in enter it or of the pronoun in safely, or it could be a state implied from the ha’ and mim in their chests.
15:48: No fatigue or exhaustion will touch them therein. That is, exhaustion and fatigue. And they will not be removed from it. This is evidence that the bliss of Paradise is permanent and will not end, and that its people will remain there. Its food is permanent. This is Our provision, which will never run out. (Surah Sad: 54).
15:49: This verse is similar to the words of the Prophet (peace be upon him): "If the believer knew what punishment is with God, no one would hope for His Paradise. If the disbeliever knew what mercy is with God, no one would despair of His mercy." Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Abu Hurairah. It was mentioned earlier in Al-Fatihah. Thus, a person should remind himself and others, fearing and hoping. Fear is more prevalent in health than in sickness. It was mentioned in the hadith that the Prophet (peace be upon him) came out to the companions while they were laughing and said: Are you laughing while Paradise and Hell are before you? This was difficult for them, so the verse was revealed. Al-Mawardi and Al-Mahdawi mentioned this.
15:50: And the wording of al-Tha'labi on the authority of Ibn Umar said: "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at us from the door through which the Banu Shaybah enter while we were laughing and said: 'Why are you laughing? I do not see you laughing.' Then he turned away until he was at the Black Stone, then he retreated and said to us: 'When I came out, Gabriel came to me and said: O Muhammad, why do you make My servants despair of My mercy? Tell My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Most Merciful, and that My punishment is the most painful punishment.'" Despair is despair, hope is neglect, and the best of matters are those in the middle.
15:51: The Almighty said: And tell them about the guests of Abraham. The guests of Abraham: the angels who gave him the good report of a son and the destruction of the people of Lot. They were mentioned earlier. Abraham, peace be upon him, was called the father of guests, and his palace had four doors so that no one would miss him. The guest was called a guest because he is related to you and stays with you. The ruling on the guest in Hud has already been mentioned enough, praise be to God.
15:52: When they entered upon him is the plural of the predicate because the guest is a noun that can be used for singular, plural, dual, masculine and feminine, like the source. He added it and added it, inclined it, and from it is the hadith: When the sun sets, and the guest of the arrow, and the grammatical addition. "They said, 'Peace'" meaning they greeted him with peace. He said, 'Indeed, we are afraid of you' meaning terrified and afraid. He only said this after he brought the calf near and saw that they were not eating, as mentioned previously in Hud. It was said: He denied peace, and peace was not customary in their country.
15:53: They said, 'Do not be afraid.' That is, the angels said, "Do not be afraid. 'Indeed, We give you good tidings of a learned boy.'" That is, forbearing, as Muqatil said. The majority said: learned. And he is Isaac.
15:54: He said, 'Have you given me good tidings that old age has touched me?' An is a verbal noun, meaning that old age has touched me and my wife. It was mentioned earlier in Hud and Ibrahim, where it says: So what are you giving me good tidings of? is an interrogative of astonishment. It was also said: a real interrogative. Al-Hasan read tawajal with a damma on the ta'. Al-A'mash read bashartomouni without an alif, and Nafi' and Shaibah read tabashiroon with a kasra on the noon and a light sukoon, like atahaajoni, and its explanation was mentioned earlier. Ibn Kathir and Ibn Muhaisin read tabashiroon with a kasra on the noon and a shaddah, meaning you give me good tidings, so the noon was assimilated into the noon. The rest read tabashiroon with the noon in the accusative case without an addition.
15:55: The Almighty said: They said, 'We have given you good tidings in truth' meaning that there is no successor, and that a child is inevitable. So be not of the despairing meaning of those who despair of having a child, and he had despaired of having a child due to extreme old age. The general reading is (of the despairing) with an alif. Al-A'mash and Yahya bin Waththab read of the despairing without an alif. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr. It is shortened from the despairing. It is possible that it is from the language of those who said: qanat yaqnat, like ḍarā yahdhūr. The opening and closing of the noon from yaqnat are two languages that were read with them. It was reported in it yaqnat with a damma. It did not come in it qanat yaqnat. Whoever opens the noon in the past and future, he combines the two languages, so he takes in the past the language of those who said: qanat yaqnat, and in the future the language of those who said: qanat yaqnat, as mentioned by Al-Mahdawi.
15:56: That is, the deniers who have gone astray from the right path. This means that he excluded the boy because of his old age, not because he despaired of the mercy of God Almighty.
15:57: There are two issues: First: When he knew that they were angels - as they informed him of an extraordinary matter, which was the good report of a child - he said: What is the matter with you? A matter is a serious matter. That is, what is your matter and your affair and what have you come with?
15:58: "They said, 'We have been sent to a people of criminals,' meaning, misguided polytheists. There is an implied meaning in the speech, meaning, we have been sent to a people of criminals to destroy them.
15:59: Except the family of Lot his followers and people of his religion. Indeed, We will save them. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read for them with a light pronunciation of anja. The rest read: with a heavy pronunciation of naja, and Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it. Salvation and deliverance mean deliverance.
15:60: Except his wife He excluded his wife from the people of Lot, and she was a disbeliever, so she joined the criminals in destruction. The story of the people of Lot has been presented in Al-A'raf and Surah Hud sufficiently. We have decreed that she is among those who remain behind meaning We have decreed and written that she is among those who remain in the punishment. Al-Ghabir means the one who remains. He said: Don't throw dust at the shoal, you don't know what the outcome will be. Dust is the remains of milk. Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal read Qadarna with a light pronunciation here and in An-Naml, and the rest stressed it. Al-Harawi: It is said Qadr and Qadr, meaning one and the same. Second: There is no disagreement among the people of the language and others that the exception from negation is affirmation and from affirmation is negation. So if a man says: I owe him ten dirhams, minus four, minus one dirham, the acknowledgment of seven is established, because the dirham is an exception from the four, and it is affirmed because it is an exception from a negated thing, and the four was negated because it was an exception from an affirmative, which is ten, so the dirham returned to the six and became seven. Likewise, if he said: I owe him five dirhams, minus one dirham, minus two-thirds of it, he owes four dirhams and a third. Likewise, if he said: I owe so-and-so ten, minus nine, minus eight, minus seven, the second exception refers to what came before it, and the third to the second, so he owes two dirhams, because ten is affirmation and eight is affirmation, so their total is eighteen. And nine is negation and seven is negation, so sixteen are dropped from eighteen, and two dirhams remain, which is the amount due by the acknowledgment and nothing else. So His, the Most High, saying: “Indeed, We were sent to a people of criminals, Except the family of Lot. Indeed, We will save them all, Except his wife.” So He excluded the family of Lot from the criminal people, then He said Except his wife, so He excluded her from the family of Lot, so in the interpretation it goes back to the criminal people as we explained. And this is the ruling in divorce. If he said to his wife: You are divorced three times except two except one, she is divorced twice, because the one goes back to the remainder of what was excepted from, which is the three. And so is everything that came from this, so understand it.
15:61: God Almighty says: So when the messengers came to the family of Lot, meaning I do not know you.
15:62: He said, 'You are a people who are denounced.' It was said: They were young men and he saw their beauty, so he feared for them from the temptation of his people. This is denial.
15:63: They said, 'Rather, we have brought you that about which they were in doubt.' That is, they doubted that it would befall them, which was the punishment.
15:64: And We have brought you the truth meaning the truthfulness. It was also said: the punishment. And We are truthful meaning in their destruction.
15:65: So set out with your family during a part of the night. It was mentioned in Hud. And follow their backs. That is, be behind them so that none of them lag behind and be punished. And let none of you look back. They were forbidden from looking back so that they could hasten their journey and get away from the village before dawn surprised them. It was also said that the meaning is, Do not look back. "And go where you are commanded." Ibn Abbas said: It means Ash-Sham. Muqatil: It means Safad, a village of Lot. It was mentioned earlier. It was also said that it was going to the land of Abraham in a place called Al-Qayn. It was called Al-Yaqin because when Abraham accompanied the messengers, he said to Gabriel: From where will the earth swallow them up? He said: From here. He set a limit for it, and Gabriel went away. When Lot came, he sat with Abraham and they awaited that punishment. When the earth shook, Abraham said: I am certain in God. So it was called Al-Yaqin.
15:66: God Almighty says: And We decreed for him meaning We inspired Lot. That is the matter, that the root of these people will be cut off in the morning is similar to So the root of the people who did wrong will be cut off (al-An’am 6:45). Meaning at dawn. And it has been mentioned before.
15:67: And the people of the city came meaning the people of Lot's city rejoicing rejoicing at the guests, hoping to commit an immoral act.
15:68: He said, 'These are my guests.' So do not disgrace them.
15:69: And fear God and do not be disgraced. It may be from khizā, which means humiliation and disgrace, or it may be from khizāyah, which means shyness and shame. This was mentioned previously in Hud.
15:70: "They said, 'Did we not forbid you from speaking about any of the people if we intended to do them an immoral act?'" That is, from adding someone to someone because we wanted to do them an immoral act. And they meant strangers by their action, according to Al-Hasan. It was mentioned previously in Al-A'raf. And it was said: Or did we not forbid you from speaking about any of the people if we intended to do them an immoral act?
15:71: He said, 'These are my daughters, if you are going to do something.'" That is, marry them and do not incline towards what is forbidden. This was explained previously in Hud.
15:72: It has three issues: First: Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: All the commentators said that God Almighty swore here by the life of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to honor him, that his people from Quraysh were wandering blindly in their drunkenness and wavering in their confusion. I said: And thus said Judge Iyad: The people of interpretation agreed on this that it is an oath from God, the Most High, by the life of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Its origin is the damma of the ‘ayn from ‘umr, but it was opened due to frequent use. Its meaning is and your survival, O Muhammad. It was also said and your life. This is the ultimate in glorification and the ultimate in righteousness and honor. Abu al-Juza’ said: God did not swear by the life of anyone other than Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he is the most honorable of creation in His sight. Ibn al-Arabi said: (What prevents God, the Most High, from swearing by the life of Lot and granting him as much honor as He wills? And whatever favor God gives to Lot, He gives to His weak ones as honor to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he is more honorable to God than him. Or do you not see that He, the Most High, gave Abraham friendship and Moses the ability to speak to Him, and He gave that to Muhammad, so if He swears by the life of Lot, then the life of Muhammad is higher. And He does not move from one statement to another without mentioning it except for necessity). I said: What he said is good, because His oath by the life of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have been an interjection in the story of Lot. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr Abdul Rahim bin Abdul Karim said in his interpretation: It is possible to say: This goes back to the people of Lot, meaning they were in their drunkenness, wandering blindly. It was also said: Lot preached to his people and said, These are my daughters. The angels said: O Lot, by your life, indeed, in their drunkenness, they are wandering blindly. They do not know what will happen to them in the morning. If it is said: God swore by the fig and the olive and Mount Sinai, so what is in that? It is said to him: There is nothing that God swears by except that this is an indication of its superiority over what is included in its count, so likewise our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, must be better than those included in his count. Life and life with a damma on the ‘ayn or a fatha are rich and their meaning is the same, except that it is not used in swearing except with a fatha due to frequent use. And you say: May God grant you a long life, meaning I ask God to grant you a long life. And by your life is raised as a subject and its predicate is omitted. The meaning is by your life, from what he swore by. Second: Many scholars disliked that a person say by my life, because it means by my life. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said: It is disliked for a man to say by my life, because he is swearing by his own life, and that is the speech of weak men. Malik said something similar: The weak among men and women swear by your life and your livelihood, and it is not the speech of men. Even if God, the Most High, swore by it in this story, that is a statement of the honor of the position and the elevation of its status, so nothing else should be attributed to it or used for anything else. Ibn Habib said: By your life should be used in speech for this verse.” Qatada said: It is from the speech of the Arabs. Ibn Al-Arabi said: And I say the same: But the Shari’ah has decided on its usage and returned the oath to it. I said: The oath with by your life and by my life and the like is found in Arab poetry and eloquent speech, and Al-Nabigha said: By my life, my life is not easy for me. You have spoken like a hero to the opponents. last: By your life, death has never missed a young man, like a long, slack-jawed man who has been bent over by the hand. last O you who married Thuraya Suhayl, may God give you a long life, how they meet last: If Banu Qushair were pleased with me, by God, I would be pleased with their satisfaction. Some scholars of meaning said: This is not permissible, because it is not said that God has a life span, but rather He, the Most High, is eternal. This was mentioned by Al-Zahrawi. Third: We have already discussed what is permissible to swear by and what is not permissible to swear by in Al-Ma’idah. We mentioned there the statement of Ahmad ibn Hanbal about the one who swears by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he must make expiation. Ibn Khuwayzmandad said: Whoever permits swearing by other than God Almighty, which is permissible to glorify with a right, is not saying that an oath requires expiation, except that the one who intended to lie is blameworthy, because inwardly he is belittling that which he must glorify. They said: And the statement of God Almighty by your life means by your life. And when God Almighty swears by the life of His Prophet, then He only wanted to make it clear to us that it is permissible for us to swear by his life. According to the Maliki school of thought, the meaning of his saying: By your life and the fig and the olive (al-Tin 95:1) and and the Mount * and the Inscribed Book (al-Tur 52:1-2) and and the star when it goes down (al-Najm 53:60) and and the sun and its brightness (Ash-Shams: 1) and I swear by this city * and you are a resident in this city * and by a father and what he begot (al-Balad 90:1-3) all of this means: By the Creator of the fig and the olive, and by the Lord of the Inscribed Book, and by the Lord of the city in which you are a resident, and by the Creator of your livelihood and your life, and by the right of Muhammad, so the oath and the vow are made by Him, glory be to Him, not by the created. Ibn Khuwayzmandad said: Whoever permits an oath by other than God, the Most High, has interpreted the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The mountain is more honorable in the sight of God than your fathers who died in the Age of Ignorance. Malik took the hadith at face value. Ibn Khuwaizmandad said: Those who permitted this also provided evidence that the oaths of Muslims have been in effect since the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until this day, in which they swear by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the extent that the people of Medina, until this day, if one of them brings a case against his companion, he says: Swear to me by the right of what this grave contains, and by the right of the inhabitant of this grave, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and likewise by the Sacred Sanctuary and the great sacred sites, the corner, the Maqam, the Mihrab, and what is recited in it.
15:73: The Almighty's saying: So the blast overtook them at sunrise is an accusative of state, meaning at the time of sunrise. It is said: the sun shone, meaning it illuminated, and shone if it rose. It was said: they are two languages with the same meaning. And the people shone, meaning they entered at the time of sunrise. Like they became morning and evening, which is what is meant in the verse. It was said: he meant the rising of dawn. It was said: the first of the punishment was at dawn and extended until sunrise, so the complete destruction was at that time. And God knows best. And the blast is the punishment.
15:74: And the mention of Sijil was presented.
15:75: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: For those who see things clearly. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim narrated in Nawadir Al-Usul “from the hadith of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: For those who see things clearly.” This is the saying of Mujahid. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Beware of the insight of the believer, for he sees with the light of God - then he recited - ‘Indeed in that are signs for those who see things clearly.’ He said: This is a strange hadith. Muqatil and Ibn Zayd said: For those who see things clearly, for those who think. Ad-Dahhak: For those who observe. The poet said: Or whenever a tribe came to Ukaz, they would send to their chief to look for Qatada said: For those who consider. Zuhair said: They are a place of entertainment for the friend and an elegant sight for the discerning observer. Abu Ubaidah said: For those who have insight, and the meaning is close. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim narrated from a hadith of Thabit on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God, the Almighty, has servants who know people by their signs. The scholars said: Signs are derived from the word wasm, which is the sign by which one deduces what is desired other than it. It is said: I saw good in him if you saw the mark of that in him, and from this is the saying of Abdullah bin Rawahah to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I saw good in you, I know it, and God knows that I have a steady vision last: I saw his majesty when I saw him and I said that the man was from the Hashim family A man is described as someone who makes a mark for himself by which he is known. A man is described as someone who seeks out the best pastures. He recited: And they became like soft palm trees, heading towards the destination of a traveler looking forward. Tha'lab said: The one who looks at you from your forehead to your feet. The origin of tawasam is verification and contemplation. It is taken from wasam which is the effect of a sharp edge on the skin of a camel or other animal. This is done through good intelligence, sharpness of mind, and clarity of thought. Another added: And emptying the heart of the world's stuffing, and purifying it from the filth of sins, the turbidity of morals, and the superfluity of the world. Nahshal narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas for those who look at signs: For the people of righteousness and goodness. The Sufis claimed that it is a miracle. It was said: Rather, it is evidence by signs. Some signs appear clearly to everyone at first glance, and some are hidden and are not apparent to everyone and are not perceived at first glance. Al-Hasan said: "The ones who look at things are those who look at things and know that the One who destroyed the people of Lot is able to destroy the infidels. This is one of the apparent signs." Similar to it is the saying of Ibn Abbas: No one asked me about anything except that I knew whether he was a jurist or not. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Shafi’i and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan that they were in the courtyard of the Kaaba and a man was at the door of the mosque. One of them said: I think he is a carpenter, and the other said: Rather, he is a blacksmith. Those present rushed to the man and asked him. He said: I used to be a carpenter and today I am a blacksmith. It was narrated on the authority of Jundub ibn Abdullah Al-Bajali that he came upon a man reciting the Quran. He stopped and said: Whoever listens, God will listen to him, and whoever shows off, God will show off to him. We said to him: It is as if you have presented this man. He said: This man is reciting the Quran to you today and tomorrow he will become a Kharijite. So he was the head of the Kharijites, and his name was Mirdas. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that Amr ibn Ubayd entered upon him and said: This is the master of the young men of Basra if he does not speak. So what happened to him was fate, until most of his brothers abandoned him. He said to Ayoub: This is the master of the young men of Basra, and he did not make any exceptions. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Sha'bi that he said to Dawud Al-Azdi while he was arguing with him: You will not die until your head is branded, and that was the case. It was narrated that a group of people from Madhhij, including Al-Ashtar, entered upon Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him. He looked at him and straightened his head and said: Who is this? They said: Malik bin Al-Harith. He said: What is wrong with him, may God kill him! I see that the Muslims will have a difficult day because of him, and he caused the strife that happened. It was narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Affan may God be pleased with him: Anas bin Malik entered upon him, and he had passed by the market and looked at a woman. When he looked at him, Uthman said: One of you enters upon me while there is the trace of adultery in his eyes! Anas said to him: Is there revelation after the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him)? He said: No! But it is proof, insight, and truthfulness. And many of the Companions and Followers may God be pleased with them all are like him. Second: Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: “If it is proven that physiognomy and discernment are among the means of understanding meanings, then no ruling is based on that, and neither a physiognomist nor a discerner is to be taken into account. The chief judge of Sham, the Maliki, in Baghdad during the days I was in Sham, used to rule by physiognomy in rulings, following the path of Iyas Ibn Muawiyah when he was a judge. And our sheikh, Fakhr Al-Islam Abu Bakr Al-Shashi, composed a section in response to him, which he wrote to me in his own handwriting and gave to me. And that is correct, for the means of understanding rulings are known by the Shari’ah and are definitely understood, and physiognomy is not among them.”
15:76: God Almighty says: And indeed it meaning the villages of Lot’s people. is on a straight path meaning on the path of your people, O Muhammad, to the Levant.
15:77: Indeed in that is a sign for the believers. That is, a lesson for those who believe.
15:78: And indeed, the companions of the thicket were wrongdoers. He means the people of Shu'ayb, they were the companions of thickets, meadows, and fruitful trees. The thicket is the thicket, which is a group of trees, and the plural is ayk. It is narrated that their tree was always dry, which is the maql. Al-Nabigha said: A dove, with my coming, sweeps away the cold of the forest, and smears his gums with kohl. It was said: Al-Aykah is the name of the village. It was also said that it is the name of the town. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Aykah is the walika of their city, like Bakkah is to Mecca. The story of Shuaib and his people was mentioned earlier.
15:79: And indeed, they are on a clear path meaning on a path that is clear in itself, meaning the city of the people of Lot and the place of the People of the Thicket, which those who pass by them will consider.
15:80: The word stone has many meanings: one of them is the stone of the Kaaba. The other is the sacred place, God the Almighty said: And a forbidden stone (al-Furqan 25:53), meaning forbidden and forbidden. The stone is the mind, God the Almighty said: For the one with reason (al-Fajr 89:5). The stone is the stone of the shirt, and the opening is more eloquent. The stone is the female horse. The stone is the circling of Thamud, and this is what is meant here, meaning Madinah, Al-Azhari said: Qatada: It is between Mecca and Tabuk, and it is the valley in which Thamud is. Al-Tabari: It is a land between Hijaz and Ash-Sham, and they are the people of Salih. He said: The Messengers means Salih alone, but whoever denies a prophet has denied all the prophets, because they are of one religion in the principles, so it is not permissible to differentiate between them. It was said: They denied Salih and those who followed him and those who came before him from the prophets as well. And God knows best. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Al-Hijr during the Battle of Tabuk, he ordered them not to drink from its well or draw water from it. They said: We have kneaded and drawn water. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to pour out the water and to throw away the dough.” In Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: “The people came down with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Al-Hijr, the land of Thamud. They drew water from its wells and kneaded the dough with it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to pour out what they had drawn and feed the dough to the camels. He ordered them to draw water from the well that the female camel would drink from.” It was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar who said: “We passed by Al-Hijr with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to us: ‘Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves unless you are weeping, for fear that what happened to them will happen to you. Then he warned and hastened.” I said: In this verse, which the Lawgiver explained and its ruling and clarified his command, there are eight issues, which scholars have deduced and jurists have differed about some of them. The first of them: It is disliked to enter those places, and some scholars have interpreted entering the graveyards of the infidels as such. If a person enters any of those places and graveyards, then he should do so in the manner that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) guided us to, of consideration, fear, and hastening. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do not enter the land of Babylon, for it is cursed. Question: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that what they had drawn from the well of Thamud be poured out and that what had been kneaded and baked with it be thrown away because it was water of wrath, so it was not permissible to benefit from it in order to escape God’s wrath. He said, Feed it to the camels. I said: This is the ruling on impure water and what is kneaded with it. Second: Malik said: That which is not permissible to use of food and drink may be fed to camels and cattle, since they are not obligated to do so. He also said about impure honey: It is fed to bees. Third: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered that what is kneaded with this water be fed to camels, and he did not order that it be discarded as he ordered with the meat of domesticated donkeys on the day of Khaybar. This indicates that the meat of donkeys is more forbidden and more severe in its impurity. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered that the earnings of the cupper be fed to the camel and the slave, and this was not for the sake of prohibition or impurity. Al-Shafi’i said: If it were forbidden, he would not have ordered him to feed it to his slave, because he is worshipping in it as he worships in himself. Fourth: In his (peace and blessings of God be upon him) order to feed the camels dough, there is evidence that it is permissible for a man to carry impurity to his dogs so that they may eat it, contrary to those of our companions who forbade that and said: The dogs should be released on it and not carried to them. Fifth: His command, may God bless him and grant him peace, to draw water from the well of the she-camel is evidence of seeking blessings from the relics of the prophets and righteous people, even if their eras have passed and their traces have disappeared. Just as the first is evidence of hating the people of corruption and denouncing their homes and relics. This, even though the truth is that inanimate objects are not to be blamed, but that which is associated with the beloved is beloved, and that which is associated with the hated and abhorrent is hated, as Katheer said: I love Sudan for its love, so much so that I love black dogs for its love. As another said: I pass by the houses, the houses of Layla, I approach this wall and that wall It is not those lands that captivate my heart, but the love of those who inhabit those lands. Sixth: Some scholars forbade praying in this place and said: It is not permissible to pray there because it is a place of wrath and a place of anger. Ibn al-Arabi said: So this place is an exception to the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The earth has been made for me a place of prostration and purification. It is not permissible to perform tayammum with its soil, or to perform ablution with its water, or to pray there. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade praying in seven places: in a garbage dump, a slaughterhouse, a graveyard, on the main road, in a bathroom, in camel watering places, and on top of the House of God.” In this regard, on the authority of Abu Marthad, Jabir and Anas: The chain of transmission of the hadeeth of Ibn ‘Umar is not that strong, and Zayd ibn Jubayrah has been criticized for his memory. Our scholars have added: a usurped house, a church, a synagogue, a house in which there are statues, usurped land, or a place where you face a sleeping person, or the face of a man, or a wall on which there is impurity. Ibn al-Arabi said: Among these places are those that are forbidden for the right of others, and those that are forbidden for the right of God, and those that are forbidden for the sake of proven impurity or its predominance. What is forbidden for the sake of impurity, if a clean garment is spread in it, such as a bathroom and a cemetery is in it or to it, then that is permissible in the Mudawwana. Abu Musab mentioned that it is disliked. Our scholars differentiated between old and new cemeteries for the sake of impurity, and between the cemeteries of Muslims and polytheists, because it is a house of torment and a place of wrath like a stone. Malik said in al-Majmu`ah: One should not pray in camel pens, even if a garment is required, as if he saw two reasons for it: covering oneself with it and repelling it, so it spoils the prayer of the one praying. If it is one, then there is no problem, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to do, in the authentic hadith. Malik said: One should not pray on a rug that has statues on it except out of necessity. Ibn al-Qasim disliked praying towards the qiblah in which there are statues, and in a usurped house, but if he did that, it would suffice. Some of them mentioned from Malik that praying in a usurped house is not valid. Ibn al-Arabi said: This, in my opinion, is unlike land, as a house cannot be entered without permission, and even if land is owned, the mosque is established in it and ownership does not invalidate it. I said: The correct view - God willing - that which is indicated by observation and the hadith is that prayer in any pure place is permissible and correct. And what was narrated from the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: This is a valley in which there is a devil, and Muammar narrated it from Al-Zuhri, who said: And leave the place where you were overcome by heedlessness. And the saying of Ali: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade me from praying in the land of Babylon, for it is cursed. And his saying, peace be upon him, when he passed by Al-Hijr of Thamud: Do not enter upon these tormented people unless you are crying, and his prohibition of praying in camel watering places and other things in this chapter, then it is returned to the agreed upon principles and the evidence whose origin is correct. Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Omar said: The preferred opinion in our view in this regard is that this valley and other places on earth are permissible to pray in all of them as long as there is no certain impurity in them that prevents that. There is no meaning to the argument of those who argue that the place of the letter nun for prayer is the place of Satan and a cursed place in which prayer should not be performed. Everything that has been narrated in this regard regarding the prohibition of praying in the cemetery, in the land of Babylon, in camel pens, and other things of this meaning, all of that in our view is abrogated and rejected due to the generality of his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace: The entire earth has been made a place of prostration and purification for me, and his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace, informing us that this is from its virtues and from what it has been enriched with. According to the people of knowledge, its virtues cannot be abrogated, changed, or diminished. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I have been given five things - and it has been narrated as six, and it has been narrated as three and four, and it goes up to more than nine, and he said about them - that no one before me was given them. I was sent to the red and the black, and I was aided by terror, and my nation was made the best of nations, and spoils were made lawful for me, and the earth was made a place of prostration and purification for me, and I was given intercession, and I was sent with the most comprehensive words, and while I was asleep, the keys of the earth were brought to me and placed in my hand, and I was given al-Kawthar, and the prophets were sealed with me.” It was narrated by a group of the Companions. Some of them mention some of them, and some of them mention what no one else mentioned, and they are all authentic. It is permissible to add to his virtues and it is not permissible to subtract from them. Do you not see that he was a slave before he was a prophet, and then he was a prophet before he was a messenger? This is also narrated from him. He said: And I do not know what will be done with me or with you (al-Ahqaf 46:9). Then the verse was revealed: That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come. (al-Fath 48:2) And he heard a man say to him: O best of creation, so he said: That is Abraham. And he said: Let none of you say I am better than Jonah, son of Matta. And he said: The master Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, peace be upon them. Then he said after all of that: I am the master of the sons of Adam, and I do not boast. So his virtues, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to increase until God took him, so from here we said: It is not permissible to abrogate, except, or decrease them, and it is permissible to increase them. And with his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: The earth has been made a place of prostration and purification for me, we permit prayer in the graveyard, the bathroom, and in any place on earth if it is pure from impurities. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Dharr: Wherever the prayer overtakes you, pray, for the entire earth is a place of prostration. Al-Bukhari mentioned this and did not specify a specific place in the hadith. As for those who used the hadith of Ibn Wahb as evidence, he said: Yahya bin Ayoub told me, on the authority of Zaid bin Jubayra, on the authority of Dawud bin Husayn, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar. The hadith of al-Tirmidhi that we mentioned is a hadith that Zaid bin Jubayra narrated alone and he rejected it, and this hadith is not known to have a chain of transmission except through the narration of Yahya bin Ayoub, on the authority of Zaid bin Jubayra. Al-Layth bin Sa’d wrote to Abdullah bin Nafi’, the freed slave of Ibn Umar, asking him about this hadith, and Abdullah bin Nafi’ wrote to him: I do not know of anyone who narrated this on the authority of Nafi’ except that he said something false about him. Al-Halwani mentioned it on the authority of Sa’id bin Abi Maryam on the authority of al-Layth, and it does not specify the cemetery of the polytheists from others. It was narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, who said: “My beloved, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade me from praying in the cemetery, and he forbade me from praying in the land of Babylon, for it is cursed.” Its chain of transmission is weak and unanimously agreed upon as weak. Abu Salih, who narrated it on the authority of Ali, is Sa’id bin Abd al-Rahman al-Ghifari, a man from Basra who is not well-known and it is not authentic for him to have heard from Ali, and those below him are unknown and not known. Abu Omar said: There is a hadith on the topic from Ali, from his saying, not traceable back to the Prophet, when the chain of transmission was established. It was narrated by Al-Fadl bin Dukayn, who said: Al-Mughirah bin Abi Al-Hurr Al-Kindi told us, who said: Abu Al-Anbas Hajar bin Anbas told me, who said: We went out with Ali to the Kharijites, and when we passed Syria, he landed in the land of Babylon. We said: O Commander of the Faithful, the evening has come, the prayer, the prayer, but he refused to speak to anyone. They said: O Commander of the Faithful, it has come. He said: Yes, but I will not pray in a land that God has swallowed up. Al-Mughirah bin Abi Al-Hurr is trustworthy from Kufa, as stated by Yahya bin Ma’in and others. Hajar bin Anbas was one of the great companions of Ali. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The entire earth is a place of prayer except the graveyard and the bathroom. Al-Tirmidhi said: Sufyan Al-Thawri narrated it from Amr bin Yahya from his father from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as a mursal hadith, and it seems to be more authentic and more correct. Abu Omar said: So it is not permissible to use it as evidence for those who do not see the mursal hadith as evidence, and if it had been proven, the correct view would have been as we mentioned. We do not say, as some of those who adhere to the Madani school of thought have said, that the cemetery in this hadith and others is specifically intended to refer to the cemetery of the polytheists, because he said: the cemetery and the bathroom with the definite article, so it is not permissible to refer that to a cemetery or a bathroom without a bathroom without a reference to it, so it is a statement for which there is no evidence from the Book or the Sunnah or a sound hadith, and it has no place in analogy or reason, and the meaning of the speech does not indicate it nor does the hadith go beyond it. The specification of the one who specified the cemetery of the polytheists is not without one of two aspects: Either it is because the disbelievers go to it with their feet, so there is no meaning to mentioning the cemetery specifically, because every place they are in with their bodies and feet is like that, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was too great to speak about something that has no meaning. Or it is because it is a place of wrath, for if that were the case, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have built his mosque in the cemetery of the polytheists, and he would not have dug it up, leveled it, and built on it. If it were permissible for someone to specify a cemetery from the cemeteries for prayer in, then the cemetery of the polytheists would be more deserving of specialization and exception because of this hadith.
