Whoever dislikes praying in a cemetery does not distinguish one cemetery from another, because the alif and lam indicate a type, not a known thing. If there was a difference between the cemetery of the Muslims and the cemetery of the polytheists, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would have made it clear and not given him time, because he was sent to clarify. If it were permissible for an ignorant person to say: such-and-such cemetery, it would be permissible for another to say: such-and-such bathroom, because in the hadeeth there is the cemetery and the bathroom. Likewise his saying: the garbage dump and the slaughterhouse, it is not permissible to say: such-and-such garbage dump, nor such-and-such slaughterhouse, nor such-and-such road, because it is not permissible to control the religion of God. The scholars agreed that performing tayammum on a polytheist graveyard is permissible if the place is clean, pure and clean. They also agreed that whoever prays in a church or synagogue on a clean place, his prayer is valid and permissible. This was mentioned previously in Surat Bara’ah. It is known that a church is closer to being a place of wrath than a cemetery, because it is a place where God is disobeyed and disbelieved in, but the cemetery is not like that. The Sunnah has mentioned that synagogues and churches are to be taken as mosques. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Talq ibn ‘Ali who said: We went out as a delegation to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and we pledged allegiance to him and prayed with him, and we informed him that there is a synagogue for us in our land, and he mentioned the hadith in which it says: So when you come to your land, break your synagogue and take it as a mosque. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of ‘Uthman ibn Abi al-‘As: “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered him to make the mosque of Ta’if where their idolaters were.” This was mentioned previously in Bara’ah. It is sufficient for you that the Prophet’s mosque (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was founded on piety and built in a polytheist graveyard, and it is an argument against everyone who dislikes praying there. Among those who disliked praying in a graveyard, whether it belongs to Muslims or polytheists, were Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah, Al-Awza’i, Al-Shafi’i and their companions. According to Al-Thawri, one should not repeat the prayer. According to Al-Shafi’i, it is sufficient if he prays in a graveyard in a place where there is no impurity, based on the well-known hadiths on that, and the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Pray in your homes and do not turn them into graves, and the hadith of Abu Marthad Al-Ghanawi that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Do not pray towards graves and do not sit on them. These two hadiths are authentic in terms of their chain of transmission, but they are not evidence, because they are open to interpretation. One should not refrain from praying in any pure place except with evidence that is not open to interpretation. None of the Muslim jurists differentiated between the graveyards of Muslims and polytheists, except for what we have mentioned of the fallacy of the statement that should not be considered, and it has no basis in consideration or in any authentic report. Eighth: A wall into which filth and excrement are thrown so that it may be honored, so one should not pray in it until it is watered three times, based on what was narrated by Ad-Daraqutni on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding a wall into which filth and excrement are thrown. He said: If it is watered three times, then pray in it. He also narrated it from the hadith of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar: “He was asked about these walls into which filth and manure are thrown, can one pray in them? He said: If it is watered three times, then pray in it.” This was traced back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. They differed in the chain of transmission, and God knows best.
15:81: The Almighty said: And We gave them Our signs meaning with Our signs. Like His saying: Give us our food (al-Kahf 18:62), meaning with our lunch. What is meant is the she-camel, and there were many signs in her: her emergence from the rock, the closeness of her offspring when she emerged, her size so that she did not resemble a she-camel, and the abundance of her milk so that it was sufficient for them all. It is possible that there were other signs besides the she-camel, such as the well and others. So they turned away from her meaning they did not take heed.
15:82: Sculpting in Arabic: carving and carving. He carved it in the broken form means he polished it. And the carving is the polishing. And the carving is what is carved with. And in the revelation: Do you worship what you carve? (al-Saffat 37:95) meaning you carve and make. So they used to make houses for themselves in the mountains due to their great strength. Safe meaning from falling on them or being destroyed. And it was said: Safe from death. And it was said: from punishment.
15:83: So the blast overtook them in the morning meaning at the time of dawn, and it is an accusative of state. The blast was mentioned previously in Hud and Al-A'raf.
15:84: What they earned did not avail them of money and fortresses in the mountains, nor did what they were given of power.
15:85: The Almighty said: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and all that is between them except in truth meaning for the sake of disappearance and annihilation. It was said: meaning to reward the doer of good and the wrongdoer, as He said: And to God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth that He may reward those who do evil for what they have done and reward those who do good with good (al-Najm 53:31). And indeed, the Hour is coming meaning it will happen, so each will be rewarded for his deeds. So pardon with gracious pardon like And leave them with gracious leave (al-Muzzammil 73:10), meaning overlook them, O Muhammad, and pardon with gracious pardon, then it was abrogated by the sword. Qatada said: It was abrogated by His statement: So seize them and kill them wherever you find them (al-Nisa 4:91). And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: I have come to you with slaughter and I was sent with harvest, and I was not sent with agriculture, as Ikrimah and Mujahid said. It was said: It is not abrogated, and that he ordered forgiveness of himself in what is between him and them. Forgiveness means turning away, according to Al-Hasan and others.
15:86: Your Lord is the Creator meaning the One who determines creation and morals. The Knower of the people of harmony and hypocrisy.
15:87: Scholars differed regarding the seven Mathani. Some said: Al-Fatihah. This was said by Ali bin Abi Talib, Abu Hurairah, Al-Rabi bin Anas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Al-Hasan and others. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, through reliable chains of transmission, from the hadith of Ubayy bin Ka'b and Abu Sa'id bin Al-Mu'alla. It was mentioned earlier in the interpretation of Al-Fatihah. Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Praise be to God, the Mother of the Qur'an, the Mother of the Book, and the Seven Mathani. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. This is a text, and it was mentioned earlier in Al-Fatihah. The poet said: I ask you by the house of the Qur’an, the Mother of the Book, the seven oft-repeated verses Ibn Abbas said: They are the seven long ones: Al-Baqarah, Al Imran, An-Nisa, Al-Ma'idah, Al-An'am, Al-A'raf, Al-Anfal and At-Tawbah together, as there is no naming between them. An-Nasa'i narrated: Ali bin Hajar told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God the Almighty: Seven of the Mathani, he said: The seven long ones, and they were called Mathani because the lessons, rulings and punishments were repeated in them. Some people denied this and said: This verse was revealed in Mecca, and whoever was sent down from the long ones had something at that time. It was answered that God the Almighty sent down the Qur'an to the lowest heaven and then sent it down from there in stars, so what He sent down to the lowest heaven is as if it had been given to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, even if it had not been sent down to him yet. Among those who said that they are the seven long ones are: Abdullah bin Mas'ud, Abdullah bin Umar, Saeed bin Jubair and Mujahid. Jarir said: May God reward Al-Farazdaq when he spends the night neglecting the Mufassal and Muthani. It was said: Al-Mathani is the entire Qur’an. God Almighty said: A Book whose verses are consistent and oft-repeated (al-Zumar 39:23). This is the opinion of Ad-Dahhak, Tawus, and Abu Malik, and Ibn Abbas said the same. It was called Mathani because the report and stories were repeated in it. Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib said, mourning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: It was a bright light that guided people to the revelation of the Holy Quran. That is, the Qur’an. It was said: What is meant by the seven Mathani are the sections of the Qur’an, such as commands and prohibitions, good tidings and warnings, giving examples, enumerating blessings, and report of generations. This was said by Ziyad ibn Abi Maryam. The first is correct because it is explicit. We have already mentioned in Al-Fatihah that there is nothing in calling it Mathani that prevents calling others by that name, except that if a text is reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there is an authentic text from him about something that can be interpreted, then we should stop at it. The Almighty’s saying: And the Great Qur’an contains an implied meaning, which is: that Al-Fatihah is the Great Qur’an, as it includes what is related to the principles of Islam. This has been mentioned previously in Al-Fatihah. It has been said that the waw is an insertion, meaning: And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses of the Great Qur’an. And from this is the saying of the poet: To the venerable king, the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded place It was mentioned earlier when he said: Guard strictly the prayers, especially the middle prayer (al-Baqarah 2:238).
15:88: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Do not extend your eyes meaning: I have enriched you with the Qur’an over what is in the hands of the people, for he is not one of us who does not sing with the Qur’an, meaning he is not one of us who sees that he is not satisfied with what he has of the Qur’an until his sight aspires to the adornments of this world while he has the knowledge of the Master. It is said that he met seven caravans from Basra and Adhra’at of the Jews of Qurayza and Nadir in one day, in which were wheat, perfume, jewels, and sea goods. The Muslims said: If this wealth were ours, we would strengthen ourselves with it and spend it in the way of God. So God the Almighty revealed: And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated [verses] meaning they are better for you than the seven caravans, so do not extend your eyes to them. Ibn Uyaynah agreed with this and cited his saying, peace be upon him: He is not one of us who does not sing with the Qur’an meaning he who does not feel satisfied with it. This meaning was mentioned earlier in the book. The meaning of pairs among them is similar in blessings, meaning the rich are similar to each other in wealth, so they are pairs. Second: This verse requires a warning against constantly longing for worldly pleasures, and for the servant to devote himself to the worship of his Lord. And similar to it is And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, the splendor of worldly life, by which We test them. (Ta-Ha 20:131) The verse. It is not so, for it was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Of your worldly things, women and perfume have been made beloved to me, and the delight of my eyes is in prayer. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, was preoccupied with women, as is human nature and a desire for human creation, and he preserved perfume, and his eyes were not content except in prayer when communing with God. He saw that communing with Him was more appropriate and more deserving than that. And in the religion of Muhammad there was no monasticism and a complete dedication to righteous deeds as there was in the religion of Jesus, but God Almighty legislated a pure, easy-going religion free from hardship, light on the human being, taking from humanity its desires and returning to God with a sound heart. The readers and the sincere virtuous people saw that abstaining from pleasures and being sincere to the Lord of the earth and the heavens is more appropriate today, because the world is dominated by what is forbidden, and the servant is forced in his livelihood to mix with those with whom it is not permissible to mix and to befriend those with whom it is forbidden to befriend. So the readers were better, and fleeing from the world is more correct and more just for the servant. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A time will come upon the people when the best wealth of the Muslim will be sheep that he follows to the peaks of the mountains and to the places where rain falls, fleeing with his religion from trials.” God the Almighty said: And do not grieve over them meaning, do not grieve over the polytheists if they do not believe. It was said: The meaning is, do not grieve over what they enjoyed in this world, for you will have something better than it in the Hereafter. It was also said: Do not grieve over them if they are punished, for they are the people of punishment. And lower your wing to the believers meaning, be gentle with those who believe in you and are humble towards them. Its origin is that when a bird brings its chick close to itself, it spreads its wing and then seizes the chick, so this was made a description of how a person brings his followers close. It is said: So-and-so has lowered his wing, or is dignified and calm. The two wings of the son of Adam are his sides, and from this, And bring your hand to your wing (Ta-Ha: 22), and the wing of the bird is its hand. The poet said: It is enough for you, young man, for a leader of a people to extend a wing over my sick brother. Either humble or gentle.
15:89: There is an omission in the speech, meaning that I am the warner who makes clear the punishment, so the object was omitted, since the warning indicates it, as He said in another place: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ‘Aad and Thamud (Fussilat 41:13).
15:90: It was said: The Kaf is redundant, meaning I warned you of what We sent down upon those who divided, like His saying: There is nothing like Him (al-Shura 42:11). It was also said: I warned you of what We sent down upon those who divided. It was also said: The meaning is as We sent down upon those who divided, meaning from the punishment and We sufficed you against the mockers, so proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists who transgressed, for We sufficed you against those leaders from whom you were receiving what you were receiving. There are seven opinions regarding the dividers: First: Muqatil and Al-Farraa said: They are sixteen men sent by Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira during the season. They divided the paths, valleys and passes of Mecca, saying to those who took them: Do not be deceived by this one who came among us claiming prophethood, for he is crazy. And sometimes they said he is a magician, a poet, or a soothsayer. They were called the dividers because they divided these paths, so God caused them to die the worst death. They appointed Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira as a judge at the door of the mosque, and when they asked him about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would say: They are the truth. Second: Qatada said: They are a group of the infidels of Quraysh who divided the Book of God, making some of it poetry, some of it magic, some of it divination, and some of it legends of the ancients. Third: Ibn Abbas said: They are the People of the Book who believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. And Ikrimah said the same: They are the People of the Book, and they were called the dividers because they were mocking, some of them would say: This Surah is for me and this Surah is for you. And this is the fourth opinion. Fifth: Qatada said: They divided their book, so they divided it, scattered it, and distorted it. Sixth: Zaid bin Aslam said: What is meant are the people of Salih, who divided over killing him, so they were called dividers, as God Almighty said: They divided by God that we would surely kill him and his family (al-Naml 27:49). Seventh: Al-Akhfash said: They are a people who took oaths and swore an oath. It was said: They are Al-Aas bin Wa’il, Utbah and Shaiba, the sons of Rabi’ah, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, Abu Al-Bukhtari bin Hisham, Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, Umayyah bin Khalaf, and Munabbih bin Al-Hajjaj. Al-Mawardi mentioned this.
15:91: This is the description of the dividers. It was said: It is the subject and its predicate is We will ask them. The singular of the two parts is a bite, from the verb to divide something, meaning to separate it, and every division is a bite. Some of them said: It was originally a limb, then the waw was missing, and that is why the two parts were pluralized, just as they said: Izzeen in the plural of Izzah, and the original is Izzwah. And so are Thaba and Thabeen. The meaning goes back to what we mentioned in the dividers. Ibn Abbas said: They believed in some and disbelieved in some. It was said: They divided their statements about him and made it lies, magic, divination and poetry. I divided him, meaning I separated him. The poet - he is Ru'bah - said: God's religion is not a solution That is, in separate parts. It is said: its missing letter is ha’ and its root is ‘adhah’, because ‘adhah’ and ‘adh’ayn in the language of Quraysh mean magic. They say to the magician: ‘Aadah’ and to the witch ‘Aadah’. The poet said: I seek refuge in my Lord from those who blow on knots of biting gums. In the hadith: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the one who bites and the one who seeks to be bitten, and he explained: the witch and the one who seeks to be bewitched. The meaning is: the one who slanders the Quran a lot and they spread lies about it, so they said: magic and legends of the ancients, and that it is fabricated, and so on. The same as `udhah in deficiency is lip, and the original is lipha. Just as they said: sunnah, and the original is sanah, so they reduced the original ha and kept the ha of the sign, which is for the feminine. It was said: it is from `udhah, which is gossip. `udhiyah is slander, which is that a person bites it and says about it what is not in it. It is said: `adhahhu `adhah, he accused him of slander. And I have bitten it, meaning I have come with slander. Al-Kisa’i said: `udhah is lying and slander, and its plural is `udhun, like `azzah and `azun. God the Almighty said: Those who have made the Qur’an into parts. It is said: they have bitten it, meaning they believed in what they liked of it and disbelieved in the rest, so their disbelief has nullified their faith. Al-Farra’ believed that it was taken from the tree of the valley, which grows like a thorn.
15:92: The Almighty said: By your Lord, We will surely question them all meaning, We will surely question those who were mentioned about what they did in this world. In Al-Bukhari: Several scholars said about His statement: By your Lord, We will surely question them all * About what they used to do about There is no god but God. I said: This has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim narrated: Al-Jarud bin Muadh told us: Al-Fadl bin Musa told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Bishr bin Nahik, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement:
15:93: By your Lord, We will surely question them all * About what they used to do." He said: About saying "There is no god but God." Abu Abdullah said: Its meaning to us is about the truthfulness of "There is no god but God" and its fulfillment, because God the Most High mentioned the work in His revelation, saying: "About what they used to do, and He did not say About what they used to say." Although it is possible that the saying is also the work of the tongue, what is meant by it is what the linguists know, that the saying is saying and the work is work. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "About There is no god but God, meaning about fulfilling it and being truthful to its statement. As Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Faith is not by adornment, nor is religion by wishful thinking, but rather what is established in the hearts and confirmed by actions. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever says There is no god but God sincerely will enter Paradise. It was said: O Messenger of God, and what is its sincerity? He said: That it prevents him from the forbidden things of God." Narrated by Zaid bin Arqam. It was also narrated from him that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God has promised me that no one from my nation will come to me with ‘There is no god but God’ and mix it with anything else, except that Paradise will be guaranteed for him. They said: O Messenger of God, what is mixed with ‘There is no god but God’? He said: “Out of eagerness for the world and collecting it and meaning it. They say the words of the prophets and do the deeds of the tyrants.” Anas bin Malik narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no god but God protects the servants from God’s wrath so long as they do not give priority to their worldly affairs over their religion. But if they give priority to their worldly affairs over their religion and then say ‘There is no god but God’, it will be rejected and God will say, ‘You have lied.’” Its chains of transmission are in Nawader al-Usul. I said: The verse in its generality indicates that everyone will be questioned and held accountable, whether they are disbelievers or believers, except for those who enter Paradise without being held accountable, as we explained in the Book of At-Tadhkirah. If it is said: Will the disbeliever be questioned and held accountable? We say: There is a difference of opinion about this, and we mentioned it in At-Tadhkirah. What appears is that he will be questioned, based on the verse and His statement: Stop them, for indeed, they will be questioned 37:24 and His statement: “Indeed, to Us is their return. Then, upon Us is their account” (al-Ghashiyah 88:25-26). If it is said: God the Almighty said: And the criminals will not be asked about their sins (al-Qasas 28:78) and He said: So on that Day, neither man nor jinn will be asked about his sin (al-Rahman 55:39), and He said: And God will not speak to them on the Day (al-Baqarah 2:174), and He said: Indeed, from their Lord, that Day, they will be veiled (al-Mutaffifin 83:15). We say: The Resurrection has places, so there is a place where there will be questioning and speaking, and a place where that will not be. Ikrimah said: The Day of Resurrection will be held in different situations, and He will ask them in some of them and not in others. Ibn Abbas said: He will not ask them a question of inquiry and inquiry, Did you do such and such? because God knows everything. Rather, He will ask them a question of rebuke and rebuke, saying to them: Why did you disobey the Qur’an and what is your proof for it? Qatrib relied on this statement. It was said: We will question them all, meaning the accountable believers. This is explained by the statement of God the Almighty: Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure. (al-Takathur 102:8). The general statement is more appropriate, as mentioned. And God knows best.
15:94: The Almighty said: So proclaim that which you are commanded meaning that which you are commanded to do, meaning convey the message of God to all of creation so that the proof is established against them, for God has commanded you to do so. And sharding means splitting. And the people split apart means they dispersed, and from this is On that Day they will be split apart" (al-Rum 30:43) meaning they will disperse. And "shardtuhu fanashada" means it split. And the root of "sharding is dividing and splitting". Abu Dhu'ayb said, describing the donkey and his female donkey: As if they were a lute, and as if it were joy overflowing onto the cup and cracking That is, it separates and splits. So his statement, Proclaim that which you are commanded Al-Farra’ said: He meant, Proclaim the matter, meaning, make your religion manifest. So, ma with the verb in this case is like a verbal noun. Ibn Al-A’rabi said: The meaning of Proclaim what you are commanded is, intend. And it was said, Proclaim what you are commanded means, divide their gathering and their word by calling them to monotheism, for they will be divided by some responding. So, the split in this case refers to the split of a group of disbelievers. God the Almighty said: And turn away from the polytheists meaning, do not care about their mockery or pay attention to what they say, for God has declared you innocent of what they say. Ibn Abbas said: It was abrogated by His statement: Then kill the polytheists (al-Tawbah 9:5). Abdullah bin Ubaid said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) continued to hide until God the Almighty’s statement: Then proclaim what you are commanded was revealed, so he and his companions went out. Mujahid said: He meant reciting the Qur’an aloud in prayer. And turn away from the polytheists do not pay attention to them. Ibn Ishaq said: When they persisted in their evil and increased their mockery of God’s Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him), God the Almighty revealed: “Then proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists. Indeed, We are sufficient for you against the mockers. Those who set up with God another deity. They are going to know.”
15:95: Meaning: Declare what you are commanded to do and do not fear anyone but God, for God will suffice you against your harm as He sufficed you against those who mocked you. They were five of the leaders of the people of Mecca, and they were Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira who was their leader, Al-Aas bin Wa'il, Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib bin Asad Abu Zama'a, Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth, and Al-Harith bin Al-Talalatlah. God destroyed them all, it was said on the day of Badr on the same day, because they mocked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The reason for their destruction, as mentioned by Ibn Ishaq, was that Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while they were circumambulating the House. He stood up and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and Al-Aswad bin Al-Muttalib passed by him and threw a green leaf in his face, so he went blind and his eye hurt, so he started hitting the wall with his head. Al-Aswad bin Abd Yaghuth passed by him and he pointed to his stomach, so his stomach vomited and he died from it of love. (It is said: Habna (with a kasra) Habna and Habna for the passive participle whose belly became large with yellow water, so he is Ahban, and the woman is Habna, as stated in Al-Sahah). Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira passed by him and pointed to the mark of a wound at the bottom of his heel, which had occurred to him years before, while he was dragging his paths. That was because he passed by a man from Khuza’ah who was feathering his arrows, and one of his arrows got stuck in his garment and scratched his leg with that scratch, which was nothing, so it fell back and killed him. Al-Aas bin Wa’il passed by him and pointed to the fifth of his foot, so he went out on a donkey with him, intending to go to Taif, so he lay down with him on a thorn, so a thorn entered the fifth of his foot and killed him. Al-Harith bin Al-Talalatah passed by him, so he pointed to his head and blew pus and was killed. A difference close to this has been mentioned regarding the cause of their death. It was said that they are the ones meant by the Almighty’s saying: So the roof fell upon them from above them (al-Nahl 16:26). He likened what happened to them in their death to the roof falling upon them, as will come.
15:96: This is the description of the mockers. It was said: It is a beginning and its predicate is they will know.
15:97: God Almighty says: And We certainly know that your breast is constrained meaning your heart, because the breast is the location of the heart. Because of what they say meaning because of what you hear of your denial and rejection of your words, and what you and your companions among your enemies suffer from.
15:98: There are two issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: So glorify meaning, hasten to prayer, for it is the ultimate glorification and the ultimate sanctification. This is an explanation of His saying: And be among those who prostrate. It is no secret that the ultimate closeness in prayer is during prostration, as the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so make supplication sincere. That is why He specifically mentioned prostration. Second: Ibn al-Arabi said: Some people thought that what was meant by the command here was prostration itself, so they saw this place as a place of prostration in the Qur’an. I saw the Imam in the prayer niche of Zachariah in the Holy House, may God purify him, prostrating in this place and I prostrated with him in it, but the majority of scholars did not see that. I said: Abu Bakr al-Naqqash mentioned that there is a prostration here according to Abu Hudhayfah and Yaman ibn Ri’ab, and he saw that it is obligatory.
15:99: There is only one issue - that certainty is death. He ordered him to worship Him since His servants fell short in serving Him, and that this is obligatory upon Him. If it is said: What is the benefit of His saying until certainty comes to you and His saying and worship your Lord is sufficient in ordering worship? It is said to him: The benefit in this is that if He said and worship your Lord absolutely and then worshipped Him once, he would be obedient, and if He said until certainty comes to you its meaning would be do not leave this until you die. If it is said: How did He, the Most High, say and worship your Lord until certainty comes to you and did not say forever, the answer is that certainty is more eloquent than His saying: forever, because the word forever can mean a single moment or all of eternity. This meaning has been presented. What is meant is the continuation of worship throughout his life, as the righteous servant said: And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I live (Maryam 19:31). It is based on this that if a man says to his wife: You are divorced forever, and he says: I intended a day or a month, then he has to take her back. And if he said: I divorced her during her lifetime, he would not take her back. The evidence that certainty is death is the hadith of Umm Al-Ala’ Al-Ansariyyah, who was one of those who pledged allegiance, in which it says: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “As for Uthman - I mean Uthman bin Maz’un - certainty has come to him, and I hope good for him. By God, I do not know, and I am the Messenger of God, what will happen to him.” And he mentioned the hadith. Al-Bukhari may God have mercy on him was the only one to narrate it! And Umar bin Abdul Aziz used to say: I have never seen certainty more similar to doubt than people’s certainty of death, and then they do not prepare for it, meaning as if they are doubtful about it. It has been said: Certainty here is the truth in which there is no doubt about your victory over your enemies, as Ibn Shajarah said, and the first is more correct, and it is the saying of Mujahid, Qatadah and Al-Hasan. And God knows best. Jubair bin Nufayr narrated on the authority of Abu Muslim Al-Khawlani that he heard him say that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “It has not been revealed to me to accumulate wealth and be among the merchants, but it has been revealed to me to glorify the praises of your Lord and be among those who prostrate and worship your Lord until certainty comes to you.”
16:1: It is all Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata' and Jabir. It is called Surat Al-Na'am because of the blessings God enumerated in it for His servants. It was said that it is Meccan except for the words of God the Almighty: And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted (al-Nahl 16:126), which were revealed in Medina regarding the mutilation of Hamza and the people killed at Uhud. And other than the words of God the Almighty: And be patient, and your patience is not but through God (al-Nahl 16:127). And other than the words of God the Almighty: Then indeed, your Lord is for those who emigrated (al-Nahl 16:110). As for His words: And those who emigrated for the cause of God after they were wronged (al-Nahl 16:41), it is Meccan, regarding the emigration to Abyssinia. Ibn Abbas said: It is Meccan except for three verses that were revealed in Medina after the killing of Hamza, and they are His saying: And do not exchange the covenant of God for a small price (al-Nahl 16:95) - to His saying - with the best of what they used to do (al-Nahl 16:96). God the Almighty said: The command of God has come, so do not be impatient. It was said: It has come means will come, so it is like saying: If you honor Me, I will honor you. It was previously mentioned that God’s report of the past and the future are the same, because He will inevitably come, like His saying: And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire (al-A’raf 7:44). And the command of God is His punishment for those who persist in polytheism and deny His Messenger. Al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj, and Ad-Dahhak said: It is what the Qur’an brought of His obligations and rulings. There is some ambiguity in this, because it was not narrated that any of the Companions hastened God’s obligations before they were imposed upon them. As for those who hastened the punishment and chastisement, this was narrated from many of the infidels of Quraysh and others, to the point that An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith said: O God, if this is the truth from You (al-Anfal 8:32), so he hastened the punishment. I said: Ad-Dahhak may have used as evidence the words of Umar may God be pleased with him: “I agreed with my Lord in three matters: in the station of Abraham, in the veil, and in the captives of Badr.” Narrated by Muslim and Al-Bukhari. It was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah. Az-Zajjaj said: It is what He promised them as recompense for their disbelief, and it is like His saying: Until, when Our command comes and the oven overflows (Hud 11:40). It was said: It is the Day of Resurrection or what indicates its nearness from its signs. Ibn Abbas said: When the verse The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split (al-Qamar 54:1) was revealed, the disbelievers said: This one claims that the Day of Resurrection has drawn near, so refrain from some of what you used to do. They refrained and waited, but they did not see anything. They said: We do not see anything! Then the verse The reckoning of the people has drawn near (al-Anbiya 21:1) was revealed. They feared and waited for the Hour to be near, but the days passed and they said: We do not see anything! Then the verse God's command has come was revealed, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims jumped up and were afraid. Then the verse Do not hasten it was revealed, so they were reassured. Then the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I and the Hour have been sent like these two, and he pointed with his two fingers: the index finger and the one next to it. He said: It almost overtook me, but I overtook it. Ibn Abbas said: The sending of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was one of the signs of the Hour, and when Gabriel passed by the people of the heavens as a messenger to Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), they said: God is Great, the Hour has come. The Almighty says: Glory be to Him and exalted above what they associate with Him. That is, He is far removed from what they describe Him with, that He is not able to bring about the Hour. This is because they say: No one is able to resurrect the dead, so they describe Him with the inability that only a created being can be described with, and that is polytheism. It was also said: Above what they associate with Him meaning from their association. It was also said: What means which, meaning He is exalted above those who associate with Him.
16:2: Al-Mufaddal read on the authority of Asim the angels descend and the original is they descend, so the verb is attributed to the angels. Al-Kisa'i read on the authority of Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim with a difference from him and Al-A'mash the angels descend without the name of the agent. Al-Ja'fi read on the authority of Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim We descend the angels with a noon as the name of the agent, the rest He descends with a ya as the name of the agent, and the pronoun in it is for the name of God Almighty. It was narrated on the authority of Qatada We descend the angels with a noon and with a light pronunciation. Al-A'mash read tanzal with a fatha on the ta and a kasra on the zay, from descent. The angels in the nominative case like the angels descend (al-Qadr 97:4). With the spirit meaning with revelation, which is prophethood, said Ibn Abbas. Similar to it is He casts the spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants (Ghafir 40:15). Al-Rabi' bin Anas: With the speech of God, which is the Qur’an. It was said: It is the explanation of the truth that must be followed. It was said that they are the spirits of creation, as Mujahid said, no angel descends except with a spirit. And it was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that the spirit is a creation of God the Almighty like the images of the son of Adam, no angel descends from the sky except with one of them. And it was said with mercy, as Al-Hasan and Qatadah said. And it was said with guidance, because hearts are revived by it as bodies are revived by spirits, and this is the meaning of what Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Zajjaj said: The spirit is that in which there is life from God’s command by guiding to His command. Abu Ubaidah said: The spirit here is Gabriel. And the ba’ in his statement: with the spirit means with, like your saying: he went out with his clothes, meaning with his clothes. From His command means by His command. On whomever He wills of His servants meaning on those whom God chose for prophethood. This is a response to their statement: Why was this Qur’an not sent down to a great man from the two cities? (al-Zukhruf 43:31). Warn that there is no god except Me, so fear Me is a warning against worshipping idols, and that is why the warning came, because its origin is a warning against what is feared. And this is indicated by His statement: so fear Me. And that is in the accusative case because the preposition was removed, meaning that you should warn the people of disbelief that there is no god but God, so that is in the accusative case because the preposition was dropped or because the warning was made against him.
16:3: The Almighty says: He created the heavens and the earth in truth meaning for the sake of disappearance and annihilation. It was said: in truth meaning to indicate His power, and that He has the right to command His servants to obey Him and to revive creation after death. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him meaning from these idols that are not able to create anything.
16:4: The Almighty said: He created man from a sperm-drop. When He mentioned the evidence for His Oneness, He then mentioned man, his opposition, and his transgression of his stage. Man is the name of the species. It was narrated that what was meant by it was Abi bin Khalaf al-Jumahi. He came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a rotten bone and said: Do you think that God will revive this after it has rotted? And in this also was revealed: Has not man seen that We created him from a sperm-drop? Then at once he is a clear adversary? (Ya-Sin 36:77). That is, He created man from water that comes out from between the backbone and the ribs, then He transferred him through stages until he was born and grew up such that he disputes over matters. So the meaning of the speech is astonishment at man And he sets forth for Us an example and forgets his own creation. (Ya-Sin 36:78). His saying: And at once he is a clear adversary means a disputer, like the relative in the sense of the appropriate. That is, he disputes with God Almighty about His power. And clear means apparent in his dispute. It was said: He clarifies his dispute with falsehood. Al-Mubeen: is the one who expresses what is in his mind through his speech.
16:5: It has three issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: And the grazing livestock He has created for you. When He mentioned man, He mentioned what He has bestowed upon him. The grazing livestock are camels, cows, and sheep. The most common words used are na’am and ana’am for camels, and it is said for the group, but it is not said for sheep alone. Hassan said: The fingers are gone, so the atmosphere is empty for the virgin's home The land of the Bani Al-Hasahs is deserted and covered by mountains and sky. And there was still a companion in its meadows, yes and God willing. Here, the word blessings refers specifically to camels. Al-Jawhari said: Blessings is the singular of an’am which means grazing water. This name is most often used for camels. Al-Farra’ said: It is masculine and not feminine. They say: This is a blessing that has been mentioned, and it is pluralized as an’man like haml and hamlaan. Cattle are both masculine and feminine. God Almighty said: from what is in their bellies (al-Nahl 16:66). In another place: from what is in their bellies (al-Mu’minun 23:21). Cattle are in the accusative case in apposition to human, or by an implied verb, which is more correct. Second: - The Almighty said: Warmth. Warmth: heat, which is what is warmed by its wool, fur, and hair, clothing, blankets, and clothing. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Its warmth is its offspring, and God knows best. Al-Jawhari said in As-Sahah: Warmth is the offspring of camels and their milk and what is benefited from them. God Almighty said: For you therein is warmth. And in the hadith: For us from their warmth is what they have submitted to the covenant. Warmth also: heat, you say from it: the man's warmth is warmth like he hated hatred. And likewise warm warmth like thirsty thirst. And the noun is warmth in the kasra and it is the thing that warms you, and the plural is warmers. You say: He has no warmth, because it is a noun. And do not say: You have no warmth, because it is a source. And you say: Sit in the warmth of this wall, meaning its essence. And a man is warm if he wears what warms him. And likewise a man is warm and a woman is warm. The garment warmed him and he warmed himself with the garment and warmed himself with it, and warmed himself with it, which is a verb, meaning he wore something that warms him. And our night was warm, and a warm day on the basis of fa’il and a warm night, and so are the garment and the house. And the warmer are the many camels, because some of them warm each other with their breaths, and it may be stressed. And the warmer are the camels with a lot of hair and fat, according to al-Asma’i. And al-Shamakh recited: How can a heater owner lose his heaters while they are freezing? God Almighty said: And benefits. Ibn Abbas said: The benefits are the offspring of every animal. Mujahid: Riding, carrying, milk, meat, and butter. And from them you eat. He mentioned the benefit of eating alone because it is the most beneficial. It was said: The meaning is: And from their meat you eat when slaughtering. Third: This verse indicates woolen clothing, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the prophets before him, such as Moses and others, wore it. In the hadith of Al-Mughira: So he washed his face and he was wearing a cloak of Syrian wool with narrow sleeves.... The hadith was narrated by Muslim and others. Ibn Al-Arabi said: It is the symbol of the pious, the clothing of the righteous, the badge of the Companions and the Followers, and the choice of the ascetics and the gnostics. It is worn softly, coarsely, finely, closely, and poorly. A group of Sufis are attributed to it, because it is their clothing in most cases, so the ya’ is for attribution and the ha’ is for femininity. One of their sheikhs recited to me in the Holy House, may God purify it: People quarreled and disagreed about the Sufi and thought it was derived from wool. I do not give this name to anyone but a pure and Sufi young man, so he was called a Sufi.
16:6: Beauty is what one adorns and beautifies with. Beauty means goodness. A man with dammah has been adorned with beauty, so he is handsome, and a woman is beautiful, and also beautiful, according to Al-Kisa’i. And he recited: She is as beautiful as a full moon, surpassing all creation in beauty. And Abu Dhuib said: Your beauty, my dear friend He means: Adhere to your beauty and modesty and do not be sad with an ugly sadness. Our scholars said: Beauty is in the form and composition of creation, and it is in the inner morals, and it is in actions. As for the beauty of creation, it is something that the sight perceives and brings to the heart in harmony, so the soul clings to it without knowing the reason for that or attributing it to any human being. As for the beauty of morals, it is their being of praiseworthy qualities such as knowledge, wisdom, justice, chastity, suppressing anger and wanting good for everyone. As for the beauty of actions, it is their existence in harmony with the interests of creation and bringing benefits to them and repelling evil from them. The beauty of livestock and beasts is from the beauty of creation, and it is visible to the eyes and in agreement with the insights. Among their beauty is their abundance and people say when they see them, These are the camels of so-and-so, as al-Suddi said. And because when they go out, their beauty increases and their status becomes great and hearts cling to them, because at that time their humps and udders are the largest, as Qatada said. For this reason, Rawah is mentioned before Sirah because of the perfection of its milk and the pleasure of the soul with it at that time. And God knows best. Ashab narrated on the authority of Malik that he said: God the Almighty says: And for you therein is adornment when you bring them back home and when you send them out to pasture. This refers to the livestock when they go out to pasture and graze them. Rawah is their return in the evening from the pasture, and Sirah is their morning. You say: I let the camels go out, I let them go out to pasture and let them go out to pasture, and they went out to pasture. The transitive and intransitive are the same.
16:7: It has three issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: And bear your burdens. The burdens are the burdens of people, such as goods, food, and other things, and it is what a person finds difficult to carry. It was said: What is meant is their bodies, as indicated by the Almighty’s saying: And the earth will bring forth its burdens. (Az-Zalzalah: 2). The city is Mecca, according to Ikrimah. It was said: It is generally understood in every city whose path is pure. And the hardship of the souls: its difficulty and the utmost effort. The general reading is with a kasra on the shin. Al-Jawhari said: And the shaq is hardship, and from it is the Almighty’s saying: You would not have attained it except with great difficulty. This may be opened, as narrated by Abu Ubaidah. Al-Mahdawi said: The kasra and opening of the shin in shaq are close, and they both mean hardship, and it is from the shaq in a stick and the like, because it is affected by it like difficulty from a person. Al-Tha’labi said: Abu Ja’far read except with great difficulty of the souls and they are two dialects, like parchment and paper and plaster and plaster and ratl and ratl. And he recites the poet’s saying with the kasra and fatha of the sheen: And a man with camels who runs and thinks they are his, my brother, is a pimp who splits them and is persistent. It may be in the sense of a source, from shaqqatu alayhi ashaq shaqan. Shaq is also in the broken form half, it is said: I took shaq al-sha’ah and shaq al-sha’ah. The intended meaning of the verse may be this meaning, that is, you would not have reached it except with a deficiency in strength and the loss of a part of it, that is, you would not have reached it except with half of your strength and the loss of the other half. Shaq is also the side of the mountain. In the hadith of Umm Zar’: He found me among the people of Ghanima in Shaqq. Abu Ubaid said: It is the name of a place. Shaqq also means the brother, it is said: She is my brother and the shaq of my soul. Shaqq is the name of a soothsayer from the soothsayers of the Arabs. Shaq also means the side, and from it is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: If he cried behind her, she turned to him with a crack, and her crack was beneath me, and he did not move. It is shared. Second - From God the Almighty with livestock in general, and camels were mentioned specifically here in carrying heavy loads over all other livestock, as sheep are for grazing and slaughtering, cows are for plowing, and camels are for carrying loads. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “While a man was leading his cow that had been loaded, the cow turned to him and said: ‘I was not created for this, but rather I was created for plowing.’ The people said: ‘Glory be to God,’ in amazement and fear. A cow speaks?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘And I believe in it, and so do Abu Bakr and Umar.’” This hadith indicates that cows are not loaded or ridden, but rather they are for plowing, eating, offspring, and messengers. Third: This verse is evidence of the permissibility of traveling with animals and carrying heavy loads on them, but only to the extent that they can bear, without overloading and with gentleness in walking. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded us to be gentle with them, to give them rest, and to take care to check on their fodder and water. Muslim narrated from Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you travel in a time of abundance, give the camels their share of the land, and if you travel in a year, hasten to clean them. Narrated by Malik in Al-Muwatta’ from Abu Ubaid from Khalid ibn Ma’dan. Mu’awiyah ibn Qurrah narrated that Abu Ad-Darda’ had a camel called Damun, and he used to say: O Damun, do not argue with me before your Lord. Animals are dumb and cannot find what they need for themselves, nor can they express their needs. Whoever takes comfort in accompanying them and then neglects their needs has neglected gratitude and is exposed to argument before God Almighty. Matar bin Muhammad narrated: Abu Dawud told us, Ibn Khalid told us, Al-Musayyab bin Adam told us: I saw Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, hitting a camel and saying: You are loading your camel with more than it can bear.
16:8: It contains eight issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: And horses in the accusative case, in apposition, meaning, and He created horses. Ibn Abi Ubaidah read and horses, mules, and donkeys in the nominative case in all of them. Horses are called horses because of their swaggering gait. The singular of horse is kha’il, like the singular of dha’in. It was said that it has no singular. This was mentioned previously in Al Imran, and we mentioned the hadiths there. When the Almighty mentioned horses, mules, and donkeys separately, it indicates that they did not fall under the term cattle. It was said that they did fall under the term livestock. But He mentioned them separately because of what is related to them in terms of riding, as it is common in horses, mules, and donkeys. Second: The scholars said: God Almighty has given us possession of livestock and beasts and has made them subservient to us, and has permitted us to harness them and benefit from them as a mercy from Him Almighty to us. And whatever an animal has been given to a person to own and is permitted to harness, renting it for him is permissible by consensus of the scholars, and there is no disagreement among them on that. The ruling on renting mounts and beasts is mentioned in the books of jurisprudence. Third: There is no disagreement among scholars regarding renting beasts and mounts for carrying loads and traveling, based on the Almighty’s saying: And carry your loads (al-Baqarah 2:17). They permitted a man to rent an animal or a mount to a specific city, even if he did not specify where he would dismount, how many watering places he would dismount at, how he would travel, and how many stops he would make on his way. They accepted what is customary among people in this regard. Our scholars said: Renting is similar to sales in what is permissible and forbidden. Ibn al-Qasim said: If someone rents an animal to a certain place for a well-worn garment, but he did not describe its patch or its length, it is not permissible, because Malik does not permit this in a sale, and he does not permit in the rental price anything except what is permissible in the sale price. I said: There is no difference of opinion on this, God willing, because it is a lease. Ibn al-Mundhir said: All the scholars whose works are preserved have agreed that if someone hires an animal to carry ten qafiz of wheat, and it loads what he stipulated and it is lost, then nothing is due from him. And likewise if he loads ten qafiz of barley on it. They differed on the one who hires an animal to carry ten qafiz, and it loads eleven qafiz on it. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr used to say: He is responsible for the value of the animal and he is liable for the rent. Ibn Abi Layla said: He is liable for the value of the animal according to the extra load. This is the opinion of al-Nu’man, Ya’qub, and Muhammad. Ibn al-Qasim, the companion of Malik, said: He is not liable according to Malik if the extra qafiz does not damage the animal, and he knows that the animal is not damaged in such a case. The owner of the animal is entitled to the rent for the extra qafiz along with the first lease, because its damage is not due to the extra. This is unlike exceeding the distance, because exceeding the distance is considered complete, so he is liable if it is lost, whether a little or a lot. The increase over the stipulated load is a combination of permission and prohibition. If the increase does not cause damage in the same way, it is known that its destruction is something he was permitted to do. Fourth: The scholars differed regarding a man who rents an animal for a known fee to a specified place, and he goes beyond that place and then returns to the place he was authorized to go to. A group said: If he goes beyond that place, he is liable and he does not owe rent for the transgression. This is what Al-Thawri said. Abu Hanifa said: The wage is his for what he named, and he does not have a wage for what he did not name, because he went against it and is liable. This is what Yaqub said. Al-Shafi’i said: He is liable for the rent he named, and the rent of a similar amount for what he went beyond that, and if it is damaged, he is liable for its value. The seven jurists said something similar, the elders of the people of Medina said: If he reached the distance and then increased, he is liable for the rent of the increase if it is safe, and if it is damaged, he is liable. Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr said: He is liable for the rent and the guarantee. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: This is what we say. Ibn Al-Qasim said: If the renter reaches the destination for which he rented and then increases by a mile or so or miles or a large increase and the animal is damaged, then its owner has his original rent and the option to take the rent for the excess no matter how much it is, or the value of the animal on the day of the transgression. Ibn Al-Mawaz: It has been narrated that he is liable even if he increases by a step. Ibn Al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik regarding the increase in a mile or the like: As for what people tend to do in the stage, he is not liable. Ibn Habib said on the authority of Ibn Al-Majshun and Asbagh: If the increase is small or he exceeds the time for which he rented it by a little, then he returns with it safely to the place to which he rented it and it dies, or it dies on the way to the place to which he rented it, then he is only entitled to the rent for the excess, as a return for what he borrowed from a deposit. If it increased a lot, which is equivalent to the number of days in which its market changes, then he is liable, as if it died after exceeding the time or distance, because if it was a small increase, which he knows did not help in killing it, then its destruction after returning it to the place where it was authorized is like the destruction of what was borrowed from the deposit after returning it, inevitably. And if the increase was a lot, then that increase helped in killing it. Fifth - Ibn Al-Qasim and Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: God the Almighty said: And horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride and as an adornment So He made them for riding and adornment and did not make them for eating, and something similar was narrated from Ashhab. For this reason, our companions said: It is not permissible to eat the meat of horses, mules and donkeys, because when God the Almighty specified riding and adornment, He indicated that everything else is the opposite. And He said about livestock: And of them you eat you eat what God has blessed of them of warmth and benefits, so He permitted us to eat them with the prescribed slaughter. And Ibn Abbas and Al-Hakam bin Uyaynah used this verse as evidence. Al-Hakam said: Horse meat is forbidden in the Book of God, and he recited this verse and the one before it and said: This is for eating and this is for riding. Ibn Abbas was asked about horse meat and he disliked it, and he recited this verse and said: This is for riding, and he recited the verse before it And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and many benefits then he said: This is for eating. Malik, Abu Hanifa and their companions, Al-Awza’i, Mujahid, Abu Ubaid and others said the same. They cited as evidence what was narrated by Abu Dawud, Al-Nasa’i, Al-Daraqutni and others on the authority of Salih bin Yahya bin Al-Miqdam bin Ma’dikarib on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather on the authority of Khalid bin Al-Waleed: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade on the day of Khaybar the eating of the meat of horses, mules and donkeys, and any fanged beast of prey or created bird.” This is the wording of Al-Daraqutni. Al-Nasa’i also narrated on the authority of Khalid bin Al-Waleed that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: It is not permissible to eat the meat of horses, mules and donkeys. The majority of jurists and hadith scholars said: It is permissible. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hanifa. A group deviated from the prohibition, including Al-Hakam as we mentioned. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hanifa. Al-Ruwayani narrated the three narrations on his authority in Bahr Al-Madhhab according to the Shafi’i school of thought. I said: The correct view that is indicated by observation and the hadith is that it is permissible to eat horse meat, and that there is no binding proof in the verse and the hadith. As for the verse, it does not indicate the prohibition of horses, because if it indicated that, it would indicate the prohibition of donkey meat, and the surah is Meccan, and what need was there to renew the prohibition of donkey meat in the year of Khaybar when it is proven in the hadiths that horses are permissible as will come. Also, when God the Almighty mentioned livestock, He mentioned the majority of their benefits and the most important thing about them, which is carrying heavy loads and eating, and He did not mention riding or plowing with them or anything else explicitly, and they may be ridden and plowed, God the Almighty said: Who has made for you the grazing livestock that you may ride some of them and eat some of them (Ghafir 40:79). And He said about horses: That you may ride them and as an adornment, so He also mentioned the majority of their benefits and the purpose of them, and He did not mention carrying heavy loads on them, and they may be carried as is seen, so that is why He did not mention eating. And his Prophet, peace be upon him, who was entrusted with explaining what was revealed to him, explained it as follows. It does not follow that it was created for riding and adornment that it should not be eaten. This cow was given the ability by its Creator, who made all things speak, and it said: I was only created for cultivation. It follows from the reason that horses are not eaten because they were created for riding that cows are not eaten because they were created for cultivation. The Muslims have unanimously agreed that it is permissible to eat them, and so are horses according to the established Sunnah concerning them. Muslim narrated from the hadith of Jabir who said: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade the meat of domesticated donkeys on the day of Khaybar and permitted the meat of horses.” Al-Nasa’i said from Jabir: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, fed us horse meat on the day of Khaybar and forbade us from the meat of donkeys.” In a narration from Jabir, he said: “We used to eat horse meat during the time of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him.” If it is said: The narration from Jabir that they ate it in Khaybar is a narration of a situation and a case in a particular case, so it is possible that they were slaughtered out of necessity, and the cases of circumstances cannot be used as evidence. We said: The narration from Jabir and his information that they used to eat horse meat during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) removes that possibility. If we accept it, then we have the hadith of Asma’ who said: “We slaughtered a horse during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while we were in Madinah and we ate it.” Narrated by Muslim. Any interpretation without a preference in opposition to the text is nothing but a claim, and should not be paid attention to or heeded. Ad-Daraqutni narrated a good addition that removes any interpretation in the hadith of Asma’. Asma’ said: “There was no horse during the time of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that wanted to die, so we slaughtered it and ate it.” So its slaughter was only for fear of its death, not for any other reason. And God is the Grantor of success. If it is said: An animal with hooves is not to be eaten like a donkey? We say: This is an analogy based on similarity, and the masters of the principles of jurisprudence differed in their statement about it. If we accept it, then it is invalidated by the pig, because it has a hoof and is different from the hoofed animals. And if the analogy is in opposition to the text, then it is invalid and should not be paid attention to. Al-Tabari said: Their consensus on the permissibility of riding what was mentioned for eating is evidence of the permissibility of eating what was mentioned for riding. Sixth: As for mules, they are included with donkeys. If we say that horses are not eaten, then they are born from two sources that are not eaten. If we say that horses are eaten, then they are born from something that is eaten and something that is not eaten, then the prohibition prevails over what is required in the principles. Likewise, the slaughter of a child born between two infidels, one of whom is qualified for slaughter and the other is not qualified for it, is not slaughter and the slaughter is not permissible. The discussion of the prohibition of donkeys has already passed in Al-An’am, so there is no point in repeating it. The prohibition of eating a donkey has been explained by the fact that it showed its evil essence when it copulated with a male and committed sodomy, so it was called filth. Seventh: The verse is evidence that there is no zakat on horses, because God the Almighty has bestowed upon us what He has permitted us from them and honored us with from their benefits, so it is not permissible to impose a cost on them except with evidence. Malik narrated from Abdullah bin Dinar from Sulayman bin Yasar from Arak bin Malik from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no zakat on a Muslim for his slave or horse. Abu Dawud narrated from Abu Hurayrah from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: There is no zakat on horses and slaves except the zakat al-fitr for slaves. Malik, al-Shafi’i, al-Awza’i, al-Layth, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad said the same. Abu Hanifah said: If they are all females or males and females, then there is a dinar for each horse if it is grazing, and if he wishes to evaluate them, he may give five dirhams for every two hundred dirhams. He argued with a hadith from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: In grazing horses, for each horse there is a dinar and with his saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Horses are three… the hadeeth. And in it: And he did not forget the right of God in their necks or their backs. The answer to the first is that it is a hadeeth that was not narrated except by Ghurak al-Sa’di from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from his father from Jabir. Ad-Daraqutni said: Ghurak is the only one who narrated it from Ja’far and he is very weak, and those below him are weak. As for the hadeeth, the right mentioned in it is to go out on them when the call to prayer occurs and they are designated to fight the enemy if that is required of him, and to carry those who are stranded on them if they need that, and this is obligatory upon him if that is required, just as it is required of him to feed them when necessary, so these are the rights of God in their necks. If it is said: This is the right that is in their backs and the right that is in their necks remains, it is said: It has been narrated: The right of God in them is not forgotten and there is no difference between his saying: The right of God in them or in their necks and backs, because the meaning refers to one thing, because the right is related to them as a whole. A group of scholars said: The right here is to own it well, to provide for its satiation, to be kind to it, and to ride it without difficulty, as came in the hadith: Do not make their backs chairs. Their necks were mentioned specifically because necks and necks are often borrowed in places of necessary rights and obligatory duties, such as the saying of God Almighty: Then the freeing of a believing slave (An-Nisa’: 92). They used this and borrowed it so much that they applied it to quarters and wealth. Do you not see the saying of many: The robe is covered when he smiles and laughs, and the necks of money are closed because of his laughter. Also, the animal on which zakat is due has a nisab of its kind, and since horses are excluded from that, we know that zakat is not due on them. Also, his requiring zakat on females alone but not males is a contradiction on his part, and there is no distinction between them in the hadith. We compare females to males in negating zakat, as it is an animal acquired for its offspring, not for its milk, and zakat is not due on its males, so it is not due on its females like mules and donkeys. It has been narrated on his authority that there is no zakat on its females even if they are alone, like its males alone, and this is what the majority are of the opinion. Ibn Abd al-Barr said: The hadith on zakat on horses from Umar is authentic from the hadith of al-Zuhri and others. It was narrated from Malik, narrated by Juwayriyyah from al-Zuhri that al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid said: I saw my father assess the horses and then give their zakat to Umar. This is an argument for Abu Hanifa and his sheikh Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman. I do not know of any of the jurists of the regions who required zakat on horses other than them. Juwayriyyah is the only one who reported it from Malik, and he is trustworthy. Eighth - The Almighty’s saying: And adornment is in the accusative case with an implied verb, meaning: And He made it an adornment. It was said: It is an object for which. Adornment is what one adorns oneself with, and this beauty and adornment, even though it is from the pleasures of this world, God the Almighty has permitted it to His servants. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Camels are honor for their owners, sheep are a blessing, and horses have goodness in their forelocks. Narrated by Al-Barqani and Ibn Majah in Al-Sunan. It was mentioned previously in Al-An’am. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, combined honor in camels because they contain clothing, food, milk, pregnancy, and raiding, even if they lack the ability to charge and flee. He placed the blessing in sheep because they contain clothing, food, drink, and many children, as they give birth three times a year, in addition to the tranquility that follows them, and they carry their owner with them by lowering their wing and being soft on their side, unlike the furry ones. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, linked the forelocks of horses for the rest of time because of the spoils they bring for earning and living, and what they lead to in terms of conquering enemies, overcoming infidels, and raising the word of God Almighty. God the Almighty said: And He creates what you do not know. The majority said: From creation. It was said: From the types of insects and vermin in the depths of the earth, on land and in the sea, which humans have not seen or heard of. It was said: And He creates what you do not know of what God has prepared in Paradise for its people and in Hell for its people, which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. Qatada and As-Suddi said: It is the creation of worms in clothes and worms in fruits. Ibn Abbas: A spring under the Throne, narrated by Al-Mawardi. Al-Tha’labi: Ibn Abbas said: To the right of the Throne is a river of light like the seven heavens and the seven earths and the seven seas seventy times. Gabriel enters it every dawn and washes himself, increasing in light to his light, beauty to his beauty, and greatness to his greatness. Then he shakes himself and God brings out from every feather seventy thousand drops, and from every drop seven thousand angels come out, seventy thousand of whom enter every day to the Frequented House, and in the Kaaba there are seventy thousand who do not return to it until the Day of Resurrection. A fifth statement - which was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “It is a white land, the distance of the sun is thirty days, filled with people who do not know that God Almighty is disobeyed on earth. They said: O Messenger of God, who are the children of Adam? He said: They do not know that God created Adam. They said: O Messenger of God, where is Iblis among them? He said: They do not know that God created Iblis - then he recited: ‘And He creates what you do not know.’” Al-Mawardi mentioned it. I said: And from this meaning is what Al-Bayhaqi mentioned on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: “God has servants beyond Andalusia, as between us and Andalusia, they do not see that God’s disobedience is created, their lands are pearls and rubies, and their mountains are gold and silver, they do not till or plant or do any work, they have trees at their doors that have fruit which is their food and trees that have broad leaves which are their clothing, he mentioned it in the beginning of creation from the book of the names and attributes. And it was narrated from the hadith of Musa bin Uqbah on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah Al-Ansari that he said the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I have been given permission to speak about an angel of God’s angels who bears the Throne, between the lobe of his ear and his shoulder is a journey of seven hundred years.’”
16:9: The Almighty said: And upon God is the direction of the way meaning upon God is the clarification of the direction of the way, so the complement, which is the clarification, was omitted. The way: Islam, meaning upon God is its clarification through messengers, arguments, and proofs. And the direction of the way: seeking help on the path, it is said: a straight path, meaning it leads to the desired goal. And among them is one who deviates meaning among the path is one who deviates, meaning one who deviates from the truth and is not guided by it, and from this is the saying of Imru' al-Qais: And from the path is the unjust and the guidance is the one who intends the path and from it is the one who has income Tarafa said: Aduliya or from the ships of Ibn Yamen, the sailor sometimes goes astray and is guided by it Al-Aduliyah: A ship attributed to Adoli, a village in Bahrain. Adoli is the sailor, as stated in Al-Sahah. In the Qur’an, And that this is My straight path, so follow it and do not follow [other] paths. (al-An’am 6:153) and it has been mentioned before. It was said that the meaning is: And among them is he who deviates from the path of truth, meaning he deviates from it and is not guided to it. There are two opinions about them: One of them is that they are people of different desires, Ibn Abbas said. The second is the sects of disbelief such as Judaism, Zoroastrianism, and Christianity. In the Mushaf of Abdullah and among you is he who deviates, and Ali read it likewise and among you with the letter Kaf. It was said that the meaning is: and from it is he who deviates, meaning from the path. So -man means about. Ibn Abbas said: That is, whoever God wants to guide, He makes the path of faith easy for him, and whoever He wants to misguide, He makes faith and its branches difficult for him. It was said that the meaning of intending the path is your journey and your return. The path is singular in meaning of the plural, and that is why the metaphor was made feminine, saying: and from it, and the path is feminine in the language of the people of Hijaz. The Almighty’s saying: If He had willed, He would have guided you all. He made it clear that the will belongs to God Almighty, and it corrects what Ibn Abbas went to in interpreting the verse, and it responds to the Qadarites and those who agreed with them as mentioned above.
16:10: Drink is what is drunk, and the tree is well-known. That is, trees, arbors, and plants grow from the rain. And tasimoon means you graze your camels. It is said: samat as-sa'imah tasomoon means she grazed, so she is sa'imah. As-sa'im and as-sa'im have the same meaning, and it is the grazing money. The plural of as-sa'im and as-sa'imah are sawa'im. And I asma it means I took it out to graze, so I am musaym and she is musama and as-sa'imah. He said: You deserve the most beautiful son of Masima The root of the word sum is to send away in the pasture. It can be marked. And His statement: marked (Al Imran 3:125). Al Akhfash said that it can be marked and sent, from your saying: Sum fiha al-khayil meaning sent them out, and from this comes the word saimah. It came with the letter ya and nun because the horses were marked and their riders were on them.
16:11: The Almighty said: He causes to grow for you thereby crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and from all kinds of fruits. Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim nanbat with a nun for emphasis. The general reading is with a ya’ meaning God causes to grow for you. It is said: the earth grew and anbat have the same meaning, and the grass grew and anbat have the same meaning. Al-Farra’ recited: I saw the needy people around their homes, weaving cotton around them until the grass grew. Any plant. And God caused it to grow, so it is a plant, not according to analogy. And the boy grew, his pubic hair grew. And the tree grew, its planting, it is said: Your life span grew between your eyes. And the boy grew, I raised him. And the plant is the place of the plant, it is said: How beautiful is the plant of the Banu so-and-so, meaning what their money and children grow on. And a plant grew for them if a young generation grew up for them. And the Banu so-and-so are evil plants. And the nawabat are from the young and ignorant. And the nabit is a tribe from Yemen. And the yanbut is a tree, all according to al-Jawhari. And the olive is the plural of zaytunah. And the tree itself is called an olive, and the fruit is called an olive. The ruling on the zakat of these fruits has already passed in Surat al-An’am, so there is no point in repeating it. Indeed in that is the sending down and the growing. A sign means an indication. For a people who reflect.
16:12: The Almighty said: And He has subjected to you the night and the day meaning for rest and deeds, as He said: And out of His mercy He has made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty (al-Qasas 28:73). And the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected by His command meaning they are submissive to know the times and the ripening of fruits and crops and to be guided by the stars in the darkness. Ibn Amir and the people of Ash-Sham read and the sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected in the nominative case as the subject and predicate. The rest read it in the accusative case in apposition to what preceded it. Hafs read from Asim with the nominative case and the stars, subjected is its predicate. It was also read and the sun, the moon, and the stars in the accusative case.
