Subjected in the nominative case, and it is the predicate of a deleted subject meaning they are submissive, and in the reading of those who put it in the accusative case it is a confirmed state, like His saying: And He is the truth, confirming (al-Baqarah 2:91). Indeed in that are signs for a people who understand. That is, from God what He alerted them to and guided them to.
16:13: It has three issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: And what He has disseminated meaning He has subjected to you what He has disseminated on the earth. Dhara’ means created. God disseminated the creation, He disseminates them disseminating them, so it is Dhari’, and from it comes the word dharī’, which is the offspring of the two heavy things, except that the Arabs dropped the hamza on it, and the plural is dharārī. It is said: God has caused your dharā’ and dharūk to grow, meaning your offspring. The root of dharū and dharū is to separate from a plural. In the hadith: Dhar’ al-Nār, meaning that they were created for it. Second: What God the Almighty has created of it, submissive and tamed, such as beasts, livestock, trees, and others, and other things. The evidence for this is what Malik narrated in Al-Muwatta’ on the authority of Ka’b Al-Ahbar, who said: If it were not for the words that I say, the Jews would have made me a donkey. He was asked: What are they? He said: I seek refuge in the face of God the Almighty, than which there is nothing greater, and in the perfect words of God, which neither the righteous nor the wicked can transgress, and in all the beautiful names of God, those I know of them and those I do not know, from the evil of what He created, originated, and dispersed. And in it on the authority of Yahya bin Sa’id that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on a night journey and saw an evil spirit from the jinn pursuing him with a torch of fire,” the hadith. And in it: And the evil of what He has dispersed on earth. We have mentioned it and what is similar to it in other places. Third - The Almighty’s saying: of varying colors. “Different” is in the accusative case as a state. Its colors are its forms and appearances, meaning the animals and trees and others. Indeed in that meaning in the variation of their colors. is a sign meaning a lesson. For a people who remember meaning who are admonished and know that in the subjugation of these components are signs of the Oneness of God Almighty, and that no one else is able to do that.
16:14: It contains nine issues: First - The Almighty said: And it is He who has subjected the sea. Subjecting the sea is enabling humans to control it and tame it by riding, enjoying the sea, and other things. This is a blessing from God upon us. If He had willed, He could have given it power over us and drowned us. We have already discussed the sea and its catch. He called it meat here, and according to Malik, meat is of three types: the meat of quadrupeds is a type, the meat of feathered animals is a type, and the meat of aquatic animals is a type. It is not permissible to sell one type for another type with a difference. It is permissible to sell the meat of cows and wild animals for the meat of birds and fish with a difference. Likewise, the meat of birds for the meat of cows, wild animals, and fish is permissible with a difference. Abu Hanifa said: All meats are of different types, like their origins. So cow meat is a type, sheep meat is a type, camel meat is a type, and wild animals are different, as are birds and fish. This is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi'i. The other opinion is that all livestock, game, birds, and fish are one type and it is not permissible to differentiate between them. The first opinion is the well-known opinion of his school of thought among his companions. Our evidence is that God the Almighty differentiated between the names of livestock in their lives, saying: “Eight pairs: of sheep, two, and of goats, two” (al-An’am 6:143). Then He said: And of camels, two, and of cattle, two (al-An’am 6:144). When He led all of them to meat, He said: Lawful to you are the beasts of cattle (al-Ma’idah 5:1). He grouped them under one meat because their benefits are similar, like the meat of sheep and goats. And He said in another place: And the meat of fowl of whatever they desire (al-Waqi’ah 56:21). This is the plural of bird, which is one, because God the Almighty said: nor a bird that flies with its wings (al-An’am 6:38). So He grouped all the meat of birds under one name. And He said here: tender meat, so He grouped the types of fish under one name, so its young ones were like its adults in grouping them together. It was narrated from Ibn ‘Umar that he was asked about the meat of goats and the meat of rams, is it the same thing? He said: No, and there was no one who disagreed with him, so it became like a consensus, and God knows best. There is no argument for the one who opposes the prohibition of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of selling food except like for like, because food in general includes wheat and other foods, but it does not include meat. Do you not see that when the speaker says: I ate food today, it is not understood from it that it was eaten meat? Also, it is contradicted by the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If the two types differ, then sell them however you wish. And this is two types. Also, we have agreed on the permissibility of selling meat for bird meat with a difference, not because it is selling food for which there is no zakat, selling for meat for which there is no zakat, likewise selling fish for bird meat with a difference. Second - As for locusts, it is well-known among us that it is permissible to sell some of them for others with a difference. It was mentioned from Sahnun that he forbade that, and some of the later scholars tended towards that and saw it as something that is saved. Third: Scholars differed regarding someone who swears not to eat meat. Ibn al-Qasim said: He breaks his oath with each of these four types. Ashab said in al-Majmu’ah: He only breaks his oath with all the meat of livestock, not wild animals or anything else, taking into consideration custom and tradition, and giving it precedence over the general linguistic expression, which is better. Fourth - The Almighty’s statement: And you extract from it ornaments which you wear. He means pearls and coral, as the Almighty said: From them come forth pearls and coral. (al-Rahman 55:22). Extracting ornaments is only what is known of salt. It is said that there is seawater in emerald. Al-Hudhali made a mistake in his statement in describing the pearl: So he brought her a pearl, slapping her face with the water of the Euphrates flowing. So He made it from sweet water. So the adornment is true and it is the gift of God Almighty to Adam and his children. Adam was created and crowned and adorned with the wreath of Paradise, and sealed with the ring that Solomon, son of David, inherited from him, may God’s prayers be upon them, and it was called the Seal of Glory, according to what was narrated. Fifth - God Almighty has bestowed upon men and women a general favor with what comes out of the sea, and He does not forbid them anything from it. Rather, God Almighty has forbidden men gold and silk. It was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not wear silk, for whoever wears it in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter. We will discuss this in Surat Al-Hajj, God willing. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wore a gold ring, and made its stone on the palm of his hand, and engraved on it Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and the people adopted the same. When he saw that they had adopted it, he threw it away and said: I will never wear it again. Then he adopted a silver ring, and the people adopted silver rings. Ibn Umar said: After the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the ring was worn by Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Uthman, until it fell from Uthman into the well of Aris. Abu Dawud said: The people did not differ about Uthman until the ring fell from his hand. The scholars agreed that it is permissible for men to wear silver rings in general. Al-Khattabi said: It is disliked for women to wear silver rings, because it is part of men’s clothing. If they do not find gold, then they should yellow it with saffron or something similar. The majority of scholars from the early and later generations are of the opinion that it is forbidden for men to wear gold rings, except for what was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman and Khabbab, which is an unusual disagreement, and neither of them was informed of the prohibition or abrogation. And God knows best. As for what Anas ibn Malik narrated: “He saw on the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, One day, he handed over a ring made of silver. Then people made rings of silver and wore them. The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) threw away his ring, so the people threw away their rings. - Narrated by the two Sahihs, and the wording is from Al-Bukhari - so it is according to the scholars, and they are from Ibn Shihab, because what the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) threw away was a gold ring. It was narrated by Abdul Aziz bin Suhaib, Thabit, and Qatadah from Anas, and it is contrary to what Ibn Shihab narrated from Anas, so it is obligatory to judge by the group on one person if he contradicts it, with the witness for the group from the hadith of Ibn Umar. Sixth - If it is proven that it is permissible for men to wear a silver ring and adorn themselves with it, Ibn Sirin and other scholars disliked engraving it or having the mention of God on it. A group of scholars permitted engraving it. Then if the name of God or a word of wisdom or words from the Qur’an are engraved on it and he puts it on his left hand, can he enter the toilet with it and clean himself with his left hand? Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Malik considered it light. It was said to Malik: If there is the mention of God on the ring and he wears it on his left hand, can he clean himself with it? He said: I hope it is light. It was narrated from him that it is disliked, but it is preferable. Most of his companions forbade it. Hammam narrated from Ibn Jurayj from Al-Zuhri from Anas who said: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered the toilet, he would put his ring on.” Abu Dawud said: This is a strange hadith. It is only known from Ibn Jurayj from Ziyad bin Sa’d from Al-Zuhri from Anas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) made a ring of silver and then threw it away. Abu Dawud said: No one narrated this except Hammam. Seventh - Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a ring of silver and engraved on it Muhammad is the Messenger of God and said: I have taken a ring of silver and engraved on it Muhammad is the Messenger of God, so no one should engrave on his engraving.” Our scholars said: This is evidence of the permissibility of engraving the name of the ring’s owner on his ring. Malik said: It is the custom of the caliphs and judges to engrave their names on their rings, and his prohibition, peace be upon him, is: No one should engrave on the engraving of his ring, because that is his name and description in the message of God to His creation. The people of Ash-Sham narrated that it is not permissible to take a ring for anyone who is not in authority. A hadith was narrated on this matter on the authority of Abu Rayhana, which is a hadith that is not an argument due to its weakness. His saying, peace be upon him: No one should engrave on his engraving refutes it, and indicates the permissibility of taking a ring for all people, if it is not engraved on the engraving of his ring. The engraving on Al-Zuhri’s ring was Muhammad asks God for well-being. The engraving on Malik’s ring was God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim mentioned in Nawader Al-Usul that the inscription on the ring of Moses, peace be upon him, was For every term there is a book and it was mentioned in Al-Ra’d. Omar bin Abdul Aziz was informed that his son had bought a ring for a thousand dirhams, so he wrote to him: I have heard that you bought a ring for a thousand dirhams, so sell it and feed a thousand hungry people with it, and buy an iron ring for a dirham, and write on it May God have mercy on the one who knows his own worth. Eighth - If someone swears not to wear jewelry and wears pearls, he has not broken his oath. Abu Hanifa said the same. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: Because even though the linguistic name includes it, he did not mean it by the oath, and oaths are specific to custom. Do you not see that if someone swears not to sleep on a bed and sleeps on the ground, he has not broken his oath? Likewise, if someone does not light himself with a lamp and sits in the sun, he has not broken his oath. Even if God Almighty called the earth a bed and the sun a lamp. Al-Shafi’i, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad said: If someone swears not to wear jewelry and wears pearls, he has broken his oath, because God Almighty said: And extract from it ornaments which you wear (al-Nahl 16:14). What comes out of it are pearls and coral. Ninth - The Almighty's saying: And you see the ships plying therein. The ship and seafaring have been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah and other books. And His saying: Pursuant Ibn Abbas said: Skippers, from jarat to traverse. Saeed bin Jubayr: Interjection. Al-Hasan: Mawaqir. Qatada and Ad-Dahhak: meaning it goes and comes, coming and going with one wind. And it was said: Pursuant is a deep sea, and the origin of makhr is splitting the water to the right and left. The ship makhrat ploughs plows and plows, makhran and makhwaran if it runs, splitting the water with a sound, and from this is the Almighty's saying: And you see the ships plowing therein meaning skippers. Al-Jawhari said: The swimmer plows if he splits the water with his chest, and the land plows is he splits it for agriculture, and he plows it with water if he holds back the water in it until it becomes spacious, meaning it is suitable for good crop growth. Al-Tabari said: “Al-Makhr in the language is the sound of the wind blowing, and it is not restricted to being in water. He said: Among that is the saying of Wasil, the freed slave of Abu Uyaynah: If one of you wants to urinate, let him blow the wind, meaning let him look at its sound in the bodies from where it blows, and avoid facing it so that his urine does not return to him. “And that you may seek of His bounty” meaning and ride for trade and seeking profit. And that you may be grateful All of this was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. Praise be to God.
16:15: The Almighty said: And He cast into the earth firm mountains. That is, fixed mountains. To mount means to be fixed and established. He said: So I was patient, knowing that, free to anchor if the coward's soul rises That it may shake with you means lest it shake, according to the Kufians. And it is disliked that it shake, according to the Basrans. And the meed is the disturbance right and left, the thing is moved, and the branches are swayed, and the man is strutted. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: God created the earth and it began to shake and sway, so the angels said: This does not rest anyone on its back, so it became anchored by the mountains, and the angels did not know from what the mountains were created. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: When God created the earth, it shuddered and tilted and said: O Lord! Will You place upon me someone who commits sins and transgressions, and throws corpses and stench upon me! So God, the Most High, anchored in it mountains that you see and that you do not see. Al-Tirmidhi narrated at the end of the book of interpretation: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Al-Awam bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When God created the earth, it began to shake, so He created the mountains and returned them to it until it settled. The angels were amazed at the strength of the mountains. They said: O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is stronger than mountains? He said: Yes, iron. They said: O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is stronger than iron? He said: Yes, fire. They said: O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is stronger than fire? He said: Yes, water. They said: O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is stronger than water? He said: Yes, the wind. They said: O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that is stronger than the wind? He said: Yes, the son of Adam gives charity with his right hand, hiding it from his left.” Abu ‘Eisa said: This is a strange hadith that we do not know of as being traceable back to the Prophet except through this chain of transmission. I said: In this verse there is clearest evidence of the use of causes, and He was able to make them still, but not the mountains. This meaning has been presented before. And rivers means He made rivers in them, or He cast rivers into them. And paths means roads and paths. Perhaps you will be guided meaning to where you intend to go in the country, so that you will not go astray or become confused.
16:16: It has three issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: And signs. Ibn Abbas said: The signs are the landmarks of the roads during the day, meaning He made signs for the roads by which one can be guided. And by the star they are guided. He means by the night, and the star refers to the stars. Ibn Waththab read and by the star. Al-Hasan: with a damma on the nun and the jim together, and he meant the stars, so he shortened it, as the poet said: The poor man among us is a judge who has ruled that you must return the water when the star sets. The same applies to those who read the star, except that it is quiescent for the sake of lightness. It is possible that the star is the plural of star, like ceiling and ceiling. There is a difference of opinion about the stars. Al-Farra’ said: Capricorn and Farqadaan. It was said: The Pleiades. The poet said: Even if the star sets in the dark and the green grass is twisted and harvested Some of it is twisted and some of it is harvested, and that will be when the Pleiades rise. Al-Kalbi said: The signs are the mountains. Mujahid said: They are the stars, because some stars are used to guide people, and some are signs that are not used to guide people. This was said by Qatada and Al-Nakha’i. It was said: The speech ended with His statement and signs, then He began and said: and by the star they are guided. According to the first: That is, He made for you signs and stars by which you are guided. And among the signs are the winds by which one is guided. And there are two opinions regarding what is meant by guidance: One of them - in travels, and this is the opinion of the majority. The second - in the direction of prayer. Ibn Abbas said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the statement of God the Almighty: and by the star they are guided. He said: It is Capricorn, O Ibn Abbas, upon it is your direction of prayer and by it you are guided on your land and your sea. Al-Mawardi mentioned it. Second - Ibn al-Arabi said: As for all the stars, only those who know their risings and setting can be guided by them, and the difference between the southern and northern ones among them is small, and that is in the others. As for the Pleiades, only those who are guided by all the stars can be guided by them. And the guidance for everyone is by Capricorn and the two Farqadayn, because they are among the stars with limited risings, apparent azimuths, fixed in place, so they revolve around the fixed pole in a complete rotation, so they are always the guidance of creation on land if the paths are obscured, and at sea when ships are sailing, and in the qiblah if the azimuth is unknown, and that is in general by placing the pole on the back of your left shoulder, so whatever you face is the azimuth of the direction. I said: Ibn Abbas asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the star, and he said: It is Capricorn, upon which your qiblah is, and by it you are guided on your land and your sea. That is because the last of Capricorn is the daughters of the smaller Naash, and the pole upon which the qiblah is straight is between them. Third: Our scholars said: The ruling on facing the Qiblah is of two types: One of them is that he sees it and witnesses it, so he must face it, hit it, and aim in its direction with his entire body. The other is that the Kaaba is such that he cannot see it, so he must face it and meet it with the signs, which are the sun, the moon, the stars, the winds, and everything by which its direction can be known. And whoever is absent from it and prays, striving to do so, facing a direction other than its direction, and he is one of those who can do so, then his prayer is invalid. So if he prays striving to do so, seeking evidence, then it becomes clear to him after finishing his prayer that he prayed facing a direction other than the Qiblah, he must repeat it if it was during its time, and that is not obligatory upon him, because he has fulfilled his obligation as he was commanded. This meaning has already been explained in full in Al-Baqarah, and praise be to God.
16:17: The Almighty said: Is He who creates? He is God the Almighty. Like He who does not create? He means idols. Will you not remember? He spoke about the idols that do not create, harm or benefit, just as He spoke about those who have reason according to what the Arabs used in that regard, for they used to worship them, so they were mentioned with the word min like His statement: Have they inspired legs? (al-A’raf 7:195). It was said: because the pronoun in the mention is linked to the Creator. Al-Farra' said: It is like the Arabs' saying: The rider and the sentence were confused for me, so I do not know who this is and who that is, even if one of them is not human. Al-Mahdawi said: He asks about the Creator Almighty with -man and does not ask about Him with -ma, because -ma is only used to ask about species, and God Almighty does not have a species. Therefore, he answered Moses, peace be upon him, when he said to him: Who is your Lord, O Moses? (Ta-Ha 20:49) and did not answer when he said to him: And what is the Lord of the worlds? (al-Shu’ara 26:23) except with the answer -man and he ignored the answer -ma when the question was invalid. The meaning of the verse: He who is able to create the aforementioned things is more deserving of worship than he who is a creation that neither harms nor benefits, This is the creation of God, so show me what those other than Him have created. (Luqman 31:11) Show me what they have created on the earth. (Fatir 35:40).
16:18: The Almighty said: And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them. This was mentioned in Ibrahim. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
16:19: And God knows what you conceal and what you declare meaning what you conceal and what you reveal. All of this has been fully discussed above.
16:20: The Almighty’s saying: And those they invoke besides God The general reading is yad’un with a ta’ because what precedes it is an address. Abu Bakr narrated from Asim and Hubayrah from Hafs yad’un with a ya’, and this is the reading of Ya’qub. As for His saying: what you conceal and what you declare, they all read with a ta’ as an address, except for what Hubayrah narrated from Hafs from Asim that he read with a ya’. They do not create anything means they are not able to create anything, and they create.
16:21: Dead, not alive meaning they are dead, meaning the idols, they have no souls in them and they do not hear or see, meaning they are inanimate, so how can you worship them when you are better than them when alive. And they do not perceive meaning the idols. When will they be resurrected? As-Salami read iyan with a kasra on the hamza, and they are two dialects, its position is accusative with -يبزونand it is in the meaning of a question. The meaning is: they do not know when they will be resurrected. And he referred to them as he referred to humans, because they claimed that they understand and know and intercede for them with God Almighty, so he addressed them accordingly. And it has been said: God will resurrect the idols on the Day of Resurrection and they have souls, so they will disavow their worship, and in this world they are inanimate and you do not know when they will be resurrected. Ibn Abbas said: The idols will be resurrected and the souls will ride in them with their devils, so they will disavow their worship, then the devils and polytheists will be ordered to the Fire. It was said: The idols will be thrown into the fire by their worshippers, then the devils and polytheists will be ordered to the fire. It was also said: The idols will be thrown into the fire with their worshippers on the Day of Resurrection, the evidence for this is: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell (al-Anbiya 21:98). It was also said: The speech ended when He said: They do not create anything, but they are created then He began by describing the polytheists as dead, and this death is the death of disbelief. And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected meaning, the disbelievers do not know when they will be resurrected, meaning the time of resurrection, because they do not believe in resurrection until they prepare to meet God. It was also said: meaning, they do not know when the Hour will be, and perhaps it will be soon.
16:22: The Almighty said: Your God is one God when he explained the impossibility of associating partners with God Almighty, he explained that the worshipped is one, there is no lord other than Him and no worshipped other than Him. Then those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are in denial meaning they do not accept preaching and remembrance is of no use in them, and this is a refutation of the Qadarites. And they are arrogant meaning they are arrogant and too proud to accept the truth. The meaning of arrogance has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah.
16:23: Indeed, God knows what they conceal and what they declare meaning of speech and action, so He will reward them. Al-Khalil said: Indeed, God knows what they conceal and what they declare, meaning of speech and action, so He will reward them. Al-Khalil said: Indeed, God knows what they conceal and what they declare, and it is said: They did that, so it is said: They will surely regret it. Meaning, truly, Hell is theirs. This has been discussed in detail in Hud. Indeed, He does not love the arrogant meaning, He does not reward them or praise them. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Ali that he passed by some poor people who had brought some broken bread among themselves and they were eating, so they said: Food, O Abu Abdullah, so he got down and sat with them and said Indeed, He does not love the arrogant. When he finished, he said: I have answered you, so answer me. So they went with him to his house, so he fed them, gave them drink, and gave them something, and they left. The scholars said: Every sin can be covered up and hidden except for arrogance, which is a transgression that must be made public, and it is the root of all disobedience. In the authentic hadith: The arrogant will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection like ants, and people will trample them underfoot because of their arrogance. Or as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Their bodies will be made small for them on the Day of Resurrection until their smallness will harm them, and they will be made large for them in the Fire until their greatness will harm them.
16:24: God the Almighty said: And when it is said to them, 'What has your Lord sent down?' meaning, when it is said to those mentioned above who do not believe in the Hereafter and whose hearts deny the Resurrection What has your Lord sent down?. It was said that the speaker was Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, and that the verse was revealed about him, and he went to Al-Hirah and bought the hadiths Kalila and Dimna and he used to read to the Quraysh and say: Muhammad does not read to his companions except the legends of the ancients, meaning it is not from the revelation of our Lord. It was said that the believers are the ones who said to them as a test, so they answered by saying: Legends of the ancients, so they admitted to denying something that is the legends of the ancients. Legends are falsehoods and nonsense. It was mentioned previously in Al-An'am. The statement about What has your Lord sent down is like the statement about What do they spend? (al-Baqarah 2:215), and His statement: Legends of the ancients is the predicate of a deleted subject, the meaning: What He sent down are the legends of the ancients.
16:25: The Almighty's saying: That they may bear their burdens. It was said: It is the lam of ki, and it is related to what preceded it. It was also said: It is the lam of consequence, like His saying: That they may be an enemy and a grief for them. (al-Qasas 28:8). That is, their saying in the Qur'an and the Prophet led them to bear their burdens, meaning their sins. Complete They did not leave anything of it due to a calamity that befell them in this world because of their disbelief. It was also said: It is the lam of command, and the meaning is a threat. And of the burdens of those whom they misguide without knowledge. Mujahid said: They will bear the burden of those whom they misguide, without diminishing anything from the sin of the misguider. In the hadith: "Any caller who calls to misguidance and is followed will have upon him the burdens of those who follow him, without diminishing anything from their burdens. And any caller who calls to guidance and is followed will have the same reward as them, without diminishing anything from their reward." Narrated by Muslim with the same meaning. The word min is for the genus, not for the partiality. The callers to misguidance will bear the burdens of those who follow them. His statement, without knowledge, means that they lead people astray out of ignorance of the sins that are required of them, for if they knew, they would not have led people astray. How evil is that which they bear, meaning how evil is the burden that they bear. Similar to this verse is: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens in addition to their own burdens Al-Ankabut 13. At the end of Al-An’am, we have already explained His statement, And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another Al-An’am 164. The Almighty says: And God will save those who fear Him. It was also read: and saves meaning from polytheism and sins. With their sanctuary according to the general reading because it is a verbal noun. The Kufians read: With their sanctuaries and this is permissible, just as you say with their happiness. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) explained this verse from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said: "God will gather with every person his deeds, and the believer's deeds will be with him in the best form and sweetest scent. So whenever there is terror or fear, He says to him, "Do not be afraid, for you are not what is meant by it, nor are you what is meant by it. So when that becomes too much for him, he says, How good you are, so who are you? He says, Do you not know that I am your righteous deeds? You have burdened me with my burden. By God, I will carry you and defend you." This is the one about whom God said: "And God will save those who fear Him with their sanctuary. No harm will touch them, nor will they grieve. God is the Creator of all things, and He is the Guardian over all things," meaning He is the Preserver and Guardian of it. This has been mentioned previously.
16:26: The Almighty said: Those before them had already plotted meaning, peoples who preceded them in disbelief with the previous messengers, so the good end was for the messengers. Then God attacked their structure from the foundations, and the roof fell upon them from above them. Ibn Abbas, Zaid bin Aslam, and others said: It was Nimrod bin Canaan and his people, they wanted to ascend to the sky and fight its people, so they built the tower to crack from it after he did what he did to the eagles, so it fell. As was explained at the end of Surah Ibrahim. The meaning of Then God attacked their structure is that His command came to the structure, either by an earthquake or a wind, and destroyed it. Ibn Abbas and Wahb said: The length of the tower in the sky was five thousand cubits, and its width was three thousand. Ka'b and Muqatil said: Its length was two leagues, then a wind blew and threw its head into the sea and the rest fell upon them. When the edifice fell, people's tongues were confused from fear on that day, and they spoke seventy-three languages, and that is why it was called Babylon. Before that, there was no language except Syriac. This meaning was mentioned in Al-Baqarah. Ibn Hormuz and Ibn Muhaisin read Al-Saqf with a damma on both the seen and the qaf. Mujahid made a damma on the seen and a sukoon on the qaf for ease, as mentioned in By the star in both versions. It is more likely that it is the plural of saqf. The foundations are the bases of a building, and if the foundations are damaged, the building will fall. And his saying: from above them Ibn Al-A'rabi said: And he almost made you know that they were under it. The Arabs say: A roof fell on us and a wall fell on us if he owned it, even if it did not fall on them. So he came with his saying: from above them to remove this doubt in the speech of the Arabs, so he said: from above them meaning it fell on them and they were under it, so they perished and did not escape. It was said: What is meant by the roof is the sky, meaning that the punishment came to them from the sky that is above them, as Ibn Abbas said. It was said: His statement: Then God struck their building from the foundations is a metaphor, and the meaning is: He destroyed them, so they were like someone whose building fell on him. It was also said: The meaning is: God nullified their deeds, so they were like someone whose building fell on him. It was also said: The meaning is: He invalidated their plot and their planning, so they perished as someone who had the roof collapsed on him from above. Based on this, there is a difference of opinion about those on whom the roof fell. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd said what was mentioned above. It was also said: It was Bukhtanasar and his companions, as some of the commentators said. It was also said: What is meant are the dividers whom God mentioned in Surat Al-Hijr, as Al-Kalbi said. Based on this interpretation, the meaning of the metaphor emerges, and God knows best. And the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive meaning from where they thought they were safe. Ibn Abbas said: It means the mosquito with which God destroyed Nimrod.
16:27: The Almighty said: Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them meaning He will disgrace them with the punishment and humiliate them and disgrace them. And He will say, 'Where are My partners?' meaning in your claim and in your claim, meaning the gods that you worshipped instead of Me, and this is a question of rebuke. Those about whom you were hostile meaning you were hostile to My prophets because of them, so let them ward off this punishment from you. Ibn Kathir read sharikay with an open yaa without a hamza, and the rest read it with a hamza. Nafi' read tashaqoon with a kasra on the noon as an addition, meaning you were hostile to Me regarding them. The rest read it with a fatha. Those who were given knowledge said Ibn Abbas said: meaning the angels. It was said: the believers. Indeed, disgrace today meaning humiliation and disgrace on the Day of Resurrection. And evil meaning the punishment. On the disbelievers.
16:28: The Almighty said: Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves. This is a description of the disbelievers. And wronging themselves is an accusative of state, meaning they are wronging themselves if they bring themselves to the sources of destruction. "Then throw down peace" means surrender. That is, they acknowledged God's Lordship and submitted at death and said: We were not doing any evil meaning any polytheism. So the angels said to them: Yes you were doing worse. Indeed, God is Knowing of what you were doing. Ikrimah said: This verse was revealed in Medina about a people who had converted to Islam in Mecca and had not emigrated, so the Quraysh expelled them to Badr against their will and killed them there. So he said: Those whom the angels take in death by taking their souls. Wronging themselves in their stay in Mecca and their abandonment of emigration. "Then throw down peace" means in their departure with them. There are three interpretations of this: One of them is that it is a peace treaty, as Al-Akhfash said. The second: submission, as stated by Qatrib. The third: submission, as stated by Muqatil. We did not do any evil meaning any disbelief. Yes, indeed, God is Knowing of what you used to do meaning that their actions were the actions of the disbelievers. It was said that when some of the Muslims saw the small number of believers, they returned to the polytheists, so this verse was revealed about them. According to the first opinion, no disbeliever or hypocrite will leave this world until he submits, surrenders, submits, and is humiliated, and neither repentance nor faith will benefit them at that time, as He said: So their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment (Ghafir 40:85). This meaning has already been mentioned. It was mentioned in Al-Anfal that the disbelievers die by beating and humiliation, and likewise in Al-An’am. We have mentioned this in the Book of Remembrance.
16:29: The Almighty says: Then enter the gates of Hell meaning that will be said to them at death. It was said: It is good report for them of the torment of the grave, as it is one of the gates of Hell for the disbelievers. It was said: The second level cannot reach it, for example, except by entering the first level, then the second, then the third, like this. It was said: Each level has a separate gate, so some enter from one gate and some enter from another. And God knows best. Eternally therein meaning staying there. Evil is the abode meaning the place of the arrogant who are arrogant about faith and worshipping God Almighty, and He explained it with His true statement: Indeed, when it was said to them, 'There is no god but God,' they were arrogant (al-Saffat 37:35).
16:30: God the Almighty said: And it will be said to those who feared God, 'What has your Lord sent down?' They will say, 'Good.' That is, they will say, He sent down good. And the discussion is complete. And what in this case is one name. And a man from the Arabs would come to Mecca during the season and ask the polytheists about Muhammad, peace be upon him, and they would say, A magician, a poet, a soothsayer, or a madman. And he would ask the believers and they would say, God sent down goodness and guidance upon him, meaning the Qur'an. And it was said that this will be said to the people of faith on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Tha'labi said: If it is said, why is the answer raised in His statement, Legends of the ancients, and erected in His statement, Good? The answer is that the polytheists did not believe in the revelation, so it is as if they said, What Muhammad says are legends of the ancients. And the believers believed in the revelation and said, He sent down good. And this is understood from the grammar, and praise be to God. God the Almighty says: For those who do good in this world is good. It was said: This is from the words of God the Almighty. It was also said: This is from the words of those who feared God. The good here is Paradise, meaning whoever obeys God will have Paradise tomorrow. It was also said: For those who do good today is good in this world from victory, conquest and spoils. And the home of the Hereafter is better. That is, what they will receive in the Hereafter of the reward of Paradise is better and greater than the home of this world, because it will perish and the Hereafter will remain. And what an excellent home for the righteous. There are two interpretations of this. Al-Hasan said: The meaning is And what an excellent home for the righteous is this world, because they will receive the reward of the Hereafter and entry into Paradise through their work in it. It was also said: The meaning is And what an excellent home for the righteous is the Hereafter. This is the opinion of the majority. And this is how it is.
16:31: Gardens of Eden instead of the house, so it was raised. It was said: It was raised on the assumption that they are gardens, so they are explained by his saying: the house of the righteous, or it could be raised by the beginning, the estimation: Gardens of Eden, yes, the house of the righteous. They enter it is in the place of the description, meaning entered. It was said: Gardens is raised by the beginning, and its predicate is they enter it, and on this the statement of Al-Hasan is derived. And God knows best. Rivers flow beneath it its meaning was presented in Al-Baqarah. They will have therein whatever they wish meaning of what they wished and wanted. Thus does God reward the righteous meaning God rewards the righteous like this reward.
16:32: Those whom the angels take in death while they are good. Al-A'mash and Hamzah read the angels take their souls in death in both places with a ya', and Abu Ubaid chose it, because it was narrated from Ibn Mas'ud that he said: The Quraysh claimed that the angels are females, so mention them. The rest with a ta', because what is meant by it is the group. There are six opinions about good: The first - good is pure from polytheism. The second - righteous. The third - their actions and words are pure. The fourth - good souls, confident in what they will receive from the reward of God Almighty. The fifth - their souls are good at returning to God. The sixth: good is that their death is good and easy, with no difficulty or pain, unlike the way in which the soul of the disbeliever and the confused person is taken. And God knows best. "They say, 'Peace be upon you'" has two possible meanings: The first - that the peace is a warning to them of death. The second - that it is good report for them of Paradise, because peace is security. Ibn Al-Mubarak said: Haywah told me that Abu Sakhr told me on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi that he said: When the soul of a believing slave is in a deep state, the Angel of Death comes to him and says: Peace be upon you, O friend of God. God sends you peace. Then he recites this verse: “Those whom the angels take in death while they are good, they say, ‘Peace be upon you.’” Ibn Mas’ud said: When the Angel of Death comes to take the soul of a believer, he says: Your Lord sends you peace. Mujahid said: The believer is given good report of the righteousness of his children after him so that his eyes may be comforted. We have already discussed this in the Book of Remembrance and mentioned there the reports that have been transmitted with this meaning, and praise be to God. His statement: Enter Paradise has two possible meanings: One of them is that it means be given good report of entering Paradise. The second is that they will say that to them in the Hereafter. Because of what you used to do means in this world of good deeds.
16:33: The Almighty says: Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them? This refers to the disbelievers, meaning that they are waiting for nothing but that the angels should come to them to take their souls while they are wronging themselves. Al-A'mash, Ibn Waththab, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read the angels come to them with a ya'. The rest read it with a ta' as mentioned above. Or the command of your Lord comes meaning with the punishment of killing like the day of Badr, or the earthquake and sinking in this world. It was said that what is meant is the Day of Resurrection. The people did not await these things because they did not believe in them, but their refusal to believe made the punishment obligatory upon them, so that was attributed to them, meaning that the punishment was their end. Thus did those before them meaning they persisted in disbelief, so the command of God came to them and they perished. And God did not wrong them meaning by punishing and destroying them, but they wronged themselves by associating partners with God.
16:34: The Almighty says: So the evil of what they did befell them. It was said: There is an inversion of the meaning, the meaning is: Thus did those before them, so the evil of what they did befell them. And God did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves, so the punishments of their disbelief and the recompense of the evil of their deeds befell them. And that which they used to mock encompassed them and surrounded them. That which they used to mock meaning the punishment of their mockery.
16:35: The Almighty said: And those who associate others with God say, ‘If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him.’ That is, anything, and of is a relative clause. Al-Zajjaj said: They said it in mockery, and if they had said it out of belief, they would have been believers. This has already been explained in Surat Al-An’am, explaining its meaning and syntax, so there is no point in repeating it. Thus did those before them. That is, those who came before them did this kind of denial and mockery of the messengers, and they were destroyed. Then is there upon the messengers except the clear notification? That is, they are only required to convey the message, and as for guidance, it is up to God the Almighty.
16:36: The Almighty says: And We have certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], 'Worship God' meaning, worship God alone. And avoid Taghut meaning, leave everything worshipped besides God, such as Satan, soothsayers, idols, and everyone who calls to misguidance. And among them are those whom God guided meaning, He guided them to His religion and worship. And among them are those upon whom misguidance was decreed meaning, by the previous decree upon them, so that they died in their disbelief. This refutes the Qadarites, because they claimed that God guided all people and granted them success in guidance, and God the Almighty says: And among them are those whom God guided, and among them are those upon whom misguidance was decreed and this has been mentioned before in more than one place. So travel through the land meaning, travel as a lesson through the land. Then see how was the end of the deniers meaning, how their final fate was ruin, torment, and destruction.
16:37: The Almighty said: If you are eager for their guidance meaning if you seek their guidance, O Muhammad, with all your effort. Indeed, God does not guide he who goes astray meaning He does not guide he who has been led astray by God, meaning he who has been previously led astray by God, He does not guide him. This is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud and the people of Kufa. So -يهديis a future tense verb and its past tense isَه د. Andمنis in the accusative case with -يهديand it is possible thatَه دي َه ديmeans he is guided, he is guided, Abu Ubaid narrated it from al-Farra' who said: Just as it was read amn la yahdi illa an yahdi Among those who do not guide unless they are guided (Yunus 10:35) meaning he is guided. Abu Ubaid said: We do not believe that anyone narrated this other than al-Farra', and he is not accused of what he narrates. An-Nahhas: It was narrated to me on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid that the meaning of La yahdi man yudal is from the knowledge of that from him and it was previously known to him, he said: And yahdi does not mean yahtadi unless it is yahdi or yahdi. And according to al-Farra’ yahdi means yahtadi, so man is in the nominative case, and what refers to man is the deleted ha’ from the relative clause, and what refers to the name of in is the pronoun implied in yudhl. The rest read La yahdi with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the dal, and Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it, meaning whoever God misguides, no guide has guided him, his evidence is his statement: He whom God misguides, there is no guide for him (al-A’raf 7:186) and man is in the nominative case as a name for what its agent has not been named, and it means who, and what refers to it from its relative clause is deleted, and what refers to the name of in from then God is the pronoun implied in yudhl. And they have no helpers its meaning was presented.
16:38: God the Almighty said: And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths. This is an astonishment at their doing, as they swore by God and exaggerated in their oath that God will not resurrect those who die. The astonishment is that they show their glorification of God by swearing by Him, but then they prove that He is unable to resurrect the dead. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: A Muslim man had a debt to a polytheist, so he took it from him. Some of his words included: And what I hope for after death is that it is such and such. The polytheist swore by God: God will not resurrect those who die. So the verse was revealed. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that a man said to Ibn Abbas: O Ibn Abbas, some people claim that Ali will be resurrected after death before the Hour, and they interpret this verse. Ibn Abbas said: They lied! This verse is general for people. If Ali were to be resurrected before the Day of Resurrection, we would not have married his women or divided his inheritance. Yes is a response to them, meaning, Yes, He will resurrect them. A true promise upon Him is a confirmed source, because His statement He will resurrect them indicates the promise, that is, the promise of resurrection is a true promise. But most people do not know that they will be resurrected. In Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “God Almighty said: The son of Adam denied Me, although he had no right to do so, and he insulted Me, although he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying, ‘He will not restore me as He began me.’ As for his insulting Me, it is his saying, ‘God has taken a son,’ while I am the One, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.” This has been mentioned before and will come.
16:39: The Almighty said: To make clear to them meaning to show them that over which they differ meaning the matter of resurrection. And that those who disbelieved in the resurrection and swore by it may know that they were liars. It was said: The meaning is that We sent to every nation a messenger to make clear to them that over which they differ, and that over which the polytheists and Muslims differed are matters: including resurrection, idol worship, and the acknowledgment of a people that Muhammad is true but their imitation prevented them from following him, such as Abu Talib.
16:40: I teach them that creation is easy for Him, meaning if We want to resurrect someone who dies, then there is no effort or fatigue on Us in bringing them back to life, nor in anything else that We create, because We only say to them, Be, and they are. Ibn 'Amir and Al-Kisa'i read be in the accusative case in apposition to that We say. Al-Zajjaj said: It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as an answer to be. The rest say in the nominative case, meaning that it is. This has been discussed in detail in Al-Baqarah. Ibn Al-Anbari said: The word thing was applied to what was known to God before creation because it is like what existed and was witnessed. And in the verse is evidence that the Qur'an is not created, because if His saying be were created, it would need a second saying, and the second would need a third and a sequence, and it would be impossible. And in it is evidence that God Almighty wills all events, good and bad, benefit and harm. The evidence for that is that whoever sees in His authority what he dislikes but does not will, then it is for one of two reasons: either because he is ignorant and does not know, or because he is overcome and cannot bear it, and that is not permissible in His description, glory be to Him. Evidence has been established that He is the Creator of the acquisition of servants, and it is impossible for Him to be the doer of something without will for it, because most of our actions occur contrary to our intention and will. If God Almighty did not will them, then those actions would occur without intention. This is the statement of the naturalists, and the monotheists have agreed on its opposite and its corruption.
16:41: The Almighty said: And those who emigrated for the cause of God after they had been wronged The meaning of emigration has already been mentioned in An-Nisa', which is leaving homelands, family and relatives for the sake of God or for the sake of God's religion, and leaving bad deeds. It was said: Fi means lam, meaning for God. After they had been wronged meaning they were tortured for the sake of God. It was revealed about Suhaib, Bilal, Khabbab and Ammar, the people of Mecca tortured them until they said to them what they wanted, then when they were free they emigrated to Medina, said Al-Kalbi. It was said: It was revealed about Abu Jandal bin Suhayl. Qatada said: What is meant are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, the polytheists oppressed them in Mecca and expelled them until a group of them fled to Abyssinia, then God settled them in the abode of emigration and made for them supporters from among the believers. The verse includes everyone. We will surely provide them with good in this world There are six opinions about good: The first - the descent to Medina, said Ibn Abab, Al-Hasan, Al-Sha'bi and Qatada. Second: The good provision, as stated by Mujahid. Third: Victory over their enemy, as stated by Ad-Dahhak. Fourth: It is a tongue of truth, as stated by Ibn Jurayj. Fifth: The conquests of lands they conquered and the states they had therein. Sixth: The praise they had in this world, and the honor their children had therein. All of that was gathered for them by the grace of God, and praise be to God. And the reward of the Hereafter is greater meaning, and the reward of the Hereafter is greater, meaning, greater than anyone could know before seeing it. And when you look, you will see pleasure and great dominion. (al-Insan 76:20) If they only knew meaning, if these wrongdoers knew that. It was said: It refers to the believers. Meaning, if they saw the reward of the Hereafter and witnessed it, they would know that it is greater than the good of this world. It was narrated that when Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, gave the Muhajireen a stipend, he would say: This is what God promised you in this world, and what He has stored for you in the Hereafter is more, then he recited this verse to them.
16:42: It was said: those who is a substitute for the first those who. It was also said: from the pronoun in We will give them a place to live. It was also said: they are those who were patient in their religion. And upon their Lord they put their trust in all their affairs. Some of the people of investigation said: the best of creation are those who are patient when faced with a matter, and if they are unable to do something they put their trust. God Almighty said: those who are patient and upon their Lord they put their trust.
16:43: The Almighty said: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed. The general reading is yuhi with a ya and a fatha on the ha. Hafs from Asim read nuhi with a nun of majesty and a kasra on the ha. It was revealed about the polytheists of Mecca when they denied the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: God is greater than for His Messenger to be a human being, so why did He not send us an angel? God Almighty responded to them by saying: And We did not send before you to the past nations, O Muhammad except men of human origin. So ask the people of the message Sufyan said: meaning the believers among the People of the Book. If you do not know they will tell you that all the prophets were human beings. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. Ibn Abbas said: The people of the message are the people of the Qur'an. It was also said: The people of knowledge, and the meaning is close.
16:44: With clear proofs and scriptures It was said: With clear proofs is related to We sent. And in the speech there is an inversion, meaning We did not send before you with clear proofs and scriptures except men - that is, other than men, so except means other, like his saying: There is no god but God, and this is the saying of Al-Kalbi - We revealed to them. And it was said: In the speech there is an omission indicated by We sent, meaning We sent them with clear proofs and scriptures. And With clear proofs is not related to the first -We sent according to this saying, because what comes before except does not work on what comes after it, but rather it is related to We sent which is understood, meaning We sent them with clear proofs. And it was said: It is the object of you know and the ba is redundant, or it is accusative with the implication of I mean, as Al-A'sha said: And there is no protector if he comes to the neighborhood fearful or saying, except He, the one who is in pain. That is, I mean the one who is blamed. And the clear proofs: the arguments and evidences. And the verses: the books. And it was mentioned before in Al Imran. And We have sent down to you the message meaning the Qur’an. So that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them in this book of rulings, promises and threats through your words and actions. So the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is explaining on behalf of God Almighty what He intended from what He summarized in His book of the rulings of prayer and zakat, and other than that which He did not detail. And this meaning was mentioned before in full in the introduction to the book, and praise be to God. And perhaps they will reflect so they will be admonished.
16:45: The Almighty said: Then do those who plot evil deeds feel secure that God will not cause the earth to swallow them up? That is, by evil deeds. This is a threat to the polytheists who schemed to invalidate Islam. That God will not cause the earth to swallow them up. Ibn Abbas said: Just as He caused Qarun to swallow up the earth. It is said: The place was swallowed up means it went into the earth. And God caused the earth to swallow him up, meaning it made him disappear into it. From this is His statement: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home (al-Qasas 28:81). Khassan means to be swallowed up in the earth and Khassan means to be swallowed up. The question is in the sense of denial, meaning that they should not feel secure from a punishment that will befall them as it befell the deniers. Or that the punishment will come to them from where they do not perceive as He did with the people of Lot and others. It was said: He means the Day of Badr, for they were destroyed that day, and none of it was in their account.
16:46: Or He takes them in their turning meaning in their travels and actions, as Qatada said. So they will not escape meaning they will not outrun God or outstrip Him. It was said: in their turning on their beds wherever they are. Ad-Dahhak said: by night and by day.
16:47: Or He takes them with fear. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: That is, with a decrease in their wealth, livestock and crops. Ibn al-A'rabi said the same: That is, with a decrease in wealth, lives and fruits until He destroys them all. Ad-Dahhak said: It is from fear, meaning: He takes a group and leaves a group, so the rest fear that what happened to its companion will happen to them. Al-Hasan said: with fear that he will take the village and the other village will fear him, and this is the meaning of the statement before it exactly, and they both go back to the first meaning, and that fear is decrease, his fear decreases him, and the time fears him and betrays him with the letter fa and the letter nun has the same meaning, it is said: So-and-so betrayed me my right if he diminishes you. Dhu al-Rummah said: No, it is the longing for a home that is betrayed by the passing clouds and the passing dust. Labid said: Betrayed by my coming and going That is, its meat and fat are reduced. Al-Haitham bin Adi said: Al-Takhwāf with the letter fa’ means to reduce, a language for Azdashnu’ah. And he recited: I fear their treachery, my money and my gifts, chains in my throats that clank Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: While Omar bin Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him was on the pulpit, he said: O people, what do you say about the statement of God the Almighty: Or He seizes them in fear? The people were silent. Then an old man from Banu Hudhayl said: This is our language, O Commander of the Faithful. Fear means diminishment. Then a man came out and said: O so-and-so, what has happened to your religion? He said: You have made it fearful, meaning you diminish it. So he returned and informed Omar. Omar said: Do the Arabs know that in their poetry? He said: Yes. Our poet Abu Kabir Al-Hudhali said, describing a camel whose hump is diminished by its gait after it had been well-mannered and well-built: The travelers feared it as a monkey, just as the ships feared it at the spring. Omar said: O people, stick to your diwan of pre-Islamic poetry, for it explains your writing and the meanings of your words. The hump became long and rose, so it is tamik. Ships and ships are what wood is used to pull. Al-Layth bin Saad said: in fear in haste. It was said: in rebuke for the sins they have committed, and this was also narrated from Ibn Abbas. Qatada said: in fear that he will punish or overlook. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful meaning He does not hasten, but rather He gives respite.
16:48: Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Yahya and Al-A'mash read tarawa with a ta', as if the address is to all people. The rest read it with a ya', as a predicate for those who plot evil deeds, and this is the preferred choice. From something means from an upright body that has a shade from a tree or a mountain, as Ibn Abbas said. Even though all things hear and obey God the Almighty. Its shade is shaded Abu Amr, Ya'qub and others read it with a ta' to feminize shadows. The rest read it with a ya', and Abu Ubaid chose it. That is, it leans from one side to another, and at the beginning of the day it is in one state and shrinks, then at the end of the day it returns to another state, so its rotation and leaning from one place to the place of its prostration, and from this the shade was called in the evening: fa', because it returned from the west to the east, meaning it returned. And fa' is the return, and from this is until it returns to the command of God (al-Hujurat 49:9). The meaning of this statement was narrated from Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and others, and this meaning was mentioned in Surat Ar-Ra'd. Al-Zajjaj said: It means the prostration of the body, and its prostration is its submission and what is seen in it of the traces of craftsmanship, and this is general for every body. The meaning of and they are humbled is submissive and humiliated. And dakhur means smallness and humiliation. It is said: A man is humbled with the fat-ha, so he is humbled, and God made him humble. Dhu al-Rummah said: There is nothing left but a burrow in a hole in a land other than yours. This is how Al-Mawardi attributed it to Dhu Al-Rummah, and Al-Jawhari attributed it to Al-Farazdaq. He said: Al-Makhis was the name of a prison in Iraq, meaning a place of humiliation. He said: Don't you see me as a rich and generous man, who was built after Nafi'a, a miserable man? He made the right hand singular in his saying: on the right and the left hand plural, because the meaning of the right hand, even if it is one, is the plural. If he had said: on the right and the left, and the right and the left, or the right and the left, or the right and the left, it would have been permissible, because the meaning is for the multiplicity. Also, it is the custom of the Arabs, when two signs come together in one thing, to make one of them plural and the other singular, like the saying of the Most High: God has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing Al-Baqarah 2:7 and His saying: And He brings them out from darkness into the light Al-Ma’idah 5:16. If he had said on their hearing and to the lights, it would have been permissible. It is permissible to return the right hand to the word what and the left to its meaning. And there is much like this in speech. The poet said: The people of Al-Wardun and Taym in the hands of Saba, their necks were bitten by the skin of buffaloes. He did not say skins. It was said: He limited the right because if the sun rises and you are facing the Qiblah, the shadow spreads on the right, then in a state it leans towards the north, then it becomes dark, so he called it Shama’il.
16:49: The Almighty said: And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures meaning of everything that moves on the earth. And the angels means the angels who are on the earth, and He mentioned them alone because they are distinguished by their honorable status, so He distinguished them from the description of crawling by mentioning them even though they are included in it, like His saying: In them are fruits and palm trees and pomegranates (al-Rahman 55:68). It was said: because they are excluded from the group of crawling things because God gave them wings, so they were not included in the group and that is why they were mentioned. It was said: He meant And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens of the angels, the sun, the moon, the stars, the winds and the clouds, and whatever is on the earth of creatures and the angels of the earth prostrate. And they are not arrogant about worshipping their Lord. This is a response to the Quraysh when they claimed that the angels are daughters of God.
16:50: The meaning of they fear their Lord above them is the punishment and torment of their Lord, because the destructive torment only descends from the sky. It was said: The meaning is they fear the power of their Lord which is above their power, so there is an omission in the speech. It was said: The meaning of they fear their Lord above them means the angels, they fear their Lord and they are above what is on the earth of creatures and yet they fear, so it is more appropriate to fear those below them. The evidence for this statement is the Almighty’s statement: and they do what they are commanded meaning the angels.
16:51: The Almighty said: And God said, Do not take two gods. It was said: The meaning is do not take two gods. It was also said: His saying two came as an emphasis. And since the true God is not multiple and whoever is multiple is not a god, He limited himself to mentioning two, because He intended to negate multiplicity. He is only one God meaning His holy self. Rational and legal evidence has been established for His oneness as was previously explained in Al-Baqarah and we mentioned it in His one name in the explanation of the names, and praise be to God. So fear Me meaning fear. And it was previously mentioned in Al-Baqarah.
16:52: The Almighty said: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him belongs the religion, everlasting. Religion means obedience and sincerity. And everlasting means always, as Al-Farra' said, narrated by Al-Jawhari. To pour something is to pour and to be persistent, meaning it lasts. And a man persists in a matter if he is consistent in it. The meaning is: Obedience to God is obligatory forever. Among those who said everlasting are: Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak. And from this is the Almighty's saying: And for them is a lasting punishment (al-Saffat 37:9), meaning everlasting. Ad-Du'ali said: I do not seek praise that is small, but rather I will always be blamed for the rest of my life. It was said: Wasb means fatigue and exhaustion, meaning that obedience to God is obligatory even if the servant becomes tired in it. And from this is the saying of the poet: He does not hold the leg from where, nor does he pour, nor does he bite on his yellow hump. Ibn Abbas said: Wasaba is obligatory. Al-Farra and Al-Kalbi: Pure. Do you fear other than God? That is, you should not fear other than God. So ghair is in the accusative case with you fear.
16:53: The Almighty said: And whatever blessing you have is from God. Al-Farra' said: What means reward. And the ba' in with you is related to an implied verb, meaning: And whatever blessing you have. From blessing meaning good health, abundant provision, and children are from God. It was said: The meaning is: And whatever blessing you have is from God. Then when harm touches you meaning sickness, calamity, and drought. To Him you cry out meaning you make a loud cry in supplication. It is said: Ja'ar, yajuran, juwaran. And ja'ar is like khuwar, it is said: Ja'ar al-taurus, yajuran, meaning it cried out. Some of them read a calf with a body that has a juwar, as narrated by Al-Akhfash. And the man cried out to God, meaning he supplicated. Al-A'sha said, describing a cow: She went around three times in a day and a night, and the denunciation was that she was a guest and a merchant.
16:54: Then when the hardship is removed from you meaning the affliction and illness. A party of you will associate others with their Lord after the affliction is removed and after the distress. So the meaning of the statement is astonishment at associating others with God after being saved from destruction. This meaning is repeated in the Qur'an, and it was mentioned previously in Al-An'am and Yunus, and it will come in Glory be to Him and others. Al-Zajjaj said: This is specific to those who disbelieve.
16:55: That they may disbelieve in what We have given them meaning that they may deny the blessing of God that He bestowed upon them of removing harm and calamity. That is, they associated partners with God in order to deny, so the lam is the lam of ki. It was also said that it is the lam of consequence. It was also said: That they may disbelieve in what We have given them meaning that they may make the blessing a reason for disbelief, and all of this is an evil act, as He said: And disbelief is a wickedness to the soul of the benefactor Enjoy yourselves is a threatening command. Abdullah read Say, Enjoy yourselves. You will soon know meaning the outcome of your affair.
16:56: The Almighty said: And they assign to that which they do not know a share of what We have provided for them. He mentioned another type of their ignorance, and that they assign to that which they do not know that it can harm or benefit - namely idols - something of their wealth by which they draw near to it, as stated by Mujahid, Qatadah, and others. So -يعلمونaccording to this refers to the polytheists. It was said that it refers to the idols, and it was followed by the waw and the nun in the manner of those who understand, so it is a response toماand the object ofيعلمis omitted, and the meaning is: And these disbelievers assign to the idols that do not know anything a share. The explanation of this meaning has already been mentioned inالعناعin His statement: And they said, 'This is for God,' according to their claim, and this is for our partners. (العناع: 86) Then He returned from the report to the address, saying: By God, you will be asked. This is a question of rebuke. About what you were inventing, meaning what you were fabricating of lies about God that He commanded you to do this.
16:57: The Almighty’s saying: And they attribute to God daughters was revealed about Khuza’ah and Kinanah, for they claimed that the angels were the daughters of God, so they used to say: Attach daughters to daughters. “Glory be to Him.” He has exalted Himself and glorified Himself above what they have attributed to Him of taking children. And they will have whatever they desire. That is, they attribute to themselves sons and are disgusted by daughters. The position of what is raised as the subject, and the predicate is for them, and the discussion is complete when He says: Glory be to Him. Al-Farra’ permitted it to be accusative, on the assumption: And they attribute to themselves whatever they desire. Al-Zajjaj denied it and said: The Arabs use in such a case the word and they attribute to themselves.
16:58: God the Almighty said: And when one of them is given the good report of a female meaning, one of them is informed of the birth of a girl. His face remains dark meaning, changed, and it does not mean blackness, which is the opposite of whiteness, but rather it is a metaphor for his grief over the girl. The Arabs say about anyone who encounters something bad: his face has turned black with grief and sadness, as Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Mawardi narrated that what is meant is the blackness of the complexion, and he said: This is the opinion of the majority. And he is full of grief meaning, full of grief. Ibn Abbas said: Sad. Al-Akhfash said: He is the one who suppresses his anger and does not express it. It was said: He is the one who is grieved and closes his mouth and does not speak from grief, taken from the word kazama which is tightening the mouth of the water skin, as Ali bin Isa said. This meaning was mentioned previously in Surah Yusuf.
16:59: The Almighty said: He hides himself from the people meaning he disappears and disappears. From the evil of what he was given good report meaning from the evil of the grief, shame and shyness that will befall him because of the girl. Does he hold it back? He mentioned the metaphor because it is a response to what. On humiliation meaning humiliation. And this is how Isa Al-Thaqafi read on humiliation and humiliation is humiliation in the language of Quraysh, as Al-Yazidi said and Abu Ubaid narrated it from Al-Kisa'i. Al-Farra' said: It is little in the language of Tamim. Al-Kisa'i said: It is affliction and hardship. Al-Khansa' said: We humiliate the souls, and the souls on the day of calamity will remain for them Al-A'mash read Is he holding him back on evil Al-Nahhas mentioned it. He said: Al-Jahdary read or is he burying her in the dust which contradicts his statement with the female and requires him to read Is he holding her back. It was said: The humiliation refers to the girl, meaning does he hold her while she is humiliated in his eyes. It was also said: It refers to the child for whom he was born, does he hold her against his will or bury her in the dust? This is what they used to do when they buried their daughters alive. Qatada said: Mudar and Khuza'a used to bury their daughters alive, and the most severe of them in this were Tamim. They claimed that they feared being oppressed and that people who were not equal to them coveted them. Whenever Sa'sa'ah ibn Najiyah, the uncle of Al-Farazdaq, felt something like that, he would send camels to the father of the girl to make her feel ashamed of that. Al-Farazdaq said, boasting: My uncle who prevented the birth of infants and revived the stillborn, so he did not bury them alive. It was said: He hid it means he concealed it from the distance so that it is not recognized, like something hidden in the dirt to hide it from sight, and this is possible. Issue - It was reported in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: “A woman came to me with her two daughters, and she asked me for something but she did not find anything with me except one date, so I gave it to her. She took it and divided it between her two daughters and did not eat anything from it. Then she got up and went out with her two daughters, and she entered upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she told him her story. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Whoever is afflicted with a calamity among daughters, then is informed that in being patient with them and being kind to them is what protects from the Fire. ’” It was narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: “A poor woman came to me carrying two daughters, so I fed her three dates. She gave each of them a date, and she raised a date to her mouth to eat. Her two daughters asked for it, so she split the date that she wanted to eat between them. I was impressed by her behavior, so I mentioned what I had done to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: ‘God, the Almighty, has made Paradise obligatory for her because of it or freed her from the Fire because of it. ’” It was narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever supports two girls until… They both said: On the Day of Resurrection, he and I will come, and he joined his fingers together. Muslim, may God have mercy on him, also narrated them both. Abu Naim al-Hafiz narrated from the hadith of al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Wa’il on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has a daughter and educates her well, teaches her well, and bestows upon her the blessings of God that He bestowed upon him, she will be a covering or a veil for him from the Fire. And Uqayl ibn Ulafa proposed to his daughter al-Jarba’, saying: Even if I am given a thousand dowries, two slaves, and ten camels I love my in-laws to the grave Abdullah bin Tahir said: Every father has three sons-in-law who look after his daughter’s affairs. If the son-in-law is praised, A husband takes care of her, a tent shelters her, and a grave covers her, but the best of them is the grave. How evil is that which they judge. That is, in attributing daughters to their Creator and attributing sons to them. Similar to Do you have the male and He has the female? That, then, is an unfair division. (al-Najm 53:21-22) That is, a reward, and it will come.
16:60: The Almighty said: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter meaning for those who describe daughters to God is an evil example meaning an evil characteristic of ignorance and disbelief. It was said: It is God's description of them as having a wife and a son. It was also said: Meaning torment and Hellfire. And to God is the highest example meaning the highest description of sincerity and monotheism, as Qatada said. It was also said: Meaning the highest attribute that He is the Creator, Provider, Able and Rewarder. Ibn Abbas said: An evil example is Hellfire, and the highest example is the testimony that there is no god but God. It was also said: There is nothing like Him.
