It was also said: And to God is the highest example like His saying: "God is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light" (al-Nur 24:35). If it is said: How did He add the example here to Himself when He said: So do not make comparisons for God, the answer is that His saying: So do not make comparisons for God, meaning the comparisons that necessitate similarities and deficiencies, that is, do not make a comparison for God that necessitates deficiency and likening Him to creation. And the highest example is His description of Him with that which has no likeness or peer, glory be to Him and He is far above what the wrongdoers and deniers say, far above. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, its meaning has been presented previously.
16:61: The Almighty said: And if God were to punish people for their wrongdoing meaning their disbelief and their fabrications, and their hastening. He would not have left upon it meaning on the earth, so it is a metaphor for something not mentioned, but it is indicated by His saying: of a creature because a creature does not move except on the earth. The intended meaning of a creature is a disbelieving creature, so it is specific. It was said: The meaning is that if the fathers were destroyed for their disbelief, there would not have been children. It was said: The intended meaning of the verse is general, meaning if God were to punish the creation for what they earned, He would not have left upon the face of this earth a creature, not a prophet or anyone else. This is the saying of Al-Hasan. Ibn Mas`ud said and recited this verse: If God were to punish the creation for the sins of the sinners, the punishment would have afflicted all of creation, even the dung beetle in its hole, and He would have withheld the rain from the sky and the plants from the earth, so the creatures would have died. But God takes with forgiveness and bounty, as He said: And He pardons much (al-Shura 42:30). So when their term has come meaning the term of their death and the end of their lives. They will not be delayed an hour, nor will they be advanced. This has been mentioned before. If it is said: How can they be destroyed when there is among them a believer who is not a wrongdoer? It is said: The destruction of the wrongdoer is made a revenge and a punishment, and the destruction of the believer is compensated with the reward of the Hereafter. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When God intends to punish a people, the punishment afflicts whoever is among them, then they are resurrected according to their intentions. And on the authority of Umm Salamah, she was asked about the army that is swallowed up by the earth, and that was during the time of Ibn al-Zubayr, so she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A seeker seeks refuge in the House, and an army is sent to him, and when they are in a desert on the earth, they are swallowed up. I said: O Messenger of God, what about the one who was unwilling? He said: He will be swallowed up with them, but he will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection according to his intention. We have already mentioned this meaning in detail in the Book of Remembrance, and it has been mentioned in Al-Ma’idah and at the end of Al-An’am, what is sufficient in it, and praise be to God. It was said: And when their time comes meaning when the Day of Resurrection comes. And God knows best.
16:62: The Almighty said: And they attribute to God that which they hate meaning daughters. And their tongues describe falsehood meaning their tongues say falsehood. That they will have the best Mujahid said: It is their saying that they will have sons and God will have daughters. Lying is the object of describing and that is in the place of half instead of lying, because it is an explanation of it. It was said: The best is the good reward, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid and Ibn Muhaisin read lying with the kaf, dhal and baa raised as an attribute of the tongues, and likewise And do not say about what your tongues describe falsehood and lying is the plural of liar, like messenger and messengers and patient and patience and thankful and thankful and thankful. No is a response to their saying, and the statement is complete, meaning it is not as you claim. It is true that they will have the fire meaning it is true that they will have the fire. It has already been presented in full. And that they will be the forerunners left and forgotten in the Fire, said Ibn al-A’rabi, Abu Ubaidah, al-Kisa’i and al-Farra’, and it is the opinion of Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid. Ibn Abbas and Sa’id ibn Jubayr also said: banished. Qatada and al-Hasan: hastened to the Fire, brought forward to it. The one who is the forerunner is the one who goes to the water, and from this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I will be your forerunner to the Cistern, meaning I will be ahead of you. Al-Qatami said: They hastened us and they were among our companions, just as a camel hurried to its destination. Al-Furt: those who are ahead in seeking water. Al-Ward: those who are behind. Nafi’ read in the narration of Warsh Mufarithoon with a kasra on the ra’ and a shaddah on it, and it is the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud and Ibn Abbas, and its meaning is extravagant in sins and disobedience, meaning they went to extremes in it. It is said: So-and-so went to extremes on so-and-so if he was rude to him and said to him more evil than he said. Abu Ja’far Al-Qari’ read Mufarithoon with a kasra on the ra’ and a shaddah on it, meaning they are wasting God’s command, so it is from neglecting what is obligatory.
16:63: God the Almighty said: By God, We sent to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds pleasing to them. That is, their evil deeds. This is a consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that his people had disbelieved in the prophets who came before him. So he is their protector today, that is, he will support them in this world, according to their claim. And for them is a painful punishment, in the Hereafter. It was also said: So he is their protector, that is, their companion in the Fire. Today means the Day of Resurrection, and it was given the name today because of its fame. It was also said that they will be told on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:This is your protector, so seek his support so that he may save you from the punishment, as a way of rebuking them.
16:64: The Almighty said: And We have not sent down to you the Book meaning the Qur’an except that you may make clear to them that over which they differed of religion and rulings, so that the argument against them may be established by your explanation. Guidance and mercy is connected to the position of His statement: to make clear because its position is accusative. The metaphor of the speech is: And We have not sent down to you the Book except as clarification for the people. And guidance meaning right guidance and mercy for the believers.
16:65: The Almighty said: And God sends down from the sky meaning the clouds. water, and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness. The speech returns to enumerating blessings and explaining the perfection of power. Indeed in that is a sign meaning an indication of the resurrection and of His oneness, since they knew that their deity cannot do anything. So this indication is for a people who hear from God Almighty with their hearts, not their ears. For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but blind are the hearts which are within the breasts (al-Hajj 22:46).
16:66: It contains ten issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: And indeed, in the livestock is a lesson for you. We have already discussed livestock, which here are the four types: camels, cows, sheep, and goats. For a lesson means an indication of God’s power, oneness, and greatness. The origin of a lesson is to represent something in order to know its reality through similarity, and from it then take heed. Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: The lesson in the livestock is their subjugation to their masters and their obedience to them, and your rebellion against your Lord and your opposition to Him in everything. One of the greatest lessons is an innocent person carrying a guilty person. The second - the Almighty’s saying: We give you to drink. The reading of the people of Medina, Ibn Amir, and Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr with the fat-ha on the nun from saqa I give yasqa. The rest and Hafs from Asim read with the damma on the nun from asqa I give yasqa, and this is the reading of the Kufians and the people of Mecca. It was said: They are two dialects. Labid said: He watered my people, Bani Majd, and watered Namir and the tribes from Hilal. It was said: It is said that what is from your hand to your mouth, you water it. So if you make it a place to drink or expose it to drink with its mouth or plant it, you say, you water it. This was said by Ibn Aziz, and it was mentioned earlier. A group read tasqikum with a ta’, which is weak, meaning the livestock. It was read with a ya’, meaning God the Almighty waters you. The reciters are on the two previous readings, so the fatha on the noon is the language of Quraysh and the damma on it is the language of Himyar. Third - The Almighty’s saying: Of what is in their bellies. People differed about what the pronoun in His saying of what is in their bellies refers to. It was said: It refers to what precedes it, which is the feminine plural. Sibawayh said: The Arabs choose from the cattle with the report of the singular. Ibn al-Arabi said: I do not see it relied on except from this verse, and this does not resemble its position nor is it appropriate to comprehend it. It was said: Since the collective word, which is the generic noun, is masculine and feminine, and it is said: He is the cattle and she is the cattle, it is permissible for the pronoun to refer to the masculine, and this was said by al-Zajjaj. Al-Kisa’i said: Its meaning is from what is in the bellies of what we mentioned, so it refers to what is mentioned, and God the Almighty said: “Indeed, it is a reminder. So whoever wills may remember it.” (Abasa 80:11-12) And the poet said: Like chickens, we pluck their crops. And there are many similar examples. Al-Kisa’i said: from what is in their bellies meaning from what is in the bellies of some of them, since males do not have milk, and this is what Abu Ubaidah relied on. Al-Farra’ said: Cattle and livestock are one and the same, and livestock is masculine, and that is why the Arabs say: This is a coming blessing, so the pronoun refers to the word livestock which has the same meaning as livestock. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The masculine refers to the meaning of the plural, and the feminine to the meaning of the group, so he mentioned it here in consideration of the plural word, and he made it feminine in Surat Al-Mu’minun in consideration of the Friday word, so he said: We give you to drink from what is in their bellies (al-Mu’minun 23:21). With this interpretation, the meaning is well organized. The feminine is in consideration of the group word and the masculine is in consideration of the plural word, more than the sands of Yabrin and the deserts of Palestine. Fourth - Some of the great scholars, namely Judge Ismail, inferred from the return of this pronoun that the milk of a stallion indicates prohibition. He said: It was brought in the masculine form because it refers to the mention of blessings, because milk for the male is considered, and therefore the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled that the milk of a stallion is prohibited when Aisha denied it in the hadith of Aflah, the brother of Abu al-Qais The woman has the right to water and the man has the right to fertilize, so it was shared between them. The statement about the prohibition of the milk of a stallion has already been made in Women, and praise be to God. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: From between excrement and blood, pure milk. God the Almighty pointed out His great power by bringing out the milk pure between excrement and blood. Excrement is the manure that descends into the rumen, so when it comes out it is not called excrement. It is said: The rumen excreted if it brought out what was in it. The meaning is that the food is made up of what is in the rumen and blood, then the milk is purified from the blood. God the Almighty informed that this milk comes out from between that and the blood in the veins. Ibn Abbas said: The animal eats fodder, so when it settles in its rumen it cooks it, so its lower part is excrement, its middle is milk, and its upper part is blood. The liver is in charge of these types, so it divides the blood, distinguishes it, and tests it in the udder, and the milk flows in the udder, while the excrement remains as it is in the rumen. A profound wisdom, for what avail are the warnings? (al-Qamar 54:5). Pure means from the redness of the blood and the filth of the excrement, and they are combined in one vessel. Ibn Bahr said: Pure is its whiteness. Al-Nabigha said: With the purest of green-shouldered Jordans Any sleeve egg. This is a power that only befits the one who is in charge of everything with interest. Sixth - Al-Naqqash said: This is evidence that semen is not impure. Others have also said the same and argued by saying: Just as milk comes out from between excrement and blood pure and permissible, so too it is permissible for semen to come out of the urinary tract pure and permissible. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is great ignorance and a heinous misconception. Milk is reported to be a blessing and a favor emanating from power in order to be a lesson, so all of that necessitates the description of purity and pleasure, and semen is not of this state so that it can be included in it or analogized to it. I said: This may be opposed by saying: Which of them is greater and more sublime than the emission of semen from which the honored human being is born? God the Almighty said: It comes forth from between the backbone and the ribs (Al-Tariq: 7), and He said: And God has made for you mates from among yourselves and has made for you from your mates sons and grandchildren (Al-Tariq: 7). This is the ultimate in gratitude. If it is said: It becomes impure when it comes out through the urinary tract, we say: That is what we mean, for the impurity is incidental and its origin is pure. It has been said: Its exit is not the exit of urine, especially in women, for the entrance of the penis into it and the exit of the child is not the exit of urine according to what the scholars have said. This has been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. If it is said: Its origin is blood, so it is impure, we say: It is invalidated by musk, for its origin is blood and it is pure. Among those who said that it is pure are Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr and others, based on the hadith of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said: “I used to rub it from the garment of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) while it was dry with my fingernail.” Al-Shafi’i said: If it is not rubbed, then there is nothing wrong with it. Saad bin Abi Waqqas used to rub semen off his clothes. Ibn Abbas said: It is like phlegm. Remove it from yourself with idhkhira and wipe it with a rag. If it is said: It has been proven from Aisha that she said: “I used to wash semen off the clothes of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him), then he would go out to pray in that clothes and I would look at the traces of washing on it.” We say: It is possible that she washed it out of disgust, like the things that are removed from clothes, such as impurity, and this would be a reconciliation between the hadiths. And God knows best. Malik and his companions and Al-Awza’i said: It is impure. Malik said: Washing a wet dream off clothes is an obligatory matter that is agreed upon by us, and it is the opinion of the Kufians. It is narrated from Umar bin Al-Khattab, Ibn Mas’ud, and Jabir bin Samurah that they washed it off their clothes. Ibn Umar and Aisha differed about it. The followers agreed on these two opinions regarding the impurity and purity of semen. Seventh - In this verse there is evidence of the permissibility of benefiting from milk for drinking and other purposes. As for the milk of a dead animal, it is not permissible to benefit from it, because it is a pure liquid that was obtained from an impure vessel. This is because the udder of a dead animal is impure and milk is pure, so when it is milked it becomes taken from an impure vessel. As for the milk of a dead woman, our companions differed concerning it. Those who said that a person is pure whether alive or dead, then it is pure. Those who said that it becomes impure with death, then it is impure. According to both opinions, it is proven to be forbidden, because a child may be nourished by it as he is nourished by a snake. This is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Breastfeeding is that which produces flesh and strengthens bones. He did not specify, and this has already been mentioned in An-Nisa’. Eighth - The Almighty said: Pleasant to the drinkers meaning delicious and easy, and the one who drinks it does not choke on it. It is said: the drink is easy to swallow, meaning it enters the throat easily, and the drinker swallowed it, and I swallowed it, I swallow it, transitive and intransitive, and the best is to swallow it is agitation. It is said: give me time and do not rush me, and the Almighty said: He swallows it but can hardly swallow it (Ibrahim 14:17). The swallow with a kasra on the seen is that which swallows your choking. It is said: water swallows choking, and from this the saying of Al-Kumait: It was a good thing that I was sad It was narrated that no one has ever choked on milk, and this was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ninth - In this verse there is evidence for the use of sweets and delicious foods and eating them. It is not said that this contradicts asceticism or distances it, but if it is done from its proper place and without extravagance or excess. This meaning has been mentioned previously in Al-Ma'idah and other books. In the Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of Anas who said: I gave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, all of these drinks in my cup: honey, wine, milk, and water. Some of the reciters disliked eating faloodeh and milk from food, while most scholars permitted it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he was at a table with Malik bin Dinar, and faloodeh was brought to him and he refused to eat it, so Al-Hasan said to him: Eat! For you have to drink more than this from cold water. Tenth - Abu Dawud and others narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was brought milk and he drank it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘When one of you eats food, let him say: O God, bless it for us and feed us better than it.’ And when he is given milk to drink, let him say: O God, bless it for us and give us more of it, for nothing replaces food and drink except milk.’” Our scholars said: How could it not be so when it is the first thing that a person is nourished with and by which the body and body grow? It is a food free from corruption and by which the body is strengthened. God the Almighty made it a sign for Gabriel of the guidance of this nation which is the best nation. He said in the Sahih: “Then Gabriel came to me with a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk. I chose milk. Gabriel said to me: ‘You have chosen the natural disposition. If you had chosen wine, your nation would have gone astray.’” Then, in supplication for more of it is a sign of fertility and the appearance of goodness and blessings, so it is all blessed.
16:67: There are two issues: First - The Almighty’s saying: And from the fruits of the palm trees. At-Tabari said: The meaning is: And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines is what you take, so he deleted what and the evidence for its deletion is his saying: from it. It was said: The deletion of the deleted thing is something, and the matter is close. It was said: The meaning of from it is from what was mentioned, so there is no deletion in the speech and this is more appropriate. It is permissible for his saying: and from the fruits to be in apposition to the livestock, meaning and for you from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines is a lesson. It is permissible for it to be in apposition to from what, meaning and We also give you drinks from the fruits. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Sakra intoxication. Sakra is that which intoxicates. This is the well-known view in the language. Ibn Abbas said: This verse was revealed before the prohibition of alcohol. What he meant by sakra was alcohol, and by good provision was everything that is eaten and drunk lawfully from these two trees. This view was shared by Ibn Jubayr, Al-Nakha’i, Al-Sha’bi and Abu Thawr. It has been said that sakra means vinegar in the language of Abyssinia, and good provision means food. It has also been said that sakra is the sweet, lawful juice, and it was called sakra because it may become intoxicating if left alone, and when it reaches intoxication, it is forbidden. Ibn Al-Arabi said: “The most correct of these views is the view of Ibn Abbas, and this can be interpreted in one of two ways: Either it was before the prohibition of alcohol, or the meaning is: God has blessed you with the fruits of palm trees and grapes, from which you take what God has forbidden you out of aggression on your part, and what He has permitted you out of agreement or with the intention of benefiting yourselves. The correct view is that this was before the prohibition of alcohol, so it is abrogated, because this verse is Meccan by consensus of the scholars, and the prohibition of alcohol is Medinan.” I said: So, the fact that sugar is vinegar or sweet juice is not abrogated, and the verse is decisive and good. Ibn Abbas said: The Abyssinians call vinegar sugar, except that the majority of scholars say that sugar is wine, including Ibn Masoud, Ibn Omar, Abu Razin, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Abi Laila, Al-Kalbi and others who were mentioned above, all of them said: Sugar is what God has forbidden from their two fruits. And the linguists said the same: Sugar is the name for wine and what intoxicates, and they recited: Bad health and bad drinking is their drinking when they are drunk and intoxicated. Good provision: what God has made lawful of their two fruits. It was said: His statement you take from it intoxicant is a report item with the meaning of a question in the sense of denial, i.e. do you take from it intoxicant and leave good provision, such as vinegar, raisins, and dates, like His statement: They are the immortals (al-Anbiya 21:34), i.e. I understand the immortals. And God knows best. Abu Ubaidah said: Intoxicant is taste. It is said: This is intoxicant for you, meaning taste. And he recited: I made the faults of the most generous people into sugar That is, He made their blame a taste. This is the choice of Al-Tabari, that sugar is what is eaten from food and it is permissible to drink it from the fruits of palm trees and grapes, and it is good provision, so the wording is different but the meaning is the same, like I only complain of my suffering and my grief to God (Yusuf 12:86) and this is good and there is no abrogation, except that Al-Zajjaj said: This statement of Abu Ubaidah is not known, and the people of interpretation are against it, and he has no proof in the verse that he recited, because its meaning according to others is that he describes that it ferments with the faults of people. The Hanafis said: What is meant by his saying: intoxication is what does not intoxicate from wines, and the evidence for that is that God, the Most High, has bestowed His favor upon His servants with what He created for them from that, and favor does not occur except with something permissible and not something forbidden, so that is evidence of the permissibility of drinking less than intoxicating wine, so if it leads to intoxication then it is not permissible, and they supported this from the Sunnah with what was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: God has forbidden wine itself and intoxication from other than it. And what was narrated by Abdul Malik bin Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: “I saw a man come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was at the corner, and he gave him a cup, so he raised it to his mouth and found it hard, so he returned it to its owner. Then a man from the people said to him: O Messenger of God, is it forbidden? He said: Bring me the man. So he was brought to him, and he took the cup from him, then he called for water and poured it into it, then he raised it to his mouth and frowned, then he called for water again and poured it into it, then he said: If these vessels become difficult for you, break their backs with water. It was narrated: “That he, peace be upon him, would have some wine made for him and he would drink it that day, and when it was the second or third day, the servant would give it to him to drink if it had changed, and if it had been forbidden, he would not have given it to him to drink.” Al-Tahawi said: Abu Awn Al-Thaqafi narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaddad on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Wine itself is forbidden, whether a little or a lot, and intoxication from every drink. Al-Daraqutni also included it. In this hadith and others like it, it is stated that other than wine itself is not forbidden as it was forbidden. Wine itself. They said: Wine is the drink of grapes, there is no disagreement about it. Another piece of their evidence is what was narrated by Sharik bin Abdullah, Abu Ishaq Al-Hamadani told us on the authority of Amr bin Maymun, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab said: We eat the meat of these camels, and nothing cuts it from our stomachs except wine. Sharik said: I saw Al-Thawri drinking wine in the house of the scholar of his time, Malik bin Mughal. The answer is that their statement: God Almighty has bestowed His favor upon His servants, and His favor is only through what He has permitted, is correct. However, it is possible that this was before the prohibition of wine, as we have explained, in which case it would have been abrogated, as we have stated previously. Ibn al-Arabi said: If it is said, How can this be abrogated when it is a report and abrogation is not allowed in the report? We say: “This is the speech of one who has not verified the Shari’ah. We have already explained that if the report is about real existence or about giving a reward as a favor from God, then it is something that abrogation is not allowed in. However, if the report includes a legal ruling, then the rulings are changed and abrogated, whether they came with a report or a command. Abrogation does not refer to the wording itself, but rather to what it includes. If you understand this, you will have left the foolish type that God spoke about the disbelievers in His statement: “And when We substitute a verse for a verse - and God is most knowing of what He sends down - they say, ‘You are only an inventor.’ But most of them do not know.” (al-Nahl 16:101) The meaning is that they were ignorant of the fact that the Lord commands what He wills and orders what He wills, and He removes from that with His justice what He wills and confirms what He wills, and with Him is the Mother of the Book. I said: This is a heinous slander, so that the good scholars are included in it with the infidels in their lack of understanding. The issue is a fundamental one, which is whether reports about the legal rulings can be abrogated or not. There is disagreement about that, and the correct view is that it is permissible for this verse and what is similar to it, and because the report about the legitimacy of a ruling includes a request for that which is permissible, and that request is the legal ruling that is used as evidence for its abrogation. And God knows best. As for the hadiths they mentioned, the first and second are weak, because it has been narrated from him (peace be upon him) with a proven chain of transmission that he said: Every drink that intoxicates is forbidden, and he said: Every intoxicant is wine, and every intoxicant is forbidden, and he said: Whatever intoxicates in large amounts, a small amount of it is forbidden. Al-Nasa’i said: These are the people of steadfastness and justice, and they are famous for the soundness of their transmission, and Abd al-Malik cannot take the place of one of them, even if he was supported by a group of his ilk, and God is the Grantor of success. As for the third, even if it is correct, he did not give it to the servant as if it was an intoxicant, but rather he gave it to him because its smell had changed. The Prophet (peace be upon him) hated to have a bad smell from it, so he did not drink it. That is why his wives tricked him into drinking Zainab’s honey, saying to him: We smell a musty smell from you, meaning a bad smell. So he did not drink it after that. It will come in the chapter on prohibition. As for the hadith of Ibn Abbas, something different has been narrated from him from the narration of Ata’, Tawus and Mujahid, that he said: Whatever intoxicates in large amounts, a small amount of it is forbidden. Qais ibn Dinar narrated it from him. Likewise, his fatwa on intoxicants was said by Ad-Daraqutni. The first hadith was narrated from him by Abdullah ibn Shaddad, and the group disagreed with him, so the statement about it was dropped with what was proven from the Prophet (peace be upon him). As for what was narrated from ‘Umar, that he said: Nothing cuts it in our stomachs except wine, he meant something other than intoxicants, based on the evidence we mentioned. An-Nasa’i narrated from ‘Utbah ibn Farqad, who said: The wine that ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattab drank had turned sour. Al-Nasa’i said: What indicates the authenticity of this is the hadith of al-Sa’ib. Al-Harith ibn Maskeen said, “I read it to him while I was listening on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim: Malik told me on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid, that he told him that Umar ibn al-Khattab came out to them and said: ‘I found the smell of alcohol on so-and-so, and he claimed that it was a lacquer drink, and I will ask about what he drank, so if it was intoxicating, I will flog him.’ So Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, flogged him in full.” And he said in his sermon on the pulpit of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And after, O people, the prohibition of wine has been revealed, and it is from five things: grapes, honey, dates, wheat, and barley. Wine is that which intoxicates the mind. This has been mentioned in Al-Ma’idah. If it is said: Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i and Abu Ja’far Al-Tahawi permitted its drinking, and he was the imam of his time, and Sufyan Al-Thawri used to drink it. We say: Al-Nasa’i mentioned in his book that the first one to permit intoxicants from wines was Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i, and this is a slip of the tongue from a scholar, and we have warned against the slip of a scholar, and there is no argument in the statement of anyone with the Sunnah. Al-Nasa’i also mentioned from Ibn Al-Mubarak, who said: I did not find a concession regarding intoxicants from anyone authentically except from Ibrahim. Abu Usamah said: I have not seen a man more inquisitive about the Levant, Egypt, Yemen, and the Hijaz than Abdullah Ibn Al-Mubarak. As for Al-Tahawi and Sufyan, if that was authentically reported from them, then those imams who disagreed with them regarding the prohibition of intoxicants would not have used them as evidence, despite what was proven from the Sunnah. However, Al-Tahawi mentioned: In his great book on differences, there is a difference of opinion. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said in his book Al-Tamhid: Abu Jaafar Al-Tahawi said: The Ummah agreed that if grape juice becomes strong and boils and produces foam, then it is wine and whoever permits it is a disbeliever. They differed about the infusion of dates if it reaches and intoxicates. He said: This shows you that the hadith of Yahya bin Abi Katheer from Abu Hurairah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Wine is from these two trees, the palm tree and the grape,” is not acted upon by them, because if they had accepted the hadith, they would have declared the one who permits the infusion of dates to be a disbeliever. So I accepted that nothing is included in the forbidden wine except grape juice that has become strong and reached the point of intoxication. He said: Then it is not without the prohibition being attached to it only, and nothing else is being compared to it, or it is obligatory to compare it, so we found that they all compared the infusion of dates to it if it reaches and intoxicates in large quantities, and the same applies to the infusion of raisins. He said: So it is obligatory by analogy to that that all drinks that intoxicate are prohibited. He said: It has been narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Every intoxicant is forbidden. He dispensed with the need for a chain of transmission because everyone accepted it. The difference between them is in its interpretation. Some of them said: He meant by it the type of thing that intoxicates. Some of them said: He meant by it that which causes intoxication, just as it is not called a killer except when there is killing. I said: This indicates that it is forbidden according to Al-Tahawi based on his statement, so it is obligatory by analogy to prohibit all drinks that intoxicate. Ad-Daraqutni narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that she said: God did not prohibit it because of its name, but rather He prohibited it because of its consequences. So every drink that has consequences like those of wine is forbidden, just as wine is forbidden. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The people of Kufa came with well-known reports, and if people differ about something, it must be referred back to the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger (peace be upon him). What was narrated from some of the followers that drinking a drink that intoxicates in large amounts, then the people have sins for which they seek forgiveness from God. This is not devoid of one of two meanings: Either a person made a mistake in interpreting a hadith he heard, or a man who committed a sin so that he might increase his seeking forgiveness from God Almighty, and the Prophet (peace be upon him) is God’s proof over the first and last of this nation. It has been said in the interpretation of the verse: It was mentioned for consideration, meaning that the One who is able to create these things is able to resurrect, and this consideration does not differ whether wine is permissible or forbidden, so taking alcohol does not indicate prohibition, and it is as God Almighty said: “Say: In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people” (al-Baqarah 2:219) and God knows best.
16:68: It has three issues: First - His Almighty saying: And your Lord inspired the bee. We have already discussed revelation and that it may mean inspiration, which is what God Almighty creates in the heart from the beginning without an apparent reason, and it is from His Almighty saying: And by the soul and He who proportioned it, and inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness. (Ash-Shams: 7-8). And from that are the animals and what God Almighty creates in them of attaining their benefits and avoiding their harms and managing their livelihood. And God Almighty informed us of that about death, saying: It reports its report, because your Lord has inspired it. (Az-Zalzalah: 4-5). Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i Al-Harbi said: God Almighty has a power in death, the nature of which is not known, no messenger from God came to it, but God Almighty made it known, that is, He inspired it. There is no disagreement among the interpreters that revelation here means inspiration. Yahya bin Waththab read to the bees with a fat-ha on the ha. And it was called a bee because God Almighty inspired it with the honey that comes out of it, as Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Jawhari: The word bee and bee-bee are used for both males and females, so much so that it is said: yasub. The word bee is feminine in the language of the people of Hijaz, and every plural has only one letter between it and its singular. It was narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: All flies will be in the Fire, making it a torment for the people of the Fire, except the bee. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim mentioned it in Nawader Al-Usul. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade the killing of the ant, the bee, the hoopoe, and the shrike.” It was also narrated by Abu Dawud, and it will come in the ants, God willing. The second - the Almighty’s saying: That you take for yourself in the mountains, houses, and in the trees. This is if it has no owner. And in what they build. God made the bees’ houses in these three types, either in the mountains and their niches, or in the hollows of trees, or in what the son of Adam builds in the form of huts, hives, walls, and others. The meaning of arsh here is prepared, and it is most often used in what is done with the perfection of branches and wood and the arrangement of their shades. From this comes the arsh that was made for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr, and from this comes the word arsh. It is said: arsh ya’rash and ya’rash with a kasra or damma on the ra’, and it was recited with both of them. Ibn ‘Amir recited with a damma and the rest of them with a kasra, and there is a difference of opinion regarding that from ‘Aasim. Third - Ibn al-Arabi said: Among the wonders of what God created in bees is that He inspired them to make their homes hexagonal, and so they connected until they became like a single piece. This is because the shapes from the triangle to the swarm, if each one of them is collected with its likes, they do not connect and there is a space between them, except for the hexagonal shape, which if it is collected with its likes, it connects as if it is like a single piece.
16:69: The Almighty said: Then eat of all the fruits because they only eat the blossoms of the trees. Then follow the ways of your Lord made easy meaning the paths of your Lord. Paths: roads, and He added them to Him because He is their Creator. That is, enter the ways of your Lord to seek provision in the mountains and through the trees. Dhula is the plural of Dhuluul which means led, meaning obedient and subservient. So Dhula is a state of the bees. That is, they are led and go wherever their owner wants, because they follow their owners wherever they go, said Ibn Zayd. It was said that what is meant by His saying Dhula is the paths. He says: Its paths are made easy to follow, and Al-Tabari chose it, and Dhula is a state of the paths. And the dragonfly is the master of the bees, if it stands it stands and if it walks it walks. The Almighty says: There emerges from their bellies a drink of varying colors in which there is healing for people. There are nine issues in this: First: The Almighty said: It comes forth from their bellies. The address returned to the report of order to enumerate the blessing and draw attention to the lesson, so He said: It comes forth from their bellies a drink, meaning honey. The majority of people are of the opinion that honey comes forth from the mouths of bees. It was reported from Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said in his contempt for the world: The most honorable clothing of the son of Adam in it is the saliva of a worm, and the most delicious drink he drinks is the vomit of a bee. So it appears from this that it is not from the mouth. In short, it comes forth and it is not known from within it or below it, but its repair is not completed except by the fever of its breath. Aristotle made a house of glass to see how it was made, but it refused to work until he smeared the inside of the glass with clay, mentioned by Al-Ghaznawi. He said: From their bellies because the transformation of foods does not occur except in the belly. Second - The Almighty’s saying: Its colors vary means its types, including red, white, yellow, solid, and liquid. The mother is one and the children are different, which is evidence that the ability varied it according to the variety of food, just as its taste varies according to the difference in pastures. From this meaning is the saying of Zainab to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The bees were frightened when they compared its smell to the smell of the Maghafir. Third: The Almighty’s saying, In it is healing for people. The pronoun refers to honey. The majority said that in honey is healing for people. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Farra’ and Ibn Kaysan: The pronoun refers to the Qur’an, that is, in the Qur’an is healing. An-Nahhas said: This is a good statement, or in what we have narrated to you of verses and proofs is healing for people. It was also said that in honey is healing. This statement is also clear, because most of the drinks and pastes that are used for treatment are originally from honey. Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: Whoever says that it is the Qur’an is far-fetched. I do not think it is correct from them, and even if it is correct by transmission, it is not correct rationally, because the context of the entire speech is honey, and there is no mention of the Qur’an in it. Ibn Atiyyah said: Some of the ignorant people believed that this verse refers to the people of the house and Banu Hashim, and that they are the bees, and that the drink is the Qur’an and wisdom. Some of them mentioned this in the assembly of Al-Mansur Abu Ja’far Al-Abbasi, and a man who was present said to him: May God make your food and drink from what comes out of the bellies of Banu Hashim. He made those present laugh, and the other was dumbfounded, and the absurdity of his statement became clear. Fourth: The scholars differed regarding the statement of God the Almighty: Therein is healing for people - is it general or not? A group said that it is general in every situation and for everyone. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he did not complain of an ulcer or anything except that he put honey on it, even if a boil came out on him, he would smear it with honey. Al-Naqqash narrated on the authority of Abu Wajrah that he used to apply honey to his eyes, use honey as a mouthwash, and use honey as a medicine. It was narrated that Awf bin Malik Al-Ashja’i fell ill and it was said to him: Shall we not treat you? He said: Bring me water, for God the Almighty says: And We sent down from the sky blessed water. Then he said: Bring me honey, for God the Almighty says: Therein is healing for people. And bring me oil, for God the Almighty says: From a blessed tree. So they brought him all of that, so he mixed it all together and drank it and was cured. Some of them said that it is general: it is mixed with vinegar and cooked and drunk and is beneficial in every situation from every illness. A group said that this is specific and does not require generality in every illness and every person, but rather it is report that it heals as other medicines heal in some cases and in some cases more than others, so the benefit of the verse is that it is report from him that it is a medicine because healing is widespread with it and it has become a mixture and a source for medicines in drinks and ointments, and this is not the first word that has been specified, as the Qur’an is full of it, and in the language of the Arabs the general often comes in the meaning of the specific and the specific in the meaning of the general. What indicates that it is not general is that healing is an indefinite noun in the context of affirmation and there is no generality in it according to the agreement of the people of the language and the investigators of the people of knowledge and the various people of the principles. But a group of the people of truth and determination carried it in generality, so they used to heal with honey from all pains and diseases, and they used to heal their illnesses with the blessing of the Qur’an and the soundness of belief and conviction. Ibn al-Arabi: And whoever’s intention is weak and his religion is overcome by it, his habit is to take it understood according to the doctors’ saying, and all are from the rule of the doer of what he wills. Fifth: If someone were to say: We have seen those who are benefited by honey and those who are harmed by it, so how can it be a cure for people? It would be said to him: Water is the life of everything, and we have seen those who are killed by water if they take it for an ailment that opposes it in the body, and we have seen the cure of honey in most of these drinks. Al-Zajjaj said: Its meaning is that the doctors have agreed, one and all, to praise the general benefit of saknajabin in every disease, and its origin is honey, as are all the other pastes, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had resolved the disease of confusion and removed the possibility when he ordered the one who was complaining of stomach pain to drink honey. When his brother informed him that it only increased his diarrhea, he ordered him to drink it again, and he was cured. He said: God is truthful and your brother's stomach is lying Sixth: Some heretical doctors objected to this hadith and said: Doctors have agreed that honey is laxative, so how can it be prescribed for someone who has diarrhea? The answer is that this statement is even in itself, since he has achieved belief in his Prophet, peace be upon him, so he uses it in the manner and in the place that he ordered him to, with good intention and good nature, so he sees its benefit and realizes its blessing, as happened to the owner of this honey and others, as mentioned above. As for what was narrated about the consensus, it is evidence of his ignorance of the transmission, since he did not specify and make it general. Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Mazari said: It should be known that diarrhea occurs from many types, including diarrhea resulting from indigestion and diarrhea, and doctors agree in such a case that its treatment is to leave it to nature and its actions, and if it needs something to help with diarrhea, it helps as long as the strength remains, but holding it back is harmful. So if it becomes clear, then if this becomes clear, we say that it is possible that this man had diarrhea due to fullness and diarrhea, so the Prophet, peace be upon him, ordered him to drink honey, so he increased it until the substance was finished, so the diarrhea stopped, and drinking honey agreed with him. If this is outside the scope of the medical profession, then this indicates the objector’s ignorance of that profession. He said: We do not rely on the statement of our Prophet to prove that the doctors believe him, but if they lied about him, we would lie about them and disbelieve in them and believe him, may God bless him and grant him peace. If we find through observation the truth of what they said, then we need to interpret the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and interpret it in a way that is correct, since evidence has been established that he does not lie. Seventh: In the words of God the Almighty: In it is healing for people is evidence of the permissibility of treating oneself by drinking medicine and other things, contrary to those scholars who disliked that. It is a response to the Sufis who claim that guardianship is not complete unless one is satisfied with all the affliction that has befallen him, and it is not permissible for him to treat himself. There is no meaning for those who deny that. The Sahih narrated on the authority of Jabir on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: For every illness there is a cure, so if the cure for the illness is found, he will be cured by God’s permission. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Usamah ibn Sharik that the Bedouins said: Should we not seek treatment, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes, O servants of God, seek treatment, for God has not created a disease without creating a cure or medicine for it, except for one disease. They said: O Messenger of God, what is it? He said: Old age. The wording of al-Tirmidhi, and he said: A good and authentic hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Khazamah on the authority of his father, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said: O Messenger of God, do you think that there are incantations that we recite, a medicine that we treat ourselves with, and a precaution that we avoid, do they repel anything from the decree of God? He said: They are from the decree of God. He said: A good hadith, and no hadith is known for Abu Khazamah other than this hadith. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If there is any good in your medicines, it is in the incision of a cupper, a drink of honey, or a cauterization with fire. I do not like to be cauterized.” Narrated by Sahih. The hadiths on this topic are too numerous to count. The majority of scholars agree that treatment and incantation are permissible. It was narrated that Ibn Umar used to be cauterized for a sting and used incantations for a scorpion sting. It was narrated from Ibn Sirin that Ibn Umar used to give his son the antidote. Malik said: There is nothing wrong with that. Those who disliked that cited what Abu Hurayrah narrated, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘A nation will enter Paradise, all of them. They did not seek incantations, nor did they use cauterization, nor did they take omens, and they put their trust in their Lord.’” They said: “The believer must leave that, holding fast to God, putting his trust in Him, having confidence in Him, and devoting himself to Him. God, the Most High, knows the days of illness and the days of health. If people were keen to reduce or increase that, they would not be able to do so. God, the Most High, said: ‘No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into being. ’” Among those who held this view were a group of people of virtue and tradition, and it is the view of Ibn Mas`ud and Abu al-Darda’, may God be pleased with them. Uthman ibn Affan entered upon Ibn Mas`ud during the illness in which he died, so Uthman said to him: What do you complain of? He said: My sins. He said: What do you desire? He said: The mercy of my Lord. He said: Shall I not call a doctor for you? The doctor said: He made me sick. He mentioned the hadith and will come in full in Fadl al-Waqi’ah, God willing. Waki’ mentioned: Abu Hilal told us on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Qurra who said: Abu al-Darda’ fell sick, so they visited him and said: Shall we not call a doctor for you? The doctor said: Lay me down. This is what al-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham said, and Sa’id ibn Jubayr disliked incantations. Al-Hasan disliked drinking all medicines except milk and honey. The first scholars responded to the hadith by saying that it is not an argument, because it is possible that he intended a type of cauterization that is disliked, as evidenced by the Prophet’s cauterization of Ubayy on the Day of the Confederates when he was struck with a spear. He said: Healing is in three things, as mentioned above. It is possible that he intended incantations with something that is not in the Book of God, and God Almighty said: And We send down from the Qur’an that which is healing as will be explained. He incantated his companions and ordered them to do so as will be explained. Eighth: Malik and a group of his companions held that there is no zakat on honey even if it is eaten or eaten. Al-Shafi’i’s opinion differed on it, and what he definitively stated in his new opinion is that there is no zakat on it. Abu Hanifa said that zakat is obligatory on honey, whether it is a little or a lot, because according to him the minimum amount is not a condition. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said that there is nothing on it until it reaches eight farqs, and the farq is thirty-six Iraqi pounds. Abu Yusuf said that there is one skin for every ten skinks, adhering to what al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is one skin for every ten skinks of honey. Abu ‘Isa said that there is something wrong with its chain of transmission, and nothing significant is authentically reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in this matter, and this is what most scholars act upon. Ahmad and Ishaq say, and some scholars said that there is nothing on honey. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying, Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought. That is, they consider. And among the lessons in the bee is the fairness of view and the subtlety of thought in its wondrous affair, so that certainty bears witness that the One Who inspired it with the delicate craftsmanship despite its weak structure and its skill in its deception in its varying conditions is God, the Most High, as He said, And your Lord inspired the bee. Then it eats sour and bitter and sweet and salty and harmful weeds, so God, the Most High, makes it into sweet honey and a cure. And in this is evidence of His power.
16:70: The Almighty said: And God created you, then He will cause you to die. He explained its meaning: And among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age. That is, He willed it and made it weak. It was said: The one whose strength and mind diminish and who becomes senile and the like. Ibn Abbas said: It means to the lowest point of life, he becomes like a child who has no mind. The meaning is close. In Sahih Al-Bukhari: "On the authority of Anas bin Malik, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek refuge, saying: O God, I seek refuge in You from laziness, I seek refuge in You from cowardice, I seek refuge in You from senility, and I seek refuge in You from miserliness." And in the hadith of Sa`d bin Abi Waqqas: And I seek refuge in You from being returned to the most decrepit age. The hadith was included by Al-Bukhari: So that he does not know anything after having known it. That is, he returns to the state of childhood and does not know what he knew before of matters due to extreme old age. It has been said: This does not happen to the believer because the believer’s knowledge is not taken away from him. It has also been said that the meaning is so that he does not do anything after having knowledge. So he expressed action with knowledge because of his need for it, because the effect of arrogance on his action is more powerful than its effect on his knowledge. The intended meaning is to argue with those who deny the resurrection, meaning that the One who returned him to this state is able to kill him and then bring him back to life.
16:71: The Almighty said, And God has favored some of you over others in provision, meaning He made among you rich and poor, free and slave. Then those who are favored, meaning in provision, will not return their provision to those whom their right hands possess, meaning the master will not return anything of what he has provided to those whom his right hand possesses until the slave and the owner are equal in wealth. This is an example that God gave for idol worshippers, meaning if your slaves are not equal with you, then how can you make My slaves equal with me? Since their slaves did not share their wealth with them, it was not permissible for them, meaning to share with God Almighty, in the worship of other than Him, such as idols and stone altars and other things that are worshipped, such as the angels and prophets, even though they are His slaves and creation. Its meaning was narrated by Al-Tabari, and it was also said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and others. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas also that it was revealed about the Christians of Najran when they said Jesus is the son of God, so God said to them, Then those who are favored will not return their provision to those whom their right hands possess. That is, the master will not return what his right hand possesses of what he has provided until the master and the slave are equal in the money according to the law, so how can you accept for me what you do not accept for yourselves, so you make for me a son from among my slaves? And similar to it is, “He has set forth for you an example from among yourselves: Do you have from those whom your right hands possess partners in what We have provided for you, so that you are equal in it?” as will come, and this indicates what will come, and this indicates that the slave does not own what will come earlier.
16:72: The Almighty said: And God has made for you mates from among yourselves made means created, and it was mentioned before. From among yourselves mates means Adam created Eve from him. It was also said that the meaning is He made for you from among yourselves, meaning from your kind and type and according to your creation, as He said: There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves meaning from among the humans. This is a response to the Arabs who believed that they used to marry the jinn and have intercourse with them, to the extent that it was narrated that Omar bin Hind married a ghoul from them and he used to hide her from the lightning so that she would not see it and be frightened. Then one night, the lightning flashed and the otter saw it and said: Amr, and she was frightened, so he never saw her again. This is one of her lies, and although it is permissible in the judgment and wisdom of God, it is a response to the philosophers who deny the existence of the jinn and transform their food. Wives A man's wife is his second wife, for he is an individual, so when she is added to him, they are two wives. The addition was made to him and not to her because he is her origin in existence, as mentioned before. The Almighty’s saying, And He has given you from your wives sons and grandchildren, contains five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying, And He has made for you from your wives sons, is clear in enumerating the blessing in the sons and the existence of the sons is from both of them, but since the creation of the newborn was in her and his separation from her, he was attributed to her, and that is why he followed her in slavery and freedom and became like her in financial status. Ibn al-Arabi said, I heard the Imam of the Hanbalis in Madinah al-Salam, Abu al-Wafa’ Ali ibn Aqil, say: The son only followed the mother in financial status and became like her in slavery and freedom because he was separated from the father as a sperm that has no value or financial status or benefit, but he acquired what he acquired through her and from her, so for that reason he followed her. As if a man ate dates on a man’s land and a seed fell into the ground from the hand of the eater and it became a palm tree, then it is the property of the owner of the land and not the eater by consensus of the nation because it was separated from the eater and has no value. The second: The Almighty’s saying: And grandchildren. Ibn al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Malik that he asked him about the Almighty’s saying: Sons and grandchildren. He said: The grandchildren are servants and helpers in my opinion. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s saying: And grandchildren. He said: They are helpers. Whoever helps you has become your grandchild. It was said to him: Do the Arabs know that? He said: Yes, and they say it. Or have you not heard the poet say: The grandchildren were surrounded by the camels and their hands were covered with the camels’ crisis. That is, the quickest of the servants and the maidservants. One servant is a maidservant. Al-A’sha said: She charged her unknown with Yemeni camels, if the camels were to be worn by the camels’ shepherds That is, they hastened. Ibn Arafa said: The Hafdah among the Arabs means helpers, so whoever does a job, obeys in it and hastens, he is a Hafdah. He said: And from this is their saying We strive to you and hasten, and the Hafdan means speed. Abu Ubaid said: The Hafd is work and service. Al-Khalil bin Ahmad said: The Hafdah among the Arabs means servants, and Mujahid said it, and Al-Azhari said it was said that the Hafdah are the sons of sons. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and it was said that they are the two sisters, and Ibn Masoud, Alqamah, Abu Al-Dhaha, Saeed bin Jubayr, and Ibrahim said it. And from this is the saying of the poet: If my soul had been willing, I would have had countless grandchildren. But she is the same as Ali Abi Ayouf, who is stubborn and filthy to melt the mean ones And Zur narrated on the authority of Abdullah who said: The grandchildren are the in-laws. Ibrahim said the same and the meaning is close. Al-Asma’i said: The brother-in-law is the one who was from the woman’s side, such as her father, brother and the like, and the in-laws are both of them. It is said that so-and-so is the in-law of so-and-so and he is his wife. Abdullah’s statement: They are the two sisters has both meanings. It is possible that he meant the woman’s father and the like of her relatives, and it is possible that he meant: And He made for you from your wives sons and daughters whom you marry so that you will have two sisters because of them. Ikrimah said: The grandchildren are from the benefit of a man from his children and its origin is from hafad yahfad with the fatha of the ‘ayn in the past and the kasra of it in the future. If he hastens in his walk as Katheer said. Grandchildren are the ones who keep the house together. It is said: Hafdat and Ahfadat are two dialects if you serve. It is also said Hafid and Hafid like Khadim and Khudum and Hafid and Hafda like Kafir and Kafir. Al-Mahdawi said that whoever makes Hafda the servants made it separate from what preceded it, intending to present it as if he said He made for you grandchildren and He made for you from your wives sons. I said: What Al-Azhari said, that the grandchildren are the children of the children, is the apparent meaning of the Qur’an, rather its text. Do you not see that he said: And He has made for you from your wives sons and grandchildren, so He made the grandchildren and the sons from them. Ibn Al-Arabi said: What is most apparent to me in His statement sons and grandchildren is that the sons are the children of the man from his loins and the grandchildren are the children of his son, and there is no more force in the wording than this, and the interpretation of the verse according to this is: And He has made for you from your wives sons and from the sons grandchildren. He said its meaning is good. Third: If we branch off from the statement of Mujahid, Ibn Abbas, Malik, and the linguists in their statement that the grandchildren are servants and helpers, then the service of the son and wife has been excluded from the Qur’an in the most wonderful statement that Ibn al-Arabi said. Al-Bukhari and others narrated “on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d: that Abu Asid al-Sa’idi invited the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to his wedding, and his wife was their servant.” The hadith was mentioned previously in Surat Hud, and in the Sahih, “on the authority of Aisha, she said: I twisted the necklaces of the body of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with my own hands.” The hadith is why our scholars said that she should spread the bedding, cook the pot, and clean the house according to her situation and the custom of her. God Almighty said, And He made from her her husband that he might find rest in her. So it is as if He combined for us in her dwelling, enjoyment, and a type of service according to custom. Fourth: A man should serve his wife in whatever service is light and help her, as Aisha narrated: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be doing his family’s chores, and when he heard the call to prayer, he would go out.” This is the statement of Malik, and it helps her. In the morals of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would mend sandals, clean the house, and sew clothes. Aisha said when she was asked: What did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, do in his house? She said: He was a human being like other human beings. He would mend his clothes, milk his sheep, and serve himself. Fifth: He should spend on one female servant, and it has been said that he should spend on more, according to wealth and status. This is a matter that is based on custom, which is one of the principles of the Sharia. Arab women and desert dwellers serve their husbands in fetching water and tending animals. City women, the poor among them serve their wives in what is easy and help them. As for the wealthy, they serve their husbands and live in luxury with them if they have the position to do so. If it is a problematic matter and the wife stipulates that, then she should testify that he has known that she is one of those who does not serve herself, so he has committed to serving her. This should be implemented and the claim regarding it should be dismissed. The Almighty says: And He has provided you with good things meaning fruits, grains, and animals. Then is it in falsehood meaning idols. Ibn Abbas said: They believe The majority read it with a ya. Abu Abd al-Rahman read it with a ta and in the grace of God meaning Islam. They disbelieve
16:73: The Almighty said: And they worship besides God that which possesses no provision for them from the heavens meaning rain and the earth meaning plants anything. Al-Akhfash said it is a substitute for provision. Al-Farra’ said it is in the accusative case because provision is placed upon it, meaning they worship that which does not possess, that is, provide them with anything. And they are not able meaning they are not able to do anything, meaning idols.
16:74: So do not make comparisons for God meaning do not liken these inanimate objects to Him, because He is One, All-Powerful, and there is no likeness to Him, as has been mentioned previously.
16:75: It has five issues: The first is the saying of the Most High: God sets forth an example. God the Most High draws attention to the misguidance of the polytheists. This is consistent with what preceded it of mentioning God’s blessings upon them and the lack of anything like that among their gods. God sets forth an example, that is, he explained a similarity. Then He mentioned that and said: A slave owned. That is, just as a slave owned by someone who has no control over his affairs is not the same to you as a free man who has been provided with a good provision, so too are I and these idols. So the one who is an example in this verse is a slave with this characteristic, owned by someone who has no control over his wealth or his own affairs, but he is only subjected to the will of his master. It is not necessary from the verse that all slaves are of this description, for the indefinite noun in the affirmation does not require comprehensiveness according to the people of the language as mentioned above, but rather it indicates one, so if it comes after a command or prohibition or added to a source, it is for the generality of the communist, like his saying: Free a man and do not humiliate a man, and the source is like freeing a slave, so any man who is freed has been released from the responsibility of the address, and an exception is valid from it, and Qatada said that this example is for the believer and the disbeliever, so Qatada went to the fact that the owned slave is the disbeliever because he does not benefit in the hereafter from anything from his worship, and that the meaning of and whom We have provided with good provision from Us is the believer, and the first is based on the majority of the people of interpretation. Al-Asamm said that what is meant by the owned slave is the one who may be more captivating than his master and have a more radiant face, and he is submissive to his master and is not able to do anything except what he has permitted him to do, so God Almighty said as an example. That is, if this is your affair and the affair of your slaves, you have made dead stones partners with God Almighty in His creation and worship, and they do not understand or hear. Second: Muslims understood from this verse and the one before it that the slave is less in rank than the free man in ownership and that he does not own anything. Even if he owns, the people of Iraq said that slavery contradicts ownership, so he does not own anything at all. This is the new opinion of al-Shafi’i, and this is what al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin said. Some of them said: He owns, except that his ownership is incomplete because his master has the right to take it from him at any time he wants. This is the opinion of Malik and those who followed him, and this is what al-Shafi’i said in the old opinion. This is the opinion of the people of the apparent meaning. For this reason, our companions said: He is not obligated to worship money, such as zakat and expiations, nor from the worship of the body that which cuts him off from serving his master, such as Hajj, jihad, and other things. The benefit of this issue is that if his master owns a female slave, it is permissible for him to have intercourse with her by right of possession. If he owns forty sheep and a year passes over them, the master is not obligated to pay zakat on them because they belong to someone else, nor is the slave because his ownership is not stable. Al-Iraqi says that it is not permissible for him to have intercourse with the female slave, and zakat on the nisab is obligatory on the master as it was. The evidence for this issue for both groups is in the books of disagreement. The most conclusive evidence for us is the saying of God Almighty: God is He Who created you and then provided for you. He made the slave and the free man equal in provision and creation. “And he, peace be upon him, said: Whoever frees a slave and he has wealth,” so he attributed the wealth to him. Ibn Omar saw his slave taking a concubine with his wealth and did not criticize him for that. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that a slave of his divorced his wife twice, so he ordered him to take her back by right of possession. This is evidence that he owns what he has and does with it what the owner does with his property unless his master takes it away. And God knows best. Third: Some scholars have used this verse as evidence that the divorce of a slave is between his master and that the sale of a female slave is her divorce, relying on the Almighty’s saying, He has no power over anything. He said, “Its apparent meaning indicates that he has no power over anything at all, neither over ownership nor anything else, so it is general, unless evidence indicates otherwise. In what we have mentioned from Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas, there is what indicates specificity, and God Almighty knows best.” Fourth: Abu Mansur said in his creed that provision is what is nourished, and this verse refutes this specification, as does the Almighty’s saying: And from what We have provided for them they spend and Spend from what We have provided for you and other than that, “The Prophet’s saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, ‘My provision is placed under the shade of my spear’” and “His saying: The provisions of my nation are in the hooves of their horses and the points of their spears.” So all spoils of war are provision, and everything that is validly benefited from is provision, and it has levels, the highest of which is that which is nourished. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, limited the aspects of benefit in his saying: “The son of Adam says, ‘My wealth, my wealth. Do you have from your wealth anything except what you have eaten and finished, or worn and worn out, or given in charity and passed on?” The meaning of clothing includes riding and other things. In the tongues of the hadith scholars, hearing is provision, meaning hearing the hadith, and it is authentic. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement, And whom We have provided from Us with a good provision is the believer, who obeys God in himself and his wealth. The disbeliever, as long as he does not spend in obedience, becomes like a slave who does not own anything. Are they equal? That is, they are not equal. He did not say they are equal because whom is an indefinite noun that is suitable for one, two, plural, masculine and feminine. It was said that a slave is owned and whom We have provided are intended to be common in gender. Praise be to God, but most of them do not know that is, He is the One who deserves praise, not what they worship besides Him, since the idols have no favor upon them, from a hand or a favor for which they should be praised. Rather, complete praise is due to God, because He is the Benefactor, the Creator. But most of them that is, most of the polytheists do not know that praise is due to Me, and all the favor is from Me. He mentioned most while he means everyone, so it is specific and intended to be general. It was said that is, but most of creation do not know, and that is because most of them are polytheists.
16:76: The Almighty said: And God presents an example of two men, one of them mute. This is another example that God presented for Himself and for the idol. The mute who is unable to do anything is the idol, and the one who commands justice is God, the Almighty. This was said by Qatada and others. Ibn Abbas said: The mute was a slave who belonged to Uthman, may God be pleased with him, and he used to offer him Islam but he refused, and Uthman commanded justice. It was also narrated from him that it was an example for Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and a freedman of his who was an infidel. It was said that the mute was Abu Jahl, and the one who commanded justice was Ammar ibn Yasir al-Ansi. Anas with the letter nun is a tribe from Madhhij and was an ally of Banu Makhzum, the people of Abu Jahl. Abu Jahl used to torture him for Islam and torture his mother Sumayyah, who was a freedwoman of Abu Jahl. He said to her one day, I only believed in Muhammad because you love him for his beauty. Then he stabbed her in the vagina with a spear and she died. She is the first martyr to die in Islam. May God have mercy on her. From the book Al-Naqqash and others. This will be explained in the verse of compulsion, God willing. Ata’ al-Abkam Abi bin Khalaf said: He did not speak good. And he is a burden on his master meaning his people because Uthman bin Maz’un used to harm them. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Hisham bin Amr bin al-Harith, he was an unbeliever, did little good, and was hostile to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that the unbeliever is the mute and the one who commands justice is the believer as a whole. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is good because it is general. The mute is the one who does not speak. It was said: the one who does not reason. It was said: the one who neither hears nor sees. In the interpretation: The mute here is the idol, indicating that he has no power or command, and that someone else moves it and carves it, so it is a burden on him. God is the one who commands justice, the victor over all things. It was said that the meaning is: he is a burden on his master, meaning a burden on his guardian and relatives, and a burden on his companion and cousin. The orphan may also be called a burden because he is a burden on the one who takes care of him. From the saying of the poet: I eat everyone's money before my youth if my bones are not strong And the whole is also the one who has no son or father, and the whole is the dependents and the plural is the kulul, it is said from it: the whole knife is yakul kala, meaning its blade became thick so it did not cut. Wherever he directs it, it does not bring good. The majority read it, yajhuhu, which is the line of the Qur’an, meaning wherever its owner sends it, it does not bring good because it does not know or understand what is said to it, nor does it understand about it. Yahya bin Waththab read wherever it is directed as a passive verb, and it was also narrated from Ibn Masoud that it is directed as a direct address. Is he equal to one who commands justice and is on a straight path? That is, is this mute equal to one who commands justice on the straight path? God Almighty says: The Day they emerge from the graves quickly, as if they were, toward an idol, hastening. A day instead of their day before it, and the general reading is yukhrujuun with a fatha on the ya and a damma on the ra as the named agent. As-Salami, Al-Mughirah and Al-A'sha from Asim read yukhrujuun with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the ra as a passive verb. Al-Ajdath: graves, the singular is jadth. It has been mentioned in Surah Yasin. Sira'an when they hear the final shout to answer the caller, and it is an accusative of state. As if they were to a target they hasten is the general reading with a fatha on the noon and a jazm on the sad. Ibn Amir and Hafs read with a damma on the noon and the sad. Amr ibn Maymun, Abu Raja and others read with a damma on the noon and a sukoon on the sad. Nasb and nasb are two languages like weakness and weakness. Al-Jawhari: Nasb is what is placed in the accusative case and is worshipped instead of God, and likewise nasb with a damma, and it may be moved. Al-A'sha said: And do not place that which is placed in the accusative case for well-being, and God is your Lord, so worship He wanted to worship you, so he stopped with the alif, as you say: I saw Zayd. The plural is ansaab. And his saying: and this monument means beware of this monument. Monsoon is evil and affliction, and from it is the saying of God the Almighty: {Indeed, Satan has touched me with hardship and torment} (Surah Sad: 41). Al-Akhfash and Al-Farraa said: Monsoon is the plural of monument like rahn and rahn, and monuments are the plural of monument, so it is the plural of plural. It was also said: Monsoon and monuments are one and the same. It was also said: Monsoon is the plural of nisab, which is a stone or an idol that is sacrificed to, and from it is the saying of God the Almighty: {And that which is sacrificed on stone altars} (Surah al-Ma’idah 5:3). It was also said: Monsoon, Monsoon, and Monsoon have one meaning, as it was said Umar, Umar, and Umar. An-Nahhas mentioned that Ibn Abbas said: To a monument, to a goal, which is that which you direct your sight to. Al-Kabi said: To something erected, a flag or a banner.
