Al-Hasan said: When the sun rose, they would rush to their monuments that they worshipped instead of God, the first of them not turning back from the last of them. They hasten means they hurry. And ifad means to hasten. The poet said: The knights of Dhibyan are under the iron, like jinn, they are overwhelmed by genius. Abqar: a place that the Arabs claim is the land of the jinn. Labid said: Old men and young men like the paradise of Abqar. Al-Layth said: The camels rushed, and their owner made them hurry. Ifad is transitive, while ifad in the verse is intransitive. It is said: Fadda, “afada,” and istawfad meaning to hurry.
16:77: The Almighty's saying, And to God belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Its meaning was presented. This is connected to His saying, Indeed, God knows, while you do not know. That is, the legislation of what is lawful and what is forbidden is only appropriate for those who are aware of the consequences of their interests, and you, O polytheists, do not understand them, so why do you have control? And the matter of the Hour is not but as the blink of an eye. And you will exceed it with your deeds. The Hour is the time in which the Resurrection will occur. It was called an hour because it will surprise people in an hour, and the creation will die with a shout. A blink of an eye means quickly. It is said that he glanced at it quickly and glanced at it. The point of interpretation is that since the Hour was bound to come, it was made close like the blink of an eye. Al-Zajjaj said, He did not mean that the Hour will come in the blink of an eye, but rather he described the speed of the ability to bring it about, that is, He says to the thing, Be," and it is. It was said that it was used as an example of the blink of an eye because it will catch sight of the sky despite its distance from the earth. It was said that it is a representation of closeness, as the speaker says: A year is only a moment and the like. It was said: The meaning is with God as well, not with the one being addressed. It was said: Or it is in the position of Indeed, God is capable of all things as mentioned above.
16:78: The Almighty said, And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers not knowing a thing. He mentioned that among His blessings is that He brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers as children, having no knowledge of anything. There are three sayings about this: The first is that you do not know anything of what He took from you as a covenant in the loins of your fathers. The second: You do not know anything of what He decreed for you of happiness and misery. The third: You do not know anything of your benefits. The speech was completed, then He began by saying, And He gave you hearing, sight, and hearts, meaning that with which you know and perceive, because God gave that to His servants before bringing them forth from the wombs, and He only gave them that after He brought them forth, meaning, He gave you hearing so that you would hear the commands and prohibitions, and sight so that you would see the effects of His creation, and hearts so that you would reach His knowledge. Hearts is the plural of fu'ad, like ghurab and aghrabah. It has been said that within His statement, And He gave you hearing, is the confirmation of speech, because whoever does not hear does not speak, and if the sense of hearing is found, speech is found. Al-A'mash ibn Thabit and Hamza read ummahatukum here and in An-Nur, Az-Zumar and An-Najm with a kasra on the hamza and the meem. As for Al-Kisa'i, he broke the hamza and opened the meem. This was only to follow the rest with a damma on the hamza and a fatha on the meem according to the original. The original form of ummahat is ummat, so the ha' was added for emphasis, just as they added the ha' in ahraqat al-ma', the original form of which is arqat. This meaning was mentioned previously in Al-Fatihah, so that you may be grateful. There are two interpretations of it. One of them is that you are grateful for His blessings. The second means that you see the effects of His creation, because seeing them leads to gratitude.
16:79: The Almighty said: Have they not seen the birds controlled in the atmosphere of the sky? None holds them up except God. Yahya bin Wathab, Al-A'mash, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Yaqub read tarawa with a ta' as an address, Abu Ubaid chose it. The rest read it with a ya' as a report. Subjected is subjected to the command of God Almighty. Al-Kalbi said it. It was also said: Subjected and subjected for your benefits. In the atmosphere of the sky the atmosphere is what is between the sky and the earth. He added the atmosphere to the sky because of its height above the earth. And in His saying subjected is evidence of a subject who subjected them and a manager who enabled them to act. None holds them up except God in the case of contraction, expansion, and alignment. He explained to them how they should consider them in His Oneness. Indeed in that are signs meaning signs, lessons, and indications for a people who believe in God and in what His messengers brought.
16:80: It contains ten issues: The first is the saying of the Most High, He made for you meaning a place. And everything that is above you and shades you is a roof and sky, and everything that carries you is earth, and everything that covers you from your four sides is a wall, and when they are arranged and connected, it is a house. This verse contains an enumeration of the blessings of God Almighty upon people in the houses. He first mentioned the houses of cities, which are for long-term residence. And His saying, dwelling means that you dwell in them and your limbs rest from movement. And you may move in it and rest in another place, except that the saying came out on the most common. And He counted this among the blessings, for if He had willed, He created the servant forever in a state of turmoil like the heavens, that would have been as He created and willed. And if He had created him still like the earth, it would have been as He created and willed. But He created him as a creation that can act in two ways, and his state differs between the two states, and He repeated how and where, and dwelling is a source that describes the singular and the plural. Then the Most High mentioned the houses of movement and travel, which are: The second: He said, And He has made for you from the hides of cattle, houses which you find light, meaning from the carpets and leather. Houses, meaning the tents and domes that are easy for you to carry on your journeys. On the day of your departure, departure is the travel of the desert in the migration and movement from one place to another. From this is the saying of Antarah: The departure of those whose separation I expect, and the speckled crow ran among them, and the departure also included the litter. He said: Do the caravans trouble you when they depart and when the crows come forth at the onset of separation? It was read with a sukoon on the ‘ayn and a fatha on it, like hair and hair. It was said that it may include houses made of leather, houses made of hair, and houses made of wool, because these are made of skins due to their being fixed in them. Ibn Salam tended towards that, and it is a good possibility. His saying, and from their wool, is the beginning of a statement, as if he said, made furniture, meaning clothing, bedding, and other things. The poet said: The caravans provoked you when they appeared in this beautiful outfit of furniture. It is possible that what he meant by his saying from the skins of cattle is only the houses of leather, as we mentioned first, and his saying and from their descriptions is in apposition to his saying from the skins of cattle, meaning that they also made houses. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is something that was widespread in those lands, but our country was far from it, so tents are not pitched here except from linen and wool. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had a tent made of leather, and the leather of Taif is very expensive, sophisticated in craftsmanship, and beautiful in complexion. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not consider it a luxury nor did he see it as extravagance, because it is one of the blessings that God, the Most High, has bestowed upon us and permitted in His pleasures. Its benefits are evident in the shelter and shade that the human race cannot escape. One of the strange things that happened is that I visited some of the ascetics among the heedless, with some of the hadith scholars. We entered upon him in a linen tent, and my companion, the hadith scholar, offered to carry him to his home as a guest, and he said, This is a place where the heat is abundant, and the house is more comfortable for you and more pleasant for me in you. He said, This tent is plentiful for us, and in our making it was insignificant. I said, “It is not as you claim. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who was the leader of the ascetics, had a tent made of leather from Taif, which he would travel with and seek shade under.” I was astonished and saw it in a state of shame, so I left it with my companion and left him. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And from their wool, their fur, and their hair. God, the Exalted, permitted the use of sheep’s wool, camel’s hair, and goat’s hair, as He permitted the greatest of them, which is slaughtering them and eating their meat. He did not mention cotton and flax because they were not found in the lands of the Arabs addressed by it. Rather, He enumerated for them the blessings He bestowed upon them, and they were addressed in what they knew and understood. Whatever takes the place of these and takes their place is included in the usage and blessing as its entrance. This is like the Almighty’s saying: And He sends down from the sky, from mountains, hail. So He addressed them with hail because they knew that it descended frequently among them, and He was silent about mentioning snow because it was not found in their lands, and it is similar to it in description and benefit. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned them together in purification, saying: O God, wash me with water, snow, and hail. Ibn Abbas said: Snow is a white thing that descends from the sky, and I have never seen it. It was said that the omission of mentioning cotton and flax was only to avoid luxury, since the clothing of God’s righteous servants is wool. This is questionable, for He, the Almighty, says: O children of Adam, We have bestowed upon you clothing to conceal your private parts, as was explained previously in Al-A’raf. And He said here, And He made for you garments, so He referred to cotton and linen in the word garments, and God knows best. And furniture, Al-Khalil said, means goods joined together from furniture, since he said more: And the empty, jet-black, decorated body is as thick as the trunk of a palm tree. Ibn Abbas: Furniture, clothes, and it has been mentioned before. This verse includes the permissibility of benefiting from wool, fur, and hair in all cases. Therefore, our companions said: The wool and hair of a dead animal is pure and it is permissible to benefit from it in all cases, and it is washed for fear that dirt may have stuck to it. Likewise, Umm Salamah narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: There is nothing wrong with the skin of a dead animal if it is tanned, and its wool and hair if it is washed, because death does not make it permissible. Whether it is the hair of an animal whose meat is eaten or not, such as the hair of a human being or a pig, it is all pure. Abu Hanifa said the same, but he added to us and said: The horn, tooth, and bone are like hair. He said that because none of these things have a soul, they do not become impure with the death of the animal. Al-Hasan al-Basri, al-Layth ibn Sa`d, and al-Awza`i said that all hair is impure, but it is purified by washing. There are three narrations from al-Shafi`i: The first is that it is pure and does not become impure with death. The second is that it is impure. The third is the difference between the hair of the son of Adam and others. The hair of the son of Adam is pure and what is other than it is impure. Our evidence is the generality of the words of God Almighty: And from their wool Al-Ma’idah 2:17. So He bestowed His favor upon us by making it possible for us to benefit from it and did not specify the hair of the dead from the slaughtered, so it is a generality unless there is evidence to prevent it. Also, the basic principle is that it is pure before death by consensus, so whoever claims that it has changed to impurity must provide evidence. If it is said that His words Forbidden to you are dead animals are an expression of the sentence, we say that we specify it with what we have mentioned, because it is explicitly stated in mentioning wool and your verse does not mention it explicitly, so our evidence is more appropriate. And God knows best. Sheikh Imam Abu Ishaq, the Imam of the Shafi’is in Baghdad, relied on the fact that hair is a part connected to the animal by creation, so it grows with its growth and becomes impure with its death like all other parts. It was answered that growth is not evidence of life because plants grow and are not alive. If they relied on the continuous growth of what is on the animal, we relied on the clarity that indicates the lack of sensation, which indicates the lack of life. As for what the Hanafis mentioned about the bone, tooth, and horn being like hair, what is well-known among us is that that is impure like meat. Ibn Wahb said something similar to what Abu Hanifa said, and we have a third opinion: Are the ends of the horns and hooves attached to their roots or to the hair? There are two opinions. Likewise, the hairy part of the feathers is ruled by the same rule as the hair, and the bone part of it is ruled by the same rule. Our evidence is the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not benefit from anything that is dead. This is general in it and in every part of it except for what is proven by evidence. Among the conclusive evidence for that is the statement of God Almighty: “He said: Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed?” And God Almighty said: And look at the bones, how We raise them up? And He said: Then We covered the bones with flesh. And He said: Will we then be rotten bones? So the origin is the bones, and the soul and life are in them as in the flesh and skin. And in the hadith of Abdullah bin Ukaim: Do not benefit from the skin or sinews of the dead. If it is said: It has been proven in the Sahih that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the sheep of Maymunah: Why did you not benefit from its skin? They said: O Messenger of God, it is dead. He said: It is only forbidden to eat it. And the bone is not eaten. We say: The bone is eaten, especially the bone of a suckling camel, a kid, and a bird. The bone of an adult is roasted. It is eaten, and what we mentioned before indicates the presence of life in it. What was pure with life and permissible with slaughter becomes impure with death. And God knows best. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying, From the hides of livestock, is general in meaning the hides of living and dead animals, so it is permissible to benefit from the hides of dead animals even if they are not tanned. This is what Ibn Shihab, Al-Zuhri, and Al-Layth Ibn Saad said. Al-Tahawi said: We did not find any of the jurists, the imams of fatwas in the countries after the followers. As for Ibn Shihab, this is correct from him, and it is the saying of his father, the majority of the people of knowledge. It has been narrated from them that this opinion is different from this opinion, but the first is more famous. I said: Al-Darqutni mentioned in his Sunan the hadith of Yahya bin Ayoub on the authority of Yunus and Aqil on the authority of Al-Zuhri, the hadith of Baqiyah on the authority of Al-Zubaidi, the hadith of Muhammad bin Katheer Al-Abdi and Abu Salamah Al-Manqari on the authority of Sulayman bin Katheer on the authority of Al-Zuhri, and he said at the end of them: These are authentic chains of transmission. Sixth: The scholars differed on whether the hide of a dead animal is purified or not if it is tanned. Ibn Abd al-Hakam mentioned something similar to the view of Ibn Shihab on this, and Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad mentioned it in his book on the authority of Ibn Abd al-Hakam as well: Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said, and it is the view of al-Zuhri and al-Layth. He said: The apparent view of Malik is what Ibn Abd al-Hakam mentioned, which is that tanning does not purify the hide of a dead animal, but it is permissible to benefit from it in dry things, and one should not pray on it or eat from it. In al-Mudawwana by Ibn al-Qasim, whoever usurps the hide of a dead animal that has not been tanned and destroys it, then he must pay its value. He narrated that this was the view of Malik. Abu al-Faraj mentioned that Malik said, whoever usurps the hide of a dead animal that has not been tanned, then there is nothing on him. Ismail said, unless it belongs to a Zoroastrian. Ibn Wahb and Ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated on the authority of Malik that it is permissible to sell it. This applies to the hide of any dead animal except the pig alone, because zakat is not applied to it, so tanning is more appropriate. Abu Umar said: It is permissible to use any skin that is considered smart for ablution and other purposes. Malik disliked performing ablution in a vessel made of dead animal hide after tanning, according to a difference of opinion. Once he said that he disliked it only for himself, and he disliked praying over it and selling it. A group of his companions followed him in this. As for most of the people of Medina, they were on the permissibility and approval of this, based on the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Any hide that is tanned has become pure. This is what most of the people of Hijaz and Iraq, from the people of jurisprudence and hadith, agreed upon. It is the choice of Ibn Wahb. Seventh: Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, may God be pleased with him, said that it is not permissible to benefit from the hides of dead animals in any way, even if they are tanned, because they are like the meat of dead animals. And the report about benefiting after tanning refutes his statement and he provided evidence with “the hadith of Abdullah bin Ukaim - narrated by Abu Dawud who said: The letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was read to us in the land of Juhayna and I was a young boy: Do not benefit from the dead animal with its hide or sinews.” And “In another narration: A month before his death.” It was narrated by Al-Qasim bin Mukhaymara on the authority of Abdullah bin Ukaim who said: Our sheikhs told us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to them. Dawud bin Ali said: I asked Yahya bin Ma’in about this hadith and he weakened it and said: It is nothing. He only says: The sheikhs told me. Abu Omar said: If it were proven, it would be possible that it contradicts the hadiths narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Aisha, Salamah bin Al-Muhabbak and others, because it is possible that the meaning of the hadith of Ibn Ukaim is: Do not benefit from the dead animal with its hide before tanning. If it is possible that it does not contradict, then we do not have the right to make it contradictory, and we must use the two reports as much as possible. And the hadith of Abdullah bin Ukaim, even if it was a month before the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as came in the report, it is possible. That the story of Maymunah and Ibn Abbas hearing from him: Any hide that is tanned is purified was a week or less before his death, and God knows best. Eighth: It is well-known among us that pig skin is not included in the hadith and is not included in the generality. Likewise, according to al-Shafi’i, al-Awza’i and Abu Thawr, the dog is not purified by tanning except the skin of an animal whose meat is eaten. Ma’n ibn ‘Isa narrated on the authority of Malik that he was asked about pig skin if it is tanned and he disliked it. Ibn Wadah said: I heard Sahnun say that there is nothing wrong with it. Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Hakam, Dawud ibn ‘Ali and his companions also said this, based on the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): Anything that has been tanned has become pure. Abu ‘Umar said: It is possible that he meant by this saying all skins that are commonly used for benefit. As for the pig, it is not included in the meaning because its skin is not commonly used for benefit, as slaughtering is not done on it. Another proof is what al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: The hide is the skin of cows and camels and other than that, it is only called hide, not hide. I said: The skin of a dog and the meat of an animal whose meat is not eaten are also not commonly used for benefit, so they are not purified. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Eating any fanged beast of prey is forbidden. So there is no slaughtering of it, just as there is no slaughtering of a pig. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Al-Miqdam bin Ma’dikarib, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade silk, gold, and tiger skins. Ninth: The jurists differed regarding the tanning that purifies the hides of dead animals. What is it? The companions of Malik, and this is the well-known view of his school of thought, said: Everything that tans the hide with, whether salt, qaraz, alum, or other than that, is permissible to benefit from. Abu Hanifa and his companions said the same, and it is the view of Dawud. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions on this issue: One of them is this, and the other is that it is not purified except with alum and qaraz because it is the known tanning method during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Khattabi concluded, and God knows best, what Al-Nasa’i narrated: “On the authority of Maymunah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that some men from Quraysh passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, dragging a sheep of theirs that was like a horse. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Why don’t you take its hide? They said: It is dead. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Water and qaraz purify it.” Tenth: The Almighty’s saying, furniture. Furnishings are the household goods, the singular of which is athathu. This is the saying of Abu Zayd al-Ansari. Al-Umawi said that furnishings are the household goods, the plural of which is athath and athath. Others said that furnishings are all types of money, and it does not have a singular form from the same word. Al-Khalil said that its origin is from abundance and the gathering of some goods together until they become numerous, and from this comes the poetry of athith, meaning many. And ath, the poetry of so-and-so, yaathath athath, if it is abundant and intertwined. Imru’ al-Qais said: A branch adorns the back, jet black, thick as the trunk of a palm tree. It was said: Furniture is what is worn and spread out. It was furnished if you made furniture. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, furniture is money. The statement about the time was presented, and here it is an unspecified time according to each person, either by his death or by the loss of those things that are furniture. From this word is the saying of the poet: The caravans provoked you when they appeared in this beautiful outfit of furniture.
16:81: It has six issues: The first is the Almighty’s saying, shades. Shades are everything that one finds shade under, such as houses and trees. His saying, of what He created, includes all people who are shaded. The second: The Almighty’s saying, Aknanan Aknan is the plural of Kun, which is the protector from rain, wind, and other things. Here, they are the caves in the mountains that God made a provision for the Creator to take refuge in, fortify themselves in, and isolate themselves from creation in them. “In the Sahih, it is said that at the beginning of his life, peace be upon him, he used to worship in the cave of Hira and stay in it for nights.” The hadith. In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left Mecca as an emigrant, fleeing from his people, fleeing for his religion with his companion Abu Bakr, until they reached a cave in Mount Thawr. They hid in it for three nights. Abdullah ibn Abu Bakr, a young, cultured boy who had been taught, would spend the night with them there. He would leave them at dawn and would become with the Quraysh in Mecca as if he had spent the night. He would not hear of anything they were about to do without remembering it until he came to them with report of that when darkness fell and Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Abu Bakr’s freed slave, would graze a gift of sheep over them, and he would let them rest for them when an hour of the evening had passed. They would spend the night in Rasul, which was the milk of their gift and their food, until Amir ibn Fahira Baghalas does this every night of those three nights. He mentioned the hadith. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it. Third: The Almighty’s saying, “And He has made for you garments to protect you from the heat,” meaning the shirt, the singular of which is sirbal, and garments to protect you from your violence, meaning the armor that protects people in war. From this is the saying of Ka’b ibn Zuhair: The smell of the lions is the heroes, their clothing is woven by David in the battle, their garments are garments. Fourth: If someone says: How did He say And He has made for you shelters in the mountains and not mention the plains, and He said to protect you from the heat and not mention the cold? The answer is that the people were people of mountains and not people of plains, and they were people of heat and not people of cold, so He mentioned to them His blessings that are specific to them, just as He mentioned wool and other things, and He did not mention cotton, linen, or snow, as mentioned above, because it was not in their country. This meaning was said by Ata’ al-Khurasani and others. Also, mentioning one of them indicates the other, and from this is the saying of the poet: I do not know if I go to a land seeking good, which of the two is more suitable for me Is it the good that I seek or the evil that seeks me? Fifth: The scholars said regarding the Almighty’s statement, And garments to protect you from your violence, this is evidence that servants should take up the equipment of jihad to help them fight their enemies. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wore it to protect against injury, even though he was seeking martyrdom. It is not for the servant to seek it by submitting to death, stabbing with spears, or striking with swords. Rather, he wears it for the sake of war, so that he has the strength to fight his enemy, and he fights so that the word of God is supreme, and God does what He wills. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Thus He will perfect His favor upon you that you may submit. Ibn Muhaisin and Hamid read it is perfected with two ta’s of His favor, in the nominative case, as if it were the subject. The rest read it with a damma on the ya’, as if God is the one who will perfect it. And you submit, according to the reading of Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah, you submit with a fatha on the ta’ and the lam, meaning you are safe from wounds. Its chain of transmission is weak. It was narrated by Ibad ibn al-Awwam on the authority of Hanzala on the authority of Shahr on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The rest read it with a damma on the ta’, and its meaning is you submit and obey God and obey Him in gratitude for His favors. Abu Ubaid said: The preferred reading of the majority is because what God has bestowed upon us of Islam is better than what He has bestowed of safety from wounds.
16:82: The Almighty says, But if they turn away, meaning they turn away from looking, reasoning, and believing, then upon you is only the notification, meaning that upon you is only the notification, and as for guidance, that is up to Us.
16:83: The Almighty said, They know the favor of God Al-Suddi said, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, that is, they know his prophethood, then they deny it and call him a liar. Mujahid said, "He means what God enumerated for them in this Surah of favors, that is, they know that it is from God and they deny it by saying that they inherited it from their fathers, and Qatada said something similar. Awn ibn Abdullah said, "It is a man saying, 'If it were not for so-and-so, such-and-such would have happened, and if it were not for so-and-so, I would not have attained such-and-such.'" And they know that benefit and harm are from God. Al-Kalbi said, "It is that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them of all of these favors, they recognized them and said, 'Yes, they are all favors from God, but they are through the intercession of our gods.' And it was said, They know the favor of God by their turning to it and they deny it by not being grateful for it." And a sixth possibility is that they know it in times of hardship and deny it in times of ease. Seventhly, it is possible that they know it through their words and deny it through their actions. Eighthly, it is possible that they know it in their hearts and deny it with their tongues, similar to and they denied it, although their souls were certain of it “and most of them are disbelievers” meaning all of them, as mentioned above.
16:84: The Almighty’s saying, And the Day We shall raise up from every nation a witness, is similar to how [will it be] when We bring from every nation a witness, and it has already been mentioned, Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved, meaning in apologizing and speaking like His saying, And permission will not be given to them to apologize, and that is when Hell closes in on them as mentioned in the beginning of Al-Hijr. And it will come, nor will they be asked to repent, meaning they will not be asked to please their Lord, because the Hereafter is not a place of obligation, and they will not be left until the return of this world to repent. The root of the word is from reproach, which is grieving. It is said, He reproached him, if he finds fault with him. So if he negotiates with him about what he was reproached for, it is said, He reproached him. So if he returns to your satisfaction, then he has repented. The noun is reproach, and it is the return of the reproached to what pleases the reproacher. Al-Harawi said, and Al-Nabigha said: If you are wronged, then you are a slave whom you have wronged. If you are someone who can complain, then someone like you can complain.
16:85: God Almighty says: And when those who did wrong see the punishment, meaning the punishment of Hell by entering it, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved, meaning they will not be given respite, as there is no repentance for them. Then...
16:86: The Almighty said, And when those who associate others with God see their partners, meaning their idols and statues that they worshipped, and that is because God will resurrect their worshipped ones and they will follow them until they lead them to the Fire. In Sahih Muslim: "Whoever worships something, let him follow it. So whoever worships the sun will follow the sun, and whoever worships the moon will follow the moon, and whoever worships false gods will follow the false gods." The hadith was narrated by Anas and Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, and in it: So the one with the cross will have his cross, and the one with the pictures will have his pictures, and the one with the fire will have his fire, and they will follow what they used to worship. And he mentioned the hadith. They will say, 'Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to call upon besides You.' So they will cast down to them the word, 'Indeed, you are liars.' That is, the gods will cast down to them the word, meaning they will speak in denial of those who worshipped them, that they were not gods and did not command them to worship them, so God will make the idols speak until the disgrace of the disbelievers becomes apparent. It was said: What is meant by that are the angels whom they worshipped.
16:87: And they will submit to God on that Day in submission meaning the polytheists, meaning they will surrender to His punishment and submit to His might. It was also said that the worshipper and the worshipped will surrender and submit to His judgment over them. And what they used to invent will be lost to them meaning that what Satan made attractive to them and what they hoped for from the intercession of their gods will be removed from them.
16:88: The Almighty said: Those who disbelieved and averted from the way of God - We will increase for them punishment over the punishment. Ibn Mas'ud said: Scorpions with fangs like tall palm trees, and snakes like the necks of camels, and vipers like the humpbacked ones that strike them, and that is the increase. It was said that the meaning is that they will emerge from the Fire into the freezing cold, and they will rush to the Fire because of its intense cold. It was also said that the meaning is that We will increase the leaders in punishment over the lowly, so one of the two punishments is for their disbelief and the other punishment is for their aversion because of what they used to cause corruption in this world through disbelief and disobedience.
16:89: The Almighty says: And the Day We will raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves. They are the prophets, witnesses over their nation on the Day of Resurrection, because they conveyed the message and called them to faith. In every era there is a witness, even if he is not a prophet. There are two opinions about them: one of them is that they are the imams of guidance who are the successors of the prophets. The second is that they are the scholars through whom God preserved the laws of His prophets. I said: So, based on this, there was no period in which there were not those who believed in the oneness of God, such as Quss bin Sa’idah, Zayd bin Amr bin Nufayl, about whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He will be sent as a nation by himself, Satih, and Waraqa bin Nawfal, about whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw him immersing himself in the rivers of Paradise. These and those like them are an argument against the people of their time and a witness against them. And God knows best. His statement: And We have brought you as a witness against these people was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah and An-Nisa. The Almighty’s saying: And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things. Similar to it is: We have neglected nothing in the Book. It has already been mentioned, so let us look there. Mujahid said: As clarification for what is permissible and what is forbidden.
16:90: It has six issues: The first is the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, God commands justice and doing good. It was narrated on the authority of Uthman bin Maz’un that he said: When this verse was revealed, I recited it to Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and he was amazed and said: O family of Ghalib, follow him and you will be successful, for by God, God sent him to command you to have good morals. And in a hadith, when Abu Talib was told: Your nephew claims that God revealed to him Indeed, God commands justice and doing good, the verse, he said: Follow my nephew, for by God, he only commands good morals. And Ikrimah said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira: Indeed, God commands justice and doing good, to the end of it, and he said: O my nephew, repeat it? So he repeated it to him, and he said: By God, it has sweetness and freshness, and its root is lush and its top is fruitful, and it is not the speech of a human being. And Al-Ghaznawi mentioned that Uthman bin Maz’un was the reciter. Uthman said: “I did not initially convert to Islam except out of shyness before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until this verse was revealed while I was with him, and faith settled in my heart. I recited it to Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, and he said: O son of my brother, repeat it. So I repeated it, and he said: By God, it has a sweetness.” And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Ibn Masoud said: This is the most comprehensive verse in the Qur’an for the good that is done and the evil that is avoided. Al-Naqqash narrated that it is said: The zakat of justice is benevolence, the zakat of power is forgiveness, the zakat of wealth is good reputation, and the zakat of prestige is a man’s writing to his brothers. Second: Scholars differed in the interpretation of justice and benevolence. Ibn Abbas said: Justice is there is no god but God, and benevolence is performing the obligatory duties. It was also said: Justice is the obligatory duty and benevolence is the voluntary duty. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Justice here is the equality of the inner self and benevolence, that the inner self is better than the outward self. Ali ibn Abi Talib: Justice is fairness and benevolence is generosity. Ibn Atiyyah said: Justice is everything that is obligatory from beliefs and laws in fulfilling trusts, leaving injustice, fairness, and giving rights. And benevolence is doing everything that is recommended. Some things are all recommended and some are obligatory, except that the limit of its sufficiency is included in justice, and the completion that exceeds the sufficiency is included in benevolence. As for the statement of Ibn Abbas, there is a consideration in it because performing the obligatory duties is Islam as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) explained in the hadith of Gabriel’s question, and that is justice. Rather, doing good is the completion and what is recommended is according to what is required by the explanation of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in the hadith of Gabriel’s question, saying, Worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you. If this is authentic from Ibn Abbas, then he only meant the obligatory duties as completion. Ibn Al-Arabi said, Justice between the servant and his Lord is preferring His right over his own self, giving priority to His pleasure over his own desires, avoiding deterrents, and obeying commands. As for justice between him and himself, it is preventing himself from that which leads to his destruction. God the Almighty said, And he forbade the soul from desire, and refraining from following desires and adhering to contentment in every situation and meaning. As for justice between him and people, it means offering sincere advice and avoiding betrayal in both small and large matters, and being fair to them in every way, and not harming anyone in word or deed, neither in secret nor in public, and being patient with whatever calamity befalls you from them, and the least of that is fairness and avoiding harm. I said: This detail in justice is good and just. As for ihsan, our scholars said: ihsan is the source of ahsan, yahsanan, and it is said in two meanings: one of them is transitive by itself, like you say: I did well in such-and-such, meaning I made it good and completed it, and it is transferred with the hamza from hasan al-shay’. The second is transitive with a preposition, like you say: I did well to so-and-so, meaning I conveyed to him what he would benefit from. I said: In this verse, both meanings are intended together, for the Almighty loves from His creation the kindness of some to others, even the bird in your prison and the cat in your house, you should not fail to care for them with your kindness, and the Almighty is independent of their kindness, and from Him come kindness, blessings, favors, and favors. It is in the hadith of Gabriel in the first meaning, not the second, for the first meaning refers to the perfection of worship and its observance by performing it in a correct and perfect manner, and observing the Truth in it, and being mindful of His greatness and majesty in the state of beginning and the state of continuing, and this is what is meant by His saying that you worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you. And the masters of hearts in this observance are in two states: One of them is dominated by the sight of the Truth, so it is as if He sees Him, and perhaps the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, referred to this state in his saying: And the delight of my eyes was made in prayer. And the second does not end with this, but it is dominated by the fact that the Truth, glory be to Him, is watching it and observing it, and this is referred to in His saying, the Most High: Who sees you when you stand up * And your turning among those who prostrate and His saying: Except that We were witnesses over you when you depart therein Third: The Almighty’s statement, And give to the kindred, meaning the kinship. He says: He gives them money, as He said, And give to the kindred his due, meaning maintaining ties with them. This is a case of connecting the recommended with the obligatory, and Al-Shafi’i used it as evidence in obligating giving to the freed slave, as will be explained later. He only specified the kindred because their rights are more important and maintaining ties with them is more obligatory, to emphasize the right of the womb from which God derived its name and made maintaining ties with Him a part of maintaining ties with Him. So “He said in the Sahih: Are you not pleased that I maintain ties with those who maintain ties with you and sever ties with those who sever ties with you?” Especially if they are poor. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And He forbids immorality, wrongdoing, and rebellion. Immorality is every ugly thing in speech or action. Ibn Abbas said: It is adultery. And wrongdoing is what the Shari’ah has forbidden, and it includes all sins, vices, and baseness of all kinds. It was said that it is polytheism. And rebellion is arrogance, injustice, hatred, and transgression. Its reality is exceeding the limit, and it is included under wrongdoing, but the Almighty mentioned it specifically out of concern for it due to its severe harm. In the hadith: “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: There is no sin more swiftly punished than rebellion.” And he, peace be upon him, said: The rebel is defeated. And God has granted victory to the one who is rebelled against. And in some of the revealed books: If a mountain were to rebel against a mountain, He would make the rebel of them both crumble. Fifth: Imam Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Bukhari translated in his Sahih and said: Chapter on the statement of God the Most High: “Indeed, God commands justice and the doing of good and liberality to kith and kin and forbids immorality and wrongdoing and oppression. He admonishes you that you may be reminded.” And His statement: Your oppression is only against yourselves. “Then he oppressed him, God will surely aid him.” And refraining from stirring up evil against a Muslim or a disbeliever. Then he mentioned the hadith of Aisha about Labid bin Al-A’sam bewitching the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Battaal said: So he, may God be pleased with him, interpreted these verses as refraining from stirring up evil against a Muslim or a disbeliever, as indicated by the hadith of Aisha where he, peace be upon him, said: As for God, He has healed me, but as for me, I hate to stir up evil against the people. The reason for that, and God knows best, is that he interpreted the statement of God the Most High: Indeed, God commands justice and the doing of good as an exhortation to be kind to the wrongdoer and refrain from punishing him for his wrongdoing. If it is said: How is this interpretation correct in the verses about oppression? It was said that the reason for that, and God knows best, is that when God informed His servants that the harm of oppression is directed at the oppressor by His saying, Your oppression is only against yourselves, and the Almighty guaranteed victory for the oppressed, it was more appropriate for the oppressed to thank God for what He guaranteed of victory and to respond to that by forgiving the oppressed. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did the same with the Jew who had bewitched him, and he had the right to take revenge on him by His saying, And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted, but he preferred forgiveness, taking into account His saying, And whoever is patient and forgives - indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination. Sixth: This verse includes enjoining good and forbidding evil, and we have already discussed them. It was narrated that a group of people brought their agent to Abu Ja`far al-Mansur al-`Abbasi, so the agent argued with them and defeated them, saying that they had not proven against him any great injustice or oppression in anything. Then a young man from the people stood up and said: O Commander of the Faithful, God commands justice and benevolence, and He has been just and has not been benevolent. Abu Ja`far was amazed at his accuracy and dismissed the agent.
16:91: There are three issues: The first is the statement of God the Almighty: And fulfill the covenant of God which is a general term for everything that is concluded with the tongue and that a person commits to, such as a sale, a relationship, or a covenant in a matter that is in accordance with his religion. This verse is included in the statement: Indeed, God commands justice and doing good because the meaning is: Do such-and-such and refrain from such-and-such, so it was connected to that estimate. It was said that it was revealed regarding the pledge of allegiance of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Islam. It was also said: It was revealed regarding the commitment to the oath that was in the pre-Islamic era, and Islam came to fulfill it. This was said by Qatada, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd, and the general term includes all of that as we have explained. Sahih narrated on the authority of Jubayr ibn Mut’im who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no oath in Islam, and whatever oath was in the pre-Islamic era, Islam only increases its strength, meaning in supporting the truth, upholding it, and providing assistance. This is similar to the Hilf al-Fudul mentioned by Ibn Ishaq. He said: The tribes of Quraysh gathered in the house of Abdullah bin Jud’an because of his honor and lineage, so they made a contract and pledged that they would not find anyone in Mecca who had been wronged, whether from its people or others, except that they would stand with him until his grievance was redressed. So the Quraysh called that alliance the Hilf al-Fudul, meaning the alliance of virtues. Here, Fudul is the plural of fadl for abundance, like fals and fulus. Ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I witnessed an alliance in the house of Abdullah bin Jud’an that I would not have loved to have red camels for, if it were called upon in Islam, I would have responded.” Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Walid bin Utbah attacked Hussein bin Ali over his money, due to the authority of Al-Walid, for he was the emir of Medina. Hussein bin Ali said to him: I swear by God that you will do me justice in my right, or I will take my sword and stand in the mosque of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then call for the Hilf al-Fudul. Abdullah bin al-Zubayr said: And I swear by God that if he calls upon us, I will take my sword and then…” I will stand with him until he gets his rights, or we will all die. This report reached Al-Miswar bin Makhramah, and he said the same. This report reached Abd al-Rahman bin Uthman bin Ubayd God al-Taimi, and he said the same. When this report reached Al-Walid, he vindicated him. Scholars said that this oath that was in the pre-Islamic era is what Islam strengthened and the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, singled it out from the generality of his statement, There is no oath in Islam. The wisdom behind that is that the Shari’ah came with the support of taking revenge on the oppressor, taking the right from him, and delivering it to the oppressed. It made that obligatory in the Shari’ah as a general obligation on whoever is able from those who are accountable, and gave them the way against the oppressors. God Almighty said, “The way is only against those who oppress people and rebel in the land without right. Those will have a painful punishment.” And in the Sahih: Support your brother, whether he is an oppressor or oppressed. They said, O Messenger of God, we support him when he is oppressed, so how do we support him when he is an oppressor? He said, Take him by the hand. In another narration: Prevent him from oppression, for that is supporting him. And it was mentioned before that he, peace be upon him, said, If people see an oppressor and do not take him by the hand, God will soon afflict them all with a punishment from Him. Second: The Almighty’s saying, And do not break oaths after confirming them. He says after emphasizing and making them more severe. It is said confirmation and confirmed and confirmed and confirmed and they are two languages. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And you have made God a guarantor over you, meaning a witness, and it is said a protector, and it is said a guarantor. He only said it after emphasizing it to differentiate between an oath and one that is confirmed by resolve and a meaningless oath. Ibn Wahb and Ibn Al-Qasim from Malik said: Emphasis is a person’s swearing about one thing repeatedly, repeating the oaths three times or more, like saying: By God, I will not decrease it from such and such, and by God, I will not decrease it from such and such, and by God, I will not decrease it from such and such. He said: The expiation for that is one, like the expiation for an oath. Yahya bin Saeed said: They are the covenants and the oath, but the difference between them is that the covenant is not expiated. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A banner will be raised for every traitor on the Day of Resurrection at his backside according to the extent of his treachery, and it will be said: This is the treachery of so-and-so. As for the oath by God, God, the Almighty, has prescribed expiation for it with one characteristic and the solution of what the oath was based on. Ibn Umar said: Emphasis is that he swears twice, but if he swears once, then there is no expiation for it, and this was mentioned previously in Al-Ma’idah.
16:92: The Almighty said: And do not be like the one who untwists her spun thread after it was strong, into separate parts. An-Naqad is the singular form of Nakth, and the noun is Nakth and An-Naqd, and the plural is Ankath. So this verse likens the one who swears, makes a covenant, and concludes his covenant, then breaks it, to a woman who spins her thread, twists it tightly, then unwinds it. It is narrated that there was a foolish woman in Mecca called Raytah bint Amr ibn Ka'b ibn Sa'd ibn Taym ibn Murrah who used to do that, so the likening was made to her. Al-Farra' said it, and Abdullah ibn Kathir and As-Suddi narrated it, but they did not name the woman. Mujahid and Qatadah said: This is an example, not for a specific woman, and Ankath is the accusative of state. And Al-Dakhl means deception, trickery, and fraud. Abu Ubaidah said: Every matter that is not correct is included. That one nation is more numerous than another nation. The commentators said: This verse was revealed about the Arabs, whose tribes, if they allied with another tribe, then one of them came with a large and strong tribe and entered it, betrayed the first and broke its covenant and returned to this greater one - said Mujahid - so God the Most High said: Do not break covenants because one group is more numerous than another group or has more wealth, lest you break your oaths when you see the abundance and spaciousness in this world for your polytheistic enemies. The intended meaning is to forbid returning to disbelief because of the abundance of the disbelievers and the abundance of their wealth. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is: Do not betray a people because of their small number and your large number, or because of your small number and their large number, and you have strengthened them with oaths. Arba means more. From rabaa, something grows if it increases, and the pronoun in bih may refer to the fulfillment that God has commanded. It is possible that it refers to usury, meaning that God Almighty tested His servants with envy and some of them seeking to gain the upper hand over others, and He tested them with that to see who struggles with his soul and opposes it, and who follows it and acts according to its desires, and this is the meaning of His statement, God only tests you with it, and He will make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ, of resurrection and other things.
16:93: The Almighty says, And if God had willed, He could have made you one nation, meaning, of one religion. But He leaves astray whom He wills, by abandoning them, out of His justice toward them. And He guides whom He wills, by granting them success, out of His grace toward them. He will not be questioned about what He does, but you will be questioned. The verse refers to the people of destiny, as you can imagine, and the lam in Wa-li-bayyinna and La-ta'salun with the doubled nun indicate an implied oath, meaning, And God will make clear to you, and you will be questioned.
16:94: The Almighty said, And do not take your oaths as a means of deception between you, He repeated this for emphasis, lest a foot slip after it had been firmly established, exaggerating the prohibition of it due to its great position in religion and its recurrence in dealing with people, meaning do not make oaths that involve deception and corruption, lest a foot slip after it had been firmly established, meaning from faith after knowing God. This is a metaphor for the upright person who falls into great evil and falls into it, because if the foot slips, it transfers a person from a state of good to a state of evil. And from this meaning is the saying of many: When we met, it was fixed and I slipped The Arabs say to every afflicted person after recovery or someone who has fallen into trouble and lost his footing, as the poet says: You will be denied the lead if you are ahead and killed if you slip It is said of someone who made a mistake in something, then God Almighty threatened him with punishment in this world and a great punishment in the Hereafter. This threat is only for those who broke the covenant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Whoever made a covenant with him and then broke his covenant has left the faith. For this reason He said, And taste the evil because you averted from the path of God, meaning because you averted. And tasting the evil in this world is what befalls them of misfortune.
16:95: The Almighty’s saying, And do not exchange the covenant of God for a small price. He forbade bribery and taking money in exchange for breaking the covenant, meaning do not break your covenants for a small worldly gain. It was only a small amount, even if it was a lot, because it is something that will pass away, so it is truly a small amount, and this is what is meant by His saying, What you have will run out, but what is with God is everlasting. So He explained the difference between the state of this world and the state of the Hereafter, in that the former will run out and change, while what is with God of the gifts of His grace and the bliss of His Paradise is permanent and will not pass away for whoever fulfills the covenant and remains steadfast in the contract. And he who said it did well: Money, both lawful and unlawful, will run out one day, but its sins will remain tomorrow. A pious person is not pious to his God until his food and drink are good. last: Suppose the world is thrown to you by force, isn't that the fate of the one who is moving? Your world is nothing but a shade that covers you and then gives way to disappearance. The Almighty said: And We will surely reward those who were patient meaning in Islam and acts of obedience and against disobedience with the best of what they used to do meaning of acts of obedience and made them better because everything else of good is permissible, and the reward is only for acts of obedience in terms of the promise from God. Asim and Ibn Kathir read and We will surely reward with a nun for emphasis, the rest with a ya. It was said that this verse and do not buy up to here was revealed about Imru’ al-Qais ibn Abis al-Kindi and his opponent Ibn Aswa’. They were arguing over a piece of land, and Imru’ al-Qais wanted to swear, but when he heard this verse, he refused and acknowledged his right. And God knows best.
16:96: God Almighty says: “Whatever you have will perish, but what is with God is everlasting. And We will surely reward those who are patient according to the best of what they used to do.”
16:97: The Almighty's saying, Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life. A condition and its answer. There are five opinions regarding the good life: The first: It is lawful sustenance. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ata', and Ad-Dahhak. The second: Contentment. This was said by Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Zaid bin Wahb, and Wahb bin Munabbih. It was narrated by Al-Hakam on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is the opinion of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. The third: It is guiding him to perform acts of obedience, for they will lead him to the pleasure of God. Ad-Dahhak said its meaning. He also said: Whoever does righteousness while he is a believer, in poverty and ease, his life will be good. Whoever turns away from the remembrance of God, and does not believe in his Lord or do righteous deeds, his life will be difficult and there is no good in it. Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd said: It is Paradise. This was also said by Al-Hasan. He said: Life is not good for anyone except in Paradise. It was also said: It is happiness. This was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: It is the sweetness of obedience. Sahl bin Abdullah Al-Tustari said: It is that the servant’s management is removed and his management is returned to God. It was said: It is independence from creation and need for the truth. It was said: It is contentment with fate. And We will surely reward them meaning in the Hereafter for the best of what they used to do. He said: And We will surely revive it. Then he said: And We will surely reward them because whoever is suitable for the singular and the plural, so he repeated it once for the wording and once for the meaning, and it has been mentioned previously. Abu Saleh said: Some people from the people of the Torah, some from the people of the Gospel, and some from the people of idols sat down. These said: We are better, and these said: We are better. So this was revealed.
16:98: There is one issue, which is that this verse is connected to His statement, And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things. So if you begin to recite it, then seek refuge with God from Satan coming to you and preventing you from contemplating it and acting upon what is in it. He does not mean seeking refuge after reciting, but it is like saying, When you eat, say, 'In the name of God,' meaning, when you want to eat. "Jubair ibn Mut'im narrated on the authority of his father, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he began the prayer, say, 'O God, I seek refuge in You from Satan, from his whispering, his puffing, and his spitting.'" And "Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to seek refuge in his prayer before reciting." Al-Kaya al-Tabari said: He narrated from some of the early Muslims seeking refuge after reciting in general, citing as evidence the statement of God, the Most High, So when you recite the Qur'an, then seek refuge with God from Satan, the accursed. There is no doubt that the apparent meaning of this requires that seeking refuge be after reciting, like His statement, the Most High, So when you have completed the prayer, remember God, standing and sitting. However, other meanings are possible, such as His statement, the Most High, "And when you say, So be just. And if you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition. What is meant by this is not that he asks her from behind a partition after asking previously. Similar to this is the saying of the one who says, If you say, then be truthful. And If you enter ihram, then wash yourself, meaning before entering ihram. The meaning in all of this is that if you want that, then so is seeking refuge. This meaning has been presented, and the statement about seeking refuge has been presented in full.
16:99: The Almighty said, Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe, meaning to lead them astray and disbelieve, meaning that you have no power to force them to commit an unforgivable sin. Sufyan said this, and Mujahid said that he has no proof for what he calls them to of sins. It was said that he has no authority over them at all, because the Almighty God diverted His authority from them when the enemy of God, Satan, may God curse him, said, And I will mislead them all, Except for Your chosen servants among them. God Almighty said, Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them, except for those who follow you of the deviators. I said: We have already explained that this is a general term that includes specialization. Adam seduced Eve, peace be upon them, with his authority, and he disturbed the times of the virtuous by saying: Who created your Lord? As was explained at the end of Al-A’raf.
16:100: The Almighty said: His authority is only over those who take him as a guardian meaning obey him. It is said: I took him as a guardian meaning I obeyed him. And I turned away from him meaning I turned away from him. And those who associate others with Him meaning with God, said Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak. It was also said that it refers to Satan, said Ar-Rabi' bin Anas and Al-Qutbi. The meaning is: And those who associate others with Him. It is said: I disbelieved in this word meaning because of it, and So-and-so became knowledgeable about you meaning because of you. That is, those who take Satan as a guardian are polytheists with God.
16:101: The Almighty said: And when We substitute a verse for another verse - and God is most knowing of what He sends down. It was said: The meaning is We substituted an old law for a new law. Ibn Bahr Mujahid said this, meaning We removed a verse and replaced it with another. The majority said: We abrogated a verse with a verse that was more severe on them. Abrogation and substitution are the removal of something and the substitution of another in its place. We have already discussed abrogation in full in Surat Al-Baqarah. They said, meaning the infidels of Quraysh. You are only an inventor, meaning a liar and a fabricator. This was because they saw the change in the ruling, so God said: Rather, most of them do not know, that God legislated the rulings and replaced some with others.
16:102: And his saying, Say, 'The Holy Spirit has brought it down' means Gabriel brought down the entire Qur'an, its abrogating and abrogated parts. "It was narrated with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Aamer Al-Sha'bi, who said, 'Israfil was assigned to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for three years, so he would bring him word after word, then Gabriel brought down the Qur'an to him.'" And in Sahih Muslim also, it says that an angel who had never descended to earth before brought down Surat Al-Hamd to him, as was explained in Al-Fatihah. From your Lord with the truth meaning from the speech of your Lord, to strengthen those who believe meaning with what is in it of proofs and verses, and guidance meaning it is guidance, and good tidings for the Muslims.
16:103: The Almighty said: And We certainly know that they say, 'It is only a human being who teaches him.' There is a difference of opinion regarding the name of the one they said only teaches him. It was said: He is the young man of Al-Fakih bin Al-Mughira, whose name was Jabr. He was a Christian and then converted to Islam. When they heard from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, what had happened and what was to come, even though he was illiterate and did not read, they would say: Only Jabr teaches him, and he is a foreigner. So God Almighty said: The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, and this is a clear Arabic tongue. That is, how could Jabr, who is a foreigner, teach him this speech, from which neither mankind nor the jinn can contradict even a single surah or more. Al-Naqqash mentioned that Jaber’s client used to beat him and say to him: Do you teach Muhammad? He would say: No, by God, he teaches me and guides me. Ibn Ishaq said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as I have been told, often used to sit at Al-Marwah with a Christian boy called Jaber, a slave of Banu Al-Hadrami. He used to read books. The polytheists said: By God, he does not teach Muhammad. None brings him except Jaber the Christian. Ikrimah said: His name is Yaish, a slave of Banu Al-Hadrami. The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, used to teach him the Qur’an. Al-Mawardi mentioned it. Al-Tha’labi mentioned on the authority of Ikrimah and Qatadah that he was a boy of Banu Al-Mughirah named Yaish. He used to read foreign books. Quraysh said: Only a human being teaches him. So this verse was revealed: Al-Mahdawi on the authority of Ikrimah is a boy of Banu Amir bin Lu’ay and his name is Yaish. Abdullah bin Muslim Al-Hadrami said: We had two Christian boys from the people of Ain Al-Tamr, one of them was named Yasar and the other was named Jabr. This is what Al-Mawardi, Al-Qushayri and Al-Tha’labi mentioned, except that Al-Tha’labi said: One of them was called Nabt and was nicknamed Abu Fakiha and the other Jabr. They were polishers who made swords and they used to read a book of theirs. Al-Tha’labi used to read the Torah and the Gospel, Al-Mawardi and Al-Mahdawi the Torah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pass by them and hear them recite. The polytheists would say: He is learning from them. So God revealed this verse and disproved them. It was said that they meant Salman Al-Farsi, may God be pleased with him. This was said by Al-Dahhak. It was also said that he was a Christian in Mecca named Balaam, who was a boy who used to recite the Torah. This was said by Ibn Abbas. The polytheists would see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he would enter and leave him, so they would say: Balaam is teaching him. Al-Qutbi said: There was a Christian man in Mecca called Abu Maysarah who spoke Roman. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would sometimes sit with him and the infidels would say: Muhammad is only learning from him. So this verse was revealed. In another narration, it was said that he meant Addas, the slave of Utbah ibn Rabi’ah. It was said: Abis was the slave of Huwaytib bin Abdul-Uzza and Yasar Abu Fakiha, the client of Ibn Al-Hadrami, and they had converted to Islam, and God knows best. I said: All of them are possible, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, may have sat with them at different times to teach them what God had taught him, and that was in Mecca. Al-Nahhas said: These statements are not contradictory, because it is possible that they alluded to all of these people, and they claimed that they were teaching him. I said: As for what Ad-Dahhak mentioned that it was Salman, then there is a flaw in it because Salman only came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina, and this verse is Meccan. The tongue of the one they incline toward is foreign. Inclination is the inclination. It is said to have deviated from the right path and it was mentioned in Al-A’raf. Hamza read it Yalhadun with the opening of the ya and the ha meaning the tongue of the one they incline toward and point to is foreign. Foreignness is concealment and the opposite of clarity. A foreign man and a foreign woman, meaning they do not speak clearly. From this comes the word ajam the tail because it is hidden, and ajama the beast because it does not speak clearly about itself. And I made the book foreign means I removed its foreignness. The Arabs call everyone who does not know their language and does not speak their speech a foreigner. Al-Farra’ said: The foreigner is the one who has foreignness in his tongue even if he is from the Arabs, and the foreigner or the foreigner is the one whose origin is from the foreigners. Abu Ali said: The foreigner is the one who does not speak clearly, whether he is an Arab or a non-Arab. Likewise the foreigner and the foreigner who is attributed to the non-Arabs, even if he is eloquent. He meant the Qur’an by the tongue, because the Arabs say the poem and the verse are tongues. The poet said: The tongue of evil brings it to us, and you betrayed us, and I did not expect you to betray us He means by the tongue the poem And this is a clear Arabic tongue meaning the most eloquent of Arabic.
16:104: The Almighty says: Indeed, those who do not believe in the verses of God meaning these polytheists who do not believe in the Qur’an God will not guide them, and they will have a painful punishment.
16:105: The Almighty's saying, Only those who do not believe in the verses of God invent lies. This is the answer to the Prophet's description of them, may God bless him and grant him peace, as inventing them. And those are the liars. This is an exaggeration in describing them as liars, meaning that every lie is small in comparison to their lie. It is said that a desert lied, but it is not said that he is a liar, because the verb may be intransitive or intransitive. As for the description, it is intransitive, and for this reason it is said: Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray, but it is not said that he is a disobedient and a misguider. So if it is said: So-and-so lied, so he is a liar, it is an exaggeration in describing him as a liar, as Al-Qushayri said.
16:106: It contains twenty-one issues: First: The Almighty’s saying, Whoever disbelieves in God, this is connected to His saying, And do not break your oaths after confirming them, so it was an exaggeration in the description of lying, because its meaning is do not turn away from the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning whoever disbelieves after his belief and turns away, then upon him is the wrath of God. Al-Kalbi said, it was revealed about Abdullah bin Saad bin Abi Sarh, Muqays bin Subaba, Abdullah bin Khatal, and Qays bin Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira. They disbelieved after their belief, then He said, Except for one who is forced. Al-Zajjaj said, Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief instead of Whoever invents a lie, meaning that only one who disbelieves in God after his belief invents a lie, because he saw the statement to the end of the exception as incomplete, so he connected it to what came before it. Al-Akhfash said, From the beginning and its predicate is omitted, so it is sufficient for it to have a predicate from the second verse, like saying, “Whoever comes to us who does good, we will honor him. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Except for one who is forced. This verse was revealed about Ammar bin Yasir, according to the commentators, because he approached some of what they had urged him to do. Ibn Abbas said: The polytheists took him and took his father, his mother, Sumayyah, Suhayb, Bilal, Khabbab, and Salim, and tortured them. Sumayyah was tied between two camels, and a spear was brought before her, and she was told: You have converted to Islam for the sake of men. So she was killed, and her husband Yasir was killed, and they were the first two people killed in Islam. As for Ammar, he gave them what they wanted with his tongue, under duress, so he complained about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: How do you find your heart? He said: Reassured by faith. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If they return, then return. “And Mansur bin Al-Mu’tamir narrated from Mujahid, who said: The first female martyr in Islam was Umm Ammar, who was killed by Abu Jahl, and the first male martyr was Mahja’, the freed slave of Umar.” And Mansur also narrated from Mujahid, who said: The first to show Islam were seven: the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Bakr, Bilal, and Khabbab. And Suhaib, Ammar, and Sumayyah, the mother of Ammar. As for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Abu Talib prevented him, and as for Abu Bakr, his people prevented him and took the others and dressed them in iron armor and then melted them in the sun until they were exhausted from the heat of the iron and the sun. When it was evening, Abu Jahl came to them with a spear and began to curse and rebuke them. He came to Sumayyah and began to curse her and speak obscenely, then he stabbed her vagina until the spear came out of her mouth and killed her, may God be pleased with her. He said: The others said that they were not asked except for Bilal, for he did not consider himself worthless for the sake of God. So they began to torture him and say to him, Return from your religion, and he kept saying, One, one, until they got tired of him. Then they tied him up and put a rope of palm fiber around his neck and sent him to their children to play with him between the two wooden houses of Mecca until they got tired of him and left him. Ammar said: We all said what they said, had God not helped us except Bilal, for he did not consider himself worthless for the sake of God, so he was humiliated by his people until they got tired of him and left him. The correct view is that Abu Bakr bought Bilal and freed him. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid that some people from Mecca believed, so some of the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him) in Medina wrote to them to migrate to us, for we do not see you as being from us until you migrate to us. So they set out intending to go to Medina until the Quraysh tribe caught up with them on the way and tempted them, so they disbelieved under duress. This verse was revealed about them. They mentioned the two narrations on the authority of Mujahid: Ismail ibn Ishaq. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: ‘Whenever Ammar was given the choice between two matters, he chose the more correct of the two. ’ This is a hasan ghareeb hadith. Anas ibn Malik narrated that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: ‘Paradise longs for three: Ali, Ammar, and Salman ibn Rabi’ah. ’ Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a ghareeb hadith, and we do not know it except through the hadith of Al-Hasan ibn Salih. Third: Since God Almighty permitted disbelief in Him, which is the foundation of the Sharia, when forced, and He did not hold anyone accountable for it, the scholars applied all branches of the Sharia to it. If one is forced to do it, he is not held accountable for it and no ruling is based on it. This is what the famous hadith came from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: My nation has been lifted from error, forgetfulness, and what they are forced to do. The hadith and report, even if its chain of transmission is not authentic, its meaning is authentic by agreement of the scholars. This was said by Judge Abu Bakr Ibn al-Arabi. Abu Muhammad Abd al-Haqq stated that its chain of transmission is authentic. He said: Abu Bakr al-Asili mentioned it in al-Fawa’id and Ibn al-Mundhir in the book al-Iqna’. Fourth: The scholars have agreed that if someone is forced to disbelieve, even if he fears that he will be killed, he is not sinful if he disbelieves while his heart is at peace with faith, and his wife is not separated from him, and he is not judged as a disbeliever. This is the opinion of Malik, the Kufians, and the Shafi’i, except for Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, who said: If he shows polytheism, he is an apostate in appearance and between him and God the Most High, he is a Muslim, and his wife is separated from him, and he is not to be prayed over if he dies, and he does not inherit from his father if he dies a Muslim. This is a opinion that is refuted by the Book and the Sunnah. God the Most High said: Except for one who is forced (al-Baqarah 2:17), and He said: Except that you guard yourselves against a fearful guard (al-Baqarah 2:17), and He said: “Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves - they say: ‘In what were you?’ They say: ‘We were oppressed on the earth.’” (al-Baqarah 2:17), and He said: Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children. (al-Baqarah 2:17) So God excuses the oppressed who refrain from abandoning what God has commanded, and the one who is forced is only oppressed and does not refrain from doing what he has been commanded, as stated by al-Bukhari. Fifth: A group of scholars said that the permission only came in words, but there is no permission in actions, such as forcing them to prostrate to someone other than God, or to pray in a direction other than the Qiblah, or to kill or beat a Muslim, or to eat his money, or to commit adultery, or to drink alcohol, or to eat usury. This is narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri may God be pleased with him, and it is the opinion of Al-Awza’i and Sahnoon, among our scholars. Muhammad bin Al-Hasan said: If a prisoner is told to prostrate to this idol, or I will kill you, he says: If the idol is facing the Qiblah, then he should prostrate and his intention should be God Almighty, and if it is not facing the Qiblah, then he should not prostrate even if they kill him. The correct view is that he should prostrate even if it is not facing the Qiblah, and what is more appropriate for prostration in this case is in the Sahih: “On the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, he said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to pray while facing from Mecca to Medina on his mount, wherever he was facing. He said: “And in this was revealed the verse: ‘So wherever you turn, there is the Face of God. ’” In another narration, he would pray Witr on it, but he would not pray the obligatory prayer on it.
