If this is permissible on a journey in a safe situation due to the fatigue of getting off the mount to perform voluntary prayers, then how about this? And he who limited the permission to the statement cited the statement of Ibn Mas`ud: There is no speech that would ward off two lashes from a person of authority except that I would speak it. So he limited the permission to the statement and did not mention the action, and there is no proof in this because it is possible that he made an example of both and he meant that the action is in the same ruling. And a group said: Compulsion in action and speech is the same if faith is concealed. This was narrated from `Umar ibn al-Khattab and Makhul, and it is the statement of Malik, and a group of the people of Iraq. Ibn al-Qasim narrated from Malik that whoever is forced to drink alcohol and abandon prayer or break the fast in Ramadan, the sin is lifted from him. Sixth: The scholars agreed that if someone is forced to kill someone else, it is not permissible for him to proceed with killing him or violating his sanctity by flogging or otherwise. He must be patient with the affliction that has befallen him, and it is not permissible for him to ransom himself with someone else. He must ask God for well-being in this world and the hereafter. There was a difference of opinion regarding adultery. Mutraf, Asbagh, Ibn Abd al-Hakam, and Ibn al-Majshun said that no one should do that, and if he kills, he did not do it. If he does, then he is a sinner and must be punished. Abu Thawr and al-Hasan said the same. Ibn al-Arabi said that it is correct that it is permissible to commit adultery and there is no punishment for it, contrary to those who obligated it because they saw that it is an innate desire that cannot be compelled to do so, and they overlooked the reason that caused the desire, which is the compulsion to do so, which is what dropped its ruling. Rather, the punishment must be imposed for a desire that was prompted by a voluntary reason, so he compared something to its opposite and did not make it permissible with the correctness of his opinion. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said in his rulings: Our companions differed regarding when a man is compelled to commit adultery. Some of them said: He must be punished because he only does it by choice, and some of them said: There is no punishment for him. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: This is correct. Abu Hanifa said: If someone other than the sultan forced him, he should be punished. If the sultan forced him, then the analogy is that he should be punished. However, he preferred that he not be punished. His two companions disagreed with him and said that there is no punishment for him in either case. They did not take into account the prevalence and said: Whenever it is known that he will escape being killed by committing adultery, it is permissible for him to spread. Ibn al-Mundhir said: There is no punishment for him and there is no difference between the sultan in this regard and someone other than the sultan. Seventh: The scholars differed regarding the divorce of a person under duress and his emancipation. Al-Shafi’i and his companions said: He is not obligated to do anything. Ibn Wahb mentioned on the authority of Umar, Ali and Ibn Abbas that they did not see his divorce as anything. Ibn al-Mundhir mentioned it on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, Ata’, Tawus, al-Hasan, Shuraih, al-Qasmus, al-Malik, al-Awza’i, Ahmad, Ishaq and Abu Thawr. A group permitted his divorce. This was narrated on the authority of al-Sha’bi, al-Nakha’i, Abu Qilabah, al-Zuhri and Qatadah. It is the opinion of the Kufians. Abu Hanifa said: The divorce of a person under duress is obligatory because he did not lack more than consent, and its existence is not a condition for divorce, like the one who jokes. This is a false analogy, because the one who jokes intends to pronounce divorce and is satisfied with it, while the one who is forced is not satisfied and has no intention of divorce. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: Actions are only by intentions. And in Bukhari: Ibn Abbas said about the one who is forced by thieves and divorces him, it is nothing. And Ibn Omar, Ibn al-Zubayr, al-Sha’bi and al-Hasan said the same. Al-Sha’bi said that if the thieves force him, it is not a divorce, but if the ruler forces him, it is a divorce. Ibn Uyaynah explained it and said: The thief proceeds to kill him, but the ruler does not kill him. Eighth: As for the sale of a person who is forced or coerced, there are two cases for it. The first is that he sells his property for a right that is due to him. This is a past and permissible matter that cannot be returned to according to the jurists, because he is obligated to pay the right to its owner other than the sold item. Since he did not do that, his sale was voluntary on his part and is binding on him. As for the sale of a person who is forced unjustly or coercively, this is a sale that is not permissible for him and he is more entitled to his goods and takes them without a price. The buyer is subject to the price of that oppressor. If the goods are lost, he is subject to its price or its value, or more than that, from the oppressor if the buyer was not aware of his oppression. Mutraf said: Whoever among the buyers knows the condition of the person who is forced, then he is responsible for what he bought of his slaves and goods, like the usurper. And whenever the buyer innovates in that, such as manumission, management, or imprisonment, the person who is forced is not obligated, and he is entitled to take his goods. Sahnun said: Our companions and the people of Iraq are unanimously agreed that the sale of a person who is forced to an oppressor or tyrant is not permissible. Al-Abhari said that it is a consensus. Ninth: As for the marriage of a person under duress, Sahnun said: Our companions agreed to invalidate the marriage of a person under duress, male or female, and they said that it is not permissible to continue with it because it has not been concluded. Muhammad ibn Sahnun said: The people of Iraq permitted the marriage of a person under duress and said: If he is forced to marry a woman for ten thousand dirhams and a dowry of the same amount is one thousand dirhams, then the marriage is permissible and he is obligated to pay the thousand and the surplus is void. Muhammad said: Just as they invalidated the excess over the thousand, they are also obligated to invalidate the marriage under duress. Their statement is contrary to the established Sunnah in the hadith of Khansa bint Khidham al-Ansariyyah and his command, may God bless him and grant him peace, to invest in their goods, which has been mentioned previously, so their statement has no meaning. Tenth: If the person forced to marry her has intercourse with her without being forced to have intercourse or consent to the marriage, then the marriage is binding on him according to us for the specified dowry and the punishment is averted from him. If he says: I had intercourse with her without my consent to the marriage, then he is subject to the punishment and the specified dowry, because he is claiming that the specified dowry is invalidated. The woman is punished if she proceeds while knowing that he was forced to marry. As for the woman forced to marry and have intercourse, there is no punishment on her and she is entitled to the dowry. The one who has intercourse is punished and he is aware of it. Sahnun said this. Eleventh: If a woman is forced to commit adultery, there is no punishment for her, based on his saying, Except for him who is forced, and his saying, peace be upon him: Indeed, God has forgiven my nation for mistakes, forgetfulness, and what they are forced to do, and based on the saying of God, the Most High: Indeed, after their compulsion, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning girls. In this sense, Omar ruled regarding the female slave who was forced by a slave, and he did not punish her. The scholars agree that there is no punishment for a woman who was forced. Malik said: If a woman is found to be pregnant and she does not have a husband and she says she was forced, then that is not accepted from her and she is subject to the punishment, unless she has evidence or comes bleeding that she committed adultery or something similar. He cited as evidence the hadith of Omar ibn al-Khattab: If evidence is established, or there is pregnancy or confession, Ibn al-Mundhir said: I say the first opinion. Twelfth: They differed about the obligation of the dowry for the one forced. Ata’ and Al-Zuhri said that she is entitled to a dowry similar to that of her peers, and this is the opinion of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr. Al-Thawri said that if the punishment is carried out on the one who committed adultery with her, the dowry is void. This was narrated from Al-Sha’bi, and the companions of Malik and the people of opinion said the same. Ibn Al-Mundhir said that the first opinion is correct. Thirteenth: If a person is forced to convert his wife to Islam because it is not permissible, he should convert her, and he should not kill himself to save her, nor should he bear harm in order to free her. The basis for that is what Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abraham, peace be upon him, migrated with Sarah and entered with her a village in which there was a king or a tyrant. He sent to him, Send her to me. So he sent her. He went to her and she stood up to perform ablution and pray, and she said, O God, if I have believed in You and Your Messenger, then do not give this disbeliever power over me. So he fell asleep until he kicked her with his foot. This hadith also indicates that since Sarah was not to be blamed, so too is the one who was forced not to be blamed, and there is no punishment for what is greater than seclusion, and God knows best. Fourteenth: As for the oath of one who is forced, it is not binding according to Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Abu Thawr and most scholars. Ibn Al-Majishun said: It does not matter whether he swears in obedience to God or in disobedience if he is forced to swear. Asbagh said: Mutraf said: If he is forced to swear in disobedience to God or in his action there is no disobedience, then the oath is void. But if he is forced to swear in obedience, such as if the governor takes a corrupt man and forces him to swear by divorce, not to drink alcohol, or not to commit corruption or cheat in his work, or a father makes his son swear as a discipline for him, then the oath is binding, even if the one who was forced made a mistake in what he was required to do. Ibn Habib said this. Abu Hanifa and those who followed him from the Kufians said: If he swears not to do something and then does something, he has broken his oath. They said: Because the one who was forced has the right to conceal his oath in its entirety, so since he did not conceal it and his intention went against what he was forced to do, then he intended to swear. The first scholars argued that if he was forced to do it, then his intention is contrary to his statement because he was reluctant to do what he swore. Fifteenth: Ibn al-Arabi said: It is strange that our scholars differed on whether coercion to break an oath is binding or not. This is an Iraqi issue that was conveyed to us from them. Neither was this issue nor were they. What difference, O group of our companions, is there between coercion to an oath in that it is binding and breaking an oath in that it does not occur? So fear God and review your insights and do not be deceived by this narration, for it is a stain on knowledge. Sixteenth: If a man is forced to swear an oath, otherwise his money will be taken, such as tax collectors, unjust messengers, and aggressors. Malik said that he has no taqiyya in that, and that a person only protects himself with his oath from his body, not his money. Ibn al-Majishun said that he does not break his oath even if he protects himself from his money and does not fear for his body. Ibn al-Qasim said the words of Mutraf, and he narrated it from Malik. Ibn al-Hakam and Asbagh said the same. I said that the statement of Ibn Al-Majshun is correct, because defending money is like defending oneself, and this is the statement of Al-Hasan and Qatadah, and it will come. “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Your blood, your wealth, and your honor are sacred to you.’” He also said: “Every Muslim is sacred to another Muslim: his blood, his wealth, and his honor.” Abu Hurairah narrated that a man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, what do you think if a man comes to take my money? He said: Do not give him your money. He said: What do you think if he fights me? He said: I will fight him. He said: What do you think if he kills me? He said: Then you are a martyr. He said: What do you think if I kill him? He said: He is in the Fire. Narrated by Muslim, and the discussion of it has already been mentioned. Mutraf and Ibn Al-Majshun said: If the one who swears an oath to the unjust ruler before he asks him to do so, in order to defend what he fears for his money and body, and he swears to him, then it is binding on him. Ibn Abd al-Hakam and Asbagh said the same. Ibn al-Majshun also said about someone who was taken by an oppressor and swore to him that he would divorce him absolutely without making him swear and leaving him, and he was lying. He only swore out of fear that he would beat him, kill him, and take his money. If he only voluntarily swore the oath out of overwhelming fear and hope of being saved from his oppression, then he has entered into coercion and nothing is upon him. If he did not swear out of hope of being saved, then he has committed perjury. Seventeenth: The scholars who have investigated the matter said: If the person being forced utters kufr, it is not permissible for him to use it on his tongue except as an indirect expression, because indirect expressions are an alternative to lying. Whenever this is not the case, he is a kafir, because coercion has no authority over indirect expressions. An example of this is if someone says to him, Disbelieve in God, and he says, Allahi, and he adds the yaa. Likewise, if someone says to him, Disbelieve in the Prophet, and he says, He is a disbeliever in the Prophet, with a shaddah, which is the elevated place on the ground. It is applied to what is made of palm leaves, like a table, so he intends one of them in his heart and is absolved of kufr and is absolved of his sin. If someone says to him, Disbelieve in the Prophet, with a hamza, he says, He is a disbeliever in the Prophet, meaning the informant, any informant like Tulayha and Musaylimah the Liar. Or he means the Prophet about whom the poet said: So, the gravel became a small gravel instead of the prophet from the writer. Eighteenth: The scholars agreed that whoever is forced to disbelieve and chooses to be killed will have a greater reward from God than whoever chooses the concession. They differed about someone who was forced to do something that is not permissible for him, other than killing. The companions of Malik said that taking it with severity and choosing killing and beating is better in the sight of God than taking the concession. This was mentioned by Ibn Habib and Sahnoon. Ibn Sahnoon mentioned from the people of Iraq that if he is threatened with killing, cutting off, or beating from which he fears death, then he may do what he was forced to do, such as drinking alcohol or eating pork. If he does not do it until he is killed, then we fear that he will be sinful, because he is like someone who is forced. Khabbab ibn al-Arat narrated: We complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reclining on his cloak in the shade of the Kaaba. I said: Will you not seek victory for us? Will you not pray for us? He said: ((There were those before you who would seize a man and have a hole dug for him in the ground and place him in it. Then a saw would be brought and placed on his head and cut in half and combed with iron combs, except for his flesh and bones. But that would not turn him away from his religion. By God, this matter will be completed until a rider travels from Sana’a to Hadramawt, fearing none but God. This matter will be completed until a rider travels from Sana’a to Hadramawt, fearing none but God and a wolf on his back. His description, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the previous nations is a way of praising them and being patient with the hardships for the sake of God, and that they did not disbelieve outwardly and concealed faith in order to ward off the punishment from themselves. This is an argument from those who preferred beating, killing, and humiliation over the concession and residence in the abode of Paradise. This will be further explained in Surat Al-Ukhdood, God willing. Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Al-Faraj Al-Baghdadi said: Shureih bin Yunus narrated to us on the authority of Ismail bin Ibrahim on the authority of Yunus bin Ubaid, on the authority of Al-Hasan: That the spies of Musaylima seized two men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and took them to Musaylima. He said to one of them: Do you bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: Do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God? He said: Yes. So he let him go. He said to the other: Do you bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: And do you bear witness that I am the Messenger of God? He said: I am deaf and cannot hear. So he brought him forward and struck his neck. So this one came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I am ruined! He said: ((And what ruined you))? So he mentioned the hadith. He said: ((As for your companion, he took the trust, but as for you, you took the concession. On what you are now? He said: I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. He said: ((You are on what you are))” The concession is for someone who is sworn by an unjust ruler against himself or to guide him to a man or a man’s money. Al-Hasan said: If If he feared for himself and his money, then let him swear and not expiate his oath. This is the opinion of Qatada if he swears against himself or his money. The scholars’ opinions on this have already been mentioned. Musa bin Muawiyah mentioned that Abu Saeed bin Ashras, the companion of Malik, was made to swear by the Sultan in Tunis against a man whom the Sultan wanted to kill, that he did not give him shelter or know where he was. Ibn Ashras swore to him, and Ibn Ashras knew where he was at that time and had given him shelter. So he made him swear by divorce three times, and Ibn Ashras swore to him. Then he said to his wife: Stay away, so she stayed away from him. Then Ibn Ashras rode until he came to Al-Bahlol bin Rashid of Kairouan, and told him the report. Al-Bahlol said to him: Malik said that you have broken your oath. Ibn Ashras said: I heard Malik say that, but I only wanted a concession, or something to that effect. Al-Bahlol bin Rashid said to him: Al-Hasan Al-Basri said that you have not broken your oath. Ibn Ashras went back to his wife and took Al-Hasan’s opinion. Abdul Malik bin Habib said: Ma'bad told me on the authority of Al-Musayyab bin Sharik on the authority of Abu Shaybah who said: I asked Anas bin Malik about a man who is caught by another man, do you think he should swear to protect him with his oath? He said: Yes, and for me to swear seventy oaths and break my oath is more beloved to me than to point out a Muslim. Idris bin Yahya said: Al-Walid bin Abdul Malik used to order spies to spy on people and bring him report. He said: One of them sat in the circle of Raja bin Haywah and heard some of them slandering Al-Walid, so he reported that to him and said: O Raja! I am being mentioned badly in your gathering and you did not change it! He said: That was not the case, O Commander of the Faithful. Al-Walid said to him: Say: Is it God, there is no god but Him? He said: God, there is no god but Him. Al-Walid ordered the spy to be flogged seventy lashes, and he would meet Raja and say: O Raja, through you the rain is drawn, and seventy lashes on my back! Raja would say: Seventy lashes on your back are better for you than a Muslim man being killed. Nineteenth - The scholars differed regarding the limit of coercion. It was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he said: A man is not safe if you frighten him, tie him up, or beat him. Ibn Masoud said: There is no word that would ward off two lashes from me except that I would speak it. Al-Hasan said: Taqiyya is permissible for the believer until the Day of Resurrection, except that God Almighty does not make taqiyya in killing. Al-Nakha’i said: Chaining is coercion, and imprisonment is coercion. This is the opinion of Malik, except that he said: The frightening threat is coercion even if it does not happen if the injustice of that transgressor is proven and he carries out what he threatens with. According to Malik and his companions, there is no time limit for beating and imprisonment. Rather, it is what is painful from the beating, and what is from imprisonment that causes distress to the one who is being coerced. According to Malik, the coercion of the ruler and others is coercion. The Kufians contradicted themselves, as they did not consider imprisonment and chaining coercion to drink alcohol and eat carrion, because there is fear of death from them. They considered them coercion in his confession that so-and-so owes me a thousand dirhams. Ibn Sahnoon said: Their consensus that severe pain and suffering constitutes coercion indicates that coercion can be without causing loss of life. Malik held that if someone is forced to swear an oath by threat, imprisonment, or beating, he must swear and not break his oath. This is the view of al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Abu Thawr, and most scholars. Al-Muwfiyyah Al-Ashreen - And from this chapter is what has been proven: There are some metaphors that are an alternative to lying. Al-A'mash narrated on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i that he said: There is no harm if a man hears something about you, for you to say: By God, God knows what I said about you. Abdul-Malik bin Habib said: Its meaning is that God knows what you said, and it appears to be a denial of what was said, and there is no perjury on the part of the one who said that in his oath, nor is there a lie in his speech. Al-Nakha'i said: They had some words from the riddles of oaths that they used to ward off lies from themselves, they did not see that as lying and did not fear perjury in it. Abdul-Malik said: They used to call that metaphor from speech, if it was without deceit or trickery in the right. Al-A'mash said: If someone came to Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i and he hated to go out to him, he would sit in the mosque of his house and say to his maid: Tell him, by God, he is in the mosque. Mughirah narrated on the authority of Ibrahim that he would permit a man from the expedition, if they were presented to their leader, to say: By God, I will not be guided except by what is guided to me by someone other than me, and I will not ride except by what is carried by someone other than me, and similar statements. Abd al-Malik said: He meant by his saying (other than me) God Almighty, He is the one who guides him and He is the one who carries him, so they did not see in this a man breaking his oath, nor lying in his words, and they disliked for this to be said in deception, injustice, and denial of the truth, so whoever dared to do so sinned in his deception and did not have to make expiation for his oath. Twenty-one - The Almighty said: But whoever opens his breast to disbelief meaning he is able to accept disbelief, and no one has the power to do that except God, so it is a response to the Qadarites. Breast is in the accusative case as a direct object. Upon them is wrath from God, and for them is a great punishment which is the punishment of Hell.
16:107: The Almighty’s saying: That meaning that anger is because they preferred the life of this world meaning they chose it over the Hereafter and that God “that” is in the accusative case in apposition to that “does not guide the disbelieving people” then he described them and said:
16:108: God Almighty says: Those are the ones whose hearts God has sealed meaning from understanding the sermons, and whose hearing from the words of God Almighty, and whose sight from looking at the verses, and those are the heedless of what is intended for them.
16:109: The Almighty’s saying, There is no doubt that they, in the Hereafter, will be the losers. It was presented.
16:111: The Almighty said, On the Day every soul will come disputing for itself, meaning that God is Forgiving and Merciful in that. Or He mentioned them on the Day every soul will come disputing for itself, meaning that it will dispute and argue for itself. It was reported in the hadith that everyone will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:My soul, my soul, due to the intensity of the terror of the Day of Resurrection, except Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he will be asked about his nation. And in the hadith of Omar, he said to Ka'b al-Ahbar: O Ka'b, our fear has agitated us. Tell us and alert us. Ka'b said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if you were to meet on the Day of Resurrection with the deeds of seventy prophets, you would be at times like those of the Prophets, and you would only care about yourself. Hell will have a sigh, and no close angel or chosen prophet will remain but that he will fall prostrate on his knees, even Abraham, the friend of God, will make a request and say: O Lord, I am Your friend Abraham. I ask You today for nothing but myself. He said: O Ka'b, where do you find that in the Book of God? He said: The Most High said: The Day every soul will come to argue for itself, and every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and they will not be wronged. Ibn Abbas said about this: The disputes among the people will continue on the Day of Resurrection until the soul argues with the body, and the soul will say: O Lord of the soul, You created it from You. I had no hand with which to strike, no foot with which to walk, no eye with which to see, no ear with which to hear, and no mind with which to comprehend, until You came and entered this body, and the various types of torment were doubled for it and You saved it. Then the body will say: O Lord, You created me with Your hand, and I was like a piece of wood. I had no hand with which to strike, no foot with which to walk, no sight with which to see, and no hearing with which to hear. Then this came like a ray of light, and with it…” My tongue spoke, my eyes saw, my feet walked, and my ears heard. So, the various types of punishment were weakened for him, and He saved me from it. He said, “God sets forth for them an example: a blind man and a lame man who entered a garden in which there were fruits. The blind man did not see the fruit, and the lame man did not reach it. So the lame man called out to the blind man, ‘Come to me and carry me, so that I may eat and you may feed me.’ So he approached him and carried him, and they ate some of the fruit. So upon whom will the punishment be? He said, ‘Upon you both is the punishment.’” Al-Tha’labi mentioned it.
16:112: The Almighty said: "And God sets forth an example: a village. This is connected to the mention of the polytheists, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had called upon the polytheists of Quraysh and said: O God, make Your punishment severe upon Mudar and make it years for them like the years of Joseph. So they were afflicted with famine until they ate bones. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent food to them and distributed it among them. It was safe." Its people were not attacked. "Its provision came to it abundantly from every place." From land and sea, its like. "The fruits of everything are brought to it." The verse. "So it denied the favors of God. An'am is the plural of ne'am like ashdad is the plural of severity. It was said that na'ami is the plural of bo'si and ab'us." This denial is a denial of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. "So God made it taste, that is, He made its people taste the garment of hunger and fear." He called it a garment because it appeared on them from emaciation, paleness of color, and bad condition, which is like a garment. "Because of what they used to do," that is, from disbelief and sins. Hafs ibn Ghiyath read it. And Nasr bin Asim, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Al-Hasan, Abu Amr, as narrated by Abdul-Warith, Ubaid, Abbas, and Al-Khawf, in the accusative case, by making it taste it, in apposition to the clothing of hunger, and making it taste fear, which is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sending his troops that used to surround them. The origin of taste is in the mouth, then it is borrowed and used in place of affliction, and Mecca was given as an example for other countries, meaning that despite being close to the House of God and the construction of His Mosque, when its people disbelieved, famine struck them, so how about other villages? It was said: It is Medina, which believed in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then disbelieved in the blessings of God due to the killing of Uthman bin Affan and what happened in it after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of tribulations. This is the saying of Aisha and Hafsa, the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that it is an example given for any village that was in this condition from among the other villages.
16:113: The Almighty said, And there had certainly come to them a messenger from among themselves, but they denied him. This indicates that it was Mecca, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatadah. So the punishment seized them, which is the famine that occurred in Mecca. It was said that the hardships and hunger were among them.
16:114: The Almighty said, So eat of what God has provided for you, meaning, eat, O Muslims, from the spoils. It was said that the address was to the polytheists because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent them food out of compassion for them. This is because when they were afflicted with hunger for seven years, and the Arabs cut off their food supplies by the Prophet's command, they ate burnt bones, carcasses, dead dogs, hides, and 'alhaz, which is hair that is treated with blood. Then the leaders of Mecca spoke to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they were exhausted and said, This is the torment of men, so what about women and children? Abu Sufyan said to him, "O Muhammad, you have come to command the upholding of kinship ties and forgiveness, and your people have perished, so pray to God for them, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he permitted the people to carry food to them while they were still polytheists."
16:115: The discussion of this is complete in Surat Al-Baqarah.
16:116: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying when you describe “ma” here is a source, meaning for description. It was said that the lam is the lam of reason, and awjal means do not say for the sake of your description of lies by removing the preposition, meaning for the sake of your tongues describing lies. Lying was read with a damma on the kaf, dhal and ba’ as a description of tongues, and it was mentioned before. Al-Hasan read here specifically lying with a fatha on the kaf and a dhal and ba’ as a description of ma, the meaning being, do not say for the description of your tongues lies. It was said that it is a substitute for ma, meaning do not say for the lies that your tongues describe, this is lawful and this is unlawful, in order to invent lies about God. The verse is addressed to the infidels who forbade the lakes and the sawa’ib and permitted what is in the bellies of livestock, even if it is dead. His saying this is lawful is a reference to the dead animals in the bellies of livestock, and everything they permitted. His saying this is unlawful is a reference to the lakes and sawa’ib and everything they forbade. “Indeed, those who invent lies about God will not succeed. A little enjoyment.” That is, the pleasures of this world that they are in will soon disappear. Al-Zajjaj said: Their provision is a little provision. It was also said: They will have a little provision, then they will be returned to a painful punishment. Second: Al-Darami Abu Muhammad narrated in his Musnad that Harun told us on the authority of Hafs on the authority of Al-A’mash who said: I never heard Ibrahim say halal or haram, but he used to say they disliked and they liked. Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: It was not among the people’s fatwas to say this is halal and this is haram, but rather they used to say beware of such and such, and I would not do that. The meaning of this is that what is permissible and forbidden is only for God the Almighty, and no one has the right to say or state this explicitly about a particular thing unless the Almighty Creator informs about it and what ijtihad leads to in it being forbidden, he says: I dislike such and such. Malik used to do the same, following the example of those who came before him from the people of fatwa. If it is said: He said about the one who said to his wife you are forbidden to me that she is forbidden, and it is three times. The answer is that when Malik heard Ali ibn Abi Talib say that it is forbidden, he followed his example. The evidence for the prohibition may be strong for the mujtahid, so there is no problem in that case saying that, just as he says that usury is forbidden in things other than the six things. Malik, may God have mercy on him, often says that it is forbidden and not appropriate for usurious money and what contradicts interests and deviates from the path of objectives, due to the strength of the evidence for that.
16:117: The Almighty said: A brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment.
16:118: The Almighty’s statement, And as for those who are Jews, makes clear that livestock and crops are permissible for this nation, but as for the Jews, some things were forbidden to them. We have forbidden what We related to you before, that is, in Surat Al-An’am. And We did them no wrong, that is, by forbidding them what We forbade them, but they wronged themselves, so We forbade them those things as a punishment for them, as mentioned previously in Surat An-Nisa.
16:119: The Almighty said, Then your Lord is for those who do evil, meaning polytheism. This was said by Ibn Abbas and it was mentioned previously in An-Nisa.
16:120: The Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth. Peace be upon him, he called the polytheists of the Arabs to the religion of Abraham, as he was their father and the builder of the House by which they were glorified. The nation is the man who gathers goodness, and its implications have been presented. Ibn Wahb and Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik that he said it reached me that Abdullah ibn Masoud said: May God have mercy on Muadh, he was a nation obedient. It was said to him: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, God the Almighty mentioned Abraham, peace be upon him, with this. Ibn Masoud said: The nation is the one who teaches people goodness, and the obedient is the one who is obedient, and obedience has been presented in Surat al-Baqarah, and inclining toward truth is in Surat al-An'am.
16:121: The Almighty said, Grateful meaning he was grateful for His blessings blessings is the plural of blessing, and it has been mentioned before He chose him meaning He selected him and guided him to a straight path * And We gave him good in this world It was said a good son, and it was said good praise, and it was said prophethood, and it was said prayer is linked to prayers upon Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the testimony of faith. It was said that there are no people of religion who do not take him as their guardian, and it was said that it is the continuation of his hospitality and the visitation of his grave. And God gave him all of that and increased him, may God bless him and grant him peace. And indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous from means with, meaning with the righteous because he was also with the righteous in this world, and this was mentioned before in Al-Baqarah.
16:122: God Almighty said: And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous.
16:123: Ibn Omar said: He was ordered to be followed in the rituals of Hajj as Gabriel taught Ibrahim, peace be upon him. At-Tabari said: He was ordered to be followed in disavowing idols and adorning oneself with Islam. It was said that he was ordered to be followed in all of his religion except what he was ordered to leave. This was said by some of the companions of Al-Shafi’i, according to what Al-Mawardi narrated. The correct view is to follow in the beliefs of the Shari’ah, not the branches, because God the Almighty said: To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. Question: In this verse there is evidence of the permissibility of the better following the lesser for what was mentioned in the fundamentals and acting upon it, and there is no attainment of the better in that because the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is the best of the prophets, peace be upon them, and he was ordered to follow their example, so he said: So follow their guidance. And he said here: Then We revealed to you, ‘Follow the religion of Abraham.’
16:124: The Almighty said, The Sabbath was only made for those who differed therein. That is, it was not in the law of Abraham nor from his religion, but it was lenient and not strict. The Sabbath was a strict punishment for the Jews in rejecting work and not enjoying their livelihood because of their differences in it. Then Jesus, peace be upon him, came with Friday and said: Devote yourselves to worship on one day every seven days. They said: We do not want their festival to be after our festival. So they chose Sunday. The scholars differed about how they differed. A group said: Moses, peace be upon him, ordered them to have Friday and designated it for them and informed them of its superiority over others. So they debated with him about whether the Sabbath was better. So God said to him: Leave them to what they chose for themselves. It was said: God Almighty did not specify it for them, but rather He ordered them to glorify a day on Friday, so their efforts differed in specifying it. The Jews specified Saturday because God Almighty finished creating on it, and the Christians specified Sunday because God Almighty began creating on it, so He bound each of them to what his efforts led him to, and God specified Friday for this nation without leaving them to their efforts, as a favor and blessing from Him, so it was the best nation. The Sahih narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We are the last and the first on the Day of Resurrection, and we are the first to enter Paradise, but they were given the Book before us and we were given it after them, so they differed about it, so God guided us to the truth regarding which they differed. So this is their day regarding which they differed, so God guided us to it. He said: Friday, so today is ours, and tomorrow is for the Jews and the day after tomorrow is for the Christians. His saying: This is their day regarding which they differed strengthens the saying of the one who said: It was not specified for them, because if it had been specified for them and they were stubborn, it would not have been said that they differed, but rather it should have been said that they differed about it and were stubborn. What also strengthens it is his saying: Peace be upon him: God led those who came before us astray from Friday prayer. This is a text in the meaning. It came in some of its versions This is their day which God imposed upon them, and they differed about it. It is an argument for the first statement. It was narrated: God prescribed Friday prayer for those who came before us, and they differed about it, and God guided us to it, so people follow us in it. The Almighty’s saying, Upon those who differed therein, means on Friday, as we have explained. They differed over their prophets Moses and Jesus. The connection to what came before is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded following the truth, and God warned the nation against differing over it, lest He be severe on them as He was severe on the Jews.
16:125: There is one issue: This verse was revealed in Mecca at the time of the command to make peace with the Quraysh, and the command to call to the religion of God and His law with gentleness and kindness, without harshness or harshness. This is how Muslims should be admonished until the Day of Judgment. It is decisive regarding the disobedient monotheists and abrogated by fighting against the disbelievers. It has been said: If these conditions are possible for the disbelievers and it is hoped that they will believe in him without fighting, then it is decisive regarding them. And God knows best.
16:126: It has four issues: First: The majority of the commentators agreed that this verse is Medinan, and was revealed regarding the mutilation of Hamza on the day of Uhud. This was mentioned in Sahih al-Bukhari and in the Book of Seerah. An-Nahhas held that it is Meccan, and the meaning is connected to what preceded it from Mecca in a good connection, because the ranks are graduated from the one who is called and admonished to the one who argues to the one who is rewarded for his actions. But what the majority narrated is more authentic. Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the polytheists left the dead of Uhud, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left and saw a sight that upset him. He saw Hamza’s stomach had been split open, his nose cut off, and his ears cut off. He said: If it were not for the fact that it would sadden women or become a tradition after me, I would have left him until God resurrects him from the bellies of wild beasts and birds. I would have mutilated seventy men in his place. Then he called for a cloak and covered his face with it. His feet came out, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, covered his face and put idhkhir on his feet, then he brought him forward and said ten takbirs over him. Then the man would be brought and placed in his place, and Hamza would be placed in his place until he prayed seventy prayers over him. There were seventy dead. When they were buried and he had finished with them, this verse was revealed: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction until His saying: And be patient, and your patience is not but through God. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was patient and did not mutilate anyone. Ismail bin Ishaq transmitted it from Ishaq from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. The hadith of Ibn Abbas is more complete. Al-Tabari narrated on the authority of a group that said: This verse was revealed concerning someone who has been wronged, and he should not take from his wrongdoer, if he is able, anything but the equivalent of his wrong, and he should not extend it to anyone else. Al-Mawardi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Sirin and Mujahid. Second: The scholars differed regarding someone who was wronged by a man in taking money, then the wrongdoer entrusted the wronged person with money. Is it permissible for him to betray him in the amount that he wronged him? A group said: He is permitted to do that, including Ibn Sirin, Ibrahim al-Nakha’i, Sufyan, and Mujahid, and they cited as evidence this verse and the generality of its wording. Malik and a group with him said: He is not permitted to do that, and they cited as evidence the saying of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Fulfill the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you. Narrated by al-Daraqutni. This has been mentioned in full in Surat al-Baqarah. It was mentioned in Musnad Ibn Ishaq that this hadith was only reported about a man who committed adultery with another woman, then the other man was able to have intercourse with the second man’s wife by leaving her with him and traveling. So that man consulted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the matter, and he said to him: Return the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you. Based on this, Malik’s statement regarding the matter of money is strengthened, because betrayal is a consequence of that and is a vice from which there is no escape, so he should avoid it for himself. If he is able to take revenge on money that was not entrusted to him, then it is as if that is permissible and as if God has ruled for him, just as if he is able to take the ruling from the ruler. It has been said that this verse was abrogated, abrogated by And be patient, and your patience is not except through God. Third: In this verse there is evidence of the permissibility of equivalence in retaliation. Whoever kills with an iron object shall be killed with it, and whoever kills with a stone shall be killed with it. The amount required shall not be exceeded. This meaning has been presented in full in Surat Al-Baqarah, and praise be to God. Fourth: God Almighty called the harms in this verse punishment, and the punishment is actually the second, and He only did that so that the two words would be equal and the introductory meaning of the statement would be consistent. This is the opposite of His saying: And they plotted, and God plotted, and His saying: God mocks them, for the second here is the metaphor and the first is the reality, as Ibn Atiyah said.
16:127: There is one issue: Ibn Zayd said that it was abrogated by the fighting, and the majority of people are of the view that it is decisive, meaning be patient by forgiving the punishment, by punishing with the same punishment that they were punished with of mutilation. And do not grieve over them, meaning over the dead of Uhud, for they have gone to the mercy of God. And do not be in distress, distress is the plural of distress. The poet said: Reveal our distress and make room The majority of scholars read with the opening of the letter Ḍād and Ibn Kathir read with the opening of the letter Ḍād and it was narrated from Nafi’ and it is a mistake from those who narrated it. Some linguists said: The opening and closing of the letter Ḍād are two dialects for the source. Al-Akhfash said: Da’iq and Da’iq are the source of Da’iq and Yadīq. The meaning is: Do not let your chest be constricted by their disbelief. Al-Farra’ said: Da’iq is what your chest is constricted by, and Da’iq is what is in something that is spacious and narrows like a house or a garment. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: “They are the same. It is said: “In his chest is narrow” and Da’iq Al-Qatbi is Da’iq and Da’iq is a lightened Da’iq, meaning do not be in a tight situation, so lighten it like Hayn and Hayn. Ibn Arafa said: A man is said to be narrow if he is stingy, and “Adhāq if he is poor. His statement, Indeed, God is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good means from indecencies and major sins with victory, assistance, favor, righteousness and support. The meaning of Ihsan was mentioned before. It was said to Harim ibn Hibban when he was dying: Advise us, so he said: I advise you with the verses of God and the end of Surat An-Nahl “Invite to the way of your Lord” and so on. Surah An-Nahl has been completed, and praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.
16:128: God Almighty says: Indeed, God is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good.
17:1: Interpretation of Surah Al-Isra This Surah is Meccan, except for three verses: The Almighty said: And they almost incited you. It was revealed when the delegation of Thaqeef came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and when the Jews said: This is not the land of the prophets. The Almighty said: And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter with a truthful entrance and let me exit with a truthful exit.’ The Almighty said: Indeed, your Lord encompasses mankind. Muqatil said: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who were given knowledge before him. Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him said about the Children of Israel, the Cave, and Maryam that they are from the first generations, and they are from my generation, meaning from his old earnings. In the name of God, the most gracious, the most merciful God Almighty says: “Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.” It has eight issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Glory be to God Glory be to God is a noun that is used in the place of a verbal noun, and it is not stable, because it does not follow the grammatical rules, nor does the definite article enter into it, nor does a verb come from it, nor is it declined because there are two extra words at the end of it. You say: I glorified God as a glorification and as a glory, like I disbelieved the oath as takfiran and kufrana. And its meaning is the sanctification and innocence of God Almighty from all deficiency. It is a great remembrance of God Almighty that does not allow for anything other than it. As for the poet’s saying: I say when his pride came to me, Glory be to the one who made Alqamah proud. Rather, he mentioned it in a rare way. Talha bin Ubaidullah Al-Fayadh, one of the ten, narrated that he said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: What is the meaning of Subhan God? He said: I purify God from all evil. The factor in it, according to the doctrine of Sibawayh, is the verb whose meaning is not from its wording, since no verb is derived from its wording, such as qad al-qarfa’ squatting and istamma al-sama’ the deaf. So the meaning, according to him, is: I purify God, purifying Himself. So Subhan God came in place of your saying tanzihan purifying Himself. The second: The Almighty’s saying, He took His servant by night. The word by night has two meanings: sara and asra, like saqa and asqa, as mentioned above. He said: A storm from Gemini is blowing on him, bringing freezing cold to the north. Another said: Al-Nadira neighborhood, the mistress of the chamber, came to me as a prisoner, but she did not travel So he combined the two languages in the two verses. And Israa’ means the night journey. It is said: I travelled by night and by night, and I travelled by night. The poet said: And a dewy night I walked, and none of its secrets deprived me. It was said: Asra walked at the beginning of the night, and Sara walked at the end of it, and the first is more known. Third: The Almighty’s saying, By His servant. The scholars said: If the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a more honorable name than this, He would have called him by it in that lofty state. And in its meaning, they recited: Oh people, my heart is with Zahra, and the one who hears and sees it knows it. Do not call me except by O Abdha, for it is the most honorable of my names. It was mentioned earlier. Al-Qusharri said: When God Almighty raised him to the presence of the sublime, and elevated him above the upper planets, He made him bear the name of servitude out of humility to the nation. Fourth: The Isra’ was established in all the hadith compilations, and it was narrated from the Companions in all parts of Islam, so it is mutawatir in this manner. Al-Naqqash mentioned twenty Companions who narrated it. Al-Sahih narrated from Anas bin Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was brought Al-Buraq, which is a tall white animal, bigger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, and it places its hoof where it reaches its sight. I rode it until I came to the Holy House. I tied it to the ring to which the prophets were tied. Then I entered the mosque and prayed two rak’ahs in it. Then I came out and Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me with a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk, and I chose the milk. Gabriel said, ‘You have chosen the fitrah. ’ Then he ascended with us to the heavens.” Among what is not in the two Sahihs is what was narrated by Al-Ajuri and Al-Samarqandi. Al-Ajuri said on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri regarding the words of God Almighty: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from Al-Masjid Al-Haram to Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed. Abu Saeed said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us about the night he was taken on the Night Journey. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was met by a beast that was most similar to a mule, with two flapping ears. It was Al-Buraq, which the prophets used to ride before. I rode it and it set off, its hands falling as far as its sight could reach. Then I heard a call to my right: O Muhammad, take it easy so that I may ask you. So I continued and did not turn away from it. Then I heard a call to my left: O Muhammad, take it easy so that I may ask you. So I continued and did not turn away from it. Then I met a woman wearing all the adornments of this world, raising her hands and saying: Take it easy so that I may ask you. So I continued and did not turn away. Then I came to the Holy House of Jerusalem, Al-Aqsa, and I got off the beast and tied it in the ring in which the prophets used to be tied. Then I entered the mosque and prayed in it. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to me: What did you hear, O Muhammad? So I said: I heard a call to my right: O Muhammad.” He said: Take it easy until I ask you. I went and did not go up to him. He said: That is the caller of the Jews. If I had stopped, your nation would have become Jews. He said: Then I heard a call to my left: Take it easy until I ask you. I went and did not go up to him. He said: That is the caller of the Christians. If you had stopped, your nation would have become Christians. He said: Then a woman met me wearing all the adornments of the world, raising her hands, saying: Take it easy. I went and did not go up to her. He said: That is the world I stopped at. I chose the world over the Hereafter. He said: Then two vessels were brought to me, one of them had milk and the other had wine. It was said to me: Take and drink whichever you want. I took the milk and drank it. Gabriel said to me: You have attained the natural disposition. If you had taken the wine, your nation would have gone astray. Then he brought the Ascension through which the souls of the sons of Adam ascend. It was more beautiful than what you have seen. Have you not seen how the dead person fixes his sight towards it? He ascended with us until we came to the door of the lowest heaven. Gabriel asked to be opened. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They opened for me and greeted me. There was an angel guarding the heaven. He was called Ismail. With him were seventy thousand angels, with each angel a hundred. A thousand. He said: None knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. Then he said: Then we proceeded to the fifth heaven and there I saw Aaron bin Imran, the beloved of his people, and around him were many followers of his nation. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, described him and said: He had a long beard, his beard almost reaching his navel. Then we proceeded to the sixth heaven and there I saw Moses, so he greeted me and welcomed me. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, described him and said: A man with much hair. If he had two shirts on him, his hair would come out of them. Al-Bazzar narrated that a horse was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he charged on it, and with every step he widened his sight. It was narrated in the description of Buraq from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “While I was sleeping in the sanctuary, someone came to me and nudged me with his foot. I followed the person and saw that it was Gabriel, peace be upon him, standing at the door of the mosque with him a beast smaller than a mule and larger than a donkey. Its face was the face of a human being, its hoof was the hoof of a hoofed animal, its tail was the tail of a bull, and its mane was the mane of a horse. When Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought it close to me, it was frightened and spread out its mane. Gabriel, peace be upon him, stroked it and said: O Buraq, do not be frightened by Muhammad, for by God, no close angel or sent prophet has ridden you who is better than Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor more honorable to God than him. She said: I know that he is like that and that he is the master of intercession, and I love to be in his intercession. I said: You will be in my intercession, God willing.” Abu Saeed Abdul Malik bin Muhammad Al-Naysaburi narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by Idris, peace be upon him, in the fourth heaven, he said: Welcome to the righteous brother whom we were promised to see, but we did not see him until tonight. He said: “And therein was Mary, daughter of Imran, who had seventy palaces of pearls, and the mother of Moses, son of Imran, had seventy palaces of red coral crowned with pearls, their doors and beds of one vein.” When he ascended to the fifth heaven and its people were glorifying God, “Glory be to Him who combined snow and fire. Whoever says it once will have a reward like theirs,” Gabriel, peace be upon him, opened the door for him, and he saw an old man, the most beautiful of whom had never been seen, with large eyes, his beard reaching close to his navel, almost like his hair was disheveled, and around him were people sitting, to whom he was telling stories. I said: O Gabriel, who is this? He said: Aaron, the beloved of his people. And he mentioned the hadith. This is a brief summary of the hadiths of the Isra’ outside of the two Sahihs. Abu al-Rabi’ Sulayman ibn Sab’ mentioned them in full in the book Shifa’ al-Sudur. For him. There is no disagreement among the scholars and the group of biographers that prayer was only imposed on the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca at the time of the Isra’ when he ascended to heaven. They differed about the date of the Isra’ and the form of prayer, and whether the Isra’ was with his soul or his body. These are three issues related to the verse, and they are what we should stop at and research, and they are more important than listing those hadiths. I will mention what I have come across in terms of the sayings of the scholars and the differences of the jurists, with the help of God Almighty. As for the first issue - which is whether the Isra’ was with his soul or his body - the predecessors and successors differed about his sin, so a group went to the fact that it was a Isra’ with the soul, and his person did not leave his bed, and that it was a vision in which he saw the truths, and the vision of the prophets is true. This was held by Muawiyah and Aisha, and it was narrated from Al-Hasan and Ibn Ishaq. A group said: The Israa was with the body while awake to the Holy House, and to the heavens with the soul, and they argued with the words of God Almighty: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, so He made the Farthest Mosque the ultimate Israa. They said: If the Israa was with his body to something other than the Al-Aqsa Mosque, He would have mentioned it, as it would have been more eloquent in praise. Most of the Salaf and Muslims went to the view that it was a Israa with the body and while awake, and that he rode Al-Buraq in Mecca, and arrived at the Holy House and prayed there, then he was taken on the Israa with his body, and this is indicated by the hadiths that we have referred to and the verse. There is no impossibility in the Israa with his body and his wandering while awake, and one does not deviate from the apparent and the truth to interpretation except in the case of impossibility, and if it was a dream, He would have said with the soul of His servant and not with His servant. His saying: His sight did not swerve, nor did it go astray indicates that. If it had been a dream, there would have been no sign or miracle in it, and Umm Hani' would not have said to him: Do not speak to people, lest they call you a liar, nor would Abu Bakr have been superior in believing him, and Quraysh would not have been able to denounce and disbelieve him. Quraysh called him a liar in what he told them, until some people who had believed apostatized. If it had been a dream, he would not have been surprised. The polytheists said to him: If you are truthful, then tell us about our caravan, where you met it. He said: In such and such a place, I passed by it and so-and-so was frightened. It was said to him: What did you see, so-and-so? He said: I did not see anything except that the camels were frightened. They said: Then tell us when the caravan will come to us. He said: It will come to you on such and such a day. They said: At what time? He said: I do not know, the sun rising from here faster or the caravan rising from here. The man said: On that day, the sun has risen. A man said: This is your caravan that has come out. They asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the description of Jerusalem, so he described it to them, although he had not seen it before. Al-Sahih narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw myself in Al-Hijr and the Quraysh were asking me about things in Jerusalem that I had not confirmed, so I was distressed as I had never been distressed before. Then God raised it up for me to look at it, and they did not ask me about anything except that I informed them of it.” The hadith. The statement of Aisha and Muawiyah: The Prophet’s soul was taken on a night journey was objected to because she was young and had not been seen, nor had she narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for Muawiyah, he was a disbeliever at that time, and had not seen the situation, nor had he narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Whoever wants to add to what we have mentioned, let him refer to the book Al-Shifa by Qadi Iyad, and he will find healing from that. He cited as evidence for Aisha the words of God Almighty: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, so he called it a vision. This is refuted by the words of God Almighty: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night, and it is not said about sleep that he was taken on a night journey. Also, it may be said about seeing with the eYa-Sin 36:a vision, as will be explained in this surah. In the texts of the authentic hadiths, there is clear evidence that the Night Journey was by body, and if the hadith is reported with something that is permissible in the mind in the power of God Almighty, then there is no way to deny it, especially in a time of breaching customs, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on the ascension, so it is not far-fetched that some of it was by vision, and this is what is interpreted as his saying, peace be upon him, in the Sahih: While I was at the house, between sleeping and awake.” It is possible that he referred to the Night Journey as sleeping. And God knows best. The second issue: Concerning the date of the Isra’ Night Journey, scholars have also differed on this, and they differed on this with Ibn Shihab. Musa bin Uqbah narrated from him that he was taken on a night journey to Jerusalem one year before he left for Medina. Yunus narrated from him from Urwah from Aisha, who said: Khadija died before prayer was made obligatory. Ibn Shihab said: This was seven years after the mission of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Waqasi narrated from him that he was taken on a night journey five years after his mission. Ibn Shihab said: Fasting was made obligatory in Medina before Badr, and zakat and Hajj were made obligatory in Medina, and alcohol was forbidden after Uhud. Ibn Ishaq said: He was taken on a night journey from the Sacred Mosque to the Al-Aqsa Mosque, which is Jerusalem, and Islam originated in Mecca among the tribes. Yunus bin Bakir narrated from him that he said: Khadija prayed with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he will come. Abu Omar said: This shows you that the Isra’ was years before the Hijra, because Khadija died five years before the Hijra, and it was said three years, and it was said four years. The statement of Ibn Ishaq contradicts the statement of Ibn Shihab, although Ibn Shihab differed from him as mentioned above. Al-Harbi said: He was taken on the Night Journey on the twenty-seventh night of the month of Rabi’ al-Akhir, one year before the Hijra. Abu Bakr Muhammad bin Ibn Ali bin al-Qasim al-Dhahabi said in his history: He was taken on the Night Journey from Mecca to Jerusalem, and he ascended to the heavens eighteen months after his mission. Abu Omar said: I do not know of anyone from the people of the biography who said what al-Dhahabi narrated, and his statement was not based on anyone to whom this knowledge is attributed from them, nor did he trace it back to anyone to whom this knowledge is attributed from them, nor did he trace it back to anyone who could be used as evidence against them. The third issue: As for the obligation of prayer and its form when it was imposed, there is no disagreement among the scholars and the group of the people of biography that prayer was only imposed in Mecca on the night of the Isra’ when he was taken up to heaven, and this is stated in the Sahih and other books. They only differed about its form when it was imposed. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she imposed two rak’ahs, two rak’ahs, then the prayer of residence was increased and it was completed to four, and the prayer of travel was left at two rak’ahs. This is what Al-Sha’bi, Maymun ibn Mihran, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said. Al-Sha’bi said: Except for Maghrib. Yunus bin Bakir said: Ibn Ishaq said: Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when prayer was made obligatory upon him, meaning during the Night Journey. He nudged him with his heel towards the side of the valley, and a spring of water gushed forth. Gabriel performed ablution while Muhammad, peace be upon them, was looking on. He washed his face, sniffed water in the nose, rinsed his mouth, wiped his head, ears, and feet up to the ankles, and sprinkled water over his private parts. Then he stood up to pray two rak’ahs with four prostrations. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, and God had satisfied his eyes and his soul was at ease, and what he loved of the command of God Almighty had come to him. So he took Khadija’s hand, then brought her to the spring and performed ablution as Gabriel had done, then he and Khadija performed two rak’ahs and four prostrations. Then he and Khadija would pray together. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that it was made obligatory four rak’ahs when at home and two rak’ahs when traveling. Nafi’ bin Jubayr and Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan Al-Basri said the same, and it is the saying of Ibn Jurayj. And what is consistent with that was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was narrated. They did not differ that Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended on the morning of the Night Journey at noon, and taught the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the prayer and its times. Yunus bin Bakir narrated on the authority of Salim, the freed slave of Abu al-Muhajir, who said: I heard Maymun bin Mihran say: The first prayer was two, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed four, so it became a Sunnah, and the prayer was confirmed for the traveler and it is complete. Abu Omar said: This is a chain of transmission that cannot be relied upon, and his saying, so it became a Sunnah is a strange statement. Likewise, al-Sha’bi’s excluding Maghrib alone and not mentioning Fajr is a statement that has no meaning. The Muslims have agreed that the obligation of prayer in the city is four except Maghrib and Fajr, and they do not know anything other than that in practice and widespread transmission, and the difference in what was originally obligatory does not harm them. Fifth: We have already discussed the ear in Al-Ma’idah, and praise be to God. And we have already mentioned in Al-Imran that the first mosque to be built on earth was the Sacred Mosque, then the Al-Aqsa Mosque. And that there were forty years between them from the hadith of Abu Dharr, and the building of the Al-Aqsa Mosque by Solomon, peace be upon him, and his supplication for it from the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr and the reason for combining that, so ponder it there, there is no point in repeating it. And we mention here his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Do not undertake a journey except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, this mosque of mine, and the Mosque of Elijah or Bayt al-Maqdis.” Narrated by Malik from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah. It indicates the superiority of these three mosques over all other mosques. For this reason, the scholars said: Whoever vows to pray in a mosque that cannot be reached except by journey and riding, should not do so, and should pray in his mosque, except in the three mosques mentioned, because whoever vows to pray in them should go to them. Malik and a group of scholars said about someone who vows to guard a border crossing: He must fulfill it wherever the guard is, because it is an act of obedience to God, the Almighty. Abu al-Bukhtari added to this hadith the mosque of al-Jund, but it is not authentic and is fabricated. It was mentioned in the introduction to the book. Sixth: The Almighty said: To the Farthest Mosque. Al-Aqsa was named so because of the distance between it and the Sacred Mosque, and it was the farthest mosque from the people of Mecca on earth, and it was venerated by visiting. Then He said, Whose surroundings We have blessed. It was said: with fruits and rivers. It was also said: with those who were buried around it from the prophets and righteous people, and with this He made it sacred. Muadh ibn Jabal narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “God Almighty says, ‘O Sham, you are the chosen one from My lands, and I am driving to you the chosen one from My servants. ’” To show him some of Our signs. This is a way of diversifying the speech. The signs that God showed him are among the wonders that He informed the people about, and his Isra’ from Mecca to the Farthest Mosque in one night, which was a month’s journey, and his ascension to the heavens and his description of the prophets one by one, as was proven in Sahih Muslim and others. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing. It was mentioned above.
17:2: That is, We honored Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with the Night Journey, and We honored Moses with the Book, which is the Torah. And We made it that is, that Book. It was said, Moses. It was said that the meaning of the statement is: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night and gave Moses the Book, so he moved from absence to reporting about Himself, may He be glorified and exalted. It was said that the meaning of Glory be to Him who took His servant by night is that We took him, as indicated by what follows it in His statement: To show him some of Our signs. So, We gave Moses the Book was taken to mean. That you do not take Abu Amr read they take with the letter ya. The rest read it with the letter ta. So it is a way of diversifying the address. A trustee means a partner, according to Mujahid. It was said: A guarantor of their affairs, as narrated by Al-Farraa. It was said: A Lord whom they rely on in their affairs, as Al-Kalbi said. Al-Farraa said: Sufficient, and the meaning is: We entrusted him in the Book that you do not take a trustee besides Me. It was said: The meaning is so that you do not take. And the agent: the one to whom the matter is entrusted.
17:3: That is, O offspring of those whom We carried, on the call, said Mujahid and narrated from him Ibn Abi Nujayh. What is meant by offspring is everyone who is relied upon by the Qur’an, and they are all those on earth, mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. Al-Mawardi said: He means Moses and his people from the Children of Israel, and the meaning is O offspring of those whom We carried with Noah, do not associate partners. And Noah was mentioned to remind them of the blessing of salvation from drowning for their fathers. Sufyan narrated from Hamid from Mujahid that he read offspring with a fatha on the dhal and a shaddah on the ra and the ya. This reading was narrated by Aamer bin Al-Wajid from Zaid bin Thabit. It was also narrated from Zaid bin Thabit offspring with a kasra on the dhal and a shaddah on the ra. Then he explained that Noah was a grateful servant who thanked God for His blessings and did not see good except from Him. Qatada said: Whenever he put on a garment, he would say: In the name of God, and when he took it off, he would say: Praise be to God. This is what Muammar narrated from him. Muammar narrated from Mansur from Ibrahim who said: When he thanked God, he said: In the name of God. When he finished eating, he said: Praise be to God. Salman Al-Farsi said: Because he used to thank God for his food. Imran bin Saleem said: Noah was called a grateful servant because when he ate, he said: Praise be to God who fed me. If He willed, He could have made me hungry. When he drank, he said: Praise be to God who gave me drink. If He willed, He could have made me thirsty. When he dressed, he said: Praise be to God who clothed me. If He willed, He could have stripped me. When he sat down, he said: Praise be to God who kept me away from harm. If He willed, He could have kept it in me. The meaning of the verse is: You are from the descendants of Noah, and he was a grateful servant. So you are more deserving of following his example than your ignorant fathers. It was said: The meaning is that Moses was a grateful servant when God made him from the descendants of Noah. It was also said that it is permissible for descendants to be a second object for you take and for his saying: a trustee to mean all together, so that is permissible in both readings, I mean the ya’ and the ta’ in you take. It is also permissible in both readings for descendants to be a substitute for his saying a trustee because it means the whole, so it is as if he said: Do not take descendants from our camel with Noah. It is permissible to put it in the accusative case by implying I mean and I praise, and the Arabs may put it in the accusative case for praise and blame. It is permissible to put it in the nominative case as a substitute for the implied in you take in the reading of those who read with the ya’, but that is not good for those who read with the ta’ because the one being addressed cannot be replaced by the absent one. It is permissible to put it in the genitive case as a substitute for the Children of Israel in both ways. As for the one from his saying you should not take, it is according to the reading of those who read with the ya’ in the accusative case by deleting the preposition, the estimate: We guided them so that they would not take. It is appropriate according to the reading of the ta’ for it to be redundant and the statement is implied as mentioned above. It is appropriate for it to be interpreted with the meaning of no and it has no place in parsing. no is for prohibition, so it is a departure from the report to the prohibition.
17:4: The Almighty said: And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Book. Saeed bin Jubair and Abu Al-Aaliyah read in the books in the plural form. The singular form may be used and its meaning is plural, so the two readings have the same meaning. The meaning of decree is We informed and informed, Ibn Abbas said: Qatada said: We judged, and the origin of decree is to decide something and finish it. It was said: We decreed or We inspired, and that is why He said to the Children of Israel. According to Qatada, to means upon, meaning We decreed and ruled over them. Ibn Abbas also said this. What is meant by the Book is the Preserved Tablet. You will surely corrupt. Ibn Abbas read You will surely corrupt. Isa Al-Thaqafi read You will surely corrupt. The meaning in both readings is close, because if they corrupt, what is meant by corruption is violating the rulings of the Torah. On the earth means the land of Ash-Sham, Jerusalem, and what is adjacent to it. Twice, and let it be announced The lam in let you corrupt and let it be announced is the lam of an implied oath, as mentioned above. With great arrogance means arrogance, oppression, tyranny, overpowering, dominance, and aggression.
17:5: The Almighty said: And when the first of the two promises came to pass meaning the first of the two times of their corruption. We sent against you servants of Ours of great might they were the people of Babylon, and Nebuchadnezzar was over them the first time when they denied Jeremiah and wounded him and imprisoned him, as Ibn Abbas and others said. Qatada said: He sent Goliath against them and killed them, so he and his people were of great might. Mujahid said: An army from Persia came to them to spy on their report, and Nebuchadnezzar was with them, so he memorized their story from among his companions, then they returned to Persia and there was no fighting, and this was the first time, so some of them were scouting throughout the lands, but not killing. Al-Qushayri mentioned Abu Nasr. Al-Mahdawi mentioned on the authority of Mujahid that Nebuchadnezzar came to them and the Children of Israel defeated him, then he came to them a second time and killed them and destroyed them completely. Abu Nujayh narrated it on the authority of Mujahid, as mentioned by Al-Nahhas. Muhammad Ibn Ishaq said in a long story: The defeated Sennacherib, the king of Babylon, came with six hundred thousand banners, under each banner were one hundred thousand horsemen. He encamped around Jerusalem, and God Almighty defeated him and killed all of them except Sennacherib and five of his scribes.
