The king of the Children of Israel, whose name was Siddiqah, sent in pursuit of Sennacherib, and he took with him the five, one of them Nebuchadnezzar, and he threw the mosques around their necks and paraded them around Jerusalem and Aelia for seventy days, giving them two loaves of barley every day for each man. Then he released them and they returned to Babylon. Then Sennacherib died after seven years, and Nebuchadnezzar succeeded him, and events escalated among the Children of Israel, and they made the forbidden permissible and killed their prophet Isaiah. Nebuchadnezzar came to them and entered Jerusalem with his soldiers and killed the Children of Israel until he annihilated them. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud said: The first corruption was the killing of Zechariah. Ibn Ishaq said: Their corruption the first time was killing the Shiites of the Prophet of God in the tree, because when their friend, the king, died, their affair was confused and they competed for the kingdom and killed each other without listening to their prophet, so God Almighty said to him, Stand among your people and inspire with your tongue. When he finished what God inspired him with, they attacked him to kill him, so he fled and a tree split open for him and he entered it, and Satan caught up with him and took a fringe of his garment and showed it to them, so they put a saw in the middle of it and sawed it until they cut it and cut him in the middle. Ibn Ishaq mentioned that some scholars told him that Zachariah died a death and was not killed, but rather the one killed was Isaiah. Saeed bin Jubair said about the words of God Almighty And We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they ravaged through the dwellings, that he is Sennacherib from the people of Nineveh in Mosul, the king of Babylon. This is contrary to what Ibn Ishaq said, and God knows best. It was also said that they were the Amalekites and they were infidels, as Al-Hasan said. The meaning of Jasaw is: they wreaked havoc and killed, and the same is true of Jasaw, Haasaw, and Dasaw, said by Ibn Aziz, and it is the saying of Al-Qutbi. Ibn Abbas read: Haasaw with a silent Ha. Abu Zaid said: Al-Haws, Al-Jaws, Al-Aws, and Al-Haws: wandering at night. Al-Jawhari said: Al-Jaws is the source of your saying Jasaw Khallal Al-Diyar, meaning they went through them and sought what was in them as a man wanders through the report, meaning he seeks it, and the same is true of Al-Ijtiyas. Al-Jawsan with a fat-ha is the night-flood, and it is the saying of Abu Ubaidah. Al-Tabari said: They wandered between the houses seeking them and killing them, going and coming, so he combined the saying of the linguists. Ibn Abbas said: They walked and went back and forth between the houses and dwellings. Al-Farraa said: They killed you between your houses, and he recited for Hassan: And among us is he who met the enemies with the sword of Muhammad, and with it he trampled the armies. Qatrib said: They came down. He said: We invaded their homes by force and destroyed their desert, binding them. And it was a promise that would be fulfilled, meaning a decree that would not be broken.
17:6: The Almighty said: Then We gave you back the upper hand over them meaning the state and the return, and that was when you repented and obeyed. Then it was said: That was by David killing Goliath or by killing someone else, according to the disagreement over who killed them. And We reinforced you with wealth and children until your situation returned to what it was. And We made you more numerous meaning more numerous and men than your enemy. The word nafir comes from nafar with a man from his clan. It is said: nafir and nafir like qadir and qadir. It is possible that nafir is the plural of nafar like kabab and ma'iz and ubayd. The poet said: So, Qahtaan is more honorable than his father and Himyar is more honorable than a group of people Meaning: After this first incident, they became more united and better off, as a reward from God Almighty for their return to obedience.
17:7: The Almighty says: If you do good, you do good for yourselves. That is, the benefit of your good deeds will return to you. And if you do evil, it is against her meaning it is upon her, like “Peace be upon you”, meaning peace be upon you. He said: Proudly slain by the hands and mouth That is, on the hands and on the mouth. At-Tabari said: The lam means to, meaning, if you do wrong, then to her, meaning, to her the wrongdoing will return, based on the Almighty’s saying: Because your Lord inspired her with the earthquake, meaning to her. It was also said: So she has the reward and punishment. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: So she has a Lord who forgives wrongdoing. Then it is possible that this was addressed to the Children of Israel at the beginning, meaning, you did wrong, so killing, captivity, and destruction befell you, then you did good, so the kingdom, supremacy, and order returned to you. And it is possible that this was addressed to the Children of Israel in the time of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning, you knew that your ancestors deserved punishment for disobedience, so expect the same. Or it is addressed to the polytheists of Quraysh in this way, so when the promise of the Hereafter comes from your corruption, that is, they killed John the son of Zakariya, peace be upon them, the second time, a king from the Children of Israel called Lakht killed him, as al-Qutbi said. Al-Tabari said: His name was Herod. He was mentioned in Al-Tarikh. He was forced to kill a woman named Azbal. Al-Suddi said: The king of the Children of Israel honored Yahya bin Rakriya and consulted him about the matter. The king consulted him about marrying the daughter of his wife, but he forbade him from her and said: She is not permissible for you. Her mother held a grudge against Yahya, peace be upon him. Then she dressed her daughter in fine red clothes, perfumed her, and sent her to the king while he was drinking. She ordered her to approach him, and if he wanted her, she would refuse until he gave her what she asked for. When he answered, she asked that the head of Yahya bin Zakariya be brought in a golden basin. She did that until the head of Yahya bin Zakariya was brought and the head was speaking until it was placed in front of him and he was saying: She is not permissible for you, but she is permissible for you. When morning came, his blood was boiling, so he threw dirt on it and it boiled over him. He continued throwing dirt on him until he reached the city wall while it was boiling. This was mentioned by Al-Tha’labi and others. Ibn Asakir Al-Hafiz mentioned in his history on the authority of Al-Hussein bin Ali, who said: There was a king among these kings who died and left behind his wife and daughter, and his brother inherited his kingdom. He wanted to marry his brother’s wife, so he consulted Yahya bin Zakariya about that, and the kings at that time acted according to the commands of the prophets. So he said to him: Do not marry her, for she is a prostitute. The woman realized that he had mentioned her and turned him away from her, so she said: Where is this from! Until she heard that it was from Yahya, so she said: Yahya will be killed or he will be removed from his kingdom. So she went to her daughter and made her, then she said: Go to your uncle in front of the assembly, for if he sees you he will call you and seat you in his lap, and say: Ask me whatever you want, for you will not ask me for anything except that I will give you. So when he says that to you, say: I ask only for the head of Yahya. He said: And if one of the kings spoke about something in front of the assembly and it did not go through, he would be stripped of his kingdom, so she did that. He said: So death came to him because he killed Yahya, and death came to him because he left his kingdom, so he chose his kingdom and killed him. He said: So the earth swallowed up her mother. Ibn Jud'an said: So I told this hadith to Ibn al-Musayyab, and he said: Did I not tell you how Zakariya was killed? I said: No. He said: When Zakariya killed his son, he ran away from them and they followed him until he came to a tree with a trunk. It called him to it and it folded over him, and a fringe of his garment remained that the winds blew. They went to the tree but did not find any trace of him after that, and they looked at that fringe, so they called for a saw and cut down the tree and cut him down with it. I said: It was mentioned in Al-Tabari’s Great History that Abu Al-Sa’ib told me that Abu Mu’awiyah told us on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Al-Munhal on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Jesus, son of Mary, sent John, son of Zakariya, with twelve of the disciples to teach the people. He said: Among the things they forbade them from was marrying their brother’s daughter. He said: Their king had a niece who pleased them… And he mentioned the story in its meaning. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: John, son of Zakariya, was sent with two of the disciples to teach the people. Among the things they taught them was forbidding them from marrying their sister’s daughter. Their king had a niece who pleased him, and he wanted to marry her. She had a need that he would fulfill every day. When her mother heard that they had forbidden marriage to their sister’s daughter, she said to her: When you enter upon the king and he says: Do you have a need, say: My need is that you slaughter John, son of Zakariya. He said: Ask me for something other than this! She said: I do not ask you for anything but this. When she refused, he called for a basin and slaughtered him. A drop of his blood dripped onto the ground and continued to boil until God sent Nebuchadnezzar against them. He made it up to himself to kill some of them for that blood until it subsided. So he killed seventy thousand of them for that blood. In another narration, seventy-five thousand. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It is the blood money of every prophet. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, I killed seventy thousand people with Yahya bin Zakariya, and if he fights with your daughter’s son, seventy thousand will fight. Sameer bin Atiyah said: Seventy prophets were killed on the rock in Jerusalem, including Yahya bin Zakariya. Zaid bin Waqid said: I saw the head of Yahya, peace be upon him, when they wanted to build the mosque of Damascus. It was taken out from under a corner of the dome next to the mihrab, facing east. His skin and hair were in the same condition, unchanged. Qura bin Khalid said: The sky did not weep for anyone except for Yahya bin Zakariya and Al-Hussein bin Ali, and its weeping made it red. Sufyan bin Uyaynah said: The son of Adam is most lonely in three situations: the day he was born, when he goes out to their home; the night he is raised with the dead, when he is surrounded by neighbors like he has never seen before; and the day he is resurrected, when he witnesses a scene like he has never seen before. God the Almighty said to Yahya in these three situations: Peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is resurrected alive. All of it is from the mentioned history and there is a difference of opinion about who was sent to them the last time, so it was said: Bukhtanasr. Al-Qushayri Abu al-Nasr said it, and he did not mention anyone else. Al-Suhayli said: This is not correct, because the killing of John was after the ascension of Jesus, and Bukhtanasr was a long time before Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon them, and before Alexander, and between Alexander and Jesus there were about three hundred years, but what was meant the other time was when they killed Isaiah, for Bukhtanasr was alive at that time, so he was the one who killed them and destroyed the Holy House and followed them to Egypt and expelled them from it. Al-Tha’labi said: And whoever narrated that Bukhtanasr was the one who invaded the Children of Israel when they killed John, son of Zakariya, then he made a mistake according to the people of biography and history because they agree that Bukhtanasr invaded the Children of Israel when they killed Isaiah and during the reign of Jeremiah. They said: From the era of Jeremiah and the destruction of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar to the birth of John the son of Zechariah, peace be upon them, is four hundred and sixty-one years. This is because they count from the era of the destruction of Jerusalem to its reconstruction during the reign of Kosk as seventy years, then from after its reconstruction to the appearance of Alexander in Jerusalem as eighty-eight years, then from after the reign of Alexander to the birth of John as three hundred and sixty-three years. I said: Al-Tabari mentioned all of it in his history, may God have mercy on him. Al-Tha’labi said: What is correct of that is what Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned when God raised Jesus from among them and they killed John. Some people say: When they killed Zachariah, God sent to them a king from the kings of Babylon called Khordos. He marched to them with the people of Babylon and appeared to them with bad luck. Then he said to the leader of his soldiers: I swore by my God that if God made me prevail over Jerusalem, I would kill them until their blood flowed in the midst of my army. He ordered that they be killed until that reached them. The leader entered Jerusalem and found boiling blood in it. He asked them and they said: The blood of a sacrifice that we offered but it was not accepted from us for eighty years. He said: You did not believe me. So seven hundred and seventy of their leaders were slaughtered over that blood, but it did not calm down. So seven hundred of their young men were brought and they were slaughtered over the blood, but it did not calm down. So he ordered seven thousand of their captives and their wives to be slaughtered over the blood, but it did not cool down. So he said: O Children of Israel, tell me the truth before I do not leave among you a fire-blower, whether female or male, except that I kill him. So when they saw the effort, they said: This is the blood of a prophet from among us who used to forbid us from many things that angered God, so we killed him. So this is his blood. His name was Yahya ibn Zakariya. He never disobeyed God for the blink of an eye, nor did he even think of disobeying Him. He said: Now you have believed me, and he fell down in prostration and then said: For such a thing He will take revenge on you, and he ordered the doors to be closed and said: Bring out whoever is here from the army of Khordos, and he was alone with the Children of Israel and said: O Prophet of God, O Yahya bin Zakariya, my Lord and your Lord knows what has befallen your people because of you, so calm down by God’s permission before I do not leave a single one of them. So the blood of Yahya bin Zakariya calmed down by God’s permission and the killing was lifted from them and he said: O Lord, I believe in what the Children of Israel believe in and I confirm it, so God Almighty revealed to one of the heads of the prophets: This leader is a true believer. Then he said, The enemy of God, Khordos, has ordered me to kill so many of you that your blood will flow in the midst of his army, and I will not disobey him. So he ordered them to dig a trench and ordered their wealth of camels, horses, mules, donkeys, cows, and sheep to be slaughtered until the blood flowed into the army. Then he ordered the dead who had been killed before that to be thrown onto the livestock he had killed. Then he turned away from them to Babylon, and he had almost annihilated the Children of Israel. I said: A long hadith has been reported in this chapter from the hadith of Hudhayfah, and we have written it in the book of the remembrance in parts in the chapters on the report of the Mahdi. We will mention from it here what clarifies the meaning of the verse and explains it so that there is no need for an explanation. Hudhayfah said: I said, O Messenger of God, the Holy House was great in the sight of God, of great importance and of great value. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is one of the most noble houses that God built for Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them, from gold, silver, pearls, rubies and emeralds. When Solomon, son of David, built it, God subjected the jinn to him, and they brought him gold and silver from the mines, and they brought him jewels, rubies and emeralds. God, the Most High, subjected the jinn to him until they built it from these kinds. Hudhayfah said: I said, O Messenger of God, how were these things taken from the Holy House? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Children of Israel disobeyed God and killed the prophets, God empowered over them Bukhtanasr, who was one of the Magians, and his kingdom lasted for seven hundred years. This is what God said: And when the first of the two promises came to pass, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they scoured through the dwellings. And it was a promise fulfilled. They entered Jerusalem, killed the men, took the women and children captive, and took the money and all that was in Jerusalem of these kinds, and loaded them on seventy thousand and one hundred thousand wagons until they deposited them in the land of Babylon. They continued to employ the Children of Israel and to rule them with shame, punishment and humiliation for a hundred years. Then God Almighty had mercy on them and inspired a king of the Persian kings to go to the Magians in the land of Babylon and to rescue those of the Children of Israel who were in their hands. So that king went to them until he entered the land of Babylon and rescued those who remained of the Children of Israel from the hands of the Magians and rescued that jewelry that was from Jerusalem and God returned it to him as it was the first time and said to them: O Children of Israel, if you return to sins, we will return to you with captivity and killing, and this is His saying: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you, but if you return, we will return. So when the Children of Israel returned to Jerusalem, they returned to sins, so God empowered the Roman king Caesar over them, and this is His saying: So when the promise of the Hereafter comes to pass, they will disfigure your faces and enter the temple as they entered it the first time and destroy with utter destruction what they had seized. He invaded them by land and sea, took them captive, killed them, and seized their wealth and women. He took the jewelry of all of Jerusalem and carried it on seventy thousand and one hundred thousand camels until he deposited it in the Church of Gold, where it is now until the Mahdi takes it and returns it to Jerusalem. It is a thousand and seven hundred ships that he will dock in Jaffa until it is transported to Jerusalem, and with it God will gather the first and the last... and he mentioned the hadith. God the Almighty said: So when the promise of the Hereafter comes meaning of the two times. The answer to if is omitted, meaning We sent them, indicated by We sent the first one to disfigure your faces, meaning by captivity and killing, so that the trace of sadness would appear on your faces. So lisawu is related to the omitted word, meaning We sent servants to do to you what would disfigure your faces. It was said: The faces are meant to humiliate them. Al-Kisa’i read linsu’u with a noon and a fatha on the hamza, a verb describing itself, most prominent, based on his saying: And We decreed, and We sent, and We returned. And something similar was narrated by Ali. And its confirmation is the reading of Abu linsu’un with a noon and a letter of emphasis. Abu Bakr, Al-A’mash, Ibn Waththab, Hamzah and Ibn ‘Amir read lisawu with a ya’ on the singular and a fatha on the hamza. It has two interpretations: one of them is God disfigures your faces, and the second is Lisu’u wa’d wajjukum. The rest read lisawu with a ya’ and a damma on the hamza on the plural, meaning So that the servants who are men of great power may disfigure your faces. And let them enter the mosque as they entered it the first time and let them be destroyed. That is, let them destroy and perish. Qatrib said: let them demolish. The poet said: People are only two workers: one worker builds what he builds and the other raises it. They did not prevail means they overcame it from your country totally.
17:8: The Almighty said: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you. This is what they informed about in their book. And perhaps is a promise from God that He will remove their punishment, and perhaps from God it is obligatory. To have mercy upon you after taking revenge on you, and that is how it was, so their number increased and He made kings from them. And if you return, We will return. Qatada said: So they returned, so God sent Muhammad, peace be upon him, to them, so they pay the jizyah with humiliation, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas. This is contrary to what you have mentioned before in the hadith and elsewhere. Al-Qushayri said: The punishment came upon the Children of Israel twice at the hands of the disbelievers, and once at the hands of the Muslims. This was when they returned, so God returned to them. Based on this, the statement of Qatada is correct. And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers, meaning a confinement and a prison, from the word hasr, which means confinement. Al-Jawhari said: It is said that he confined him, he confined him, a mat, meaning he made it tight for him and surrounded him. And the mat is the narrow, miserly person. Al-Hasir: the barriah. Al-Hasir: the side. Al-Asma’i said: It is what is between the vein that appears on the side of the camel and horse, transverse and above it, to the end of the side. Al-Hasir: the king, because it is veiled. Labid said: And the flasks of the necks were overcome as if they were jinn standing at the door of the mat It is narrated: And the position of the necks was overcome. So that ghalab is a substitute for maqama, as if he said: And the Lord of the necks. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah:...at the end of the mat That is, at the edge of the rug, by Al-Nu'man bin Mundhir. The mat is the confinement. God Almighty said: And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers. Al-Qushayri said: The one who spreads out is called a mat, because some mats are woven on top of each other. Al-Hasan said: That is, a mattress and a cradle. He went to the mat that is spread out, because the Arabs call a small rug a mat. Al-Tha'labi said: This is a good interpretation.
17:9: The Almighty said: Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright. When He mentioned the Ascension, He mentioned what was decreed for the Children of Israel, and that was an indication of the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then He explained that the Book that God revealed to him was a cause of guidance. The meaning of to that which is most upright is the path that is most sound, most just, and most correct. So that is an adjective for an omitted description, meaning the path to a stronger text. Al-Zajjaj said: for the state that is most upright, which is the oneness of God and belief in His messengers. This was said by Al-Kalbi and Al-Farraa. God Almighty says: And He gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds. It was mentioned earlier. That they will have means that they will have a great reward meaning Paradise.
17:10: And those who do not believe in the Hereafter meaning, He gives them good tidings that their enemies will be punished. The Qur’an is mostly promise and threat. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: And He gives good tidings with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the shin. It has been mentioned.
17:11: God Almighty says: And man invokes evil as he invokes good. Ibn Abbas and his counterpart said: It is a man’s supplication against himself and his children when he is annoyed with something he does not want to be answered: O God, destroy him, and the like. God His supplication for well-being is like his supplication to his Lord to grant him well-being. If God answered his supplication for evil against himself, he would perish, but by His grace, He does not answer him in that regard. Similar to this is: And if God were to hasten evil for the people as they hasten good. This has already been mentioned. It was also said that it was revealed about Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith. He used to supplicate and say: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. It was also said that it means to supplicate for what is forbidden as one supplicates for what is permissible. The poet, Ibn Jami’, said: I circumambulate the House with those who circumambulate, and I lift up my lower garment I prostrate at night until morning and recite from the decisive revelation May the one who relieves Joseph’s distress make the owner of the litter available to me. Al-Jawhari said: It is said of someone that he is a majlis council, meaning he is relied upon. A majlis is also one of the majlis of the pilgrims. A majlis is an example of a cauldron: a sword strap. The waw is omitted from wa-yad'u insan in pronunciation and luck, but it is not omitted in meaning because its position is nominative, so it was omitted because it precedes a silent lam, like the verse of God the Almighty: {We will call the guardians, and God will blot out falsehood. And God will give the believers. The crier will call, but what good are the warnings?} (Al-Jawhari 13:19), meaning that haste is his nature, so he is quick to ask for evil as he is quick to ask for good. It was said that he referred to Adam, peace be upon him, when he stood up before the soul was fully implanted in him. Salman said: The first thing that God created of Adam was his head, so He began to watch while He created his body. When it was the time of the afternoon, his legs remained and the soul had not been breathed into them, so he said: O Lord, hasten before nightfall. This is why He said: {And man is impatient.} Ibn Abbas said: When the trumpet blast reached his navel, he looked at his body and tried to stand up but was unable to, this is why He said: {And man is impatient.} Ibn Masoud said: When the spirit entered his eyes, he looked at the fruits of Paradise. When it entered his stomach, he desired food, so he jumped up, before the spirit reached his feet, in haste, to the fruits of Paradise. That is when he says, Man was created in haste, as Al-Bayhaqi mentioned. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God created Adam in Paradise, He left him as long as God willed. Then Satan circled around him to see what he was like. When he saw that he was hollow, he knew that he had been created in a way that could not control himself. It was said that he, peace be upon him, was handed over as a captive to Sawda. He groaned all night, so she asked him, and he said, I groan because of the severity of my stature and captivity. So she let go of his shoulders, and when she slept, he ran away. She informed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and he said, May God cut off your hand. When morning came, she was expecting the calamity, so he, peace be upon him, said, I asked God Almighty to make my supplication for those of my family who do not deserve mercy, because I am a human being who gets angry as humans get angry. Then the verse was revealed. This was mentioned by Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr, may God have mercy on him. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, he said, “I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say: O God, Muhammad is only a human being who gets angry as other humans get angry. I have made a covenant with You that You will not break. So any believer whom I have harmed, insulted, or flogged, make it an expiation for him and a means of drawing him closer to You on the Day of Resurrection. There are narrations on this topic from Aisha and Jabir. It was said that the meaning of “and mankind is hasty” is that he prefers the immediate, even if it is little, over the deferred, even if it is great.
17:12: The Almighty says: And We have made the night and the day two signs meaning, two indications of Our Oneness, Our existence, and the perfection of Our knowledge and power. The sign in them is: the approach of each one of them from where He does not know, and its turning away to where He does not know. The decrease of one with the increase of the other and vice versa is also a sign. Likewise, the light of day and the darkness of night. This has already been mentioned, We erased the sign of the night, and He did not say, We erased the night. So when He added the sign to the night and the day, it indicates that the two signs mentioned belong to them, not to them. And erased means obliterated. In the hadith, it is mentioned that God the Almighty commanded Gabriel, peace be upon him, to place his wing over the face of the moon, obliterating its light. It was like the sun in light, and the blackness that is seen in the moon is a result of the obliteration. Ibn Abbas said: God made the sun seventy parts and the moon seventy parts, so He erased sixty-nine parts of the moon's light and made it with the light of the sun. So the sun has one hundred and thirty-nine parts and the moon has one part. It was also narrated from him: “God created two suns from the light of His throne. He made what He previously knew would be a sun, like the world according to its measure between its easts and its wests. He made the moon less than the sun. He sent Gabriel, peace be upon him, and he commanded his wing over his face three times, while on that day it was a sun. Its light was obliterated and its light remained. The blackness that you see on the moon is the effect of erasure. If you saw a sun, you would not know night from day.” The first was mentioned by Al-Tha’labi and the second by Al-Mahdawi, and it will come with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ali may God be pleased with him and Qatadah said: What is meant by erasure is the black spot on the moon, so that the light of the moon would be less than the light of the sun, thus distinguishing night from day. And We made the sign of the day seeing means We made its sun illuminating for the eyes. Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala’ said: That is, one can see with it. Al-Kisa’i said: It is from the Arabs’ saying absara’ an-nahar if it shines and becomes in a state that one can see with. It was said: It is like their saying khabith mukhbath if its companions are wicked. And a man is weak if his animals are weak, so is the day seeing if his people are seeing. So that you may seek bounty from your Lord. He means to manage your livelihood. And he did not mention rest at night, as what was mentioned in the day was sufficient. And he said in another place: It is He who made for you the night that you may rest therein and the day seeing. And that you may know the number of years and the account. That is, if He had not done that, night would not have been distinguished from day, nor would account and count be known. And everything We have explained in detail, that is, from the rulings of obligation, and it is like His saying: an explanation of everything. We have not neglected anything in the Book. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God completed His creation, and none of His creation remained except Adam, He created a sun from the light of His throne and a moon, and they were both two suns. As for that which was in God’s foreknowledge to leave as a sun, He created it like the world between its east and its west. As for that which was in God’s foreknowledge to create as a moon, He created it smaller than the sun in size, but their smallness is only seen in the extreme height of the sky and their distance from the earth. If God had left the sun and moon as He created them, night would not have been known from day, nor would the worker know how long he would work, nor the fasting person how long he would fast, nor would the woman know how to observe her waiting period, nor would she know the times of prayers and pilgrimage, nor would debts be due, nor when they sow and plant, nor when they would rest for their bodies. It is as if God looked at His servants, and He is more merciful to them than they are to themselves, so He sent Gabriel, who commanded his wing to fly over the face of the moon three times, while it was a sun at that time. The light was extinguished from it, and the light remained in it. This is what He said: And We have made the night and the day two signs. The verse.
17:13: His saying, the Most High: And every man We have fastened his fate to his neck. Al-Zajjaj said: The mention of the neck is an expression for adherence, just as a necklace adheres to the neck. Ibn Abbas said: His fate is his deeds and what has been decreed for him of good and evil, and it accompanies him wherever he is. Muqatil Al-Kalbi said: His good and evil are together and will not leave him until he is held accountable for it. Mujahid said: His deeds and his provision. It was narrated from him that no child is born except that around his neck is a piece of paper on which is written whether he is wretched or blessed. Al-Hasan said: We have fastened his fate to him, meaning his wretchedness and happiness, and what has been decreed for him of good or evil and what has been decreed for him from destiny, meaning it was given to him at the time of division in eternity. It was said that what was meant by this is obligation, meaning We have decreed for him the obligation of the Shari’ah, and it is such that if he wanted to do what he was commanded to do and refrain from what he was forbidden from doing, he could do so. And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread wide open. Meaning, the book of his fate which is around his neck. Al-Hasan, Abu Raja’ and Mujahid read: Tayyiru without an alif. This is what was narrated in the hadith: O God, there is no good except Your good, no omen except Your omen, and no lord except You. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ban Muhaisin, Abu Ja`far, and Ya`qub read it with a fat-ha on the ya` and a damma on the ra`, meaning, And the bird will bring forth for him a book. So, a book is in the accusative case as a state. It is possible that the meaning is, And a bird will come forth and become a book. Yahya ibn Waththab read it with a damma on the ya` and a kasra on the ra`, and it was narrated from Mujahid, meaning, God will bring forth. Shaybah and Muhammad ibn Al-Sumai` read it, and it was also narrated from Abu Ja`far, And he will come forth with a damma on the ya` and a fat-ha on the ra`, as a passive verb, meaning, And the bird will bring forth for him a book. The rest read it with a damma on the noon and a kasra on the ra`, meaning, And We will bring forth. Abu `Amr supported this reading by saying, We have obliged him. Abu Ja`far, Al-Hasan, and Ibn `Amir read it with a damma on the ya`, a fat-ha on the lam, and a shaddah on the qaf, meaning, It will be given to him. The rest read it with a fat-ha on the ya`, meaning, He will see it spread out. He said, Manshuran is hastening the good report for the good report and the rebuke for the bad. Abu Al-Sar Al-Adawi said, and he recited this verse, And We have fastened every person’s bird to his neck. He said, “They are two spreads and a fold. As for what I live, O son of Adam, it is your spread-out record, so hope in it as you wish. When you die, it is folded, and when you are resurrected, it is spread out.”
17:14: Read your book. Al-Hasan said: A person reads his book, whether he is illiterate or not. Your own soul is sufficient as a judge against you today. One of the righteous said: This is a book, your tongue is its pen, your saliva is its ink, and your limbs are its paper. If you dictate to your memorizers, nothing will be added to it or taken away from it. Whenever you deny something in it, it will be your witness against you. God
17:15: The Almighty says: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] himself, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own detriment. That is, each person will be held accountable for himself, not for others. So whoever is guided, the reward for his guidance is his, and whoever goes astray, the punishment for his disbelief is upon him. And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another. This was mentioned in Al-An'am. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, he said to the people of Mecca: Follow me and disbelieve in Muhammad and I will bear your burdens, so this verse was revealed, meaning that Al-Walid will not bear your sins, but the sin of each one of them is upon him. It is said: Wazar yazra wazran wazra meaning sin. Wazr is a heavy weight, the plural is awzar, and from this it is derived that they carry their burdens on their backs, meaning the weights of their sins. He has been burdened if he carries, so he is a wazir, and from this is the word wazir minister of the sultan who carries the weight of his state. The letter ha’ in his statement is a metaphor for the soul, meaning that a sinful soul will not be held accountable for the sin of another, to the point that a mother will meet her son on the Day of Resurrection and say, O my son! Was not my lap a comforter for you? Was not my breast a drink for you? Was not my belly a vessel for you? Yes, O mother! She will say, O my son! My sins have weighed me down, so bear one sin from them! He will say, Go away from me, O mother! For I am busy with my sin today, away from you. Question: Aisha may God be pleased with her cited this verse in response to Ibn Umar when he said: The dead is tormented by the crying of his family. Our scholars said: She was led to do that because she did not hear it, and it contradicts the verse. There is no reason to deny it, as the narrators of this meaning are many, such as Umar and his son, Al-Mughira bin Shu’bah, and Qayla bint Mukhrama, and they are certain of the narration. So there is no reason to make a mistake in their narration. There is no contradiction between the verse and the hadith, which is interpreted as if wailing was part of the will of the dead and his custom, as the pre-Islamic era used to do, to the point that Tarafa said: If I die, mourn me as I deserve, and make my pockets heavy, O daughter of Ma'bad. And he said: Until the year, then peace be upon you both, and whoever cries for a whole year has apologized Al-Bukhari tended towards this. A group of scholars, including Dawud, believed in the apparent meaning of the hadith, and that he was only being punished for their wailing, because he neglected to forbid them from it before his death and to discipline them with it. So he was being punished for his negligence in that, and for abandoning what God commanded him to do, saying: Protect yourselves and your families from a Fire. Not for any sin other than that, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: And We never punish until We have sent a messenger. That is, We did not leave creation in vain, but We sent messengers. This is evidence that rulings are not established except by the Shari’ah, contrary to the Mu’tazilah who say that reason judges what is bad and good, permits and prohibits. This has been discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah. The majority are of the opinion that this applies to this worldly life, that is, God does not destroy a nation with a punishment except after sending them a message and warning. A group said: This is general in this world and the hereafter, based on God the Almighty’s statement: Every time a group is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, ‘Did there not come to you a warner?’ They will say, ‘Yes, there did come to us.’ Ibn Atiyyah said: What is supported by the view is that Adam’s mission with monotheism and spreading beliefs among his children, along with establishing evidence indicating the Creator, along with sound nature, obligated everyone in the world to believe and follow God’s Shari’ah. Then this was renewed in the time of Noah after the disbelievers drowned. This verse also gives the possibility of its wording in this way regarding those to whom no message reached, and they are the people of the intervals whose existence has been estimated by some scholars. As for what was narrated that God the Almighty will send to them on the Day of Resurrection and to the insane and the children, this is an unsound hadith, and it does not require what the Shariah gives that the Hereafter is not a place of obligation. Al-Mahdawi said: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that God the Almighty will send on the Day of Resurrection a messenger to the people of the interval and the mute, the deaf and the dumb, and those among them who wanted to obey him in this world will obey him, and he recited the verse, narrated by Muammar on the authority of Ibn Tawus on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Hurairah, mentioned by Al-Nahhas. I said: This is suspended, and it will come with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet at the end of Surat Taha, God willing. It is not correct, and some people have used as evidence that if the people of Algeria hear about Islam and believe, then there is no obligation on them in the past, and this is correct. And whoever the call has not reached is not deserving of punishment from the perspective of reason, and God knows best.
17:16: There are three issues: First: God Almighty informed us in the previous verse that He did not destroy the cities before sending the messengers, not because it would be ugly for Him to do so, but because it was a promise from Him, and He does not break His promise. So if He wanted to destroy a city while fulfilling His promise as God Almighty said, He would command its affluent people to commit sin and injustice therein, so the word of destruction would come true for it. This teaches you that whoever perishes perishes by His will, for He is the One who causes the causes and leads them to their ends so that the previous word from God Almighty would come true. The second: The Almighty’s saying: We have commanded. Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, Abu Raja’, Abu al-Aaliyah, al-Rabi’, Mujahid and al-Hasan read We have commanded with a shaddah, and it is the reading of Ali, may God be pleased with him, meaning We have given power to its wicked ones, so they disobeyed therein, and if they did that, We will destroy them. Abu Uthman al-Nahdi said We have commanded with a shaddah on the mim, meaning We made them rulers and rulers, and Ibn Aziz said the same. And He commanded them means He has power over them. And al-Hasan also read Qatadah, and Abu Haywah al-Shami, and Ya’qub and Kharijah from Nafi’ and Hammad ibn Salamah from Ibn Kathir and Ali and Ibn Abbas with differences from them We have commanded with a long vowel and a light vowel, meaning We have increased its tyrants and rulers, al-Kisa’i said. Abu Ubaidah said: I commanded him with a long vowel and I commanded him, two languages meaning I made him many, and from it is the hadith: The best wealth is a mare that is commanded or a well-trodden path, meaning one that produces many offspring and offspring. Ibn Aziz also said: Amarna and Amrna have the same meaning, meaning much of us. Also on the authority of Al-Hasan and Yahya bin Muammar, Amarna with the short vowel and the kasra on the fa’lana, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Qatada and Al-Hasan said: The meaning is much of us. Abu Zaid and Abu Ubaid narrated something similar, but Al-Kisa’i rejected it and said: It is not said of abundance except “Amarna with the long vowel. He said: Its origin is Amarna but it was shortened, narrated by Al-Mahdawi. In Al-Sahah: Abu Al-Hasan said: Amar malhu with the short vowel means it became abundant. And Amar al-Qawm means they became numerous. The poet said: Some people do not inherit the share of Qad’ad. And God commanded what God commanded with extension. Al-Tha’labi: And it is said for a lot of things, and the verb from it is: the people commanded something if they became many. Ibn Mas’ud said: We used to say in the pre-Islamic era for a tribe if they became many: the command of the Banu so-and-so, Labid said: All the free people have a fate, no matter how many you count. If they are envied, they will be lowered, and if they are commanded one day, they will be destroyed and miserable. I said: In the hadith of Heraclius, the authentic hadith: The command of Ibn Abi Kabshah has been ordered, indeed the king of the yellow people fears him, meaning he has become numerous. And all of it is intransitive, and that is why Al-Kisa’i rejected it, and God knows best. Al-Mahdawi said: Whoever reads amar it is a language, and the reason for the transitivity of amar is that he likened it to Umar in that the majority was the closest thing to the building, so a number is like a number of Umar. The rest of them are from amr, meaning we ordered them to obey as an excuse, warning, intimidation, and threat. So they rebelled, meaning they disobeyed us. So the word was made true upon them, so the threat became obligatory upon them, from Ibn Abbas. And it was said: We ordered them, we made them emirs, because the Arabs say: an emir who is not commanded, meaning not commanded. And it was said: its meaning is we sent its arrogant ones. Harun said: And it is the reading of Abu we sent the greatest criminals among them, so they rebelled. Al-Mawardi mentioned it. Copper fever: Aaron said in the reading of Abu: And when We desire to destroy a city, We send therein its greatest criminals, and they plot therein, so the word comes into effect upon it. It is permissible that Our command means We multiplied it, and from this is the best of wealth, a mare that is commanded, as mentioned above. And some people said: Commanded follows a mare that is destroyed, like the mornings and evenings. And like His saying: Return, visited, not turned back. And based on this, it is not said: God commanded them in the sense of He multiplied them, rather it is said His command and His command. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose the reading of the general public. Abu Ubaid said: We chose Our command because the three meanings come together in it: command, emirate, and multitude. And the luxurious: the pampered, and they were singled out for the command because others follow them. The third is the Almighty’s saying: So We destroyed it. That is, We uprooted it through destruction. Destruction is mentioned as a source to exaggerate the torment that befell them. In the Sahih, in the hadith of Zaynab bint Jahsh, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out one day, frightened, his face red, saying: ‘There is no god but God. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today a hole has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this.’ And he made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it. She said: ‘So I said, O Messenger of God, will we be destroyed while there are righteous people among us?’ He said: ‘Yes, if evil increases.’” We have already discussed this matter, and that if sins become apparent and are not changed, they are a cause of the destruction of all, and God knows best.
17:17: The Almighty says: And how many generations have We destroyed after Noah. That is, how many people disbelieved and were destroyed. He is frightening the disbelievers of Mecca. The mention of the generation has already been mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-An'am. Praise be to God. And sufficient is your Lord, concerning the sins of His servants, as Knower and Seeer. Knowing and All-Knowing of them, He sees their deeds. This has already been mentioned.
17:18: The Almighty said: Whoever desires the immediate meaning this world, and what is meant is the immediate abode, so He used the adjective to describe the described. We hasten for him therein what We will for whomever We will meaning We do not give him from it except what We will, then We hold him accountable for his deeds, and his consequence is entering the Fire. Blameable and rejected meaning expelled and banished from the mercy of God. This is the description of the immoral hypocrites and the hypocritical hypocrites, who dress up as Muslims and obey in order to obtain the immediate worldly gains of spoils and other things, but that work will not be accepted from them in the Hereafter, and they will not be given in this world any spoils or other things, so that work will not be accepted from them in the Hereafter, and they will not be given in this world except what is allotted to them. It was mentioned earlier in Hud that this verse indicates those absolute verses, so reflect on it.
17:19: And whoever desires the Hereafter meaning the Hereafter. And strives for it with the necessary effort meaning he does acts of obedience for it. And he is a believer because acts of obedience are not accepted except from a believer. Then those, their effort will be appreciated meaning accepted and not rejected. It was said: Multiplied meaning their good deeds will be multiplied to ten, to seventy, to seven hundred times, and to many times over, as was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah when it was said to him: Did you hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God rewards for a single good deed with a thousand thousand good deeds? He said: “I heard him say: ‘God rewards for a single good deed with a thousand thousand good deeds.’”
17:20: The Almighty says: To both We provide from the bounty of your Lord. I know that He provides for the believers and the disbelievers. And the bounty of your Lord is not restricted. That is, it is withheld and forbidden, from the root word prohibition, which means prohibition and prohibition.
17:21: Then the Almighty said: See how We have favored some of them over others in provision and work, some are few and some are many. And the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference meaning for the believers, so the disbeliever, even if he is given plenty in this world once, and the believer is given little once, the Hereafter is only divided once by their deeds, so whoever misses something from it will not make it up in it.
17:22: And His saying, Do not make with God another god is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation. It was said that the address is to the human being, so you will sit down meaning you will remain blamed and forsaken with no supporter or guardian.
17:23: It contains sixteen issues: The first is wa-qada meaning he ordered, obligated, and made obligatory. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah said: This is not a judgment of a ruling, but rather a judgment of an order. In the Mushaf of Ibn Mas`ud it is wa-sā’ī which is the reading of his companions and the reading of Ibn Abbas as well, and Ali and others, and it is also with Ubayy ibn Ka`b. Ibn Abbas said: It is wa-sā’ī rabbik and one of the two waws was attached so it was read wa-qada’ī rabbik because if it were about the judgment no one would have disobeyed God. Ad-Dahhak said: It was corrupted for some people to wa-sā’ī because the waw and the sad were mixed when the Mushaf was written. Abu Hatim mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas the same as what Ad-Dahhak said and said: On the authority of Maymun ibn Mihran that he said: According to the statement of Ibn Abbas, there is light, God the Most High said: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you (Al-Nisa’ 1:10). Abu Hatim refused that Ibn Abbas had said that. He said: If we said this, the heretics would have attacked our Qur’an. Then our scholars, theologians, and others said that the word qada is used in the language in several ways: qada means command, as in the saying of God the Almighty: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him meaning a command. Qada means creation, as in the saying of God the Almighty: Then He completed them as seven heavens in two days meaning He created them. Qada means judgment, as in the saying of God the Almighty: Then decide what you will decide meaning rule as you rule. Qada means completion, as in the saying of God the Almighty: The matter about which you are asking has been decided meaning it has been completed. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: So when you have completed your rites and His saying the Almighty: So when you have completed the prayer and Qada means will, as in the saying of God the Almighty: When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is and Qada means covenant, as in the saying of God the Almighty: And you were not on the western side when We decreed the matter to Moses If the decree can bear these meanings, then it is not permissible to say that sins are by the decree of God, because if what is meant by it is a command, then there is no disagreement that this is not permissible, because God Almighty did not command them, as He does not command immorality. Zakariya bin Salam said: A man came to Al-Hasan and said that he had divorced his wife three times. He said: You have disobeyed your Lord and she has separated from you. The man said: God has decreed that upon me! Al-Hasan, who was eloquent, said: God has not decreed that! That is, God has not commanded it, and he recited this verse: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him. Second: God Almighty commanded us to worship Him and make Him One, and He made being dutiful to parents connected to that, just as He connected thanking them with thanking Him, saying: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment. And He said, “Be grateful to Me and to your children. To Me is the final destination.” And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abdullah, he said: I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which deed is most beloved to God Almighty? He said: Praying on time. He said: Then what? He said: Then being kind to one’s parents. He said: Then what? He said: Jihad in the way of God. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informed us that being kind to one’s parents is the best of deeds after prayer, which is the greatest pillar of Islam. He arranged that with then, which gives order and time. Third: Part of being dutiful and kind to them is not to insult them or disobey them, because that is a major sin without dispute. This is what was stated in the established Sunnah. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Among the major sins is a man insulting his parents. They said: O Messenger of God, does a man insult his parents? He And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age with you, say not to them a word of contempt, nor repel them but speak to them a generous word. said: Yes, a man insults a man’s father in return for insulting his father, or insults his mother in return for insulting his mother. Fourth: Disobeying parents is opposing their permissible purposes, just as being dutiful to them is agreeing with their purposes. Accordingly, if that command is not a sin, even if that command is permissible in its essence, and likewise if it is recommended. Some people have said that commanding them to do what is permissible makes it recommended for the child, and commanding them to do what is recommended increases its emphasis in its recommendation. Fifth: Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar, who said: I had a wife whom I loved, but my father hated her and ordered me to divorce her, but I refused. I mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: O Abdullah ibn Umar, divorce your wife. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Sixth: Al-Sahih narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Who is most deserving of my good companionship? He said: Your mother. He said: Then who? He said: Your mother. He said: Then who? He said: Your mother. He said: Then who? He said: Your father. This hadeeth indicates that the love and compassion for the mother should be three times the love for the father, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned the mother three times and mentioned the father only the fourth time. If this meaning is understood, it will be confirmed by the eye. This is because the difficulty of pregnancy, the difficulty of childbirth, and the difficulty of breastfeeding and raising children are unique to the mother, not the father. These are three positions that the father is absent from. It was narrated from Malik that a man said to him: My father is in the land of the blacks, and he has written to me to come to him, but my mother prevents me from doing so. He said to him: Obey your father, but do not disobey your mother. Malik’s statement indicates that dutifulness to her is equal in his view. Al-Layth was asked about this issue, and he ordered him to obey the mother, and he claimed that she deserves two-thirds of dutifulness. The hadeeth of Abu Hurayrah indicates that she deserves three-quarters of dutifulness, and it is the proof against those who disagree. Al-Muhasibi claimed in his book Al-Ri’ayah that there is no disagreement among scholars that the mother has three-quarters of righteousness and the father has one-quarter, based on the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him. And God knows best. Seventh: Honoring one’s parents does not only mean that they are Muslims. Rather, if they are unbelievers, one should honor them and be good to them if there is a covenant with them. God Almighty said: God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them. And in Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Asma’, she said: My mother came while she was a polytheist during the time of the Quraysh and their period when they made a treaty with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with her father. So I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My mother came and she is desirous, should I maintain ties with her? He said: Yes, maintain ties with your mother. It was also narrated on the authority of Asma’ who said: My mother came to me desirous during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, should I maintain ties with her? He said: Yes. Ban ‘Uyaynah said: Then God Almighty revealed about her: God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion. The first is suspended and the second is connected. Eighth: It is part of being kind and righteous to them if jihad is not required, not to fight except with their permission. It was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asking his permission to go to jihad. He said: Are your parents alive? He said: Yes. He said: Then strive in jihad for them. The wording of Muslim is not in Sahih Muslim. He said: Yes, and I left them crying. He said: Go and make them laugh as you made them cry. In another report, he said: Sleeping with your parents on their bed while they laugh and play with you is better for you than striving with me. This was mentioned by Ibn Khuwayr Mandad. The wording of Al-Bukhari in the Book of Honoring Parents: Abu Nu`aym told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to pledge allegiance to him for emigration, and he left his parents crying. He said: Go back to them and make them laugh as you made them cry. Ibn al-Mundhir said: In this hadith is the prohibition of going out without the permission of the parents unless the mobilization takes place. When it does take place, then going out becomes obligatory for everyone. This is clear in the hadith of Abu Qatada that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent out the army of the princes..., and he mentioned the story of Zaid bin Haritha, Ja`far bin Abi Talib, and Ibn Rawahah, and that the crier of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called after that: The prayer is congregational. So the people gathered and he praised God and thanked Him, then he said: O people, go out and support your brothers and let no one stay behind. So the people went out on foot and on horseback in intense heat. His saying, Go out and support your brothers, indicates that the excuse for staying behind from jihad is only if the call to prayer has not taken place, along with his saying, peace be upon him. If you are called to arms, then go forth. I said: In these hadiths there is evidence that when the obligatory or recommended actions are combined, the most important of them should be given precedence. This accounting meaning has been fully explained in the book Al-Ri’ayah. Ninth: They differed regarding the polytheist parents. Is it permissible for him to go out with their permission if jihad is a communal obligation? Al-Thawri used to say: He should not go out to fight except with their permission. Al-Shafi’i said: He can go out to fight without their permission. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The grandfathers are fathers and the grandmothers are mothers, so a person should not go out to fight except with their permission. I do not know of any evidence that requires this for other brothers and other relatives. Tawus used to consider striving for sisters to be better than jihad in the way of God, the Almighty. Tenth: Part of being dutiful to them is maintaining ties with those who love them. In Sahih, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: One of the most pious acts of piety is for a man to maintain ties with his father after his death. Abu Usaid, who was a Badri, narrated that he said: I was sitting with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when a man from the Ansar came and said: O Messenger of God, is there anything left to be done to show kindness to my parents after their death? He said: Yes. Praying for them, asking forgiveness for them, fulfilling their covenant after their death, honoring their friends, and maintaining ties of kinship for which you have no kinship except through them. This is what is left for you to do. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to give gifts to Khadija’s friends out of kindness and loyalty to her, she being his wife. So what do you think of your parents? Eleventh: The Almighty’s statement: If one or both of them reach old age with you Al-Baqarah 1:118. He specified the state of old age because it is the state in which they need His kindness due to the change in their situation with weakness and old age. So He obligated in this state to take into account their conditions more than He obligated before, because in this state they have become a burden on Him, so they need Him to fulfill from them in old age what they needed from Him in their youth. Therefore, He mentioned this state specifically. Also, a person’s long stay usually causes him to become burdened and boredom occurs and impatience increases, so he shows his anger towards his parents and his veins swell for them, and he becomes ungrateful towards them with the evidence of his sonship and lack of religion. The least of what is disliked is what he shows with his hesitant breathing out of impatience. He was commanded to meet them with words described as honorable, and they are free from every defect, so He said: And do not say to them a word of disrespect, nor repel them, but speak to them words of honor. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In spite of his nose, in spite of his nose. It was said: O Messenger of God? He said: Whoever finds his parents in old age, one or both of them, and does not enter Paradise. Al-Bukhari said in the Book of Honoring Parents: Musaddad told us, Barr bin al-Mufaddal told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: In the dust of a man who is mentioned in my presence and does not send blessings upon me. In the dust of a man who finds his parents in old age, or one of them, and they do not admit him into Paradise. In the dust of a man who enters Ramadan and then it passes before he is forgiven. Ibn Abi Uways told us, my brother told me, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Bilal, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Hilal, on the authority of Sa`d ibn Ishaq ibn Ka`b ibn `Ujrah al-Salami, on the authority of his father, may God be pleased with him, who said: Ka`b ibn `Ujrah, may God be pleased with him, said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They brought Al-Munir, and when he came out, he ascended to the pulpit. He ascended the first step and said, Ameen. Then he ascended the second and said, Ameen. Then when he ascended the third, he said, Ameen. When he finished and came down from the pulpit, we said, O Messenger of God, we heard from you today something we did not hear from you before. He said, And did you hear it? We said, Yes. He said, “Gabriel, peace be upon him, interrupted and said, ‘After him who witnessed Ramadan and was not forgiven. ’ So I said, “Ameen.” When I ascended the second step, he said, ‘After him who was mentioned in your presence and did not send blessings upon you. ’ I said, Ameen. When I ascended the third step, he said, ‘After him who witnessed his parents reaching old age, or one of them, and they did not admit him to Paradise. ’ I said, Ameen. Abu Nu`aym narrated to us, Salamah ibn Wardan narrated to us, I heard Anas, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit one step and said, Amen. Then he ascended a third step and said, Amen. Then he sat up and sat down. His companions said, O Messenger of God, on what do you believe? He said, “Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me and said, ‘May the nose of the one in whose presence you are mentioned be rubbed in the dust and who does not send blessings upon you.’ So I said, ‘Amen. May the nose of the one who has one or both of his parents alive and does not enter Paradise be rubbed in the dust.’ So I said, ‘Amen.’” The hadith. Happy is he who seizes the opportunity to be dutiful to them, lest he miss out on it with their death and regret it. Miserable is he who is chaste with them, especially he who is commanded to be dutiful to them. And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age with you, say not to them a word of contempt, nor repel them but speak to them a generous word. Twelfth: The Almighty said: And do not say to them so much as ‘uff.’ That is, do not say to them anything that would show the slightest disgust. On the authority of Abu Raja’ al-Attardi, he said: Uff is foul, obscene, and hidden speech. Mujahid said: Its meaning is that if you see from them in an old state the excrement and urine that they saw from you when you were young, do not find them disgusting and say ‘uff.’ The verse is more general than this. ‘Uff’ and ‘taff’ are the dirt of the nails. And it is said for everything that is annoying and burdensome: ‘Uff to him.’ Al-Azhari said: ‘Taff’ also refers to something insignificant. ‘Uff’ is read with a lowered tanween, just as sounds are lowered and given a tanween, as you say: ‘Shhh and mah.’ There are ten languages for it: ‘Uff, ‘Uff, ‘Uff, ‘Uff and ‘Uff, ‘Uff, ‘Uff, ‘Uff for you’ with a kasra over the hamza, ‘Uff with a damma over the hamza and a sukoon over the fa’, and ‘Uff with a light fa’. In the hadith: Then he threw the edge of his garment over his nose and said, Uff, uf. Abu Bakr said, Its meaning is to be proud of what he smelled. Some of them said, “The meaning of ‘uf’ is to despise and belittle. It is taken from ‘af’ which means little.” Al-Qutbi said, “Its origin is to blow something up and it falls on you from someone who threw it, or dust or something else. And for a place you want to remove something to sit in, so this word was said to you, ‘It is heavy.’” Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said, Uff is dirt between the nails, and ‘taff’ is their clippings. Al-Zajjaj said, The meaning of ‘uf’ is stench. Al-Asma’i said, Uff is dirt from the ear, and ‘taff’ is dirt from the nails. It was used so often that it was mentioned for everything that causes harm. It was narrated from the hadith of ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, If God knew of anything worse than disobedience to parents, He would have mentioned it. So let the righteous do whatever he wants to do and not enter Hellfire. And let the disobedient do whatever he wants to do and not enter Paradise. Our scholars said: His saying “Uff” to parents is the worst thing because he rejected them, rejected the blessing, denied the upbringing, and rejected the commandment that He gave him in the revelation. Uff is a word used for everything that is rejected. That is why Abraham said to his al-Nas 114:Uff to you and to what you worship other than God. That is, he rejected you and these idols with you. Thirteenth: The Almighty’s saying: And do not scold them. Scolding means reprimanding and harshness. And speak to them a generous word, meaning soft and gentle, such as: O my father and O my mother, without naming them or giving them a nickname. This was said by Ata’. Abu al-Haddaj al-Tujibi said: I said to Saeed ibn al-Musayyab: I have known everything in the Qur’an about being kind to one’s parents except the saying: And speak to them a generous word. What is this generous word? Ibn al-Musayyab said: The words of a sinful servant to a harsh, rough master.
17:25: God the Almighty says: Your Lord knows best what is in your hearts. That is, from believing in mercy and compassion for them, or from other forms of disobedience, or from making the outward appearance of their righteousness a yaa. Ibn Jubayr said: He means the initiative that is sown, such as a slip or a mistake, that occurs from a man to his parents or one of them, he does not mean anything wrong with that. God the Almighty said: If you are righteous: that is, sincere in your intention to be righteous towards your parents, then God will forgive the initiative. And His statement: Indeed, He is Forgiving to those who turn back to God, He promised forgiveness with the condition of righteousness and returning after returning to obeying God the Almighty. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: He is the servant who repents, then sins, then repents, then sins. Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him said: The one who turns back to God is the one who is mindful, who seeks forgiveness for his sins when he remembers them. Ubayd bin Umair said: They are those who remember their sins in private, then seek forgiveness from God the Almighty. These sayings are similar. Awn Al-Aqili said: The repentant are those who pray the Duha prayer. In Sahih: The prayer of the repentant when the young camels are hungry. The true meaning of the word is from the word aba ya’ub which means to return.
17:26: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And give the relative his right: meaning, just as you respect the rights of your parents, maintain family ties, then give charity to the poor and the wayfarer. Ali bin Al-Hussain said about the Almighty’s saying: And give the relative his right: They are the relatives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded that they be given their rights from the public treasury, meaning from the share of relatives from the war and spoils, and it is addressed to the governors or those who take their place. He added to this verse what is required of maintaining family ties, filling a gap, offering financial assistance when in need, and helping in every way. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And do not be wasteful means: Do not be extravagant in spending in what is not right. Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, said: Extravagance is spending money in what is not right, and there is no extravagance in doing good deeds. This is the opinion of the majority. Ashab said on the authority of Malik: Extravagance is taking money from its rightful place and spending it in what is not right, and it is wastefulness, and it is forbidden.
17:27: Because God the Almighty said: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils. His saying brothers means that they are in their ruling, since the wasteful strive to corrupt like the devils, or that they do whatever their souls tempt them, or that they will be paired with them if they are in the Fire, three opinions. And the brothers here is the plural of brother by non-kinship, and from that is the saying of God the Almighty: The believers are but brothers. And the saying of God the Almighty: And Satan is ever ungrateful to his Lord, meaning beware of following him and imitating him in corruption. And Satan is the generic name. Ad-Dahhak read the brothers of Satan separately, and this is also recorded in the Mushaf of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him. Third: Whoever spends his money on desires in excess of his needs and exposes it thereby is a spendthrift. Whoever spends the profit of his money on his desires and to preserve his origin or rank is not a spendthrift. Whoever spends a dirham on something forbidden is a spendthrift, and he is restricted from spending the dirham on something forbidden, but he is not restricted from spending it on desires unless there is fear that it will be exhausted.
17:28: It has three issues: The first: That He, the Most High, the Most Great, singled out His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by saying: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for. This is an amazing discipline and a gentle and wonderful statement, meaning, do not turn away from them in a lighthearted way, despite your wealth and ability, thus depriving them. It is only permissible to turn away from them when there is a weakness that arises or an obstacle that hinders, and at that time you hope from God, the Most High, the Most Great, to open the door of goodness so that you can reach it to comfort the one who asked. If the situation prevents you, then say to them a gentle word. The second: In the reason for its revelation. Ibn Zayd said: The verse was revealed about a people who used to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he refused to give them, because he knew that they spent their money on corruption. So he used to reject the words of God the Almighty: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for. He said: This is not about mentioning the parents. Some people from Muzaynah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him to carry them, so he said: I do not find anything to carry you on, so they turned away with tears streaming from their eyes out of grief. Then God the Almighty revealed: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for. And mercy is the bounty. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Then speak to them a gentle word. He ordered him to supplicate for them, meaning make their poverty easy for them by your supplication for them. It was also said: Supplicate for them a supplication that includes victory and reform for them. It was also said: The meaning is: But if you turn away, meaning if you turn away, O Muhammad, from giving them due to straitened circumstances, then speak to them a gentle word, meaning say the best words and make the most simple excuse, and supplicate for them for abundant provision, and say: If you find it, you will do it and be generous, for that works in his soul’s joy as a consolation. And when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked and did not have anything to give, he would remain silent, waiting for provision to come from God, the Almighty, the Most High, out of dislike of refusing. So this verse was revealed. So when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was asked and did not have anything to give, he would say: May God provide for us and you from His grace. According to this interpretation, al-hammah means the awaited provision. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ikrimah. The pronoun in about them refers to those mentioned above from among the fathers, relatives, the poor, and wayfarers. And a soft and easy word means soft, kind, and good. It is a passive participle with the meaning of the subject, from the word yusr like al-maymun, meaning a beautiful promise, as we have explained. And he who said it well did: Do not be a piece of paper that I give to those who ask for it, for I am soft and flexible. Those who ask will not be deprived of goodness from my character, either my loyalty or my good reward. You say: I made such-and-such easy for you if you prepared it.
17:29: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And do not make your hand chained to your neck. This is a metaphor for the miser who is unable to give out any of his money from his heart, so he gave him an example of the chain that prevents him from acting with the hand. In Sahih al-Bukhari and Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) gave an example of a miser and a giver of charity. They are like two men wearing iron cloaks, whose hands are forced to their breasts and collarbones. Every time the giver gives charity, the cloak expands from him until it covers his fingers and erases his traces. And every time the miser intends to give charity, the cloak shrinks and each link takes its place. Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with him said: I saw the Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) putting his fingers in his cloak like this. If you had seen him expand it, it would not expand. Second: The Almighty’s statement: And do not spread it out completely. Spreading out the hand is an example of losing money. If one closes the hand, what is in it is retained, while spreading it out takes away what is in it. All of this is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant is his nation. This has often been mentioned in the Quran, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was their master and intermediary to their Lord. He used to refer to them according to the Arabs’ custom in this regard.
