Also, he, peace be upon him, did not save anything for tomorrow, and he would go hungry until a stone would be tightened on his stomach from hunger. Many of the Companions spent all their money in the way of God, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not rebuke them or denounce them because of the soundness of their faith and the strength of their insight. God, the Exalted, forbade extravagance in spending and spending what one has in one’s hand of money for someone who fears regret for what has left his hand. As for someone who trusts in the promise of God, the Almighty, and His great reward for what he has spent, then this is not what is meant by the verse. And God knows best. It was said: This address was to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically about himself, in which he taught him how to spend and ordered him to be economical. Jabir and Ibn Masoud said: A boy came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: My mother asks you for such and such. He said: I don’t have anything today. He said: We will tell you to clothe me with your shirt. So he took off his shirt and gave it to him and sat in the house naked. In Jabir’s narration: Bilal approached for prayer and waited for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to come out, and hearts were aroused. Some of them entered and found him naked, so this verse was revealed. All of this is about spending on charity. As for spending on corruption, both a little and a lot of it is forbidden, as mentioned above. Third: This verse forbids letting one’s grief run wild over what comes first from asking the believers, lest the one who comes after that be left with nothing, or lest the one who spends on them neglect his family. And similar to it are the words of wisdom: I have never seen extravagance except that with it wasted rights. And this is from the verses of the jurisprudence of the situation, so its ruling is not made clear except by considering a person from the people. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: So you will sit down blamed and regretful. Ibn Arafa said: He means do not be extravagant and do not waste your wealth, leaving you regretful and cut off from spending and spending, just as a camel is regretful, which is one whose strength has gone and cannot be revived. From this is the statement of the Almighty: Your sight will return to you, humbled and regretful, meaning weary and cut off. Qatada said: That is, regretful for what has passed from you, so he made it from regret, and there is some error in this, because the agent of regret is regret and loss, and it is not said regretful, and the blamed is the one who is blamed for wasting his wealth or blamed by someone who does not give him.
17:30: God Almighty says: “Indeed, your Lord expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it. Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Knowing and Seeing.”
17:31: There are two issues: First: We have already discussed this verse in Al-An’am, and praise be to God. Poverty means poverty and lack of property. A man is impoverished, meaning he has nothing left but the malqat, which are large, smooth stones. Al-Hudhali said, describing a hunter: She was given a very strong and powerful spear if she poisoned the poisonous ones. The singular is malqa. Al-Aqdar is the diminutive of al-Aqdar, which is a short man. Al-Hasheef from the Thayyat means good character. Samat passed. Shammar said: Amlaq is intransitive and transitive, amlaq if he becomes poor, and time impoverished what is in his hand. Aws said: I am not flattered by the troubles that befall me The second: The Almighty’s saying: khataan: khataan is the reading of the majority with a kasra on the kha and a sukoon on the ta and with a hamza and shortened. Ibn Amir read khata with a fatha on the kha and the ta and a shortened hamza, and it is the reading of Abu Jaafar Yazid. These two readings are taken from khata if the sin is committed intentionally. Ibn Arafa said: It is said that he khataan fi sinbu khataan if he sinned in it, and akhtaan if he took a wrong path intentionally or unintentionally. He said: It is said khataan in the meaning of akhtaan. Al-Azhari said: It is said khata yakhtaan khataan if he deliberately made a mistake, like athama ya’thama ghathman. And akhtaan if he did not do it intentionally, ikhtaan and khataan. The poet said: Leave me alone, my mistake and my correction are upon me, and I did not waste money The noun khata stands for mistakes, and is the opposite of correctness. There are two forms of it: short, which is good, and long, which is little. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, khata with a fatha on the kha, a sukoon on the ta and a hamza. Ibn Kathir read it with a kasra on the kha, a fatha on the ta and a long hamza. An-Nahhas said: I do not know of a basis for this reading, and that is why Abu Hatim considered it khata. Abu Ali said: It is a source of khata’a yakhati’, although we do not find khata’a, but we found takhata’a, which is the passive form of khata’a, so he guided us to it. From this is the saying of the poet: Nobility has mistaken his guts and my day has ended, so I did not hurry And another said in describing Maha: The sniper followed him until he found him with his trunk in the stagnant water pool. Al-Jawhari: He made a mistake, meaning he missed him. Awfi bin Matar Al-Mazini said: Tell my aunt Jabir that your friend was not killed Nobility has mistaken his guts and my last day has come, so he did not hurry Al-Hasan read khataa with the kha and taa open and the hamza extended. Abu Hatim said: This is not known in the language and it is an impermissible mistake. Abu al-Fath said: Khataa is from akhta’ata, like ataa is from ata’ata. It is a noun meaning a source. Also from al-Hasan: khataa with the kha and taa open and with a tanween without a hamza.
17:32: There is one issue: Scholars said: The Almighty’s saying: And do not come near to adultery is more eloquent than saying: And do not commit adultery, because its meaning is: Do not come near to adultery. Adultery is extended and shortened, two languages. The poet said: It was a duty to say what you say, just as adultery was a duty to be stoned. And a way: is an accusative of specification, the meaning is: and his way is an evil way. That is, because it leads to the Fire. And adultery is one of the major sins, and there is no disagreement about it and its ugliness, especially with the wife of the neighbor. And it results in using the child of another and taking him as a son and other things of inheritance and corrupting lineages due to the mixing of waters. And in the Sahih, it is reported that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to a woman who was lying on the ground at the door of a tent and said: Perhaps he wanted to touch it, so they said: Yes. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was thinking of cursing him with a curse that would enter his grave with him. How can he inherit it when it is not permissible for him? How can he use it when it is not permissible for him?
17:33: The Almighty said: And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. This has already been discussed in Al-An’am. God Almighty says: “And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, but let him not exceed limits in taking life. Indeed, he has been supported.” There are three issues in this: First: The Almighty’s statement: And whoever is killed unjustly means without a reason that warrants killing. We have made for his heir means for the one who deserves his blood. Ibn Khuwayr Mandad said: The heir must be male, because He singled him out for guardianship with the masculine form. Ismail bin Ishaq mentioned in His statement: We have made for his heir what indicates that women are excluded from the general term guardian, so there is no harm. Women have no right to retaliation for that, nor does her forgiveness have any effect, and she does not have the right to exact retribution. The opponent said: What is meant here by the guardian is the inheritor, and God Almighty said: The believing men and believing women are allies of one another. And He said: And those who believed and did not emigrate - you have no right to their guardianship in any way. And He said: And those of kinship are more worthy of one another in the Book of God. This necessitated establishing retaliation for all the heirs. As for what they mentioned that the guardian is apparently masculine and is one, it is as if what was in the meaning of the gender is equal for the male and the female, and its completion is in the books of disagreement. Sultan, meaning authority, if he wants to kill, or if he wants to pardon, or if he wants to take the blood money, said Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, and Ad-Dahhak, Ashhab, and Ash-Shafi’i. Ibn Wahb said: Malt said: The Sultan demanded it until it was delivered to him. Ibn Al-Arabi said: These statements are close, and the clearest of them is the statement of Malik: It is the command of God. Then the command of God, the Almighty, was not mentioned explicitly, so the scholars differed concerning it. Ibn Al-Qasim said, on the authority of Malik and Abu Hanifa: Killing specifically. Ashhab said: The choice, as mentioned earlier, and Ash-Shafi’i said the same. This meaning has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And let him not exceed limits in killing. There are three opinions: He should not kill anyone other than his killer, said Al-Hasan, Ad-Dahhak, Mujahid, and Saeed bin Jubair. Second: He should not kill two people instead of his guardian, as the Arabs used to do. Third: He should not mutilate the killer, said Talq bin Habib. All of this is intended because it is an excess that is forbidden. The discussion of this has already been completed in Al-Baqarah. The majority read yaraf with a ya, meaning the guardian. Ibn Amir, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read tasraf with a ta above it, which is the reading of Hudhayfah. Al-Ala’ bin Abdul Karim narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: It is for the first killer, and the meaning according to us is: Do not exceed limits, O killer. At-Tabari said: It is in the sense of addressing the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Imams after him, meaning: Do not kill anyone other than the killer. In the wording of Abi, Do not exceed limits in killing. Third: The Almighty’s statement: Indeed, he was supported means, he means the guardian. If it is said: And how many a guardian has been forsaken and does not attain his right? We say: “The support is sometimes by the appearance of the proof and other times by its fulfillment and by their combination a third time, so whichever it is, it is a victory from God, the Most High and Exalted.” Ibn Kathir narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Indeed, the one who was killed was supported. An-Nahhas said: The meaning of his statement is that God supported him through his guardian. It was narrated that in the reading of Abi, do not be excessive in killing, for the guardian of the one who was killed was supported. An-Nahhas said: Abayn with the letter ya is for the guardian, because it is only said: He should not be excessive if he has the right to kill, so this is for the guardian. It is also permissible with the letter ta and is for the guardian, except that it requires changing the addressee. Ad-Dahhak said: This is the first thing revealed in the Qur’an regarding killing, and it is Meccan.
17:34: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, until he reaches maturity. It has been discussed in Al-An’am. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And fulfill the covenant. We have already discussed this in more than one place. Al-Zajjaj said: Everything that God has commanded and forbidden is from the covenant. The covenant was something that was asked about, so it was deleted, like His saying: And they do what they are commanded to do. And it was said: The covenant is asked to rebuke the one who breaks it, so it is said: I broke it, just as the girl buried alive is asked to rebuke the one who buried her alive.
17:35: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And give full measure when you measure. This was also discussed in Al-An’am. This verse requires that the seller must measure, and this has already been mentioned in Surat Yusuf, so there is no point in repeating it. Al-Qistas, with a damma or kasra on the qaf, is the scale in the Roman language, as stated by Ibn ‘Aziz. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Qistas is the scale, whether it is small or large. Mujahid said: Al-Qistas is justice, and he used to say: It is a Roman language, as if it was said to the al-Nas 114:Weigh with justice in your weight. Ibn Kathir, Abu ‘Amr, Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and ‘Aasim, according to the narration of Abu Bakr, read Al-Qistas with a damma on the qaf. Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs from ‘Aasim read it with a kasra on the qaf, and they are two languages: Second: The Almighty’s saying: That is better and more suitable for outcome, meaning fulfilling the measure and establishing the weight is better in the sight of your Lord and more blessed and more suitable for outcome, meaning the consequence. Al-Hasan said: It was mentioned to us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No man is able to do something forbidden and then abandons it, having nothing but fear of God Almighty, except that God will replace it for him in this world before the Hereafter with something better for him than that.
17:36: It has six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And do not follow means do not follow what you do not know and that does not concern you. Qatada said: Do not say I saw when you did not see, and I heard when you did not hear, and I knew when you did not know. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said the same. Mujahid said: Do not criticize someone for something you do not know. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said the same. Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: It is false testimony. Al-Qutbi said: The meaning is do not follow intuition and suspicion, and they are all close together. The root of qafw is slander and false accusation, and from this is the saying of the Prophet, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: We are the sons of Al-Nadr bin Kinanah. We do not follow our mothers nor do we deny our fathers, that is, we do not attribute our mothers’ lineage. Al-Kumait said: I do not accuse the innocent without guilt, nor do I follow the guards if we follow them. It is said: qafwatu aqfuhu, waqafatu aqwafuhu, waqfatuhu if you follow his traces. And from this comes the word qafah for their following the traces and the rhyme of everything is its last, and from this comes the rhyme of poetry, because it follows the verse. And from this comes the name of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, al-Muqfi, because he came last of the prophets. And from this comes the word qaif, who is the one who follows the trace of the likeness. It is said: qaf al-qaif yaquwuf if he did that. And you say: faqut al-athar, by placing the fa before the qaf. Ibn Atiyyah: It seems that this is from the Arabs’ play on some words, as they said: ra’mali fi li-’omri. Al-Tabari narrated from a group that they said: qaf and qaf, like ‘ata and ‘ata. Mundhir ibn Sa’id went to the view that qaf and qaf are like jabadh and jadhb. In short, this verse forbids lying and slandering, and similar false and bad statements. Some people read, as narrated by al-Kisa’i, taqwaf with a damma on the qaf and a sukoon on the fa. Al-Jarrah read the letter fa with the letter fa open. This is the language of some people, but Abu Hatim and others rejected it. Second: Ibn Khuwayr Mandad said: This verse includes the ruling on fortune-tellers, because when He said: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge, it indicates the permissibility of that of which we have knowledge. So whatever a person knows or what he thinks is most likely, it is permissible to rule by it. And with this we have provided evidence to prove the drawing of lots and eagerness, because it is a type of preponderance of suspicion. And it may be called knowledge by extension. So the fortune-teller attributes the child to his father through the similarity between them, just as the jurist attributes the branch to the root through the similarity. In the Sahih on the authority of Aisha. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon me, happy, his face beaming with joy, and said: Didn’t you see that Mujazziz looked at Zaid bin Haritha and Usama bin Zaid, who had a blanket covering their heads, but their feet were showing, and he said: Some of these feet belong to some. And in the hadith of Yunus bin Yazid: Mujazziz was a soothsayer. Third: Imam Abu Abdullah Al-Mazari said: The pre-Islamic era used to cast aspersions on Usama’s lineage because he was very black, and Zaid, his father, was whiter than cotton. This is how Abu Dawud mentioned it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Salih. Judge Iyad said: Other than Ahmad, Zaid was rosier in complexion, and Usama was very dark-skinned. Zaid ibn Haritha was a pure Arab from Kalb, and he was taken captive, as will come in Surat Al-Ahzab, God willing: Fourth: The majority of scholars have provided evidence for referring to a fortune teller when there is a dispute over a child, based on the pleasure of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he says this fortune teller. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not one who would be pleased by falsehood and not be pleased with it. Abu Hanifa, Ishaq, Ath-Thawri and their companions do not accept this, holding fast to the Prophet’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, abolishment of doubt in the hadith of cursing, as will come in Surat An-Nur, God willing: Fifth: Those who take the sayings of the fortune tellers differed as to whether this should be taken into account in the children of free women and slave women or is it limited to the children of slave women? There are two opinions. The first is the opinion of Al-Shafi’i and Malik may God be pleased with them in the narration of Ibn Wahb from him, and the well-known opinion of his school is to limit it to the children of the slave woman. The correct opinion is what Ibn Wahb narrated from him and what Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him said, because the hadith that is the basis for this chapter only occurred in the case of free women. Usamah and his father were free, so how can the reason for which the evidence of the ruling was derived be nullified, which is the motive for it? This is something that is not permissible according to the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence. Likewise, these people differed as to whether the saying of one fortune teller is sufficient or two are necessary because it is testimony. Ibn Al-Qasim said the first, and it is the apparent meaning of the hadith, rather its text. Malik and Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with them said the second. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those one will be questioned. That is, each one of them will be asked about what he acquired. The heart will be asked about what he thought about and believed, and the hearing and sight about what he saw and heard. It was said that the meaning is that God Almighty will ask man about what he has contained: his hearing, sight, and heart. Similar to this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock. So man is a shepherd over his limbs, so it is as if he said that man was responsible for all of this, so it is with the deletion of an added word. The first meaning is more eloquent in the argument, because his denial comes from his limbs, and that is the height of shame, as He said: Today We shall seal up their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn, and His statement: Their hearing, their sight, and their skins will bear witness against them as to what they used to do. He referred to the hearing, sight, and heart as those because they are senses that have perception, and He made them responsible in this verse, so they are in the state of one who has reason, so He referred to them as those. Sibawayh, may God have mercy on him, said about the Almighty’s statement: I saw them prostrating to Me, “He only said: I saw them in the stars,” because when He described them as prostrating, which is from the action of one who has reason, He referred to them with a metaphor of one who has reason, and this has been mentioned previously. Al-Zajjaj narrated that the Arabs refer to what has reason and what does not have reason as those, and he and Al-Tabari recited: Blame the houses after the house of Al-Lawa and life after those days This is a matter to be considered. As for the verse, the narration of it is from the peoples, and God knows best. The Almighty said: Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure. Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out one day or night and found Abu Bakr and Umar. He said: What brought you out of your homes at this hour? They said: Hunger, O Messenger of God. He said: "By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the One who delayed you has brought me out. Go." So they went with him. Then he came to a man from the Ansar, but he was not in his house. When the woman saw him, she said: Welcome and welcome. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: Where is so-and-so? She said: He is bringing us fresh water. Then the Ansari came and looked at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his two companions, then said: Praise be to God! No one today has more generous guests than I. He went and brought them a bunch of dates containing fresh dates, dried dates, and fresh dates. He said: Eat from these. He took the knife, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: "Beware of... And the milking ones) so he slaughtered for them, and they ate from the sheep) and from that bunch of dates, and drank, and when they were full and satisfied, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Abu Bakr and Umar: (By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you will be asked about the pleasures of this day, on the Day of Resurrection. Hunger drove you out of your homes, and you did not return until this pleasure befell you).” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, and he said about it: (By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, among the pleasures that you will be asked about on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:cool shade, pleasant dates, and cool water). He gave the man from the Ansar a nickname, and said: Abu Al-Haytham bin Al-Tayhan. And he mentioned his story. I said: The name of this Ansari man is Malik ibn al-Tayhan, and his nickname is Abu al-Haytham. And regarding this story, Abdullah ibn Rawaha says, praising Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayhan: I have never seen a nation as proud as Islam, nor a group as friendly as the guests of Al-Irashi. A prophet, a friend, a guide to the nation, and the best of the children of Eve, branch and element. So they arrived at the appointed time and the decree was destined, and the decree of God was a decree and a measure. To a man from Najd who rivals the suns of the morning with his generosity, glory and pride And the knight of God's creation in every raid, if the people wear nailed iron Then he ransomed them and brought them near to his village. He did not let them stay except fat and full of dates. Abu Naim Al-Hafiz mentioned, on the authority of Abu Usayb, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to us at night, so I went out to him. Then he passed by Abu Bakr and called him. He came out to him and he went until he entered a garden belonging to some of the Ansar. He said to the owner of the garden: Feed us with fresh dates. So he brought a bunch of dates and put them down and they ate. Then he called for water and drank it. Then he said: You will be asked about this on the Day of Resurrection. Umar took the bunch of dates and threw them on the ground until the fresh dates scattered towards the face of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: O Messenger of God, will we be asked about this on the Day of Resurrection? He said: “Yes, except for three things: a piece of bread with which to satisfy his hunger, a garment with which to cover his private parts, or a hole in which to shelter from the heat and cold.” The people of interpretation differed regarding the bliss that was asked about, and there are ten opinions: One of them is: security and health, as stated by Ibn Masoud. The second is: health and leisure, as stated by Saeed bin Jubair. And in Bukhari, on his authority, peace be upon him: (Two blessings which many people are deceived about: health and free time). The third: perception through the senses of hearing and sight, as stated by Ibn Abbas. In the Qur’an: Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those one will be questioned. (al-Isra’ 17:36) And in the Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Abu Sa’id, they said, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: (The servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to him: Did I not give you hearing and sight, wealth and children...) The hadith. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, who said: A good and authentic hadith. Fourth: The pleasure of food and drink, said by Jabir bin Abdullah Al-Ansari. The hadith of Abu Hurairah indicates this. Fifth: It is lunch and dinner, said by Al-Hasan. Sixth: The statement of Makhul Al-Shami: It is filling stomachs, cool drinks, shade of dwellings, moderation of character, delight of character, and delight of sleep. It was narrated by Zaid bin Aslam on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: On that Day you will be asked about pleasures, meaning about full stomachs.... Then he mentioned it. Al-Mawardi mentioned it and said: This question applies to both the disbeliever and the believer, except that the question of the believer is good report that he will be given both the pleasures of this world and the pleasures of the Hereafter. The question of the disbeliever is a rebuke for having met the pleasures of this world with disbelief and disobedience. Some people said: This question about every pleasure only applies to the disbelievers, because… It was narrated that when this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of the food I ate with you in the house of Abu Al-Haytham bin Al-Tayhan, of barley bread, meat, ripe dates, and fresh water? Are you afraid that this is among the blessings that we will be asked about? He, peace be upon him, said: That is for the disbelievers. Then he recited: And do We reward anyone but the ungrateful? (Saba’: 17). Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr mentioned it. Al-Hasan said: No one will be asked about blessings except the people of Hellfire. Al-Qushayri said: The combination of the two narrations is that everyone will be asked, but the question of the disbelievers is a rebuke because he has abandoned gratitude. The question of the believer is a question of honor because it is gratitude. This is the blessing in every blessing. I said: This statement is good, because the wording is general. Al-Faryabi said: Warqa’ narrated to us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty: Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure, he said: Everything from the pleasures of this world. Abu Al-Ahwas narrated on the authority of Abdullah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: (God Almighty will enumerate His blessings upon the servant on the Day of Resurrection, until He enumerates to him: So-and-so asked me to marry her to you, and he calls her by her name, so I married her to you.) And in Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: When this verse was revealed: Then you will surely be asked that Day about pleasure, the people said: O Messenger of God, about which pleasure shall we be asked? They are the two black ones, the enemy is present, and our swords are on our shoulders. He said: That will happen. And it was narrated that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first thing that the servant will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection - meaning the servant - will be: Did We not make your body healthy and give you cold water to drink?” He said: “The hadith of Ibn ‘Umar said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will call one of His servants and make him stand before Him and ask him about his status as He asks him about his wealth.’” Status is inevitably one of the pleasures of this world. Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: It is a healthy body and a good soul. This is the seventh opinion. It was also said: Sleeping with security and well-being. Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah said: That which satisfies hunger and covers the private parts of rough food and clothing will not be asked about on the Day of Resurrection, but rather he will be asked about pleasures. He said: The evidence for this is that God, the Most High, settled Adam in Paradise and said to him: You shall neither be hungry therein nor naked, nor thirsty therein nor exposed to the sun’ (Ta-Ha: 118-119). So these four things - that which satisfies hunger, that which quells thirst, and that which conceals…” It is from the heat, and he covers his private parts with it - for Adam, peace be upon him, absolutely, he is not held accountable for it, because he needs it. I said: Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr mentioned something similar to this. He said: Among the things that a servant will not be asked about are clothing to cover his private parts, food to support his back, and a place to protect him from the heat and cold. I said: This is taken from his saying, peace be upon him: (The son of Adam has no right to anything other than these qualities: a house to live in, a garment to cover his nakedness, and rough bread and water.) Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. An-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Rough bread means that it has no condiment. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: Bliss is what God bestowed upon us through Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. In the Qur’an, it is stated: God has certainly bestowed a great favor upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves. (Al Imran 3:164) Al-Hasan and Al-Mufaddal also said: “It is the simplification of the laws and the ease of the Qur’an. God the Almighty said: “And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty.” (al-Hajj 22:78), and He the Almighty said: And We have certainly made the Qur’an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember? (al-Qamar 54:17). I said: All of these are blessings, so the servant will be asked about them: Did he give thanks for that or was he ungrateful? The previous statements are more evident. And God knows best.
17:37: It has five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And do not walk on the earth exultantly. This is a prohibition against arrogance and an order to be humble. Exultation is intense joy. It was also said: It is haughtiness in walking. It was also said: It is a person exceeding his limits. Qatada said: It is arrogance in walking. It was also said: It is insolence and wickedness. It was also said: It is activity. These sayings are similar but they are divided into two parts: one is reprehensible and the other is praiseworthy. So arrogance, haughtiness, conceit, and a person exceeding his limits are reprehensible, while joy and activity are praiseworthy. God the Almighty described Himself with one of them, as in the authentic hadith: God is more pleased with the repentance of a servant than a man. Laziness is reprehensible in the Shariah, and activity is its opposite. Arrogance and what is similar to it may be praiseworthy, but this is against the enemies of God and the oppressors. Abu Hatim Muhammad Ibn Hibban narrated on the authority of Ibn Jabir Ibn Atik on the authority of his father on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “There is jealousy that God hates and there is that which God loves, and there is conceit that God loves and there is that which God hates. As for the jealousy that God loves, it is jealousy in religion, and the jealousy that God hates is jealousy in other than His religion, and the conceit that God loves, a man’s conceit in battle and when giving charity, and the conceit that God hates, is conceit in falsehood.” Abu Dawud narrated it in his Musannaf and others. They recited: Do not walk on the earth except in humility, for there are many people beneath it who are more exalted than you. Even if you are in glory, protection and strength, how many people have died who were more secure than you? Second: A person’s preoccupation with hunting and the like out of arrogance without need for that is included in this verse, as is the torture of an animal and its use for no reason. As for men who rest on the rare day and hour of their day in which they force themselves to lie down and rest in order to help themselves with righteous work, such as studying knowledge or praying, this is not included in this verse. The Almighty said: Marriage. The majority read it with the opening of the ra. The reading of the group Fiman, Ya’qub narrated, is with the breaking of the ra based on the active participle. The first is more expressive, because your saying: Zaid came running is more expressive than your saying: Zaid came running. So too is your saying marriage. Marriage is a verbal noun that is more expressive than saying marriage. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, you will never tear the earth apart means you will never enter its interior and know what is in it, and you will never reach the mountains in height, meaning you will never be equal to the mountains in height or reach your height. It is said: to tear a garment means to split, and to tear the earth means to cut it. Tearing is a wide part of the earth. Meaning, you will never tear the earth with your greatness and walking on it. And you will never reach the mountains in height with your greatness, meaning, with your power you will not reach this level, rather you are a humble slave, surrounded from below and above you, and the one who is surrounded is confined and weak, so arrogance is not appropriate for you. What is meant by to tear the earth here is to penetrate it, not to cut it in distance, and God knows best. Al-Azhari said: Its meaning is you will never cross it. Al-Nahhas: This is clearer, because it is taken from kharaq which is a wide desert. It is said: So-and-so is more akhraq than so-and-so, meaning he travels more, has more honor and is more secure. It is narrated that Saba’ subdued the earth with his armies, east and west, plain and mountain, and killed masters and took captives, and thus he was called Saba’ and the people submitted to him. When he saw that, he separated from his companions for three days, then he went out to them and said: When I attained what no one else attained, I saw the beginning of thanking for these blessings, and I did not see anything more effective in that than prostrating to the sun when it rose, so they prostrated to it, and that was the first worship of the sun. This is the consequence of arrogance, haughtiness and mirth. We seek refuge in God from that.
17:38: Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: All of that was evil in the sight of your Lord and detestable. This is a reference to the whole of what was mentioned previously of what He commanded and prohibited. This is valid for singular and plural, feminine and masculine. Asim, Ibn Amir, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Masruq read bad with the addition of bad to the pronoun. Therefore, he said: Makruha is in the accusative case as the predicate of kana. Bad is what is detestable and is what God, the Almighty, does not approve of and does not command. God, the Almighty, mentioned in this verse from His saying: And your Lord has decreed until His saying: was evil, commanded and prohibited. He does not describe all of it as evil, so that what is commanded is included in what is prohibited. Abu Ubaid chose this reading. Because in Abu’s reading, All of that was his evil, this can only be for addition. Ibn Kathir, Nafi’ and Abu Amr read bad with the tanween, meaning that everything that God and His Messenger prohibited is evil. And on this the speech was cut off at his saying: And the best interpretation, then he said: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge, and do not walk, then he said: All of that was bad with the tanween. And it was said: His saying: And do not kill your children until this verse was bad, not good, so they made each encompassing what is prohibited without others. And his saying: disliked is not an attribute of bad, but rather it is a substitute for it and the estimate was bad and it was disliked. And it was said: Disliked is a second predicate for it was carried on the word each, and bad is carried on the meaning in all of these things mentioned before. Some of them said: And an attribute of bad, because since it was a feminine that is not real to be described, it is permissible to be described with a masculine. Ibn Ali al-Farisi weakened this and said: If the feminine is mentioned, then what comes after it should be masculine, and the only leniency is that the verb attributed to the feminine is absent and it is in the form of what indicates the masculine, do you not see the saying of the poet: There is no rain and its rain and its rain and its rain and its land is not green and its vegetation is not green It is considered ugly by them. If someone said: The most barren land, it would not be ugly. Abu Ali said: But it is permissible for his saying disliked to be a substitute for bad. And it is permissible for it to be a state of the pronoun in with your Lord, and for with your Lord to be in the place of an attribute of bad. Fifth: Scholars have used this verse as evidence to condemn dancing and engaging in it. He said: And do not walk on the earth exultantly. And he condemned the arrogant. Dancing is the most extreme form of exultation and insolence. Are we not those who compare wine to alcohol because they both cause intoxication and joy? So why do we not compare the reed and the melody of poetry with it to the tambourine, flute, and drum because they come together? How ugly is a bearded man, and how can he be if he is gray-haired, dancing and clapping to the rhythm of melodies and reeds, especially if they are the voices of women and beardless men, while he is good to those who have before him death, questioning, resurrection, and the path, then he is to one of the two abodes, shining with the sun of splendor in dancing, and clapping like women do. I have seen sheikhs of an age who did not show their age from smiling, let alone laughing, despite my frequent mixing with them. Abu al-Faraj Ibn al-Jawzi, may God have mercy on him, said: Some of the sheikhs told me on the authority of Imam al-Ghazali that he said: Dancing is foolishness between the shoulders that does not go away except by playing. This chapter will be further explained in Al-Kahf and elsewhere, God willing.
17:39: This refers to these manners, stories and rulings that are included in these previous verses that were brought down by Gabriel, peace be upon him. That is, these are the actions that are required by the wisdom of God, the Almighty, in His servants and His creation for them of good morals, wisdom, laws of sound meanings and virtuous actions. Then He connected His statement, And do not make to what came before of prohibitions. The address is to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, and what is meant is every human being who hears the verse. And the one who is rejected is the one who is humiliated, banished and excluded. This has been mentioned previously in this surah. And if he says in supplication, O God, repel Satan from us, that is, keep him away.
17:40: This is a response to the one who said that the Arabs are the daughters of God, and they also had daughters along with the sons, but he meant: Should He keep the sons for you instead of Him and make the daughters shared between you and Him? You are saying a terrible thing meaning in the sight of God Almighty.
17:41: The Almighty said: And We have certainly diversified meaning We have explained. It was also said that We repeated. In this Qur'an was said to be redundant, and the meaning is: And We have certainly diversified this Qur'an, like And make good for me in my offspring meaning make good my offspring. And diversification: diversifying something from one direction to another. What is meant by this diversification is clarification and repetition. It was also said: contrast, meaning We diversified between the sermons so that they may remember, consider, and take heed. The general reading is diversified with renewal on the increase wherever it occurs. Al-Hasan read it with alleviation. And His saying in this Qur'an means examples, lessons, wisdom, sermons, rulings, and information. Al-Tha'labi said: I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn say in the presence of Imam Sheikh Abu al-Tayyib: The Almighty's saying, We have divided has two meanings. One of them is that He did not make it a single type, but rather a promise and a threat, clear and ambiguous, a prohibition and an order, abrogating and abrogated, report and parables, such as the division of winds from east to west, south to north, and the division of verbs from past and future, commands and prohibitions, actions, subject and object, and the like. The second is that it was not revealed all at once, but in stages, such as His saying, And a Qur'an which We have divided into parts, and its meaning is that We divided Gabriel, peace be upon him, to you. That they may remember is the reading of Yahya, al-A'mash, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i, that they may remember with a lightened vowel. Likewise in al-Furqan, And We have indeed divided it among them that they may remember with a shaddah. Abu Ubaid chose it because its meaning is that they may remember and be admonished. Al-Mahdawi said: Whoever stresses li-dhakkiru means contemplation. Likewise, whoever recites li-yadhikru and similar to the first is And We have certainly conveyed to them the Word that perhaps they will be reminded. The second is And remember what is in it. “And it does not increase them” meaning the transformation and reminder. Except aversion meaning distancing themselves from the truth and neglecting to look and consider. This is because they believed in the Qur’an that it was a trick, magic, divination, and poetry.
17:42: The Almighty's saying: Say, 'If there were other gods with Him,' This is connected to the Almighty's saying: And do not make with God another god. It is a response to the idol worshippers. As they say. Ibn Kathir and Hafs read they say with a ya'. The rest read you say with a ta' as a direct address. If they would have sought meaning the gods. A way to the Lord of the Throne. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: They would have sought with God a dispute and a fight as the kings of the world do to each other. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, may God be pleased with him, said: The meaning is if they sought a way to reach Him in order to remove His kingdom, because they are His partners. Qatada said: The meaning is if the gods sought to be close to the Lord of the Throne, and sought to be close to Him because they are below Him, and the people believed that the idols bring them closer to God, so if they believed that the idols are in need of God, the Most High, then they have nullified their being gods.
17:43: Glory be to Him, and He is far above what they say, far above. He, glory be to Him, has purified, sanctified, and glorified Himself from what is not befitting of Him. And glorification means sanctification. And it has been mentioned before.
17:44: The Almighty's saying: The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. He repeated the pronoun of a rational being to the heavens and the earth, because He attributed to God the action of a rational being, which is glorification. And His saying: and whoever is in them means the angels, mankind, and jinn. Then He made all things general in His saying: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. There is a difference of opinion regarding this generality, whether it is specific or not. A group said: It is not specific, and what is meant by it is glorification of evidence. And every created thing bears witness against itself that God Almighty is the Creator and Able. A group said: This glorification is real, and everything in general glorifies God with a glorification that humans do not hear or understand. What the ancients said, that it is the result of artifice and evidence, would have been an understandable matter, and the verse speaks of glorification that is not understood. They were answered that what is meant by His saying: You do not understand are the disbelievers who are presented for consideration and do not understand the wisdom of God, the Most High, in things. A group said: His saying: Of anything is general, and its meaning is specific to every living and sleeping thing, and this is not the case with inanimate objects. From this is the saying of Ikrimah: The tree glorifies God, but the column does not glorify God. Yazid al-Raqashi said to al-Hasan while they were eating and the tray was brought forward: Does this tray glorify God, O Abu Saeed? He said: It used to glorify God once, meaning that the tree used to glorify God when it was bearing fruit and in moderation, but now it has become a greased tray. I said: This statement is supported by the Sunnah in what was proven from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) passed by two graves and said: “They are being punished, but they are not being punished for a major sin. As for one of them, he used to go about spreading gossip, and as for the other, he did not clean himself from urinating.” He said: So he called for a fresh palm branch, split it in two, then planted one on this one and one on that one, then said: Perhaps it will be made easier for them as long as they do not dry. His (blessings and peace of God be upon him) saying as long as they do not dry indicates that as long as they are fresh, they glorify God, but when they dry, they become solid. And God knows best. In the Musnad of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi: So he placed one half on one of them and the other half on the other, and said: Perhaps the punishment will be made easier for them as long as there is some wetness in them. Our scholars said: This can be understood from planting trees and reciting the Qur’an on graves. If it is made easier for them by trees, then how about a believing man reciting the Qur’an? We have explained this meaning in the book At-Tadhkira in a clear manner, and that the reward of what is given to the dead reaches him. Praise be to God for that. According to the second interpretation, there is no need for that, because everything, inanimate and otherwise, glorifies God. I said: This interpretation and this statement are supported by the Book in the words of the Most High: “And remember Our servant David, the possessor of strength. Indeed, he was one who frequently turned back [to God]. Indeed, We subjected the mountains to him, exalting [God] in the evening and at sunrise.” And His saying: And among them are those who fall down for fear of God according to the words of Mujahid, and His saying: And the mountains fall down in devastation * Because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned in his Raqa’iq that Mis’ar told us on the authority of Abdullah bin Wasil on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah who said: Abdullah bin Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, said: A mountain says to a mountain: O so-and-so, did anyone who remembered God the Almighty pass by today? If he says yes, be pleased with him. Then Abdullah recited: And they say, ‘The Most Merciful has taken a son’ 1:10. He said: Do you think they hear falsehood and do not hear good? And in it on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: There is no morning or evening except that the uprooters of the earth call out to one another: O my neighbor, did a slave pass by you today who prayed to God or remembered God over you? Some say no, and some say yes, and she sees that this is an advantage for her. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No jinn, human, tree, stone, mud or anything else hears the voice of the muezzin but that it will testify for him on the Day of Resurrection. Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan and Malik in his Muwatta’ from the hadith of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri may God be pleased with him. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abdullah may God be pleased with him who said: We used to hear the food glorifying God while it was being eaten. In another narration on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him: We used to eat with the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and we would hear him glorifying God. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “I know a stone in Mecca that used to greet me before I was sent as a prophet. I know it now.” It was said that it was the Black Stone, and God knows best. There are many narrations with this meaning, and we have mentioned a number of them in Al-Lum’ Al-Lu’lu’iyyah in explanation of Al-‘Ishraniyat Al-Nabawiyyah by Al-Qadari may God have mercy on him. The narration of Al-Jad’ is also well-known in this regard, and Al-Bukhari narrated it in several places in his book. If this is proven in one inanimate object, it is permissible in all inanimate objects, and there is no impossibility in any of that, for everything glorifies God in general. And Al-Nakha’i and others said the same: It is general in what has a soul and what does not have a soul, even the creaking of a door. And they used as evidence the hadiths that we mentioned. And it was said: The glorification of inanimate objects is that they call the one looking at them to say: Glory be to God! because they do not perceive. And the poet said: It is received with a rosary from wherever it goes, and the heart of the seer is settled with trembling. That is, whoever sees it says: Glory be to its Creator. The correct view is that everything glorifies God, based on the reports indicating that. If that glorification was a glorification indicating that, then what specificity would there be for David? Rather, that is the glorification of the statement of the creation of life and the utterance of glorification, as we mentioned. The Sunnah has stated what the apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates about the glorification of everything, so saying that is more appropriate. And God knows best. Al-Hasan, Abu Amr, Ya’qub, Hafs, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Khalaf read ta-faqhunu with a ta’ to feminize the subject. The rest read it with a ya’, and Abu Ubaid chose it. He said: It is a barrier between the verb and the femininity. Indeed, He was Forbearing about the sins of His servants in this world. Forgiving to the believers in the Hereafter.
17:45: "On the authority of Asma bint Abi Bakr, may God Almighty be pleased with them both, she said: When the Surah Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, was revealed, the one-eyed woman, Umm Jamil bint Harb, came wailing and holding a stick in her hand, saying: We disobeyed him, refused his command, and neglected his religion. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting in the mosque with Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him. When Abu Bakr saw her, he said: O Messenger of God, she has come and I am afraid that she will see you! The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: She will not see me. He recited the Qur’an, so hold fast to it as he said. He recited: And when you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible veil. So she stopped at Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and she did not see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so she said: O Abu Bakr, I have been told that your companion satirized me! He said: No, by the Lord of this House, he did not satirize you. He said: She turned away saying: Quraysh know that I am the daughter of their master. Saeed bin Jubair may God be pleased with him said: When the verse, Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he! was revealed, Abu Lahab’s wife came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him was with him. Abu Bakr said: Why don’t you move away from her so that she doesn’t hear what will hurt you, for she is a vulgar woman. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I will be separated from her, but she did not see him. She said to Abu Bakr: O Abu Bakr, your companion has insulted us! He said: By God, he does not recite or write poetry. She said: And you believe him. She turned back. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God, did she not see you? He said: No. The angel remained between me and her, covering me until I left. Ka’b may God be pleased with him said about this verse: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to cover himself from the polytheists with three verses: the verse in al-Kahf 18:Indeed, We have placed coverings over their hearts, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. The verse in Al-Nahl: Those are the ones over whose hearts, hearing and vision God has sealed. The verse in al-Jathiyah 45:Have you seen he who has taken as his god his own desire, and God has sent him astray due to knowledge and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put over his vision a veil? The verse. So when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited them, he would cover himself from the polytheists. Ka’b may God be pleased with him said: So I told them to a man from the people of Ash-Sham, so he went to the land of the Romans and stayed there for a while, then he fled, so they went out in pursuit of him, so he recited them, and they were with him on a path, but they did not see him. Al-Tha’labi said: This which they narrate from Ka’b, I told it to a man from the people of Rayy, so he was taken prisoner in Daylam, so he stayed for a while, then he fled. They went out in search of him, and he read to them until their clothes touched his clothes, but they could not see him. I said: And to this verse is added the beginning of Surah Yasin until His saying: So they do not see. For in the biography of the Prophet’s migration, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the stay of Ali, may God be pleased with him, in his bed, it is said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and took a handful of dirt in which there was dirt, and God Almighty took away their sight from him so that they did not see him, so he began to sprinkle that dirt on their heads while he was reciting these verses from Ya-Sin 36:“Ya Seen. By the Wise Qur’an. Indeed, you are among the messengers. On a straight path. A revelation from the Almighty, the Merciful.” until His saying: And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them so that they do not see. Until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished these verses, and not a man remained among them except that he had dirt placed on his head, and he went away to wherever he wanted to go. I said: It happened to me in our country, Andalusia, in a scattered fortress in the district of Cordoba like this. That was because I fled before the enemy and withdrew to a side from him. It was not long before two horsemen came out in pursuit of me while I was sitting in an open area with nothing to cover me from them, and I was reading the beginning of Surah Yasin and other parts of the Qur’an. They came upon me and then returned from where they came, and one of them said to the other: This is Dibla, meaning Satan. And God, the Almighty, blinded their sight so that they did not see me, and praise be to God abundantly for that. It was said: The hidden veil is a seal God has placed on their hearts so that they do not understand it or comprehend the wisdom in it, as Qatada said. Al-Hasan said: That is, because they turned away from your reading and ignored you, they are like someone between you and him a veil in your inability to see you, as if there were covers over their hearts. It was said: It was revealed about a people who used to harm the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when he recited the Qur’an, and they were Abu Jahl, Abu Sufyan, Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, Umm Jameel, the wife of Abu Lahab, and Huwaytib. So God, the Most High, concealed His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from their sight when he recited the Qur’an, and they would pass by him without seeing him. This was said by Al-Zajjaj and others. This is the exact meaning of the first statement, and it is the most apparent in the verse, and God knows best. His statement, concealed has two opinions: One of them is that the veil is concealed from you and you do not see it. The second is that the veil conceals from you what is behind it, and concealed means concealing.
17:46: God the Almighty says: And We have placed over their hearts coverings. Coverings are the plural of Kinan, which is what covers something. It was mentioned earlier in Al-An'am. That they may understand it means so that they do not understand it, or out of hatred that they may understand it, meaning that they understand what is in it of commands, prohibitions, wisdom and meanings. This is a refutation of the Qadarites. And in their ears is deafness means deafness and heaviness. There is an implied meaning in the speech, meaning that they may hear it. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an means you say: There is no god but God while you are reciting the Qur'an. Abu Al-Jawza' Aws bin Abdullah said: There is nothing that drives Satan away from the heart more than saying: There is no god but God. Then he recited: And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn their backs in aversion. Ali bin Al-Hussein said: It is His saying: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This was mentioned earlier in the Basmalah: And they turn their backs in aversion It was said: He meant by that the polytheists. It was said that devils. And nafaruun is the plural of nafir, like shahud is the plural of shahid, and qa’ud is the plural of qa’id, so it is accusative in the state. And it is permissible for it to be a source other than the first letter, since his saying walawu means nafaru, so its meaning would be nafaru nafaru.
17:47: God the Almighty said: We know best what they listen to when they listen to you. It was said: The letter ba is redundant in His statement by it meaning they listen to it. They used to listen to the Qur'an from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and then they would flee and say: He is a magician and bewitched, as God the Almighty informed us about them, as stated by Qatada and others. And when they were whispering meaning they were whispering about your matter. Qatada said: Their whispering was that he was crazy, that he was a magician and that he brings up legends of the ancient Egyptians, and other things. It was said: It was revealed when Utbah invited the nobles of Quraish to a meal that he had prepared for them, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered upon them and recited the Qur'an to them and called them to God, so they whispered, saying: A magician and a madman. It was said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Ali to prepare a meal and invite the nobles of the polytheists of Quraysh to it. Ali did that, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon them and recited the Qur’an to them and called them to monotheism, and said: “Say: There is no god but God, so that the Arabs will obey you and the non-Arabs will submit to you.” But they refused, and they were listening to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were saying in secret: He is bewitched and he is bewitched. So the verse was revealed. Al-Zajjaj said: An-Najwa is the name of the source, meaning, when they were whispering, meaning he was walking. When the wrongdoers say, Abu Jahl, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and others like them. You are following none but a bewitched man, meaning someone who was wanted and whom magic had made insane and his affairs were confused. They say that to turn people away from him. Mujahid said: Bewitched means deceived, like his saying: How are you bewitched? meaning from where are you deceived? Abu Ubaidah said: Bewitched means that he has magic, meaning a lung, so he cannot do without food and drink, so he is like you and not an angel. The Arabs say to a coward: His magic has blown up. And everyone who eats or drinks from a human being or something else is bewitched and charmed. Labid said: If you ask us what we are, then we are birds from this enchanted people Imru Al-Qais said: He showed us two places for an unseen matter and we were enchanted by food and drink. That is, we feed and entertain ourselves. In the hadith, “On the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: Who is this woman who is equal to me among the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died between my throat and my chest?”
17:48: The Almighty said: See how they put forth for you examples. He was amazed at their fabrication, how they sometimes say, magician, "madman, and sometimes poet. They have gone astray and cannot find a way," meaning tricks to turn people away from you. It was also said: They have gone astray from the truth and cannot find a way, meaning to guidance. It was also said: A way out of the contradiction in their words in their saying: madman, magician, poet.
17:49: God the Almighty said: And they said, 'When we are bones and fragments' meaning, they said while they were whispering when they heard the Qur'an and heard the matter of al-Qiyamah 75:If he had not been bewitched and deceived, he would not have said this. Ibn Abbas said: Fatat means dust. Mujahid: dirt. And Fatat is what is broken and decayed of everything, such as crumbs, debris and rubble, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, Al-Kisa'i, Al-Farra' and Al-Akhfash. It is said from it that the thing was rafat means it was smashed, so it is marfut. Shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation? "Ana" is an interrogative and what is meant by it is denial and rejection. "Khul'an" is in the accusative case because it is a source, meaning a new resurrection. This was the ultimate denial from them.
17:50: The Almighty said: "Say: Be you stones or iron." That is, say to them, O Muhammad, be, in a way that makes it impossible, stones or iron in strength and power. At-Tabari said: That is, if you are amazed at God's creation of bones and flesh for you, then be stones or iron if you are able. Ali bin Isa said: Its meaning is that if you were stones or iron, you would not have escaped God Almighty if He wanted you, except that it was stated in the form of a command, because it is more eloquent in its obligation. It was said: Its meaning is if you were stones or iron, He would have returned you as He began you, and He would have caused you to die and then brought you back to life. Mujahid said: The meaning is, be whatever you wish and you will be returned. An-Nahhas said: This is a good statement, because they cannot be stones, but the meaning is that they have acknowledged their Creator and denied the resurrection, so it was said to them, Feel the possibility of being whatever you wish, for if you were stones or iron, you would have been resurrected as you were created the first time.
17:51: Or a creation of what is great in your hearts. Mujahid said: He means the heavens, the earth, and the mountains because of their greatness in the souls. This is the meaning of what Qatada said. He says, Be whatever you wish, for God will cause you to die and then resurrect you. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar, Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas, Ibn Jubayr, Mujahid also, Ikrimah, Abu Salih, and Ad-Dahhak said: He means death, because there is nothing greater in the soul of the son of Adam than it. Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt said: Death has a terrible effect on souls. He says: If you were created from stone or iron or were death, I would surely cause you to die and resurrect you, because the power with which I created you, with the power with which I will bring you back. This is the meaning of His statement: And they will say, ‘Who will bring us back?’ Say, ‘He who created you the first time.’ And in the hadith it says: Death will come on the Day of Resurrection in the form of a white ram, and it will be slaughtered between Paradise and Hell. It was said that he meant resurrection, because it was greater in their hearts, as Al-Kalbi said. He created you means He created you and brought you into being. And they will shake their heads at you. The rajaz poet said: He lowered his head towards me and covered his face. He also said: So-and-so moved his head, meaning he moved it. It is transitive and intransitive, as narrated by Al-Akhfash. It is also said: His tooth moved, meaning it moved and fell out. The rajaz poet said: And she lowered her teeth Another said: When she saw me, she lowered her head for me. Another said: There is no water in the reading room unless you rise with a tambourine above the dry place Al-Mahal and Al-Mahala: the great pulley used to draw water for camels. And they say, ‘When is it?’ meaning the resurrection and the return of this time. Say, ‘Perhaps it is near.’ meaning it is near, because perhaps is obligatory, similar to And what do you know? Perhaps the Hour is near. And Perhaps the Hour is near. And everything that is coming is near.
17:52: The Almighty says: On the Day He calls you and you respond with praise to Him. Supplication: the call to the place of assembly with words that all creatures hear, in which God Almighty calls them to come out. It was said: with the shout that they hear, which will be a call for them to gather on the Day of Resurrection. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: You will be called on the Day of Resurrection by your names and the names of your fathers, so make your names good. “Then you will respond with His praise,” meaning with their deserving praise for bringing life back to life. Abu Sahl said: That is, praise be to God, just as he said: By the grace of God, I do not wear the garment of an immoral person, nor do I cover myself with treachery. It was said: Praising God with your tongues. Saeed bin Jubair said: The infidels will emerge from their graves saying: Glory be to You and praise be to You, but their acknowledgment of that Day will not benefit them. Ibn Abbas said: By His praise, by His command, meaning you will say that He is your Creator. Qatada said: By knowing and obeying Him. It was said: The meaning is by His power. It was said: By His calling you. Our scholars said: This is correct, because the blowing of the trumpet is only a reason for the people of the graves to emerge, and in reality it is the emergence of creation by the call of the Truth. God the Almighty said: The Day He will call you, and you will respond with His praise. So they will stand and say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. He said: The Day of Resurrection is a day that begins with praise and ends with it. God the Almighty said: The Day He will call you, and you will respond with His praise. And He said at the end of it: “And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said: Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.” And you think that you have remained but a little. Meaning between the two blasts, and that is because the torment will be withheld from those being tormented between the two blasts, and that is for forty years, then they will sleep. That is what the Almighty said: Who has raised us from this place of ours? So it is specific to the disbelievers. Mujahid said: The disbelievers have a period of slumber before the Day of Resurrection, in which they will find the taste of sleep. Then when the people of the graves are called, they will rise in terror. Qatada said: The meaning is that the world will seem insignificant in their eyes and will become small when they see the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan: And you think that you have remained but a little in the world because of the length of your stay in the Hereafter.
17:53: Indeed, Satan is ever a clear enemy to man. That is, a severe enemy. This was mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah. In the hadith, some people were sitting remembering God, the Almighty, so Satan came to interrupt their gathering, but the angels prevented him. Then he came to some people sitting near them who were not remembering God, so he stirred up trouble between them, so they quarrelled and jumped up. These people who were remembering God said, Let us come and reconcile between our brothers. So they got up and interrupted their gathering, and Satan was happy with that. This is part of his enmity.
17:54: The Almighty says: "Your Lord is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you; or if He wills, He will punish you." This is addressed to the polytheists, and the meaning is: If He wills, He will guide you to Islam and have mercy upon you, or He will cause you to die in polytheism and punish you. This was said by Ibn Jurayj. And the word "most knowing means all-knowing," similar to their saying: God is the Greatest, meaning great. It was said: The address is to the believers, meaning if He wills, He will have mercy upon you by protecting you from the disbelievers of Mecca, or if He wills, He will punish you by giving them power over you. This was said by Al-Kalbi. "And We have not sent you as a guardian over them." This means, We have not entrusted you with preventing them from disbelief, nor have We given you their faith. It was also said: We have not made you a guarantor for them to be taken by them. This was said by Al-Kalbi. The poet said: I remembered Abu Arwa and spent the night as if I were the agent of the cold of past matters. Any sponsor.
17:55: The Almighty said: "And your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth. And We have certainly preferred some prophets over others." He repeated after saying: Your Lord knows best about you to clarify that He is their Creator and that He made them different in their morals, appearances, conditions and wealth, Does He not know who created? (al-Mulk 67:14). And likewise, some prophets were preferred over others out of His knowledge of their condition. This was discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah. And We gave David the Psalms. The Psalms: a book in which there is neither lawful nor unlawful, nor obligations nor limits, but rather it is a supplication, praise and glorification. That is, just as We gave David the Psalms, do not deny that Muhammad was given the Qur'an. And he is in the argument with the Jews.
17:56: The Almighty said: "Say: Call upon those you claim besides Him." When the Quraysh were afflicted with famine and complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, God revealed this verse, meaning: Call upon those you worship besides God and claim that they are gods. Al-Hasan said: He means the angels, Jesus, and Ezra. Ibn Masoud said: He means the jinn. They do not have the power to remove harm from you meaning the famine for seven years, according to Muqatil. Nor to change from poverty to wealth and from sickness to health.
17:57: The Almighty said: Those who call upon Those is the subject of those, those is an attribute of those, and the relative pronoun is omitted, meaning they call upon them. Meaning those are the ones who are called upon. And seek is the predicate, or it could be a state, and those who call upon is the predicate, meaning they call upon His servants to worship Him. Ibn Mas'ud read You call upon with the ta' of addressing. The rest read it with the ya' of the predicate. There is no disagreement that it is with the ya'. In Sahih Muslim from the Book of Interpretation on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas'ud regarding the Almighty's statement: Those who call upon, seeking a means of access to their Lord, he said: A group of jinn converted to Islam and were worshipping, but those who were worshipping remained in their worship, and the group of jinn converted to Islam. In another narration, he said: It was revealed about a group of Arabs who were worshipping a group of jinn, so the jinn converted to Islam and the humans who were worshipping them were unaware, so Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord was revealed. It was also narrated from him that they were the angels who were worshipped by tribes of Arabs, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: Ezra and Jesus. And they seek, they ask God for nearness and closeness, and they implore God the Most High in seeking Paradise, which is the means. God the Most High informed them that the worshipped seek closeness to their Lord. The ha and mim in their Lord refer to the worshippers or the worshipped or all of them. As for they call upon, it refers to the worshippers. And they seek, on the worshipped. Which of them is nearest is the subject and predicate. It is permissible for Which of them is nearest to be a substitute for the pronoun in they seek, and the meaning is that which of them is nearest seeks a means of approach to God. “And they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to be feared.” That is, it is feared and no one is safe from it, so one should beware of it and fear it. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Hope and fear are two times for a person, so if they are equal, his conditions will be sound, but if one of them is more prevalent, the other will be nullified.
17:58: The Almighty said: And there is no town but that We will destroy it meaning, destroy it. Before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. Muqatil said: As for the righteous, it will be with death, and as for the wicked, it will be with punishment. Ibn Mas'ud said: If adultery and usury appear in a town, God will permit their destruction. It was said: The meaning is that there is no unjust town, which is strengthened by His statement: And We would not destroy the towns except while their people were wrongdoers (al-Qasas 28:59). That is, let the polytheists beware, for there is no unbelieving town but that punishment will befall it. That was in the Book meaning, in the tablet. Inscribed means written. The line is the script and writing, and it is originally a source. The line with a fat-ha is the same. Jarir said: Whoever wants, I will sell him my money and I will divorce him. The Tayyim will not complete a single line in their register. Al-Khal’ah with a damma on the kha’: the best of money. The plural of sutra is astār, like sabab and asbāb, then the plural is astāhir. The plural of sutra is astār and sutur, like aflās and fulūs. The word kitab here refers to the Preserved Tablet.
17:59: The Almighty said: And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs that they proposed except that they would deny them and perish as He did to those who were before them. Qatada, Ibn Jurayj, and others said its meaning. So God the Almighty delayed the punishment from the infidels of Quraysh because He knew that among them were those who would believe and among them were those who were born believers. It was mentioned previously in Al-An'am and elsewhere that they asked God to turn Safa into gold for them and for the mountains to move away from them, so Gabriel came down and said: If you wish, what your people asked for will be, but if they do not believe, they will not be given respite. And if you wish, you can wait with them. He said: No, but wait with them. The first is in the accusative case because the prevention occurred to them, and the second is in the nominative case. The ba’ in by the signs is redundant. The metaphor of the speech is: And nothing prevented us from sending the signs except the denial of the former peoples. And God is not prevented from something, so the meaning is the exaggeration in that He does not do, so it is as if He was prevented from it. Then He explained what He did to those who asked for the signs but did not believe in them, saying: And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, meaning a sign that illuminates and shines on the truth of Salih and on the power of God Almighty. This has been mentioned before. But they wronged therewith, meaning they wronged by denying it. It was said: They denied it and disbelieved that it was from God, so God destroyed them with punishment. And We do not send the signs except as a warning, there are five opinions on this: The first: The lessons and miracles that God Almighty made at the hands of the messengers as signs of warning to frighten the deniers. Second: They are verses of vengeance to frighten people from sins. Third: They change conditions from childhood to youth, then to middle age, then to gray hair, so that you may consider the change of your conditions and fear the consequences of your actions. This is the saying of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may God be pleased with him. Fourth: The Qur’an. Fifth: The terrible death, said by Al-Hasan.
17:60: God the Almighty said: And when We said to you, 'Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people,' Ibn Abbas said: The people here are the people of Mecca, and His encompassing them is His destruction of them, meaning that God will destroy them. He mentioned it in the past tense to confirm its occurrence. And by this promised destruction, He meant what happened on the Day of Badr and the Day of the Conquest. It was said: The meaning of encompassed the people is that His power encompassed them, so they are in His grasp and are unable to escape His will, as stated by Mujahid and Ibn Abi Nujayh. Al-Kalbi said: The meaning is His knowledge encompassed the people.
