It was said: What is meant is His protection from the people that they would kill him until he conveyed the message of his Lord, meaning, We did not send you as a guardian over them, but rather you are responsible for conveying it, so convey it with your effort, for We will protect you from them and preserve you, so do not fear them, and go forth with what He commanded you to do of conveying the message, for Our power encompasses everything, as stated by Al-Hasan, Urwah, Qatadah, and others. The Almighty said: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. When He explained that the revelation of the verses of the Qur’an included intimidation, He added to it the mention of the verse of the Night Journey, which is mentioned at the beginning of the Surah. And in Bukhari and Tirmidhi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the Almighty said: And We have not made the vision which We showed you except a trial for the people. He said: It is a vision that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw on the night he was taken on the Night Journey Israa' to the Holy House in Jerusalem. He said: And the accursed tree in the Qur'an is the tree of Zaqqum. Abu 'Eisa al-Tirmidhi said: This is a saheeh hadeeth. And Ibn 'Abbas said: Aisha, Mu'awiyah, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, Sa'eed ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, Ibn Abi Nujayh and Ibn Zayd said: The trial was the apostasy of people who had converted to Islam when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told them that he was taken on the Night Journey. It was also said: It was a dream. This verse declares it to be corrupt, because there is no trial in a dream, and no one would deny it. And Ibn 'Abbas said: The vision in this verse is the vision of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he would enter Makkah in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, so he returned and the Muslims were tempted by that, so the verse was revealed. And the following year he entered it, and God revealed: God has certainly fulfilled the vision of His Messenger in truth (al-Fath 48:27). This interpretation is weak, because the surah is Meccan and that vision was in Medina. And he said in a third narration: He, peace be upon him, saw in a dream the Banu Marwan jumping on his pulpit like monkeys. This upset him, so he was told: This is the world that they have given him. So he was relieved. He did not have a pulpit in Mecca, but it is possible that he saw in Mecca the same vision as the pulpit in Medina. This third interpretation was also said by Sahl ibn Sa’d, may God be pleased with him. Sahl said: This dream is that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, saw the Banu Umayya jumping on his pulpit like monkeys. He was saddened by his humiliation, and he did not laugh again from that day until he died, peace be upon him. Then the verse was revealed informing him that this is because of their rule and ascension, and God makes it a trial and a test for the people. Al-Hasan ibn Ali recited in his sermon regarding his pledge of allegiance to Mu’awiyah: And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time. (Al-Anbiya’: 111). Ibn Atiyyah said: There is a problem with this interpretation, and neither Uthman, nor Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, nor Mu’awiyah are included in this dream. God the Almighty said: And the accursed tree in the Qur’an There is an inversion, meaning that We did not make the vision that We showed you and the accursed tree in the Qur’an except as a trial for the people. And its trial is that when they were frightened by it, Abu Jahl said in mockery, And this is Muhammad threatening you with a fire that burns stones, then he claims that it grows trees and fire eats trees, and we do not know Zaqqum except as dates and foam. Then Abu Jahl ordered a slave girl to bring dates and butter and said to his companions: Catch some. It has been said that the one who said, We do not know Zaqqum except as dates and butter was Ibn Al-Zubayri when he said: May God increase Zaqqum in your home, for it is dates and butter in the language of Yemen. It is possible that both of them said that. Some of the weak were also tempted by this statement, so God the Almighty informed His Prophet, peace be upon him, that He only made the Night Journey and the mention of the tree of Zaqqum as a trial and a test so that those who had previously disbelieved would disbelieve and those who had previously believed would believe. It was also narrated that Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, was told on the morning of the Isra’: Your companion claims that he came from Jerusalem last night! He said: If he said that, then he has told the truth. He was then asked: Do you believe him before you hear from him? He said: Where are your minds? I believe him with the report from heaven, so why should I not believe him with the report from Jerusalem, when heaven is much farther away than that? I said: This report was mentioned by Ibn Ishaq, and its text is: He said: It was from the hadith that reached me about the Prophet’s Night Journey, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Abdullah bin Masoud, Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, Aisha, Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan, Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan, Ibn Shihab Al-Zuhri, Qatadah, and others from the people of knowledge, what was gathered in this hadith, each of them narrating from him some of what he mentioned about his affair when he was taken on the Night Journey, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in his Night Journey and what he mentioned about it was a trial and a test, and his affair was from the affair of God Almighty in His power and authority in which there is a lesson for those of understanding, and guidance and mercy and steadfastness for whoever believed and was truthful and was certain of the affair of God Almighty, so he was taken on the Night Journey, may God bless him and grant him peace, however He willed and as He willed, to show him of His signs what He wanted, until he saw what he saw of His command and His great authority, and His power with which He does what He wants. Abdullah bin Masoud, as I have heard, said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought the Buraq - the beast on which the prophets before him were carried, placing its hoof at the end of its sight - so he was carried on it, then his companion took him out, seeing the signs between heaven and earth, until he reached the Holy House, and he found Abraham, Moses, and Jesus in it, with a group of prophets who had gathered for him, so he prayed with them, then three vessels were brought: a vessel containing milk, a vessel containing wine, and a vessel containing water. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I heard a voice say when it was presented to me: If he takes the water, he will drown and his nation will drown, and if he takes the wine, he will go astray and his nation will go astray, and if he takes the milk, he will be guided and his nation will be guided. So I took the vessel of milk and drank, and Gabriel said to me: You have been guided and your nation has been guided, O Muhammad.” Ibn Ishaq said: I was told on the authority of Al-Hasan that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: While I was sleeping in the sanctuary, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me and nudged me with his foot, so I sat up and did not see anything. Then I returned to my bed, and he came to me a second time and nudged me with his foot, so I sat up and did not see anything. Then I returned to my bed, and he came to me a third time and nudged me with his foot, so I sat down. He took hold of my arm and I got up with him, then he went out to the door of the mosque and there was a white animal between a mule and a donkey, with two wings on its thighs, with which it nudged its feet, and it placed its hoof where it reached its end. It carried me on it and then went out with me, not missing me and I not missing it.” Ibn Ishaq said: It was narrated on the authority of Qatada that he said: It was narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When I approached him to mount him, the sun was shining, so Gabriel placed his hand on his mount and then said: Are you not ashamed, O Buraq, of what you are doing? By God, no servant of God before Muhammad mounted you who was more honorable to Him than him. He said: So he was ashamed until his sweat dripped, then he stopped until I mounted him. Al-Hasan said in his hadith: “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went and Gabriel went with him until he reached the Holy House, and he found Abraham, Moses, and Jesus in it, with a group of prophets. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led them in prayer, then he was brought two vessels: one of them had wine and the other had milk. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the vessel of milk and drank from it and left the vessel of wine. He said: Gabriel said to him: The natural disposition has been guided, and your nation has been guided, and wine has been forbidden to you. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to Mecca. When morning came, he went to Quraysh and told them the report. Most of the people said: This, by God, is the clear matter! By God, the caravan travels from Mecca to Syria for a month, going back for a month and coming back for a month, and Muhammad goes in one night and returns to Mecca! He said: Many of those who had accepted Islam apostatized, and the people went to Abu Bakr and said: What do you think, Abu Bakr, about your companion? He claims that he came to the Holy House tonight, prayed in it, and returned to Mecca. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, said: You are lying about him. They said: Yes, here he is in the mosque telling the people about it. Abu Bakr said: By God, if he said that, then he has spoken the truth, so what is wrong with you? By God, he tells me that report comes to him from the heaven to the earth at any hour of the night or day, and I believe him. This is beyond what you are amazed at. Then he came until he reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Prophet of God, have you told these people that you came to Jerusalem tonight? He said: Yes. He said: O Prophet of God, describe it to me, for I have already visited it. Al-Hasan said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He was raised to me until I looked at him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to describe him to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: You have spoken the truth, I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. Every time he described something to him, he said: You have spoken the truth, I bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. He said: Until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, reached Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him: And you, Abu Bakr, are the truthful. On that day, he called him the truthful. Al-Hasan said: And God, the Most High, revealed about those who apostatized from Islam for that reason: “And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. And the accursed tree is in the Qur’an. And We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression.” This is the hadith of Al-Hasan about the Night Journey of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what was included in it from the hadith of Qatadah. And he mentioned the rest of the Night Journey from those who came before in the biography. Ibn Abbas said: This tree is the Umayyads, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, denied the ruling. This is a weak, innovated statement, and the Surah is Meccan, so this interpretation is far-fetched, unless this verse is Medinan, and that has not been proven. Aisha said to Marwan: May God curse your father while you are in his loins, so you are part of God’s curse. Then he said: And the accursed tree is in the Qur’an, and the curse of this tree did not occur in the Qur’an, but God cursed the infidels and they are the ones who ate it. The meaning is: And the accursed tree is the ones who ate it. This could be based on the Arabs’ saying for every food. Harmful and hated: cursed. Ibn Abbas said: The cursed tree is this tree that twists around the tree and kills it, meaning the thorn. And We frighten them meaning with Zaqqum. But it only increases them the frightening in disbelief.
17:61: The Almighty said: And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam.' The mention of Satan being the enemy of man has already been made, so the conversation drifted to mention Adam. The meaning is: Remember the persistence of these polytheists and their insolence towards their Lord, the story of Iblis when he disobeyed his Lord and refused to prostrate, and said what he said, which is what God the Almighty informed us in His saying: "So they prostrated, except Iblis. He said, 'Should I prostrate to one You created from clay?'" That is, from clay. This is a question of denial. The creation of Adam has already been discussed in full in Surat Al-Baqarah and Surat Al-An'am.
17:62: He said, 'Have you seen me?' meaning, Satan said. The kaf is an emphasis of the address. This which You have honored over me meaning, You have favored over me. He saw the essence of fire better than the essence of clay, but he did not know that essences are similar. This was mentioned in Al-A'raf. This is the accusative of 'are'ayt', which describes it. And honor is a comprehensive name for everything that is praised. And in the speech there is an omission, the meaning of which is: Tell me about this which You have favored over me, why did You favor him when You created me from fire and created him from clay? So it was omitted because the listener knows. And it was said: There is no need to estimate the omission, meaning, do you see this which You have honored over me, so that I will do such and such to him. The meaning of I will seize you in the statement of Ibn Abbas is: I will take control of them. Al-Farra' said it. Mujahid said: I will contain them. Ibn Zayd said: I will lead them astray. The meaning is close, meaning, I will eradicate his offspring by seducing and misleading, and I will overwhelm them. It was narrated from the Arabs: The locusts destroyed the crops if they completely wiped them out. It was also said: Its meaning is I will drive them wherever I want and I will lead them wherever I want. From their saying: I put a halter on the horse, I put a halter on its mouth. And likewise I put a halter on it. The first saying is close to this, because it only destroys the crops with a halter. The poet said: I complain to you about a year that has taken its toll on us and weakened us. And our money was seized and swept away Except a few means the infallible ones, and they are those whom God mentioned in His statement: Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority. But Iblis said that out of conjecture, as God the Most High said: And Iblis proved true about them his conjecture (Saba’: 20), or he knew that it is human nature to be prone to lust, or he based it on the words of the angels: Will You place therein one who will cause corruption therein? (al-Baqarah 2:30). Al-Hasan said: He thought that because he whispered to Adam, peace be upon him, but he did not find him determined.
17:63: The Almighty said: He said, 'Go.' This is an insulting command, meaning, do your best, for we have given you respite. And whoever follows you meaning, obeys you from the descendants of Adam. Then Hell will be your recompense, a full recompense. That is, abundant, according to Mujahid and others. It is an accusative of the source. It is said: I provided it abundantly, and he provided the money himself, he fled abundantly, so he is abundant, so it is intransitive and transitive.
17:64: It contains six issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And provoke means to slip and belittle. Its root is to cut, and from it comes the word tafazza which means to tear a garment. The meaning is to provoke him by cutting him off from the truth. And fear provoked him, meaning it made him belittle it. And he sat down, not reassured. And istafizza is a command to make it impossible, meaning you are not able to mislead anyone, and you have no authority over anyone, so do whatever you want. Second: The Almighty’s saying: With your voice and his voice is every caller who calls to disobeying God Almighty, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Mujahid: Singing, flutes, and amusement. Ad-Dahhak: The sound of the flute. Adam, peace be upon him, had settled the children of Abel on the top of the mountain, and the children of Qabil on the bottom, and among them were beautiful daughters, so the liar flutes played and they could not control themselves from descending and committing adultery, mentioned by Al-Ghaznawi. It was said: With your voice, your whispering. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And attack them with your cavalry and infantry. The root of Ijlab is to drive with a tumultuous movement from the driver. It is said: Ajlab Ijlaban. Jalb and jalbah are sounds. You say from it: Jalaba with emphasis. Jalab means to attack something, and Jilba means to attack it, Jalban and Jalban. Jalbat al-shay’ ila nafsi and Ijtalbatuhu mean the same thing. And Ajlab ‘ala al-‘Adi means to gather against them. So the meaning is to gather against them whatever you can of your tricks. Most of the commentators said: He means every rider and pedestrian in disobedience to God. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: He has horses and men from the jinn and mankind, so whatever rider and pedestrian fights in disobedience to God is from the horses and men of Satan. Saeed bin Jubair and Mujahid narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: Every horse that travels in disobedience to God, and every man that walks in disobedience to God, and every money that is acquired through unlawful means, and every child born out of desire is for Satan. And rajul is the plural of rajil, like sahab and sahib. Hafs read wa rajalka with a kasra on the jim and ma as two dialects. It is said: rajul and rajul meaning rajil. Ikrimah and Qatadah read wa rajalka as a plural. Fourth: And share with them in wealth and children meaning make yourself a partner in that. So share with him in wealth is spending it in disobedience to God, said Al-Hasan. It was also said: It is what they acquired unlawfully, said Mujahid. Ibn Abbas: What they used to forbid from Al-Bahira, Al-Sa’ibah, Al-Wasilah, and Al-Ham. Qatada said. Ad-Dahhak: What they used to slaughter for their gods. And the children, it was said: They are the children of fornication, said Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and Abdullah ibn Abbas. And from him also: It is what they killed from their children and committed crimes against them. And from him also: It is naming them Abd Al-Harith, Abd Al-Uzza, Abd Al-Lat, Abd Al-Shams, and the like. And it was said: It is the dyeing of their children in disbelief until they became Jews and Christians, like the Christians do with their children by immersing them in the water that is theirs, said Qatada. A fifth statement - It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, who said: If a man has intercourse with a woman without saying Bismillah, the jinn will wrap themselves around his urethra and have intercourse with her. This is what God Almighty said: No man or jinn has touched them before them (al-Rahman 55:56), and it will come. It was narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Among you are those who have gone west. I said: O Messenger of God, who are those who have gone west? He said: Those who have a common race of jinn. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim in Nawadir Al-Usul. Al-Harawi said: They were called the west because a strange race entered them. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim said: “The jinn have a similarity to the sons of Adam in matters and mixing, so some of them marry among them. Bilqis, the Queen of Sheba, had one of her parents from the jinn. This will be explained, God willing.” Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: He promised them meaning from them false hopes, and that there will be no resurrection or reckoning, and that if there is a reckoning and Paradise and Hell, then you are more deserving of Paradise than others. This is strengthened by the Almighty’s statement: He promises them and arouses false hopes in them, but Satan promises them nothing but delusion (An-Nisa’: 120) meaning falsely. It was said that he promised them, meaning he promised them victory over whoever intended to harm them. This matter to Satan is a threat and warning to him. It was also said that it is a mockery of him and those who followed him. Sixth: The verse indicates the prohibition of flutes, singing and amusement, as He says: And incite whomever you can among them with your voice and attack them according to the statement of Mujahid. Whatever is the voice of Satan or his actions and what he finds pleasing, it is obligatory to avoid it. Nafi’ narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he heard the sound of a flute, so he put his fingers in his ears and turned his mount away from the road while saying: O Nafi’! Do you hear? I said yes, so he continued until I said no, so he put his hands and turned his mount back to the road and said: I saw the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) hear the sound of a shepherd’s flute and do the same. Our scholars said: If this is what they did with a sound that does not go beyond moderation, then what about the singing and flutes of the people of this time? This will be further explained in Surah Luqman, God willing.
17:65: The Almighty said: Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority. Ibn Abbas said: They are the believers, and we have already discussed this. And sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs. That is, a protector from being accepted by Satan, and a guardian from his plot and evil deceit.
17:66: The Almighty said: Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you through the sea. Driving means driving, and from it the Almighty said: Have you not seen that God drives the clouds? (al-Nur 24:43). And the poet said: O rider, mixing your mount, ask the Banu Asad, what is this sound? And to drive the ark: to drive it with a gentle wind. The ark here is a plural, and it has been mentioned before. The sea is a large amount of water, whether fresh or salty, and this name is often used for salt. This verse is a warning about the blessings and graces of God upon His servants, meaning your Lord who has bestowed upon you such and such, so do not associate anything with Him. That you may seek of His bounty meaning in trade. It has been mentioned before. Indeed, He is ever Merciful to you.
17:67: The Almighty said: And when harm touches you at sea Harm is a term that includes the fear of drowning and stopping one from sailing. The horrors of its states are its turbulence and waves. Wandered are those you call upon except Him Wander means perished and is a derogatory expression for those who call upon a god other than God. The meaning of this verse is that the disbelievers believe that their idols are intercessors and have virtue, and each one of them knows by instinct a knowledge that he is unable to refute that idols have no effect in great hardships, so God stopped them from that in the state of the sea where tricks are cut off. But when He delivered you to land, you turned away meaning from sincerity. And man is ever ungrateful man here is the disbeliever. It was said: And man's nature is ungrateful for blessings except for those whom God protects, so man is the word for the species.
17:68: The Almighty said: Do you then feel secure that He will not cause a part of the land to swallow you up? He explained that He is able to destroy them on land even if they were safe from the sea. Khasf is when the earth collapses with something. It is said: a well is khasif if its foundation collapses. A khasif spring means its pupil has sunk into the head. A spring of water is khasifah meaning its water has sunk. The sun was eclipsed meaning it disappeared from the earth. Abu Amr said: A khasif is a well that is dug in rocks so its water does not stop abundantly. The plural is khasf. The side of the land is the side of the earth, and He called it a side because it becomes a side after the sinking. Also, the sea is a side and the land is a side. It was said: They were on the coast of the sea, and its coast is the side of the land, and they were safe from the terrors of the sea, so He warned them of what they felt safe from on land just as He warned them of what they feared from the sea. Or He sends upon you a violent wind, meaning a strong wind, which throws pebbles, which are small stones, as Abu Ubaidah and Al-Qutbi said. Qatada said: It means stones from the sky that pelt them, as was done to the people of Lot. The cloud that throws hail is called a hasib, and the wind that carries dust and gravel is also called a hasib or hasbah. Labid said: It happened to her that her family lost all their possessions and all their husks. Al-Farazdaq said: We are receiving a reception in the north of the Levant, which will strike us with hailstones like scattered cotton wool. Then you will not find for yourselves a protector or a supporter to protect you from the wrath of God.
17:69: The Almighty said: Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time? meaning into the sea. Then He will send upon you a violent wind. Al-Qassif is a strong wind that breaks violently, from qasaf al-shay' yuqsufhu, meaning it breaks it violently. Qasaf is also: amusement and play, it is said: it is a generator. Then He will drown you for what you disbelieved. That is, for your disbelief. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read We will swallow you up or send upon you that We will return you, then We will send upon you and drown you with the letter nun in the five for emphasis, and because of his saying: Upon us the rest with the letter ya, because of his saying in the verse before: it. Abu Ja`far, Shaibah, Ruways and Mujahid read Fathagarakum with the letter ta as an adjective for the wind. Al-Hasan and Qatadah narrated Fathagarakum with the letter ya with emphasis on the letter ra. Abu Ja`far read the winds here and throughout the Qur'an. It was said: Al-Qassif is the one who destroys on land, and Al-`Aseef is the one who drowns in the sea, as narrated by Al-Mawardi. And his saying: Then you will not find any way to pay us for it. Mujahid said: A revenant. An-Nahhas: It is from revenge. And likewise it is said to everyone who demands revenge or something else: pay and pay and from it then pay with what is acceptable (al-Baqarah 2:178) meaning demand.
17:70: It has three issues: First: The Almighty said: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam the verse. When He mentioned the terror, He also mentioned the children of grace upon them. We honored the double of honor, meaning We made for them honor, meaning honor and superiority. This is the honor of negating deficiency, not the honor of money. This honor includes creating them in this form in the length of stature and beauty of appearance, and carrying them on land and sea, which no animal other than the children of Adam can carry by his will, intention and planning. And He singled them out with what He singled them out with of food, drink and clothing, and this is God’s expansion of animals as the expansion of the children of Adam, because they earn money in particular and not animals, and they wear clothes and eat compound foods. The ultimate goal of every animal is to eat raw meat or uncompounded food. Al-Tabari narrated from a group that the preference is to eat with his hand and the rest of the animals with their mouths. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, mentioned by Al-Mahdawi and Al-Nahhas, and it is the saying of Al-Kalbi and Muqatil, mentioned by Al-Mawardi. Ad-Dahhak said: He honored them with speech and discrimination. Ata: He honored them by straightening their stature and extending it. Yaman: By having a beautiful appearance. Muhammad ibn Kaab: By making Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, one of them. It was said that He honored men with beards and women with forelocks. Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: By giving them dominion over all creation, and subjugating all creation to them. It was also said: By speaking and writing. It was also said: By understanding and discernment. The correct view that is relied upon is that the preference was only by the mind, which is the mainstay of accountability, and by it God is known and His words are understood, and one is led to His bliss and the belief in His messengers. However, since it did not fulfill all that was intended for the servant, messengers were sent and books were revealed. An example of the law is the sun, and an example of the mind is the eye. If it is opened and healthy, it sees the sun and perceives the details of things. Some of the peoples mentioned above are stronger than others. God has also made some animals have characteristics by which He favors the son of Adam, such as the running of the horse, its hearing and sight, the strength of the elephant, the courage of the lion, and the generosity of the rooster. Honor and preference are only by the mind, as we have explained. And God knows best. Second: A group said: This verse requires that the angels are preferred over mankind and the jinn, since they are the exceptions in the Almighty’s saying: nor the angels brought near (An-Nisa’: 172). This is not necessarily the case in the verse, but rather the preference in it is between mankind and the jinn, for in this verse God only enumerated for the children of Adam what He has made special for them from among all other animals, and the jinn are the preferred many, and the angels are those excluded from the preferred many, and the verse did not mention them, but rather it is possible that the angels are better, and it is possible that the opposite is true, and it is possible that they are equal, and in general the discussion does not end with certainty in this matter. Some people avoided speaking about this, just as they avoided speaking about the preference of some prophets over others, since in the hadith: Do not choose between the prophets, and do not prefer me over Jonah, son of Matta. This is nothing, because there is a text in the Qur’an about preference between the prophets. We have explained this in Surat Al-Baqarah, and there is a discussion in it about the preference of the angels and the believer. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And We provided them with good things meaning delicious food and drink. Muqatil said: ghee, honey, butter, dates, and sweets. He made the provision of others what is not hidden from you of straw, bones, and other things. And We preferred them over many of those We created with [definite] preference meaning over the beasts, animals, wild animals, and birds by dominance and control, reward and recompense, preservation, discrimination, and accurate insight. Fourth: This verse refutes what was narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Deprive yourselves of good food, for Satan is only strengthened by it running through the veins. Many Sufis use this as evidence for refraining from eating good foods, but it has no basis, because the Qur’an refutes it, and the established Sunnah contradicts it, as has been stated in more than one place. Abu Hamid al-Tusi narrated that Sahl used to eat jujube leaves for a period of time, and he ate fine fig leaves for three years. Ibrahim ibn al-Banna mentioned that he accompanied Dhul-Nun from Akhmim to Alexandria, and when it was time for him to break his fast, I took out a loaf of bread and some salt that I had with me, and said: Come here. He said to me: Is your salt fine? I said: Yes. He said: You will not succeed! I looked at his bag and saw in it a little barley gruel from which he was sipping. Abu Yazid said: I did not eat anything that the sons of Adam eat for forty years. Our scholars said: This is something that it is not permissible to force the soul to do, because God the Almighty has honored man with wheat and made its husks for their animals, so it is not right to compete with animals in eating straw. As for barley gruel, it causes colic, and if a person limits himself to barley bread and coarse salt, his temperament will be distorted, because barley bread is cold and drying, and salt is dry and astringent and harms the brain and eyesight. If the soul dies to what is good for it and is prevented, then the wisdom of the Creator, glory be to Him, has been corrected by cooling it down, then this affects the body, so this action is contrary to the Shariah and reason. It is known that the body is the mount of man, and if he is not kind to the mount, it will not reach its destination. It was narrated from Ibrahim bin Adham that he bought butter, honey, and fresh bread, and he was asked: All of this? He said: If we find it, we eat it like men eat, and if we do not find it, we are patient like men. Al-Thawri used to eat meat, grapes, and faloodeh, then he would stand up for prayer. There are many examples of this from the predecessors. Sufficient evidence has been presented of it in Al-Ma’idah, Al-A’raf, and others. The first is extremism in religion, if it is authentically reported from them: “And monasticism, which they invented for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them.” (al-Hadid 57:27)
17:71: God Almighty said: On the Day We will call every people with their leader. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding God Almighty’s saying: On the Day when We will call every people with their leader, he said: “One of them will be called and given his book in his right hand, and his body will be stretched out to him sixty cubits, his face will be whitened, and a crown of sparkling pearls will be placed on his head. He will go to his companions and they will see him from afar and say, ‘O God, bring us this and bless us in this,’ until he comes to them and says, ‘Rejoice, for each of you will have something like this.’ As for the disbeliever, his face will be blackened and his body will be stretched out to him sixty cubits in the image of Adam, and he will wear a crown. His companions will see him and say, ‘We seek refuge in God from the evil of this! O God, do not bring this to us.’ He said: ‘So he will come to them and they will say, ‘O God, disgrace him.’ He will say, ‘May God distance you, for each man among you is like this.’” Abu ‘Eisa said: This is a hasan ghareeb hadith. Similar to this is the statement of God, “And you will see every nation kneeling. Every nation will be called to its book. Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.” (Al-Jathiyah 45:28). The book is called a leader because it is referred to in order to know their deeds. Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said: By their Imam, meaning by their book, meaning by the book of each person among them in which is his deeds, his guide, so whoever is given his book in his right hand. Ibn Zayd said: By the book revealed to them. That is, each person will be called by the book he used to recite, so the people of the Torah will be called by the Torah, and the people of the Qur’an by the Qur’an, and it will be said to him: O people of the Qur’an, what did you do, did you comply with its commands, did you avoid its prohibitions? And so on. Mujahid said: By their Imam, by their Prophet, and the Imam is the one who is followed. So it will be said: Bring the followers of Abraham, peace be upon him, bring the followers of Moses, peace be upon him, bring the followers of Satan, bring the followers of idols. So the people of truth will stand and take their book with their right hands, and the people of falsehood will stand and take their book in their left hands. Qatadah said the same. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: By the Imam of their time. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, in his saying: The Day when We will call every people with their Imam. He said: “Everyone will be called with the Imam of their time, the Book of their Lord, and the Sunnah of their Prophet. He will say: ‘Bring the followers of Abraham, bring the followers of Moses, bring the followers of Jesus, bring the followers of Muhammad - may the best prayers and peace be upon them.’ Then the people of truth will stand up and take their Book in their right hands. He will say: ‘Bring the followers of Satan, bring the followers of the leaders of misguidance, an Imam of guidance and an Imam of misguidance.’” Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: With their Imam, meaning with their deeds. Ibn Abbas said the same. Then it will be said: Where are those who are content with what is decreed? Where are those who are patient in the face of what is forbidden? It was also said: With their schools of thought. Then they will call upon those whom they followed in the world: O Hanafi, O Shafi’i, O Mu’tazilite, O Qadari, and so on. They will follow him in good or evil, or in truth or falsehood. This is the meaning of the statement of Abu Ubaidah. It was mentioned earlier. Abu Hurairah said: The people of charity are called from the door of charity, and the people of jihad...? The hadith in full Abu Sahl: It is said, Where is so-and-so the praying and fasting person? And the opposite is the one who tambourines and backbites. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: With their imam, with their mothers. And the imam is the plural of mother. The wise men said: There are three aspects of wisdom in that, the first of which is for the sake of Jesus. The second is to show the honor of al-Hasan and al-Husayn. The third is so that the children of fornication will not be disgraced. I said: There is a problem with this statement, because in the authentic hadith on the authority of Ibn Omar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, He will raise a banner for every traitor and say, ‘This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.’ Narrated by Muslim and Al-Bukhari. His statement, This is the treachery of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, is evidence that people will be called in the Hereafter by their names and the names of their fathers. This refutes those who say that they will only be called by their mothers’ names because that conceals the faults of their fathers. And God knows best. The Almighty’s statement: So whoever is given his record in his right hand strengthens the statement of those who say: With their leader, with their book. It is also strengthened by His statement: We have recorded all things in a clear register (Ya-Sin 36:12). Then those will read their record and will not be wronged a thread. The thread is in the crack of the seed. This has already been mentioned in An-Nisa’.
17:72: God the Almighty said: And whoever is blind in this meaning in this world from considering and seeing the truth. He will be blind in the Hereafter meaning in the matter of the Hereafter and blind. Ikrimah said: A group of people from Yemen came to Ibn Abbas and asked him about this verse, so he said: Read what came before it, your Lord is He who drives the ship for you in the sea - to - as a distinction. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever is blind in these blessings and signs that he saw, he is blind to the Hereafter that he has in this world, he is blind to the blessings of the Hereafter. It was said: The meaning is whoever is blind to the blessings that God bestowed upon him in this world, he is blind to the blessings of the Hereafter. It was said: The meaning is whoever was blind in this world in which He was given respite and granted ease and promised to accept repentance, he is blind in the Hereafter in which there is no repentance. Al-Hasan said: Whoever is a disbeliever and astray in this world, he is blind in the Hereafter, as He said: And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind (Ta-Ha 20:124) and the verses. He said: “And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf. Their refuge will be Hell.” It was said: The meaning of his saying: He will be blind in the Hereafter in all the sayings: He is more blind, because it is from blindness of the heart, and the same is not said about blindness of the eye. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: Because it is a creation like the hand and the foot, so he did not say what blinded him, just as he does not say what supported him. Al-Akhfash said: He did not say that because it has more than three letters, and its root is blind. Some grammarians have permitted what blinded him and what blinded him, because its verb is blind and blind. Al-Farra’ said: An old man in Busra told me that he heard the Arabs say: How black his hair is. The poet said: There is no shade or fruit for you in the high places, and in the low places you have the ghosts of old men. As for the kings, you are today the meanest of them all and the whitest of them is the cook’s robe. Abu Bakr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i made the vowels inclined, and the two letters were left blank, and the rest opened them. Abu Amr made the first vowel inclined and the second open. And he has gone astray means that he cannot find a way to guidance.
17:73: Saeed bin Jubair said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to touch the Black Stone during his circumambulation, but the Quraysh prevented him and said: We will not let you touch it until you touch our gods. He thought to himself and said: What does it matter if I touch it after they invite me to touch the stone? God knows that I hate it. But God Almighty refused that and revealed this verse to him, as stated by Mujahid and Qatadah. Ibn Abbas said in the narration of Ata’: It was revealed about the delegation of Thaqeef, who came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him for something outrageous, saying: Let us enjoy our gods for a year until we take what is offered to them as gifts. When we take it, we will break them and submit, and make our valley sacred as Mecca was made sacred, so that the Arabs may know our superiority over them. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to give them that, so this verse was revealed. It was said: It is the saying of the elders of Quraysh to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Drive away from us these ignorant ones and clients so that we may sit with you and listen to you. So he wanted to do that until he was forbidden from doing so. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Quraysh were alone with the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) one night until morning, talking to him, exaggerating his status, and treating him with disdain and ostentatiousness. They said: You do something that no one else does, and you are our master, O our master. They kept at him until he almost came close to them in some of what they wanted, then God protected him from that, and God revealed this verse. The meaning of to tempt you is to remove you. It is said: You tempted a man from his opinion if you removed him from what he was on, as Al-Harawi said. It was also said that they divert you, but the meaning is the same. From that which We have revealed to you meaning the ruling of the Qur’an, because giving them what they asked for would be contrary to the ruling of the Qur’an. To invent something else about Us meaning to fabricate something about Us other than what We have revealed to you. This is the saying of Thaqeef: And our valley is sacred just as Makkah is sacred, its trees, birds and wild animals. If the Arabs ask you why you singled them out, say: God commanded me to do this so that it will be an excuse for you. And if they had done what they wanted, they would have taken you as a friend, meaning if you had done what they wanted, they would have taken you as a friend, meaning they would have been your friend and befriended you. It is taken from the word khalla with a dammah, which means friendship, because of his inclination towards them. It was also said: They would have taken you as a friend, meaning poor. It is taken from the word khalla with a fathah on the kha, which means poverty, because of his need for them.
17:74: The Almighty said: And had We not established you meaning on the truth and protected you from agreeing with them. You would have almost inclined toward them meaning leaned. A little meaning a little inclined. Qatada said: When this verse was revealed, the Prophet, peace be upon him, said: 4044 O God, do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye. It was said: The apparent address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but its hidden meaning is to inform about Thaqeef. The meaning is: And they almost inclined towards you, meaning they almost informed about you that you inclined towards what they said, so their action was attributed to him metaphorically and broadly, as you say to a man: You almost killed yourself, meaning the people almost killed you because of what you did, as mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. It was said: He did not intend to incline towards them, rather the meaning is: And were it not for God’s grace upon you, you would have inclined towards agreeing with them, but God’s grace was completed upon you so you did not do it, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri. Ibn Abbas said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was infallible, but this is a definition for the nation so that none of them incline towards the polytheists in any of the rulings and laws of God Almighty.
17:75: And His statement: Then We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death meaning if you had relied upon it, We would have made you taste twice the punishment of life in this world and twice the punishment of death in the Hereafter. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others. This is the ultimate threat. The higher the degree, the greater the punishment for disobedience. God the Almighty said: O wives of the Prophet! Whoever among you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her twofold (al-Ahzab 33:30). The double of something is its equivalent twice, and the double may be the share, as God the Almighty said: For each is double (al-A’raf 7:38) meaning a share. This was mentioned previously in Al-A'raf.
17:76: This verse is said to be Madani, as mentioned in the beginning of the surah. Ibn Abbas said: The Jews were jealous of the Prophet's position in Madinah, so they said: The prophets were sent to Ash-Sham, so if you are a prophet then go there, for if you go there we will believe you and have faith in you. This resonated in his heart because of what he loved about their Islam, so he left Madinah one stage later, and God revealed this verse. Abdur-Rahman bin Ghanam said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on the Tabuk expedition, intending nothing but Ash-Sham. When he arrived at Tabuk, he revealed: And they were about to expel you from the land after the surah had been completed, and he was ordered to return. It was also said that it is Makkan. Mujahid and Qatadah said: It was revealed about the people of Makkah's concern to expel him, and if they had expelled him they would not have been given a respite, but God ordered him to emigrate, so he left. This is more correct, because the surah is Makkan, and because what preceded it is report about the people of Makkah, and the Jews were not mentioned. And his saying: from the land means the land of Makkah. As he said: I will never leave the land (Yusuf 12:80), meaning the land of Egypt, his evidence is And how many a city was stronger than your city which expelled you (Muhammad 47:13), meaning Mecca. Its meaning is: Its people intended to expel him, so that is why he added to it and said: expelled you. It was said: All the infidels intended to lure him out of the land of the Arabs by conspiring against him, but God prevented him, and if they had expelled him from the land of the Arabs, they would not have been given respite, and this is the meaning of his saying: And then they will not remain behind you except a little. Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah read they will not remain behind you except a little. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, and Abu Amr read behind you, and its meaning is after you. Ibn ‘Amir, Hafs, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read behind you, and Abu Hatim chose it, considering his saying: Those who stayed behind rejoiced in their sitting behind the Messenger of God (al-Tawbah 9:81), and its meaning is also after you. The poet said: The houses were destroyed by their disagreement, as if the Shawatibs had spread a mat between them. Basat Al-Bawasit, in Al-Mawardi. It is said: A woman split the palm branch if she splits it to make mats from it. Abu Ubaid said: Then the shatiba throws it to the sieve. It was also said: Khalafak means after you. And Khilafak means opposing you, as mentioned by Ibn Al-Anbari. Except a little has two meanings: One of them: The period of time they stayed after him was between their expulsion of him and their killing on the day of Badr. This is the statement of those who mentioned that they were Quraysh. Second: What happened between that and the killing of Banu Qurayzah and the expulsion of Banu Nadir, and this is the statement of those who said that they were the Jews.
17:77: The Almighty said: The way of those We sent before you of Our messengers meaning they are punished as the way of those We sent, so it is accusative with the implication of they are punished, so when the preposition was dropped, the verb worked, as Al-Farraa said. It was said: It is accusative with the meaning of sunna the way of those We sent. It was said: It is accusative with the estimation of deleting the kaf, the estimation is they will not remain behind you except a little like the way of those We sent, so do not stop on this estimation on his saying: except a little and stop on the first and second. Before you of Our messengers is a good stop. And you will not find any change in Our way meaning there is no breaking of its promise.
17:78: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun. When He mentioned the plots of the polytheists, He commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, to be patient and to maintain prayer, and in it is seeking victory over the enemies. And similar to it is: “And We certainly know that your breast is constrained by what they say. So exalt [God] with praise of your Lord and be among those who prostrate.” (al-Hijr 15:97-98). The meaning of establishing prayer was mentioned earlier in the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. This verse, by consensus of the commentators, refers to the obligatory prayers. The scholars differed regarding the decline of the sun, with two opinions: One: It is the sun’s disappearance from the sky’s servant, as stated by Omar and his son, Abu Hurairah, Ibn Abbas, and a group of scholars from the Tabi’in and others. The second: That the sun sets, as stated by Ali, Ibn Masoud, and Ubayy ibn Ka’b, and it was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Mawardi said: Whoever made the sun’s disappearance a name for its setting, it is because a person rubs his eyes with his palm to make them clear when it is setting, and whoever made it a name for its disappearance, it is because he rubs his eyes because of the intensity of its rays. Abu Ubaid said: Its disappearance is its setting. And the sun has disappeared, meaning it has set. And Qutrub recited: This is the place where my feet are, Rabah Dhab, until I rubbed them with ease Barah with the first letter b open is on the same weight as hizam and qatam and raqas is one of the names of the sun. Al-Farra’ narrated it with the first letter b closed and it is the plural of rahah which means the palm, meaning it disappeared while he was looking at it and he put his palm on his eyebrow. And from this is the saying of Al-Ajjaj: The sun is about to set, I push it with my palm so it can move Ibn al-A'rabi said: Al-Zahlufah is a smooth sloping place, because they slide on it. He said: Al-Zahlufah is like rolling and pushing. It is said: I pushed him and he slipped. It is also said: The sun has set. Dhu al-Rummah said: Lamps that are not led by stars nor by the setting sun Ibn Atiyah said: “Daluk is the inclination - in the Arabic language - so the beginning of Daluk is the noon prayer and the end of it is the sunset. From the time of Daluk until sunset it is called Daluk, because it is in a state of inclination. So God the Almighty mentioned the prayers that occur in the state of Daluk and at it, so this includes Dhuhr, Asr, and Maghrib, and it is correct that Maghrib is included in the darkness of the night. Some people have said that the time of Dhuhr prayer continues from Dhuhr until sunset, because God the Almighty has made its obligation dependent on Daluk, and this is all Daluk, as Al-Awza’i and Abu Hanifa said in preference. Malik and Al-Shafi’i referred to it in the case of necessity. Second: The Almighty’s saying: “Until the darkness of the night.” Malik narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The sun’s decline is its inclination, and the darkness of the night is the gathering of the night and its darkness. Abu Ubaidah said: The darkness is the blackness of the night. Ibn Qays al-Ruqayyat said: This night has become dark and I complain of worry and insomnia It has been said: The dusk of the night is the disappearance of twilight. It has also been said: The approach of its darkness. Zuhair said: Her hands kept giving generously, while she was distracted, until darkness and dusk fell. It is said: Ghasaq al-layl ghusuqan. Ghasaq is a noun with a fatha on the sin. The root of the word is from the word silaan. It is said: Ghasaqat al-'ayn if it flows, taghsaq. And the wound ghasaqan, meaning yellow water flowed from it. And the muezzin aghsaq, meaning he delayed the Maghrib prayer until the twilight of the night. Al-Farra' narrated: Ghasaq al-layl and aghsaq, and dhalam and adhalam, and daja and ajja, and ghabs and aghbas, and ghabsh and aghbash. Al-Rabi' bin Khathim used to say to his muezzin on a cloudy day: Ghasaq, aghsaq. He said: He delayed the Maghrib prayer until the night ghasaq, which is its darkness. Third: The scholars differed regarding the last time for Maghrib. It was said that its time is one time and there is no time for it except when the sun is hidden. This was made clear in the Imamate of Gabriel, as he prayed it on both days at one time, which is sunset. This is the apparent view of the Maliki school of thought according to his companions. It is also one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i in the well-known view from him, and Al-Thawri said the same. Malik said in Al-Muwatta’: When the twilight disappears, the time for Maghrib has ended and the time for ‘Isha’ has begun. This is what Abu Hanifa and his companions, Al-Hasan bin Hayy, Ishaq, Abu Thawr and Dawud said, because the time from sunset to twilight is all dusk. And the hadith of Abu Musa, in which it says: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked about Maghrib on the second day and delayed it until it was when twilight fell, narrated by Muslim. They said: This is more appropriate than the reports of the Imamate of Gabriel, because he was delayed in Madinah and the Imamate of Gabriel was in Makkah, and the delayed is more appropriate than his action and command, because it abrogates what came before it. Ibn Al-Arabi claimed that this is the well-known view of the Maliki school of thought, and his view in his Muwatta’ which he recited throughout his life and dictated during his life. The point here is that the rulings related to nouns are related to their beginnings or their ends, or is the ruling connected to all of them? The strongest view is that the ruling is connected to their beginnings so that mentioning them is not superfluous. If it is connected to their beginnings, then it is then considered whether it is connected to all of them until the end. I said: The opinion of expansion is more likely. Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Muhammad Abdul-Ghani bin Saeed narrated from the hadith of Al-Ajlah bin Abdullah Al-Kindi from Abu Al-Zubayr from Jabir who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left Mecca close to sunset and did not pray Maghrib until he reached Sarif, which is nine miles away. As for the opinion of abrogation, it is not clear even if the date is known, because combining is possible. Our scholars said: The hadiths of Gabriel are interpreted as preferring the time of Maghrib, and therefore the nation agreed on hastening it and hastening to it at sunset. Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: We do not know of any Muslim who delayed the establishment of Maghrib in a congregational mosque after sunset. The hadiths of expansion clarify the time of permissibility, so the conflict is removed and combining is valid, and it is more appropriate than preference according to the agreement of the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence. No, it includes applying each of the two pieces of evidence, and the opinion of abrogation or preference is the omission of one of them. And God knows best. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And the Qur’an of dawn. The word Qur’an is in the accusative case in two ways: One of them is that it is in apposition to the prayer, meaning: And establish the Qur’an of dawn, meaning the morning prayer, as Al-Farra’ said. The people of Basra said: It is in the accusative case for enticement, meaning then you should recite the Qur’an of dawn, as Al-Zajjaj said. And it is referred to as the Qur’an specifically, and not the other prayers, because the Qur’an is the greatest of them, since its recitation is long and aloud, as is well-known and written, also from Al-Zajjaj. I said: The practice of Medina has been established on the desirability of lengthening the recitation in the morning prayer to an extent that does not harm those behind it - he recites in it the long surahs of the Mufassal, followed by the Dhuhr and Jumu’ah - and shortening the recitation in the Maghrib prayer and making it moderate in the Asr and Isha’ prayers. It has been said that the Asr prayer is shortened like the Maghrib prayer. As for what was reported in Sahih Muslim and other books about lengthening where shortening is established, or shortening where lengthening is established, such as his recitation of the two Mu’awwidhat in the dawn prayer - as narrated by al-Nasa’i - and the recitation of al-A’raf, al-Mursalat and al-Tur in the Maghrib prayer, then it is abandoned by practice. And because of his denunciation of Mu’adh’s lengthening when he led his people in the Isha’ prayer and began with Surat al-Baqarah. It was reported in Sahih. And with his ordering the imams to shorten it, he said: O people, some of you are repulsive, so whoever among you leads the people in prayer should make it short, for among them are the young and the old, the sick and the weak, and those with a need. He also said: If one of you prays alone, let him prolong it as he wishes. All of this is recorded in the Sahih Hadith. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And the Qur’an of dawn is evidence that there is no prayer without recitation, because He called the prayer the Qur’an. Scholars have differed regarding recitation in prayer. The majority of them held that it is obligatory for the imam and the individual to recite the Umm al-Qur’an in every rak’ah. This is the well-known opinion of Malik. It was also narrated from him that it is obligatory in most of the prayer. This is the opinion of Ishaq. It was also narrated from him that it is obligatory in one rak’ah, as was said by Al-Mughira and Sahnun. It was narrated from him that recitation is not obligatory in any part of the prayer. This is the most severe of the narrations from him. It was also narrated from Malik that it is obligatory in half of the prayer, and this is the opinion of Al-Awza’i. It was also narrated from Al-Awza’i and Ayoub that it is obligatory for the imam, the individual, and the person being led in prayer in every case. This is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i. It has been fully discussed in Al-Fatihah. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: It was witnessed. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his saying: ‘And the recitation of the dawn prayer. Indeed, the recitation of the dawn prayer is witnessed.’ He said: It is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.” This is a good and authentic hadith. It was narrated by Ali bin Musahir on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Abu Saeed on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The virtue of praying together over praying alone is twenty-five degrees. The angels of the night and the angels of the day gather in the morning prayer. Abu Hurairah said: “Recite, if you wish, the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed.” For this reason, one should pray early in the morning. Whoever does not pray early, his prayer will not be witnessed except by one of the two groups of angels. For this reason also, Malik and Ash-Shafi’i said: Praying early in the morning is better. Abu Hanifa said: It is better to combine praying early in the morning with dawn. If he misses that, then praying early in the morning is better than praying early in the morning. This is contrary to what the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to do, which was to constantly pray early in the morning. Also, it would cause one to miss out on the witnessing of the angels of the night. And God knows best. Seventh: Some scholars have used the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it as evidence that the dawn prayer is neither part of the night prayer nor part of the day prayer. I said: According to this, the afternoon prayer is neither part of the night prayer nor part of the day prayer, because in the Sahih, “on the authority of the eloquent Prophet, peace be upon him, in what Abu Hurairah narrated: Angels take turns among you at night and during the day, and they gather at the afternoon prayer and the dawn prayer.” The hadith. It is known that the afternoon prayer is during the day, so the dawn prayer is also during the night, but it is not like that. Rather, it is during the day like the afternoon prayer, as evidenced by fasting and faith, and this is clear.
17:79: It contains six issues: The Almighty said: And from the night “min” is for partialization. The fa in His statement so strive is a coordinator of an implied word, meaning get up and pray at night. With it means with the Qur’an. And praying at night is from the word hujood and it is one of the opposites. It is said: hajood means sleeping, and hajood means staying up late, as opposites. The poet said: Did she not visit and the people of Mina are asleep? I wish her shadow would return to Mina. last: Did you not knock on our door while our companions were asleep? So, the burdens of generosity became more generous. Meaning asleep. And wujud and tahajjud have the same meaning. And wujudtuhu means to afflict him, and wujudtuhu means to wake him up. Tahajjud is waking up after a sleep, so it became a name for prayer, because one pays attention to it. So tahajjud is getting up for prayer from sleep. Al-Aswad, Alqamah, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad and others said its meaning. Ismail ibn Ishaq al-Qadi narrated from the hadith of al-Hajjaj ibn Umar, the companion of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Does any of you think that if he gets up at night all night that he has prayed tahajjud? Tahajjud is prayer after sleep, then prayer after sleep, then prayer after sleep. This is how the prayer of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was. It was also said: al-hajjud is sleep. It is said: a man stayed up late and threw off the hajjud, which is sleep. And the one who gets up for prayer is called muttahjid, because the muttahjid is the one who throws off the hajjud, which is sleep, from himself. This verb is similar to tahawwab, taharja, ta'athim, hanath, taqdir, and tajans, if it throws off from himself. And similar to it is the saying of God Almighty: And you remained joking (al-Waqi’ah 56:65). Its meaning is that you regretted, that is, you rejected joking from yourselves, which is the cheerfulness and happiness of the soul. It is said that a man is joking if he is very happy and laughs. The meaning of the verse: And a time of the night in which I stay up in prayer and reading. Second: The Almighty’s saying: A voluntary prayer for you, meaning an honor for you, as stated by Muqatil. The scholars differed about singling out the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for mention without his nation. It was said: The night prayer was obligatory for him because of his saying: A voluntary prayer for you, meaning an obligation in addition to the obligation imposed on the nation. I said: There are two aspects to this interpretation: One of them: calling the obligatory act a voluntary act, and this is a metaphor, not a reality. Second: His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: Five prayers that God has imposed on His servants. And the Almighty said: They are five and they are fifty. I do not change my opinion. This is a text. So how can it be said that he imposed on him an additional prayer in addition to the five? This is not correct, even though it was narrated from him, peace be upon him: “Three things are obligatory upon me and for my nation: voluntary night prayer, witr, and siwak.” It was said: The night prayer was voluntary from him and was initially obligatory for everyone, then the obligation was abrogated and night prayer became voluntary after obligatory, as Aisha said, as will be explained in Surat Al-Muzzammil, God willing. Based on this, the command to perform voluntary prayers is recommended and the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he is forgiven. So if he voluntarily does something that is not obligatory upon him, that is an increase in status. And others from the nation do voluntary prayers as expiations and to make up for a deficiency in the obligatory prayer. Mujahid and others said its meaning. It was said: It is a gift, because a servant does not attain a greater gift of happiness than success in worship. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station. There are four different opinions regarding the praiseworthy station: The first: and it is the most correct - intercession for the people on the Day of Resurrection, as stated by Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said: The people will be on the Day of Resurrection as corpses, each nation following its prophet saying: O so-and-so, intercede, until intercession ends with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. That is the day when God will raise him to the praised station. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Anas, he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us: When the Day of Resurrection comes, people will gather together and go to Adam and say to him, Intercede for your descendants. He will say, “I am not for it, but you should go to Abraham, peace be upon him, for he is the friend of God.” They will go to Abraham and he will say, I am not for it, but you should go to Moses, for he spoke to God. Moses will be brought and he will say, “I am not for it, but you should go to Jesus, peace be upon him, for he is the spirit of God and His word.” Jesus will be brought and he will say, “I am not for it, but you should go to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.” He will be brought and I will say, I am for it. He mentioned the hadith. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise.” He was asked about it. He said: It is intercession. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Fourth: If it is proven that the praised station is the matter of intercession that the prophets, peace be upon them, are competing for, until the matter ends with our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, so he intercedes with this intercession for the people of the situation to hasten their reckoning and to be relieved from the horror of their situation, and it is specific to him, peace and blessings be upon him, and for that reason he said: I am the master of the children of Adam, and I do not boast. Al-Naqqash said to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) about three intercessions: the general intercession, the intercession to be the first to enter Paradise, and the intercession for the people of major sins. Ibn Atiyyah: It is well-known that there are only two intercessions: the general intercession, and the intercession to remove the sinners from the Fire. This second intercession is not contested by the prophets, rather they intercede and the scholars intercede. Judge Abu al-Fadl Iyad said: The intercessions of our Prophet (peace be upon him) on the Day of Resurrection are five intercessions: the general intercession. The second is to admit people to Paradise without being held accountable. The third is for people from the monotheists of his nation who deserved Hell because of their sins, so our Prophet (peace be upon him) will intercede for them, and for whomever God wills to intercede and they will enter Paradise. This intercession is what the innovators, the Khawarij and the Mu'tazilah, denied, forbidding it based on their corrupt principles, which is the rational entitlement based on goodness and badness. The fourth is about those sinners who entered Hell and will be released through the intercession of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and other prophets, angels, and their believing brothers. The fifth is about increasing the ranks in Paradise for its people and elevating them, and the Mu’tazila do not deny this, nor do they deny the intercession of the first gathering. Fifth: Judge Iyad said: It is known from widespread transmission that the righteous predecessors asked for the intercession of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and desired it. Based on this, no attention should be paid to the statement of those who said: It is disliked to ask God to grant you the intercession of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because it is only for sinners. It may be, as we mentioned, to lighten the reckoning and increase the degrees. Then every rational person who acknowledges his shortcomings and is in need of forgiveness, who does not take his deeds for granted and fears that he will be among those who perish, and this speaker is required not to supplicate for forgiveness and mercy, because they are also for those who commit sins. All of this is contrary to what is known from the supplications of the predecessors and successors. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever says when he hears the call, “O God, Lord of this perfect call and the established prayer, grant Muhammad - may God bless him and grant him peace - the means and the excellence and raise him to the praised station which You promised him,” my intercession will be permissible for him on the Day of Resurrection.” The second statement: The praised position is giving him the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection. I said: There is no contradiction between this statement and the first, because he will have the banner of praise in his hand and will intercede. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am the master of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and I do not boast. I will hold the banner of praise, and I do not boast. There will be no prophet on that day, Adam or anyone else, except that he will be under my banner.” Hadith. The third statement: What Al-Tabari narrated from a group, including Mujahid, that they said: The praised station is that God the Most High will seat Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, with him on His throne, and they narrated a hadith about that. Al-Tabari supported the permissibility of that with an exaggeration of opinion, and it only comes out with a subtlety in meaning, and there is some distance in it. However, it is not denied that it was narrated, and knowledge interprets it. Al-Naqqash mentioned from Abu Dawud Al-Sijistani that he said: Whoever denies this hadith is accused in our view, the people of knowledge have not ceased to speak about it, whoever denies its permissibility is interpreting it. Abu Omar said: And Mujahid, even if one of the imams interprets the Qur’an, he has two opinions that are abandoned by the people of knowledge: one of them is this and the second is in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: Some faces, that Day, will be radiant, looking at their Lord (al-Qiyamah 75:22-23). He said: Waiting for the reward, not from looking. I said: This was mentioned in the chapter of Ibn Shihab in the hadith of revelation. It was also narrated from Mujahid regarding this verse that he said: He will seat him on the throne. This interpretation is not impossible, because before God created all things and the throne was self-sufficient, then He created things without needing them, but rather to demonstrate His power and wisdom, and to make known His existence, His oneness, the perfection of His power and His work with all His perfect actions. He created for Himself a throne on which He rose as He wished without it being in contact with Him, or the throne being a place for Him. It was said: He is now in the manner in which He was before He created space and time, so according to this statement it is the same in permissibility that He seated Muhammad on the throne or on the earth, because God’s sitting on the throne does not mean moving, disappearing, and changing states from standing and sitting and the state that occupies the throne, rather He is seated on His throne as He informed about Himself without how. And His seating Muhammad on the throne does not necessitate for him the attribute of divinity or remove him from the attribute of servitude, rather it is raising his position and honoring him over His creation. As for his statement in al-Naba 78:with him, it is like his statement: Indeed, those who are with your Lord (al-A’raf 7:206), and My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise (al-Tahrim 66:11), and Indeed, God is with the doers of good (al-Ankabut 29:69) and the like. All of that is related to the rank, status, favor, and high degree, not to the place. Fourth: He will be taken out of Hell through his intercession for whoever is taken out. This was said by Jabir ibn Abdullah. It was mentioned by Muslim. We have mentioned it in the Book of Remembrance, and God is the Grantor of success. Sixth: Scholars differed about whether standing at night is a cause for the Praised Station, with two opinions: One of them is that the Creator, the Most High, makes whatever He wills of His action a cause for His grace without knowing the reason for it, or knowing the reason for it. The second is that standing at night involves seclusion with the Creator and communion without people, so He gave seclusion with Him and communion with Him in standing, which is the Praised Station. And people are differentiated in it according to their degrees, and the most noble of them in it is the degree of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he is given what no one else is given and intercedes for what no one else intercedes for. And perhaps from God Almighty is obligatory. And station is an accusative of circumstance, meaning in a station or to a station. At-Tabari reported on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Praised Station is the station in which I intercede for my nation.” So the station is the place in which a person stands for great matters, such as stations before kings.
17:80: It was said: The meaning is, Take me as a trust of truth, and send me on the Day of Resurrection as a mission of truth, to connect with His saying, Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise, as if when He promised him that, He ordered him to supplicate so that He would fulfill the promise to him. It was also said: He brought me into what was commanded and brought me out of what was forbidden. It was also said: He taught him what to supplicate with in his prayers and other things, to bring him out from among the polytheists and bring him into a place of security, so He brought him out of Mecca and made him go to Medina. This meaning was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca, then he was ordered to emigrate, so And say, My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and bring me out a truthful exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority was revealed. He said: A good and authentic hadith. Ad-Dahhak said: It is his exit from Mecca and his entry into Mecca on the day of the conquest in safety, Abu Sahl when he returned from Tabuk and the hypocrites had said: The more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble (al-Munafiqun 63:8), meaning bringing honor and bringing victory into Mecca. And it was said: The meaning is, Enter me into the matter with which You have honored me of prophethood with a truthful entrance and bring me out of it with a truthful exit when You cause me to die. Mujahid said that its meaning is that entrance and exit with a damma on the mim mean entering and exiting, like His statement, Make me descend to a blessed abode (al-Mu’minun 23:29), a descent in which I do not see anything I dislike. This is the reading of the general public. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Nasr bin Asim read entrance and exit with a fatha on the two mims meaning entering and exiting. The first is a quadrilateral and this is a trilateral. Ibn Abbas said: Enter me into the grave with a truthful entrance at death and bring me out with a truthful exit at the resurrection. And it was said: Enter me wherever You have entered me with truth and bring me out with truth, meaning do not make me one of those who enter with one face and exit with another, for the one with two faces will not be honorable with You. And it was said: The verse is general in all matters that one undertakes and attempts in travels and deeds, and awaits the disposition of fate in death and life.
