So it is a supplication, and its meaning is: O Lord, set right my rank in all matters and my chest. And His statement, And grant me from Yourself authority. Nasir. Al-Sha’bi and Ikrimah said: That is, a firm argument. Al-Hasan went to the fact that it is honor, victory, and the manifestation of his religion over all religions. He said: So God promised him that he would take away the kingdom of Persia, Rome, and others and give it to him.
17:81: There are three issues: First: Al-Bukhari and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered Mecca in the year of the conquest, and around the Ka`bah were three hundred and sixty idols. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to stab them with a stick in his hand, and sometimes he said with a stick, and he said: ‘The truth has come and falsehood has vanished, for falsehood is bound to vanish. The truth has come, and falsehood can neither begin nor bring it back.’” The wording of Al-Tirmidhi. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Likewise in the hadith of Muslim: an idol. In another narration: an idol. Our scholars said: They were this number because they used to venerate an idol on one day and set aside the greatest of them for two days. His saying: So he began to stab them with a stick in his hand. It is said that they were fixed with lead, and that whenever he stabbed an idol in its face, it would fall on its back, or in its back, it would fall on its face. He used to say: ‘The truth has come and falsehood has vanished, for falsehood is bound to vanish.’” Abu `Umar and Al-Qadi `Iyad narrated it. Al-Qushayri said: Not a single idol remained of them except that… He went down on his face, then ordered it to be broken. The second: In this verse there is evidence of breaking the idols of the polytheists and all the idols if they are overcome by them, and the meaning includes breaking all the instruments of falsehood, and what is only suitable for disobeying God, such as tambourines, lutes, and flutes that have no meaning except to distract from the remembrance of God the Most High. Ibn al-Mundhir said: And in the meaning of idols are the images made of mud and wood and the like, and everything that people make that has no benefit except the forbidden distraction, and it is not permissible to sell anything of it except idols that are made of gold, silver, iron, and lead, if they are changed from what they are and become carved or cut, then it is permissible to sell them and buy with them. Al-Muhallab said: And whatever of the instruments of falsehood is broken and there is benefit in their body after breaking them, then their owner is more deserving of it as a property, unless the imam sees burning them with fire in the sense of severity and punishment in money, and the burning of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with him, has already been mentioned, and the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, intended to burn the homes of those who did not attend the congregational prayer, and this is a basis for punishment in money with his saying, peace be upon him, about the she-camel that was cursed by its owner: Leave her, for she is cursed.” So he removed her kingdom from her as a punishment for her companion, and as a punishment for what she had called upon him for. Omar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, poured milk mixed with water over his companion. Third: What we mentioned of the interpretation of the verse, see “His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: By God, Jesus, son of Mary, will descend as a just judge. He will break the cross, kill the pigs, abolish the jizyah, and leave the camels alone so that no one will run after them.” The hadith was narrated by the two Sahihs. From this chapter, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, tore the curtain that had pictures on it, and this is also evidence of the corruption of pictures and musical instruments as we mentioned. All of this prohibits the prohibition of taking them and requires their owner to change them. The owners of these pictures will be punished on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to them: Bring to life what you have created, and that is enough for you! This meaning will come in An-Naml, God willing. His saying: And say, ‘The truth has come,’ meaning Islam, and it was said: the Qur’an, as Mujahid said, and it was said: jihad, and falsehood has perished, as Mujahid said. The correct thing is to generalize the wording to the possible end, so the interpretation is that the Shari’ah has come with everything that is contained within it, falsehood has perished, falsehood has become void, and from this is the perishing of the soul, which is its nullity. It is said that his soul perished, it perished, and I destroyed it, Indeed, falsehood is bound to perish, meaning it will not remain, and the truth is what is established.
17:82: It contains seven issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And We send down The majority read it with a nun, and Mujahid read and We send down with a light ya, and Al-Marwazi narrated it from Hafs, and min is for the beginning of the goal, and it is correct that it is for clarifying the type, as if he said: And We send down what contains healing from the Qur’an. And in al-Naba 78:Whoever does not seek healing from the Qur’an, then God will not heal him, and some of the interpreters denied that min is for partiality, because it is preserved from requiring that some of it is not healing in it, Ibn Atiyyah: This does not require him, rather it is correct that it is for partiality according to the fact that its sending down is only part, so it is as if he said: And We send down from the Qur’an something that is healing, what is in it is all healing. Second: The scholars differed about whether it is a cure, with two opinions: One of them is that it is a cure for the hearts by removing ignorance from them and removing doubt, and to uncover the heart from the disease of ignorance in order to understand the miracles and matters that indicate God Almighty. The second is a cure for apparent diseases by incantation and seeking refuge and the like. The imams narrated, and the wording is from Al-Darqutni, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent us on a military expedition of thirty riders. He said: So we stopped at a group of Arabs and asked them to host us, but they refused. He said: Then the chief of the tribe was stung, so they came to us and said: Is there anyone among you who can incant from a scorpion sting? In the narration of Ibn Qatah: The king is dying. He said: I said: Yes, but I will not do so until you give us something. They said: Then we will give you thirty sheep. He said: So I recited to him Al-Hamdulillah Rabb Al-Alamin seven times and he recovered. In the narration of Sulayman ibn Qatah on the authority of Abu Sa`id, he recovered and recovered. He sent us the inn and sent us the sheep. My companions and I ate the food and they refused to eat from the sheep, until we came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I told him the report. He said: How do you know that it is a charm? I said: O Messenger of God, something has been put in my mind. He said: Eat and feed us from the sheep. He included it in the Book of Sunan, and included it in the Book of Praise from the hadith of Al-Sari ibn Yahya, he said: Al-Mu`tamir ibn Sulayman told me on the authority of Layth ibn Abi Salim on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: It is beneficial, by God’s permission, for leprosy, madness, elephantiasis, stomach ailments, tuberculosis, fever and the soul to write with saffron or with ochre, meaning I seek refuge in the perfect words of God. And all of His names are general, from the evil of the poisonous and the gloomy, from the evil of the evil eye, from the evil of an envier when he envies, from Abu Farwa and his offspring,” thus he said, and he did not say from the evil of Abu Qutra, the evil eye: which afflicts with evil, says: I seek refuge in Him from every evil scourge, and as for his saying: I seek refuge in Him from the incidents of the gathering, he says: It is time and it is said severity, and the poisonous: the specific, it is said: How is the poisonous and the general, and the poisonous is the poison, and from Abu Farwa and his offspring and he said: Thirty-three angels came to their Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, and said: It has poured on our land, so He said: Take soil from your land and wipe your forelocks, or he said: We advise you of the incantation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, I will never succeed who conceals it or takes shackles for it, then write the opening of the book and four verses from the beginning of Al-Baqarah, and the verse in which the winds are directed and the Throne Verse and the two verses after it, and the endings of Surat Al-Baqarah from the place To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth (al-Baqarah 2:284), to the end of it, and ten from the beginning of Al- Imran and ten from the end of it, and the first verse of An-Nisa, and the first verse of Al-Ma’idah, and the first verse of Al-An’am, and the first verse of Al-A’raf, and the verse in Al-A’raf Indeed, your Lord is God, who created the heavens and the earth (al-A’raf 7:54), until the verse is concluded, and the verse in Yunus from the place “Moses said, ‘What you have brought is magic. Indeed, God will invalidate it. Indeed, God does not amend the work of corrupters.’” (Yunus 10:81), and the verse in Taha, “And throw down what is in your right hand, it will swallow up what they have made. Indeed, what they have made is only the trick of a magician. And the magician will not succeed, wherever he is.” (Ta-Ha 20:69), and ten from the beginning of As-Saffat, and Say, He is God, the One. (al-Ikhla 112:1), and the two Mu’awwidhat, write in a clean vessel, then wash it three times with clean water, then take three handfuls of it, then perform ablution with it as he does for prayer, and perform ablution before his ablution for prayer until he is pure before performing ablution with it, then pour it. On his head, chest and back, and he does not use it for istinja’, then he prays two rak’ahs, then he seeks healing from God, the Almighty and Majestic, and he does that for three days, as much as it takes to write a book each day, in another narration: And from the evil of Abu Qatra and his offspring, and he said: Then wipe your forelocks and he did not doubt. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Aisha: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to blow on himself during the illness in which he died, reciting the two protective surahs. When he became seriously ill, I used to blow on him with them and wipe himself with his hand because of its blessing. So I asked Al-Zuhri how he used to blow. He said: He used to blow on his hands, then wipe his face with them. Malik narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Aisha: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ill, he would recite the two protective surahs over himself and spit or spit.” Abu Bakr ibn Al-Anbari said: The linguists said: The linguists said that the interpretation of nafath is to blow without saliva, and the meaning of tafal is to blow with saliva. The poet said: If he recovers, I will not spit on him, but if he is missing, he is entitled to compensation. And Dhu al-Rummah said: And from the depths of the deep water, a year has passed above it. Whenever the people sense its water, they spit. He wanted to blow sparkle, and what the scholars have said about blowing will come in Surat Al-Falaq, God willing. Third: Ibn Masoud narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, disliked incantations except with the two Mu’awwidhat. Al-Tabari said: This is a hadith that cannot be used as evidence in religion, because its transmitters are those who do not know. If it were authentic, it would either be a mistake or abrogated, because of his, peace be upon him, saying in al-Fatihah 1:How do you know that it is an incantation? If incantations with the two Mu’awwidhat are permissible, and they are two surahs from the Qur’an, then incantations with the rest of the Qur’an are like them in permissibility, because it is all Qur’an. It was narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said: “The cure for my nation is in three things: a verse from the Book of God, a lick of honey, or a cut from a cupper.” Raja’ Al-Ghanawi said: Whoever does not seek healing with the Qur’an will not be healed. Fourth: The scholars differed regarding the Nashr, which is to write something from the names of God or from the Qur’an, then wash it with water, then wipe the patient with it or give him to drink. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab permitted it. It was said to him: A man is taken from his wife, is it permissible for him to be released and Nashr? He said: There is nothing wrong with it, and what is beneficial is not forbidden, and Mujahid did not see that verses from the Qur’an should be written and then washed and then given to the person who is frightened. Aisha used to recite the two Mu’awwidhat in a vessel and then order that it be poured over the patient. Al-Mazari Abu Abdullah said: The Nashr is a well-known matter among the people of incantation, and it was called that because it spreads from its owner, i.e. it is released, and from them is Al-Hasan and Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i. Al-Nakha’i said: I fear that a calamity will befall him, and it seems that he went to the point that what the Qur’an brings is closer to being followed by a calamity than to providing healing. Al-Hasan said: I asked Anas and he said: They mentioned from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that it is from the devil. Abu Dawud narrated from “the hadith of Jabir bin Abdullah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about ecstasy and he said: It is from the work of the devil.” Ibn Abd Al-Barr said: These are soft traces and have possible aspects, and it has been said: This is carried if it is outside of what is in the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from the known treatment, and the Nashr is from the type of medicine, so it is a washing away of something that has merit, so it is Like the ablution of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is nothing wrong with incantations as long as there is no polytheism in them. Whoever among you is able to benefit his brother, let him do so.” I said: We have mentioned the text in the bulletin with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, and that this can only be from the Book of God, so let it be relied upon. Fifth: Malik said: There is nothing wrong with hanging books that contain the names of God the Almighty on the necks of the sick as a way of seeking blessings from them if the one who hangs them does not intend to ward off the evil eye by hanging them. This means before something of the affliction descends on the healthy animal or human being, for fear of the evil eye descending. Everything that is hung after the affliction descends from the names of God the Almighty and His book is a hope for relief and recovery from God the Almighty, so it is like the permissible incantations that the Sunnah has mentioned as permissible for the evil eye and other things. It was narrated by Abdullah bin Amr that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of you is frightened in his sleep, let him say: I seek refuge in the perfect words of God from His anger and the evil of His punishment and from the evil of the devils and their presence.” Abdullah used to teach it to his sons, whoever of them reached puberty, and whoever did not reach puberty, he wrote it and hung it on them. If it is said: It was narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever hangs something, it will be entrusted to him.” And Ibn Mas`ud saw an amulet tied on the mother of his son, so he pulled it hard and cut it off and said: The family of Ibn Mas`ud To those who are rich in polytheism. Then he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Amulets, charms, and love charms are from polytheism. It was said: What is love charms? He said: What she endears herself to her husband. It was narrated on the authority of Uqbah ibn Aajir al-Juhani that he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever hangs an amulet, may God not perfect his life. Whoever hangs a talisman, may God not give him peace in his heart. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: The amulet is a necklace with amulets on it, and the love charm is beads. Abu Omar said: The amulet in the speech of the Arabs is a necklace, and its meaning according to the people of knowledge is what is hung around the necks of necklaces for fear of the evil eye or something else that it may descend or not descend before it descends, so may God not perfect his health and well-being. Whoever hangs a love charm, which is similar in meaning, may God not give him peace, meaning may God not bless him in what he is in of well-being. And God knows best. All of this is a warning against what the people of ignorance used to do of hanging amulets and necklaces, and they thought that they would protect them and ward off calamity from them, but no one can ward that off except God, the Almighty, and He is The healer and the afflicted, He has no partner, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade them from what they used to do in their ignorance, and on the authority of Aisha she said: What is hung after the calamity descends is not from the amulets, and some of the people of knowledge disliked hanging the amulet in any case before the calamity descends and after it, and the first statement is more correct in the trace and consideration, God Almighty willing, and what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud may mean by what he disliked hanging other than the Qur’an things taken from fortune-tellers and soothsayers, because healing with the Qur’an whether hung or not is not polytheism, and his saying, peace be upon him: Whoever hangs something is entrusted to it, so whoever hangs the Qur’an should take charge of it and not entrust it to anyone else, because the Almighty is the one sought after and relied upon in healing with the Qur’an, and Ibn al-Musayyab was asked about the talisman, should it be hung? He said: If it is on a reed or a piece of paper, it is a protection, and this is on the condition that what is written is the Qur’an. And on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he did not see anything wrong with a man hanging something from the Book of God if he put it down during intercourse or when defecating. And Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn `Ali permitted the talisman to be hung on children, and Ibn Sirin did not see anything wrong with something from the Qur’an being hung by a person. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying, And a mercy to the believers, is the relief of distress, the purification of faults, and the expiation of sins, along with the reward that the Almighty has bestowed upon them for reciting it, as Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites a letter from the Book of God will receive a good deed for it, and a good deed is multiplied by ten. I do not say that Alif, Lam, Meem is a letter, but rather Alif, Lam, and Meem are letters.” He said: This is a good, authentic, strange hadith. And it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss has already been mentioned, because of their denial. Qatada said: No one sits with the Qur’an except that he leaves it with an addition or a subtraction, then he recited, And We send down from the Qur’an that which is a healing and a mercy to the believers, and similar to this verse is His saying, “Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guide and a healing. But those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is, upon them, blindness.’” (Fussilat 41:44), and it was said: It is a healing in the obligatory duties and rulings because of the clarification in it.
17:83: The Almighty said: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself. That is, those whom the Qur'an increases in loss are characterized by turning away from contemplating the signs of God and being ungrateful for His blessings. It was said that it was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, and the meaning of turned away is that he became arrogant and distant, and far away is the reverse of it, and the meaning is: he distanced himself from fulfilling the rights of God Almighty. It is said: the thing is far away, and I distanced it and I distanced myself from it mean the same thing, that is, I distanced myself and I distanced myself, so I distanced myself, that is, I removed it so it became distant, and they distanced themselves, and the distant place is the distant place. Al-Nabaghah said: You are like the night that overtakes me, even if I think that the distance from you is vast. Ibn Amir read in the narration of Ibn Dhakwan na’a like ba’a, the hamza is at the end, and it is in the manner of the heart from na’a, as it is said: ra’a and ra’a, and it was said: it is from na’u which is rising and standing, and it may also be said for falling and sitting na’u, and it is from the opposites, and it was read wa-na’ta’ with the fatha of the noon and the kasra of the hamza, and the general na’a is in the weight of ra’a, And if evil touches him, he is hopeless meaning if he is afflicted with hardship from poverty or illness or misery, he despairs and loses hope, because he does not trust in the grace of God Almighty.
17:84: The Almighty said: "Say: Each one acts according to his nature." Ibn Abbas said: his side, and Ad-Dahhak said it, Mujahid: his nature, and from him: his sharpness, Ibn Zayd: according to his religion, Al-Hasan and Qatada: his intention, Muqatil: his nature, Al-Farra: according to his method and the school of thought that he was created with, and it was said: Say: Each one acts according to what is most difficult for him and most likely to be correct in his belief, and it was said: it is taken from the form, it is said: you are not according to my form nor my likeness, the poet said: Every person who is similar to him does what a person does, so he is his family The form is the example, the counterpart and the beat, as the Almighty said: And another of his likeness are pairs (Surah Sad: 58), and the form with a broken shin is the form, it is said: a beautiful-looking girl, and all of these sayings are close, and the meaning is: that everyone works according to what is similar to his origin and the morals that he is accustomed to, and this is a censure of the disbeliever and praise of the believer, and the verse and the one before it were revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira, Al-Mahdawi mentioned it So your Lord knows best who is best guided in the way meaning the believer and the disbeliever and what will happen from each one of them, and it was said: best guided in the way meaning quicker to be accepted, and it was said: better in religion, and it was narrated that the Companions, may God be pleased with them, discussed the Qur’an, so Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, said: I read the Qur’an from beginning to end and I did not see in it a verse more hopeful and better than the saying of the Blessed and Exalted: “Say: Each one works according to his nature” for nothing is similar to the servant except disobedience and nothing is similar to the Lord except forgiveness, and Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: I read The Qur’an from beginning to end, I have not seen a verse in it that is more hopeful and better than the words of God Almighty: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful: The revelation of the Book is from God, the Almighty, the Knowing, the Forgiver of sin, the Accepter of repentance, the Severe in penalty, the Lord of bounty (Ghafir 40:1-3). Forgiveness of sins is based on acceptance of repentance, and in this there is an indication for the believers. Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, said: I read the entire Qur’an from beginning to end, and I have not seen a verse that is more hopeful and better than the words of God Almighty: Inform My servants that it is I who am the Forgiving, the Merciful (al-Hijr 15:49). Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: I read the Qur’an from beginning to end, and I have not seen a verse that is more hopeful and better than the words of God Almighty: “Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.’” (al-Zumar 39:53). I said: I read the Qur’an from beginning to end and I did not see a verse better and more hopeful than the words of God Almighty: Those who believe and do not mix their belief with injustice - those will have security, and they are [rightly] guided. (al-An’am 6:82)
17:85: Al-Bukhari, Muslim and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah, who said: While I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a field, and he was leaning on a palm branch, the Jews passed by. Some of them said to each other: Ask him about the spirit. He said: What is it that makes you angry about him? Some of them said: He will not meet you with anything that you dislike. They said: Ask him. So they asked him about the spirit, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, held back and did not answer them at all. I knew that revelation was being sent to him, so I stood still. When the revelation came down, he said: (And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord. And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.)", the wording of Al-Bukhari. In Muslim: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent, and in it: And what they have been given. People differed about the spirit that was asked about, which spirit is it? It was said: It is Gabriel. Qatada said: He said: Ibn Abbas was concealing it. It was said: It is Jesus. It was said: The Qur’an, as will be explained at the end of Al-Shura. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: He is an angel from the angels who has seventy thousand faces, in each face seventy thousand tongues, in each tongue seventy thousand languages. He glorifies God Almighty in all those languages. God Almighty creates from every glorification an angel who flies with the angels until the Day of Resurrection. Al-Tabari mentioned it. Ibn Atiyyah said: I do not think the statement is correct from Ali, may God be pleased with him. I said: Al-Bayhaqi narrated: Abu Zakariya told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, Abu Al-Hasan Al-Taraifi told us: Uthman bin Saeed told us: Abdullah bin Salih told us, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Salih, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: And they ask you about the spirit, he says: The spirit is an angel. And with his chain of transmission, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Salih, Abu Haran with a kasra on the ha told me: Yazid bin Samurah, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, that he said regarding His statement, the Most High: And they ask you about the spirit, he said: It is an angel from the angels who has seventy thousand faces... The hadith with its wording and meaning. And Ata narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The spirit is an angel who has eleven wings and a thousand faces, who glorifies God until the Day of Resurrection, mentioned by Al-Nahhas, and on his authority: An army from the soldiers of God who have hands and feet who eat food, mentioned by Al-Ghaznawi, and Al-Khattabi said: And some of them said: It is an angel from the angels with a description that they placed from the greatness of creation, and most of the people of interpretation went to the fact that they asked him about the spirit and its path in the human body, and how it mixes with the body. And the connection of life to Him, and this is something that only God Almighty knows, and Abu Saleh said: The soul was created like the creation of the children of Adam, and they are not children of Adam, for they have hands and feet, and the correct thing is vagueness, because of His saying: (Say: The soul is from the command of my Lord), meaning it is a great matter and a great affair from the command of God Almighty, vague about it and leaving out its details, so that man knows with certainty his inability to know the truth of himself with knowledge of its existence, and if man is like this in knowing himself, then his inability to perceive the truth of the Truth is more appropriate, and the wisdom of that is the inability of the mind to perceive the knowledge of a creature adjacent to it, indicating that it is more incapable of perceiving its Creator. God the Almighty said: And of knowledge you have been given only a little. There is a difference of opinion as to who was addressed by this. A group said: Only the questioners. A group said: What is meant is the Jews as a whole. This is the reading of Ibn Mas`ud: And what they have been given. He narrated it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. A group said: What is meant is all of them, and this is the correct reading. This is the reading of the majority: And what you have been given. The Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: How can we not be given of knowledge except a little while we have been given the Torah, which is wisdom? And whoever has been given wisdom has been given much good? So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, opposed them with the knowledge of God, and they were defeated. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stated explicitly in his saying in some hadiths: No, meaning that what is meant by what you have been given is the entire world. This is because the Jews said to him: Do you mean us or your people? He said: No. It is in this meaning that the verse was revealed: And if all the trees on the earth were pens (Luqman 31:27). At-Tabari, may God have mercy on him, narrated this! It has been said: Those who asked about the soul were the Quraysh. The Jews said to them, “Ask him about the People of the Cave, about Dhul-Qarnayn, and about the soul. If he tells you about two and withholds one, then he is a prophet.” So he told them the story of the People of the Cave and the story of Dhul-Qarnayn, as will come. And he said about the soul: Say, ‘The soul is from the command of my Lord,’ meaning from the matter that no one knows except God. Al-Mahdawi and other commentators mentioned this on the authority of Ibn Abbas.
17:86: The Almighty’s saying: And if We willed, We could surely take away that which We have revealed to you meaning the Qur’an, meaning just as We were able to send it down, We could. And if I willed, I could take it away until the creation forgot it. This is connected to His saying: And of knowledge you have been given only a little meaning if I willed that I should take away that little, I could do so. Then you would not find for yourself concerning it a protector over Us meaning a supporter who would return it to you, except as a mercy from your Lord meaning but We do not will that as a mercy from your Lord, so it is an exception that is not from the first. And it was said: except that your Lord has mercy on you, so He does not take it away.
17:87: The Almighty said: Indeed, His favor upon you has been great If He made you the master of the children of Adam, and gave you the praised station and this noble book, and Abdullah bin Masoud said: The first thing you will lose from your religion is trustworthiness, and the last thing you will lose is prayer, and that this Qur'an is as if it has been taken away from you, you will wake up one day and you will not have anything of it with you. A man said: How can that be, O Abu Abd al-Rahman! We have established it in our hearts and established it in our copies of the Qur'an, we teach it to our children and our children teach it to their children until the Day of Resurrection! He said: It will be taken away in one night and will take away what is in the copies of the Qur’an and what is in the hearts, so that people will become like animals. Then Abdullah recited: {And if We will, We can surely take away that which We have revealed to you}. Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated it with a similar meaning. He said: Abu Al-Ahwas informed us on the authority of Abdul Aziz ibn Rafi’ on the authority of Shaddad ibn Muqal who said: Abdullah, meaning Ibn Mas’ud, said: This Qur’an that is among you is about to be taken away from you. I said: How can it be taken away from us when God has established it in our hearts and established it in our copies of the Qur’an?! He said: It will be taken away in one night and will take away what is in the hearts and will take away what is in the copies of the Qur’an, and people will become poor because of it. Then he recited: {And if We will, We can surely take away that which We have revealed to you}. This is a sound chain of transmission. Ibn Umar said: The Hour will not come until the Qur’an returns from where it was revealed, making a sound like the sound of bees. God will say: What is the matter with you? It will say: O Lord, from You I came out and to You I will return. I recite but no one acts upon me. I recite but no one acts upon me. I said: The meaning of this has been transmitted from the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas and Hudhayfah. Hudhayfah said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Islam will be worn out as the embroidery on a garment wears out, until no one knows what fasting, prayer, rituals, or charity are. The Book of God will be destroyed in one night, and not a single verse of it will remain on earth. There will remain groups of people, old and old, who will say: We found our fathers saying this, ‘There is no god but God,’ and they do not know what prayer, fasting, rituals, or charity are.” Silah said to him: ‘Nothing but God will benefit them!’ And they do not know what prayer, fasting, rituals, or charity are. Hudhayfah turned away from him, then he repeated it three times, and Hudhayfah turned away from him each time. Then Hudhayfah turned to him and said: O Silah! It will save them from the Fire, three times. It was narrated by Ibn Majah in Sunan. Abdullah bin Omar said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out with his head bandaged due to pain, so he laughed. He ascended the pulpit, praised God and thanked Him, then said: O people, what are these books that you are writing? Books other than the Book of God. God is about to become angry with His Book and will not leave a page or a heart without taking from it.” They said: O Messenger of God, what about the believing men and women on that Day? He said: Whoever God wants good for, He will leave in his heart There is no god but God. It was mentioned by Al-Tha’labi, Al-Ghaznawi, and others in the interpretation.
17:88: That is, as a helper and supporter, like when poets cooperate in reciting a verse of poetry. It was revealed when the infidels said: If we wished, we could say something like this. So God Almighty called them liars. The discussion of the miraculous nature of the Qur’an has already been mentioned at the beginning of the book. Praise be to God. They will not come is the answer to the oath in if and it may be made jussive to indicate a condition. The poet said: If what I told you today is true, then I will stay in the hot day for the sun to shine
17:89: The Almighty said: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example. That is, We directed the statement in it with every example that must be considered, from the verses and lessons and encouragement and intimidation, commands and prohibitions and stories of the ancients, Paradise and Hell and the Resurrection. But most of the people refused except disbelief. He means the people of Mecca. He made the truth clear to them and opened the way for them and gave them respite until it became clear to them that it was the truth, but they refused except disbelief when the truth became clear. Al-Mahdawi said: There is no argument for the Qadari in their saying: It is not said that he refused except for the one who refused to do what he is able to do, because even if the disbeliever is not able to believe in the judgment of God upon him by turning away from it and His sealing on his heart, he was able at the time of the respite and respite to seek the truth and distinguish it from falsehood.
17:90: The Almighty said: And they said, 'We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth.' The verse was revealed about the leaders of Quraysh, such as Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi'ah, Abu Sufyan, Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, Abu Jahl, Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Abu Al-Bukhtari, Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, and others. This is because when they were unable to oppose the Qur'an and were not satisfied with it as a miracle, they gathered, as Ibn Ishaq and others mentioned, after sunset at the back of the Ka'bah. Then some of them said to each other: Send to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and speak to him until you make excuses for him. So they sent to him: The nobles of your people have gathered to speak to you, so go to them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them, thinking that they had changed their minds about what he had spoken to them about. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was keen, loved their guidance, and was saddened by their difficulty, until he sat with them and they said to him: O Muhammad! We have been sent to you to speak to you, and by God we do not know of any Arab who has brought upon his people what you have brought upon your people. You have insulted the fathers, and by God we do not know of any Arab who has brought upon his people what you have brought upon your people. You have insulted the fathers, and you have insulted the gods, and you have made fools of dreams, and you have divided the community. There is no ugly matter that I have not done between us and you, or as they said to him. If you have only come with this hadith to seek money, we will collect for you from our money until you are the wealthiest among us. If you are only seeking honor among us, we will make you our leader. If you want a king, we will make you our king. If what comes to you is a vision that you see that has overcome you, and they used to call the follower of the jinn a vision, then perhaps that is what we have spent our money seeking medicine for you until we cure you of it or excuse you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: What is wrong with me is that you say that I have not come with what I have come to you to seek your money, nor honor among you, nor kingship over you, but God has sent me to you as a messenger and revealed to me a book and commanded me to be I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you. If you accept from me what I have brought to you, then it is your portion in this world and the Hereafter, but if you reject it, I will be patient for the sake of God’s command until God judges between me and you, or as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said. They said, O Muhammad, if you are not accepting from us anything that we have offered you, then you know that there is no one among the people who has a narrower land, less water, or a harsher life than us, so ask your Lord who sent you with what He sent you with, so let him remove these mountains that have become narrow for us, and expand our land for us and cut through it rivers like the rivers of the Levant, and let him send to us those of our fathers who have passed away, and let among those He sends to us be Qusayy ibn Kilab, for he was a truthful old man, so we will ask them about what you say, is it true or false? If they believe you and you do what we ask, then we will believe you, and we will know your status with God the Most High, and that He sent you as a Messenger as you say. So he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them, “I have not been sent to you for this. I have only come to you from God the Most High with what He sent me with, and I have conveyed to you what I have sent to you. If you accept it, it is your portion in this world and the hereafter. If you reject it, I will be patient for the sake of God until God judges between me and you. They said: If you do not do this for us, then take it for yourself! Ask your Lord to send with you an angel who will confirm what you say and will speak to us about you, and ask Him to make for you gardens, palaces, and treasures of gold and silver that will make you independent of what we see you seeking, for you stand in the markets and seek a living as we seek it, so that we may know your virtue and your status with your Lord if you are a Messenger as you claim. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: I will not do this, nor am I the one who asks his Lord for this, nor was I sent with this to you, but God sent me as a bearer of good tidings and a warner, or something like that. If you accept what I have brought to you, then it is your portion in this world and the Hereafter, and if you reject it, I will be patient for the sake of God’s command until God judges between me and you. They said: Then cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces as you claim that your Lord, if God wills, will do, for we will not believe you unless you do it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is up to God, the Almighty, if He wills, He will do it to you. They said: O Muhammad, how did your Lord know that we would sit with you and ask you about what we asked you about and request from you what we request, so He would come to you? He will teach you what you have brought us back with, and will tell you what He will do to us since we do not accept what you have brought us. It has reached us that only a man from Yamamah called Ar-Rahman is teaching you this, and by God we will never believe in Ar-Rahman. We have excused ourselves to you, O Muhammad, and by God we will not leave you and what you have conveyed from us until we destroy you or you destroy us. And their speaker said: We worship the angels, who are the daughters of God. And their speaker said: We will not believe in you until you bring God and the angels and a tribe. So when they said that to the Messenger of God, he stood up from them and with him stood Abdullah bin Abi Umayya bin Al-Mughira bin Abdullah bin Umar bin Makhzum, who was his cousin, and he was from Atika bint Abdul Muttalib, and he said to him: O Muhammad! Your people offered you what they offered you and you did not accept it from them. Then they asked you for themselves things so that they would know your status with God as you say, and they would believe you and follow you, but you did not do it! Then they asked you to take for yourself what would know your favor to them and your status with God, but you did not do it! Then they asked you to hasten for them some of the punishment with which you threaten them, but you did not do so! Or something like that. By God, I will never believe in you until you take a ladder to the sky, then climb it while I watch until you reach it, then bring with you a document with four angels to testify that you are as you say. By God, if you did that, you would not think that I would believe you! Then he turned away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away to his family, sad and sorry for what he had missed from his people when they called him, and for what he saw of their distancing him. All of this is the wording of Ibn Ishaq, and Al-Wahidi mentioned on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then God Almighty revealed: “And they said, ‘We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth.’” Yanbu’an means the eyes, on the authority of Mujahid, and it is a verb from naba’a yanbu’, and Asim, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read tajajr lana with a lightened vowel, and Abu Hatim chose it because the spring is one, and they did not differ in the gushing forth of rivers that it is doubled. Abu Ubaid said: The first is like it, Abu Hatim said, it is not like it, because the first is followed by yanbu’ which is one, and the second is followed by rivers which are plural, and the doubled vowel indicates plurality. It was answered that yanbu’an even if it is one, what is meant by it is plural, as Mujahid said. Spring is a water spring, plural springs.
17:91: God Almighty says: Or you have a garden of palm trees and grapes and rivers gush forth within it abundantly. Qatada read: or you will have a garden in the middle of it meaning in the middle of it.
17:92: God Almighty said: Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments, as you have claimed, or you bring God and the angels face to face. Or the sky falls is the reading of the general public, and Mujahid read or the sky falls on the attribution of the action to the sky, a scavenging definitely, from Ibn Abbas and others, and the scavenging with the opening of the seen is the plural of scavenging, and it is the reading of Nafi', Ibn Amir and Asim, the rest a scavenging with the sukun of the seen, Al-Akhfash said: Whoever reads a scavenging of the sky makes it singular, and whoever reads a scavenging makes it plural, Al-Mahdawi said: And whoever sukun the seen, it is permissible for it to be the plural of scavenging and it is permissible for it to be a source, from scavenging something if you cover it, so it is as if they said: Drop it as a layer on us, and Al-Jawhari said: The scavenging is a piece of something, it is said: Give me a scavenging of your garment, and the plural is scavenging and scavenging, and it is said: the scavenging and the scavenging are one, Or you bring God and the angels as a tribe meaning witnessing, from Qatada and Ibn Jurayj, Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Abbas said: As a guarantor, Muqatil said: A martyr, Mujahid: It is the plural of the tribe, meaning The angels are of different types, tribe by tribe. It was said: They are guarantors who guarantee that you will bring him to us.
17:93: The Almighty said: Or you have a house of adornment meaning of gold, according to Ibn Abbas and others. Its origin is adornment, and adorned is decorated, and the adornments of water are its paths. Mujahid said: I did not know what adornment was until I saw it in the reading of Ibn Masoud a house of gold, meaning we will not submit to you with this poverty that we see. Or you ascend into the sky meaning you ascend. It is said: I ascended the ladder, I ascended, if I ascended and ascended like it. And we will not believe in your ascension meaning for the sake of your ascension, and it is a source like he went, he goes, he goes, he descends, likewise he rose, he ascends, he ascends, until you bring down to us a book that we can read meaning a book from God Almighty to every man of us, as God Almighty said: But every man of them wants to be given spread out pages (Al-Muddathir: 52), Say, Glory be to my Lord and the people of Mecca and Syria read, He said, Glory be to my Lord, meaning The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that to glorify God Almighty above being incapable of anything and above being objected to in an action. It was said: All of this is astonishment at God Almighty being incapable of anything and above being objected to in an action. It was said: All of this is astonishment at the extremes of their disbelief and their suggestions. The rest say on the matter, that is, say to them, O Muhammad, Was I that is, what am I except a human messenger following what is revealed to me from my Lord, and God does whatever He wills of these things that are not within the power of humans. Have you heard of any human being who came with these signs? Some atheists said: This is not a convincing answer, and they made a mistake because he answered them and said: I am only a human being and I am not able to do anything that you asked me, and I do not have the right to choose from my Lord, and the messengers before me did not bring to their nations everything they wanted and sought, and my way is their way, and they were limited to what God gave them of His signs indicating the truth of their prophethood, so if they established proof for them, it would not be necessary for their people to suggest anything else, and if it were necessary for God to bring them everything they suggested of signs, then it would be necessary for Him to bring them whomever they chose from the messengers, and it would be necessary for every person to say: I do not believe until I am brought a sign contrary to what others asked for. This leads to the fact that the management is up to the people, and the management is up to God the Most High.
17:94: The Almighty said: And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them meaning the messengers and books from God calling to it, except that they said out of ignorance, Has God sent a human being as a messenger? meaning God is too great for His messenger to be from among the humans, so God Almighty explained their extreme stubbornness because they said: You are like us, so we are not required to submit, and they neglected the miracle. The first an is in the accusative case by dropping the preposition, and the second an is in the nominative case by preventing meaning: And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them except their saying: Has God sent a human being as a messenger?
17:95: God Almighty knows that the angel is only sent to the angels, because if He sent an angel to the humans, they would not be able to see him in the form in which he was created. Rather, He enabled the prophets to do that by creating in them what they could see so that it would be a sign and a miracle for them. A similar verse to this has already been mentioned in Al-An'am, which is His statement: “And they said, ‘Why was an angel not sent down to him?’ And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not have been reprieved. And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man.” (Al-An'am: 8-9), and we have already discussed this.
17:96: God Almighty said: “Say: Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.” It is narrated that the infidels of Quraish said when they heard his statement: Are you anything but a human messenger? So who will testify that you are the Messenger of God? Then the verse was revealed: “Say: Sufficient is God as a witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Knowing and Seeing.”
17:97: The Almighty says: And whomever God guides, he is the one who is guided. That is, if God had guided them, they would have been guided. And whomever He sends astray, you will find for them no protectors besides Him. That is, no one will guide them. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces. There are two interpretations of this: First: That this is an expression of hastening them to Hell, from the Arab saying: The people advanced on their faces if they hurried. Second: They will be dragged on their faces to Hell on the Day of Resurrection, just as is done to those who exaggerate in their desires and torture in this world. This is the correct view, based on the hadith of Anas that a man said: O Messenger of God, those who are gathered on their faces, will the disbeliever be gathered on his face? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is not the One Who made him walk on his two feet able to make him walk on his face on the Day of Resurrection? Qatadah said when he heard this: Yes, by the glory of our Lord. Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim. It is enough for you, Blind, dumb and deaf. Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said: That is, blind to what pleases them, dumb to speak with an argument, deaf to what benefits them. According to this statement, their senses will remain as they were. It was said: They will be gathered in the manner that God described them with, so that this will be an increase in their torment, then that will be created for them in Hell, so they will see, based on the statement of God the Most High: And the criminals will see the Fire and think that they will fall into it. (al-Kahf 18:53), and they will speak, based on the statement of God the Most High: Leave there. “They will be destroyed” (al-Furqan 25:13), and they heard, as God Almighty said: They will hear its wrath and its roaring (al-Furqan 25:12). Muqatil bin Sulayman said: When it is said to them, Be gone into it and do not speak, they will become blind, not seeing, deaf, not hearing, and dumb, not understanding. It was said: They became blind when they entered the Fire due to its intense blackness, and their speech was cut off when it was said to them, Be gone into it and do not speak, and the roaring and inhaling took away their hearing, so they did not hear anything. Their refuge is Hell, meaning their abode and place of residence. Whenever it subsides, meaning calms down, according to Ad-Dahhak and others, Mujahid, it was extinguished. It is said: The fire subsided, it subsided, it was extinguished, and I hid it. We increased them in a blazing Fire, meaning a blazing Fire, and the calming of its blazing is without any decrease in their pain or any alleviation of their torment. It was said: When it wanted to subsid, like His statement, And when you recite the Qur’an (al-Furqan 25:13). Isra: 45].
17:98: The Almighty said: That is their recompense because they disbelieved in Our signs. That is the punishment for their disbelief. And they said, ‘When we are bones and dust, will we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?’ So they denied the resurrection.
17:99: So God answered them and said: Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them and has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt? It was said: There is an inversion in the speech, meaning, have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth, and has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt, is able to create the likes of them? The term is the duration of their existence in this world and then their death, and that is something about which there is no doubt since it is witnessed. It was said: It is the answer to their saying: Or the sky will fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed. It was said: It is the Day of Resurrection. But the wrongdoers refused except to disbelieve, meaning the polytheists except to deny that term and the signs of God. It was said: That term is the time of resurrection, and there should be no doubt about it.
17:100: The Almighty said: “Say: If you possessed the treasures of the mercy of my Lord,” meaning the treasures of provisions. It was also said: the treasures of blessings, and this is more general. Then you would withhold for fear of spending, from miserliness, and it is the answer to their saying: We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth so that we may have ample living, meaning if you had ample living, you would also have been miserly. It was said: The meaning is if one of the creatures possessed the treasures of God, he would not have been as generous with them as God Almighty was, for two reasons: One of them: He must keep some of it for his expenses and what will benefit him. The second: That he fears poverty and fears nothingness, and God Almighty is exalted in His generosity above these two states. Spending in this verse means poverty, as Ibn Abbas and Qatada said. The linguists have narrated that he spent, became destitute, became needy, and became stingy if his money was little. And man is stingy, meaning miserly and tight-fisted. It is said: he was stingy with his family, he is stingy and tight-fisted, qatar and qaturaan, if he was tight-fisted with them in spending. Likewise, stinginess and tight-fisting, three languages. There are two opinions regarding this verse: One of them: It was revealed specifically about the polytheists, as stated by Al-Hasan. The second: It is general, which is the opinion of the majority, and Al-Mawardi mentioned.
17:101: The Almighty’s saying: And We gave Moses nine clear signs. There is a difference of opinion regarding these verses. It was said that they mean the verses of the Book, as narrated by Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Safwan bin Assal Al-Muradi: That two Jews said to one another: Let us go to this prophet and ask him. He said: Do not say to him prophet, for if we hear him he will have four eyes. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about the saying of God Almighty: And We gave Moses nine clear signs. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not associate anything with God, do not commit adultery, do not kill a soul that God has forbidden except by right, do not steal, do not practice magic, do not walk with an innocent person to the ruler so that he may kill him, do not consume usury, do not accuse a chaste woman, and do not flee from battle. Shu’bah was not sure: And upon you, O group of Jews in particular, do not transgress on the Sabbath. So they kissed his hands and feet and said: We bear witness that you are a prophet. He said: So what prevents you from submitting? They said, David prayed to God that there would always be a prophet among his descendants, and we fear that if we submit, the Jews will kill us. Abu ‘Eisa said, “This is a good and authentic hadith. It has already been mentioned in Surat al-Baqarah.” It has been said that the verses mean miracles and evidence. Ibn ‘Abbas and al-Dahhak said, “The nine verses: the staff, the hand, the tongue, the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood are detailed verses.” Al-Hasan and al-Sha’bi said, The five mentioned in al-A’raf mean the flood and what was connected to it, the hand, the staff, the years, and the decrease in fruits. Something similar was narrated from al-Hasan, except that he makes the years and the decrease in fruits one, and he made the ninth, The staff will swallow up what they fabricate. It was also narrated from Malik, except that he replaced the years and the decrease in fruits with: the sea and the mountain. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said, “They are the five that are in al-A’raf 7:the sea, the staff, the stone, and the obliteration of their wealth.” The explanation of these verses has been fully explained, praise be to God. So ask the Children of Israel when Moses came to them, meaning, ask them, O Muhammad, when Moses came to them with these verses, as was explained in Yunus. This is a question. A question to let the Jews know the truth of what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was saying. Pharaoh said to him, Indeed, I think, O Moses, that you are bewitched. That is, a magician with your strange actions. This was said by Al-Farra’ and Abu Ubaidah. So the object was placed in the place of the subject, as you say, This is ominous and auspicious, meaning ominous and auspicious. It was also said, deceived, and it was also said, overpowered, as was said by Muqatil. Other than this was said, and it was mentioned previously. On the authority of Ibn Abbas and Abu Nahik, they read, So he asked the Children of Israel, as a report, meaning, Moses asked Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel and set them free and set them free and send them with him.
17:102: The Almighty said: "He said: You have certainly known what these have sent down meaning the nine verses, and sent down means created, except the Lord of the heavens and the earth, insights" meaning indications by which one can prove His power and oneness. The common reading is I have known with the opening of the ta', addressing Pharaoh, and Al-Kisa'i read with the closing of the ta', which is the reading of Ali, may God be pleased with him, and by God, the enemy of God did not know, but Moses was the one who knew, so it reached Ibn Abbas and he said: It is I have certainly known and he used as evidence the Almighty's saying: "And they denied it, while their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance" (al-Naml 27:14), and Pharaoh was attributed to stubbornness, and Abu Ubaid said: What is taken from us is the opening of the ta', and it is the most correct for the meaning that Ibn Abbas used as evidence, and because Moses cannot be used as evidence for his saying: I have known, and he is the messenger who calls, and if with all of this the reading from Ali was correct, it would have been evidence, but it is not proven from him, rather it is from Kulthum Al-Muradi and he is unknown and not known And we do not know anyone who read it except Al-Kisa’i. It was said: Moses attributed to Pharaoh the knowledge of these miracles because Pharaoh knew the extent of what the magicians were capable of doing, and that what Moses did is not capable of being done by a magician, and that he is not able to do anything except to do bodies and own the heavens and the earth. Mujahid said: Moses entered upon Pharaoh on a winter day and he was wearing a blanket of his, so Moses threw his staff and behold it was a snake, and Pharaoh saw the sides of the house between its two ends, so he was frightened and made noise in his blanket, And indeed, O Pharaoh, you are doomed. Suspicion here means certainty, and doom is also destruction and loss. Al-Kumait said: Quda'ah saw in the days a vision of a persevering and steadfast person. That is, lost and loser, meaning in its affiliation to Yemen. It was said: cursed. It was narrated by Al-Munhal on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And Abaan bin Taghlib said it and recited: O our people, do not seek to wage war against us foolishly, for foolishness and aggression are both sinful. Any cursed one, and Maymun bin Mihran said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Mathburan is deficient in mind, and Al-Ma’mun looked at a man and said to him: O Mathbur, so he was asked about him, he said: Al-Rashid said: Al-Mansur said to a man: Mathbur, so I asked him, and he said: Maymun bin Mihran told me and he mentioned it and Qatada said: Perished, and also on his authority and Al-Hasan and Mujahid: Destroyed, and Thabur means destruction, it is said: May God destroy the enemy, he destroyed him, and it was said: Prevented from good, the linguists reported: What prevented you from such and such, meaning what prevented you from it, and May God destroy him, he destroys him, Al-Zubayri said: If I follow Satan in the ways of error, and whoever deviates from his inclination will be doomed. Ad-Dahhak: Mathburan bewitched. He responded to him as he said to him, with a different wording. Ibn Zayd said: Mathburan insane, without a mind.
17:103: God Almighty says: So he wanted to expel them from the land. That is, Pharaoh wanted to expel Moses and the Children of Israel from the land of Egypt by killing or banishing them, so God Almighty destroyed him.
17:104: The Almighty said: And We said afterward meaning after his drowning, to the Children of Israel, dwell in the land meaning the land of Ash-Sham and Egypt, Then when the promise of the Hereafter comes meaning the Resurrection, We will bring you in droves meaning from your graves mixed from every place, the believer will be mixed with the disbeliever, they will not know each other and none of you will be aligned with his tribe or his revelation. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: We will bring you all together from different directions, and the meaning is one. Al-Jawhari said: The group is what people from different tribes have gathered together. It is said: the people came in their group and their group, meaning their mixtures. The Almighty said: We will bring you in droves meaning gathered and mixed, and the food of a group is if it is mixed from two types or more, and so-and-so is the group of so-and-so, meaning his friend. Al-Asma’i said: The group is a plural and does not have a singular, and it is like all, and the meaning is: that they will emerge from the graves at the time of resurrection. Like locusts scattered, mixed together and not recognizing each other. Al-Kalbi said: Then when the promise of the Hereafter comes, meaning the coming of Jesus, peace be upon him, from heaven.
17:105: The Almighty’s saying: And with the truth We sent it down, and with the truth it has come down. This is connected to what came before from the mention of miracles and the Qur’an and writing, which goes back to the Qur’an. The reason for the repetition in His saying and with the truth it has come down is that the meaning of the first may be: We made it obligatory to send it down with the truth, and the meaning of the second may be: And it came down and in it was the truth, like his saying he went out with his clothes, meaning and he was wearing his clothes. And it was said that the ba’ in the first and with the truth is in the meaning of with, meaning with the truth, like your saying the prince rode with his sword, meaning with his sword, and with the truth we descend meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning it came down upon him, just as you say I sent down Yazid. And it was said: It is possible that the meaning is and with the truth we decreed that it should come down, and likewise it came down.
17:106: The Almighty’s saying: And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts in order that you may recite it to the people over a period of time. The doctrine of Sibawayh is that a Qur’an is in the accusative case with an implied verb that is explained by the apparent, and the majority of people read farqanahu with a light ra’, and its meaning is we explained it and clarified it, and we distinguished in it between truth and falsehood, as Al-Hasan said, and Ibn Abbas said: we separated it, and Ibn Abbas, Ali, Ibn Masoud, Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Qatadah, Abu Raja’ and Al-Sha’bi read qarqanahu with a shaddah, meaning we revealed it little by little, not all at once, except that in the reading of Ibn Masoud and Ubayy it is farqanahu ‘alayk. There is a difference of opinion about the period of time in which the Qur’an was revealed. It was said: in twenty-five years. Ibn Abbas: in twenty-three. Anas: in twenty. This is according to the difference of opinion about the age of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. There is no difference of opinion that it was revealed to the lowest heaven all at once. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. On a period of time means that it was prolonged little by little. This Qur’an is consistent according to the reading of Ibn Mas’ud, that is, We revealed it verse by verse and surah by surah. As for the first opinion, on a period of time means that it was recited slowly and in a melodious tone. This was said by Mujahid, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Jurayj. The reciter gives the recitation its due of its recitation, improvement, and sweetening it with a beautiful voice as much as possible, without intonation or singing that would lead to changing the wording of the Qur’an by adding or subtracting, for that is forbidden, as mentioned at the beginning of the book. The reciters agreed to add a damma to the meem in makth, except for Ibn Al-Muhaisin, who read makth with a fatha on the meem. It is said: mukth, mukth, and mukth, three languages. Malik said: on a period of time means to recite it slowly and in a melodious tone. The Almighty’s saying: And We sent it down gradually is an exaggeration and emphasis with the source of the previous meaning, meaning We sent it down star after star, and if they were to take all the obligations at one time, they would flee.
17:107: The Almighty said: "Say: Believe in it or do not believe" meaning the Qur'an. This is from God the Almighty as a way of rebuking and threatening them, not as a way of giving them a choice. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it meaning before the revelation of the Qur'an and the emergence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they are the believers of the People of the Book, according to the statement of Ibn Jurayj and others. Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning of when it is recited to them is their Book, and it was said that the Qur'an falls upon their faces in prostration and it was said that they are a people from the descendants of Ishmael who held fast to their religion until God the Almighty sent the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, among them Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl and Waraqa ibn Nawfal. Based on this, He does not mean those who were given the Book, but rather those who were given the knowledge of religion. Al-Hasan said: Those who were given knowledge are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mujahid said: They are people from the Jews, and this is more apparent because of His statement before it when it is recited to them meaning the Qur'an according to the statement of Mujahid, they were when they heard what God the Almighty revealed of the Qur'an They prostrated themselves and said: Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled. It was said: When they recited their book and what was revealed to him of the Qur’an, they would be humble, prostrate, and glorify God, and they would say: This is what is mentioned in the Torah, and this is his description, and God’s promise of him will inevitably come true. They inclined toward Islam, so the verse was revealed about them. A group said: What is meant by those who were given knowledge before him is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the pronoun in before him refers back to the Qur’an according to the pronoun in His statement: Say, ‘Believe in it.’ It was said: The two pronouns refer to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the mention of the Qur’an was resumed in His statement: When it is recited to them.
17:108: God Almighty says: And they say, ‘Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord will be fulfilled.’ Evidence of the permissibility of glorifying God during prostration. In Sahih Muslim and others, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say frequently during his prostration and bowing: ‘Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. O God, forgive me.’”
17:109: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And they fall upon their chins, weeping. This is an exaggeration in their description and praise for them, and it is the right of everyone who is characterized by knowledge and has acquired some of it, where he can reach this level, so he is humble when listening to the Qur’an and is humble and submissive. In Musnad Al-Darimi, Abu Muhammad, on the authority of Al-Taymi, said: Whoever is given knowledge that does not make him weep, it is appropriate that he has not been given knowledge, because God Almighty described the scholars. Then he recited this verse, Al-Tabari also mentioned it. The chins are the plural of chin, which is the meeting of the two beards. Al-Hasan said: The chins are an expression for the beards, meaning they place them on the ground in the state of prostration, which is the height of humility. The lam means on, you say he fell on his mouth, meaning on his mouth. Ibn Abbas said: And they fall upon their chins in prostration meaning on the faces. The chins were specifically mentioned because the chin is the closest thing to the human face. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: Prostration on the chin is not permissible, because the chin here is an expression for the face, and something may be used to refer to what is next to it and some of it to all of it, so it is said: he fell. He prostrated on his face, even if he did not prostrate on his cheek or his eye. Do you not see his saying: Proudly slain by the hands and mouth He only meant: He fell dead on his face and hands. Second: The Almighty’s saying: they weep is evidence of the permissibility of weeping in prayer out of fear of God Almighty, or for disobeying Him in the religion of God, and that this does not interrupt it or harm it. Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned on the authority of Hammad ibn Salamah on the authority of Thabit al-Banani on the authority of Mutraf ibn Abdullah ibn al-Shakheer on the authority of his father who said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was praying and there was a sound in his chest like the sound of a cauldron from weeping. And in the book of Abu Dawud: And in his chest there was a sound like the sound of a millstone from weeping. Third: The jurists differed regarding groaning. Malik said: Groaning does not interrupt the prayer for the sick, and I dislike it for the healthy. Al-Thawri said the same. Ibn al-Hakam narrated on the authority of Malik: Clearing his throat, groaning, and blowing do not interrupt the prayer. Ibn al-Qasim said: It interrupts. Al-Shafi’i said: If he has letters that are heard and understood, it interrupts the prayer. Abu Hanifa said: If it is from fear of God, it does not interrupt, but if it is from pain, it interrupts. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Yusuf that his prayer in all of that is complete, because no sick or weak person is free from groaning. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And increases their humility. The discussion of humility was presented in Surat Al-Baqarah and will come.
17:110: The Almighty said: “Say: Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious. Whichever [name] you call upon, He has the best names.” The reason for the revelation of this verse: The polytheists heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, calling out O God, O Most Merciful, so they said: Muhammad was ordering us to call upon one God, but he was calling upon two gods. Ibn Abbas said this. Makhul said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed at night and said in his supplication: O Most Merciful, O Most Merciful. A polytheist heard him, and there was a man of the Most Merciful in Yamamah. That listener said: What is the matter with Muhammad calling upon the Most Merciful of Yamamah? So the verse was revealed explaining that they are two names for one Name. If you call upon Him by God, then that is it, and if you call upon Him by the Most Merciful, then that is it. It was said: They used to write at the beginning of the books: In Your Name, O God. So the verse was revealed: It is from Solomon, and indeed, it is in the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. (al-Naml 27:30) So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. The polytheists said: We know this Most Merciful, but what is the Most Merciful? So the verse was revealed. It was said: The Jews said: Why do we not hear in the Qur’an a name that is abundant in the Torah, meaning the Most Merciful. So the verse was revealed, and he recited: Talha bin Masraf Whoever you call upon, He has the best names meaning that which requires the best descriptions and the most honorable meanings. The goodness of names is only directed by the improvement of the Sharia, its generality and its text. In addition to that, it requires good and honorable meanings, and it is by revelation. It is not correct to place a name for God in view except by revelation from the Qur’an or the hadith or consensus, as we explained in the book Al-Asna in explaining the beautiful names of God. The Almighty’s saying: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice. There are two issues in this: First: They differed on the reason for its revelation into five opinions: First: What Ibn Abbas narrated regarding the words of God Almighty: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice. He said: It was revealed while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in hiding in Mecca, and when he prayed with his companions, he would raise his voice with the Qur’an. When the polytheists heard that, they would curse the Qur’an, the One who revealed it, and the One who brought it. So God Almighty said: And do not recite your prayer aloud so that the polytheists would hear your recitation, and do not recite it in a low voice from your companions so that they would hear the Qur’an, and do not recite it in that loud voice, and seek a way between that. He said: He means between the loud and the low voice. Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi, and others, and the wording is Muslim’s. Low voice is lowering the voice and being still. It is said to the dead when he is cold: You have become low. The poet said: Nothing remains but a faint soul and a pale human eye The gloater pitied her for what happened to her. Woe to the one for whom the gloater pitied her. Second: What Muslim also narrated on the authority of Aisha regarding the Almighty’s saying: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice. She said: This was revealed regarding supplication. Third: Ibn Sirin said: The Arabs used to recite their testimony of faith out loud, so the verse was revealed about that. I said: According to this, the verse includes concealing the testimony of faith. Ibn Masoud said: It is from the Sunnah to conceal the testimony of faith. This was mentioned by Ibn al-Mundhir. Fourth: What was narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin also that Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, used to recite it quietly, and Umar used to recite it aloud. They were asked about that, and Abu Bakr said: I only commune with my Lord, and He knows my need for Him. Umar said: I drive away Satan and awaken the sleepy. So when this verse was revealed, it was said to Abu Bakr: Raise your voice a little, and it was said to Umar: Lower your voice a little. This was mentioned by al-Tabari and others. Fifth: What was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas also that its meaning is do not recite aloud during the daytime prayer, and do not recite in a low voice during the night prayer. Yahya bin Salam and Al-Zahrawi mentioned it, and it included the rulings on reciting aloud and silently in voluntary and obligatory prayers. As for voluntary prayers, the worshipper has the choice of reciting aloud or silently at night and during the day. Likewise, it was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to do both. As for obligatory prayers, their ruling on recitation is known at night and during the day.
