Sixth statement: Al-Hasan said: God says: Do not show off to people by praying in public, and do not do it badly. Ibn Abbas said: Do not pray to show off to people, and do not abandon it for fear of people. Second: God Almighty used the word prayer here to refer to recitation, just as He used the word recitation to refer to prayer in His statement: “And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed.” This is because each of them is connected to the Hereafter, because prayer includes recitation, bowing, and prostration, and they are among its parts. So He used the word part to refer to the whole, and the word part to refer to the whole, according to the Arabs’ custom in metaphor, which is common. From this is the authentic hadith: I have divided the prayer between Me and My servant, meaning the recitation of Al-Fatihah, as mentioned above.
17:111: The Almighty says: And say, ‘Praise be to God, who has not taken a son.’ This verse is a response to the Jews, Christians, and Arabs who say, Ezra, Jesus, and the angels are the offspring of God Almighty. God is exalted above what they say! And He had no partner in the kingdom because He is One and has no partner in His kingdom or in His worship. And He had no protector from humiliation Mujahid said: The meaning is that He did not ally with anyone nor seek anyone’s support, meaning that He had no supporter to protect Him from humiliation and thus be a defender. Al-Kalbi said: He had no protector from the Jews and Christians, because they are the most humiliated of people, in response to their saying: We are the sons of God and His beloved. Al-Hasan ibn Al-Fadl said: And He had no protector from humiliation meaning that He was not humiliated and would need a protector or a supporter due to His glory and pride. And He glorified Him with complete glorification meaning that He glorified Him with complete glorification. It is said: The most eloquent expression of the Arabs in the meaning of glorification and reverence is: God is Great, meaning He described Him as being greater than everything. The poet said: I saw God is greater than everything, trying and most of them are soldiers When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered into prayer, he would say: God is Great. The beginning of the Book has been mentioned. Umar ibn al-Khattab said: The servant’s saying, God is Great is better than the world and what is in it. This verse is the conclusion of the Torah. Mutraf ibn Abdullah narrated on the authority of Ka’b, who said: The Torah began with the opening of Surat al-An’am and this surah was concluded. In al-Naba 78:It is the verse of glory. It was narrated by Mu’adh ibn Anas on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Amr ibn Shu’ayb narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather, who said: “Whenever a boy from Banu Abd al-Muttalib spoke clearly, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would teach him: ‘Say: Praise be to God,’ and the verse.” Abd al-Hamid ibn Wasil said: I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: “Whoever recites: ‘Say: Praise be to God,’ the verse, God will write for him a reward equal to the earth and mountains, because God the Most High says about someone who claims to have a son: ‘The heavens almost burst from him, and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse.’ This is the verse.” It was reported that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered a man who complained to him about his debt to recite: ‘Say: Call upon God or call upon the Most Merciful,’ to the end of the surah, then he would say: I put my trust in the Ever-Living, Who never dies, three times.
18:1: It is Meccan according to all commentators. It was narrated from a group that the beginning of the Surah was revealed in Medina until the words: Jarza and the first is more correct. It was narrated about its merits from the hadith of Anas that he said: Whoever recites it will be given a light between the heaven and the earth and will be protected from the trial of the grave. Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Abi Farwa said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not guide you to a Surah that is accompanied by seventy thousand angels, its greatness filling the space between the heaven and the earth for the one who recites it like that? They said: Yes, O Messenger of God? He said: Surah Ashab al-Kahf. Whoever recites it on Friday will be forgiven until the next Friday and three more days, and will be given a light that reaches the heaven and will be protected from the trial of the Antichrist. Al-Tha'labi mentioned it, and al-Mahdawi also with a similar meaning. In Musnad al-Darimi on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, he said: Whoever recites Surah al-Kahf on Friday night will have a light that will shine for him between him and the Ancient House. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Darda’, that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surat Al-Kahf will be protected from the Antichrist. In another narration: From the end of Surat Al-Kahf. In Muslim, there is a hadith from Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an: Whoever wants to attack him - meaning the Antichrist - should recite to him the opening verses of Surat Al-Kahf. Al-Tha’labi mentioned it and said: Samurah bin Jundub said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever recites ten verses from Surat Al-Kahf by heart will not be harmed by the trial of the Antichrist, and whoever recites the entire surah will enter Paradise. God Almighty says: Praise be to God, who has sent down to His servant the Book and has not made therein any crookedness.
18:2: The Almighty said: Standing Ibn Ishaq mentioned that the Quraysh sent Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith and Uqbah bin Abi Mu'ayt to the Jewish rabbis and said to them: Ask them about Muhammad and describe to them his characteristics and tell them what he said, for they are the people of the first book, and they have knowledge that we do not have of the knowledge of the prophets. So they went out until they arrived in Medina, and asked the Jewish rabbis about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and described his affair to them, and informed them of some of his sayings, and said to them: You are the people of the Torah and we have come to you so that you may tell us about this companion of ours. So the Jewish rabbis said to them: Ask him about three things that we will command you to do, for if he tells you about them then he is a prophet sent, and if he does not then the man is a liar, so give him your opinion. Ask him about the youths who passed away in the first era, and what their affair was, for they had an amazing story. Ask him about a wandering man who has traveled to the east and west of the earth, and what his story was. Ask him about the spirits, and what they are. If he tells you about that, then follow him, for I am a prophet. If he does not, then he is a slanderer, so do with him what you see fit. Then An-Nadir ibn Al-Harith and Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’ayt came to Mecca to meet Quraysh and said: “O people of Quraysh, we have come to you with a decision that will settle the matter between you and Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Jewish rabbis ordered us to ask him about things that they ordered us to do. If he tells you about them, then he is a prophet, but if he does not, then the man is a liar. So give him your opinion about him.” So they went to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: “O Muhammad, tell us about a trial that occurred in the early days. They had a strange story, and about a man who was a wanderer who had reached the east and west of the earth. Tell us about the spirits, what they are.” So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: I will tell you what you asked about tomorrow, and he did not make an exception. So they left him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) remained, as they claim, for fifteen nights, without God revealing to him any revelation about that, nor did Gabriel come to him, until the people of Mecca became alarmed and said: Muhammad promised us tomorrow, and today is fifteen nights, and we have woken up and he has not told us anything about what we asked him about. And until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) became sad. God, may God bless him and grant him peace, delayed the revelation from him, and he was distressed by what the people of Mecca were saying. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him from God, the Almighty, with the Surah of the People of the Cave, in which He reproached him for his grief over them, and the report of what they asked him about regarding the matter of the young men, the man who circumambulated and the men who were walking. Ibn Ishaq said: It was mentioned to me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: You have been held back from me, O Gabriel, until I had bad thoughts. Gabriel said to him: “And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs whatever is before us and whatever is behind us and whatever is between that. And your Lord is not forgetful.” (Maryam 19:64) So God, the Blessed and Exalted, opened the Surah with His praise, and mentioned the prophethood of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they denied him that, so he said: Praise be to God, who has sent down to His servant the Book, meaning Muhammad, You are a Messenger from Me, meaning a fulfillment of what they asked about regarding your prophethood, and has not made therein any crookedness * [but] straight, meaning balanced, with no difference in it. To warn of a severe punishment from Him meaning, an immediate punishment in this world, and a painful torment in the Hereafter, meaning from your Lord who sent you as a Messenger. And to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward.
18:3: The Almighty said: Residing therein forever meaning the eternal home in which they will not die, those who believed you in what you brought from what others denied you, and did what you commanded them to do. And to warn those who say, 'God has taken a son' meaning the Quraysh in their saying: We worship the angels, who are the daughters of God. They have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers those who magnified their arrogance and the defect of their religion. A grave word that comes out of their mouths meaning their saying that the angels are the daughters of God. "They say nothing but a lie. So perhaps you would kill yourself through grief over them, if they do not believe in this message" out of his grief over it when he missed out on what he had hoped for from them, meaning do not do it. Ibn Hisham said: kill yourself through grief destroy yourself, according to what Abu Ubaidah told me. Dhu al-Rummah said: Oh, you who are suffering from anguish over something that fate has carved from your hands! The plural of which is bakhoon is bakha’ah. This verse is in one of his poems. The Arabs say: I have given him my advice and myself, meaning I have exerted myself for him. Indeed, We have made that which is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed. Ibn Ishaq said: meaning which of them will follow My command and act in obedience to Me. And indeed, We will make that which is on it [a] barren plain. That is, the earth, and that which is on it will perish and disappear, and the return is to Me, so I will reward each according to his knowledge, so do not be saddened or grieved by what you see and hear therein. Ibn Hisham said: Sa’id is the face of the earth, and its plural is sa’d. Dhu al-Rummah said, describing a young gazelle. As if in the morning you are restoring the plain with a tank of bone-headed hose This verse is in one of his poems. The plain also means the road. It was mentioned in the hadith, Beware of sitting on the plains, meaning the roads. The islands are the land that does not grow anything, and its plural is ajraz. It is said: a year of jaraz and years of ajraz, which is the year in which there is no rain. There is drought, dryness, and hardship. Dhu al-Rummah said, describing camels: The ribs and the bones were folded up and nothing remained but the wounded ribs. Ibn Ishaq said: Then he turned to the story of the report regarding what they asked him about regarding the young men and said: Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder? That is, among My signs in what I placed upon the servants of My proof was something more wondrous than that. Ibn Hisham said: The inscription is the book that was numbered with their report, and its plural is raqm. Al-Ajjaj said: And the fixed place of the numbered Qur’an and this verse in his rajazah, Ibn Ishaq said: Then he said: “When the youths took refuge in the cave and said, ‘Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and prepare for us from our affair right guidance.’ So We sealed their ears within the cave for a number of years. Then We raised them up that We might test which of the two parties had best calculated the term that they had tarried.” Then he said: We relate to you their story in truth, meaning with the truth of the report. “Indeed, they were youths who believed in their Lord, and We increased them in guidance. And We strengthened their hearts when they stood up and said, ‘Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never invoke besides Him any deity. We had certainly said then an outrageous thing.’” That is, they did not associate anything with Me. You associated with Me something of which you had no knowledge. Ibn Hisham said: Excessiveness is exaggeration and going beyond the truth. A’sha ibn Qays ibn Tha’labah said: Do you stop, but the ones who are extravagant stop, like the stabbing that wastes the oil and the twisting? This verse is in one of his poems. Ibn Ishaq said, “These are our people who have taken gods besides Him. Why do they not produce for them a clear authority?” Ibn Ishaq said, That is, a conclusive argument. “Who then does more wrong than he who invents a lie about God? And when you have withdrawn from them and that which they worship except God, then take refuge in the cave. Your Lord will spread out for you of His mercy and will prepare for you from your affair ease. And you will see the sun, when it rises, inclining away from their cave to the right, and when it sets, passing them by to the left while they are in an open space thereof.” Ibn Hisham said, Tazawar means inclining, and it is from falsehood. Abu al-Zahf al-Kulaibi said, describing a country: The dew has dried up on our love. I visit the five-year-old mounts. These two couplets are in one of his poems. And she passes them by on the left she passes them by and leaves them on her left. Dhu al-Rummah said: To the women who bow their bows, looking north, with the knights on their right. This is a verse in one of his poems. The gap: the spaciousness, and its plural is fajaa. The poet said: Dress your people in a beautiful and modest way until they are permitted and the gap between the houses is resolved. That is from the signs of God meaning in the argument against those who knew that about their affairs from the People of the Book, from whom these people were commanded to ask you about them regarding the truth of your prophethood by verifying the report about them. “He whom God guides is the guided one, and he whom He sends astray - you will find for him no protector to guide him. And you think them awake while they are asleep. And We turn them to the right and to the left, and their dog is stretching out his forelegs at the entrance.” Ibn Hisham said: The entrance is the door. Al-Absi, whose name is Abd ibn Wahb, said: In a desert land where hunting is not forbidden, and my knowledge there is not from you This verse is in his verses. Al-Wasid also means courtyard, and its plural is Sayyad, Wasd, and Sadan. If you had looked at them, you would have turned away from them in flight to His saying: Those who prevailed over their affair said, the people of authority and kingship among them, “We will surely build a mosque over them. * They will say” meaning the Jewish rabbis who ordered them to ask about them, “Three, the fourth of them is their dog. And they say five, the sixth of them is their dog, guessing at the unseen. And they say seven, the eighth of them is their dog. Say, “My Lord knows best their number. None knows them except a few. So do not dispute about them” meaning do not be stubborn with them except an outward dispute, and do not consult anyone of them about them for they have no knowledge of them. “And never say of anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow’, except [if] God wills. And remember your Lord when you forget and say, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer to the right path than this.’” That is, do not say of anything they ask you about as you said about this, I will bring you out tomorrow, and except for the will of God. And remember your Lord when you forget and say, Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer to the right path than this, for you do not know what I will do in that. And they remained in their cave for three hundred years, and they added nine, that is, they will say that. “Say, ‘God knows best how long they remained. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. He sees and hears it. They have not besides Him any protector, and He shares in His rule anyone.’” That is, nothing of what they asked you about was hidden from Him. I said: This is what occurred in the biography of the story of the People of the Cave, we mentioned it in its order. And the story of Dhu al-Ranin will come, then we return to the beginning of the surah and say: The meaning of praise be to God has been presented. Al-Akhfash, Al-Kisa’i, Al-Farra’, Abu Ubaid and the majority of commentators claimed that at the beginning of this surah there is an advancement and a delay, and that the meaning is: Praise be to God who sent down to His servant the Book upright and did not make it crooked. And upright is in the accusative case as a state. Qatada said: The speech is in its context without advancement or delay, and its meaning is: And did not make it crooked, but We made it upright. Ad-Dahhak’s statement about it is good, and that the meaning is: Straight, meaning straight wisdom with no error, corruption or contradiction in it. And it was said: upright on the previous books confirms it. And it was said: upright with arguments forever. Crooked is the object, and crookedness with a kasra on the ‘ayn in religion, opinion, command and path. And with a fatha on it in objects such as wood and walls, and it was presented. There is no crookedness in the Qur’an, i.e. a defect, i.e. it is not contradictory or different, as God Almighty said: And if it had been from other than God, they would have found within it much discrepancy (An-Nisa’: 82). It was said: i.e. He did not make it created, as was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding God Almighty’s statement: An Arabic Qur’an without any crookedness (al-Zumar 39:28). He said: Not created. Muqatil said: Crookedness means difference. The poet said: I always treat my friend with kindness, and there is no good in someone who is crooked in his friendship. To warn of a severe punishment meaning to warn Muhammad or the Qur'an. There is an implication in it, meaning to warn the disbelievers of God's punishment. This is Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim from Him with a sukoon on the dal and a damma on the noon and a kasra on the ha', and the ha' is joined with a ya'. The rest with Him with a damma on the dal and a sukoon on the noon and a damma on the ha'. Al-Jawhari said: There are three languages for with Him: Ladan, Walada, Walad. He said: From his beard to his throat. The throat is a language for the throat. God Almighty says: And He gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward, meaning Paradise, abiding therein forever, not to an end. Even if the good tidings are interpreted as clarification, there is no need for the preposition that in that. The good reward is the great recompense that leads to Paradise.
18:4: The Almighty says: And to warn those who say, ‘God has taken a son.’ They are the Jews who said, Ezra is the son of God, the Christians who said, The Messiah is the son of God, and the Quraysh who said, The angels are the daughters of God. So the warning at the beginning of the Surah is general, and this is specific to those who say, God has a son.
18:5: The Almighty said: They have no knowledge of it of is a connection, meaning they have no knowledge of that statement, because they are imitators who said it without evidence. Nor their fathers meaning their ancestors. Great is the word word is an accusative of explanation, meaning that word is great. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Mihya bin Ya'mar, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read word in the nominative case, meaning the word is great, meaning their saying that God has taken a son. According to this reading, there is no need to imply anything. It is said that something is great if it is great, and a man is old if he becomes old. It comes out of their mouths is in the place of an attribute. They say nothing but a lie meaning they say nothing but a lie.
18:6: The Almighty said: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them Bakh'a meaning destroyer and killer, and it has been mentioned before. Their traces is the plural of Athar, and it is also said Athar. The meaning is, over the traces of their turning away and their satisfaction with you if they do not believe in this message meaning the Qur'an out of grief" meaning sorrow and anger over their disbelief, and it is in the accusative case for explanation.
18:7: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it. There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty’s statement: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it. “What” and adornment are the objects of everything on the face of the earth, so it is general because it indicates its Creator. Ibn Jubayr said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He meant by adornment men, Mujahid said. Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: That the adornment is the caliphs and princes. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God the Almighty: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, he said: The scholars are the adornment of the earth. A group said: He meant the blessings, clothing, fruits, greenery, water, and the like of this that has adornment, and it does not include the solid mountains and everything that has adornment in it such as snakes and scorpions. The people are more deserving of generality, and that everything on the earth has adornment in terms of its creation, making, and perfection. The verse is an explanation of consolation, meaning, O Muhammad, do not worry about the world and its people, for We have only made that a test and trial for its people. Some of them will reflect and believe, and some of them will disbelieve. Then the Day of Resurrection will be before them, so do not let their disbelief be too great for you, for We will reward them. Second: The meaning of this verse refers to the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): The world is green and sweet, and God has made you successors in it to see how you behave. And his saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): What I fear most for you is what God will bring forth for you of the flowers of the world. They said: What are the flowers of the world? He said: The blessings of the earth. Both were narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri. The meaning is that the world is pleasant to taste and wonderful to look at, like sweet fruit that is wonderful to see. So God tests His servants with it to see which of them is best in deeds. That is, who is most indifferent to it and abandons it. There is no way for the one who returns to disobeying what God has adorned for him except that He helps him to do so. For this reason, ‘Umar used to say in it, as mentioned by al-Bukhari: “O God, we cannot help but rejoice in what You have adorned for us. O God, I ask You to spend it in its rightful place.” So he supplicated to God to help him spend it in its rightful place. This is the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him: Whoever takes it willingly will be blessed in it, and whoever takes it greedily will be like the one who eats and is never satisfied. And so is the one who has much of this world, not content with what he gets from it, but his concern is to collect it, and that is due to his lack of understanding of God the Most High and His Messenger, for with it comes temptation and the lack of safety is predominant. And he who has become a Muslim and has been provided with what is sufficient and God has given him what He has given him has succeeded. Ibn Atiyyah said: My father, may God be pleased with him, used to say regarding His statement: the best of deeds the best of deeds is taking what is right and spending in what is right along with faith, performing the obligatory duties, avoiding what is forbidden, and doing a lot of what is recommended. I said: This is a good statement, concise in its wording and eloquent in its meaning. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered it in one statement, which is his statement to Sufyan ibn Abdullah al-Thaqafi when he said: O Messenger of God, tell me something about Islam that I will not ask anyone after you about, in another narration: except you. He said: “Say: I believe in God, then be steadfast.” Narrated by Muslim. Sufyan al-Thawri said: The best of deeds is the least of them who are ascetic in it. Abu Issam al-Asqalani also said: The best of deeds is the one who abandons it. The scholars’ expressions differed regarding asceticism. Some people said: Shortening one’s hope is not eating rough food or wearing a cloak, as Sufyan al-Thawri said. Our scholars said: He spoke the truth, may God be pleased with him! For he who shortens one’s hope does not indulge in fine food or dress in exquisite clothing, and takes from this world what is easy, and is content with what is sufficient for him. Some people said: Hating praise and loving admiration. This is the statement of al-Awza’i and those who followed him. Some people said: Abandoning the world entirely is asceticism, whether one likes to abandon it or not. This is the saying of Fadil. On the authority of Bishr ibn al-Harith, he said: Love of the world is love of meeting people, and asceticism in the world is asceticism in meeting people. And on the authority of al-Fadl also: The sign of asceticism in the world is asceticism in people. And some people said: The ascetic is not an ascetic until leaving the world is more beloved to him than taking it, said by Ibrahim ibn Adham. And some people said: Asceticism is to be ascetic in the world in your heart, said by Ibn Mubarak. And a group said: Asceticism is the love of death. And the first saying includes these sayings in meaning, so it is more appropriate.
18:8: The Almighty said: And indeed, We will make what is on it a barren plain. Its explanation was presented. Abu Sahl said: Soil with no vegetation in it, as if its vegetation was cut off. And al-Jarz means to cut, and from it comes the word al-Jarz a year of cutting. And the rajaz poet said: The years have swept them away And the barren land in which there is no night and no building or anything else, as if it was cut off and removed, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, for the land will be flat and nothing hidden in it. An-Nahhas: And barren land in the language is the land in which there is no vegetation. Al-Kisa’i said: It is said that the land is barren, and the people barren it, they barren it if they eat everything that came from it of plants and crops, so it is barren and barren.
18:9: The Almighty's saying: Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder? The doctrine of Sibaih is that when Amm comes without being preceded by an interrogative alif, it means rather and an interrogative alif. It is the disconnected one. It was said: Amm is in apposition to the meaning of the interrogative in perhaps, or it means an interrogative alif in denial. Al-Tabari said: It is a confirmation to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, on his account that the companions of the cave were a wonder, in the sense of denying that to him, i.e. do not consider that as great as the questioners from the infidels considered it to you, for the rest of the signs of God are greater than their story and more widespread. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ibn Ishaq. The address is to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, because the polytheists asked him about the missing youths, and about Dhul-Qarnayn and about the spirit. And the revelation was delayed, as mentioned above. When it was revealed, God the Almighty said to His Prophet, peace be upon him: Do you think, O Muhammad, that the story of the People of the Cave, from Al-Kalbi: The creation of the heavens and the earth, is more amazing than their story? Ad-Dahhak: What I have informed you of from the unseen is more amazing. Al-Junayd: Your affair in the Night Journey is more amazing. Al-Mawardi: The meaning of the statement is negation, i.e. I would not have thought had it not been for our informing me. Abu Sahl: A question of confirmation, i.e. I thought that, for they are amazing. The cave is the wide opening in the mountain, and that which is not wide is a delusion. Al-Naqqash narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik that he said: The cave is the mountain, and this is not well-known in the language. Some people differed about Ar-Raqim. Ibn Abbas said: I know everything in the Quran except four: Ghaslin, Hanan, Awah, and Ar-Raqim. He was once asked about Ar-Raqim, and he said: Kaab claimed that it was a village from which they left. Mujahid said: Ar-Raqim is a valley. As-Suddi said: Ar-Raqim is the rock that was on the cave. Ibn Zayd said: Ar-Raqim is a book whose matter God concealed from us, and He did not explain its story to us. A group said: Ar-Raqim is a book on a copper tablet. Ibn Abbas said: It is on a lead tablet on which the infidels from whom the young men fled wrote their story and made it their history. They mentioned the time of their disappearance, how many they were, and who they were. Al-Farra’ said the same, he said: Ar-Raqim is a lead tablet on which their names, lineages, religion, and those who fled were written. Ban Atiyah said: It appears from these narrations that they were a people who recorded events, and that is from the nobility of the kingdom, and it is a useful matter. These sayings are taken from Ar-Raqm, and Namah is a book that is numbered. And from it comes Arqam for its planning. And from it is the valley’s number, meaning the place where the water flows and bends. What was narrated from Ibn Abbas is not contradictory, because the first statement was heard from Ka’b. The second statement may be that the inscription was known after him. Saeed bin Jubair narrated from him that Ibn Abbas mentioned the People of the Cave and said: The young men were lost, so their families searched for them but did not find them. So that was brought to the king, so he said: Let there be report for them. He made a green tablet of lead and wrote their names on it and put it in his storeroom. So that tablet is the inscription. It was said: Two believers were in the king’s house, so they wrote the matter of the young men, their names and their lineages on a tablet of lead, then put it in a copper coffin and put it in the building. And God knows best. And from Ibn Abbas also: The inscription is a written book that they had in it the law that they held fast to from the religion of Jesus, peace be upon him. Al-Naqqash said from Qatada: The inscription was their dirhams. Anas bin Malik and Al-Sha’bi said: The inscription was their dog. Ikrimah said: The inkwell is the inkwell. It was said: The inscription is the golden tablet under the wall that Al-Khidr erected. It was also said: The inscription is the people of the cave that collapsed on them, so he mentioned each one of them who did the best job. I said: And in this is a well-known report narrated by the two Sahihs, and Al-Bukhari agreed with it. Some people said: God told about the People of the Cave, but He did not tell anything about the People of Ar-Raqim. Ad-Dahhak said: Ar-Raqim is a town in Rome in which there is a cave in which there are twenty-one souls as if they were sleeping in the form of the People of the Cave, so according to this they are other young men who were afflicted with what happened to the People of the Cave. God knows best. And it was said: Ar-Raqim is a valley near Palestine in which there is the cave, taken from Raqmah of the valley, which is a place of water. It is said: Go to Raqmah and leave the bank, Al-Ghaznawi mentioned it. Ibn Atiyyah said: And in Ash-Sham, according to what I have heard from many people, there is a cave in which there are dead people, and its neighbors claim that they are the People of the Cave, and over them is a mosque and a building called Ar-Raqim, and with them is a dog that is a spear. And in Andalusia in the direction of Granada, near a village called Lusha, there is a cave in which there are dead people and with them is a dog that is a spear, and most of them have had their flesh stripped away and some of them are still together. The past centuries have passed and we have not found any trace of knowledge about their affair. It is claimed that they are the People of the Cave. I went to them and saw them in the year 504 in this state, and there was a mosque over them. Near them was a Roman building called Al-Raqim, as if it were a man-made palace, some of whose walls remained. It is in a deserted area, in ruins. At the top of Granada, facing the qibla, are the ruins of an ancient Roman city called the city of Decius. We found in its ruins strange things, such as graves and the like. I said: What was mentioned about his seeing them in Andalusia is that they are not them, because God the Most High said about the People of al-Kahf 18:If you had looked at them, you would have turned away from them in flight and would have been filled with terror of them (al-Kahf 18:18). Ibn Abbas said to Muawiyah when he wanted to see them: God has prevented someone better than you from doing that, and that will come at the end of the story. Mujahid said about His statement: They were, among Our signs, a wonder, he said: They are a wonder. This is how Ibn Jurayj narrated it from him. He goes to the fact that it is not a denial of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, being with him. They are amazing. It was narrated that [Abi] Najih said on his authority: He says that it is not the most amazing of our verses.
18:10: The Almighty said: When the young men took refuge in the cave. It was narrated that they were a people from the nobles of the city of Decius, the infidel king, and it was said about him Decius. It was narrated that they were surrounded and fenced with gold with forelocks, and they were from the Romans and followed the religion of Jesus. It was said: They were before Jesus, and God knows best. And Abbas said: A king from the Muk called Decius appeared over a city of the Roman cities called Ephesus. It was said that Tarsus was after the time of Jesus, peace be upon him, so he ordered the worship of idols, so he called its people to worship idols, and there were seven young men there who were secretly worshipping God, so their report was reported to the king and they feared him so they fled at night, and they passed by a shepherd with a dog so he followed them and they took refuge in the cave so the king followed them to the mouth of the cave, and he found traces of their entry but did not find traces of their exit, so they entered and God blinded their eyes so they did not see anything, so the king said: Close the door of the cave on them so that they die in it of hunger and thirst. Mujahid narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that these young men were in the religion of a king who worshipped idols, sacrificed to them, and disbelieved in God. The people of Medina followed him in this. The young men received knowledge from some of the disciples - according to what al-Naqqash mentioned - or from the believers of the nations before them. (So they believed in God and saw with their own eyes the ugliness of the people’s actions. So they took themselves to adhere to the religion and worship God. So their matter was brought to the king and he was told: They have abandoned your religion, belittled your gods, and disbelieved in them. So the king summoned them to his council and ordered them to follow his religion and sacrifice to his gods. He threatened them with death for abandoning that. So they said to him, as it was narrated: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth until His saying: And when you withdrew from them. It was narrated that they said something similar to this speech, but it was not the same. So the king said to them: You are two young fools who have no minds, and I will not hasten you, but I will wait. So go to the one who made you fall and think about your opinion and return to my command. And he set a time limit for them in that. Then he traveled during The deadline came, so the young men consulted about escaping with their religions. One of them said to them: I know of a cave in such-and-such a mountain, in which my father used to put his sheep. Let us go and hide in it until God opens for us. So they went out, as was narrated, playing with the scepter and the ball, rolling it towards their path so that people would not notice them. It was narrated that they were educated, and when a festival came, they went out to it and rode with the people. Then they began to play with the goljan until they escaped. Wahb ibn Munabbih narrated that the beginning of their affair was that of a disciple of Jesus, son of Mary, who came to the city of the People of the Cave. He wanted to enter it, so he hired himself from the owner of the bathhouse who was working there. The owner of the bathhouse saw great blessing in his work, so he gave him all his affairs. Young men from the city knew that man, and God Almighty knew them, so they believed in him and followed him in his religion, and their mixing with him became famous. One day, the king’s son came to that bathhouse with a woman and wanted to be alone with her, but that disciple ruined him and he stopped. Then he came again and ruined him and cursed him, and carried out his intention to enter the bathhouse with the prostitute. So he entered and they both died in it. So that disciple and his companions were accused of killing them, so they all fled until they entered the cave. Other things were said about their exit. As for the dog, it was narrated that it was their hunting dog. It was narrated that they saw a shepherd who had a dog on their way, so the shepherd followed them according to their opinion and the dog went with them, as Ibn Abbas said. The dog’s name was Hamran, and it was said Qutmir. As for the names of the People of the Cave, they are foreign, and the chain of transmission for knowing them is weak. What Al-Tabari mentioned is this: Maksalmina, who was the eldest of them and the one who spoke on their behalf, and Mahsimilinina and Yamlikha, who was the one who went with the paper to the city when they were awakened from their sleep, and Martus, Kashutush, Dinmus, Yatonus, and Berunus. Muqatil said: The dog belonged to Maksalmina and he was the oldest of them and the owner of the sheep. Second: This verse is explicit about fleeing with one’s religion and abandoning one’s family, children, relatives, friends, homelands and wealth for fear of tribulation and the hardships that a person may encounter. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fled with his religion, as did his companions, and he sat in the cave, as mentioned previously in Surat An-Nahl. God the Most High has stated this in Bara’ah, which has been mentioned previously. They abandoned their homelands and abandoned their land, homes, families, children, relatives and brothers, hoping for safety with their religion and salvation from the tribulation of the disbelievers. So, living in the mountains and entering caves, isolating oneself from people, being alone with people and being alone with the Creator, and allowing one to flee from the oppressor is the Sunnah of the Prophets (peace and blessings of God be upon them) and the saints. The virtue of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is isolation, and the virtue of the group of scholars is especially when tribulations appear and people become corrupt. God the Most High has stated this in His Book, saying: So take refuge in the cave (al-Kahf 18:15). Scholars said: Isolation from people is sometimes in the mountains and valleys, sometimes on the coasts and in the ribat, and sometimes in the houses. It was reported in the hadith: If there is a trial, then hide your place and hold your tongue, and it did not specify a place over another. A group of scholars have made isolation: isolate yourself from evil and its people with your heart and your actions, even if you are among them. Ibn al-Mubarak said in the interpretation of isolation: that you are with the people, and if they engage in the remembrance of God, engage with them, and if they engage in something else, then remain silent. Al-Baghawi narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The believer who mixes with people and is patient with their harm is better than the believer who does not mix with them and is not patient with their harm. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The monasteries of the believers are their homes, from the correspondence of al-Hasan and others. Uqbah ibn Amir said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: What is salvation, O Messenger of God? He said: O Uqbah, hold your tongue, let your home suffice you, and repent for your sins. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A time will come upon the people when the best property of a Muslim man will be sheep, which he will follow along the mountain passes and the places of palaces, fleeing with his religion from trials. Narrated by Al-Bukhari. It was narrated by Ali ibn Saeed on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Waqid who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the year 180 comes, celibacy, isolation, and monasticism on the tops of mountains will be permissible for my nation. It was also narrated by Ali bin Saad on the authority of Abd bin Mubarak on the authority of Mubarak bin Fadala on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A time will come upon the people when no one who has a religion will be safe from his religion unless he flees with his religion from one high place to another or from one rock to another. When that happens, livelihood will not be attained except by disobeying God. When that happens, celibacy will be permissible.” They said: O Messenger of God, how can celibacy be permissible when you command us to marry? He said: “When that happens, a man’s corruption will be at the hands of his parents. If he has no parents, his destruction will be at the hands of his wife. If he has a wife, his destruction will be at the hands of his children. If he has no children, his destruction will be at the hands of his relatives and neighbors.” They said: How is that, O Messenger of God? He said: They will taunt him for his difficult livelihood and burden him with what he cannot bear. At that point, he will put himself in situations in which he will perish.” I said: The conditions of people in this regard differ. There is a man who has the strength to live in caves and caverns in the mountains, and this is the highest condition because it is the condition that God chose for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the beginning of his affair, and He stated it in His Book, informing about the young men, saying: And when you have withdrawn from them and what they worship except God, then take refuge in the cave. And there is a man for whom isolation in his house is easier and more comfortable. Some men from the people of Badr isolated themselves and remained in their homes after the killing of Uthman, and they did not go out except to their graves. And there is a man who is in between them and has the strength to endure mixing with people and their harm, so he is with them outwardly and opposes them inwardly. Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned that Wahib ibn al-Ward told us that a man came to Wahb ibn Munabbih and said: The people have fallen into what they have fallen into, and I have thought to myself not to mix with them. He said: Do not do that, for you need people and they need you, and you have needs of them and they need you, but be deaf yet hearing, blind yet seeing, silent yet speaking. It has been said that every place that is far from people is included in the meaning of mountains and valleys, such as seclusion in mosques, and staying on coasts for guarding and remembrance, and staying in homes to flee from the evils of people. The hadiths mention valleys, mountains, and following sheep - and God knows best - because that is what is most common in places where one secludes himself. So every place that is far from people is included in its meaning, as we have mentioned, and God is the Grantor of success and with Him is protection. Uqbah ibn Amir narrated that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Your Lord is amazed at a shepherd on the top of a mountainside who calls the adhan for prayer and prays, and God, the Mighty and Sublime, says: Look at My servant calling the adhan and establishing the prayer, fearing Me. I have forgiven My servant and admitted him to Paradise.” Narrated by An-Nasa’i. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And provide for us from our affair right guidance. When they fled from those who were pursuing them, they occupied themselves with supplication and sought refuge in God the Almighty and said: Our Lord, grant us from Yourself mercy, meaning forgiveness and provision. And provide for us from our affair right guidance, granting guidance to right guidance. Ibn Abbas said: He came out of the cave in safety, and it was said that this is correct. From this meaning is that when a matter worried him, peace be upon him, he would resort to prayer.
18:11: The Almighty's saying: So We sealed their ears in the cave for a number of years refers to God casting sleep upon them. This is one of the eloquent verses of the Qur'an that the Arabs admitted their inability to produce anything like it. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, We prevented them from hearing, because when a sleeper hears, he wakes up. Ibn Abbas said: We sealed their ears with sleep, that is, We blocked their ears from the penetration of sounds into them. It was said: The meaning of So We sealed their ears is that We answered their prayer, and We averted from them the evil of their strength, and We put them to sleep, and the whole meaning is close. Qatrib said: This is like the Arabs saying, the prince seals the hands of his subjects if he prevents them from corruption, and the master seals the hands of his slave who is authorized to trade if he prevents him from acting. Al-Aswad bin Ya'fur, who was blind, said: And among the incidents, I do not care that I was hit on the ground with axes As for singling out the ears for mention, it is because they are the organ from which sleep is greatly corrupted, and rarely is a sleeper’s sleep interrupted except by his ear, and the sleep of one whose hearing is impaired is not complete. And from the mention of the ear in sleep, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: That is a man in whose ear the devil urinated. Narrated by Saheeh. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) pointed to a man who slept for a long time and did not get up at night. And ‘aadan is an adjective for the years, meaning they are counted, and the intention is to express abundance, because a little does not need a number because it has been known. And ‘aadan is a verbal noun, and ‘aadan is the name of the counted, like naqd and lakhat. Abu ‘Ubaidah said: ‘aadan is an accusative of the verbal noun. Then some people said: God the Most High explained the number of those years after that, saying: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years, and they added nine. (al-Kahf 18:25)
18:12: The Almighty said: Then We raised them up meaning after they had slept. And the one who is revived or aroused from his sleep is called resurrected because he was prevented from being resurrected or moving about. God the Almighty said: That We may know which of the two parties counted the time. That We may know is an expression for that thing coming into existence and observing it. This is in the manner of the speech of the Arabs, meaning that We may know that it exists. Otherwise, God the Almighty would have known which of the two parties counted the time. Az-Zahr read that He may know with a ya’ and the two parties are the two groups. What is apparent from the verse is that the one party is the young men if they thought that they would be resurrected a little. The second party is the people of Madinah during whose era the young men were sent, when they had a history of the matter of the young men. This is the opinion of the majority of the commentators. A group said: They are two parties of the disbelievers, who differed about the time of the People of the Cave. It was said: They are two parties of the believers. Other things were said that are not connected to the words of the verse. Counted is a past tense verb. Extended is in the accusative case as a direct object, as Abu Ali said. Al-Farra’ said: It is in the accusative case as a distinguishing feature. Al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative case as a circumstance, meaning which of the two parties counted their stay in the time, and the time is the limit. Mujahed said: Amda means number, and this is an explanation of the meaning by way of approximation. At-Tabari said: Amda is accusative by labthaw Ibn Atiyyah: This is not correct. As for the one who said that it is accusative for explanation, then it is wrong for him that af’al is not from a verb of four letters except in the irregular form, and ahsa is a verb of four letters. It may be argued for him by saying: af’al in four letters is common, like your saying: what he gave him for money and gave him for good. And he said in describing his pool, may God bless him and grant him peace: Its water is whiter than milk and Umar ibn al-Khattab said: So it is more wasteful for what he made of it.
18:13: The Almighty's saying: We relate to you their story in truth. When the Almighty's saying: That We may know which of the two parties is most precise necessitated a difference that occurred regarding the duration of the youths, He followed it with the good that He, the Almighty, knows who ordered them to do the truth that occurred. And the Almighty's saying: They are youths, meaning young men and adolescents, He ruled for them to be youthful when they believed without an intermediary. Likewise, the people of the language said: The head of youth is faith. Al-Junayd said: Youth is giving generously, refraining from harming others, and refraining from complaining. It was said: Youth is avoiding forbidden things and hastening to do good deeds. And other things were said. This statement is very good because it includes in its meaning all that was said about youth. God the Almighty said: And We increased them in guidance. That is, We made it easy for them to do righteous deeds, by turning to God the Almighty, distancing themselves from people, and by being renouncer of this world. This is an increase in faith. Al-Suddi said: He increased their guidance with the shepherd’s dog when they chased him away and stoned him for fear that he would bark at them and warn them. The dog raised his hands to the sky like a caller, so God made him speak. He said: O my people, why did you chase me away? Why did you stone me? Why did you beat me? By God, I knew God forty years before we knew Him. So God increased their guidance with that.
18:14: The Almighty's saying: And We strengthened their hearts is an expression of the intensity of determination and strength of patience, which God gave them until they said in front of the infidels: "Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any god besides Him. We would have certainly said then an outrageous thing." And since fear and weakness of the soul are similar in proportion to dissolution, it is good in the intensity of the soul and strength of determination to be likened to binding, and from this it is said: So-and-so is steadfast, if his soul does not separate from fear and war and other things. And from this is the binding on the heart of Moses' mother. And the Almighty's saying: And that He may bind your hearts and plant firmly thereby your feet (al-Anfal 8:11). The Almighty's saying: When they stood up and said contains two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: When they stood up and said has three possible meanings: One of them: That this is a description of their position before the infidel king - as mentioned above - and it is a precedent that requires connection to the heart, as they disobeyed his religion and rejected his majesty in the essence of God. The second meaning, as has been said, is that they were the sons of the nobles of that city, so they went out and gathered behind that city without an appointment, and the eldest of them said: I find myself that my Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, so they said: And we are also arguing within ourselves. So they all stood up and said: (Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any god besides Him. We have certainly spoken an outrage.) That is, if we call upon any god other than Him, then we have spoken injustice and impossibility. The third meaning: that the word standing expresses their determination to flee to God Almighty and to oppose people, as you say: So-and-so stood up to such-and-such a matter if he resolved to do it with the utmost seriousness. Second: Ibn Atiyah said: The Sufis depended on the saying of God swt: When they stood up and said, ‘Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth,’ 2:100. I said: This is an incorrect dependence! These people wandered and remembered God for His guidance, and they thanked Him for the blessings and favors He bestowed upon them, then they wandered on their faces, cut off from their Lord, fearing their people. This is the way of God with the messengers, prophets, and virtuous saints. Where is this from stamping the ground with the feet and dancing with the sleeves! Especially in these times when hearing the beautiful voices of the marmots and swallows, far from it! By God, there is what is between the earth and the heaven. Moreover, this is forbidden according to the group of scholars, as will be explained in Surah Luqman, God willing. And it was mentioned in Glory be to Him about His saying: And do not walk upon the earth exultantly (al-Isra’ 17:73), and that is sufficient. Imam Abu Bakr al-Tarsusi said, when he was asked about the Sufi doctrine, he said: As for dancing and ecstasy, the first to innovate it were the companions of al-Samari, when he made for them a calf with a body that mooed, they stood dancing around it and ecstasied. It is the religion of the infidels and the worshippers of the calf, as will come.
18:15: The Almighty said: These are our people who have taken gods besides Him. That is, some of them said to one another: These are our people, meaning the people of our time and our country, who worshipped idols out of imitation without proof. If only means why. Why do they not bring against them a clear authority? meaning an argument for their worship of idols. It was said: If only refers to the gods, meaning why do they not establish evidence against the idols that they are gods? So their saying If only is a challenge with the meaning of incapacity, and if they are not able to do that, then no attention should be paid to their claim.
18:16: The Almighty said: And when you withdrew from them It was said: It is from what God said to them. That is, when you withdrew from them, then they took refuge in the cave. It was also said: It is from what their leader Yamlikha said, according to what Ibn Atiyya mentioned. Al-Ghaznawi said: Their leader, Makslamina, said that to them, that is, when you withdrew from them and withdrew from what they worship. Then he made an exception and said except God, that is, you did not abandon His worship, so it is a discontinuous exception. Ibn Atiyya said: This is on the assumption that those from whom the People of the Cave fled did not know God, nor did they have knowledge of Him, and they only believed in idols in their divinity. If we assume that they knew God as the Arabs used to do, but they associated their idols with Him in worship, then the exception is connected, because the avoidance occurred in everything that the infidels worship except for the sake of God. In the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Masoud and what they worship besides God, Qatada said this is its interpretation. I said: And what Abu Naim al-Hafiz mentioned on the authority of Ata al-Khurasani is indicative of this regarding the Almighty’s statement: And when you withdrew from them and what they worshipped except God. He said: There were young men from a people who worshipped God and worshipped other gods with Him, so the young men withdrew from the worship of those gods but did not withhold from the worship of God. Ibn Atiyah: According to what Qatada said, al-A is in the position of ghayr and ma in His statement and they worship none but God is in the accusative case, in apposition to the pronoun in His statement you have withdrawn from them. And within this verse, some of them said to each other: If we separate from the disbelievers and are alone with God the Most High, then let us make the cave our refuge and trust in God, for He will extend His mercy to us, and spread it upon us, and provide us with relief in our affair. And all of this is a supplication according to the worldly life, and they were confident from God in the matter of their afterlife. And Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, may God be pleased with him, said: The People of the Cave were sages, and the name of the cave is Hayyum. Mirfaqan is read with a kasra or a fatha on the m, and it is that which one is comforted by. And likewise the elbow of a person is his elbow, and some of them make al-Mirfaq with a fatha on the m the place like the mosque, and they are the two ghats.
18:17: The Almighty said: And you will see the sun, when it rises, inclining away from their cave on the right. That is, you see, O addressee, the sun when it rises, inclining away from their cave. The meaning is: If you had seen them, you would have seen them thus, not that the addressee saw them in reality. Tawazāwār means to move away and incline, from azwār. Zūr means inclination. Azwār in the eye is the one who inclines to look in a direction, and it is used for other than the eye, as Ibn Abi Rabi’ah said: I am afraid of the people visiting me From the word, Antara said: Fazur from the fall of the back of the neck with his milk In the hadith of Azura Mu’tah, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw in the bed of Abdullah bin Rawahah a veil over the bed of Ja’far and a cloak. Ibn Haritha. The people of the two sanctuaries and Abu Amr read tazāwur with the assimilation of the ta’ into the za’, and the original is tātazāwur. Asim, Hamzah, and al-Kisa’i read tazāwur with the za’ lightened. Ibn ‘Amir read tazūr like tahmar. Al-Farra’ narrated tazwāwur like tahmar, all with the same meaning. And when you set, you qardhāhum The majority read it with the ta’ meaning you leave them, as Mujahid said. Qatada said: An-Nahhas leaves them: This is well-known in the language. The Basrans narrated that it is said: qardhā yaqrāduhu if he leaves it. The sun, when it rises, inclines away from their cave to the right, meaning the right of the cave, and when it sets, it passes by them to the left, meaning the north of the cave, so it does not hit them at the beginning of the day or at the end of the day. Their cave was facing the daughters of Na’sh in the land of Ar-Rūm, so the sun would incline away from them, rising and setting, but it would not reach them, so it would harm them with its heat, change its colors, and wear out their clothes. It has been said that their cave had a barrier on the south side and a barrier on the west side while they were in its corner. Al-Zajjaj said that the action of the sun was a sign from God, without the cave’s door being in a direction that required that. A group read Yadqardhum with a ya from qardh which means cutting, meaning the cave cuts them off with its shadow from the sunlight. It has been said: And when it sets, Taqardhum meaning a little of it strikes them, taken from the word qiradah of gold and silver, meaning the sun gives them a little of its rays. They said: Its touching them in the evening was a correction for their bodies. In short, the sign in that is that God the Most High sheltered them in a cave of this description, not in another cave where they would be harmed by the sun’s rays spreading over them most of the day. Based on this, it is possible that the sun was turned away from them by the shade of clouds or some other reason. The aim is to explain that we protect them from the onset of calamity and the change of bodies and colors to them, and from being harmed by sea or cold. And they are in a gap thereof meaning from the cave. A wide gap, the plural of which is gaps and gaps, like rakwa, rakaa, and rakawat. The poet said: We filled every valley and gap with men and horses, without any weakness or isolation. That is, they were in a state where a breeze would hit them. That is from the signs of God, He was kind to them, and this strengthens what Al-Zajjaj said. The commentators said: Their eyes were open while they were asleep, so the one who saw them would think they were awake. It was also said: You would think they were awake because of their frequent tossing and turning, like someone who is awake in his bed. Awake is the plural of awake and awake, which means someone who is alert.
18:18: The Almighty said: And they are asleep as they say: And they are a people bowing, prostrating, and sitting, so He described the group with the source. And We turn them to the right and to the left Ibn Abbas said: So that the earth does not consume their flesh. Abu Hurairah said: That they have two turns every year. It was said: Once every year. Mujahid said: Once every seven years. A group said: They only turned in the last nine, but not in the three hundred. The apparent meaning of the words of the commentators is that the turning was from the action of God, and it is permissible for it to be from a king by the command of God, so it is attributed to God Almighty. The Almighty’s saying: And their dog stretched out his forelegs at the entrance. There are four issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And their dog. Amr bin Dinar said: Among the things that were taken from the scorpion is that it should not harm anyone. It said at night: May God bless Noah. Among the things that were taken from the dog is that it should not harm anyone who attacks it [when it says]: And all of them stretched out their forelegs at the threshold. Most of the commentators agree that it is a real dog, and it was for one of them to hunt or for his crops or his sheep, according to what Muqatil said. And there is a great difference in its color, mentioned by Al-Tha’labi. And its interpretation. Whichever color you mention, you hit it, until it was said the color of a stone and it was said the color of the sky. And there is also a difference in its name, from Ali: Rayyan. Ibn Abbas: Qutmir. Al-Awza’i: Mushir. Abdullah bin Salam: Basit. Ka’b: Suhaib. With us today it is permissible in our law. Ibn Abbas said: They fled at night, and they were seven, and a shepherd passed by with a dog, so he followed them according to their religion. Kaab said: They passed by a dog that barked at them, so they chased it away. It came back and they beat it repeatedly. Then the dog stood on its feet and raised its hands to the sky as if it were supplicating. Then it spoke and said: Do not be afraid of me! I love the revelations of God Almighty, so sleep so that I may guard you. Second: It was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Ibn Umar that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever keeps a dog, except a hunting or livestock dog, will have two qirats deducted from his reward every day. Sahih also narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever keeps a dog, except a sheep dog, or a hunting dog, or a farm dog, will have one qirat deducted from his reward every day. Al-Zuhri said: It was mentioned to Ibn Umar that Abu Hurairah said: May God have mercy on Abu Hurairah! He was a farmer. The established Sunnah indicates that dogs are kept for hunting, farming, and livestock. The deduction in the reward of whoever keeps them is for something other than that of benefit, either because the dog frightens the Muslims and disturbs them with its barking, or to prevent the angels from entering the house, or to dirty it, according to what Al-Shafi’i sees, or not to violate the prohibition against keeping something that has no benefit, and God knows best. He said in one of the two narrations two qirats and in the other one qirat. This may be due to two types of dogs, one of which is more harmful than the other, such as the black dog which the Prophet (peace be upon him) ordered to be killed, and he did not include it in the exception when he forbade killing it, as is stated in the hadith of Jabir, which was narrated in Sahih, and he said: You should stick to the black, white dog with two spots, for it is a devil. It may also be due to the difference in locations, so if he keeps it in Madinah, for example, or in Makkah, it will decrease by two qirats and if he changes it by one qirat, but as for what is permissible to keep, it will not decrease, such as the horse and the cat. And God knows best. Third: The permissible livestock dog according to Malik is the one that walks with the animals, not the one that guards them in the house from thieves. And all crops are those that guard them from wild animals at night or during the day, not from thieves. Others than Malik permitted keeping them for thieves of livestock and crops. The rulings on dogs have been presented in Al-Ma’idah sufficiently, and praise be to God. Fourth: Ibn Atiyah said: My father, may God be pleased with him, told me that he heard Abu al-Fadl al-Jawhari, in the mosque of Egypt, say from the pulpit of his sermon in the year 469 AH: Whoever loves the people of goodness will attain their blessings. A dog loves the people of goodness and accompanies them, so God mentioned him in His perfect revelation. I said: If some dogs have attained this high degree by accompanying and mixing with the righteous and saints, to the extent that God Almighty informed us of that in His Book, the Most High, then what do you think of the believing, modern companions who mix with and love the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, the best of family? Narrated Sahih: Anas bin Malik said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was leaving the mosque, we met a man at the door of the mosque and said: O Messenger of God, when will the Hour be? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What have you prepared for it? The man seemed to be resigned, then he said: O Messenger of God, I have not prepared much prayer, fasting, or charity for it, but I love God and His Messenger. He said: Then you will be with those you love. In another narration, Anas bin Malik said: We were never happier after Islam than when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then you will be with those you love. Anas said: So I love God and His Messenger, Abu Bakr, and Umar, and I hope to be with them even if I do not do their deeds. I said: What Anas held onto includes every soul among Muslims, so our hopes were attached to that even though we were negligent, and we hoped for the mercy of the Most Merciful even though we were not deserving. A dog loved a people, so God mentioned him with them! So how about us when we have the contract of faith and the word of Islam, and the love of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference” (Al-Isla’: 70). A group said: It was not a dog in reality, but rather one of them, and he had sat at the entrance of the cave as a vanguard for them, just as the star following Gemini was called a dog, because it is to it as a dog is to a human, and it is called: the dog of the tyrant. Ibn Atiyyah said: It was named after the animal that is constant in that place. However, this statement is weakened by the mention of the outstretched arms, because in custom it is a description of the dog in reality, and from it is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And none of you should stretch out his arms like a dog. Abu Omar bin Al-Mutraz narrated in the book Al-Yawaqit that it was read and their dog stretched out its forelegs at the entrance, so it is possible that what is meant by the dog is this man according to what was narrated, since stretching out the arms and sticking to the ground with the face raised to look is the appearance of the suspicious one who is hiding himself. It is possible that what is meant is: By the dog, the dog. Jaafar bin Muhammad al-Sadiq read and their dog, meaning the owner of the dog. The Almighty said: He spread out his arms The active participle is used in the sense of lighting because it is a description of a state and it was not intended to inform about the dog's action. The arm is from the tip of the elbow to the tip of the middle finger. Then it was said: He spread out his arms for a long time. And it was said: The dog slept, and that was one of the signs. And it was said: He slept with his eye open. And the courtyard is the yard, as said by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Ibn Jubayr, and any courtyard of the cave, and the plural is Sayyad and Wasad. And it was said: The door. And Ibn Abbas also said it. And he recited: In a vast open land, its hunting is my preserve, and my good deeds there are not denied. It was mentioned earlier. Ata’ said: The threshold of the door, and the closed door is the locked one. I closed the door and I closed it. The threshold is the plant with close roots, so it is common, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: If you had looked at them The majority of scholars read it with a kasra on the waw. Al-A’sha and Yahya ibn Waththab read it with a damma. If you had looked at them, you would have fled from them. “And you would have been filled with terror from them.” That is, because God the Almighty surrounded them with terror and encompassed them with awe. It was also said: Because of the wildness of their place, as if God had sheltered them in this apparently wild place to make people flee from them. It was also said: People were hidden from them by terror, and none of them dared to approach them. It was also said: They fled from them because of the length of their hair and nails. This was mentioned by Al-Mahdawi, Al-Nahhas, Al-Zajjaj, and Al-Qushayri. This is far-fetched, because when they woke up, some of them said to each other: We stayed a day or part of a day. This indicates that their hair and nails were in the same condition, unless it is said: They only said that before they looked at their nails and hair. Ibn Atiyah said: The correct thing about their matter is that God, the Almighty, preserved for them the state in which they slept, so that it would be a sign for them and others among them. Their clothes did not wear out, nor did their appearance change. The one who went to the city did not recognize anything except the features of the land and the building. If he had a state in his soul that he would deny, it would have been more important to him. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Abbas, and the people of Mecca and Medina read lamalta minhum with a shaddah on the lam, based on a doubling that is more common in the language. The emphasis came in the saying of Al-Mukhbal Al-Sa’di: When Al-Nu'man attacked the people in a state of ihram, he filled Ka'b bin Awf's chains with it. The majority read terror with a sukoon on the ‘ayn. Abu Ja’far read it with a damma. Abu Hatim said: These are two dialects. Farrar is an accusative in the state of the word and terror is a second object or a distinguishing feature.
18:19: The Almighty said: And thus We raised them up that they might question one another. Baath: movement from stillness. The meaning is: Just as We struck their ears and increased their guidance and turned them upside down, We also raised them up, meaning We awakened them from their sleep to the state they were wearing, their clothes and their conditions. The poet said: And the young men of truth have been sent with magicians, and they all said between Aath and Nashwan That is, also. The lam in His statement: that they may ask each other is the lam of becoming and the lam of consequence, like His statement: that they may be an enemy and a cause of grief for them (al-Qasas 28:8). So He sent them not for the sake of their asking each other. God Almighty said: They said, ‘We stayed a day or part of a day.’ That is because they entered it in the morning and God sent them at the end of the day. Their leader, Tamlikha or Maksalmina, said: God knows best how long it will last. The Almighty’s saying: Then send one of you with this money of yours to the city. There are seven issues in it: First: Ibn Abbas said: Their shoes were like the hooves of a quarter, mentioned by Al-Nahhas. Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Ibn Amir, Al-Kisa’i and Hafs from Asim read buraqkum with a kasra on the ra’. Abu Amr, Hamza and Abu Bakr from Asim read buraqkum with a sukoon on the ra’, so they deleted the kasra because of its heaviness, and they are two dialects. Al-Zajjaj read buraqkum with a kasra on the waw and a sukoon on the ra’. It is narrated that they woke up hungry, and that the envoy was Tamlikha, who was the youngest of them, according to what Al-Ghaznawi mentioned. The city is Ephesus, and it is said that it is Tarsus, and its name in the pre-Islamic era was Ephesus, but when Islam came they named it Tarsus. Ibn Abbas said: They had dirhams with them on which was the image of the king who was in their time. The second: The Almighty’s saying: So let him see which food is purest. Ibn Abbas said: It is permissible to slaughter, because the people of their country used to slaughter in the name of the idol, and there were people among them who hid their faith. Abbas said: Most of them were Magians. It was said: The purest food means the most blessed. It was said: They ordered him to buy what he thought was food for two or three people so that no one would see it, meaning the most blessed. It was said: They ordered him to buy what he thought was food for two or three people so that no one would see it, then when it was cooked it would suffice for a group, and that is why it was said that food was rice. It was said that it was a stepchild. It was said that it was dates, and God knows best. It was said that the purest is tastier. It was said that it was cheaper. So let him bring you provision from it meaning sustenance. And let him be gentle meaning in entering the city and buying food. And let no one inform you meaning let him not tell. It was said: If he is found guilty, then his brothers should not fall into what he fell into.
18:20: The Almighty said: If they gain the upper hand over you, they will stone you. Al-Zajjaj said: It means with stones, which is the worst kind of killing. It was also said: They will throw insults and curses at you, but the first is more correct, because he was determined to kill them as mentioned in their stories. Stoning in what was mentioned before was a punishment that was different from the people, as it is more effective for all the people of that religion, since they share in it. Third: In this paper mission there is evidence of agency and its validity. Ali bin Abi Talib appointed his brother Aqeel on behalf of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, and there is no disagreement about it in general. Agency was known in the pre-Islamic era and Islam. Do you not see how Abd al-Rahman bin Awf appointed Umayya bin Khalaf to take care of his family and his entourage in Mecca, meaning to protect them, and Umayya was a polytheist, and Abd al-Rahman committed to Umayya to protect his entourage in Medina as a reward for his actions. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Awf who said: I wrote to Umayya bin Khalaf a letter to protect me in my saghiya in Mecca and I would protect him in his saghiya in Medina. When I mentioned Ar-Rahman, he said: I do not know Ar-Rahman! He wrote to me with your name that was in the pre-Islamic era, so Abd Amr wrote to him and mentioned the hadith. Al-Asma’i said: The saghiya of a man are those who incline toward him and come to him, and it is taken from sagha, which means to incline, and everyone who inclines toward or is with something has inclined toward it and listened, from the book of actions. Fourth: Agency is a contract of representation, which God Almighty permitted due to the need for it and the interest in doing so, as not everyone is able to handle his affairs except with the help of others or with luxury, so he appoints someone to relieve him. Our scholars have proven its authenticity with verses from the Book, including this verse, the Almighty’s saying: and those who work on it (al-Tawbah 9:60) and His saying: Go with this shirt of mine (Yusuf 12:93). As for the Sunnah, there are many hadiths, including the hadith of Urwah Al-Barqi, which was mentioned at the end of Al-An’am. Jabir ibn Abdullah narrated that he said: “I wanted to go to Khaybar, so I went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I said to him: I want to go to Khaybar.
