He said: When you go to my agent, take from him fifteen wasqs, and if he seeks a sign from you, then place your hand on his collarbone.” Narrated by Abu Dawud. There are many hadiths with this meaning, and the consensus of the ummah on its permissibility is sufficient. Fifth: Agency is permissible in every right in which representation is permissible. If the usurper appoints you as an agent, it is not permissible, and he is the agent, because every forbidden action cannot be performed by an agent. Sixth: In this verse there is a wonderful point, which is that the agency was only with taqiyya for fear that someone would discover them because of their fear for themselves. The permissibility of appointing someone with an excuse is agreed upon, but as for someone who has no excuse, the majority are of the opinion that it is permissible. Abu Hanifa and Sahnun said: It is not permissible. Ibn al-Arabi said: It is as if Sahnun took it from Asad ibn al-Furat and ruled with it during his days of judgment, and perhaps he used to do that with the people of injustice and tyranny, to be fair to them and humiliate them, and this is the truth, because agency is assistance and is not for the people of falsehood. I said: This is good, but as for the people of religion and virtue, they may appoint someone even if they are present and healthy. The evidence for the validity of the permissibility of the agency of a healthy witness is what was reported by the two Sahihs and others on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man had a camel that was on the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he came to collect it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Give it to him. They asked for a new camel but found nothing but a new one above it. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Give it to him. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The best of you is the one who pays the debt best. Bukhari This hadeeth, despite its authenticity, indicates the permissibility of appointing a person who is present and healthy in body, because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered his companions to give him the old camel that he had, and that was his appointment for them to do so. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was neither sick nor travelling. This refutes the statement of Abu Hanifa and Sahnun in their statement that it is not permissible to appoint a person who is present and healthy in body except with the consent of his opponent. This hadeeth contradicts their statement. Seventh: Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad said: This verse includes partnership because the paper was for all of them. It includes the permissibility of agency because they sent someone they had appointed to buy, and it includes the permissibility of eating with companions and mixing their food together, even if some of them eat more than others. Similar to this is the saying of God the Almighty: And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers (al-Baqarah 2:220) as was explained previously in Al-Baqarah. For this reason, our companions said about a poor person who is given charity and mixed with the food of a rich person and then eats with him: that is unjust. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and everyone who bought a sacrificial animal for him did so. Ibn Al-Arabi said: There is no evidence for that in the verse, because it is possible that each one of them gave it separately, so there would be no partnership in it. There is no reliance in this issue except on two hadiths: One of them: Ibn Omar passed by a saying that they were eating dates, so he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade pairing unless a man asks his brother’s permission. Second: The hadith of Abu Ubaidah about the army of the Khattab. This is less apparent than the first, because it is possible that Abu Ubaidah gave them enough of that food and did not gather them together for it.
18:21: The Almighty said: And thus We made them known meaning We showed them and made them visible. A'thara is a transitive verb with a hamza, and the root of stumbling is in the foot. That they may know that the promise of God is true meaning the Muslim nation during whose era the People of the Cave were resurrected. That is because Decius died and centuries passed and a righteous man ruled the people of that land, so the people of the town disagreed about the gathering and the resurrection of the bodies from Graves, some people failed in that and excluded it and said: Only the souls are burried and the body is eaten by the earth. Some of them said: The soul and body will be resurrected together. This was a great loss for the king and he remained confused, not knowing how to make his matter clear to them, until he put on sackcloth and sat on the ashes and supplicated to God Almighty with an argument and explanation. God made the people of the cave stumble. It is said that when they sent one of them with their money to the city to bring them provisions from it, his person was strange and his dirhams were strange because of the long time. So he was carried to the king and he was righteous and had believed and those with him believed. When he looked at him, he said: Perhaps this is one of the young men who went out during the reign of King Decius, for I was praying to God to show me them. He asked the young man and he told him. The king was pleased with that and said: Perhaps God has sent you a sign, so let us go to the cave with him. So he rode with the people of the city to them. When they approached the cave, Tamlikha said: I will enter upon them so that they will not be terrified. So he entered upon them and informed them of the matter and that the nation is a nation of Islam. It was narrated that they were pleased with that and went out to the king and venerated him and he venerated them, then they returned to their cave. Most of the narrations say that they died the death of truth when Tamlikha spoke to them, as follows. And whoever had doubts about the resurrection of the bodies returned to certainty. This is the meaning of We found them (so that they may know that the promise of God is true) meaning so that the king and his subjects may know that the resurrection is true and the resurrection is true when they dispute among themselves about their affair. And they used that one person as evidence for their story and were afraid to enter upon them, so the king said: Build a structure over them, so those who followed the religion of the youths said: Build a mosque over them. And it was narrated that some of the people went to cover up the cave and leave them in it hidden. And it was narrated from Abdullah bin Omar that God the Almighty blinded the people at that time to their trace and concealed them from them, so that called for building the structure because it was a landmark for them. And it was said: The king wanted to bury them in a golden chest, but someone from them came to him in a dream and said: You wanted to put us in a golden chest, so do not do that, for we were created from dust and to it we will return, so leave us. Here, forbidden and permissible issues arise. Building mosques on graves, praying in them, building on them, and other things that the Sunnah includes as a prohibition are forbidden and not permissible, as Abu Dawud and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed the women who visit graves and those who build mosques and lamps on them. Al-Tirmidhi said: There is a good hadith on this topic on the authority of Abu Hurayrah and Aisha on the authority of Ibn Abbas. The two Sahihs narrated on the authority of Aisha that Umm Habibah and Umm Salamah mentioned a church they had seen in Abyssinia in which there were pictures of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When a righteous man died among them, they would build a mosque over his grave and make those pictures in it. They are the worst of creation in the sight of God Almighty on the Day of Resurrection.” This is the wording of Muslim. Our scholars said: This forbids Muslims from taking the graves of prophets and scholars as mosques. The imams narrated on the authority of Abu Marthad al-Ghanawi that he heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: Do not pray toward graves or sit on them. This is the wording of Muslim. That is, do not take them as a qiblah and pray toward them or toward them as the Jews and Christians did, for that would lead to worshipping those in them, as was the reason for worshipping idols. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, warned against such a thing and blocked the means that lead to it, saying: God’s wrath is severe against a people who take the graves of their prophets and righteous people as places of worship. The two Sahihs narrated on the authority of Aisha and Abdullah bin Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was afflicted, he began to cover his face with his cloak. When he felt distressed by it, he would uncover his face and say while doing so: The curse of God be upon the Jews and Christians, for they took the graves of their prophets as places of worship, warning against what they had done. Muslim narrated on the authority of Jabir, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade plastering graves, sitting on them, or building over them.” Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade plastering graves, writing on them, building over them, or stepping on them. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good and authentic hadith on the authority of Abu al-Hayaj al-Asadi, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib said to me: Shall I not send you on what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent me on? Do not leave any statue without obliterating it, nor any raised grave without leveling it - in one narration - nor any picture without obliterating it. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it. Our scholars said: The apparent prohibition of making graves high and elevated, and that they should be level. Some scholars have said this. The majority of scholars have said that this fourth that is ordered to be removed is what is in excess of the marking, and the grave remains with what is known and respected, and that is the description of the grave of our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the grave of his two companions, may God be pleased with them - according to Malik in Al-Muwatta - and the grave of our father Adam, may God bless him and grant him peace, according to what Al-Daraqutni narrated from the hadith of Ibn Abbas. As for raising the many buildings, it is an adornment of this world in the first stages of the afterlife, and an imitation of those who used to venerate graves and worship them. Considering these meanings and the apparent prohibition, it should be said: It is forbidden. The marking of the grave: its height of a handspan, taken from the camel’s hump. Water is sprinkled on it so that it does not spread with the wind. Al-Shafi’i said there is nothing wrong with plastering the grave. Abu Hanifa said: The grave should not be plastered or plastered, and no building should be raised over it so that it falls. There is nothing wrong with sucking stones as a sign, based on what Abu Bakr Al-Athram narrated: Musaddad narrated to us, Nuh bin Diraj narrated to us, on the authority of Abaan bin Taghlib, on the authority of Jaafar bin Muhammad, who said: Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to visit the grave of Hamza bin Abdul Muttalib every Friday and she marked it with a rock. Abu Omar mentioned it. As for the reward: Burial in a coffin, which is permissible, especially in soft soil. It was narrated that Daniel, may God’s prayers be upon him, was in a coffin made of stone, and that Joseph, may God’s prayers be upon him, recommended that a coffin be made of glass and thrown into a well for fear that it would be worshipped. It remained that way until the time of Moses, may God’s prayers be upon them all. An old woman guided him to it, so he lifted it up and placed it in the pen of Isaac, may God bless him and grant him peace. In Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Waqqas that he said during the illness in which he died: Make a grave for me and erect a monument of bricks over me, as was done for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Lahd: It is to make a slit in the ground and then dig another grave on the side of the slit on the side of the Qiblah if the ground is solid. The deceased is put in it and covered with bricks. In our view, it is better than the slit, because it is what God chose for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu Hanifa said the same. He said: The Sunnah is the slit. Al-Shafi’i said: The slit. Bricks are disliked in the slit. Al-Shafi’i said: There is nothing wrong with them because they are a type of stone. Abu Hanifa and his companions disliked it because bricks are for the perfection of the building, and the grave and what is in it are subject to decay, so perfection is not appropriate for it. Based on this, stone and brick are equated. It was said that bricks leave traces of fire, so they are disliked as a sign of optimism. Based on this, a distinction is made between stone and brick. They said: Bricks and reeds are recommended because it was narrated that a bundle of reeds was placed on the grave of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was narrated from Sheikh Imam Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Hanafi, may God have mercy on him, that he permitted making a coffin in a desert because of the softness of the ground. He said: If a coffin is made of iron, there is nothing wrong with it, but it should be covered with dirt and the upper layer should be covered with clay, near the deceased, and light bricks should be placed on the right and left of the deceased so that it becomes like a grave. I said: From this meaning is the placement of the velvet in the grave of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because Medina is a salt marsh. Shuqran said: By God, I went to cover the velvet under the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the grave. Abu Isa al-Tirmidhi said: The hadith of Shuqran is a strange hadith.
18:22: The Almighty said: They will say, 'Three, their dog was the fourth.' The pronoun in they will say refers to the people of the Torah and the contemporaries of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is because they differed about the number of the People of the Cave. This difference is explicit. It was said that what is meant by it are the Christians, because a group of them were present at the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Najran, and the People of the Cave were mentioned. The Jacobites said: They were three, their dog was the fourth. The Nestorians said: They were five, their dog was the sixth. And he said. And the Musallizis said: They were seven, their dog was the eighth. And it was said: It is a report about the Jews who ordered the polytheists to ask the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the People of the Cave. The waw in his statement, and their dog was the eighth, is the grammarians' way of saying that it is a waw of conjunction that entered at the end of the report about their number, to detail their matter, and to indicate that this is the most that was said. If it were dropped, the statement would be correct. A group including Ibn Khalawayh said: It is the waw of eight. Al-Tha'labi narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash that Quraysh used to say in their number six, seven and eight, so they would insert the waw in the eight. Al-Qaffal narrated something similar, saying: Some people used to say that the number among the Arabs ended at seven, so if it was necessary to increase it, another report would be started by inserting the waw, like His statement: The repentant, the worshippers then He said: And those who forbid evil and those who guard (al-Tawbah 9:112). The evidence for this is that when He mentioned the gates of Hell until, when they reach it, its gates are opened without the waw, and when He mentioned Paradise, He said: Its gates are opened with the waw. And He said: Better than you, Muslims then He said: And virgins so seven was the end of the number for them as ten is now for us. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: Such speech is arbitrary, and seven is the end of the number for them! Then it is refuted by the statement of God Almighty: "He is God, other than whom there is no god, the King, the Holy, the Peace, the Guardian of Security, the Preserver of Faith, the Almighty, the Compeller, the Proud" and He did not mention the eighth name with the waw. Some people who came to the conclusion that their number is seven said: The waw was mentioned in His statement: seven and their eighth to indicate that this number is the truth, and that it is different from the other numbers that the People of the Book mentioned. For this reason, the Almighty said in the two previous sentences a slander at the unseen and did not mention it in the third sentence and did not criticize it in any way. It is as if He said to His Prophet, they are seven and their eighth is their dog. And slandering is speaking based on conjecture. It is said for everything that is specific: slander in it, and stoning and stoning, as He said: War is nothing but what you have learned and tasted, and it is not about the translated hadith I said: Al-Mawardi and Al-Ghaznawi mentioned: Ibn Jarirj and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They were eight, and they made the statement of God Almighty: And the eighth of them was their dog meaning the owner of their dog. This is what strengthens the path of the grammarians in the waw, and that it is as they said. Al-Qushayri said: The waw was not mentioned as a far-fetched imposition, and it is like his statement in another place: And We did not destroy a city but that it had a known book (al-Hijr 15:4) and in another place: But that it had warners * a reminder (Ash-Shu’ara’: 208-209). God the Almighty said: “Say: My Lord knows best their number.” God the Almighty commanded His Prophet, peace be upon him, in this verse to refer the knowledge of their number to Him, the Almighty. Then He informed that the knowledge of that among mankind is few. What is meant by it is the people of the Book, according to Ata’. Ibn Abbas used to say: I am from that group, they were seven and the eighth of them was their dog, then he mentioned the seven by their names, and the dog’s name was Qutmir, a tiger dog, above the Qalti and below the Kurdi. Muhammad bin Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said that it was a Chinese dog, but the correct one is that it was Zubayri. He said: There is no narrator left in Nishapur who wrote this hadith from me except for someone who was not able to. Abu Amr Al-Hairi said that it was written from me. God the Almighty said: So do not dispute about them except with an outward dispute. That is, do not dispute about the People of the Cave except with what We have revealed to you, which is referring knowledge of their number to God the Almighty. It was said: The meaning of what is meant by outward is that you say: It is not as you say, and the like, and do not argue with a matter that has been estimated in that. In this is evidence that God the Almighty did not clarify their number to anyone, so that is why He said: Except with an outward dispute (al-Kahf 18:22), meaning going, as He said: This is a complaint whose shame is apparent from you, and he is not permitted in this verse to argue, but his saying, except for argument is a metaphor from where the People of the Book argue with him. I heard his arguing with them, then he qualified it as apparent, so he differed from the real blameworthy water. The pronoun in his saying, among them refers back to the People of the Cave. And in his saying, from them refers back to the People of the Book who are opposing. And his saying, so do not argue about them means, then count their number, so he omitted the number because the apparent meaning of the statement indicates it. The Almighty said: And do not consult anyone of them about them. It was narrated that he, peace be upon him, asked the Christians of Najran about them and was forbidden from asking. This is evidence that Muslims are forbidden from consulting the People of the Book regarding any knowledge.
18:23: God Almighty said: And never say of anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow.’
18:24: The Almighty’s saying: Except that God wills in two issues: First: The scholars said: God the Almighty rebuked His Prophet, peace be upon him, for what he said to the infidels when they asked him about the spirits, the youths, and Dhul-Qarnayn: Tomorrow I will tell you the answer to your questions. He did not make an exception in that, so the revelation was withheld from him for fifteen days until that was difficult for him and the infidels spread rumors about him, so this Surah was revealed to him as a relief. And He commanded in this verse not to say about any matter, I will do such and such tomorrow, unless he linked that to the will of God the Almighty, so that he would not be fulfilling the ruling of the report, because if he said, I will do that, and he did not do it, then he would be lying, and if he said, I will do that, God willing, then he would not be fulfilling what he was being informed about. The lām in His statement for something is like fi, or as if he said for the sake of something. Second: Ibn Atiyah said: People spoke about this verse regarding the exception in the oath, and the verse is not about oaths, but rather it is about the Sunnah of exception in other than the oath. And his saying: except that God wills in the speech there is an omission that is supported by the apparent meaning and improved by brevity, its meaning is: except that you say except that God wills, or except that you say God willing. So the meaning is: except that you mention God’s will, so except that God wills is not among the words that are forbidden. I said: What Ibn Atiyyah chose and approved of is the statement of Al-Kisa’i, Al-Farra’, and Al-Akhfash. The Basrans said: The meaning is except by the will of God. So if a person says, I will do this, God willing, then it means by the will of God. Ibn Atiyyah said: A group said, Except if God wills, is an exception to His statement, And do not say, He said: This statement was narrated by Al-Tabari and he responded to it, and it is so corrupt that it should not have been narrated. The statement about the exception in the oath and its ruling has been presented in Al-Ma’idah. God the Almighty said: And remember your Lord when you forget There is a question in this, which is the command to remember after forgetting - and there is a difference of opinion about the commanded remembrance, so it was said: It is His saying: "And say: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer than this in right conduct" Muhammad al-Kufi, the interpreter, said: It is in its wording what everyone who did not make an exception is commanded to say, and it is an expiation for forgetting the exception. The majority said: It is a supplication for which he is sinned without this specification. And it was said: It is his saying God willing which he forgot when he swore. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that if he forgot the exception and then remembered even after a year, he did not break his oath if he had sworn. This is the saying of Mujahid. Ismail Ibn Ishaq narrated that from Abu al-Aaliyah regarding God the Almighty's saying: And remember your Lord when you forget He said: He makes an exception if he remembers Him. Al-Hasan: As long as he is in the gathering of remembrance. Ibn Abbas: Their two years, Al-Ghazawi mentioned it and said: It is interpreted as making up for the blessing of the exception to get rid of the sin. As for the exception that is useful in ruling, it is not valid unless it is connected. As-Suddi: That is, every prayer in which you forget something, remember it and it will remind you of it. It was said: Remember it if you forget something else or forget yourself, for that is the reality of remembrance. This verse is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is the opening of a speech according to the most correct opinion, and it is not an exception in the oath at all, and it also applies to all of his nation, because it is a ruling that is repeated among people due to its frequent occurrence. And God is the Grantor of success.
18:25: God the Almighty said: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine. This is better than the length of their stay from God the Almighty. And in the reading of Ibn Masoud And they said, They remained At-Tabari said: The Children of Israel differed about the length of time that they had after they were stumbling upon it until the time of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Some of them said: They remained three hundred and nine years. So God the Almighty informed His Prophet that this length of time was while they were asleep, and that what came after that was unknown to mankind. So God the Almighty commanded that knowledge of that be referred to Him. Ibn Atiyyah said: So his saying on this they remained the first means in the sleep of the cave, and the second they remained means after they were stumbling upon it until the time of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), or until the time of their demise by the affliction. Mujahid: until the time of the revelation of the Qur'an. Ad-Dahhak: until they died. Some of them said: When he said: And they increased by nine, people did not know whether it was hours, days, a group, months, or years. The Children of Israel differed according to that, so God Almighty ordered that knowledge be returned to Him regarding the nine, so it is ambiguous according to this. The apparent meaning of the speech of the Arabs is that it is years, and the apparent meaning of their matter is that they got up and entered the cave shortly after Jesus, and there were still a remnant of the disciples. And other than this was said as follows. Al-Qushayri said: The nine cannot be understood as nine nights and nine hours because the years were mentioned before, just as you say: I have a hundred and five dirhams, and what is understood from it is five dirhams. Abu Ali said and they increased by nine meaning they increased by staying nine, so it was deleted. Ad-Dahhak said, when the verse And they remained in their cave for three hundred was revealed, they said years, whether months, days, or months, so God revealed years. Al-Naqqash related the meaning that they remained for three hundred solar years according to the number of days, so since the information here was for the Arab prophet, nine was mentioned, since the concept in his view was from the lunar years, and this addition is what is between the two calculations. Al-Ghaznawi mentioned something similar. That is, according to the difference in the years of the sun and the moon, because it differs in every thirty-three and a third of a year by one year, so in three hundred it is nine years. The majority read three hundred years with the tanween of one hundred and the tanween of one year, according to this as a substitute or an explanatory apposition. It was said: as an explanation and distinction. And years is in place of one year. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read by adding one hundred to years, and leaving out the tanween, as if they made years like one year if the meaning of them is the same. Abu Ali said: These numbers that are added in the famous hadith to the singular, about three hundred men and a garment, may be added to the plural. In the Mushaf of Abdullah three hundred years, and Ad-Dahhak read three hundred years with a waw. Abu Amr read differently nine with a fatha on the ta’, and the majority read it with a kasra. Al-Farra’, Al-Kisa’i, and Abu Ubaidah said: The estimate is that they remained in their cave for three hundred years.
18:26: The Almighty said: "Say: God knows best how long they stayed." It was said: after their death until the Qur'an was revealed about them, according to Mujahid. Or until they died, according to Ad-Dahhak, or until the time they changed due to decay, according to what was mentioned above. And it was said: how long they stayed in the cave, which is the period that God the Almighty mentioned about the Jews, even though they mentioned an increase and a decrease. That is, no one knows the knowledge of that except God or whoever taught Him that. To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. God the Almighty said: I see and hear with it meaning what I see and hear. Qatada said: No one sees or hears more than God. These are expressions about perception. It is possible that the meaning is I see with it meaning with His revelation and guidance He guided you and your arguments and the truth of matters, and I hear with it the world, so they are two matters not in the way of astonishment. It was said: The meaning is that He sees them and encompasses them with what God said about them. They have no protector besides Him meaning the People of the Cave had no protector to protect them besides God. It is possible that the pronoun in them refers to the contemporaries of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, from the disbelievers. The meaning is: These who differed in the length of their stay have no protector besides God to manage their affairs, so how can they be more knowledgeable than Him, or how can they learn without Him informing them. The Almighty’s saying: And let no one share in His rule. It was read with a ya’ and raising the kaf, meaning reporting from God Almighty. Ibn ‘Amir, Al-Hasan, Abu Raja’, Qatada and Al-Jahdary read and do not associate with a ta’ from above and a sukoon on the kaf, referring to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. His saying and do not associate is in apposition to his saying and see with him and hear. Mujahid read and let him share with a ya’ from below and in the jussive mood. Ya’qub said: I do not know its meaning. Question: There is a difference of opinion about the People of al-Kahf 18:did they die and perish, or were they asleep and their bodies preserved? It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he passed by Syria during one of his retreats with some people at the location of the cave and its mountain. The people walked with him to it and found bones and said: These are the bones of the People of the Cave. Ibn Abbas said to them: Those are people who perished and disappeared a long time ago. A monk heard him and said: I did not think that any of the Arabs would know this. It was said to him: This is the cousin of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. A group narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Let Jesus, son of Mary, perform Hajj with the People of the Cave, for they have not yet performed Hajj. This was mentioned by Ibn Atiyyah. I said: It is written in the Torah and the Gospel that Jesus, son of Mary, is the servant and messenger of God, and that he will pass by Ruja’ as a pilgrim or performer of Umrah, or God will bring that together for him and God will make his disciples the People of the Cave and the Inscription, and they will pass by as pilgrims, for they did not perform Hajj and did not die. We have mentioned this report in full in the Book of Remembrance. So based on this, they are asleep and have not died until the Day of Resurrection, but they will die before the Hour.
18:27: The Almighty said: "And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. There is no changing His words." It was said: This is part of the story of the People of the Cave, meaning follow the Qur'an, for there is no changing the words of God nor going back on what He has told us of the story of the People of the Cave. Al-Tabari said: There is no changing what He has promised with His words to the people of His disobedience and those who oppose His Book. And you will not find you besides Him if you do not follow the Qur'an and oppose it a refuge meaning a shelter. It was said a refuge. Its origin is inclination, and whoever takes refuge in it has inclined towards it. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahim said: This is the end of the story of the People of the Cave. When Muawiyah raided Al-Madhiq towards Al-Ruwah, and Ibn Abbas was with him, he reached the cave in which the People of the Cave were. Muawiyah said: If only He would reveal these to us so that we could look at them. Ibn Abbas said: God has prevented someone better than you from doing that. He said: If I had looked at them, I would have turned away from them in flight. He said: I will not stop until I know their knowledge. He sent a people for that. When they entered the cave, God sent a wind upon them that brought them out. Al-Tha’labi also mentioned this. He mentioned that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked God to show him them. He said: You will not see them in this world, but send to them four of the best of your companions to convey your message to them and call them to faith. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel, peace be upon him: How do I send them? He said: Spread your cloak and have Abu Bakr sit on one end of it, Umar on the other, Uthman on the third, Ali on the fourth, Ali ibn Abi Talib, then call the gentle wind that is subservient to Salman, for God the Almighty commands it to obey you. So he did, and the wind carried them to the door of the cave, and they pulled out a stone from it. The dog charged at them, and when he saw them, he moved his head and wagged his tail and motioned to them with his head to enter. So they entered the cave and they said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings. God restored the souls of the youths, and they stood up with the most severe of them and said: Peace be upon you and the mercy of God and His blessings. They said to them: O group of youths, the Prophet Muhammad ibn Abdullah, may God bless him and grant him peace, sends you his greetings. They said: And upon Muhammad, the Messenger of God, peace as long as the heavens and the earth remain, and upon you is what you have conveyed. They accepted his religion and submitted. Then they said: Send Muhammad, the Messenger of God, our greetings. They went to their beds and went to their sleep until the end of time when the Mahdi emerges. It is said: The Mahdi will greet them and God will revive them, then they will return to their sleep and will not rise until the Hour comes. Gabriel informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of what had happened to them, then the wind blew them back, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How did you find them? So they told him the story, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, do not separate me from my companions and in-laws, and forgive those who love me and love my family, my special people and my companions. It is also said: The People of the Cave entered the cave before Christ, so God the Almighty informed Christ of their story, then they were sent during the period between Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is also said: They were before Moses, peace be upon him, and that Moses mentioned them in the Torah, and for this reason the Jews asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is also said: They entered the cave after Christ, and God knows best which of them it was.
18:28: The Almighty said: And be patient with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening. This is an example. And His saying: And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening. (Al-An'am: 52) in Surah Al-An'am. The discussion of it has already passed. Sulayman Al-Farsi, may God be pleased with him, said: Those whose hearts were to be reconciled came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Uyaynah bin Hisn and Al-Aqra bin Habis. They said: O Messenger of God, if you were to sit in the front of the gathering and remove these people and their cloaks from us - meaning Salman and Abu Dharr and the poor Muslims, and they were wearing wool cloaks and nothing else - we would sit with you and talk to you and learn from you. So God, the Almighty, revealed: "And recite what has been revealed to you of the Book of your Lord. There is no changing His words, and you will not find any refuge besides Him. And be patient with those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His countenance." Until he reached: Indeed, We have prepared for the wrongdoers a Fire whose walls will surround them. Threatening them with the Fire. "Then the Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "He searched until he found them at the back of the mosque, remembering God. He said, 'Praise be to God, who did not cause me to die until He commanded me to be patient with men from my nation. With you is life and with you is death. '" They want His face, meaning to obey Him. Nasr ibn Malik, Malik ibn Dinar, and Abu Abd al-Rahman recited and do not repel those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, and their proof is that it is in the black with the letter waw. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: This does not require that their books say life and prayer with the letter waw, and the Arabs hardly say the morning because it is well-known. It was narrated from al-Hasan and do not turn your eyes away from them, meaning do not let your eyes go beyond them to other prophets of this world, seeking its adornments. Al-Yazidi narrated it. It was said: Do not look down on them, as it is said that someone is turned away from by the eye, meaning he looks down on them. You desire the adornments of the worldly life meaning you adorn yourself by sitting with these leaders who suggested excluding the poor from your gathering. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not want to do this, but God forbade him from doing it. This is nothing more than His saying: If you associate others with God, your work will surely become worthless (al-Zumar 39:65), even though God protected him from associating partners with God. You desire is a present tense verb in the place of a circumstantial, meaning do not count your eyes as desiring, like the saying of Imru’ al-Qays: I told him, "Don't cry. You are either trying to become a king or die, so we will excuse you." Some of them claimed that the correct speech is: Do not turn your eyes away from them, becauseتعدis transitive in itself. It was said to him: And what was mentioned in the recitation of raising the eyes leads to the meaning of do not turn your eyes away from them, do not turn your eyes away from them, do not turn your eyes away from them. So the action is attributed to the eyes and it is in fact directed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as God Almighty said: So do not let their wealth impress you (al-Tawbah 9:55). So admiration was attributed to the wealth, and the meaning is: Do not let their wealth impress you, O Muhammad. And what makes it clearer is what Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is do not turn your eyes away from them to others who have good looks and adornments. God the Almighty said: And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance. Juwaybir narrated on the authority of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn ‘Abis regarding the words of God the Almighty: And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance. He said: It was revealed about Umayyah ibn Khalaf Al-Jumahi, because he called the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to do something that he disliked, such as the poor abandoning it and bringing the leaders of Mecca closer to him. So God the Almighty revealed: And do not obey him whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance. Meaning, the one whose heart We have sealed from monotheism. And follows his desire. Meaning, polytheism. And whose affair is [in] excess. It was said that it is from neglect, which is falling short and showing inability by abandoning faith. It was also said that it is from excess and exceeding the limit. The people said: We are the nobles of Mudar, if we submit, all people will submit. This was from arrogance and excess in speech. It was also said: Excessively means ahead in evil, from their saying: He preceded him in an affair, meaning he preceded. It was said: The meaning of aghafna qalbhu is that we found him negligent, as you say: I met so-and-so and praised him, meaning I found him praiseworthy. Umar ibn Ma'dikarib said to Banu al-Harith ibn Ka'b: By God, we asked you, but you were not stingy, and we fought you, but you did not answer, and we satirized you, but we did not defeat you, meaning we did not find you stingy, nor cowardly, nor defeating you. It was said: "And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance" was revealed about Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari. It was mentioned by Abd al-Razzaq, and al-Nahhas narrated it on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri. And God knows best.
18:29: The Almighty said: And say, 'The truth is from your Lord.' So whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve. The truth is in the nominative case as a predicate of the implied subject. And say, He is the truth. It was said: It is in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is in His statement, From your Lord. And from your Lord. The meaning of the verse: Say, O Muhammad, to those whose hearts We have made heedless of Our remembrance: O people! From your Lord is the truth. To Him belongs success and failure, and in His hand is guidance and misguidance. He guides whomever He wills to believe, and misguides whomever He wills to disbelieve. There is nothing to do with that. So God gives the truth to whomever He wills, even if he is weak, and He deprives whomever He wills, even if he is strong and rich. I do not drive away the believers based on your desires. So if you wish, then believe, and if you wish, then disbelieve. This is not a license or a choice between belief and disbelief, but rather it is a threat and a warning. That is, if you disbelieve, Hell has been prepared for you, and if you believe, Paradise is yours. God Almighty said: Indeed, We have prepared meaning, for the wrongdoers meaning, for the disbelieving deniers, a Fire whose canopies will surround them. Al-Jawhari said: “The canopy is one of the canopies that are extended over the courtyard of the house. And every house made of a canopy is a canopy.” Ru’yah said: Oh, Hakam bin Al-Mundhir bin Al-Jaroud, the canopy of glory is extended over you It is said: A house of Masradaq. Salamah bin Jandal said, mentioning Abu Ruz and his killing by Al-Nu’man bin Al-Mundhir under the feet of elephants: He is the entrance to the house of Al-Nu'man, whose name is Hadour Al-Fioul, after the house of Masradaq. Ibn Al-Arabi said: its canopy is its wall. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: A wall of fire. Al-Kalbi: A neck that emerges from the fire and surrounds the infidels like a pen. Al-Qutbi: The canopy is the partition that is around the tent. Ibn Aziz said the same. It was said: Smoke that surrounds the infidels on the Day of Resurrection, and it is what God mentioned in Surat Al-Mursalat when He says: Go to the shade of three branches (al-Mursalat 77:30) and His statement: And a shade of scorching heat (al-Waqi’ah 56:43), as said by Qatada. It was said: It is the sea surrounding the world. Ya`la ibn Umayya narrated: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The sea is Hell. Then he recited: A fire whose canopy surrounds them. Then he said: By God, I will never enter it as long as I am alive, and not a drop of it will touch me. Al-Mawardi mentioned it. Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from the hadith of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The canopy of Hell has four walls, each wall is a distance of forty years’ journey. And he narrated it in it: A good, sound, strange hadith. I said: This indicates that the canopy is what is above the infidels of smoke or fire, and its walls are as described. God the Almighty said: And if they call for help, they will be helped with water like molten copper, which scalds their faces. Ibn Abbas said: Mahl is a thick water like the dregs of oil. Mujahid: Pus and blood. Ad-Dahhak: Black water. “And Hell is black,” its water is black, “its trees are black,” and its people are black. Abu Ubaidah said: “It is everything that has been melted from the gems of the earth, such as iron, lead, copper, and tin, and it surges with boiling. That is mahhl.” Something similar was narrated from Ibn Masoud. Saeed bin Jubair said: It is that which has reached its peak heat. He said: “Mahl is a type of tar. It is said: “He molten the badger,” so it is mahmool. It was also said: It is poison. The meanings of these sayings are close. At-Tirmidhi narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in his statement: like molten oil, he said: Like cloudy oil, so when he brings it to his face, it scalds his face. Abu Eisa said: We only know this hadith from Rashdin bin Saad, and Rashdin has been criticized for its memory. And it was narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his statement: And he will be given to drink from a water of purulent blood, swallowing it (Ibrahim 14:16-17), he said: (It is brought close to his mouth and he dislikes it, but when it is brought close to him, it burns his face and the scalp of his head falls off. If he drinks it, it cuts his intestines until it comes out of his anus. God Almighty says: And they will be given to drink scalding water, so it will sever their intestines (Muhammad 47:15), he says: “And if they call for help, they will be given water like molten copper, which will burn their faces. What an evil drink and what an evil resting place!” He said: A strange hadith. The linguists have agreed on them. In As-Sahah: (Mahl) is molten copper. Ibn Al-A’rabi: Mahl is molten lead. Abu Amr said: Mahl is the dregs of oil. Mahl is also pus and blood. In the hadith of Abu Bakr: Bury me in these two garments of mine, for they are for molten metal and dust. And Mahlfa Mujahid said: Its meaning is gathered, as if he had gone to the meaning of companionship. Ibn Abbas: A home. Ata: a place of rest. It was also said: a cradle. Al-Qatabi said: a seat. The meaning is close, and its origin is from the word mutaka’a, from which it is said: I leaned on the elbow. The poet said: She said to him and exulted: Is there not a young man who will lead the people in the early morning? It is said: A man is resting on his elbow and cannot sleep. Abu Dhu’ayb al-Hudhali said: The friend slept and I spent the night in comfort, as if my eyes were slain by the sap of a bitter tree.
18:30: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - never will We allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds. When He mentioned what He has prepared for the disbelievers of humiliation, He also mentioned what the believers will receive of reward. There is an implied meaning in the speech, meaning that We will not allow to be lost the reward of any who did well among them. As for any who did well among the non-believers, his work will be nullified. Work is in the accusative case as a specification, and if you wish, you can apply best to it. It was said: Never will We allow to be lost the reward of any who did well in deeds, an interjectional statement, and the predicate is His statement.
18:31: God the Almighty said: For them are Gardens of Eden. "Gardens of Eden" is the navel of Paradise, meaning its center, and the rest of the gardens surround it. It is mentioned in the plural form because of its vastness, because every spot of it is suitable to be a garden. Qabil: Eden is residence. It is said: Eden in a place if he resides in it. And Edenat the country means settling in it. And the camels Edenat in a place so they stuck to it and did not leave it, and from it Gardens of Eden meaning gardens of residence. And from it the mine was named with a kasra on the dal, because people reside in it in summer and winter. And the center of everything is its mine. Eden: the she-camel that resides in grazing. Eden is a country, said Al-Jawhari. "Rivers flow beneath them" has been mentioned in more than one place. "They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold" is the plural of bracelet. Saeed bin Jubair said: On each one of them are three bracelets: one of gold, one of silver, and one of pearls. I said: This is stated in the Qur’an. He said here of gold and in Al-Hajj and Fatir he said: of gold and pearls (al-Hajj 22:23) and in al-Insan 76:of silver (al-Insan 76:21). Abu Hurairah said: I heard my friend, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The adornment of the believer reaches where the ablution reaches. Narrated by Muslim. Al-Farra’ narrated:َهْل ونwith a fat-ha on the ya’, a sukoon on the ha’, and a fat-ha on the lam, light. It is said: a woman adorned herself, so she is haliyyah if she wore jewelry. And the adornment of something with the eyes of adorning it, was mentioned by An-Nahhas. And the bracelet is the bracelet of a woman. The plural is aswarah, and the plural is aswarah. And it was readُْواو عهاه أهلوهُو منذَب (al-Zukhruf 43:53) and the plural may be aswar. And God the Most High said: They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold. Al-Jawhari said. Ibn Aziz said: Asawara is the plural of aswara, and aswara is the plural of sawar and swar, and it is what is worn on the arm made of gold. If it is made of silver, then it is qalb, and its plural is qalbah. If it is made of horn or ivory, then it is musk, and its plural is musk. An-Nahhas said: Qatrab narrated that one of the asawara is iswar. Qatrab is an anomaly, and Yaqub and others left him out and did not mention him. I said: It has been mentioned in Sahih Al-Bukhari and Abu Amr bin Al-Ala said: Its singular is Iswar. The commentators said: Since women wore bracelets and crowns in this world, God Almighty made that for the people of Paradise. God Almighty says: And they will wear green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade. Fine silk is the thin, delicate type, singular: musnadassa, as Al-Kisa’i said. Brocade is the thicker type - according to Ikrimah - which is silk. The poet said: You bet they wear feelings once and brocade is their clothing another time Brocade is silk. Ibn Bahr: woven with gold. Al-Qatabi: Persianized Al-Jawhari: its diminutive is Abiraq. It was said: it is Istaf’ala from Al-Bariq. The correct view is that there is agreement between the two languages, as there is nothing in the Qur’an that is not from the language of the Arabs, as mentioned above, and God knows best. Green was mentioned specifically because it is in agreement with the sight, because whiteness scatters the sight and causes pain, and blackness is blameworthy, and greenness is between whiteness and blackness, and that gathers the rays, and God knows best. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas that he said: While we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, a man came to him and said: O Messenger of God, tell us about the henna clothes, are they created or woven? Some of the people laughed. He said to them: Who are you laughing at, an ignorant person who asks a scholar? So let him sit for a while or a little. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Where is the one who asked about the clothes of Paradise? He said: Here I am, O Messenger of God. He said: No, rather the fruits of Paradise will split from it. He said it three times. Abu Hurairah said: The home of the believer is a hollow pearl in the middle of which is a tree that grows garments. He will take with his finger, or he said his two fingers, seventy garments arranged in the home and coral. Yahya bin Salam mentioned it in his interpretation, and Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned it in his Raqa’iq. We have mentioned its chain of transmission in the book of At-Tadhkirah. It is mentioned in the hadith that each one of them will have a garment with two faces, each face having a color, and they will speak in a voice that the listener will like. One face will say to the other: I am more honorable to the friend of God than you. I approach his body and you do not. The other will say: I am more honorable to the friend of God than you. I see his face and you do not see. God the Almighty said: Reclining therein on couches couches is the plural of couch, which is the beds in the bridal chambers. It was said that it is the furnishings in the bridal chambers, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. Ibn Abbas said that it is the beds of gold and they are crowned with pearls and rubies and the cushions are on them. The couch is between Sana’a and Ayla and between Aden and Jabiyah. The root of the word mutak’iyyin is mutak’iyyin, and likewise itaka is its root is awtaka’a, and the root of taka’a is waka’a, and from it is taka’a for leaning on something, so the waw was changed to a ta’ and assimilated. A man waka’a is someone who reclines a lot. Yes, the reward and good resting place means the gardens, the opposite of and bad resting place which was mentioned earlier. If it were na’amat it would have been permissible because it is the name of Paradise. And on this and a good resting place and Al-Bara’ bin Azib narrated: That a Bedouin stood up to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing with knowledge on his she-camel Al-Adhba’, and he said: I am a Muslim man, so tell me about this verse: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds the verse, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “You are not far from them, nor are they far from you, they are these four: Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali, so inform your people that this verse was revealed about them.” Al-Mawardi mentioned it, and Al-Nahhas attributed it in the book The Meaning of the Qur’an, he said: Abu Abdullah Ahmad bin Ali bin Sahl told us, he said: Muhammad bin Hamid told us, he said: Yahya bin Al-Durais told us, on the authority of Zuhair bin Mu’awiyah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, he said: A Bedouin stood up, and he mentioned it and Al-Suhayli attributed it in the book Al-I’lam. And we have narrated all of that with permission, and praise be to God.
18:32: The Almighty said: And present to them an example of two men. This is an example of someone who is proud of the world and disdains sitting with the believers, and it is connected to His saying: And be patient. There is a difference of opinion regarding the names and identification of these two men. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed about two brothers from the people of Makkah from Makkah from Makkah, one of them was a believer, and he is Abu Salamah Abdullah bin Abdul Asad bin Hala bin Abdullah bin Omar bin Makhzoum, the husband of Umm Salamah before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The other was a disbeliever, and he is Al-Aswad bin Abdul Aswad. They are the two brothers mentioned in Surah As-Saffat in His saying: A speaker among them said, 'Indeed, I had a companion.' (al-Saffat 37:51) Each of them inherited four thousand dinars, so one of them spent his money in the way of God and asked his brother for something, and he said what he said. This was mentioned by Al-Tha'labi and Al-Qushayri. It was said: It was revealed about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of Makkah. It was said: It is an example for all those who believe in God and all those who disbelieve. It was said: It is like La’yaynah ibn Hasan and his companions with Sulayman and Suhaib and his companions. God likened them to two men from the Children of Israel, two brothers, one of them was a believer and his name was Judah, according to Ibn Abbas. Muqatil said: His name was Tamlikha. The other was an unbeliever and his name was Qartush. They are the two whom God described in Surat As-Saffat. Muhammad ibn As-Sahn Al-Muqri’ also mentioned that the name of the better of the two was Tamlikha and the other was Qartush. They were partners and then they divided the money, so each of them had three thousand dinars. The believer bought slaves from them for a thousand and freed them, and for the Qaniyah thousand he bought clothes and clothed the naked, and for the third thousand he bought food and fed the hungry. He also built a mosque and did good. The other man used his wealth to marry wealthy women, bought livestock and cattle, and raised them to a great height. He traded with the rest of them and made a profit until he surpassed the wealth of the people of his time. The first man became needy, so he wanted to employ himself in a garden to serve it, so he said: If I went to my partner and companion and asked him to employ me in some of his gardens, I would hope that that would be better for me. So he came to him, but he could hardly reach him because of the thick veil. When he entered upon him, recognized him, and asked him what he needed, he said to him: Did I not divide the wealth with you in half? What did you do with your wealth? He said: I bought with it from God Almighty something better and more lasting. He said: Are you truly one of those who believe? I do not think that rumours are widespread! I see you as nothing but a fool, and your reward for your foolishness is nothing but deprivation. Do you not see what I did with my wealth that it led to what you see of wealth and good condition? That is because I earned it and you acted foolishly. Get out of my presence. Then came the story of this rich man, which God the Most High mentioned in the Qur’an about the encompassing of his fruit and its disappearance from the origin of what was sent upon it of evil of account. Al-Tha’labi mentioned this story with a different wording, but the meaning is close. Ata’ said: They were partners who had eight thousand dinars. It was said: They inherited it from their father and they were two brothers, so they divided it. One of them bought land for a thousand dinars, so he said to his companion: O God, so-and-so has bought land for a thousand dinars, so they said: O God, so-and-so built a house for a thousand dinars and gave it in charity. Then his companion built a house for a thousand dinars, so he said: O God, so-and-so built a house for a thousand dinars, and I will buy from You a house in Paradise for a thousand dinars, so he gave it in charity. Then he married a woman and spent a thousand dinars on her, so he said: O God, so-and-so married a woman for a thousand dinars, and I seek from You a woman from Paradise for a thousand dinars, so he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then he bought servants and goods for a thousand dinars, and I will buy from you servants and goods from Paradise for a thousand dinars, so he gave a thousand dinars in charity. Then he was in dire need and said: Perhaps my friend will do me a favor. So he went to him and said: What happened to your money? So he told him his story. He said: You are one of those who believe in this story! By God, I will not give you anything! Then he said to him: You worship names of God, and I worship nothing but an idol. His friend said: By God, I will admonish him. So he admonished him, reminded him and frightened him. He said: Let us go fishing, and whoever catches the most is in the right. They said to him: O brother, the world is too insignificant to God for Him to make it a reward for a doer of good or a punishment for an unbeliever. He said: So he forced him to go out with him, so God tested them both. The unbeliever would throw his net and call upon the name of his idol, and fish would come up flowing out. The believer would throw his net and call upon the name of God, but nothing would come up for him in it. So he said to him: What do you think? I have more than you in this world in share, position and number, and likewise I will be better than you in the Hereafter, if what you claim is true. He said: The angel in charge of them was upset, so God Almighty commanded Gabriel to take him and go with him to Paradise and show him the dwellings of the believer therein. When he saw what God had prepared for him, he said: By Your glory, what he attained in this world will not harm him after his destiny is this. And he showed him the dwellings of the disbeliever in Hell. He said: By Your glory, what he attained in this world will not benefit him after his destiny is this. Then God the Most High took the soul of the believer and destroyed the unbeliever with a punishment from Him. When the believer settled in Paradise and saw what God had prepared for him, he and his companions began to ask each other, and he said: Indeed, I had a companion (al-Saffat 37:51) saying, Are you indeed among those who believe? (al-Saffat 37:51), and a caller called out: O people of Paradise, are you looking forward? So he looked into Hell and saw him in the depths of Hell. Then the verse was revealed: And present to them an example. God the Most High explained the state of the two brothers in this world in this surah, and explained their state in the Hereafter in Surah As-Saffat in His statement: Indeed, I had a companion * saying, ‘Are you indeed among those who believe?’ _ to His statement _ For the like of this let the workers work. (al-Saffat 37:51-61) Ibn Atiyyah said: Ibrahim bin Al-Qasim Al-Kabet mentioned in his book on the wonders of the countries that the two gardens of Tahir Tanis were these two gardens, and they belonged to two brothers, so one of them sold his share of the other and spent it in the obedience of God until the other reproached him, and it happened. There was a dialogue between them, so God Almighty drowned her in one night, and this verse refers to her. It has been said that this is a parable that God Almighty gave for this nation, and it is not report of a previous situation, to make them renounce the world and desire the hereafter, and most of it is a warning and a deterrent, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. The context of the verse indicates the opposite of this, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: And We surrounded them with palm trees meaning, We surrounded them on both sides with palm trees. Haffaaf is the side, and its plural is ahfafah. It is also said: The people surrounded so-and-so, huffawan hafan, meaning, they went around him. From this comes huffain around the throne (al-Zumar 39:75). And We placed between them crops meaning, We placed palm trees around the grapevines, and crops in the middle of the grapevines. Both gardens meaning, each one of the gardens produced its fruit completely, which is why He did not say produced. There is a difference of opinion about the word both and both as to whether it is singular or dual. The people of Basra said: It is singular, because both and both in emphasizing the two are like kull in the plural, and it is a singular noun that is not dual, so if it follows an apparent noun it is in the nominative, accusative and genitive in the same state. You say: I saw both of the two men and both of the two men came to me and I passed by both of the two men. If it is connected to an implied noun, the alif is changed to a ya in the position of the genitive and accusative, you say: I saw both of them and I passed by both of them, just as you say upon them. Al-Farra’ said: It is dual, and it is taken from kull, so the lam was lightened and the alif was added for the dual. Likewise, both are for the feminine, and they are only added to the genitive and are not spoken with one, and if it was spoken with it, it would be said: kull and kulta and both of them and both of them. He cited as evidence the saying of the poet: On each of her legs is a single phalanx, both of which are connected by an appendix. He wanted to say in one of her legs, so he made it singular. This statement is weak according to the people of Basra, because if it were dual, its alif in the accusative and genitive cases would have to be a ya’ with the apparent noun, and because the meaning of both is different from the meaning of all, because both is for encompassing, and both indicates a specific thing. As for this poet, he deleted the alif out of necessity and assumed that it was extra, and what is necessary cannot be made an argument, so it is proven that it is a singular noun like ma’i, except that it was placed to indicate the dual, just as their saying nahnu is a singular noun that indicates two or more, as is indicated by the saying of Jarir: Both of my days are a day of repentance, even if we only visit her occasionally. So he reported about both a singular day, just as he reported by saying she came, and if it were dual, he would have said she came and a day. There is also a difference of opinion about the alif of both. Sibawayh said: The alif of both is for femininity and the ta’ is a substitute for the lam of the verb, which is a waw, and the original is kulwa, and it was only replaced with a ta’ because in the ta’ is the sign of femininity, and the alif in kulwa may become a ya’ with the pronoun and thus it is removed from the sign of femininity, so in replacing the waw it became a ta’ to emphasize the femininity. Abu Omar al-Jarmi said: The ta’ is attached and the alif is the lam of the verb, and its estimation according to him is fa’tal, and if the matter was as he claimed, they would have said in the nisba to it kaltuwi, so when they said kulwi and dropped the ta’, it indicates that they made it run like the ta’ in sister, if you are attributed to her, you say akhwi, al-Jawhari mentioned it. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: Grammarians have permitted, in other than the Qur’an, to carry it on the meaning, and to say: Both gardens produced their fruit, because the preferred meaning is both of them produced. Al-Farra’ permitted: Both gardens produced their fruit, because the meaning is all of the gardens. He said: In Abdullah’s reading: Both gardens produced their fruit. The meaning according to al-Farra’ is: Everything from the gardens produced its fruit. And food with a damma on the hamza is the fruit of the palm tree and the tree. Everything that is eaten is food, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: Its food is everlasting (al-Ra`d: 35). And it was mentioned before: And you did not wrong anything from it meaning it did not decrease.
18:33: The Almighty said: And We caused a river to gush forth within them. That is, We caused a river to flow and split between the two gardens. And he had fruit. Abu Ja`far, Shaibah, `Asim, Ya`qub, and Ibn Ishaq read thimr with a fatha on the tha` and the meem. Likewise, his statement, and his fruit was surrounded, is the plural of thimrah. Al-Jawhari said: The fruit is thimr, like kitab and kutubu, and the plural of thimr is atthmar, like an`aq and `anq. The fruit also means fruitful money, and it can be pronounced lightly or heavily. Abu `Amr read wakan lahthimr with a damma on the tha` and a sukoon on the meem, and he explained it as types of money. The rest read it with a damma on both letters. Ibn `Abbas said: gold, silver, and money. Something similar to this has already been explained in Al-An`am. Al-Nahhas said: Ahmad bin Shuaib told us, he said: Imran bin Bakkar told me, he said: Ibrahim bin Al-Ala Al-Zubaidi told us, he said: Shuaib bin Ishaq told us, he said: Harun told me, he said: Aban told me, on the authority of Tha’lab, on the authority of Al-A’mash, that Al-Hajjaj said: If I heard someone recite and it had fruit, I would cut off his tongue. So I said to Al-A’mash that Al-Hajjaj said: If I heard someone recite and it had fruit, I would cut off his tongue. So she said to Al-A’mash: Will you take that? He said: No! Nor the blessing of the eye. So he used to recite fruit and take it from all the fruit. Al-Nahhas said: So the estimation according to this statement is that he pluralized fruit to fruits, then pluralized fruits to fruits, and it is good in Arabic, except that the first is more similar, and God knows best, because his saying, Both gardens produced their fruit indicates that it had fruit. God Almighty said: Then he said to his companion while he was conversing with him. That is, he was discussing the matter with him and answering him. Conversation is answering, and dialogue is responding. It is said: I spoke to him, but he did not find an answer, and he did not return to a question, nor a question, nor a conversation, nor a dialogue, meaning he did not return an answer.
18:34: The Almighty said: I am more than you in wealth and stronger in men. The group is the group, which is less than ten. Here, what is meant is the followers, servants, and children, as explained above.
18:35: The Almighty says: And he will enter his Paradise. It was said: He took the hand of his believing brother and walked around him in it and showed it to him. And he was unjust to himself, meaning by his disbelief, and it is a sentence in the place of a state. And whoever enters his exile into the Fire by his disbelief is unjust to himself.
18:36: The Almighty said: He said, 'I do not think that this will ever perish.' He denied the perishing of the house. And I do not think that the Hour will come. That is, I do not think that the resurrection will happen. And if I am returned to my Lord. That is, even if I am resurrected, just as He gave me these blessings in this world, He will give me something better than it because of His honor for me. This is the meaning of His statement: I will surely find something better than it as a return. He only said that when his brother called him to believe in the resurrection and the gathering. In the manuscripts of Mecca, Medina, and Syria from it. In the copies of the Qur'ans of the people of Basra and Kufa from it in the singular form, and the dual form is better because the pronoun is closer to the two gardens.
18:37: God Almighty says: His companion said to him Judah or Tamlikha, according to the dispute over his name. Have you disbelieved in He who created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then proportioned you as a man? He admonished him and explained to him that what he acknowledged of these things that no one denies is more wonderful than the resurrection. And formed you as a man means He made you of moderate stature and background, with healthy male limbs.
18:38: The Almighty said: But He is God, my Lord This is how Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami and Abu al-Aaliyah read it. It was narrated from al-Kisa'i that But He is God means but the matter is God, my Lord, so he implied its name in it. The rest read but we with the alif. Al-Kisa'i said: It has an advancing and delaying, its meaning is: but God is my Lord, so the hamza was deleted from ana in order to make it lighter due to frequent use, and one of the two noons was assimilated into the other, and the alif of ana was deleted in connection and confirmed in stopping. Al-Nahhas said: The doctrine of al-Kisa'i, al-Farra' and al-Mazini is that the original is lakin ana by throwing the movement of the hamza on the noon of lakin, so the hamza was deleted and the noon was assimilated into the noon, so the stop is on it, lakin, and it is the alif of ana to show the movement. Abu Ubaid said: The original is lakin ana, so the alif was deleted and two noons met, so the emphasis came for that reason, and al-Kisa'i recited to us: There is a frown on the handsome face of Hanawat, and whoever says it is a liar He meant: To God you are, so he dropped one of the two lāts from to God and deleted from you. Another said and brought it according to the original: You throw me the sideways, meaning you are guilty, and you turn me over, but I will not tell you anything But I said Abu Hatim: They narrated from Asim but we are God my Lord and he claimed that this is a mistake, meaning proving the alif in the insertion. Al-Zajjaj said: Proving the alif in but we are God my Lord in the insertion is good, because the alif was deleted from ana and they brought it instead. He said: And in the reading of Abu but we are God my Lord and Ibn Amir and Al-Masili from Nafi and Ruways from Yaqub read but we are in the case of stopping and connecting together with proving the alif. And the poet said: I am the sword of the tribe, so know me as Hamid, the one who has scattered the hump Al-A'sha said: How can I, and the impersonation of rhymes after my gray hair, that is enough of a disgrace There is no disagreement in proving it in the pause. He is God, my Lord He is the pronoun of the story, the matter, and the command, like His statement, Then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror (al-Anbiya 21:79) and His statement, Say, He is God, the One. “And I do not associate with my Lord anyone.” Its implication indicates that the other brother was a polytheist who worshipped other than God Almighty. It is possible that he meant I do not see wealth and poverty except from Him, and I know that if He wanted to take away the worldly life from the owner, He would have been able to do so, and He is the One who brought me poverty. It is imperative that he meant your denial of the resurrection, whose fate is that God Almighty is not able to do so, and this is to render the Lord, glory be to Him, incapable, and whoever renders Him, glory be to Him, incapable is likening Him to His creation, which is polytheism.
18:39: The Almighty’s saying: “Why did you not say, when you entered your garden, ‘What God wills has occurred. There is no power except with God.’” There are two issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Why did you not say, when you entered your garden, ‘What God has willed! There is no power except with God’? That is, it is a rebuke and advice from the believer to the disbeliever and a response to him, if he said I do not think that this will ever perish and what is in the nominative case, meaning: This garden is what God has willed. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farra’ said: The matter is what God has willed, or it is what God has willed, meaning the matter is the will of God Almighty. It was said: The answer is implied, meaning what God has willed will be, and what He does not will will not be. There is no power except with God meaning whatever wealth you have accumulated is by the power and strength of God Almighty, not by your power and strength, and if He had willed to take away the blessing from it, it would not have been accumulated. Second: Ashhab said: Malik said: Everyone who enters his house should say this. Ibn Wahb said: Hafs ibn Maysarah told me: I saw written on the door of Wahb ibn Munabbih: Whatever God wills, there is no power except with God. It was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said to Abu Hurairah: Shall I not guide you to a word from the treasures of Paradise? I said: Yes. He said: There is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Almighty. It was narrated that whoever enters his house or My servant leaves and submits, “Muslim included it in his Sahih from the hadith of Abu Musa. In it: He said: O Abu Musa or O Abdullah ibn Qays, shall I not guide you to a word from the treasures of Paradise?” In another narration: A treasure from the treasures of Paradise. She said: What is it, O Messenger of God? He said: There is no power or strength except with God. And from him he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Shall I not guide you to a word from the treasures of Paradise? I said: Yes. He said: There is no power or strength except with God, the Most High, the Almighty. It was narrated that “Whoever enters or leaves his home and says: ‘In the name of what God wills, there is no power except with God,’ the devils will flee from him and God will send down blessings upon him. Aisha said: ‘If a man leaves his home and says: In the name of God, the angel says: You are guided. If he says: What God wills, the angel says: You are protected. If he says: There is no power except with God, the angel says: You are protected.’” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever says, meaning when he leaves his home: ‘In the name of God, I put my trust in God, there is no power or strength except with God,’ it will be said: You are protected and the devil will move away from him.” This is a strange hadith that we do not know except from this source. Abu Dawud also narrated it and added to it, saying to him: You are guided, sufficed, and protected. Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a man goes out of the door of his house or the door of his home, there are two angels with him assigned to him. So if he says, ‘In the name of God,’ they say, ‘You are guided.’ And if he says, ‘There is no power or strength except with God,’ they say, ‘You are protected.’ And if he says, ‘I put my trust in God,’ they say, ‘You are protected.’ Then his companions meet him and say, ‘What do you want from a man who has been guided, protected, and sufficed?’” Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah said in ‘Ulum al-Hadith: Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzaymah was asked about the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Paradise and Hell argued, and this one said, ‘This one, meaning Paradise, admits the weak.’ Who is the weak one? He said: The one who clears himself of power and strength means twenty or fifty times a day. Anas bin Malik said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever sees something that pleases him and says: ‘Whatever God wills, there is no power except with God,’ the evil eye will not harm him.” A group of people said: There is no one who says: Whatever God wills, it will be, and something befalls him, except that he is pleased with it. It was narrated that whoever says four things will be safe from four things: Whoever says these things will be safe from the evil eye. Whoever says: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs will be safe from the trickery of Satan. Whoever says: I entrust my affair to God will be safe from the trickery of people. Whoever says: There is no god but You, Most High, I have been among the wrongdoers will be safe from grief. God the Almighty said: If you see me, I am less than you in wealth and children. “If” is a condition, if you see is in the subjunctive mood, and the answer is then perhaps my Lord and ana is a separator with no syntactic position. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case to emphasize the nun and the ya’.
