Isa bin Omar read if you see me, I am less than you in wealth and children in the nominative case, making ana the subject and less its predicate, and the sentence is in the position of the second object, and the first object is the nun and the ya’, except that the ya’ was deleted because the kasra indicates it, and its inclusion is Hajid Baghdadi and it is the original because it is the name in reality.
18:40: The Almighty said: So perhaps means perhaps, meaning perhaps my Lord. That He will give me something better than your garden meaning in the Hereafter. And an elephant in this world. And sends upon it meaning upon your garden. Hisban meaning targets from the sky, the singular of which is hisbanah, as stated by Al-Akhfash, Al-Qutbi, and Abu Ubaidah. The Bedouin said: Al-Hisbanah and Al-Sahaba, and Al-Hisbanah means the pillow, and Al-Hisbanah and Al-Sa'iqa. Al-Jawhari said: Al-Hisban with the dammah: torment. Abu Ziyad Al-Kalabi said: Hisban meaning locusts struck the earth. Hesban is also hisab, and God the Almighty said: The sun and the moon follow a precise calculation (Al-Rahman: 5), and hisab here was explained as such. Al-Zajjaj said: Hisab is from hisab, meaning he sends upon it the torment of hisab, which is the calculation of what your hands have earned, so it is from the category of deleting the added. Hesban is also: short arrows that are shot in one shot, and it was from the shooting of the Chosroes. And the targets from the sky are torment. Then it becomes a slippery ground meaning a white land in which no plants grow and no foot can stand on it. It is the most harmful land after it was the most beneficial land, and slippery is an emphasis on the description of the ground, meaning feet slip from it because of its smoothness. It is said: a slippery place with the movement meaning it is slippery, and it is originally the source of your saying: his foot slipped, slipping, and someone else made it slip. Slipping is also the rump of an animal. Ru’bah said: As if she is a slut at the slippery slope Al-Mazlaqa and Al-Mazlaqa: the place where one cannot stand. The same applies to Al-Zalaqah. Al-Zalaq Al-Halaq, his head slipped, he made him slip, he shaved it, Al-Jawhari said. Al-Zalaq Al-Maghluq, like An-Naqd and An-Naqd. It is not meant that it becomes a slippery place, but rather it is meant that no growth can be avoided in it, like the head if it is shaved, no hair remains on it, Al-Qushayri said.
18:41: The Almighty said: Or its water becomes sunken meaning sunken and gone, so it becomes the land without water after it was the land with water. Sunken is a source that is used in place of a noun, just as one says: a man of fasting and breaking the fast, justice and contentment, virtue and falsehood, and the women of Noah. The masculine and feminine, dual and plural are the same in it. Omar bin Kathloum said: His horses remain Noah's, and his reins are tied tightly to them. last: Pour out their tears like hyenas and answer Noah, wailing, standing up. Any mourners. It was said: Or its water becomes deep, so the noun was omitted, like And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82), mentioned by Al-Nahhas. Al-Kisa’i said: Deep water, and the water has sunk, it has sunk, it has sunk, it has sunk, it has entered the head. And it has sunk, it has sunk, it is a language in it. He said: His eye was jealous or not The sun set, meaning it set. Abu Dhu'ayb said: Is time anything but a night and a day, or the rising of the sun and its changing? You will not be able to seek it meaning you will not be able to return the sunken water, nor will you be able to obtain it by any trick. It was said: You will not be able to seek anything else instead of it, and this is where the debate and warning of his brother ended in this hadith.
18:42: The Almighty's saying: And its fruit was encompassed is a noun whose subject is not named, and it is the source. It is possible for the lowered word to be in the nominative case. The meaning of was encompassed by its fruit is that he destroyed all of his wealth. This is the first way in which God Almighty fulfilled His brother's warning. So he began to turn his hands over means that the disbeliever began to strike one hand against the other in regret, because this comes from someone who is regretful. It was said: His kingdom was turned over so that he did not see in it any compensation for what he had spent, and this is because the kingdom may be expressed by the hand, from their saying: And in his hand is wealth, meaning in his kingdom is wealth. His saying So he became indicates that this destruction occurred at night, like His saying: "So a company from your Lord swept over it while they were asleep. So it became like a harvested field" (al-Qalam 68:19-20). It is also said: I spent such and such in this house and I spent on it. And they are empty on their thrones meaning empty, some of them have fallen on others. It is taken from the verb khawat an-nujum which means they are empty and it means they have fallen. This is from the saying of God the Almighty: Then those are their houses, empty because of what they did (al-Naml 27:52). It is also said fallen, just as it is said she is empty on her thrones meaning she has fallen on her roofs. So he combined the destruction of the fruit and the root for him, and this is one of the greatest blessings of God upon me, and I knew that it was by the power of God and I did not deny Him. This is regret from him when regret is of no use to him.
18:43: The Almighty said: And he had no company to aid him other than God a company is the subject of be and for him is the predicate to aid him in the place of the description, meaning a supporting company. It is possible that to aid him is the predicate. The first view according to Sibawayh is more appropriate because for him has been mentioned before, and Abu al-Abbas disagrees with him, and argues with the words of God the Almighty: And he had no equal to Him (al-Ikhla 112:4). Sibawayh permitted the other. And to aid him is in the meaning of a company, because its meaning is people, and if it was in the wording, he would have said and he had no company to aid him, meaning a group and a community to whom he could resort. And he was not victorious meaning immune, as Qatada said. It was said: reclaiming what he had lost. The derivation of the word group was mentioned earlier in Al Imran, and the ha replaces the ya that was missing from the middle of it. Its root is fay’ like fi’ because it is from fa’, and its plural is fa’un and fa’a’at, like shayat and waladat and muda’at. That is, he did not have a clan to protect him from the punishment of God, and those servants and children he boasted about went astray from him.
18:44: The Almighty said: There is the guardianship of God, the Truth. There is a difference of opinion regarding the factor in His statement there, which is an adverb. It was said: The factor in it is and he had no group nor was there, meaning he did not help nor was he victorious there, meaning because of the torment that befell him. It was said: The discussion was completed when He said victorious. The factor in His statement there: the guardianship, and its estimation on the advancement and delay: the guardianship of God, the Truth, there, meaning on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Amr and Al-Kisa'i read the Truth in the nominative case as an attribute of the guardianship. The people of Medina and Hamza read the Truth in the genitive case as an attribute of God Almighty, and the estimation: to God, the Possessor of the Truth. Al-Zajjaj said: the Truth is permissible in the accusative case as a source and emphasis, as you say: this is yours truly. Al-A'mash, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read the guardianship with a kasra on the waw, the rest with a fatha on it, and they have the same meaning like breastfeeding and breastfeeding. It was said: Wilayat with the fatha comes from mawala, like His saying: God is the ally of those who believe (al-Baqarah 2:257). That is because God is the ally of those who believe (Muhammad 47:11). With the kasra it means authority, power and leadership, like His saying: And the command on that Day is God’s (al-Infitar 82:19) meaning His is the dominion and judgment on that Day, meaning His command will not be referred to anyone, and the dominion at all times belongs to God, but claims and delusions will be removed on the Day of Resurrection. Abu Ubaid said: It is with the fatha of the waw for the Creator, and with the kasra for the created. He is the best in reward meaning God is the best in reward in this world and the hereafter for whoever believes in Him, and there is nothing else to be hoped for from Him, but He meant in the opinion of the ignorant, meaning He is the best of those who are hoped for. And the best of consequences Asim, Al-A’mash, Hamza and Yahya read ‘aqaba with the qaf silent, and the rest with the damma, and they have the same meaning, meaning He is the best of consequences for whoever hopes and believes in Him. It is said: This is the consequence of so-and-so’s matter, its outcome, and its end, meaning its end.
18:45: The Almighty said: And present to them the similitude of the life of this world. That is, describe to these arrogant people who asked you to expel the poor believers the similitude of the life of this world, that is, liken it to it. Like water which We sent down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingled with it that is, with the water, until it became even. It was said: The vegetation mingled with each other when the water descended upon it, because vegetation only mingles and multiplies with rain. This meaning was previously explained in Yunus. The wise men said: The Almighty likened the world to water because water does not settle in one place. Likewise, the world does not remain in one state, and because water does not remain in one state, so does the world. And because water does not remain and disappear, so does the world perish. And because no one is able to enter water or get wet, likewise the world, no one who enters it is safe from its temptation and its affliction. And because if water is in a certain amount, it is beneficial and causes growth, but if it exceeds the amount, it is harmful and destructive. Likewise, the world, enough of it is beneficial and its excess is harmful. In the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “A man said to him: O Messenger of God, I want to be among the successful. He said: Leave the world and take from it like stagnant water, for a little of it is sufficient and a lot of it covers.” In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He has succeeded who has embraced Islam and has been provided with what is sufficient and God has made him content with what He has given him. “So it became” meaning the plant Hasheem meaning broken from dryness and crumbled, meaning because the water had been cut off from it, so this was omitted for the sake of brevity because the speech indicates it. And Hashem is the breaking of a dry thing. And Hasheem is from the broken dry plant, and the decayed tree is taken by the woodcutter as he pleases. From this is their saying: So-and-so is nothing but Hasheem, a generous man, if he is generous. And a Hasheem man means weak in body. And so-and-so was broken on him if he was kind. And what is in the udder of a camel was broken if he milked it. It is said: He smashed the tharid, and from it came the name of Hashim bin Abd Manaf, whose name was Amr, and Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri said about him: Amr Al-Ala broke the tharid for his people, and the men of Mecca were lean and old. The reason for this was that the Quraysh were afflicted with years that took away their wealth, so Hashim went to Ash-Sham and ordered a lot of bread to be baked for him, so he carried it in the camels in the ghara’ir until he reached Mecca, and he smashed that bread, meaning he broke it and mixed it, and slaughtered those camels, then he ordered the cooks to cook it, then it struck them, so he was named Hashim. The winds scatter it means they scatter it, said Abu Ubaidah. Ibn Qutaybah: it blows it away. Ibn Kaysan: it takes it and comes. Ibn Abbas: it turns it, and the meanings are close. Talhah ibn Musarraf read tadhrihi ar-riyyah. Al-Kisa’i said: And in Abdullah’s reading tadhrihi. It is said: the wind dharthuh tadhrihi dharwan and [tadhrihi] dharyan and dhartuhu tadhrihi idhra’ if it flew with it. Al-Farra’ narrated: I turned the man from his horse, meaning I flipped him. Sibawayh and Al-Farra’ recited: I said to him, Aim and do not strain him, lest he slip from the other end of the stone and you slip. God Almighty says: And God is over all things competent of creation, destruction, and revival. Glory be to Him!
18:46: The Almighty said: Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world. Zeinata is permissible, and it is the predicate of the beginning in the dual and singular. Wealth and children are the adornment of the life of this world because in wealth there is beauty and benefit, and in children there is strength and defense, so it became the adornment of the life of this world, but with it there is an indication of the description of wealth and children, because the meaning is: Wealth and children are the adornment of this despised life, so do not pursue them with your souls. It is a response to Uyaynah Yanhasn and his likes when they boasted of wealth and honor, so the Almighty informed that whatever was of the adornment of the life of this world is a delusion that passes and does not remain, like chaff when the wind scatters it. What remains is what was of the provisions of the grave and the provisions of the Hereafter. It was said: Do not tie your heart to wealth because it is a passing spoil, nor to women because today they are with you and tomorrow they are with someone else, nor to the ruler because today they are for you and tomorrow they are for someone else. It is sufficient for this to be said by God Almighty: Your wealth and your children are but a trial (al-Taghabun 64:15) and He Almighty said: Indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them (al-Taghabun
18:47: The Almighty said: And the Day We set the mountains in motion and you see the earth barren. Some grammarians said: The meaning is: And the lasting and righteous deeds are better with your Lord on the Day We set the mountains in motion. An-Nahhas said: This is a mistake because of the waw. It was said: The meaning is: And remember the Day We set the mountains in motion, meaning We bring them down from their places on the face of the earth, and We set them in motion as We set the clouds in motion, as He said in another verse: And they will pass as the clouds pass (al-Naml 27:88), then they will be broken and return to the ground, as He said: And the mountains will be leveled with a single slap, and will become scattered dust (Al-Waqi'ah: 5-6). Ibn Kathir, Al-Hasan, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read and the Day they will pass with a damma on the taa and a fatha on the yaa. The mountains is in the nominative case as a passive verb. Ibn Muhaisin and Mujahid read and the Day the mountains will pass with a fatha on the taa, lightened from sara. The mountains is in the nominative case. Evidence of Abu Amr’s reading And when the mountains are set in motion (al-Takwir 81:3) and evidence of Ibn Muhsin’s reading And the mountains will move with a movement (al-Tur 52:10). Abu Ubaid chose the first reading Nasir with a noon because of his saying And We have gathered them. The meaning of prominent is apparent, and there is nothing covering it from mountains, trees, or buildings, meaning its fruits have been uprooted, its mountains have been uprooted, and its buildings have been demolished, so it is prominent and apparent. The people of interpretation agree with this statement. It was said: And you see its mountains, and its buildings have been demolished, so it is prominent and apparent. The people of interpretation agree with this statement And you see the earth exposed meaning what is in it of treasures and dead people has been exposed, as He said: And it casts out what is in it and becomes empty (al-Inshiqaq 84:4) and He said: And the earth will bring forth its burdens (Az-Zalzalah: 2). This is the statement of Ata’. And We have gathered them means to the place of standing. We did not leave any of them behind meaning we did not leave anyone behind. It is said: I left something meaning I abandoned it. Antara said: I left him covered in dust, and the people were between wounded and wounded. That is, I left it. Leaving means abandoning, and from it comes treachery, because he left loyalty. And the pond of water was called a pond because the water went and was left. And from it comes the woman’s braids because she leaves them behind her. And he says: We have gathered their righteous and their wicked, their jinn and their humans.
18:48: The Almighty said: And they will be presented before your Lord in rows in rows is in the accusative case as a state. Muqatil said: They will be presented row after row like the rows of prayer, every nation and group in rows, not because they are one row and it was said all together, like His saying: Then come in rows (Ta-Ha 20:64) meaning all together and it was said standing. Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Abdul Rahman bin Mandah narrated in the Book of Monotheism on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Indeed, God Almighty will call out on the Day of Resurrection in a loud voice that is not frightening, O My servants, I am God, there is no god but Me, the Most Merciful of the merciful, the Most Just of judges, and the Swiftest of reckoners. O My servants, there is no fear for you today, nor will you grieve. Present your argument and make your answer easy, for you will be questioned and held accountable. O My angels, make My servants stand in rows on the tips of their toes for the reckoning." I said: This hadith is extremely clear in explaining the verse, and many of the commentators did not mention it. We wrote it in the book of At-Tadhkirah, and from it we quoted it, praise be to God. You have come to Us as We created you the first time. That is, it will be said to them: You have come to Us barefoot and naked, with no wealth or children. It was also said: Single, as evidenced by the statement: And you have come to Us alone as We created you the first time. (Al-An`am: 94), which has been mentioned previously. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, We resurrected you as We shaved you. Rather, you claimed is addressed to those who denied resurrection, that is, you claimed in this world that you would not be resurrected and that We would not set an appointment for you for resurrection. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, she said: I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. I said: O Messenger of God! Men and women looking at each other? He said: O Aisha, the matter is more serious than looking at each other. Uncircumcised, meaning uncircumcised.” This has been explained previously in Al-An`am.
18:49: The Almighty’s saying: And the Book was placed is a generic noun, and there are two interpretations of it: One of them is that it is the books of deeds in the hands of the servants, as stated by Muqatil. The second is that it is the accounting, as stated by Al-Kalbi, so he expressed the accounting with the book because they are held accountable for their written deeds. The first statement is more apparent, as stated by Ibn Al-Mubarak, who said: Al-Hakam or Abu Al-Hakam informed us - Na’im was not sure - on the authority of Ismail bin Abd Al-Rahman on the authority of a man from Banu Asad, who said: Umar said to Ka’b: Woe to you, Ka’b! Tell us from the hadith of the Hereafter. He said: Yes, O Commander of the Faithful! When the Preserved Tablet is raised on the Day of Resurrection, no one among the creation will remain except that he will be looking at his deeds. He said: Then the scrolls containing the deeds of the servants will be brought and scattered around the Throne. This is the saying of God the Almighty: “And the Book will be laid open, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, ‘Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great but that it has recorded it?’” Al-Suddi said: The small is what is less than polytheism, and the great is polytheism, but that it has recorded it. Ka’b said: Then the believer will be called and given his book in his right hand, and he will look at it and see his good deeds are apparent to the people, and he will read his bad deeds so that each one will say, I had good deeds, but they were not mentioned. So God wanted to show him all of his deeds until, when he had reduced what was in the book, he would find at the end of it all that he has been forgiven and that he is among the people of Paradise. At that time, he will go to his companions and say, “Here, read my book. Indeed, I thought that I would meet my account.” (al-Haqqah 69:19-20) Then he will be called to disbelief and given his book in his left hand, then it will be wrapped up and placed behind his back and his neck will be twisted. This is the saying of God the Almighty: “And as for he who is given his book Behind his back (al-Inshiqaq 84:10) So he looks into his book and his bad deeds are apparent to the people, and he looks into his good deeds so that he does not say, “Then will I be rewarded for the bad deeds?” When Al-Fudayl bin Iyad recited this verse, he would say, Woe to me! They complain to God Almighty about the minor sins before the major ones. Ibn Abbas said, The minor sin is smiling, and the major sin is laughing, meaning what was done in disobedience to God Almighty, as Al-Tha’labi mentioned. Al-Mawardi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the minor sin is laughing. I said: It is possible that it is a minor sin if it is not in a sin, because laughing at a sin is approval of it and approval of a sin is a sin, and based on this it is a major sin, so the reason for combining this is this and God knows best. Or laughter, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi, is to be understood as smiling, and God the Almighty said: So he smiled, laughing at her statement (al-Naml 27:19). Saeed bin Jubair said: Minor sins are minor sins such as touching and kissing, and major sins are sexual intercourse and adultery. This has already been explained in An-Nisa. Qatada said: The people complained about the counting, but no one complained of injustice, so beware of small sins, for they accumulate on their doer until they destroy him. This has already been explained. The meaning of He counted them is that He counted them and encompassed them, and the counting was added to the book as an extension. And they found what they did present means they found the recompense of what they did present. It was also said: They found the reward for what they did present. And your Lord does not wrong anyone meaning He does not punish anyone for someone else’s crime. Nor does He punish him for something he did not know about. This was said by Ad-Dahhak. It was also said: He does not reduce the reward of the obedient, nor does He increase the punishment of the disobedient.
18:50: The Almighty said: "And when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was one of the jinn, and he disobeyed the command of his Lord." This was presented in full in Al-Baqarah. Abu Ja`far Al-Nahhas said: In this verse there is a question. It is said: What is the meaning of disobeyed the command of his Lord? There are two opinions on this: One of them - and it is the school of thought of Al-Khalil and Sibawayh - is that the meaning is that disobedience came to him as he was commanded, so he disobeyed, so the reason for the disobedience was the command of his Lord, as you say: I fed him when he was hungry. The other opinion - and it is the school of thought of Muhammad bin Qatrib - is that the meaning is: He disobeyed and refused the command of his Lord. Will you then take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me? The Almighty stopped the disbelievers in a rebuke by saying: Will you then take him, O children of Adam, and his descendants as allies while they are your enemies? That is, enemies, so it is a generic name. Evil is the substitute for the wrongdoers. That is, evil is the worship of Satan as a substitute for the worship of God. Or, what a miserable substitute for God! And there is disagreement as to whether Iblis has offspring from his loins. Al-Sha’bi said: A man asked me and said, Does Iblis have a wife? I said, That is a wedding that I did not witness. Then I remembered His statement, Will you then take him and his offspring as allies? I knew that there can be no offspring except from a wife, so I said, Yes. And Mujahid said, Iblis inserted his vagina into his own vagina and laid five eggs, and this is the origin of his offspring. And it was said, “God created for him a penis in his right thigh and a vagina in his left, so he has intercourse with this one and every day ten eggs emerge, and from each egg seventy male and female devils emerge, so he flies while he is flying, and the one with the greatest status in the eyes of his father is the one who is the greatest temptation among the children of Adam.” And some people said, He has no children or offspring, and his offspring are his helpers from the devils. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: The summary is that God Almighty informed us that Satan has followers and offspring, and that they whisper to the children of Adam, who are their enemies. We do not have a proven method for how they reproduce and for the offspring to arise from Satan, so the matter is settled on a correct transmission. I said: What is proven in this chapter from the authentic hadith is what Al-Hamidi mentioned in Al-Jami’ Bayn Al-Sahihayn on the authority of Imam Abu Bakr Al-Barqani that he included in his book with a chain of transmission on the authority of Abu Muhammad Abdul-Ghanbi bin Saeed Al-Hafiz /N Rawabah Asim on the authority of Abu Uthman on the authority of Salman who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Do not be the first to enter the market nor the last to leave it, for in it Satan laid eggs and hatched them. This indicates that Satan has offspring from his loins, and God knows best. Ibn Atiyyah said: His saying his offspring the apparent meaning of the wording indicates the whisperers from the devils who do evil and carry on falsehood. Al-Tabari and others mentioned that Mujahid said: The offspring of Iblis are the devils, and he considered them to be Zalanbro, the owner of the markets, who places his banner in every market between heaven and earth, placing that banner on a shop or on whoever opens it and the last to close it. Thabar, the one who brings calamities, who orders that faces be beaten and pockets be torn, and prayers for woe and war. And the one-eyed one who is the owner of the doors of fornication. And the one who brings report, he brings it and throws it in people's mouths, so they do not renew its origin. And the one who, if a man enters his house and does not greet or mention the name of God, his sight is of the goods that he does not raise or place properly, and if he eats and does not mention the name of God, he eats with him. Al-A'mash said: And I sometimes enter the house and do not mention God or greet, and I see a latrine and I say: Raise this! And I argue with them, then I remember and say: Dasim Dasim, I seek refuge in God from him. Al-Tha'labi and others added on the authority of Mujahid: And the white, which is the one who whispers to the prophets. And Sakhr, which is the one who stole the ring of Solomon, peace be upon him. And Al-Walhan, which is the one who purifies himself and whispers in it, and Al-Aqees, which is the one who prays and whispers in it. And Marra, which is the one who sings the psalms, and he is nicknamed by it. And Al-Haffaf is in the deserts, misleading people and causing them to wander. And from them is Al-Ghailan. Abu Mut'i' Makhul bin Al-Fadl Al-Nasafi narrated in the book Al-Lu'lu'iyyat on the authority of Mujahid that Al-Haffaf is the one who drinks, and Al-Qaws is the one who plants trees, and Al-A'war is the one who attends the doors of the sultan. Ad-Darani said: Iblis has a devil called Al-Mutaqadi, who sues the son of Adam and tells about a deed he did in secret twenty years ago, so he tells about it in public. Ibn Atiyyah said: This and similar things are not supported by a sound chain of transmission. The discussion on this meaning has been long and has brought up stories that are far from the truth. I have not come across anything authentic about this except what was in the book of Muslim: That there is a devil for prayer called Khanzab. And At-Tirmidhi mentioned: That there is a devil for ablution called Al-Walhan. I said: As for what was mentioned about the specification in the name, it is correct. As for him having followers, helpers and soldiers, it is definitive. We have mentioned the authentic hadith that he has children from his loins, as Mujahid and others said. And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud, he said: The devil appears in the form of a man and comes to people and tells them a lie, so they disperse and one of them says, I heard a man whose face I know but whose name I do not know talking. In Musnad Al-Bazzar, on the authority of Salman Al-Farsi, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not, if you can, be the first to enter the market place or the last to leave it, for it is the battlefield of Satan and in it he sets up his banner. In Musnad Ahmad bin Hanbal, he said: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak informed us, he said: Sufyan informed us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Sulami, on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, he said: When Satan wakes up, he sends out his soldiers and says: Whoever misguides a Muslim, I will crown him. He says: Someone will say to him: I did not stop with so-and-so until he divorced his wife. He says: He is about to get married. And another will say: I did not stop with so-and-so until he was sterile. He says: He is about to be righteous. He said: The speaker says: I did not stop with so-and-so until he drank. He said: You. He said: And he says: I did not stop with so-and-so until he committed adultery. He said: You. He said: I did not stop with so-and-so until he was killed. He said: You! In Sahih Muslim on the authority of Jabir, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Satan places his throne on the water, then he sends out his troops, and the one closest to him in status is the one who causes the greatest temptation. One of them comes and says: I did such-and-such. They say: You did nothing. He said: Then one of them comes and they say: You did not leave him until you separated him from his family. He brings him close or he said: He weighs him down and he says: Yes, you.” It has been mentioned previously. I heard our Sheikh, the Imam Abu Muhammad ibn al-Mu’ti, in the port of Alexandria say: A devil called al-Baydawi appears to the poor who are fasting continuously. When hunger overcomes them and harms their brains, he reveals to them a light and radiance until it fills the houses. They think that they have reached the point of fasting, but that is from God, and it is not as they thought.
18:51: The Almighty said: I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves. It was said: The pronoun refers to Iblis and his offspring, meaning I did not consult them in the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, rather I created them as I wanted. It was also said: I did not make Iblis and his offspring witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, meaning the souls of the polytheists, so how could they take them as allies instead of Me? It was also said: The metaphor in His statement: I did not make them witness refers to the polytheists, and to people in general, so the verse includes a response to groups of astrologers, people of nature, and those who are arbitrary among doctors and others who engage in these things. Ibn Atiyyah said: I heard my father, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the jurist Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Muadh al-Mahdi in Mahdia say: I heard Abdul Haqq al-Siqilli say this statement, and he interpreted this interpretation of this verse, and that it is a response to these groups, and some of the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence mentioned this. Ibn Atiyyah said: I say: The intended target of the verse is Iblis and his offspring, and in this way the refutation is directed to the aforementioned groups, and to the soothsayers, the Arabs, and those who glorify the jinn, when they say: I seek refuge in the Mighty One of this valley, since all of these groups are attached to Iblis and his offspring and they led everyone astray, so they are the first intended by those who lead astray, and these groups fall under their meaning. Al-Tha’labi said: Some of the people of knowledge said I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth in response to the astrologers who said: The spheres occur in the earth and in some of them in others, and his saying: and the earth is in response to the people of geometry when they said: The earth is spherical and the spheres move beneath it, and people are attached to it and beneath it, and his saying: nor did He create themselves is in response to the naturalists when they claimed that natures are the agents of souls. Abu Ja’far read I did not make them witness with a noon and an alif for emphasis. The rest read with a ta’ as evidenced by his saying: and I did not take meaning I did not seek their help in creating the heavens and the earth nor did I consult them. And you would not have taken the misguiders meaning the devils. It was also said: the infidels. As a support meaning helpers. It is said: I sought help from someone if I sought his help and became strong. The original meaning of it is the arm of the hand, then it is used in place of the support, because the hand is based on the arm. It is said: he aided him and aided him on such-and-such if he helped him and supported him. From this is His statement: We will strengthen your arm with your brother meaning we will aid you with your brother. The word arm is used as a metaphor, and God Almighty does not need anyone's help. He specifically mentioned the misguiders to increase blame and rebuke. Abu Ja`far al-Jahdari read and you were not with the opening of the ta', meaning and you were not, O Muhammad, taking the misguiders as a support. There are eight ways to describe arm: arm with the opening of the 'ayn and the closing of the dad, which is the reading of the majority, and it is the most eloquent. Ardhan with the opening of the 'ayn and the closing of the dad, which is the language of Banu Tamim. Ardhan with the closing of the 'ayn and the dad, which is the reading of Abu Amr and al-Hasan. Udhdan with a damma on the 'ayn and a sukoon on the dad, which is the reading of Ikrimah. Udhdan with a kasra on the 'ayn and a fatha on the dad, which is the reading of Ad-Dahhak. Udhdan with a fatha on the 'ayn and the dad, which is the reading of Isa bin Omar. Harun Al-Qari narrated Udhdan and the eighth language is Udhdan according to the language of those who said: shoulder and thigh.
18:52: God the Almighty said: And the Day He will say, 'Call upon My associates whom you claimed.' That is, remember the Day God will say: Where are My associates? That is, call upon those whom you associated with Me, so that they may protect you from My punishment. He only says that to idol worshippers. Hamzah, Yahya, and Isa bin Umar read We say with a noon. The rest read it with a yaa', because He said: My associates, and He did not say: Our associates. So call upon them, that is, they did that. But they did not respond to them, that is, they did not respond to their support, and they did not hold anything back from them. And We placed between them a barrier. Anas bin Malik said: It is a valley in Hell of pus and blood. Ibn Abbas said: That is, We placed a barrier between the believers and the disbelievers. It was said: Between the idols and their worshippers, similar to His statement: So We removed between them. Ibn al-A'rabi said: Everything that is a barrier between two things is a barrier. Ibn Wahb narrated on the authority of Mujahid regarding the words of God the Almighty: Mowbaqan he said: A valley in Hell called Mowbaq. Nawf Al-Bakali said the same except that he said: It separates between them and the believers. Ikrimah: It is a river in Hell that flows with fire, on its banks are snakes like black mules, so when they attack them to seize them, they cry out for help from them by rushing into the fire. Zaid bin Dirham narrated on the authority of Anas bin Malik who said: Mowbaqan is a valley of pus and blood in Hell. Ata and Ad-Dahhak said: Destruction in Hell, and from this it is said: His sins caused him to perish. Abu Ubaidah said: An appointed place for destruction. Al-Jawhari: Wabaq yabq and Bawqan halaka, and Mowbaq is like the appointed, a verbal noun from wa’ada ya’ud, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: And We made between them a place of destruction. There is another language for it: Wabaq yubq and Baqan. There is a third language for it: Wabaq yabq with a kasra in both of them, and awbaqa means He destroyed him. Zuhair said: Whoever buys praise with his money will be afraid of every ugly and deadly sin. Al-Farra’ said: He made their communication in this world a destruction for them in the hereafter.
18:53: The Almighty said: And the criminals will see the Fire. The root of saw is ra'a. The ya was changed to an alif because of its openness and the openness of what preceded it. For this reason, the Kufians claimed that saw is written with a ya, and some Basrans agreed with them in this statement. As for the clever Basrans, among them Muhammad ibn Yazid, they write it with an alif. Al-Nahhas said: I heard Ali bin Sulayman say: I heard Muhammad bin Yazid say: It is not permissible to write madā and ramā and all those with a ya’ except with an alif, and there is no difference between those with a ya’ and those with a waw in writing, just as there is no difference between them in pronunciation. If it were necessary to write those with a ya’ with a ya’, then it would be necessary to write those with a waw with a waw. Despite this, they contradict themselves and write ramā with a ya’ and ramāhu with an alif. If the reason is that they are with a ya’, then it is necessary to write ramāhu with a ya’, then they write dhān, the plural of dhūwah, and kasā, the plural of kiswah, and they are with a ya’, and this is something that does not happen and is not proven on the basis of the origin. They thought that they would fall into it. “They thought” here means certainty and knowledge, as He said: I told them they thought I had two thousand armed men. That is, they were certain, and this has been mentioned before. Ibn Abbas said: They were certain that they would attack it. It was also said: They saw it from a far away place, so they thought that they would attack it, and they thought that it would take them immediately. In the hadith: The disbeliever sees Hell and thinks that it will befall him from a distance of forty years’ travel. “Watching” means being closely involved in something. It was narrated on the authority of Alqamah that he read, So they thought that they would be meeting it, meaning that they would gather in it, and lafaf is the plural. And they found no escape from it, meaning an escape because it surrounds them on all sides. Al-Qutbi said: A place to which they can turn. It was also said: A refuge to which they can resort, and the meaning is the same. It was also said: The idols did not find a way out of the fire for the polytheists.
18:54: The Almighty's saying: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an from every [kind of] example. This has two possible meanings: One: What He mentioned to them of lessons and past generations. The second: What He explained to them of the evidence of divinity, which was mentioned previously in Glory be to Him. So in the first meaning, it is a warning, and in the second, it is an explanation. And man is most disputatious of anything. That is, disputatious and argumentative, and what is meant by it is Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith and his argumentation in the Qur'an. It was said that the verse is about Abi ibn Khalaf. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, the disbeliever is most disputatious of anything, and the evidence that he meant the disbeliever is his saying: And those who disbelieve argue with falsehood. Anas narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection from among the unbelievers, and God will say to him: What did you do with what I sent you? He will say: O Lord, I believed in You and confirmed Your messengers and acted according to Your Book. God will say to him: This is Your record, and there is nothing of that in it. He will say: O Lord, I do not accept what is in this record. It will be said to him: These guardian angels are bearing witness against you. He will say: I do not accept them, O Lord, and how can I accept them when they are not from Me or from me? God the Most High will say: Is this the Preserved Tablet or the Book that has testified to that? He will say: O Lord, did You not save me from injustice? He will say: Yes. He will say: O Lord, I will not accept except a witness against me from myself. God the Most High will say: Now shall We send against you a witness from yourself? He will ponder who from himself will bear witness against him. Then his mouth will be sealed, then his limbs will speak of polytheism, then he will be left alone to speak and he will enter the Fire, and some of him will curse others, saying to his limbs: May God curse you, for it was from you that I used to struggle. His limbs will say: May God curse you. Do you know that God the Most High conceals a statement? That is what God the Most High said: “And man is most disputatious of anything.” “ It was narrated by Muslim with the same meaning from the hadith of Anas as well. And in Sahih Muslim, “ On the authority of Ali, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to him and Fatima and said: Do you not pray? I said: O Messenger of God, our souls are in God’s hand, so if He wills to resurrect us, He will resurrect us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away when I said that to him, and then I heard him as he was turning away, striking his thigh and saying: “Man is most argumentative of anything.”
18:55: The Almighty said: And what prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them meaning the Qur'an, Islam, and Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. And to ask forgiveness of their Lord except that the precedent of the former peoples should come to them meaning Our precedent in destroying them, meaning what prevented them from believing was My judgment upon them in that, and if I had judged them to believe they would have believed. The precedent of the former peoples is the custom of the former peoples in the torment of extermination. It was said: The meaning is: And what prevented the people from believing was their request that the precedent of the former peoples should come to them, so it was deleted. The precedent of the former peoples is to witness the torment, so the polytheists requested that and said: O God, if this is the truth from You the verse. Or the torment should come to them before is an accusative in the state, and its meaning is clearly, as Ibn Abbas said. Al-Kalbi said: It is the sword on the day of Badr. Muqatil said: Suddenly. Abu Ja`far, `Asim, Al-A`mash, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read qablan with two dhammahs, meaning all types of torment, the plural of qabil like sabil and subul. An-Nahhas: Al-Farra’s school of thought is that qablan is the plural of qabil, meaning scattered, one after the other. He also believes that the meaning could be apparent. Al-A’raj said: His reading of qablan meant all of them. Abu Amr said: His reading of qablan was qablan, and its meaning was apparent.
18:56: The Almighty said: And We do not send the messengers except as bearers of good tidings meaning of Paradise for those who believe. And as warners meaning frightening those who disbelieve with punishment. This has been mentioned before. And those who disbelieve argue with falsehood to refute thereby the truth It was said: It was revealed about those who divided, they were arguing about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: A magician, a madman, a poet, and a soothsayer, as mentioned before. The meaning of refute is to remove and invalidate. The root of dahdh is slipping. It is said: his foot dahdh, meaning it slipped, tahdhdh, and the sun dahdh from the middle of the sky, and his argument dahdhdh, meaning it became invalid, and God refuted it. Refutation is slipping. In describing the path: “And the bridge will be struck over Hell, and intercession will be made, and they will say, ‘O God, save, save.’ It was said, ‘O Messenger of God, what is the bridge?’ He said, ‘A slippery slope,’ meaning that the foot will slip on it.” Tarafa said: Abu Munther, you sought loyalty, but you gave it up and you were stubborn as a camel strays from the right path. And they took My verses meaning the Qur'an and that with which they were warned of the threat in jest. What means the source, meaning the warning. It was said: it means which, meaning they took the Qur'an and that with which they were warned of the threat in jest, meaning play and falsehood. This was explained in (Al-Baqarah) previously. It was said: it is what Abu Jahl said about the butter and dates, this is Zaqqum. It was said: it is their saying about the Qur'an, it is magic, confused dreams and legends of the ancients, and they said to the Messenger: Is this not a human being like you? "And they said, 'Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man from the two cities?' and What did God intend by this as an example?"
18:57: The Almighty says: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord and then turns away from them? That is, no one is more unjust to himself than he who is admonished by the verses of his Lord, but then takes them lightly and turns away from accepting them. And forgets what his hands have put forth That is, he abandons his disbelief and sins and does not repent from them. Forgetting here means abandonment. It was said that the meaning is he forgot what he had put forth for himself and received the punishment, and the meanings are close. Indeed, We have placed coverings over their hearts, lest they understand it, and in their ears, deafness because of their disbelief, that is, We prevented faith from entering their hearts and ears. And if you call them to guidance meaning to faith they will never be guided. It was revealed about a specific people, and it responds to the Qadarites’ statement. The meaning of this verse has already been mentioned in Glory be to God and others.
18:58: The Almighty says: And your Lord is the Forgiving, the Possessor of Mercy meaning for sins. This is specific to the people of faith and not the disbelievers, as evidenced by His statement: Indeed, God does not forgive association with Him. "Possessor of Mercy" has four interpretations: One is the Possessor of pardon. The second is the Possessor of reward, and in these two ways it is specific to the people of faith and not the disbelievers. The third is the Possessor of favor. The fourth is the Possessor of guidance, and in these two ways it includes the people of faith and the disbelievers, because He bestows favors in this world upon the disbeliever as He bestows favors upon the believer. He has made His guidance clear to the disbeliever as He has made it clear to the believer, even though the believer is guided by it and not the disbeliever. The meaning of His statement: "If He were to punish them for what they have earned meaning of disbelief and sins, He would have hastened the punishment for them" but He gives respite. "Rather, for them is an appointed time" meaning a predetermined term to which they are delayed. Similar to "For every report is a fixed time, For every term is a book" meaning when it comes, it will not be delayed for them, either in this world or in the Hereafter. They will not find besides Him a refuge, meaning a shelter. This was said by Ibn Abbas and Ibn Zayd, and Al-Jawhari narrated it in As-Sahah. The verb wa’ala, yai’il, wa’ulan, wa’ulan, on the basis of fa’ul, meaning he took refuge. The verb wa’ala is derived from the root fa’il, meaning he sought salvation. Mujahid said: Muharizan. Qatadah: Waliyan. Abu Ubaidah: Munjaan. It was also said: Muhaysan, but the meaning is the same. The Arabs say: La wa’alat nafshu meaning la walat nafshu he did not escape, and from this is the saying of the poet: No, you left it to the Amiris and did not speak Al-A'sha said: I may make the master of the house forget me, and he may be wary of me, but he will not be able to do so. Anything that survives.
18:59: The Almighty said: And those towns We destroyed. "Those" is in the nominative case as a subject. "The towns" is an adjective or a substitute. "Destroyed them" is in the predicate case and is based on the meaning, because the meaning is the people of the towns. It is permissible for "those" to be in the accusative case according to the opinion of those who said: Zaid I struck him, meaning and those towns whose story We told you about, such as the towns of Aad, Thamud, Madyan and the people of Lot, We destroyed them when they were unjust and disbelieved. "And We appointed for their destruction an appointed time" meaning a known time that you did not count. "Destroy is from destruction. Asim read destruction with a fatha on the meem and lam, and it is the source of destruction. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' permitted for their destruction" with a kasra on the lam and a fatha on the meem. An-Nahhas: Al-Kisa'i said: It is more beloved to me because it is from "destruction." Az-Zajjaj: a name for time and the estimate: for the time of their destruction, as it is said: the she-camel came to her resting place.
18:60: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And when Moses said to his boy, ‘I will not depart.’ The majority of scholars and historians are Moses bin Imran mentioned in the Qur’an, there is no other Moses in it. A group including Nawf al-Bakali said: He is not the son of Imran, but rather he is Moses bin Mansha bin Joseph bin Jacob, and he was a prophet before Moses bin Imran. This statement was indicated by Ibn Abbas in Sahih al-Bukhari and others. His boy: He is Joshua bin Nun. He was mentioned previously in (Al-Ma’idah) and the last of (Joseph). Whoever said he is the son of Mansha, then the boy is not Joshua bin Nun. I will not depart means I will not stop walking. The poet said: And may God keep my people, with the praise of God, adorned and glorious It was said, I will not leave you I will not leave you. Until I reach the meeting place of the two seas meaning their confluence. Qatada said: It is the Persian and Roman seas. Mujahid said the same. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is an arm extending from the Atlantic Ocean from north to south in the land of Persia from behind Azerbaijan. The corner where the two seas meet, which is next to the land of Syria, is the meeting place of the two seas according to this statement. It was said: They are the Jordan Sea and the Red Sea. It was said: The meeting place of the two seas is near Tangier, Muhammad ibn Ka'b said. It was narrated on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b that it is in Africa. Al-Suddi said: Al-Kar and Al-Ras are in Armenia. Some scholars said: It is the Andalusian sea from the Atlantic Ocean, narrated by Al-Naqqash, and this is something that is often mentioned. A group said: They are Moses and Al-Khidr, and this is a weak statement. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, but it is not authentic, because the matter is clear from the hadiths that he was only named a sea of water. The reason for this story is what was narrated by the two Sahihs on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Moses, peace be upon him, stood up as a preacher among the Children of Israel and was asked who was the most knowledgeable of people. He said: I am. So God rebuked him because he did not refer the knowledge to Him. So God revealed to him: I have a servant at the confluence of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you. Moses said: O Lord, how can I deal with him? He said: Take a fish with you and put it in a basket. Wherever you lose the fish, it is there. And he mentioned the hadith, and the wording is from Al-Bukhari. Ibn Abbas said: When Moses and his people appeared in the land of Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When they settled in the house, God ordered him to remind them of the days of God. So he preached to his people and reminded them of the goodness and blessings that God had given them when He saved them from the people of Pharaoh, destroyed their enemy, and made them successors on earth. Then he said: And God spoke to your Prophet directly, and chose him for Himself, and bestowed upon me love from Him, and gave you everything you asked of Him, and made you the best of the people of the earth, and provided you with honor after humiliation, and wealth after poverty, and the Torah after you were ignorant. So a man from the Children of Israel said to him: We know what you are saying, so is there a way? Is there anyone on earth who is more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of God? He said: No. So God rebuked him when he did not refer the knowledge to Him, so God sent Gabriel: O Moses, how do you know where I put my knowledge? Yes! I have a servant at the confluence of the two seas who is more knowledgeable than you, and he mentioned the hadith. Our scholars said: His statement in the hadith is more knowledgeable than you means with the rulings of detailed events and the rulings of specific incidents, not absolutely, as evidenced by the statement of Al-Khidr to Moses: You have knowledge that God has taught you that I do not know, and I have knowledge that He has taught me that you do not know. Based on this, it is true that each of them is more knowledgeable than the other in relation to what each of them knows and the other does not know. When Moses heard this, his noble soul and high ambition yearned to acquire knowledge of what he did not know, and to meet the one about whom it was said: He is more knowledgeable than you, so he resolved and asked the question of the humble about how to proceed, so he was ordered to depart in any case. He was told to carry a salted whale with him in a basket - which is a basket - for wherever it lives and you miss it, there is the way. So he set off with his young man when he came to him, striving to seek, saying: I will not leave until I reach the meeting place of the two seas. "Or I will spend ages" with a damma on the ha and the qaf, which is time. The plural is ahqab. The qaf may be sukun, so it is said: haqab. It is eighty years, and it is said: more than that. The plural is huqab. A huqab with a kasra on the ha is the singular of huqab, which is years. Second: In this is the jurisprudence of the scholar’s journey in search of an increase in knowledge, and seeking assistance in that from a servant and a companion, and seizing the opportunity to meet the virtuous and the scholars even if their countries are far away, and that was the habit of the righteous predecessors, and because of that the travelers reached the prevailing fortune, and obtained the striving and success, so their feet were firmly planted in the sciences, and they were granted the best types of remembrance, reward, and virtue. Al-Bukhari said: Jabir bin Abdullah traveled a month’s journey to Abdullah bin Anis in a hadith. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And when Moses said to his servant, scholars have three opinions about it: One of them: That he was with him serving him, and a young man in the speech of the Arabs is a young man, and since servants are mostly young men, the servant is called a young man out of good manners, and the Shari’ah encouraged this in the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Let none of you say, ‘My slave’ or ‘My maidservant’, but say, ‘My boy’ or ‘My girl’. This is an exhortation to humility, and this was mentioned previously in Yusuf. The boy in the verse is the servant, and he is Joshua bin Nun bin Ephraim bin Joseph, peace be upon him. It is said that he is the nephew of Moses, peace be upon him. It is said that he was called Moses’ boy because he stuck to him to learn from him, even though he was free. This is the meaning of the first verse. It is said that he was called a boy because he took the place of a boy, and he is a slave. God the Almighty said, “And he said to his young men, ‘Put their merchandise in their saddlebags. ’” And He said, She seeks to seduce her young man. Ibn al-Arabi said, “The apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates that he was a slave. In the hadith, it says that he was Joshua bin Nun. In the Tafsir, it says that he was his nephew. All of this is not certain, and it is safer to hesitate about it.” Fourth: The Almighty said: Or I pass ages. Abdullah bin Omar said: A period is eighty years. Mujahid: seventy autumns. Qatada: time. An-Nahhas: What the linguists know is that a period and a period are an indefinite, unlimited period of time, just as a group or a people are indefinite, unlimited, and its plural is periods.
18:61: The Almighty's saying: But when they reached the place where they met, they forgot their fish, and it took its course into the sea, running. The pronoun in His saying: between them refers to the two seas, as Mujahid said. A running path is a path, as Mujahid said. Qatada said that the water froze and became like a running path. The majority of commentators say that the fish remained empty in its path, and that Moses walked on it following the fish until the path led him to an island in the sea, where he found Al-Khidr. The apparent meaning of the narrations and the Book is that he found Al-Khidr on the shore of the sea. His saying: they forgot their fish was only the young man's forgetfulness, so it was said that the meaning is that he forgot to tell Moses what he saw of his condition, so he attributed the forgetfulness to them because of their companionship, like His Almighty's saying: From them emerge pearls and coral but it only comes out of the salt, and His saying: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you? The messengers are from mankind, not from the jinn. And in Bukhari, he said to his boy: I will not charge you except that you inform me so that the fish may leave you, he said: I have not charged you much, so that is what the Almighty said: And when Moses said to his boy Joshua bin Nun - not from Saeed - he said: While he was in the shade of a rock in a rich place, the fish struck and Moses was asleep, so his boy said: I will not wake him, until when he woke up he forgot to inform him, and the fish struck until he entered the sea, so God held back the flow of the sea from him until it was as if his mark was on a stone, Amr said to me: This is how it is as if his mark was on a stone and he shaved between his thumbs and the two thumbs next to them. And in another narration: And God held back the flow of the water from the fish so that it became like an arch, so when he woke up his companion forgot to inform him about the fish, so they went for the rest of their day and night,
18:62: Until the next day, Moses said to his servant, "Bring us our breakfast. We have certainly suffered much fatigue in this journey of ours." Moses did not find any fatigue until he passed the place that God had commanded, so his servant said to him, "Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish. None made me forget to mention it except Satan." It was said that the forgetfulness was from them, because God Almighty said, I forgot. So the forgetfulness was attributed to them, because the beginning of carrying the fish was from Moses because he was the one who ordered it, so when they went, his servant was the one carrying it until they took refuge at the rock and dismounted. So when they passed means the fish there forgotten - that is, abandoned - so when Moses asked for breakfast, the servant attributed the forgetfulness to himself when addressing him, and God only mentioned their forgetfulness when they reached the junction of the two seas, which is the rock, so Moses was a partner in forgetting, because forgetfulness is delay, from that is their saying in supplication: May God prolong your life. When they left the rock, they delayed their whale from carrying it, and neither of them carried it. So it is permissible to attribute it to them because they left and abandoned the whale. The Almighty’s saying: Bring us our food contains one issue, which is taking provisions for travel. It is a response to the ignorant and foolish Sufis who storm the wilderness and deserts, claiming that this is reliance on the One, Almighty God. This is Moses, the Prophet of God and the one who spoke to Him from the people of the earth, who took provisions despite his knowledge of his Lord and his reliance on the Lord of the servants. And in Sahih al-Bukhari: Some people from Yemen used to perform Hajj without taking provisions, and they would say: We are the trusting ones. When they arrived, they would ask people. So God revealed: And take provisions. This has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. There is a difference of opinion as to what Moses’ provisions were. Ibn Abbas said: It was a salted fish in a basket, and they would eat from it for lunch and dinner. When they reached the rock on the shore of the Harrah, his young man put down the basket, and the fish found the current of the sea, so the fish moved in the basket, so the basket turned over and the fish escaped. The young man forgot to tell Moses the story of the fish. It was said: The fish was a guide to the location of Al-Khidr, based on his saying in the hadith: Take a fish with you in a basket, and wherever you lose the fish, it is there. Based on this, they would have taken provisions other than the fish, and this was mentioned by our Sheikh, Imam Abu Al-Abbas, and he chose it. Ibn Atiyah said: My father, may God be pleased with him, said: I heard Abu al-Fadl al-Jawhari say in his sermon: Moses walked to the place of communion and remained forty days without needing food. When he walked to Bashir, hunger overtook him for part of a day. His saying: tired means tired, and tiredness is fatigue and hardship. It was said: He meant hunger here, and in this is evidence of the permissibility of reporting what a person feels of pain and illness, and that this does not detract from contentment, nor from submission to fate, but only if it does not come from annoyance or discontent.
18:63: And in his saying: And nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan, that with the verb is interpreted as a source, and it is accusative as a substitute for inclusion from the pronoun in mansahih, and it is a substitute for the apparent from the implied, meaning, and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan. And in the Mushaf of Abdullah: And nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan. And this was only mentioned by Joshua in the context of apologizing for what Moses said: I will not charge you except that you inform me so that the fish will leave you, so he said: I have not been charged much, so he apologized with that statement. The Almighty’s saying: And it took its way in the sea as a wonder may be from what Joshua said to Moses, meaning the whale took its way as a wonder for the people. It may be that his saying: And it took its way in the sea is the end of the report, then he resumed the wonder and said to himself: Amazing about this matter. The place of wonder is that a whale died and its left side was eaten and then it came back to life after that. Abu Shuja’ said in the book of Al-Tabari: I saw it - I brought it - and behold, it was a half of a whale with one eye, and another half in which there was nothing. Ibn Atiyyah said: And I saw it and the half in which there was nothing had a thin shell with no thorns under it. It may be that his saying: And it took its way is a report from God the Almighty, and that is in two ways: Either it is informing about Moses that he took the whale’s way in the sea as a wonder, meaning he was amazed by it, or it is informing about the whale that it took its way as a wonder for the people. Among the strange stories narrated in Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse is that the whale came to life because it was touched by water from a spring there called the Spring of Life. It has never touched anything without it coming to life. In the interpretation: The sign was that the whale came to life. It was said: When Moses descended after his exhaustion on the journey, on a rock next to which was the water of life, some of that water touched the whale and it came to life. Al-Tirmidhi said in his hadith: Sufyan said: Some people claim that there is a spring of life near that rock, and nothing touches its water without it coming to life. He said: The whale had eaten from it, and when the water dripped on it, it came to life. The author of the Book of the Bride mentioned that Moses, peace be upon him, performed ablution from the Spring of Life, and a drop dripped from his beard onto the whale and it came to life. And God knows best.
18:64: God the Almighty said: That is what we were seeking. That is, Moses said to his servant, "The matter of the fish and its loss is what we were seeking. The man we came for is then." So they returned, tracing their tracks so that they would not lose their way. In Bukhari: They found Khidr on a green rug in the middle of the sea, covered with his garment, one end under his feet and the other under his head. Moses greeted him, so he uncovered his face and said: Is there peace in your land?! Who are you? He said: I am Moses. He said: Moses of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes. He said: What is your business? He said: You have come to teach me from what you have been taught of right guidance. The hadith. Al-Tha'labi said in the Book of Brides: Moses and his servant found Al-Khidr sleeping on a green rug in the water, wrapped in a green garment. Moses greeted him, so he uncovered his face and said: How can there be peace in our land?! Then he raised his head and sat up straight and said: And upon you be peace, O Prophet of the Children of Israel. Moses said to him: How do you know me? Who told you that I am the Prophet of the Children of Israel? He said: The one who told you about me and directed you to me. Then he said: O Moses, you have been busy with the Children of Israel. Moses said: My Lord sent me to you to follow you and learn from your knowledge. Then they sat talking, and a swallow came and carried water in its beak, and the story is mentioned as follows.
18:65: The Almighty said: "And they found one of Our servants." The servant is Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, according to the majority of scholars and according to the established hadiths. Those whose words are not reliable disagreed and said: Al-Khidr is not the companion of Moses, but rather another scholar. Al-Qushayri also narrated this statement, saying: Some people said that he was a righteous servant, and the correct view is that he was Al-Khidr, and this is what was reported from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mujahid said: He was called Al-Khidr because when he prayed, everything around him would turn green. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Al-Khidr was called so because he sat on a white fur and it began to shake green beneath him. This is a strange authentic hadith. Fur here is the surface of the earth, as stated by Al-Khattabi and others. Al-Khidr is a prophet according to the majority of scholars. It was also said that he was a righteous servant who was not a prophet, and the verse testifies to his prophethood, because the inner workings of his actions can only be through revelation. Also, a person does not learn or follow anyone except those above him, and it is not permissible for someone who is not a prophet to be above a prophet. It was also said that he was an angel from whom God ordered Moses to learn from what he had acquired of hidden knowledge. The first is correct, and God knows best. God Almighty says: We gave him mercy from Us. Mercy in this verse means prophethood. It was also said: it means blessing. And We taught him knowledge from Us meaning knowledge of the unseen. Ibn Atiyyah: Al-Khidr’s knowledge was knowledge of the inner meanings that had been revealed to him. The outward appearances of rulings do not give his actions according to them. Moses’ knowledge was knowledge of rulings and fatwas based on the outward appearances of people’s words and actions.
18:66: The Almighty’s saying: Moses said to him, ‘Shall I follow you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment?’ There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty’s statement: Moses said to him, ‘Shall I follow you?’ This is a question of flattery, and the addressee is exaggerating in good manners. The meaning is: Will it be agreeable to you and easy for you? This is like the hadith: “Can you show me how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution?” And according to some interpretations, the Almighty’s statement: Can your Lord send down to us a table spread with food from the heaven? comes likewise, as explained previously in Al-Ma’idah. Second: In this verse there is evidence that the learner is subordinate to the scholar, even if the ranks differ. It should not be thought that in Moses’ learning from al-Khidr there is anything that indicates that al-Khidr was better than him, for what the inferior knows may be an exception to the superior, and superiority is for the one whom God has preferred. So if al-Khidr was a saint, then Moses is better than him, because he is a prophet, and a prophet is better than a saint. And if he was a prophet, then Moses preferred him with the message. And God knows best. And guidance is the second object of you learned.
18:67: He said Al-Khidr: You will not be able to have patience with me meaning that you, O Moses, cannot be patient with what you see of my knowledge, because the phenomena that are your knowledge do not give it, and how can you be patient with what you see as wrong and you have not been informed of the wisdom in it, nor the path of correctness?
18:68: This is the meaning of his saying: And how can you be patient about something you do not know? The prophets do not approve of something wrong, and it is not permissible for them to approve. That is, you cannot remain silent in accordance with your custom and your rule. Khabra is in the accusative case as a distinction transferred from the subject. It was said: as a source that meets in meaning, because his saying: You did not know means you did not inform him, so it is as if he said: you did not inform him of report, and Mujahid referred to this. The one who is knowledgeable about matters is the one who knows their secrets and what he experiences of them.
18:69: The Almighty said: He said, 'You will find me, if God wills, patient.' That is, I will be patient by God's will. And I will not disobey you in any matter. That is, I have committed myself to obeying you. There is a difference of opinion regarding the exception, does it include His statement, And I will not disobey you in any matter or not? It was said: It includes it like His statement, Men and women who remember God often. It was said: He made an exception in patience, so he was patient. What was made an exception in His statement, And I will not disobey you in any matter? So he objected and asked. Our scholars said: That was from him, because patience is a future matter and he does not know how his condition will be in it, and the negation of the sin is determined and is present in the present, so the exception in it contradicts the determination to do it. It is possible to differentiate between them by the fact that patience is not acquired by us, unlike doing the sin and not doing it, because all of that is acquired by us, and God knows best.
18:70: The Almighty said: He said, ‘If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I tell you about it’ meaning until I am the one who explains it to you. This is from Al-Khidr as discipline and guidance for what requires constant companionship. If he had been patient and persistent, he would have seen wonders, but he objected a lot, so separation and turning away were necessary.
18:71: God Almighty says: So they set out, and when they boarded the ship, he tore it open. There are two issues in this: First: In Sahih Muslim and Al-Bukhari: So they set out walking along the seashore, and a ship passed by, so they spoke to them to carry them, and they recognized Al-Khidr, so they carried him without a rope. When they got on the ship, Moses was surprised to find Al-Khidr had removed one of the ship’s planks with an axe. Moses said to him: People who carried us without a rope, and you deliberately attacked their ship and punctured it in order to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing.
18:72: He said, 'Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?' He said, 'Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my affair with hardship.' He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And the first was forgetfulness from Moses. He said: A bird came and landed on the edge of the ship and pecked a pecket in the sea, so Al-Khidr said to him: My knowledge and your knowledge of God's knowledge is only like what this bird took from this sea. Our scholars said: The edge of the ship is its edge, and the edge of everything is its edge, and from it the edge of the mountain, which is its defined top. Knowledge here means what is known, as he said: And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge, meaning of His information, and this is a metaphor from Al-Khidr, meaning my information and your information have no effect on God's knowledge, just as what this bird took from this sea has no effect in comparison to the water of the sea, and he only used the sea as an example for him because it is most of what he sees of what is in our hands, and the use of the word deficiency here is permissible with the intention of representation and understanding, as there is no deficiency in God's knowledge, and there is no end to His information. Al-Bukhari explained this meaning when he said: By God, my knowledge and your knowledge are not compared to the knowledge of God except as this bird takes from the sea with its beak. In the interpretation of the verse on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: When Al-Khidr breached the ship, no one saw anyone but Moses. He was a slave whom no one could see except the eye of the one whom God wanted to see. If the people had seen him, they would have prevented him from breaching the ship. It was said: The people of the ship went to an island, and Al-Khidr stayed behind and breached the ship. Ibn Abbas said: When Al-Khidr breached the ship, Moses stepped aside and said to himself: What would I have done with the company of this man! I was among the Children of Israel, reciting the Book of God to them morning and evening, and they would obey me! Al-Khidr said to him: O Moses, do you want me to tell you what your soul has told you? He said: Yes, he said such and such. He said: You have spoken the truth. Al-Tha’labi mentioned it in the Book of Brides. Second: The breach of the ship is evidence that the guardian may reduce the orphan’s money if he sees it as good, such as if he fears that his income will be lost unjustly and some of it will be destroyed. Abu Yusuf said: It is permissible for the guardian to appease the ruler by giving some of the orphan’s money instead of some. Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read li-yaghraq with a ya’, ahlha in the nominative case as the subject of yaghraq, so the lam according to the reading of the group in li-yaghraq is the lam of the outcome like yakunu lahum ‘udun wa haznan and according to the reading of Hamza it is the lam of ki, and he did not say li-yaghraqni because what overcame him at the time was his extreme compassion for them and his consideration of their rights. And imra means astonishment, as Al-Qutbi said. And it was said: it is reprehensible, as Mujahid said. Abu Ubaidah said: The matter is the great calamity, and he recited: My peers have suffered a terrible, terrible punishment from me. Al-Akhfash said: It is said that he ordered something, he orders something, if it became intense, and the noun is the order.
18:73: The Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot.’ There are two opinions on its meaning: One of them is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This is an indirect expression. The other is that he forgot and apologized. This indicates that forgetfulness does not require accountability, that it does not fall under accountability, and that no ruling of divorce or anything else is related to it, as has been mentioned previously. If he had forgotten the second time, he would have apologized.
18:74: God the Almighty said: So they set out, until they met a boy, and he killed him. In Bukhari, Ya'la said, Sa'id said: He found boys playing, so he took a disbelieving boy, laid him down, and slaughtered him with a knife. He said, 'Have you killed a pure soul without a soul?' He did not commit an oath. In the two Sahihs and Sahih al-Tirmidhi: Then they got out of the ship, and while they were walking on the shore, al-Khidr saw a boy playing with the boys, so al-Khidr took his head in his hand and tore it off with his hand and killed him. Moses said to him: Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? You have certainly done a terrible thing.
18:75: He said, 'Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?' He said, This is more severe than the first.
18:76: He said, 'If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep company with me, for you have received an excuse from me.' Bukhari's wording: In the interpretation: Al-Khidr passed by some boys playing, so he took a boy by the hand, the brightest of them all, and took a stone and struck him on the head with it until it crushed him, killing him. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: No one saw him except Moses, and if they had seen him, they would have prevented him from the boy.
