I said: There is no difference between these three cases, as it is possible that he first stamped him with a stone, then laid him down and slaughtered him, then pulled out his head, and God knows best what happened in that regard, and it is sufficient for you what came in the Sahih. The majority read: Zakiyyah with an alif. The Kufians and Ibn Amir read: Zakiyyah without an alif and with a shaddah on the ya’. It was said: The meaning is the same, as Al-Kisa’i said. Tha’lab said: Zakiyyah is more eloquent. Abu Amr said: Zakiyyah is the one who has never sinned, and Zakiyyah is the one who sinned and then repented. God the Almighty said: A young boy. The scholars differed about the young boy, was he an adult or not? Al-Kalbi said: He was an adult who used to cut off the road between two villages, and his father was one of the nobles of one of the villages, and his mother was one of the nobles of the other village, so Al-Khidr seized him and wrestled him to the ground, and tore his head from his body. Al-Kalbi said: The young boy’s name was Shimon. Ad-Dahhak said: Haysun. Wahb said: His father’s name was Salas and his mother’s name was Rahmi. Al-Suhayli narrated that his father’s name was Kazir and his mother’s name was Sahwa. The majority said: He was not an adult, and that is why Moses said: Pure and did not sin. This is what is required by the word young boy, because the word young boy is used for men who have not yet reached puberty, and the equivalent of young girl is used for women. Al-Khidr killed him because he knew his secret, and that he was naturally a disbeliever, as in the authentic hadith, and that if he had reached puberty, he would have exhausted his parents with disbelief. Killing a young child is not impossible if God permits it, because God the Almighty is the doer of what He wills, and is able to do whatever He wills. In the Book of Brides, when Moses said to Al-Khidr: You have killed a pure soul - the verse - Al-Khidr became angry and tore off the boy’s left shoulder, peeled the flesh off it, and on the bone of his shoulder was written: Unbeliever who will never believe in God. The proponents of the first opinion argued that the Arabs keep the boy’s name, and from this is the saying of Layla Al-Akhiliya: He cured her of the incurable disease she had. If a boy shook the canal, he would give her water to drink. Safwan said to Hassan: Receive the flies of the sword from me, for I am a young man, and if I am provoked, I am not a poet. In the hadith, it is stated that this boy was spreading corruption on earth, and he swore to his parents that he did not do it, so they would swear to his oath, and protect him from anyone who sought him. They said: His saying: unless it was for killing a soul implies that if it was for killing a soul, there would be no harm in it, and this indicates the boy’s age, otherwise if he had not reached puberty, it would not have been obligatory to kill him for killing a soul, but it was permissible to kill him because he was an adult and disobedient. Ibn Abbas said: He was a young man who used to cut off the road. Ibn Jubayr believed that he had reached the age of accountability based on the reading of Abi and Ibn Abbas And as for the boy, he was a disbeliever, and his parents were believers. Disbelief and faith are attributes of those who are accountable, and they are not applied to those who are not accountable except by virtue of their subordination to their parents, and the boy’s parents were believers according to the text, so the name of disbeliever cannot be applied to him except by reaching puberty, so it must be referred to. The word boy comes from aghtlam, which means intense sexual desire. God the Almighty says: Nakra People differed as to which of the two is more eloquent, Imra or His saying Nakra. A group said: This is a clear killing, and there is something to be expected, so Nakra is more eloquent. A group said: This is a single killing, and that is a group killing, so Imra is more eloquent. Ibn Atiyyah said: I think they have two meanings, and His saying: Imra is more horrific and terrible because it is expected and great, and Nakra is clear in corruption because its abhorrent act has already occurred, and this is clear. His saying: "He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me" is a condition and it is binding, and Muslims are bound by their conditions, and the most deserving of conditions or to be fulfilled are those that the prophets committed to, and were committed to the prophets. His saying: You have conveyed from Me an excuse indicates that the apology is made once in general, and the proof is made from the second time with certainty, as Ibn al-Arabi said. Ibn Atiyyah: It is likely that this story is also the basis for the terms of judgments, which are three, and the days of the one being blamed are three, so reflect on it. God the Almighty said: So do not accompany me This is how the majority read it, meaning follow me. Al-A’raj read tasahhabni with a fat-ha on the ta’ and the ba’ and a shaddah on the noon. It was also read tasahhabni meaning follow me. Ya’qub read tasahhabni with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the ha’. Sahl narrated it on the authority of Abu Amr. Al-Kisa’i said: Its meaning is do not let me accompany you. You have reached an excuse from me meaning you have reached a level that makes it an excuse for not accompanying me. The majority read: from me with a damma on the daal, except that Nafi’ and Asim lightened the noon, so it is ladun connected to the speaker’s ya’ in ghulami wa farsi, and the letter before the ya’ was broken as in this. Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim ladunni with a fat-ha on the lam, a sukoon on the daal, and a lightened noon. It was narrated on the authority of Asim, Ladni with a damma on the lam and a sukoon on the dal. Ibn Mujahid said: This is a mistake. Abu Ali said: This mistake may be due to the narration, but according to the standard Arabic language, it is correct. The majority read Udhran. Isa read Udhran with a damma on the dhal. Ad-Dani narrated that Abi narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Udhri with a kasra on the ra and a ya after it. Question: Al-Tabari narrated that: “Whenever the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) supplicated for someone, he would start with himself. One day he said: ‘May God have mercy on us and on Moses. If he had been patient with his companion, he would have seen wonders. But he said: ‘Do not be my companion, for you have received an excuse from me.’” And in Sahih Muslim, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “May God have mercy on us and on Moses. If he had not been hasty, he would have seen wonders. But he was held responsible by his companion. If he had been patient, he would have seen wonders.” He said: And whenever he mentioned one of the prophets, he would start with himself: May God have mercy on us and on my brother so-and-so. And in Bukhari, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he said: “May God have mercy on Moses. We wish that he had been patient until he told us about their affair.” Dhimmah with the open voiced dhal, and it means blame with the open and broken dhal, and it is tenderness and shame from that sanctity: it is said: I was held responsible by you, blame, and dhimmah. It is as if he was ashamed of his repeated opposition, and of the harsh denunciation that came from him.
18:77: It contains thirteen issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Until, when they came to the people of a town in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abi bin Ka’b on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: mean, so they went around the gatherings and “asked the people of it for food, but they refused to offer them hospitality. Then they found therein a wall about to collapse” he said: leaning. He said: So he straightened it al-Khidr with his hand. Moses said to him: People we came to, but they did not offer us hospitality, nor did they offer us food. “If you had wished, you could have taken payment for it. He said: This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on Moses. I wish he had been patient until he told us about their report.” Second: The scholars differed regarding the village. It was said: It is Ablah, as Qatada said, and Muhammad bin Sirin said the same. It is the stingiest village and the farthest from the sky. It was also said: Antioch. It was also said: In the island of Andalusia, as narrated by Abu Hurairah and others, and it is mentioned that it is the Green Island. A group said: It is Bajrawan, which is in the region of Azerbaijan. Al-Suhayli narrated and said: It is Barqa. Al-Tha’labi is a village of the Romans called Nazareth, and the Christians are attributed to it. All of this is according to the disagreement regarding which part of the earth the story of Moses took place. And God knows best the truth of that. Third: When Moses, peace be upon him, watered the two daughters of Shu’aib, he was in greater need than when he came to the village with al-Khidr. He did not ask for food, but rather watered them first, and in the village they asked for food. There are many differences in this for scholars, including that Moses was alone in the story of Madyan and in the story of al-Khidr, following someone else. I said: And this meaning is consistent with what he said at the beginning of the verse to his young man: “Bring us our breakfast. We have certainly suffered much fatigue on this journey of ours.” So he became hungry out of consideration for his companion Joshua, and God knows best. It was said: Since this was a journey of discipline and he was entrusted with the burden of hardship, and it was a journey of migration, he was entrusted with the aid and support of food. Fourth: This verse is evidence of asking for sustenance, and that whoever is hungry must ask for what satisfies his hunger, contrary to the ignorant Sufis. Asking for food is asking for food, and what is meant here is asking for hospitality, as evidenced by His statement: But they refused to host them. Therefore, the people of the village deserved to be criticized and accused of meanness and miserliness, as our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, described them. Qatadah said about this verse: The worst villages are those that do not host guests and do not recognize the right of the wayfarer. It is clear from this that hospitality was obligatory upon them, and that Al-Khidr and Moses only asked for what was due to them of hospitality, and this is more appropriate for the state of the prophets and the position of the virtuous and the saints. Hospitality has been discussed previously in Hud, and praise be to God. God forgives Al-Hariri for making light of this verse and acting rashly, and making a mistake and slipping, and using it as evidence of begging and insistence, and that this is not a defect in the one who does it, nor does it diminish him, so he said: If you respond, then there is no shortcoming in responding to you. Moses and Al-Khidr responded before. I said: This is playing with religion, and a departure from respecting the prophets. It is a literary slap in the face, and a ridiculous slip. May God have mercy on the righteous predecessors, for they exaggerated in their advice to every person of sound mind, and they said: No matter how much you play with something, beware of playing with your religion. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: A wall. The wall and the walls have the same meaning. In the hadith: Until the water reaches the walls. A worthy place has a wall built around it, and its root is to raise. The tree ajdara grew, and from it smallpox. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: It wants to collapse means it is close to falling. This is a metaphor and expansion. It was explained in the hadith by saying: leaning. This was evidence of the existence of metaphor in the Qur’an, and this is the view of the majority. All actions that are rightfully attributed to a living, speaking being, when they are attributed to an inanimate object or an animal, are metaphors, meaning that if a human were in its place, he would be in compliance with that action. This There are many examples of this in the speech and poetry of the Arabs, including the saying of Al-A’sha: Do you desist while those who are extravagant do not desist? Like stabbing, in which the oil and the twist are lost. So he added the prohibition to the insult. And from that is the saying of another: The spear wants Abu Baraa's chest and he wants the blood of Bani Aqil Another said: An age surrounds me with a camel, a time that intends to do good Another said: On a mission, he split their heads like axes when they want blades. That is, fixed in the ground, from their saying, the blade of the sword if fixed in the throw, so he likened the impact of the swords on their heads to the impact of axes on the ground, for the axe falls in it and fixes itself and hardly comes out. Hassan bin Thabit said: If meanness were attributed, he would be an ugly-faced, one-eyed slave from Thaqif. Antara said: He was frightened by the sound of the spear and complained to me with tears and snorted. This meaning was explained by saying: If he knew what the dialogue was about, he would have complained. This is very common in this sense. It is from this that people say: My house overlooks so-and-so’s house. And in the hadith: The fire complained to its Lord. Some people forbade metaphor in the Qur'an, including Abu Ishaq al-Isfarayini, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Dawud al-Isfahani and others, because the speech of God Almighty and the speech of His Messenger, to be taken literally, is more appropriate for the one with virtue and religion, because it narrates the truth as God Almighty informed us in His Book. Among the evidence they used was that they said: If God Almighty addressed us metaphorically, it would also be necessary to describe Him as metaphorical, because turning from the literal to the metaphorical would require inability to be literal, and this is impossible for God Almighty. God Almighty said: On the Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do. And He Almighty said: And they will say, 'Is there any more?' And He Almighty said: When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its wrath and its roaring. And He Almighty said: It calls whoever turns back and turns away and The Fire complained to its Lord. And: Hell and Paradise argued and there was nothing like it in reality, and that its Creator, who made everything speak, made it speak. And in Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Then his mouth will be sealed and his thigh will be told, ‘Speak.’ Then his thigh, flesh and bones will speak of his deeds. This is so that he may excuse himself, and that is the hypocrite, and that is the one with whom God is angry.” This is in the Hereafter. As for in this world, it is narrated in Al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the Hour will not come until wild beasts speak to mankind, and until a man speaks to the tip of his whip and the strap of his sandal, and his thigh informs him of what his family did after him.” Abu ‘Isa said: There is a hadith on this topic from Abu Hurairah, and this is a good, rare hadith. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: So he established it. It was said: He demolished it and then sat down to build it. So Moses said to Al-Khidr: If you had wished, you could have taken payment for it, because he did something that deserved payment. Abu Bakr Al-Anbari mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of [Ubayy ibn Ka’b] on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he recited: So they found therein a wall about to collapse, so he demolished it and sat down to build it. Abu Bakr said: If the chain of transmission of this hadith is authentic, then it is in accordance with the Messenger’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, interpretation of the Qur’an. Some of the narrators inserted an interpretation of the Qur’an in a place and interpreted it as Qur’an that was missing from the Mushaf of Uthman, according to what some of the critics said. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: He wiped it with his hand and established it, so it stood up. This statement is correct, and it is most similar to the actions of the prophets, may God bless them and grant them peace, and even the saints. In some reports: The thickness of that wall was thirty cubits by the cubit of that century, and its length on the surface of the earth was five hundred cubits, and its width was fifty cubits, so Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, straightened it, that is, he leveled it with his hand, so it became straight. Al-Tha’labi said this in the book Al-Ara’is. So Moses said to Al-Khidr: If you wanted, you could have taken a wage for it, that is, food that you would eat. So in this is evidence of the miracles of the saints, and likewise what was described of the conditions of Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, in this chapter are all extraordinary matters, if we assume that he is a saint and not a prophet. The Almighty’s saying: And I did not do it of my own accord indicates his prophethood and that the duties and rulings were revealed to him, just as the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, were revealed, except that he is not a messenger, and God knows best. Eighth: It is obligatory for a person not to sit under a leaning wall for fear of it falling, but rather to walk quickly if he is passing by it, because in the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: If one of you passes a leaning tarpaulin, let him walk quickly. Abu Ubaid al-Qasim ibn Salam said: Abu Ubaidah used to say: The tarpaulin is similar to the view of the Persians, in the form of a minaret and a tall building. Jarir said: I twisted it, pruning the veins, pruning it, as if I were on a tarpaulin It is said: Wakan yakan if he sat. In Al-Sahah: The tarbal is the high piece of the wall, and the great rock protruding from the mountain, and the tarabils of the Levant are its monasteries. It is said: Tarbal urinated if he stretched it upwards. Ninth: The miracles of the saints are proven, as indicated by the proven reports and the continuous verses, and none denies them except the innovating denier or the corrupt deviant. The verses are what God the Most High informed about Maryam about the appearance of winter fruits in the summer, and summer fruits in the winter - as mentioned above - and what appeared at her hand when she ordered the palm tree, which was dry, to bear fruit, and she was not a prophet, according to the disagreement. What appears at the hand of Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, of the breach of the ship, the killing of the boy, and the erection of the wall is evidence of this. Some scholars said: It is not permissible to say that he was a prophet, because proving prophethood is not permissible by individual reports, especially since it was narrated by way of continuous narration - without being open to interpretation - by the consensus of the nation that he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: There is no prophet after me. And God Almighty said: And the Seal of the Prophets. Al-Khidr and Elias are both still alive with this honor, so it is necessary that they are not prophets, because if they were prophets, then it would be necessary that there be a prophet after our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, except for what is indicated in the hadith of Jesus that he will descend after him. I said: Al-Khidr was a prophet - as mentioned above - and there is no prophet after our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that is, no prophet will ever claim prophethood after him, and God knows best. Tenth: People differed as to whether it is permissible for a saint to know that he is a saint or not. There are two opinions: One of them is that it is not permissible, and that what appears on his hands must be observed with an eye of fear of deception, because there is no certainty that it is a deception and a lure for him. It was narrated from Al-Sarri that he used to say: If a man entered a garden and a bird from the top of every tree spoke to him in an eloquent tongue: Peace be upon you, O saint of God, if he did not fear that it was a deception, he would have been deceived. And because if he knew that he was a saint, the fear would have been removed from him and he would have been secure. And one of the conditions of a saint is that fear should continue until the angels descend upon him, as God Almighty said: The angels descend upon them, [saying], ‘Do not fear and do not grieve.’ And because a saint is one who is sealed with happiness, and the consequences are hidden and no one knows what he will be sealed with. For this reason, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Actions are judged by their endings. The second statement: It is permissible for a saint to know that he is a saint. Don't you see that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is permissible to know that he is a saint? There is no disagreement that it is permissible for others to know that they are saints of God, the Most High, so it is permissible for him to know that. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, informed us about the state of the ten of his companions, that they are from the people of Paradise. However, that did not remove their fear, rather they were more reverent of God, the Most High, and more fearful and awe-inspiring. So if that is permissible for the ten and it does not remove their fear, then so is it for others. Al-Shibli used to say: I am safe on this side. When he died and was buried, the Daylamites crossed the Tigris that day and took control of Baghdad. People say: Two calamities: the death of Al-Shibli and the crossing of the Daylam. It is not said that it is possible that this was a means of enticement, because if that were permissible, then it would be permissible for the Prophet not to know that he was a prophet and a saint of God, because it is permissible for that to be a means of enticement. So when that was not permissible because it would invalidate miracles, this was not permissible because it would invalidate miracles. What was narrated about the appearance of miracles at the hands of Balaam and his renunciation of religion after that, based on his saying: Then he renounced it, does not state in the verse that he was a saint and then the sainthood was renounced from him. What was narrated that what was shown at his hands was something that is similar to miracles is individual reports that do not require knowledge, and God knows best. The difference between a miracle and a miracle is that a condition for a miracle is concealment, while a condition for a miracle is manifestation. It was said: A miracle is what appears without a claim, and a miracle is what appears when the prophets claim, so they are asked for proof and the effect of that appears. The conditions of a miracle were mentioned in the introduction to the book, and praise be to God alone, with no partner. As for the hadiths that were reported indicating the proof of miracles, among them is what Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent ten men as a secret expedition and put in charge of them Asim bin Thabit Al-Ansari, the grandfather of Asim bin Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him. They set out until they reached Al-Hada, which is between Usfan and Mecca. They mentioned a tribe of Hudhayl called Banu Lihyan, so they sent out to them about two hundred men, all of them archers. They tracked them down until they found their food, dates that they had taken from Medina. They said: These are dates from Yathrib. They tracked them down. When Asim and his companions saw them, they took refuge in Fadfad, and the people surrounded them. They said to them: Come down and give us your hands, and we will pledge and covenant that we will not kill any of you. Asim bin Thabit, the commander of the expedition, said: By God, I will not come down today under the protection of the infidel. O God, inform your Prophet about us. They shot arrows and killed Asim with seven men. Three men came down to them with a pledge and covenant, and they were Khubayb Al-Ansari, Ibn Al-Dathna, and another man. When they were able to overpower them, they released them. The third man said: This is the beginning of treachery! By God, I will not accompany you, for I have an example in these people - meaning the dead - so they dragged him and treated him so that he would accompany them, but he did not, so they killed him. They went with Khubayb and Ibn al-Dathna until they sold them in Mecca after the Battle of Badr. Banu al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal ibn Abd Manaf bought Khubayb, and it was Khubayb who killed al-Harith ibn Amir on the day of Badr. Khubayb remained with them as a prisoner. Ubayd God ibn Ayyadh informed him that the daughter of al-Harith had told him that when they had gathered, he had borrowed a razor from her to sharpen with, so she lent it to him. Then a son of mine took it while I was unaware until he came to him. She said: I found him sitting on his thigh with the razor in his hand, and I was startled by a fear that Khubayb recognized in my face. He said: Are you afraid that I will kill him? I would not have done that. She said: By God, I have never seen a prisoner better than Khubayb. By God, I found him one day eating a bunch of grapes in his hand, and he was bound with iron, and there was no fruit in Mecca. She used to say: This is a provision that God Almighty has provided for Khubayb. When they took him out of the sanctuary to kill him outside, Khubayb said to them: Let me bow two rak’ahs. So they left him, so he bowed two rak’ahs, then he said: If it were not for the fact that you think that what is in me is fear of death, I would have increased it. Then he said: O God, count them in number, and kill them one by one, and do not leave a single one of them. Then he said: I do not care when I kill a Muslim on which side my death is for God This is in the essence of God, and if He wills, He will bless the limbs of a torn limb. Then Banu Al-Harith killed him, and it was Khabib who established the two Rak'ahs for every Muslim who was killed with patience. So God responded to Asim on the day he was killed, and he informed the Prophet (peace be upon him) and his companions of their report and what had happened to them. Some of the infidels of Quraysh sent to Asim when they heard that he had been killed, to bring something of him that they could recognize, and he had killed one of their leaders on the day of Badr, so God sent upon Asim something like a shade of wasps, which protected him from their messengers, and they were not able to cut off any of his flesh. Ibn Ishaq said about this story: When Asim bin Thabit was killed, Hudhayl wanted his head to sell it to Salafah bint Saad bin Shahid. She had vowed when her two sons were killed at Uhud that if she could get hold of his head, they would drink wine from his skulls, but Ad-Dabr prevented them. When she stood between him and them, they said: Leave him until evening, then he will go away from him, and we will take him. Then God sent the valley, which carried Asim and he left. Asim had made a covenant with God that he would never touch a polytheist, nor would a polytheist ever touch him, during his lifetime. So God prevented him after his death from what he had refrained from during his lifetime. And on the authority of Amr bin Umayyah Ad-Damri: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent him as a spy alone, and he said: I came to the wood of Khubayb and climbed it, fearing spies, so I released him, and he fell to the ground, then it rushed in and retreated a little, then it turned around as if the ground had swallowed him. And in another narration there is an addition: We have not mentioned any wound to Khubayb until this hour, as mentioned by Al-Bayhaqi. Eleventh: It is not denied that the guardian has money and a trust with which he protects his money and his children. The companions and their money are enough for you, along with their guardianship and virtue, and they are the proof against others. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “While a man was in a desert, he heard a voice in a cloud saying, ‘Water the garden of so-and-so.’ That cloud moved away and emptied its water into a lava field, and behold, one of those clouds had absorbed all that water. He followed the water and saw a man standing in his garden, moving the water with his shovel. He said, ‘O servant of God, what is your name?’ He said, ‘So-and-so is the name he heard in the cloud.’ He said to him, ‘O servant of God, why did you ask me my name?’ He said, ‘I heard a voice in the cloud whose water is this saying, ‘Water the garden of so-and-so, in your name. So what do you do with it?’ He said, ‘Since you have said this, I look at what comes out of it and give a third of it in charity, and I and my family eat a third, and I return a third of it to it.’” And in another narration, And I give a third of it to the poor, the beggars, and the wayfarer. I said: This hadith does not contradict his statement, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: Do not take a farm and be content with the world. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Masoud, and he said about it a good hadith, for it is understood to refer to the one who takes it as a means of increasing it or enjoying its pleasures and prosperity. As for the one who takes it as a livelihood with which he protects his religion and his family, taking it with this intention is one of the best deeds, and it is one of the best kinds of money. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, good money for the good man. People have talked a lot about the miracles of the saints, and what we have mentioned about it is sufficient. And God is the guide to success. Twelfth: The Almighty’s saying: I would have taken a wage for it. This is evidence of the validity of hiring, which is the tradition of the prophets and saints, as will be explained in Surat Al-Qasas, God willing. The majority read I would have taken and Abu Amr read I would have taken and this is the reading of Ibn Masoud, Al-Hasan, and Qatada, and they are two languages with the same meaning of taking, like your saying: taba’a and ataba’a, and taqa and attaqa. Some of the reciters supported the dhal in the ta’, and some of them did not assimilate it. In the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka’b: If I had wanted, I would have been given a wage. This was issued by Moses as a question in the form of an offer, not an objection.
18:78: Then Al-Khidr said to him: This is a parting between me and you by virtue of what you had stipulated for yourself. His repetition of between me and you and his enemy to him about between us is for emphasis. Sibawayh said: Just as it is said, May God disgrace the liar from me and you, meaning from us. Ibn Abbas said: Moses' words about the ship and the boy were for God, and his words about the wall were for himself to seek something from this world, so that was the reason for the parting. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: That wall was a wall whose height in the sky was one hundred cubits. Thirteenth: The Almighty’s saying: I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience. The interpretation of something is its outcome, meaning He said to him: I will tell you why you did what you did. It was said in the interpretation of these signs that happened to Moses with Al-Khidr: They are an argument against Moses, and a wonder to him. That is because when he denied the matter of the breach in the ship, he was called: O Moses, where was this plan of yours while you were in the chest thrown in the sea! So when he denied the matter of the boy, he was told: Where is your denial of this compared to your prodding the Copt and your judgment on him! So when he denied the construction of the wall, he was told: Where is this compared to your lifting the stone of the well for the daughters of Shu’aib without payment!
18:79: The Almighty said: As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea. This was used as evidence by those who said that the poor are in a better condition than the needy. This meaning has already been fully explained in Surah Bara'ah. It has been said that they were merchants, but since they were travelers with few resources in the midst of the sea, and in a state of weakness to fend off calamities, they were referred to as poor, since they were in a state that was pitiable. This is like saying to a rich man who was struck by a sudden disaster or a calamity: poor. Ka'b and others said: It belonged to ten poor brothers who inherited it from their father, five of whom were in a state of weakness and five of whom were working at sea. It has also been said that there were seven of them, each of whom had a state of weakness that was not like the other. Al-Naqqash mentioned their names. As for the workers, one of them was a leper, the second was one-eyed, the third was lame, the fourth was a leper, and the fifth had a fever that never stopped for a lifetime, and he was the youngest of them. The five who could not work were: blind, deaf, mute, crippled, and insane. The sea they worked on was between Persia and Rome. Al-Tha'labi mentioned it. A group read: Limasakeen with a shaddah on the seen, and there was a difference of opinion about that. It was said: They are the sailors of the ship, because the misak is the one who holds the ship's man, and all service is suitable for holding him, so they were all called misakeen. A group said: He meant by misakeen the tanning of the musuk, which is hides, the singular of which is musk. The most apparent reading is misakeen with a shaddah, the plural of miskeen, and that its meaning is: The ship belongs to weak people who should be pitied. And God knows best. God the Almighty said: So I wanted to make it defective. That is, to make it have a defect. It is said: I found fault with something and it became defective, so it is defective and faulty. And His statement: And behind them was a king who seized every ship by force. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr read saheeha. Ibn Abbas and Uthman ibn Affan also read saliha. The root of behind means behind. Some of the commentators said: He was behind him and they would return to him. Most of them are of the opinion that the meaning of behind here is in front, which is supported by the reading of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr: And before them was a king who seized every intact ship by force. Ibn Atiyah said: Behind them is in my opinion appropriate, and that is because these words come with consideration of time, and that is because the existing preceding event is the forward, and that which comes after it is the backward, and it is what is behind, and that is contrary to what appears at first sight. Consider these words in their places where they appear, and you will find that they are consistent. The meaning of this verse is: These people, their work and their efforts will come after him in time, the usurpation of this kingdom. And whoever reads in front of them meant in place, that is, as if they were walking to a country. And his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: The prayer is in front of you means in place, otherwise their being at that time was in front of the prayer in time. Consider this article, for it is a relief from the commotion of these words. Qatada found in the book of al-Tabari: And behind them was a king. Qatada said: In front of them. Don’t you see him saying: Behind them is Hell while he is in front of them? This statement is not correct, and this is the foreignness that al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan was upset about, as al-Zajjaj said. I said: What this Imam chose was preceded by Ibn Arafa. Al-Harawi said: Ibn Arafa said: The speaker says: How did he say behind him when it is in front of him? Abu Ubaid and Abu Ali Qatrib claimed that this is one of the opposites, and that behind is in the meaning of in front, but this is not obtained, because in front is the opposite of behind, and this is only valid at times, like when you say to a man if he made a promise in Rajab for Ramadan and then said: And behind you is Sha’ban, it is permissible even if it was in front of him, because it replaces him until the time of his promise. Al-Qushayri also referred to this statement and said: This is only said at times, and it is not said to a man in front of you that he is behind you. Al-Farra’ said: And others permitted it, and the people were not aware of the report of the king, so God Almighty informed Al-Khidr even of the defect in the ship, and Al-Zajjaj mentioned it. Al-Mawardi said: The Arabs differed in using behind instead of in front into three opinions: One of them: It is permissible to use it in any case and in any place and it is one of the opposites. God Almighty said: Behind them is Hell meaning in front of them. And the poet said: Do you expect the Banu Marwan to listen to me and obey me, while my people Tamim and the desert are behind me? It means in front of me. The second: that behind is used in place of in front of in times and times because a person passes it and it becomes behind him and it is not permissible in anything else. The third: that it is permissible in objects that have no face like two stones facing each other, each one behind the other and it is not permissible in anything else, and this is the saying of Ali bin Isa. There is a difference of opinion regarding the name of this king, so it was said: Hadad bin Badad. And it was said: Al-Jalandi, and Al-Suhayli said it. Al-Bukhari mentioned the name of the king who took every ship by force, so he said: He is Hadad bin Badad and the name of the murdered boy was Jaysur, and this is how we recorded it in Al-Jami’ from the narration of Yazid Al-Marwazi, and in a narration other than this, Haysur with a ha’, and I have a third narration in the margin of the book: It is Haysun. He used to take every good ship by force, and that is why Al-Khidr criticized it and tore it up, so in this there is jurisprudence working with interests if its face is proven, and the permissibility of repairing all of the money by spoiling some of it, and this has been mentioned previously. In Sahih Muslim there is the reason for the wisdom of tearing up the ship, and that is his saying: So when the one who is harnessing it comes, he finds it torn up and passes over it, so repair it with a piece of wood, the hadith. And you get from this encouragement to be patient in times of hardship, how many benefits are contained in that which is disliked, and this is the meaning of His saying: And perhaps you dislike a thing which is good for you.
18:80: The Almighty said: And as for the boy, his parents were believers. It was stated in the authentic hadith: He was created a disbeliever on the day he was created. This supports the apparent meaning that he was not an adult, and it is possible that it is report about him even though he was an adult, and this has been mentioned previously. God the Almighty said: So we feared that he would overburden them. It was said: This is from the words of Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, and this is what the context of the speech testifies to, and it is the saying of many commentators, meaning we feared that he would overburden them with transgression and disbelief, and God had permitted him to strive to kill people in this manner. It was also said: This is from the words of God the Almighty and Al-Khidr spoke about it. Al-Tabari said: Its meaning is so we knew, and Ibn Abbas said the same, meaning so we knew. This is like the way he referred to knowledge with fear in his saying: Except that they fear that they will not be able to keep within the limits set by God. It was narrated that Ubayy read So your Lord knew. It was said: Fear means dislike. It is said: I separated them for fear that they would fight, meaning dislike of that. Ibn Atiyyah said: What is most apparent to me in explaining this interpretation, even though the wording contradicts it, is that it is a metaphor, meaning that if the created beings and those being addressed knew his condition, they would fear overburdening the parents. Ibn Masoud read fear your Lord, and this is clear in the metaphor, and this is similar to what occurred in the Qur’an regarding God Almighty from perhaps and perhaps, and that all that is in all of this of hope and expectation and fear and dread is only sufficient for you, O those addressed, and exhausts them makes them groan and burdens them, and the meaning is that his love makes them follow him so they go astray and become religious with his religion.
18:81: The Almighty said: So We intended that their Lord should substitute for them a son. The majority of scholars read it with a fat-ha on the ba' and a shaddah on the dal. Asim read it with a sukoon on the ba' and a light dal, meaning that God should grant them a son. Better than him in purity meaning in religion and righteousness. It is said: badala and wabadala like mahal and amahla and nazala and wanzala. And nearer in kinship Ibn Abbas read kinship. The poet said: How can I wrong a slave girl who is kind and merciful? The rest are silent, and from this is the saying of Ru’bah ibn al-‘Ajaj: O you who sent down mercy upon Idris and cursed Satan It was differed from Abu Amr. Rahma is in apposition to zakat. It is said: Rahma rahma and rahma, and its alif is for the feminine, and its masculine is rahma. It was said: Rahm here means womb. Ibn Abbas read it and connect rahma meaning womb, and he also read purer than it. Ibn Jubayr and Ibn Jurayj said that they are a substitute for a girl. Al-Kalbi said that a prophet from the prophets married her and she bore him a prophet, and God guided a nation from the nations through him. Qatada: She bore twelve prophets. Ibn Jurayj also said that the mother of the boy on the day he was killed was pregnant with a Muslim boy and the one killed was an unbeliever. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: She gave birth to a slave girl who gave birth to a prophet. In another narration: God replaced her with a slave girl who gave birth to seventy prophets. Jaafar bin Muhammad said this on the authority of his father. Our scholars said: This is far-fetched, and the number of prophets is not known except among the Children of Israel, and this woman was not among them. We learn from this verse that calamities caused by the loss of children are not to be trivialized, even if they are pieces of the heart. Whoever submits to fate, his end will be clear. Qatada said: His parents rejoiced when he was born and grieved when he was killed. If he had survived, it would have led to their destruction. It is obligatory for every person to be satisfied with the decree of God, for God’s decree for the believer in what he dislikes is better for him than His decree for him in what he loves.
18:82: The Almighty said: And as for the wall, it belonged to two boys. These two boys were young, as indicated by their description as orphans, and their names were Asram and Sareem. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: They are not orphans after reaching puberty. This is what appears. It may be possible that the term orphan will remain for them after reaching puberty if they are orphans, in the sense of compassion for them. It was previously mentioned that orphanhood in people is due to the loss of the father, and in other animals it is due to the loss of the mother. His statement, in the city, indicates that a village is called a city, and from this is the hadith: I was commanded to create a village that will eat villages. And in the hadith of the migration, Whose people are you? The man said, From the people of Medina, meaning Mecca. God the Almighty said: And beneath it was a treasure for them. People differed about the treasure. Ikrimah and Qatada said: It was a physical wealth, which is what is apparent from the word treasure, as in the language it means accumulated wealth, and we have already discussed it. Ibn Abbas said: It was a sign in buried pages. He also said: It was a tablet of gold on which was written: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. I am amazed at the one who believes in destiny, how he grieves. I am amazed at the one who believes in provision, how he tires. I am amazed at the one who believes in death, how he rejoices. I am amazed at the one who believes in the reckoning, how he is heedless. I am amazed at the one who believes in the world and its vicissitudes with its people, how he feels reassured by them. There is no god, there is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Something similar was narrated from Ikrimah and Umar, the freed slave of Ghafra, and Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, narrated it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. God the Almighty said: And their father was a righteous man. The apparent meaning of the wording and the previous one is that their father was Dunya. It was said: He is the seventh father, said by Ja’far bin Muhammad. It was also said: The tenth, so they preserved him even though he was not mentioned as righteous. He was called Kashh, said by Muqatil. Their mother’s name was Dunya, mentioned by Al-Naqqash. This indicates that God the Almighty preserves the righteous man in himself and in his children, even if they are far away from him. It has been narrated that God the Almighty preserves the righteous man in seven of his offspring, and this is indicated by His Almighty saying: Indeed, my ally is God, who has sent down the Book, and He is the ally of the righteous. The Almighty’s saying: And I did not do it of my own accord implies that al-Khidr was a prophet, and the disagreement on that has already been mentioned. That is an interpretation means explanation. That which you could not have patience for A group read you could. The majority read you could shine. Abu Hatim said: This is how we read it as it is written in the Mushaf. Here are five issues: First: If someone says that the youth of Moses was not heard mentioned at the beginning of the verse or at the end of it, he will be told: There is a difference of opinion on that. So Ikrimah said to Ibn Abbas: The youth of Moses was not heard mentioned even though he was with him? He said: The youth drank from the water and became immortal, and the scholar took him and closed a ship over him and then sent him into the sea and it will continue to surge with him in it until the Day of Resurrection. That is because he was not allowed to drink from it, so he drank from it. Al-Qushayri said: If this is proven, then the youth is not Joshua bin Nun, for Joshua bin Nun lived after Moses and was his successor, and it is more apparent that Moses dismissed his youth when he met Al-Khidr. Our Sheikh, Imam Abu Al-Abbas, said: It is possible that he was satisfied with mentioning the one who was followed instead of the one who followed, and God knows best. Second: If someone were to say: How did Al-Khidr attribute the story of extracting the treasure of the two boys to God Almighty, and say about the breach in the ship: So I wanted to damage it, thus attributing the damage to himself? It would be said to him: He attributed the will in the wall to God Almighty because it was a new matter in a long time that was hidden from the unseen, so it was good to single out this place for mentioning God Almighty, and if Al-Khidr intended that, then what he knew was that God Almighty intended it. It was said: Since all of that was good, He attributed it to God Almighty, and attributed the defect of the ship to Himself out of respect for etiquette, because it is a word of defect, so he behaved himself by not attributing the will in it to anyone but himself, just as Abraham, peace be upon him, behaved himself in his saying: And when I am ill, it is He who cures me. So he attributed the action before and after to God Almighty, and attributed the illness to himself, since it is a meaning of deficiency and calamity, so no words are attributed to Him, glory be to Him, except what is good from them and not what is bad. This is like what God Almighty said: In Your hand is all good, and He limited himself to it, so He did not attribute evil to Him, even though good and evil, harm and benefit are in His hand, since He is capable of all things, and He is All-Knowing of all things. There is no objection to what he, peace be upon him, narrated from his Lord, glory be to Him, that He will say on the Day of Resurrection: "O son of Adam, I was sick and you did not visit Me. I asked you for food and you did not feed Me. I asked you for drink and you did not give Me drink." This is an address and a gentle reproach, the implication of which is to define the grace of the Majestic One and the amounts of reward for these deeds. This meaning has been presented above. And God knows best. And God may attribute to Himself whatever He wishes, and we do not attribute to Himself except what He has permitted us to of beautiful descriptions and noble actions. He is far above all shortcomings and defects. And He said about the boy: So We intended, as if He attributed the killing to Himself and the change to God. And the most severe is the perfection of creation and intellect. We have already discussed this in Al-An'am, and praise be to God. Third: Our Sheikh, Imam Abu al-Abbas, said: Some heretics from the Batiniyya went to a path that requires these legal rulings, so they said: These general legal rulings are only to be ruled upon by the prophets and the common people, but as for the saints and the elite, they do not need those texts, rather what is required of them is what occurs in their hearts, and they are ruled upon by what predominates in their thoughts. They said: This is because their hearts are pure from impurities and are free from others, so the divine sciences and divine truths are revealed to them, so they stand on the secrets of the universe and know the rulings of the particulars, and with them they are independent of the rulings of the general laws, as happened to al-Khidr, for he was independent of what was revealed to him of the sciences, from what Moses had of those understandings. And it came in what they transmit: Consult your heart, even if the fatwa-givers give you a fatwa. Our Sheikh, may God be pleased with him, said: This statement is heresy and disbelief. Its speaker should be killed and not given a chance to repent, because it is a denial of what he has learned from the laws. God, the Most High, has implemented His Sunnah and executed His wisdom, such that His rulings are not known except through His messengers, the ambassadors between Him and His creation. They are the ones who convey His message and His words, who explain His laws and rulings. He chose them for this and singled them out for what is there, as God, the Most High, said: “God chooses from the angels messengers and from the people. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing.” And God, the Most High, said: God knows best where to place His message. And God, the Most High, said: Mankind was one community, and God sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners. And other verses. In short, absolute knowledge, necessary certainty, and the consensus of the predecessors and successors have been obtained that there is no way to know the rulings of God the Most High, which are related to His commands and prohibitions, and none of them can be known except through the messengers. So whoever says that there is another way to know His commands and prohibitions other than the messengers, such that one can do without the messengers, then he is a disbeliever, and he should be killed and not given a chance to repent, and he does not need to ask or answer him. Then it is a statement that there are prophets after our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, whom God made the Seal of His Prophets and Messengers, so there is no prophet or messenger after him. The explanation of that is that whoever says that he takes from his heart and that whatever he falls into is the ruling of God the Most High, and that he acts according to it, and that he does not need a book or a Sunnah, then he has proven for himself the special status of prophethood, for this is similar to what he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: The Holy Spirit breathed into my soul Hadith. Fourth: The majority of people believed that Al-Khidr died, peace be upon him. A group said: He is alive because he drank from the spring of life, and that he will remain on earth, and that he will perform Hajj to the House. Ibn Atiyyah said: The discussion on this meaning has been extensive, and he mentioned in his book many things about Ali bin Abi Talib and others, and none of them stand up to reason. If Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, were alive and performing Hajj, he would have a presence in the religion of Islam, and God is the All-Knowing of the details of things, there is no Lord other than Him. What indicates that Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, is dead now is his saying, peace be upon him: Have you seen this night of yours? No one will remain from those who are on the face of the earth today. I said: This is what Al-Bukhari went for and Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi chose it, and the correct opinion is the second one, which is that it is alive according to what we mention. The hadith was included by Muslim in his Sahih on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the ‘Isha’ prayer one night at the end of his life. When he had finished, he stood up and said: ‘What do you think of this night of yours? After a hundred years, no one on the face of the earth will remain.’ Ibn ‘Umar said: ‘So, are the people in the statement of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in what they say of these hadiths about a hundred years? Rather, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘No one on the face of the earth today will remain.’ He meant by that that century would be destroyed. He also narrated it from the hadith of Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say a month before he died: You ask me about the Hour, but its knowledge is with God. I swear by God that there is not a soul on the earth that will live a hundred years. In another narration, Salim said: We discussed that it is “created on that day.” In another narration: There is not a soul today that will live a hundred years and be alive on that day. Abd al-Rahman, the owner of the water-skin, explained it and said: The age will decrease. Abu Sa`id al-Khudri narrated something similar to this hadith. Our scholars said: The gist of what this hadith includes is that he, peace and blessings be upon him, informed us a month before his death that everyone from the children of Adam who was present at that time would not live more than a hundred years, based on his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: There is not a soul that will live a hundred years. This wording does not include the angels or the jinn, since it has not been authenticated from them that they are like that, nor the irrational animal, based on his saying: Anyone who is on the face of the earth. This is only said based on the original meaning of it being applied to those who have reason, so it is clear that what is meant is the children of Adam. Ibn Omar explained this meaning, saying: He means by that that century will be destroyed. There is no argument for those who use it as evidence for the invalidity of the statement of those who say that Al-Khidr is alive, due to the generality of his statement: (There is no soul that has been breathed), because the generality, even if it confirms its comprehensiveness, is not a text in it, rather it is subject to specification. Just as it does not include Jesus, peace be upon him, because he did not die and was not killed, so he is alive according to the text of the Qur’an and its meaning, and it does not include the Antichrist, although he is alive according to the evidence of the hadith of Al-Jassasah, likewise it does not include Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, and he is not a witness to the people, nor one of those who mix with them to the point that it occurs to them when they are talking to each other, so a generality like this does not include him. It has been said that the People of the Cave are alive and are performing Hajj with Jesus, peace be upon him, as mentioned above. And the same applies to the young man of Moses in the statement of Ibn Abbas, as we mentioned. Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi mentioned in his book Al-Ara'is: The correct view is that Al-Khidr was a long-lived prophet who was hidden from sight. Muhammad ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated on the authority of Damrah ibn Rabi'ah on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shawdhab who said: Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, is from the descendants of Persia, and Elias is from the Children of Israel. They meet every year during the season. And on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar who said: Al-Khidr and Elias will remain alive on earth as long as the Qur'an is on earth. When it is lifted, they will die. Our Sheikh, Imam Abu Muhammad Abdul-Mu'ti ibn Mahmoud ibn Abdul-Mu'ti al-Lakhmi mentioned in his explanation of the message by al-Qushayri many stories about a group of righteous men and women who saw Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, and met him. Their sum indicates the utmost suspicion of his life, along with what was mentioned by al-Naqqash, al-Tha'labi, and others. It was stated in Sahih Muslim: The Antichrist will come to some of the salt marshes near Madinah, and on that day a man will come out to him who is the best of people - or - from the best of people. The hadith, and at the end of it Abu Ishaq said: meaning that this man is Al-Khidr. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya mentioned in the book Al-Hawatif with a chain of transmission that goes back to Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he met Al-Khidr and taught him this supplication, and he mentioned that in it is a great reward, forgiveness, and mercy for whoever says it after every prayer, and it is: O He Who is not distracted by one hearing from another, and O He Who is not misled by questions, and O He Who is not tired of the importunity of the importunate, let me taste the coolness of Your pardon and the sweetness of Your forgiveness. He also mentioned from Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, in this very supplication something similar to what was mentioned from Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, in hearing it from Al-Khidr. He also mentioned the meeting of Elias with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. If it is permissible for Elias to have remained until the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then it is permissible for Al-Khidr to have remained. It has been mentioned that they would meet at the House every year, and that when they parted they would say: “Whatever God wills, whatever God wills. None can avert evil except God. Whatever God wills, whatever God wills. Whatever blessing there is is from God. Whatever God wills, whatever God wills. I put my trust in God. God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.” As for the story of Elias, it will come in Al-Saffat, God willing. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr mentioned in the book Al-Tamhid on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) died and was covered with a garment, a voice called from the direction of the house. They heard his voice but did not see his person: “Peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of God, peace be upon you, O people of the house. Every soul will taste death” - the verse - “In God there is a replacement for every lost one, a substitute for every lost one, and consolation for every calamity. So trust in God, and be happy with Him, for the one who is afflicted is the one who is deprived of reward.” So they thought that he was Al-Khidr (peace and blessings of God be upon him), meaning the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The definite article in his statement on the earth is for the covenant, not for the species. It is the land of the Arabs, as evidenced by their movement in and towards it, mostly, but not the land of Gog and Magog. The farthest reaches of the islands of India and Sindh are places whose name does not ring a bell, and whose knowledge is not known. And there is no answer about the Antichrist. Al-Suhayli said: There is a great deal of disagreement about the name of Al-Khidr. Ibn Munabbih said: Abliya bin Malkan bin Faligh bin Shalih bin Arfakhshad bin Sam bin Noah. It was said: He is the son of Amil bin Samaqhin bin Aria bin Alqama bin Esau bin Isaac, and that his father was a king, and that his mother was the daughter of Persia and her name was Alma, and that she gave birth to him in a cave, and that he found there a sheep suckling him every day from the sheep of a man from the village, so the man took him and raised him, and when he grew up, the king - his father - asked for a scribe and gathered the people of knowledge and nobility to write the scrolls that were revealed to Abraham and Seth, and among the scribes who came to him was his son Al-Khidr, and he did not know him, so when he admired his handwriting and knowledge, and searched for the truth of his matter, he knew that he was his son, so he took him to himself and put him in charge of the people, then Al-Khidr fled from the kingship for reasons that would take too long to mention until he found the spring of life and drank from it, so he is alive until the Antichrist comes out, and he is the man whom the Antichrist will kill and cut up, then God Almighty will revive him. It was said: He did not live to see the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and this is not correct. Al-Bukhari and a group of the people of hadith, including our Sheikh Abu Bakr Ibn al-Arabi, may God Almighty have mercy on him, said: He died before the end of the hundred years, based on his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: Until the beginning of a hundred years, no one will remain on this earth from those who are on it, meaning whoever was alive when he said this statement. I said: We have mentioned this hadith and discussed it, and we have explained the life of Al-Khidr until now, and God knows best. Fifth: It was said: When Al-Khidr went to leave Moses, Moses said to him: Give me advice. He said: Be smiling and do not laugh, and leave obstinacy, and do not walk without need, and do not burden the sinners with their sins, and weep over your sin, O son of Imran.
18:83: The Almighty said: "And they ask you about Dhul-Qarnayn. Say, 'I will recite to you a report about him.'" Ibn Ishaq said: And the story of Dhul-Qarnayn was that he was given what no one else was given, so the means were extended to him until he reached the countries to the east and west of the earth, and he did not step on a land except that he had power over its people, until he reached the east and the west to what was beyond him of creation. Ibn Ishaq said: Someone who narrates hadiths from the non-Arabs told me about what they inherited from the knowledge of Dhul-Qarnayn that Dhul-Qarnayn was from the people of Egypt, his name was Marzban bin Mardaba the Greek, from the descendants of Yunan bin Yafith bin Noah. Ibn Hisham said: His name was Alexander, and he was the one who built Alexandria, so it was named after him. Ibn Ishaq said: Thawr bin Yazid told me on the authority of Khalid bin Ma'dan Al-Kila'i - and Khalid was a man who had met the people - "that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about Dhul-Qarnayn, so he said: A king wiped the earth from beneath it with the means.” Khalid said: Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, heard a man saying: O Dhul-Qarnayn, so he said: O God, forgive me! Were you not satisfied to be named after the names of the prophets, so you named yourselves after the names of the angels! Ibn Ishaq said: God knows which of them it was. Did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say that or not? And what he said is true. I said: It has been narrated from Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, similar to what Omar said, he heard a man calling another, O Dhul-Qarnayn, so Ali said: Is it not enough for you to name yourself with the names of prophets, so you also name yourself with the names of angels! And from him that he was a righteous slave king with a kasra on the lam who advised God and He supported him. And it was said: He was a prophet sent by whom God Almighty conquered the earth. And Al-Daraqutni mentioned in the Book of report that an angel called Rabaqeel used to descend upon Dhul-Qarnayn, and that angel is the one who will fold the earth on the Day of Resurrection, and will destroy it so that the feet of all creation will fall in the wakefulness, according to what some scholars have mentioned. Al-Suhayli said: This is similar to his being entrusted with Dhul-Qarnayn who cut across the earth from east to west, just as the story of Khalid bin Sinan in subjugating fire to him is similar to the state of the angel entrusted with it, who is Malik, peace be upon him and all the angels together. Ibn Abi Khaithama mentioned in his book Al-Bid’a Khalid bin Sinan Al-Absi and mentioned his prophethood, and mentioned that Malik, the keeper of Hell, was assigned to him from the angels. One of the signs of his prophethood was that a fire called the Fire of Al-Hadathan used to come out to the people from a cave and consume them and they could not stop it, so Khalid bin Sinan stopped it and it did not come out after that. There is a great deal of disagreement about the name of Dhul-Qarnayn and the reason for which he was called that. As for his name, it was said that he is Alexander the Greek Macedonian king, and his qaf is stressed and it is said: the Macedonian. It was also said that his name is Hermes. It was also said that his name is Herdis. Ibn Hisham said that he is Al-Sa’b bin Dhi Yazan Al-Himyari from the descendants of Wa’il bin Himyar. The statement of Ibn Ishaq was mentioned above. Wahb bin Munabbih said that he is Roman. Al-Tabari mentioned a hadith from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: "That Dhul-Qarnayn was a young man from the Romans." This is a hadith with a weak chain of transmission, Ibn Atiyyah said. Al-Suhayli said: What appears from the science of report is that they are two: One of them was during the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, and it is said that he is the one who ruled in favor of Abraham, peace be upon him, when they brought their case before him in Bir al-Saba’ in Ash-Sham. The other was close to the time of Jesus, peace be upon him. It was said that he was Afridun, who killed Bayurasp bin Arundasp, the tyrannical king, during the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, or some time before that. As for the difference in the reason for which he was named, it was said that he had two braids of hair, so he was named after them, as mentioned by al-Tha’labi and others. Braids are the horns of the head, and from this is the saying of the poet: I kissed her mouth, taking hold of her horns, and drank the bleeding with the cold water of the trough. It was said: He saw in the beginning of his kingdom as if he was holding the two horns of the sun, so he narrated that, and it was interpreted that he would overcome what the sun scattered upon him, so he was called Dhul-Qarnayn. It was also said: He was called that because he reached the west and the east, so it was as if he had captured the two horns of the world. A group said: When he reached the rising of the sun, he revealed its horns by vision, so he was called Dhul-Qarnayn, or the two horns of the devil in it. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He had two horns under his turban. Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali, may God be pleased with him, about Dhul-Qarnayn, was he a prophet or a king? He said: Neither this nor that, he was a righteous servant who called his people to God Almighty, so they wounded him on his horn, then he called them, so they wounded him on his other horn, so he was called Dhul-Qarnayn. They also differed about the time of his reign, some said: It was after Moses. Some said: It was during the period after Jesus. It was said: It was during the time of Abraham and Ishmael. Al-Khidr, peace be upon him, was the bearer of his greatest standard, and we have mentioned him in (Al-Baqarah). In short, God Almighty empowered him and made him king, and kings submitted to him. It was narrated that all the kings of the entire world are four: two believers and two unbelievers. The two believers are Solomon bin David and Alexander, and the unbelievers are Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar. A fifth will rule from this nation, according to the Almighty’s saying: That He may make him prevail over all religions. He is the Mahdi. It has been said that he was called Dhul-Qarnayn because he was of noble descent from a noble family on both sides of his father and mother. It has also been said that two centuries of people became extinct during his time while he was alive. It has also been said that when he fought, he fought with both his hands and his stirrups. It has also been said that he was given knowledge of the apparent and the hidden. It has also been said that he entered darkness and light. It has also been said that he was the king of Persia and Rome.
18:84: The Almighty said: Indeed, We established him in the land. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: The clouds were made subservient to him, the means were extended for him, and the light was spread out for him, so that night and day were the same for him. And in the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir, "The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to some men from the People of the Book who asked him about Dhul-Qarnayn, so he said: His first command was that he was a young Roman slave who was given a kingdom. He traveled until he reached the land of Egypt and built a city there called Alexandria. When he finished, a king came to him and took him up. He said to him, Look at what is beneath you. He said, I see my city alone, I see nothing else. The king said to him, “That is the entire land, and this darkness that you see surrounding it is the sea. God Almighty only wanted to show you the land and He has given you authority over it. So travel through the land and teach the ignorant and establish the knowledgeable.” God the Almighty said: And We gave him from every thing a cause. Ibn Abbas said: From every thing knowledge that leads to what he wants. Al-Hasan said: A means to reach where he wants. It was also said: From every thing that creation needs. It was also said: From every thing that kings seek help from, such as conquering cities and subduing enemies. The root of the word cause is the rope, so it was used as a metaphor for everything that leads to something.
18:85: Fata'aba'a sabe'an Ibn 'Aamer read Fata'aba'a sabe'an with its connection, meaning he followed one of the reasons that he was given. Al-Akhfash said: I followed him and I followed him with the same meaning, like I rode behind him and I rode behind him, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: Except for he who snatches a snatch, then a piercing flame pursues him. And from this is the following in speech, like hasan bisna' and qubi shaqih. Al-Nahhas said: Abu Ubaid chose the reading of the people of Kufa, he said: Because it is from the journey, and he and Al-Asma'i narrated that it is said: he followed him and followed him if he walked and did not catch up with him, and he followed him if he caught up with him, Abu Ubaid said: And similar to it is Fata'aba'ahum mashriqan Al-Nahhas said: And this distinction, even though Al-Asma'i narrated it, is not acceptable except with a reason or evidence. And the saying of God the Almighty: Fata'aba'ahum mashriqan is not in the hadith that they caught up with them, but rather the hadith is: When Moses, peace be upon him, and his companions came out of the sea and Pharaoh and his companions came, the sea closed over them. The truth in this is that to follow, to be followed, and to follow are languages that have the same meaning, which is to walk. It may be possible for it to be accompanied by a catch-up or not.
18:86: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he found it setting in a spring of murky water. [Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr and Ibn Amir], Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read Hamiyyah meaning hot. The rest read Hamiyyah meaning with a lot of murky water, which is black mud. You say: The well became murky with murky water with a sukoon if you removed its murky water. The well became murky with murky water, which is Hamiyyah from murky water, so the hamza was lightened and changed to a ya'. The two readings may be combined and it may be said: It was hot and had murky water. Abdullah bin Amr said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at the sun when it set and said: The blazing fire of God. Were it not for the command of God that restrains it, it would have burned everything on the earth. Ibn Abbas said: My father taught me to read it as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught it: in a hot spring. Muawiyah said: It is hot. Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas said: Then I am with the Commander of the Faithful. So they appointed Ka’b as a judge between them and said: O Ka’b, how do you find this in the Torah? He said: I find it setting in a black spring. Ibn Abbas agreed. The poet, who was Tubba’ Al-Yamani, said: Before me, Dhul-Qarnayn was a Muslim king to whom kings would submit and prostrate. He reached the West and the East, seeking the means of command from a wise guide. He saw the setting of the sun at sunset in the spring of Dhi Khalab and Thaat Harmad. Al-Khalb: Mud. Al-Tha’at: Mud. Al-Haramd: Black. Al-Qaffal said: Some scholars said: What is meant is not that he reached the sun, both in the west and the east, until he reached its center and touched it, because it revolves with the sky around the earth without sticking to the earth, and it is too large to enter any spring on earth, rather it is many times larger than the earth. Rather, what is meant is that he reached the end of the building from the west and the east, and he found it, in the opinion of the eye, setting in a muddy spring, just as we see it on smooth earth as if it is entering the earth. For this reason, he said: He found it rising on a people for whom We had not made any covering from it. He did not mean that it rose on them by touching them and sticking to them, rather he meant that they were the first ones on whom it rose. Al-Qutbi said: It is possible that this spring is from the sea, and it is possible that the sun sets behind it, with it, or at it, so the letter of description takes the place of its companion, and God knows best. And he found there a people meaning at the spring, or at the end of the spring, and they are the people of Jabris, and it is called in Syriac: Jirjisa, and it is inhabited by a people from the descendants of Thamud, the rest of whom believed in Salih, mentioned by Al-Suhayli. Wahb bin Munabbih said: Dhul-Qarnayn was a Roman man, the son of an old woman from among their old women who had no other children but him, and his name was Alexander. When he reached adulthood and was a righteous slave, God Almighty said: O Dhul-Qarnayn! I am sending you to the nations of the earth, and they are nations with different languages, and they are the nations of all the earth, and they are of different types: two nations between which is the entire length of the earth, and two nations between which is the entire width of the earth, and nations in the middle of the earth, including the jinn and mankind and Gog and Magog. As for the two between which is the length of the earth, one nation is at the setting of the sun and is called Nasik, and as for the other, it is at its rising and is called Mansak. As for the two between which is the width of the earth, one nation is in the right part of the earth and is called Hawil, and as for the other, which is in the left part of the earth, it is called Tawail. So Dhul-Qarnayn said: My God! You have called me to do a great matter that only You can estimate. So tell me about these nations: with what strength can I outnumber them? With what patience can I endure them? And in what language can I speak to them? How can I understand their language when I have no strength? Then God the Almighty said: I will make you victorious with what I have given you, I will expand your chest so that you hear everything, I will establish your understanding so that you will understand everything, I will clothe you with awe so that nothing will frighten you, and I will subject to you the light and the darkness so that they will be soldiers from your soldiers, the light will guide you from before you, and the darkness will protect you from behind you. When he was told that, he went with those who followed him, and he went to the nation that was at the setting of the sun, because it was the closest nation to him and it was an ascetic, and he found crowds that only God the Almighty could count, and strength and might that only God could bear, and different tongues, and scattered desires, so he outnumbered them with darkness, and he set up around them three armies of the soldiers of darkness as much as he surrounded them from every place, until he gathered them in one place, then he entered upon them with the light and called them to God the Almighty and to His worship, and some of them believed in Him and some of them disbelieved and turned away from Him, so he entered upon those who had taken the darkness as his allies and it covered them from every place, so it entered their mouths, noses, eyes, and houses.
