And they were overwhelmed from every side, so they were confused and raged and feared that they would perish, so they cried out to God Almighty with one voice: We believe, so He removed it from them, and took them by force, and they entered into His call, so He recruited from the people of the West great nations and made them one army, then he set out with them leading them, and the darkness drove them and guarded him from behind and the light in front of them led him and guided him, and he walked in the right side of the earth, seeking the nation in the right region of the earth, which is Hawil, and God Almighty made his hand, heart, mind and sight subservient, so he did not make a mistake when he did a work, so when they came to a ford or a sea, he built ships from small planks like sandals and arranged them in an hour, then he put in them all those with him from those nations, so when he crossed the seas and rivers, he split them and gave each man a plank so that he did not care about carrying it, so he reached Hawil and did with them as he did with a hermit, so they believed, so he finished with them, and took their armies and set out to the other side of the earth until he reached a hermitage at sunrise, so he worked in it and recruited From it, soldiers as he did in the first, then he returned until he took the left side of the earth, intending to interpret, and it is the nation that faces Hawil between them the width of the earth, so he did in it as he did in the previous one, then he turned to the nations in the middle of the earth from the jinn and mankind and Gog and Magog, and when he was on some of the way from the east of the Turks’ separation, a righteous nation from mankind said to him: O Dhul-Qarnayn! Indeed, between these two mountains there are many creatures of God’s creation, they are countless, and there is no resemblance to mankind among them, and they are like beasts, they eat grass, and prey on animals and wild animals as wild beasts prey on them, and they eat all the insects of the earth from snakes and scorpions and geckos and every living thing that God Almighty created on the earth, and God Almighty did not create their growth to grow in one year, so if the period is long they will fill the earth and expel its people, so shall we give you a tribute on condition that you build a dam between us and them? And he mentioned the hadith, and there will come from the description of Gog and Magog and the Turks, as they are a type of them, what is sufficient in it. God the Almighty said: We said, ‘O Dhul-Qarnayn!’ Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: If he was a prophet, then it is a revelation, and if he was not a prophet, then it is an inspiration from God the Almighty. Either you punish or you treat them with good. Ibrahim bin Al-Sarri said: He gave him the choice between these two as he gave Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, the choice when he said: Then if they come to you, then judge between them or turn away from them, and the like. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that God the Almighty gave him the choice between these two judgments. Al-Nahhas said: Ali bin Sulayman responded to his statement, because it is not authentic that Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet and would be addressed with this, so how could he say to his Lord, the Almighty: Then he will be returned to his Lord? And how could he say: Then We will punish him, and be addressed with the letter nun? He said: The meaning is, we said, O Muhammad, they said, O Dhul-Qarnayn. Abu Ja`far Al-Nahhas said: What Abu Al-Hasan said does not necessitate anything. As for his saying: We said, ‘O Dhul-Qarnayn,’ it is possible that God Almighty addressed him through the tongue of a prophet at his time, and it is possible that He said this to him as He said to His prophet: Then either a favor from Us afterwards or a ransom. As for the problem of Then We will punish him, then he will be returned to his Lord, its meaning is that when God Almighty gave him the choice between killing in His Almighty saying: Either you punish and keeping him alive in His Almighty saying: Or you take good care of them.
18:87: He said to those al-Nas 114:As for he among you who has wronged, that is, persisted in disbelief, We will punish him, that is, by killing him, then he will be returned to his Lord, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment, that is, severely in Hell.
18:88: And as for he who believed meaning repented from disbelief, and did righteousness Ahmad bin Yahya said: That is in the accusative case in Either you punish or you take good treatment of them He said: If it had been raised, it would have been correct with the meaning of either, as he said: So go, either to fulfill a need or to find a good and friendly resting place. Falha jaz' al-husna is the reading of the people of Medina, Abu Amr and Asim. Falha jaz' al-husna is in the nominative case as a subject or as a fixed sentence. Al-husna is in the accusative case as an addition and the tanween is deleted for the addition, meaning he has the reward of al-husna with God the Most High in the Hereafter, which is Paradise. So he added the reward to Paradise, like his saying: the truth of certainty and to the abode of the Hereafter, as al-Farraa said. It is possible that he means by al-husna the righteous deeds. It is possible that the reward is from Dhul-Qarnayn, meaning I give it to him and favor him. It is permissible to delete the tanween due to the meeting of two quiescent letters and al-husna is in the nominative case as a substitute according to the Basrans, and according to the translation according to the Kufians. According to this, Ibn Abi Ishaq read Falha jaz' al-husna except that you did not delete the tanween, and it is better. The rest of the Kufians read Falha jaz' al-husna in the accusative case with the tanween, meaning he has the reward of al-husna. Al-Farraa said: Jaz' is in the accusative case as a distinction. It was said: on the source, and Al-Zajjaj said: it is a source in the place of the state, meaning rewarding it with a reward. Ibn Abbas and Masruq read fa lahu jazā’ al-husna in the accusative case without a tanween. According to Abu Hatim, it is on the deletion of the tanween due to the meeting of two quiescent letters like fa lahu jazā’ al-husna in one of the two faces. Al-Nahhas: This according to others is a mistake because it is not a place for deleting the tanween due to the meeting of two quiescent letters, and its estimation would be: fa lahu al-thawaab jazā’ al-husna.
18:89: The Almighty’s saying: Then he followed a way. The meaning of followed was previously mentioned, and followed has the same meaning, that is, he took a path and stations.
18:90: Until it reached the rising of the sun. Mujahid and Ibn Muhaisin read it with the opening of the meem and the lam. It is said: The sun and the planets rose, rising and rising. The rising and rising are also the place of its rising, said Al-Jawhari. The meaning is that it reached the place of a people between whom and the rising of the sun there was no one from the people. The sun rises far beyond that, so this is the meaning of the Almighty's saying: He found it rising on a people. There is disagreement about them. Wahb ibn Munabbih said what was mentioned above, and that it is a nation called Mansak, which is the opposite of Nasik, and Muqatil said the same. Qatada said: They are called Zanj. Al-Kalbi said: They are Taris, Hawil, and Mansak, barefoot, naked, blind to the truth, copulating like dogs, and fighting like donkeys. It was said: They are the people of Jabaliq, and they are from the descendants of the believers of Aad who believed in Hud, and they are called Marqisa in Syriac. Those at the setting of the sun are the people of Jabris, and each of the two cities has ten thousand gates, between every two gates is a farsakh. Behind Jabliq are nations, namely Tafil and Tars, and they are neighbors of Gog and Magog. The people of Jabris and Jabliq believed in the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He passed by them on the Night Journey and called them, but they responded. He called the other nations, but they did not respond. Al-Suhayli mentioned this and said: I have summarized all of this from a long hadith narrated by Muqatil ibn Hayyan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. At-Tabari narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable back to Muqatil, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: We have not made for them any covering besides it meaning a veil to protect themselves from it when it rises. Qatada said: There was no covering between them and the sun. They were in a place where no building could be built, and they would be in groups until the sun had set and they would return to their livelihoods and fields. That is, they would not protect themselves from it in a mountain cave or a house to protect themselves from it. Umayya said: I found men in Samarkand talking to people. One of them said: I went out until I passed China, and it was said to me: There is a day and a night’s journey between you and them. So I hired a man to show them to me until I came to them in the morning. I found one of them spreading out one ear and covering himself with the other, and my companion spoke well to them. So we spent the night with them, and they said: Why have you come? We said: We came to see how the sun rises, and while we were like that we heard a sound like a clanging sound, so I fainted, then I regained consciousness and they were anointing me with oil, and when the sun rose over the water it was like oil, and the edge of the sky was like a tent, so when it rose they brought me into their flock, and when the day rose and the sun declined over their heads they went out to catch fish and throw them in the sun to cook. Ibn Jurayj said: An army came to them once, and the people said to them: The sun will not rise while you are in it, so they said: We will not leave until the sun rises. Then they said: What are these bones? They said: By God, these are the bones of an army upon which the sun rose here and they died. He said: So they turned and fled into the land. Al-Hasan said: Their land had no mountains or trees, and it could not support a building, so when the sun rose over them they would go down into the water, and when it rose above them they would go out, and they would graze like animals.
18:91: I said: These statements indicate that there is no city there. And God knows best. Perhaps some of them entered the river, and some of them entered the stream, so there is no contradiction between the statement of Al-Hasan and Qatada.
18:92: God Almighty said: Then he followed a way.
18:93: Until, when he reached between the two dams which are two mountains on the side of Armenia and Azerbaijan. He found beyond them meaning behind them: a people who could hardly understand a word. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read yafqhoo with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the qaf from afqa if it made clear, meaning they could not understand speech other than themselves. The rest read it with a fatha on the ya' and the qaf, meaning they knew. Both readings are correct, so they did not understand anyone other than themselves nor did anyone else understand them.
18:94: The Almighty said: "They said, 'O Dhul-Qarnayn,' meaning a righteous nation of mankind said to him: 'Indeed, Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land.'" Al-Akhfash said: Whoever hamzates Ya'juj and makes the two alifs from the root says: Ya'juj yaf'ul and Majuj maf'ul as if it is from ajij an-Nar. He said: Whoever does not hamzate and makes the two alifs extra says: Ya'juj from Yajjat and Majuj from Majjat and they are not declined. Ru'bah said: If Gog and Magog were together and returned and sought help accordingly Al-Jawhari mentioned it. It was said: The reason they are not declined is because they are two foreign names, like Talut and Goliath, which are not derived, and their reasons for preventing inflection are foreignness, definiteness, and femininity. A group said: It is an Arabized word from aj and ajjaj, and its reasons for preventing inflection are definiteness and femininity. Abu Ali said: It is possible that they are both Arabic. Whoever hamzas Yajuj Gog and Gog then it is on the weight of yaf’ul like yarbu’, from your saying ajat an-nar fire meaning it was lit, and from it is ajij heated, and from it is salt malah ajaj bitter salt. Whoever does not hamza, it is possible that he lightened the hamza and changed it to an alif like ra’s ra’s. As for Majuj, it is a maf’ul from aj, and the two words are from the same root in derivation. Whoever does not hamza, it is possible that he lightened the hamza, and it is possible that it is fa’ul from maj, and the inflection was left in them for femininity and definiteness as if it were the name of a tribe. There is a difference of opinion about their corruption. Sa’id bin Abdul Aziz said: Their corruption is eating the son of Adam. A group said: Their corruption was expected, meaning they would cause corruption, so they sought a way to guard against them. A group said: Their corruption is injustice, oppression, killing, and all other forms of corruption known to mankind, and God knows best. There are reports about their description, their exodus, and that they are the sons of Japheth. Abu Hurairah narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Shem, Ham and Japheth were born to Noah. Shem gave birth to the Arabs, the Persians and the Romans, and among them were good. Japheth gave birth to Gog and Magog, the Turks and the Slavs, and among them were no good. Ham gave birth to the Copts, the Berbers and the Sudanese.” Ka’b al-Ahbar said: Adam, peace be upon him, had a wet dream and his water mixed with the dust, so he was sorry, and they were created from that water. They are connected to us through the father’s side, not the mother’s side. This is questionable, because the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them, do not have wet dreams, but rather they are from the children of Japheth. This is also what Muqatil and others said. Abu Sa’id al-Khudri narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that he said: Not a single one of them will die until a thousand men are born to his loins. Meaning Gog and Magog. Abu Saeed said: They are twenty-five tribes behind Gog and Magog. Not a single one of these or Gog and Magog will die until a thousand men are born to his loins. This was mentioned by Al-Qushayri. Abdullah bin Masoud said: I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Gog and Magog, and he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Gog and Magog are two nations, each nation is four hundred thousand nations, each nation the number of which is known only to God. No man among them dies until a thousand males are born to him from his loins, all of whom have taken up arms. It was said: O Messenger of God, describe them to us. He said: They are three types, one type of them is like the cedar - a tree in the Levant, the height of the tree is one hundred and twenty cubits - and one type is the same in width and length, about an arm's length, and one type spreads out one ear and covers itself with the other, they do not pass by an elephant, a wild animal, or a pig except that they eat it and they eat whoever dies from them, their vanguard is in the Levant and their rear guard is in Khorasan, they drink the rivers of the East and the Sea of Galilee, and God bestows blessings from Mecca, Medina, and Jerusalem. And Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: And another type of them is a span's length, they have the claws and fangs of wild beasts, the call of doves, the mating of beasts, the howling of wolves, and hair that protects them from the heat and the cold, and large ears, one of which is fur in which they spend the winter, and the other is skin in which they spend the summer, they dig the dam until they almost pierce it, then God restores it to how it was, and they say: We will pierce it tomorrow, God willing, so they pierce it and go out, and the people fortify themselves in the fortresses, they shoot to the sky and the arrow returns to them stained with blood, then God Almighty destroys them with the scum in Their necks. Al-Ghaznawi mentioned it. Ali said about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Gog and Magog are a nation with four hundred princes, and so is Magog. None of them will die until he sees a thousand knights from his descendants.” I said: It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, and it was included by Ibn Majah in Al-Sunan. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Gog and Magog dig every day until they almost see the rays of the sun. The one who is over them says, ‘Go back, you will dig it again tomorrow.’ So God will make it even more intense than it was before, until their time has come and God Almighty wants to send them against the people. They dig until they almost see the rays of the sun. He says, ‘Go back, you will dig it again tomorrow, God willing.’ So they make an exception and return to it as it was when they left it. They dig it and come out to the people and dry up the water, and the people fortify themselves against them in their forts. They shoot their arrows towards the sky, and the blood that they have preserved returns to them, and they say, ‘We have subdued the people of the earth and overcome the people of the heavens.’ So God Almighty sends upon them a gnat in their napes and kills them with it.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose hand is my soul, the beasts of the earth grow fat and are grateful for their meat. Al-Jawhari said: The she-camel is grateful, and she is grateful, and the udder is full of milk. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Dhul-Qarnayn saw them, and the height of each one of them was like half of a square man among us. They had claws in the place of nails, molars and fangs like those of wild beasts, and jaws like those of camels. They were covered with a thick layer of hair that covered them, and each one of them had two large ears, one of which he would cover himself with and the other would lie flat on his back. Each one of them had known his appointed time and would not die until a thousand men had emerged from his loins if he was a male, and a thousand females had emerged from his womb if she was a female. Al-Suddi and Al-Dahhak said: The Turks were a group of Gog and Magog who went out to attack, then Dhul-Qarnayn came and struck the dam, so they remained on this side. Al-Suddi said: The dam was built on twenty-one tribes, and one tribe remained from them below the dam, so they were the Turks. Qatada said the same. I said: If this is the case, then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, described the Turks as he described Gog and Magog, saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: The Hour will not come until the Muslims fight the Turks, a people whose faces are like hammered shields, who wear hair and walk in hair. In another narration, They wear hair shoes. Narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud, and others. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, knew their number, their great number, and the strength of their power, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Leave the Turks as long as they leave you.” At that time, nations emerged from them that none can count except God Almighty, and none can repel them from the Muslims except God Almighty, until they were like Gog and Magog or their vanguard. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Bakra that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “People from my nation will settle in a place called Basra, near a river called Tigris, which will have a bridge over it. Its people will be numerous and it will be one of the cities of the immigrants.” Ibn Yahya said: Abu Muammar said: “It will be one of the cities of the Muslims. When it is the end of time, the Banu Qantura will come with broad faces and small eyes until they settle on the bank of the river. Its people will be divided into three groups: one group will take the tails of cows and wild animals and will perish; one group will take them for themselves and will disbelieve; and one group will put their children behind their backs and fight them and they will be the martyrs.” The place of the land is the quiet place. Basra is the soft rocks and it was named after it. The Banu Qantura are the Turks. It is said that Qantura is the name of a slave girl who belonged to Abraham, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and she bore him children and the Turks came from their lineage. The Almighty’s saying: Shall we then assign you a tribute on condition that you place a barrier between us and them? There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: Shall We then make for you a tax? is a question for the sake of good manners. Kharj means made. It was also read Kharaj, and Kharj is more specific than Kharaj. It is said: Add Kharaj, your head, and the tax of your city. Al-Azhari said: Kharaj refers to the tax, and it refers to the spoils of war, and it refers to the poll tax, and the yield. Kharaj is the name for what is taken from the obligatory duties in the money. Kharj is the source. The Almighty’s saying: On the condition that you make between us and them a barrier means a filling, and filling is what is placed one part on top of the other until it is connected. And a garment is patched, said Al-Harawi. It is said: I filled the hole, I filled it with a broken filling, meaning I blocked it. Raddm is also the name, and it is the dam. It was said: Raddm is more expressive than Sadd, if the dam is everything that is blocked with, and Raddm is placing something on something else, such as stones, dirt, or the like, until a strong veil is formed from that. From this, Raddum is his garment if he patched it with dense patches, one on top of the other. And from it is the saying of Antarah: Did the poets leave the ruins? Any of the words that are compounded on top of each other. It was read Sada with a fatha on the seen, so Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: Damm is the noun and fathah is the source. Al-Kisa'i said: Fathah and Damm are two languages with one meaning. Ikrimah, Abu Amr ibn Al-Ala' and Abu Ubaidah said: Whatever was created by God and no one participated in it with work is with Damm, and whatever was made by humans is with Fathah. The people of this opinion are required to read Sada with Fathah, and before it Bayn Al-Sadayn with Damm, and this is the reading of Hamza and Al-Kisa'i. Abu Hatim said on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah the opposite of what Abu Ubaidah said. Ibn Abi Ishaq said: Whatever your eyes saw is Sadd with Damm, and whatever you do not see is Sadd with Fathah. Second: This verse is evidence of the establishment of prisons, the confinement of corrupt people in them, and preventing them from doing what they want. They are not left as they are, but rather they are beaten severely and imprisoned or bailed and released, as Omar, may God be pleased with him, did.
18:95: The Almighty’s saying: “He said: What my Lord has established me in is better.” There are two issues in this. The first is the Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘What my Lord has empowered me with is better.’ The meaning is that Dhul-Qarnayn said to them: What God has extended of power and dominion is better than your provisions and your wealth, but help me with the strength of your bodies, meaning with men and work from among you with your bodies, and the tools with which I will build the dam, which is the dam. This is support from God Almighty for Dhul-Qarnayn in this dialogue, because if the people had gathered provisions for him, no one would have helped him and they would have left him to build, and helping him with themselves is more beautiful for him and will speed up the completion of this work, and perhaps what they mentioned to him is greater than the provisions. Ibn Kathir alone read ma makkanni with two noons. The rest read ma makkanni what my Lord has empowered me with. Second: In this verse there is evidence that the king was obligated to protect the creation by preserving their integrity, closing their gaps, and repairing their breaches, from their wealth that comes to them as spoils, and their rights that their treasury collects under his hand and supervision, even if the rights eat it up, and the provisions run it out, it is upon them to make up for that from their wealth, and he is obligated to look after them well, and that is with three conditions: First: He does not monopolize anything from them. Second: He begins with those in need and helps them. Third: That they should be given equally among themselves according to their status. If it is exhausted after this and remains empty, and events bring about something, they will give their lives before their wealth. If that does not suffice, then their wealth will be taken from them according to an estimate and spent with management. When they offered Dhul-Qarnayn money to suffice them from what they feared from the aggression of Gog and Magog, he said: I do not need it, but I need you. So help me with strength, meaning serve with yourselves with me, for the wealth is with me and the men are with you. He saw that the wealth would not suffice them, for if he took it as a wage, that would decrease what he needed, so the wage would return to them. So volunteering to serve bodies was more appropriate. The rule of the matter is that no one’s wealth is permissible except in the event of a necessity that arises, so that money is taken openly, not secretly, and it is spent with justice, not with monopolization, and with the opinion of the group, not with tyranny in the matter. And God Almighty is the guide to what is right.
18:96: The Almighty said: Bring me the iron sheets meaning give me the iron sheets and hand them over. He ordered them to carry the tool, and all of this is only a request for a gift that does not mean a gift, but rather a request for handing over, because it has been connected to his saying: He will not take the saddle from them, so all that remains is a request for handing over, and the works of the bodies. The iron sheets are pieces of iron. The root of the word is gathering, and from it is the lion's coat of hair that has gathered on its shoulder. And I wrote the book, meaning I wrote it and gathered its letters. Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal read Radma aituni from the coming which is the arrival, meaning bring me the iron sheets, so when the preposition was dropped, the verb was erected in the manner of the poet's saying: I ordered you to do good... The preposition was deleted, so the verb was placed in the accusative case. The majority read Zabar with a fatha on the ba’. Al-Hasan read it with a damma on it. All of that is the plural of zabra, which is a large piece of it. The Almighty said: Until when it was level meaning the building, so it was omitted because the speech was too strong for it. Between the two mountainsides Abu Ubaidah said: They are the two sides of the mountain, and they were called that because they meet, that is, because they meet. Al-Zuhri and Ibn Abbas said the same, as if he was ignoring the other, from the two mountainsides. The poet said: Both shells are pierced by her light, lighting up like a lamp in the dark. A tall building is called a sadaf, likening it to the side of a mountain. In the hadith: If he passed by a sloping sadaf, he would walk quickly. Abu Ubaid said: Sadaf and goal are every great, high building. Ibn Atiyyah: Sadafan are two mountains facing each other. One is not called Sadaf, but rather Sadafan is said for two, because one of them faces the other. Nafi, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read Al-Sadafayn with a fatha on the sad and a shaddah on it and a fatha on the dal. This is the reading of Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, and it is the choice of Abu Ubaidah because it is the most famous language. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir and Ibn Amr read Al-Sadafayn with a damma on the sad and the dal. Asim read Abu Bakr’s narration Al-Sadafayn with a damma on the sad and a sukoon on the dal, like Al-Jarf and Al-Jarf. It is a lightening. Ibn Al-Majishun read it with a fatha on the sad and a damma on the dal. Qatada read Bayn Al-Sadafayn with a fatha on the sad and a sukoon on the dal, and all of that has the same meaning, which is the two mountains facing each other. God the Almighty said: He said, ‘Blow,’ to the end of the verse, meaning on the iron slabs with bellows. This is because he would order a tray of slabs and stones to be placed, then firewood and coal would be lit on it with bellows until it became hot. When iron was lit, it would become like fire. This is what God the Almighty said: Until, when He made it a fire. Then molten copper, lead, or iron would be brought, according to the difference in the diameter, and he would pour it on that arranged tray. When it coalesced, it became strong and some parts stuck to others, he would start placing another tray again, until the flag was level and became a solid mountain. Qatada said: It is like inky hail, one part black and one part red. “It is narrated that a man came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God! I have seen the dam of Gog and Magog. He said: How did you see it? He said: I saw it like inky hail, with a yellow path, a red path, and a black path. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have seen it. The meaning of “until He made it a fire” is like a fire. The meaning of bring me molten copper is give me molten copper so that I may pour it on it, in an advancing and delaying manner. Whoever reads bring me then the meaning according to him is come, let me pour copper on it. According to most commentators, molten copper is molten copper, and its origin is from qatr, because when it is melted it liquefies as water liquefies. A group said: qatr is molten iron. A group including Ibn al-Anbari said: molten lead. It is derived from qatr, which liquefies qatr. And from it is And We made a spring of qatr flow for him (Saba’: 12).
18:97: The Almighty said: And they were not able to climb it meaning Gog and Magog were not able to climb it or ascend it, because it is smooth and level with the mountain, and the mountain is high and cannot be reached. The height of the dam is two hundred and fifty cubits. It was narrated: Its length between the two ends of the mountains is one hundred farsakhs, and its width is fifty farsakhs, said Wahb ibn Munabbih. And they were not able to tunnel through it because of its great width and strength. It was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Today, a hole was opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this. Wahb ibn Munabbih counted ninety in his hand - and in another narration - and made a circle with his thumb and the finger next to it, and he mentioned the hadith. Yahya ibn Salam mentioned on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi `Aruba on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Abu Rafi` on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Gog and Magog will breach the dam every day until, when they can almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them will say: ‘Go back, you will breach it tomorrow.’ But God will restore it to its worst state ever. When their time has come and God wants to send them against the people, they will dig until, when they can almost see the rays of the sun, the one who is over them will say: ‘Go back, you will dig it, God willing.’ So they will return to it as it was when they left it, so they will breach it and come out to the people.” The hadith has been mentioned previously. God the Almighty said: So they were not able with a light taa according to the reading of the majority. It was said: It is a language meaning they were able. It was said: Rather, they were able to do so, and it was common in the speech of the Arabs until some of them deleted the taa from it and said: ista'a. Some of them deleted the taa from it and said: ista'a yasti'a meaning he was able to do, and it is a well-known language. Hamza alone read So they were not able with a shaddah on the taa as if he meant they were able to do, then he assimilated the taa into the taa and stressed it, and it is a weak reading, Abu Ali said: It is not permissible. Al-A'mash read Fama itaqatawa antuharuhu wa ma itaqatawa lahu with the taa in both places.
18:98: The Almighty said: He said, 'This is a mercy from my Lord.' The speaker was Dhul-Qarnayn, and he indicated by this the dam, the strength over it, and the benefit of it in repelling the harm of Gog and Magog. Ibn Abi Ubla read This is a mercy from my Lord. The Almighty said: Then when the promise of my Lord comes meaning the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: the time of their emergence. He made it level meaning level with the ground. From this is the Almighty’s saying: When the earth is leveled (al-Fajr 89:21). Ibn Arafah said: meaning it is made level with no mounds in it. From this is the Almighty’s saying: He made it level. Al-Yazidi said: meaning level. It is said: a she-camel is dakaa if its hump is gone. Al-Qutbi said: meaning he made it crushed and stuck to the ground. Al-Kalbi said: in pieces, broken. He said: Did someone else destroy a cave and it collapsed? Al-Azhari said: It is said dakkatah, meaning you crushed it. Whoever reads daka’a means making the mountain into flat land, which is a hill that is not yet a mountain, and its plural is dakawat. Hamza, Asim, and Al-Kisa’i read daka’a with a long vowel, likening it to a she-camel that has no hump. There is an omission in the speech, the meaning of which is: He made it like daka’a, and this omission must be estimated, because the dam is masculine, so it cannot be described as daka’a. Whoever reads daka, it is the source of dakka yadaka, meaning to demolish and crush, and it is possible that ja’ala means to create. Dakka is placed in the accusative case as a state. Likewise, the accusative case in the reading of whoever extends it has two possible meanings.
18:99: The Almighty said: And We will leave some of them that Day surging against others. The pronoun in We will leave refers to God, the Almighty, meaning We will leave the jinn and mankind surging against each other on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: We will leave Gog and Magog on that Day meaning when the dam is complete surging against each other. The metaphor of the waves for them is an expression of confusion and hesitation among some of them, like those who are distracted by worry and fear, so He likened them to the waves of the sea that are agitated by some parts. It was also said: We will leave Gog and Magog on the day the dam is opened surging in the world, mixed up due to their great number. I said: These are three opinions, the most evident of which is the middle one, and the most distant of which is the last one. The first is good, because the Resurrection was mentioned earlier in the interpretation of the Almighty’s saying: So when the promise of my Lord comes to pass. And God knows best. The Almighty’s saying: And the Trumpet will be blown was mentioned previously in Al-An’am. “Then We will gather them together” meaning the jinn and mankind on the Day of Resurrection.
18:100: And We shall present Hell meaning, We shall make it visible to them. On that Day, to the disbelievers, presented.
18:101: Those whose eyes is in the accusative case as an adjective for the disbelievers. "In a cover from My remembrance" meaning they are like someone whose eyes are covered so he does not see the signs of God Almighty. "And they were unable to hear" meaning they were unable to hear the words of God Almighty, so they are like someone who is deaf.
18:102: The Almighty said: Do those who disbelieve think? That is, do they think? Ali, Ikrimah, Mujahid, and Ibn Muhaisin read Afhasab with a sukoon on the seen and a damma on the ba', meaning it is sufficient for them. To take My servants meaning Jesus, the angels, and Ezra. Besides Me as protectors and that I will not punish them, so there is an omission in the speech. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, do they think that this will benefit them? Indeed, We have prepared Hell for the disbelievers as an accommodation.
18:103: The Almighty’s saying: “Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds?” to His saying: in weight. There are two issues in it: First: The Almighty’s statement: “Say: ‘Shall We inform you of the greatest losers as to [their] deeds?’” - the verse - indicates that among the people are those who do deeds while thinking that they are doing good, but their efforts have been in vain. What causes the efforts to be in vain is either corruption of belief or hypocrisy, and what is meant here is disbelief. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Mus’ab who said: I asked my father, Say, ‘Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds?’ Are they the Kharijites? He said, No, they are the Jews and the Christians. As for the Jews, they denied Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and as for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise, saying, There is no food or drink in it. The Kharijites are those who break God’s covenant after ratifying it, and Sa`d used to call them the wicked. The meaning of the verse is a rebuke, that is, say to these disbelievers who worshipped other than Me: Their efforts and hopes will be disappointed tomorrow, and they will be the biggest losers in their deeds.
18:104: They are those whose efforts have been lost in worldly life, while they think that they are doing well in worshipping someone other than Me. Ibn Abbas said: He means the disbelievers of Mecca. Ali said: They are the Khawarij of Harura. He said once: They are the monks who live in monasteries. It was narrated that Ibn al-Kawwa asked him about those who are the greatest losers in deeds, so he said to him: You and your companions. Ibn Atiyyah said: All of this is weakened by the statement of God after that: Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in the meeting with Him, so their deeds have become worthless. None of these groups disbelieve in God, in the meeting with Him, in the resurrection and the Hereafter. Rather, this is a description of the polytheists of Mecca who worship idols. Ali and Sa`d may God be pleased with them mentioned people who took their share of this verse. Actions is in the accusative case as a specification. Habatat is the reading of the majority with a kasra on the ba. Ibn Abbas read Habatat with a fatha on it.
18:105: Ibn Atiyyah said: All of this is weakened by the Almighty’s statement after that: Those are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord and in the meeting with Him, so their deeds have become worthless. None of these groups disbelieve in God, His meeting, the Resurrection, and the Hereafter. Rather, this is a description of the idolaters of Mecca. Ali and Sa`d, may God be pleased with them, mentioned people who took their share of this verse. Actions is an accusative of specification. Habatat is the reading of the majority with a kasra on the ba’. Ibn Abbas read Habatat with a fatha on it. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight. The majority of scholars read naqeem with the nun of majesty. Mujahid read it with the ya’ of the third person singular, meaning God Almighty will not establish. Ubayd ibn Umayr read fa-l-yawum and he must read wazn. Mujahid also read fa-l-yawum and wazn and likewise, Mujahid read and they will not establish on the Day of Resurrection any weight. Ubayd ibn Umayr said: The great, tall, gluttonous, drunk man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, but he will not weigh as much as a mosquito’s wing in God’s sight. I said: This is not said in terms of opinion, and its meaning has been proven in the two Sahihs of Bukhari and Muslim on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “A great, fat man will come on the Day of Resurrection, but he will not weigh as much as a mosquito’s wing in the sight of God. Read, if you wish, ‘We will not assign to them any weight on the Day of Resurrection.’” The meaning is that they will have no reward, and their deeds will be met with punishment. They will have no good deeds that will be weighed in the scales of the Day of Resurrection, and whoever has no good deeds will be in the Fire. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri said: Deeds will be brought like the mountains of Tihamah, but they will not weigh anything. It was said: It is possible that he meant a metaphor, as if he said: They will have no value with us on that day. And God knows best. In this hadith there is jurisprudence in blaming fat for those who burden themselves with it, because that involves burdening themselves with food and being preoccupied with it instead of doing good deeds. Rather, it indicates the prohibition of eating more than what is sufficient for the purpose of luxury and fat. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The most hated of men to God Almighty is the fat scholar. From the hadith of Imran bin Husayn, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: The best of you are my generation, then those who come after them - Imran said, and I do not know if he mentioned two or three generations after his generation - Then after you will be a people who bear witness but are not asked to bear witness, and they betray but are not trusted, and they make vows but do not fulfill them, and fatness will appear among them This is a blame. The reason for that is that fatness is acquired from eating too much and gluttony, and ease, comfort, security, and indulging oneself in its desires. So he is a slave to himself, not a slave to his Lord. Whoever is in this state will inevitably fall into what is forbidden, and every meat that is born from ill-gotten gains, the Fire is more deserving of it. God the Almighty has blamed the disbelievers for eating too much, saying: And those who disbelieve enjoy themselves and eat as cattle eat, and the Fire will be a residence for them So if the believer imitates them and enjoys their comforts in all his circumstances and times, then where is the reality of faith and the fulfillment of the duties of Islam?! And whoever eats and drinks a lot, his greed and greed increase, and his laziness and sleep increase at night, so his day is wandering and his night is sleeping. This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-A’raf, and the scale has been mentioned in it, and that it has two pans in which the records of deeds are weighed, so there is no point in repeating it. And he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said when they laughed at Hams, who cut the leg of Ibn Masoud while he was climbing the palm tree: You laugh at a leg that is weighed according to the deeds of the people of the earth. This indicates that people are weighed, as mentioned by Al-Ghaznawi.
18:106: The Almighty’s saying: That is their recompense. “That” is an indication of leaving the meter, and it is in the nominative case as a subject. Their recompense is its predicate, and Hell is a substitute for the subject, which is that. “What” in His saying: Because they disbelieved is a source, and mockery is belittling and ridicule, and it has been mentioned previously.
18:107: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging. Qatada said: Al-Firdaws is the highest, middle, highest, best, and most sublime part of Paradise. Abu Umamah Al-Bahili said: Al-Firdaws is the navel of Paradise. Ka'b said: There is no Paradise higher than Al-Firdaws, in which are those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever believes in God and His Messenger, establishes prayer, and fasts Ramadan, it is incumbent upon God to admit him into Paradise, whether he strives in the cause of God or stays in the land in which he was born.” They said: O Messenger of God, shall we not give people good report? He said: “In Paradise there are one hundred levels that God has prepared for those who strive in the cause of God. Between each level is like the distance between the heavens and the earth. So if you ask God, the Most High, then ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise - I think he said - and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it flow the rivers of Paradise.” Mujahid said: Al-Firdaws is a garden in Roman. Al-Farra’ is Arabic. Al-Firdaws is a garden in Paradise. Firdaws is the name of a meadow below Al-Yamamah. The plural is Firdaws. Umayyah ibn Abi Al-Salt Al-Thaqafi said: Their homes at that time were full of gardens, palm trees, and onions. Al-Faradis is a place in the Levant. And the word karam mufradis means a pergola.
18:108: Keeping it eternal means permanent. Not seeking to be transferred from it to another place. "Hawl" means to be transferred, as Abu Ali said. Al-Zajjaj said: A state of one's place is hawl, just as one says: "great greatness." He said: It is also possible that it is from "haylah", meaning they do not find a home other than it. Al-Jawhari said: "Hawl" means to move from one place to another, and the noun is hawl, and from it is the saying of God Almighty: "Keeping it eternal, not seeking to be transferred from it."
18:109: The Almighty said: "Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted." Nafad means that something is complete and emptied, and it has been mentioned before. Even if We brought the like of it as a supplement, meaning an increase over the sea in number or weight. In the Mushaf of Abi Madada, Mujahid, Ibn Muhaysin, and Hamid read it this way. Maddad is in the accusative case as a distinguishing feature or a state. Ibn Abbas said: The Jews said when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: And you have not been given of knowledge except a little, they said: How can that be when we have been given the Torah, and whoever has been given the Torah has been given much good? So the verse was revealed: "Say: If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted," and it was said: The Jews said: You have been given wisdom, and whoever has been given wisdom has been given much good, then you claimed that you have no knowledge of the spirit?! So God Almighty said: Say: Even if you have been given the Qur'an and you have been given the Torah, then they are little in comparison to the words of God Almighty. Ibn Abbas said: The words of my Lord meaning the sermons of my Lord. It was said: What he meant by words is the ancient speech that has no end or limit. Even though it is one, it is permissible to express it in the plural form because of the pearls of words it contains, and because it takes their place. So it is permissible to express it in the plural form for emphasis. Al-A’sha said: A pure, clear face adorned with good makeup and wrists So he used the word labbat to mean the core. In the revelation: We are your allies (Fussilat 41:31) and Indeed, it is We who sent down the message (al-Hijr 15:9) and Indeed, it is We who bring to life and cause to die (al-Hijr 15:23) and also Indeed, Abraham was a nation (Al-Naml: 120) because he took the place of a nation. It was said: meaning that the expressions and indications that indicate the meanings of the meanings of His speech, glory be to Him, have not been exhausted. Al-Suddi said: meaning that if the sea was ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be exhausted before the attributes of Paradise, which is the abode of reward, were exhausted. Ikrimah said: The sea would be exhausted before the reward of the one who said, There is no god but God was exhausted. Similar to this verse: And if all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea were replenished thereafter by seven more seas, the words of God would not be exhausted (Luqman 31:27). Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read before it was exhausted with the letter ya because the verb came before it.
18:110: God Almighty said: Say, ‘I am only a human being like you, to whom is revealed.’ That is, I do not know anything except what God Almighty teaches me, and God Almighty’s knowledge is innumerable. I was only commanded to inform you that there is no god but God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, that is, hopes to see Him and His reward and fears His punishment, let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Jundub bin Zuhair Al-Amiri, who said: O Messenger of God, I do the work for the sake of God Almighty, and I want the face of God Almighty, but if He sees it, it will please me. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God is good and does not accept anything but what is good and does not accept what you share in. So the verse was revealed. And Tawus said: A man said: O Messenger of God! I love jihad in the way of God Almighty and I love for him to see my place, so this verse was revealed.” Mujahid said: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God! I give charity and maintain family ties, and I do that only for the sake of God Almighty, and that is mentioned about me and I am praised for it, and that pleases me and pleases me. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent and did not say anything. Then God Almighty revealed: “So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.” I said: All of them are intended, and the verse includes all of that and other deeds. The authentic hadith of Abu Hurairah about the three who will be judged first among people has already been mentioned in Surah Hud. The discussion of hypocrisy has already been mentioned in Surah An-Nisa, and we have mentioned enough of the hadiths there. Al-Mawardi said: All of the scholars of interpretation said: The meaning of the Almighty’s statement: And he does not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord is that he does not show off his deeds to anyone. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim, may God have mercy on him, narrated in Nawadir Al-Usul that he said: My father, may God have mercy on him, told us: Makki bin Ibrahim told us: Abdul Wahid bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Ubadah bin Nassi, who said: I came to Shaddad bin Aws while he was praying and he was crying. I said: What made you cry, O Abu Abd al-Rahman? He said: It is a hadith that I heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) one day. When I saw something on his face that made me sad, I would say: May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God, what do I see on your face? He said: Something that I fear for my nation after me. I said: What is it, O Messenger of God? He said: Polytheism and hidden desire. I said: O Messenger of God! And will your nation associate partners with God after you? He said: O Shaddad, they do not worship the sun, the moon, a stone, or an idol, but they show off with their deeds. I said: Is showing off polytheism? He said: Yes. I said: What is hidden desire? He said: One of them goes to bed fasting and is exposed to worldly desires, so he breaks his fast. Abdul Wahid said: So I met Al-Hasan and said: O Abu Saeed! Tell me about showing off, is it polytheism? He said: Yes, don’t you read: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone. Ismail bin Ishaq narrated: Muhammad bin Abi Bakr told us: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, who said: Ubadah bin As-Samit and Shiddad bin Aws were sitting and they said: We fear for this nation from polytheism and hidden desire. As for hidden desire, it is from women. They said: We heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever prays a prayer to show off has committed shirk, and whoever fasts a fast to show off has committed shirk. Then he recited, So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone. I said: The interpretation of hidden desire has been different from this, and we have mentioned it in An-Nisa’. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Al-Hasan was asked about sincerity and hypocrisy, so he said: Sincerity is that you like to conceal your good deeds and do not like to conceal your bad deeds. If God reveals your good deeds to you, you say, This is from your grace and kindness, and this is not from my actions or my doing. And remember the words of God the Almighty: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone. “And those who give what they give” (al-Mu’minun 23:60) the verse, they give with sincerity, and they fear that it will not be accepted from them. As for hypocrisy, it is seeking the soul’s share from its work in this world. It was said to him, how can this be? He said: Whoever seeks through an action between himself and God the Almighty other than the face of God the Almighty and the Hereafter, then it is hypocrisy. Our scholars, may God be pleased with them, said: Hypocrisy may lead to people mocking him, as it is narrated that Tahir ibn al-Husayn said to Abu Abdullah al-Marwazi: How long have you been in Iraq, O Abu Abdullah? He said: I entered Iraq twenty years ago and I have been fasting for thirty years, so he said: O Abu Abdullah, we asked you about a matter and you answered us about two matters. Al-Asma’i narrated that a Bedouin prayed for a long time and there were people beside him, so they said: How beautiful is your prayer?! He said: And I am fasting in spite of that. How is this in comparison to the statement of al-Ash’ath ibn Qays when he prayed and shortened it, so it was said to him that you shortened it, so he said: He did not mix it with hypocrisy, so he was freed from their belittling by denying hypocrisy from himself and the affectation of his prayer, and the cure for hypocrisy was mentioned in An-Nisa’ from the statement of Luqman, and that it is concealing one’s deeds. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim narrated: My father, may God Almighty have mercy on him, told us: Al-Hammani told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Sheikh, on the authority of Muqal bin Yasar, who said: Abu Bakr said and bore witness to it on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned polytheism, he said: It is more hidden among you than the crawling of an ant. I will show you something that, if you do it, will remove from you the small and major forms of polytheism. Say: O God, I seek refuge in You from associating partners with You while I know, and I ask Your forgiveness for what I do not know. Say them three times.” And Umar [and] Ibn Qais al-Kindi said: I heard Muawiyah recite this verse on the pulpit: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord, and he said: It is the last verse that was revealed from the heavens. And Umar said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “It was revealed to me that whoever recites, ‘So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work,’ a light will be raised for him from Aden to Mecca, filled with angels praying for him and asking forgiveness for him.” Mu’adh ibn Anas said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever recites the beginning and end of Surat al-Kahf, it will be a light for him from his head to his feet, and whoever recites it all, it will be a light for him from the earth to the heavens. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, a man said to him, I intend to get up at night, but sleep overcomes me. He said, “If you want to get up at any time of the night, then recite when you lie down, ‘Say, ‘If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord,’ to the end of the surah, for God Almighty will wake you up whenever you want at night.” Al-Tha’labi, may God be pleased with him, mentioned these virtues. In Musnad al-Darimi, Abu Muhammad, told us, Muhammad ibn Kathir, on the authority of Abadah, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish, who said, Whoever recites the end of Surat al-Kahf at an hour when he wants to get up at night, he will get up. Abadah said, We tested it and found it to be like that. Ibn al-Arabi said: Our great Sheikh al-Tartushi used to say: Do not let the times take you away from competing with your peers and maintaining ties with your brothers. God Almighty concluded the statement by saying: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.
19:1: It is Meccan by consensus. It has ninety-eight verses. When the Battle of Badr took place, and God killed the leaders of the infidels in it, the infidels of Quraysh said: Your revenge is in the land of Abyssinia, so send gifts to the Negus, and send to him two men of your opinion, perhaps he will give you from Quraysh what he has, so you can kill them for those of you who were killed at Badr. So the infidels of Quraysh sent Amr ibn al-Aas and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi’ah, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of their sending, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri, and wrote with him to the Negus. He went to the Negus and read the letter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he called Ja’far ibn Abi Talib and the Muhajireen, and sent for the monks and priests and gathered them, then he ordered Ja’far to recite the Qur’an to them, so he recited Surat Maryam Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad and they stood up with tears in their eyes, for they are the ones about whom God Almighty revealed: And you will find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, “We are Christians. That is because among them are priests and monks and because they are not arrogant.” (al-Ma’idah 5:82). And he recited until His saying: The two witnesses. Abu Dawud mentioned it. And in the Seerah, the Negus said: Do you have with you something of what he brought from God? Ja`far said: Yes, so the Negus said to him: Recite it to me. He said: So he recited Kaf Ha Ya `Ain Sad and by God the Negus cried until his beard was wet, and their bishops cried until their beards were wet when they heard what was recited to them, so the Negus said: This and what Moses brought came out of one lamp, go, by God I will never hand them over to you, and he mentioned the rest of the story. God the Almighty says: Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad The discussion was presented in the beginnings of the surahs. Ibn Abbas said about Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad: The Kaf is from Kaf, the Ha is from Haad, the Ya is from Hakim, the Ain is from Aleem, and the Sad is from Sadiq. This was mentioned by Ibn Aziz Al-Qushayri on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Its meaning is Sufficient for His creation, a guide for His servants, His hand is above their hands, All-Knowing of them, Truthful in His promise. This was mentioned by Al-Tha'labi on the authority of Al-Kalbi, Al-Suddi, Mujahid, and Al-Dahhak. Al-Kalbi also said: The Kaf is from Karim, Kabir, and Kaf, the Ha is from Haad, the Ya is from Raheem, the Ain is from Aleem and Azim, and the Sad is from Sadiq, and the meaning is the same. It was also narrated by Ibn Abbas: It is one of the names of God the Most High. It was narrated by Ali may God be pleased with him that it is the name of God the Almighty and he used to say: O Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad forgive me. This was mentioned by Al-Ghaznawi. Al-Suddi: It is the greatest name of God, if asked by it, He gives, and if called upon by it, He answers. Qatadah: It is one of the names of the Qur'an. This was mentioned by Abd Al-Razzaq on the authority of Muammar on his authority. It was said: It is the name of the surah, and it is the choice of Al-Qushayri in the beginning of the letters. Based on this, it was said: The end of the speech is when he said: Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad as if it is an announcement of the name of the surah, as you say: Book of such and such or Chapter of such and such, then you proceed to the intended meaning. Ibn Jaafar read these letters disconnected, and the rest connected them. Abu Amr inclined the ha and opened the ya, and Ibn Amir and Hamza did the opposite, and Al-Kisa'i, Abu Bakr and Khalaf inclined them both. The people of Medina Nafi and others read them between the two pronunciations, and the rest opened them. Kharijah reported that Al-Hasan used to add a damma to the kaf, and others reported that he used to add a damma to the ha, and Ismail bin Ishaq reported that he used to add a damma to the ya. Abu Hatim said: It is not permissible to add a damma to the kaf, the ha and the ya. Al-Nahhas said: The reading of the people of Medina is among the best of this, and inclination is permissible in the ha and the ya. As for the reading of Al-Hasan, it was problematic for a group until they said: It is not permissible, including Abu Hatim. The statement about it is what Harun al-Qari’ explained. He said: Al-Hasan used to smell the nominative case, so the meaning of this is that he used to nod, as Sibawayh narrated that some Arabs say: prayer and zakat with a nod towards the waw, and that is why it is written in the Qur’an with a waw. Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Asim and Ya’qub made the dal clear in the spelling of Sad, and it is the choice of Abu Ubaid, and the rest assimilated it.
19:2: The Almighty said: A mention of the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zechariah. There are three issues: The first is the saying of God the Almighty: Mention of the mercy of your Lord in raising mention there are three opinions. Al-Farra' said: It is raised by Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad. Al-Zajjaj said: This is impossible, because Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad is not what God the Almighty informed us about Zachariah, and God the Almighty has informed us about him and what he gave us good report of, and Ka Ha Ya Ain Sad is not from his story. Al-Akhfash said: The estimate is, in what he tells you about the mention of the mercy of your Lord. The third opinion: The meaning is this that he recites to you is the mention of the mercy of your Lord. It was said: Mention of the mercy of your Lord is raised by an implied subject, meaning this is the mention of the mercy of your Lord. Al-Hasan read: Mention of the mercy of your Lord meaning this that is recited from the Qur'an is the mention of the mercy of your Lord. Mention is read as a command. Mercy is written and stopped with the letter ha, as is everything similar to it. There is no difference in it among grammarians, and they based their reasoning on that this letter ha is for the feminization of nouns to differentiate them from verbs. Second: The Almighty’s saying: His servant. Al-Akhfash said: It is in the accusative case because of mercy. “Zakariya” is a substitute for it, just as you say: This is a mention of Zayd’s beating of Amr, so Amr is in the accusative case because of the beating, just as His servant is in the accusative case because of mercy. It was said: It is in the order of precedence and delay, meaning: Your Lord mentioned His servant Zakariya with mercy, so His servant is in the accusative case because of the mention, as mentioned by Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farraa. Some of them read His servant Zakariya in the nominative case, which is the reading of Abu Al-Aliyah. Yahya bin Ya’mar read remembered in the accusative case, meaning this Qur’an mentioned the mercy of His servant Zakariya. The languages and readings of Zakariya were mentioned previously in (Al-Imran).
19:3: Third: The Almighty's saying: When he called upon his Lord with a secret call is like His saying: "Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly. Indeed, He does not like transgressors" (al-A’raf 7:55), which has been mentioned before. Calling is supplication and desire, meaning he communed with his Lord in his prayer niche. The evidence for this is His saying: The angels called to him while he was standing praying in the prayer niche (Al Imran 3:39), so it is clear that He answered him in his prayer, just as he called in prayer. There is a difference of opinion about his concealing this call. It was said: He concealed it from his people so that he would not be blamed for asking for a child when he was old, and because it was a worldly matter, so if he was answered, he would achieve his goal, and if he was not answered, no one would know about it. It was said: He was sincere in it and no one knew about it except God Almighty. It was said: Since hidden deeds are better and further from hypocrisy, he concealed it. It was said: Hiddenly secretly from his people in the dead of night. All are possible, but the first is more apparent, and God knows best. It was previously mentioned that the recommended supplication is to be hidden in Surat Al-A’raf, and this verse is explicit in that, because God Almighty praised Zakariya for that. Ismail narrated: Musaddad told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abd al-Rahman, who is the son of Abi Kabsha, on the authority of Saad bin Abi Waqqas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The best remembrance is that which is silent, and the best provision is that which suffices. This is general. Yunus ibn Ubayd said: Al-Hasan believed that the imam should supplicate in the Qunut and those behind him should say Amen without raising their voices. Yunus recited: When he called upon his Lord a call in secret. Ibn al-Arabi said: Malik recited the Qunut in secret, and al-Shafi’i recited it aloud, but reciting it aloud is better, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate with it aloud.
19:4: The Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened.’ There are two issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have become feeble.’ “Weak” was read with the three vowels, meaning weak. It is said: Weak means weak, so he is weak. Abu Zayd said: Weak means weak and Weakens means weak. The bone was mentioned because it is the pillar of the body, and it is its foundation, and it is the basis of its construction. So if it becomes weak, it collapses and all of its strength falls. And because it is the strongest and hardest part of it, so if it becomes weak, what is behind it is weaker than it. And he made it singular because the singular is what indicates the meaning of the genus, and his intention is that this genus, which is the pillar and foundation, and the strongest part of which the body is composed, has been afflicted with weakness. If he had made it plural, he would have intended another meaning, which is that not some of its bones have become weak, but all of them. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And the head was engulfed with gray hair. Abu Amr assimilated the seen into the sheen. This is one of the best metaphors in Arabic speech. The ignition is the spreading of the rays of fire, and he likened it to the spreading of gray hair on the head. He says: I grew old and weak. He added the ignition to the place of the hair and its origin, which is the head. He did not add the head, as he was satisfied with the knowledge of the addressee that it was the head of Zachariah, peace be upon him. Gray has two aspects in its accusative case: One of them: It is a verbal noun because the meaning of grayed is grey, and this is the opinion of Al-Akhfash. Al-Zajjaj said: It is an accusative of distinction. Al-Nahhas: The opinion of Al-Akhfash: It is more appropriate because it is derived from a verb, so the verbal noun is more appropriate for it. Gray hair is the mixing of white hair with black. Third: The scholars said: It is recommended for a person to mention in his supplication what we know of God the Almighty and what is appropriate for submission, because His Almighty’s saying: And my bones have weakened is a manifestation of submission. And His saying: And I have never been, in my supplication to You, my Lord, unhappy is a manifestation of the habits of His favor in answering his supplications, meaning I have never been unhappy in my supplication to You, meaning you have never disappointed my supplication when I called upon You, meaning you have accustomed me to answering in the past. It is said: He was unhappy with such-and-such, meaning he was tired in it and did not achieve his goal. And from some of them that a needy person asked him and said: I am the one who was kind to him at such-and-such a time, so he said: Welcome to the one who intercedes through us and fulfills his need.
19:5: The Almighty’s saying: And indeed, I feared my relatives after me, and my wife was barren, so grant me from Yourself an heir. There are seven issues in it: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And indeed, I feared the relatives. Uthman bin Affan, Muhammad bin Ali, Ali bin Al-Hussein, may God be pleased with them, and Yahya bin Ya’mar read khaft with a fatha on the kha’, a shaddah on the fa’, a kasra on the ta’, and a sukoon on the ya’ from al-mawali because it is in the nominative case with khaft, and its meaning is that I was cut off by death. The rest read khaft with a kasra on the kha’, a sukoon on the fa’, a damma on the ta’, and a nasb on the ya’ from al-mawali because it is in the accusative case with khaft. “Al-mawali” here are the relatives, paternal uncles, and agnates who follow him in lineage. The Arabs call paternal uncles the followers. The poet said: Hold on, cousins, hold on, loyalists. Don't dig up what was buried among us. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada said: He feared that they would inherit his money and that his descendants would inherit him, so he feared that no one other than his son would inherit him. A group said: His masters were neglecting religion, so he feared that his religion would be lost upon his death, so he sought a guardian to take care of the religion after him. This statement was narrated by Al-Zajjaj. Based on this, he did not ask who would inherit his money, because prophets do not inherit. This is the correct of the two statements in interpreting the verse, and that he, peace and blessings be upon him, intended the inheritance of knowledge and prophethood, not the inheritance of money, because it was proven that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “We, the prophets, do not leave any inheritance. What we leave behind is charity.” In the book of Abu Dawood: “The scholars are the heirs of the prophets, and the prophets did not leave behind dinars or dirhams. They left behind knowledge.” This will be further explained when he says: He inherits me. Second: This hadith is included in the chain of transmission of the interpretation, because God Almighty said: And Solomon inherited David (al-Naml 27:16), and it is about the words of Zakariya: Then grant me from Yourself an heir * Who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob and it is a specification of the generality in that, and that Solomon did not inherit from David money that David left behind after him, but rather he inherited wisdom and knowledge from him, and likewise Yahya inherited from the family of Jacob, and this is what the people of knowledge of the interpretation of the Qur’an said except for the Rafidis, otherwise what was narrated from Al-Hasan that he said: He will inherit me money and and inherit from the family of Jacob prophecy and wisdom, and every statement that contradicts the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is rejected and abandoned, as Abu Omar said. Ibn Atiyyah said: Most of the commentators are of the opinion that Zakariya only meant inheriting money, and it is possible that the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We prophets do not inherit do not mean generality, but rather that it is the most common thing for them, so reflect on it. It is more apparent and more appropriate for Zachariah, peace be upon him, to want to inherit knowledge and religion, so the inheritance would be borrowed. Do you not see that when he asked for a guardian and did not specify a son, God Almighty fulfilled his hope in the most perfect way. Abu Saleh and others said: His saying from the family of Jacob means knowledge and prophethood. Third: The Almighty’s saying: From behind me. Ibn Kathir read it with a long vowel and a hamza and a fatha on the ya’. It was narrated from him that he also read it with a short vowel and a fatha on the ya’ like ‘asa’i. The rest read it with a hamza and a long vowel and a sukoon on the ya’. The reciters read khaft like samt except what we mentioned from ‘Uthman. It is a very strange and far-fetched reading, to the extent that some scholars claimed that it is not permissible. He said: How can he say: The followers feared after me, meaning after my death while he was alive?! An-Nahhas: The interpretation of it is that he does not mean by his saying: from behind me meaning after my death, but from behind me at that time, and this is also far-fetched and requires evidence that they were few at that time, and God Almighty has informed us with what indicates abundance when they said: That is from the report (Al Imran 3:44). Ibn ‘Atiyyah: From behind me means after me in time, so it is the back according to what was mentioned in (Al-Kahf). Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And my wife was barren. His wife is Isha’ bint Faqudha bin Qabil, and she is the sister of Hannah bin Faqudha, as stated by Al-Tabari. Hannah is the mother of Mary, according to what was stated previously in (Al Imran. Al-Qutbi said: The wife of Zachariah is Isha’ bint Imran, so according to this statement, Yahya is the son of Jesus’ maternal uncle, peace be upon them, in reality. According to the other statement, he is the son of his mother’s maternal uncle. In the hadith of the Night Journey, he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: I met my maternal cousins, Yahya and Isa, as evidence for the first statement. And God knows best. The barren woman is the one who does not give birth due to old age, and this has been explained in (Al Imran). The barren woman is also the one who does not give birth except due to old age. And from this is the saying of God Almighty: And He renders whom He wills barren (al-Shura 42:50). And likewise the barren man, and from this is the saying of Amer bin At-Tufayl: What a bad young man I am! If I am blind, barren, and a coward, what excuse will I have before every witness? Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: Then grant me from Yourself a successor. This is a question and a supplication. He did not explicitly state that he had a son because of what was known about his condition and his distance from him because of the woman. Qatada said: This happened to him when he was seventy-something years old. Muqatil: Ninety-five years old, and this is more likely, because he was convinced that he would not have children because of his old age, and for this reason he said: And I have reached extreme old age. A group said: Rather, he asked for a son, then he asked that the answer be that he live until he inherits from him, to avoid the answer being in the son but he is cut short and the purpose is not achieved. Sixth: The scholars said: The supplication of Zakariya, peace be upon him, for a son was only to manifest his religion, revive his prophethood, and multiply his reward, not for the world. His Lord had accustomed him to answering, and for this reason he said: And I have never been unhappy in my supplication to You, my Lord, meaning in my supplication to You. This is a good means, to intercede with Him through His blessings, to seek His favor through His favor. It is narrated that a man met Hatim al-Jud and asked him, so Hatim said to him: Who are you? He said: I am the one who did good to him the first year, so he said: Welcome to the one who intercedes for us on our behalf. If it is said: How did Zakariya proceed to ask for something that violates the norm without permission? The answer is that this is permissible in… And in the Qur’an there is what reveals this meaning, for the Almighty said: “Whenever Zechariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found with her provision. He said, ‘O Mary, from where did you get this?’ She said, ‘It is from God. Indeed, God provides for whom He wills without account.’” (Al Imran 3:37) So when he saw the extraordinary event, his taste for his supplication being answered was firm, so the Almighty said: “There, Zechariah called upon his Lord. He said, ‘My Lord, grant me from Yourself good offspring.’” (Al Imran
19:6: The Almighty’s saying: He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, and make him, my Lord, pleasing. There are four issues in it: The first: The Almighty’s saying: He inherits me. The people of the Two Sanctuaries, Al-Hasan, Asim, and Hamzah read He inherits me and he inherits in the nominative case in both of them. Yahya bin Ya’mar, Abu Amr, Yahya bin Waththab, Al-A’mash, and Al-Kisa’i read them in the jussive case, and they are not the answer to Give according to the doctrine of Sibawayh. Rather, its meaning is that if you give him, he will inherit me and he will inherit. The first is more correct in meaning because he asked for a described heir, meaning, grant me from you the guardian whose condition and description are like this, because among guardians there are those who do not inherit. So he said: Grant me the one who will be my heir. Abu Ubaid said this. He rejected the jussive reading, saying: Because its meaning is, if you give him, he will inherit. How can God Almighty inform about this when He knows it better than him?! An-Nahhas: This is a thorough argument, because the answer to the command according to grammarians has the meaning of condition and reward. You say: Obey God and He will admit you to Paradise, meaning if you obey Him, He will admit you to Paradise. Second: An-Nahhas said: As for the meaning of He inherits me and inherits from the family of Jacob, the scholars have three answers to this. It was said: It is the inheritance of prophethood. It was said: It is the inheritance of wisdom. It was said: It is the inheritance of wealth. As for their saying that it is the inheritance of prophethood, it is impossible, because prophethood is not inherited, and if it were inherited, someone would have said: People are related to Noah, peace be upon him, and he is a prophet sent by God. The inheritance of knowledge and wisdom is a good doctrine, and in the hadith: The scholars are the inheritors of the prophets. As for the inheritance of wealth, it is not forbidden, even though some people have denied it, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We do not inherit what we leave behind is charity.
