This is not an argument, because one person informs about himself by informing the group. This may be interpreted to mean, We do not bequeath what we left behind as charity, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not leave behind anything to be inherited from. Rather, what God Almighty permitted him to do was during his lifetime, as He, may His name be blessed, said: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger. (al-Anfal 8:41), because the meaning of for God is for the path of God, and from the path of God is that which is in the interest of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, as long as he is alive. If it is said: In some narrations, We, the prophets, do not bequeath what we leave behind as charity, then both interpretations are applicable to it, that what means which. And the other is that he who is in this situation does not bequeath. Abu Omar said: The scholars differed in the interpretation of his, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: We do not bequeath what we leave behind as charity, into two opinions: One of them, which is the majority and is the opinion of the majority, is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, does not bequeath and what he left behind is charity. The other: Our Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not leave any inheritance, because God Almighty singled him out by making all of his wealth charity as an increase in his virtue, just as He singled out in marriage things that He permitted for him and prohibited for others. This statement was made by some of the people of Basra, including Ibn Ulayyah, and all the scholars of the Muslims are on the first statement. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Of the family of Jacob. It was said: He is Jacob of Israel, and Zachariah was married to the sister of Mary, daughter of Imran, and her lineage goes back to Jacob, because she is from the descendants of Solomon, son of David, who is from the descendants of Judah, son of Jacob, and Zachariah is from the descendants of Aaron, brother of Moses, and Aaron and Moses are from the descendants of Levi, son of Jacob, and the prophecy was in the tribe of Jacob, son of Isaac. It was said: What is meant by Jacob here is Jacob, son of Mathan, brother of Imran, son of Mathan, father of Mary, two brothers from the lineage of Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them, because Jacob and Imran are sons of Mathan, and the sons of Mathan are the leaders of the children of Israel, as stated by Muqatil and others. Al-Kalbi said: The family of Jacob was his maternal uncles, and he is Jacob, son of Mathan, and the king was among them, and Zachariah was from the descendants of Aaron, son of Imran, brother of Moses. Qatada narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God Almighty have mercy on Zachariah and his heirs. Jacob did not leave because he was a foreigner. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And make him, my Lord, pleasing. That is, pleasing in his morals and actions. It was also said: pleased with Your judgment and destiny. It was also said: a righteous man with whom You are pleased. Abu Saleh said: a prophet, just as You made his father a prophet.
19:7: The Almighty's saying: O Zachariah There is an ellipsis in the speech, meaning that God answered his prayer and said: O Zachariah, indeed We give you good tidings of a boy whose name will be John. This good tidings included three things: First: The answer to his prayer, which is an honor. Second: The giving of a son, which is a strength. Third: That he be named alone, and the meaning of naming him was mentioned earlier in (Al Imran). Muqatil said: He named him John because he was alive between an old father and an old mother, and this is questionable, because of what was mentioned earlier that his wife was barren and could not give birth. And God knows best. God the Almighty said: We have not made for him before any namesake meaning, We did not name anyone before Yahya with this name. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, Qatada, Ibn Aslam, and Al-Suddi. God the Almighty bestowed favor upon him by not entrusting his naming to the parents. Mujahid and others said: Similar means like and equivalent, and it is like His statement, the Almighty: Do you know of any similar to Him? (Maryam 19:65) meaning like and equivalent, as if it is from the sameness and superiority, and this is far-fetched, because he is not preferred over Abraham and Moses, except in a specific matter such as leadership and exclusivity, as was explained previously in (Al Imran). Ibn Abbas also said: Its meaning is that barren women did not give birth to a son like him. It was said: God the Almighty stipulated the precedence because He wanted to create after him someone better than him, which is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. In this verse there is evidence and proof that the superior names are worthy of preference, and the Arabs used to choose them in naming because they are more prominent and purer from being offensive, so a speaker said: The names of the red-eyed ones touch the ground with their eyelashes. Ru'bah said to the genealogist Al-Bakri when he asked him about his lineage: I am the son of Al-Ajaj, so he said: I have been brief and known.
19:8: The Almighty's saying: He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a boy?' is not in the sense of denying what God the Almighty has informed us of, but rather in the way of astonishment at the ability of God the Almighty to produce a son from a barren woman and an old man. It was said: Other than this, which was previously explained in (Al Imran), And I have reached extreme old age. It means the end of old age, dryness and dehydration. The same applies to 'asa. Al-Asma'i said: 'asa something is 'aswaan and 'asa is extended, meaning it has dried up and hardened. The old man has 'asa ya'su 'asa and has turned away and has grown old like 'ata. It is said: 'ata al-shaykh ya'tu 'atiyan and 'atiyan he has grown old and turned away. 'atawat ya so-and-so has become 'atawat 'atwan and 'atiyan. The original is 'atawa because it is from the words with a waw, so they replaced the waw with a ya' because it is its sister and it is lighter than it, and the verses are on the ya's, and whoever said: atiyan disliked the damma with the kasra and the ya'. The poet said: Only the newborn is excused, but not the one who is old in age. Ibn Abbas read ‘Asiya, and it is also in the Mushaf of Abi. Yahya bin Waththab, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs read ‘Atiya with a kasra on the ‘ayn, and so do Jathiya and Salaya wherever they are. Hafs added a damma to the ‘ayn specifically, and so did the rest in all of them, and they are two dialects. It was said: ‘Atiya is qasi, it is said: a king is ‘At if he is hard-hearted.
19:9: The Almighty said: "He said: Thus said your Lord: It is easy for Me." That is, the angel said to him: Thus said your Lord. The kaf is in the nominative case, meaning the matter is thus, that is, as it was said to you: It is easy for Me. Al-Farra' said: His creation is easy for Me. And I created you before that is, before Yahya. This is the reading of the people of Medina, Basra, and Asim. The rest of the Kufians read And We created you with a noon and an alif in the plural for emphasis. The first reading is more like the black one. And you were not a thing that is, just as God Almighty created you after nonexistence and you were not a thing existing, so He is able to create Yahya and bring him into existence.
19:10: The Almighty said: He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign.' He asked for a sign to carry it after the angels gave him the good report, and after the Almighty said: And I created you before, when you were nothing. This is an increase in reassurance, meaning complete the blessing by making a sign for me, and that sign would be an increase in blessing and honor. It was said: He asked for a sign that would show him that the good report of Yahya was from Him, not from Satan, because Satan made him think that. Ad-Dahhak said this, and it is the meaning of As-Suddi's statement. This is questionable, because God the Almighty informed him that the angels called him, as mentioned previously in (Al-Imran) He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three nights, sound.' This was mentioned previously in (Al-Imran, so there is no point in repeating it.
19:11: The Almighty’s saying: So he came out to his people from the sanctuary and inspired them to glorify God morning and evening. There are five issues in it: First: The Almighty’s saying: So he came out to his people from the prayer niche, meaning he looked down on them from the prayer niche. The prayer niche is the highest place and the most honorable of places to sit. They used to make prayer niches in places that were elevated on the ground. Its evidence is the prayer niche of David, peace be upon him, as will come. People differed in its derivation. A group said: It is taken from war, as if its adherents were fighting Satan and desires. A group said: It is taken from war with the opening of the ra’, as if its adherents were facing war, fatigue, and exhaustion from it. Second: This verse indicates that it was permissible for their imam to be higher than the congregation in their prayer. The jurists of the countries differed on this issue. Imam Ahmad and others permitted it, adhering to the story of the pulpit. Malik forbade it in the case of a great deal of height, but not a small amount, and his companions explained the prohibition by fear of arrogance for the imam. I said: This is questionable, and the best of what is in it is what Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Hammam that Hudhayfah led the people in prayer in Madain on a bench, and Abu Mas`ud took hold of his shirt and pulled it, and when he finished his prayer he said: Didn’t you know that they used to forbid this - or - forbid that! He said: Yes, I remembered when you extended it to me. It was also narrated on the authority of `Adi bin Thabit al-Ansari who said: A man told me that he was with Ammar ibn Yasir in Al-Madain, and the prayer was called. Ammar ibn Yasir came forward and stood on a bench to pray while the people were below him. Hudhayfah came forward and took him by the hand, and Ammar followed him until Hudhayfah made him get down. When Ammar finished his prayer, Hudhayfah said to him: Didn’t you hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If a man leads the people in prayer, he should not stand in a place higher than their place or something like that? Ammar said: That is why I followed you when you took me by the hand. I said: These are three of the companions who reported the prohibition of that, and none of them used the hadith of the pulpit as evidence against the other, indicating that it was abrogated. What indicates that it was abrogated is that it contains an additional action in the prayer, which is going down and going up, so it was abrogated just as speech and greeting were abrogated. This is more appropriate than the excuse our companions gave, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was protected from arrogance, because many of the imams are found to have no arrogance. Some of them gave the excuse that the height of the pulpit was easy, and God knows best. The Almighty said: Then He inspired them to glorify Him morning and evening. Al-Kalbi, Qatada, and Ibn Munabbih said: He inspired them by pointing. Al-Qatabi: He gestured. Mujahid: He wrote on the ground. Ikrimah: He wrote in a book. In the speech of the Arabs, revelation means writing, and from this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: Except for the four dark ones, which are as if they were the remnants of revelation in the pages of the scrolls. Antara said: He revealed pages from the era of Khosrau and presented them to Ajam Tamtami. Bakrah and 'Asha' are two adverbs. Al-Farra' claimed that 'Asha' is feminine and may be masculine if it is not pronounced in the plural. He said: 'Asha' may be the plural of 'Eshiyah'. Fourth: The ruling on the allusion has been presented in Al Imran. Our scholars differed regarding someone who swore not to speak to a person and wrote him a letter or sent him a messenger. Malik said: He breaks his oath unless he intended to speak to him directly, then went back on it. He said: He does not intend to write and breaks his oath unless he returns the letter before it arrives. Ibn al-Qasim said: If he reads his letter, he breaks his oath. The same applies if the one who swore reads the letter of the one he swore to. Ashhab said: He does not break his oath if the one who swore reads it. This is clear, because he did not speak to him or initiate a conversation with him, unless he intended that he not know the meaning of his words, in which case he breaks his oath. This is based on the statement of Ibn al-Qasim. If he swore to speak to him, he does not fulfill his oath except by speaking to him directly. Ibn al-Majishun said: If he swore that if he knew such and such, he would inform him or tell him, and he wrote to him or sent a messenger to him, he fulfilled his oath. Even if they both knew it, he did not fulfill his oath until he informed him, because their knowledge is different. Fifth: Malik, Al-Shafi’i and the Kufians agreed that if a mute person writes the divorce with his own hand, it is binding on him. The Kufians said: Unless a man was mute for days and wrote it, then none of that is permissible. Al-Tahawi said: Muteness is different from accidental silence, just as accidental inability to have intercourse due to illness or the like for a day or so is different from hopeless inability to have intercourse, such as insanity in the chapter on the woman’s option in separation.
19:12: The Almighty said: O Yahya, take the Book with strength. There is an omission in the speech, the meaning is that a son was born to him and God Almighty said to the newborn: O Yahya, take the Book with strength. This is an abbreviation that the speech indicates. The Book is the Torah without dispute. With strength means with diligence and effort, said Mujahid. It was said: knowledge of it, memorization of it and acting upon it, which is adherence to its commands and refraining from its prohibitions, said Zaid bin Aslam, and it was mentioned previously in (Al-Baqarah). And We gave him judgment while he was a boy. It was said: the judgments and knowledge of them. Muammar narrated that the boys said to Yahya: Let's go play, so he said: You were not created for playing. So God Almighty revealed: And We gave him judgment while he was a boy. Qatada said: He was two or three years old. Muqatil said: He was three years old. A boy is an accusative of state. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever recites the Qur'an before reaching puberty is among those who were given judgment while he was a boy. It was narrated in the interpretation of this verse on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Every son of Adam will come on the Day of Resurrection with a sin, except for John, son of Zechariah. Qatada said: John, peace be upon him, never disobeyed God in a small or big matter, nor did he think of a woman. Mujahid said: John’s food was grass, and tears flowed from his cheeks. The meaning of His statement, and chaste and modest (Al Imran 3:39) has already been discussed in (Al Imran).
19:13: The Almighty said: And compassion from Us "Compassion is in apposition to judgment". It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: By God, I do not know what compassion is? The majority of commentators said: Compassion is pity, mercy, and love, and it is an action of the soul. Al-Nahhas: There are two opinions on the meaning of compassion from Ibn Abbas: One of them: He said: God Almighty showed compassion to him with mercy. The other opinion is what He gave him of the mercy of people until He saved them from disbelief and polytheism. Its origin is from the yearning of a camel for her young. It is said: Hananak and Hananik. It was said: They are two languages with one meaning. Hananik is the dual of Hanan. Abu Ubaidah said: The Arabs say: Hananak O Lord and Hananik O Lord, meaning Your mercy. Imru' al-Qais said: And the Banu Shamji bin Jarim give it to their goat, your compassion, the compassionate one. Tarafa said: Abu Munther, you have perished, so let some of us outlast your kindness. Some evil is less serious than others. Al-Zamakhshari said: Hanan means mercy for his parents and others, compassion and pity. Sibawayh recited: Hanan said: What brought you here? Are you of noble lineage, or do you know the tribe? Ibn al-A'rabi said: Hanan is an attribute of God, the Most High, with emphasis on the Raheem. Hanan, with emphasis on the Raheem, means compassion and mercy. Hanan means provision and blessing. Ibn Atiyyah said: Hanan in the speech of the Arabs also means the great things in the essence of God, such as the saying of Zaid bin Amr bin Nufail in the hadith of Bilal: By God, if you kill this slave, I will make his grave Hanan. Al-Harawi mentioned this report and said: In the hadith of Bilal, Waraqa bin Nawfal passed by him while he was being tortured and said: By God, if you kill him, I will make him Hanan, meaning I will wipe myself with him. Al-Azhari said: Its meaning is that I will be compassionate towards him and have mercy on him because he is one of the people of Paradise. I said: So compassion is tenderness, and Mujahid said the same. And tenderness means compassion from us towards him or from him towards creation. Al-Hutay’ah said: Have mercy on that king, for every situation has its own words. Akram: Love. And the affection of a man for his wife for their love. The poet said: Hanan said: What brought you here? Are you of noble lineage, or do you know the tribe? God the Almighty says: And alms. Alms are purification, blessing, and development in the ways of goodness and righteousness. That is, We made him blessed for the people, guiding them. It was also said that the meaning is that We purified him with good praise for him, just as witnesses purify a person. It was also said that alms were charity given to his parents, as Ibn Qutaybah said. And he was pious. That is, obedient to God the Almighty, and for this reason he did not commit a sin or commit one.
19:14: The Almighty said: And dutiful to his parents. Dutifulness means being dutiful, which means being very dutiful. Jabbar means arrogant. This is a description of Yahya, peace be upon him, as being gentle and humble.
19:15: The Almighty said: "And peace be upon him the day he was born." Al-Tabari and others said: Its meaning is security. Ibn Atiyyah: What is most apparent to me is that it is the customary greeting, so it is more honorable and more prominent than security, because security is obtained by denying disobedience from him, which is the lowest degree of it. Rather, the honor lies in God's greeting him and saluting him in situations where man is extremely weak, in need, helpless, and in need of God, the Almighty, the All-Powerful. I said: This is the statement of Al-Hasan, and we have already mentioned its meaning from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah in Surah Glory be to Him when Yahya was killed. Al-Tabari mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan that Jesus and John met - and they were cousins - and John said to Jesus: Pray to God for me, for you are better than me. Jesus said to him: Rather, you pray to God for me, for you are better than me. May God greet you, and I greeted myself. Some scholars extracted the superiority of Jesus from this verse about greeting, by saying: His indication in greeting himself and his status with God Almighty, which necessitated that when He decided and narrated in the decisive revelation, is greater in status than greeting him. Ibn Atiyyah said: There is a face for each.
19:16: The Almighty says: And mention in the Book Mary the story to the end. This is the beginning of a story that is not from the first. The address is to Muhammad, peace be upon him, meaning, tell them her story so that they may know the perfection of Our power. When she withdrew means she moved away and distanced herself. Nadh means casting and throwing, God Almighty said: So they threw him behind their backs (Al Imran 3:187). From her people meaning from those who were with her. And when is a substitute for Mary a substitute of inclusion, because the times include what is in them. And intidhād means seclusion and isolation. People differed as to why she withdrew. Al-Suddi said: She withdrew to purify herself from menstruation or postpartum bleeding. Another said: To worship God, and this is good. That is because Mary, peace be upon her, was dedicated to the custodianship of the temple and its service and worship in it, so she withdrew from the people for that, and entered the mosque to the side of the prayer niche in its east to be alone for worship, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, entered upon her. His saying: an eastern place means a place on the eastern side. The east with a sukoon on the ra’ is the place where the sun rises. The east with a fatha on the ra’ is the sun. The place was specifically named the east because they used to venerate the east and from where the lights rise, and the eastern directions were better than everything else, as narrated by al-Tabari. He narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: I know best people why the Christians took the east as a qiblah, because of the saying of God the Almighty: When she withdrew from her people to a place in the east So they took the birth of Jesus, peace be upon him, as a qiblah, and they said: If anything on earth was better than the east, Mary would have given birth to Jesus, peace be upon him, in it. People differed about the prophethood of Mary. It was said that she was a prophetess because of this sending and dialogue with the angel. It was said that she was not a prophetess, but rather a human example spoke to her, and her vision of the angel was what Gabriel saw in the description of Dihya when he asked him about faith and Islam. The first is more apparent. We have already discussed this meaning in full in (Al Imran) and praise be to God.
19:17: The Almighty said: So We sent to her Our Spirit It was said: It is the spirit of Jesus, peace be upon him, because God Almighty created spirits before bodies, so He installed the spirit in the body of Jesus, peace be upon him, which He created in her womb. It was also said that it is Gabriel, and the spirit was attributed to God Almighty specifically and honorably. It appears that it is Gabriel, peace be upon him, because He said: So he appeared to her meaning the angel appeared to her. A human being is an explanation or a state of smooth meaning of equal creation, because she could not bear or look at Gabriel in his form. And when she saw a man with a handsome appearance in the form of a human being who had torn the veil over her, she thought that he wanted to harm her. Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to her: He said, ‘I am only the messenger of your Lord to give you a pure boy.’ He made the gift from him because the notification of it was from him. Warsh read on the authority of Nafi’ li-yahib laka meaning God sent me to give you a gift. It was said: The meaning of li-yahib with the hamza is based on the meaning, that is, he said: I sent him to give you a gift. It is possible that li-yahib without the hamza is in the meaning of the hamza, then the hamza was lightened. So she said, Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you should be fearful. That is, one who fears God. Al-Bakali: Gabriel, peace be upon him, retreated in fear from the mention of the Most Gracious, the Blessed and Exalted. Al-Tha'labi: He was a righteous man, so she sought refuge with him in amazement. It was also said: Taqi is a verbal noun meaning you were one who is feared. In Al-Bukhari, Abu Wa'il said: Mary knew that the pious person was wise when she said, If you should be fearful. It was also said: Taqi is the name of a well-known wicked person at that time, as said by Wahb ibn Munabbih, narrated by Makki and others. Ibn Atiyyah: He is weak and lost due to speculation.
19:18: God Almighty said: “She said: ‘Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Gracious from you, if you should be fearing God.’”
19:19: God Almighty said: He said, ‘I am only a messenger from your Lord to give you a pure boy.’
19:20: When Mary heard that from him, she asked about his path, so she said, How can I have a boy when no man has touched me? meaning through marriage. And I have not been unchaste. She mentioned this to emphasize, because her saying, No man has touched me includes what is permissible and what is forbidden. It was said: She did not rule out anything from the power of God, the Most High, but she wanted to know how this child would be? From the husband in the future, or would God create him from the beginning? It was narrated that when Gabriel, peace be upon him, said this to her, he blew into the pocket of her shirt and her sleeve, as Ibn Jurayj said. Ibn Abbas said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, took the sleeve of her shirt with his finger and blew into it, and she became pregnant with Jesus at that moment. Al-Tabari said: The Christians claimed that Mary became pregnant with Jesus when she was thirteen years old, and that Jesus lived until he was taken up for thirty-two years and some days, and that Mary lived after he was taken up for six years, so her total life was more than fifty years.
19:21: And His saying: And We will make him is related to something omitted, meaning, We will create him to make him: a sign indicating Our amazing power and a mercy for those who believe in him and it was a matter decreed predestined and written on the tablet.
19:22: The Almighty said: Then she withdrew with him to a remote place meaning she moved with the pregnancy to a distant place. Ibn Abbas said: To the farthest part of the valley, which is the valley of Bethlehem, between it and Elijah, four miles. She only moved away to escape the taunting of her people for giving birth without a husband. Ibn Abbas said: It was only after she became pregnant that she gave birth immediately. This is what appears, because God the Almighty mentioned withdrawing after pregnancy. It was said: Other than that, as follows:
19:23: The Almighty said: Then the birth pangs drove her to the trunk of the palm tree. He forced her to come, and it is a transitive verb that begins with a hamza. It is said: he brought it and he brought it to such and such a place, just as it is said: he went with it and he made it go away. Shabil read and it was narrated on the authority of Asim that he surprised her from the word surprise. In the Mushaf of Abi, it is: So when the birth pangs came to her. Zuhair said: A neighbor came to us relying on us, fear and hope came to him The majority read al-makhād with the fathah on the meem. Ibn Kathir, according to what was narrated from him, read it with the kasrah, which is labor pains and the severity of childbirth and its pains. A woman is in labor pains, labor pains and labor pains. A she-camel is makhād, meaning her birth is near. To the trunk of the palm tree as if she was looking for something to lean on and cling to, as a pregnant woman clings to due to the severity of labor pains. The trunk is the dry stem of the palm tree in the desert that has no fronds or branches, and for this reason, it was not said to the palm tree. “She said, ‘Oh, I wish I had died before this.’” Mary, peace be upon her, wished for death for religious reasons for two reasons: First, she feared that people would think badly of her in her religion and would taunt her, which would tempt her. Second, lest people fall into slander and accusation of adultery because of her, which is fatal. At this level, wishing for death is permissible, and this meaning has been explained in Surah Yusuf, peace be upon him. Praise be to God. I said: I have heard that Mary, peace be upon her, heard the call of one who said: Get out, you who are worshipped other than God, so she was saddened by that, and she said: Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten. In the speech of the Arabs, forgetfulness is a trivial thing that is likely to be forgotten and no one feels pain for losing it, such as a peg or a rope for a traveler and the like. It was narrated from the Arabs that when they wanted to leave a home, they would say: Protect your women. Ansa is the plural of nasi, which is a trivial thing that is overlooked and forgotten. From this is the saying of Al-Kumait, may God be pleased with him: Do you make us a bridge for a ravenous dog, while I am not forgotten in Ma'ad and I do not enter? Al-Farraa said: “An-Nasee is what a woman throws away from her illness. So Mary’s saying: “An-Naseeya Mansya” means a menstrual period that was thrown away. An-Naseeya was read with a fat-ha on the nun and they are two dialects like al-Hajar and al-Hajar and al-Water and al-Water. Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi read with a hamza Nas’an with a kasra on the nun. Nawf al-Bakali read Nas’an with a fat-ha on the nun from God postponed his time meaning He delayed it. Abu al-Fath and al-Dani narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ka’b. Bakr ibn Habib read Nas’an with a shaddah on the seen and a fat-ha on the nun without a hamza. At-Tabari narrated in her stories that when she became pregnant with Jesus, peace be upon him, her sister also became pregnant with John. Her sister came to visit her and said: O Mary, do you know that I am pregnant? She said to her: And I find that which is in my womb prostrating to that which is in your womb. That is because it was narrated that she felt her fetus falling with its head towards Mary’s womb. Al-Suddi said: That is because of His statement: Confirming a word from God and honorable and chaste and a prophet from among the righteous (Al Imran 3:39). It was also mentioned from her stories that she went out fleeing with a man from the Children of Israel called Joseph the Carpenter, who used to serve with her in the mosque and did so for a long time. Al-Kalbi said: It was said to Joseph - and she was named after him - that she had become pregnant from adultery, so the king will kill her, so he fled with her. On the way, they intended to kill her, but Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said to him: It is from the Holy Spirit. Ibn Atiyyah said: All of this is weak. This story requires that she became pregnant, and continued to be pregnant according to the custom of women, and the narrations agreed that she gave birth to him after eight months. Ikrimah said this, and that is why it was said: A child of eight months does not live to protect the privacy of Jesus. It was also said: She gave birth to him after nine. It was also said: After six. What we mentioned from Ibn Abbas is more correct and clear. And God knows best.
19:24: The Almighty said: And he called to her from beneath her The meem was read with a fatha or a kasra. Ibn Abbas said: What is meant by from is Gabriel, and Jesus did not speak until she brought him to her people, and Alqamah, Ad-Dahhak, and Qatadah said this, so in this there is a sign and indication for her that this is one of the extraordinary matters in which God has a great purpose. And His saying: That you do not grieve is an explanation of the call, and that is explained as meaning which, meaning: So do not grieve over your birth. Your Lord has made a stream beneath you means Jesus. And a stream is a man of great character and a master. Al-Hasan said: By God, he was a stream of men. It is said: So-and-so was generous to so-and-so, meaning he was honored. So-and-so is a stream of a noble people. The majority said: He pointed to her to the stream that was near the trunk of the palm tree. Ibn Abbas said: That was a river whose water had been cut off, so God Almighty made it flow for Mary. And the river is called a stream because the water flows in it. The poet said: A ladder from which you can see the valleys, if you drink in secret, it will be clear Labid said: They were in the middle of the secret show and a crack in the wall, adjacent to her pen It was said: Jesus called her, and that was a miracle, a sign, and a reassurance to her heart, but the first is more apparent. Ibn Abbas read: An angel called her from beneath her. They said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, was in a spot on the earth lower than the spot she was on.
19:25: The Almighty said: “And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates. So eat and drink and be refreshed.” There are four issues in it: The first: The Almighty’s saying:تهقهَهَهHe ordered her to shake the dry trunk to see another sign in reviving the dead trunk. Theبin His saying:بْلدهis an emphatic redundant letter, as is said: take the reins, and give with your hand. God the Almighty said: Then let him extend a rein to the sky (al-Hajj 22:15) meaning let him extend a rein. It was said: the meaning is, and shake towards you fresh dates on the trunk of the palm tree. تهقهَهَهmeans it falls, so he assimilated the ta’ into the seen. Hamza readتهقهَهَهin a lightened form, so he deleted the one that others had assimilated. Asim read in the narration of Hafsتهقهَهَهwith a damma on the ta’ in a lightened form and a kasra on the qaf. It was read تهقهَهَهwith the two ta’s pronounced, and َيسهقهwith a ya’ and the assimilation of the ta’, andتهقهَوو... with a ta’ for the palm tree and a ya’ for the trunk. These are nine readings mentioned by Al-Zamakhshari, may God have mercy on him. Rutban is in the accusative case with shaking, meaning if you shake the trunk, you shake it Rutban yanya. In short, the accusative case of Rutban varies according to the meanings of the readings. Sometimes the verb is based on the trunk, sometimes on shaking, and sometimes on the palm tree. Janya means it has become good and suitable for picking, and it is from yatinat al-thumra. It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud - but it is not authentic - that he read Tatastutu 'alayka rutban yanya fresh ripe dates. Mujahid said: Rutban yanya fresh ripe dates He said: It was 'Ajwa dates". Abbas ibn al-Fadl said: I asked Abu Amr ibn al-Ala' about his saying: "Rutban yanya" fresh ripe dates, and he said: It did not wither. He said: Its interpretation is: It did not dry up, wither, or move away from the hands of its picker, and this is the correct view. Al-Farra' said: "Al-Janya and Al-Majnu" are one and the same. He believes that they are like the slain and the slain, the wounded and the wounded. Others than al-Farra' said: The harvest is the one cut off from one palm tree, and taken from the place where it grew. They recited: And good fruits in spacious gardens and branches of trees whose harvest is close by By harvest he means what is harvested from it, that is, cut and taken. Ibn Abbas said: It was a rotten trunk, and when she shook it, she looked at the top of the trunk and saw that the palm fronds had appeared, then she looked at the date palms that had emerged from between the palm fronds, then it turned green and became dates, then it turned red and became fresh dates, then it became ripe dates, all of that in the blink of an eye, and the fresh dates began to fall into her hands, and none of them were split. Second: Some people have inferred from this verse that although provision is inevitable, God Almighty has entrusted the son of Adam to strive for what is in it, because He commanded Mary to shake the palm tree to see a sign, and the sign would have been that it would not shake. Third: The command to be obligated to earn a living is the way of God the Almighty for His servants, and that this does not undermine trust in Him, contrary to what the ignorant ascetics say. This meaning and the disagreement about it have already been mentioned. Before that, her sustenance came to her without her earning it, as He said: Whenever Zachariah entered upon her in the sanctuary, he found with her provision (Al Imran 3:37) the verse. Then, when she gave birth, she was commanded to shake the trunk of the tree. Our scholars said: When her heart was empty, God freed her limbs from fatigue. Then, when she gave birth to Jesus, her heart became attached to his love, and her secret was occupied with his speech and his command, He entrusted her to her earnings, and returned her to the habit of clinging to the causes in His servants. Al-Tabari narrated on the authority of Ibn Zayd that Jesus, peace be upon him, said to her: Do not be sad. She said to him: How can I not be sad when you are with me?! Neither a husband nor a slave! What excuse do I have before the people?! I wish I had died before this and was forgotten and forgotten. Then Jesus said to her: I will suffice you from speaking. Fourth: Al-Rabi’ bin Khaitham said: “I do not think that there is anything better for a woman in childbirth than fresh dates, based on this verse. If God had known something that was better than fresh dates for a woman in childbirth, He would have fed it to Mary. That is why they said: Dates are a custom for a woman in childbirth from that time, as is the tahneek. It was also said: If her delivery is difficult, there is nothing better for her than fresh dates, and there is nothing better for the sick than honey. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this. Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: God the Almighty said: “Fresh and ripe.” Fresh dates are those that have become good without being engraved or spoiled. Engraving is to engrave from the bottom of the unripe date until it becomes fresh. This is disliked. Malik meant that this is hastening something before its time, so no one should do it. If someone does it, it does not permit its sale or make it a ruling on its goodness. This statement has already been mentioned in Al-An’am. Praise be to God. On the authority of Talhah bin Sulayman, Janiya with a kasra on the jim for imitation, meaning We have made for you in the fresh and ripe dates two benefits: one is eating and drinking, the second is comfort for the heart, because they are miracles.
19:26: This is the meaning of the Almighty's saying: So eat and drink and be comforted meaning eat from the jinn, drink from the secret, and be comforted by seeing the Prophet's son. It is read with the opening of the qaf, which is the reading of the majority. Al-Tabari narrated the reading and be comforted with the kasra of the qaf, which is the language of Najd. It is said:قر عينان يِر ويِقر with the damma and kasra of the qaf, and God comforted his eye and it was comforted. It is taken from qar and qarrah, which are cold. A tear of joy is cold, and a tear of sadness is hot. This group was weak and said: All tears are hot, so the meaning of God comforted his eye is God calmed his eye by looking at the one he loves until it is comforted and still, and so-and-so is the comfort of my eye, meaning my soul is comforted by his closeness. Al-Shaibani said: and be comforted means sleep, urge it to eat, drink, and sleep. Abu Amr said: May God comfort his eye means put his eye to sleep, and remove his wakefulness. Ayna is in the accusative case as a specification, like when you say: Tabah Nafsan. The verb in reality is for the eye, so that was transferred to the possessor of the eye, and the one who was the subject in reality is in the accusative case as an explanation. Similar to it are: Tabah Nafsan, Taqat'at Shaman, Tasabt Abrak, and many others like it. The Almighty said: So if you see any human being, say, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast.’ There are three issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: So if you see The original form of tareen is taraeen, so the hamza was deleted as it was deleted from taraa, and its fat-ha was transferred to the raa, so it became tareen. Then the first yaa was changed to an alif because of its movement and the openness of what preceded it, so two quiescent letters met, the alif that was changed from the yaa and the yaa of femininity, so the alif was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so it became tareen. Then the nun was deleted as a sign of the jussive because in is a conditional letter and ma is a relative clause, so it remained taraa. Then the nun of emphasis entered it, and it is heavy, so the yaa of femininity was broken because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, because the heavy nun is like the two nun of the first word, which is quiescent, so it became tareen. And in this manner, Ibn Duraid said: Either you see my head is the same color And the mouth says: Either you see my head is lowered The letter nun was introduced here as a prelude to ma, just as the letter lam of the oath is also introduced as a prelude to its entry. Talha, Abu Ja’far, and Shaiba read tarin with a sukoon on the ya and a fatha on the nun, lightly. Abu al-Fath said: It is anomalous. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Then say, ‘Indeed, I have vowed’ This is the answer to the condition, and it contains an implied meaning, so he asked you about your son. Then say, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Gracious a fast’ meaning silence, as Ibn Abbas and Anas bin Malik said. In the reading of Ubayy bin Ka’b, Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Gracious a fast meaning silence. It was narrated from Anas. And from him also, and they were silent with a waw, and the difference in the two pronunciations indicates that the letter was mentioned as an explanation, not as a Qur’anic verse. So if it is accompanied by a waw, then it is possible that it is other than fasting. What the reports from the people of hadith and the narrators of the language have followed is that fasting is silence, because fasting is abstinence and silence is abstinence from speech. It was said: It is the well-known fasting, and silence was required of them on the day of fasting except by gesture. Based on this, the reading of Anas is and they were silent with a waw, and that silence was for them in fasting as a commitment to the vow, just as whoever among us vows to walk to the House, this requires ihram for Hajj or Umrah. The meaning of this verse is that God the Almighty commanded her through the tongue of Gabriel, peace be upon him - or her son according to the previous disagreement - to refrain from speaking to people, and to refer to her son in that so that her shyness would be removed, and the verse would be made clear and her excuse would be established. The apparent meaning of the verse is that it was permissible for her to say these words in the verse, and this is the opinion of the majority. A group said: The meaning of say is by gesture, not by speech. Al-Zamakhshari: It includes that keeping silent about the foolish is obligatory, and the one who humiliates the foolish person will not find a distance. Third: If someone vows not to speak to any human being, it may be said that it is an act of worship and he is bound by the vow. It may also be said that this is not permissible in our Sharia because it involves hardship and tormenting the soul, like vowing to stand in the sun and the like. Based on this, the vow of silence was in that Sharia, not in our Sharia, and it has been mentioned previously. Ibn Mas`ud ordered whoever did this to speak. This is the correct view: According to the hadith of Abu Israel, narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zaid and Al-Suddi said: The Sunnah of fasting for them was to abstain from eating and speaking. I said: It is part of our Sunnah during fasting to refrain from bad speech. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If one of you is fasting, he should neither utter obscenities nor act ignorantly. If someone fights him or insults him, he should say, ‘I am fasting.’” And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does not give up false speech and acting upon it, God has no need for him to give up his food and drink.
19:27: God the Almighty said: So she brought him to her people, carrying him. It was narrated that when Mary was reassured by the signs she had seen, and knew that God the Almighty would clarify her excuse, she brought him, carrying him, from the remote place where she had secluded herself. Ibn Abbas said: She left them when the sun rose, and came to them at noon carrying a boy, so the pregnancy and birth occurred in three hours of the day. Al-Kalbi said: She gave birth where her people did not notice her, and she remained forty days in childbirth, then she came to her people carrying him, and when they saw her with the boy, they were sad, and they were a righteous household, so they said in denial: You have certainly done something unprecedented. That is, you have done something great, like someone who fabricates something. Mujahid said: Faraa means great. Saeed bin Mas'adah said: It means fabricated and made up. It is said: Faraait and Afraait have the same meaning. And a child from fornication is like a fabricated thing. God the Almighty said: And let them not bring forth a slander which they have invented between their hands and their feet (al-Mumtahanah 60:12) meaning a child with the intention of attributing it to the husband and not from him. It is said: So-and-so is doing a great deed. Abu Ubaidah said: Al-Fari is the strange and rare. Al-Akhfash said the same. He said: A strange slander. Al-Fari is to cut off as if it is something that breaks the norm, or it cuts off the statement that it is strange and rare. Qatrib said: Al-Fari is new from the water skins, meaning I have come with something new and unique that no one has done before. Abu Haywah read: something strange with a silent ra. Al-Suddi and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: When she brought it to her people carrying it, the Children of Israel heard about it, so their men and women gathered, and a woman stretched out her hand to hit her, but God dried up her half and she became pregnant just like that. Another said: I see nothing but that she committed adultery, so God Almighty silenced her. The people avoided hitting her or saying a word to her that would hurt her, and they began to speak to her in a soft and gentle manner. They said: O Mary, you have done something unprecedented, meaning something great. The rajaz poet said: You fed me a yearling date palm, rotten, worm-eaten and stony. You were running away from it You glorify him.
19:28: The Almighty said: O sister of Aaron People differed about the meaning of this sisterhood, and who is Aaron? It was said: He is Aaron, the brother of Moses, and what is meant is someone we thought was like Aaron in worship who does something like this. It was said: According to this, Mary was from the descendants of Aaron, the brother of Moses, so she was attributed to him by sisterhood because she was from his descendants, just as a Tamimi is called: O brother of Tamim, and an Arab is called O brother of the Arabs. It was said: She had a brother from her father whose name was Aaron, because this name was common among the Children of Israel as a blessing from the name of Aaron, the brother of Moses, and he was the most virtuous man among the Children of Israel, as Al-Kalbi said. It was said: This Aaron was a righteous man at that time among the Children of Israel, a worshipper devoted to God Almighty, called Aaron, so they attributed her to his brothers because she was on his path before, as she was dedicated to the service of the trade, meaning O this righteous woman, you were not worthy of that. Ka'b al-Ahbar said in the presence of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, may God be pleased with her: Mary is not the sister of Aaron, the brother of Moses. Aisha said to him: You have lied. He said to her: O Mother of the Believers, if the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it, then he is more truthful and informed. Otherwise, I find that there was a period of six hundred years between them. He said: So she remained silent. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, he said: “When I came to Najran, they asked me and he said: You recite ‘O sister of Aaron’ and Moses came before Jesus by such and such. So when I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I asked him about that, and he said: They used to name themselves after their prophets and righteous people before them.” It was mentioned in some of its chains of transmission in other than Sahih that the Christians said to him: Your friend claims that Mary is the sister of Aaron and there were six hundred years between them?! Al-Mughira said: So I did not know what to say, and he mentioned the hadith. The meaning is that it is a name that matches a name. From this we learn that it is permissible to name people after the names of prophets, and God knows best. I said: The authentic hadith indicates that there was a long period of time between Moses, Jesus and Aaron. Al-Zamakhshari: There were a thousand years or more between them. So it is not conceivable that Mary was the sister of Moses and Aaron. Even if it is authentic, then whenever Al-Suddi said it, it was because she was from his lineage. This is like saying to a man from a tribe: O brother of so-and-so. And from it is his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: The brother of Sada’a has called for prayer, so whoever calls for prayer will perform it. This is the first statement. Ibn Atiyyah: A group said that there was at that time an immoral man named Harun, so they attributed it to him as a form of reproach and rebuke. Al-Tabari mentioned it, but he did not name the one who said it. I said: Al-Ghaznawi mentioned it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he was an example of immorality, so it was attributed to him. The meaning is: Your father and mother were not worthy of this act, so how did you do it?! This is an insinuation that takes the place of explicitness. In our view, this requires the prescribed punishment, and we will discuss it in Surat An-Nur, God willing. This last statement is refuted by the authentic hadith, which is an explicit text, so no one can speak with it, and there is no fault in it. Praise be to God. Omar bin Luja’ At-Taymi recited: Your father was not a bad man.
19:29: It has five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: “So she pointed to him. They said, ‘How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?’” Mary, peace be upon her, adhered to what she was commanded to do, which was to refrain from speaking. It was not mentioned in this verse that she uttered, Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast. Rather, it was mentioned that she pointed. This strengthens the statement of those who said that her command to say was only intended to indicate. It is narrated that when she pointed to the child, they said: Her belittling us is more severe for us than her adultery. Then they said to her, by way of confirmation: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? “Was” here does not mean the past, because everyone had been a child in the cradle. Rather, it means he is now. Abu Ubaidah said: Was here is superfluous, as he said: Our neighbors were generous. It was said: It means existence and occurrence, as in His statement: And if he is in hardship (al-Baqarah 2:280), which was mentioned earlier. Ibn Al-Anbari said: It is not permissible to say that it is redundant and that it has made a boy the subject, nor to say that was means happened, because if it had the meaning of occurrence and occurrence, then the predicate would be dispensed with. You say: was the free man and that is sufficient. The correct view is that man is in the meaning of the recompense and was means was, the meaning is: whoever is a boy in the cradle, how do we speak to him?! Just as you say: How can I give someone who does not accept a gift? That is, whoever is does not accept. The past may be mentioned in the meaning of the future in the recompense, as in His statement: Blessed is He who, if He wills, can grant you better than that - gardens beneath which rivers flow (al-Furqan 25:10), that is, if He wills, He can grant. And you say: whoever is kind to me, there is from me the like of it, that is, whoever is kind to me, there is from me the like of it. And the cradle it was said: It was a bed like a cradle. And it was said: the cradle here is the mother’s lap. It was said: The meaning is how do we speak to someone whose way is to sleep in the cradle because of his smallness? When Jesus, peace be upon him, heard their words, he said to them from his bed, I am the servant of God. This is the second: It was said: Jesus, peace be upon him, was breastfeeding, and when he heard their words, he stopped breastfeeding and turned his face towards them, leaned on his left, and pointed at them with his right index finger, and said, I am the servant of God. The first thing he uttered was the acknowledgment of his servitude to God Almighty and His Lordship, in response to those who went to extremes after him regarding his status and the Book, the Gospel. It was said: He gave him the Book in that state, and he understood it and taught it, and He gave him prophethood as He taught Adam all the names, and he used to fast and pray. This is extremely weak, as we will explain in the issue after this. It was said: That is, He ruled that I was given the Book and prophethood in eternity, even if the Book was not revealed at that time, and this is more correct.
19:30: God Almighty said: “He said: I am the servant of God. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.”
19:31: And He has made me blessed meaning blessed and beneficial in religion and calling to it and teaching it. At-Tastari: And He has made me enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, guide the lost, support the oppressed, and help the distressed. And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat meaning that I should perform them when the obligation comes to me and I am able to perform them, according to the last correct opinion. As long as I live is in the accusative case as a circumstance, meaning the continuation of my life.
19:32: And dutiful to my mother Ibn Abbas said: When he said and dutiful to my mother and did not say my father, it is known that it is something from God Almighty. And He has not made me a tyrant meaning arrogant and haughty, killing and hitting in anger. It was said: The tyrant is the one who does not see anyone's right over him at all. Miserable meaning disappointed in goodness. Ibn Abbas: Disobedient. It was said: Disobedient to his Lord. It was said: He did not make me abandon His command so that I would be miserable as Iblis was miserable when he abandoned His command. Third: Malik bin Anas, may God have mercy on him, said about this verse: How hard it is for the people of destiny! Jesus, peace be upon him, informed us of what was decreed for him, and what would happen until he died. It was narrated in the stories of this verse from Ibn Zayd and others that when they heard Jesus’ speech, they submitted and said: This is indeed a great matter. It was narrated that Jesus, peace be upon him, spoke this verse in his childhood, then he returned to the state of children, until he walked in the manner of humans until he reached the age of boys, so his speech was to show his mother’s innocence, not that he was one of those who had a mind at that time, and it is as God, the Most High, will make the limbs speak on the Day of Resurrection. It was not narrated that he continued to speak, nor that he prayed when he was a day or a month old. If his speech, glorification, preaching, and prayer continued in his childhood from the time of birth, it would have been something like that which cannot be concealed. All of this indicates the corruption of the first statement, and clearly states the ignorance of its speaker. It also indicates that he spoke in the cradle, unlike the Jews and Christians. The evidence for that is the consensus of the sects that it was not limited. Her innocence from adultery was proven by his words in the cradle. This verse indicates that prayer, zakat, and honoring one’s parents were obligatory for previous nations and past centuries. It is something whose ruling is established and has not been abrogated in the Sharia of his command. Jesus, peace be upon him, was extremely humble. He ate trees, wore hair, sat on the ground, and took refuge wherever the night fell. He had no home. May God bless him and grant him peace. Fourth: Pointing is like speech, and understanding is what understanding is saying. How could it not be, when God Almighty told us about Mary, saying: So she pointed to him, and the people understood from her her intention and purpose, so they said: How can we speak? This has already been mentioned in full in Al Imran. Fifth: The Kufians said: The slander of a mute is not valid, nor is his cursing valid. A similar report was narrated from Al-Sha’bi, and Al-Awza’i, Ahmad, and Ishaq said the same. Slander is only valid according to them with the explicit mention of adultery without its meaning, and this is not valid from a mute person necessarily, so he was not a slanderer, and he cannot be distinguished by the gesture of adultery from lawful intercourse or doubt. They said: And cursing according to us is testimony, and the testimony of a mute is not accepted by consensus. Ibn Al-Qassar said: Their statement that slander is not valid except by explicit mention is invalid in all languages except Arabic, and so is the gesture of a mute. What they mentioned about the consensus regarding the testimony of a mute is wrong. Malik stated that his testimony is acceptable if his gesture is understood, and that it takes the place of the utterance of testimony, but with the ability to utter it, it does not occur from him except by utterance. Ibn Al-Mundhir said: The opponents hold the mute responsible for divorce, sales, and all other rulings, so slander should be like that. Al-Muhallab said: In many chapters of jurisprudence, the indication may be stronger than the speech, such as his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: I and the Hour have been sent like these two. We know the closeness between them by the amount of time the middle finger is longer than the index finger. And the consensus of minds that seeing is stronger than reporting is evidence that a sign may in some places be stronger than speech.
19:33: "And peace be upon me" means safety upon me from God Almighty. Al-Zajjaj said that peace was mentioned before this without the alif and lam, so it was good to mention the alif and lam in the second. And his saying: The day I was born means in this world. It was said: from the devil's insinuations as mentioned previously in (Al Imran). And the day I die means in the grave. And the day I am raised alive means in the hereafter, because he has three states: in this world alive, in the grave dead, and in the hereafter raised, so he is safe in all his states, and this is the meaning of what Al-Kalbi said. Then his speech stopped in the cradle until he reached the age of boys. Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that a woman saw Jesus, peace be upon him, bringing the dead back to life, and healing the blind and the leper in all his signs, so she said: Blessed is the womb that carried you, and the breast that breastfed you, so Jesus, peace be upon him, said to her: Blessed is he who recites the Book of God Almighty and follows what is in it and acts upon it.
19:34: The Almighty said: That is Jesus, son of Mary. That is, that which we mentioned is Jesus, son of Mary, and that is how they believed him, not as the Jews say that he was a stray from the right path, and that he is the son of Joseph the carpenter, nor as the Christians say: that he is God or the son of God. The Word of Truth. Al-Kisa'i said: The Word of Truth is an attribute of Jesus, that is, that is Jesus, son of Mary, the Word of Truth. And it is called the Word of Truth as it is called the Word of God, and the Truth is God Almighty. Abu Hatim said: The meaning is the Word of Truth. And it was said: The estimate is that this speech is the Word of Truth. Ibn Abbas said: He means that this is the speech of Jesus, peace be upon him, the Word of Truth, not falsehood, and the Word was attributed to the Truth as He said: The promise of truth which they were promised (al-Ahqaf 46:16) meaning the promise of truth. And He said: And the home of the Hereafter is better (Yusuf 12:109) meaning nor the home of the Hereafter. Asim and Abdullah bin Amir read the Word of Truth in the accusative case as a state, meaning I say a true word. And the factor has the meaning of the indication in that. Glass: It is a source, i.e. I say the truth, because what precedes it indicates it. It was said: Praise. It was said: Enticement. Abdullah read, The truth said. Al-Hasan read, The truth said with a damma on the qaf, and likewise in (Al-An’am) The truth said (al-An’am 6:73). The saying, the saying, and the saying have the same meaning, like fear, fear, and fear. Which is from the description of Jesus. About it they are in doubt meaning they doubt, meaning that is,... Then two of them said to the third: Say about him. He said: He is the son of God, and they are the Nestorians. So the two of them said: You lied. Then one of the two said to the other: Say about him. So he said: He is the third of three. God is God and he is God, and his mother is God, and they are the Israelites, the kings of the Christians. The fourth said: You lied, rather he is the servant of God and His Messenger and His Spirit and His Word, and they are the Muslims. So each man of them had followers - according to what he said - so they fought and he was victorious over the Muslims. This is what God Almighty said about them: And they kill those who enjoin justice among the people (Al Imran 3:21). Qatada said: They are those about whom God Almighty said: Then the parties differed among themselves they differed about him and became parties, so this is the meaning of His statement: about which they are in dispute with the voiced taa from above, and this is the reading of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and others. Ibn Abbas said: Then her cousin Maryam passed by with her son to Egypt, and they stayed there for twelve years until the king whom they feared died. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. I said: It appears in the history of Egypt, as I have seen and as stated in the Gospel, that when Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem, Herod was king at that time, and that God Almighty inspired Joseph the carpenter in a dream and said to him: Arise, take the child and his mother, and go to Egypt and stay there until I tell you, for Herod intends to seek Jesus to destroy him. So he arose from his sleep and obeyed the command of his Lord, and took Jesus Christ and his mother Mary and came to Egypt. When he came to Egypt, he descended into the well of Balsam, which is outside Cairo, and his clothes were washed in that well, for Balsam does not grow or grow except in that land, and from it comes the oil that is mixed with the oil with which the Christians are baptized. That was a single bottle in the days of the Egyptians and had great value, and it had a very great value in the hearts of the Christian kings, such as the King of Constantinople, the King of Sicily, the King of Ethiopia, the King of Nubia, the King of the Franks and other kings, when the kings of Egypt presented it to them, and it was dearer to them than any gift of value. On that journey, Jesus Christ reached the city of Ashmunin and Qusqam, now known as Al-Muharraqah. That is why Christians still venerate it and come to it on Easter from everywhere, because it is the end of what he reached in the land of Egypt, and from there he returned to the Levant. And God knows best.
19:35: The Almighty said: It is not for God meaning it is not appropriate for Him and it is not permissible to take a son. “From” is a conjunction of the speech, meaning that he takes a son. That is in the nominative case as the subject of was, meaning it is not for God to take a son, meaning it is not part of His attribute to take a son. Then He cleared Himself of what they said and said: Glory be to Him that He should have a son. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. This was presented in full in (Al-Baqarah)
19:36: And indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord The people of Medina, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read that with a fat-ha, and the people of Kufa read that with a kasra on the hamza, as a new sentence. This is indicated by Abu's reading Be and it is * Indeed, God without a waw in conjunction with He said, I am a servant of God. There are opinions regarding the opening: The school of thought of Al-Khalil and Sibawayh is that the meaning is, and because God is my Lord and your Lord, and likewise and that the mosques belong to God (al-Jinn 72:18), so that is in the accusative case according to them. Al-Farra' permitted it to be in the genitive case by deleting the lam, and he also permitted it to be in the genitive case with the meaning, and He enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I live, and that God is my Lord and your Lord. Al-Kisa'i permitted it to be in the nominative case with the meaning, and the command is that God is my Lord and your Lord. There is a fifth opinion: Abu Ubaid narrated that Abu Amr ibn al-Ala said it, which is that the meaning is: And He decreed that God is my Lord and your Lord, so it is conjoined with His saying: a matter from His saying: When He decrees a matter, and the meaning is when He decrees a matter and decrees that God. That is not used in this estimation, nor in the third estimation. It is permissible to start with it in the remaining ways. “So worship Him. This is a straight path,” meaning a straight religion with no crookedness in it.
19:37: The Almighty said: Then the parties differed among themselves "Min" is redundant, meaning the parties differed among themselves. Qatada said: meaning what is between them. So the groups of the People of the Book differed regarding the matter of Jesus, peace be upon him. The Jews differed with slander and magic. The Nestorians among the Christians said: He is the son of God. The Angels are the third of three. The Jacobites said: He is God. So the Christians broke their fast and went too far, and the Jews neglected and fell short. This was mentioned previously in (An-Nisaa'). Ibn Abbas said: What is meant by the parties are those who formed parties against the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and denied him from the polytheists. "So woe to those who disbelieved from the scene of a tremendous Day" meaning from witnessing the Day of Resurrection. The scene means the source, and the witnesses are the presence. It is permissible for the presence to be for them, and it is added to the circumstance because it occurs in it, as it is said: Woe to so-and-so from fighting on such-and-such a day, meaning from his presence on that day. It was said: The scene means the place where the creation witnesses, like the gathering place for the place to which the creation is gathered. It was said: Woe to those who disbelieved because they attended the great scene in which they gathered for consultation, and they agreed to disbelieve in God, and their saying: God is the third of three.
19:38: God the Almighty said: I will hear of them and see the Day they come to Us. Abu al-Abbas said: The Arabs say this in a place of astonishment, so they say: I hear of Zayd and see of Zayd, meaning how much I hear and see him. He said: Its meaning is that his Prophet was astonished by them. Al-Kalbi said: No one will hear or see them on the Day of Resurrection, when God the Blessed and Exalted says to Jesus: Did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as gods besides God?' (al-Ma’idah 5:116) It was said: I hear means obedience, meaning how much they obey God on that Day. But the wrongdoers today means in this world. In clear error. What error is clearer than for a person to believe that a person like himself, whom the wombs carried, ate and drank, and passed urine and needed, is a god?! And whoever describes him like this is deaf and blind, but he will see and hear in the Hereafter when he sees the punishment, but that will not benefit him. Qatada and others said its meaning.
19:39: The Almighty said: And warn them of the Day of Regret when the matter is decided. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud that he said: No one enters Hell except that he has a house in Paradise and he regrets it. It was said: Regret occurs when he is given his book in his left hand. When the matter is decided means the reckoning is completed, and the people of Paradise are admitted to Paradise and the people of Hell are admitted to Hell. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a white ram and will be stopped between Paradise and Hell. It will be said, ‘O people of Paradise, do you recognize this?’ They will look up and look and say, ‘Yes, this is death.’ He said, ‘Then it will be said, ‘O people of Hell, do you recognize this?’ They will look up and look and say, ‘Yes, this is death.’ He said, ‘Then it will be ordered to be slaughtered. Then it will be said, ‘O people of Paradise, eternity and no death.’ O people of Hell, eternity and no death.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, ‘And warn them of the Day of Regret when the matter will be decided while they are in heedlessness and they will not believe.’” Al-Bukhari narrated it with the same meaning on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, and Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, and at-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Sa’id, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, ‘It is a good and sound hadith.’ We have mentioned this in the Book of Remembrance and explained there that the disbelievers will remain eternal with these hadiths and verses in response to those who said that the attribute of anger will cease, and that Iblis and those disbelievers who followed him, such as Pharaoh, Haman, Qarun, and their likes, will enter Paradise.
19:40: The Almighty says: Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it. That is, We cause its inhabitants to die, so we inherit it. And to Us they will be returned on the Day of Resurrection, so We will reward everyone according to his deeds. This has been mentioned previously in Al-Hijr and other verses.
19:41: The Almighty said: "And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet." The meaning is: And mention in the Book that was revealed to you, which is the Qur'an, the story of Abraham and his report. The meaning of friend has already been mentioned in (An-Nisa) and the derivation of truthfulness in (Al-Baqarah), so there is no point in repeating it. The meaning of the verse is: Read to them, O Muhammad, in the Qur'an the story of Abraham, for they have known that they are from his descendants, for he was a monotheist, a Muslim, and he did not take rivals to others. So these people did not take rivals to others?! It is as He said: And who would turn away from the religion of Abraham except one who makes a fool of himself? (al-Baqarah 2:130).
19:42: The Almighty said: When he said to his father, who was Azar, and it was mentioned earlier. O my father, it was mentioned earlier in (Joseph), Why do you worship? meaning, for what do you worship: that which does not hear, nor see, nor avail you at all? meaning idols.
19:43: O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you meaning of certainty and knowledge of God and what will happen after death, and that whoever worships other than God will be punished. So follow me to what I call you to. I will guide you to a straight path meaning I will direct you to a straight religion in which there is salvation.
19:44: O my father, do not worship Satan meaning do not obey him in what he orders you to do of disbelief. Whoever obeys something in disobedience has worshipped it. Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful. "Was" is an additional relative clause. It was said that it means it became. It was also said that it means the state, meaning he is for the Most Merciful. "Disobedient and Aas" have the same meaning, as Al-Kisa'i said.
19:45: O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will afflict you meaning if you die as you are. I fear can mean I know. It is also possible for I fear to be in its original form, so the meaning would be: Indeed, I fear that you will die in your disbelief and the punishment will afflict you. Then you will be a friend of Satan meaning a companion in the Fire.
19:46: He said, 'Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham?' That is, do you turn away from them to someone else? If you do not desist, I will stone you. Al-Hasan said: He meant with stones. Ad-Dahhak: With words, that is, I will curse you. Ibn Abbas: I will beat you. It was also said: I will expose your affair. And leave me for a long time. Ibn Abbas said: That is, stay away from me, with your honor intact, so that no shame will come to you from me. At-Tabari chose this, so his saying, for a long time in this case is a state of Abraham. Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: for a long time for a long time, and from this is the saying of Al-Muhalhil: The mountains cracked at his death and the sand dunes wept for him. Al-Kisa’i said: It is said that I abandoned him for a long time, a long time, a long time, a long time. According to this statement, it is a circumstance, and it means long time.
19:48: The Almighty's saying: And I will withdraw from you: separation and isolation, and its explanation was presented in (Al-Kahf). And His saying: Perhaps I will not be, through the supplication of my Lord, unhappy It was said: He meant by this supplication that God Almighty would grant him a family and children through whom he would be strengthened so that he would not feel lonely by separating from his people.
19:49: That is why he said: So when he had left them and what they worshipped besides God, We gave him Isaac and Jacob meaning We comforted his loneliness with a son, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It was said: Perhaps indicates that the servant is not certain whether he will remain in knowledge or not in the future. It was said: He prayed for his father to be guided. So Perhaps is doubt because he did not know whether his prayer would be answered in that regard or not. The first is more apparent.
19:50: And His saying: And We made for them a high tongue of truth means We praised them with good praise, because all religions praise them well. The tongue is masculine and feminine, and this has been mentioned previously.
19:51: The Almighty said: And mention in the Book Moses meaning, recite to them from the Qur’an the story of Moses. Indeed, he was sincere in his worship, not showing off. The people of Kufa read it with the opening of the lam, meaning, We made him sincere and made him chosen.
19:52: And We called to him meaning We spoke to him on Friday night. From the right side of the Mount meaning to the right of Moses. The tree was on the right side of the mountain when Moses came from Madyan to Egypt, as stated by al-Tabari and others, because mountains have no right or left. And We brought him near in private is in the accusative case as a state, meaning We spoke to him without revelation. It was said: We brought him near to bring the station near until We spoke to him. Waki' and Qubaysah reported on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God, the Almighty: And We brought him near in private meaning He brought him near until he heard the scratching of the pens.
19:53: And We bestowed upon him, out of Our mercy, his brother Aaron, a prophet. That was when he asked, saying: And appoint for me a helper from my family, Aaron, my brother. (Ta-Ha 20:29).
19:54: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And mention in the Book Ishmael. There is a difference of opinion about it. Some say: He is Ishmael, son of Ezekiel. God sent him to his people and they flayed the skin of his head. God Almighty gave him the choice of whatever punishment He wished, so he pardoned him and was satisfied with His reward, and entrusted their affair to Him in His pardon and punishment. The majority say that he is the sacrificed Ishmael, the father of the Arabs, son of Abraham. It has also been said that the sacrificed one was Isaac, and the first is more apparent based on what was mentioned above and will come in (Al-Saffat), God willing. God Almighty singled him out with the truth of the promise, even though it was found in other prophets, as an honor and a tribute to him, like the nicknames such as Al-Haleem, Al-Awah, and Al-Siddiq, and because it is the well-known and well-known of his qualities. Second: Keeping a promise is praiseworthy and is a characteristic of the prophets and messengers, and its opposite, which is breaking a promise, is reprehensible, and this is a characteristic of the immoral and hypocrites, as was explained previously in Bara’ah. God the Almighty praised His Prophet Ismail and described him as keeping his promise. There is a difference of opinion about that. It was said that he promised himself to be patient in the face of slaughter, so he was patient until he was ransomed. This is according to those who believe that he was the one being slaughtered. It was also said that he promised a man that he would meet him in a place, so Ismail came and the man waited for a day and a night. When it was the next day, he came and said to him, I have been waiting for you here since yesterday. It was also said that he waited for him for three days. Our Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did the same before he was sent as mentioned by al-Naqqash and narrated by al-Tirmidhi and others. On the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hamsa’, he said: I pledged allegiance to the Prophet (peace be upon him) with a sale before he was sent, and he had some left, so I promised him that I would bring it to him in his place, but I forgot. Then I remembered after three days, so I came and found him in his place, so he said: “O young man, you have made it difficult for me. I have been waiting for you here for three days.” The wording of Abu Dawud. Yazid al-Raqashi said: Ismail waited for him for twenty-two days, as mentioned by al-Mawardi. In the book of Ibn Salam, he said that he waited for him for a year. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he promised a friend of his that he would wait for him in a place, so he waited for him for a year. Al-Qushayri mentioned that he said: He did not leave his place for a year until Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: The merchant who asked you to sit for him until he returns is Satan, so do not sit, and there is no honor for him. This is far-fetched and not correct. It has been said that Ismail did not promise anything without fulfilling it, and this is a correct statement, and it is what is required by the apparent meaning of the verse, and God knows best. Third: From this chapter, the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The promise is a debt. And in the hadith: And any believer is obligated, meaning in the morals of the believers.
