We only said that it is not obligatory by imposition due to the consensus of scholars on what Abu Omar narrated that whoever promises money should not strike with the creditors with it, so we said that obligating its fulfillment is good with chivalry, and it should not be judged by it. The Arabs are praised for fulfillment, and condemned for breaking a promise and treachery, and so are all nations. And the one who said it well: Whenever a free man says to someone in need, Yes, he fulfills it, and the free man is the guarantor of the need. There is no disagreement that loyalty deserves praise and thanks, and that breaking it deserves blame. God Almighty has praised those who are true to their promises and fulfill their vows, and this is enough praise and commendation, and that which they break is blame. Fourth: Malik said: If a man asks another man to give him a gift and he says yes, then he decides not to do so, then I do not think he is obligated. Malik said: If that was to pay off a debt and he asked him to pay it off on his behalf and he said yes, and there are two men to testify against him, then how is it more likely that he is obligated if two testify against him? Abu Hanifa and his companions, Al-Awza’i, Al-Shafi’i and all the jurists said: Nothing is obligatory from the waiting period because they are benefits that were not received in the case of a loan because they are incidental, and in other cases they are people and objects that were gifted and not received, so the owner has the right to take them back. In Al-Bukhari: “And mention in the Book Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise.” Ibn Ashwa’ ruled according to the promise and mentioned that on the authority of Samura bin Jundub. Al-Bukhari said: I saw Ishaq bin Ibrahim citing the hadith of Ibn Ashwa’ as evidence. Fifth: And he was a messenger and a prophet. It was said: Ishmael was sent to Jurhum. And all the prophets were true to their promises, and Ishmael was mentioned specifically to honor him. And God knows best.
19:55: Sixth: And he used to command his people. Al-Hasan said: He means his nation. And in the wording of Ibn Masoud: And he used to command his people, Jurhum and his children, to pray and give zakat. And he was pleasing to his Lord. That is, pleasing, pure and righteous. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: Whoever says mardi builds it on radhiyyat. They said: The people of Hijaz say: mardu. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' said: Some Arabs say ridwan and ridyan and ridhwan on mardu, and ridhyan on mardi. The Basrans do not permit saying anything other than ridwan and ribwan. Abu Ja'far Al-Nahhas said: I heard Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj say: They make mistakes in writing and write riba with a ya, then they make mistakes in what is more severe than this and say ribyan, and nothing is permissible except ribwan and ridwan. God the Almighty said: And whatever you give in interest, it may increase within the wealth of the people. (al-Rum 30:39)
19:56: The Almighty said: "And mention in the Book, Idris. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet." Idris, peace be upon him, was the first to write with a pen, the first to sew clothes and wear sewn clothing, and the first to study the science of stars, arithmetic, and their paths. He was called Idris because of his frequent study of the Book of God. God sent down thirty pages to him, as in the hadith of Abu Dharr. Al-Zamakhshari: It was said that Idris was called Idris because of his frequent study of the Book of God. His name was Enoch, but this is incorrect, because if it were an active participle from the word daras, there would only be one reason for it, which is knowledge, and it would have been declined. Its inability to be declined is evidence of its foreignness. Likewise, Iblis is foreign and is not from iblas as they claim, nor is Jacob from al-'aqab, nor is Israel from Israel as Ibn al-Sikkit claimed. Whoever does not investigate or train in the craft will make many such mistakes. It is possible that the meaning of Idris, peace be upon him, in that language is close to that, so the narrator thought it was derived from daras. Al-Tha'labi, Al-Ghaznawi and others said: He is the grandfather of Noah, which is a mistake. It was previously stated in Al-A'raf. It was also mentioned in the biography that Noah, peace be upon him, was the son of Lamech, the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, who is the prophet Idris, as they claim. And God knows best. He was the first of the sons of Adam to be given prophethood, and he wrote with a pen. He was the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Cainan, the son of Janish, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, may God bless him and grant him peace.
19:57: The Almighty said: And We raised him to a high station. Anas bin Malik, Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, and others said: It means the fourth heaven. This was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ka’b al-Ahbar said the same. Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak said: It means the sixth heaven. Al-Mahdawi mentioned this. I said: It was reported in Al-Bukhari on the authority of Sharik bin Abdullah bin Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas bin Malik say: “The Night of the Prophet’s Night Journey (peace be upon him) from the Kaaba Mosque” The hadith, in which it says: In each heaven there are prophets - he named them - including Idris in the second heaven. This is an error, and the correct view is that he is in the fourth heaven. This is how Thabit al-Bunani narrated it on the authority of Anas ibn Malik on the authority of the Prophet (peace be upon him), mentioned by Muslim in his Sahih. Malik ibn Sa’sa’ah narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: When I was taken up to the heaven, I came upon Idris in the fourth heaven. Narrated by Muslim as well. The reason for his ascension, according to what Ibn Abbas, Ka’b and others said, was that he was walking one day on an errand and was struck by the sun’s glare. He said: O Lord, I have walked one day, so how about someone who carries it for five hundred years in one day! O God, lighten its weight for him. He meant the angel in charge of the sun’s orbit. Idris said: O God, lighten its weight for him and carry some of its heat for him. When the angel woke up, he found the lightness of the sun and the shade to an extent he did not know. He said: O Lord, You created me to carry the sun, so what did You decree regarding it? God the Almighty said: “As for My servant Idris, He asked Me to lighten its load and heat for You, and I answered him. He said: “O Lord, unite me with him and establish a friendship between me and him.” So God permitted him until he came to Idris, and Idris, peace be upon him, was asking Him. He said: “I have been informed that You are the most honorable of the angels and the most powerful with the Angel of Death, so intercede for me with Him so that He may delay my death, so that I may increase in gratitude and worship.” The king said: God does not delay a soul when its time has come. The king said to him: I know that, but it is better for my soul. He said: Yes. Then he carried him on his wing and raised him to the sky and placed him at sunrise. Then he said to the Angel of Death: I have a friend from among the sons of Adam who interceded on my behalf with you to delay his time. He said: That is not up to me, but if you would like to know him, I will inform him when he will die. He said: Yes. Then he looked in his register and said: You are asking me about a man whom I do not see dying ever. He said: How? He said: I do not see him dying except at sunrise. He said: So I came to you and left him there. He said: Go, and I do not see you finding him except dead. By God, nothing remains of Idris’ life. The king returned and found him dead. Al-Suddi said: One day he slept and the heat of the sun was intense. He got up in distress because of it, and said: O God, lighten the heat of the sun for the Angel of the Sun and help him with its burden, for he is dealing with a blazing fire. Then the Sun Angel woke up and a throne of light was set up for him, with seventy thousand angels on his right and the same number on his left serving him, and taking care of his affairs and work under his rule. The Sun Angel said: O Lord, where did I get this from? He said: A man from the sons of Adam called Idris prayed for you. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ka’b. He said: The Sun Angel said to him: Do you want something? He said: Yes, I wish I could see Paradise. He said: So he raised him on his wing, then flew with him. While he was in the fourth heaven, he met the Angel of Death looking into the sky, looking right and left. The Sun Angel greeted him and said: O Idris, this is the Angel of Death, so greet him. The Angel of Death said: Glory be to God! And for what purpose did you raise him here? He said: I raised him to show him Paradise. He said: God the Most High commanded me to take the soul of Idris in the fourth heaven. I said: O Lord, where is Idris in the fourth heaven? So I descended and behold, he was with you. Then He took his soul and raised it to Paradise, and the angels buried his body in the fourth heaven. This is what the Almighty said: And We raised him to a high station. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Every day, Idris was raised in worship as was raised for the people of the earth in his time. The angels were amazed by him and the Angel of Death longed for him, so he asked his Lord’s permission to visit him and He gave him permission. He came to him in the form of a human being. Idris, peace be upon him, used to fast during the day. When it was time to break his fast, He invited him to his food but he refused to eat. He did that to him for three nights, but Idris denied him and said to him: Who are you? He said: I am the Angel of Death. I asked my Lord’s permission to accompany you and He gave me permission. He said: I have a need of you. He said: What is it? He said: That you take my soul. Then God revealed to him to take his soul, so He took him and returned him to him after an hour. The Angel of Death said to him: What is the benefit of taking your soul? He said: So that I may taste the agony of death and be more prepared for it. Then Idris said to him after an hour: I have another need of you. He said: What is it? He said: That you raise me up to the sky so that I may look at Paradise and Hell. So God Almighty permitted him to raise him up to the heavens, and he saw Hell and fainted. When he regained consciousness, he said: Show me Paradise. So He admitted him into Paradise. Then the Angel of Death said to him: Come out so that you may return to your abode. So he clung to a tree and said: I will not come out of it. So God Almighty sent an angel as a judge between them, and he said: Why do you not come out? He said: Because God Almighty said: Every soul will taste death (Al Imran 3:185) and I tasted it, and He said: There is not one of you but will pass over it (Maryam 19:71) and I did pass over it, and He said: And they will not be removed from it (Al Hijr: 48). So how can I come out? God Almighty said to the Angel of Death: By My permission he entered Paradise and by My command he will be removed. So he is alive there. That is what God Almighty said: And We raised him to a high station [An-Nahhas said: Idris said: And they will not be removed from it It is possible that God knows best that this is Idris, and then the Qur’an was revealed about him. Wahb bin Munabbih said: Idris sometimes revels in Paradise, and sometimes worships God Almighty with the angels in Heaven.
19:58: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Those are the ones upon whom God bestowed favor from among the prophets, from the descendants of Adam, meaning Idris alone. And among those We carried with Noah, meaning Abraham alone. And among the descendants of Abraham, meaning Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob. And among the descendants of and Israel, Moses, Aaron, Zachariah, John, and Jesus. So Idris and Noah had the honor of being close to Adam, and Abraham had the honor of being close to Noah, and Ishmael, Isaac, and Jacob had the honor of being close to Abraham. And among those We guided, meaning to Islam, and chose, with faith. When the verses of the Most Gracious are recited to them, Shibl ibn Abbad al-Makki read is recited in the masculine form because the feminine is not real with the presence of a separator. They fell down in prostration and weeping, describing them as being humble before God and weeping. This has already been mentioned in Glory be to God. It is said: He cried, weeping, weeping, and he cried, but Al-Khalil said: If you shorten the crying, it is like sadness, meaning there is no sound with it, as the poet said: My eyes cried and it was right to cry, but crying and wailing are of no use. Prostrating is in the accusative case as a state, and crying is in apposition to it. Second: This verse indicates that the verses of the Most Gracious have an effect on the hearts. Al-Hasan said: When the verses of the Most Gracious are recited to them, they fall down in prostration and weeping in prayer. Al-Asamm said: What is meant by the verses of the Most Gracious are the books that contain His Oneness and His proofs, and that they used to prostrate when they were recited, and weep when they were mentioned. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that what is meant by it is the Qur’an in particular, and that they used to prostrate and weep when it was recited. Al-Kiya said: In this is evidence from his statement that the Qur’an is what was recited to all the prophets, and if that were the case, then the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have been the only one to whom it was revealed. Third: Abu Bakr al-Razi used this verse as evidence that prostration during the Qur’an is obligatory for the listener and the reader. Al-Kiya said: This is far-fetched, as this description includes all the verses of God the Most High. He combined prostration with crying, and thereby demonstrated the method of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, in their glorification of God the Most High and His verses, and it does not indicate that this is obligatory for a specific verse. Fourth: The scholars said: Whoever recites a prostration should supplicate in it with what is appropriate for its verses. If he recites Surat As-Sajdah “Alif, Lam, Meem. Tanzeel,” he should say: O God, make me among those who prostrate to Your face, glorify You with praise, and I seek refuge in You from being among those who are arrogant towards Your command. If he recites the prostration Glory be to You, he should say: O God, make me among those who weep to You, who are humble before You. If he recites this, he should say: O God, make me among Your servants who are blessed, who are guided, who prostrate to You, and who weep when Your verses are recited.
19:59: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: Then there came after them a posterity meaning bad children. Abu Ubaidah said: Hajjaj bin Ibn Jurayj told us on the authority of Mujahid who said: That will be when the Hour comes, and the righteous people of this nation, the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will depart, some of them committing fornication with others in the alleys. We have already discussed successors in Al-A’raf, so there is no point in repeating it. Second: The Almighty’s saying: They wasted the prayer. Abdullah and Al-Hasan read they wasted the prayers in the plural. It is a reproach and a text that wasting the prayer is one of the major sins for which its doer will be destroyed, and there is no disagreement on that. Omar said: And whoever wasted it is even more wasted of what is other than it. They differed about who is meant by this verse. Mujahid said: The Christians came after the Jews. Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, Mujahid also, and Ata’ said: They are a people from the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, at the end of time, meaning that there will be in this nation those with this description, not that they are the ones meant by this verse. They also differed about the meaning of wasting it. Al-Qurazi said: It is wasting it through disbelief and denial. Al-Qasim bin Mukhaymara and Abdullah bin Mas’ud said: It is wasting its times and not fulfilling its rights, and this is correct. And if you pray it alone, it is not valid and does not count, because of his saying to the man who prayed and came and greeted him: Go back and pray, for you have not prayed, three times. Narrated by Muslim. Hudhayfah said to a man who was praying and he was slowing down: How long have you been praying this prayer? He said: Forty years. He said: You have not prayed, and if I died while praying this prayer, I would have died not following the nature of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Then he said: A man may shorten the prayer and complete it and do it well. Narrated by al-Bukhari and the wording is from al-Nasa’i. In al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Abu Mas’ud al-Ansari, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A prayer in which a man does not straighten his back during bowing and prostration is not valid. He said: A good and authentic hadith. The scholars among the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who came after them acted upon this. They believe that a man should straighten his back during bowing and prostration. Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and Ishaq said: Whoever does not straighten his back during bowing and prostration, his prayer is invalid. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That prayer is the prayer of the hypocrite, sitting watching the sun until it is between the horns of Satan, then he stands up and pecks it four times, remembering God only a little. This is a criticism of those who do that. Forwah ibn Khalid ibn Sinan said: The companions of Ad-Dahhak once delayed a leader in the afternoon prayer until the sun was about to set, so Ad-Dahhak recited this verse, then said: By God, I would rather leave it than waste it. The summary of what is said in this regard is that whoever does not maintain the perfection of its ablution, bowing, and prostration is not maintaining it, and whoever does not maintain it has wasted it, and whoever wastes it is more wasteful of what is other than it, just as whoever maintains it, God will preserve his religion for him, and there is no religion for one who does not pray. Al-Hasan said: They neglected the mosques and occupied themselves with crafts and causes. And they followed desires meaning pleasures and sins. Third: Al-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Anas bin Hakim Al-Dhabi that he came to Medina and met Abu Hurairah and said to him: O young man, shall I not tell you a hadith that may benefit you? I said: Yes. He said: The first thing for which people will be brought to account on the Day of Resurrection from their deeds is the prayer. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, will say to His angels - and He knows best -: Look at the prayer of My servant, did he complete it or lack thereof? If it was complete, it will be recorded for him as complete, but if he lacked something from it, He will say: Look at whether My servant has any voluntary prayers. If he has any voluntary prayers, He will say: Complete My servant’s obligatory prayers from his voluntary prayers. Then deeds will be taken accordingly. Yunus said: I think it was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the wording of Abu Dawud. He said: Musa ibn Ismail narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated to us, from Zurara ibn Awfa, from Tamim ad-Dari, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with this meaning. He said: Then the zakat is like that, “Then the deeds will be taken accordingly.” An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Hammam on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Harith ibn Qubaysah on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The first thing for which the servant will be brought to account on the Day of Resurrection will be his prayer. If it is sound, then he will succeed and prosper, but if it is corrupt, then he will fail and be a loser.” Hammam said: I do not know if this is from the words of Qatadah or from the narration. “If something is missing from his obligatory prayer, He will say: ‘Look, does My servant have any voluntary prayers to complete what is missing from the obligatory prayer?’ Then the rest of his deeds will be like that.” Abu al-Awam disagreed with him and narrated it on the authority of Qatada on the authority of al-Hasan on the authority of Abu Rafi’ on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first thing for which a servant will be brought to account on the Day of Resurrection will be his prayer. If it is found to be complete, it will be recorded as complete, but if something is missing from it, God will say: ‘Look to see if you can find any voluntary prayers for him to complete what he missed of his obligatory prayers. Then the rest of the deeds will be conducted according to that.’” Al-Nasa’i said: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us, saying: An-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, on the authority of al-Azraq ibn Qays, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ya’mar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The first thing for which a servant will be brought to account on the Day of Resurrection will be his prayer. If he completed it, then all is well. Otherwise, God Almighty will say: ‘Look for My servant who has done voluntary prayers. If He finds any voluntary prayers for him, He will say: ‘Complete the obligatory prayers with them.’” Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said in the book Al-Tamhid: As for completing the obligatory prayer from the voluntary prayer, it only happens - and God knows best - for someone who forgot about an obligatory prayer and did not perform it, or did not do its bowing and prostration properly and did not know how much of that was. As for someone who left it, or forgot and then remembered it and did not perform it intentionally, and was busy with the voluntary prayer from performing its obligation while he was remembering it, then his obligatory prayer from his voluntary prayer is not completed, and God knows best. A strange hadith has been narrated from the hadith of the people of Ash-Sham in this chapter, narrated by Muhammad bin Himyar from Amr bin Qais Al-Sakuni from Abdullah bin Qart from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever prays a prayer in which he does not complete his bowing and prostration, some of his glorifications will be added to it until it is complete. Abu Omar said: This is not preserved from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except from this source, and it is not strong. Even if it is authentic, its meaning is that he left a prayer that he had completed in his opinion, but it is not considered complete. I said: A person should do his obligatory and voluntary prayers well, so that he will have a voluntary prayer that he finds in addition to his obligatory prayer and that will bring him closer to his Lord, as God Almighty said: My servant continues to draw closer to Me with voluntary prayers until I love him. The hadith. If a voluntary prayer completes an obligatory prayer, then its ruling in meaning is the ruling of an obligatory prayer. Whoever is not good at praying an obligatory prayer, then it is more appropriate that he does not perform a voluntary prayer well. Indeed, people’s voluntary prayers are extremely deficient and flawed because they consider them insignificant and insignificant, to the point that they are not considered important. By God, there are those who are pointed out and thought to have knowledge, and they perform their voluntary prayers in this way. Rather, their obligatory prayers are pecking at them like a rooster due to their lack of knowledge of the hadith, so how about the ignorant who do not know? The scholars have said: No bowing, prostration, standing after bowing, or sitting between the two prostrations are sufficient until one is upright in bowing, standing, prostrating, and sitting. This is the correct view in the hadith, and the majority of scholars and people of insight agree with it. This is the narration of Ibn Wahb and Abu Mus’ab from Malik. This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. If this is the case, how can this voluntary prayer complete what was missing from this obligatory prayer due to ignorance or forgetfulness?! Rather, all of that is incorrect and unacceptable, because it was not done in a way that was required. And God knows best. The Almighty said: And they followed desires. And on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And they followed desires, he is from the sons of the constructed and the mounted the seen, and the wearing of the famous. I said: Desires are what a person agrees with, desires, suits, and does not avoid. In Sahih: Paradise is surrounded by hardships and Hell is surrounded by desires. What was mentioned about Ali, may God be pleased with him, is part of this. God Almighty says: Then they will meet with error. Ibn Zayd said: Evil, misguidance, or disappointment. He said: Whoever finds good, people praise him for his actions, and whoever goes astray will not lack someone to blame him for his error. Abdullah bin Masoud said: It is a valley in Hell. The linguists understand that they will encounter this Ghayy, as God the Almighty said: And whoever does that will meet a sin (al-Furqan 25:68). It is more apparent that Ghayy is the name of the valley, named after those who go astray. Kaab said: At the end of time, there will appear people with whips like the tails of cows, then he recited: Then they will encounter Ghayyun, meaning destruction and misguidance in Hell. And from him: Ghayy is a valley in Hell, the furthest bottom and the hottest. In it is a well called Al-Baheem. Whenever Hell subsides, God the Almighty opens that well and Hell is set ablaze in it. Ibn Abbas said: Ghay is a valley in Hell, and the valleys of Hell seek refuge from its heat. God Almighty has prepared that valley for the adulterer who persists in adultery, for the addicted drinker of alcohol, for the usurer who does not stop taking interest, for the disobedient, for the false witness, and for the woman who brings a child to her husband that is not his.
19:60: The Almighty says: Except for those who repent meaning from neglecting the prayer and following desires, so they return to obeying their Lord. And believe in Him “and do righteous deeds. For those will enter Paradise.” Abu Ja`far, Shaibah, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Abu `Amr, Ya`qub, and Abu Bakr read they enter with a fatha on the kha’. The rest read with a fatha on the ya’. And they will not be wronged at all meaning nothing will be deducted from their righteous deeds, except that for every good deed they will be credited with ten to seven hundred.
19:61: Janāt Adn instead of Jannah, so it was in the accusative case. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: Janāt Adn is permissible as a subject. Abu Hatim said: If it were not for the line, it would have been Jannah Adn, because before it was they will enter Jannah. "Which the Most Gracious has promised His servants in the unseen," meaning whoever worships Him and keeps His covenant in the unseen. It was said: They believed in Jannah but did not see it. "His promise was to be fulfilled. Matyaan is the object of itiyaan." Whatever reaches you, you have reached it. You say: Sixty years have passed for me, and I have reached sixty years. And good has reached me from so-and-so, and I have reached good from him. Al-Qutbi said: "Matyaan means to come," so it is the object with the meaning of the agent. "Matyaan is hamzated because it is from ata, which means yatu." Whoever lightens the hamzah makes it an alif. Al-Tabari said: The promise here is the promised one, which is Jannah, meaning His friends will come to it.
19:62: They will not hear therein ill speech meaning in Paradise. Illiteracy means false speech, obscenity, idle talk, and useless talk. An example of this is the hadith: If you say to your friend on Friday, ‘Listen,’ while the imam is delivering the sermon, then you have spoken frivolously. It is also narrated, I have spoken frivolously, which is the language of Abu Hurairah, as the poet said: And the pilgrims' flocks are restrained from idle talk and obscene speech. Ibn Abbas said: Idle talk is everything that does not contain the remembrance of God, meaning their speech in Paradise is praising and glorifying God. “Except peace” means they will hear peace, so it is from the discontinuous exception, meaning the peace of some of them to others, and the peace of the King to them, as stated by Muqatil and others. Peace is a comprehensive name for goodness, and the meaning is that they will hear nothing therein except what they love. God the Almighty said: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening meaning they will have whatever they desire of food and drink, morning and evening, meaning in the amount of these two times, as there is no morning and no evening, like God the Almighty’s saying: Its morning is a month and its evening is a month (Saba’ 34:12) meaning the amount of a month, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jurayj and others said its meaning. It was said: The moderate conditions of the people of Paradise made them aware of it, and the most pleasant blessing for the Arabs was the ability to eat and drink morning and evening. Yahya bin Abi Katheer and Qatada said: The Arabs in their time were those who could find lunch and dinner together, so that was the pleasant thing, so it was revealed. It was said: That is, their provision therein is uninterrupted, as He said: And their bellies will be filled therewith (al-Waqi’ah 56:33) neither interrupted nor forbidden. It is like saying: I wake up and spend the evening in Your remembrance. That is, my remembrance of You is constant. It is possible that the morning is before they are preoccupied with their pleasures, and the evening is after they are done with their pleasures, because it includes periods of transition from one state to another. This goes back to the first statement. Az-Zubayr ibn Bakkar narrated on the authority of Ismail ibn Abi Uways who said: Malik ibn Anas said: The food of the believers is twice a day, and he recited the statement of God the Almighty: And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening. Then he said: God the Almighty compensated the believers in fasting with the pre-dawn meal instead of lunch so that they may be strengthened by it to worship their Lord. It was said: This was mentioned because the nature and form of lunch is different from the nature and form of dinner, and only kings know this. Likewise, in Paradise, the provision of lunch will be different from the provision of dinner, and the blessings will be repeated to them so that they may increase in enjoyment and happiness. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim included in Nawadir Al-Usul a hadith from Aban on the authority of Al-Hasan and Abu Qilabah, who said: “A man said: O Messenger of God, is there night in Paradise? He said: What made you say this? He said: I heard God the Almighty mention in the Book: “And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening.” I said: The night is between morning and evening. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no night there, but rather light and radiance. Morning comes to evening and evening comes to morning, and the best gifts from God the Almighty come to them at the times of prayer that they used to pray in the world, and the angels greet them. This is the ultimate explanation of the meaning of the verse, and we have mentioned it in the Book of Remembrance. The scholars said: There is neither night nor day in Paradise, but they will be in light forever. They only know the difference between the night and the day by the lowering of the veils and the closing of the doors, and they know the difference between the day and the raising of the veils and the opening of the doors. This was mentioned by Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi, al-Mahdawi, and others. The Almighty's saying: The Fire they will be exposed to has six aspects: It could be in the nominative case as a substitute for evil. It could also mean it is the Fire. It could be in the nominative case as a subject. Al-Farra' said: It could be in the nominative case with the pronoun referring back to the Fire they will be exposed to. So these are four aspects for the nominative case. Al-Farra' permitted the accusative case because after it is a pronoun and before it is something connected to it. Al-Akhfash permitted the genitive case as a substitute for the torment. The majority of scholars agree that this exposure is in the Barzakh. Some scholars have used as evidence to confirm the torment of the grave the words: The Fire they will be exposed to morning and evening as long as the world exists. Likewise, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Muqatil, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: This verse indicates the torment of the grave in this world. Don't you see that He says about the torment of the Hereafter: And on the Day the Hour appears, 'Admit the family of Pharaoh into the severest torment.' In the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: The souls of the family of Pharaoh and those like them among the disbelievers will be shown to the Fire in the morning and the evening, and it will be said, This is your home. And it was also narrated from him: Their souls are in the bodies of black birds that go to Hell in the morning and in the evening twice a day, and that is its presentation. Shu'bah narrated from Ya'la ibn Ata' who said: I heard Maymun ibn Mihran say: When Abu Hurairah was called, he would call out: We have entered the morning, and praise be to God, and the family of Pharaoh was shown to the Fire. And when evening came, he would call out: We have entered the evening, and praise be to God, and the family of Pharaoh was shown to the Fire. No one heard Abu Hurairah except that he would seek refuge in God from the Fire. In the hadith of Sakhr ibn Juwayriyah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the unbeliever dies, he is shown to the Fire in the morning and the evening. Then he recited: The Fire will be shown to them in the morning and the evening. And when the believer dies, his soul is shown to Paradise in the morning and the evening. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Umar that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him in the morning and the evening. If he is among the people of Paradise, then he is among the people of Paradise, and if he is among the people of Hell, then he is among the people of Hell. And it is said: This is your seat until God raises you to it on the Day of Resurrection.” Al-Farra’ said: In the morning and the evening, according to the amounts of that in this world. This is the statement of Mujahid. He said: In the morning and the evening. He said: From the days of this world. Hammad ibn Muhammad al-Fazari said: A man said to al-Awza’i: “We saw birds emerging from the sea, heading towards the west, small eggs in flocks, and only God knows their number. At dusk, they return, like the rest, black.” He said: Those birds have in their crops the souls of Pharaoh’s family. They are exposed to the Fire morning and evening. They return to their nests with their feathers burned and turned black. At night, their feathers grow white and the black ones scatter. Then they go out in the morning and are exposed to the Fire morning and evening. Then they return to their nests. That is their habit as long as they were in this world. Then, when the Day of Resurrection comes, God the Most High will say: Enter the family of Pharaoh into the severest punishment, which is the Abyss. Al-Awza’i said: It has reached us that they were one million and six hundred thousand. And they went out in the morning is a verbal noun that is made an adverbial phrase for spaciousness. And evening is connected to it, and the speech is complete. Then you begin and on the Day the Hour comes with the word enter in the accusative case, with His saying: Enter. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with they are exposed in the sense of they are exposed to the Fire in this world. and on the Day the Hour comes so you do not stop at it. Nafi`, the people of Medina, Hamzah and Al-Kisa`i read it asإخدلوwith a sukoon on the alif and a kasra on the kha fromخخدلand this is the preferred reading of Abu Ubaid, meaning God commands the angels to admit them, and his evidence is the Fire will be exposed to it. The rest read it asإخدلوwith a sukoon on the alif and a damma on the kha fromدخخل, meaning it will be said to them: Enter O the family of Pharaoh, the most severe torment and this is the preferred reading of Abu Hatim. He said: In the first reading,خلis the first object andإشدis the second object with the genitive omission, and in the second reading it is accusative because it is a vocative complement, and the family of Pharaoh: those who follow his religion and his school of thought, and if those who follow his religion and school of thought are in the most severe torment then that is closer to that. Ibn Masoud narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “A person is born a believer, lives as a believer, and dies as a believer. Among them was John, son of Zechariah, who was born a believer, lived as a believer, and died as a believer. A person is born a disbeliever, lives as a disbeliever, and dies as a disbeliever. Among them was Pharaoh, who was born a disbeliever, lived as a disbeliever, and died as a disbeliever.” Al-Nahhas mentioned this. Al-Farra’ made the verse an inversion of the meaning: Enter Pharaoh’s family into the severest punishment. “The Fire, they will be exposed to it morning and evening.” So he made the exposure to be in the Hereafter, which is contrary to what the majority have stated regarding the order of the speech according to its context as mentioned above. And God knows best.
19:63: The Almighty said: That is the Paradise which meaning this Paradise whose people's conditions We have described We inherit with a light pronunciation. Ya'qub read We inherit with a fatha on the waw and a shaddah on the ra. The preferred pronunciation is the light pronunciation, because the Almighty said: Then We caused the Book to be inherited (Fatir 35:32). Of Our servants is he who was righteous Ibn Abbas said: meaning of he who feared Me and acted in obedience to Me. It was said: It is on the basis of advancement and delay, its meaning: We inherit whoever was righteous among Our servants.
19:64: Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: What prevented you from visiting us more than you visit us? He said: Then this verse was revealed: “And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord” until the end of the verse.” He said: This is a good and rare hadith. Al-Bukhari narrated: Khallad bin Yahya told us, Umar bin Dharr told us: I heard my father narrating on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: What prevented you from visiting us more than you visit us? Then this verse was revealed: And we do not descend except by the command of your Lord until the end of the verse. He said: This was the answer to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mujahid said: “The angel delayed coming to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he came to him and said: What delayed you? He said: How can we come to you when you do not cut your nails, trim your moustaches, clean your eyebrows, or use siwak cleaning of your teeth?” Mujahid said: So the verse was revealed about this. Mujahid also said, as did Qatadah, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Muqatil, and Al-Kalbi: Gabriel was delayed from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when his people asked him about the story of the People of the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit, and he did not know how to answer them, and he hoped that Gabriel would come to him with an answer to what they asked about. Ikrimah said: So he delayed coming to him for forty days. Mujahid said: Twelve nights. It was also said: Fifteen days. It was also said: Thirteen. It was also said: Three days. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "You delayed me until my suspicions worsened and I longed for you, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, said: I was longing, but I am a commanded servant. When I am sent, I descend, and when I am detained, I am detained." So the verse was revealed: And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. And the verse was revealed: By the forenoon, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor does He hate you. (al-Duha 93:1-3). This was mentioned by Al-Tha'labi, Al-Wahidi, Al-Qushayri, and others. It was said: It is report from the people of Paradise that they will say upon entering it: And we do not descend to this Paradise except by the command of your Lord. Based on this, the verse is connected to what came before it. Based on what we mentioned from the sayings, it was said: It is not connected to what came before it, and the Qur'an is a chapter, then the chapters include sentences, and a sentence may be separated from a sentence. And We do not descend means that God the Most High said: Say, O Gabriel, And We do not descend except by the command of your Lord. This has two possible meanings: One of them: If We are commanded, We descend to you. Second: If your Lord commands you, We will send down to you. The command, according to the first, is directed towards the descent, and according to the second, it is directed towards the revelation. And the Almighty’s saying: To Him belongs meaning to God. What is before us means He knows what is before us. And what is behind us and what is between that Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj said: What has passed before us of the worldly affairs, and what will be after us of its affairs and the affairs of the Hereafter. And what is between that of the Barzakh. Qatada and Muqatil said: To Him belongs what is before us of the affairs of the Hereafter. And what is behind us means what has passed of the world. And what is between that means what is between the two blasts and between them is forty years. Al-Akhfash: What is before us means what was before we were created. And what is behind us means what will be after we die. And what is between that means what will be from our creation until we die. It was said: What is before us means reward and punishment and the affairs of the Hereafter. And what is behind us means what has passed of our deeds in the world. And what is between that means what will be from this time until the Day of Resurrection. And a fifth possibility is: What is before us means the sky. And what is behind us means the earth. And what is between that means what is between the sky and the earth. Ibn Abbas said in a narration: To Him belongs what is before us meaning the world to the earth and what is behind us meaning the heavens - and this is the opposite of what came before it - and what is between that meaning the air. The first was mentioned by Al-Mawardi and the second by Al-Qushayri. Al-Zamakhshari: It was said that it is what has passed of our lives and what is to come, and the state in which we are. He did not say: what is between those two because what is meant is what we mentioned, as He said: Neither a pregnant woman nor a mature virgin between that (al-Baqarah 2:68) meaning between what we mentioned. And your Lord is not forgetful meaning forgetful if He wants to send to you He sends. It was said: The meaning is He did not forget even if the revelation was delayed from you. It was said: The meaning is that He is All-Knowing of all things, past and future, and He does not forget anything of them.
19:65: The Almighty said: Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them meaning their Lord and Creator and Creator of what is between them and Owner of what is between them. Just as the management of time is to Him, so is the management of things to Him. So worship Him meaning alone for that. This indicates that the acquisitions of creation are done by God Almighty, as the people of truth say, and this is the true statement, because the Lord in this context cannot be interpreted in any of its meanings except as the Owner. If it is proven that He is the Owner of what is between the heaven and the earth, then the acquisition of creation is included in that, and His worship is obligatory, since it is proven that He is the Owner in the absolute sense, and the reality of worship is obedience with the utmost submission, and no one deserves it except the Owner who is worshipped. And be patient in His worship meaning in His obedience, and do not grieve over the delay of revelation from you, but rather occupy yourself with what you have been commanded to do. The root of istabar is ṣaṭabār, but the combination of the ta’ and the sad became difficult due to their difference, so the ta’ was replaced with a ta’, as you say about fasting: istaṭam. Do you know of anyone named after him? Ibn Abbas said: He means, do you know of a son for him, i.e., someone similar, or an example, or a likeness who deserves the same name as him, which is Ar-Rahman. Mujahid said that it is taken from the word ṣamaḥ. Isra’il narrated on the authority of Samak on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Do you know of anyone named Ar-Rahman? An-Nahhas said: This is the most authentic chain of transmission that I know of that has been narrated in this form, and it is a correct statement, Ar-Rahman is only said for God. I said: This has already been explained in the Basmalah. Praise be to God. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Do you know of anyone with a namesake? He said: For example. Ibn al-Musayyab: Just. Qatada and al-Kalbi: Do you know of anyone who calls God Almighty by other than God, or who is called God except God? And do means no, meaning you do not know. And God knows best.
19:66: God the Almighty said: And man says, 'When I die, will I then be brought forth alive?' Here man is Abi bin Khalaf, he found rotten bones and crushed them with his hand, and said: Muhammad claimed that we will be resurrected after death, said Al-Kalbi, mentioned by Al-Wahidi, Al-Tha'labi and Al-Qushayri. Al-Mahdawi said: It was revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and his companions, and it is the saying of Ibn Abbas. The lam in lasofah kharjahani is for emphasis. It is as if it was said to him: When I die, will I then be brought forth alive? So he said: When I die, will I then be brought forth alive? He said: That is denial, so the lam came in the answer as it was in the first saying, and if he had been a beginner, the lam would not have been included, because it is for emphasis and affirmation, and he is denying the resurrection. Ibn Dhakwan read Idha ma matu as a statement. The rest read it as a question according to their origins with a hamza. Al-Hasan and Abu Haywah read lasofah kharjahani, he said it as a mockery because they do not believe in the resurrection. And the human being here is the infidel.
19:67: The Almighty said: Or does not man remember? That is, does this speaker not remember We created him before That is, before his question and his saying this saying And he was nothing? So the repetition is like the beginning, so it does not contradict. The people of Kufa, except for Asim, and the people of Mecca, Abu Omar and Abu Jaafar, read Or does not remember. Shaibah, Nafi' and Asim read Or does not remember with a light pronunciation. The preferred pronunciation is with a heavy emphasis, and its original form is to remember, because the Almighty said: Only those with understanding will remember (al-Ra'd: 19) and its sisters. In the letter Abi, or does not remember, and this reading is according to the interpretation because it is contrary to the script of the Mushaf. The meaning of remember is to think, and the meaning of remember is to pay attention and know, as al-Nahhas said.
19:68: The Almighty said: By your Lord, We will surely gather them together. He swore by Himself after establishing the proof that He will gather them from their graves to the Hereafter just as He gathers the believers. And the devils means We will gather the devils as their companions. It was said: Every disbeliever will be gathered with a devil in a chain, as He said: Gather those who did wrong and their companions (Saffat: 22). Al-Zamakhshari: The and in and the devils may be for conjunction and in the sense of with, and it is more appropriate in the sense of with. The meaning is that they will be gathered with their companions from the devils who misled them, they will pair every disbeliever with a devil in a chain. If you say that this is if what is meant by humans is the disbelievers in particular, but if what is meant is people in general, then how can it be right to gather them with the devils? I say: If all people are gathered together in one gathering and among them are the disbelievers coupled with the devils, then they will be gathered with the devils just as they were gathered with the disbelievers. If you say: Why are the happy ones not separated from the wretched in the gathering as they were separated from them in the recompense? I say: There is no distinction between them in the gathering place, and they are brought where they kneel around Hell, and they are brought with them to the Fire so that the happy ones may witness the conditions from which God saved them and delivered them, so that their happiness increases, and their joy increases, and they gloat over the enemies of God the Most High and their enemies, so that their distress and regret increases, and what angers them from the happiness of the friends of God and their gloating over them increases. If you say: What is the meaning of bringing them kneeling? I say: If a person interprets it specifically, then the meaning is that they ascend from the gathering place to the shore of Hell, as they were in the state they were in at the gathering, kneeling on their knees, not walking on their feet. This is because the people of the gathering place were described as kneeling, God the Most High said: And you will see every nation kneeling (al-Jathiyah 45:28) in the usual state in the positions of contracts and transfers, of its people kneeling on their knees. Because of the excitement and anxiety in that, and the release of the winds contrary to tranquility, or because of the severity of the matter that befalls them, with which they cannot stand on their feet, so they kneel on their knees. If it is interpreted in general terms, then the meaning is that they kneel on their knees when they reach the shore of Hell. However, kneeling is an implied state, just as they were kneeling on their knees at the station, because it is one of the consequences of stopping for the reckoning, before continuing to the reward and punishment. It is said that the meaning of We will surely bring them around Hell kneeling is kneeling on their knees, according to Mujahid and Qatadah, meaning that due to the severity of what they are in, they are not able to stand. And around Hell may mean inside it, as you say: the people sat around the House, meaning inside it, circling it. So his saying: around Hell according to this may be after entering. And it may be before entering. And kneeling is the plural of jath. It is said: He knelt on his knees, he knelt and he knelt, kneeling, and kneeling on the basis of fa’ul in them. And someone else made him kneel. And a people kneel also, like he sat sitting and people sitting, and he kneeled also with a kasra on the jim because of the kasra after it. And Ibn Abbas said: Kneeling are groups. And Muqatil said: A group, and according to this interpretation it is the plural of Jathwa, Jathwa, and Jathwa are three languages, and they are the collected stones and the collected dirt, so the people of wine are separate, and the people of fornication are separate, and so on, Tarafa said: You see two bodies of dirt, on which are solid sheets of tin arranged. Al-Hasan and Ad-Dahhak said: Kneeling on the knees. According to this interpretation, it is the plural of jath as mentioned above. This is due to the narrowness of the place, meaning that they cannot sit completely. It was also said: Kneeling on their knees for arguing, like the Almighty’s saying: Then on the Day of Resurrection you will surely dispute before your Lord (al-Zumar 39:31). Al-Kumait said: They left their leaders on their knees, while they were below the leaders, horned.
19:69: The Almighty said: Then We will surely extract from every sect meaning, We will extract from every nation and people of religion whoever of them is most rebellious against the Most Merciful An-Nahhas: This verse is problematic in its syntax, because all the reciters read anyone in the nominative case except for Harun the one-eyed reciter, for Sibawayh narrated from him: Then We will surely extract from every sect any one of them in the accusative case, which is the same as anyone of them, so we extract. Abu Ishaq said that there are three opinions regarding the nominative case of anyone of them. Al-Khalil bin Ahmad said, as Sibawayh narrated from him: It is in the nominative case based on the narration, and the meaning is: Then We will extract from every sect the one who is said, because of his rebellion, Which of them is most rebellious against the Most Merciful? Al-Khalil recited, saying: I was refused a house by a girl, so I refused, there is no blame and no one is deprived So I refused, as if it were said to him, Neither is he in difficulty nor is he deprived. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: “I saw Abu Ishaq choosing this statement and approving of it. He said: Because it is the meaning of the statement of the people of interpretation. He claimed that what is “Then We will surely extract from every sect” is Then We will surely extract from every group the most rebellious, then the most rebellious. It is as if he begins the punishment with the most rebellious of them, then the one who follows him. This is the text of Abu Ishaq’s statement regarding the meaning of the verse. Yunus said: We will surely extract is like the verbs that are cancelled, and which one is raised as the beginning. Al-Mahdawi: The verb which is We will surely extract according to Yunus is suspended. Abu Ali said: The meaning of that is that it works in the place of which one is most rebellious, not that it is cancelled. And it is not suspended according to al-Khalil and Sibawayh like We will surely extract, rather it is suspended with verbs of doubt and the like, unless it is certain that it will happen. Sibawayh said: Ayyum is built on the damma because it differs from its sisters in deletion, because if you said: I saw the one who is better and who is better, it would be ugly, until you say who is better, and deletion in ayyum is permissible. Abu Ja`far said: I do not know any grammarian who did not make a mistake in this, and I heard Abu Ishaq say: What shows me that Sibawayh made a mistake in his book except in two places, this is one of them. He said: We know that Sibawayh parsed ayy when it is singular because it is added to a noun, so how can he build it when it is added to a noun?! Abu Ishaq did not mention, as far as I know, except these three opinions. Abu Ali: The construction is required according to Sibawayh's school of thought, because what is recognized by it was deleted from it, which is the pronoun, despite its need for it, just as what is recognized by it was deleted in min qabl and min ba`d despite the need for the added to it, because the relative clause clarifies and explains the relative, just as the added to clarifies and specifies the added to it. Abu Ja`far said: There are four sayings about it other than these three mentioned by Abu Ishaq. Al-Kisa’i said: Lanza`an is used for the meaning, as you say: I put on some clothes and ate some food. Lanza`an does not come after ayyim so it is in the accusative case. Al-Mahdawi added: Rather, the verb, in his view, comes in the place of min kulli shia and his saying: ayyim asd is a renewed sentence raised by the beginning, and Sibawayh does not see the addition of min in the obligatory. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is then Lanza`an by calling, and the meaning of Lanza`an is we call. Al-Mahdawi said: Nady is a verb that is attached if it is followed by a sentence, like I thought so it works in meaning but not in wording. Abu Ja`far said: Abu Bakr ibn Shuqayr narrated that some of the Kufians say that ayyim has the meaning of condition and reward, so what preceded it did not work on it, and the meaning is: Then we will pull out from every group whether they agree or not, as you say: I hit the people, whichever of them got angry, and the meaning is whether they got angry or not. Abu Ja`far said: So these are six sayings, and I heard Ali bin Sulayman narrating on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid who said: Ayyum is related to Shi`ah, so it is raised by the beginning, and the meaning is: Then We will extract from those who cooperated, any of them, meaning from those who cooperated, so We will see which of them is most rebellious against the Most Merciful, and this is a good saying. Al-Kisa’i narrated that cooperation is cooperation. And `atya is accusative for clarification.
19:70: Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of it, burning meaning most deserving of entering the Fire. It is said: He burned, burned, like the thing went away, it went away, and it fell, it fell, it fell, it fell, and Al-Jawhari said: It is said: I burned a man with fire if you put him in the fire and made him burn it, then if you threw him into it as if you wanted to burn him, you say: I burned him with the alif and I burned him with the alif. It was also read and he burns with a blazing fire. And whoever lightens it, it is from their saying: So-and-so was burned with fire with the kasra he was burned, God the Almighty said: They are most deserving of it, burned. Al-Ajjaj said: By God, if it weren't for the fire, we would not have reached it. It is also said: He endured the matter if he suffered its heat and intensity. Al-Tahawi said: Their bravery does not wear out, even if they wage war from time to time. I warmed myself by the fire and prayed there. Abu Zubaydah said: I endured the heat of their war as one endures the chills of a cold. So-and-so does not warm himself in his fire if he is unbearably brave.
19:71: The Almighty said: “There is not one of you but will pass over it. This is an inevitability which must be accomplished by your Lord.” There are five issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: And among you This is an oath, and the and includes it. It is explained by the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: No Muslim will have three children die and be touched by the Fire, except by fulfilling an oath. Al-Zuhri said: It seems that he means this verse: There is not one of you but will pass over it. This was mentioned by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi. His saying: Except by fulfilling an oath is included in the Musnad interpretation, because the meaning of the oath mentioned in this hadith according to the people of knowledge is the saying of God Almighty: There is not one of you but will pass over it. It has been said that what is meant by the oath is the saying of God Almighty: By the scatterers, scatter (al-Dhariyat 51:1) to His saying: “You are only promised truth. And indeed, the Recompense is coming to pass” (al-Dhariyat 51:6). The first is more famous, and the meaning is similar. Second: People differed about the entrance. It was said: The entrance is the entrance. It was narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The roses enter, neither the righteous nor the wicked will remain except that they will enter it, so it will be cool and safe for the believers as it was for Abraham. “Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.” Abu Omar attributed it to him in the book of At-Tamhid. It is the saying of Ibn Abbas, Khalid bin Ma’dan, Ibn Jurayj and others. It was narrated on the authority of Yunus that he used to recite There is not one of you but will pass by it Al-Wurud Al-Dhukul, on the interpretation of the arrival, so some of the narrators made a mistake in it and included it in the Qur’an. In Musnad Al-Darimi on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “People will enter the Fire, then they will emerge from it according to their deeds. Some of them will be as quick as the blink of an eye, then like the wind, then like the presence of a horse, then like a diligent rider on his saddle, then like a man walking briskly.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said regarding this issue to Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq al-Khawarij: As for me and you, we will inevitably return to it. As for me, God will save me from it, but as for you, I do not think He will save you because of your denial. Many scholars feared the realization of entering and ignorance of the beginning, and we have explained this in At-Tadhkirah. A group said: Entering means passing over the Sirat. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas’ud, Ka’b Al-Ahbar, and As-Suddi. As-Suddi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hasan also said: Entering does not mean entering. Rather, you say: I entered Basra, but I did not enter it. He said: Entering means passing over the Sirat. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Some linguists based their opinion on al-Hasan’s school of thought, and they cited as evidence the words of God Almighty: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it (al-Anbiya’: 101). They said: So no one whom God has promised to remove from it will enter the Fire. These people used to recite then with the opening of the thā “We will save those who feared God.” The others, the people of the first article, cited as evidence against them that the meaning of His words: Those will be removed from it is from the torment in it and the burning in it. They said: So whoever enters it without feeling it, nor sensing any pain or suffering from it, is removed from it in reality. They provide evidence with the words of God Almighty: Then We will save those who feared God with the thā with the thā with the thā in the damma, so then indicates salvation after entering. I said: In Sahih Muslim: “Then the bridge will be struck over Hell and intercession will be granted, and they will say, ‘O God, save, save.’ It was said, ‘O Messenger of God, what is the bridge?’ He said, ‘A slippery slope in which there are hooks, claws, and thorns that are in Najd, in which there is a thorn called Al-Sa’dan. The believers will pass by like the blink of an eye, like lightning, like the wind, like a bird, like the best horses and riders. Some will be saved, some will be scratched, some will be sent, and some will be crushed in the fire of Hell.’” The hadith. This is what was used as evidence by those who said that crossing the bridge is the arrival that this verse includes, not entering it. A group said, ‘Rather, it is the arrival of a lookout, insight, and proximity. This is because they will be present at the place of reckoning, which is near Hell, and they will see it and look at it during the state of reckoning. Then God will save those who feared Him from what they looked at, and they will be taken to Paradise. ‘And warn the wrongdoers,’ meaning they will be ordered to the Fire. God Almighty said, ‘And when he reached the water of Madyan’ (al-Qasas 28:23) meaning he looked at it, not entered it. Zuhair said: When they reached the blue water, they put down the sticks of the campers. Hafsa narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: None of the people of Badr and Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire. She said: I said: O Messenger of God, where is the statement of God the Most High: There is not one of you but will pass over it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What is it: Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees. Narrated by Muslim from the hadith of Umm Mubashir, who said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say in the presence of Hafsah. Al-Zajjaj supported this statement with the statement of God the Most High: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it. (Al-Anbiya’: 101). Mujahid said: The believers’ entry into Hell is the fever that afflicts the believer in this world, and it is the believer’s portion of Hell, so he will not be prevented from it. Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, visited a sick person who had been ill, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Be of good cheer, for God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: ‘It is My Fire which I send upon My believing servant so that it may be his portion of the Fire.’” Abu Omar narrated it. He said: Abd al-Warith ibn Sufyan told us. He said: Qasim ibn Asbagh told us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Sayegh told us. He said: Abu Usamah told us. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Abu Salih al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who visited a sick person and mentioned him. And in the hadith: Fever is the believer’s share of Hellfire. A group said: The roses are seen in the grave, from which the winner is saved, and whoever is destined to enter it prays, then he exits from it through intercession or other means of God Almighty’s mercy. They cited as evidence the hadith of Ibn Umar: When one of you dies, his seat will be shown to him in the morning and the evening. The hadith. Waki’ narrated on the authority of Shu’bah on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib on the authority of a man on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Regarding the statement of God the Most High: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, he said: This is addressed to the disbelievers. It was narrated on his authority that he used to recite and there are some of you in response to the verses before it regarding the disbelievers, His statement: “By your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils. Then We will surely bring them around Hell on their knees. Then We will extract from every sect those of them who were most rebellious against the Most Merciful. Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of burning therein.” and there are some of you is how Ikrimah and a group read it, and according to them there is no division in this recitation. A group said: What is meant by of you are the disbelievers, and the meaning is: Say to them, O Muhammad. This interpretation is also easy to understand, and the Kaf in minkum refers back to the Ha in lanhashrunahum wa al-shayatin, then lanhajanhum bayna jahanna majthiyan We will hasten their gathering and the devils, then we will bring them around Hell on their knees. So the Kaf’s return to the Ha is not denied, as this is known in the words of God the Almighty: “And their Lord will give them a pure drink. Indeed, this is your reward, and your effort has been appreciated.” (al-Insan 76:21-22), meaning it was for them, so the Kaf returned to the Ha. Most said: The one being addressed is the entire world, and all must be mentioned, and this is what caused the disagreement about the mention. We have explained the opinions of scholars about it. The apparent meaning of the mention is entering, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Then the Fire will touch him, because the real meaning of touch in the language is contact, except that it will be cool and safe for the believers, and they will escape from it unharmed. Khalid ibn Ma’dan said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they will say: Did not our Lord say: We will return to the Fire? It will be said: You have indeed entered it and found it ashes. I said: This statement gathers the scattered statements, for whoever enters it and is not harmed by its flames and heat has been kept away from it and saved from it. God the Almighty saved us from it by His grace and generosity, and made us among those who entered it and entered it safely, and exited it victorious. If it is said: Will the prophets enter the fire? We say: We do not say this, but we say: All creation enters it as indicated by the hadith of Jabir at the beginning of the chapter. The sinners enter it because of their crimes, and the saints and the fortunate ones because of their intercession, so there is a distance between the two entrances. Ibn al-Anbari said, citing the Mushaf of Uthman and the reading of the common al-Nas 114:It is permissible in the language to return from addressing oneself in absentia to addressing oneself in direct speech, as He said: “And their Lord will give them a pure drink. Indeed, this was your reward, and your effort was appreciated.” [al-Insan 21-22], so he replaced the letter kaf with the letter ha. This meaning was previously mentioned in Yunus. Third: The exception in his saying, peace be upon him: Except for the oath’s fulfillment, may be an interrupted exception: but the oath’s fulfillment, and this is well-known in the speech of the Arabs, and the meaning is that the fire will not touch him at all, and the speech was completed here and then he began, Except for the oath’s fulfillment, meaning but the oath’s fulfillment is necessary in the saying of the Most High: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, which is crossing the bridge or seeing or entering in safety, so there is nothing of touching in that, because of his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: If three of your children die and you are patient with them, they will be a shield for you from the Fire. Paradise means protection and concealment. Whoever is protected from the Fire and concealed from it, it will never touch him at all, and if it touched him, he would not be protected. Fourth: This hadith explains the first because it mentions the Hisbah, and for this reason Malik made it an explanation of it. This second hadith also restricts what Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever has three children die who have not yet reached puberty, they will be shielded from the Fire - or - will enter Paradise. So his saying, peace be upon him: They have not yet reached puberty - and according to the scholars, its meaning is that they have not yet reached puberty and have not yet reached the age of being required to break their oath - is evidence that the children of Muslims are in Paradise - and God knows best - because if mercy descends upon their fathers, it is impossible for them to be shown mercy for the sake of someone who has not been shown mercy. This is a consensus among the scholars that the children of Muslims are in Paradise, and no one disagreed with this except a group that deviated from the Jabariyah and made them subject to the will, and this is an abandoned statement that is rejected by the consensus of the hujjah who cannot be contradicted, and it is not permissible for the likes of them to make a mistake, in addition to what was narrated from the Prophet, peace be upon him, from the reports of trustworthy and just individuals, and that his saying, peace be upon him: “The wretched one is he who was wretched in his mother’s womb, and the happy one is he who was happy in his mother’s womb. The angel descends and writes down his life span, his deeds, and his provision.” The hadith is specific, and whoever among the children of the Muslims dies before earning a living is among those who were happy in their mother’s womb and were not wretched, as evidenced by the hadiths and consensus. Likewise, “The saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Aisha, may God be pleased with her: O Aisha, God created Paradise and created its people while they were in the loins of their fathers, and He created Hell and created its people while they were in the loins of their fathers. It is weak and rejected by consensus and the reports. Talha bin Yahya, who narrates it, is weak and cannot be relied upon. This hadith is one of those that he narrated alone, so it should not be considered. Shu`bah narrated on the authority of Mu`awiyah bin Qurrah bin Iyas al-Muzani on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that a young son of a man from the Ansar died and he was grieved over him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Would you not like to come to a gate of Paradise without finding it opened for you? They said: O Messenger of God, is it specifically for him or for all Muslims? He said: Rather, for all Muslims. Abu Omar said: This is an authentic and correct hadith, meaning what we mentioned with the consensus of the majority, and it contradicts and rejects the hadith of Yahya. Abu Omar said: The correct view in my opinion regarding this hadith and similar reports is that it is for those who maintain performing their obligatory duties, avoid major sins, are patient and seek reward in their misfortune, for the address was not directed in that era except to a people whose situation was mostly as we have described, and they are the Companions, may God be pleased with them all. Al-Naqqash mentioned from some of them that he said: The statement of God, the Most High: “And there is not one of you but will pass over it” was abrogated by His statement: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it (Al-Anbiya’: 101). This is weak, and this is not a place for abrogation. We have already explained that if the Fire does not touch him, then he has been removed from it. And in the report: The fire will say to the believer on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:O believer, your light has extinguished my flame. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: It was an inevitability decreed upon your Lord. Inevitability means the imposition of a decree, meaning that it was inevitable. Decided means that God Almighty decreed it upon you. Ibn Masoud said: meaning an obligatory portion.
19:72: The Almighty said: Then We will save those who feared God meaning We will purify them And We will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees. This is one of the things that indicate that the word enter is entering, because He did not say: And We will admit the wrongdoers. This meaning has already been fully explained. The doctrine is that the one who commits a major sin, even if he enters it, will be punished according to his sin and then he will be saved. The Murji'ah said: He will not enter. The Wa'idiyyah said: He will remain. This has already been explained in more than one place. Asim al-Jahdari and Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah read Then We will save with a light Anja save. This is the reading of Hamid, Ya'qub, and al-Kisa'i. The rest read it with a heavy Thamma with a fat-ha on the Thaa meaning there. Then is an adverb except that it is constructed because it is not complete, so it is constructed as Dha was constructed. The Ha may be for indicating movement, so it is deleted in connection, and it may be for the feminization of the place, so it is maintained in connection as Taa.
19:73: God the Almighty said: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear proofs meaning, to the disbelievers who were previously mentioned in His saying: When I die, will I then be brought forth alive? (Maryam 19:66). And He said about them: And We will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees meaning, when the Qur'an is recited to them, they are strengthened by the world and say: What is the matter with us - if we are on falsehood - having more wealth and more men? Their aim is to introduce doubt into the weak and to make them believe that whoever has a lot of wealth indicates that he is right in his religion, as if they did not see a poor person among the disbelievers or a rich person among the Muslims, and they did not know that God the Almighty has kept His friends away from being deceived by the world and excessively inclined towards it. And clear proofs means fluent words, summarizing meanings, clarifying objectives, either clear, or ambiguous followed by clarification with clear verses, or clarification by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in word or deed. Or the phenomena of the miracle that he challenged with and was not able to oppose. Or arguments and proofs. The correct way is to be a confirmed state, like the Almighty’s saying: And it is the truth, confirming (al-Baqarah 2:91) because the verses of God Almighty are only clear and arguments. Those who disbelieved said meaning the polytheists of Quraysh, Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith and his companions. To those who believed meaning the poor companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they were scrawny, and their lives were rough, and their clothes were shabby, and the polytheists used to comb their hair, oil their heads, and wear their best clothes, so they said: To the believers: Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company? Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaysin, Hamid, and Shibl bin Ibad read maqaman with a damma on the meem, and it is the place of residence, and it is permissible for it to be a source meaning residence. The rest read maqaman with a fatha, meaning a home and a dwelling. It was said: The station is the place where great matters are held, meaning which of the two groups has more prestige and supporters. And the best assembly meaning a council, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. And on his authority also the view, which is the council in the language, and it is the club, and from it the house of the assembly because the polytheists consult in it about their affairs, and his seated one in the club called out to him and said: I call him Al Waleed and Jaafar The word al-nadi refers to the assembly of people and their speaker, as well as the word al-nadiwa a symposium, al-nadi a club, al-forum a forum, and al-muntada a forum. If the people disperse, then it is not a nudi a gathering, as al-Jawhari said.
19:74: The Almighty said: And how many generations before them have We destroyed. That is, a nation and a group. They were better in furnishings. That is, in abundant provisions.
