He said: A branch adorns the back, jet black, thick as the trunk of a palm tree. Furniture is the household goods. It was said: It is the new bedding and the worn-out is what is worn. Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Tusi recited the following: Umm al-Walid has been with us for ages and the furniture of the house has become tattered. Ibn Abbas said: appearance. Muqatil: clothes. Waraya means a beautiful sight. There are five readings for it: The people of Medina read Waraya without a hamza. The people of Kufa read Waraya with a hamza. Yaqub narrated that Talhah read Waraya with one lightened ya. Sufyan narrated on the authority of al-A’mash on the authority of Abu Dhibyan on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They are the best furniture and clothing with a zay. So these are four readings. Abu Ishaq said: It is permissible to say They are the best furniture and clothing with a ya followed by a hamza. An-Nahhas: The reading of the people of Medina in this is good and there are two explanations for it: One of them: that it is from ra’ita then the hamza was lightened and replaced with a ya, and the ya was assimilated into the ya. This was good so that the beginnings of the verses would agree because they are not hamza-less. Based on this, Ibn Abbas said: Ar-ra’i is the viewer, so the meaning is: They are the best furniture and clothing. The second aspect: Their skins are saturated with blessings, so the hamza is not permissible according to this. In the narration of Warsh from Nafi’ and Ibn Dhakwan from Ibn Amir, Warya with the hamza is according to the first aspect. This is the reading of the people of Kufa and Abu Amr from ra’ita according to the original. And the reading of Talha bin Masraf Warya with one light ya’ I think is a mistake. Some grammarians have claimed that its original was hamza, then the hamza was changed to a ya’, then one of the two ya’s was deleted. Al-Mahdawi: It is permissible for it to be Warya then it was changed to a ya’ so it became ra’iya, then the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the ya’ and it was deleted. Some of them have read Warya with the heart, which is the fifth reading. Sibawayh narrated a ra’ meaning saw. Al-Jawhari: From the hamza he made it from the view from ra’ita, which is what the eye saw of a good condition and apparent clothing. Abu Ubaidah recited for Muhammad bin Numayr Al-Thaqafi, saying: The caravans missed you when they saw this beautiful furniture. Whoever does not add a hamza, either it is to soften the hamza or it is from rawayt alawnahum wa jaludhum rayyan, meaning it became full and beautiful. As for the reading of Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, al-A’sam al-Makki, and Yazid al-Barbari, zayya with a zay, it means appearance and beauty. It is possible that it is from zawayt, meaning it gathered, so its root is zawaya, then the waw was changed to a ya’. From this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The earth was gathered for me means it was gathered, meaning that this did not benefit them at all from the punishment of God Almighty, so let these people live as long as they want, for their fate is death and punishment even if they live long, or the immediate punishment that God Almighty will take them with.
19:75: The Almighty said: "Say: Whoever is in error" meaning in disbelief then let the Most Merciful extend for him a term meaning let him leave him in his transgression of ignorance and disbelief, so its wording is the wording of a command but its meaning is report, meaning whoever is in error, the Most Merciful extends for him a term until his deception is prolonged and that is more severe for his punishment. Similar to it is: We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin (AAl Imran 3:178) and His statement: And We leave them in their transgression wandering blindly (Al An'am: 110) and there are many like it, meaning let him live as long as he wants and let his life be extended, for his destiny is death and punishment. This is the ultimate threat and warning. It was said: This is a supplication that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded, you say: Whoever steals my money, let God cut off his hand, so it is a supplication against the thief. It is the answer to the condition. Based on this, His statement: then let him extend is not report. God the Almighty says: Until, when they see what they are promised. He said: They saw because the word who is suitable for both singular and plural. If with the past tense has the meaning of the future, meaning until they see what they are promised. The punishment here is either the victory of the believers over them, so they are punished with the sword and captivity, or the Hour comes and they are sent to the Fire. Then they will know who is worse in position and weaker in soldiers. That is, the truths will be revealed at that time. This is a response to their saying: Which of the two parties is better in position and better in company?
19:76: The Almighty said: And God increases those who are guided in guidance. That is, God makes the believers steadfast in guidance, increases their victory, and sends down verses that increase certainty as a reward for them. It was said: He increases their guidance by their belief in the abrogating and abrogated texts that others disbelieved in. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said the same meaning. A third possibility is: That is, And God increases those who are guided to obedience in guidance to Paradise, and the meaning is close. The meaning of increasing deeds and increasing faith and guidance has been discussed previously in (Al Imran) and others. And the lasting good deeds has been discussed previously in (Al Kahf. Better in reward with your Lord meaning recompense: And better in return meaning in the Hereafter than what the disbelievers boasted about in this world. And the return is a source like the return, meaning and better in return for the one who does it with the reward. It is said: This is more beneficial to you, meaning more beneficial to you. It was said: The best return meaning a place to return, as everyone returns to the work he did.
19:77: The Almighty said: Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our verses? The imams narrated - and the wording is from Muslim - on the authority of Khabbab, who said: I had a debt from Al-Aas bin Wa’il, so I went to him to collect it, and he said to me: I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad. He said: I said to him: I will not disbelieve in him until you die and are resurrected. He said: And I will be resurrected after death?! Then I will pay you when you return to wealth and children. Wakee' said: This is what Al-A'mash said, so this verse was revealed: Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, I will surely be given wealth and children" until His saying: "And he will come to Us alone." In another narration he said: I was a blacksmith in the pre-Islamic era, so I worked for Al-'As bin Wa'il, so I came to him to collect his wages. Al-Bukhari also narrated it. Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: Khabbab was a blacksmith, so he made jewelry for Al-'As and then collected his wages. Al-'As said: I do not have anything to pay you today. Khabbab said: I will not leave you until you pay me. Al-'As said: O Khabbab, what is the matter with you?! You were not like this, although you were a good requester. Khabbab said: I was on your religion, but today I am on the religion of Islam and have left your religion. He said: Do you not claim that there is gold, silver and silk in Paradise? Khabbab said: Yes. He said: Then delay me until I pay you in Paradise - mockingly - for by God, if what you say is true, then I will pay you in it, and by God, you, Khabbab, and your companions are not more deserving of it than me. Then God Almighty revealed: Have you seen he who disbelieves in Our verses? meaning Al-Aas bin Wa’il, the verses.
19:78: He has revealed the unseen. Ibn Abbas said: Look in the Preserved Tablet?!. Mujahid said: He knows the unseen so that he knows whether he is in Paradise or not?! Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Gracious? Qatada and Ath-Thawri said: That is, a righteous deed. It was said: It is monotheism. It was said: It is from the promise. Al-Kalbi said: He made a covenant with God Almighty that he would enter Paradise. No was responded to him, that is, that was not the case, he did not reveal the unseen, and he did not take a covenant with the Most Gracious, and the discussion was completed when he said: No. Al-Hasan said: The verses were revealed about Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira. The first is more correct because it is recorded in the Sahihs. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read and a child with a damma on the waw, and the rest read it with a fatha. There are two differences regarding the damma and fatha: One of them: They are two languages with the same meaning, it is said child and child just as it is said nonsense and nonsense. Al-Harith bin Halza said: I have seen people who have had wealth and children. Another said: I wish so-and-so was in his mother's womb, and I wish so-and-so was the son of a donkey The second: Qais makes the word child with the damma plural and the word child with the fatha singular. Al-Mawardi said: “In the words of God Almighty: “I will surely be given wealth and children,” there are two aspects: One: He meant in Paradise mocking what God Almighty promised for obeying and worshipping Him, said Al-Kalbi. The second: He meant in this world, which is the opinion of the majority, and there are two possible aspects to it: One: If I persist in the religion of my fathers and worship my gods, I will be given wealth and children. The second: If I were on falsehood, I would not have been given wealth and children.” I said: Al-Kalbi’s statement is more similar to the apparent meaning of the hadiths, rather their text indicates that. Masruq said: I heard Khabbab bin Al-Arat say: I came to Al-Aas bin Wael Al-Sahmi to demand a right that I owed him. He said: I will not give you anything until you disbelieve in Muhammad. I said: Not until you die and are resurrected. He said: Will I die and then be resurrected?! I said: Yes. He said: I have wealth and children there so I will pay you. Then this verse was revealed. Al-Tirmidhi said: I said: Yes. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. God the Almighty said: He has revealed the unseen. Its alif is an interrogative alif because am comes after it, and its meaning is rebuke. Its original form is Atala'a, but the second alif was deleted because it is an alif of connection. If it is said: Why did they not add a long vowel after the alif and say Atala'a as they said: "Say: Al-Hamd" (al-Naml 27:59), Aal-Dhikrān haram (Al-An'am: 143)? It is said to him: The original form in this was God as Aal-Dhikrān, so they replaced the second alif with a long vowel to differentiate between the interrogative and the declarative. This is because if they had said: God is the best without a long vowel, the interrogative would have been confused with the declarative. They did not need this long vowel in His statement: Atala'a because the alif of interrogation is open and the alif of declarative is closed. This is because you say in interrogative: Atala'a? Attara'a? Ashtafa'a? Astaghfirut? with the alif open, and you say in declarative: Atala'a, Iftara'a, Ashtafa'a, Astaghfirut lahum with the kasra. So they made the difference with the fatha and the kasra and did not need another difference.
19:79: The Almighty's saying: No The first half does not mention No, but it is mentioned in the second half. It has two meanings: One: meaning truly. The second: meaning no. So if it means truly, it is permissible to stop at what precedes it, then begin No meaning truly. And if it means no, it is permissible to stop at No, as in this verse, because the meaning is: No, the matter is not like this. And it is permissible to stop at His saying: A covenant and begin No meaning truly We will write down what he says. And likewise the Almighty's saying: "Perhaps I will do righteousness in that which I left behind. No" (Al-Mu'minun: 100) It is permissible to stop at No and at I left. And His saying: And they have a sin against me, so I fear that they will kill me * He said, No The stop at No is because the meaning is, no - and the matter is not as you think So go with Our verses, indeed We are with you, listening (Ash-Shu'ara: 15). So the truth has no place in this meaning. Al-Farraa said: Kala is like sawfa because it is a conjunction, and it is a letter of response, so it is as if it were na’am and la in sufficiency. He said: If you make it a conjunction for what comes after it, you do not stop on it, like saying: Kala, by the Lord of the Kaaba. Do not stop on Kala, because it is like ay, by the Lord of the Kaaba. God the Almighty said: Kala, by the moon (al-Muddaththir 74:32). Stopping on Kala is ugly because it is a conjunction for the oath. Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Sa’dan used to say the same thing about Kala as Al-Farraa said. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning of Kala is deterrence and warning. Abu Bakr ibn Al-Anbari said: I heard Abu Al-Abbas say: You do not stop on “Kala throughout the Qur’an, because it is a response and the benefit comes in what comes after it.” The first statement is the statement of the scholars of tafsir. God Almighty says: We will record what he says. That is, We will record what he says and reward him for it in the Hereafter. And We will extend for him the punishment. That is, We will increase his punishment upon his punishment.
19:80: And We shall inherit from him what he says meaning, We shall take away from him what We gave him in this world of wealth and children. Ibn Abbas and others said: meaning, We shall inherit from him the wealth and children after We have destroyed him. It was also said: We shall deprive him of what he desired in the Hereafter of wealth and children, and We shall give it to another Muslim. And he shall come to Us alone meaning, alone, with no wealth, children, or clan to support him.
19:81: The Almighty said: And they took besides God gods that they might be for them a source of strength meaning the polytheists of Quraysh. And honor means helpers and protection, meaning children. And honor also means generous rain, as Al-Harawi said. The apparent meaning of the speech is that honor refers to the gods that they worshipped besides God. And it is singular because it means a source, meaning that they might attain honor through them and protect themselves from the punishment of God.
19:82: Then God the Almighty said: No meaning that the matter is not as they thought and imagined, but they disbelieve in their worship, meaning that they deny that they worshipped idols, or the gods deny that the polytheists worshipped them, as He said: We declare to You that they have disavowed us (al-Qasas 28:63). This is because idols are inanimate objects that do not know how to worship. And they will be against them meaning helpers in their dispute and denial. According to Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak: They will be enemies to them. Ibn Zayd: They will be a trial for them, so their gods will be gathered, and minds will be created for them so that they will speak, and say: O Lord, punish these who worshipped us instead of You. No here may mean no, or it may mean truly, meaning truly they will disbelieve in their worship. Abu Nahik read: No, they will disbelieve with the tanween. It was also narrated from him with the damma and fatha of the kaf. Al-Mahdawi said: Kala is a deterrent, warning, alert and response to a previous statement. It may also be used to confirm what comes after it and alert to it, as in His statement: No indeed, man transgresses (al-Alaq 96:6). So one should not stop on it in this way, and stop on it in the first meaning. If both meanings are suitable for it, then it is permissible to stop on it and begin with it. So whoever adds the nun to Kala in His statement: No indeed, they will disbelieve in their worship with the opening of the kaf, then it is the source of Kul and its accusative with an implied verb, and the meaning is all this opinion and belief No, meaning their taking of gods to be for them a source of honor, so he stops on this with honor and with Kala. And likewise in the reading of the group, because it is suitable for responding to what comes before it and confirming what comes after it. And whoever narrated the closing of the kaf with the nun, then it is also accusative with an implied verb, as if he said: They will disbelieve No indeed, they will disbelieve in their worship meaning the gods. I said: Four meanings are obtained in Kala: confirmation, which is that it means truly, negation, warning, and a conjunction for an oath, and one should only stop at the first of them. Al-Kisa'i said: La negates only, and Kala negates one thing and affirms another. So if it is said: I ate dates, you say: No, I ate honey, not dates. So in this word, what precedes it is negated, and what follows it is confirmed. The opposite can be singular or plural, like the enemy and the messenger. It was said: The opposite occurred in the place of a source, meaning that they will be a help to them, so this is why it was not pluralized. This is in contrast to His statement: So that they may be for them a strength. And strength is a source, so is what occurs in contrast to it. Then it was said: The verse is about idol worshippers, so he treated idols as those who have reason, following the assumption of the infidels. It was said: It is about those who worship Christ, or the angels, or the jinn, or the devils, and God knows best.
19:83: The Almighty said: Have you not seen that We have sent the devils against the disbelievers? That is, We have given them power over them to seduce them, when He said to Satan: And incite with your voice whomever you can among them (al-Isra’ 17:64). It was said that We sent means We left, it is said: I sent the camel, meaning I left it, meaning We left the devils with them and did not protect them from accepting them. Al-Zajjaj: We decreed. To incite them Ibn Abbas said: To incite them from obedience to disobedience. And from him: To tempt them with evil: Go on, go on with this matter, until you throw them into the fire. The first was narrated by Al-Tha'labi, and the second by Al-Mawardi, and the meaning is the same. Ad-Dahhak: To tempt them, to seduce them. Mujahid: To disintegrate them, and its origin is movement and boiling, and from it is the report narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: He stood up to pray, and his stomach was sizzling like the sizzling of a cauldron from crying. The pot was boiling violently. Azz means to excite and tempt. God Almighty said: Have you not seen that We have sent the devils upon the disbelievers, to incite them with agitation? That is, to tempt them to sin. Azz means to mix. Azz means to combine some of it with others. Al-Jawhari said this.
19:84: The Almighty said: So do not hasten them meaning, do not ask for punishment for them. We only count for them a [decade] Al-Kalbi said: Their terms, meaning the days, nights, months, and years until the end of the term of punishment. Ad-Dahhak said: Breaths. Ibn Abbas: That is, We count their breaths in this world as We count their years. It was said: Steps. It was said: Pleasures. It was said: Moments. It was said: Hours. Qatrib said: We count their deeds. It was said: Do not hasten them, for We only delay them so that they may increase in sin. It was narrated that Al-Ma'mun recited this Surah, and passed by this verse while a group of jurists were with him, so he motioned with his head to Ibn As-Sammak to admonish him, so he said: If the breaths are counted, and they have no extension, then how quickly they will run out. It was said in this meaning: Your life is a series of breaths, and every time one of them passes, a part of you is diminished. What kills you every night brings you back to life, and what drives you to do what is meant to mock you It is said: The breaths of the son of Adam between the day and the night are twenty-four thousand breaths: twelve thousand breaths in the day, and twelve thousand in the night - and God knows best - so they are counted and enumerated, and they have a known number, and they have no extension, so how quickly they run out.
19:85: The Almighty’s saying: The Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation. There is an omission in the speech, meaning to the Paradise of the Most Merciful, and the abode of His honor. Like His saying: Indeed, I am going to my Lord, and He will guide me. (al-Saffat 37:99) and as in the report: Whoever migrates for the sake of God and His Messenger, his migration is for the sake of God and His Messenger. Wafd is a noun for those who come, just as it is said: fasting, breaking the fast, and visiting. It is the plural of waafid, like rakab and rakib, sahib and sahib. It is from wafad yafida wafdana wawfud and wafada, if he went out to a king for a conquest or an important matter. Al-Jawhari: It is said that someone came to the prince, meaning he came as a messenger, so he is a waafid. The plural is wafd like sahib and sahib. The plural of wafd is wafd and wufud, and the noun is wafada, and I sent him to the prince, meaning I sent him. In the interpretation: Wafda means riders on the purebred horses of their obedience. This is because the one who comes is usually a rider, and wafd is the riders, and it is singular, because it is a source. Ibn Jurayj: Wafda on purebred horses. Amr ibn Qays al-Mala’i said: When the believer comes out of his grave, his deeds will meet him in the best form and the sweetest scent, and he will say: Do you know me? He will say: No - except that God has made your scent pleasant and your form beautiful. He will say: That is how I was in this world, I am your good deeds, as long as I rode you in this world, ride me today, and he will recite: The Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation (10:31). And the disbeliever will be met by his deeds in the ugliest form and the most foul odor, and he will say: Do you recognize me? He will say: No - except that God has made your form ugly and your odor foul. He will say: That is how I was in this world, I am your evil deeds, as long as I rode you in this world, and today I will ride you.” He will recite: And they will bear their burdens on their backs (10:31). And its chain of transmission is not authentic. Ibn al-Arabi said this in Siraj al-Muridin. Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahim ibn Abd al-Karim al-Qushayri mentioned this report in his interpretation, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, with its wording and meaning. He also said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Whoever loves horses will come to God Almighty on horses that do not defecate or urinate, their reins made of red ruby, green chrysolite, and white pearls, and their saddles made of brocade and silk. Whoever loves riding camels will ride on steeds that do not defecate or urinate, their reins made of ruby and chrysolite. Whoever loves riding ships will ride on ships made of ruby. They will be safe from drowning and from terrors. He also said on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: "When the verse was revealed, Ali may God be pleased with him said: O Messenger of God! I have seen the kings and their delegations, but I have not seen a delegation except on horseback. So what is the delegation of God? The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said: They will not be gathered on their feet nor will they be driven, but they will be given she-camels from the she-camels of Paradise, the likes of which no creation has ever seen, their saddles made of gold and their reins made of emerald. They will ride them until they knock on the door of Paradise." Al-Tha'labi's wording in this report from Ali is clearer. "And Ali said when this verse was revealed, I said: O Messenger of God! I have seen the kings and their delegations, but I have not seen a delegation except on horseback. He said: O Ali, when the one who returns from God the Most High, the angels will meet the believers with she-camels with white saddles and golden reins. On each mount there will be a garment that the world does not equal. So each believer will wear a garment, then their mounts will travel with them and the she-camels will fall with them until they reach Paradise, and the angels will meet them, saying: 'Peace be upon you. You have done well, so enter it to abide eternally.'" (al-Zumar 39:73) I said: This report states that they will not ride or wear clothes except from the place of standing. As for when they exit the graves, they will walk barefoot, naked and uncircumcised to the place of standing, based on the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) delivered a sermon among us and said: O people, you will be gathered before God, the Most High, barefoot, naked and uncircumcised. The hadith was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, and will be mentioned in full in Surat Al-Mu'minun, God willing. It was mentioned in Al-Imran from the hadith of Abdullah bin Unays with the same meaning, and praise be to God. It is not far-fetched that both states will be found for the fortunate ones, so the hadith of Ibn Abbas would be specific, and God knows best. Abu Hurairah said: A delegation on camels. Ibn Abbas said: Riders who will be brought she-camels from Paradise, with saddles of gold and saddles and reins of emerald, and they will be gathered on them. Ali said: By God, they will not be gathered on their feet, but on she-camels with saddles of gold and saddles of rubies. If they intend to carry them, they will move, and if they move them, they will fly. It was said: They will be gathered on whatever they like of camels, horses or ships, as mentioned above from Ibn Abbas. And God knows best. It was said: He said that because it is the custom of delegations among the Arabs to come with good report and await rewards, so the pious await giving and reward.
19:86: And We shall drive the criminals to Hell in droves. Driving is urging people to walk. And driving is thirsty, as Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurairah may God be pleased with them, and Al-Hasan said. Al-Akhfash, Al-Farra', and Ibn Al-A'rabi said: barefoot, walking. It was also said: in groups. Al-Azhari said: that is, thirsty walking, like camels drinking water, so it is said: the tribe of so-and-so came. Al-Qushayri said: And his saying: driving indicates thirst, because water is usually brought to those who are thirsty. And in the interpretation: thirsty walking, their necks are cut from thirst, and if the criminals are driven to Hell, then the righteous are gathered to Paradise. It was also said: driving means the arrivals, like you say: I came to you to honor you, that is, to honor you, that is, We will drive them to drink from Hell. I said: There is no contradiction between these sayings, for they are driven thirsty, barefoot, and walking in groups. Ibn Arafa said: The rose is the people who go to water, so the thirsty were called roses because they sought to go to water, just as you say: a people of fasting, meaning fasting, and a people of visitor, meaning visitors. It is a noun in the form of a source, and the singular of them is a visitor. The rose is also a group of birds and camels who go to water. The rose is the water that is brought to drink. This is from the category of alluding from one thing to another. The rose is a part of the Qur’an, it is said: I read my rose. The rose is the day of fever if it takes its owner for a while. So it appears to be a common word. The poet said, describing Qalib: He is ambitious if the rose is planted on it Any water-seeker who wants water.
19:87: The Almighty's saying: They do not possess intercession meaning these disbelievers do not possess intercession for anyone except for he who has made a covenant with the Most Merciful and they are the Muslims, so they possess intercession, so it is an exception of something from something other than its type, meaning but whoever has made a covenant with the Most Merciful intercedes, so whoever is in the accusative case according to this. It was said: It is in the nominative case as a substitute for the waw in they possess, meaning no one possesses intercession with God except for he who has made a covenant with the Most Merciful then he possesses, and according to this the exception is connected. And the criminals in His saying: And We will drive the criminals to Hell in droves includes the disbelievers and the sinners, then He informed that they do not possess intercession except the sinful believers, so they possess it by interceding for them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I will continue to intercede until I say, ‘O Lord, intercede for me on behalf of those who say, ‘There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God.’ He will say, ‘O Muhammad, it is not yours, but mine.’” Narrated by Muslim with the same meaning, and it has been mentioned before. The narrations have shown that the people of virtue, knowledge, and righteousness intercede and they are granted intercession. According to the first opinion, the statement is connected to His statement, And they have taken other gods besides God that they may be a source of honor for them. So the intercession of idol worshippers will not be accepted for anyone tomorrow, nor will the intercession of idols be accepted for anyone, and they will not possess the intercession of anyone for them, meaning no intercession will benefit them, as He said, So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them. (al-Muddaththir 74:48). It was said, meaning, We will gather the righteous and the criminals, and no one will possess the intercession except for one who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, meaning if God permits him to intercede, as He said, Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? (al-Baqarah 2:255). This covenant is what He said, Or has he taken a covenant from the Most Merciful? It is a comprehensive expression for faith and all the good deeds by which its owner reaches the level of one who intercedes. Ibn Abbas said: The covenant is there is no god but God. Muqatil and Ibn Abbas also said: No one intercedes except the one who testifies that there is no god but God, and disavows all power and strength except for God, and hopes for none but God the Most High. Ibn Masoud said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say to his companions: Is any of you unable to make a covenant with God every morning and evening? It was said: O Messenger of God, what is that? He said: He says every morning and evening: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, I covenant with You in this life that I bear witness that there is no god but You alone, without partner, and that Muhammad is Your servant and Messenger. Do not leave me to myself, for if You leave me to myself, You will distance me from good and bring me closer to evil. I trust only in Your mercy. So make for me a covenant with You that You will fulfill on the Day of Resurrection, for You do not fail to fulfill Your promise. When he says that, God will set a seal on it and place it under the Throne. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will call out, Where are those who have a covenant with God? So he will stand and enter Paradise.
19:88: The Almighty said: And they say, 'The Most Gracious has taken a son' meaning the Jews and Christians, and whoever claims that the angels are daughters of God. Yahya, Al-A'mash, Hamza, Al-Kisa'i, Asim, and Khalaf read: child with a damma on the waw and a sukoon on the lam, in four places: From this surah, the Almighty said: I will surely be given wealth and children (Maryam 19:77), which has been mentioned previously, and His saying: That they attribute to the Most Gracious a son * And it is not befitting for the Most Gracious to take a son. And in Surah Nuh: His wealth and his son (Nuh: 21). Ibn Kathir, Mujahid, Hamid, Abu Amr, and Ya'qub agreed with them in (Nuh) in particular. The rest in all of them with a fatha on the waw and the lam, and they are two languages like Arabs and Arabs and Ajam and Ajam. He said: I have seen people who have had wealth and children. Another said: I wish so-and-so was in his mother's womb. I wish so-and-so was the son of a donkey. Al-Nabigha said about the meaning of this: Wait, may all peoples, wealth and children be sacrificed for you. Fath. Qais make the word walad with the dammah a plural and the word walad with the fathah a singular. Al-Jawhari said: The word walad may be singular and plural, and so is the word walad with the dammah. And among the proverbs of Banu Asad: Your son is from my blood, your heels. And the word walad may be the plural of walad like asad and asad. And the word walad with the kasrah is a dialect for walad. An-Nahhas said: Abu Ubaidah differentiated between them, and he claimed that the word walad refers to both the family and the child. Abu Ja`far said: This is a rejected statement that no one among the linguists knows, and the word walad and walad can only be the son of a man, and his son is his son, except that walad is more common in the speech of the Arabs, as he said: Wait, may all nations, wealth and children be sacrificed for you. Abu Ja`far said: I heard Muhammad ibn al-Walid say: It is permissible for a boy to be the plural of boy, just as one says wathn and wathn, and lion and lion, and it is permissible for a boy and boy to have one meaning, just as one says ajam and ajam, and arab and arab, as mentioned above.
19:89: The Almighty said: You have certainly done something terrible meaning a great evil, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others. Al-Jawhari said: Id and idda are the calamity and the terrible matter, and from it the Almighty's saying: You have certainly done something terrible and likewise id is like fa'il. The plural of idda is idd. And ada fulan dahiyya ta'dahu iddan with the fat-ha and id also means severity. And id means dominance and strength. The rajaz poet said: I was given a hardship and a painful death after I had been strong and patient. His words ended. Abu Abdullah and Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Salami read Ada with the opening of the hamza. An-Nahhas / It is said Ada yu’da adaan so he is Ada and the noun is Id if he comes with something great and reprehensible. The rajaz poet said: My peers have suffered a terrible, terrible punishment from me. On the authority of Ghair al-Nahhas, al-Tha’labi: There are three languages in it: Ida with a kasra, which is the reading of the common people, Ada with a fatha, which is the reading of al-Salami, and Aad like Maad, which is a language of some Arabs. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Abu al-Aaliyah, and it seems to be taken from the word weight. It is said: The pregnancy weighed him down, it weighed him down.
19:90: The Almighty's saying: The heavens almost The reading of the general public here and in (Ash-Shura) is with the letter taa. The reading of Nafi', Yahya and Al-Kisa'i is yakkad with the letter yaa because the verb came before it. They almost burst from it means they crack. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Hafs and others read it with a taa after the yaa and stressed the taa from the word the breaking here and in (Ash-Shura). Hamzah and Ibn Amir agreed with them in (Ash-Shura). They read here yafitarna from the breaking and Abu Amr, Abu Bakr and Al-Mufaddal read it in the two surahs. It is the choice of Abu Ubaid, because of the Almighty's saying: When the sky is split (al-Infitar 82:1) and His saying: The sky is split by it (al-Muzzammil 73:18). And His saying: And the earth is split means it is cracked. And the mountains collapse in devastation Ibn Abbas said: Destruction means falling with a loud sound. In the hadith: O God, I seek refuge in You from destruction and collapse. Shammar said: Ahmad bin Ghayath al-Marwazi said: Demolition is demolition and collapse is an eclipse. Al-Layth said: It is severe destruction, like a wall that collapses once. It is said: The matter destroyed me and destroyed my pillar, meaning it broke me and reached me. Al-Harawi said this. Al-Jawhari: The collapse of the building means it broke and weakened it. The calamity destroyed it, meaning its pillar weakened. The mountain collapsed, meaning it broke. Al-Asma’i: The weak man is the weak man. A man says to another man when he threatens him: I am not weak. Ibn al-A’rabi said: The weak man is the generous and noble one. As for the weak coward, he is the weak man with a kasra. He recited: They are not easy in wars if the speech is complicated over the burning coals The rumbling is the sound of a wall or something similar falling. You say from it: hud yahdhud with a kasra hadidan. The hadd is a sound that the people of the coast hear, coming to them from the sea, making a roar on the ground. An earthquake may be one of them, and its roar is its rumbling. An-Nahhas: hada is a verbal noun, because the meaning of takhra is to collapse. Another said: a state, meaning crushed.
19:91: That they invoke a son for the Most Gracious "That is in the accusative case according to Al-Farra' with the meaning of because they invoke and from that they invoke, so the position of that" is in the accusative case due to the omission of the preposition. Al-Farra' claimed that Al-Kisa'i said: It is in the genitive case due to the estimation of the preposition. Ibn Al-Mubarak mentioned: Musa'ar told us, on the authority of Wasil, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah, who said: Abdullah bin Mas'oud said: The mountain says to the mountain, "O so-and-so, did anyone remember God today? If it says, Yes," be pleased with him. Then Abdullah recited, "And they say, 'The Most Gracious has taken a son'" 2:17, and said: Do you think they hear falsehood and do not hear good?! He said: Aouf told me on the authority of Ghalib bin Ajrad who said: A man from the people of Ash-Sham told me in the mosque of Mina, he said: When God the Most High created the earth and created the trees in it, there was not a tree on earth that the children of Adam came to except that they gained benefit from it, and they had benefit from it, so the earth and the trees remained like that until the wicked ones of the children of Adam spoke that great word, their saying: The Most Gracious has taken a son, so when they said it, the earth trembled and the trees trembled. Ibn Abbas said: The mountains and the trees in them trembled, and the seas and the whales in them trembled, so from that came thorns in the whales and thorns in the trees. Ibn Abbas also said and Kaab: The heavens and the earth and the mountains were terrified, and all the creatures except the two heavy things, and they were about to disappear, and the angels became angry and Hell was blazing, and the trees trembled, and the earth became dark and barren when they said: God has taken a son. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: The enemies of God almost brought about the Hour upon us, because of the words of God the Almighty: "The heavens almost burst from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in devastation, because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son." Ibn al-Arabi said: And it is true, for it is a great statement that was preceded by fate and destiny. And were it not that the Creator, blessed and exalted be He, is not abased by the disbelief of the disbeliever, nor raised by the faith of the believer, nor does this increase His kingdom, just as that does not decrease His kingdom, none of this would have occurred on tongues. But He is the Holy, the Wise, the Forbearing, so He did not care after that about what the falsifiers say.
19:92: The Almighty’s saying: It is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son. There are four issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful to take a son negates the existence of a son for Himself, glory be to Him, the Most High, because a son requires gender and occurrence, as we explained in (Al-Baqarah), meaning that is not appropriate for Him, nor is He described with it, nor is it permissible for Him, because a son does not come except from a father who has a father and an origin, and God, glory be to Him, is far above that and is sanctified. He said: In the head of a nobleman, a towering phoenix, beyond which there is no plain or mountain
19:93: There is none in the heavens and the earth but will come to the Most Merciful as a servant. "Inna is a negative meaning what," meaning there is none in the heavens and the earth but will come on the Day of Resurrection acknowledging His servitude, submissive and humiliated, as He said: "And all will come to Him in humiliation" (al-Naml 27:87) meaning humiliated and submissive, meaning all of creation is His servants, so how can one of them be His son, the Almighty, the Exalted, far above what the wrongdoers and deniers say, far above. "Ati is written with a yaa," but the original is the tanween, but it was deleted for the sake of lightness and it was added. Second: In this verse is evidence that it is not permissible for the son to be owned by the father, contrary to those who said: He buys him and owns him and does not free him unless he frees him. God Almighty has made clear the contradiction between children and ownership, so if the father owns his son through some kind of disposition, he is freed on his behalf. The evidence for this from this verse is that God Almighty made sonship and slavery in opposite ends, so He denied one and affirmed the other, and if they were combined, this statement would not have any benefit that can be used as evidence. In the authentic hadith: A son cannot repay his father unless he finds him a slave, buys him, and frees him. Narrated by Muslim. So if the father does not own his son despite his status over him, then the son is more deserving of the father’s lack of ownership due to his inability to do so. Third: Ishaq bin Rahawayh interpreted his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: Whoever frees a share of his in a slave means that what is meant by it is the male slaves and not the female slaves, so it is not complete for whoever frees a share of a female slave, and this is contrary to what the majority of the predecessors and those who came after them went with, as they did not differentiate between the male and the female, because the word slave is meant by the gender, as God Almighty said: There is none in the heavens and the earth but comes to the Most Merciful as a slave for it certainly includes the male and female slave. And Ishaq held fast to the fact that he narrated the slave in the feminine. Fourth: Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God Almighty says: “The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to do so, and he insulted Me, and he had no right to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying, ‘He will not restore Me as He began me,’ and the first creation is not easier for Me than His restoration. As for his insulting Me, it is his saying, ‘God has taken a son,’ while I am the One, the Self-Sufficient. He neither begets nor is He begotten, and there is none comparable to Me.” This has been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah and elsewhere, and repeating it in a place like this is very good.
19:94: The Almighty says: He has counted them meaning He knows their number. And He counted them completely is an emphasis, meaning that not one of them is hidden from Him. I said: We have found among His names, glory be to Him, Al-Muhsin, I mean in the Sunnah from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, and the derivation of this verb indicates it. Professor Abu Ishaq Al-Isfarayini said: Among them is Al-Muhsin, and it is distinguished by the fact that He is not distracted by multitude from knowledge, such as the brightness of light, the intensity of the wind, and the falling of leaves. He knows at that time the parts of the movements in every leaf. How could He not know when He is the One who creates, and He said: Does He not know who created? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted? (al-Mulk 67:14). It was found in the interpretation of Ibn Abbas that the meaning of He has counted them and counted them a [precise] count means that they acknowledged His servitude and bore witness to His Lordship.
19:95: The Almighty said: And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone meaning one with no supporter and no wealth to benefit him, as the Almighty said: The Day when neither wealth nor children will be of any benefit * Except for him who comes to God with a sound heart (Ash-Shu'ara: 88-89) So nothing will benefit him except what he has done of deeds. And He said: And all of them will come to Him in the wording of all and in the meaning they came to Him. Al-Qushayri said: This indicates that you would not be pleased for yourselves with the enslavement of your children, and all of them are His slaves, so how could you be pleased for Him with what you would not be pleased for yourselves? And He responded to them in a similar matter, that they would not be pleased for themselves with daughters, and they say: The angels are the daughters of God, God is exalted above that, and their saying: The idols are the daughters of God. And He said: So whatever was for their partners does not reach God, and whatever was for God reaches their partners (Al-An'am: 136).
19:96: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who have believed meaning truthful. And done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection meaning love in the hearts of His servants. As narrated by Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Sa`d and Abu Hurayrah: that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, [said]: “If God loves a servant, He calls Gabriel, ‘I have loved so-and-so, so love him.’ He said: ‘So he calls out in the heavens, and then love descends for him among the people of the earth. This is what God, the Most High, says: ‘The Most Merciful will bestow love upon them.’ And if God hates a servant, He calls Gabriel, ‘I have hated so-and-so.’ He calls out in the heavens, and then hatred descends for him on the earth.” He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. It was narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim with a similar meaning, and by Malik in al-Muwatta’ and in Nawadir al-Usul. Abu Bakr ibn Sabeq al-Umawi told us: Abu Malik al-Junbi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God has given the believer familiarity, affection and love in the hearts of the righteous and the angels who are close to Him - then he recited - ‘Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.’” There is disagreement about who it was revealed to. It was said that it was about Ali, may God be pleased with him. Al-Bara’ bin Azib narrated that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali bin Abi Talib: Say, O Ali, O God, make for me a covenant with You and make for me in the hearts of the believers affection. So the verse was revealed, as mentioned by al-Tha’labi. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. God the Almighty made for him affection in the hearts of the servants. No believer meets him without respecting him, and no polytheist or hypocrite meets him without respecting him. Harim ibn Hayyan used to say: No one turns his heart to God the Almighty except that God the Almighty turns the hearts of the people of faith to him, until He grants him their affection and mercy. It was said: God the Almighty makes for them affection in the hearts of the believers and the angels on the Day of Resurrection. I said: If he is beloved in this world, he will be so in the Hereafter, for God Almighty loves only a pious believer, and is not pleased with anyone but one who is sincere and pure. May God Almighty make us among them by His grace and generosity. Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God Almighty loves a servant, He calls Gabriel, peace be upon him, and says: ‘I love so-and-so, so love him.’ Gabriel loves him, then he calls out in the heavens and says: ‘God loves so-and-so, so love him.’ The people of the heavens love him. Then acceptance is placed for him on earth. And when He hates a servant, He calls Gabriel, peace be upon him, and says: ‘I hate so-and-so, so hate him.’ Gabriel hates him, then he calls out to the people of the heavens: ‘God hates so-and-so, so hate him.’ They hate him, then hatred is placed for him on earth.”
19:97: The Almighty said: We have only made it easy for you in your language meaning the Qur'an, meaning We explained it in your Arabic language and made it easy for those who ponder and reflect on it. It was also said: We revealed it to him in the Arabic language so that it would be easy for them to understand. That you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a quarrelsome people Al-Ladd is the plural of al-ald, which means the fiercely quarrelsome, and from this is the Almighty's saying: The most quarrelsome of opponents (al-Baqarah 2:204) and the poet said: I spend the night in seclusion from worries, as if I were arguing with people who are always arguing. Abu Ubaidah said: The stubborn is the one who does not accept the truth and claims falsehood. Al-Hasan: The stubborn is the one who is deaf to the truth. Al-Rabi’ said: He has deaf ears of hearts. Mujahid: Immoral. Ad-Dahhak: Arguing about falsehood. Ibn Abbas: Severe in argument. It was said: The unjust who does not straighten out, and the meaning is the same. They were specifically warned about it, because the one who has no stubbornness is easily led.
19:98: The Almighty says: And how many generations before them have We destroyed meaning a nation and a group of people, frightening the people of Mecca. Do you perceive anyone of them or hear a sound from them? In the accusative case, meaning do you see anyone of them and find. Or hear a sound from them meaning a sound, according to Ibn Abbas and others, meaning they have died and achieved their deeds. It was said: a sound, said by Ibn Zayd. It was said: a sound or movement that cannot be understood, said by Al-Yazidi and Abu Ubaidah, like the sound of a battalion, and Abu Ubaidah recited the verse of Labid: She was worried about her friend's concern, so she was scared of him, and her friend was sick. It was said: The low sound. And from it, the spear is buried if its tip is hidden in the ground. And Tarafa said: And the two truths heard the apprehension of the secret of a hidden focus or a denouncing voice Dhu al-Rummah said, describing a bull that hears the sound of a hunter and dogs: If he senses a desolate place, he will sneak in the sound of what he hears as a lie. That is, there is no lie in his listening, that is, he is honest in his listening. And the clever one is called nadas and nadas, just as one says hadar and hadar, and yaqz and yaqz. And the report is the hidden voice, and so is rakaz, and rakaz: buried money. And God Almighty knows best.
20:1: Surah Taha, peace be upon him, is Meccan according to everyone. It was revealed before the conversion of Omar, may God be pleased with him. Al-Daraqutni narrated in his Sunan on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: Omar went out carrying his sword, and it was said to him: Your brother-in-law has converted to Islam. Omar came to them and with them was a man from the Muhajireen called Khabab, and they were reading Surah Taha. He said: Give me the book that you have so that I may read it - and Omar, may God be pleased with him, was reading the books - so his sister said to him: You are unclean and none shall touch it except the purified, so get up and wash or perform ablution. Omar, may God be pleased with him, got up and performed ablution and took the book and read Surah Taha. Ibn Ishaq mentioned it in detail: Omar went out carrying his sword, intending to kill the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He was met by Nu'aym ibn Abdullah, who said: Where are you going, Omar? He said: I want to kill Muhammad, this Sabean who divided the Quraysh, belittled their dreams, criticized their religion, and cursed their gods. So kill him. Nu'aym said to him: By God, your soul has deceived you, Omar. Do you think that Banu Abd Manaf will leave you walking on earth after you have killed Muhammad?! Will you not return to your family and set their affairs straight?! He said: And who are the people of my house? He said: Your brother-in-law and cousin Saeed bin Zaid, and your sister Fatima bint Al-Khattab, by God they have become Muslims and followed Muhammad in his religion, so you should go after them. He said: So Omar went back to his sister and his brother-in-law, and with them was Khabbab bin Al-Arat with a scroll on which was Surat Ta Ha and he was reciting it to them. When they heard Omar’s voice, Khabbab disappeared into their bedroom or into a part of the house, and Fatima bint Al-Khattab took the scroll and put it under her thigh. Omar heard Khabbab reading to them when he came close to the house, and when he entered he said: What is this murmuring that you heard? They said to him: I did not hear anything. He said: Yes, by God, I was told that you two followed Muhammad in his religion. Then he attacked his brother-in-law Saeed bin Zaid, and his sister Fatima bint Al-Khattab rose to stop him from hitting her husband, but he hit her and wounded her. When he did that, his sister and his brother-in-law said to him: Yes, we have become Muslims and believe in God and His Messenger, so do whatever you want. When Omar saw the blood on his sister, he regretted what he had done and was afraid. He said to his sister, Give me this scroll that I heard you reading just now, so that I may see what Muhammad has brought. Omar was a writer, and when he said that, his sister said to him, We fear for it from you. He said to her, Do not be afraid, and he swore to her by his gods that he would return her when he read it. When he said that, she hoped that he would become a Muslim, and she said to him, Brother, you are impure because of your polytheism, and none may touch it except the pure. Omar got up and washed himself, and she gave him the scroll in which was Ta Ha. When he read the beginning of it, he said, How beautiful and honorable these words are! When Khabbab heard that, he went out to him and said to him, “O Omar, by God, I hope that God has chosen you for the supplication of His Prophet, for I heard him yesterday saying, ‘O God, support Islam with Abu al-Hakam ibn Hisham or with Umar ibn al-Khattab.’ So, be careful, O Umar.” Then he said to him, Guide me, Khabbab, to Muhammad so that I may go to him and become a Muslim, and he mentioned the hadith. Question: Al-Darimi Abu Muhammad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Blessed and Exalted, recited Ta-Ha and Ya-Seen two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. When the angels heard the Qur’an, they said: ‘Blessed is the nation upon which this is sent down, and blessed are the wombs that bear this, and blessed are the tongues that speak this.’” Ibn Furak said that the meaning of his statement, God, the Blessed and Exalted, recited Ta-Ha and Ya-Seen, is that He made His speech apparent, heard, and understood by whomever He wanted from among the angels of His creation at that time. The Arabs say, ‘I read something’ if you follow it, and they say, ‘This she-camel has never read a lineage in her womb,’ meaning, no child has appeared in her. Based on this, the speech is permissible, and His ears and minds read it with expressions that He creates and writing that He creates. This is the meaning of our saying, ‘We have recited the speech of God,’ and the meaning of His statement, ‘So recite what is easy for you of the Qur’an’ (al-Muzzammil 73:20), ‘So recite what is easy for you of it’ (al-Muzzammil 73:20). Some of our companions said that the meaning of his statement, He read, is that he spoke it, and that is a metaphor, like their saying, I tasted this statement, meaning I tested it. And from that is his statement, So God made them taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do (al-Naml 27:112), meaning God tested them with it, so He called that a taste, and fear is not tasted in reality, because taste in reality is with the mouth and not with any other limb. Ibn Furak said: What we said first is more correct in interpreting this report, because the speech of God is eternal and ancient, prior to all events, and only those of His creation who He wills hear and understand according to what He wills in times and periods, not that the existence of His speech itself is related to a period and time. The Almighty’s saying: Ta-Ha. The scholars differed about its meaning. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, said: It is one of the secrets. Al-Ghaznawi mentioned it. Ibn Abbas said: Its meaning is O man. Al-Bayhaqi mentioned it. It was said: It is a well-known language in Ukl. It was also said: In Ukk. Al-Kalbi said: If you said in Ukk to a man O man, he would not respond until you said Ta-Ha. Al-Tabari recited a poem about that, saying: I called Taha to fight, but he did not answer, so I was afraid that he would be a traitor. It is narrated: Muzayla. Abdullah bin Amr said: Oh my beloved, in the language of Ak, Al-Ghaznawi mentioned it and Qatrib said: It is in the language of Tayy, and he recited for Yazid bin Al-Muhalhil: Foolishness is one of your characteristics. May God not bless the cursed people. And also Al-Hasan said: The meaning of Ta-Ha is O man. And Ikrimah said the same, and he said: It is like that in Syriac, as Al-Mahdawi mentioned it, and Al-Mawardi narrated it from Ibn Abbas as well, and Mujahid. And Al-Tabari narrated that it is in Nabataean O man. And this is the saying of Al-Suddi, Saeed bin Jubair, and Ibn Abbas as well, who said: Foolishness is one of your creatures. May God not sanctify the souls of the cursed. Ikrimah also said: It is like you saying O man in the language of Abyssinia, as mentioned by Al-Tha’labi. The correct view is that even though it is found in another language, it is from the language of the Arabs as we mentioned, and that it is a Yemeni language in ‘Ak, Tayy, and ‘Akl as well. It was said: It is one of the names of God the Most High, and an oath by which He swore. This was also narrated on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. It was also said: It is a name for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, by which God the Most High named him as He named him Muhammad. It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I have ten names with my Lord. It was mentioned that among them are Ta-Ha and Ya-Seen. It was said that it is the name of the Surah and a key to it. It was said that it is an abbreviation of the speech of God, which God the Most High has chosen for His Messenger to know. It was said that they are separate letters, each of which indicates a meaning. There was a difference of opinion on that. It was said that Ta-ha is the tree of Tuba, and Ha-ha is the abyss of Hell. The Arabs express the whole thing by part, as if he swore by Paradise and Hell. Saeed bin Jubair said: Ta-ha is the opening of His name Tahir and Tayyib, and Ha-ha is the opening of His name Hadi. It was said: Ta-ha, O one who desires intercession for the nation, Ha-ha, O one who guides creation to God. It was said that Ta-ha is from purity, and Ha-ha is from guidance, as if he is saying to his Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: O one who is pure from sins, O one who guides creation to the Knower of the Unseen. It was said that Ta-ha is the drums of the invaders, and Ha-ha is their awe in the hearts of the disbelievers. al-Sharh 94:The Almighty said: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve (Al Imran 3:151) and His saying: And He cast terror into their hearts (Al Ahzab: 26). It was said: The letter Ta is the joy of the people of Paradise in Paradise, and the letter Ha is the humiliation of the people of Hell. A sixth opinion: The meaning of Ta Ha is Blessed is he who is guided, as stated by Mujahid and Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah. A seventh opinion: The meaning of Ta Ha is Ta’a al-Ard, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to endure the hardship of prayer until his feet almost swelled, and he needed to rest between his feet, so it was said to him: Ta’a al-Ard, meaning do not tire yourself out until you need to rest, as narrated by Ibn al-Anbari. Judge Iyad mentioned in al-Shifa’ that al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed, he would stand on one leg and raise the other, so God Almighty revealed Ta Ha, meaning Ta’a al-Ard, O Muhammad, We have not sent down the Qur’an to you to make you miserable. Al-Zamakhshari: On the authority of Al-Hasan, Taha and he interpreted that it was an order to trample, and that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to stand in his night prayers on one of his feet, so he was ordered to trample the ground with both feet together, and that the original was ta’a and its hamza was changed to a ha’ just as it was changed to an alif in yatta in the one who said:...... There is no pasture Then he built on this matter, and the ha’ is for silence. Mujahid said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions used to tie ropes to their chests in the night prayer due to the length of standing, then that was abrogated by the obligation, so this verse was revealed. Al-Kalbi said: When the revelation came down to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca, he strove in worship, and his worship became intense, so he used to pray all night for a period of time until this verse was revealed, so God Almighty commanded him to lighten up his burden by praying and sleeping, so this verse abrogated the night prayer, so after this verse he used to pray and sleep. Muqatil and Ad-Dahhak said: When the Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he and his companions said, so they prayed, and the infidels of Quraysh said: God did not send down this Qur’an to Muhammad except to make him miserable, so God Almighty sent down Ta Ha saying: O man, We have not sent down the Qur’an to you to make you miserable, meaning to tire you out, as will come. According to this statement: Ta Ha means to trample the earth, so the ha and the alif are the pronoun for the earth, meaning to trample the earth with your feet in your prayers, and the hamza was softened and became a silent alif. A group read Ta Ha and its original form is Ta’a meaning to trample the earth, so the hamza was deleted and the silent ha was inserted. Zur ibn Hubaish said: A man read to Abdullah ibn Mas’ud Ta Ha * We did not send down the Qur’an upon you to make you miserable. Abdullah said to him: Ta Ha. He said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, was he not commanded to trample the earth with one’s foot or two feet? He said: Ta Ha. This is how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught it to me. Abu Amr and Abu Ishaq made the ha’ inflected and opened the ta’. Abu Bakr, Hamza, al-Kisa’i and al-A’mash made them inflected. Abu Ja’far, Shaiba and Nafi’ read them between the two pronunciations, and Abu Ubaid chose it. The rest read them with emphasis. Al-Tha’labi said: They are all correct and eloquent languages. An-Nahhas: There is no reason for the inclination, according to most Arab scholars, for two reasons: One of them is that there is neither a ya’ nor a kasra here, so the inclination would be correct, and the other reason is that the ta’ is one of the letters that prevents inclination, so these are two clear reasons.
20:2: The Almighty said: We have not sent down the Qur'an to you to make you miserable. It was read as Ma nazla 'alayka al-Qur'an la'ilaha al-ma'ariqa. An-Nahhas said: Some grammarians say this is the lam of negation, and some of them say it is the lam of denial. Abu Ja'far said: I heard Abu al-Hasan bin Kaysan say: It is the lam of khifd, and the meaning is We have not sent down the Qur'an to you to make you miserable. And miserable is lengthened and shortened. It is one of the words with the letter waw. The root of miserable in the language is hardship and fatigue, meaning We have not sent down the Qur'an to you to make you tired. The poet said: The wise man suffers in bliss with his wisdom, but the ignorant man enjoys misery. The meaning of lashaka to tire yourself out is your excessive regret for them and their disbelief, and your sorrow that they believe, like the saying of God the Almighty: {Then perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them} (al-Kahf 18:6), meaning that all you have to do is convey and remind, and it was not written for you that they would inevitably believe after you did not neglect to deliver the message and good advice. It was narrated that Abu Jahl - may God curse him - and Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that you are wretched because you have abandoned the religion of your fathers. The response to that was that the religion of Islam and this Qur’an are the ladder to attaining every success and the reason for attaining every happiness, and what the disbelievers contain is wretchedness itself. According to the previous sayings, he, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed at night until his feet swelled, so Gabriel said to him: Save yourself, for it has a right over you, meaning that We did not send down the Qur’an to you to exhaust yourself in worship and make yourself taste extreme hardship, and you were not sent except with the easy-going Hanifiyah.
20:3: The Almighty said: Except as a reminder for him who fears. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: It is a substitute for tashqa meaning We did not send it down except as a reminder. Al-Nahhas: This is a far-fetched interpretation, and Abu Ali denied it because the reminder is not misery, but rather it is accusative as a source, meaning We sent it down so that you may be reminded by it, a reminder, or as an object for the sake of it, meaning We did not send down the Qur'an to you so that you may be miserable by it, We sent it down only as a reminder. Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl said: There is an inversion in it, its meaning is: We did not send down the Qur'an to you except as a reminder for him who fears, and lest you be miserable.
20:4: Tanzilan is a verbal noun, meaning We sent it down as a revelation. It was said: instead of his saying: A reminder. Abu Haywah al-Shami read Tanzil in the nominative case, meaning this is a revelation. From Him who created the earth and the high heavens meaning the high and lofty, and it is the plural of al-'aliyah, like his saying: major and minor, major and minor, informing about His greatness, might and majesty.
20:5: Then he said: The Most Gracious is firmly established on the Throne. The accusative is permissible for praise. Abu Ishaq said: The genitive is for the substitute. Saeed bin Mas'adah said: The nominative means He is the Most Gracious. An-Nahhas: The nominative is permissible for the subject, and the predicate is To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. So do not stop at established and at the substitute for the implied in created, so it is permissible to stop at established. And likewise if it is the predicate of a deleted subject, and do not stop at the high. The meaning of establishment has been mentioned previously (in Al-A'raf). What Sheikh Abu Al-Hasan and others have gone to is that He is established on His Throne without limit or how, as is the establishment of the created. Ibn Abbas said: He means the creation of what was and what will be until the Day of Resurrection and after the Resurrection.
20:6: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is under the soil meaning what is under the rock, which no one knows what is under it except God. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It means the seventh earth. Ibn Abbas: The earth is on Nun, and Nun is on the sea, and the two ends of Nun, its head and tail, meet under the Throne, and the sea is on a green rock, the greenness of the sky from it, and it is the one about which God Almighty said: Then be in a rock or in the heavens or in the earth (Luqman 31:16), and the rock is on the horn of a bull, and the bull is on the soil, and no one knows what is under the soil except God Almighty. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: On the face of the earth there are seven seas, and the earths are seven, between every two earths there is a sea, so the lowest sea is on the edge of Hell, and were it not for its size, the abundance of its water and its coldness, Hell would have burned everything on it. He said: Hell is on the back of the wind, and the back of the wind is on a veil of darkness whose magnitude is known only to God Almighty, and that veil is on the earth, and to the earth the knowledge of creation ends.
20:7: God the Almighty says: And if you speak aloud, then indeed, He knows the secret and what is even more hidden. Ibn Abbas said: The secret is what a person tells others in secret, and more hidden than that is what he conceals in his soul that no one else has told him. And he also said: The secret is what you talk about in your soul, and more hidden than the secret is what you will tell yourself of that which has not happened and is yet to come. You know what your soul keeps secret today, but you do not know what you will keep secret tomorrow. And God knows what you keep secret today and what you will keep secret tomorrow. The meaning is: God knows the secret and what is even more hidden than the secret. Ibn Abbas also said: The secret is what the son of Adam keeps secret in his soul, and more hidden is what is hidden from the son of Adam of what he will do and he does not know it. So God the Almighty knows all of that, and His knowledge of what has passed of that and what will come is one knowledge, and all of creation is in His knowledge as one soul. Qatada and others said: The secret is what a person conceals in his soul, and more hidden than that is what has not happened and no one has concealed. Ibn Zayd said: The secret is from the creation, and He concealed from it His secret, the Almighty and Majestic. Al-Tabari denied that, and said: What concealed is what is not in the secret of man and will be in his soul, as Ibn Abbas said.
20:8: "God, there is no god but He. His are the best names." God is raised by the beginning, or by the implication of the subject, or by the replacement of the pronoun in knows. He made Himself unique, glory be to Him, and that is because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called the polytheists to worship God alone, with no partner for Him, and that was difficult for them, so when Abu Jahl heard him mention the Most Gracious, he said to Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira: Muhammad forbids us from calling upon another god with God, while he is calling upon God and the Most Gracious, so God, the Most High, revealed: "Say, 'Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious. Whichever you call upon, He has the best names.'" (Al-Isra': 110) He is One, and His names are many, then He said: "God, there is no god but He. His are the best names." And we have already mentioned this in Surat Al-A'raf.
20:9: The Almighty said: And has the story of Moses come to you? The scholars of meaning said: It is a question, affirmation and affirmation, and its meaning is: Has it not come to you? It was said: Its meaning is: It has come to you, as Ibn Abbas said. Al-Kalbi said: His story had not come to him yet, then he informed him.
20:10: "When he saw a fire, he said to his family, 'Stay here; I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I can bring you a torch from it or find at the fire some guidance.'" Ibn Abbas and others said: This was when the term had expired and he set out with his family, coming from Madyan, intending to go to Egypt. He had taken the wrong route. Moses, peace be upon him, was a jealous man. He would accompany people at night and leave them during the day out of jealousy, lest they see his wife. He made the wrong choice of company - as was previously known to God Almighty - and it was a dark night. Muqatil said: It was a Friday night in the winter. Wahb ibn Munabbih: Moses asked permission from Shuaib to return to his mother, and he gave him permission. He went out with his family and his sheep, and a boy was born to him on the way, on a cold, snowy winter night. He had deviated from the road and his livestock had scattered. Moses struck a fire, but the kindling did not ignite anything, when he saw a fire in the distance to the left of the road. “He said to his family, ‘Stay here. I have seen a fire.’” Ibn Abbas said: When he headed towards the fire, he saw the fire in a jujube tree. He stood amazed at the beauty of that light and the intense greenness of that tree. Neither the intense heat of the fire changed the beauty of the greenery of the tree, nor the abundance of the tree’s water nor the blessing of the greenery changed the beauty of the light of the fire. Al-Mahdawi said: He saw the fire - according to what was narrated - and it was in a bramble tree, so he headed towards it, but it was delayed from him, so he turned back and felt fear in his soul, then it approached him and God Almighty spoke to him from the tree. Al-Mawardi: It was a fire with Moses, and it was a light with God Almighty. Hamzah read for his family, stay with a damma on the ha’, and so it is in al-Qasas. An-Nahhas said: This is according to the language of those who say: I passed by him, man, so he came with it according to the original, and it is permissible except that Hamzah went against his original in these two places in particular. He said: Stay and did not say reside, because staying requires permanence, and staying is not like that. And to see means to see, said Ibn al-A’rabi. And from this is His statement: If you perceive in them sound judgment (An-Nisa’: 6) meaning you know. And to see means to hear the voice, and al-Qabas is a flame of fire, and so is al-Miqbas. It is said: I took a fire from him, I took a flame, so he gave me a flame from it, and likewise Iqtabasat minhu nara and Iqtabasat minhu ‘ilm also meaning I benefited from it. Al-Yazidi said: Iqtabasat al-rajul ‘ilm and Iqtabastuhu nara, so if you sought it for him, you say Iqtabastuhu. Al-Kisa’i said: Iqtabastuhu nara or ilm are the same. He said: I also took it from them. Guidance means a guide.
20:11: The Almighty said: So when he came to it meaning the fire, he was called meaning from the tree, as in Surat Al-Qasas, meaning from its direction and side, as will come: O Moses, indeed I am your Lord.
20:12: The Almighty’s saying: So take off your shoes, for you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa. There are five issues in it: First: The Almighty’s saying: Then take off your shoes. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “On the day that his Lord spoke to Moses, he was wearing a woolen cloak, a woolen jacket, a woolen cap, and woolen trousers. His sandals were made of the hide of a dead donkey.” He said: This is a strange hadith that we do not know except from the hadith of Hamid al-A’raj Hamid - he is the son of Ali al-Kufi - is a fabricator of hadith, and Hamid bin Qais al-A’raj al-Makki, the companion of Mujahid, is trustworthy. The cap is the small skullcap. The common people read inni with a kasra, meaning he was called and it was said to him, O Moses, I am. Abu Ubaid chose this. Abu Amr, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, and Hamid read inni with a fatha on the alif, acting as a call. The scholars differed about the reason for which he was ordered to take off his sandals. Taking off means pulling off. A sandal is what you make to protect your feet from the ground. It was said that he was ordered to throw away his sandals because they are impure since they are made of hide that was not slaughtered. This was said by Ka’b, Ikrimah, and Qatadah. It was said: He was ordered to do this in order to attain the blessing of the sacred valley, and for his feet to touch the soil of the valley, as stated by Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj. It was also said: He was ordered to take off his shoes out of humility and humbleness when communing with God Almighty. This is what the predecessors did when they circumambulated the House. It was also said: Out of respect for that place, just as the sanctuary is not entered with shoes out of respect for it. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: It was said to him, Tread the ground barefoot as you enter the Kaaba barefoot. It is customary among kings to take off your shoes and for a person to reach the height of humility, so it is as if Moses, peace be upon him, ordered this in this manner, and he did not care whether his shoes were from a dead animal or not. Malik did not see himself riding an animal in Medina on land, with its soil containing the greatest honor and the noble Paradise. From this meaning is his saying, peace and blessings be upon him, to Bashir ibn Al-Khasasiyah while he was walking between the graves with his shoes on If you are in such a place, take off your shoes. He said: So I took them off. And a fifth opinion: That is an expression of emptying his heart of the matter of family and children. Family may be expressed by the shoe. And it is also in the interpretation: Whoever sees that he is wearing two shoes, he will marry. And it was said: Because God Almighty spread for him the carpet of light and guidance, and he should not step on the carpet of the Lord of the Worlds with his shoe. And it may be possible that Moses was ordered to take off his shoes, and that was the first obligation upon him, just as it was the first thing that was said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Arise and warn. And your Lord glorify. And your garments purify. And uncleanliness avoid.” (al-Muddaththir 74:2-5) And God knows best what is meant by that. Second: In the hadith that Moses, peace be upon him, took off his shoes and threw them from behind the valley. Abu Al-Ahwas said: Abdullah visited Abu Musa in his house, and the prayer was called, so Abu Musa stood up, and Abu Musa said to Abdullah: Come forward. Abdullah said: Come forward, you are in your house. So he came forward and took off his shoes, and Abdullah said: Are you in the holy valley?! And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Saeed bin Yazid, he said: I said to Anas: Did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pray in two sandals? He said: Yes.
