Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed on the day of the conquest and placed his sandals on his left.” Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, who said: “While the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was praying with his companions, he took off his shoes and placed them on his left. When the people saw that, they took off their shoes. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had finished the prayer, he said: ‘What made you take off your shoes?’ They said: ‘We saw you take off your shoes, so we took off our shoes.’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘Gabriel came to me and informed me that there was filth on them. He said: ‘When one of you comes to the mosque, let him look. If he sees filth or dirt on his shoes, let him wipe it off and pray in them.’” Abu Muhammad ‘Abd al-Haqq authenticated it. It combines the two hadiths before it and removes the contradiction between them. The scholars did not differ on the permissibility of praying in shoes if they were clean from impurity. Some scholars even said that praying in them is better, which is the meaning of the words of God the Almighty: ‘Take your adornment at every mosque.’ (al-A’raf 7:31), as mentioned above. Ibrahim Al-Nakha’i said about those who take off their shoes: I wish that a needy person would come and take them. Third: If you take them off, take them off between your legs, because Abu Hurairah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When one of you prays, let him take off his shoes between his feet. Abu Hurairah said to Al-Maqburi: Take them off between your feet and do not disturb a Muslim with them. And what was narrated by Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib may God be pleased with him that the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) took them off from his left because he was an imam, so if you are an imam or alone, then do that if you like, and if you are a follower in the row, do not disturb with them those on your left, and do not place them between your feet so that they distract you, but in front of your feet. And it was narrated from Jubayr bin Mut’im that he said: A man placing his shoes between his feet is an innovation. Fourth: If there is an impurity in them that is agreed upon to be impure, such as blood and excrement from the urine of human beings, nothing purifies them except washing with water, according to Malik, Ash-Shafi’i and most scholars. If there is a difference of opinion about the impurity, such as the urine and wet droppings of animals, does wiping the sandal or sock purify it or not? We have two opinions. Al-Awza’i and Abu Thawr stated that wiping it with soil is sufficient without detailing it. Abu Hanifa said: It is removed if the scratching and rubbing dry, and nothing removes its moisture except washing, except urine, in which case nothing is sufficient according to him except washing. Ash-Shafi’i said: Nothing purifies any of these except water. The correct opinion is that of those who said: Wiping purifies the sandal and sock, according to the hadith of Abu Sa’id. But if the sandal and sock are made of the skin of a dead animal, if it is not tanned, then it is impure by consensus, except for what Az-Zuhri and Al-Layth stated, as was explained previously in Surah An-Nahl. The statement on removing impurity has been mentioned in Surah Bara’ah, and praise be to God. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa. The sacred means the purified. The holy means purity, and the sacred land means the purified, and it was named thus because God the Almighty expelled the disbelievers from it and populated it with believers. God the Almighty has given some places more grace than others, just as He has given some times more grace than others, and the same for some animals. And God can give what He wills. Based on this, there is no consideration for it being sacred by expelling the disbelievers and settling the believers, as others shared in that with Him. Tuwa is the name of the valley according to Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others. Ad-Dahhak said: It is a deep, round valley like Al-Tawi. Ikrimah read Tawi. The rest read Tawi. Ad-Dahhak said: It is a deep, round valley like Al-Tawi. Ikrimah read Tawi. The rest: Tawa Al-Jawhari said: Tawa is the name of a place in the Levant, its taa is broken and closed, and it is declined and not declined. Whoever declines it makes it the name of a valley and a place and makes it indefinite, and whoever does not decline it makes it a town and a spot and makes it definite. Some of them said: Tawa is like Tawa and it is the dual thing, and they said in his statement the sacred Tawa: Tawa twice meaning sanctified. Al-Hasan said: Blessing and sanctification were dualized in it twice. Al-Mahdawi mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: that it was called Tawa because Moses folded it at night when he passed by it and it rose to the top of the valley, so it is a verbal noun that does something that is not from its wording, so it is as if he said: You are in the sacred valley which you folded Tawa, meaning you passed it and folded it with your walking. Al-Hasan: Its meaning is that it was sanctified twice, so it is a verbal noun from the word tawa which you folded Tawa also.
20:13: The Almighty said: And I have chosen you meaning I have selected you for the message. The people of Medina, Abu Amr, Asim, and Al-Kisa'i read And I have chosen you. Hamza read And I have chosen you. The meaning is the same, except that And I have chosen you here is more appropriate in two ways: First, it is more similar to writing, and second, it is more appropriate to the order of the speech, because the Almighty said: O Moses, indeed I am your Lord, so take off your sandals and the address was made in this order, as An-Nahhas said. The Almighty’s statement: Then listen to what is revealed contains one issue. Ibn Atiyah said: My father told me - may God have mercy on him - he said: I heard Abu al-Fadl al-Jawhari - may God have mercy on him - say: When it was said to Moses, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: Then listen to what is revealed, he stood on a stone, leaned against a stone, placed his right hand on his left, put his chin on his chest, and stood listening, and all of his clothing was wool. I said: Good listening as it should be has been praised by God, who said: Those who listen to speech and follow the best of it - those are the ones whom God has guided (al-Zumar 39:18) and He has condemned those who are contrary to this description, saying: We know best what they listen to (al-Isra’ 17:47) the verse. So He praised the one who listens attentively to His speech while being present in mind, and He commanded His servants to do so as an etiquette for them, saying: And when the Qur’an is recited, listen to it and be silent that you may receive mercy (al-A’raf 7:204) and He said here: So listen to what is revealed because in this way one attains understanding from God, the Most High. It was narrated on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: Among the etiquettes of listening are stillness of the limbs, lowering the gaze, listening with the ears, being present in mind, and being determined to act. That is listening as God, the Most High, loves, and it is for the servant to restrain his limbs and not occupy them. His heart is occupied with what he hears, he lowers his gaze so that his heart is not distracted by what he sees, he limits his mind so that he does not think of anything other than what he hears, and he resolves to understand and acts according to what he understands. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: The beginning of knowledge is listening, then understanding, then memorization, then action, then dissemination. So if the servant listens to the Book of God the Most High and the Sunnah of His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, with a sincere intention for what God loves, He will make him understand as he loves, and will place light in his heart for him.
20:14: The Almighty’s saying: “Indeed, I am God. There is no god but Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.” There are seven issues in it: First: There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of His statement: For My remembrance. It was said: It is possible that he means for you to remember Me in it, or he means for me to remember you with praise in the highest place in it. The source, according to this, may be added to the subject and the object. It was said: The meaning is, he who maintains the prayer after monotheism. This is a reminder of the great value of prayer, as it is supplication to God the Most High, and standing before Him. According to this, prayer is remembrance. God the Most High called prayer remembrance in His statement: So hasten to the remembrance of God (al-Jumuah 62:9). It was said: What is meant is if you forget and then remember, then pray, as in the hadith: Then let him pray it when he remembers it. That is, the prayer is not dropped due to forgetfulness. Second: Malik and others narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, let him pray it when he remembers it, for God Almighty says: ‘And establish prayer for My remembrance.’” Abu Muhammad Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa`id narrated from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Hajjaj - and he is the first Hajjaj from whom Yazid ibn Zurai` narrated - he said: Qatada told us on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who sleeps through a prayer and forgets about it. He said: Its expiation is that he prays it when he remembers it. Ibrahim bin Tahman narrated it on the authority of Hajjaj, and Hammam bin Yahya narrated it on the authority of Qatada. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever forgets a prayer, its time should be up if he remembers it. His statement, Let him pray it if he remembers it, is evidence of the obligation of the one who is asleep or inattentive to make it up, whether the prayer is many or few. This is the view of most scholars. An unusual disagreement has been reported that is not to be taken into account, because it contradicts the text of the hadith from some people that with regard to more than five prayers, he is not obligated to make it up. I said: God the Almighty commanded the establishment of prayer, and specified specific times, as He said: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun (al-Isra’ 17:78) and other verses. Whoever establishes at night what he was commanded to establish during the day, or vice versa, his action is not in accordance with what he was commanded to establish, and he will not be rewarded for his action, and he is a sinner. Accordingly, he is not required to make up for what he missed in its time. If it were not for his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, let him pray it when he remembers it, no one would benefit from a prayer that occurred at a time other than its time. In this regard, it is a making up, not a performance, because making up is a new command and not the first command. Third: As for the one who intentionally abandons the prayer, the majority also agree that he must make it up, even if he is a sinner, except for Dawud. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Ash'ari al-Shafi'i agreed with him, as narrated by Ibn al-Qassar. The difference between the one who intentionally abandons the prayer, the one who forgets, and the one who is asleep is the reduction of the sin. The one who intentionally abandons the prayer is sinful, and all of them are to be made up. The evidence for the majority is the statement of God the Almighty: Establish prayer and He did not differentiate between it being during its time or after it. This is a command that requires it to be made up. Also, the command to make up the prayer of the one who is asleep and the one who forgets has been proven, even though they are not sinful, so the one who intentionally abandons it is more deserving. And also his saying: Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, and forgetting is abandonment. God Almighty said: They forgot God, so He forgot them (al-Tawbah 9:67) and They forgot God, so He made them forget themselves (al-Hashr 59:19), whether it was with forgetfulness or not, because God Almighty does not forget, rather its meaning is He left them, and We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten (al-Baqarah 2:106), meaning We leave it. And likewise remembrance occurs after forgetting and after something else. God Almighty said: Whoever remembers Me in himself, I will remember him in Myself and the Almighty does not forget, but its meaning is I know. So the meaning of his saying: if he remembers it is that he knows it. Also, if the debts of human beings are related to a time, then the time comes, their payment is not dropped after they become due, and they are among those that are dropped by release, it was more appropriate for the debts of God the Almighty that the release is not valid for them, so their payment is not dropped except with His permission. Also, we have agreed that if someone intentionally misses a day of Ramadan without an excuse, it is obligatory to make it up, and so is the prayer. If it is said, it was narrated from Malik: Whoever intentionally misses a prayer does not make it up ever. So the indication is that what has passed does not return, or it is a statement that was made out of severity, as was narrated from Ibn Masoud and Ali: Whoever breaks the fast in Ramadan intentionally, it is not expiated by fasting for a lifetime, even if he fasts it. However, it is necessary to fulfill the obligation by making up for it instead of performing it, or following it with repentance, and God does after that what He wills. Abu al-Matous narrated from his father from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Whoever intentionally breaks his fast one day in Ramadan will not be considered as having fasted for the rest of his life, even if he fasts that day. This may mean that if it is authentic, it would mean that it is a severe punishment. It is a weak hadith narrated by Abu Dawud. Expiation has been mentioned in authentic hadiths, and in some of them it is to make up for the day. Praise be to God Almighty. Fourth: His saying, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, the hadith specifies the generality of his saying, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: The pen is lifted from three: from the sleeper until he wakes up. What is meant by lifting here is lifting the sin, not lifting the obligation from him. This is not from the category of his saying: and from the boy until he has a wet dream, even though that came in one trace, so stop at this principle. Fifth: Scholars differed on this meaning regarding someone who remembers a missed prayer while it is the last time for a prayer, or remembers a prayer while he is praying. The summary of the Maliki school of thought is that if someone remembers a prayer and the time for another prayer has come, he should start with the one he forgot if it is five prayers or less, even if the time for this one has passed. If it is more than that, he should start with the one whose time has come. This is similar to the school of thought of Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri and al-Layth, except that Abu Hanifa and his companions said: According to us, ordering is obligatory during the day and night if there is enough time for the missed prayer and the prayer of the time. If he fears missing the time, he should start with it. If it is more than the prayer of the day and night, ordering is not obligatory according to them. It was narrated from al-Thawri that ordering is obligatory, and he did not differentiate between a little and a lot. This is the conclusion of the Shafi’i school of thought. Al-Shafi’i said: The preferred view is to start with the missed prayer unless he fears missing this one. If he does not do that and starts with the prayer of the time, it is sufficient for him. Al-Athram mentioned that ordering is obligatory according to Ahmad in the prayer of sixty years or more. He said: No one should pray a prayer while remembering what came before it because it spoils it. Al-Darqutni narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said: “If one of you remembers a prayer during an obligatory prayer, let him begin with the one he is in. When he finishes it, he should pray the one he forgot.” Omar bin Abi Omar is unknown. I said: If this is correct, it would be an argument for Al-Shafi’i to begin with the prayer of the time. What is correct is what the people of Sahih narrated on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah: “On the day of the Trench, Umar began to curse the infidels of Quraysh and said: O Messenger of God, I almost prayed the afternoon prayer until the sun was about to set. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, I have prayed it. So we went down to Al-Bathaan and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution, and we performed ablution. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed the afternoon prayer after the sun had set, then he prayed the sunset prayer after it.” This is a text on starting with the missed prayer before the present one, especially since the time for the sunset prayer is one and narrow and not extended in the months according to us and according to Al-Shafi’i as mentioned above. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Ubaidah bin Abdullah bin Mas’ud on the authority of his father: “The polytheists distracted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from four prayers on the day of the Trench, until as much of the night as God willed had passed. So he ordered Bilal to call the adhan, so he stood up and called the adhan, then he called the iqamah and prayed the noon prayer, then he called the iqamah and prayed the afternoon prayer, then he called the iqamah and prayed the sunset prayer, then he called the iqamah and prayed the night prayer. From this, the scholars have proven that whoever misses a prayer must make it up in order as he missed it if he remembers it at the same time. They differed if he remembers a missed prayer in a tight time frame, and they have three opinions: He begins with the missed prayer even if the time for the present prayer has passed, and this is what Malik, Al-Layth, Al-Zuhri and others said, as we have mentioned. The second: He begins with the present prayer, and this is what Al-Hasan, Al-Shafi’i, the scholars of hadith, Al-Muhasibi and Ibn Wahb from our companions said. The third: He chooses and brings forward whichever of them he wants, and this is what Ashhab said. The first aspect: The abundance of prayers. There is no disagreement that one should start with the present prayer with the abundance, as stated by Judge Iyad. They differed on the amount of the little, so according to Malik: five or less, and it was said: four or less, according to the hadith of Jabir, and there is no disagreement in the school of thought that six is a lot. Sixth: As for the one who remembers a prayer while he is praying, if he is behind the imam, then everyone who said that the order is obligatory and whoever did not say that, continues with the imam until he completes his prayer. The basis for this is what Malik and al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “If one of you forgets a prayer and does not remember it until he is with the imam, then let him pray with the imam. When he finishes his prayer, let him pray the prayer he forgot, then let him repeat the prayer he prayed with the imam.” This is the wording of Ad-Daraqutni. Musa bin Harun said: Abu Ibrahim At-Tarjumani narrated to us, saying: Saeed narrated it to us and traced it back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he made a mistake in tracing it back. If he retracted his attribution, then he was guided to the correct view. Then they differed. Abu Hanifa and Ahmad bin Hanbal said: He should pray the one he remembered, then pray the one he prayed with the imam, unless there are more than five prayers between them, based on what we have mentioned previously from the Kufians. This is the view of a group of the companions of Malik from Medina. Al-Kharqi narrated from Ahmad bin Hanbal that he said: Whoever remembers a prayer while he is in another, then he should complete it and make up the one he remembered, and repeat the one he was in if there is plenty of time. If he fears that the time will end while he is in it, then he should believe that he should not repeat it, and it will suffice him, and he should make up the one he owes. Malik said: If someone remembers a prayer while he is in a prayer in which he has already prayed two rak’ahs, he should say the salutation after his two rak’ahs. If he is an imam, it collapses on him and those behind him and is invalidated. This is the apparent meaning of the Maliki school of thought, but it is not the case with the people of insight among his companions, because his statement regarding someone who remembers a prayer in a prayer in which he has already prayed one rak’ah is that he should add another to it and say the salutation. If he remembers it in a prayer in which he has already prayed three rak’ahs, he should add a fourth to it and say the salutation, and it becomes a voluntary prayer that is not invalidated. If it collapses on him as he mentioned and is invalidated, he is not commanded to add another to it, just as if he breaks his ablution after a rak’ah, he does not add another to it. Seventh: Muslim narrated on the authority of Abu Qatada who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us a sermon and mentioned the hadith of ablution in full, and he said in it: Do you not have an example? Then he said: There is no negligence in sleeping, rather the negligence is for the one who does not pray the prayer until the time for the next prayer comes. So whoever does that should pray it when he wakes up for it, and when the next day comes, let him pray it at its time. And Ad-Daraqutni narrated it in this way with the same wording as Muslim. So its apparent meaning requires repeating the missed prayer twice when it is remembered and the presence of a similar prayer at the next time. This apparent meaning is supported by what Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Imran bin Husayn, and he mentioned the story and said at the end of it: Whoever among you catches the dawn prayer the next day in a good way, let him perform the same prayer with it. I said: This is not to be taken literally, and it is not repeated more than once, because of what Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Imran bin Husayn, who said: “We set out with the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) on a raid - or he said on a secret mission - and when it was the time of dawn we camped. We had not woken up until the heat of the sun woke us up, and each one of us would jump up in fright and astonishment. When the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) woke up, he ordered us to set out, then we set out until the sun had risen high, and the people had completed their needs. Then he ordered Bilal to call the adhan and we prayed two rak’ahs. Then he ordered him to call the iqamah and we prayed the morning prayer. We said: O Prophet of God, shall we not perform it on time the next day? The Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) said to them: God forbids you from usury and accepts it from you.” Al-Khattabi said: I do not know of anyone who said that this is obligatory, and it seems that the order to do so is recommended in order to preserve the virtue of the time in performing the prayer. The correct view is to abandon the work, based on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: God forbids you from usury and accepts it from you. And because the authentic chains of transmission from the hadith of Imran bin Husayn do not contain any of that addition, except what was mentioned from the hadith of Abu Qatada, which is possible, as we have explained. I said: Al-Kaya al-Tabari mentioned in his Ahkam al-Qur’an that some of the Salaf contradicted his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: “Whoever forgets a prayer should pray it when he remembers it. There is no expiation for it except that.” He said: He should be patient until its time is like that and pray it. If he misses the dawn prayer, he should pray it the next day. This is a far-fetched and strange statement.
20:15: The Almighty’s saying: The Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives for. This is a problematic verse. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he read I almost conceal it with a fat-ha on the hamza. He said: He made it apparent. So that it may be recompensed means making the recompense apparent. It was narrated by Abu Ubaid on the authority of Al-Kisa’i on the authority of Muhammad bin Sahl on the authority of Waqqa’ bin Iyas on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair. An-Nahhas said: There is no other chain of transmission for this narration. I said: And Abu Bakr al-Anbari narrated it in the Book of Response. My father told me, Muhammad ibn al-Jahm told us, al-Farra’ told us, and al-Kisa’i told us, H - and Abdullah ibn Najiyah told us, Yusuf told us, Yahya al-Hamani told us, Muhammad ibn Sahl told us. An-Nahhas said: Better than this chain of transmission is what Yahya al-Qattan narrated on the authority of al-Thawri on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr: that he recited I almost concealed it with a damma on the hamza. I said: As for Ibn Jubayr’s reading I akhfayha with the opening of the hamza with the aforementioned chain of transmission, Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is to reveal it from khafayt al-shay’, I akhfayhu if I reveal it. Al-Farra’ recited for Imru’ al-Qais: If you bury the disease, we will not fear it, and if you start war, we will not sit back. He wanted to show it. Some linguists have said: It is possible that akhfayha with a damma on the hamza means he showed it, because it is said: Khafaytu al-shay’ and akhfaytuhu if you show it. Akhfaytuhu is one of the letters of opposites and refers to covering and showing. Abu Ubaidah said: Khafaytu and akhfaytu have the same meaning. An-Nahhas said: This is good, and he narrated it from Abu al-Khattab, who is a leader of the leaders of the language, and there is no doubt about his truthfulness. Sibawayh narrated from him and recited: If you conceal the disease, we will not fear it, and if you start a war, we will not sit back. This is how Abu Ubaidah narrated it on the authority of Abu al-Khattab with a damma on the nun. Imru al-Qais also said: Their secrets are hidden from their tunnels, as if their secrets were hidden and thin from the evening brought That is, he showed them. It was narrated: (from a cloud that is mounted) instead of (from a bringing evening). Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: Another interpretation of the verse is: The Hour is coming, I am almost. The speech was interrupted at I am almost and after it is implied I am almost bringing it, and the beginning is I conceal it so that every soul may be rewarded. Dhaby al-Barjami said: I intended to do it but did not, and I almost did. I wish I had left Uthman's wives crying over him. He wanted and I almost did, so he implied with almost a verb like the implied verb with it in the Qur’an. I said: This is what Al-Nahhas chose, and he falsified the statement before it, so he said: It is said: He concealed the thing, he conceals it, if he reveals it, and it has been narrated that it is also said: He concealed it, if he reveals it, and it is not well-known. He said: I saw Ali bin Sulayman, when the meaning of I conceal it was unclear to him, he turned to this statement, and said: Its meaning is like the meaning of I conceal it. Al-Nahhas said: The meaning is not as it appears, especially since I conceal it is an anomalous reading, so how can the correct and common reading be returned to the anomalous reading, and the meaning of the implied is more appropriate, and the estimate would be: The Hour is coming, I am about to bring it, and coming indicates that I will bring it, then he said: I conceal it as the beginning. This is a correct meaning, because God the Almighty has concealed the Hour, which is the Resurrection, and the Hour in which a person dies so that a person may work, and the matter is ambiguous with Him, so He does not delay repentance. I said: According to this statement, the lam in to be rewarded is related to to hide it. Abu Ali said: This is from the category of negation and not from the category of opposites. The meaning of to hide it is that its concealment was removed, which is its covering like the concealment of the concealments, which are the cloaks. The singular is khafa' with a kasra on the kha' that which wraps the water skin, and if its covering is removed, it appears. From this is their saying: I complained to him, meaning I removed his complaint, and I prepared him, meaning I accepted his preparation and did not need him to return it. Abu Hatim narrated from Al-Akhfash: that kada is an emphatic redundant word. He said: And similar to it is If he puts out his hand, he can hardly see it (al-Nur 24:40) because some of the darknesses that God mentioned come between the observer and the one being looked at. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Jubayr, and the meaning is: The Hour is coming, I conceal it so that every soul may be rewarded for what it strives for. The poet said: Quick to attack, he sharpens his weapon, and his horn barely breathes. He wanted to breathe. Another said: And I do not blame myself for what happened to me, and I do not think that I can succeed with what I have achieved. Meaning: And that I should not succeed in what I have achieved, so I almost is an emphasis on the speech. It was said: The meaning is I almost hid it i.e. I came close to that, because if you say: Zaid is standing, it is possible that he stood up, or that he did not stand up. And the evidence that he concealed it is indicated by a different meaning for this answer. Linguists said: The meaning of I almost did among the Arabs is: I came close to doing the action but did not do it, and I almost did means: I did after delaying. And the evidence for this is the statement of God, the Almighty, So they slaughtered it, but they almost did it (al-Baqarah 2:71) meaning: And they did after delaying because it was difficult for them to find the cow. And I almost did may mean I did not do it and I almost if the speech is emphasised by I almost. And it was said: The meaning of I almost hid it is I mean I concealed it. Al-Anbari said: And the evidence for this eloquent saying from poetry is: Almost, almost, and that is the best will, if the one who was in love returned to what had passed Meaning: She wanted and I wanted. Ibn Abbas and most of the commentators said, as mentioned by al-Tha'labi: The meaning is I almost hid it from myself, and this is how it is in Abi's copy of the Qur'an. In Ibn Mas'ud's copy of the Qur'an: I almost hid it from myself, so how could any creature know it? And in some readings: So how could I reveal it to you. It is understood that it came according to what is customary among the Arabs in their speech, that if one of them goes too far in concealing something, he says: I almost hid it from myself. And nothing is hidden from God Almighty, and Qatrib and others said its meaning. And the poet said: Days when Hind accompanies me, I tell her what I hide from myself of my needs and secrets How can he tell her what he keeps secret? And from this is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And a man who gives charity and conceals it so that his left hand does not know what his right hand spends. Al-Zamakhshari. It was said that its meaning is: I almost hide it from myself. There is no evidence in the speech for this omission, and an omission for which there is no evidence is discarded. What deceived them is that in the Mushaf of Abi it says: I almost hide it from myself. And in some Mushafs it says: I almost hide it from myself, so how can I reveal it to you? I said: It was said that the meaning of the statement of the one who said I almost hid it from myself, is that its concealment was from me and from myself and not from anyone else. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas: I almost hid it from myself, and Talha bin Amr narrated it from Ata. Ali bin Abi Talha narrated from Ibn Abbas who said: I do not reveal it to anyone. It was narrated from Saeed bin Jubair who said: He has concealed it. This is on the basis that almost is redundant. That is, the Hour is coming, I conceal it, and the benefit of concealing it is to frighten and intimidate. It was said: So that you may be rewarded is related to the statement of God Almighty: And establish prayer, so there is an inversion in the speech, that is, establish prayer to remind Me, So that every soul may be rewarded for what it strives for, that is, for its striving. The Hour is coming, I almost conceal it. And God knows best. It was said: It is related to His statement: Coming, that is, the Hour is coming to be rewarded.
20:16: So let not he who does not believe in it and follows his own desires turn you away from it meaning let not him who does not believe in it and follows his own desires turn you away from believing in it. So you perish meaning you will be destroyed. It is in the accusative case as a response to the prohibition.
20:17: It has five issues: The first is the saying of God the Almighty: And what is that in your right hand? It was said: This address from God the Almighty to Moses was a revelation, because He said: Then listen to what is revealed. The prophet must have a miracle in himself by which he knows the truth of his prophethood, so He showed him in the staff and in himself what I saw for that. It is possible that what he saw in the tree was a sufficient sign for him in himself, then the hand and the staff would be an additional confirmation and a proof with which he would present his people. There is a difference of opinion regarding what in His saying: And what is that? Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farra’ said: It is an incomplete noun connected to your right hand, meaning what is in your right hand? He also said: That means this, and if he had said: What is that, it would have been permissible, meaning what is that thing? The purpose of the question is to establish the matter so that Moses would say: It is my staff, to establish the argument against him after he confessed, otherwise God knew what it was in eternity. Ibn Al-Jawhari said: In some of the narrations, God the Almighty rebuked Moses for adding the staff to Himself in that place, so He said to him: Throw it down to see the wonder from it, so you will know that you have no control over it and it is not added to you. Ibn Abi Ishaq read ‘asi in the dialect of Hudhayl, and similarly ya bashri and muhyi have been mentioned previously. Al-Hasan read ‘asai with a kasra on the ya because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. Similar to this is the reading of Hamza and you are not my helpers (Ibrahim 14:22). And from Ibn Abi Ishaq, the ya is quiescent. Second: In this verse there is evidence that the question was answered with more than what was asked, because when he said: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses, he mentioned four meanings: which are: adding the staff to him, and he should have said a staff, and leaning, and the ability to lean, and the absolute purposes. So Moses mentioned from the benefits of his staff its greatness and its majority, and he made the rest of that more beautiful. And in the hadith, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about sea water, so he said: Its water is pure and its dead are permissible.” And a woman asked him about the child when she brought him to him and said: Is this why he performed Hajj? He said: Yes, and you will be rewarded. There are many similar hadiths.
20:18: Third: The Almighty said: I lean on it meaning I support myself on it when walking and standing, and leaning is from it. And I beat it with it "And I beat it" also, mentioned by An-Nahhas. It is the reading of An-Nakha'i, meaning I beat the leaves with it, meaning I strike the branches of the tree so that its leaves fall, making it easy for my sheep to reach it and eat it. The rajaz poet said: I beat my sheep with a stick from the soft arak and bisham trees It is said: He cheered on his sheep, with a damma on the ha’ in the future tense. And he cheered to the man, with a fatha. And also he cheered for the known, he cheered, and I cheered: And in the hadith of Omar: I cheered one day and kissed while I was fasting. Shammar said: That is, I was happy and desired. He said: And it is permissible to have a cheer in the meaning of cheer. The shepherd said: He magnified the vision, cheered his heart, and gave good report to a soul he had previously blamed. Any joy. The root of the word is softness. It is said: a soft man and a soft husband. Ikrimah read Ahs with a non-voweled sin. It was said: they are two languages with the same meaning. It was also said: their meanings are different. Hash with a voiced sin is hitting the tree, and has without a voiced sun is driving sheep away. Al-Mawardi mentioned this, as did Al-Zamakhshari. Ikrimah said: Ahs with a sin means he leaned on it, driving it away, and has is driving sheep away. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: And I have therein other needs meaning necessities. The singular of it is ma’ribah, ma’ribah, and ma’ribah. He said other in the singular form, because ma’rib has the meaning of a group, but ma’hi’ is in the appendix of a plural of what cannot be made singular and referred to by that, because that is like a feminine singular, like the Almighty’s statement: And to God belong the best names, so invoke Him by them (al-A’raf 7:180) and His statement: O mountains, echo with Him (Saba’: 10). This was mentioned previously in ((Al-A’raf)). Fifth: Some people enumerated the benefits of the stick, including Ibn Abbas, who said: If I reach the top of a well, I shorten the rope and connect it with the stick. If the heat of the sun hits me, I stick it in the ground and throw something on it to shade me. If I fear something from the vermin of the earth, I kill it with it. If I walk, I throw it on my shoulder and hang the bow, quiver, and saddlebag on it, and I fight wild beasts with it for the sheep. Narrated from Maymun bin Mahran who said: Holding a stick is a tradition of the prophets and a sign of the believer. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: It has six characteristics: a tradition of the prophets, an adornment for the righteous, a weapon against enemies, a help for the weak, a grief for the hypocrites, and an increase in acts of obedience. It is said: If a believer has a stick, Satan flees from him, the hypocrite and the wicked are in awe of him, it is his direction of prayer when he prays, and a strength when he is tired. Al-Hajjaj met a Bedouin and said: Where have you come from, O Bedouin? He said: From the desert. He said: What is in your hand? He said: My staff, I use it to pray, I prepare it for my equipment, I drive my beast with it, I strengthen myself with it on my journey, I lean on it in my walk to make my stride wider, I jump with it the river, it keeps me safe from stumbling, I throw my cloak on it to protect me from the heat, warm me from the cold, and bring me closer to what is far from me, it is the carrier of my journey, and the strap of my container, I use it to stand when striking, I knock with it on doors, I protect myself with it from the gnawing dogs, it takes the place of the spear in thrusting, and the sword in dueling with peers, I inherited it from my father, and I bequeath it to my son after me, I use it to herd my sheep, and I have other uses for it, many of which are too numerous to count. I said: The benefits of the stick are many, and it has many aspects in the Shariah: one of them is that it is used as a qiblah in the desert. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had a goat that he would set up for himself so that he could pray towards it. When he went out on the day of Eid, he would order a spear to be placed in front of him so that he could pray towards it. This is proven in Saheeh al-Bukhari. The spear, goat, meteorite and instrument are all names for one thing. He had a stick with a crooked end that he would point at a stone if he could not kiss it. This is also proven in Saheeh al-Bukhari and in al-Muwatta’ on the authority of al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid that he said: ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him ordered Ubayy ibn Ka’b and Tamim al-Dari to lead the people in eleven rak’ahs. The reciter would recite by the hundreds until we would lean on sticks due to the length of standing, and we would not leave until dawn. In Saheeh al-Bukhari and Saheeh Muslim it is reported that he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had a belt. There is consensus that the preacher should deliver the sermon leaning on a sword or a stick. The stick is taken from a noble origin and a noble metal, and only an ignorant person would deny this. God gathered for Moses in his staff great proofs and mighty signs, in which even the stubborn magicians believed. Solomon used it for his sermons, his exhortations, and his long prayers. Ibn Masoud was the owner of the Prophet’s staff, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his goat. He used to deliver sermons with the staff - and that is enough of a virtue for the honor of the staff - and the caliphs and great orators followed that, and the custom of the Arabs, the eloquent and fluent, was to take the belt and the staff and lean on it when speaking, in gatherings and sermons. The Shu’ubiyyah denounced the Arab orators for taking the belt and pointing with it to meanings. The Shu’ubiyyah hated the Arabs and preferred the Persians. Malik said: Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib used to hold the belt and seek help from it. Malik said: When a man grows old, he is not as strong as the youth when standing. I said: And in his walk, as some of them said: I used to walk on two legs, leaning on them, so I started walking on one wooden one. Malik, may God have mercy on him and be pleased with him, said: When the rain came to the people, they would go out with sticks to lean on, to the point that the young men would hold back their sticks, and Rabi’ah might take the stick from someone sitting with him until he stood up. Among the benefits of the stick is for a man to strike his wives with it in a way that would improve them, and improve his situation and their situation with him. And from this is his saying, peace be upon him: As for Abu Jahm, he does not put his stick down from his shoulder, in one of the narrations. “It was narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he said to a man who advised him: Do not raise your stick from your family, fear God the most. Narrated by Ubadah ibn al-Samit, reported by al-Nasa’i. And from this meaning is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Hang your whip where your family can see it.” This was mentioned earlier in An-Nisa’. Among its benefits is that it alerts people to moving from this house, as was said to some ascetics: Why do you walk with a cane when you are neither old nor sick? He said: I know that I am a traveler, and that it is a fortress, and that the cane is a tool for travel. So some poets took it and said: I carried the stick, not because weakness made it necessary for me to carry it, nor because I bent over from old age. But I forced myself to carry it to let her know that the resident was on a journey.
20:19: God Almighty said: He said, ‘Throw it down, O Moses.’ When God Almighty wanted to train him in receiving prophethood and its duties, He ordered him to throw down the staff.
20:20: So he threw it down Moses, and God changed its characteristics and attributes. It was a two-branched stick, but the two branches became a mouth for it, and it became a snake that moved, walked, and swallowed stones. When Moses, peace be upon him, saw it, he saw a lesson, so he turned back and did not look back (al-Naml 27:10)
20:21: Then God said to him: Take it and do not fear because he felt fear within himself (Ta-Ha 20:67) meaning that what befalls humans befell him. It was narrated that Moses took it with the sleeve of his cloak and was forbidden from doing so, so he took it in his hand and it became a staff as it was the first time and this is its first behavior, and this sign was shown to him so that he would not be frightened by it if he threw it to Pharaoh. It was said that after that the staff would walk with him and talk to him and he would hang his loads on it, and the two branches would light up for him at night like a candle, and when he wanted to draw water, the two branches would turn like a bucket, and when he desired a fruit he would stick it in the ground and that fruit would bear fruit. It was said that it was from the myrtle of Paradise. It was said that Gabriel brought it to him. It was said that it was an angel. It was said that Shu'aib said to him: Take a staff from that house, so that staff fell into his hand, and it was the staff of Adam, peace be upon him, with which he descended from Paradise. And God knows best. God the Almighty said: And behold, it was a serpent, darting about. An-Nahhas: A serpent is permissible. It is said: It came out and behold, Zayd was sitting and sitting. The pause is a serpent with the letter ha. And to run is to walk quickly and lightly. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It turned into a male snake that swallows rocks and trees. When he saw it swallowing everything, he feared it and ran away from it. And on the authority of some of them: He was only afraid of it because he knew what Adam had suffered from it. And it was said that when his Lord said to him: Do not fear, his fear was removed and his soul was reassured that he put his hand in its mouth and took hold of its jaw. We will restore it to its former state. I heard Ali bin Sulayman say: The estimate is its state, like And Moses chose his people (al-A’raf 7:155). He said: And it is permissible for it to be a source because the meaning of We will restore it is We will make it walk.
20:22: The Almighty said: And put your hand to your side. Outside of the Qur'an, it is permissible to put a damma with a fatha on the meem or a kasra on it due to the meeting of two quiescent letters. The fatha is better because it is light, and the kasra is according to the original. The damma is permissible by imitation. The root of the word hand is handy on the basis of fa`al, as indicated by ayda. The diminutive of it is yadiya. The wing is the upper arm, as stated by Mujahid. He said: to means under. Qatrab: to your side to your pocket, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: I hug him to my chest and my wing It was said: To your side, so he expressed the side with the wing because it is inclined in the place of the wing. It was also said: To you. Muqatil said: To means with, i.e. with your wing. And It comes out white without evil without leprosy, a bright light that shines at night and during the day like the light of the sun and the moon, and brighter. On the authority of Ibn Abbas and others: So it came out a light that differed from its color. And white is accusative in the state, and it is not declined because it has two feminine alifs that do not leave it, so it is as if their adherence is a second reason, so it is not declined in the indefinite, and they differed from the ha’ because the ha’ separates from the noun. And without evil is from the connection of white as you say: it turned white without evil. Another sign other than the staff. So he took out his hand from an Egyptian coat of mail that had rays like the rays of the sun that blinded the sight. And sign is accusative in apposition to white, said Al-Akhfash. Al-Nahhas: It is a good statement. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that we have given you another sign, or we will give you, because when he said: It comes out white without blemish, he indicated that he had given him another sign.
20:23: To show you some of Our greatest signs meaning the greatest. He should have said the greatest, but he said the greatest to match the beginnings of the verses. It was said: There is an implication in it, meaning to show you some of Our greatest signs, the evidence for this is the statement of Ibn Abbas that the hand of Moses is the greatest of His signs.
20:24: The Almighty said: Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed. When He saw him with the staff and hand, and showed him what indicated that he was a messenger, He ordered him to go to Pharaoh and to call him. Transgressed means disobeyed, was arrogant, disbelieved, was tyrannical, and crossed the limit.
20:25: "He said, 'My Lord, expand for me my chest * And ease for me my task * And untie the knot from my tongue * That they may understand my speech * And appoint for me a helper from my family * Aaron, my brother.'" He asked for help to deliver the message. It is said that God informed him that He had bound Pharaoh's heart and that he would not believe, so Moses said, My Lord, how can You command me to come to him when You have bound his heart? An angel from the treasurers of the wind came to him and said, O Moses, go to what God has commanded you to do. Moses then said, My Lord, expand for me my chest, meaning expand it and enlighten it with faith and prophethood.
20:26: And make my task easy for me meaning make easy for me what you ordered me to do, which is to deliver the message to Pharaoh.
20:27: And untie the knot from my tongue meaning the lisp that was in it from the ember of the fire that he extinguished in his mouth when he was a child. Ibn Abbas said: There was a tangle in his tongue. That was because he was in Pharaoh's lap one day when he was a child, and he slapped him and took hold of his beard and pulled it out. Pharaoh said to Asiya: This is my enemy, so bring the slaughterers. Asiya said: Take it easy, for he is a child who does not differentiate between things. Then she brought two basins and put embers in one of them and a pearl in the other. Gabriel took Moses' hand and put it on the fire until he lifted the ember and put it in his mouth on his tongue, and that was the tangle. It was narrated that his hand was burned and that Pharaoh tried hard to treat it but it did not heal. When he called him, he said: To which Lord are you calling me? He said: To the One who healed my hand when I was unable to do so. And some of them said: His hand was not healed so that he would not put it in the same bowl with Pharaoh and the prohibition of eating together would be established between them. Then there was a difference of opinion as to whether that stumbling block went away. It was said: It went away based on his saying: You have been granted your request, O Moses. And it was said: It did not go away completely, based on his saying, narrating from Pharaoh: And he could hardly make himself clear (al-Zukhruf 43:52). And because he did not say: Untie all my tongue, this indicates that there remained in his tongue some holdback. And it was said: It went away completely based on his saying: You have been granted your request. And Pharaoh only said: And he could hardly make himself clear (al-Zukhruf 43:52) because he knew that stumbling block in his upbringing, and it was not proven to him that the affliction had gone away. I said: This is questionable, because if that were the case, Pharaoh would not have said: He could hardly make himself clear when Moses spoke to him in a smooth and eloquent tongue. And God knows best. It was said: That knot occurred in his tongue when he was communing with his Lord, so that he would not speak to anyone other than Him except with His permission.
20:28: They understand my saying means they know what I say to them and understand it. In Arabic, understanding means comprehension. An Arab said to Isa bin Omar: I testify that you are knowledgeable about jurisprudence. You say from it: the man understood, with a kasra, and so-and-so does not understand or understand. And I made you understand something. Then it is limited to the science of Sharia, and the one who knows it is a jurist. He understood, with a damma, understanding, and God made him understand, and he understood if he engaged in that. And I understood him if I discussed knowledge with him, as al-Jawhari said.
20:29: The minister who supports is like the one who eats with the one who eats with him, because he bears the burden of the sultan, i.e. his weight. In the book of Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad: I heard my aunt say that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever among you is given a job and God intends good for him, He will appoint for him a righteous minister who, if he forgets, will remind him, and if he remembers, he will help him. And from this meaning is his saying, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him: “God did not send a prophet or appoint a successor except that he had two entourages: one entourage that enjoined him to do good and urged him to do it, and another entourage that enjoined him to do evil and urged him to do it. The one who is protected is the one whom God protects.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari. So Moses asked God to appoint a minister for him, but he did not want to be limited to ministership so that he would not be a partner in prophethood. If it were not for that, it would have been permissible for him to appoint him as a minister without asking.
20:30: And he appointed, saying: Aaron. And it is in the accusative case as a substitute for his saying: a minister. And it is in the accusative case with make as an advancement and a delay, and the meaning is: And make for me Aaron, my brother, a minister. And Aaron was older than Moses by one year, and it was said: by three.
20:31: Strengthen my back with it meaning my back. The word azr means back, from the location of the two hips, and its meaning is that my soul is strengthened with it. Azr means strength, and azrahu means he strengthened him. And from this is the saying of God Almighty: So he strengthened him, so he became strong (al-Fath 48:29). And Abu Talib said: Didn't our father Hashim strengthen his resolve and command his sons to stab and beat? It was said: Azr is help. That is, it is a help that straightens my affairs. The poet said: I strengthened my resolve with him and realized that he is the brother of poverty, the one whose ways are narrow for him Aaron was fleshier than Moses, taller, whiter, and more eloquent. He died three years before Moses. There was a mole on Aaron's forehead, a mole on the tip of Moses' nose, and a mole on the tip of his tongue. No one before him had this mole, and no one after him will have it. It was said that it was the cause of the knot in his tongue. And God knows best.
20:32: And let him share my affair meaning in prophecy and conveying the message. The commentators said: Aaron was in Egypt at that time, so God commanded Moses to come with Aaron, and He revealed to Aaron while he was in Egypt to meet Moses, so he met him one stage and told him what was revealed to him, so Moses said to him: God commanded me to go to Pharaoh, so I asked my Lord to make you a messenger with me. The common people read Akhy Ishdad by connecting the alif, and And Ishrakhu by opening the hamza in supplication, meaning, strengthen my back, O Lord, and let him share with me in my affair. Ibn Amir, Yahya bin Al-Harith, Abu Haywah, Al-Hasan, and Abdullah bin Abi Ishaq read Ishdad by cutting the alif, and And Ishrakhu meaning I, O Lord, in my affair. An-Nahhas said: They put the two verbs in the subjunctive mood as an answer to his saying: And appoint for me a minister. This reading is strange and far-fetched, because an answer to something like this can only be derived from the meaning of condition and reward, so the meaning would be: If you appoint for me a minister from my family, I will strengthen my resolve with him and make him a partner in my affair. His affair is the prophethood and the message, and this is not up to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform about it. Rather, he asked God Almighty to make him a partner with him in the prophethood. The opening of the ya’ of brother is by Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr.
20:33: So that we may glorify You abundantly. It has been said that the meaning of glorify You is that we pray to You. It is possible that the glorification is with the tongue. That is, we purify You from what is not befitting of Your majesty. And abundantly is an adjective for a deleted source. It is also possible that it is an adjective for a time. Assimilation is good.
20:34: And so on, And we remember You often.
20:35: You were All-Seeing of us. Al-Khattabi said: All-Seeing is the one who sees, and All-Seeing is the one who knows the hidden aspects of things. So the meaning is, All-Knowing of us and aware of us in our childhood, so You were good to us, so be good to us as well, O Lord.
20:36: The Almighty said: He said, ‘Your request has been granted, O Moses.’ When he asked him to expand his chest and make the matter easy to what he mentioned, his request was answered and what he sought and desired came to him. The request is the request, a verb in the sense of a passive participle, like you say bread in the sense of baked and ate in the sense of eaten.
20:37: And the Almighty’s saying: And We have certainly bestowed upon you another time meaning before this, which is His, glory be to Him, protecting him from the evil of his enemies at the beginning, and that was when he was slaughtered. And God knows best. And the favor is kindness and favor.
20:38: And his saying: When We revealed to your mother what was revealed. It was said: We revealed means We inspired. And it was said: It was revealed to her in a dream. And Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed to her as it was revealed to the prophets.
20:39: Throw him into the Ark. Muqatil Mu'min of the family of Pharaoh said that he was the one who made the Ark and dragged it, and his name was Ezekiel. The Ark was made of sycamore. Throw him into the sea. That is, throw him into the sea: the Nile River. Let him cast him in. Al-Farra' said: Throw him into the sea. This is a command that contains the meaning of recompense. That is, throw him in, and the sea will cast him in. This is also the saying of God: Follow our path, and we will bear your sins. (Al-'Ankabut: 12). An enemy of mine and an enemy of his will take him, meaning Pharaoh. So she made an Ark, made a mat in it, and put Moses in it, and covered his head and his ribs - meaning his cracks - then she threw him into the Nile. A large river flowed from it in the house of Pharaoh, so God drove him in that river to the house of Pharaoh. It was narrated that she put ginned cotton in the Ark, put it in it, covered it and plastered it, then she threw it into the sea. A large river led from it to Pharaoh's garden. While he was sitting at the head of a pond with Asiya, there was the Ark. He ordered it to be brought out. It was opened and there was a young boy. The people woke up. The enemy of God loved it so much that he could not help but be patient. The apparent meaning of the Qur'an indicates that the sea threw it up on its shore, which is its beach. Pharaoh saw the Ark on the shore and ordered it to be taken. It is possible that the sea threw it up in a place on the shore, where the mouth of Pharaoh's river was, and then the river led it to the pond. And God knows best. It was said that Pharaoh's daughter found it and she had leprosy. When she opened the Ark, she was cured. It was narrated that when they picked up the Ark, they tried to open it but could not, and they tried to break it but they were exhausted. Asiya came closer and saw a light inside the Ark. She treated it and opened it. There was a young boy between his eyes, and he was sucking milk on his thumb, so they loved him. Pharaoh had a leprous daughter and the doctors said to him: You will not be cured except by the sea, which contains a resemblance to a human being and its cure is its saliva. So the leprous woman smeared her leprosy with his saliva and was cured. It was said: When she looked at his face she was cured. And God knows best. It was said: She found him a slave girl of Pharaoh's wife, and when Pharaoh looked at him he saw a boy with the most beautiful face of people, so Pharaoh loved him, and that is what God the Almighty said: And I have bestowed upon you love from Me. Ibn Abbas said: God loved him and made him beloved to His creation. Ibn Atiyyah said: He bestowed upon him a touch of beauty that those who saw it could hardly bear to be without. Qatada said: There was beauty in Moses' eyes and no one saw him without loving and adoring him. Ikrimah said: The meaning is: I placed beauty and grace in you so that no one sees you without loving you. At-Tabari said: The meaning is: I bestowed My mercy upon you. Ibn Zayd said: I made everyone who saw you love you until Pharaoh loved you and you were saved from his evil, and Asiya bint Muzahim loved you and adopted you. And let it be done under My eyes. Ibn Abbas said: He means that it was under My eyes where you were placed in the chest, where the chest was thrown into the sea, and where the maids of Pharaoh’s wife picked you up. They wanted to open the chest to see what was in it, but one of them said: Do not open it until you bring it to your mistress, for it is more favorable for you with her, and more likely that she will not accuse you of finding something in it and taking it for yourselves. Pharaoh’s wife did not drink water except what those maids drew. So they took the chest to her closed, and when she opened it, she saw a boy the likes of whom she had never seen before, and he bestowed his love upon her, so she took him and went with him to Pharaoh, and she said to him: A comfort of the eye for me and for you. (al-Qasas 28:9) Pharaoh said to her: As for you, yes, but as for me, no. It has reached us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If Pharaoh had said, ‘Yes, he is a comfort to me and to you,’ he would have believed and been truthful. She said, Give him to me and do not kill him, so he gave him to her. It has also been said, And let him be raised and fed in my sight, meaning that he should be raised and fed in my presence, as Qatada said. An-Nahhas said: This is well-known in the language. It is said, I made the horse and I made it if you took good care of it. The meaning is, And let him be raised in my sight means you did that. It has also been said that the lam is related to what follows it in His statement, When your sister walks, in terms of precedence and delay, when is an adverb for let him be made. It has also been said that the waw in let him be made is redundant. Ibn al-Qa’qa’ read let him be made with a sukoon on the lam as a command, and it appears to be for the addressee and the commanded is absent. Abu Nahik read let him be made with a fatha on the ta’. The meaning is that your movement and actions should be by my will and in my sight. Al-Mahdawi mentioned this.
20:40: When your sister walks The agent in when she walks is thrown or makes. It is possible that it is a substitute for when We revealed and his sister's name is Mary. "She says: Shall I direct you to someone who will take care of him?" That is because she went out to find out about him, and when Moses was given to Pharaoh by his wife, she sought wet nurses for him, and he did not take from anyone until his sister came, took him and placed him in her lap and gave him her breast, so he sucked it and was happy with it. They said to her: You will stay with us, so she said: I have no milk, but I will direct you to someone who will take care of him and they will be sincere to him. They said: Who is she? She said: My mother. They said: Does she have milk? She said: The milk of my brother Aaron. Aaron was older than Moses by one year. It was said: Three. It was said: Four. That is because Pharaoh had mercy on the Children of Israel and spared them from killing for four years, and Aaron was born during that time, as Ibn Abbas said. Then the mother came and he kissed her breast. This is what God Almighty said: So We returned you to your mother. In the Mushaf of Abu, We returned you “so that her eye might be cooled and she would not grieve.” Abdul Hamid narrated from Ibn Amir so that her eye might be cooled with a kasra on the qaf. Al-Jawhari said: And He cooled the eye with it and cooled the eyes with it. A man with cool eyes, and his eye has been cooled, is cooled and cooled, the opposite of heated. And God cooled his eye means He gave it to him until it is cooled and does not aspire to someone above him, and it is said: until it cools and does not heat up. For joy there is a cold tear, and for sadness there is a hot tear. This meaning was presented in (Maryam). And do not grieve means over your loss. And you killed a soul Ibn Abbas said: He killed an infidel Copt. Kaab said: He was twelve years old at that time. In Sahih Muslim: His killing was a mistake, as will come. So We saved you from grief means We saved you from fear, killing, and imprisonment. And We tested you with trials means We tested you with a test until you were fit for the message. Qatada said: We tested you with a trial. Mujahid said: We purified you with purity. Ibn Abbas said: We tested you with things before the message, the first of which was his mother carrying him in the year in which Pharaoh was slaughtering children, then throwing him into the river, then preventing him from breastfeeding except from his mother's breast, then dragging him by Pharaoh's beard, then taking him to the coal instead of the pearl, which warded off the killing of Pharaoh, then the Copt killed him and he went out fearing and watching, then his tending the sheep to train himself in tending people. It is said: A young goat from the sheep followed him most of the day, tiring him out, then he took him and kissed him and held him to his chest, and said to him: You have tired me and tired yourself, and he was not angry with him. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: This is why God chose him as a speaker, and this has already been mentioned in An-Nisa. God the Almighty says: So you remained with the people of Madyan for years. He means ten years, completing the two terms. Wahb said: He remained with Shu’ayb for twenty-eight years, ten of which were the dowry of his wife Safoor, the daughter of Shu’ayb, and eighteen he stayed with her until he had a child with her. And His statement: Then you came at a measured time, O Moses. Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan said: He means in accordance with the prophethood and message, because prophets are not sent until they are forty years old. Mujahid and Muqatil said: According to a measured time is a promise. Muhammad ibn Ka’b said: Then you came at the time I determined for you to come. The meaning is the same. That is, you came at the time we wanted to send you. The poet said: He attained the caliphate or it was a destiny for him as his Lord gave Moses according to destiny.
20:41: The Almighty said: And I created you for Myself. Ibn Abbas said: That is, I chose you for My revelation and My message. It was also said: I created you means I created you, taken from the word craft. It was also said: I strengthened you and taught you so that you might convey My commands and prohibitions to My servants.
20:42: Go, you and your brother, with My verses. Ibn Abbas said: He means the nine verses that were revealed to him. And do not slacken in remembering Me. Ibn Abbas said: Weaken, meaning in the matter of the message. Qatada said the same. It was also said: Invent falsehood. The poet said: Muhammad has not slept since God forgave him for his past and future sins. Weakness, lethargy, fatigue and exhaustion. Imru’ al-Qais said: Wipe if the swimmers on the sand raise dust with the kicked iron It is said: I became weak in the matter, so I am weak and a she-camel is weak, and I made it weak and tired. So-and-so does not become weak, meaning he does not stop. Aban interpreted the meaning of the verse in this way, and he cited as evidence the words of Tarafa: As if the pots standing in front of them were domes they built that never stop boiling. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas also: Do not be slow. And in the reading of Ibn Masoud: Do not be slow in remembering Me, praising Me, glorifying Me, and conveying My message.
20:43: It has four issues: God Almighty said: Go both of you. He said at the beginning of the verse: Go, you and your brother, with My signs. And He said here: Go both of you. So it was said: God Almighty commanded Moses and Aaron in this verse to reach out to Pharaoh’s call, and He first addressed Moses alone to honor him, then He repeated it for emphasis. And it was said: He explained with this that it is not enough for one of them to go. And it was said: The first was commanded to go to all the people, and the second to go to Pharaoh.
20:44: Second: In the Almighty's saying: Then speak to him with gentle speech is evidence of the permissibility of enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and that this is done with gentle speech for the one who has the strength and is guaranteed infallibility. Don't you see that He said: Then speak to him with gentle speech? And He said: Do not fear, for I am with you, hearing and seeing, so how about us, for we are more deserving of that. Then the one enjoining and forbidding will obtain what he desires and attain what he seeks, and this is clear. Third: People differed about the meaning of his saying softly. A group of them, Al-Kalbi and Ikrimah, said: It means his nickname. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Al-Suddi said the same. Then it was said: His nickname is Abu Al-Abbas. It was said: Abu Al-Walid. It was said: Abu Marra. According to this statement, giving a kunya to a disbeliever is permissible if he is a respected and honorable person and he hopes for his conversion to Islam. This may be permissible even if he does not hope for his conversion to Islam, because hope is not a reality that requires action. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a noble person from a people comes to you, honor him. He did not say, Even if you hope that he will convert to Islam. Honoring him includes calling him by his nickname. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Safwan ibn Umayya: He said to Saad: Did you not hear what Abu Habbab said, meaning Abdullah bin Ubayy? It was narrated in the Israelite narrations that Moses, peace be upon him, stood at the door of Pharaoh for a year, not finding a messenger to convey a message until he went out. What God has told us about that happened to him, and that was a consolation for those who came after him from the believers in their conduct with the oppressors, and your Lord knows best who is guided. It was said that Moses said to him: Believe in what you have come with, and worship the Lord of the Worlds, on the condition that you will have youth that will not grow old until death, and a kingdom that will not be taken from you until death, and your life will be extended by four hundred years, and when you die you will enter Paradise. This is the gentle statement. Ibn Masoud said: The gentle statement is the statement of God Almighty: Then say, ‘Would you like to be purified? And I will guide you to your Lord so that you may fear Him?’ (al-Nazi’at 79:18-19) It was said that the gentle statement is the statement of Moses: O Pharaoh, we are messengers of your Lord, Lord of the Worlds. He called him by this name because he loved him more than anything else that was said to him, as we call a king and the like. I said: A soft speech is a speech that is not harsh. It is said: Because something softens, softness, and something is soft and softness is an abbreviation of it, and the plural is softness. So if Moses was commanded to speak to Pharaoh softly, then it is more appropriate for those below him to follow that example in their speech, and to command them to do good in their speech. God Almighty said: And speak to people in good terms (al-Baqarah 2:83). As explained in (Al-Baqarah), and praise be to God. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Perhaps he will remember or fear. Its meaning is: on your hope and desire, so the expectation in it is only related to the human side, as stated by the great grammarians: Sibawayh and others. It was mentioned earlier in the beginning of (Al-Baqarah). Al-Zajjaj said: Perhaps is the word for hope and desire, so He addressed them with what they understand. It was said: Perhaps here means interrogation, and the meaning is see if he remembers. It was said: It means so that. It was said: It is a statement from God Almighty about what Aaron said to Moses, perhaps he will remember or fear, as stated by Al-Hasan. It was said: Perhaps and perhaps are in the entire Qur’an for what has happened. And Pharaoh remembered when he was about to drown and feared, so he said: I believe that there is no god except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims (Yunus 10:90). But that did not benefit him, as stated by Abu Bakr Al-Warraq and others. Yahya bin Muadh said about this verse: This is your gentleness with the one who says I am the god, so how about your gentleness with the one who says you are the god?! It has been said that Pharaoh relied on what Moses said when he called him, and consulted his wife, and she believed and advised him to believe. So he consulted Haman, who said: Do not do it. After you were a master, you will become a slave, and after you were a lord, you will become a master. And he said to him: I will restore you to youth. So he dyed his beard black, and he was the first to dye it.
20:45: The Almighty said: They said, 'Our Lord, indeed we fear that he will overreach us or that he will transgress.' Ad-Dahhak said: Yufrat means to hasten. He said: Yuftagh means to transgress. An-Nahhas said: The meaning is that we fear that something from him will overreach us. Al-Farra' said: Farrat minhu amr means to overflow. He said: And he overflowed means to transgress. He said: And he overflowed means to leave. The majority read Yufrat with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the ra', and its meaning is that he hastens and rushes to punish us. It is said: Farrat minni amr means to overflow. And from this comes the word Fart fi al-ma' which is the one who precedes the people to the water. That is, he will punish us with the punishment of the one who overreaches in sin, which is the one who is ahead in it, as Al-Mubarrad said. A group of them, including Ibn Muhaisin, read Yufrat with a fatha on the ya' and the ra'. Al-Mahdawi said: Perhaps it is a language. And from him also with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the ra', and its meaning is that someone will drive him to rush to us. A group read yufrit with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the ra’, and Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Ibn Muhaisin also read it this way. Its meaning is that he is excessive in harming us. The rajaz poet said: The foreigner has been too harsh on us and hastened.
20:46: There are two issues: First: The scholars said: When they were afflicted with what afflicts humans of fear for themselves, God the Almighty made them know that Pharaoh would not reach them or his people. This verse refutes those who said: He was not afraid, and fear of enemies is God’s law with His prophets and saints despite their knowledge of Him and their trust in Him. Al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, did well when he told the one who reported on the authority of Aamer bin Abdullah - that he camped with his companions on the road to Ash-Sham at a body of water, and a lion came between them and the water, so Aamer came to the water and took what he needed from it, and it was said to him: You have put your life at risk. He said: For the spears to clash in my belly is more beloved to me than for God to know that I fear something other than Him. He who was better than ‘Amir feared Moses, peace be upon him, when he said to him: “The eminent ones are conspiring against you to kill you, so go out. Indeed, I am to you among the sincere advisers.” So he went out from it, fearing and watching. He said: My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people. (al-Qasas 28:20-21) And he said: So he entered the city in the morning, fearing and watching. (al-Qasas 28:18) And he said when the magicians threw down their ropes and staffs: “So Moses felt fear within himself. We said: Fear not. Indeed, you are the superior.” (Ta-Ha: 67-68) I said: And from this, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) dug the trench around Medina to protect the Muslims and their money, while it was from trust and confidence in his Lord in a place that no one had reached. Then, there was something from his companions that no one is ignorant of, from their moving from their homes, once to Abyssinia, and once to Medina, fearing for themselves from the polytheists of Mecca, and fleeing for their religion that they would tempt them away from it by torturing them. Asma bint Umays said to Umar when he said to her, “We preceded you in migration, so we are more deserving of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) than you,” “You have lied, O Umar. No, by God, you were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he fed your hungry and preached to your ignorant, and we were in a distant and hateful home - or land - in Abyssinia, and that was for the sake of God and His Messenger. By God, I will not eat food or drink a drink until I remember what I said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and we were being harmed and afraid.” The hadith in its entirety was narrated by Muslim. The scholars said: The one who claims something about himself that is contrary to what God has created in the souls of the children of Adam is a liar. God has created them to flee from what harms them, causes them pain, or destroys them. They said: There is no harmer more harmful than a wild beast of ‘Aad in the desert of the earth to one who has no weapon with which to repel it, such as a sword, spear, arrow, bow, or the like. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, I am with you both means victory, assistance, and power over Pharaoh. This is like saying: The prince is with so-and-so, if you mean that he protects him. His saying: I hear and I see is an expression of the perception with which nothing is hidden, blessed be God, Lord of the worlds.
20:47: The Almighty said: So go to him and say, 'We are messengers of your Lord.' There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: So go to him and say that to him.
