Then send the Children of Israel with us. That is, leave them alone. And do not torment them. That is, by forcing them to work and toiling in work. The Children of Israel were under Pharaoh's severe torment. Their sons were slaughtered, their women were kept alive, and they were made to work in clay and bricks and build cities in a way they could not bear. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. Ibn Abbas said: He meant the staff and the hand. It was said: Pharaoh said to him: What is it? So he put his hand in the pocket of his shirt, then took it out white and it had rays like the rays of the sun, its light overcame the light of the sun and he was amazed by it. He did not see the staff except on the day of adornment. "And peace be upon those who follow guidance." Al-Zajjaj said: That is, whoever follows guidance is safe from the wrath and punishment of God Almighty. He said: It is not a greeting, and the evidence for that is that it is not the beginning of a meeting or a speech. Al-Farra: Peace be upon those who follow guidance and those who follow guidance.
20:48: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment meaning destruction and devastation in this world and eternity in Hell in the Hereafter is upon those who deny the prophets of God and turn away from faith. Ibn Abbas said: This is the most hopeful sign for the monotheists because they did not deny or turn away.
20:49: The Almighty said: He said, 'Who is your Lord, O Moses?' Pharaoh mentioned Moses without Aaron at the beginning of the verses. It was said: He singled him out for mention because he was the one who had the message, the speech, and the sign. It was said: They both conveyed the message even if he was silent, because at the time of speaking only one speaks, and if he stops, the other supports and backs him up. So we have a useful knowledge in this structure, that if two people are entrusted with a matter and one of them carries it out and the other person is present there and does not need him at one time and not another, that they have carried out the matter they were entrusted with and carried it out and deserved the reward, because God the Almighty said: Go to Pharaoh and He said: Go, you and your brother and He said: And say to him so He ordered them both to go and to speak, then He informed us at the time of the address by His saying: Who is your Lord? that he was present with Moses.
20:50: He said Moses: Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form meaning that it is known by its attributes, and it does not have a proper name so that it can be said so-and-so, rather He is the Creator of the world, and He is the One who gave each creature a form and image, and if the address was to both of them they would have said: They said our Lord. And created it is the first object of gave, meaning He gave His creation everything they need and are comfortable with, or the second of them, meaning He gave each thing its form and shape that matches the benefit assigned to it, according to the statement of Ad-Dahhak as follows. Then He guided Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubayr and As-Suddi said: He gave each thing its mate from its kind, then He guided it to its mate, food, drink and dwelling. And from Ibn Abbas: Then He guided it to intimacy, meeting and marriage. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: He gave each thing its goodness, and guided it to what is good for it. Mujahed said: He gave everything an image. He did not make the creation of man in the creation of animals, nor the creation of animals in the creation of man. Rather, He created everything and determined it with a determination. The poet said: And He has created everything, and so does God, whatever He wills, He does. By creation he means the image, and this is the opinion of Atiyah and Muqatil. Ad-Dahhak said: He gave each thing that He created the benefit assigned to it and corresponding to it. Meaning the hand for striking, the foot for walking, the tongue for speaking, the eye for seeing, and the ear for hearing. It was also said: He gave each thing what He inspired it with of knowledge or craftsmanship. Al-Farra’ said: He created the man for the woman, and for each male what matches him from the females, then He guided the male to the female. So the meaning of this is that He gave each thing like its creation. I said: This is the meaning of what Ibn Abbas said. The verse in its generality includes all opinions. Zaidah narrated on the authority of Al-A’mash that he read Who gave to each thing its creation with a fat-ha on the lam, which is the reading of Ibn Abi Ishaq and Nasir narrated it on the authority of Al-Kisa’i and others, meaning He gave the children of Adam everything He created that they need. So the two readings agree in meaning.
20:51: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: “He said: ‘Then what is the matter?’” The matter is the state, meaning what is its state and its affair? So he informed him that its knowledge is with God the Almighty, meaning that this is from the knowledge of the unseen that you asked about, and it is from what God the Almighty has kept to Himself and no one knows it but Him. And I am only a servant like you, I do not know of it except what the Knower of the Unseen has informed me of, and the knowledge of the conditions of the generations is written with God in the Preserved Tablet. And it was said: The meaning is: So what is the matter with the first generations that they did not acknowledge that? That is, so what is the matter with them that they went and worshipped other than your Lord. And it was said: He asked him about the deeds of the first generations, so he informed him that they are counted with God the Almighty, and preserved with Him in a book. That is, they are written, so He will reward them tomorrow for them and on them. And by the book he meant the Preserved Tablet. And it was said: It is a book with some of the angels. Second: This verse and similar ones that came before and will come indicate the recording and writing of knowledge so that it is not forgotten. For memorization may be afflicted by the defects of error and forgetfulness. And a person may not memorize what he hears, so he records it so that it does not go away from him. We narrated with a continuous chain of transmission on the authority of Qatada that it was said to him: Should we write what we hear from you? He said: What prevents you from writing when the Gracious, the All-Knowing has informed you that He writes?
20:52: He said: "Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord does not err, nor does He forget." And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God decreed creation, He wrote in His book concerning Himself, and it is placed with Him: ‘My mercy prevails over My wrath.’” Al-Khatib Abu Bakr narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: “A man from the Ansar used to sit with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, listening to hadith from him and he liked it but he did not memorize it. He complained about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God! I hear hadith from you that I like but I do not memorize it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Use your right hand, and he pointed to the line.” This is a text. The majority of the Companions and Followers agreed on the permissibility of writing and recording knowledge, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded: He wrote the sermon he gave during the Hajj for Abu Shah - a man from Yemen - when he asked him to write it down. Narrated by Muslim. Amr bin Shuaib narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Restrict knowledge by writing. Muawiyah ibn Qurra said: He who does not write knowledge, his knowledge is not considered knowledge. Some people have gone so far as to prohibit writing. Abu Nadrah narrated that Abu Saeed was asked: Should we write this hadith of yours? He said: Why do you make it the Qur’an? But memorize it as we have memorized it. Among those who did not write were Al-Sha’bi, Yunus ibn Ubayd, Khalid Al-Hadha’ - Khalid said: I never wrote anything except one hadith, and when I memorized it, I erased it - Ibn Awn and Al-Zuhri. Some of them used to write, and when they memorized it, they erased it, such as Muhammad ibn Sirin and Asim ibn Damrah. Hisham ibn Hassan said: I never wrote a hadith except the hadith of Al-A’maq, and when I memorized it, I erased it. I said: We have mentioned something like this about Khalid Al-Hadha’. And the hadith of Al-A’maq was included by Muslim at the end of the book: The Hour will not come until the Romans descend into the depths - or - Dabiq. This hadith is mentioned in the Book of Tribulations. Some of them would memorize and then write down what they memorized, including Al-A’mash, Abdullah bin Idris, Hisham, and others. This is a precaution for memorization. Writing is more important in general, and the verses and hadiths were mentioned in this way. It was narrated from Omar, Ali, Jabir, and Anas, may God be pleased with them, and those who came after them from the great followers such as Al-Hasan, Ata, Tawus, and Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, and those who came after them from the people of knowledge. God the Almighty said: And We wrote for him on the tablets of all things (al-A’raf 7:145). And God the Almighty said: And We had already written in the Psalms, after the remembrance, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants (Al-Anbiya’: 105). And God the Almighty said: And decree for us in this world [that which is] good (al-A’raf 7:156). And God the Almighty said: “And everything they did is in the scriptures. And everything small and great is recorded” (al-Qamar 54:52-53). And he said: Its knowledge is with my Lord in a Book and other verses. Also, knowledge is not recorded except by the Book, then by comparison, study, commitment, preservation, discussion, questioning and examination of the transmitters and trust in what they transmitted. Books were disliked by those of the early generation because of the recent era and the closeness of the chain of transmission, lest the writer rely on it and neglect it, or be reluctant to memorize it and act upon it. But since the time is far apart, the chain of transmission is not close, the paths are different, the transmitters are similar, the affliction of forgetfulness is an obstacle, and illusion is not safe, then restricting knowledge to the Book is more appropriate and more effective, and the evidence for its obligation is stronger. If someone argues with the hadith of Abu Saeed from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Do not write from me, and whoever writes other than the Qur’an, let him erase it. Narrated by Muslim. The answer is that this was in the past, so it was abrogated by his command to write, and his permission for Abu Shah and others to do so. Also, this was so that nothing would be mixed with the Qur’an that was not from it. Likewise, what was narrated from Abu Sa’id also - we were keen for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to give us permission to write, but he refused - if it is preserved, then it was before the migration, and when it was not safe to be occupied with it instead of the Qur’an. Third: Abu Bakr al-Khatib said: The hadith should be written in black, then ink in particular, not ink, because black is the most pigmented of colors, and ink is the most lasting of colors throughout the ages. It is the tool of the knowledgeable and the equipment of the people of knowledge. Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Hanbal said: My father told me: Al-Shafi’i saw me in his assembly and there was ink on my shirt and I was hiding it, so he said: Why do you hide it and cover it? Indeed, ink on the garment is part of chivalry because its image in the eyes is black, and in the minds it is white. Khalid bin Yazid said: The ink on the garment of the hadith master is like the perfume on the bride’s garment. Abu Abdullah al-Balawi took this meaning and said: The ink of the inkwells is fragrant for men and fragrant for women from saffron This is suitable for the clothes of that and this is suitable for the clothes of a horse Al-Mawardi mentioned that Abdullah bin Suleiman, as he narrated, saw a trace of yellowness on some of his clothes, yellowness, so he took some ink from the inkwell and smeared it with it, then he said: Our ink is better than saffron, and he recited: Saffron is the perfume of virgins and the ink of the sun is the perfume of men Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: My Lord does not err, nor does He forget. There are five different opinions about its meaning. The first: It is the beginning of a statement, to exonerate God Almighty from these two attributes. The statement was completed in His saying: in a Book. Al-Zajjaj said the same, and that the meaning of does not err is does not perish, from His saying: Will we then go astray in the earth? (al-Sajdah 32:10). Nor does He forget anything, He exonerated Him from perishing and forgetting. The second statement: Does not err does not make mistakes, Ibn Abbas said, meaning He does not make mistakes in planning, so whoever He gives respite, He gives him respite for a reason, and whoever He hastens, He has a reason for his hastening. The third statement: Does not err does not disappear. Ibn Al-A’rabi said: The root of error is concealment. It is said: the forgetful person is astray if he forgets to remember something. He said: The meaning of My Lord does not err, nor does He forget is that nothing is hidden from Him, nor is He hidden from anything. The fourth statement was also said by Al-Zajjaj and Al-Nahhas, and it is the most similar in meaning: God Almighty informed us that He does not need a book, and the meaning is that He does not lose knowledge of any of the things or their awareness, and He does not forget what He knows of them. I said: This statement goes back to the meaning of Ibn al-A'rabi's statement. A fifth statement: La yudalal Rabbiyy wa la yansa is in the position of an attribute of Kitab, meaning the Book is not astray from God, the Almighty, meaning it is not gone from Him. Wala yansa means it does not forget Him, so they are two attributes of Kitab. Based on this, the speech is connected and does not stop at Kitab. The Arabs say: The thing went astray for me if I did not find it, and Adhaltuhu ana if I left it in a place and did not find it there. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Isa bin Omar, Ibn Muhaisin, Asim al-Jahdari and Ibn Kathir read, as Shibl narrated from him, La yudalal with a damma on the ya' meaning my Lord does not waste it nor forget it. Ibn Arafa said: Misguidance among the Arabs is taking a path other than the intended one. It is said: He went astray from the road, and he lost something if he lost it. And from this, those who read La yudalal Rabbiyy read, meaning it is not lost. This is the doctrine of the Arabs.
20:53: The Almighty said: Who made the earth a cradle for you. "Who" is in the position of an attribute of my Lord, meaning my Lord who made does not go astray. It is possible that it is the predicate of an implied subject, meaning He is "Who. It is possible that it is in the accusative case with the implied I mean. The Kufians read mahdān here and in az-Zukhruf with the opening of the mīm and the sukūn of the hā. The rest read mahādān and Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose it because they agreed on the reading Have we not made the earth a cradle?" (an-Naba': 6). An-Nahhas: The plural is more appropriate because "mahdān" is a verbal noun and this is not the position of a verbal noun except with the deletion of the word, meaning a cradle. Al-Mahdawi: And whoever reads "mahdān it is possible that it is a verbal noun like fursh" meaning He made the earth a cradle for you, and it is possible that it is with the deletion of the added word, meaning a cradle. And whoever reads "mahādān it is possible that it is singular like furash. And it is possible that the plural of mahd" is used as a noun and is broken. The meaning of "mahādān" is a bed and a resting place on which you settle. "And He has made for you therein paths" meaning roads. Similar to "And God has made for you the earth a carpet * That you may walk therein wide paths" (Nuh 71:19-20) and God the Almighty said: "Who has made for you the earth a bed and has made for you therein paths that you may be guided" (al-Zukhruf 43:10). "And sent down water from the sky" its meaning was presented. This is the last of Moses' words, then God the Almighty said: "Then We brought it forth." It was said: It is all from Moses' words, and the meaning is "Then We brought it forth" meaning by plowing and processing, because the water sent down is the reason for the emergence of plants. The meaning of "pairs" is types and similarities, meaning different kinds of plants of different pairs and colors. Al-Akhfash said: The estimate is different pairs of plants. He said: Plants may be diverse, so "varied" may be an attribute of pairs, and it may be an attribute of plants. "Varied is taken from the word shat" meaning to be scattered. It is said: "Amr shat" meaning scattered. "Washat al-amr shatan wa shatatan means to be scattered, and istashta" is similar to it. And also dispersion. And he scattered him, he dispersed him. And my people scattered me, meaning they divided my affair. And dispersion means scattered. Ru’bah said, describing camels: They came together and knocked separately, stirring up the bright Sakhtita. A scattered mouth means a gaping hole. A diverse people, and diverse things. You say: they came scattered, meaning dispersed, and the singular is shat, as Al-Jawhari said.
20:54: The Almighty's saying: Eat and pasture your livestock is a command of permission. And pasture is from the verb ra'at which means groomed and its owner pastured it, meaning he fed it and let it out, intransitive and transitive. Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding meaning the minds. The singular is nahyah. He said that to them because they are the ones whose opinion is followed. It was said: because they forbid oneself from bad deeds. And all of this is from Moses as an argument against Pharaoh to prove the Creator in response to his saying: He said, 'Who is your Lord, O Moses?' And he explained that the Creator is only proven today by His actions.
20:55: The Almighty’s saying, From it We created you, means Adam, peace be upon him, because he was created from the earth, as stated by Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj and others. It was also said: Every sperm is created from dust, as indicated by the apparent meaning of the Qur’an. Abu Hurairah narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no newborn child but that some of the dust of his grave is sprinkled over him. Narrated by Abu Naim al-Hafiz in the chapter on Ibn Sirin. He said: This is a strange hadith from the hadith of Awn. We did not write it except from the hadith of Abu Asim al-Nabil, who is one of the trustworthy scholars from Basra. This meaning has already been explained in Surat al-An’am from Ibn Mas’ud. Ata’ al-Khurasani said: When the sperm falls into the womb, the angel assigned to the womb sets out and takes some of the dust of the place where it will be buried and sprinkles it over the sperm. Then God creates the soul from the sperm and from the dust. This is what God the Most High said: From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time. And in the hadith of al-Bara’ from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “When the soul of a believing servant departs, the angels ascend with him, and they do not pass by a group of angels except that they say, ‘What is this good soul? ’ They say, ‘So-and-so, son of so-and-so,’ using the best of the names they used to call him with in the world. So they ask permission for it to be opened, and it is opened, and those closest to it accompany it from each heaven to the heaven next to it until it reaches the seventh heaven. Then God, the Almighty, says, ‘Write for My servant a book in ‘Illiyyin and return him to the earth, for from it I created them, and into it I will return them, and from it I will bring them out another time. ’ So his soul is returned to his body.” And he mentioned the hadith. We have mentioned it in full in the book of At-Tadhkirah, and it was narrated from the hadith of ‘Ali, may God be pleased with him, as Al-Tha’labi mentioned. The meaning of and into it We will return you is after death, and and from it We will bring you out means for the resurrection and the reckoning. another time refers to His statement, from it We created you, not to we will return you. It is like saying: I bought a camel, a house, and another camel. The meaning is: We brought you out of the earth, and we will bring you out of the earth again after death.
20:56: The Almighty says: And We showed him all Our signs meaning the miracles indicating the prophethood of Moses. It was also said: God’s proofs indicating His Oneness. But he denied and refused meaning he did not believe. This indicates that he disbelieved out of stubbornness, because he saw the signs with his own eyes, not through report. Similar to this is: And they denied them, although their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance (al-Naml 27:14).
20:57: God Almighty said: He said, ‘Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?’ When he saw the signs that Moses had brought him, he said: It is magic. The meaning is: You have come to make people think that you have come with a sign that requires following you and believing in you, so that you may prevail over our land and over us.
20:58: So we will bring you magic like it meaning we will oppose you with something similar to what you have brought so that it will become clear to the people that what you have brought is not from God. So make between us and you an appointment is a source, meaning a promise. It was said that the appointment is a name for the place of the promise, as God the Almighty said: And indeed, Hell is their appointed time, all together (al-Hijr 15:43). So the appointment here is a place. It was said that the appointment is a name for the time of the promise, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, their appointed time is the morning (Hud 11:81). So the meaning is: Make for us a known day, or a known place. Al-Qushayri said: It is more apparent that it is a source, and that is why he said: We will not fail to fulfill it meaning we will not fail to fulfill that promise. Failure is to promise something and not fulfill it. Al-Jawhari said: The appointment is the appointment, time, and place, as is the appointment. Abu Ja`far ibn Al-Qa`qa`, Shaibah, and Al-A`raj read We will not fail to fulfill it in the subjunctive mood as an answer to his saying Make. And whoever raises it, it is an adjective for appointment and the meaning is: an appointment that will not be missed. A place other than Ibn Amir, Asim and Hamza read it with a damma on the seen. The rest read it with a kasra, and they are two languages like ‘Ada and ‘Ada and Tuwa and Tuwa. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose a kasra on the seen because it is the high and eloquent language. An-Nahhas said: The kasra is more well-known and famous. And they all added a nunation to the waw, and it was narrated from Al-Hasan, and it was differed from him to add a damma on the seen without a nunation. And there was a difference in its meaning, so it was said: other than this place, Al-Kalbi said. And it was said: and a level place where what we have explained in it becomes clear to people, Ibn Zayd said. Ibn Abbas: half. Mujahid: fair, and from him also and Qatada: justice between us and you. An-Nahhas said: The people of interpretation agree that the meaning of sawa is half and justice, and this is a good statement. Sibawayh said: It is said: sawa and sawa, meaning justice, meaning a place of justice between two places in which there is justice. Its origin is from your saying: He sat in the middle of the house with the extension, meaning in its middle, and the middle of everything is its justice. And in the hadith of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, And thus We have made you a middle nation (al-Baqarah 2:143) meaning justice. And Zuhair said: Show us a plan that is fair and just for us. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Qatabi said: He was in the middle between the two groups. Abu Ubaidah recited for Musa bin Jaber Al-Hanafi: Our father had settled in a town between Qais Qais Ailan and Al-Fazar. Al-Fazar: Sa`d bin Zaid Manat bin Tamim. Al-Akhfash said: Sawa if it means other than or means justice, there are three languages for it: If you add a damma to the seen or a kasra, you shorten both of them. If you open it, you lengthen it. You say: a place of sawaan, sawaan, and sawaan, meaning justice and moderation between the two groups. Musa bin Jaber said: We found our father had settled in the town The house. It was said: A place other than meaning a destination. The author of this statement recited: If my beloved wished she would never come back to me, or if I wished I would never come back to anyone but her And he says: I passed by a man other than you, other than you, meaning other than you. And they are the same in this matter, or if you like, they are the same. And they are the same for the plural and they are worse, and they are equal like eight, not according to analogy. And place is in the accusative case as the second object of made. And it is not appropriate to make it in the accusative case with the appointment as an object or an adverb for it, because the appointment has been described, and the nouns that work like verbs when they are described or made diminutive cannot work because they are not like a verb, and it is not appropriate to carry it as an adverb that takes the place of the second object, because if the appointment is followed by an adverb, the Arabs do not make it like sources with adverbs, but they are flexible in it, like the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, their appointment is the morning (Hud 11:81)
20:59: And your appointment is on the day of adornment. There is a difference of opinion about the day of adornment. Some say it is a day of celebration in which they would adorn themselves and gather. Qatada, Al-Suddi, and others said this. Ibn Abbas and Saeed bin Jubair said: It was the day of Ashura. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: It was a market day in which they would adorn themselves. Qatada also said this. Ad-Dahhak said: Saturday. It was also said: The day of Newroz, mentioned by Al-Tha'labi. It was also said: The day when the Gulf is broken, because they would go out on it to enjoy and take a walk, and at that time the Egyptian lands would be safe from the Nile. Al-Hasan, Al-A'mash, Isa Al-Thaqafi, Al-Salami, and Hiba from Hafs read the day of adornment in the accusative case. It was narrated from Abu Amr, meaning on the day of adornment, our appointment is fulfilled. The rest read it in the nominative case as a predicate of the subject. And that people are gathered at noon. That is, and the people are gathered, so that is in the nominative case according to the reading of those who read day in the nominative case. The conjunction of and that he will gather strengthens the reading of the nominative case, the place of the nominative case according to the reading of the one who reads day in the nominative case. The conjunction of and that he will gather strengthens the reading of the nominative case, because an cannot be a circumstance, even if the explicit source is a circumstance like the arrival of the pilgrim, because the one who says: I will come to you the arrival of the pilgrim does not say I will come to you that the pilgrim will come. An-Nahhas: It is more appropriate than this for it to be in the position of the accusative case in conjunction with adornment. Ad-Duha is feminine, the Arabs make it diminutive without a ha' so that its diminutive does not resemble the diminutive of Dhuhwa, said An-Nahhas. Al-Jawhari said: The morning of the day is after sunrise, then after it Ad-Duha, which is when the sun rises, shortened, feminine and masculine, so whoever feminizes it went to the plural of Ad-Duha, and whoever masculines went to the noun of the verb like Sard and Naghar, and it is a circumstance that is not established like magic, you say: I met him at dawn, Ad-Duha if you mean by it the morning of your day you do not add a tanween, then after it Ad-Duha is extended and masculine, and it is when the highest part of the day is reached. And he specified the forenoon because it is the beginning of the day, so if the matter had been extended between them, there would have been plenty of time during the day. It was narrated from Ibn Masoud, Al-Jahdary and others, And that the people will be gathered at forenoon, meaning that God will gather the people and something similar. And from some of the reciters, And that you will gather the people, meaning that you, O Pharaoh, will gather the people. And from Al-Jahdary also, And that we will gather with the letter nun. And He promised them that day, so that the word of God would be elevated, His religion would appear, the disbeliever would be subdued, and falsehood would perish before all witnesses. And in the crowded gathering, to strengthen the desire of those who desire the truth, and to end the limit of the falsifiers and their followers. The one who narrates that matter will increase knowledge in every desert and city, and it will spread among the people of the hair and the city.
20:60: The Almighty said: Then Pharaoh turned away and gathered his plot meaning his tricks and magic, and what is meant is gathering the magicians. Ibn Abbas said: They were seventy-two magicians, with each magician of them ropes and sticks. It was also said: They were four hundred. It was also said: They were twelve thousand. It was also said: Fourteen thousand. Ibn Al-Munkadir said: They were eighty thousand. It was also said: They were gathered around a leader called Shimon. It was also said: His name was John, and with him were twelve captains, with each captain twenty overseers, with each overseer a thousand magicians. It was also said: They were three hundred thousand magicians from Fayoum, three hundred thousand magicians from Upper Egypt, and three hundred thousand magicians from the countryside, so they became nine hundred thousand, and their leader was blind. Then he came meaning the appointed time came.
20:61: Moses said to them meaning he said to Pharaoh and the magicians Woe to you is a prayer for woe upon them. It has the meaning of a source. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj said: It is accusative meaning God imposed woe upon them. He said: It is permissible for it to be a call like the Almighty's saying: Woe to us from those who sent us (Ya-Sin 36:52). Do not invent a lie against God meaning do not invent lies about Him, do not associate partners with Him, and do not say that miracles are magic. He will destroy you with a punishment from Him, meaning He will uproot you with destruction. It is said about it: saht and asaht with the same meaning. Its origin is from the exhaustion of poetry. The Kufians read fisahtakum from asaht, the rest read fisahtakum from saht. This is the language of the people of Hijaz and the first is the language of Banu Tamim. It is accusative as an answer to the prohibition. Al-Farazdaq said: There was a time, O Ibn Marwan, when nothing was left of money except what was wiped out or wasted. Al-Zamakhshari: This is a verse that people are still struggling to find the right grammar for. And he who fabricates has failed, meaning he has lost and perished. And he who claims from God what He has not permitted has failed in mercy and reward.
20:62: The Almighty said: And they disputed their affair among themselves meaning they consulted, meaning the magicians. And they whispered secretly Qatada said They said: If what he brought was magic, then we will defeat him, and if it was from God, then he will have a decision, and this is what they whispered. It was said that what they whispered was their saying: Indeed, these two are magicians the verse, as stated by Al-Suddi and Muqatil. It was said that what they whispered was their saying: If we are defeated, we will follow him, as stated by Al-Kalbi, his evidence is what appeared of the consequences of their affair. It was said: Their secret was that they said when Moses said to them Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against God (Ta-Ha 20:61): This is not the speech of a magician. Al-Najwa is the secret conversation that can be a noun and a source, and its explanation was presented in (An-Nisaa)
20:63: The Almighty said: Indeed, these two are magicians. Abu Amr read Indeed, these two are magicians. It was narrated on the authority of Uthman and Aisha, may God be pleased with them, and others from the Companions, and so did Al-Hasan, Saeed bin Jubair, Ibrahim Al-Nakha'i, and others from the Followers. Among the reciters were Isa bin Omar and Asim Al-Jahdary, according to what An-Nahhas mentioned. This reading is in accordance with the grammar and contrary to the Mushaf. Az-Zuhri, Al-Khalil bin Ahmad, Al-Mufaddal, Abaan, Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Kathir, and Asim in the narration of Hafs from him read Indeed, these two with a light in "are magicians. Ibn Kathir stresses the nun of these two." This reading is free from contradicting the Mushaf and from corrupt grammar, and its meaning is that these two are nothing but magicians. The Medinans and Kufians read "Indeed, these two with a stress on in are magicians," so they agreed with the Mushaf and differed from the grammar. Al-Nahhas said: These are three readings that the group narrated from the imams. It was narrated from Abdullah bin Masoud that he read: Indeed these two are magicians. Al-Kisa’i said about Abdullah’s reading: Indeed these two are magicians without a lam. Al-Farra’ said about the letter of Abi: Indeed these two are magicians. These are three other readings that are interpreted, not that it is permissible to read them because they contradict the Qur’an. I said: The scholars have six opinions regarding the recitation of the people of Medina and Kufa. Ibn al-Anbari mentioned them at the end of his book Al-Radd, Al-Nahhas in his I'rab, Al-Mahdawi in his Tafsir, and others who included the words of some of them in others. Some people made mistakes with them, so Abu Amr said: I am ashamed before God to recite "Indeed, these two" and Urwah narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she was asked about the words of God, the Most High: "But those firmly rooted in knowledge" (An-Nisa': 162), then He said: "And those who establish" (al-Ma’idah 5:69) and in (Al-Ma'idah) "Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and Indeed, these two are magicians", so she said: O son of my sister! This is a mistake by the writer. Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, said: There is a mistake in the Mushaf, and the Arabs will correct it with their tongues. Abaan bin Uthman said: I read this verse in the presence of Abu Uthman bin Affan, and he said: It is a mistake and a mistake, so someone said to him: Why don't you change it? He said: Leave it, for it does not forbid what is permissible nor does it permit what is forbidden. The first of the six opinions is that it is the language of Banu al-Harith ibn Ka’b, Zubayd, Khatham, and Kinanah ibn Zayd. They make the nominative, accusative, and genitive of two words with the alif. They say: The two Zayds came, I saw the two Zayds, and I passed by the two Zayds. From this is the saying of God Almighty: And I could not have made you aware of it (Yunus 10:16) based on what was mentioned above. Al-Farra’ recited a poem on the authority of a man from Banu Asad - he said: I have not seen anyone more eloquent than him: He lowered his head like a brave man, and if he had seen a way for his brave fang to stab him, he would have been deaf. They say: His hands were broken and his upper body was ridden, meaning his hands and his upper body. Their poet said: He was struck between his ears by a blow that made him bury himself in the dust. Another said: They flew over them, mushrooms flew over them On them and on her. Another said: Her father and her father's father have reached the peak of glory. That is, her father's father and her goal. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: This statement is one of the best interpretations of the verse, since this language was well-known, and it was narrated by someone whose knowledge and trustworthiness are accepted, including Abu Zaid al-Ansari, who said: If Sibawayh says, "Someone I trust told me," then he only means me. Abu al-Khattab al-Akhfash, who is a leader of the leaders of language, al-Kisa'i and al-Farra', all said this according to the language of Bani al-Harith ibn Ka'b. Abu Ubaidah narrated from Abu al-Khattab that this is the language of Bani Kinanah. Al-Mahdawi: And others narrated that it is the language of Khatham. An-Nahhas said: Among the most obvious statements in this regard is the statement of Sibawayh: Know that when you dualize a singular noun, you add two additional letters to it, the first of which is a long vowel and a soft letter, which is the letter of i'rab. Abu Ja'far said: Sibawayh's statement: which is the letter of i'rab, necessitates that the original does not change, so "inna ha-dahan" came in its original form to show that. God Almighty said: "Satan has overcome them" (Al-Mujadilah: 19) and He did not say istihadha, so this came to indicate the original, and likewise "inna ha-dahan" and do not think about the denial of those who denied this language if the imams have narrated it. The second statement: That "in" means yes, as Al-Kisa'i narrated from Asim who said: The Arabs use "an to mean yes, and Sibawayh narrated that in" means ajal, and Muhammad ibn Yazid and Ismail ibn Ishaq Al-Qadi used to hold this opinion. An-Nahhas said: I saw Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj and Ali ibn Sulayman hold this opinion. Al-Zamakhshari: Abu Ishaq was impressed by it. An-Nahhas: And Ali bin Sulaiman told us, he said: Abdullah bin Ahmad bin Abdul Salam An-Naysaburi told us, then I met this Abdullah bin Ahmad and he told me, he said: Umair bin Al-Mutawakkil told me, he said: Muhammad bin Musa An-Nawfali from the descendants of Harith bin Abdul Muttalib told us, he said: Amr bin Jami’ Al-Kufi told us on the authority of Ja’far bin Muhammad on the authority of his father on the authority of Ali - who is the son of Al-Hussein - on the authority of his father on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with them all, he said: I cannot count how many times I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say on his pulpit: Indeed, all praise is due to God, we praise Him and seek His help. Then he says: I am the most eloquent of all the Quraysh, and the most eloquent after me is Aban ibn Sa`id ibn al-`As. Abu Muhammad al-Khaffaf said: Umair said: Its parsing according to the scholars of Arabic and grammar is Indeed, all praise is due to God in the accusative case, except that the Arabs make in in the meaning of yes, as if he, may God bless him and grant him peace, meant yes, all praise is due to God. This is because the orators of the Age of Ignorance used to begin their sermons with yes. The poet said in the meaning of yes: They said you betrayed me, so I said, perhaps the traitor will attain glory and satisfy his thirst. Abdullah bin Qais Al-Ruqayyat said: The firstborn of the blamers in my youth would blame me and I would blame him They say, "Grey hair has covered you, and you have grown old. I said, It is..." Therefore, it is permissible for the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, these two are magicians to mean yes and not to be accusative. An-Nahhas said: Dawud ibn al-Haytham recited to me? He said: Tha’lab recited to me: I wonder if there is a cure for the lover’s pain of loving them when they meet Al-Nahhas said: This is a good statement, except that there is something wrong with it, because it is only said: Yes, Zayd is outside, and the lam is hardly used here, even though the grammarians have spoken about that and said: The lam is intended to be presented, as he said: My uncle is you and from Jarir, his uncle will attain glory and honor his uncles last: Umm Al-Halis, an old woman, is satisfied with the neck bone of a sheep. That is, for my uncle and for Umm Al-Halis. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the verse is that these two are magicians, then the subject was deleted. Al-Mahdawi: Abu Ali and Abu Al-Fath bin Jinni denied it. Abu Al-Fath said: The deleted they was not deleted until after it was known, and if it was known, then its knowledge sufficed with its confirmation with the lam, and it is ugly to delete the confirmed and leave the confirmed. The third statement was also said by Al-Farra: I found the alif a support that is not the lam of the verb, so I added a nun to it and did not change it, as I said: who then I added a nun to it and said: The ones with you came to me, and I saw the ones with you, and I passed by the ones with you. The fourth statement was said by some of the Kufians, he said: The alif in these two is similar to the alif in they do, so it was not changed. The fifth statement: Abu Ishaq said: The ancient grammarians say that the ha’ here is implied, and the meaning is: These two are magicians. Ibn al-Anbari said: So the ha’ which is the accusative of in was implied, and these two is the predicate of in and magicians raises it because they is implied, and the meaning is that these two are magicians for them. What is more likely according to the proponents of this answer is that the ha’ is the subject of in and these two is raised by the beginning, and what follows it is the predicate of the beginning. The sixth statement: Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: I asked Abu al-Hasan ibn Kaysan about this verse, and he said: If you wish, I will answer you with the answer of the grammarians, and if you wish, I will answer you with my statement, so I said: With your statement, so he said: Ismail ibn Ishaq asked me about it, so I said: The statement with me is that since this was said in the place of the nominative, accusative, and genitive in the same state, and the dual should not change the singular for it, the dual was treated as the singular, so he said: How good this is if someone preceded you in saying it so that he would be familiar with it, Ibn Kaysan said: So I said to him: So the judge says it so that he would be familiar with it, so he smiled. God the Almighty says: They want to expel you from your land with their magic and do away with your best way. This is from what Pharaoh said to the magicians, meaning their goal is to corrupt your religion that you are following, as Pharaoh said: Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that corruption will appear on earth. (Ghafir 40:26). It is said: So-and-so has a good way, meaning he has a good way. It is also said: The way of the people is the best speech, and this is what they should follow and emulate. So the meaning is: And they go with your masters and leaders, to attract them. Or they go with the Children of Israel, who are the best, even though they were slaves to you because of their lineage to the prophets. Or they go with the people of your way, so the complement was deleted. Mithla is the feminine of most just as one says afdal and fazla. The way is feminine according to the word, even though it refers to men. It is permissible for the feminization to be for the group. Al-Kisa’i said: By your way is by your tradition and your mark. Mithla is an adjective, like saying an old woman. The Arabs say: So-and-so is on the right path, meaning on the straight path.
20:64: The Almighty's saying: So gather your plan. Consensus is the ruling and determination on something. You say: I gathered to go out and on the exit, meaning I resolved. The reading of all the countries is So gather except for Abu Amr, who read So gather with a continuous vowel and a fat-ha on the meem. He used as evidence his saying: So gather his plan then he came. An-Nahhas said, and what was narrated to me from Muhammad bin Yazid, that he said: Abu Amr must read differently from this reading of his, which is the reading that most people follow. He said: Because he used as evidence gather and the Almighty's saying: So gather his plan has been established, so it is unlikely that it is after it So gather and it is likely that it is after it So gather meaning resolve and find, and since that was mentioned before, it is necessary that this be different from its meaning. It is said: A matter that is agreed upon and agreed upon. An-Nahhas said: The reading of Abu Amr is correct So gather meaning gather every plan for you and every trick and include it with its brother. Abu Ishaq said the same. Al-Tha’labi: The reading with the alif cut off and the mim broken has two meanings: One of them: meaning gathering. You say: I gathered the thing and gathered it, meaning one thing. In Al-Sahah: And I gathered the thing, I made it all together. Abu Dhu’ayb said, describing a donkey: It is as if she is in a panic between the two tribes of Nabai and the women of Dhu al-Arja’a, a gathering of looters. Any group. The second: It means determination and perfection. The poet said: I wonder, for hopes are of no avail, will I ever become one day when my affair is resolved? Any firm one. Then come in rows. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: All together. It was said: Rows so that your awe is greater. It is accusative because the verb occurs upon it according to the saying of Abu Ubaidah, who said: It is said: I came to the row meaning the prayer place, so the meaning according to him is come to the place where you gather on the day of Eid. It was narrated from some of the eloquent Arabs: I was not able to come to the row, meaning the prayer place. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that the meaning is then come and the people are lined up, so it would be a verbal noun in the place of the state. That is why it was not pluralized. It was read then come with a kasra on the meem and a ya. Whoever left out the hamza replaced the hamza with an alif. And today he who prevailed has succeeded meaning he who overcame. And all of this is from what the magicians said to each other. It was said: from what Pharaoh said to them.
20:65: God Almighty said: “They said, ‘O Moses,’ meaning the magicians. ‘Either you throw down your staff from your hand, or we will be the first to throw down.’ They were polite with Moses, and that was the reason for their faith.
20:66: He said, 'Rather, throw.' But behold, their ropes in the speech were omitted, i.e., they threw, the meaning indicated it. Al-Hasan read and their sticks with a damma on the 'ayn. Harun al-Qari' said: The language of Banu Tamim is and their sticks and al-Hasan takes it. The rest use it with a kasra following the kasra on the sad. Similar to it are dali and dali and qasi and qasi. It appeared to him from their magic that they were moving. Ibn Abbas, Abu Haywah, Ibn Dhakwan and Ruh from Ya'qub read khayal with a ta', and they attributed it to the sticks and ropes since they are feminine. This is because they smeared the sticks with mercury, and when the sun's heat hit them, they trembled and shook. Al-Kalbi said: It appeared to Moses that the earth was alive and that it was moving on its belly. It was read khayal in the sense of imagined and its path is the path of imagination. Whoever read yakhyal with a ya' attributed it to the plot. It was read nakhil with a noon on the basis that God is the One who imagines the trial and trial. It was said: The subject is that it is striving, so that is in the nominative case, meaning that he imagines that it is striving, as Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Farra’ claimed that its position is in the accusative case, meaning that it is, then the ba’ was deleted. The meaning in the first version is: He was made to think that their magic and their trickery were like that, until he thought that it was striving. Al-Zajjaj said: Whoever reads with the ta’ made that in the accusative case, meaning that he imagined that it was striving. He said: It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a substitute for the pronoun in imagination, which refers back to the ropes and sticks, and the substitute in it is a substitute for inclusion. And ta’isa means that it walks.
20:67: The Almighty said: So Moses felt fear within himself meaning he concealed it. It was also said: he found. It was also said: he sensed. That is, from the snakes, and this is based on what occurs from human nature as mentioned above. It was also said: he feared that the people would be tempted before he threw his staff. It was also said: he feared when the revelation was delayed to him about throwing the staff that the people would disperse before that and be tempted. Some of the people of truth said: the reason was that when Moses, peace be upon him, met the magicians and said to them: Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against God, or He will destroy you with a punishment (Ta-Ha 20:61), he turned and saw Gabriel on his right, so he said to him: O Moses, be gentle with the friends of God. Moses said: O Gabriel, these are magicians who came with great magic to nullify the miracle, support the religion of Pharaoh, and reject the religion of God. You say: Be gentle with the friends of God! Gabriel said: They are with you from now until the afternoon prayer, and after the afternoon prayer they are in Paradise. When he said that to him, Moses felt a sense of dread and thought that he did not know what God knew about me, so perhaps I would now be in a state, and God’s knowledge about me would be different from it, as these people were.
20:68: When God knew what was in his heart, God revealed to him, Do not fear, for you are the highest, meaning the one who will prevail over them in this world and in the highest ranks in Paradise, because of the prophethood and selection that God has given you. The root of khaifa is khawfa, but the waw was changed to a yaa because of the kasra of the khaa.
20:69: The Almighty said: And throw down what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have made. He did not say and throw down your staff. It is possible that it is a diminutive of it, meaning do not care about the multitude of their ropes and staffs. Throw down the small, individual stick in your right hand, because by the power of God it will swallow it up despite its unity and multitude, and its smallness and greatness. It is possible that it is a glorification of it, meaning do not pay attention to these many large bodies, because in your right hand there is something greater than all of them, and these, despite their multitude, are the least and most insignificant thing compared to them, so throw it down and it will swallow it up, by God's permission, and will destroy it. Talqaf in the subjunctive mood is the answer to the command, as if he said: If you throw it, it will swallow up, meaning it will take and swallow. As-Salami and Hafs read talqaf with a silent lām from lāqāf yalqāf to swallow. Ibn Dhakwan, Abu Haywah al-Shami and Yahya ibn al-Harith read talqaf without the tā and raising the fā, meaning that it will swallow up. The address is to Moses. It was said: to the stick. And the word laqf means to take quickly. It is said: laqafat al-shay’ with a kasra alqafhu laqf I caught something and talaqafatuhu I caught it also means to grab it quickly. On the authority of Yaqub: It is said that a man is laqafa thaqaf light and skillful. And the word laqf with a fatha means the wall falling. And laqf with a fatha means that the basin laqf the basin fell, meaning that it was rushed from below and widened. And talaqafa with a fatha and talaqama with a fatha have the same meaning. It has been mentioned in al-A’raf with a kasra. laqmat with a kasra is laqma with a kasra, and talaqamatuhu with a fatha if he swallowed it in a while. And likewise lamah with a kasra if he swallowed it. ma sana’u what they made means that which they made. And likewise inma sana’u in the nominative case sihr magic with a kasra on the seen and a sukoon on the ha’, and this is the reading of the Kufians except for Asim. There are two views on this: One of them: that kayd is added to sihr in imitation without estimating an omission. And the second: that there is an omission in the speech, meaning kayd of a magician. The rest read kayd in the accusative case because the action of making is upon it, and ma is a plural and does not imply a ha’, sahir is an addition. In reality, according to this reading, kayd is an addition to the magician, not to magic. It is permissible to open an to mean because what they made is the trick of a magician. And the magician will not succeed wherever he comes from meaning he will not win or escape wherever he comes from on earth. It was said: wherever he schemed. The ruling on the magician and the meaning of magic has already passed in (Al-Baqarah), so consider it there.
20:70: The Almighty said: So the magicians fell down in prostration when they saw the enormity of the matter and the extraordinary nature of the staff, as it swallowed all the ropes and sticks they had contrived with, and it was the load of three hundred camels, then it returned to being a staff, and no one knows where the ropes and sticks went except God the Almighty. This meaning has already been mentioned in (Al-A'raf) and the matter of the staff is complete. They said, 'We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.'
20:71: He said, 'You have believed in him' meaning in him, it is said: he believed in him and he believed in him, and from this So Lot believed in him (al-Ankabut 29:26) and in Al-A'raf He said, 'You have believed in him before I gave you permission' (al-A’raf 7:123). A denial from him to them, meaning you transgressed and did what I did not command you to do. Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic meaning your leader in teaching, and he only defeated you because he was more skilled in it than you. Pharaoh only wanted by his saying this to make people think that they would not follow them and believe as they believed, otherwise Pharaoh knew that they did not learn from Moses, but rather they had learned magic before Moses came and was born. Then I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees meaning on the trunks of palm trees. Suwayd ibn Abi Kahil said: They crucified Al-Abdi on the trunk of a palm tree, and no old man sneezed except on his trunk. So he cut them up and crucified them until they died, may God have mercy on them. Ibn Muhaisin read here and in Al-A’raf, So I will cut them up, and I will crucify you, with the alif open and the letter cut pronounced with a light cut and crucify. “And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting,” meaning me or the Lord of Moses.
20:72: The Almighty said: They said meaning the magicians We will not give you preference meaning we will not choose you over what has come to us of clear proofs. Ibn Abbas said: He means certainty and knowledge. Ikrimah and others said: When they prostrated, God showed them in their prostration their homes in Paradise, so that is why they said: We will not give you preference. Pharaoh's wife was asking who had won, and she was told: Moses and Aaron had won, so she said: I believe in the Lord of Moses and Aaron. So Pharaoh sent to her and said: Look for the largest rock, and if she continues with what she said, then throw it on her. So when they came to her, she raised her eyes to the sky and saw her home in Paradise, so she continued with what she said, so her soul was taken away, and the rock was thrown on her body, although there was no soul in her body. It was said: The leader of the magicians said to the one he trusted when he saw what he saw of Moses’ staff: Look at this snake, are you afraid that it might be a jinn or are you not afraid? It is the work of the Creator, from whom nothing is hidden. He said: I am not afraid. He said: I have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses. And He Who created us It was said: It is conjoined with What has come to us of clear proofs meaning we will not prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs nor over He Who created us, meaning we created. It was said: It is an oath, meaning by God we will not prefer you. Then decide what you decide The meaning is what you decide. What here, which is with the verb, is not like a source, because that is connected to verbs, while this is connected to a subject and predicate. Ibn Abbas said: Then make what you make. It was said: Then rule what you rule, meaning of cutting and solidifying. The ya was deleted from qadi in the connection because it was still and the tanween was still. Sibawayh chose to keep it in the pause because the reason for the two still letters was removed. You only decree this worldly life means that your command is only carried out in it. It is in the accusative case as a circumstantial, and the meaning is: You only decree the enjoyment of this worldly life. Or the time of this worldly life, so the object is deleted. It is also possible that the estimation is: You only decree the affairs of this worldly life, so it is in the accusative case as the object, and ma is a conjunction because of in. Al-Farra' permitted the nominative case on the condition that ma means who and the ha is deleted from declares and this worldly life is in the nominative case.
20:73: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord meaning we believed in God alone, with no partner, and in what Moses brought to us that He may forgive us our sins meaning the polytheism they were doing. And what you forced us to do of magic "what" is in the accusative case, conjoined with the sins. It was said: it has no position and it is negative, meaning that He may forgive us our sins of magic and what you forced us to do. An-Nahhas: The first is more appropriate. Al-Mahdawi: There is more to it, because they said: "Shall we have a reward if we are the victors?" (Ash-Shu'ara: 41) This is not the statement of those who were forced, and because compulsion is not a sin, even though it is possible that they were forced to learn it when they were young. Al-Hasan said: They were taught magic as children, then they practiced it of their own free will later. It is possible that "what" is in the nominative case as a subject and the predicate is implied, and the estimate is: And what you forced us to do of magic is removed from us. And "of magic according to this statement and the first statement is related to you forced us". And that ma is a negative related to our sins. “And God is better and more lasting,” meaning His reward is better and more lasting, so the complement was deleted, as Ibn Abbas said. And it was said: God is better for us than you and more lasting in punishment for us than your punishment for us. And this is the answer to His statement: And you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting. And it was said: God is better for us if we obey Him, and more lasting in punishment than you if we disobey Him.
20:74: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal It was said: It is from what the magicians said when they believed. It was also said: It is the beginning of a speech from God Almighty. The metaphor in indeed refers to the matter and the affair. It is permissible that whoever comes, and from it the poet's saying: Whoever enters the church one day will find therein a camel and a gazelle. He meant that he who enters, that is, this is the matter, that the criminal enters Hell, and the believer enters Paradise. And the criminal is the disbeliever. And it was said: the one who commits sins and earns them. And the first is more likely, because of His saying: For him is Hell, wherein he will neither die nor live. And this is the description of the disbelieving, lying, denier - as was explained previously in Surat An-Nisa and other verses - so he does not benefit from his life nor find rest in his death. The poet said: Is there no soul that does not die, so that its misery ends, and it does not live a life that has any taste? It was said: The soul of the unbeliever is suspended in his throat, as God Almighty informed us about it, so he does not die from its separation, nor does he live with its stability. The meaning of whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal is whoever comes to the appointment with his Lord.
20:75: The meaning of and whoever comes to Him as a believer is that he dies upon it and comes to Him believing in it. He has done means he has done righteous deeds meaning acts of obedience and what he was commanded to do and what he was forbidden to do. Then those will have the highest degrees meaning the lofty degrees that the attributes fall short of. His statement, and whoever comes to Him as a believer indicates that what is meant by the criminal is the polytheist.
20:76: The Almighty’s saying: Gardens of Eden is an explanation of the degrees and a substitute for them, and Eden is the residence, and its explanation has been presented. Underneath them meaning beneath their chambers and beds rivers flow of wine, honey, milk and water, and this has been presented. Abiding therein meaning staying permanently. And that is the reward of he who purifies himself meaning he who purifies himself from disbelief and sins. And whoever said that this is from the sayings of magicians said: Perhaps the magicians heard it from Moses, or from the Children of Israel, since there were people among them in Egypt, and among them was also the believer from the family of Pharaoh. I said: It is possible that this was an inspiration from God to them, causing them to speak about it when they believed, and God knows best.
20:77: The Almighty said: And We inspired Moses, saying, 'Travel by night with My servants.' This has been fully discussed. And strike for them a dry path through the sea. That is, dry, with no mud or water in it. Moses struck the sea and gave it a nickname, and drowned Pharaoh, so there is no point in repeating it. Do not fear being overtaken. That is, being caught up with by Pharaoh and his soldiers. And do not fear. Ibn Jurayj said that the companions of Moses said: This is Pharaoh who has caught up with us, and this sea has covered us. So God revealed: Do not fear being overtaken, nor do you fear. That is, do not fear being overtaken by Pharaoh, nor do you fear drowning from the sea that it might touch you if it overtakes you. Hamza read Do not fear as an answer to the command. The meaning is that if you strike for them a path through the sea, do not fear. Do not fear is a new sentence based on the meaning: Nor do you fear. Or it may be in the subjunctive mood and the alif is filled with a fatha, like his saying: So they led us astray from the path (al-Ahzab 33:67), or it may be like the saying of the poet: As if you have never seen a Yemeni prisoner before me Assuming the vowel is deleted as the vowel is deleted in the correct word. This is the view of Al-Farra’. Another said: I satirized Zaban, then I came to apologize for satirizing Zaban. You did not satirize and did not claim Another said: Didn't the report reach you, spreading report of what happened to the camels of Banu Ziyad? Al-Nahhas said: This is one of the worst mistakes to interpret the Book of God, the Almighty, as anomalous poetry. Also, what he brought from poetry does not resemble anything in the verse, because the ya and waw are different from the alif, because they move and the alif does not move. If the poet is forced to consider them to be moving, then the movement is deleted for the jazm, and this is impossible in the alif. The first reading is clearer because after it nor fear is agreed upon without jazm, and there are three interpretations in it: The first: That nor fear is in the position of a state of the addressee, the interpretation is strike for them a dry path in the sea, neither afraid nor afraid. The second: That it is in the position of an adjective for the path, because it is conjoined with dryness, which is an adjective, and the interpretation is that you do not fear in it, so the referent from the adjective is deleted. The third: That it is disconnected, the predicate of a deleted beginning, the interpretation is and you do not fear.
20:78: The Almighty said: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers meaning he pursued them and his soldiers with him. It is also read Fataba'ahum with emphasis, so the ba in bijunudihi returns the verb to the second object, because taba'a is transitive to one object. That is, he followed them to catch up with his soldiers, that is, with his soldiers, as it is said: the prince rode with his sword, that is, with his sword. And whoever cuts off Fataba'a, it is transitive to two objects: so it is possible that the ba is redundant, or it is possible that it was limited to one object. It is said: taba'ahu, ataba'ahu, lahaqah, and lahaqah all mean the same thing. And his saying: bijunudihi is in the place of the state, as if he said: So he pursued them, driving his soldiers. "So what covered them from the sea covered them" meaning what drowned them from the sea befell them, and it was repeated to mean glorification and knowledge of the matter.
20:79: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them meaning he led them astray from the right path and did not guide them to good or salvation, because he had determined that Moses, peace be upon him, and those with him would not escape him, because the sea was in front of them. So when Moses struck the sea with his staff, twelve paths split from it, and between the paths was water standing like mountains. And in Surat Ash-Shu'ara' So each section was like a great mountain (Ash-Shu'ara': 63) meaning a great mountain, so each tribe took a path. And God inspired the mountains of water to interlock, so they became networks, and they could see each other and hear each other's speech. This was one of the greatest miracles and greatest signs. So when Pharaoh approached and saw the paths in the sea and the water standing, he made them think that the sea had done this out of awe of him, so he and his companions entered and the sea closed over them. It was said that his saying: And did not guide is an emphasis on his leading them astray. It was said: It is the answer to Pharaoh’s saying: I do not show you except what I see, and I do not guide you except to the path of right conduct (Ghafir 40:29), so God Almighty denied him. Ibn Abbas said: And he did not guide means he did not guide himself, but rather he destroyed himself and his people.
20:80: The Almighty said: O Children of Israel, We have delivered you from your enemy. When He delivered them from Pharaoh, He said to them, This is so that they may be grateful. "And We made an appointment with you on the right side of the Mount. Side is in the accusative case as the second object of We made an appointment." It is not appropriate for it to be in the accusative case as an adverb of place, because it is a purely vague adverb of place. Verbs and verbal nouns are transitive to adverbs of place without a preposition if they are vague. Makki said: This is a basic principle that is not disputed. The meaning of the verse is: And We made an appointment with you to come to the side of the Mount, then the noun was deleted. An-Nahhas said: That is, We ordered Moses to command you to go out with him so that he could speak to him in your presence and you could hear the speech. It was said: Moses promised after drowning Pharaoh that he would come to the right side of the Mount and give him the Torah. So the promise was for Moses, but they were addressed with it because the promise was for their sake. Abu Amr read Wa wa’adnakum without an alif, and Abu Ubaid chose it, because the promise was from God Almighty to Moses specifically, and a promise can only be made by two people. This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. “The right” is in the accusative case, because it describes the side, and the mountain has neither a right nor a left. So if it is said: Take to the right of the mountain, it means take to your right from the mountain. The mountain was to the right of Moses when he came to it. And We sent down upon you manna and quails meaning in the wilderness, and this has already been mentioned.
20:81: Eat from the good things We have provided for you meaning from the delicious provisions. It was also said: from what is lawful, since no human being has made any effort in it, so that doubt would enter into it. And do not transgress therein meaning do not let abundance and well-being lead you to disobey, because transgression is going beyond what is permissible. It was also said: the meaning is, do not be ungrateful for the blessing and do not forget to thank the One who bestowed it upon you. It was also said: that is, do not exchange it for anything else, as He said: Would you exchange that which is better for that which is less? (al-Baqarah 2:61). It was also said: Do not store up any of it for more than a day and a night. Ibn Abbas said: So that what they have stored up will worm its way into them, and were it not for that, no food would ever worm its way. So My wrath will descend upon you meaning it will be necessary and will descend, and it is in the accusative case with the fa' in response to the prohibition in His statement: And do not transgress. "My wrath will descend upon you, and whoever incurs My wrath has certainly perished. Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Waththab and Al-Kisa'i read fihal with a damma on the ha', and man yahllul" with a damma on the first lam. The rest read it with a kasra, and they are two dialects. Abu Ubaidah and others narrated that it is said: "hala yahllu means it became obligatory, and hala yahllu" means it descended. Al-Farra' also said: The damma is from hulul meaning it occurred, and the kasra is from wujub. The two meanings are close, except that the kasra is more appropriate, because they agreed on the statement of Al-Ash'ari: "and a lasting torment will descend upon him" (Hud 11:39). And the wrath of God is His punishment, vengeance and torment. "hawa" means he has perished, meaning he has reached the abyss, which is the depth of the Fire, from hawa yahwu hawyan meaning he fell from a high place to a low place, and hawa fulan means he died. Ibn al-Mubarak said: Ismail bin Ayyash told us: Tha’laba bin Muslim told us on the authority of Ayoub bin Bashir on the authority of Shafi al-Asbahi who said: In Hell there is a mountain called Ascending, which the disbeliever ascends for forty autumns before he ascends it. God Almighty said: I will make him ascend with a mighty ascent (al-Muddaththir 74:17). And in Hell there is a palace called Hawa, from the top of which the disbeliever is thrown, and he falls for forty autumns before he reaches its base. God Almighty said: And whoever incurs My wrath has certainly fallen. And he mentioned the hadith, and we have mentioned it in the Book of Remembrance.
20:82: The Almighty said: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents meaning from polytheism. And believes and does righteousness then is guided, meaning he remained in his faith until he died upon it, as stated by Sufyan Ath-Thawri, Qatadah and others. Ibn Abbas said: meaning he did not doubt his faith, as stated by Al-Mawardi and Al-Mahdawi. Sahl bin Abdullah Al-Tustari and Ibn Abbas also said: He remained upon the Sunnah and the Jama'ah, as stated by Al-Tha'labi. Anas said: He followed the Sunnah of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as stated by Al-Mahdawi, and Al-Mawardi narrated it from Al-Rabi' bin Anas. A fifth statement: He did the right thing, as stated by Ibn Zayd, and from him also he learned knowledge to be guided on how to act, as stated by Al-Mahdawi the first, and Al-Tha'labi the second. Al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: He knew that there is a reward for that and a punishment for it, as stated by Al-Farra'. An eighth statement: Then he was guided is in the guardianship of the family of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as stated by Thabit Al-Bunani. The first statement is the best of these statements - God willing - and the rest of them go back to it. Wakee’ said on the authority of Sufyan: We used to hear regarding the words of God Almighty: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents meaning from polytheism and believes meaning after polytheism and does righteousness “prays and fasts” then is guided “and dies in that state.”
20:83: The Almighty said: And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses? meaning what made you precede them. It was said: By the people he meant all the Children of Israel, so based on this it was said: He appointed Aaron as his successor over the Children of Israel, and he went out with him with seventy men to the appointed time. So his saying: They are on my trail does not mean that they are walking behind him heading towards him, but rather he meant that they are near me waiting for me to return to them. And it was said: Rather, Aaron was ordered to follow his trail with the Children of Israel and join him. And some people said: He meant the seventy people whom he had chosen, and when Moses approached the mountain, he preceded them out of longing to hear the word of God. And it was said: When he came to Tursina with the promise, he longed for his Lord, and the distance became long for him because of the intensity of his longing for God Almighty, so the matter became difficult for him until he tore his shirt, then he could not wait until he left them and went alone, so when he stood in his place God Almighty said: And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?
20:84: So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) remained perplexed about the answer and he referred to it by saying: "They are on my heels." He only asked him about the reason that made him hurry by saying: "What?" So he informed about their coming by the heels. Then he said: "And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased." So he referred to mentioning the longing and his sincerity in seeking pleasure. Abd al-Razzaq mentioned on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah regarding his statement: "And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased," he said: Longing. And Aisha may God be pleased with her when she went to bed would say: Bring me the glorious Qur'an. Then she would be brought the Qur'an and she would hold it in her chest and sleep with it, consoling herself with that. It was narrated by Sufyan on the authority of Misa'ar on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her. "And when it rained, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would take off his clothes and strip off until the rain fell on him and he would say: It is a recent occurrence with my Lord. This is from the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who came after him, in the sense of longing. Therefore, God, blessed be His name, said in what is narrated from him: (The longing of the righteous to meet Me has been long, and I am even more longing to meet them.) Ibn Abbas said: God knew, but He said, And what made you hasten away from your people? out of mercy for Moses, and honoring him with this statement, and calming his heart, and tenderness towards him, so he said in response to his Lord: They are the ones following in my footsteps. Abu Hatim said: Isa said: Banu Tamim say: They are the ones following in my footsteps shortened and extended, and the people of Hijaz say the ones following in my footsteps. Al-Farra’ narrated: They are the ones following in my footsteps. Abu Ishaq Al-Zajjaj claimed that this has no basis. Al-Nahhas said: It is as he said, because this is not something that can be added, so it is like my guidance. It is not without one of two aspects: Either it is an ambiguous name, so its addition is impossible, or it is in the meaning of those, so it is not added either, because what comes after it is complete and it is definite. Ibn Abi Ishaq read: Nasr and Rawis on the authority of Yaqub, on my trace, with a kasra on the hamza and a sukoon on the tha’, and it means trace, two languages. And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You might be pleased meaning I hastened to the place that You commanded me to go to so that You might be pleased with me. It is said: a man who is hasty, hasty, hasty, and hasty between haste, and haste is the opposite of slowness.
20:85: The Almighty said: So We have tried your people after you meaning We tested them and tried them by asking them to find evidence for God Almighty. And the Samiri led them astray meaning he called them to misguidance or he was the cause of it. It was said: We tested them and threw them into temptation: meaning We made the worship of the calf attractive to them, and for this reason Moses said: It is only your temptation (al-A’raf 7:155). Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Samiri was from a people who worshipped cows, so he settled in the land of Egypt and entered the religion of the Children of Israel outwardly, but in his heart was what was in it of the worship of cows. It was said: He was a Copt, and he was a neighbor of Moses, who believed in him and went out with him. It was said: He was a great man from the great men of the Children of Israel, from a tribe known as the Samaria, and they are known in the Levant. Saeed bin Jubair said: He was from the people of Kerman.
20:86: The Almighty said: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. This is a state, and its full explanation has already been given in Al-A'raf. He said, 'O my people, did not your Lord promise you a good promise?' God Almighty promised them Paradise if they remained obedient to Him, and He promised them that He would let them hear His words in the Torah through Moses, so that they would act according to what was in it and deserve the reward for their actions. It was said: He promised them victory and triumph. It was also said: His promise was in His statement: And indeed, I am Forgiving to whoever repents and believes. The verse. Has the covenant been prolonged for you? That is, have you forgotten, as was said, and something may be forgotten due to the length of the covenant. Or did you want the wrath of your Lord to descend upon you? "Did descend" means it must be and descend. Anger is punishment and vengeance. The meaning is: Or did you want to do an action that would be the cause of the wrath of God descending upon you, because no one seeks the wrath of God, but rather he may commit what would be the cause of wrath. "So you broke your promise to me" because they promised him that they would remain obedient to God Almighty until he returned to them from Mount Tur. It was said: He promised them after him the meals, but they stopped.
20:87: "They said, 'We did not break your appointment by our own power'" with the opening of the meem, and this is the reading of Nafi', Asim, and Isa bin Omar. Mujahid and Al-Suddi said: Its meaning is with our ability. Ibn Zayd: We did not control ourselves, meaning we were forced.
