Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir read "by our own power" with the breaking of the meem. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it because it is the elevated language. It is the source of the verb "malakat al-shay', I own it, I own it, a kingdom." The source is added to the subject and the object is deleted, because he said: "by our own power" is correct, rather we made a mistake, so it is an admission of their mistake. Hamza and Al-Kisa'i read "by our own power" with the closing of the meem, and the meaning is by our authority. That is, we did not have the power to break your appointment. Then it was said that his saying: They said is general and what is meant by it is specific, that is, those who remained steadfast in obeying God until He returned to them from the Mount said: We did not fail to meet you by our will and they were twelve thousand, and all the Children of Israel were six hundred thousand. But we carried with a damma on the ha’ and a shaddah on the meem with a kasra, Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, Hafs and Ruways read it. The rest read it with a fatha on both letters and a light one. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it because they carried the people’s jewelry with them and they did not carry it unwillingly. Burdens means heavy loads from the people’s adornments meaning from their jewelry, and they borrowed it when they wanted to go out with Moses, peace be upon him, and they made them think that they were meeting for a festival or a banquet. It was said: It is what they took from the people of Pharaoh when the sea threw them up to the shore. It was called burdens because they were sins, that is, it was not permissible for them to take it and it was not permissible for them to take the spoils, and also burdens are weights in the language. So we threw it meaning that the burden of what we had with us of jewelry was too heavy for us, so we threw it into the fire to melt, meaning we threw it into it. It was also said: We threw it to the Samaritan so that you could come back and make up your mind about it. Qatada said: The Samaritan said to them when the people were slow to see Moses: He was only held back from you because of the jewelry you have, so they gathered it and gave it to the Samaritan, so he threw it into the fire.
20:88: And he fashioned a calf for them from it, then he threw on it a handful of the traces of the Prophet's horse, which was Gabriel, peace be upon him. Muammar said: The horse that Gabriel was riding was life, and when he threw the handful on it, it became a calf with a body that mooed. And mooing is the sound of cows. Ibn Abbas said: When the jewelry was poured into the fire, the Samaritan came and said to Aaron: O Prophet of God, should I throw what is in my hand - and he thought that it was like some of the jewelry that others had brought - so he threw dirt into it and said: Be a calf with a body that moos, and it was as he said, for affliction and trial, so it mooed once and was not followed by another. It was said: Its mooing and sound were with wind, because he had made holes in it, and when wind entered its body it mooed but there was no life in it. This is the saying of Mujahid. According to the first saying, it was a calf of flesh and blood, which is the saying of Al-Hasan, Qatada and Al-Suddi. Hammad narrated on the authority of Samak on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Aaron passed by the Samaritan while he was making the calf, and he said: What is this? He said: It benefits and does not harm. He said: O God, give him what he asked for in his heart. He said: O God, I ask you to make him moo. And when he mooed, they prostrated themselves, and the mooing was because of Aaron’s supplication. Ibn Abbas said: It mooed like the mooing of a living calf. It was narrated that Moses said: O Lord, this Samaritan brought out for them a calf with a body that mooed from their jewelry, so who made the body and the mooing? God the Blessed and Exalted said: I. Moses, peace be upon him, said: By Your glory and majesty and Your elevation and Your power, none led them astray except You. He said: You have spoken the truth, O Wise of the wise. All of this has been mentioned previously in Surat Al-A’raf. And they said, ‘This is your god and the god of Moses.’ That is, the Samaritan and those who followed him said, and they were inclined to liken God to Him, as they said: Make for us a god as they have gods (al-A’raf 7:138). So he forgot means he preferred Moses and went looking for him but did not know where he was, and he lost his way to his Lord. It was said that its meaning is: Moses left him here and went out looking for him. That is, Moses left his God here. Israel narrated on the authority of Samak on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: That is, Moses forgot to tell you that he was his God. It was said that the address is about the Samaritan. That is, the Samaritan left what Moses commanded him to do of faith, which is a preference, as Ibn al-A'rabi said.
20:89: Then God the Almighty said, arguing with them: Do they not see meaning consider and think about that He does not return to them with speech meaning He does not speak to them. It was said: He does not return to lowing and sound. And He does not possess for them harm or benefit So how can He be a god?! The one whom Moses, peace be upon him, worships harms and benefits and rewards and gives and prevents. That He does not return means that He does not return, so the verb was raised and that was lightened and the pronoun was deleted. This is the choice in seeing, knowledge and conjecture. He said: In the youth of the swords of India, they knew that whoever is barefoot and wears shoes will perish. It may be deleted with emphasis. He said: If I were a lizard, you would know my kinship, but I am a black man with big lips. But you.
20:90: God Almighty says: And Aaron had already said to them before, that is, before Moses came and returned to them, O my people, you have only been tested by it, that is, you were tested and led astray by it, that is, by the calf, and your Lord is the Most Merciful, not the calf, so follow me, in His worship, and obey my command, not the command of the Samaritan. Or follow me in my journey to Moses and abandon the calf.
20:91: So they disobeyed him and said, We will not cease to be devoted to it meaning, we will not cease to worship the calf until Moses returns to us to see if he will worship it as we worshipped it. They thought that Moses was worshipping the calf, so Aaron separated from them with twelve thousand of those who did not worship the calf. When Moses returned and heard the shouting and the commotion and they were dancing around the calf, he said to the seventy with him: This is the sound of the tribulation.
20:92: When Aaron saw it, he took hold of his hair with his right hand and his beard with his left in anger and said, "O Aaron, what prevented you when you saw them going astray?" That is, they lost their way and disbelieved. "That you do not follow. Do is redundant for follow my command and advice." It was said: What prevented you from following me in denouncing them? It was said: Its meaning is, why didn't you fight them when you knew that if I were among them, I would fight them for their disbelief? It was said: What prevented you from joining me when they were tempted?
20:93: Did you disobey my command? He means that your standing among them while they worshipped other than God is disobedience from you to me, as Ibn Abbas said. It was said: Its meaning is why did you not leave them so that your leaving them would be a rebuke and a warning to them. The meaning of Did you disobey my command? It was said: His command is what God Almighty narrated about him: And Moses said to his brother Aaron, Take my place among my people and do right and do not follow the way of the corrupters. (al-A’raf 7:142) So when he stayed with them and did not exaggerate in preventing them and denouncing them, he attributed it to his disobedience and opposition to his command. Question: All of this is the basis for enjoining good and forbidding evil, changing it and leaving its people, and that the one who resides among them, especially if he is satisfied, his ruling is the same as their ruling. This meaning has already been mentioned in Al Imran, An-Nisa, Al-Ma’idah, Al-An’am, Al-A’raf and Al-Anfal. Imam Abu Bakr Al-Tartushi may God have mercy on him was asked: What does our master the jurist say about the Sufi school of thought? I know - may God protect his life - that a group of men gathered, and they would frequently mention God the Almighty and Muhammad (peace be upon him), then they would strike a stick on a piece of leather, and some of them would stand up and dance and become excited until they would faint, and they would bring something to eat. Is it permissible to be present with them or not? Please advise us, may you be rewarded. This is what they say: Oh Sheikh, stop committing sins before you become divided and make mistakes. Do good for yourself as long as it benefits you. Youth has passed and your hair has turned grey And in such and similar cases. The answer: - May God have mercy on you - the Sufi doctrine is idleness, ignorance and misguidance. Islam is nothing but the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger. As for dancing and ecstasy, the first to encourage it were the companions of the Samaritan, when he made for them a calf with a body that mooed, they began to dance around it and ecstasy. It is the religion of the infidels and the worshippers of the calf. As for the rod, the first to be used by the heretics was to distract the Muslims from the Book of God Almighty. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to sit with his companions as if there were birds on their heads out of dignity. Therefore, the ruler and his deputies should prevent them from attending mosques and elsewhere. It is not permissible for anyone who believes in God and the Last Day to attend with them or help them in their falsehood. This is the doctrine of Malik, Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and other imams of the Muslims. And God is the Grantor of success.
20:94: God the Almighty said: O son of my mother, do not seize me by my beard or by my head. Ibn Abbas: He took his hair with his right hand and his beard with his left, because jealousy for God made him his master, meaning do not do this so that they think that it is from you to belittle or punish. It has been said that Moses, peace be upon him, did this without belittling or punishing him, as a person seizes his beard. This has been mentioned in full in (Al-A'raf) and God the Almighty knows best what His Prophet, peace be upon him, intended. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You have divided the Children of Israel.' That is, I feared that I would go out and leave them, and you had ordered me to go out with them. If I went out, some people would follow me and some people would stay behind with the calf, and perhaps the matter would lead to bloodshed. I feared that if I rebuked them, a fight would break out and you would blame me for that. This is Aaron’s answer to Moses, peace be upon him, about his saying: Did you disobey my command? And in al-A’raf 7:“Indeed, the people considered me weak and almost killed me. So do not let the enemies rejoice over me” (al-A’raf 7:150) because you ordered me to be with them. It has been mentioned before. The meaning of and you did not wait for my word is you did not act according to my advice to preserve it, as Muqatil said. Abu Ubaidah said: you did not wait for my covenant and my arrival.
20:95: Then Moses left him and turned to the Samaritan and said, What is the matter with you, O Samaritan? That is, what is your matter and your affair, and what made you do what you did? Qatada said: The Samaritan was a great man among the Children of Israel from a tribe called Samaria, but the enemy of God became a hypocrite after he crossed the sea with Moses. So when the Children of Israel passed by the Amalekites while they were worshipping their idols, They said, O Moses, make for us a god as they have gods. (al-A’raf 7:138) So the Samaritan took advantage of this and knew that they were inclined to worship the calf, so he made the calf.
20:96: So the Samaritan said in response to Moses: I saw what they did not see meaning: I saw what they did not see. I saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, on the horse of life, so I thought to myself that I would take a handful of his trace, but I did not throw it on anything except that it became a soul, flesh and blood. So when they asked you to make a god for them, my soul made that seem good to me. And Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: When Gabriel descended to ascend with Moses, peace be upon him, to the heavens, the Samaritan saw him from among the people, so he took a handful of the horse's trace. And it was said that the Samaritan said: I saw Gabriel on the horse, and it was making its stride as far as the eye could see, so I thought to myself that I would take a handful of its trace, but I did not throw it on anything except that it became a soul and blood. And it was said: He saw Gabriel on the day he descended on Ramkah and Daqiq, so he advanced the horses of Pharaoh to enter the sea. It is said that the mother of the Samaritan placed him in a cave when she gave birth to him, fearing that Pharaoh would kill him. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and put the hand of the Samaritan in the mouth of the Samaritan, and he suckled honey and milk. Then he went to him and recognized him from that time. This meaning was mentioned in Al-A'raf. It is said that the Samaritan heard the words of Moses, peace be upon him, when he made two statues of wax, one of them a bull and the other a horse, and threw them into the Nile, seeking the grave of Joseph, peace be upon him, which was in a stone coffin in the Nile. The bull brought him on his horn, and the Samaritan spoke the words that he heard from Moses, and threw the handful into the belly of the calf, and it became fragrant. Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i, Al-A'mash, and Khalaf read By what you have not seen with the ta' of addressing. The rest read with the ya' of reporting. Abi bin Ka'b, Ibn Mas'ud, Al-Hasan, and Qatadah read Fa-qabasat Qabsa with an unvoiced sad. It was narrated from Al-Hasan with a damma on the qaf of qabsa and an unvoiced sad. The rest read Fa-qabasat Qabsa with the voiced dad. The difference between them is that grasping is done with the whole hand, and grasping is done with the tips of the fingers, and the like, such as khadam and qadam. The fist with a damma on the qaf is the amount that is grasped, as mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. Al-Jawhari did not mention a fist with a damma on the qaf and an unvoiced sad, but rather he mentioned the fist with a damma on the qaf and an unvoiced dad, which is what you grasp of something. It is said: He gave him a fistful of gruel or dates, meaning a handful of it, and sometimes it is said with a fatha. He said: And grasping with a kasra on the qaf and an unvoiced sad is a large number of people. Al-Kumait said: You have the two mosques of God, the two graves, and you have a handful of pebbles from among the richest and the poorest. So I threw it away means I threw it in the bucket. And my soul tempted me means it adorned it, said Al-Akhfash. Ibn Zayd said: My soul told me. The meaning is close.
20:97: God Almighty said: He said, ‘Then go.’ That is, Moses said to him, Then go, that is, from among us. For in this life you will have the right to say, ‘No touch.’ That is, neither yesterday nor yesterday throughout your life. So Moses banished him from his people and ordered the Children of Israel not to mix with him, nor come near him, nor speak to him as a punishment for him. The poet said: Tamim, like the Samaritan, said: The Samaritan does not want to touch you. Al-Hasan said: God made the punishment of the Samaritan that he should not touch people and that they should not touch him, a punishment for him and for those who were like him until the Day of Resurrection. It is as if God, the Almighty, made the ordeal difficult for him, by making him not touch anyone and not allowing anyone to touch him, and made that a punishment for him in this world. It is said: He was afflicted with obsessive thoughts, and the origin of obsessive thoughts is from that time. Qatada said: Their remnants to this day say that - no touching - and if one of the others touches one of them, they both die at the same time. It is said: Moses intended to kill the Samaritan, but God, the Almighty, said to him: Do not kill him, for he is generous. It is said that when Moses said to him: Then go, for in this life you will have the right to say no touching, he was afraid and fled and wandered in the wilderness with wild beasts and beasts, not finding anyone to touch him until he became like someone who says no touching, because of his distance from people and people being far from him, as the poet said: A flag bearer with a mask, until the Azd say, No competition. Question: This verse is the basis for banishing the people of innovation and sins and abandoning them and not mixing with them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did that with Ka’b ibn Malik and the three who stayed behind. Whoever seeks refuge in the Haram and is required to be killed is not to be killed according to some jurists, but he is not to be dealt with, sold to, or bought from, and it is exhausting to leave. From this category is banishment as a punishment for adultery. All of this has been mentioned in its place, so there is no point in repeating it. Praise be to God alone. Harun al-Qari’ said: The language of the Arabs is la masas with a kasra on the seen and a fatha on the meem, and grammarians have spoken about it. Sibawayh said: It is built on the kasra as you say hit the man. Abu Ishaq said: la masas is a negation and the kasra is from the sign of femininity, you say: I did it, woman. Al-Nahhas said: I heard Ali bin Sulaiman say: I heard Muhammad bin Yazid say: If something is defective in three ways, it must be built, and if it is defective in two ways, it must not be declined, because after leaving the declension there is nothing but construction. So Masaas and Darak are defective in three ways: one is that it is modified, one is that it is feminine, and one is definite. So when construction is required in it and the alif before the seen is silent, the seen is broken because of the meeting of two silent letters, as you say: hit the man. And I saw Abu Ishaq go to the view that this statement is wrong, and he obliged Abu al-Abbas if he calls a woman by the name of Pharaoh, he builds it, and no one says this. Al-Jawhari said in Al-Sahah: As for the Arabs saying La Masaas, like Qatam, it is built on the kasra because it is modified from the source, which is touch. Abu Haywah read La Masaas. “And indeed, you have an appointment that you will not fail to fulfill,” meaning on the Day of Resurrection. And the appointment is a source, meaning that you have a promise for your punishment. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read takhalafhu with a kasra on the lam, and it has two meanings: One of them is: you will come to him and will not find him left behind, just as you say: I praised him, meaning I found him praised. The second is as a threat, meaning you must go to him. The rest read it with a fatha on the lam, meaning: God will not leave him behind you. The Almighty said: And look at your God, to whom you have remained. That is, you have remained and abode. Adhering means adhering, and its root is I shaded. He said: Except that the freed ones are better for him, so they are more suitable for him Meaning: better. And Al-A'mash also read it with two lams according to the original. And in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, dhalt with a kasra on the dhaal. It is said: I continued to do such and such if I did it during the day, and dhalt and dhalt. So whoever says dhalt deletes the first lam for ease, and whoever says dhalt puts the vowel of the lam on the dhaal. And lanharqannahu is the reading of the common people with a damma on the noon and a stressed raa from haraqa yahriqu. Al-Hasan and others read with a damma on the noon and a sukoon on the haa and a light raa, from ahraqa yahriquhu. Ali, Ibn Abbas, Abu Ja'far, Ibn Muhaisin and Ashhab Al-'Uqaili read lanharqannahu with a fatha on the noon and a light damma on the raa, from haraqat al-shay' aharqahu haraqan bi radtuhu wa hakattu bi haraqatu wa hakattu bi haraqatu, and from it their saying: haraqa nabah yaharquhu wa yaharquhu i.e. he crushed it until a creaking sound was heard from it, so the meaning of this reading is lanbardanhu with files, and the filer is called al-muharrq. The first two readings mean burning with fire. It may be possible to combine this in it. Al-Suddi said: The calf was slaughtered and flowed from it as flows from a calf when slaughtered, then its bones were cooled with a file and burned. In the letter of Ibn Masoud, it is: We will slaughter it, then we will burn it. The flesh and blood, when burned, become ashes, so it is possible to scatter them in the sea, but gold does not become ashes. It was said: Moses knew what made the gold ashes, and that this was one of his signs. The meaning of We will blow it away is We will scatter it. Abu Raja read We will blow it away with a damma on the seen, two dialects. Nasaf is shaking something to blow it away, which is winnowing. Mansaf is what food is blown away with, and it is something erect and raised above the chest. Nasafah is what falls from it. It is said: Remove the nasaafah and all of the pure. It is said: So-and-so came to us as if his beard was scatter, narrated by Abu Nasr Ahmad bin Hatim. Mansafah is a tool used to remove a building. To blow up a building means to remove it. A camel blows up grass, meaning it uproots it from its roots. To uproot something means to pull it out, on the authority of Abu Zaid.
20:98: The Almighty said: “Your god is only God, other than whom there is no god. His knowledge encompasses all things.” Not the calf, meaning His knowledge encompasses all things. The verb is derived from knowledge, and the accusative is used for explanation. Mujahid and Qatada read His knowledge encompasses all things.
20:99: The Almighty said: Likewise the kaf is in the accusative case as an attribute of a deleted source. That is, just as We related to you the story of Moses, Likewise We relate to you stories likewise from the report of what came before, to be a consolation for you, and to indicate your truthfulness. And We have given you from Ourself a reminder meaning the Qur'an. And the Qur'an was called a reminder because of the reminder in it, just as the Messenger was called a reminder because the reminder was revealed to him. And it was said: We have given you from Ourself a reminder meaning honor, as the Almighty said: And indeed, it is a reminder for you (al-Zukhruf 43:44) meaning honor and mention of your name.
20:100: God Almighty says: Whoever turns away from it meaning the Qur’an, and does not believe in it, and does not act according to what is in it, he will bear a burden on the Day of Resurrection meaning a great sin and a heavy load.
20:101: They will abide therein eternally meaning they will reside therein, meaning in his recompense, and his recompense is Hell. And evil will be their burden on the Day of Resurrection meaning what an evil burden they will bear on the Day of Resurrection. Dawud ibn Rafi' read For he will bear.
20:102: The Almighty's saying: On the Day the Trumpet is blown The general reading is Yanfakh with a damma on the yaa' for the passive verb. Abu Amr and Ibn Abi Ishaq read with a noon as the name of the agent. Abu Amr provided evidence with the Almighty's saying: And We gather with a noon. And from Ibn Hormuz Yanfakh with a fatha on the yaa' meaning Israfil will blow. Abu Ayyad: In the Trumpet. The rest: In the Trumpet. This has been presented in full in (Al-An'am) and in the Book of Remembrance. Talhah bin Masraf read And will be gathered with a damma on the yaa' the criminals in the nominative case, unlike the Mushaf. The rest read And We gather the criminals meaning the polytheists. Zarqan is a state of the criminals, and zarq is the opposite of kohl. The Arabs consider zarqan eyes to be a bad omen and criticize it, meaning their creation is disfigured by the blueness of their eyes and the blackness of their faces. Al-Kalbi and Al-Farraa said: Zarqan means blind. Al-Azhari said: Thirsty, their eyes have turned blue from the intensity of thirst. Al-Zajjaj said the same, he said: Because the blackness of the eye changes and turns blue from thirst. It was said: It is false greed if it is followed by disappointment. It is said: My eyes turned white from my long wait for such-and-such. A fifth saying: What is meant by blueness is the staring of the eyes from the intensity of fear. The poet said: Your eyes are blue, son of a mule, like every gazelle's eyes are blue from meanness. It is said: A man with blue eyes, and a woman with blue eyes, clearly blue. The noun is zarqa. His eye is blue with a kasra, and his eye is blue, and his eye is blue with zarqaqan. Saeed bin Jubair said: Ibn Abbas was asked about his statement: And We will gather the criminals on that Day blue, and he said in another place: And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf (al-Isra’ 17:97), so he said: The Day of Resurrection has states, so there is a state in which they will be blue, and a state in which they will be blind.
20:103: They whisper among themselves The root of khuft in the language is stillness, then it was said that someone who lowers his voice has lowered it. They whisper, Mujahid said, meaning some of them say to each other in the gathering secretly If you remained meaning as long as you remained, meaning in this world, and it was said: in the graves except for ten meaning ten nights. And it was said: He meant what is between the two blasts, which is forty years, the punishment is lifted from the disbelievers during that period - according to Ibn Abbas - so they shorten that period. Or the period of their stay in this world due to the severity of what they see of the horrors of the Day of Resurrection.
20:104: And it will seem to the best of them, that is, the most just in speech, the most rational, and the most knowledgeable of them in his own eyes, that they only remained one day, meaning their stay in this world, according to Qatada, so the meaning is: except like a day. And it was said: that because of the horror of the rising, they forgot what they were in of worldly pleasures until they saw it as a day. And it was said: what he meant by a day is their stay between the two blasts, or their stay in the graves as mentioned above. And ten and a day are in the accusative case with you remained.
20:105: The Almighty said: And they ask you about the mountains meaning about the condition of the mountains on the Day of Resurrection. Say This came with a fa and every question in the Qur'an Say without a fa except this, because the meaning is if they ask you about the mountains then say, so the statement includes the meaning of a condition. And God knew that they would ask Him about them, so He answered them before the question, and those were questions that they asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about, so the answer came after the question, and that is why it was without a fa, and this is a question that they had not asked him about yet, so understand it. Blows it away means blows it away. Blowing away Ibn al-A'rabi and others said: He uproots it by uprooting it, then turns it into sand that flows like a torrent, then makes it like carded wool that the winds blow away like this and like this. He said: And wool is not made of wool except dyed, then like scattered dust.
20:106: He leaves it meaning he leaves its places a flat plain Al-Qa' is the smooth ground without plants or buildings, said Ibn Al-A'rabi. Al-Jawhari said: The plain is the flat part of the ground, and the plural is aqwa', aqwa', and qi'an, the waw became a ya' because of the kasra before it. Al-Farra' said: The plain is the swamp and the saffaf is the barren. Al-Kalbi said: It is that in which there is no vegetation. It was said: The flat part of the ground is as if it is in a single row in its flatness, said Mujahid. The meaning is the same in the plain and the plain, so the plain is the exposed place, and the saffaf is the smooth flat. Sibawayh recited: How many sand dunes and knots are there before your house? Qa'an is in the accusative case as a state and Safasaf.
20:107: And La Ta'ara is in the position of an adjective. In it is a crookedness. Ibn al-A'rabi said: Al-Awj is the crookedness in the valleys. And al-Amat is the Nabak. Abu Amr said: Al-Amat is the Nabak, and they are the small hills, the singular of which is Nabak, meaning it is a flat land with no depression or elevation. You say, it is full, so it is not a Matt, and I filled the water skin with a fullness without a Matt, meaning there is no relaxation in it. Al-Amat in the language is a high place. Ibn Abbas said: Awj is a slope. He said: And Al-Amat is the trace like the strap. And from him also Awj, a valley, and La Amta is a hill. And from him also: Al-Awj is the depression and Al-Amat is the elevation. Qatada said: Awj is a crack, and La Amta means a hill. Yaman said: Al-Amat is the cracks in the ground. And it was said: Al-Amat is when a place in the open space or mountain becomes thick and narrow in another place, narrated by al-Suli. I said: This verse falls under the category of incantations. Warts are treated with it, which we call barariq (singular: baruqa). They appear on the body, especially on the hand. Take three sticks of barley straw, with a knot at the end of each stick. Pass each knot over the warts and recite the verse once. Then bury the sticks in a damp place. They will rot and the warts will rot, leaving no trace of them. I tried this on myself and on others and found it beneficial, God willing.
20:108: The Almighty says: On that Day they will follow the Caller meaning Israfil, peace be upon him, when he blows the Trumpet. Without any crookedness meaning they will have no turning away from it, meaning from his call, they will not deviate or turn away, rather they will hasten to it and not deviate from it. Most scholars agree with this. It was also said: Without any crookedness meaning to his call. It was also said: They will follow the Caller with a following without any crookedness, so the source is implied, and the meaning is: They will follow the voice of the Caller to the place of assembly, similar to: And listen on the Day when the Caller will call from a place nearby (Qaf: 41) the verse. And it will come. And the voices will be hushed meaning they will be humbled and still, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the report of Az-Zubayr came, the walls of Madinah and the humble mountains were humbled, so every tongue there was silent out of awe. For the Most Gracious meaning for his sake. So you will not hear except a whisper A whisper is a low voice, said Mujahid. On the authority of Ibn Abbas: A lowly sensation. Al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj: It is the sound of feet falling on each other until the place of resurrection. From this comes the saying of the rajaz poet: They walk with us whispering It means the sound of camels' hooves as they walk. The lion is called al-Hamoos because it whispers in the darkness, meaning it treads quietly. Ru'bah said, describing himself as strong: A lion beats the lion, the elephant, and the buffalo. And the food was chewed, meaning it was chewed with its mouth closed. The rajaz poet said: I have seen wonders since yesterday, old women like five coughs They eat what I make, whisper by whisper. It was said: Whispering is moving the lip and tongue. Abi bin Kaab read: They do not speak except in a whisper. The meaning is close, that is, no speech, talk, or footsteps are heard from them. The structure of H M S is originally concealment, however it is conjugated, and from it are the whispered letters, which are ten and are collected in your saying: Hatha shakhs fasakt. The letter is called whispered because the dependence on its position is weak until the breath flows with it.
20:109: The Almighty says: On that Day, no intercession will benefit except for one to whom the Most Gracious has given permission. "Min" is in the accusative case as an exception coming from the first, meaning that intercession will not benefit anyone except the intercession of one to whom the Most Gracious has given permission. "And was pleased with his word" means that his word regarding intercession was pleased. It was said: The meaning is that intercession will only benefit for one to whom the Most Gracious has given permission to intercede, and he has a word that pleases. Ibn Abbas said: It is the saying, "There is no god but God."
20:110: The Almighty says: He knows what is before them meaning of the matter of the Hour. And what is behind them of the matter of this world, as stated by Qatada. It was also said: He knows what they will end up with of reward or punishment. And what is behind them what they left behind them in this world. Then it was said: The verse is general for all creation. It was also said: What is meant are those who follow the caller. Praise be to God. God the Almighty says: And they do not encompass it in knowledge. The ha in it refers to God the Almighty, meaning no one encompasses it in knowledge, as encompassing implies limitation, and God is exalted above limitation. It was said: It refers back to knowledge, meaning no one encompasses in knowledge what God knows. Al-Tabari said: The pronoun in their hands, “behind them,” and encompass refers back to the angels. God informs those who worship them that they do not know what is before them and what is behind them.
20:111: The Almighty said: And faces were humbled meaning they were humiliated and submissive, as Ibn al-A'rabi and others said. And from this the prisoner was called 'Aan. Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: A King on the throne of heaven, dominant, before whose glory faces bow and prostrate He also said: I turn my face and all my creation to Him, among those who prostrate to Him, thanking Him. Al-Jawhari said: “Anna means to submit and be humbled, and someone else helped him, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: “And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining.” It is also said: Anna fihim fulan as a prisoner, meaning he remained among them in his captivity and was detained. And someone else meant him to be imprisoned. Al-Ani is the captive. A people are Anat and women are Awan. Matters have been revealed to him. Ibn Abbas said: Anat means to be humbled. Mujahid said: to be humble. Al-Mawardi: The difference between humiliation and humility - although their meanings are close - is that humiliation is to be humbled, and humility is to humble oneself before someone who is obedient. Al-Kalbi said: Anat means to know. Atiyah Al-Awfi: to surrender. Talq bin Habib said: He placed his forehead and nose on the ground in prostration. An-Nahhas: And faces will be humbled has two meanings: One of them: that this is in the hereafter. And Ikrimah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. He said: bowing and prostrating. The meaning of will be humbled in the language is subjugation and victory, and from this the lands were conquered by force, meaning by victory. The poet said: They did not take it by force out of affection, but the supervisor’s beating made her resign. It was said: It is from the word ‘ana’ meaning fatigue, and people were referred to with faces, because the signs of humiliation are only evident in the face. To the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining. There are three interpretations of the Self-Sustaining. The first is that He is the One who manages creation. The second is that He is the One who is in charge of every soul for what it has earned. The third is that He is the Eternal One who does not disappear or perish. This has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. “And he who bears injustice has failed.” That is, he who bears polytheism has lost.
20:112: The Almighty said: And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer because deeds are not accepted without faith. And of in His statement: of righteous deeds is for partiality, meaning any of the righteous deeds. It was said: for the genus. So he shall not fear Ibn Kathir, Mujahid and Ibn Muhaisin read yakhf in the subjunctive mood as an answer to His statement: And whoever does. The rest read yakhf in the nominative case as a predicate, meaning he does not fear, or he does not fear. Injustice meaning a decrease in the reward for his obedience, nor an increase in his bad deeds. Nor diminishment by diminishing his right. Digestion is a decrease and a break. It is said: I digested that from my right, meaning I reduced it and left it. This digests food, meaning its weight decreases. A woman with a thin side and a thin stomach. Al-Mawardi: The difference between injustice and oppression is that injustice is the prevention of all rights, and oppression is the prevention of some rights, and oppression is injustice even if they differ in one respect. Al-Mutawakkil Al-Laythi said: The humiliated and the mean are the people of their oppressed and wronged master. Al-Jawhari said: A man who is oppressed and wronged means he is wronged. And he oppressed him if he wronged him and denied him his right.
20:113: The Almighty said: And thus meaning as We have explained to you in this Surah of explanation, thus We have made it an Arabic Qur’an meaning the language of the Arabs. And We have diversified therein of warning meaning We have provided what is in it of intimidation and threat, reward and punishment. That they may fear meaning that they may fear God and avoid His disobedience and beware of His punishment. Or that it may cause them to remember meaning an admonition. Qatada said: caution and piety. It was said: honor, so the remembrance here means honor, like His statement: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people (al-Zukhruf 43:44). It was said: meaning that they may remember the punishment with which they were threatened. Al-Hasan read or we shall cause it to be with a nun, and it was narrated from him that the tha was raised and jazm was made.
20:114: The Almighty said: So exalted is God, the True King. When the servants knew the greatness of His blessings and the revelation of the Qur'an, He declared Himself free from children and rivals, saying: So exalted is God, meaning, glorified is God, the True King, meaning, the Possessor of Truth. And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you. He taught His Prophet how to receive the Qur'an. Ibn Abbas said: He, peace be upon him, would hasten to Gabriel and recite before Gabriel finished the revelation, out of keenness to memorize it and out of compassion for the Qur'an for fear of forgetting it. So God forbade him from doing that and revealed: And do not hasten with the Qur'an. (Ta-Ha: 114). This is like His saying: Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. (al-Qiyamah 75:16), as will come. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid: He said: Do not recite it before you understand it. It was said: And do not hasten, meaning do not ask for its revelation before it is completed, i.e. before its revelation comes to you. It was said: The meaning is: Do not throw it to people before you receive a statement of its interpretation. Al-Hasan said: It was revealed about a man who slapped his wife in the face, so she came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking for retaliation. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, made retaliation hers, so Men are the protectors and maintainers of women (An-Nisa’: 34) was revealed. For this reason, he said: And say, ‘My Lord, increase me in knowledge’ meaning understanding, because he, peace be upon him, ruled with retaliation and God refused that. Ibn Mas’ud and others read before we judge with a nun and a kasra on the dhad and He revealed it with the accusative.
20:115: God the Almighty said: And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot. Al-A'mash read it differently from him, Fansa with a sukoon on the ya', and it has two meanings: One: He left, meaning he left the command and the covenant, and this is the opinion of Mujahid and most of the commentators, and from it is They forgot God, so He forgot them (al-Tawbah 9:67). And the second is that Ibn Abbas said: Nase here is from forgetfulness and forgetfulness, and the human being was only taken from it because He made a covenant with him and he forgot. Ibn Zayd said: He forgot what God made a covenant with him regarding that, and if he had been determined, he would not have obeyed his enemy Satan. According to this opinion, it is possible that Adam, peace be upon him, at that time was taken by forgetfulness, even though forgetfulness is removed from us today. The meaning of before is before he ate from the tree, because he was forbidden from it. What is meant is to console the Prophet, peace be upon him, meaning that the obedience of the sons of Adam to Satan is an old matter, meaning that if these people broke the covenant, then Adam also had a covenant with Us and he forgot, as narrated by Al-Qushayri and Al-Tabari. That is, if these disbelievers, O Muhammad, turn away from My signs, and disobey My messengers, and obey Satan, then their father Adam did that before. Ibn Atiyyah said: This interpretation is weak, because Adam is an example of the disbelievers who deny God, which is nothing, and Adam only disobeyed based on an interpretation, so in this there is a disgrace to him, may God bless him and grant him peace. Rather, what appears in the verse is either that it is the beginning of stories that have no connection to what came before it, or that its connection is that when Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded not to hasten with the Qur’an, he made an example of a prophet before him who was commanded but forgot and was punished, so that the warning would be more severe and the command to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be more effective. The command here is in the meaning of a testament, and forgot means left, and forgetting out of forgetfulness is not possible here, because punishment is not related to the forgetful. And the determination to continue with the belief in anything it was, and Adam, peace be upon him, believed that he would not eat from the tree, but when Satan whispered to him, he did not resolve to stick to his belief. The thing that was commanded to Adam was not to eat from the tree, and he knew that Satan was his enemy. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of his statement: And We found in him no determination. Ibn Abbas and Qatada said: We found in him no patience to avoid eating from the tree, nor any persistence in adhering to the command. An-Nahhas said: It is also the case in the language. It is said: Someone has determination, meaning he is patient and steadfast in avoiding sins until he is safe from them. From this: So be patient, as were patient the messengers of determination (al-Ahqaf 46:35). And from Ibn Abbas also and Atiyah Al-Awfi: Preservation, not a command, meaning he did not refrain from what I forbade until he forgot, and he left the knowledge of that by leaving out evidence, and that is because Satan said to him: If you eat it, you will remain in Paradise, meaning the exact same tree, but he did not obey him, so he called him to a tree similar to that which was included in the general prohibition, and it was necessary to provide evidence for it, but he did not do so, and he thought that it was not included in the prohibition, so he ate it based on an interpretation, and one who knows that it is a sin does not forget something. Ibn Zayd said: Determination is preserving the command of God. Ad-Dahhak said: Resolve of a matter. Ibn Kaysan said: Insistence and not intending to return to sin. Al-Qushayri said: “The first is closer to the interpretation of the statement, and for this reason some people said: Adam was not one of the resolute messengers, because God Almighty said: ‘And We found in him no resolve.’” Al-Mu’azzam said: All the messengers were resolute. In the report: There is no prophet who did not make a mistake or intend to make a mistake, except for John, son of Zechariah. If Adam had been excluded from the ranks of those with resolve because of his sin, all the prophets would have been excluded except John. Abu Umamah said: If the dreams of the children of Adam were collected from the time God created creation until the Day of Resurrection and were placed on one side of a scale, and Adam’s dream was placed on the other side, they would outweigh them. God Almighty said: And We found on his part no resolve.
20:116: God Almighty said: “And when We said to the angels, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ they prostrated, except for Iblis. He refused.” It was presented in full in (Al-Baqarah)
20:117: So We said, 'O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so do not let him expel you both from Paradise.' He forbade, and its meaning is: Do not accept from him, for that would be a reason for your expulsion from Paradise. "And you will be miserable," meaning you and your wife, because they are in the same condition. D, and he did not say: then you will be miserable, because the meaning is known, and Adam, peace be upon him, is the one being addressed, and he is the intended one. Also, since he was the one who worked for it and earned it, then misery was more specific. It was said: The expulsion will be upon them both, and the misery is upon Adam alone, and it is the misery of the body. Do you not see that he followed it with his saying: Indeed, for you is that you will neither hunger therein nor go naked, meaning in Paradise, and that you will neither thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun, so he informed him that in Paradise he will have all of this: clothing, food, drink, and housing, and that if you neglect the commandment and obey the enemy, he will expel you from Paradise, so you will be miserable with fatigue and exhaustion, meaning you will be hungry, naked, thirsty, and the sun will strike you, because you will be returned to the ground if you are expelled from Paradise. And he specifically mentioned misery and did not say then you will be miserable, in order to teach us that the wife’s expenses are upon the husband, and since that day, the expenses of women have been upon husbands. So since Eve’s expenses were upon Adam, so are her daughters’ expenses upon the sons of Adam by right of marriage. And He informed us in this verse that the expenses that are due to the woman from her husband are these four: food, drink, clothing, and housing. So if he gives her these four, then he has given her from her expenses. If he has more after that, then he is rewarded. As for these four, she is indispensable for them, because with them the soul is established. Al-Hasan said that what is meant by His statement, and she is miserable is the misery of this world. The son of Adam is not seen except as a toiler. Al-Farra’ said: It is that he eats from the labor of his own hands. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: A red bull was sent down to Adam, so he used to plow with it, and he would wipe the sweat from its forehead. This is his misery that God, the Most High, spoke of. It was said: When he was sent down from Paradise, the first of his misery was that Gabriel sent down to him grains from Paradise, and he said: O Adam, plant this. So he plowed and planted, then harvested, then threshed, then cleaned, then ground, then kneaded, then baked. Then he sat down to eat after the fatigue, and his loaf of bread rolled from his hand until it reached the bottom of the mountain, and Adam ran after him until he was tired and his forehead was sweating. He said: O Adam, thus He has provided for you with fatigue and misery, and He has provided for your children after you as long as you were in the world.
20:118: The Almighty’s saying: You shall neither hunger therein nor go naked, nor thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun’s rays. There are two issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: You will not be hungry therein meaning in Paradise nor naked.
20:119: And that you will not be thirsty therein meaning you will not be thirsty. Thirst is thirst. And you will not be exposed to the sun meaning you will not come out to the sun and feel its heat. There is no sun in Paradise, but rather an extended shadow, like the time between dawn and sunrise. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The day of Paradise is like this: and he pointed to the time of the prayer of the dawn prayer. Abu Zaid said: The road is exposed to the sun when it appears to you and becomes apparent. I was exposed to the sun and I was exposed to the sun with a kasra with a sweat. I was also exposed to the sun with an extended sunrise, I appeared and I was exposed with a fatha like it, and the future tense is the sun in both languages. Omar bin Abi Rabi'ah said: She saw a man, either when the sun is in the morning or when it is dark. It is narrated in the hadith that Ibn Omar saw a man in ihram who had taken shelter in the shade, so he said: Offer a sacrifice for the one for whom you have entered ihram. This is how the hadith scholars narrate it, with a fatha on the alif and a kasra on the ha’ from the word adha. Al-Asma’i said: It is: Offer the sacrifice for the one for whom you have entered ihram, with a kasra on the alif and a fatha on the ha’, from the word dhaya adha, because he ordered him to stand out in the sun. From this is the saying of God Almighty: And that you will neither thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun’s rays. And he recited: I sacrificed for him so that I could take shelter in his shade if the shade becomes a scorpion on the Day of Resurrection Abu Amr and the Kufians, except for Asim in the narration of Abu Bakr from him, read and you with the opening of the hamza in apposition to that you do not hunger. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case in apposition to the place, and the meaning is: and for you that you will not be thirsty therein. The rest read it with the kasra as a new sentence, or in apposition to that you are.
20:120: The Almighty’s saying: Then Satan whispered to him was mentioned previously in (Al-A’raf). He said meaning Satan O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that will not decay? This indicates that it was spoken to him directly, and that he entered Paradise in the belly of the snake, as was mentioned previously in (Al-Baqarah), and the tree was specified there, and what the scholars have to say about it, so there is no point in repeating it.
20:121: So they ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten together over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. It was mentioned in full in (Al-A'raf) and Al-Farra' said: And they began in Arabic means they approached. He said: It was said: They began to stick fig leaves to themselves. The Almighty’s saying: And Adam disobeyed his Lord and went astray. There are six issues in it: First: The Almighty’s saying: And disobeyed. The discussion of the sins of the prophets was presented in Al-Baqarah. Some of our later scholars said that what should be said is that God the Almighty has informed of the occurrence of sins by some of them, and attributed them to them, and rebuked them for them, and they informed about that about themselves, and disavowed it, and sought forgiveness for it and repented, and all of that was mentioned in many places that do not accept interpretation in their entirety, even if it accepts individual interpretations, and all of that does not detract from their positions, but rather those matters that occurred from them in a rare manner, and by mistake and forgetfulness, or an interpretation that called for that, are good deeds in relation to others, and in their right they are bad deeds in relation to their positions and high status, since the minister may be held accountable for what the governor is rewarded for, so they feared that in the situation of the Resurrection, despite their knowledge of security, safety and peace. He said: And this is the truth. Al-Junayd did well when he said: The good deeds of the righteous are the bad deeds of those who are close to God. Even though the texts testify to the occurrence of sins on their part, this does not detract from their positions, nor does it detract from their rank. Rather, He has taken care of them, chosen them, guided them, praised them, purified them, selected them, and chosen them, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them. Second: Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: It is not permissible for any of us today to tell that about Adam unless we mention it during the words of God Almighty about him, or the words of his Prophet. As for him starting that from himself, it is not permissible for us regarding our fathers who are closest to us, who are similar to us, so how about our oldest, greatest, most honorable father, the foremost Prophet, whom God Almighty excused, repented to, and forgave him. I said: If this is not permissible in the case of a created being, then reporting about the attributes of God Almighty, such as the hand, the foot, the finger, the side, the descent, and other things, is more deserving of prohibition, and it is not permissible to begin with anything of that except during the recitation of His Book or the Sunnah of His Messenger. For this reason, Imam Malik ibn Anas, may God be pleased with him, said: Whoever describes something of the essence of God Almighty, such as His statement: And the Jews say, ‘The hand of God is chained’ (al-Ma’idah 5:64), and points with his hand to his neck, his hand will be cut off. Likewise in the case of hearing and sight, that will be cut off from him, because he likened God Almighty to himself. Third: The imams narrated, and the wording is from Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Adam and Moses argued, and Moses said: O Adam, you are our father who has disappointed us and expelled us from Paradise. Adam said: O Moses, God Almighty has chosen you with His speech and He wrote to you with His hand, not Moses: Do you blame me for something that God decreed for me forty years before He created me? So Adam argued with Moses three times. Al-Muhallab said: His saying: So Adam argued with Moses means he defeated him with the argument. Al-Layth bin Saad said: The proof in this story of Adam against Moses, peace be upon them, was valid because God Almighty forgave Adam his sin and accepted his repentance. Moses could not have reproached him for a sin that God Almighty had forgiven him for. Therefore, Adam said: You are Moses to whom God gave the Torah, in which there is knowledge of everything. I found in it that God had decreed that I should commit a sin and had decreed that I should repent from it, and thereby removed blame from me. Do you blame me, while God does not blame me? Ibn Omar argued with something like this against the one who said to him: Uthman fled on the day of Uhud. Ibn Omar said: Uthman is not guilty, because God Almighty has forgiven him by saying: And God has forgiven them. It has been said: Adam, peace be upon him, was a father, and his reproach is not part of his piety, as if it were something that would be reproached to others, for God Almighty says about the disbelieving parents: And be kind to them in this world (Luqman 31:15). For this reason, when Abraham, peace be upon him, was told by his father while he was a disbeliever: If you do not desist, I will stone you, and leave me alone for a long time, he said, “Peace be upon you” (Maryam 19:46-47). So how about a father who is a prophet whom his Lord has chosen, accepted his repentance, and guided. Fourth: As for the one who committed sins and was not forgiven, the scholars are unanimously agreed that it is not permissible for him to use an argument like Adam’s, saying, You blame me for killing, committing adultery, or stealing, when God has decreed that for me. The nation is unanimously agreed that it is permissible to praise the doer of good for his good deeds, and to blame the doer of evil for his evil deeds, and to enumerate his sins against him. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: So he went astray meaning his life was ruined. Al-Naqqash narrated it and Al-Qushayri chose it. I heard our Sheikh, the reciter Abu Ja`far Al-Qurtubi, say: So he went astray meaning his life was ruined by his descent to the world. And going astray means corruption, and this is a good interpretation, and it is more appropriate than the interpretation of those who say: So he went astray means he went astray, from going astray which is the opposite of right guidance. It was said: Its meaning is he was ignorant of the place of his right guidance, meaning he was ignorant that that tree was the one he was forbidden from, and going astray is ignorance. And from some of them: So he went astray means he ate a lot. Al-Zamakhshari said: And this, although correct according to the language of those who change the broken ya before it to an alif, and say in fani and baqa: fani and baqa and they are the sons of Tayy, is a bad interpretation. Sixth: Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: Some people say: Adam disobeyed and went astray, but he is not called a sinner or a goon, just as someone who sews once is called a sewer, but he is not called a tailor unless he sews repeatedly. It was said: It is permissible for the master to say about his slave when he disobeys what it is not permissible for anyone else to say, and this is an exaggeration. What is attributed of this to the prophets is either minor sins, or he left what is better, or before prophethood. I said: This is good. Imam Abu Bakr bin Furak, may God Almighty have mercy on him, said: This was from Adam before the prophethood.
20:122: The evidence for this is the Almighty's statement: Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided him. He mentioned that the selection and guidance were after the disobedience, and if this was before the prophethood, then sins are permissible for them in one way, because before the prophethood there was no law for us to believe in them, so if God Almighty sent them to His creation and they were trustworthy in their performance and infallible, then what sins they had committed in the past would not harm them. This is valuable, and God knows best.
20:123: God the Almighty said: "He said, 'Descend from it, both of you.'" He addressed Adam and Iblis. "From it" means from Paradise. He said to Iblis: "Get out of it, disgraced and expelled." (al-A’raf 7:18) So perhaps he was expelled from Paradise to a place in the sky, then he was sent down to Earth. "Some of you are enemies to others." It was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah, meaning you are an enemy to the serpent and to Iblis, and they are enemies to you. This indicates that His saying, "Descend," was not addressed to Adam and Eve, because they were not enemies, and Adam's descent included Eve's descent. "Then if there comes to you guidance from Me," meaning right guidance and true words. It was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. "So whoever follows My guidance, meaning the messengers and books, will neither go astray nor suffer." Ibn Abbas said: God the Almighty has guaranteed that whoever recites the Qur'an and acts according to what is in it will not go astray in this world, nor suffer in the Hereafter, and he recited the verse. On his authority: Whoever recites the Qur’an and follows what is in it, God will guide him from misguidance and protect him on the Day of Resurrection from a bad reckoning. Then he recited the verse.
20:124: And whoever turns away from My remembrance meaning My religion, and the recitation of My Book, and acting in accordance with what is in it. It was said: from the evidences that I revealed. It is possible that the remembrance refers to the Messenger, because the remembrance was from him. Then he will have a straitened life meaning a narrow life. It is said: a straitened home and a straitened life, in which one and two, masculine and feminine, and plural are the same. Antara said: If they catch up, I will repeat, and if they are forced to fight, I will be more severe, and if they are wrapped in hardship, I will lower it. He also said: If fate could be represented, it would be represented by me when they descend into a difficult home. It was read as dhanka with the weight of fa’la: The meaning of that is that God the Almighty made with religion submission, contentment, and reliance on Him and His portion, so its owner spends from what God the Almighty has provided him with generosity and ease and lives a comfortable life, as God the Almighty said: We will surely cause him to live a good life (al-Naml 27:97). The one who turns away from religion is overcome by greed that keeps him aspiring to increase in this world, and he is controlled by grief that restrains his hand from spending, so his life is difficult and his condition is dark, as some of them said: No one turns away from the remembrance of his Lord except that his time is darkened for him, his provision is disturbed, and he is in a difficult life. Ikrimah said: Dhanka means unlawful earnings. Al-Hasan: the food of thorny plants and zaqqum. And a fourth statement, which is correct. It is the torment of the grave. This was said by Abu Saeed Al-Khudri and Abdullah bin Masoud, and Abu Hurairah narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet: On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we have mentioned it in the Book of Remembrance, Abu Hurairah said: The grave of the disbeliever will be so narrow that his ribs will overlap, and this is a difficult life. And We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. It was said: Blind in one state and seeing in another state, and it was mentioned at the end of Glory be to God. It was said: Blind to the argument, said Mujahid. It was said: Blind to the directions of goodness, not guided to any of them. It was said: Blind to the means to ward off punishment from himself, like the blind man who has no means to do what he does not see.
20:125: He said, 'My Lord, why have you raised me blind?' meaning, for what sin have you punished me with blindness. And I was seeing meaning, in this world, and it is as if he thought that he had no sin. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: meaning, Why have you raised me blind to my argument and I was seeing meaning, knowing my argument. Al-Qushayri: This is far-fetched, since the disbeliever has no argument in this world.
20:126: He said, 'Thus did Our signs come to you.' That is, God Almighty said to him, Thus did Our signs come to you. That is, Our proof of Our Oneness and Power. But you forgot them. That is, you left them and did not consider them, and you turned away from them. And thus today you will be forgotten. That is, you will be left in torment, meaning Hell.
20:127: And thus do We recompense him who transgresses meaning, just as We recompense he who turns away from the Qur'an, and from looking at and contemplating created things, and transgresses the limit in disobedience. And does not believe in the signs of his Lord meaning, does not believe in them. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe meaning, more terrible than a difficult life and the punishment of the grave. And more lasting meaning, more permanent and steadfast, because it does not end or cease.
20:128: The Almighty says: Have they not been guided? He means the people of Mecca, meaning, has the report of those generations before them whom We destroyed not become clear to them, walking in their homes when they traveled and went out for trade in search of a living, and they see the lands of the past nations, and the past generations are empty, meaning, do they not fear that what happened to the infidels before them will happen to them? Ibn Abbas, Al-Salami and others read nahda lahum with a noon, which is clearer. Yahda with a yaa is problematic because of the subject, so the Kufians said: kam is the subject, An-Nahhas, and this is a mistake, because kam is an interrogative, so what precedes it does not work on it. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, has the matter not been guided to them by Our destruction of those whom We destroyed? The reality of yahda indicates guidance, so the subject is guidance, meaning: Has the guidance not been guided to them? Al-Zajjaj said: kam is in the accusative case with ahlakkana.
20:129: The Almighty said: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable. There is an advancing and delaying in this, meaning, and had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord and a specified term, it would have been inevitable, as Qatada said. Adherence means concomitance, meaning the punishment would have been inevitable for them. And he implied the noun of was. Al-Zajjaj said: And a specified term is in apposition to word. Qatada said: What is meant is the Resurrection, as Al-Qutabi said. It was also said: Their delay is until the Day of Badr.
20:130: The Almighty's saying: So be patient over what they say. The Almighty commanded him to be patient over what they say: He is a magician, he is a soothsayer, he is a liar, and so on. The meaning is: Do not pay attention to them, for their punishment has a set time that is neither advanced nor delayed. Then it was said: This was abrogated by the verse on fighting. And it was said: It was not abrogated, since the disbelievers were not eradicated after the verse on fighting, but rather most of them remained. The Almighty said: And glorify the praises of your Lord before the rising of the sun. Most of the commentators said: This is a reference to the five daily prayers: before the rising of the sun the dawn prayer, and before its setting the afternoon prayer, and from the times of the night the darkness and the ends of the day “the sunset and the noon prayer, because the noon prayer is at the end of the first day and the beginning of the other day, so they are at two ends of it, and the third end is the sunset, which is the time of sunset. It was said: The day is divided into two parts separated by the meridian, and each part has two ends, so at the meridian there are two ends, the other of the first part and the first of the other part, so he said about the two ends “ends” in the manner of your hearts have become inclined (al-Tahrim 66:4). Ibn Furak referred to this view in Al-Mushkil. It was said: The day is for the genus, so each day has an end, and it is for the plural because it returns to every day. And the times of the night are its hours, and the singular of the times is I and I is when. A group said: What is meant by the verse is voluntary prayer, as Al-Hasan said. The Almighty says: Perhaps you will be satisfied with the opening of the ta’, meaning perhaps you will be rewarded for these deeds with what pleases you. Al-Kisa’i and Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim tarḍā with the damma of the ta’, meaning perhaps you will be given what pleases you.
20:131: The Almighty said: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment. Its meaning was previously mentioned in (Al-Hijr). Azwaajan is the object of m3ta'ana. "Flower" is in the accusative case as a state. Al-Zajjaj said: "Flower is in the accusative case with the meaning of m3ta'ana because its meaning is that we made for them the life of this world a flower, or with an implied verb which is ja'ala" meaning we made for them the flower of this worldly life, also from Al-Zajjaj. It was said: It is a substitute for the ha' in "bih" in the place, as you say: I passed by your brother. Al-Farra' indicated that it is in the accusative case as a state, and the factor in it is "m3ta'ana", he said: As you say I passed by the poor man, and he estimated it: We gave them enjoyment with it, the flower of life in this world and an adornment in it. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a source like "san'a God" (al-Naml 27:88) and "wa'ad God" (al-Rum 30:6), and there is a view on this. It is better to put it in the accusative case and delete the tanween because of its sukoon and the sukoon of the lam of life, as it was read nor the night outstrips the day (Ya Sin: 40) with the accusative of the day with preceding on the assumption of deleting the tanween because of its sukoon and the sukoon of the lam, and life would be in the genitive case as a substitute for what in his saying: to that which we have enjoyed, so the estimation would be: and do not stretch your eyes toward the life of this world as a flower, meaning in a state of its flower. And it is not good for flower to be a substitute for what in the position in his saying: to that which we have enjoyed, because to tempt them is related to we have enjoyed, and the flower of the life of this world means its adornment with plants. And flower, with the fatha on the zay and the ha’, is the light of the plant. And flower, with the damma on the zay and the fatha on the ha’, is the star. And Banu Zahra with the sukoon on the ha’, said Ibn Aziz. And Isa ibn Umar read flower with the fatha on the ha’ like river and river. And it is said: a shining lamp, meaning it has a shine. And the flowers of trees are what delights from their colors. In the hadith: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had a bright color, meaning bright in color. Everything that is bright is called bright, and it is the best of colors. To test them in it meaning to try them. It was also said: To make that a trial and misguidance for them. The meaning of the verse: Do not give weight, O Muhammad, to the adornments of this world, for they will not last. And do not extend is more eloquent than do not look, because the one who extends his sight is only driven to do so by a combined desire, and the one who looks may not have that. Question: Some people said: The reason for the revelation of this verse is what Abu Rafi’, the freed slave of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated. He said: “A guest visited the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he sent me, peace be upon him, to a Jewish man and said: Tell him that Muhammad says to you: A guest has visited us and we do not have anything to serve him, so sell me such and such a quantity of flour, or give me a loan until the crescent of Rajab. He said: No, unless you provide a pledge. He said: So I returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He said: By God, I am trustworthy in heaven and trustworthy on earth. If he gave me a loan or sold me something, I would pay him back. Go to him with my armor.” And the verse was revealed to console him for the world. Ibn Atiyah said: This is objectionable as a reason, because the surah is Meccan and the story mentioned is Medinan, at the end of the life of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he died and his armor was mortgaged to a Jew because of this story that was mentioned. Rather, it appears that the verse is consistent with what came before it, and that is that God Almighty rebuked them for not taking into consideration the previous nations, then threatened them with deferred punishment, then commanded His Prophet to despise their affair, to be patient with their words, and to turn away from their wealth and what they have in their hands of this world, because that is gone from them and will lead to disgrace. I said: And likewise what was narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he passed by the camels of Banu al-Mustaliq and they were frowning in their urine and dung from fat, so he covered himself with his garment and then moved on, because of the saying of the Almighty: And do not strain your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them 1:10. Then he said: And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting 1:10, meaning the reward of God for patience and lack of concern for the world is more appropriate, because it remains and the world will perish. And it was said: He means by this provision what God opens for the believers of lands and spoils.
20:132: The Almighty said: And enjoin prayer upon your family. The Almighty commanded him to enjoin prayer upon his family and to perform it with them, and to be patient and consistent in it. This is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and its generality includes all of his nation, and his family in particular. After this verse was revealed, he, peace be upon him, would go every morning to the house of Fatima and Ali, may God be pleased with them, and say: Prayer. It is narrated that whenever Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with him, saw any report or conditions of the sultans, he would rush to his house and enter it, reciting And do not extend your eyes - the verse - until His saying: And remain. Then he would call for prayer: Prayer, may God have mercy on you, and he would pray. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, would wake up the people of his house for the night prayer and pray while reciting the verse. God the Almighty said: We do not ask you for provision meaning we do not ask you to provide for yourself and them, and to be distracted from prayer because of provision, rather we are responsible for providing for you and them. So when a distress befell his family, he would order them to pray. God the Almighty said: “And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me. Indeed, it is God who is the Provider” (al-Dhariyat 51:56-58). The Almighty says: And the best outcome is for the righteous. That is, Paradise is for the righteous, meaning the praiseworthy outcome. And there may be an outcome for those who are not righteous, but it is blameworthy, so it is as if it does not exist.
20:133: The Almighty says: And they said, 'Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?' He means the infidels of Mecca, meaning why does Muhammad not bring us a sign that requires necessary knowledge? Or an apparent sign like the she-camel and the staff. Or why does he not bring us the signs that we suggest as he brought to the prophets before him. God the Almighty said: Did there not come to them a clear proof of what was in the former scriptures? He means the Torah, the Gospel, and the previous scriptures. This is the greatest sign, as He informed us of what is in them. The scriptures was read with a light pronunciation. It was said: Did not come to them a sign indicating his prophethood with what they found in the previous scriptures of good tidings? It was also said: Did not come to them the destruction of the nations who disbelieved and suggested signs? What would assure them that if the signs came to them, their condition would not be the same as those people? Abu Ja`far, Shaibah, Nafi`, Abu `Amr, Ya`qub, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Hafs read Awlma ya’tuhum with a ta’ to feminize bayyinah. The rest read it with a ya’ to precede the verb, and because bayyinah is the explanation and proof, so they returned it to the meaning, and Abu `Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose it. Al-Kisa’i narrated: Did not come to them a clear proof of what was in the former scriptures? He said: And according to this, a clear proof of what was in the former scriptures is permissible. Al-Nahhas said: If you add a nunation to bayyinah and raise it, you make ma a substitute for it, and if you make it accusative, then it is in the state, and the meaning is: Did not what was in the first scriptures come to them clearly?
20:134: The Almighty said: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it meaning before the mission of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the revelation of the Qur’an, they would have said meaning on the Day of Resurrection, Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger? meaning why did You not send us a messenger so we could have followed Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced? “humiliated and disgraced” was read without naming its doer. Abu Sa’id al-Khudri narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the one who perished during the interval, the insane, and the newborn, he said: The one who perishes during the period says, No book or messenger came to me. Then he recited, And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, “Our Lord, why did You not send us a messenger?” - the verse - and the insane person says, My Lord, You have not given me a mind by which I could understand good or evil. And the newborn says, My Lord, I did not attain the ability to do good. So a fire is raised for them and He says to them, Return it and enter it. He said, “So he returns it or enters it who, in the knowledge of God, was happy if he had attained the ability to do good, and he who, in the knowledge of God, was miserable if he had attained the ability to do good, is held back from it. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, says, “You disobeyed Me, so how would My messengers have come to you?” And it is narrated as a narration attributed to Abu Saeed, and there is a view in it. We have explained it in the Book of Remembrance, and it is used as evidence by those who say that children and others are tested in the Hereafter. So we follow is an accusative in response to the specification. Your signs means what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. Before we are humiliated meaning in the punishment. And disgraced in Hell, said Ibn Abbas. And it was said, Before we are humiliated in this world by the punishment. And we will be disgraced in the Hereafter with its punishment.
20:135: Say, everyone who is waiting meaning, say to them, O Muhammad, everyone who is waiting, meaning all the believers and the unbelievers, is waiting for the circles of time and for whom victory will be. Then wait, and you will know who are the companions of the straight path and who is guided meaning the straight religion and guidance, and the meaning is: then you will know by victory who is guided to the religion of truth. It was said: then you will know on the Day of Resurrection who is guided to the path of Paradise. In this there is a type of threat, intimidation and warning with which the surah ends. It was read, then you will know. Abu Rafi' said: I memorized it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned it. Min is in the nominative case according to Al-Zajjaj. Al-Farra' said: It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case like And God knows the corrupter from the reformer (al-Baqarah 2:220). Abu Ishaq said: This is wrong, because the interrogative does not affect what precedes it, and min here is an interrogative in the nominative case, and the meaning is: Are we the people of the straight path, or are you?
