An-Nahhas said: Al-Farra’ believes that the meaning of min ashab as-sirat as-sirat as-sirat is those who have not gone astray, and that the meaning of man ahtada is those who went astray and then were guided. Yahya bin Ya’mar and Asim Al-Jahdari read fasya’lamun min ashab as-sirat as-sirat with a shaddah on the waw followed by the feminine alif on the form fa’la without a hamza, and the feminization of as-sirat is rare and irregular, as God the Most High said: Guide us to the straight path (al-Fatihah 1:6), so it came in the masculine form in this and other forms, and Abu Hatim rejected this and said: If it is from as-saw, it must be said as-suwa, and if it is from as-saw, it must be said as-siya with a kasrah on the seen, and the original form is as-sawya. Al-Zamakhshari said: As-saw was read to mean the middle and just, or the level. An-Nahhas: The permissibility of the reading of Yahya bin Ya’mar and Al-Jahdari is that the original is bad and the quiescent letter is not a strong barrier, so it is as if he changed the hamza to a damma and replaced it with a waw as it is replaced with an alif if what precedes it is open. It is complete and praise be to God alone.
21:1: Meccan according to everyone, and it is one hundred and twelve verses. God the Almighty said: The reckoning of mankind has drawn near. Abdullah bin Masoud said: The Cave, Maryam, Taha, and the Prophets are among the first freed slaves, and they are from my generation. He means those who have put forward what they have earned and memorized from the Qur’an, like money that has been given back. It was narrated that a man from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was building a wall, and another passed by him on the day this Surah was revealed. The one who was building the wall said: What was revealed from the Qur’an today? The other said: The reckoning of mankind has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness turning away was revealed. So he shook his hand from the building and said: By God, I will never build again, for the reckoning has drawn near.” Draw near means the time has drawn near when they will be held accountable for their deeds. For the people Ibn Abbas said: What is meant by the people here are the polytheists, as evidenced by God the Almighty’s statement: Except that they listen to it while they are playing until His statement: Then do you then practice magic while you see? It was said: People in general, even if those referred to at that time were the infidels of Quraysh, as is indicated by the verses that follow. Whoever knows that the Hour is approaching will have shortened his hope, and his soul will be content with repentance, and he will not rely on the world, so it is as if what was never was when it is gone, and everything that is coming is near, and death is inevitably coming, and the death of every person is the occurrence of his hour, and the Resurrection is also near in comparison to what has passed of time, so what remains of the world is less than what has passed. Ad-Dahhak said: The meaning of their reckoning has drawn near for the people is their punishment, meaning the people of Mecca, because they were impatient for the punishment they were promised in denial, and their killing was on the Day of Badr. An-Nahhas: It is not permissible in speech to say their reckoning has drawn near for the people, lest an implied word precede an explicit word that cannot be intended to delay. And they are in heedlessness, turning away is the beginning of the report. The accusative is permissible in places other than the Qur’an as a state. There are two views on this: One of them: And they are in heedlessness, turning away from the world and the Hereafter. The second: from preparing for the reckoning and from what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought. According to Sibawayh, this waw means when, and it is what grammarians call the waw of state, as God Almighty said: It will overwhelm a party of you and a party whose souls are concerned (Al Imran 3:154).
21:2: The Almighty said: Whatever reminder comes to them from their Lord is newly revealed. "Newly revealed is an adjective for reminder. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' permitted newly revealed to mean whatever comes to them is newly revealed," in the accusative case as a state. Al-Farra' also permitted "newly revealed to be raised as an adjective for the reminder, because if you delete from, you would raise reminder," meaning whatever reminder comes to them from their Lord is newly revealed. He means in the descent and recitation of Gabriel to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he would send down surah after surah, and verse after verse, just as God Almighty would send it down to him at one time after another, not that the Qur'an is created. It was said: The reminder is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, reminds them of and admonishes them with. He said: "From their Lord" because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, does not speak except by revelation, so the Prophet's admonition and warning is a reminder, and it is newly revealed. God Almighty said: "So remind, for you are only a reminder." (al-Ghashiyah 88:21). It is said: So-and-so is in the gathering of remembrance. It was said: The male is the Messenger himself, said Al-Husayn bin Al-Fadl based on the evidence in the context of the verse: Is this anything but a human being like you? (al-Anbiya 21:3). If he meant by male the Qur’an, he would have said: Is this anything but legends of the ancients? The evidence for this interpretation is the Almighty’s statement: And they say, ‘Indeed, he is mad.’ But it is not but a reminder to the worlds. (al-Qalam 68:51-52) meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And He said: God has sent down to you a reminder, a Messenger. (al-Talaq 65:10-11). Except that they listen to it, meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, or the Qur’an from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or from his nation. And they play. The waw is the waw of state, indicating it. Their hearts are distracted. The meaning of play is that they are distracted. It was said: they are busy. If its interpretation is carried to amusement, then what they are distracted with can have two meanings: One: with their pleasures. The second: by listening to what is recited to them. If its interpretation is taken to mean preoccupation, then what they are preoccupied with can have two meanings: One: with the world because it is a game, as God Almighty said: The life of this world is only play and amusement (Muhammad 47:36). The second: they are preoccupied with criticizing it and objecting to it. Al-Hasan said: Whenever the reminder is renewed to them, they continue in ignorance. It was said: they listen to the Qur’an mockingly.
21:3: The Almighty said: Their hearts are distracted meaning their hearts are heedless, turning away from the remembrance of God, preoccupied with contemplation and understanding, from the saying of the Arabs: I was distracted from the remembrance of something if you left it and forgot about it, he was distracted, he was distracted and distracted. Heedless is an adjective that precedes the noun, and it is the right of the adjective to follow the described in all parsing, so if the adjective precedes the noun, it is in the accusative case like His saying: Their eyes are downcast (al-Qalam 68:43) and And their shades are drawn low over them (al-Insan 76:14) and Heedless hearts the poet said: For the glory of a lonely ruin that appears like a defect He meant: a desolate ruin. Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' permitted Lahiyyat Qulubhum in the nominative case, meaning their hearts are heedless. Others permitted the nominative case as a predicate after a predicate and with an implied subject. Al-Kisa'i said: It is possible that the meaning is, except that they listened to it, their hearts are heedless. And those who wronged whispered secretly meaning they whispered among themselves about lying, then he explained who they were and said: Those who wronged meaning those who associated partners with God, so those who wronged is a substitute for the and in asraw and it refers to the people mentioned earlier, and this statement does not stop at the secret conversation. Al-Mubarrad said: It is like your saying: Those in the house set out, Banu Abdullah, so Banu is a substitute for the and in set out. It was said: It is a nominative case of blame, meaning they are the ones who wronged. It was said: On the deletion of the saying, the estimation: those who did wrong say and the saying was deleted, like “And the angels will enter upon them from every gate * Peace be upon you” (al-Ra’d 13:23-24). Al-Nahhas chose this saying, he said: The evidence for the correctness of this answer is that after it Is this anything but a human being like you? And a fourth saying: It is accusative in the sense that I mean those who did wrong. Al-Farra’ permitted it to be in the genitive sense that the reckoning of the people who did wrong has approached, and it is not stopped on this face on the whispering and stopped on the three previous faces before it, so these are five sayings. Al-Akhfash permitted the nominative in the language of those who said: The fleas ate me, and it is good, God Almighty said: Then many of them became blind and deaf (al-Ma’idah 5:71). And the poet said: With you, the struggle was won without the efforts, so the arrows were guided to the goals Another said: But his father and mother are in Hauran, squeezing his relatives Al-Kisa’i said: It contains an inversion, and its meaning is: And those who did wrong kept their secrets secret. Abu Ubaidah said: Khaṣraw here is one of the opposites, so it is possible that they concealed their speech, and it is possible that they revealed it and announced it. God the Almighty said: Is this anything but a human being like you? That is, they whispered among themselves and said: Is this the male who is the Messenger, or is this who calls you anything but a human being like you, who is not distinguished from you in anything, who eats food and walks in the markets as you do? And they did not know that God the Almighty made it clear that it is not permissible for Him to send to them anyone but a human being so that they may understand and teach them. Do you then come to magic? That is, what Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, brought was magic, so how do you come to him and follow him? So God informed His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, of what they whispered about. Magic in the language is everything that is deceptive and has no truth or validity. And you see that he is a human being like you, like: And you understand because the mind sees things. It was said: The meaning is: Do you accept magic while you know that it is magic? It was also said: The meaning is: Do you turn to falsehood while you know the truth? The meaning of the statement is rebuke.
21:4: The Almighty said: He said, 'My Lord knows what is said in the heaven and the earth' meaning nothing is hidden from Him of what is said in the heaven and the earth. And in the copies of the Qur'an of the people of Kufa, it says, My Lord meaning Muhammad said, My Lord knows what is said meaning He knows what you whispered to each other. And it was said: The first reading is more appropriate, because they kept this saying secret, so God Almighty revealed it to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and commanded him to say this to them. An-Nahhas said: Both readings are correct and they are like two verses, and in them is the benefit that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded and that he said as he was commanded.
21:5: And the Almighty’s saying: Rather, they said, ‘Confused dreams.’ Al-Zajjaj said: That is, they said that what he brings is confused dreams. And another said: That is, they said it is a mixture like mixed dreams, that is, horrors he saw in a dream. Mujahid and Qatada said its meaning, and from it is the saying of the poet: Like a dream that was deceived by its dreamer Al-Qatabi said: It is a false vision, and the poet said about it: Hadiths of Ta-Sin-Mim or Saraab, a mirage that shimmers for the traveler and the dreams of the dreamer Al-Yazidi said: Al-Adjadha is that which has no interpretation. This has already been mentioned in Yusuf. When they saw that the matter was not as they said, they changed from that and said: Rather, he invented it. Then they changed from that and said: Rather, he is a poet. That is, they were confused and could not settle on anything. They said once that it was magic, another time that it was a confused dream, another time that he invented it, and another time that he was a poet. It was said: That is, one group said that he was a magician, another group that it was a confused dream, another group that he invented it, and another group that he was a poet. Invention is fabrication, and this has already been mentioned. Then let him bring us a sign as the former ones were sent. That is, as Moses was sent with the staff and other signs, and like the she-camel of Salih. They knew that the Qur’an was neither magic nor a vision, but they said: He should bring us a sign that we can suggest, and they did not have the right to suggest after they saw a single sign. Also, if they do not believe in a verse that is of the same type as what they are the most knowledgeable about, and there is no room for doubt about it, then how can they believe in a verse other than it? Even if He cured the blind and the leper, they would say: This is from the category of medicine, and that is not from our profession. Rather, their question was out of stubbornness, since God had given them sufficient verses. God Almighty made it clear that if they had believed, He would have given them what they asked for, as God Almighty said: “And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. And if He had made them hear, they would have turned away while they were averse.” (al-Anfal 8:23)
21:6: The Almighty said: No city believed before them. Ibn Abbas said: He means the people of Salih and the people of Pharaoh. We destroyed it means it was in Our knowledge that it would be destroyed. Do they believe? He means they believe, meaning they did not believe in the signs and were uprooted. If these people had seen what they suggested, they would not have believed, because of the previous decree that they would not believe either. Rather, their punishment was delayed because We knew that in their loins there were those who would believe. From is redundant in His statement: From a city like His statement: There is not one of you who can prevent Him from it (al-Haqqah 69:47).
21:7: The Almighty said: And We did not send before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed. This is a response to their saying: Is this anyone but a human being like you? and to give comfort to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that He did not send before you except men. So ask the people of the message if you do not know. He means the people of the Torah and the Gospel who believed in the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as Sufyan said. He called them the people of the message because they mentioned the report of the prophets that the Arabs did not know. The infidels of Quraysh used to consult the people of the book about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Zayd said: By the message he meant the Qur'an, meaning ask the believing scholars from the people of the Qur'an. Jabir al-Ju'fi said: When this verse was revealed, Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: We are the people of the message. It has been proven by continuous narration that the messengers were from among humans, so the meaning is do not start with denial and by saying that the messenger should be from among the angels, but rather debate with the believers so that they may explain to you the permissibility of the messenger being from among humans. The king is not called a man, because man is used for what has the opposite of its word. You say: man and woman, man and boy. So his saying: except men from the children of Adam. Hafs, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read: We revealed to them. Question: The scholars did not differ that the common people must imitate their scholars, and that they are the ones meant by the words of God Almighty: So ask the people of the message if you do not know (al-Nahl 16:43). They agreed that the blind person must imitate someone else whom he trusts to distinguish the direction of the qiblah if he is confused about it. Likewise, the one who has no knowledge or sight of the meaning of what he believes in must imitate his scholar. Likewise, the scholars did not differ that the common people are not permitted to issue fatwas, due to their ignorance of the meanings from which it is permissible to make what is permissible and what is forbidden.
21:8: The Almighty says: And We did not make them bodies that do not eat food. The pronoun in We made them refers to the prophets, meaning We did not make the messengers before you outside the nature of humans who do not need food and drink. And they were not immortal means they do not die. This is an answer to their saying: This is only a human being like you (Al-Mu'minun: 33) and their saying: What is this Messenger that eats food? (al-Furqan 25:7). Body is a generic noun, and that is why He did not say bodies. It was said: He did not say bodies, because He meant and We did not make each one of them a body. The body is the body, you say from it: it was embodied, just as you say from the body it was embodied. The body is also saffron or similar dye, and it is also blood. Al-Nabigha said: And no body was spilled on the idols Al-Kalbi said: The body is the embodied entity in which the soul eats and drinks. According to this statement, what does not eat or drink is a body. Mujahid said: The body is what does not eat or drink. According to this statement, what eats and drinks is a soul. Al-Mawardi mentioned this.
21:9: God Almighty says: Then We fulfilled the promise to them meaning the prophets, that is, by saving them, granting them victory, and destroying those who denied them. And whomever We willed meaning those who believed the prophets. And We destroyed the transgressors meaning the polytheists.
21:10: The Almighty said: Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book meaning the Qur'an. In it is your remembrance is raised by the beginning and the sentence is in the accusative position because it is an attribute of the Book, and what is meant by remembrance here is honor, meaning in it is your honor, like: And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people (al-Zukhruf 43:44). Then He alerted them with the question that means stopping, so the Almighty said: Do you not understand? It was said: In it is your remembrance, meaning the remembrance of your religion, the rulings of your law, and what you will end up with of reward and punishment. In it is your remembrance, meaning the remembrance of your religion, the rulings of your law, and what you will end up with of reward and punishment. Do you not understand these things that we mentioned?! Mujahid said: In it is your remembrance meaning your speech. It was said: Your noble morals, and your good deeds. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Working with what is your life. I said: These conditions have one meaning, and the first includes them all, since they are all an honor, and the book is an honor for our Prophet, peace be upon him, because it is his miracle, and it is an honor for us if we act according to what is in it, its evidence is his saying, peace be upon him: The Qur'an is an argument for you or against you.
21:11: The Almighty says: And how many a city have We destroyed which was unjust. He means cities that were in Yemen. The people of interpretation and report said: He meant the people of Hadur and a prophet named Shuaib bin Dhi Mahdam was sent to them, and the grave of this Shuaib is in Yemen on a mountain called: Dhannan, which has much snow, and he is not Shuaib, the owner of Midian, because the story of Hadur was before the time of Jesus, peace be upon him, and after hundreds of years from the time of Solomon, peace be upon him, and that they killed their prophet and the people of the message killed at that time a prophet of theirs named Hanzala bin Safwan, and Hadur was in the land of Hijaz in the direction of Ash-Sham, so God inspired Jeremiah to go to Bukhtanasr and inform him that I have given him power over the land of the Arabs, and that I will take revenge on them through you, and God inspired Jeremiah to carry Maad bin Adnan on the Buraq to the land of Iraq, so that the vengeance and calamity will not befall him with them, for I will extract from his loins a prophet at the end of time named Muhammad, so he carried Maad when he was twelve years old, and he was with the children of Israel until he grew up and married a woman named Ma’ana, then Bukhtanasr rose up with the armies and ambushed the Arabs in a place - and he was the first to take ambushes according to what they mentioned Then he launched raids on Hadhur, killing, capturing, and destroying the populated area, and did not leave a trace of Hadhur, then he turned back to Sawad. And kam is in the accusative case with qasamna. And qasm is breaking, it is said: I broke the back of so-and-so and his tooth was broken, if it was broken, and the meaning here is destruction. As for fasm with fa, it is a crack in something without separation, the poet said: As if he were a silver bullet, he woke up in the playground of the neighborhood's virgins, separated And from it the hadith: And it was separated from him, and his forehead was dripping with sweat. And his saying: She was unjust means unbelieving, meaning her people. Injustice is putting something in the wrong place, and they put unbelief in place of faith. And We created meaning We brought into existence and brought into existence after their destruction another people.
21:12: When they felt meaning they saw Our punishment. It is said: I felt weakness from it. Al-Akhfash said: They felt they feared and expected. When they are running from it meaning they are fleeing and running away. Running is running with force. Running is moving the leg, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: Strike with your foot (Sad: 42). I made the horse run with my foot, I urged it to run, then it became more common until it was said that the horse ran when it ran, but this is not the original. The correct thing is that the horse ran on something whose doer is not named, so it is run.
21:13: Do not run means do not flee. It was said that the angels called out to them when they were defeated, mocking them and saying: Do not run. "And return to what you have indulged in" meaning to your blessings that were the cause of your arrogance. The one who is indulgent is the one who is comfortable. It is said: He indulged someone in luxury, meaning he made his livelihood easy for him. God, the Almighty, indulged them in luxury, as He said: "And We indulged them in luxury in the life of this world" (Al-Mu'minun: 33). "Perhaps you will ask" means perhaps you will ask for something from your worldly life, mocking them, as Qatada said. It was said: The meaning of "Perhaps you will ask" is about the punishment that has befallen you, so that you may be informed about it. It was said: The meaning of "Perhaps you will ask" is that you believe as you used to ask before the calamity befell you. They were told that in mockery, rebuke and rebuke.
21:14: They said, 'Woe to us!' When the angels said to them, Do not run! and called out, Oh, revenge for the prophets! And they did not see anyone speaking to them, they knew that it was God Almighty who had sent their enemy over them by killing the prophet who was sent to them. Then they said, Woe to us! We were indeed wrongdoers! So they admitted that they had been wrongdoers when admission was of no use.
21:15: And that was their call meaning they did not stop saying: Woe to us, indeed we were wrongdoers. "Until We made them a harvest" meaning with swords as crops are harvested with a sickle, said Mujahid. Al-Hasan said: meaning with punishment. "Extinguished" meaning dead. Extinguishment is dormancy, like the extinguishing of fire when it is put out, so the extinction of life is likened to the extinction of fire, just as it is said of someone who has died that he has been extinguished, likening the extinguishing of fire.
21:16: The Almighty says: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play. That is, in vain and in vain, but rather to draw attention to the fact that they have a powerful Creator whose command must be obeyed, that He will reward the wrongdoer and the doer of good. That is, We did not create the heaven and the earth for some people to wrong others, or for some to disbelieve, or for some to disobey what He commanded, and then die without transgressing, nor to be commanded in this world to do good nor forbidden from evil. This playfulness denied by the Wise One is the opposite of wisdom.
21:17: The Almighty's saying: If We had intended to take a diversion When some people believed that He had a son, He said: If We had intended to take a diversion and diversion is a woman in the language of Yemen, as Qatada said. Uqbah bin Abi Jasra said - and Tawus, Ata' and Mujahid came to ask him about the Almighty's saying: If We had intended to take a diversion - so he said: Diversion is the wife, and Al-Hasan said the same. Ibn Abbas said: Diversion is the child, and Al-Hasan also said the same. Al-Jawhari said: Diversion can also be used as a metaphor for sexual intercourse. I said: And from it is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: Didn't you claim today that I have grown old and that people like me don't enjoy playing? Sexual intercourse is called amusement because it is a distraction for the heart, as he said: And there is a place for friends to play and a place to see. Al-Jawhari: And the Almighty’s saying: If We had wanted to take a diversion, they said a woman, and it is said: a son. We would have taken it from Our presence, meaning from Our presence, not from you. Ibn Jurayj said: From the people of heaven, not from the people of earth. It was said: He wanted to respond to those who said that idols are daughters of God, meaning how can your sculpture be a son for us? Ibn Qutaybah said: The verse is a response to the Christians. If We were to do, Qatadah, Muqatil, Ibn Jurayj, and Al-Hasan said: The meaning is we would not have done, like You are only a warner (Fatir 35:23) meaning you are only a warner. And if means denial, and the discussion ends when He said: We would have taken it from Our presence. It was said: It is in the sense of a condition, meaning if we were to do that, but we are not going to do that because it is impossible for us to have a son, because if that were the case, we would not have created Paradise, Hell, death, resurrection, or accountability. It was said: If We wanted to take a son by way of adoption, we would have taken him from Our presence from the angels. Some people tended towards this, because the will may be related to adoption, but taking a child is impossible, and the will is not related to the impossible, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri.
21:18: God the Almighty says: Rather, We cast the truth upon falsehood. Qadhf means throwing, meaning We cast the truth upon falsehood. And it destroys it means It subdues it and destroys it. The root of damg is to cut off the opinion until it reaches the tears, and from it comes the word damighah. The truth here is the Quran, and falsehood is the devil according to Mujahid, who said: Everything in the Quran of falsehood is the devil. It was said: Falsehood is their lie and describing God the Almighty with attributes other than His, such as a son and other things. It was said: He meant the truth as an argument, and likened them to falsehood. It was said: The truth is sermons, and falsehood is sins, and the meanings are close. The Quran includes both the argument and the sermon. Then it is gone meaning it is destroyed and ruined, as Qatada said. And for you is woe meaning the torment in the Hereafter because of your describing God with what is not permissible to describe. Ibn Abbas said: Woe is a valley in Hell, and this has been mentioned previously. Of what you describe meaning of what you lie about, according to Qatada and Mujahid, similar to He will recompense them for their description (al-An’am 6:139) meaning for their lies. It was said: Of what you describe God with of the impossibility, which is His taking a son, glory be to Him.
21:19: The Almighty said: And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth meaning dominion and creation, so how can it be permissible to associate with Him what is His servant and creation? And from Him meaning the angels whom you mentioned are the daughters of God. They are not arrogant meaning they are not averse to worshiping Him and submitting to Him. And they do not tire meaning they become exhausted, as stated by Qatada. It is taken from the word hasir which is a camel that has run down due to exhaustion and fatigue. It is said: the camel hasar yasr husr, it became exhausted and was worn out, and istahsar and tahsar are similar to it, and I have regretted it, it is transitive and intransitive, and I have also regretted it, so it is hasir. Ibn Zayd said: They do not get bored. Ibn Abbas: They do not disdain. Abu Zayd said: They do not tire. It was said: They do not lose heart, as mentioned by Ibn al-A'rabi, and the meaning is the same.
21:20: They glorify God night and day meaning they pray and remember God and glorify Him always. They never slacken meaning they never weaken or get tired. They are inspired to glorify and sanctify Him as they are inspired to self. Abdullah bin Al-Harith said: I asked Ka'b and said: Do they not have anything to do with glorifying God? Does anything distract them from it? He said: Who is this? I said: From the sons of Abdul Muttalib. He embraced me and said: O son of my brother, does anything distract you from self?! Glorifying God is like the self to them. This verse has been used as evidence by those who say that the angels are better than the sons of Adam. It has been mentioned before, and praise be to God.
21:21: The Almighty said: Or have they taken gods from the earth who can resurrect? Al-Mufaddal said: The purpose of this question is denial, i.e. they have not taken gods who are able to bring the dead back to life. It was said: Or means whether, i.e. did these polytheists take gods from the earth who can bring the dead back to life? Or here does not mean rather, because that would require them to create the dead unless Or is understood with the question, then Or is disconnected and the meaning is correct, said Al-Mubarrad. It was said: Or is in apposition to the meaning, i.e. did We create the heaven and the earth in play, or is this what they added to Us from Us so that it would be a source of doubt for them? Or do the gods they have taken on earth bring the dead back to life so that it would be a source of doubt? It was said: Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book in which is your remembrance, so will you not reason? (al-Anbiya 21:10) Then it was connected to it with reproach, and according to these two interpretations, Or is connected. The majority read yanshrūn with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the sheen from anshr God al-mayyit fanashar meaning He revived him so he was brought to life. Al-Hasan read it with a fatha on the ya’, meaning they live and do not die.
21:22: The Almighty said: If there were within them gods besides God, they both would have been ruined. That is, if there were in the heavens and the earth gods worshipped besides God, they would have been ruined. Al-Kisa'i and Sibawayh said: Except means other than, so when you put except in the place of other, the noun that comes after it is parsed in the same way as other, as he said: Every brother who leaves his brother, by your father's life, except Al-Farqadhan Sibawayh narrated: If there had been a man with us except Zaid, we would have perished. Al-Farra’ said: Except here is in the place of except, and the meaning is: If there were gods in them other than God, their people would have been corrupted. Another said: That is, if there were two gods in them, the plan would have been corrupted, because if one of them wanted something and the other the opposite, one of them would be powerless. It was said: The meaning of they would have been corrupted is they would have been ruined and those in them would have perished due to the dispute that occurred due to the difference that occurred between the partners. So glory be to God, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe. He cleared Himself and commanded the servants to clear Him of having a partner or a son.
21:23: The Almighty's saying: He will not be questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned is a crushing blow to the Qadarites and others. Ibn Jurayj said: The meaning is that the creation will not ask Him about His decree regarding His creation, and He will ask the creation about their deeds, because they are slaves. He explained by this that whoever will be questioned about his deeds tomorrow, like the Messiah and the angels, is not fit for divinity. It was said: He will not be held accountable for his deeds, while they will be held accountable. It was narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him that a man said to him: O Commander of the Faithful, does our Lord like to be disobeyed? He said: Will our Lord be disobeyed by force? He said: Tell me, if He prevents me from guidance and grants me ruin, has He done me good or wrong? He said: If He prevents you from your right, then He has done wrong, and if He prevents you from His bounty, then it is His bounty, which He gives to whom He wills. Then he recited the verse: He will not be questioned about what He does, while they will be questioned. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When God Almighty sent Moses and spoke to him, and revealed the Torah to him, he said: O God, You are a great Lord. If You wanted to be obeyed, I would have obeyed, and if You wanted not to be disobeyed, I would not have been disobeyed. You love to be obeyed, yet in that you are disobeyed, so how is this, O Lord? So God revealed to him: I am not asked about what I do, but they are asked.
21:24: The Almighty's saying: "Or have they taken other gods besides Him? He repeated the astonishment at taking other gods besides Him, exaggerating the rebuke, that is, their description as mentioned previously in the creation and the revival, so or means is it" as mentioned previously, so let them bring proof for that. It was said: The first is an argument from the rational side, because He said: "They will resurrect" and revive the dead, far from it! The second is an argument from the transmitted, that is, bring your proof from this side, so in which book was this revealed?! In the Qur'an or in the books revealed to all the prophets?! "This is a reminder from me with the sincerity of monotheism in the Qur'an, and a reminder from before me" in the Torah and the Gospel, and what God revealed of the books, so look, is there in any of these books that God commanded taking other gods besides Him? The laws did not differ in what is related to monotheism, but they differed in the commands and prohibitions. Qatada said: The reference to the Qur’an means: This is a reminder of those with me with what is required of them of what is lawful and unlawful. And a reminder of those before me of the nations who were saved by faith and perished by polytheism. It was also said: A reminder of those with me with what they will receive of reward for faith and punishment for disbelief. And a reminder of those before me of the previous nations regarding what will be done to them in this world and what will be done to them in the Hereafter. It was also said: The meaning of the statement is a threat and a warning, meaning do whatever you want, for soon the veil will be lifted. Abu Hatim narrated that Yahya bin Ya’mar and Talhah bin Musarraf read This is a reminder of those with me and a reminder of those before me with the tanween and the kasra on the meem, and he claimed that there is no basis for this. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: In this reading: The meaning is: This is a reminder of what was revealed to me of what is with me and a reminder of those before me. It was also said: A reminder of what was before me, meaning I came with what the prophets before me came with. Rather, most of them do not know the truth. Ibn Muhaysin and al-Hasan read the truth with the nominative case meaning it is the truth and this is the truth. Based on this, it is stopped at they do not know and it is not stopped at the accusative reading they are turning away meaning from the truth, which is the Qur’an, so they do not contemplate the argument of monotheism.
21:25: The Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him. Hafs, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read We revealed to him with a noon, because of the saying, We sent. "That there is no god but Me, so worship Me means We said to everyone, There is no god but God." So the evidence of reason testifies that He has no partner, and the transmission from all the prophets is present, and the evidence is either rational or transmitted. Qatada said: No prophet was sent except with monotheism, and the laws differ in the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an, and all of that is based on sincerity and monotheism.
21:26: The Almighty said: "And they say, 'The Most Gracious has taken a son. Glory be to Him.'" It was revealed about Khuza'ah, when they said: The angels are daughters of God, and they used to worship them in the hope of their intercession for them. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatadah, who said: The Jews said - Muammar said in his narration - or groups of al-Nas 114:A circumciser to the jinn, and the angels are from the jinn, so God, the Almighty, said: Glory be to Him, sanctifying Him. Rather, they are servants, meaning, rather, they are servants, honored, meaning, not as these infidels claimed. Al-Zajjaj allows the accusative case to mean, rather, He has taken honored servants. Al-Farra' permitted it to refer it to a son, meaning, rather, We have not taken them as a son, rather, We have taken them as honored servants. The son here is for the plural, and it may be singular and plural son. It is also possible for the word son to be for the gender, as it is said that someone has money.
21:27: They do not precede Him in speech meaning they do not speak until He says, and they do not speak except what He commands them. And they act by His command meaning by obeying Him and His commands.
21:28: He knows what is before them meaning He knows what they have done and what they will do, said Ibn Abbas. And also from him: What is before them is the Hereafter, and what is behind them is the world, the first was mentioned by Al-Tha'labi, and the second by Al-Qushayri. And they do not intercede except for him with whom He is pleased Ibn Abbas said: They are the people of the testimony that there is no god but God. And Mujahid said: They are everyone with whom God is pleased, and the angels intercede tomorrow in the Hereafter as in Sahih Muslim and others, and in this world also, for they seek forgiveness for the believers and for those on the earth, as stated in the revelation as follows. And they meaning the angels are fearful of Him meaning fearful of Him and are not safe from His deceit.
21:29: The Almighty said: And whoever among them says, 'I am a god besides Him' Qatada, Ad-Dahhak and others said: This verse refers to Iblis, as he claimed partnership and called for the worship of himself, and he was one of the angels, and none of the angels said, I am a god other than Him. It was said: The reference is to all the angels, meaning that the one who said, We will recompense him with Hell. This is evidence that even though they were honored with infallibility, they are worshippers, and are not compelled to worship as some of the ignorant thought. Ibn Abbas used this verse as evidence that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the best of the people of heaven. This was mentioned previously in (Al-Baqarah). Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers meaning, just as We recompense this one with the Fire, so do We recompense the wrongdoers who place divinity and worship in the wrong place.
21:30: The Almighty said: Have not those who disbelieved seen that The general reading is awlam with the waw. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, and Shibl ibn Ibad read alam yar without the waw, and this is how it is in the Meccan Mushaf. Alam yar means know. Those who disbelieve that the heavens and the earth were joined together. Al-Akhfash said: was because they are two types, as the Arabs say: they are two black camels, and as God Almighty said: Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist. (Fatir 35:41) Abu Ishaq said: was because he refers to the heavens with the singular word sky, and because the heavens were one sky, and so were the earths. He said: was joined together and did not say was joined together, because it is a source, and the meaning was that they were joined together. Al-Hasan read was joined together with the opening of the taa. Isa ibn Umar said: This is correct and it is a language. Al-Ratq is the opposite of al-Fitq. Al-Fitq was patched, so it was patched, meaning it was healed. And from this comes the word al-Ritqa for the joined vagina. Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Ata’, al-Dahhak and Qatada said: It means that they were one thing stuck together, then God separated them with air. Ka’b also said: God created the heavens and the earth, one upon the other, then He created a wind in the middle of them and opened it with it, and made the heavens seven and the earths seven. A second statement was said by Mujahid, al-Suddi and Abu Salih: The heavens were united in one layer, then He split them apart and made them seven heavens. Likewise the earths were patched together in one layer, then He split them apart and made them seven. Al-Qatabi narrated it in his Uyun al-Akhbar, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, regarding the words of God Almighty: Have those who disbelieve not considered that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them? He said: The heaven was created alone and the earth was created alone, so He separated from these seven heavens, and from these seven earths. He created the highest earth and made its inhabitants the jinn and mankind, and He split rivers in it and caused fruits to grow in it, and He made seas in it and called it Ra’aan, its width is a journey of five hundred years. Then He created the second earth like it in width and thickness and made people in it whose mouths are like the mouths of dogs and their hands are the hands of people, and their ears are the ears of camels and their hair is the hair of sheep. When the Hour approaches, the earth will cast them to Yajuj and Majuj, and the name of that earth is Ad-Daqa’. Then He created the third earth, its thickness is a journey of five hundred years, and from it is air to the earth. In the fourth earth, He created darkness and scorpions for the people of Hell like black mules, and it has tails like the tails of tall horses, some of which eat others and they gain power over the children of Adam. Then God created the fifth earth, similar in thickness, length and width, in which are chains, shackles and fetters for the people of Hell. Then God created the sixth earth, whose name is Mad, in which are black stones, and from it was created the soil of Adam, peace be upon him. Those stones will be raised on the Day of Resurrection, and each stone is like a huge mountain. It is made of sulfur and is hung around the necks of the disbelievers, burning until it burns their faces and hands. This is what God, the Almighty, says: Its fuel is men and stones (al-Baqarah 2:24). Then God created the seventh earth, whose name is Arabia, in which is Hell, in which are two gates, one called Sijjin and the other Al-Ghilaq. As for Sijjin, it is open and to it the book of the disbelievers ends, and upon it the Companions of the Table and the people of Pharaoh are presented. As for Al-Ghilaq, it is closed and will not be opened until the Day of Resurrection. It was mentioned in (Al-Baqarah) that there are seven earths, between every two of them is a journey of five hundred years, and more clarification will come at the end of (At-Talaq), God willing. A third statement was made by Ikrimah, Atiyah, Ibn Zayd, and Ibn Abbas, as well, in what Al-Mahdawi mentioned: The heavens were sealed and did not rain, and the earth was sealed and did not produce vegetation, so He split the heavens with rain, and the earth with vegetation. Similar to the statement of God Almighty: And the sky with its paths, and the earth with its rifts (al-Tariq 86:11-12). At-Tabari chose this statement, because after it is And We made from water every living thing, so will they not believe? I said: And with it comes the consideration of observation and witnessing, and for this reason He informed of that in more than one verse, to indicate the perfection of His power, and of the resurrection and recompense. And it was said: It is easy for them to get angry and to force the enemies. Hernia repair, hernia repair, and the cancellation and conclusion of matters And in the words of God Almighty: And We made from water every living thing, there are three interpretations: The first: That He created everything from water, as stated by Qatada. The second: That He preserved the life of everything with water. The third: And We made from the water of the loins every living thing, as stated by Qatrib. And We made means We created. Abu Hatim al-Busti narrated in his Sahih Musnad, “From the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: I said: O Messenger of God! When I see you, my soul is at peace, and my eyes are comforted. Tell me about everything. He said: Everything was created from water. The hadith. Abu Hatim said that Abu Hurairah’s statement: (Tell me about everything) meant everything created from water. The evidence for the correctness of this is the answer of the Chosen One to him where he said: “Everything was created from water,” even though it was not created. This is another argument other than what was mentioned before about the heavens and the earth being sewn together. It was said: The whole may be mentioned in the sense of some, like His statement: And I have been given of all things (al-Naml 27:27) and His statement: Everything was destroyed (al-Ahqaf 46:45). The correct view is the generality, because of his statement, peace be upon him: Everything was created from water. And God knows best. Do they not believe? That is, do they not believe in what they see, and that this did not happen by itself, but by the Creator of its existence and the Manager who brought it into existence? It is not permissible for that Creator to be created.
21:31: The Almighty said: And We placed on the earth firm mountains meaning fixed mountains. lest it should shake with them meaning lest it should shake with them, nor move so that it could be settled, as stated by the Kufians. The Basrans said: The meaning is the hatred that it should shake. And movement is turning. It is said: he stretched his head, meaning he turned. It has been mentioned in detail in (An-Nahl). And We placed therein paths meaning in the firm mountains, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Paths are the paths. A path is the wide road between two mountains. It was said: And We placed on the earth paths meaning paths, and this is the choice of At-Tabari, because he said: Perhaps they will be guided meaning that they will be guided to travel on the earth. Paths is an interpretation of paths, because a path may be a passable road or it may not be. It was said: So that they may be guided by considering it to their religion.
21:32: The Almighty said: And We have made the sky a protected ceiling meaning protected from falling and hitting the ground. The evidence for this is the Almighty's statement: And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission (al-Hajj 22:65). It was also said: Protected by the stars from the devils, as Al-Farraa said. The evidence for this is the Almighty's statement: And We have preserved it from every devil expelled (al-Hijr 15:17). It was also said: Protected from demolition and destruction, and from anyone reaching it by trickery. It was also said: Protected so it does not need a pillar. Mujahid said: Raised. It was also said: Protected from polytheism and sins. And they meaning the disbelievers are turning away from its signs Mujahid said: meaning the sun and the moon. He added the signs to the sky because they are placed in it, and He added the signs to Himself in several places because He is the One Who does them. He explained that the polytheists neglected to look at the heavens and their signs, their night and day, their sun and moon, their orbits, winds and clouds, and what is in them of the power of God Almighty. If they had looked and considered, they would have known that they have one powerful Creator, so it is impossible for Him to have a partner.
21:33: The Almighty said: And it is He who created the night and the day. He mentioned another blessing: He made the night for them to rest in, and the day for them to use for their livelihoods. And the sun and the moon, meaning He made the sun a sign of the day, and the moon a sign of the night, to teach the months and years and the reckoning, as was explained in (Subhan). Each means of the sun, moon, stars, planets, night and day swims in an orbit meaning they run and move quickly like a swimmer in water. God the Almighty said, and He is the most truthful of speakers: And those who swim, swimming (An-Nazi'at: 3). The horse that extends its hand in running is called a swimmer. In grammar, he did not say: they swim nor does she swim. Sibawayh's school of thought is that when he informed about them with the action of someone who has reason and made them in obedience like someone who has reason, he informed about them with the waw and the nun. Al-Farra' said something similar. This meaning was previously mentioned in (Yusuf). Al-Kisa'i said: He said: They glorify because it is the beginning of a verse, as God Almighty said: We are all victorious (al-Qamar 54:44) and He did not say victorious. It was said: The running is for the sphere, so it was attributed to it. The most correct is that the car runs in the sphere, which is seven spheres below the closed heavens, which are the domain of the angels and the causes of the kingdom. The moon is in the lowest sphere, then Mercury, then Venus, then the sun, then Mars, then Jupiter, then Saturn, and the eighth is the sphere of the zodiac, and the ninth is the greatest sphere. The sphere is one of the spheres of the stars. Abu Amr said: It is permissible to make it plural with the form fa`l like asad and asad and khashab and khashab. The root of the word is from dawaran, and from it is falakat the spindle, for its roundness. From it it was said: falak the woman's breast is taflikan, and tafalak means to turn. In the hadith of Ibn Mas`ud: I left my horse as if it was turning in an sphere. As if, due to its turning, it was likened to the sphere of the sky around which the stars revolve. Ibn Zayd said: The spheres are the courses of the stars, the sun, and the moon. He said: It is between the sky and the earth. Qatada said: The ark is a circle in the sky revolving with the stars while the sky remains fixed. Mujahid said: The ark is like the shape of the iron of a millstone and it is its pole. Ad-Dahhak said: Its ark is its course and the speed of its movement. It was said: The ark is a restrained wave and the course of the sun and moon is in it, and God knows best.
21:34: The Almighty said: And We have not granted to any human being before you immortality meaning perpetual life in this world. It was revealed when they said: We are waiting for Muhammad to meet his fate. This is because the polytheists were denying his prophethood and saying: He is a poet whom we are waiting for his fate, and perhaps he will die as the poet of Banu so-and-so died. So God the Almighty said: The prophets before you have died, and God has taken care of their religion with victory and protection, so this is how we protect your religion and your law. If you die, will they be immortal? meaning will they understand, like the poet's saying: They threw me away and said, O Khuwaylid, do not be afraid. I said, and I denied the faces, They are them. Which is more important! It is a question of denial. Al-Farraa said: The letter fa was used to indicate the condition, because it is the answer to their saying he will die. It is also permissible that it was used because the meaning is: Make the immortals understand if I die! Al-Farraa said: The letter fa may be deleted or implied because the i'rab in hum is not clear. That is, if I die, they will die too, so there is no gloating over death. Matt and matt are read with a kasra or a damma on the meem, which are two languages.
21:35: The Almighty’s saying: Every soul will taste death was mentioned in (Al Imran) And We test you with evil and with good as trial “Trial” is a source with a different wording. That is, We test you with hardship and ease, with what is permissible and what is forbidden, so We see how grateful and patient you are. And to Us you will be returned that is, to be rewarded for your deeds.
21:36: The Almighty said: And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you only in ridicule. That is, they take you only in ridicule. Ridicule is mockery, and it has been mentioned before. They are the mockers who were mentioned at the end of Surah Al-Hijr in His statement: Indeed, We will suffice you against the mockers. (al-Hijr 15:95). They used to criticize those who denied the divinity of their idols, while they denied the divinity of the Most Gracious, and this is the height of ignorance. Is this the one? That is, they say: Is this the one? So He implied the statement, which is the answer to if. His statement: They take you only in ridicule is an interjectional statement between if and its answer, He mentions your gods, that is, with evil and fault. And from this is the statement of Antarah: Do not mention my dowry and what I fed him, lest your skin be like the skin of a mangy dog. That is, do not criticize my dowry. And they are disbelievers in the remembrance of the Most Gracious that is, in the Qur’an. They the second they is an emphasis on their disbelief, that is, they are the disbelievers, an exaggeration in describing them as disbelievers.
21:37: The Almighty said: He created man from haste meaning he rode on haste and was created hasty, as God the Almighty said: God is He who created you from weakness (al-Rum 30:54) meaning He created man weak. It is said: He created man from evil, meaning evil if you exaggerate in describing him with it. It is also said: You are only going and coming. Meaning you are going and coming. Meaning, man's nature is haste, so he rushes many things even if they are harmful. Then it was said: What is meant by man is Adam, peace be upon him. Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Suddi said: When the spirit entered the eyes of Adam, peace be upon him, he looked at the fruits of Paradise, and when it entered his stomach he desired food, so he jumped up before the spirit reached his feet in haste to the fruits of Paradise, so that is His saying: He created man from haste. It was said: Adam was created on Friday at the end of the day, and when God revived his head, he hurried and asked to complete the breathing of the spirit into him before sunset, as Al-Kalbi, Mujahid and others said. Abu Ubaidah and many of the scholars of meaning said: The calf is clay in the Himyarite language. And they recited: The palm tree grows between the water and the calf It was said: What is meant by human beings is all people. It was also said that what is meant is: Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith bin Alqamah bin Kalda bin Abd Al-Dar in the interpretation of Ibn Abbas, meaning that it is not appropriate for someone who was created from insignificant clay to mock the signs of God and His Messengers. It was also said: It is from the inverted, meaning the creation of the calf from a human. This is the doctrine of Abu Ubaidah. Al-Nahhas: This statement should not be answered with in the Book of God, because the inversion only occurs in poetry by necessity, as he said: Adultery was punishable by stoning. And its counterpart is this verse: And man is ever hasty (al-Isra’ 17:11) and it was mentioned in (Glory be to Him). I will show you My signs, so do not be impatient This strengthens the first statement, and that man’s nature is justice, and that he was created in a way that cannot be controlled, as he said, peace be upon him, according to what was mentioned in (Glory be to Him). What is meant by the signs is what indicates the truth of Muhammad, peace be upon him, from the miracles, and what He made for him from the praiseworthy outcome. And it was said: What they asked for from the punishment, so they wanted to hasten and said: When will this promise be? And they did not know that everything has a set term. It was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith. And His statement: If this is the truth (al-Anfal 8:32). Al-Akhfash Saeed said: The meaning of Man was created from haste is that he was told Be and he was, so the meaning of Do not be impatient according to this statement is that whoever says to a thing Be and it is, is not unable to show the signs that they hastened.
21:38: And they say, 'When will this promise be?' meaning the promised one, just as one says, God is our hope, meaning the one we hope for. It was said that the meaning of the promise here is the threat, meaning the one who promises us punishment. It was also said that it is the Resurrection. If you are truthful, O group of believers.
21:39: The Almighty says: If those who disbelieve knew Knowledge here means knowledge, so it does not require a second object, like You do not know them, God knows them (al-Anfal 8:60). The answer to if is omitted, meaning if they knew the time when they will not ward off the Fire from their faces or from their backs, nor will they be aided and knew it, they would not have hastened the threat. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning they would have known the truth of the promise. It was said: the meaning is if they knew it, they would not have persisted in disbelief and would have believed. Al-Kisa'i said: it is a warning of the certainty of the Hour, meaning if they knew it with certainty, they would have known that the Hour is coming.
21:40: And it is indicated by Rather, it will come upon them suddenly meaning suddenly, meaning the Resurrection. It was said: the punishment. It was also said: the Fire, so they will not be able to find a way, so it will confuse them. Al-Jawhari said: It will confuse him with a conceit that will take him by surprise. God the Most High said: Rather, it will come upon them suddenly, so it will confuse them. Al-Farra' said: So it will confuse them meaning it will confuse them. It is said: So it will surprise them. "So they will not be able to repel it" meaning divert it from their backs. "Nor will they be given respite" meaning they will not be given respite or delay for repentance and apology.
21:41: The Almighty says: And messengers before you were mocked. This is a consolation and comfort to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He says: If these people mock you, then messengers before you were mocked, so be patient as they were patient. Then He promised him victory and said: So it encompassed that is, it surrounded and surrounded those who disbelieved and mocked them and mocked them that which they used to mock that is, the recompense for their mockery.
21:42: The Almighty said: "Say: Who will guard you?" That is, guard and preserve you. Guarding means protection and preservation. God protected him, meaning He preserved and guarded him. It is said: Go in God's protection, and I was cautious of them, meaning I was on my guard. The poet, Ibn Harmah, said: Salma, may God protect her, was stingy with something that would have caused her misery. Another said: I made my camel kneel and looked at him Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' narrated Qal man yaklukum with the opening of the lam and the sukoon of the waw. They narrated Man yakla'kum with the softening of the hamza in both versions, but what is known is the emphasis of the hamza and this is the reading of the common people. As for Yakla'kum, it is a mistake for two reasons as mentioned by An-Nahhas: The first is that ani instead of the hamza only occurs in poetry. The second is that they say in the past tense kallitahu, so the meaning is reversed, because kallitahu caused pain to his kidney, and whoever says to a man Kallak God has prayed against him that God will afflict him with pain in his kidney. Then it was said: The way of the expression is the way of the question and what is meant by it is negation. And its meaning is: Say, There is no protector for you “at night” when you sleep and “during the day” when you rise and deal with your affairs. From the Most Gracious meaning from His punishment and wrath, like the Almighty’s saying: So who can protect me from God? (Hud 11:63) meaning from the punishment of God. And the address is to those of them who acknowledge the Maker, meaning if you acknowledge that He is the Creator, then He is the One who is able to bring about the punishment that you are hastening. Rather, they are from the remembrance of their Lord meaning from the Qur’an. And it was said: from the admonitions of their Lord. And it was said: from knowing Him. Turning away heedless and neglectful.
21:43: The Almighty said: Or do they have gods? The meaning is: They inspire, and the mim is a connection. To protect them from Us meaning from Our punishment. They are unable meaning those whom these infidels claim that they will support them are unable to support themselves so how can they support their worshippers? Nor do they accompany Us Ibn Abbas said: They are prevented. And from him: They are protected, and this is the choice of Al-Tabari. The Arabs say: I am your protector and companion from so-and-so, meaning I protect from him. The poet said: He calls out at the top of his voice, seeking refuge from her and the spears flapping around him. Muammar narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid who said: They will be victorious means they will be protected. Qatada said: That is, God will not accompany them with goodness, nor will He make His mercy their companion.
21:44: God the Almighty said: Rather, We have given enjoyment to these and their fathers. Ibn Abbas said: He means the people of Mecca. That is, We have expanded for them and their fathers in its pleasures and prolonged their life in the pleasure, so they thought that it would not be removed from them, so they were deceived and turned away from contemplating the proofs of God the Almighty. Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its borders? That is, by conquering it for you, O Muhammad, land after land, and opening it country after country from what surrounds Mecca. Al-Hasan and others said its meaning. It was said: by killing and capturing, as Al-Kalbi narrated. The meaning is the same. The discussion of this has already been completed in (Al-Ra'd). Understand the victors meaning the infidels of Mecca after We have reduced their borders, rather you will conquer them and be victorious over them.
21:45: God the Almighty said: Say, 'I only warn you by revelation.' That is, I frighten you and warn you by the Qur'an. And the deaf do not hear the call. That is, the one whose heart God has deafened, sealed his hearing, and covered his vision with a veil, preventing him from understanding the verses and hearing the truth. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami and Muhammad ibn al-Sumaiqa' read and he does not hear with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the meem for what the agent is not named, the deaf in the nominative case, meaning that God does not hear them. Ibn 'Amir and al-Sulami also, Abu Haywah and Yahya ibn al-Harith read and you do not hear with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the meem, the deaf in the accusative case, meaning that you, O Muhammad, do not make the deaf hear the call, so the addressee is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some linguists rejected this reading. He said: He should have said: When you warn them. Al-Nahhas said: That is permissible, because the meaning is known.
21:46: The Almighty said: And if a whiff of the punishment of your Lord should touch them, Ibn Abbas said: A little. Qatada said: A punishment. Ibn Kaysan: Little and the least of something, taken from the whiff of musk. He said: And Umrah is one of the noblest women, her garments are fragrant with musk. Ibn Jurayj: A share, as it is said: So-and-so gave so-and-so a share of his gift, if he gave him a share of the money. The poet said: When I came to you, hoping for your bounty, you gave me a breath that pleased the Arabs. That is, the soul was at ease with her. In the language, the word nafah means a small push, so the meaning is, even if the slightest bit of torment touches them, they will surely say, ‘Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.’ That is, transgressors, so they confess when confession will not benefit them.
21:47: The Almighty said: And We will set up the just scales on the Day of Resurrection, so that not a soul will be wronged at all. Scales is the plural of scale. It was said: It indicates on its surface that every accountable person has a scale on which his deeds are weighed, so the good deeds are placed on one pan, and the bad deeds on the other. It was said: It is possible that there are scales for a single worker, and each scale weighs a type of his deeds, as He said: A king whose justice determines all events, so every event has its own scale. It could be one scale expressed in the plural form. Al-Lalaka’i, the hafiz Abu al-Qasim, narrated in al-Sunnah on the authority of Anas, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet: “An angel is assigned to the scales, and the son of Adam will be brought and made to stand between the two pans of the scale. If he is heavier, the angel will call out in a voice that all creation will hear: ‘So-and-so is blessed with a happiness after which he will never be miserable.’ But if he is heavier, the angel will call out: ‘So-and-so is miserable with a misery after which he will never be happy.’” It was narrated on the authority of Hudhayfah may God be pleased with him who said: “The owner of the scales on the Day of Resurrection will be Gabriel (peace be upon him). It was also said that the scales have two pans, threads, a tongue, and the falcon, so the plural refers to them. Mujahid, Qatada, and Ad-Dahhak said: The scales are mentioned as an example, but there is no scale, rather it is justice. What the reports have reported, and the majority are in agreement with, is the first opinion. This has been explained in Al-A’raf and also in Al-Kahf. We have mentioned it in full in the book At-Tadhkirah, and praise be to God. “Al-Qist” means justice, meaning there is no shortcoming or injustice in it, as is the case in the weight of this world. Al-Qist is an attribute of scales, and it is singular because it is a source. It is said: a scale of justice, two scales of justice, and scales of justice. Like men of justice and contentment. The Qast group read it with a sad. For the Day of Resurrection meaning for the people of the Day of Resurrection. It was said that the meaning is on the Day of Resurrection. So no soul will be wronged at all meaning that the good of a good person will not be diminished nor will the evil of a bad person be increased. And if it is the weight of a mustard seed Nafi’, Shaiba and Abu Ja’far read the weight of a grain in the nominative case here, and in (Luqman) it means if it occurs or is restricted, so it is complete and does not need a predicate. The rest read the weight in the accusative case meaning even if the work or that thing is a weight. The weight of a thing is its scale of its like. We brought it with a shortened alif is the reading of the majority, meaning we brought it and brought it to reward it and for it. It is brought by the grain, if he had said by it, meaning by the weight, it would have been permissible. It was said that the weight of a grain is nothing other than the grain, so that is why he said We brought it. Mujahid and Ikrimah read We came with a long vowel meaning we rewarded it. It is said: ata yu’ati muwata’at. And sufficient are We as accountants meaning as accountants for what they have done of good and evil. It was also said: as accountants because no one is faster in accounting than us. Accounting is counting. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her: “A man sat in front of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God! I have two slaves who lie to me, betray me, and disobey me, and I curse them and beat them, so how can I be with them? He said: Their betrayal, disobedience, and lying to you, and your punishment of them, if your punishment of them is commensurate with their sins, it will be sufficient, neither for you nor against you. If your punishment of them is less than their sins, it will be a favor to you, and if your punishment is greater than their sins, they will have avenged the favor from you.” The man stepped aside and began to cry and shout. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you not read the Book of God Almighty: And We will set up the scales of justice on the Day of Resurrection, so that no soul will be wronged at all. The man said: By God, O Messenger of God, I do not find anything better for myself and these people than to part with them. I bear witness that they are all free.” This is a strange hadith.
21:48: The Almighty said: And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion and a light. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah that the Criterion is a light without a waw in the state. Al-Farraa claimed that deleting the waw and bringing it are the same, as God Almighty said: Indeed, We have adorned the nearest heaven with an adornment of stars * And as protection. (Saffat: 6-7) meaning protection. Al-Zajjaj responded to this statement. He said: Because the waw comes for a meaning, so it is not added. He said: The interpretation of (the Criterion) is the Torah, because it contains the distinction between what is forbidden and what is permissible. He said: And a light is like in it is guidance and light. (al-Ma’idah 5:46) Ibn Zayd said: (the Criterion) here is the victory over the enemies, as evidenced by the Almighty's statement: And We did not send down to Our Servant on the Day of Criterion. (al-Anfal 8:41) meaning the Day of Badr. Al-Tha'labi said: This statement is more similar to the apparent meaning of the verse, because the waw is included in the word light, so the meaning of the verse is: And We gave Moses and Aaron victory and the Torah, which is the light and the reminder. For the righteous.
21:49: Those who fear their Lord in secret meaning in the absence, because they have not seen God Almighty, but they know through observation and reasoning that they have a Lord who is capable, who rewards for deeds, so they fear Him in their secrets and in their solitude in which they are absent from people. And they are fearful of the Hour meaning of its events before repentance. Fearful meaning fearful and apprehensive.
21:50: And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down (al-Anbiya 21:50) meaning the Qur'an. Then will you, O Arabs, deny it? It is a miracle and you are not able to produce anything like it. Al-Farra' permitted This is a blessed reminder which We have sent down to mean We sent it down blessed.
21:51: The Almighty said: And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgment. Al-Farra' said: That is, We gave him his guidance before that is, before prophethood, that is, We enabled him to contemplate and reason, when night fell upon him and he saw the star, the sun, and the moon. It was said: before that is, before Moses and Aaron. According to this, sound judgment means prophethood. Most commentators agree with the first, as He said to Yahya: And We gave him judgment while he was a boy (Maryam 19:12). Al-Qurazi said: His sound judgment means his righteousness. And We were well-versed in him that is, he was worthy of sound judgment and fit for prophethood.
21:52: The Almighty said: When he said to his father It was said: The meaning is, remember when he said to his father, so the speech would have been completed when he said: And We were knowing of it. It was also said: The meaning is, And We were knowing of it * when he said So the speech would be connected and not stopped at his saying: knowing. "To his father who is Azar and his people Nimrod and those who followed him What are these statues" meaning idols. A statue is a name given to a manufactured thing that resembles a creation of God Almighty. It is said: I likened a thing to a thing, meaning I likened it to it. The name of that represented thing is a statue. "To which you are devoted" meaning you are established in its worship.
21:53: They said, 'We found our fathers worshipping it.' That is, we worship it in imitation of our ancestors.
21:54: He said, 'You and your fathers were in manifest error.' That is, in loss by worshipping them, as they are inanimate objects that neither benefit nor harm nor know.
21:55: They said, 'Have you come to us with the truth?' That is, have you come with the truth in what you say? Or are you one of the players? That is, a joking player.
21:56: He said, 'Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth.' That is, I am not playing, rather your Lord and the One who manages you is the Creator of the heavens and the earth. Who created them. That is, He created them and made them original. And I am of that among the witnesses. That is, that He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. A witness clarifies the ruling, and from this is God has testified (Al Imran 3:18) God clarified, so the meaning is: And I will clarify with evidence what I say.
21:57: The Almighty's saying: And by God, I will surely destroy your idols He informed us that he did not suffice with verbal argument, but rather he broke their idols, an act of one who was confident in God Almighty, preparing himself to endure hardship in defense of the religion. The ta' in by God is specific to swearing by the name of God alone, the waw is specific to every manifest, and the ba' is specific to every implied and manifest. The poet said: By God, he will remain a lonely man for days, with gazelles and myrtle trees strutting around him. Ibn Abbas said: By God’s sanctity, I will surely plot against your idols, meaning I will plot against them. And plotting is deception. Kadah means plotting. Kadah means plotting. War is sometimes called plotting. It is said: So-and-so fought and did not encounter plotting. And everything you deal with, you plot against him. After they turned their backs means departing and going. And they had a festival every year in which they would gather, so they said to Ibrahim: If you came with us to our festival, our religion would please you. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud, as will be explained in As-Saffat. So Ibrahim said to himself: By God, I will surely plot against your idols. Mujahid and Qatadah said that Ibrahim only said that in secret from his people, and only one man heard it, and he was the one who disclosed it to them. One person reports on someone with the report of the group if what he reported is something that pleases others. And similar to it is: They say, ‘If we return to the city, the more honorable will surely expel therefrom the more humble.’ (al-Munafiqun 63:8) It was said: He said it after the people had left, and only the weak ones remained, so they were the ones who heard him. Abraham had found a way to stay behind them by saying: I am ill (al-Saffat 37:89), meaning weak and unable to move.
21:58: The Almighty said: So He made them fragments meaning crumbs. And fragmentation means breaking and cutting. Jadhth means breaking and cutting something. And fragmentation and fragmentation are what is broken from it, and the damma is more eloquent than breaking it. Al-Jawhari said it. Al-Kisa'i: And the stones of gold are called fragments, because they are broken. Al-Kisa'i, Al-A'mash, and Ibn Muhaisin read Jathath with a kasra on the jim, meaning breaking and cutting. The plural of Jadhth is dry straw, like Khafif and Khafaf and Zarif and Zaraf. The poet said: Cutting down idols in their altar is for the sake of God, the Most High, the Almighty. The rest with the dammah, and Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it. Like the wreck and the remains, one is a fragment. And this is the plot that he swore to do to them. And he said: So he made them, because the people believed in their idols as divine. Ibn Abbas, Abu Nahik, and Abu Sammal read fragments with the fathah of the jim, and the fathah and the kasrah are two languages like harvest and harvest. Abu Hatim: The fathah, the kasrah, and the doubt mean the same thing, narrated by Qatrib. Except for a great one for them meaning the greatest of the gods in creation, for he did not break it. Al-Suddi and Mujahid said: He left the largest idol and hung the axe with which he broke the idols around its neck, to use it as evidence against them. Perhaps they will return to it meaning to Abraham and his religion “if the evidence is established against them. And it was said: “Perhaps they will return to it” meaning to the largest idol in breaking it.
21:59: The Almighty says: They said, 'Who did this to our gods? Indeed, he is among the wrongdoers.' The meaning is that when they returned from their festival and saw what had happened to their gods, they said, in a manner of inquiry and denial: Who did this to our gods? Indeed, he is among the wrongdoers. It was said: Who is not an interrogative, but rather it is a subject and its predicate is among the wrongdoers. That is, the one who did this is a wrongdoer.
21:60: The first is more correct, because he said: We heard a young man mentioning them. This is the answer to Who did this? The pronoun in they said refers to the weak people who heard Ibrahim, or one person as mentioned above. The meaning of mentioning them is to criticize and revile them, so perhaps he is the one who did this. People differed about the reason for raising Ibrahim. Al-Zajjaj said: It is raised in the sense that it is said to him, he is Ibrahim, so it is the predicate of a deleted subject, and the sentence is reported. He said: It is permissible for it to be raised in the vocative and its damma is a construction, and it takes the place of what its agent is not named.
