It was said: It is raised on the basis that it is the object of what its agent is not named, on the basis that Ibrahim is not indicative of the person, but rather the pronunciation of it is made indicative of the construction of this word, meaning that this saying and this word are said to him, just as you say the weight of a verb or three letters are added, so it does not indicate in any way the person, but rather you indicate by your pronunciation the word itself. In this way you say: I said Ibrahim, and it is a sound object that is considered a saying and speech, so it is not difficult after that to build the verb in it for the object. This is the choice of Ibn Atiyah in raising it. Professor Abu Al-Hajjaj Al-Ashbili Al-A’lam said: It is raising by neglect. Ibn Atiyah said: When he saw the aspects of raising as if they did not clarify the meaning they intended, he went to raise it without anything, just as the stripping and the nudity may raise the factors of the beginning. And the young man is the young man and the young woman is the young woman. Ibn Abbas said: God did not send a prophet except a young man. Then he recited: We heard a young man mentioning them.
21:61: The Almighty’s saying: They said, ‘Bring him before the eyes of the people.’ There is one issue in this, which is: When the report reached Nimrod and the nobles of his people, they were reluctant to take him without evidence, so they said: Bring him openly in the sight of the people so that they may see him perhaps they will testify against him for what he said, so that it would be openly in front of the people so that they may see him, perhaps they will testify against him for what would be an argument against him. It was said: perhaps they will testify to his punishment so that no one would do what he did. Or perhaps some people will testify that they saw him breaking the idols, or perhaps they will testify to his stabbing of their gods, so that they will know that he deserves punishment. I said: This is evidence that no one was held accountable for the claim of another regarding what came before, because God Almighty said, Then bring him before the eyes of the people so that they may bear witness. This is how it is in our law, and there is no disagreement about it.
21:62: The Almighty’s saying: They said, ‘Did you do this to our gods, O Abraham?’ There are four issues in it: First: Since the hearing was not general and the testimony was not proven, they asked him whether he did it or not. There is an omission in the speech, so Abraham came when he was brought and they said: Did you do this to the gods?
21:63: So Abraham said to them, as an argument against them: Rather, their eldest did it. That is, he was jealous and angry that he and the younger ones would be worshipped with him, so he did this to them, so if they speak, then ask them. So he linked the action of the eldest to the speech of the others, alerting them to the corruption of their belief. It is as if he said: Rather, he is the doer if these speak. And in the speech there is an introduction to this interpretation in his saying: Then ask them, if they speak. And it was said: He meant rather, their eldest did it if they speak. He explained that whoever does not speak and does not know does not deserve to be worshipped. His saying was an indirect expression, and in indirect expressions there is an alternative to lying. That is, ask them, if they speak, then they are truthful, and if they do not speak, then he is not the doer. And within these words there is an admission that he is the doer, and this is the correct view because he counted it against himself, so it indicates that it was made in the form of an indirect expression. This is because they worshipped them and took them as gods besides God, as Abraham said to his father: O my father, why do you worship that which hears not and sees not? (Maryam 19:42) - the verse - so Abraham said: Rather, their chief did it, so that they would say that they do not speak, nor benefit, nor harm. So he would say to them: Then why do you worship them? So the proof would be established against them. For this reason, it is permissible for the nation to impose falsehood with the opponent until he returns to the truth of his own accord, for it is closer in proof and more decisive for doubt, as he said to his al-Nas 114:This is my Lord (al-An’am 6:77) and This is my sister and Indeed, I am sick (Saffat: 89) and Rather, their chief did it. Ibn Al-Samiq read Rather, he did it with a shaddah on the lam, meaning perhaps the doer is their chief. Al-Kisa’i said that stopping at his statement: Rather, he did it means that he did it from his action, then he begins this chief of them. It was said: That is, why did they not deny that it was their chief’s action? This is an obligation with the wording of the report. Whoever believes in worshipping her must prove that she actually does it, and the meaning is: Rather, their greatest one did what you are required to do. Second: Al-Bukhari, Muslim, and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Prophet Abraham never lied about anything except three things: his saying, ‘I am sick,’ his saying to Sarah, my sister, and his saying, ‘Rather, their leader did it.’” The wording of Al-Tirmidhi. He said: A good and authentic hadith. It was mentioned in Al-Isra’ in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, in the story of Abraham. He said: He mentioned his statement in the Kawkab: This is my Lord. Based on this, the lies would be four, except that the Messenger, peace be upon him, denied those by saying: “The Prophet Abraham never lied except in three lies, two of which were about God, his statement: “I am sick” (37:89) and his statement: Rather, their elder did it, and one concerning Sarah.” The hadith is worded by Muslim. The reason for his statement in the Kawkab: This is my Lord not being considered a lie is because - and God knows best - he was in a state of childhood when he said that, and not in a state of accountability. Or he said it to his people, asking them in a way of rebuke and denial, and the question mark was deleted. Or as an argument against his al-Nas 114:to draw attention to the fact that what changes is not suitable for Lordship. All of these aspects have been presented in (Al-An’am), and praise be to God. Third: Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi said: In this hadith there is a great point that breaks the back, which is that he, peace be upon him, said: “Ibrahim did not lie except in three lies, two of which were about the religion of God and about his saying: ‘I am sick’ and his saying: ‘Rather, their chief did it’. He did not mention his saying ‘This is my sister’ in the name of God the Most High, even though he pushed her away in a way that was disliked. However, since Ibrahim, peace be upon him, had a share in it in protecting his bed and protecting his family, he did not make it in the name of God. This is because nothing is made in the name of God and His Self except the pure work free from the impurities of this world. The excuses that go back to the self if they are pure for the religion are for God the Most High, as He said: ‘Unquestionably, to God belongs pure religion’ (al-Zumar 39:3). If this had come from us, it would have been for God, but the status of Ibrahim required this. And God knows best. Fourth: Our scholars said: Lying is reporting something other than what it is. It is more apparent that what Abraham said in what he, peace be upon him, reported was from the metaphors, even if they were metaphors and good deeds and arguments in character and indications, but they affected the rank, and lowered Muhammad’s status and Abraham was ashamed of them, so he said them according to what was mentioned in the hadith of intercession, for the prophets fear what others do not fear out of reverence for God, for what was appropriate for his rank in prophethood and friendship was to proclaim the truth and declare the matter however it was, but he was given permission so he accepted the permission and what happened from the story happened, and for this reason it came in the hadith of intercession “I have only taken a friend from behind behind” with the accusative of behind in both of them on the construction like fifteen, and as they said: my neighbor house by house, and it occurred in some copies of Muslim from behind from behind with the repetition of from, and then it is not permissible to build on the fat-ha, but rather each one of them is built on the damma, because it is cut off from the addition and intended the added like before and after, and if he did not intend the added, it is parsed and the nun is not declined, because its alif is for the feminine, because they said in its diminutive And Rayyah, Al-Jawhari said: It is anomalous. Based on this, the fat-ha is valid in both of them with the presence of min in them. The meaning is that I was a friend who came after others. It is understood from this that the friendship was not valid in its entirety except for the one for whom the praiseworthy position was valid on that day, as mentioned above. And he is our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
21:64: The Almighty says: So they returned to themselves meaning they returned to each other as one who is cut off from his argument and is aware of the soundness of his opponent's argument. And they said, 'Indeed, you are the wrongdoers' meaning by worshipping someone who does not utter a word and does not control himself for a moment. How can he benefit his worshippers and ward off harm from them when he does not turn the axe away from his head?
21:65: The Almighty said: Then they lowered their heads meaning they returned to their ignorance and worship and said: You have certainly known that these do not speak.
21:66: So he said, cutting off what they were raving about and confounding them in what they were saying, Do you worship instead of God that which can neither benefit you nor harm you?
21:67: Fie upon you meaning the stench is upon you "and what you worship other than God. Will you not reason?" It was said: They lowered their heads meaning they bowed their heads in shame before Abraham, and there is a problem with that, because he did not say they lowered their heads with the opening of the kaf, but rather he said: They lowered their heads meaning they returned to what they were upon at the beginning, and Ibn Abbas said the same, he said: Misery overtook them so they returned to their disbelief.
21:68: The Almighty said: They said, 'Burn him.' When they were cut off from the argument, pride in sin took hold of them and they turned to the path of oppression and domination and said, Burn him. It was narrated that the one who said this statement was a man from the Kurds from the Bedouins of Persia, that is, from its desert, as stated by Ibn Omar, Mujahid, and Ibn Jurayj. It is said that his name was Hayzar, so God caused the earth to swallow him up, and he will be in it until the Day of Resurrection. It was also said that their king Nimrod said it. And support your gods by burning Abraham because he cursed and insulted them. It was reported that Nimrod built a tower that was eighty cubits long and forty cubits wide. Ibn Ishaq said: They collected firewood for a month and then lit it, and it burned and became intense, to the point that a bird would pass by its sides and be burned by the intensity of its blazing. Then they tied up Abraham and put him in the catapult, chained. It is said that Satan made the catapult for them that day. Then the heavens and the earth and all that is in them of angels and all creation, except the two heavy burdens, rang with one groan: Our Lord! Abraham, there is no one on earth who worships You except him, and he is burned in You, so give Us permission to help him. God the Almighty said: “If he seeks help from any of you or calls upon Me, then let him help him, for I have given him permission to do so. But if he does not call upon anyone other than Me, then I know him best and I am his Guardian.” When they wanted to throw him into the fire, the water-bearer came to him - who was in the air - and said: O Abraham, if you wish, we can put out the fire with water. He said: I have no need of you. The angel of the wind came to him and said: If you wish, you can blow away the fire. He said: No. Then he raised his head to the sky and said: “O God, You are the One in the heavens and I am the One on earth. No one worships You except me. God is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.” Ubayy ibn Ka’b may God be pleased with him narrated on the authority of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): “When Abraham was chained to be thrown into the fire, he said, ‘There is no god but You. Glory be to You, Lord of the worlds. To You be praise, and to You be dominion. You have no partner.’ Then they threw him into the catapult from a great distance. Gabriel met him and said, ‘O Abraham, do you have a need?’ He said, ‘As for you, no.’ Gabriel said, ‘Then ask your Lord.’ He said, ‘It is sufficient for me to ask that He knows my condition.’”
21:69: Then God, the Most High, said, and He is the most truthful of speakers: "O fire, be coolness and peace upon Abraham." Some scholars said: God made in it coolness to remove its heat, and heat to remove its coolness, so it became peace upon him. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: If He had not said "coolness and peace," its coolness would have been more severe upon him than its heat, and if He had not said upon Abraham, its coolness would have remained forever. Some scholars mentioned: God, the Most High, sent down a carpet from Paradise and spread it out in Hell, and God sent down angels: Gabriel, Michael, the Angel of Coolness, and the Angel of Safety. Ali and Ibn Abbas said: If its coolness had not been followed by peace, Abraham would have died from its coolness, and no fire remained that day except that it was extinguished. They thought that it meant him. Al-Suddi said: God commanded every branch of the tree to return to its tree and cast its fruit. Ka'b and Qatadah said: The fire did not burn Abraham except his bonds. So he remained in the fire for seven days and no one was able to approach the fire. Then they came and found him standing and praying. Al-Munhal bin Amr said that Ibrahim said: I have never been more comfortable than the days I was in the fire. Kaab, Qatada and Al-Zuhri said: On that day, there was no creature that did not put out the fire for him except the gecko, which used to blow on him. Therefore, the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) ordered it to be killed and named it Fuwaisqa. Shuaib Al-Hammani said: Ibrahim was thrown into the fire when he was sixteen years old. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibrahim was thrown into the fire when he was twenty-six years old. The first was mentioned by Al-Tha’labi and the second by Al-Mawardi, and God knows best. Al-Kalbi said: All the fires of the earth cooled while a leg was being cooked. Nimrod saw him from the palace sitting on the throne, comforting him, and the Angel of Shadows comforted him. He said: Yes, your Lord is an excellent Lord! I will sacrifice four thousand cows to him and he refrained from it.
21:70: The Almighty said: And they intended against him a plot meaning Nimrod and his companions intended to plot against him so We made them the greatest losers in their deeds, and We responded to their plot against them by empowering the weakest of Our creation. Ibn Abbas said: God empowered against them the weakest of His creation, the mosquito, and Nimrod did not stop until he saw the bones of his companions and horses looming, eating their flesh and drinking their blood, and one of them fell into his nostril and continued to eat until it reached his brain, and the most honorable of people to him was the one who struck his head with an iron pestle, and he remained like this for about four hundred years.
21:71: The Almighty said: And We saved him and Lot to the land which We blessed for the worlds. He means that We saved Abraham and Lot to the land of Ash-Sham, and they were in Iraq, and Abraham, peace be upon him, was his uncle, as Ibn Abbas said. It was said: It was blessed because of its abundant fertility, fruits, and rivers, and because it is the mines of the prophets. Blessing is the continuity of goodness, and from this comes the camel's kneeling when it remains in its place and does not move. Ibn Abbas said: The blessed land is Mecca. It was also said: Jerusalem, because God sent most of the prophets from it, and it is also abundant in fertility and growth, with sweet water, and from it it is dispersed in the earth. Abu Al-Aaliyah said: There is no sweet water except that it descends from the sky to the rock in Jerusalem, then it is dispersed in the earth. Ka'b Al-Ahbar said something similar. It was said: The blessed land is Egypt.
21:72: The Almighty says: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift meaning an addition, because he prayed for Isaac and Jacob was given an additional gift without a prayer, so it was an additional gift, meaning an addition to what he asked for, as he said: My Lord, grant me from among the righteous (Saffat: 100). A child's son is called an additional gift, because he is an addition to a son. And each of them We made righteous meaning that each of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob We made righteous and working in obedience to God. Making them righteous is only achieved by creating righteousness and obedience for them, and by creating the ability to obey, then whatever the servant acquires is created by God Almighty.
21:73: The Almighty said: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command. That is, leaders who are followed in good deeds and acts of obedience. The meaning of by Our command is what We sent down to them of revelation, commands, and prohibitions. It is as if He said they guide by Our Book. It was said: The meaning is they guide people to Our religion by Our command to them to guide creation and call them to monotheism. And We inspired in them the doing of good deeds that is, to do acts of obedience. And establishing prayer and giving zakah, and they were worshippers of Us that is, obedient.
21:74: The Almighty said: And to Lot We gave wisdom and knowledge. "Lot" is in the accusative case with an implied verb indicated by the second, meaning, and We gave Lot, We gave him. It was also said: meaning, remember Lot. Wisdom is prophethood, and knowledge is knowledge of the matter of religion and how judgment is made between opponents. It was also said: "Knowledge" is both, and the meaning is the same. "And We saved him from the city that was doing evil deeds" meaning Sodom. Ibn Abbas: There were seven cities, Gabriel, peace be upon him, changed six and left one for Lot and his family, and it is Zaghar, which has fruit from the region of Palestine to the border of Sarat, and it has many villages to the border of the Hijaz Sea. And regarding the evil deeds that they were doing, there are two opinions: One of them is: sodomy as mentioned above. The second is: flatulence, meaning they used to fart in their clubs and gatherings. It was also said: flatulence and the omission of pebbles, and it will come. "Indeed, they were an evil, wicked people" meaning they went against the obedience of God, and wickedness is going out, and this was mentioned above.
21:75: And We admitted him into Our mercy in prophecy. It was said: in Islam. It was said: Paradise. It was said: What he meant by mercy was his salvation from his people He is among the righteous.
21:76: The Almighty said: And Noah, when he called before meaning, remember Noah when he called, that is, he called. Before meaning before Abraham and Lot against his people, which is His saying: The disbelievers are a dwelling place (Nuh 71:26) and he said when they denied him: Indeed, I am overcome, so help (al-Qamar 54:10). So We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great distress meaning from drowning. Distress is intense grief and his family meaning the believers among them.
21:77: And We gave him victory over the people who denied Our signs. Abu Ubaidah said: From means on. It was also said: The meaning is: We took revenge for him from the people who denied Our signs. So We drowned them all, meaning the young and the old among them.
21:78: It contains twenty-six issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And David and Solomon when they gave judgment. That is, remember them when they gave judgment. The statement when they gave judgment did not mean that they both gave judgment together, even if they gave it together in speech, because two judges gave judgment on one judgment that is not permissible. Rather, each one of them gave judgment on his own, and Solomon was the one who understood it through God Almighty’s making him understand. In the tillage has two different opinions: It was said: It was a crop, as Qatadah said. It was said: A vineyard with clusters of grapes, as Ibn Masoud and Shuraih said. The tillage is said in both of them, and in the crop it is further from being a metaphor. Second: The Almighty’s saying: When the sheep of the people grazed therein meaning they grazed therein at night. Nafsh means grazing at night. It is said: Nafsha at night, and hamalt at day, if they grazed without a shepherd. And their owner made them nafsh. And camels are nafash. And in the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr: The seed in Paradise is like the belly of a camel that spends the night nafsh, meaning grazing. Narrated by Al-Harawi. Ibn Sidah said: The word hamal is not used for sheep, but rather it is used for camels. Third: The Almighty’s statement: And We were witnesses to their judgment is evidence that the minimum number of people in a group is two. It was said: What is meant are the two judges and the one being judged, and that is why He said to their judgment.
21:79: Fourth: The Almighty said: And We made Solomon understand it meaning He made him understand the issue and the ruling, so He referred to it as what indicated it had preceded. Solomon's ruling was superior to his father's ruling in that it ensured that each of them would keep his property, and his soul would remain content with that, and that is because David, peace be upon him, saw that he should give the sheep to the owner of the farm. A group said: Rather, he should give the sheep to the owner of the farm, and the farm to the owner of the sheep. Ibn Atiyyah said: According to one opinion, it is similar that he saw the sheep resisting the crop that was spoiled. According to the second opinion, he saw them resisting the crop and the harvest. So when the two opponents came out to Solomon, and he was sitting at the door from which the opponents exited, and they used to enter to David from another door, he said: What did the Prophet of God, David, rule between you? They said: He ruled that the sheep go to the owner of the farm. He said: Perhaps the ruling is not this, so go with me. So he came to his father and said: O Prophet of God, you ruled with such and such, and I saw what is more lenient for everyone. He said: What is it? He said: The sheep should be given to the owner of the farm, so that he may benefit from their milk, fat and wool, and the farm should be given to the owner of the sheep to take care of it. When the crop returns to the condition that the sheep had inflicted on it the following year, each of them should return his money to the other. David said: You have succeeded, my son, may God not cut off your understanding. And he ruled as Solomon had ruled. Ibn Masoud, Mujahid and others said the same meaning. Al-Kalbi said: David valued the sheep and the vineyard that the sheep had spoiled, so the two values were equal, so he gave the sheep to the owner of the vineyard. Al-Nahhas said the same. He said: He ruled that the sheep belonged to the owner of the farm, because their price was close to his. As for Solomon’s ruling, it has been said: The value of what he took from the sheep and the value of what the sheep spoiled were also equal. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: And to each of them We gave judgment and knowledge. Some people interpreted that David, peace be upon him, did not make a mistake in this incident, but rather he was given judgment and knowledge. They interpreted His statement: And We gave Solomon understanding of it as a virtue that he had over David, and his virtue goes back to David, and a father is pleased with his son’s superiority over him. A group said: Rather, it is because he did not hit the desired point in this incident, but God praised him because he had judgment and knowledge that could be referred to in other incidents. As for this, Solomon was right and David, peace be upon them, was wrong. It is not impossible for the prophets to make mistakes and errors as they do with others, but they are not approved of, even if others approve of them. When Al-Walid demolished the church of Damascus, the king of the Romans wrote to him: You have demolished the church that your father saw fit to leave. If you were right, your father was wrong, and if your father was right, you were wrong. Al-Walid replied: “And David and Solomon, when they gave judgment concerning the field, when the sheep of the people had pastured therein. And We were witnesses to their judgment. And We gave Solomon understanding of it. And to each of them We gave judgment and knowledge.” Some people said: David and Solomon, peace be upon them, were prophets who judged according to what was revealed to them. So David ruled by revelation, and Solomon ruled by revelation by which God abrogated David’s judgment. Based on this, And We gave Solomon understanding of it means by way of revelation that abrogates what was revealed to David, and Solomon ordered that it be conveyed to David. That is why he said: And to each of them We gave judgment and knowledge. This is the opinion of a group of scholars, including Ibn Furak. The majority said: Their judgment was based on independent reasoning, and it is: Sixth: Scholars differed about the permissibility of ijtihad for the prophets. Some people forbade it, while the scholars permitted it, because there is no rational impossibility in it, because it is a legal proof, so it is impossible for the prophets to use it as evidence, as if God the Almighty said to him: If you are convinced of such and such, then be certain that what you are convinced of is my ruling, and convey it to the nation, then this is not impossible in reason. If it is said: It is only evidence if there is no text, and they do not lack it. We say: If the angel did not descend, then the text is absent in their view, and they became like other mujtahids in searching for the meanings of the texts they have. The difference between them and other mujtahids is that they are infallible from error, mistake, and shortcoming in their ijtihad, while others are not like that. The majority also believed that all the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them, are infallible from error and mistake in their ijtihad. Abu Ali Ibn Abi Hurairah, one of the companions of Al-Shafi’i, said that our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was singled out from them in that it is permissible for them to make mistakes, and the difference between him and other prophets is that there was no one after him who could correct his mistakes, and for this reason God Almighty protected him from them, and after other prophets He sent someone to correct his mistakes. It has been said that it is general for all prophets, and that our Prophet and other prophets, may God bless them and grant them peace, are equal in permitting mistakes, except that they do not approve of his approval, so it was not considered in it that the prophets who came after them could correct it. “This is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a woman asked him about the waiting period, so he said to her: “Attack wherever you want,” then he said to her, Stay in your house until the deadline. A man said to him: Tell me, if I am killed patiently, hoping for reward, will anything prevent me from entering Paradise? He said: No. Then he called out and said: Except for debt. This is what Gabriel, peace be upon him, told me. Seventh: Al-Hasan said: If it were not for this verse, you would have seen the judges perishing, but God praised Solomon for his correctness and excused David for his diligence. People have differed regarding those who strive in branches of knowledge if they differed. A group said: The truth is with God in one aspect, and He has established evidence for that, and has made the diligent scholars search for it and look into it. Whoever finds the desired eye in the issue is absolutely correct, and he has two rewards: a reward for diligence and a reward for hitting the mark. Whoever does not find it is correct in his diligence but mistaken in that he did not hit the mark, so he has a reward and is not excused. So Solomon found the desired eye, which is what he understood. A group saw that the mistaken scholar is not sinful for his mistake even if he is not excused. A group said: The truth is with one aspect, and God did not establish evidence for it, but rather left the matter to the diligent scholars’ consideration. Whoever hits it is correct, and whoever errs is excused and rewarded. He is not worshipped for hitting the eye, but we are worshipped only by diligence. The majority of the Sunnis said, and this is what is preserved from Malik and his companions, may God be pleased with them: The truth in the issues of branches is in both sides, and every mujtahid is correct, and what is required is only what he thinks is best, and every mujtahid has led him to what he thinks is best. The evidence for this statement is that the companions and those who came after them decided that some of them disagreed with others, and none of them saw that it should be based on his statement without a statement of opposition. From this is Malik’s response, may God have mercy on him, to Al-Mansur Abu Ja’far about people basing their opinion on Al-Muwatta’. If a scholar says something permissible, then that is the truth, so what is specific to that scholar is with God Almighty and to everyone who takes his statement, and likewise in the opposite case. They said: Even if Solomon, peace be upon him, understood the ideal and most likely issue, then the first is not a mistake, and this is how they interpret his statement, peace be upon him: If a scholar makes an effort and makes a mistake, meaning he makes a mistake in what is best. Eighth: Muslim and others narrated on the authority of Amr ibn al-Aas that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “If a judge issues a ruling, exerting his own effort and getting it right, he will have two rewards. If he issues a ruling, exerting his own effort and getting it wrong, he will have one reward.” This is how the hadith is worded in the book of Muslim: If he issues a ruling, exerting his own effort. So he began with the ruling before exerting his own effort, and the matter is the opposite, for exerting his own effort takes precedence over the ruling, so it is not permissible to issue a ruling before exerting his own effort by consensus. Rather, the meaning of this hadith is: If he wants to issue a ruling, as he said: So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge with God (al-Nahl 16:98), then at that time he wants to exert his own effort in the case. This confirms what the scholars of the principles of jurisprudence said: The mujtahid must renew his consideration when a case occurs, and he should not rely on his previous ijtihad, because it is possible that something different from what appeared to him at first may appear to him a second time, unless he remembers the pillars of his ijtihad and is inclined towards it, in which case he does not need to resume his consideration based on another sign. Ninth: The reward is only for the erring ruler if he is knowledgeable in ijtihad, Sunnah, and analogy, and the judgments of those who came before him, because his ijtihad is an act of worship and he is not rewarded for the mistake, but rather the sin is removed from him only. As for the one who is not a place for ijtihad, he is a burdensome person and is not excused for making a mistake in the ruling, but rather he fears for it the greatest sin. This is indicated by his other hadith, narrated by Abu Dawud: Judges are three Hadith. Ibn al-Mundhir said: He is only rewarded for his effort in seeking the truth, not for his error. What supports this is the Almighty’s saying: And We gave it to Solomon 1:13. Al-Hasan said: He praised Solomon and did not criticize David. Tenth: Abu al-Tammam al-Maliki mentioned that Malik’s school of thought is that the truth lies in one of the opinions of the mujtahids, and not in the opinions of those who differ, and this is what most jurists said. He said: Ibn al-Qasim narrated that he asked Malik about the differences of opinion among the companions, and he said: There are those who are wrong and those who are right, and the truth is not in all of their opinions. It was said that this opinion is the well-known opinion of Malik, and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn agreed with it. Those who said this cited the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, and they said: It is a text that among the mujtahids and the judges there are those who are wrong and those who are right. They said: And the statement that every mujtahid is right leads to something being permissible or forbidden, and obligatory or recommended. The people of the first opinion cited the hadith of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called out to us on the day he returned from the Confederates: No one should pray the ‘Asr prayer except in Banu Qurayzah. Some people feared missing the time, so they prayed without Banu Qurayzah. The others said: “We will not pray except where the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded us, even if we miss the time.” He said: He did not rebuke either of the two groups. They said: “If one of the two groups had been mistaken, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would have specified him.” It could be said: Perhaps he was silent about specifying the mistaken ones because he was not sinful, but rather rewarded, so he did not need to specify him. And God knows best. The issue of ijtihad is long and complex, and this summary that we have mentioned is sufficient in the meaning of the verse, and God is the Grantor of success in guidance. Eleventh: Another section is related to the verse: which is the judge’s return after his judgment from his own ijtihad to another ijtihad that is more valid than the first, as David, peace be upon him, did that. Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, differed on that. Abdul Malik and Mutraf said in Al-Wadiha: He has that as long as he is in his position. However, if it is another position, he does not have that right, and he is like any other judge. This is the apparent statement of Malik, may God have mercy on him, in Al-Mudawwana. Sahnun said about his return from an ijtihad in which there is a statement to another that he sees as more valid, he does not have that right. Ibn Abdul Hakam said the same. They said: He resumes the judgment based on what he believes is stronger. Sahnun said: Unless he forgot what he believed was stronger at that time, or was mistaken and ruled based on something else, then he has the right to overturn it. However, if he ruled based on what he believed was stronger at that time, then something else became stronger after that, then there is no way to overturn the first ruling. Sahnun said this in his son’s book. Ashhab said in the book of Ibn Al-Mawaz: If his return to the most correct opinion is regarding money, then he has the right to annul the first opinion, but if it is regarding divorce, marriage, or emancipation, then he does not have the right to annul it. I said: The judge may retract his ruling if it becomes clear to him that the right belongs to someone else as long as he is in his position. And so it is in the letter of Umar to Abu Musa, may God be pleased with them both, narrated by Al-Daraqutni, and we have mentioned it in (Al-A'raf) without detailing it, and it is the evidence for the apparent statement of Malik. And the scholars did not differ that if the judge rules arbitrarily and contrary to the scholars, then it is rejected, even if it was based on ijtihad. But if a judge follows up on the ruling of another judge, then that is not permissible for him, because it is very harmful in terms of overturning rulings, replacing the lawful with the unlawful, and not adhering to the laws of Islam. And none of the scholars challenged the refutation of what the other narrated, but rather he ruled according to what appeared to him. Twelfth: Some people said: David, peace be upon him, did not carry out the ruling and it became clear to him what others said. Others said: He was not a ruling but rather a youth. I said: And this is how you interpret what Abu Hurairah narrated on his authority, peace be upon him, that he said: “While two women were with their sons, a wolf came and took the son of one of them. One of them said to her friend: He only took your son. The other said: He only took your son. They brought their case to David, and he ruled in favor of the elder. They went to Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them, and told him. He said: Bring me a knife so I can split him between you. The younger one said: No, may God have mercy on you, he is her son. So he ruled in favor of the younger one. Abu Hurairah said: I had never heard of a knife except on that day. We used to say nothing but a dagger.” Narrated by Muslim. As for the statement that this was from David, it is weak, because he was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his fatwa was a ruling. As for the other statement, it is far-fetched, because God Almighty said: When they gave judgment concerning the field, so He made clear that each one of them had already ruled. Likewise, His statement in the hadith: So he ruled in favor of the elder one, indicates the enforcement and accomplishment of the ruling. He who said: It was from the law of David that it should be ruled in favor of the older woman because she was older, is far from the truth, because older and younger are purely general in claims, like tall and short, black and white, and that does not necessitate giving preference to one of the litigants until a ruling is made for him or against him for that reason. This is one of the things that is decisive in understanding what the laws came with. What should be said is that David, peace be upon him, only ruled in favor of the older woman for a reason that required him to give preference to her statement. The hadith did not mention specifying it, as there was no need for it. It is possible that the child was in her hand, and he knew that the other was unable to provide evidence, so he ruled in her favor to keep what was as it was. This interpretation is the best that has been said about this hadith. It is what the rule of legal claims, in which the differences in laws are unlikely to be confirmed, testifies to. It is not said: If David ruled for a legitimate reason, then how was it permissible for Solomon to overturn his ruling? The answer is: Solomon, peace be upon him, did not overturn his father’s ruling, but rather he devised a clever trick that made the minor premise appear true to him, which is that when he said: Bring the knife, I will cut it between you, the minor premise said: No. So it became clear to him from the evidence of compassion in the minor premise, and the lack of it in the major premise, along with what may have been added to that from the evidence that he obtained knowledge of its truthfulness, so he ruled according to it. Perhaps he was one of those who were permitted to rule according to his knowledge. Al-Nasa’i translated this hadith as the ruling of the judge according to his knowledge. He also translated for him the latitude for the judge to say to something that he does not do, do it, so that the truth may be made clear. He also translated for him the overturning of the judge, which no one else, who is like him or more important than him, can rule according to. Perhaps the elder sister acknowledged that the child was for the younger sister when she saw Solomon’s firmness and seriousness in that, so he ruled that the child was for the younger sister. This would be like if the judge ruled by oath, and when he went to swear, someone came who extracted from the wrongdoing what required his admission, then he would be ruled on by that admission before and after the oath, and this would not be a case of overturning the first ruling, but rather a case of changing rulings according to the change of causes. And God knows best. In this hadith there is jurisprudence that the prophets were permitted to rule by ijtihad, and we have mentioned it. In it there is jurisprudence that the judges use tricks by which rights are extracted, and this is through the strength of intelligence and cleverness, and practicing the conditions of creation, and there may be religious insight and luminous foresight in the people, and this is the grace of God which He gives to whomever He wills. In it there is evidence for those who say that the mother is to be attributed, and this is not the well-known Maliki school of thought, and this is not the place to mention it. In short, Solomon’s ruling in this story is included in His praise of him in His saying: So We made Solomon understand it. Thirteenth: We have already discussed the issue of cultivation and the ruling in this incident in our Sharia: that the owners of the walls must protect their walls and crops during the day, then guarantee the like for the like, and the value for the valuable. The basis for this issue in our Sharia is “what our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ruled regarding the she-camel of Al-Bara’ bin Azib. It was narrated by Malik on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Haram bin Sa’d bin Muhaysa: “A she-camel belonging to Al-Baraa entered a man’s garden and caused damage to it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ruled that the people of the gardens must guard them at night, and that the people responsible for what the livestock cause at night are responsible for.” This is how all the narrators narrated it without a chain of transmission. The companions of Ibn Shihab also narrated it from Ibn Shihab, except Ibn Uyaynah, who narrated it from Al-Zuhri from Saeed and Haram bin Saad bin Muhaysah: that a she-camel, and he mentioned something similar with the same meaning. Ibn Abi Dhi’b narrated it from Ibn Shihab that he had heard that Al-Baraa’s she-camel entered a people’s garden, just like the hadith of Malik, except that he did not mention Haram bin Saad bin Muhaysah or anyone else. Abu Umar said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b did nothing, except that he corrupted its chain of transmission. Abd Al-Razzaq narrated it from Muammar from Al-Zuhri from Haram bin Muhaysah from his father from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and Abd Al-Razzaq did not follow him in that and they denounced his statement from his father. It was narrated by Ibn Jurayj on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hanif told me that a she-camel entered the garden of some people and caused damage. So he attributed the hadith to Ibn Shihab on the authority of Abu Umamah, and he did not mention that the she-camel belonged to Al-Baraa. It is possible that the hadith is on the authority of Ibn Shihab on the authority of Ibn Muhaysah, and on the authority of Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab, and on the authority of Abu Umamah - and God knows best - so he narrated it on the authority of whomever he wanted from them according to what he had, and they are all trustworthy. Abu Umar said: Even though this hadith is mursal, it is a well-known hadith that was mursal by the imams, and trustworthy people narrated it, and the jurists of Hijaz used it and accepted it, and it was practiced in Madinah, and it is sufficient for you that the people of Madinah and all the people of Hijaz used this hadith. Fourteenth: Malik and the majority of the imams held that the hadith of al-Bara’ was correct, and Abu Hanifa and his companions and a group of the Kufians held that this ruling was abrogated, and that if animals spoil crops during the night or day, their owner is not obligated to do anything, and their spoilage was included in the generality of his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace: The wound of a dumb animal is a compensation. So he based all its actions on its wound. It is said that no one preceded Abu Hanifa with this statement, and there is no proof for him or for those who followed him in the hadith of the dumb animal, and its abrogation of the hadith of Al-Baraa’ and opposition to it, because the conditions of abrogation are non-existent, and the conflict is only valid if one of them cannot be used except by negating the other. The hadith The wound of a dumb animal is a compensation is a generality agreed upon, then he made crops and walls specific to it with the hadith of Al-Baraa’, because if it had come from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in one hadeeth: The wound of a dumb animal is a compensation during the day and not at night, and in crops, walls and tillage, this would not have been impossible to say, so how can it be said that this is a conflict?! Rather, this is from the category of generality and specificity according to what is mentioned in the principles. Fifteenth: If it is said: What is the wisdom in the Lawgiver separating night and day, and Al-Layth bin Sa’d said: The owners of livestock are responsible for everything that is spoiled by night and day, but they are not responsible for more than the value of the livestock? We say: The difference between them is clear, and that is that the owners of livestock have a need to send their livestock to graze during the day, and most of them are those who have crops to tend to them during the day and protect them from whoever wants them, so he made the preservation of that during the day the responsibility of the owners of the crops, because it is the time for dealing with livelihood, as God Almighty said: And We have made the day for livelihood (An-Naba’: 11). So when night comes, the time has come for everything to return to its place and rest, as God Almighty said: Is there a god other than God who can bring you a night in which you can rest? (al-Qasas 28:72) and He said: And He has made the night for rest (al-An’am 6:96). The owners of livestock return their livestock to their places to protect them, so if the owner of the livestock is negligent in returning them to his home, or is negligent in controlling them and preventing them from spreading out at night until they are ruined, Something, so he has to guarantee it, so the ruling was based on what was more appropriate and lenient, and that was kinder to both parties, easier for both groups, and more protective of the money, and the morning has become clear to the one with two eyes, but to the one with sound senses, and as for the saying of Al-Layth: He does not guarantee more than the value of the livestock, Abu Omar said: I do not know where Al-Layth bin Saad said this, except that he makes it an analogy to the slave who commits a crime, who does not kill for more than his value, and his master is not obligated for his crime for more than his value, and this is weak in face, as he said in Al-Tamhid and in Al-Istidhkar, so he contradicted the hadith in The wound of the dumb woman is compensated and contradicted the she-camel of Al-Bara, and a group of scholars preceded him in that, including Ata’. Ibn Jurayj said: I said to Ata’: The crop is damaged by livestock at night or during the day? He said: Its owner guarantees and pays. I said: Was there a prohibition on him or not? He said: Yes! He pays. I said: What does he pay? He said: The value of what his donkey, beast, and livestock ate. Muammar said on the authority of Ibn Shabramah: The crop is valued in the state in which it was damaged in dirhams. It was narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab and Omar bin Abdul Aziz, may God be pleased with them: The owner of the livestock is responsible for it day or night, through chains of transmission that are not authentic. Sixteenth: Malik said: The crops that livestock ruined at night are based on hope and fear. He said: The walls that are guarded and those that are not guarded, and the forbidden and the unforbidden are the same, their owners are liable for what they damaged at night, no matter how much, even if it is more than their value. He said: If an animal gets loose at night and steps on a sleeping man, its owner is not liable for anything, but this only applies to walls, crops, and plowing. Ibn Abd al-Hakam mentioned this from him. Ibn al-Qasim said: What livestock ruined at night is from the owner’s money, even if it is multiples of its price, because the crime is from him since he did not tie it up, and the rams are not like slaves. Sahnun, Asbagh, and Abu Zaid narrated this from Ibn al-Qasim. Seventeenth: It is not necessary to consider whether the crop will grow or not, as is done with a young child. Isa said on the authority of Ibn al-Qasim: Its value would be if its sale were permissible. Ashab and Ibn Nafi’ said in al-Majmu’ah on his authority: Even if its goodness is not apparent. Ibn al-Arabi: The first is stronger because it is its quality, so it is evaluated as every spoiled thing is evaluated according to its quality. Eighteenth: If the one who caused the damage was not judged to have anything until it grew and was repaired, then if there was a benefit in it before that, such as grazing or something, he is liable for that benefit. But if there was no benefit in it, then there is no liability. Asbagh said: He is liable, because the damage has been realized and the repair is not from his side, so it is not taken into account. Nineteenth: It was mentioned in the book of Ibn Sahnun that the hadith only came in the case of cities that are surrounded by walls. As for countries that are connected crops that are not enclosed, and orchards as well, the owners of the livestock are responsible for what they spoil during the night or day. It is as if he went to the point that leaving the training of animals in such countries is a crime, because they will inevitably spoil. This is a deviation from the statement of Al-Layth. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth: Asbagh said in Madinah: It is not for the owners of livestock to take their livestock out to the villages of cultivation without a guard. The scholars based this on the fact that the area is either a cultivated area or a pasture area. If it is a cultivated area, then livestock are not allowed to enter it except for what is invasive and is upon their owners to protect it, and what they spoil, their owner is responsible for night or day. If it is a pasture area, then the owner who plowed it in it is responsible for protecting it, and there is nothing upon the owners of the livestock. Twenty-first: Livestock are divided into two types: predators and guards. Malik divided them into two types. Predatory livestock are those that are accustomed to crops and fruits. Malik said: They are to be removed and sold in a country where there is no crops. This was narrated by Ibn al-Qasim in al-Kitab and others. Ibn Habib said: Even if its owner dislikes that. Malik said the same about an animal that is harmful and destroys crops: They are to be removed and sold. As for what can be avoided, its owner is not ordered to remove it. Twenty-second: Asbagh said: Bees, pigeons, geese, and chickens are like livestock. Their owners are not prevented from keeping them even if they cause harm. The people of the village must protect their crops. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is a weak narration that should not be paid attention to. Whoever wants to find something that benefits him from that does not harm others will be able to do so. As for benefiting from what he keeps by harming someone, there is no way to do so. He, peace be upon him, said: No harm nor reciprocating harm. According to Ibn al-Qasim, these wild animals in Medina are not subject to any liability on their owners except after advance notice. Ibn al-Arabi: I see that they are liable before advance notice if they are wild animals. Twenty-third: Abd al-Razzaq reported on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada on the authority of al-Sha’bi that a sheep fell into a weaver’s yarn, so they brought their dispute to Shuraih. Al-Sha’bi said: Wait for him, for he will ask them whether it fell at night or during the day. So he did. Then he said: If it was at night, he is liable, but if it was during the day, he is not liable. Then Shuraih recited: When the sheep of the people were scattered therein. He said: The sweeping is at night and the caressing is during the day. I said: And from this chapter is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The wound of a dumb animal is a compensation, the hadith. Ibn Shihab said: The compensation is the waste, and the dumb animal is the beast. Our scholars said: The apparent meaning of his saying: The wound of a dumb animal is a compensation, is that what the beast alone destroys is not a penalty, and this is agreed upon. So if there is a guide, driver, or rider with it and one of them loads it onto something and it destroys it, then the ruling on the destroyer is applicable to him. If it was a crime that is guaranteed by retaliation and the loading was intentional, then retaliation is applicable and there is no difference of opinion about it, because the beast is like a tool. If it was unintentional, then the blood money is on the agnatic group. And in the case of money, there is a fine for the money. Twenty-fourth: They differed about the one who was struck by her leg or tail. Malik, Al-Layth, and Al-Awza’i did not guarantee its owner, but Al-Shafi’i, Ibn Abi Layla, and Ibn Shabrama guaranteed him. They differed about the wild animal, so the majority of them said that it is like any other animal, but Malik and some of his companions guaranteed him. Twenty-fifth: Sufyan bin Hussein narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The man is a tyrant. Ad-Daraqutni said: Only Sufyan ibn Husayn narrated it, and he was not followed in it. The hadith masters of Az-Zuhri disagreed with him, including Malik, Ibn Uyaynah, Yunus, Muammar, Ibn Jurayj, Az-Zubaidi, Uqayl, Layth ibn Sa`d, and others. They all narrated it from Az-Zuhri and said: The mute animal is a tyrant, the well is a tyrant, and the mine is a tyrant. They did not mention the man, which is correct. Likewise, Abu Salih As-Samman, Abd Ar-Rahman Al-A`rad, Muhammad ibn Sirin, Muhammad ibn Ziyad, and others narrated from Abu Hurayrah, and they did not mention the man is a tyrant, which is what is preserved from Abu Hurayrah. Twenty-sixth: His saying: And the well is a tyrant. Its location has been narrated. And the fire. Ad-Daraqutni said: Hamza bin Al-Qasim Al-Hashemi told us, Hanbal bin Ishaq told us: I heard Abu Abdullah Ahmad bin Hanbal say regarding the hadith of Abd Al-Razzaq: The hadith of Abu Hurairah And the fire is a tyrant is nothing, it was not in the books, it is false, it is not authentic. Muhammad bin Mukhallad told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Hani’ told us: I heard Ahmad bin Hanbal say: The people of Yemen write the fire as the well and they write the well, meaning something like that. And Abd Al-Razzaq was taught The fire is a tyrant. Al-Ramadi said: Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar said: I do not see it except as a mistake. Abu Omar said: The hadith of Muammar was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Hammam bin Munabbih from Abu Hurairah from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The fire is a tyrant. Yahya bin Ma’in said: Its original meaning is the well, but Muammar corrupted it. Abu Omar said: Ibn Ma'in did not provide evidence for what he said, and this is not how the hadiths of trustworthy people are transmitted. Wakee' reported on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Husain on the authority of Yahya bin Yahya Al-Ghassani, who said: A man burned his camel, and a spark of fire came out and burned something of his neighbor's. He said: So Ibn Husain wrote about it to Omar bin Abdul Aziz may God be pleased with him, and he wrote to me that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: The dumb animal is a tyrant, and I think that fire is a tyrant. It was narrated: And the grazing animal is a tyrant instead of the dumb animal. This is what was reported in the wording of this hadith, and for each meaning there is a correct wording mentioned in the explanation of the hadith and books of jurisprudence. God the Almighty said: And We subjected the mountains with David, to glorify God. Wahb said: David would pass by the mountains glorifying God and the mountains would respond to him with glorification, and so would the birds. It was also said: When David felt a lull, he would command the mountains and they would glorify God until he yearned. That is why He said: And We subjected meaning that We made them obey him when he commanded them to glorify God. It was also said: Their movement with him was their glorification, and glorification is taken from swimming, the evidence for which is the Almighty’s statement: O mountains, echo with him (Saba’ 34:10). Qatada said: Glorifying God means praying with him when he prayed, and glorification is prayer. Both are possible. This is what God the Almighty did to them, because the mountains do not have reason, so their glorification is evidence of God’s transcendence from the attributes of the helpless and the created.
21:80: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And We taught him the making of coats of mail for you. Meaning, making armor with iron for it. And among the Arabs, clothing means all weapons, whether it be a coat of mail, a shield, a sword, or a spear. Al-Hudhali said, describing a spear: I have a garment for the wretched, like silk on the forehead of a frightened sheep. Clothes are everything that is worn. Ibn Al-Sikkit recited: Dress for each situation according to its own clothes, either its blessings or its misery. God Almighty meant here the armor, which means something worn, such as riding and milking. Qatada said: The first person to make armor was David. It was only plates, so he was the first to string and shave it. Second: The Almighty’s saying: To fortify you, to protect you. “From your strength” meaning from your war. It was also said: From the sword, arrow, and spear, meaning from the tools of your strength, so the complement was omitted. Ibn Abbas: From your strength from your weapons. Ad-Dahhak: From the war of your enemies. The meaning is the same. Al-Hasan, Abu Jaafar, Ibn Amir, Hafs, and Ruh read to fortify you with the ta’ in response to the description. It was also said: On the clothing and protection which is the armor. Shaibah, Abu Bakr, Al-Mufaddal, Ruways, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read to fortify you with the nun because of His saying: And We taught it. The rest read with the ya’, making the verb for the clothing, or the meaning is that God fortifies you. Are you then grateful? meaning for making the blessing of armor easy for you. It was also said: Are you then grateful by obeying My Messenger. Third: This verse is the basis for adopting crafts and means, and it is the saying of the people of reason and intelligence, not the saying of the ignorant fools who say that this was only legislated for the weak. The reason is the law of God in His creation. Whoever challenges this has challenged the Book and the Sunnah, and attributed what we mentioned to weakness and lack of grace. God the Almighty has informed us about His Prophet David, peace be upon him, that he used to make armor, and he also used to make palm leaves, and he used to eat from the work of his hand. Adam was a farmer, Noah was a carpenter, Luqman was a tailor, and Saul was a tanner. It was said: a water carrier. Thus, craftsmanship is what keeps a person from people, and wards off harm and distress from himself. In the hadith: God loves the weak, self-restrained, professional believer, and hates the importunate beggar. This will be further explained in Surat Al-Furqan. It has been mentioned previously in more than one verse, and it is sufficient, praise be to God.
21:81: The Almighty said: And to Solomon was the wind, blowing violently. That is, We subjected to Solomon the wind, blowing violently. It is said: the wind blew, meaning it became strong, so it is a violent and violent wind. In the language of Banu Asad: the wind blew, so it is a violent and violent wind. As-saf is straw, so the strong wind was named after it, because it blows it violently and flies. Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, al-Salami, and Abu Bakr read And to Solomon was the wind, raising the ha' as a break from what preceded it, and the meaning is, and to Solomon was subjected to the wind, as subject and predicate. It runs by his command to the land which We have blessed, meaning the Levant. It is narrated that it used to run with him and his companions to wherever he wanted, then return him to the Levant. Wahb said: When Solomon, son of David, went out to his council, the birds would gather around him, and the jinn and humans would stand up for him until he sat on his throne. He was a man of war who would not stop from war. When he wanted to wage war, he would order wood to be stretched out and people, beasts, and grain equipment to be hoisted onto it. Then he would order a storm to lift it up. Then he would order a soft wind to blow it away, and it would pass by him for a month in the evening and a month in the morning. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: They flow by His command, gently, wherever He wills. (Sad: 36) Soft wind means gentleness. And We are Knowing of all things. That is, of all things We do, knowing of His management.
21:82: God the Almighty says: And among the devils are those who dive for him meaning, We subjected to him those who dive, meaning under the water. That is, they extract gems for him from the sea. Diving is going under the water, and he dived into the water. The one who attacks something is a diver. The diver is the one who dives in the sea for pearls, and his action is diving. And they do work less than that meaning other than that of diving, said Al-Farra'. It was said: What is meant by that are the niches, statues, and other things that he subjects them to. And We were their guardians meaning their deeds. Al-Farra' said: Guardians for them from corrupting their deeds, or provoking any of the children of Adam in the time of Solomon. It was said: Guardians from fleeing or refusing. Or We protected them from going against his command. It was said: The bath, lime, mills, bottles, and soap are from the extraction of devils.
21:83: God the Almighty said: "And Job, when he called upon his Lord." That is, remember Job when he called upon his Lord. "Verily, adversity has touched me." That is, adversity has befallen me in my body, in my wealth, and in my family. Ibn Abbas said: He was called Job because he was a great supporter of God the Almighty in every situation. It was narrated that Job, peace be upon him, was a Roman man of great wealth. He was pious, God-fearing, and merciful to the poor. He took care of orphans and widows, honored guests, and delivered the message to travelers, grateful for God's blessings. He entered with his people upon a great tyrant, so they spoke to him about his situation. Job began to speak softly to him because of the crops he had. So God tested him by taking away his wealth and family, and by causing harm to his body until his flesh was scattered and worms began to grow in his body, until the people of his village expelled him outside the village, and his wife used to serve him. Al-Hasan said: He remained like that for nine years and six months. When God wanted to relieve him, He said to him: Strike with your foot; this is a spring of cool water to wash and a drink (Sad: 42) in it is your healing, and I have given you your family, wealth, children, and the like thereof with them. And in (Sad) we will come what the commentators have to say about the story of Job regarding the devil’s control over him, and the response to them, God willing. There are fifteen opinions regarding Job’s statement: Harm has touched me: The first: He jumped up to pray but was unable to get up, so he said: Harm has touched me, informing about his condition, not complaining about his affliction. Anas narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. The second: It is an admission of inability, so it was not contrary to patience. The third: He, the Almighty, made it appear on his tongue to be an argument for those afflicted after him to disclose what had befallen them. The fourth: He made it appear on his tongue to oblige the human being to be weak in bearing affliction. The fifth: Revelation was cut off from him for forty days, so he feared his Lord’s abandonment, so he said: Harm has touched me. This is the opinion of Ja’far ibn Muhammad. Sixth: His students who used to write about him, when his condition led to what it led to, erased what they had written about him, and said: This has no value with God. So he complained of the harm caused by the revelation and religion being lost from the hands of the people. This is something whose chain of transmission is not authentic. And God knows best, as Ibn al-Arabi said. Seventh: A worm fell from his flesh, so he picked it up and put it back in its place, but it bit him, so he cried out, Harm has touched me. It was said, Can you be patient with us? Ibn al-Arabi said: This is very far-fetched, although it requires a sound narration, and there is no way to find it. Eighth: The worms were eating his body, so he was patient until one worm ate his heart and another his tongue, so he said, Harm has touched me, because he was busy with the remembrance of God. Ibn al-Arabi said: How good this would be if it had a chain of transmission and was not a broad claim. Ninth: He made it ambiguous to him as to the direction in which the affliction befell him, whether it was discipline, torture, specialization, testing, provision, or purification, so he said, Harm has touched me, meaning harm. The ambiguity is regarding the direction in which the affliction befell him. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is an unnecessary exaggeration. Tenth: It was said to him: Ask God for well-being. He said: I lived in bliss for seventy years and I lived in affliction for seven years, and then I asked Him. He said: Harm has touched me. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is possible, but there is no authentic report about his stay for a period of time, nor about this story. Eleventh: His harm was the saying of Satan to his wife: Prostrate to me. He feared that her faith would be lost and she would perish and he would be left without a guarantor. Twelfth: When the affliction appeared to him, his people said: He has made us angry and disgusted with him, so let him leave us. So his wife took him out to the outskirts of the town. Whenever they went out, they would see him and take him as a bad omen and they would be pessimistic about seeing him. They said: Let him go far away where we cannot see him. So he went out to a distance from the town, and his wife would take care of him and carry his food to him. They said: She is taking him and mixing with us, and because of him his harm will return to us. So they wanted to cut her off from him, but he said: Harm has touched me. Thirteenth: Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair said: Job had two brothers who came to him and stood from a distance, unable to approach him because of his foul odor. One of them said: If God had known any good in Job, He would not have afflicted him with this affliction. He had not heard anything more severe for him than this word. At that point, he said: Harm has touched me. Then he said: O God, if You know that I have never slept full while I know where someone is hungry, then grant me the truth. Then a voice from the heaven called out: My servant has spoken the truth, and they were both listening, proud and prostrating. Fourteenth: The meaning of harm has touched me is the gloating of enemies. That is why he was asked: What was more severe for you in your affliction? He said: The gloating of enemies. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is possible, because the brother of Moses asked him for well-being from that, and he said: The people considered me weak and almost killed me, so do not let the enemies gloat over me. (al-A’raf 7:150) Fifteenth: His wife had locks of hair, so when she was prevented from doing anything to anyone because of him, she knew what would happen to him, so she cut off her locks of hair and bought food with them from someone who would provide for her and brought it to him. He used her locks to help him with his activities and movements, but when he did not have them and wanted to move around, he was unable to, so he said: Harm has touched me. It was said: When she bought food with her locks, Satan came to him in the guise of a man and said to him: If your family is unjust, then I will seize you and shave her hair. So Job swore that he would flog her, so the trial on the woman’s heart was more severe than the trial on Job’s heart. I said: And the sixteenth statement: It was mentioned by Ibn al-Mubarak: Yunus bin Yazid informed us on the authority of Aqeel on the authority of Ibn Shihab, “that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned one day the Prophet Job, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what afflicted him of affliction, the hadith. And in it: that some of his brothers who were patient with him and were with him said: O Prophet of God, I am amazed by your matter and I mentioned it to your brother and companion, that He has afflicted you with the loss of your family and wealth and in your body, for eighteen years until you reached what you see, will He not have mercy on you and relieve you! You have committed a sin that I do not think anyone has reached! Job, peace be upon him, said: ((I do not know what they are saying except that my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, knows that I used to pass by two men arguing and each one swearing by God - or by a group arguing - so I would return to my family and expiate for their oaths, intending that no one who mentioned Him would sin and no one would mention Him except in truth)) So he called upon his Lord, “Indeed, distress has afflicted me and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.” And his supplication was only a presentation that he presented to God, the Blessed and Exalted. He tells him what has reached him, patient for what is from God, the Blessed and Most High, in it.” And he mentioned the hadith. And the seventeenth statement: I heard it, but I did not find it, that a worm fell from his body, so he sought it to return it to its place, but he did not find it, so he said: Harm has touched me, because he lost the reward for the pain of that worm, and he wanted the reward to remain for him until the time of recovery, and this is good, except that it needs a chain of transmission. The scholars said: His saying Harm has touched me was not impatience, because God, the Most High, said: Indeed, We found him patient (Sad: 44), rather it was a supplication from him, and impatience is in complaining to creation, not to God, the Most High, and supplication does not contradict contentment. Al-Tha’labi said: I heard our teacher Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib say: I attended a gathering filled with jurists and men of letters in the Sultan’s palace, so I was asked about this verse after their consensus that the statement of Job was a complaint, and God, the Most High, said: Indeed, We found him patient (Sad: 44)
21:84: I said: This is not a complaint, but rather a supplication, its explanation is So We answered him, and the answer follows the supplication, not the complaint. So they approved of it and were pleased with it. Al-Junayd was asked about this verse, and he said: He made him aware of the need of the questioner in order to bestow upon him the generosity of giving. God the Almighty said: So We removed the affliction that was upon him, and We gave him his family and the like thereof with them. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: It was said to Job, peace be upon him: We have given you your family in Paradise. If you wish, We will leave them for you in Paradise, and if you wish, We will give them to you in this world. Mujahid said: So God the Almighty left them for him in Paradise and gave him the like thereof in this world. An-Nahhas said: The chain of transmission on their authority is sound. I said: Al-Mahdawi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ad-Dahhak said: Abdullah bin Masoud said: The people of Job had died except for his wife, so God Almighty revived them in less than the blink of an eye, and gave him the same number along with them. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas also: His sons had died, so they were revived for him, and he had children the same number along with them. And Qatada, Ka’b al-Ahbar, Al-Kalbi, and others said the same. Ibn Masoud said: His children died, and they were seven males and seven females, and when he recovered, they were resurrected for him, and his wife gave birth to seven sons and seven daughters. Al-Tha’labi: This statement is more similar to the apparent meaning of the verse. I said: Because they died as a test before their appointed times, as was explained in Surah Al-Baqarah in the story of those who left their homes, thousands in number, for fear of death (al-Baqarah 2:243). And in the story of the seventy who were struck by the thunderbolt and died and then were brought back to life, that is because they died before their appointed times, and likewise here, and God knows best. According to the saying of Mujahid and Ikrimah, the meaning is: And We gave him his family in the Hereafter, and the like of them with them in this world. And in al-Naba 78:God sent Gabriel, peace be upon him, to him when he kicked the ground with his foot and a spring of hot water appeared, and he took his hand and shook it and the worms scattered from it, and he dived into the water and his flesh grew and he returned to his home, and God returned his family to him and the like of them with them, and a cloud arose the size of the foundations of his house and rained golden locusts for three days and nights. Gabriel said to him: Are you satisfied? He said: And who is satisfied with God! Surplus. God revealed to him: I have praised you for your patience before and after you fell into the affliction. Had I not placed patience under every hair of yours, you would not have been patient. A mercy from Us means We did this to him as a mercy from Us. It was also said: We tested him so that his reward would be great tomorrow. And a reminder for the worshippers means and a reminder for the worshippers, because if they remember Job’s affliction, his patience with it, and his trial of him, even though he was the best of the people of his time, they will prepare themselves to be patient with the hardships of this world, as Job did. This will be a reminder to them to continue worshipping and to endure harm. There is a difference of opinion regarding the duration of his stay in the affliction. Ibn Abbas said: The duration of the affliction was seven years, seven months, seven days, and seven nights. Wahb said: Thirty years. Al-Hasan said: Seven years and six months. I said: And what is more correct than this, and God knows best, is eighteen years. It was narrated by Ibn Shihab from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it was mentioned by Ibn al-Mubarak and it was mentioned earlier.
21:85: The Almighty said: And Ishmael and Idris who is Enoch and it was mentioned before and Dhul-Kifl meaning remember them. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim included in Nawader Al-Usul and others from the hadith of Ibn Umar on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There was a man among the Children of Israel called Dhul-Kifl who did not hesitate to commit a sin. He pursued a woman and gave her sixty dinars on condition that he would have intercourse with her. When he sat with her as a man sits with his wife, she trembled and wept. He said: ‘What makes you weep?’ She said: ‘Because of this deed, by God I have never done it.’ He said: ‘Did I force you?’ She said: ‘No, but need drove me to do it.’ He said: ‘Go, it is yours. By God, I will never disobey God after this.’ Then he died that night. They found written on the door of his house: ‘God has forgiven Dhul-Kifl.’” Abu ‘Isa al-Tirmidhi also included it. Its wording is: “On the authority of Ibn ‘Umar, may God be pleased with them both, he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrate a hadith. If I had only heard it once or twice - until he counted seven times - I would not have narrated it. But I heard it more than that. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Dhul-Kifl was from the Children of Israel and did not hesitate to commit a sin. A woman came to him and he gave her sixty dinars on condition that he would have intercourse with her. When he sat down with her as a man sits with his wife, she trembled and wept. He said: What makes you weep? Did I force you? She said: No, but he did something I had never done before and nothing made me do it except need. He said: You are doing this and what I did, go, it is yours. He said: By God, I will never disobey God after that. He died that night and in the morning it was written on his door: “God has forgiven Dhul-Kifl.” He said: A good hadith. It was said that when Al-Yasa’ grew old, he said: If I appointed a man as a successor over the people so that I may see how he acts. He said: Who will guarantee me three things: fasting during the day, praying at night, and not getting angry while he is making up the debt? A man from the descendants of Esau said: I will. He turned him away, then he said the same thing the next day. The man said: I will. He appointed him as a successor and he fulfilled it, so God praised him and he was called Dhul-Kifl because he undertook a matter. This was stated by Abu Musa, Mujahid, and Qatadah. Amr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith said: Abu Moses narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Dhul-Kifl was not a prophet, but he was a righteous servant who took responsibility for the work of a righteous man when he died. He used to pray to God one hundred times a day, so God praised him well every one hundred times. Kaab said: There was a disbelieving king among the Children of Israel, and a righteous man passed by his country and said: By God, if I leave this country, I will offer Islam to this king.
