So he offered it to him and he said: What is my reward? He said: Paradise - and he described it to him - He said: Who will guarantee that for me? He said: I will. So the king converted to Islam and gave up the kingdom and devoted himself to obeying his Lord until he died. He was buried and in the morning they found his hand coming out of the grave and on it was a green note written in white light: God has forgiven me and admitted me to Paradise and fulfilled the guarantee of so-and-so. The people rushed to that man to take faith from them and guarantee them what he had promised the king. So he did that and they all believed and he was called Dhul-Kifl. It was said: He was a chaste man who would take care of every person who fell into a calamity, accusation or claim, and God would save him through his hands. It was also said: He was called Dhul-Kifl because God Almighty took care of his efforts and work twice as much as the work of any other prophet who was in his time. The majority are of the opinion that he was not a prophet. Al-Hasan said: He was a prophet before Elijah. It was also said: He was Zachariah under the care of Mary. Everyone is among the patient meaning upon the command of God and performing His obedience and avoiding His disobedience.
21:86: And We admitted them into Our mercy meaning into Paradise for they are among the righteous.
21:87: The Almighty said: And Dhul-Nun meaning, remember Dhul-Nun, which is a nickname for Yunus bin Matta because the nun swallowed him. The nun is the whale. In the hadith of Uthman, may God be pleased with him, he saw a handsome boy and said: Blacken his nun so that the evil eye will not harm him. Tha'lab narrated on the authority of Ibn al-A'rabi: The nun is the blemish that is on the chin of a young boy, and the meaning of blacken is to make it black. When he went away in anger Al-Hasan, Al-Sha'bi, and Saeed bin Jubayr said: Angry for his Lord, the Almighty. Al-Tabari and Al-Qutbi chose it, and Al-Mahdawi approved of it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud. Al-Nahhas said: Perhaps someone who does not know the language would deny this, but it is a correct statement. The meaning is: Angry for the sake of his Lord, as you say: I became angry for you, meaning for your sake. The believer becomes angry for the sake of God, the Almighty, if he disobeys. Most linguists say that "the Prophet's saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Aisha: Make a condition of loyalty to them" is from this. Al-Qutbi went to extremes in supporting this statement. In the report describing Yunus 10:He was narrow-chested, but when he carried the burdens of prophethood, he collapsed under them as a quarter collapses under a heavy load, so he went on his way like a runaway. This anger was small. He was not angry with God, but he was angry for God when He lifted the punishment from them. Ibn Masoud said: He ran away from his Lord, meaning from the command of his Lord until He commanded him to return to them after the punishment was lifted from them, for he was threatening his people with the descent of the punishment at a specific time, and he left them at that time, and the punishment overtook them, so they supplicated, so it was lifted from them, and Yunus did not know of their repentance, so he went angry, and it was his right not to go except with specific permission. Al-Hasan said: God Almighty commanded him to go to his people, so he asked to wait to get ready, so God hastened him until he asked to take a sandal to wear, but he did not wait, and it was said to him: The matter is more urgent than that - and he was narrow-minded - so he went out angry for his Lord, so this is a statement, and the statement of Al-Nahhas is the best that has been said in its interpretation. That is, he went out in anger for the sake of his Lord, that is, he was angry with his people because of their disbelief in his Lord. It was said that he was angry with his people when their matter and their stubbornness became too much for him, so he went fleeing with his life, and he could not bear their harm, although God had commanded him to stick with them and to supplicate, so his sin was that he left them without God’s permission. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak, and that Yunus was a young man and had not yet carried the burdens of prophethood, and for this reason the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was told, And do not be like the companion of the fish (al-Qalam 68:48). Ad-Dahhak also said that he went out in anger with his people, because when his people did not accept him, and he was a messenger from God, the Almighty, they disbelieved in this, so it was necessary for him to be angry with them, and it is upon everyone to be angry with those who disobey God, the Almighty. A group of them, including Al-Akhfash, said: He only went out in anger because of the king who was over his people. Ibn Abbas said: The prophet Isaiah and the king who was at that time named Hezekiah wanted to send Jonah to the king of Nineveh, who had invaded the children of Israel and taken many of them captive, to speak to him so that he would send the children of Israel with him. At that time, the prophets were inspired, and the matter and policy were left to a king they had chosen, so he would act on the inspiration of that prophet. God had inspired Isaiah: Tell King Hezekiah to choose a strong, trustworthy prophet from the children of Israel and send him to the people of Nineveh to order them to let go of the children of Israel, for I have cast into the hearts of their kings and their tyrants the desire to let them go. Jonah said to Isaiah: Did God command you to send me out? He said: No. He said: Did He name me to you? He said: No. He said: Here are trustworthy, strong prophets. They insisted, so he went out in anger with the Prophet, the king and his people. He came to the Roman Sea and his story happened. He was afflicted with the belly of the whale because he left the matter of Isaiah. That is why God the Almighty said: Then the whale swallowed him, and he was blameworthy. (al-Saffat 37:142) The blameworthy is the one who does what he is blamed for. What he did was either a minor sin or he left the first. It was said that he went out and he was not a prophet at that time, but a king of the kings of the Children of Israel ordered him to go to Nineveh to call its people to the command of Isaiah. He refused that his going to them be by the command of anyone other than God, so he went out in anger with the king. When he was saved from the belly of the whale, God sent him to his people, so he called them and they believed in him. Al-Qushayri said: It is more apparent that this anger was after God the Almighty sent him, and after the punishment was lifted from the people after it had overtaken them, because he hated the punishment being lifted from them. I said: This is the best that has been said about him, as will be explained in (Al-Saffat), God willing. It was said: It was among the morals of his people to kill whoever they found lying about him, so he feared that he would be killed, so he became angry and fled until he boarded a ship, which calmed down and did not sail. The people of the ship said: Is there a runaway among you? He said: I am he. And what happened from his story happened, and he was tested in the belly of the whale to test him for a small sin, as He said about the people of UHud 11:Until, when you failed (Al Imran 3:152) until His saying: And that God may test those who believe (Al Imran 3:141). So the sins of the prophets are forgiven, but testing may occur and that includes a warning against repeating it. A fourth saying: He did not anger his Lord, nor his people, nor the king, and that is from their saying anger when he is angry. The agent may be one, so the meaning is that when he promised his people punishment and left them, they repented and the punishment was removed from them. When he returned and knew that they had not perished, he was disgusted by that and left as a fugitive. This verse is recited: I get angry that Tamim is cursed with Daram Any nose. This is questionable, because it is said to the one who says this: Even if that anger is from arrogance, arrogance must be mixed with anger, and that anger, even if it is subtle, is against whom?! And you say that he was not angry with his Lord or his people! God the Almighty said: So he thought that We would not have power over him, so he cried out in the darkness. It was said that its meaning is that Satan made him slip and he thought that God could not punish him. This is a rejected and undesirable statement, because it is disbelief. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, narrated by Al-Mahdawi and Al-Tha’labi on the authority of Al-Hasan. Al-Tha’labi mentioned and said, ‘Ata’ and Saeed bin Jubair and many scholars mean: So he thought that We would not make it difficult for him. Al-Hasan said: It is from the Almighty’s saying: God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it (al-Ra’d 13:26), meaning He restricts it. And His saying: And whoever He restricts his provision (al-Talaq 65:7). I said: This is more similar to what Saeed and Al-Hasan said. Qadr, Qadara, and Qatar mean the same thing, meaning he made it difficult, and this is the saying of Ibn Abbas as mentioned by Al-Mawardi and Al-Mahdawi. It was said: It is from Qadr, which is the decree and ruling, meaning he thought that We would not decree punishment upon him, as said by Qatada, Mujahid, and Al-Farra. It is taken from Qadr, which is the ruling, not ability and capability. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Abbas Ahmad bin Yahya Tha’lab that he said regarding the statement of God, the Almighty: So he thought that We would not decree upon him, it is from Qadr, not from power. It is said from it: God decreed good for you, He decrees it as Qadr, meaning God decreed good for you. Tha’lab recited: The evenings of Al-Lawa will never return to us, as long as the fresh peace prevails. That time that passed will not return. Blessed are you, what can happen will happen. Thank you. Meaning that what you estimate and decree will happen. Scholars have adopted these two interpretations. Omar bin Abdul Aziz and Al-Zuhri read: Fathaan an lan yaqdur alayhi with a damma on the noon and a shaddah on the dal from the word qadaar. Al-Mawardi narrated this reading from Ibn Abbas. Ubaid bin Umair, Qatada and Al-A'raj read: An lan yaqdur alayhi with a damma on the yaa' and a shaddah on the dal as a passive verb. Ya'qub, Abdullah bin Abi Ishaq, Al-Hasan and Ibn Abbas also read Yaqdur alayhi with a damma on the yaa' and a fatha on the dal as a lightened passive verb. Al-Hasan also said: Fathaan an lan yaqdur alayhi. The rest read: Naqadar with a fatha on the noon and a kasra on the dal, all of which mean qadaar. I said: These two interpretations were interpreted by scholars regarding the statement of the man who never did any good for his family when he died and they burned him: By God, if God has power over me the hadith, according to the first interpretation, it means: By God, if God is harsh on me and is excessive in holding me accountable and punishing me for my sins, then that will happen. Then he ordered that he be burned due to his extreme fear. According to the second interpretation: That is, if it was previously in God's decree and judgment that He would punish every criminal for his crime, then God will punish me for my crime and sins with a punishment that He will not punish anyone in the worlds except me. His hadith was narrated by the imams in Al-Muwatta' and elsewhere. The man was a believer who believed in monotheism. It was mentioned in some of its chains of transmission: (He did not do any good except monotheism) and when God the Almighty said: Why did you do this? He said: Out of fear of You, O Lord. And fear is only for a believing believer, God the Almighty said: Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge (Fatir 35:28). It has been said that the meaning of He thought that we would not be able to do anything to him is a question, and its interpretation is: Do you think? So the question alif was deleted for brevity, and this is the saying of Sulayman [Abu] al-Mu’tamir. Judge Mundhir ibn Sa’id narrated that some of them read Do you think with an alif. God Almighty says: “Then he called out in the darkness, ‘There is no god except You; exalted are You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.’” There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Then he called out in the darknesses. The scholars differed about the plural of darknesses and what is meant by it. A group of them, Ibn Abbas and Qatada, said: The darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the whale. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya mentioned that Yusuf bin Musa told us, Ubaidullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amr bin Maimun, who said: Abdullah bin Masoud told us regarding the treasury, he said: When the whale swallowed Yunus, peace be upon him, it threw him down to the bottom of the earth, and Yunus heard the pebbles glorifying God, so he called out in the darknesses, three darknesses: the darkness of the belly of the whale, the darkness of the night, and the darkness of the sea, “There is no god but You, glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.” So We cast him out onto the open shore while he was sick, like a bald young bird that has no feathers. A group of them, Salim bin Abi Al-Ja’d, said: The darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the whale that swallowed the first whale. It is correct to express darkness only for the belly of the first whale, as he said: In the depths of the well and in all its directions there is darkness, so its plural is permissible. Al-Mawardi mentioned: It is possible to express darkness for the darkness of sin, the darkness of hardship, and the darkness of loneliness. It was narrated: God the Almighty revealed to the whale: (Do not harm a hair of it, for I have made your belly its prison and have not made it your food) It was narrated: That Yunus, peace be upon him, prostrated in the belly of the whale when he heard the glorification of the whales at the bottom of the sea. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya mentioned that Al-Abbas bin Yazid Al-Abdi told us, Ishaq bin Idris told us, Jaafar bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Al-Hassan, who said: When the whale swallowed Yunus, peace be upon him, he thought that he had died, so he stretched out his legs, but he had not died, so he stood up as usual to pray and said in his supplication: (And I have taken for yourself a place of prostration where no one has taken). Abu Al-Ma’ali said: His, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying: Do not prefer me over Jonah, son of Matta. The meaning is that I was not closer to God than him when I was at the Lote Tree of the Limit, and he was at the bottom of the sea in the belly of the whale. This indicates that the Creator, glory be to Him, is not in a direction. This meaning was previously mentioned in Al-Baqarah and Al-A’raf. “There is no god except You; glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.” He means what he did wrong in, which was not to be constant with his people and to be patient with them. It was also said: in going out without permission. And that was not a punishment from God, because prophets cannot be punished, but rather it was a test. And those who do not deserve punishment may be disciplined, such as children, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. And it was also said: among the wrongdoers in my supplication for punishment upon my people. And Noah supplicated against his people, but he was not held accountable. Al-Wasiti said about its meaning: He purified his Lord from injustice and attributed injustice to himself as an admission and deserving. And similar to this is the saying of Adam and Eve: Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves (al-A’raf 7:23), as they were the reason for putting themselves in a place other than that in which they were placed. Second: Abu Dawood narrated on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The supplication of Dhul-Nun in the belly of the whale: ‘There is no god but You, glory be to You. Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.’ No Muslim man has ever supplicated with it for anything without it being answered.” It has been said: It is the greatest name of God. Saad narrated it on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. In the hadith: In this verse God made a condition for whoever calls upon Him that He will answer him as He answered him and save him as He saved him, and that is His saying: And thus do We save the believers. Here there is no explicit supplication, but rather the meaning of His saying: Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers. So he admitted to the wrongdoing, and it was an allusion.
21:88: The Almighty said: And thus do We deliver the believers meaning, We deliver them from their worries because of their previous deeds. This is His saying: And had he not been of those who glorify God, he would have remained inside its belly until the Day they are resurrected. This is a protection from God the Almighty for His servant Yunus, He protected for him the right of His worship, and preserved the reins of his previous obedience. Al-Ustadh Abu Ishaq said: Dhul-Nun accompanied the whale for a few days, and until the Day of Resurrection he will be called Dhul-Nun, so what do you think of a servant who worshipped Him for seventy years, and this would be in vain for him! He would not think that of him. From the worry meaning from the belly of the whale. The Almighty said: And thus do We save the believers. The general reading is with two nuns from anja yanji. Ibn Amir read naji with one nun and a double jim and a sukoon on the ya for the past tense verb and the implied source, meaning, and thus do We save the believers, just as you say, daraba Zaidan, meaning the striking struck Zaid. And he recited: If a female camel gave birth to a puppy, the puppy would curse all dogs. He wanted to curse the curse with that puppy. And the letter ya’ was made quiescent according to the dialect of those who say baqi wa raḍī and do not move the letter ya’. Al-Hasan read and they were terrified of what remained of the interest (al-Baqarah 2:278) because it was difficult to move the letter ya’ preceded by a kasra. And he recited: How long will the wine of gray hair ferment and lead me to the graves of camels? I wonder if the Day of Judgment comes and the reckoning is called, where will be the destination? The sukoon of the yaa in da'i is due to the difficulty of moving it and before it is a kasra. The agent of hada al-mashib, meaning they found the camel's gray hair, I wish I knew where its destination is. This is the interpretation of al-Farra', Abu Ubayd and Tha'lab in correcting this reading. Abu Hatim and al-Zajjaj made a mistake and said: It is a mistake, because it is the accusative of a noun whose agent is not named. Rather, it is said: Najee al-Mu'minun, just as it is said: Karameh al-Salihun. It is not permissible to strike Zayd in the sense of striking Zayd, because there is no benefit [in it] since striking indicates striking. It is not permissible to use such a verse as evidence against the Book of God Almighty. Abu Ubayd has another opinion - and al-Qutbi said it - which is that he assimilated the nun into the jim. Al-Nahhas: This opinion is not permissible according to any of the grammarians, because the point of articulation of the nun is far from the point of articulation of the jim, so it is not assimilated into it. It is not permissible in man jaa' bil-hasanah (al-An'am 6:160) to say jaa' bil-hasanah. Al-Nahhas said: I have not heard anything better in this than what I heard from Ali ibn Sulayman. He said: The original form is nanji, so one of the two noons is deleted because they come together, just as one of the two ta’s is deleted because they come together, like the Almighty’s saying: And do not be divided (Al Imran 3:103). The original form is tataffaraqu. Muhammad ibn al-Sumaiq and Abu al-Aaliyah read And thus We save the believers, meaning God saved the believers, and it is good.
21:89: The Almighty said: And Zachariah, when he called upon his Lord. That is, remember Zachariah. He was mentioned earlier in (Al Imran. My Lord, leave me not alone. That is, alone, without children, and this was mentioned earlier. And You are the best of inheritors. That is, the best of those who remain after everyone who dies. He only said And You are the best of inheritors because of what was mentioned earlier in His statement: He will inherit me. (Maryam 19:6) That is, know that you will not waste your religion, but do not cut off this virtue, which is the upholding of the religion, from my descendants. This was explained earlier in (Maryam.
21:90: The Almighty said: So We answered him meaning We answered his prayer: And We granted him John. This has been fully mentioned above. And We made his wife good for him. Qatada, Saeed bin Jubayr, and most of the commentators said: She was barren, but she became fertile. Ibn Abbas and Ata' said: She was ill-tempered and had a long tongue, but God made her good-tempered. I said: It is possible that she combined the two meanings and made the one of good character and fertile. They mean the prophets named in this surah they used to hasten to do good deeds. It was said: The metaphor refers back to Zachariah, his wife, and John. The Almighty’s saying: And they call upon Us in hope and fear contains two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And they call upon Us in hope and fear. That is, they flee to Us and call upon Us in times of ease and times of hardship. It was said: The meaning is that they call upon Us at the time of their worship and they are in a state of hope, desire, awe and fear, because desire and awe are intertwined. It was said: Desire is raising the palms of the hands to the sky, and fear is raising the backs of them, as said by Khasif. Ibn Atiyyah said: The summary of this is that the habit of every human being who calls upon Us is to seek help with his hands. Desire, in terms of seeking, is good for him to direct the palms of the hands toward what is being sought, since it is a place of giving or by which he possesses. Fear, in terms of warding off harm, is good for him to throw that away and indicate its departure and avoid it by shaking the hand or the like. Second: Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) raised his hands in supplication, he would not lower them until he wiped his face with them. The difference in raising the hands has been mentioned in Al-A’raf, and we mentioned this hadith and others there. According to the opinion of raising, people differed about its description and to where. Some of them preferred to spread out his hands, raising them level with his chest and their palms towards his face. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas. Ali used to supplicate with the palms of his hands, and Anas said something similar, and this is the apparent meaning of the hadith of Al-Tirmidhi. And the saying of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): If you ask God, ask Him with the palms of your hands and do not ask Him with the backs of them, and wipe your faces with them. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Omar and Ibn al-Zubayr that they raised them to his face, and they provided evidence with the hadith of Abu Saeed al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood at Arafat and began to supplicate, placing the backs of his hands next to his face, and raising them above his breasts and below his shoulders. It was said: until they were level with his face and their backs next to his face. Abu Ja`far al-Tabari said: The correct thing to say is that all of these narrations narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) are in agreement and do not differ in meaning. It is possible that this was from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) due to the different states of supplication, as Ibn `Abbas said: If one of you points with one finger, then it is sincerity. If he raises his hands level with his chest, then it is supplication. If he raises them until they are above his head and their backs next to his face, then it is supplication. Al-Tabari said: Qatada narrated from Anas that he said: I saw the Prophet (peace be upon him) supplicating with the back and palm of his hands. Raghaba and Rahaban are accusative as a source, meaning they desire desire and they fear fear. Or as an object for the sake of which, meaning for desire and fear. Or as a state. Talha ibn Musarraf read wa yad'uuna with one noon. Al-A'mash read it with a damma on the ra' and a sukoon on the ghain and the ha' like sickness and miserliness, and lack and harm are two dialects. Ibn Waththab and Al-A'mash also read Raghaba and Rahaban with a fatha on the ra' and a sukoon on the ghain and the ha', and they are two dialects like river and river and rock and rock. This reading was narrated from Abu Amr. And they were humble and submissive to us meaning humble and submissive.
21:91: The Almighty said: And who guarded her chastity meaning, remember Mary who guarded her chastity. He mentioned her and she was not one of the prophets so that the mention of Jesus, peace be upon him, would be complete. That is why He said: And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds and did not say two signs because the meaning of the statement is: And We made their affair and their matter and their story a sign for the worlds. Al-Zajjaj said that the sign in them is one, that she gave birth to him without a male. According to the doctrine of Sibawayh, the estimate is: And We made her a sign for the worlds and We made her son a sign for the worlds, then it was deleted. According to the doctrine of Al-Farraa: And We made her a sign for the worlds and her son, like His statement, may He be glorified: And God and His Messenger are more worthy that they should please Him (al-Tawbah 9:62). It was said that among her signs was that she was the first woman to be accepted in a vow in worship. Among them is that God, the Almighty, nourished her with provision from Himself that He did not make at the hands of any of His servants. It was said that she never breastfed. And she was chaste means she was pure and refrained from immorality. It was said that what is meant by the vulva is the shirt, i.e. no suspicion was attached to her garment, i.e. her garments were pure. And the vulva of the shirt are four: the sleeve, the upper part, and the lower part. Al-Suhayli said: Do not let your thoughts go to anything other than this, for it is a subtle metaphor because the Qur’an is purer in meaning, more balanced in wording, more subtle in reference, and better in expression than to mean what the thoughts of the ignorant go to, especially since the breathing is from the Holy Spirit by the command of the Most Holy, so He added the Holy to the Most Holy, and He purified the Holy and the purified from false suspicion and conjecture. Then We breathed into her of Our Spirit means We commanded Gabriel until he breathed into her armor, and with that breath We caused the Messiah to breathe into her womb. This has already been mentioned in An-Nisa’ and Maryam, so there is no point in repeating it. A sign means a mark and wonder for creation, a sign of the prophethood of Jesus, and an indication of the power of what We will.
21:92: The Almighty said: Indeed, this nation of yours is one nation. When he mentioned the prophets, he said: All of them are united in monotheism. So the nation here means the religion which is Islam, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others. As for the polytheists, they have opposed all of them. And I am your Lord means their God alone. So worship Me means single out Me in worship. Isa bin Omar and Ibn Abi Ishaq read: Indeed, this nation of yours is one nation and Husayn narrated it from Abu Amr. The rest of them read one nation in the accusative case as a categorical statement due to the indefinite noun coming after the completion of the statement, as stated by Al-Farra'. Al-Zajjaj said: Nation is in the accusative case as a state, meaning in the state of its unity on the truth, meaning this is your nation as long as it is one nation and you are united on monotheism, but if you are divided and opposed, then no one who opposes the truth is among the people of the true religion, and it is like you say: So-and-so is my chaste friend, meaning as long as he is chaste, but if he opposes chastity, then he is not my friend. As for the nominative, it may be in apposition to your nation or with an implied subject, i.e. this is your nation, this is one nation. Or it may be a predicate after a predicate. If your nation were to be in the accusative case in apposition to this, it would be permissible and one nation would be the predicate of if.
21:93: The Almighty said: And they divided their affair among themselves meaning they were divided in religion, said Al-Kalbi. Al-Akhfash, they differed about it. What is meant are the polytheists, he condemned them for opposing the truth and taking gods besides God. Al-Azhari said: meaning they divided in their affair, so their affair is intransitive by deleting in. According to this, the divided is intransitive, and according to the first, it is transitive. What is meant is all of creation, meaning they made their affair in their religions definitive and divided it among themselves, so some are monotheists, some are Jews, some are Christians, and some are worshippers of kings or idols. All to Us will return meaning to Our judgment, so We will reward them.
21:94: The Almighty said: So whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer "of" is for partiality, not for gender, since the one who is obligated is not able to perform all the acts of obedience, whether obligatory or voluntary, so the meaning is: whoever does something of the acts of obedience, obligatory or voluntary, and he is a monotheist Muslim. Ibn Abbas said: believing in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. "There is no denial for his effort" meaning there is no denial for his work, meaning his reward will not be lost or covered. The opposite of denial is faith. Denial is also denial of a blessing, and it is the opposite of gratitude. He denied it ungratefully and ungratefully. In the wording of Ibn Mas'ud, there is no denial for his effort. "And indeed, We are its recorders", preserving his work. Similar to it is: "Never will I allow to be lost the work of a worker among you, whether male or female" (Al Imran 3:195) meaning all of that is preserved for reward.
21:95: The Almighty said: And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed that they will not return. The reading of Zaid bin Thabit and the people of Medina is and forbidden. This is the choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. The people of Kufa say and forbidden. It was narrated from Ali, Ibn Masoud, and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them. They are two dialects like halal and halal. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Saeed bin Jubair and forbidden with the opening of the ha and the meem and the kasra of the ra. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and Abu Al-Aliyah and forbidden with the damma of the ra and the opening of the ha and the meem. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas and forbidden and from him also and forbidden, "and forbidden. It was also narrated from Ikrimah and forbidden. It was narrated from Qatada and Matar Al-Warraq and forbidden." Nine readings. Al-Salami read "on a town which I have destroyed." There is a difference of opinion regarding la in His statement: They will not return. It was said: It is a connection. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and Abu Ubaid chose it, meaning: It is forbidden for a village that We destroyed to return after destruction. It was said: It is not a connection, but rather it is fixed, and forbidden means obligatory, meaning it is obligatory for a village, as Al-Khansa’ said: It is forbidden that I do not see time crying over its sorrows except that I cry over a rock She wants her brother, so no is fixed according to this statement. An-Nahhas said: The verse is problematic, and among the best and most important things that have been said about it is what was narrated by Ibn Uyaynah, Ibn Ulayyah, Hisham, Ibn Idris, Muhammad Ibn Fadil, Sulayman Ibn Hayyan, and Mu’alla on the authority of Dawud Ibn Abi Hind on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the statement of God Almighty: And it is forbidden for a town which We have destroyed, he said: It is necessary that they do not return, he said: They do not repent. Abu Ja`far said: The derivation of this is clear in the language, and its explanation is that the meaning of haraam is to prohibit and prevent something, just as the meaning of halal is to permit and not prevent it. So if haraam and haram mean obligatory, then its meaning is that the exit from it is restricted and prevented, so it has entered the category of what is forbidden by this. As for the statement of Abu `Ubayd: that la is redundant, a group of people have rejected it, because it is not added in such a place, nor in what is problematic. If it were redundant, the interpretation would also be far-fetched, because if he meant and it is forbidden for a town that We have destroyed to hope for the world, then this is of no benefit, and if he meant repentance, then repentance is not forbidden. It was said: There is an implied meaning in the speech, that is, and it is forbidden for a town that We have ruled to exterminate, or to seal its hearts, that any action from them be accepted because they do not return, meaning they do not repent. This was said by al-Zajjaj and Abu `Ali, and la is not redundant. This is the meaning of the statement of Ibn `Abbas.
21:96: The Almighty said: Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose We have already discussed them. There is an ellipsis in the speech, meaning until, when the dam of Gog and Magog is let loose, like And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82). And they stream down from every hill Ibn Abbas said: They come from every high place, meaning because of their great numbers, they stream down from every direction. A hump is a raised part of the ground, and the plural is hudab, taken from the hump of the back. Antara said: My hands did not tremble, nor did I feel proud of their successive visits to me from the hump. It was said: They slip away means they go out, and from this is the saying of Imru’ al-Qais: So, remove my clothes from your clothes and they will slip away It was said: They hasten, and from this is the saying of Al-Nabigha: The wolf's lion became a boat, and the night became cold upon it, so it slipped away. It is said: The wolf's honey is honey and honey when it grows and runs fast. In the hadith: Honey lied to you meaning you walk fast. Al-Zajjaj said: "Naslan is the gait of a wolf when it runs fast. It is said: Naslan so-and-so in the enemy, yansalā with kasra and damma naslā and nasulan and naslāna, meaning he hastened. Then it was said about those who rush from every side: they are Yajuj and Majuj, and this is the most apparent, and it is the saying of Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas. It was said: all of creation, for they will be gathered to the place of standing, and they will rush from every direction. It was read in the Shawa'idh: they rush from every grave, taken from His saying: "Then from the graves they rush to their Lord" (Ya-Sin 36:51). Al-Mahdawi narrated this reading from Ibn Mas'ud and Al-Tha'labi from Mujahid and Abu Al-Sahbaa.
21:97: The Almighty said: And the true promise has drawn near meaning the Resurrection. Al-Farra', Al-Kisa'i and others said: The waw is an extra, inserted letter, and the meaning is: until when Gog and Magog are opened, the true promise has drawn near, so the answer to if has drawn near. Al-Farra' recited: When we passed the neighborhood square and he went away That is, he turned aside, and the waw is redundant, and from this is the saying of God the Almighty: And he laid him on his forehead, and We called him (al-Saffat 37:103-104), meaning, We called him to his forehead. Al-Kisa’i permitted the answer to if to be Then the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror and his saying: And the true promise has drawn near to be conjoined with the verb which is a condition. The Basrans said: The answer is omitted and the meaning is: They said, Woe to us, and this is the saying of Al-Zajjaj, and it is a good saying. God the Almighty said: And those who have taken protectors besides Him, ‘We do not worship them except that they may bring us nearer to God.’ (al-Zumar 39:3) The meaning is: They said, We do not worship them, and the omission of a statement is common. The Almighty says: Then behold, it will be staring. “It” is the pronoun for the eyes, and the eyes mentioned after it are an explanation of it, as if He said: Then behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring at the coming of the promise. And the poet said: By the life of her father, my wife will never say, Malik bin Abi Kaab has fled from me. So he referred to the woman travelling with her father, then he made her apparent. Al-Farra’ said: It is a pillar, like for indeed the eyes are not blind (al-Hajj 22:46). It was said that the speech was completed when he said: It the meaning is: then it, meaning the Resurrection, is prominent and occurring, that is, from its proximity as if it is coming and present, then he began and said: The eyes of those who disbelieved are staring by presenting the report before the beginning, that is, the eyes of those who disbelieved are staring from this day, that is, from its terror, they can hardly blink, they say: Woe to us, we were wrongdoers in our disobedience, and we placed worship in the wrong place.
21:98: It has four issues: God the Almighty said: Indeed, you and what you worship. Ibn Abbas said: This is a verse that people do not ask me about! I do not know. They knew it and did not ask about it. It was said: What is it? He said: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. You will surely enter it.” When it was revealed, it was difficult for the infidels of Quraysh, and they said: He insulted our gods. They went to Ibn al-Zubayri and told him. He said: If I were present, I would have responded to him. They said: What did you say? He said: I used to say to him: This is the Messiah whom the Christians worship and the Jews worship Ezra. Do they understand that he is fuel for Hell? The Quraysh were amazed by his statement, and they saw that Muhammad had been defeated. So God Almighty revealed: Indeed, those for whom good has preceded from Us - those will be removed from it (Al-Anbiya’: 101). And in this regard, And when the son of Mary is cited as an example (al-Zukhruf 43:57) meaning Ibn Az-Zubayri, behold, your people turn away from him (al-Zukhruf 43:57) with a broken sad, meaning they make a noise, and it will come. Second: This verse is the basis for the statement of generality and that it has specific formulas, contrary to those who said: It does not have a formula established to indicate it, and this is false because of what this verse and others indicate. This is Abdullah bin Al-Zubayri, who understood what in his ignorance as all of those who worshipped, and the Quraysh agreed with him on that, and they are the eloquent Arabs, and the fluent tongue, and if it were not for generality it would not be correct to make an exception from it, and that was found, so it is for generality and this is clear. Third: The reading of the common people with the silent sad, meaning that you, O group of disbelievers, and the idols that you worship besides God are the fuel of Hellfire, said Ibn Abbas. Mujahid, Ikrimah and Qatadah said: its firewood. Ali ibn Abi Talib and Aisha may God be pleased with them read the firewood of Hellfire with the ta’. Ibn Abbas read the hadab with the voiced dad. Al-Farra’ said: He means pebbles. He said: It was mentioned to us that the hadab in the language of the people of Yemen means firewood, and everything that you stir up fire with and ignite it with is hadab, mentioned by Al-Jawhari. And the kindling is mahdab. Abu Ubaidah said about the verse of God the Almighty: the fuel of Hellfire: everything you throw into the fire, you have pebbled it with. It is clear from this verse that the people of the disbelievers and what they worship of idols are firewood for Hellfire. Similar to this verse is the verse of God the Almighty... It was said: What is meant by the stones are sulfur stones, as mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah and that the fire is not a torment or punishment for the idols, because they did not sin, but it is a torment for those who worship them: first with regret, then it is gathered on the fire and its fire is more intense than any fire, then they are tormented by it. It is heated and sticks to them to increase their torment. It was said: It was only placed in the fire as a rebuke for their worship. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: You will enter it, meaning you will enter it. The address is to the polytheists who worship idols, meaning you will enter it with the idols. It is permissible to say: The address is to the idols and their worshippers, because even though the idols are inanimate, they may be described by human metaphors. The scholars said: This does not include Jesus, Ezra, or the angels, may God’s prayers be upon them, because what is for non-humans. If He had intended that, He would have said: and who. Al-Zajjaj said: Because those addressed in this verse are the polytheists of Mecca and no one else.
21:99: The Almighty said: If these were gods, they would not have entered it. That is, if the idols were gods, their worshippers would not have entered the fire. It was said: The worshippers and the worshipped would not have entered it, and for this reason He said: And all therein will abide eternally.
21:100: The Almighty said: Therein they will have a sigh meaning for those who entered the Fire from the disbelievers and devils. As for the idols, there is a difference of opinion about them, will God Almighty revive them and torment them until they sigh or not? There are two opinions: And the sigh is the sound of the soul of the distressed coming out of the heart. It was mentioned in (Hud). And they will not hear therein It was said: There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is that they will not hear anything therein, because they will be gathered deaf, as God Almighty said: And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf (al-Isra’ 17:97). And in hearing things there is spirit and comfort, so God prevented the disbelievers from that in the Fire. It was said: They will not hear what pleases them, rather they will hear the voice of the one who is in charge of torturing them from the guards. It was said: If it is said to them, Be gone into it, and do not speak (al-Mu’minun 23:108), they will then become deaf and dumb, as Ibn Mas’ud said: If those who remain will remain in Hellfire forever, they will be placed in coffins of fire, then the coffins will be placed in other coffins in which there are nails of fire, so they will not hear anything, and none of them will see that there is anyone in Hell who is tormenting someone other than him.
21:101: The Almighty said: Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us meaning Paradise they will be removed from it meaning the Fire “so the meaning of the statement is an exception, and for this reason some of the people of knowledge said: “Indeed” here means except and there is no other such word in the Qur’an. Muhammad ibn Hattab said: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, reciting this verse on the pulpit: Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us and he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Uthman is one of them.
21:102: The Almighty said: They do not hear its hissing sound meaning the sound of the fire and the movement of its flames. Hissing and feeling are movement. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ata' who said: Abu Rashid Al-Haruri said to Ibn Abbas: They do not hear its hissing sound Ibn Abbas said: Are you crazy? So where is the Almighty's saying: There is not one of you but will pass over it (Maryam 19:71) and His saying: Then He will lead them to the Fire (Hud 11:98) and His saying: To Hell, a continuous flow (Maryam 19:86). And it was from the supplication of those who came before: O God, take me out of the Fire unharmed, and admit me into Paradise as a winner. Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi said: On the Sirat there are snakes that bite the people of Hell and they say: Hiss, hiss. It was said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, they will not hear the sound of the people of Hell, and before that they will hear it, and God knows best. And they will abide in that which their souls desire meaning they will remain in it, and their souls desire it and their eyes delight in it. He said: And you will have therein whatever your souls desire, and you will have therein whatever you request. (Fussilat 41:31)
21:103: The Almighty said: The greatest terror will not grieve them. Abu Ja`far and Ibn Muhaisin read will not grieve them with a damma on the ya' and a kasra on the zay. The rest read with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the zay. Al-Yazidi said: Hazanahu is the language of Quraysh, and ahzanahu is the language of Tamim, and both were read with it. The greatest terror is the terrors of the Day of Resurrection and the Resurrection, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan said: It is the time when the servants are ordered to the Fire. Ibn Jurayj, Sa`id ibn Jubayr, and Ad-Dahhak said: It is when the Fire covers its people, and death is slaughtered between Paradise and Hell. Dhu An-Nun Al-Misri said: It is severance and separation. And on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “There are three who will be on the Day of Resurrection in a mound of fragrant musk, and the greatest terror will not grieve them: a man who leads a people, hoping for reward, and they are pleased with him; a man who gives ear to a people, hoping for reward; and a man who was afflicted with lightning in this world, but it did not distract him from obeying his Lord.” Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman said: I passed by a man who was beating his slave, so the slave pointed to me, so I spoke to his master until he forgave him. Then I met Abu Sa`id al-Khudri and told him, and he said: O son of my brother! Whoever helps one in distress, God will free him from the Fire on the Day of the Greatest Terror. I heard that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the angels will meet them means the angels will meet them at the gates of Paradise, congratulating them and saying to them: This is your day which you were promised. It was said: The angels of mercy will meet them when they emerge from the graves. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas: This is your day means they will say to them, but the omission of which you were promised indicates honor.
21:104: The Almighty said: The Day We fold the heaven Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa', Shaibah ibn Nasah, al-A'raj and al-Zuhri read the heaven with a damma on the ta' the heaven in the nominative case for what its agent is not named. Mujahid folds means God folds the heaven. The rest read fold with the nun of majesty. The accusative of the day is in apposition to the deleted ha' in the relative clause, the meaning is: that which you were promised on the day We fold the heaven. Or it could be accusative with return from His statement: As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. Or with His statement: They will not be saddened meaning the greatest terror on the day We fold the heaven. Or with the omission of remember, and He meant by the heaven the genus, the evidence for this is: And the heavens are folded in His right hand (al-Zumar 39:67). Like folding the scroll for the book. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: That is, like folding the page on what is in it, so the lam means on. And also from Ibn Abbas the name of the scribe of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it is not strong, because the scribes of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are known, this is not one of them, nor is there anyone among his companions whose name is the recorder. And Ibn Abbas, Ibn Omar and Al-Suddi also said: The recorder is an angel, and he is the one who folds up the books of the sons of Adam when they are raised to him. And it is said that he is in the third heaven, and the deeds of the servants are raised to him, and the guardians assigned to creation raise them to him every Thursday and Monday, and among his helpers, as they mentioned, were Harut and Marut. And the record is the instrument, and it is a name derived from the record, which is writing, and its origin is from the record, which is the bucket, you say: I argued with the man if you took out a bucket and he took out a bucket, then it was borrowed and correspondence and review were called review. And the ruler recorded a recording. And Al-Fadl bin Al-Abbas bin Utbah bin Abi Lahab said: Whoever debates with me debates with a noble man who fills the bucket to the limit of distress Then he built this name on a verb such as hamra, tamra, and bala. Abu Zur’ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir read katay as-sajjil with a damma on the seen and the jim and a light lam. Al-A’mash and Talhah read katay as-sajjil with a fatha on the seen, a sukoon on the jim, and a light lam. An-Nahhas said: The meaning is the same, God willing. The completion is in His statement: for the book. The folding in this verse has two possible meanings: One is the stairs, which is the opposite of spreading. God Almighty said: And the heavens are rolled up in His right hand (al-Zumar 39:67). The second is concealment, obscurity, and erasure, because God Almighty erases and obliterates its features and clouds its stars. God the Almighty said: When the sun is wrapped up, and when the stars are scattered (al-Takwir 81:1-2), And when the sky is stripped away (al-Takwir 81:11). For the Book and the speech is complete. The reading of Al-A’mash, Hafs, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, Yahya and Khalaf is: For the Book in the plural, then He resumed the speech and said: As We began the first creation, We will repeat it meaning We will gather them barefoot, naked and uncircumcised as they began in the bellies. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection naked and uncircumcised. The first of creation to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Abraham, peace be upon him.” Then he recited: As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) delivered a sermon among us and said: O people, you will be gathered before God barefoot, naked and uncircumcised. “As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. A promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.” The first of the creations to be clothed on the Day of Resurrection will be Abraham, peace be upon him. He mentioned the hadith. We have already mentioned this chapter in full in the book At-Tadhkirah. Sufyan Ath-Thawri narrated on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl on the authority of Abu Al-Zura’ on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud who said: God the Almighty sends water from beneath the Throne like the semen of men, and their flesh and bodies grow from it as the earth grows soil. He then recited: As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is that We will destroy everything and annihilate it as it was the first time. Based on this, the statement is connected to His statement: The Day We fold up the heaven, meaning We will fold it up and return it to destruction and annihilation, so that it will be nothing. It was said: We will annihilate the heaven and then return it once again after folding it up and disappearing, like His statement: The Day the earth will be replaced by another earth, and the heavens [as well]. (Ibrahim 14:48) The first statement is more correct and is similar to His statement: And you have certainly come to Us alone as We created you the first time (al-An’am 6:94) and His statement, the Almighty: “And they will be presented before your Lord in rows: ‘You have certainly come to Us’” (al-Kahf 18:48). A promise is in the accusative case as a source, meaning We promised a promise. Upon Us is to fulfill and fulfil it, meaning resurrection and re-establishment, so there is an omission in the statement. Then He, the Almighty, confirmed that by His statement: Indeed, We were Doing. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of Indeed, We were Doing is that We were able to do whatever We willed. It was said: Indeed, We were Doing means what We promised you, and it is as He said: His promise was to be fulfilled (al-Muzzammil 73:18). It was said: Was is to inform of what had come before of His judgment. It was also said: a relative clause.
21:105: The Almighty said: And We have written in the Psalms The Psalms and the Book are one, and therefore it is permissible to call the Torah and the Gospel Zabur. Zabart means written and its plural is Zabar. Saeed bin Jubair said: The Zabur is the Torah, the Gospel and the Qur'an. After the Reminder which is in the heaven that the earth the land of Paradise will be inherited by My righteous servants narrated by Sufyan from Al-A'mash from Saeed bin Jubair. Al-Sha'bi: The Zabur is the Psalms of David, and the Reminder is the Torah of Moses, peace be upon him. Mujahid and Ibn Zayd: The Zabur are the books of the prophets, peace be upon them, and the Reminder is the mother of the book which is with God in the heaven. Ibn Abbas said: The Zabur are the books that God sent down to His prophets after Moses, and the Reminder is the Torah sent down to Moses. Hamza read in the Zabur with a damma on the zay, the plural of Zabar. The earth will be inherited by My righteous servants. The best that has been said about it is that it refers to the land of Paradise, as Saeed bin Jubair said, because the earth in this world was inherited by the righteous and others. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others. Mujahid and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: The evidence for this interpretation is the statement of God the Almighty: And they will say, 'Praise be to God, Who has fulfilled His promise to us and has given us the earth as an inheritance.' (al-Zumar 39:74) And from Ibn Abbas: It refers to the Holy Land. And from him also: It refers to the land of the disbelieving nations, which the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will inherit through conquests. It has been said that what is meant by this is the Children of Israel, based on the statement of God the Almighty: And We gave as an inheritance to the people who were oppressed the eastern regions of the earth and the western regions which We had blessed. (al-A’raf 7:137) Most of the commentators agree that what is meant by the righteous servants is the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Hamzah read My righteous servants with a sukoon on the yaa.
21:106: Indeed, in this meaning in what was mentioned in this surah of preaching and warning. It was said: In the Qur'an is a message for a people who worship. Abu Hurairah and Sufyan al-Thawri said: They are the people of the five daily prayers. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: Worshipping is obedient. And the worshipper is the one who is humble and submissive. Al-Qushayri said: It is not far-fetched that every rational person is included in it, because by nature he is humble before the Creator, and he is such that if he contemplated the Qur'an and applied it, it would lead him to Paradise. Ibn Abbas also said: They are the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, who pray the five daily prayers and fast the month of Ramadan. This is the same as the first statement.
21:107: The Almighty said: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds. Saeed bin Jubair said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a mercy to all people. Whoever believed in him and confirmed his truthfulness was blessed, and whoever did not believe in him was saved from the sinking and drowning that befell the nations. Ibn Zayd said: He meant by the worlds the believers in particular.
21:108: The Almighty said: Say, ‘It is only revealed to me that your God is one God.’ So it is not permissible to associate partners with Him. Are you Muslims? That is, are you submitting to the Oneness of God Almighty, that is, then submit, as the Almighty said: Then will you not desist? (al-Ma’idah 5:91), that is, desist.
21:109: The Almighty said: But if they turn away meaning if they turn away from Islam "then say: I have warned you on equal terms" meaning I have informed you clearly that we are at war with each other, not at peace, like the Almighty's saying: But if you fear treachery from a people, throw back to them on equal terms (al-Anfal 8:58) meaning I have informed them that you have broken the covenant, meaning you and they are equal, so no party has a binding covenant with regard to the other party. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is I have informed you of what was revealed to me on an equal basis in knowledge of it, and I have not revealed to anyone anything that I have concealed from others. And I do not know "If is a negative in the sense of what" meaning I do not know. "Is what you are promised near or far" meaning the deadline of the Day of Resurrection that no one knows, neither a sent prophet nor a close angel, as Ibn Abbas said. It was said: I have informed you of war, but I do not know when I will be permitted to fight you.
21:110: The Almighty says: He knows what is said aloud and He knows what you conceal, meaning polytheism, which is the metaphor for it.
21:111: And I do not know, perhaps it is meaning perhaps the respite a trial for you meaning a test to see how you will do, and He knows best. And an enjoyment for a time It was said: until the end of the period. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw the Umayyads in his dream, dictating the people, so Al-Hakam left him and informed the Umayyads of that, so they said to him: Go back and ask him when that will be. So God Almighty revealed: And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far "And I do not know, perhaps it is a trial for you and an enjoyment for a time" (al-Anbiya 21:111) He is saying to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say that to them.
21:112: The Almighty said: Say, My Lord, judge with justice. The Surah concluded by ordering the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to delegate the matter to Him and expect relief from Him, meaning, judge between me and these deniers and grant me victory over them. Saeed narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: The prophets used to say, Our Lord, judge between us and our people with truth (al-A’raf 7:89). So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was ordered to say, My Lord, judge with truth. So whenever he met the enemy, he would say, knowing that he was on the right and his enemy was on the wrong, My Lord, judge with truth, meaning, rule with it. Abu Ubaidah said: The adjective here was used in place of the described and the meaning is: My Lord, judge with Your true judgment. My Lord is in the accusative case because it is a vocative complement. Abu Ja'far ibn al-Qa'qa' and Ibn Muhaysin read Say, My Lord, judge with truth with a damma on the ba'. An-Nahhas said: This is a mistake according to grammarians, they do not accept a man who has come until you say, O man who has come or something similar. Ad-Dahhak, Talhah, and Yaqub read, He said, ‘My Lord, I judge with truth’ with the alif open, the kaf open, and the mim closed. That is, Muhammad said, My Lord, I judge with truth from every judge. Al-Jahdary read, Say, ‘My Lord, I judge with truth’ meaning, I judge matters with truth. “And our Lord, the Most Gracious, is sought for help against that which you describe,” meaning, you describe Him of disbelief and denial. Al-Mufaddal and As-Salami read, What you describe, with the ya’ as a statement. The rest read it with the ta’ as a statement. The eleventh part of Al-Qurtubi’s interpretation has been completed. It will be followed, God willing, by the twelfth part, which begins with: Surat Al-Hajj.
22:1: It is Meccan, except for three verses: The Almighty said: "These two are opponents" to the end of three verses, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Mujahid. It was also reported from Ibn Abbas that they are four verses, to His saying: "The punishment of the burning fire". Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Abbas also said: It is Medinan - and Qatadah also said: It is Medinan - except for four verses: "And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet - to - The punishment of a barren day" so they are Meccan. Al-Naqqash counted ten verses that were revealed in Medina. The majority said: The surah is mixed, some of it is Meccan and some of it is Medinan. This is the most correct, because the verses require that, because "O mankind is Meccan, and O you who believe" is Medinan. Al-Ghaznawi: It is one of the wonders of the surahs, it was revealed at night and during the day, in travel and at home, Meccan and Medinan, peaceful and warlike, abrogating and abrogated, clear and ambiguous, different in number. I said: And what was narrated about its merit was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Abu Dawood, and Al-Darqutni on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, is Surat Al-Hajj superior in that it contains two prostrations? He said: Yes, and whoever does not prostrate should not recite them. The wording of Al-Tirmidhi. He said: This is a good hadith, but its chain of transmission is not strong. Scholars differed on this. It was narrated on the authority of Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him and Ibn Umar that they said: Surat al-Hajj is superior because it contains two prostrations. This is what Ibn Mubarak, al-Shafi’i, Ahmad and Ishaq said. Some of them thought that it contains only one prostration, which is the opinion of Sufyan al-Thawri. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Tha’labah who said: I saw Umar ibn al-Khattab prostrating twice in al-Hajj. I said: In the morning prayer? He said: In the morning prayer. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Imran bin Husayn that when the following verse was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a terrible thing” - until His saying: - but the punishment of God is severe. He said: This verse was revealed to him while he was on a journey, so he said: Do you know what day that will be? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: That is the day when God will say to Adam, Send those who will be sent to Hellfire. He said: O Lord, what are those sent to Hellfire? He said: Nine hundred and ninety-nine to Hellfire and one to Paradise. The Muslims began to cry, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Come close and aim straight, for there has never been a prophethood except that there was ignorance before it. He said: “The number is taken from ignorance, if it is complete, otherwise it is completed from the hypocrites. And the example of you and the nations is like a spot on the arm of an animal or a birthmark on the side of a camel.” Then he said: I hope that you will be a quarter of the people of Paradise. So they said: Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be a third of the people of Paradise. So they said: Allahu Akbar. Then he said: I hope that you will be half of the people of Paradise. So they said: Allahu Akbar. He said: I do not know whether he said two-thirds or not. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. It has been narrated from other sources on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Imran bin Husayn. In it: “The people despaired until they did not even show a smile. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw it, he said: Work and be happy, for by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you are with two creatures that are not with anything except that they increase it: Gog and Magog, and whoever died from the children of Adam and the children of Satan. He said: So some of what they were feeling was relieved from the people, so he said: Work and be happy, for by the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, you are among the people like a mole on the side of a camel or like a mark on the arm of an animal.” He said: A good and authentic hadith. And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Sa`id Al-Khudri, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God the Most High says, ‘O Adam!’ He says, ‘At your service and with your goodness, and goodness is in your hands.’ He says, ‘Here come the people of Hell.’ He says, ‘And what are the people of Hell?’ He says, ‘From every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine.’ He says, ‘That is when the young will turn gray and every pregnant woman will drop her burden, and you will see the people drunk, but they are not drunk, but the punishment of God is severe.’ He says, ‘That was difficult for them.’ They said, ‘O Messenger of God, who is that man?’ He said, ‘Be glad, for from Gog and Magog there are a thousand, and from you there is a man.’” And he mentioned the hadith in a similar manner to what was mentioned in the hadith of Imran bin Husayn. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas mentioned that Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Nafi` told us that Salamah told us that `Abd al-Razzaq told us that Mu`mar told us on the authority of Qatadah on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said, “‘O people, fear your Lord. Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing.’” - to - but the punishment of God is severe. He said, It was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was on a journey. He raised his voice with it until his companions came to him and said: Do you know what day this is? This is the day when God the Almighty will say to Adam, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Adam, arise and send forth a group of the people of Hell, from every thousand, nine hundred and ninety-nine to Hell and one to Paradise. This was difficult for the Muslims, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Straighten your steps and come close and be glad, for by the One in Whose hand is my soul, you are among the people like a mole on the side of a camel or like a mark on the forearm of a donkey. And with you are two creatures that never associate with anything except that they increase it: Gog and Magog and those who perish from among the disbelieving jinn and mankind.” The Almighty says: O mankind, fear your Lord. What is meant by this call are those who are accountable, that is, fear Him in His commands and do not abandon them, and in His prohibitions and do not proceed with them. And fearing means being cautious of what is disliked. This has been discussed in detail at the beginning of (Al-Baqarah), so there is no point in repeating it. The meaning is be cautious by obeying Him and avoiding His punishment. God the Almighty said: Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a terrible thing. An earthquake is a violent movement, and from it: And they were shaken until the Messenger said (al-Baqarah 2:214). The root of the word is from the root zala ‘an al-ma’ak, meaning to move. And God made his foot shake, meaning to move it. This word is used to exaggerate something. It was said: It is the well-known earthquake, which is one of the signs of the Hour, which will occur in this world before the Day of Resurrection. This is the opinion of the majority. It was also said: This earthquake will occur in the middle of the month of Ramadan, and after it the sun will rise from the west. And God knows best.
22:2: The Almighty’s saying: On the Day you see it The ha in you see it refers, according to the majority, to the earthquake, and this is strengthened by the Almighty’s saying: Every nursing mother will forget that which she nursed, and every pregnant woman will abort her pregnancy. Breastfeeding and pregnancy are only in this world. A group said: The earthquake will be on the Day of Resurrection, and they argued with the hadith of Imran bin Husayn that we mentioned, in which it says: Do you know what day that is... The hadith. This is what is required by the context of Muslim in the hadith of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri. His saying: be distracted means be preoccupied, said Qatrib. And he recited: A blow that removes the head from its resting place and makes the friend leave his friend It was said: She forgets. It was said: She plays. It was said: She is entertained, and the meaning is close. From what she breastfed. Al-Mubarrad said: What means a source, meaning she forgets about breastfeeding. He said: This indicates that this earthquake is in this world, as there is no pregnancy or breastfeeding after the resurrection. Unless it is said: Whoever dies pregnant will be resurrected pregnant and will give birth to her pregnancy from terror, and whoever dies breastfeeding will be resurrected likewise. It is said: This is like what God the Almighty said: A Day when the children will turn gray (al-Muzzammil 73:17). It was said: It will be with the first blast. It was said: It will be with the establishment of the Hour, until people move from their graves at the second blast. It is possible that the earthquake in the verse is an expression of the horrors of the Day of Resurrection, as God the Almighty said: Poverty and hardship have touched them, and they were shaken (al-Baqarah 2:214), and as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: O God, defeat them and shake them. The benefit of mentioning the horror of that day is to encourage people to prepare for it and to get ready with good deeds. Calling the earthquake something is either because it is certain to happen, so it is easy to call it something when it does not exist, since certainty is similar to existence. Or it is about the outcome, meaning that if it happens, it is something great. It is as if the name was not used now, but the meaning is that if it happens, then it is something great, and that is why it astounds the nursing mothers and intoxicates the people, as He said: And you will see the people drunk meaning from its horror and from the fear and panic that overtakes them. But they are not drunk from wine. The scholars of meaning said: And you will see the people as if they are drunk. This is indicated by the reading of Abu Zur'ah Harim bin Amr bin Jarir bin Abdullah And you will see the people with a damma on the ta', meaning you think and it seems to you. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read sakra without an alif. The rest read sakara and they are two languages for the plural of sakran, like kasala and kasali. And the earthquake is the violent movement. And oblivion: is neglecting something due to the emergence of something that distracts from it, such as worry, pain, or something else. Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is that she leaves her child because of the distress that has befallen her.
22:3: The Almighty said: And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge. It was said that what is meant is Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, who said: God the Almighty is not able to revive one who has perished and turned to dust. And follows that is, in his saying that, every rebellious devil is a rebel.
22:4: It is decreed for him that whoever takes him as a friend Qatada and Mujahid said: meaning whoever takes Satan as a friend. He will mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze.
22:5: The Almighty’s saying: O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection - to His saying - named contains twelve issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: If you are in doubt about the Resurrection. This is an argument against the One who knows the first beginning. His saying: If you are in doubt includes the suspension. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan read Al-Baath with the fat-ha on the ‘ayn, which is a dialect for Al-Baath according to the Basrans. According to the Kufians, it is with the lightening of Baath. The meaning is: O people, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection. Then We created you meaning We created your father who is the origin of mankind, meaning Adam, peace be upon him, from dust. “Then We created his offspring” from a drop of semen, which is the sperm. It is called a drop of semen because of its smallness, and it is a small amount of water, and it may also refer to a large amount of it, and from this the hadith: Until the rider travels between the two drops, fearing no injustice. He meant the sea of the East and the sea of the West. And the drops: the drop. A drop that drips and drips. And a night of dripping is always dripping. Then from a clot which is congealed blood. The clot is the fresh blood, meaning the fresh. It was said: intense red. Then from a lump of flesh which is a small amount of meat that can be chewed, and from it the hadith: Behold, in the body is a morsel of flesh. These stages are four months. Ibn Abbas said: And in the ten days after the four months the soul is breathed into it, so that is the waiting period of a woman whose husband has died, four months and ten days. Second: Yahya bin Zakariya bin Abi Zaida narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, on the authority of Aamer, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and on the authority of Ibn Omar: That when the sperm settles in the womb, an angel takes it in his hand and says: O Lord, is it male or female, wretched or happy, what is the term and the effect, in which land will it die? Then it is said to him: Go to the Mother of the Book, for you will find in it the story of this sperm. So he goes and finds its story in the Mother of the Book, so it is created, eats its sustenance and treads its traces, and when its term comes, it is taken and buried in the place that was destined for it. Then Aamer recited: O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust. And in the Sahih on the authority of Anas bin Malik - and he traced the hadith back - he said: “God has entrusted the womb with an angel who says, ‘O Lord, a sperm-drop! O Lord, a clot! O Lord, a lump of flesh!’ So when God wants to decree a creation, the angel says, ‘O Lord, male or female, wretched or happy. What is the provision? What is the life span?’ And it is written like this in the womb of his mother.” Also in Sahih, “On the authority of Hudhayfah ibn Asid al-Ghifari, he said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: If forty-two nights pass over the sperm, God sends an angel to it, who shapes it and creates its hearing, sight, skin, flesh, and bones. Then he says, “O Lord, is it male or female?” And he mentioned the hadith. And in Sahih, “On the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) told us, and he is the truthful and believed one: “The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty days, then he is a clot for a similar period, then he is a lump of flesh for a similar period, then the angel is sent to breathe the spirit into him, and he is commanded with four words: to write down his provision, his life span, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or happy...” This hadith explains the first hadith, for it says: “The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb for forty days as a drop of semen, then forty days as a clot, then forty days as a lump of flesh, then the angel is sent to breathe the spirit into him.” So these are four months, and in the ten days the angel breathes the spirit, and this is the waiting period for a woman whose husband has died, as Ibn Abbas said. His statement: The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother’s womb was explained by Ibn Mas’ud. Al-A’mash was asked: What is gathered in his mother’s womb? He said: Khaithamah told us, he said: Abdullah said: When the sperm falls into the womb and God wants to create from it a human being, it flies in the woman’s skin under every nail and hair, then it stays for forty days, then it becomes blood in the womb. That is its collection, and this is the time when it is a clot. Third: The attribution of creation and shaping to the angel is a metaphorical attribution, not a real one, and that what emanated from him was the action in the embryo at the time of shaping and forming by the power, creation and invention of God. Do you not see that He, glory be to Him, has attributed to Him the real creation, and cut off from it the attribution of all creation, saying: And We have certainly created you, then We shaped you (al-A’raf 7:11). And He said: “And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging” (al-Mu’minun 23:12-13). And He said: O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection - then indeed We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop (Al-Taghabun: 2). Then He said: And He shaped you and perfected your forms (Ghafir 40:64). And He said: Indeed, We created man in the best stature (al-Tin 95:4) and He said: He created man from a clot (al-Alaq 96:2). And other verses, with what is indicated by conclusive evidence that there is no Creator of any of the creations except the Lord of the Worlds. And so is the statement regarding His statement: Then He sends the angel and breathes into it the spirit, meaning that the breathing is the reason for God creating the spirit and life in it. And so is the statement regarding all the usual causes, for it is by the creation of God Almighty and not by anyone else. So ponder this principle and hold fast to it, for in it is salvation from the doctrines of the people of misguidance, the naturalists and others. Fourth: The scholars did not differ that the soul is breathed into the foetus after one hundred and twenty days, which is the completion of four months and its entry into the fifth, as we have explained in the hadiths. And it is relied upon in what is needed of rulings in the case of affiliation in the event of a dispute, and in the obligation of expenses for the pregnancy of divorced women, because of his certainty of the movement of the foetus in the womb. And it has been said: This is the wisdom in the woman’s waiting period after death, which is four months and ten days, and this entry into the fifth ensures the womb is clear by reaching this period if no pregnancy appears. Fifth: The sperm is definitely nothing, and no ruling applies to it if the woman expels it if it does not come together in the womb. It is as if it were in the man’s loins.
