If she expels it as a clot, we have ascertained that the sperm has settled, come together, and transformed into the first conditions that would establish it as a child. Based on this, the expulsion of the clot and what is above it from the lump of flesh is the expulsion of a pregnancy, by which the womb is cleansed, the waiting period ends, and the ruling of the mother of a child is established for her. This is the school of Malik may God be pleased with him and his companions. Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him said: The expulsion of the clot is not taken into account, but rather the appearance of the image and outline is considered. If the outline is hidden and it is flesh, then there are two opinions based on transmission and deduction. The explicit statement is that the waiting period ends with it and she is not the mother of a child. They said: Because the waiting period ends with flowing blood, so it is more appropriate to do otherwise. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Created and uncreated. Al-Farra’ said: Created means completely created, and uncreated means the miscarriage. Ibn al-A’rabi said: Created means that its creation has begun, and uncreated means that it has not yet been conceived. Ibn Zayd said: Created means that in which God created the head, hands, and feet, and uncreated means that in which He has not created anything. Ibn al-Arabi said: If we go back to the original derivation, then the sperm, the clot, and the lump of flesh are created, because all of them are created by God Almighty. If we go back to the formation, which is the end of creation, as God Almighty said: Then We produced him as another creation (al-Mu’minun 23:14), then that is what Ibn Zayd said. I said: Creation comes from creation, and it has the meaning of abundance. Whatever the stages follow has been created one creation after another. If it is a sperm, then it is created. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Then We produced him as another creation (al-Mu’minun 23:14), and God knows best. It has been said that His statement: formed and unformed refers to the child himself, not to the miscarriage, meaning that some of them the Lord Almighty completes their embryo and creates all of their organs, and some of them are premature, incomplete, and not complete. It has been said that the created is when a woman gives birth at the full term. Ibn Abbas said: The created is what was alive, and the unformed is the miscarriage. He said: Is it okay to cry when you are not well-mannered? Where is the firmness and modesty? Seventh: The scholars agreed that a slave woman is an umm walad mother of a child because she miscarries a fully formed child. According to Malik, Al-Awza’i and others, it is an umm walad a lump of flesh whether it is formed or not. Malik said: If he knows that it is a umm walad a lump of flesh. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa said: If something of the creation of the sons of Adam has become clear to him, such as a finger, an eye or something else, then she is an umm walad mother of a child. They agreed that if the newborn cries out, then the funeral prayer should be performed over him. If he does not cry out, then the funeral prayer should not be performed over him, according to Malik, Abu Hanifa, Al-Shafi’i and others. It was narrated from Ibn ‘Umar that the funeral prayer should be performed over him, and so said Ibn Al-Musayyab, Ibn Sirin and others. It was narrated from Al-Mughira bin Shu’bah that he used to order the funeral prayer over the miscarried child, and he would say: Name them, wash them, shroud them and embalm them, for God has honored your great and small with Islam. He would recite this verse: Indeed, We created you from dust - to - and unformed. Ibn Al-‘Arabi said: Perhaps Al-Mughira bin Shu’bah meant by the miscarried child that which has become clear, so it is the one who is named, and that which has not become clear does not exist. Some of the Salaf said: Prayer is performed for him when the soul is breathed into him and he is four months old. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If the newborn cries out, he inherits. Cries out: raising the voice. So every newborn who does that, or moves, sneezes, or breathes, he inherits because of the evidence of life in him. This is what Sufyan al-Thawri, al-Awza’i, and al-Shafi’i held. Al-Khattabi said: The best of it is the opinion of the people of opinion. Malik said: He has no inheritance even if he moves or sneezes, as long as he does not cry out. It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, al-Sha’bi, al-Zuhri, and Qatadah. Eighth: Malik may God be pleased with him said: Whatever a woman expels from a lump of flesh or a clot or what is known to be a child if her stomach is struck, then there is a blood money for it. Al-Shafi’i said: There is nothing in it until its creation is clear. Malik said: If the fetus is aborted and does not cry out, then there is a blood money for it. Whether it moves or sneezes, then there is a blood money for it at all, until it cries out, then there is a full blood money for it. Al-Shafi’i may God be pleased with him and all the jurists of the countries said: If its life is known by movement, sneezing, crying out, or anything else by which its life is certain, then there is a blood money for it. Ninth: Judge Ismail stated that a woman’s waiting period ends with a miscarriage, and he argued that it is a pregnancy, and said: God Almighty said: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth (al-Talaq 65:4). Judge Ismail said: The evidence for that is that he inherits from his father, which indicates his existence as a creation and his being a child and a pregnancy. Ibn Al-Arabi said: None of these rulings are connected to him unless he is created. I said: What we mentioned about the derivation and his saying, peace and blessings be upon him: Indeed, each of you is gathered together in his mother’s womb indicates the correctness of what we said. And because the one who miscarries the clot and the lump of flesh is true of the woman if she miscarries it, that is, she was pregnant and gave birth to what was settled in her womb, so she is included in the saying of God Almighty: And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth (al-Talaq 65:4). And because she gave birth to the beginning of the child from a sperm embodied like a plan, and this is clear. Tenth: Ibn Majah narrated: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah narrated to us, Khalid bin Mukhallad narrated to us, Yazid narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Malik Al-Nawfali, on the authority of Yazid bin Ruman, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man falling in front of me is more beloved to me than a knight I leave behind me. Al-Hakim included it in his book, Ma’rifat Ulum al-Hadith, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: He is more beloved to me than a thousand knights I leave behind me. Eleventh: To show you means: the perfection of Our power through Our control over the stages of your creation. And We place in the wombs was read with the accusative Naqr and Nakhrij We take out. Abu Hatim narrated it on the authority of Abu Zaid on the authority of Al-Mufaddal on the authority of Asim who said: Abu Hatim said: The accusative is for conjunction. Al-Zajjaj said: Naqr is in the nominative only, because the meaning is not: We did that to place in the wombs whomever We will, but rather He created them, the Almighty, to guide them to the right path and righteousness. It was said: The meaning is to show them the matter of resurrection, so it is an interjection between the two statements. This group read Wanqar with the nominative, meaning: We place. This is the reading of the majority. It was read: And We place in the nominative and He takes out you with the ya’, and the nominative is permissible according to this. Ibn Waththab read What We will with the kasra on the noon. The appointed term differs according to the fetus [and] fetus, so there are those who miscarry and there are those whose matter is completed and who come out alive. He said, Whatever We will, and did not say whoever We will, because it refers to the pregnancy, meaning that He places in the wombs whatever We will of the pregnancy and the embryo, which is inanimate, so He referred to it with the word what. Twelfth: The Almighty’s saying: Then We bring you forth as children, meaning children, so it is a generic name. Also, the Arabs may name the plural with the singular name. The poet said: He makes me fall in love with her and makes me swear that the critics are not my prince He did not say princes. Al-Mubarrad said: It is a noun that is used as a source like contentment and justice, so it applies to the singular and plural. God the Almighty said: Or children who are not aware of the private parts of women (al-Nur 24:31). Al-Tabari said: It is an accusative of distinction, like the Almighty’s saying: But if they give up willingly to you anything of it (al-Nisa 4:4). It was said: The meaning is then We bring forth each one of you as a child. A child is used from the time of separation of the boy until puberty. The offspring of every wild animal is also a child. It is said: a child girl, two child girls, a child slave girl, a child boy, and two child boys. It is also said: a child and a child girl, two children, two children, and children. It is not said: children. A woman has a child. A female gazelle with her child, and she is close to giving birth. The same is true of a female camel, and the plural is matafil and matafil. A child with a fat-ha on the taa is soft. It is said: a child girl, meaning soft, and the fingers of a child. The night has become a child if its darkness comes. And the child with movement: after the afternoon, when the sun begins to set. And the child also: rain. He said: Luhad Jada Child of the Pleiades Then that you may reach your full strength. It was said that then is redundant like the and in His statement: Until, when they come to it and its gates are opened (al-Zumar 39:73), because then is one of the letters of sequence like the and. “Your full strength” is the perfection of your minds and the end of your powers. Its explanation has already been mentioned in Al-An’am. “And among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit and lowest stage of life,” meaning the worst and lowest of it, which is old age and senility, so that he does not understand. For this reason, He said: So that he may not know anything after having known. As He said in Surat Ya-Sin 36:And whom We grant long life, We reverse him in creation (Ya-Sin 36:68). And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would supplicate and say: O God, I seek refuge in You from miserliness, I seek refuge in You from cowardice, I seek refuge in You from being sent back to the worst part of life, and I seek refuge in You from the trial of this world and the torment of the grave.” Narrated by Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Sa’d, who said: He used to teach them to his sons as a schoolmaster teaches his young boys. This meaning has already been mentioned in An-Nahl. The Almighty’s statement: And you will see the earth lifeless is a stronger indication of the Resurrection. In the first, He said: For We created you from dust, addressing a group. In the second, He said: And you will see the earth, addressing one person. Thus, the wording was separated from the wording, but the meaning is connected in terms of the argument against those who deny the Resurrection. Lifeless means dry, not growing anything, as Ibn Jurayj said. It was also said: wasted. And wasted means erosion. Al-A’sha said: The dead woman said, Why is your body so pale? I see your clothes are worn out. Al-Harawi: Hamdah means dry and full of dust. Shammar said: It is said: The trees of the earth are hammad if they have decayed and gone. And their voices are hammad if they are still. The hammadah of the earth is that there is no life in it, no plants, no branches, and no rain has fallen on it. In the hadith: Until he almost died of hunger meaning he was dying. It is said: the garment became worn out and the fire died down. God the Almighty said: So when We send down upon it water, it quivers meaning moves. Shaking is intense movement. It is said: I shook something and it shook, meaning I moved it and it moved. The camel driver shook the camels and they shook when they moved in their gait with his driving. And the planet shook in its swoop. And a shaking planet. So the earth shakes with the plants, because the plants do not emerge from it until some of them are removed from each other in a subtle removal, so He called it shaking metaphorically. It was said: Its plants shook, so the noun was omitted, as Al-Mubarrad said. And its shaking is the intensity of its movement, as the poet said: It bends when it stands and sways when it walks, just as a branch of the laurel tree sways with green leaves. The vibration in plants is more evident than in the ground. And it rose means it rose and increased. It was also said: it swelled, and the meaning is the same, and its origin is increase. The thing ribā yarbūn means it increased, and from it is ribā and rabwah. Yazid ibn al-Qa’qa’ and Khalid ibn Ilyas read wa rabā’at meaning it rose until it became like a guard, and it is the one who protects the people on something high, so he is rabī’ah and rabī’ah as an exaggeration. Imru’ al-Qays said: We sent a prophet before that, as slender as a wolf of the Ghadah tree, walking in distress and fearing it. And brought forth means brought forth. Of every pair means color. Bahij means beautiful, according to Qatada. That is, it delights whoever sees it. And bahij is goodness. It is said: a man of bahij. And he has bahij with the letter damma with bahajah and bahajah, so he is bahij. And he delighted me with his beauty. And since he described the earth as producing vegetation, it indicates that his saying: shaken and swelled refers to the earth, not to the vegetation. And God knows best.
22:6: The Almighty said: That is because God is the Truth after mentioning the need of all beings for Him and their being subjected according to His power and choice in His statement: O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection - to His statement - Bright. He said after that: "That is because God is the Truth and that He gives life to the dead and that He is over all things competent * and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that God will raise up those in the graves". So the Almighty and Exalted alerted with this that everything other than Him, even if it is truly existent, has no reality of itself, because it is subjected and spent. The True Truth is the absolute existent, the absolute rich, and the existence of every existent is due to the necessity of its existence, and for this reason He said at the end of the Surah: And that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood (al-Hajj 22:62). The Truth is the existing, constant, who does not change or disappear, and He is God the Almighty. It was said: He has the right over His servants. It was said: The Truth means in His actions. Al-Zajjaj said: That is in the nominative case, meaning the matter is what was described to you and explained. Because God is the Truth meaning because God is the Truth. He said: It is possible for that to be in the accusative case, meaning God did that because He is the Truth. And that He brings the dead to life meaning that and that He is over all things competent meaning that He is able to do whatever He wills.
22:7: And that the Hour is coming is an appositive to his statement: That is because God is the Truth in terms of wording, and not an appositive in meaning, since it is not said that God did what was mentioned that the Hour is coming, rather it is necessary to imply an action that includes it, i.e. and that they should know that the Hour is coming without a doubt i.e. without a doubt. And that God will raise up those in the graves meaning for reward and punishment.
22:8: God the Almighty said: And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book. That is, a clear proof. It was revealed about An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith. It was also said: About Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, as stated by Ibn Abbas. Most of the scholars agree that it was revealed about An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith like the first verse, so they are in one group, and the repetition is for exaggeration in the blame, as you say to a man, blaming and rebuking him: You did this! It is possible that the repetition is because he described him in every verse with an addition, so it is as if he said: An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith disputes about God without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil, and An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith disputes about God without knowledge and without guidance or an enlightening Book, to lead people astray from the path of God. It is like saying: Zaid curses me and Zaid hits me, and it is a useful repetition, as stated by Al-Qushayri. It has also been said that about a dozen verses were revealed about him. The first verse means that he denied resurrection, and the second means that he denied prophethood and that the Qur’an was revealed from God. It has been said that it was said by Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith that the angels were daughters of God, and this is an argument about God Almighty. Min is in the nominative case as a subject. The predicate is in His statement: And of mankind.
22:9: The second of his affection is an accusative of state. It can be interpreted in two meanings: One of them: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: He is Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, he turned his neck in joy and pride. The other meaning: And it is the saying of Al-Farraa - that the estimate: And among the people is he who disputes about God without knowledge, the second of his affection, meaning turning away from the remembrance, mentioned by Al-Nahhas and Mujahid and Qatada said: Twisting his neck in disbelief. Ibn Abbas: Turning away from what he is called to in disbelief. The meaning is the same. Al-Awza'i narrated on the authority of Mukhallad bin Hussein on the authority of Hisham bin Hassan on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: The second of his affection to lead astray from the way of God He said: He is the one who innovates. Al-Mubarrad: The affection is what is bent from the neck. Al-Mufaddal said: The affection is the side, and from it is their saying so-and-so looks at his affections, meaning at his sides. And the man's affection is from his head to his hips. And likewise the affection of everything is its sides. It is said: So-and-so turned away from me if he turned away from you. The meaning is that he turned away from the truth in his argument and did not consider his words. It is like the Almighty’s saying: “And he turned away arrogantly as if he had not heard it” (Luqman 31:7). And the Almighty’s saying: They turned their heads (al-Munafiqun 63:5). And His saying: He turned away and distanced himself (al-Isra’ 17:83). And His saying: He went to his family, strutting (al-Qiyamah 75:33). To mislead from the path of God meaning from obeying God the Almighty. It is read to mislead with the opening of the ya’. The lam is the lam of consequence, meaning he argues and misleads, like the Almighty’s saying: To be for them an enemy and a cause of grief (al-Qasas 28:28) meaning that it was like that for them. And similar to it is: When a party of you associated partners with their Lord * To disbelieve (al-Nahl 16:54-55). For him in this world is disgrace meaning humiliation and degradation because of the ugly mention of him on the tongues of the believers until the Day of Resurrection, as He said: And do not obey every worthless swearer (al-Qalam 68:10) and the verse. And the Almighty said: May the hands of Abu Lahab perish, and perish he (al-Masad 111:1). It was said that the disgrace here is killing, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith on the day of Badr with patience, as mentioned at the end of Al-Anfal. And We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the Burning Fire meaning the fire of Hell.
22:10: That is because of what your hands have put forth. That is, it will be said to him in the Hereafter when he enters the Fire: That is the punishment because of what your hands have put forth of sins and disbelief. The word hand refers to the whole, because the hand that acts and strikes is for the whole. And that means this, as mentioned earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah.
22:11: The Almighty said: And among mankind is he who worships God on the edge of the earth “of” is in the nominative case as a subject, and the completion is turned on his face according to the reading of the majority lost. And this verse is report about the hypocrites. Ibn Abbas said: He means Shaybah ibn Rabi’ah, who had converted to Islam before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared, and when revelation came to him, Shaybah ibn Rabi’ah apostatized. Abu Sa’id al-Khudri said: A Jewish man converted to Islam and lost his sight and wealth. He had a bad omen about Islam, so he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Excuse me! He said: Islam is not to be excused. He said: I have not found any good in this religion of mine! I have lost my sight, wealth, and children! He said: O Jew, Islam melts men as fire melts dross from iron, silver, and gold. Then God Almighty revealed: And among mankind is he who worships God on the verge. Israel narrated on the authority of Abu Hasin on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: And among mankind is he who worships God on the verge. He said: A man would come to the city and if his wife gave birth to a boy and his horses produced, he would say, This is a good religion. But if his wife did not give birth and his horses did not produce, he would say, This is a bad religion. The commentators said: It was revealed about some Bedouins who would come to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and convert to Islam. If they were granted ease, they would stay, and if they were afflicted with hardship, they would apostatize. It was also said: It was revealed about Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith. Ibn Zayd and others said: It was revealed about the hypocrites. The meaning of on the edge is on doubt, as Mujahid and others said. Its reality is that he is weak in his worship, like the weakness of one who stands on a verge that is disturbed in it. The verge of everything is its edge and its edge alone, and from it is the verge of the mountain, which is its defined top. It was said: on the edge means on one face, which is to worship Him in ease and not in hardship. If they worshipped God with gratitude in ease and patience in hardship, they would not have worshipped God on the verge. It was said: On the edge on a condition, and that is because Shaiba bin Rabi’ah said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, before his matter became apparent: Pray to your Lord to provide me with wealth, camels, horses and children so that I may believe in you and be guided to your religion. So he prayed for him and God Almighty provided him with what he wished for. Then God Almighty wanted to test him and test him, and He knows best about him, so He took from him what he had been provided with after he had become Muslim, so he apostatized from Islam. So God Almighty revealed about him: And of the people is he who worships God on the edge, meaning a condition. Al-Hasan said: He is the hypocrite who worships God with his tongue without his heart. In short, this is the one who worships God on the edge, not completely. He explained this by saying: If good befalls him, meaning a healthy body and a comfortable life, he is satisfied and remains on his religion. But if a trial befalls him, meaning the opposite of that with which he is tested, he turns back on his face, meaning he apostatizes and returns to the face he was on of disbelief. “He has lost this world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss.” Mujahid, Humayd ibn Qays, al-A’raj, al-Zuhri, and Ibn Abi Ishaq - and it was narrated on the authority of Ya’qub - read loser of this world with an alif, in the accusative case as a state. Accordingly, one should not stop at his face. His loss of this world is that he will have no share in the spoils or praise, and the loss of the Hereafter is that he will have no reward in it.
22:12: The Almighty said: He calls upon other than God meaning this is the one who returns to disbelief and worships an idol that neither benefits nor harms. That is the farthest misguidance said Al-Farra’ Al-Tawil.
22:13: The Almighty said: He calls upon him whose harm is nearer than his benefit meaning this one who turned on his face calls upon someone whose harm is nearer than his benefit, meaning in the Hereafter because he entered the Fire through his worship, and he did not see any benefit from him at all, but he said: His harm is nearer than his benefit to elevate the statement, like the Almighty's statement: And either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error (Saba': 24). It was said: They worship them thinking that they will intercede for them tomorrow, as the Almighty said: And they worship besides God that which neither harms them nor benefits them, and they say, 'These are our intercessors with God' (Yunus 10:18). The Almighty also said: We worship them only that they may bring us nearer to God (al-Zumar 39:3). Al-Farra', Al-Kisa'i, and Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning of the statement is an oath and a delay, meaning he calls upon God for someone whose harm is nearer than his benefit. So the lam is brought forward in the wrong place. Min is in the accusative case with yad'u and the lam is the answer to the oath. Dharah is the subject and aqrab is its predicate. An-Nahhas weakened the delay of the lam and said: The lam has no ability to change its position or delay. I said: The right of the letter lam is to be presented and it may be delayed. The poet said: My uncle is you and from Jarir, his uncle will attain glory and honor his uncles That is, you are my uncle, and it has been mentioned before. An-Nahhas: Ali bin Sulaiman narrated to us on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid, who said: There is an ellipsis in the speech, and the meaning is that he calls upon the one whose harm is closer than his benefit, a god. An-Nahhas said: I think this statement was a mistake on the part of Muhammad bin Yazid, because it has no meaning, because what comes after the lam is a subject, so it is not permissible to put god in the accusative case, and I think that Muhammad bin Yazid’s school of thought is nothing but the statement of Al-Akhfash, and it is the best that has been said about the verse in my opinion, and God knows best. He said: He calls upon means he says, and whoever is a subject and its predicate is elliptical, and the meaning is that he says to the one whose harm is closer than his benefit, his god. I said: Al-Qushayri, may God have mercy on him, mentioned this statement on the authority of Al-Zajjaj and Al-Mahdawi on the authority of Al-Akhfash, and he completed its parsing, saying: Ya’du’u means says, and man is a subject, and darah is a second subject, and aqrab is its predicate, and the sentence is the relative clause of man, and the predicate of man is omitted, and the meaning is he says to whom his harm is closer than his benefit is his God, and similar to it is the statement of Antarah: They call Antar and the spears are like the shafts of a well in the frankincense of the dark-skinned man. Al-Qushayri said: The disbeliever who says the idol is my god does not say its harm is closer than its benefit, but the meaning is that the disbeliever says to the one whose harm is closer than his benefit in the Muslims’ saying, My god and my God. It is like the saying of God the Almighty: O magician, call upon your Lord for us (al-Zukhruf 43:49), meaning, O magician, with those who call you a magician. Al-Zajjaj said that it is possible for calls upon to be in the position of a state, and in it is an omitted ha, meaning that is the distant misguidance that he calls upon, meaning in the state of his calling upon it, so in calls upon there is an implied ha, and one stops at this on calls upon. His saying: To the one whose harm is closer than his benefit is a new statement raised by the beginning, and its predicate is the worst protector, and this is because the lam is for an oath and emphasis, so it was made the beginning of the statement. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that that means who, and it is in the accusative case because calls occurs before it, meaning that which is the distant misguidance calls, as He said: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses? (Ta-Ha 20:17) meaning what is that. Then His saying: For whom is his harm? is a subject statement, and What an evil protector is the predicate of the subject. The interpretation of the verse according to this is: He calls, which is the distant misguidance. He presented the object, which is who, as you say: Zayd strikes, and Abu Ali approved of it. Al-Zajjaj claimed that the grammarians overlooked this statement, and he recited: Lentils, what do you have to do with the emirate? I escaped and you are carrying a divorce. Any and which. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Farraa also said: It is permissible for yad’u to be repeated on what preceded it, in order to increase this action which is supplication, and it is not transitive since you have made it transitive first, meaning he supplicates besides God to that which neither benefits him nor harms him, like I hit Zayd, I hit, then you deleted yad’u at the end, being satisfied with the first. Al-Farraa said: It is permissible for to whom harm is nearer to break the lam, meaning he supplicates to the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit, God the Almighty said: Because your Lord has inspired her (Al-Zalzalah 49:5), meaning to her. Al-Farraa and Al-Qaffal also said: The lam is a connection, meaning he supplicates to the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit, meaning he worships Him. And it is the same in the reading of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud. Labi’as al-mawla means in mutual support, and Labi’as al-‘ashir means companion, friend, and intimate friend. Mujahid means the idol.
22:14: The Almighty says: Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. After mentioning the state of the polytheists, the hypocrites, and the devils, He also mentioned the state of the believers in the Hereafter. Indeed, God does what He wills. That is, He rewards whomever He wills and punishes whomever He wills. So for the believers is Paradise by virtue of His true promise and His grace, and for the disbelievers is Hell by virtue of His previous justice, not that the action of the Lord is explained by the action of the servants.
22:15: The Almighty said: Whoever thinks that God will not support him in this world and the Hereafter - let him stretch out a way to the heaven. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: One of the best things that has been said about it is that the meaning is whoever thinks that God will not support Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that he is prepared to cut off the victory that he has been given. Let him stretch out a way to the heaven. That is, let him seek a trick to reach the heaven. Then let him cut off. That is, let him cut off victory if it is prepared for him. Then let him see whether his plot will avert it. His plot is what angers him about the victory of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The benefit of the statement is that if the plot and trick are not prepared for him by doing such a thing, he will not be able to cut off victory. Ibn Abbas also said: The metaphor in May God support him refers to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and even if he was not mentioned, all the speech indicates him, because faith is faith in God and in Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and turning away from religion is turning away from the religion that Muhammad brought, meaning whoever thinks that those who are hostile to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and whoever worships God on the basis of the word We will not support Muhammad, then let him do such and such. Ibn Abbas also said that the ha refers to whoever, and the meaning is: whoever thinks that God will not provide for him, then let him choke, then let him kill himself, because there is no good in a life devoid of God’s help. And victory, according to this statement, is provision. The Arabs say: Whoever supports me, God will support him, meaning whoever gives me, God will give him. And from that is the saying of the Arabs: a victorious land, meaning rain-fed. Al-Faq’asi said: You do not give a man more than he deserves, nor do you own the part that the rain supports. And Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: Whoever thinks that God will not support him meaning that He will not provide for him. This is the saying of Abu Ubaidah. It was said that the ha refers to the religion, and the meaning is: Whoever thinks that God will not support his religion. Then let him extend a rope meaning a rope. The rope is what is used to reach something. To the sky to the roof of the house. Ibn Zayd: It is the well-known sky. The Kufians read Then let him cut with a sukoon on the lam. An-Nahhas said: This is far-fetched in Arabic, because then is not like waw and fa, because it is stopped on and is separate. In the reading of Abdullah, Falaqti’uhu, then let him see whether they will remove his guile that which enrages him. It was said that ma means who, meaning will they remove his guile that enrages him? So the ha was deleted to make it lighter. It was said that ma means the source, meaning will they remove his guile that enrages him?
22:16: The Almighty said: And thus We have sent it down as clear signs meaning the Qur’an. And that God meaning and thus that God guides whom He wills He made the existence of guidance dependent on His will, for He is the Guide and there is no guide other than Him.
22:17: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who believed meaning in God and in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And those who were Jews are the Jews, who are affiliated with the religion of Moses, peace be upon him. And the Sabians are a people who worship the stars. And the Christians are those affiliated with the religion of Jesus. And the Magians are the fire worshippers who say that the world has two origins: light and darkness. Qatada said that there are five religions, four for Satan and one for the Most Merciful. It was said that the Magians are originally impure because they practice impurity, and the letters meem and noon alternate like ghaym and ghayn, and aym and ayin. All of this has been mentioned in full in Surat Al-Baqarah. And those who associated others with God are the Arabs who worship idols. Indeed, God will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection meaning He will judge and rule. For the disbelievers is Hell, and for the believers is Paradise. It was said that this distinction is so that the truthful can be distinguished from the false through necessary knowledge, and today the truthful can be distinguished from the false through observation and reasoning. God is Witness over all things meaning of the actions, movements and words of His creation, so nothing of them escapes Him, glory be to Him! His statement, God will judge between them is the predicate of in in His statement, Indeed, those who believe, just as you say: Indeed, Zayd, good is with him. Al-Farra' said: It is not permissible in the statement, Indeed, Zayd, his brother is leaving, and he claimed that it is only permissible in the verse because the statement has the meaning of recompense, meaning whoever believes and whoever becomes a Jew or a Christian or a Sabian, He will judge between them, and their reckoning is with God, the Almighty. Abu Ishaq responded to Al-Farra's statement, and he found his statement ugly: It is not permissible to say, Indeed, Zayd, his brother is leaving, he said: Because there is no difference between Zayd and those, and in is used with every subject, so you say, Indeed, Zayd is leaving, then you bring in and say, Indeed, Zayd is leaving. The poet said: The Caliph, God has clothed him in a garment of glory, through which good endings are hoped for.
22:18: The Almighty said: Have you not seen that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth? This is the vision of the heart, meaning, have you not seen with your heart and mind? The meaning of prostration was presented in (Al-Baqarah), and the prostration of inanimate objects in (Al-Nahl). And the sun is conjoined with whoever. And so is and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the beasts and many of the people. Then he said: And many upon whom the punishment is justified This is a problem in terms of grammar, how did it not become accusative to conjoin what the verb worked on, like And the wrongdoers - for them He has prepared a painful punishment (al-Insan 76:31)? Al-Kisa'i and Al-Farra' claimed that if it were to become accusative it would have been good, but the nominative was chosen because the meaning is and many refused to prostrate, so it would be subject and predicate, and the discussion was completed when he said and many of the people. It is permissible for it to be conjoined, on the condition that prostration is humility and submission to the management of God, the Almighty, from weakness and strength, health and sickness, good and bad, and this includes everything. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, based on the estimation: And he humiliated many, upon whom the punishment is due, and the like. It was said: The speech ended when he said: and the beasts, then he began and said: and many people in Paradise and many upon whom the punishment is due. And likewise it was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: The meaning is: And many people are in Paradise and many upon whom the punishment is due, as mentioned by Ibn al-Anbari. Abu al-Aaliyah said: There is no star, moon, or sun in the heavens except that it prostrates to God when it sets, then it does not turn away until it is given permission to return from its place of rising. Al-Qushayri said: This was mentioned in a chain of transmission report regarding the sun, so this is a real prostration, and its necessity is the composition of life and reason in this prostrator. I said: The chain of transmission report that he referred to was narrated by Muslim, and it will come in Surat Ya Sin when God the Almighty says: And the sun runs to its resting place (Ya Sin: 38). The meaning of prostration in language has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. God the Almighty says: And he whom God humiliates - for him there is none to honor him. That is, whoever He humiliates with misery and disbelief, no one is able to ward off humiliation from him. Ibn Abbas said: Whoever is negligent in worshipping God will end up in the Fire. Indeed, God does what He wills means that their destiny is the Fire, so no one can object to Him. Al-Akhfash, Al-Kisa’i, and Al-Farra’ narrated: And he whom God humiliates - for him there is none to honor him. That is, honor.
22:19: The Almighty said: These two are opponents who disputed about their Lord. Muslim narrated on the authority of Qais bin Abbad who said: I heard Abu Dharr swearing that These two are opponents who have disputed about their Lord was revealed about those who came out on the day of Badr: Hamza, Ali, Ubaidah ibn al-Harith, may God be pleased with them, Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah, and al-Walid ibn Utbah. Muslim, may God have mercy on him, concluded his book with this hadith. Ibn Abbas said: These three verses were revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina about three believers and three disbelievers, and he named them, as Abu Dharr mentioned. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: I will be the first to kneel to dispute before God on the Day of Resurrection, meaning the story of his duel with his two companions, as mentioned by al-Bukhari. Hilal ibn Yasaaf, Ata’ ibn Yasar, and others agreed with this statement. Ikrimah said: What is meant by the two opponents is Paradise and Hell. They disputed, and Hell said: He created me for His punishment. And Paradise said: He created me for His mercy. I said: There is a hadith on the dispute between Heaven and Hell on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Paradise and Hell argued, and one said: The tyrants and the arrogant will enter me. And another said: The weak and the poor will enter me. So God, the Most High, said to the one: You are My punishment, with which I punish whomever I will, and He said to the other: You are My mercy, with which I have mercy on whomever I will, and each of you will have her fill.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari, Muslim and Al-Tirmidhi, who said: A good and authentic hadith. Ibn Abbas also said: They are the People of the Book. They said to the believers: We are closer to God than you, and our Book preceded you, and our Prophet came before your Prophet. And the believers said: We are more deserving of God than you. We believed in Muhammad, we believed in your Prophet and in the Book that was revealed to him, and you know our Prophet and you abandoned him and disbelieved in him out of envy. So this was their dispute, and this verse was revealed about them. This is the statement of Qatada, and the first statement is more correct. It was narrated by Al-Bukhari on the authority of Hajjaj bin Munhal on the authority of Hisham on the authority of Abu Hashim on the authority of Abu Majlaz on the authority of Qais bin Ibad on the authority of Abu Dharr, and Muslim on the authority of Amr bin Zararah on the authority of Hisham, and it was narrated by Sulayman Al-Taymi on the authority of Abu Majlaz on the authority of Qais bin Ibad on the authority of Ali, who said: This verse was revealed about us and in our duel on the day of Badr: These two are opponents who have disputed about their Lord - until His saying - the punishment of the burning fire. Ibn Kathir read These two are opponents with a shaddah on the nun in these two. Al-Farra’ interpreted the opponents as two groups of people of two religions, and he claimed that one opponent was the Muslims and the other was the Jews and Christians, who disputed about the religion of their Lord. He said: So he said: They disputed because they are a plural. He said: If he had said they disputed, it would have been permissible. Al-Nahhas said: This is the interpretation of someone who has no knowledge of the hadith or the books of the people of interpretation, because the hadith about this verse is well-known. It was narrated by Sufyan al-Thawri and others on the authority of Abu Hashim on the authority of Abu Majlaz on the authority of Qays ibn Abbad who said: I heard Abu Dharr swearing that this verse was revealed about Hamza, Ali, Ubaidah ibn al-Harith ibn Abdul Muttalib, Utbah and Shaybah the sons of Rabiah, and al-Walid ibn Utbah. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala narrated this on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas. There is a fourth opinion that they are all believers and all disbelievers, regardless of their religion. This was said by Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ata ibn Abi Rabah, Asim ibn Abi al-Najud, and al-Kalbi. This opinion of generality includes what was revealed about them and others. It was said: It was revealed about the dispute over resurrection and recompense, as some people said it and others denied it. So those who disbelieved means from the sects mentioned above. For them will be cut out garments of fire meaning sewn and made smooth, and fire was likened to garments because it is a garment for them like garments. And his saying: cut out means that garments of fire will be cut out for them in the Hereafter. It was mentioned in the past tense because whatever was from the report of the Hereafter, what was promised of it is like the actual reality. God the Most High said: And when God said, ‘O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people?’ (al-Ma’idah 5:116) meaning God the Most High says. It is possible to say that those garments have now been prepared for them to wear when they go to the Fire. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Of fire is of copper, so those garments are of copper that have been melted and they are the garments mentioned in the molten state of the night, and there is nothing in the vessels that is hotter than it. It was said: The meaning is that the Fire has surrounded them as the torn garments surround them when they wear them, so from this aspect they have become garments because in encompassing they are like garments, like And We have made the night as a covering (An-Naba’: 10). Boiling water will be poured over their heads meaning hot water boiling in the fire of Hell. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The boiling water will be poured over their heads, and the boiling water will penetrate until it reaches their stomachs, and what is in their stomachs will melt until it flows out of their feet, and it will be returned to how it was.” He said: A good, authentic, rare hadith.
22:20: يسخis melted.معها ما في حمصand sahr is the melting of fat. And sahrah is that which has melted from it. It is said: I sahrut something and it melted, meaning I melted it and it melted, so it is sahir. Ibn Ahmar said, describing a young quail: It tells of a finding that was thrown into a sand dune, melted by the sun, but not melted. That is, the sun melts it, so he is patient with that. And the skins meaning, the skins are burned, or the skins are roasted, because the skins do not melt, but rather everything is combined with what is appropriate for it, so it is as you say: I came to him and he fed me tharid, yes by God, and bitter milk, meaning, he gave me milk to drink. And the poet said: I fed her straw and cold water.
22:21: And they will have iron maces meaning they will strike and repel with them. The singular is muqama, and muqama is also like a whip, which is used to strike the elephant's head. You may have qamamathu if you hit it with it. Qamamathu and aqamatuhu have the same meaning, meaning you have subdued and humiliated him, so he was subdued. Ibn al-Sikkit said: I suppressed the man from me if he attacked you and you repelled him from you. It was said: Al-Qama' are hammers, and they are also the marazib. In the hadith: “In the hand of every angel of the guardians of Hell is a whip with two branches. He strikes a blow and with it seventy thousand fall.” It was said: The whips are whips of fire, and they are called that because they subdue the one being struck, that is, they humiliate him.
22:22: The Almighty said: Whenever they want to get out of it meaning from the Fire. They are returned to it by being struck with whips. Abu Dhabiyan said: It was mentioned to us that they try to get out of the Fire when it swells and boils with them, and they are thrown into it to the top of its doors, and they want to get out, but the keepers return them to it with whips. It was said: When their grief intensifies in it, they flee, and whoever of them reaches its edge, the angels return them to it with whips, and they say to them, And taste the punishment of the burning meaning the burning, like the painful and the painful. It was said: The noun of burning comes from burning. Something is burned by fire and is burned, and the noun is burning and burning. Taste: contact with which the taste is perceived, and here it is an expansion and what is meant by it is their perception of pain.
22:23: The Almighty said: Indeed, God will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. When He mentioned one of the two opponents, which is the disbeliever, He mentioned the state of the other opponent, which is the believer. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold. "Of" is a relative clause. Bracelets is the plural of bracelet, and the singular of bracelet is bracelet, and there are three languages for it: the damma of the seen, the kasra of it, and the iswar. The commentators said: Since the kings used to wear bracelets and crowns in this world, God made that for the people of Paradise, and there is no one from the people of Paradise who does not have three bracelets on his hand: a bracelet of gold, a bracelet of silver, and a bracelet of pearls. He said here and in Fatir 35:"Of bracelets of gold and pearls" (Fatir 35:33) and He said in Surat al-Insan 76:"And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver" (al-Insan 76:21). And in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah I heard my friend, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, say: "The adornment of the believer reaches where the ablution reaches." It was said: Eagles adorn themselves with gold and men with silver. There is a view on this, and the Qur’an rejects it. "And pearls Nafi', Ibn al-Qa'qa', Shaybah, and Asim read here and in Surat al-Mala'ikah pearls" in the accusative case, meaning they adorn themselves with pearls. They provided evidence that it is written in all the copies of the Qur'an here with an alif. Likewise, Ya'qub, al-Jahdari, and 'Isa ibn 'Umar read it in the accusative case here and in the genitive case in Fatir, following the Qur'an, and because it is written here with an alif and there without an alif. The rest read it in the genitive case in both places. Abu Bakr did not pronounce the word "pearls" with a hamza in the entire Qur'an, and it is what is extracted from the sea from the inside of a shell. Al-Qushayri said: What is meant is the setting of bracelets with pearls, and it is not far-fetched that there will be a bracelet of solid pearls in Paradise. I said: This is the apparent meaning of the Qur’an, rather its text. Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever reads and pearls in the accusative case should stop at it and not at gold. Al-Sijistani said: Whoever puts pearls in the accusative case, the sufficient stop is of gold, because the meaning is and they adorn themselves with pearls. Ibn al-Anbari said: It is not as he said, because if we put pearls in the accusative case, we arrange it according to the wording of bracelets, and if we put it in the accusative case, we arrange it according to the interpretation of bracelets, and it is as if we said: they adorn themselves with bracelets and pearls therein. So in the accusative case it is like in the accusative case, so there is no meaning to cutting it off from the first. The Almighty says: And their clothing therein will be silk. That is, everything they wear of their furnishings, clothing, and curtains will be silk, which is much better than what is in this world. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter, and whoever drinks alcohol in this world will not drink it in the Hereafter, and whoever drinks from a vessel of gold or silver will not drink from it in the Hereafter.” Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The clothing of the people of Paradise, the drink of the people of Paradise, and the vessels of the people of Paradise. If it is said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) equated these three things and that he forbade them in the Hereafter, will he forbid them when he enters Paradise? We say: Yes! If he does not repent from them, he will be forbidden from them in the Hereafter even if he enters Paradise, because he hastened to do what God forbade him in this world. It is not said: It is only forbidden at the time when he is being tormented in the Fire or during the length of his stay in the place of standing. As for when he enters Paradise, no, because being deprived of any of the pleasures of Paradise for someone who is in Paradise is a type of punishment and accountability, and Paradise is not a place of punishment, nor is there accountability in it in any way. So we say: What you mentioned is possible, were it not for what came that which refutes this possibility and rejects it from the apparent meaning of the hadith that we mentioned. And what the imams narrated from the hadith of Ibn Umar from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever drinks alcohol in this world and does not repent from it will be deprived of it in the Hereafter. The basic principle is to adhere to the apparent meaning until a text is presented that refutes it. Indeed, a text has been presented that confirms the authenticity of what we have mentioned, which is what Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated in his Musnad: Hisham told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Dawud al-Sarraj, on the authority of Abu Sa`id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the Hereafter, and if he enters Paradise, the people of Paradise will wear it, but he will not wear it. This is a clear text and its chain of transmission is authentic. If and if he enters Paradise, the people of Paradise will wear it, but he will not wear it is from the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then this is the ultimate statement. If it is from the words of the narrator as mentioned, then he is more knowledgeable about what is said and more certain of the situation, and something like it cannot be said based on opinion, and God knows best. The same is true of whoever drinks alcohol and does not repent. “And whoever uses vessels of gold and silver” Just as he does not desire the status of someone higher than him, and that is not a punishment, likewise he does not desire the wine or silk of Paradise, and that is not a punishment. We have mentioned all of this in the book Al-Tadhkirah in full, and praise be to God, and we mentioned in it that the trees of Paradise and their fruits will blossom into the garments of Paradise, and we have mentioned this in Surat Al-Kahf.
22:24: God the Almighty says: And they are guided to the good of speech meaning they are directed to that. Ibn Abbas said: He means there is no god but God and praise be to God. It was said: the Qur'an, then it was said: This is in this world, they are guided to the testimony and the recitation of the Qur'an. And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy meaning to the path of God. The path of God is His religion, which is Islam. It was said: They are guided in the Hereafter to the good of speech, which is praise be to God, because they will say tomoral-Saff 61:Praise be to God who has guided us to this guidance, praise be to God who has removed sorrow from us, so there is no idle talk or lies in Paradise, so what they say is good speech. And they are guided to the path of God in Paradise, because there is nothing in Paradise that contradicts the command of God. It was said: The good of speech is what comes to them from God of good tidings And they are guided to the path of the Praiseworthy meaning to the path to Paradise.
22:25: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: Indeed, those who disbelieve and turn away refers the speech back to the polytheists of the Arabs when they turned away the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from the Sacred Mosque in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah. This is because it was not known that they had turned away before that group, unless he meant that they turned away individuals from among the people, as that had occurred at the beginning of the mission. And turning away: prevention, meaning that they turn away. And with this, the future was connected to the past. It was said: The waw is redundant. And they turn away is the predicate of if. This corrupts the intended meaning, and the predicate is omitted and understood when he said and the beginning is its estimation: they lost when they perished. And and they turn away came in the future because it is a verb that they perpetuate, as came the statement of God the Almighty: Those who believe and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of God (al-Ra’d 13:28), so it is as if He said: Indeed, those who disbelieve are prone to turning away. If He had said that indeed, those who disbelieved and turned away, it would have been permissible. Al-Nahhas said: And in my book on the authority of Abu Ishaq, he said: And it is permissible for the predicate to be - and this is the correct view - We will make him taste a painful punishment. Abu Ja`far said: This is a mistake, and I do not know what the reason for it is, because it came with the predicate of in in the subjunctive mood, and also because it is the answer to the condition, and if it were the predicate of in the condition would remain without an answer, especially since the verb in the condition is future and therefore must have an answer. Second: The Almighty’s statement: And the Sacred Mosque. It was said: It is the mosque itself, and this is the apparent meaning of the Qur’an, because it did not mention anything else. It was also said: The entire sanctuary, because the polytheists prevented the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from it in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, so he went out of it. God Almighty said: And they prevented you from Al-Masjid Al-Haram (al-Fath 48:25) and He said: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from Al-Masjid Al-Haram (al-Isra’ 17:1). This is correct, but what is meant here by the important mention is the intended meaning of that. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Which We have appointed for mankind meaning for prayer, circumambulation, and worship. It is like His saying: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind (Al Imran 3:96). The same is the one who dwells therein as the one who visits The one who dwells therein is the one who resides and stays there. The one who visits there is the Bedouin and whoever comes to them. He says: The same in respecting its sanctity and performing the rituals therein, the one who is present and the one who comes from the country, so the people of Mecca are not more deserving than the one who migrates to it. It was said: The equality is only in its houses and dwellings, the one who resides there is not more deserving than the one who comes to it. This is based on the fact that the Sacred Mosque is the entire sanctuary, and this is the saying of Mujahid and Malik, narrated by Ibn al-Qasim. It was narrated from Umar, Ibn Abbas, and a group that the one who comes has the right to stay wherever he finds it, and it is upon the owner of the house to shelter him whether he likes it or not. This was said by Sufyan al-Thawri and others. And so it was for a matter in the early days, their houses were without doors until theft increased, so a man made a door and Omar denounced him and said: Do you close a door in the face of the pilgrim to the House of God? He said: I only wanted to protect their belongings from theft, so he left it and the people made doors. It was also narrated from Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, that he used to order the removal of the doors of the houses of Mecca during the season, so that whoever came could enter and stay where he wanted, and tents were pitched in the houses. It was narrated from Malik that the houses are not like the mosque and their inhabitants have the right to abstain from them and to stay alone, and this is the practice today. The majority of the nation said this. This dispute is based on two principles: One of them is whether the houses of Mecca belong to their owners or to the people. There are two reasons for the dispute: One of them is whether Mecca was conquered by force, so it would be spoils, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not divide it and left it for its people and those who came after them, as Omar, may God be pleased with him, did with the land of Sawad and forgave them the land tax as he forgave their captivity and enslavement as a kindness to them, unlike the rest of the infidels, so it remains as it is, not sold or rented, and whoever reaches a place first is more entitled to it. This is what Malik, Abu Hanifa and Al-Awza’i said. Or its conquest was a peace treaty - and Al-Shafi’i went to this - so their houses would remain in their hands, and they would dispose of their property as they wished. It was narrated that Omar bought the house of Safwan bin Umayya for four thousand and turned it into a prison, and he was the first to be imprisoned in Islam, as was explained previously in the verse about the warriors in Surat Al-Ma’idah. It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was imprisoned on suspicion. Tawus hated prison in Mecca and said: A house of torment should not be in a house of mercy. I said: What Malik said is correct, and the apparent meaning of the established hadiths indicates that it was conquered by force. Abu Ubaid said: We do not know of any other land in Mecca that resembles it. Ad-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Alqamah ibn Nadlah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, passed away, and the quarters of Mecca were not called anything but Al-Sawa’ib. Whoever needed it could stay there, and whoever was independent of means could stay there. And he added in another narration: and Uthman. It was also narrated on the authority of Alqamah ibn Nadlah al-Kinani, who said: The houses of Mecca during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them, were called Al-Sawa’ib. They were not sold. Whoever needed it could stay there, and whoever was independent of means could stay there. It was also narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God the Most High has made Mecca sacred, so it is forbidden to sell its houses or eat its price. He said: Whoever eats anything from the rent of the houses of Mecca, he is eating fire.” Al-Daraqutni said: This is how Abu Hanifa narrated it, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he made a mistake in that. He also made a mistake in his statement, ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abi Yazid, who is actually Ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qaddah. The correct view is that it is a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Daraqutni also attributed it to ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Makkah is a place where its quarters are not sold and its houses are not rented. Abu Dawud narrated, “On the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: I said, O Messenger of God, shall I not build you a house or a building in Mina that will shade you from the sun? He said, No, it is only a place for those who come to it first.” Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, held fast to the words of God Almighty: Those who were expelled from their homes, and attributed it to them. And he, peace be upon him, said on the day of the conquest: Whoever closes his door is safe, and whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe.” Fourth: The majority of people read sawa’a in the nominative case, which is in the beginning, and al-’akif is its predicate. It was said that the predicate is sawa’a and it is advanced, meaning the one who is staying in it and the one who is going out are the same, and this is the saying of Abu Ali, and the meaning is: which we made for the people a qiblah or a place of worship, the one who is staying in it and the one who is going out are the same. Hafs from Asim read sawa’a in the accusative case, which is the reading of Al-A’mash. This also has two possible meanings: One: that it is a second object of ja’ala, and al-’akif is raised by it because it is a verbal noun, so it works like an active participle because it is in the meaning of mustawa. The second meaning: that it is a state of the pronoun in ja’alahu. A group read sawa’a in the accusative case, al-’akif in the genitive case, and al-’akif in apposition to al-nas, the meaning being: which we made for the people, the one who is staying in it and the one who is going out. Ibn Kathir’s reading in stopping and connecting is with a ya’, and Abu Amr stopped without a ya’ and connected with a ya’. Nafi’ read without a ya’ in connecting and stopping. People agreed that it was established in the Sacred Mosque itself, but they differed in Mecca, which we have mentioned. Fifth: And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice is a condition, and its answer is We will make him taste a painful punishment. In the language, ilhad means inclination, except that God the Most High made it clear that inclination to injustice is what is meant. There is a difference of opinion regarding injustice. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And whoever intends therein to commit an act of injustice He said: Polytheism. Ata’ said: Polytheism and killing. It was said: Its meaning is hunting its pigeons, cutting down its trees, and entering it in a way that is not forbidden. Ibn Umar said: We used to say that ilhad in it is for a person to say: No, by God! And Yes, by God! And No, by God! Therefore, he had two tents, one outside the Haram and the other inside the Sacred Sanctuary. So when he wanted to pray, he would enter the Sacred Sanctuary tent, and when he wanted to do some business, he would enter the outside tent, to protect the Sacred Sanctuary from their saying: No, by God and Yes, by God, when God magnified the sin in it. Likewise, Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas had two tents, one outside the Haram and the other inside the Sacred City. When he wanted to rebuke his family, he would rebuke them outside the Haram, and when he wanted to pray, he would pray in the Haram. He was asked about that and he said: We used to say that it is blasphemy in the Haram to say, No, by God, and Yes, by God. Sins are multiplied in Mecca just as good deeds are multiplied. So the sin is two sins, one by the transgression itself and the second by disregarding the sanctity of the Sacred City. And so it is with the sacred months. It has been mentioned before. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Ya’la bin Umayya that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Monopolising food in the Haram is an atheism. This is what Omar ibn al-Khattab said. The general meaning applies to all of this. Sixth: Some of the interpreters, including Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd, believed that this verse indicates that a person will be punished for the sins he intends in Mecca, even if he does not commit them. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of Ibn Masoud and Ibn Umar. They said: If a man intended to kill a man in this house while he was in Aden, God would punish him. I said: This is correct, and this meaning has been explained in Surat Nun and the Pen, as will be explained there, God willing. Seventh: The letter ba in bi-ilhad is redundant, just as it is redundant in the Almighty’s saying: It grows with oil (al-Mu’minun 23:20). And based on this, they interpreted the poet’s saying: We are the sons of Ja'dah, the owners of the falaj. We strike with the sword and hope for relief. He meant: We hope for relief. Al-A'sha said: Our spears have guaranteed the livelihood of our children. Any livelihood. Another said: Didn't the report reach you, spreading report of what happened to the camels of Banu Ziyad? That is, what she encountered, and the letter ba is redundant, and it is common. Al-Farra’ said: I heard a Bedouin and asked him about something, and he said: I hope for that, meaning I hope for that. And the poet said: In a Yemeni valley, the Shath grows at its top and bottom with Marakh and Shabhan. That is, the relaxed. This is the opinion of Al-Akhfash, and the meaning according to him is: And whoever intends to commit an act of injustice therein. The Kufians said: The preposition ba was added because the meaning is to commit an act of injustice, and the preposition ba is added and deleted. It is possible that the interpretation is: And whoever intends to commit an act of injustice therein. This animosity and injustice include all sins from disbelief to minor sins, so due to the great sanctity of the place, God the Almighty threatened for the evil intention therein. And whoever intends an evil but does not do it will not be held accountable for it except in Mecca. This is the opinion of Ibn Masoud and a group of the Companions and others, and we have mentioned it above.
22:26: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And when We appointed for Abraham the site of the House meaning, remember when We appointed for Abraham. It is said: I appointed him a home and I appointed him a home. Just as it is said: I made you dwelling and I made you dwelling. The lam in His saying: for Abraham is a conjunction for emphasis, like His saying: He placed behind you (al-Naml 27:72). This is the saying of Al-Farra’. It was said: We appointed for Abraham the site of the House meaning, We showed him its origin so that he could build it. It had been destroyed by the flood and other things. When the time of Abraham, peace be upon him, came, God ordered him to build it. He came to its location and began to look for a trace. Then God sent a wind that revealed the foundation of Adam, peace be upon him, and he arranged its foundations on it, as was explained previously in (Al-Baqarah). It was said: We appointed is a place of residence, a verb that is transitive with lam, like we made, meaning we made for Abraham the site of the House a place of residence. The poet said: How many noble brothers I have, I have buried with my own hands Second: That you do not associate is addressed to Abraham, peace be upon him, according to the majority. Ikrimah read that you do not associate with a ya’, conveying the meaning of the statement that was made to him. Abu Hatim said: It is necessary to put the kaf in the accusative case in this reading, meaning so that he does not associate. It was said: That is a lightened version of the heavy one. It was said that it is explanatory. It was said that it is redundant, like So when the bearer of good tidings came (Yusuf 12:96). In the verse, there is a criticism of those who associated from the inhabitants of the House, meaning this was the condition upon your father and those after him and you, but you did not fulfill it, rather you associated. A group said: The address of His statement: that you do not associate is to Muhammad, peace be upon him, and he ordered the purification of the House and the call to Hajj. The majority are of the opinion that this is for Abraham, and this is the most correct. Purifying the House is general in disbelief and innovations and all impurities and blood. It was said: He meant by it purification from idols, as God the Almighty said: So avoid the uncleanness of idols (al-Hajj 22:30), and that is because Jurhum and the Amalekites had idols in the place of the House and around it before Ibrahim, peace be upon him, built it. It was said: The meaning is, purify My House from being worshipped by idols. This is a command to show monotheism in it. The scholars have already mentioned what is sufficient about purifying the Sacred Mosque and other mosques in Surah Bara’ah. Those who stand are those who pray. God the Almighty mentioned the greatest of the pillars of prayer, which are standing, bowing, and prostrating.
22:27: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And proclaim to mankind the Hajj. The majority of people read and proclaim with a shaddah on the dhal. Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan and Ibn Muhaisin read and proclaim with a light dhal and a long alif. Ibn Atiyyah said: This was misprinted by Ibn Jinni, as he narrated from them and proclaim as a past tense verb, and he parsed it accordingly by making it an appositive to we have established. And the pronunciation is notification, and it was mentioned previously in Bara’ah. Second: When Abraham, peace be upon him, finished building the House, and it was said to him: Announce the Hajj to the people, he said: O Lord! How can my voice reach? He said: Announce and I must deliver it. So Abraham, the friend of God, ascended Mount Abu Qubais and shouted: O people! God has commanded you to perform the Hajj to this House so that He may reward you with Paradise and protect you from the punishment of the Fire. So perform the Hajj, and those who were in the loins of men and the wombs of women responded to him: Here I am, O God, here I am! Whoever responds on that day performs the Hajj according to the response. If he responds once, then once, and if he responds twice, then twice. And the Talbiyah was based on that, as Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr said. It was narrated on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib that he said: Ibn Abbas said to me: Do you know what the origin of the Talbiyah was? I said: No! He said: When Abraham, peace be upon him, was commanded to announce the Hajj to the people, the mountains lowered their heads and the villages were raised for him, so he called to the people to perform the Hajj and everything responded to him: Here I am, O God, here I am. It was said: The address to Abraham, peace be upon him, was completed when he said prostration, then he informed them that they were required to perform the prescribed punishment. A third opinion: The address in His saying that you do not associate is addressed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is the opinion of the people of insight, because the Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so everything in it that is addressed is to him unless there is conclusive evidence to the contrary. Here is another evidence that indicates that the address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is that you do not associate with Me with the letter ta’, and this is addressing someone who is present, and Abraham, peace be upon him, is absent, so the meaning according to this is: And when We designated for Abraham the site of the House, We made for you the proofs of the Oneness of God Almighty and that Abraham used to worship God alone. The majority of people read by Hajj with the letter ha’ open. Ibn Abi Ishaq read it in the entire Qur’an with the letter ha’ closed. It was said: Abraham’s call is part of what he was commanded to do of the laws of religion. And God knows best. Third: The Almighty’s saying: They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel. He promised the people’s response to the Hajj, whether on foot or riding. He only said: They will come to you even though they were coming to the Kaaba because the one calling was Ibrahim, so whoever comes to the Kaaba as a pilgrim is as if he has come to Ibrahim, because he answered his call, and in this is an honor for Ibrahim. Ibn Atiyyah said: Men is the plural of Rajil, like Tajar and Tajar, and Sahib and Sahib. It was said: Rijal is the plural of Rajil, and Rajil is the plural of Rajil, like Tajar and Tajar, and Sahib and Sahib and Sahib. It may be said in the plural: Rijal, with emphasis, like Kafir and Kafir. Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ikrimah read Rijal with a damma on the ra’ and a light jim, and it is rare in the plural forms, and it was narrated from Mujahid. Mujahid read Rijal with the weight of Fa’ali, so it is like Kasra. An-Nahhas said: There are five aspects to the plural of Rajil: Rijal like Rikab, which is what was narrated from Ikrimah, and Rijal like Qiyam, Rijlah, Rijal, and Rijal. What was narrated from Mujahid is that the men are not known, and it is more likely that it is without a nunation like kasali and sakari, and if it were to be nun it would be fa’ala, and fa’al in the plural is rare. And men are mentioned before riders because of their increased fatigue from walking. And on every lean camel they come because the meaning of wasted is the meaning of wasted ones. Al-Farra’ said: And it is permissible to say “comes according to the wording. And the wasted is the emaciated camel that is tired from travel, it is said: he was wasted, was wasted, so God described it as the destination that it ended up in Mecca. And He mentioned the reason for the wastedness and said: They come from every deep pass meaning the length of the journey affected it. And the pronoun was returned to the camels to honor them for intending Hajj with their owners, as He said: And the charging horses, panting (al-Adiyat 100:1) about the horses of jihad to honor them when they strive in the way of God. Fourth: Some of them said: He said men because men usually go out to Hajj, not women. So his saying men is like your saying: This is a man, and this is far-fetched, because He said: And on every lean animal meaning riders, so men and women were included in it. And when God the Almighty said: men and began with them, this indicates that the Hajj of a person on foot is better than the Hajj of a person on a rider. Ibn Abbas said: I do not regret anything I missed except that I did not perform Hajj on foot, for I heard God the Almighty say: They come to you on foot. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Ibrahim and Ismail, peace be upon them, performed Hajj on foot. The companions of Ibn Masoud read they come and this is the reading of Ibn Abi Ubla and Ad-Dahhak, and the pronoun refers to the people. Fifth: There is no disagreement about the permissibility of riding and walking, but they differed about which of them is better. Malik, Al-Shafi’i and others held that riding is better, following the example of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and because of the great expense and the magnification of the rituals of Hajj by the preparations for riding. Others held that walking is better because of the hardship it entails on the soul, and because of the hadith of Abu Sa’id who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions performed Hajj on foot from Medina to Mecca, and he said: ‘Tie your waists with your loins,’ and he walked at a trot.” Narrated by Ibn Majah in his Sunan. There is no disagreement that, according to Malik, riding is better for all rituals, following the example of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Sixth: Some scholars have used the omission of the sea in this verse as evidence that the obligation of Hajj by sea is dropped. Malik said in Al-Mawaziyah: I do not hear the sea mentioned, and this is familiarity, not that its omission necessitates the omission of the obligation in it, because Mecca is not on the shore of a sea, so people come to it in ships, and whoever takes the sea must come to Mecca either on foot or on a lean camel, so the two states of arrival were mentioned, and dropping the obligation of Hajj by the sea alone is not much or strong.
