But if it is accompanied by an enemy, fear, severe terror, or an illness that befalls a person, then Malik, Al-Shafi’i, and the majority of people are of the opinion that the obligation is dropped by these excuses, and that it is not a feasible way. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: The author of Al-Istithhar mentioned some words in this meaning, the apparent meaning of which is that the obligation is not dropped by any of these excuses, and this is weak. I said: And weaker than weak, and its explanation has already been mentioned in (Al-Baqarah). And the path is the wide road, and the plural is paths. And it has been mentioned in (Al-Anbiya). And the deep means far. And the reading of the group is ya’tun they come. And the companions of Abdullah read ya’tun they come, and this is for the riders, and ya’tun they come is for the camels, as if he said: And on lean camels they come from every deep path (i.e. far), and from it is a deep well (i.e. with a deep bottom), and from it: Dark and empty of penetration Seventh: They differed regarding the one who reaches the House, whether he should raise his hands when he sees it or not. Abu Dawud narrated that he said: Jabir ibn Abdullah was asked about a man who sees the Kaaba and raises his hands. He said: I did not think that anyone would do this except the Jews. We performed Hajj with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, but we did not do it. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The hands are raised in seven places: the beginning of the prayer, facing the House, Safa and Marwa, the two places of standing, and the two Jamarat. Al-Thawri, Ibn Mubarak, Ahmad and Ishaq agreed with this hadith of Ibn Abbas, and they weakened the hadith of Jabir, because the narrator of Muhajir al-Makki is unknown. Ibn Umar used to raise his hands when seeing the House. The same was reported from Ibn Abbas.
22:28: It contains twenty-three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: That they may witness meaning, give permission for the Hajj, they come to you on foot and on horseback to witness, meaning, to be present. Witnesses are those who attend. Benefits for them meaning the rituals, such as Arafat and the Sacred Monument. It was said that it means forgiveness. It was said that it means trade. It was said that it is general, meaning that they may be present for benefits for them, meaning whatever pleases God the Almighty in matters of this world and the Hereafter. This was said by Mujahid and Ata’ and it was chosen by Ibn al-Arabi, as it includes all of that from rituals, trade, forgiveness, and benefits in this world and the Hereafter. There is no disagreement that what is meant by His saying: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord (al-Baqarah 2:198) is trade. Second: And mention the name of God on known days. The discussion of the known and numbered days has already been mentioned in (Al-Baqarah). What is meant by mentioning the name of God is mentioning the name of God when slaughtering and sacrificing, such as saying: In the name of God, and God is greater, O God, from You and for You. And such as saying when slaughtering: Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice (Al-An`am: 162) the verse. The disbelievers used to slaughter in the names of their idols, so the Lord explained that it is obligatory to slaughter in the name of God, and this has already been mentioned in (Al-An`am). Third: The scholars differed regarding the time of slaughtering on the Day of Sacrifice. Malik, may God be pleased with him, said: After the imam’s prayer and slaughtering, unless he delays it to a point where he transgresses, in which case following him is not permissible. Abu Hanifa took into consideration the completion of the prayer without slaughtering. Al-Shafi’i considered the beginning of the time for prayer and the amount of time that he expected in it with the two sermons, so he considered the time without the prayer. This is the narration of Al-Muzani from him, and it is the saying of Al-Tabari. Al-Rabi’ mentioned from Al-Buwayti that Al-Shafi’i said: No one should slaughter until the imam slaughters, unless he is one of those who do not slaughter. If he prays and finishes the sermon, slaughtering is permissible. This is similar to the saying of Malik. Ahmad said: When the imam leaves, then slaughter. This is the saying of Ibrahim. The most correct of these sayings is the saying of Malik, “because of the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) led us in prayer on the Day of Sacrifice in Medina. Some men came forward and sacrificed, thinking that the Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) had already sacrificed. The Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) ordered those who had sacrificed to repeat it by sacrificing another animal, and not to sacrifice until the Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) had sacrificed. Narrated by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, who said: There are other reports on this topic from Jabir, Jundub, Anas, Uwaimir ibn Ashqar, Ibn Umar, and Abu Zayd al-Ansari. This is a good and authentic hadith, and the practice according to [most] scholars is that one should not sacrifice in the city until the imam prays. Abu Hanifah used as evidence the hadith of al-Baraa, in which it says: “Whoever slaughters after the prayer has completed his ritual and has followed the Sunnah of the Muslims.” Narrated by Muslim as well. He linked the slaughtering to the prayer and did not mention the slaughtering, and the hadith of Jabir restricts it. Likewise, the hadith of Al-Baraa’ also, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The first thing we begin with on this day of ours is to pray, then we return and slaughter, so whoever does that has followed our Sunnah. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: I do not know of any disagreement among the scholars that whoever slaughters before the prayer and is from the people of the city is not sacrificing, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever slaughters before the prayer, that is a meat sheep. Fourth: As for the people of the desert and those who do not have an imam, the well-known Maliki school of thought is that they should determine the time of slaughtering by the imam, or the imam closest to him. Rabia and Ata’ said about those who do not have an imam: If he slaughters before sunrise, it is not acceptable, but it is acceptable if he slaughters after it. The people of opinion said: It is acceptable for them after dawn. This is the opinion of Ibn al-Mubarak, as reported by al-Tirmidhi. They held fast to the words of God the Almighty: And mention the name of God on known days over what He has provided for them of grazing livestock, so He added the slaughtering to the day. Is the day from the rising of dawn or from the rising of the sun? There are two opinions. There is no disagreement that slaughtering the sacrifice before the rising of dawn on the day of sacrifice is not acceptable. Fifth: They differed on how many days of sacrifice are there? Malik said: Three, the day of sacrifice and two days after it. Abu Hanifa, Ath-Thawri and Ahmad ibn Hanbal said the same. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah and Anas ibn Malik without any difference of opinion from them. Ash-Shafi’i said: Four, the day of sacrifice and three days after it. Al-Awza’i said the same. It was narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them. It was also narrated on their authority like Malik and Ahmad. It was said: It is the day of sacrifice specifically, which is the tenth of Dhul-Hijjah. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Sirin. Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Jabir ibn Zayd said: Sacrifice in all regions is one day and in Mina is three days. Al-Hasan al-Basri narrated three narrations on this: One of them is as Malik said, the second is as Ash-Shafi’i said, and the third is until the last day of Dhul-Hijjah. When the crescent of Muharram appears, then there is no sacrifice. I said: This is the statement of Sulayman ibn Yasar and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman, and they narrated a mursal hadith with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, which was included by al-Daraqutni: The sacrifices are until the crescent of Dhul-Hijjah and it is not authentic, and our evidence is the saying of God the Almighty: On known days the verse, and this is a small collection, but what is certain of it is the three, and what comes after the three is not certain so it is not acted upon. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr said: The scholars agreed that the day of sacrifice is the day of sacrifice, and they agreed that there is no sacrifice after the end of Dhul-Hijjah, and in my opinion the only valid opinions in this regard are two: One of them is the opinion of Malik and the Kufians. The other is the opinion of Al-Shafi'i and the Shami. These two opinions were narrated from the Companions, so there is no point in engaging in what contradicts them, because what contradicts them has no basis in the Sunnah or in the opinion of the Companions, and what is outside of these two is abandoned to them. A sixth opinion was narrated from Qatadah, which is that the day of sacrifice is the day of sacrifice and six days after it, and this is also outside of the opinion of the Companions so there is no meaning to it. Sixth: They differed regarding the nights of sacrifice, whether they are included with the days and slaughtering is permissible on them or not. It was narrated from Malik in the well-known view that they are not included and slaughtering at night is not permissible. The majority of his companions and the people of opinion agree with this, because God the Almighty said: And mention the name of God during the days. So he mentioned the days, and mentioning the days is evidence that slaughtering at night is not permissible. Abu Hanifah, Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr said: The nights are included with the days and slaughtering on them is permissible. Something similar was narrated from Malik and Ashab, and Ashab differentiated between the sacrificial animal and the sacrifice, so he permitted the sacrificial animal but did not permit the sacrifice at night. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: On what He has provided for them meaning on slaughtering what He has provided for them. Of the livestock and the livestock here are camels, cows, and sheep. The livestock are the livestock, so it is like saying the first prayer and the congregational mosque. Eighth: Eat from it is an order that means encouragement according to the majority. It is recommended for a man to eat from his sacrificial animal and to give most of it in charity, while they permit giving all of it in charity and eating all of it. A group deviated and made eating and feeding obligatory based on the apparent meaning of the verse, and on the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: So eat, save, and give in charity. Al-Kia said: The Almighty’s statement, So eat from it and feed others indicates that it is not permissible to sell all of it or give all of it in charity. Ninth: The blood of expiation is not eaten by its owners. The well-known school of Malik may God be pleased with him is that he does not eat from three things: the penalty for hunting, the vow to the poor, and the ransom for harm. He may eat from other things if they reach their place, whether obligatory or voluntary. A group of the Salaf and jurists of the regions agreed with him on this. Tenth: If he eats what he was forbidden from, does he have to pay the equivalent of what he ate or pay a full sacrificial animal? There are two opinions in our school of thought, and Ibn al-Majishun said the first. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is the truth, and he does not have to do anything else. Likewise, if he vows a sacrificial animal for the poor and eats from it after it reaches its destination, he does not have to pay anything other than what he ate - contrary to the Mudawwana - because the slaughtering has taken place, and the transgression was only on the meat, so he has to pay the equivalent of what he transgressed into. The Almighty’s statement: And let them fulfill their vows indicates the obligation to give the vow, whether it is blood, an offering, or something else. This indicates that it is not permissible to eat from the vow in fulfillment of the vow, and the same applies to the penalty for hunting and the ransom for harm, because what is required is to bring it complete, without any loss of meat or anything else. If he eats from that, then he must offer a complete offering. And God knows best. Eleventh: Should he pay the value of the meat or should he pay food? In the book of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik, it is stated that he should pay food. The first is more correct, because food is only in exchange for the entire offering when it is not possible, an act of worship, and the ruling on transgression is not the ruling on worship. Twelfth: If any of this guaranteed sacrificial animal, which is the penalty for hunting, the ransom for harm, or the vow of the poor, is damaged before its destination, its owner may eat from it and feed the rich and the poor and whoever he likes, and he may not sell any of its meat, skin, or necklaces. Ismail bin Ishaq said: Because if the guaranteed sacrificial animal is damaged before it reaches its destination, he must replace it, and for that reason it is permissible for its owner to eat from it and feed others. If the voluntary sacrificial animal is damaged before it reaches its destination, it is not permissible for him to eat from it or feed others, because since he does not have to replace it, it is feared that he may do that to the sacrificial animal and slaughter it without it being damaged, so the people were cautious, and thus the action was carried out. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Najiyah al-Aslami that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a sacrificial animal with him and said: If any of it is damaged, slaughter it, then dip his sandal in its blood, then leave him with the people. And with this hadith, Malik and Al-Shafi’i in one of his two opinions, and Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, and the people of opinion and those who followed them in voluntary sacrifice said: The one who drives it should not eat anything from it, and he should leave it for the people to eat it. And in Sahih Muslim: Neither you nor any of your companions eat from it. Ibn Abbas and Ash-Shafi’i said in their other statement, and Ibn Al-Mundhir chose it, and they said: He nor any of his companions should eat from it. Abu Omar said: His (peace be upon him) saying: Neither you nor any of your companions should eat from it is only found in the hadith of Ibn Abbas. It is not in the hadith of Hisham bin Urwah from his father from Najiyah. It is more authentic to us than the hadith of Ibn Abbas, and this is the practice of the jurists. His (peace be upon him) saying: Leave it alone with the people includes his companions and others. Ash-Shafi’i and Abu Thawr said: Whatever is from the sacrificial animal is obligatory, so he should not eat from it. Whatever is voluntary and ritual, he should eat from it, give it as a gift, save it, and give in charity. Mut’ah and Qiran are rituals according to him. A similar view is the view of Al-Awza’i. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: He may eat from the sacrificial and voluntary sacrificial animal, but he may not eat from anything else that is obligatory due to the ruling of ihram. It was narrated from Malik: He may not eat from the blood of corruption. And based on this, he does not eat from the blood of the one who has been killed, as stated by al-Shafi’i and al-Awza’i. Malik held that the penalty for hunting was made by God for the poor, as He, the Most High, said: Or an expiation of feeding the poor (al-Ma’idah 5:95). And he said about the ransom for harm: Then a ransom of fasting or charity or sacrifice (al-Baqarah 2:196). And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ka’b ibn ‘Ujrah: Feed six poor people, giving each poor person a mudd, or fast for three days, or sacrifice a sheep. The vow to the poor is explicit, but other than that, the gifts remain based on the original statement of his: And the sacrificial animals, We have made them for you among the rites of God - to his statement - So eat from them. And: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Ali, may God be pleased with him, ate from the sacrificial animal that he brought and drank from the broth. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was a Qarin according to the most correct sayings and narrations, so his sacrificial animal was obligatory according to this. What Abu Hanifa relied on is incorrect. And God knows best. God Almighty permitted eating from the gifts because the Arabs did not think it was permissible to eat from their ritual sacrifices. So God Almighty commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to oppose them. So it is no wonder that this is how he legislated and conveyed it, and this is what he did when he gave gifts and entered ihram, may God bless him and grant him peace. Thirteenth: So eat from it. Some scholars said: The Almighty’s statement: So eat from it abrogates their action, because they used to forbid themselves the meat of the sacrifices and would not eat from it - as we said in the gifts - so God abrogated that with His statement: So eat from it, and with the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Whoever sacrifices should eat from his sacrifice. Because peace be upon him, he ate from his sacrifice and his offering. Al-Zuhri said: It is from the Sunnah to eat from the liver first. Fourteenth: Most scholars have said that it is recommended to give one-third in charity, feed one-third, and eat one-third himself and his family. Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik: We do not have a known and described division for sacrifices. Malik said in his hadith: It was reported to me on the authority of Ibn Masoud, and the blind are not required to do so. It was narrated in Sahih and Abu Dawud said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sacrificed a sheep and then said: O Thawban, prepare the meat of this sheep. He said: I continued to feed him from it until he arrived in Madinah. This is a clear text on the obligation. Al-Shafi’i’s opinion differed. One of them said: He should eat half and give the other half in charity, based on the words of God the Almighty: So eat from it and feed the poor and needy. So he mentioned two people. And another time he said: He should eat a third, give a third as a gift, and give a third to charity, based on the words of God the Almighty: So eat from it and feed the needy and the poor. (al-Hajj 22:36) So he mentioned three people. Fifteenth: The traveler is addressed with the sacrifice as he is addressed with it to the resident, since the original address is general, and this is the opinion of all scholars. Abu Hanifa and Al-Nakha’i disagreed with this, and it was narrated from Ali, and the hadith is evidence against them. Malik excluded from the travelers the pilgrim in Mina, so he did not see that he had to offer a sacrifice, and Al-Nakha’i said the same. This was narrated from the two caliphs Abu Bakr and Umar and a group of the Salaf may God be pleased with them, because the pilgrim is originally addressed with the offering, so if he wants to offer a sacrifice he makes it an offering, and the people other than the pilgrims were only commanded to offer the sacrifice so that they would resemble the people of Mina and thus obtain a share of their reward. Sixteenth: Scholars differed on saving into four opinions. It was narrated from Ali and Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them, through a sound chain of transmission that one should not save from the sacrifices after three days. They also narrated it from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it will come later. A group said: What was narrated about the prohibition of saving has been abrogated, so one may save it for any time one likes. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri and Buraidah Al-Aslami said the same. A group said: It is permissible to eat from it absolutely. A group said: If people need it, then one should not save it, because the prohibition was only for a reason, which is his saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: I only forbade you because of the flood that has come. When it was lifted, the previous prohibition was lifted because its reason was lifted, not because it was abrogated. A fundamental issue arises here, which is: Seventeenth: It is the difference between lifting a ruling by abrogation and lifting it because its cause has been removed. Know that a ruling that has been lifted by abrogation will never be ruled upon, and a ruling that has been lifted because its cause has been removed will be returned to the cause. So if needy people came to the people of a town during the time of Eid al-Adha, and the people of that town did not have the means to satisfy their need except for sacrificial animals, then it would be necessary for them not to save them for more than three days, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did. Eighteenth: The hadiths that were mentioned in this chapter regarding prohibition and acceptance are authentic and proven. The prohibition and permission came together, as is stated in the hadith of Aisha, Salamah ibn al-Akwa’, and Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, narrated by Sahih. And Sahih narrated on the authority of Abu Ubayd, the freed slave of Ibn Azhar, that he witnessed the Eid with Umar ibn al-Khattab. He said: Then I prayed the Eid prayer with Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. He said: He prayed for us before the sermon, then he preached to the people and said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has forbidden you to eat the meat of your sacrifice for more than three nights, so do not eat it. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade eating the meat of sacrificial animals for more than three days. Salim said: Ibn Umar did not eat the meat of sacrificial animals for more than three days. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Nabisha that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “We had forbidden you from eating its meat for more than three days so that it would suffice you. God has brought abundance, so eat, save, and trade. Beware, these days are days of eating, drinking, and remembering God, the Almighty and Majestic.” Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: This statement is the best that has been said on this subject so that the hadiths agree and do not contradict each other, and the statement of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, and Uthman are limited, because the people were in dire need, so he did as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did when the flood came. The evidence for this is what Ibrahim ibn Sharik told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Laith told us, he said: Al-Harith ibn Ya`qub told me, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Yazid, on the authority of his wife, that she asked Aisha, may God be pleased with her, about the meat of the sacrificial animals, and she said: Ali ibn Abi Talib came to us from a journey, so we came to him from it, but he refused to eat until he asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he asked him and he said: Eat from Dhul-Hijjah to Dhul-Hijjah. Al-Shafi’i said: Whoever says that saving food after three days is forbidden has not heard the dispensation. Whoever says that it is dispensable absolutely has not heard the prohibition of saving food. Whoever says that it is forbidden and dispensable has heard both of them and acted according to them. And God knows best. In Surah Al-Kawthar, there will be a discussion of the difference in the obligation of the sacrifice and its recommendation, and that it abrogates every previous slaughter, God willing. Nineteenth: The Almighty’s saying: And feed the wretched, needy. “Poor” is an attribute of the wretched, which is the one who has been afflicted with misery and extreme poverty. It is said: Ba’isa yabasa ba’san if he has become poor, so he is ba’isa. It may also be used for someone who has been afflicted with a calamity of time, even if he is not poor. From this is his saying, peace be upon him: But the wretched Saeed bin Khawlah. It is said: a wretched man, meaning severe. And he became wretched, meaning severe, and from this the Almighty said: And We seized those who did wrong with a wretched punishment (al-A’raf 7:165), meaning severe. And the more the meat of the sacrifice was given in charity, the greater the reward. And there is a difference of opinion about the amount that may be eaten, which we have mentioned. It was said that it is half, based on His saying: So eat and feed others. And it was said that it is two-thirds, based on His saying: So eat and save and trade, meaning seek reward by feeding others. And there was a difference of opinion about eating and feeding others. It was said that they are obligatory. It was said that they are recommended. It was said that there is a difference between eating and feeding others, so eating is recommended and feeding others is forbidden, and this is the saying of Al-Shafi'i.
22:29: Al-Muwaffah Twenty: The Almighty said: Then let them complete their untidiness meaning, after slaughtering the sacrifices and gifts, let them complete what remains of the Hajj, such as shaving, throwing stones, removing unkempt hair, and the like. Ibn Arafa said: That is, let them remove their filth. Al-Azhari said: Taffath is trimming the moustache, cutting the nails, plucking the armpit hair, and shaving the pubic hair. This is when exiting the state of ihram. Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: Taffath in the speech of the Arabs means removing unkempt hair. I heard Al-Azhari say: Taffath in the speech of the Arabs is not known except from the words of Ibn Abbas and the people of interpretation. Al-Hasan said: It is removing the unkempt hair of ihram. It was said: Taffath is all the rituals of Hajj, narrated by Ibn Omar and Ibn Abbas. Ibn al-Arabi said: If it was authentically reported from them, it would be an argument for the honor of companionship and their mastery of the language. He said: This word is strange, and the Arabs did not find any poetry about it, nor did they master any information about it. However, I looked for tafath in the language and saw Abu Ubaidah Muammar ibn al-Muthanna say: It means cutting the nails, trimming the moustache, and everything that is forbidden to the pilgrim except for marriage. He said: There is no poetry about it that can be used as evidence. The companions of al-Ayn said: tafath is throwing stones, shaving, shortening, slaughtering, and cutting the nails, moustache, and armpits. Al-Zajjaj and al-Farra mentioned something similar, but I do not think that they took it except from the words of the scholars. Qatrib said: tafath means that a man has a lot of dirt. Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: They shaved their heads, did not shave their hair, and did not remove lice or nits. What Qatrub referred to is what Ibn Wahb said on the authority of Malik, and it is the correct view of tafath. This is the linguistic form of tafath, but its legal reality is that if the pilgrim or the one performing umrah slaughters his sacrificial animal, shaves his head, removes his dirt, purifies himself, cleanses himself, and dresses himself, then he has removed his tafath and fulfilled his vow, and a vow is what is binding on a person and what he undertakes. I said: What he narrated on the authority of Qatrib and what he mentioned of poetry was mentioned by Al-Mawardi in his interpretation, and he mentioned another verse and said: They spent their time weeping and crying, then they went to Najd and did not wait for Ali. Al-Tha’labi said: The root of the word taftath in the language is dirt. The Arabs say to a man who they find disgusting: How dirty and filthy you are. Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt said: Their armpits are hot, they do not throw away scum, and they remove lice and nits from themselves. Al-Mawardi: It was said to some of the righteous: What is the meaning of the disheveled state of the pilgrim? He said: So that God Almighty may witness from you that you are turning away from taking care of yourself, and He will know your sincerity in devoting yourself to His obedience. Twenty-first: And let them fulfill their vows. They were commanded to fulfill vows absolutely, except for what was a sin, because of his saying, peace be upon him: There is no fulfillment of a vow to disobey God, and his saying: Whoever vows to obey God, let him obey Him, and whoever vows to disobey Him, let him not disobey Him. “And let them circumambulate the Ancient House.” The circumambulation mentioned in this verse is the circumambulation of farewell, which is one of the obligatory acts of Hajj. Al-Tabari said: There is no disagreement among the interpreters about that. Twenty-second: Hajj has three Tawafs: Tawaf al-Qudum, Tawaf al-Ifadah, and Tawaf al-Wadaa. Ismail bin Ishaq said: Tawaf al-Qudum is a Sunnah, and it is not waived for adolescents, Meccans, or anyone who enters ihram for Hajj from Mecca. He said: The obligatory Tawaf that is not waived in any way is Tawaf al-Ifadah, which is performed after Arafat. God the Almighty said: Then let them complete their untidiness, fulfill their vows, and perform Tawaf around the Ancient House. He said: This is the Tawaf that is obligatory in the Book of God the Almighty, and it is what releases the pilgrim from his entire ihram. Al-Hafiz Abu Omar said: What Ismail mentioned about Tawaf al-Ifadah is the opinion of Malik according to the people of Medina, and it is the narration of Ibn Wahb, Ibn Nafi’, and Ashab from him. It is the opinion of the majority of scholars among the jurists of Hijaz and Iraq. Ibn al-Qasim and Ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated from Malik that Tawaf al-Qudum is obligatory. Ibn al-Qasim said in more than one place in al-Mudawwana and he also narrated it from Malik: The obligatory tawaf is the tawaf of the one coming to Mecca. He said: Whoever forgets the tawaf upon entering Mecca or forgets a round of it, or forgets the sa’i or a round of it until he returns to his country and then remembers, if he has not met the women, he should return and perform the tawaf and the sa’i, then perform the ‘umrah and offer a sacrifice. This is like what he said about the one who forgets the tawaf of farewell. According to this narration, both tawafs are obligatory, as well as the sa’i. As for the tawaf of the chest, which is called the farewell tawaf, Ibn al-Qasim and others narrated from Malik about the one who performed the tawaf of farewell without ablution: he should return from his country and perform the farewell unless he performed a voluntary tawaf after that. This is what Malik and his companions agreed upon, and that his voluntary tawaf suffices him for the obligatory tawaf that is required of him. They also agreed that whoever does something voluntarily from the actions of Hajj during his Hajj, and that thing is obligatory in Hajj and its time has passed, then his voluntary tawaf becomes obligatory and not voluntary, unlike prayer. If voluntary prayer replaces the obligatory prayer in Hajj, then the tawaf for entering Makkah is more likely to replace the tawaf of farewell, except for the tawaf that was performed after throwing the pebbles at Jamrat al-Aqaba on the Day of Sacrifice or after it for farewell. The narration of Ibn Abd al-Hakam from Malik is different from that, because it states that the tawaf of entry with the sa’i replaces the tawaf of farewell for the one who returns to his country with the sacrificial animal, just as the tawaf of farewell with the sa’i replaces the tawaf of arrival for the one who did not perform the tawaf or the sa’i when he entered Makkah with the sacrificial animal. Whoever said this said: The tawaf of entry is obligatory and the tawaf of farewell is obligatory because one of them replaces the other, and because it has been narrated from Malik that whoever forgets one of them returns from his country, as we have mentioned, and because God, the Almighty, has only made one tawaf obligatory for the pilgrim by saying: And proclaim to mankind the Hajj, and He said in the context of the verse: And let them go around the Ancient House, and the waw in this verse and others, according to them, does not require a rank except by revelation. Al-Tabari narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Salamah who said: I asked Zuhair about the words of God Almighty: And let them go around the Ancient House, and he said: It is the farewell circumambulation. This indicates that it is obligatory, and it is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i, because he, peace be upon him, permitted a menstruating woman to depart without doing the circumambulation, and he does not permit it except in what is obligatory. Twenty-third: The interpreters differed regarding the reason for describing the house as antique. Mujahid and Al-Hasan said: Ancient is old. It is said: an antique sword, and it has become old, meaning it has become ancient. This is a statement that is supported by consideration. In the Sahih: It is the first mosque built on earth. It was said to be ancient because God freed it from being dominated by a tyrant who would humiliate it until the end of time. Ibn al-Zubayr and Mujahid said the same. In al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Ancient House was named so because no tyrant has prevailed over it. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith, and it has been narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a mursal form. If someone mentions Al-Hajjaj bin Yusuf and his setting up of a catapult on the Kaaba until he broke it, it will be said to him: He only freed it from the tyrannical infidels, because if they came to the Kaaba rebelliously and did not believe in the sanctity of the House, and intended to harm the Kaaba, it would be protected from them and their hands would not reach it, that would be an indication that God, the Almighty, diverted them from it by force. As for the Muslims who believed in its sanctity, if they refrained from it, that would not be an indication of its status with God like what would be from it in the hand of the enemies. So God, the Almighty, limited this group from refraining by prohibition and threat, and did not go beyond that to diverting by compulsion and necessity, and He made the Hour their appointed time, and the Hour is more terrible and bitter. A group said: It was named Ancient because he never owned its location. A group said: It was named Ancient because God, the Almighty, frees the necks of sinners from punishment in it. It was said: He was called Ateeq because he was freed from drowning in the flood, said Ibn Jubeir. It was also said: Ateeq is the generous one. And freedom is generosity. Tarafa said, describing the horse’s ear: Two instruments in which you know freedom, like my frightened listener in the middle of the rain Emancipation of slaves: leaving the humiliation of slavery for the honor of freedom. It is possible that ateeq is a praiseworthy attribute that indicates the quality of something, as Omar said: I was carried on an old horse, the hadith. The first statement is more correct in terms of consideration and the authentic hadith. Mujahid said: God created the House two thousand years before the Earth, and it was called ateeq for this reason, and God knows best.
22:30: It contains eight issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: That may be in the nominative case with the estimation: your obligation is that, or that is the duty. And it may be in the accusative case with the estimation: comply with that. And similar to this eloquent indication is the saying of Zuhair: This is not like someone who gets tired of his plan in the middle of the dew if he speaks The sacred things intended here are the acts of Hajj referred to in His statement: Then let them complete their rites and fulfill their vows, and this includes venerating the places, as stated by Ibn Zayd and others. This can be summed up by saying: The sacred things are obeying the command in its obligatory duties and Sunnahs. His statement: Then it is better for him with his Lord, meaning that veneration is better for him with his Lord than neglecting any of them. It was said: That veneration is better than his good things that he benefits from, and it is not for preference but rather it is a number of good things. Second: The Almighty’s statement: And grazing livestock have been made lawful to you to eat them, which are camels, cows, and sheep. Except what is recited to you meaning in the Book of the forbidden things, which are dead animals, animals killed by a deadly gunshot, and their likes. This is connected to the command of Hajj, because in Hajj there is slaughtering, so it is clear what is permissible to slaughter and eat its meat. It was said: Except what is recited to you other than the permissibility of hunting while you are in a state of ihram. Third: The Almighty’s saying: So avoid the uncleanliness of idols. The uncleanliness is the dirty thing. The idol is the statue made of wood, iron, gold, silver, etc., and the Arabs used to set it up and worship it. The Christians set up the cross and worship it and venerate it, so it is also like a statue. “Adi bin Hatim said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I had a cross of gold around my neck. He said: “Throw this idol from you,” meaning the cross. Its origin is from the word wathana which means to stay in its place. The idol is called an idol because it is set up and fixed in a place and does not move from it. He means: Avoid worshipping idols. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jurayj. He called it rajs because it is the cause of rajs, which is torment. It was said that he described it as rajs, and rajs is impurity, so it is impure by law. Impurity is not an intrinsic description of objects, but rather it is a legal description from the rulings of faith. It cannot be removed except by faith, just as purification is not permissible except with water. Fourth: of in His statement: of idols. It was said that it is to clarify the type, so his prohibition of the filth of idols only occurs, and the prohibition of all other filth remains in other places. It is possible that it is to indicate the beginning of the goal, so it is as if he prohibited them from filth in general, then specified for them its beginning from which it would reach them, since idol worship encompasses all corruption and filth. Whoever says that of is for partiality has reversed the meaning of the verse and corrupted it. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And avoid false statement. Falsehood means falsehood and lies. It is called falsehood because it deviates from the truth, and from it they turned away from their cave (al-Kahf 18:17), and the city of Zawra’ means leaning. And everything other than the truth is falsehood, falsehood, and falsehood. In the hadith, he, peace be upon him, stood up as a preacher and said: False testimony is equal to polytheism, he said two or three times. Meaning that it is combined with idol worship in the prohibition against it. Sixth: This verse includes a threat against false testimony. If the ruler finds a false witness, he should chastise him and call out about him so that he is known, lest anyone be deceived by his testimony. The ruling on his testimony differs if he repents. If he is a man of justice who is well-known and prominent in it, it is not accepted, because there is no way to know his state of repentance, as he cannot do more acts of worship than he is doing. If he is less than that, then he should strive in worship and his state of piety should increase before his testimony. In the Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: Among the greatest of major sins are associating partners with God, disobeying parents, bearing false witness, and speaking falsely. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reclining, then he sat up and kept repeating it until we said, If only he would stop.
22:31: Seventh: Hanafa' for God means upright or Muslims inclined to the truth. The word Hanafa' is one of the opposites and can be used to refer to uprightness or inclination. Hanafa' is an accusative in the state of being. It has been said: Hanafa' is a pilgrims, and this is a specification with no argument. Eighth: The Almighty’s statement: And whoever associates others with God, it is as if he had fallen from the sky. That is, on the Day of Resurrection, he will be in the position of someone who does not possess any benefit for himself and cannot ward off harm or punishment from himself. He will be in the position of someone who has fallen from the sky, and he is not able to ward off harm or punishment from himself. The meaning of and the birds snatch him away is that they tear him apart with their claws. It was said: This is when his soul leaves and the angels ascend with it to the lowest heaven, but it is not opened for it and it is thrown to the earth, as in the hadith of Al-Baraa’, which we mentioned in At-Tadhkirah. As-Saheeq means far away, and from it is the Almighty’s statement: So away with the companions of the Blaze (al-Mulk 67:11), and the statement of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: Damn it, damn it.
22:32: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: That has three aspects. It was said: It is in the nominative case as a subject, meaning that is the command of God. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case as a predicate of a deleted subject. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, meaning they followed that. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And whoever honors the symbols of God The symbols are the plural of ritual, and it is everything that God has in it that I feel and know, and from it is the slogan of the people in war, meaning their mark by which they recognize each other. And from it is the marking of the sacrificial animal, which is stabbing it in its right side until blood flows and it becomes a mark, so it is called a ritual in the sense of a marked one. So the symbols of God are the signs of His religion, especially what is related to the rituals. Some people said: What is meant here by praising the sacrificial animal is caring about it and exaggerating in it, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and a group said. And in it is a subtle allusion, because the very origin of buying the sacrificial animal may lead to doing what is necessary, so it does not indicate sincerity, so if he honors it while obtaining the sufficiency of what is less than that, then no action will appear from him except the honoring of the law, and it is from the piety of the heart. And God knows best. Third: The pronoun in it refers back to the action included in the speech. If he had said then it would have been permissible. It was said that it refers back to the rituals, meaning that the veneration of the rituals, so the complement was deleted because the speech indicated it, so the metaphor refers back to the rituals. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: For it is from the piety of the hearts. “The hearts” was read in the nominative case as the subject of the source, which is piety. And he added piety to the hearts because the reality of piety is in the heart. For this reason, he, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, said in the authentic hadith: Piety is here, he said, pointing to his chest.
22:33: Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: Therein are benefits for you, meaning the body, such as riding, milk, offspring, wool, and other things, if its Lord does not send it as a gift. But when He sends it, it is the appointed term, as Ibn Abbas said. So when it becomes a body, there are also benefits in it, such as riding it when needed, and drinking its milk after watering its young. In Sahih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man leading a sacrificial animal and said: Ride it. He said: It is a sacrificial animal. He said: Ride it. He said: It is a sacrificial animal. He said: Ride it, woe to you.” In the second and third verses. It was narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah that he was asked about riding the sacrificial animal, so he said: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Ride it in moderation if you are forced to ride it until you find a back. The appointed time according to this statement is its slaughter, as stated by Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah. Sixth: Some scholars have said that riding a sacrificial animal is obligatory based on the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Ride it. Among those who took it literally are Ahmad, Ishaq, and the people of the apparent meaning. Ibn Nafi’ narrated on the authority of Malik: There is nothing wrong with riding a sacrificial animal in a non-excessive manner. The well-known view is that one should not ride it unless he is forced to do so based on the hadith of Jabir, for it is restricted, and what is restricted nullifies what is not. Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa said something similar. Then if he rides it when necessary, he should dismount, as Ismail al-Qadi said. This is what Malik’s school of thought indicates, and it is contrary to what Ibn al-Qasim mentioned, that he is not obligated to dismount. His proof is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) permitted him to ride, so it is permissible for him to take it with him. He said: If you resort to it until you find a back indicates the correctness of what Imam Al-Shafi’i and Abu Hanifa may God be pleased with them said, and what Ismail narrated from the Maliki school of thought. It was stated explicitly that “the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw a man leading a sacrificial animal and he was exhausted, so he said: Ride it.” Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i said: If it is less than the permissible riding, then he must pay its value and give it in charity. Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: Then its place of rest is at the Ancient House, meaning that it ends at the House, which is the Tawaf. His statement: its place of rest is taken from the ihram of the pilgrim. The meaning is that all the rituals of Hajj, from standing at Arafat, throwing the pebbles, and running, end at the Tawaf al-Ifadah at the Ancient House. According to this interpretation, the House itself is intended, as Malik said in Al-Muwatta. Ata’ said: It ends at Mecca. Al-Shafi’i said: To the Haram. This is based on the fact that the rituals are the bodies, and there is no reason to specify the rituals with their generality and to negate the specificity of mentioning the House. And God knows best.
22:34: The Almighty said: And for every nation We have appointed a ritual. When the Almighty mentioned the sacrifices, He made clear that no nation was without them, and the nation is the people gathered on one doctrine, meaning that for every group of believers We have appointed a ritual. The ritual is the slaughter and the shedding of blood, as Mujahid said. It is said: Nasak if he slaughtered, he sacrifices a ritual. The sacrifice is Nasika, and its plural is Nasak, and from it the Almighty said: Or charity or a sacrifice (al-Baqarah 2:196). And the ritual is also obedience. Al-Azhari said about the Almighty's saying: And for every nation We have appointed a ritual: It indicates the place of slaughter in this place, he meant the place of the ritual. It is said: Mansak and Mansak, two languages, and it was read with them. The Kufians except Asim read it with a kasra on the seen, the rest with a fatha on it. Al-Farraa said: The ritual in the speech of the Arabs is the usual place for good or evil. It was said that the rituals of Hajj are for people to return to it, from standing at Arafat, throwing pebbles, and running. Ibn Arafa said about His statement: And for every nation We have appointed a ritual, meaning a way of obeying God the Most High. It is said: a ritual followed the way of his people if he followed their way. It was also said: a ritual of a festival, said by Al-Farra. It was also said: a pilgrimage, said by Qatada. The first statement is more apparent, because God the Most High said: That they may mention the name of God over what He has provided for them of livestock, meaning over slaughtering what He has provided for them. So God the Most High commanded that when slaughtering, He be mentioned and that the slaughter be for Him, because He is the Provider of that. Then the wording returned from reporting about the nations to reporting those present, meaning: God is one for all of you, so the same is true of the slaughtered animal, it should be done sincerely for Him. The Almighty’s saying: To Him they submitted means they believed and submitted to His right, His face, and His blessings. It is possible that He means submission, meaning they obeyed and submitted to Him. God the Almighty says: And give good tidings to the humble ones. The humble ones are the humble and submissive believers. The humble ones are those who are on the lowest ground, meaning give them good tidings of a great reward. Amr ibn Aws said: The humble ones are those who do not wrong, and if they are wronged, they do not take revenge. Mujahid said, as narrated by Sufyan on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh: The humble ones are those who are reassured by the command of God the Almighty.
22:35: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Their hearts were fearful meaning they were afraid and wary of disobeying Him. So He described them as fearful and apprehensive when He was mentioned, due to the strength of their certainty and their observance of their Lord, as if they were before Him, and He described them as patient and establishing and maintaining prayer. It was narrated that this verse, His saying: And give good tidings to the humble was revealed about Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali, may God be pleased with them. The majority of scholars read prayer in the accusative case as an addition, and Abu Amr read prayer in the accusative case as a result of the assumption of the nun and that its deletion was for the sake of lightening due to the length of the name. Sibawayh recited: The guardians of the tribe's shame... Second: This verse and similar to the words of God Almighty: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith; and upon their Lord they rely (al-Anfal 8:2), and the words of God Almighty: “God has sent down the best statement: a consistent Book, repeated. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver at it. Then their skins and their hearts soften at the remembrance of God” (al-Zumar 39:23). This is the state of those who know God, who fear His wrath and punishment, not as the ignorant common people and the innovating rabble do with their screaming and roaring, and braying that resembles the braying of donkeys. It is said to those who do that and claim that it is piety and reverence: You have not reached the level of the state of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor the state of his companions in their knowledge of God Almighty, fear of Him, and reverence for His Majesty. Despite that, their state when admonished was understanding of God and crying out of fear of God. And likewise God the Most High described the states of the people of knowledge when they hear His remembrance and recite His Book. Whoever is not like this is not on their guidance or their path. God the Most High said: “And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of what they have recognized of the truth. They say, ‘Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses.’” (al-Ma’idah 5:83) This is a description of their state and an account of their words. Whoever is a follower of the Sunnah, let him follow the Sunnah. Whoever deals with the states of the insane and madness is among the worst of them. Madness has many types. It was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Anas bin Malik that “the people asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they overwhelmed him with questions. One day, he went out and ascended the pulpit and said: Ask me, do not ask me about anything except that I will explain it to you as long as I am in this position. When the people heard that, they were afraid that something was about to happen to me. Anas said: So I started looking right and left, and every person had his head wrapped in his garment and was crying. And he mentioned the hadith. The discussion of this issue has been discussed more fully than this in Surat Al-Anfal. Praise be to God.
22:36: It contains ten issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And the body. Ibn Abi Ishaq read and the body as two languages, the singular of which is badana. Just as it is said: fruit, fruit, and fruit, and wood, wood, and wood. In the revelation: And he had fruit. It was read as fruit as two languages. It was called badana because it fattens, and fatanaty is fat. It was said that this name is specific to camels. It was said that badana is the plural of badana with the opening of the ba’ and the dal. It is said: a man’s badana with the damma of the dal if he became fat. And badana with the shaddah on it if he grew old and aged. In the hadith: I have grown fat means I have grown old and aged. It was also narrated that he has grown fat, but it has no meaning, because it is contrary to his description, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it means a lot of flesh. It is said: A man has a fat body, he becomes fat and obese, so he is badan, meaning huge. Second: The scholars differed on whether the term badan is used for animals other than camels, such as cows, or not. Ibn Masoud, Ata’, and Al-Shafi’i said: No. Malik and Abu Hanifa said: Yes. The benefit of the difference of opinion is regarding someone who vowed a badan and could not find a badan or could not afford it but could afford a cow. Is it acceptable for him or not? According to the school of thought of Al-Shafi’i and Ata’, it is not acceptable. According to the school of thought of Malik, it is acceptable. What is correct is what Al-Shafi’i and Ata’ went to, “because of what the Prophet, peace be upon him, said in the authentic hadith on Friday: Whoever goes in the first hour, it is as if he has offered a camel, and whoever goes in the second hour, it is as if he has offered a cow.” The hadith. His distinction between the cow and the camel indicates that the cow is not called a camel, and God knows best. Also, the Almighty’s saying: And when its sides have fallen down indicates that, as the description is specific to camels. Cows lie down and are slaughtered like sheep, as will come. Our evidence is that the camel is taken from fatness, which means largeness, and largeness is found in both of them. Also, the cow in drawing closer to God Almighty by shedding blood is like the camel, so that the cow is permissible in sacrificing for seven like camels. This is an argument for Abu Hanifa, as Al-Shafi’i agreed with him on that, and that is not in our school of thought. Ibn Shajarah narrated that the sheep are called a camel, and this is an unusual saying. The camel is the camel that is offered as a sacrifice to the Kaaba. The sacrifice is general for camels, cows, and sheep. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Of the symbols of God is a text that they are some of the symbols. And His saying: There is good for you in them means the benefits that were mentioned above. The correct view is that it is general in the good of this world and the hereafter. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: Then mention the name of God over them while they are in rows. That is, slaughter them in the name of God. Sawaf means their legs are in rows. Camels are slaughtered while standing, tied up. The origin of this description is in horses. It is said: The horse is lined up, so it is safaan if it stands on three legs and bends the hump of the fourth, and the hump is the end of the hoof. And when they want to slaughter a camel, one of its hands is tied so it stands on three legs. Al-Hasan, Al-A’raj, Mujahid, Zaid bin Aslam, and Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari also read Sawafi as Sawaf with a kasra on the fa’ and a light tanween on it, and it means the one before it, but the ya’ was deleted for lightening, contrary to the norm. Sawaf is the reading of the majority with a fatha on the fa’ and a shaddah on it, from Saff yasif. One sawaf is safa, and one sawafi is safayyah. Ibn Mas’ud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Abu Ja’far Muhammad bin Ali read Sawafin with a noon, the plural of Safnah. Its singular is not safna, because fa’il is not pluralized as fawa’il except in specific letters that cannot be used as an analogy, and they are faris and fawaris, halak and hawalik, and khalaf and khalaf. The safna is the one that has raised one of its hands with its mind so that it does not become disturbed. From this is the saying of God the Almighty: The pure, steeds (Sad: 31). And Amr ibn Kulthum said: We left the horses devoted to him, imitating our leaders. It is narrated: His horses remain, Noah, imitating them, and our pure ones have helped him. Another said: The first row is like the third row, and it is still like the third row. Abu Amr Al-Jarmi said: The saphenous vein is a vein in the front of the foot. When it is struck on a horse, it raises its foot. Al-A’sha said: And every quantity like the trunk of the sycamore tree, when it is pure, it will reach the peak of the sky. Fifth: Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Abi Tha’lab told me that he asked Ibn Shihab about the Sawaf, and he said: Tie it up and then line it up. Malik ibn Anas told me the same. All scholars are of the opinion that this is desirable, except Abu Hanifa and al-Thawri, who permitted it to be slaughtered kneeling and standing. Ata’ differed and considered it desirable to slaughter it kneeling. The correct view is that of the majority, based on the statement of God the Almighty: And when its sides have fallen down meaning it falls after its slaughtering, and from this the word the sun has fallen down. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ziyad ibn Jubayr, “Ibn Umar came upon a man who was slaughtering his sacrificial animal kneeling and said: Send it as a list, bound by the Sunnah of your Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr on the authority of Jabir, some of its lists remained. Sixth: Malik said: If a person is weak or fears that his sacrificial animal will escape, then I see no harm in slaughtering it while it is tied up. The preferred method is to slaughter camels standing and not tied up, unless that is not possible, then they should be tied up and not hamstrung, unless there is fear that he will become weak and unable to handle it. Slaughtering them while standing is better than hamstrung. Ibn Umar used to take the spear in his hand when his hands were strong, and he would slaughter it in its chest and bring it out over its hump. When he became old, he would slaughter them while standing because of his weakness, and another man would hold the spear with him, and another would hold its reins. Cows and sheep lie down. Seventh: It is not permissible to slaughter before dawn on the day of sacrifice by consensus. Likewise, the sacrifice is not permissible before dawn. When dawn comes, the sacrifice is permissible in Mina, and they do not have to wait for their imam to slaughter, unlike the sacrifice in other countries. The place of sacrifice is Mina for every pilgrim, and Mecca is for every pilgrim performing the minor pilgrimage. If the pilgrim slaughters in Mecca and the pilgrim performs the minor pilgrimage in Mina, neither of them is at fault, God willing. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And when its sides have set. It is said: The sun has set if it has set, and the wall has set if it has fallen. Qais bin Al-Khatim said: Banu Awf obeyed a prince who forbade them from peace until it was the first duty. Aws bin Hajar said: Did not the sun, the moon and the planets eclipse the obligatory mountain? God Almighty says: And when its sides fall down meaning when it falls on its sides dead. He used a metaphor for death by falling on the side, just as He used a metaphor for slaughtering and slaughtering by saying: Then mention the name of God over it. Metaphors are more eloquent in most cases than explicit statements. The poet said: So I left him, the lions, to pick him up between his head and Al-Mu'tasim. Antara said: And she struck the horns of her ram, and they quarreled. That is, he fell murdered on the ground, and there are many examples. The obligation for the one in a state of ritual impurity after slaughter is a sign of the bleeding and the soul leaving it, which is the time of eating, that is, the time close to eating, because it begins with skinning and cutting off part of the slaughtered animal and then cooking it. And it is not skinned until it cools down because that is a form of torture, and for this reason Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: Do not rush souls to perish. Ninth: The Almighty’s statement: So eat from them is a command that means encouragement. All scholars recommend that a person eat from his sacrificial animal, and that there is reward and compliance in that, since the people of the Age of Ignorance did not eat from their sacrificial animal, as mentioned above. Abu al-Abbas ibn Shuraih said: Eating and feeding are recommended, and he may limit himself to whichever he wants. Al-Shafi’i said: Eating is recommended and feeding is obligatory. If he feeds all of them, it is sufficient for him, but if he eats all of them, it is not sufficient for him. This is in what is voluntary. As for the obligatory blood sacrifices, it is not permissible to eat any of them, as mentioned above. Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: And feed the contented and the needy. Mujahid, Ibrahim, and At-Tabari said: His saying: And feed is a command of permission. And the contented is the one who asks. It is said: A man was content, he is content if he asked, with the opening of the letter nun in the past and the breaking of it in the future, he is content, he is content, if he is chaste and content with his language and does not ask, like Hamd, he praises, contentment and contentment and contentment and contentment, said Al-Khalil. And from the first is the saying of Al-Shamakh: A man's wealth improves him and makes him rich, but his poverty is more honorable than his contentment. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: Some Arabs mentioned Al-Qanoo’ to mean contentment, which is satisfaction, self-restraint, and refraining from asking. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Raja’ that he read: And feed the Qanoo’, and the meaning of this is different from the first. It is said: A man is Qanoo’, so he is Qanoo’ if he is satisfied. As for the one who asks, he is the one who comes to you asking for what you have, whether he is asking or silent. Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi, Mujahid, Ibrahim, Al-Kalbi, and Al-Hasan bin Abi Al-Hasan said: The one who asks is the one who objects without asking. Zuhair said: Those who are plentiful are provided with sustenance, while those who are few are given generosity and kindness. Malik said: The best thing I have heard is that the contented is the poor, and the needy is the visitor. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan that he read and the needy and its meaning is the same as the meaning of the needy. It is said: He exposed him and he exposed him and he exposed him if he exposes himself to what he has or asks for it. Al-Nahhas mentioned this.
22:37: It has five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Their meat will not reach God. Ibn Abbas said: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to stain the Kaaba with the blood of sacrificial animals, so the Muslims wanted to do that, so the verse was revealed. The blood of the sacrifice is not related to the Almighty Creator, but it was expressed metaphorically as acceptance, meaning: it will not reach Him. Ibn Abbas said: it will not ascend to Him. Ibn Isa said: He will not accept their meat or their blood, but rather piety from you will reach Him, meaning that whatever is intended for His sake is what He accepts, ascends to Him, hears, and rewards for it. From this is the hadith: Actions are but by intentions. The reading is He will not reach God and He will attain Him with the letter ya in both of them. And from Ya’qub with the letter ta in both of them, referring to the meat. The second: The Almighty’s saying: Thus has He subjected them to you from His glory upon us by making them subservient and enabling us to control them, although they are larger than us in body and stronger than us in limbs. This is so that the servant may know that matters are not as they appear to the servant in terms of management, but rather they are according to what the Almighty, the Powerful wants. So the small overcomes the great so that creation may know that the victor is God, the One, the Subduer over His servants. Third: The Almighty’s saying: So that you may glorify God for having guided you. The Almighty mentioned mentioning His name over it in the verse before it, as He, the Mighty and Sublime, said: Then mention the name of God over it. Here He mentioned the glorification. Ibn Omar, may God be pleased with him, used to combine them when he slaughtered his sacrificial animal, saying: In the name of God and God is the greatest. This was part of his understanding, may God be pleased with him. In the Sahih, “On the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sacrificed two white, horned rams. He said: I saw him slaughtering them with his hand, and I saw him placing his foot on their sides, and he mentioned the name of God and glorified God.” Scholars differed on this. Abu Thawr said: Saying Bismillah is obligatory, like saying Allahu Akbar in prayer. All scholars agree that it is recommended. If someone says another dhikr that includes one of God’s names and means saying Bismillah, it is permissible. Similarly, if he says Allahu Akbar only, or La ilaha illa God, as stated by Ibn Habib. If he does not mean saying Bismillah, then saying Bismillah is not permissible and it is not eaten. This was stated by Ash-Shafi’i and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan. All scholars, including our companions and others, disliked sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when saying Bismillah during slaughtering or mentioning him. They said: Only God is mentioned here. Ash-Shafi’i permitted sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when slaughtering. Fourth: The majority of scholars are of the view that it is permissible for the one sacrificing to say, O God, accept it from me. Abu Hanifa disliked this, and the evidence for this is what was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, in which it says: Then he said: In the name of God, O God, accept from Muhammad and the family of Muhammad and the nation of Muhammad. Then he sacrificed him. Some of them preferred to say that based on the text of the verse: “Our Lord, accept from us. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing.” (al-Baqarah 2:127). Malik disliked their saying: O God, from You and to You, and he said: This is an innovation. Ibn Habib from our companions and Al-Hasan permitted that. The evidence for them is what Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, slaughtered two horned, white, and black rams on the day of sacrifice. When he turned them, he said: I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth. And he recited until the words: And I am the first of the Muslims. “O God, from You and for You, on behalf of Muhammad and his nation, in the name of God, and God is greatest.” Then he slaughtered. Perhaps this report did not reach Malik, or it was not authentic to him, or he saw the practice contradicting it. This is what his statement indicates: It is an innovation. And God knows best. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: And give good tidings to the doers of good. It was narrated that it was revealed about the four caliphs, as mentioned in the verse before it. As for the apparent meaning of the wording, it requires generality for every doer of good.
22:38: It was narrated that it was revealed because of the believers when they increased in number in Mecca and the infidels harmed them and those who migrated migrated to the land of Abyssinia. Some of the believers in Mecca wanted to kill whoever they could of the infidels and assassinate, betray and scheme, so this verse was revealed until His saying: ungrateful. So in it, the Almighty promised to defend and forbade in the clearest way treachery and betrayal. The emphasis on treachery has already been mentioned in (Al-Anfal), and that: "A banner is raised for the traitor at his backside, according to the extent of his treachery. It is said: This is the treachery of so-and-so." It was said: The meaning is that he defends the believers by making them successful until faith is firmly established in their hearts, so that the infidels are not able to turn them away from their religion. If they are forced, He protects them so that they do not turn back in their hearts. It was said: He defends the believers by making them superior with an argument. Then a rare infidel kills a believer, and God defends that believer by taking him to His mercy. Nafi’ read yadfa’ defending and lawla dafa’ defending. Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read yadfa’ defending and lawla dafa’ defending. Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa’i read yadfa’ defending and lawla dafa’ defending God. Yadfa’ means repelling, like ‘aqabat al-las I punished the thief and ‘a’a God may He grant him well-being. The source is dfa’an defense. Al-Zahrawi narrated that dfa’an is the source of dfa’ defending, like hasabah hisab.
22:39: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Permission is given to those who fight. It was said: This is an explanation of His saying: Indeed, God defends those who believe, meaning He repels from them the evils of the infidels by permitting them to fight and granting them victory. There is an implied meaning in it, meaning He gave permission to those who are fit to fight in the fight, so it was omitted because the speech indicates what was omitted. Ad-Dahhak said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked permission to fight the infidels when they harmed them in Mecca, so God revealed: Indeed, God does not like any traitorous ungrateful person. Then when he migrated, Permission is given to those who are being fought because they were wronged was revealed. This abrogates everything in the Quran about turning away and not forgiving. It is the first verse revealed about fighting. Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr said: It was revealed when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina. An-Nasa’i and At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was expelled from Mecca, Abu Bakr said: They expelled their Prophet so that he would perish. Then God Almighty revealed: ‘Permission to fight is given to those who are being fought because they have been wronged. And indeed, God is competent to give them victory.’ Abu Bakr said: ‘I knew that there would be fighting.’” [Al-Tirmidhi] said: This is a good hadith. More than one person narrated it on the authority of Sufyan on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Muslim Al-Batin on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr, without it saying: on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Second: In this verse there is evidence that permission is from the Shari’ah, contrary to the Mu’tazilah, because his saying: permitted means permitted, and it is a word used in the language to permit everything that is forbidden. This meaning has been mentioned previously in (Al-Baqarah) and other places. And permitted was read with a fat-ha on the hamza, meaning God permitted. They fight with a kasra on the ta’, meaning they fight their enemy. And they fight was read with a fat-ha on the ta’, meaning the polytheists fight them, who are the believers. That is why He said: because they were wronged meaning they were expelled from their homes. The Almighty’s saying: Tell those who believe to forgive is in the subjunctive mood as an answer to say in imitation of a condition and a consequence, like your saying, Get up and you will find good. It was said that it is with the deletion of the lam, and it was said that it means Tell them to forgive and they will forgive. So it is an answer to an omitted command that the speech indicated, as Ali ibn Isa said and Ibn al-Arabi chose. The verse was revealed because a man from Quraysh cursed Umar ibn al-Khattab and he wanted to beat him. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is not authentic. Al-Wahidi, al-Qushayri and others mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The verse was revealed about Umar with Abdullah ibn Ubayy in the Battle of Banu al-Mustaliq, as they camped at a well called al-Marisi’, so Abdullah sent his slave to draw water, but he was slow to come to him, so he said: What kept you? He said: The servant of Umar ibn al-Khattab sat at the mouth of the well, and did not let anyone draw water until he had filled the water skins of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Abu Bakr, and had filled the water skins of his master. Abdullah said: Our example and the example of these people is as it is said: Fatten your dog and it will eat you. When what he said reached Umar may God be pleased with him, he took up his sword, intending to go to him to kill him. Then God revealed this verse. This is the narration of Ata’ from Ibn Abbas, and Maimun ibn Mihran narrated from him that he said: “When the verse ‘Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan?’ (Al-Baqarah 2:245) was revealed, a Jew in Madinah called Phinehas said: ‘I need the Lord of Muhammad!’ He said: When Umar heard that, he took up his sword and went out in search of him. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: ‘Your Lord says to you: Tell those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the days of God.’ I know that Umar took up his sword and went out in search of the Jew, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent someone to follow him. When he came, he said: ‘O Umar! Put down your sword. He said: O Messenger of God, you have spoken the truth. I bear witness that you have been sent with the truth. He said: Your Lord says, “Tell those who believe to forgive those who do not expect the days of God.” He said: No harm! By He who sent you with the truth, you will not see anger on my face. I said: What Al-Mahdawi and An-Nahhas mentioned is the narration of Ad-Dahhak on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it is the saying of Al-Qurazi and As-Suddi, and based on this the abrogation in the verse is correct, and that the verse was revealed in Madinah or during the raid of Banu Al-Mustaliq, so it is not abrogated. The meaning of they forgive is that they pardon and overlook, and the meaning of they do not hope for the days of God is that they do not hope for His reward. It was said: that is, they do not fear the wrath and punishment of God. It was said: hope means fear, like His saying: What is the matter with you that you do not hope for God with majesty? (Nuh 71:13), meaning you do not fear His greatness, and the meaning is: you do not fear like the punishment of the past nations, and the days are used to express events. It was said: they do not hope for God’s victory for His friends and His punishment of His enemies. It was said: the meaning is they do not fear the al-Qiyamah 75:That He may reward a people for what they used to earn. The general reading is li-jazi with a ya’ meaning that God may reward. Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Ibn ‘Amir read linjazi. With the letter nun for emphasis. Abu Ja`far, Al-A`raj, and Shaiba read li-jazi with a dammah on the ya’ and a fathah on the zay for the passive verb, (wa qawman in the accusative case. Abu `Amr said: This is an obvious mistake. Al-Kisa’i said: Its meaning is that He may reward a people with the reward. Similar to it is: And thus do We save the believers (Al-Anbiya’: 18), according to the reading of Ibn `Amir and Abu Bakr in Surat Al-Anbiya’. The poet said: If a female camel gave birth to a puppy, the puppy would curse all dogs. Any insult
22:40: It contains seven issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Those who were expelled from their homes This is one of the things they were wronged with, and they were only expelled because they said: Our Lord is God alone. So His saying: Except that they say, Our Lord is God is an interrupted exception, meaning but because they said, Our Lord is God, as Sibawayh said. Al-Farra’ said that it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, and he estimated it to be returned to the preposition with, and this is the saying of Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj, and the meaning according to him is: Those who were expelled from their homes unjustly except because they said, Our Lord is God, meaning they were expelled because of their monotheism, the people of idols expelled them. And those who were expelled is in the accusative case instead of His saying: For those who fight. Second: Ibn al-Arabi said: Our scholars said that before the Pledge of Aqaba, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not permitted to go to war and blood was not permissible for him. Rather, he was commanded to call to God, be patient in the face of harm, and forgive the ignorant for a period of ten years, in order to establish God’s proof against them, and to fulfill His promise with which He bestowed His grace in His saying: And We never punish until We have sent a messenger (al-Isra’ 17:15). So the people continued in their tyranny and did not provide clear evidence. The Quraysh had persecuted those of his people who followed him from the emigrants until they tempted them away from their religion and exiled them from their lands. Some of them fled to Abyssinia, some went out to Medina, and some endured the harm. When the Quraysh rebelled against God Almighty and rejected His command and denied His Prophet, peace be upon him, and tortured those who believed in Him, worshipped Him alone, and believed in His Prophet, peace be upon him, and held fast to His religion, God permitted His Messenger to fight, resist, and seek victory over those who had wronged them, and He revealed, Permission is given to those who are being fought against because they have been wronged - until His saying - the matters.
