Third: In this verse there is evidence that the action of the forced refuge is attributed to the one who forced him to take refuge, because God Almighty attributed the expulsion to the disbelievers, because the speech is about the meaning of estimating the sin and imposing it. This verse is like the Almighty’s saying: When those who disbelieved expelled him (Bara’ah: 40), and the speech in both of them is the same, and it was mentioned previously in (Bara’ah) and praise be to God. Fourth: And had God not repelled some people by means of others, meaning, had God not prescribed for the prophets and believers the killing of enemies, the polytheists would have taken control and suspended the places of worship that the masters of religions had made clear. However, He repelled by making fighting obligatory so that the people of religion could devote themselves to worship. Jihad is an ancient matter among nations, and by it laws were made right and acts of worship were united. It is as if He said: Permission was given to fight, so let the believers fight. Then He strengthened this matter in fighting by saying: And had God not repelled some people, meaning, had it not been for fighting and jihad, the truth would have prevailed in every nation. So whoever finds jihad abhorrent among the Christians and Sabians is contradicting his doctrine, because had it not been for fighting, the religion that they defend would not have remained. Also, these places that were established before their distortion and alteration and before those religions were abrogated by Islam were mentioned for this meaning, meaning, had it not been for this repelling, the churches would have been demolished in the time of Moses, and the monasteries and churches in the time of Jesus, and the mosques in the time of Muhammad, peace be upon him. I would have demolished is from served the building, meaning I would have demolished it so it would have collapsed. Ibn Atiyah said: This is the most correct interpretation of the verse. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him that he said: Had God not repelled the infidels from the followers and those who came after them through the companions of Muhammad (peace be upon him). Although this means repelling one people by another, the meaning of fighting is more appropriate, as mentioned above. Mujahid said: Had God not repelled the oppression of a people through the testimony of just people. A group said: Had God not repelled the oppression of the oppressors through the justice of the rulers. Abu al-Darda’ said: Had God not repelled those in the mosques from those who are not in the mosques, and those who fight from those who do not fight, the punishment would have come to them. A group said: Had God not repelled the punishment through the supplication of the virtuous and good people, and other details that explain the meaning of the verse. This is because the verse necessarily requires someone who is repelled from the people and something that is repelled from them, so reflect on that. Fifth: Ibn Khuwayzmandad said: This verse includes the prohibition of demolishing the churches, churches, and fire houses of the People of the Covenant. They should not be allowed to create anything that was not there, nor should they increase the width or height of the building. Muslims should not enter them or pray in them. Whenever they increase, they must be demolished. The churches and churches that exist in the lands of war should be demolished. The reason why what is in the lands of Islam for the People of the Covenant is not demolished is because it is considered their homes and their property that they have pledged to maintain. It is not permissible for them to be allowed to increase because that would reveal the causes of disbelief. It is permissible to demolish a mosque in order to rebuild it, and Uthman, may God be pleased with him, did that with the mosque of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Sixth: It was read lhdhma with a light and heavy dal. Sawami' is the plural of sam'ah, its weight is faw'ala, and it is a tall building with an iron top. It is said: he raised the top of the tharidah, meaning he raised it and sharpened it. A man with a sharp heart, meaning he is a sharp-witted man. The one with a sharp speech is a man with a sharp ear. It was also said: he is the one with a small ear among people and others. Before Islam, it was specific to Christian monks and Sabian worshippers - said by Qatada - then it was used for the minaret of Muslims. Al-Bay' is the plural of Bay'ah, which is the church of Christians. Al-Tabari said: It was said that they are the churches of the Jews, then Mujahid added something that does not require that. Walawat Al-Zajjaj and Al-Hasan said: They are the churches of the Jews, and in Hebrew it is saluta. Abu Ubaidah said: The saluta are houses built for Christians in the wilderness where they pray during their travels. They are called saluta, then it was Arabized and said saluta. In salawat there are nine readings mentioned by Ibn Atiyah: Salawat, Salawat, Salawat, Salaluli, on the weight of fa’uli, salub with a single ba’, the plural of salib, saluth with a triple tha’ on the weight of fa’ul, salawat with a damma on the sad and lam and an alif after the waw, saluthan with a damma on the sad and lam and a shortened alif after the triple tha’, saluthan with a kasra on the sad and a sukoon on the lam and a kasra waw after a ya’, after a dotted tha’ with three dots, after an alif. An-Nahhas mentioned: It was narrated on the authority of Asim al-Jahdari that he read wa salub, and it was narrated on the authority of ad-Dahhak wa saluth with a voiced tha’ with three dots, and I do not know whether to open the sad or close it. I said: So here come ten readings. Ibn Abbas said: Prayers are churches. Abu Al-Aaliyah: Prayers are the mosques of the Sabians. Ibn Zayd: They are the prayers of the Muslims that are cut off if the enemy enters them and the mosques are demolished. So on this basis, the demolition was borrowed for the prayers from where it was disrupted, or he meant the place of prayers and the added was deleted. According to the saying of Ibn Abbas, Al-Zajjaj and others, the demolition is the reality. Al-Hasan said: Demolishing the prayers is abandoning them. Qatrab: They are the small monasteries and no one has heard of them. Khasif believed that the purpose of these names is to divide the places of worship of the nations. Monasteries are for monks, churches are for Christians, prayers are for Jews, and mosques are for Muslims. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is more apparent that they are intended to exaggerate in mentioning the places of worship. These names are shared by nations in their names, except for the church, which is specific to Christians in the Arabic language. The meanings of these names are in the nations that have a book from ancient times. In this verse, neither the Magians nor the polytheists are mentioned, because these have nothing to protect, and the remembrance of God is only found among the people of religious laws. An-Nahhas said: The name of God is mentioned therein, which in the speech of the Arabs, based on the true view, should be The name of God is mentioned therein referring to the mosques and not to anything else, because the pronoun follows them. It is permissible for it to refer to monasteries and what follows it, and the meaning would be the time of their religious laws and their establishment of the truth. Seventh: If it is said: Why are the mosques and prayer places of the People of the Covenant given precedence over the mosques of the Muslims? It is said: Because they are older in construction. And it is said: Because they are closer to demolition and the mosques are closer to remembrance, just as the former was delayed in His statement: And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds (Fatir 35:32). Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And God will surely support those who support Him, meaning those who support His religion and His Prophet. Indeed, God is Strong, meaning Able. Al-Khattabi said: Strong can mean Able, and whoever is strong over something has power over it. Mighty, meaning great and noble, as Al-Zajjaj said. It was said that it means the impregnable that cannot be resisted, and we have explained them both in the book Al-Asna in explaining the beautiful names of God.
22:41: Al-Zajjaj said: those is in the accusative case in response to those, meaning in His statement: And God will surely support those who support Him. Another said: those is in the genitive case in response to His statement: Permission is given to those who fight, and those who, if We establish them in the land are four of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and there is no one else on the earth except them. Ibn Abbas said: What is meant are the Muhajireen, the Ansar, and the Tabi'un in righteousness. Qatada said: They are the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ikrimah said: They are the people of the five prayers. Al-Hasan and Abu Al-Aaliyah said: They are this nation, if God grants them victory, they establish prayer. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: He means the governors. Ad-Dahhak said: It is a condition that God, the Almighty, has imposed on those to whom He has given power, and this is good. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong is obligatory upon the ruler and upon the scholars who come to him. People are not required to order the ruler, because that is necessary and obligatory for him, and they are not required to order scholars, because the proof is obligatory for them.
22:42: This is a consolation and comfort to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. That is, there were prophets before you who lied and were determined to destroy the deniers, so follow their example and be patient.
22:43: It has the same interpretation as verse forty-two.
22:44: And Moses denied meaning Pharaoh and his people denied him. As for the Children of Israel, they did not deny him, so it was not linked to what preceded it, so it would be and the people of Moses. "So I granted respite to the disbelievers" meaning I delayed the punishment from them. "Then I seized them" so I punished them. "So how was My denunciation?" An interrogative meaning change, meaning then look at how My changing of the blessings they were in with punishment and destruction was, so I will do the same to the deniers from Quraysh. Al-Jawhari said: Denunciation and denunciation are changing something reprehensible, and something reprehensible is one of the reprehensible.
22:45: The Almighty said: How many a town have We destroyed meaning, We destroyed its people. The discussion of how many has already been mentioned in (Al Imran. While it was unjust meaning, with disbelief. It is desolate on its thrones was mentioned in Al Kahf. And a well without a rest and a lofty palace Al-Zajjaj said: And a well without a rest is in apposition to of a town meaning, and of the people of a town and of the people of a well. Al-Farraa' thinks that and a well is in apposition to its thrones. Al-Asma'i said: I asked Nafi' bin Abi Na'im, is the well and the wolf pronounced with a hamza? He said: If the Arabs pronounce them with a hamza, then pronounce them with a hamza. Most of the narrators from Nafi' pronounce them with a hamza, except Warsh, whose narration from him is without a hamza in them, and the original is the hamza. The meaning of derelict is abandoned, as Ad-Dahhak said. It was said: empty of its people because of their destruction. It was also said: deep in the water. It was said: Deprived of its buckets and its gifts, and the meaning is close. And a lofty palace. Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, and Muqatil said: High and tall. Adi bin Zaid said: It is made of marble and covered with lime, so that birds can nest in its peaks. That is, he raised it. Saeed bin Jubair, Ata’, Ikrimah, and Mujahid said: plastered, from the word shid, which means plaster. The rajaz poet said: Do not think that I am a man, like a water snake between mud and stone. Imru Al-Qais said: There is no place but one built with Jandal Ibn Abbas said: Mushaid means fortified, and Al-Kalbi said the same. It is a passive participle with the meaning of Maf'ul, like Bai' means Mabi'u. Al-Jawhari said: Mushaid is that which is done with shed. Shaid with a kasra: everything with which a wall is covered, such as plaster or tiles, and with a fatha it is the source. You say: Shada yashiduhu shidan jasasuhu. Mushaid with a shaddah is the extended. Al-Kisa'i said: Mushayid is for the singular, from the Almighty's saying: And a lofty palace and Mushaid is for the plural, from the Almighty's saying: In lofty towers (An-Nisa': 78). And in the speech there is an omitted implied meaning: and a lofty palace like it is disabled. It is said: This well and the palace are well-known in Hadhramaut, for the palace overlooks a mountain peak that cannot be climbed, and the well is on a slope where the wind does not leave anything that falls into it except that it pulls it out. The owners of the palaces are the kings of the cities, and the owners of the wells are the kings of the desert, meaning so we destroyed these and those. Ad-Dahhak and others mentioned, as mentioned by Al-Tha'labi and Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan Al-Muqri and others, that the well of Al-Ras was in Aden in Yemen in Hadhramaut, in a town called Hadhur, where four thousand of those who believed in Salih descended and were saved from the punishment with Salih. Then Salih died, so the place was called Hadhramaut, because when Salih visited him, he died. So they built Hadhur and settled on this well, and they appointed a man called Al-Alas ibn Jalas ibn Suwaid as their governor, as mentioned by Al-Ghaznawi. Al-Tha'labi: Jalhas ibn Jalas. He had a good reputation among them and was their governor, and they made his minister Siharib ibn Sawada. They stayed for a long time and multiplied until they became numerous. The well used to water the entire city and its desert and all that was in it of animals, sheep, cows, and other things, because it had many pulleys set up on it, and many men were assigned to it, and there were troughs with a noon made of marble, which are like many basins filled for people, and some for animals, some for cows, and some for sheep. The guardians used to water it by day and by night, and they had no other water. The life of the king they ordered was long, and when death came to him, he was smeared with oil so that his image would not change. This is what they used to do when one of their number died, and he was one of those whom they honored. When he died, they were upset by this and saw that their affair had been ruined, and they all cried out in tears. Satan seized the opportunity and entered the king’s body many days after his death, and spoke to them and said: I have not died, but I have been absent from you so that I may see your actions. They rejoiced greatly, and he ordered his confidants to set up a veil between him and them and to speak to them from behind it so that death would not be recognized in his image. So they set up an idol behind the veil that neither ate nor drank. He told them that he would never die and that he was their god. Satan spoke all of this through his tongue, so many of them believed him and some of them doubted, and the believers who denied them were fewer than those who believed him. Whenever an advisor spoke to them, he rebuked and subdued them. So they applauded his worship, so God sent to them a prophet to whom revelation came down in sleep and not when awake, his name was Hanzala bin Safwan, so he informed them that the image is an idol without a soul, and that Satan had led them astray, and that God does not resemble creation, and that the angel cannot be a partner with God, and he preached to them and advised them and warned them of the power and vengeance of their Lord, so they harmed him and opposed him while he was preaching to them and not giving them advice, until they killed him in the market and threw him into a well, and then the vengeance befell them, so they spent the night satiated and satisfied with water and in the morning the water of the well had dried up and its supply had stopped, so they cried out all together and the women and children cried out, and the animals cried out with thirst, until death overwhelmed them and destruction encompassed them, and wild beasts succeeded them in their land, and foxes and hyenas in their homes, and their gardens and wealth were replaced by lote trees and thorns of the thorns and the thorns of the lion, so that nothing was heard in them except the roaring of the jinn and the roaring of the lion, we seek refuge in God from His tyranny, and his insistence on what necessitates his wrath. Al-Suhayli said: As for the lofty palace, it was a palace built by Shaddad bin Aad bin Iram, and nothing like it was built on earth - according to what they mentioned and claimed - and its condition is also like the condition of this well mentioned in its loneliness after its companionship, and its desertedness after its inhabited place, and no one can approach it for miles, because of what is heard in it of the chanting of the jinn and the strange sounds after the comfort and comfortable life and the splendor of the kingdom and the order of the people like a thread, so they perished and did not return, so God Almighty mentioned them in this verse as an admonition, a lesson and a reminder, and a reminder and a warning against the consequences of disobedience and the bad end of disobedience, we seek refuge in God from that and we seek refuge in Him from the bad outcome. It was said: The one who destroyed them was Nebuchadnezzar, as mentioned previously in Surat Al-Anbiya’ in His saying: And how many a city have We destroyed (Al-Anbiya’: 11), so their well was neglected and their palaces were destroyed.
22:46: The Almighty said: Have they not traveled through the land? meaning the infidels of Mecca and seen these cities so they would be admonished and beware of God's punishment that would befall them as it wasfall those before them. So that they may have hearts by which to reason. He attributed reason to the heart because it is its location, just as the location of hearing is the ear. It has been said that the location of reason is the brain, and it was narrated from Abu Hanifa, but I do not think it is authentic. For indeed, eyesight is not blind. Al-Farra' said: The ha' is a pillar, and it is permissible to say for, and this is the reading of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, and the meaning is the same, the masculine is for the report, and the feminine is for eyes or the story, meaning that eyesight is not blind, or the story. Eyes are not blind meaning that the eyes' sight is fixed for them. But blind are the hearts which are within the breasts meaning from comprehending the truth and considering. Qatada said: The seeing sight was made for language and benefit, and the beneficial sight is in the heart. Mujahid said: But an eye has four eyes, meaning that every person has four eYa-Sin 36:two eyes in his head for his worldly life, and two eyes in his heart for his afterlife. If the eyes of his head are blind and the eyes of his heart see, his blindness will not harm him at all. But if the eyes of his head see and the eyes of his heart are blind, his sight will not benefit him at all. Qatada and Ibn Jubayr said: This verse was revealed about Ibn Umm Maktum the blind man. Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said: When the verse {And whoever is blind in this world} (al-Isra’ 17:72) was revealed, Ibn Umm Maktum said: O Messenger of God, I am blind in this world, so will I be blind in the Hereafter? Then the verse {For indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but blind are the hearts which are within the breasts} was revealed. That is, whoever is blind in his heart to Islam in this world will be in the Hellfire in the Hereafter.
22:47: The Almighty's saying: And they ask you to hasten the punishment was revealed about Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith, and it is His saying: Then bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful (al-Ahqaf 46:22). It was said: It was revealed about Abu Jahl bin Hisham, and it is His saying: O God, if this is the truth from You (al-Anfal 8:32). And God will not fail in His promise meaning in sending down the punishment. Al-Zajjaj said: They hastened the punishment, so God informed them that nothing escapes Him, and He sent it down to them in this world on the day of Badr. God the Almighty said: And indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of those which you count. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: It means from the days in which God created the heavens and the earth. Ikrimah said: It means from the days of the Hereafter. God informed them that if they hasten Him with punishment in short days, He will bring it to them in long days. Al-Farra’ said: This is a warning to them that their punishment will extend in the Hereafter, meaning a day of their punishment in the Hereafter will be a thousand years. It was said: The meaning is: Indeed, a day in fear and hardship in the Hereafter is like a thousand years of the years of this world in which there is fear and hardship, and likewise the Day of Bliss by analogy. Ibn Kathir, Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read from what they count with a double ya’ underneath, and Abu Ubaid chose it because of His statement: and they hasten you. The rest read it with a ta’ of address, and Abu Hatim chose it.
22:48: God Almighty says: And how many a town did I grant respite to meaning, I granted it respite despite its insolence. Then I seized it meaning, with punishment. And to Me is the destination.
22:49: God Almighty says: “Say, ‘O mankind,’ meaning the people of Mecca. ‘I am only a warner to you,’ meaning a frightening warner. The warning was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. ‘Clearing,’ meaning I explain to you what you need regarding your religious affairs.
22:50: So those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and noble provision. Meaning Paradise.
22:51: And those who strive against Our signs meaning to invalidate Our signs. Failing meaning overcoming and making difficulties, said Ibn Abbas. Al-Farraa: Obstinate. Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr said: Discouraging people from Islam. Al-Akhfash said: Obstinate and competing. Al-Zajjaj: meaning thinking that they can defeat Us because they thought that there would be no resurrection, and they thought that God had no power over them, said Qatada. This is also the meaning of the reading of Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr Failing without a doubled alif. It is possible that its meaning is that they can defeat the believers in their belief in the Prophet (peace be upon him) and in the signs, said Al-Suddi. It was said: meaning they attribute weakness to those who follow Muhammad (peace be upon him), like their saying: I ignored him and I sinned against him. Those are the companions of Hellfire.
22:52: It has three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: He wished meaning he read and recited. And Satan cast into his wish meaning his reading and recitation. It was mentioned previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. Ibn Atiyyah said: It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he used to recite: And We did not send before you any messenger, prophet, or inspired one. This was mentioned by Muslimah ibn Al-Qasim ibn Abdullah, and Sufyan narrated it from Amr ibn Dinar from Ibn Abbas. Muslimah said: So we found the inspired ones holding fast to prophethood - according to the reading of Ibn Abbas - because they spoke of lofty matters of the report of the unseen, and they spoke with inner wisdom, so they were correct in what they spoke and were protected in what they spoke, like Omar ibn Al-Khattab in the story of Sariyah and what he spoke of lofty proofs. I said: Abu Bakr al-Anbari mentioned this report in his book al-Radd. My father, may God have mercy on him, told me: Ali ibn Harb told us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us: Amr told us: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he recited: And We did not send before you any messenger, prophet, or inspired one. Abu Bakr said: This is a hadith that should not be taken as meaning that it is the Qur’an. The inspired one is the one to whom revelation is sent in his sleep, because the visions of the prophets are revelation. Second: The scholars said: This verse is problematic from two aspects: The first: That some people believe that the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them, are among those who are messengers and among those who are not messengers. Others believe that it is not permissible to say a prophet unless he is a messenger. The evidence for the correctness of this is the Almighty’s saying: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet. So He made the message obligatory for the prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And the meaning of prophet is to inform on behalf of God Almighty, and the meaning of inform on behalf of God Almighty is the sending itself. Al-Farra’ said: The messenger is the one who was sent to the creation by sending Gabriel, peace be upon him, to him visibly. And the prophet is the one whose prophethood is inspiration or a dream, so every messenger is a prophet but not every prophet is a messenger. Al-Mahdawi said: This is the correct view, that every messenger is a prophet but not every prophet is a messenger. And Judge Iyad mentioned the same in the book Al-Shifa. He said: The correct view and what the great majority agree upon is that every messenger is a prophet, but not every prophet is a messenger. He provided evidence with the hadith of Abu Dharr, and that the messengers from the prophets are three hundred and thirteen, the first of them being Adam and the last of them being Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The other aspect in which there is a problem is: Third: The hadiths narrated about the revelation of this verse, none of which are authentic. Among the things that the infidels used to deceive the common people was their saying: The prophets are right and they are not helpless in anything, so why did Muhammad not bring us punishment when we had exaggerated in our enmity towards him? They also used to say: They should not be subject to forgetfulness or error, so the Lord, glory be to Him, made clear that they are human beings, and the one who brings punishment is God, the Most High, as He wills, and it is permissible for humans to forget, make mistakes, and make mistakes until God establishes His verses and abolishes the tricks of Satan. Al-Layth narrated on the authority of Yunus on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Al-Harith bin Hisham, who said: The Messenger of God (may God's peace and blessings be upon him) recited: And the star when it goes down. When he reached: Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other? he forgot and said: Indeed, their intercession is hoped for. The polytheists and those in whose hearts was disease met him and greeted him and rejoiced, but he said: Indeed, that is from Satan. Then God revealed: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet [al-Nahhas said: This is a disconnected hadith and it contains this great matter. Likewise the hadith of Qatada and he added to it: And for them are the high cranes. More disconnected than this is what al-Waqidi mentioned on the authority of Kathir ibn Zayd on the authority of al-Muttalib ibn Abdullah who said: "All the polytheists prostrated except al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, for he took some dirt from the ground and raised it to his forehead and prostrated on it. He was a very old man. It is said that he was Abu Uhayha Sa`id ibn al-`As, until Gabriel (peace be upon him) came down and recited to the Prophet (may God's peace and blessings be upon him), and he said: "What did I bring you?" And God revealed: "You were about to incline toward them a little" [al-Isra': 74]. Al-Nahhas said: This is a strange and disconnected hadith, especially from the hadith of Al-Waqidi. In Al-Bukhari, it is mentioned that the one who took a handful of dirt and raised it to his forehead was Umayyah ibn Khalaf. The rest of Al-Nahhas’s words on the hadith will come - God willing - at the end of the chapter. Ibn Atiyyah said: This hadith, which says the high cranes was mentioned in the books of tafsir and the like, but Al-Bukhari and Muslim did not include it, and no famous compiler, to my knowledge, mentioned it. Rather, the doctrine of the people of hadith requires that the devil threw, and they do not specify this reason or any other. There is no disagreement that the devil’s throwing is only for audible words, by which the tribulation occurred. Then people differed about the form of this throwing, and what is in the tafsirs and is the famous saying is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke those words on his tongue. My father, may God be pleased with him, told me that he met in the East some of the elders of scholars and theologians who said: This is not permissible for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who is infallible in conveying the message. Rather, the matter is that Satan uttered a word that the infidels heard when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other? His voice was so close to the voice of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the matter was confused for the polytheists, and they said: Muhammad recited it. A similar interpretation was narrated from Imam Abu Al-Ma’ali. It was said: What was cast was the devil of mankind, like the Almighty’s saying: And they make noise therein (Fussilat 41:26). Qatadah: It is what he recited while asleep. Judge Iyad said in the book Ash-Shifa after mentioning the evidence of the truthfulness of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that the nation agreed in the way of communication that he is infallible in reporting something other than what it is, neither intentionally nor deliberately nor by mistake or inadvertence: Know, may God honor you, that we have two points of view in discussing the problems of this hadith: One: in weakening its origin, and the second: in accepting it. As for the first point of view, it is sufficient for you that this hadith was not narrated by any of the people of authenticity, nor narrated it with a sound, connected, trustworthy chain of transmission. Rather, the commentators and historians who are fond of everything strange, who pick up everything that is sound and weak from the newspapers, are fond of it and its like. Abu Bakr Al-Bazzaz said: We do not know of this hadith being narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a connected chain of transmission that is permissible to mention, except what Shu’bah narrated from Abu Bishr from Sa’id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas, as I think. The doubt in the hadith is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca... and he mentioned the story. And no one narrated it from Shu’bah except Umayyah ibn Khalid, and others who send it back from Sa’id ibn Jubayr. It is only known from Al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas. Abu Bakr, may God have mercy on him, has shown you that he does not know of any paths that are permissible to mention other than this, and it contains the weakness that we have pointed out, along with the doubt that we have mentioned about it, which is not trustworthy and has no truth to it. As for the hadith of Al-Kalbi, it is something that it is not permissible to narrate from him or mention due to its strong weakness and falsehood, as Al-Bazzaz, may God have mercy on him, indicated. What is from it in the Sahih is: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited ‘By the Star’ in Mecca and prostrated, and the Muslims, polytheists, jinn, and humans prostrated with him.” This is an attenuation of it through transmission. The second objection is based on accepting the hadith even if it is authentic. May God protect us from its authenticity, but in any case, the imams of the Muslims have answered it with answers, some of which are weak and some of which are good. What appears and is most likely to be interpreted as accepting it is that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was, as his Lord commanded him, reciting the Qur’an in a measured manner, and detailing the verses in his recitation, as narrated by trustworthy people from him. It is possible that Satan was watching those pauses and inserting into them what he had fabricated of those words, imitating the tone of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that the infidels who approached him could hear him. They thought that it was the words of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they spread it. This did not detract from the Muslims’ belief that the surah had been preserved before that as God revealed it, and they were certain of the Prophet’s state of condemning and criticizing idols, as was known from him. Thus, what was narrated about the Prophet’s sadness over this spread and suspicion was the cause of this tribulation, and God the Most High said: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet (al-Hajj 22:52). I said: This interpretation is the best that has been said about this. Sulayman ibn Harb said: In means with, meaning that Satan cast into the hearts of the infidels when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited, like the Almighty’s saying: And you remained among us (Ash-Shu’ara’: 18) meaning with us. This is the meaning of what Ibn ‘Atiyyah narrated from his father from the scholars of the East, and Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-‘Arabi referred to it, and said before him: This verse is a clear statement of our purpose, evidence of the correctness of our doctrine, and a basis for the innocence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from what is attributed to him that he said it, and that is because God the Almighty said: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech meaning in his recitation. So God the Almighty informed us that it is part of His ways with His messengers and His conduct with His prophets that if they said something about God the Almighty, Satan would add to it from himself as he does with all sins. He says: I threw such and such in the house and threw such and such in the bag. This is explicitly stated that the devil added to what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, not that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it. Then he mentioned the meaning of the words of Ayyad until he said: No one was guided to this except al-Tabari due to his great stature, the purity of his thought, the breadth of his knowledge, and the strength of his arm in insight. It is as if he pointed to this purpose and aimed at this goal, and he wrote after he mentioned many narrations about it, all of which are false and have no basis. If your Lord had willed, no one would have narrated them or written them down, but He does what He wills. As for other interpretations, what some people have narrated that Satan forced him to say such and such is impossible, because Satan has no power to deprive man of choice. God Almighty said, informing us about this: And I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me (Ibrahim 14:22). If Satan had this power, then none of the children of Adam would have the power to obey. Whoever imagines that Satan has this power is saying the dualists and the Magians that good is from God and evil is from Satan. And whoever said that this occurred to him by mistake said: It is not far-fetched that he heard the two words from the polytheists and they were from his memory, so what he had memorized occurred while reciting the surah by mistake. Based on this, it is permissible for them to make a mistake and they are not to be held accountable for it. God the Almighty revealed this verse as a prelude to his excuse and consolation, lest it be said that he went back on some of his recitation. He explained that such a thing occurred to the prophets by mistake, and forgetfulness is only denied from God the Almighty. Ibn Abbas said: A devil called Al-Abyad came to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in the form of Gabriel (peace be upon him) and threw into the recitation of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for. Although this interpretation is more similar to the one before it, the first interpretation is relied upon, so one should not deviate from it to another, because the established scholars have chosen it. The weakness of the hadith suffices for any interpretation, and praise be to God. What also indicates its weakness and weakening in the Book is the Almighty’s statement: And indeed, they almost tempted you (al-Isra’ 17:73), the two verses, as they reject the report that they narrated because God the Almighty mentioned that they almost tempted him until he fabricated a lie, and that if He had not made him steadfast, he would have relied on them. The implication and meaning of this is that God the Almighty protected him from fabricating a lie and made him steadfast until he did not relied on them a little, so how about a lot? And they narrate in their weak reports that he went beyond reliance and fabrication by praising their gods, and that he said, peace and blessings be upon him: You fabricated against God and said what He did not say. This is against the meaning of the verse, and it weakens the hadith if it is authentic, so how about when it is not authentic. This is like the Almighty’s statement: “And had it not been for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, a party of them would have resolved to mislead you. But they mislead only themselves, and they do not harm you at all” (An-Nisa’: 113). Al-Qushayri said: Quraysh and Thaqif demanded that he face them when he passed by their gods, and they promised him to believe in them if he did so, but he did not do so! Nor would he do so! Ibn al-Anbari said: The Messenger did not approach nor did he lean. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, they almost did, and the in and lam were used for emphasis. It has been said that the meaning of wish is not recite. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God Almighty: Except when he wishes, he said: Except when he speaks, Satan casts into his wish, he said: In his hadith, Then God abrogates what Satan casts, he said: God nullifies what Satan casts. Al-Nahhas said: This is one of the best, most sublime and most important things that have been said about the verse. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hanbal in Egypt said a paper in interpretation, narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talhah, If a man traveled to Egypt intending to do so, it would not be much. The meaning is: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spoke to himself, Satan would throw it into his speech as a precaution, saying: If you asked God Almighty to give you booty, the Muslims would expand, and God Almighty knows that goodness lies elsewhere, so what Satan throws in is nullified, as Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them said. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ both reported to wish when he spoke to himself, and this is what is known in the language. They also reported to wish when he recited. It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas, and it was said by Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, and others. Abu Al-Hasan Ibn Mahdi said: This wishing has nothing to do with the Qur’an or revelation. Rather, when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had empty hands of money, and he saw the poor condition of his companions, he would wish for the world in his heart and with the whisperings of Satan. Al-Mahdawi reported from Ibn Abbas that the meaning is: When he spoke, Satan would throw it into his speech, and this is the choice of At-Tabari. I said: The Almighty’s statement: That He may make what Satan casts a trial Al-Baqarah 2:17, refutes self-talk. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: There is no disagreement that Satan casts only for audible words, through which the trial occurred, and God knows best. Al-Nahhas said: If the hadith were authentic and its chain of transmission was connected, then the meaning would be correct, and the meaning of Saha would be omitted, and its interpretation would be: Have you seen them, Al-Lat and Al-‘Uzza, and the speech would be complete, then he omitted and the high cranes meaning the angels for their intercession the pronoun refers to the angels. As for the one who narrated: For they are the high cranes, then in his narration there are answers, including that the statement is omitted as the Arabs use in many things, and it is permissible for it to be without omission, and it is a rebuke, because before it is Have you seen? and this would be an argument against them, if it was in prayer then speech was permissible in prayer. It was narrated in this story that what was recited was: Have you seen Al-Lat and Al-‘Uzza? And Manat, the third, the other? And the high cranes. And their intercession is to be hoped for. Its meaning was narrated from Mujahid. Al-Hasan said: He meant by the high gharaniq the angels, and this is how Al-Kalbi interpreted the gharaniqah to mean the angels. This is because the infidels believed that the idols and angels were the daughters of God, as God the Most High narrated about them, and He responded to them in this Surah by saying: Do you have the male and He has the female? God denied all of their sayings. And hoping for intercession from the angels is correct, but when the polytheists interpreted it to mean that this male meant their gods and Satan confused them with that, God abrogated what Satan suggested, and God perfected His verses, and removed the recitation of those two words in which Satan found a way to confuse, just as much of the Qur’an was abrogated and its recitation was removed. Al-Qushayri said: This is not correct, because He said: Then God abrogates what Satan suggests, meaning He nullifies it, and the intercession of the angels is not invalid. And God is Knowing and Wise. “Knowing” of what He revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Wise in His creation.
22:53: God the Almighty says: That He may make what Satan casts into a trial meaning misguidance. For those in whose hearts is disease meaning polytheism and hypocrisy. And whose hearts are hard so that they do not soften to the command of God the Almighty. Al-Tha'labi said: In this verse is evidence that the prophets may be forgetful, absent-minded, and make mistakes due to the whisperings of Satan or when the heart is preoccupied until it makes a mistake, then it is alerted and returns to the correct one, and this is the meaning of His statement: Then God abrogates what Satan casts into the sky, then God establishes His verses. However, the mistake is according to what one of us makes a mistake. As for what is added to it from their saying: Those are the lofty cranes, then it is a lie against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because it glorifies idols, and this is not permissible for the prophets, just as it is not permissible for someone to recite some of the Qur'an and then recite poetry and say: I made a mistake and thought it was the Qur'an. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissent. That is, the unbelievers are in disagreement, disobedience, and opposition to God Almighty and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah. Praise be to God alone.
22:54: The Almighty said: And that those who have been given knowledge may know meaning the believers. It was also said: the People of the Book. That meaning that which is most perfect of the verses of the Qur'an is the truth from your Lord, so that they may believe in it and their hearts may submit to it meaning they may be humbled and calmed. It was also said: they may be sincere. And indeed, God is the Guide of those who believe Abu Haywah read: And indeed, God is the Guide of those who believe with the tanween. To a straight path meaning He makes them steadfast on guidance.
22:55: The Almighty said: And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it. That is, in doubt about the Qur'an, as Ibn Jurayj said. And others: about the religion, which is the straight path. And it was said: from what Satan put on the tongue of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they say: Why did he mention idols with goodness and then turn away from them? Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read in doubt with a damma on the meem. The kasra is more known, as al-Nahhas mentioned. Until the Hour comes to them meaning the Resurrection. Suddenly meaning suddenly. Or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day al-Dahhak said: The punishment of a day that has no night, which is the Day of Resurrection. al-Nahhas: The Day of Resurrection was called barren because there is no day like it after it, and this is the meaning of what al-Dahhak said. The barren in the language is an expression for someone who does not have a child, and since the child is between the parents and the days follow one another before and after, the following was made in it by distance like the form of birth, and since there is no day after that day, it was described as barren. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatada said: What is meant is the punishment of the Day of Badr, and the meaning of barren is that it has no equal in its magnitude, because the angels fought on it. Ibn Jurayj: Because they did not look at the night on it, but rather they were killed before the evening, so it became a day with no night. And the same is the meaning of Ad-Dahhak’s statement that it is the Day of Resurrection, because it has no night. And it was said: Because there was no compassion or mercy on it, and it was barren of all good, and from this is the saying of God Almighty: When We sent upon them the barren wind (al-Dhariyat 51:41), meaning that there is no good in it and it does not bring rain or mercy.
22:56: The Almighty said: "The dominion that Day will belong to God. He will judge between them." This means that on the Day of Resurrection, it will belong to God alone, with no one to dispute or oppose Him. Dominion is the vastness of what is decreed for the one who has control over affairs. Then He explained His judgment, saying: Then those who believe and do righteous deeds will be in the Gardens of Delight.
22:57: And those who disbelieve and deny Our verses - for them is a humiliating punishment. I said: It may be possible that the reference with that day is to the day of Badr, in which he ruled that the infidel would be destroyed and the believer would be happy, and he, peace be upon him, said to Omar: How do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said, Do whatever you want, for I have forgiven you.
22:58: The mention of the emigrants who died and were killed was singled out as a preference and honor for them over all other dead people. The reason for the revelation of this verse is that when Uthman ibn Maz'un and Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad died in Madinah, some people said: He who is killed in the cause of God is better than he who dies a natural death. So this verse was revealed, making them equal, and that God will provide them all with a good provision. The apparent meaning of the Shari'ah indicates that the one who is killed is better. Some scholars have said: The one who is killed in the cause of God and the one who dies in the cause of God is a martyr, but the one who is killed has the advantage of what he suffered for the sake of God. Some of them said: They are equal, and they cited as evidence the verse, and the words of God the Almighty: And whoever emigrates from his home for the cause of God and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has become incumbent upon God (An-Nisa': 100), and the hadith of Umm Haram, who was thrown down from her mount and died but was not killed, so the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said to her: You are among the first,” and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith of Abdullah bin Atik: “Whoever leaves his home as an emigrant in the cause of God and falls from his mount and dies, or is bitten by a snake and dies, or dies a natural death, his reward is with God. Whoever dies by falling, he deserves the final destination.” Ibn al-Mubarak reported on the authority of Fadala ibn Ubayd in a hadith in which he mentioned two men, one of whom was hit by a catapult in a raid and died, and the other died there. Fadala sat with the dead man, and it was said to him: You left the martyr and did not sit with him? He said: I do not care which of their two graves you are sent from. Then he recited the words of God the Almighty: And those who have emigrated for the cause of God and were killed or died 2:107. Sulayman ibn Amir said: Fadala was the emir of the quarters in Rhodes, and he went out with the funerals of two men, one of whom was killed and the other had died. He saw the people leaning towards the grave of the dead man, so he said: I see you, O people, leaning towards the grave of the dead man! By the One in Whose Hand is the interpretation, I do not care which of their two graves you are sent from. Recite the words of God the Almighty: And those who have emigrated for the cause of God and were killed or died. This is what Al-Tha’labi mentioned in his interpretation, and it is the meaning of what Ibn Al-Mubarak mentioned. And the one who said that the one who was killed has an additional merit provided evidence for that which was proven from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was asked: Which jihad is best? He said: The one whose blood is shed and whose horse is hamstrung. If the one whose blood is shed and whose horse is hamstrung is the best of the martyrs, then it is known that the one who does not have that characteristic is inferior. Ibn Amir and the people of Ash-Sham read killed with emphasis to indicate abundance. The rest read it with emphasis.
22:59: He will surely admit them to an entrance that will please them. That is, Paradise. The people of Medina read it as an entrance with a fat-ha on the meem, meaning an entrance. The rest read it with a damma, and it has already been mentioned in (Subhan). And indeed, God is Knowing and Forbearing. Ibn Abbas said: He is Knowing of their intentions, Forbearing in punishing them.
22:60: The Almighty said: That and whoever punishes "That" is in the nominative case, meaning that is the matter that we have related to you. Muqatil said: It was revealed about a group of polytheists in Mecca who encountered a group of Muslims two nights before the end of Muharram. They said: The companions of Muhammad hate fighting in the sacred month, so attack them. The Muslims urged them not to fight them in the sacred month, but the polytheists refused except by fighting. So they attacked them, and the Muslims stood firm and God granted them victory over the polytheists. The Muslims felt some resentment about fighting in the sacred month, so this verse was revealed. It was also said: It was revealed about a group of polytheists who mutilated a group of Muslims whom they had killed on the day of Uhud, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, punished them in kind. So the meaning of "And whoever punishes with the like of that with which he was punished" is whoever repays the oppressor with the like of that which he oppressed him. So the recompense of punishment was called retribution because the two actions are the same in form, so it is like "And the recompense of an evil is an evil like it" (al-Shura 42:40). And like So whoever has transgressed against you, transgress against him in proportion to his transgression against you (al-Baqarah 2:194). It has been mentioned before. Then he was wronged meaning with speech and disturbance from his homeland, because the polytheists denied their prophet and harmed those who believed in him and expelled him and them from Mecca, and supported in their expulsion. God will surely aid him meaning God will surely aid Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, because the disbelievers transgressed against them. Indeed, God is Pardoning and Forgiving meaning He pardoned the believers for their sins and their fighting in the sacred month and covered up.
22:61: The Almighty said: That is because God merges the night into the day. That is, what I have told you about the victory of the oppressed is that I am the one who merges the night into the day, and no one is able to do what I am able to do. That is, whoever is able to do this is able to support His servant. The meaning of merges the night into the day has already been mentioned in (Al Imran. And that God is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. He hears words and sees actions, so nothing escapes Him, not even the weight of an atom or the creeping of an ant, but He knows it, hears it, and sees it.
22:62: The Almighty says: That is because God is the Truth meaning the Possessor of Truth, so His religion is the truth and His worship is the truth. And the believers deserve victory from Him by virtue of His true promise. And that what they call upon besides Him is falsehood meaning the idols that have no merit in worship. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Ibn Amir, and Abu Bakr read and that what you call upon with the ta' of addressing, and Abu Hatim chose it. The rest read it with the ya' of reporting here and in Luqman, and Abu Ubaid chose it. And that God is the Most High meaning the High above everything by His power, and the High above likenesses and rivals, the Holy above what the wrongdoers say of attributes that do not befit His Majesty. The Great meaning the One described with greatness, majesty, and great status. It was said: The Great is the Possessor of Pride. Pride is an expression of the perfection of the Self, meaning that He has absolute existence forever and ever, so He is the First, Eternal, and the Last, Everlasting after the annihilation of His creation.
22:63: The Almighty’s saying: Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? is evidence of His perfect power, meaning that whoever has the power to do this has the power to restore life after death, as God the Almighty said: So when We send down upon it water, it quivers and swells (Fussilat 41:39). And there are many like it. So it becomes green is not an answer, so it is accusative, but rather it is a predicate according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh. Al-Khalil said: The meaning is: Pay attention! God sent down water from the sky, and it was such and such, as He said: Didn't you ask the strong quarter to speak? And will the desert of Samlaq tell you today? Meaning: I asked him and he spoke. It was said that it is a question of confirmation, i.e. I have seen, so ponder how it becomes! Or it is a conjunction because the meaning is: Have you not seen that God sends down? Al-Farra’ said: Have you not seen is a predicate, as you say in speech: Know that God the Almighty sends down water from the sky. Then the earth becomes green i.e. full of greenery, as you say: green and vegetated, i.e. full of greenery and beasts. It is an expression of its hastening after the rain descends with plants and its continuation in this way usually. Ibn Atiyyah said: It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: This only happens in Mecca and Tihamah. The meaning of this is that he took his saying: Then it becomes to mean the morning of the night of the rain, and he went to the fact that this greening is delayed in all lands. I saw this in the farthest Sous. The rain fell at night after a drought, and that sandy land that the winds had blown away became green with weak, delicate plants. Indeed, God is Kind and Aware Ibn Abbas said: Aware of what the servant contains of despair when the rain is delayed. Kind with the provisions of His servants. It was said: He is kind in extracting plants from the earth, and is aware of their needs and poverty.
22:64: The Almighty says: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, in creation and dominion, and everything is in need of His management and perfection. And indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, so He does not need anything, and He is the Praiseworthy in every situation.
22:65: The Almighty said: Have you not seen that God has subjected to you whatever is on the earth? He mentioned another blessing, so He informed that He has subjected to His servants what they need of animals, trees, and rivers. And the ark means He has subjected to you the ark while it is running. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj read and the ark in the nominative case as the subject and what follows is its predicate. The rest read it in the accusative case in accordance with His statement: what is on the earth. "And He holds back the heaven from falling upon the earth" meaning He hates it to fall. The Kufians said: So that it does not fall. His holding it back is the creation of stillness in it, one state after another. "Except by His permission" meaning except by God's permission for it to fall, so it falls by His permission, meaning by His will and His trickery. "Indeed, God is to the people Kind and Merciful" meaning in these things that He has subjected to them.
22:66: The Almighty said: And it is He who gave you life meaning after you were sperm. Then He causes you to die when your appointed times have come to an end. Then He will bring you to life meaning for the reckoning, reward and punishment. Indeed, man is ungrateful meaning he is ungrateful for the signs that have appeared indicating His power and oneness. Ibn Abbas said: He means Al-Aswad bin Abdul Asad, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, Al-Aas bin Hisham and a group of polytheists. It was said: He said that because it is common for man to be ungrateful for blessings, as the Almighty said: And few of My servants are grateful (Saba’: 13).
22:67: The Almighty said: For every nation We have appointed a ritual meaning a law. They are its followers meaning they practice it. So let them not dispute with you over the matter meaning let none of them dispute with you over what is prescribed for your nation, as laws existed in every era. A group narrated that this verse was revealed because of the disbelievers' argument over the matter of slaughtering animals, and their saying to the believers: You eat what you slaughtered but you do not eat what God slaughtered of dead animals, so what God killed was more deserving for you to eat than what you killed with your knives, so the verse was revealed because of this argument. This has already been mentioned in (Al-An'am), praise be to God. The scholars' statement regarding the Almighty's statement: a ritual has already been mentioned. His statement: They are its followers indicates that the ritual is the source, and if it were the place, he would have said they are its followers. Al-Zajjaj said: So let them not dispute with you over the matter meaning let them not argue with you, and the evidence for this is even if they argue with you. It is said: They disputed with him, so how did he say, Do not dispute with you? The answer is that the meaning is, Do not dispute with them. The verse was revealed before the command to fight. You say: Do not let so-and-so strike you, so do not fight with him. This falls under the category of mutual action. It is not said: Do not let Zayd strike you, meaning, Do not strike Zayd. Abu Majlaz read, Do not let him disobey you in the matter, meaning, Do not let him replace you or overcome you from your religion. The reading of the group is from the word dispute. The wording of prohibition in both readings refers to the infidels, but what is meant is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And call to your Lord, meaning to His Oneness, His religion, and belief in Him. Indeed, you are on guidance, meaning religion. Straight, meaning straight, with no crookedness in it.
22:68: The Almighty said: And if they argue with you meaning they dispute with you, O Muhammad, meaning the polytheists of Mecca. “Then say: God knows best what you do” meaning their denial of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Muqatil said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, on the Night Journey while he was in the seventh heaven when he saw the greatest signs of his Lord, so God revealed to him: And if they argue with you with falsehood, then defend them by saying: God knows best what you do of disbelief and denial, so God the Almighty commanded him to ignore their arguments to protect himself from being preoccupied with their stubbornness, and there is no answer for the stubborn.
22:69: God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection meaning between the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his people. Concerning that over which you differed meaning in your disagreement My signs, and then you will know the truth from falsehood. Question: In this verse there is good etiquette that God taught His servants in responding to someone who argues obstinately and disputingly, which is not to respond or debate, and to reject this statement that God taught to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It has been said that this verse was abrogated by the sword, meaning to remain silent about opposition and to be content with saying: God will judge between you.
22:70: The Almighty says: Do you not know that God knows what is in the heaven and the earth? That is, since you have known this, O Muhammad, and are certain, then know that He also knows what you differ over, and He will judge between you. It has been said that it is a question of confirmation for someone else. That is in a book. That is, everything that happens in the world is written with God in the Mother of the Book. That is easy for God. That is, deciding between those who differ is easy for God. It has been said that the meaning is that the writing of the pen, which He commanded to write down what will happen until the Day of Resurrection, is easy for God.
22:71: The Almighty says: And they worship meaning the infidels of Quraysh. Besides God, that for which He has not sent down any authority meaning an argument or proof. It was mentioned earlier in (Al Imran). And that of which they have no knowledge, and for the wrongdoers there is no helper.
22:72: God the Almighty said: And when Our verses are recited to them as clear proofs, meaning the Qur'an. You recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve disapproval, meaning anger and frowning. They are almost violently attacking, meaning they are violently attacking. The word satwa means to attack someone, whether by hitting or cursing. Those who recite Our verses to them. Ibn Abbas said: They are violently attacking them. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: They strike them. Ad-Dahhak said: They seize them by the hand, and the meaning is the same. The root of satwa is coercion. And God is the possessor of severe attacks, meaning severe seizures. "Say: 'Shall I inform you of something worse than that - the Fire?'" That is, more hateful than this Qur'an that you hear, it is the Fire. So it is as if they said: What is worse? It was said: It is the Fire. It was also said: Shall I inform you of something worse than what befalls the reciter of the Qur'an among you? It is the Fire. So this is a warning to them for their attacks on those who recite the Qur'an. The word fire can be in the nominative, accusative, or genitive cases. The nominative case is fire, or she is the fire. The accusative case means I mean, or it is based on the implication of a verb like the second, or it can be based on the meaning, i.e. I know of you worse than that fire. The genitive case is for substitution. God has promised it to those who disbelieve on the Day of Resurrection. And wretched is the destination meaning the place to which they will go, which is the fire.
22:73: The Almighty's saying: O mankind, a parable has been made, so listen to it. This is connected to His saying: And they worship besides God that for which He has not sent down any authority. He only said: A parable has been made because God's arguments against them by making parables are closer to their understanding. If it is said: So where is the parable that was made? There are two views: The first: Al-Akhfash said: There is no parable, but the meaning is they made a parable for me, so listen to their words, meaning that the disbelievers made a parable for God by worshipping someone other than Him, so it is as if he said they made someone similar to me in my worship, so listen to the report of this likeness. The second: Al-Qutbi said: And the meaning is O mankind, a parable of someone who worships gods who are unable to create a fly, and if the fly takes something from them, they are unable to rescue it from it. An-Nahhas said: The meaning is that God, the Almighty, made a parable for what is worshipped besides Him. He said: This is one of the best things that has been said about it, meaning that God has shown you a likeness and for your object of worship. Those you call upon besides God The general reading is call upon with the letter ta. As-Salami, Abu Al-Aaliyah and Yaqub read call upon with the letter ya as a predicate. What is meant are the idols that they worshipped besides God, and they were around the Kaaba, and they were three hundred and sixty idols. It was said: the masters who turned them away from obeying God the Almighty. It was said: the devils who led them to disobey God the Almighty, and the first is more correct. They will not create a fly The fly is one name for the male and female, and the small plural is adhbaan and the large plural is dhibaan, like gharaab and aghrabah and gharaban, and it was named thus because of its frequent movement. Al-Jawhari: The fly is well-known, the singular is dhibaanah, and do not say dhibaanah. And lamdhibah is what flies are driven away with. And the fly of the camel's teeth is its edge. And the fly of the sword is its tip with which it strikes. And the fly of the eye is its human being. And the fly is the remainder of the religion. And the fly of the day is if nothing remains of it except a remainder. And oscillation is movement. And oscillation is the movement of something suspended in the air. And oscillation is the male for its hesitation. And in the hadith: He who is protected from the evil of its flies. This is something he did not mention, I mean his saying: And in the hadith: And if a fly should steal something from them, they cannot rescue it from it. Rescue and rescue means deliverance. Ibn Abbas said: They used to coat their idols with saffron until it dried up, and then it would come and steal it. Al-Suddi said: They used to make food for the idols, and the flies would land on it and eat it. The weakness of the seeker and the sought. It was said: The seeker is the gods and the sought is the fly. It was also said the opposite. It was said: The seeker is the worshipper of the idol and the sought is the idol. So the seeker seeks from this idol by drawing near to it, and the idol is the one sought. It was also said: And if a fly should steal from them something, they cannot rescue it from it. It refers to its pain in biting their bodies until it robs them of their patience and dignity. The fly was singled out for four reasons: its insignificance, weakness, disgustingness, and abundance. If this, which is the weakest and most contemptible of animals, is not capable of being created by those who worship it instead of God Almighty to create something like it and ward off its harm, then how can it be permissible for them to be worshipped gods and obeyed lords? This is one of the strongest arguments and clearest proofs.
22:74: The Almighty said: They did not appreciate God as He should be appreciated. That is, they did not glorify Him as He should be glorified, since they made these idols partners with Him. It was mentioned in Al-An’am. Indeed, God is Strong and Exalted in Might. It was mentioned earlier.
22:75: The Almighty said: God chooses from the angels messengers and from the people. The Surah ends with God choosing Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to deliver the message, meaning that sending Muhammad is not an innovation. It was said that Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira said: Or the Reminder was sent down to him from among us, so the verse was revealed. And He informed that the choice is up to Him, glory be to Him. Indeed, God is All-Hearing of the words of His servants. All-Seeing of whom He chooses from among His creation for His message.
22:76: He knows what is before them means what they have sent forth. And what is behind them means what they left behind, like His statement in Ya-Sin 36:Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have sent forth means what is before them. And their traces (Ya-Sin 36:12) means what they left behind. And to God are all matters returned.
40:60: The Almighty said: O you who have believed, bow and prostrate. It was mentioned at the beginning of the surah that it was preferred by two prostrations, and this second prostration was not considered by Malik and Abu Hanifa to be among the obligatory prayers, because he linked bowing with prostration, and that what was meant by it was the obligatory prayer, and he singled out bowing and prostration as an honor for prayer. The discussion of bowing and prostration has already been explained in (Al-Baqarah) and praise be to God alone. The Almighty says: And worship your Lord meaning obey His command. And do good is recommended in all matters other than the obligatory duties that are valid in other contexts. God the Almighty says: And your Lord says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' (Surah al-A’raf 7:10) An-Nu'man ibn Bashir narrated: I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say, Supplication is worship. Then he recited, "And your Lord says, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you. Indeed, those who disdain My worship will enter Hell [rendered] humiliated." Abu 'Eisa said: This is a hasan saheeh hadith. This indicates that supplication is worship. Most of the commentators said the same, and that the meaning is: Deem Me alone and worship Me; I will accept your worship and forgive you. It was also said that it is remembrance, supplication, and asking. Anas said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Let one of you ask his Lord for all his needs, even asking Him for the thong of his sandal if it breaks. It is also said that supplication means abandoning sins. Qatada narrated that Ka`b al-Ahbar said: This nation has been given three things that no nation before them was given except a prophet: When a prophet became an adult, it was said to him: You are a witness over your nation. And God Almighty said to this nation: That you may be witnesses over mankind (al-Baqarah 2:143). And it was said to the Prophet: There is no difficulty for you in religion. And He said to this nation: And He has not placed upon you in religion any difficulty. (al-Hajj 22:78). And it was said to the Prophet: Call upon Me and I will answer you. And He said to this nation: Call upon Me and I will answer you. I said: Something like this is not said from the perspective of opinion. It was narrated by Layth on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab on the authority of Ubadah ibn as-Samit, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “My nation has been given three things that were given only to the prophets. When God, the Most High, sent a prophet, He said, ‘Call upon Me and I will respond to you.’ And He said to this nation, ‘Call upon Me and I will respond to you.’ And when God sent a prophet, He said, ‘He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty.’ And He said to this nation, ‘He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty.’ (al-Hajj 22:78). And when God sent a prophet, He made him a witness over his people and made this nation witnesses over the people.” At-Tirmidhi al-Hakim mentioned it in Nawadir al-Usul. Khalid al-Rubai’i used to say: I am amazed at this nation! It was said to it, ‘Call upon Me and I will respond to you.’ He commanded them to supplicate and promised them that He would respond, and there was no condition between them. Someone said to him, ‘Like what?’ He said: Such as the statement of God the Almighty: And give good tidings to those who believe and do righteous deeds (Al-Baqarah 2:25), which is a condition. And His statement: And give good tidings to those who believe that they will have a sure footing (Yunus 10:2), which does not contain a condition of deeds. And such as His statement: So call upon God, making your religion sincere to Him (Al-Baqarah 2:25), which is a condition. And His statement the Almighty: Call upon Me; I will respond to you does not contain a condition. The ummah would turn to their prophets for their needs, to the point that they would ask the prophets for that on their behalf. It has been said that this is from the category of the absolute and the qualified, as explained previously in Al-Baqarah. That is, I will respond to you if you wish, like His statement: He will remove that to which you call, if He wills (Al-An’am 6:41). And the response may be in something other than what is sought, according to the hadith of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, as explained previously in Al-Baqarah, so reflect on it there. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, and Rawis on the authority of Yaqub, Ayyash, and on the authority of Abu Amr, Abu Bakr, and al-Mufaddal on the authority of Asim read saidakhaluun with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the kha’ for what the agent is not named. The rest read yadkhaluun with a fatha on the ya’ and a damma on the kha’. The meaning of dakharin is humiliated and submissive, as mentioned previously.
22:78: The Almighty's statement: And strive in the cause of God with the striving due to Him It was said: He meant by it the striving against the disbelievers. It was also said: It is an indication of complying with everything that God has commanded, and refraining from everything that God has forbidden, meaning strive against yourselves in obeying God and turning them away from desires, and strive against Satan in repelling his whispers, and against the oppressors in repelling their oppression, and against the disbelievers in repelling their disbelief. Ibn Atiyyah said: Muqatil said: This verse is abrogated by the Almighty's statement: So fear God as much as you are able (al-Taghabun 64:16). Hibat God also said: His statement the striving due to Him and His statement in the other verse: the fear of Him due to Him (AAl Imran 3:102) are abrogated by alleviating the difficulty in these commands to the ability. There is no need to estimate abrogation, because this is what was referred from the beginning of the ruling, because the striving due to Him is that from which hardship is lifted. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best of your religion is the easiest. Abu Jaafar Al-Nahhas said: This is something that cannot be abrogated, because it is obligatory upon a person, as Haywah bin Shuraih narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The mujahid is the one who struggles against himself for the sake of God Almighty. And as Abu Ghalib narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah, “A man asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Which jihad is best? At the first Jamarat, he did not answer him. Then he asked him at the second Jamarat, he did not answer him. Then he asked him at the Jamarat al-Aqaba, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Where is the questioner? He said: Here I am. He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A word of justice in the presence of an unjust ruler. God Almighty says: “He has chosen you,” meaning He has chosen you to defend His religion and adhere to His command. This is an emphasis on the command to strive, meaning that you must strive because God has chosen you for Him. The Almighty’s saying: And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty contains three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: From hardship meaning from distress. It was mentioned previously in Al-An’am. This verse includes many rulings, and it is one of the things that God has given to this nation. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: This nation was given three things that were given only to a prophet: It was said to the prophet, Go, for there is no hardship upon you. This nation was told, And He has not placed upon you in religion any hardship. The prophet is a witness over his nation, and this nation was told, So that you may be witnesses over the people. (al-Baqarah 2:143) And it was said to the prophet, Ask and you will be given. This nation was told, Call upon Me, and I will respond to you. (Ghafir
23:1: All Meccan according to everyone It contains nine issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: The believers have succeeded. Al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Anas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: When God created the Garden of Eden and planted its trees with His own hand, He said to it, ‘Speak.’ It said, ‘The believers have succeeded.’ Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Sa’ib, who said: I attended the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of the conquest, and he prayed facing the Kaaba. He took off his shoes and placed them on his left, and he began to recite Surat Al-Mu’minun. When he mentioned Moses or Jesus, peace be upon them, he had a cough, so he bowed down. Muslim narrated it with the same meaning. And in Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, he said: “When the revelation was sent down to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the sound of bees buzzing was heard near his face. One day, it was sent down to him and we stayed for an hour, then he was relieved and faced the qiblah, raised his hands and said: O God, increase us and do not decrease us, and honor us and do not humiliate us, and give us and do not deprive us, and give us preference and do not give others preference over us, and satisfy us and be satisfied with us - then he said - Ten verses were sent down to me, whoever performs them will enter Paradise - then he recited - The believers have succeeded" until he finished ten verses. Ibn al-Arabi authenticated it. An-Nahhas said: The meaning of “whoever performs them” is whoever performs them and does not contradict what is in them, as you say: So-and-so performs his knowledge. Then after these verses, the obligation of ablution and Hajj was sent down, so he entered with them. Talha ibn Musarraf recited The believers have succeeded with a damma on the alif as a passive verb, meaning they remained in reward and goodness.
