The meaning of success has already been mentioned in the beginning of (Al-Baqarah), linguistically and in meaning, and praise be to God alone.
23:2: The second: The Almighty’s saying: Humble. Al-Mu’tamir narrated on the authority of Khalid on the authority of Muhammad bin Sirin, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to look at the sky during prayer, and God Almighty revealed this verse: ‘Those who are humble in their prayer.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to look where he prostrated.” In Hisham’s narration: The Muslims used to turn around during prayer and look until God Almighty revealed: ‘Indeed, the believers have succeeded * Those who are humble in their prayer.’ So they turned to their prayer and began to look in front of them. The scholars’ ruling on the one who is praying has already been mentioned in the Qur’an, when it says: So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. (Surat al-Baqarah 2:144). The meaning of humility, both linguistically and in meaning, has also been mentioned in the Qur’an, when God Almighty says: And indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive. (Surat al-Baqarah 2:45) The location of humility is the heart, so if one is humble, all of the limbs will be humbled by his humility, as he owns them, as we explained at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah. When a man of knowledge performed the prayer and stood up for it, he would fear the Most Merciful, not extending his gaze to anything or thinking about something from this world. Ata’ said: It means not playing with anything on one’s body during prayer. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw a man playing with his beard during prayer and said: If this man’s heart were humble, his limbs would be humble.” Abu Dharr said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When one of you stands up to pray, mercy faces him, so do not move the pebbles. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. The poet said: In prayer is all goodness and virtue, because in it the souls submit to God. The first duty of our religion and the last thing that remains if religion is lifted Whoever stands up to say Takbir will be met with mercy and will be like a slave knocking at his master’s door. And he became a confidant to the Lord of the Throne when he prayed. How blessed he would be if he had been humble. Abu [Imran] Al-Joni narrated that he said: It was said to Aisha: What was the character of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? She said: Do you recite Surat Al-Mu’minun? It was said: Yes. She said: Recite, so it was recited to her: The believers have succeeded - until it reached - they guard. Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would look to the right and to the left during his prayer, and would not turn his neck behind his back.” Ka’b ibn Malik said in his long hadith: Then I pray close to him - meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - and I steal glances at him. When I turn to my prayer, he looks at me, and when I turn towards him, he turns away from me... the hadith, and he did not order him to repeat it. Third: People differed about humility, is it one of the obligatory acts of prayer or one of its virtues and complements? There are two opinions. The first is correct, and its location is the heart, and it is the first knowledge to be taken away from people. This was said by Ubadah ibn al-Samit. It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Nufayr from Abu al-Darda’, and he said: This is a good and strange hadith. Al-Nasa’i also narrated it from the hadith of Jubayr ibn Nufayr from Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja’i through a sound chain of transmission. Abu ‘Eisa said: Mu’awiyah ibn Salih is trustworthy according to the people of hadith, and we do not know anyone who spoke about him except Yahya ibn Sa’id al-Qattan. I said: Muawiyah bin Saleh Abu Amr, and it is said Abu Omar Al-Hadrami Al-Himsi, the judge of Andalusia. Abu Hatim Al-Razi was asked about him and he said: He is trustworthy in hadith, his hadith is written but not used as evidence. Yahya bin Ma’in’s opinion differed regarding him, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi, Ahmad bin Hanbal, and Abu Zur’ah Al-Razi deemed him trustworthy, and Muslim used him as evidence in his Sahih.
23:3: The meaning of idle talk and zakat was mentioned in ((Al-Baqarah)), so there is no point in repeating it. Ad-Dahhak said: idle talk here means polytheism. Al-Hasan said: it is all sins. This is a comprehensive statement that includes the statement of those who said: it is polytheism, and the statement of those who said: it is singing, as Malik bin Anas narrated from Muhammad bin Al-Munkadir, as will be explained in (Luqman). The meaning of Fa'ilun is performers, and it is eloquent, and it came in the speech of the Arabs. Umayyah bin Abi Al-Salt said: Those who feed the poor in the year of crisis and those who pay zakat
23:4: The interpretation of the third verse includes it.
23:5: Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And those who guard their private parts. Ibn al-Arabi said: One of the strange things about the Qur’an is that these ten verses are general for men and women, like all other words in the Qur’an that are open to all of them, for they are general for them, except for His saying: And those who guard their private parts. He only addressed men with it specifically, not wives, as evidenced by His saying: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess. And the woman’s guarding of her private parts is known from other evidence, such as the verses on chastity in general and in particular, and other evidence. I said: According to this interpretation of the verse, it is not permissible for a woman to be penetrated by someone she owns, according to the consensus of scholars, because she is not included in the verse. However, if she frees him after she owns him, it is permissible for him to marry her, just as it is permissible for anyone else according to the majority of scholars. It was narrated from Ubayd God ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, al-Sha’bi and al-Nakha’i that if she freed him when she owned him, they would remain married. Abu ‘Umar said: None of the jurists of the regions say this, because according to them, her owning him invalidates the marriage between them, and that is not a divorce, but rather annulment of the marriage. And if she frees him after she owns him, he cannot take her back except through a new marriage, even if she is in his waiting period. Fifth: Muhammad bin Abdul-Hakam said: I heard Harmalah bin Abdul-Aziz say: I asked Malik about a man who flogs Umairah, so he recited this verse: And those who guard their private parts - until His saying: the transgressors. This is because they refer to the male by Umairah, and the poet says about him: If you are in a valley where there is no one to visit, then flog Umairah. There is no harm or blame. The people of Iraq call it masturbation, which is derived from semen. Ahmad ibn Hanbal, despite his piety, permits it, and argues that it is the removal of waste from the body, so it is permissible when necessary. Its origin is bloodletting and cupping. Most scholars forbid it. Some scholars said: It is like doing it to oneself. It is a sin that Satan introduced and spread among people until it became a saying. I wish it had not been said. If evidence for its permissibility were established, a man of honor would turn away from it because of its baseness. If it is said: It is better than marrying a female slave, we say: Marrying a female slave, even if she is an infidel, according to the view of some scholars, is better than this, although others have also said this. However, masturbation has weak evidence and is shameful for a lowly man, so how about an adult man?!
23:6: Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Except from their wives. Al-Farra’ said: That is, from their wives whom God has made lawful for them, they do not go beyond. Or what their right hands possess is in the accusative case, conjoined with their wives, and what is a source. This necessitates the prohibition of adultery and what we said about masturbation and temporary marriage, because the woman who is enjoyed does not take the place of wives, she does not inherit nor is she inherited from, her child is not attributed to him, and he does not leave her marriage by a divorce that is renewed for her, but rather he leaves with the expiration of the period for which she was contracted and she becomes like a hired woman. Ibn al-Arabi: If we say that temporary marriage is permissible, then she is a wife for a period of time and the name of wife is applied to her. If we say that the truth that the nation has agreed upon is the prohibition of temporary marriage, then she is a wife and is not included in the verse. I said: The benefit of this disagreement is whether the punishment is required and the child is not attributed to him, like in clear fornication, or whether the punishment is waived due to doubt and the child is attributed to him. There are two opinions of our companions. Mut’ah marriage has had states in terms of permissibility and prohibition. Among them is that it was permissible, then the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) prohibited it at the time of Khaybar, then he permitted it during the conquest campaign, then he prohibited it later. This was said by Ibn Khuwayzmandad from our companions and others, and Ibn al-Arabi referred to it. The discussion of it has already been completed in An-Nisa’.
23:7: Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: But whoever seeks beyond that, then those are the transgressors. So He called the one who marries what is not permissible an aadi, and He imposed the punishment on him for his transgression. The sodomite is a transgressor in the Qur’an and language, as evidenced by the Almighty’s statement: Rather, you are a transgressing people. (Ash-Shu’ara’: 166) and as mentioned previously in (Al-A’raf), so it is obligatory that the punishment be carried out on them, and this is clear and there is no doubt about it. I said: There is a consideration in it, unless he is ignorant or interpreting it, even though there is consensus that the saying of God the Almighty: And those who guard their private parts * Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they will not be blamed is specific to men and not women. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: A woman took her slave as a concubine, and that was mentioned to Umar, so he asked her: What made you do that? She said: I thought it was permissible for me to have sex with my right hand just as it is permissible for a man to have sex with a woman whom he possesses. Umar consulted the companions of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) about stoning her, and they said: She interpreted the Book of God the Almighty in a way other than its interpretation, so she is not to be stoned. Umar said: No crime! By God, I will never make her permissible for a free man after that. He punished her for that and averted the punishment from her, and he ordered the slave not to approach her. On the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah that he heard his father say: I was in the presence of Umar bin Abdul Aziz when a woman came to him with her handsome slave boy and said: I kept him a secret but my cousins prevented me from doing so. I am like a man who has a slave girl and has intercourse with her, but my cousins prevented me. Umar said: Did you marry before him? She said: Yes. He said: By God, were it not for your ignorance, I would have stoned you. But go and sell him to someone who will take him to a country other than hers. And behind means other than, and it is the object of sought after, meaning whoever sought other than wives and slave girls owned by him. Al-Zajjaj said: meaning whoever sought what comes after that, so the object of seeking is omitted, and behind is an adverb. And that refers to every male, whether feminine or masculine. Then those are the transgressors, meaning those who exceed the limit, from exceed means to exceed the limit and transgress it.
23:8: Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And those who are to their trusts and their covenants attentive * And those who are constant in their prayers. The majority of scholars read to their trusts in the plural. Ibn Kathir read it in the singular. Trust and covenant include everything that a person carries out in terms of his religious and worldly affairs, in word and deed. This includes dealing with people, making appointments, and other things, and the goal of that is to preserve it and fulfill it. Trust is more general than covenant, and every covenant is a trust in what precedes it, whether it is a word, deed, or belief.
23:9: Ninth: The majority read their prayers and Hamza and Al-Kisa’i read their prayers in the singular form. This singular form is a generic noun, so it has the meaning of the plural. Preserving the prayer means performing it and hastening to it at the beginning of its times, and completing its bowing and prostration. This has been fully discussed in (Al-Baqarah)
23:10: Then he said: Those are the inheritors meaning whoever acts according to what is mentioned in these verses, they are the inheritors, meaning they inherit the dwellings of the people of Hell from Paradise. In the report on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, "God the Most High has made for every person a dwelling in Paradise and a dwelling in Hell. As for the believers, they will take their dwellings and inherit the dwellings of the disbelievers, and He will make the disbelievers in their dwellings in Hell." It was narrated by Ibn Majah with the same meaning. On the authority of Abu Hurairah also, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is none among you but has two homes, a home in Paradise and a home in Hell. When he dies and enters Hell, the people of Paradise inherit his home. This is what God Almighty says: ‘Those are the inheritors.’” Its chain of transmission is authentic.
23:11: It is possible that obtaining Paradise is called inheritance in terms of obtaining it without others, so it is a pseudonym in two ways: And Paradise is the highest part of Paradise, its middle and its best part. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Al-Rabi’ bin Al-Nadr, Umm Haritha, and he said: A good and authentic hadith. In the hadith of Muslim: So if you ask God, ask Him for Al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise, and from it the rivers of Paradise flow. Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hibban said: His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace: For it is the middle of Paradise means that Al-Firdaws is in the middle of Paradise in width and it is the highest part of Paradise, meaning in height. All of this confirms the statement of Abu Hurayrah: Al-Firdaws is the center of Paradise from which the rivers of Paradise flow. The word, according to what Mujahid said, is Roman and Arabized. It was said that it is Persian and Arabized. It was said that it is Ethiopian, and if that is confirmed, then it is in agreement between the languages. Ad-Dahhak said: It is Arabic and it means vineyard, and the Arabs say for vineyards Firadis. “They will abide therein forever,” so it was made feminine in the sense of Paradise.
23:12: It has five issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And We have certainly created man. Here, man is Adam, peace be upon him, as Qatada and others said, because he was extracted from clay. The pronoun in His saying: Then We made him refers back to the son of Adam, even though it was not mentioned due to the fame of the matter, as the meaning is only suitable for him. Similar to that is: Until it was hidden by the veil (Surah Sad: 32). It was said: What is meant by the lineage is the son of Adam, as Ibn Abbas and others said. According to this, the lineage is the essence of water, meaning semen. The lineage is an active participle from the word sl, which is extracting something from something. It is said: I extracted the hair from the dough, or the sword from its sheath and it was pulled out. From this is His saying: So, remove my clothes from your clothes and they will slip away The sperm is a lineage, and the child is a descendant and a lineage. He meant the water that flows from the back in a stream. The poet said: Then he came with a fierce lion, a strong and powerful beast, who was not immune. Another said: Hind is nothing but an Arabian mare, descended from mares, and is ridden by a mule. His saying: from clay means that the origin of Adam is from clay. I said: That is, from pure clay. As for his son, he is from clay and semen, as we explained at the beginning of Surat Al-An’am. Al-Kalbi said: The progeny is clay, if you squeeze it, it slips out from between your fingers, so what comes out is the progeny.
23:13: Second: The Almighty’s saying: Sperm drop. We have already discussed the sperm drop, the clot, and the lump of flesh, and the rulings related to them at the beginning of Hajj. Praise be to God for that.
23:14: Third: The Almighty said: Then We produced him as another creation. People differed about the other creation. Ibn Abbas, Al-Sha'bi, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ad-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: It is the breathing of the soul into him after he was inanimate. And from Ibn Abbas: His emergence into the world. Qatada said from a group: The growth of his hair. Ad-Dahhak: The emergence of teeth and the growth of hair. Mujahid: The completion of his youth. It was narrated from Ibn Omar. The correct view is that it is general in this and other things, such as speech, perception, good attempt, and attainment of rational knowledge until he dies. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: So blessed be God, the best of creators. It is narrated that when Omar bin Al-Khattab heard the beginning of the verse up to His saying: another creation, he said: So blessed be God, the best of creators. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is how it was revealed. And in Musnad Al-Tayalisi: And the verse was revealed: And We created man from an extract of clay (al-An`am 6:93), and when it was revealed, I said: Blessed be God, the best of creators. So So blessed be God, the best of creators was revealed. It is narrated that the one who said that was Mu`adh ibn Jabal. It is narrated that the one who said that was `Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh, and for this reason he apostatized and said: I will come with the same as Muhammad comes with. And in it was revealed: “And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about God or says, ‘It has been revealed to me,’ while nothing has been revealed to him? And he who says, ‘I will reveal the like of what God has revealed’” (al-An`am 6:93), as was explained previously in (al-An`am). And the Almighty’s saying Blessed is a verbal noun from barakah. The best of creators is the most perfect of makers. It is said of someone who makes something that he created it, and from this is the saying of the poet: Because you create what you have created, and some people create and then do not create. Some people have denied this word for people, and that creation is attributed to God Almighty. Ibn Jurayj said: He said, The best of creators because God Almighty permitted Jesus, peace be upon him, to create, and some of them were confused about that. The word is not denied for humans in the sense of making, but rather it is denied in the sense of invention and bringing into existence from nothing. Question: From this verse, Ibn Abbas said to Omar when he asked the elders of the Companions about the Night of Power, and they said: God knows best, so Omar said: What do you say, O Ibn Abbas? He said: O Commander of the Faithful, God Almighty created the heavens seven and the earths seven, and created the son of Adam from seven and made his provision in seven, so He showed it on the night of the twenty-seventh. Omar, may God be pleased with him, said: Are you unable to produce what this boy, whose hair did not come together, has produced? This hadith in full is in Musnad Ibn Abi Shaybah. Ibn Abbas meant He created the son of Adam from seven by this verse, and by his saying: And made his provision in seven His saying: Then We caused to grow therein grain, and grapes and herbage, and olives and palm trees, and gardens dense with trees, and fruits and pastures (Abasa 80:27-31) the verse. The seven of them are for the son of Adam, and the father is for the livestock. The son of Adam eats the reeds and women become fat from them, this is one saying. It was said: the reeds are the vegetables because they are reeds, so they are the provision of the son of Adam. It was said: The sticks and the father are for livestock, and the remaining six are for the son of Adam, and the seventh is for livestock, as it is one of the greatest provisions for the son of Adam.
23:15: The Almighty said: Then after that you will surely die meaning after creation and life. An-Nahhas: It is said in this meaning dead.
23:16: Then he informed about the resurrection after death, saying: Then on the Day of Resurrection you will be resurrected.
23:17: The Almighty said: And We have certainly created above you seven paths. Abu Ubaidah said: meaning seven heavens. It was narrated from him that it is said: I placed some of it above others, so the heavens were called paths because some of them are above others. The Arabs call everything above something a path. It was also said: because they are the paths of the angels. And We were not unaware of creation. Some scholars said: meaning of the creation of the heaven. Most of the commentators said: meaning of all of creation lest it should fall upon them and destroy them. I said: It is possible that the meaning is And We were not unaware of creation, meaning in taking care of its interests and preserving it, which is the meaning of the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining, as mentioned above.
23:18: It has four issues: First: This verse is one of the blessings of God Almighty upon His creation and among the things He has bestowed upon them, and among the greatest blessings is water, which is the life of bodies and the growth of animals. The water sent down from the sky is of two types: This is what God the Almighty mentioned and informed us that He deposited in the earth, and made it stored in it for people to drink and find when they need it, and it is the water of rivers and springs and what is extracted from wells. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and others that he only meant the four rivers: Seyhan, Ceyhan, the Nile of Egypt, and the Euphrates. Mujahid said: There is no water on earth except that it is from the sky. This is not absolute, otherwise the salt water is fixed in the earth, so it is possible to limit His statement to fresh water, and there is no doubt that God the Almighty has placed water on the earth and sent down water from the sky. It has been said that His statement: And We sent down water from the sky is a reference to fresh water, and that its origin is from the sea, God the Almighty raised it with His kindness and good judgment from the sea to the sky, until it became pleasant by that raising and ascending, then He sent it down to the earth for people to benefit from it, and if it were the case with sea water, it would not have benefited from its salinity. Second: The Almighty’s statement: in due measure meaning according to a suitable amount, because if it were many it would be destroyed. And from this is the statement of the Almighty: “And there is not a thing but that with Us are its depositories. And We do not send it down except according to a known measure” (al-Hijr 15:21). And indeed, We are Able to take it away meaning the stored water. This is a threat and a warning, meaning that it is within Our power to take it away and make it disappear, and people would perish from thirst and their livestock would perish. This is like the statement of the Almighty: Say, ‘Have you considered, if your water were to become sunken?’ - meaning sunken - then who could bring you flowing water? (al-Mulk 67:30). Third: Al-Nahhas mentioned: It was read to Abu Yaqub Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Yunus on the authority of Jami’ bin Sawada, who said: Saeed bin Sabeq told us, who said: Muslima bin Ali told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God the Almighty sent down five rivers from Paradise to Earth: the Sihon, which is the river of India; the Jayhun, which is the river of Balkh; the Tigris and Euphrates, which are the rivers of Iraq; and the Nile, which is the river of Egypt. God the Almighty sent them down from one spring of the springs of Paradise at the lowest level of its levels on the wings of Gabriel, peace be upon him. He deposited them in the mountains and made them flow in the earth and made benefits for people in all kinds of their livelihoods. This is what He the Almighty said: “And We sent down from the sky water in a measured amount and settled it in the earth.” So when Gog and Magog came out, God the Almighty sent Gabriel and lifted from the earth the Qur’an and knowledge and all the five rivers and lifted them to the heaven. This is what God the Almighty said: And indeed, We are Able to take it away. So when these things were lifted from the earth, its people would have the best of religion and this world.” Fourth: Everything that came down from the sky, whether stored or not, is pure and purifying, and one bathes with it and performs ablution with it, as will be explained in (Al-Furqan)
23:19: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Then We created meaning We made that the cause of vegetation, and We brought it into existence through it and created it. The Almighty mentioned palm trees and grapes because they are the fruit of the Hijaz in Taif, Madinah and other places, as At-Tabari said. And because they are also the most noble of fruits, so He mentioned them to honor them and draw attention to them. For you in them meaning in the gardens. Fruits other than dates and grapes. It is possible that it refers specifically to palm trees and grapes because there are ranks and types in them, and the first is more general for all fruits. Second: If someone swears not to eat fruit, according to our narration, he breaks his oath by eating green beans and the like. Abu Hanifa said that he does not break his oath by eating gourds, cucumbers, and carrots, because they are legumes, not fruits. The same applies to walnuts, almonds, and pistachios, because these things are not considered fruits. If he eats apples, peaches, apricots, figs, or pears, he breaks his oath. The same applies to watermelons, because all of these things are eaten for enjoyment before and after meals, so they are fruits. The same applies to dry things, except dry watermelons, because they are only eaten in some countries. He does not break his oath by eating Indian watermelons, because they are not considered fruits. If he eats grapes, pomegranates, or fresh dates, he does not break his oath. His two companions disagreed with him and said that he breaks his oath, because these things are among the most precious fruits, and are eaten for enjoyment. They are mentioned separately in the Book of God, the Almighty, because their meanings are perfect, like the specification of Gabriel and Michael from the angels. Abu Hanifa argued by saying: He once linked these things to fruit, saying: In them are fruits, palm trees, and pomegranates (al-Rahman 55:68), and once He linked fruit to these things, saying: And fruits and herbage (Abasa 80:31). The linked is not the linked to, and it is not appropriate for wisdom to mention one thing with two different words in the place of the favor. Grapes and pomegranates are sufficient in some countries, so they are not fruit, and because what is fruit, there is no difference between its fresh and dry, and the dry of these things is not considered fruit, so their fresh is the same.
23:20: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And a tree Tree is in apposition to gardens. Al-Farra’ permitted the nominative case because the verb did not appear, meaning And there is a tree, meaning the olive tree. He mentioned it alone for its great benefits in the lands of the Levant, the Hijaz, and other lands, and the lack of care for it by watering, digging, and other such things as are taken care of in other trees. It emerges is in the place of an adjective. From Mount Sinai means that God originally caused it to grow from this mountain that God blessed. Mount Sinai is from the land of the Levant and it is the mountain on which God spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, as stated by Ibn Abbas and others. It was mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah and Al-A’raf. Al-Tur is a mountain in the speech of the Arabs. It was said that it is one of the Arabized words of the Persians. Ibn Zayd said that it is the mountain of Jerusalem extending from Egypt to Ayla. There is disagreement about Sinai. Qatada said that it means good, and this interpretation requires that Al-Tur be given a nunation as an adjective. Mujahid said that it means blessed. Muammar said on the authority of a group that it means trees, and they require that Al-Tur be given a nunation. The majority said: It is the name of a mountain, as you say Mount Uhud. Also from Mujahid: Sinai is a specific stone to which the mountain was attributed because it is near it. Muqatil said: Every mountain that bears fruits is Sinai, meaning good. The Kufians read it with a fatha on the seen in the weight of fa’la’, and fa’la’ is common in the speech of the Arabs, it is prevented from being declined in the definite and indefinite because at the end of it is the feminine alif, and the feminine alif is attached to what it is in, and there is no fa’la’ in speech, but whoever reads Sinai with a kasra on the seen makes it fa’laal, so the hamza in it is like the hamza of harba’, and it was not declined in this verse because it was made the name of a spot. Al-Akhfash claimed that it is a foreign name. The second: The Almighty’s saying: It grows with oil. The majority read it grows with a fatha on the ta’ and a damma on the ba’, and the meaning is: it grows with the oil, as you say: Zaid went out with his weapon. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the ba’. There was a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of this reading. Abu Ali al-Farsi said: The meaning is its fruits grow with the oil, so the object is omitted. It was said: The ba’ is redundant, like: And do not throw yourselves into destruction (al-Baqarah 2:195). This is the view of Abu Ubaidah. The poet said: We strike with the sword and hope for relief Another said: They are free women, not housewives, with black eyes, who do not recite the Surahs. Abu Ali also said something similar to this, and it has been mentioned previously. It was said: Nabata and Anbata have the same meaning, so the meaning is as mentioned previously in the reading of the majority, and it is the view of Al-Farra and Abu Ishaq, and from it is the saying of Zuhair:...even if the grass grows Al-Asma’i denies Anbat, and accuses Zuhair’s poem which contains: I saw the needy people around their homes, planting cotton in it, until the grass grew. Any plant. Al-Zuhri, Al-Hasan and Al-A'raj read tanbat bi-dahn with the ta' raised and the ba' in the accusative. Ibn Jinni and Al-Zajjaj said: It is the ba' of the state, meaning it grows and with it its oil. In Ibn Mas'ud's reading: It comes out with the oil and it is the ba' of the state. Ibn Durastawayh: Dihn is soft water, tabbanat from inbanat. Zur ibn Hubaish read tanbat - with the ta' in the damma and the ba' in the kasra - dihn without the ba' in the accusative. Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik and Al-Ashhab read it with dihan. The meaning of the verse is to enumerate the blessing of oil to man, which is one of the pillars of blessings that health cannot do without. The meaning of olive includes all olive trees, regardless of their variety according to the regions. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And a dye for the eaters. The majority of scholars have read it. A group and asbagh are read in the plural. Aamer bin Abd Qais read and enjoyment, meaning the oil that is used to dye food. It is said: sabbagh and sabbagh, like dabbagh and dabbagh, and labas and labas. And every condiment that is used as a condiment is a dye, as narrated by Al-Harawi and others. The origin of dye is that with which a garment is colored, and the condiment is likened to it because bread is colored by dye if it is dipped in it. Muqatil said: Adam is olives, and fat is oil. And God Almighty has placed in this tree adam and fat, so the dye is based on this olive. Fourth: There is no disagreement that everything that is dyed with liquids such as oil, ghee, honey, syrup, vinegar, and other such substances is a condiment. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, specified vinegar when he said: Vinegar is a good condiment. It was narrated by nine of the Companions, seven men and two women. Among those who narrated it in Sahih are Jabir, Aisha, Kharijah, Umar and his son Ubayd God, Ibn Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, Samurah ibn Jundub, Anas, and Umm Hani’. Fifth: There is a difference of opinion regarding solids such as meat, dates, olives, and other solids. The majority of scholars say that all of these are condiments. So whoever swears not to eat condiments and then eats meat or cheese, he has broken his oath. Abu Hanifa said: He does not break his oath, and his two companions disagreed with him. It was narrated from Abu Yusuf the same as Abu Hanifa. Vegetables are not condiments according to all of them. Al-Shafi’i has two opinions regarding dates, and the well-known opinion is that they are not condiments, based on what he said in At-Tanbih. It was said that he has broken his oath, and the correct opinion is that all of these are condiments. Abu Dawud narrated from Yusuf bin Abdullah bin Salam, who said: I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, take a piece of barley bread and put a date on it and say: This is the condiment for this. And he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The best condiment of this world and the hereafter is meat. Abu Omar mentioned it. Al-Bukhari included a chapter on condiments and cited the hadith of Aisha. Condiments are derived from the word mu’addama which means to agree, and these things agree with bread, so they are condiments. In the hadith about him, peace be upon him: Eat condiments even with water. According to Abu Hanifa, the true meaning of condiment is that which comes together in a way that cannot be separated, such as vinegar, oil, and the like. As for meat, eggs, and the like, they do not go with bread, but rather go beyond it, such as watermelon, dates, and grapes. The bottom line is that everything that needs to go with bread in eating is a condiment, and everything that does not need to be eaten and is eaten separately is not a condiment, and God knows best. Sixth: Al-Tirmidhi narrated from the hadith of Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Eat olive oil and anoint yourselves with it, for it is from a blessed tree. This hadith is only known from the hadith of Abd al-Razzaq, and he was confused about it. He might mention in it ‘Umar from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, or he might narrate it with doubt, saying: I think it is from ‘Umar from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Or he might say: From Zayd ibn Aslam from his father from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Muqatil said: The mountain was specifically mentioned for olives because the first olives grew from it. It was said that the olive was the first tree to grow in the world after the flood. And God knows best.
23:21: The Almighty said: “And indeed, in livestock there is a lesson for you. We give you drink from what is in their bellies, and for you therein are many benefits, and from them you eat. And upon them and upon the ships you are carried.” The discussion of them was presented in (Al-Nahl) and praise be to God. And in Hud there is the story of the ship and Noah, and sailing the sea in more than one place.
23:22: The Almighty said: And upon it meaning and upon the livestock on land. And upon the ships in the sea. You are carried and on land one carries camels, so it is possible that the metaphor refers to some of the livestock. It was narrated that a man rode a cow in the early days and God Almighty made it speak with him, so it said: We were not created for this! Rather, we were created for cultivation.
23:23: The Almighty’s saying: You have no god other than Him. It was read in the accusative case in response to the word, and in the nominative case in response to the meaning. It has already been mentioned in ((Al-A’raf)).
23:24: The Almighty said: This is only a human being like you, who wants to dominate you meaning to dominate you and be superior to you by being followed and we are his followers. And if God had willed, He would have sent down angels meaning if God had willed that nothing be worshipped other than Him, He would have made His Messenger an angel. We have not heard of this meaning of a call like his. It was said: We have not heard of a human being like him, meaning of the message of his Lord. Among our forefathers meaning among past nations, as Ibn Abbas said. The ba in with this is redundant, meaning we have not heard of this being among our forefathers.
23:25: Then some of them turned to one another and said: He meaning Noah is only a man possessed by madness meaning madness who does not know what he is saying. So wait for him for a time meaning wait for his death. It was said: until his madness becomes apparent. Al-Farra' said: What is meant by a time here is not a specific time, but rather it is like saying: Leave him until a certain day.
23:26: So he said when they persisted in their disbelief: My Lord, support me because they have denied it. That is, take revenge on those who did not obey me and did not listen to my message.
23:27: So We inspired him meaning We sent messengers to him from heaven to build the ark as explained above. The Almighty said: So walk therein meaning enter it and make it your home. It is said: I made him walk in such-and-such and I made him walk in it if you enter it. Abd Manaf ibn Rib’ al-Hudhali said: Until they lead them in a swarm, like camels chasing strays. Of every pair two. Hafs read of every with tanween, the rest with addition, and it has been mentioned. Al-Hasan said that Noah did not carry on the ship anything except what gives birth and lays eggs. As for the bugs, flies, and worms, he did not carry any of them, but rather they came out of the clay. The discussion of the ship has already passed, and the discussion of it is complete, and praise be to God.
23:28: The Almighty said: And when you have ascended, meaning, you have risen. You and those with you on the ship, riding. Then say, ‘Praise be to God,’ meaning, thank God for saving you. From the wrongdoing people, and from drowning. Praise be to God: the word of every thankful person to God. Its explanation has already been given in Al-Fatihah.
23:29: The Almighty said: And say, 'My Lord, let me descend at a blessed place.' The general reading is manzil with a damma on the meem and a fatha on the zay, based on the source which is sending down, meaning send me down a blessed place. Zur ibn Hubaish and Abu Bakr on the authority of Asim and al-Mufaddal read manzil with a fatha on the meem and a kasra on the zay based on the place, meaning send me down to a blessed place. Al-Jawhari: Manzil with a fatha on the meem and zay is the descent, which is the solution. You say: I descended a descent and a place. He said: If I remind you of the house, its home is a camel, I cry, and the tears of the eyes flow down. Record The word manzil is in the accusative case because it is a verbal noun. An-nazlahu is also used to describe someone else. An-nazlahu is used to describe someone else. An-nazlahu is used to describe someone else. An-nazlahu is also used to describe order. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: This was when he got out of the ship, like the Almighty’s statement: “Descend with peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon nations from among those with you” (Hud 11:48). It was also said: When he entered it, so based on this, his statement blessed means with safety and salvation. I said: In short, the verse is a teaching from God Almighty to His servants when they ride and when they dismount to say this, and even when they enter their homes and greet them, they say it. It was narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that when he entered the mosque, he would say: O God, let me descend to a blessed abode, for You are the best of those who grant abode.
23:30: The Almighty said: Indeed in that are signs meaning in the matter of Noah and the ark and the destruction of the disbelievers. Signs meaning evidence of the perfection of God's power, and that He will support His prophets and destroy their enemies. And indeed We were to test meaning We were only testing the nations before you, meaning We tested them by sending messengers to them so that the obedient and the disobedient would be revealed and their condition would become clear to the angels, not so that the Lord would seek new knowledge. It was said: meaning We treat them as those who are being tested. This meaning was mentioned previously in (Al-Baqarah) and others. It was said: And indeed We were meaning We were.
23:31: God Almighty says: Then We produced after them meaning after the destruction of Noah’s people. Another generation It was said: They are the people of Aad.
23:32: So We sent among them a Messenger from among themselves meaning Hud, because there was no nation established after the people of Noah except 'Ad. It was said: They were the people of Thamud. So We sent among them a Messenger meaning Salih. They said: The evidence for this is the statement of God Almighty at the end of the verse: So the shriek seized them similar to it: And the shriek seized those who did wrong (Hud 11:67). I said: Among those who took the cry were also the people of Madyan, the people of Shu`ayb, so it is not far-fetched that they were them, and God knows best. From them means from their clan, they knew his birth and origin so that their repose until his words would be greater.
23:33: The Almighty said: And the chiefs said meaning the nobles, leaders and chiefs. Of his people who disbelieved and denied the meeting with the Hereafter meaning the resurrection and the reckoning. And We provided them with luxury in the life of this world meaning We made the blessings of this world abundant for them until they became arrogant and were given luxury, which is like a gift. This is only a human being like you, he eats from what you eat and drinks from what you drink so he has no advantage over you because he needs food and drink as you do. Al-Farra' claimed that the meaning of and drinks from what you drink is based on the deletion of from, meaning from what you drink, and this is not permissible according to the Basrans and does not require deletion at all, because ma if it is a source does not need a pronoun, so if you make it mean who then you delete the object and do not need to imply from.
23:34: And if you obey human beings like yourselves, then indeed you will be losers. He means that you will be deceived by abandoning your gods and following him without any favor from him over you.
23:35: Does He promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth? That is, resurrected from your graves. The first an is in the accusative case because ya'addukum is on it, and the second is a substitute for it. This is the doctrine of Sibawayh. The meaning is: Does He promise you that you will be brought forth when you die? Al-Farra' said: In Abdullah's reading, Does He promise you when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth. It is like saying: I think if you come out, you will regret it. Al-Farra', Al-Jarmi, and Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mubarrad said that the second sentence is repeated for emphasis, because the speech is long, repeating it is good. Al-Akhfash said: The meaning is: Does He promise you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth? The second an is in the nominative case with an implied verb, as you say: Today is the fighting. So the meaning is today the fighting will happen. Abu Ishaq said: It is permissible to say, He promises you that when you die and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth, because the meaning of He promises you is, He says that you will be brought forth.
23:36: Ibn Abbas said: It is a word for distance, as if they said, Far is what you are promised, meaning that this will not happen, which is what is mentioned about the resurrection. Abu Ali said: It is like a verb, meaning after what you are promised. Al-Anbari said: There are ten languages for Hayyat: Hayyat lak with a fat-ha on the taa', which is the reading of the group. Hayyat lak with a dhammah on the taa', and it is narrated on the authority of Abu Jaafar ibn al-Qa'qa'. Hayyat lak with a dhammah and tanween, and it is narrated on the authority of Isa ibn Umar Hayyat lak with a dhammah on the taa'. Al-Tha'labi said: Nasr ibn Asim and Abu al-Aaliyah read it this way: Hayyat lak with a dhammah on the tanween, and Abu Haywah al-Shami read it this way, and al-Tha'labi also mentioned it. Hayyat lak with an nasb and tanween. Al-Ahwas said: I remembered the days of my youth, but it is impossible for them to return to you. The seventh language: Ayhat Ayhat, and Al-Farra’ recited: Oh, oh, the agate and those in it, and oh, the vinegar with the agate, we continue it Al-Mahdawi said: Issa Al-Hamdani read hayhat hayhat with a sukoon. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Some Arabs say ayhan with a nun, and some say ayyuha with a nun. Al-Farra’ recited: And without me, the notables and the veil are all concealment, oh what I desire and far away These are ten languages. Whoever says hayhat with the taa' open makes it like ayn and kayf. It was said: because they are two compound tools like khamshara and baalbek and ram hormuz, and you stop on the second with the haa, as you say khamshara and sab'a ash-sha'ra. Al-Farra' said: Its accusative is like the accusative of thummat and rabbat, and it is possible that the fatha is following the alif and the fatha that precedes it. Whoever breaks it makes it like ams and ha'ula'. He said: It is impossible for her to return to you Al-Kisa'i said: Whoever breaks the ta' stops on it with the ha', so he says hayhaah. Whoever makes it nasb stops with the ta' if he wishes with the ha'. Whoever makes it damma, then on the basis of examples like mandu, qat, and haith. Whoever reads hayhaat with tanween, it is a plural and goes with it to the indefinite, as if he said ba'dan ba'dan. It was said: it was lowered and the nun is a resemblance to the sounds like their saying ghaaq and taq. Al-Akhfash said: It is permissible for hayhaat to be a plural, so the ta' in it is the ta' of the collective feminine. Whoever reads hayhaat, it is permissible for its akhlas to be a declined noun with the meaning of distance, and he did not make it a noun for the verb and make it a construct. It was said: he likened the ta' to the ta' of the plural, like the Almighty's saying: And when you depart from 'Arafat (2:198). Al-Farra' said: It seems that I prefer to stop on the ta', because some Arabs lower the ta' in every case, so it is like 'Arafat and Malkut and the like. Mujahid, Isa bin Omar, Abu Amr bin Al-Ala, Al-Kisa’i and Ibn Kathir would stop on it hayahah with a ha. It was also narrated from Abu Amr that he would stop on hayhat with a ta, and the rest of the reciters would do the same because it is a letter. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Whoever makes them one letter and does not separate one from the other, stops on the second with a ha and does not stop on the first, and says: hayhat hayahah, just as he says khamshara, as mentioned above. Whoever intends to separate one from the other, stops on both of them with a ha and a ta, because the origin of ha is a ta.
23:37: The Almighty says: It is nothing but our worldly life. "It" is a metaphor for the world, meaning that life is nothing but what we are in, not the afterlife that promises us after the resurrection. "We die and live." It is said: How did they say we die and live while they do not acknowledge the resurrection? There are several answers to this, including that the meaning is: We will be dead, meaning sperm, then we will live in the world. It was said: There is an inversion in this, meaning that it is nothing but our worldly life, in which we live and die, as He said: "And prostrate and bow down" (Al Imran 3:43). It was said: "We die means the fathers, and we live" means the children. "And we will not be resurrected" after death.
23:38: The Almighty said: He is only a man meaning the Messenger. Only a man who has invented meaning fabricated. A lie against God, and we are not believers in him.
23:39: "He said, 'My Lord, support me because they have denied.'"
23:40: He said, 'In a little while' meaning in a little while, and ma is an additional emphatic word. They will surely regret their disbelief, and the lam is the lam of the oath, meaning, by God, they will surely regret it.
23:41: So the blast overtook them in the commentaries: Gabriel, peace be upon him, shouted at them with one shout along with the wind with which God Almighty destroyed them, and they all died. So We made them scum meaning they perished and lifeless like the scum of a flood, which is what it carries of the old grass and reeds that have dried up and crumbled. So away with the wrongdoing people meaning destruction to them. It was said, Away with them from the mercy of God, and it is an accusative of the source. The same applies to watering for him and grazing.
23:42: The Almighty said: Then We produced after them meaning after the destruction of these people. Other generations meaning nations. Others Ibn Abbas said: He means the Children of Israel, and there is an omission in the speech: So they denied their prophets, so We destroyed them.
23:43: No nation can precede its appointed time "of" is a relative clause, meaning no nation can precede its appointed time and not delay it, like the Almighty's saying: "So when their time comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede it" (al-A’raf 7:34).
23:44: The meaning of tatara is to be repeated, and they follow one another as encouragement and intimidation. Al-Asma'i said: I sent him successive letters, one after the other, except that there was a pause between each one of them and the next. Another said: Mutawatara means succession without a pause. Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read tatara with tanween as a verbal noun in which tanween was inserted on the opening of the ra', like you say: hamdan wa shukran, so the pause on this is on the alif that replaces the tanween. It is possible that it is attached to Ja'far, so it is like arta' and 'alaq, as he said: It is hung in a ball and in a ball If he stops in this manner, then the inclination is permissible, provided that he intends to stop on the attached alif. Warsh read between the two words, such as sakra and ghadba, and it is a collective noun, such as shatta and asa. Its origin is watra from muwatara and tawatur, so the waw was changed to a ta, such as at-taqwa, at-taklaan, and tijah and the like. It was said: it is watar and it is the individual, so the meaning is we sent them individually. An-Nahhas: According to this, it is permissible to say tatra with a kasra on the first ta, and its position is accusative as a source, because the meaning of then we sent is watarna. It is permissible for it to be in the position of a state, meaning continuous. fa-ta’abana afdahutu means with destruction. wa-ka’alakahum ahadith is the plural of hadithah, which is what is spoken about, like a’jab, the plural of a’jubah, which is what is marveled at. Al-Akhfash said: This is only said about evil, We made them stories, and it is not said about good, as it is said: So-and-so became a story, meaning a lesson and example, as He said in another verse: So We made them stories and tore them apart, all torn apart (Saba’: 19). I said: It may be said that so-and-so is a good hadith, if it is restricted to mentioning that, and from this is the saying of Ibn Duraid: A person is only a story after his death, so be a good story for those who understand.
23:45: The Almighty said: Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs and clear authority. It was presented.
23:46: The meaning of high is arrogant and oppressive of others through injustice, as God Almighty said: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land (al-Qasas 28:4).
23:47: They said, 'Shall we believe in two men like ourselves?' The verse was also presented.
23:48: The meaning of among the doomed is drowning in the sea.
23:49: The Almighty said: And We gave Moses the Scripture meaning the Torah, and Moses was specifically mentioned because the Torah was revealed to him on Mount Sinai, and Aaron was a caliph among his people. If he had said: And We gave them both, it would have been permissible, as He said: And We gave Moses and Aaron the Criterion (al-Anbiya 21:48).
23:50: The Almighty said: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign. It was mentioned in (Al-Anbiya') And We sheltered them on a high ground having stability and a spring. A high ground is a raised place on the earth, and it was mentioned in (Al-Baqarah). What is meant by it here in Abu Hurairah's statement is Palestine. And from him also Ramla, and it was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Al-Musayyab, and Ibn Salam said: Damascus. Ka'b and Qatadah said: Jerusalem. Ka'b said: It is the closest land to the sky by eighteen miles. He said: I was lying in a grave on a hill, buffeted by south and north winds. Ibn Zayd said: Egypt. Salim Al-Aftas narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair: And We settled them on a high ground. He said: The elevated part of the earth. With a place of rest means flat, on which one can settle. It was also said: With fruits, and for the sake of the fruits, the inhabitants settle on it. A spring is running water that is visible to the eyes. It is said: Ma’in and Ma’an, just as it is said: Raghif and Raghf, said by Ali bin Sulaiman. Al-Zajjaj said: It is the running water in the eyes, so the meem according to this is redundant like its redundancy in Mabi’, and likewise the meem is redundant in the opinion of those who said that it is the water that is seen with the eye. It was also said: It is Fa’il with the meaning of Maf’ul. Ali bin Sulaiman said: It is said that the water is flowing if it is flowing, so it is Ma’in and Ma’youn. Ibn Al-A’rabi: The flowing water is flowing and smooth, and it is also flowing and flowing, and the waters of Ma’nan.
23:51: It has three issues: First: It was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O people, God is good and accepts only that which is good. God has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, saying: ‘O messengers, eat from the good foods and work righteousness. Indeed, I, of what you do, am Knowing.’” And the Most High has said: O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided for you. Then He mentioned - a man who travels far, disheveled and dusty, stretching his hands to the sky, O Lord, O Lord, while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and he has been nourished with unlawful things. So how can his supplication be answered?” Second: Some scholars said: The address in this verse is to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and that he placed him in the position of the messengers, as he said: To whom the people said (Al Imran 3:173) meaning Nu’aym ibn Mas’ud. Al-Zajjaj said: This is an address to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and the plural indicates that all the messengers were commanded thus, meaning eat from what is lawful. Al-Tabari said: The address is to Jesus, peace be upon him, it was narrated that he used to eat from his mother’s spinning. It is well-known that he used to eat from wild herbs. The reason for his address to Jesus is what we mentioned of his appreciation for Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, as an honor to him. It was said: This statement was addressed to every prophet, because this is their way that they should be upon. So the meaning is: And We said, O messengers, eat from the good things, as you say to a merchant: O merchants, you should avoid usury, so you are addressing him in this sense. This is coupled with the fact that this article is suitable for all of his kind, for they were never addressed together, may God’s prayers be upon them all, but rather each one was addressed in his own time. Al-Farra’ said: It is like saying to one man: Stop your harm to us. Third: God the Almighty equated the prophets and the believers in the address regarding the obligation to eat what is lawful and avoid what is unlawful, then He included all of them in the threat contained in His saying: Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do. May God’s prayers and peace be upon His messengers and prophets. If this is the case with them, then what do all people think of themselves? We have already discussed good things and provision in more than one place, and praise be to God. In His saying, peace be upon him: He extends his hands, is evidence of the permissibility of extending the hands when supplicating to the heavens, and the disagreement and discussion of this have already been mentioned, and praise be to God. His saying, peace be upon him: How can that be answered? is by way of improbability, meaning that he is not worthy of having his supplication answered, but it is permissible for God to answer him out of favor, kindness, and generosity.
23:52: It has four issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And indeed, this nation of yours is one nation. The meaning is: What was mentioned above is your religion and your nation, so adhere to it. The nation here is the religion, and its implications have been mentioned above, including the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, we found our fathers upon a religion (al-Zukhruf 43:23), meaning upon a religion. Al-Nabigha said: I swore and left no doubt for you. Can a slave be held accountable while he is obedient? Second: It was read and this with a kasra on in for severing, and with a fatha on it and a shaddah on the nun. Al-Khalil said: It is in the accusative case because the preposition has not been removed, meaning I know that this is your religion that I have commanded you to believe in. Al-Farra’ said: that is related to an implied verb, the meaning of which is: and know that this is your nation. According to Sibawayh, it is related to His statement: so fear God, and the meaning is fear God because your nation is one. This is like the statement of God the Most High: And that the mosques are for God, so do not invoke with God anyone (al-Jinn 72:18), meaning because the mosques are for God, so do not invoke with Him other than Him. And like His statement: for the mutual security of the Quraysh, meaning let them worship the Lord of this House for the mutual security of the Quraysh. Third: This verse strengthens the fact that the Almighty’s statement, O Messengers, is addressing all of them, and that it is based on the assumption that they were present. If you assume that O Messengers is addressing Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, then the connection between this verse and His statement, Then be cut off, is clear. As for His statement, And I am your Lord, so fear Me, even if it was said to the prophets, then their nations are included in it in meaning, then a connection is appropriate after that.
23:53: So they were cut off meaning they separated, meaning the nations, meaning they made their religions religions after they were ordered to unite. Then the Almighty mentioned that each of them was impressed by his opinion and his misguidance, and this is the height of misguidance. Fourth: This verse refers to the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Behold, those before you from the People of the Book split into seventy-two sects, and this nation will split into seventy-three sects, seventy-two of which will be in Hellfire and one of which will be in Paradise, and that is the Jama’ah.” Narrated by Abu Dawud, and narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who added: They said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? He said: What I and my companions are upon. Narrated by Abdullah ibn Amr. This shows that the division warned against in the verse and the hadith is in the fundamentals and principles of the religion, because they are called religions, and it is stated that adhering to any of those religions necessitates entering Hellfire. The same cannot be said about the branches, because it does not necessitate changing the religions or punishing in Hellfire. God the Most High said: To each of you We prescribed a law and a method. (al-Ma’idah 5:48) God the Almighty said: Zubran meaning books they made up and misguidances they invented, as stated by Ibn Zayd. It was also said that they divided the books, so a group followed the scrolls, a group followed the Torah, a group followed the Psalms, and a group followed the Gospel. Then they changed and substituted all of them, as stated by Qatada. It was also said that each group took a book that they believed in and disbelieved in everything else. Zubran with a damma on the ba’ is the reading of Nafi’, the plural of Zabur. Al-A’mash and Abu Amr differed from him, Zubran with a fatha on the ba’, meaning pieces like pieces of iron, as stated by God the Almighty: Bring me sheets of iron (al-Kahf 18:96). Every party means a group and a religion. With what they have means what they have of the religion. Rejoicing means admiring it.
23:54: This verse is an example of Quraysh addressing Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding their situation, connected by his saying: So leave them in their immersion for a time meaning leave those who are in the same position as those who came before, and do not be distressed by delaying the punishment for them, for everything has its time. In the language, ghamrah is what engulfs you and what rises above you, and its origin is covering, and from it comes ghamr, hatred, because it covers the heart. Ghamr is abundant water because it covers the earth. Ghamr is the cloak that covers people with gifts. He said: If he smiles and laughs, the necks of money will be closed because of his laughter. What is meant here is confusion, heedlessness and misguidance. So-and-so entered the crowd of people, i.e., into their throng. And the Almighty’s statement: until a time, Mujahid said: until death. So it is a threat, not a time limit, as one would say: The day will come to you.
23:55: The Almighty said: Do they think that what We provide them with of wealth and children? "What" means which, that is, do they think, O Muhammad, that what We give them in this world of wealth and children is a reward for them? It is only a lure and a delay, not hastening in good deeds. There are three opinions regarding the report of "that", one of which is that it is omitted. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that We hasten them with it in good deeds, and it was omitted. Hisham Al-Darir said a precise opinion, he said: "Anma" is the good deeds, so the meaning became: We hasten them with it, then he made it clear and said "in good deeds", and there is no omission in it according to this estimation. The doctrine of Al-Kisa'i is that "Anma" is one letter, so it does not need to estimate the omission, and it is permissible to stop at his saying: "and sons." Whoever says: "Anma is two letters, then there must be a pronoun that refers from the report to the name of that and the stop is not complete at and sons." Al-Sakhtiyani said: It is not appropriate to stop at wabanin because yahasboon needs two objects, so the two objects are completed by fi al-khayrat. Ibn al-Anbari said: This is a mistake because an is sufficient as a noun of an and its predicate, and it is not permissible to bring a second object after an.
23:56: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Salami and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra read yusara'a with a ya', so that its subject is our support. This may be without deletion, i.e. He hastens to provide them with support. It may also be deletion, and the meaning is that God hastens to them. It was read yusara'a lahum fi al-khayrat and there are three ways to do this: One of them is with deletion. It may be yusara'a al-imdad. It may be that lahum is a noun for something whose subject is not named, as mentioned by al-Nahhas. Al-Mahdawi said: Al-Hurr al-Nahwi read nusara'a lahum fi al-khayrat and this is the meaning of the reading of the group. Al-Tha'labi said: The correct reading is the reading of the common people, because of his saying Namdhum. Rather, they do not feel that this is a trial for them and a lure.
23:57: The Almighty said: Indeed, those who are fearful of their Lord When He finished mentioning the disbelievers and threatening them, He followed that by mentioning the believers who hasten to do good deeds and promising them, and He mentioned that with their most eloquent attributes. And fearful is fearful and apprehensive of what God Almighty has frightened them with.
23:58: And those who believe in the verses of their Lord.
23:59: And those who do not associate anything with their Lord.
23:60: And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful. Al-Hasan said: They give sincerely and fear that it will not be accepted from them. At-Tirmidhi narrated: "On the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, she said: I asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about this verse: "And those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful." Aisha said: Are they those who drink alcohol and steal? He said: No, O daughter of As-Siddiq, but they are those who fast, pray, and give charity, and they fear that it will not be accepted from them. Those are the ones who hasten to do good deeds." Al-Hasan said: We have known people who were more afraid that their good deeds would be rejected than you are of your bad deeds that you would be punished for them. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, Ibn Abbas, and An-Nakha'i recited: And those who give what they give shortened from coming. Al-Farra’ said: Even if this reading from Aisha was authentic, it would not contradict the reading of the group, because the hamza of the Arabs requires an alif in all cases when writing, so it is written sala al-rajul with an alif after the seen, and yastadhahu with an alif between the zay and the waw, and shay’ wa shay’ with an alif after the ya’, so it is not strange according to the doctrine of these people to write yu’tu with an alif after the ya’, so this wording, based on this script, can have two readings: yu’tu ma a’tawa and yu’tu ma a’tawa. The only thing that the group is based on is that it can have two possible interpretations: One of them is: And those who give what they give of zakat and charity, while their hearts are fearful. The other is: And those who give to the angels who record the deeds of the servants what they give, while their hearts are fearful. So the object was omitted in this chapter because its meaning is clear, just as it was omitted in the statement of God the Almighty: Therein people are given relief, and therein they press (Yusuf 12:49), and the meaning is they press sesame and grapes, so the object was abbreviated because its interpretation is clear. The original letter is as it is spelled in the Imam yatu’u with an alif replaced by a hamza, so the alif was written as a waw because of the brotherhood of the long and soft letters in the secret, as narrated by Ibn al-Anbari. Al-Nahhas said: What is known from the reading of Ibn Abbas is and those who come what they come and it is the reading narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and its meaning is they do what they do, as narrated in the hadith. And fear is like compassion and fear, so the pious and the repentant fear the matter of the consequence and what he will see after death. And in His saying: Indeed, to their Lord we will return is a reminder of the conclusion. And in Sahih al-Bukhari: Actions are judged by their endings. As for the one who mixes things up, he should be under fear that the threat of his mixing up will be carried out against him. The scholars of thoughts said: The one who knows fears obeying Him more than he fears disobeying Him, because disobedience is erased by repentance, and obedience is sought by correcting the obligation. They means because they, or because they will return to their Lord.
23:61: The Almighty says: Those hasten to good deeds meaning to acts of obedience, so that they may attain the highest ranks and chambers. It was read they hasten to good deeds meaning they are quick to do them. they hasten means they race those who precede them to them, so the object is omitted. Al-Zajjaj said: they hasten is more eloquent than they hasten. And they are the first to it. The best thing that has been said about it is that they are the first to its times. This indicates that prayer at the beginning of its time is better, as mentioned in (Al-Baqarah). And whoever is ahead in something is the first to it, and whoever is behind from it has been preceded by his death. So the lam in to it according to this statement means to, as he said: That your Lord has inspired it (al-Zalzalah 99:5) meaning inspired it. And Sibawayh recited: My camel turned away from the Yamamah valley, and I did not intend to visit anyone but you from its people. On the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the meaning of and they are the first to do it, happiness has been given to them by God, and therefore they hastened to do good deeds. It was said: The meaning is that they are the first to do good deeds.
23:62: The Almighty's saying: And We charge no soul except [with that within] its capacity has already been mentioned in (Al-Baqarah) and that it abrogates all that has been mentioned in the Shariah about charging what is not possible. And with Us is a book that speaks the truth The most apparent of what has been said about it is that he meant the book of enumeration of deeds that the angels carry, and he attributed it to himself because the angels wrote in it the deeds of the servants by his command, so it speaks the truth. In this there is a threat and despair from injustice and oppression. The word speaking is permissible in the book, and what is meant is that the prophets speak what is in it. And God knows best. It was said: He meant the Preserved Tablet, and everything has been established in it, so they do not go beyond that. It was said: The reference in his saying And with Us is a book is the Qur'an, and God knows best, and each is possible, but the first is more apparent.
23:63: The Almighty said: Rather, their hearts are in a state of confusion about this. Mujahid said: meaning, in a covering, heedlessness, and blindness to the Qur'an. It is said: The water covered him if it covered him. A river covers whoever enters it. A man is immersed in the opinions of people. It was said: Ghamrah because it covers the face. From this, he entered into the midst of people and their veil, meaning in what he covers of the crowd. It was said: Rather, their hearts are in a state of confusion meaning, in confusion and blindness, meaning from what was described of the righteous deeds in the previous verses, as Qatada said. Or from the Book that speaks the truth. And they have deeds other than that, they are doing them. Qatada and Mujahid said: meaning, they have sins that they must do without the truth. Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: The meaning is that they have bad deeds that they did not do without what they are upon, they must do them without the deeds of the believers, and they will enter the Fire because of them, because of what preceded them of misery. Thirdly, it is possible that it is injustice to creation along with disbelief in the Creator, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. The meaning is close.
23:64: Until when We seized their affluent ones with punishment meaning with the sword on the day of Badr, as Ibn Abbas said. Ad-Dahhak said: He meant with hunger when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “O God, make your punishment severe upon Mudar. O God, make it suffer years like the years of Joseph.” So God afflicted them with famine and hunger until they ate bones, dead animals, dogs and carrion, and their wealth was destroyed by their supplication, as an ox does. Al-A’sha said, describing a cow: She went around three times in a day and a night, and the objection was that she would host and trade. Al-Jawhari said: “Jawar is like lowing. It is said: The bull roared, meaning it cried out. Some of them read it as a calf with a body that roared, as narrated by Al-Akhfash. And the man cried out to God Almighty, supplicating with prayer. Qatada: They cry out in repentance, but it is not accepted from them. He said: He alternates between the prayers of the King, at breakfast, prostration, and at night. Ibn Jurayj said: “Until when We seized their affluent ones with punishment” they are those who were killed at Badr at once they cried out they are those in Mecca, so he combined the two previous statements, and it is good.
23:65: Do not cry out today, for you are from Us meaning from Our punishment. You will not be helped you will not be prevented and your impatience will not benefit you. Al-Hasan said: You will not be helped by the acceptance of repentance. It was said: The meaning of this prohibition is to inform, meaning that if you supplicate, it will not benefit you.
23:66: The Almighty says: My verses were recited to you, but you were turning back on your heels. The verses refer to the Qur'an. Were recited to you means read. Ad-Dahhak said: Before you were punished by killing and turned back means you went back behind you. Mujahid: You were delayed, and its origin is to go back in reverse. The poet said: They claimed that they were on the path to salvation, but they turned back on their heels. Here it is a metaphor for turning away from the truth. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, read on your backs instead of on your heels, “you turn back” with a damma on the kaf.
23:67: And arrogant is a state, and the pronoun in it, the majority said: It refers to the sanctuary or the mosque or the city which is Mecca, even if it was not mentioned before because of its fame in the matter, i.e. they say we are the people of the sanctuary so we do not fear. It was said: The meaning is that they believe in themselves that they have the greatest rights over people and homes due to the mosque and the sanctuary, so they are arrogant because of that, and arrogance is not from the truth. A group said: The pronoun refers to the Qur'an from where the verses were mentioned, and the meaning is: Hearing my verses causes you arrogance and tyranny, so do not believe in it. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is a good statement. An-Nahhas: The first statement is better, and the meaning is: They boast about the sanctuary and say we are the people of the sanctuary of God Almighty. The Almighty’s saying: Samarra, you are deserted. There are four issues in it: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Samarra tahjiroon “Samarra” is in the accusative case as a state, and its meaning is talking and it is a group of people talking at night. It is taken from samar which is the shadow of the moon, and from it is samra colour and they used to talk around the Kaaba in the samra of the moon, so talking was named after it. Al-Thawri said: The shadow of the moon is called samar, and from it is samra in colour, and it is called fakht, and from it is said fakhatah. Abu Raja’ read samar which is the plural of samir, as he said: Don't you see the dark-skinned people and my condition? In the hadith of Qaylah: If her husband comes from the Samir, meaning from the people who stay up late at night, it is a singular noun with the meaning of a group, like the Hadir, which is the people who come to the water, and the Baqir is the plural of cows, and the Jamil is the plural of camels, male and female, and from this is the saying of the Almighty: Then We bring you out as children (al-Hajj 22:5), meaning children. It is said: a people of Samr, Samr, and Samir, and its meaning is staying up late at night, taken from Samr, which is what falls on the trees from the moonlight. Al-Jawhari said: the Samir is also the Samar, and they are the people who stay up late, just as the pilgrim is called Hajjaj, and the poet said: And Samer spent a long time having fun and chatting It is as if he named the place where people gather to chat. It was said: He used the word Samir, which means chatting, because it was used in the place of time, like the poet’s saying: Without them, if you come to them for a night of singing, the singing of the female singers and a gathering they will be overwhelmed with He said: Samra, because its meaning is: If you come to them at night, you will find them chatting. Sameer’s sons are: night and day, because he chats during them. It is said: I will never do it as long as Sameer’s sons chat. It is also said: Sameer is time, and he built it night and day. I will not do it as-samr and the moon, meaning as long as people chat on a moonlit night. I will not do it as-samir al-layali. Al-Shanfari said: There I do not hope for a life that pleases me, a night owl covered in crimes As-Sammar with the fat-ha means thin milk. The Arabs used to sit and chat, and this made it necessary for them to know the stars, because they would sit in the desert and see the risings from the setting. The Quraysh used to sit around the Kaaba in gatherings about their falsehoods and disbelief, so God criticized them for that. And tahjaroon is read with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the jim from ahjara, if he spoke obscenely. And with the nasb on the ta’ and a damma on the jim from hajar al-marid if he raved. Its meaning is: they speak obsessively and badly about the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and about the Quran, according to Ibn Abbas and others. Second: Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: He disliked staying up late when this verse was revealed: Staying up late at night, ignoring it, meaning that God Almighty condemned people who stay up late in disobedience to God Almighty, either in delirium or in harm’s way.
