Do you not see the saying of God, the Almighty, to His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction (al-Nahl 16:125) and His saying to Moses and Aaron: So speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear (Ta-Ha: 44). All of these are good aspects, and this is the best of them. It has been narrated that no one wrote In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful before Solomon. In the reading of Abdullah: And it is from Solomon with an additional waw. Second: The description of the Book as noble is the ultimate description. Do you not see the words of God the Almighty: Indeed, it is a noble Qur’an (al-Waqi’ah 56:77)? The people of this time describe the Book as important, beloved, and blessed. If it belongs to a king, they say: the noble, and they omit the noble out of negligence, although it is the best characteristic. As for the description of the noble, the Qur’an has been described with it in the words of God the Almighty: “And indeed, it is a noble Book. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it.” (Fussilat 41:41-42) This is its noble status, and it is not for anyone but Him. So avoid it in your books, and replace it with the lofty, in fulfillment of the right of guardianship and protection of religion. This was said by Judge Abu Bakr Ibn Al-Arabi. Third: It was the custom of the ancients, when they wrote, to start with themselves, from so-and-so to so-and-so, and this is what the narrations came with. Al-Rabi’ narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: “No one was more revered than the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and when his companions wrote, they started with themselves.” Ibn Sirin said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: When the people of Persia wrote, they started with their leaders, and a man should not start with anyone but himself. Abu Laith said in his book Al-Bustan: “If he had started with the one to whom the letter was written, it would have been permissible, because the nation had agreed upon it and did it for a benefit they saw in it, or it abrogated what was before. So, what is best in our time is to start with the one to whom the letter is written, then with himself, because starting with himself is considered belittling and arrogant towards the one to whom the letter is written, unless he is writing to one of his slaves or one of his slaves.” Fourth: If a person receives a letter with a greeting or something similar, he should respond, because a letter from someone who is absent is like a greeting from someone who is present. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he considered returning a letter obligatory, just as he considered returning a greeting. And God knows best. Fifth: They agreed to write In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful in all letters and letters, and to seal them, because that is further from suspicion. This is how the script was written, and it was narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said: Any letter that is not stamped with a fathah is unsealed. In the hadith: The most honorable letter is its seal. Some of the men of letters, Ibn al-Muqaffa’, said: Whoever writes a letter to his brother without sealing it has treated him lightly, because a seal is a seal. Anas said: “When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wanted to write to the dictionary, it was said to him: ‘They only accept a letter that has a seal on it.’ So he made a seal and engraved on its stone: ‘There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God.’ It is as if I can see its whiteness and brightness on his hand.”
27:30: Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: “Indeed, it is from Solomon, and indeed, it is: In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” And indeed, it with the kasra in both of them, meaning that the speech, or indeed, the subject of the speech, In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Al-Farra’ permitted that it is from Solomon and that it is with the fatha on both of them, on the condition that they are in the nominative case instead of the book, meaning that it was thrown to it that it is from Solomon. He permitted them to be in the accusative case with the deletion of the preposition, meaning because it is from Solomon and because it is, as if she explained his generosity by it being from Solomon and beginning it with In the name of God. Al-Ashhab Al-Uqaili and Muhammad bin Al-Sumaiqa’ read: Do not transgress with the voiced ghayn, and it was narrated from Wahb bin Munabbih, and from ghala it means to transgress and be arrogant. It goes back to the meaning of the group’s reading.
27:31: God Almighty says: And come to me in submission, meaning submissive, obedient, and faithful.
27:32: There are three issues: First: The Almighty said: She said, ‘O eminent ones, advise me in my affair.’ The eminent ones are the nobles of the people, and this has already been discussed in Surah Al-Baqarah. Ibn Abbas said: “She was with her, it was said, a thousand. It was also said: twelve thousand. It was also said: with each saying a hundred thousand. The saying is the king, less than the greatest king. So she began to practice good manners with her people, and consult them in her affair, and informed them that this was a regular practice with her in every matter that came up, by saying: “I would not decide a matter until you witness it.” So how about this major calamity? So the eminent ones addressed her in a way that would please her, by informing her of their strength and might, then they entrusted the matter to her consideration. This is a good discussion from everyone. Qatada said: We were told that she had three hundred and thirteen men who were her advisors, each man of them over ten thousand. Second: This verse provides evidence of the validity of consultation. God Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, And consult them in the matter (Al Imran 3:159) in Al Imran either to seek help from opinions or to appease the guardians. God the Almighty praised the virtuous by saying: And their affair is by consultation among them (al-Shura 42:38). Consultation is an ancient matter, especially in war. This is Bilqis, a pre-Islamic woman who used to worship al-Shams 91:“She said, ‘O eminent ones, advise me in my affair. I will not decide on a matter until you witness it.’” To test their resolve to resist their enemy, their resolve in establishing their affair, and their persistence in obeying her, with her knowledge that if they did not sacrifice their lives, wealth, and blood for her, she would not have the power to resist her enemy. And if her affair and their resolve and diligence did not come together, that would be an aid to their enemy against them. And if she did not test what they had and know the extent of their resolve, she would not have insight into their affair. Perhaps in her tyranny of opinion there was weakness in her obedience, and she was an interfering in assessing their affair. And in consulting them and taking their opinion there was an aid to what she wanted from the strength of their power and the intensity of their defense. Do you not see their saying in response: “Ta, Seen. These are the verses of the Qur’an and a clear Book.” Ibn Abbas said: One of them was so strong that he would gallop his horse until it became hot and he would close his thighs, and that was enough to make him feel strong.
27:33: Third: The Almighty said: And the matter is in your hands, so consider what you will command. They submitted the matter to her consideration despite the strength, courage and severity they had shown her. When they did that, she was informed of the actions of the kings in the villages they had conquered. In these words, there was fear for her people, caution and awe of the matter of Solomon, peace be upon him.
27:34: The Almighty's saying: "And so they do." It was said: It is from the words of Bilqis to emphasize the meaning she intended. Ibn Abbas said: It is from the words of God the Almighty, informing Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and his nation of that and informing them of it. Wahb said: When she read the book to them, she did not know the name of God, so she said: What is this? Some of the people said: We think this is nothing but a great Afreet from the jinn who uses this king to do whatever he wants, so they silenced him. Another said: I see them as three Afreet, so they silenced him, so a young man who had learned said: O mistress of kings! Solomon was a king to whom the King of Heaven had given a great kingdom, and he did not speak a word without beginning it with a name for God. God is the name of the King of Heaven, and the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful are His attributes. Then she said: Advise me on my command. They said: We are the ones with strength in fighting and with great might in war and confrontation, and the command is up to you. They referred their command to her when they had tested her opinion on the blessing, so see what you command. She said: When kings enter a city, they corrupt it and make the most honorable of its people lowly. They humiliate its nobles so that things will be right for them. So God fulfilled her words. "And thus they do." Ibn al-Anbari said: "And they made the most honorable of its people the most humble." This is a complete pause, so God Almighty said in confirmation of her statement: "And thus they do." Similar to it is in Surat al-A’raf 7:"The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, 'This is indeed a learned magician. He wants to expel you from your land.'" The speech was completed, so Pharaoh said: "Then what do you command?" Ibn Shajarah said: It is a statement by Qays, so the pause is "Thus they do, meaning, And thus Solomon does when he enters the land."
27:35: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And indeed, I am sending to them a gift. This is from her good foresight and planning, meaning that I am testing this man with a gift, meaning that I am testing this man with a gift, and I am giving him precious money, and I am sending him the wealth of the kingdom. If he is a worldly king, money will please him and we will work with him accordingly. But if he is a prophet, money will not please him and he will stick with us in matters of religion, so we should believe in him and follow his religion. So, he sent him a great gift, the details of which are more detailed than most people. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: I sent him a brick of gold, and the messengers saw the walls of gold and they thought what they had brought was small. Mujahid said: I sent him two hundred male slaves and two hundred female slaves. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “With twelve male slave girls whom she dressed as boys, and twelve female slaves whom she dressed as women, and in the hands of the slave girls were plates of musk and amber, and with twelve noble women carrying milk of gold, and with two beads, one of them not pierced and the other pierced with a crooked hole, and with a cup without anything in it, and with a staff that the kings of Himyar used to pass around, and she sent the gift with a group of her people.” It was said: The messenger was only one, but he was accompanied by followers and servants. It was also said: She sent a man from the nobles of her people called Al-Mudhir ibn Amr, and she included with him men of sound mind and intelligence, and the gift was one hundred male slave girls and one hundred female slaves, and they were distinguished in their dress. She said to the boys: When Solomon speaks to you, then speak to him with feminine language, resembling the language of women, and she said to the slave girls: Speak to him with harsh language, resembling the language of men, and it was said: The hoopoe came and informed Solomon of all of this.” It was said that God informed Solomon of that, so he ordered Solomon, peace be upon him, to pave a space of nine farsakhs from its location with bricks of gold and silver. Then he said: Which animals have you seen the most beautiful on land and sea? They said: O Prophet of God, we saw in the sea such-and-such animals with spots of different colors, with wings, manes and forelocks. So he ordered them and they came and bound the right and left of the battlefield, and the bricks of gold and silver, and they threw down their fodder for them. Then he said: To the jinn, bring your children. So he made them stand - the most handsome of youths - on the right and left of the battlefield. Then Solomon, peace be upon him, sat on his throne in his council, and four thousand golden chairs were placed for him on his right and the same on his left, and he seated the prophets and scholars on them, and he ordered the devils, the jinn, and mankind to line up in rows of leagues, and he ordered the wild beasts, the beasts, the vermin, and the birds to line up leagues on his right and left. When the people approached the field and looked at Solomon’s kingdom, and saw the beasts, the most beautiful of which their eyes had never seen, grazing on the bricks of gold and silver, their souls shriveled up to them, and they threw away the gifts they had with them. In some narrations: When Solomon ordered them to pave the field with gold and silver bricks, he ordered them to leave a place on their way the size of a carpet on the ground, not covered. When they passed by it, they feared that they would be accused of that, so they threw down what they had with them in that place. When they saw the devils, they saw a terrible, terrifying sight, so they were frightened and fled. The devils said to them: Pass on, there is no harm to you. So they passed by a group of jinn, humans, animals, birds, wild beasts, and beasts until they stopped before Solomon. Solomon looked at them with a pleasant look and a cheerful face. She had said to her messenger: “If he looks at you with an angry look, then know that he is a king, so do not be frightened by his appearance, for I am more honorable than him. If you see a man with a radiant complexion, then know that he is a prophet sent, so understand his words and respond.” So the hoopoe informed Solomon of that as mentioned above. She took a golden bag and put in it a single pearl without a hole, and a bead with a crooked hole. She wrote a letter with her messenger in which she said: If you are a prophet, distinguish between the chosen ones and the chosen ones, and inform me of what is in the bag, and show me the top of the staff from its bottom, and pierce the pearl with a straight hole, and put the bead’s thread in, and fill the cup with water from dew that is neither from the earth nor from the sky. When the messenger arrived and stood before Solomon, he gave him the queen’s letter. He looked at it and said: What is the truth? It was brought to him and he moved it, and Gabriel told him what was in it, and then Solomon told them. The messenger said to him: You have spoken the truth. So he pierced the pearl and put the thread in the bead. Solomon asked the jinn and humans about the hole in it, but they could not. So he said to the devils: What is the opinion about it? They said: It should be sent to the termite. So the termite came and took a hair in its mouth until it came out the other side. Solomon said to it: What do you need? It said: My provision will be in the tree. So he said to it: That is for you. Then Solomon said: Who will string this bead? It said: A white worm. I will string it, O Prophet of God. The worm took the string in its mouth and entered the hole until it came out the other side. Solomon said to it: What do you need? It said: You make my provision in fruits. He said: That is for you. Then he distinguished between the boys and the girls. Al-Suddi said: He ordered them to perform ablution, so the man would pour water onto his hand and foot in a gentle stream, and the girls would pour from the hand so that the left would not be on the right hand, and from the right to the left, so he distinguished between them with this. It was also said: The girl would take water from the vessel with one hand, then carry it on the other, then strike it on the face, and the boy would take water from the vessel and strike it on the face, and the girl would pour it on the inside of her forearm, and the boy on the back of his forearm, and the girl would pour water, and the boy would pour it on his hands, so he distinguished between them with this. Ya`la ibn Muslim narrated on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr who said: Bilqis sent two hundred female slaves and said: If he is a prophet, he will know the males from the females. So he ordered them to perform ablution. Whoever performed ablution, starting with his elbow before his hand, was said to be female. Whoever started with his hand before his elbow was said to be male. Then he sent the staff into the air and said: Whichever of the two heads reaches the ground first is its origin. He ordered the horses to be made to run until they sweated and the cup was filled with their sweat. Then Solomon returned the gift. It was narrated that when he sent the gift to her and her messenger told her what he had seen, she said to her al-Nas 114:This is a shot from the sky. Second: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would accept gifts and reward them, but would not accept charity. This was also the case with Solomon (peace be upon him) and all the other prophets (peace be upon them all). Bilqis made accepting or rejecting a gift a sign of what was in her heart, based on what we mentioned about Solomon being a king or a prophet, because he said to her in a letter: Do not exalt yourselves above me, but come to me in submission. No ransom is accepted for this, and no gift is taken from him. This is not from the category established in Islamic law regarding accepting gifts in any way. Rather, it is a bribe and selling what is right for what is wrong, and it is an impermissible bribe. As for an absolute gift for endearment or to show affection, it is permissible in every permissible way and in every situation, and this is as long as it is not shared. Third: If it was from a polytheist, then in the hadith it says: I was forbidden from the foam of the polytheists, meaning their support and gifts. It was narrated from him, peace be upon him, that he accepted it, as in the hadith of Malik on the authority of Thawr ibn Zayd ad-Dailami and others. A group of the ignorant said that they were abrogated, and others said that there is nothing abrogating or abrogated in them. The meaning is that he did not accept a gift from someone who hoped to prevail over him, take his country and enter Islam. This was the case of Solomon, peace be upon him. From someone like this, he was forbidden to accept his gift, implying that he should refrain from it. This is the best interpretation of the scholars in this, as it combines the hadiths. It was said that it was not a gift. Fourth: Giving gifts is recommended, and it builds affection and removes enmity. Malik narrated from Ata’ ibn Abdullah al-Khurasani that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Shake hands, and resentment will disappear. Exchange gifts, and you will love one another, and enmity will disappear.” Mu’awiyah ibn al-Hakam narrated: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: Exchange gifts, for it weakens affection and removes resentments in the heart. Ad-Daraqutni said: Ibn Bujayr is the only one who narrated it from his father from Malik, and he was not satisfied with it. It is not authentically reported from Malik or from Az-Zuhri. Ibn Shihab said: It has reached us that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Exchange gifts among yourselves, for gifts remove resentment. Ibn Wahb said: I asked Yunus about resentment, what it was, and he said: Resentment. This hadith was connected by Al-Waqqasi Uthman from Az-Zuhri, and it is weak. In short: It has been proven that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to accept gifts, and this is a good example. One of the benefits of giving a gift in accordance with the Sunnah is that it removes grudges between people and brings both the giver and the recipient a sense of respect when meeting and sitting together. It is well said by the one who said: People's kindness to each other creates a bond in their hearts. And you plant in the conscience love and affection and you gain them beauty when they attend last: Gifts are more fortunate when they come to you than a son is to a caring father. Fifth: It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Your companions are your partners in gifts. There is a difference of opinion regarding its meaning. Some said: It is to be understood in its apparent meaning. Others said: He shares with them out of generosity and chivalry, and if he does not do so, he is not forced to do so. Abu Yusuf said: This applies to fruits and the like. Some of them said: They are his partners in joy, not in gifts. This hadith applies to the likes of the people of the suffah, the khawaniq, and the ribat. However, if there are scholars who specialize in it, then his companions do not share in it. If he includes them, then that is generosity and munificence from him. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: Then she will look meaning waiting with what the messengers will return. Qatada, may God have mercy on her, said: If she was wise in her Islam and her polytheism, she would have known that guidance is accepted by people. The alif was dropped in with to differentiate between what the report. It may be permissible to keep it, he said: Why did he insult me like a pig wallowing in ashes?
27:36: God the Almighty said: "And when he came to Solomon, he said, 'Do you support me with wealth?'" Meaning, the messenger Solomon came with the gift. He said, "Do you support me with wealth?" Hamzah, Ya'qub, and Al-A'mash read it with one doubled noon and a fixed ya' after it. The rest read it with two noons, which is the preference of Abu Ubaid, because it is in all copies of the Qur'an with two noons. Ishaq narrated from Nafi' that he used to read "Atmadamudoon" with one lightened noon followed by a ya' in pronunciation. Ibn Al-Anbari said: In this reading, it is necessary to add the ya' when pausing, in order for it to conform to the spelling of the Qur'an. The original form of the doubled noon is that the doubled noon was lightened from this position, just as it was lightened from: Ash-hadu Anka Aalim, the original form of which is: Anka Aalim. And on this meaning the one who read: They argue about them, do you argue about God built, and the Arabs said: Men hit and intend, and its original form is they hit me and intend me, because it is an assimilation of they hit me and they intend me. The poet said: You are a terrifying presence, and the best of you is for Layla, Al-Hasha, Al-Bagham, and Al-Aynan. The original form is tarhabini, but it was shortened. The meaning of are you providing me with more money than what you see of my money? God the Almighty said: {So what God has given me is better than what He has given you} Is Islam, kingship, and prophethood better than what He has given you? So I should not rejoice in wealth. The word atanah appears in all copies of the Qur’an without a ya’. Abu Amr, Nafi’, and Hafs read atanah God with an open ya’, and when they pause, they delete it. As for Ya’qub, he keeps it when pausing and deletes it when connecting due to the meeting of two sukoon letters. The rest do not use a ya’ in both cases. {Rather, you rejoice in your gift} because you are people of boasting and multiplying in this world.
27:37: The Almighty says: Return to them. That is, Solomon said to Al-Mundhir bin Amr, the leader of the delegation, Return to them with their gift. "We will surely come to them with soldiers they cannot resist." The lam of the oath and the nun are inseparable. An-Nahhas said: I heard Abu Al-Hasan bin Kaysan say: It is a lam of emphasis. This is also what he believed, that all lams are three and no more: a lam of emphasis, a lam of command, and a lam of khufd. This is the opinion of the most skilled grammarians, because they return a thing to its origin, and this is only possible for someone trained in Arabic. The meaning of "they cannot resist it" is that they will have no power over it. "And We will surely expel them from it meaning from their land humiliated and debased." It was also said: "from it" meaning from the city of Saba'. The city has been mentioned previously in His statement: "Indeed, when kings enter a city, they corrupt it." Evidence They have taken away their kingdom and glory. "And they are humiliated" meaning humiliated and degraded from smallness, which is humiliation if they do not submit. So her messenger returned to her and informed her, and she said: I know that he is not a king and we do not have the strength to fight one of God's prophets. Then she ordered her throne to be placed in seven rooms, one inside the other, in the last of seven palaces. The doors were closed, guards were placed over it, and she headed towards it with twelve thousand Qil of the kings of Yemen, under each Qil a hundred thousand. Ibn Abbas said: Solomon was awe-inspiring and would not start with anything until he had this thing asked about. One day he saw a commotion close to him and said: What is this? They said: Bilqis, O Prophet of God. Solomon said to his soldiers - and Wahb and others said: To the jinn.
27:38: The Almighty said: "Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?" Abdullah ibn Shaddad said: Bilqis was a farsakh away from Solomon. He said: "Which of you will bring me her throne?" She had left her throne in Sheba and appointed guards to it. It was also said: She was sent with the gift. She sent her messengers among her army to trick Solomon into killing him before he was ready to deal with her if he was seeking Malik. When he knew that, he said: "Which of you will bring me her throne?" Ibn Abbas said: He was ordered to bring the throne before he wrote the letter to her, and he did not write to her until the throne came to him. Ibn Atiyyah said: The apparent meaning of the verses is that this statement was from Solomon after her gift came and he returned it, and he sent the hoopoe with the letter. This is the view of the majority of interpreters. They differed about the benefit of summoning her throne. Qatada said: It was mentioned to him that it was great and magnificent, so he wanted to take it before Islam protected her and her people and destroyed their wealth, and Islam is based on this religion. This is the opinion of Ibn Jurayj. Ibn Zayd said: He summoned it to show her the power that is from God, and to make it a proof of his prophethood, for he took it from her houses without an army or war, and Muslims in this interpretation do not mean surrendered, which is the opinion of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Zayd also said: He wanted to test her intelligence and for this reason he said: Disguise her throne for her, so we may see if she will be guided. It was also said: The jinn feared that Solomon, peace be upon him, would marry her and she would bear him children, and they would continue to be subjected to servitude and slavery to Solomon’s descendants. Solomon said: There was a defect in her intelligence, so he wanted to test her with her throne. Qaybil said: He wanted to test the truthfulness of the hoopoe in his statement: And for her is a mighty throne. This was said by Al-Tabari. Qatada said: He wanted to see it because of the hoopoe’s description. The first opinion is supported by most scholars, based on the Almighty’s statement: Before they come to Me in submission (al-Naml 27:38). And because if she had converted to Islam, her property would have been forbidden to him and could not be brought to him except with her permission. It was narrated that it was made of silver and gold, studded with rubies and gems, and that it was inside seven chambers with seven locks on it.
27:39: The Almighty said: An Ifrit from the jinn said This is how the majority read it. Abu Raja' and Isa Al-Thaqafi read: Ifriyya. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq may God be pleased with him. In the Hadeeth: God hates the Ifriyya Al-Nafriyya. Nafarriyya is a follow-up to Ifriyya. Qatada said: It is the cunning. An-Nahhas said: If a strong person is accompanied by malice and cunning, he is called Afar, Ifriyya, Ifriyya, Ifriyya, and Ifariyya. It was also said: Ifriyya means leader. A group read Qal Afar with a kasra on the 'ayn, as narrated by Ibn Atiyya. An-Nahhas said: Whoever says Ifriyya pluralizes it as Afar, and whoever says Ifriyya has three ways of pluralizing it. If he wishes, he says Ifriyya, and if he wishes, he says Afar, because the ta' is redundant, just as it is said: Tawagh in the plural of Taghut. If someone wishes, he replaces the ta' with a ya' and says 'Afari. The Ifriyya is one of the strong, rebellious devils. The letter taa is redundant. They said: The man became covered in dust if he caused harm to himself. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: His name is Da’wan. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he is Sakhr al-Jinn. From this name is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: Like a planet following a demon, directed in the blackness of the night Al-Kisa’i recited: When their devil, the demon, said, You have neither dominion nor stability. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “An ‘Efrit from the jinn attacked me last night, trying to interrupt my prayer. God gave me power over him, so I let him go.” And he mentioned the hadith. In Al-Bukhari, it is said: He attacked me last night instead of He kept attacking me. In Al-Muwatta’, it is narrated on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’id that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was taken on a night journey and saw an ‘Efrit from the jinn pursuing him with a torch of fire. Every time the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) turned around, he saw him. Gabriel said: Shall I not teach you some words that, if you kill them, his torch will be extinguished and he will fall into it? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Yes. He said: “I seek refuge in God, the Generous, and in the perfect words of God, which neither a pious nor a wicked person can transgress, from the evil of what descends from the sky and the evil of what ascends therein and the evil of what He has scattered on the earth and the evil of what emerges from it, and from the trials of the night and the day, and from the intruders of the night and the day, except one who knocks with good, O Most Merciful.” God the Almighty said: I will bring it to you before you rise from your seat meaning in the assembly in which he judges. And indeed, I am for this strong and trustworthy meaning strong in carrying it. Trustworthy with regard to what is in it. Ibn Abbas: Trustworthy with regard to a woman's vagina was mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. So Sulayman said: I want faster than that, so "He who had knowledge of the Scripture said: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you" Most of the commentators agree that the one who had knowledge of the Scripture was Asaf ibn Barkhiya, who was from the Children of Israel. He was a truthful person who memorized the Greatest Name of God, which if asked by it, he would give, and if called upon by it, he would respond. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: "The Greatest Name of God by which Asaf ibn Barkhiya called upon God is: O Ever-Living, O Self-Sustaining." It was said: It is in their language, and it is called Sharaahiya. Al-Zuhri said: The one who had the Greatest Name of God called upon God: O our God and the God of all things, One God, there is no god but You, bring me her throne, and it appeared before him. Mujahid said: He supplicated and said: O our God and God of all things, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Al-Suhayli said: The one who had knowledge of the Book was Asaf bin Barkhiya, the cousin of Solomon, and he had the greatest name of God among the names of God. It was also said: It was Solomon himself, but such an interpretation is not correct in the context of speech. Ibn Atiyyah said: A group said it was Solomon, peace be upon him, and the addressee in this interpretation was the genie when he said: I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, as if Solomon was impatient for that, so he said to him in a way that belittled him: I will bring it to you before you blink. Those who said this statement used as evidence the words of Solomon, This is from the bounty of my Lord. I said that what Ibn Atiyyah mentioned was said by An-Nahhas in his book, Ma’ani Al-Quran, and it is a good statement, God willing. Bahr said: He is an angel who has the Book of Destiny in his hand. God sent him when the Ifrit spoke. Al-Sahli said: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Muqri’ mentioned that it was Dubbah bin Ad, and this is not correct at all because Dubbah was the son of Ad bin Tabakha, and his name was Amr bin Elias bin Mansour Nizar bin Ma’ad. Ma’ad lived during the reign of Nebuchadnezzar, which was a long time after the reign of Solomon. So if Ma’ad was not during the reign of Solomon, then how could Dubbah bin Ad, who was five fathers after him? This is clear to anyone who contemplates it. Ibn Lahi’ah: He is Al-Khidr, peace be upon him. Ibn Zayd said: The one who had knowledge of the Book was a righteous man who was on an island in the sea. He went out that day to see who was inhabiting the land, whether he worshipped God or not. He found Solomon, so he called on one of the names of God Almighty, and the throne was brought to him. A seventh statement: He was a man from the Children of Israel named Yamlikha who knew the Greatest Name of God, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri. Qala Ibn Abi Bazza said: The man who had knowledge of the Book was named Astum, and he was a worshipper among the Children of Israel. Al-Ghaznawi mentioned him. Muhammad ibn al-Nakdar said: It is Sulayman, peace be upon him. However, people think that he had a name, but that is not the case. Rather, he was a learned man from the Children of Israel to whom God gave knowledge and understanding. He said: I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you He said: Bring it. He said: You are a prophet of God, the son of a prophet of God. If you call upon God, He will bring it to you. So God called upon Sulayman, and God brought him the throne. An eighth saying: It is Gabriel, peace be upon him. Al-Nakha’i said it, and it was narrated from Ibn Abbas. And the knowledge of the Book, according to this, is his knowledge of the revealed books of God, or what is in the Preserved Tablet. It was said: He knew the letter of Sulayman to Bilqis. Ibn Atiyyah said: The majority of people agree that he was a righteous man from the Children of Israel named Asaf ibn Barkhiya. It was narrated that he prayed two rak'ahs, then said to Solomon, O Prophet of God, extend your gaze. So he extended his gaze toward Yemen and behold, the Throne. No sooner had Solomon looked back than he found the Throne at it. Mujahid said: It means continuing to look until one blinks, defeated and miserable. It was also said that he meant the amount of time it takes to open one's eye and then blink. It is like saying, Do such-and-such in the blink of an eye. This is more likely because if the ifrit was from Solomon, then it is a miracle. But if it was from Asaf or another of God's saints, then it is a miracle, and the miracle of a saint is a miracle of the Prophet. Al-Qushayri said: The miracles of the saints were denied by those who said that the one who had knowledge of the Book was Solomon. He said to the ifrit, I will bring it to you before you blink. According to these people, what the ifrit did is neither a miracle nor a miracle, because the jinn are capable of such things. A substance does not separate two places in one state. Rather, it is conceived of as God annihilating the substance in the far east, then returning it in the second state, which is the state after nonexistence, God the substance in the far east, then returning it in the second state, which is the state after nonexistence in the far west. Or He annihilates the intermediate places, then returning them. Al-Qushayri said: Wahb narrated it from Malik. It has also been said: Rather, it was brought in the air, said Mujahid. And it was between Solomon and the throne as between Kufa and Al-Hirah. Malik said: It was on the right, and Solomon, peace be upon him, was in Ash-Sham. In the commentaries: The throne of Bilqis was pierced from the place it was in, then it sprang forth before Solomon. Abdullah ibn Shaddad said: And the throne appeared from a tunnel under the earth, and God knows best which of them it was.
27:40: The Almighty says: And when he saw it settled near him, meaning, firmly established with him. He said, ‘This is from the bounty of my Lord,’ meaning, this victory and empowerment are from the bounty of my Lord. That He may test me, Al-Ahfash said, means to see whether I will be grateful or ungrateful. Another said: The meaning of That He may test me is to worship Me, and it is a metaphor. The original meaning of to test is to test me, meaning, to test me whether I will be grateful for His blessings or ungrateful for them. And whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself, meaning, the benefit of that returns to himself, since he deserves, through his sharing, the completion of the blessing, its continuity, and more of it. Gratitude is the condition for an existing blessing, and through it a lost blessing is attained. And whoever is ungrateful—then indeed, my Lord is Free of need, meaning, from gratitude, Generous in bounty.
27:41: God the Almighty says: "He said, 'Disguise her throne for her,' meaning, change it. It was said: He made its top its bottom, and its bottom its top. It was also said: He changed it by adding or subtracting. Al-Farra' said: He ordered it to be disguised because Satan told him: There is something wrong with her mind, so he wanted to test her. It was also said: The jinn feared that Solomon would take her as provisions and have children from her, thus they would remain subservient to the family of Solomon forever. So they said to Solomon: She is weak of mind, and her legs are like those of a donkey. So he said: "Disguise her throne for her," so that we may know her mind. A soothsayer from the jinn was a sincere advisor to Solomon, and he said: How can I see her feet without asking her to uncover them? He said: I will put water in this palace, and I will put glass over the water, so she will think it is water, so she will lift her garment and see her feet. This is the palace that God the Almighty spoke about.
27:42: God the Almighty said: So when she came meaning Bilqis, it was said to her, “Is this your throne? She said, It is as if it were the same. She likened it to the same because she had left it locked, so she neither acknowledged nor denied it. So Solomon knew the perfection of her mind. Ikrimah said: She was wise and said, It is as if it were the same. Muqatil said: She recognized it, but she made it seem like it was to them as they made it seem like it to her. If she had been told, Is this your throne, she would have said, Yes, it is. Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl also said the same. It was said: Shlyman wanted to show her that the jinn were subservient to him, as were the devils, so that she would know that she was a prophet and believe in him. This was said in response to her concealing the matter in the chapter on boys and slave girls. And we were given knowledge before her It was said: This is from the words of Bilqis, meaning we were given knowledge of the truth of Solomon’s prophethood before this verse about the throne. And we were Muslims obedient to his command. It was said: It is from the words of Solomon, meaning we were given knowledge of God's ability to do whatever He wills before this time. It was also said: And we were given knowledge of her conversion to Islam and her coming willingly before her arrival. It was also said: It is from the words of Solomon's people. And God knows best.
27:43: The Almighty said: And what she used to worship besides God prevented her. Stopping at besides God is good, and the meaning is: What she used to worship of the sun and the moon was prevented from worshipping God, so ma is in the nominative case. An-Nahhas said: The meaning is, her worship of other than God and her worship of it prevented her from learning what We taught her, from submitting. It is permissible for ma to be in the accusative case, and the interpretation would be: And Solomon prevented her from what she used to worship besides God, meaning He stood between her and him. It is permissible for the meaning to be: And God prevented her from worshipping other than God, so an was deleted and the verb was transitive. Similar to it is: And Moses chose his people (al-A’raf 7:155) meaning from his people. Sibawayh recited: I informed Abdullah that I had found a noble woman whose masters were mean at heart. He claimed that the meaning, according to him, is that she was informed about Abdullah. Indeed, she was from a disbelieving people. Saeed bin Jubair read: that she with a fat-ha on the hamza, and it is in the accusative case meaning because it is. It is possible for it to be a substitute for what, in which case it would be in the nominative case if what was the agent of the repelling. The kasra is for resumption.
27:44: The Almighty said: It was said to her, ‘Enter the palace.’ The interpretation according to Sibawayh is: Enter the palace, so the verb to was omitted. Abu al-Abbas makes a mistake in this, saying: Because entered indicates something entered. The palace was a plate of glass with water underneath it and fish in it. He made it to show her a king, You have been greatly exalted by its kingship, said Mujahid. Mujahid said: There was water from the bottles behind it I thought it was a pool, meaning water. It was said: The palace is the palace, according to Abu Ubaidah. As he said: Their flags are considered monuments It was said: The palace is the courtyard, just as it is said: This is the palace of the house and its hall, with one meaning. Abu Ubaidah narrated in Al-Gharib Al-Musannaf that the palace is every tall building raised from the ground, and that the tall, smooth. An-Nahhas: The origin of this is that every builder who does one work is called a palace, from their saying: clear milk if it does not resemble water and from their saying: he stated the matter, and from it: clear Arab. It was said: He made it to test what the jinn would say about her that her mother was a jinn and her husband was a donkey, said Wahb ibn Munabbih. When she saw the abyss, she was startled and thought that he intended to drown her. She was amazed at the smoothness of his chair on the water, and she saw what startled her, and she had no choice but to obey the order. And she uncovered her legs, and behold, they were the most beautiful legs of people, free from what she had said to the jinn, except that she had much hair. When she reached this height, Solomon said to her after turning his gaze away from her: Indeed, it is a palace smoothed of glass. The smooth is not polished, and from it comes the word al-Murad. A man rebelled when his beard was slow to grow after reaching puberty, Al-Farra’ said. And from this comes the word marda’a a tree with no leaves on it. And marda’a a sandy area if it does not grow. And marda’ is also the elongated one, and from it the fortress was called marda’a a strong one. Abu Salih: tall in the shape of a palm tree. And Ibn Shajarah: wide in length and width. He said: I went early in the morning and found them before noon in the desert. Any wide shields. At that point, Bilqis surrendered, submitted, became a Muslim, and admitted to being wronged, as will be mentioned. When Solomon, peace be upon him, saw her feet, he said to his devilish advisor: How can I remove this hair without harming my body? So he directed him to use hair removal cream, and from that day on, hair removal cream and baths became popular. It is narrated that Solomon married her at that time and settled her in Syria, as stated by Ad-Dahhak. Saeed bin Abdul Aziz said in Al-Naqqash: He married her and returned her to her kingdom by right hand, and he used to come to her once a month in the wind, and she gave birth to a boy whom he named Dawud, who died during his time. In some reports, the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Bilqis had the most beautiful legs of all women in the world, and she is one of the wives of Solomon, peace be upon him, in Paradise.” Aisha said: Does she have better legs than me? So he, peace be upon him, said: You will have better legs than her in Paradise. Al-Qushayri mentioned this. Al-Tha’labi reported on the authority of Abu Musa that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first person to have baths was Solomon, son of David. When he pressed his back against the wall and its heat touched him, he said, ‘Oh, the punishment of God!’ Then he loved it intensely and confirmed its ownership by right. He ordered the jinn to build three fortresses for it, the likes of which people had never seen: Salhun, Baynun, and Umdan. Then Solomon would visit it once a month and stay there for three days. Al-Sha’bi narrated that some people from Himyar dug up the cemetery of the kings and found in it a vaulted grave in which was a woman wearing garments woven with gold, and at her head was a marble tablet on which was written: O people, turn together and lie in the graves of Jesus. So that you may know that I am the one who was called the time of Bilqis The king's palace was built in Himyar, and it was familiar to my people. I was in my kingdom and his management, forcing the sneezers for God’s sake My husband, Solomon the Prophet, who was a teacher of the Torah And He subjected to him the wind as a ship, sometimes blowing like a stork. With the son of David, the Prophet, whom the Most Merciful sanctified with sanctification Muhammad ibn Ishaq and Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Solomon did not marry her, but he said to her: Choose a husband, so she said: Someone like me does not marry while I had such a kingdom. So he said: That is inevitable in Islam. So she chose Dhu Tabi’a, king of Hamdan, so he married her to him and returned her to Yemen, and ordered Zuba’a, the prince of the jinn of Yemen, to obey him, so he built factories for him, and he remained the prince until Solomon died. Some people said: There is no authentic report about him, neither that he married her nor that he married her. She is Bilqis bint al-Sarh ibn al-Hadahid ibn Sharahil ibn Adad ibn Hadr ibn al-Sarh ibn al-Haras ibn Qays ibn Saifi ibn Saba’ ibn Yashjub ibn Ya’rub ibn Qahtan ibn Aber ibn Shalih ibn Arfakhshad ibn Sam ibn Noah. And her limit, Al-Hadad, was a great king who had forty sons, all of whom were kings. He was the king of the whole land of Yemen. Her father, Al-Sarh, used to say to the kings of Al-Adraf, “None of you is equal to me,” and he refused to marry any of them. So they married him to a woman from the jinn called Rayhana bint Al-Sakn, and she bore him Balqama, who is also Bilqis. He had no other sons. Abu Hurairah said that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said, One of Bilqis’s parents was a jinn. Then her father died, and her people divided over her into two groups. They appointed a man as their ruler, but his conduct was bad, and he committed adultery with the women of his subjects. Bilqis became jealous and offered herself to him, so he married her. She made him drink wine until she cut off his head, and she placed him at the door of her house, and they made her their king. Abu Bakra said: Bilqis was mentioned to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he said: A people who entrust their affairs to a woman will never prosper. It is said that the reason her father married a jinn was that he was a minister to a tyrannical king who used to rape the women of his subjects. The minister was jealous and did not marry. Once, on the road, he accompanied a man whom he did not like. He said: Do you have a wife? He said: I will never marry, for the king of our country rapes women from their husbands. The Prophet said: If you marry my daughter, he will never rape her. The Prophet said: He will rape her. He said: We are a people of jinn who cannot be controlled. So he married his daughter and she bore him Bilqis. Then her mother died and Bilqis built a palace in the desert. Her father spoke of her story incorrectly, and report of her reached the king, so he said: So-and-so, you have this beautiful girl with you and you will not bring her to me, even though you know my love for women! Then he ordered him to be imprisoned, so Bilqis sent to him, I am in your hands, so he got ready to go to her palace. When he was about to enter with those with him, the female slaves from the daughters of the jinn, like the image of the sun, came out to him and said to him, Are you not ashamed?! Our lady says to you, are you bringing these men with you to your family? So he gave them permission to leave and he entered and… So she locked the door behind him, killed him with sandals, cut off his head and threw it to his army, and they ordered her to rule over them. She remained like that until the hoopoe heard about her to Solomon, peace be upon him. When Solomon had alighted at one of his dwellings, the hoopoe said: “Solomon is busy with his descent. So he ascended towards the sky and saw the length and breadth of the world. He saw the world to the right and to the left and saw a garden belonging to Bilqis in which there was a hoopoe. The name of that hoopoe was ‘Afeer. So ‘Afeer al-Yaman said to ‘Afeer al-Yaman, ‘From where have you come? And where are you going?’ He said: “I have come from Syria with my companion Solomon. From where have you come?” He said: “The kingdom of the jinn, mankind, devils, birds, beasts, wind and everything between the sky and the earth. So where are you from?” He said: From this country, its king is a woman called Bilqis. Her hands were made of twelve thousand camels, under the hand of each camel were one hundred thousand fighters, besides women and children. So he set out with him and looked at Bilqis and her king, and returned to Solomon at the time of the afternoon prayer. Solomon had missed him at the time of prayer and could not find him, and they were without water. Ibn Abbas said in a narration: A breeze from the sun fell on him. So he said to the minister of birds: Whose place is this? He said: O Prophet of God, this is the place of the hoopoe. He said: Where did it go? He said: I do not know, may God guide the kingdom. Solomon became angry and said: I will surely punish him with a severe punishment [the verse]. Then he called for the eagle, the master of birds, the most ferocious and fiercest of them, and said: What do you want, O Prophet of God? He said: Bring the hoopoe right away. So the eagle raised itself up from the sky until it clung to the air. It looked at the world like a bowl in front of one of you, and suddenly it saw the hoopoe coming from the right. It pounced on it and dug its claws into it. Then the hoopoe said to him, I ask you by God, who has given you power and your words over me, to have mercy on me. So he said to him, Woe to you, and may my hope be bereaved of you! God's prophet Solomon swore that he would torture you or slaughter you. Then he brought him and the vultures and all the birds' armies met him. They said, Woe to you! God's prophet threatened you, but said, 'What is my power and what am I? Didn't he make an exception?' They said, Yes! He said, 'Or let him bring me clear authority.'" Then he entered upon Salman, who raised his head and lowered his tail and wings in humility to Solomon, peace be upon him. Solomon said to him, "Where were you in your service and your place? I will surely torture you severely or slaughter you. The hoopoe said to him, O Prophet of God! Remember that you stand before God as I stand before you." Solomon's skin shuddered and trembled, and he forgave him. Akrima said: God prevented Solomon from slaughtering the hoopoe because it was dutiful to its parents, bringing food to them and giving them water. Then Solomon said to it: What took you so long? The hoopoe replied: God has told us about Bilqis, her throne, and her people, as previously explained. Al-Mawardi said: The claim that Bilqis’s mother was a jinn is absurd to the mind due to the difference between the sexes, the difference in natures, and the separation of the two bodies, because the human being is physical and the jinn are spiritual. God created the human being from clay like pottery, and created the jinn from a smokeless flame of fire. This difference prevents mixing, and reproduction is impossible with this difference. I said: The statement has been made, and reason does not reject it with what has been reported in this regard. If we look at the origin of creation, then its origin is water, as was previously explained, and there is nothing further to that, and God knows best. And in the revelation: And share with them in wealth and children (al-Isra’ 17:64), as was previously mentioned. And God Almighty said: No man or jinn had touched them before them (Al-Rahman: 56), as will come in Al-Rahman. God the Almighty said: She said, ‘My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself’ meaning, by the polytheism she was upon. This was stated by Ibn Shajarah. Sufyan said: “That is, by the suspicion she had imagined about Solomon, because when she was commanded to enter the palace, she thought it was a sea, and that Solomon wanted to drown her in it. But when it became clear to her that it was a palace of smooth glass, she knew that she had wronged herself by that suspicion.” In was broken because it is a subject after qall. Some Arabs open it and thus qall is applied to it. And I submitted with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds If ma’ is silent, then it is a particle that has a meaning, with no difference between grammarians. If it is opened, then there are two opinions about it: One of them is that it has the meaning of a circumstance as a noun. The other is that it is a preposition built on the fat-ha, as stated by an-Nahhas.
27:45: The Almighty’s saying: And We had certainly sent to Thamud their brother Salih, [saying], ‘Worship God.’ The meaning of it was presented earlier: And at once they were two disputing parties. Mujahid said: That is, a believer and a disbeliever. He said: The dispute is what God the Almighty related in His saying: Do you know that Salih was sent by his Lord? (al-A’raf 7:75) until His saying: disbelievers. It was said: Their dispute was that each party said: We are on the truth and you are not.
27:46: God the Almighty said: He said, ‘O my people, why do you hasten the evil before the good?’ Mujahid said: The punishment before mercy. The meaning is: Why do you delay the faith that brings you reward, and bring forward the disbelief that necessitates the punishment? The disbelievers would say, out of extreme denial: Bring us the punishment. It was also said: That is, why did you do something that would merit the punishment? Not that they sought to hasten the punishment. Why do you not ask forgiveness of God? That is, why do you not repent to God from polytheism? Perhaps you will receive mercy? So that you may receive mercy, and this has already been mentioned.
27:47: The Almighty said: They said, ‘We consider you and those with you to be ill-omened.’ That is, we consider you to be ill-omened. And ill omen is misfortune. Nothing is more harmful to one’s opinion or more corrupting to one’s mind than believing in bad omens. Whoever thinks that the lowing of a cow or the cawing of a crow can reverse fate or avert destiny has spoken out. The poet said: The bird of fate does not change fate, so excuse time and do not blame it. Any day is special to Saud, and fates descend every day It is not an owl, and in it there is good fortune and bad luck, which flow from one people to another. Arabs were the majority of people, and when they wanted to travel, they would scare away a bird. If it flew to the right, they would move on and be auspicious, but if it flew to the left, they would go back and be unlucky. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade that and said, Leave the birds alone and their nests alone, as explained previously in Al-Ma’idah. Your bird is with God, meaning your misfortunes. Rather, you are a people being tested, meaning you are being tried. It was also said, You are being punished for your sins.
27:48: The Almighty said: "And there were in the city meaning in the city of Salih, which is Al-Hijr nine men" meaning nine men from the sons of the most noble of them. Ad-Dahhak said: These nine were the notables of the people of the city, and they used to spread corruption in the land and order corruption, so they sat by a huge rock and God accepted it from them. Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: I was informed that they used to lend dinars and dirhams, and that was part of the corruption in the land. Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab also said the same. It was also said: Their corruption was that they used to pursue people's faults and not cover them up. It was also said something else. What is necessary from the verse is what Ad-Dahhak and others said, that they were the most prominent, most capable, and most wealthy of the people, and they were people of great disbelief and sin, and the gist of their matter was that they used to spread corruption and not reform. A group is the name for a group, so it is as if they were leaders, each of whom had a group following him. The plural is "arhat and arahit". He said: Woe to the war that brought about the loss of a group of people and they were relieved. These people mentioned were the owners of the barren camel, as mentioned by Ibn Atiyah. I said: There is a difference of opinion regarding their names. Al-Ghaznawi said: Their names are Qadar bin Salaf, Musaddaa, Aslam, Dasma, Dhuhaim, Dhima, Dhaim, Qatal, and Sadaq. Ibn Ishaq: Their leader is Qadar bin Salaf and Musaddaa bin Mihri, then seven followed them, they are Bala bin Mila, Duair bin Ghanim, Dhu’ab bin Mihraj, and four whose names are not known. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned their names on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih: Al-Hudhayl bin Abd Rabb, Ghanim bin Ghanim, Riyab bin Mihraj, Musaddaa bin Mihraj, Umair bin Kurdiyya, Asim bin Makhrama, Sabit bin Sadaqah, Sam’an bin Safi, Qadar bin Salaf, and they are the ones who tried to hamstring the she-camel, and they were the most stubborn of the people of Salih, and they were from the sons of their nobles. Al-Sahli: Al-Naqqash mentioned the nine who were corrupting the land and not reforming it, and he called them by their names. This is not controlled by any narration, but I am mentioning it based on my own effort and guesswork. However, we will mention it based on what we found in the book of Muhammad ibn Habib, and they are: Musad’ ibn Dahr. It is also said Dahm, Qadar ibn Salaf, Harim, Sawab, Riyab, Dab, Dam’a, and Du’ayn ibn Umair. I said: Al-Mawardi mentioned their names on the authority of Ibn Abbas, saying: They are Dam’a, Da’im, Haram, Harim, Dab, Sawab, Riyab, Mastah, and Qadar, and they were in the land of Al-Hijr, which is the land of Ash-Sham.
27:49: The Almighty’s saying: They said, ‘We will surely spend the night with him and his family.’ It is possible that they divided is a future tense verb and it is a command, meaning some of them said to each other, swear. It is also possible that it is past tense in the sense of a state, as if he said: They said, dividing by God. The evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Abdullah: They cause corruption in the land and do not reform. They rebelled against God, and there is no they said in it. We will surely spend the night with him and his family, then we will say to his heir. The reading of the general public is with a noon in both of them, and Abu Hatim chose this. Hamzah and Al-Kisa’i read it with a ta’ in both of them, and added a damma to the ta’ and lam to indicate that they addressed each other in this, and Abu Ubaid chose this. Mujahid and Hamid read it with a ya’ in both of them, and added a damma to the ya’ and lam to indicate the report. Surprising the enemy at night. The meaning of his heir is the people of Salih who have the right to shed blood. We did not witness the destruction of his family means we were not present, and we do not know who killed him or his family. And indeed, we are truthful in our denial of his killing. Muhalik means destruction, but it could also be the place. Asim and As-Sulami read it with a fatha on the meem and the lam, meaning destruction. It is said: He struck yadrubu meaning a strike. Al-Mufaddal and Abu Bakr read it with a fatha on the meem and a genitive on the lam, so it is a noun of place like majlis council for a place to sit in. It could also be a verbal noun, like the Almighty’s saying: To Him is your return (Yunus 10:4), meaning your return.
27:50: God the Almighty said: And they planned a plan, and We planned a plan, while they perceived not. Their plan was what was narrated that these nine, when it was the first of three days after the she-camel was hamstrung, and Salih had informed them of the coming punishment, they agreed and formed an alliance to come to Salih's house at night and kill him and his family who were specifically related to him. They said: If he was lying in his threat and we inflicted on him what he deserved, but if he was telling the truth, we would have hastened him before us and cured ourselves. Mujahid and others said the same. Ibn Abbas said: God the Almighty sent the angels that night, and the house of Salih was filled with them. The nine came to Salih's house brandishing their swords, and the angels killed them by throwing stones at them, and they did not see who was throwing them. Qatada said: They went out quickly to Salih, and he sent an angel with a rock in his hand and killed them. Al-Suddi said: They descended onto a cliff of land, and it collapsed with them, and God destroyed them beneath it. It was said that they hid in a cave near the house of Salih, and then a rock fell on them, crushing them all. This was their plan, and God planned to punish them for that.
27:51: The Almighty said: "Then see how was the outcome of their plot. Indeed, We destroyed them and their people, all together." That is, by the blast that destroyed them. It has been said that the destruction of all of them was by the blast of Gabriel. However, it appears more apparent that the nine were destroyed by a single punishment, then the rest were destroyed by the blast and the rumbling. Al-A'mash, Al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Asim, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i used to read it as ana with the fat-ha. Ibn Al-Anbari said: According to this school of thought, it is not appropriate to pause at the outcome of their plot because ana dammarnahum is the predicate of kan. So it is permissible to put it in the nominative case, following the outcome. It is also permissible to put it in the accusative case, according to Al-Farra', and in the genitive case, according to Al-Kisa'i, meaning: because We destroyed them and because We destroyed them. It is permissible to put it in the accusative case, following the case of kayfa. According to these schools of thought, it is not appropriate to stop at makrahum. Ibn Kathir, Nafi` and Abu `Amr read: Inna damasurnahum with a kasra on the alif as a new sentence. According to this school of thought, it is appropriate to stop at makrahum. An-Nahhas said: It is permissible to put `aqibah in the accusative case as the predicate of kana and for inna to be in the nominative case as the subject of kana. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case with an implied subject to clarify the consequence, and the estimate is: It is: We destroyed them. Abu Hatim said: In the letter of Abu, that we destroyed them is confirmation of its opening.
27:52: The Almighty’s saying: Those are their houses, desolate because of what they did. The general reading is in the accusative case as a state according to Al-Farra’ and An-Nahhas, meaning empty of its inhabitants, in ruins with no inhabitants in it. Al-Kisa’i and Abu Ubaidah said: “(... “Indeed in that is a sign for a people who know. And We saved those who believed” in Salih.
27:53: The Almighty said: And they feared God and were wary of His punishment. It was said that four thousand men believed in Salih. The rest left with their bodies - according to Muqatil and others - a wound like chickpeas. It was red on the first day, then yellow the next day, then black on the third. The she-camel was hamstrung on Wednesday and they died on Sunday. Muqatil said: Those wounds burst, and Gabriel shouted at them during that time and they calmed down. That was in the forenoon. Salih and those who believed with him left for Hadhramaut. When he entered it, Salih died, and it was named Hadhramaut. Ad-Dahhak said: Then the four thousand built a city called Hadhura, as was explained previously in the story of the people of the message.
27:54: God Almighty says: And Lot, when he said to his people meaning, and We sent Lot, or mention Lot when he said to his people and they were the people of their ancestors. And he said to his al-Nas 114:Do you commit immorality the ugly, heinous act while you see that it is immorality, and that is greater than your sins. And it was said: Some of you come to one another while you are looking at it. And they did not conceal their transgression and rebellion.
27:55: The Almighty said: Do you indeed approach men with desire instead of women? He mentioned it again because of its extreme ugliness and heinousness. Rather, you are a people who are ignorant of either the prohibition or the punishment. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh chose to lighten the second hamza in a'annakum. As for writing, the way to write it is to write it with two alifs in all the ways, because it is an introductory hamza with the alif of interrogation added to it.
27:56: God the Almighty says: “But the answer of his people was only that they said, ‘Expel the family of Lot from your city. Indeed, they are people who purify themselves.’” That is, from the backsides of men. They said that to mock them, as Mujahid said. Qatada said: By God, they criticized them for no fault, because they purified themselves from evil deeds.
27:57: God Almighty said: “So We saved him and his family, except for his wife. We predestined her to be among those who remained behind.” Asim read: We predestined in a lightened form, but the meaning is the same. It is said that you have predestined something with a predestined meaning, and you have predestined it.
27:58: The Almighty says: “And We rained down upon them a rain. Evil was the rain of those who were warned.” That is, those who were warned but did not accept the warning. This has been explained previously in Al-A’raf and Hud.
27:59: The Almighty says: "Say, 'Praise be to God, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen.'" Al-Farra' said: The scholars of semantics said: It was said to Lot, Say, 'Praise be to God,' for their destruction. A group of scholars disagreed with Al-Farra' on this and said: It is addressed to our Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, meaning, Say, 'Praise be to God,' for the destruction of the disbelievers of the past nations. An-Nahhas said: This is more appropriate because the Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and everything in it is addressed to him, peace be upon him, except for that which its meaning is only valid for others. It was also said that the meaning, i.e., "Say, 'O Muhammad, praise be to God, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen,'" means his nation, peace be upon them. Al-Kalbi said: God chose them through His knowledge and obedience. Ibn Abbas and Sufyan said: They are the companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. It was also said that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was commanded to recite these verses that speak of proof, emphasizing His Oneness, His power over all things, and His wisdom, and to begin by praising Him. Peace be upon His prophets and the chosen ones of His servants. It contains good teachings, admonitions on beautiful etiquette, and encourages seeking good luck and blessings from the two remembrances, and making sure that their status allows one to accept what is conveyed to the listeners, listen to it, and place it in their hearts in the position the listener desires. Scholars, orators, and preachers have inherited this etiquette from generation to generation. They praised God and sent blessings upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before every beneficial knowledge, before every sermon, and at the beginning of every sermon. The messengers followed them and wrote the beginnings of their letters to him about conquests, congratulations, and other important events. God the Almighty said: Those whom He has chosen He chose, that is, He asked him, and they are the prophets, peace be upon them, and the evidence for that is the Almighty’s saying: “And peace be upon the messengers” (Al-Salafat: 181). Is God better? Abu Hatim permitted Is God better with two hamzas. An-Nahhas: We do not know of anyone who followed him in that, because this extension was brought to differentiate between the question and the report, and this is the alif of stopping, and better here does not mean better than you, but rather it is like the saying of the poet: I insult him, but he is not his equal. May God sacrifice for your sake. The meaning is: the one of you who is evil will be ransomed for the one who is good. It is not permissible for it to have the meaning of from because if you say: So-and-so is worse than so-and-so, then there is evil in each of them. It was also said that the meaning is: Is the good in this one or in the one you associate with him in worship? Sibawayh said: Is happiness more beloved to you or misery? And he knew that happiness was more beloved to him. It was also said that it is in its form of comparative, and the meaning is: God is better or what you thank, and which of His rewards is better or the punishment of what you associate with Him? It was also said that He said that to them because they believed that there was good in worshipping idols, so God Almighty addressed them based on their belief. It was also said that the wording is interrogative and its meaning is report. Abu Amr, Asim, and Ya’qub read: they associate with a ya as report. The rest read it as address, and this is the preferred choice of Abu Ubaid Abu Hatim. So when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would recite this [verse], he would say: Rather, God is better, more lasting, more majestic, and more generous.
27:60: The Almighty says: From Him who created the heavens and the earth. Abu Hatim said: Its meaning is, are your gods better or He who created the heavens and the earth? This has been mentioned before. Its meaning is: He had power over their creation. It was also said that the meaning is, is the worship of your idols better or the worship of He who created the heavens and the earth? So it is a rebuttal to the meaning that preceded it, and it contains the meaning of rebuke to them, and drawing attention to the power of God the Almighty and the inability of their gods. Then We caused to grow thereby gardens of delight. A garden is a garden that has a wall around it. Delight is a beautiful sight. Al-Farra' said: A modern garden is a walled garden. If there is no wall around it, then it is a garden and not a garden. Qatada and Ikrimah said: Gardens are palm trees of delight, and delight is adornment and beauty, which delights whoever sees it. It was not for you to make its trees grow. Ma is for negation and means prohibition and prevention from doing this, meaning it was not for humans and is not possible for them, and it is not within their ability, to make its trees grow, as they are incapable of doing something like it, because that is bringing something out of nothingness into existence. I say: This may be used as evidence to prohibit the depiction of anything, whether it has a soul or not. This is the opinion of Mujahid. This is supported by the words of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): God the Almighty said, 'And who is more unjust than he who tries to create a creation like My creation? Let them create an atom or a grain or a barley groat.' Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said, "I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say, 'God the Almighty said,' and he mentioned it. Thus, he included in the blame, threat, and denunciation everyone who depicts something that God created or imitates Him in resembling His creation in what He alone, glory be to Him, has created and invented. This is clear. The majority are of the view that depicting something that does not have a soul is permissible, as is earning from it. Ibn Abbas said to the one who asked him to make images: If you must do it, then make trees and things that have no soul. This was also narrated by Muslim. Forbidding is better, and God knows best, for what we have mentioned. This will be further explained in Saba’, God willing. Then he said, by way of rebuke: Is there a god with God? That is, is there a god with God who can help him in that? Rather, they are a people who equate someone with God. It was said: They deviate from the truth and the intention, that is, they disbelieve. It was said: A god is raised by with, meaning: Is there a god with God? Woe to you. Stopping at with God is good.
27:61: The Almighty said: Is He who has made the earth a resting place? meaning a stable place. And placed rivers in its midst, meaning in its center, like: And We caused a river to gush forth within them (al-Kahf 18:33). And placed for it firm mountains, meaning mountains that hold it together and prevent it from moving. And placed between the two seas a barrier, preventing the bitter waters from being mixed with torment. Ibn Abbas said: A power from His power, so this does not change that, and that does not change this, and a barrier means prevention. Is there a god with God? meaning, since it is proven that no one else has power over this, then why do they worship that which neither harms nor benefits? Rather, most of them do not know, meaning, it is as if they are ignorant of God, so they do not know what is due to Him in terms of Oneness.
27:62: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him? Ibn Abbas said: He is the one in dire need. Al-Suddi said: He who has neither power nor strength. Dhun-Nun said: He is the one who has severed ties with anyone but God. Abu Ja`far and Abu `Uthman Al-Naysaburi said: He is the bankrupt. Sahl ibn `Abdullah said: He is the one who, when he raises his hands to God supplicating, has no means of performing any act of obedience before Him. A man came to Malik ibn Dinar and said: I ask you by God to supplicate for me, for I am in need. He said: Then ask Him, for He responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him. The poet said: I call upon God while the situation is difficult for me, but He keeps on giving me relief. Many a brother has a bad face and finds a way out for himself when he calls upon God. Second: In Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi, on the authority of Abu Bakra, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the supplication of the distressed: “O God, I hope for Your mercy, so do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye, and set right all my affairs. There is no god but You.” Third: God the Almighty has guaranteed that He will answer the one in need if he calls upon Him. He has informed us of this about Himself. The reason for that is that the necessity of resorting to Him arises from sincerity and cutting the heart off from everything else. Sincerity has a place and a pledge with Him, glory be to Him, whether it is found with a believer or a disbeliever, obedient or wicked, as God the Almighty says: “Until, when you are in the ships and they sail with them by a good wind and they rejoice in it, there comes a stormy wind and the waves come upon them from every side and they think that they are surrounded, they supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion, ‘If You should save us from this, we will surely be among the grateful.’” (Yunus 10:22) And His statement: But when He has delivered them to the land, at once they associate others with Him. (al-Ankabut 29:65) So He answered them when they were in need and had sincerely believed, even though He knew that they would return to their polytheism and disbelief. God the Almighty says: And when they embark on a ship, they supplicate God, sincere to Him in religion. (al-Ankabut 29:65) So He answers the one in need when he is in need and sincere. In the hadith: “Three supplications are answered without a doubt: the supplication of the oppressed, the supplication of the traveler, and the supplication of a parent for his child.” This was mentioned by the author of Ash-Shihab, and it is a hadith. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said to Muadh when he sent him to the land of Yemen: And fear the supplication of the oppressed, for there is no veil between them and God. In the book of Ash-Shihab: Beware the supplication of the oppressed, for it is carried by the clouds, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, says, By My Glory and Majesty, I will surely aid you, even if it is after a while. This is also authentic. Al-Ajurri narrated from the hadith of Abu Dharr from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: I will not reject it, even if it comes from the mouth of an unbeliever. So the oppressed person is answered in accordance with his sincerity and necessity, as required by His generosity, and in response to his sincerity, even if he is an unbeliever. Likewise, if he is wicked in his religion, then the wickedness of the wicked and the unbelief of the unbeliever do not diminish or weaken the sovereignty of their Master, so what He has decreed for the one in need does not prevent Him from answering him. He explained that answering the supplication of the oppressed with victory over his oppressor is as He wills, whether by subduing him, taking revenge on him, or empowering another oppressor over him to subdue him, as He, the Almighty, said: And thus do We let some wrongdoers have power over others (al-An’am 6:129). He emphasized the speed of answering it by saying: carried on clouds. And its meaning, and God knows best, is that God, the Almighty, entrusts His angels with receiving the supplication of the oppressed and carrying it on clouds, so they ascend with it to the heavens, and the heavens are the direction of supplication so that all the angels can see it. This shows the assistance of the oppressed and their intercession for him to have his supplication answered, out of mercy for him.
