In this there is a warning against injustice in general, because it incurs God’s wrath, disobedience to Him, and opposition to His command, as He said on the tongue of His Prophet in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere: O My servants, I have forbidden it to Myself and made it forbidden amongst you, so do not wrong one another. [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] The oppressed person is in need, and the traveler is close to him, because he is cut off from his family and homeland, isolated from his friend and intimate, and his heart does not find comfort in anyone who can help or support him because of his alienation. So his need is sincere towards the Master, so he turns to Him for refuge, and He is the One who answers the one in need when he calls upon Him. Likewise, the supplication of the father against his son does not come from him, despite what he knows of his compassion and mercy for him, except when his inability to do so is complete, his need is sincere, and he has despaired of being dutiful to his father, despite the presence of his harm. So the Truth hastens to answer him. God the Almighty says: {And removes evil} meaning harm. Al-Kalbi said: Injustice. {And makes you successors to the earth} meaning its place. He destroys some people and creates others. In the book of Al-Naqqash: {That is, He makes your children successors to you}. Al-Kalbi said: A succession of disbelievers who will settle in their land, and obey God after their disbelief. {Is there a god with God?} is a rebuke, as if he said: Is there a god with God? Woe to you? {Is there a god with God?} So god is raised by with. It is permissible for it to be raised by implying: Is there a god with God who does that, so you worship Him?}. Stopping at with God is good. {Little do you remember} Abu Omar, Hisham, and Ya`qub read they remember with a ya’ as a predicate like His statement: {But most of them do not know} and: {Exalted is God above what they associate with Him.} So He informed about what comes before and after it, and Abu Hatim chose this. The rest read it with a ta’ as an address for His statement: {And makes you successors to the earth}.
27:63: The Almighty says: Who guides you meaning shows you the way in the darkness of the land and sea when you travel to the country you are heading to by night and day. It was said: He made the deserts of the land that have no landmarks, and the depths of the seas as if they were darkness, because they have no sign to guide oneself. And who sends the winds as broadcasting before His mercy" meaning before the rain according to the agreement of the people of interpretation. "With God rather He does that and helps him with it God is above what they associate besides Him.
27:64: The Almighty said: Is He who initiates creation and then repeats it? They used to acknowledge that He is the Creator and Provider, so He obligated them to repeat, meaning that if He is able to initiate, then it is necessary for Him to be able to repeat, and that is easier for Him. Is there a god with God who creates, provides, initiates, and repeats? Say, ‘Bring your proof,’ meaning your argument that I have a partner, or your argument that anyone other than God created any of these things, “if you should be truthful.
27:65: God the Almighty says: Say, ‘No one in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except God.’ Some of them said: He concealed His unseen from creation, and no one knew about it lest any of His servants feel secure from His deception. It was also said: It was revealed about the polytheists when they asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the Hour. Min is in the nominative case, and the meaning is: Say, ‘No one knows the unseen except God.’ It is a substitute for Min, as Al-Zajjaj said. Al-Farra’ said: What comes after illa is in the nominative case because what precedes it is a denial, like his saying: No one has gone except your father, and the meaning is the same. Al-Zajjaj said: Min is in the accusative case as an exception, and it means in the speech.” An-Nahhas said: I heard him use this verse as evidence against someone who believed an astrologer, and he said: I fear that he will disbelieve in this verse. I said: This has already been fully discussed in Al-An'am. Aisha said: Whoever claims that Muhammad knows what will happen tomorrow has greatly slandered God, and God the Almighty says: Say, ‘None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except God.’ Narrated by Muslim. It was narrated that an astrologer entered upon Al-Hajjaj and Al-Hajjaj detained him. Then he took some pebbles and counted them. Then he said, How many pebbles are in my hand? The astrologer counted and said, Such and such, and he was correct. Then he detained him and took some pebbles but did not count them. Then he said, How many are in my hand? He counted and was wrong. Then he counted and was wrong. Then he said, O Commander, I think you do not know their number. The man said, No. The man said, Then how can I not be correct? The man said, What is the difference? The man said, I counted that and it is beyond the bounds of the unseen, but you did not count this, so it is unseen. “None in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except God.” This has already been discussed in Al-Imran, and praise be to God.
27:66: This is the reading of most of the people, including Asim, Shaibah, Nafi’, Yahya ibn Thabit, Al-A’mash, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i. Abu Ja’far, Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Hamid read:بال دراكfromدريكا. Ata’ ibn Yasar, his brother Sulayman ibn Yasar, and Al-A’mash read:بال دراكwithout a hamza and with a shaddah. Ibn Muhaisin read:بال دراكas a question. Ibn Abbas read: بالwith the addition of the ya’أدراكwith a hamzat qata’ and a shaddah on the dal and an alif after it. An-Nahhas said: Its chain of transmission is a saheeh chain of transmission, it is from the hadeeth of Shu’bah which he traces back to Ibn Abbas. Harun Al-Qari’ claimed that the reading of Abu wasبال تاداراك علمهمand Al-Tha’labi narrated that it is in the letter of Abu or taDARAKA. The Arabs use bal in place of umm and umm in place of bal if there is a question at the beginning of the sentence, like the poet’s saying: I swear to God, I don’t know whether to say it or to leave it to my beloved Rather, all. An-Nahhas said: The first and last readings have the same meaning, because the root of adharaka is tadārak, the dal was assimilated into the ta’ and an alif was added. There are two opinions regarding its meaning: One of them is that the meaning is: Rather, their knowledge will be completed in the Hereafter, because they saw everything they were promised with their own eyes, so their knowledge of it was completed. The other opinion is that the meaning is: Rather, their knowledge will continue today in the Hereafter, so they said: It will be, and they said: It will not be. There are also two opinions in the second reading: One of them is that its meaning is: It will be completed in the Hereafter, and it is like the first. Mujahid said: Its meaning is: Their knowledge will be completed in the Hereafter and they will know it when they witness it, at a time when their knowledge will not benefit them, because they were deniers in this world. The other opinion is that it means denial, and this is the view of Abu Ishaq. The validity of this opinion is proven by the fact that after it Rather, they are blind to it, meaning their knowledge did not complete the knowledge of the Hereafter. It was also said: Rather, their knowledge will go astray and disappear in the Hereafter, so they have no knowledge of it. The third reading: bala idrak has the same meaning as bala idrak. Ifta`ala and tafa`ala may also come with the same meaning, therefore izdawajuwa was corrected to mean tazawajuwa. The fourth reading: There is only one saying that has the meaning of denial, as someone says: Did I fight you?! Then the meaning would be: You did not catch up. Based on this, the reading of Ibn Abbas is based: bala adarak `alamhum fi al-akhira meaning: He did not catch up. Al-Farra` said: It is a good saying, as if he directed it to mock those who deny the resurrection, like when you say to a man whom you accuse of lying: By my life, you have caught up with the predecessors, so you narrate what I narrate! And you accuse him of lying. A seventh reading: bala idrak with a fatha on the lam, he changed to a fatha because it is light. Something similar to this was reported from Qatrib in Qum al-Layl, as he changed to a fatha. The same applies to Ba` al-Thawb and the like. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned in the book: “And it was read bala a’drak with two hamzas bala a’drak with an alif between them bala a’drak (am tadrak) amm tadrak (amm idrak) so these are twelve readings. Then he began to give reasons for the different readings and said: If you say, what is the reason for reading bala a’drak as a question? I say: It is a question in the way of denying the realization of their knowledge. And the same is true for those who read amm tadrak and amm tadrak because it is the word “am” which means bala and the hamza. As for those who read bala a’drak as a question, its meaning is yes they know when they will be resurrected. Then he denied their knowledge of its being, and if he denied their knowledge of its being, they would not have any awareness of the time of its being, because knowledge of the time of the event is dependent on knowledge of the eventuality of the eventuality. in the Hereafter concerning the Hereafter and its meaning. Rather, they are in doubt about it meaning this world. Rather, they are blind to it meaning in their hearts, one of them is blind. It was said: uncle, and its origin is blind, the ya was deleted for the sake of the two quiescent ta’s, and it was not permissible to move it because of the heaviness of the movement in it.
27:67: God the Almighty says: And those who disbelieved said meaning the polytheists of Mecca, If we have become dust and our fathers, will we indeed be brought forth? This is how Nafi' recites it here and in Surah Al-Ankabut. Amr recited it with two interrogative pronouns, except that he lightened the hamza. Asim and Hamza also recited it with two interrogative pronouns, except that they pronounced the two hamzas fully. Everything we mentioned in both surahs is the same. Al-Kisa'i, Ibn 'Amir, Ruways, and Ya'qub recited:أخَذاwith two hamzasإنذناwith two noons as a predicate in this surah, and in Surah Al-Ankabut with two interrogative pronouns. Abu Ja'far and Al-Nahhas said: The readingإَذا نذبذا بذانذا وذابذانذا وذإخنذا نذيذْغرروَذis in accordance with the script and is good. Abu Hatim criticized it and said, and this is the meaning of his words:إخَذاis not with two interrogative pronouns, andأخنذا is an interrogative pronoun, and it contains َإ, so how can something in the interrogative category apply to what precedes it? How can it be known what comes after in from what comes before it? And how can it be said tomorrow if Zaid is outside? If there is a question in it, it is further away, and if this is asked about it, it would be problematic for what he mentioned. Abu Ja`far said: I heard Muhammad bin Al-Waleed say: We asked Abu Al-Abbas about a difficult and thankful verse from the Qur’an, which is the saying of God the Most High: And those who disbelieve say, ‘Shall we guide you to a man who will inform you, when you are torn apart, that you will indeed be in a new creation?’ (Saba’ 34:7) He said: If the function of idh is to inform you, it is impossible, because he will not inform them at that time, and if what comes after in works on it, the meaning is correct, and it is an error in Arabic to make what comes before in work on what comes after it. This is a clear question. I thought it should be mentioned in the surah it is in. As for Abu Ubaid, he favored Nafi’s reading and responded to those who combined two interrogative pronouns. He provided evidence for this with the words of God the Almighty: Then if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels? (Al Imran 3:144) and His words: Then if I die, will they be the immortals? (Al Anbiya’ 21:34). This response to Abu Amr Asim, Hamzah, Talhah, and Al A’raj does not necessitate anything, nor does it resemble the verse he presented. The difference between them is that the condition and its answer are equivalent to one thing, and the meaning of Then if I die, will they be the immortals? (Al Anbiya’ 21:34) is: Then if I die, will they be immortals? Similar to this is: Is Zaid munqala’ Is Zaid going and nor is it heavy Is Zaid going because they are equivalent to one thing, but this is not the case in the verse, because the second is a clause that stands on its own and can be used as an interrogative pronoun, while the first is a statement that can be used as an interrogative pronoun. As for those who omitted the interrogative pronoun from the second and included it in the first, they read: Then will we, when we have become dust and our fathers, [O Muhammad]? They omitted it from the second because the statement contains evidence of it in the sense of denial.
27:68: The Almighty said: “We were promised this, we and our fathers before. This is nothing but legends of the ancients.” This was mentioned in Surah Al-Mu’minun. The prophets used to exaggerate the warning about the resurrection, and everything that was coming was near.
27:69: God Almighty says: Say, ‘Travel through the land.’ That is, Say to these infidels travel in the lands of Syria, the Hijaz, and Yemen. Then see that is, with your hearts and your insights how was the end of the criminals who denied their messengers.
27:70: The Almighty said: And do not grieve over them meaning over the disbelievers of Mecca if they do not believe. And do not be in distress in difficulty because of what they are plotting. This was revealed regarding the mockers who divided up the punishment of Mecca, and we have already mentioned them. It was also read: in distress with a kasra, and this was mentioned at the end of An-Nahl.
27:71: God Almighty says: And they say, ‘When will this promise come to pass?’ That is, when will the punishment come to us because of our denial, if you should be truthful.
27:72: The Almighty said: “Say: Perhaps there will be some of that which you are hastening” meaning, of the punishment, as Ibn Abbas said. It is from radfahu if he followed him or came after him, and the lam is inserted because the meaning is approached you and is near to you. Or it is related to the source. It was said: its meaning is with you. Ibn Shajarah said: followed you, and from this comes the word radfa of the woman because he followed her from behind her, and from this is the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb: The blackness has returned to whiteness in his partings. No welcome to the whiteness of gray hair when it follows. Al-Jawhari said: “And he followed him with an order, linguistically, in the sense of ‘he followed him with’, like ‘he followed him with’ and ‘he followed him with the same meaning. Khuzaymah bin Malik bin Nahd said: If Gemini follows the Pleiades, I will have bad thoughts about the family of Fatima. Meaning Fatima bint Yadhkur bin Anza, one of the Qariths. Al-Farra’ said: (Radfa lakum) means he approached you, and that is why he said: (Lakum). It was said: Radfahu and Radfa lahu have the same meaning, so the lam is added for emphasis, also from Al-Farra’. Just as you say: I naqaddtuhu and naqdtu lahu, I kaltuhu and weightuhu, I kaltu lahu and weightuhu, and the like. (Some of what you are hastening) of the punishment, so that was on the day of Badr. It was said: the punishment of the grave.
27:73: God Almighty says: And indeed, your Lord is full of bounty to mankind in delaying punishment and providing sustenance, but most of them are not grateful for His bounty and blessings.
27:74: The Almighty said: And indeed, your Lord knows what their breasts conceal meaning what their breasts conceal and what they declare meaning what they reveal of matters. Ibn Muhaisin and Hamid read: َما تكو fromكاننت شيءif you conceal something here. Inالقصص its meaning is: what their breasts conceal, and it is as if the pronoun in the breasts is like a moving body. And whoever reads: َكاit is the known, it is said:اكنتش هَاif you conceal it in yourself.
27:75: God the Almighty says: And there is nothing hidden within the heaven or earth but is in a clear register. Al-Hasan said: The ghaybah here is the Resurrection. It was also said that it means the torment of the heaven and the earth that was hidden from them, as narrated by Al-Naqqash. Ibn Shajarah said: The ghaybah here is everything that God the Almighty has concealed from His creation and hidden from them, and this is general. The ha' was added to the word ghaybah to indicate the plural, meaning: There is no characteristic hidden from creation except that God knows it and has recorded it in the Mother of the Book with Him, so how could what these people conceal and what they declare be hidden from Him? It was also said that it means everything that is recorded in the Mother of the Book, He brings it forth for its appointed term. As for the torment that they hasten, it has a set term that will not be delayed or advanced. The Book is the Preserved Tablet, in which God has recorded what He wills so that He may inform whomever He wills of His angels.
27:76: God Almighty says: Indeed, this Qur’an narrates to the Children of Israel most of that over which they differ. This is because they differed about many things, to the point that they cursed one another, so this verse was revealed. The meaning is: This Qur’an explains to them what they would have differed about had they taken it, and that is what they distorted from the Torah and the Gospel, and what rulings they omitted from their hard work. And it means the Qur’an.
27:77: The Almighty's saying: As guidance and mercy to the believers. He specified the believers because they are the ones who will benefit from it. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them with His judgment. That is, He will judge between the Children of Israel regarding their differences in the Hereafter, rewarding the truth and falsehood. It was also said that He will judge between them in this world and will make manifest what they have distorted. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Invincible, the Victorious, whose command cannot be rejected.
27:78: God Almighty says: The All-Knowing from whom nothing is hidden.
27:79: The Almighty says: So rely upon God meaning, entrust your affair to Him and depend on Him, for He is your supporter. Indeed, you are upon the clear truth meaning, the apparent truth. It was also said: the manifest one for whoever contemplates the correct path.
27:80: The Almighty says: Indeed, you do not hear the dead meaning the disbelievers because they neglect to contemplate, they are like the dead, they have no sense or mind. It was said: This is for someone who knows that he will not believe. And the deaf do not hear the call meaning the disbelievers who are like the deaf in accepting admonitions, so when they are called to choose, they turn away and act as if they do not hear, similar to the verse: Deaf, dumb, and blind (Al-Baqarah 2:18) as mentioned above. Ibn Haysun, Hamid, Ibn Kathir, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Abbas, on the authority of Abu Amr, read: And the deaf do not hear with a fat-ha on the ya' and the meem, in the nominative case as the subject. The rest read nine in the present tense of I heard, the deaf in the accusative case. Question: Aisha may God be pleased with her used this verse as evidence to deny that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had made the dead of Badr hear. So I examined the matter through rational reasoning and settled on this verse. It has been authenticated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: You are not better at hearing than they. Ibn Atiyyah said: It seems that the story of Badr was a breach of Muhammad’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) habit, in that God restored their awareness by which they heard his words. Had it not been for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informing us that they had heard, we would have interpreted his calling to them as a rebuke to those who remained of the disbelievers, and as a healing for the hearts of the believers. I said: Al-Bukhari may God be pleased with him narrated that Abdullah bin Muhammad heard Ruh bin Ubadah say: Saeed bin Abi Farwabah told us on the authority of Qatadah who said: Anas bin Malik mentioned to us on the authority of Abu Talha that the Prophet of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) ordered on the day of Badr that twenty-four men from the leaders of Quraysh be thrown into one of the valleys of Badr, a filthy and dirty valley. When he gained victory over a people, he would stay in the courtyard for three nights. When it was the third day at Badr, he ordered his mount to be taken and its saddle was strapped onto it, then he walked, and his companions followed him. They said: We do not think he sets out except for some need, until he stood on the edge of the well and began calling them by their names and the names of their fathers: O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, would it please you to obey God and His Messenger? We have found that what our Lord promised us is true. Have you found that what your Lord promised is true? Umar said: O Messenger of God, what speaks are bodies that have no souls? The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you do not hear what he says better than they. He said: Qatada: God revived them so that they could hear His words of repentance, belittlement, vengeance, envy, and regret. Muslim also narrated it. Al-Bukhari said: Uthman told us, Abdah told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, stood by the well of Badr and said: Have you found what your Lord promised to be true? Then he said: They are now [hearing what I am saying]. This was mentioned to Aisha, who said: “The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, only said that they are now] so that they may know that what I used to say to them is the truth.” Get up and recite: You cannot make the dead hear, until I recited the verse. This verse was contradicted by the story of Badr and the greeting of peace upon graves, and by what was narrated concerning that, that souls are at the edge of graves at times, and that the dead hear the sound of sandals when they leave, and other things. If the dead did not hear, then peace would not be given to him. This is clear and we have explained it in the Book of Remembrance.
27:81: The Almighty said: And you cannot guide the blind from their misguidance meaning their disbelief, meaning it is not in your power to create faith in their hearts. Hamzah read: And you cannot guide the blind from their misguidance like His statement: Then can you guide the blind? (Yunus 10:43). The rest read: Bahadi al-Ammi and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. In ar-Rum it is similar. All of them stopped at Bahadi with a ya' in this surah and without a ya' in ar-Rum following the Mushaf. Except for Ya'qub, who stopped in both of them with a ya'. Al-Farra' and Abu Hatim permitted: And you cannot guide the blind and this is the original. In the version of Abdullah, And you cannot guide the blind means you cannot hear. Except for those who believe in Our verses Ibn Abbas said: meaning, except for those whom You created for happiness, so they are sincere in their monotheism.
27:82: God the Almighty says: And when the Word comes to pass against them, We will produce for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them. There is a difference of opinion as to the meaning of the Word comes to pass and the creature. Some say that the meaning of the Word comes to pass is that wrath is due upon them. Qatadah said: Mujahid said: That is, the Word will be fulfilled upon them that they will not believe. Ibn Umar and Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri may God be pleased with them said: If they do not enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, wrath is due upon them. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: The Word comes to pass with the death of scholars, the loss of knowledge, and the removal of the Qur'an. Abdullah said: Recite the Qur'an frequently before it is removed. They said: These copies of the Qur'an will be removed, so how about what is in the hearts of men? He said: It will be carried out at night and in the morning they will find it deserted, and they will forget There is no god but God and will adhere to the sayings and poetry of the Age of Ignorance, and that will be when the Word comes to pass against them. I said: Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar narrated it. He said: Abdullah bin Yusuf Al-Thaqafi narrated to us. Abdul Majeed bin Abdul Aziz narrated to us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Safwan bin Saleem, on the authority of a son of Abdullah bin Masoud may God be pleased with him, on the authority of his father, who said: Visit this House often before it is taken up and people forget its location, and recite the Qur’an often before it is taken up. They said: O Abu Abdul Rahman, will these copies of the Qur’an be taken up, so what about what is in the hearts of men? He said: So they will wake up and say, ‘We used to speak and say things,’ and they will revert to the poetry and hadiths of the Age of Ignorance, and that will be when the word will come to pass against them. It was said: The word is the words of God the Most High: “But the word from Me will come into effect: ‘I will surely fill Hell.’” (32:13) So the word came to pass that punishment is obligatory upon these people, and when they reach a point where their repentance is not accepted and no believing children are born to them, then at that time the Resurrection will take place. Al-Qushayri mentioned it. A sixth statement: Hafsa bint Sirin said: I asked Abu Al-Aaliyah about the statement of God the Most High: And when the word comes to pass against them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them. He said: God revealed to Nuh 71:None of your people will believe except those who have already believed. (Hud 11:36) It was as if I had been given a gift and then it was removed. An-Nahhas said: This is a good answer, because people are being tested and given a reprieve because among them are believers and righteous people. And those whom God the Most High knows will believe and repent, that is why He gave them respite and commanded us to take the jizyah. So when this is removed, the statement will be made obligatory upon them, and they will become like the people of Noah when God the Most High said: None of your people will believe except those who have already believed. (Hud 11:36) I said: All the sayings, upon reflection, come back to one meaning. The evidence for that is the last part of the verse: That people were not certain of Our signs. It was also read as that with a fat-ha on the hamza, and this will come later. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “There are three things, if they come out, no soul will benefit from its faith if it did not believe before or earned any good through its faith: the rising of the sun from the west, the Antichrist, and the beast of the earth.” This has already been mentioned. There is much disagreement over the identification of this beast, its description, and from where it will come out. We have mentioned this in the book At-Tadhkirah, and we will mention it here in full, God willing. The first of the sayings is that it is a young camel of Salih, and this is the most correct - and God knows best - because Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi mentioned in his Musnad on the authority of Hudhayfah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mentioned the beast and said: “It will have three outings in a lifetime. It will emerge in the farthest desert, but its mention will not reach the village - meaning Mecca - then it will lie in wait for a long time, then it will emerge another time after that, and its mention will spread in the desert, but its mention will reach the village - meaning Mecca. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Then while the people were in the greatest of mosques, the sanctity of which God has enshrined, the best of which God has enshrined, the Sacred Mosque, they were not startled by anything except it foaming between the Rakhin and the Maqam, shaking the dust off its head. The people ran away from it in groups and together, and a group of believers stood firm and knew that they would not be unable to defeat God. It began with them, transforming their faces until it became like a shining star, and it turned in the earth, and no seeker could catch it and no fugitive could escape from it, until a man would seek refuge from it in prayer, and it would come to him from behind and say, ‘O so-and-so, now you are praying.’ It would turn to him and name him on his face.” Then it will set out and people will share the wealth and they will make peace in the cities and the believer will be known from the disbeliever until the believer will say, O disbeliever, fulfill my right. The evidence for this hadith is that it is the young camel, as he said: And it was roaring. The roaring is for camels, because when the young camel was killed, it ran away and a stone opened for it and it entered its stomach and then closed over it, and it remains in it until it comes out by the permission of God, the Almighty. It was narrated that it is a furry, hairy animal with legs sixty cubits long. It is said that it is the spy, and this is the opinion of Abdullah ibn Amr. It was narrated from Ibn Amr that it has the creation of humans, and it is in the clouds and its legs are on the earth. It was narrated that it has gathered the creation of every animal. Al-Mawardi and Al-Tha'labi said: Its head is the head of a bull, its eye is the eye of a pig, its ear is the ear of an elephant, its horns are the horns of a deer, its neck is the neck of an ostrich, its chest is the chest of a lion, its color is the color of a tiger, its flank is the flank of a cat, its tail is the tail of a ram, its legs are the legs of a camel, between each joint are twelve cubits - Al-Zamakhshari: the cubits of Adam, peace be upon him - and with it comes forth the staff of Moses and the ring of Solomon, so it pricks the face of the Muslim with the staff of Moses with a white prick, and his face turns white, and it pricks the face of the disbeliever with the ring of Solomon, peace be upon him, and his face turns black, as said by Ibn Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them both. In the book Al-Naqqash, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: The beast is the snake overlooking the wall of the Kaaba, which was uprooted by the eagle when the Quraysh wanted to rebuild the Kaaba. Al-Mawardi narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Kaab on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he was asked about the dara, and he said: By God, it has no sin, and it has a beard. Al-Mawardi said: In this statement of his, there is an indication that it is from humans, even if he did not state it explicitly. I said: For this reason - and God knows best - some of the later commentators said: It is more likely that this beast is a speaking human being who debates and argues with the people of innovation and disbelief until they are cut off, so whoever is destroyed will perish with clear evidence, and whoever is alive will live with clear evidence. Our Sheikh, Imam Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Umar al-Qurtubi said in his book al-Mufhim: According to this speaker, it was closer to the saying of God Almighty, It will speak to them. Based on this, there is no specific sign in this beast that is unusual, and it is not one of the ten signs mentioned in the hadith, because the existence of debaters and argumentators against the people of innovation is plentiful, so it does not have a specific sign for it, so it should not be mentioned with the ten, and the special nature of its existence is removed if the statement is made. Then there is a shift from calling this virtuous, knowledgeable, debating human being, whom the people of the earth are supposed to call by the name of human, scholar, or imam, to calling him a beast. This is a departure from the custom of the eloquent and from the veneration of scholars, and this is not the practice of the wise. What is better is what the commentators said, and God knows best the truth of matters. I said: The ambiguity about this beast has been resolved by what we mentioned in the hadith of Hudhayfah, so let it be relied upon. There is disagreement about the place from which it will emerge. Abdullah ibn Umar said: It will emerge from Mount Safa in Mecca. It will crack and then it will emerge from it. Abdullah ibn Amr said something similar and said: If I wanted to place my foot on the place where it will emerge, I could do so. It was narrated in a hadith from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): “The earth will split open and reveal the beast while Jesus, peace be upon him, will circumambulate the House with the Muslims from the direction of Al-Mas’a. And it will emerge from Safa and will mark between the eyes of the believer, he is a believer, a mark like a shining star, and it will mark between the eyes of the disbeliever, a black mark, he is a disbeliever.” It was mentioned in the hadith that it has fur and feathers, as mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. And it was narrated from Ibn Abbas that it will emerge from a ravine and its head will touch the clouds while its feet are on the earth and have not emerged. And the staff of Moses and the ring of Solomon, peace be upon them, will emerge with it. On the authority of Hudhayfah: He would go out on three expeditions: one expedition to some of the deserts and then lie in wait, one expedition to the villages where the leaders would fight until much bloodshed occurred, and one expedition to one of the greatest mosques. And the most honorable, the most noble, and the most excellent of them. Al-Zamakhshari: It emerges from between the corner opposite the house of Bani Majzum to the right of those leaving the mosque, so some people flee, and some people stand and watch. It was narrated from Qatada that it emerges in Tihama. It was narrated that it emerges from the mosque of Kufa from where the oven of Noah, peace be upon him, bubbled. It was also said: From the land of Taif. Abu Qabil said: Abdullah bin Amr kicked the ground of Taif and said: From here will emerge the beast that will speak to the people. It was also said: From some of the valleys of Tihama. Ibn Abbas said. It was also said: From a rock in the valley of Ajyad. Abdullah bin Amr said. It was also said: From the Sea of Sodom. Wahb bin Munabbih said. Al-Mawardi mentioned these last three sayings in his book. Al-Baghawi Abu al-Qasim Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Abdul Aziz said: Ali bin al-Ja`d told us on the authority of Fadil bin Marzouq al-Raqashi al-Agharr - and Yahya bin Ma`in was asked about him and he said he was trustworthy - on the authority of Atiyah al-`Awfi on the authority of Ibn `Umar who said: The beast will emerge from a crack in the Ka`bah like the gallop of a horse for three days, but a third of it will not emerge. I said: These are the sayings of the Companions and the Followers about the emergence of the Beast and its description. They refute the statement of the commentators who said: The Beast is a talking human being who debates the people of innovation and disbelief. Abu Umamah narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The Beast will emerge and brand people on their snouts. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. (It speaks to them) with a damma on the ta’ and a shaddah on the lam with a kasra – from speech – is the reading of the common people, as indicated by Abu’s reading (It informs them). Al-Suddi said: It will speak to them about the invalidity of religions other than the religion of Islam. It was also said: It will speak to them in a way that will upset them. It was also said: It will speak to them with a smooth tongue and will say to a voice that can be heard from near and far, Indeed, people were not certain of Our signs, meaning about my emergence, because its emergence is one of the signs. And it will say: Indeed, the curse of God be upon the wrongdoers. Abu Zur’ah, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, and Abu Raja’ read: (It speaks to them) with a fatha on the ta’ from the word kalam, which is the jarj. Ikrimah said: It means it will brand them. Abu Al-Juza’ said: I asked Ibn Abbas about this verse talk to them or talk to them so he said: By God, it speaks to them and speaks to them, it speaks to the believer and speaks to the disbeliever and the wicked, meaning it wounds him. Abu Hatim said: talk to them is like you say wound them, he thinks that it is an increase in talk to them. The people were not certain of Our verses The Kufians, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Yahya read an with a fatha. The people of the Two Holy Mosques, the people of Syria and the people of Basra read in with a kasra over the hamza. An-Nahhas said: There are two opinions regarding the fatha, and so is the kasra over the hamza. Al-Ahfash said: The meaning is that, and so did Ban Mas’ud read ban. Abu Ubaidah said: Its position is accusative because the verb occurs on it, meaning it informs them that the people. Al-Kisa’i and Al-Farra’ read inna al-nas with a kasra as a new sentence. Al-Ahfash said: It means it says that the people, meaning the disbelievers. They have no certainty in Our verses, meaning in the Qur’an and in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This will happen when God will not accept faith from a disbeliever and only believers and disbelievers will remain in God’s knowledge before it comes out. And God knows best.
27:83: The Almighty said: And the Day We shall gather from every nation a company meaning a group and a community. of those who denied Our signs meaning the Qur’an and Our signs that are upon the truth. And they will be driven in ranks meaning they will be pushed and driven to the place of reckoning. Al-Shamakh said: How many Khamis have we distributed and how many leaders have we been given? Qatada said, They distribute, meaning the first of them returns to the last of them. Until when they come, he said, Meaning, I am a monotheist. “And you did not encompass it with knowledge,” meaning its falsehood, so you turned away from it. Rather, you lied, being ignorant and not providing evidence.
27:84: The Almighty says: What were you doing? This is a rebuke and a rebuke, meaning what were you doing when you did not search for it or think about what was in it? And the word fell upon them because of their wrongdoing. Meaning, the punishment was due to them because of their wrongdoing, meaning their polytheism.
27:85: God Almighty says: They will not speak meaning they will have no excuse or argument. It was also said: Their mouths will be sealed so they will not speak, as most commentators have said.
27:86: The Almighty said: Have they not seen that We have made the night for them to rest therein meaning that they settle down and sleep and the day to see meaning that one can see in it for the pursuit of sustenance. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe in God. He mentioned the evidence of His divinity and power, meaning have they not risen as We have made them so that they may believe.
27:87: The Almighty said: And the Day the Trumpet is blown. That is, remember the Day or mention them when the Trumpet is blown. Al-Farra's school of thought is that the meaning is: And that is the Day the Trumpet is blown. He permitted deletion, but the correct meaning of the Trumpet is that it is a horn of light that Israfil will blow. Mujahid said: Like a trumpet. It was also said: It is the trumpet in the language of the people of Yemen. Its explanation and the scholars' opinions on this have already been mentioned in Al-An'am. Then everyone in the heavens and the earth will be terrified, except whom God wills. Abu Hurairah said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: When God finished creating the heavens, He gave it to Israfil, who is placing it on his mouth, staring at the Throne, waiting for the command to blow. I said: O Messenger of God, what is the Trumpet? He said: “A mighty horn, by Him Who sent me with the truth, the width of its chamber is like the width of the evening and the earth. Then it will be blown three times: the first will be the blast of terror, the second will be the blast of the stunned twilight, and the third will be the blast of resurrection and rising before the Lord of the worlds.” And he mentioned the hadith. It was mentioned by Ali ibn Ma’bad, al-Tabari, al-Tha’labi and others, and Ibn al-Arabi authenticated it. I have mentioned it in Kitab al-Tadhkira and we have discussed it there. The correct view concerning the blowing of the trumpet is that there will be two blasts, not three, and that the blast of terror will be in reference to the blast of the stunned twilight because the two are inseparable from each other, meaning they will be terrified and die from it, or to the blast of resurrection, which is the preferred view of al-Qushayri and others, for he said in his commentary on this verse: What is meant is the second blast, meaning they will come to life in terror, saying, Who has raised us from our beds? (Yasin 36:52), and they will witness from the matter that will terrify and frighten them, and this blast will be like the sound of a trumpet for the creation to gather in the land of recompense. Qatada said it and Al-Mawardi said: And the Day the Trumpet is blown, meaning the resurrection from the graves. He said: There are two opinions about this fear: One of them is that it is hastening and responding to the call, as they say: I hastened to you regarding such-and-such, if they hastened to your call for your assistance. The second opinion is that the fear here is the usual fear of fear and sadness, because they were disturbed from their graves, so they were startled and afraid. This is more similar to the two opinions. I said: The Sunnah is based on the established hadith of Abu Hurayrah and the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr, which indicates that there will be two blasts, not three. Muslim included them, and we mentioned them in the Book of Remembrance, and it is correct, God willing, that there will be two blasts. God Almighty said: And the Trumpet will be blown, and all who are in the heavens and all who are on the earth will fall unconscious except whom God wills. So He made an exception here, just as He made an exception in the case of the blast of terror, indicating that it will be one. Ibn al-Mubarak narrated on the authority of al-Hasan that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Between the two blasts will be forty years. In the first, God will kill every living thing, and in the second, God will bring every dead thing to life.” If it is said: God Almighty said: On the Day when the Great Earthquake will shake, followed by the Second (an-Nazi’at 79:6-7) until He said: It will be only one blast (an-Nazi’at 79:13), and this apparently indicates that there will be three. It was said to him: It is not like that. Rather, what is meant by the second blast is the second blast, which will cause the creation to emerge from their graves. This is what Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Ibn Zayd and others said. Mujahid said: They are two shouts: the first will kill everything by God’s permission, and the second will revive everything by God’s permission. Ata’ said: The shaking is the Resurrection and the following is the Resurrection. Ibn Zayd said: The shaking is death and the following is the Hour. And God knows best. Except for whom God wills. Then there is a difference of opinion as to who is excluded from this. In the hadith of Abu Hurairah it says that they are the martyrs with their Lord, and they are provided for, and the terror only reaches those who are still alive. This is the opinion of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, that they are the martyrs wearing swords around the Throne. Al-Qushayri said: The prophets are included among them, because they have happiness along with prophethood. It was also said: The angels. Al-Hasan said: He excluded groups of angels who will die between the two blasts. Muqatil said: He means Gabriel, Michael, and the Angel of Death. It was also said: The wide-eyed houris. It was also said: They are the believers, because God Almighty said after this: Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it, and they, from the terror of that Day, will be secure. Some of our scholars said: What is correct is that no authentic hadith has been reported specifying them, and all are possible. I said: The hadith of Abu Hurayrah was hidden from him, and Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi authenticated it, so let him rely on it, because a text regarding specification and other than that is a matter of personal opinion, and God knows best. It was said: Other than this, as will come in Az-Zumar. His statement, So whoever is in the heavens will be terrified is a past tense verb, and will be blown is a future tense verb, so it is said: How can a past tense be conjoined with a future tense verb? Al-Farra’ claimed that this is based on the meaning, because the meaning is: When the trumpet is blown, then everyone will be terrified. Except whom God wills is in the accusative case as an exception. And all will come to Him in humiliation Abu Amr, Al-Kisa’i, Nafi’, Ibn ‘Amir, and Ibn Kathir read they came to Him making it a future tense verb. Al-A’mash, Yahya, Hamzah, and Hafs from ‘Asim read and all will come to Him restricted to the past tense verb, and Ibn Mas’ud read the same. On the authority of Qatada: (And every one of them came to Him humiliated) An-Nahhas said: In my book on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the recitations, whoever reads (And every one of them came to Him) alone with the wording (everyone), whoever reads (they came to Him), he pluralizes it according to its meaning. This statement is an ugly mistake, because if he says (And every one of them came to Him), he has not made it singular but rather made it plural. If he made it singular, he would have said (He came to Him), but whoever says (They came to Him) made it plural according to the meaning and used it in the past tense because he returned it to (So he was startled), and whoever reads (And every one of them came to Him), he also carried it according to the meaning and said (They came to Him) because it is a disconnected sentence from the first. Ibn Nasr said: It has been reported from Ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, what he did not say, and Abu Ishaq stated: (And every one of them came to Him humiliated) and he reads (They came to Him), so whoever made it singular, then it is for the word (everyone), and whoever made it plural, then it is for its meaning. He wants what came in the Quran or other than it of the unification of the report of (all) so it is based on the wording or the plural so it is based on the meaning, so Abu Jaafar did not take this meaning. Al-Mahdawi said: And whoever read (and all of them came to Him humbled) it is a verb from coming and it is taken to mean (all) without its wording, and whoever reads (and all of them came to Him humbled) it has the active participle from came. And the evidence for that is the saying of the Most High: And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone (Maryam 19:95) And whoever reads (and all of them came to Him) it is taken to mean the wording of (all) without its meaning and it is taken (humiliated) to mean, and its meaning is humbled, from Ibn Abbas and Qatada. And it has been mentioned in Al-Nahl.
27:88: The Almighty said: And you will see the mountains, thinking them rigid, while they will pass as the clouds pass. Ibn Abbas said: That is, standing, yet they will move quickly. Al-Qutbi said: That is because the mountains are gathered and move, so in the eyes’ vision they are as if they were standing while they are moving. Likewise, everything great and numerous is too numerous for the eye to see, due to its great number and the distance between its edges. In the eyes of the observer it is as if it is standing still while it is moving. Al-Nabigha said in describing an army: They are as reckless as the mountain, stopping for the pilgrims and the passengers are neglecting them. Al-Qushayri said: “This is the Day of Resurrection, meaning that due to their large number, they will be as if they were stationary, that is, standing still in plain sight, even though in themselves they move like clouds. The accumulated clouds will appear to be standing still while they are moving, that is, they will pass by like clouds until nothing of them remains. So God, the Most High, said: ‘And the mountains will be set in motion and will become a mirage.’ (An-Naba’: 20) It is said that God, the Most High, described the mountains with different descriptions, all of which go back to the earth being emptied of them and what they had been hidden being exposed. The first description is being crushed, which is before the earthquake. Then they will become like fluffy wool, which is when the sky becomes like coarse wool. God combined the two, saying: ‘The Day the sky will be like molten molten metal, and the mountains will be like wool.’ (al-Ma’arij 70:8-9) The third state is that they will become like dust, which is when they are cut apart after having been like wool. The fourth state is that they will be blown away, because with the aforementioned conditions they will be stable in their places and the earth beneath them will not be exposed, so they will be blown away to reveal themselves. When they are blown away, it will be by sending winds upon them.” The fifth case is that the winds lift it to the surface of the earth, making it appear as a ray of light in the air, like dust. When you look at it from a distance, you think it is solid bodies due to its density. In reality, it is passing by, except that its passing behind the winds is as if it were crushed and disintegrated. The sixth case is that it is a mirage. When you look at its location, you will not find anything of it, like a mirage. Muqatil said: It falls to the earth and is leveled with it. Then it was said: This is a parable. Al-Mawardi said: There are three opinions about what it was used for: The first is that it is a parable that God Almighty used for the world, making the one looking at it think that it is standing still like mountains, but it is taking its share of disappearing like the clouds. This was said by Sahl ibn Abdullah. The second is that it is a parable that God used for faith, you think it is fixed in the heart and its deeds are ascending to the sky. The third is that it is a parable that God used for the soul when the soul exits and the soul travels to the throne. The work of God, who perfected all things meaning, this is from the doing of God, and whatever is an doing of His is perfect. The word tarā see comes from seeing with the eyes, and if it were from seeing with the heart, it would have two objects. The original form is tarā see, so the vowel of the hamza was placed on the ra, so the ra was moved and the hamza was deleted. This is the way to lighten the hamza if it is preceded by a sukoon, except that lightening is necessary for tarā see. The people of Kufa read tahsab recite with a fatha on the sin, which is the standard, because it is from hāsab to think, but it has been narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that it was different, that he read it with a kasra in the future tense, so it would be on the form fa`il to do good, like na`am to appreciate and ba`isa to be pleased with, and it has been reported that ya`isa deep is from the sound form. In Arabic speech, no other letters are known except these letters. (And it will pass like the passing of clouds) The meaning is that it will pass like the passing of clouds, so the adjective is used in place of the described noun and the complement in place of the complement to it. So the mountains will be removed from their places on the face of the earth, and will be gathered and moved as the clouds move, then they will be piled up and return to the earth as He said: And the mountains will be leveled with dust (al-Waqi’ah 56:5). (The making of God) according to Al-Khalil and Sibawayh is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, because when He, the Almighty, said: And it will pass like the passing of clouds, it indicates that He made that with a making, and the accusative case is permissible for the purpose of enticement, meaning look at the making of God. So it is stopped on this at (the clouds) and it is not agreed upon with the advance The first is the predicate. It is permissible to raise it on the assumption that it is God’s creation. Who perfected everything means made it perfect. From this is the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): May God have mercy on whoever does a job and perfects it. Qatada said: Its meaning is he made everything good, and perfection is perfection. It is said: A man who is tasaqan, meaning he is skilled at things. Al-Azhari said: He made it permissible from Ibn Taqan, who is a man from Aad whose arrow never missed, so he was used as an example. It is said: He is more archer than Ibn Taqan, then it is said to every skilled person who is tasaqan. He is All-Aware of what you do with the ta’ as an address, as is the reading of the majority. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Hisham read it with the ya’.
27:89: The Almighty said: Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them said: The good deed is There is no god but God. Abu Ma'shar said: Ibrahim Abraham used to swear by God, there is no god but Him, and he did not exclude that the good deed is There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Ali ibn al-Haysin ibn Ali may God be pleased with them said: A man was consoled, and whenever he was alone in a place, he would say: There is no god but God alone, with no partner for Him. While he was in the land of the Romans, in a rough and barren land, he raised his voice and said: There is no god but God alone, with no partner for Him. A man came out to him on a horse wearing white clothes and said to him: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, this is the word about which God the Almighty said: Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it. Abu Dharr narrated that he said: I said: O Messenger of God, advise me. He said: Fear God, and if you do a bad deed, then follow it with a good deed that will erase it. She said: O Messenger of God, is There is no god but God among the good deeds? He said: Among the best of good deeds. In another narration, he said: Yes, it is the best of good deeds. Al-Bayhaqi mentioned this. Qatada said: Whoever brings a good deed with sincerity and monotheism. It was also said: Performing all of the obligatory duties. I said: If he says There is no god but God in its true form and as it should be - as explained previously in Surah Ibrahim - then he has come with monotheism, sincerity and abundance. Then for him is better than it. Ibn Abbas said: That is, goodness from it has reached him. Mujahid said: It was also said: For him is the beautiful reward, which is Paradise. Better is not for preference. Ikrimah and Ibn Jurayj said: As for him having better than it, meaning from faith, then no, because there is nothing better than someone who says There is no god but God, but he has better than it. It was also said: Then for him is better than it is for preference, meaning the reward of God is better than the deeds, words and remembrance of the servant. Likewise, the pleasure of God is better for the servant than the deeds of the servant, as said by Ibn Abbas. It was also said: This goes back to multiplication, because God the Most High gives him ten for one, and for faith in a short period of time the eternal reward, as said by Muhammad ibn Ka’b, and according to Ar-Rahman ibn Zayd. And they will be safe from the terror of that Day. Asim, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read the terror of that Day with the addition. Abu Ubaid said: I like this better because it is the more general of the two interpretations, that is, security from all the terrors of that Day. If he says from the terror of that Day, it becomes as if it is a terror without a terror without a terror. Al-Qushayri said: It was read from the terror with the tanween, then it was said that it means a single terror, as he said, The greatest terror will not grieve them (Al-Anbiya’: 103). It was also said that it means a large number because it is a verbal noun and a verbal noun is suitable for a large number. I said: Therefore, the two readings have the same meaning. Al-Mahdawi said: Whoever reads (فزعَم يوميض) with the tanween, the word (يوميض) is in the accusative case with the verbal noun which is (فزعة). It is permissible for it to be an adjective forفزعand to be related to something omitted, because verbal nouns are described by time nouns and described by them. It is permissible for it to be related to the active participle which is َأموand the addition is based on expansion in circumstances. Whoever deletes the tanween and opens the meem, it is in the accusative case because it is a time adverbial, and the i’rab in the time adverbial is not established, so when it is added to something that is not established or inflected, it is in the accusative case. Sibawayh recited: While people are distracted by their most important affairs, the greedy person is like a thief.
27:90: The Almighty said: And whoever brings evil meaning polytheism, as stated by Ibn Abbas, Al-Nakha'i, Abu Hurairah, Mujahid, Qays ibn Sa'd, and Al-Hasan. This is the consensus of the people of interpretation that the good deed is there is no god but God and that the evil deed is polytheism in this verse. Then their faces will be thrown into the Fire. Ibn Abbas said: It was thrown. Ad-Dahhak said: It was cast down. It is said, He turned the vessel upside down, meaning, He turned it upside down. The intransitive form of this is he turned it upside down. This rarely occurs in Arabic speech. Will you be recompensed? meaning, it will be said to them, Will you be recompensed? It may also be from the words of God, or it may be from the words of the angels, Except for what you used to do, meaning, except for the recompense for your deeds.
27:91: The Almighty said: I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, who has made it sacred. He means Mecca, which God has made sacred, i.e., He has made it a safe sanctuary, in which no blood shall be shed, no one shall be wronged, no game shall be hunted, and no trees shall be cut down, as has been explained previously in more than one place. Ibn Abbas read: which He has made sacred as an adjective for the city. The reading of the group is alludhi who which is in the accusative case as an adjective for Lord. If it had been with the definite article, you would have said al-muharramha. If it had been an adjective for the city, you would have said al-muharramha huwa. It is necessary to make the pronoun with the definite article clear, because the verb is directed at someone other than the one to whom it belongs. If you say whom He has made sacred, you would argue that you should say huwa whom He has made sacred, and to Him belongs everything, creation and dominion. And I have been commanded to be among the Muslims, i.e., among those who oppose His command and believe in His Oneness.
27:92: The Most High said: And that I recite the Qur'an meaning, my command is to recite the Qur'an, that is, to read it. So whoever is guided will have the reward of his guidance. And whoever goes astray then I have nothing upon me except the conveyance. This was abrogated by the verse on fighting. An-Nahhas said: (And that I recite) is in the accusative case with the letter an. Al-Farra' said: In one of the two readings, it is (And that I recite), and he claimed that it is in the position of a command, and that is why the waw was deleted from it. An-Nahhas said: We do not know of anyone who recited this reading, and it contradicts all the copies of the Qur'an.
27:93: The Almighty says: And say, 'Praise be to God,' meaning for His blessings and for guiding us. He will show you His signs, meaning in yourselves and in others, as He says: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves. (Fussilat 41:53) and you will recognize them, meaning the evidence of His power and oneness in yourselves, in the heavens, and on the earth. Similar to His statement: And on the earth are signs for those of certainty * And in yourselves, so will you not see? (al-Dhariyat 51:20-21). And your Lord is not unaware of what you do. The people of Medina, the people of Ash-Sham, and Hafs from Asim read it with the ta' as a direct address, because of His statement: He will show you His signs, and you will recognize them, so the speech is in a consistent manner. The rest read it with the ya' as if referring to what preceded it. So whoever is guided, so he informed about that sign. The surah is complete. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds, and may God bless our Master Muhammad, his family, and his companions and grant them peace.
28:1: All of it is Meccan according to Al-Hasan and Ata'. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said that it was revealed between Mecca and Medina, except for one verse that was revealed between Mecca and Medina. Ibn Salam said that it was revealed during the migration of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Medina. It is the verse in which God the Almighty says: Indeed, He who enjoined upon you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a place of return. Muqatil said: It contains from Medina the verse: Those to whom We gave the Scripture until His saying: We seek not the ignorant. It is thirty-eight verses. The Almighty’s saying: Ta, Seen, Meem. We have already discussed this.
28:2: The Almighty said: These are the verses of the clear Book. (Those) is in the nominative case meaning this, those, and (verses) is a substitute for it. It is also permissible for it to be in the accusative case with (we recite) and (verses) is also a substitute for it, and you put it in the accusative case as you say: I hit Zayd. And (Al-Mubeen) means the one who makes clear his blessing and goodness, and the one who makes clear the truth and falsehood, and the lawful from the unlawful, and the stories of the prophets, and the prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is said: the thing became clear and evident, meaning it became apparent.
28:3: The Almighty said: We recite to you, [O Muhammad], from the report of Moses and Pharaoh, in truth, for a people who believe. He mentioned the story of Moses, peace be upon him, Pharaoh, and Korah, and provided evidence against the polytheists of Quraysh, and explained that Korah's kinship to Moses did not benefit him despite his disbelief, and likewise the kinship of Quraysh to Muhammad. He explained that Pharaoh was arrogant and haughty on earth, and that was part of his disbelief, so let him avoid arrogance on earth, as well as being arrogant with his wealth, and these are from the conduct of Pharaoh and Korah. We recite to you means Gabriel recited to you by Our command from the report of Moses and Pharaoh meaning from their story. From is for some, and From the story is a mute word. We recite to you means We recite to you some of its story, like the Almighty's saying: It grows with oil (al-Mu’minun 23:20). The meaning of with truth means with the truth in which there is no doubt or falsehood. For a people who believe means those who believe in the Qur’an and know that it is from God. As for those who do not believe, they do not believe that it is true.
28:4: The Almighty said: Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself in the land meaning he was arrogant and tyrannical, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi. Qatada said: He exalted himself in his soul from the worship of his Lord through his disbelief and claimed divinity. It was also said: Through his kingdom and authority, so he became exalted from the carving of his hand. (in the land) meaning the land of Egypt. And he made its people sects meaning groups and classes in service. Al-A’sha said: A town whose Tigris River is terrifying to the point that you see it seeking Shiites. He oppressed a group of them meaning from the Children of Israel. "He slaughtered their sons and kept their women alive. Indeed, he was of the corrupters." This was discussed previously in Surat Al-Baqarah when He said, They subjected you to the worst torment, slaughtering your sons (al-Baqarah 2:49). This is because the priests told him: A child will be born among the Children of Israel at whose hands your salt will be lost, or the astrologers told him that, or he saw a dream that was interpreted in this way. Al-Zajjaj said: It is amazing how foolish he was, he did not realize that if a priest tells the truth, killing will be of no benefit, and if he lies, there is no point in kissing. It was also said: He divided them into factions, so he mocked each group of the Children of Israel for a separate matter. Indeed, he was of the corrupters meaning on earth through knowledge, sins, and tyranny.
28:5: The Almighty said: And We desired to bestow a favor upon those who were oppressed in the land. That is, to be generous to them and bestow favors. This is a story that has already been told. And make them leaders. Ibn Abbas said: Leaders in goodness. Mujahid: Callers to goodness. Qatada: Governors and kings. His evidence is the Almighty’s statement: And made you kings. (al-Ma’idah 5:20) I said: This is more knowledgeable, for the king is an imam who is followed and emulated. And We will make them heirs to Pharaoh’s kingdom, so they will inherit his kingdom, and the Copts will inhabit your lands. This is the meaning of the Almighty’s saying: And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience (al-A’raf 7:137).
28:6: The Almighty says: And We will establish them in the land meaning We will make them able to control the land and its people until they take control of it, meaning the land of Ash-Sham and Egypt. And We will show Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers meaning We want to see Pharaoh. Al-A'mash, Yahya, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it as (and sees) with a ya' as a triliteral verb from ra'a Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers in the nominative case because it is the subject. The rest read we see with a damma on the noon and a kasra on the ra' as a quadriliteral verb from ara yaree, and it is in line with the sentence because before it is (and We want) and after it is (and We will establish). Pharaoh and Haman and their soldiers are in the accusative case because the verb occurs. Al-Farra’ permitted the word wa-yari Fir’awn with a damma on the ya’, a kasra on the ra’, and a fatha on the ya’, meaning and God will show Fir’awn what they were wary of. This is because they were informed that their destruction would be at the hands of a man from the Children of Israel, so they were fearful of them. So God showed them what they were wary of. Qatada said: A fortune teller of Fir’awn’s – and the fortune teller and the astrologer – said that a child will be born this year who will take away your kingdom. So Fir’awn ordered the killing of the children that year. It has been mentioned previously.
28:7: God the Almighty says: And We inspired the mother of Moses, saying, 'Suckle him.' The meaning of revelation and its dreams has already been mentioned. There is disagreement about this aspect of Moses' mother. A group said: It was a word in her sleep. Qatadah said: It was inspiration. A group said: It was an angel appearing to her. Muqatil said: Gabriel came to her with that. Based on this, it is a revelation of information, not inspiration. All agree that she was not a prophetess, but rather the angel was sent to her in the manner of an angel speaking to a bald person, a leper, or a blind person in the well-known hadith, narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, which we have already mentioned in Surat al-Bara'ah. Other than that, what has been narrated about angels speaking to people without prophethood. She greeted Imran ibn Husayn, so he was not a prophet. Her name was Ayarkha, and it was also said Ayya Khat, according to what al-Suhayli mentioned. Al-Tha'labi said: Moses' mother was Lawha bint Hand ibn Lawi ibn Ya'qub. That I breastfeed him. Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz read it: That I breastfeed him, with a kasra on the noon and an alif wasl. He deleted the hamza of I breastfeed for ease, then he broke the noon because of the meeting of two sukoon letters. Mujahid said: The revelation regarding breastfeeding was before birth. Another said: After it. Al-Suddi said: When Moses' mother gave birth to Moses, she was commanded to breastfeed him immediately after birth and to do with him what is mentioned in the verse, because the fear occurred immediately after birth. Ibn Jurayj said: She was commanded to breastfeed him for four months in an orchard, and if she feared that he would cry out - because her milk would not be enough - she would do this to him. The first is more apparent, but the second is supported by the statement: And when you fear for him idha for the future. It is narrated that she made a chest for him from the desert and covered it with pitch from the inside, and placed Moses in it and threw him into the Nile in Egypt. The story of this has already been mentioned in Ta-Ha. Ibn Abbas said: When the Children of Israel multiplied in Egypt, They oppressed the people and learned of their sins, so God sent the Copts against them, and they subjected them to terrible torture, until God saved them through Moses. Wahb said: I was informed that Pharaoh slaughtered seventy thousand newborns in pursuit of Moses, and it is said: ninety thousand. It is narrated that when she approached and the labor pains struck her, and one of the midwives in charge of the pregnant women of the Children of Israel was with her, she said: May your love benefit me today. So she treated her, and when he fell to the ground, a light between his eyes astonished her, and every joint of her trembled, and his love entered her heart. Then she said: I did not come to you except to kill your newborn and inform Pharaoh, but I have found for your son a love I have never found the like of, so protect him. When she went out, she came to Pharaoh’s spies, wrapped him in a rag and placed him in a blazing oven. She did not know what to do because her mind was lost. They searched but found nothing, so they left and she did not know where he was. She heard his crying from the oven, and God had made the fire cool and safe for him. God the Almighty said: And do not fear. There are two interpretations: One: Do not fear for him drowning, as stated by Ibn Zayd. The second: Do not fear for him being lost, as stated by Yahya ibn Salam. And do not grieve. There are also two interpretations: One: Do not grieve for his separation, as stated by Ibn Zayd. The second: Do not grieve that he will be killed, as stated by Yahya ibn Salam. It was said that she put him in a coffin, the length of which was five spans and its width five spans, and she put the key with the coffin and threw it into the sea after breastfeeding him for four months. Others said: Three months. Others said: Eight months, and in the narration of Al-Kalbi: It was narrated that when the carpenter finished preparing the coffin, he went to Pharaoh with report of it, so he sent someone to take it, but God blinded his eyes and his heart so he did not know the way, and he was certain that he was the child whom Pharaoh feared, so he believed from that time, and he is the believer of the family of Arawn. This was mentioned by Al-Mawardi. Ibn Abbas said: When he disappeared from her, Satan made her regret it and she said to herself: If he were slaughtered in my presence so I could shroud him and cover him up, that would be more beloved to me than throwing him into the sea. Then God Almighty said: Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers, meaning to the people of Egypt. Al-Asma’i narrated that he heard a Bedouin girl chanting and saying: I ask God to forgive me for all my sins. I accepted a person who was not his wife. Like a gazelle lying softly in its dhow, and it was midnight and I did not reach it, so I said: God told you, how eloquent you are! She said: Is this considered eloquence when God Almighty says: And We inspired the mother of Moses, saying, ‘Suckle him’ (al-Ma’idah 14:1-15). So He combined in one verse two commands, two prohibitions, two pieces of report and two glad tidings.
28:8: The Almighty said: So Pharaoh’s family picked him up so that he would become to them an enemy and a grief. Since picking him up would lead to him being to them an enemy and a grief, the lam in so that he would be is the lam of consequence and the lam of becoming, because they only took him so that he would be to them a delight, but the consequence of that was that he would become to them an enemy and a grief. So this is the case with the money, as the poet said: And for the fates, every wet nurse raises us, and our homes are built for the destruction of time. Another said: For death, parents become their children, just as homes are built for the destruction of time. The consequence of a building is destruction, even if it is something that is currently rejoiced over. Picking up is finding something without seeking or wanting it. The Arabs say about what they found without seeking or wanting it: I picked it up, picking it up. And I found so-and-so picking it up. The rajaz poet said: And a spring of water I gathered And from it is the lost property. And it has been mentioned in the rulings in Surat Yusuf, sufficiently. Al-A’mash, Yahya, Al-Mufaddal, Hamza, Al-Kisa’i and Khalaf read: and sadness with a damma on the ha’ and a sukoon on the za’. The rest read it with a fatha on both of them, and Abu Ubaid chose it. Abu Hatim said that it is emphasized. They are two languages, like ‘ad’ and ‘ad’, ‘saqm’ and ‘isqam’, and ‘rushd’ and ‘rushd’. Indeed, Pharaoh and Haman and his minister was from the Copts. And their soldiers were sinners meaning disobedient, polytheistic and sinful.
28:9: God the Almighty said: "And the wife of Pharaoh said, 'A comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him.'" It is narrated that Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, saw the ark floating in the sea, so she ordered it to be brought to her and opened. She saw a little boy in it, and she took pity on him and loved him. She said to Pharaoh, A comfort of the eye for me and for you. That is, he is the comfort of the eye for me and for you. So comfort is the predicate of an implied subject, as stated by Al-Kisa'i. Al-Nahhas said: There is another far-fetched interpretation of this, mentioned by Abu Ishaq. He said: It is in the nominative case with the subject and predicate do not kill him. It is only added later because the meaning becomes that he is known to be the comfort of the eye. It is permissible for the meaning to be: If he is the comfort of the eye for me and for you, then do not kill him. It was said that the discussion ended with the statement and for you. Al-Nahhas said: The evidence for this is that in the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: And the wife of Pharaoh said, "Do not kill him. A comfort of the eye for me and for you." It is permissible to put the accusative in the sense of do not kill the apple of my eye and yours. And she said, Do not kill him, and she did not say do not kill him, so she was addressing Pharaoh as tyrants are addressed, and as they speak about themselves. It was also said that she said, Do not kill him, for God brought him from another land and he was not from the Children of Israel. Perhaps he will benefit us so we may attain good from him or we may adopt him as a son. And she could not bear children, so she asked Pharaoh for Moses as a gift, and he gave him to her. And when Pharaoh saw the vision and told it to his priests and scholars—as mentioned above—they said to him, A boy from the Children of Israel will corrupt your kingdom. So the Children of Israel began to slaughter children, and he saw that this would cut off their lineage, so he returned to slaughtering one year and keeping alive the next. Aaron was born in the year of keeping alive, and Moses was born in the year of slaughter. God Almighty says: And they do not perceive. This is the beginning of a statement from God Almighty, meaning that they do not perceive that their destruction is due to him. It was also said that this is from the woman’s statement, meaning that the Children of Israel do not know that we picked him up, and they do not perceive anything except that he is our son. The commentators differed as to the time when Pharaoh’s wife said, A comfort to me and you. One group said: That was when he picked up the Ark, after she informed Pharaoh about it, and when she informed him, he quickly understood that it was from the Children of Israel, and that it was intended to save him from being slaughtered, so he said: Bring me the two slaughtered ones. His wife said what he mentioned, and Pharaoh said: But not for me. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If Pharaoh had said yes, he would have believed in Moses and he would have been a comfort to his eyes. Al-Suddi said: “Rather, she raised him until he matured, and Pharaoh saw in him chivalry and thought he was from the Children of Israel and took him in his hand. Moses reached out his hand and plucked Pharaoh’s beard, and he then intended to slaughter him. Then she addressed him with this, and tested it for him with the ruby and the ember, so his tongue was burned and he tied the knot, as mentioned above in Ta Ha. Al-Farra’ said: I heard Muhammad bin Marwan who was called Al-Suddi narrating on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Rather, she said, “A comfort of the eye for me and for you, not,” then she said, You kill him. Al-Farra’ said: This is a mistake. Ibn Al-Anbari said: It was ruled a mistake because it was like that, You kill him with the letter nun, because it is a future verb in the nominative case until the accusative or the jussive enters it, so the letter nun in it is a sign of the nominative. Al-Farra’ said: What strengthened you in rejecting it is the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, And the wife of Pharaoh said, “Do not kill him, a comfort of the eye for me and for you, by bringing forward do not kill him.
28:10: God the Almighty said: And the heart of Moses' mother became empty. Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Imran Al-Jawni, and Abu Ubaidah said: Empty means devoid of the remembrance of everything in this world except the remembrance of Moses. Al-Hasan, Ibn Ishaq, and Ibn Zayd also said: Empty is from the revelation that was sent to her when she was commanded to throw him into the sea.
