And do not fear, nor grieve, and the covenant that He made with her that He would bring him back and make him one of the messengers. Then Satan said to her: O mother of Moses, you hated that Pharaoh would kill Moses, so you drowned him! Then she heard that her son had fallen into Pharaoh's hand, so the enormity of the affliction made her forget what had been God's covenant with her. Abu Ubaidah said: Empty means averse. Al-Kisa'i: forgetful and oblivious. It was said: Desperate. Narrated by Saeed bin Jubair bin Al-Qasim from Malik: It is the loss of reason. The meaning is that when she heard that he had fallen into the hands of Pharaoh, her mind went blank from extreme panic and astonishment. Similar to this is the saying of God the Almighty: And their hearts are empty (Ibrahim 14:43), meaning they are hollow and have no minds, as mentioned previously in Surah Ibrahim. This is because the hearts are the seat of the minds. Do you not see the saying of God the Almighty: So that they will have hearts by which to reason (al-Hajj 22:46). This is indicated by the reading of those who read: in fear. An-Nahhas is the most correct of these first sayings, and the one they said is more knowledgeable about the Book of God the Almighty. So if he was empty of everything except the mention of Moses, then he is empty of revelation. Abu Ubaidah’s saying empty of worry is an ugly mistake, because after it is She would have almost disclosed it, had We not strengthened her heart. Narrated Saeed bin Jubair from Ibn Abbas who said: She almost said, and his two sons, and Fadalah bin Ubaid Al-Ansari may God be pleased with him, Muhammad bin Al-Sameeq, Abu Al-Aaliyah and Ibn Muhaisin read: Faza’an with Fa and Ain from Faza’, meaning afraid that he would be killed. Ibn Abbas: Qar’an with Qaf, Ra and Ain, which refers to the reading of the group Farghan, and that is why the head that has no hair is called Aqra’, because it is devoid of hair. Qatrib narrated that some of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) read: Farghan with Fa, Ra and Ghain without Alif, and it is like saying Hadran and Batilan, it is said: Their blood is between them Fargh, meaning wasted, and the meaning is that her heart was empty and gone and she was left without a heart due to the severity of what befell her. Regarding the statement of God the Almighty: And the morning there are two views, one of them is: that she threw him at night and her heart became empty during the day. Second: She threw it during the day, and the meaning of became is became, as the poet said: The Caliphs carried out the righteous order and the city became Al-Walid's If she almost means that she almost did. When the pronoun was deleted, the nun was made sukoon. It is the lightened in and that is why the lam was included in to reveal it meaning to make his matter apparent, from to appear if it appeared. Ibn Abbas said: that is, she cried out when she threw him: Oh my son! As-Suddi said: She almost said when she carried him to breastfeed and nurse him, He is my son. It was said that when he grew up, she heard people saying, Moses, son of Pharaoh, so it was difficult for her and her chest tightened, and she almost said, He is my son. It was said that the ha in to him refers to the revelation, meaning: If she was to reveal the revelation that We revealed to her, then We would return it to her. The first is more apparent. Ibn Mas'ud said: She almost said, I am his mother. Al-Farra' said: She almost revealed his name because of the tightness in her chest. Had We not strengthened her heart, Qatada said: With faith. As-Suddi said: With protection. It was also said: With patience. And the connection to the heart: Inspiring patience. So that you may be among the believers meaning among those who believe in God’s promise when He said to her: Indeed, We will return it to you. And He said: So that you may disclose it and did not say: So that you may disclose it, because adjectival letters may be added to speech. You say: I took the rope or with the rope. And it was said: meaning that you may disclose the statement about it.
28:11: God the Almighty said: And she said to his sister, 'Follow him.' That is, the mother of Moses said to the sister of Moses: Follow his footsteps until you know about him. Her name was Maryam bint Imran, and her name matched the name of Maryam, the mother of Jesus, peace be upon him, as mentioned by Al-Suhayli and Al-Tha'labi. Al-Mawardi reported on the authority of Al-Dahhak that her name was Kalthama. Al-Suhayli said: Kalthum. This came in a hadith narrated by Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said to Khadija: Do you know that God married me to you in Paradise, Maryam bint Imran, Kulthum, the sister of Moses, and Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh? She said: Has God told you this? He said: Yes. She said: With comfort and children. "Then she saw him from afar," meaning from afar, as said by Mujahid. And from this comes the word "al-ajbi." The poet said: Do not deprive me of what I have attained due to my impurity, for I am a stranger among the domes. Its origin is from a place called janb. Ibn Abbas said: an janb meaning from one side. An-Nu’man ibn Salim read: an janb meaning from a direction. It was also said: from longing. Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’ said that it is a language of Judham, they say: I janbt ilaik meaning I longed for him. It was also said: an janb meaning from her distancing herself from him, so they did not know that she was his mother by any means. Qatada said: She kept looking at him from one side as if she did not want him. He used to read: an janb with a fatha on the jim and a sukoon on the noon. And they did not perceive that she was his sister because she was walking on the seashore until she saw that they had taken him.
28:12: The Almighty said: And We had forbidden him wet nurses before meaning before the arrival of his mother and sister. And places is the plural of wet nurse. And whoever says wet nurses, it is the plural of wet nurse, and mifa'al is for multiplication, and the ha' is not added to it to differentiate between the feminine and the masculine because it is not a verb, but whoever says wet nurse, he added the ha' to emphasize, as it is said matarabah. Ibn Abbas said: A wet nurse should not be brought to him so that he can kiss her. This is a prohibition, a prevention, not a prohibition, a law. Imru' al-Qais said: She tried to defeat me, but I told her to stop. I am a man whose defeat is forbidden to you. Any impossibility. When his sister saw that, she said: Shall I direct you to a household who will take care of him for you? [The verse]. They said to her when she said: And they are sincere to him. How do you know? Perhaps you know his family? She said: No, but they are keen on pleasing the king and desire his wet nurse. Al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj said: It was said to her when she said: And they are sincere to him, “You know the family of this boy, so direct us to them.” She said: I meant them as sincere to the king. So she directed them to Moses’ mother, so she went to her with their orders and brought her. The boy was in Pharaoh’s hand, nursing him out of compassion and crying, asking to be nursed. Pharaoh handed him over to her. When he found the boy in Pharaoh’s hand, nursing him out of compassion and crying, asking to be nursed, he handed him over to her. When he found the boy, the breast of his slave girl, he accepted her breast. Ibn Zayd said: They were suspicious when she said that, so she said: And they are sincere to the king. And Qaybil said: When she said: Shall I direct you to a household that will take care of him for you? and they were asking too much in asking for a wet nurse whose breast he would accept, so they said: Who is she? She said: Who is she? She said: My mother. It was said: Does she have milk? She said: Yes! The milk of Aaron - and he was born in a year in which boys were not killed - so they said: You have spoken the truth, by God. And they are sincere to him meaning they have compassion and sincere advice. It was narrated that it was said to the mother of Moses when he breastfed from her: How did he breastfeed from you and not from anyone else? She said: I am a woman with good husbands and good milk. No boy is born without him breastfeeding from me. Abu Omar al-Jawni said: Pharaoh used to give Moses’ mother a dinar every day. Al-Zamakhshi said: If you ask how it was permissible for her to take payment for breastfeeding her son, I say: She did not take it as payment for breastfeeding, but it was war property that she took in a permissible manner.
28:13: The Almighty says: So We returned him to his mother meaning, We returned him, and God had softened the enemy's heart towards him, and We fulfilled the promise to her. That her eye might be refreshed meaning with her son. And not grieve meaning with the separation from her son. And that she might know that the promise of God is true meaning, so that she might know that it would happen, for she knew that his return to her would happen. But most of them do not know meaning, most of Pharaoh's people did not know, meaning, they were unaware of the estimation and secret of the decree. It was said: meaning, most people do not know that the promise of God in everything He promised is true.
28:14: God the Almighty says: And when he reached his full strength and was mature, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. We have already discussed maturity in Al-An'am. Rabi'ah and Malik's statement that it is maturity is the first thing said about it, because God the Almighty says: Until they reach the age of marriage (An-Nisa': 6). That is the beginning of maturity, and its maximum is thirty-four years, and this is the statement of Sufyan Ath-Thawri. Ibn Abbas said: He reached forty years. Wisdom is wisdom before prophethood. It was also said: Understanding of religion. Its explanation was previously mentioned in Al-Baqarah and other surahs. Knowledge is understanding according to As-Suddi. It was also said: Prophethood. Mujahid said: Understanding. Muhammad ibn Ishaq: That is, knowledge of what is in his religion and the religion of his fathers. He had nine children from the Children of Israel who would listen to him, follow his example, and gather around him, and this was before prophethood. And thus do We reward the doers of good. That is, just as We rewarded the mother of Moses when she submitted to God’s command, and threw her son into the sea and believed in God’s promise, so We returned her son to her with gifts and a glance while she was safe, then We gave him reason, wisdom, and prophethood. And thus do We reward every doer of good.
28:15: God the Almighty says: And he entered the city while its people were unaware. It was said: When Moses, peace be upon him, realized the truth of his religion, he criticized the people of Pharaoh, and that became widespread, so they frightened him, so he spoke to them. He would not enter Pharaoh's city except in fear and in secret. Al-Suddi said: At the time of this story, Moses was in the habit of being attached to Pharaoh, and he used to ride mounts until he was called Moses, son of Pharaoh. One day, Pharaoh rode and went to a city in Egypt called Memphis - Muqatil said it was two farsakhs from Egypt - then Moses learned that Pharaoh had stopped, so he rode his servant and reached that city at noon, which is the time of heedlessness, as Ibn Abbas said. He also said: It is between the evening and night prayers. Ibn Ishaqf said: Rather, the city of Egypt itself, and Moses, at that time, had openly opposed Pharaoh, and criticized their worship of Pharaoh and idols. One day, he entered the city of Kafr Nabwan while its people were unaware. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatada said: It was noon when people were asleep. Ibn Zayd said: Pharaoh had rebelled against Moses and expelled him from the city, and he was absent from it for years. He came while the people were heedless, having forgotten his command and after their covenant with him. That was the day of Ubayd. Ad-Dahhak said: He asked to enter the city when its people were heedless, so he entered when he knew that they were heeding him. One of them killed a man before he was ordered to kill him, so he asked forgiveness of his Lord and He forgave him. It is said in speech: He entered the city when its people were heedless, but it is not said: At a time when its people were heedless. So the word 'ala was used in this verse because what is meant is heedlessness, so this is like saying: I came heedlessly, or if you like, you can say: I came at a time of heedlessness. And so is the verse. And he found therein two men fighting, one of them from his party The meaning is, if someone looked at it, he would say: This is from his party, meaning from the Children of Israel, and this is from his enemy meaning from the words of Pharaoh. Then one of his party sought his aid meaning he asked for his support and assistance. This is also what He said in the verse after it: And behold, he who had sought his aid the day before sought his aid meaning he sought his aid against another Copt. He aided him because aid for the oppressed is a duty in all religions and is imposed in all laws. Qatada said: The Copt wanted to force the Israelite to carry firewood to Pharaoh's kitchen, but he refused, so he sought aid from Moses. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He was a baker for Pharaoh. So Moses prodded him Qatada said: With his staff. Mujahid said: With his hand, meaning he pushed him. The prodding, the lakaz, and allahu akbar have the same meaning, which is to strike with the whole hand together like knotting seventy-three. Ibn Mas'ud read: fa-lakazhu. It was said: The prodding is to the beard and the prodding is to the heart. Al-Tha'labi related that in the copy of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud it is fa-nakazhu with the letter nun but the meaning is the same. Al-Jawhari said on the authority of Abu Ubaidah: Lakaz is hitting the chest with the plural. Abu Zaid said: On the entire body. Lahaz is hitting with the plural hand on the chest like Lakaz, also on the authority of Abu Ubaidah. Abu Zaid said: It is in the plural on the lahazim and the neck, and the man is malhaz with a kasra on the m. Al-Asma’i said: Nakazahu, meaning he hit and pushed him. Al-Kisa’i: Nahazahu is like Nakazahu and Wakozahu, meaning he hit him and pushed him. And Lahda Lahdan means he pushed him to humiliate him so he is Malhud, and likewise Lahdakahu. Tarflah said, criticizing a man: He is slow to respond to the caller, quick to commit adultery, and submissive, according to the consensus of men. Any cannon, but it is emphasized for the large number. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: “He guided me - meaning the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him - to a direction that hurt me.” Narrated by Muslim. Moses, peace be upon him, did that without intending to kill him, but rather intending to push him away, so his soul was in him. This is the meaning of: He finished him off. And everything that you have done and finished with, you have finished with it. He said: He bit him, so Ashja' killed him. He said, 'This is from the work of Satan,' meaning from his temptation. Al-Hasan said, It was not permissible to kill an unbeliever at that time, because it was a time when he had ceased fighting. "Indeed, he is a clear, misleading enemy," one report after another.
28:16: God the Almighty says: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me.' So He forgave him. Moses, peace be upon him, regretted that prod which had caused his soul to perish. His regret led him to submit to his Lord and seek forgiveness for his sin. Qatada said: By God, he knew the way out, so he sought forgiveness. Then the Prophet, peace be upon him, continued to count that against himself, even though he knew that he had been forgiven, to the point that on the Day of Resurrection he would say: 'I killed a soul I was not commanded to kill.' He only counted it against himself as a sin. He said, 'I have wronged myself, so forgive me.' This is because it is not permissible for a prophet to kill until he is commanded to do so. Also, prophets fear things that others do not fear. Al-Naqqash said: He did not kill him intentionally, intending to kill, but rather he poked him with a prod to avert his wrongdoing. It has also been said that this happened before he became a prophet. Ka'b said: He was twelve years old at that time, and his killing was still a mistake, as a nudge or a shove usually does not kill. Muslim narrated on the authority of Salim ibn Abdullah that he said: O people of Iraq! I do not ask you about minor sins, but I make you commit major sins! I heard Abu Abdullah ibn Umar say: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: The trial will come from here - and he pointed with his hand towards the east - “from where the horns of Satan rise, and you will strike the necks of one another. Moses killed only those of Pharaoh’s family by mistake, so God the Almighty said: “And you killed a soul, but We saved you from distress and tested you with a trial” (Ta-Ha: 40).”
28:17: The Almighty said: He said, ‘My Lord, because You have bestowed favor upon me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals.’ There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: He said, ‘My Lord, because You have bestowed favor upon me’ meaning of knowledge, wisdom, and monotheism, I will never be a supporter of the criminals meaning a helper to the disbelievers. Al-Qushayri said: He did not say because You have bestowed favor upon me of forgiveness, because this was before the revelation, and he did not know that God had forgiven him for that murder. Al-Mawardi said: Because You have bestowed favor upon me has two interpretations: One: of forgiveness, and this is what Al-Mahdawi and Al-Tha’labi mentioned. Al-Mahdawi said: Because You have bestowed favor upon me of forgiveness, so you did not punish me. The second interpretation: of guidance. I said: His statement, So He forgave him indicates forgiveness, and God knows best. Al-Zamakhshari said: God's statement, Because You have bestowed Your favor upon me, may be an oath with an omitted answer, meaning, I swear by Your favor upon me of forgiveness that I may repent, "for I will never be a supporter of the criminals. Or it may be an appeal, as if he said, My Lord, forgive me by the right of what You have bestowed upon me of forgiveness, for if You protect me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals." By supporting the criminals, what is meant is either the company of Pharaoh and joining his ranks, and increasing his numbers, as he used to ride with him like a son with his father, and he was called the son of Pharaoh, or by supporting someone whose support leads to crime and sin, like the support of the Israelite that led to killing whom it was not permissible for him to kill. It was said: He meant that even if I do wrong in this, I will kill the one I was not commanded to do, so I will not abandon supporting the Muslims against the criminals. Based on this, the Israelite was a believer, and supporting the believer is obligatory in all religious laws. It was said in some narrations: That Israelite was an unbeliever, and he was only told that he was one of his followers because he was an Israelite and did not want to agree with him in religion. Based on this, he regretted helping an unbeliever against an unbeliever, so he said, I will never be an ally of the unbelievers after this. It was also said: This is not a statement, but rather a supplication, meaning, I will never be an ally after this, meaning, O Lord, do not make me an ally of the criminals. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is, O God, I will never be an ally of the criminals. He claimed that this statement of his was the statement of Ibn Abbas. Al-Nahhas said: It is more appropriate for it to have the meaning of a statement and more closely resembles the flow of speech, as one says, I will not disobey you because you have bestowed favor upon me. This is the true statement of Ibn Abbas, not what Al-Farra’ narrated, because Ibn Abbas said, He did not make an exception, so he was tested the next day. An exception is not made in a supplication, one does not say, O God, forgive me if you wish. The most amazing thing is that Al-Farra’ narrated that this Abbas was, and then narrated his statement. I said: This meaning has already been summarized and explained in Surat An-Naml, and that it is a statement, not a supplication. Ibn Abbas did not make an exception, so he was tested with it again, meaning he did not say, I will not be, God willing. This is similar to His statement, And do not incline toward those who do wrong. (Hud 11:113) Second: Salamah ibn Nabit said: Abdurrahman ibn Muslim sent to Ad-Dahhak the stipend of the people of Bukhara and said: Give them. He said: Excuse me. He kept on asking him to excuse him until he did. Then he was asked: What is wrong with you giving them when you do not pay them anything? He said: Excuse me. He kept asking him to excuse him until he did. Then he was asked: What is wrong with you giving them when you do not pay them anything? He said: I do not like to help the oppressors in any of their affairs. Ubayd ibn Al-Walid Al-Wasafi said: I said to Ata ibn Abi Rabah: I have someone who holds his pen, but he only calculates what comes in and goes out, and he has children; if he did not do that, he would be in need and in debt. He said: Who is the head? I said: Khalid bin Abdullah Al-Qasri said: Have you not read what the righteous servant said: My Lord, because You have bestowed favor upon me, I will never be a supporter of the criminals. Ibn Abbas said: He did not make an exception, so he was tested with it a second time, and God aided him. So, your brother should not aid them, for God will aid him. Ata’ said: It is not permissible for anyone to aid injustice, or write for it, or accompany it, and that if he does any of that, then he has become an aid to the oppressors. In the hadith: “A crier will call out on the Day of Resurrection, ‘Where are the oppressors and those like them, and the helpers of the oppressors?’ Even the one who finds their inkwell or sharpens their pen will be gathered in an iron coffin and thrown into Hellfire.” It is narrated from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, that he said: “Whoever walks with an oppressed person to help him in his oppression, God will make his feet firm on the path on the Day of Resurrection, the day when feet will slip. And whoever walks with an oppressor to help him in his oppression, God will make his feet slip on the path on the day when feet will slip.” And in the hadith: Whoever walks with an oppressor has committed a crime. Walking with an oppressor is not a crime unless he walks with him to help him, because he has committed what God Almighty has forbidden in His saying, the Most High: And do not cooperate in sin and aggression (Al-Ma’id: 2).
28:18: The Almighty says: So he began in the city, fearful. It has been mentioned in Taha and other verses that the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them, are afraid, in response to those who said that, and that fear does not contradict knowledge of God or trust in Him. It was said: He began fearing that the soul would be taken by it. It was also said: Fearing that his people would accuse him. It was also said: Fearing God Almighty. Waiting. Saeed bin Jubair said: He looks around in fear. And Qaybil: Waiting for the request, waiting for what people would say. Qatada said: Waiting means waiting for the request. And it was said: He went out to find out the report, and no one knew about the killing of the Copt except the Israelite. And became may mean he became, meaning when he was killed he became fearful. And it may mean that he entered in the morning, meaning the morning of the day following his day. And fearing is accusative as the predicate of became, and if you wish it is in the state, and the adverbial phrase is in the place of the predicate. And behold, he whom he had sought for help the day before cried out to him. That is, behold, his Israelite companion whom he had saved the day before was fighting another Copt whom he wanted to subjugate. And crying out to him is seeking help. It comes from screaming, because the one seeking help screams and makes a noise in requesting aid. He said: Whenever a screaming, terrified person came to us, our screams would fill the air with tears. It was said: This Israelite Al-Mustansir Al-Samaritan was mistreated by Pharaoh’s cook, so he carried firewood to the kitchen. Al-Qushayri mentioned it. Alladhi is in the nominative case, and istathquhu is in the predicate position. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as a state. Amrs refers to the day before your day, and it is built on the kasra not because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. If the definite article or the addition enters it, it is possible, so it is parsed with the nominative and the fatha according to most grammarians. Some of them build it with the definite article and the lam. Sibawayh and others narrated that some Arabs treat Amrs as something indeclinable in the nominative case only, and sometimes a poet is forced to do this in the genitive and accusative cases. The poet said: I saw something amazing yesterday So he lowered the subject with madh and the good language is the nominative, so he made ays in the lowering its course in the nominative according to the second language. Moses said to him, ‘Indeed, you are clearly a heretic.’ A heretic is someone who is a loser, meaning because you are fighting someone you cannot stand. It was also said: “One who is misguided among misguidance. Yesterday I killed a man because of you, and today you are calling me to another.” A heretic is a fa’il from aghawa to incite, and it means maghwā, and it is like al-jaba’ to ache and al-‘alaym to hurt in the sense of the painful and the hurtful. It was also said: Al-ghawi means the seducer. Meaning, you are a heretic in fighting someone whose evil you cannot repel from yourself. Al-Hasan said: He only said to the Copt, You are clearly a heretic in mocking this Israelite and he wanted to attack him. It is said: batash to beat, yabatash to beat, and yabatash to beat. The dammah is more correct because it is an intransitive verb. He said, ‘O Moses, do you want to kill me?’ Ibn Jarir said: Moses wanted to hit the Copt, but the Israelite thought that he wanted him because he spoke harshly to him. He said, Do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? The Copt heard what he said and spread it out. It was also said that the Israelite wanted to hit the Copt, but Moses forbade him. The Copt was afraid of him, so he said, Do you want to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? “If you want” means whatever you want. Unless you are a tyrant on earth meaning a fighter. Ikrimah and Ash-Sha’bi said: A person is not a tyrant until he kills two people unjustly.
28:19: God Almighty says: And you do not want to be among the reformers. That is, among those who reconcile between people.
28:20: God the Almighty says: And there came a man Most of the people of interpretation said: This man is Ezekiel bin Saburah, the believer of the family of Pharaoh, and he was the cousin of Pharaoh, mentioned by Al-Tha'labi. It was also said: Talut, mentioned by Al-Sahli. Al-Mahdawi said on the authority of Qatadah: Shimon, the believer of the family of Pharaoh. It was also said: Shamaan. Al-Daraqutni said: Shamaan is not known with the miraculous shin except as the believer of the family of Pharaoh. It was narrated that Pharaoh ordered the killing of Moses, but that man preceded him with the report, so He said, O Moses, indeed the chiefs are taking counsel over you meaning they are consulting about killing you because of the Copt whom you killed the day before. It was also said: they are giving orders to one another. Al-Azhari said: The people took counsel and conspired, meaning they ordered one another, similar to his saying: And consult among yourselves in what is right (al-Talaq 65:6). Al-Nimr bin Talib said: I see that people have created a habit and in every incident they are ordered Then go out, for I am among your sincere advisers. So he went out from it, fearful and waiting.
28:21: God Almighty said: He said, ‘My Lord, save me from the wrongdoing people.’ It was said: The tyrant who does whatever he wants, whether it be beating or killing, is unjust, does not consider the consequences, and does not repel evil with what is better. It was also said: The arrogant one who does not humble himself before God’s command.
28:22: The Almighty said: And when he turned toward Madyan, he said, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way.’ When Moses, peace be upon him, went out fleeing alone and in fear, with nothing with him of provisions, a mount, or shoes, towards Madyan because of the relationship between him and them, because Madyan was from the descendants of Abraham, and Moses was from the descendants of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham. He saw his condition and his lack of knowledge of the road, and his lack of provisions and other things, he entrusted his matter to God Almighty by saying: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way. This is the condition of someone in need. I said: It was narrated that he ate tree leaves, and before he could reach them, his sandals fell off. Abu Malik said: Pharaoh was looking for him and told them about a goat. He said to Moses: Follow me, so he followed him and Moses guided him to the road. It was said that he gave him the goat and it became his staff. It was narrated that he took his staff to herd sheep from Madyan. This is more common and more correct. Muqatil and Al-Suddi said: God sent Gabriel to him, and God knows best. There were eight days between Madyan and Egypt, as Ibn Jubayr and the people said. The king of Madyan was not for Pharaoh.
28:23: It contains twenty-four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And when he came to the water of Madyan, Moses, peace be upon him, walked until he came to the water of Madyan, meaning he reached it. His coming to the water means he reached it, not that he entered it. The word coming may mean entering the place where he came to drink, or it may mean looking at it and reaching it even if he did not enter. So Moses’ coming to this water was by reaching it, and from this is the saying of Zuhair: When they reached the blue water, they put down the sticks of the campers. These meanings were mentioned previously in His statement: There is not one of you but will pass over it (Maryam 19:71). Madyan is not declined as it is a well-known town. The poet said: The monks of Madyan, if they saw you, would come down and protect you from the peaks of the mountains. It was said: A tribe from the descendants of Madyan bin Ibrahim, and it was mentioned previously in Al-A’raf. The nation: a large group. And they water means their livestock. And from below them means a direction towards which he came, so he reached the two women before he reached the nation, and he found them repelling, and its meaning is they prevent and restrain, from which his saying, peace be upon him: So let men be repelled from my Cistern. And in some copies of the Qur’an: Two restraining women repelling. It is said: Dhāda yadhūd if he restrained. And Dhādat means I detained something. The poet said: I spend the night at the door of rhymes as if I am fending off a swarm of wild beasts with it. That is, they drive away, restrain, and prevent. Ibn Salam: They prevent their sheep so that they do not mix with the sheep of the people. The object was omitted, either to confuse the addressee, or because he knows enough. Ibn Abasa said: They drive their sheep away from the water for fear of the strong waterers. Qatada: They drive people away from their sheep. An-Nahhas said: The first is more appropriate, because after it is: They said, ‘We do not water until the shepherds depart.’ If they had been driving people away from their sheep, they would not have told us the reason for delaying their watering until the shepherds depart. When Moses, peace be upon him, saw that from them, He said, ‘What is the matter with you?’ That is, what is your business? Ru’bah said: Oh wonder what is wrong with him and yours Ibn Atiyyah: The use of the question in speeches is only in the case of a calamity, or a persecution, or someone who is pitied, or someone who commits an evil act, so it is as if he is in general evil, so they informed him of their story, and that their father is a very old man, so the meaning is: he is not able, due to his weakness, to take care of his sheep, and that they, due to their weakness and lack of energy, are not able to compete with the strong, and that their habit is to wait until the people leave the water and it is empty, and then they return. Ibn Amir and Abu Amr read: issur from sadr, which is the opposite of ward, meaning the shepherds return. And the rest (issued with a damma on the ya from asdara, meaning until they send their livestock from their watering place. And the shepherds are the plural of shepherd, Musal, merchant and merchants, and companion and companions. A group said: The wells were uncovered, and the crowd of people prevented them, so when Moses wanted to water them, the people crowded and overpowered them to the water until he watered, so one of them described it as force. A group said: They were following their leftovers in the cisterns, so if they found some in the basin, that was their watering place, and if there was no leftover, their sheep would be thirsty, so Moses felt sorry for them, so he went to a well that was covered and the people were watering from another one, and its bucket could only be lifted by seven, said Ibn Zayd. Ibn Jurayj: ten. Ibn Abbas: thirty. Al-Zajjaj: forty, so he lifted it. And he watered for the two women, so it is about lifting the rock and its bank by force. And it was said: Their well was one, and that the rock was lifted from it after the water carriers had separated. If it was the habit of the two women to drink leftovers. Omar bin Maymun narrated on the authority of Omar bin Al-Khattab that he said: When the shepherds were looking for water, they covered the well with a rock that could only be removed by ten men. Then Moses came, removed it, and drew water from one well, so they did not need anyone else, so he gave them water to drink. Second: If it is said, “How could it be permissible for the Prophet of God, who was Shuaib, peace be upon him, to be content with his daughters watering the livestock?” He is told, “That is not forbidden, and religion does not prohibit it. As for chivalry, people differ in other matters, and custom is mixed in this regard. The Arabs’ conditions in this regard are different from those of the non-Arabs, and the way of the Bedouins is different from that of the urbanites, especially if the situation is one of necessity.”
28:24: The Almighty says: Then he turned to the shade to the shade of a tamarisk tree, as Ibn Mas'ud said. He was asked about what he would eat, saying: Indeed, I am, for whatever good you send down to me, in need. He had not tasted food for seven days, and his stomach was stuck to his back, so he offered a supplication without making a clear request. This is how all the commentators narrated that he asked in this statement for what he would eat. Good can mean food, as in this verse, and it can mean ownership, as in the statement: If he leaves something good (Al-Baqarah 2:180) and his statement: And indeed, he is intense in his love of good (Al-'Adiyat 51:8). It can mean strength, as in the statement: Are they good or the people of Tubba'? It can also mean worship, as in the statement: And We inspired them to do good deeds (Al-Anbiya' 21:73). Ibn Abbas said: He had been overcome by hunger, and his color had turned green from eating the greens in his stomach, and he was the most honored of creation in the sight of God. It is narrated that he did not reach Madyan before his feet fell off. This is significant and indicates the insignificance of this world in the sight of God. Abu Bakr ibn Tahir said about His statement, Indeed, I am, for whatever good You may send down to me, needy, meaning that for whatever good You may send down to me, I am needy until You make me independent of anyone other than You. I said: What the commentators mentioned is gone, because God Almighty enriched him through Shuaib.
28:25: Fourth: The Almighty said: Then one of them came to him walking shyly. This statement is an abbreviation indicated by the apparent meaning, Ibn Ishaq estimated it as: So they went to their father quickly, as it was their custom to be slow in watering their flocks. They told him what had happened to the man who had watered their flocks. So he ordered the elder of his two daughters - or it was said the younger - to summon him for himself. She came according to what is in this verse. Amr ibn Maymun said: She was not a fast-moving woman, neither a traveler nor a visitor. It was said: She came to him covering her face with the sleeve of her armor, as said by Umar ibn al-Khattab. It was narrated that the name of one of them was Leah and the other was Sepphoris, the daughters of Jethro, and Jethro is Shu'ayb, peace be upon him. It was also said: The son of Abu Shu'ayb, and that Shu'ayb had already died. Most people believe that they are the two daughters of Shu`ayb, peace be upon him, and this is the apparent meaning of the Qur’an. God the Almighty said: And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu`ayb (Al-A`raf: 85) This is how it is in Surah Al-A`raf. In Surah Ash-Shu`ara’: The companions of the thicket denied the messengers, * When Shu`ayb said to them (Ash-Shu`ara’: 176-177). Qatadah said: God the Almighty sent Shu`ayb to the companions of the thicket and the companions of Madyan. The disagreement over his father’s name has already been mentioned in Al-A`raf. It was narrated that when the message came to Moses, peace be upon him, he said: I will follow her. There were three miles between Moses and her father, and a wind blew and she folded her shirt and described her buttocks. Moses was embarrassed to look at her, so he said: Go back behind me and guide me to the road with your voice. It was also said that Moses initially said: “Stand behind me, for I am a Hebrew man who does not look at women’s backsides. Guide me to the right or the left.” This is the reason for her describing him as trustworthy, as Ibn Abbas said. Moses reached a preacher and told him his story from beginning to end. The preacher comforted him by saying, "Do not fear. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people." Midian was outside Pharaoh's kingdom. Food was brought to him, but Moses said, "I will not eat. We are a family who will not sell our religion for the earth full of gold." Shu'aib said, "This is not in exchange for watering the land. It is my custom and the custom of my fathers to welcome guests and feed people." So Moses ate.
28:26: Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: One of the two women said, ‘O my father, hire him.’ This is evidence that hiring was a known and permissible practice for them, and it was the same in every religion. It is a natural necessity and a benefit of mixing between people, contrary to the original, as he was deaf to hearing it.
28:27: The Almighty says: Indeed, I want to marry you verse. This includes the guardian offering his daughter to the man, and this is an established Sunnah. Salih Madyan offered his daughter to Salih Bani Israel, and Umar ibn al-Khattab offered his daughter Hafsa to Abu Bakr and Uthman, and the gifted woman offered herself to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It is good for a man to offer his female guardian, or a woman herself, to a righteous man, following the example of the righteous predecessors. Ibn Umar said: When Hafsa became a widow, Umar said to Uthman: If you wish, I will marry you to Hafsa bint Umar. The hadith is only narrated by al-Bukhari. Seventh: This verse is evidence that the guardian has no share in marriage, because a righteous debtor took charge of it, and this is what the jurists of the regions said. Abu Hanifa disagreed with this, as has been mentioned previously. Eighth: This verse indicates that a father may marry off his adult virgin daughter without consulting her. Malik said the same and used this verse as evidence. This is his apparent bias in this regard. His citing it as evidence indicates that he relied on the Isra’iliyyat, as mentioned above. Al-Shafi’i and many scholars also said the same as Malik on this issue. Abu Hanifah said: If a young girl reaches puberty, no one should marry her off without her consent, because she has reached the age of accountability. However, if she is still young, then he may marry her off without her consent, because she does not have permission and consent that would change the matter.
28:28: Ninth: The followers of Al-Shafi'i used his statement, I want to marry you, as evidence that marriage is conditional upon the use of the words marriage and marriage. This is what Rabi'ah, Abu Thawr, Abu Ubaid, Dawud, and Malik said, although they differed from him. Our scholars said, in the well-known view, The marriage contract is valid even if the word is used. Abu Hanifa said, It is valid even if the word is used, which implies that you are permanently married. As for the Shafi'is, they have no proof in this verse because it was legislated before us, and they do not see it as proof for anything, according to the well-known view among them. As for Abu Hanifa and his followers, Al-Thawri, and Al-Hasan ibn Hayy, they said, "The marriage contract is valid with the wording of a gift or otherwise if it has been witnessed, because divorce occurs explicitly or implicitly. They said, "The same applies to marriage." They said: What the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) specified was the exclusion of the private parts from compensation, not marriage by the word gift. Ibn al-Qasim followed them and said: If he gave his daughter as a gift intending to marry her off, I do not remember anything from Malik regarding this, but in my opinion it is permissible like a sale. Abu Umar said: The correct view is that a marriage contract cannot be concluded by the word gift, just as a gift of any property cannot be concluded by the word marriage. Also, marriage requires explicit mention for the annulment to occur, and it is the opposite of divorce, so how can it be compared to it? They have agreed that marriage cannot be concluded by saying, I have made it lawful for you and so too by a gift. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, You have made their private parts lawful for you by the word of God, meaning the Quran. There is no mention of a marriage contract by the word gift in the Quran, rather it contains marriage and wedlock. Permitting marriage by the word gift nullifies some of the special features of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Tenth: The Almighty’s saying: One of these two daughters of mine indicates that it is an offer, not a contract, because if it were a contract, we would specify the one being contracted with, because even though the scholars have differed about the permissibility of a sale if he said: I have sold you one of these two slaves of mine for such-and-such a price, they have agreed that this is not permissible in marriage, because it is an option, and some of the option does not attach to marriage. Eleventh: Al-Makki said: This verse contains specific characteristics regarding marriage, including that it does not specify a wife, nor does it set a starting period, and it makes the dowry a rental, and it allows for income in cash. I said: These are four issues included in the eleventh issue. The first: Of the four issues of specification, our scholars said: As for specification, it seems that it was in the second stage of bargaining, but the matter was presented in general terms and specified later. It has been said that he married him to Saffuriya, who was the younger. It is narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: “If you are asked which of the two terms Moses fulfilled, say the better and more fulfilling of the two. And if you are asked which of the two women he married, say the younger, who was the one who came to succeed him and who said: ‘O my father, hire him. Indeed, the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy.’” It has been said that the wisdom in marrying the younger to him before the older, even though the older was more in need of men, was that he expected that he would be drawn to her, because he saw her in his message and he agreed with her in his inclination to her father with her. If he had presented the older to him, he might have made him feel he had chosen something while he was harboring something else. Other reports have been said, and God knows best. In some reports, it is said that he married the older, as narrated by Al-Qushayri. Second: As for mentioning the beginning of the period, there is nothing in the verse that requires its omission, rather it is silent. So either they made it clear, otherwise it is from the beginning of the time of the contract. Third: As for marriage by hiring, it is clear from the verse, and it is a matter that our Shari’ah has established, and it occurred in the hadith of the one who knew nothing but some of the Qur’an, narrated by the Imams, and in some of its chains of transmission: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him, ‘What have you memorized of the Qur’an?’ He said, ‘Surat al-Baqarah and the one following it.’ He said, ‘Then teach her twenty verses and she is your wife.’” The scholars differed on this issue and had three opinions: Malik disliked it, Ibn al-Qasim forbade it, and Ibn Habib permitted it, and it is the opinion of al-Shafi’i and his companions. They said, It is permissible for a free man to benefit from his wife as a dowry, such as sewing, building, or teaching the Qur’an. Abu Hanifah said, It is not valid. He permitted him to marry her if his slave served her for a year, or let her live in his house for a year, because the slave and the house are property, and her service itself is not property. Abu al-Hasan al-Karkhi said: The marriage contract using the word hiring is permissible, as God the Almighty says: Then give them their due compensation (An-Nisa’: 24). Abu Bakr al-Razi said: It is not valid because the hiring contract is a temporary contract, while the marriage contract is perpetual, so they are incompatible. Ibn al-Qasim said: It is annulled before the divorce and continued after it. Asbagh said: If he brought something in cash, then there is a difference of opinion about it, but if the marriage contract is not concluded, then that is more serious. If he abandons it, it continues in any case, based on the story of Shu’ayb. This was stated by Malik, Ibn al-Mawaz, and Ashhab. This verse was relied upon by all of the earlier and later scholars in this case. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: This verse includes marriage on the basis of hiring, and the contract is valid. It is disliked to make the hiring contract a dowry, and the dowry should be money, as God the Almighty said: That you seek chaste women with your wealth (An-Nisa’: 24). This is the opinion of all our companions. Fourth: As for his statement: And he consummated the marriage but did not pay the dowry, people differed on this. Did he consummate the marriage when the contract was made or when he traveled? If it was when the contract was made, then what did he pay? Our scholars have prohibited consummation until he pays the dowry, even if it is a quarter of a dinar. This was stated by Ibn al-Qasim. If he consummated the marriage before paying the dowry, then it is valid, because the later scholars among our companions said: Paying the dowry early or part of it is recommended. However, since the dowry was the care of sheep, he paid the dowry to begin the service. If he consummated the marriage while he traveled, then a long wait for the marriage is permissible, even if it is for a lifetime, without any conditions. However, if there is a condition, then it is not permissible unless the purpose is valid, such as preparing for consummation or waiting for the wife to be ready for consummation if she is young. This was stated by our scholars. Twelfth: In this verse there is a permissible combination of leasing and marriage. Our scholars have differed on this with three opinions: First: Abu Zayd said in eight: It is disliked from the beginning, but if it occurs, it is valid. Second: Malik and Ibn al-Qasim said in the well-known view: It is not permissible and is annulled before and after consummation, due to the difference in their objectives like all other disparate contracts. Third: Ashhab and Asbagh permitted it. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is the correct view and the verse indicates it. Malik said: Marriage is most similar to sales, so what is the difference between leasing and selling, or between selling and marriage? Branch: If her sincerity is teaching permissible poetry, it is valid. Al-Muzani said: This is like what the poet said. The servant says: My benefit, my wealth, and the fear of God are the best things I have gained. If he taught her poetry that contained satire or obscenity, it would be as if he had given her wine or pork. Thirteenth: The Almighty’s statement: On condition that you hire me for eight years. Service is mentioned in general terms. Malik said that it is permissible and should be interpreted according to custom, so there is no need to mention service in naming the worker. This is the apparent meaning of the story of Moses, as he mentioned an absolute contract of employment. Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i said: It is not permissible unless he is named because he is unknown. Al-Bukhari included a chapter on the one who hired a worker, specifying the period of time but not the work, based on the Almighty’s statement: On condition that you hire me for eight years. Al-Muhallab said: It is not as he translated it, because the work for them was known, such as watering, plowing, herding, and similar work in the desert, which was the profession of the people there. This is customary, even if the person doing the work or their amounts were not specified. For example, if someone says to him: You will plow such-and-such a year and herd such-and-such a year, then this is only according to what is customary in desert service. What is not permissible in the case of a group is that the period of time is unknown, and the work is unknown and not customary, so it is not permissible until it is known. Ibn al-Arabi said: The commentators mentioned that he was appointed to tend sheep, but this was not narrated through a sound chain of transmission. However, they said that Salih Madyan had no work other than tending sheep, so what was known about his condition was sufficient to be appointed to serve there. Fourteenth: The scholars unanimously agreed that it is permissible for a shepherd to hire a shepherd for a specific period of time, for a specific wage, to tend a limited number of sheep. If the number is a specific number, our scholars have detailed this. Ibn al-Qasim said: It is not permissible unless a stipulation is made regarding a replacement if he dies. This is a very weak narration. Salih Madyan hired Musa to look after his sheep, and he saw them without stipulating a replacement. If the sheep were unspecified and not named or specified, it is permissible according to our scholars. Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi’i said: It is not permissible due to its ignorance. Our scholars relied on custom, as we mentioned earlier, and that a shepherd should be given according to his ability to bear the burden. Some of our scholars added that it is not permissible even if the hirer knows his ability to bear the burden. This is correct, as Salih Madyan knew the ability of Musa to lift the stone. Fifteenth: Malik said: The shepherd is not liable, and he is believed in what is lost or stolen, because he is trustworthy like an agent. Al-Bukhari titled: “Chapter: If the shepherd or the agent sees a sheep dying or something spoiled, then he should repair what he fears spoiling.” He cited the hadith of Ibn Ka’b ibn Malik from his father: They had sheep grazing in Sal’. A slave girl of ours saw one of our sheep dying, so she broke a stone and slaughtered it. He said to them: “Do not eat until I ask the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him)” - or he sent someone to ask him - and he asked the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) - or he sent someone to him - and he ordered that it be eaten. Ubaydullah said: I like that it is a slave girl and that it was slaughtered. Al-Muhallab said: “It is part of the jurisprudence that the shepherd and the agent should be believed in what they are entrusted with until evidence of treachery and lying is shown against them. This is the fear of Malik and the group.” Ibn al-Qasim said: If someone fears death for a sheep and slaughters it, he is not liable, but he is believed if he brings it slaughtered. Another said: He is liable until he explains what he said. Sixteenth: Ibn Qasim and Ashab differed regarding whether a shepherd has intercourse with female livestock without the permission of their owners and they die. Ibn Qasim said: He is not liable, because the growth is part of the improvement and growth of the property. Ashab said: He is liable. The statement of Ibn Qasim is more similar to the evidence of the hadith of Tha’b, and that he is not liable for what he lost due to his own efforts, if he is a righteous person and someone who is known to care for the property. However, if he is a person of immorality and corruption and the owner of the property wants to compensate him, he does so, because it is not believed that he saw the death of the sheep because of what is known of his immorality. Seventeenth: It has not been reported what Moses' wages were, but Yahya ibn Salam narrated that the salih of Madyan ordered Moses to give birth to a calf that was different in colour from its mother. Then God revealed to Moses, "Throw your staff among them and they will all give birth to calves that were different in colour from their mothers. Others than Yahya said, Rather, he ordered Moses to give birth to a calf that was different in colour from its mothers." Al-Qushayri mentioned that when Shu`ayb hired Moses, he said to him: Enter such-and-such a house and take one of the sticks that are in the house. Moses took out a stick, which Adam had taken out of Paradise, and the prophets had inherited until it reached Shu`ayb. Shu`ayb ordered him to throw it in the house and take another stick. He entered and took out that stick, and did so seven times, but none of them fell into his hand except that one. Shu`ayb knew that he had a matter to answer for. When morning came, he said to him: “Drive the sheep to the fork in the road, and take from your right, as there is not much grass there, and do not take from your left, as there is much grass there and a large dragon that does not accept livestock.” So he drove the livestock to the fork in the road, and they took to the left, and he was unable to control them. Moses slept, and the dragon came out. The stick rose, and its two branches became iron, and it fought the dragon until it killed him. It returned to Moses, peace be upon him. When Moses awoke, he saw the stick stained with blood, and the dragon killed. He returned to Shu`ayb in the evening. Shu`ayb was blind, and he touched the sheep, and behold, the traces of fertility. He looked at her and asked her about the story. She told him, and Shu`ayb was overjoyed and said, Whatever livestock gives birth to this year is bicolored. So all the young goats that year were bicolored. Shu`ayb knew that Moses had a high standing with God. `Uyaynah ibn Hain narrated that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Moses rewarded himself for his satiety and chastity. Shu`ayb said to him, You may have from them i.e., from the offspring of his sheep whatever is born that is bicolored and does not contain azouz, fushush, kamoosh, dhuboob, or tha`ool. Al-Harawi said, “Shaal `azouz is the weeping one, derived from `azaaz, which means hard ground. A sheep has become azooz. A fashush is the one whose milk is fluffed up without milking, due to the width of the urethra. Similar to it are futuh and tharwar. Among their proverbs is, “I will expel your anger and pride from your head.” It is also said, The water skin will fluff up if it releases wind. And from it is the hadith: The devil blows between the buttocks of one of you until he thinks he has relieved himself meaning he blows weakly. And the small udder is the one with the small udder, also it is the kameesh, it is called that because of the shrinkage of its udder, and from it it is said: a man with the kameesh of the izar. And the kashood is like the kamoosh. And the narrow urethral opening is the lizard, the milking is done by squeezing it hard. And the fox is the ewe that has an extra teat, which is the tha’l. And the tha’l is the extra tooth, and that extra is the ra’ul. And a man is ath’al. And the tha’l has a narrow outlet for milk. Al-Harawi said that the interpretation of Qalb Lun in the hadith is that it came in a color other than that of its mothers. Eighteenth: Renting for unknown consideration is not permissible, because the birth of the sheep is unknown. There are fertile lands where the birth of the sheep is known with certainty, as well as their number of days and the health of their young, such as Egypt and other lands. However, this is not permissible in our Sharia, because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade uncertainty, and forbade the dams and the malaqīh. The dams are what is in the wombs of females, and the malaqīh is what is in the loins of males. Contrary to that, the poet said: Inoculated in the belly of a pregnant fang This was explained in Surat Al-Hijr. Rashid bin Muammar permitted hiring sheep for a third or a quarter. Ibn Sirin and Ata’ said: The cloth is woven for a share of it, and Ahmad said the same. Nineteenth: Compatibility in marriage is considered. Scholars differed as to whether it relates to religion, wealth, lineage, or some combination of these. The correct view is that it is permissible for a freedman to marry Arab or Quraysh women, based on the words of God the Almighty: The most honorable of you in the sight of God is the most righteous of you. (al-Hujurat 49:13) Moses came to Salih of Madyan as a stranger, banished, afraid, alone, hungry, and naked. He married him to his daughter when he ascertained his religion and saw his condition, and he ignored everything else. We have presented this issue comprehensively, praise be to God. Al-Muwaffiyah twentieth: Some of them said: What Shuaib did was not a mention of the woman’s dowry, but rather it was a condition for himself based on what the Bedouins do. They would stipulate the dowry of their daughters and say: I have such and such for myself, and he delegated the dowry, and the marriage of delegation is permissible. Ibn al-Arabi said: What the Bedouins do is a gift and an increase in the dowry, and it is forbidden and not befitting of the prophets. As for if the guardian stipulates something for himself, the scholars differed regarding what the husband takes from his hand and does not enter the woman’s hand, with two opinions: One of them is that it is permissible and the other is that it is not permissible. What is correct in my opinion is the division, because the woman is either a virgin or previously married. If the woman has previously married, then it is permissible, because her marriage is in her hand, and the guardian only has the right to directly conclude the contract, and it is not forbidden to take compensation for it as the agent takes, and that is invalid. If it occurs, it is annulled before consummation and confirmed afterward according to the well-known narration. Praise be to God. Twenty-first: When he mentioned the condition and followed it with the voluntary act in the ten, each one of them was excluded according to its ruling, and the other was not included in the first, and the obligation and the voluntary act were not shared. Therefore, the agreed-upon conditions are written in contracts. Then it is said, He volunteered such-and-such, so the condition is carried out according to its path, and the voluntary act is according to its ruling, and the obligation is separated from the voluntary act. It was said: And from the wording of Sa’ib when in the wording of contracts, the marriage contract is that he married her to him more deserving than he married her to him, as will be explained in al-Ahzab. Shu’ayb made the eight years a condition, and left the tenth to chivalry. Twenty-second: The Almighty said: “He said, ‘That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, there will be no aggression against me.’” When Shuaib finished speaking, Moses, peace be upon him, confirmed it and repeated its meaning to ensure that the condition occurred in eight years. Whichever is an interrogative in the accusative case governed by I fulfilled, and the two terms is in the genitive case by adding any to them, and what is a relative clause for emphasis and to understand the meaning of the condition and its answer is there will be no aggression, and that aggression is in the accusative case governed by not. Ibn Kaysan said: What is in the genitive case by adding any to it, which is indefinite, and the two terms is a substitute for it. Likewise in His statement: Then by mercy from God (Al Imran 3:159), meaning mercy in place of what. Makki said: He was careful not to include anything superfluous in the Quran, and he would come up with a way to exclude it from being superfluous. Al-Hasan read: Whichever with the ya as a preposition. Ibn Masoud read: Which of the two terms is what you have fulfilled? The majority read: Adwan with a damma on the ‘ayn, and Abu Haywah with a kasra on it. The meaning is: I have no responsibility nor demand for more than that. Adwan is exceeding what is not required, and the arguments are the years. The poet said: Whose house is Qannah al-Hajar? Stronger than arguments and time. The singular is argument with a kasra on the ha. And God is witness over what we say. It was said: It is from the words of Moses. And it was said: It is from the words of the woman’s father. So the two righteous men, may God’s prayers be upon them, were satisfied with God as a witness against them and they did not witness anyone among creation. The scholars differed over the obligation of ishad in marriage, and it is: Twenty-third: There are two opinions: One of them is that it is not valid except with two witnesses. This is what Abu Hanifa and Al-Shafi’i said. Malik said that it is valid without witnesses because it is a contract of exchange, so witnessing is not required for it. What is required is that it be announced and stated clearly. The difference between marriage and fornication is the tambourine. This issue has been fully discussed in Surah Al-Baqarah. In Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Hurairah [on the authority of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him], “A man from the Children of Israel asked some of the Children of Israel to lend him a thousand dinars. He said, ‘Bring me witnesses so that I may witness them.’ He said, ‘God is sufficient as a witness.’ He said, ‘Bring me a guarantor.’ He said, ‘God is sufficient as a guarantor.’ He said, ‘You have spoken the truth.’ So he gave it to him.” He mentioned the hadith.
28:29: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And when Moses had fulfilled the term, Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: A Christian man asked me which of the two terms Moses had fulfilled. I said: I will not know until I go to the scholar of the Arabs and ask him – meaning Ibn Abbas – so I went to him and asked him, and he said: He fulfilled the most complete and most perfect of the two. I informed the Christians and he said: By God, this scholar has spoken the truth. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) asked Gabriel about that and he told him that he had fulfilled twenty years. At-Tabari narrated on the authority of Mujahid that he had fulfilled ten and ten after that. It was narrated by Al-Hakam ibn Abaan on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is weak. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And he traveled with his family. It was said: This is evidence that a man can take his family wherever he wants, because of the privilege of guardianship and the increase in status he has over them, unless he commits himself to something. The believers are bound by their conditions, and the conditions that are most deserving of being fulfilled are those by which you have made private parts lawful. Third: The Almighty’s saying: He perceived a fire from the side of the Mount The verse has been discussed previously Ta Ha. The word jadhura with a kasra on the jim is the reading of the common people, and Hamzah and Yahya have a damma, and Asim, As-Sulami, and Zayd ibn Hubaysh have a fatha. Al-Jawhari said: Jadhwa, Jadhwa, and Jadhwa are blazing embers, and the plural is Jadhan, Jadhan, and Jadhwa. Mujahid said about the Almighty’s saying: Or a spark of fire meaning a piece of embers, he said: It is in the language of all Arabs. Abu Ubaidah said: Jadhwa is like Jadmah, which is a thick piece of wood, whether there is fire at the end of it or not. Ibn Muqbil said: Layla's woodcutters began to seek her abundantly, without mooing or groaning. He said: He threw a burning ember at Qais, and its heat and flames were very intense.
28:30: The Almighty said: So when he came to it meaning the tree, he put its pronoun before it. He was called from the bank of the valley The first and second (from) indicate the beginning of the goal, meaning the call came to him from the bank of the valley from the tree. And (from the tree) is a substitute for his saying: (from the bank of the valley), a substitute of inclusion, because the tree was growing on the bank, and the bank of the valley and its shore are its side, and the plural is shatan and shores, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri. Al-Jawhari said: It is said the shore of the valleys and it is not plural. And a man walked on a bank and he walked on another bank. The right means on the right of Moses. It was said: on the right of the mountain. In the blessed spot Al-Ashab Al-Uqaili read: (in the spot) with the opening of the ba. Their saying baqa'an indicates a spot, just as it is said jafna and jafan. And whoever says baqa'a said baqa' like ghurfa and it was said: 'awsaj. And from it came his stick, as mentioned by Al-Zamakhshari. And it was said: jujube, and the jujube when it grows large is called gharqad. And in the hadith: It is from the tree of the Jews. So when Jesus descends and kills the Jews who were with the impostor, not one of them hides behind a tree except that it speaks and says, O Muslim, there is a Jew behind me, come and kill him. Except for the gharqad tree, for it is from the tree of the Jews and it does not speak. Narrated by Muslim. Al-Mahdawi said: “God the Most High spoke to Moses, peace be upon him, from above His throne and made him hear His words from the tree as He willed.” It is not permissible to describe God the Most High as moving, disappearing, or anything similar to that from the attributes of created beings. Abu Al-Ma’ali said: “The people of meaning and the people of truth say that whoever God the Most High has spoken to and has singled out with the highest rank and the ultimate goal, then he realizes His eternal and sanctified speech, free from any resemblance to letters, sounds, expressions, tones, or various languages. Just as God has singled out him with the stations of miracles, completed His blessings upon him, and granted him the vision of Him, he sees God the Most High, exalted from any resemblance to bodies or the laws of accidents. There is no equal to Him, the Most High, in His essence and attributes. The ummah is unanimously agreed that the Lord the Most High singled out Moses, peace be upon him, and other chosen angels with both of these qualities.” Professor Abu Ishaq said: The people of truth are agreed that God the Almighty created in Moses (peace be upon him) a meaning by which he understood His speech, and that he was the only one who heard it, and that He is capable of doing the same for all of His creation. They differed about our Prophet (peace be upon him) - did he hear the speech of God's camels on the night of the Isra', and whether Gabriel heard his speech? There are two opinions, one of which is the established transmission, and that is missing. They agreed that the creation heard him when the Quran was recited, meaning that they heard the expression by which they understood its meaning, without hearing it in person. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud ibn Kulab said: Moses (peace be upon him) understood the eternal speech of God from created sounds that God the Almighty established in some of the pools. Abu Al-Ali said: This is rejected, rather it is necessary that Moses (peace be upon him) was the only one who could perceive the speech of God the Almighty in a breach of custom, even if he (peace be upon him) had not said that, he was the only one who was able to speak to God. The Almighty Lord made him hear His Mighty Word and created for him essential knowledge, so that he knew that what he heard was the speech of God, and that the One who spoke to him and called to him was God, Lord of the Worlds. It is mentioned in the stories that Moses, peace be upon him, said: I heard the speech of my Lord with all my limbs, and I did not hear it from just one of my sides. This meaning has already been fully explained in (Al-Baqarah). O Moses (O Moses) is in the accusative case with the omission of the letter har meaning O Moses. Indeed, I am God, Lord of the worlds negates the lordship of anyone other than Him, glory be to Him. With these words, he became one of the chosen ones of God, the Almighty, and not one of His messengers, because he does not become a messenger except after being commanded to deliver the message, and the command to deliver it only came after these words.
28:31: The Almighty’s saying: And throw down your staff is in apposition to O Moses! This was discussed previously in An-Naml and Ta-Ha. Retreating is in the accusative case as a state, and so is the case with his saying: And did not return is also in the accusative case as a state. O Moses, come forward and do not fear. Wahb said: It was said to him, Go back to where you were. So he went back and wrapped his coat of arms around his hand. The angel said to him: Tell me, if God wills to afflict you with what you fear, will it benefit you to free your hand? They said: No, but I am weak and was created from a weak person. Then he uncovered his hand and put it in the mouth of the snake, and it returned to being a staff. Indeed, you are among those who are safe, meaning from what you fear.
28:32: The Almighty's saying: Put your hand into your bosom verse, the saying of and draw near to you from fear min is related to wali guardian, meaning turn away, retreating from fear. Hafs, As-Sulami, Isa ibn Umar, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read: min ar-rahab from fear with a fatha on the ra' and a sukoon on the ha'. Ibn Amir and the Kufians except Hafs read it with a damma on the ra' and a jazm on the ha'. The rest read it with a fatha on the ra' and the ha'. Abu Ubaid and Abu Ham preferred it, because of the Almighty's saying: And they call upon Us in hope and fear (Al-Anbiya': 90). All of these are dialects and it means fear. The meaning is that if your hand and its rays are destroyed, then put it in your bosom and return it to it, and it will return to how it was. It was also said that God commanded him to draw his hand to his chest so that the fear of the snake would leave him. On the authority of Mujahid and others, and Ad-Dahhak narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Ibn Abbas said: There is no one who is overcome by fear after Moses, peace be upon him, and then he puts his hand on his chest except that the fear goes away from him. It is narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, may God have mercy on him, that a scribe was writing in front of him, and a gust of wind slipped from him, so he was embarrassed and broken, so he stood up and struck the ground with his pen. Umar said to him: Take your pen and close your wing, and let your fear go away, for I have never heard it from anyone more than I heard it from myself. It was also said that the meaning is: Close your hand to your chest so that God may take away the fear in your chest. Moses was trembling with fear, either of the people of Pharaoh or of the snake. Closed wing means stillness, like the saying of God the Almighty: {And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy} (al-Isra’ 17:24) meaning gentleness. And likewise His saying: {And lower your wing to those who follow you of the believers} (Ash-Shu’ara’: 215) meaning be gentle with them. Al-Farra’ said: “By ‘wing’ he meant his stick. Some of the semantic experts said: ‘Rahab’ is the sleeve in the language of Himyar and Banu Hanifa. Muqatil said: A Bedouin woman brought me something while I was eating, so I filled my hand and pointed to her, and she said: ‘Here in my rahba’, meaning in my sleeve. Al-Asma’i said: I heard a Bedouin say to another: ‘Give me your rahba’. So I asked him about the rahba’ and he said: ‘The sleeve’. Based on this, its meaning would be to hold it close and take it out of the sleeve, because he took the stick and put it in his sleeve. His saying: ‘Put your hand in your pocket’ indicates that it is the right hand, because the pocket is on the left. Al-Qushayri mentioned it. I said: What they interpreted as putting the hand to the chest indicates that the pocket is located in the chest. This has been explained in Surat An-Nur. O Al-Zamakhshari, one of the innovations in interpretations is that the word “rahab” means sleeve in the Himyarite dialect, and that they say Give me from what is in your rahab. I wonder how it is linguistically correct! Has it been heard from trustworthy narrators whose Arabic is acceptable? Then I wonder how it is located in the verse, and how it is applied in detail like all other words of the revelation. On the night of the supplication, Moses, peace be upon him, was wearing nothing but a cloak with no ambush. Al-Qushayri said: His statement, And draw your wing towards you, means the hands, if we say he meant security from the terror of the snake. It was said, And draw your wing towards you, meaning roll up your sleeves and get ready to bear the burdens of the message. I said: Based on this, it was said: Indeed, you are among the secure ones, meaning among the messengers, based on the statement of God the Almighty: Indeed, in My presence the messengers do not fear. (al-Naml 27:10) Ibn Bahr said: According to this interpretation, he became a messenger with this statement. It was also said that he became a messenger with his statement: These two are proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs, and the pledge is the hand and the staff. Ibn Kathir read it with a shaddah on the noon, while the others lightened it. Abu ‘Amara narrated on the authority of Abu al-Fadl on the authority of Abu Bakr on the authority of Ibn Kathir, Fa-Dhanika without a light pronunciation and the ya’. Abu ‘Amr also said that the dialect of Hudhayl is: Fa-Dhanika without a light pronunciation and the ya’. The dialect of Quraysh is: Fa-Dhanika as Abu ‘Amr and Ibn Kathir read it. There are five explanations for this: It was said that the nun was doubled in place of the dropped alif in that which is the dual of the nominative dhal, which is nominative at the beginning, and the alif of dhal was deleted because the alif of the dual entered it, and no attention was paid to the meeting of two quiescent letters, because its original form was fadhanik, so the first alif was deleted in place of the doubled nun. It was also said that the doubled letter is for emphasis, just as they inserted the lam in that. Makki: It was said that whoever stressed it based it on the language of those who said that about the singular, so when he built it, he confirmed the lam after the nun of the dual, then he assimilated the lam into the nun according to the rule of assimilating the second into the first. The basic principle is that the first is always assimilated into the second, unless there is a reason for that, in which case the second is assimilated into the first. The reason that prevented assimilating the first into the second is that if he did that, a stressed lam would replace the nun that denotes the dual, and the wording of the dual would change, so the second was assimilated into the first for that reason, so it became a stressed nun. It was said that since that was incompatible, he confirmed the lam before the nun, then he assimilated the first into the second according to the principles of assimilation, so it became a stressed nun. It was said that it was stressed to differentiate it from the apparent one whose nun is dropped by addition, because dhan is not added. It was said that it is to differentiate between the established noun and it. And likewise the reason for stressing the nun in (al-ladhaani) and (hadhaan). Abu Amr said: Abu Amr singled out this letter for emphasis, not every dual of the same type, because of the paucity of its letters, so he read it with emphasis. Whoever reads (fa-dhanika) with a ya’ and a light nun, the original according to him is (fa-dhanika) with emphasis, so he replaced the second nun with a ya’ because of the dislike of doubling, just as they said: la amalihu in la amalhu, so they replaced the second laam with an alif. Whoever reads with a ya’ after the heavy nun, the reason is that he saturates the kasra of the nun, so the ya’ is born from it.
28:33: God Almighty said: He said, ‘My Lord, I have killed one of them, and I fear that they will kill me.’
28:34: The Almighty says: Then send him with me as a support meaning a helper, derived from the word aradtuhu meaning I aided him. Support is aid. The poet said: Haven't you seen that Asram was bad and the best of people were in heart and money? Copper and he ruined it and ruined it, meaning he helped it, and he left the hamza for ease. Nafi’ read it this way and it has the same meaning as the hamza. Al-Mahdawi said: It is possible that leaving the hamza is from their saying I know more about the hundred meaning he added to it, and it is as if the meaning is he sent him with me to increase my belief. Muslim ibn Jundub said this. And the poet recited the following saying: And dark-skinned, his heels were like the cores of reeds, his body was more than ten inches long. Thus, Al-Mawardi recited this verse: He has destroyed. Al-Ghaznawi and Al-Jawhari recited it in Al-Sahah, He has thrown, and he said: And the hard reed, and the reed is a dry date that crumbles in the mouth with a hard seed. He said, describing a spear: And brown. The verse. Al-Jawhari said: “The badness of something is bad, so it is bad, meaning corrupt.
