I ruined it, and I spoiled it, and I helped it also means I aided it. You say, I ruined it with my soul, meaning I was a cloak for it, which is a support. God the Almighty said: “Then send him with me as a support to support me.” An-Nahhas said: “And he narrated his badness: a cloak, and the plural of cloak is cloaks.” Asim and Hamza read: supports me in the nominative case, and the rest jazm, which is the choice of Abu Hatim in response to a supplication. Abu Ubaid chose to raise the subject to the state of the ha’ in (arsalahu), meaning he sent him a cloak confirming the state of confirmation, like his saying: Send down to us a table from the sky that will be (al-Ma’idah 5:114), meaning that it will be, a state that is diverted to the future. It is also possible that it is an attribute of his saying: (a cloak). Indeed, I fear that they will lie if I do not have a minister or helper, because they can hardly understand what I am saying.
28:35: So God Almighty said to him: We will strengthen you through your brother, meaning He will make you stronger through him. This is a metaphor, because the strength of the hand comes from the arm. Tarafa said: O Banu Labani, you are not in any hand but Me. A hand that has no support. It is said in a supplication for good: May God strengthen you. And in its opposite: May God weaken your arm. “And We will make for you both an authority” meaning an argument and proof. So that they will not reach you with harm with Our signs meaning that you will protect yourself from them with Our signs. It is permissible to stop at to you and for the speech to be inverted and postponed. It was said that the meaning is You and those who follow you will be the victors with Our signs. Al-Akhfash and Al-Tabari said this. Al-Mahdawi said: In this, the relative clause is presented before the relative pronoun, unless it is understood that you both will be victorious with Our signs, you and those who follow you will be the victors. And by signs he meant all of his miracles.
28:36: God Almighty says: So when Moses came to them with Our clear signs, meaning obvious and evident, they said, ‘This is nothing but invented magic,’ “a lie, fabricated magic, and we have never heard of this among our forefathers. It was said that these signs are what Moses used as rational arguments to prove monotheism. It was also said that they were his miracles.
28:37: The Almighty said: And Moses said The general reading is with the waw. Mujahid, Ibn Kathir and Ibn Mahsin read: (said) without the waw, and this is how it is in the mushaf of the people of Mecca. My Lord knows best who has brought guidance meaning right direction. From Him and to whom it will belong The Kufians except Asim read: will belong with the ya' and the rest with the ta'. This has been mentioned before. The final abode meaning the abode of recompense. It the ha' is a pronoun for the command and the matter. The wrongdoers will not succeed.
28:38: God the Almighty said: And Pharaoh said, ‘O eminent ones, I do not know of any god for you other than me.’ Ibn Abbas said: There were forty years between him and his saying, I am your highest lord (al-Nazi’at 79:24). The enemy of God lied, but rather knew that he had a Lord who created him and his people. If you ask them who created them, they will surely say, ‘God.’ (al-Zukhruf 43:87) He said: Then light a fire for me, O Haman, over the clay, meaning cook the bricks for me, according to Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him. Qatada said: He was the first to make bricks and build with them. When Pharaoh ordered his minister Haman to build the tower, Haman gathered workers—it was said that he was fifty thousand builders, in addition to his followers and hired servants—and ordered the bricks and plaster to be cooked, the wood to be sawn, and the nails to be driven in. They built and raised the building and erected it to a level that no building had reached since God created the heavens and the earth. The builder was unable to stand on its top, until God willed to test them in it. Al-Suddi narrated: Pharaoh climbed to the roof and threw his spear towards the sky, and it came back covered in blood. He said to him, I have killed Moses. It was narrated that Gabriel, peace be upon him, was sent by God Almighty when he said this, so he struck the tower with his wing and cut it into three pieces: one piece on Pharaoh’s army, killing a million of them, one piece in the sea, and one piece in the west, and everyone who worked in it perished. And God knows best about the consequences of that. And indeed, I think he is among the liars. Suspicion here is doubt, so he disbelieved based on doubt, because he saw proofs that would not be relied upon by a person of common sense.
28:39: God Almighty says: And he was arrogant meaning he was proud he and his soldiers meaning he refused to believe in Moses. On the earth without right meaning through aggression, meaning he had no argument to refute what Moses had brought.
28:40: God Almighty said: So We seized him and his soldiers, and they were two million six hundred thousand. Then We cast them into the sea, meaning We threw them into the salty sea. Qatada said: A sea beyond Egypt called Isaf in which God drowned them. Wahb and Al-Suddi said: The place where God drowned them is near Al-Qulzum and is called Bazhan Marirah, and it remains angry to this day. Muqatil said: It means the Nile River. This is weak, but the first is the more well-known. So see, O Muhammad, how was the end of the wrongdoers, meaning the end of their affair.
28:41: The Almighty says: And We made them leaders meaning We made them leaders who are followed in disbelief, so he will bear their burden and the burden of those who follow them, until their punishment is greater. It was said: God made the elite of his people leaders of the lowly among them, so they call to Hell. It was also said: Leaders who are followed by those who have lessons and are admonished by those who have insight. They call to the Fire meaning to the deeds of the people of Hell, and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be aided.
28:42: The Almighty said: And We pursued them in this world with a curse meaning We ordered the servants to curse them, so whoever mentioned them, we cursed them. It was also said: meaning We obligated the curse on them, meaning the servant from good. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will be among the detested meaning among the destroyed and hated. This was said by Ibn Kaysan and Abu Ubaidah. Ibn Abbas said: Those with deformed creation, with black faces and blue eyes. It was said: Among the worshipped. It is said: May God make him ugly, meaning He removed him from all good. And qabbahu and qabbahu means He made him ugly. Abu Amr said: I made his face ugly with the light vowel meaning I made it ugly. The poet said: May God make ugly all the knuckles, and may God make ugly the jerboa, and may God make ugly Dharma. And the word Day was used in the place of in this world and dispensed with the conjunction in his statement: of the detestable ones just as he dispensed with it in his statement: They will say, ‘Three, their fourth being their dog’ (al-Kahf 18:22). It is possible that the agent in Day is an implied one indicated by his statement: They are of the detestable ones, so it would be like his statement: The Day they see the angels - no good report that Day will there be for the criminals (al-Furqan 25:22). It is possible that the agent in Day is his statement: They are of the detestable ones, even if the circumstance is advanced. It is possible that it is an object of breadth, as if he said: And We pursued them in this world with a curse and a curse on the Day of Resurrection.
28:43: God the Almighty says: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture meaning the Torah, as stated by Qatada. Muhyi ibn Salam said: It is the first book - meaning the Torah - in which the obligations, limits, and rulings were revealed. It was also said that the Book here is six of the eight seven that God revealed to the Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This was stated by Ibn Abbas, and it was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. After We destroyed the former generations Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "God did not destroy a people, a generation, or a town with a punishment from the sky or the earth since He revealed the Torah to Moses, except for the town that was transformed into apes. Have you not seen the words of God the Almighty: "And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture after We destroyed the former generations" meaning after the people of Noah, 'Aad, and Thamud. It was also said: meaning after We drowned Pharaoh and his people and caused the earth to swallow Qarun. "Insights for the people" meaning We gave him the Book as insights. That is, so that they may see. And guidance that is, from misguidance for those who act upon it. And mercy for those who believe in it. Perhaps they will remember that is, so that they may remember this blessing and remain steadfast in their faith in this world, and trust in their reward in the Hereafter.
28:44: God Almighty said: And you were not meaning you were not, O Muhammad on the western side meaning on the western side of the mountain. The poet said: He who gave guidance to the Prophet gave you a light that adorns the western pulpit. When We decreed to Moses the matter when We charged him with Our command and forbade him from what We had promised and bound him with Our covenant. It is also said: that is, when We decreed your matter to Moses and mentioned you with the best mention. Ibn Abbas said: When We decreed means We informed him that the nation of Muhammad is the best of nations. And you were not among the witnesses meaning among those present.
28:45: The Almighty said: But We brought forth generations meaning after Moses and life was prolonged for them until they forgot the remembrance of God, meaning His covenant and command. Similar to this is: And a long period was prolonged for them, so their hearts hardened (al-Hadid 57:16). The apparent meaning of this necessitates that a reminder occurred to our Prophet, peace be upon him, at that time, and that God would send him, but the period was prolonged, and hardness prevailed, so the people forgot that. It was also said: We gave Moses the Book and took covenants from his people, then the covenant was prolonged and they disbelieved, so We sent Muhammad as a renewer of the religion and calling people to it. The Almighty said: And you were not residing among the people of Madyan meaning residing like the place of Moses and Shu'aib among them. Al-Ajjaj said: So he stayed where the host entered That is, the resident guest. And His statement: You recite to them Our verses means you remind them of the promise and the threat. But We were messengers means We sent you to the people of Mecca, and We gave you a book containing this report, and had it not been for that, you would not have known it.
28:46: God the Almighty said: And you were not beside the Mount when We called. Just as you were not present on the western side when God sent Moses to Pharaoh, so too you were not present on the Mount when We called Moses when he came to the appointed time with the seventy. Umar ibn Dinar narrated that the Prophet said: It was called, 'O nation of Muhammad, I answered you before you called upon Me and I gave you before you asked Me.' This is what He said: And you were not beside the Mount when We called. Abu Hurairah said - and in a narration from Ibn Abbas - that God the Almighty said: O nation of Muhammad, I have answered you before you called upon Me. The meaning of the verse according to this is: You were not beside the Mount when God the Almighty spoke to Us. "Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before? They said, 'Two magicians supporting one another.'" That is, Moses and Muhammad and his nation. He said: "O Lord, show them to me." God the Almighty said: "You will not reach them, and if you wish, I will call them and make you hear their voice." He said: "Yes, O Lord." God the Almighty said: O nation of Muhammad! They responded from the loins of their fathers. He said: I have already responded to you before you called upon Me. The meaning of the verse according to this is: You were not beside the Mount when We spoke to Moses, so We called to your nation and informed him of what We had written for you and your nation of mercy until the end of the world. But We did that as a mercy from Us to you. Al-Akhfash said: Mercy is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, meaning, but We had mercy on you as a mercy. Al-Zajjaj said: It is in the accusative case because of the father who did that to you for the sake of mercy. An-Nahhas said: You did not witness the stories of the prophets, nor were they recited to you, but We sent you and revealed them to you for mercy. Al-Kisa’i said: It is on the report of was, meaning: but it was a mercy. He said: The fourth is permissible in the sense of it is a mercy. Al-Zajjaj: The nominative case means, but He did that as a mercy. “That you may warn a people to whom no warner came before you” meaning the Arabs, meaning you did not witness that report, but We revealed it to you as a mercy to those to whom you were sent so that you may warn them with it that they may remember.
28:47: The Almighty says: And had it not been that a calamity would have befallen them meaning the Quraysh, or it was said: the Jews, for what their hands have put forth of disbelief and sins. He mentioned the hands specifically because most earning occurs through them. The answer to had it not been is omitted, meaning had it not been that a punishment would have befallen them because of their previous sins, and they would have said, 'Our Lord, had You not sent us a messenger,' we would not have sent the messengers. It was said: We would have hastened the punishment upon them. The messengers were sent to remove the treachery of the disbelievers, as mentioned previously in Glory be to Him and at the end of Ta Ha. Then we will follow Your signs is in the accusative case as a response to the exhortation. And we will be is in apposition to it, among the believers among the believers. Some have used this verse as evidence, saying that reason necessitates belief and gratitude, because He said: for what their hands have put forth, and that necessitates punishment, since the obligation was established before the sending of the messengers, and that can only be done by reason. Al-Qushayri said: “The correct interpretation is that what was omitted is ‘If it weren’t for this, there would be no need to renew the sending of messengers.’ That is, these disbelievers have no excuse, since the previous laws and the call to monotheism had reached them, but the period had been long. So if We punished them, one of them might say, ‘The period with the messengers has been long,’ and he would think that this is an excuse, and they have no excuse after the report of the messengers had reached them. But We have completely removed the excuse and completed the clarification, so We sent you, O Muhammad, to them. And God has decreed that He does not punish a servant until after the clarification and proof have been completed and the messengers have been sent.”
28:48: God the Almighty said: So when the truth came to them from Us meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, they said meaning the disbelievers of Mecca Why was he not given the like of what Moses was given? of the staff and the white hand, and the Quran was revealed to him all at once like the Torah. They had heard about the matter of Moses before Muhammad, so God the Almighty said: Did they not disbelieve in what Moses was given before? They said, Two magicians who cooperated with one another in magic. Al-Kalbi said: The Quraysh sent to the Jews and asked them about the mission of Muhammad and his affair. They said: We find it in the Torah with his description and characteristics. When the answer came back to them, they said, Two magicians who cooperated with one another. They said, “Say: The Jews taught the polytheists and said to Muhammad, ‘Why were we not given the like of what Moses was given?’” He said, He was given the Torah all at once. This argument is directed against the Jews, that is, did these Jews not disbelieve in what was given to Moses when they said about Moses and Aaron, They are magicians. And Indeed, we are disbelievers in both of them. The Kufians read: Sahiran without an alif. Meaning, the Gospel and the Quran. It was also said: the Torah and the Criterion, as said by Al-Farra’. It was also said: the Torah and the Gospel, as said by Abu Razin. The rest read Sahiran with an alif. There are three opinions on this. One of them: Moses and Muhammad, peace be upon them. This is the opinion of the polytheists of the Arabs. This is what Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said. The second: Moses and Aaron. This is what the Jews said to them at the beginning of their mission. This is what Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Ibn Zayd said. So the statement is an argument against him. This indicates that what was omitted in His statement, Had it not been that a disaster should have befallen them, is that We would not have specified the sending of messengers, because the Jews acknowledged the prophethoods but they distorted and changed them and deserved punishment. So He said: We have completely removed their excuse with the sending of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The third: Jesus and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is what the Jews say today. Qatada also said the same. It was said: Did not all the Jews disbelieve in what was given to Moses in the Torah of the mention of the Messiah, the Gospel and the Qur’an, so they saw Moses and Muhammad as magicians and the two books as magic.
28:49: The Almighty said: “Say, ‘Then bring a book from God that is better guidance than both of them. I will follow it,’” meaning, say, O Muhammad, since you polytheists have disbelieved in these two books, “Then bring a book from God that is better guidance than both of them. I will follow it,” so that this will be an excuse for you for disbelief, if you should be truthful, that they are two forms of magic, or that you have rebelled against a book that is better guidance than the books of Moses and Muhammad, peace be upon them. This strengthens the Kufi reciters of two magics. I will follow it Al-Farra’ said: In the nominative case, because it is an attribute of the book, and book is an indefinite noun. He said: And if you make it jussive – which is the correct view – then it is on the condition.
28:50: God Almighty says: But if they do not respond to you O Muhammad, that they should produce a book from God, then know that they only follow their own desires meaning the opinions of their hearts and what they consider good and what Satan makes attractive to them, and that they have no proof. And who is more astray than he who follows his own desire without guidance from God meaning no one is more astray than him. Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people.
28:51: God Almighty says: And We have certainly connected to them the Word meaning, We followed one part of it with another, and We sent messenger after messenger. Al-Hasan read:وصلin a lightened form. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Ahfash said: The meaning ofوصل is We completed, as you connect something. Ibn Uyaynah and Al-Suddi said: We explained. Ibn Abbas said the same. Mujahid said: We separated. And he used to recite it that way. Ibn Zayd said: We connected to them the report of this world with the report of the Hereafter, until it is as if they are in the Hereafter in this world. The scholars of semantics said: We followed and followed, and We sent down the Qur’an, some of it following some: promises and threats, stories and lessons, advice and sermons, wanting them to remember and succeed. Its root is from connecting ropes to each other. The poet said: So tell the Banu Marwan, what is the matter with the covenant and the weak rope that keeps on connecting? Imru' al-Qais said: Darir Kakhdrov Al-Walid ordered him to turn his hands with a connecting thread The pronoun in lahum refers to Quraysh, according to Mujahid. It was also said that it refers to the Jews. It was also said that it refers to all of them. The verse is a refutation of those who said, Why was Muhammad not given the Qur’an all at once? “Perhaps they will remember.” Ibn Abbas said: They will remember Muhammad and believe in him. It was also said: They will remember and fear that what was revealed to those before them will be revealed to them. This was said by Ali ibn Isa. It was also said: They will remember and fear that what was revealed to those before them will be revealed to them. This was said by Ali ibn Isa. It was also said: Perhaps they will be admonished by the Qur’an when they worship idols. This was narrated by Al-Naqqash.
28:52: The Almighty's saying: Those to whom We gave the Scripture before it - they believe in it. God informed us that some of the Children of Israel who were given the Scripture before the Qur'an believed in the Qur'an, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and Salman. This includes the Christian scholars who converted to Islam, and they were forty men who came to Madinah with Ja'far ibn Abi Talib, thirty-two men from Abyssinia, and eight men who came from Syria and were the imams of the Christians: among them Yahyra the monk, Abraha, Al-Ashraf, Amir, Ayman, Idris, and Nafi'. Al-Mawardi named them this way, and God revealed this verse and the one after it about them. Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured. Qatada said this. It was also narrated from him that it was revealed about Abdullah ibn Salam, Tamim Al-Dari, Al-Jarud Al-Abdi, and Sulayman Al-Farsi. They converted to Islam, so this verse was revealed about them. Rafa'ah Al-Qurazi said: It was revealed about ten, and I was one of them. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: This was revealed about the Negus and his companions. He sent twelve men to sit with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Abu Jahl and his companions were close to them, so they believed in the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). When they left him, Abu Jahl and those with him followed them. He said to them: May God disappoint you, our rider, and make you ugly as a delegation. You soon believed him. We have never seen a rider more foolish or ignorant than you. They said: Peace be upon you. We have not spared ourselves guidance. For us are our deeds, and for you are your deeds. This has been fully discussed in Surah al-Ma’idah, when it says: And when they hear what has been revealed to the Messenger (al-Ma’idah 5:83). Abu al-‘Aliyah said: These are people who believed in Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before he was sent, and some of them had lived to see him. Before him means before the Qur’an. It was also said: “Before Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) they believe in him” meaning in the Qur’an or in Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him).
28:53: God Almighty says: “And when it is recited to them, they say, ‘We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord.’” That is, when the Qur’an is recited to them, they say, “We believe in what is in it. “Indeed, we were before it,” that is, before its revelation, or before the mission of Muhammad, peace be upon him, submitting Muslims, that is, monotheists, or believing that Muhammad would be sent and the Qur’an would be revealed to him.
28:54: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Those will be given their reward twice for what they patiently endured. It is proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Musa that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three who will be given their reward twice: a man from the People of the Book who believed in his Prophet and lived to see the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and believed in him, followed him, and confirmed his truthfulness, so he will have two rewards; a slave who fulfilled the right of God, the Almighty, and the right of his master, so he will have two rewards; and a man who had a female slave, whom he fed and fed well, then educated and educated her well, then freed her and married her, so he will have two rewards.” Al-Sha’bi said to Al-Khurasani: Take this hadith without qualification, because a man would travel to Madinah for less than this, and Al-Bukhari also included it. Our scholars said: Since each of these was addressed with two commands from two directions, each of them deserved two rewards. The People of the Book was addressed by his Prophet, then he was addressed by our Prophet, so he answered him and followed him, so he gets the reward of both religions. Likewise, the slave is commanded by God and by his master. The Lord of the nation, when he carried out what he was addressed to do in raising and disciplining his female slave, he revived her with the revival of upbringing. Then, when he freed her and married her, he revived her with the revival of freedom that he attached to his position in it. So, they did what they were commanded to do regarding her. So, each of them deserves two rewards. Then, each of the two righteous deeds is multiplied in itself, the good deed is tenfold, so the rewards are multiplied. Therefore, it was said: The slave who fulfills the rights of his master and the rights of God is better than the free man, and this is what Abu Omar ibn Abdul Barr and others accepted. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: A slave who does good deeds will have two rewards. By the One in Whose Hand is Abu Hurairah’s soul, were it not for jihad in the cause of God, Hajj, and being dutiful to my mother, I would have loved to die a slave. Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab said: It has reached us that Abu Hurairah did not perform Hajj until she died because of her company. In Sahih Muslim, it is also narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “How good it is for kings to die while worshipping God well and being the companions of their master. How good it is for them.” Second: The Almighty’s saying: Because they were patient is general in their patience with their religion, then with this and with the harm they encounter from the infidels and other than that. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And they repel evil with good meaning they repel. Dara’a means to repel, and dara means to push away. In the hadith: Push away the prescribed punishments with doubtful things. It was said: They repel harm with tolerance and kind words. It was also said: They repel sins with repentance and seeking forgiveness. According to the first opinion, it is a description of noble morals, meaning whoever says something to them that is unfair, they do not reprimand him and he responds with kind words that repel it. This is a verse of truce, and it was from the early days of Islam. It was abrogated by the verse of the sword, but its ruling remained in effect for things less than disbelief, and the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will practice it until the Day of Judgment. From this is his saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to Muadh: And follow the bad with a good one, and it will erase it, and treat people with good character. Among good character is repelling what is disliked and harmful, and being patient in the face of harshness by ignoring it and speaking kindly. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: And from what We have provided them, they spend. He praised them for spending from their wealth in acts of obedience and in accordance with the Shari’ah, and in that there is an urging to give charity. Spending may also be from the body through fasting and prayer. Then He also praised them for turning away from idle talk, as the Almighty said: And when they pass by ill speech, they pass by with dignity. (Al-Furqan 25:72) meaning, when they heard the harm and insults the polytheists said to them, they turned away from it, meaning they did not engage in it. “And they said, ‘To us our deeds, and to you your deeds, [so] peace be upon you.’” meaning, they left it, like His statement: “And when the ignorant address them, they say, ‘Peace.’” (Al-Furqan 25:63) meaning, to us our religion, and to you your religion. “Peace be upon you” means, We give you security from us, for we do not wage war against you, nor do we revile you. It has nothing to do with greeting. Al-Zajjaj said: This was before the command to fight.
28:55: God Almighty says: We do not seek the ignorant, meaning do not seek them out for argument, discussion, or insults.
28:56: God Almighty said: Indeed, you do not guide whom you love. Al-Zajjaj said: The Muslims agreed that it was revealed about Abu Talib. I said: What is correct to say is that most of the commentators agreed that it was revealed concerning Abu Talib, the uncle of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and this is the text of the hadith of Bukhari and Muslim, and we have already discussed that Surah Bara’ah. Abu Ruq said that his statement, But God guides whom He wills, refers to Al-Abbas. Qatada said the same. And He knows best who are guided. Mujahid said: For whomever He has destined to be guided. It was said that the meaning of whom You love is whomever You love to be guided. Jubair ibn Mut’im said: No one heard the revelation being delivered to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) except Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, for he heard Gabriel saying: O Muhammad, recite: Indeed, you do not guide whom You love, but God guides whom He wills.
28:57: God the Almighty said: And they say, 'If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land.' This is what the polytheists of Mecca said. Ibn Abbas said: The one who said that from Quraysh was Al-Harith bin Uthman bin Nawfal bin Abd Manaf Al-Qurashi. He said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "We know that what you say is true, but what prevents us from following the guidance with you and believing in you is the fear that the Arabs will snatch us away from our land - meaning Mecca - because they unite in opposition to us, and we cannot control them." This was one of their excuses, so God the Almighty answered their excuses by saying: Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary? That is, one of security. This is because the Arabs were in the Age of Ignorance, raiding one another and killing one another, while the people of Mecca were safe wherever they were, due to the sanctity of the sanctuary. So God informed us that He had made them safe due to the sanctity of the House, and had protected their enemy from them, so they did not fear that the Arabs would violate a sanctuary in fighting them. And snatching away means that it does not happen quickly, and this has been mentioned before. Yahya ibn Salam said: He said: You were safe in my sanctuary, eating my sustenance and worshipping others besides me. Do you fear when you worship me and believe in me? The fruits of all things are gathered to it meaning the fruits of every land and country are gathered to it, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It is said: He gathered the water in the basin, meaning he collected it. The basin is the great basin. Nafi` read: تجىبىwith a ta`, for the fruits. The rest read it with a ya`, because of his saying:كل شيand Abu `Ubaid chose it. He said: Because there is a barrier between the feminine noun and its verb, and also because the fruits are plural and not a true feminine. Rizqan min laduna means from us. But most of them do not know meaning they do not understand, meaning they are heedless of the evidence, and that the One who provided for them and made them secure in the past while they were disbelievers will provide for them if they become Muslim, and will prevent the disbelievers from them in their Islam. Rizqan is in the accusative case as a result of the action. It is permissible to make it accusative as a verbal noun in meaning, because the meaning ofتجىتىis to be provided for.يتجىwas read: يتجىwith a noon from jinna, and its transitivity is with ila like you sayيتجى لى فيهandيتجى لى الِافة.
28:58: The Almighty said: And how many a city have We destroyed that was filled with insolence in its life. He explained to those who imagined that if they had believed, the Arabs would have fought them that the fear of abandoning faith is greater. How many a people have disbelieved, then destruction and insolence befell them, as Az-Zajjaj said. Its life means in its life. So when he deleted in, the verb became transitive, as Al-Mazini said. Az-Zajjaj is like his statement: And Moses chose from his people seventy men (Al-A'raf 7:155). Al-Farra' said: It is in the accusative case for explanation. He said, as you say: Malik was insolent and proud. Its equivalent according to him is: Except for him who makes a fool of himself (Al-Baqarah 2:130) and so it is according to him. But if they, of good will, give up to you anything of it (An-Nisa' 4:4). The accusative case of definite nouns for explanation is impossible according to the Basrans, because the meaning of explanation and distinction is that it is one indefinite noun that indicates a genus. It was said: It is in the accusative case with batarat and the meaning of batarat is ignorant, so the meaning is: She was ignorant of the gratitude for her livelihood. Those are their dwellings, which were not inhabited after them except a little meaning, after the destruction of their inhabitants, only a few dwellings were inhabited and their traces are ruins. The exception refers to the dwellings, meaning some of them are inhabited, as Al-Zajjaj said. It was objected to, and it was said: If the exception referred to the dwellings, he would have said except a little, because you say: The people were not inhabited except a little, raising it if what was inhabited is a little. So those are their dwellings, which were not inhabited except by travelers and those who passed by the road for a day or part of a day, meaning, after them, only... were inhabited. Ibn Abbas said: Only travelers or passersby inhabited it for a day or an hour. And We were the inheritors meaning of what they left behind after their destruction.
28:59: The Almighty said: And your Lord would not destroy the cities meaning the cities whose people were disbelieving. Until He sends to its mother It was read with a damma or kasra on the hamza to follow the accusative, meaning Mecca, and a messenger meaning Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said: in its mother meaning in its largest city, a messenger to warn them. Al-Hasan said: in its beginnings. I said: Makkah is the greatest of cities because of its sanctity and because it was the first, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, the first House of worship established for mankind (Al Imran 3:96). It was singled out as the greatest because the Messenger was sent to it, because the Messengers were sent to the nobles and they lived in the cities and they were around it. This meaning was mentioned at the end of Surah Yusuf. He recites to them Our verses “recites” is in the position of an adjective, meaning he is telling them that the punishment will descend upon them if they do not believe. And We would not destroy the cities and the nun was dropped for the sake of addition like wronging themselves (al-Nahl 16:28). Except while their people were wrongdoers meaning I did not destroy them except after they deserved to be destroyed because of their persistence in disbelief after they had been excused. This is a statement of His justice and holiness over injustice. God the Almighty has informed us that He will not destroy them except if they deserved to be destroyed due to their wrongdoing, and He will not destroy them despite them being wrongdoers except after confirming the proof and obligation of sending the Messengers, and He does not make His knowledge of their condition an proof against them. And He exalted Himself from destroying them while they were not unjust, as the Almighty said: And your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly while their people were righteous (Hud 11:117). So He stated in His statement unjustly that if He had destroyed them while they were righteous, that would have been injustice to them from Him, and that His state in His wealth and wisdom is contrary to injustice. He indicated that with the letter of negation and its lam, as the Almighty said: And God would not let your faith go to waste (al-Baqarah 2:143).
28:60: God the Almighty says: And whatever you have been given of anything O people of Mecca is but the enjoyment of worldly life and its adornment meaning you enjoy it for the duration of your life, or for a period of your life, then either you leave it or it leaves you. And what is with God is better and more lasting meaning better and more lasting, meaning the Hereafter, which is Paradise. Do you not then understand? That what is lasting is better than what is perishable. Abu Amr read: َيذْغقخلروwith a ya’. The rest read it with a ta’ indicating address, and this is the preferred choice, based on God’s saying: And what you have been given.
28:61: The Almighty says: Is he to whom We have promised a good promise which he will surely attain? meaning Paradise and the reward it contains like he to whom We have given enjoyment of worldly life then he is given part of what he desired then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth meaning in the Fire. Similar to this is the verse in which God says: And had it not been for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth (37:57). Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Hamzah ibn Abdul Muttalib and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. Mujahid said: It was revealed about the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Abu Jahl. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: It was revealed about Hamzah and Ali, and about Abu Jahl and 'Ammarah ibn al-Walid. It was also said: It was revealed about 'Ammar and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, as al-Suddi said. Al-Qushayri said: The correct view is that it was revealed about the believer and the disbeliever in a general manner. Al-Tha’labi: In short, it was revealed about every unbeliever who enjoyed well-being and wealth in this world, but will have Hell in the Hereafter, and about every believer who was patient in the face of worldly trials, trusting in God’s promise, and will have Paradise in the Hereafter.
28:62: God Almighty says: And the Day He will call to them meaning God will call to these polytheists on the Day of Resurrection and say, ‘Where are My partners?’ according to your claim that they will support you and intercede for you. Those upon whom the word has come into effect will say, Those upon whom the word of punishment has come into effect meaning the word of punishment has come into effect, and they are the leaders, Al-Kalbi. Qatada said: They are the devils.
28:63: The Almighty says: Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray. That is, we invited them to error. It was said to them: Did you lead them astray? They said: We led them astray as we were led astray. They meant: Did we lead them astray as we were led astray. “We disavow ourselves before You.” That is, we disavow each other. The devils disavow those who obeyed them, and the leaders disavow those who accepted them, as the Almighty says: Friends that Day will be enemies to each other, except for the righteous. (al-Zukhruf 43:67)
28:64: God the Almighty says: And it will be said meaning to the disbelievers, Call upon your partners meaning seek aid from your gods that you worshipped in this world to aid you and defend you. So they called upon them meaning they sought aid from them. But they did not respond to them meaning they did not answer them and did not benefit from them. And they will see the punishment, if only they were guided. Al-Zajjaj said: The answer to if is omitted, and the meaning is: If only they were guided, guidance would have saved them, and they would not have been subjected to the punishment. It was also said: If only they were guided, they would not have called upon them. It was also said that the meaning is: When they saw the punishment, they wished that they were guided in this world, guidance would have saved them, and when they saw the punishment, if only they were guided in this world, they would not have seen the punishment on the Day of Resurrection.
28:65: God Almighty says: What did you answer the messengers? That is, God says to them: What was your answer to the prophets sent to you when they conveyed My messages to you?
28:66: God the Almighty said: And the report will be hidden from them that Day meaning the arguments will be hidden from them, as stated by Mujahid, because God had given them an excuse in this world, so they will have no excuse or argument on the Day of Resurrection. report means information. He called their arguments report because they are information that they will narrate. They will not ask one another meaning they will not ask one another about the arguments, because God the Almighty has refuted their arguments, as stated by Ad-Dahhak. Ibn Abbas said: They will not ask one another meaning they will not utter any argument. It was also said: They will not ask one another at that hour, and they will not know how to respond due to the horror of that hour, then they will respond after that. He mentioned their saying: By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists (Al-An'am 6:23). Mujahid said: They will not ask one another about lineages. It was also said that they will not ask one another to bear any of their sins, as stated by Ibn Abbas.
28:67: God Almighty says: But as for him who repents meaning from polytheism and believes meaning and does righteousness performing the obligatory duties and increasing the voluntary ones it is likely that he will be among the successful meaning among those who win happiness. And it is likely is obligatory from God.
28:68: His saying, the Most High: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses. This is connected to the mention of the partners whom they worshipped and chose for intercession, meaning that the choice regarding intercessors lies with God, not with the polytheists. It was said that this is the response of Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira when he said: Why was this Qur'an not sent down to some great man from the two cities? (al-Zukhruf 43:31) He meant himself, he claimed, and Urwah ibn Mas'ud Al-Thaqafi from At-Ta'if. It was also said that this is the response of the Jews when they said, If the messenger to Muhammad had been other than Gabriel, we would have believed in him. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is, your Lord creates whomever He wills from among His creation and chooses from among them whomever He wills to obey Him. Yahya ibn Salam said: The meaning is, And your Lord creates whomever He wills from among His creation, meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and chooses the supporters for His religion. I said: In Al-Bazzar’s book, it is authentically transmitted on the authority of Jabir: (God the Almighty chose my companions over all the worlds, except for the prophets and messengers. He chose for me from my companions four - meaning Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, and Ali - and made them my companions, and among my companions there is goodness. He chose my nation over all other nations, and He chose for me from my nation four generations.) Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated from Amr ibn Dinar from Wahb ibn Munabbih from his father regarding the words of God the Almighty: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses, he said: Among the livestock are sheep, and among the birds are pigeons. The complete pause is and chooses. Ali ibn Sulayman said: This is a complete pause, and it is not permissible for what to be in the accusative case with chooses, because if it were in the accusative case, nothing would apply to it. He said: This is a refutation of the Qadarites. An-Nahhas said: The complete pause is and chooses meaning He chooses the messengers. They had no choice meaning He does not send whomever they choose. Abu Ishaq said: And chooses this is the complete chosen pause, and it is permissible for ma to be in the accusative case with yakhtaar and the meaning would be that he chooses that in which they have the choice. Al-Qushayri said: The first is the correct one because they agreed to stop at his statement, and chooses. Al-Mahdawi said: This is more similar to the doctrine of the Sunnis, and ma in his statement, They had no choice is a general negation of all things, that the servant has any choice in them other than what he acquires through the power of God, the Almighty. Al-Zamakhshari said: They had no choice is an explanation of his statement, And chooses, because its meaning is that he chooses what he wants, and for this reason the conjunction was not included, and the meaning is that the choice is for God, the Most High, in His actions, and He is most knowing of the aspects of wisdom in them, meaning that none of His creation has the right to choose over Him. Al-Zajjaj and others permitted ma to be in the accusative case with yakhtaar. Al-Tabari denied that ma is a negative, lest the meaning be that they did not have the choice in the past and they do have it in the future, and because no negation speech preceded it. Al-Mahdawi said: This is not necessary, because ma negates the present and the future, as it does not, and therefore it worked in its function, and because the verses were revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding what he was asked about, and regarding what he was asked about, and regarding what they were determined to do, even if that was not in the text. The interpretation of the verse according to At-Tabari is: And He chooses for His guardianship the best of His creation, because the polytheists used to choose the best of their wealth and make it for their gods, so God the Most High said: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses for the guidance of His creation from those who were predestined for happiness in His knowledge, just as the polytheists chose the best of their wealth for their gods. So died according to this is for those who have reason and it has two meanings: who and the best is raised as a subject and they is the predicate and the sentence is the predicate of was. Its similarity is like your saying: Zayd was his father from the divorced and there is weakness in it, because there is no pronoun in the speech that refers back to the subject of was unless an omission is estimated in it, in which case it is permissible with distance. The two meanings of what At-Tabari said have been narrated from Ibn Abbas. Al-Tha’labi said: And what is a negation, meaning they have no choice over God. This is more correct like the saying of God the Most High: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision (Al-Ahzab 33:36). Muhammad Al-Warraq said: Trust in the Most Gracious in everything you want, for God decrees and decides. When the Lord of the Throne desires something for His servant, He befalls him, and the servant has no choice. A person may perish due to his caution, but he may be saved by the grace of God when he is cautious. Another said: The servant is impatient, the Lord is powerful, time is changeable, and sustenance is apportioned. All good is in what He has chosen for our creation, and in choosing anything else there is blame and misfortune. Some scholars said that no one should undertake any worldly matter until he asks God for the best in it, by praying two rak'ahs of istikharah prayer, and in the first rak'ah after the Fatiha he should recite: Say, ‘O you disbelievers’ (Al-Kafirun 72:1) and in the second rak'ah: Say, ‘He is God, the One’ (Al-Ikhlas 113:1). Some sheikhs preferred to recite in the first rak'ah: “And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses. It is not for them to choose” (Al-Ikhlas 72:1), and in the second rak'ah: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision (Al-Ikhlas 72:1). And all is good. Then he should recite this supplication after the salutation. And this is what Al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught us to seek guidance from God in all matters, just as he taught us a surah from the Qur’an. He said: “If any one of you intends to do something, let him perform two rak’ahs other than the obligatory prayer, then let him say: ‘O God, I seek Your guidance by Your knowledge, and I seek Your power by Your power, and I ask You from Your great bounty, for You are able and I am not able, and You know and I do not know, and You are the Knower of the unseen. O God, if You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair – or he said, in my immediate and future affairs – then decree it for me and make it easy for me, and then bless me. O God, if You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my worldly life, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affair – or he said, in my immediate and future affairs – then turn it away from me and turn me away from it, and decree for me what is good when it is, and then make me content with it.’” Aisha narrated on the authority of Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with them both: “When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, intended to do something, he would say: ‘O God, make it good for me and choose for me.’” Anas narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Anas, if you intend to do something, then seek guidance from your Lord regarding it seven times, then look at what comes to your heart, for therein lies goodness. The scholars said: He should empty his heart of all thoughts so that he is not inclined to any matter. Then, whatever comes to his heart, he should act upon, for therein lies goodness, God willing. If he intends to travel, he should plan to travel on a Thursday or a Monday, following the example of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Then, God glorified and exalted Himself with His true statement, saying: Glory be to God, meaning, sanctification and glorification, "from what they associate with Him. And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they declare." Ibn Muhays and Hamid read: َتكwith a fatha on the ta' and a damma on the kaf. This has been mentioned previously in Surat An-Naml, praising God that He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and that nothing is hidden from Him.
28:69: God Almighty says: And your Lord knows what their hearts conceal and what they declare.
28:70: The Almighty’s saying: “And He is God, there is no god but Him. To Him be praise in the first and the last. His is the command, and to Him you will be returned.” Its meaning was presented earlier, and that He is the One and Only, and that all praise is due to Him, and that there is no command except His, and to Him is the final destination.
28:71: God Almighty said: Say, ‘Have you considered if God made the night continuous for you?’ That is, always. And from this is the saying of Tarafa: By your life, my day is not clouded by sadness, nor my night is eternal. God Almighty made it clear that He provided the means of livelihood so that they could be grateful for His blessings. What god other than God can bring you light? That is, a light in which you seek a livelihood. It was also said: a day in which you can see your livelihood and in which fruits and plants grow. Do you not hear? Hearing of understanding and acceptance.
28:72: The Almighty said: Say, ‘Have you considered, if God made the day continuous for you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than God could bring you a night in which to rest?’ That is, in which you would rest from fatigue. Do you not see? What error you are in by worshipping other than Him? So if you acknowledge that none is able to bring you night and day other than Him, then why are you grateful for Him?
28:73: God Almighty says: And of His mercy He has made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein meaning in them. It was also said that the pronoun refers to time, which is night and day. And that you may seek of His bounty meaning that you may ask for His provision therein, meaning in the day, so and that you may be grateful was omitted.
28:74: God the Almighty says: And the Day He will call to them and say, 'Where are My partners whom you used to claim?' This pronoun is repeated because of the difference in the two options. They will be called once and it will be said to them, Where are My partners whom you used to claim? So they will call to the idols but they will not respond, and their confusion will be revealed. Then they will be called once and He will speak to the disbelievers, as God the Almighty says: And God will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection (Al-Baqarah 2:174). But God the Almighty commands someone to rebuke them and rebuke them, and establish proof against them in the place of reckoning. It was said: It is possible that it is from God, and His statement, And God will not speak to them is when it is said to them, Be gone into it, despised and do not speak to you (Al-Mu'minun 33:108). And He said, My partners is because they gave them a share of their wealth.
28:75: God the Almighty said: And We will bring forth from every nation a witness meaning a prophet, according to Mujahid. It was said: They are the just ones of the Hereafter who will bear witness against the servants regarding their deeds in this world. The first is more evident, based on God the Almighty's saying: How will it be then, when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these? (An-Nisa': 41). The witness of every nation is its messenger who bears witness against it. The witness who is present means that We brought their messenger who was sent to them. Then We said, 'Bring forth your proof' meaning your argument. So they knew that the truth belongs to God meaning they knew the truth of what the prophets had brought. And what they used to invent means that it was lost to them and became void. What they used to invent means that they invented lies about God the Almighty because they had other gods to worship with Him.
28:76: The Almighty's saying: Indeed, Korah was from the people of Moses. When God Almighty said: And whatever you have been given is but the enjoyment of worldly life and its adornment (al-Qasas 28:60), He explained that Korah was given it and was deceived by it, but it did not protect him from God's punishment, just as it did not protect Pharaoh. You, polytheists, are not greater in number or wealth than Korah and Pharaoh. So, his soldiers and wealth did not benefit Pharaoh, and his kinship to Moses and his treasures did not benefit Korah. An-Nakha'i, Qatada and others said: Moses' cousin Lahha was Korah ibn Yazhar ibn Qahath ibn Levi ibn Ya'qub, and Muwayy ibn Imran ibn Qahab. Ibn Ishaq said: He was Moses' uncle from both his father and mother. It was also said: He was his maternal uncle's son. It was not declined because of its foreignness and definiteness. And whatever is on the pattern of fa’ul and is not suitable for the definite article is not declined in the definite noun and is declined in the indefinite noun. However, if the definite article is suitable for it, it is declined if it is a masculine noun such as Ṭawūs and Ḥarāqūd. Al-Zajjaj said: If qārūn was from qarnaṭal-shay’, it would have been declined. Fabgā ʿalayhum means that he increased the length of his garment by a handspan. This was said by Shahr ibn Hawshab. In the hadith: God does not look at one who cuts his garment out of arrogance. It was also said that his ḥarāq was his disbelief in God, the Almighty, this was said by Ad-Dahhak. It was also said that his ḥarāq was his belittling of them due to his great wealth and children. This was said by Qatadah. It was also said that his ḥarāq was his attributing the treasures that God had given him to himself through his knowledge and cunning. This was said by Ibn Bahr. It was also said that his ḥarāq was his saying: If the prophethood was for Moses and the altar and offerings were for Aaron, then what is for me! So it was narrated that when Moses crossed the sea with them and the message was for Moses and the joy was for Aaron in his soul and their feelings. Then he said to Moses, "The matter is up to you both, and I have nothing. How long must I be patient?" Moses said, This is what God has done. Moses said, By God, I will not believe you until you bring a sign. So he ordered the leaders of the Children of Israel to each bring his staff. So he tied it together and threw it into the tent where the revelation was received. They guarded their staffs at night, and in the morning, behold, Aaron's staff was shaking and had green leaves - and it was made of almond wood. Korah said, This is nothing more amazing than what you are doing of magic. "So he transgressed against them" means injustice. Yahya ibn Salam and Ibn al-Musayyab said: Korah was a rich worker for Pharaoh over the Children of Israel. Rather, he transgressed against them and oppressed them and was one of them. Seventh: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When God the Almighty ordered the stoning of the adulterer, Qarun went to a prostitute and gave her money, and made her claim that he had committed adultery with her and that he had impregnated her. This was very difficult for Moses and he made her swear by God, who parted the sea for the Children of Israel and sent down the Torah to Moses, that she would tell the truth. God intervened with her and she said: I bear witness that you are innocent, and that Qarun gave me money and made me say what I said, and you are the truthful one and Qarun is the liar. So God gave the matter of Qarun to Moses and ordered the earth to obey him. So he came to him saying to the earth: O earth, take him, O earth, take him, and it took him little by little while he cried out for help, O Moses! Until he sank into the earth, along with his house and his companions who were of his faith. It was narrated that God the Almighty revealed to Moses: My servants sought your help and you did not have mercy on them. But if they had called upon Me, they would have found Me near and responsive. Ibn Jurayj: It has been reported to us that they are swallowed up by a person’s stature every day, and they will not reach the lowest part of the earth until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Al-Dunya mentioned in his book Al-Faraj: Ibrahim bin Rashid told me: Dawud bin Mihran told me, on the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim, on the authority of Marwan bin Janah, on the authority of Yunus bin Maysarah bin Halbas, who said: Qarun met Yunus in the darkness of the sea, so Qarun called out to Yunus and said: O Yunus, repent to God, for you will find Him at the first step you take to Him. Yunus said: What prevented you from repenting? He said: My repentance was given to my cousin, but he refused to accept it from me. In the hadith: When Qarun reaches the bottom of the seventh earth, Israfil will blow the trumpet. And God knows best. Al-Suddi said: The prostitute’s name was Sabrata, and Qarun offered her two thousand dirhams. Qatada: He crossed the sea with Moses and was called Al-Munwar because of the beauty of his voice in the Torah, but the enemy of God was a hypocrite, just as the Samaritan was. God the Almighty said: "And We gave him of the treasures." Ata' said: The owners of many of the treasures of Joseph, peace be upon him. Al-Walid bin Marwan said: He was engaged in alchemy. "Its keys" in and its subject and predicate are in the relative clause of ma and ma is the object of we gave. An-Nahhas said: I heard Ali bin Salman say: How ugly is what the Kufians say about relative clauses, that it is not permissible for the relative clause of which and its sisters to be in and what it works on. In the Qur'an: its keys are ma in. It is the plural of muftah open with a kasrah, which is what is opened with. And whoever says miftah says keys. And whoever says it is the treasurers, its singular is muftah open with a fathah. "To burden the group" la tan'u bil-'asbah The best that has been said about it is that the meaning is to burden the group, meaning to make them lean with its weight. So when the ta' was opened, it was replaced with the ba'. Just as they said: He takes away misery and misery takes away. Fasal to bear the burden of the group so he made the group bear, meaning it rose heavily, like his saying, like your saying stand up with us, meaning make us rise. And it is said: Naa yanu’ naw’an if he rose heavily. The poet said: She is burdened with her last legs, so she does not rise, and she walks slowly, and soon she will be amazed. Another said: I took but did not own it, and intended but did not care, as if I were chained for a long time, and it burdened me if it burdened me, on the authority of Abu Zaid. Ubaidah said: His statement to bear the burden of the group is reversed, and the meaning is for the group to bear it, i.e. to carry it. Abu Zaid: It is burdened with the load if it carries it. The poet said: We found an alliance, a poor successor, a slave who, when he is unable to bear the burden, stops. The first is the meaning of what Ibn Abbas, Abu Saleh and Al-Suddi said. It is the opinion of Al-Farra’ and Al-Nahhas chose it. Just as one says: I went with him and I made him go, I brought him and I surprised him, and we brought him and he moaned. As for their saying: I have with him what upset him and he was far away, this is an imitation that should have been said and he was far away. Similar to it is the food congratulated me and showed me, and he took what was presented and what happened. It was said: It is taken from the distance which is the slave. From it is the saying of the poet: They are far from us, but their love is not far away. The heart is bound to them wherever they are. Badil bin Maysarah read: yanu’ with a ya’, meaning that one of them or the mentioned one may be burdened, so it was carried on the meaning. Abu Ubaidah said: I said to Ru’bah bin Al-Ajaj regarding his statement: It has black and white lines as if there is vitiligo on the skin. If you mean lines, say as if they are, and if you mean black and variegated, say as if they are both. He said: I meant all of that. There are eleven opinions regarding the group of people who are loyal to one another: The first: Three men, said Ibn Abbas. It was also reported from him: From three to ten. Mujahid said: The group of people here is between twenty and fifteen. It was also reported from him: Between ten and fifteen. It was also reported from him: From ten to five. The first was mentioned by Al-Tha’labi, the second by Al-Qushayri and Al-Mawardi, and the third by Al-Mahdawi. Abu Salih, Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, Qatada, and Al-Dahhak said: Forty men. Al-Suddi: Between ten and forty. Qatada also said this. Ikrimah said: Some of them say forty, and some say seventy. This is the opinion of Abu Salih that the group of people is seventy men, mentioned by Al-Mawardi. The first was mentioned by Al-Tha’labi. It was also said: Sixty men. Sa’id bin Jubayr said: Six or seven. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid said: Between three and nine, which is the group. Al-Kalbi said: Eleven, based on the statement of Joseph’s brothers: And we are a group (Yusuf 12:8). Muqatil also said the same. Khaithamah said: I found in the Bible that the keys to the treasuries of Qarun and Qarūn were sixty bright, white-footed mules, and that they would be too heavy to carry. One of them would not be more than a finger’s length. For each one of them was a treasure of money. If that treasure were divided among the people of Basra, they would disbelieve. Mujahid said: The keys were made of camel hide. It was also said: From cow hide to make them easier for him. They were carried with him as he rode seventy mules, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri. It was also said: On forty mules. This is the statement of Ad-Dahhak. It was also narrated from him: His keys were his vessels. Abu Salih also said: What is meant by the keys are the treasuries, and God knows best. When his people said to him meaning the believers from the Children of Israel, as As-Suddi said. Yahya bin Salam said: The people here are Moses. Al-Farra’ said: It is a plural that is intended to mean one person, like His statement: Those to whom the people said (Al Imran 3:173). It is Nu’aym bin Mas’ud, as mentioned above. Do not rejoice means do not show off or be arrogant. Indeed, God does not like the exultant meaning the arrogant, as Mujahid and Al-Suddi said. The poet said: I am not happy when life makes me happy, nor do I humble myself in its changing circumstances. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is do not rejoice over money, because rejoicing over money does not fulfill its right. Mubashar ibn Abdullah said: Do not rejoice, lest you spoil it. The poet said: If you do not cease fulfilling a trust and settling another, the deposits will make you happy, i.e., they will spoil you. Abu Amr said: The debt made him happy means it burdened him. And he made it more difficult: If you... the house. And his secret made him happy, so it is the same. Al-Zajjaj said: The happy ones and the happy ones are the same. Al-Farraa differentiated between them and said: The meaning of the happy ones is those who are in a state of joy, and the happy ones are those who will rejoice in the future. He claimed that the same applies to greed and covetous, dead and dead. Evidence contrary to what he said is the statement of God the Almighty: Indeed, you will die, and indeed, they will die Az-Zumar 39:30, and He did not say dead. Mujahid also said: The meaning of do not rejoice is do not seek God does not like the happy ones, i.e., the transgressors. Ibn Bahr said: Do not be stingy, for God does not like arrogance and transgression.
28:77: The Almighty says: And seek, through that which God has given you, the home of the Hereafter. That is, seek, through that which God has given you of this world and the home of the Hereafter, which is Paradise. For it is the right of the believer to spend this world in that which will benefit him in the Hereafter, not in tyranny and oppression. God the Almighty said: And do not neglect your portion of this world. There is a difference of opinion regarding this. Ibn Abbas and the majority said: Do not waste your life in not doing righteous deeds in this world, as the Hereafter is only known for it, and a person's portion is his lifespan and his righteous deeds in it. So, according to this interpretation, it is a severe admonition. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: It means, do not waste your portion of this world in enjoying and seeking lawful things, and in considering the consequences of this world. So, according to this interpretation, it is about being gentle with him and correcting the matter he desires. This is something that must be used with the one being admonished, for fear of being severe, as stated by Ibn Atiyyah. I said: These two interpretations were combined by Ibn Umar in his saying: Plough for your worldly life as if you will live forever, and work for your afterlife as if you will die tomorrow. And from Al-Hasan, he mentioned the surplus and withheld what he could. Malik said: It is eating and drinking without extravagance. And it was said: By his share he meant the shroud. So this is a continuous sermon, as if they were saying: Do not forget that you will leave all of your wealth except this share of yours, which is the shroud. And something similar to this is the saying of the poet: Your share of what all time has gathered is two garments in which you wrap yourself and embalming materials. Look at the one who owned the whole world. Did he leave it with anything but cotton and a shroud? Al-Arabi said: The most creative thing about it, in my opinion, is the saying of Qatada: And do not forget your lawful portion, for it is your portion in this world, and how good this is. “And do good as God has done good to you,” meaning, obey God and worship Him as He has bestowed upon you. And from this is the hadith: What is ihsan? He said: It is to worship God as if you see Him. And it was said: It is an order to be kind to the poor.” Ibn al-Arabi said: There are many sayings about it, the gist of which is using God’s blessings in obeying Him. Malik said: Eating and drinking without extravagance. Ibn al-Arabi said: “I think that Malik wanted to refute those who go to extremes in worship and asceticism, for the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) loved sweets, drank honey, used to eat barbecued meat, and drank cold water. This meaning has been mentioned in more than one place.” And do not seek to spread corruption on the earth, meaning, do not commit sins. Indeed, God does not like corrupters.
28:78: God the Almighty said: He said, 'It was only given to me because of knowledge I have.' Meaning the knowledge of the Torah. It was narrated that he was the most knowledgeable of people about it and the most knowledgeable about it. He was one of the seventy scholars chosen by Moses for the appointment. Ibn Zayd said: It was only given to me because of his knowledge of my virtue and his pleasure with me. His saying, with me, means that I have that God the Almighty gave me these treasures because of his knowledge that I deserved them because of his virtue in me. It was also said: It was given to me because of my knowledge of the ways of trade and earnings, as Ali ibn Isa said. He did not know that if God had not made it easy for him to acquire them, he would not have gathered them with him. Ibn Abbas said: Because of my knowledge of the art of goldsmithing, referring to the science of alchemy. Al-Naqqash narrated: Moses, peace be upon him, taught him a third of the art of alchemy, Joshua a third, and Aaron a third. Korah, who was a believer, deceived them both until he learned what they had and practiced alchemy, so his wealth increased. It was also said that Moses taught alchemy to three: Joshua bin Nun, Caleb bin Yufana, and Korah. Al-Zajjaj chose the first opinion and rejected the statement of those who said that he practiced alchemy. He said: Because alchemy is false and has no basis in reality. It was also said that Moses taught his sister alchemy, and she was the wife of Qalun. Moses’ sister taught Korah, and God knows best. God the Almighty says: Did he not know that God had destroyed before him meaning the punishment. Of the generations meaning the disbelieving nations. Those mightier than him in strength and greater in accumulation meaning of wealth. If wealth indicated superiority, He would not have destroyed them. It was said that strength refers to tools, and the accumulation refers to helpers and supporters. The statement was made as a rebuke from God the Almighty to Qarun, meaning, Did Qarun not know that God had destroyed before him the generations? “And the criminals will not be asked about their sins” meaning, they will not be asked. A question of seeking repentance, as He said: Nor will they be asked to repent (An-Nahl 16:84), So they will not be of those who are pardoned (Fussilat 41:24). Rather, they will be asked as a question of rebuke and rebuke, as He said: By your Lord, We will surely question them all (Al-Hijr 15:92). This was said by Al-Hasan. Mujahid said: The angels will not ask anyone about the criminals, for they will be known by their features, for they will be gathered with black faces and blue eyes. Qatada said: The criminals will not be asked about their sins because they are obvious and numerous, rather they will enter Hell without being held to account. It was also said: The criminals of this nation will not be asked about the sins of the ancestors who were punished in this world. It was also said: He destroyed those generations that He destroyed with knowledge of their sins, so He did not need to ask them about their sins.
28:79: The Almighty said: So he came out to his people in his finery meaning to the Children of Israel in what he saw as the finery of worldly life, such as clothing, animals, and beautification on a festival day. Al-Ghaznawi said: On Saturday. In his finery meaning with his finery. The poet said: If the people flew away for fear of death, they settled in the souls of the dead. That is, with the souls. He set out with seventy thousand of his followers, wearing saffron-colored garments. He was the first to dye his clothes saffron-colored. As-Suddi said: With a thousand white slave girls on white mules with saddles of Dhuhl and purple patches. Ibn Abbas said: He set out on gray mules. Mujahid said: On white mules with purple saddles, and wearing saffron-colored garments. That was the first day saffron was seen. Qatada said: He set out on four thousand animals wearing red garments, including a thousand white mules wearing red patches. Ibn Jurayj said: He set out on a gray mule wearing purple, and with him were three hundred slave girls on gray mules wearing red garments. Ibn Zayd said: He set out with seventy thousand wearing saffron-colored garments. Al-Kalbi said: He set out wearing a green garment that God had sent down to Moses from Paradise, but Qarun stole it from him. Jabir ibn Abdullah may God be pleased with him said: His adornment was crimson. I said: Crimson is a red form like purple, and purple in the language is a red dye, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri. “Those who desire the life of this world said, ‘Oh, would that we had like that which Qarun has been given. Indeed, he is one of great fortune.’” That is, a plentiful portion of this world. Then it was said: This is from the saying of the believers of that time, they wished for money like his, desiring this world. It was also said: It is from the saying of people who did not believe in the Hereafter nor desire it, and they are the disbelievers.
28:80: God Almighty says: And those who were given knowledge said, and they were the rabbis of the Children of Israel to those who wished for his place, Woe to you! The reward of God is better, meaning Paradise. “For whoever believes and does righteous deeds. And none will attain it except the steadfast,” meaning that none will attain righteous deeds, or none will attain Paradise in the Hereafter except those who are steadfast in obeying God. Its pronoun is permissible because it is related to the meaning of what He says: the reward of God.
28:81: God the Almighty said: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. Muqatil said: When Moses commanded the earth to swallow him up, the Children of Israel said: He only destroyed him to inherit his wealth, because he was his cousin, the brother of his father. So God the Almighty caused the earth to swallow him and his home and all his wealth after three days. Then God revealed to Moses: I will never return the earth's obedience to anyone after you. It is said: The place was swallowed up, meaning it went into the earth. And God caused the earth to swallow him up, meaning it disappeared into it. And from this is the saying of God the Almighty: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home. He was swallowed up in the earth and it was swallowed up by him. And the eclipse of the moon is its eclipse. Tha'lab said: The sun was eclipsed and the moon was eclipsed. This is the best speech. And eclipse is deficiency. It is said: So-and-so was satisfied with the eclipse, meaning deficiency. For he had no company meaning a group. To aid him other than God, and he was not among those who defended himself meaning those who resisted the eclipse that befell him. It is narrated that Qarun descended a height every day, until he reached the bottom of the lowest earth, and Israfil blew the trumpet. This has been mentioned previously, and God knows best.
28:82: The Almighty said: And those who had wished to be in his place yesterday became regretful of that wish and said, 'Woe to God!' [Woe] is a particle of regret. An-Nahhas said: The best that has been said in this regard is the statement of Al-Khalil, Sibawayh, Yunus, and Al-Kisa'i that the people were awakened or made aware, so they said, Woe. The regretful Arab says during his regret, Woe. Al-Jawhari said: Woe is a word of amazement, and 'Woe to God!' Al-Khalil said: It is separated; you say, Woe, then you begin by saying, As if. Al-Tha'labi said: Al-Farra' said, It is a word of confirmation, like you say, 'Do you not see God's creation and benevolence?' It was mentioned that a Bedouin woman said to her husband, Woe to your son! He said, Woe to him, as if he is behind the house," meaning, do you not see him? Ibn Abbas and Al-Hasan said: "Woe is a word of initiation and confirmation, and its meaning is: Indeed, God expands provision." It was said: It is an alert, like ala in your saying won’t you do and amma in your saying how about as for now. The poet said: She asked me for divorce when she saw me. She said, Why have you come to me with something strange? And as if he who has a lineage is loved, and he who is poor lives a life of hardship. Qatrib said: It is Woe to you. He dropped the lam and added the kaf, which is for addressing, to woe. Antara said: The saying of the knights, Woe to Antar, has healed my soul and cured its illness. An-Nahhas and others denied it and said: The meaning is not correct because the people did not address anyone and say to him Woe to you, and if that were the case then it would have been in the kasra. Also, deleting the lam from Wailak is not permissible. Some of them said: The complexity of Woe to you is that I know that, so I implied I know. Ibn al-A'rabi said: And as if God means I know. And it was said: It means, did you not see that God? Al-Qutbi said: It means mercy for you in the language of Himyar. Al-Kisa'i said: Wa has a sense of amazement. It is also narrated from him to stop at Wa and he said the word is a word of grief. And whoever said Woe to you and stopped at the Kaf, its meaning is I am amazed because God expands provision and I am amazed because the disbelievers will not succeed. The Kaf should be a letter of address and not a noun, because Wa is not something that is added. Rather, it is written connected because when it is used frequently, it makes what comes after it look like one thing. "Had it not been that God had bestowed His favor upon us with faith and mercy and protected us from the same transgression and arrogance of Qarun, He would have caused the earth to swallow us up." Al-A'mash read: "Had it not been that God had bestowed His favor upon us." Hafs read: "He would have caused the earth to swallow us up," with the subject named. The rest: with the subject named, and this is the preference of Abu Ubaid. In the version of Abdullah, it is: "Do not cause the earth to swallow us up, as you say, Go with us." Al-A'mash and Talhah ibn Musarraf read this in the same way. Abu Hatim preferred the reading of the group for two reasons: The first is his statement: "So We caused the earth to swallow him and his home."
