The second is his statement: Had it not been that God had bestowed His favor upon us, so it is more appropriate for it to be attributed to God, the Most High, because His name is close to Him. "And it is as if the disbelievers will not succeed" with God.
28:84: The Almighty’s saying: Whoever brings a good deed will have better than it. This was mentioned in An-Naml. Ikrimah said: There is nothing better than There is no god but God. Rather, the meaning is: Whoever brings “There is no god but God will have better than it. And whoever brings an evil deed meaning polytheism then those who do evil will not be recompensed except for what they used to do. That is, he will be punished in accordance with his deeds.
28:85: The Almighty says: Indeed, He who enjoined upon you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a place of return. The Surah ends with the good report of His Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) that he will return to Mecca, conquering his enemies. It was said: It is good report for him of Paradise. The first opinion is more common and is the opinion of Jabir ibn Abdullah, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others. Al-Qutbi said: A man's place of return is his country, because he goes away and then returns. Muqatil said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) left the cave at night, migrating to Medina, not on the right road, for fear of being pursued. When he returned to the road and descended to Al-Juhfah, he recognized the road to Mecca and longed for it. Gabriel said to him: God says: Indeed, He who enjoined upon you the Qur'an will surely bring you back to a place of return, meaning to Mecca, appearing over it. Ibn Abbas said: This verse was revealed in Al-Juhfah, and it was neither Meccan nor Medinan. Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas: To a place of return means: to death. It was also narrated from Mujahid, Ikrimah, Az-Zuhri and Al-Hasan: The meaning is that He will bring you back to the Day of Resurrection. This is the preferred opinion of Az-Zajjaj. It is said: Between me and you is the ‘Ad, meaning the Day of Resurrection, because people will return to it alive on that day, and Fard means was sent down. It was also narrated from Mujahid, Abu Malik and Abu Salih: To a return to Paradise. This is the opinion of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri and Ibn Abbas as well, because he entered it on the Night of the Isra’. It was also said: Because his father Adam came out of it. Say, ‘My Lord knows best,’ meaning, say to the disbelievers of Mecca when they say, Indeed, you are in manifest error, “My Lord knows best who has brought guidance and who is in manifest error,” Me or you?
28:86: The Almighty said: And you did not expect that the Scripture would be revealed to you meaning, you did not know that We would send you to a successor and send down the Qur’an to you. Except as a mercy from your Lord. Al-Kisa’i said: It is an interrupted exception meaning but. “So do not be a supporter of the disbelievers” meaning, an aid and helper to them. This has been mentioned before in this surah.
28:87: The Almighty said: And let not their words, lies, and their actions turn you away from the verses of God after they have been sent down to you. Meaning their words, lies, and their actions. Do not pay attention to them and go about your business and affairs. Jacob read: yusdunak with a jazm on the noon. He also read: yusdunak from asdahu meaning to repel him, and it is a dialect for Kalb. The poet said: People who turned people away from them with the sword as the waterwheels turn away from the noses of pigeons And invite to your Lord meaning to monotheism. This includes truce and promises. All of this was abrogated by the verse of the sword. The reason for this verse was that the Quraysh were calling on the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to venerate their idols. At that point, Satan threw the matter of the cranes into his wish, as mentioned above, and God knows best.
28:88: The Almighty said: And do not invoke with God another deity meaning do not worship other than Him, for there is no deity except Him. This is a negation of every deity to be worshipped and an affirmation of His worship. Everything will perish except His Face Mujahid said: It means except Him. Al-Sadiq said: It means His religion. Abu Al-Aaliyah and Sufyan said: It means except what is intended for His Face, meaning what is intended to draw near to Him. He said: I ask forgiveness of God for a sin that the Lord of the servants has counted. To Him belongs the face and the action. Muhammad bin Yazid said: Al-Thawri told me that he asked Abu Ubaidah about the statement of God Almighty: Everything will perish except His Face, so he said: Except for His prestige, just as you say that someone has a face among the people, meaning prestige. His is the judgment in the first and the last, and to Him you will be returned. Al-Zajjaj said: His Face is an exception. If it had been in a place other than the Qur’an, except for His Face would have been in the nominative case, meaning that everything other than His Face will perish, just as He said: Every brother is separated from his brother, by your father’s life, except for Al-Farqadhan The meaning is that every brother other than the two stars will be separated from his brother. And to Him you will return means you will return to Him.
29:1: It is entirely Meccan according to Al-Hasan, Ikrimah, Ata', and Jabr. It is entirely Medinan according to one of the opinions of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. The other opinion of both of them, which is the opinion of Yahya ibn Salam, is that it is Meccan except for ten verses from the beginning, which were revealed in Medina concerning the Muslims who were in Mecca. Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him said: It was revealed between Mecca and Medina. It has nineteen verses. God Almighty said: Alif, Lam, Meem.
29:2: God Almighty says: Do people think that they will be left to say, ‘We believe’ and they will not be tested? The statement was presented at the beginnings of the surahs. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is, God knows best. It was also said that it is the name of the surah. It was also said that it is the name of the Qur’an. Ahsab is an interrogative intended to confirm and rebuke, and its meaning is conjecture. An yatarku is in the accusative case with Hasab, and its conjunction takes the place of two objects according to Sibawayh. An the second part of An yaqulu is in the accusative case in one of two ways: meaning that they say, or that they say, or that they say. The other way is that it is for repetition, and the meaning is “Alif, Lam, Meem. * Do people think that they will be left alone?” Ahsab that they will say, ‘We believe,’ and they will not be tested? Ibn Abbas and others said: What is meant by Alif, Lam, Meem are a group of believers who were in Makkah, and the infidels from Quraysh used to harm and torture them for their Islam, such as Salamah ibn Hisham, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, Al-Walid ibn Al-Walid, Ammar ibn Yasir, Yasir’s father, Sumayyah’s mother, a number from Banu Makhzum, and others. Their chests would tighten because of this, and perhaps they would find it strange that God would allow disbelievers among the believers. Mujahid and others said: This verse was revealed as a comfort and to teach that this is God’s way of worshipping Him, as a test and trial for the believers. Ibn Atiyyah said: Even though this verse was revealed for this reason or something similar in meaning, it will remain in the Ummah of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and its ruling will exist for the rest of time. This is because the trial from God will remain in the borders of the Muslims with captivity, the affliction of the enemy, and other things. If every place is considered, then it will have diseases and various types of trials. However, what resembles the ordeal of the Muslims with the Quraysh is what we mentioned about the matter of the enemy in every border. I said: How beautiful what he said, and he was truthful in what he said, may God be pleased with him. Muqatil said: It was revealed about Mahja’, the freed slave of Umar ibn al-Khattab, who was the first of the Muslims on the day of Badr. Amir ibn al-Hadrami shot him with an arrow and killed him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on that day: The martyrs will fill Mahja’, and he is the first of this nation to be called to the gates of Paradise. His parents and wife were grieved for him, so the following was revealed: “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left alone?” Al-Sha’bi said: The opening of this Surah was revealed about some Muslims who were in Mecca. The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to them from al-Hudaybiyyah that their declaration of Islam would not be accepted until they fought one another. So they left, but the polytheists pursued them and harmed them. So this verse was revealed about them: “Alif, Lam, Meem. Do people think that they will be left alone?” So they wrote to them: Such and such a verse has been revealed about you. They said: We will go out, and if anyone follows us, we will fight him. So the polytheists followed them and said: We will fight them. But those who had previously prevented them, and some of them escaped, so this verse was revealed about them: Then your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted. (al-Nahl 16:110) and they are being tested means they are being tested. That is, I think that those who were alarmed by the harm of the polytheists will be persuaded to say, We are believers, and they will not be tested in their faith, their lives, and their wealth with what will reveal the truth of their faith.
29:3: The Almighty said: And We certainly tried those before them meaning, We tested those who came before, like Abraham who was thrown into the distance, and like a people who were sawed with saws for the sake of God's religion but did not turn back from it. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Khabbab ibn al-Arat: They said: We complained to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while he was reclining on his cloak in the shade of the Kaaba. We said to him: Will you not seek victory for it? Will you not pray for us? He said: "There were those before you who would seize a man, and a hole would be dug for him in the ground, and he would be placed in it. Then a saw would be brought and placed on his head, cut in half, and his flesh and bones would be combed with iron combs, but that did not turn him from his religion. By God, this matter will be completed until a rider will travel from Sana'a to Hadramawt fearing none but God and the wolf for his sheep, but you are impatient." Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri who said: I entered upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) while he was ill. I put my hand on him and felt his heat between my hands above the blanket. I said: O Messenger of God, how hard it is for you. He said: This is how we are; the trial is doubled for us and the reward is doubled for us. She said: O Messenger of God, which people are most severely tested? He said: The Prophets. I said: Then who? He said: Then the righteous, if one of them is tested with poverty until he finds nothing but a cloak which he loves, and if one of them rejoices in the trial as one of you rejoices in prosperity. Sa'id ibn Abi Waqqas narrated: I said: O Messenger of God, which people are most severely tested? He said: The Prophets, then the next most like him, then the next most like him. A man is tested according to his religious commitment. If his religious commitment is firm, his trial will be severe, but if his religious commitment is weak, he will be tested according to his religious commitment. Trials will not leave a person until they leave him walking on the earth with no sin upon him. “Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid narrated that Jesus, peace be upon him, had a minister. One day he rode a horse and a wild animal seized him and ate him. Jesus said: ‘O Lord, he is my minister in your religion, my helper against the Children of Israel, and my successor over them. You have set a dog over him and it has eaten him.’ He said: ‘Yes, he had a high status with me, but I did not find his deeds able to reach it, so I tested him with this in order for him to reach that status.’” Wahb said: “I read in the book of one of the disciples: ‘If you are taken on the path of affliction, it will make your eyes poor, for it has taken you on the path of the prophets and the righteous. But if you are taken on the path of ease, then weep for yourself, for you have been deviated from its path.’” God the Almighty says: Then God will surely make evident those who are truthful. That is, God will surely show those who are truthful in their faith. This meaning has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah and other verses. Al-Zajjaj said: “So that the truthfulness of the truthful person may be known by his truthfulness. He knew the truthful person from the liar before He created them both, but the intention was for the knowledge of what he would be rewarded for to come true. He only knows the truthfulness of the truthful person in reality and in the event that it will occur, and He knew that it would occur.” An-Nahhas said: “There are two opinions on this: One of them is that “they believed” is derived from truth and the liars is derived from lie which is the opposite of truthfulness, so the meaning would be, So God will make evident those who were truthful and said, ‘We are believers’ and believed the same, and those who lied when they believed otherwise. The other opinion is that they believed is derived from truth which means steadfastness, and the liars is derived from lie which means to be defeated. So the meaning would be, God will surely make evident those who stood firm in war and those who were defeated, as the poet said: A lion that has scattered and hunts men if the lion lies about his peers, he has made la`lamn in place of filabayyunna as a metaphor. The reading of the group is falay`lamn with a fatha on the ya’ and the lam. Ali bin Abi Talib read it with a damma on the ya’ and a kasra on the lam, which explains the meaning of what An-Nahhas said. It has three possible meanings: The first: That He will make known in the Hereafter these truthful and liars with their status in His reward and punishment and with their deeds in this world, meaning that He will make them aware of what they did. The second: That the first object is omitted, meaning, So let the people and the world know these truthful and liars, meaning He will disgrace them and make them evil, these in good and those in evil, and that is in this world and the Hereafter. The third: That it is from the sign, meaning He places for every sect a sign by which it is known. So the verse according to this has reference to the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Whoever conceals a secret, God will clothe him in its cloak.
29:4: God the Almighty says: Or do those who do evil deeds think that they can outsmart Us meaning, they will overtake Us and defeat Us before We hold them accountable for what they do? Ibn Abbas said: He means Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, Abu Jahl, Al-Aswad, Al-‘As ibn Hisham, Shaibah, ‘Utbah, Al-Walid ibn ‘Utbah, ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu’it, Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan, and Al-‘As ibn Wa’il. Evil is that which they judge meaning evil is the judgment they make concerning the attributes of their Lord, that He is preceded, while God is Able to do all things. Ma is in the accusative case meaning evil is a thing or judgment they judge. It is also permissible for Ma to be in the nominative case meaning evil is a thing or judgment. This is the opinion of Al-Zajjaj. Ibn Kaysan estimated it with two other estimates other than those: First, that the position of Ma Yahkimun is like a single thing, as you say, I liked what you did, meaning your action. So Ma and the verb are a verbal noun in the nominative case, the estimate being evil is their judgment. Another interpretation is that ma has no syntactic position, and it has taken the place of the noun for sa’a, and likewise for na’am and bi’sa. Abu al-Hasan ibn Kaysan said: I prefer to give ma a position in everything I am able to do, like the saying of the Almighty: Then by mercy from God (Al Fir’awn: 159) and also Then by their breaking of the covenant (al-Ma’idah 5:13) and also Which of the two terms you fulfill (al-Qasas 28:28). ma is in the accusative case in all of this and what follows is subordinate to it, and likewise, Indeed, God is not ashamed to make an example of a mosquito (al-Baqarah 2:26). ma is in the accusative case and mosquito is subordinate to it.
29:5: The Almighty said: Whoever hopes for the meeting with God - then indeed, the term of God is coming. Hope means fear, as Al-Hudhali said in describing Asal: If a bee stings him, he will not be stung by it The commentators agreed that the meaning is: Whoever fears death, let him do righteous deeds, for it will inevitably come to him. An-Nahhas mentioned this. Az-Zajjaj said: The meaning of hopes to meet God is the reward of God. Min is in the nominative case as a subject in the position of a predicate, and it is in the position of a jussive mood due to the condition. Yarju is in the position of a predicate of kana, and the recompense is for the term of God is coming, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
29:6: God the Almighty says: And whoever strives, strives only for himself meaning, whoever strives in the religion, and is patient in fighting the disbelievers and performing acts of obedience, then he only strives for himself, meaning that the reward for that is all for him, and no benefit from that returns to God. Indeed, God is free from need of the worlds meaning, from their deeds. It was said that the meaning is, whoever strives for himself, not seeking the face of God, then God has no need of his striving.
29:7: God the Almighty says: And those who have believed meaning, have been truthful and done righteous deeds - We will surely remove from them their misdeeds meaning, We will cover them by forgiving them. And We will surely reward them with the best of what they used to do meaning, with their best deeds, which are acts of obedience. Then it was said: It is possible that every sin they committed in polytheism will be removed from them, and they will be rewarded for the good deeds they did in Islam. It is also possible that their misdeeds in both disbelief and Islam will be removed from them, and they will be rewarded for their good deeds in both disbelief and Islam.
29:8: The Almighty’s saying: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. This was revealed about Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, as narrated by Al-Tirmidhi. He said: It was revealed in four verses, and he mentioned a story. Sa’d’s mother said: Hasn’t God commanded us to be dutiful? By God, I will not eat food or drink anything until I die or become an unbeliever. He said: Whenever they wanted to feed her, they would open her mouth, and this verse was revealed: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. Abu ‘Eisa said: This is a good and authentic hadith. It was narrated on the authority of Sa’d that he said: I was dutiful to my mother, so I converted to Islam. She said, “Either you abandon your religion, or I will not eat or drink until I die, and you will be mocked at me and it will be said, ‘O killer of your mother.’ I lived a day and then I said, ‘O mother, even if you had a hundred souls, and they came out one by one, I would not abandon this religion of mine. So if you wish, eat, and if you wish, do not eat.’ When she saw that, she ate and the following verse was revealed: “But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me…” 17:1. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, the maternal brother of Abu Jahl, and his mother did the same. It was also narrated from him: It was revealed about the entire nation if they are patient in the face of God’s trial, except for a friend. And good is in the accusative case according to the Basrans for repetition, meaning, We enjoined him to do good. It was said: It is with definiteness, and we enjoined him to do good, just as you say, I enjoined him to do good, meaning to do good. The people of Kufa said: It was interpreted as, And We enjoined upon man to do good, so he was destined to do it. The poet said: I am amazed at Dahma when they complain about us, and at Abu Dahma when he advises us. Good for them, as if they feared us He advises us to do good to them, as in his saying, So he began to wipe [p. 33], meaning he wiped. It was said that its meaning is, And We enjoined upon him a good matter, so the adjective was used in place of the described, the complement was deleted and the complement to it was used in its place. It was said that its meaning is, We obliged him to do good. The reading of the common people is: Hasan with a damma on the ha’ and a sukoon on the seen. Abu Raja’, Abu Al-Aliyah and Ad-Dahhak read it with a fatha on the ha’ and the seen. Al-Jahdary read: Ihsanan as a verbal noun, and this is also in the Mushaf of Abu, the meaning is: And We enjoined upon man to do good to them, goodness. It is not made accusative by our enjoining, because it has already completed its two objects. To Me is your return is a warning against obeying parents in the sense of disbelief. Then I will inform you of what you used to do.
29:9: The Almighty says: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will surely admit them among the righteous. The Almighty repeated the example of the state of the faithful workers to motivate souls to attain their ranks. His statement: We will surely admit them among the righteous is an exaggeration in meaning, for those are at the pinnacle of righteousness and its furthest ends. If the believer attains this ruling, he will attain its fruit and reward, which is Paradise.
29:10: God the Almighty says: And of the people is he who says, 'We believe in God,' This verse was revealed about the hypocrites who used to say, We believe in God. But when he is harmed for the sake of God, he considers the trial of the people i.e., their harm to be like the punishment of God" in the Hereafter, so he turns away from his faith. It was said: He was alarmed by that just as he is alarmed by the punishment of God and cannot be patient about the Hereafter, so he turned away from his faith. It was also said: He was alarmed by that just as he is alarmed by the punishment of God and cannot be patient about being harmed for the sake of God. "And if victory comes to the believers from your Lord, these apostates will surely say, Indeed, we were with you, but they are lying. So God said about them: Is not God more knowing of what is in the breasts of the worlds? Meaning, God knows what is in their breasts better than they know themselves. Mujahid said: This was revealed about people who believed with their tongues, but when a trial from God or a calamity befalls them, they are tempted. Ad-Dahhak said: It was revealed about some hypocrites in Makkah who used to believe, but when they were harmed, they would return to polytheism. Ikrimah said: “Some people had embraced Islam, but the polytheists forced them to go out with them to Badr. Some of them were killed, so God revealed: ‘Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves…’” (An-Nisa’: 97) So the Muslims in Madinah wrote about it to the Muslims in Makkah, so they went out and the polytheists caught up with them, and some of them were tempted, so this verse was revealed about them. It was also said: “It was revealed about ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah. He embraced Islam and then abandoned it, then he was harmed and injured and apostatized. Abu Jahl and Al-Harith, his two half-brothers, tortured him. Ibn ‘Abbas said: “He lived for a long time after that and his Islam was good.”
29:11: God Almighty says: And God will surely make evident those who believe and He will surely make evident the hypocrites. Qatada said: It was revealed about the people whom the polytheists returned to Mecca.
29:12: God Almighty said: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, ‘Follow our way’ meaning our religion. And We will bear your sins is a command. Al-Farra’ and Al-Zajjaj said: It is a command in the interpretation of the condition and consequence, meaning if you follow our way, we will bear your sins, as He said: I said, Call and call, for the most beautiful voice is when two callers call. That is, if you call, I will call. Al-Mahdawi said: The occurrence of indeed, they are liars after it is based on the meaning, because the meaning is: if you follow our path, we will bear your sins. So since the matter goes back in meaning to the report, the denial was applied to it as it is applied to the report. Mujahid said: The polytheists of Quraysh said: We and you will not be resurrected, so if there is a burden upon you, then upon us, meaning we will bear what is required of you. And bearing here means carrying, not carrying on the back. It was narrated that the one who said that was Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira.
29:13: The Almighty's statement: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens besides their own burdens means that they will bear the sins of those they wronged after their own good deeds are finished. This meaning was narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and it was mentioned earlier in Al Imran. Abu Umamah al-Bahili said: [The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection with many good deeds, and retribution will continue to be taken from him until his good deeds are used up. Then he will be called to account, and God, the Almighty, will say: 'Take retribution from Me.' The angels will say: 'What good deeds remain for him?' Then he will be called to account, and God, the Almighty, will say: 'Take retribution from My servant.' The angels will say: 'What good deeds remain for him?' He will say: 'Take from the sins of the wronged one and place them on him.'" Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens besides their own burdens. Qatadah said: Whoever calls to misguidance will bear its burden and the burden of those who act upon it, without detracting from their burden in the slightest. Similar to this is the saying of God the Almighty: That they may bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection, and also some of the burdens of those whom they misled without knowledge (al-Nahl 16:25). Similar to this is the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): Whoever introduces an evil into Islam will bear its burden and the burden of those who act upon it after him, without that detracting from their burden in the slightest. This was narrated from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and others. Al-Hasan said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Whoever calls people to guidance, is followed and acts upon it, will have a reward like that of those who follow him, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. But whoever calls people to misguidance, is followed and acts upon it after him, will have a burden like that of those who act upon it among those who follow him, without that detracting from their burden in the slightest.” Then Al-Hasan recited: And they will bear their own burdens and other burdens with their burdens. I said: This is mursal and it is the meaning of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, which was narrated by Muslim. The text of the hadith of Anas ibn Malik on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) is that he said: “Anyone who calls to misguidance and is followed will have a burden like that of those who follow him, without it detracting from their reward in the slightest. Anyone who calls to guidance and is followed will have a reward like that of those who follow him, without it detracting from their reward in the slightest.” Narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Sunan. There are other hadiths on this topic from Abu Jahfiyah and Jarir. It has been said that what is meant is the helpers of oppressors. It has also been said that it means the innovators if they are followed in their innovations. It has also been said that it means the innovators of new traditions if those who come after them know about them. The meanings are close and the hadith encompasses all of that.
29:14: God the Almighty says: And We had certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years. The story of Noah was mentioned as a consolation to his Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), meaning that the prophets before you were tested by the disbelievers, but they were patient. Noah was mentioned specifically because he was the first messenger sent to the Earth, which was filled with disbelief, as was previously explained in Hud. And no prophet from his people encountered what Noah encountered, as was previously explained in Hud, on the authority of Al-Hasan. It was narrated on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Anas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The first prophet sent was Noah. Qatada said: He was sent from the Arabian Peninsula. There is a difference of opinion regarding the length of his life. Some say: The length of his life is what God the Almighty mentioned in His Book. Qatada said: He remained among them for three hundred years before he called them, and he called them for three hundred years, and he remained after the flood for three hundred and fifty years. Ibn Abbas said: Noah was sent when he was forty years old, and he remained among his people for a thousand years minus fifty. He lived for sixty years after the flood until people became numerous and widespread. It was also narrated from him that he was sent when he was two hundred and fifty years old, and he remained among them for a thousand years minus fifty, and he lived two hundred years after the flood. Wahb said: Noah lived for a thousand four hundred years. Kaab al-Ahbar said: Noah remained among his people for a thousand years minus fifty, and he lived for three hundred and fifty years after the flood, so his total age was one thousand six hundred and fifty years. A similar narration was narrated from al-Hasan. al-Hasan said: When the Angel of Death came to Noah to take his soul, he said: O Noah, how long have you lived in this world? He said: Three hundred before I was sent, and a thousand years minus fifty among my people, and three hundred and fifty years after the flood. The Angel of Death said: How did you find this world? Noah said: It is like a house with two doors, you enter through this and exit through that. It was narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “When God sent Noah to his people, He sent him when he was two hundred and fifty years old. He stayed among his people for one thousand years minus fifty, and he remained after the flood for two hundred and fifty years. When the Angel of Death came to him, he said: ‘O Noah, O greatest of the prophets, O tall one, O long-lived one, O one whose prayers are answered, how do you see this world?’ He said: ‘It is like a man who has a house built for him with two doors. He enters through one and exits through the other.’” Ibn al-Wardi said: Noah built a house of reeds, and it was said to him: ‘If only you had built something other than this.’ He said: ‘That is too much for one who dies.’ Abu al-Muhajir said: ‘If only Noah had lived with his people for one thousand years minus fifty, then he would have stopped at a house of hair.’ It was said to him: ‘O Prophet of God, build a house.’ He said: ‘I will die today or I will die tomorrow.’” Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Five hundred years passed for Noah during which he did not approach women, and he was afraid of death. Muqatil and Juwaybir said: When Adam (peace be upon him) grew old and his bones became frail, he said, O Lord, how long will I labor and strive? He said, O Adam, until a circumcised son is born to you. So Noah was born to him after ten wombs, and he was then a thousand years old minus sixty. Some of them said, minus forty years. And God knows best. Noah was the son of Lamech, the son of Methuselah, the son of Idris, who is Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Cainan, the son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam. Noah’s name was Sakan home. He was called Sakan home because people after Adam inhabited him, and he was their father. He had Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Shem fathered the Arabs, the Persians, and the Romans, and in all of these there was goodness. Japheth fathered the Turks, the Slavs, Gog and Magog. There is no goodness in any of these. Ibn Abbas said: In the children of Shem there was whiteness and swarthiness, and in the children of Ham there was blackness and a little whiteness. In the children of Japheth—who are the Turks and the Slavs—there was yellowness and redness. He had a fourth son, Canaan, who would drown. He would call them to God, the Most High. When they disbelieved, he would cry and wail over them. Al-Qushayri Abu Qasim Abdul Karim mentioned in his book Al-Takhbir: He believes that Noah’s name was Yashkur, but because of his frequent crying over his sin, God revealed to him, O Noah, how much you wail. So he was named Noah. It was said, O Messenger of God, what was his sin? He said, He passed by a dog and said to himself, ‘What is wrong with me?’ So God revealed to him, ‘Create something better than this.’ Yazid Al-Raqashi said, He was named Noah because of how much he wailed over himself. If it is said: Why did He say: one thousand years minus fifty years and not say nine hundred and fifty years? There are two answers to this: The first: What is meant by it is to increase the number, so the mention of the thousand was more in wording and more in number. The second: What was narrated that he was given a thousand years of life, so he gave fifty years of his life to some of his children, and when death approached him, he went back to completing the thousand, so God Almighty mentioned that to indicate that the deficiency was from him. So the flood seized them. Ibn Abbas, Saeed bin Jubair, and Qatada said: rain. Ad-Dahhak: drowning. And it was said: death. It was narrated by Aisha, may God be pleased with her, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And from it is the saying of the poet: A devastating flood of death swept them away. An-Nahhas said: It is said of every great deal that encompasses everyone, whether it be rain, killing, or flooding death, and they are wrongdoers. It is a clause in the position of a circumstantial adverbial phrase, and a thousand years is in the accusative case as an adverbial phrase. Except fifty years is in the accusative case as an exception to the imperative. According to Sibawayh, it is like a direct object because it is dispensed with like a direct object. As for Al-Mubarrad, Abu Al-Abbas Muhammad bin Yazid, it is a direct object. It is as if you said you excepted Zayd. Warning: Hassan bin Ghaleb bin Nujayh Abu Al-Qasim Al-Masry narrated, Malik bin Anas narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Gabriel used to remind me of the merits of Umar, so I said, ‘O Gabriel, how much do you reach the merits of Umar?’ He said to me, ‘O Muhammad, if I had stayed with you as long as Noah stayed among his people, I would not have reached the merits of Umar for you.’” Al-Khatib Abu Bakr bin Thabit Al-Baghdadi mentioned this, and he said: Hassan bin Ghaleb is the only one who narrated it on the authority of Malik, and his hadith is not authentic.
29:15: The Almighty’s saying: So We saved him and the companions of the ship is connected to the ha “and made it a sign for the worlds.” The ha and the alif in made it refer to the ship, or to the punishment, or to salvation. There are three opinions.
29:16: The Almighty says: And Abraham. Al-Kisa'i said: And Abraham is in the accusative case because of We saved, meaning it is in apposition to. Al-Kisa'i considered it permissible for it to be in apposition to Noah, and the meaning is, And We sent Abraham. A third opinion is that it is in the accusative case meaning Abraham repeated. When he said to his people, 'Worship God,' meaning, single Him out for worship. And fear Him, meaning, fear His punishment and chastisement. That is better for you, better than worshipping idols, if you only knew.
29:17: God the Almighty says: You only worship idols besides God meaning statues. Abu Ubaidah said: The Dammah is what is made from gold, silver, or copper, and the idol is what is made from plaster or stones. Al-Jawhari: An idol is a statue, and the plural is wathn and awthun, lions and lions. And you create falsehood Al-Hasan said: The meaning of you create is that you carve, so the meaning is that you only worship idols and you manufacture them. Mujahid said: Ifk is lying, and the meaning is that you worship idols and create lies. Abu Abd Al-Rahman read: and you create. It was also read: you create meaning to increase from creation, and you create from you lie meaning to lie and fabricate. It was also read: afka and there are two interpretations: that it is a verbal noun like kadhab and laab and ifk is a lightened form of it like kadhab and al-ifk and it is an adjective on the basis of fa`l, meaning a false creation, meaning of falsehood and invalidity. And (idols is in the accusative case because of you worship and what is a conjunction. It is permissible to raise awthān in the nominative case other than in the Qur’an, making what the subject of an, and you worship its relative clause, and the ha’ was deleted due to the length of the noun and making awthān the predicate of in. As for takhalafūn ifkān, it is in the accusative case because of the verb and nothing else. And likewise, They do not possess for you provision, so seek provision from God meaning direct your desire for your provisions to God, so ask Him alone and not anyone else.
29:18: The Almighty said: And if you deny, then nations before you have denied. It was said: It is from the words of Abraham, meaning that denying is the habit of the infidels, and the messengers are only responsible for conveying the message.
29:19: The Almighty says: Have they not seen how God originates creation? The general reading is with the letter ya as a statement and a rebuke to them, and this is the preference of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. Abu Ubaid said: When mentioning the nations, it is as if he said, Have they not seen the nations how? Abu Bakr, Al-A'mash, Ibn Waththab, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read tarawa with the letter ta as an address, because of His statement, And if you deny. It has also been said that And if you deny is an address to Quraysh and is not from the words of Abraham. Then He will repeat it means succession and resurrection. It has also been said that the meaning is, Have they not seen how God originates the fruits, so they come to life and then perish, then He will repeat them forever? Likewise, He begins the creation of man, then takes possession of him after creating from him a son, and from the son a son. And likewise with all other animals. So if you see His ability to originate and bring into existence, then He is able to repeat. Indeed, that, for God, is easy, because when He wants a thing, He says to it, Be, and it is.
29:20: The Almighty said: Say, ‘Travel through the land.’ That is, tell them, O Muhammad, travel through the land. And see how He began creation. Despite their multitude, varying forms, different languages, colors, and natures, and look at the dwellings of past generations, their destruction, and their traces, how He destroyed them, so that you may know thereby the perfection of God’s power. Then God will produce the final creation. Abu Amr and Ibn Kathir read: an-nasha’ah with a fat-ha on the shin, and they are two dialects like ra’fah and ra’afah and the like. Al-Jawhari said: God created him, and the noun is an-nasha’ah and an-nasha’ah, and with a long vowel, according to Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’. Indeed, God has power over all things.
29:21: The Almighty said: And He punishes whom He wills meaning with His justice. And He has mercy on whom He wills meaning with His grace. And to Him you will be returned means you will return and be returned. And you will not frustrate Him on earth or in heaven Al-Farra’ said: Its meaning is nor will those in heaven frustrate God and it is ambiguous in Arabic, because of the pronoun that did not appear in the second part. It is like Hassan’s saying: So whoever among you satirizes the Messenger of God, praises him, and supports him, it is the same. He wanted to praise and support him equally, so he implied min, as Abdurrahman ibn Zayd said. Similar to it is the saying of God, the Most High: And there is not one of us but has a known position. (37:164) meaning who has. The meaning is that the people of the earth on earth and the people of the heavens are not beyond God’s power if they disobey Him. Qatrib said: Not even in the heavens if you were in them, just as you say: So-and-so cannot escape me in Basra or here, meaning he cannot escape me in Basra if he went to it. It was said: They cannot escape on the earth or in the heavens. Al-Mubarrad said: The meaning is not even in the heavens, based on the fact that min is not a relative pronoun, but tamun is indefinite and in the heavens is an adjective for it, so the adjective was used in place of the noun. Ali ibn Salman rejected this and said: it is not permissible. He said: If the word man is indefinite, then it must be described, and its description is like the relative clause, and it is not permissible to delete the relative pronoun and leave the relative clause. He said: The meaning is that people were addressed with what they understand, and the meaning is that if you were in the sky, you would not have been able to defeat God, as He said: Even if you were in lofty towers (An-Nisa’: 87).
29:22: God Almighty says: And you have no protector or helper besides God. It is permissible to say helper in the nominative case in the accusative case, and from is redundant.
29:23: The Almighty said: And those who disbelieve in the signs of God and the meeting with Him meaning in the Quran according to the place, and the names are those have despaired of My mercy meaning of Paradise, and despair was attributed to them, and the meaning is they have despaired. These verses are an objection from God Almighty as a reminder and warning to the people of Mecca. Then the speech returns to the story of Abraham. He said.
29:24: God Almighty says: But the answer of his people when he called them to God Almighty was only that they said, ‘Kill him or burn him.’ Then they agreed to burn him. But God saved him from the Fire meaning from its harm. There are certainly signs in that meaning in saving him from the great Fire so that it did not burn him after he was thrown into it. The general reading is: Jawab with the accusative of the ba’ as the predicate of kana and that they said is in the nominative case as the subject of kana. Salim Al-Aftas and Amr bin Dinar read: Jawab with the nominative case as the subject of kana and that is in the accusative case as the predicate.
29:25: God the Almighty said: And Abraham said, ‘You have only taken idols besides God out of affection among you in worldly life.’ Hafs and Hamzah read: affection among you. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Al-Kisa’i read: affection among you. Al-A’mash narrated from Abu Bakr from Asim and Ibn Wathab and Al-A’mash read: affection among you. The rest read: affection among you. As for Ibn Uthair’s reading, there are three interpretations. Al-Zajjaj mentioned two of them: The first is that affection is raised as a predicate of in and ma is in the meaning of who. The meaning is that what you have taken as idols besides God is affection among you. The other interpretation is that it is an implied subject, meaning it is affection or that is affection among you. The meaning is your gods or your group is affection among you. Ibn al-Anbari said: idols is a good pause for those who raised the affection by implying that it is affection between you, and for those who raised the affection as a predicate if they did not pause. The third reason that he did not mention is that affection is raised as a subject and in the life of this world is its predicate. As for adding affection to between you, then he made between you a noun not a circumstance, and grammarians say he made it a direct object for breadth. Sibawayh said: O thief of the house tonight. It is not permissible for it to be added to it while it is a circumstance for a reason that is not the place to mention it. And whoever raised affection and added a nun to it, then it has the meaning of what was mentioned, and between you in the accusative case as a circumstance. And whoever lowered affection and did not add a nun to it, made it a direct object by the occurrence of the taking on it and made only a single letter and did not make it in the meaning of the one who. It is permissible to put affection in the accusative case as a direct object, as you say: I came to you seeking good, and I intended to have affection for so-and-so between you in the genitive case. Whoever puts the nun on affection and puts it in the accusative case, then it is as mentioned between you in the accusative case without an addition. Ibn al-Anbari said: Whoever reads: affection between you and affection between you does not stop at the idols, but stops at the life of this world. The meaning of the verse is that they made the idols love one another for the sake of them and for their worship in this world. Then on the Day of Resurrection some of you will disbelieve in others and curse one another, the idols will disown their worshippers and the leaders will disown the common people, as God the Almighty said: Friends that Day will be enemies to one another, except for the righteous. (al-Zukhruf 43:67) And your refuge is the Fire is addressed to idol worshippers, both leaders and followers. It has been said that idols are included in it, as God Almighty says: Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell (Al-Anbiya’: 98).
29:26: God the Almighty says: So Lot believed in him. Lot was the first to believe in Abraham when he saw the fire as cool and safe for him. Ibn Ishaq said: Lot believed in Abraham and he was his nephew, and Sarah believed in him and she was his cousin. And he said, 'Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord.' An-Nakha'i and Qatada said: The one who said, Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord was Abraham, peace be upon him. Qatada said: He emigrated from Kutha, which is a village in the plains of Kufa, to Harran, then to Ash-Sham, with his nephew Lot bin Haran bin Tarikh, and his wife Sarah. Al-Kalbi said: He emigrated from the land of Harran to Palestine. He was the first to emigrate from the land of disbelief. Muqatil said: Abraham emigrated when he was seventy-five years old. It was said: The one who said, Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord was Lot, peace be upon him. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Qatada who said: The first person to migrate to God Almighty with his family was Uthman ibn Affan may God be pleased with him. Qatada said: I heard Al-Nadr ibn Anas say: I heard Abu Hamza, meaning Anas ibn Malik, say: Uthman ibn Affan set out with Ruqayyah, the daughter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), to the land of Abyssinia. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was slow to receive report of them. A woman from Quraysh came and said: O Muhammad, I saw your brother-in-law with his wife. He said: In what state did you see them? She said: I saw him carrying his wife on a donkey like this beast and he was encouraging her. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: May God accompany them both. Uthman is the most deserving of migrating with his family after Lot. Al-Bayhaqi said: This was regarding the first migration. As for the second migration to Abyssinia, it was, as Al-Waqidi claimed, in the fifth year of the mission of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). To my Lord means to please my Lord and to what He commanded me. For He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. This was mentioned earlier. Migration was discussed earlier in Surat An-Nisa’ and elsewhere.
29:27: The Almighty says: And We bestowed upon him Isaac meaning that God bestowed upon him sons, so He bestowed upon him Isaac as a son and Jacob as a son's son. He bestowed upon him Isaac after Ishmael, and Jacob as a son of Isaac. And We bestowed upon his descendants prophethood and the Scripture God did not send a prophet after Abraham except from his loins. He used the singular form of the Scripture because He intended the source, like prophethood, and what is meant is the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion. So it is an expression of the plural. The Torah was sent down to Moses from the descendants of Abraham, the Gospel to Jesus from his descendants, and the Criterion to Muhammad from his descendants, may God's prayers and peace be upon him and upon them all. And We gave him his reward in this world means that all religions would agree upon him, as stated by Ikrimah. Sufyan narrated on the authority of Humayd ibn Qays who said: Saeed ibn Jubayr ordered a man to ask Ikrimah about the words of God, the Most High: And We gave him his reward in this world. Ikrimah said: All religions claim him and say he is one of us. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: He has spoken the truth. Qatadah said: “It is similar to His words: “And We gave him good in this world” (An-Nahl 16:122), meaning a good outcome, righteous deeds, and good praise. This is because the people of his religion followed him. It was said: We gave him his reward in this world means that most of the prophets were from his descendants. And indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous. “In the Hereafter” is not included in the relative clause, but rather it is a clarification. This has been explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah. All of this is an encouragement to follow the example of Abraham in being patient in adhering to the true religion.
29:28: God the Almighty says: And Lot, when he said to his people Al-Kisa'i said: The meaning is, And We saved Lot or We sent Lot. He said: This interpretation is more preferable to me. It is also possible that the meaning is, "And mention Lot when he said to his people, rebuking or warning them: "Indeed, you commit an immorality such as no one before you has committed before among the worlds." Do you The reading of this and its explanation were presented previously in Surat Al-A'raf. The story of Lot and his people were presented previously in Al-A'raf and Hud as well. "And you block the way" It was said: They were highwaymen, said by Ibn Zayd. It was said: They used to take people from the roads to commit immorality, narrated by Ibn Shajarah. It was said: It means cutting off offspring by switching from women to men, said by Wahb ibn Munabbih. That is, they were satisfied with men instead of women. I said: Perhaps everyone was among them, so they used to rob the road to take money and commit indecency, and thus they were satisfied with women.
29:29: God the Almighty says: And you commit evil in your assemblies. The club is the gathering. There is a difference of opinion regarding the evil that they used to commit there. A group said: They used to throw pebbles at women, and they would make light of strangers and those who spoke ill of them. "It was narrated by Umm Hani' from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Umm Hani' said: I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the statement of God the Almighty: "And you commit evil in your assemblies." He said: They used to throw pebbles at whoever passed by them and make fun of them. That was the evil that they used to commit." Narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad. It was mentioned by al-Nahhas, al-Tha'labi, al-Mahdawi, and al-Mawardi. Al-Tha'labi reported that Mu'awiyah said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: "The people of Lot used to sit in their gatherings, and every man would have a bowl of pebbles to throw. When a passerby passed by them, they would throw them, and whichever of them got it was more deserving of it." Meaning, he would go to commit the immoral act. This is what God said: And you commit evil in your gatherings. Aisha, Ibn Abbas, Al-Qasim bin Abi Buzah, and Al-Qasim bin Muhammad said: They used to fart in their gatherings. Mansour said on the authority of Mujahid: They used to come to men in their gatherings, and some of them would see others. Mujahid said: Among their practices were playing with pigeons, applying henna to their fingers, whistling, stoning, and abandoning modesty in all their affairs. Ibn Atiyyah said: These things may be found among some of the sinners among the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so refraining from them is obligatory. Makhool said: In this nation there are ten of the morals of the people of Lot: chewing gum, applying henna to the fingers, untying the lower garment, plucking the fingers, wearing a turban around the head, interlocking them, throwing stones, whistling, slander, and sodomy. Ibn Abbas said: The people of Lot committed sins other than indecency, including being unjust to one another, insulting one another, farting in their gatherings, slandering, playing dice and chess, wearing dyed clothes, fighting with roosters, butting rams, applying henna to their fingers, men dressing like women and women like men, and imposing taxes on every passerby. Despite all this, they associated partners with God and they were the first to commit sodomy and lesbianism. When Lot (peace be upon him) confronted them with these abominations, they reverted to denial and obstinacy, saying: Bring us the punishment of God, meaning that that will not happen and cannot be done. They did not say this except because they were determined to believe his lie. It is not human nature for a stubborn person to say this. Then Lot, peace be upon him, sought help from his Lord, so He sent their `Ablis angels to punish them. They came to Abraham first, bringing good report of Lot’s victory over his people, as was explained previously in Hud and other surahs. Al-A’mash, Ya`qub, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read: We will surely save him and his family with a light pronunciation. The rest stressed it. Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read: Indeed, We will save you and your family with a light pronunciation. The rest stressed it. They are the two Ghattan: Anja and Naja mean the same thing, as was previously mentioned. Ibn `Amir read: Indeed, We will send down with a heavy pronunciation, and this is the reading of Ibn `Abbas. The rest stressed it.
29:30: God Almighty said: He said, ‘My Lord, help me against the corrupting people.’
29:31: God Almighty says: “And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, ‘Indeed, we will destroy the people of this city. Indeed, its people were wrongdoers.’”
29:32: God Almighty said: “He said, ‘Indeed, within it is Lot.’ They said, ‘We know best who is within it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind.’”
29:33: God Almighty says: “And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed because of them and felt straitened for them and said, ‘Do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will save you and your family, except for your wife; she will be among those who remain behind.’”
29:34: God Almighty says: Indeed, We will send down upon the people of this city a punishment from the sky because they were defiantly disobedient.
29:35: God Almighty said: And We have certainly left of it a clear sign for a people who use reason. Qatada said: They are the stones that were left. Abu Al-Aaliyah said the same. It was also said: Some people from this nation will be stoned with them. Ibn Abbas said: They are the traces of their ruined homes. Mujahid said: It is the black water on the surface of the earth. All of that will remain, so there is no contradiction.
29:36: The Almighty said: And to Madyan We sent their brother Shu'ayb meaning, We sent to Madyan, and their mention and corruption have already been made in Al-A'raf and Hud. And hope for the Last Day Yunus the grammarian said: meaning, fear the Hereafter in which there is recompense for deeds. And do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption meaning, do not disbelieve, for it is the root of all corruption. Uthw and Uthy are the most severe forms of corruption. Uthy and Uthy have the same meaning. This has already been mentioned. It has also been said: And hope for the Last Day meaning, believe in it, for the people used to deny it.
29:37: God Almighty says: But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became within their homes, fallen down.
29:38: The Almighty says: And 'Aad and Thamud. Al-Kisa'i said: Some of them said that it refers to the beginning of the surah, meaning, And We certainly tested those before them and tested 'Aad and Thamud. He said: I prefer it to be conjoined with and the earthquake seized them and seized 'Aad and Thamud. Al-Zajjaj claimed that the meaning is, And We destroyed 'Aad and Thamud. It was also said that the meaning is, "And remember 'Aad when We sent to them Hud, but they denied him, so We destroyed them. And to Thamud also, We sent Salih, but they denied him, so We destroyed them with the blast, just as We destroyed 'Aad with the barren wind." And indeed, O company of disbelievers, there are signs from their dwellings in Al-Hijr and Al-Ahqaf, indicating their destruction, so the subject of making clear was omitted. And Satan made their deeds pleasing to them, meaning their vile deeds, so they thought them exalted. So He averted them from the path, meaning from the path of truth. And they had insight. There are two opinions on this: One of them is: And they had insight into their misguidance. This was said by Mujahid. The second is: They had insight and knew the truth from falsehood through clear proofs. This opinion is more likely because one only says so-and-so has insight if he knows something in its true form. Al-Farra' said: They were rational people with insight, but their insight did not benefit them. It was also said: They came and it was clear to them that the punishment had befallen them.
29:39: The Almighty said: And Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman. Al-Kisa'i said: If you wish, it can be interpreted as referring to 'Aad, and it would be what it is. Or if you wish, it can be interpreted as and He averted them from the path and Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman were averted. It was also said: That is, We destroyed these people after the messengers came to them. So they were arrogant in the land from the truth and from the worship of God. And they were not forerunners meaning, they would have failed. It was also said: Forerunners in disbelief, but many centuries preceded them in disbelief, so We destroyed them.
29:40: The Almighty says: So We seized each one for his sin. Al-Kisa’i said: So each one is from the root word We seized meaning We seized each one for his sin. And among them were those upon whom We sent a violent storm meaning the people of Lot. A violent storm brings small pebbles. It is used for every punishment. And among them were those whom the blast seized meaning Thamud and the people of Madyan. And among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow meaning Qarun. And among them were those whom We drowned the people of Noah and the people of Pharaoh. And God would not wrong them because He warned them, gave them respite, sent messengers to them, and removed any excuse.
29:41: The Almighty says: The parable of those who take protectors other than God is like that of the spider. Al-Ahfash said: Like the spider is a complete pause, then he related its story and said: has taken a house. Ibn al-Anbari said: This is a mistake, because has taken a house is a relative clause for the spider, as if he said: Like the one who has taken a house. So it is not appropriate to pause at the relative clause without the relative pronoun. It is like his saying: Like the donkey who carries volumes (al-Jumuah 62:5), so it is considered a relative clause for the donkey, and it is not appropriate to pause at the spider, because when he intended to liken its house that does not protect it from anything, the gods that do not benefit or harm were likened to it. And indeed, the flimsiest of houses meaning the weakest of houses is the house of the spider. Ad-Dahhak said: He struck an example of the weakness and frailty of their gods, so he likened them to the house of the spider. If they only knew. “If” is related to the house of the spider. That is, if they knew that worshipping idols is like making a spider’s web, which does not benefit them at all, and that this is their example, they would not have worshipped it, because they know that a spider’s web is weak. Grammarians said: The ta’ in the word al-‘ankabut the spider at the end is redundant because it is omitted in the diminutive and plural forms, and it is feminine. Al-Farra’ reported that it is masculine and recited: On their downpour, they have houses as if spiders had built them. It is narrated: On their rains, some of them have houses Al-Jawhari and Al-Hatal said: It is the name of a mountain. The spider is the well-known small creature that weaves a delicate, loose web in the air. The plural is Anakeeb, Anakeeb, Akab, Akab, and Aakab. It has been said that it is called Ankab and Aknabah. The poet said: As if a spider's web falls from its mines onto its reins It is made smaller and is called anikab. It was narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Maysarah that the spider is a devil that was transformed by God the Almighty. Ata’ al-Khurasani said: The spider spun its web twice, once for David when Goliath was pursuing him, and once for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and that is why it was forbidden to kill it. It was narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him that he said: Purify your homes from the spider’s web, for leaving it in the house causes inheritance for the poor, and preventing the consumption of yeast causes poverty.
29:42: The Almighty said: Indeed, God knows whatever they invoke besides Him. ma means who and min is for partialization. If it were redundant for emphasis, the meaning would have been reversed. The meaning is: Indeed, God knows the weakness of what they worship besides Him. Asim, Abu Amr, and Ya'qub read yad'un with a ya', which is the preferred choice of Abu Ubaid, due to the nations mentioned before it. The rest read it with a ta', indicating address.
29:43: The Almighty says: And these examples We present meaning this example and others mentioned in Al-Baqarah, Al-Hajj, and others. We present them we explain them to the people. But none will comprehend them except those of knowledge,” meaning those of knowledge about God, as Jabir narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The one who is knowledgeable is he who understands God, acts in obedience to Him, and avoids His wrath.
29:44: God Almighty says: God created the heavens and the earth in truth, meaning with justice and equity. It was also said: with His speech and power, and that is the truth. Indeed in that is a sign, meaning a mark and indication, for the believers, the truthful.
29:45: It has four issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Recite is a command to recite and to be persistent in it. The threat to those who turn away from it has already been mentioned in Ta Ha, and in the introduction to Iktab there is the command to urge people to do it, and the Kitab refers to the Qur’an. Second: The Almighty’s statement: And establish prayer. The address is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his nation. Establishing prayer means performing it at its appointed times, including its recitation, bowing, prostration, sitting, testimony of faith, and all its conditions. This has been explained previously in Surat Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. Third: The Almighty’s statement: Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing. He means that the five daily prayers are what expiate the sins committed in between, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: Tell me, if there were a river at the door of one of you and he bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt remain on him? They said: No dirt would remain on him. He said: That is like the five daily prayers; any dirt on him would remain. They said: No dirt would remain on him. He said: That is like the five daily prayers; by them God wipes away sins. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, and he said about it: It is an authentic hadith. Ibn Umar said: The prayer here refers to the Qur’an. The meaning is that which is recited in prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, adultery and sins. I say: And from this is the authentic hadith: I have divided the prayer between Me and My servant into two halves, meaning the recitation of Al-Fatihah. Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, Ibn Jurayj and Al-Kalbi said: As long as the servant is in prayer, he does not commit any indecency or wrongdoing. That is, prayer prohibits as long as you are in it. Ibn Atiyyah said: “This is foreign. How can this be compared to what Anas ibn Malik narrated: A young man from the Ansar used to pray with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and he would not leave any indecency or stealing without committing it. This was mentioned to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said: “Prayer will prohibit it.” He soon repented and his condition improved. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Did I not tell you? There is a third interpretation of this verse, which is the one accepted by the scholars, the Sufi sheikhs, and the commentators. It was said that what is meant by establish prayer is its continuity and fulfillment of its limits. Then he informed us of a ruling from him that prayer prohibits its performer and those who perform it from indecency and wrongdoing, because it contains the recitation of the Quran, which includes admonition. Prayer occupies the entire mind of the one praying. When the one praying enters his prayer niche and humbles himself before his Lord, remembering that he is standing before Him, that He watches over him and sees him, his soul becomes sound and humble, and anticipation of God the Most High enters it, and awe of it is evident in his limbs. No sooner does he cease to do so than another prayer overshadows him, returning him to the best state. This is the meaning of these hadiths, because this is how the prayer of the believer should be. I said: Especially if he makes himself feel that this might be his last action. This is more eloquent in its purpose and more complete in its meaning, because death has no specific age, no specific time, and no known illness, and there is no disagreement about this. It was narrated from some of the early Muslims that when he stood up to pray, he would tremble and his face would turn pale. He was spoken to about that and he said: I have stood before God, the Most High, and it is my right to do this with the kings of the world, so how about with the King of Kings? This is a prayer that inevitably prevents indecency and wrongdoing. Whoever’s prayer revolves around being satisfied, with no humility, remembrance, or virtues in it, like our prayer—and if only it were sufficient—then that will leave its performer from his status wherever he was. If he is on a disobedient path that distances him from God, the Most High, then the prayer will leave him continuing in his distance. Based on this, the hadith narrated from Ibn Mas’ud, al-Hasan, and al-A’mash states: Whoever’s prayer does not prevent him from indecency and wrongdoing, it only increases his distance from God. It was narrated that al-Hasan transmitted it from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, but its chain of transmission is not authentic. Ibn Atiyyah said: I heard my father may God be pleased with him say: If we consider and consider its meaning, it is not permissible to say that the prayer of the sinner distances him from God, as if it were a sin. Rather, this can be understood to mean that it does not bring him closer to God, but rather leaves him in his state and his sin, of immorality, evil, and distance. So, the prayer only increases him in confirming that distance which was his path, as if it distanced him from God when he was not charged with distance. It was said to Ibn Mas`ud: So-and-so prays a lot. He said: It only benefits the one who obeys it. She said: In summary, the intended meaning of the hadith is: It only increases his distance from God, and he only increases his hatred from God because of it. This indicates that the prayer of the one who commits indecency and wrongdoing has no value, because the sins are overwhelming for the one who commits them. It was also said that it is a statement with the meaning of a command, meaning that the one praying should desist from indecency and wrongdoing. Prayer itself does not prohibit, but it is the reason for desisting. It is like the statement of God the Almighty: This is Our Book which speaks against you with the truth (al-Jathiyah 45:29) and His statement: Or have We sent down to them authority so that it speaks about what they used to associate with Him? (Al-Rum: 35). Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: And the remembrance of God is greater. He said, God’s remembrance of you is greater than your remembrance of Him. It was also said: Your remembrance of God in your prayers and in reciting the Quran is better than everything. It was also said: The meaning is that when the remembrance of God is forbidden, the time for remembrance is abandoned. It was also said: The meaning is: And the remembrance of God to forbid immorality and wrongdoing is greater or greater, and greater can mean great. Ibn Zayd and Qatadah said: And the remembrance of God is greater than everything, meaning better than all acts of worship without remembrance. It was also said: The remembrance of God prevents sin, because the one who remembers Him does not disobey Him. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: I believe that the meaning is: And the remembrance of God is greater in general, meaning that He forbids immorality and wrongdoing. The part of it that is in prayer does that, and likewise it does outside of prayer, because refraining can only be done by the one who remembers God and is mindful of Him. The reward for that is that God the Almighty remembers him, as in the hadith: Whoever remembers Me to himself, I will remember him to Myself, and whoever remembers Me in an assembly, I will remember him in an assembly better than them. The movements in prayer have no effect on what is forbidden, and beneficial remembrance is with knowledge, and the heart turning and being free from anything except God. As for that which does not go beyond the tongue, it has a different level. God the Almighty’s remembrance of the servant is the bestowal of guidance and the light of knowledge upon him, and that is the fruit of the servant’s remembrance of his Lord. God the Almighty said: So remember Me; I will remember you. (al-Baqarah 2:152) The rest of the verse is a type of warning and urging to be mindful.
29:46: There are two issues: First: The scholars differed concerning the statement of God the Almighty: {And do not argue with the People of the Scripture.} Mujahid said: This is a decisive statement, so it is permissible to argue with the People of the Scripture in a way that is best, in the sense of calling them to God the Almighty, and pointing out His proofs and signs, hoping that they will respond to faith, not in a way that leads to error or harshness. According to this, His statement, {Except for those among them who have wronged} means they wronged you, otherwise they are all wrongdoers in general. It was also said that the meaning is: Do not argue with those among the People of the Scripture who believed in Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), such as Abdullah ibn Salamah and those who believed with him. {Except in a way that is best}, meaning by agreeing with what they narrated to you of the stories of their early generations and other things. According to this interpretation, His statement, {Except for those who have wronged} means those among them who remained in their disbelief, such as those who disbelieved and betrayed among the tribes of Qurayzah, Nadir, and others. According to this interpretation, the verse is also decisive. It was also said that this verse was abrogated by the verse on fighting. God the Almighty says: Fight those who do not believe in God (al-Tawbah 9:29). Qatada said: Except those who do wrong means they attributed to God a son, and said: The hand of God is chained (al-Ma’idah 5:64) and Indeed, God is poor (Al Imran 3:181). These are the polytheists who waged war and did not pay the jizyah, so they were victorious over them. An-Nahhas and others said: Whoever says it was abrogated argued that the verse was revealed in Mecca, and at that time there was no obligatory fighting, no demand for jizyah, or anything else. Mujahid’s statement is good, because it cannot be said that God’s rulings were abrogated except by a report that eliminates the excuse, or by a rational argument. Ibn al-Arabi favored this statement. He said to the believers: War, so fight them with the sword until they believe or pay the jizyah. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And say, ‘We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you.’ Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah who said: The People of the Book used to recite in Hebrew and interpret it in Arabic, to the people of Islam. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do not believe the People of the Book and do not disbelieve them.’ “And say, ‘We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you.’” Abdullah ibn Mas’ud narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not ask the People of the Book about anything, for they will never guide you astray. Either you disbelieve in what is right or you believe in what is false.” In Al-Bukhari: Humaid ibn Abd al-Rahman heard Mu’awiyah speaking to a group of Quraysh in Madinah, and he mentioned Ka’b al-Ahbar and said: He is one of the most truthful of these narrators who narrate from the People of the Book, and we will still test him for lying.
29:47: God Almighty says: “And thus We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book. So those to whom We have given the Book believe in it. And among these are those who believe in it. And none reject Our verses except the disbelievers.”
29:48: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And you did not recite before it any Scripture. The pronoun in before it refers to the Scripture, which is the Qur’an revealed to Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him. That is, you, O Muhammad, did not read before it, nor did you go to the People of the Scripture. Rather, We revealed it to you, and it is the ultimate in miracles and includes the unseen and other things. So, if you were among those who read a Scripture and wrote letters, the falsifiers would have had doubts, meaning among the People of the Scripture. They had a reason for their doubt, and they said, What we find in our books is that he is illiterate and does not read or write, and that is not true. Mujahid said: The People of the Scripture used to find in their books that Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon him, could neither write nor read, so this verse was revealed. An-Nahhas said: It is evidence of his prophethood to the Quraysh, because he neither read nor wrote, nor did he mix with the People of the Scripture, and there were no People of the Scripture in Mecca. So he came to them with report of the prophets and nations, and the doubt and suspicion were removed. Second: Al-Naqqash mentioned in his interpretation of this verse on the authority of Al-Sha’bi that he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die until he wrote. He also attributed the hadith of Abu Kabsha Al-Saluli, which includes: That he, may God bless him and grant him peace, read a document from ‘Uyaynah ibn Hisn and explained its meaning. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: All of this is weak, and Al-Baji’s statement, may God have mercy on him, is part of it. I said: It was reported in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Al-Bara’ in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali: Write the condition between us, “In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. This is what Muhammad, the Messenger of God, has agreed upon.” The polytheists said to him: If we knew that you were the Messenger of God, we would follow you - and in another narration, we would pledge allegiance to you - but write Muhammad ibn Abdullah. So he ordered Ali to erase it, but Ali said: By God, I will not erase it. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Show me its place. So he showed it to him, so he erased it and wrote Ibn Abdullah. Our scholars, may God be pleased with them, said that this means that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, erased that word, which was the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his own hand, and wrote Ibn Abdullah in its place. Al-Bukhari narrated it with a more explicit version of this. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the letter and wrote. And he added in another chain of transmission: And he did not know how to write. So Jum’ah said: This is what appears to be from him and that he wrote with his own hand, including al-Samani, Abu Dharr and al-Baji. They saw that this does not detract from his being illiterate, nor does it contradict his saying: And you did not recite before it any book, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand nor his saying: Indeed, we are an unlettered nation; we do not write, nor do we calculate. Rather, they saw it as an addition to his miracles and a confirmation of the truthfulness and authenticity of his message, because he wrote without learning how to write, nor was it given its causes. Rather, God, the Most High, made movements in his hand and pen, and the lines were understandable to Ibn ‘Abdullah who read them. So this was extraordinary, just as he was a Muslim who learned the knowledge of the first and the last without learning or acquiring it. So this was more eloquent in his miracles and more great in his virtues. The name of the illiterate did not go away from him because of that. Therefore, the narrator said about him in this case: And he did not know how to write. So the name of the illiterate remained with him even though he said he wrote.
