Our Sheikh Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Umar said: “Many of the jurists of Andalusia and others have denied this, and they have strongly denounced it, and they have accused its speaker of disbelief. This is evidence of the lack of theoretical knowledge and the lack of success in declaring Muslims to be infidels. They did not realize, because declaring a Muslim to be an infidel is like killing him, according to what has been reported from him (peace be upon him) in the Sahih, especially when it comes to accusing someone whose knowledge, virtue and leadership the people of this era have testified to. However, the issue is not definitive, rather its basis is the apparent meaning of authentic hadiths, but reason does not accept it as false. There is no evidence in the Shari’ah that would deny its occurrence.” I said: Some of the later scholars said that it is a miraculous miracle. It is said to him: It would have been an undeniable miracle, had it not been contradictory to another miracle, which is that he was illiterate and could not write. And with his being illiterate in an illiterate nation, the proof was established, the deniers were silenced, and the doubt was resolved. So, God the Almighty freed his hand to write, and it would be a miracle. But the miracle is that he does not write, and it is impossible for miracles to repel each other. The meaning of wrote and took the pen is that he ordered someone to write with it from among his scribes. And there were twenty scribes among the scribes of the revelation before him, may God bless him and grant him peace. Third: Judge Iyad mentioned, “On the authority of Muawiyah, that he was writing in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to him: ‘Put down the inkwell, and the pen’s letters, and the ba’, and the sin’, and do not make the mim’s letters crooked, and God has made it beautiful, and the Most Gracious has lengthened, and the Most Merciful has been generous.’” The judge said: Even if the narration that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote is not authentic, it is not far-fetched that he was granted the knowledge of this, and was prevented from reading and writing. I said: This is the correct view on this matter, that he did not write a single letter, but rather he was ordered to write. Likewise, he did not read or spell. If you say: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) spelled when he mentioned the Antichrist, saying: Written between his eyes is ‘Kaaf-e-Far’ and you say that there is a miracle in his being illiterate. God the Most High said: And you did not recite before him any scripture (al-Baqarah 2:17) and He said: (Indeed, we are an unlettered nation. We do not write, nor do we calculate). So how is this? The answer is what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stated explicitly in the hadeeth of Hudhayfah, and the hadeeth is like the Qur’an in part. In the hadeeth of Hudhayfah: Every believer, literate and illiterate, will read it. He stated in that regard those who are illiterate other than those who are literate. This is very clear.
29:49: God the Almighty says: Rather, they are clear signs meaning the Qur'an. Al-Hasan said: Al-Farra' claimed that Abdullah's recitation of Rather, they are clear signs means, Rather, the verses of the Qur'an are clear signs. Al-Hasan said: Similar to it is: This is insight (Al-A'raf 7:203). If this were the case, it would have been permissible, similar to it: This is a mercy from my Lord (Al-Kahf 18:98). Al-Hasan said: This nation has been given the ability to memorize, while those before them would not read their book without looking, and if they closed it, none would memorize what was in it except the prophets. Ka'b said, describing this nation: They are wise scholars, and they are prophets in jurisprudence. In the breasts of those who have been given knowledge means that this Qur'an is not as the falsifiers claim, that it is magic or poetry, but rather it is signs and proofs by which the religion of God and His rulings are known. And it is also in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge, and they are the companions of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the believers in him, they memorize it and recite it. He described them as having knowledge because they distinguished with their understanding between the speech of God and the speech of humans and not devils. Qatada and Ibn Abbas said: Rather, it is meaning Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) clear signs in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge of the People of the Scripture, they find it written with them in their books with this description: illiterate, who neither reads nor writes, but they wronged themselves and concealed it. This is the preferred opinion of At-Tabari. The evidence for this statement is the reading of Ibn Mas`ud and Ibn As-Sameeq: Rather, these are clear signs and the peace be upon him was signs, not a single sign, because he indicated many things of the religion, so this is why he said: Rather, it is clear signs and it was said: Rather, he is the possessor of clear signs, so the complement was omitted. And none reject Our verses except the wrongdoers meaning the disbelievers, because they denied his prophethood and what he brought.
29:50: God the Almighty says: And they say, ‘Why were no signs sent down to him from his Lord?’ This is what the polytheists said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and its meaning is, Why was a sign not sent down to him like the signs of the prophets? It was also said: Just as Salih brought the she-camel, Moses brought the staff, and Jesus brought the dead back to life. That is, Say to them, O Muhammad: The signs are only with God, so He brings them as He wishes, if He wishes He sends them, and I am not with me. I am only a clear warner. Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i recited: Ayah in the singular form. The rest used the plural form. This is the choice of Abu Ubaid, because God the Almighty says: Say, ‘The signs are only with God.’
29:51: The Almighty says: Was it not sufficient for them that We sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book which is recited to them? This is an answer to their saying: Why were not verses sent down to him from his Lord? That is, was it not sufficient for the polytheists to produce verses from this miraculous Book which you challenged them to produce the like of, or a surah from it, but they failed? And if you brought them the verses of Moses and Jesus, they would say: This is magic, but we do not know magic, and speech is within their power. Yet they were unable to oppose it. It was said that the reason for the revelation of these verses is what Ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Umar ibn Dinar on the authority of Yahya ibn Ja'dah who said: A shoulder strap containing a book was brought to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he said: It is sufficient for a people who are astray that they turn away from what their Prophet brought to what a prophet other than their Prophet brought, or a book other than their book. So God the Almighty revealed: Was it not sufficient for them that We sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book? Narrated by Abu Muhammad al-Darimi in his Musnad. The scholars of tafsir mentioned it in their books. Concerning such a matter, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Umar, He is not one of us who does not chant the Qur’an, meaning that he is satisfied with it and does not need anything else. This is the interpretation of Al-Bukhari may God have mercy on him of the verse. If meeting his Lord is worth ten good deeds or more for each letter, as we mentioned in the introduction to the book, then turning away from it to anything else is misguidance, loss, deception, and deficiency. Indeed in that meaning in the Qur’an is mercy in this world and the hereafter. It was said: mercy in this world by saving them from misguidance. And a reminder in this world by guiding them to the truth for a people who believe.
29:52: God the Almighty says: Say, ‘Sufficient is God as a Witness between me and you.’ That is, say to those who deny you, “Sufficient is God as a Witness to the truth of what I claim, that I am His Messenger and that this Qur’an is His Book. “He knows what is in the heavens and the earth.” That is, nothing is hidden from Him. This is an argument against them to prove the validity of His testimony against them, because they have acknowledged His knowledge, so it is necessary for them to acknowledge His testimony. And those who believe in falsehood. Yahya ibn Salam said: Iblis. It was also said: The worship of idols and statues, as Ibn Shajar said. And disbelieved in God. That is, because they denied His messengers and rejected His Book. It was also said: Because of what they associated with Him of idols and attributes to Him of children and opposites. “Those are the losers,” in themselves and their deeds in the Hereafter.
29:53: The Almighty says: And they ask you to hasten the punishment. When He warned them of the punishment, they said, in extreme denial, Hasten this punishment for us. It was said that the one who said that was An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith and Abu Jahl when they said, O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky. (al-Anfal 8:32) And their saying, Our Lord, hasten for us our portion before the Day of Reckoning. (Sad: 16) And His saying, And were it not for a specified term, regarding the descent of the punishment. Ibn Abbas said: It means, I did not promise you that I would not punish your people and delay them until the Day of Resurrection. Its explanation is: Rather, the Hour is their appointed time. (al-Qamar 54:46) Ad-Dahhak said: It is the duration of their lives, the time that God has determined for their destruction and punishment, as Ibn Shajarah said. It was said: It is the killing on the Day of Badr. In short, every punishment has a term that is neither advanced nor delayed. His evidence is His statement: For every report there is a appointed time (al-An’am 6:67). The punishment has come upon them means that which they hastened. And it will come upon them suddenly meaning suddenly. And they perceive not meaning they do not know that it will descend upon them.
29:54: The Almighty says: They urge you to hasten the punishment. That is, they urge you to hasten them, even though Hell has been prepared for them and will inevitably surround them. So what is the meaning of hastening? It was said that it was revealed regarding Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya and his companions among the polytheists when they said: Or should the sky fall upon us in fragments, as you have claimed? (Al-Isra': 92).
29:55: The Almighty’s saying: The Day the punishment will cover them from above them. It was said: It is connected to what came before it, meaning the Day the punishment will befall them from above them and from beneath their feet, and when the punishment will cover them, Hell will surround them. He only said: and from beneath their feet for the sake of approximation, otherwise covering from above is more general, as the poet said: I fed her straw and cold water. Another said: The leaders of the horses who were on the offensive were without spears or shields. And he says, 'Taste.' The people of Medina and Kufa read it as, And we say, with a noon. The rest read it with a ya. Abu Ubaid chose it, because of the statement, Say, 'Sufficient is God.' It is possible that the angel assigned to them says, Taste. Both readings go back to the same meaning, that is, the angel says, by our command, Taste.
29:56: The Almighty says: O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious. This verse was revealed to encourage the believers who were in Makkah to emigrate - according to Muqatil and Al-Kalbi - so God informed them of the vastness of His earth, and that remaining in a place where the disbelievers are harmed is not right. Rather, the correct thing is to seek to worship God on His earth, and that staying in a place where the disbelievers are harmed is not right. Rather, the correct thing is to seek to worship God on His earth with His righteous servants. That is, if you are in difficulty in showing your faith there, then emigrate to Madinah, for it is spacious, to show monotheism there. Ibn Jubayr and Ata' said: This verse applies to a land in which there is oppression and evil, and migration from it to a land of truth is required. Malik said the same. Mujahid said: My earth is spacious, so they emigrated and fought. Mutraf ibn Ash-Shakheer said: The meaning is that My mercy is vast. And also on the authority of God the Almighty: Indeed, My provision for you is vast, so seek it on the earth. Sufyan al-Thawri said: If you are in an expensive land, then move to another one and fill your bag with bread for a dirham. It was said: The meaning is: Indeed, My land, which is the land of Paradise, is vast. So worship Me until I inherit it for you. So worship Me “Me” is in the accusative case with an implied verb, meaning, so worship Me, so worship Me. So one of the two verbs was substituted for the second, and the fa in His statement: So worship Me has the meaning of a condition, meaning, if a place becomes too small for you, then worship Me elsewhere, because My land is vast.
29:57: The Almighty's saying: Every soul will taste death, then to Us you will be returned. This was mentioned earlier in Al Imran. Rather, He mentioned it here to belittle the matter of this world and its fears. It is as if some of the believers considered the consequences that would befall him if he left his homeland in Mecca, that he would die or go hungry or something like that, so God belittled the matter of this world. Meaning, you will inevitably die and be gathered to Us, so hasten to obey God and migrate to Him and to do what He commands. Then He promised the believing, working people, dwelling in Paradise as an encouragement from Him, and He mentioned the reward that they will receive. Then He described them by saying, Those who are patient and upon their Lord rely. Abu Omar, Ya'qub, Al-Jahdary, Ibn Abi Ishaq, Ibn Muhaysin, Al-A'mash, Hamzah, Al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read: O My servants with a sukoon on the ya'. The rest read it with a fatha. My land was conquered by Ibn Amir and inhabited by the rest. It was narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever flees for his religion from one land to another, even if it is a handspan away, will be entitled to Paradise and will be a companion of Muhammad and Abraham, peace be upon them. Then to Us you will be returned As-Salami and Abu Bakr read on the authority of Asim: they will return with a ya’, because of His statement: Every soul will taste death. The rest read it with a ta’, because of His statement: O My servants who have believed. Some of them recited: Death is always calling for our shroud, while we are oblivious to what is intended for us. Do not rely on the world and its flowers, even if you are adorned with its beautiful garments. What did the beloved and neighbors do? Where are those who were her home? Death gave them a dirty cup and made them hostage under the layers of dirt.
29:58: The Almighty said: And those who have believed and done righteous deeds - We will surely assign to them lofty chambers in Paradise. Ibn Masoud, Al-A’mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read, لنِتويهنهمwith a tha’ instead of the ba’ from thawa which means residence, meaning We will give them a place to dwell in. Rawis read on the authority of Ya’qub, Al-Jahdary, and Al-Sulami:لىبويونههمwith a ya’ instead of the nun. The rest said,لنِبويهنهمmeaning We will accommodate them in lofty chambers plural of gurfah which is a high, elevated room. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Sahl ibn Sa’d that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise will see the people of the chambers above them as you see a brilliant star setting on the horizon, whether in the east or the west, because of the difference between them. They said: O Messenger of God, those are the dwellings of the prophets; none but them will attain them. He said: Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they are men who believed in God and believed the messengers. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, in Paradise there are chambers whose backs can be seen from their insides and whose insides can be seen from their backs. A Bedouin stood up and said: For whom are they, O Messenger of God? He said: They are for the one who speaks pleasantly, feeds the poor, fasts regularly, and prays to God at night while people are asleep. We have expanded on this verse in the Book of Remembrance. Praise be to God.
29:59: God Almighty says: Those who are patient and put their trust in their Lord.
29:60: The Almighty said: And how many a creature carries not its own provision! God provides for it and for you. Al-Wahidi narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, who said: Hajjaj bin Al-Minhal narrated to us on the authority of Al-Zuhri - who is Abd Al-Rahman bin Ata' - on the authority of Ata' on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until he entered one of the walls of the Ansar. He began to chew on some dates and eat them. He said: O Ibn Umar, why don't you eat? She said: I don't desire it, O Messenger of God. He said: But I desire it, and this is the fourth morning. I have not tasted any food. If I wanted, I could have called upon my Lord, and He would have given me something like the kingdom of Chosroes and Caesar. So how, O Ibn Umar, if I remain among a people who hide their provision for a year, faith weakens." He said: We did not leave until the following was revealed: "And how many a creature carries not its own provision! God provides for it and for you. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing." I said: This is weak, and it is weakened by the fact that the Prophet (peace be upon him) used to save up for his family their food for a year. Al-Bukhari and Muslim agreed on this. The Companions used to do that, and they are the role models, the people of certainty, and the leaders for those who came after them from the righteous and trusting. Ibn Abbas narrated that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said to the believers in Mecca when the polytheists harmed them: Go out to Medina and emigrate, and do not live near the oppressors. They said: We have no home or property there, and no one to feed us or give us water. So the verse: “And how many a creature carries not its provision. God provides for it and for you.” was revealed, meaning: it does not have its provision stored up with it, and likewise you, God provides for you in the house of al-Hijrah. This is more similar to the first statement. We have previously discussed ka-ayn and that this ayn has the letter kaf added to it, and it has the meaning of kam. According to al-Khalil and Sibawayh, the interpretation is like a number, meaning like a large number of creatures. Mujahid said: It means the camel and the beasts eat with their mouths and do not carry anything. Al-Hasan said: It eats on time and does not store for a future. It was said: It does not carry its provision meaning it is not able to provide for itself. God provides for it wherever it goes. And you and it was said: It means the carrier. Al-Naqqash narrated: What is meant is the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who eats and does not store. She said: It is not a thing, because the Almighty said: The word beast is general, and it is not used in common usage to refer to humans, so how about the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him? This has already been mentioned in the ants when He said: And when the word comes to pass against them, We will produce for them a creature from the earth that will speak to them (An-Naml 27:82). Ibn Abbas said: Beasts are every moving animal, so none of them carries its provision or stores it except the son of Adam, the ant, and the mouse. Some of them said: I saw the nightingale hoarding its nest. The magpie is called a hider, except that it forgets it. May God provide for her and for you. He makes a distinction between the eager and the one who relies on his provision, the one who desires and the one who is content, the needy and the helpless, so that the patient does not think that he is provided for by his skin, and the helpless one does not imagine that he is prevented by his inability. In the Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: If you were to put your trust in God as He should be put, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds that go out in the morning hungry and return in the evening with full crops. “And He is the All-Hearing” of your supplications and your saying, We do not find anything to spend in Madinah, the All-Knowing of what is in your hearts.
29:61: God the Almighty said: And if you ask them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' (Al-Baqarah 2:170). When the polytheists taunted the Muslims with poverty and said, If you were on the truth, you would not be poor, this was a delusion, and there were also poor people among the disbelievers, God removed this doubt. The same applies to those who said, If we emigrate, we will not find anything to spend. And if you acknowledge that God is the Creator of these things, how can you doubt provision? The One in whose hand is the creation of all things is not incapable of providing provision for His servant, and that is why He connected it.
29:62: The Almighty says: God expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. “How then are they deluded?” That is, how can they disbelieve in My Oneness and turn away from My worship? God expands provision for whom He wills That is, the matter of provision does not differ with belief or disbelief, so expansion and restriction come from Him, so do not be reproached for poverty, for everything is by divine decree and predestination. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things of your conditions and your wealth. It was also said that He is Knowing of what is good for you, whether poverty or expansion.
29:63: God Almighty says: And if you ask them, ‘Who sends down water from the sky?’ That is, from the clouds as rain. And revives thereby the earth after its lifelessness. That is, its humpback and the drought of its inhabitants. They will surely say, ‘God.’ That is, if you acknowledge that and do not associate partners with Him and await the return. If He is able to do that, then He is the One who is able to enrich the believers, so He repeated it for emphasis. Say, ‘Praise be to God.’ That is, for the clear proofs and evidence of His power. But most of them do not reason. That is, they do not ponder these proofs. It was also said: Praise be to God for their acknowledgment of that. It was also said: for sending down water and reviving the earth.
29:64: The Almighty said: And this worldly life is nothing but diversion and amusement. That is, something to be amused with and played with. That is, whatever God has given the rich of this world vanishes and disappears, like a game that has no reality or stability. Some of them said: If this world remains for you, it will not remain for them. And he recited: The world returns to us differently than it was, and other things happen after that. The nights pass by with gatherings and divisions, and stars rise and set. Whoever thinks that his happiness will last forever, that is impossible, happiness does not last May God forgive those who made their worries one and believed that circles do not revolve I said: All of this is in worldly matters of money, status, and clothing in excess of what is necessary for living and the strength to obey. As for that which is for God, it is from the Hereafter, and it is that which will remain, as He said: And there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor. (Al-Rahman: 27), meaning whatever was sought by it for His reward and pleasure. And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the life. That is, the home of eternal life that does not cease and in which there is no death. Abu Ubaidah claimed that life, life, and the living, with a kasra on the ha’, are one and the same. As he said: And you will see that life is living. Another says: The word al-hayyun is all on the pattern fa’ul like ‘asa. And al-hayyun refers to every living thing. Hayyun is a spring in Paradise. It was also said that the root of hayyun is hayyun, but one of them was replaced with a waw because of the two letters coming together. If only they knew is how it is.
29:65: God Almighty said: And when they embark on a ship meaning ships and fear drowning, they supplicate God, devoting their religion to Him meaning truthful in their intentions, and they abandon the worship of idols and supplications to them. But when He delivers them to land, at once they associate others with Him meaning they call upon others besides Him, and that for which He has not sent down authority. It was said that their association with God is when someone says, Had it not been for God and the leader or the sailor, we would have drowned, so they make what God did for them of salvation a barrier between God and His creation.
29:66: The Almighty says: That they may disbelieve in what We have given them and that they may enjoy themselves. It was said that they are lam ki, meaning that they may disbelieve and that they may enjoy themselves. It was also said that when they associate others with God means that the result of their association with God is that they deny the blessings of God and enjoy themselves in this world. It was also said that they are lam amr meaning threat and intimidation. That is, disbelieve in what We have given you of blessings and salvation from the sea and enjoy yourself. The evidence for this is the reading of Abu wa tamta'u. Ibn al-Anbari said: This is strengthened by the reading of al-A'mash, Nafi' and Hamzah: wa tamta'u with the lam jazm. An-Nahhas said: wa tamta'u lam ki, and it is permissible for it to be lam amr because the original lam of the command is kasra, except that it is a command with the meaning of threat. Whoever reads wa tamta'u with sukoon on the lam did not make it lam ki, because the lam of ki cannot be sukoon. This is the reading of Ibn Kathir, Al-Maseebi, and Qaloon on the authority of Nafi’, and Hamza, Al-Kisa’i, and Hafs on the authority of Asim. The rest read it with a kasra on the lam. Abu Al-Aaliyah read: “That they may disbelieve in what We have given them. So enjoy yourselves, and you are going to know.” This is a threat and a warning.
29:67: God the Almighty says: Have they not seen that We have made a secure sanctuary? Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd said: It is Mecca and they are feathers, God the Almighty has given them security therein. And people are being snatched away from all around them. Ad-Dahhak said: They kill each other and take each other captive. Snatching means taking quickly. This has been mentioned in Al-Qasas and its equivalents. God the Almighty reminded them of this blessing so that they would submit to Him in obedience. That is, He made for them a secure sanctuary in which they were safe from captivity, raids, and killing, and He saved them on land as He saved them at sea, so they began to associate partners with God on land but not at sea. This is astonishment at the contradiction of their conditions. Then do they believe in falsehood? Qatadah said: Then in polytheism. Yahya ibn Salam said: Then in Satan. "Then in the favor of God they deny?" Ibn Abbas said: "Then in the favor of God?" Ibn Shajarah said: "Then in the bounty and kindness of God." Ibn Salam said: “Is it the guidance that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought?” Al-Naqqash said: Is it the feeding of them against hunger and the security of them against fear that they disbelieve? This is an expression of astonishment and denial that is presented as a question.
29:68: God the Almighty says: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God? That is, no one is more unjust than he who makes a partner or a son with God, and when he commits an immorality he says: We found our fathers doing it, and God has commanded us to do it. (al-A’raf 7:28) Or he denied the truth when it came to him. Yahya ibn Salam said: With the Qur’an. Al-Suddi said: With Tawhid. Ibn Shajarah said: “With Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him.” Each statement includes both statements. Is there not in Hell an abode for the disbelievers? That is, a permanent residence. It is a question of confirmation.
29:69: God the Almighty says: And those who strive for Us meaning, strive against the disbelievers for Us. That is, seeking Our pleasure. Al-Suddi and others said: This verse was revealed before fighting was made obligatory. Ibn Atiyyah said: It was before the customary jihad, but it is a general jihad for the religion of God and to seek His pleasure. Al-Hasan ibn Abi Al-Hasan said: The verse is about the servants. Ibn Abbas and Ibrahim ibn Adham said: It is about those who are blind to it and know. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever acts according to what he knows, God will teach him what he does not know. Some scholars tended toward His statement: And fear God, and God will teach you. (Al-Baqarah 2:282) Umar ibn Abdul Aziz said: Our shortcoming in knowing what we do not know is our shortcoming in acting according to what we know. If we acted on some of what we know, it would give us knowledge that our bodies would not be able to comprehend. God the Almighty says: And fear God, and God will teach you. (Al-Baqarah 2:282) Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: Jihad mentioned in this verse is not only fighting the infidels, but it also includes supporting the faith, refuting the wrongdoers, and suppressing the oppressors. Its greatest aspect is enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong. From this comes striving with one's soul in obedience to God, which is the greater jihad. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said to Ibn al-Mubarak: If you see people differing, then stick to the mujahideen and the frontier dwellers, for God says: We will surely guide them. Ad-Dahhak said: The symbol in this world is like Paradise in the Hereafter. Whoever enters Paradise in the Hereafter will be safe, and likewise whoever adheres to the Sunnah in this world will be safe. Abdullah ibn Abbas said: And those who strive in Our obedience - We will surely guide them to the ways of Our reward. This includes all opinions under the generality of obedience. Similar to this is the statement of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: Wisdom says: Whoever wrongs Me and does not find Me, let him seek Me in two situations: by acting according to what he knows best, and avoiding the worst of what he knows. Al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: There is an inversion of the Qur'an, meaning those whom We have guided are those who strive for Us. We will surely guide them to Our ways meaning the path to Paradise, as stated by Al-Suddi. Al-Naqqash: He will guide them to the religion of truth. Yusuf ibn Asbat said: The meaning is, 'We will surely purify their intentions, their charities, their prayers, and their fasting.' And indeed, God is with the doers of good is a lam of emphasis and the negation of with" was introduced in one of two ways: that it is a noun, and the lam of emphasis is only added to nouns, or it is a particle, so it is added to it because it has the meaning of stability, as you say, 'Indeed, Zaid is in the house.' And "with" when it is sukun is a particle and nothing else. And when it is opened, it may be a noun, or a preposition, but it is more likely that it is a particle that came for a meaning. The meaning of doing good and the doers of good were mentioned previously in "Al-Baqarah" and other surahs. And He, the Almighty, is with them in victory and assistance, preservation and guidance, and with everyone in His encompassing and power. So there is a distance between the two types of being with.
30:1: Surah Ar-Rum is entirely Meccan without dispute, and it has sixty verses. God the Almighty says: {The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land.} At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri who said: When the Day of Badr took place, the Romans were victorious over the Persians, and the believers were amazed by that, so the following was revealed: {The Romans have been defeated.} In the lowest land - until His saying - The believers rejoice “in God’s victory.” He said: So the believers rejoiced at the Romans’ victory over the Persians. He said: This is a strange hadith from this chain of transmission. This is how Nasr ibn Ali Al-Jahdhami read {The Romans have been defeated.} And he also narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Abbas in a more complete manner: Ibn Abbas said about the statement of God, the Almighty, {Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated * In the lowest land} He said: Defeated and were defeated. He said: The polytheists wanted the Persians to prevail over the Romans because they and they were idolaters, and the Muslims wanted the Romans to prevail over the Persians because they were People of the Book. So he mentioned it to Abu Bakr, who mentioned it to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said: Indeed, they will be defeated. So Abu Bakr mentioned it to them, and they said: Set a time limit between us and you. If we are victorious, we will have such-and-such, and if you are victorious, you will have such-and-such. So he set a time limit of five years, but they did not prevail. So he mentioned it to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he said: Why didn’t you make it less than - I think he said ten - He said: Abu Sa’id said: And less than ten. He said: Then the Romans appeared later. He said: So that is what God said: {Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated} - until His saying - And on that day the believers will rejoice * In God’s victory. Sufyan said: I heard that they were victorious over them on the Day of Badr. Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a hasan sahih ghareeb hadith. It was also narrated on the authority of Niyar bin Mukram Al-Aslami who said: When the verse: "Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, but after their defeat they will overcome. Within three to four years," was revealed, the Persians were the ones who had conquered the Romans on the day this verse was revealed. The Muslims loved the Romans to be victorious over them because they were the People of the Book. Concerning this, the words of God were revealed: "And that Day the believers will rejoice in the victory of God. He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful." The Quraysh loved the Persians to be victorious because they were not the People of the Book and had no faith that would be resurrected. When this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr As-Siddiq may God be pleased with him went out shouting in the outskirts of Makkah: "Alif, Lam, Meem. The Romans have been defeated in the nearest land, and after their defeat they will overcome. Within three to five years." Some of the Quraysh said to Abu Bakr, "This is between us and you. Your companion claims that the Romans will defeat the Persians in three to four years. Shall we not bet on it?" He said, Yes. That was before betting was forbidden, so Abu Bakr and the polytheists made a bet and agreed upon a wager. They said to Abu Bakr, How much will you make for a few years? Three to nine years? Then name a middle ground between us and you. They heard that it would be six years. The six years passed before they were victorious, so the polytheists took Abu Bakr's pledge. When the seventh year began, the Romans defeated the Persians. The Muslims criticized Abu Bakr for naming him six years. He said: Because God, the Most High, said, within a few years. He said: And many people embraced Islam at that time. Abu 'Eisa said: This is a good, sound, and rare hadith. Al-Qushayri, Ibn 'Atiyyah, and others narrated that when the verses were revealed, Abu Bakr went out with them to the polytheists and said: Would you be pleased if the Romans were victorious? Our Prophet, the Most High, told us from God, that they would be victorious within a few years. Ubayy ibn Khalaf and his brother Umayyah, or it was said Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, said to him: O Abu Fadil! - using his kunya, O Abu Bakr - Let us bet on this matter. So Abu Bakr bet on them. Qatadah said: That was before gambling was forbidden, before gambling was forbidden. They made the bet five she-camels and the term was three years. It was said: They made the bet three she-camels. Then he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He said: Why don't you take precautions? The few are between three, nine, and ten! But go back and increase their bet and increase their time limit. Abu Bakr did so, and they made the camels one hundred and the time limit nine years. The Romans were victorious during the time limit. Al-Sha'bi said: They emerged victorious in nine years. Al-Qushayri: The well-known narrations indicate that the Romans emerged on the seventh day after the Persians defeated the Romans. Perhaps Al-Sha'bi's narration is a misprint from seven to nine by some of the transmitters. In some narrations: He made the camels seven to nine years. It is said that it was the last of the conquests of Khosrow I, during which he conquered Constantinople and built the House of Fire in it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was informed of that and he was displeased, so God, the Most High, revealed these two verses. Al-Naqqash and others narrated: When Abu Bakr As-Siddiq may God be pleased with him wanted to migrate with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Ubayy ibn Khalaf clung to him and said to him: Give me a guarantor for the risk if I am defeated. So his son Abdur-Rahman guarantored it for him. When my father wanted to go to Uhud, Abdur-Rahman asked him for the guarantor and he gave him a guarantor. Then my father died in Mecca from a wound inflicted by the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Romans defeated the Persians on the day of Hudaybiyyah, after nine years of their mourning. Al-Sha'bi said: That period had not passed before the Romans defeated the Persians, tied up their horses in Al-Mada'in, and built a Roman city. Abu Bakr swindled my father and took the money for the risk from his heirs. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Give it in charity, so he gave it in charity. The commentators said: The reason for the Romans’ victory over Persia was a woman in Persia who gave birth to nothing but kings and heroes. Khosrow said to her: I want to appoint one of your sons to lead an army that I will send out to the Romans. She said: This is Hormuz, more cunning than a fox and more cautious than a falcon. And so is Farkhan, one of Sinan’s and more penetrating than Nubl. And this is Shahr Bazan, more forbearing than so-and-so. Choose. So he chose the forbearing one and appointed him. So he marched to the Romans with the people of Persia and defeated the Romans. Akrima and others said: When Shahr Bazan defeated the Romans, he destroyed their lands until he reached the Gulf. His brother Farkhan said, You saw me sitting on the throne of Khosrau. Khosrau wrote to Shahr Bazan, Send me Farkhan's head. But he did not do so. Khosrau wrote to Persia, I have appointed Farkhan over you and dismissed Shahr Bazan. He wrote to Farkhan that if he took office, he should kill Shahr Bazan. Farkhan wanted to kill Shahr Bazan, but Shahr Bazan brought out three letters from Khosrau ordering him to kill Farkhan. Shahr Bazan said to Farkhan, "Khosrau wrote to me to kill you on three letters, and I have always consulted him about you. Will you kill me for one letter?" So he restored the kingdom to his brother. Shahr Bazan wrote to Caesar, the king of the Romans, and they cooperated against Khosrau. The Romans defeated Persia, and Khosrau died. The report reached the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day of Hudaybiyyah, and the Muslims who were with him rejoiced. This is what God, the Most High, said: The Romans have been defeated in the lowest land, meaning the land of Ash-Sham. Akrima: Adhra’at, which is between the land of the Arabs and the Levant. It was said that Caesar sent a man called Yahnes and Khosrau sent Shahr Bazan, and they met at Adhra’at and Busra, which is the closest land of the Levant to the land of the Arabs and Persians. Mujahid: It is a place between Iraq and the Levant. Muqatil: In Jordan and Palestine. And the meaning of adda is closer. Abu Atiyah said: If the incident was in Adhra’at, then it is one of the lowest lands in comparison to Mecca, and it is the one mentioned by Imru’ al-Qais in his saying: Her skirt is from the arms and her people are in Yathrib, the lowest part of her house, a high view If the incident occurred in Al-Jazira, it was closer in comparison to the land of Khosrau, and if it was in Jordan, it was closer to the land of the Romans. When this happened and the Romans were victorious, the infidels were pleased, so God gave good tidings to His servants that the Romans would be victorious and the state would be theirs in the war. We have already discussed the openings of the surahs. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, Ali bin Abi Talib, and Muawiyah bin Qurra read Ghalabat Ar-Rum with a fat-ha on the ghain and the lam. The interpretation of this is that what happened on the day of Badr was that the Romans were defeated, which was a shock to the infidels of Quraysh and pleased the Muslims. So God gave good tidings to His servants that they would also be defeated in a few years. Abu Hatim mentioned this interpretation. Abu Jaafar Al-Nahhas said: Most people read Ghalabat Ar-Rum with a damma on the ghain and a kasra on the lam. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar and Abu Saeed Al-Khudri that they read Ghalabat Ar-Rum and they read Sayyaghalbuun. Abu Hatim narrated that Asma narrated on the authority of Harun: This is the reading of the people of Ash-Sham. Ahmad ibn Hanbal says: This Asma is weak. Abu Hatim narrated many narrations on his authority. The hadith indicates that the reading with the damma on the ghain was predominant. This information was evidence of the prophethood of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, because the Romans had defeated the Persians. God, the Almighty, informed his prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that the Romans would defeat the Persians in a few years, and that the believers would rejoice at that, because the Romans were People of the Book. This was part of the knowledge of the unseen that God, the Almighty, had informed them of, which they did not know. He ordered Abu Bakr to bet them on that and to exaggerate the bet. Then betting was forbidden later, and it was abrogated by the prohibition of gambling. Ibn Atiyyah said: The reading with the damma on the ghain is more correct. People agreed that sighalbuun, with the fatha on the ya, refers to the Romans. It is narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that it is also with the damma on the ya in sighalbuun. In this reading, the meaning is reversed, which is agreed upon in the narrations. Abu Jaafar Al-Nahhas said: Whoever recites they will be victorious then the meaning according to him is: and the Persians after their defeat, meaning after they were defeated, they will be victorious. It was narrated that the Romans defeated the Persians at Badr, as was mentioned in the hadith of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri and the hadith of Al-Tirmidhi. It was narrated that this was on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, and that the report arrived on the day of the Pledge of Ridwan, as was said by Ikrimah and Qatadah. Ibn Atiyyah said: On both days there was victory from God for the believers. People have mentioned that the reason for the Muslims' joy at the victory of the Romans and their concern for them to be victorious is that the Romans were People of the Book like the Muslims, and the Persians were among the people of idols, as was explained in the hadith. Al-Nahhas said: Another statement, which is more correct, is that their joy was due to the fulfillment of God’s promise, as it contained evidence of prophethood, because God, the Blessed and Exalted, had informed them of what would happen in a few years, and it happened. Ibn Atiyyah said: It is appropriate to explain that by what is required by reasoning, such as the desire to defeat the smaller enemy because it is easier to bear, and when the larger enemy is defeated, the fear of him increases. So, consider this meaning, along with what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was hoping for, the emergence of his religion and the law of God with which he was sent, and his victory over the nations, and the desire of the infidels of Mecca for God to send him a king who would eradicate him and relieve them of him. It was said: Their joy was due to the victory of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, over the polytheists, because Gabriel had informed them of the humiliation of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr, as narrated by Al-Qushayri. I said: It is possible that their joy in the whole was from that, so they interpreted their victory over their enemy and the victory of the Romans also and the brevity of God’s promise. Abu Haywah al-Shami and Muhammad ibn al-Sumaiqa’ read min ba’d ghalabihum with a sukoon on the lam, and they are two dialects, like taghn and taghn. Al-Farra’ claimed that the original is min ba’d ghalabihum so the ta’ was deleted as it was deleted in the saying of God the Almighty: And the establishment of prayer, and its root is and the establishment of prayer. An-Nahhas said: This is a mistake that would not be surprising to many grammarians, because the establishment of prayer is a verbal noun from which a deletion was made due to the weakness of its verb, so the ta’ was made a replacement for the deleted part, and ghalaba is not weak and nothing was deleted from it. Al-Asma’i narrated: tarada tardan he drove away, jalab jalban he conceived and halab halban he milked, and ghalaba ghalban he defeated. So what is the deletion in this? And is it permissible to say in akal aklan and the like: a deletion from it? In a few years the ha’ was deleted from ba’d something to differentiate between the masculine and feminine, and this has been discussed previously in Yusuf. And the noon in saniya was opened because it is the plural of Muslim. Some Arabs say in a few years just as they say in two washings. It is permissible to make the plural of year a rational plural with waw, noon, ya and noon, because something has been deleted from it and this plural is made to replace the deficiency in its singular, because the root of year is sanah or sanwah, and the seen in it has been broken to indicate that its plural is outside its norm and pattern. This is the opinion of the Basrans. Al-Farra' is obliged to add a damma to it because he says: The damma is evidence of the waw and a waw has been deleted from year in one of the two opinions, and no one we know of adds a damma" to it. God the Almighty said: "To God belongs the command before and after." God the Almighty informed us of His uniqueness in decree and that whatever has befallen the world of dominance and other things is from Him and by His will and power. So God said, "The command" means the implementation of the rulings. "Before and after" means before this dominance and after it. It was also said: "Before everything and After everything. Before and After" are two adverbials that are made clear with the damma because they are definite by deleting what is added to them and they come to include what is deleted. They differ from the definition of nouns and similar letters in inclusion, so they are made clear. The damma was chosen because of their resemblance to the singular vocative in that if it is indefinite and added to a noun, its structure is removed. This is also the case with them, so they are made damma. It is also said: "Before and After. Al-Kisa'i reported from some of Banu Asad that To God belongs the command before and after" the first is in the genitive case with a tanween, and the second is in the damma without a tanween. Al-Farra' reported "Before and After" are in the genitive case without a tanween. An-Nahhas denied it and rejected it. Al-Farra' said in his book: There are many things in the Qur'an that are clearly wrong, including that he claimed that "before and after are permissible, but he only allows before and after" because they are indefinite. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is "from before and from after. And on that Day the believers will rejoice * in God's victory" mentioned above. "He gives victory to whom He wills" meaning from among His allies, because His victory is limited to His allies overcoming His enemies. As for His enemies overcoming His allies, that is not His victory, but rather a test and may be called triumph. "And He is the Exalted in Might in His vengeance, the Merciful" to those who obey Him.
30:2: God Almighty said: The Romans have been defeated.
30:3: God Almighty says: In the lowest land, but after their defeat they will overcome.
30:4: God Almighty says: “Within a few years. To God belongs the command before and after. And on that Day the believers will rejoice.”
30:5: God Almighty says: “By the victory of God, He gives victory to whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.”
30:6: The Almighty says: The promise of God - God never breaks His promise, because His words are true. But most people do not know, meaning the disbelievers, who are more numerous. It has also been said that what is meant are the polytheists of Mecca. The word God’s promise is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, meaning that He promised that promise.
30:7: Then God the Almighty explained the extent of what they know, saying: They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, meaning the affairs of their livelihood and their worldly affairs: when to sow and when to harvest, how to plant and how to build. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and Qatadah. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the construction of their palaces, the digging of their rivers and the planting of their trees, and the meaning is the same. It was also said: It is what the devils throw at them of worldly matters when they eavesdrop from the lowest heaven. This was said by Saeed ibn Jubayr. It was also said: It is the outward and the inward, as He said elsewhere: Or an outward aspect of speech? (Ar-Ra’d: 33). I said: The statement of Ibn Abbas is more similar to the outward appearance of worldly life, to the point that Al-Hasan said: By God, one of them has such a high level of worldly knowledge that he would save a dirham and tell you its weight, but he does not know how to pray. Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mubarrad said: Khosrow divided his days and said: A windy day is suitable for sleeping, a cloudy day is for hunting, a rainy day is for drinking and amusement, and a sunny day is for necessities. Ibn Khalawayh said: He was not the most knowledgeable of them about worldly affairs. They only know the outward appearance of worldly life. And they are heedless of the Hereafter, meaning of knowing it and working for it. They are heedless. Some of them said: It is a misfortune to see yourself in the morning in the form of a hearing and seeing man. He is aware of every misfortune in his money, but if he is afflicted with a debt, he does not feel it.
30:8: God Almighty says: “Have they not reflected within themselves? God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. And indeed, many of the people, concerning the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers.” God the Almighty says: In themselves is an adverbial phrase for disbelief with an object, transitive to which is the preposition yatfakkaru, because they were not commanded to think about the creation of themselves, but rather they were commanded to use disbelief in the creation of the heavens and the earth and themselves, so that they may know that God did not create the heavens and other things except with the truth. Al-Zajjaj said: There is an ellipsis in the speech, meaning so that they may know, because the speech contains evidence for it. Except with the truth Al-Farra' said: Its meaning is except for the truth, meaning reward and punishment. It was also said: except to establish the truth. It was also said: with the truth with justice. It was also said: with wisdom, and the meanings are close. It was also said: with the truth, meaning that He is the Truth and the Truth created them, and this is evidence of His Oneness and Power. And a specified term means that the heavens and the earth have a term to which they will end, which is the Day of Resurrection. This is a reminder of annihilation, that every creature has a term, and of the reward of the good-doer and the punishment of the evil-doer. It was also said: and a specified term means that He created what He created at a time He specified because by creating that thing it is in it. And indeed, many people, in the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers. The lam is for emphasis, and the meaning is: are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord, in the order of precedence and delay, meaning they are disbelievers in the resurrection after death. And you say: Indeed, Zaid is sitting in the house. If you had said: Indeed, Zaid is sitting in the house, it would have been permissible. But if you had said: Indeed, Zaid is sitting in the house, it would not have been permissible, because the lam is only used to emphasize the subject of in and its predicate, and if you use them, it would not have been permissible. And likewise, if you say: Indeed, Zaid is sitting in the house, it would not have been permissible.
30:9: God the Almighty says: Have they not traveled through the land and observed with their eyes and hearts, how was the end of those before them who were stronger than them in strength and tilled the earth that is, they turned it over for cultivation, because the people of Mecca were not people of tillage. God the Almighty says: tilled the earth (al-Baqarah 2:71). And populated it more than they have populated it that is, those people populated it more than these people, so their cultivation and long life did not benefit them. And their messengers came to them with clear proofs that is, with miracles. It was also said: with rulings, but they disbelieved and did not believe. So it was not God who would wrong them by destroying them without sin, messengers, or proof. But they were wronging themselves by polytheism and disobedience.
30:10: God the Almighty says: Then the end of those who did evil was the worst. Al-Su'i is the feminine form of Al-Aw's, which is the ugliest, just as Al-Hasan is the feminine form of Al-Ahsan. It was said that it means Hellfire here, as said by Ibn Abbas. The meaning of they did evil is that they associated partners with God, indicated by the fact that they denied the signs of God. Al-Su'i is the name of their Hell, just as Al-Husna is the name of Paradise. Because they denied the signs of God means because they lied, as Al-Kisa'i said. It was also said that it means because they lied. Nafi', Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read Then was the end of the religion in the nominative case as the subject of kana. It was mentioned because its feminine form is not real. Al-Su'i is the predicate of kana. The rest read it in the accusative case as the predicate of kana. Al-Su'i in the nominative case is the subject of kana. It is possible that its name is at-Takdib, so the meaning would be: Then the denial was the end of those who did evil, and al-Sawwa is a source for they did evil, or an attribute of something omitted, meaning the evil trait. It was narrated on the authority of al-A’mash that he read: Then the end of those who did evil was evil, raising al-Sawwa. An-Nahhas said: Evil is the most severe evil, and the verbal form of it is that they denied the signs of God. It was said: with Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the Qur’an, as al-Kalbi said. Muqatil: with the punishment that he would bring down upon them. Ad-Dahhak: with the miracles of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. And they used to mock at them.
30:11: God Almighty says: God begins creation, then repeats it, then to Him you will be returned.
30:12: Abu Amr and Abu Bakr read it with a ya'. The rest read it with a ta'. God the Almighty said: The Day the Hour will arise, the criminals will be in despair. Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami read it with a fatha on the lam. What is known in the language is: a man is in a state of ablas if he is silent and his argument is cut off, and there is no hope that he will have an argument. Similar to it is: to be perplexed, as al-Ajjaj said: Hey friend, do you know a consecrated drawing? He said yes, I know it and Abelsa Some grammarians have claimed that Iblis is derived from this, and that he was Iblis because his argument was cut off. An-Nahhas: If it were as he said, it would have had to be declined, but in the Qur’an it is indeclinable. Az-Zajjaj: The silent one who is cut off in his argument, despairing of ever being guided to it.
30:13: And they had no intercessors among their partners meaning those whom they worshipped other than God and they were disbelievers in their partners they said they were not gods so they disavowed them and I disavowed them, as mentioned previously in more than one place.
30:14: The Almighty said: And on the Day the Hour appears, that Day they will be separated, meaning the believers from the disbelievers. Then He explained how they will be separated, saying: As for those who have believed, An-Nahhas said: I heard Az-Zajjaj say: The meaning of as is leave what we were doing and take up something else. Sibawayh said the same: Its meaning is that no matter what we are doing, take up something other than what we were doing.
30:15: They are in a meadow, intoxicated. Ad-Dahhak said: A meadow is paradise, and meadows are paradises. Abu Ubaid said: A meadow is something that is low, but if it is elevated, it is a hill. Another said: A meadow is at its best when it is in a high, rough place, as Al-A'sha said: What a garden of the gardens of sadness, green and lush, upon which pouring rain pours The sun laughs at it, a planet in the east, full of abundant vegetation. A day more fragrant than her, and nothing is better than her when the origin is near However, it is not called a rawdah unless it has vegetation. If it does not have vegetation and it is elevated, then it is a canal. Other than this has been said about a canal. Al-Qushayri said: The rawdah among the Arabs is what grows around a pond of vegetables, and there was nothing among the Arabs better than it. Al-Jawhari: The plural is rawdh and riyadh, the waw became a ya because of the kasrah before it. A rawdh is about half a water skin. In a pond there is a rawdah of water if its upper part is covered. Abu Amr recited: A meadow from which I watered my fresh water. Yahburun Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Abbas said: They honor. It was also said: They enjoy, and Mujahid and Qatadah said the same. It was also said: They are pleased. As-Suddi said: They rejoice. And the word habra among the Arabs means: happiness and joy, as mentioned by Al-Mawardi. Al-Jawhari said: The word habar means joy, which is happiness. It is also said: Habaru yahburu with the letter dammah as report and habra. God Almighty said: So they are in a meadow, habarun meaning they are praising, honoring, and being pleased. A man is haburu, which is derived from habar. An-Nahhas said: Al-Kisa'i narrated that habartuhu means I honored him and blessed him. I heard Ali bin Sulayman say: It is derived from their saying: On his teeth is a mark, so yahaburun means the mark of bliss is clear on them. And the word habar is derived from this. The poet said: Do not fill the camel with sweat, do you not see the one who drives it? It was said: Its origin is from the word tahbeer which means to improve, so they improve themselves. It is said: So-and-so has good ink and salt if he is handsome and has a good appearance. It is also said: because ink and dates are good with the fat-ha, and this is as if it is the source of your saying: I made him habeeru habeer if you made him beautiful. The first is a noun, and from it is the hadith: A man will emerge from the fire whose ink and salt have gone. Yahya bin Abi Katheer said in Rawdat Yahbeerun: Listening is in Paradise. Al-Awza’i said the same, he said: When the people of Paradise begin to listen, not a tree of Paradise will remain but will sing praise and glorification. Al-Awza’i said: No one among God’s creation has a better voice than Israfil, so when he begins to listen, he will interrupt the prayers and glorifications of the people of the seven heavens. Al-Awza’i added: “There is not a tree in Paradise that is not shaken, and there is not a curtain or door that is not shaken and opened, and there is not a ring that is not humming with the colors of its humming, and there is not a thicket of golden thickets that is not affected by the sound of sounds in its niches, so those niches resound with the most varied tunes, and there is not a slave girl from the maidens of the wide-eyed houris that is not singing her songs, and the birds her melodies, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, inspires the angels to answer them and make My servants who have purified their ears from the flutes of Satan hear, so they are answered with spiritual melodies and voices, and these voices mix and become one tremor, then God, the Most High, says: ‘O David, stand at the foot of My throne and glorify Me.’ So David rushes forward to glorify his Lord with a voice that drowns out the sounds and makes them clear, and the pleasure is multiplied, and that is what God, the Most High, says: ‘And they are in a meadow, rejoicing.’” Al-Tirmidhi, the wise, mentioned it. Al-Tha'labi mentioned from the hadith of Abu Darda': The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was mentioning the people, and he mentioned Paradise and what it contains of spouses and blessings, and among the people was a Bedouin who said: O Messenger of God, is there anyone who can listen to music in Paradise? He said: Yes, O Bedouin! Indeed, in Paradise there is a river whose banks are virgins, each with a five-inch egg, singing with voices the likes of which no creation has ever heard. That is the best of the blessings of Paradise. A man asked Abu Darda': What do they sing with? He said: Praise be to God. The Khamsaniyah is the one with a slender upper body, the Khamsanah is the one with a five-inch belly, and the fat lower body. I said: All of this is from the bliss, joy and honor, so there is no contradiction between those sayings. And this is from the words of God Almighty: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes 32:17 as will come, and the words of the Prophet (peace be upon him): In it is that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. It has been narrated that in Paradise there are trees with silver bells on them, so when the people of Paradise want to listen, God sends a wind from under the Throne, and it falls on those trees and moves those bells with sounds that if the people of this world heard them, they would die of joy. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this.
30:16: The Almighty says: And as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, this has already been discussed. And the meeting with the Hereafter, meaning the resurrection. These will be brought to the punishment, meaning they will reside. It has also been said: gathered. It has also been said: tormented. It has also been said: descending. From this is the Almighty’s saying: When death approaches one of you, (al-Baqarah 2:180), meaning it befalls him, as Ibn Shajarah said, and the meanings are close.
30:17: There are three issues: First: The Almighty's statement: So glory be to God the verse. There are three opinions on this: First: It is addressed to the believers, commanding worshippers and urging them to pray at these times. Ibn Abbas said: The five daily prayers are mentioned in the Quran. He was asked: Where? He said: God the Almighty said: So glory be to God when you reach the evening the Maghrib and Isha prayers, and when you reach the morning, the Fajr prayer, and when you reach the afternoon, and when you reach the noon prayer. Ad-Dahhak and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said the same. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said: The verse refers to four prayers: Maghrib, Fajr, Asr, and Dhuhr. They said: The last Isha prayer is in another verse in and at the approach of the night (Hud 11:114) and in mentioning the times of private parts. An-Nahhas said: The commentators agree that this verse So glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning refers to the prayers. I heard Ali ibn Sulayman say: In my opinion, its true meaning is: So glorify Him in the prayers, because glorification occurs in prayer, and this is the second opinion. The third statement: So glorify God when you go to bed and when you wake up. Al-Mawardi mentioned the first statement, and his wording therein is: Pray to God when you go to bed and when you wake up. There are two views on naming the prayer as tasbih. The first is because it includes mention of glorification in bowing and prostration. The second is derived from the word tasbih, which means prayer. From this comes the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): They will have a tasbih on the Day of Resurrection, meaning prayer.
30:18: Second: The Almighty's saying: And to Him be praise in the heavens and the earth is an interjection between the speech about the constant praise of His blessings and favors. It was said: The meaning of To Him be praise is prayer to Him, since it is specific to the recitation of Al-Hamd. The first is more apparent, because praise be to God is a type of glorifying God Almighty and urging people to worship Him and to continue His blessings, so it is a different type than prayer, and God knows best. He began with the Maghrib prayer because the night precedes the day. In Surah Subhan, He began with the Dhuhr prayer, since it was the first prayer that Gabriel led the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Mawardi said: He specified the night prayer with the name Tasbeeh and the daytime prayer with the name Al-Hamd because during the day a person is in fluctuating states that require praising God Almighty for them, and at night he is in seclusion that requires declaring God free from evil in it, so that is why the night prayer was named Al-Hamm. Third: Ikrimah read, Sometimes you spend the evening and sometimes you accompany, meaning, Sometimes you spend the evening and sometimes you spend the morning. So, he deleted it for the sake of alleviation, and the ruling on it is like the ruling on, Beware of a Day when no soul shall suffice for another soul at all. (Surat al-Baqarah 2:123) And about ‘ashiyyah, Al-Jawhari said: “The ‘ashiyyah and the ‘ashiyah are from the Maghrib prayer until the night prayer. You say, ‘I came to him yesterday in the evening’ and ‘ashiyyah yesterday.’” The diminutive of ‘ashiyyah is ‘ashiyan, not according to the rule of the amplified form, as if they made the diminutive ‘ashiyan, and the plural is ‘ashiyanat. It was also said in its diminutive: with a kasra and a long vowel like ‘ashi. The two ‘asha’s are Maghrib and ‘ashiyyah. Some people claimed that ‘ashiyyah is from the sun’s zenith until the break of dawn, and they recited: We went out in the morning, at dawn, at night, and then at noon. Al-Mawardi: The difference between evening and nightfall is that evening is the beginning of darkness after sunset, and nightfall is the end of the day when the sun sets. It is derived from the word ‘asha’, which means a lack of light from the observer, like a lack of sunlight.
30:19: God Almighty says: “He brings the living out of the dead and brings the dead out of the living, and He gives life to the earth after its lifelessness. And thus you will be brought out.” He demonstrated the perfection of His power, that is, just as He revived the earth by producing plants after its dormancy, so He will revive you through resurrection. This is evidence of the validity of analogy, and the statement, He brings the living out of the dead, has already been mentioned in the Surah Al Imran.
30:20: His saying, And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly, you were human beings dispersing.
30:21: God Almighty says: “And among His signs is that He created for you mates from among yourselves, that you may find tranquility in them, and He has put between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.”
30:22: God Almighty says: “And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and colors. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.”
30:23: God Almighty says: “And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.”
30:24: God Almighty says: “And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, [causing] fear and hope, and that He sends down water from the sky and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.”
30:25: God Almighty says: “And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. Then, when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you come forth.”
30:26: The Almighty says: And among His signs is that He created you from dust. That is, among the signs of His Lordship and Oneness is that He created you from dust, that is, He created your father from it, and the branch is like the root. This was previously explained in Al-An’am. And that is in the nominative case as a subject, and so is that He created for you mates from among yourselves. “Then you are human beings spreading out” Then you are rational, speaking beings who act in what is essential to your livelihood. He would not have created you in vain. Whoever is able to do this is worthy of worship and glorification. The meaning of He created for you mates from among yourselves is women with whom you may find peace. From among yourselves means from the sperm of men and from your kind. It was said that what is meant is Eve, whom He created from Adam’s rib, as Qatada said. And He has placed between you affection and mercy. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: Affection is sexual intercourse, and mercy is children. Al-Hasan also said the same. It was also said: Affection and mercy are the affection of their hearts towards one another. Al-Suddi said: Affection is love, and mercy is preemption. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: Affection is the love of a man for his wife, and mercy is his mercy towards her that he would harm her. It is said that man is originally from the earth and in him is the strength of the earth, and in him is the vagina from which his creation began, so he needs a place of rest. Woman was created as a place of rest for man. God the Most High said: And among His signs is that He created you from dust. And He said: And among His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them. So the first comfort a man feels with a woman is his tranquility with her, which is the boiling of strength in her. That is because when the vagina is carried in it, the semen is stirred towards it, so it finds tranquility towards her and through her he is freed from the arousal. And the vagina was created for men from women, as God the Most High said: And you leave what your Lord has created for you of your mates (Ash-Shu’ara’: 166). So God the Almighty informed men that this position in them was created for men, so she must make it available whenever the husband calls her. If she refuses, then she is unjust and will be in great difficulty. Sufficient for you is what is proven in Sahih Muslim from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, no man calls his wife to his bed and she refuses him, but the One in heaven is angry with her until he is pleased with her. In another version: If a woman spends the night avoiding her husband’s bed, the angels curse her until morning. And among His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth [Surah Al-Baqarah], and they acknowledged that God is the Creator. And the diversity of your tongues and colors [Surah Al-Baqarah] means the tongue and the mouth, and this includes the difference in languages: from Arabic to Persian, Turkish and Roman. And the colors differ in images: from white, black and red, so you can hardly see one person without distinguishing him from the next. These things are not the action of the sperm nor the action of the parents, so there must be an agent, so it is known that the agent is God, the Most High, and this is one of the clearest proofs of the Planner and Creator. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge [Surah Al-Baqarah], meaning for the righteous and the wicked. Hafs read: for those of knowledge with a kasra on the lam, the plural of world. And among His signs is your sleep by night and by day. It has been said that there is an inversion of the meaning in this verse: And among His signs is your sleep by night and your seeking of His bounty by day. The preposition was omitted because it is connected to the night and is conjoined to it. The waw takes the place of a preposition when it is connected to the conjoined noun in particular, so sleeping at night is evidence of death, and acting during the day is evidence of resurrection. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen. He means hearing with understanding and contemplation. It has also been said that they hear the truth and follow it. It has also been said that they hear the sermon and fear it. It has also been said that they hear the Qur'an and believe it, and the meanings are close. It has also been said that among them were those who, when the Qur'an was recited while they were present, would plug their ears so as not to hear. So God, the Almighty, made these proofs clear to Him. And among His signs is that He shows you lightning, causing fear and hope. It was said that the meaning is that He shows you, but the that was omitted because the speech indicates it. Tarafa said: Oh you who blame me for the green of war and witnessing pleasures, will you make me immortal? It was said: It is an inversion of the former, meaning that He shows you lightning as one of His signs. It was also said: And among His signs is a sign with which He shows you lightning, as the poet said: Life is nothing but two tarts, one of which I die, and the other I struggle to live. It was said: that is, among His signs is that He shows you lightning, for fear and hope of His signs. Al-Zajjaj said this, so it is a sentence connected to another sentence. For fear, that is, for the traveler. And hope for the resident, said Qatadah. Ad-Dahhak: For fear of lightning, and hope for rain. Yahya ibn Salam: For fear of the cold that will destroy the crops, and hope for the rain that will revive the crops. Ibn Bahr: For fear that the lightning will be a deceptive lightning that does not bring rain, and hope that it will bring rain. He recited the words of the poet: Let not your lightning be a deceptive lightning, for the best lightning is that which is accompanied by rain. Another said: He wanted water without any provision except for the lightning that passed through the clouds. And the deceptive lightning: that which does not bring rain, as if it is deceiving. And from this it is said to someone who promises but does not fulfill: You are only like a deceiving lightning. And deceit is also: the clouds that do not have rain. And it is said: deceiving lightning, with the addition. “And He sends down from the sky water and revives the earth with it after its lifelessness. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.” Previous. And among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command [An] is in the nominative case as mentioned previously, meaning that they stand and hold fast by His power without pillars. It was also said: by His management and wisdom, meaning that He holds them up without pillars for the benefit of creation. It was also said: by His command with His permission, but the meaning is the same. Then when He calls you with a single call from the earth, at once you will emerge [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] meaning that the One Who did these things is able to raise you from your graves, and what is meant is the speed of that happening without delay or hesitation, just as the obeyed caller answers the one he calls, as the murderer said: I called Kilab by his name, and it was as if I called the top of a mountain, or he was faster. He means by the top of the mountain: the echo or the stone when it rolls down. And this is connected to the rising of the heavens and the earth with then because of the enormity of what will happen in that matter and His ability to do something similar, which is that He says: O people of the graves, arise, so not a soul from the first or the last will remain but will rise and look, as God Almighty said: Then He will blow into it again, and at once they will be standing, looking on Az-Zumar 39:68. The first if in God Almighty’s statement: When He calls you is for the condition, and the second in God Almighty’s statement: When you is for surprise, and it replaces the fa in the answer to the condition. The reciters agreed on the opening of the ta here in taharijoon. They differed regarding the one in Al-A’raf. The people of Madinah read: And from it you will emerge A’raf 7:25 with a damma on the ta, while the people of Iraq read it with a fatha, and Abu Ubaid is inclined towards this. The two meanings are close, except that the people of Madinah distinguished between them due to the context of the speech. The context of the speech in Al-A’raf with a damma is more similar, since death was not of their doing, and so was the expulsion. The opening in Surat Ar-Rum is more like the order of the speech, meaning if he calls you, you will go out, i.e., you will obey, so the action with them is more like that. And this going out will be at the final blast of Israfil, as mentioned above and will come. And it was read: you will go out, with a damma and a fatha on the ta’. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this and did not add anything to this, and he did not mention the difference we mentioned, and God knows best. To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth, as creation, king, and servant. All are devoutly obedient to Him. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Every devoutly obedient mention of the Qur’an is an act of obedience.
