An-Nahhas said: Obeying in the obedience of submission. It was also said: Obeying is accompanied by servitude, either by statement or by implication. This was said by Ikrimah, Abu Malik, and As-Suddi. Ibn Abbas said: Obeying and praying. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: All are devoutly obedient to Him, meaning they will stand on the Day of Resurrection, as He said: The Day mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds (Al-Mutafaqeen: 6), meaning for the reckoning. Al-Hasan said: All are devoutly obedient to Him, testifying that they are His servants. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Obeying and sincere.
30:27: And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it. The beginning of his creation is with his conception in the womb before his birth, and as for his return, it is his revival after death with the second blast of the resurrection. So He made what is known about the beginning of his creation evidence of what is hidden about his return, inferring what is witnessed from what is absent. Then He emphasized that by saying, And it is easier for Him. Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Umar read: He begins. 'Umar means He begins creation from the beginning. He begins. His evidence for this is the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, it is He who begins and repeats. (al-Buruj 85:13). The evidence for the reading of the common people is His statement: As He began you, you will return. (al-A’raf 7:29). Easier means easy, meaning that the return is easy for Him, as stated by Ar-Rabi' ibn Khaitham and Al-Hasan. Easier means easy, because nothing is easier for God than anything else. Abu Ubaid said: Whoever interprets ahwa as an expression for preferring one thing over another, his statement is rejected by the Almighty’s statement: And that is easy for God (An-Nisa’: 30) and by His statement: And their preservation does not burden Him (al-Baqarah 2:225). The Arabs interpret af’al as fa’il, and from this is the statement of Al-Farazdaq: He who made the sky high built for us a house whose pillars are stronger and taller Its pillars are dear and long. Another said: By God, I do not know, and I am afraid of where death will pass first. He wanted to say: I am afraid. Abu Ubaidah also recited: I will give you estrangement, and I swear to you that I will lean towards you despite estrangement. He wanted to lean: And Ahmad bin Yahya recited: Men wished that I would die, and if I die, then that is a path in which I am not alone. He meant: with one. Another said: By your life, Al-Zubayr is generous with his good deeds over the years and is better. Any and virtuous. And from this is their saying: God is Great, but its meaning is God the Great. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: In the recitation of Abdullah Masoud, it is easy for Him. Mujahid, Ikrimah and Ad-Dahhak said: The meaning is that the repetition is easier for Him - that is, God - than the beginning, that is, easier, even though all of it is easy for God Almighty. Ibn Abbas said this. The reason for this is that this is a parable that God Almighty gave to His servants, saying: Repeating something is easier for the creation than its beginning, so the resurrection should be easier for those who were able to begin it, according to you and among you, than the creation. It was said: The pronoun in for Him refers to the creation, that is, it is easier for Him, that is, for the creation. They will be shouted at once and they will stand and it will be said to them: Be, and they will be. That is easier for them than being sperm, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then fetuses, then children, then adults, then young men, then men or women. Ibn Abbas and Qutrub said this. It was said: Easier, easier. He said: It is easy for Asma that the distance between us has gone far, and he yearns for her and longs for her. That is, it was made easy for her. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Khaitham said about the verse, And it is easier for Him, that is, nothing is difficult for God. Ikrimah said: The disbelievers were amazed at God’s reviving the dead, so this verse was revealed. And to Him belongs the highest example, that is, whatever He, the Almighty and Majestic, willed was. Al-Khalil said: The example is the description, that is, to Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth, just as He said: The example of Paradise, which the righteous have been promised (Ar-Ra’d: 35), that is, its description. We have already discussed that. Mujahid said: The highest example is the statement, There is no god but God, meaning that which has the highest description, that is, the most exalted, which is the description of Oneness. Qatadah said the same: The highest example is the testimony that there is no god but God, and this is refuted by the verse, He sets forth for you an example from among yourselves (al-Rum 30:28), as we will explain earlier, God willing. Az-Zajjaj said: And to Him belongs the highest example in the heavens and the earth, that is, His statement, And it is easier for Him, He has set forth an example for you, so what is difficult and what is easy, means the first interpretation. Ibn Abbas said: That is, there is nothing like Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise was mentioned above.
30:28: There are two issues in this: The first: The Almighty said: From yourselves then He said: From partners then He said: From what your right hands possess The first from is for beginning, as if He said: He took an example and extracted it from the closest thing to you, which is yourselves. The second is for partiality, and the third is redundant to emphasize the question. The verse was revealed about the infidels of Quraysh, who used to say in the Talbiyah: Here I am, you have no partner except a partner who is yours, you own him and what he owns. Saeed bin Jabr said and Qatada said: This is an example that God gave to the polytheists, and the meaning is: Would any of you be pleased that his slave be like him in his wealth and soul? If you are not pleased with this for yourselves, how can you make them partners with God? Second: Some scholars said: This verse is a principle for partnership between creation due to their need for one another and its denial for God, the Exalted. This is because when He, the Almighty, says: “He sets forth for you an example from yourselves: Do you have any of what your right hands possess?” (Al-Baqarah 2:17), they should say: Our slaves are not our partners in what You have provided us! It is said to them: How can you imagine that you would absolve yourselves from sharing with your slaves and consider My slaves as My partners in My creation? This is a corrupt judgment, lack of insight and blindness of heart! So if the partnership between slaves and their masters in what the masters own is nullified and all creation is slaves of God, the Exalted, then it is nullified that anything in the world could be a partner with God in any of His actions. All that remains is that He is One and it is impossible for Him to have a partner, since partnership requires assistance, and we are in need of assisting one another with money and work, and the Eternal Precedence is far removed from that, the Almighty and Exalted. This issue is better for the student than memorizing an entire collection of jurisprudence, because all physical acts of worship are not valid unless this issue is corrected in the heart, so understand that.
30:29: The Almighty says: Rather, those who do wrong follow their own desires without knowledge. When the proof was established against them, He stated that they worship idols by following their own desires in worshipping them and imitating their ancestors in that. Then who can guide one whom God has led astray? That is, there is no guide for one whom God has led astray. This is a refutation of the Qadarites. And they will have no helpers.
30:30: The Almighty's saying: "So set your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth. [Adhere to] the fitrah of God." There are three issues: First: Al-Zajjaj said: Fitrah is in the accusative case meaning follow the fitrah of God. He said: Because the meaning of So set your face toward the religion is follow the true religion and follow the fitrah of God. Al-Tabari said: Fitrah of God is a verbal noun derived from the meaning of So set your face toward because its meaning is: He created people upon that fitrah. It was also said that its meaning is: follow the religion of God for which He created people. According to this statement, the pause on Hanif is complete. According to the first two statements, it is connected, so one does not pause on Hanif. Fitrah is called religion because people are created for it. God, the Almighty, says: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me. (al-Dhariyat 51:56) It is said: upon it, meaning for it, as in the saying of God the Almighty: And if you do evil, it is for it (al-Isra’ 17:7). The address of set your face to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is an order to him to set his face towards the straight religion, as He said: So set your face towards the right religion (Al-Rum: 43), which is the religion of Islam. Setting the face is straightening the purpose and the strength to strive in the deeds of religion. The face was mentioned specifically because it encompasses the senses of man and is the most noble of them. His nation is included in this address by agreement of the people of interpretation. And Haneef means moderate, inclined away from all the distorted and abrogated religions. Second: In Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every child is born except that he is born in a state of fitrah - in another narration: according to this religion - his father makes him a Jew, a Christian, or a Zoroastrian, just as an animal gives birth to a whole animal. Do you see any among them whose tails are mutilated?” Then Abu Hurairah said: “And read, if you wish, ‘The fitrah of God in which He has created mankind. There is no change in the creation of God.’” In another narration: until you yourselves mutilate it. They said: O Messenger of God, what do you think of one who dies young? He said: God knows best what they would have done. Wording by Muslim. Third: Scholars differed regarding the meaning of the fitrah mentioned in the Qur’an and Sunnah, with several opinions, including Islam, as stated by Abu Hurairah, Ibn Shihab and others. They said: This is what is known among the majority of the early Muslims among the people of interpretation. They provided evidence from the verse and the hadith of Abu Hurairah, and supported that with the hadith of ‘Iyadh ibn Himar al-Majashi’i that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the people one day: Shall I not tell you what God told me in His Book? That God created Adam and his children as monotheists, Muslims, and God gave them what is lawful and what is unlawful… The hadith. And with his saying (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Five are from the fitrah… Among them, he mentioned trimming the mustache, which is one of the Sunnahs of Islam. Based on this interpretation, the meaning of the hadith is that the child was created free from disbelief based on the covenant that God took from the descendants of Adam when He brought them forth from his loins, and that if they die before reaching adulthood in Paradise, they will be children of Muslims or children of disbelievers. Others said: Al-Fitra is the beginning upon which God created them, that is, upon what God created His creation upon, that He created them for life and death, happiness and misery, and to what they will become at maturity. They said: Al-Fitra in the speech of the Arabs means the beginning. Al-Fater is the beginner, and they provided evidence for that with what was narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: I did not know what Fater the heavens and the earth was until two Arabs came arguing about a well, and one of them said: I created it, meaning I created it. Al-Marwazi said: Ahmad ibn Hanbal used to hold this opinion, then he abandoned it. Abu Omar said in his book Al-Tamhid: What Malik stated in his Muwatta and mentioned in the chapter on predestination therein of the narrations - indicates that his school of thought on that was something like this, and God knows best. Among the evidence they used as evidence is what was narrated on the authority of Ka’b al-Qurazi regarding the words of God Almighty: A party He has guided and a party upon whom error is due (al-A’raf 7:30). He said: Whoever God began to create for misguidance, He will turn him into misguidance even if he performs acts of guidance. And whoever God began to create for guidance, He will turn him into guidance even if he performs acts of misguidance. God began to create Iblis for misguidance and he performed acts of happiness with the angels, then God returned him to what He began to create him for. He said: And he was among the disbelievers. I said: Ka’b’s statement has already been mentioned in Al-A’raf, and its meaning has been transmitted with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the hadith of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was called to the funeral of a young boy from the Ansar, so I said: O Messenger of God, blessed is this bird from the birds of Paradise, who did not do evil nor was he afflicted with it! He said: Or is it something else, O Aisha? Indeed, God created people for Paradise, He created them for it while they were in the loins of their fathers, and He created people for Hell, He created them for it while they were in the loins of their fathers.” Narrated by Ibn Majah in Al-Sunan. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came out to us with two books in his hand and said: ‘Do you know what these two books are?’ We said: ‘No, Messenger of God, unless you tell us.’ He said to the one in his right hand: ‘This is a book from the Lord of the Worlds in which are the names of the people of Paradise, the names of their fathers and their tribes. Then it is summarized at the end of them, so nothing will ever be added to them or taken away from them. ’ Then he said to the one in his left: ‘This is a book from the Lord of the Worlds in which are the names of the people of Hellfire, the names of their fathers and their tribes. Then it is summarized at the end of them, so nothing will ever be added to them or taken away from them. ’” He mentioned the hadith and said about it: It is a good hadith. A group said: The meaning of God’s statement: ‘He has created mankind upon it’ and his statement: ‘Every newborn is born upon the fitrah’ is not general. Rather, what is meant by people are the believers, because if everyone was created upon Islam, no one would have disbelieved. It has been proven that He created people for Hellfire, as God the Almighty said: ‘And We have certainly created for Hell’ (al-A’raf 7:179). And He brought forth offspring from the loins of Adam, black and white. He said about the boy who was killed by Al-Khidr, he was marked as an unbeliever on the day he was marked. Abu Saeed Al-Khudri narrated that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led us in the Asr prayer during the day, and in it: And among what we have memorized is that he said: “Behold, the children of Adam were created in different classes. Among them is he who is born a believer, lives as a believer and dies as a believer, and among them is he who is born an unbeliever, lives as an unbeliever and dies as a believer, and among them is he who has good judgment and good request.” Hammad bin Salamah mentioned it in Musnad Al-Tayalisi, he said: Ali bin Zaid told us on the authority of Abu Nadrah on the authority of Abu Saeed. They said: Generality with the meaning of specificity is common in the Arabic language. Do you not see the saying of God, the Almighty: And everything was destroyed (al-Ahqaf 46:25), and He did not destroy the heavens and the earth? And His saying: And We opened to them the gates of every good thing (al-An’am 6:44), and He did not open to them the gates of mercy. Ishaq bin Rahawayh Al-Hanthali said: The discussion ended with His statement: So direct your face toward the religion, inclining toward truth. Then he said: The fitrah of God, meaning that God created mankind with a fitrah that will either lead to Paradise or Hellfire. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) referred to this in his statement: Every newborn is born in a state of fitrah. That is why he said: There is no changing the creation of God. Our Sheikh Abu Al-Abbas said: Whoever says that it precedes happiness and misery, this is only appropriate for the fitrah mentioned in the Quran, because God the Most High said: There is no changing the creation of God. As for the hadith, no, because He informed in the rest of the hadith that it can be changed and altered. A group of people of jurisprudence and theoretician said: The fitrah is the creation upon which the newborn was created in the knowledge of his Lord. It is as if he said: Every newborn is born with a creation by which he knows his Lord when he reaches the age of knowledge. He means a creation different from the creation of animals, whose creation does not enable them to know Him. They argued that fitrah is creation and al-Fâtir is the Creator, based on the statement of God, the Almighty: Praise be to God, Creator of the heavens and the earth (Fâtir:1), meaning their Creator. And by His statement: And why should I not worship He who created me? (Yâ Seen:24), meaning my creation. And by His statement: Who created them (Al-Anbiya:56), meaning their creation. They said: So fitrah is creation, and al-Fâtir is the Creator. They denied that a newborn is born with disbelief or faith, knowledge or denial. They said: Rather, a newborn is usually healthy, by nature and constitution, with no faith, disbelief, denial or knowledge. Then they believe in disbelief and faith after puberty when they reach maturity. They argued based on the statement in the hadith: Just as an animal gives birth to a whole animal - meaning healthy - do you perceive any mutilated growth in it? Meaning one with one’s ear cut off. So the hearts of the sons of Adam are like those of animals because they are born complete in creation, with no defects, then their ears and noses are cut off, so it is said: These are bahâ’ir free-born and these are sâ’ib free-born. He says: “Similarly, the hearts of children at the time of their birth have neither disbelief nor faith, nor knowledge nor denial, just like grazing animals. But when they reach maturity, the devils tempt them, so most of them disbelieve, while God protects the fewest of them.” They said: “If children had been created with some disbelief or faith at the beginning of their lives, they would never have abandoned it. We may find them believing and then disbelieving.” They said: “It is logically impossible for a child at the time of his birth to understand disbelief or faith, because God brought them forth in a state in which they did not understand anything. God the Most High said: “And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers not knowing a thing.” (al-Nahl 16:78) So whoever does not know anything, it is impossible for him to disbelieve or believe, or to know or deny.” Abu ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Barr said: This is the most correct of what has been said about the meaning of the fitrah natural disposition with which people are born. Another proof for this is God the Most High’s saying: You will only be recompensed for what you used to do. (al-Tur 52:16) and Every soul is a pledge for what it has earned. (al-Muddaththir 74:38) And whoever has not reached the age of action is not held in pledge for anything.” And He said: And We never punish until We have sent a Messenger (al-Isra’ 17:15). And when they agreed to pay the blood money, retaliation, prescribed punishments, and sins from themselves in this world, the Hereafter was more deserving of that. And God knows best. It is impossible for the innate nature that reminds of Islam to be, as Ibn Shihab said, because Islam and faith are: words with the tongue, belief in the heart, and actions with the limbs, and this is absent from a child, and no rational person would be ignorant of that. As for Al-Awza’i’s statement: I asked Al-Zuhri about a man who had a slave, would it be permissible for a boy to free him while he is a breastfed infant? He said: Yes, because he was born in a state of innate nature, meaning Islam. However, his freedom is more acceptable according to those who permit it, because his ruling is the ruling of his parents. Others disagreed with them and said: Only those who fasted and prayed are eligible for obligatory manumission. There is no evidence in God’s statement, As He began you, you will return (al-A’raf 7:29), nor in the fact that God seals a person with what He has decreed and predestined for him, that a child is born as a believer or a disbeliever, since reason has testified that at that time he is not among those who can understand either faith or disbelief. The hadith which states that people are created in different classes is not among the hadiths that cannot be criticized, because it was transmitted only by Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud’an, and Shu’bah used to speak about it. However, his statement, He is born a believer, can be interpreted as meaning that he is born to be a believer, and he is born to be a disbeliever, based on God’s prior knowledge of him. There is no more consideration in his statement in the hadith, I have admitted these people to Paradise and created these people for Hellfire, than what they will end with, not that they, during their childhood, are among those who deserve Paradise or Hellfire, or are able to understand whether they believe or disbelieve. I said: And the same choice of Abu Omar and the evidence for it was adopted by more than one of the scholars, including Ibn Atiyyah in his interpretation of the meaning of fitrah, and our Sheikh Ibn Abbas. Ibn Atiyyah said: What is relied upon in the interpretation of this word is that it is the nature and disposition in the soul of the child, which is prepared and ready for him to distinguish between the creations of God, the Most High, and to use it as evidence about his Lord, and to know His laws and believe in Him. It is as if God, the Most High, said: “Set your face toward the religion that is the true faith, which is the fitrah of God, upon which mankind was created to be prepared. However, they are exposed to obstacles, such as the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ‘Every child is born in a state of fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew or an Egyptian.’ The mention of the parents is only an example of the obstacles, which are many. Our Sheikh said in his own words: God, the Most High, created the hearts of the children of Adam capable of accepting the truth, just as He created their eyes and ears receptive to what is seen and heard. As long as they remain in this state of acceptance and this capacity, they will grasp the truth and the religion of Islam, which is the true religion.” The correctness of this meaning is indicated by his statement: Just as an animal produces a whole animal, do you perceive among them any that are mutilated? Meaning that the animal gives birth to its offspring with a perfect creation, free from defects. If it were left as it was, it would remain perfect and free from defects. However, it is manipulated by cutting off its ear or branding its face, and defects and imperfections occur to it, and it deviates from its original form. The same applies to humans, and this is a real simile, the meaning of which is clear. I said: This statement is in agreement with the first statement in meaning, and that this was after realization when they understood the matter of the world, and the proof of God against them was confirmed by what He established of the apparent signs: the creation of the heavens and the earth, the sun and the moon, the land and the sea, and the alternation of night and day. Then when their desires were known within them, the devils came to them and called them to Judaism and Christianity, and their desires went right and left, and that if they died young, they would be in Paradise, I mean all the children, because when God Almighty brought forth the offspring of Adam from his loins in the form of atoms, they acknowledged His Lordship, and this is His Almighty saying: And when your Lord took from the children of Adam - from their loins - their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], ‘Am I not your Lord?’ They said, ‘Yes, we testify.’ (al-A’raf 7:172). Then He returned them to the loins of Adam if they acknowledged His Lordship and that He is God, there is no god but Him. Then He writes the servant in his mother’s womb as wretched or blessed according to the first book. So whoever was wretched in the first book will live until the pen runs over him, and the covenant taken from him in the loins of Adam regarding polytheism will be annulled. And whoever was blessed in the first book will live until the pen runs over him and he will become blessed. And whoever of his Muslim children dies young before the pen runs over him will be with their fathers in Paradise. And whoever was from the children of polytheists and died before the pen runs over him will not be with their fathers because they died according to the first covenant taken from them in the loins of Adam and the covenant was not annulled. This is the opinion of a group of the people of interpretation, and it reconciles the hadiths. And the meaning of his saying, peace be upon him, when he was asked about the children of polytheists, he said: God knows best what they would have done, meaning if they had reached adulthood. This interpretation is also indicated by the hadith of Al-Bukhari on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace - the long hadith of the vision, in which he said, peace be upon him: “As for the tall man in the garden, he is Abraham, peace be upon him. As for the children around him, every child is born in a state of fitrah.” It was said: O Messenger of God, and the children of the polytheists? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And the children of the polytheists. This is a text that resolves the dispute, and it is the most authentic hadith narrated on this topic. Other hadiths have flaws and are not from the hadiths of the leading jurists, as stated by Abu Omar ibn Abdul Barr. It was narrated on the authority of Anas that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: “They did not have good deeds for which they would be rewarded and thus be among the kings of Paradise, nor did they have bad deeds for which they would be punished and thus be among the people of Hellfire, so they are servants to the people of Paradise.” Yahya ibn Salam mentioned this in his commentary. We have expanded on this issue in the book At-Tadhkira and mentioned in the book Al-Muqtabas in the explanation of the Muwatta of Malik ibn Anas what Abu Omar mentioned about it, and praise be to God. It was also mentioned by Ishaq ibn Rahawayh who said: Yahya ibn Adam told us who said: Jarir ibn Hazim told us on the authority of Abu Raja’ Al-Attardi who said: I heard Ibn Abbas say: The affairs of this nation will continue to be favorable or similar - or a statement similar to these two - until they speak or look into children and predestination. Yahya ibn Adam said: I mentioned it to Ibn Al-Mubarak and he said: Can a person remain silent due to ignorance? I said: So are we commanded to speak? He said: So he remained silent. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: The nature of God upon which He created people is poverty and destitution, and this is good, because from the time of birth until the time of death, one is poor and needy. Yes! And in the Hereafter. God the Almighty says: There is no change in the creation of God meaning this innate nature cannot be changed by the Creator. And the command cannot be contrary to this in any way, meaning that whoever comes after Him will not be miserable, nor will whoever He created be happy, be miserable. Mujahid said: The meaning is: There is no change in the religion of God. This was also said by Qatadah, Ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, Ibn Zayd, and An-Nakha'i. They said: This is its meaning in beliefs. Ikrimah said: It was narrated from Ibn Abbas and Umar ibn Al-Khattab that the meaning is: There is no change in the creation of God among animals by castrating their males. Thus, its meaning is the prohibition of castrating male animals. This has already been mentioned in the chapter on women. That is the right religion meaning that is the straight judgment, as Ibn Abbas said. Muqatil said: That is the clear reckoning. It was also said: That is the right religion, meaning the religion of Islam is the right and straight religion. But most people do not know meaning they do not reflect and realize that they have a Creator who is worshipped, and an eternal God whose judgment and ruling have already occurred.
30:31: The Almighty's saying: turning to Him has different meanings. Some say: returning to Him in repentance and sincerity. Yahya ibn Salam and Al-Farra' said: approaching Him. Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd said: obedient to Him. It has also been said: repenting to Him for sins. From this is the saying of Abu Qais ibn Al-Aslat: If they repent, then Banu Sulaym and their people Hawazin have repented. The meaning is the same, for naab, taaba, thaba, and abb mean to return. Al-Mawardi said: There are two opinions regarding the origin of inaaba: One of them is that its origin is to cut off, and from it is taken the name naab because it is cutting off, so it is as if inaaba is to turn to God Almighty in obedience. The second: Its origin is to return, taken from naab yanub if he returns time after time, and from it is the turn because it is to return to a habit. Al-Jawhari said: And he turned back to God means he approached and repented. The turn is the singular of nawb, you say: your turn has come and your turn has come, and they take turns turning among themselves in water and other places. And it is in the accusative case as a state. Muhammad bin Yazid said: Because the meaning of: Turn your face, so turn your faces in repentance. Al-Farra’ said: The meaning is: Turn your face and those with you in repentance. It was said: It is in the accusative case as a cut off, meaning turn your face yourself and own those who turn to Him, because the command is His, a command for his nation, so it is appropriate to say turning to Him, and God the Most High said: {O Prophet, when you divorce women} (al-Talaq 65:1). And fear Him means fear Him and comply with what He has commanded you to do. And establish prayer and do not be among those who associate others with God. He made it clear that worship is of no benefit except with sincerity, so He said: And do not be among those who associate others with God. This has been explained previously in Surat An-Nisa’, Surat Al-Kahf, and others.
30:32: Of those who have divided their religion Abu Hurairah, Aisha, and Abu Umamah interpreted it as referring to the people of the Qiblah, who follow whims and innovations. This has already been explained in Al-An'am. Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas said: Those who have divided their religion are the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians. Qatadah and Muammar said the same. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read it as: they left their religion, and Ali ibn Abi Talib read it that way, meaning they left their religion that must be followed, which is Tawhid. And they became sects meaning factions, as Al-Kalbi said. It was also said: religions, as Muqatil said. Every party rejoices in what it has meaning they are pleased and conceited, because they did not discern the truth, which they must discern. It was also said: This was before the obligatory duties were revealed. A third opinion is that sins against God, the Almighty, may be caused by rejoicing in disobeying Him, and that is Satan and highway robbers, and others, and God knows best. Al-Farraa claimed that it is permissible for the completion to be and do not be among the polytheists and the meaning to be: among those who abandoned their religion and became sects, as a new sentence, and that it could be connected to what preceded it. An-Nahhas: If it is connected to what preceded it, then according to the insightful, it is based on the addition of the letter, as God Almighty said: The eminent ones among his people who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed among them, to those who believed. (al-A’raf 7:75) If it were without a letter, it would be permissible.
30:33: God the Almighty says: And when harm touches people meaning drought and hardship they call upon their Lord to lift that from them turning to Him Ibn Abbas said: Turning to Him with all their hearts, not associating anything with Him. The meaning of these words is astonishment, the astonishment of His Prophet at the polytheists for neglecting to turn to God the Almighty despite the successive arguments against them, meaning when these disbelievers are touched by harm of sickness or hardship, they call upon their Lord, meaning they seek His help to relieve what has befallen them, turning to Him alone and not to idols, because they know that there is no relief from them. Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him meaning well-being and blessings. At once a party of them associate others with their Lord meaning they associate others with Him in worship.
30:34: The Almighty's saying: That they may disbelieve in what We have given them. It was said: It is the lam of ki. It was also said: It is the lam of command in which there is a meaning of threat, as the Almighty said: So whoever wills - let him believe; and whoever wills - let him disbelieve. al-Kahf 18:29. Then enjoy yourselves, and you will soon know. It is a threat and a warning. In the Mushaf of Abdullah: And that they may enjoy themselves, meaning that they are forbidden from that in order to enjoy themselves. It is a statement about an absent person, like: that they may disbelieve. According to the script of the Mushaf, it is an address after the statement about an absent person, meaning enjoy yourselves, you who do this.
30:35: The Almighty's saying: Or have We sent down to them authority? is an interrogative that implies a decree. Ad-Dahhak said: A sultan means a book, and so did Qatada and Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas. He also expanded the discussion of the word to include the book. Al-Farra' claimed that the Arabs feminize sultan, saying: The sultan has decreed it against you. As for the Basrans, the masculine form is more eloquent, and this is how the Qur'an came about. The feminine form is permissible according to them because it means an argument, i.e. an argument that speaks for your polytheism, as Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak also said. Ali ibn Sulayman said on the authority of Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Zayd: Sultan is the plural of sultan, like raghīf and raghfān, so its masculine form is in the plural sense and its feminine form is in the group sense. We have also discussed the subject of sultan in detail in Al Imran. Sultan is that by which a person repels from himself a matter that warrants punishment, as God the Almighty said: Or I will slaughter him, or he brings me clear authority. (al-Naml 27:21)
30:36: God the Almighty says: And when We give people a taste of mercy, they rejoice in it, meaning fertility, abundance, and well-being, said Yahya bin Salam. Al-Naqqash: blessing and rain. It was also said: security and ease, and the meanings are close. They rejoice in it, meaning in mercy. But if evil befalls them, meaning affliction and punishment, said Mujahid. Al-Suddi: drought. Because of what their hands have put forth, meaning because of the sins. At once they despair, meaning they lose hope of mercy and relief, said the majority. Al-Hasan said: Despair is abandoning the obligations of God the Almighty in secret. Qanuta yaqnutu, which is the reading of the common people. Qanuta yaqnutu, which is the reading of Abu Omar, Al-Kisa'i, and Ya'qub. Al-A'mash read: Qanuta yaqnutu, with a kasra in both, like hasaba yahsubu. The verse describes the disbeliever; he despairs when faced with hardship and becomes arrogant when faced with blessings, as it was said: Like a bad donkey, if you hang it on people’s spears, it brays when it gets hungry. Many people whose faith is not firmly established in this way, as has been mentioned elsewhere, but the believer thanks his Lord when he is blessed and hopes in Him when he is in difficulty.
30:37: God Almighty says: Do they not see that God expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it? That is, He expands goodness in this world for whom He wills or restricts it. So poverty should not lead them to despair. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
30:38: The Almighty's saying: Then give the relative his right contains three issues: The first: Since we mentioned earlier that He, the Almighty, expands provision for whomever He wills and decrees that whoever is provided with abundant provision should provide sufficiency to the poor in order to test the gratitude of the rich. The address is to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and what is meant is him and his nation, because He said: That is best for those who desire the countenance of God and He commanded giving to relatives because of their closeness of kinship, and the best charity is that which is given to a relative, and in it is maintaining kinship ties. The Messenger of God, peace be upon him, preferred charity given to relatives over freeing slaves. He said to Maymuna when she freed a slave girl: If you had given her to your maternal uncles, your reward would have been greater. Second: There is a difference of opinion regarding this verse. Some say that it was abrogated by the verse on inheritance. Others say that there was no abrogation, but rather the relative has a binding right to be kind to others in all circumstances, and this is the correct view. Mujahid and Qatadah said: Maintaining kinship ties is an obligation from God, the Almighty, to the point that Mujahid said: No charity will be accepted from anyone whose kinship is in need. It was also said that what is meant by kinship are the relatives of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. The first view is more correct, as their right is clearly stated in the Book of God, the Almighty, in His saying: Then for God is a fifth of it, and for the Messenger and for near relatives (al-Anfal 8:41). Others say that the command to give to near relatives is recommended. Al-Hasan said: His right is to be supported in times of ease, and to speak to someone in times of difficulty. And the needy Ibn Abbas said: meaning, feed the beggar while circumambulating, and the wayfarer means the weak, so He made hospitality obligatory. All of this has been discussed in detail and explained in its proper places, and praise be to God. Third: That is better for those who desire the countenance of God. That is, giving what is due is better than withholding it if the intention is to seek the countenance of God and draw closer to Him. And those are the successful. That is, those who will achieve their desired reward in the Hereafter. This has already been discussed in Surat Al-Baqarah.
30:39: The words of God the Almighty: And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the people's wealth - it does not increase with God. There are four issues: First: When He mentioned what is intended by it for His sake and for which He will reward, He mentioned that description and what is also intended by it for His sake. The majority of scholars read aytamat with a long vowel, meaning you gave. Ibn Kathir, Mujahid, and Hamid read it without a long vowel, meaning what you did in interest that it may increase, just as you say I did something right and I did something wrong. They agreed on the long vowel in His words: and what you give in zakat. Interest is an increase, and its meaning has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah. There it is forbidden and here it is permissible. This proves that it is of two types: what is permissible and what is forbidden. Ikrimah said about the words of God the Almighty: And whatever you give in interest that it may increase within the people's wealth, "Usury is of two types: permissible interest and forbidden interest. As for permissible interest, it is that which guides, seeking what is better than it. Ad-Dahhak said about this verse: It is the lawful usury that is given as a gift in order to be rewarded with something better than it, neither for it nor against it. He has no reward for it and there is no sin on him. Ibn Abbas also said: And whatever interest you give, intending that a man may give something in the hope of being rewarded with something better than it, that is the one that does not increase with God, nor is its owner rewarded, but there is no sin on him. And for this meaning the verse was revealed. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Jubayr, Tawus and Mujahid said: This verse was revealed about the gift of reward. Ibn Atiyyah said: And whatever is similar to it, which a person does in order to be rewarded for it, such as greetings and other things, even if there is no sin in it, there is no reward in it and no increase with God Almighty. Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said the same. In the book of An-Nasa'i, it is narrated on the authority of Abdur-Rahman ibn Alqamah that he said: “A delegation of Thaqeef came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) with a gift. He said: ‘Is it a gift or charity? If it is a gift, then it is intended for the sake of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and to fulfill a need. If it is charity, then it is intended for the sake of God Almighty.’ They said: ‘No, rather it is a gift.’ So he accepted it from them and sat with them asking them and they asking him.” Ibn Abbas and Ibrahim An-Nakha’i also said: This was revealed about a people who give to their relatives and brothers in the hope of benefiting, supporting, and being kind to them, and to increase their wealth for the sake of their own benefit. Ash-Sha’bi said: The meaning of the verse is that whatever a person serves someone with or does for them in order to benefit from it in this world, that benefit that results from service does not increase with God. It was said that this was forbidden for the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in particular, as God Almighty says: And do not bestow a favor, expecting more in return Al-Muddaththir 77:6. Thus, it is forbidden to give something and then take more in return. It was said: It is forbidden usury. The meaning is: The matter does not exceed this statement in the sight of God. It is not ruled by the one who takes it, but rather it is for the one from whom it is taken. Al-Suddi said: The verse was revealed regarding the usury of Thaqeef, because they knew about usury and the Quraysh knew about it among them. Second: Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: The verse clearly indicates that someone who gives a gift seeks an increase in the reward from people's money. Al-Muhallab said: The scholars differed regarding someone who gives a gift seeking a reward. He said: I only meant the reward. Malik said: The matter should be looked into. If someone like him seeks a reward from the one to whom the gift was given, then he is entitled to it, such as a gift from a poor person to a rich person, a gift from a servant to his master, or a gift from a man to his leader or someone of higher standing. This is one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i. Abu Hanifa said: He is not entitled to a reward if he did not stipulate it, which is the other opinion of al-Shafi'i. He said: A gift for a reward is invalid and of no benefit because it is a sale for an unknown price. Al-Kufi argued that the subject of a gift is voluntary donation. If we required compensation for it, the meaning of donation would be nullified and it would have the meaning of opposition. The Arabs distinguished between the word for sale and the word for gift, so they made the word for sale refer to that for which compensation is due, while gift is the opposite. Our evidence is what Malik narrated in his Muwatta’ from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him that he said: Any man who gives a gift thinking that it will bring him reward, then he is bound by his gift until he is satisfied with it. A similar narration was narrated from ‘Ali may God be pleased with him who said: “Gifts are of three types: a gift intended for the sake of God, a gift intended for the sake of people, and a gift intended for reward. The gift of reward may be revoked by its owner if he does not receive reward for it.” Al-Bukhari may God have mercy on him included a chapter on reward in gifts and included the hadith of ‘Aishah who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to accept gifts and reward them. He rewarded a she-camel and rewarded someone who disapproved of the gift when the owner asked for reward. He disapproved of the gift out of displeasure because it was in excess of its value.” Narrated by al-Tirmidhi. Third: What Ali may God be pleased with him mentioned and his explanation of the gift is correct. That is because the giver is not permitted in his gift in three cases: First, that he intends thereby the face of God the Almighty and seeks a reward from Him. Second, that he intends thereby the faces of people to show off so that they will praise and commend him for it. Third, that he intends thereby the reward from the one to whom it was given. This has already been discussed. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Actions are judged by their intentions, and each person will have but what he intended. But if he intends thereby the face of God the Almighty and seeks a reward from Him, then he will have that with God by His grace and mercy. God the Almighty said: And whatever you give in zakat, desiring the Face of God - those will receive a multiplying reward. Likewise, whoever connects his relatives to be a relative so that he is not a total, then the intention in that is followed. If it is to show that it is for the worldly sake, then it is not for the sake of God, but if it is because of the right of kinship that he has over him and the bond of kinship between them, then it is for the sake of God. As for the one who intends to show off by giving his gift to people so that they will praise him and commend him for it, there is no benefit for him in his gift, nor any reward in this world or in the Hereafter. God Almighty said: O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities with reminders or injury as does one who spends his wealth [only] to be seen by people. (al-Baqarah 2:264) If a person intends to receive a reward from the one to whom he gave his gift, then he is entitled to what he intended with his gift, and he has the right to take it back unless he receives its value, according to the doctrine of Ibn al-Qasim, or unless he is satisfied with more than its value, according to the apparent statement of Umar and Ali, which is the statement of Mutraf in al-Wadiha: that the gift is what is in effect, even if it increases or decreases, then the donor has the right to take it back even if the one to whom he gave gave him a reward of more than it. It has been said: that it was in effect and did not change, then he takes what he wants. It has been said: the value is due from him, like in a marriage of delegation. However, if it was after the loss of the gift, then he is only entitled to its value, by consensus, Ibn al-Arabi said. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: that it may grow. The majority of the seven reciters read: li-yarbu with a ya’, attributing the verb to usury. Nafi’ alone read: with a damma on the ta’ and a silent waw, addressing the female, meaning that you will be frequent visitors. This is the reading of Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Al-Sha’bi. Abu Hatim said: This is our reading. Abu Malik read: li-tabarbuha with a feminine pronoun. So it will not grow with God means that they will not be purified, nor will He reward them for it, because He only accepts that which is done purely for Him. This has been mentioned previously in An-Nisa’. And whatever you give in zakat Ibn Abbas said: meaning in charity. You seek the countenance of God - it is those who will be multiplied meaning the one who accepts it and multiplies it for him tenfold or more, as He said: Who is it that would loan God a goodly loan so He may multiply it for him many times over? Al-Baqarah 2:245 And He said: And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of God and to strengthen themselves is like that of a garden on a height Al-Baqarah 2:265 And He said: These are the multiplied. He did not say you are the multiplied because He changed from addressing to the third person, like His statement: Until, when you are in the ship and it sails with them Yunus 10:22. And there are two opinions about the meaning of the multiplied: One of them is that their good deeds are multiplied, as we mentioned. The other is that their goodness and bliss are multiplied, meaning they are people of multiples, as it is said: So-and-so is maqw if his camels are strong, the beginning of strong people. And he is musmin if his camels are fat, and he is mu'tash if his camels are thirsty. And weak if his camels are weak, and from this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O God, I seek refuge in You from the wicked, the wicked, the accursed Satan. The wicked is the one who has been afflicted with wickedness. It is said: So-and-so is wicked, meaning he is wicked, in himself. And wicked: his companions are wicked.
30:40: The Almighty's saying: God is He Who created you is a subject and a predicate. The speech returns to the argument against the polytheists and that He is the Creator, the Provider, the One who causes death and gives life. Then He said in the form of a question: Is there among your partners any who does any of that? He does not do. Then He cleared Himself of rivals, opposites, companions, or children by His true saying: Glory be to Him, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him. He added partners to them because they used to refer to them as gods and partners, and to give them from their wealth.
30:41: God the Almighty says: Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea. Scholars differed about the meaning of corruption on land and sea. Qatadah and As-Suddi said: Corruption is polytheism, and it is the greatest corruption. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and Mujahid said: Corruption on land is when a son of Adam kills his brother, such as Cain killing Abel. And in the sea, it is the king who seized every ship by force. It was also said that corruption is drought, lack of vegetation and the loss of blessings. Ibn Abbas said something similar: It is the decrease in blessings due to the deeds of the servants so that they may grow rich. An-Nahhas said: This is the best statement made about the verse. It was also narrated from him that corruption in the sea is the cessation of its catch due to the sins of the sons of Adam. Atiyyah said: When rain decreases, diving decreases, fishermen fail, and sea creatures go blind. Ibn Abbas said: When it rains, the seashells open, and whatever falls from the sky is pearl. It was also said that corruption is the decline in prices and lack of livelihood. It was said: Corruption is sins, highway robbery, and injustice, meaning that this work has become an obstacle to agriculture, construction, and trade, and the whole meaning is close. The land and the sea are the two well-known and famous in the language and among the people, not what some of the servants said: that the land is the tongue and the sea is the heart, to reveal what is on the tongue and hide what is in the heart. It was also said: The land is the deserts, and the sea is the villages, said by Ikrimah. The Arabs call cities seas. Qatadah said: The land is the people of the column, and the sea is the people of the villages and countryside. Ibn Abbas said: The land is what is from the cities and villages not on a river, and the sea is what is on the bank of a river, said Mujahid, he said: By God, it is not your sea, but every village on running water is a sea. An-Nahhas said its meaning, he said: There are two opinions about its meaning: One of them: Attraction has appeared in the land, meaning in the deserts and its villages, and in the sea, meaning in the sea cities, like in the verse: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82) meaning the scarcity of rain and high prices have appeared. Because of what the hands of people have earned so that He may taste some meaning the punishment of some of what they have done then it was deleted. Another saying: That sins appeared on land and sea, so God withheld rain from them and raised their prices so that He might make them taste the punishment for some of what they did. Perhaps they will return means that they might repent. Ibn Abbas said with the letter nun - which is the reading of Al-Salami, Ibn Muhaisin, Qanbal, and Ya’qub for emphasis - meaning that We will make them taste the punishment for some of what they did.
30:42: God Almighty says: Say, ‘Travel through the land.’ That is, say to them, O Muhammad, travel through the land so that they may take a lesson from those who came before them and see what was the end of those who denied the messengers. Most of them were polytheists, that is, disbelievers, so they were destroyed.
30:43: The Almighty says: So direct your face toward the right religion. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, direct your intention and make your direction following the right religion. Meaning Islam. It was said: The meaning is make the truth clear and be extreme in your excuses, and be busy with what you are doing and do not grieve over them. Before there comes a Day from God which there is no repelling That is, God will not repel it from them, and if He does not repel it, no one will be able to repel it. According to people other than Sibawayh, it is permissible to say there is no repelling, but according to Sibawayh, this is far-fetched, unless there is a conjunction in the speech. What is meant is the Day of Resurrection. On that Day they will be divided Ibn Abbas said: It means they will be scattered. The poet said: We were Mani Jadhima for a long time until it was said that we would never split. That is, they will not separate. Similar to the Almighty’s statement: On that Day they will be separated “a group in Paradise and a group in the Blaze.” The root is yastasda’u they will split apart, and it is said: the people split apart if they disperse, and from this the word headache is derived, because it splits the hairs of the head.
30:44: The Almighty says: Whoever disbelieves, upon him shall be his disbelief meaning the recompense for his disbelief. And whoever does righteousness - then for themselves they prepare meaning they prepare for themselves in the Hereafter a bed, a home, and a resting place through righteous deeds. From this comes the word cradle for a child. A cradle is a mattress. You have spread out and leveled the mattress. Preparing matters means arranging and fixing them. Preparing an excuse means extending and accepting it. Preparing means being able. Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated on the authority of Mujahid: Then for themselves they prepare meaning: in the grave.
30:45: The Almighty says: That He may reward those who have believed. That is, they prepare themselves so that God may reward them from His bounty. It was also said that they prepare themselves so that God may reward them, that is, to distinguish the disbeliever from the Muslim. Indeed, He does not like the disbelievers.
30:46: The Almighty says: And among His signs is that He sends the winds as good tidings. That is, among the signs of His perfect power is sending the winds as good tidings, that is, with rain because they precede it. This has already been explained in Al-Hijr. And that He may give you a taste of His mercy. That is, rain and fertility. And that the ships may sail. That is, in the sea when they blow. He only increased this by His command because the winds may blow but not be favorable, so ships must be anchored and tricks made to stop them. Sometimes they will storm and sink them by His command. And that you may seek of His bounty. That is, provision through trade. And perhaps you will be grateful. For these blessings through monotheism and obedience. All of this has already been explained.
30:47: God the Almighty says: And We had certainly sent before you messengers to their people, and they came to them with clear proofs meaning miracles and clear arguments. Then We took retribution meaning they disbelieved, so We took retribution from those who disbelieved. And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers “Haqq” is the accusative of the predicate of kana, and Nasr is its subject. Abu Bakr would pause at Haqq, meaning Our punishment was incumbent, then he said: It is incumbent upon Us to support the believers is the subject and predicate, meaning He informed that He does not break His promise, and there is no breaking of promise in Our report. It was narrated from the hadith of Abu Darda’ who said: I heard the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: There is no Muslim who defends the honor of his brother except that it is incumbent upon God the Almighty to avert the fire of Hell from him on the Day of Resurrection. Then he recited: And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers. This was mentioned by An-Nahhas, Ath-Tha’labi, Az-Zamakhshari, and others.
30:48: The Almighty says: God is He who sends the winds. Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read: Al-Rih in the singular form. The rest read it in the plural form. Abu Amr said: Everything that denotes mercy is plural, and everything that denotes torment is singular. The meaning of this verse and others has already been explained in Al-Baqarah. Kasfan is the plural of kisfa, which means a piece. In the reading of Al-Hasan, Abu Ja'far, Abd Al-Rahman Al-A'raj, and Ibn Amir, it is kasfan with a sukoon on the seen. It is also the plural of kisfa, as one says sidrah and sidr. According to this reading, the pronoun that follows it refers back to it, i.e., you see the rain coming out of the kisfa, because every plural has the ha' between it and its singular and nothing else, so the masculine form is good. Whoever reads kafsan, according to him, the rain refers back to the clouds. In the reading of Ad-Dahhak, Abu Al-'Aliyah, and Ibn Abbas, it is: you see the rain coming out of its gap. It is possible that khalal is the plural of khalal. So when it afflicts with it means with rain. Whoever He wills of His servants, at once they rejoice they rejoice when rain falls upon them.
30:49: And if they were, before it was sent down upon them, in despair meaning, they were hopeless and depressed, and grief had appeared on them because of the withholding of rain from them. And before is a repetition according to Al-Akhfash meaning emphasis, and most grammarians agree with this statement, as stated by An-Nahhas. Qutrub said: The first before is for the sending down and the second for the rain, meaning, if they were before the sending down, before the rain. It was also said: The meaning is before the sending down of rain upon them, before the crops. The rain indicates the crops because it is caused by it. It was also indicated by they saw it yellow as will be mentioned later. It was also said: The meaning is before the clouds, before seeing it, and this statement was chosen by An-Nahhas, meaning before seeing the clouds, in despair meaning, hopeless. The clouds were mentioned previously.
30:50: The Almighty's saying: Then look at the traces of God's mercy meaning the rain, that is, look with insight and deduction, that is, they deduced from this that the One over whom He has power is able to revive the dead. Ibn Amir, Hafs, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read it as Athar in the plural. The rest read it as Singular because it is an adjunct to a singular noun. The effect is the subject of Yahya, and it is possible that the subject is the name of God. Whoever reads Athar in the plural, it is because God's mercy can be intended to mean abundance, as God the Almighty said: And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them (Ibrahim 14:34). Al-Jahdary, Abu Haywah, and others read Kifayat yathiyya al-ard with a ta'. The feminine gender was transferred to the word mercy because the effect of mercy takes its place, so it is as if it is mercy, that is, how mercy revives the earth or the effects. Yahya means God the Almighty revives or the rain or the effect for those who read it with a ya'. How He revives the earth is in the accusative case as a state, based on the meaning, because the word is a question and the state is the predicate. The meaning is: Look at the effect of God's mercy reviving the earth after its death. Indeed, He is the Reviver of the dead, and He is over all things competent. Proof of the unseen from the witness.
30:51: The Almighty said: And if We send a wind and they see it yellow meaning the wind, and the wind can be made masculine. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: It is not forbidden to make any non-real feminine masculine, such as I liked the house and the like. It was also said: They saw the clouds. Ibn Abbas said: "The crops, which are the traces, and the meaning is: They saw the traces yellowing." The yellowing of the crops after their greening indicates that it will not rain, and the wind indicates that it does not pollinate. They would have continued to disbelieve after it means they would have continued to do so. The past tense is good in place of the future tense because of the meaning of recompense in the speech, and recompense can only occur in the future, as Al-Khalil and others said.
30:52: The Almighty says: For indeed, you cannot make the dead hear. That is, the arguments are clear, O Muhammad, but because they are accustomed to imitating their forefathers in disbelief, their minds have died and their insights have become blind. Therefore, you will not be able to make them hear or guide them. This is a refutation of the Qadarites. You will not hear except those who believe in Our verses meaning, you will not hear God’s admonitions except those who believe in the evidence of monotheism and for whom guidance was created. This was mentioned previously in An-Naml, and the phrase with the guidance of the blind was used here without the letter yaa.
30:53: God Almighty says: “And you cannot guide the blind from their misguidance. You can only make hear those who believe in Our verses, and they are Muslims.”
30:54: The Almighty's saying: God is He Who created you from weakness He mentioned another proof of His power in the soul of man so that we may consider. The meaning of: from weakness is from a weak spot. It was said: from weakness, meaning in a state of weakness, which is what they were in the beginning of childhood and young age. Then He made, after weakness, strength means youth. Then He made, after strength, weakness means old age. Asim and Hamzah read it with a fatha on the dad in both of them, the rest with a damma. Two dialects, and the damma is the language of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. Al-Jahdary read: from weakness, then made after weakness with a fatha in both of them, weakness with a damma in particular. He wanted to combine the two dialects. Al-Farra' said: The damma is the language of Quraysh, and the fatha is the language of Tamim. Al-Jawhari: Weakness and weakness: the opposite of strength. It was said that weakness with a fatha is in opinion, and with a damma is in the body, and from this is the hadith about the man who used to cheat in sales: that he would buy but his knot was weak. And old age is a verbal noun like old age, and the verbal noun can be used for a sentence, and the same is said about weakness and strength. He creates what He wills meaning strength and weakness. And He is the All-Knowing of His planning. The All-Powerful over His will. The Kufi grammarians permitted the opening of the 'ayn to be pronounced with a fat-ha on the 'ayn, as well as anything that contains a throat letter as a second or third letter.
30:55: The Almighty's statement: And on the Day the Hour will appear, the criminals will swear, meaning the polytheists will swear, They did not remain [in the world] more than an hour. This does not negate the punishment of the grave, as it has been authenticated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) through more than one chain of narration that he sought refuge from it and commanded others to seek refuge from it. Among this is what was narrated by Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard Umm Habibah saying: 'O God, protect me by means of my husband, the Messenger of God, and by means of Abu Sufyan, and by means of my brother Mu'awiyah.' The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to her: 'You have asked God for fixed terms of life and allotted provisions, but ask Him to punish you with the punishment of Hell and the punishment of the grave.'" This is in well-known hadiths narrated by Muslim, al-Bukhari, and others. We have already mentioned a number of them in the Book of Remembrance. Concerning the meaning of they did not remain more than an hour, there are two opinions: One of them is that there must be an end before the Day of Resurrection. Based on this, they said: We did not remain more than an hour. Another saying: That they mean in this world because of its transience and cessation, as God Almighty said: On the Day they see it, it will be as if they had not remained [in the world] except for an afternoon or a morning thereof (al-Nazi’at 79:46), as if they had not remained except for an hour of a day, even though they had sworn to something unseen and something they did not know. God Almighty said: Thus they were lying meaning they were lying in this world. It is said: A man is akka if he is turned away from truthfulness and goodness. And a land that is forbidden from rain. A group of people of insight have claimed that there cannot be a lie about what they are in on the Day of Resurrection, and the Qur’an indicates otherwise. God the Almighty said: Thus were they deluded, meaning just as they were turned away from the truth in their oath that they had not remained except for an hour, so too were they turned away from the truth in this world. God the Almighty said: Then the only trial they had was that they said, ‘By our Lord, we were not polytheists.’ See how they denied it. al-An’am 6:23-24
30:56: God the Almighty says: And those who have been given knowledge and faith will say, 'You have remained in the Book of God until the Day of Resurrection.' There is disagreement about those who have been given knowledge. Some say it is the angels. Others say it is the prophets. Others say it is the scholars of the nations. Others say it is the believers of this nation. Others say it is all the believers, meaning the believers will say to the unbelievers in response to them, 'You have remained in your graves until the Day of Resurrection.' The fa in His statement, This is the Day of Resurrection is the answer to an omitted condition indicated by the speech, figuratively: If you deny the Resurrection, then this is the Day of Resurrection. Ya'qub narrated from some of Al-Farra' that it is Al-Hasan's reading: 'until the Day of Resurrection' with a fat-ha, and this is one of the throat letters. It was said that the meaning of in the Book of God is in the judgment of God. Others say that there is an inversion in the speech, meaning that those who have been given knowledge and faith will say, 'You have remained until the Day of Resurrection.' This was said by Muqatil, Qatadah, and As-Suddi. Al-Qushayri said: Based on this, those who have been given knowledge means the Book of God. It was said: Those who were judged in the Book with knowledge, This is the Day of Resurrection, meaning the day that you denied.
30:57: God the Almighty says: On that Day, no excuse will benefit those who did wrong. That is, neither knowledge of the Resurrection nor apologies on that Day will benefit them. It was said: When the believers responded to them, they asked to return to the world and apologized, but they were not excused. Nor will they seek forgiveness. That is, their condition will not be the same as that of someone who seeks forgiveness and returns. It is said: I sought his forgiveness, so he excused me, meaning I appeased him, so he appeased me. This is when you were against him. The true meaning of I appeased him is: I removed his reproach. This will be explained in Fussilat. Asim, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read: On that Day, no excuse will benefit with a ya', and the rest with a ta'.
30:58: God Almighty says: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur’an from every [kind of] example. That is, from every example to guide them to what they need and alert them to monotheism and the truthfulness of the messengers. And if you bring them a sign, that is, a miracle, such as the splitting of the sea, the staff, and others, those who disbelieve will surely say, ‘You are nothing but falsifiers.’ That is, you follow falsehood and magic.
30:59: Likewise meaning just as God has sealed their hearts so that they do not understand the verses from God, so too God seals the hearts of those who do not know the evidence of monotheism.
30:60: "So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is truth." That is, be patient in the face of their harm, for God will support you. And do not let those who have no certainty impress you. That is, do not provoke you away from your religion. Those who have no certainty It was said: He is An-Nadr ibn Al-Harith. The address is to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), but what is meant is his nation. It is said: So-and-so impresses so-and-so, meaning he treated him with ignorance until he led him to follow in error. It is in the accusative case with the prohibition, emphasized with the heavy nun, so it is built on the fatha, as two things are stated when one of them is joined to the other. Those who have no certainty is in the nominative case, and some Arabs say al-ladhūn is in the nominative case. This has been mentioned previously in Al-Fatihah.
31:1: The Almighty said: Alif, Lam, Meem.
31:2: God Almighty says: These are the verses of the Wise Book.
31:3: God Almighty says: Guidance and mercy for the doers of good.
31:4: God Almighty says: Those who establish prayer and give zakat and, of the Hereafter, are certain.
31:5: It is a Meccan surah consisting of two verses. Qatada said: The first is, And if all the trees on the earth were pens, to the end of the two verses. Ibn Abbas said: It is composed of three verses, the first of which is, And if all the trees on the earth were pens. It consists of thirty-four verses. The Almighty says: “Alif, Lam, Meem. These are the verses of the Wise Book.” We have already discussed the openings of the surahs, and those is in the nominative case with an implied subject, meaning this and those. It is also said: Those are the verses of the Wise Book instead of those. The Book is the Qur’an. And the Wise is the definitive, meaning there is no flaw or contradiction in it. Guidance and mercy for the doers of good. It was said that it was from Dhu al-Hikmah and it was said that it was from al-Hakim. Guidance and mercy is in the accusative case as a state, like: This she-camel of God is a sign for you (al-A’raf 7:73). This is the reading of the Medinans, Abu Umar, Asim, and al-Kisa'i. Hamzah read it: guidance and mercy in the nominative case, and this is from two aspects: One of them: with an implied subject, because it is the first verse. The other: that it is the predicate of that. The doer of good is the one who worships God as if he sees him, and if he does not see him, then He sees him. It was said: they are the doers of good in religion, which is Islam. God the Most High said: And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to God (al-Nisa': 125). Those who establish prayer is in the place of an attribute. The nominative case is permissible for certainty, meaning: they are the ones, and the accusative case with an implied meaning. We have already discussed this verse and the one after it in al-Baqarah and others.
31:6: The Almighty said: And of mankind is he who buys the amusement of speech [Min] in the nominative case as a subject. And amusement of speech means singing, according to Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas and others. An-Nahhas said: It is forbidden in the Qur'an and Sunnah, and the meaning is: Who buys that which is amusement, male or female, like in the verse: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82) or the meaning could be: Since he only bought it, he buys it and exaggerates its price as if he bought it for amusement. I said: This is one of the three verses that scholars have used as evidence for the undesirability and prohibition of singing. The second verse is the Almighty’s saying: And you are steadfast (al-Najm 53:61). Ibn Abbas said: It is singing in the Himyarite language, asmadi lana, meaning sing for us. The third verse is the saying of God the Almighty: And incite with your voice whomever you can among them (al-Isra’ 17:64). Mujahid said: Singing and musical instruments. This has already been discussed in Subhan. At-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Abu Umamah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do not sell female singers, nor buy them, nor teach them, and there is no good in trading in them, and their price is unlawful. Concerning such matters, this verse was revealed: And of mankind is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [people] from the way of God (al-Isra’ 17:64). Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a strange hadith. It is only narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim on the authority of Abu Umamah, and Al-Qasim is trustworthy, and ‘Ali ibn Yazid is considered weak in hadith, according to Muhammad ibn Ismail. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: Ibn Mas‘ud, Ibn ‘Abbas, Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah and Mujahid interpreted it this way. Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi mentioned it on the authority of Al-Hasan, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and Al-Nakha’i. I said: This is the most that has been said about this verse, and Ibn Masoud swore by God, there is no god but Him, three times, that it is singing. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Abu Al-Sahbaa Al-Bakri, who said: Abdullah bin Masoud was asked about the verse: And of mankind is he who buys idle talk, so he said: Singing, by God, there is no god but Him, repeating it three times. Ibn Umar narrated that it is singing, and so did Ikrimah, Maymun bin Mihran, and Makhul. Shu’bah and Sufyan narrated on the authority of Al-Hakam and Hammad on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah bin Masoud said: Singing causes hypocrisy to grow in the heart, and Mujahid said the same, and he added: Idle talk in the verse means listening to singing and similar falsehood. Al-Hasan said: Idle talk is musical instruments and singing. Al-Qasim bin Muhammad said: Singing is falsehood, and falsehood is in the Fire. Ibn Al-Qasim said: I asked Malik about it, and he said: God, the Most High, said: So what is there after the truth except error? (Yunus 10:32). Is it true? Al-Bukhari included a chapter on Every amusement is false if it distracts from obeying God, and Whoever says to his companion, ‘Come, let’s gamble,’ and the statement of God the Almighty: And of mankind is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [people] from the way of God without knowledge and takes it in ridicule. His statement, if it distracts [people] from the way of God, is taken from the statement of God the Almighty: to mislead [people] from the way of God. And also from Al-Hasan: It refers to disbelief and polytheism. Some people interpreted it as referring to the hadiths that amuse the people of falsehood and play. It was said that it was revealed about Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, because he bought the books of the Persians, Rustam and Isfandiyar, and he used to sit in Makkah. When the Quraysh said that Muhammad said such and such, he would laugh at him and tell them the hadiths of the kings of the Persians, saying, My hadith is better than the hadith of Muhammad. This was narrated by Al-Farra’, Al-Kalbi, and others. It was also said that he used to buy female singers and would not pass by anyone intending to become a Muslim except that he would go with him to his female singer and say, Feed him, give him drink, and sing to him. And he would say, This is better than what Muhammad invites you to of prayer, fasting, and fighting in his presence. This statement and the first are clear in referring to buying. A group said: The purchase in this verse is metaphorical, and the verse was revealed regarding the hadiths of the Quraysh and their distraction with the matter of Islam and their involvement in falsehood. Ibn Atiyyah said: So, abandoning what is required to be done and complying with these reprehensible acts was purchasing them, as God Almighty said: Those are the ones who have purchased error in place of guidance Al-Baqarah 2:16, and they purchased disbelief in place of faith, meaning they exchanged it for it and chose it over it. Mutraf said: Purchasing the amusement of speech is its desirability. Qatadah said: Perhaps he does not spend money on it, but listening to it is purchasing it. I said: The first statement is the most correct of what has been said in this regard, due to the authentic hadith on it, and the statements of the Companions and Followers regarding it. Al-Tha’labi and Al-Wahidi added in the hadith of Abu Umamah: “There is no man who raises his voice in singing except that God sends two devils against him, one on this shoulder and the other on that shoulder, and they continue to strike their feet until he is the one who silences.” Al-Tirmidhi and others narrated from the hadith of Anas and others on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: “Two cursed and wicked sounds that I have forbidden: the sound of a flute and the wailing of a devil at a tune or joy, and the wailing of a calamity, slapping cheeks and tearing garments.” Ja’far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: I was sent to break the flutes. Narrated by Abu Talib Al-Ghailani. Ibn Bishran narrated on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was sent to destroy flutes and drums.
