Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If my nation does fifteen things, calamities will befall it - and he mentioned among them: if female singers and musical instruments are taken.” And in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: And female singers and musical instruments appear. Ibn al-Mubarak narrated on the authority of Malik ibn Anas on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir on the authority of Anas ibn Malik who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever sits with a female singer and listens to her, molten lead will be poured into his ear on the Day of Resurrection. Asad ibn Musa narrated from Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salamah from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir who said: We have been informed that God the Almighty will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Where are My servants who purified themselves and their ears from amusement and the flutes of Satan? Let them be permitted the gardens of musk and inform them that I have made My pleasure permissible upon them. Ibn Wahb narrated a similar version from Malik from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, adding after the words: musk: Then He will say to the angels: Let them hear My praise, thanks, and glorification. And inform them that they have no fear, nor will they be disgraced. This meaning has been narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever listens to the sound of singing will not be permitted to hear the spiritualists. It was said: Who are the spiritualists, O Messenger of God? He said: The reciters of the people of Paradise. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim Abu Abdullah in Nawadir al-Usul. We have mentioned in the book al-Tadhkira with similar examples: Whoever drinks alcohol in this world will not drink it in the hereafter, and whoever wears silk in this world will not wear it in the hereafter. And so on. All of that is correct in meaning as we have explained there. From the narration of Makhul from Aisha, she said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Whoever dies and has a singing slave girl with him, do not pray over him. For this and other narrations, the scholars have prohibited singing. This is the second issue: It is the usual singing among those who are famous for it, which stirs the souls and arouses them to passion and flirtation, and the licentiousness that stirs the still and awakens the hidden. If this type is in poetry in which the mention of women and their beauty are mentioned and alcohol and forbidden things are mentioned, there is no disagreement about its prohibition, because it is amusement and blameworthy singing by consensus. As for what is free from that, a little of it is permissible in times of joy, such as weddings and Eid, and when one is energetic for hard work, as was the case in digging the trench and at the borders of Anjasha and Salamah ibn al-Akwa’. As for what the Sufis have innovated today of addiction to listening to singing with musical instruments such as the shabbat, the tar, musical instruments and strings, it is prohibited. Ibn al-Arabi said: As for the drum of war, there is no harm in it, because it invigorates the soul and terrifies the enemy. And in the inkwell there is hesitation. The tambourine is permissible. Al-Jawhari: They may have called the shepherd’s reed with which he plays it, Hair’ah and Yara’ah. Al-Qushayri said: It was played in front of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on the day he entered Madinah. Abu Bakr wanted to rebuke him, but the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Leave them, Abu Bakr, until the Jews know that our religion is spacious. So they started playing it and saying: We are the daughters of the carpenter, what a wonderful neighbor Muhammad is. It has been said that the drum is like the tambourine in marriage, and similarly, the instruments used for marriage are permissible to be used in it in a way that improves speech and for someone who is not religious. Third: Continuously engaging in singing is foolishness that invalidates testimony; if it does not continue, then it is not valid. Ishaq bin Isa al-Tabbaa’ said: I asked Malik bin Anas about what the people of Madinah permit regarding singing. He said: Only the immoral do it among us. Abu al-Tayyib Tahir bin Abdullah al-Tabari said: “As for Malik bin Anas, he forbade singing and listening to it. He said: If someone buys a female slave and finds her to be a singer, should he return her due to a defect? This is the opinion of all the people of Madinah, except for Ibrahim bin Sa’d. Zakariya al-Saji narrated from him that he saw no harm in it.” Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: As for Malik, it is said that he was knowledgeable in the craft, but his opinion was that it was forbidden. It was narrated that he said: “I learned this craft when I was a young scholar. My mother said to me: ‘O my son, this craft is only suitable for one with a handsome face, but you are not like that. So seek religious knowledge.’ So I became a Rabia’ah, and God made that a good thing.” Abu Tayyib al-Tabari said: As for the school of thought of Abu Hanifa, it dislikes singing even though drinking wine is permitted, and it considers listening to singing a sin. This is also the school of thought of all the people of Kufa: Ibrahim, al-Sha'bi, Hammad, al-Thawri and others. There is no disagreement among them on this. Likewise, no disagreement is known among the people of Basra regarding its dislike and prohibition, except for what was narrated on the authority of Ubayd God ibn al-Hasan al-Anbari that he did not see anything wrong with it. He said: As for the school of thought of al-Shafi'i, he said: Singing is disliked because it resembles falsehood, and whoever indulges in it is a fool whose testimony is rejected. Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi mentioned three narrations on the authority of his imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal. He said: Our companions mentioned the permissibility of singing on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Khalal and his companion Abd al-Aziz, but they only referred to the odes that were recited in their time. He said: This is what Ahmad did not dislike, and what is indicated by it is that he was asked about a man who died and left behind a son and a female slave, and the boy needed to sell her. He said: Can she be sold as a simple slave girl worth twenty thousand? He said: She cannot be sold except as a simple slave girl. Abu al-Faraj said: Ahmad said this because this singing slave girl does not sing poems of asceticism, but rather songs of enchanting poetry that arouse passion. This is evidence that singing is forbidden, because if it were not forbidden, it would not be permissible to waste money on an orphan. This is like what Abu Talha said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I have wine for orphans. He said: Polish it. If it were permissible to reclaim it, he would not have ordered the waste of orphans’ money. Al-Tabari said: “The scholars of the regions agreed unanimously on the undesirability of singing and its prohibition. Only Ibrahim ibn Sa’d and Ubaydullah al-Anbari separated from the group, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Stick to the great masses” and Whoever separates from the group dies a death of the ignorant. Abu al-Faraj said: “Al-Qaffal, one of our companions, said: The testimony of a ma’ni and a dancer is not accepted.” I said: Since it has been proven that this matter is not permissible, then taking payment for it is not permissible. Abu Omar bin Abdul Barr claimed that there was consensus on the prohibition of payment for this. It was mentioned in Al-An'am when he said: And with Him are the keys of the unseen (Al-An'am: 59). That is enough for you. Fourth: Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: As for listening to female singers, it is permissible for a man to listen to the singing of his female slave, since nothing of her is forbidden to him, neither her outward appearance nor her inward appearance, so how can he be prevented from enjoying her voice? As for it being impermissible for women to uncover themselves before men, nor to tear down their veils, nor to listen to filth, if that deviates from what is permissible and impermissible, it is forbidden from the beginning and uprooted from its roots. Abu al-Tayyib al-Tabari said: As for listening to singing from a woman who is not a mahram, the followers of al-Shafi’i said it is not permissible, whether she is free or a slave. He said: Al-Shafi’i said: If the owner of a female slave gathers people to listen to her, then he is a fool whose testimony is rejected. Then he made a mistake in his statement and said: She is cuckoldry. He only made her owner a fool because he calls people to falsehood, and whoever calls people to falsehood is a fool. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: To mislead from the path of God. The general reading is with a damma on the ya’, meaning to mislead others from the path of guidance, and if he misleads others then he himself has gone astray. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Abu Amr, Ruways, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read it with a fatha on the ya’ as intransitive, meaning to mislead himself. And take it in jest is the reading of the Medinans, Abu Omar, and Asim in the nominative case in apposition to whoever buys. It is permissible for it to be a new sentence. Al-A’mash, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read: And take it in the accusative case in apposition to “to mislead. From both readings, it is not appropriate to pause at the statement: without knowledge, and to pause at the statement: in jest. The ha’ in take it in jest is a metaphor for the verses. It is permissible for it to be a metaphor for the path, because the path is feminine and masculine. For those is a humiliating punishment, meaning severe, which will humiliate them. The poet said: I was afraid for the Christians after the cross suffered humiliating torture.
31:7: The Almighty said: And when Our verses are recited to him, meaning the Qur’an. And he turns away, meaning he turns away. Arrogantly is the accusative of state. As if he did not hear them, as if there was deafness in his ears, meaning heaviness and deafness. This has already been mentioned. Then give him tidings of a painful punishment, has also been mentioned.
31:8: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have gardens of pleasure.
31:9: The Almighty says: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have gardens of pleasure. When He mentioned the punishment of the disbelievers, He also mentioned the pleasures of the believers. They will abide therein meaning, forever. The promise of God is true meaning, God promised them this true promise, without breaking it. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. This was also mentioned previously.
31:10: The Almighty's saying: He created the heavens without any pillars that you can see. You can see them is in the accusative case as an attribute of pillars, so it could be then pillars and you cannot see. It is also possible for it to be in the accusative case as a state of the heavens and there are no pillars then at all. An-Nahhas: I heard Ali ibn Sulayman say: It is better to be a new sentence, there are no pillars then, as Makki said. And without pillars is the completion. We have already discussed this verse in Ar-Ra'd. And He cast into the earth firmly set mountains. "lest it should shake" is in the accusative case, meaning, lest it should shake. The Kufians interpret it to mean so that it does not shake. "And We dispersed therein every kind of creature and sent down water from the sky and produced therein every noble kind." From Ibn Abbas: of every beautiful color. Ash-Sha'bi interpreted it as referring to people, because they are created from the earth. He said: Whoever among them goes to Paradise is noble, and whoever among them goes to Hell is mean. Others have interpreted the sperm as being created from dust, and the apparent meaning of the Qur’an indicates this.
31:11: The Almighty says: This is the creation of God is a subject and predicate. Creation means created, that is, what you mentioned of what you designate as God's creation, that is, God's creation, that is, He created it without a partner. Then show me, O polytheists, what those other than Him have created, meaning the idols. Rather, the wrongdoers, that is, the polytheists, are in manifest error, that is, apparent loss. What is an interrogative in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is that and that in the sense of who. "Creation is based on a deleted ha, meaning show me" as to what those other than Him have created. The sentence is in the accusative case with "show me." According to this statement, you say: "What did you learn? Grammar or poetry? It is permissible for what to be in the accusative case with show me and if" to be redundant. According to this statement, he says: "What did you learn? Grammar or poetry?"
31:12: The Almighty said: And We had certainly given Luqman wisdom as a direct object, and Luqman was not declined because at the end of it there is an extra alif and noon, so it is similar to the dual fa'laan, so it was not declined in the definite form because that is a second weight, and it was declined in the indefinite form because one of the two weights had disappeared, as stated by An-Nahhas. He is Luqman bin Ba'oura bin Nahor bin Tarah, and he is Azar of Abraham, this is how Muhammad bin Ishaq attributed him. It was also said that he is Luqman bin Anqa'a bin Sarun, and he was a Nubian from the people of Ayla, as mentioned by Al-Suhayli. Wahb said: He was the nephew of Job. Muqatil said: It was mentioned that he was the maternal cousin of Job. Al-Zamakhshari said: He is Luqman bin Ba'oura, the nephew of Job or the son of his maternal cousin, and it was also said that he was one of the sons of Azar, he lived for a thousand years and David, peace be upon him, lived during his lifetime and took knowledge from him, and he used to issue fatwas before the mission of David, but when he was sent, he stopped issuing fatwas, so it was said to him, and he said: Should I not be satisfied since I have been sufficient? Al-Waqidi said: He was a judge among the Children of Israel. Saeed bin Al-Musayyab said: Luqman was a black man from the blacks of Egypt with thick lips. God gave him wisdom and prevented him from prophethood. The majority of interpreters agree that he was a saint and not a prophet. Ikrimah and Al-Sha'bi agreed that he was a prophet, and based on this, wisdom means prophethood. The correct view is that he was a wise man by the wisdom of God - which is the correctness in beliefs, understanding of religion and reason - a judge among the Children of Israel. He was black with cracked feet and thick lips, as Ibn Abbas and others said. It was narrated from the hadith of Ibn Umar that he said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: Luqman was not a prophet, but he was a servant who thought a lot and had good faith. He loved God, so God loved him, so He bestowed wisdom upon him and gave him the choice to make him a caliph who would rule with justice. He said: O Lord, if you give me the choice, I will accept well-being and leave affliction, and if you decide upon me, then I will hear and obey, for You will protect me. Ibn Atiyyah mentioned this. Al-Tha'labi added: The angels said to him in a voice they could not see: Why, O Luqman? He said: "Because the ruler is in the toughest and most difficult of positions. The oppressed come to him from every direction. If he is humiliated in this world, that is better than being honorable in it. Whoever chooses this world over the Hereafter, this world will be denied him and he will not attain the Hereafter." The angels were amazed at the beauty of his speech. He slept and was given wisdom, and he awoke to speak with it. Then David was called after him and he accepted it - meaning the caliphate - without making any conditions as Luqman had made. He fell into sin more than once, but God pardoned him every time. Luqman supported him with his wisdom, so David said to him: Blessed are you, O Luqman! You have been given wisdom and affliction has been averted from you. David was given the caliphate and was tested with affliction and tribulation. Qatada said: God Almighty gave Luqman the choice between prophethood and wisdom, and he chose wisdom over prophethood. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him while he was asleep and sprinkled wisdom on him, and in the morning he was still speaking it. It was said to him: How did you choose wisdom over prophethood when your Lord gave you the choice? He said: If He had sent me a firm resolve with prophethood, I would have hoped for His support in it. But He gave me the choice, and I feared that I would be too weak for prophethood, so wisdom was dearer to me. There is a difference of opinion about his profession. Some say he was a tailor, as stated by Saeed bin Al-Musayyab. He said to a black man: Do not be sad because you are black, for three of the best people were blacks: Bilal, Mahja’, the freed slave of Umar, and Luqman. It was also said that he used to gather firewood every day for his master. He said to a man looking at him: If you see me with thick lips, then soft words come out of them, and if you see me black, then my heart is white. It was also said that he was a shepherd, and a man who knew him before saw him and said to him: Are you not the slave of so-and-so? He said: Yes. He said: What has brought you to this point? He said: The decree of God, fulfilling trusts, speaking the truth, and leaving what does not concern me. Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Jabir said. Khalid Al-Rubai’i said: He was a carpenter, and his master said to him: Slaughter a sheep for me and bring me the tastiest two morsels of it. So he brought him the tongue and the heart, and the master said to him: Was there nothing in it tastier than these? He remained silent, then he ordered him to slaughter another sheep and said to him: Throw away the two most vile morsels. So he threw away the tongue and the heart. Then he said to him: I ordered you to bring me the two most delicious morsels and you brought me the tongue and the heart. And I ordered you to throw away the two most vile morsels and you threw away the tongue and the heart?! He said to him: There is nothing better than these two when they are good, and nothing worse than these two when they are bad. I said: This meaning is transmitted in more than one hadith, including the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): “Beware, indeed in the body there is a morsel of flesh which, if it is sound, the entire body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the entire body is corrupt. Beware, it is the heart.” Many authentic and famous narrations were reported in Al-Lisan, including his saying (peace be upon him): “Whoever God protects from the evil of two things will enter Paradise: what is between his jaws and his legs…” The hadith. Luqman has many well-known sayings, this is one of them. He was asked: Who is the worst of people? He said: The one who does not care if people see him doing wrong. I said: This also has a meaning that is elevated. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “All of my nation will be forgiven except those who commit their sins openly. Among the sins committed openly is for a man to do something at night and then in the morning, although God has concealed him, he says, ‘O so-and-so, I did such-and-such last night,’ although his Lord had concealed him all night. In the morning, he uncovers what God had concealed from him.” Abu Hurairah narrated it and Bukhari recorded it. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: I have read some of Luqman’s wisdom that is more valuable than ten thousand chapters. It was narrated that he entered upon David (peace be upon him) while he was stringing together his armor, and God had softened iron for him like clay. He wanted to ask him, but wisdom overcame him and he remained silent. When he finished it, he put it on and said, You are an excellent garment of war. David said, Silence is wisdom, but few do it. David said to him, By right, you are called wise. God the Almighty’s statement: That I should be grateful to God has two interpretations: One of them is that an has the meaning of which explaining it, i.e., we said to him, Be grateful. The other interpretation is that it is in the accusative case and the verb is included in its relative clause, as Sibawayh reported: I wrote to him to get up, but he finds this interpretation far-fetched. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is, And We gave Luqman wisdom to be grateful to God the Almighty. It was also said: That I should be grateful to God the Almighty, so he was grateful, and thus he was wise in his gratitude to us. Gratitude to God means obeying Him in what He has commanded. The linguistic reality and meaning of Surat Al-Baqarah and other verses have already been discussed. And whoever is grateful is grateful only for himself, i.e., whoever obeys God the Almighty does what he does for himself, because the benefit of the reward returns to him. And whoever is ungrateful, i.e., is ungrateful to the blessings and does not believe in the Oneness of God, then indeed, God is Free of need of His creation, Praiseworthy before creation, i.e., praised. Yahya ibn Salam said: He is free of need of His creation, Praiseworthy in His actions.
31:13: God Almighty said: And when Luqman said to his son while he was advising him, Al-Suhayli said: His son's name was Tharan, according to Al-Tabari and Al-Qutbi. Al-Kalbi said: Mishkam. It was also said: An'am, as narrated by Al-Naqqash. Al-Qushayri mentioned that his son and wife were disbelievers, and he continued advising them until they converted to Islam. I said: This is indicated by His statement: “Do not associate anything with God. Indeed, association is a great wrong.” In Sahih Muslim and elsewhere on the authority of Abdullah, he said: When the verse Those who have believed and do not mix their belief with injustice (al-An’am 6:82) was revealed, it was difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and they said: Who among us does not wrong himself? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: It is not as you think. Rather, it is as Luqman said to his son: O my son, do not associate anything with God. Indeed, association is a great wrong.” There is a difference of opinion regarding His statement: Indeed, association is a great wrong. Some say that it is from the words of Luqman. It was said: It is a statement from God, the Most High, disconnected from Luqman’s speech, connected to it to confirm the meaning. This is supported by the well-known hadith that when the verse: Those who have believed and not mixed their belief with injustice was revealed, the companions of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, were afraid and said: Who among us has not committed injustice? Then God, the Most High, revealed: Indeed, associating others with God is a great wrong, and their fear was calmed. Their fear is only calmed by it being a statement from God, the Most High. Fear may also be calmed by God mentioning that about a servant whom He has described as wise and right. When is in the accusative case meaning remember. Al-Zajjaj said in his book on the Qur’an: When is in the accusative case with We gave and the meaning is: We had certainly given Luqman wisdom when he said. An-Nahhas said: I think it is a mistake, because there is a waw in the speech that prevents that. He said: O my son, with a kasra on the yaa, because it indicates the deleted yaa, and whoever opens it with a fatha, because in his opinion, the fatha is light. This has been discussed previously in Hud. His saying: O my son is not a true diminutive, even though it is pronounced as such. Rather, it is a softening, just as one says to a man: O my brother, and to a boy: It is good.
31:14: It contains eight issues: First: The Almighty's saying: And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents These two verses are an interjection during Luqman's advice. It was said that this is among what Luqman enjoined upon his son, and God informed him of it, meaning that Luqman said to his son: Do not associate partners with God and do not obey your parents in associating partners with God, for God enjoined upon them in obeying them in a way that does not constitute polytheism or disobedience to God Almighty. It was also said that it was: And when Luqman said to his son, And We said to Luqman regarding what We gave him of wisdom, and We enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, meaning We said to him, Thank God, and We said to him, And We enjoined upon man. It was also said that it was: And when Luqman said to his son, Do not associate partners with God, and We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, good treatment, and We have commanded people to do this, and Luqman commanded his son to do this. Al-Qushayri mentioned these sayings. The correct view is that these two verses were revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, as mentioned previously in Al-'Ankaboot, and the majority of commentators agree with this. The gist of this chapter is that obeying parents is not required in committing a major sin or in neglecting an individual obligation. Obedience to them is obligatory in what is permissible. It is preferable to recommend something in neglecting acts of obedience, such as the command to fight collectively, and answering one’s mother in prayer when it is possible to repeat it. This is stronger than recommending something, but it may be explained by fear of her death or similar things that permit interrupting the prayer, so it is not stronger than recommending something. Al-Hasan disagreed with this detail and said: If his mother gives him pleasure from attending the Isha prayer out of compassion, then he should not obey her. Second: Since God, the Most High, singled out the mother with the degree of mention of pregnancy and the degree of mention of breastfeeding, she obtained three ranks, and the father obtained one. Similar to that is the statement of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, when a man said to him: Whom should I be dutiful to? He said: Your mother. He said: Then who? He said: Your mother. He said: Then who? He said: Your father. So He gave him a quarter of the dutifulness, as in this verse. All of this has already been mentioned in Subhan. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And here, with weakness, meaning she carried him in her womb, and she became weaker every day. It was said: A woman is weak in creation, then pregnancy weakens her. Isa Al-Thaqafi read: And here, with weakness, with the ha’ open in both. It was narrated on the authority of Abu Amr. And here has one meaning. Qanab bin Umm Sahib said: Is there anyone who can stop the critics and admonish them? Indeed, the critics have weakness and weakness in them. It is said: wahan yahen, wahan yuhaan, wahan yahen, like waram yarm. Wahanan is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, as mentioned by Al-Qushayri. An-Nahhas: on the second object by dropping the preposition, meaning I carried it weakly upon weakly. The majority read: wa weasaluh, and Al-Hasan and Yaqoub read: wa fadluhu, and they are two dialects, meaning his weaning is at the end of two years, and what is meant by weaning is weaning, so it was expressed by its goal and end. It is said: he separated from such-and-such and was distinguished, and the young camel is named after it. Fourth: People agree that the period of breastfeeding is two years in the chapter on rulings and expenses. As for the prohibition of milk, a group set it at one year, no more and no less. A group said: If a boy is weaned before the age of two and stops drinking milk, then whatever he drinks after that within the two years is not prohibited. This has been fully discussed in Surah Al-Baqarah. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: that you be grateful to Me. “An” is in the accusative case according to Al-Zajjaj, and the meaning is: And We have enjoined upon man, concerning his parents, to be grateful to Me. An-Nahhas said: It is better to have An as an explanatory particle, and the meaning is: We told him to be grateful to Me and to your parents. It has been said: Thanks are to God for the blessing of faith, and to the parents for the blessing of upbringing. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: Whoever prays the five daily prayers has thanked God Almighty, and whoever supplicates for his parents after the prayers has thanked them.
31:15: Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: “But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.” We have explained that this verse and the one before it were revealed concerning Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas when he converted to Islam, and that his mother, Hamna bint Abi Sufyan ibn Umayya, swore that she would not eat, as mentioned in the verse before it. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And accompany them in this world with appropriate kindness. This is an adjective for a deleted source, meaning, accompany them with appropriate kindness. It is said, accompany them with appropriate kindness. And accompany them with appropriate kindness means what is appropriate. The verse is evidence of maintaining ties with unbelieving parents as much as possible if they are poor, and speaking gently and calling them to Islam. Asma bint Abi Bakr Al-Siddiq said to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) when her maternal aunt, or according to some reports, her foster mother, had come to her. She said: “O Messenger of God, my mother has come to me and she is eager to maintain ties with her. Should I maintain ties with her?” He said: Yes, and she is eager to support her. It was also said that this means about Islam. Ibn Atiyyah said: It appears to me that she was eager to maintain ties with her, and she would not have approached Asma had it not been for her need. Asma’s mother is Qutaylah bint Abd Al-Uzza ibn Abd Asad. Aisha and Abd Al-Rahman’s mother is Umm Ruman, who embraced Islam early on. Eighth: The Almighty’s saying: And follow the way of him who turns back to Me is a command to the entire world, as if he were the one commanded. To turn back means to incline or return to something, and this is the way of the prophets and the righteous. Al-Naqqash narrated that the one commanded was Sa’d, and the one who turned back was Abu Bakr. He said: When Abu Bakr converted to Islam, Sa’d, Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf, Uthman, Talhah, Sa’id and Az-Zubair came to him and said: Have you believed? He said: Yes. So this verse was revealed: Is one who is devoutly obedient during periods of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord? Az-Zumar 39:9. When the Sunnis heard it, they believed, so God the Almighty revealed about them: And those who avoid false deities, lest they worship them and turn back to God - for them are good tidings. Az-Zumar 39:17-18. It was said that the one who turned back was the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Abbas said: When Sa’d converted to Islam, his brothers Amir and Uwaymir converted with him, and no polytheist remained from them except Utbah. Then God Almighty promised to resurrect those in the graves and return to Him for recompense and to be held accountable for their small and great deeds.
31:16: God Almighty says: “O my son, if it be the weight of a mustard seed and be within a rock or within the heavens or within the earth, God will bring it forth. Indeed, God is Subtle and Acquainted.” Meaning: Luqman said to his son, O my son! This statement of Luqman was intended to inform his son of the extent of God's power. This was the goal that he was able to understand, because it is said that the mustard seed cannot be weighed by the senses, as it cannot be weighed in a scale. That is, if a person had a provision the weight of a mustard seed in these situations, God would bring it so that He may direct it to the One for whom it is provided. That is, do not worry about provision until you are preoccupied with it and neglect performing your duties or following the path of one who turns to Me. I said: And from this meaning is the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to Abdullah ibn Masoud: Do not worry too much about what is destined to happen and what you are provided for will come to you. This verse speaks volumes about the fact that God, the Most High, has encompassed all things in knowledge and has counted all things, glory be to Him, He has no partner. It was narrated that Luqman’s son asked his father about a seed that falls to the bottom of the sea, does God know about it? So Luqman responded to him with this verse. It was said: The meaning is that he meant deeds, sins and acts of obedience, that is, whether a good deed or a sin is like a seed that God brings, that is, it does not provide for the person who is destined to receive it. In this sense, the sermon conveys hope and intimidation. This is in addition to the clarification of God Almighty. The first statement does not contain any hope or fear. God the Almighty said: The weight of a grain is an expression that is suitable for jewels, meaning the size of a grain, and it is also suitable for deeds, meaning what weighs similarly the size of a grain. What supports the view of those who say that it is from jewels is the reading of Abdul Karim Al-Jazari: fatakun with a kasra on the kaf and a shaddah on the noon, and from kan which means something covered. The majority of the reciters read: in takun with a taa above mithqal in the accusative as the predicate of kana, and its subject is implied and its meaning is: your question, according to what was narrated, or disobedience and obedience according to the second opinion, and the correctness of it is indicated by the statement of Luqman’s son to his father: O my father, if I commit a sin where no one can see me, how will God know about it? Luqman said to him: O my son, if it is the weight of a mustard seed, it will be in a rock, the verse. His son continued to tremble until he died, as Muqatil said, and the pronoun in it is the pronoun of the story, like you say: it is Hind coming, meaning the story is that if it is the weight of a grain. The Basrans allow: it is Zaid, I struck him, meaning the story is. The Kufians do not permit this except in the feminine, as we mentioned. Nafi’ read: mithqal in the nominative case. Based on this, tak goes back to the meaning of mustard, meaning if tak is a mustard seed. It was said: A verb was attributed to mithqal that has a feminine marker since it was added to a feminine word from which it is derived, because the mithqal of a mustard seed is either bad or good, as He said: Then for him is ten times the like thereof (al-An’am 6:160). So he made it feminine even though the mithqal is masculine, because he meant good deeds. This is like the saying of the poet: Walking as the spears shook, their tops were blown away by the breezes And tak here means it happens so do not make it a report. God the Almighty says: Then it will be in a rock. It has been said that the meaning of this statement is exaggeration and completion of understanding, meaning that His Almighty power encompasses what is in the folds of a rock, what is in the folds of a rock, and what is in the heavens and the earth. Ibn Abbas said: The rock is under the seven earths and the earth is above it. It has also been said that it is the rock on the back of the whale. Al-Suddi said: It is a rock in the heavens and the earth, rather it is behind seven earths over which an angel is established, because He said: Or in the heavens or on the earth. Both of them suffice and there is no need for His saying: Then it will be in a rock for emphasis, like His saying: Read in the name of your Lord who created * Created man from a clinging substance (al-Alaq 96:1-2), and His saying: Glory be to Him who took His Servant by night (al-Isra’ 17:1).
31:17: There are three issues: First: The Almighty's statement: O my son, establish prayer. He advised his son to perform the greatest acts of obedience, which are prayer, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong. He only wants this after he has implemented that in himself and is deterred from doing wrong. Here are the acts of obedience and virtues combined. And he did well who said: Start with yourself and stop it from doing wrong. If it stops doing wrong, then you are wise. In the verses mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. Second: The statement of God the Almighty: And be patient over what befalls you requires changing the evil even if it causes you harm. It is a notification that the one changing it will sometimes be harmed, and this amount is by way of encouragement and strength in the essence of God. However, it is not by way of obligation. We have already discussed this in detail in Surah Al Imran and Surah Al Ma'idah. It has also been said that He commanded him to be patient over the hardships of this world, such as illnesses and others, and not to turn from impatience to disobeying God the Almighty. This is a good statement because it is general. God the Almighty says: Indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination. Ibn Abbas said: The true meaning of faith is patience in the face of hardships. It was also said that establishing prayer, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong are among the matters worthy of determination, i.e., among the matters that God has determined and commanded. Ibn Jurayj said: It is possible that he meant that this is among the noble morals and the determination of the resolute people who tread the path of salvation. Ibn Jurayj’s statement is more correct.
31:18: God Almighty says: “And do not turn your cheek away from people and do not walk through the earth exultantly. Indeed, God does not like everyone self-deluded and boastful.” There are three issues: First: Nafi`, Abu `Amr, Hamza, Al-Kisa`i and Ibn Muhaisin read: tas`a`ar with an alif after the sad. Ibn Kathir, `Asim, Ibn `Amir, Al-Hasan and Mujahid read: tas`a`ar. Al-Jahdary read: tas`a`ar with a sukoon on the sad, and the meanings are close. `Sa`r means inclination, and from it is the saying of the Bedouin: And time has established `A`ra, after I established its `A`ra. And from it is the saying of `Umar ibn Hani Al-Taghlabi: And when the tyrant turned his cheek, We would raise him from his slant, and he would stand up. Al-Tabari recited: Then stand up. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is a mistake, because the rhyme of the poem is lowered. In another verse: We stood up for him from his trembling cheek. Al-Harawi said: “Do not turn away from them, meaning do not turn away from them out of arrogance. It is said: A camel has been afflicted with a disease that twists its neck. Then it is said to the arrogant person: He has a turn away and is sick. So the meaning of: Do not turn away is: Do not keep your cheek turned away.” In the hadith: A time will come upon the people when there will be none among them but the arrogant or the cripple. The one who turns away with a face out of arrogance, and he meant the increase of people who have no religion. In the hadith: Everyone who turns away is cursed, meaning everyone who has pomp and arrogance. Second: The meaning of the verse: And do not turn your cheek toward people out of arrogance, admiration, or contempt for them. This is the interpretation of Ibn Abbas and a group. It was also said: It is to turn your jaw when someone is mentioned in your presence as if you despise him. So the meaning is: Turn toward them humbly, friendly, and relaxed. And if the youngest of them speaks to you, listen to him until he completes his story. And the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to do the same. I said: And from this meaning is what Malik narrated from Ibn Shihab from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not hate one another, do not turn your backs on one another, and do not envy one another. O servants of God, be brothers. It is not permissible for a Muslim to abandon his brother for more than three days.” Turning away from one another means ignoring and refraining from speaking, greeting, and the like. Turning away is called turning away because if you hate someone, you turn away from him and turn your back on him, and this is what he will do to you. If you love someone, you turn your face toward him and face him to please him and for him to please you. So the meaning of turning away from one’s face is found in the one who turns his cheek, and Mujahid interpreted the verse in this way. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad said: His statement, And do not turn your cheek to people is as if he forbade a person from humiliating himself unnecessarily. Similarly, it was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A person should not humiliate himself. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And do not walk on the earth exultantly, meaning swaggering and arrogant. A verbal noun in the accusative case, and it has already been mentioned in Subhan. It is activity and walking happily without being busy or in need. The people of this character are always proud and arrogant, so the arrogant person walks swagger. Yahya bin Jaber Al-Ta’i narrated on the authority of Ibn A’id Al-Azdi on the authority of Udayf bin Al-Harith who said: I came to Jerusalem with Abdullah bin Ubayd bin Umair. He said: We sat with Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-As and I heard him say: The grave speaks to the servant when he is placed in it and says: O son of Adam, what has deceived you about Me? Didn’t you know that I am the House of Solitude? Didn’t you know that I am the House of Darkness? Didn’t you know that I am the House of Truth? O son of Adam, has I deceived you? You used to walk around Me in a haughty manner. Ibn A’id said: I said to Ghudayf: What is fadad, O Abu Asma’? He said: Like some of your walk, O son of my brother, sometimes. Abu Ubayd said: The meaning is: This is arrogant. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever trails his garment out of arrogance, God will not look at him on the Day of Resurrection. The boastful is the one who enumerates what he has been given without frowning at God Almighty, as stated by Mujahid. This expression also includes boasting about lineage and other things.
31:19: God Almighty says: “And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice. Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the braying of donkeys.” There are six issues in it: The first: The Almighty’s statement: And be moderate in your pace. When He forbade him from reprehensible behavior, He revealed to him the noble behavior that he should have, so He said: And be moderate in your pace, meaning, be moderate in it. Moderation is between haste and slowness, meaning, do not crawl like someone who is dying, nor jump like a clever person. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Walking quickly takes away the glory of the believer. As for what was narrated from him (peace be upon him) that he would hurry when he walked, and Aisha’s statement about Omar may God be pleased with them both: When he walked, he would hurry, she meant speed that is higher than the crawling of someone who is dying, and God knows best. God the Almighty has praised those with this characteristic, as explained previously in Al-Furqan. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And lower your voice meaning do not force yourself to raise your voice and only take what you need from it, because raising your voice louder than necessary is a force that is harmful. The meaning of all of this is humility. Omar said to a muezzin who forced himself to raise the call to prayer more than he could bear: I was afraid that your apron might burst! The muezzin was Abu Mahdhura Samurah ibn Mu’ayr. The apron is the area between the navel and the pubis. Third: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the braying of donkeys. Meaning, the ugliest and most monstrous of them. From this, he came to us with an unpleasant face. The donkey is an example of strong criticism and insult, as is its braying. Among their vulgarity when mentioning it alone is that they avoid it and refrain from mentioning it explicitly, so they say: the one with the long ears, as it is a euphemism for disgusting things. It is considered among the bad manners to mention a donkey in the company of honorable people. There are those among the Arabs who do not ride a donkey out of disdain, even if it is very manly. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to ride it out of humility and submission to God Almighty. Fourth: The verse provides evidence that the ugliness of raising one's voice when addressing or arguing is due to the ugliness of the voices of donkeys, because they are loud. In the Sahih, it is narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If you hear the braying of donkeys, then seek refuge in God from Satan, for they have seen a devil. It has also been narrated that no donkey brays or dog barks unless it sees a devil. Sufyan al-Thawri said: The braying of everything is glorification of God except the braying of donkeys. Ata’ said: The braying of donkeys is a supplication against the oppressors. Fifth: This verse is an admonition from God Almighty to refrain from shouting in people’s faces out of contempt for them, or to refrain from shouting altogether. The Arabs used to take pride in their loud voices and other things, so whoever had a louder voice was more honorable, and whoever had a lower voice was more humiliated, until their poet said: Loud speech, loud sneezing, loud breathing, loud blessings He runs after the lion, and men are superior to him in his general character. God Almighty forbade this pre-Islamic behavior by saying: The most disagreeable of sounds is the braying of donkeys. That is, if anything were to be feared for its sound, it would be the donkey. He made them equal in this example. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: The sound of donkeys. The lām is for emphasis. The word sawt is singular even though it is added to the group because it is a verbal noun and the verbal noun indicates abundance. It is the verbal noun of sāt to make a sound, which means to make a sound, so it is a voice. It is also said: He made a sound tasawwātuan, so he is a voiceless person. A man with a loud voice means someone with a loud voice, like their saying: a man with wealth and attainment, meaning a man with much wealth and giving.
31:20: God Almighty says: Have you not seen that God has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth?
31:21: The Almighty says: Have you not seen that God has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth? He mentions His blessings upon the children of Adam, and that He has subjected to them whatever is in the heavens, such as the sun, moon, stars, and angels who protect them and bring them benefits, and whatever is on the earth, including mountains, trees, fruits, and countless others. And has bestowed His favors upon you means He has completed and perfected them. Ibn Abbas and Yahya ibn Ammarah read: and Asbagh with a sad instead of a seen, because the letters of emphasis attract the seen from its lower part to its upper part, returning it to a sad. And blessings: with a ni'mah like Sidrat and Sidr with a fat-ha on the dall, and this is the reading of Nafi', Abu Amr, and Hafs. The rest read: ni'mah in the singular, and the singular indicates abundance, like the Almighty's saying: And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them (Ibrahim 14:34). This is the reading of Ibn Abbas from several authentic sources. It was said that its meaning is Islam. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Ibn Abbas when he asked him about this verse: The outward meaning is Islam and your good character, and the inward meaning is what He has concealed from you of your evil deeds. An-Nahhas explained this by saying that Saeed ibn Jubayr said about God’s statement, “He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may (al-Ma’idah 5:6),” that He said: He will admit you into Paradise. The completion of God’s favor upon a servant is that He admits him into Paradise. Thus, since Islam leads to Paradise, it is called a favor. It was also said that the outward meaning is health and perfect character, and the inward meaning is knowledge and reason. Al-Muhasibi said: The outward meaning is the blessings of this world, and the inward meaning is the blessings of the Hereafter. It was also said that the outward meaning is what is seen with the eyes of wealth, status, beauty among people, and the success of acts of obedience, while the inward meaning is what a person finds within himself of knowledge of God, good faith, and what God, the Most High, wards off from the servant of calamities. Al-Mawardi listed nine sayings on this subject, all of which go back to this. God the Almighty said: And of mankind is he who disputes about God without knowledge. Its meaning was previously mentioned in Al-Hajj and elsewhere. It was revealed about a Jew who came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Muhammad, tell me about your Lord, what is He made of? Then a thunderbolt came and took him, as Mujahid said. This thunder has already passed. It was also said that it was revealed about Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, just as he says: The angels are daughters of God, as Ibn Abbas said. He disputes he argues without knowledge meaning without proof nor guidance nor an illuminating Book meaning clear light, except for Satan and what he conveys to them. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you Al-An’am 6:121. Otherwise, it is the imitation of ancestors as in the verse after. Or if Satan were to invite them to the punishment of the Blaze, they would follow him.
31:22: The Almighty says: And whoever submits his face to God meaning, whoever devotes his worship and intention to God Almighty. And he is a doer of good because worship without ihsan or knowledge of the heart is of no benefit. Similar to this is the verse: And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer (Ta-Ha: 112). In the hadith of Gabriel, peace be upon him, he said: So tell me about ihsan? He said: It is to worship God as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then He sees you. He has grasped the most trustworthy handhold (al-Baqarah 2:2). Ibn Abbas said: There is no god but God, and this has already been mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah. Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, As-Sulami, and Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Yasar recited: And whoever submits. An-Nahhas: And in this I know that he submits, as God Almighty said: Say, ‘I have submitted my face to God’ (Al Imran 3:20). The meaning is: I have submitted my face to God. I have devoted my worship to God Almighty. And many people use I submit, except that what is used in I submitted means I paid. It is said: I submitted in wheat, and it may also be said: I submitted. Az-Zamakhshari said: Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him read: And whoever submits with the emphasis. It is said: I submit your affair and I submit your affair to God Almighty. If you say: Why is it transitive with lam in God Almighty’s saying: Yes, whoever submits his face to God (al-Baqarah 2:112)? I say: Its meaning with lam is that he made his face, which is his self and his soul, safe for God, meaning purely for Him. And its meaning with to refers to that he submitted himself to Him, just as one submits goods to a man if he hands them over to him. What is meant is to put one’s trust in Him and entrust Him with it. And to God is the outcome of all matters, meaning their fate.
31:23: God Almighty says: “And whoever disbelieves - let not his disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did.” That is, We will reward them. Indeed, God is Knowing of that within the breasts.
31:24: We grant them enjoyment for a little meaning, We keep them in this world for a short period of time during which they can enjoy themselves. Then We compel them meaning, We force them and drive them. To a severe punishment which is the punishment of Hell. The word man is used for both singular and plural, which is why He said: His disbelief. Then He said: Their return. What follows is in accordance with the meaning.
31:25: God Almighty says: And if you ask them, ‘Who created the heavens and the earth?’ they will surely say, ‘God.’ That is, they acknowledge that God is their Creator, so they do not worship anyone other than Him. Say, ‘Praise be to God.’ That is, for the religion to which He has guided us, and praise belongs only to Him. But most of them do not know. That is, they do not consider or reflect.
31:26: To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, meaning both dominion and creation. Indeed, God is the Free of need, meaning He is independent of His creation and their worship. He only commanded them to benefit them. The Praiseworthy, meaning He is praised for His creation.
31:27: When he argued with the polytheists with what he argued, he made clear that the meanings of His speech, glory be to Him, are inexhaustible and endless. Al-Qaffal said: When he mentioned that He subjected to them whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and that He bestowed blessings, he pointed out that if the trees were pens and the seas were ink with which He wrote the wonders of God's creation, indicating His power and oneness, those wonders would not be exhausted. Al-Qushayri said: The meaning of those words is attributed to the predestined, and it is more appropriate to interpret the verse as referring to the eternal speech. The created must have an end, so if it is negated from His predestined things, then it is negating the end from what is capable of being created in the impossible. As for what existence has limited and enumerated, it must have a finiteness, and the eternal is truly endless. We discussed the meaning of God's words at the end of Al-Kahf. Abu Ali said: What is meant by words, and God knows best, is what is in the predestined, not what came out of it into existence. This is something like what Al-Qaffal said. The purpose is to inform people of the multitude of meanings of the Words of God, which are in themselves infinite. The matter was made easy for human understanding by what is finite because it is the greatest amount known to mankind, not that it can be penetrated by more than these pens and seas. The meaning of the revelation of the verse indicates that what is meant by the Words is the ancient speech. Ibn Abbas said: The reason for this verse is that the Jews said: O Muhammad, how can we mean by this statement And of knowledge you have been given only a little Al-Isra’ 17:85 while we have been given the Torah in which is the speech of God and His rulings, and you believe that it explains everything? So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: The Torah is a little of a lot, and this verse was revealed. The verse is Medinan. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: It has become clear that the words here mean knowledge and the realities of things, because He, the Almighty, knew before He created what He would create in the heavens and the earth of every thing, and He knew what was in it of the weight of an atom, and He knew all the species and what they are made of hair and limb, and what leaf is in the tree, and what kinds of creation are in it, and what kinds of taste and color it disposes of. So if He had named every creature separately, and named its parts according to what He knew of its little and much and what conditions it changed to, and what increased in it in each age, and had explained every tree separately and what it branched out to, and had estimated what dries of that in each age, then He wrote the explanation of each one of them according to what God, the Most High, has encompassed of it, and then the sea was ink for that explanation that God, the Blessed and Exalted, explained about those things, and seven seas added to it after it, the explanation of those things would have been more. I said: This is the meaning of Al-Qaffal’s statement, and it is a good statement, God willing. Some people said: The Quraysh said: This speech of Muhammad will be completed and then end, so this verse was revealed. Al-Suddi said: The Quraysh said: How much Muhammad speaks! So this verse was revealed. God the Almighty says: And the sea replenishes it. The majority of scholars read it in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is in the clause after it, and the clause is in the position of a circumstantial, as if he said: And the sea is in this state, as Sibawayh estimated it. Some grammarians said: It is in apposition to an because it is in the position of a subject in apposition. Abu Amr and Ibn Ishaq read: The sea in the accusative case as a apposition to ma, which is the noun of an. It was also said: That is, even if the sea replenishes it, meaning it increases it. Ibn Hormuz and Al-Hasan read: Yumduhu, from amada. A group said: This means extending one thing over another, as you say: the Nile extended the gulf, meaning it increased it. And extending something is something that is not part of it. This has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah and Surat Al-Imran. Ja'far ibn Muhammad read: And the sea is its ink. The Words of God will not be exhausted has already been mentioned. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise has also been mentioned. Abu Ubaid said: The sea here is the fresh water that produces pens, but salt water does not produce pens.
31:28: The Almighty says: He created you and resurrected you only as a single soul. Ad-Dahhak said: The meaning is that the beginning of your creation is only as the creation of a single soul, and your resurrection on the Day of Resurrection is only as the resurrection of a single soul. An-Nahhas said: The grammarians understood it this way, meaning except as the creation of a single soul, like: And ask the township (Yusuf 12:82). Mujahid said: Because He says to the little and the many, Be, and it is. The verse was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Abu al-Asadain, Munabbih, and Nabih, the sons of al-Hajjaj ibn al-Sabbaq. They said to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "God created us in stages: a drop, then a clot, then a lump of flesh, then bones. Then He says, 'We will raise up a new creation all in one hour!'" So God revealed: He created you and resurrected you only as a single soul, because what is difficult for His servants is not difficult for God, and His creation of the world is like His creation of a single soul. Indeed, God is Hearing of what they say, Seeing of what they do.
31:29: The Almighty says: Have you not seen that God merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night? This was mentioned in Al-Hajj and Al-Imran. And He has subjected the sun and the moon. That is, He subdued them by rising and setting, determining the terms of life and completing benefits. Each runs to a specified term. Al-Hasan said: Until the Day of Resurrection. Qatada said: Until its time in its rising and setting, neither exceeding it nor falling short of it. And that God, of what you do, is Acquainted. That is, whoever has power over these things must be All-Knowing of them, and the One who knows them is All-Knowing of your deeds. The common reading of the verse is you know with the ta' as an address. Al-Sulami, Nasr ibn Asim, and Al-Duri, on the authority of Abu Amr, read it with the ya' as a statement.
31:30: That means God Almighty did that so that you would learn and acknowledge that God is the Truth and that what they invoke besides Him is falsehood meaning Satan, as stated by Mujahid. It was also said: what they associated with God Almighty of idols and statues. And that God is the Most High, the Grand High in His status, Great in His authority.
31:31: The Almighty says: Have you not seen that the ark meaning the ships sails in the place of the predicate. through the sea by the grace of God meaning His kindness to you and His mercy to you in your deliverance from it. Hormuz read: by the graces of God, plural of grace, which is the plural of safety. The original was to move the 'ayn but it was made quiescent. that He may show you some of His signs from the particle for the particle, meaning that He may show you the sailing of the ships, said Yahya ibn Salam. Ibn Shajarah said: Among His signs is what you witness of God's power in it. Al-Naqqash: what God provides them from it. Al-Hasan said: The key to the seas is the ships, the key to the earth is the roads, and the key to the heaven is supplication. Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful meaning patient with His judgment and grateful for His blessings. The scholars of semantics said: He intended this characteristic for every believer, because patience and gratitude are among the best characteristics of faith. The sign is the mark, and the mark is not evident in the heart of every believer, it is only evident for the one who is patient in the face of affliction and grateful in prosperity. Al-Sha’bi said: Patience is half of faith, gratitude is half of faith, and certainty is all of faith. Have you not seen the words of God Almighty: Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful and His words: And on the earth are signs for those of certainty (al-Dhariyat 51:20). And he, peace be upon him, said: “Faith is two halves: half patience and half gratitude.”
31:32: The Almighty said: And when waves cover them like canopies. Muqatil said: Like mountains. Al-Kalbi said: Like clouds. Qatada said: The plural of canopy, likening waves to it due to their size and height. Al-Nabigha said in describing a sea: Green, with shades on its edges, like the splitting of the jugs. The wave, which is singular, is likened to a shadow, which is plural, because waves come one after another and overlap each other like shadows. It has also been said that it has the meaning of plural, but it is not pluralized because it is a verbal noun. Its origin is from movement and crowding, from which: the sea surged, and people surged. Kaab said: Then we came to a sea in the middle of which were Abyssinians, some of them bareheaded and some masked. Muhammad ibn al-Hanifah read: waves like shadows plural of shadow. Call upon God, making religion sincere to Him monotheistic to Him, calling upon none but Him for their salvation, and this has been mentioned before. Then when He delivered them means from the sea. to the land, then among them was he who was moderate Ibn Abbas said: Fulfilling what he pledged to God at sea. Al-Naqqash: meaning he was just in his pledge, and he fulfilled on land what he pledged to God at sea. Al-Hasan said: A moderate person is a believer who adheres to monotheism and obedience. Mujahid said: A goal in the statement is implied for disbelief. It was said: There is an omission in the speech, and the meaning is: Among them is he who is moderate and among them is a disbeliever. The omission is indicated by the statement of God the Almighty: And none rejects Our verses except every treacherous, ungrateful person Al-Khattar means the traitor. And Al-Khattar is the worst form of treachery. Amr ibn Ma’dikarib said: If you saw Abu Umair, you would fill your hands with treachery and deceit. Al-A'sha said: Al-Bablaq is a unique man from Tayma, whose home is a strong fortress and whose neighbor is not a traitor. Al-Jawhari said: Khatar is treachery. It is said: he betrayed him, so he is khatar. Al-Mawardi: It is the opinion of the majority. Atiyah said: It is the denier. It is said: he khtar, yakhtar, and ikhtar with the damma and kasra, khataran, mentioned by Al-Qushayri. Denying the verses means denying their essence. And denying the verses means denying their evidence.
31:33: God the Almighty says: O mankind, fear your Lord meaning the disbeliever and the believer, that is, fear Him and declare Him alone. And fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all. The meaning of will avail was previously mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah and elsewhere. If it is said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever has three sons who die before they reach puberty, the Fire will not touch him except to fulfill his oath. And he said: Whoever is tested with any of these daughters and treats them kindly, they will be a shield for him from the Fire. It was said to him: The meaning of this verse is that a father will not bear the sin of his son, nor will a child bear the sin of his father, nor will one be held accountable for the other. The meaning of the hadiths is that the reward for patience in the face of death and kindness to daughters shields the servant from the Fire, and the son will precede him to Paradise. Indeed, the promise of God is truth meaning the Resurrection. So let not the life of this world deceive you meaning let not the Deceiver delude you with its adornments and what it calls for, so that you rely on it and rely on it and abandon working for the Hereafter. And let not the Deceiver deceive you about God. The common reading here and in Surat Al-Mala’ikah and Surat Al-Hadid is with a fat-ha on the ghain. Mujahid and others say that it refers to Satan, who deceives people and gives them false hope in this world and distracts them from the Hereafter. In Surat An-Nisa’ it says: He promises them and gives them false hope (An-Nisa’: 120). Simak ibn Harb, Abu Haywah and Ibn As-Sumaiq’ read it with a damma on the ghain, meaning do not be deceived. It is as if it is the source of gharra yaghir ghururan. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: It means to commit a sin while hoping for forgiveness.
31:34: Al-Farra' claimed that this is the meaning of negation, i.e. no one knows it except God. Abu Ja'far Al-Nahhas said: It came to have both a negative and an affirmative meaning because the Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) informed him of that, because he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in his interpretation of the verse: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him (Al-An'am: 59): It is this. I said: We have mentioned in Surat Al-An'am the hadith of Ibn Umar in this, narrated by Al-Bukhari. And in the hadith of Gabriel (peace be upon him), he said: Tell me about the Hour? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The one being asked about it does not know more than the one asking. There are five things that no one knows except God: God has knowledge of the Hour, sends down the rain, knows what is in the wombs, and no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow. He said: You have spoken the truth. Abu Dawud At-Tayalisi's wording. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: Everything that your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was given except five: God has knowledge of the Hour (Al-An'am: 59) to the end of the verse. Ibn Abbas said: These five are known only to God, and no close angel or sent prophet knows them. Whoever claims to know any of these has disbelieved in the Quran, because he has contradicted it. Moreover, the prophets know much of the unseen, as God has informed them of. The intention is to invalidate the existence of soothsayers, astrologers, and those who seek rain from the stars. Many things may be known through long experiences, such as the male or female nature of a pregnancy, and other things, as previously mentioned in Al-An'am. Experience may differ, custom may be broken, and knowledge remains with God alone. It was narrated that a Jew used to calculate the stars, so he said to Ibn Abbas: If you wish, I will tell you your son's star sign, and that he will die in ten days, but you will not die until you go blind, and I will not die a year before I die. He said: Then where will you die, O Jew? He said: I do not know. Ibn Abbas said: God has spoken the truth: And no soul knows in what land it will die. Ibn Abbas returned and found his son with a fever, and he died after ten days. The Jew died before the year had passed, and Ibn Abbas died blind. Ali ibn al-Husayn, the narrator of this hadith, said: This is the most amazing hadith. Muqatil said: This verse was revealed about a man from the desert named al-Warith ibn Amr ibn Haritha. He came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: My wife is pregnant, so tell me what she will give birth to. Our land is barren, so tell me when the rain will fall. I know when I will give birth, so tell me when I will die. I know what I know today, so tell me what I will do tomorrow, and tell me when the Hour will come. So God revealed this verse. This was mentioned by al-Qushayri and al-Mawardi. Abu al-Malih narrated on the authority of Abu ‘Uzza al-Hudhali that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: When God wishes to take the soul of a servant in a land, He makes him need it, and he does not cease until he arrives there. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour until His saying: In what land you will die. This was mentioned by al-Mawardi, and Ibn Majah narrated it with a similar meaning from the hadith of Ibn Mas’ud. We have already mentioned it in full in Kitab al-Tadhkira. The general reading of and descends is doubled. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa’i read it with a light pronunciation. Ubayy ibn Ka’b read: In which land do the rest of us reside? Al-Farra’ said: He was satisfied with the feminization of earth from the feminization of any. It was said: He meant by earth the place, so he mentioned it. The poet said: Neither rain nor its flour nor its flour nor its land that produces its vegetation. Al-Akhfash said: It is permissible to say I passed by a slave girl, meaning a female slave, or any slave girl. Sibawayh likened the feminization of any to the feminization of all in their saying: all of them. “Indeed, God is All-Knowing, All-Aware.” All-Aware is an adjective for All-Knowing or a predicate after a predicate. And God knows best.
32:1: The Almighty said: Alif, Lam, Meem.
32:2: It is a Meccan verse, except for three verses that were revealed in Medina, which are the verse in which God the Almighty says: Is he who is a believer like he who is a defiantly disobedient? This is a complete three verses, as stated by Al-Kalbi and Muqatil. Others said: Except for five verses, from the verse in which God the Almighty says: Their sides forsake each other - to the verse - that which you used to deny (al-Sajdah 32:16-20), and it is thirty verses. It was also said that it is twenty-nine. In the Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite in the Fajr prayer on al-Jumuah 62:"Alif, Lam, Meem. The revelation of" As-Sajdah, Has there not come over man a period of time? (As-Dahr: 1) Hadith. Ad-Darimi and Abu Muhammad narrated in his Musnad on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not sleep until he had recited: “Alif, Lam, Meem. The revelation of the Book” Al-Sajdah and Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion Al-Mulk:1. Ad-Darimi said: Abu Al-Mughira informed us, saying: Abda told us on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan who said: Recite the savior, which is “Alif, Lam, Meem. The revelation of the Book” Al-Mulk:1, for it has reached me that a man used to recite it and would not recite anything else, and he committed many sins. So it spread its wing over him and said: My Lord, forgive him, for he used to recite me often. So the Lord interceded for it on his behalf and said: Write for him a good deed for every sin and raise him a degree. God the Almighty says: (The verse:) (The verse:) '...
32:3: The Almighty says: Or do they say, 'He invented it?' This is the disconnected 'umm' which is estimated by 'bal' and the interrogative 'alif', meaning, 'Rather, do they say?' It indicates a shift from one hadith to another, for He, the Almighty, has confirmed that it is a revelation from the Lord of the Worlds, and that is something about which there is no doubt. Then He turns away from that to His saying: Or do they say, 'He invented it?' meaning, he fabricated it and made it up. Rather, it is the truth from your Lord. He denied their claim of fabrication. That you may warn a people Qatada said: meaning Quraysh, who were an illiterate nation to whom no warner came before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. That you may warn is related to what precedes it, so do not pause on who is your Lord. It is permissible for it to be related to something omitted, the estimate being: He sent it down so that you may warn a people, so it is permissible to pause on who is your Lord. What is in His saying: that which came to them is a negation. From a warner is a relative clause, and warner is in the nominative case, and it is the frightening teacher. It was said: What is meant by the people are the people of the period between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, as Ibn Abbas and Muqatil said. It was also said: The proof was established for God Almighty against them by warning the messengers who came before them, even if they had not seen a messenger. This meaning was previously mentioned.
32:4: The Almighty says: God is He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days. He made them aware of the perfection of His power so that they might listen to the Qur'an and reflect. The meaning of: created, originated and came into being after nothingness and after it had been nothing. in six days from Sunday to Friday. Al-Hasan said: of the days of this world. Ibn Abbas said: Today is one of the six days in which God created the heavens and the earth, the length of which is one thousand years of the years of this world. Ad-Dahhak said: in six thousand years, meaning in a period of six days of the days of the Hereafter. Then He established Himself on the Throne was mentioned previously in Al-A'raf, Al-Baqarah and other surahs. We have mentioned the scholars' views on this in full in Al-Kitab Al-Asna fi Sharh Asma God Al-Husna. Thamma is not for order, but rather it has the meaning of and. "You have besides Him neither protector nor intercessor." That is, the disbelievers have neither a protector nor an intercessor to protect them from their punishment. The nominative case is permissible in the place of "and. Then will you not remember?" regarding His power and His creations.
32:5: God the Almighty says: He directs the affair from the heaven to the earth. Ibn Abbas said: He sends down the decree and predestination. It was also said: The revelation descends with Gabriel. Omar bin Murrah narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Sabit who said: The affairs of this world are directed by four: Gabriel, Michael, the Angel of Death, and Israfil, may God's peace be upon them all. Gabriel is in charge of the winds and the armies. Michael is in charge of rain and water. The Angel of Death is in charge of taking the souls. Israfil descends with the affair. It has been said that the Throne is the seat of direction, just as what is below the Throne is the seat of detail. God the Almighty said: "Then He established Himself on the Throne and subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. He directs the affair and details the verses." (Ar-Ra'd: 2) What is below the heavens is the seat of control. God the Almighty said: And We have certainly distributed it among them that they may remember. (al-Furqan 25:50) God the Almighty says: Then it will ascend to Him. Yahya ibn Salam said: It is Gabriel who ascends to the heaven after descending with the revelation. Al-Naqqash: It is the angel who manages the affairs from heaven to earth. It was also said: It is the report of the people of the earth ascending to Him with its bearers from the angels, as said by Ibn Shajarah. On a Day the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count. It was also said: Then it will ascend to Him, meaning that affair and management will return to Him after the end of the world. On a Day the extent of which is a thousand years, which is the Day of Resurrection. According to the previous opinions, the writing in ascends is a metaphor for the angel, and it was not mentioned because it is understood from the meaning. It was explicitly stated in the words of a questioner: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him. Al-Ma'arij: 4 The pronoun in to Him refers to the sky, according to the language of those who mention it, or to the place of the angel to whom he returns, or to the name of God, the Most High, meaning the place where He established it. And if it returns to God, then it has returned to the sky, i.e., to the Lote Tree of the Limit, for to it ascends what ascends from the earth and from it descends what descends to it. The meaning of that is established in Sahih Muslim. The ha in muqaddima refers to management, and the meaning is: the length of that management was a thousand years of the years of the world, i.e. He decrees the affair of everything for a thousand years in a single day, then He sends it to His angels, and when that has passed, He decrees for another thousand years, and so on forever. This was said by Mujahid. It was also said that the ha refers to ascension. It was also said that the meaning is that He manages the affairs of this world until the Hour comes, then that affair ascends to Him, and He judges it in a day whose length is a thousand years. It was also said that the meaning is that He manages the affair of the sun in its rising and setting and its return to its place of rising, in a day whose length in distance is a thousand years. Ibn Abbas said: The meaning is that if someone other than the angel had walked it, its duration would be a thousand years, because the descent is five hundred and the ascent is five hundred. This was narrated from a group of commentators, and it is the preferred choice of al-Tabari, mentioned by al-Mahdawi. It is the meaning of the first statement. That is, Gabriel, due to his speed of travel, can travel a thousand years in one of your days. This was mentioned by al-Zamakhshari. Al-Mawardi reported from Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak that the angel ascends in one day a journey of a thousand years. Qatadah reported that the angel descends and ascends in a day the duration of which is a thousand years, so the duration of his descent is five hundred years, and the duration of his ascent is five hundred, according to Qatadah and al-Suddi. According to Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak, the descent is a thousand years, and the ascent is a thousand years. Of what you count means of what you calculate of the days of this world. This day refers to a period of time estimated at a thousand worldly years, and it is not a day that encompasses a day between two nights, because that is not with God.
