The Arabs sometimes express the duration of an afternoon with a day, as the poet said: Two days, one day of gatherings and clubs, and one day of marching to the enemies for retribution. He does not mean two days divided, but rather he meant that their time will be divided into two halves, so he expressed each of the two halves with a day. Ibn Abi Ubla read: it is based on the passive voice. It was also read: they count with the letter ya. As for the statement of God, the Most High, on a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, this is problematic with this verse. Abdullah ibn Fayruz al-Daylami asked Abdullah ibn Abbas about this verse and about His statement, on a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. He said: These are days that God, the Most High, has named, and I do not know what they are. I hate to say about them what I do not know. Then Saeed ibn al-Musayyab was asked about them, and he said: I do not know. So I informed him of what Ibn Abbas said, and Ibn al-Musayyab said to the questioner: This Ibn Abbas was afraid to say about it, and he is more knowledgeable than me. Then the scholars discussed this, and it was said that the verse A questioner asked refers to the Day of Resurrection, unlike this verse. The meaning is that God, the Most High, made it as difficult for the disbelievers as fifty thousand years, as Ibn Abbas said. The Arabs describe the days of hardship as long and the days of happiness as short. He said: A day like the shadow of a spear, its length shortened, the blood of the wineskin fell on us and the flowers lined up It was said: The Day of Resurrection has days, some of which are a thousand years long and some of which are fifty thousand years long. It was also said: The times of Resurrection are different, so the disbeliever will be punished with one type of punishment for a thousand years, then he will move to another type whose duration will be fifty thousand years. It was also said: The stations of the Resurrection will be fifty stations, each station a thousand years. So the meaning of: He will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is a thousand years is an amount of time, or a station on the Day of Resurrection. An-Nahhas said: The word day in the language means time, so the meaning is: The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him during a time the extent of which is a thousand years, and at another time the extent of which is a thousand years, and at another time the extent of which is fifty thousand years. Wahb ibn Munabbih narrated on a day the extent of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The distance between the lowest part of the earth and the Throne. Al-Tha’labi narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Qatadah, and Ad-Dahhak regarding the words of God the Almighty: The angels and the Spirit will ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years (al-Ma’arij 70:4), he meant from the earth to the Lote Tree of the Limit where Gabriel is. God the Almighty says: Gabriel and the angels who are with him from the people of his station will travel a journey of fifty thousand years in one day of the days of this world. His saying, to it means to the place to which God the Almighty commanded them to ascend. This is like the saying of Abraham, peace be upon him: Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me 37:99, meaning the land of Ash-Sham. God the Almighty also says: And whoever emigrates from his home to God 4:100, meaning to Madinah. Abu Hurairah said that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: An angel from my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, came to me with a message, then he raised his foot and placed it above the sky and the other on the ground, without raising it yet.
32:6: The Almighty says: He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. That is, He knows what is hidden from creation and what is present to them. This means I as explained earlier in Surat Al-Baqarah. The statement contains a sense of threat and warning, that is, be sincere in your actions and words, for I will reward them.
32:7: The Almighty says: Who perfected everything which He created Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr and Ibn Amir read it: He created it with a sukoon on the lam. The rest read it with a fatha. Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim chose it for simplicity. It is a past tense verb in the accusative case as an adjective for thing. The meaning, as narrated from Ibn Abbas, is: He perfected everything which He created, i.e. He brought it to life as He wanted, without changing it from His will. Another saying is: Everything He created is good, because no one is able to produce anything like it, and it indicates its Creator. Whoever makes the lam sukoon, it is a verbal noun according to Sibawayh, because his saying: He perfected everything which He created indicates: He created everything in a creation, so it is like: God made (al-Naml 27:88) and God's Book is upon you (al-Nisa 4:24). According to others, it is accusative as a substitute for all, meaning He who created everything in the best way. According to some grammarians, it is a second object, meaning: He made everything He created better, understand better, and know better. So it takes two objects, meaning He made everything He created better. It was said: It is in the accusative case as an explanation, and the meaning is: He made everything better in creation. It was also said: It is in the accusative case by dropping the preposition, and the meaning is: He created everything better. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas, and better means he perfected and perfected, so it is better in terms of what it is for the purposes for which it was intended. From this meaning, Ibn Abbas and Ikrimah said: The back of a monkey is not beautiful, but it is perfected and precise. Abu Nujayh narrated from Mujahid: He created everything better. He said: He perfected it. It is like the saying of God the Most High: Who gave each thing its form and nature (Ta-Ha: 50). Meaning, He did not create man in the form of an animal, nor did He create the animal in the form of a man. It is permissible to say: He created him in the nominative case, assuming that is how He created him. It was said: It is a generality in wording but a specificity in meaning, and the meaning is: He created everything good. It was said: It is general in wording and meaning, meaning that He made everything He created beautiful, even the dog was made beautiful in its creation, as Ibn Abbas said. Qatada said: There is beauty in the monkey’s anus. God Almighty says: And He began the creation of man from clay, meaning Adam.
32:8: Then He made his offspring from an extract of despised water. This was mentioned in Al-Mu'minun and elsewhere. Al-Zajjaj said: From despised water is weak. Another said: Despised has no significance for people.
32:9: Then He proportioned him He returned to Adam, that is, He proportioned his creation. And breathed into him of His spirit Then He returned to his offspring and said: And made for you hearing and sight. It was said: Then He made that insignificant water a balanced creation, and placed the spirit in it and added it to Himself as an honor. Also, it is from His action and creation, just as He added the servant to it by saying: My servant. He expressed it by the blowing because the spirit is of the same kind as the wind. This has been explained previously in Surat An-Nisa and elsewhere. You are little grateful That is, then you do not give thanks, but rather you are ungrateful.
32:10: The Almighty said: And they said, ‘Shall we, when we are lost in the earth,’ This is the statement of those who deny resurrection, meaning we have perished, become worthless, and turned to dust. Its origin is from the Arab saying: The water was lost in the milk when it disappeared. The Arabs say about something that has been overcome by something else until its trace is hidden: it has gone astray. Al-Akhtal said: I was the speck in a turbid, foaming wave, the one who brought it threw it as a gift of misguidance. Qatrib said: The meaning of we went astray is that we were lost on earth. He recited the words of Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubani: So his misguided ones returned with clear eyes, and Hazm and Nael left him in the Golan. Ibn Muhaisin and Yahya bin Ya'mar read: dalalana with a kasra on the lam, and it is a dialect. Al-Jawhari said: He has gone astray means he has led astray. God the Almighty said: "Say: 'If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment'" (Saba 34: 1050). This is the dialect of Najd and it is the most eloquent. The people of Aliyah say: I went astray with a kasra on the lam - he led astray. He is astray, which is misguidance and loss. And he led him astray means he lost him and destroyed him. It is said: The dead person went astray if he was buried. He said: Then his misguided ones returned... Al-Bayt Ibn Al-Sikkit. I lost my camel if it went away from you. And I lost the mosque and the house: if you do not know their location. And so is every permanent thing that cannot be guided to. And in the hadith, Ali said, God led him astray, meaning He led him astray from him, meaning He concealed from him, from the saying of God the Almighty: Will we then be lost in the earth? Meaning, we are hidden. And God led him astray is grace. You say: You guide the lost one but do not guide the lost one. Al-A’mash and Al-Hasan read: Sallalana with a sad, meaning you are. And it is the reading of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Al-Nahhas: Sallalana is not known in the language, but it is said: Salla al-Lahm and Asal, and Khamm and Akhm if they rot. Al-Jawhari said: Salla al-Lahm yasal - with a kasra - salulan, meaning it rotted, whether cooked or raw. Al-Hutay’ah said: That is a young man who gives his all, and his meat is not spoiled by his sword. The origin of the same is Inna lillah fi khalq jadeed meaning Shall we create after that a new creation? It is also read: Aaana. An-Nahhas: This is a difficult question in Arabic. It is said: What is the operator in if? And if does not affect what comes after it on what comes before it. The question in the interrogative is more difficult because what comes after the interrogative is more likely not to affect what comes before it from in how and when they are combined. The answer to the reading of those who read: Inna is that the operator we went astray and to the reading of those who read: Aaana is that the operator is implied, and the meaning is we will be resurrected if we die. There is also another question in this. It is said: What is the answer to if according to the first reading because it has the meaning of a condition? The statement in that is that after it is a past tense verb, so this is permissible. Rather, they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord meaning they do not deny the ability of God to resurrect, because they acknowledge His ability but they believe that they will not be held accountable, and that they do not say God.
32:11: There are two issues: The first: The Almighty's saying: "Say: The Angel of Death will take you in death." When He mentioned their exclusion from resurrection, He mentioned their taking in death and that He will bring them back. He will take you in death is from the root tawafa to take the number or thing if he takes it all and seizes it all. It is said: God took him in death, meaning He took his soul and then seized him. And I took my money from so-and-so in full, meaning I took it in full. The Angel of Death is called Azrael and means servant of God, as mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. His actions are all by the command of God, His creation and invention. It is narrated in the hadith: God takes the souls of all animals without the Angel of Death, as if he takes their lives away. This was mentioned by Ibn Atiyyah. I said: It has been narrated otherwise, and that the Angel of Death takes the souls of all creatures, even fleas and mosquitoes. Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated on the authority of his father who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Be gentle with my companion, for he is a believer. The Angel of Death, peace be upon him, said: “O Muhammad, be at ease and be content, for I am gentle with every believer. Know five times a day, so much so that I know their young and old better than they know themselves. By God, O Muhammad, if I wanted to take the soul of a mosquito, I would not be able to do so until God is the one who commands it to be taken.” Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali said: I have been informed that he looks over them at the times of prayers. Al-Mawardi mentioned this. Al-Khatib Abu Bakr Ahmad bin Ali bin Thabit al-Baghdadi said: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan bin Muhammad al-Khalal told me: Abu Muhammad Abdullah bin Uthman al-Saffar told us: Abu Bakr Hamid al-Masri told us: Yahya bin Ayyub al-Alaaf told us: Sulayman bin Muhair al-Kalabi told us: I was in the presence of Malik bin Anas may God be pleased with him when a man came to him and asked him: Abu Abdullah, are fleas the angels of death who take their souls? God takes the souls at the time of their death (al-Zumar 39:42). Ibn Atiyyah said after mentioning the hadith: It is the same with the children of Adam, except that it is a kind of honor in that there is an angel and angels with him in taking their souls. So God created the Angel of Death and created through him the taking of souls, extracting them from the bodies and bringing them out of them. God created an army to be with him and to know his actions by his command. God the Almighty said: And if you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve (al-Anfal 8:50). And He also said: Our messengers took them (al-Zumar 39:42). This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-An’am. And the Creator of all things, the true doer of every action. God the Almighty said: God takes the souls at the time of their death and those that do not die during their sleep. “He who created death and life” Al-Mulk:2. He gives life and causes death. So the Angel of Death takes the soul, while the helpers treat it, and God the Almighty takes the soul. This is the combination of the verses and the hadith. However, since the Angel of Death is in charge of this through an intermediary and direct action, taking the soul is attributed to him, just as creation is attributed to the Angel, as mentioned in the chapter on Hajj. It was narrated from Mujahid that the world is in the hands of the Angel of Death like a basin in the hands of a person, taking from wherever he wishes. This meaning was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and we have mentioned it in the Book of Remembrance. It was narrated that when God the Almighty entrusted the Angel of Death with the task of taking souls, he said: O Lord, You have made me mentioned in a bad way and the children of Adam revile me. God the Almighty said to him: I make causes and reasons for death, such as illnesses and diseases, to which they attribute death, so no one remembers You except with good. We have mentioned it in full in the Tadhkira - and we have mentioned that he calls the souls and they come to him and he takes them, then he hands them over to the angels of mercy or punishment - which contains healing for whoever wants to understand that. Second: Some scholars have used this verse as evidence for the permissibility of agency, based on His statement, And He is entrusted with you, meaning He takes the souls. Ibn al-Arabi said: “This is taken from its wording, not its meaning. If this were to be the case, we would have said regarding His statement, “Say, ‘O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of God to you all’” (al-A’raf 7:158): that it is a representation of God Almighty and an agency in conveying His message. We would also have said regarding His statement, Give the zakat (al-Baqarah 2:43) that it is an agency, for God Almighty has guaranteed sustenance for every creature and has given special food to the rich. He has instructed them that the sustenance of the poor is with them, and He has commanded that it be delivered to them in a known amount at a known time. He has planned it with His knowledge, implemented it with His judgment, and determined it with His wisdom. Rulings are not connected to words unless they relate to their original subjects for their desired purposes. If they appear for a purpose other than their intended purpose, then they are not connected to them.” Do you not see that buying and selling are known in both wording and meaning? God Almighty said: Indeed, God has purchased from the believers their lives and their properties in exchange for that they will have Paradise. It cannot be said that this verse is evidence of the permissibility of a master selling his slave, because the two objectives are different. However, if there is no alternative to the meanings, then it can be said that this verse is evidence that a judge may delegate someone to take a right from someone who is owed it by force, without the judge having any actual power to do so, or being bound by his consent if that is the case.
32:12: The Almighty says: And if you could but when the criminals will hang their heads before their Lord Subject and predicate. Al-Zajjaj said: The address to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, is also an address to his nation. The meaning is: If you could, O Muhammad, see those who deny the resurrection on the Day of Resurrection, you would see wonders. Abu al-Abbas's opinion is different from this, and that the meaning is: O Muhammad, say to the criminal, If you could but see when the criminals will hang their heads before their Lord, you would regret what you have done. Hanging their heads means out of regret, shame, sadness, humiliation, and grief. Before their Lord means when their Lord is held to account and their deeds are rewarded. Our Lord means they will say, Our Lord. We have seen, meaning we have seen what we used to lie. And we have heard what we used to deny. It was said: Our sight is the truth of Your threat. And we have heard the confirmation of Your messengers. They saw when sight could not benefit them, and they heard when hearing could not benefit them. So return us, meaning to the world. "We will do righteous deeds. Indeed, we are certain." That is, we believe in the resurrection. This was stated by Al-Naqqash. It was also said: We believe in what Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) brought, that it is the truth. This was stated by Yahya ibn Salam. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: So God, the Most High, denied them, saying: And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed, they are liars. (Al-An'am: 28). It was also said: The meaning of we are certain is that our doubts have now been removed. They used to hear and see in this world, but they did not reflect. They were as if they neither see nor hear. But when they are awakened in the Hereafter, it will be as if they had heard and seen. It was also said: Our Lord, You have the proof. We saw Your messengers and the wonders of Your creation in this world, and we heard their words, so we have no proof. This is an admission from them. Then they asked to be returned to this world so that they would believe.
32:13: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: When they said, "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world] and we will do righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain," He responded to them by saying, And if We willed, We could have given every soul its guidance. He said, If I willed, I could have guided all of mankind, and none of them would have differed. But the word from Me will come into effect (al-Quran 2:17). Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned it in his Raqa'iq in a long hadith. We have also mentioned it in al-Tadhkirah. An-Nahhas said, And if We willed, We could have given every soul its guidance. There are two opinions on its meaning: One of them is that it is in this world. The other is that the context of the speech indicates that it is in the Hereafter, meaning if We willed, We could have returned them to this world and the trial as they asked: "But the word from Me will come into effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together." That is, the word from Me will come into effect: I will surely punish those who disobey Me with the fire of Hell. God the Blessed and Exalted knew that if He sent them back, they would return, as He the Most High said: And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. This guidance means creating knowledge in the heart. The Mu'tazila interpret it as: If We willed, We could have compelled them to guidance by showing them tremendous signs. However, doing so would not be a good thing because it defeats the purpose for which the obligation was imposed, which is the reward that is only deserved by what the person charged with the obligation does of his own free will. The Imamiyyah interpreted it as: “It is permissible that He intended to guide them to the path to Paradise in the Hereafter, and He did not punish anyone. However, the true meaning of this is that He would fill Hellfire. Therefore, in our view, God the Most High is not obligated to guide everyone to it.” They said: “Rather, what is obligatory is the guidance of the infallible ones. As for the one who has sinned, it is permissible to guide him to Hellfire as a punishment for his actions.” However, the permissibility of that is prohibited, as they are certain that the intent is to guide them to faith. Scholars have discussed these two interpretations sufficiently in the fundamentals of religion. The closest answer to this is: It is no longer possible for us and for you to believe that God, the Almighty, would guide them by force, coercion, or compulsion. This leads to the doctrine of the Jabriyah, which is a despicable doctrine according to us and you. All that remains is that the guided believers are only guided by God, the Almighty, to faith and obedience by choice, so that the obligation is valid. Whoever wishes may believe and obey by choice, not by compulsion. God, the Almighty, says: For whoever among you wills to go straight (al-Takwir 81:28), and He says: So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way (al-Muzzammil 73:19). Then He followed these two verses with His saying: And you do not will except that God wills. Thus, the faith of the believers is based on their own will, and He denied that they will except that God wills. For this reason, the Jabriyah neglected to see that their guidance to faith is linked to the will of God, the Almighty. They said: The creation is compelled in all of their obedience, paying attention to His saying: And you do not will except that God wills. The Qadarites went to extremes when they saw that their guidance to faith was dependent on the will of the servants. They said: People are the creators of their actions, referring to the Almighty’s saying: For whoever among you wills to go straight. Our school of thought is moderation in belief, and it is a school of thought between the schools of the Jabriyah and the Qadariyah, and the best of matters are those in the middle. This is because the people of truth said: We differentiate between what we are forced to do and what we choose. That is, we perceive a difference between the trembling movement that occurs in a person’s hand without his effort or control or being coupled with his ability, and the movement of choice if he moves his hand in a movement similar to the movement of trembling. Whoever does not differentiate between the two movements: the movement of trembling and the movement of choice—both existing within himself and perceptible in his hand through his observation and the perception of his senses—is mentally deficient, unstable in his senses, and outside the party of the rational. This is the clear truth, and it is a path between the paths of isolation and neglect. And: Both ends of the intention of matters are reprehensible, and in this regard, the scholars who have insight chose to call this position between the two positions earning, and they took this name from the Noble Book of God, which is His saying, the Most High: For her is what she has earned, and against her is what she has earned (al-Baqarah 2:286).
32:14: His Almighty saying: Then taste for having forgotten the meeting of this Day of yours There are two opinions on this: One of them is that it is from forgetfulness that is not accompanied by remembrance, meaning they did not work for this day, so they were in the position of those who have forgotten. The other is that you forgot because of what you left, and likewise We have forgotten you. Muhammad bin Yazid provided evidence with His Almighty saying: And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot (Ta-Ha 20:115). He said: The evidence that it means left is that God the Almighty informed about Iblis that he said: Your Lord did not forbid you from this tree except that you should become angels (al-A’raf 7:20). So if Adam had been forgetful, he would have reminded him. And he recited: As if a skewer was coming out from the side of his page, and they forgot about him at Muftah. That is, they abandoned it. If it was due to forgetfulness, they would have done it once. Ad-Dahhak said: You forgot, meaning you abandoned my affair. Yahya ibn Salam said: That is, you abandoned faith in frivolity on this day. We forgot you means we abandoned you from goodness, as As-Suddi said. Mujahid said: We left you in torment. In resuming his statement: Indeed, We forgot you, the verb is constructed on in and its subject is a doubling of the vengeance against them. The meaning is: So taste this, meaning what you are in of lowered heads, shame, and grief due to forgetting God. Or taste the eternal torment, which is permanent and unending in Hell. For what you used to do means in this world of sins. Taste may also be expressed by what occurs to the soul even if it is not desired, because it senses it like its sense of the taste of food. Omar ibn Abi Rabi’ah said: Taste her abandonment if you claim that it is corruption. Perhaps your claim is a lie. Al-Jawhari: I tasted what so-and-so has, meaning I experienced it. And you tasted the bow if you pull it and look at it to see how tight it is. And God made him taste the consequences of his actions. Tufail said: So taste as we tasted on the day of Mahjar, of rage in our livers and resentment. And I tasted it, i.e. I tasted it bit by bit. And a matter that is tasted, i.e. experienced and known. The poet said: The era of the courtesans is like the era of the rich, and the taste of the rich is more delicious. And the gourmet: the bored.
32:15: God Almighty says: Only those believe in Our verses who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and exalt [God] with praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant. This is a consolation for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meaning that because they are accustomed to disbelief, they do not believe in you. Only those who reflect on it and take heed from it believe in you and the Qur’an. They are the ones who, when the Qur’an is recited to them, fall down in prostration. Ibn Abbas said: Ruku’. Al-Mahdawi said: This is according to the view of those who believe in ruku’ when reciting the prostration, and they provide evidence with the words of God Almighty: And he fell down in prostration and repented (Surah Sad: 24). It was said that what is meant by it is prostration, and most scholars agree with this, meaning they fell down in prostration to God Almighty on their faces in glorification of His signs and fear of His wrath and punishment. And glorify the praises of their Lord meaning they mixed glorification with praise, meaning they declared His sanctity and thanks, so they said in their al-Sajdah 32:Glory be to God and His praise, Glory be to my Lord, the Most High, and His praise, meaning glorifying God Almighty above what the polytheists say. Sufyan said: And glorify the praises of their Lord meaning they prayed in praise of their Lord. And they are not too arrogant to worship Him, said Yahya ibn Salam. Al-Naqqash: They are not too arrogant to worship Him as the people of Mecca were too arrogant to prostrate.
32:16: The Almighty says: Their sides forsake their beds meaning they raise themselves up and turn away from the places of lying down. The word is in the accusative case as a state, meaning their sides forsake them. Al-madajee' is the plural of madja', which is a place of sleeping. It may also refer to the time of lying down, but it is a metaphor, and the literal meaning is more appropriate. An example of this is the saying of Abdullah ibn Rawahah: And among us is the Messenger of God reciting his book when the dawn breaks brightly. He spends the night turning away from his bed when the polytheists make his beds heavy. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Rummani said: Tajawwaf means moving aside. It is also used in forgiving someone who has made a mistake in cursing or the like. Al-Janub is the plural of Janb side. There are two opinions regarding what their sides turn away from their beds for: One of them: To remember God, either during prayer or otherwise, as stated by Ibn Abbas and Al-Dahhak. The second: For prayer. Regarding the prayer for which their sides turn away, there are four opinions: One of them: Moving around at night, as stated by the majority of commentators, and most people agree with it. It is the one that contains praise, and it is the opinion of Mujahid, Al-Awza’i, Malik ibn Anas, Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aliyah, and others. This is indicated by the statement of God the Almighty: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes because they permitted they hid with what was hidden. And God knows best. Its explanation will follow. There are many hadiths about the night prayer, including the hadith of Muadh ibn Jabal that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Shall I not guide you to the doors of goodness? Fasting is a shield, and charity extinguishes sin as water extinguishes fire, and a man’s prayer in the depths of the night - he said, then he recited: ‘Their sides forsake their beds’ - until he reached: ‘they know.’” Narrated by Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad, and by Qadi Ismail ibn Ishaq and Abu ‘Eesa al-Tirmidhi, who said about it: A good and authentic hadith. The second: The ‘Isha’ prayer, which is called ‘Atmah’, as stated by al-Hasan and ‘Ata’. In al-Tirmidhi. It was narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that this verse, Their sides forsake their beds, was revealed regarding waiting for the prayer called Isha. He said: This is a good and rare hadith. The third: The movement between Maghrib and Isha. This was said by Qatada and Ikrimah. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that this verse, Their sides forsake their beds, to supplicate their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them, they spend, he said: They used to move between Maghrib and Isha. The fourth: Ad-Dahhak said: The movement of one’s sides is for a man to pray Isha and Fajr in congregation. This was said by Abu Darda and Ubadah. I said: This is a good statement, and it combines the sayings in meaning, because the one who waits for the Isha prayer until he prays it is in prayer and remembrance of God, the Almighty, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A man remains in prayer as long as he waits for the prayer. Anas said: What is meant by the verse is waiting for the last Isha prayer, because the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to delay it until about a third of the night. Ibn Atiyyah said: The pre-Islamic people used to sleep at the beginning of sunset and at any time a person wanted, so waiting for the Isha prayer came as strange and difficult. The one who prays Fajr prayer in congregation, especially at the beginning of its time, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to pray it. It is customary for whoever maintains this prayer at or at the beginning of its time to get up at dawn, perform ablution, pray, and remember God, the Almighty, until dawn breaks, thus avoiding the beginning and end of the night. This is further supported by what Muslim narrated on the authority of Uthman ibn Affan, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Whoever prays the Isha prayer in congregation, it is as if he spent half the night in prayer, and whoever prays the Fajr prayer in congregation, it is as if he spent the entire night in prayer. The wording of Al-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud in this hadith is: Whoever attends the Isha prayer in congregation, it is as if he spent half the night in prayer, and whoever prays the Isha and Fajr prayers in congregation, it is as if he spent the entire night in prayer. It was previously mentioned in Surat An-Nur on the authority of Ka’b that whoever prays four rak’ahs after the last Isha prayer, it is as if he spent the night in prayer. Hassan's hadiths have been narrated on the merits of the prayer between sunset and night prayers and the night prayer. Ibn al-Mubarak said: Yahya ibn Ayoub told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj or Ibn Abi al-Hajjaj told me that he heard Abdul Karim narrating that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever performs ten rak'ahs between sunset and night prayers, a palace will be built for him in Paradise. Umar ibn al-Khattab said to him: Then our palaces and houses will increase in number, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: God is greater and better - or he said - better. Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As said: The prayer of the first two is the seclusion between sunset and night prayers until people return to prayer. Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to pray at that time and say: The prayer of heedlessness is between sunset and night prayers. Ibn al-Mubarak mentioned this. Al-Tha'labi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever refrains from sleeping between sunset and night prayers, two palaces will be built for him in Paradise a distance of a year's journey. In them are trees such that if the people of the east and west were to settle in them, they would be filled with fruit." This is the prayer of the repentant and the heedlessness of the heedless. One of the supplications that is answered and not rejected is the supplication between sunset and evening prayers. Chapter on the virtue of forsaking one's beds: Ibn al-Mubarak reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, a crier will call out: Today you will know who are the companions of the vineyard. Let those who are grateful to God in every situation arise, and they will arise and be set out on their way to Paradise. Then he will call out a second time: Today you will know who are the companions of the vineyard. Let those whose sides forsook their beds arise, They call upon their Lord in fear and hope, and spend out of what We have provided them. He said: So they will rise and go to Paradise. Then he will call out a third time: Today you will know who are the companions of the vineyard. Let those arise who were not distracted by commerce or sale from the remembrance of God and performance of prayer and giving zakah, fearing a Day when the hearts and eyes will turn about. They will rise and be set out on their way to Paradise. Al-Tha'labi narrated on the authority of Asma' bint Yazid that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "When God gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will come and call out in a voice that all of creation will hear: Today the people of the assembly will know who is most deserving of generosity. Let those whose sides used to forsake their beds arise. They will arise, and they will be few. Then he will call out a second time: Today you will know who is most deserving of generosity. Let those whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God arise. They will arise. Then he will call out a third time: Today you will know who is most deserving of generosity. Those who are grateful to God in every situation, in prosperity and adversity, will arise. They will arise, and they will be few. They will all travel to Paradise, and then the rest of the people will be held to account." Ibn al-Mubarak said: Muammar told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu al-Ala’ ibn al-Shakheer, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: There are three at whom God laughs and is pleased with them: A man who gets up at night and leaves his bed and warmth, then performs ablution and does it well, then gets up to pray. God says to His angels: What made My servant do what he did? They say: Our Lord, You know him better than we do. He says: I know him better, but tell Me. They say: I hoped for something from him and he hoped for it, and I feared something from him and he feared it. He says: I bear witness that I have secured him from what he feared and made obligatory for him what he hoped for. He said: A man who was on a raid and encountered the enemy and his companions were defeated, but he held firm until he was killed or God granted them victory. God says to His angels a story similar to this. A man who travels at night and, at the end of the night, he and his companions dismount. His companions sleep and he gets up to pray. God says to His angels... and he mentioned the story. The Almighty says: They call upon their Lord in the accusative case as a state, meaning calling upon. It is possible that it is a new description, meaning that their sides forsake each other and they also call upon their Lord in every situation, day and night. Out of fear is the object for which. It may be a verbal noun. Out of hope is the same, meaning out of fear of the punishment and hope for the reward. And out of what We have provided them they spend "out of what can mean which" and can be a verbal noun. In both interpretations, it must be separate from "out of what we spend". It was said that it means the obligatory zakat. It was also said that it means the voluntary zakat. These people are more praiseworthy.
32:17: God Almighty says: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as reward for what they used to do. Hamzah read: Ma akhfa lahum with a sukoon on the yaa. The others read it with a fatha. In Abdullah’s reading, it is ma nakhfi with a damma on the noon. Al-Mufaddal narrated from Al-A’mash ma yakhfi lahum with a damma on the yaa and a fatha on the faa. Ibn Mas’ud and Abu Hurairah read: Man qara’ a’yin. Whoever makes the yaa’ sukoon in his saying ma akhfa, then it is a future tense verb and its alif is the alif of the speaker. Ma is in the accusative case with akhfa, which is an interrogative, and the sentence is in the accusative case because it is in the position of two objects, and the pronoun referring to ma is omitted. Whoever opens the yaa, then it is a past tense verb in the passive voice. Ma is in the nominative case as the subject, and the predicate is akhfa and what follows it, and the pronoun in akhfa refers to ma. Al-Zajjaj said: Ma akhfa lahum is read with the meaning of ma akhfa God lahum, and this is the reading of Muhammad ibn Ka’b, and ma is in the accusative case. Al-Mahdawi: Whoever reads: qara’ a’yin, it is the plural of qurra, and the plural is good in it because it is added to the plural, and the singular is because it is a verbal noun for the genus. Abu Bakr Al-Anbari said: “This does not contradict the Qur’an, because the ta’ of qarrah is written as a ta’ according to the dialect of those who connect to the pause, just as they write rahmatullah with a ta’. The one who read it should not be surprised by the alif being dropped in writing, even though it is present in the pronunciation, just as the alif being dropped in as-sama’ is not surprised by the fact that it is fixed in the tongue and pronunciation. The intended meaning is that God has informed them of the bliss that no soul, human being, or angel has created. Concerning the meaning of this verse, the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: “God the Almighty said, ‘I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and has never crossed the mind of man. ’ Then he recited this verse: ‘Their sides forsake their beds’ until His saying: ‘because of what they used to do. ’” Narrated by Sahih from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa’d Al-Sa’idi. Ibn Mas’ud said: It is written in the Torah: ‘Upon God is for those who forsake their beds that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. ’” Ibn Abbas said: The matter in this is too great and grand to be explained. I said: This honor is for the highest-ranking person in Paradise, as was explained in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba, tracing it back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Moses, peace be upon him, asked his Lord, ‘O Lord, what is the lowest-ranking person in Paradise?’ He said: ‘It is a man who comes after the people of Paradise have entered, and it is said to him: Enter Paradise.’ He says: ‘O Lord, how is that, when the people have settled in their stations and taken what they have acquired?’ It is said to him: ‘Would you be pleased to have a kingdom like that of a king of the kings of this world?’ He says: ‘I am pleased, O Lord.’ He says: ‘That is for you, and the like thereof, and the like thereof, and the like thereof, and the like thereof, and the like thereof.’ He says: ‘The fifth time, I am pleased, O Lord.’ It is said: ‘This is for you, and ten times the like thereof, and for you is whatever your soul desires and your eye delights.’ He says: ‘I am pleased with your kindness.’ He says: ‘O Lord, who is the highest in status?’ He said: ‘Those are the ones whose honor I have planted with My Hand and sealed, so that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.’ He said: ‘And its confirmation with the Book of God is the saying of the Most High: “No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for eyes as reward for what they used to do.’” It has been narrated on the authority of Al-Mughira, with a chain of transmission ending with him, saying: Muslim also narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God, the Blessed and Exalted, says: ‘I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, let alone what I have informed you of.’ Then he recited: ‘No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes.’” Ibn Sirin said: What is meant by this is looking at God, the Exalted. Al-Hasan said: The people concealed their deeds, so God, the Exalted, concealed for them that which no eye has seen and no ear has heard.
32:18: There are three issues in this: First: The Almighty's statement: Is he who is a believer like he who is a sinner? They are not equal. Meaning, the believer is not like the sinner, and for this reason We have given these believers the great reward. Ibn Abbas and Ata' ibn Yasar said: The verse was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib and Al-Walid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt. They argued and Al-Walid said: I am more eloquent than you, have sharper spears, and I am more capable of striking back against an army - and it was narrated: I am more complete in an army - in body. Ali said to him: Be quiet! You are a sinner. So the verse was revealed. Al-Zajjaj and Al-Nahhas mentioned that it was revealed about Ali and Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt. Ibn Atiyyah said: Based on this, the verse must have been revealed in Mecca, because Uqba was not in Medina, but was killed on the way to Mecca on the way back from Badr by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The other opinion is challenged by the application of the term sinner to Al-Walid. This may have been at the beginning of Al-Walid’s conversion to Islam due to something he had in his heart, or because of what was narrated of him transmitting from Banu Al-Mustaliq what had not happened, until the verse If a wicked person brings you report, verify it (al-Hujurat 49:6) was revealed concerning him, as will be explained in Al-Hujurat. It is also possible that the Shari’ah applied this to him because he was on the verge of what he was seeking, and he was the one who drank alcohol during the time of Uthman may God be pleased with him, and he led the people in the dawn prayer, then he turned and said: Do you want me to tell you more? And similar things that would take too long to mention. Second: When God the Almighty divided the believers and the immoral ones whom He deemed immoral by disbelief - because the denial at the end of the verse requires that - this required denying the heavens and the earth between the believer and the unbeliever. For this reason, He forbade retaliation between them, since one of the conditions for the obligation of retaliation is equality between the killer and the killed. Our scholars have used this as evidence against Abu Hanifa for killing a Muslim for a non-Muslim. He said: He meant to deny equality here in the Hereafter in reward and in this world in justice. We interpret this generally, which is more correct, since there is no evidence that specifies it, as Ibn al-Arabi said. Third: The Almighty’s saying: They are not equal. Al-Zajjaj and others said: From is suitable for both singular and plural. An-Nahhas said: From is the word from that represents a group, so he said: They are not equal. This is the saying of many grammarians. Some of them said: They are not equal to two, because two is a plural, because one is plural with another. Al-Zajjaj also said this. The hadith is considered valid according to this saying, because it is from Ibn Abbas. Others said: Is he who is a believer was revealed about Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, like he who is a sinner about Al-Walid ibn Uqba ibn Abi Mu’ayt. The poet said: Isn't death the same between them if they die and are in the graves?
32:19: The Almighty says: As for those who have believed and done righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge. He informed us about the location of the two groups tomorrow. For the believers are the Gardens of Refuge, meaning they will take refuge in the Gardens. He added the Gardens to the refuge because that place includes Gardens. Nuzul means hospitality. The Nuzul is what is prepared for the guest or the lodger. It was mentioned at the end of Al Imran and it is accusative as a state of the Gardens, meaning the Gardens are prepared for them. It may also be the object of the verb.
32:20: And as for those who disobeyed, that is, those who abandoned faith to disbelief, their refuge is the Fire, that is, their abode therein. Whenever they wish to get out of it, they will be returned to it, that is, if the flames of the Fire push them to the top of it, they will be returned to their place in it, because they hope to get out of it. This was mentioned previously in Hajj. And it will be said to them, that is, the keepers of Hell will say to them, or God will say to them: Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny. Taste is used in both a tangible and a conceptual sense, and this was explained previously in this surah.
32:21: God the Almighty says: And We will make them taste of the lesser punishment. Al-Hasan, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ad-Dahhak, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and Ibrahim An-Nakha'i said: The lesser punishment is the calamities and ailments of this world with which the servants are tested until they repent. Ibn Abbas said the same. It was also narrated from him that it refers to the prescribed punishments. Ibn Mas'ud, Al-Husayn ibn Ali, and Abdullah ibn Al-Harith said: It is killing by the sword on the day of Badr. Muqatil said: Seven years of famine in Mecca until they ate carcasses. Mujahid said the same. It was also narrated from him: The lesser punishment is the punishment of the grave. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said the same. They said: The greater punishment is the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Qushayri said: It was also said that it is the punishment of the grave. This is questionable, because of His statement: Perhaps they will return. He said: Whoever interprets the punishment to mean killing says: Perhaps they will return, meaning that whoever remains of them will return. There is no disagreement that the greater punishment is the punishment of Hellfire, except for what was narrated from Ja'far ibn Muhammad that it is the emergence of the Mahdi with the sword. The lesser punishment is the high prices. It has been said that the meaning of His statement, Perhaps they will return, according to Mujahid and Al-Baraa’, is that perhaps they want to return and seek it, like His statement, So send us back that we may do righteousness 32:12. The intention to return is called returning, just as the intention to stand is called standing, in His statement, When you rise to prayer 5:6. This is indicated by the reading of those who read, they return in the passive form, as mentioned by Al-Zamakhshari.
32:22: God Almighty says: And who is more unjust meaning no one is more unjust to himself. than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord meaning His proofs and signs. then turns away from them by refusing to accept. Indeed, We will take retribution from the criminals for their denial and turning away.
32:23: God the Almighty said: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, so be not in doubt about meeting him. That is, O Muhammad, do not be in doubt about meeting Moses, as Ibn Abbas said. He met him on the Night of the Isra'. Qatadah said: The meaning is: Do not be in doubt that you will meet him on the Night of the Isra'. The meaning is the same. It was also said: Do not be in doubt about meeting Moses on the Day of Resurrection, and you will meet him on that Day. It was also said: Do not be in doubt about meeting Moses with the Scripture and accepting it, as Mujahid and Az-Zajjaj said. Al-Hasan said in a similar meaning: And We had certainly given Moses the Scripture, so he was harmed and denied, so do not be in doubt that he will meet you with what he met of denial and harm. The ha' refers to something omitted, and the meaning is from meeting what he met. An-Nahhas said: This is a strange statement, except that it is from the narration of Umar ibn Ubayd. It was said that there is an inversion of the verse, and the meaning is: Say, The Angel of Death who has been assigned to you will take you, so do not be in doubt about meeting Him. So it came as an objection between And We gave Moses the Scripture and And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel. The pronoun in And We made it has two meanings: One of them is: We made Moses, as Qatada said. The second is: We made the Scripture, as Al-Hasan said.
32:24: And We made from among them leaders meaning leaders and role models who are sacrificed for the sake of their religion. The Kufians read it as A'immah an-Nahhas Imams of an-Nahhas, which is a mistake according to all grammarians, because it combines two hamzas in one word, and this is a matter of precise grammar. al-Sharh 94:The original form is ummah, then the vowel of the meem was placed on the hamza and the meem was assimilated, and the second hamza was lightened so that two hamzas would not come together. Combining two hamzas in two letters is far-fetched, but in one letter, it is only permissible to lighten the second, such as when you say Adam and another. It is also said: this is more aom than this and ayyam, with waw and yaa. This has already been mentioned in Bara’ah, and God knows best. They guide by Our command means they call creation to obey Us. By Our command means We commanded them to do that. It was also said: By Our command meaning by Our command, meaning they guide people to Our religion. Then it was said: What is meant are the prophets, peace be upon them, as Qatada said. It was also said: What is meant are the jurists and scholars. When they were patient is the general reading of when with a fatha on the lam, a shaddah on the meem, and a fatha on it, meaning when they were patient. Yahya, Hamza, al-Kisa’i, Khalaf, and Ruways on the authority of Ya’qub read: When they were patient meaning because of their patience We made them leaders. Abu Ubaid chose it based on Ibn Masoud’s reading of ma sabaru with the letter ba. This patience is patience in religion and affliction. It was also said: they were patient in avoiding the world.
32:25: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. That is, He will judge and rule between the believers and the disbelievers. He will reward each according to what he deserves. It was also said that He will judge between the prophets and their people, as narrated by Al-Naqqash.
32:26: God the Almighty says: Have they not been guided? Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, Qatadah, and Abu Zaid on the authority of Ya'qub read nahd lahum with a noon, and this is a clear reading. An-Nahhas: There is a problem with the ya', because it is said: A verb never has an agent, so where is the agent in yahdi? Grammarians discussed this, and al-Farra' said: kam is in the nominative case for yahdi. This contradicts the grammarians' principle in their statement that the interrogative does not affect what precedes it or kam in any way, I mean what precedes it. Abu al-Abbas's school of thought is that yahdi indicates guidance, and the meaning is, has God not guided them to guidance? It was also said that the meaning is, has God not guided them? So the meaning of ya' and noon is the same, meaning, have We not made clear to them Our destruction of the disbelieving generations before them. Al-Zajjaj said: Kam is in the accusative case with ‘we destroyed them’ “walking in their dwellings. The pronoun in ‘walking’ may refer to those who walk in the dwellings of those who were destroyed, meaning that these people walk without taking heed. It may also refer to those who were destroyed, so it would be a state, and the meaning is: We destroyed them while they were walking in their dwellings. “In that are signs. Will they not then hear?” God’s signs and admonitions and take heed.
32:27: God the Almighty said: Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land? That is, do they not know that as We have decreed that We drive the water to the dry land in which there is no vegetation, We will revive it? Al-Zamakhshari said: Jarz is the land whose vegetation has been barren, i.e. cut off, either due to the lack of water or because it has been grazed and removed. And that which does not grow, such as marshes, is called Jarz, and this is indicated by God's statement: And We bring forth thereby crops. Ibn Abbas said: It is a land in Yemen. Mujahid said: It is Abyan. Ikrimah said: It is the thirsty land. Ad-Dahhak said: It is the dead, thirsty land. Al-Farra' said: It is the land in which there is no vegetation, and he said: It is with the letter 'ayn' because of the definite article, except that it is permissible according to the saying of Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak. The chain of transmission from Ibn Abbas is sound and there is no objection to it. This is only an adjective, and the adjective is for definiteness. Al-Asma'i said: It is the land that does not grow anything. Muhammad bin Yazid said: It is unlikely that it is for land with the definite article, and it is derived from their saying: a man who is greedy if he does not leave anything without eating it. Al-Zajir said: He is a greedy man who cries when he is hungry. He eats dates but does not throw away the pits. And also the she-camel Jaruz: if it eats everything it finds. And the sword Jaraz: meaning cutting and cutting. And Jarazt al-Jarrad al-Zar’a: if it uprooted the crops by eating them. Al-Farra and others narrated that it is said: a land of Jaraz, Jarz, Jarz, and Jarz. And likewise Bakhl, Raghab, and Rahab, in the four four languages. It has been narrated that this land has no rivers, and it is far from the sea, and only every year there comes to it a valley, so they plant three times every year. And from Mujahid also: It is the land of the Nile. And We bring forth with it meaning with water. Cultivation from which their livestock eat of grass and hay. And themselves of grain, seed, and fruits. They see this and know that We are able to bring them back. And We bring forth is in apposition to We drive or punctuated by what precedes it. Our livestock eat from it is in the accusative case as an adjective.
32:28: God Almighty says: And they say, ‘When will this conquest come, if you should be truthful?’
32:29: God the Almighty says: And they say, 'When will this conquest be, if you should be truthful?' (Al-'Araf: 89) The word when is in the nominative case, but it can also be in the accusative case as an adverbial phrase. Qatadah said: The conquest is the judgment. Al-Farra' and Al-Qutbi said: It means the conquest of Mecca. More appropriate than this is what Mujahid said, who said: It means the Day of Resurrection. It is narrated that the believers said: God the Almighty will judge between us on the Day of Resurrection, rewarding the doer of good and punishing the wrongdoer. The disbelievers said in mockery: When will the Day of Conquest be? i.e., this judgment. A judge is called a conqueror or opener because things are opened and separated by his hand. In the Qur'an: Our Lord, judge between us and our people in truth. (Al-'Araf: 89) This has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah and other verses. Say, 'On the Day of Conquest,' is an adverbial phrase. Al-Farra' permitted the nominative case. The faith of those who disbelieve will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved. That is, they will be given a delay or respite to repent, whether the Day of Conquest was the Day of Badr or the Conquest of Mecca. They were killed in Badr, and on the day of the conquest they fled, so Khalid bin Al-Walid pursued them and killed them.
32:30: The Almighty's statement: So turn away from them. It was said that its meaning is so turn away from their foolishness and do not answer them except with what you are commanded to do. And wait, for they are waiting. That is, wait for the Day of Conquest, the day when God will judge you against them. Ibn Abbas said: So turn away from them, meaning from the polytheists of Quraysh of Mecca. This was abrogated by the sword in Surat Bara'ah in His statement: Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. (al-Tawbah 9:5). And wait, meaning My appointment with you. It was said that it means the Day of Badr. For they are waiting. That is, they are waiting for you for the events of the time. It was said that the verse is not abrogated, since turning away can occur with an order to fight, such as a truce or other such matter. It was also said that he turned away from it after the proof was delivered, and wait, for they are waiting. If it is said: How can they await the Resurrection when they do not believe? There are two answers to this: One of them is that the meaning is that they are awaiting death, which is one of the causes of the Resurrection, in which case this is a metaphor. The other: that among them are those who doubt and among them are those who believe in the Resurrection, so this is an answer to these two categories. And God knows best. Ibn al-Samiq’ read: Indeed they are waiting with a fat-ha on the dhal. It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid and Ibn Muhaysin. Al-Farra’ said: This is not correct except with an omitted word, meaning: they are waiting for them. Abu Hatim said: The correct one is the kasra, meaning await their punishment, for they are awaiting your destruction. It has been said that Ibn al-Samiq’s reading with a fat-ha on the dhal means: and await their destruction, for they are more deserving of awaiting their destruction, meaning that they are doomed to perish, and await that, for the angels in heaven are awaiting it, as mentioned by al-Zamakhshari. This is the meaning of al-Farra’s statement. And God knows best.
33:1: Medinan according to all of them. It was revealed about the hypocrites and their harming of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), their slander of him and his marriage, etc. It has seventy-three verses, and this surah was equal to Surah Al-Baqarah. It included the verse of stoning (“The old man and the old woman, if they commit adultery, stone them both. It is a punishment from God. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.”) Abu Bakr Al-Anbari mentioned it on the authority of Ubayy ibn Ka’b. The scholars interpret this to mean that God, the Most High, raised to Himself from the confederates what is more than what is in our hands, and that the verse of stoning was raised in wording. Ahmad bin Al-Haitham bin Khalid told us, he said: Abu Ubaid Al-Qasim bin Salam told us, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, on the authority of Abu Lahi’ah, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, she said: Surat Al-Ahzab was equal to two hundred verses during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. When the Mushaf was written, only what is now was recorded from it. Abu Bakr said: So the meaning of this from the words of the Mother of the Believers, Aisha, is that God Almighty raised to him from Surat Al-Ahzab what is more than what we have. I said: This is one of the ways of abrogation, and the discussion of it has been presented in full in Surat Al-Baqarah, and praise be to God. And Zur narrated that he said: Ubayy ibn Ka’b said to me: How many verses do you count in Surat Al-Ahzab? I said: Seventy-three verses. He said: By the One by Whom Ubayy ibn Ka'b swears, it would be equal to Surat Al-Baqarah or longer. We have recited from it the verse of stoning: “The old man and the old woman, if they commit adultery, stone them both. It is a punishment from God. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise.” My father meant that this was part of what was abrogated from the Quran. As for what is narrated that this addition was on a scroll in Aisha’s house and a rooster ate it, it is a fabrication of the atheists and the Rafidis. God the Almighty said: O Prophet, fear God The word i is pronounced with a damma because it is a singular vocative, and the warning is necessary for it. The Prophet is an adjective for any according to grammarians, except for Al-Akhfash, who says: It is a relative clause for any. Makki: A singular noun is not known in Arabic speech as a relative clause for anything. An-Nahhas: This is a mistake according to most grammarians, because the relative clause can only be a sentence. The trick for him in what he said is that since it is an intransitive adjective, it is called a relative clause. This is how the Kufians call the adjective of an indefinite noun a relative clause for it. It is not permissible to put it in the accusative case according to the position according to most grammarians. Al-Mazini permitted it, making it like your saying: O Zayd the elegant, putting the elegant in the accusative case in place of Zayd. Makki: This is an adjective that can be dispensed with, and an adjective of ay that cannot be dispensed with, so it is not appropriate to place it in the accusative case. Also, if the adjective of ay is the vocative in meaning, it is not appropriate to place it in the accusative case. It was narrated that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, he loved the Islam of the Jews: Qurayza, Nadir, and Banu Qaynuqa. Some of them followed him in hypocrisy, so he was gentle with them and honored their young and old. If someone said something ugly, he would overlook it, and he would listen to them. So it was revealed. It was said that it was revealed, according to what al-Wahidi, al-Qushayri, al-Tha’labi, al-Mawardi, and others mentioned, about Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Abu al-A’war Amr ibn Sufyan. They settled in Medina upon Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salus, the head of the hypocrites after Uhud. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had given them security on the condition that they would speak to him. So Abdullah ibn Sa’d ibn Abi Sarh and Ta’mah ibn Ubayraq rose up with them, and they said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while Umar ibn al-Khattab was with him: Refuse to mention our goddesses al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat, and say that they have… Intercession and protection for those who worship it, and we leave you to your Lord. What they said grieved the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So Omar said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, give me permission to kill them. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have given them safety. Omar said: Go out under the curse and wrath of God. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to leave Medina, and this verse was revealed: O Prophet, fear God meaning fear God and do not obey the disbelievers from the people of Mecca, meaning Abu Sufyan, Abu al-A’war, and Ikrimah, and the hypocrites from the people of Medina, meaning Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Tu’mah, and Abdullah ibn Sa’d ibn Abi Sarh, in what you have been forbidden from, and do not incline toward them for God is ever Knowing of their disbelief and Wise in what He does to them. Al-Zamakhshari: It was narrated that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl ibn Abi Jahl, and Abu al-A’war as-Sulami came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) regarding the truce that had been concluded between him and them, and with them stood Abd God ibn Ubayy, Mu’tab ibn Qushayr, and al-Jadd ibn Qays. They said to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Refuse to mention our gods, and he mentioned the report with the same meaning as the previous one, and that the verse was revealed regarding breaking the covenant and abandoning the truce, and do not obey the disbelievers from the people of Mecca and the hypocrites from the people of Medina in what they have asked of you. It was narrated that the people of Mecca called upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to renounce his religion and they would give him half of their wealth and marry his daughter to Shaybah ibn Rabi'ah. The hypocrites of Medina feared that they would kill him if he did not renounce his religion, so this verse was revealed. An-Nahhas said: “And his statement, ‘Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Wise,’ indicates that he was inclined towards them to invite them to Islam. That is, if God, the Almighty, had known that there would be benefit to your inclination towards them, He would not have forbidden you from it, because He is Wise.” Then it was said: The addressee is to him and his nation.
33:2: The Almighty says: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord meaning the Qur'an. It contains a warning against following the rituals of the Age of Ignorance and a command to fight them and oppose them. It also contains evidence for abandoning following opinions despite the existence of a clear text addressing Him and His Ummah: Indeed, God is ever, with what you do, Acquainted. The general reading is with a ta' indicating address, and this is the preferred choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. As-Sulami, Abu Umar and Ibn Abi Ishaq read: They do with a ya' indicating the report. The same is the case in His statement: He is Seeing of what you do (al-Ahzab 33:9). And put your trust in God means depend on Him in all your affairs, for He is the One who protects you and will not harm you if he lets you down.
33:3: And sufficient is God as a Disposer of affairs A protector and a sheikh from the people of Ash-Sham said that a delegation from Thaqeef came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they asked him to let them enjoy Al-Lat for a year - the tyrant that Thaqeef used to worship - and they said: So that the Quraysh may know our status with you. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, understood that and then the verse was revealed: And put your trust in God, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs meaning sufficient for you in what you fear from them. And God is in the nominative case because it is the subject, and Disposer of affairs is in the accusative case as clarification or condition.
33:4: It contains five issues: First - Mujahid said: It was revealed about a man from Quraysh who was called Dhu al-Qalbain the two hearts because of his cunning. He used to say: I have two hearts inside me, and I understand better with each of them than Muhammad. He said: He was from Fihr. Al-Wahidi, Al-Qushayri and others said: It was revealed about Jamil ibn Muammar Al-Fihri, and he was a man who memorized what he heard. The Quraysh said: He would not memorize these things unless he had two hearts. He used to say: I have two hearts, and I understand better with them than Muhammad. When the polytheists were defeated on the day of Badr, along with Jamil ibn Muammar, Abu Sufyan saw him in the caravan with one of his sandals hanging from his hand and the other from his foot. Abu Sufyan said: What is the condition of the people? He said: They were defeated. He said: Why is one of your sandals in your hand and the other on your foot? He said: I did not feel anything except that they were on my feet. Then they knew on that day that if he had two hearts, he would not have forgotten his sandal in his hand. Al-Sahli said: It was Jameel bin Muammar Al-Jumahi, and he is the son of Muammar bin Habib bin Wahb bin Hudhafah bin Jumah, and Jumah’s name was Taym, and he was called the one with two hearts, so the verse was revealed about him, and about him the poet says: How will I stay in the city after Jameel bin Muammar has had his fill of it? I said: This is what Jamil ibn Muammar said. Al-Zamakhshari said: Jamil ibn Asad Al-Fahri. Ibn Abbas said: The reason for it is that some of the hypocrites said: Muhammad has two hearts, because when he was in one thing, he turned to another and then returned to his former state. So they said that about him, and God, the Almighty, denied them. It was also said: It was revealed about Abdullah ibn Khatal. Al-Zuhri and Ibn Hayyan said: It was revealed as an example about Zayd ibn Haritha when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, adopted him. So the meaning is: Just as a man cannot have two hearts, so too can one child be born to two men. An-Nahhas said: This is a weak statement that is not linguistically sound, and it is from the interrupted hadiths of Al-Zuhri, narrated by Muammar from him. It was also said: It is a metaphor for the liar, meaning just as a man cannot have two hearts, so too can the wife of the liar not be his mother until she is safe for him. It was also said: One of the hypocrites would say: I have a heart that commands me to do such and such, and a heart that commands me to do such and such. So the hypocrite has two hearts, so the purpose is to refute hypocrisy. It has been said: Disbelief and belief in God Almighty cannot coexist in one heart, just as two hearts cannot coexist in one cavity. The meaning is: Two opposing beliefs cannot coexist in one heart. The verse as a whole negates things that the Arabs believed in at that time, and informs of the truth of the matter, and God knows best. The second - the heart is a small piece in the shape of a pine cone, which God Almighty created in man and made it a place for knowledge, so the servant can count with it knowledge that is not heard in books, God Almighty writes it in it with the divine script, and records it in it with divine preservation, until he counts it and does not forget anything of it, and it is between two touches, a touch from the angel and a touch from the devil, as the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said. Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, and it has been mentioned previously in Al-Baqarah, and it is the place of thoughts and whispers, the place of disbelief and faith, the place of persistence and repentance, and the path of anxiety and tranquility. The meaning of the verse is that disbelief and faith, guidance and misguidance, repentance and persistence cannot come together in the heart. This is a denial of everything that anyone has imagined in this regard, whether literal or metaphorical, and God knows best. Third - God the Almighty informs us in this verse that no one has two hearts. This is an attack on the hypocrites mentioned above, meaning that it is only one heart, so it either has faith or disbelief, because the degree of hypocrisy is intermediate, so God the Almighty denied it and explained that it is only one heart. Based on this, a person cites this verse whenever he forgets something or is confused, saying as an apology: God has not made for any man two hearts in his chest. Fourth - The Almighty said: And He has not made your wives whom you declare not to be your mothers. This means a man saying to his wife: You are to me like the back of my mother. This is mentioned in Surat Al-Mujadilah, as will be explained later, God willing. Fifth - The Almighty’s saying: And He has not made your adopted sons your sons. The commentators agreed that this was revealed about Zayd ibn Haritha. The imams narrated that Ibn Umar said: We did not call Zayd ibn Haathah anything but Zayd ibn Muhammad until the following verse was revealed: Call them by the names of their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. Zayd, according to what was narrated by Anas ibn Malik and others, was a captive from Syria. He was taken captive by horses from Tihamah. Hakim ibn Hizam ibn Khuwaylid bought him and gave him as a gift to his aunt Khadija. Khadija gave him to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who freed him and adopted him. He stayed with him for a while. Then his uncle and father came seeking to ransom him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them, before the mission: “Give him a choice. If he chooses you, then he is yours without ransom.” The experience of slavery with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was based on his freedom and his people. Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said at that time: O people of Quraysh, bear witness that he is my son, he inherits from me and I inherit from him. He used to go around the circles of Quraysh, bearing witness to that. His uncle and father were pleased with that and left. When his father was taken captive, he used to go around Syria saying: I cried for Zaid and I did not know what he had done, whether he was alive and could be hoped for, or whether his time had come before him. By God, I do not know, and I am asking myself, will the plain or the mountain overwhelm you after I leave? Oh, I wonder! Is there a way back for you in this world? Your return to me is enough for me in this world. The sun reminds me of him when it rises and his memory is displayed when it sets And if the winds blow, his memory stirs. Oh, how long and how great my grief is for him. I will work hard to make the camels walk on the earth and will not ask for roaming or the camels will get tired My life or my death comes to me, for every person will perish, even if hope deceives him. He was informed that he was in Mecca, so he came to him and died there. It was narrated that he came to him and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him the choice as we mentioned and he left. There will come a mention of him and his virtue and honor in his saying: And when Zaid had no longer any need for her, We married her to you (al-Ahzab 33:37), God willing. Zaid was killed by his death in the land of Ash-Sham in the year eight of the Hijra. “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had ordered him in that campaign and said: If Zaid is killed, then Ja’far, and if Ja’far is killed, then Abdullah ibn Rawahah. So the three were killed in that campaign, may God Almighty be pleased with them all. When the report of Zaid and Ja’far’s death reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he wept and said: My two brothers, my comforter, and my confidant.”
33:5: It contains six issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: Call them by the names of their fathers was revealed about Zayd ibn Haritha, as explained above, and in the saying of Ibn Umar: We did not call Zayd ibn Haritha anything but Zayd ibn Muhammad, and it is evidence that adoption was practiced in the pre-Islamic era and in Islam, and people inherited and supported one another by it, until God abrogated that with His saying: Call them by the names of their fathers, that is more just in the sight of God meaning more just. So God lifted the ruling of adoption and prevented the use of its term, and guided with his statement that it is better and more just to attribute a man to his father by lineage. It is said: In the pre-Islamic era, if a man liked a man’s skin and charm, he would take him into his own hands and give him the share of the male children from his inheritance. He would attribute him to him and say, So-and-so, son of so-and-so. An-Nahhas said: This verse abrogates what they were doing regarding adoption, and it is from the abrogation of the Sunnah by the Qur’an. So He ordered that whoever they called should be called to his known father. If he did not have a known father, they should attribute him only to his loyalty. If he did not have a known father, they should say to him, O my brother, meaning in religion. God the Most High said: The believers are but brothers. (al-Hujurat 49:10) Second: If a person attributes a person to his adoptive father, if it was by mistake, meaning that his tongue slipped into it unintentionally, then there is no sin and no blame, because God the Almighty said: {And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred [but] [only] for what your hearts intended.} [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] Similarly, if you attribute a man to someone other than his prophet, and you believe that he is his father, then you are not to be blamed for that, as Qatada said. This does not apply to what is predominantly attributed to adoption, as was the case with Al-Miqdad ibn Amr, for his lineage was predominantly attributed to him, so he was hardly known except as Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad, for Al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth had adopted him during the pre-Islamic period and was known by that name. When the verse was revealed, Al-Miqdad said: I am the son of Amr, and despite that, the general application remained applicable to him. No one in the past has heard of anyone who disobeyed in an absolute manner, even if it was deliberate. The same applies to Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, who was called by Abu Hudhayfah. There are others who adopted and attributed themselves to someone other than their father, and became famous for that and it became predominant. This is in contrast to the case of Zayd ibn Haritha, as it is not permissible to say about him Zayd ibn Muhammad. If someone says it deliberately, he has sinned, as God the Almighty says: But [instead of] what your hearts intended, meaning, then you are to blame, and God knows best. Therefore, He said after that: And God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning, He forgives intentionally and is Merciful in removing the sin of error.
