Third: It has been said that the statement of God, the Blessed and Exalted: And there is no blame upon you for that in which you erred is general, meaning there is no blame upon you for anything in which you erred. The fatwa of Ata’ and many of the scholars was on this: If a man swears not to leave his debtor until he has received his due from him, and he takes from him what he sees as good dinars and finds them to be counterfeit, then he is not liable for anything. Likewise, if someone swears not to greet so-and-so, and he greets him even though he does not know him, then he does not break his oath, because he did not do that intentionally. The ma is in the accusative case in response to ma which is with you erred. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case with an implied subject, and the meaning is: But that for which you will be held accountable is what your hearts intended. Qatada and others said: Whoever attributes a man to someone other than his father, while he mistakenly believes that he is his father, then that is from the things in which God has lifted blame. It has been said that it is to say to him in addressing him: O my son, without straw. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: That is your statement with your mouths. “With your mouths” is an emphasis on the falsehood of the statement, meaning that it is a statement that has no reality in existence. It is only a statement of my tongue. This is like saying: I will walk to you on foot, meaning that you only mean by that charity. This is common, and this meaning has been presented before in more than one place. And God speaks the truth. The truth is an attribute of a deleted source, meaning He speaks the true statement. Guides means He explains, so it is transitive without a preposition. Fifth: The claimants, plural of the claimant, is the one who is claimed to be the son of someone other than his father or claims someone other than his father. The source is the call with the kasra, so God Almighty commanded the claimants to be called back to their fathers for kinship. Whoever is ignorant of that and their lineage is not known is a client and brother in religion. Al-Tabari mentioned that Abu Bakrah read this verse and said: I am one of those whose father is not known, so I am your brother in religion and your client. The narrator said about him: If he had known - by God - that his father was a donkey, he would have claimed to be related to him. The men of hadith say about Abu Bakrah: Nafi’ ibn al-Harith. Sixth: Al-Sahih narrated on the authority of Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas and Abu Bakra, both of whom said: My ears heard it and my heart understood it, Muhammad saying: Whoever claims a father other than his own, knowing that he is not his father, Paradise is forbidden to him. And in the hadith of Abu Dharr, he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: There is no man who knowingly claims to be the father of someone other than his own is guilty of disbelief.
33:6: It contains nine issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves. With this verse, God Almighty removed rulings that were in the early days of Islam, including: “That he, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not pray over a dead person who had a debt. Then, when God granted him conquests, he said: “I have more right to the believers than they have to themselves. So whoever dies while in debt, I am responsible for paying it off. But whoever leaves behind wealth, it is for his heirs.” Narrated by the two Sahihs. They also contain: And whoever among you leaves behind a debt or a loss, I am his protector. Ibn al-Arabi said: Now the situation has been reversed with regard to sins. If they leave behind wealth, the agnates are limited in it, and if they leave behind loss, it is handed over to them. This is the interpretation of the guardianship mentioned in this verse, as explained by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And a warning: There is no perfume after a bride. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: Some of the knowledgeable scholars said that he is more entitled to them than their own selves, because their selves call them to destruction, and he calls them to salvation. Ibn ‘Atiyyah said: This is supported by his statement, may God bless him and grant him peace: I will hold you by your belt from the Fire, and you are rushing into it like a bed. I said: This is a good statement about the meaning of the verse and its interpretation, and the hadith that was mentioned was included by Muslim in his Sahih, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: My example and that of my nation is like that of a man who kindled a fire and the animals and moths began to fall into it, and I held you by your belt while you were rushing into it.” Jabir said something similar. And you escape from my hand. The scholars said: The belt is for the trousers, and the knot is for the lower garment. So if a man wants to hold someone he fears will fall, he takes that place and sleeps. This is an example of the striving of our Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in our salvation, and his eagerness to free us from the destruction that lies ahead of us, as he has more right to us than to themselves. But because of our ignorance of the extent of that and the dominance of our desires over us and the victory of our enemy, the evil eye, over us, we have become more insignificant than a bed and more humiliated than a bed. There is no power or strength except in God, the Most High, the Almighty! It was said: It is more deserving of them, meaning that if he commands something and the soul calls for something else, then the command of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) is more deserving. It was also said: It is more deserving of them, meaning he is more deserving of ruling over the believers and implementing his ruling in themselves, meaning in what they rule for themselves that contradicts his ruling. Second - Some scholars said: The Imam must pay off the debts of the poor from the public treasury, following the example of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as he clearly stated that he must do so when he said: It is upon him to pay it off. Loss, with a fat-ha on the letter ḍād, is the source of da’a, then it was made a name for everything that is about to be lost, such as children and dependents who have no one to support them, and money that has no value. The land was called da’a because it is exposed to loss, and the plural is da’a with a kasra on the letter ḍād. Third: The Almighty’s saying: And his wives are their mothers. God the Almighty honored the wives of His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) by making them the mothers of the believers, meaning in the obligation of respect, kindness, and reverence, and the prohibition of marriage for men and their veiling, may God be pleased with them, unlike mothers. It was said: Since their compassion for them was like the compassion of mothers, they were given the status of mothers. Then this motherhood does not entail inheritance like adoptive motherhood, and it is permissible to marry their daughters, and they are not considered sisters to people. The number of the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) will come in the verse of choice, God willing. People differed as to whether they are the mothers of men and women or the mothers of men only. There are two opinions: Al-Sha’bi narrated on the authority of Masruq on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that a woman said to her: O slave girl. She said to her: I am not your mother, I am only the mother of your men. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This is correct. I said: There is no benefit in limiting the permissibility to men only and not women. What appears to me is that they are the mothers of both men and women, out of respect for their rights over men and women. This is indicated by the opening verse: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves. This necessarily includes both men and women, and this is indicated by the hadith of Abu Hurayrah and Jabir. Thus, the Almighty’s statement: and his wives are their mothers refers to all of them. Then, in the Mushaf of Ubayy ibn Ka’b, it says: and his wives are their mothers and he is a father to them. Ibn Abbas read: from themselves and he is a father to them. All of this weakens what Masruq narrated, if it is authentic, in terms of preference. If it is not authentic, then its use as evidence for specificity is invalid, and we remain with the original principle, which is the generality that comes first to understanding, and God knows best. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the ordinance of God than the believers and the emigrants. It was said that by the believers he meant the Ansar, and by the emigrants he meant the Quraysh. There are two opinions on this: One of them: It abrogates the inheritance by emigration. Saeed narrated on the authority of Qatadah who said: It was revealed in Surat al-Anfal 8:And those who believed and did not emigrate - you have no guardianship over them at all until they emigrate. [Al-Anfal, 72], so the Muslims inherited by emigration. So a Muslim Bedouin did not inherit anything from his Muslim emigrant relative until he emigrated. Then that was abrogated in this surah by His saying: And those of kinship are nearer to one another. The second: That it abrogates the inheritance by oath and brotherhood in religion. Hisham bin Urwah narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of Al-Zubayr: And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the ordinance of God. That is because when we Quraysh came to Madinah, we came without any wealth, and we found the Ansar to be the best of brothers, so we made them brothers, so they made us brothers and made them brothers. So Abu Bakr made Kharijah bin Zaid brothers. And I made Ka'b ibn Malik a brother, and I came and found that the weapon had weighed him down. By God, he had died and had not inherited this world except for me, until God Almighty revealed this verse, and we returned to our inheritance. It was confirmed from Urwah that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made Az-Zubayr and Ka'b ibn Malik brothers. Ka'b inherited on the day of Uhud, and Az-Zubayr came leading him by the reins of his mount. If Ka'b had died on that day, suffering from laughter and wind, Az-Zubayr would have inherited him. Then God Almighty revealed: And those of kinship are nearer to one another in the Book of God. So God Almighty made clear that kinship is nearer to an oath, so the inheritor by oath was left and they inherited by kinship. The discussion of the inheritance of those of kin has already passed in Al-Anfal. His statement: in the Book of God may mean the Qur'an, and it may mean the Preserved Tablet in which He decreed the affairs of His creation. And among the believers is connected to most near, not to His statement: and those of kinship by consensus, because that would have required a specification to some of the believers, and there is no disagreement about its generality. This is the solution to its difficulty, as Ibn al-Arabi said. An-Nahhas said: And those of kinship have more right to one another in the ordinance of God than the believers and the emigrants. It is possible that of the believers is connected to those of kinship, and the meaning would be: And those of kinship among the believers and the emigrants. It is also possible that the meaning is: And those of kinship have more right to one another in the ordinance of God, except for what is permissible for the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to be called Mothers of the Believers. And God knows best. Fifth: There is a difference of opinion about whether they are like mothers in being a mahram and it is permissible to look at them, in two aspects: First: They are a mahram and it is not forbidden to look at them. Second: Looking at them is forbidden because the prohibition of marrying them was only to preserve the right of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) over them, and part of preserving his right was the prohibition of looking at them. And because when Aisha may God be pleased with her wanted a man to enter upon her, she would order her sister Asma to breastfeed him so that he would become a son to her sister through breastfeeding, and thus he would become a mahram and it is permissible to look at them. As for those whom the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divorced during his lifetime, there is a difference of opinion about the establishment of this prohibition for them in three aspects: One of them: This sanctity was established for them in order to give priority to the sanctity of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The second: This is not established for them, rather they are like all other women because the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, established their infallibility and said: My wives in this world are my wives in the Hereafter. Third: If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had intercourse with her, her sanctity and marriage were established, even if he divorced her, in order to preserve his sanctity and protect his privacy. If he did not have intercourse with her, this sanctity was not established for her. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, intended to stone a woman whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had divorced and then married, but she said: Why is this, when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not impose a veil on me, nor was I called the Mother of the Believers? So Umar, may God be pleased with him, refrained from doing so. Sixth: Some people said: It is not permissible to call the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, a father, because God Almighty said: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men. But it is said: Like a father to the believers, as He said: I am to you in the position of a father, the most knowledgeable of you… The hadith was narrated by Abu Dawud. What is correct is that it is permissible to say that he is a father to the believers, i.e. in sanctity. The Almighty’s statement: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men means in lineage, and this will come. Ibn Abbas read: of themselves, and he is a father to them and his wives. Umar heard this reading and disapproved of it and said: Recite it, boy. He said: It is in my father’s copy of the Qur’an. He went to him and asked him, and my father said to him: The Qur’an distracted me, and you were distracted by bargaining in the markets. He was harsh with Umar. It has been said regarding the statement of Lot, peace be upon him, These are my daughters (al-Hijr 15:71) that he only meant the believing women, i.e. marry them, and this has been mentioned previously. Seventh: Some people said: His daughters are not called sisters of the believers, nor are their maternal uncles called maternal uncles and aunts of the believers. Al-Shafi’i, may God be pleased with him, said: Al-Zubayr married Asma’ bint Abi Bakr Al-Siddiq, who was the sister of Aisha, and he did not say she was the aunt of the believers. Some people stated this and said: Mu’awiyah is the maternal uncle of the believers, meaning in terms of sanctity, not in terms of lineage. Eighth: The Almighty’s statement: {Except that you do to your guardians a good deed} meaning kindness in life and a will at death, meaning that this is permissible. This was stated by Qatada, Al-Hasan, and Ata’. Muhammad ibn Al-Hanafiyyah said: It was revealed regarding the permission of a will for a Jew or a Christian, meaning that this should be done with a guardian or relative, even if the latter is a disbeliever. The polytheist is a guardian by lineage but not by religion, so a will should be made for him. The scholars differed as to whether to make a disbeliever a guardian. Some permitted it, others forbade it. Some referred the matter to the ruler, including Malik may God have mercy on him. Mujahid, Ibn Zayd, and Al-Rummani held that the meaning is: to your guardians among the believers. The wording of the verse supports this view. The generalization of the guardian is also good, and guardianship by lineage does not exclude a disbeliever, but rather encourages him to be shown love as a guardian of Islam. Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: That was written in the Book. The Book has two possible meanings mentioned previously in the Book of God. And written comes from your saying I wrote the Book if you recorded it in lines. Qatada said: That is, it is written with God Almighty that no disbeliever shall inherit a Muslim. Qatada said: And in some readings it was written with God. Al-Qurazi said: That was in the Torah.
33:7: God Almighty says: And when We took from the prophets their covenant meaning their pledge to fulfill what they were entrusted with, and that some of them would give good tidings to others and confirm each other, meaning it was written down when God wrote what would happen, and when God Almighty took covenants from the prophets and from you O Muhammad and from Noah and Abraham and Moses and Jesus son of Mary and He only singled out these five even though they were included in the group of prophets to give them preference. It was said: because they are the owners of the laws and books, and the resolute ones among the messengers and the leaders of the nations. It is possible that this is an exaltation in severing the alliance between the Muslims and the disbelievers, meaning this is something in which the laws did not differ, meaning the laws of the prophets, peace and blessings be upon them, meaning that at the beginning of Islam there was inheritance through migration, a confirmed reason in the religion, then they inherited through kinship with faith, which is a reason and a plot. As for inheritance between a believer and a disbeliever, it was not in the religion of any of the prophets from whom covenants were taken, so do not be lenient in religion and do not cooperate with the disbelievers. And its equivalent is: He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah - to His saying - and do not be divided therein (al-Shura 42:13). And whoever abandons division in religion abandons the friendship of the disbelievers. And it was said: meaning the Prophet is closer to the believers than they are to themselves. This was written in the Book and covenants were taken from the prophets. And We took from them a firm covenant meaning a strong and great pledge to fulfill what they committed to in conveying the message, and that some of them would be truthful to others. The covenant is the oath to God Almighty, so the second covenant is a confirmation of the covenant with the oath. It was said: The first is the acknowledgment of God Almighty, and the second is in the matter of prophethood. Similar to this is the saying of God Almighty: “And when God took a covenant from the prophets, ‘Whatever I have given you of the Book and wisdom and then there comes to you a Messenger confirming what is with you, you must believe in him and support him.’ He said, ‘Have you acknowledged and taken upon yourself My covenant?’” (Al Imran 3:81) The verse means that He took from them that they should declare that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, should declare that there is no prophet after him, and He mentioned Muhammad first. Qatada narrated on the authority of Al Hassan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of God was asked about the Almighty’s saying: And when We took a covenant from the prophets, and from you and from Noah, he said: I was the first of them in creation and the last of them in resurrection. Mujahid said: This was in the back of Adam, peace and blessings be upon him.
33:8: The Almighty’s saying: To question the truthful about their truthfulness has four aspects: One of them: to ask the prophets about their conveying of the message to their people, as narrated by Al-Naqqash. In this there is a warning: A] If the prophets are asked, then how about others? Second: To ask the prophets about what their people answered them, as narrated by Ali bin Issa. Third: To ask the prophets, peace be upon them, about fulfilling the covenant that he took from them, as narrated by Ibn Shajarah. Fourth: To ask the truthful mouths about the sincere hearts. In the revelation: Then We will surely question those to whom messages were sent, and We will surely question the messengers. (al-A’raf 7:6) It has been said before: The benefit of asking them is to rebuke the disbelievers, as God Almighty said: Did you say to the people? (al-Ma’idah 5:116) And He has prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment. It is the torment of Hell.
33:9: That is, the Battle of the Trench, the Confederates, and Banu Qurayzah. It was a difficult situation followed by blessings, prosperity, and happiness. It included many rulings and dazzling, precious verses. We will mention from that, with the help of God Almighty, what is sufficient in ten issues: First: There is a difference of opinion about which year it was. Ibn Ishaq said: It was in Shawwal of the fifth year. Ibn Wahb and Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik, may God have mercy on him: The Battle of the Trench was in the fourth year, and it was on the same day between her and Banu Qurayzah, and there were four years between Banu Qurayzah and al-Nadir. Ibn Wahb said: He heard Malik say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered fighting from Medina, and that is the saying of God the Almighty: When they came upon you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes turned away and the hearts reached to the throats. He said that on the day of the Trench. The Quraysh came from here, the Jews from here, and the Najdis from here. Malik means: Those who came from above them were Banu Qurayzah, and from below them were the Quraysh and Ghatafan. The reason for that was that a group of Jews, including Kinanah ibn al-Rabi’ ibn Abi al-Haqiq, Salam ibn Abi al-Haqiq, Salam ibn Mishkam, Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadriyyah, Hudhah ibn Qays, and Abu Ammar from Banu Wa’il, and they were all Jews, were the ones who formed the parties, incited, and gathered. They went out with a group of Banu al-Nadir and a group of Banu Wa’il, and they came to Mecca and called for war against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they promised them from themselves the help of whoever volunteered for that, so the people of Mecca responded to that, then the aforementioned Jews went out to Ghatafan. So he invited them to do the same and they responded. So the Quraysh went out led by Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and the Ghatafan went out with their leader Uyaynah ibn Hisn ibn Hudhayfah ibn Badr al-Fazari over the Fazara, al-Harith ibn Auf al-Murri over the Banu Murrah, and Mas`ud ibn Rukhaila over the Ashja`. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) heard of their gathering and going out, he consulted his companions. Salman advised him to dig the trench and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) accepted his advice. The Muhajirun said that day: Salman is from us. The Ansar said: Salman is from us! The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Salman is from us, the people of the house. The trench was the first battle Salman witnessed with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he was a free man at that time. He said: O Messenger of God, when we were surrounded, we would dig a trench. The Muslims worked hard in the trench, but the hypocrites retreated and began to sneak away. So verses from the Quran were revealed about them, mentioned by Ibn Ishaq and others. Whoever among the Muslims had completed his share would return to another, until the trench was completed, and in it were clear signs and indications of the prophethood. I said: In what we mentioned of this report there is jurisprudence, which is: The second: The Sultan consults his companions and his confidants in the matter of fighting. This has already been mentioned in Al Imran and An-Naml. It includes fortifying oneself against the enemy with what is safe from means and using them. This has already been mentioned in more than one place. It includes that the digging of the trench is to be divided among the people, so whoever has finished helps whoever has not finished, so the Muslims are one hand against whoever is not them. In Al Bukhari and Muslim, “On the authority of Al Bara’ bin Azib, he said: When the day of the Confederates and the trench of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took place, I saw him carrying dirt from the trench until the dust covered the skin of his stomach from me, and he had a lot of hair. Then I heard him chanting the words of Ibn Rawahah and saying: O God, if it were not for You, we would not have been guided, given charity, or prayed. So send down tranquility upon us and plant firmly our feet if we meet them.” As for the verses it contains, they are: Third: Al-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abu Sakina, a man of the editors, on the authority of a man of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered the digging of the trench, a rock appeared and prevented them from digging. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) stood up, took the pickaxe, and placed his cloak towards the trench and said: “And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth” (Al-An`am: 115), the verse. A third of the rock flew away while Salman the Persian was standing watching. A flash of lightning flashed with the strike of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then he struck the second time and said: And the verse has been fulfilled. The other third flew away. A flash of lightning flashed and Salman saw it. Then he struck the third time and said: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth (Al-An`am: 115), the verse. The remaining third flew away. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out, took his cloak, and sat down. Salman said: O Messenger of God, I saw you when you struck! You do not strike a strike except that there is a flash of lightning with it. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Did you see that, Salman? He said: Yes, by the One Who sent you with the truth, O Messenger of God! He said: When I struck the first strike, the cities of Kisra and those around it and many cities were shown to me until I saw them with my own eyes.” - Someone present said to him: From his companions, O Messenger of God, ask God to open it for us and grant us their lands as booty and destroy their country by our hands. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then I struck the second blow and the cities of Caesar and what was around them were shown to me until I saw them with my own eyes. They said, O Messenger of God, ask God Almighty to open it for us and grant us their children as booty and destroy their country by our own hands. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then I struck the third blow and the cities of Abyssinia and what was around them were shown to me until I saw them with my own eyes. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said at that time: Leave the Abyssinians as long as they leave you and leave the Turks as long as they leave you. It was also narrated on the authority of Al-Baraa’ who said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered us to dig the trench, we were shown a rock that the pickaxe could not reach. We complained about that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came, threw down his garment, took the pickaxe, and said: ‘In the name of God.’ He struck one blow and broke a third of the rock. Then he said: ‘God is Great. I have been given the keys to Syria. By God, I can see its red palaces from where I am now.’ Then he struck another blow and said: ‘In the name of God.’ He broke another third. Then he said: ‘God is Great. I have been given the keys to Persia. By God, I can see the white palace of Mada’in.’ Then he struck three times and said: ‘In the name of God.’ He broke the rock and said: ‘God is Great. I have been given the keys to Yemen. By God, I can see the gate of Sana’a.’” Sahih Abu Muhammad Abd al-Haqq Fourth: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, finished digging the trench, the Quraysh advanced with ten thousand men, including those from Kinana and Tihamah. Ghatafan advanced with those from Najd, who encamped beside Uhud. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims went out until they encamped at the back of Sala’, with three thousand men, and they struck their camp, and the trench was between them and the polytheists. He appointed Ibn Umm Maktum over Medina, according to Ibn Shihab. The enemy of God, Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Nadri, went out and came to Ka’b ibn Asad al-Qurazi, who was the one who held the contract of Banu Qurayzah and their leader. He had made a truce with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and concluded a covenant with him. When Ka’b ibn Asad heard Huyayy ibn Akhtab, he closed the door of his fortress and refused to open it for him. He said to him, Open for me, my brother. He said to him, “I will not open for you, for you are an ill-omened man. You call me to oppose Muhammad, and I have made a covenant with him and I have not seen from him anything but loyalty and truthfulness, so I will not break what is between me and him.” Huyayy said, Open for me until… I will talk to you and leave you. He said: I will not. He said: You are only afraid that I will eat your grass. Ka'b became angry and opened the door for him. He said: O Ka'b! I have come to you with the glory of the age. I have come to you with the Quraysh and its leaders and with Ghatafan and its chiefs who have agreed to exterminate Muhammad and those with him. Ka'b said to him: By God, you have come to me with the humiliation of the age and with no rain. Woe to you, O Huyayy! Leave me, for I will not do what you invite me to do. So Huyayy kept promising and deceiving Ka’b until he returned to him and made a pact with him to abandon Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions and to go with them. Huyayy ibn Akhtab said to him: If the Quraysh and Ghatafan go back, I will come to you with those Jews who are with me. When the report of Ka’b and Huyayy reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he sent Sa’d ibn Ubadah, the chief of the Khazraj, and Sa’d ibn Mu’ad, the chief of the Aws, and sent with them Abdullah ibn Rawahah and Khawwat ibn Jubayr. The Messenger of God said to them: “Go to Banu Qurayzah. If what was said to us is true, then speak to us gently and do not weaken the people’s resolve. But if it is a lie, then tell the people about it openly.” So they went until they reached them and found them doing the worst of what was said to them about them. They spoke ill of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: He has no covenant with us. Sa’d ibn Mu’adh cursed them and they cursed him. There was a sharpness in him, so Sa’d ibn Ubadah said to him: Stop cursing them, for what is between us and them… Moreover, Sa`d and Sa`d came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) in a group of Muslims and said: `Udl and al-Qarah are treacherously attacking the companions of al-Raji`, Khubayb and his companions. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: `Rejoice, O Muslims!’ At that time, the calamity became great and fear intensified. The enemy of the Muslims approached them from above, meaning from above the valley from the east, and from below them from the valley from the west, until they had bad thoughts about God. The hypocrites revealed much of what they had been hiding. Some of them said: Our houses are vulnerable, so let us return to them, for we fear for them. Among those who said that was Aws ibn Qayzi. Some of them said: Muhammad promises us that he will open the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar, yet one of us today does not feel safe going to the toilet! Among those who said that was Mu'tab bin Qushair, one of the sons of Amr bin Awf. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that the Muslims were in dire straits. He sent to Uyaynah bin Hisn al-Fazari and to al-Harith bin Awf al-Murri, who were the leaders of Ghatafan, and gave them a third of the fruits of Medina so that they would leave with those of Ghatafan who were with them and abandon Quraysh and return with their people from them. This statement was a bargain and not a contract. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw that they had repented and were satisfied, he went to Sa'id bin Mu'adh and Sa'd bin Ubadah and mentioned that to them and consulted them. They said: O Messenger of God, is this something you like, so we do it for you, or something God has commanded you, so we listen to it and obey it, or something you do for us? He said: Rather, it is something I will do for you. By God, I would not do it except because I saw that the Arabs had shot you with a single bow. Saad bin Muadh said to him: O Messenger of God, we and these people were polytheists, worshipping idols. We did not worship God nor did we know Him. They never hoped to obtain any fruit from us except by buying or hosting. But when God honored us with Islam, guided us to it, and made us strong through you, we give them our money! By God, we will not give them anything but the sword until God judges between us and them!! The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was pleased with that and said: You can do that. He said to Uyaynah and Al-Harith: Support us, for you have nothing with us but the sword. Saad took the document, which did not contain the testimony, so he erased it. Fifth: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims remained as they were, and the polytheists were besieging them and there was no fighting between them, except that the horsemen of the Quraysh, Amr ibn Abd Wudd al-Amri from Banu Amir ibn Luay, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, Hubayrah ibn Abi Wahb, and Dirar ibn al-Khattab al-Fihri, who were the horsemen of the Quraysh and their bravest, advanced until they stopped at the trench. When they saw it, they said: This is a trick that the Arabs had never plotted. Then they headed for a narrow place in the trench, and they struck their horses and they charged in with them. They crossed the trench and were between the trench and Sala’. Ali ibn Abi Talib went out with a group of Muslims until they took the gap from which they had charged in, and the horsemen advanced towards them. Amr ibn Abd Wudd had been wounded on the day of Badr, so he did not witness anyone. On the day of the trench, he wanted to see where he was, so when he and his horses stopped, he called out: Who will fight in a duel? Then Ali ibn Abi Talib came out to him and said: O Amr, as we have heard, you made a covenant with God that if you are invited to one of two options, you will take one of them. He said: Yes. He said: Then I invite you to God and Islam. He said: I have no need for that. He said: Then I invite you to Al-Bazzaz. He said: O son of my brother, by God I do not want to kill you because of what happened between me and your father. Ali said to him: And by God I also want to kill you. Amr ibn Abd Wudd became angry and got off his horse, hamstrung it and headed towards Ali. They fought and fought and quarreled between them until they were separated. No sooner had the quarrel settled than Ali was seen on Amr’s chest, cutting off his head. When his companions realized that Ali had killed him, they rushed the gap with their horses, defeated and fleeing. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said about that: Nasr al-Hajar from the foolishness of his opinion and Nasrat the religion of Muhammad with a strike I fought him and left him sprawling like a tree trunk between your hills and valleys. I refrained from wearing his clothes even if I were the one who was dripping with the adultery of my clothes Do not think that God will let down His religion and His Prophet, O group of parties. Ibn Hisham said: Most scholars of the biography doubt Ali’s claim. Ibn Hisham said: Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl threw down his spear that day while fleeing from Amr, so Hassan ibn Thabit said about that: Flee and throw us your spear, perhaps you are Akram, you did not do it And you will be like the enemy of shadows, unless you deviate from the norm. You did not find your back comfortable, as if your back was the back of a pony Ibn Hisham said: Far’al is a young hyena. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, was in the fortress of Bani Haritha, and Umm Sa’d ibn Mu’adh was wearing a shortened shield from which his arm had protruded, and in his hand was his spear, and he was saying: Stay a little while and catch up with the battle. There is no harm in death if it is the appointed time. On that day, Saad bin Muadh was shot with an arrow that cut off his eyelids. There is disagreement about who shot it. Some say it was shot by Hubban bin Qais bin Al-Arqa, one of the Banu Amir bin Luay. When he hit him, he said to him: Take this, I am the son of Al-Arqa. Saad said to him: May God make your face sweat in the fire. It is also said that the one who shot him was Khafajah bin Asim bin Habban. It is also said that the one who shot him was Abu Usamah Al-Jashmi, an ally of Banu Makhzum. Hassan had a funny story with Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib that day, mentioned by Ibn Ishaq and others. Safiyyah bint Abdul Muttalib may God be pleased with her said: “On the day of the Confederates, we were in the fortress of Hassan ibn Thabit, and Hassan was with us with the women and children, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions were at the throats of the enemy and could not leave us. Suddenly, a Jew started circling, so I said to Hassan: ‘Reveal this verse and kill him.’ He said: ‘I am not the one for this, O daughter of Abdul Muttalib!’ So I took a pole and went down from the fortress and killed him. I said: ‘O Hassan, go down and loot him.’ Nothing prevented me from looting him except that he was a man. So he said: ‘I have no need for his loot, O daughter of Abdul Muttalib!’ So I went down and looted him.” Abu Omar ibn Abdul Barr said: A group of biographers denied this about Hassan and said: If Hassan had any cowardice, I would not have described them. He would have satirized those he used to satirize during the pre-Islamic and Islamic periods, and he would have satirized his son Abdul Rahman with this, for he often satirized people, from the Arab poets such as Al-Najashi and others. Sixth: Nu`aym ibn Mas`ud ibn `Amir al-Ashja`i came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of God, I have become Muslim, but my people do not know of my Islam. So order me as you wish.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, “There is only one man from Ghatafan. If you were to go out and abandon us, if you could, it would be more beloved to us than your remaining with us. So go out, for war is deception.” Nu`aym ibn Mas`ud went out until he came to Banu Qurayzah—who had been their companion in the pre-Islamic period—and said, O Banu Qurayzah, you know my love for you and the special relationship between me and you. They said, Say, for you are not accused by us. He said to them, “The Quraysh and Ghatafan are not like you. The country is your country, and your wealth, children, and women are yours. The Quraysh and Ghatafan have come to fight Muhammad and his companions, and you have supported them against him. If they see a chance, they will seize it. But if it is not that, they will return to their country and leave you alone with the man, for you have no power over him. Do not fight with the people until…” Take a pledge from them. Then he went out until he came to the Quraysh and said to them: I know them and my friendship with you, O people of Ali. They said: We will do so. He said: You know that the Jews of Mash'ar regretted what happened in their abandonment of Muhammad and they sent to him: We regret what we did. Would it please you if we take from the Quraysh and Ghatafan some of their noblemen and give them to you so that you may strike off their necks and then we will be with you against what remains of them until we eradicate them? Then he came to Ghatafan and said the same thing. When it was Saturday night, and that was the doing of God Almighty for His Messenger and the believers, Abu Sufyan sent to Banu Qurayzah Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl with a group of Quraysh and Ghatafan saying to them: We are not in a place of settlement, the hooves and the hoof have perished, so go out tomorrow morning to fight until we fight Muhammad. They sent to them: Today is Saturday, and you know what happened to us who transgressed on the Sabbath. Despite that, we will not fight with you until you give us a hostage. When the messenger returned with that, they said: By God, Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud has told the truth. They sent the messengers back to them and said: By God, we will never give you a hostage. Come out with us if you wish, otherwise there will be no covenant between us. Banu Qurayzah said: By God, Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud has told the truth. God disappointed them, and their word became divided. God sent against them a violent wind on a very cold night, and the wind began to overturn their vessels and tip their cooking pots over. Seventh: “When the report of their disagreement reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he sent Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman to bring him report of them. He came to them and hid in their midst and heard Abu Sufyan saying: ‘O people of Quraysh, let each man recognize his companion.’ Hudhayfah said: ‘So I took the hand of my companion and said: Who are you?’ He said: ‘I am so-and-so.’ Then Abu Sufyan said: ‘Woe to you, O people of Quraysh! By God, you have not become a permanent residence. The mounts and hoofs have perished, and Banu Qurayzah have betrayed us. We have encountered from this wind what you see. Our buildings cannot hold together, our pots cannot stand, and our fires cannot be set up. So depart, for I am departing.’ He jumped on a group and the rope on his hand had not been loosened until he was standing. Hudhayfah said: ‘Had it not been for the covenant of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he sent me, in which he said to me: ‘Go to the people and find out what they are up to and do not say anything,’ I would have killed him with an arrow. Then I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they were departing and found him standing praying in a cloak belonging to one of the His women are boilers - Ibn Hisham said: boilers are a type of thing from Yemen - so I told him and he praised God. I said: This hadith of Hudhayfah is mentioned in Sahih Muslim, and it contains great verses. It was narrated by Jarir on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of Ibrahim Al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, who said: “We were with Hudhayfah and a man said: If I had lived to see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, I would have fought with him and done well. Hudhayfah said: You would have done that! I saw us with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of the Confederates, and a strong wind and cold caught us, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Is there not a man who will bring me report of the people, so that God may make him with me on the Day of Resurrection? We remained silent, and none of us answered him. Then he said: Is there not a man who will bring us report of the people, so that God may make him with me on the Day of Resurrection? So we kept silent and no one answered him. He said: “Get up, Hudhayfah, and bring us report of the people.” I had no choice but to get up when he called me by my name. He said: Go and bring me report of the people and do not frighten them against me. When I turned away from him, it was as if I were walking in a bathhouse until I reached them. I saw Abu Sufyan praying his back by the fire, so I put an arrow in the bow and wanted to shoot it, but I remembered the words of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Do not frighten them against me, for if I shot it, I would have hit him. So I returned walking in something like a bathhouse. When I came to him and told him the report of the people and finished, I decided. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) dressed me in an extra cloak that he was wearing when he prayed. I remained asleep until morning. When I was hit, he said: Get up, Noman. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) woke up and the confederates had gone, he returned to Medina and the Muslims laid down their weapons. Gabriel (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to him in the form of Dihya ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi, wearing a piece of brocade. He said to him: O Muhammad, if you are… You have laid down your weapons, but the angels have not laid down their weapons. God commands you to go out to Banu Qurayzah, and I will advance towards them and shake their fortresses. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded them: Eighth: A crier announced: No one should pray Asr except in Banu Qurayzah. Some people feared missing the time, so they prayed without Banu Qurayzah. Others said: “We will not pray Asr except where the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded us, even if the time is missed.” He said: “He did not criticize either of the two groups. In this, there is jurisprudence that confirms the opinion of the diligent scholars.” Its explanation has already been mentioned in the chapter on the Prophets. When Sa`d ibn Mu`adh was struck by an arrow, he supplicated to his Lord, saying: “O God, if You have spared any of the war against Quraysh, then spare me for it, for there are no people I would rather fight than a people who denied Your Messenger and expelled him. O God, if You have put an end to war between us and them, then make it a martyrdom for me, and do not let me die until an eye is comforted in Banu Qurayzah.” Ibn Wahb narrated from Malik, who said: “It reached me that Sa`d ibn Mu`adh passed by Aisha may God be pleased with her and some other women with her in a tall roof. He was wearing a tight-fitting coat with the sleeves rolled up, and there were traces of yellowness on it, and he was reciting: Stay a little while and you will realize the battle. There is no harm in death if the time comes. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: I am not afraid that Sa`d will be injured today except in his extremities. So he was injured in his ankle. Ibn Wahb and Ibn al-Qasim narrated on the authority of Malik that Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: I have never seen a man more handsome than Sa`d ibn Mu`adh, except for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he was injured in his ankle, and then he said: O God, if the war against Qurayzah has left nothing of his life, then take me to You, and if a remnant of him remains, then keep me alive so that I may fight with Your Messenger against his enemies. So when he ruled over Banu Qurayzah, he died, and the people rejoiced and said: We hope that his prayer has been answered. Ninth: “When the Muslims went out to Banu Qurayzah, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave the banner to Ali ibn Abi Talib, and appointed Ibn Umm Maktum as his successor in Medina. Ali and a group with him rose up until they reached Banu Qurayzah and fought them. They heard them cursing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ali turned back to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: O Messenger of God, do not go to them. He approached him and said to him: I think you heard them cursing me. If they saw me, they would stop doing that. He rushed to them and when they saw him, they stopped. He said to them: You have broken the covenant, O brothers of the monkeys. God has made you His brother and has brought down His punishment upon you. They said: I was not ignorant, O Muhammad, so do not act ignorantly towards us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended and besieged them for twenty-odd days. Their master Ka’b offered them three options to choose from whichever they wanted: Either they submit to Islam and follow Muhammad in what he brought, and they would submit. He said: And protect your wealth, women, and children, for by God, you know that you will find it written in your book, or they will kill their children.” And their women, then they advance and fight until they die, the last one of them. Or they attack the Muslims on Saturday night while they are at peace and kill them. They said to him: As for Islam, we will not submit to it nor will we violate the rulings of the Torah, and as for killing our sons and women, what is their reward, the poor ones among us, that we kill them while we do not transgress on the Sabbath? Then they sent to Abu Lubaba, and they were allies of Banu Amr ibn Auf and the rest of the Aws. He came to them and they gathered their sons, their livestock and their men to him and said to him: O Abu Lubaba, do you think we should submit to the rule of Muhammad? He said: Yes, and he pointed to his throat - it is slaughter if you do it. Then Abu Lubabah regretted it immediately and realized that he had betrayed God and His Messenger and that it was a matter that God would not conceal from His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he set out for Madinah and did not return to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He tied himself to a pole and swore that he would not leave his place until God accepted his repentance. His wife would untie him at the time of every prayer. Ibn Uyaynah and others said: The verse was revealed about him: O you who have believed, do not betray God and the Messenger or betray your trusts (al-Anfal 8:27). And he swore that he would never enter the land of Banu Qurayzah, a place where he had committed a sin. When the report of Abu Lubabah’s actions reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: If he came to me, I would ask forgiveness for him, but since he did what he did, I will not release him until God Almighty releases him. So God Almighty revealed concerning Abu Lubabah: And others have acknowledged their sins (al-Tawbah 9:102). When the Qur’an was revealed concerning him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his release. When morning came, Banu Qurayzah submitted to the judgment of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Aws rushed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: “O Messenger of God, you know that they are our allies, and you have helped Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul with Banu Nadir, allies of the Khazraj. So our share will not be more detrimental or lesser in your view than the share of others, for they are our clients.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: O people of Aws, are you not pleased that a man from among you should rule over them? They said: Yes. He said: “That was up to Sa’d ibn Mu’adh, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had pitched a tent for him in the mosque.” To visit him soon after his illness from the wound he sustained in the Battle of the Trench. So he ruled concerning them that the fighters should be killed, the children and women should be taken captive, and their wealth should be divided. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: You have ruled concerning them by the grace of God Almighty from above seven heavens. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that they should be taken out to a place in the market place of Medina today - at the time of Ibn Ishaq - and trenches were dug there. Then, peace be upon him, he ordered that their necks should be struck off in those trenches. On that day, Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka’b ibn Asad were killed. They were the leaders of the people, and they were between six hundred and seven hundred. Huyayy was wearing a white robe that he had torn on every side, the size of a fingertip, fingertip by fingertip, so that it would not be stolen. When he looked at the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he was brought with his hands bound around his neck with a rope, he said: By God, I do not blame myself for my enmity towards you. But he who lets God down will be let down Then he said: O people, there is no harm in the command of God, the Book, the Predestination, and the epic battle that was written for the Children of Israel. Then he sat down and his head was struck off, and one of their women was killed, and she was his daughter, the wife of Al-Hakam Al-Qurazi, who threw the millstone on Khallad bin Suwaid and killed him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered the killing of all those who had hair and left those who did not. Atiyah Al-Qurazi was among those who did not have hair, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spared him, and he is mentioned among the Companions. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gave the children of Az-Zubayr ibn Batta to Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, but Abdur-Rahman ibn Az-Zubayr spared them and converted to Islam, leaving behind some companions. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) also gave Rifa’ah ibn Samu’l Al-Qurazi to Umm Al-Mundhir, Salma bint Qays, the sister of Sulait ibn Qays of Banu An-Najjar, who used to pray facing both Qiblahs. Rifa’ah converted to Islam, leaving behind some companions. The narration of Ibn Wahb and Ibn Al-Qasim from Malik is that he said: Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas came to Ibn Batta, who had a hand in his hand, and said: I ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) to give you the hand that you have with me. He said: This is what a generous person does to a generous person. Then he said: How can a man who has no children or family live? Thabit came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) gave him his children and family. Then he came and informed him. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: How can a man who has no money live? Then Thabit came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and asked for him. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) gave him his money. The Prophet returned to him and informed him. He said: What happened to Ibn Abi Al-Haqiq, whose face was like a Chinese mirror? He said: He was killed. He said: What did the two councils do, meaning Banu Ka'b ibn Qurayzah and Banu Amr ibn Qurayzah? He said: They were killed. He said: What did the two groups do? He said: We were killed. He said: I absolve myself from responsibility and I will never find a bucket to water the palm trees again. So join me with them. He came to kill him, but he killed him. The hand that Ibn Bata had with Thabit was that he captured him on the day of Bu'ath, so he cut off his forelock and set him free. Tenth: God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) divided the wealth of Banu Qurayzah, giving three shares to the horseman and one share to the foot soldier. It has also been said that one share is for the horseman and one share for the foot soldier. The Muslims had thirty-six horses at that time. From their captives, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) acquired Rayhanah, one of the spoils of war, between Amr ibn Janafah and Amr ibn Qurayzah. It remained with him until he died (peace and blessings of God be upon him). It has been said that the spoils of Qurayzah were the first spoils that were divided between the horseman and the foot soldier, and the first spoils to which one-fifth was made. It was previously mentioned that the first of that was during the expedition of Abdullah ibn Jahsh, and God knows best. Abu Omar said: The refinement of that is that the spoils of Qurayzah were the first spoils to which one-fifth was made after the revelation of the verse: And know that whatever you obtain of spoils - indeed, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger (al-Anfal 8:41). Abdullah ibn Jahsh had given one-fifth before that during his expedition, and then the Quran was revealed similarly to what he did, and that was from his virtues, may God have mercy on him. The conquest of Qurayzah took place at the end of Dhul-Qi'dah and the beginning of Dhul-Hijjah in the fifth year of the Hijrah. When the matter of Banu Qurayzah was completed, the prayer of the virtuous and righteous man Sa'd ibn Mu'adh was answered. His wound opened and his vein opened, his blood flowed and he died, may God be pleased with him. He is the one about whom the hadith came: The Throne of the Most Merciful shook at his death meaning that the inhabitants of the Throne from the angels rejoiced at the arrival of his soul and shook for him. Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik: Yahya ibn Sa`id told me: Seventy thousand angels descended upon the death of Sa`d ibn Mu`adh, and they had never descended to the Earth before that. Malik said: On the day of the Trench, only four or five Muslims were martyred. I said: The six Muslims who were martyred on the day of the Trench, according to what the scholars of biographies have mentioned, were: Sa`d ibn Mu`adh Abu `Amr from Banu `Abd al-Ashhal, Anas ibn Aws ibn `Atik and `Abdullah ibn Sahl, both also from Banu `Abd al-Ashhal, al-Tufayl ibn al-Nu`man and Tha`laba ibn Ghanima, both from Banu Salamah, and Ka`b ibn Zayd from Banu Dinar ibn al-Najjar. He was struck by an arrow and killed, may God be pleased with them. Three infidels were killed: Mubanah ibn Uthman ibn Ubayd ibn al-Sabbaq ibn Abd al-Dar, who was struck by an arrow and died from it in Mecca. It has been said that he was Uthman ibn Umayyah ibn Munabbih ibn Ubayd ibn al-Sabbaq, and Nawfal ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi. He stormed the trench and became entangled in it and was killed. The Muslims seized his body. It was narrated on the authority of al-Zuhri that they gave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ten thousand dirhams for his body, but he said: We have no need for his body or its price. So he left them alone with him and Amr ibn Abd Wudd, whom he killed in a duel. Khallad ibn Suwayd ibn Tha’bah ibn Amr from Banu al-Harith ibn al-Khazraj had advanced and been martyred on the day of the battle of Qurayzah against the Muslims. A woman from Banu Qurayzah threw a millstone at him and he fell. Abu Sinan ibn Muhsin ibn Harithan al-Asadi, the brother of Ukasha ibn Muhsin, died during the siege. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, buried him in the cemetery of Banu Qurayzah, in which the Muslims bury their inhabitants today. No one else from the infidels of Qurayzah did not attack the believers after this. Al-Khandaq. Al-Darimi Abu Muhammad narrated in his Musnad: Yazid bin Harun told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Tha’lab, on the authority of Al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Sa’d Al-Khudri, on the authority of his father, who said: We were detained on the day of the Trench until the night had passed, until we were sufficient. This is what God, the Almighty, said: “And God sufficed the believers in fighting. And God is Powerful and Exalted in Might.” (al-Ahzab 33:25) So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Bilal to call the noon prayer, and he did well, as he used to pray it on time. Then he ordered him to call the afternoon prayer, and he prayed it. Then he called the sunset prayer, and he prayed it. Then he ordered him to call the evening prayer, and he prayed it. That was before the verse, But if you fear, then on foot or riding. (al-Baqarah 2:139) was revealed. An-Nasa’i also reported this issue. We have already mentioned many rulings regarding the expeditions for those who reflect on them in ten issues. Then we will return to the beginning of the verses, and there are nineteen verses that include what we have mentioned. God the Almighty said: When there came to you armies meaning the Confederates so We sent upon them a wind. Mujahid said: It is the north wind, sent upon the Confederates on the day of the Trench until it threw down their pots and tore down their tents. He said: And the armies and the angels, and they did not fight that day. Ikrimah said: The south side said to the north side on the night of the Confederates: Go to support the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The north side said: Indeed, Muhwah does not travel at night. So the wind that was sent upon them was the north wind. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was aided by the north wind and destroyed the ‘Ad by the south wind. This wind was a miracle for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) because the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Muslims were close to it, there was nothing between them and it except the width of the trench and they were at the end of it, and they had no report of it. And soldiers you did not see. It was read with the letter ya meaning the polytheists did not see them. The commentators said: God sent the angels against them, so they pulled out the pegs and cut the ropes of the tents, extinguished the fires, overturned the pots, and the horses fought one another. God sent terror upon them, and the angels’ glorification increased on the sides of the army until the leader of every tent would say: O sons of so-and-so, come to me. So when they gathered, he would say to them: Escape, escape, because of the terror God had sent upon them. And God is Seeing of what you do. It was read: they do, with the letter ya as report, and this is the reading of Abu Amr. The rest with the letter ta meaning from digging the trench and taking precautions from the enemy.
33:10: The Almighty said: When they came upon you from above you and from below you When is in the accusative case meaning remember. And likewise, when a group of them said from above you, meaning from above the valley, which is its highest point towards the east, from it came Awf ibn Malik in Banu Nasr, Uyaynah ibn Hisn in the people of Najd, and Tulaiha ibn Khuwaylid al-Asadi in Banu Asad. And from below you, meaning from the valley towards the west, came Abu Sufyan ibn Harb over the people of Mecca, and Yazid ibn Jahsh over the Quraysh. And from it came Abu Sufyan ibn Harb over the people of Mecca and Yazid ibn Jahsh over the Quraysh. And Abu al-A’war al-Sulami came with Huyayy ibn Akhtab the Jew among the Jews of Banu Qurayzah with Amir ibn al-Tufayl from the direction of the Trench. And when the eyes swerved meaning stared. And it was said: turned away and did not turn except to their enemy in astonishment from the intensity of the terror. And the hearts reached the throats meaning they moved from their places in the chests until they reached the throats, which are the throats, the singular of which is hanjarah. Had it not been that the throats were too narrow for them, they would have come out. Qatada said this. And it was said: it is in the sense of exaggeration according to the Arabs’ doctrine, with the omission of almost. He said: If we get angry with a harmful anger, we tear the veil of the sun or it bleeds It is said that the lungs open up when one is afraid, and the heart rises until it almost reaches the larynx, for example. This is why it is said of a coward: His magic swelled. It is also said that it is a proverb used to describe the intensity of fear, with hearts reaching the throats, even if they remain in their places while life remains. Its meaning is said by Ikrimah. Hammad bin Zaid narrated on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Ikrimah who said: Her fear reached it. It is more apparent that he meant the heart’s turmoil and beating, meaning that it was as if its intense turmoil reached the throat, and the throat and throat with the addition of the letter nun are the letters of the throat. And you think about God suspicions. Al-Hasan said: The hypocrites thought that the Muslims would be uprooted and the believers thought that they would be victorious. It was said: It is addressed to the hypocrites, meaning you said that Muhammad and his companions have perished. The reciters differed regarding the statement of God the Most High: suspicions, the messenger, and the way, at the end of the surah. Nafi’ and Ibn ‘Amir confirmed its alifs in time and connection. It was narrated on the authority of Abu ‘Amr and Al-Kisa’i that they adhered to the script of the Mushaf, the Mushaf of ‘Uthman and all the Mushafs in all countries. Abu ‘Ubaid chose it, except that he said: The reciter should not insert the recitation after them, but he should stop at them. They said: Because the Arabs do that in the rhymes and openings of their poetry. He said: We brought the ulcers, the caravans do not mobilize the last ones to the first ones Abu Amr, Al-Jahdary, Yaqoub, and Hamza read it without it in both connected and paused speech. They said: It is extra in the script, just as the alif was added in the saying of God Almighty: And they would have placed among you (al-Tawbah 9:47), so they wrote it like this and other than this. As for poetry, it is a place of necessity, unlike the Qur’an, which is the most eloquent of languages, and there is no necessity in it. Ibn al-Anbari said: The one who read al-Zunun, al-Sabil, and al-Rasul without an alif in the three letters and wrote them in the Qur’an with an alif did not contradict the Qur’an, because the alif in ata’ana and included in the beginning of al-Rasul, al-Zunun, and al-Saabil sufficed from the final alif at the end, just as the alif of Abi Jaad sufficed from the alif of Hawaz. And there is another argument: that the alif was given the position of a fatha, and what circles is a support for the movement that precedes and the intention in it falls, so when it was worked on this, the alif with the fatha was like one thing, the pause requires their fall, and it is worked on that the image of the alif in the script does not require a place in the pronunciation, and that it is like the alif in Sihrān, “Fatār al-Samawā wa al-Ard,” Wa’dna Musa, and what is similar to them, which is deleted from the script but is present in the pronunciation, and it is dropped from the script. And there is a third argument in it, which is that it was written according to the language of those who say: I met the man, and it was read in the dialect of those who say: I met the man, without an alif. Ahmad Yahya told us on the authority of a group of linguists that they narrated on the authority of the Arabs: The man stood up, with a waw, and I passed by the man with a ya, in both connected and stopped words, and I met the man, with an alif in both cases. The poet said: Amira's questions about her father during the army confess the passengers So he established the alif in the word rakab based on this language. The other said: If Gemini follows the Pleiades, I will have bad thoughts about the family of Fatima. Based on this language, Bani Nafi` and others recited, and Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, and Al-Kisa`i recited it with it in the pause and deleted it in the connection. Ibn Al-Anbari said: If someone connected without an alif and stopped with an alif, then it is permissible to argue that the alif was needed when pausing in order to ensure that the fatha remained, and that the alif supports and strengthens it.
33:11: Here for the near place and there for the far, and there for the middle and it refers to the time, that is, at that time the believers were tested to distinguish the sincere from the hypocrites. This trial was one of fear, fighting, hunger, confinement and conflict. And they shook a violent shaking meaning they moved. Al-Zajjaj said: Every source of the doubled Fa'alal allows for the kasra and fatha like qalqaltuh qalqalān qalqālān and zalzalaw zalzān and zilzālan. The kasra is better because the non-double is on the kasra like darhajatuhu dahrajān. The general reading is with the kasra of the zay. Asim and Al-Jahdary read zalzālān with the fatha of the zay. Ibn Salam said: That is, they moved with fear with a violent shaking. Ad-Dahhak said: It is their removal from their places until they had nothing but the place of the trench. It was also said: It is their disturbance from what they were doing, so some of them were disturbed in themselves and some of them were disturbed in their religion. There it is possible that the worker was afflicted, so it does not stop there. And it is possible that it is and you think about God suspicions, so it stops there.
33:12: God the Almighty said: And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, ‘God and His Messenger have promised us nothing but delusion,’ meaning, falsehood in speech. This is because Tu’mah ibn Ubayraq, Mu’tab ibn Qushayr and a group of about seventy men said on the day of the Trench: How can He promise us the treasures of Chosroes and Caesar when none of us can even defecate? They only said that because what the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said when striking the rock had become widespread among the companions, as mentioned previously in the hadith of al-Nasa’i. Then God the Almighty revealed this verse.
33:13: The Almighty said: And when a group of them said, ‘O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you to stay, so go back.’ The word group refers to one person or more, and what is meant here is Aws ibn Qayzi, the father of Arabah ibn Aws, about whom Al-Shamakh says: If a banner is raised for glory, Araba will receive it with her right hand. Yathrib is the city and God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called it Taybah and Tabah. Abu Ubaidah said: Yathrib is the name of a land and Medina is a district of it. Al-Suhayli said: It was called Yathrib because the one who settled there from the Amalekites was named Yathrib bin Ameel bin Mahlail bin Awad bin Lawdh bin Iram. There is a difference in some of these names. The Banu Ameel are those who inhabited Al-Juhfah and the floods swept them away and Al-Juhfah was named after them. A place to stay for you, so return is the general reading. Hafs, Al-Sulami, Al-Jadri and Abu Haywah read it with a damma on the m. It is a verbal noun from aqama yaqim, meaning there is no residence or place to reside in. Whoever reads with a fatha, it is the name of a place, meaning there is no place but you reside in it. Farjū means to your homes. He ordered them to flee from the army of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Abbas said: The Jews said to Abdullah bin Ubayy bin Salul and his companions from al-Munafiqun 63:What makes you kill yourselves at the hands of Abu Sufyan and his companions! So return to Al-Madinah, for we are with the people and you are safe. God the Almighty said: And a party of them asked permission of the Prophet to return to their homes in Madinah, and they are Banu Haritha ibn al-Harith, according to Ibn Abbas. Yazid ibn Ruman said: Aws ibn Qayzi said that to a group of his people. They say, ‘Our houses are vulnerable,’ meaning, they are lost and unprotected, and they are close to the enemy. It was also said: they are vulnerable to thieves because they are devoid of men. It is said that a house is vulnerable and has a vulnerability, and the houses of ‘Urwah and ‘Awar are one-eyed, so it is ‘Ma’war. It was also said: ‘Awrah has a vulnerability.’ And every place that is not forbidden or concealed is ‘Urwah, as al-Harawi said. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Mujahid, and Abu Raja’ al-Attardi read: ‘Awrah’ with a kasrah on the waw, meaning short walls with flaws in them. The Arabs say: So-and-so has a vulnerability if it is not secure. And a knight is one-eyed if a flaw appears in it for striking and stabbing. The poet said: When you meet them, you will not find a sick person in the house, nor a grieving guest, nor a widowed neighbor. Al-Jawhari K and Al-Awrah every defect that is feared in a breach or war of coppers: It is said that a place is one-eyed if a defect is apparent in it, and that a knight is one-eyed if the place of the defect is apparent in it. Al-Mahdawi: And whoever breaks the waw in Awrah is anomalous and similar to it is their saying: A man who is one-eyed, meaning he has nothing. The analogy was that he should be made famous, so he said: Shame like the day of departure and a man of wealth, their root is Ruh and Mawla. Then God Almighty said: And it is not a defect as a refutation of them and a response to what they mentioned. They only want to flee meaning they only want to escape. It was said: from killing and it was said: from religion. Al-Naqqash narrated that this verse was revealed about two tribes of the Ansar: Banu Haritha and Banu Salamah, and they intended to leave their positions on the day of the Trench, and about them God Almighty revealed: When two parties among you were about to lose heart [Al Imran] the verse. When this verse was revealed, they said: By God, what we intended did not upset us, for God is our protector. Al-Suddi said: The one who asked his permission to go to them was two men from the Ansar from Banu Haritha, one of them was Abu Arabah ibn Aws, and the other was Aws ibn Qayzi. Al-Dahhak said: And eighty men returned without his permission.
33:14: The Almighty said: And if it had entered upon them from its regions meaning the houses or the city, meaning from its sides and corners. The singular is qatr, which is the side and the region, and qutr is also a language for country. Then they were asked for the trial, they would have come to it meaning they would have resorted to it. This is according to the reading of Nafi` and Ibn Kathir with the short vowel. The rest read it with the long vowel, meaning they would have given it from themselves, and this is the choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim. It has been reported in the hadith: The companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were tortured for the sake of God and asked for polytheism, so everyone was given what they asked except Bilal. This is evidence for the long vowel reading of giving, and evidence for the short vowel reading is his statement: And they had already made a covenant with God before that they would not turn their backs This indicates that they would have come to it with the short vowel. There are two aspects to the trial here: One of them is that they were asked to fight for partisanship, they would have rushed to it. Ad-Dahhak said the second: Then they were asked for polytheism, they would have answered, Yes, quickly, Al-Hasan said. And they did not stay there meaning in Madinah after the disbelief was given, except for a little while until they perished. As-Suddi and Al-Qutbi said. Al-Hasan and Al-Farra’ said that most of the commentators said: That is, they were not held back from the temptation of polytheism except for a short time, and they would have responded to polytheism quickly, and that was due to the weakness of their intentions and their excess. If the parties had mixed with them, they would have shown disbelief.
33:15: God Almighty says: And they had already made a covenant with God before, meaning before the Battle of the Trench and after Badr. Qatada said: This is because they were absent from Badr and saw what God had given the people of Badr of honor and victory, so they said: If God makes us witness to a fight, we will fight. Yazid ibn Ruman said: They, the Banu Haritha, intended to fail along with Banu Salamah on the day of Uhud, but when what happened to them happened, they pledged to God that they would not do anything like it again. Then God mentioned to them what they had given of themselves, And the covenant of God will be questioned about, meaning one will be held accountable for it. Muqatil and Al-Kalbi said: “They were seventy men who pledged allegiance to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the night of Al-Aqabah and said: Stipulate for yourself and your Lord whatever you wish. He said: I stipulate for my Lord that you worship Him and do not associate anything with Him, and I stipulate for myself that you protect me from what you protect your women, your wealth, and your children. They said: What will we get if we do that, O Prophet of God? He said: For you is victory in this world and Paradise in the Hereafter.” This is what God the Most High said: And the covenant of God will be questioned about, meaning that God will ask them about it on the Day of Resurrection.
33:16: The Almighty said: Say, ‘Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing.’ That is, whoever’s time has come to die or be killed, then flight will not benefit. And then you will not enjoy yourself except for a little. That is, in this world after fleeing until your time has expired, and everything that is coming is near. Al-Saji narrated on the authority of Ya’qub Al-Hadrami, And then you will not enjoy yourself with a ya and in some narrations, And then you will not enjoy yourself is in the accusative case with then and the nominative case means and you will not enjoy yourself. “And then” is cancelled and it is permissible to use it. This is its ruling if it is preceded by waw and fa. If it is a subject, it is in the accusative case with it, so you say: If God honors you.
33:17: God Almighty says: “Say: Who is it that can protect you from God?” That is, prevent you from Him. If He intends to do you harm That is, destruction or intends to do you mercy That is, good, victory, and well-being. And they will not find for themselves besides God any protector or helper That is, no close relative who can benefit them or any supporter who can aid them.
33:18: The Almighty said: God knows those among you who hold back meaning those among you who object to turning people away from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is derived from aqaqani 'an kada meaning to turn me away from it. Awaq is used to describe many people. And those who say to their brothers, 'Come to us' in the dialect of the people of Hijaz and others. They say: Halmu for the group and Halmi for the woman, because the original is: ha which is for warning. Lam was added to it, then the alif was deleted for the sake of brevity. It was built on the fatha and the kasra or damma were not permissible for it because it is not declined.
