The meaning of Hallam is come and these are two groups, meaning from you, those who discourage and hinder. Hallam is prevention and diversion. It is said: Aqah means ya'uqquhu, 'awqan, and 'awqah and etaaqah mean the same thing. Muqatil said: They are Abdullah bin Ubayy and his companions, the hypocrites. And those who say to their brothers, 'Come to us' There are three opinions about them: One of them is that they are the hypocrites who said to the Muslims: Muhammad and his companions are nothing but a head eaten by him and he and those with him are doomed, so come to us. The second: They are the Jews from the Banu Quraiza, they said to their brothers from al-Munafiqun 63:Come to us, meaning come to us and leave Muhammad, for he is doomed, and if Abu Sufyan is victorious, not a single one of you will remain. The third: What Ibn Zayd narrated: That a man from the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was among spears and swords, so his brother - who was from his mother and father - said: Come to me, you and your companion have been followed, meaning you and your companion have been surrounded. So he said to him: By God, I will tell him about your situation. So he went to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, to tell him, but he found that Gabriel, peace be upon him, had come down to him with the words of God Almighty: {Indeed, God knows those among you who hold back and those who say to their brothers, Come to us.} Al-Maroudi and Al-Tha’labi also mentioned it, and their wording is: Ibn Zayd said: This was on the day of the Confederates. A man went from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and found his brother before him a loaf of bread, a roasted meal, and wine. He said to him: You are in this, while we are among spears and swords? So he said: Come to this, for you and your companions have been followed, and by the One by whom you swear, he will never meet Muhammad with it. He said: You have lied. So he went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him. He found that Gabriel had revealed to him this verse: And they do not come to battle except a little, for fear of death. It was also said: They do not attend battle except for show and reputation.
33:19: The Almighty’s saying: {Stingy with you} meaning miserly with you, meaning with digging the trench and spending in the way of God, as stated by Mujahid and Qatadah. It was said: with fighting with you, and it was said: with spending on your poor and needy, and it was said: stingy with the spoils if they acquired them, as stated by Al-Suddi, and it was placed in the accusative case as a state. Al-Zajjaj said: Its accusative case according to Al-Farra’ is from four aspects: One of them: that it is on blame, and it is permissible for it to be in the accusative case with him, meaning they hinder, miserly, and it is permissible for the estimation to be: and the speakers are stingy, and it is permissible with him: and they do not come to battle except a little, miserly, meaning that they come to it, miserly with the poor with the spoils. An-Nahhas: It is not permissible for the factor in it to be the hindering ones or the speakers, lest there be a distinction between the relative clause and the relative pronoun. Ibn al-Anbari: Except for a little is not complete because ash-ha is related to the first, so it is accusative in four ways: One: That it is accusative as a severance from the hindered, as if he said: God knows those who hinder from fighting and are stingy with spending on the poor Muslims. It is permissible for it to be accusative as a severance from the speakers, meaning they are stingy. It is permissible to make it accusative as a severance from what is in they come, as if he said: And none come to battle except cowards and misers. It is permissible to make ash-ha as a slander, so from this fourth way, it is good to stop at his saying: Except for a little. “Stingy with you” is a good stop, and likewise ash-ha about good is a state of the implied in salqukum and it is the factor in it. So when fear comes, you will see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one who has fainted from death. He described them as cowardly, and this is how the coward looks right and left, narrowing their gaze, and perhaps he faints. And fear has two ways: One: From fighting the enemy when he approaches, as al-Suddi said. Second: Fear of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, if he is defeated. Ibn Shajarah said, I saw them looking at you, fearing the fighting according to the first statement, and of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, according to the second. Their eyes roll due to their loss of reason, so that they cannot look in any direction. It was said: Due to their intense fear, being wary that killing will come to them from every direction. So when the fear is gone, they will smite you with sharp tongues. Al-Farra’ narrated that they smite you with a sad and a preacher muslaq and muslaq if he is eloquent. The origin of the sound is from it. “The saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: May God curse the one who shaves, the one who cuts, and the one who tears. Al-A’mash said: In them is glory, space, and help, and in them is the eloquent suitor Qatada said: Its meaning is that they stretched out their tongues against you at the time of dividing the spoils, saying: Give us, give us, for we have witnessed with you. So when it is time for the spoils, the most miserly and most outspoken people are the ones who speak the truth, but at the time of battle, they are the most cowardly and fearful people. An-Nahhas said: This is a good statement, because after it, they are miserly with good. And it was said: The meaning is that they exaggerated in their quarreling and arguing with you. Al-Qatabi said: The meaning is that they hurt you with harsh words. As-Salq: harm, and from it is the saying of the poet: We have boiled our waters with our sticks until we bent down “Stingy with good” meaning with wealth. Yahya ibn Salam said it. It was also said: with money, that they spend it in the way of God. Al-Suddi said it. Those did not believe, meaning in their hearts, even if they outwardly believed. The hypocrite is a disbeliever in reality, because God, the Almighty, described them as disbelievers. So God rendered their deeds worthless meaning He did not reward them for them if they did not intend the pleasure of God through them. And that was easy for God has two possible meanings: their hypocrisy was easy for God, and the second is that rendering their deeds worthless for God was easy.
33:20: The Almighty said: They think that the confederates have not gone away meaning, out of cowardice, they think that the confederates have not departed, but they have departed, but they did not spread out in the march. And if the confederates come meaning, if the confederates return to them to fight, they would like to be nomads among the bedouins They wish that they were with the bedouins, out of caution against being killed and in ambush for calamities. Tahla ibn Musarraf read: If they were nomads among the bedouins, out of caution against being killed and in ambush for calamities. Talha ibn Musarraf read: If they were nomads among the bedouins It is said: Bad and Bada like ghaz and ghazee and it is extended like sai'im and sawwam Bada. So-and-so goes out to the desert, which is badawah and badawah with kasra and fatha, and the root of the word is from badaw which means to appear. They ask and Ya'qub read in the narration of Ruways: They ask about your report meaning about the report of the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, they talk: Have Muhammad and his companions not perished? Have Abu Sufyan and his confederates been defeated?! That is, they wish they were in the desert asking about your report without witnessing the fighting, due to their extreme cowardice. It was also said: That is, due to their cowardice, they always ask about the report of the believers and whether they were wounded. It was also said: There were among them on the outskirts of the city those who had not been present at the Battle of the Trench, and they kept asking about your report and wishing for the defeat of the Muslims. And if they had been among you, they would not have fought except a little that is, shooting arrows and stones for the sake of showing off and seeking fame. And if that had been for God, it would have been very little.
33:21: There are two issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern. This is a rebuke to those who stayed behind from fighting, meaning that you had a role model in the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) as he sacrificed himself to support the religion of God in his march to the Trench. The role model is the example. Asim read it with a damma on the hamza. The rest read it with a kasra. They are two dialects, and the plural is the same according to al-Farra’. The reason according to him is the damma in the dialect of the one who has a kasra in the singular, the difference between the ones with a waw and the ones with a ya’, so they say kiswa and kisan, and lahyah and lahyah. Al-Jawhari said: The role model and the model with the damma and kasra are two dialects, and the plural is asa and isa. It was narrated by Uqbah ibn Hassan al-Hijri from Malik ibn Anas from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar: There has certainly been for you in the Messenger of God an excellent pattern. He said: In the hunger of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Khatib Abu Bakr Ahmad mentioned it and said: Uqbah ibn Hassan was the only one who narrated it from Malik, and I did not write it except with this chain of transmission. The second: The Almighty’s saying: an example. An example is a model, and an example is that which is emulated, that is, one is consoled by it, so one follows it in all one’s actions and is consoled by it in all one’s circumstances. His face was wounded, his front tooth was broken, his uncle Hamza was killed, his stomach was hungry, and he did not die except patient, accepting reward, grateful, and satisfied. On the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of Abu Talha, he said: We complained to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we lifted one stone from our stomachs, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lifted two stones.” Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and said about it: A strange hadith. And the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said when he was wounded: O God, forgive my people, for they do not know. And it was mentioned before: For whoever hopes for God and the Last Day. Saeed bin Jubair said: The meaning is for whoever hopes to meet God through his faith and believes in the resurrection which is the recompense for deeds. And it was said: That is, for whoever hopes for God’s reward on the Last Day. And the skilled grammarians do not allow to write yarja except without an alif when it is for a singular person, because the reason for the plural is not in the singular. And remember God often out of fear of His punishment and hope for His reward. And it was said: In. And it was said: For whoever was a substitute for his saying for you. The Basrans do not permit it because the absent person cannot be substituted for the one being addressed. Rather, the lam in for whoever is related to goodness and aswa is the name of kan, and for you is the predicate. There is a difference of opinion as to whom this address is intended, with two opinions: One of them: The hypocrites in apposition to what was mentioned before of their address. The second: The believers, because of His saying: For whoever hopes for God and the Last Day. There is a difference of opinion regarding this example of the Messenger, peace be upon him, as to whether it is obligatory or recommended. There are two opinions: One of them: It is obligatory until evidence of recommendation is presented. The second: It is recommended until evidence of obligation is presented. It is possible that it is carried over to the obligation in matters of religion, and to the recommendation in matters of this world.
33:22: The Almighty said: And when the believers saw the confederates and some Arabs say: Raa’a is on the heart “they said: This is what God promised us” meaning the Almighty’s saying in Surat al-Baqarah 2:Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such [trial] has not yet come to you as came to those who passed on before you? (al-Baqarah 2:214) the verse. So when they saw the confederates on the day of the Trench, they said: This is what God and His Messenger promised us. Qatada said: A second statement was narrated by Katheer bin Abdullah bin Amr Al-Muzani on the authority of his father on the authority of his grandfather who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) wrote in the year when the confederates were mentioned, and he said: Gabriel (peace be upon him) informed me that my nation will be victorious over them - meaning the palaces of Al-Hirah and the cities of Kisra - so be glad of the victory. The Muslims were filled with joy and said: Praise be to God, a true promise, for He promised us victory after the siege. The confederates emerged and the believers said: This is what God and His Messenger promised us. Al-Maroudi mentioned: What We Promised Us: If you make what means who, then the ha’ is deleted. If you make it a source, then it does not need a pronoun. And it only increased them in faith and submission. Al-Farra’ said: And looking at the confederates increased them. Ali bin Sulayman said: Saw indicates seeing, and the feminine of saw is not real. The meaning is: Seeing only increased their faith in the Lord and submission to the decree. Al-Hasan said: If he had said: It only increased them, it would have been permissible. And when the matter became difficult for the Muslims and the stay in the trench was prolonged, he (peace be upon him) stood on the hill on which the Mosque of Victory was located one night, anticipating what God had promised him of victory and said: Who will bring us the best of them and he will have Paradise? But no one answered him. He asked a second and a third time, but no one answered him. Then he looked to the side and said: Who is this? Hudhayfah asked: Didn’t you hear what I said last night? Hudhayfah said: I said: O Messenger of God, hardship and distress prevented me from answering you. He said: Go until you enter among the people and hear their speech and bring me report of them. O God, protect him from before him and behind him and from his right and from his left until you return him to me. Go and do not say anything until you come to me. So Haifa set off with his weapon and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hand saying: O Crier of the distressed and O Answerer of the needy, relieve my worry, my grief and my distress, for You see my condition and the condition of my companions. Then Gabriel came down and said: God has heard your prayer and has spared you the terror of your enemy. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell on his knees and spread out his hands and lowered his eyes and said: Thank you, thank you for having mercy on me and my companions. And Gabriel informed him that God Almighty had sent a wind upon them, so he gave his companions good report of that. Hudhayfah said: So I reached them and their fires were blazing, and a strong wind with pebbles in it blew them away and did not leave a fire without extinguishing it and no building without overthrowing it. They began to shield themselves with pebbles. Abu Sufyan went to his mount and shouted to the Quraysh 106:Escape, escape! And Uyaynah ibn The fortress of Al-Ahras bin Awf and Al-Aqra’ bin Habis, and the parties dispersed. The morning came and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to Medina, and he had as much hair as God willed. Fatima came to him with a bath, and she was washing his head. Gabriel came to him and said: “I have put down my weapons, but the people of heaven have not. I continued to follow them until I passed Al-Rawha’ with them.” Then he said: Get up to Banu Qurayza. Abu Sufyan said: I kept hearing the clatter of weapons until I passed Al-Rawha’.
33:23: So that God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills or accept their repentance. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. The Almighty said: Among the believers are men in the nominative case as a subject, and the indefinite article is appropriate to begin with because they were truthful is in the position of an adjective. And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow “who” is in the nominative case as a subject, and likewise and among them is he who is waiting and the predicate is in the genitive case. And na’b means a vow and a covenant. You say from it: I na’bt “anhaab” with the dammah. The poet said: If a dog wails on people, they are more deserving of the crown of the Majestic and Generous Another said: We may love glory, we may love it Another said: Should I weep and die, or should I be misled and false? Al-Bukhari, Muslim and Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Anas who said: My uncle Anas ibn An-Nadr - I was named after him - did not witness the Battle of Badr with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he felt very sad about it and said: I was absent from the first battle that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) witnessed. By God, if God lets me witness another battle with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after that, God will let me see what I will do. He was afraid to say anything else, so he witnessed the Battle of Uhud with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) the following year. Saad ibn Malik met him and said: O Abu Amr, where are you? He said: Ah, the scent of Paradise! I found it without anyone, so he fought until he was killed, and eighty-two wounds were found on his body between blows, stabs, and arrows. My aunt, Ar-Rabi’ bint An-Nadr, said: I did not recognize my brother except by my fingertips. And this verse was revealed: “Men who have been true to what they pledged to God. Among them is he who has fulfilled his vow, and among them is he who awaits [his chance]. And they have not changed [their covenant] by any change.” The wording of At-Tirmidhi. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said regarding the words of God the Almighty: Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. (al-Ahzab 33:23) The verse: Among them was Talha bin Ubaid God, who remained with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until his hand was injured. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Talha has made Paradise obligatory. And in Al-Tirmidhi on his authority: The companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to an ignorant Bedouin: Ask him about someone who has passed away, who he is? They did not dare to ask him because they respected and feared him. The Bedouin asked him but he turned away from him. Then he asked him but he turned away from him. Then I looked out of the door of the mosque and I was standing on a green hill. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw me, he said: Where is the one who asked about someone who has passed away? The Bedouin said: I am, O Messenger of God. He said: This is one of those who have passed away. He said: This is a good and strange hadith. We do not know it except from the hadith of Yunus ibn Bakir. Al-Bayhaqi narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah: That when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) returned from Uhud, he passed by Mus`ab ibn `Umair who was being killed on the way. He stopped over him and supplicated for him, then he recited this verse: “Among the believers are men true to what they pledged to God. And among them is he who has fulfilled his vow” - to - exchanging. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “I bear witness that these are witnesses before God on the Day of Resurrection, so go to them and visit them. And by He in Whose Hand is my soul, no one will greet them until the Day of Resurrection except that they will return his greeting.” It was said: Naḥt means death, meaning he died as he pledged, according to Ibn `Abbas. Naḥt also means time and period. It is said: So-and-so fulfilled his vow if he died. Dhu al-Rummah said: Aisha Far Al-Harithioun died after he met his death at the Huber horse meeting. And the word na’bah also means need and ambition. Their speaker says: I have no love for them. What is meant by the verse and meaning in this passage by na’bah is not the vow, as we mentioned first, that is, some of them exerted their effort to fulfill their covenant until they were killed, such as Hamza, Sa’d ibn Mu’adh, Anas ibn al-Nadr, and others. And some of them are waiting for martyrdom, but they did not change their covenant and vow. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he read: And among them are those who have fulfilled their vow, and among them are those who are waiting, and among them are those who have changed. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said: This hadith is rejected by the people of knowledge because it contradicts the consensus, and because it is an attack on the believers and the foot soldiers whom God praised and honored with truthfulness and loyalty. What is known is a clever changer, and what is found among their group is a changer, may God be pleased with them. That God may reward the truthful for their truthfulness means that God commanded jihad in order to reward the truthful in the Hereafter for their truthfulness. And punish the hypocrites in the Hereafter: If He wills meaning that if He wills to punish them, He will not grant them success in repentance, and if He does not will to punish them, He will accept their repentance before death.
33:24: Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
33:25: The Almighty said: And God repelled those who disbelieved in their fury, and they did not attain any good. Muhammad bin Amr said, tracing it back to Aisha: She said: Those who disbelieved here are Abu Sufyan and Uyaynah bin Badr. Abu Sufyan returned to Tihamah and Uyaynah returned to Najd. And God spared the believers the fighting by sending upon them a wind and soldiers until they returned and Banu Qurayzah returned to their strongholds. So He spared the matter of Qurayzah by terror. And God is Strong Most Expert Mighty Who cannot be defeated.
33:26: The Almighty says: And He brought down those who supported them among the People of the Scripture from their fortresses meaning those who supported the Confederates: Quraysh and Ghatafan, who are Banu Qurayzah, and their story has already been mentioned. From their fortresses meaning their strongholds, the singular of which is sisa. The poet said: The bulls fell down and the women of Tim rushed to the oxen. Hence, the weaver’s company, in which the warp and weft are made, was called: Saisa. Duraid bin Al-Samma said: I came to him and the spears were hitting him like the sound of spears hitting a stretched cloth. From it: the rooster’s clucking which is on its leg, and the cow’s horns are its horns, because they protect it and sometimes it was mounted on spears in place of the tips, and it is said: God cut off its clucking, meaning its root, And cast terror into their hearts, a group you kill and they are the men, and you take captive a group and they are the women and children as mentioned above, And He made you inherit their land and their homes and their wealth and a land which you have not yet trodden He said: Yarizad bin Ruman and Ibn Zayd and Muqatil: meaning Hunayn, and they had not attained it, so God promised it to them, and Qatada said: We used to say that it was Mecca, and Al-Hasan said: It is Persia and Rome, and Ikrimah said: Every land will be conquered until the Day of Resurrection.
33:27: And God has power over all things has two meanings: One of them: He is powerful over whatever He wills for His servants of punishment or forgiveness, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq said. The second: He is powerful over whatever fortresses and villages He wills to conquer, as al-Naqqash said. It was said: And God has power over all things of what He has promised you, powerful, His power cannot be rejected and incapacity is not permissible for Him, the Most High. It is said: you take captive and you take captive, with the kasra and damma of the seen, as al-Farra’ related.
33:28: It contains eight issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: O Prophet, tell your wives. Our scholars said: This verse is connected to the meaning of what came before regarding the prohibition of harming the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He was harmed by some of his wives. It was said: They asked him for something of this world’s goods. It was said: An increase in expenses. It was said: They harmed him because of the jealousy of some of them towards others. It was said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that this verse be recited to them and that they be given the choice between this world and the Hereafter. Al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, said: Whoever owns a wife does not have to give her the choice. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that his wives be given the choice, and they chose him. The gist of that is that God Almighty gave the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the choice between being a prophet and a king and offered him the keys to the treasures of this world and between being a poor prophet. He consulted Gabriel, and they advised him to be poor, so he chose her. When he chose her, who was the higher of the two positions, God Almighty ordered him to give his wives the choice, as there might be among them someone who would hate to stay with him due to the hardship, out of respect for him. It was said: The reason for which he required the choice was that one of his wives asked him to formulate… She had a gold ring, so he made a silver ring for her and plated it with gold - and it was said with saffron - but he refused, unless it was gold. Then the verse of choice was revealed, so he gave them the choice, and they said, We have chosen God and His Messenger. And it was said: If one of them chose separation, then God knows best. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated, and the wording is from Muslim, “On the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said: Abu Bakr entered to ask permission to see the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and found people sitting at his door, and he had not given permission to any of them. He said: So he gave permission to Abu Bakr and he entered. Then Umar came and asked permission to see him and found the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sitting with his wives around him, silent and stunned. He said: By God, I will say something that will make the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laugh. He said: O Messenger of God, if you saw the daughter of Kharijah asking me for money and I went to her and slapped her on the neck, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed and said: They are around me as you see asking me for money. Then Abu Bakr got up to Aisha and slapped her on the neck, and Umar got up to Hafsa and slapped her on the neck. Both of them said: You ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) for something he does not have!! They said: By God, we will never ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for anything he does not have. Then he kept away from them for a month or twenty-nine days, then this verse was revealed to him: “O Prophet, tell your wives” until he reached For the good among you is a great reward. He said: So he started with Aisha and said: O Aisha, I want to present to you a matter that I would like you not to rush into until you consult your father. She said: What is it, O Messenger of God? So he recited the verse to her. She said: Is it with you, O Messenger of God, that I should consult my parents! Rather, choose God and His Messenger and the Hereafter. And I ask you not to tell any of your wives what you said: Do not ask any of them about me except that I will tell her. Indeed, God did not send me to be a burden, but He sent me as a teacher and a facilitator. And Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that his wives be given a choice. He began with me and said: O Aisha, I am going to mention to you a matter, so do not be hasty until you consult your parents. She said, and he knew that my parents would not have ordered me to leave him. She said, Then he said: God says, “O Prophet, tell your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you and release you with a gracious release.” Until he reached: For the good among you is a great reward. Is it in this that I should consult my parents? For I want God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter. And the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did as I did. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. The scholars said: As for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordering Aisha to consult her parents, it was because he loved her and was afraid that her extreme youth would lead her to choose to separate from him, and he knew from her parents that they would not advise them to separate from him. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Say to your wives. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had wives, some of whom he had consummated the marriage with, some of whom he had married but had not consummated the marriage with, and some of whom he had proposed to but had not consummated the marriage with. The first of them was Khadija bint Khuwaylid ibn Asad ibn Abd al-Uzza ibn Qusayy ibn Kilab. She was previously married to Abu Hala, whose name was Zuraat ibn al-Nabbash al-Asadi. He was previously married to Atiq ibn A’idh, and she bore him a boy named Abd Manaf. She bore Abu Hala Hind ibn Abi Hala, who lived until the time of the plague, and died there. It is said that the one who lived until the time of the plague was Hind ibn Hind. I heard his mourner say when he died, And Hind ibn Hindah is the stepchild of the Messenger of God. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not marry anyone other than Khadija except her until she died. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her, she was forty years old. She died after seven years of prophethood had passed, and it was said ten. She was sixty-five years old when she died. She was the first woman to believe in him, and all of his children were from her, except for Ibrahim. Hakim ibn Hizam said, “Khadija died, so we took her out of her house and buried her in al-Hujun. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went down into her grave, and it was not the custom at that time to pray over her.” Among them: Sawda bint Zam’a bin Qais bin Abd Shams Al-Amiriya, she converted to Islam long ago and pledged allegiance, and she was married to her cousin called Al-Sakran bin Amr, who also converted to Islam, and they all migrated to the land of Abyssinia in the second migration. When they arrived in Mecca, her husband died, and it was said that he died in Abyssinia, so she was not permitted to propose to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he married her and consummated the marriage with her in Mecca, and migrated with her to Medina. When she grew old, he wanted to divorce her, but she asked him not to do so and to leave her with their women, and she made her night for Aisha - according to what is mentioned in the Sahih - so he kept her, and she died in Medina in Shawwal of the year fifty-four. Among them was Aisha, the daughter of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, who was named after Jubair bin Mut’im. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to her, but Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, let me take her from Jubair gently. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her in Mecca two years before the Hijra, and it was said three years before, and he consummated the marriage with her in Medina when she was nine years old. She remained with him for nine years, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died when she was eighteen years old. She did not marry any other virgin other than her, and he died in the year fifty-nine, and it was said fifty-eight. Among them was Hafsa bint Umar ibn al-Khattab, the Quraysh woman from the tribe of Adawiyah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her and then divorced her. Gabriel came to him and said: God commands you to return to Hafsa, for she was a woman who fasted and prayed, so return to her. Al-Waqidi said: She died in Sha’ban of the year forty-five during the caliphate of Mu’awiyah, which was the year sixty years old. It was also said that she died during the caliphate of Uthman in Medina. Among them: Umm Salamah, whose name was Hind bint Abi Umayyah al-Makhzumiyyah - and Abi Umayyah’s name was Suhayl - the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her to him during the remaining nights of Shawwal in the year four. He married her to her son Salamah, according to the correct view, and her son’s age was young. She died in the year fifty-nine, and it was said: in the year sixty-two, and the first is more correct. Saad bin Zaid prayed over her, and it was said Abu Hurayrah. She was buried in al-Baqa’ when she was eighty-four years old. Among them: Umm Habibah, whose name was Ramlah bint Abi Sufyan. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri to the Negus to propose marriage to Umm Habibah, so he married her to him. That was in the year seven of the Hijra. The Negus gave the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, four hundred dinars as a dowry and sent her with Shurahbil ibn Hasana. She died in the year forty-four. Al-Daraqutni said: Umm Habibah was married to Ubayd God ibn Jahsh, and he died in Abyssinia as a Christian. The Negus married her to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and gave them a dowry of four thousand on his behalf, and sent her to Shurahbil ibn Hasana. Among them: Zainab bint Jahsh ibn Riab al-Asadiyyah, whose name was Barra, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, named her Zainab, and her father’s name was Barra, so he said: O Messenger of God, change my father’s name, for righteousness is insignificant. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: If your father had been a believer, we would have named him after a man from among us, the people of the house, but I have named him Jahsh, and Jahsh is from righteousness. Al-Daraqutni mentioned this hadith: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her in Medina in the year five of the Hijra, and she died in the year twenty, at the age of fifty-three. Among them: Zainab bint Khudhaymah bin Al-Harith bin Abdullah bin Amr bin Abd Manaf bin Hilal bin Arim bin Sa’sa Al-Hilaliyah. She was called in the pre-Islamic era the mother of the poor because she fed them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her in Ramadan, thirty-one months after the Hijra. She stayed with him for eight months and died during his lifetime at the end of Rabi’ Al-Awwal, thirty-nine months after the Hijra. She was buried in Al-Baqi’. Among them: Juwayriyah bint al-Harith ibn Abi Dharar al-Khuza’iyah al-Mutlaqiyah, who was married to her in Gaza, and she fell into the lot of Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas, so he wrote a contract with her, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fulfilled her contract and married her. That was in Sha’ban of the year six, and her name was Barra, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, named her Juwayriyah. She died in Rabi’ al-Awwal of the year fifty-six, and it was said: in the year fifty, and she was sixty-five years old. Among them: Safiyyah bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab al-Haruniyah, whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took captive on the day of Khaybar and chose her for himself. She converted to Islam and he freed her, making her freedom her dowry. In Sahih, she fell into the lot of Dihya al-Kalbi, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, bought her for seven heads. She died in the year fifty, and it was said: in the year fifty-two, and she was buried in al-Baqi’. Among them: Rayhana bint Zaid bin Amr bin Khanaqah from Banu Nadir. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took her captive and freed her, and married her in the year six. She died on her way back from the Farewell Pilgrimage, so he buried her in Al-Baqi’. Al-Waqidi said: She died in the year sixteen, and Umar prayed over her. Abu Al-Faraj Al-Jawzi said: I heard someone say: He had intercourse with her by right of possession, but he did not free her. I said: And for this reason, and God knows best, Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Rahman al-Suhayli did not mention her among the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Among them: Maymunah bint al-Harith al-Hilaliyah, whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married in Sarif, ten miles from Mecca, in the year seven of the Hijra during the Umrah of al-Qadiyah. She was the last woman whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married, and God Almighty decreed that she died in the place where the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, built a house for her and she was buried there, in the year sixty-one, and it was said: sixty-three, and it was said: sixty-eight. These are the famous wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with whom he had intercourse, may God be pleased with them: As for those he married but did not consummate the marriage with, among them was Al-Kalabiya. They differed about her name. Some said it was Fatima, some said it was Umra, and some said it was Al-Aliya. Al-Zuhri said: He married Fatima bint Al-Dahhak Al-Kalabiya, and she sought refuge from him, so he divorced her. She used to say: I am the wretched one. He married her in Dhul-Qi’dah in the year eight of the Hijra, and she died in the year sixty. Among them: Asma bint Al-Nu’man bin Al-Jun bin Al-Harith Al-Kindiyyah, who is Al-Juniyah. Qatada said that when he entered upon her, he called her and she said: Come here, so he divorced her. Another said: She is the one who sought refuge from him. And in Al-Bukhari [on the authority of Sahl bin Sa’d and Abu Asid, they said]. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married Umaimah bint Shuraheel. When she entered upon him, he extended his hand to her, and it seemed that she disliked that. So he ordered Abu Sayyid to prepare her and clothe her in two garments. In another version, Abu Usaid said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought Al-Juniyah, and when he entered upon her, he said: Give me yourself. She said: Would a queen give herself to a commoner? He reached out with his hand to put it on her so that she would calm down. She said: I seek refuge in God from you! He said: He has been tortured because of Muadh. Then he came out to us and said: O Abu Asid, clothe her with two kinds of provisions and send her back to her family. Among them: Qatilah bint Qays, sister of Al-Ash'ath bin Qays. Al-Ash'ath married her to him, then he returned to Hadhramaut and took her to him. He heard of the death of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he sent her back to her country. He apostatized and she apostatized with him. Then Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl married her. Abu Bakr was very upset by that, so Umar said to him: By God, she is not one of his wives. He did not choose her, nor did he keep her away. God has absolved her of him because of her apostasy. Urwah denied that he had married her. Among them: Umm Sharik Al-Azdiya, whose name was Ghaziya bint Jabir bin Hakim. She was previously married to Abu Bakr bin Abi Salma, but the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, divorced her without consummating the marriage with her. She was the one who offered herself to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was said that the one who offered herself to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was Khawlah bint Hakim. Among them: Khawlah bint al-Hudhayl ibn Hubayrah, whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married, but she died before she reached him. Among them: Sharaf bint Khalifa, sister of Dihya, whom he married but did not consummate the marriage. Among them: Laila bint Al-Khatim, Qais’s sister. He married her, but she was jealous, so she asked him to leave her, so he dismissed her. Among them: Khawlah bint Hudhayl, the daughter of Hubayrah. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her, but she died before Kinda could reach him. She was brought back after he had died. Among them: the daughter of Jundub bin Damrah al-Junda’iyah. Some of them said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her, and some of them denied the existence of that. Among them: Al-Ghafariyah: Some of them said, “He married a woman from Ghafar and ordered her to take off her clothes. He saw whiteness and said: Al-Halqi with your family. It is said that he saw the whiteness in Al-Kalabiyyah. These are the women with whom he was engaged but did not consummate the marriage. As for those who are engaged, his marriage with them is not completed, and whoever gives herself to him. Among them: Umm Hani’, the daughter of Abu Talib, whose name was Fakhita. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to her, but she said: “I am a woman who has been afflicted.” She apologized to him, and he excused her. Among them: Daba’a bint Aamer. Among them: Safiyyah bint Bashamah bin Nadlah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to her. Her children were taken captive, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave her the choice and said: If you wish, I will, and if you wish, I will marry you. She said, My husband. So he sent her, and Banu Tamim cursed her. This was said by Ibn Abbas. Among them: Umm Sharik, who was mentioned above. Among them: Laila bint Al-Khatim, who was mentioned above. Among them: Khawlah bint Hakim ibn Umayya, who offered herself to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, but he postponed her, so Uthman ibn Mazun married her. Among them: Jamrah bint Al-Harith bin Awf Al-Murri. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to her, but her father said: There is something wrong with her, but she had not. So her father returned to her and she had become leprous. She is the mother of Shabib bin Al-Barsa’, the poet. Among them: Sawda Al-Qurashiyya, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed to her and she was afflicted. She said: I fear that my children will cry at your head. So he praised her and prayed for her. Among them: A woman whose name was not mentioned. Mujahid said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, proposed marriage to a woman, and she said: I seek your permission from my father. So I met her father, and he gave her permission. Then I met the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: We have covered ourselves with no blanket but you These are all the wives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He had two concubines: Maria the Copt and Rayhana, according to Qatada. Another said he had four: Maria, Rayhana, and another woman he had taken captive, and a slave girl whom Zainab bint Jahsh had given to him as a gift. Third: The Almighty’s saying: If you should desire the life of this world and its adornment. If is a condition and its answer is Come on, so the choice is contingent upon a condition. This indicates that the choice and divorce contingent upon a condition are valid and are executed and carried out, contrary to the ignorant innovators who claim that if a man says to his wife: You are divorced if you enter the house, then the divorce does not take place if she enters the house because the legal divorce is the one that is carried out immediately and nothing else. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: His Almighty’s saying Then come is the answer to the condition and it is the action of the group of women from the Almighty’s saying, and it is a call to come to Him. It is said: Come with the meaning of come, it was placed on someone who has majesty and elevation, then the usage became for every caller to come. As for in this place, it is on its origin, as the caller is the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. I have enjoyed you We have already discussed the enjoyment in Al-Baqarah, and it was read I have enjoyed you with a damma on the ‘ayn, and likewise and I have released you with a damma on the ha’ as a new beginning. The beautiful lamp is that it is a divorce according to the Sunnah without harm or obligatory prevention for her. Fifth: The scholars differed on how the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave his wives the choice, with two opinions: The first: He gave them the choice, with God’s permission, to remain married or to divorce them, and they chose to remain married. This was said by Aisha, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Sha’bi, Ibn Shihab, and Rabi’ah. Some of them said: He gave them the choice between this world, so he would separate from them, and the Hereafter, so he would keep them so that they would have a higher status as their husbands had. He did not give them the choice of divorce. This was mentioned by Al-Hasan and Qatadah. Among the Companions, Ali was mentioned in what Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated from him, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not give his wives the choice except between this world and the Hereafter. I said: The first statement is more correct, based on the statement of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, when she was asked about a man giving his wife a choice, and she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave us a choice. Was it a divorce? In another narration: So we chose it, but he did not consider it a divorce. Nothing has been proven from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, except the commanded choice between remaining and divorce. Therefore, he said: O Aisha, I am going to mention something to you, so do not rush into it until you consult your parents. The hadith is well known. It is not mentioned that seeking advice in choosing the world and its adornments over the hereafter, so it is proven that seeking advice either occurred in separation or marriage, and God knows best. Sixth: Scholars differed regarding the woman who has the choice if she chooses her husband. The majority of scholars from the Salaf and others, and the imams of fatwa, said: He is not obligated to divorce her, not once or more. This is the opinion of Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ali, Ibn Mas`ud, Yazd ibn Thabit, Ibn Abbas, and Aisha. Among the Successors are Ata’, Masruq, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Rabi’ah and Ibn Shihab. It was also narrated from Ali and Zayd: If she chooses her husband, then it is one irrevocable divorce. This is the opinion of al-Hasan al-Basri and al-Layth. Al-Khattabi and al-Naqqash narrated it from Malik and they held that his saying: Choose is a euphemism for the occurrence of divorce. If he adds it to her, then a divorce occurs, like his saying: You are irrevocable. The correct opinion is the first, based on the statement of Aisha: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) gave us a choice, and we chose him, and he did not consider it a divorce against us. It was narrated by the two Sahihs. Ibn al-Mundhir said: The hadith of Aisha indicates that if a woman has the choice, then it is not a divorce. It indicates that her choice of herself necessitates a divorce and indicates a third meaning, which is that if a woman has the choice, then it is a divorce in which her husband has the right to take her back, since it is not permissible for the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) to divorce her contrary to what God commanded. This was narrated from Umar, Ibn Mas’ud and Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Abi Layla, al-Thawri and al-Shafi’i said the same. It was narrated from Ali that if she chooses herself, then it is one irrevocable divorce. This is the opinion of Abu Hanifa and his companions. It was narrated by Ibn Khuwaiz Mandad on the authority of Malik. It was narrated on the authority of Zayd ibn Thabit that if she chooses herself, then it is three. This is the opinion of al-Hasan al-Basri, and Malik and al-Layth said the same, because ownership only comes about through that. It was narrated on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him that if she chooses herself, then it is nothing. It was narrated on his authority that if she chooses her husband, then it is one revocable divorce. Seventh: A group of Medinans and others held that giving her ownership and choice are the same, and that judgment is what you have judged in both cases. This is the opinion of Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salamah. Ibn Shaban said: Many of our companions have chosen this view, and it is the opinion of a group of the people of Medina. Abu Umar said: Most of the jurists are of the same opinion, and the well-known opinion of the Maliki school is the difference between them. According to Malik, giving her ownership is what a man says to his wife: I have given you ownership, meaning I have given you ownership of what God has made for me of divorce, one, two, or three. Since it is permissible for him to give her some of that and not some, and he claims that, the correct opinion is his statement with his oath if he denies it. A group of the people of Medina said: He has the right to deny giving her ownership and choice, whether it is the woman who has been consummated with or the first time. This is the well-known opinion of Malik. Ibn Khuwayz Mandad narrated from Malik that the husband can deny giving her the choice of three divorces, and it is considered an irrevocable divorce, as Abu Hanifa said. Abu al-Jahm also said the same. Sahnun said: Most of our companions hold this opinion. And the conclusion of the Maliki school of thought: If a woman has the choice and she has been consummated with has chosen herself, then it is the entire divorce, and if her husband denies it, then we do not deny it to him, and if she chooses only one, then it is nothing, and the choice is absolute, either she takes it or leaves it, because the meaning of choice is release. God Almighty said in the verse of choice: Then come, I will provide for you and release you with a gracious release (al-Ahzab 33:28). So the meaning of release is absolute, God Almighty said: Divorce is twice, then either keep [her] according to acceptable terms or release [her] with good treatment (al-Baqarah 2:229). And release [her] with good treatment is the third divorce. This was narrated from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as mentioned above. And from the meaning, his saying: Choose me or choose yourself requires that he has no right to her if she chooses herself, and he does not own anything from her, if he has given her the right to take out what he owns from her or to stay with him if she chooses him. So if she chooses part of the divorce, she has not acted according to the requirements of the word, and she is like someone who has been given the choice between two things and chooses something other than them. As for the one with whom he has not consummated the marriage, then he has the right to deny her in Choice and ownership if it exceeds one, because it becomes clear immediately. Eighth: The narrations differed from Malik regarding when she has the option. He once said: She has the option as long as she is in the meeting before standing up or engaging in something that indicates aversion. If she does not choose and does not decide anything until they leave their meeting, then whatever was due to her is void. This is what most of the jurists are based on. He once said: She has the option forever as long as it is not known that she left, and this is known by allowing him to have intercourse with her through intercourse or direct contact. Based on this, if she refuses and does not choose anything, he has the right to take her to the judge to sign or drop it. If she refuses, the judge drops her ownership. According to the first opinion, if she takes on something other than that, such as talking, working, walking, or something that is not within the option, as we mentioned, then her option is dropped. Some of our companions used as evidence for this opinion the words of God Almighty: So do not sit with them until they engage in another conversation (An-Nisa’: 140). Also, the husband gave her the right to speak in order to know the option from her, so it became like a contract between them. If she accepts it, otherwise it is dropped, like someone who says: I have given you a gift or pledged allegiance to you. If he accepts, otherwise the ownership remains as it is. This is the opinion of Al-Thawri, the Kufians, Al-Awza’i, and Al-Layth. Al-Shafi'i and Abu Thawr, and it is the preferred opinion of Ibn al-Qasim. The basis of the second narration is that it came into her possession and she gave it to her husband through his giving it to her. When she took possession of it, it was obligatory for it to remain in her possession just as it remained in her husband's possession. I said: This is correct, because he, peace be upon him, said to Aisha: I am going to mention something to you, so do not be hasty until you consult your parents. Narrated by al-Bukhari, and authenticated by al-Tirmidhi. It was mentioned earlier in the chapter, and it is an argument for those who say that if a man gives his wife or her property a choice, she has the right to decide on it, even from their seat. This was narrated from al-Hasan and al-Zuhri, and Malik said it in one of his two narrations. Abu Ubaid said: What we have in this chapter is following the Sunnah regarding Aisha in this hadith, when he gave her the choice until she consulted her parents, and he did not consider her getting up from her seat as an exit from the matter. Al-Marwazi said: This is the most correct of the sayings in my opinion, and Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tahawi said it.
33:29: God Almighty says: And if you desire God and His Messenger and the home of the Hereafter, then indeed, God has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.
33:30: The Almighty’s saying: O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear immorality contains three issues: First: The scholars said: When the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) chose the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), God thanked them for that and said, honoring them: It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that, nor to exchange them for other wives (al-Anfal 2:17). And He explained their ruling over others, saying: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God or to marry his wives after him, ever. And He made the reward for obeying them and the punishment for disobeying them greater than for others, saying: O wives of the Prophet, whoever among you commits a clear immorality, the punishment will be doubled for her. So God informed us that whoever among the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commits an immorality - and God protected His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him) from that, as mentioned in the Hadith of the Slander - the punishment will be doubled for her, due to the nobility of their status, the excellence of their degree, and their precedence over all other women. Likewise, the Shariah has made clear in more than one place, as has been explained more than once, that whenever sanctities are doubled and violated, the punishments will be doubled. For this reason, the punishment for a free man is doubled for a slave, and for a previously married woman is doubled for a virgin. It was said: Since the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were the source of revelation and the abode of God’s commands and prohibitions, the command was stronger for them and was more binding on them due to their status than on others, so the reward and punishment were doubled for them. It was also said: This is due to the great harm in their crimes of harming the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so the punishment was commensurate with the greatness of the crime of harming the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). God the Almighty said: Indeed, those who harm God and His Messenger - God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter. Al-Kaya al-Tabari chose this opinion. Second: Some people said: If adultery had been committed by one of them - and God had protected them from that - then she would have been punished twice because of her great punishment, just as the punishment for a free woman is increased over that for a slave woman. Punishment means punishment. God the Almighty said: And let a party of the believers witness their punishment. Based on this, the meaning of double is multiples or twice. Abu Ubaidah said: The double of something is two things until it becomes three. Abu Amr said the same, as al-Tabari narrated from him, so two punishments like it are multiplied to it, so it becomes three punishments. al-Tabari deemed it weak. Likewise, it is not correct, even though the wording indicates a possibility. The reward being twice invalidates this statement, because the punishment for an immoral act is equivalent to the reward for obedience, as Ibn Atiyyah said. al-Nahhas said: Abu Amr differentiated between multiplies and multiplies. He said: multiplies for the many times, and multiplies twice. He read multiplies for this reason. Abu Ubaidah said: (He doubles her punishment) means making it three punishments. An-Nahhas said: The distinction that Abu Amr and Abu Ubaidah came with is not known to any linguist that I know of. The meaning of (He doubles and He weakens) is the same, that is, He makes it double, as you say: If you pay me a dirham, I will pay you double it, meaning twice as much, meaning two dirhams. And the evidence for this is We will give her her reward twice over, and the punishment will not be more than the reward. And He said in another place, Give them double the punishment, meaning twice. Muammar narrated on the authority of Qatadah, The punishment will be doubled for her twice over, he said: The punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: It appears that by double he meant double, because he said, We will give her her reward twice over. As for wills, if a person bequeaths to a person twice his child’s share, then it is a will that he be given three times his share, because wills are based on custom among people, and the interpretation of the word of God is based on the Arabic language, and double in Arabic means like to what is in excess, and it is not limited to double. It is said, This is double this, meaning like it. And this is double it, meaning twice it. So double in origin means an unlimited increase. God the Most High said, For those is a double reward, and He did not mean like or double. All of this is the opinion of Al-Azhari. In An-Nur we have already mentioned the difference of opinion regarding the punishment for slandering one of them, and praise be to God. Third: Abu Rafi’ said: ‘Umar may God be pleased with him used to recite Surah Yusuf and Surah Al-Ahzab frequently in the morning prayer. When he reached O wives of the Prophet, he would raise his voice. He was asked about that, and he said: Remind them of the covenant. The majority of scholars read Man ya’t with a ya’. Likewise, Man yaqunt based on the word man. Qunut means obedience, as mentioned earlier. Ya’qub read Man ta’t and Taqunt with a ta’ above, based on the meaning. Some people said: When a lewdness is definite, it refers to adultery and sodomy. When it is indefinite, it refers to all other sins. When it is described, it refers to disobedience to one’s husband and corrupt treatment of him. A group said: Rather, His statement with a manifest lewdness includes all sins. The same applies to lewdness, however it is mentioned. Ibn Kathir read Mubinnah with a fatha over the ya’. Nafi’ and Abu Amr read it with a kasra over it. A group read: (Nadhi'aaf) with a damma on the noon and the accusative of (al-'adhaab). This is the reading of Ibn Muhaisin. This is a reciprocal verb from one root, like Taraqt an'al and Aaqabat al-Lis. Nafi', Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read (Yudhi'aaf) with a ya' and a fatha on the 'ayn, (al-'adhaab) in the nominative case. This is the reading of al-Hasan, Ibn Kathir and 'Isa. Ibn Kathir and Ibn 'Amir read (Nadhi'aaf) with a kasra on the doubled 'ayn, (al-'adhaab) in the accusative case. Muqatil said: This doubling of the punishment only applies to the Hereafter, because the reward will also be given twice in the Hereafter. This is good because the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not commit an immorality that warrants a hadd punishment. Ibn 'Abbas said: The wife of the Prophet never rebelled; she only betrayed faith and obedience. Some of the commentators said: The punishment they were promised with (double) is the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, so too is the reward. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is weak, unless the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) were not exempted from the punishment of the Hereafter and the punishment of this world, as is the case with people, based on the hadith of Ubadah ibn as-Samit. This is something that has not been narrated about the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and it has not been preserved to confirm it. The scholars of tafsir agree that the noble provision is Paradise, as mentioned by an-Nahhas.
33:31: And whoever among you is obedient to God and His Messenger and does righteousness - We will give her her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a noble provision.
33:32: God the Almighty said: O wives of the Prophet, you are not like anyone among women if you fear God meaning in virtue and honor. He said: (like anyone) and did not say like one, because one is negated from masculine and feminine, singular and plural. It may also be said of something that is not human, such as: there is no one among them, neither a sheep nor a camel. Women were mentioned specifically because among those mentioned before were Asiya and Mary. Qatada pointed to this, and the difference in preference between them was mentioned earlier in Al Imran, so reflect on it there. Then he said: if you fear God meaning you fear God. So he explained that virtue is only complete for them on the condition of fearing God, because of what God granted them of the company of the Messenger and the great position they held with him, and the revelation of the Quran concerning them. God the Almighty said: And do not speak in a soft voice in the accusative case of prohibition, except that it is constructed like the past tense. This is the school of thought of Sibawayh, meaning do not speak softly. God commanded them to have eloquent speech and articulate words, and not to speak in a way that would show a connection in the heart with what appears soft, as was the case with Arab women when they spoke to men in a soft and softened voice, like the speech of nannies and prostitutes. So He forbade them from such a thing. God the Almighty says: Fetamaa in the accusative case as a response to the prohibition. He in whose heart is disease meaning doubt and hypocrisy, from Qatada and Al-Suddi. It was said: longing for immorality, which is lewdness and flirting, said Ikrimah. This is more correct, and hypocrisy has no role in this verse. Abu Hatim narrated that Al-A'raj read (Fetamaa) with a fatha on the yaa and a kasra on the meem. An-Nahhas said: I think this is a mistake, that he read (Fetamaa) with a fatha on the meem and a kasra on the 'ayn in apposition to (takhadduna), so this is a good and fine interpretation. It is permissible for (Fetamaa) to mean submission or speech. God the Almighty says: And speak in an appropriate manner. Ibn Abbas said: He commanded them to enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. A woman is encouraged, when addressing strangers and those forbidden to her by marriage, to speak harshly without raising her voice, as a woman is commanded to lower her voice. In short, an appropriate speech is the correct speech that is not rejected by the Sharia or people.
33:33: The Almighty’s saying: And abide in your houses and do not display yourselves like that of the times of the former ignorance. There are four issues in this: The first: The Almighty’s saying: And dwell The majority read (and dwell) with a kasra on the qaf. Asim and Nafi’ read it with a fatha. As for the first reading, it has two interpretations: One of them: that it is from dignity, as you say, waqar yaqrur waqar, meaning he settled, and the matter is qar, and for women qarn, like ‘Adan, there is a weight. The second interpretation: which is the saying of al-Mubarrad, that it is from qarārār, as you say: iqarār bi-l-makān with a fatha on the ra’, he acknowledged, and the original is iqarna, with a kasra on the ra’, so the first ra’ was deleted for ease, as they said in dhallaltu: zalta, and musasat: māsta, and they transferred its vowel to the qaf, and they dispensed with the alif of connection due to the vowel of the qaf. Abu Ali said: Rather, the Ra’ was replaced by a Ya’ due to the undesirability of doubling, as it was replaced in Qirat and Dinar, and the vowel of the letter it was replaced from would be the Ya’, so the meaning would be Iqirna, then the vowel of the Ya’ is transferred to the Qaf due to the undesirability of moving the Ya’ with a Kasra, so the Ya’ is dropped due to the meeting of two Sukoons, and the Hamzat al-Wasl is dropped due to the movement of what follows it, so it becomes (Qarn). As for the reading of the people of Madinah and Asim, it is according to the dialect of the Arabs: I resided in the place if I stayed there with a Kasra on the Ra’ Iqarra with a Fatha on the Qaf, from the root Hamd yahamd, and it is the dialect of the people of Hijaz, mentioned by Abu Ubaid in Al-Gharib Al-Musannaf on the authority of Al-Kisa’i, and he is one of his most prominent teachers, and Al-Zajjaj and others mentioned it. The original is (Iqarna), the first Ra’ was deleted due to the burden of doubling, and its vowel was transferred to the Qaf, so you say Qarn. Al-Farra’ said: It is like you say: Ihsata Sahibak, meaning: Did you feel? Abu Uthman Al-Mazini said: “It was stated in the Kasra no other form, from the word ‘qarrat al-‘ayn’ the delight of the eye. It is not permissible to state ‘qarrat fi al-makan’ the place’ the Kasra, rather it is ‘qarrat’ with the Fatha on the Ra’. What is rejected from this does not detract from the recitation if it is proven from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so what is proven from him regarding the recitation is used as evidence for the correctness of the language. Abu Hatim also said that ‘Qarn’ has no school of thought in the speech of the Arabs. Al-Nahhas said: As for Abu Hatim’s statement: “It has no school of thought,” it has been contradicted, and there are two schools of thought regarding it: One of them is what Al-Kisa’i narrated, and the other is what I heard Ali bin Sulayman say. He said: It is from ‘qarrat bih ‘ayn’, ‘aqarra’ the delight of the eye, and the meaning is: And be content with it in your homes. This is a good interpretation, except that the hadith indicates that it is from the first. As it was narrated that ‘Ammar said to ‘Aisha may God be pleased with her: ‘God has commanded you to be content in your home.’ She said: ‘O Abu Al-Yaqzan, you have not ceased to speak the truth!’ He said: ‘Praise be to God who has put them on your tongue.’” Ibn Abi Ubla read wa-aqarna with an alif wasl and two ra’s, the first one broken. Second: The meaning of this verse is the command to remain in one’s home. Although the address is to the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), others are included in the same sense. This would be the case if there was no evidence that specifically addresses all women. How could it be that the Shari’ah is replete with the command for women to remain in their homes and refrain from leaving them except in cases of necessity, as has been mentioned previously in more than one place? So God the Most High commanded the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to remain in their homes, and addressed them with this to honor them. He forbade them from displaying their beauty, and indicated that this was the practice of the first Jahiliyyah, saying: And do not display yourselves like that of the times of the first Jahiliyyah. The meaning of displaying one’s beauty has been mentioned previously in An-Nur. Its true meaning is to reveal what has been covered, which is better. It is derived from breadth. It is said that one has a tooth crown if they are scattered, as Al-Mubarrad said. People differed regarding the first Jahiliyyah. Some said that it was the time when Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was born, and that women would wear a pearl shield and walk in the middle of the street, exposing themselves to men. Al-Hakam ibn Uyaynah said: Between Adam and Noah, which was eight hundred years, and they were told of a reprehensible life story. Ibn Abbas said: Between Noah and Idris. Al-Kalbi said: Between Noah and Abraham. It was said: Women used to wear a pearl shield with unstitched sides, and thin clothes without covering their bodies. A group said: Between Moses and Jesus. Al-Sha’bi said: “Between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon him.” Abu Al-Aaliyah said: It was the time of David and Solomon, during which women used to wear a shirt made of pearls with unstitched sides. Abu Al-Abbas Al-Mubarrad said: And the first Jahiliyyah is as the ignorant Jahiliyyah say. He said: “Women in the ignorant Jahiliyyah used to show what was shameful to show, to the point that a woman would sit with her husband and her friend, and her friend would be alone with what was above the lower garment and her husband would be alone with what was below the lower garment, and one of them might ask his companion for something else.” Mujahid said: “Women used to walk among men, and that was tabarru’ showing off. Ibn Atiyyah said: What appears to me is that he referred to the pre-Islamic period that they had fallen into, so they were ordered to change their ways of life there, which was the way of the infidels before the Shari’ah, because they had no jealousy, and the women were not veiled, and he made it more appropriate in relation to what they were upon, and the meaning is not that there was another pre-Islamic period. The name pre-Islamic period was given to that period before Islam, so they said: pre-Islamic among the poets. Ibn Abbas said in Al-Bukhari: I heard my father say about pre-Islamic period, and other than that. I said: This is a good statement. It is objected that the Arabs were people of austerity and hardship for the most part, and that luxury and display of adornment only happened in previous times, and that is what is meant by the first ignorance, and that the intended meaning of the verse is to differ from those who came before them in walking in a coquettish manner and flirting and displaying their beauty to men, and other things that are not permissible according to the Shari’ah. This includes all statements and is general to them, so they should stay at home, and if there is a need to go out, then let it be in a completely relaxed and comfortable manner. And God is the Grantor of success. Third: Al-Tha'labi and others mentioned that whenever Aisha may God be pleased with her recited this verse, she would cry until her veil was soaked. It was mentioned that Sawda was asked: Why don't you perform Hajj or Umrah as your sisters do? She said: I have performed Hajj and Umrah, and God has commanded me to stay in my house. The narrator said: By God, she did not leave the door of her room until her funeral procession had left. May God be pleased with her! Ibn al-Arabi said: I have entered more than a thousand villages, and I have never seen women who protected their families or were more chaste than the women of Nablus, the place where Abraham (peace be upon him) was thrown into the fire. I stayed there and I never saw a woman on the road during the day except on Fridays, for they would go out until the mosque was filled with them. Then, when the prayer was over and they returned to their homes, I would not see a single one of them until the next Friday. I saw chaste women in Al-Aqsa Mosque who did not leave their place of seclusion until they were martyred there. Fourth: Ibn Atiyyah said: Aisha’s may God be pleased with her crying was only because of her travel during the Battle of the Camel, and then Ammar said to her: God has commanded you to remain in your home. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The Rafidah may God curse them relied on this verse to blame the Mother of the Believers Aisha may God be pleased with her when they said that she disobeyed the command of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when she went out leading armies, participating in wars, and entering into the difficult situation of stabbing and striking, in a manner that was not imposed on her and was not permissible for her. They said: Uthman was besieged, and when she saw that, she ordered her mounts to be brought forward to go to Mecca. Marwan said to her: Stay here, O Mother of the Believers, and repel these rabble, for reconciling people is better than your Hajj. Ibn Al-Arabi said: Our scholars may God have mercy on them said: Aisha may God be pleased with her vowed to perform Hajj before the Fitna discord, and she did not see any reason to abandon her vow. If she had gone out during that rebellion, it would have been right for her. As for her going out to the Battle of the Camel, she did not go out for a war, but the people clung to her and complained to her about the great tribulation and the quarrel they had become. They hoped for her blessing and hoped to feel shy before her if she stood up to the people. She thought that, so she went out following the example of God in His saying: “There is no good in much of their private conversation, except for those who enjoin charity or righteousness or conciliation between people.” And His saying: “And if two parties among the believers should fight, then make peace between them.” The command to make peace is addressed to all people, male and female, free and slave. God, the Almighty, did not will, by His foreordained decree and His enforceable judgment, that reconciliation should take place. Rather, quarrels and wounds occurred until both sides were almost annihilated. Some of them took the camel and hamstrung it. When the camel fell on its side, Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr caught up with Aisha, may God be pleased with her, and carried her to Basra. She set out with thirty women, whom Ali accompanied until they delivered her to Madinah, pious, devout, diligent, and successful in interpreting and rewarded for what she did, since everyone who strives in judgments is correct. The name of this camel was mentioned in An-Nahl, and it is by this that day it is known. God the Almighty said: {And establish prayer and give zakah and obey God and His Messenger} meaning, in what He has commanded and forbidden. {God only desires to keep away the uncleanness from you, O people of the House} Al-Zajjaj said: It was said that it refers to the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And it was said that it refers to his wives and family who are the people of his House, as will be explained later. And (the people of the House) is in the accusative case of praise. He said: Or if you wish, it is in the form of a substitute. He said: The nominative and genitive cases are permissible. An-Nahhas said: If it is in the genitive case as a substitute for the kaf and the mim, it is not permissible according to Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Yazid. He said: It is not a substitute for the female addressee or the one being addressed, because they do not need clarification. {And purify you with a thorough purification} is a verbal noun that contains a sense of emphasis.
33:34: There are three issues: First: The Almighty’s saying: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom. These words indicate that the people of the house are his women. The scholars differed regarding the people of the house, who are they? Ata’, Ikrimah and Ibn Abbas said: They are his wives specifically, no men with them. They believed that the house refers to the dwellings of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), based on the Almighty’s saying: And remember what is recited in your houses. A group, including Al-Kalbi, said: They are Ali, Fatimah, Al-Hasan and Al-Hussein specifically. There are hadiths on this topic from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). They cited as evidence the words of God the Almighty: That He may remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the House, and purify you with the letter mim. If it had been for women specifically, it would have been from you and purify you. However, it is possible that it was used in the form of family, as a man may say to his companion: How are your family? meaning your wife and women, and he may reply: They are fine. God the Almighty said: Do you wonder at the decree of God? The mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, O people of the House. What appears from the verse is that it is general and includes all members of the household, including spouses and others. The statement, and purifies you, is because the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Ali, Hasan, and Husayn were among them. When both male and female are present, the masculine gender is predominant. Therefore, the verse requires that the wives are among the members of the household, because the verse is about them and they are being addressed, as indicated by the context of the speech. And God knows best.
