Umm Salamah said: “This verse was revealed in my house, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn and entered with them under a Khaybar cloak and said: ‘These are my family’ - and he recited the verse - and said: ‘O God, remove uncleanness from them and purify them with a thorough purification.’ Umm Salamah said: ‘Am I with them, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘You remain where you are and you are upon good.’” Narrated by al-Tirmidhi and others, who said: This is a strange hadith. Al-Qushayri said: “Umm Salamah said: I put my head into the cloak and said: ‘Am I among them, O Messenger of God?’ He said: ‘Yes.’” Al-Tha'labi said: They are Banu Hashim. This indicates that the house refers to the lineage, so Al-Abbas, his paternal uncles and his paternal uncles are among them. Something similar was narrated from Zayd ibn Arqam may God be pleased with them all. According to Al-Kalbi, his statement, And remember is the beginning of addressing God, the Most High, i.e., addressing the command of God, the Most High, to the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as an admonition and enumerating the blessings by mentioning what is recited in their homes of the verses of God and wisdom. The scholars of ta'wil said: The verses of God are the Qur'an. And wisdom is the Sunnah. The correct view is that his statement, And remember is linked to what precedes it. He said, From you because he said, People. People are masculine, so He called them - even if they were females - by the masculine name, and that is why it became From you. The statement of Al-Kalbi and his likes should not be taken into account, as there are things he said in this interpretation that, if he had been in the time of the righteous predecessors, they would have prevented him from doing that and restricted him. All the verses, from His saying: O Prophet, tell your wives to His saying: Indeed, God is Kind and All-Knowing, are arranged one after the other. So how could there be separate speech in the middle for others?! This is something that happened in the reports: “When this verse was revealed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he called for Ali, Fatimah, Hasan, and Husayn. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took a cloak and wrapped it around them, then he pointed to the sky and said: ‘O God, these are my family. O God, remove uncleanness from them and purify them with a thorough purification.’” This is a supplication from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to them after the verse was revealed. He wanted to include them in the verse in which the wives were addressed. Al-Kalbi and those who agreed with him made it specifically for them, but it is a supplication for them outside of the revelation. Second: The word remembrance has three possible meanings: First: Remember the place of blessing, as God has placed you in homes where God’s verses and wisdom are recited. Second: Remember the verses of God and appreciate their value, and reflect on them so that they are on your mind and you may take heed from God’s admonitions. Whoever is in this state should improve their actions. Third: Remember means memorize, recite, and teach them on your tongues. It is as if God is saying: Memorize God’s commands and prohibitions, and that is what is recited in your homes from the verses of God. So God the Almighty commanded them to report what was revealed of the Quran in their homes, and what they saw of the Prophet’s actions (peace and blessings be upon him) and what they heard of his sayings, so that they may convey that to the people, so that they may act upon it and follow its example. This indicates the permissibility of accepting the report of an individual, whether from men or women, in matters of religion. Third: Ibn al-Arabi said: “In this verse there is a wonderful issue, which is that God the Almighty commanded His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) to convey what was revealed to him of the Qur’an, and to teach what he knew of the religion. So if he recited to one person or whatever he happened to know, the obligation was dropped from him, and it was upon whoever heard him to convey it to others. He was not obligated to mention it to all of the Companions, nor was it upon him, if his wives knew that, to go out to the people and tell them such and such was revealed or such and such was. For this reason we say: It is permissible to act on the report of Busrah regarding the obligation of ablution after touching the penis, because she narrated what she heard and conveyed what she memorized. It is not necessary for him to convey that to the men, as Abu Hanifa said, although it was narrated from Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas and Ibn ‘Umar.”
33:35: There are two issues: First: Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Umm Amara Al-Ansariyya that she came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: I do not see everything mentioned except for men, and I do not see women mentioned at all! Then this verse was revealed: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women (verse). This is a good and rare hadith. The Muslims is the subject of indeed. “And the Muslim women” is an appositive to it. The Basrans allow them to be raised, but Al-Farra’ does not allow it except in cases where the i’rab is not clear. Second: In this verse, God the Almighty began by mentioning Islam, which encompasses faith and the actions of the limbs. Then He mentioned faith specifically, highlighting that it is the greatness and pillar of Islam. And the obedient is the worshipper and the obedient. And the truthful: meaning that he fulfills what he was entrusted with. And the patient in refraining from desires and in performing acts of obedience, whether in difficulty or in pleasure. And the humble is the one who fears God. And the one who gives charity, both obligatory and voluntary. And it was said: specifically, the obligatory, but the first is more praiseworthy. And the fasting person is the same. And those who guard their private parts, men and women meaning from what is impermissible, such as adultery and other things. And in His statement, and the guarding women, there is an omission indicated by the previous, meaning: and their guardians, so He sufficed with what came before. And in and those who remember, there is also a similar statement, and similar to it is the saying of the poet: And as if its backs were covered in blood, and I felt a golden color Sibawayh narrated: (color of gold) in the accusative case. The nominative case is only permissible with the deletion of the ha’, as if he said: and I sensed it, for the one who raised color. And the one who remembers is said to be at the end of prayers, in the morning and evening, in bed and upon waking from sleep. All of this has been presented in detail in its places, and what results from it of benefits and rulings, so there is no need to repeat it. Praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds. Mujahid said: One does not remember God often until he remembers Him while standing, sitting and lying down. Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, said: Whoever wakes up his family at night and they pray four rak'ahs, they will be recorded among those who remember God frequently, both men and women.
33:36: "It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error." God Almighty says: “It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any option in their decision. And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.” There are four issues: The first: Qatada, Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid narrated about the reason for the revelation of this verse: That the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) proposed to Zaynab bint Jahsh, who was his cousin. She thought that the proposal was for himself, but when it became clear that he wanted her for Zayd, she disliked it and refused. So the verse was revealed. Zaynab then submitted and married him. In another narration: She refused, and so did her brother Abdullah, because of her lineage from Quraysh, and that Zayd had been a slave only yesterday, until this verse was revealed. Her brother said to him: Order me to do whatever you wish, so he married her to Zayd. It was said that it was revealed about Umm Kulthum bint Uqba ibn Abi Mu’ayt, who had offered herself to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he married her to Zayd ibn Haritha. She and her brother disliked that and said: We only wanted the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so we married someone else. So the verse was revealed because of that, so they agreed to marry Zayd, as Ibn Zayd said. Al-Hasan said: It is not permissible for a believing man or woman to disobey God Almighty and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they command something. Second: The words what was, “what should be,” and the like mean prohibition and prevention. They are used to forbid something and rule that it should not happen, as in this verse. Perhaps the impossibility of that thing is rational, as in the saying of God the Almighty: It is not for you to cause its trees to grow An-Naml 27:60. Perhaps the knowledge of its impossibility is based on Islamic law, as in the saying of God the Almighty: It is not for a human being that God should give him the Scripture and wisdom and prophethood Al-Imran 3:79, and His saying: And it is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil Ash-Shura 42:51. Perhaps it is used in recommended acts, as in the saying: It is not for you, so-and-so, to abandon the voluntary acts, and the like. Third: This verse is evidence, indeed a clear text, that compatibility is not a consideration in lineage, but rather in religion, contrary to the views of Malik, Al-Shafi’i, Al-Mughirah, and Sahnun. This is because freed slaves married within the Quraysh. Zayd married Zaynab bint Jahsh. Al-Miqdad ibn Al-Aswad married Duba’ah bint Az-Zubayr. Abu Hudhayfah married Salim to Fatimah bint Al-Walid ibn Utbah. Bilal married the sister of Abd Al-Rahman ibn Awf. This meaning has been mentioned before in more than one place. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: that they should have choice in their affair. The Kufians read it with a ya’. This is the preferred choice of Abu Ubaid because he differentiated between the feminine and its verb. The rest read it with a ta’ because the word is feminine, so feminizing its verb is good. The masculine form is based on the fact that khayra means choice, so khayra is a verbal noun meaning choice. Ibn al-Sameeq read khayra with a sukoon on the ya’. This verse is part of the Almighty’s statement: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves al-Ahzab 33:6. Then God threatened and informed that whoever disobeys God and His Messenger has gone astray. This is the clearest evidence of the view of the majority of our jurists, the jurists of Imam al-Shafi’i and some of the legal theorists, that the form af’al indicates obligation in its original form, because God the Blessed and Exalted denied the choice of the accountable person when hearing His command and the command of His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then He called the one who remained free to choose when the command was issued the name of disobedience, then He linked the disobedience to that misguidance, so it was necessary to interpret the command as obligation. And God knows best.
33:37: "And when you said to him whom God had bestowed favor upon and you had bestowed favor, 'Keep your wife to yourself and fear God,' while you concealed within yourself that which God was about to disclose and you feared the people, while God has more right that you should fear Him. So when Zaid had no longer any need for her, We married her to you in order that there should be no blame upon the believers concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need for them. And the command of God is to be done." There are nine issues: The first: Al-Tirmidhi narrated: Ali bin Hajar narrated: Dawud bin Az-Zubayr narrated from Dawud bin Abi Hind from Ash-Sha’bi from Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: “If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had concealed anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse: ‘And when you said to him whom God had bestowed favor upon’ meaning with Islam, ‘and whom you had bestowed favor’ with emancipation, so you emancipated him, ‘Keep your wife to yourself and fear God.’ And you concealed within yourself that which God was about to reveal, and you feared the people, while God has more right that you should fear Him’ until His saying, ‘and the command of God is to be done.’ And when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her, they said: He married the wife of his son. So God, the Most High, revealed: ‘Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets.’” The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) adopted him when he was young, and he lived until he became a man called Zayd ibn Muhammad. Then God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: “Call them by the names of their fathers; that is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients.” So-and-so is the client of so-and-so, and so-and-so is the brother of so-and-so. That is more just in the sight of God, meaning more equitable. Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a strange hadith that has been narrated on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of ‘A’ishah may God be pleased with her. She said: “If the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had concealed any of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse: “And when you said to him whom God had bestowed favor upon and whom you had bestowed favor.” This word was not narrated in full. I said: This is the amount that Muslim included in his Sahih, and it is the same that Al-Tirmidhi authenticated in his Jami’. In Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Anas bin Malik: That this verse, And you conceal within yourself that which God is to bring to light, was revealed concerning Zaynab bint Jahsh and Zayd bin Haritha. Umar, Ibn Mas’ud, Aisha, and Al-Hasan said: God did not reveal to His Messenger a verse more difficult for him than this verse. Al-Hasan and Aisha said: If the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had concealed any of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse because of its difficulty for him. It was narrated in the hadith that: Zayd went to bed in the evening, and Zayd said: And Zayd could not control me, and I cannot control him except what God has prevented him from me, so he cannot control me. This is the narration of Abu Usmah Nuh bin Abi Maryam, who traces the hadith back to Zaynab that she said that. In some narrations: That Zayd felt a pang of anger when he wanted to approach her, so this is close to that. Zayd came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: Zaynab hurts me with her tongue and does this and that, and I want to divorce her. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: Keep your wife and fear God (al-An’am 2:17). So Zayd divorced her, and then the following verse was revealed: And when you said to him whom God had bestowed favor and whom you had bestowed favor (al-An’am 2:17). People differed in the interpretation of this verse. Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and a group of commentators, including al-Tabari and others, said that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) expressed his approval of Zaynab bint Jahsh while she was married to Zayd, and he was eager for Zayd to divorce her so he could marry her. Then when Zayd informed him that he wanted to divorce her, and that he complained about her harsh speech, disobedience to orders, her hurtful tongue, and her pride in her honor, he said to him: Fear God - that is, in what you say about her - and keep your wife, while he was concealing his eagerness for Zayd to divorce her. This is what he was hiding in his heart, but he adhered to what was required of him in enjoining what is right. Muqatil said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married Zaynab bint Jahsh to Zayd and she stayed with him for a while. Then one day, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Zayd seeking him. He saw Zaynab standing. She was white, beautiful, and well-built, one of the most perfect women of Quraysh. He fell in love with her and said: Glory be to God, the Changer of hearts. Zaynab heard the glorification and mentioned it to Zayd. Zayd became alert and said: O Messenger of God, give me permission to divorce her, for she is arrogant, acts haughty toward me, and hurts me with her tongue. He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Keep your wife and fear God. It was said: God sent a wind that lifted the curtain while Zaynab was spending her time in her home. He saw Zaynab and it fell in love with him, and it fell in love with Zaynab that she had fallen in love with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). That was when he came seeking Zayd. Zayd came and she told him about that, so it fell in Zayd’s heart to divorce her. Ibn Abbas said: And you hide in your soul love for her. And you fear the people means you feel shy of them. It was said: You would fear and hate the scholars of the Muslims if you said he started it, and they say he ordered a man to divorce his wife and then married her after he divorced her. And God has more right that you should fear Him in all circumstances. It was said: God has more right that you should be ashamed of Him, and do not order Zaid to keep his wife after God informed you that she would be your wife, so God rebuked him for all of this. It was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn: “God had revealed to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Zayd would divorce Zaynab and that he would marry her by virtue of God’s marriage to her. When Zayd complained to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about Zaynab’s behavior and that she did not obey him, and informed him that he wanted to divorce her, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, as a matter of good manners and advice: ‘Fear God in what you say and keep your wife, knowing that he will separate from her and marry her.’ This is what he concealed in his soul, and he did not want to order him to divorce her when he knew that he would marry her. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, feared that people would say that he would marry Zaynab after Zayd, since he was his freed slave, and he had ordered him to divorce her. So God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rebuked him for this degree of fearing people in something that God had permitted him, by saying: ‘Keep her, knowing that he will divorce her.’ And He informed him that God is more deserving of fear, that is, in every situation.” Our scholars, may God have mercy on them, said: This statement is the best that has been said in interpreting this verse, and it is the one that the people of investigation among the commentators and the established scholars such as Az-Zuhri, Judge Bakr ibn Al-Ala’ Al-Qushayri, Judge Abu Bakr ibn Al-Arabi and others agreed upon. What is meant by God’s statement, and you fear people, is the hypocrites’ rumour that He forbade marrying the wives of one’s sons and married his son’s wife. As for the narration that the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, loved Zaynab, the wife of Zayd, and that some of the licentious people may have used the word love, this only comes from someone who is ignorant of the infallibility of the Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, from such a thing, or who takes his sanctity lightly. At-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim said in Nawader Al-Usul, and he attributed his statement to Ali ibn Al-Hussein, “Ali ibn Al-Hussein brought this from the treasury of knowledge, a gem among gems and a pearl among pearls, that God rebuked him because He had informed him that this would be one of his wives, so how could He then say to Zayd, ‘Keep your wife for yourself, and keep you for fear that people would say, ‘He married his son’s wife,’ while God has more right that you should fear Him.” Al-Nahhas said: Some scholars said: This is not a sin on the part of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Do you not see that he was not commanded to repent or seek forgiveness for it? It may be that something is not a sin, but something else is better than it, and he concealed that to himself for fear that it would tempt people. Second: Ibn al-Arabi said: If it is asked, why did he say to him, Keep your wife when God had informed him that she was his wife? We say: He wanted to test from him what God did not know about his desire for her or his desire for her, so Zayd showed him aversion and dislike for her that he had not known about his affair with her. If it is asked, How could he order him to hold on to her when he knew that separation was inevitable? This is a contradiction. We say: Rather, it is correct for sound objectives, to establish proof and know the consequences. Do you not see that God, the Most High, orders the servant to believe when He knows that he will not believe? So there is nothing in the contradiction of the object of the order with the object of knowledge that prevents it from being ordered rationally and wisely. This is precious knowledge, so be certain of it and accept it. His statement, And fear God, means in divorcing her, so do not divorce her. He intended a prohibition of purification, not a prohibition of prohibition, because it is better not to divorce her. It was also said: Fear God and do not criticize her in relation to arrogance and the harm caused by the husband. And conceal in your soul was said to mean his heart’s attachment. It was also said: Zayd’s separation from her. It was said: He knew that Zaid would divorce her because God had informed him of that. Third: It was narrated on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said to Zaid: I do not find in myself anyone more trustworthy than you, so propose to Zainab Ali. He said: So I went and turned my back to her out of respect for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and proposed to her. She was happy and said: I will not do anything until my Lord commands me. So she went to her mosque and the Qur’an was revealed, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her and consummated the marriage with her. I said: The meaning of this hadith is established in Sahih. An-Nasa'i included a translation for it A woman's prayer when she proposes marriage and seeks guidance from her Lord. The imams narrated, and the wording is from Muslim, on the authority of Anas, who said: “When Zainab's waiting period ended, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said to Zaid: ‘Mention her to me.’ So Zaid went until he came to her while she was kneading her dough. He said: ‘When I saw her, it became so great in my heart that I could not look at her because the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) mentioned her, so I turned my back on her and turned back on my heels. I said: ‘O Zainab, has the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sent someone to remind you?’ She said: ‘I will not do anything until my Lord commands me.’ So she went to her place of prayer and the Qur’an was revealed. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) came and entered upon her without permission. He said: ‘I saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) feeding us bread and meat when the day was very long…’” The hadith. In another narration, Until they abandoned it. In a narration from Anas also, he said: “I never saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) hold a wedding feast for any of his wives as he held for Zaynab. He slaughtered a sheep.” Our scholars said: His (peace be upon him) saying to Zayd, Mention her to me, means propose to her, as explained in the first hadith. This was a test and trial for Zayd, to demonstrate his patience, submission, and obedience. I said: It may be inferred from this that a person may say to his friend: Propose marriage to so-and-so for his divorced wife, and there is nothing wrong with that. And God knows best. Fourth: When she entrusted her affair to God and it was valid to entrust her to Him, God took charge of her marriage. That is why He said: And when Zaid had no longer any need for her, We married her to you. Imam Ja’far ibn Muhammad narrated on the authority of his forefathers that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: We married her to you. When God informed him of that, he consummated the marriage with her without permission, nor renewing the marriage contract, nor specifying a dowry, nor anything that would be a condition of our rights or a law for us. This is one of the characteristics of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), which no one else shares with him, according to the consensus of the Muslims. That is why Zaynab used to boast to the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), saying: Your fathers married you, and God married me. Narrated by Al-Nasa’i on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: Zaynab used to boast to the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), saying: God the Almighty married me from the heaven. It was in this context that the verse of hijab was revealed, which will come later. Fifth: The one who has been blessed in this verse is Zayd ibn Haritha, as we have explained, and his story was presented at the beginning of the Surah. It was narrated that his uncle met him one day, and he had come to Mecca on some business. He said: What is your name, boy? He said: Zaid. He said: Whose son? He said: Ibn Haritha. He said: Ibn Sharahil al-Kalbi. He said: What is your mother’s name? He said: Sa’da. I was with my maternal uncles, Tayy. So he hugged him to his chest. He sent for his brother and his people, and they came. They wanted him to stay with them. They said: Whose are you? He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah. So they came to him and said: This is our son, so return him to us. He said: Show him to him, and if he chooses you, then take his hand. So he sent for Zaid and said: Do you know these people? He said: Yes, this is my father, this is my brother, and this is my uncle. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What kind of companion have I been to you? He cried and said: Why did you ask me about that? He said: I give you the choice. If you want to join them, then follow, and if you want to stay, then I am one of those you know. So he said: I do not choose anyone over you. So his uncle pulled him and said: O Zaid, you chose slavery over your father and uncle. So he said: By God, servitude to Muhammad is more beloved to me than being with you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Bear witness that I am an heir and the one to be inherited. And it was not ceased to be said: Zayd ibn Muhammad until the words of God Almighty were revealed: Call them by the names of their fathers and Muhammad is not the father of any of your men were revealed. Sixth: Imam Abu Al-Qasim Abdul Rahman Al-Suhayli may God be pleased with him said: He was called Zayd ibn Muhammad until the verse, Call them by the names of their fathers, was revealed. He said, I am Zayd ibn Haritha. And it was forbidden for him to say, I am Zayd ibn Muhammad. But when this honor and pride was taken away from him, and God knew how much he loathed that, He honored him with a distinction that He did not give to any of the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), which is that He named him in the Qur’an, as God the Almighty said, And when Zayd had no longer any need for her, meaning Zaynab. And whoever God the Almighty mentioned by his name in the Wise Remembrance until his name became a part of the Qur’an recited in the prayer niches, He praised him greatly. This was a comfort to him and a compensation for the pride in Muhammad’s (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fatherhood of him. Haven't you seen the words of Ubayy ibn Ka'b when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: God has commanded me to recite to you such-and-such a Surah? He wept and said: Were you mentioned there? His weeping was out of joy when he was informed that God had mentioned him. So how about someone whose name has become a part of the Quran that is recited immortally and will never perish? The people of this world will recite it when they recite the Quran, and the people of Paradise will do the same forever. It will always be on the tongues of the believers, just as it will always be mentioned specifically before the Lord of the Worlds. For the Quran is the eternal speech of God, and it will remain and will never perish. So this name of Zayd is in the honored, elevated, purified scriptures. The honorable and righteous scribes will remember it in recitation." This is not the name of any believer except for one of the prophets, and for Zayd ibn Haritha it is compensation from God for what was taken from him. And He added to the verse, saying: "And when you said to the one upon whom God had bestowed favor," meaning with faith, thus indicating that he is among the people of Paradise. He knew that before he died, and this is another virtue. Seventh: The Almighty’s saying: And desire. Desire is every need that a person has a desire for. The plural is awtars. Ibn Abbas said: meaning he achieved what he wanted of his need, meaning intercourse. And it contains an implied meaning when he satisfied his desire with her and divorced her, We married her to you. The Ahl al-Bayt read it as I married her to you. And it was said: Desire is an expression for divorce? Qatada said this. Eighth: Some people have taken from this verse, and from the words of Shu`ayb: Indeed, I want to marry you (al-Qasas 28:27), the conclusion that the order of this meaning in the dowries should be: Marry her to him, so the pronoun for the husband is placed first, as in the two verses. Likewise, his saying, peace be upon him, to the man of the cloak: Go, for I have married her to you for what you have of the Qur’an. Ibn `Atiyyah said: “This is not necessary, because the husband in the verse is addressed, so it is good to place him first. In the dowries, the spouses are equal, so place whomever you wish first, and there remains no preference except to the degree of men, and that they are the protectors and maintainers.” Ninth: The Almighty’s saying: We have married her to you is evidence of the validity of the guardian in marriage? The disagreement on this has been mentioned previously. It was narrated that Aisha and Zainab boasted, so Aisha said: I am the one whom the angel brought to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in a piece of silk, and he said: This is your wife. Narrated by Sahih. Zainab said: I am the one whom God married from above seven heavens. Al-Sha’bi said: Zainab used to say to the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, “I can prove you with three things. None of your women can prove you with them. My grandfather and your grandfather are one, and God married you to me from the heavens, and the ambassador for this is Gabriel.” It was narrated from Zainab that she said: When I fell in the heart of the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, Zaid could not control me, and I cannot resist him except by what God, the Almighty, prevents me from, so he cannot control me.
33:38: "There is no blame upon the Prophet for what God has enjoined upon him. This is the way of God with those who passed on before. And ever is the command of God a decree decreed. Those who convey the messages of God and fear Him and do not fear anyone except God. And sufficient is God as Accountant." His statement, The way of God with those who passed on before is an address from God to the entire Ummah. He informed them that this and similar practices are the earliest practices of the prophets, that they should attain what is permissible for them. That is, He prescribed for Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, the liberality of marriage, the practice of the past prophets like David and Solomon. David had one hundred wives and three hundred concubines, and Solomon had three hundred wives and seven hundred concubines. Al-Tha'labi reported on the authority of Muqatil and Ibn al-Kalbi that the reference is to David, peace be upon him, since God brought him together with the one he was tempted by. Sunnah is in the accusative case as a source, meaning God prescribed for him a broad practice. And those who passed on are the prophets, as evidenced by their description later in His statement, those who convey the messages of God.
33:39: "Those who convey the messages of God and fear Him and do not fear anyone except God. And sufficient is God as Accountant."
33:40: God Almighty says: “Muhammad is not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets. And God is Knowing of all things.” There are three issues: First: When he married Zainab, people said: He married his son's wife. So the verse was revealed, meaning that he is not his son, so his wife is forbidden to him, but he is the father of his female slave in reverence and glorification, and his women are forbidden to them. With this verse, God removed what was in the hearts of the hypocrites and others, and made it known that Muhammad was not the father of any of the men who were his contemporaries in reality. This verse did not mean that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not have a son, as he had male children: Ibrahim, Qasim, At-Tayyib, and Mutahhar, but no son of his lived to become a man. As for Hasan and Husayn, they were children, not men who were his contemporaries. Second: The Almighty’s saying: But the Messenger of God. Al-Akhfash and Al-Farra’ said: meaning, but he was the Messenger of God. They permitted But the Messenger of God and Seal in the nominative case. Ibn Abi Ubla and some people also read But the Messenger of God in the nominative case, meaning he is the Messenger of God and the Seal of the Prophets. A group read But with a shaddah on the nun and put the Messenger of God in the accusative case as the subject of But and the predicate was omitted. Asim alone read Seal with a fathah on the ta, meaning that they sealed with it, so it is like a seal and a stamp for them. The majority read it with a kasrah on the ta, meaning that he sealed them? That is, he came last of them. It was said: Seal and Seal are two dialects, like Taba’a and Taba’a, and Daniq and Daniq, and Tabaq from meat and Tabaq. Third: Ibn Atiyyah said: These expressions, according to the group of scholars of this nation, past and present, are received in a complete generality, the implication of which is that there is no prophet after him, may God bless him and grant him peace. What Judge Abu al-Tamba mentioned in his book called Al-Hidayah, regarding allowing the possibility of ambiguity in the wording of this verse, is weak. What al-Ghazali mentioned regarding this verse, and this meaning in his book called Al-Iqtisad, is, in my opinion, heresy and a malicious attempt to confuse the belief of Muslims in the finality of prophethood of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, so beware of it, and God is the guide with His mercy. I said: It has been narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no prophethood after me except what God wills. Abu Omar said: He means dreams, and God knows best, which are a part of it, as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Nothing will remain of prophethood after me except the good dream. Ibn Masoud recited: From among your men, but a prophet who sealed the prophets. Al-Rummani said: With him, may God bless him and grant him peace, he sealed the reform, so whoever does not reform through him, his reform is hopeless. I said: And from this meaning is his saying, peace be upon him: I was sent to perfect good morals. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “My example and that of the prophets is like that of a man who built a house, completing it and perfecting it except for the place of one brick. The people entered it and were amazed by it and said, ‘If only it weren’t for the place of the brick!’ The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said, ‘In that place, I came and sealed the prophets.’” And something similar was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, except that he said: I am the brick and I am the seal of the prophets.
33:41: God Almighty says: O you who have believed, remember God with much remembrance. God the Almighty has commanded His servants to remember Him, thank Him, and to do so frequently for the blessings He has bestowed upon them. God the Almighty has made this without limit because it is easy for the servant. And because of the great reward for it, Ibn Abbas said: No one is excused for abandoning the remembrance of God except one whose mind is overcome. Abu Saeed narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Remember God often until they say he is crazy. It has also been said that frequent remembrance is that which is based on sincerity of the heart, while little remembrance is that which is considered hypocrisy, such as remembrance with the tongue.
33:42: And glorify Him morning and evening. God Almighty says: (And glorify and praise Him, O Muhammad! That is, occupy your tongues in most of your situations with glorifying, praising, praising, and magnifying God. Mujahid said: These are words that are said by the pure, the one in a state of minor ritual impurity, and the one in a state of major ritual impurity. It was also said: Call upon Him. Jarir said: Do not forget to say the Duha prayer. Joseph called upon his Lord, and He chose him when they both glorified Him. It was said: What is meant is pray to God in the morning and evening, and prayer is called glorification. Fajr, Maghrib, and Isha were mentioned specifically because they are more deserving of being encouraged, due to their connection to the ends of the night. Qatada and Al-Tabari said: The reference is to the Fajr and Asr prayers. Asil is the evening, and its plural is Asa’il. The root means the original, and its plural is Asal, as Al-Mubarrad said. Another said: The root is the plural of Asil, like Raghif and Raghf. It has been mentioned before. Question: This verse was revealed in Medina, so it has no relevance for those who claim that prayer was first prescribed as two prayers at the ends of the day. The narration in this regard is weak and should not be paid attention to or relied upon. We have already discussed how prayer was prescribed and what scholars have said about it in Subhan wa al-Hamdulillah.
33:43: "It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels [ask Him to do so], that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And ever is He, to the believers, Merciful." God Almighty says: It is He who sends blessings upon you. Ibn Abbas said: When the verse Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet was revealed, the Muhajireen and Ansar said: This is for you specifically, O Messenger of God, and we have no say in it. So God Almighty revealed this verse. I said: This is one of the greatest blessings from God Almighty to this nation and evidence of its superiority over all other nations. He said: You are the best nation produced for mankind (Al Imran 3:110). God’s invocation for a servant is His mercy and blessings upon him. The angels’ invocation is their supplication for the believers and their seeking forgiveness for them, as He said: And they ask forgiveness for those who believe (Ghafir 40:7), and the following will follow. In the hadith: The Children of Israel asked Moses, Does your Lord, the Majestic and Almighty, pray? He thought it was very important, so God, the Majestic and Almighty, revealed: My invocation is that My mercy precedes My wrath. An-Nahhas mentioned this. Ibn Atiyyah said: “A group narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: ‘O Messenger of God, how does God’s invocation for His servants occur?’ He said: ‘Glory be to God, the Holy One, My mercy precedes My wrath.’” There is disagreement over the interpretation of this statement. Some say that it is a word from God Almighty, which is His invocation for His servants. It was said: Glory be to God, the Holy is from the words of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he presented it before his utterance of the word which is God’s prayer, which is My mercy precedes My wrath, from the point of view that the questioner understood that he imagined in God’s prayer for His servants an aspect that is not befitting of God Almighty, so he presented the glorification and exaltation before his information. The Almighty says: That He may bring you out from darkness into the light, meaning from misguidance to guidance. The meaning of this is to establish them on the path of guidance because they were on the path of guidance at the time of the address. Then the Almighty informed them of His mercy toward the believers to comfort them, saying: And He is ever Merciful to the believers.
33:44: "Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be, 'Peace,' and He has prepared for them a noble reward." There is a difference of opinion as to who the pronoun in they meet Him refers to. Some say it refers to God, meaning He is Most Merciful to the believers, so He will protect them from God's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. On that day they will meet Him. And their greeting means the greeting of each other. "Peace" means safety for us and you from God's punishment. It was also said that this greeting is from God, meaning that He will save them from calamities, or give them good tidings of safety from fears. On the Day they meet Him means on the Day of Resurrection after entering Paradise. Al-Zajjaj said that its meaning is "Peace" and he cited as evidence the words of God, the Almighty: "And their greeting therein is Peace" (Yunus 10:10). It was also said that it means on the Day they meet Him, meaning on the Day they meet the Angel of Death. It was reported that He does not take the soul of a believer without greeting him. Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib said: Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be "Peace." So the Angel of Death greets the believer when taking his soul, and he does not take his soul until he greets him.
33:45: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner * And one who invites to God by His permission and an illuminating lamp. This verse is a way to comfort the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the believers, and to honor them all. This verse includes six of his (peace and blessings of God be upon him) names. Our Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) has many names and noble attributes, which are mentioned in the Quran, the Sunnah, and earlier books. God called him Muhammad and Ahmad in His Quran. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “According to what was narrated from him by trustworthy and just narrators: I have five names: I am Muhammad, I am Ahmad, I am Al-Mahi through whom God will eliminate disbelief, I am Al-Hashir, at whose feet people will be gathered, and I am Al-Aqib.” In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Jubair ibn Mut’im: God called him Kind and Merciful. It also states on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to give us names of himself, saying: I am Muhammad, Ahmad, Al-Muqaffi, Al-Hashir, the Prophet of Repentance, and the Prophet of Mercy.” Judge Abu al-Fadl Iyadh, in his book entitled Al-Shifa, traced what was stated in the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him), and what was transmitted in earlier books. The Ummah gave him many names and attributes, and their meanings were found in them. Judge Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi mentioned in his rulings regarding this verse sixty-seven names of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him). The author of Wasilat al-Muta'abidin ila Mubada'at Sayyid al-Mursalin reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) had one hundred and eighty names, and whoever wanted them would find them there. Ibn Abbas said: When this verse was revealed, "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) summoned Ali and Muadh and sent them to Yemen and said, 'Go and give good tidings and do not repel, and make things easy and do not make them difficult, for it has been revealed to me...'" and he recited this verse. God the Almighty says: Witness Sa'id said on the authority of Qatadah: Witnessing over his Ummah by conveying the message to them, and over all other nations by conveying the message through their prophets, and so on. And a bringer of good tidings means to the believers of God's mercy and Paradise. And a warner means to the disobedient and the deniers of the Fire and eternal torment. And a caller to God means conveying monotheism and adopting it, and fighting the disbelievers. By His permission here means: by His command to you, and His decreeing that at its proper time and place. And an illuminating lamp here is a metaphor for the light contained in His law. It was said: And a lamp means a guide from the darkness of misguidance, and you are like a shining lamp. He described it as illuminating because there are lamps that do not shine if their wick is weak and thin. In the speech of some: Three things tire you: a slow messenger, a lamp that does not shine, and a table for which someone is waiting to come. Some of them were asked about the lonely ones, so he said: A covering darkness and a lukewarm lamp. An-Nahhas narrated that Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharbi narrated to us, on the authority of Shaiban al-Nahwi, who said: Qatadah narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse, O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner * And an inviter to God, by His permission, and an illuminating lamp was revealed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Ali and Muadh and said: Go and give good tidings and do not make things difficult, for the verse has been revealed to me tonight: O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bringer of good tidings and a warner from the Fire, And an inviter to God, he said: The testimony that there is no god but God, “by His permission, by His command, and an illuminating lamp, he said: No, by the Qur’an. Az-Zajjaj said: And a lamp, meaning an illuminating lamp, meaning a shining book. He also permitted it to mean: and a reciter of the Book of God.
33:46: And calling to God by His permission and an illuminating lamp
33:47: "And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from God great bounty. And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites and ignore their harm and rely upon God. And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs." God the Almighty says: And give good tidings to the believers. The waw connects one sentence to another, and the meaning is disconnected from the one before it. God the Almighty commanded Him to give the believers good tidings of the great bounty from God the Almighty. According to Az-Zajjaj: Of a radiant lamp, or And following a radiant lamp, is conjoined with the kaf, not in We sent you. Ibn Atiyyah said: My father may God be pleased with him said to us: This is one of the most hopeful verses in my opinion in the Book of God the Almighty, because God the Almighty commanded His Prophet to give the believers good tidings that they have great bounty with Him. God the Almighty made the great bounty clear in His saying: "And those who have believed and done righteous deeds will be in gardens of Paradise, having whatever they wish with their Lord. That is the great bounty." (al-Shura 42:22). So the verse in this surah is a report, and the one in Ha Mim. Ain Sin Qaf is an explanation of it. And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, meaning do not obey them in what they suggest of flattery in religion, and do not acquiesce to them. The disbelievers: Abu Sufyan, Ikrimah, and Abu Al-A'war As-Sulami? They said: O Muhammad, do not speak ill of our gods, and we will follow you. The hypocrites were Abdullah ibn Ubayy, Abdullah ibn Sa'd, and Tu'mah ibn Ubayraq. They urged the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to respond to them under the pretext of benefit. And leave their harm means, leave them alone in recompense for their harming you. So God, the Blessed and Exalted, commanded him to refrain from punishing them and to overlook their mistakes. According to this interpretation, the verbal noun for the disbelievers was abrogated from the verse, and its abrogator was the Verse of the Sword. There is a second meaning in this verse: i.e., turn away from their words and what harms you, and do not be distracted by them. According to this interpretation, the verbal noun for the verse was abrogated by the Verse of the Sword. This is Mujahid's interpretation, and the verse was abrogated by the Verse of the Sword. And put your trust in God He commanded him to put his trust in Him and comforted him with His saying: And sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs. The strength of this statement is a promise of victory. The Disposer of affairs is the protector who is in charge of the matter.
33:48: Do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and ignore their harm and put your trust in God, and sufficient is God as Disposer of affairs.
33:49: "O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then you have no waiting period to count for them. So provide for them and release them with graciousness." There are seven issues: The first: The Almighty’s statement: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them When the story of Zayd and his divorce of Zaynab occurred, and she had been consummated with, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) proposed to her after her waiting period had ended, as we explained, God addressed the believers with the ruling on a wife who is divorced before consummation of the marriage, and He explained that ruling to the female slave. So if a divorced woman has not been possessed, there is no waiting period due, according to the text of the Book and the consensus of the ummah on that. But if he consummates the marriage with her, then she must observe the waiting period, according to consensus. Second: Marriage is actually intercourse. The contract is called marriage because it is closely related to it, as it is a path to it. Similar to this is their calling wine a sin because it is a cause of committing sin. The word marriage is not mentioned in the Book of God except in the sense of a contract, because it is in the sense of intercourse, which is one of the etiquettes of the Qur’an. It is referred to by the words: touching, contact, proximity, covering, and coming together. Third: Some scholars have used as evidence the verse in which God the Almighty says: Then you divorced them and the phrase then as evidence that divorce does not occur except after marriage, and that whoever divorces a woman before marriage, even if he specified her, is not bound by it. This was stated by more than thirty companions, followers, and imams. Al-Bukhari named twenty-two of them. It was narrated from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): There is no divorce before marriage, meaning that divorce does not take place until marriage has taken place. Habib ibn Abi Thabit said: Ali ibn al-Husayn may God be pleased with him was asked about a man who said to a woman: If I marry you, you are divorced. He said: "It is nothing. God the Almighty mentioned marriage before divorce." A group of scholars said: Divorce of a specific person, tribe, or country is binding before marriage, including Malik and all his companions, and a great number of scholars of this nation. We have already discussed the validity of this argument and the evidence of both groups. Praise be to God. So if he says: Every woman I marry is divorced, and every slave I buy is free, he is not bound by anything. If he says: Every woman I marry for twenty years, or If I marry from the town of so-and-so or from the tribe of so-and-so, she is divorced, then divorce is binding on him unless he fears hardship for himself due to the long years, or his lifespan is not likely to reach that age, in which case he may marry. Divorce is not binding on him if he makes it general because it restricts the options for marriage. If we prevented him from marrying, it would be difficult and hardship would be feared for him. Some of our companions said: If he finds something to amuse himself with, he should not marry, and that is nothing. This is because necessities and excuses remove rulings, so this person, from the standpoint of necessity, is like someone who did not swear an oath. This was stated by Ibn Khuwayz Mandad. Fourth: Dawud and those who supported his view argued that if a woman who has been divorced with a revocable divorce is taken back by her husband before her waiting period ends and he divorces her before having intercourse with her, then she does not have to complete her waiting period or any future waiting period because she was divorced before consummating the marriage. Ata ibn Abi Rabah and a group said: She must complete her waiting period from her first divorce. This is one of the two opinions of Al-Shafi’i because his divorce of her if he did not have intercourse with her is like someone who divorced her during her waiting period before taking her back. Whoever divorces his wife once during each period of purity should continue and not start over. Malik said: If he divorces her before having intercourse with her, she does not build on the past period of her waiting period, but she begins a future waiting period from the day he divorced her. Her husband has wronged himself and made a mistake if he took her back and has no need for her. This is the view of most scholars because she is like wives who have been consummated with in terms of maintenance, housing, etc. Therefore, she starts her waiting period from the day she was divorced. This is the view of the majority of jurists of Basra, Kufa, Mecca, Medina, and Syria. Al-Thawri said: The jurists among us are unanimously agreed upon this. Fifth: If the divorce was irrevocable and he married her during the waiting period and then divorced her before consummating the marriage, the scholars differed on this as well. Malik, Ash-Shafi’i, Zufar, and Uthman Al-Batti said: She is entitled to half the dowry and to complete the remainder of the first waiting period. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Ata’, Ikrimah, and Ibn Shihab. Abu Hanifah, Abu Yusuf, Ath-Thawri, and Al-Awza’i said: She is entitled to a full dowry for the second marriage and a future waiting period. They treated her as a woman who had been consummated with because of her waiting period from his semen. Dawud said: She is entitled to half the dowry, and she does not have to complete the remainder of the first waiting period or a future waiting period. The correct opinion is what Malik and Ash-Shafi’i said, and God knows best. Sixth: This verse is specific to the statement of God the Almighty: Divorced women shall wait concerning themselves three menstrual periods Al-Baqarah 2:228, and to His statement: And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation - if you doubt, their period is three months At-Talaq 65:4. This has already been discussed in Al-Baqarah, and the discussion of temporary marriage has also been discussed therein, so there is no need to repeat it here. And set them free with gracious freedom has two interpretations: First, that it is paying the temporary marriage according to means of means or difficulty, as stated by Ibn Abbas. Second, that it is divorcing her while she is pure and without intercourse, as stated by Qatada. It has also been said: Set them free after the divorce to their families, so the man and the divorced woman cannot be together in one place. Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: Then give them a temporary compensation. Saeed said: It was abrogated by the verse in Al-Baqarah, which is His statement: And if you divorce them before you have touched them and you have already specified for them a dowry, then give half of what you specified. Al-Baqarah 2:237, meaning He did not mention the temporary compensation. This has been discussed in detail in Al-Baqarah. His statement: And set them free means divorce them. Setting them free is a euphemism for divorce according to Abu Hanifa, because it is used in reference to something else and requires intention. According to Al-Shafi’i, it is explicit. It has been discussed previously in Al-Baqarah, so there is no point in repeating it. Beautifully is a Sunnah, not an innovation.
33:50: "O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their dowries and those your right hand possesses from what God has given you [as booty] and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet - if the Prophet wishes to marry her - exclusively for you, not including the believers. We know what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives and those their right hands possess so that there will be no blame upon you. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful." There are nineteen issues: The first: Al-Suddi narrated on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib, who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) proposed marriage to me, so I apologized to him, and he excused me.” Then God, the Most High, revealed: “Indeed, We have made lawful to you your wives to whom you have given their dowries, and those your right hand possesses from what God has bestowed upon you, and the daughters of your paternal uncles, and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you.” She said: Then was I not lawful to him? Because I did not emigrate; I was among those who were freed. Abu ‘Eesa included it and said: This is a good hadith, and we do not know it except from this source. Ibn al-‘Arabi said: It is very weak, and this hadith has not been narrated through a sound chain of transmission that could be used as evidence. Second: “When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave his wives a choice and they chose him, it was forbidden for him to marry other women or replace them, as a reward for their actions.” The evidence for that is the Almighty’s statement: It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that (al-Baqarah 2:17). Was it permissible for him to divorce one of them after that? It was said: It was not permissible for him to do so as a reward for them for choosing him. It was also said: It was permissible for him to do that like any other person, but he was not to marry another woman in her place. Then this prohibition was abrogated and he was permitted to marry any other woman he wished. The evidence for that is the Almighty’s statement: Indeed, We have made lawful to you your wives (al-Baqarah 2:17). Permissibility requires a prior prohibition. His wives who were during his lifetime were not forbidden to him, but it was forbidden for him to marry foreign women, so the permissibility was directed towards them. And because He said in the context of the verse: and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts (al-Baqarah 2:17). It is known that he did not have any of his paternal cousins, paternal aunts, maternal uncles, or maternal aunts under him, so it is established that it was permissible for him to marry this woman from the outset. Although this verse was recited first, it was revealed after the verse it abrogated, like the verses about death in Surat Al-Baqarah. People have differed in their interpretation of the verse: Indeed, We have made lawful to you your wives. Some have said that what is meant by it is that God has made it lawful for him to marry any woman to whom he gives her dowry. This was stated by Ibn Zayd and Ad-Dahhak. Based on this, the verse permits all women except those who are mahrams. Another said that what is meant is that We have made lawful for you your wives, meaning those who are with you, because they have chosen you over this world and the hereafter. This was stated by the majority of scholars. This is the apparent meaning, because the statement: You have been given their dowries is in the past tense, and a past tense verb cannot have a future meaning except under certain conditions. According to this interpretation, the matter would be difficult for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This interpretation is supported by the statement of Ibn Abbas: "The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would marry whomever he wished, and this was difficult for his wives. When this verse was revealed and it forbade him from women except those whom he had named, his wives were pleased with that." I say: The first statement is more correct, based on what we have mentioned. Its authenticity is also indicated by what was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Ataa, who said: Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die until God Almighty made women lawful for him. He said: This is a good and authentic hadith. Third: The Almighty’s statement: and what your right hand possesses. God the Almighty made concubines lawful for His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, and for his community in an absolute manner. He made wives lawful for His Prophet, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, in an absolute manner, and He made them lawful for all creation in a number of ways. And His statement: from what God has bestowed upon you means that He has returned it to you from the disbelievers. And spoils of war may be called booty, meaning from what God has bestowed upon you of women taken by force and coercion. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: And the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts meaning that We have made that permissible for you in addition to the wives to whom you have given their dowries and those whom your right hand possesses, according to the majority of scholars, because if He had intended that We have made permissible for you every woman whom you married and to whom you have given their dowry, He would not have said after that: And the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, because that is included in what came before. I said: This is not necessary. Rather, these were specifically mentioned as an honor, as God Almighty said: In them are fruits, palm trees, and pomegranates (al-Rahman 55:68). And God knows best. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: those who emigrated with you has two opinions: The first: It is not permissible for you to marry any of your relatives, such as the daughters of your paternal uncle Al-Abbas and others from the sons of Abdul Muttalib, the daughters of the sons of Abdul Muttalib, and the daughters of your maternal uncles from the sons of the daughters of Abd Manaf bin Zuhrah, except for those who have become Muslim, based on the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): A Muslim is one from whose tongue and hand the Muslims are safe, and a muhajir is one who abandons what God, the Most High, has forbidden. The second: It is not permissible for you to marry any of them except those who emigrated to Madinah, based on the statement of the Almighty: And those who believed but did not emigrate - you have no right to them in any way until they emigrate (al-Anfal 8:72). Whoever does not emigrate is perfect, and whoever does not perfect is not suitable for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who was perfect, honored, and exalted, peace and blessings of God be upon him. Sixth: The Almighty’s statement: with you. Here, with you means participation in the migration, not companionship in it. So whoever migrates, it is permissible for him, whether he was in his company when he migrated or not. It is said: So-and-so entered and left with me, meaning his action was like my action, easy, as your actions were not combined. If you had said: We left, this would have required both meanings: participation in the action and combination in it. Seventh: God the Blessed and Exalted mentioned the paternal uncle individually and the aunts in the plural. He also said: your maternal uncle and your aunts. The wisdom behind that is that the paternal uncle and maternal uncle in general are generic names like the poet and the poetic poet, but the same is not true for the paternal aunt and maternal aunt. This is a linguistic convention, so the discussion of it came with the ultimate goal of removing confusion. This is subtle, so reflect on it, as Ibn al-Arabi said. Eighth: The Almighty’s statement: And a believing woman is in apposition to We have made lawful meaning: And We have made lawful for you a woman who gives herself to you without a dowry. There is disagreement regarding this meaning. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not have a woman except through a marriage contract or through possession by the right hand. As for gifts, he did not have any of them.” He said: She was given to him as a gift. I said: What is in the two Sahihs strengthens and supports this statement. Muslim narrated on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that she said: I used to be jealous of those who gave themselves to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I would say: Are you not ashamed? A woman gives herself to a man until God revealed: You may defer to any of them you wish and take to yourself whom you wish. I said: By God, I do not think your Lord except hastens to fulfill your desire. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Aisha that she said: Khawlah bint Hakim was among those who gave themselves to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. This indicates that there was more than one of them. And God knows best. Al-Zamakhshari: It was said that the gifts were four: Maymunah bint Al-Harith, Zainab bint Khuzaymah, the mother of the poor, the Ansariyah, Umm Sharik bint Jabir, and Khawlah bint Hakim. I said: There is a difference of opinion on some of this. Qatada said: She is Maymunah bint al-Harith. Al-Sha'bi said: She is Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, the mother of the poor, a woman from the Ansar. Ali bin al-Husayn, al-Dahhak, and Muqatil said: She is Umm Sharik bint Jabir al-Asadiyyah. Urwah bin al-Zubayr said: She is Umm Hakim bint al-Awqas al-Sulamiyyah. Ninth: There is a difference of opinion regarding the name of the donor herself. Some say it is Umm Sharik al-Ansariyya, her name is Ghaziya. Others say it is Ghazilah. Others say it is Layla bint Hakim. Others say it is Maymunah bint al-Harith when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) proposed to her. The suitor came to her while she was on her camel, so she said: The camel and what is on it belong to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Others say it is Umm Sharik al-Amiriyah, and she was married to Abu al-Akr al-Azdi. Others say it is married to al-Tufayl ibn al-Harith, and she bore him Sharik. Others say that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married her, but this is not proven. God knows best. Abu ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-Barr mentioned it. Al-Sha’bi and ‘Urwah said: She is Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, the mother of the poor. And God knows best. Tenth: The majority of people read if she is given with a kasra on the alif, and this requires a new command, meaning that if it happens, then it is permissible for him. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid that they said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not have a woman as a gift, and we have provided evidence to the contrary. The imams narrated through Sahl and others in the Sahihs: “A woman said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: I have come to give you myself as a gift. He remained silent until a man stood up and said: Marry her to me if you have no need for her.” If this gift was impermissible, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not have remained silent, because he does not approve of falsehood when he hears it. However, it is possible that his silence was waiting for clarification, so the verse was revealed regarding permissibility and choice, so he chose to leave her and marry her to someone else. It is possible that he remained silent while considering the matter until a man stood up and demanded it. Al-Hasan al-Basri and Ubayy ibn Ka’b read… Al-Shaabi says that it is with a fat-ha on the alif. Al-A’mash read it as a believing woman who gave. An-Nahhas said: “The kasra on ‘in’ is used to gather the meanings because it is said that they are women. When it is fat-ha, the meaning is for a specific one because the fat-ha is used as a substitute for ‘woman,’ or in the sense of ‘because.’” Eleventh: The Almighty’s statement: a believing woman indicates that a disbelieving woman is not permissible for him. Imam al-Haramayn said: There is a difference of opinion about the prohibition of a free disbelieving woman for him. Ibn al-Arabi said: The correct opinion in my opinion is that she is prohibited for him. And with this he is distinguished from us, because whatever is from the side of virtues and honor, his share of it is greater, and whatever is from the side of deficiencies, his distance from them is purer. So it is permissible for us to marry free women from the People of the Book, but he, peace and blessings be upon him, due to his majesty, restricted it to believing women. Thus, it was not permissible for him to marry someone who did not emigrate, due to the deficiency of the virtue of emigration, so it is more appropriate that a disbelieving woman from the People of the Book is not permissible for him, due to the deficiency of disbelief. Twelfth: The Almighty’s statement: If she gives herself is evidence that marriage is a contract of exchange based on specific characteristics, which has been mentioned previously in An-Nisa’ and other books. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: If she gives herself to the Prophet, she is permissible. Al-Hasan read: that she gives herself with a fat-ha over the hamza. That is in the accusative case. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, because. Another said: that she gives herself is a substitute for inclusion from woman. Thirteenth: The Almighty's statement: If the Prophet wishes to marry her meaning if the woman offers herself to him and the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) accepts her, then she is permissible for him, but if he does not accept her, then that is not binding. Similarly, if a woman offers something to a man, then he is not obligated to accept it. However, it is one of the noble morals of our Prophet to accept the gift of the donor. The noble people consider that rejecting her is a common wickedness, a stain on the donor, and a pain in his heart. So God made this clear regarding His Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) and made it a Quran to be recited to remove hardship from him and to invalidate the falsehood of people in their customs and sayings. Fourteenth: The Almighty's statement: Purely for you. Meaning, women offering themselves as a gift purely and exclusively is not permissible. It is not permissible for a woman to offer herself to a man. The reason for this distinction is that if she had requested a fixed dowry before consummation, she would not have the right to do so. However, in our case, the woman who has delegated her right may request a dowry before consummation, and a dowry equivalent to that of her peers after consummation. Fifteenth: The scholars unanimously agreed that a woman giving herself as a gift is not permissible, and that this wording of the gift does not constitute a marriage contract, except for what was narrated from Abu Hanifa and his two companions, who said: If she gives herself as a gift and he witnesses that he has given her a dowry, then that is permissible. Ibn Atiyya said: Their statement only permits the expression and the wording of the gift, otherwise the actions they stipulated are the actions of marriage itself. This issue has been fully discussed in the stories. Praise be to God. Sixteenth: God Almighty has singled out His Messenger in the rulings of the Sharia with meanings that no one else has shared with him in the matter of obligation, prohibition, and permission. This is an advantage that has been bestowed upon him over the nation, and a status that has been singled out for him. Thus, things were imposed upon him that were not imposed upon others, actions were prohibited for him that were not prohibited to them, and things were permitted for him that were not permitted to them. Agreed upon and disputed. As for what is obligatory upon him, there are nine: First: Night prayer. It is said that night prayer was obligatory upon him until he died, based on the Almighty’s saying: O you wrapped in garments, arise by night (al-Muzzammil 73:1-2). What is stated is that it was obligatory upon him, then it was abrogated by the Almighty’s saying: And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you (al-Isra’ 17:179), which will come later. Second: Forenoon. Third: Eid al-Adha. Fourth: Witr, which is included in the category of night prayer. Fifth: Siwak. Sixth: Paying off the debt of someone who died in financial difficulty. Seventh: Consulting wise people about matters other than religious law. Eighth: Giving women the choice. Ninth: If he did an action, he would confirm it. Another added: It was obligatory upon him if he saw an evil action, he would denounce it and make it public, because his approving of that action by others indicates its permissibility, as mentioned by the author of Al-Bayan. As for what is forbidden to him, there are ten in total: First: The prohibition of zakat on him and his family. Second: Voluntary charity on him, and there are different details regarding his family. Third: The treachery of the eyes, which is to show something other than what he conceals, or to be deceived about what is required. Some of the infidels have been condemned when he was given permission, then he spoke to him leniently when he entered. Fourth: God has forbidden him, if he wears a garment for his female slave, to take it off or God will judge between him and his enemy. Fifth: Eating while reclining. Sixth: Eating foul-smelling foods. Seventh: Exchanging his wives, and this will come. Eighth: Marrying a woman who dislikes his company. Ninth: Marrying a free woman from the People of the Book. Tenth: Marrying a female slave. God forbade him things that He did not forbid to others, out of His sanctity and purification. He forbade him from writing, reciting poetry, or teaching it, to confirm his argument and demonstrate his miracle. God the Almighty said: And you did not recite before it any scripture, nor did you inscribe it with your right hand. (al-Ankabut 29:48). Al-Naqqash mentioned that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not die until he wrote, and the former is the more well-known version. He forbade him from looking at what people enjoyed. God the Almighty said: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them. (al-Hijr 15:88). As for what was permissible for him, may God bless him and grant him peace, they are sixteen in total: First: The best of the spoils. Second: Taking one-fifth of the fifth or one-fifth. Third: Continuous marriage. Fourth: Marrying more than four wives. Fifth: Marriage as a gift. Sixth: Marriage without a guardian. Seventh: Marriage without a dowry. Eighth: Marrying while in a state of ihram. Ninth: The division of the spoils between spouses is waived for him, and this will come. Tenth: If he sees a woman, her husband must divorce her, and it is permissible for him to marry her. Ibn al-Arabi said: This is what the Imam of the Two Sanctuaries said, and what the scholars have said about the story of Zayd regarding this meaning has already passed. Eleventh: That he freed Safiyyah and made her freedom her dowry. Twelfth: His entering Mecca without being in a state of ihram, and there is a difference of opinion regarding this. Thirteenth: Fighting in Mecca. Fourteenth: That he does not inherit. This was mentioned in the section on analysis because if a man approaches death due to illness, most of his property is removed from him, leaving him with only one-third pure, and the property of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) remains, as was explained in the verse on inheritance, and Surah Maryam also explains it. Fifteenth: His marriage remains after death. Sixteenth: If he divorces a woman, his prohibition on her remains, and she cannot remarry. Most of these three categories have been presented in detail in their places. And they will come, God willing. It was permissible for him (peace and blessings be upon him) to take food and drink from the hungry and thirsty, even if those with him feared death, as God the Almighty said: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves. It is incumbent upon every Muslim to protect the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) with himself. It was permissible for him to protect himself. God honored him by making spoils of war permissible. The earth was made a place of prostration and purification for him and his nation. There were prophets whose prayers were not valid except in mosques. He was aided by terror, so the enemy feared him from a distance of a month’s journey. He was sent to all of creation, while before him, prophets were sent to some people and not to others. His miracles were made like the miracles of the prophets before him and even more.
