The miracle of Moses (peace be upon him) was the staff and the gushing of water from the rock. The moon split for the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and water gushed out from between his fingers (peace and blessings be upon him). The miracle of Jesus (peace and blessings be upon him) was raising the dead and healing the blind and the leper. Pebbles glorified God in the hand of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and a tree trunk yearned for him, and this is more eloquent. God favored him over them by making the Qur’an his miracle, and making his miracle in it remain until the Day of Resurrection. For this reason, his prophethood was made eternal and not abrogated until the Day of Resurrection. Seventeenth: The Almighty’s saying: to marry her meaning to have sexual intercourse with her. It is said: to marry and to have sexual intercourse, like to be amazed and to be amazed, and to hasten and to hasten. It is permissible for istinkaah to mean to request sexual intercourse, or to request intercourse. Khalasa is in the accusative case as a state, as stated by Al-Zajjaj. It was said: it is a state of a pronoun connected to an implied verb indicated by the implied verb, meaning: We have made lawful for you your wives, and We have made lawful for you a believing woman, We have made her lawful for you purely, in the form of a gift, without a dowry, and without a guardian. Eighteenth: The Almighty’s saying: except for the believers. The benefit of this is that even though the infidels are addressed by the branches of the Sharia according to us, they have no role in that, because the application of rulings to them is only based on the assumption of Islam. God the Almighty says: We have already known what We have enjoined upon them concerning their wives. That is, what We have enjoined upon the believers, which is that they may not marry more than four women, with a dowry, proof of their marriage, and a guardian. This meaning was stated by Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Qatadah, and others. Nineteenth: The Almighty’s statement: So that there will be no difficulty for you meaning, distress in a matter in which you need ease. That is, We have made this statement and explained this so that there will be no difficulty for you. So so that there will be no difficulty is connected to His statement: Indeed, We have made lawful for you your wives meaning, so that your heart will not be distressed until it appears from you that you have sinned before your Lord in any way. Then the Almighty made all the believers feel comfortable with His forgiveness and mercy, saying: And God is Forgiving and Merciful.
33:51: "You may defer to any of them you wish, and you may take to yourself any you wish. And if you desire of those you have set aside, there is no blame upon you. That is more likely that their eyes may be comforted, and they will not grieve, and they will be satisfied with what you have given them all. And God knows what is in your hearts, and God is Knowing and Forbearing." There are eleven issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: You postpone whomever you wish. It is read with a hamza and without a hamza, and they are two dialects. It is said: I postponed the matter and I postponed it if you delay it. And you take refuge is with a damma, it is said: He took refuge in it with a long alif with a damma to it. And He took refuge with a short alif with a damma to it. Second: Scholars differed in the interpretation of this verse, and the most correct statement about it is that it was given the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) more laxity in not dividing his time between his wives, so he was not obligated to divide his time between them. This statement is what is appropriate to what has been mentioned, and it is the meaning of which is proven in the Sahih on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her. She said: I used to feel jealous of those who gave themselves to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and I would say: Would a woman give herself to a man? Then when God the Almighty revealed: You may defer to any of them you wish, and take to yourself whom you wish, and whomever you desire of those you have set aside Al-Ma'mun 14:1-15, she said: I said: By God, I do not see your Lord except that He hastens to fulfill your desire. Ibn Al-Arabi said: This statement proven in the Sahih is what should be relied upon. The intended meaning is that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had a choice regarding his wives: if he wanted to divide, he could divide them, and if he wanted to leave them, he could leave them. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was singled out by leaving the matter to him, but he would divide it himself without it being imposed on him, to please their souls and protect them from jealous words that would lead to inappropriate things. It was said that dividing was obligatory for the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), but this obligation was abrogated by this verse. Abu Razin said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) intended to divorce some of his wives, but they said to him, ‘Divide for us whatever you wish.’ Among those he sheltered were Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Salama, and Zaynab, so their division of himself and his wealth was equal between them.” Among those he deferred were Sawda, Juwayriyya, Umm Habiba, Maymunah, and Safiyya, so he would divide for them whatever he wished. It was said that what is meant are those who give themselves. Hisham ibn Urwa narrated on the authority of his father on the authority of Aisha regarding his statement, You may defer whomever you wish of them, she said: This refers to those who give themselves. Al-Sha’bi said: “They are those who give themselves. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) married some of them and left some of them.” Al-Zuhri said: We do not know that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) postponed any of his wives. Rather, he accommodated them all. Ibn Abbas and others said: The meaning is that he may divorce whomever he wishes from those under his guardianship, and keep whomever he wishes. Other than this has been said. In any case, the meaning of the verse is that it is permissible and lax for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). What we have chosen is the most correct, and God knows best. Third: Hibat God said in Al-Nasikh and Al-Mansukh that His statement, You may postpone whomever you wish (al-Ahzab 33:52), abrogates His statement, It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that (al-Ahzab 33:52), and the verse. He said: There is no abrogating verse in the Book of God that preceded the abrogated verse except this. His statement is weak in several respects. In Al-Baqarah, the waiting period for a woman who has died is four months and ten days, and it abrogates the year and preceded it. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: And whoever you desire of those you have set aside. “Ibtga’i” means sought, and ibtga’i means to seek. “Izal” means to remove, and azalah means removal. That is, if you want to take in a woman from those you have set aside from the division and take her into your care, then there is no harm in that. The same applies to the ruling on postponement, as one side indicates the other. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: There is no blame upon you meaning there is no inclination. It is said: The ship ran aground meaning it tilted towards the ground. That is, there is no blame or rebuke upon you. Sixth: The Almighty’s saying: That is more likely to make their eyes content. Qatada and others said: Which of the choices We gave you in their company is more likely to make them satisfied, since it was from Us? Because if they knew that the action was from God, their eyes would be satisfied with it and they would be content, because when a person knows that he has no right to something, he would be satisfied with what he was given, even if it was little. But if he knew that he had a right, what he was given would not satisfy him, and his jealousy and eagerness would intensify. So what God did for His Messenger by delegating the matter to him regarding his wives was more likely to make them satisfied with him, and to make their eyes content with what he allowed them, without their hearts being attached to more than that. It was read: ََنَنُع ْنْعَنِرtheir eyes with a ḍammah on the ta’ and the accusative case of ‘ayn. ََنَنُع ْنْعَنِرtheir eyes is in the passive form. “And peace be upon him, he was strict with himself in taking care of the settlement between them, to please their hearts as we mentioned before, and he would say: O God, this is my power in what I own, so do not blame me for what You own and I do not,” meaning his heart, for his preference for Aisha, may God be pleased with her, without showing that in any of his actions. And during his illness in which he died, he was carried around to the houses of his wives, until he asked their permission to stay in Aisha’s house. Aisha said: The first time the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, complained was in the house of Maymuna, so he asked his wives’ permission to be sick in her house, meaning Aisha’s house, and they gave him permission. The hadith was included in Sahih. And in Sahih also on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would check up, saying: Where am I today? Where will I be tomorrow?” impatience On the day of Aisha, may God be pleased with her. She said: When my day came, God Almighty took him between my throat and my neck, may God bless him and grant him peace. Seventh: Should a man be just between his wives, giving each one of them a day and a night? This is the opinion of most scholars. Some of them said that it is obligatory at night but not during the day. His wife's right is not waived by her illness or menstruation, and he is obligated to stay with her during her day and night. Should he be just between them when he is sick as he does when he is well? Unless he is unable to move, he stays where his illness overwhelms him. When he recovers, he resumes dividing his time. Slaves and free women, women of the Book and Muslims are the same in this. Abd al-Malik said: A free woman has two nights and a slave woman has one night. As for concubines, there is no division between them as between free women, and they have no share in it. Eighth: He may not bring them together in one house except with their consent, and he may not enter the house of one of them on the day or night of the other without need. There is disagreement about his entering out of need and necessity. The majority are of the opinion that it is permissible, such as Malik and others. In the book of Ibn Habib, it is forbidden. Ibn Bakir narrated from Malik from Yahya ibn Sa’id that Mu’adh ibn Jabal had two wives, and when it was the day of one of them, he would not drink water from the house of the other. Ibn Bakir said: Malik told us from Yahya ibn Sa’id that Mu’adh ibn Jabal had two wives who died in the plague. So he drew lots between them as to which of them would be first to die. Ninth: Malik said: “He should be fair between them in spending and clothing if they are of equal means. This is not necessary in cases of different status.” Malik permitted favoring one of them in clothing without favoritism. As for love and hate, they are outside the scope of earnings, so fairness in them is not possible. This is the meaning of the Prophet’s saying in his division: O God, this is my action in what I own, so do not blame me for what You own and I do not. An-Nasa’i and Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her. In the book of Abu Dawud, it refers to the heart, and it is indicated by the words of God the Almighty: And you will never be able to be equal between wives, even if you should strive to do so. An-Nisa’ 4:129 and His saying: And God knows what is in your hearts. This is the reason for mentioning it specifically here, to alert us that He knows what is in our hearts regarding our inclination towards some of our women over others, and He is the All-Knowing. Nothing is hidden from Him on earth or in heaven (Al Imran 3:5). He knows the secret and what is even more hidden (Ta Ha: 7). However, He permitted this, as the servant cannot divert his heart from that inclination, and this is what His statement: And God is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful refers to. It has been said regarding His statement: That is more likely to make their eyes cool which is the tenth: that is, that is more likely to make him not grieve if he does not bring one of them with the other and he witnesses selfishness and inclination. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever has two wives and inclines towards one of them will come on the Day of Resurrection with one side leaning. And they are satisfied with what I have given them all is an emphasis on the pronoun, meaning and they are all satisfied. Abu Hatim and Al-Zajjaj permitted and they are satisfied with what I have given them all as an emphasis on the pronoun in I have given them. Al-Farra' did not permit it because the meaning was not based on this, as the meaning was and each one of them is satisfied, and the meaning is not with what I have given them all. An-Nahhas and what he said are good. Eleventh: The Almighty’s statement: And God knows what is in your hearts is a general statement, and the reference is to what is in the heart of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) of love for one person over another. The meaning also includes the believer. In Bukhari, on the authority of Amr ibn al-‘As: “The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) sent him in command of the army of Dhat al-Salasil, so I came to him and said: Who is the most beloved person to you? He said: Aisha. I said: Of men? He said: Her father. I said: Then who? He said: Umar ibn al-Khattab…” So he counted a number of men. The discussion of the heart has been sufficiently presented at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, and at the beginning of this surah. It is narrated that Luqman the Wise was a carpenter slave, and his master told him: Slaughter a sheep and bring me the best two parts of it, so he brought him the tongue and the heart. Then Luqman ordered him to slaughter another sheep, and the master told him: Throw away the worst two parts, so he threw away the tongue and the heart. Luqman said: I ordered you to bring me the best two parts, so you brought me the tongue and the heart, and I ordered you to throw away the worst two parts, so you threw away the tongue and the heart!? He said: There is nothing better than them when they are good, and nothing worse than them when they are bad.
33:52: "It is not lawful for you to take other women after this, nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you, except those your right hand possesses. And ever is God, over all things, a Watcher." There are seven issues: The first: Scholars differed in their interpretation of his statement: It is not lawful for you to marry women after that, with seven opinions: The first: It was abrogated by the Sunnah, and what abrogated it was the hadith of Aisha, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not die until women were made lawful for him.” And it was mentioned previously. Second: It was abrogated by another verse. Al-Tahawi narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah who said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) did not die until God made it lawful for him to marry whomever he wished except a mahram.” This is the verse in which God the Almighty says: You may put off any of them you wish and take to yourself whomever you wish. An-Nahhas said: And this, and God knows best, is the most correct of what has been said about the verse, and it is the opinion of Aisha alone regarding abrogation. It may be possible that Aisha meant that this was made lawful for him by the Qur’an. This is also the opinion of Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Abbas, Ali ibn al-Husayn, and Ad-Dahhak. Some of the Kufi jurists objected and said: It is impossible that this verse, meaning: You may put off any of them you wish, was abrogated by It is not lawful for you to marry other women after that, when it comes before it in the Qur’an upon which the Muslims are unanimously agreed. He preferred the opinion of those who said it was abrogated by the Sunnah. An-Nahhas said: “This objection is not binding and its proponent is mistaken because the Qur’an is like a single Surah, as is authentically reported from Ibn Abbas: God revealed the Qur’an all at once to the lowest heaven in the month of Ramadan.” It is clear to you that the objection of this objector does not necessitate that the Almighty’s saying: And those of you who die and leave wives behind them - they shall bequeath to their wives a year’s maintenance without removing them (al-Baqarah 2:240) is abrogated according to the opinion of the people of interpretation. We do not know of any disagreement among them regarding the verse before it. And those of you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves four months and ten days. (al-Baqarah 2:234) Third: That the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was forbidden from marrying other wives because they chose God, His Messenger, and the Hereafter. This is the opinion of Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, and Abu Bakr ibn Abd Al-Rahman ibn Al-Harith ibn Hisham. An-Nahhas said: This opinion could have been thus, but it was abrogated. Fourth: Since it was forbidden for them to marry after him, it was forbidden for him to marry anyone other than them. This was said by Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hanif. Fifth: It is not lawful for you to marry women after that, meaning after the categories that were named. This was said by Ubayy ibn Ka’b, Ikrimah, and Abu Razin, and it is the choice of Muhammad ibn Jarir. Whoever said that permission was absolute for him said here: It is not lawful for you to marry women means it is not lawful for you to marry Jewish or Christian women. This is a far-fetched interpretation. It was narrated from Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Ikrimah as well. This is the sixth opinion. Mujahid said: So that she will not be a disbeliever or for the believers. Is this opinion far-fetched? Because he meant it: after the Muslim women, and Muslim women were not mentioned. He also meant nor that you exchange them meaning, nor that you divorce a Muslim woman in order to exchange her for a woman of the People of the Book. Seventh: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was permitted to marry whomever he wished, but this was abrogated. He said: This was also the case with the prophets before him, may God bless them and grant them peace. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said this. Second: The Almighty’s saying: Nor that you exchange them for other wives. Ibn Zayd said: This is something that the Arabs used to do. One of them would say: Take my wife and give me your wife. Al-Daraqutni narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The exchange in pre-Islamic times was for a man to say to a man: Give me back your wife and I will give you back my wife and I will give you more? Then God the Almighty revealed: Nor that you exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty should please you. He said: “Uyaynah ibn Hisn al-Fazari entered upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Aisha was with him. He entered without permission, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: ‘O Uyaynah, where is the permission?’ He said: ‘O Messenger of God, I have not asked permission to enter upon a man from Mudar since I became an adult.’ He said: ‘Who is this red-skinned woman next to you?’ The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘This is Aisha, the Mother of the Believers.’ He said: ‘Shall I not reveal to you the best of creation?’ He said: ‘O Uyaynah, God has forbidden that.’ He said: ‘When he left, Aisha said: ‘O Messenger of God, who is this?’ He said: ‘An obeyed fool, and as you see, he is the master of his people.’” At-Tabari, An-Nahhas, and others rejected what Ibn Zayd narrated from the Arabs, that they used to exchange their wives. Al-Tabari said: The Arabs never did this. What was narrated in the hadith of Uyaynah ibn Hisn that he entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Aisha was with him... the hadith is not an alteration, nor did he intend that. Rather, he looked down on Aisha because she was a young girl, so he said this statement. I said: What we mentioned from the hadith of Zayd ibn Aslam on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the substitution was in the pre-Islamic era indicates the opposite of what was denied of that, and God knows best. Al-Mubarrad said: It was read la halul with a ya’ and a ta’. So whoever reads it with a ta’ then it means a group of women, and with a ya’ from below it means all women. Al-Farra’ claimed that he said: The reciters agreed on the reading with a ya’? This is wrong. How can it be said: The reciters agreed when Abu Amr read it with a ta’ without disagreement from him! Third: The Almighty’s saying: And even if their beauty pleases you. Ibn Abbas said: “This was revealed because of Asma’ bint Umays. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with her beauty when Ja’far ibn Abi Talib died, and he wanted to marry her, so the verse was revealed.” This is a weak hadith, as stated by Ibn al-Arabi. Fourth: This verse is evidence that it is permissible for a man to look at the woman he wants to marry. Al-Mughira ibn Shu’ba wanted to marry a woman, so the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said to him: Look at her, for it is more likely to create harmony between you. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said to another: Look at her, for there is something in the eyes of the Ansar. Narrated by Sahih. Al-Hamidi and Abu al-Faraj al-Jawzi said: It means yellow or blue. And it was said: reddened. Fifth: The command to look at one's fiancée is only for the sake of guidance to what is in one's best interest. If one looks at her, he might see in her something that would encourage him to marry her. What indicates that the command is for guidance is what Abu Dawud mentioned in the hadith of Jabir from the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) that he said: If one of you proposes marriage to a woman, and he is able to see in her that which will encourage him to marry her, then let him do so. His statement, and if he is able to do so, cannot be said of what is obligatory. This is the view of the majority of jurists, including Malik, al-Shafi’i, the Kufians, and others, as well as the scholars of the apparent meaning. Some people disliked this, not caring about what they said, based on the saheeh hadeeths and the statement of God, the Most High: Even if their beauty should please you. Sahl ibn Abi Hathma said: I saw Muhammad ibn Maslama chasing Thubaytah bint Ad-Dahhak over a rent in one of the rents of Madinah, so I said to him: Do you do this? He said: Yes. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: If God puts in the heart of one of you the desire to propose to a woman, then there is nothing wrong with him looking at her. Rent means a roof, in the language of the people of Syria and Hijaz. Abu Ubaid said: The plural of ijar is ajajir and ajajira. Sixth: There is a difference of opinion as to what is permissible to look at of her. Malik said: He may look at her face and hands, but he may not look except with her permission. Al-Shafi’i and Ahmad said: With her permission or without her permission if she is covered. Al-Awza’i said: He may look at her and strive to look at the fleshy parts of her body. Dawud said: He may look at the rest of her body, adhering to the apparent meaning of the word. The principles of Islamic law refute him in prohibiting looking at the private parts. And God knows best. Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: Except what your right hand possesses. Scholars differed regarding the permissibility of marrying a disbelieving female slave for the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). There are two opinions: 1. She is permissible due to the generality of His statement: Except what your right hand possesses. This was stated by Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ata’ and Al-Hakam. They said: The Almighty’s statement: It is not lawful for you other women after this, means that women other than the Muslims are not permissible for you. As for Jewish, Christian and polytheist women, they are forbidden to you. This means that it is not permissible for you to marry a disbelieving woman and thus become a mother to the believers, even if her beauty pleases you, except what your right hand possesses, in which case he may take her as a concubine. The second opinion: She is not permissible, as he is too high to be able to have intercourse with a disbelieving woman. God the Almighty said: And do not hold on to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women. Al-Mumtahanah 66:15. So how about the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Except what your right hand possesses, in the nominative case instead of women. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case as an exception, but this is weak. It may be a source, and the meaning is: except for your right hand, and owner means owned, and it is in the accusative case because it is an exception from something other than the first type.
33:53: "O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given to you for a meal, not awaiting its preparation. But when you are invited, then enter. And when you have eaten, disperse and do not seek entertainment for conversation. Indeed, that used to annoy the Prophet, and he would be shy of you, while God is not shy of the truth. And when you ask women for something, ask them from behind a partition. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to annoy the Messenger of God or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of God enormity." There are sixteen issues: The first: The Almighty’s saying: Do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when permission is given to you. “An” is in the accusative case, meaning: except when permission is given to you, and the exception is not from the first. To food, not awaiting its container. The accusative case is in the state of circumstance, meaning do not enter in this state. It is not permissible except in the accusative case as an attribute of the food, because if it were an attribute, the subjects would have been made clear, and He would have said: Not awaiting its container (you). A similar example of this is: This man is with a man who is constantly with him. If you wish, you can say: This man is with a man who is constantly with him. This verse includes two al-Qasas 28:The first is about etiquette in eating and sitting. The second is about the hijab. Hammad ibn Zayd said: This verse was revealed about the heavy-laden ones. As for the first story, the majority of commentators agree that its reason is that “when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) married Zaynab bint Jahsh, the wife of Zayd, he held a wedding feast for her and invited the people. When they had eaten, a group of them sat talking in the house of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and his wife was facing the wall. They became heavy-laden for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). Anas said: I do not know whether I told the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) that the people had left or he told me. He said: He went until he entered the house, and I went to enter with him, but he threw a curtain between us, and the hijab was revealed. He said: The people were admonished as they were admonished, and God the Almighty revealed: “O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet” until His saying: Indeed, that is in the sight of God an enormity. Narrated by Sahih. Qatada and Muqatil said in the book of al-Tha’labi: This reason occurred in the house of Umm Salamah. The first is correct, as narrated by Al-Sahih. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about some believers who used to wait for the food of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so they would enter before the food was ready. They would sit until it was ready, then they would eat and not leave. Ismail bin Abi Hakeem said: This is the etiquette with which God has taught the heavy-duty. Ibn Abi Aisha said in Al-Tha’labi’s book: It is enough for you about the heavy-duty that the Shari’a could not tolerate them. As for the story of the veil, Anas bin Malik and a group said: Its reason was the command to sit in Zainab’s house, the story mentioned above. Aisha may God be pleased with her and a group said: Its reason was that Umar said: I said: O Messenger of God, your women are entered upon by both righteous and wicked people, so why don’t you order them to veil themselves? So the verse was revealed. Al-Sahih narrated on the authority of Ibn Umar that he said: Umar said: I agreed with my Lord in three matters: regarding the Station of Ibrahim, regarding the veil, and regarding the captives of Badr. This is the most correct of what has been said about the matter of hijab. All other sayings and narrations are weak and unsustainable. The weakest of them is what was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud: That `Umar ordered the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to wear hijab. Zaynab bint Jahsh said: O Ibn al-Khattab, you are jealous of us, and the revelation is being sent down to our homes. So God, the Most High, revealed: And when you ask them for anything, ask them from behind a partition. This is false, because hijab was revealed on the day of the wedding with Zaynab, as we have explained. Narrated by al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, and others. It was also said that “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was eating with some of his companions, and the hand of one of them touched `Aisha’s hand, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) disliked it,” so the verse on hijab was revealed. Ibn `Atiyyah said: It was the custom of the people, when they had food for a banquet or the like, that whoever wanted to come to the invitation would arrive early, waiting for the food to be cooked and ready. Likewise, when they finished, they sat down like that. So God forbade the believers from such things in the house of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The prohibition included all the believers, and the people adhered to God Almighty’s etiquette for them in that, so He forbade them from entering except with permission when eating, not before, in order to wait for the food to be cooked. Second: The Almighty’s statement: The houses of the Prophet is evidence that the house belongs to the man, and he is entitled to it, since God Almighty attributed it to him. If it is said: God Almighty said: “And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of God and wisdom. Indeed, God is ever Kind and Aware” (al-Ahzab 33:34), we say: Attributing houses to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is attributing ownership, and attributing houses to spouses is attributing a place, as evidenced by the fact that He gave permission for them to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and permission is only for the owner. Third: Scholars differed regarding the houses of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), as his family lived in them after his death. Was it their property or not? There are two opinions. One group said: It was their property, as evidenced by the fact that they lived in them after the death of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) until their deaths, as the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) gave that to them during his lifetime. The second opinion is that it was housing, just as a man lives with his family, and it was not a gift. Their living there continued until their death. This is the correct view, and it is what Abu Omar ibn Abdul Barr, Ibn Al-Arabi and others accepted. This is part of their maintenance, which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) exempted for them, just as he exempted their expenses when he said: “My heirs shall not share a dinar or a dirham. Whatever I leave behind after the expenses of my family and the expenses of my workers is charity.” This is what the scholars said. They said: This is indicated by the fact that their heirs did not inherit their homes. They said: If it had been their property, their heirs would have undoubtedly inherited it from them. They said: And in leaving that to their heirs is evidence that it was not their property, but rather their residence during their lives. So when they died, that was added to the mosque that benefits all Muslims, just as the expenses that they had were added to the estate of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they passed away, so it was added to the original money and spent on the benefits of the Muslims that benefit all of them. And God is the Grantor of success. The Almighty says: not waiting for its time meaning not waiting for the time of its ripening. La-na-ha is shortened, and there are variants for it: inna with a kasra on the hamza. Al-Shaibani said: And Khosrau when his sons divided it with swords as the butcher divided it Death brought him into labor one day, and every pregnant woman is perfect. Ibn Abi Ubaidah read: Ghairin nazareen inah in the genitive case as an attribute of food. Al-Zamakhshari said: This is not correct, because it was made in a way other than what it is intended for. It is the right of the pronoun of what it is intended for to be brought forward into the word, so it is said: Ghairin nazareen anta like you say: Hind hit Zayd. And and with a fatha over it, and and with a fatha over the hamza and a long vowel. Al-Hutay’ah said: I delayed dinner until Suhayl or Sirius, so the pot became too long for me. It means until the rising of Suhail. And ana is a source of ana which means that something is finished, ready, and attained. Fourth: The Almighty’s statement: “But when you are invited, then enter. And when you have eaten, disperse.” He emphasized the prohibition, and specified the time of entry to be upon permission, as a matter of politeness, and to protect the honorable presence from disliked complacency. Ibn Al-Arabi said: The meaning of the statement is: But if you are invited and given permission to enter, then enter. Otherwise, the invitation itself is not sufficient permission to enter. The fa in the answer to idha is necessary because it contains a meaning of recompense. Fifth: The Almighty's statement, So when you have eaten, disperse. God the Almighty commands, after feeding, that everyone disperse. The intent is to make it obligatory to leave the house once the purpose of eating is completed. The evidence for this is that entering the house is forbidden, but it was only permitted for the purpose of eating. So, when the eating is completed, the permissible reason is removed and the prohibition returns to its original state. Sixth: This verse is evidence that the guest eats on the property of the host and not on his own property, because He said: So when you have eaten, disperse, so He did not give him more than the food, nor did He add anything else to it, and the property remained as it was. Seventh: The Almighty’s statement: nor entertaining conversation is in apposition to His statement: not observing. And ghayra is in the accusative case as a state of the kaf and the mim in lakum, meaning not observing or entertaining. The intended meaning is: Do not remain entertained by conversation as the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) did at the wedding feast of Zaynab. Indeed, that used to bother the Prophet, so he would feel shy before you, but God is not shy before the truth, meaning He does not refrain from stating and revealing it. Since that happens to humans for reasons of shyness, God denied the reason for it in humans. In the Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of Umm Salamah, who said: “Umm Sulaym came to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, God is not shy before the truth. Does a woman have to perform ghusl if she has a wet dream? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: If she sees water.” Eighth: The Almighty’s statement: And when you ask them for something (al-Baqarah 2:170). Abu Dawud at-Tayalisi narrated on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that Umar said: I agreed with my Lord in four matters… The hadith. And in it: I said, O Messenger of God, if you imposed a veil on your women, then both the righteous and the wicked would enter upon them. So God Almighty revealed: And when you ask them for something, ask them from behind a partition. There is a difference of opinion regarding the property. Some say it is what is borrowed and enjoyed. Others say it is a fatwa. Others say it is scrolls of the Qur’an. The correct view is that it is general and includes all that can be requested from utensils and all other amenities for religious and worldly purposes. Ninth: In this verse is evidence that God Almighty has permitted asking them from behind a veil about a need that arises, or a matter about which they are seeking a fatwa. This includes all women in the sense, and what is included in the principles of the Sharia that the woman is entirely ‘awrah, her body and her voice, as mentioned above. It is not permissible to reveal that except for a need such as testifying against her, or an illness that may be in her body, or asking her about something that arises and is determined by her. Tenth: Some scholars have argued that the testimony of a blind man is permissible because people took testimony from the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) from behind a veil. They also believe that a blind man may have intercourse with his wife based on his knowledge of her speech. Most scholars permit his testimony, but Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi’i, and others do not. Abu Hanifa said: It is permissible in matters of lineage. al-Shafi’i said: It is not permissible except in matters that he saw before he lost his sight. Eleventh: The Almighty’s statement: That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. He means that it is better for men to think about women, and for women to think about men. That is, it removes suspicion, distances blame, and provides greater protection. This indicates that no one should trust themselves to be alone with someone who is not permissible for them. Avoiding that is better for their condition, more protective of their soul, and more complete in their chastity. Twelfth: The Almighty says: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God (al-An’am 1:17). This is a reiteration of the reason and an emphasis on its ruling, and the emphasis on reasons is stronger in rulings. Thirteenth: The Almighty’s saying: And that you should not marry their wives after him, ever. Ismail bin Ishaq narrated: Muhammad bin Ubaid narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah, that a man said: If the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) were to die, I would marry Aisha. Then God revealed: And his wives are their mothers. Al-Qushayri Abu Nasr Abd al-Rahman said: Ibn Abbas said: A man from the leaders of Quraysh, one of the ten who were with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) on Hira’, said to himself: If the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) were to die, I would marry Aisha, and she is my cousin. Muqatil said: He is Talhah bin Ubaidullah. Ibn Abbas said: This man regretted what he had said to himself, so he walked to Mecca on foot and carried ten horses for the sake of God, and he freed slaves, so God expiated his sins. Ibn Atiyyah said: It was narrated that it was revealed because some of the Companions said: If the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) were to die, I would marry Aisha. report of that reached the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and he was hurt by it. This is how Ibn Abbas referred to him by some of the Companions. Makki narrated on the authority of Muammar that he said: He is Talha ibn Ubayd God. I said: And this is what An-Nahhas narrated from Muammar that it was Talhah, but this is not authentic. Ibn Atiyyah said: May God bless Ibn Abbas! In my opinion, this is not authentic regarding Talhah ibn Ubaydullah. Our Sheikh, Imam Abu Al-Abbas, said: This statement has been narrated from some of the virtuous Companions, and may they never say such a thing! It is a lie in its transmission, and such a statement is only befitting of ignorant hypocrites. It is narrated that a hypocrite said when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married Umm Salamah after Abu Salamah, and Hafsah after Khunais ibn Hudhafah: Why does Muhammad marry our women? By God, if he died for our sake, the arrows would be on his wives. So the verse was revealed regarding this, and God forbade marrying his wives after him, and granted them the ruling of mothers. This is one of his special characteristics, distinguishing his honor and drawing attention to his status (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Shafi’i may God have mercy on him said: “It is not permissible for anyone to marry the wives of the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) whom he died, and whoever considers that permissible is an unbeliever, based on the words of God the Almighty: ‘It is not for you to harm the Messenger of God or to marry his wives after him, ever.’” It has been said that marrying his wives is prohibited because they are his wives in Paradise, and a woman in Paradise will be with her last husband. Hudhayfah said to his wife: If you want to be my wife in Paradise if God gathers us there, then do not marry after me, for a woman will be with her last husband. We have already mentioned what the scholars have said about this in the Book of Remembrance about the gates of Paradise. Fourteenth: Scholars differed regarding the wives of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) after his death. Did they remain wives or was the marriage contract terminated by death? If the marriage contract terminated by death, is there a waiting period for them or not? Some say: Do they have a waiting period? Because he died, and the waiting period is an act of worship. Other say: Do they not have a waiting period? Because it is a period of waiting during which they do not wait for permission to marry. This is the correct view, based on the saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): I did not leave behind me the maintenance of my family. It was also narrated: My family. This is a specific term for wives, so he maintained their maintenance and housing for them throughout their lives because they were his wives, and they were forbidden to anyone else. This is the meaning of the continuation of the marriage contract. Rather, death, in his case (peace be upon him), was considered to be like the absence of someone else because they are definitely his wives in the afterlife, unlike other people, because a man does not know whether he will be with his family in the same house. Perhaps one of them is in Paradise and the other is in Hell. Thus, the reason for the creation’s right was cut off, but it remained in the case of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: My wives in this world are my wives in the afterlife. He, peace be upon him, said: Every cause and lineage will be cut off except my cause and lineage, for it will remain until the Day of Resurrection. Section: As for his wives, peace be upon him, whom he separated from during his lifetime, such as Al-Kalbiyyah and others, was it permissible for anyone else to marry them? There is a difference of opinion on this. The correct view is that it is permissible. This is based on what was narrated that Al-Kalbiyyah, whom the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, separated from, was married by Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, as mentioned above. It was also said that the one who married her was Al-Ash'ath ibn Qays Al-Kindi. Judge Abu Al-Tayyib said: The one who married her was Muhajir ibn Abi Umayyah, and no one denied this, which indicates that it is a consensus. Fifteenth: The Almighty’s saying: Indeed, that was in the sight of God a great sin. This means harming the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or marrying his wives. He made that one of the major sins, and there is no sin greater than it. Sixteenth: We have explained the reason for the revelation of the hijab from the hadith of Anas and the saying of Umar. He used to say to Sawda when she went out, and she was a tall woman: We have seen you, O Sawda, out of eagerness for the hijab to be revealed. So God revealed the verse of the hijab. There is no distance in the revelation of a verse in light of all these reasons, and God knows best. However, when Zainab bint Jahsh died, he said: No one should attend her funeral except a mahram from her, out of consideration for the hijab that was revealed because of her. Asma bint Umays directed him to cover her in the bier in the dome, and informed him that she had seen that in Abyssinia, so Umar did it. It was narrated that this was done at the funeral of Fatimah, the daughter of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him).
33:54: Whether you reveal something or conceal it, then indeed, God is ever, over all things, Knowing. The Creator, glory be to Him, knows what is apparent and what is hidden, what was and what will not be. Nothing that has happened or will happen is hidden from Him. This is how He is praised in general, and He is worthy of praise and thanks. What is meant by it here is a rebuke and a threat to those who were previously hinted at in the verse before it, those referred to in His saying: That is purer for your hearts and their hearts, and those referred to in His saying: And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of God or to marry his wives after him, ever. So it was said to them in this verse: Indeed, God knows what you conceal of these beliefs and hateful thoughts and He will punish you for them. So this verse became a transition from what preceded it, explaining it. And God knows best.
33:55: There is no blame upon them concerning their fathers, or their sons, or their brothers, or their brothers’ sons, or their sisters’ sons, or their women, or those their right hands possess. And fear God. Indeed, God is, over all things, a Witness. There are three issues: First: When the verse of hijab was revealed, fathers, sons, and relatives said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: And we also speak to them from behind a veil? So this verse was revealed. Second: In this verse, God the Almighty mentioned those to whom a woman may appear. He did not mention the paternal uncle or maternal uncle because they are considered parents. The paternal uncle may be called a father. God the Almighty said: We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael Al-Baqarah 2:133. Ishmael was the paternal uncle. Al-Zajjaj said: The paternal uncle and maternal uncle may describe the woman to their two sons, because a woman is permissible for a paternal uncle and a maternal aunt, so he disliked them seeing each other. Al-Sha’bi and Ikrimah disliked a woman removing her veil in front of her paternal uncle or maternal uncle. Some of the mahrams are mentioned in this verse, and all of them are mentioned in Surat An-Nur. This verse is part of those, and we have discussed it fully there. Praise be to God. Third: The Almighty’s statement: And fear God. When God the Almighty mentioned the dispensation for these categories and the permissibility was established, He connected the command to them to fear God with a general connection. This is extremely eloquent and concise, as if He said, Limit yourselves to this and fear God in it so that you do not go beyond it to anything else. He specifically mentioned women and singled them out in this matter, due to their lack of caution and their frequent indulgence. And God knows best. Then the Almighty threatened with His statement: Indeed, God is, over all things, Witness.
33:56: "Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation." With this verse, God honored His Messenger (peace be upon him) during his life and death, mentioned his status with Him, and purified the evil deeds of those who harbored evil thoughts about him, or about his wives and the like. Prayer from God means His mercy and pleasure, from the angels means supplication and seeking forgiveness, and from the community means supplication and glorification of Him. Question: Scholars differed regarding the pronoun in His statement, they pray. One group said: The pronoun refers to God and the angels. This is a statement from God, the Most High, with which He honors His angels, and so the objection that came in the preacher’s statement, Whoever obeys God and His Messenger has been guided, and whoever disobeys them has gone astray, does not apply to it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “What a bad preacher you are! Say: ‘And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger,’” as reported by Sahih Al-Bukhari. They said: Because no one has the right to mention God together with something else in a pronoun, and God can do with that as He wishes. Another group said: There is an ellipsis in the speech, meaning that God prays and His angels pray, and there is no mention of a pronoun in the verse, and this is permissible for humans to do. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not say You are a bad preacher because of this meaning. Rather, he said it because the preacher paused at and whoever disobeys them and paused. They provided evidence for this with what Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Adi bin Hatim that a preacher delivered a sermon in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: Who obeys God and His Messenger and who disobeys them? The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Get up or go, what a bad preacher you are. However, it is possible that when he made a mistake in pausing and said to him: What a bad preacher, he corrected all of his speech after that, and said: “Say: And who disobeys God and His Messenger?” as in the book of Muslim. This supports the first opinion because he did not pause at and who disobeys them. Ibn Abbas read and His angels in the nominative case, in place of the name of God before entering in. The majority read it in the accusative case, in apposition to the written word. The Almighty’s saying: “O you who have believed, pray upon him and greet him with peace.” There are five issues in this: First: The Almighty’s saying: O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and salute him with a worthy salutation. God the Almighty commanded His servants to send blessings upon His Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and not upon any of His other prophets, as an honor to him. There is no disagreement that sending blessings upon him is obligatory once in a lifetime, and at all times. It is one of the obligatory confirmed Sunnahs that no one can abandon or neglect except one who is no good. Al-Zamakhshari: If you say, are sending blessings upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) obligatory or recommended? I say, Rather it is obligatory. They differed about the circumstances in which it is obligatory. Some of them made it obligatory whenever he is mentioned. In the Hadeeth: Whoever is mentioned in my presence and does not send blessings upon me, then he will enter Hell, so may God cast him far away. It is narrated that he was asked: “O Messenger of God, what do you think of the words of God, the Almighty: ‘Indeed, God and His angels send blessings on the Prophet?’” The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “This is from the hidden knowledge, and had you not asked me about it, I would not have told you about it. God, the Almighty, has assigned two angels to me. Whenever I am mentioned in the presence of a Muslim and he sends blessings on me, those two angels say, ‘May God forgive you,’ and God, the Almighty, and His angels say in response to those two angels, ‘Amen.’ Whenever I am mentioned in the presence of a Muslim servant and he does not send blessings on me, those two angels say, ‘May God not forgive you,’ and God, the Almighty, and His angels say to those two angels, ‘Amen.’” Some of them said: It is obligatory once in every gathering, even if it is mentioned repeatedly, as they said regarding the verse of prostration and the sneezing greeting. Likewise, in every supplication, at its beginning and end. Some of them made it obligatory throughout a lifetime. They also said the same regarding the pronunciation of the two testimonies of faith. What is required by precaution is to pray at every mention, due to the reports that have been reported regarding that. Second: The narrations differed regarding the manner of sending blessings upon him, may God bless him and grant him peace. Malik narrated on the authority of Abu Mas`ud al-Ansari that he said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to us while we were in the assembly of Sa`d ibn `Ubadah. Bashir ibn Sa`d said to him: ‘God has commanded us to send blessings upon you, O Messenger of God. How should we send blessings upon you?’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained silent until we wished he had not asked him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Say: O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings upon Abraham and upon the family of Abraham in the worlds. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. And peace, as you have known.’” An-Nasa’i narrated a similar narration on the authority of Talhah, omitting the phrase in the worlds and instead saying: “And peace, as you have known.” There are narrations on this topic from Ka`b ibn `Ujrah, Abu Humayd as-Sa`idi, Abu Said al-Khudri, Ali ibn Abi Talib, Abu Hurayrah, Buraydah al-Khuza`i, Zayd ibn Kharijah, and it is said Ibn Haritha. The imams of the scholars of hadith included it in their books. Al-Tirmidhi authenticated the hadith of Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah. Muslim included it in his Sahih with the hadith of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi. Abu 'Umar said: Shu'bah and ath-Thawri narrated from al-Hakam ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah who said: When the verse, O you who have believed, invoke blessings upon him and salute him with a worthy salutation, was revealed, a man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: "O Messenger of God, we know what 'peace be upon you' means, but how do we pray?" He said: "Say: 'O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings upon Abraham. And bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad as You blessed Abraham and the family of Abraham. Indeed, You are Praiseworthy and Glorious.'" This is the wording of the hadith of ath-Thawri, not the hadith of Shu'bah. It is included in the interpretation attributed to him of the verse, "Indeed, God and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and salute him with a worthy salutation." So He explained how to send blessings upon him and taught them in the greetings how to greet him, which is to say: "Peace be upon you, O Prophet, and the mercy of God and His blessings." Al-Mas'udi narrated on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Fakhita, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said: When you send blessings upon the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then send blessings upon him well, for you do not know, perhaps that will be presented to him. They said: Then teach us. He said: Say: O God, place Your blessings, mercy, and blessings upon the master of messengers, the leader of the righteous, and the seal of the prophets, Muhammad, Your servant, prophet, and messenger, the leader of goodness, the guide of goodness, and the messenger of mercy. O God, raise him to a praiseworthy station that the first and the last will envy. O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon Abraham and upon the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. O God, send Your blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent Your blessings upon Abraham and upon the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. We narrated with a continuous chain of transmission in the book Ash-Shifa by Qadi Iyad on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) counted them in his hands and said: Count them in the hands of Gabriel, and he said: Thus it was revealed from the Lord of Glory: O God, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad as You sent blessings upon Abraham and upon the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. O God, bestow Your blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad as You bestowed Your blessings upon Abraham and upon the family of Abraham. You are indeed Praiseworthy and Glorious. O God, have mercy upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad as You had mercy... Ibn Al-Arabi said: Some of these narrations are sound and some are weak. The soundest of them is that which Malik narrated, so rely on it. The narration of someone other than Malik about the increase of mercy with prayer and other things is not strong. Rather, people should look at their religions as they look at their money. They do not take a defective dinar in a sale, but rather they choose the sound and good one. Likewise, only what is authentically attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) is to be taken from the narrations of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), lest it fall into the category of lying about the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), for while he is seeking excellence, he has attained deficiency, and perhaps he has attained clear loss. Third: Concerning the virtue of sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), it was proven that he (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever sends blessings upon me, God will send blessings upon him tenfold. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: Sending blessings upon Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) is the best form of worship, because God the Almighty and His angels undertake it, then He commanded the believers to do so, while other acts of worship are not like this. Abu Sulayman al-Darani said: Whoever wants to ask God for something, let him begin by sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), then ask God for his need, and then end by sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), because God the Almighty accepts both prayers and He is too generous to reject what comes between them. Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab narrated from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him that he said: “A supplication is blocked from the heavens until blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) are sent. When the blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) are sent, the supplication is lifted.” The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever sends blessings upon me in a book, the angels will continue to send blessings upon him as long as my name is in that book. Fourth: Scholars differed regarding sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) during prayer. The majority and the majority agree that it is one of the recommended and recommended acts of prayer. Ibn al-Mundhir said, “It is recommended that no one prays a prayer without sending blessings upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). If someone omits that, then his prayer is valid according to the school of Malik, the people of Medina, Sufyan al-Thawri, the people of Kufa who are among the people of opinion, and others. This is the opinion of most scholars.” It was narrated from Malik and Sufyan that it is recommended during the final tashahhud, and that omitting it during the tashahhud is a sinner. Al-Shafi’i held an exception and required the omitting of it during prayer to repeat it. Ishaq required it to be repeated even if it was intentionally omitted, not due to forgetfulness. Abu ‘Umar said, “Al-Shafi’i said, ‘If someone does not send blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in the final tashahhud after the tashahhud and before the salutation, then he should repeat the prayer.’” He said, If he sends blessings upon him before that, then it is not valid. This is a statement reported by Harmalah ibn Yahya. It is hardly ever found such a statement from al-Shafi’i except through the narration of Harmalah from him, who was one of his senior companions who wrote his books. The companions of Al-Shafi'i followed it, leaned towards it and debated over it, and in their view it is the foundation of his school of thought. At-Tahawi claimed that no other scholar held this view except him. Al-Khattabi, one of the companions of Al-Shafi'i, said: It is not obligatory in prayer. This is the opinion of the majority of jurists except Al-Shafi'i, and I do not know of any role model for him in this regard. The evidence that it is not one of the obligatory prayers is the practice of the righteous predecessors before Al-Shafi'i and their consensus on it. He was strongly criticized on this issue. The testimony of Ibn Mas'ud, which Al-Shafi'i chose and which the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) taught him, does not include sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The same applies to everyone who narrated the testimony of faith from him (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn 'Umar said: Abu Bakr used to teach us the testimony of faith on the pulpit as you teach children in school. 'Umar also taught it on the pulpit, and it does not mention sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I said: Muhammad ibn al-Mawaz, one of our companions, said that sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) during prayer is obligatory, as mentioned by Ibn al-Qassar and Abd al-Wahhab. Ibn al-Arabi chose it because of the authentic hadith: God has commanded us to send blessings upon you, so how should we send blessings upon you? He knew the prayer and its time, so its manner and time were specified. Ad-Dharaqutni reported on the authority of Abu Ja’far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn that he said: “If I performed a prayer in which I did not send blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) or upon his family, I would see that it is not complete.” It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The correct view is that it is Abu Ja’far’s statement. Ad-Daraqutni said this. Fifth: The Almighty’s saying: “And greet him with peace.” Judge Abu Bakr ibn Bakir said: This verse was revealed to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and God commanded his companions to greet him. Likewise, those who came after them were commanded to greet him when they attended his grave and when he was mentioned. An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah on the authority of his father: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, came one day and joy was evident on his face. I said: ‘We see joy in your face!’ He said: ‘The angel came to me and said: O Muhammad, your Lord says: Is it not pleasing to you that no one sends blessings upon you except that I send blessings upon him ten times, and no one greets you except that I greet him ten times.’” On the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘There is none among you who greets me when I die except that his greeting comes to me through Gabriel, saying: O Muhammad, this is so-and-so, son of so-and-so, greeting you. ’ So I say: ‘And upon him be peace, the mercy of God, and His blessings. ’” An-Nasa’i narrated on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘God has angels who travel throughout the earth, conveying to me the greetings of my nation. ’ Al-Qushayri said: Greeting means saying: ‘Peace be upon you. ’”
33:57: Indeed, those who abuse God and His Messenger - God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment. There are five issues: First: Scholars differed regarding how harming God is done. The majority of scholars said: It means disbelief, attributing to Him a wife, a son, or a partner, and describing Him with what is not befitting of Him, like the Jews may God curse them said: “The Jews say: The hand of God is chained.” And the Christians said: The Messiah is the son of God. And the polytheists said: The angels are the daughters of God, and the idols are His partners. And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, God the Most High said: The son of Adam denied Me, though he had no right to do so, and he reviled Me, though he had no right to do so… The hadith was mentioned previously in Surah Maryam. And in Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: God the Most High said: “The son of Adam harms Me, saying: ‘Oh, what a disappointment in time.’ So let none of you say: ‘Oh, what a disappointment in time,’ for I am time. I alternate its night and day, and if I wish, I can take them away.” This is how this hadith was attributed to Abu Hurairah in this narration. It was also attributed to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him): “The son of Adam does not harm Me by cursing time, though I am time. I alternate night and day.” Also narrated by Muslim. Ikrimah said: It means by depicting and exposing oneself to doing what only God does by carving images and other things. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God curse the image-makers. I said: Is this what strengthens Mujahid’s statement about prohibiting the depiction of trees and other things? Because all of that is an invention and an imitation of the action of God, which He is the only One with. This was mentioned previously in Surat An-Naml and Al-Hamdulillah. A group said: This is based on the omission of an adjective, meaning: They harm the friends of God. As for harming His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is everything that harms him from words in more than one meaning, and from actions as well. As for their saying: He is a magician, a poet, a mad soothsayer. As for their actions: He broke his front tooth and split his face on the day of Uhud, and in Mecca they threw the placenta on his back while he was prostrating, and other things. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed about those who slandered him because he married Safiyya bint Huyayy. He stated the harming of God and His Messenger and restricted the harming of believing men and women, because harming God and His Messenger can only be unjustly, ever. As for harming believing men and women, it is from this... and from this... Second: Our scholars said: “Assailing the leadership of Usamah ibn Zayd is harming him, peace be upon him.” It was narrated in Sahih on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: “The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, sent an expedition and appointed Usamah ibn Zayd as their leader. People criticized his leadership, so the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, stood up and said: ‘If you criticize his leadership, you used to criticize his father’s leadership before. By God, he was created for leadership and was one of the people I love most, and this is one of the people I love most after him.’” This expedition, and God knows best, is the one that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, prepared with Usamah and appointed him as their leader. He ordered him to raid Abna, which is the village near Mu’tah, the place where Zayd killed his father, along with Ja’far ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Rawahah. He ordered him to avenge his father, and he criticized those who had doubts about his leadership, given that he was a client and that he was young, as he was eighteen years old at that time. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, died before this expedition had set out from Medina and had not yet left it. Abu Bakr carried it out after the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Third: In this hadith is the clearest evidence of the permissibility of a mawla or a person of less esteem leading others in prayer, except for the greater imamate. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) appointed Salim, the mawla of Abu Hudhayfah, to lead the prayer in Quba, and he led them in prayer, among whom were Abu Bakr, Umar, and other prominent figures of Quraysh. Al-Sahih narrated on the authority of Amir ibn Wathilah that Nafi’ ibn Abd al-Harith met Umar in Usfan, and Umar had appointed him over Mecca. He said: Who have you appointed over this valley? He said: Ibn Abza. Umar asked: Who is Ibn Abza? He said: A mawla of ours. Umar said: So I appointed a mawla over them. He said: He is a reciter of the Book of God and he is knowledgeable about the inheritance laws. Umar said: “Your Prophet said: ‘God raises some people by this Book and lowers others by it.” Fourth: Usamah may God be pleased with him was al-Hab ibn al-Hab, and that was what he was called. He was very black, and his father Zayd was white as cotton. This is how Abu Dawud mentioned it on the authority of Ahmad ibn Salih. Others than Ahmad said: Zayd had a rosy complexion, and Usamah was very dark-skinned. It is narrated that “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to look after Usamah when he was young, and he would wipe his mucus and clean his nose, saying: If Usamah were a girl, we would have adorned him, prepared him, and made him beloved by our wives.” It has been mentioned that the reason for the Arabs’ apostasy after the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was that when he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was on Mount Arafat on the eve of Arafat with the group, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) delayed for a while because of Usamah until he came to him. They said: He was only delayed for this reason! In contempt of him. So this statement of theirs was the reason for their apostasy. Al-Bukhari mentioned it in his book Al-Tarikh with the same meaning. And God knows best. Fifth: Omar may God be pleased with him used to allocate five thousand for Usamah and two thousand for his son Abdullah. Abdullah said to him: You have given Usamah preference over me although you witnessed what he did not. He said: Usamah was more beloved to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) than you, and his father was more beloved to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) than your father. So, may God be pleased with him, he preferred the one beloved by the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) over the one he loved. Thus, one should love what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) loved and hate what he hated. Marwan responded to this love with its opposite, as he passed by Usamah ibn Zayd while he was praying at the door of the Prophet’s house (peace and blessings be upon him). Marwan said to him: I only wanted us to see your standing, and we have seen your standing. God did to you and he said an ugly word. Usama said to him: You have hurt me, and you are obscene and vulgar. I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God Almighty hates the obscene and vulgar. So look at the difference between the two actions and compare the difference between the two men. The Umayyads hurt the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in his beloved ones, and contradicted him in his beloved ones. The Almighty's saying: May God curse them means they are far from all good. In the language, cursing means exclusion, and from it comes the word li'an. And has prepared for them a humiliating punishment has been mentioned in more than one place. All praise is due to God, Lord of the Worlds.
33:58: And those who harm believing men and believing women for [something] other than what they have earned have certainly borne upon themselves a slander and a manifest sin. Harming believing men and women also occurs through ugly actions and words, such as slander and fabricated outrageous lies. This verse is similar to the verse in An-Nisa’: And whoever commits a sin or a crime and then attributes it to an innocent person has certainly taken upon himself a slander and a manifest sin (An-Nisa’: 112), as stated here. It has been said that harming someone includes taunting them with a reprehensible status, a reprehensible profession, or something that would burden them if they heard it, because harming them is generally forbidden. God distinguished between harming them, harming the Messenger, and harming the believers, making the former disbelief and the latter a major sin. He said regarding harming believers: They have certainly taken upon themselves a slander and a manifest sin, which we have already explained. It was narrated that ‘Umar ibn Al-Khattab said to Ubayy ibn Ka’b, “I read this verse last night and was terrified by it: ‘And those who harm believing men and women for [something] other than what they have earned…’ By God, I beat them and rebuke them.” But Ubayy said to him, “O Commander of the Faithful, you are not one of them. You are only a teacher and a corrector.” It has been said that the reason for the revelation of this verse was that Omar saw a slave girl from the Ansar and beat her, and he disliked what he saw of her adornment. Her family came out and harmed Omar verbally, so God revealed this verse. It has also been said that it was revealed about Ali, because the hypocrites were harming him and lying about him, may God be pleased with him.
33:59: "O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful." There are six issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: Say to your wives and your daughters. We have already discussed the preference of his wives one by one. Qatada said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) died leaving nine. Five from the Quraysh 106:Aisha, Hafsa, Umm Habiba, Sawda, and Umm Salama. Three from the rest of the Arabs: Maymuna, Zainab bint Jahsh, and Juwayriyya. And one from Banu Harun: Safiyya. As for his children, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) had both male and female children. His male children: Al-Qasim, his mother Khadija, and he was called by this name, peace be upon him. He was the first of his children to die, and he lived for two years. Urwah said: Khadija gave birth to Al-Qasim, Al-Tahir, Abdullah, and Al-Tayyib for the Prophet, peace be upon him. Abu Bakr Al-Barqi said: It is said that Al-Tahir is Al-Tayyib, who is Abdullah. Ibrahim, his mother Maria Al-Qibtiyya, was born in Dhul-Hijjah in the eighth year of the Hijra, and died at the age of sixteen months, and some say eighteen, as mentioned by Al-Daraqutni. He was buried in Al-Baqi. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: He has a wet nurse who will nurse him to perfection in Paradise. All of the Prophet's (peace and blessings be upon him) children were from Khadija, except for Ibrahim. All of his children died during his lifetime, except for Fatima. As for his female children, among them is Fatima Al-Zahra bint Khadija, who gave birth to her while the Quraysh were building the Kaaba five years before the Prophethood. She was the youngest of his daughters. Ali may God be pleased with them both married her in the second year of the Hijra in Ramadan and consummated the marriage with her in Dhul-Hijjah. It was also said that he married her in Rajab, and she died shortly after the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him). She was the first of his family to join him. May God be pleased with her. Among them: Zainab, her mother Khadija married her cousin Abu Al-Aasi bin Al-Rabi’, and Al-Aasi’s mother was Hala bint Khuwaylid, Khadija’s sister. Abu Al-Aasi’s name was Laqit. It was also said that it was Hashim. It was also said that it was Hisham. It was also said that it was Muqsim. She was the eldest daughter of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She died in the year 8 AH, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) descended into her grave. Among them: Ruqayyah, whose mother was Khadija, married Utbah ibn Abi Lahab before the Prophethood. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sent and the verse, Perish the hands of Abu Lahab (al-Masad 111:1) was revealed to him, Abu Lahab said to his son: My head is inviolable from yours if you do not divorce his daughter, so he left her and had not consummated the marriage with her. She converted to Islam when her mother Khadija converted to Islam, and she and her sisters pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when the women pledged allegiance to him. Uthman ibn Affan married her, and the women of Quraysh used to say when Uthman married her: The two best people a human being has ever seen are Ruqayyah and her husband Uthman. She migrated with him to Abyssinia during the two migrations. She had a miscarriage from Uthman, and then gave birth to Abdullah, who was known as Uthman in Islam. When he was six years old, a rooster pecked him in the face and he died. She did not bear him any children after that. She migrated to Medina and fell ill while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was preparing for Badr. So, Uthman took her over as his successor. She died while the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) was at Badr, seventeen months after the Hijra. Zayd ibn Haritha came as a herald from Badr, and he entered Medina when the earth was being covered over Ruqayyah. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) did not witness her burial. Among them: Umm Kulthum, whose mother was Khadija, married Utaybah ibn Abi Lahab, Utbah’s brother, before the Prophethood. His father ordered him to divorce her for the reason mentioned in the case of Ruqayyah, but he did not consummate the marriage with her. She remained in Mecca with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him).
