She converted to Islam when her mother did, and pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) along with her sisters when the women did. She migrated to Medina when the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) migrated. When Ruqayyah died, Uthman married her, and was thus called Dhu al-Noorayn. She died during the lifetime of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) in Sha’ban of the year 9 AH. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) sat on her grave, and Ali, al-Fadl, and Usama descended into her grave. Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkar mentioned that the eldest of the Prophet’s (peace and blessings be upon him) children was al-Qasim, then Zaynab, then Abdullah, who was called al-Tayyib and al-Tahir. He was born after the Prophethood and died young. Then came Umm Kulthum, then Fatimah, then Ruqayyah. Al-Qasim died in Mecca, followed by Abdullah. Second: Since it was the custom of Arab women to be promiscuous, and they would uncover their faces as slave girls do, and that was an invitation for men to look at them and their thoughts would be disturbed, God commanded His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, to command them to let their jilbabs hang down over them if they wanted to go out to relieve themselves. They used to defecate in the desert before toilets were made, and so there was a difference between them and slave girls. Free women were recognized by their covering, and men, whether single or young, would refrain from opposing them. Before this verse was revealed, a woman from the believing women would defecate to relieve themselves, and some wicked men would approach her, thinking she was a slave girl. She would shout at him, and he would go away. They complained about that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And because of that, the verse was revealed. Its meaning was said by Al-Hasan and others. Third: The Almighty’s saying: of their outer garments. The word jilbab is the plural of jilbab, which is a garment larger than the khimar. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Masoud that it is the cloak. It was also said that it is the veil. The correct view is that it is the garment that covers the entire body. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Umm Atiyyah, she said: O Messenger of God, what if one of us does not have a jilbab? He said: Let her sister dress her in one of her jilbabs. Fourth: People differed about the manner in which it should be loosened. Ibn Abbas and Ubaidah al-Salmani said: It is for the woman to twist it until nothing is visible of her except one eye with which she sees. Ibn Abbas and Qatadah also said: It is for her to twist it over the forehead and tighten it, then fold it over the nose, even if her eyes are visible, but it covers the chest and most of the face. Al-Hasan said: It covers half of her face. Fifth: God the Almighty has commanded all women to cover themselves, and that this should only be done with something that does not reveal their skin, except when she is with her husband, in which case she may wear whatever she wants, because he has the right to enjoy her however he wants. It has been proven that “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) woke up one night and said: Glory be to God! What trials have been sent down tonight and what treasures have been opened! Who will wake up the companions of the house? How many a woman is clothed in this world but naked in the Hereafter?” It was narrated that “When Dihya al-Kalbi returned from Heraclius and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gave him a Coptic garment, he said: ‘Make a shirt for yourself and give your companion a shirt to cover herself with.’” A shirt is half. Then he said to him: ‘Tell her to wear something underneath it so that it does not reveal her.’ Abu Hurairah mentioned the thinness of women’s clothing and said: ‘Those who are clothed yet naked are soft and miserable.’” Some women from Banu Tamim entered upon Aisha may God be pleased with her wearing thin garments. Aisha said, If you are believers, then this is not the dress of believing women, but if you are not believers, then enjoy it. A bride was brought to Aisha may God be pleased with her wearing a saffron-colored Coptic veil. When Aisha saw her, she said, A woman who wears this does not believe in Surat An-Nur. It was authentically reported that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Women who are clothed yet naked, who encroach on others and are led astray, with heads like the humps of camels, will not enter Paradise or even smell its fragrance. Umar may God be pleased with him said, What prevents a Muslim woman, if she needs something, from going out in her own cloak or the cloak of her neighbor, in secret, such that no one will know about it until she returns home? Sixth: The Almighty’s statement: That is more likely that they will be known, meaning the free women, so that they do not mix with the slave women. When they are known, they will not be met with the slightest opposition, out of respect for the rank of freedom, so that desires are cut off from them. The meaning is not that a woman should be known so that she knows who she is. When Omar may God be pleased with him saw a slave woman covering herself, he would hit her with a whip, preserving the attire of the free women. It has been said that covering and covering oneself is obligatory now for everyone, free women and slave women. This is like the fact that the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade women from going to the mosques after the death of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), with his saying: Do not prevent the female slaves of God from the mosques of God, so that Aisha may God be pleased with her said: If the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had lived until our time, he would have forbade them from going out to the mosques. The women of the Children of Israel were also forbidden from wearing jilbabs. And God is Forgiving and Merciful. This was a way for women to get used to not wearing jilbabs before this lawful command.
33:60: "If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease and the agitators in the city do not desist, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little while. * Cursed are they; wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed in a utter slaughter. * Such is the way of God with those who passed on before. And you will not find in the way of God any change." There are five issues: First: The Almighty’s statement: If the hypocrites do not desist verse. The commentators agree that the three descriptions refer to one thing, as Sufyan ibn Sa’id narrated on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Abu Razin, who said: The hypocrites, those in whose hearts is a disease, and the agitators in the city He said: They are one thing, meaning that they have combined these things. And the and is inserted. As he said: To the honorable king, the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowded He wanted to go to the king, Al-Qarm Ibn Al-Hammam, the lion of the battalion, and he had already mentioned Surat Al-Baqarah. It was also said that among them were some who spread rumors, some who followed women out of suspicion, and some who cast doubt on Muslims. Ikrimah and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: Those in whose hearts is disease means those in whose hearts is adultery. Tawus said: This verse was revealed concerning women. Salamah ibn Kuhayl said: It was revealed concerning those who commit indecencies, and the meanings are close. It was also said that the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease are one thing, expressed in two words, the evidence for which is the verse about the hypocrites at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. The rumor-mongers in Madinah were people who used to inform the believers of things that upset them about their enemy. When the armies of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) set out, they would say: They have been killed or defeated, and the enemy has come to you, said Qatada and others. It was also said that they used to say: The people of the Suffa are celibate people, meaning those who harass women. It was also said that they are a group of Muslims who spread false report out of love for discord. Among the people who spread slander were Muslims, but they indulged in it out of love for sedition. Ibn Abbas said: Irjaf means seeking sedition, and irjaf means spreading lies and falsehood to cause concern. It was also said that it means moving hearts. It is said: The earth trembled, meaning it moved and shook, trembling violently. Irjafan means severe turmoil. Ar-Rajjaf is the sea, so named because of its turmoil. The poet said: Those who eat meat every evening until sunset in Rajaf Arjaf: one of the raghaf of report. They spread rumors about something, i.e. they delved into it. The poet said: Even if you reproach us for killing him and spread rumors about Islam, he is a transgressor and an envious person. Another said: You threaten me with rumours, you son of a bitch, while in rumours you find meanness and weakness. Spreading rumors is forbidden because it causes harm. The verse indicates that causing harm through spreading rumors is forbidden. Second: The Almighty’s saying: We will surely tempt you against them, meaning, We will give you power over them so that you can eradicate them by killing them. Ibn Abbas said: They did not cease harming women, and that God tempted him against them. Then He, the Almighty, said: And never pray funeral over any of them who dies, nor stand at his grave (al-Tawbah 9:84), and that He ordered him to curse them, and this is the temptation. Muhammad bin Yazid said: He tempted him with Hamal in the verse that follows this one, as the speech is connected to it, which is His saying, the Almighty: Wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed with a terrible slaughter. This contains the meaning of a command to kill them and seize them, meaning this is their ruling if they persist in hypocrisy and spreading rumors. In the hadith of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: Five are to be killed within the sacred precincts and outside. This contains the meaning of a command just like the verse. An-Nahhas said: This is one of the best things said about the verse. It was said that they had ceased spreading rumors, so he was not tempted by them. The lam of an-naghrinak is the lam of an oath, and the oath applies to it, and the lam was inserted in in to prepare for it. Third: The Almighty's statement: Then they will not be your neighbors therein meaning in the city. Except for a little is in the accusative case as a state of the pronoun in they will be your neighbors, so the matter was as the Almighty said because they were only few in number. This is one of Al-Farra's two answers, and he preferred it, meaning they will not be your neighbors except when they are few in number. The other answer is that the meaning is except for a little time, meaning they will not stay with you except for a short period, meaning they will not be your neighbors therein except for a short period until they perish, so it is an adjective for a deleted verbal noun or adverbial phrase. And this is based on the fact that whoever is with you, residing in the city, is a neighbor. This has already been mentioned in the chapter on women. Fourth: The Almighty's statement: Cursed This is the complete statement according to Muhammad ibn Yazid, and it is in the accusative case as a state. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Cursed for a little while is a good pause. An-Nahhas said: It is permissible for the completion to be except for a little and for cursed to be in the accusative case as an insult, as 'Isa ibn 'Umar read: And his wife, the carrier of firewood Al-Masad 76:14. It was narrated from some grammarians that he said: The meaning is that wherever they are found, they will be taken cursed. This is a mistake and what was mentioned with the retribution before it does not apply. It was also said that the meaning of the verse is that if they persist in their hypocrisy, they will have no place in Madinah unless they are expelled and cursed. This was done to them, because when Surah Bara’ah was revealed, they gathered, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “O so-and-so, get up and leave, for you are a hypocrite. O so-and-so, get up.” So their Muslim brothers got up and took charge of getting them out of the mosque. Fifth: The Almighty’s statement: The way of God is in the accusative case as a verbal noun, meaning that the way of God, the Exalted and Majestic, is for those who slander the prophets and display their hypocrisy, to be captured and killed. And you will not find any change in the way of God meaning any transformation or alteration, as narrated by Al-Naqqash. Al-Suddi said: It means that whoever is killed justly, there is no blood money on his killer. Al-Mahdawi: This verse is evidence of the permissibility of not carrying out the threat, and the evidence for that is the hypocrites remaining with him until he died. It is well known that people of virtue fulfill their promise and delay their threat, and this has been mentioned previously in Al-Imran and others.
33:61: Cursed wherever they are found, they will be seized and killed in a terrible manner.
33:62: "That is the way of God with those who passed on before. And you will not find any change in the way of God."
33:63: People ask you about the Hour. Say, "Its knowledge is only with God. And what makes you know? Perhaps the Hour is near." God the Almighty says: People ask you about the Hour. When these people who harmed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) were threatened with punishment, they asked about the Hour, denying it and suggesting that it would not happen. Say, 'The knowledge thereof is only with God.' That is, answer their question and say, "The knowledge thereof is with God. God's concealment of its time from me does not invalidate my prophethood. It is not a condition of a prophet to know the unseen without being taught by God, the Exalted. "And what makes you know? That is, what does he know? Perhaps the Hour will be near." That is, in a near future. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he pointed to his index and middle fingers. This was reported by the scholars of Sahih. It was also said that the Hour will not be near. So the feminine "ha was omitted, shifting the hour to the day, as in His statement, Indeed, the mercy of God is near to the doers of good. He did not say near," shifting mercy to forgiveness, as its feminine form is not inherently feminine. This has already been fully discussed. It was also said that the time of the Hour was concealed so that the servant would be prepared for it at all times.
33:64: Indeed, God has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a Blaze * wherein they will abide forever, finding neither protector nor helper. God the Almighty says: Indeed, God has cursed the disbelievers. That is, He expelled them and kept them away. Cursing means expulsion and banishment from mercy. This has already been explained in Surat Al-Baqarah. And has prepared for them a Blaze, wherein they will abide forever. Blaze is feminine because it means fire. They will find neither protector nor helper to save them from God’s punishment and eternity therein.
33:65: They will abide therein forever, finding neither protector nor helper.
33:66: God the Almighty says: On the Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire. The general reading is with a damma on the ta' and a fatha on the lam, as a passive verb. 'Isa al-Hamdani and Ibn Ishaq read: ََنَعلنَنِر برَروand a kasra on the lam, in the accusative case. 'Isa also read:َنَنلعبنٌر برَروَه العَنِهُْرُر منا َنَعتنَناThe Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire. This turning over is the change of their colors by the scorching of the Fire, sometimes turning black and green the next. And when their skins are replaced with other skins, then they will wish that they had never disbelieved. They will say, 'Oh, would that we had.' It is also possible that the meaning is: They will say on the Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire, Oh, would that we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger, meaning we did not disbelieve and thus be saved from this punishment as the believers were saved. This alif is used in commas, so it is stopped on it and not connected to it. The same applies to al-Sabila, which was mentioned earlier in the surah. Al-Hasan read:ِهَنا َنْعتنَنا ِناَنَءاIndeed, we obeyed our masters with a kasra on the ta', the plural ofِناَنةmasters. This is a warning against imitation. Sayyids is the plural of sayyid, which is an active verb, like kataba and fajra. Our sayyids is the plural of plural. Sayyids and the elders have the same meaning. Qatada said: They are the ones who were fed in the Battle of Badr. The most apparent is the generality of the leaders and chiefs in polytheism and misguidance, meaning we obeyed them in disobeying You and in what they led us into. So they led us astray from the way, meaning from the way, which is monotheism. So when the preposition was deleted, the verb was connected and made accusative. Misguidance does not take two objects without a preposition, like His statement: Indeed, he led me astray from the remembrance (al-Furqan 25:29).
33:67: And they said, 'Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our dignitaries, and they led us astray from the way.'
33:68: The Almighty says: Our Lord, give them double the punishment. Qatada said: The punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. It was also said: The punishment of disbelief and the punishment of misguidance, meaning, punish them with a double punishment as You punished us, for they went astray and led others astray. And curse them with a great curse. Ibn Mas'ud and his companions, Yahya and Asim read it with the letter ya. The rest read it with the letter tha. Abu Hatim, Abu Ubaid and An-Nahhas preferred this, based on the Almighty's saying: Those are the ones cursed by God and cursed by the cursers. Al-Baqarah 2:159. This meaning is common. Muhammad ibn Abi As-Sarri said: I saw in a dream that I was in the mosque of Ashkelon and a man was debating with me about someone who hates the companions of Muhammad. He said: And curse them with a great curse, then he repeated it until I lost sight of him, and he only says it with the letter tha. The reading with the letter ba goes back in meaning to the letter tha because what is great is great and immense.
33:69: O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses; but God cleared him of what they said, and he was honorable in the sight of God. When God the Almighty mentioned the hypocrites and disbelievers who harmed the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) and the believers, He warned the believers against being harmed, and forbade them from imitating the Children of Israel in harming their Prophet Moses. People differed about the reason Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) and Moses were harmed. Al-Naqqash related that they harmed Muhammad (peace be upon him) by saying: Zayd ibn Muhammad. Abu Wa’il said: They harmed him because the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) divided a portion, and a man from the Ansar said: This division was not done for the sake of God. This was mentioned to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and he became angry and said: May God have mercy on Moses, he was harmed more than this and he was patient. As for the harm done to Moses, peace be upon him, Ibn Abbas and a group said: It is what is included in the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and that is that he said: “The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, and Moses, peace be upon him, used to cover himself a lot and hide his body. Some people said, ‘He is leprous or a leper, or he has a disease.’ One day he went to bathe in a spring in the land of Ash-Sham and put his clothes on a rock. The rock ran away with his clothes, and Moses followed him naked, saying, ‘My clothes are a rock, my clothes are a rock,’ until he reached a group of the Children of Israel. They looked at him, and he was the best of them in character and the most just of them in appearance, but he was not what they said. This is what God Almighty said, ‘So God cleared him of what they said.’” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim with the same meaning. Muslim's version: He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "The Children of Israel used to bathe naked, looking at each other's private parts. Moses, peace be upon him, used to bathe alone. They said, 'By God, nothing prevents Moses from bathing with us except that he is urinary.'" One day he went to bathe and put his garment on a stone, but the stone ran away with his garment. Moses, peace be upon him, ran after him, saying, 'My garment, stone, my garment, stone,' until the Children of Israel looked at Moses' private parts and said, 'By God, there is nothing wrong with Moses.' The stone stood up and looked at him. It took its garment and began to strike the stone." Abu Hurairah said: By God, there were six or seven marks on the stone from which Moses struck the stone. This is one saying. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, that he said: They harmed Moses by saying, 'He killed Aaron.' This is because Moses and Aaron went out from the desert to a mountain, and Aaron died there. Moses came, and the Children of Israel said to Moses, 'You killed him, and he was kinder to us than you and more loving toward us.'" So they harmed him with that, so God the Almighty ordered the angels to carry him until they paraded him among the Children of Israel, and they saw a great sign that proved to them the truth of Moses, and there was no sign of killing on him. It has been said that the angels spoke of his death, and only the marble knew the location of his grave, and that God the Almighty made him deaf and mute. Aaron died before Moses in the wilderness, and Moses died two months before the end of the period of the wilderness. Al-Qushayri narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him: God the Almighty revived Aaron, and he informed them that He did not kill him, then he died. It has been said that the harm to Moses (peace be upon him) was their accusation of sorcery and madness. The first is correct. It is possible that they did all of that, and God exonerated him from all of that. Question: The fact that Moses (peace be upon him) placed his garment on the stone and entered the water naked is evidence of its permissibility, which is the view of the majority of scholars. Ibn Abi Layla forbade it and cited as evidence an invalid hadith, which is the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): Do not enter the water except with a loincloth, for the water is inhabited. Judge Iyad said: It is weak according to the scholars. I said: As for it being recommended to cover oneself, according to what Israel narrated on the authority of Abd al-A’la that al-Hasan ibn Ali entered a pond wearing his cloak and wrapping himself in it. When he came out, he was asked: I only covered myself from someone who sees me and I do not see him, meaning from my Lord and the angels. If it is said: How did Moses, peace be upon him, call the stone with the call of someone who has reason? It is said: Because the stone emanated an action of someone who has reason. And the stone is a vocative singular noun with the letter of calling omitted, as God Almighty said: Joseph, turn away from this (Yusuf 12:29). And my garment is in the accusative case with an implied verb, meaning: Give me my garment, or leave my garment, so the verb was omitted because the circumstance indicates it. God the Almighty says: And he was honored in the sight of God meaning great. Honorable among the Arabs means someone of great status and high position. It is narrated that whenever he asked God for something, He would give it to him. Ibn Masoud read: And he was a servant of God. It was also said that the meaning of honorable is that he spoke to Him directly. Abu Bakr al-Anbari said in Kitab al-Radd: Those who challenge the Quran claim that the Muslims have made a mistake and that he was honored in the sight of God, and that the correct version in his view is And he was a servant of God and honored. This indicates the weakness of his intention, the deficiency of his understanding, and the paucity of his knowledge. This is because if the verse were to be interpreted as saying And he was a servant, then the praise of Moses, peace be upon him, would be diminished. This is because honorable people are honored by the people of this world, by the people of his time, and by the people of the Hereafter. Therefore, one should not dwell on the place of praise, because if he was honored by the people of this world, then that would be a blessing from God upon him, and no praise from God would be evident along with it. When God Almighty clarified the place of praise by saying: And he was held in high esteem by God, he deserved honor and the greatest elevation because he was held in high esteem by God. So, without the word, the most excellent praise and the greatest commendation were diverted from the Prophet of God.
33:70: God the Almighty says: O you who have believed, fear God and speak words of appropriate justice. Meaning, intentionally and truthfully. Ibn Abbas said: Meaning, correctly. Qatada and Muqatil said: It means, say words of appropriate justice regarding Zaynab and Zayd, and do not attribute to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) what is impermissible. Ikrimah and Ibn Abbas also said: The correct statement is There is no god but God. It was also said: It is that which appears to be in agreement with its inner meaning. It was also said: It is that which is intended solely for the sake of God. It was also said: It is reconciling those who quarrel. It is derived from aiming an arrow to achieve its target. Correct statement includes good deeds, so it is general in all that was mentioned and other than that. The apparent meaning of the verse indicates that it only refers to what is contrary to the harm that was said about the Messenger and the believers. Then the Almighty promised that He will reward correct speech by correcting deeds and forgiving sins. That is enough for you as a degree and elevated position. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger that is, in what he has commanded and forbidden, has certainly achieved a great attainment.
33:71: "He will rectify for you your deeds and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys God and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great victory."
33:72: God Almighty says: “Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it and feared it; but man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant. * That God may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women and that God may accept the forgiveness of the believing men and believing women. And ever is God Forgiving and Merciful.” Since God, the Almighty, has mentioned in this Surah the rulings, He has commanded us to adhere to His commands. Trustworthiness encompasses all religious duties according to the most correct opinion, which is the opinion of the majority. Al-Tirmidhi, the wise Abu Abdullah, narrated: Ismail bin Nasr told us, on the authority of Salih bin Abdullah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid bin Jawhar, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “God, the Almighty, said to Adam, ‘O Adam, I offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth, and they could not bear it. Will you bear it and what is in it?’ He said, ‘And what is in it, O Lord?’ He said, ‘If you bear it, you will be rewarded, but if you neglect it, you will be punished.’ So he bore it and what is in it, and he did not remain in Paradise except for the time between the first prayer and the afternoon prayer, until Satan expelled him from it.” Trustworthiness is the obligatory duties that God has entrusted His servants with. There are different opinions regarding the details of some of them. Ibn Mas’ud said: It applies to financial trusts such as deposits and others. It was narrated from him that it applies to all obligatory duties, and the most severe of them is financial trustworthiness. Ubayy bin Ka’b said: It is part of trustworthiness for a woman to be entrusted with her private parts. Abu Dardaa said: Ghusl after sexual impurity is a trust, and God the Almighty has not entrusted the son of Adam with anything of his religion other than it. In a hadith, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Trustfulness is prayer. If you wish, you can say, I have prayed, and if you wish, you can say, I have not prayed. The same applies to fasting and ghusl after sexual impurity. Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As said: “The first thing God the Almighty created of man was his private parts. He said, ‘This is a trust I have entrusted to you, so do not treat it except with due care. If you guard it, I will guard you.’ So the private parts are a trust, the ear is a trust, the eye is a trust, the tongue is a trust, the stomach is a trust, the hand is a trust, the foot is a trust, and one who has no trust has no faith.” As-Suddi said: “It refers to Adam entrusting his son Cain with his children and family, and his betrayal of him by killing his brother. This is because God the Almighty said to him, ‘O Adam, do you know that I have a house on earth?’ He said, ‘O God, no.’ He said, ‘Then I have a house in Mecca, so go to it.’ He said to the sky, ‘Guard my son with trust,’ but it refused. He said to the earth, ‘Guard my son with trust,’ but it refused. He said the same to the mountains, but they refused.” So He said to Cain, Keep my son in trust. He said, Yes, you will go and come back and find your son as you please. So Cain returned and found that he had killed his brother. This is what God, the Most High, said, Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, and they declined to bear it. (Surah Al-Araf: 10) Muammar narrated from Al-Hasan that the Trust was offered to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains. They said, What is in it? It was said to them, If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do evil, you will be punished. They said, No. Mujahid said, “When God created Adam, He showed it to him. He said, “What is it?” He said, If you do well, I will reward you, and if you do evil, I will punish you. He said, You have thus undertaken it, O Lord. Mujahid said, Between you bearing it and my being expelled from Paradise, there was only the time between noon and afternoon prayers. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God, the Most High, Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, (Surah Al-Araf: 10) He said, “Trust is the obligations. God, the Almighty, offered it to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains. If they fulfilled it, He would reward them, and if they neglected it, He would punish them.” They hated that and were afraid, not because it was a sin, but out of respect for the religion of God, the Almighty, that they would not carry it out. Then He offered it to Adam, and he accepted it with what it contained. An-Nahhas said: This is the opinion of the commentators. It was said: When death approached Adam, peace be upon him, he was commanded to offer the Trust to all creation. He offered it, but none accepted it except his sons. It was also said: This Trust is what God, the Almighty, deposited in the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and all creation. One of the proofs of His Lordship is that they made it known, and they made it known, except for man, who concealed it and denied it. This was said by some of the theologians. The meaning of We offered is We made known, just as you say: I offered a slave girl for sale. The meaning is that We offered the Trust and its squandering to the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, from among the angels, mankind, and jinn, but they refused to bear it, meaning to bear its burden, as God, the Almighty, said: And let them bear their own burdens and other burdens in addition to their own Al-‘Ankabut 29:13. And man bore it Al-Hasan said: What is meant is the disbeliever and the hypocrite. Indeed, he was unjust to himself, ignorant of his Lord. So this answer is a metaphor, like: And ask the town (Yusuf 12:82). And there is another answer that is literal, that He offered the heavens, the earth, and the mountains the Trust and its squandering, which is the reward and the punishment, that is, He showed it to them, but they did not bear its burden, and they feared and said: I seek neither reward nor punishment, and each one said: This is something we cannot bear, and we are your listeners and obedient to what we are commanded to do and subjected to, said Al-Hasan and others. The scholars said: It is known that inanimate objects do not understand or respond, so life must be considered according to the latter statement. This offering is an offering of choice, not obligation. And the offering to a human being is obligation. Al-Qaffal and others said: The presentation in this verse is a parable, meaning that if the heavens and the earth, despite their large bodies, were to be tasked, it would be too heavy for them to bear the burden of the laws because of the rewards and punishments that they contain. That is, the task is something that the heavens, the earth, and the mountains are truly beyond their ability to bear, and man has been tasked with it, even though he is unjust and ignorant, if he had reason. This is like His statement, If We had sent down this Qur’an upon a mountain Al-Hashr 59:21, then He said, And these examples We present to the people Al-Hashr 59:21. Al-Qaffal said: Once it is established that God sets examples, and we are informed of a report that can only be interpreted as a parable, it must be interpreted accordingly. Some people said: The verse is a metaphor, meaning that if we compare the weight of the trust to the strength of the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, we see that they cannot bear it, and that if they could speak, they would refuse and be afraid. So He expressed this meaning with His statement, Indeed, We offered the Trust Al-Hashr 59:21. This is like saying: I offered the load to the camel and it refused, meaning you compared its strength to the weight of the load, and you saw that it fell short of it. It was also said: We offered means we opposed the trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains, so these things were weak in relation to the trust, and the trust outweighed them by its weight. It was also said that the offering of the trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains was from Adam, peace be upon him. This is because when God, the Most High, made him his successor over his descendants and gave him authority over all that is on the earth of livestock, birds, and wild animals, and made a covenant with him in which He commanded him, forbade him, prohibited him, and permitted him, so he accepted it and continued to act in accordance with it. When death approached him, he asked God to teach him who would succeed him and to entrust him with the trust that he had been entrusted with. So God commanded him to offer that to the heavens with the condition that he took from them of reward if they obeyed and punishment if they disobeyed, but they refused to accept it out of fear of God’s punishment. Then He commanded him to offer that to the earth and all the mountains, but they refused. Then he ordered him to present it to his son. So he presented it to him and he accepted it with the condition, and did not fear from it what the heavens, the earth and the mountains feared. Indeed, he was unjust to himself and ignorant of the consequences of what he had entrusted to his Lord. Al-Tirmidhi, the wise Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Ali, said: I am amazed at this speaker and where he got this story from. If we look at the traces, we find them contrary to what he said. If we look at its outward appearance, we find it contrary to what he said. If we look at its inner meaning, we find it far from what he said. This is because he repeated the mention of trust and did not mention what trust is, except that he hints in his statement that he had given him authority over everything on earth, and that God had made a covenant with him in which was His commands and prohibitions, what was permissible and what was forbidden. He claimed that he had ordered him to present this to the heavens, the earth and the mountains. So what would the heavens, the earth and the mountains do with what was permissible and what was forbidden? What would be the authority over livestock, birds and wild animals? And how would it be if he presented it to his son and he accepted it as a burden on his descendants after him. At the beginning of the report in the revelation, He offered the Trust to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains until their refusal became apparent. Then He mentioned that man bore it, i.e., from himself, not that he bore it, so He called him unjust, i.e., to himself, ignorant of what was in it. As for the narrations that are contrary to what He mentioned, my father, may God have mercy on him, told me, he said, Al-Faydh bin Al-Fadl Al-Kufi told us, Al-Sari bin Ismail told us, from Amer Al-Sha’bi, from Masruq, from Abdullah bin Mas’ud, he said: When God created the Trust like a rock, then He placed it wherever He willed, then He called the heavens, the earth, and the mountains to bear it, and He said to them: This is the Trust, and it has a reward and a punishment. They said: O Lord, we have no strength to bear it. And man approached before he was called, so he said to the heavens, the earth, and the mountains: Why are you standing? They said: Our Lord called us to carry this, but we were afraid of it and could not speak. He said: So he moved it with his hand and said: By God, if you wished to carry it, I would carry it. So he carried it until it reached his knees, then he put it down and said: By God, if you wished to do more, I would do more. They said: Here you go. So he carried it until it reached his waist, then he put it down and said: By God, if you wished to do more, I would do more. They said: Here you go. So he carried it until he placed it on his shoulder, and when he was about to put it down, they said: Stay where you are, for this is a trust, and it has a reward and a punishment. Our Lord commanded us to carry it, but we were afraid of it, and you carried it without being called upon to do so. So it is around your neck and the necks of your descendants until the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, you were unjust and ignorant. He mentioned reports from the Companions and the Followers, most of which have been presented. And man carried it means he committed himself to fulfilling its rights, and in doing so he was unjust to himself. Qatadah said: Regarding the trust, he is ignorant to the extent that he entered into it. This is the interpretation of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr. Al-Hasan said: He is ignorant of his Lord. He said: The meaning of carrying it is that he betrayed it. Al-Zajjaj said: The verse is about the disbeliever, the hypocrite, and the sinners according to their status according to this interpretation. Ibn Abbas, his companions, Al-Dahhak, and others said: The human being is Adam. He carried the trust, but not a day passed before he committed the sin that expelled him from Paradise. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas that God the Almighty said to him: Will you carry this trust and what is in it? He said: What is in it? He said: If you do well, you will be rewarded, and if you do wrong, you will be punished. He said: I carry it and what is in it, between my ears and my shoulders. God the Almighty said: I will help you. I have made a veil for your sight, so close it to what is not permissible for you, and a garment for your private parts, so do not uncover them except for what is permissible for you. Some people said: Man is the entire species. This is good considering the generality of the trust as we mentioned first. Al-Suddi said: Man is Cain. God knows best. That God may punish the hypocrites, men and women. The lam in to punish is related to to carry, meaning that He carried it in order to punish the sinner and reward the obedient. It is the lam of explanation because the punishment is a result of carrying the trust. It was said that it was We offered, meaning that We offered the trust to everyone, then We gave it to mankind to expose the polytheism of the polytheist and the hypocrisy of the hypocrite so that God might punish them, and the faith of the believer so that God might reward him. And God accepts their repentance is the Hassan reading with the nominative case, separating it from the first, meaning that God accepts their repentance in all circumstances. And God is Forgiving and Merciful is predicate after predicate of was. It may be an adjective for Forgiving, or it may be a state of the pronoun. And God knows best.
33:73: "That God may punish the hypocritical men and hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men and polytheistic women, and that God may accept the repentance of the believing men and believing women. And God is Forgiving and Merciful."
34:1: It is Meccan according to everyone, except for one verse regarding which there is a difference of opinion, which is the verse in which God the Almighty says: And those who have been given knowledge will see (al-Baqarah 2:17). A group said: It is Meccan, and what is meant by the believers are the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as stated by Ibn Abbas. A group said: It is Medinan, and what is meant by the believers are those who converted to Islam in Medina, such as Abdullah ibn Salam and others, as stated by Muqatil. Qatadah said: They are the nation of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him), the believers in him, whoever he may be. It consists of fifty-four verses. The Almighty said: Praise be to God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth which is in the accusative case as an attribute or a substitute. It is also permissible for it to be in the nominative case as an implied subject, or it may be in the accusative case meaning I mean. Sibawayh reported that Praise be to God, the people of praise is in the nominative case, and that the accusative and genitive cases, complete praise and comprehensive commendation are all due to God, since all blessings are from Him. This has been discussed at the beginning of Surat Al-Fatihah. To Him be praise in the Hereafter is said to refer to the Almighty’s statement: And they will say, ‘Praise be to God, Who has fulfilled His promise to us’ Az-Zumar 39:74. It is also said that it refers to the Almighty’s statement: And their final prayer will be, ‘Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds’ Yunus 10:10. He is the One to be praised in the Hereafter just as He is the One to be praised in this world. He is the Owner of the Hereafter just as He is the Owner of the first. And He is the Wise in His actions. The All-Aware of His creation’s affairs.
34:2: The Almighty says, He knows what penetrates the earth meaning what enters it of rain and other things, as He said: He causes springs of treasures, buried goods, and the dead to spring from the earth, and there are no sacks for Him. And what comes forth from it of plants and other things. And what descends from the sky of rain, snow, hail, thunder, provisions, decrees, and blessings. Ali ibn Abi Talib recited And what We send down with a noon and a shaddah. And what ascends therein of angels and the deeds of the servants, as Al-Hasan and others said. And He is the Most Merciful, the Forgiving.
34:3: God the Almighty says: Those who disbelieve will not come to us. It was said that this refers to the people of Mecca. Muqatil said: Abu Sufyan said to the disbelievers of Mecca, "Al-Lat and Al-Uzza said: The Hour will never come to us, nor will we stumble." God the Almighty said: Say, O Muhammad, Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you. Harun narrated on the authority of Talq Al-Mu'allim, who said: I heard our sheikhs recite Say, 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you' with a ya, which they interpreted to mean, as if he said: The Resurrection or its command will surely come to you. Just as God the Almighty said: Whoever is turned away from it that Day has certainly received mercy, and that is the clear attainment. (al-Nahl 16:33) So these disbelievers acknowledge the beginning but deny the return, and this is refuted because they acknowledged the decree of resurrection and said: Even if He decreed, He does not do it. This is an arbitrary ruling after the Messengers informed us according to the Sunnah that He will resurrect creation. If report comes of something that is possible in action and possible, then denying someone whose truthfulness is obligatory is impossible. The Knower of the Unseen is in the nominative case, as read by Nafi' and Ibn Kathir, as a subject, and its predicate is not hidden from Him. Asim and Abu Amr read it with the khufs, meaning, praise be to God, the Knower. Based on this reading, it is not appropriate to pause at the phrase will come to you. Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read The Knower of the Unseen as an exaggeration and description. Not hidden from Him means, He is not absent from Him, also is hidden. Al-Farra' said: I prefer the kasr. An-Nahhas: It is the reading of Yahya ibn Waththab, and it is a well-known language. It is said azaaba or yazaaba if it means far or absent. The weight of an atom means the size of a small ant. In the heavens nor on the earth nor smaller than that nor larger in the reading of Al-A'mash nor smaller than that nor larger with the fatha in both of them in apposition to atom. The reading of the common people is in the nominative case in apposition to mithqal. Except in a clear Book He is the Knower of what He created and nothing is hidden from Him.
34:4: لهجهِهىis in the accusative case with the lam ofكى, and the meaning is:لهجهِهىwill come to you. Those who believe and do righteous deeds will receive the reward, and the disbelievers will receive the punishment. Those - meaning the believers - will have forgiveness for their sins. And a generous provision - which is Paradise.
34:5: God the Almighty says: And those who strive against Our verses meaning, to invalidate Our evidence and deny Our verses, to outsmart racing, thinking that they can evade Us, and that God is not able to resurrect them in the Hereafter, and they thought that We would neglect them, then these will have a punishment of a painful punishment. It is said: Ajazah and Ajazah if it overcomes or overpowers someone. Alaim is the reading of Nafi' with the kasrah, meaning to defeat, for rajz is the punishment. God the Almighty says: So We sent down upon those who did wrong a punishment from the sky (Al-Baqarah 2:59). Ibn Kathir and Hafs from Asim read a punishment of a painful punishment with the raf al-mim here and in Al-Hathi as a description of the punishment. Ibn Kathir, Ibn Muhaisin, Humayd ibn Qays, Mujahid, and Abu Amr read mu'jazizin mubthani meaning they discouraged people from believing in the miracles and verses of the Quran.
34:6: When he mentioned those who sought to invalidate the prophethood, he explained that those who were given knowledge will see that the Quran is true. Muqatil said: Those who were given knowledge are the believers among the People of the Book. Ibn Abbas said: They are the companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. It was also said: All Muslims, and this is more correct due to its general meaning. Seeing means knowing, and it is in the accusative case in apposition to li-jazi, meaning that he will reward and see, as stated by al-Zajjaj and al-Farra. This is questionable because his statement: he will reward is connected to his statement: The Hour will surely come to you, and it is not said: The Hour will surely come to you. Those who were given knowledge will see that the Quran is true, for they will see the Quran as true even if the Hour has not come to them. The correct view is that it is in the nominative case as a new subject, as stated by al-Qushayri. I said: If li-yarzi is related to the meaning He established that in a clear Book, then it is good to connect wa-yarā to it, meaning and He established also so that those who have been given knowledge may see that the Qur’an is the truth. It is also permissible for it to be a new sentence. Allahu is in the accusative case as the first object of li-yarā to see. Huwa al-Haqq is the second object, and it is a separator. The Kufians say huwa ‘a’mad. It is permissible to put it in the nominative case as the subject. Al-Haqq is its predicate, and the sentence is in the accusative case as the second object. The accusative is more common in both of them when it has the alif and lam according to all grammarians. The same applies to what is indefinite and does not take the alif, so it resembles the definite. If the predicate is a well-known noun, such as your saying Your brother was Zayd, then al-Farra’ claimed that the preferred option is the nominative case. Likewise, Muhammad was ‘Amr. Therefore, in choosing the nominative case, since it does not contain the definite article, it is more indefinite than your saying: Zaid was the one sitting, because this is not permissible except in the nominative case. And guides to the path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy means that the Qur’an guides to the path of Islam, which is the religion of God. And he indicated by his saying: the Almighty that He cannot be overcome. And by his saying: the Praiseworthy that the attribute of helplessness does not suit Him.
34:7: God the Almighty says: And those who disbelieve say, 'Shall we guide you to a man' - if you wish, you can assimilate the lam into the noon because it is close to it - 'who will inform you when you are torn apart' This is reporting someone who said, The Hour will not come to us, meaning, Shall we guide you to a man who will inform you? meaning, Shall we tell you how you will be resurrected after decaying in the graves? This stems from their extreme denial. Al-Zamakhshari: If you say, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was a well-known figure among the Quraysh, and his prophecy of the resurrection was widely spread among them. So what is the meaning of their saying, Shall we guide you to a man who will inform you? They denied it to them and offered to guide them to him, as one guides an unknown person in an unknown matter. I say: By that they intended to joke, mock, and ridicule, so they presented it as an adornment with some riddles that are used to argue for laughter and amusement, ignoring him and his command. And if it is in the accusative case and the agent is you have torn, said Al-Nahhas. It is not permissible for the agent to be He informs you, because He will not inform them at that time. And it is not permissible for the agent to be what comes after if, because it does not act on what precedes it, and what comes after it or its object does not precede it. Al-Zajjaj permitted the agent to be omitted, the estimation: If you tear every tear, you will be resurrected, or He informs you that you will be resurrected if you tear. Al-Mahdawi: You have torn does not work on it, because it is a complement to it, and the complement to it does not work on the complement. Some of them permitted it on the condition that if is used for retaliation in poetry. The meaning of you have torn every tear is that you have separated completely. And tearing is tearing something, it is said a torn garment, torn, torn, torn, and torn.
34:8: The Almighty's saying: Does he invent a lie against God? When the interrogative alif was introduced, the alif of connection was dispensed with, so it was deleted. The opening of the alif of interrogation was to differentiate it from the alif of connection. This was previously mentioned in Surah Maryam when God the Almighty said: He knows the unseen (Maryam 19:78) So he will die. Or is he mad? This is a refutation of what was said previously by the polytheists. The meaning is: The polytheists said: Does he invent a lie against God? Invention is penetration. Or is he mad, meaning insane, so he speaks about what he does not know. Then He responded to them by saying: Rather, those who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in the punishment and in extreme error. Meaning, the matter is not as they said. Rather, he is the most truthful of the truthful, and whoever denies the resurrection will be in the punishment tomorrow, and today in error from the right path, when they resort to challenging God and attributing slander to the one whom God supported with miracles.
34:9: God the Most High knows that He who has power over the creation of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them has power to resurrect them and hasten their punishment. He used as evidence His power over them, and that the heavens and the earth belong to Him, and that they surround them on every side. So how can they be safe from being swallowed up and destroyed as He did with Qarun and the Companions of the Thicket? Hamzah and Al-Kisa'i read If He wills, He will swallow them up the earth or He wills with the letter ya in all three verses, meaning if God wills, He will command the earth to swallow them up, or the sky to fall upon them in a crushing fragment. The rest read it with the letter noon for emphasis. As-Sulami and Hafs read it with the letter kasfan with the fatha on the seen, the rest read it with the letter sukun. Its explanation has been presented previously in Subhan and other verses. Indeed in that is a sign meaning in what we have mentioned of Our power is a clear indication. For every servant who turns back meaning one who repents and returns to God with his heart. The one who turns back is specifically mentioned because he is the one who benefits from contemplating God's proofs and verses.
34:10: And We certainly gave David bounty from Us. Explain to those who deny the prophethood of Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) that sending messengers is not something out of our control, but rather We sent messengers and supported them with miracles, and We punished those who opposed them. We gave means We gave. Bonus means something by which We gave him preference over others. There are different opinions about this bounty: 1. Prophethood. 2. The Psalms. 3. Knowledge. God the Almighty said: And We gave David and Solomon knowledge. (al-Naml 27:15). 4. Strength. God the Almighty said: And remember Our servant David, the possessor of strength. (Sad: 17). Fifth: Subjugating the mountains and people. God the Almighty said: O mountains, echo with him. Sixth: Repentance. God the Almighty said: O David, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth. (Sad: 26) Eighth: Softening iron. God the Almighty said: And We made iron soft for him. (Saba’: 10) Ninth: A beautiful voice. David, peace be upon him, had a beautiful voice and a beautiful voice. A beautiful voice is a gift and favor from God the Almighty, and it is what is meant by His saying: He increases in creation what He wills. (Fatir 35:1) as will come, God the Almighty willing. “And the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Abu Musa: ‘You have been given a flute from the flutes of the family of David.’” Scholars said: The flute and the melody are the beautiful voice, and this is why the instrument of the zumar is called a flute. Many of the jurists of the regions approved of reciting with embellishment and chanting, and this was mentioned in the introduction to the book, and praise be to God. God the Almighty said: {O mountains, echo with him} meaning, and We said, O Rahabal, echo with him, meaning glorify with him, because God the Blessed and Exalted said: {Indeed, We subjected the mountains to him, to glorify Us in the evening and at sunrise} (Sad: 18). Abu Maysarah said: It is glorification in the Ethiopian dialect, and the meaning of the mountains’ glorification is that God the Almighty created in them glorification just as He created speech in the tree, so what is heard from the glorifier is heard from them, a miracle for David, peace be upon him. It was said: The meaning is, go with him wherever he wishes, from the interpretation that it is the movement of the entire day and the descent of night. Ibn Muqbil said: We caught up with the Oboa neighborhood, pushed by the sun's rays and the side swaying. Al-Hasan, Qatada and others read: Obey with him meaning return with him, from aba ya’oob which means to return, owba and awiya and iyyaab. It was said that the meaning is: deal with him as David deals during the day. So when he recited Az-Zubun, the mountains would roar with him and the birds would listen to him as if they did what he did. Wahbah ibn Munabbih said: The meaning is: we would mourn with him and the birds would help him with that. So when he cried out in mourning, the mountains would answer him with their echo and the birds would swarm over him from above. The echo of the mountains that people hear only existed from that day until this hour. So he was supported by the help of the mountains and the birds so that he would not find a break. So when the break came, he would become agitated, that is, he would revolt and move and become strong with the help of the mountains and the birds. He had made such a sound that the wild beasts of the mountains would swarm over the beauty of his voice, and the running water would stop running at the sound of his voice. Al-Tayr the bird is in the nominative case, as read by Ibn Abi Ishaq and Nasr on the authority of Asim, Ibn Hormuz, and Muslima bin Abdul Malik. They connected it to the word mountains or to the implied word or with the good separation by preventing it. The rest use the accusative case in apposition to the position of O mountains, meaning we called out to the mountains and the birds, as Sibawayh said. Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’a also uses an implied verb meaning and we subjected the birds to him. Al-Kisa’i said it is in apposition, meaning and we gave him the birds, based on and we certainly gave David a favor from us. An-Nahhas can be an accusative with it, as you say: the water and the wood were made equal.” I heard Az-Zajjaj permit it: I stood up and Zayd, so the meaning is I responded with him and with the birds. “And We made the iron soft for him.” Ibn Abbas said: It became like wax to him. Al-Hasan said: Like dough, so he would work it without fire. Al-Suddi said: The iron in his hand was like wet clay, tamarisk, or wax, and he would shape it however he wanted, without using fire or hitting it with a hammer. Muqatil said: The shield would be emptied in a few days or some of the night, and its price would be a thousand dirhams. It was said: He was given the power to bend iron, and the reason for that is that when David, peace be upon him, was king among Israel, he met a king whom David thought was a human being. David was disguised and asked secretly about his exile and his conduct among the Children of Israel. So David said to that person who appeared to him: What do you say about this King David? The king said to him: What a good servant, were it not for a characteristic in him. David said: What is it? He said: He earns his living from the public treasury, and if he ate from the work of his hand, his virtues would be complete. So he returned and supplicated to God to teach him a trade and make it easy for him, so He taught him the trade of clothing, as God, the Almighty, said in Surat Al-Anbiya. So He softened iron for him, so he made armor. He used to make a coat of armor in one day or night worth a thousand dirhams, until he saved a lot of it and his household’s livelihood expanded. He used to give charity to the poor and needy, and he used to spend a third of his money on the interests of the Muslims. He was the first to make and take armor. Before that, it was made of plates. It is said that he used to sell each coat of armor for four thousand. The word armor is feminine if it is for war, while the word a woman’s is masculine. Question: This verse indicates that people of virtue should learn crafts, and that practicing them does not diminish their status, but rather increases their virtue and merit, as they achieve humility in themselves and independence from others, and earn lawful earnings that are devoid of gratitude. “In the Sahih, it is narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The best of what a person eats is what he earns with his own hands, and the Prophet of God, David, used to eat from what he earned with his own hands.” This has already been mentioned in the hadiths with excellence, and praise be to God.
34:11: The Almighty said: Make long coats of mail long coats of mail, meaning complete, perfect, and wide. It is said: a coat of mail, garment, or other garment covers everything it is on and less of it. And measure in secret Qatada said: Before him, coats of mail were plates and were heavy, and that is why he commanded to measure what combines lightness and strength. That is, measure what you take from these two meanings in its equal measure. That is, do not intend strength, for it will be heavy, nor lightness, for it will remove strength. Ibn Zayd said: The measurement that was mentioned is in the size of the ring, that is, do not make it small, for it will weaken and the coat of mail will not be able to defend, and do not make it large, for the wearer will be injured. Ibn Abbas said: The measurement that he commanded is in the nail, that is, do not make the nail of the coat of mail thin so it splits, nor thick so it will break the ring. It was narrated as yaqsam with the letter qaf. And the letter fa is also a narration. In the narrative The narrative is weaving the rings of armor, and from it the maker of the rings of armor was called: sirad and zarad. The letter seen was replaced by zay, as it was said: sirat and zarat. And the narrative: beads, it is said: sard yasrad if he beaded. And the mustard: the healer, and it is said sirad, Al-Shamakh said: Our horses remained in your homes one after the other, as the reins of the Khawarizmi continued to scatter. And the sarrad: the thread that is used for sewing. Labd said: Its soft, smooth pages are torn asunder, just as a lily emerges from a litter. It is said: He narrated the hadith and fasting. Narration in them means that they come together in one sequence, and it is the secret of speech. In the hadith of Aisha: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, did not narrate the hadith as you narrate it. He used to narrate the hadith, if a counter wanted to count it, he would have done so. Sibawayh said: And from this comes the word sarandi meaning a bold man. He said: Because he goes forward. The origin of that is in narrating the armor, which is to tighten it and make the order of its rings not different. Labid said: He made iron double its chains so that he could live a long life without any regrets. Abu Dhu'ayb said: And there are two chains of narration on them, which David ruled or Al-Wabigh made. And do righteous deeds. This is addressed to David and his family, as He said: Work, O family of David, with gratitude. (Saba’: 34) Indeed, I, of what you do, am Seeing.
34:12: The Almighty said: And to Solomon We subjected the wind. Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is: And We subjected to Solomon the wind. Asim read in the narration of Abu Bakr from him: The wind in the nominative case as a subject, and the meaning is to him the wind was subjected, or to be stable, that is, and to Solomon We subjected its wind, and it has the same first meaning. If someone were to say: If you say I gave Zaid a dirham and to Ma'ruf a dinar, then you raised it, then it does not have the meaning of the first, and it is possible that you did not give him the dinar. It was said: The matter is thus, but the verse is different from this in terms of meaning, because it is known that no one subjected it except God, the Almighty. Its morning is a month and its evening is a month meaning a month's journey. Al-Hasan said: He would go out from Damascus and take a nap in Istakhr, and between them is a month's journey for one who is fast, then he would go back from Istakhr and spend the night in Kabul, and between them is a month for one who is fast. Al-Suddi said: We would travel with him in one day a journey of two months. Saeed bin Jubair narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: When Solomon sat down, his companions would set up four hundred thousand chairs. Then the leaders of mankind would sit next to him, and the lowest of mankind would sit next to them, and the leaders of the jinn would sit next to the lowest of mankind, and the lowest of the jinn would sit next to them. And a flying chair would be assigned to the work of the next day that he knew. Then the wind would carry them, and the birds would shade them from the sun. So he would go from Jerusalem to Istakhr and spend the night in Jerusalem. Then Ibn Abbas recited: Its morning is a month and its evening is a month. Wahb bin Munabbih said: It was mentioned to me that there was a house on the side of the Tigris, and it was written on it - written by some of Solomon’s companions, either from the jinn or humans -: We have settled and we did not build it, and a building we found. We went from Istakhr and left it, and we are returning from it, God willing, so we will spend the night in Syria. Al-Hasan said: Solomon was so busy with the horses that he missed the afternoon prayer, so he hamstrung the horses, so God replaced them with better and faster ones. He replaced them with a caravan that would go wherever he wanted, traveling in the morning and evening for a month. Ibn Zayd said: Solomon settled in the city of Palmyra, and the devil’s command preceded his departure from Syria to Iraq, so they built it for him with stone, columns, and white and yellow marble. Al-Nabigha says about it: Except for Solomon, when God said to him, Go into the wilderness and set it apart from the hotel. And the jinn have been given permission to build Palmyra with stones and columns. Whoever obeys you, benefit him through his obedience as he obeyed you, and guide him to the right path. And whoever disobeys, punish him with a punishment that will put an end to injustice and will not leave him in a state of humiliation. These verses were found engraved on a rock in the land of Yashkur, created by some of the companions of Solomon, peace be upon him: We, with no power but that of our Lord, will go to our homelands from the land of Palmyra. If we left, our journey would have been a month and the next day would have been the last. People who willingly sold their souls to God through the victory of the Son of David, the purified prophet. They have merit and elevation in the high religion, and if they are attributed one day, they are among the best of people. When they ride the obedient wagon, the initiative hastened its month and did not fall short They were wronged by the birds who lined up with me, fluttering above them, not scatter- ing. God the Almighty said: {And We made a fountain of molten copper flow for him.} Al-Qatar refers to copper, as reported by Ibn Abbas and others. It flowed for him for a distance of three days, just as water flows. It was in the land of Yemen. The slave trader did not melt it, according to what was narrated before him. It did not melt, but it melted immediately. Today, people benefit from what God the Almighty brought forth for Solomon. Qatadah said: May God use it as He wishes. It was said to Ikrimah: Where did it flow? He said: I do not know! Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Al-Suddi said: The yellow spring flowed for him for three days and their nights. Al-Qushayri said: The specification of the flow being three days is not known, and perhaps it is a mistake of the narrator, as in a narration from Mujahid: It flowed from Sana’a for three nights from what is next to it. This indicates the location, not the duration. It appears that he made the copper flow for Solomon in his mine, a spring that flowed like springs of water, as evidence of his prophethood. Al-Khalil said: Al-Qatar means molten copper. I said: Its proof is the reading of the one who reads: From a falling drop. “And of the jinn were those who worked before him by permission of his Lord,” meaning by His command. And whoever among them deviates from Our command, which we commanded him to do in obeying Solomon, We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze, meaning in the Hereafter. This was said by most of the commentators. And it was said that it was in this world, and that is because God Almighty appointed over them—as narrated by al-Suddi—an angel with a whip of fire in his hand, so whoever deviated from the command of Solomon, He struck him with that whip from where he did not see it, burning him. Min is in the accusative case meaning And We subjected to him from the jinn those who worked. It is permissible for it to be in the nominative case, as mentioned previously in al-Rih.
34:13: It contains eight issues: First: The Almighty said: of sanctuaries and statues. The sanctuary in the language: every elevated place. And the one who prays in it is called a mihrab, because it must be raised and glorified. Ad-Dahhak said: of sanctuaries means of mosques. Qatada said the same. Mujahid said: The sanctuaries are lower than palaces. Abu Ubaidah said: The sanctuary is the most honorable of the houses in the house. He said: Like ivory dolls in the sanctuaries, or like eggs in a garden, a flower is illuminated. It was said: It is what one ascends to by stairs, like a beautiful room, as He said: When they climbed over the sanctuary (Surah Sad: 21) and His saying: So he came out to his people from the sanctuary (Maryam 19:11), meaning he looked down upon them. And in the report, he ordered that a thousand sanctuaries be made around his throne, in which were a thousand men, wearing hair-clothes, crying out to God constantly, and he was on the throne in his procession and the sanctuaries were around him, and he said to his soldiers when he mounted: Glorify God to that sign, and when they reached it, he said: Praise Him to that sign, and when they reached it, he said: Magnify Him to that other sign, so the soldiers entered with glorification and praise in one place. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And statues is the plural of statue. It is everything that is made in the form of an animal or something other than an animal. It was said: They were made of glass, copper, and marble, statues of things that were not animals. It was mentioned that they were pictures of prophets and scholars, and they were made in mosques for people to see them and increase their worship and diligence. “The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whenever a righteous man died among them, they would build a mosque over his grave and make those pictures in it.” That is, so that they would remember their worship and strive in worship. This indicates that making pictures was permissible at that time, and that was abrogated by the law of Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). This will be further explained in Surat Nuh (peace be upon him). It was said: The statues were talismans that he made, and it was forbidden for any artist to go beyond them, so he would make a statue of a fly, a mosquito, or a crocodile in a place, and he would order them not to go beyond it once as long as that statue stood. The singular of statues is statue with a kasra on the ta. He said: Oh God, I spent a day and a night playing with a girl who looked like a statue. It was said that these statues were men made of copper and he asked his Lord to breathe life into them so that they would fight in the way of God and not weave weapons among them. It was said that Isfandiyar was one of them, and God knows best. It was narrated that they made for him two lions at the bottom of his throne and two eagles above it, so that when he wanted to ascend, he would spread them out. The two lions have their arms, and when they sit, the two eagles spread their wings. Third: Al-Maki narrated in his Al-Hidayah: That a group permits photography, and they cite this verse as evidence. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is a mistake, and I do not remember from any of the imams of knowledge who permit it. I said: What Makki narrated was mentioned by An-Nahhas before him. An-Nahhas said: Some people said that making images is permissible because of this verse and because God Almighty informed us about the Messiah. Some people said: It has been proven that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade them, and warned whoever made them or adopted them. So God Almighty abrogated with this what was permissible before that. The wisdom behind that was because he was sent, peace be upon him, and images were to be worshipped, so it was more correct to remove them. Fourth: Statue is of two types: animal and dead. Dead things are of two types: inanimate and dormant. The jinn used to make all of them for Solomon, due to the generality of his statement: and statues. In the Israelite narrations, it is mentioned that statues of birds were on Solomon’s throne. If it is said: There is no generality to his statement: and statues, because it is an affirmation in an indefinite noun, and an affirmation in an indefinite noun has no generality. Rather, generality is in the negation in an indefinite noun. We say: That is how it is, but this affirmation in an indefinite noun is coupled with what necessitates it being taken as general, which is his statement: whatever He wills. So the coupling of the will with it necessitates its generality. If it is said: How did he acquire the forbidden images? We say: That was permissible in his law, but it was abrogated by our law, as we have explained. And God knows best. On the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah: Making pictures was not forbidden. Fifth: The implications of the hadiths indicate that pictures are forbidden. Then it came: Except for what was a pattern on a garment. So he was singled out from the group of pictures. Then it was proven that it was disliked by his saying, peace be upon him, to Aisha regarding the garment: Take it away from me, for every time I see it, I remember the world. Then he was forbidden from doing so by tearing the patterned garment on Aisha. Then she was forbidden from doing so by cutting two pillows for him, and the picture changed and went out of its proper form. So that is permissible if the picture on it is not in a continuous form. If it was in a continuous form, it would not be permissible, because of her saying regarding the patterned cushion: I bought it for you to sit on and use as a pillow. So he was forbidden from doing so and he was threatened with punishment for it. And it was made clear by the hadith about praying towards pictures that that is permissible regarding patterns on a garment, then the prohibition abrogated it. So this is how the matter was settled regarding it, and God knows best. This was stated by Ibn al-Arabi. Sixth: Muslim narrated on the authority of Aisha, who said: We had a curtain with a statue of a bird on it, and whenever a person entered, he would face it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Turn this around, for every time I enter and see it, I remember the world. She said: We had a velvet cloth that we used to say was made of silk, so we used to wear it. And on her authority she said: “A man entered upon the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) while I was covering myself with a curtain on which there was a picture. His face changed colour, then he took hold of the curtain and tore it, then said: ‘Among the people who will be most severely punished on the Day of Resurrection are those who imitate the creation of God, the Almighty and Majestic.’” It was narrated from her that she had a garment on which there were pictures stretched out into a niche, and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to pray towards it, so he said: ‘Take it away from me.’ She said: ‘So I took it away and made it into two pillows.’ Some scholars said: It is possible that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) tore the garment and ordered it to be left behind out of piety, because the place of prophethood and message is perfection. So reflect on that. Seventh: Al-Muzani said on the authority of Al-Shafi’i: If a man is invited to a wedding and sees an image of a living being or images of living beings, he should not enter if it is erected. If it is something that can be stepped on, there is no problem, even if it is an image of a tree. They did not differ that images on hanging curtains are disliked but not forbidden. The same applies to what is drawn or engraved in a building. Some of them made an exception for what is a pattern on a garment, based on the hadith of Sahl ibn Hunaif. I said: The Messenger of God cursed the image-makers and did not make an exception. And his saying: The makers of these images will be tormented on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to them, ‘Bring to life what you have created.’ He did not make an exception. “In Al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘A neck will emerge from the Fire on the Day of Resurrection with two eyes that see, two ears that hear, and a tongue that speaks, saying: ‘I have been entrusted with three things: with every stubborn tyrant, with everyone who invoked another god along with God, and with the image-makers.’” Abu ‘Eisa said: This is a strange, authentic, and harsh hadith. In Al-Bukhari and Muslim, “On the authority of ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘The people who will be most severely tormented on the Day of Resurrection will be the image-makers.’” This indicates the prohibition on making images of anything, wherever it may be. God, the Almighty, said: It is not for you to grow its trees (al-Naml 27:60), as explained above, so take note of that. Eighth: An exception to this is made for girls’ toys, as it was proven from Aisha may God be pleased with her that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) married her when she was seven years old, and she was brought to him when she was nine, and he played with her, and he died when she was eighteen. It was also narrated from her that she said: “I used to play with dolls in the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and I had female friends who played with me. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered, they would complain to him, so he would bring them to me so they could play with me.” Narrated by Muslim.
