The scholars said: This is due to necessity and the need of girls to be trained to raise their children. Moreover, this does not last, just as what is made from sweets or dough does not last, so it was permitted, and God knows best. God the Almighty said: {And basins like wells.} Ibn Arafa said: The well is the plural of the basin, which is a hole like a basin. He said: Like the watering places of camels. Ibn al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik: Like a hole in the ground, and the meaning is close. A thousand men would sit on one basin. An-Nahhas: And basins like the well, the first should be with the ya’, and whoever deleted the ya’ said that the alif and lam are used to enter on an indefinite noun, so it does not change its state. So when it was said jawab and the alif and lam entered, it remained as it was and the ya’ was deleted. The singular of jawabi is jabiyyah, which is the great pot, and the great, large basin in which something is collected, i.e., collected. From this comes the word jabbat al-kharaj and jabbat al-jarad, i.e., I made the cloak and gathered them in it. However, Layth narrated on the authority of Mujahid who said: The jawabi is the plural of jawbah, and the jawbah is the large hole in the mountain in which rainwater is found. Al-Kisa’i said: I collected the water in the basin and I collected it, meaning I gathered it, and the jabiyyah is the basin in which water is collected for the camels. He said: Go to the Al-Muhaq family, a plate of the Iraqi Sheikh’s money, and you will be surprised It is also narrated: Denying blame on the Al-Mahlaq family, a jug of water from the river. Copper mentioned. God the Almighty said: And fixed pots. Saad bin Jubair said: They are copper pots found in Persia. Al-Hudhahak said: They are pots made from mountains. Another said: They were carved from solid mountains by what the devils had made, their fire places are carved like this from the mountains. The meaning of fixed and stable, they cannot be carried or moved due to their size. Ibn Al-Arabi said: And this was the model of Abdullah bin Jud’an, he would climb to it in the pre-Islamic era with a ladder. Tarafa bin Al-Abd narrated from it, saying: Like the answer, you never cease to be full of hospitality or of the afflicted. Ibn al-Arabi said: I saw the Sufis in the ribat of Abu Saeed, who were valued in a similar way. They would cook together and eat together, without any of them monopolizing the others. God the Almighty says: “Work, O family of David, with gratitude. But few of My servants are grateful.” The meaning of gratitude has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah and elsewhere. “It has been narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ascended the pulpit and recited this verse, then said: ‘Three things, whoever has been given them has been given the same as what was given to the family of David.’ We said: ‘What are they?’ He said: ‘Justice in contentment and restraint; moderation in both poverty and wealth; and fear of God in secret and in public.’” Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Hakim Abu Abdullah, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. It has been narrated that David (peace be upon him) said: O Lord, how can I be able to thank You for Your blessings? My inspiration and my ability to do so are blessings from You. He said: O David, now You have made me known. This meaning has already been mentioned in Surat Ibrahim. Gratitude is the true acknowledgment of the spoils of the Benefactor and using them in obedience to Him, while ingratitude is using them in disobedience. It has been said that whoever does that, because good is less than evil, and obedience is less than disobedience, according to what was previously decreed. Mujahid said: When God the Almighty said: Work, O family of David, in gratitude, David said to Solomon: God the Almighty has mentioned gratitude, so suffice me with the daytime prayer and I will suffice you with the night prayer. David said: I am not able. He said: So suffice me.” Al-Faryabi said: I think he said until the noon prayer. He said: Yes, so suffice him. Al-Zuhri said: Work, O family of David, in gratitude, meaning say: Praise be to God. “Thank you” is in the accusative case as a direct object, meaning do an action that is gratitude. It is as if prayer, fasting, and all acts of worship are in themselves gratitude if they fill its place. This is made clear by God the Almighty’s saying: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, and few are they. (Surah Sad: 24), which is what is meant by His saying: And few of My servants are grateful. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said in his interpretation of God the Almighty’s saying: To be grateful to Me, that what is meant by gratitude is the five daily prayers. And in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to stand in prayer at night until his feet would swell. Aisha may God be pleased with her said to him: On her authority: Do you do this while God has forgiven you your past and future sins? He said: Should I not be a grateful servant? Narrated by Muslim alone. The apparent meaning of the Quran and Sunnah is that gratitude is an action of the body and is not limited to the actions of the tongue. So gratitude through actions is an action of the limbs, and grimacing through words is an action of the tongue. And God knows best. God's statement: And few of My servants are grateful. It may be that this is addressed to the family of David, or it may be that it is addressed to Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. Ibn Atiyyah said: In either case, it contains a warning and an incitement. Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him heard a man saying: O God, make me among the grateful. Umar said: What is this supplication? The man said: "Do you mean the statement of God: "And few of My servants are grateful?" Umar may God be pleased with him said: "All people are more knowledgeable than you, Umar!" It was narrated that Solomon (peace be upon him) used to mix barley, feed his family raw khichkar, and feed the poor dirhams. It was also said that he used to eat ashes and use them as pillows, but the first is more correct, since ashes are not a source of sustenance. It was narrated that he was never satisfied, so he was asked about that, and he said: "I fear that if I am satisfied, I will forget the hungry." This is from gratitude and from the little, so ponder it, and God knows best.
34:14: The Almighty said: So when We decreed death for him meaning when We decreed death for Salman until it became like a matter derived from it and death befell him nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff and that is because he was leaning on the staff (which is a stick in the Ethiopian dialect, according to al-Suddi. It was said: it is the language of the oath, mentioned by al-Qushayri) and he died like that and his condition remained hidden until he fell down dead because the staff broke due to the termite eating it, so his death was known from that, so the termite was an indicator of his death, meaning a reason for his death to appear, and he had asked God Almighty that they not know of his death until a year had passed. They differed about the reason for his asking that, with two opinions: One of them is what Qatada and others said, he said: The jinn claimed to know the unseen, so when Solomon, peace be upon him, died and his death was hidden from them, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment. Ibn Masoud said: He stayed for a year and the jinn were working in front of him until the termites ate his staff and he fell. It is narrated that when it fell, it was not known when he had died, so the termites were placed on the staff and ate from it for a day and a night, then they calculated based on that and found that he had died a year ago. It was said: The chiefs of the jinn were seven, and they were obedient to Solomon, peace be upon him. David, peace be upon him, had founded the Holy House, and when he died, he recommended to Solomon to complete the mosque of the Holy House, so Solomon ordered the jinn to do it. When his death drew near, he said to his family: Do not tell them of my death until they have completed the construction of the mosque, and there was one year left to complete it. In the story, it is said that the Angel of Death was his friend, so he asked him about the sign of his death, and he said: That a tree called the carob tree will grow from the place of your prostration. Every day, a tree would grow in the Holy House, and he would ask it: What is your name? The tree would say: My name is such and such. He would say: And for what are you? It would say: For such and such. He would order it to be cut down and planted in his garden, and he would order that its benefits and harms, its name, and what it is good for in medicine be written down. While he was praying one day, he saw a tree growing in front of him, so he said to it: What is your name? It said: The carob tree. He said: And for what are you? She said: For the destruction of this mosque. Solomon said: God would not destroy it while I am alive. You are the one on whose face is my destruction and the destruction of the Holy House! So he took it out and stuck it in his wall and then said: O God, conceal my death from the jinn so that you may know that the jinn do not know the unseen. The jinn used to tell the people that they knew things of the unseen and that they knew what would happen tomorrow. Then he put on his shroud, embalmed himself, entered the prayer niche, stood up to pray and leaned on his cane on his chair. He died and the jinn did not know until a year had passed and the mosque was completed. Abu Ja`far al-Nahhas said: This is the best thing that has been said about the verse, and its authenticity is indicated by the hadith that was narrated by the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), “Ibraaheem ibn Tahman narrated on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib on the authority of Sa’eed ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: Whenever the Prophet of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him, Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them both, prayed, he would see a tree growing between his hands and ask it, ‘What is your name?’ If it was for planting, it would be planted, and if it was for medicine, it would be written down. While he was praying one day, a tree grew between his hands and he asked, ‘What is your name?’ It said, ‘The carob tree.’ He said, ‘For what are you?’ It said, ‘To destroy this house.’ He said, ‘O God, prevent the jinn from dying so that you may know that the jinn do not know the unseen.’ So he carved a stick for it and leaned on it for a year without knowing, and it fell. So the people knew that the jinn do not know the unseen. They looked at the amount of that and found it to be a year.” In the reading of Ibn Mas’ud and Ibn Abbas: It became clear to people that if the jinn knew the unseen. And Yaqub read in the narration of Ruways, Tabayyanat al-Jinn Ghunr as the name of the agent. Nafi’ and Abu Amr, Takkal Mansatahu with an alif between the seen and the ta’ without a hamza. The rest with an open hamza in place of the alif, two dialects, except that Ibn Dakwan made the hamza quiescent for ease. The poet said about leaving out the hamza: If you crawl on the fork out of old age, then fun and flirting will be far from you Another said, with a hamza and a fatha: We have made his face humiliated and degraded. Another said: For the sake of a rope that is not your father, you tied it with a spanner, and your rope has been pulled by ropes. Another said: He pronounced the hamza on it: And the one standing has risen from his support like the old man who has risen to his support Their origin is from: Nasa’at al-Ghanam which means to drive the sheep and water them. The stick was named thus because something is driven and driven with it. Tarafa said: Amon is like the tablets of Iran, I forgot them on the ground, as if he appeared on a tower An-Nahhas said: Its derivation indicates that it has a hamza, because it is derived from nas’atuhu, meaning to delay or push it back. It was called mansa’ah because something is pushed back or delayed by it. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: It is the stick. Then he recited mansa’atu, replacing the hamza with an alif. If it is said that replacing a hamza is very ugly and is only permissible in poetry if it is far-fetched and unusual, and something like this is not absent from Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’, especially since the people of Madinah follow this reading. The answer to this is that the Arabs used the badal in this word and pronounced it like this, just as the badal occurs in other words and is not analogous to it. Abu Amr even said: I do not know who it is from, except that it is not hamza, because the hamza of what has a hamza may be omitted, and the hamza of what does not have a hamza is not permissible at all. Al-Mahdawi: And whoever reads with a silent hamza, then this is an anomaly and far-fetched, because the feminine ha’ is not preceded by anything but a vowel or an alif, but it is permissible for what is silent to be from the open letter as a sign of lightness, and it is permissible for what the hamza indicates to be an alif, not according to the rule of changing the alif to a hamza, as they changed it in their saying al-`alam and al-khalam, and it was narrated from Sa`id ibn Jubayr from a separated sa`tah with a hamza and a broken ta’, so it was said: It is from the side of the bow in the language of those who hamzated it, and the hamzah of the side of the bow was narrated from Ru`bah. Al-Jawhari said: The side of the bow is what is joined from its two ends, and the plural is siyat, and the ha’ is a replacement for the waw, and the nisba to it is siwi. Abu Ubaidah said: Ru`bah used to hamzate the side of the bow, but the rest of the Arabs did not hamzate it. And regarding the beast of the earth, there are two opinions: One of them is that it is the termite, as Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said. And others. The word dabbat al-ardh has been read with a fat-ha on the ra, and it is the singular form of ardah, as mentioned by al-Mawardi. The second: Anhababah that eats sticks. Al-Jawhari said: Al-ardah with a fat-ha: a small animal that eats wood. It is said: ardha ya’rudhan with a sukoon, so it is marudah if it ate it. God the Almighty said: Then when he fell down meaning, the jinn became aware of his death. Al-Zajjaj said: The jinn became aware of his death. Another said: The meaning is that the matter of the jinn became apparent, like in the verse: And ask the town. In the interpretation with authentic chains of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Solomon, son of David, peace be upon them both, remained for a year without knowing of his death while he was leaning on his staff, and the jinn were distracted as they were concerned with it. Then he fell down after a year. Then when he fell down, mankind became aware that if the jinn had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment. This reading is from Ibn Abbas as an interpretation. In al-Naba 78:That the jinn thanked the term for that, so wherever it was, they would bring it water. Al-Suddi said: And the clay. Have you not seen the clay that is inside wood? It is something that the devils fear in gratitude. They said: If you were to eat food and drink, we would have brought them to you. And that is in the nominative case as a substitute for the jinn. The meaning is: The matter of the jinn became apparent, so the complement was deleted, meaning it became apparent and became clear to mankind and the matter of the jinn was revealed to them that they do not know the unseen. This is a substitute for inclusion. It is permissible for it to be in the accusative case, assuming the lam is deleted. And they stayed and stayed. And the humiliating punishment is forced labor, carrying, and eating, and other than that. Solomon lived fifty-three years, and his reign lasted for forty years. He became king when he was thirteen years old, and he began building the Temple of Jerusalem when he was seventeen years old. Al-Suddi and others said: Solomon lived sixty-seven years, and his reign began when he was seventeen years old. He began building the Temple of Jerusalem when he was twenty years old, and his reign lasted fifty years. It is narrated that Solomon, peace be upon him, began the construction of the Temple of Jerusalem in the fourth year of his reign. After he finished it, he sacrificed twelve thousand bulls and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. He celebrated the day he finished building it. He stood on the rock, raised his hands to God Almighty, and said: “O God, You have given me this throne and strengthened me to build this mosque. O God, enable me to thank You for what You have bestowed upon me, and let me die following Your religion. Do not deviate my heart after You have guided me. O God, I ask You for five things for whoever enters this mosque: No sinner who enters in repentance enters it except that You forgive him and accept his repentance. No fearful person enters it except that You grant him safety. No sick person enters it except that You heal him. No one who is slandered except that You enrich him. The fifth: Do not turn Your gaze away from whoever enters it until he leaves it, except for someone who intends to commit heresy or injustice, O Lord of the worlds.” Al-Mawardi mentioned this. I said: This is more correct than what was mentioned above, that he did not complete its construction until a year after his death. The evidence for the correctness of this is what was reported by Al-Nasa’i and others with a sound chain of transmission from the hadith of Abdullah bin Amr from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: “When Salmaan bin Dawud built the Holy House, he asked God Almighty for three things: a rule that would be in accordance with his rule, and he was given it. He asked God Almighty for a kingdom that no one after him would have, and he was given it. And when he finished building the mosque, he asked God Almighty that no one would come to it with no motive other than to pray in it, and that he would emerge from his sin as on the day his mother bore him.” We mentioned this hadith in Al Imran and we mentioned its construction in Subhan.
34:15: The Almighty said: There was for Sheba in their dwelling place a sign. Nafi’ and others read it with the declension and tanween, as if it were the name of a tribe, and it was originally the name of a man. This was transmitted by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Tirmidhi narrated: Abu Kurayb and Abd ibn Hamid told us, they said: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan ibn Al-Hakam Al-Nakha’i, he said: Subrah Al-Nakha’i told us, on the authority of Furwah ibn Masik Al-Muradi, he said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, shall I not fight those of my people who have turned back with those of them who have returned? So he gave me permission to fight them and commanded me. When I left him, he asked about me: What has happened to Al-Ghatifi? He was informed that I had set out. He said: So he sent after me and brought me back. So I came to him while he was with a group of his companions, and he said: Call the people, and whoever among them has accepted Islam, and whoever has not accepted Islam accepts from him, so do not hasten until I tell you. He said: And what was revealed about Sheba was revealed. So a man said: O Messenger of God, and what is Sheba? It is a land Or a woman? He said: It is neither a land nor a woman, but a man of ten from the Arabs, six of them took the right and four took the wrong. As for those who took the wrong, they were Lahm, Judham, Ghassan, and Amala. As for those who took the right, they were Azd, Ash’ariyyun, Himyar, Kinda, Madhhij, and Anmar. A man said: O Messenger of God, who are Anmar? He said: Those from whom are Khatham and Bajila. This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu ‘Eesa said: This is a good and strange hadith. Ibn Kathir and Abu ‘Umar read li-Saba’ without a sukoon, making it the name of the tribe, and this is the choice of Abu ‘Ubaid. He proved that it is the name of a tribe because after it is fi masakinhim. An-Nahhas said: If it were as he said, it would have been in their dwellings. An additional explanation of this meaning has already been mentioned in An-Naml. The poet said in sukoon: The visitors and Taym in the heights of Saba, their necks were bitten by buffalo hides. Another said in non-morphology: From Saba', the people of Ma'rib were building without its flood. Qanbal, Abu Haywah, and Al-Jahdary read for Saba’ with a sukoon on the hamza, in their dwellings as the general reading in the plural, and it is the choice of Abu Ubaid and Abu Hatim, because they had many dwellings and not just one dwelling. Ibrahim, Hamzah, and Hafs read their dwelling in a singular form, except that they opened the kaf. Yahya, Al-A’mash, and Al-Kisa’i read it in a singular form as well, except that they broke the kaf. An-Nahhas said: The sukoon in this is clearer, because it combines the word and the meaning. So if you say their dwelling there are two possibilities: One of them is that it is singular and replaces the plural, and the other is that it is a verbal noun that is neither dual nor plural, as God Almighty said: God has set a seal upon their hearts and upon their hearing and upon their sight (Al-Baqarah 2:7), so He came with the hearing in a singular form, and likewise a seat of truth [Al-Qamar 55]. And the dwelling is like a mosque, outside of analogy, and there is nothing like it except by hearing. Ayah is the name of kan, meaning a sign indicating The ability of God Almighty is that they have a Creator who created them, and that if all creatures gathered together to produce fruit from wood, they would not be able to do so, and they would not be guided to the different types of fruits, their colors, tastes, smells, and flowers. This indicates that they only come from a knowledgeable and capable person. Two gardens may be a substitute for a sign, and it may be the predicate of a deleted subject, so it is stopped on this face at a sign, but it is not complete. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, the sign is two gardens. Two gardens is in the nominative case because it is the predicate of a deleted subject. Al-Farra’ said: It is in the nominative case as an explanation of the sign. It is permissible for a sign to be in the accusative case as the predicate of was, and it is permissible for the two gardens to be in the accusative case as a predicate also in places other than the Qur’an. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: The sign that the people of Sheba had in their dwellings was that they never saw in them a single mosquito, fly, flea, louse, scorpion, snake, or other vermin. When a caravan came to them, lice and animals were in their clothes, and when they looked at their homes, the animals died. It was said: The verse refers to the two gardens. The woman would walk in them with a basket on her head, and she would fill it with various types of fruits without touching them with her hand. Qatada said this. It was narrated that the two gardens were between two mountains on the right. Sufyan said: Two palaces were found in them, and written on one of them was: We built Silhain in seventy continuous autumns. On the other was written: We built Sarwah, a resting place and a place of rest. One of the two gardens was to the right of the valley and the other to its left. Al-Qushayri said: He did not mean two gardens, but rather he meant the right and left of the two gardens, meaning their land had orchards, trees, and fruits, and people were sheltered by their shade. Eat from the provision of your Lord, meaning they were told to eat, and there was no command, but they were able to enjoy those blessings. It was said: meaning the messengers said to them, God Almighty has permitted you to do that, meaning He has permitted you these blessings, so thank Him through obedience. From the provision of your Lord, meaning from the fruits of the two gardens. And thank Him, meaning for what He has provided you. A good land. "This is a new statement, meaning this is a good town, meaning it has many fruits. It was also said: not salt marsh. It was also said: good, there are no vermin in it because of the goodness of its air. Mujahid said: it is Sana'a. "And a Forgiving Lord" meaning the One who bestowed it upon you is a Forgiving Lord who conceals your sins. So He combined for them the forgiveness of their sins and the goodness of their land, and He did not combine that for all of His creation. It was also said: He only mentioned forgiveness to indicate that provision may contain something forbidden. This was discussed at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. It was also said: He only bestowed His favor upon them by pardoning them from the punishment of extermination by denying those who denied Him from among the previous prophets until they persisted in their insistence and were exterminated.
34:16: The Almighty says: But they turned away meaning from His command and following His messengers after they had been Muslims. Al-Suddi and Wahb said: Thirteen prophets were sent to the people of Saba' but they denied them. Al-Qushayri said: They had a leader nicknamed Al-Himar, and they lived during the period between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them. It was also said that he had a son who died, so he raised his head to the sky and spat and disbelieved. That is why it is said: More disbelieving than a donkey. Al-Jawhari said: Their saying more disbelieving than a donkey refers to a man from Aad who had lost his children and committed great disbelief. No one would pass by his land without him calling him to disbelief. If he responded, he would be killed. Then, when the flood flowed through their gardens, they dispersed throughout the country, as will be explained. That is why it is said in the proverb: They dispersed like the hands of Saba'. It was also said that the Aws and Khazraj were among them. So We sent upon them the flood of Al-'Iram. Al-'Iram, according to what was narrated from Ibn Abbas, means the dam, so the meaning is: the flood of the dam. Ata' said: Al-Aram is the name of a valley. Qatada said: Al-Aram is the valley of Saba', to which the watercourses of the valleys gathered, it was said from the sea and the valleys of Yemen. So they built a barrier between two mountains and made three gates in that barrier, one above the other. They would water from the upper one, then from the second, then from the third, according to their needs, so they became fertile and their wealth increased. But when they denied the messengers, God sent a mouse against them, which burrowed into the barrier. Wahb said: They claimed that they found in their knowledge and divination that a mouse would destroy their dam, so they did not leave a gap between two rocks without tying a cat to its side. When God's will came to pass, a red mouse approached one of those cats and chased it until it was behind the rock. Then it jumped and entered the gap that it was near and burrowed into the rope until it weakened it for the flood, while they were unaware. When the flood came, it entered that gap until it reached the dam, and the water flooded over their wealth, drowning it and burying their homes. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Aram is the name of the rat that burrowed into the dam, which is called the mole. Qatada also said it, so the flood was attributed to it because it is caused by it. Ibn Al-A’rabi also said: Al-Aram is one of the names of the mouse. Mujahid and Ibn Abi Nujayh said: Al-Aram is red water that God sent into the dam, so it split and demolished it. Ibn Abbas also said that Al-Aram is heavy rain. It was also said that Al-Aram is with a silent Ra. Ad-Dahhak said that they were in the period between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them. Amr bin Shurahbil said: Al-Aram is the mesnat and Al-Jawhari said that he said that it has no singular form from its word, and it is said that its singular is Arma. Muhammad bin Yazid said: Al-Aram is everything that is a barrier between two things, and it is what is called Al-Shukr, and it is the gathering of Arima. An-Nahhas said: What collects of rain between two mountains with a mesnat in front of it is Al-Aram, and the mesnat is what the people of Egypt call the bridge, so they would open it whenever they wanted, and when their gardens were watered, they would close it. Al-Harawi said: Al-Masnat is a braided dam built to stop a torrent. It is called Masnat because it contains the water keys. It was narrated that Al-Aram was the dam of his daughter Bilqis, the companion of Solomon, peace be upon him. It is called Al-Masnat in the Himyarite language. She built it with rock and tar, and made three gates for it, one above the other. It is derived from Al-Arama, which means severity, and from it: a strong man, meaning severe. And to conquer the bone, he a’ramuh and a’ramhu a’ram if you made it sweat, and likewise, camels a’ramt the tree, meaning they got from it. Al-Gharam with the dammah is the Iraq of bone and tree. And the bone is a’ramt, meaning it is sweaty. A boy, Arim, is a boy, Al-Gharam with the dammah, meaning fierce. And he has a’ram, ya’ram, and a’ramah with the fathah. Al-Aram. God the Almighty said: And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens of bitter food. Abu Amr read akal khamat without the tanween, as an addition. The commentators and Al-Khalil said: Khamat is the arak tree. Al-Jawhari said: Khamat is a type of arak tree that has edible fruit. Abu Ubaidah said: It is every thorny tree that has bitterness. Al-Zajjaj said: Every plant that has bitterness that cannot be eaten. Al-Mubarrad said: Khamat is everything that has changed into something undesirable. Milk is Khamat if it is lowered. The best reading according to him is dhati akal khamat with the tanween, as it is an adjective for akal or a substitute for it, because according to him, eating is the khamat. As for the addition, its permissibility can be estimated as kamal sour food or kamal bitter food. Al-Akhfash said: And the addition is better in the speech of the Arabs? Like their saying: a silk garment. And Khamat means sour milk. Abu Ubaid said that if the sweetness of milking disappears from milk without changing its taste, then it is samit. If it takes on some of the odor, then it is khamit and khamit. If it takes on some of the taste, then it is muhmal. If it still has a taste of sweetness, then it is futu. The stallion growls and roars. Someone becomes angry and arrogant. The sea becomes turbulent. The sheep is khamtatuhu khamatan: if you remove its skin and roast it, then it is khamit. If you remove its hair and roast it, then it is simit. Khamtah is the wine that has taken on the smell of ripening like the smell of apples but has not ripened yet. It is said that it is sour, as al-Jawhari said. Al-Qutbi said in Adab al-Katib: the sour is called khamtah and it is said that the khamtah is the one that has taken on some of the smell. And he recited: Raw water is neither a drug nor a remedy. The drinker burns with its meteor. And tamarisk Al-Farra' said: It is similar to the tamarisk, except that it is taller. The pulpit of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was made from it. The tamarisk has thick roots from which doors are made, and its leaves are like the leaves of the tamarisk. The singular is athalah, and the plural is athlāt. Al-Hasan said: Athal is wood. Qatadah said: It is a kind of wood similar to the tamarisk. I saw it with a chain. It was also said that it is the samr. Abu Ubaidah said: It is the tree of al-Nadhar. Al-Nadhar means gold. Al-Nadhar is wood from which bowls are made, and from it: a nādhar cup. And some little sidr Al-Farra' said: It is the samr, mentioned by al-Nahhas. Al-Azhari said: The sidr tree is sidrān: wild, not beneficial, and its leaves are not suitable for washing. It has a tannic fruit that is not eaten, and it is called the dhal. The second: A sidr that grows on water, its fruit is nabq, and its leaves are a washing plant similar to the jujube tree. Qatada said: While the trees of the people were among the best trees, God the Almighty made them among the worst trees because of their deeds, so He destroyed their fruitful trees and instead grew the arak, tamarisk, and lote-trees. Al-Qushayri said: The trees of the desert are not called paradise or orchard, but since the second occurs in opposition to the first, the term paradise was used, and it is like His Almighty’s saying: And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it (al-Shura 42:40). It is possible that his saying few refers to the whole of what was mentioned about the hafz, tamarisk, and lote-trees.
34:17: God the Almighty said: That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief. Meaning, this change is the recompense for their disbelief. The position of that is in the accusative case, meaning, We recompensed them for their disbelief. Is anyone recompensed except the ungrateful? The general reading is yajāzā with a ḍammah ya’ and a fathah zay, al-kafūr in the nominative case, as for what has no named agent. Ya’qub, Hafs, Hamzah, and al-Kisa’i read Najāzī with a noon and a kasrah zay, al-kafūr in the accusative case. Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose this, and they said: Because before it is jazīnahum We recompensed them and He did not say ‘they recompensed’. An-Nahhas: The matter is broad and the meaning is clear. If someone were to say: God created Adam (peace be upon him) from clay, and another were to say: He created Adam from clay, the meaning would be the same. Question: In this verse there is a question that is not more difficult in this Surah, which is: Why did God specify the punishment for the disbelievers and did not mention the people of sins? Scholars discussed this. Some said: This punishment, which is crushing and destruction, is not given to anyone except the one who disbelieved. Mujahid said: He punishes means he punishes, because God forgives the sins of the believer, while the disbeliever is punished for all his bad deeds. So the believer is punished but not punished because he is rewarded. Tawus said: It is the discussion in the accounting, but the believer will not be questioned in the accounting. Qatrib said the opposite of this, so he made it apply to the people of sins other than the disbelievers, and he said: The meaning is for the one who is ungrateful for blessings and commits major sins. An-Nahhas: The most appropriate thing to say about this verse and the most important thing narrated about it is that Al-Hasan said, An example for an example. On the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, she said: I heard the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) say: Whoever is brought to account will perish. I said: O Prophet of God, where is the saying of God, the Exalted and Majestic: Then he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning (al-Inshiqaq 84:8)? He said: That is only the presentation, and whoever is called to account will perish. This is a sound chain of transmission, and its explanation is: The disbeliever will be rewarded for his deeds and will be held accountable for them, and whatever good he did will be nullified. This is made clear by God’s statement in the first verse: That is how We recompensed them for their disbelief and in the second verse: And is anyone rewarded except the disbeliever? The meaning of recompensated is: he will be rewarded for every deed he did, and the meaning of We recompensed them is and in their place. This is the literal meaning of the language, even though recompensated can be used metaphorically to mean recompensated.
34:18: The Almighty says: And We placed between them and the towns which We have blessed, towns which are visible. Al-Hasan said: It means between Yemen and Syria. The towns which were blessed are: Syria, Jordan, and Palestine. It was said that there were four thousand seven hundred towns in which trees, fruits, and water were blessed. It is possible that We blessed them due to their large number. Towns which are visible. Ibn Abbas said: He means between Madinah and Syria. Qatada said: The meaning of visible is: connected on a road, they would go a mile in a town and come back and spend the night in a town. It was also said: There was a town with a market every mile, and this was the reason for the safety of the road. Al-Hasan said: A woman would go out with her spindle and carry her bag on her head, then she would be busy with her spindle and not return home until her bag was full of all the fruits, so the area between Syria and Yemen was like that. It was also said that visible means elevated, as Al-Mubarrad said. It was said: It was called apparent because of its appearance, meaning if you go beyond this one, the other will appear to you, so the villages were apparent, meaning well-known. It is said: This is an apparent matter, meaning well-known. And We ordained therein the journey meaning We made the journey between their villages and the villages that We had blessed a measured journey from house to house, and from village to village. That is, We made between every two villages half a day so that the afternoon nap would be in one village and the night would be in another. A person only travels excessively due to the lack of provisions and water and the fear of the road. If he finds provisions and is safe, he does not burden himself with hardship and stops wherever he wants. Travel therein meaning, and We said to them, travel therein, meaning this distance, so it is an order of enabling, meaning they would travel therein to their destinations if they wanted to in safety, so it is an order with the meaning of report, and it contains an implied statement. Nights and days are two adverbials, safe is an accusative of state. He said: Nights and days in the indefinite form to indicate the shortness of their journeys, meaning they did not need a long journey because they had what they needed. Qatada said: They were walking without fear, hunger, or thirst. They would walk for four months in safety, not moving one another. Even if a man encountered his father’s killer, he would not move him.
34:19: God the Almighty says: "And they said, 'Our Lord, lengthen our journeys.'" When they became arrogant and transgressed, and grew tired of comfort and could not endure ease, they wished for long journeys and toil in their livelihood, just as the Children of Israel said: "So call upon your Lord to bring forth for us from the earth its green plants." (al-Baqarah 2:61) And like Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith when he said: "O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky." (al-Anfal 8:32) So God the Blessed and Exalted answered him, and he was killed by the sword on the day of Badr, just as these people were scattered in the world and torn apart, and between them and Ash-Sham were deserts and wildernesses where they could ride their mounts and provision themselves. The common people read "Our Lord" in the accusative case as a vocative with an added meaning, and it is in the accusative case because it is a direct object, because its meaning is: I called and I prayed. They asked for lengthening their journeys. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Muhaisin and Hisham from Ibn Amir read: Our Lord, thus as a supplication after distancing. An-Nahhas: And distancing after is one in meaning, as you say: made close and made near. Abu Saleh, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah, Abu al-Aliyah, Nasr ibn Asim and Ya’qub read it. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas: Our Lord in the nominative case, distanced with a fat-ha on the ‘ayn and the dal as a predicate, meaning: Our Lord has distanced our journeys, as if God the Almighty is saying: We brought their journeys near for them, but they said, out of arrogance and pride: Our journeys have been distanced for us. Abu Hatim preferred this reading. He said: Because they did not ask for distancing, rather they asked for something closer than that nearness out of arrogance and conceit, despite their disbelief. The reading of Yahya ibn Ya’mar and Isa ibn Umar, and it is narrated from Ibn Abbas, is: Our Lord, distanced between our journeys with a stressed ‘ayn without an alif. Ibn Abbas explained it by saying: They doubted that their Lord had distanced their journeys. The reading of Sa’id ibn Abi al-Hasan, the brother of al-Hasan al-Basri, is: Our Lord, distanced between our journeys. Our Lord is a complementary call, then they informed after that and said: after our journeys, and raising between with the verb, meaning after what is connected to our journeys. Al-Farra and Abu Ishaq narrated a sixth reading like the one before it with the damma of the ‘ayn except that you put the between in the accusative case as an adverb, and its meaning in Arabic is: after our journey between our journeys. An-Nahhas: If these readings differ in meaning, it is not permissible to say one of them is better than the other, just as that is not said in individual narrations if their meanings differ, but it is a report about them that they called upon their Lord to distance between their journeys out of arrogance and evil, and it is a report about them that when He did that to them, they reported it and doubted, as Ibn Abbas said. And they wronged themselves meaning by their disbelief. So We made them stories meaning their stories are talked about, and its meaning in Arabic is: people of stories. And We tore them apart completely meaning when what happened to them happened, they dispersed and were torn apart. Al-Sha'bi said: "The Ansar went to Yathrib, Ghassan to Ash-Sham, Asad to Oman, and Khuza'ah to Tihamah. The Arabs used to make an example of them, saying: They dispersed like the hands of Saba and the hands of Saba', meaning the ways and paths of Saba. Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful person. The patient person is the one who is patient about sins, and it is a multiplication of the patient person who is praised by this name. If you mean that he is patient about sinning, then nothing is used to describe him except patient about such and such. "Grateful" for His blessings, and this meaning has already been mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah.
34:20: The Almighty’s saying: And Iblis proved true to them his assumption has four readings: Abu Ja`far, Shaibah, Nafi`, Abu `Amr, Ibn Kathir, and Ibn `Amir read it. It is narrated from Mujahid, and it is said: And Iblis proved true to them with the light vowel, Iblis thought it with the nominative, and his thought with the accusative, meaning in his assumption. Al-Zajjaj said: It is on the source, meaning he proved true to them his assumption, since he believed in his assumption, so it was accusative as a source or as an adverbial. Abu `Ali said: His thought is not accusative because it is a direct object, meaning he proved true the assumption he thought when he said: I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path (Al-A`raf: 16) and he said: I will surely mislead them all (Sad: 82) and (al-Hijr 15:39). It is permissible to transit truth to the direct object, and it is said: He believed the hadith, meaning in the hadith. Ibn Abbas, Yahya ibn Waththab, Al-A'mash, Asim, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa'i read: Sadaq with a shaddah, Zannahu in the accusative case, because the verb Sadaq occurred upon him. Mujahid said: He thought a thought, and it was as he thought, so his thought came true. Ja'far ibn Muhammad and Abu Al-Juhajah read Sadaqah alahum with a light vowel, Iblis in the accusative case, Zannahu in the nominative case. Abu Hatim said: I see no basis for this reading, and God knows best. Al-Farra' permitted this reading, and Al-Zajjaj mentioned it, and he made Zanna the subject of Sadaqah Iblis and the object. The meaning is: Iblis made him think something of them, so his thought came true. It is as if he said: And indeed, Iblis' thought came true upon them. "Upon is connected to Sadaq", just as you say: "I believed you in what I thought of you. It is not connected to Zanna" because it is impossible for any of the relative clause to precede the relative pronoun. The fourth reading is: "And indeed, Iblis believed his thought upon them with the nominative case, Iblis and Zanna, with a light vowel in Sadaq, so that Zannahu is a substitute for Iblis", which is a bad example of inclusion. Then it was said: This was about the people of Sheba, meaning they disbelieved, changed and altered after they had been Muslims except for a group of them who believed in their messengers. It was also said: This is general, meaning Iblis confirmed his assumption about all people except those who obeyed God the Almighty. Mujahid said this. Al-Hasan said: When Adam, peace be upon him, was sent down from Paradise with Eve and Iblis came down, Iblis said: Since you have received from your parents what you received, the offspring are weaker and weaker. This was an assumption from Iblis, so God the Almighty revealed: {And indeed, Iblis proved true about them his assumption.} Ibn Abbas said: Iblis said: I was created from fire and Adam was created from clay, and fire burns everything. I will surely consume his offspring, except for a few Al-Isra’ 17:62, so his assumption about them was confirmed. Zayd ibn Aslam said: Iblis said: O Lord, have you seen those whom You have honored, respected and favored over me? You do not find most of them grateful. This was an assumption from him, so Iblis confirmed his assumption about them. Al-Kalbi said: He thought that if he led them astray, they would answer him, and if he led them astray, they would obey him, so his thought was proven true. So they followed him. Al-Hasan said: He did not strike them with a whip or a stick, but rather he thought a thought, and it happened as he thought, due to his whispering. Except a party of the believers is in the accusative case as an exception, and there are two opinions on this: One of them is that it refers to some of the believers, because many of the believers sin and follow Satan in some of the transgressions. That is, no group of the believers were spared except for a group, and this is what is meant by the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, My servants - over them you have no authority Al-Isra’ 17:42. As for Ibn Abbas, it was narrated that he said: They are all the believers. Those in this is for clarification, not for discrimination. If it is said: How did Satan know that his thought was true when he does not know the unseen? It is said to him: When what he did to Adam was implemented, he was overcome by the belief that the same would be implemented to his offspring, and what he thought came true. Another answer is what was given from the words of God Almighty: And incite whomever you can among them with your voice and assault them with your cavalry and infantry (al-Isra’ 17:64). So he was given strength and ability, so he thought that he would rule over them all with that. Then when he saw that he accepted Adam’s repentance and that he would have offspring who would follow him to Paradise and said: Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them except those who follow you of the deviators (al-Hijr 15:42), he knew that he had followers and Adam had followers, so he thought that his followers were more than Adam’s followers, because of the authority of desires that was placed in his hands, and desires were placed in the bodies of humans. So he came out as he thought, as he blew into them and made those desires appear beautiful in their eyes, and extended them to them with hopes and deceptions, so the thought that he thought came true about them, and God knows best.
34:21: God the Almighty says: And he had no authority over them meaning, Iblis did not force them to disbelieve, but rather he used to supplicate and adorn. Authority means power. It was also said that it means an argument, meaning, he had no argument to follow them, but they followed him out of lust, imitation, and personal desires, not based on an argument or proof. Except that We may know who believes in the Hereafter means the knowledge of testimony by which reward and punishment occur. As for the unseen, God the Almighty knows it. The view of Al-Fazza is that the meaning is: Except that We may know that from you, just as He said: Where are My partners? (al-Nahl 16:27) according to what you say and with you. His statement: Except that We may know is not an answer to And he had no authority over them in its apparent meaning, but it is carried on the meaning, meaning, We did not give him authority except to know. So the exception is disjunctive, meaning, he had no authority over them, but We tested them with his whisperings so that We may know. So except means but. It was said that it is connected, meaning he had no authority over them, except that We gave him authority over them so that the test would be complete. It was said that it was redundant, meaning he had no authority over them, like His statement: You were the best nation (Al Imran 3:110), meaning you are the best nation. It was said that when one part of it was connected to the story of Sheba, He said: And Iblis had no authority over those disbelievers. It was said that he had no authority over them in Our previous judgment. It was said that it was only so that we may know, except to reveal. It is like you say: Fire burns wood, and another says: No, rather wood burns fire, and the first says: Come, so that we may test fire and wood, to know which of them burns the other, meaning to reveal that, even though that was known to them. It was said that it was only so that you may know. It was said that it is so that Our allies and the angels may know, like His statement: The only reward of those who wage war against God and His Messenger (Al Ma’idah: 133), meaning they wage war against the allies of God and His Messenger. It was said: That is, to distinguish, as in His statement: That God may distinguish the evil from the good (al-Anfal 8:37). This meaning has already been mentioned in Al-Baqarah and other verses. Al-Zuhri read: Except that He may know of that which He did not name. “And your Lord is Guardian over all things,” meaning that He knows everything. It was also said: He preserves everything for the servant until He rewards him for it.
34:22: God the Almighty says: Say, 'Call upon those you claim besides God.' That is, what has been mentioned previously about the matter of David and Solomon and the story of Sheba are signs of My power. So say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: Do your partners have the power to do any of that? This is a rebuke, and it implies: Call upon those you claim are gods besides God, so that they may benefit you or repel from you what God the Blessed and Exalted has decreed against you, for they do not possess that power. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and they have no partner in either of them, nor is there for Him from among them any supporter. That is, none of these people can help God create anything. Rather, God is the One Who alone can create, and He is the One Who is to be worshipped, and worshipping anyone other than Him is impossible.
34:23: God the Almighty says: And no intercession will avail meaning the intercession of the angels and others. With Him meaning with God. Except for him whom He permits The general reading is adhan with a fat-ha over the hamza because God the Almighty is mentioned first. Abu Amr, Hamza, and Al-Kisa'i read adhan with a damma over the hamza when the agent is not named. The one who permits is God the Almighty. It is permissible for it to refer to the intercessors, or it is permissible for it to refer to those for whom intercession is made. Until fear is removed from their hearts Ibn Abbas said: Fear is removed from their hearts. Qutrab said: He removes whatever fear is in them. Mujahid said: The veil will be removed from their hearts on the Day of Resurrection, meaning that intercession will not come from any of those worshipped besides God, from the angels, prophets, and idols, except that God the Almighty permits the prophets and angels to intercede while they are in extreme fear of God, as He says: And they, out of fear of Him, are fearful (al-Anbiya 21:28). Meaning: If they are given permission to intercede and the Word of God comes to them, they will be terrified because of the terrible matter that accompanies that state and the fear that they may fall short in carrying out what they have been given permission to do. Then, when it is released from their fear, they will say to the angels above them, who are the ones who bring them the revelation of permission: What did your Lord say? That is, what did God command? They will say: They said the truth, which is that He has given you permission to intercede for the believers. And He is the Most High, the Grand. So, He has the right to rule regarding His servants as He wishes. It is possible that this is permission for them in this world to intercede for other people, or it may be in the Hereafter. The statement implies that intercession will not benefit anyone except those to whom He has given permission. So, they will be terrified because of the permission that came to them out of awe of the Word of God, until, when the fear has left their hearts, they will respond with submission. It has been said that this fear is for the angels today in every matter that the Lord commands, that is, intercession will not benefit anyone except the angels who are terrified today, obedient to God, excluding inanimate objects and devils. In Sahih al-Tirmidhi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: When God decrees a matter in heaven, the angels beat their wings in submission to His word. As if it were a chain on a smooth rock. Then, when fear is removed from their hearts, they say, What did your Lord say? They say, The Truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand. He said, And the devils are one above another. He said, A good and authentic hadith. Al-Nawwas ibn Sam’an said, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘When God wants to reveal something, He speaks the revelation, and the heavens are seized by a violent trembling or shaking out of fear of God. When the people of the heavens hear that, they swoon and fall down in prostration to God, the Most High. The first to raise his head is Gabriel, and God, the Most High, speaks to him and tells him of His revelation what He wants. Then Gabriel passes by the angels, and whenever he passes by a heaven, its angels ask him, ‘What did our Lord say, O Gabriel?’ Gabriel says, ‘He said, ‘The Truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.’ He said, ‘And they all say as Gabriel said.’ Then Gabriel ends with the revelation where God, the Most High, commanded him.” Al-Bayhaqi reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse, until, when fear is removed from their hearts, that he said, “Each tribe of the jinn had a seat in the heaven from which they would listen to the revelation. Whenever the revelation came down, a sound like the passing of a chain over a smooth rock was heard. It would not descend upon the people of a heaven except that they swoon.” Then when fear is banished from their hearts, they say, What did your Lord say? They say, The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand. Then He says, The year will be such and such and such, and the jinn hear it and inform the soothsayers, and the soothsayers say, The year will be such and such, and they find it to be so. When God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they were struck by meteors. The Arabs said, when the jinn did not inform them of that, Everyone in the sky has perished. So the owner of the camels would slaughter a camel every day, and the owner of the cows would slaughter a cow every day, and the owner of the sheep would slaughter a sheep every day, until they hastened to dispose of their wealth. Then Thaqeef, who were the wisest of the Arabs, said, "O people, hold on to your wealth, for no one in the sky has perished, and this is not dispersion. Do you not see your landmarks, the stars, the sun, the moon, the night, and the day, as they are?" Satan said, An event has occurred on earth today, so bring me some soil from every land. So they brought it to him, and he began to smell it, and when he smelled the soil of Mecca, he said, This is where the event occurred. So they listened attentively, and behold, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had been sent. This meaning has already been mentioned briefly in Surah Al-Hijr. The meaning of the statement also about pelting them with meteors and burning them with them, and the explanation of that will come in Surah Al-Jinn, God willing. It has been said that they are only terrified by the coming of the Hour. Al-Kalbi and Ka’b said: There was a period of five hundred and fifty years between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, during which no messengers came. Then, when God Almighty sent Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, God Almighty spoke to Gabriel with the message. When the angels heard the speech, they thought that the Hour had come, and they were stunned by what they heard. Then, when Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended, he began to pass by each heaven, uncovering them, and they would raise their heads and say to each other, What did your Lord say? They did not know what He meant, but they said, The truth has said, and He is the Most High, the Grand. This is because Muhammad, peace be upon him, is among the signs of the Hour, according to the people of the heavens. Ad-Dahhak said: The angels who follow one another and go to the people of the earth to record their deeds. The Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, sends them. When they descend, a loud sound is heard from them. Those who are lower than the angels think it is from the matter of the Hour, so they fall down in prostration and faint until they realize that it is not from the matter of the Hour. This is a warning from God, the Most High, and information that the angels, with their selection and elevation, cannot intercede for anyone until they are given permission. But when they are given permission and they hear, they faint, and this is their state. So how can idols intercede or how can you hope for intercession while you do not acknowledge the Day of Resurrection? Al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd and Mujahid said: Until, when the terror is removed from the hearts of the polytheists. Al-Hasan, Mujahid and Ibn Zayd said: In the Hereafter, when death descends, to establish proof against them, the angels say to them: What did your Lord say in this world? They said: The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand. So they acknowledged it when acknowledgment would not benefit them, meaning they said: The truth said. The common reading is: Fazagh ‘an qulubihi fear of their hearts. Ibn Abbas read Faza’a ‘an qulubihim fear of their hearts as the nominative subject, and its subject is a pronoun referring to God. Whoever constructs it as a passive participle, the preposition and its complement are in the nominative case, and the verb in meaning refers to God, the Blessed and Exalted. The meaning in both readings is: the fear was removed from their hearts, as explained above. Similar to it is: he complained about him, if he removed from him what he was complaining about. Al-Hasan read Faza’a like the common people, except that he softened the zay, and the preposition and its complement are also in the nominative case, which is like saying: he turned away from such-and-such to such-and-such. This is the meaning of Fargh lama with a ra’ and a ghayn, and the softening is not the nominative subject. It was also narrated from Al-Hasan and Qatadah. They also narrated from them Fargh lama with a ra’ and a ghayn as the nominative subject, and the meaning is: God emptied their hearts, i.e., He removed them, i.e., He emptied them of fear and panic. The passive participle is also referred to this in this reading. Al-Hasan also narrated Fargh with a shaddah.
34:24: The Almighty says: "Say: 'Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?'" When He mentioned that their gods do not possess even an atom's weight of what the Lord has power over, He confirmed this by saying: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? That is, who creates for you these provisions that come from the heavens, meaning from the rain, sun, moon, stars, and whatever benefits they contain? And the earth, meaning from what comes out of the earth from the water and plants. That is, they cannot say, This is the action of our gods, saying, We do not know. So say, Indeed, God does that, He who knows what is in your souls. And if they say, Indeed, God provides for us, then the proof has been established that He is the One who should be worshipped. And either we or you are upon right guidance or in manifest error. This is to be fair in the proof, as when someone says, One of us is a liar, even though he knows that he is telling the truth and that his companion is a liar. Meaning: We and you are not on one matter, but on two opposing matters, and one of the two groups is guided, and that is us, and the other is astray, and that is you. So denying them is better than declaring a denial. Meaning: You are the ones who are astray when you associate partners with He who provides for you from the heavens and the earth. Or you is in apposition to the noun of inna. If it had been in apposition to the position, it would have been or you, and on guidance would be for the first only. And if you say or you, the second is more appropriate, and it is omitted from the first. It is permissible for it to be for the first, and this is the preferred choice of al-Mubarrad. He said: Its meaning is the meaning of the one who has insight to his companion, based on the validity of the threat and the support of clear evidence: One of us is lying, he has understood the meaning, just as you say: I do such-and-such and you do such-and-such, and one of us is mistaken, and he has understood that he is the one who is mistaken, so this is how it is. And we or you are on guidance or in clear misguidance. And or according to the Basrans is in its proper form and is not for doubt, but it is what the Arabs use in such a case when the informant does not want to clarify and he is aware of the meaning. Abu Ubaidah and Al-Farra’ said: It has the meaning of and, and its interpretation is: And we are upon guidance, and you are in clear error. Jarir said: A fox of the knights or winds that have adjusted them, cooking and rababa It means fox and wind. Another said: When the war became intense among us, we looked for winds or bundles.
34:25: The Almighty says: “Say, ‘You will not be asked about what we have committed’, that is, what we have acquired. ‘Nor will we be asked about what you do’, that is, I only intend what is good for you by what I am calling you to, not that I will be harmed by your disbelief. This is like His saying: ‘To you be your religion, and to me mine’ (al-Kafirun 109:6). And God will reward everyone. This is a verse of truce and abstention, and it was abrogated by the sword. It was said that this was revealed before the verse of the sword.
34:26: God Almighty says: Say, ‘Our Lord will gather us together’ meaning on the Day of Resurrection then He will judge between us in truth meaning He will judge, rewarding the guided one and punishing the misguided one. And He is the Opener meaning the Judge with truth, the Knower of the conditions of creation. All of this was abrogated by the verse of the sword.
34:27: The Almighty says: "Say: Show me those whom you have associated with Him as partners." Show me here is from seeing with the heart, so partners is the third object, meaning make me know the idols and statues which you have associated with Him, the Almighty, and have they participated in the creation of anything, then explain what it is, otherwise you would not have worshipped them. It is also possible that it is from seeing with the eyes, so partners is a condition. No means the matter is not as you claimed. It was said that No is a response to their omitted answer, as if he said: Show me those whom you have associated with Him. They said: They are the idols. So He said: No, meaning He has no partners. Rather, He is God, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
34:28: The Almighty says: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner to all mankind. That is, We have not sent you except to all mankind, i.e., generally. Thus, there is an inversion of the truth in the speech. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, We have not sent you except to gather all mankind by warning and conveying. Kafah means gatherer. It was also said that its meaning is sufficient for all mankind, meaning to suffice them. From their disbelief and invite them to Islam. The ha’ is for emphasis. It was said: meaning except for that, so the complement was deleted, meaning that which prevents people from pressing forward in conveying your message, or that which prevents them from disbelief. From this: the fold of a garment, because it is joined together. Bringing good tidings meaning of Paradise for those who obey. And a warner of the Fire for those who disbelieve. But most people do not know what is with God, and they are the polytheists, and at that time they were more numerous than the believers. And they say, ‘When will this promise come?’ meaning your appointment with us for the Hour to come. If you should be truthful? So God, the Most High, said: Say to them, O Muhammad: For you is an appointment on a Day from which you will not be delayed an hour nor will you precede it. So do not be deceived by its delay. The appointment is the appointed time. What is meant by this appointment is the time of resurrection. It was also said that it is the time of the approach of death, meaning that before the Day of Resurrection you have a specific time in which you will die and then you will know the truth of my words. It was said that what was meant by this day was the Day of Badr because that day was the appointed time for their punishment in this world according to the decree of God, the Most High. Grammarians have permitted the word mea’id yawm to be a subject, with yawm as a substitute for it, and the predicate is lakum for you. They have also permitted the word mea’id yawm to be an adverbial phrase, and the ha in anhu refers back to yawm. The word mea’id yawm la stastakhjur is not valid without a tanween. Adding yawm to what comes after it, if the ha is assumed to refer back to yawm, is because that is like adding something to itself because of the ha in the sentence. This is permissible on the condition that the ha is for the word mea’id yawm and not for the word day.
34:29: And they say, When will this promise come to pass, if you should be truthful?
34:30: Say to you, 'There is an appointed time for you on a Day from which you will not delay an hour, nor will you advance it.'
34:31: God the Almighty says: And those who disbelieve say, meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh. We will not believe in this Qur'an or in that which preceded it. Sa'id said on the authority of Qatadah: "Nor in that which preceded it of the Books and Prophets, peace and blessings be upon them." It was also said that it was from the Hereafter. Ibn Jurayj said: The one who said that was Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. It was also said: The People of the Book said to the polytheists: The description of Muhammad is in our Book, so ask him. When they asked him and it agreed with what the People of the Book said, the polytheists said: "We will not believe in this Qur'an or in that which was revealed before it of the Torah and the Gospel. Rather, we disbelieve in all of them." Before that, they used to consult the People of the Book and use their words as evidence. This revealed their contradictions and lack of knowledge. Then God the Blessed and Exalted informed them of their condition regarding what they have, saying: And if you could but see, O Muhammad, when the wrongdoers will be made to stand before their Lord, meaning imprisoned in the place of reckoning, exchanging words with one another, blaming and rebuking them after they had been friends and supporters in this world. The answer to law is omitted, meaning you would have seen a terrible and horrific matter. Then he mentioned what kind of speech they would return to, saying: Those who were oppressed from the disbelievers in this world will say to those who were arrogant who are the leaders and chiefs Had it not been for you, we would have been believers meaning you had led us astray and led us astray. The eloquent language is had it not been for you, and some Arabs say had it not been for you. Sibawayh narrated it in had it not been for you with the pronoun in the accusative case and the explicit nominative case after it being raised by the subject and its predicate being omitted. Muhammad ibn Yazid says: Had it not been for you is not permissible because the pronoun follows the explicit noun. Since the explicit noun is raised by consensus, the pronoun must also be raised. Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, “Did we avert you from guidance? This is a question with the meaning of denial, meaning we did not turn you away from guidance, nor did we force you. “After it came to you. Rather, you were criminals” meaning polytheists who persisted in disbelief. And those who were oppressed said to those who were arrogant, ‘Rather, it is your plotting by night and by day.’ The root of plotting in Arabic is deception and trickery. The verb ‘to plot’ means ‘to plot’. Al-Akhfash said: It is based on the estimation: This is your plotting by night and by day. An-Nahhas said: The meaning, and God knows best, is ‘Rather, your plotting by night and by day’, meaning your conspiring with us and calling us to disbelief has led us to do this. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: ‘Rather, your work by night and by day’. Qatadah said: ‘Rather, your plotting by night and by day has turned us away’. So the plotting was attributed to them because it occurred in them. It is like the statement of God Almighty: Indeed, when the term of God comes, it cannot be delayed Noah 7:4, so He attributed the term to Himself. Then He said: And when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour Al-A’raf 7:34, since the term was theirs. This is similar to your saying: His night is standing and his day is fasting.’ Al-Mubarrad said: ‘Rather, your plotting is by night and by day’, just as the Arabs say: His day is fasting and his night is standing.’ And Jarirah recited the following verse: We died, O Umm Ghilan, in the night, and you slept, but the night of the mounts does not sleep. And Sibawayh recited: I slept at night and my worries were revealed That is, we slept in it. And similar to it is: and the day is seeing (Ghafir 40:61). Qatada read: Rather, the plotting of the night and the day with the tanween of makr and the accusative of night and day. The meaning is: Rather, a plotting that occurs in the night and the day, so it was deleted. Sa’id ibn Jubayr read Rather, a plotting that occurs in the night and the day, with a fatha on the kaf and a shaddah on the ra’ meaning to repeat, and its nominative case is with the subject and the predicate is deleted. It is permissible for it to be nominative with an implied verb indicated by we have turned you away, as when they said to them, We have turned you away from guidance, they said, Rather, the plotting of the night and the day has turned us away. It was narrated from Sa’id ibn Jubayr: Rather, the plotting of the night and the day: The night and the day passed them by and they became heedless. It was said: The length of safety in them is like His statement: So the period was prolonged for them (al-Hadid 57:16). Rashid read Rather, the plotting of the night and the day with the accusative case, as you say: I saw him leading the pilgrims. This is only permissible in what is known. If you had said: I saw him leading Zayd, an-Nahhas would not have been permissible to mention it. When you commanded us to disbelieve in God and to attribute to Him equals, meaning likenesses, counterparts, and equals. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: So-and-so is the equal of so-and-so, meaning like him. It is also said nadid and he recited: Wherever you make me a rival, you are not my equal. This was mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. And they concealed their regret means they showed it. This is one of the opposites that can mean both concealment and display. Imru’ al-Qais said: I have overcome the guards and the horrors of the Ali clan, who were guarding me if they had allowed my death to happen. It was narrated that they buy. It was said: And they concealed their regret, meaning regret was evident in the secrets of their faces. It was said: Regret does not appear, but rather it is in the heart, and what is generated from it is only apparent, as was explained previously in Surah Yunus and Al Imran. It was said: Their display of regret was their saying: If only we had another chance, we would be among the believers (Ash-Shu’ara’: 152). It was said: They concealed their regret among themselves and did not speak out loud, as He said: And they whispered secretly (Ta-Ha 20:62). And We placed shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Shackles is the plural of chain. It is said: There is an iron chain around his neck. From this, the woman with bad character is called a chain of lice. Its origin is that the chain was made of hair and it would become lice-prone. And his hand was chained to his neck while he was chained, so he is chained. It is said: He has no family or chain. Ghale also and ghallah: the heat of thirst, and likewise ghalil is said from it: a man ghalal yaglilan ghallan so he is maghulul, according to what was not named its doer according to al-Jawhari. That is, the comprehensive rules were placed on the necks of the followers and the followed. It was said from other than these two groups. And it was said that those who disbelieved will return to them. And it was said that the speech ended with his saying: When they saw the punishment then he began and said: And We placed the shackles after that on the necks of all the disbelievers. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do? in the world.
34:32: Those who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed, Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals.
34:33: And those who were oppressed said to those who were arrogant, Rather, it was your plotting by night and by day when you ordered us to disbelieve in God and attribute to Him equals. And they concealed their regret when they saw the punishment. And We placed shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?
34:34: God the Almighty says: And We did not send to any city a warner but its affluent ones said, Qatada said: meaning its rich people, leaders, tyrants, and evil leaders to the messengers: "Indeed, we, in that with which you have been sent, disbelieve. And they said, "We are more in wealth and children," meaning, we have been given more wealth and children than you. If your Lord were not pleased with what we have of those who have been given more wealth and children, He would not have granted us that. "And we will not be punished," because whoever is kind to others, He will not punish them. So God rejected their statement and the argument they used regarding wealth, and He said to His Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him): "Say, 'Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills,' meaning, He expands it, and restricts it," meaning, He restricts it. That is, God is the One who differentiates between His servants in provisions as a test for them. None of this indicates what will be the consequences. Abundant provision in this world does not indicate happiness in the Hereafter, so do not think that your wealth and children will avail you at all tomorrow. "But most of the people do not know," because they do not reflect. Then he said in confirmation: And it is not your wealth and your children that bring you near to Us. Mujahid said: That is, nearness. And zalfa means nearness. Al-Akhfash said: That is, drawing near, and it is a verbal noun, so the position of qirba is accusative, as if he said that which brings you near to Us qanat. Al-Farra’ claimed that that which refers to both wealth and children. He has another saying, which is the view of Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj, the meaning being: It is not your wealth that brings you near to Us, nor your children that brings you near to Us. Then the predicate of the first was deleted because the second indicates it, and al-Farra’ recited: We are satisfied with what we have and you are satisfied with what you have, but the opinion differs It is permissible in places other than the Qur’an to say: By al-latīn with al-laṭayn and by al-laṭātī with al-laṭīn and “by al-laṭīn... for children specifically, meaning that the amount of wealth does not increase your status or degree with Us, nor does it bring you closer to Us. “Except for he who believes and does righteousness.” Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: The meaning is: Except for he who believes and does righteousness, his wealth and children will not harm him in this world. Layth narrated on the authority of Tawus that he used to say: O God, grant me faith and action, and spare me wealth and children, for I heard in what was revealed to me: And it is not your wealth or your children that bring you near to Us, except for he who believes and does righteousness. I said: Tawus' statement is questionable, and the meaning - and God knows best - is: Protect me from wealth and children who are arrogant or who are not good. As for good wealth and good children for a good man, then this is good, and this has already been mentioned in Al Imran, Maryam, and Al Furqan. "Min is in the accusative case as a disjunctive exception, meaning, But whoever believes and does righteous deeds, his faith and deeds will bring him closer to Me. Al-Zajjaj claimed that it is in the accusative case as an exception in apposition to the kaf and mim in taqaribukum." An-Nahhas said: This statement is wrong because the kaf and mim are for the addressee, so a apposition is not permissible. If this were permissible, then "I saw you, Zayd" would be permissible. Abu Ishaq's statement is also the statement of Al-Farra', except that Al-Farra' does not use a apposition because it is not from the wording of the Kufians. However, his statement leads to that, and he claimed that something like "Except he who comes to God with a sound heart Ash-Shu'ara' 26:89 would be in the accusative case according to him because of benefits. Al-Farra' allowed Min to be in the nominative case meaning, It is only he who believes," as he said, but I have not understood its meaning. For those, there is a double reward for what they did. This means His statement, Whoever brings a good deed will have ten times the like thereof.
