(al-An’am 6:160) Doubt means increase, meaning, they will have the reward of multiplication, which is a case of adding a verbal noun to a direct object. It has also been said, They will have a double reward. Doubt has the meaning of plural, and adding double to the reward is like adding something to itself, such as: the right of certainty, and the prayer of the first. That is, they will have the doubled reward, for one, ten to whatever increase God wills. This verse proves the superiority of wealth over poverty. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: If a believer is rich and pious, God will reward him twice, based on this verse. "And they will be in the upper chambers, secure. The general reading is jaza'a al-difl" with an addition. Az-Zuhri, Ya'qub, and Nasr ibn Asim read "jaza'a with a definite noun in the accusative case, and al-difl in the nominative case, meaning, those will have double as a reward," in the forward and backward sense. "Jaz'a al-difl" means that they will be rewarded double. "Jaz'a al-difl and jaza'a al-difl are in the nominative case, difference is a substitute for jaza'a. The majority also read al-ghurafaat in the plural, which is the preferred choice of Abu Ubaid, based on his statement, We will surely assign them lofty chambers in Paradise." Al-'Ankabut 29:58 Az-Zamakhshari said: "Al-ghurafaat" is read with a damma, fatha, and sukoon on the ra'. Al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Waththab, Hamzah, and Khalaf read "al-ghurfa in the singular form, based on his statement, Those will be rewarded the upper chamber." Al-Furqan 25:75. "Ghurfa" may refer to a collective noun or a generic noun. Ibn Abbas said: They are rooms of rubies, emeralds, and pearls. This has already been explained. Safe meaning from torment, death, illness, and sorrows. And those who strive against Our signs to invalidate Our evidence, proof, and Book. Fasteners are obstinate, thinking that they can evade Us by themselves. Those will be brought to the punishment meaning in Hell, where the guards will bring them there.
34:35: They said, We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished.
34:36: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it, but most of the people do not know.'
34:37: “It is not your wealth or your children that will bring you nearer to Us, except for those who believe and do righteousness. For those, there will be a double reward for what they did, and they will be in the chambers, secure.”
34:38: And those who strive against Our verses to frustrate them - those will be brought to the punishment.
34:39: God Almighty said: Say, ‘Indeed, my Lord expands provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him.’ He repeated it for emphasis. And whatever you spend, He will replace it. That is, say, O Muhammad, to those who are deceived by wealth and children, that God expands for whom He wills and restricts for whom He wills, so do not be deceived by wealth and children, but spend them in obedience to God, for whatever you spend in obedience to God, He will replace it. This implies that He will replace it for you. It is said: He will replace it for him and He will replace it for him, meaning He will give you both a replacement and equivalent, and that replacement will be either in this world or in the Hereafter. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “There is no day on which the servants arise but two angels descend, and one of them says: ‘O God, give to the one who spends a replacement and give to the one who withholds destruction.’” And also in it: “On the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), he said: God said to me: Spend, and I will spend on you…” The hadith. This is an indication of the replacement in this world for the same as the one who spent in it if the spending is in obedience to God. The successor may not be in this world, so it is like a supplication, as mentioned above, whether in response, atonement, or saving, and saving here is similar to it in reward. Issue: Al-Daraqutni and Abu Ahmad ibn Adi narrated on the authority of Abdul Hamid al-Hilali, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Jabir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Every good deed is charity. Whatever a man spends on himself and his family is recorded as charity for him. Whatever a man uses to protect his honor is charity. Whatever a man spends, God will replace it, except for what is spent on building or committing a sin.” Abdul Hamid said: I said to Ibn al-Munkadir: What protects a man’s honor? He said: What a poet or someone with a good tongue gives. Abdul Hamid was classed as trustworthy by Ibn Ma’in. I said: As for what is spent in disobedience, there is no dispute that he will not be rewarded for it nor will he be compensated for it. As for buildings, whatever is necessary for a person to shelter and protect, then that is compensated for and he will be rewarded for his construction. The same applies to protecting his buildings and covering his private parts. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The son of Adam has no right to anything other than these characteristics: a house to live in, a garment to cover his private parts, and bread and water.” This meaning has already been fully explained in Al-A’raf. God the Almighty says: And He is the Best of Providers. Since it is said about man: He provides for his family, and a prince provides for his army, He said: And He is the Best of Providers. The Provider among creation provides, but that is from wealth that he owns over them and then it is cut off. God the Almighty provides from treasuries that are inexhaustible and endless. And He who is brought out from nonexistence into existence is the Provider in truth, as He said: Indeed, it is God who is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Sturdy. (al-Dhariyat 51:58)
34:40: The Almighty's statement: And the Day We shall gather them all together is connected to His statement: And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are stopped. That is, if you could see them in this state, you would see a terrible thing. The addressee is the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and what is meant is him and his nation. Then He says: And if you could also see them on the Day We shall gather them all together, the worshippers and the worshipped, that is, We shall gather them for the judgment, then We shall say to the angels, Was it these that they worshipped? Sa'id said on the authority of Qatadah: This is a question, like the Almighty's statement to Jesus (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Did you tell the people to take me and my mother as gods besides God? 5:116. An-Nahhas said: The meaning is that if the angels (peace and blessings of God be upon them) denied them, this would be a rebuke to them, so it is a question of rebuke to the worshippers. They will say, 'Glory be to You,' meaning, glorifying You. You are our protector rather than them, meaning, You are our Lord whom we protect, obey, worship, and dedicate our worship to. Rather, they used to worship the jinn, meaning they obeyed Satan and his helpers. In the commentaries: That Kha'a, who were called Banu Malih from Khuza'ah, used to worship the jinn, and they claimed that the jinn appeared to them, and that they were angels, and that they were the daughters of God, as He says: And they attributed between Himself and the jinn a kinship (al-Saffat 37:158).
34:41: They said, “Glory be to You! You are our protector rather than them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them.”
34:42: God Almighty says: So today you have no power to benefit one another meaning intercession and salvation. Nor to harm meaning torment and destruction. It was also said: meaning the angels do not have the power to ward off harm from their worshippers, so the complement was omitted. And We will say to those who did wrong, ‘Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.’ It is permissible for God or the angels to say to them: Taste.
34:43: God the Almighty says: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, meaning the Qur’an. They say, ‘This is not but a man,’ meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. He wants to avert you from what your fathers used to worship, meaning your ancestors, the gods they used to worship. And they say, ‘This is not but a fabricated lie,’ meaning the Qur’an, meaning it is nothing but a fabricated lie. And those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, ‘This is not but obvious magic.’ Sometimes they say magic, and sometimes they say it is a lie. It is possible that some of them said it is magic and some of them said it is a lie.
34:44: The Almighty says: {And We gave them no books to study} meaning, they did not read in the book they were given the falsehood of what I have brought, nor did they hear it from a Messenger sent to them, as He said: {Or have We given them a scripture before it to which they cling?} (al-Zukhruf 43:21). So their denial has no basis to cling to nor any doubt attached to it, as the People of the Book say, even though they are falsifiers: We are People of the Book and laws and we rely on Messengers from the Messengers of God. Then He threatens them for their denial with His true statement: {And those before them denied} meaning, before them were people who were stronger than these in power, had more wealth and children, and lived more comfortably, so He destroyed them like Thamud and Aad. {And they did not attain} meaning, what the people of Mecca attained, {even a tenth of what We gave them} those nations. A tenth and a tenth are the same; they are two words. It was said: a tenth is a tenth. Al-Jawhari said: A tenth of something is a tenth, and they do not say this about anything other than a tenth. It was said: Those before them did not attain even a tenth of the gratitude for what We gave them. Narrated by Al-Naqqash. It was also said: God the Almighty did not give those before them a tenth of what He gave them of knowledge, explanation, argument and proof. Ibn Abbas said: There is no nation more knowledgeable than his nation, nor is there a clearer book than his book. It was also said: A tenth is a tenth of a tenth, and a tenth is a tenth of a tenth, so it would be a part of a thousand parts. Al-Mawardi: This is the most apparent, because what is meant by it is exaggeration in reduction. So they denied My messengers, so how was My censure meaning My punishment to the nations, and there is something omitted in it, and its interpretation is: So We destroyed them, so how was My censure.
34:45: "And those before them denied, but they did not attain even a tenth of what We had given them. So they denied My messengers. So how terrible was My reproach!"
34:46: God the Almighty says: Say, 'I only admonish you of one thing.' Complete the argument against the polytheists. That is, say to them, O Muhammad: I only admonish you. That is, I remind you and warn you of the evil consequences of what you are doing. With one thing means with one word that encompasses all the speech, requiring the negation of polytheism and the affirmation of deity. Mujahid said: It is there is no god but God. This is the saying of Ibn Abbas and Al-Suddi. Mujahid also said: With obedience to God. It was also said: With the Quran? Because it encompasses all the admonitions. It was also said: It is estimated as one characteristic, then He explained it by saying: That you stand up for God in pairs and individually. So an is in the accusative case as a substitute for one, or in the nominative case with an implied subject, that is, it is that you stand up. Al-Zajjaj's school of thought is that it is in the accusative case meaning that you stand up. This standing means standing to seek the truth, not the standing that is the opposite of sitting, and it is like saying: So-and-so stood up for such-and-such a matter?" That is, for the sake of God and to draw closer to Him. And as God the Almighty said: And that you deal justly with orphans (An-Nisa’: 127). In pairs and individually means alone and together, as Al-Suddi said. It was also said: alone in his opinion and consulting others, and this is a well-known saying. Al-Qutbi said: debating with others and thinking within himself, and all of the meanings are close. A fourth possibility is that in pairs refers to the work of the day and in pairs refers to the work of the night, because during the day one is together and at night one is alone, as Al-Mawardi said. It was also said that he said in pairs and individually because the mind is God’s proof against His servants, which is the intellect, so the one with the most intellect is the one with the greatest portion from God. So if they are alone, it is a single thought, and if they are in pairs, the minds meet and they see from the knowledge that which is weaker than when they are alone, and God knows best. Then consider, there is no madness in your companion. The pause according to Abu Hatim and Ibn Al-Anbari is on then consider. It was said: It is not a pause, because the meaning is: Then think, have you experienced your companion lying, or seen madness in him, or corruption in his conditions, or has he gone to someone who claims knowledge of magic or learned stories and read books, or have you known him to be greedy for your money, or are you able to oppose him in a single surah? So if you know with this thought that he is truthful, then what is this obstinacy? He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment. In Sahih Muslim, it is narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When this verse was revealed: And warn your nearest kinsmen (Ash-Shu’ara’: 214), and your sincere relatives among them, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out “until he ascended Safa and called out: ‘O Sabahah!’ They said: ‘Who is this who is calling?’ They said: ‘Muhammad.’ So they gathered around him. He said: ‘O sons of so-and-so, O sons of so-and-so, O sons of ‘Abd Manaf, O sons of ‘Abd al-Muttalib.’ So they gathered around him. He said: ‘Do you think that if I told you that horses would emerge from the foot of this mountain, would you believe me?’ They said: ‘We have never known you to lie.’ He said: ‘Then I am a warner to you before a severe punishment.’” Abu Lahab said: ‘Perish you! Did you not gather us for anything except this?’ Then he said: “Then this surah was revealed: ‘Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he!’” (al-Masad 111:1). This is how Al-A’mash read it until the end of the surah.
34:47: God Almighty says: “Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you” meaning, for conveying the message, it is yours meaning, that reward is yours if I asked you for it. My reward is only from God, and He is, over all things, Witness meaning, He is Watchful, All-Knowing, and Present over my deeds and your deeds. Nothing is hidden from Him, so He rewards everyone.
34:48: The Almighty says: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord casts the truth.' That is, He clarifies and makes the argument clear. Qatada said: With the truth through revelation. And from him: The truth is the Qur'an. Ibn Abbas said: That is, He casts falsehood with the truth, the Knower of the unseen. Isa bin Omar read the Knower of the unseen not as a substitute, that is, say, Indeed, my Lord, the Knower of the unseen, casts the truth. Al-Zajjaj said: The nominative case has two aspects: in position, because position is the position of the nominative case, or as a substitute for what is in yadhquf. An-Nahhas said: There are two other aspects to the nominative case: it can be a predicate after a predicate, and it can be with an implied subject. Al-Farra' claimed that the nominative case in such a case is more common in Arabic speech when it comes after the predicate of inna and similar to it: "Indeed, that is the truth. The People of the Fire will dispute" (p. 64). It was read: the unseen with the three vowel marks, so the unseen is like the houses, and the unseen is like the patient, and it is the matter that is absent and very hidden.
34:49: The Almighty said: Say, ‘The truth has come.’ Saeed said on the authority of Qatada: He means the Qur’an. An-Nahhas said: The meaning is, The possessor of the truth has come, meaning the book that contains proofs and arguments. Nor does falsehood originate, Qatada said: Satan, meaning Satan does not create anyone. Nor does it restore, so ma fulfills. It is permissible for it to be an interrogative meaning, In something, meaning, the truth has come, so in something is falsehood left until it restores and originates it, meaning, nothing of it remains, like His statement: Do you then see for them any remnant? (al-Haqqah 69:8), meaning, you do not see.
34:50: God the Almighty says: "Say: 'If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment.'" That is because the disbelievers said: I have abandoned the religion of your fathers and have gone astray. So God said to him: "Say, O Muhammad: 'If I have gone astray as you claim, I only go astray to my own detriment.'" The common reading of the word is dalāl with a fathah on the lam. Yahya ibn Wathāb and others read: "Say: If I have gone astray" with a kasrah on the lam and a fathah on the dad from adhāla. Error and misguidance are the opposites of guidance. I have gone astray with a fathah on the lam and I go astray with a kasrah on the dad. God the Almighty says: "Say: 'If I have gone astray, I only go astray to my own detriment.'" This is the dialect of Najd, which is the most eloquent. The people of Aliyah say I have gone astray with a kasrah and I go astray, meaning the sin of my going astray is upon myself. And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me of wisdom and eloquence. He is All-Hearing, Near, meaning He hears and is quick to respond to those who call upon Him. It was said that the meaning of the system is: Say: My Lord casts the truth and makes clear the proof. And the error of he who goes astray does not invalidate the proof. And if I went astray, I would harm myself. It does not invalidate God’s proof. And if I am guided, then that is the grace of God, since He has established me on the proof. Indeed, He is All-Hearing, All-Near.
34:51: The Almighty's saying: And if you could but see when they are terrified, there is no escape. He mentioned the state of the disbelievers at a time when they are forced to know the truth. The meaning is: If you could see when they are terrified in this world when death descends or some other punishment from God, the Almighty. Its meaning was narrated from Ibn Abbas. Al-Hasan: It is their fear in the graves from the shout. It was narrated from him that this fear is only when they emerge from their graves, and Qatada said the same. Ibn Mughaffal said: When they witness God's punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Suddi: It is their fear on the day of Badr when their necks were struck by the swords of the angels, so they were unable to flee or return to repentance. Saeed bin Khabeer: It is the army that is swallowed up in the wilderness, and one of them remains and tells the people what happened to his companions, so they are terrified. This is their fear. There is no escape means there is no escape, said Ibn Abbas. Mujahid: There is no escape. And they are seized from a place nearby meaning from the graves. It was said: Wherever they are, they are close to God, they are not absent from Him nor do they miss Him. Ibn Abbas said: It was revealed regarding eighty thousand who will attack the Kaaba at the end of time to destroy it, and as they enter the desert, the earth will swallow them up, so it is taken from a nearby place. I said: In this meaning there is a report attributed to Hudhayfah, and we have mentioned it in the Book of Remembrance. He said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, and he mentioned a tribulation that will occur between the people of the East and the West: While they are like that, the Sufyani will emerge upon them from the dry valley in a state of turmoil until he descends upon Damascus. He will send two armies, an army to the East and an army to Medina. The army will march towards the East until they descend upon the land of Babylon in the cursed city and the wicked spot, meaning the city of Baghdad. He said: They will kill more than three thousand and deflower more than one hundred women and kill three hundred rams from the descendants of Abbas. Then they will go out heading towards Syria. A banner of guidance will come out from Kufa and catch up with that army there in two nights. They will kill them, and no one will escape them. They will rescue what is in their hands of captives and spoils. His second army will descend upon Medina and plunder it for three days and nights. Then they will go out heading towards Mecca until they are in the desert. God will send Gabriel, peace be upon him, and he will say: ‘O Gabriel, go and destroy them.’ He will strike it with his foot once.” God will cause the earth to swallow them up, as God the Almighty said: And if you could but see when they are terrified, there is no escape, and they are seized from a place nearby. Only two men will remain from them, one of them a bearer of good tidings and the other a warner, and they are from Juhayna. That is why it was said: And with Juhayna is the sure report. It was also said: They were seized from a place nearby, meaning their souls were seized in their places, so they could not escape death. This is according to those who say: This is the panic at the time of death. It is possible that this is from the panic that means answer. It is said: A man was frightened, meaning he answered the one who calls out to him when fear befalls him. And from this is the report when he said to the Ansar: You are few when you are greedy and many when you are frightened. Whoever said: He meant the swallowing up or killing in this world, like the day of Badr, said: They were seized in this world before they were seized in the Hereafter. Whoever said: It is the extraction on the Day of Resurrection said: They were taken from the belly of the earth to its surface. It was also said: They were taken from a place close to Hell and thrown into it.
34:52: The Almighty said: And they said, 'We believe in it,' meaning in the Qur'an. Mujahid said: in God Almighty. Al-Hasan: in the resurrection. Qatada: in the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. And how can they seek to return from a distant place? Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said: The seeking is the return, meaning they seek to return to the world to believe, but that is far from them. From this is the saying of the poet: He wished that you would return to May and not quarrel with her Al-Suddi said: It is repentance, meaning they sought it even though it was far away, because repentance is only accepted in this world. It was said: Taanasooh means to grab. Ibn Al-Sikkit said: When a man grabs a man to grab his head and beard, it is said: Nasha yansooh nawsh. And he recited: It rushes into the basin from a height, rushing through it, crossing the desert. That is, you take the water of the basin from above and drink a lot, and thus stop drinking and become deserted so that you do not need more water. He said: And from it comes the word munawash in battle, which is when the two parties come close together. And a man who is nawash means someone who is strong. And tanawash is ta’al and ta’al and ta’al and intiyash are similar. The rajaz poet said: She was touching my neck God the Almighty said: And how can they grasp the truth from a distant place? Meaning: How can they attain faith in the Hereafter when they have disbelieved in this world? Abu Amr, Al-Kisa'i, Al-A'mash and Hamzah read: And how can they grasp the truth from a distant place with a hamza. An-Nahhas said: Abu Ubaidah finds this reading unlikely because tanawush with a hamza means distance, so how can it be: And how can they grasp the truth from a distant place? Abu Ja'far said: The reading is permissible and good, and it has two interpretations in Arabic speech, and this far-fetched interpretation does not apply to it. One of the two interpretations is that the original is unhamzed, then the waw is hamzated because the vowel in it is hidden, and that is common in Arabic speech. In the copy of the Qur'an that the group transmitted from the group: And when the messengers are fed Al-Mursalat 41:11, the original is waqtat because it is derived from time. The plural of dar is ad'ur. The other interpretation was mentioned by Abu Ishaq, who said: It is derived from na'ish, which means movement in slowness, meaning how can they move when it is distant? It is said: I took something from behind, and na'ish means something slow. Al-Jawhari said: Tanawush with a hamza means delay and separation. I delayed the matter, I delayed it, so it became delayed. It is also said: He did it naishan, meaning finally. The poet said: Naish wished he had obeyed me, but things happened after that. Another said: You have been away from your students for a long time, and you have come back late after the report has passed you by. Al-Farra’ said: The hamza and omission of the hamza in tanawsh are similar, like: dhamtu ar-rajul wa dhamtuhu, meaning I blamed him. From a distant place means from the afterlife. Abu Ishaq narrated on the authority of al-Tamimi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: And how can they say: The response, they asked him, but it is not the time to respond.
34:53: God the Almighty says: And they disbelieved in him meaning in God the Almighty. It was also said: in Muhammad before meaning in this world. And they cast aspersions on the unseen The Arabs say to anyone who speaks what he does not have the right to say: He casts aspersions and throws aspersions on the unseen. From a distant place is an example of someone who casts aspersions but hits the mark, meaning they cast aspersions and say: There is no resurrection or revival, nor Paradise or Hellfire, casting aspersions on their part, as Qatadah said. It was also said: They cast aspersions on the Qur'an and say: Magic, poetry, and legends of the ancients. It was also said: in Muhammad, and they say: He is a magician, poet, soothsayer, or madman. From a distant place meaning that God has kept them from knowing the truthfulness of Muhammad. It was also said: He meant distance from the heart, meaning from a place far from their hearts. Mujahid read: And they cast aspersions on the unseen without the named subject, meaning they cast aspersions on it. It was also said: It is cast to them by someone who misleads and leads them astray.
34:54: The Almighty says: And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire. It was said: They will be barred from salvation from the punishment. It was also said: They will be barred from what they desire in this world of their wealth and families. Qatadah's school of thought is that the meaning is that when they saw the punishment, they desired that it would be accepted from them so that they would obey God, the Almighty and Majestic, and desist from what God commands them, but they were barred from that because that was in this world and it had passed away at that time. The original form is hawala, so the vowel of the waw was changed to the ha' and it became a ya', then its vowel was deleted due to its heaviness. As He did with their followers. Al-ashya' is the plural of shi'a, and shi'a is the plural of shi'a. From before meaning with those who passed from the previous disbelieving generations. Indeed, they were in doubt meaning about the matter of the messengers, the resurrection, Paradise, and Hell. It was also said: about religion and monotheism, and the meaning is the same. Suspicious means that one is suspicious of him. It is said: a man became suspicious, meaning he became suspicious, so he is suspicious. And whoever said that it is from doubt, which is suspicion and accusation, said: It is said suspicious doubt? Just as it is said: amazing wonder and poetic poetry in emphasis. I have finished the Surah, praise be to God, Lord of the Worlds.
35:1: The Almighty said: Praise be to God, Creator of the heavens and the earth. Three scenarios are permissible for Fatir 35:the accusative as an adjective, the nominative with an implied subject, and the accusative as an expression of praise. Sibawayh said: Praise be to God, the One worthy of praise, likewise the Maker of the angels. Fatir 35:the Creator. It has already been mentioned in Joseph and others. And breaking al-fitr: splitting something. It is said: I broke it, so it split. And from this: the camel's fang grew, so it is a fatir camel. And breaking something means splitting. And a sword is fatar, meaning it has a crack in it. Antara said: My sword is like a chariot, it is like my weapon, it does not fail or break Al-Fitr: origination and invention. Ibn Abbas said: I did not know what Fatir al-Samawat wa al-Ard was until two Bedouins came to me arguing about a well. One of them said: I created it, meaning I initiated it. Al-Fitr is milking a camel with the forefinger and thumb. What is meant by the heavens and earth is the entire world. This indicates that whoever is able to initiate is able to repeat. Ja'il al-Mala'ikah does not have tanween because it is in the past tense. Rusul is a second object, and it is said with an implied verb because if the subject is in the past tense, it does not affect it. When it is used as a future tense, the tanween is deleted for ease. Ad-Dahhak recited Al-Hamdu Lillah, He created the heavens and the earth as a past tense verb. Ja'il al-Mala'ikah as-Rasul means the creation of angels. Among the messengers are Gabriel, Michael, Israfil, and the Angel of Death, may God bless them all. Al-Hasan recited Ja'il al-Mala'ikah in the nominative case. Khalid ibn Nasheet recited Ja'il al-Mala'ikah, both of which are clear. Ulu Ajana is an adjective, meaning people with wings. Two by two, three by three, and four by four. Qatada said: Some of them have two wings, some three, and some four, with which they descend from the sky to the earth, and ascend from the earth to the sky, and it is a journey of such-and-such in one time, meaning He made them messengers. Yahya ibn Salam said: To the prophets. Al-Suddi said: To the servants, with mercy or punishment. In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, with six hundred wings.” Al-Zuhri reported that Gabriel, peace be upon him, said to him: O Muhammad, if you saw Israfil, he would have twelve thousand wings, one wing in the east and one wing in the west, and the Throne is on his shoulders, and sometimes he becomes small before the majesty of God until he becomes like a wasp, and wasp is a small bird, until nothing carries the Throne of your Lord except His majesty. Ulu is the plural of dhu, just as these is the plural of dha, and their equivalents in the established form are makhadh and khalafah. We have already discussed two by two, “thalath,” and raba’ in An-Nisa’ and that they are indeclinable. He increases in creation what He wills meaning in the creation of the angels, according to most of the commentators, as mentioned by Al-Mahdawi. Al-Hasan said: He increases in creation, meaning in the wings of the angels, what He wills. Al-Zuhri and Ibn Jurayj said: It means a beautiful voice. This has been discussed in the introduction to the book. Al-Haytham Al-Farsi said: I saw the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, in my dream, and he said: You are Al-Haytham who adorned the Qur’an with your voice. May God reward you with good. Qatada said: He increases in creation what He wills: charm in the eyes, beauty in the nose, and sweetness in the mouth. It was also said: beautiful handwriting. Muhajir Al-Kila’i said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Beautiful handwriting increases the clarity of speech. It was also said: a beautiful face. It was said in the report of this verse: it is a beautiful face, a beautiful voice, and beautiful hair. Al-Qushayri mentioned it. Al-Naqqash: it is curly hair. It was also said: the mind and discernment. It was also said: sciences and crafts. Indeed, God is over all things competent of decrease and increase. Al-Zamakhshari: The verse is absolute and includes every increase in creation, such as tall stature, uprightness of form, perfection of limbs, strength of grip, prudence of mind, eloquence of opinion, boldness of heart, generosity of soul, smoothness of tongue, eloquence of speech, good manners in handling affairs, and the like, which cannot be described.
35:2: The Almighty said: Whatever mercy God opens to mankind, no one can withhold it. Grammarians have permitted, in places other than the Qur'an, no one can withhold it using the word ma and laha in the meaning. They have also permitted what is withheld, no one can send it. They have also permitted what God opens to mankind of mercy in the nominative case to be ma in the sense of who. That is, the messengers were sent as a mercy to mankind, and no one has the power to send them except God. It has also been said: Whatever God brings them of rain or provision, no one can withhold it, and whatever He withholds of that, no one can send it. It has also been said: It is supplication, as Ad-Dahhak said. Ibn Abbas: From repentance. It has also been said: From success and guidance. I said: The word mercy encompasses all of that, as it is indefinite due to being widespread and ambiguous, so it includes every mercy as an alternative, so it is general in all that was mentioned. In the Muwatta of Malik: It reached him that Abu Hurairah used to say when he woke up and the people had broken their fast: We broke our fast with the rising star of victory, then he would recite this verse: Whatever mercy God opens for mankind, none can withhold it. “And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.” It was mentioned above.
35:3: The Almighty said: O mankind, remember the favor of God upon you. The meaning of this remembrance is gratitude. Is there a creator other than? It is permissible in other than the nominative, accusative, and genitive cases. The nominative case has two aspects: One of them: It means is there a creator other than God, meaning there is no creator but God. The second aspect: It is to be an adjective in position because the meaning is: is there a creator other than God? And min is redundant. The accusative case is for exception. The genitive case is for the wording. Hamid al-Tawil said: I said to al-Hasan: Who created evil? He said: Glory be to God, is there a creator other than God, the Almighty, who created good and evil. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read: Is there a creator other than God in the genitive case. The rest read it in the nominative case. He provides for you from the sky meaning rain. And the earth meaning plants. There is no god but Him, so how are you turned away? From afka with a fat-ha, which means turning away? It is said: Ma afka 'an kida what turned you away from such-and-such, meaning What turned you away from it? It was said: It is from ifk with kasra, which means lying. This also goes back to what was mentioned above, because it is a statement that is diverted from truth and correctness, i.e., how can you deny the Oneness of God? The verse is an argument against the Qadarites because it denies a creator other than God, while they affirm two creators along with Him, as mentioned above in more than one place.
35:4: The Almighty says: And if they deny you meaning the infidels of Quraysh. Messengers before you were also denied He consoles and comforts His Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and to take as an example those who came before him in their patience. And to God all matters are returned Al-Hasan, Al-A'raj, Ya'qub, Ibn 'Amir, Abu Haywah, Ibn Muhaisin, Hamid, Al-A'mash, Hamzah, and Yahya read it. Al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with a fat-ha on the ta' as the named subject. Abu 'Ubaid chose it based on the Almighty's saying: Unquestionably, to God do all matters return (al-Shura 42:53). The rest read it as a passive verb.
35:5: The Almighty says: O mankind, indeed the promise of God is true. This is an exhortation to those who deny the Messenger after clarifying the evidence for the truth of His statement: Indeed, resurrection, reward, and punishment are true. So let not the worldly life deceive you. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The deception of worldly life is that a person is preoccupied with its pleasures and delights so much that he forgets to work for the Hereafter, to the point that he says, Oh, if only I had sent ahead for my life. "And let not the Deceiver deceive you about God." Ibn al-Sikkit and Abu Hatim said: Deceiver is the devil. "Ghorror is the plural of ghar, and ghar" is a verbal noun. "Ghorr can be a verbal noun, but this is far-fetched according to those other than Abu Ishaq, because gharratuhu is transitive, and a transitive verbal noun is usually in the form of fa'l, such as darabatuhu" I struck him striking, except in minor matters that cannot be compared to them. They said: "I adhered to him adheringly, and the disease exhausted him severely." As for the meaning of the preposition, the best that has been said about it is what Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Deceit about God is that a person commits sins and then hopes for forgiveness from God. The general reading of the word is al-Ghurur with a fatha on the ghayn, which refers to the devil, meaning, Do not let him deceive you with his whispers that he will overlook your faults because of your virtue. Abu Haywah, Abu al-Samal al-Adawi, and Muhammad ibn al-Samiq’ read it as al-Ghurur with a damma on the ghayn, which refers to falsehood, meaning, Do not let falsehood deceive you. Ibn al-Sikkit said: Al-Ghurur with a damma is what one is deceived by of the pleasures of this world. Al-Zajjaj said: Al-Ghurur may be the plural of Ghar, like Qa’id and Qa’ud. An-Nahhas said: “Or the plural of Ghar, or it is similar to their saying: The disease has worn him down, wearing him down, and he adhered to him a adherence.” Az-Zamakhshari said: Or it is a source of ghara, like luzum and nahawk.
35:6: The Almighty said: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. That is, be hostile to him and do not obey him. And his enmity is indicated to you by his expulsion of your father from Paradise, and his guarantee of your misguidance in His statement: And I will surely mislead them and arouse in them false hopes. (An-Nisa': 119) And His statement: "I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path. Then I will come to them from before them." (al-A’raf 7:16-17) So the Almighty informed us that Satan is a clear enemy to us, and He related to us his story, and what he did to our father Adam (peace be upon him), and how he volunteered to be our enemy and deceive us before and after our existence. And we, on that basis, support him and obey him in whatever he wants from us that leads to our destruction. Al-Fudayl ibn 'Iyad used to say: O liar, O slanderer, fear God and do not curse Satan in public while you are his friend in secret. Ibn Al-Sammak said: How strange that someone disobeys a doer of good after recognizing his good deeds and obeys the accursed one after recognizing his enmity. This meaning has already been clearly stated in Surat Al-Baqarah. Enemy in His statement, Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you may mean hostile, so it may be dual, plural, or feminine. It may also mean relative kinship, so it is singular in all cases, as God, the Almighty, said, For indeed, they are an enemy to me (Ash-Shu’ara’: 77). In the feminine form, according to this, there is also enemy. An-Nahhas said: “As for the statement of some grammarians that the waw is hidden and they brought the ha’, this is a mistake. Rather, the waw is a letter of flogging.” He only invites his party prevented in from working, so the verb came after it. Hizbhi means his followers. That they may be among the companions of the Blaze so this is his enmity. Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment “alladhina” could be a substitute for ashab, so it would be in the accusative case, or a substitute for hizbihi, so it would be in the nominative case. A fourth statement, and it is the best: It is in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is for them is a severe punishment, as if He, glory be to Him, explained the state of its agreement and opposition. The speech would have been completed in His statement, of the companions of the Blaze, then He began by saying, those who disbelieved will have a severe punishment. “And those who believed and did righteous deeds” is also in the nominative case as a subject, and its predicate is for them is forgiveness, meaning for their sins. And a great reward, meaning Paradise.
35:7: “Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment. But those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.”
35:8: God the Almighty said: Is he to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive? "Min" is in the nominative case as a subject and its predicate is omitted. Al-Kisa'i said: What indicates this is the statement of God the Almighty: "And let not your soul perish over them in regret." The meaning is: Is he to whom the evil of his deed has been made attractive so he sees it as good, will your soul perish over them in regret? He said: This is a novel Arabic saying that only a few know. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned it on the authority of Al-Zajjaj. Al-Nahhas said: What Al-Kisa'i said is the best that has been said about the verse, because of what he mentioned of the indication of what was omitted, and the meaning is that God the Almighty forbade His Prophet from being excessively distressed and grieving over them, as He the Almighty said: "Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief" Al-Kahf 18:6. The commentators said: Fight. Nasr ibn Ali said: I asked Al-Asma'i about the statement of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the people of Yemen: "They are the most tender-hearted and the most miserly in obedience. What is the meaning of miserly?" He said: I advise. I said to him: The people of interpretation, such as Mujahid and others, say about the statement of God the Almighty: {Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief}, that it means killing yourself. He said: It is from that exact same thing, as if he killed himself from the severity of his advice to them. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: There is an inversion in it, its metaphor is: Is he to whom the evil of his deed made attractive so he sees it as good? So do not consume yourself over them in regret. Indeed, God leaves astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. It was said: The answer is omitted in meaning: Is he to whom the evil of his deed made attractive like he who He guides? And [The meaning is missing] "Indeed, God misguides whom He wills and guides whom He wills." Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa' recited: "So not your soul. Concerning Is he to whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive?" there are four opinions. First: They are the Jews, Christians, and Magians, said by Abu Qilabah. And his evil deeds are opposition to the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. Second: They are the Khawarij, narrated by Umar ibn al-Qasim. So his evil deeds are a distortion of interpretation. Third: The devil, said by al-Hasan. And his evil deeds are seduction. Fourth: The infidels of Quraysh, said by al-Kalbi. And his evil deeds are polytheism. He said: It was revealed about al-'As ibn Wa'il as-Sahmi and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib. Another said: It was revealed about Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. "And he saw it as good" means correct, said al-Kalbi. It was also said: Beautiful. I said: The statement that it refers to the disbelievers of Quraysh is the most apparent of the statements, based on the words of God the Almighty: You are not responsible for their guidance Al-Baqarah 2:272, and His words: And let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you Al-Imran 3:176, and His words: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this message Al-Kahf 18:6, and His words: Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not believe Ash-Shu’ara’ 26:3, and His words in this verse: So do not let yourself waste away over them in regret. This is clear and obvious, meaning that your grief over their disbelief will be of no benefit, for God has led them astray. This verse refutes the statement of the Qadarites, based on what was mentioned above, meaning, “Is one to whom evil has been made attractive so that he sees it as good, desiring to guide him? But that is up to God, not up to you, and what is up to you is the conveyance. Abu Jaafar, Shaiba and Ibn Muhaisin read: “Do not go, your soul, with a damma on the ta’ and a kasra on the ha’, in the accusative case as a direct object, and the two meanings are close. “Regrets” is in the accusative case as a direct object for which, meaning do not let yourself be consumed by regrets. And upon them is the relative clause of goes away, just as you say: He perished on it out of love and died on it out of grief. It is a clarification of the one who is regretting it. It is not permissible for it to be related to regrets because the verbal noun does not precede it with its relative clause. It is permissible for it to be a state, as if all of it became regrets due to the excess of regret, as Jarir said: The hot winds tore their flesh with the night-goers until they were all gone, their chests and their backs torn. He means: They returned, both of them, all of them, and their chests, meaning that nothing remained but their whole bodies and their chests. And from this is the saying of another: As a result of them, my soul falls in regret, and remembering them makes me sick. Or a source. God is All-Knowing of what they do.
35:9: The Almighty said: And it is God who sends the winds, and they stir up the clouds, and We drive them to a dead land. Dead and dead are one and the same, and so are dead women and dead women. This is the opinion of the most skilled grammarians. Muhammad ibn Yazid said: This is the opinion of the Basrans, and he did not exclude anyone, and he supported that with conclusive evidence. He recited: Not everyone who dies and finds rest is dead, but the dead are the dead of the living. The dead person is the one who lives in a gloomy and depressed mood with little hope. He said: Do you see any difference between qayt and qayt? And he recited: Henon Lenon Aysar Banu Yasir Sawas Makrama Sons of Aysar He said: They agreed that hinun and lainun are one and the same, and so are mayit and mayit, and sayyid and sayyid. He said: So he made it after he said: And God is the One Who sent the winds for what, and this is from the category of diversifying speech. Abu Ubaidah said: Its path is that it leads to it, because he said: Then it stirs up a cloud. Al-Zamakhshari: If you say: Why did fatathir come in the present tense and not what came before it and after it? I say: To describe the situation in which the winds stir up the clouds, and to evoke that beautiful image that indicates the divine power. And thus they do with an action that has a kind of distinction and specificity in a situation that is strange, or concerns the addressee or something else, as Ta’abbata Sharran said: I found the ghoul falling in the steppe like a newspaper, Sahsahhan I hit her without astonishment, and she fell down, slain by the hands and the neighbors. Because he intended to portray to his people the state in which he was allegedly encouraged to attack the ghoul, as if he was showing them it and informing them of its true nature, in order to be amazed by his audacity in the face of every terror and his steadfastness in the face of every hardship. Likewise, the driving of the clouds to the dead land, since they were evidence of dazzling power, it was said: We drove and We revived, changing them from the third-person form to what is more specific and indicative of it. The common reading is the winds. Ibn Muhaisin, Ibn Kathir, Al-A’mash, Yahya, Hamzah, and Al-Kisa’i read the wind as a singular form. The explanation of this verse and its discussion have already been completed. Likewise the Resurrection means likewise they will be revived after you have died, from raising man a resurrection. The kaf is in the nominative case, meaning like the revival of death is the raising of the dead. On the authority of Abu Razin al-Uqayli, who said: “I said, ‘O Messenger of God, how does God bring the dead back to life, and what is the sign of that in His creation?’ He said, ‘Did you not pass by the valley of your people when it was barren, then pass by it when it was green and shining?’ I said, ‘Yes, O Messenger of God.’ He said, ‘Thus does God bring the dead back to life, and that is His sign in His creation.’” We have mentioned this hadith in Al-A’raf and elsewhere.
35:10: The Almighty’s saying: Whoever desires honor, then to God belongs all honor. Al-Farra’s interpretation is: Whoever desires the knowledge of honor. This is what others among the people of knowledge said. That is, whoever desires the knowledge of honor that does not accompany humiliation, because if honor leads to humiliation, then it is exposure to humiliation, and the honor that does not accompany humiliation belongs to God, the Almighty. All together is in the accusative case as a state. Al-Zajjaj estimated its meaning: Whoever desires honor through his worship of God, the Almighty - and honor belongs to Him, glory be to Him - then God, the Almighty, will honor him in the hereafter and in this world. I say: This is better, and it was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, as will come. To God belongs all glory. This clearly indicates that the listeners despair of His glory, and that no one else can hope for what is due to Him. Thus, the definite article is for the covenant with those who know Him - glory be to Him - and what is due to Him. This is what is understood from His true statement in Surat Yunus 10:“And let not their statement grieve you. Indeed, glory belongs to God.” (Yunus 10:65). It is possible that the Almighty wants to alert those of high status and high aspirations to where honor can be attained and from where it is deserved, so the definite article is for comprehensiveness, which is understood from the verses of this surah. Whoever seeks honor from God and is sincere in seeking it with need and humility, stillness and submission, will find it with Him - God willing - not withheld or hidden from him. “The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘Whoever humbles himself before God, God will raise him up, and whoever seeks it from someone other than Him, He will leave him to the one from whom he seeks it.’” He mentioned a people who sought honor from someone other than Him, so He said: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers - do they seek honor from them? But indeed, honor belongs entirely to God. (An-Nisa’: 139). So I will inform you clearly and without any doubt that honor belongs to Him, with which He honors whomever He wills and humiliates whomever He wills. And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, explained his statement: “Whoever desires honor, then to God belongs all honor. Whoever desires honor in both abodes, let him obey the Almighty.” This is the meaning of what Al-Zajjaj said. And he did well when he said: And when necks are humbled in humility before You, then their honor lies in their humiliation. So whoever desires honor to attain the greatest victory and enter the abode of honor - and honor belongs to God - let him seek honor in God the Almighty and take pride in Him. For whoever takes pride in a servant, God will humiliate him, and whoever takes pride in God, God will give him honor. God the Almighty says: To Him ascends good speech, and righteous action raises it. There are two issues in this: First: The Almighty says: To Him ascends the good word. And the speech is complete. Then it begins: And the righteous deed raises it, meaning: God raises it, or raises its doer. It is possible that the meaning is: And the righteous deed raises the good word, so the speech would be connected as will be explained. Ascent is the movement upward, and it is also the ascension. This is not conceivable in speech because it is an accident, but its ascent is given as an example of its acceptance, because the place of reward is above, and the place of punishment is below. Al-Zajjaj said: It is said that the matter ascended to the judge, meaning he knew it, so it means knowledge. He specifically mentioned the good and the good to clarify the reward for it. His saying to Him means it ascends to God. It was also said that it ascends to His heaven, the place where no one else’s judgment applies. It was also said that it means that the book in which the servant’s acts of obedience are written is carried to the heaven. The good word is the monotheism emanating from a good belief. It was also said that it is praise and glorification, remembrance of God and the like. They recited: Do not be satisfied with a man's sweet words until he beautifies what he says with actions. If you weigh his actions with his words, then balance them, then your brother is beauty. Ibn al-Muqaffa said: Words without action are like a vine without fat, a cloud without rain, and a bow without a string. It was said about him: The article is not complete without action, every word without action is in vain Saying without action is beautiful, and marriage without a guardian is the same. Ad-Dahhak read it with a damma on the yaa. The majority of people read it as kalam, the plural of kalima. Abu Abd ar-Rahman read it as kalam. I say: According to this, kalam can be used to mean words and vice versa. Based on this, Abu al-Qasim said: Speech is divided into three types, so he put kalam in place of kalam. And God knows best. And righteous action elevates it. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said: The meaning is, righteous action elevates good words. In the hadith, God does not accept a word without an action, and He does not accept a word or an action without intention, and He does not accept a word, an action, or an intention without adhering to the Sunnah. Ibn Abbas said: So if the servant remembers God and says good words and performs His obligatory duties, his words are elevated along with his actions, but if he says something but does not perform His obligatory duties, his words are rejected based on his actions. Ibn Atiyyah said: This statement refutes the belief of the Sunnis and is not authentically reported from Ibn Abbas. The truth is that if the sinner who abandons obligatory duties remembers God and says good words, then it will be recorded for him and accepted from him, and he will have his good deeds and bear his bad deeds. God accepts from everyone who avoids polytheism. Also, good speech is a righteous deed. The statement of the one who says that action elevates words is correct when he interprets that it increases their elevation and good standing if it is supported by them. Just as the one who does good deeds such as prayer, fasting, etc., if his deeds are interspersed with good words and remembrance of God, then his deeds are more noble. So his statement, and righteous deeds elevate him, is an exhortation, a reminder, and an encouragement to do good deeds. As for the statements that are deeds in themselves, such as Tawheed and Tasbeeh, then they are acceptable. Ibn al-Arabi said: “If a person’s speech, mentioning God, is not accompanied by righteous deeds, it will not benefit him, because whoever’s actions contradict his words, then that will be a burden on him. The realization of this is that if an action is a condition for the acceptance of a statement or is connected to it, then it will not be accepted without it. If there is no condition, then his good words are recorded for him and his bad deeds are recorded against him, and a balance is made between them. Then God decides regarding victory, gain, and loss.” I say: What Ibn al-Arabi said is a realization. It appears that righteous deeds are a condition for the acceptance of good words. It is reported in the narrations that when a servant says, There is no god but God, with sincere intention, the angels look at his deeds. If the deeds are in accordance with his words, they will all ascend, but if their deeds contradict his deeds, his words will be suspended until he repents from his deeds. Based on this, righteous deeds raise good words to God, and the euphemism in raises refers to good words. This is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Shahr ibn Hawshab, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatadah, Abu al-Aaliyah, and al-Dahhak. The good words are Tawhid, which elevates good deeds, because good deeds are not accepted except with faith and Tawhid. And the good deed is raised by the good word, so the metaphor refers to the good deed. This statement was narrated on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: The good word is the Quran, and the good deed is raised by the Quran. It was also said: It refers to God, the Almighty, meaning that God raises the good deed over the good word, because the deed is the realization of the word, and the one who does it is more tired than the one who says it, and this is the reality of speech, because God is the one who raises and lowers. The second and first are metaphors, but they are permissible and valid. An-Nahhas said: The first statement is better and more correct because of the elevation of the one who said it, and it is more appropriate in Arabic because the reciters are based on raising the deed. Even if the meaning was: And the good deed is raised by God, or the good deed is raised by the good word, but choosing is half the deed. We do not know of anyone who read it in the accusative case to anything. It was narrated on the authority of Isa ibn Umar that he said: Some people read it, and the good deed is raised by God. It was also said: And the good deed is raised by its doer, and he is the one who meant honor and knew that it was sought from God, the Almighty. Al-Qushayri mentioned it. Second: It was mentioned to Ibn Abbas that a dog breaks the prayer, so he recited this verse: To Him ascends good speech, and righteous action raises it. This is an argument based on generality, according to the doctrine of the Salaf in saying that it is general. Prayer has its conditions, so nothing breaks it except by proof of what necessitates that, such as what it was concluded with from the Qur’an, Sunnah, or consensus. Those who held this view relied on the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): Prayer is broken by a woman, a donkey, and a black dog. So I said: O Abu Dharr, what is the difference between a black dog and a white dog and a red dog? He said: The black dog is a devil. Narrated by Muslim. What contradicts this is what Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ibn Shihab’s nephew that he asked his uncle about the prayer being interrupted by something. He said: Nothing interrupts it. Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr informed me that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to lie down and pray at night, and I would stand between him and the qiblah on his wife’s bed.” God the Almighty said: And those who plot evil deeds. At-Tabari mentioned in his book, Adab An-Nufus: Yunus ibn Abd Al-A’la told me: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab Al-Ash’ari, regarding God the Almighty’s saying: And those who plot evil deeds will have a severe punishment, and the plotting of those - it is they who will perish. He said: They are the people of hypocrisy, and this is the opinion of Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah. Abu Al-A’liyyah said: They are those who plotted against the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) when they gathered in Dar An-Nadwa. Al-Kalbi said: It means those who do evil deeds in this world, fighting, meaning polytheism, so the evil deeds are done. It is said: Bar Yabur if it is destroyed and invalidated. The market is Barat, meaning it is stagnant. From this: We seek refuge in God from the destruction of the widow. And His statement: And you were a people who were destroyed (al-Fath 48:12). Meaning they were destroyed. And deception: is what is done by way of deception and trickery. This has already been mentioned in Saba’.
35:11: The Almighty said: And God created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop. Sa'id said, on the authority of Qatada, who said: He means Adam, peace be upon him. The meaning of this is: He created your origin from dust. Then from a sperm-drop, he said: meaning that which He brought forth from the loins of your fathers. Then He made you mates, he said: meaning He pairs you with one another, so the male is the mate of the female to complete her life in this world until her term ends. And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge, meaning He made you mates, so the male marries the female and they reproduce with the knowledge of God. There is no pregnancy or birth except that God is aware of it, and nothing is outside His control. And no one lives long, nor does anything decrease from his lifespan except that it is in a book, He called him lived according to what he will become. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And no one lives long except that His age is written down, how many years it is, how many months it is, how many days it is, how many hours it is, then it is written in another book: a day is decreased from his lifespan, a month is decreased, a year is decreased, until his term is completed. Saeed bin Jubair also said: Whatever has passed of its term is what is missing, and whatever is to come is what will make it live longer. So the ha’ in this case is for the one who lives longer. Saeed also said: His age is written as such and such years, then he writes below that: A day has passed, two days have passed, until he reaches the end of it. Qatada said: The one who lives longer is the one who reaches sixty years of age, and the one whose age is missing is the one who dies before sixty years. Al-Farra’s view regarding the meaning of what is missing from a long-lived person is whatever is of his age and is not missing from his age in the sense of another long-lived person, meaning that the other does not missing from his age except in a book. So the metaphor in his lifespan refers to an end other than the first. He used the ha’ as a metaphor for it as if it were the first. Similar to it is your saying: I have a dirham and a half of it, meaning another half. It was said: God has decreed the lifespan of a person as one hundred years if he obeys, and ninety if he disobeys, so whichever of them he reaches is in a book. This is similar to what the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Whoever would like his provision to be expanded and his lifespan to be extended, let him maintain the ties of kinship. That is, it is written in the Preserved Tablet: So-and-so’s lifespan will be such and such years. If he maintains the ties of kinship, his lifespan will be increased by such and such years. This was explained elsewhere in the Preserved Tablet, that he will maintain the ties of kinship; whoever looks at the first one but not the second will think that it is an increase or a decrease. This meaning was previously mentioned in the statement of God, the Most High, God blots out what He wills and confirms 13:39. The metaphor in this refers to lifespan. It was also said that the meaning is and no one who is long-lived will be old, and no one will have his lifespan reduced except in a book, that is, by the decree of God, the Most High. This meaning was narrated from Ad-Dahhak and An-Nahhas preferred it, who said: It is most similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation. A similar version was narrated from Ibn Abbas. According to this, the ha may refer to the one who is long-lived, or it may refer to someone who is not long-lived. Indeed, that, for God, is easy means writing down deeds and lifespans, and it is not difficult for Him. The common reading is yanqs with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha on the qaf. A group of them read Ya'qub yanqis, with a fatha on the ya and a damma on the qaf, meaning nothing is subtracted from his lifespan. It is said: the thing decreased by itself and someone else decreased it, and it increased by itself and someone else increased it, transitive and intransitive. Al-A'raj and Al-Zuhri read it from 'umrah' with a light meem. The rest added a damma. They are two dialects like as-sahaq and as-sahaq. And yusra'i is a counting of long and short lives, nothing is difficult for Him nor is it hidden. The verb from it is yusra. If you name a person with it, it is declined because it is fa'il.
35:12: The Almighty's saying: "And the two seas are not alike. This is fresh and sweet." There are four issues: The first: Ibn Abbas said: Fresh is sweet, and bitter is bitter. Talhah read: This is salty and bitter, with a fatha on the meem and a kasra on the lam without an alif. As for salty, it is that in which salt is placed. Isa and Ibn Abi Ishaq read: His drink is like sayyid and mayyit. And from all of them you eat tender meat. There is no disagreement that it refers to both of them. This has been discussed previously in An-Nahl. Second: The Almighty’s saying: And you extract ornaments which you wear. Abu Ishaq’s school of thought is that ornaments are only extracted from salt, so it was said from them because they are mixed. Another said: Shells that contain ornaments are only extracted from pearls and other places that have fresh water and salt, such as springs, so it is taken from them because in the sea there are fresh water springs, and between them pearls emerge when they mix. It was also said: from the rain from the sky. Muhammad bin Yazid said a fourth opinion, he said: Ornaments are only extracted from salt. An-Nahhas: This is the best of them, but this is not according to him, because they are mixed, but they were combined and then He spoke about one of them, as the Almighty said: And out of His mercy He made for you the night and the day that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty (al-Qasas 28:73). And as you say: If you saw Al-Hasan and Al-Hajjaj, you would see good and evil. And as you say: If you saw Al-Asma’i and Sibawayh, you would fill your hand with language and grammar. He knew the meaning of this, and it is a very eloquent statement, so: And from all of them you eat tender meat and extract ornaments which you wear, so they came together in the first and salt was isolated in the second. Third: In His statement, and you wear it, there is evidence that the wearing of each thing is according to its condition. So a ring is placed on the finger, a bracelet on the arm, a necklace on the neck, and an anklet on the foot. In Al-Bukhari and Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said: I said to Ubaidah: Is spreading silk like wearing it? He said: Yes. In Al-Sahih, on the authority of Anas, I stood on a mat of ours that had turned black from being worn for so long. Fourth: The Almighty’s saying: And you will see the ships plowing through it. An-Nahhas said: meaning salt water in particular. If it were not for that, He would have said both. And the ship plows through the water. This has already been mentioned in Surat An-Nahl. That you may seek of His bounty. Mujahid said: Trade in the ship to distant lands in a short period of time, as mentioned in Surat Al-Baqarah. It was also said: what is extracted from its ornaments and what is caught from its fish. And perhaps you will be grateful for what He has given you of His bounty. It was also said: for what He saved you from its terror.
35:13: The Almighty says: He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night. This was mentioned previously in Al Imran and elsewhere. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. This was mentioned previously in Luqman. That is God, your Lord; to Him belongs the kingdom. That is, this is what is established from His creation. He is the Creator, the Controller, and the Able, the Powerful, so He is the One who is worshipped. And those you invoke besides Him means idols. They do not possess even a single husk. This is what most commentators said. The husk is the thin white shell between the fruit and the pit, this was said by Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abbas said: It is the split in the pit, and this is the preferred view of Al Mubarrad, and so was Qatadah. Qatadah also said: The husk is the cone on top of the pit. Al Jawhari said: It is also said that it is the white dot on the back of the pit, from which the palm tree grows.
35:14: God the Almighty says: If you call upon them, they do not hear your call. That is, if you seek their help in times of calamity, they will not hear your call, because they are inanimate objects that neither see nor hear. And if they heard, they would not respond to you, because not every hearer is capable of speaking. Qatadah said: The meaning is, If they heard, they would not benefit you. It was also said: If We gave them minds and life so that they heard your call, they would be more obedient to God than you, and they would not have responded to you despite their disbelief. And on the Day of Resurrection they will deny your association with God, that is, they will deny that you worshipped them and will disavow you. Then it is possible that this refers to those worshipped with reason, such as the angels, jinn, prophets, and devils, that is, they will deny that what you did was true, and that they commanded you to worship them, as He said about Jesus: It is not for me to say that which I have no right to. It is possible that idols are also included in this, meaning that God revives them until you know that they are not worthy of worship. And none informs you like the All-Aware is God Almighty, meaning that no one has informed you of God’s creation better than God, so no one can inform you like Him in His work.
35:15: God Almighty says: O mankind, you are those in need of God meaning those who are in need of Him for your survival and all your affairs. Al-Zamakhshari: “If you ask, why did He define the poor? I say: He meant by that that He showed them that they are the poor type due to their intense need for Him, even though all creatures are in need of Him, people and others, because poverty is something that follows weakness, and the weaker the poor person is, the poorer he is. God Almighty testified to man’s weakness in His statement, “And He created man weak,” and He said, God is He who created you from weakness. If it had been indefinite, the meaning would have been: You are some of the poor. If you say, The poor are contrasted with The Rich, then what is the benefit of The Praiseworthy? I say: Since He established their need for Him and His independence from them, and not every rich person is beneficial through his wealth unless the rich person is generous and benevolent. And if he is generous and benevolent, the one who is benevolent praises him and deserves their praise - He mentioned The Praiseworthy to indicate that He is the Rich One who benefits His creation through His wealth, the Generous One who is benevolent toward them, and who deserves their praise through His blessings upon them.” And lightening the second hamza is the best way according to Al-Khalil, and it is permissible to lighten the first one alone or to lighten both of them and make them complete. And God is the Rich, the Praiseworthy. "He" is redundant, so it has no syntactic position. It is a subject, so its position is nominative.
35:16: The Almighty’s saying: If He wills, He can take you away. There is an ellipsis in this, the meaning is: If He wills to take you away, He will take you away, i.e., He will annihilate you. And bring forth a new creation, i.e., one more obedient and purer than you.
35:17: And that is not difficult for God meaning it is impossible, difficult, and unattainable. This was mentioned previously in (Ibrahim).
35:18: We have already discussed this, but it is disconnected from what preceded it. The original form is (Tozar), the waw was deleted following the laser. Wazirah is an adjective for something deleted, i.e. a soul bearing burdens. And the same applies to And if a heavily laden woman calls to her burden Al-Farra’ said: i.e. a heavily laden soul or an animal. He said: This applies to both males and females. Al-Akhfash said: i.e. if a heavily laden woman calls a person to carry her burden, which is her sins. The burden is what is on the back, and the burden is the woman’s burden and the palm tree’s burden, Al-Kisa’i narrated them both with the fatha only. Ibn Al-Sikkit narrated that the palm tree’s burden is opened with the fatha or the kasra. Nothing from it is carried, even if he was a relative The interpretation, according to Al-Akhfash, is: Even if the person called was a relative. Al-Farra’ permitted it even if he was a relative. This is permissible according to Sibawayh, and similar to it is And if he was in hardship, then was means occurred, or the predicate is omitted, meaning, even if among those you are asking is in hardship. Sibawayh narrated: People will be rewarded according to their deeds, if good, then good, according to this. And good, then good, according to the first. It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that he said: I was told that a Jew or a Christian will see a Muslim man on the Day of Resurrection and say to him: Did I not extend a hand to you? Did I not treat you well? He will say: Yes. Then God will say: Benefit me. So the Muslim will continue to ask God the Most High until His punishment is reduced. And a man will come to his father on the Day of Resurrection and say: “Was I not dutiful to you, concerned for you, and kind to you? And you see what I am in. So grant me one of your good deeds, or bear a bad deed for me.” He will say: What you asked of me is easy, but I fear the same as you fear. And a father will say the same to his son, and he will respond with something similar to this. A man may say to his wife: Did I not treat you well? Please bear a sin for me so that I may be saved. She will say: That is easy, but I fear what you fear. Then Ikrimah recited: And if a heavily laden woman calls to her burden, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative. Al-Fudayl ibn Iyad said: It is a woman who meets her child and says: O my son, was not my belly a vessel for you? Was not my breast a drink for you? Was not my lap a cushion for you? He will say: Yes, O mother. She will say: O my son, my sins have weighed me down, so bear one sin for me. He will say: Leave me alone, O mother, for I am too busy with my sin to care for you. God the Almighty says: You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen. That is, only those who fear the punishment of God the Almighty will accept your warning. It is similar to His saying: You can only warn those who follow the message and fear the Most Merciful unseen. God Almighty says: And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for the benefit of himself. That is, whoever is guided only seeks guidance for the benefit of himself. It was also read: And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for the benefit of himself. “And to God is the final destination.” That is, to Him is the return of all creation.
35:19: The Almighty says: The blind and the seeing are not alike, meaning the disbeliever and the believer, the ignorant and the knowledgeable. Like: Say, ‘Not alike are the evil and the good.’
35:20: Nor darkness nor light Al-Akhfash Saeed said: (La) is redundant, and the meaning is neither darkness nor light, nor shade nor heat. Al-Akhfash said: Heat only occurs during the day, and the toxic heat occurs at night, and it was also said the opposite. Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajaj said: Like heat, it occurs only during the day, and the toxic heat occurs only at night, as narrated by al-Mahdawi. Al-Farra' said: The toxic heat only occurs during the day, and the heat occurs during both. An-Nahhas: This is more correct, because heat is a fa'ul form of heat, and it has the meaning of abundance, meaning harmful heat. I said: In Sahih Muslim, it was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Fire will say, ‘O Lord, some parts of me have consumed others, so permit me to breathe.’ So He permitted it two breaths: a breath in the winter and a breath in the summer. Whatever cold or bitter cold you find is from the breath of Hellfire, and whatever heat or bitter cold you find is from the breath of Hellfire.” It was narrated from the hadith of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Sa’id on the authority of Abu Hurairah: Whatever heat you find is from its poisonous winds, and the intense cold you find is from its bitter cold. This reconciles those sayings, and that the poisonous winds and the heat occur during the night and during the day, so reflect on it. It was said that what is meant by shade and heat is Paradise and Hellfire. Paradise has permanent shade, as God Almighty said: Its food is perpetual and so is its shade. And Hellfire has heat, and As-Suddi said its meaning. Ibn Abbas said: It means the shade of the night and the heat of the poisonous winds during the day. Qatrab: The heat is the heat, and the shade is the cold.
35:22: And the living are not alike to the dead. Ibn Qutaybah said: The living are the rational ones, and the dead are the ignorant ones. Qatadah said: All of these are examples, meaning just as these things are not alike, so too the disbeliever is not alike to the believer. Indeed, God makes hear whom He wills. That is, He makes hear His friends whom He created for His Paradise. And you cannot make hear those in the graves. That is, the disbelievers whose hearts have been killed by disbelief. That is, just as you cannot make hear those who have died, so too you cannot make hear those whose hearts have died. Al-Hasan, Isa Al-Thaqafi, and Amr ibn Maymun read: can make hear those in the graves without the tanween for ease, meaning they are like the people of the graves in that they do not benefit from what they hear nor do they accept it.
35:23: The Almighty says: You are only a warner, meaning a messenger who warns. You are only responsible for conveying the message. You do not have any responsibility for guidance. Guidance is in the hands of God, the Blessed and Exalted.
35:24: The Almighty says: Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. That is, as a bringer of good tidings of Paradise to those who obey Him, and a warner of Hell to those who disobey Him. And there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them. That is, a prophet had preceded them. Ibn Jurayj said: Except for the Arabs.
35:25: God the Almighty says: And if they deny you meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh. Then those before them denied their prophets, may God console the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Their messengers came to them with clear proofs meaning obvious miracles and clear laws. And with the scriptures meaning the written books. And with the enlightening book meaning the clear one.
