The scriptures and the book are repeated, and they are one and the same because of the difference in the two words. It is said that the clear proofs, the scriptures, and the book all come back to one meaning, which is the books that were sent down to the prophets.
35:26: Then I seized those who disbelieved, and how [awful] was My punishment. That is, how was My punishment for them. Warsh confirmed the ya' in (Nakyri) from Nafi' and Shaibah whenever it occurred in connection but not in pause. Ya'qub confirmed it in both cases, and the others omitted it in both cases. All of this has passed, and praise be to God.
35:27: The Almighty said: Have you not seen that God has sent down water from the sky? This vision is the heart and the teacher, meaning, has your knowledge not ended and you have seen with your heart that God has sent down? So (an), its subject and its predicate fill the place of the two objects of the vision. Then We brought forth thereby fruits is from the category of colouring speech. Of varying colours The word (Of varying) is in the accusative case as an attribute of (fruits). Of varying colours is in the nominative case with (Of varying colours), and it is suitable to be an attribute of (fruits)) because of what it was mentioned in. It is permissible to raise it in other than the Qur’an, and similarly I saw a man going out, his father. With it means with the water and it is one, and the fruits are different. And among the mountains are streaks of white and red, of varying colours "Al-Jadeed is the plural of Jadeed", which refers to paths of varying colours, even if they are all rocks or dust. Al-Akhfash said: If it was a new plural, he would have said: Jadda with a damma on the jim and the dal, like sireer and sirr. Zuhair said: As if he had dark cheeks and long locks, and he grazes naked after the summer. It was said: Al-Jawadid is the cutting, taken from jaddat something if you cut it, as narrated by Ibn Bahr. Al-Jawhari said: The jaddah is the line on the donkey’s back that differs from its color. The jaddah is the path, and the plural is jaddah. God Almighty said: And among the mountains are streaks white and red of varying colors meaning paths that differ from the color of the mountain. And from this is their saying: So-and-so rode jaddah from the matter, if he saw an opinion in it. And a renewed garment: it has different lines. Al-Zamakhshari: Al-Zuhri read (jaddad) with the dammah, the plural of jaddah, which is jaddah, it is said: jaddah, jaddad, and jada’id, like safinah, safun, and safan. And it was interpreted by the saying of Abu Dhu’ayb: John the Serpent has four braids. It was narrated from him that (jadda) with two fat-has, which is the clear, visible path. He put it in place of the clear paths and lines that are separated from each other.
35:28: And of people and beasts It was read: (and beasts) with a light pronunciation. Similar to this light pronunciation is the reading of those who read: (nor those who have gone astray) because each of them fled from the meeting of two sukoon, so the former moved the first of them, and this one deleted the last of them, as stated by Al-Zamakhshari. And the livestock are of varying colors meaning among them are red, white, black, and other than that, and all of that is evidence of a choosing Creator. He said: (of varying colors) so he mentioned the pronoun to take into account the (of), as stated by Al-Mu'arraj. Abu Bakr bin Ayyash said: The metaphor was mentioned because it is referred back to the implied (what), its meaning: And of people and beasts and livestock are those that are of varying colors, meaning white, red, and black. And black ravens Abu Ubaidah said: The raven is intense black, so there is an inversion in the speech, and the meaning is: And among the mountains are black ravens. The Arabs say about an extremely black color like a cal-Saff 61:Aswad gharibib. Al-Jawhari said: And you say this is aswad gharibib, meaning extremely black. And if you say qarabib aswad, you make aswad a substitute for qarabib because the emphasis on colors does not come first. In the hadith, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is said: ‘Indeed, God hates the old crow,” meaning the one who dyes his hair black. Imru’ al-Qais said: The eye is aspiring, the hand is swimming, the foot is scorching, and the face is strange Another one described his generosity: One of the wonders of God’s creation is a cave from which seafarers and otters are squeezed. Likewise here is the end of the statement, meaning likewise the states of the servants differ in fear, then he resumed and said: "Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Forgiving." He means by the scholars those who fear His power. Whoever knows that He, the Almighty and Majestic, is certain of His punishment for disobedience, as Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge. He said: Those who know that God has power over all things. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: Whoever does not fear God, the Almighty, is not a scholar. Mujahid said: The scholar is he who fears God, the Almighty. Ibn Mas'ud narrated: The fear of God is sufficient as knowledge, and being deceived is sufficient as ignorance. Sa'd ibn Ibrahim was asked: Who is the most knowledgeable of the people of Madinah? He said: The most pious of them to his Lord, the Almighty. Mujahid said: The scholar is he who fears God, the Almighty. On the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him, who said: “The true jurist is he who does not make people despair of God’s mercy, nor does he allow them to commit sins against God, nor does he make them feel secure from God’s punishment, nor does he abandon the Qur’an out of a desire for something else. There is no good in worship without knowledge, nor in knowledge without understanding, nor in recitation without contemplation.” Ad-Darimi Abu Muhammad narrated on the authority of Makhul who said: “The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: ‘The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like my superiority over the least of you - then he recited this verse - ‘Only those fear God, from among His servants, who have knowledge.’ God, His angels, the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, and the letter ‘nun’ in the sea send blessings on those who teach people good.’” The report is mursal. Ad-Darimi said: Abu An-Nu'man told me, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Hazim, who said: My paternal uncle Jarir bin Zaid told me that he heard Tubba' narrating on the authority of Ka'b, who said: "I find the description of a people who learn for no purpose, and who acquire jurisprudence for no purpose, and who seek this world through the work of the Hereafter, and who wear sheepskins. Their hearts are more bitter than aloes. They are deceived by Me and deceived by Me. I swear by Me that I will bring them a trial that will leave the forbearing among them bewildered." At-Tirmidhi narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, on the authority of Abu Ad-Darda', and we have mentioned it in the introduction to the book. Az-Zamakhshari: If you say: What is the rationale for the reading of those who read Only those who fear God in the nominative case, Among His servants who have knowledge in the accusative case, and that is 'Umar bin 'Abd Al-'Aziz, and it is narrated from Abu Hanifa? I say: The fear in this reading is a metaphor, and the meaning is: He only respects and honors them as He respects and honors the one who is awe-inspiring among men from among all of His servants. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Forgiving. This is an explanation for the necessity of fear, as it indicates the punishment and subjugation of the disobedient, and the reward and forgiveness of the obedient. The one who punishes and the one who rewards have the right to be feared.
35:29: The Almighty says: Indeed, those who recite the Book of God and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly. This is a verse for the readers, the workers, the scholars who establish the obligatory and voluntary prayers, and the same applies to spending. The characteristics that the reader of the Quran should have were mentioned in the introduction to the book. They hope for a commerce that will never fail. Ahmad ibn Yahya said: The predicate of indeed is they hope. "And He will increase them from His bounty." It was said that the increase is intercession in the Hereafter. This is similar to the other verse: "Men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from remembrance - to the words - And He will increase them from His bounty." And His statement at the end of Surat An-Nisa': "But as for those who have believed and done righteous deeds, He will pay them in full their rewards and increase them from His bounty." And there we explained it. "He is Forgiving" of sins. "Appreciative" - He accepts even a little sincere work and rewards it abundantly.
35:30: "That He may give them their reward in full and increase them from His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative."
35:31: God Almighty says: And that which We have revealed to you of the Book meaning the Qur’an. It is the truth confirming what was before it meaning of the books. Indeed, God is Knowing and Seeing of His servants.
35:32: It contains four issues: First: This verse is problematic because God the Almighty said: We have chosen from among Our servants, then He said: And among them is he who wrongs himself. Scholars from the Companions, the Followers, and those who came after them have spoken about this. An-Nahhas said: “The most authentic narration on this matter is what was narrated from Ibn Abbas: (And among them is he who wrongs himself) He said: The disbeliever. Ibn Uyaynah narrated it from Amr ibn Dinar from Ata’ also from Ibn Abbas. And from Ibn Abbas also: (And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds) He said: Two groups will be saved. The Arabic interpretation would be: Among them are those from among Our servants who are wrongful to themselves, meaning disbelievers. It is said: Al-Hasan means: immoral. The pronoun in (they enter it) refers to the moderate and the foremost, not the wrongdoer. It was narrated from Ikrimah, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and Al-Farra’ that the moderate is the disobedient believer, and the foremost is the pious in general. They said: This verse is similar to God’s statement in Surat al-Waqi’ah 56:“And you were three groups.” They said: It is unlikely that among those chosen would be a wrongdoer. Mujahid narrated from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid said: (And among them is he who wrongs himself) the people on the left, (And among them is he who is moderate) the people on the right, (And among them is he who is foremost in good deeds) the foremost among all people. It was said that the pronoun in (will enter it) refers to the three categories, provided that the wrongdoer here is neither a disbeliever nor a sinner. Among those from whom this statement was narrated are Umar, Uthman, Abu Darda, Ibn Masoud, Uqbah ibn Amr, and Aisha. The meaning according to this statement is: Where would the wrongdoer be who committed minor sins? And the moderate - Muhammad ibn Yazid said: He is the one who gives this world its due and the Hereafter its due, so (Gardens of Eden which they will enter) refers to everyone according to this explanation and clarification. It was narrated from Abu Saeed Al-Khudri. Kaab Al-Ahbar said: Their shoulders will be level - by the Lord of the Kaaba - and they will excel in their deeds. Abu Ishaq and Al-Subai’i said: As for what I heard sixty years ago, all of them will be saved. Usamah ibn Zayd narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) recited this verse and said: All of them are in Paradise. Umar ibn al-Khattab recited this verse and then said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘The foremost among us will be forerunners, the moderate among us will be saved, and the wrongdoer among us will be forgiven.’” According to this statement, the object of selection in the phrase, We gave the Book as an inheritance to those We have chosen of Our servants, is understood to be a noun phrase that was omitted just as the noun phrase was omitted in And ask the town, meaning, We chose their religion. What remains is, We chose them. The pronoun referring to the relative pronoun was omitted just as it was omitted in the phrase, And I do not say to those whom your eyes despise, meaning, you look down on them. So selection is directed to their religion, as God the Most High said, Indeed, God has chosen for you this religion. An-Nahhas said: A third statement is that the wrongdoer is the one who commits major sins, and the moderate one is the one who does not deserve Paradise because his good deeds outweigh his bad deeds. So, Gardens of Eden which they will enter is for those who preceded with good deeds and nothing else. This is the opinion of a group of people of insight, because the pronoun in reality is more appropriate for what follows it. I said: The middle opinion is better and more correct, God willing, because the disbeliever and the hypocrite were not chosen by God’s praise, nor was their religion chosen. This is the opinion of six of the Companions, and that is enough for you. We will further clarify and explain it in the rest of the verse. Second: The Almighty’s statement: We have inherited the Book, meaning, We gave it. Inheritance can be a literal or metaphorical gift, as it is said about what a person receives after the death of another. The Book here refers to the meanings of the Book, its knowledge, its rulings, and its beliefs. It is as if when God, the Almighty, gave the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, the Qur’an, which contains the meanings of the revealed books, it is as if He inherited the Book that was among the nations before us to the nation of Muhammad. We have chosen means, We have selected. It is derived from safw, which means being free from impurities and turbidity. Its root is atfuna, but the ta was replaced with a ta and the waw with a ya. “Of Our servants” It was said that what is meant is the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, as Ibn Abbas and others said. The wording could have included all believers from every nation, except that the phrase inheriting the Book was only for the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and the first did not inherit it. It was said: The chosen prophets inherited the Book, meaning that it was passed from one of them to another. God the Almighty said: And Solomon inherited David, and He said: He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob. So if it is permissible for prophethood to be inherited, then so is the Book. And among them are those who wrong themselves is someone who commits a minor sin. Ibn Atiyyah said: This is a rejected statement for more than one reason. Ad-Dahhak said: The meaning of And among them are those who wrong themselves is that among their descendants is someone who wrongs himself, namely the polytheist. Al-Hasan: From their nations, based on what was previously mentioned about the disagreement over the wrongdoer. The verse is about the nation of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him. The expressions of the masters of hearts differed regarding the wrongdoer, the moderate, and the foremost. Sahl ibn Abdullah said: The foremost is the knowledgeable one, the moderate one is the learner, and the wrongdoer is the ignorant one. Dhu al-Nun al-Misri said: The wrongdoer is the one who remembers God with his tongue only, the moderate one is the one who remembers Him with his heart, and the foremost is the one who does not forget Him. Al-Antaki said: The wrongdoer is the one who says words, the moderate one is the one who does deeds, and the foremost one is the one who states conditions. Ibn Ata' said: The oppressor is the one who loves God for the sake of this world, the moderate is the one who loves Him for the sake of the Hereafter, and the foremost is the one who abandons his desire for the desire of the Truth. It was also said: The oppressor is the one who worships God out of fear of the Fire, the moderate is the one who worships God out of hope for Paradise, and the foremost is the one who worships God for His sake and not for a reason. It was also said: The oppressor is the one who has no interest in this world because he has wronged himself and left it a portion, which is knowledge and love. The moderate is the one who knows, and the foremost is the one who loves. It was also said: The oppressor is the one who frets when afflicted, the moderate is the one who is patient in the face of affliction, and the foremost is the one who takes pleasure in affliction. It was also said: The oppressor is the one who worships God out of heedlessness and habit, the moderate is the one who worships Him out of desire and fear, and the foremost is the one who worships Him out of awe. It was also said: The oppressor is the one who is given and then withheld, the moderate is the one who is given and gives generously, and the foremost is the one who withheld, then is grateful and prefers. It is narrated that two worshippers met, and he said: How are your brothers in Basra? He said: "Good. If they are given, they are grateful, and if they are denied, they are patient." He said: This is the condition of dogs in Balkh! If our servants are denied, they are grateful, and if they are given, they prefer others. It was also said: The oppressor is the one who is content with his wealth, the moderate is the one who is content with his religion, and the foremost is the one who is content with his Lord. It was also said: The oppressor is the one who recites the Quran but does not act upon it, the moderate is the one who recites the Quran and acts upon it, and the foremost is the one who recites the Quran, knows it, and acts upon it. It was also said: The foremost is the one who enters the mosque before the call to prayer, the moderate is the one who enters the mosque after the call to prayer has been made, and the oppressor is the one who enters the mosque after the Iqamah has been established, because he has wronged himself in attaining the reward and does not attain what others attain. Some of the people of knowledge said about this: Rather, the foremost is the one who catches up with the time and the congregational prayer, thus attaining the two virtues, and the moderate is the one who does not waste his time if he misses the congregational prayer, and the oppressor is the one who is heedless of the prayer until the time and the congregation are missed, so he is more deserving of oppression. It was also said: The oppressor is the one who loves himself, the moderate is the one who loves his religion, and the foremost is the one who loves his Lord. It was said: The oppressor is the one who is fair but does not act justly, the moderate is the one who is fair and acts justly, and the foremost is the one who is fair but does not act justly. Aisha may God be pleased with her said: The foremost is the one who converted to Islam before the migration. The moderate is the one who converted to Islam after the migration, and the oppressor is the one who did not convert to Islam except by the sword, and they are all forgiven. I said: Al-Tha'labi mentioned these sayings and added to them in his interpretation. In short, they are two extremes and a middle ground, which is the moderate one who adheres to the middle path, which is avoiding inclination. From this is the saying of Jabir ibn Hani al-Taghlabi: We give the kings peace as long as they intend for us, and we do not have to kill them for a forbidden reason. That is, We give them peace as long as they do not commit injustice towards us. It is not forbidden for us to kill them if they commit injustice. Therefore, the moderate person is in a position between the two positions, so he is above the one who wrongs himself and below the one who is foremost in good deeds. That is the great bounty, meaning that We gave them the Book. It was said: This selection, despite our knowledge of their faults, is a great blessing. It was also said: The promise of Paradise to these three is a great blessing. Third: People have spoken about mentioning the oppressor before the moderate and the foremost. It has been said that mentioning him first does not imply honor, like the saying of God the Almighty: The companions of the Fire are not equal to the companions of Paradise. It has also been said that the oppressor was mentioned first because of the large number of wicked people among them and their dominance, and that the moderate are few in comparison to them, and the foremost are even fewer. Al-Zamakhshari mentioned this, but no one else did. It has also been said that the oppressor was mentioned first to emphasize hope in his case, as he has nothing to rely on except the mercy of his Lord. The moderate person relies on his good opinion, and the foremost person is in his obedience. It has also been said that the oppressor was mentioned first so that he would not despair of the mercy of God, and the foremost person was kept last so that he would not become conceited about his deeds. Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sadiq may God be pleased with him said: He mentioned the oppressor first to indicate that one cannot draw closer to Him except through His mercy and generosity, and that oppression does not affect one's being chosen if there is care. Then He mentioned the moderate ones because they are between fear and hope. Then He concluded with the foremost ones so that no one feels safe from God's deception, and all of them are in Paradise by virtue of the sanctity of the word of sincerity: There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God. Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tirmidhi said: He gathered them together in the category of being chosen, to remove the reasons for giving, because choosing necessitates inheritance, not inheritance necessitates choosing. Therefore, it was said in the wisdom: Correct the lineage then claim it in the inheritance. It was also said: He mentioned the foremost ones last so that they would be closer to Paradise and reward, just as He mentioned monasteries and churches before mosques in Surat al-Hajj, so that monasteries would be closer to demolition and ruin, and mosques would be closer to the remembrance of God. It was said: When kings wanted to combine things by mentioning, they would present the lower, like the Almighty’s saying: He is swift in penalty, and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful. And His saying: He gives to whom He wills females and He gives to whom He wills males. And His saying: The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. I said: He who said it well said: The ultimate goal of this generosity is you, and it will ultimately lead to the ultimate goal.
35:33: Fourth: His statement: Gardens of Eden, which they will enter. He has grouped them in entering because it is an inheritance. The disobedient and the obedient are equal in inheritance if they acknowledge the lineage. The disobedient and the obedient are both equal to the Lord. It was also read: (Garden of Eden) in the singular, as if it were a garden specific to those who came before due to their small number, as mentioned above. And (Gardens of Eden) is in the accusative case with an implied verb that is explained by the apparent meaning, meaning they will enter Gardens of Eden, they will enter them. This is for all, and it is correct, God willing. Abu Amr read (they will enter it) with a damma on the ya and a fatha on the kha. He said: because of His statement: (they will be adorned). The discussion of God Almighty’s statement: {They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein will be silk} has already been discussed in (Al-Hajj)
35:34: And they said, 'Praise be to God, who has taken away from us sorrow.' Abu Thabit said, "A man entered the mosque and said, 'O God, have mercy on my loneliness, be comforted by my solitude, and make for me a righteous companion.' Abu Darda' said, 'If you are truthful, then I am happier with that than you. I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say, "Then We gave the Book as an inheritance to those We have chosen of Our servants. And among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds.' He said, Then this forerunner will come and enter Paradise without being brought to account. As for the moderate, he will be brought to account with an easy reckoning. As for the one who wrongs himself, he will be detained in the place where he will be rebuked and reprimanded, then he will enter Paradise. They are the ones who said, 'Praise be to God, who has taken away from us sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative.' - until His saying, and no weariness will touch us therein." It was said that it is what is taken from him in his place, meaning it is expiated for him by what befalls him of worry and sorrow. From this is the saying of God, the Most High, 'Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it,' meaning in this world." Al-Tha’labi said: This interpretation is more similar to the apparent meaning, because he said: Gardens of Eden which they will enter, and because he said: Those whom We have chosen from among Our servants, and the disbeliever and the hypocrite were not chosen. I said: This is correct. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The example of a hypocrite who recites the Qur’an is like that of basil, its fragrance is pleasant but its taste is bitter. So he informed us that the hypocrite recites it, and God, the Most High, informed us that the hypocrite will be in the lowest level of Hellfire. Many of the infidels, Jews, and Christians recite it in our time. Malik said: One who has no good in him may recite the Qur’an. Nasb means fatigue. Laghub means exhaustion.
35:35: "He who has settled us in the home of permanence by His grace. No toil will touch us therein, nor will weariness touch us therein."
35:36: The Almighty says: And for those who disbelieve is the fire of Hell. After mentioning the people of Paradise, their conditions and their words, He also mentioned the people of Hell, their conditions and their words. Its punishment will not be reduced for them so that they die is like: He will neither die therein nor live. "And its torment will not be lightened for them" is like: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins so that they may taste the punishment. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful person" meaning a disbeliever in God and His Messenger. Al-Hasan read "في يامموتونwith the letterَفنnūn, but in that case the negation would not have an answer, andفي يامموتونwould be in apposition toيحَِْا"يحَِْاmeaning they will not be allowed to die, like the Almighty's saying: "And they will not be given permission to make excuses." Al-Kisa'i said: "And they will not be given permission to make excuses is with the letterَفنin the Qur'an because it is the beginning of a verse, and Its punishment will not be reduced for them so that they die" is because it is not the beginning of a verse. What is permissible for each of them is permissible for the other.
35:37: And they will cry out therein meaning they will cry out in the fire with loud voices. Screaming is a loud voice, and the one who cries out is the one who seeks help, and the one who cries out is the one who seeks assistance. He said: Whenever a screaming, terrified person came to us, the screaming would be like the banging of pipes. Our Lord, bring us out meaning they will say, Our Lord, bring us out of Hell and return us to this world. "We will do righteousness." Ibn Abbas said: It was transmitted: There is no god but God. This is the meaning of their saying, "other than what we used to do," meaning polytheism, meaning we will believe instead of disbelief, and obey instead of disobeying, and we will comply with the commands of the Messengers. "Have We not given you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember?" This is the answer to their prayer, meaning it will be said to them: So the statement is implied. Al-Bukhari included a chapter entitled: (Chapter: Whoever reaches the age of sixty, God has excused him regarding his age, based on the saying of God, the Almighty: "Have We not given you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember, and a warner has come to you?" meaning gray hair). Abd al-Salam ibn Mutahhar narrated to us, saying, Umar ibn Ali narrated to us, saying, Ma'n ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari narrated to us, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: "God excuses a person whose life span is delayed until he reaches sixty years of age." Al-Khattabi said: He has been excused means he has reached the maximum excuse. This is similar to their saying: He who warns is excused, meaning he has established an excuse for himself in presenting his warning. The meaning is that whoever God gives a life of sixty years has no excuse left, because sixty is close to the arena of death. It is the age of repentance, humility, awaiting death and meeting God. Thus, in it there is excuse after excuse. The first is with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the two deaths are at forty and sixty. Ali, Ibn Abbas and Abu Hurairah said in their interpretation of the verse {And have We not given you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember therein?}: that it is sixty years. It has been narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said in his sermon: “And those who preceded in warning have been most lenient in excuse. And a crier from God will call out at the age of sixty: ‘Have We not given you life long enough for whoever would remember to remember? And there has come to you a warner.’” Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim narrated from Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah from Ibn Abbas that he said: “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: ‘When the Day of Resurrection comes, the call will be made to the sixty-year-olds, which is the age of which God said: “Did We not give you life long enough for whoever would remember therein to remember?”’” It was also narrated from Ibn Abbas that it is forty years. Al-Hasan al-Basri and Masruq said something similar. This statement also has a point, and it is the correct one, and the proof for it is the statement of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Until, when he reaches his full strength and reaches forty years (al-Baqarah 2:17). At forty, reason reaches its peak, and what comes before and after that is deficient in it, and God knows best. Malik said: I met the people of knowledge in our country seeking worldly life and knowledge and mingling with people, until one of them reached forty years of age. When that age came, they would isolate themselves from people and occupy themselves with the Resurrection until death came to them. This meaning has already been mentioned in Surah al-A’raf. Ibn Majah narrated from Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The life spans of my ummah will be between sixty and seventy, and the fewest of them are those who live beyond that. God the Almighty said: And a warner has come to you, so taste [the punishment]. It was also read: And a warner has come to you. There is disagreement over it. Some say it means the Qur’an. Others say it means the Messenger, as stated by Zayd ibn Ali and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, Sufyan, Wakee’, Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl, Al-Farra’ and Al-Tabari said: It is gray hair. It was also said: A warner is a fever. It was also said: The death of family and relatives. It was also said: The perfection of reason. Warner means warning. I said: Gray hair, fever, and the death of family members are all warnings of death. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: Fever is the herald of death. Al-Azhari said: What it means is that fever is the messenger of death, as if it senses its arrival and warns of its coming. Gray hair is also a warning because it comes at the age of maturity, and it is a sign of leaving the age of youth, which is the age of play and amusement. He said: I saw gray hair as a warning of death to its owner, and you are enough of a warning Another said: I told her that gray hair is a harbinger of my life, and I am not a black-faced harbinger. As for the death of family, relatives, friends and brothers, it is a warning of departure at all times and places. He said: I see you carrying them and not returning them, as if I have carried you and not returned them Another said: Death spreads the shroud every now and then, and we are oblivious to what is intended for us. As for the perfection of the mind, through it one knows the truth of things and distinguishes between good and bad deeds. The wise person works for his hereafter and desires what is with his Lord, so he is a warner. As for Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, God sent him as a bearer of good tidings and a warner to His servants, to cut off their arguments. God the Most High said: So that mankind will have no plea against God after the messengers. And He said: And We never punish until We have sent a Messenger. God the Most High said: So taste meaning the punishment of Hell, because you did not consider and take heed. For the wrongdoers have no helper meaning anyone who can protect them from God’s punishment.
35:38: God Almighty says: “Indeed, God knows the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.” Its meaning was mentioned in more than one place. The meaning is: He knew that if He returned you to the world, you would not do righteous deeds, as He said: And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden. If knower is without a tanween, it can be for the past or future tenses, but if it is with a tanween, it cannot be for the past.
35:39: The Almighty says: It is He who has made you successors upon the earth. Qatada said: One successor after another, one generation after another. The successor is the one who follows the one who preceded him. That is why it was said to Abu Bakr: O successor of God? He said: “I am not the successor of God, but I am the successor of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I am satisfied with that.” But whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief, meaning the recompense for his disbelief, which is punishment and torment. And disbelief does not increase the disbelievers except in loss, meaning destruction and misguidance.
35:40: God the Almighty says: "Say: Have you seen your partners whom you invoke?" Your partners is in the accusative case due to seeing, and it is not permissible to raise it. However, raising it may be permissible according to Sibawayh in their saying: I know Zayd, whose father is he? Because Zayd is in the sense that someone is asking about him. And if I had said: Have you seen Zayd, whose father is he? The raising would not be permissible. The difference between them is that the meaning of this is: Tell me about him. Similarly, the meaning of this is: Tell me about your partners whom you invoke besides God. Did you worship them because they have a share in the creation of the heavens, or did they create anything on the earth? Or have We given them a Scripture? That is, do they have a Scripture which We revealed to them regarding their partnership? This was a refutation of those who worshipped other than God the Almighty, because they did not find in any of the scriptures that God the Almighty commanded that anyone be worshipped other than Him. So they are on clear proof thereof. Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamzah, and Hafs from Asim read on clear proof with the singular form, and the rest pluralized it. The two meanings are close, except that the plural reading is better, because whoever reads it as on clear proof is either going against the majority, or he has come with it according to the language of someone who said: Talhat came to me, so he stopped with the ta’, and this is a rare and irregular language, as stated by An-Nahhas. Abu Hatim and Abu Ubaid said: The plural reading is better because it matches the script, because in the copy of Uthman it is bayyinat with the alif and the ta’. Rather, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion. That is, falsehoods that deceive. This is what the nobles say to the lowly: These gods will benefit you and bring you closer. It was also said that Satan promises the polytheists this. It was also said that he promises them that they will be victorious over them.
35:41: His statement, the Most High: Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist. After He explained that their gods are unable to create anything of the heavens and the earth, He explained that their Creator and Sustainer is God. Thus, nothing comes into existence except through His creation, and nothing remains except through His preservation. The word that is in the accusative case, meaning that it is disliked that they cease to exist, or lest they cease to exist. Or it can be interpreted in this sense, because the meaning is that God prevents the heavens and the earth from disappearing. Thus, there is no need to omit an implied word. This is the statement of Al-Zajjaj. And if they were to cease, no one could hold them back after Him. Al-Farra' said: That is, if they were to cease, no one could hold them back. The word that means what. He said: It is similar to His statement: And if We send a wind and they see it yellow, they will continue, after that, to disbelieve. It was said that what is meant is their disappearance on the Day of Resurrection. On the authority of Ibrahim, he said: A man from the companions of Ibn Masoud entered upon Ka’b al-Ahbar to learn knowledge from him. When he returned, Ibn Masoud said to him: What have you learned from Ka’b? He said: I heard Ka’b say: The heaven revolves on a pole like the pole of a millstone, on a column on the shoulder of an angel. Abdullah said to him: I wish you had turned back with your mount and its saddle. Ka’b lied. He did not abandon his Jewishness! God the Almighty says: (Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist) The heavens do not rotate, and if they did rotate, they would have ceased to exist. A similar hadith was narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said to a man coming from Syria: Who did you meet with? He said: Ka’b. He said: What did you hear him say? He said: I heard him say: The heavens are on the shoulder of an angel. Ka’b said: Ka’b lied. Has he not abandoned his Jewishness yet? God the Almighty says: (Indeed, God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist), and the heavens are seven and the earths are seven, but when He mentioned them, He treated them as two things, so the metaphor returned to them. It is like His saying: {The heavens and the earth were a joined entity, then We separated them}, then He concluded the verse by saying: {Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving}, because the meaning, as some of the people of interpretation mentioned, is that God holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease to exist because of the disbelief of the disbelievers, and their saying that God has taken a son. Al-Kalbi said: When the Jews said, Ezra is the son of God, and the Christians said, The Messiah is the son of God, the heavens and the earth were about to cease to exist, so God prevented them and revealed this verse about him. It is like His saying, the Almighty: {You have certainly done a thing monstrous * The heavens almost burst from it}, the verse.
35:42: The Almighty said: And they swore by God with their most solemn oaths that if a warner came to them They are the Quraysh who swore before God sent His Messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, when they heard that the People of the Book had denied their messengers, so they cursed whoever among them had denied His prophet, and they swore by God, may His name be glorified, that if a warner came to them meaning a prophet, they would surely be better guided than any of the nations meaning those who denied the messengers from the People of the Book. The Arabs wished that there would be a messenger from among them just as there were messengers from among the Children of Israel, but when what they wished for came to them, which was a warner from among themselves, they turned away from him and did not believe in him.
35:43: Arrogance means they were stubborn about faith. And the plotting of evil means the plotting of evil deeds, which is disbelief and deceiving the weak, and turning them away from faith so that their numbers would increase. The feminine form of min ahad al-umam is used to feminize ummah, as Al-Akhfash said. Hamzah and Al-Akhfash read and the plotting of evil, but the plotting of evil does not encompass, so they omitted the i'rab from the first and kept it in the second. Al-Zajjaj said: It is a mistake, and it only became a mistake because the i'rab was omitted from it. Al-Mubarrad claimed that it is not permissible in speech or poetry, because the vowel marks of i'rab cannot be omitted, as they were introduced to differentiate between meanings. Some grammarians were shocked that Al-A'mash, despite his great stature and position, would read it like this. He said: He only paused on it, so whoever recited it on his behalf was mistaken. He said: The evidence for this is that it is the complete sentence, and since the second was not the complete sentence, it was parsed by agreement, and the vowel in the second is heavier than in the first because it is a damma between two kasras. Some grammarians have cited the words of Sibawayh as evidence for Hamza in this regard, and that he and others recited: If they are crooked, I say they are the companions of the people The other said: Today I drink, not committing any sin against God, nor committing any sin. This is not an argument, because Sibawayh did not permit it, but rather he narrated it from some grammarians. And if a hadith is attributed to some scholars, then there is no argument in it, so how can it be, since it was only brought as an anomaly and due to poetic necessity, and it was contradicted. Al-Zajjaj claimed that Abu al-Abbas recited: If they are crooked, I say, People shouted. And he recited: Today I drink undeservedly By connecting the alif to the command, all of them were mentioned by An-Nahhas. Az-Zamakhshari: Hamzah read (and the plot of the evil) with a sukoon on the hamzah, due to the weight of the vowels, and perhaps he stole and thought it was a sukoon, or he paused briefly and then began (and does not encompass). Ibn Masoud read (and a bad plot). Al-Mahdawi said: And whoever sukoon the hamzah in his saying: and the plot of the evil then it is on the assumption of pausing on it, then he made the connection like a pause, or he sukoon the hamzah due to the succession of kasras and ya’s, as he said: Today I drink undeservedly Al-Qushayri said: Hamzah read (and the evil plot) with a sukoon on the hamzah, and some people made a mistake in this. Some people said: Perhaps he stopped at it because it is the end of the sentence, so the narrator made a mistake. This was narrated from him in the inclusion. We have previously discussed similar cases. We said: What is proven by widespread or continuous transmission that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) read it must be permissible, and it is not permissible to say that it is a mistake. Perhaps what was meant by those who made the mistake was that someone else was more eloquent than him, even if he was eloquent. And the evil plot does not encompass except its own people meaning that the consequences of polytheism do not befall anyone except those who associate others with God. It was said: This is a reference to their killing at Badr. The poet said: They pushed death away, so it became an arm's length after it had been encompassed by it. Any descent, and this is the saying of Qatrib. Al-Kalbi said: (Yahiq) means to surround. And the word Hawq means to surround. It is said: Haqqa bihu kanda meaning it surrounded him. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Ka’b said to him: “I find in the Torah: ‘Whoever digs a pit for his brother will fall into it.’ Ibn Abbas said: ‘Then I find that in the Qur’an.’ He said: ‘And where?’ He said: ‘Then read: ‘And evil plotting will not encompass except its own people.’” And in the proverbs of the Arabs: Whoever digs a pit for his brother will fall into it headlong. Al-Zuhri narrated that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not plot and do not help a plotter, for God says: ‘And evil plotting will not encompass except its own people.’ And do not seek or help a transgressor, for God says: ‘But whoever breaks his oath, it only breaks it to the detriment of his own soul.’” And God says: Your transgression is only against yourselves. Some of the wise men said: O you who are unjust in your actions, and injustice will be returned to the one who has been unjust How long will you count the misfortunes and forget the blessings? In the hadith: Deceit and trickery are in the Fire. His saying in the Fire means that in the Hereafter, their people will be cast into the Fire, because these are the characteristics of the disbelievers, not the characteristics of the good believers. That is why the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said in the context of this hadith: Deceit, trickery, and betrayal are not among the characteristics of the believer. In this is the most eloquent warning against adopting these reprehensible characteristics and deviating from the noble characteristics of faith. God the Almighty says: {Do they then await anything but the way of the former peoples?} That is, they are only awaiting the punishment that descended upon the first disbelievers. {And you will not find any change in the way of God, and you will not find any alteration in the way of God.} That is, God carried out the punishment upon the disbelievers, and made it a way for them. He punishes with the same punishment whoever deserves it. No one is able to change that, nor to transfer the punishment from himself to someone else. The way is the method, and the plural is sunan. It has been mentioned previously in Al Imran and He attributed it to God the Almighty. And He said in another place: {The way of those We sent before you of Our messengers.} So He attributed it to the people because the matter is connected to both sides, and it is like the term, sometimes it is attributed to God, and sometimes to the people. God the Almighty said: {Then the term of God is sure to come.} And He said: {And when their term comes.}
35:44: Between the Sunnah that He mentioned, that is, did they not see what We sent down upon Aad and Thamud, and upon Madyan and their likes when they denied the Messengers, so they pondered that by looking at their dwellings and homes, and by what they heard through continuous transmission of what happened to them, so is there not in it a lesson and clarification for them, they are not better than those nor stronger, rather those were stronger, the proof of which is His statement: And they were mightier than them in strength, and nothing in the heavens or on the earth could frustrate God. That is, if He wanted to send down a punishment upon a people, it would not frustrate Him. Indeed, He is All-Knowing, All-Powerful.
35:45: The Almighty said: And if God were to punish people for what they have earned meaning sins. He would not leave on the surface of the earth any creature Ibn Masoud said: He means all animals that creep and move. Qatada said: He did that during the time of Noah, peace be upon him. Al-Kalbi said: Of any creature means the jinn and humans, and not others, because they are charged with reason. Ibn Jarir, Al-Akhfash, and Al-Husayn ibn Al-Fadl said: He meant by creature here people alone and not others. I said: The first is more evident, because it is from a great companion. Ibn Masoud said: The dung beetle was almost tortured in its hole because of the sin of Adam’s son. Yahya ibn Abi Katheer said: A man enjoined what is right and forbade what is wrong, so a man said to him: Take care of yourself, for the oppressor only harms himself. Abu Hurairah said: You have lied? By God, besides Whom there is no god - then he said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the bustard dies of old age in its nest because of the oppression of the oppressor. Al-Thamali and Yahya ibn Salam said about this verse: God withholds the rain and everything perishes. Something similar to this has been mentioned in Surah Al-Baqarah from Ikrimah and Mujahid in the interpretation of and the cursers curse them: They are insects and animals who are afflicted with drought because of the sins of the evil scholars who conceal [the truth], so they curse them. We mentioned there the hadith of Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said about His statement: and the cursers curse them: The creatures of the earth. “But He delays them for a specified term.” Muqatil said: The specified term is what He promised them in the Preserved Tablet. Yahya said: It is the Day of Resurrection. For God is ever, over His servants i.e., over those among them who deserve punishment, Seeing. It is not permissible for the operator of if to be seeing, just as it is not permissible to say: Today, Zaid is outside. But the operator in it is came, because it resembles the letters of recompense, and the nouns with which recompense are acted upon by what comes after them. Sibawayh does not see recompense with if except in poetry, as he said: If our swords were short, our steps would reach our enemies and we would fight.
36:1: It is Meccan by consensus. It consists of eighty-three verses, except that a group said: The verse of God the Almighty: And We record what they have put forth and what they left behind (Ya-Sin 36:12) was revealed about Banu Salamah of the Ansar when they wanted to leave their homes and move near the mosque of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), as will be mentioned. In the book of Abu Dawud, it is narrated on the authority of Ma'qil ibn Yasar who said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Recite Ya Seen over your dead. Al-Ajurri mentioned, on the authority of Umm al-Darda', on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), who said: There is no dead person over whom Surah Ya Seen is recited except that God makes it easy for him. In Musnad al-Darimi, it is narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever recites Surah Ya Seen at night seeking the pleasure of God will be forgiven that night. Abu Nu'aym al-Hafiz also included it. Al-Tirmidhi narrated on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur’an is Yasin. Whoever recites Yasin, God will write for him, for reciting it, the reward of reciting the Qur’an ten times. He said: This is a strange hadith, and in its chain of transmission is Harun Abu Muhammad, an unknown sheikh. There is a hadith on this topic on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, but the hadith of Abu Bakr is not authentic because of its chain of transmission, and its chain of transmission is weak. On the authority of Aisha, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Indeed, in the Qur’an there is a surah that intercedes for its reciter and forgives its listener. It is Surah Yasin, which is called in the Torah the ‘Ma’ma’. It was said: ‘O Messenger of God, what is the ‘Ma’ma’?’ He said: ‘It provides its reciter with the good of this world and wards off from him the terrors of the Hereafter. It is called the ‘Daf’a’ and the ‘Qadi’. It was said: ‘O Messenger of God, how is that?’ He said: ‘It wards off all evil from its reciter and fulfills his every need. Whoever recites it, it will be equivalent to twenty Hajjs for him. Whoever hears it, it will be like a thousand dinars given in charity in the way of God. Whoever writes it and drinks it, it will put into his body a thousand medicines, a thousand lights, a thousand certainties, a thousand mercies, a thousand compassion, a thousand guidance, and it will remove from him every disease and malice.” Al-Tha’labi mentioned it from the hadith of Aisha, and at-Tirmidhi al-Hakim in Nawadir al-Usul from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, with a chain of transmission. In Musnad Al-Darimi, it is narrated on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab who said: Ibn Abbas said: Whoever recites Yasin in the morning will be given ease for the day until the evening. Whoever recites it at the beginning of the night will be given ease for the night until the morning. An-Nahhas narrated on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila who said: Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur’an is Yasin. Whoever recites it during the day will have his worries taken away, and whoever recites it at night will have his sins forgiven. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: The people of Paradise will only recite Ta-Ha and Yasin. Al-Marudi raised these three narrations and said: Ad-Dahhak narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Everything has a heart, and the heart of the Qur’an is Yasin. Whoever recites it at night will be given ease for that night, and whoever recites it during the day will be given ease for that day. The Qur’an will be lifted from the people of Paradise, and they will not recite anything except Ta-Ha and Yasin. Yahya ibn Abi Katheer said: I have been informed that whoever recites Surat Yasin at night will not cease to be happy until the morning, and whoever recites it in the morning will not cease to be happy until the evening. Someone who experienced it told me, mentioned by Al-Tha’labi and Ibn ‘Atiyyah. Ibn Atiyyah said: Experience confirms this. Al-Tirmidhi Al-Hakim mentioned in Nawader Al-Usul on the authority of Abd Al-A’la, who said: Muhammad bin Abi Al-Salt told us, on the authority of Umar bin Thabit, on the authority of Muhammad bin Marwan, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, who said: Whoever finds hardness in his heart, let him write Yasin in a cup with saffron and then drink it. My father, may God have mercy on him, told me: Asram bin Hawshab told us, on the authority of Baqiyyah bin Al-Waleed, on the authority of Al-Mu’tamir bin Ashraf, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Qur’an is better than everything besides God, and the superiority of the Qur’an over all other speech is like the superiority of God over His creation. So whoever respects the Qur’an has respected God, and whoever does not respect the Qur’an has not respected God. The sanctity of the Qur’an with God is like the sanctity of a parent over his child. The Quran is an intercessor whose intercession is accepted, and the intercessor whose intercession is believed. Whoever intercedes for the Quran, his intercession will be accepted, and whoever places the Quran in his presence, it will be believed. Whoever places it in front of him, it will lead him to Paradise, and whoever places it behind him, it will drive him to Hell. The bearers of the Quran are those who are surrounded by God’s mercy, clothed in God’s light, the teachers of the word of God. Whoever befriends them has befriended God, and whoever is hostile to them has been hostile to God. God the Almighty says: “O bearers of the Quran, respond to your Lord by respecting His Book. He will increase you in love and make you beloved to His servants. He will protect the listener of the Quran from the trials of this world and protect the reciter of the Quran from the trials of the Hereafter. Whoever listens to a verse from the Book of God will have a bounty from under the Throne to the borders. Indeed, in the Book of God there is a Surah called Al-Azizah, and its reciter will be called Al-Sharif on the Day of Resurrection. It will intercede for its reciter in more than Rabi’ah and Mudar, and it is Surah Yaseen.” Al-Tha’labi reported on the authority of Abu Hurairah that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Whoever recites Surah Yaseen on Friday night becomes forgiven. On the authority of Anas, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever enters the graveyard and recites Surat Yasin, God will make things easier for him on that day, and he will have good deeds equal to the number of its letters. God the Almighty says: Ya Seen There are several readings for Ya-Sin 36:The people of Medina and Al-Kisa'i read Ya Seen * By the Wise Qur'an by assimilating the letter nun into the letter waw. Abu Amr, Al-A'mash, and Hamza read Yasin by making the letter nun pronounced with a clear pronunciation. Isa ibn Umar read Yasin by making the letter nun nasb. Ibn Abbas, Ibn Abi Ishaq, and Nasr ibn Asim read Yasin with a kasra. Harun Al-A'war and Muhammad ibn Al-Sameeq read Yasin by making the letter nun damma. So these are five readings. The first reading is by assimilating as is required in Arabic, because the letter nun is assimilated into the letter waw. Among them is someone who said: The way of the letters of the alphabet is to stop on them, and assimilation only occurs in insertion. Sibawayh mentioned the nasb and made it from two aspects: One of them is that it is a direct object and not declined, because according to him it is a foreign name like Habil, and the meaning is: Remember Ya Seen. Sibawayh made it the name of the surah, and his other opinion is that it should be built on the fat-ha like kaifa and ayna. As for the kasra, Al-Farraa claimed that it is similar to the Arabs’ saying jir la af’ala, so based on this, yasan is an oath. Ibn Abbas said the same. It was also said that it is similar to ams, hizaam, these, and raqash. As for the damma, it is similar to mindh, wahayt, and qat, and to the singular vocative when you say ya rajul, for those who pause on it. Ibn Al-Sumaiq and Harun said that it has been mentioned in its interpretation ya rajul, so the damma is better for it. Ibn Al-Anbari said: Ya Seen is a good pause for those who say that it is the opening of the surah. Those who say that the meaning of Ya Seen is ya rajul did not pause on it. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas’ud, and others that it means ya human being. They said about the verse of God, “Peace be upon the family of Yasin” 37:130, that is, upon the family of Muhammad. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: It is one of the names of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and its evidence is Indeed, you are among the messengers. Al-Sayyid Al-Himyari said: O soul, do not test with advice, striving for affection, except for the family of Yasin. Abu Bakr Al-Warraq said: It means O master of mankind. It was said that it is one of the names of God, as stated by Malik. Ashhab narrated from him that he said: I asked him, Is it appropriate for someone to be called Yasin? He said: I do not think it is appropriate.
36:2: In the words of God: "Ya Seen. By the Wise Qur'an," He says, This is my name, Ya Seen. Ibn al-Arabi said, "This is a wonderful statement, because it is permissible for a servant to use a name from his Lord if it contains a meaning from Him, such as saying: All-Knowing, All-Powerful, All-Willing, and All-Speaking." Malik prohibited using the name Ya Seen because it is one of the names of God, the meaning of which is not known. Perhaps its meaning is unique to the Lord, so it is not permissible for a servant to use it before it. If it is said, God the Almighty said, "Peace be upon the family of Ya Seen," we say: This is written in alphabetical order, so it is permissible to use it as a name. This non-orthographical order is what Malik spoke about, because of the confusion in it, and God knows best. Some scholars said, "God opened this surah with the letters Ya and Seen, and in them is the sum of goodness. The opening indicates that it is the heart, and the heart is the commander over the body. Similarly, Ya Seen is the commander over all the surahs, encompassing the entire Qur'an." Then they differed about it again, so Saeed bin Jubair and Ikrimah said: It is in the language of Abyssinia. Al-Sha’bi said: It is in the language of Tayy. Al-Hasan: It is in the language of Kalb. Al-Kalbi: It is in Syriac, so the Arabs spoke it and it became part of their language. This meaning has already been mentioned in Taha and in the introduction to the book in full. Al-Qadi ‘Iyadh listed the sayings of the commentators about the meaning of Ya-Seen, so Abu Muhammad Makki narrated that “It was narrated that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I have ten names with my Lord.’” He mentioned that Ta-Ha and Ya-Seen are two of His names among them. I said: Al-Mawardi mentioned on the authority of Ali may God be pleased with him who said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: God the Almighty has named me seven names in the Qur’an: Muhammad, Ahmad, Ta-Ha, Ya-Seen, Al-Muzzammil, Al-Muddaththir, and Abdullah. Al-Qadi said this. Abu Abd al-Rahman Al-Sulami narrated on the authority of Ja’far Al-Sadiq that he meant, addressing his Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). On the authority of Ibn Abbas: Ya-Seen O man, meaning Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him). He said: It is an oath and it is one of the names of God, the Most High. Al-Zajjaj said: It was said that it means O Muhammad, and it was said O man, and it was said O man. Ibn Al-Hanafiyyah said: Ya-Seen, O Muhammad. Ka’b said: Ya-Seen is an oath by which God swore two thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. [He said: O Muhammad, you are indeed one of the messengers.] Then he said: And the Wise Qur’an. If it is understood that it is one of His names (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and it is authentically stated that it is an oath, then there is in it the glorification that was mentioned above, and the oath is confirmed by linking the other oath to it. If it was in the sense of calling, then another oath came after it to realize his message and testify to his guidance. God the Almighty swore by his name and his book that he is among those sent with his revelation to his servants, and on the straight path of his faith, i.e. a path in which there is no crookedness or deviation from the truth. Al-Naqqash said: God the Almighty did not swear to any of his prophets by the message in his book except for him, and in it is from his glorification and exaltation according to the interpretation of those who said, O Master, what is in it, “And he, peace be upon him, said: I am the master of the children of Adam,” his words end. Al-Qushayri narrated that Ibn Abbas said: The infidels of Quraysh said, You are not a messenger, and God did not send you to us. So God swore by the perfect Quran that Muhammad is among the messengers. And the Wise is perfect so that it is not exposed to falsehood and contradiction, as He said, He has perfected His verses (Hud 11:1). Likewise, He perfected its structure and meanings, so no flaw afflicts it. Al-Hakim may be with regard to God in the sense of perfect with a kasra on the kaf, like Al-Aleem in the sense of painful. On a straight path means the straight religion, which is Islam. Al-Zajjaj said: On the path of the prophets who came before you.
36:3: And he said: Indeed, you are among the messengers. The predicate of indeed.
36:4: And on a straight path is a second piece of report, meaning that you are indeed one of the messengers, and that you are indeed on a straight path. It was also said that the meaning is one of the messengers on righteousness, so his statement, on a straight path is a connection to the messengers, meaning that you are indeed one of the messengers who were sent on a straight path, like the statement of God Almighty: And indeed, you guide to a straight path * The path of God (al-Shura 42:52-53), meaning the path that God has commanded.
36:5: The Almighty’s saying: A revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful. Ibn ‘Amir, Hafs, Al-A’mash, Yahya, Hamzah, Al-Kisa’i, and Khalaf read: Tanzil with the lam in the accusative case as a verbal noun, meaning that God sent it down as a revelation. The verbal noun was added, so it became definite, like His saying: Then he struck the necks [Muhammad 4], meaning the striking of the necks. The rest read: Tanzil in the nominative case as a predicate of a deleted subject, meaning it is a revelation, or what was revealed to you is a revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful. This was also read: Tanzil in the genitive case as a substitute for the Qur’an, and Tanzil refers to the Qur’an. It was said: to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, meaning that you are one of the messengers, and that you are a revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful. So Tanzil in this case means sending, as God the Almighty said: God has sent down to you a reminder * A Messenger who recites (At-Talaq 65:10-11). It is also said: God sent the rain and sent it down with the same meaning. And Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, God’s mercy sent it down from the sky. And whoever is set up says: Indeed, you are among the messengers, a message from the Almighty, the Most Merciful. And the Almighty is the vengeful against those who disobey Him, the Most Merciful to those who obey Him.
36:6: The Almighty’s saying: That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned. Ma has no syntactic position according to most of the commentators, including Qatada, because it is a negation and the meaning is: That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned before you by a warner. It was also said that it has the meaning of who so the meaning is: That you may warn them as their fathers were warned, as Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and Qatada said. It was also said that Ma and the verb are a verbal noun, meaning that you may warn a people as their fathers were warned. Then it is possible that the Arabs were informed by continuous transmission of the report of the prophets, so the meaning is that they were not warned by the Messenger of God on their own. For a people who have not received the report of a prophet. God has said: And We have not given them any books to study, nor have We sent to them before you any warner. (Saba’ 34:44) And He has said: That you may warn a people to whom no warner came before you, that they may be guided. (Sajdah 32:3), meaning no prophet has come to them. According to the saying of those who say that the report of the prophets has reached them, the meaning is that they are now turning away and ignoring that, and the one who turns away from something is said to be unaware of it. It has also been said: They are unaware of God’s punishment.
36:7: God Almighty says: The word has come into effect upon most of them, meaning the punishment has become inevitable for most of them. So they do not believe in your warning. This applies to those whom God knew would die in their disbelief. Then He explained the reason for their abandoning faith.
36:8: Then he said: Indeed, We have placed shackles around their necks. It was said that this was revealed about Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and his two Makhzumi companions. Abu Jahl swore that if he saw Muhammad praying, he would smash his head with a stone. When he saw him, he went and raised a stone to throw it, but when he gestured to it, his hand returned to his neck and the stone stuck to his hand. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, and others. According to this, it is a metaphor, that is, he is like someone whose hand is shackled to his neck. When he returned to his companions, he told them what he had seen. The second man, who was Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, said: I will smash his head. So he came to him while he was praying in that state to throw the stone at him, but God blinded him, so he could hear his voice but not see him. He returned to his companions but did not see them until they called him. He said: By God, I did not see him, but I heard his voice. The third said: By God, I will smash his head. Then he took the stone and set off, staggering backward until he fell on his back unconscious. It was said to him, What is the matter with you? He said, “My matter is grave! I saw the man, and when I approached him, there was a stallion swaying his tail. I have never seen a stallion bigger than him. By al-Lat and al-‘Uzza, if I approached him, he would eat me.” Then God revealed, Indeed, We have placed around their necks shackles, reaching to their chins, so their heads are upturned. Ibn Abbas recited, Indeed, We have placed on their right hands. Al-Zajjaj said, And it was recited, ‘Indeed, We have placed in their hands.’ An-Nahhas said, This reading is an explanation, and it should not be recited in a way that contradicts the Qur’an. There is an omission in the speech according to the reading of the group, the estimation being, Indeed, We have placed around their necks and in their hands shackles, reaching to their chins. It is a metaphor for the hands, not the necks, and the Arabs omit such a word. Its equivalent is: {And garments that protect you from the heat} (al-Nahl 16:81). Its meaning is: {And garments that protect you from the cold}, but it was omitted because that which protects from the heat also protects from the cold. Because if the shackles are on the neck, they must also be on the hand, especially since God the Almighty said: {And they reach the chins}, so it is known that what is meant by it is the hands. {And they are raised with their heads bowed}, meaning they are raising their heads, unable to lower their heads, because whoever has his hands shackled to his chin, his head will be raised. Abdullah ibn Yahya narrated that Ali ibn Abi Talib may God be pleased with him showed them the iqmah, so he put his hands under his beard, stuck them together, and raised his head. An-Nahhas said: This is the most important narration about it, and it is taken from what Al-Asma’i related. He said: It is said: The animal iqmaht if you pull its reins to raise its head. An-Nahhas said: The qaf is replaced by the kaf because of its proximity to it. Just as it is said: I conquered him and I conquered him. Al-Asma’i said: It is said: The animal iqmaht if you pull its reins until its head is erect. And from this is the saying of the poet: And the head is covered It is said: akmāmahā, akfāḥā, and khabbātha. This one alone is without an alif, according to al-Asma’i. A camel is qāmah qamuhan: if it raises its head at the water tank and refuses to drink, so it is a qāmih and qāmih camel. It is said: he drank, then qāmih, and anqāmih, meaning if he raised his head and stopped drinking, satisfied. Your camels have qāmahāt: if they have come to the water and not drunk, and raised their heads due to an illness they have or a cold. They are qāmahā camels, a muqāmih camel, and a muqāmih female camel as well, and the plural is qāmah, not according to analogy. Bishr said, describing a ship: We sit on its sides, lowering our eyes like camels in the sun. Al-Iqmah: raising the head and lowering the gaze. It is said: Al-Ghal qamahu he raised his head from distress if he left his head raised due to his distress. The two months of qamaah: the most severe cold, and they are the two braziers, and they were named thus because when camels come to it, the cold water harms them and they lower their heads. And from this, qamahat al-sawiq the gruel is derived. It was said: It is a metaphor that God the Almighty gave them in their refusal to guide them like the refusal of one who is chained. Yahya bin Salam and Abu Ubaidah said this. And as it is said: So-and-so is a donkey, meaning he does not see the guidance. And as he said: They are shackled and chained to the right path. In al-Naba 78:Abu Dhu’ayb loved a woman in the pre-Islamic era, and when he converted to Islam, she tried to seduce him, but he refused and began to say: This house is not like the old days, O Umm Malik, but chains have surrounded the necks. The young man returned like an old man, saying nothing but justice, so the critics were relieved. He wanted to prevent us from committing adultery and immorality with the prohibitions of Islam. Al-Farra’ also said: This is a parable, meaning that we prevented them from spending in the way of God, and it is like the saying of God the Almighty: {And do not make your hand chained to your neck} (al-Isra’ 17:29). Ad-Dahhak said: It was also said that these people became, in their arrogance towards the truth, like someone who puts a shackle on his hand and then it is tied to his neck, so he remains raising his head and not lowering it, and lowering his gaze and not opening it. The arrogant person is described as having an erect neck. Al-Azhari said: When their hands were chained to their necks, the shackles raised their chins and heads upwards like camels when they raise their heads. This prevention is by creating disbelief in the hearts of the disbelievers, and among some people by depriving them of success as a punishment for their disbelief. It was said: The verse is a reference to what will be done to people in Hell tomorrow, by placing shackles and chains around their necks, as God Almighty said: When the shackles are around their necks and the chains (Ghafir 40:71), and He spoke about it in the past tense. They will be restrained has been explained previously. Mujahid said: They will be restrained and prevented from every good thing.
36:9: The Almighty said: And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier. Muqatil said: When Abu Jahl returned to his companions and did not reach the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and the stone fell from his hand, another man from Banu Makhzum took the stone and said: I will kill him with this stone. When he came close to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), God blinded him so that he did not see the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). So he returned except for his companions, but he did not see them until they called him. This is the meaning of the verse. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in his narration: "Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi'ah, and Abu Jahl and Umayyah ibn Khalaf sat watching the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to harm him. Then he (peace be upon him) came out to them reciting Yasin and had dirt in his hand. He threw it at them and recited: "And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier." So they lowered their heads until he (peace be upon him) passed by them. This has already been mentioned in Surat Subhan and in Al-Kahf the discussion of sadaan with damma or fatha on the seen has already been mentioned and they are two dialects. Fa-ghinahum means We covered their sight, and this has already been mentioned in the beginning of Al-Baqarah. Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and Yahya bin Ya’mar read Fa-ghinahum with an unvoiced ‘ayn from ‘isha’ in ‘ayn which is the weakness of her sight so that she cannot see at night. He said: * When you come to him, you will be enveloped in the light of his fire * God Almighty said: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful (al-Zukhruf 43:36) and the verse. The meanings are similar, and the meaning is that He has blinded them, as He said: And from the accidents, I don't care that I was hit on the ground with axes I did not find my way to the place where I climbed between Al-Udhaib and the land of Murad. "They do not see" meaning guidance, as Qatadah said. It was also said: Muhammad when they plotted to kill him, as As-Suddi said. Ad-Dahhak said: "And We placed before them a barrier meaning this world, and behind them a barrier" meaning the Hereafter, meaning they were blind to the resurrection and blind to accepting the laws in this world. God the Most High said: "And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them" (Fussilat 41:25) meaning they made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them and called them to deny the Hereafter. It was also said: Based on this, "before them a barrier means they were deceived by this world, and behind them a barrier" meaning denial of the Hereafter. It was also said: "before them is the Hereafter and behind them is this world, and it is the same to them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe." This was mentioned in Al-Baqarah, and the verse is a refutation of the Qadarites and others. On the authority of Ibn Shihab: Omar bin Abdul Aziz brought Ghailan al-Qadri and said: O Ghailan, I have heard that you speak about predestination. He said: They are lying about me, O Commander of the Faithful. Then he said: O Commander of the Faithful, have you seen the words of God the Most High: {Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture that We may try him; and We made him hearing and seeing. Indeed, We have shown him the way, be he grateful or ungrateful.} (al-Insan 76:2-3) He said: {Read, O Ghailan.} So he read until he reached the words: {So whoever wills may take to his Lord a way.} So he said: {Read.} He said: {And you do not will except that God wills.} So he said: {By God, O Commander of the Faithful, I have never known that this was in the Book of God.} So he said to him: O Ghailan, read the beginning of Surah Ya-Seen. So he read until he reached: {And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe.} Ghailan said: {By God, O Commander of the Faithful, it is as if I had never read it before today. I bear witness, O Commander of the Faithful, that I have repented. Omar said: O God, if he is truthful, then accept his repentance and make him steadfast, and if he is lying, then send against him someone who will not have mercy on him and make him a sign for the believers. So Hisham took him, cut off his hands and feet, and crucified him. Ibn Awn said: I saw him crucified at the gate of Damascus. We said: What is the matter with you, Ghailan? He said: The supplication of the righteous man Omar ibn Abdul Aziz fulfilled my desire.
36:10: God Almighty says: And it is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them - they will not believe.
36:11: God Almighty says: You can only warn him who follows the message meaning the Qur’an and acts upon it. And fears the Most Merciful in secret meaning, that is, the punishment and Hellfire that is hidden from people’s sight, as stated by Qatada. It was also said that he fears Him while hidden from people’s sight and while he is alone with himself. Then give him good tidings of forgiveness meaning for his sin and a noble reward meaning Paradise.
36:12: It contains four issues: First - The Almighty's saying: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life. The Almighty informed us of His bringing the dead to life in response to the disbelievers.
